title: Indications for Dose Adjustment of Thyroid Hormones in Older Patients.
authorString: Bojunga J, Koehler VF, Drey M, Jaursch-Hancke C, Denkinger M.
abstractText:
Background

Thyroid dysfunction is common in older people (persons aged 65 and above). A meta-analysis of data from European countries revealed a 4.1% prevalence of undiagnosed subclinical hypothyroidism. It was found in a primary care study from the United Kingdom that approximately 10 percent of people over age 70 were under treatment for hypothyroidism.

Methods

This narrative review is based on findings in relevant publications retrieved by a PubMed search and on the guidelines of the European Thyroid Association and the American Thyroid Association.

Results

Overtreatment with levothyroxine increases the risk of cardiovascular, cognitive, and skeletal complications (hazard ratio 1.37-2.02). Randomized controlled trials have not shown that treatment with levothyroxine (T4) improves presumed symptoms of hypothyroidism, body weight, or fatigue. In patients who are now taking levothyroxine, lowering the dose or stopping the drug should be considered; in older patients, the target range for thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) should be 4-10 mU/L. After levothyroxine is stopped, some patients remain euthyroid; in the absence of an indication, gradual tapering may be considered. Levothyroxine should not be given over the long term to patients with thyroid nodules. Subclinical hyperthyroidism in older people is associated with clinically relevant risks, particularly atrial fibrillation and bone fractures, and should therefore be treated. Its most common cause, however, is levothyroxine treatment that is either not indicated or improperly dosed.

Conclusion

While overt hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism must be treated at any age, the need to treat subclinical hypothyroidism should be individually assessed; subclinical hyperthyroidism, by contrast, generally warrants treatment given its associated risks. In view of the risks of inadequately treated hyperthyroidism and excessively dosed levothyroxine, physicians should regularly review the indication for treatment, the dosage, and the possibility of lowering the dose or discontinuing the drug.

title: Long-term outcomes of biodegradable- versus durable-polymer drug-eluting stents in patients with advanced chronic kidney disease undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a 7-year retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Yeh JK, Huang MS, Chang HY, Lee WH, Liu PY, Liu YW.
abstractText:
Objectives

Patients with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) or end-stage renal disease (ESRD) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) have high event rates, but long-term outcomes after contemporary drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation remain insufficiently defined. This study compared 7-year outcomes between biodegradable polymer DES (BP-DES) and durable polymer DES (DP-DES) in patients with stage 5 CKD or ESRD undergoing PCI.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed patients with stage 5 CKD or ESRD who underwent PCI with DES implantation between 2010 and 2019. The primary outcome was target lesion failure (TLF), defined as cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction, or clinically driven target lesion revascularization. The secondary outcome was all-cause mortality. Outcomes were compared using Cox regression, competing-risk analysis, and overlap-weighted propensity score analysis.

Results

Among 417 patients, the mean age was 66.8 ± 10.4 years, 60.4% were male, and the median follow-up was 80 months. The 84-month cumulative incidence of TLF was 49% with BP-DES and 39% with DP-DES (Gray's test, P = 0.235). The observed 7-year mortality was 37.5 and 32.6%, respectively. DP-DES was not significantly associated with TLF [adjusted hazard ratio vs. BP-DES: 0.79, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.54-1.14; P = 0.207] or mortality (adjusted hazard ratio: 0.91, 95% CI: 0.63-1.33; P = 0.634). Older age and diabetes mellitus independently predicted mortality.

Conclusion

In patients with stage 5 CKD or ESRD undergoing PCI, 7-year TLF and mortality were frequent and did not differ significantly by DES polymer type.

title: Age-adjusted baseline D-dimer predicts thrombotic events during readmission in anticoagulated patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation
authorString: Wang X, Zhang L, Zhang D, Yu J, Dai Z, Li Q, Yan X.
abstractText: Background Patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) remain at substantial risk of thrombotic and bleeding events despite oral anticoagulation, and readmission is a common and costly consequence. D-dimer reflects persistent coagulation and fibrinolysis activation and has been associated with adverse outcomes in atrial fibrillation, but whether a single baseline measurement can predict events during readmission remains unclear. Methods We retrospectively studied 1,108 anticoagulated patients with NVAF who had multiple hospitalisations at our institution between 2018 and 2022. Patients were stratified by baseline D-dimer according to an age-adjusted cut-off. The primary endpoint was a composite of thrombotic events, major bleeding and death during readmission, adjudicated by a hierarchical first-event rule. Multivariable Cox regression was performed in the 899 patients with complete CHA₂DS₂-VASc and HAS-BLED scores. Sensitivity analyses included propensity score matching (230 pairs) and a competing-risk model and a 30-day landmark analysis. The incremental value of the age-adjusted D-dimer cut-off beyond CHA₂DS₂-VASc was assessed by the C-statistic. Results The abnormal-D-dimer group had a higher incidence of the composite endpoint (24.0% vs 9.6%, P < 0.001) and of thrombotic events (19.7% vs 8.2%, P < 0.001). Abnormal D-dimer independently predicted the composite endpoint (adjusted HR 1.64, 95% CI 1.09–2.47) and thrombotic events (adjusted HR 2.02, 95% CI 1.30–3.15), but not major bleeding (HR 1.46, 95% CI 0.44–4.90) or death during readmission (HR 1.73, 95% CI 0.54–5.52). Sensitivity analyses were consistent for the composite and thrombotic endpoints, whereas bleeding and death events were too few for reliable estimates. Adding D-dimer to CHA₂DS₂-VASc improved discrimination (ΔC = 0.034, 95% CI 0.006–0.076) and reclassification (24-month NRI = 43.8%; IDI = 0.025). Conclusions In anticoagulated patients with NVAF, a baseline D-dimer above the age-adjusted cut-off independently predicts thrombotic events during subsequent readmission and provides incremental predictive information beyond CHA₂DS₂-VASc.

title: The Detection of Atrial Fibrillation by Implantable Event Recorders: A Study of Patients Who Have Had a Cryptogenic Stroke.
authorString: Wagner F, Günther A, Kirsch K, Schulze CP, Klingner C, Geis C, Brodoehl S, Weigel K, Klinner C.
abstractText:
Background

Arial fibrillation (AF) plays a role in approximately one-third of ischemic strokes. In embolic strokes of undetermined source (ESUS), paroxysmal atrial fibrillation often escapes detection; if detected, it could be an indication for oral anticoagulation. In the ARTESiA trial, the absolute benefit of anticoagulation was higher in patients who had already had a stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA) than in those who had not.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed data from 233 consecutive ESUS patients at the Jena University Hospital who had received an implanted loop recorder (ILR) over the period 2021-2025. We additionally provide a narrative review on the detection rates associated with various monitoring strategies based on pertinent publications that were retrieved by a literature search.

Results

The 12-month detection rate of paroxysmal AF was 24.0% (56/233, 95% confidence interval [19.0; 29.9]). 73.2% of the initial detections were within the first 90 days. All patients in whom AF was detected were orally anticoagulated. The 12-month detection rate was higher than in the CRYSTAL-AF trial (12.4%) and the PER-DIEM trial (15.3%), but lower than was reported by Pikija et al. (31.3%). The cutoff values with the highest positive predictive value were a stroke risk analysis (SRA) index of 2 or above (38.4%) and age 75 or above (37.9%).

Conclusion

Early, risk-adapted diagnostic testing with ILR in selected ESUS patients can detect clinically relevant AF. Advanced age and an elevated SRA index may be useful patient selection criteria. A robust number needed to treat (NNT) for the ILR strategy cannot be derived from the available one-armed registry data. The indication for ILR should be linked to its therapeutic relevance, the probability of detecting AF, and the individual hemorrhagic risk.

title: ENPP1 deficiency in siblings with apparently discordant phenotypes: case report and a review of the literature.
authorString: Wada T, Miyahara Y, Hasegawa Y, Hirata K, Matsuoka K, Ishii Y, Mochizuki N, Okamoto N, Etani Y, Kawai M.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

abstractText:
Objectives

ENPP1 deficiency encompasses a phenotypic spectrum from generalized arterial calcification of infancy (GACI) to autosomal recessive hypophosphatemic rickets type 2 (ARHR2), and phenotypic variability has been reported even among individuals carrying the same variants; however, the extent of intrafamilial phenotypic concordance remains unclear.

Case presentation

Case 1, a 20-month-old boy, presented with genu varum and fibroblast growth factor 23-mediated hypophosphatemic rickets. Genetic testing identified compound heterozygous ENPP1 variants, c.937_938insT (p.Gln313LeufsTer18), and a deletion involving exons 8-13. Ultrasonography revealed valvular calcifications, carotid intimal irregularity, and nephrocalcinosis. Case 2, his younger brother, developed fetal hydrops, diffuse cardiovascular calcification, and severe cardiac dysfunction in late gestation and died shortly after preterm birth. Postmortem examination demonstrated extensive vascular calcification consistent with GACI; genetic testing identified the same variants. A sibling-based literature review of genetically confirmed cases with shared biallelic ENPP1 variants identified 21 publications describing 26 unrelated families. Including the present family, 27 families comprising 61 affected individuals were analyzed; 24 families (88.9 %) had concordant phenotypes, whereas three (11.1 %) had discordant phenotypes. Among 19 individuals who presented with hypophosphatemia or ARHR2 without a documented history of GACI and underwent cardiovascular, calcification, and/or hearing assessment, 14 had abnormal findings.

Conclusions

Documented GACI status was generally concordant among affected siblings. Frequent cardiovascular, calcification-related, and/or hearing abnormalities in patients presenting with hypophosphatemia or ARHR2 without a documented history of GACI highlight the importance of multisystem assessment and support GACI and ARHR2 as overlapping manifestations within the ENPP1 deficiency spectrum.

title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure or Anticoagulation for Atrial Fibrillation: Navigating Heterogeneity in Clinical Evidence: JACC Evidence Review.
authorString: Bikdeli B, Arun AS, Pawar S, Dhruva SS, Butala NM, Yong C, Spatz ES, Cohen DJ, Bittl JA, Albert CM, Leon MB, Makkar RR, Nazarian S, Krumholz HM, Gupta A.

journal.title: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

abstractText: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has emerged as an alternative to long-term anticoagulation for preventing stroke or systemic embolism in selected patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) based on several randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that collectively enrolled >7,000 participants. In this JACC Evidence Review, we interpret the major RCTs as distinct experiments, clarify what each can and cannot establish, and offer a phenotype-based framework for interpreting the evidence. The most recent RCTs, OPTION, CLOSURE-AF, and CHAMPION-AF, have prompted efforts to pool the evidence into a single summary estimate. However, these trials are not one coherent evidence base; they are distinct clinical experiments that asked different questions. They differ in patient phenotype, comparator, device generation, postprocedure antithrombotic regimen, endpoint construction, and follow-up duration. Study-level meta-analysis of published reports remains methodologically valid for estimating the broad direction of effect of a device class, but when the component trials differ materially in patient phenotype, comparator, and outcome construction, the pooled estimate does not map to a common patient group or treatment decision. Patient eligibility as well as thromboembolic and bleeding risk varied markedly across trials. In addition, device technology has progressed, and comparators have evolved from warfarin to direct oral anticoagulants. Heterogeneity and insufficient details also exist about the antithrombotic therapy regimen in LAAC arms and adjunct antiplatelet therapy in control arms. Methodological issues further complicate interpretation, including the use of bleeding events (ie, the putative ancillary benefit of LAAC compared with anticoagulation) within composite endpoints tested for noninferiority, varying noninferiority margins, analytical approaches that may undermine the interpretation of noninferiority, and exclusion of periprocedural bleeding from primary safety endpoints in some trials. Finally, the standard of care for anticoagulation in AF has evolved, obviating concomitant aspirin use in stable individuals on therapeutic anticoagulation, thereby reducing bleeding risk compared with that of the control arm of LAAC RCTs. For most anticoagulation-eligible patients, anticoagulation remains the preferred first-line strategy. LAAC is a reasonable option when long-term anticoagulation is unsafe or unsustainable provided that procedural risk, adjunct antithrombotic feasibility, surveillance needs, and competing mortality are carefully considered. RCT evidence in this latter population is limited, and RCTs in other populations have features that limit their support for LAAC as an alternative to anticoagulation. Because LAAC and anticoagulation offer different types of risk, aligning the most applicable evidence with patient values through shared decision-making is central to care.

title: Rationale and Design of a Multicenter, Randomized Controlled Trial: LEAP-Block.
authorString: Zhu K, Li X, Zhu H, Li W, Wang Y, Ellenbogen KA, Gold MR, Yao Y, Fan X.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Atrioventricular block with normal cardiac function is common with right ventricular pacing, which raises risks of pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and symptomatic heart failure in some patients with high pacing burden. Left bundle-branch area pacing demonstrates protective potential to reduce the risk of heart failure on the basis of observational studies. Evidence from a large multicenter randomized controlled trial remains limited.

Methods

The LEAP-Block (Impact of Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing Versus Right Ventricular Pacing in Atrioventricular Block) study is a prospective multicenter, investigator-initiated randomized controlled trial aiming to verify the hypothesis that left bundle-branch area pacing might have superior impact to right ventricular pacing in reducing the risk of cardiovascular events in patients with atrioventricular block requiring high burden of ventricular pacing and left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50%. A total of 484 patients will be randomized to either left bundle-branch area pacing or right ventricular pacing (1:1). The primary end point is the composite events of all-cause death, heart failure events, and upgrade to biventricular pacing-delivered cardiac resynchronization therapy during at least 24 months of follow-up. Secondary end points include changes in echocardiographic, electrocardiographic, and pacing parameters and device-related complications.

Conclusions

The LEAP-Block study aims to compare the impact of left bundle-branch area pacing versus conventional right ventricular pacing in patients with atrioventricular block and preserved cardiac function with respect to midterm clinical outcomes. This trial will provide high-quality evidence for the selection of optimal pacing strategies in clinical practice.

Registration information

clinicaltrials.gov. Identifier: NCT04730921.

title: Antihypertensive treatment - achievements and perspectives in Europe by 2026 Italian, Swiss and Norwegian patient care.
authorString: Kjeldsen SE, Gravning J, Stokke MK, Burnier M, Grassi G, Mancia G.
abstractText:
Purpose

The aim of this perspective review paper is to provide a concise overview of selected aspects of contemporary hypertension care in Norway, Switzerland, and Italy; European countries with populations of approximately 5.5, 9, and 61 million inhabitants, respectively. These countries show remarkably similar prevalences of hypertension, as well as comparable proportions of hypertensive patients who are diagnosed, treated, and controlled.

Methods

Each country has contributed to the development of hypertension management in distinctive ways. This is illustrated by the evolution of hypertension care in the three countries-which advanced hypertension management through different but complementary contributions.

Results

Italy has provided extensive clinical and research expertise, together with sustained engagement in the European Society of Hypertension and in the development of European guidelines. Norway has been strongly involved in the design and conduct of many large clinical trials that helped define the clinical evidence base in the field, and with general practitioners as investigators. Also, the government financed major surveys and epidemiological studies with blood pressure (BP) as a key variable including collecting data for modern risk assessment in old people (SCORE2-Old People). Switzerland, for its part, made important contributions to the development of new antihypertensive drugs, particularly blockers of the renin-angiotensin system and calcium antagonists. Switzerland was also among the first European countries to accept, promote, and reimburse ambulatory blood pressure monitoring performed by general practitioners, already by the late 1980s.

Conclusion

We summarize novelties in text boxes besides basic principles, recent clarifications, and important unresolved issues, supported by selected key references.

title: Effects of Sacred Dances versus Conventional Physical Training on Functional Capacity and Quality of Life in Women with Heart Failure: Protocol for a Randomized Active-Controlled Crossover Non-Inferiority Trial (RED-WHF)
authorString: VON FLACH MT, Fernandes ES, Almeida MCBdA, Suarez HC, Correia MvF, Junquilho AAL, Abreu AMFdN, Dias CMCC, Ritt LEF.
abstractText: This protocol describes the RED-WHF trial, a randomized, active-controlled, two-period crossover clinical trial designed to evaluate whether Sacred Dances (SD)—as a mind-body intervention—are non-inferior to conventional physical training (PT) regarding functional capacity and quality of life in women with heart failure (HF). Sedentary behavior and emotional stress significantly worsen HF prognosis, yet conventional exercise programs face barriers in patient adherence and variable motivation. Sacred Dances, a form of low-to-moderate-intensity moving meditation, may enhance physical fitness while promoting emotional well-being and spiritual connection (flourishing). We will recruit 30 sedentary women aged 18 to 70 with stable HF (NYHA class I-III) and a documented left ventricular ejection fraction. Participants will be randomized 1:1 to one of two treatment sequences: SD followed by PT, or vice versa. Each 12-week intervention phase consists of two weekly sessions, lasting 90 minutes for SD (with 60 minutes of active dancing to allow choreography instruction) and 60 minutes for PT, separated by a 3-week washout period. Primary outcomes are functional capacity (6-minute walk test [6MWT]) and health-related quality of life (EQ-5D-5L Index and VAS). Secondary outcomes include adherence rates, spiritual attitudes (ARES scale), symptoms of depression, anxiety, and stress (DASS-21), and perceived subjective impact (EUPI-12). Statistical planning incorporates linear mixed models (LMM) with treatment, period, and sequence fixed effects, and an intention-to-treat approach with multiple imputation for missing data. To establish non-inferiority, a 30-meter margin for the 6MWT difference will be applied. The study was approved by the local Ethics Committee (CEP/EBMSP opinion 7.443.180, CAAE: 86133125.0.0000.5544) and prospectively registered in the Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials (ReBEC ID: RBR-85tkdz5).

title: Generative AI Versus Primary Care Physicians from Plan Initiation to Long-Term Maintenance of Chronic Disease Self-Management: A Vignette-Based Validation Study
authorString: Zhao Z, Yang H, Wang Q, Wang Y, Cheng W, Ma X.
abstractText:
Background:

Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) may provide personalised and dynamically adjustable support for chronic disease self-management. However, previous studies have largely focused on isolated questions and a limited range of evaluation dimensions. Objective To compare the quality of self-management advice generated by GenAI and primary care physicians (PCPs) across multiple stages of chronic disease management and evaluation dimensions. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional, source-blinded comparative evaluation using 15 standardised vignettes of diabetes and hypertension derived from authentic primary care follow-up records. Each vignette comprised three sequential management stages, with medical accuracy, readability, and behaviour-change potential assessed across the three simulated stages; individualisation and multidisciplinary integration at plan initiation; contextual adaptability during acute adjustment; and empathy during long-term maintenance. The GenAI system and 22 PCPs independently generated advice which was independently rated by three clinicians，one each from general practice, endocrinology, and cardiology. across seven dimensions. Linear mixed-effects models were used for the primary comparisons, and case-level paired and physician-distribution analyses were conducted as robustness analyses. Results The GenAI system achieved estimated marginal means above 4.0 in all dimensions except readability. It scored significantly higher than PCPs in six of the seven dimensions, with adjusted mean differences ranging from 1.16 to 1.56 points (P<.001). Readability was the only exception, with no significant difference between GenAI and PCPs (−0.22, 95% CI −0.54 to 0.11; P=.19). The GenAI mean exceeded the individual means of all recruited PCPs in the six dimensions but ranked at approximately the 23rd percentile for readability. Conclusions Our findings indicated the GenAI system may generate more highly rated self-management advice than PCPs across most evaluated dimensions but offered no advantage in readability. These findings provide pre-implementation evidence for GenAI as a potential source of structured and adaptive chronic disease self-management support. Patient-level pilot studies and subsequent randomised trials are needed to determine its acceptability and effects on behaviour and clinical outcomes.

title: Lower Preoperative Serum Magnesium Is Associated With Postoperative Atrial Fibrillation After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study
authorString: Zhang Y, Wang S, Zhang H, Lu Y, Wang Z, Wei J.
abstractText: Background Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is the most common arrhythmic complication after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). We evaluated whether pleural drainage tube placement influences POAF and identified clinical factors associated with POAF, particularly serum magnesium. Methods In this single-center retrospective cohort study, we screened 602 consecutive adults who underwent CABG between September 2020 and June 2026. The exposure was intraoperative pleural drainage tube placement, and the outcome was POAF. Associations were assessed by multivariable logistic regression, propensity score matching (PSM), inverse probability of treatment weighting, and overlap weighting. Results A total of 520 patients were included (mean age 64.8 ± 7.9 years; 372 men, 71.5%). Pleural drainage tubes were placed in 166 patients (31.9%), and POAF occurred in 135 patients (26.0%). Lower serum magnesium was independently associated with POAF in a dose-dependent manner: adjusted OR per 0.05 mmol/L increment 0.78 (95% CI 0.67–0.91, P < 0.001); magnesium tertiles showed a significant trend (P for trend = 0.011); and magnesium below the internally derived cutoff of 0.815 mmol/L was associated with increased risk (adjusted OR 1.94, 95% CI 1.19–3.15, P = 0.008; AUC 0.612). The E-value for this association was 2.13. Pleural drainage tube placement was not independently associated with POAF: crude OR 1.32 (95% CI 0.87–2.00), adjusted OR 1.36 (95% CI 0.85–2.15), and PSM OR 1.37 (95% CI 0.81–2.33). The study was underpowered to detect an OR below 1.78 for the drainage association. Conclusions Lower preoperative serum magnesium was independently associated with POAF in a dose-dependent manner, whereas pleural drainage tube placement was not. Because perioperative magnesium supplementation was not recorded, these findings cannot establish whether magnesium optimization would reduce POAF risk; this hypothesis requires prospective randomized trials. Clinical trial number: not applicable.

title: Predictors of Clinically Meaningful 1-Year Health Status Improvements Following Endovascular or Surgical Revascularization: Insights From the BEST-CLI Trial.
authorString: Smolderen KG, Menard M, Farber A, Rahman MM, Rosenfield K, Strong M, Doros G, Goodney P, Shah SK, Powell RR, Suckow B, Houland K, Siracuse J, Romain G, Cleman J, Scierka L, Mena-Hurtado C.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Despite efforts to promote limb salvage in chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), the factors associated with meaningful health status improvement after revascularization remain poorly understood. We examined predictors of meaningful 1-year health status improvement following revascularization for CLTI.

Methods

We pooled endovascular and surgical arms from the BEST-CLI (Best Endovascular Versus Best Surgical Therapy in Patients With CLTI) randomized controlled trial, including patients with CLTI (150 international sites, 2014-2019). Health status was assessed at baseline and 1 year using the peripheral artery disease-specific Vascular Quality of Life questionnaire, the generic European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, and the Short Form-12 Physical and Mental Component Summary. Distribution-based minimal clinically important difference thresholds were defined as 0.5 SD of baseline health status scores. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of no meaningful 1-year improvement (same/worsened versus improved).

Results

Among 1017 patients (72.0% men, mean age 66.8±9.7 years), clinically meaningful improvements were reported by 76.5% for Vascular Quality of Life, 52.8% European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, 56.7% for Short Form-12 Physical Component Summary, and 42.1% for Short Form-12 Mental Component Summary, regardless of revascularization type (surgical versus endovascular). Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status increased the odds of no meaningful improvement. Revascularization type was not associated with Vascular Quality of Life improvement (odds ratio, 1.059 [95% CI, 0.91-1.23]; P=0.445; C statistic=0.77).

Conclusions

One-year postrevascularization, over three-fourths of individuals with CLTI perceived meaningful improvements in peripheral artery disease-specific health, and over half improved overall physical health, regardless of procedure type. Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status predicted 1-year health status response. REGISTRATION: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02060630.

title: Global Prevalence of Obstetric Causes of Critical Illness in Pregnancy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Kuppusamy P, Kale DP, Manjrekar MR, Hardwaria P.
abstractText:
Objectives

To determine the prevalence, risks, and outcomes of obstetric causes of critically ill pregnant women admitted to the ICU.

Data sources

We searched the PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Ovid, and ScienceDirect databases up to May 15, 2026.

Study selection

We included studies reporting primary data on critically ill pregnant and postpartum women (up to 48 d post-delivery) admitted to an ICU, with relevant obstetric risk factors and maternal outcomes.

Data extraction

Two reviewers independently performed data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment using the adapted Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. The pooled prevalence was estimated using a random-effects model with 95% CIs.

Data synthesis

Of the 3,735 total records, 50 studies met the eligibility criteria, encompassing 7,756,232 women receiving obstetric care in tertiary hospitals across 20 countries, with 49,299 ICU admissions. Globally, 1.0% (95% CI, 0.8-1.3%) of pregnant and postpartum women experience critical illness and require admission to an ICU. The frequency varies according to the country's income levels, with the highest in low-income countries (4.1%) and the lowest in high-income countries (0.5%). Notably, 72.3% of ICU admissions were attributed to known obstetric causes, primarily obstetric hemorrhage (23.3%) and hypertension in pregnancy (26.9%). Nearly 33.3% of ICU patients required either respiratory or transfusion support, and the maternal mortality rate among ICU-admitted obstetric women was 8.5%.

Conclusions

Nearly one in 100 pregnancies require admission to intensive care due to critical illness, and nearly three-quarters of these admissions were due to direct obstetric causes, with high maternal morbidity and mortality. Obstetric hemorrhage and hypertensive disorders account for the majority of ICU admissions. Strengthening obstetric care in resource-limited settings through the expansion and optimization of intensive care services is essential for improving maternal and neonatal outcomes and reducing preventable morbidity and mortality.

title: High on the Heart? Cannabis Use and Cardiovascular Disease: A Systematic Review.
authorString: Chehade MJ, Haas MJ, Mooradian AD.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText: Cannabis use has increased substantially over the past 2 decades following shifts in public perception, legalization, and medical usage. Although neurological and psychiatric effects are well known, the cardiovascular effects of cannabis exposure are largely understudied. This review evaluates the cardiovascular effects of cannabis use by examining clinical evidence, epidemiological data, and underlying biochemical mechanisms. This review examines cannabis-related cardiovascular conditions, including atherosclerosis, arrhythmias, heart failure, and stroke. The analysis focused on cannabinoid composition, route of administration, frequency of use, and cardiovascular outcomes. Evidence indicates that acute and high Δ<sup>9</sup>-tetrahydrocannabinol/cannabidiol ratio cannabis use is associated with increased risks of various cardiovascular outcomes, especially among younger individuals without cardiovascular risk factors. Given rising use and increasing Δ<sup>9</sup>-tetrahydrocannabinol potency, clinicians must routinely assess cannabis exposure when evaluating cardiovascular disease, especially in younger patients. Future research must prioritize the development of standardized exposure metrics in cannabis-related cardiovascular disease research, thus allowing clinicians and patients to better understand the cardiovascular risks of cannabis use and initiate effective cessation strategies.

title: Proteomics and Risk of Incident Ischemic Stroke: Meta-Analysis of the ARIC Study and CHS.
authorString: Wang W, Wu Y, Kalani R, Ye T, Bartz TM, Zhang MJ, Pankow JS, Lakshminarayan K, Alonso A, Lutsey PL, Ballantyne CM, Matsushita K, Johansen MC, Gottesman RF, Coresh J, Pan W, Walker KA, Heckbert SR, Psaty BM, Sitlani CM, Brody JA, Finkel N, Gudmundsdottir V, Gudnason V, Longstreth WT, Chen LY, Floyd JS.
abstractText:
Background

Ischemic stroke preventive therapies have been slow to emerge due to a limited understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms. We aimed to discover new protein risk factors that are potential etiologic factors and may be candidates for therapeutic intervention.

Methods

We included ARIC study (Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities) and CHS (Cardiovascular Health Study) participants without prevalent stroke at the time of proteomic profiling (1990-1992 in ARIC and 1992-1993 in CHS). Relative concentrations of proteins in blood were assessed with aptamers (n=4954). Ischemic stroke events were adjudicated through 2019 in ARIC and 2015 in CHS. Study-specific Cox regression adjusting for ischemic stroke risk factors was used to estimate associations between proteins and incident ischemic stroke. Study-specific estimates were combined using fixed-effects meta-analysis. Replication was conducted in 2 independent cohorts (AGES-Reykjavik, UK Biobank). Proteins with a false discovery rate q value <0.05 were considered replicated. Mendelian randomization analyses assessed for potential causal associations between proteins and ischemic stroke.

Results

Median follow-up was 25 and 12 years in ARIC and CHS. 1397 out of 14 139 (10%) participants experienced an ischemic stroke. 44 proteins were significantly associated with ischemic stroke risk (P<1.0×10-5), of which 26 are novel. In 2 independent cohorts, 37 (84%) associations were directionally concordant, and 26 (59%) met criteria for replication. Mendelian randomization analyses suggested MMP12 (matrix metallopeptidase-12) and CNTN1 (contactin-1) may be causally related to ischemic stroke risk. In multivariable Mendelian randomization analyses, higher MMP12 levels had a direct protective effect on ischemic stroke risk, while CNTN1 had a direct harmful effect.

Conclusions

This proteomic and genomic investigation of ischemic stroke identified novel risk biomarkers and 2 potential etiologic CNTN1 factors that are regulated in response to atherosclerosis and obesity. If future studies confirm our findings, these results may have implications for the development of new preventive therapies.

title: Prevalence of type 2 diabetes mellitus, risk factors, and complications in Middle East and North African region: A systematic review.
authorString: Lovelin Auguskani JP, Gurusamy V, Muttipoll Dharmarajlu S, Chellathurai A, Arulappan J.
abstractText: BackgroundType 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) is a rapidly growing health challenge in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, contributing to increasing morbidity and mortality.ObjectivesThis review synthesizes evidence on the prevalence of T2DM, risk factors, and complications in the MENA region.MethodsFollowing PRISMA reporting guidelines and PROSPERO registration (CRD420251111168), systematic searches were conducted for studies published between 2015 and 2025.ResultsAcross the 19 included studies, the prevalence and burden of T2DM varied considerably across the MENA region. Regional data indicated an 85.5% increase in diabetes prevalence between 1990 and 2019, while individual population-based studies reported T2DM prevalence of 32.0% in north-eastern Tunisia and 15.3% in southwestern Iran. In Jordan, age-standardized diabetes prevalence increased from 13.0% in 1994 to 23.7% in 2017. Older age, obesity, physical inactivity, hypertension, central adiposity, family history of diabetes, and socioeconomic factors were commonly associated with T2DM. Among individuals with established T2DM, microvascular and macrovascular complications were reported in 17.7% and 10.7%, respectively, while diabetic neuropathy affected 15.3%-23.0% in selected studies. Suboptimal glycaemic and cardiovascular risk-factor control was also frequently reported.ConclusionT2DM constitutes a substantial and heterogeneous public health challenge across the MENA region. The findings indicate a need for context-specific strategies that integrate prevention, early detection, culturally appropriate lifestyle interventions, and comprehensive long-term disease management. Strengthening multidisciplinary approaches and addressing modifiable risk factors may help reduce the future health burden associated with T2DM across the region.

title: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation in Critically Ill Patients: A Systematic Review of In-Hospital and Post-Discharge Outcomes.
authorString: Tan SWZ, Lee QH, Ding W, Song Z, Koh JCK, Das Gupta K, Samuel M, Vu HL, Soong JTY, Cove ME.
abstractText:
Objectives

This systematic review and meta-analysis determines the incidence of new-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF) in critically ill patients, risks of post-discharge systemic thromboembolism, anticoagulation therapy, and the proportion diagnosed with AF post-discharge.

Data sources

A search of registered databases (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and CINAHL) was performed from inception to April 20, 2026.

Study selection

Eligible studies included critically ill patients (≥ 18 yr old) who developed NOAF during admission to general ICUs or high-dependency units. NOAF was defined as AF in patients without prior history of AF.

Data extraction

Data were independently extracted from full-text versions of included studies by nonblinded reviewers.

Data synthesis

A Bayesian meta-analysis was conducted on 54 studies (367,896 patients) with a random-effects model using R (Version 4.3.3). Pooled incidence of NOAF in critically ill patients was 10.6% (95% credible interval [CrI], 8.6-12.9%). Absolute risk of post-discharge systemic thromboembolism was 7.1% (95% CrI, 4.5-11.0%), changing to 6.9% (95% CrI, 4.2-11.6%) after age and sex adjustment. Evidence from six studies reports that critically ill patients with NOAF had 1.94 times (95% CrI, 1.23-3.29) higher relative risk of systemic thromboembolism post-discharge than patients without NOAF, rising to 2.01 (95% CrI, 1.54-2.80) with adjustment. Absolute and relative risk are evaluated with follow-up durations ranging from 1.5 months to 5 years, with variable anticoagulation exposure. Anticoagulation rates were low: 32.9% in-hospital (95% CrI, 14.6-57.9%) and 35.9% post-discharge (95% CrI, 19.7-55.9%). On follow-up, 23.9% (95% CrI, 13.9-38.5%) of critically ill patients with NOAF were subsequently diagnosed with AF.

Conclusions

Our review suggests that NOAF during critical illness is associated with significantly increased risk of post-discharge systemic thromboembolism and subsequent AF diagnosis. However, rates of anticoagulation initiation remain low, highlighting the need for improved risk stratification and targeted strategies post-discharge.

title: Clonal Hematopoiesis and Cardiovascular and Microvascular Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes: A Retrospective Analysis of the UK Biobank.
authorString: Gao Y, Zhang C, Chen D, Shi Z, Shi Q, Gu Y, Shi B, Ma C, Guo Q, Wang Y, Zhang Z, Geng B, Li M.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) has been associated with cardiovascular disease, but its associations across cardiovascular and microvascular complications in type 2 diabetes remain incompletely characterized.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed 17 893 UK Biobank participants with type 2 diabetes, whole-exome sequencing, and no prevalent cardiovascular or microvascular complications. CHIP was defined from the curated UK Biobank call set by ≥1 driver variant with a variant allele fraction ≥2%. Associations with incident outcomes were evaluated using Fine-Gray models with multiple imputation for missing covariates. Driver-gene, clone-size, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses were exploratory.

Results

CHIP was present in 670 participants (3.7%) over a median follow-up of 14.6 years. CHIP was associated with the composite cardiovascular outcome (subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR], 1.19 [95% CI, 1.00-1.42]), with heart failure showing the clearest component association (SHR, 1.43 [95% CI, 1.13-1.81]); acute coronary syndrome and stroke were not significantly associated. CHIP was also associated with the composite microvascular outcome (SHR, 1.34 [95% CI, 1.15-1.56]), broad chronic kidney disease (SHR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.05-1.57]), and retinopathy (SHR, 1.43 [95% CI, 1.15-1.77]) but not neuropathy or strict diabetes-specific nephropathy. Ten-year adjusted risk differences were 1.94% and 3.46% for the cardiovascular and microvascular composites, respectively. Among 2919 proteins, ZBP1 (Z-DNA-binding protein 1) was the only protein retained after false-discovery-rate correction; no metabolite module was associated with CHIP after correction, whereas selected lipoprotein and amino acid/lactate modules were associated with cardiovascular outcomes, particularly heart failure.

Conclusions

In adults with type 2 diabetes, CHIP was associated with a higher risk of incident microvascular complications and, among cardiovascular outcomes, most consistently with heart failure. Exploratory multiomic findings, including a protein-wide ZBP1 signal and selected metabolic associations with cardiovascular outcomes, provided additional biological context but require independent validation.

title: Medication Safety Risks Associated With Inappropriate Use of Non-Crushable Tablets in Enterally Fed Patients: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
authorString: Wang FL, Shih RL, Wang KH, Wang SR, Yang CC, Peng SM, Zhang QY, Shia BC, Chen M, Wang WM.
abstractText:
Background and objectives

Hospitalized patients receiving enteral feeding are at high risk of medication administration errors. In clinical practice, non-crushable oral tablets may be inappropriately prescribed, potentially resulting in adverse outcomes. This study examined the association between inappropriate use of non-crushable oral tablets during hospitalization and early post-discharge emergency department (ED) visits among patients receiving enteral feeding.

Methods

We conducted a nationwide population-based cohort study using a national health insurance claims database in 2020, including 173,476 hospitalized patients receiving enteral feeding. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate the association between inappropriate use of non-crushable tablets and the hazard of the first ED visit during the 3-day post-discharge follow-up period.

Results

Among 173,476 patients, 40.2% were exposed to inappropriate medication use. Exposure was associated with a significantly higher hazard of a first ED visit during the 3-day post-discharge follow-up period (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.954; 95% confidence interval, 1.721-2.217). The association varied significantly across age groups and inpatient departments, with the largest adjusted hazard ratios observed among patients aged <65 years and those treated in hematology and oncology, infectious diseases, and neurosurgery. Selected comorbidities, including hypertension, cerebrovascular accident, and dementia, were also associated with a higher hazard of an early ED visit.

Conclusion

Orders for non-crushable tablets among hospitalized patients receiving enteral feeding were common and were associated with a substantially higher hazard of an early post-discharge ED visit. The association varied across age groups and inpatient departments, although these subgroup findings should be interpreted cautiously. These findings highlight an important medication safety concern during transitions of care and support further evaluation of system-level strategies, including prescribing safeguards, clinical decision support, and multidisciplinary medication review, to improve the quality and safety of medication management.

title: Evaluating the Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Paradox in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction.
authorString: Xue R, Lee A, Jiang Y, Lau YH, Teo LLY, Wong RCC, Soon DKN, Shum KL, Huang W, Loh SY, Lin W, Chiang BSQ, Chow W, Hausenloy DJ, Yeo KK, Yap J.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Hypercholesterolemia is an established cardiovascular risk factor. However, studies in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) showed an association between low low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and increased mortality, termed the "LDL-C paradox." This study examined the impact of LDL-C on clinical outcomes in patients with HFrEF and identify distinct hypocholesterolemia subgroups using latent class analysis.

Methods

Consecutive patients with HFrEF (left ventricular EF <40%) from national registries (2016-2022) were stratified by LDL-C quartiles, with the lowest quartile ≤1.73 mmol/L. Latent class analysis was performed to identify subsets of patients in the lowest quartile. Outcomes included 1-year all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, readmission, and composite end points.

Results

Among 2188 patients, the lowest LDL-C quartile had higher 1-year all-cause mortality than Quartile 2 and 3 (P<0.05) but not Quartile 4, with no intergroup differences in cardiovascular mortality, readmissions, or composite outcomes between groups. Latent class analysis identified 2 hypocholesterolemia subgroups: pathological and nonpathological hypocholesterolemia. The pathological subgroup was older, lower weight, with higher comorbidity burden. Compared with patients with hypercholesterolemia, the pathological hypocholesterolemia subgroup had higher 1-year all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 2.14 [95% CI, 1.17-2.69], P<0.001), cardiovascular mortality (adjusted HR, 1.93 [95% CI, 1.46-2.54], P<0.001), and composite end points (adjusted HR, 1.15 [95% CI, 1.01-1.30], P=0.037), and the subgroup with nonpathological hypocholesterolemia showed comparable outcomes.

Conclusions

A distinct subset of patients with HFrEF with low LDL-C demonstrates different clinical characteristics (older and higher comorbidity burden) and poorer outcomes, potentially elucidating the "LDL-C paradox" cause in patients with HFrEF.

title: Thirty-Day All-Cause Readmissions After Pregnancy-Associated Hospitalizations With Heart Failure in the United States: Analysis of the Nationwide Readmissions Database.
authorString: Barry E, Kim MJ, Goldstein S, Denoble A, Hsueh C, Chavez P, Tabtabai S.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of pregnancy-related morbidity and mortality in the United States. There is a paucity of data regarding pregnancy-associated heart failure readmissions. This study aims to characterize the 30-day heart failure readmission patterns in pregnancy-associated admissions.

Methods

The National Readmission Database from 2016 to 2021 was used to identify women aged 13 to 49 with an index hospitalization with heart failure as the primary or secondary diagnosis during a pregnancy-related admission, identified by diagnosis-related group codes and International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) codes. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause readmission. Survey-weighted descriptive analyses and hierarchical multivariable logistic regression were used to characterize readmission patterns and identify independently associated factors.

Results

Among 19 452 eligible index hospitalizations, 2659 were followed by a 30-day readmission; the survey-weighted readmission rate was 13.5%. In the fully adjusted model, Medicare and Medicaid coverage, residence in a small metropolitan area, greater All Patient Refined Diagnosis-Related Group severity, discharge with home health care, and discharge against medical advice were associated with higher odds of readmission. Deficiency anemia, chronic pulmonary disease, diabetes without chronic complications, renal failure, solid tumor without metastasis, and cardiovascular or respiratory disorders complicating pregnancy were also independently associated with increased readmission.

Conclusions

Approximately 1 in 7 pregnancy-associated hospitalizations complicated by heart failure was followed by a 30-day all-cause readmission. Readmission risk reflected a combination of illness severity, discharge disposition, payer status, geographic location, and selected medical and pregnancy-related comorbidities. These findings support the development and evaluation of individualized, multidisciplinary transitional-care strategies for patients at highest risk.

title: Incidence of Cardiovascular Disease in a Primary Care Population of Young Adults by Disaggregated Race and Ethnicity.
authorString: Chapman R, King S, Jose PO, Avery B, Narayan GA, Rodriguez F, Yan X.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death in the United States, with well-documented racial and ethnic disparities. Data are limited on incidence among patients aged <50 years, particularly within disaggregated Asian and Hispanic subgroups and individuals identifying with multiple racial or ethnic groups. We estimated CVD incidence rates for these groups and assessed whether disparities are explained by other clinical and demographic risk factors.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study used Sutter Health Electronic Health Record data (2010-2024) for adults aged 18 to 49 years with at least 2 primary care visits and a 2-year observed baseline period free of CVD. Incident CVD was defined as myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure. We estimated incidence rates, applied age and sex standardization, and fit Cox proportional hazards models adjusting for additional risk factors.

Results

In a cohort of 1 178 551 patients, incidence was 1.14 cases per 1000 person-years (95% CI, 1.12-1.17). After standardization, Pacific Islander individuals (hazard ratio [HR], 2.90 [95% CI, 2.29-3.52]) and non-Hispanic Black individuals (HR, 2.82 [95% CI, 2.58-3.06]) had the highest incidence. Within the Asian group, Filipino individuals had the highest incidence (HR, 1.60 [95% CI, 1.42-1.79]). Hispanic subgroups showed less heterogeneity. Elevated HRs persisted among some groups after adjustment with Cox models.

Conclusions

Young adult CVD incidence varied across racial and ethnic subgroups. Elevated risk persisted in several groups after adjustment, consistent with the influence of unmeasured social drivers. These findings support collection of granular racial and ethnic data and validation of existing risk prediction tools in young adult subgroups.

title: Prognostic Value of Right Ventricular-Pulmonary Artery Coupling in Mitral Valve Surgery and Impact of Concomitant Tricuspid Valve Repair.
authorString: Kahrovic A, Herkner H, Gangl C, Zilberszac R, Coti I, Kocher A, Andreas M, Zimpfer D, Werner P.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

The prognostic impact of baseline right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling on clinical outcomes following mitral valve surgery with specific consideration of concomitant tricuspid valve repair remains uncertain.

Methods

A total of 214 patients who underwent mitral valve surgery and presented with moderate tricuspid regurgitation at the index procedure were included. Patients were classified after baseline right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling (impaired versus normal). The primary study end point was a composite outcome of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization. Secondary study end points included all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization.

Results

Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling was observed in 112 patients (52%), while 102 patients (48%) had normal right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling. The rate of concomitant tricuspid valve repair was similar between study groups (50.0% versus 49.0%, P=0.886). Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling was associated with a higher hazard of the composite outcome (adjusted hazard ratio 2.60, 95% CI 1.32-5.14, P=0.006), heart failure hospitalization (adjusted hazard ratio 3.29, 95% CI 1.27-8.54, P=0.014), and all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 2.25, 95% CI 1.11-4.59, P=0.025) during follow-up. Additionally, concomitant tricuspid valve repair in patients with moderate tricuspid regurgitation was associated with a lower hazard of the composite outcome (adjusted hazard ratio 0.45, 95% CI 0.26-0.80, P=0.007).

Conclusions

Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling is a predictor of adverse outcomes after mitral valve surgery. Concomitant tricuspid valve repair for moderate tricuspid regurgitation seems to be associated with improved outcomes.

title: Adeno-Associated Virus-Induced Humanized Hypertensive Mouse Model Validates N-Acetylgalactosamine-Conjugated Small Interfering RNA Targeting Angiotensinogen as a Long-Acting Antihypertensive Therapy.
authorString: Xiong J, Zhang S, Cheng K, Sheng Y, Lin J, Liu X, Liu T, Guo X, Zhu D, Wu L, Li R, Zhang B.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Hypertension remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, yet current therapeutic strategies lack sustained efficacy and long-term stability. Our study aimed to construct a humanized rodent model for drugs development especially currently prevalent small interfering RNA medication.

Methods

A humanized hypertensive mouse model was generated by subcutaneous injection of neonatal mice with adeno-associated viruses encoding hAGT (human angiotensinogen) and hRENIN (human renin). Blood pressure was monitored weekly via tail-cuff plethysmography. Expression of hAGT and hRENIN was assessed by ELISA, Western blot, and reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Cardiac function was evaluated by echocardiography at 4 and 6 months postinjection. Hypertension-associated comorbidities were examined through histological analysis and ELISA. A modified N-acetylgalactosamine-conjugated small interfering RNA targeting human hepatic AGT (GalNAc-siAGT) was screened and subcutaneously administered to humanized hypertensive mice, either alone or in combination with valsartan, to evaluate therapeutic efficacy.

Results

The dual adeno-associated virus-induced humanized hypertensive model exhibited a sustained hypertension for 6 months and manifested prevalent comorbidities, including heart failure and kidney disease. This modified GalNAc-siAGT demonstrated significant activity in knocking down hAGT both in vitro and in vivo. Only a single subcutaneous injection of GalNAc-siAGT in humanized hypertensive mice led to a sustained reduction in blood pressure lasting for 2 months, accompanied by cardio- and renoprotective effects. Moreover, combining GalNAc-siAGT with the renin-angiotensin system blocker, valsartan, significantly enhanced therapeutic efficacy.

Conclusions

Our study validated the antihypertensive therapeutic effect of GalNAc-siAGT in a humanized hypertensive murine model while highlighting the translational potential of this model for clinical drug development.

title: Prevalence of hypertension and associated factors among users of the Centre Hospitalier Médico-Diététique Père Morand Kleiber in Butembo, DRC: A quantitative cross-sectional study
authorString: Mundeke B, Musavuli G, Munyambethe J, Lukulirwa L, Mwenge G, Musimbulwa R, Vutseme N, Muyisa RM, Sabuni L.
abstractText: Background Hypertension is a major public health concern, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. However, local evidence on its burden and associated factors in Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) remains limited. This study aimed to determine the proportion of hypertension and identify its associated factors among users of the Centre Hospitalier Médico-Diététique Père Morand Kleiber in Butembo. Methods A quantitative cross-sectional study was conducted from June 2025 to May 2026 among 145 adults aged 25 years and older. Participants were selected using non-probability convenience sampling. Data on sociodemographic characteristics, behavioral factors, anthropometric measurements, blood pressure, and biochemical parameters were collected. Binary logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with hypertension. Results Among the 145 participants, 65 (44.8%) were hypertensive. The proportion of hypertension increased with age, from 13.6% among participants aged 25–34 years to 80.0% among those aged 65 years and older. In multivariable analysis, abdominal obesity (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 3.1; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.7–5.8; p < 0.001), male sex (aOR = 2.1; 95% CI: 1.2–3.9; p = 0.009), current smoking (aOR = 2.1; 95% CI: 1.0–4.5; p = 0.049), sedentary lifestyle (aOR = 1.9; 95% CI: 1.1–3.5; p = 0.03), and increasing age (aOR = 1.04 per year; 95% CI: 1.01–1.07; p = 0.01) were independently associated with hypertension. Unhealthy diet and alcohol consumption were not significantly associated with hypertension after adjustment. Conclusion A high proportion of participants had hypertension, with age, male sex, abdominal obesity, smoking, and sedentary lifestyle identified as independently associated factors. Strengthening routine blood pressure screening, waist circumference assessment, and lifestyle interventions may improve hypertension prevention and management in Butembo. Larger population-based studies are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Clinical characteristics, management, and short-term outcomes of acute superior mesenteric artery embolism in a cohort with a high prevalence of cardiogenic risk factors: a single-center retrospective cohort study
authorString: Yang J, Zhao J, Li G.
abstractText: Background Acute superior mesenteric artery embolism (ASMAE) is a rare, life-threatening systemic embolism associated with cardiogenic risk factors. We described its clinical features, management, and outcomes in a single-center cohort. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 28 patients with ASMAE treated between March 2023 and March 2026. Isolated mesenteric venous thrombosis, non-occlusive mesenteric ischemia, and superior mesenteric artery dissection were excluded. All patients underwent computed tomography angiography (CTA), and operative patients had surgical or pathological confirmation. Clinical, treatment, complication, discharge, and available post-discharge follow-up data were collected. Continuous variables are reported as mean ± standard deviation and categorical variables as counts and percentages. Results We included 17 men and 11 women (mean age, 71.04 ± 9.06 years). Atrial fibrillation was present in 22 patients and valvular heart disease in 12. The proximal, middle, and distal superior mesenteric artery was involved in 7, 12, and 9 patients, respectively; 9 had concurrent infarction and 11 had peritonitis. Four patients received conservative treatment and 24 entered an operative pathway. The mean operative duration was 172.04 ± 63.02 minutes. Operations included Fogarty embolectomy alone (12), embolectomy plus bowel resection (9), bowel resection alone (1), laparotomy alone (1), and AcoStream aspiration followed by open surgery (1). Intestinal ischemia occurred in 21 patients, transmural necrosis in 14, and bowel resection with anastomosis in 10. Eleven patients were discharged against medical advice; 1 survived and 10 died after discharge (post-discharge mortality, 35.7%). Seventeen patients improved before discharge, and 1 later recovered, yielding 18 patients with a favorable short-term outcome. Five of 14 operative patients with a favorable outcome were lost to follow-up; one had residual distal embolism at 1 month. Conclusions ASMAE in patients with cardiogenic risk factors was associated with a high burden of intestinal ischemia, bowel necrosis, and post-discharge death. An open revascularization-dominant strategy enabled assessment of bowel viability and resection of nonviable intestine. These findings are descriptive, not comparative; prospective studies with standardized criteria and complete follow-up are needed.

title: Beyond Cure: Post-Treatment Survival and Health Outcomes Among Pulmonary Tuberculosis Survivors in Rural India
authorString: Rai J, Rawther SCH, Kulal R.
abstractText: Background: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major public health challenge in India, particularly in rural areas. While successful treatment is marked by microbiological cure, many individuals continue to face long-term physical and emotional health complications. Globally and nationally, post-treatment outcomes are gaining attention due to their impact on quality of life, relapse risk, and mortality. Recognizing factors associated with survival and post-treatment health is essential for targeted follow-up and support. This study aimed to assess the post-treatment survival and health status of pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) patients and to identify factors influencing these outcomes. Methods: A retrospective descriptive design was used. The study was conducted among 200 pulmonary TB patients who had completed treatment at selected villages in Ramanagara district, Bangalore. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire covering socio-demographic details, treatment adherence, clinical variables, post-treatment survival, and health status including clinical, functional, and emotional domains. Descriptive and inferential statistics were used for analysis, including chi-square tests for associations. Results: Among the 200 patients, 96.5% were alive and 3.5% had died post-treatment. Most patients (90.7%) had optimum clinical health, 58% showed high functional ability, and 93.8% reported only mild emotional symptoms. Statistically significant associations were found between post-treatment survival and age, occupation, and income. Post-treatment health status was significantly influenced by ventilation, hypertension, smoking, and tobacco chewing. Clinical variables such as BMI and type of medication were not significantly associated with health outcomes. Conclusions : Post-treatment survival was high among pulmonary TB patients, but several continued to experience health limitations. Socio-demographic factors, comorbidities, and personal habits played a crucial role in determining long-term health outcomes. Emphasis on follow-up care, lifestyle modification, and supportive interventions is essential for improving the quality of life of TB survivors.

title: Predictors of In-Hospital Mortality among Hospitalized Adults with Diabetes Mellitus in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia: A Multicenter Prospective Cohort Study
authorString: Bahru YD, Berha AB, Ahmed A, Chelkeba L.
abstractText: Background Diabetes mellitus (DM) significantly increases the risk of adverse hospital outcomes; however, data on mortality predictors in sub-Saharan African hospital settings remain scarce. This study aimed to identify independent predictors of in-hospital mortality among DM patients admitted to three Ethiopian tertiary hospitals. Methods A multicenter prospective cohort study was conducted from July 2023 to February 2024, enrolling 398 DM adult patients. Baseline demographic, clinical and laboratory data were collected. Patients were followed from admission until discharge or death. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with the log-rank test estimated median survival times (MST). Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression was used to identify independent predictors of mortality, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Results Among 398 patients (55% male, median age 60 years [IQR: 50–70]), 82.9% had Type 2 DM and 93.7% had a known history of diabetes. Hypertension (61.3%) and heart failure (37.7%) were the most prevalent comorbidities. The overall in-hospital mortality rate was 7.5% (n = 30). Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed significantly shorter MST for patients with > 3 comorbidities (p = 0.002), acute hemorrhagic stroke (MST: 23 vs. 55 days, p = 0.002), sepsis (MST: 35 vs. 90 days, p = 0.001), and hospital-acquired urinary tract infection (UTI) (MST: 25 vs. 55 days, p = 0.015). After adjustment in the multivariable Cox model, five factors remained independently associated with increased mortality: >3 comorbidities (AHR = 5.50; 95% CI: 1.96–15.40; p = 0.001), community-acquired sepsis (AHR = 7.98; 95% CI: 2.44–26.14; p = 0.001), acute hemorrhagic stroke (AHR = 4.54; 95% CI: 1.07–19.24; p = 0.040), hospital-acquired UTI (AHR = 6.87; 95% CI: 1.63–29.02; p = 0.009), and failure to achieve target blood glucose levels (AHR = 3.63; 95% CI: 1.12–11.76; p = 0.032). Conclusion In-hospital mortality in Ethiopian diabetic patients is profoundly driven by acute severe infections, cerebrovascular events, high comorbidity burden, and poor glycemic control. Early risk stratification, aggressive infection management, and strict glycemic monitoring are essential to reduce the high mortality rate in this vulnerable population.

title: The role of comorbidities in the incidence and mortality of lung cancer: a large, nationwide retrospective study based on Hungarian datasets
authorString: Farkas A, Andrási K, Takács E, Temesi G, Belicza É.
abstractText: Introduction: The mortality and overall survival of lung cancer depend on various factors. In our study, we examined the prevalence and effect on mortality of comorbidities. Method Data records from Hungarian patients diagnosed with lung cancer between 2012 and 2020 were enrolled. We examined the occurrence of comorbidities and the Charlson comorbidity index prior to lung cancer diagnosis with a matched-pairs methodology. Multivariate logistic regression assessed short- and long-term mortality, while Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox regression analyzed survival probabilities. Results 42,207 patients were enrolled. The differences in the occurrences of diabetes, arrhythmia, and renal failure were not significant between case and control groups. Anemia was moderate, cardiological conditions were significantly more frequent in the case group. Charlson index showed a less favorable risk profile in the case group. Surgical patients had significantly lower crude mortality rate. The odds of mortality are significantly increased at the 0.1% level with another primary tumor appearance, anemia, cerebrovascular disease, heart failure, arrhythmia, COPD, or pneumonia. The odds of mortality are significantly lower for patients diagnosed with hypertension or asthma (p < 0.001). Operated patients have a lower Charlson comorbidity index and better hazard ratios. Higher Charlson comorbidity category is associated with higher hazard ratio for survival. Conclusion Our study demonstrates that while high Charlson Comorbidity Index scores, COPD, heart failure, cerebrovascular disease, arrhythmia, pneumonia, and anemia increase lung cancer mortality, surgery – and surprisingly, hypertension and asthma – are linked to significantly better survival. This phenomenon should be noted for screening, diagnostic methods, and treatment choice.

title: Blood Pressure Control and Variability Reduction with Clevidipine in Hypertensive Intracerebral Hemorrhage (CLEVER-ICH): A Prospective Observational Study
authorString: Hassett C, Ahrens C, Conroy G, Li Y, Lapin B, Moseley S, Lindsay J, Nagesh AB, Gomes J.
abstractText: Background Acute systolic hypertension after spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is associated with hematoma expansion and worse outcomes. Although rapid blood pressure lowering is recommended, the physiologic effects of clevidipine on high-frequency systolic blood pressure variability (BPV) in acute ICH remain incompletely characterized. Methods We conducted a single-center, prospective, open-label observational study of adults with spontaneous supratentorial ICH presenting within 12 hours of last known well who required continuous intravenous antihypertensive therapy. Clevidipine was initiated at 1 mg/hour and titrated to a target systolic blood pressure (SBP) of 130–160 mmHg. Beat-to-beat arterial SBP was recorded at 300 Hz after neurointensive care unit admission. Primary outcomes were descriptive measures of BPV before and after clevidipine initiation, including standard deviation, average real variability (ARV), and coefficient of variation (CV). Secondary outcomes included time to target SBP, time to control with stability, hematoma expansion, neurologic deterioration, hypotension exposure, and in-hospital mortality. Results Twenty patients were enrolled between March 2022 and February 2025. Mean age was 57.8 ± 15.4 years, 60% were female, and 70% were Black/African American. Median peak pre-enrollment SBP was 193.5 mmHg. Median time to achieve SBP 130–160 mmHg was 5.9 minutes (IQR 0.6–10.2), and median time to control with stability was 6.3 minutes (IQR 1.7–14.2). Patients remained within target SBP for a median 73.7% of infusion time. Relative hypotension (SBP < 130 mmHg) occurred during 9.6% of infusion time, whereas absolute hypotension (SBP < 90 mmHg) was rare (0.05%). Mean SBP decreased from 169.5 mmHg before infusion to 151.9 mmHg in the first hour and remained controlled through 12 hours. Standard deviation and ARV did not significantly change after clevidipine initiation, while CV increased modestly (7.1% vs 9.9%, p = 0.037). Hematoma expansion occurred in 30% and in-hospital mortality was 20%. Conclusions In acute spontaneous ICH, clevidipine provided rapid, sustained SBP control with minimal clinically significant hypotension and no clear increase in absolute short-term BPV. These findings support its feasibility and safety for intensive hyperacute blood pressure management.

title: Association Between Stroke Subtype and Outcomes of Edaravone Dexborneol: A Subgroup Analysis of the EXPAND (Effectiveness and Safety of Edaravone Dexborneol in Acute Ischemic Stroke) Study.
authorString: Ma G, Song Z, Hu J, Raynald, Firdaus M, Wang J, Qiu J, Shao Y, Xu J, Pan J, Zuo Y, Nguyen TN, Zhang Q, EXPAND investigators.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

The effectiveness of edaravone dexborneol among acute ischemic stroke subtypes remains unclear. We evaluated its association with clinical outcomes by stroke subtype.

Methods

This secondary analysis of the prospective EXPAND (Effectiveness and Safety of Edaravone Dexborneol in Acute Ischemic Stroke) study included patients with acute ischemic stroke treated at 72 Chinese stroke centers from December 2022 to October 2023. Patients were classified as having large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) or non-LAA stroke and grouped by edaravone dexborneol use. Primary outcomes were 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores of 0 or 1 and 0 to 2 and ordinal mRS shift. Safety outcomes were 90-day mortality, intracranial hemorrhage, and in-hospital adverse events.

Results

Among 4401 patients, 1061 (24.1%) had LAA and 3340 (75.9%) had non-LAA stroke; the median age was 65 years, and 66.8% were men. Edaravone dexborneol was associated with improved 90-day functional outcomes in the non-LAA group, including higher odds of achieving mRS 0 or 1 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.25 [95% CI, 1.06-1.47]), mRS 0 to 2 (aOR, 1.40 [95% CI, 1.15-1.71]), and a favorable mRS shift (aOR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.12-1.46]; all P<0.05). No significant functional benefit was observed in the LAA group of mRS 0 or 1 (aOR, 0.91; P=0.50), mRS 0 to 2 (aOR, 0.88; P=0.43), or mRS shift (aOR, 0.92; P=0.50). Significant interactions were observed between edaravone dexborneol and stroke subtype (P for interaction=0.03 for mRS 0 or 1, P=0.005 for mRS 0 to 2, and P=0.009 for favorable mRS shift). Safety outcomes were comparable between treatment groups.

Conclusions

Edaravone dexborneol was associated with improved 90-day functional outcomes in non-LAA but not LAA stroke.

title: Clinical Observation of Precision Haemodynamic Management Guided by Pulse Index Continuous Cardiac Output in Patients with Septic Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Yuan B, Cao Y, Cao Y, Chang X, La H, Shao J, Ma X, Liu P.
abstractText: ObjectiveThis study aimed to investigate the value of pulse index continuous cardiac output (PICCO) monitoring in assessing the relationship between cardiac function, haemodynamic evolution and prognosis in patients with septic cardiomyopathy (SCM).MethodsSixty patients with SCM were categorised into normal (left ventricular ejection fraction [LVEF] ≥ 50%, n = 21) and reduced (LVEF < 50%, n = 39) cardiac function groups. Haemodynamic parameters (cardiac index [CI], global end-diastolic volume index [GEDVI], systemic vascular resistance index [SVRI], extravascular lung water index and pulmonary vascular permeability index) were dynamically monitored via PICCO at 0, 6, 12, 24, 48 and 72 h. The 21-day mortality was recorded.ResultsThe reduced group was significantly older (62.4 ± 11.9 vs 36.4 ± 8.7 years, P < .001) with higher Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II scores (P = .028) than the normal group. Their CI remained significantly lower than that of the normal group at all time points, reaching a nadir at 24 h (2.46 ± 0.62 vs 3.65 ± 1.03 L/min·m2, P < .001). Unlike the normal group, the reduced group showed a significant GEDVI rebound at 24 h (P ≤ .05). No significant difference in SVRI was found between groups (P > .05). The 28-day cumulative mortality was 38.5% in the reduced group versus 19.0% in the normal group (P = .211).ConclusionPulse index continuous cardiac output monitoring effectively identifies haemodynamic differences across SCM cardiac functions. Patients with reduced LVEF exhibit severe cardiac depression and a 24-h decompensation window. Although mortality differences were not statistically significant in this cohort, PICCO provides vital quantifiable targets for individualised management.

title: Cytokine Signatures of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Myocarditis and the Modifying Role of Clonal Hematopoiesis: A Machine-Learning and Multi-Omics Study
authorString: Manchanda N, Chehayeb RJ, Hong D, Jeyashanmugaraja A, Singh J, Cross JL, Vijayram A, Martinez CM, Jayakrishnan R, Christofides A, Lin D, Im Y, VanOudenhove J, Biancon G, Ibrahim E, Ardasheva A, Lin EYS, Levine R, Cheng E, Halene S, Hwa J, Smith N, Villani C, Zhu H, Jha A, Kwan JM.
abstractText:
Background:

Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) myocarditis affects up to 2% of patients on ICI and has up to a 50% mortality. Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) is a risk factor for ICI myocarditis.

Objectives:

To leverage a multi-omics approach to evaluate cytokines associated with ICI myocarditis, immunosuppression resistance, CHIP in ICI myocarditis and implicated pathways and cell type contributions. Methods 236 cardio-oncology patients were enrolled, including 88 who were on ICI. Cytokine profiling from patients on ICI were sampled and analyzed using machine learning and explainable artificial intelligence. Single-cell multi-omics of peripheral blood from Yale (n=19), Stanford (n=25), and MGH (n=63) evaluated cell-type contributions of cytokines and implicated pathways. Validation of Yale proteomic analyses was done using the Stanford CYTOF dataset. Results Top features associated with ICI myocarditis included IL13, CXCL10, PDGFA, CCL13, CCL17 and KITlg. Top KEGG pathways associated with ICI myocarditis and immunosuppression resistant ICI myocarditis included JAK STAT signaling, IL17 signaling and lipid/atherosclerosis pathways. At the single-cell level, the consensus signals distinguishing myocarditis from non-myocarditis across cohorts was predominantly driven by module-level JAK STAT, T cell, and Toll like receptor activation. Similar transcription gene programs were activated in CHIP carriers including modules implicated in the pro-inflammatory immune response, such as NF kappa B, IL17, MAPK, and TNF pathways within CHIP cells spanning lymphoid (cytotoxic CD8+ NKT, and natural killer cells) and myeloid lineages. Conclusions Across cohorts, JAK STAT signaling emerges as a convergent and potentially actionable axis in ICI myocarditis that is further amplified in CHIP carriers, supporting cytokine-guided risk stratification and JAK STAT directed immunosuppression as testable strategies.

title: Hybrid and endovascular repair of aberrant subclavian artery aneurysms and Kommerell diverticulum: single-center experience and long-term outcomes.
authorString: Bozzani A, Visciglia E, Destefanis Gallo E, Quaretti P, Cionfoli N, Arbustini E, Rossini R, Salzillo I, Arici V.
abstractText:
Background

Aberrant subclavian artery (ASA) represents the most frequent congenital anomaly of the aortic arch and may occasionally develop aneurysmal dilation (aASA) at risk of dissection or rupture. Early diagnosis and tailored management are therefore crucial. We report our long-term single-center experience with endovascular and hybrid repair of aASA and Kommerell's diverticulum (KD).

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed all consecutive patients treated for aASA between January 2010 and June 2024 at our tertiary referral center. Primary endpoints were primary technical success, perioperative and late mortality, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Secondary endpoints included symptom evolution, reinterventions, and complications.

Results

Ten patients (5 females, 50%; mean age 62±19 years, range 16-80) were included. Seven (70%) presented with right ASA, and two (20%) with right aortic arch and left ASA. Seven patients (70%) were symptomatic; 43% had acute type B aortic dissection, 14% type A, and 28% descending thoracic aortic aneurysm. Four patients (40%) underwent total endovascular repair, and four (40%) hybrid procedures. Primary technical success was achieved in all cases, with no intraoperative deaths. Perioperative mortality was 10% and late mortality 30%. Complications included type II endoleak, access-site hematoma or infection, and transient upper-limb ischemia. No MACE occurred during the study period.

Conclusions

Hybrid and endovascular approaches appear to represent safe and effective alternatives to open repair for complex aASA anatomy when performed in experienced referral centers. Given the limited cohort size, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive and hypothesis-generating.

title: Prognostic Impact of Post-Contrast Acute Kidney Injury in Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease Undergoing Endovascular Aortic Repair.
authorString: Akabane K, Nakamura K, Kuroda Y, Mizumoto M, Hirooka S, Ochiai T, Arai S, Uchida T.

journal.title: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists

abstractText:
Background

Post-contrast acute kidney injury (PC-AKI) has been regarded as a serious complication after contrast administration, particularly in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). However, the prognostic significance of PC-AKI following endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) remains controversial due to heterogeneity in previous study populations. This study evaluated the association between PC-AKI and longitudinal changes in postoperative renal function and mortality in a well-defined CKD cohort undergoing EVAR.

Methods

We conducted a single-center retrospective study of patients with CKD undergoing elective, primary, and non-complex infrarenal EVAR. Patients were classified according to the presence or absence of PC-AKI.
