Longitudinal changes in serum creatinine after EVAR, dialysis initiation, all-cause mortality, and the association between contrast volume and PC-AKI were evaluated.

Results

Among 479 EVAR procedures, 164 patients with CKD were included, of whom 17 (10.4%) developed PC-AKI. The linear mixed-effects model showed a significant group-by-time interaction (P < .001). Serum creatinine remained significantly higher in the PC-AKI group than in the non-PC-AKI group at all postoperative time points. However, in the PC-AKI group, model-adjusted mean serum creatinine decreased significantly from 1.75 mg/dL in the postoperative period to 1.46 mg/dL at 12 months with an estimated change of -0.29 mg/dL (95% CI, -0.50 to -0.09; P = .003). No significant differences were observed in dialysis initiation (5.9% vs 0.7%; P = .197) or all-cause mortality (29.4% vs 23.8%; P = .565). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed no significant difference in overall survival between the groups (log-rank P = .246). In the multivariable analysis, contrast volume was not independently associated with PC-AKI (odds ratio [OR], 1.00; 95% CI, 0.98-1.01; P = .845), whereas lower preoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate remained significantly associated with PC-AKI (OR, 1.06 per 1 mL/min/1.73 m2 decrease; 95% CI, 1.01-1.12; P = .018).

Conclusion

In this study, PC-AKI may not necessarily be associated with adverse subsequent renal or survival outcomes. In addition, underlying renal vulnerability may be more closely associated with the development of PC-AKI than contrast volume alone. While PC-AKI should not be disregarded, judicious contrast use to ensure appropriate assessment may be reasonable even in patients with CKD.Clinical ImpactPost-contrast acute kidney injury (PC-AKI) occurred in approximately 10% of patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) undergoing elective, primary, non-complex infrarenal endovascular aortic repair (EVAR). Although serum creatinine remained higher in patients with PC-AKI at all postoperative time points, it decreased significantly from the postoperative period to 12 months. No significant differences were observed in dialysis initiation or overall survival between the groups. In addition, contrast volume was not independently associated with PC-AKI, whereas lower preoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate was. These findings suggest that contrast use should not be excessively restricted solely because of concerns regarding PC-AKI, and that judicious contrast use to ensure appropriate assessment may be reasonable even in patients with CKD.

title: Routine adjunctive porcine fibrin sealant sac embolization during emergency endovascular repair for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm: a before-and-after cohort study
authorString: Zheng L, Lu Z, Li P, Li X, Zhao Y, Zhang L.
abstractText: Background Routine adjunctive sac embolization extends aneurysm sac management beyond endograft exclusion during emergency endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA). We evaluated implementation of this strategy and 30-day outcomes. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 31 consecutive patients with rAAA who commenced an emergency EVAR strategy. The historical control group included 14 patients treated between 2019 and 2022; between January 2023 and June 2026, 17 patients underwent routine adjunctive porcine fibrin sealant (PFS) sac embolization. The primary outcome was 30-day postoperative all-cause mortality. We calculated the unadjusted risk difference and its 95% confidence interval. Results All 17 patients treated with PFS completed the planned embolization. Several baseline features were less favorable in the PFS era, although Edinburgh score distributions were similar between eras. Thirty-day mortality was 3/17 (17.6%) in the PFS era and 3/14 (21.4%) in the historical era. The unadjusted risk difference was − 3.8 percentage points (95% confidence interval: -32.3 to 23.4). No nontarget embolization was recorded. Two additional rupture-related deaths occurred in the PFS era beyond 30 days. Conclusions Routine adjunctive PFS sac embolization was feasible within this center's emergency EVAR workflow. This consecutive rAAA cohort provides a clinical basis for prospective controlled evaluation of the strategy and its perioperative outcomes.

title: Institutional Variation in Electroencephalography Utilization in Neonates With Complex Congenital Heart Disease Across the United States and Its Association With Outcomes.
authorString: Aly S, Elsisy MF, Qattea I, Newburger JW, Aly HZ.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Neonates with complex congenital heart disease are at increased risk for perioperative brain injury and seizures. Electroencephalography (EEG) detects clinical and subclinical seizures, but national utilization patterns remain poorly characterized.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Pediatric Health Information System (2016-2025) of neonates ≤28 days with dextro-transposition of the great arteries or single-ventricle physiology undergoing surgical repair or palliation. Mixed-effects logistic regression with hospital as a random effect identified predictors of EEG utilization.

Results

Among 13 202 neonates, 1654 (12.5%) underwent EEG monitoring. EEG monitoring was performed in only 10.8% of neonates with dextro-transposition of the great arteries, 16% of those with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, and 13% of those with non- hypoplastic left heart syndrome single-ventricle lesions. EEG utilization increased from ~6% in 2016 to >14% in 2025, while seizure detection among EEG-monitored patients increased from 13% to ~26% (both P-trend<0.01). Utilization varied substantially across hospitals (0% to >40%), persisting after adjustment for surgical volume. EEG-monitored neonates had higher seizure detection (21.8% versus 5.2%), longer length of stay (33 versus 24 days), and higher hospitalization costs ($344 719 versus $174 865; all P<0.01). In multivariable analysis, EEG utilization was independently associated with seizures (OR ~4), dextro-transposition of the great arteries, and hypoplastic left heart syndrome, but not with cardiac arrest, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, or hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy.

Conclusions

EEG utilization in neonates with complex congenital heart disease is increasing but remains low and highly variable across US centers. The association of EEG use with higher mortality and costs may reflect confounding by indication or illness severity. Standardized protocols are needed to optimize neurologic monitoring and improve long-term outcomes.

title: Association of maternal gestational exposures and child/family characteristics with non-PFO congenital heart disease in children: a multicenter retrospective case-control study
authorString: Wang H, Li W, Alifu A, Wu S, Lin S, He J, Lin S, Chen R.
abstractText: Background Congenital heart disease (CHD) is a major cause of infant morbidity and mortality. Previous studies often combined patent foramen ovale (PFO) with structural cardiac malformations, potentially increasing phenotypic heterogeneity. Objectives To identify maternal gestational exposures and child/family characteristics associated with non-PFO CHD and develop a preliminary prediction model. Methods This multicenter retrospective case-control study included 208 children from Hainan Province: 130 with non-PFO CHD and 78 with PFO. Fifty-five candidate variables were assessed. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for feature selection, followed by five machine learning models. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was used to interpret feature importance, and a nomogram was constructed. Results LASSO selected eight features, of which seven had nonzero global SHAP importance: child age in months, maternal protein intake frequency during pregnancy, history of CHD in other offspring, folic acid supplementation, frequency of family conflicts during pregnancy, maternal preconception smoking, and first-trimester hazardous substance exposure. Linear discriminant analysis (LDA) showed the best test-set performance, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.702 and a Brier score of 0.232. The nomogram achieved an AUC of 0.732, and decision curve analysis indicated potential net benefit across the evaluated threshold range. Conclusions Candidate predictors associated with non-PFO CHD were identified, and an internally evaluated nomogram was developed for preliminary risk stratification. External validation is required before clinical use.

title: Unraveling Severe Myocardial Dysfunction in Streptococcal Toxic Shock Syndrome: Beyond Septic Shock.
authorString: Dod R, Drury JK, Nguyen C, Santos J, Smallfield M, Li P.
abstractText:
Background

Group A Streptococcus is a clinically important yet underrecognized cause of inflammatory myocardial dysfunction, capable of triggering shock through toxin-mediated injury and inflammation.

Case summary

A 19-year-old woman presented with progressive fatigue, severe hypotension, and a purpuric chest rash. Laboratory investigation showed rising troponin, leukocytosis, and lactic acidosis. Echocardiography and right heart catheterization revealed significant biventricular dysfunction. She developed shock requiring mechanical circulatory support with an Impella CP and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. Corticosteroids and intravenous immunoglobulin were initiated empirically for presumed inflammatory myocarditis. Chest wall biopsy grew Group A Streptococcus, supporting the diagnosis of streptococcal toxic shock syndrome (STSS). Ultimately, she recovered cardiac function with mechanical circulatory support and targeted antimicrobial therapy.

Discussion

This case highlights severe, reversible myocardial dysfunction because of STSS.

Take-home message

STSS can precipitate severe, reversible myocardial dysfunction representing a mixed septic-cardiogenic phenotype that may mimic fulminant myocarditis.

title: Transcatheter Mitral Valve-in-Valve Implantation Despite Left Atrial Appendage Thrombosis: A Challenging Therapeutic Strategy.
authorString: Pecci A, Ravani M, Al Jabri A, Trianni GR, De Caterina AR, Berti S.
abstractText:
Background

Transcatheter mitral valve-in-valve (ViV) implantation is an alternative to redo surgery in high-risk patients with degenerated mitral bioprostheses.

Case summary

An elderly woman presented with recurrent acute pulmonary edema due to severe stenosis of a degenerated mitral bioprosthesis. Redo surgery was considered prohibitive (EuroSCORE II: 15%). Transesophageal echocardiography revealed persistent left atrial appendage (LAA) thrombosis despite appropriate anticoagulation, increasing embolic risk. Given severe symptoms and lack of viable alternatives, transseptal mitral ViV implantation was successfully performed using the FLOWer cerebral embolic protection device, without neurological complications and with excellent hemodynamic results.

Discussion

LAA thrombosis is generally considered a relative contraindication to transseptal mitral interventions because of thromboembolic risk. This case highlights the potential role of cerebral embolic protection and individualized heart team decision-making in highly selected patients.

Take-home message

Mitral ViV implantation with cerebral embolic protection may be feasible in selected patients with LAA thrombosis and prohibitive surgical risk.

title: A Validated Artificial Intelligence Model Versus Urinary Supersaturation Alone for Predicting Kidney Stone Composition.
authorString: Lantz EB, Vanderboom P, Koo K, Jannetto PJ, Lieske JC, Meeusen J, Day PL.
abstractText:
Objective

To develop and validate an artificial intelligence (AI) model that can identify kidney stone composition more accurately than the EQUIL2 urine supersaturation (SS) algorithm.

Patients and methods

Patients with both a 24-hour urine SS panel and a kidney stone composition analysis conducted within 90 days of each other between September 24, 2015, and March 15, 2024, were identified (n=13,000 unique patients). Kidney stones were classified as either majority calcium oxalate (CaOx), majority calcium phosphate (CaP), uric acid, or other. A model was developed to predict kidney stone classification using demographic characteristics plus urinary SS panel results. This model was subsequently validated on a held-out data set of paired measurements collected between March 16, 2024, and March 15, 2025 (n=1653). The urinary SS for CaOx, hydroxyapatite (CaP), brushite (CaP), and uric acid were calculated using EQUIL2 according to routine clinical practice and expressed using the delta Gibbs free energy scale.

Results

The AI model was significantly more accurate in the validation data set for identifying stone composition compared with SS alone (accuracy, 0.73 vs 0.33; P<.01). Additionally, the model outperformed SS alone in the validation data set for correctly identifying kidney stone composition in all analyses stratified into clinically relevant subgroups by age and sex.

Conclusion

In all kidney stone categories and within various subgroups, the AI model outperformed the EQUIL2-calculated SS as well as previously published AI models in the correct prediction of CaOx, CaP, and uric acid kidney stones when using the 24-hour urine SS panel.

title: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion and Percutaneous Coumadin Ridge Mass Exclusion: Two Targets, One Device.
authorString: Ottersbach A, Bisharat A, Sherev D, Azimi NA.
abstractText:
Background

Mobile cardiac masses on the coumadin ridge are rare and carry significant embolic risk, compounded by concurrent atrial fibrillation. Surgical excision may be prohibitive in patients with high bleeding risk.

Case summary

A 70-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, a HAS-BLED score of 4, and aversion to anticoagulation was referred for left atrial appendage (LAA) closure. Imaging revealed an incidental 0.56-cm mobile coumadin ridge mass consistent with papillary fibroelastoma. The Amplatzer Amulet was selected for its larger disc geometry to simultaneously occlude the LAA and exclude the mass, with follow-up confirming complete mass exclusion and stability at over 2 years.

Discussion

This is to our knowledge the first reported case of intentional simultaneous LAA occlusion and percutaneous mass exclusion, demonstrating a novel use of device geometry to manage dual embolic risk.

Take-home message

Concurrent LAA and coumadin ridge mass risk can be addressed in a single procedure through deliberate device selection using the Amulet's larger disc.

title: Transinnominate Microaxial Flow Pump Placement in a Patient With Failing Fontan Circulation as Bridge to Transplantation.
authorString: Okamura K, Trezzi M, Kavarana M, Felmly LM.
abstractText:
Background

The Impella 5.5 is a temporary microaxial ventricular assist device indicated to unload the left ventricle and support refractory heart failure. Small peripheral arteries and atypical right ventricular anatomy may preclude its use in patients with Fontan circulation.

Case summary

We report a 23-year-old man with hypoplastic left heart syndrome palliated to Fontan with refractory heart failure. Impella 5.5 was placed via the innominate artery, providing 4.5 L/min support for 13 days until heart transplantation; he was discharged in good condition.

Discussion

Transinnominate approach enables effective bridge to transplantation despite small peripheral vessels.

Novelty

This is the first reported case of Impella 5.5 as a bridge to transplant placed via transinnominate artery in an adult with failing Fontan circulation and a systemic right ventricle.

Take-home message

Impella 5.5 via transinnominate access is feasible in select patients with Fontan circulation and small peripheral vessels and serves as an effective bridge to transplantation.

title: Leadless Pacing Dyssynchrony and Diastolic Mitral Regurgitation Rescued by Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing.
authorString: Nakamura Y, Oda A, Miyazaki H, Arai S, Asano T, Shinke T.
abstractText:
Background

Dual-chamber leadless pacing depends on beat-to-beat implant-to-implant communication; heart failure-related geometric changes may expose limited communication reserve.

Case summary

A 92-year-old woman with complete atrioventricular block developed heart failure 9 months after dual-chamber leadless pacemaker implantation, with reduced atrial-to-ventricular (A-to-V) throughput, atrioventricular dissociation, ventricular functional and diastolic mitral regurgitation, and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction. Decongestion was accompanied by shortening of the projected interdevice distance, improvement in A-to-V throughput and atrioventricular synchrony, and disappearance of diastolic mitral regurgitation. Heart failure recurred despite preserved throughput and continued medical therapy. Upgrade to a transvenous dual-chamber pacemaker with left bundle branch area pacing narrowed the QRS and improved left ventricular function and mitral regurgitation.

Discussion

Pacing-induced cardiomyopathy appeared to be the dominant substrate, with dynamic A-to-V limitation as a reversible aggravating factor. Left bundle branch area pacing addressed both atrioventricular and ventricular dyssynchrony.

title: Aortic Dissection After Stage 1 Palliation.
authorString: Pook CN, Ganigara M, Javois AJ, Wong JH, Do NL, Moehlmann ML.
abstractText:
Background

Pediatric aortic dissection (AD) is rare and usually associated with hypertension or aortopathies. In this case, we present a Stanford type B dissection in an asymptomatic patient with single ventricle heart disease without known genetic aortopathy following stage 1 palliation.

Case summary

Dissection was diagnosed on routine catheterization and confirmed on computed tomography angiography. There was no progression, so no surgical intervention was pursued. He underwent stage 2 palliation at age 6 months and continues to do well.

Discussion

AD is rare in pediatrics, especially infants without aortopathy. A single iatrogenic case report after hybrid palliation has been described. Our patient had at least 2 risk factors, aortic coarctation and intermittently elevated blood pressure, that could have predisposed him to dissection.

Take-home messages

AD is rarely seen following the Norwood operation. Stanford type B AD can be safely medically managed in pediatric patients as in the adult guidelines.

title: Glomerular microangiopathy can be associated with nephrotic proteinuria due to both segmental effacement of foot processes and damage to the glomerular endothelial barrier.
authorString: Schukow CP, Holmes CJ, Li W, Kanaan HD, Zhang PL.
abstractText: Glomerular microangiopathy (GMA)-caused by etiologies including VEGF inhibition, thrombotic microangiopathy, or malignant hypertension-is frequently linked to nephrotic-range proteinuria. However, the mechanisms of severe proteinuria following glomerular filtration barrier injury remain unclear. We examined how podocyte and glomerular endothelial injury relate to significant proteinuria in GMA. Thirty-seven kidney biopsies were studied, including 10 negative controls (Group 1), 11 GMA cases associated with VEGF inhibition (Group 2), and 16 GMA cases caused by other etiologies (Group 3). Electron microscopy was used to quantify foot process effacement and assess glomerular endothelial injury. To further evaluate endothelial barrier dysfunction, Oil Red O (ORO) staining for lipoprotein deposition and colloidal iron staining for negatively charged proteoglycans were performed. Correlations between ultrastructural changes and proteinuria were analyzed statistically. Nephrotic-range proteinuria was observed in 82% (9/11) of Group 2 and 56% (9/16) of Group 3 cases. In both groups, the severity of proteinuria was significantly associated with the extent of foot process effacement, endothelial edema and detachment, and GBM double-contour formation. ORO staining demonstrated subendothelial lipoprotein accumulation along the GBM in GMA cases but not in controls, consistent with increased glomerular endothelial permeability. In addition, colloidal iron staining was markedly reduced along the GBM in GMA, indicating impaired charge-selective properties of the glomerular filtration barrier. Significant proteinuria in GMA is associated with concurrent podocyte and glomerular endothelial cell injury. Ultrastructural findings, subendothelial lipoprotein accumulation, and reduced GBM proteoglycan staining indicate that endothelial barrier dysfunction, alongside podocyte injury, contributes critically to nephrotic-range proteinuria in GMA.

title: PEth as a marker of alcohol consumption in relation to arterial cardiovascular risk factors.
authorString: Sundström A, Johansson M, Vikström S, Andersson J, Lind MM.

journal.title: Scandinavian journal of primary health care

abstractText:
Background

Alcohol has well-known detrimental effects on health. Phosphatidyl ethanol 16:0/18:1 (PEth) is a highly sensitive biomarker of alcohol consumption used in primary healthcare. The relationship between PEth concentrations and cardiovascular risk factors remains unclear. Our hypothesis was that high PEth concentrations would be associated with an unfavourable cardiovascular risk factor profile. This study aimed to investigate the associations between PEth concentrations and arterial cardiovascular risk factors.

Methods

This cross-sectional study was based on data from the Västerbotten Intervention Programme and included 2820 individuals. Health examinations were conducted, including questionnaires collecting data on cardiovascular risk factors. PEth concentrations were analysed in packed erythrocytes from blood samples collected between 1985 and 2014 and stored at -80 °C until analysis. Participants were categorised into four groups. Logistic regression analysis was used to calculate odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the association between PEth concentrations and arterial cardiovascular risk factors.

Results

The median age of participants was 50.2 years, and the median BMI was 25.9. High PEth concentrations (>0.30 μmol/L) were observed in 8.9% of participants and were associated with hypertension (OR 1.58 [95% CI 1.14-2.18]), diabetes (OR 1.89 [95% CI 1.08-3.28]), male sex (OR 2.58 [95% CI 1.90-3.50]), ever smoking (OR 5.31 [95% CI 3.75-7.52]) and lower education level (OR 2.06 [95% CI 1.32-3.22]) compared with PEth <0.01 μmol/L.

Conclusions

High PEth concentrations were associated with established risk factors for arterial cardiovascular disease. These findings should encourage a broader clinical focus when managing patients with elevated PEth concentrations.

title: Acute Kidney Injury Disrupts Cardiac Remodeling via SerpinA3N.
authorString: Pramod GS, Qu S, Zeleznova NN, Li M, Soto NH, Wang L, Hall N, Ni R, Zhao B, Gibbons J, Hassan Q, Banerjee NS, Halade GV, Lozonschi L, Lai E, Williams K, Liu R.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Cardiorenal syndrome type 3 describes cardiac injury triggered by acute kidney injury (AKI). AKI caused by ischemia reperfusion injury represents a model for kidney injury during kidney transplant. It is well known that kidney transplant recipients are at increased risk to develop cardiac fibrosis; however, the molecular mechanisms linking renal injury to myocardial remodeling or cardiac fibrosis remain unclear.

Methods

Using a C57BL/6J mouse model of ischemia reperfusion injury-AKI, we combined proteomics and RNA seqencing transcriptomics to define early cardiac responses. We validated the proteomics and RNA sequencing data with quantitative polymerase chain reaction, ELISA, cytokine array, and western blotting for profibrotic and injury markers. We assessed SerpinA3N function using a granzyme B activity assay kit and XAV939, an inhibitor of SerpinA3N. Ingenuity pathway analysis further confirmed serine protease activity inhibition and increased expression of cardiac fibrosis-related genes after AKI.

Results

Successful establishment of renal ischemia reperfusion injury causing AKI, followed by significant induction of cardiac injury. AKI significantly upregulated SerpinA3N in the heart while suppressing serine protease (granzyme B) activity. Concomitantly, AKI hearts displayed elevated profibrotic genes (FN1, COL1A1, TGF-β1), mitochondrial dysfunction, and heightened inflammatory signaling. In vitro, inhibition of SerpinA3N with XAV939 restored granzyme B activity, confirming direct suppression by SerpinA3N.

Conclusions

We conclude that SerpinA3N serves as a key mediator of cardiorenal syndrome type 3 pathogenesis, by inhibiting granzyme B, which promotes profibrotic remodeling in the heart following AKI. Targeting SerpinA3N could be a potential therapeutic approach that restores balanced extracellular matrix turnover and mitigates cardiac fibrosis.

title: Poorly Controlled Hypertension Alters Coronary Microvascular Contractile Response to Endothelin-1 Before and After Cardiac Surgery.
authorString: Banerjee D, Sabe SA, Tran CT, Cioffi WG, Choudhary G, Raker C, Sodha NR, Ehsan A, Feng J, Sellke FW.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Patients with chronic hypertension have worse outcomes following on-pump (cardioplegia and cardiopulmonary bypass [CP/CPB]) cardiac surgery. Altered vasomotor function of the coronary microvasculature to ET-1 (endothelin-1) and other agonists may underlie these differences.

Methods

Heart samples were collected from 85 patients undergoing CP/CPB enrolled in this observational study. Ex vivo coronary microvascular responses to ET-1, adenosine diphosphate, and sodium nitroprusside were assessed using video microscopy. Immunoblotting, immunohistochemistry, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and multiomics approaches were also used.

Results

Coronary microvascular contractile response to ET-1 in patients with uncontrolled hypertension was increased compared with the other 2 cohorts pre- and post-CP/CPB (P<0.05 across ET-1 10-10 to 10-7 mmol/L). Adenosine diphosphate-induced coronary microvascular vasodilation was conversely decreased (P<0.05 for adenosine diphosphate 10-5 and 10-4 mmol/L). Post-CP/CPB microvascular responses to ET-1 and adenosine diphosphate were blunted overall (P<0.05). Antagonism of pro-vasoconstrictive endothelinA receptor diminished contractile response (P<0.05). Transcriptomics and proteomics showed wide regulation of pro-vasoconstrictive pathways. Regression showed that hypertension status and cardiac mass reliably approximated ET-1-induced coronary microvascular contraction (R2 0.95 pre-CP/CPB, R2 0.86 post-CP/CPB), which, in turn, estimated change in ejection fraction pre- and post-CP/CPB (P<0.05). Patients with uncontrolled hypertension had -11% change in EF when compared with the other 2 groups pooled (P<0.05).

Conclusions

Altered coronary microvascular vasomotor function in patients with uncontrolled hypertension may jeopardize myocardial perfusion. Hypertension status and cardiac mass may be used to prognosticate this physiology, which, in turn, estimates change in ejection fraction postoperatively. Perioperative endothelin receptor blockers may benefit patients with uncontrolled hypertension and thus warrant further investigation.

title: Greenspace Exposure Reduces the Risk of Hypertension: A Large Prospective Cohort Study in Northwestern China.
authorString: He YZ, Zhang YS, Xu AM, Jiang JC, Chen W, Yang YZ, Qiu HL, Wang L, Yang BY, Zou XG, Fan SJ.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

The effects of greenspace on hypertension remain unconfirmed. This study aimed to validate this by performing a large prospective cohort study in China.

Methods

PEAHEN-China (Prospective Environment and Health Epidemiological Study in Northwestern China) recruited 5 484 119 adults in 2017 and followed them to 2021. Blood pressure levels and hypertension were measured and defined using recommended standards. Greenspace exposure was estimated using the normalized difference vegetation index and enhanced vegetation index. Cox regression models and generalized estimating equation models were used to assess the associations of greenspace with hypertension incidence and blood pressure levels, respectively. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses were also performed.

Results

During a median 3.21-year follow-up, 1 290 003 new hypertension cases occurred. Living in greener areas was significantly associated with a lower risk of hypertension and lower blood pressure levels. For example, in the adjusted models, compared with the first quartile of normalized difference vegetation index and enhanced vegetation index within a 500-m buffer, the hazard ratios of incident hypertension in the fourth quartile of the 2 metrics were 0.871 (95% CI, 0.861-0.881) and 0.896 (95% CI, 0.885-0.906). In addition, stronger associations of greenspace exposure with hypertension risk and blood pressure levels were observed in younger, male, rural, and less educated participants than their counterparts.

Conclusions

Our study indicates that neighborhood greenspace may reduce residents' odds of having hypertension, offering robust evidence for developing policies and strategies to mitigate the burden of hypertension.

title: Risk Stratification and Outcomes of Right Atrial Phasic Function in Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy: A Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Study.
authorString: Xu W, Ma X, Song Y, Dong Z, Yang S, Aisikaier K, Tang Y, Sa F, Jia X, Zhou P, Liu Y, Chen X, Chen X, Yang K, Zhao S.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Advanced arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy is associated with a high risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias (MVA) and end-stage heart failure (HF). However, the prognostic role of right atrial (RA) mechanics, as quantified by cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR), remains largely unexplored.

Methods

Consecutive patients with arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy undergoing CMR between 2014 and 2021 were retrospectively included. Demographics, clinical history, and strain parameters were collected. The primary clinical end points were end-stage HF and MVA.

Results

A total of 316 patients (mean age 38±15 years; 66.1% men) were included. Over a median follow-up of 5.3 years, 49 developed end-stage HF and 103 experienced MVA outcomes. Multivariable Cox and Fine-Gray models showed that impaired RA reservoir strain was an independent predictor of end-stage HF (hazard ratio [HR] 0.92, 95% CI 0.89-0.96, P<0.001) and MVA outcomes (subdistribution hazard ratio (sHR) 0.98, 95% CI 0.96-0.99, P=0.025), with added prognostic value beyond clinical and imaging variables, improving the C-statistic to 0.84 and 0.70, respectively. Kaplan-Meier survival curves indicated that RA reservoir strain <18.6% was associated with higher end-stage HF risk, consistent across subgroups regardless of left ventricular involvement (both log-rank P<0.05). The association between RA reservoir strain <23.0% and MVA was significant in the overall cohort (P<0.001) and in patients without left ventricular involvement (P=0.002), but not in those with left ventricular involvement (P=0.08).

Conclusions

Lower cardiac magnetic resonance-derived RA reservoir strain was independently associated with end-stage HF and MVA in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy and provided incremental prognostic value beyond conventional risk markers. These findings support RA mechanics as a potential complementary component of multichamber CMR risk assessment, pending external validation.

title: Diuretic Response in Acute Heart Failure: Prediction vs Direct Measurement.
authorString: Ivey-Miranda J, Cox Z, Udelson JE, Nunez J, Fudim M, Damman K, Biegus J, Javaheri A, Gottlieb RL, Petrie MC, Butler J, Rao VS, Collins S, Testani J.
abstractText:
Background

Limited data are available informing the variability and ability to predict diuretic response (DR) longitudinally during decongestion in acute heart failure (AHF).

Methods

The FASTR pilot trial compared the Reprieve System (n=52) to optimal diuretic therapy control (ODT) (n=44). The ability to longitudinally predict DR, quantified as urine output over the 72-hour intervention, was evaluated in the overall population using baseline characteristics. In the Reprieve arm, directly measured DR during the initial dose finding algorithm was also used to predict longitudinal DR.

Results

Baseline characteristics predicted only 24.7% (p<0.001) of the variance in DR over the course of IV diuretic therapy. As the duration of diuretic therapy increased, DR prediction worsened with no relationship to DR after 18 hours (p≥0.097). Directly measured DR strongly predicted subsequent urine output early (e.g., predicting 84.5% in the variance of the subsequent hour DR, p<0.001). However, this also decreased over time with modest correlation with DR at 24 hours (variance 12.7%; p=0.008) and no correlation after 48 hours (p=0.79). In the Reprieve group, serial DR measurement and diuretic titration occurred in 89% of patients eligible for further diuretic titration resulting in stable therapeutic DR over the study period despite the changes in DR over time.

Conclusions

Accurately predicting longitudinal DR using baseline characteristics or a single direct measurement of DR is challenging as DR changes rapidly during decongestion. Due to the dynamic nature of DR over therapy, serial assessment and diuretic titration is required to longitudinally achieve therapeutic DR in most AHF patients.

title: Cumulative Genetic Burden Defines a Gradient of Risk in <i>MYBPC3</i>-Related Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: García Hernandez S, De la Higuera Romero L, Larrañaga-Moreira JM, Mora-Ayestaran N, Valverde-Gómez M, Fernandez A, Amor Salamanca A, Peña Peña ML, Basurte-Elorz MT, Martinez Huertas S, Garcia-Ruano AB, Cárdenas Reyes I, Tingley WG, Gallego Delgado M, Pollman MJ, Fernández X, Sonicheva-Paterson N, Brogger N, Piqueras-Flores J, Varfaj F, Barriales-Villa R, Gimeno-Blanes JR, Elliott PM, Walsh R, García-Pavía P, McKenna WJ, Ochoa JP.
abstractText:
Background

MYBPC3 truncating variants (MYBPC3tv) represent the most common genetic substrate in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, yet carriers show substantial phenotypic variability despite a shared mechanism of haploinsufficiency. The contribution of additional genetic variants to this variability remains incompletely defined.

Methods

We analyzed 11 991 unrelated hypertrophic cardiomyopathy probands undergoing clinical genetic testing. Analyses focused on MYBPC3tv carriers stratified by additional intermediate-effect variants (IEVs) or second monogenic variants. IEVs were further classified as sarcomeric or nonsarcomeric. All probands were genetically characterized at a single center using standardized sequencing protocols, with uniform ascertainment of IEVs throughout the study period. Primary outcomes included age-related penetrance, maximal left ventricular wall thickness, and major adverse cardiovascular events; independent predictors were assessed by a multivariable Cox regression model.

Results

Among 2767 genotype-positive probands, MYBPC3 accounted for 47.6% of cases, with truncating variants representing 81.9% of MYBPC3-positive individuals. Within MYBPC3tv carriers, additional variants were associated with a stepwise gradient of disease severity. Median age at diagnosis decreased from 48 years in isolated carriers to 42 years in MYBPC3tv+IEV and 28 years in double-monogenic carriers, whereas mean wall thickness increased from 21.3 to 24.1 and 26.3 mm, respectively. In multivariable analyses, cumulative genetic burden remained an independent predictor of major adverse cardiovascular event. Sarcomeric IEV carriers (hazard ratio, 10.3 [95% CI, 2.3-28.7]) and biallelic MYBPC3 carriers (hazard ratio, 23.2 [95% CI, 5.3-115.0]) exhibited the highest risk, although estimates in these subgroups should be interpreted cautiously given the limited number of events. All biallelic MYBPC3 carriers were diagnosed in childhood.

Conclusions

Cumulative rare variant burden explains a subset of the phenotypic heterogeneity among MYBPC3tv carriers, defining a hierarchical gradient of disease expression. Intermediate-effect alleles and second monogenic variants, particularly biallelic MYBPC3, identify higher-risk subgroups that may benefit from intensified surveillance, individualized management, and guided therapies.

title: Therapeutically Targetable Th17-Derived miR-721 Drives Autoimmune Myocarditis.
authorString: Ruiz-Fernández I, Sánchez-Díaz R, Blanco-Domínguez R, Ortega-Sollero E, Ortego-Moltó R, Quiroga-Ortiz D, de la Fuente H, Martínez-González J, Jiménez-Borreguero LJ, López-Melgar B, Rivero F, Alfonso F, Sánchez-Madrid F, Ricote M, Martín P.
abstractText:
Background

Myocarditis is an inflammatory cardiac disease in which T helper 17 (Th17) cell-driven immune responses contribute to progression toward dilated cardiomyopathy and heart failure. Current therapies mainly rely on corticosteroids but lack specificity, while the role of miR-721, synthesized by Th17 cells, remains largely unexplored in disease pathogenesis.

Methods

We characterized the presence of mmu-miR-721 and its human homolog hsa-RNA-Chr8:96 in extracellular vesicles secreted by Th17 cells from IL-17 (interleukin-17) eGFP mice with experimental autoimmune myocarditis and from patients with myocarditis. MxCre±Ppargfl/fl mice and luciferase reporter assays were used to validate the target genes of miR-721 and hsa-RNA-Chr8:96, respectively. The functional role of miR-721 in experimental autoimmune myocarditis was investigated using lentiviral vectors overexpression and miRNA sponge molecules for inhibition. Th17 responses and heart inflammation were assessed, and echocardiography was performed after in vivo blockade of mmu-miR-721 in experimental autoimmune myocarditis mice.

Results

Both mmu-miR-721 and hsa-RNA-Chr8:96 were encapsulated in extracellular vesicles and secreted by Th17 cells of mice and patients with myocarditis. Overexpression of mmu-miR-721 in draining lymph node cells from experimental autoimmune myocarditis mice promoted Th17 differentiation via Pparg inhibition and increased RORγt and IL-17 expression. In contrast, no differences in RORγt expression were observed in the absence of Pparg, a target of miR-721, indicating that miR-721 promotes Th17 responses through Pparg repression. In addition, human PPARG was validated as a target gene of hsa-RNA-Chr8:96, as its overexpression in peripheral blood leukocytes downregulated PPARG mRNA levels, suggesting that similar pathways are involved in human pathology. Finally, in vivo blockade of mmu-miR-721 increased Pparg expression, reducing RORγt and IL-17 activation in T cells, leading to decreased leukocyte infiltration in the heart and improved cardiac function thereby ameliorating disease progression.

Conclusions

miR-721 is released by Th17 cells in extracellular vesicles and promotes Th17 responses during myocarditis through repression of PPARγ, identifying this miRNA as both a mechanistic driver of disease and a potential therapeutic target.

title: Endogenous expression of mutant RagC in mice results in early-onset dilated cardiomyopathy with features of the Long-Olsen-Distelmaier syndrome
authorString: Plata-Gomez AB, Sánchez-García E, Sagrera A, de Prado Rivas L, Santamans A, Sanz A, Ortega-Molina A, Fellmann L, Arcones AC, Leiva-Vega L, Caleiras E, Piñeiro-Yáñez E, Cogliati S, Sabio G, Efeyan A.
abstractText: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a severe heart condition often linked to arrhythmias, clots, and heart failure, for which treatments are not yet curative. Recently, de novo mutations in genes encoding components of the Rag GTPase nutrient signaling pathway, particularly in RRAGC, have been found in unrelated patients with a severe, early-onset DCM syndrome called Long-Olsen-Distelmaier. Cancer cell lines, hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes and zebrafish have been used to study this Ragopathy, but a mammalian model to investigate this syndrome has not been generated. Here, we show that mice engineered to endogenously express mutations in Serine 74 (orthologous to the Serine 75 mutated in patients), exhibit early-onset features of DCM with decreased heart size, fibrosis, diastolic dysfunction and aortic insufficiency, characteristics reminiscent of the human syndrome. Moreover, Rragc-mutant hearts display decreased left ventricular mass and interventricular septum. Endogenous heterozygous expression of Rragc mutant variants result in a milder, sublethal defective physiological cardiac growth with increased systolic and diastolic blood pressure. Mechanistically, active RagC does not cause abnormal increase in cardiomyocyte size, but leads to suppressed transcriptional activity of Tfeb and alterations in cardiomyocyte metabolism. Transcriptional profiling of neonatal mutant hearts reveals multiple signatures of impaired mitochondrial activity. Ex vivo and in vitro analyses of murine cardiomyocyte mitochondria from Rragc-mutant mice show suppressed mitochondrial respiration, disturbed complex IV multimerization and super-complex organization. These data point to abnormal early postnatal heart metabolism by deregulated nutrient - Rag GTPase signaling with a potential molecular explanation to the early onset of DCM in patients with de novo missense mutations in RRAGC, and suggests the relevance of early metabolic interventions in conditions with altered nutrient signaling

title: Barriers and Facilitators of Anti-hypertensive Medication Adherence in Kumasi, Ghana: An Exploratory Descriptive Qualitative Study
authorString: Osei-Wusu P, Boateng EA, Diji AK, Poku CA, Asante JK, Amankwaa F, Kolbila L.
abstractText: Introduction Hypertension requires long-term adherence to prescribed anti-hypertensive medication to prevent complications. Although anti-hypertensive therapy is effective, many patients experience personal, social, financial, and health-system challenges that affect consistent medication use. Understanding patients’ experiences is important for designing context-specific strategies to improve adherence. This study explored factors that influence adherence to drug therapy among hypertensive patients attending two government hospitals in Kumasi, Ghana. Methods An exploratory Descriptive Qualitative study was conducted among hypertensive patients receiving care in Kumasi, Ghana. Twenty-four participants were purposively recruited and interviewed using a semi-structured interview guide. Data were analysed thematically, guided by Braun and Clarke’s reflexive thematic analysis approach and informed by the predisposing, enabling and reinforcing constructs of the PRECEDE model. Results Three major themes emerged from the analysis: making sense of hypertension and medication use, navigating treatment and care access, and staying on treatment through motivation and support. Key facilitators included knowledge, medication routines, healthcare-provider counselling, and family support, while barriers included forgetfulness, side effects, financial constraints, service delays, medicine unavailability, and cultural and religious beliefs. Conclusions Adherence to oral anti-hypertensive medication among patients in Kumasi was shaped by the interaction of patient-related, social, and health-system factors. Improving adherence requires continuous patient education, practical medication counselling, respectful communication between healthcare providers and patients, family involvement, affordable access to medicines, and stronger health-system support for long-term hypertension care.

title: Case Report: Life-threatening left-sided portal hypertension–related bleeding due to wandering spleen in a patient with Marfan syndrome
authorString: Delfa RL, Aspite S, Coratti F, Fontanarosa L, Macrì G, Avossa A, Mastro A, Pindozzi F, Rosi M, Caloro A, Ragozzino L, Falcini M, Roccarina D, Gitto S, Falcone G, Mondaini F, Fanelli F, Marra F, Vizzutti F.
abstractText:
Background: Wandering spleen is a rare clinical entity resulting from congenital or acquired laxity of the splenic suspensory ligaments. Torsion of its elongated vascular pedicle may lead to splenic infarction, whereas gastric variceal bleeding secondary to sinistral portal hypertension is an exceptionally uncommon complication. Although Marfan syndrome has occasionally been associated with wandering spleen, hemorrhagic complications related to sinistral portal hypertension have rarely been reported. Case Presentation: A 19-year-old woman with Marfan syndrome presented with syncope followed by massive hematemesis. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed isolated fundal gastric varices without esophageal varices. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated torsion of an ectopic spleen with splenic vein outflow obstruction, sinistral portal hypertension, and gastric varices. Recurrent hemorrhage prompted emergency laparoscopic splenectomy, resulting in complete clinical recovery. Follow-up imaging and endoscopy confirmed progressive regression of the gastric varices without recurrent bleeding.

Conclusions:

This case highlights a rare but potentially life-threatening presentation of wandering spleen and emphasizes the importance of early cross-sectional imaging and timely surgical management in patients with isolated gastric variceal bleeding, particularly in the presence of connective tissue disorders.

title: Divergent Effects of Glycemic Control in Diabetic Heart Failure: Arterial Stiffness vs. Subclinical Atrial Fibrillation
authorString: Durmaz FE, Murat S, Babayigit E, Yunus GO, Dural M, Ozer O, Yorulmaz G, Mert KU.
abstractText: Background Diabetes mellitus and heart failure frequently coexist and contribute to vascular remodeling and arrhythmogenesis. While poor glycemic control promotes arterial stiffening, its relationship with device-detected subclinical atrial fibrillation (SCAF) remains unclear, particularly in longitudinal settings. Objectives To evaluate the impact of glycemic control on arterial stiffness and SCAF in patients with diabetes and heart failure with implanted cardiac devices. Methods In this prospective observational study, 86 patients with heart failure and type 2 diabetes were stratified by baseline HbA1c into strict control (< 7.0%, n = 29) and inadequate control (≥ 7.0%, n = 57). Carotid–femoral pulse wave velocity (cf-PWV) and device-detected arrhythmias were assessed at baseline and 6 months. Group comparisons and regression analyses were performed using standard statistical methods. Results Baseline cf-PWV was higher in the inadequate control group [12.0 (9.7–15.0) vs. 9.4 (8.6–11.8) m/s; p = 0.009], remaining higher at follow-up (p = 0.002). cf-PWV correlated with HbA1c (r = 0.250, p = 0.01) and diabetes duration (r = 0.296, p = 0.006). Change in PWV did not differ between groups (p > 0.05). SCAF incidence was greater in the strict control group (27.6% vs. 8.8%; p = 0.029). Patients with SCAF had lower baseline HbA1c (6.9 ± 0.7% vs. 7.9 ± 1.5%; p = 0.004). No difference was observed in ventricular arrhythmias or ICD therapies (p > 0.05). Conclusion Poor glycemic control is associated with increased arterial stiffness, whereas strict control is linked to higher SCAF incidence in diabetic heart failure. These findings support individualized glycemic targets balancing vascular protection and arrhythmic risk.

title: Tumor factors, but not cirrhosis, drive the development of baseline and incident ascites in surgically resected cholangiocarcinoma: a retrospective cohort study
authorString: Teng Y, Chen Y, Ho C, Lee P, Yang T, Huang H, Huang Y, Chen M, Chiang N, Luo J, Hou M, Wu J, Su C.
abstractText: Background Portal hypertension-related complications have emerged as important prognostic determinants in patients with cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), yet the clinical impact and pathophysiological drivers of ascites in this population have never been systematically investigated. This study aimed to clarify the impact of ascites on overall survival (OS) in patients with surgically resected CCA using a time-dependent approach and to identify the risk factors underlying baseline and incident ascites. Methods We retrospectively reviewed patients with CCA who underwent surgical resection at Taipei Veterans General Hospital between January 2013 and December 2023. Of 842 patients screened, 195 with an available histological ISHAK fibrosis assessment formed the cirrhosis-assessed cohort (baseline ascites, n = 55; no baseline ascites, n = 140). Ascites was modeled as a time-dependent covariate in a Cox analysis of OS to avoid immortal-time bias; risk factors for baseline ascites (logistic regression) and incident ascites (cause-specific Cox regression) were examined, with multiple imputation for missing data. Results Patients with baseline ascites had more late-stage tumors (III–IV, 40.0% vs. 21.6%, p = 0.009), higher CA19-9 (p = 0.001), and worse ALBI scores (p = 0.045), whereas the prevalence of cirrhosis (ISHAK > 4) did not differ (27.3% vs. 22.9%, p = 0.517). Baseline ascites was associated with worse OS (median 876 vs. 2026 days, log-rank p = 0.037). In the adjusted time-dependent model, baseline ascites (HR 1.94, 95% CI 1.12–3.38, p = 0.018) and incident ascites (HR 3.24, 95% CI 1.81–5.80, p < 0.001) independently predicted OS; ALBI grade 2/3 (HR 2.14, p = 0.002) and CA19-9 > 38 U/mL (HR 2.03, p = 0.003) were also independent predictors. Baseline ascites was independently driven by tumor factors (CA19-9 > 38 U/mL: OR 2.22, p = 0.027; clinical stage per stage: OR 1.40, p = 0.049), whereas incident ascites was driven by clinical stage (HR 1.60, p = 0.007) and macrovascular invasion (HR 4.56, p = 0.002). Conclusions In surgically resected CCA patients, baseline and incident ascites were driven predominantly by tumor factors—not by the structural status of cirrhosis—and both, particularly incident ascites, were in turn independently associated with poorer survival. Tumor factors, but not cirrhosis, determined the development of ascites in this population.

title: Long-Term Metabolic Risk Associated with Clozapine in People with Schizophrenia: A Population-based Study in Hong Kong
authorString: Chan SKW, Zhou H, Hui NY, Luo H, Tang J, Lui S, Lee HME, Halstead S, Siskind D, Perry B, Osimo E, Murray G.
abstractText: Clozapine is the only pharmacological treatment effective for treatment-resistant schizophrenia, but concerns about cardiometabolic adverse effects may discourage its use. Population-level, long-term data comparing major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and metabolic disease progression between clozapine users (ClozUs) and non-clozapine antipsychotic users (Non-ClozUs) remain scarce. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using Hong Kong Hospital Authority electronic health records (2003–2019; follow-up through 2023), comparing incident ClozUs with Non-ClozUs matched 1:3 by age, sex, and illness duration. Primary outcomes were new-onset MACE and metabolic diseases (diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, and obesity), assessed using adjusted Cox proportional-hazards models. Secondary outcomes included progression from a single metabolic condition to cardiometabolic multimorbidity or MACE; sensitivity analyses compared clozapine with olanzapine. Among 19,132 patients (mean [SD] age, 39.42 [11.85] years; 49.72% female; mean follow-up, 12.78 years), 4,783 ClozUs had risks of MACE, diabetes, and dyslipidemia comparable to Non-ClozUs, but lower risks of hypertension (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 0.76; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.68–0.84) and obesity (aHR, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.46–0.69). ClozUs also had a lower rate of progression to cardiometabolic multimorbidity or MACE (32.18% vs. 41.31%; P < 0.001). Sensitivity analyses showed lower risks of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and obesity with clozapine than with olanzapine. Older age, male sex, depression, and substance use were associated with metabolic conditions among ClozUs. These findings indicate that metabolic concerns alone should not preclude clozapine treatment and support structured, individualized cardiometabolic monitoring for people receiving antipsychotics.

title: Recurrent Sternal Dehiscence and Total Sternal Erosion Following CABG: Successful Reconstruction Using Bilateral Robicsek Wiring and Plate–Screw Fixation
authorString: Dogru A.
abstractText: Background Sternal wound complications after median sternotomy remain a serious source of morbidity despite advances in surgical techniques. Case Report: A 64-year-old male with hypertension and a history of smoking underwent elective two-vessel coronary artery bypass grafting (CABGx2) on August 7, 2024. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 7. One month later, he presented with sternal wound dehiscence and was taken for revision surgery. The previous wires were removed, and sternal fixation was achieved using a titanium plate-screw system. Despite initial stabilization, recurrent wound dehiscence occurred on postoperative day 5, and vacuum-assisted closure (VAC) therapy was continued until October 10, 2024. Owing to persistent instability and wound breakdown, a second revision was performed. Intraoperatively, the sternum was found to be completely eroded. Bilateral Robicsek wiring was applied to approximate the costal margins, bridging the sternal defect. Additional stabilization was achieved by extending plate-screw fixation to the intercostal junctions. The mediastinum was drained, the subcutaneous layer was closed with continuous Vicryl sutures, and the skin was closed with Prolene in a matrix fashion. One-month follow-up demonstrated a clean wound with complete healing and preserved thoracic stability. Conclusion In patients with total sternal erosion and failure of VAC therapy, combined bilateral Robicsek wiring and plate-screw fixation provides a durable and anatomically sound reconstruction.

title: The combined C-reactive protein–triglyceride–glucose and frailty index in relation to incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity across cohorts in China and England
authorString: Yan H, Li L, Wang M.
abstractText: Background Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) is a growing burden among middle-aged and older adults. The C-reactive protein–triglyceride–glucose index (CTI) reflects inflammatory–metabolic dysfunction, whereas the frailty index (FI) captures physiological vulnerability. Whether CTI-FI is consistently associated with incident CMM and adds predictive value across populations remains uncertain. We evaluated associations of CTI-FI with incident CMM and its incremental predictive value. Methods Adults aged ≥ 45 years were analyzed in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS; 2011–2020) and the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA; 2004–2018). CTI-FI and cumulative CTI-FI (cumCTI-FI) were evaluated in separate cohorts. Adjusted cumulative incidence curves, Cox regression, and restricted cubic splines assessed associations; C-statistics and reclassification measures quantified added predictive value. Predictive performance was compared across eight machine-learning models developed in CHARLS: CatBoost, XGBoost, Extra Trees, random forest, recursive partitioning, support vector machine, k-nearest neighbors, and neural network; the selected models were externally validated in ELSA. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses assessed consistency across participant groups and analytic choices. Results Among 7,108 participants, adjusted cumulative incidence increased across CTI-FI quartiles in both cohorts (all P < 0.001). Per-unit adjusted HRs for CTI-FI were 1.48 (95% CI, 1.37–1.60) in CHARLS and 1.31 (1.17–1.47) in ELSA; Q4-versus-Q1 HRs were 3.40 and 2.62. Nonlinearity was observed for CTI-FI and cumCTI-FI in CHARLS and for cumCTI-FI in ELSA. In CHARLS, the CTI-FI association was stronger among participants aged < 60 years, married, or without hypertension. Adding CTI-FI increased C-statistics from 0.723 to 0.759 in CHARLS and 0.745 to 0.767 in ELSA; NRI improved significantly in both cohorts (0.40 and 0.35), and IDI improved significantly in CHARLS. cumCTI-FI yielded the highest C-statistics (0.763 and 0.768), and CTI-FI showed greater discrimination than CTI or FI. XGBoost had the highest mean cross-validated AUC (0.700); external AUCs were 0.689 and 0.695. SHAP ranked CTI-FI and cumCTI-FI as leading predictors. Conclusions CTI-FI was associated with incident CMM and improved prediction beyond conventional factors in both cohorts. By integrating inflammatory–metabolic dysfunction and frailty-related vulnerability, CTI-FI supports multidimensional risk assessment. Repeated assessment may strengthen early identification and targeted CMM prevention.

title: Sociodemographic, Clinical, and Behavioral Factors Associated with Obesity among Paraguayan Adults: A Nationally Representative Cross-Sectional Study
authorString: Cañete F, Santacruz E, Gatti L, Ávalos A, Cañete N, Barceló A, Ortellado ÁJ.
abstractText: Background Although obesity has become a major global public health challenge, nationally representative evidence on its multifactorial determinants remains scarce in Paraguay. Obesity is closely linked to major noncommunicable diseases, including diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and cardiovascular diseases. This study aimed to analyze the sociodemographic, clinical, and behavioral factors associated with obesity among Paraguayan adults using nationally representative data. Methods An observational cross-sectional study was conducted using secondary data from the 2022 Paraguay WHO STEPS survey. A total of 5,098 adults aged 18–69 years were included through a stratified multistage cluster sampling design to obtain nationally representative estimates. Obesity was defined as a body mass index (BMI) ≥ 30 kg/m². Sociodemographic, clinical, and behavioral variables were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression models accounting for the complex survey design to compute adjusted odds ratios (aOR) and 95% confidence intervals (95% CI). Results The overall national prevalence of obesity was 33.0%, with a higher prevalence among women than men (37.8% vs. 28.2%). Obesity increased progressively with age, reaching 48.0% among individuals aged 40–49 years. Higher prevalence was also observed among married or cohabiting individuals, urban residents, and those in higher income brackets. In the final adjusted multivariable model, hypertension showed the strongest independent association with obesity (aOR = 2.5, 95% CI: 2.1–3.0), followed by age ≥ 40 years (aOR = 1.6, 95% CI: 1.3–1.9), urban residence (aOR = 1.3, 95% CI: 1.0–1.5), and being married or cohabiting (aOR = 1.2, 95% CI: 1.0–1.5). Lower income was associated with lower odds of obesity (aOR = 0.7, 95% CI: 0.6–0.8). No independent associations were observed for tobacco smoking, fruit and vegetable consumption, or physical activity. Conclusions Obesity affects one in three Paraguayan adults and is more strongly associated with sociodemographic and clinical characteristics than with individual behavioral factors in this population. These findings highlight the importance of addressing obesity through comprehensive public health strategies targeting social and environmental determinants rather than relying solely on individual behavioral advice. Given the cross-sectional design, causal inferences cannot be established.

title: Prevalence and correlates of multimarker hypertension-mediated organ damage in Ghanaian adults: evidence from the Ghana Heart Study
authorString: Agyapong KO, Kyeremah E, Folson A, Agyekum F, Blenman K, Appiah L, Boakye YA, Owusu I.
abstractText: Manifestations of hypertension-related organ damage have been described in several African populations. Yet a comprehensive characterization of hypertension-related damage to multiple organs and a comparison with conventionally calculated cardiovascular disease risk in a West African setting is lacking. We performed a secondary analysis of the Ghana Heart Study, which included 1 106 community-dwelling Ghanaian adults from 4 regions. Eight vascular, cardiac, and renal endpoints were determined. Multimarker HMOD (≥ 2 abnormal markers among participants with ≥ 6 measured components) was present in 20.7% and true multiorgan HMOD (≥ 2 of three organ systems) in 16.2%. Prevalence rose from 8.6% at ages < 45 years to 44.1% at ≥ 60 years. In an external- predictor model (n = 1 044), age, systolic blood pressure, hypertension, and rural residence were independently associated with multimarker HMOD; Central region residence was inversely associated. Brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV) showed the highest discrimination among continuous markers (AUC 0.832). Among 530 participants aged 40–74 years, baPWV alone (AUC 0.807) and baPWV plus the Pooled Cohort Equations (AUC 0.815) substantially outperformed the Pooled Cohort Equations alone (AUC 0.526), with improved net benefit across thresholds. Multimarker HMOD is common, strongly age- and blood pressure- dependent, and more frequent in rural settings at younger ages. baPWV may usefully complement conventional risk assessment; prospective studies are required to confirm whether baPWV-guided care improves outcomes.

title: What Is Lost When R-R Interval Time Series Are Compressed into HRV Features? A Machine-Learning Probe in Sinus Rhythm and Continuous Atrial Fibrillation
authorString: Yoshida Y.
abstractText: Heart rate variability (HRV) features provide compact representations of R-R interval (RRI) dynamics and may be suitable for feature-level physiological data transmission, but temporal information may become less accessible after aggregation. This study investigated which aspects of temporal structure remain discriminable when beat-to-beat RRI sequences are replaced by compact HRV-based representations. Sinus rhythm and continuous atrial fibrillation (CAF) datasets were analyzed. For each RRI sequence, Forward, Reverse, and Shuffle variants were generated to probe temporal direction and temporal organization. Three representations were compared: raw beat-to-beat RRI sequences, seven conventional RRI-derived HRV features, and the same seven features supplemented with Half Mean Difference, Linear Slope, and Difference Asymmetry (DAsym). Machine-learning models were used as analytical probes to assess how readily temporal differences could be discriminated from each representation, rather than as the primary object of investigation. In sinus rhythm, Raw RRI classification achieved high performance, with a peak accuracy of 0.936, allowing accurate discrimination of Forward, Reverse, and Shuffle sequences. In CAF, Raw RRI classification showed limited performance, whereas the 7-HRV representation improved Shuffle discrimination. Adding the three temporal descriptors further improved classification performance, particularly for Forward and Reverse in CAF, with a peak accuracy of 0.785. In CAF, DAsym contributed to directional discrimination, and post-hoc analysis showed a modest but consistent positive directional asymmetry (7.69 ± 10.16 ms; p < 0.001). These findings indicate that temporal discriminability depends on both the input representation and the analytical model. Compact physiological representations should be selected according to what information must remain accessible for the intended application.

title: Cardiohepatic Interactions: From Venous Congestion to Pharmacotherapy-A Narrative Review and Proposed Clinical Framework
authorString: Mawas I, Oprea D, Sascău RA, Stătescu C, Șalaru DL, Corneanu LE, Șorodoc L, Lionte C.
abstractText:
Background:

Cardiohepatic syndrome reflects bidirectional heart-liver interactions, particularly in heart failure with elevated right-sided pressures and venous congestion. Congestive hepatopathy may impair hepatic function and influence cardiovascular drug disposition. Whether congestion alters drug exposure remains uncertain.

Objective:

To review cardiohepatic interactions and propose a congestion-phenotyping framework.

Methods:

This narrative review examines venous congestion, congestive hepatopathy, liver stiffness measurement (LSM), venous excess ultrasound (VExUS), hepatic biomarkers, hemodynamics, and cardiovascular pharmacotherapy.

Results:

Elevated right-sided pressures and venous congestion cause hepatic hemodynamic stress and may produce congestive hepatopathy. Hepatic dysfunction can alter the disposition of cardiovascular medications. VExUS and LSM offer complementary assessments of systemic venous congestion and hepatic stiffness, but neither independently establishes fibrosis or guides drug dosing. Congestion-related changes in hepatic and renal function, protein binding, gastrointestinal absorption, and volume of distribution may affect cardiovascular drug pharmacokinetics (PK) and pharmacodynamics (PD). However, evidence linking quantified congestion to drug exposure or PD response remains limited. No prospective evidence validates VExUS- or LSM-guided dosing based on drug concentrations or established PK/PD targets. We propose a physiology-informed framework for incorporating congestion assessment into pharmacological decisions during decongestion.

Conclusion:

Cardiohepatic assessment should distinguish established hemodynamic effects from the unproven relationship between congestion and drug exposure. Combining clinical evaluation, biomarkers, venous ultrasound, LSM, and selected invasive hemodynamics may improve congestion phenotyping and monitoring. This framework remains hypothesis-generating, not a validated dosing strategy. Prospective studies integrating congestion measures, drug concentrations, PK/PD parameters, and outcomes are needed to determine whether congestion-informed pharmacotherapy improves safety and effectiveness.

title: Pembrolizumab-Associated Myocarditis and Myasthenic Crisis: Discordant Functional and Tissue Recovery.
authorString: Yu AM, Mohmand B, Bcharah H, Willson C, Naqvi A, Wilson ZT, Fakhri NL, Morris MF, Gopalan RS, Mookadam F.
abstractText:
Background

Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) can cause myocarditis with overlapping neuromuscular toxicity.

Case summary

A 77-year-old man developed biopsy-supported ICI myocarditis with biventricular dysfunction (left ventricular ejection fraction: 36%) after 1 pembrolizumab cycle. The course was complicated by seropositive myasthenia gravis (MG) requiring mechanical ventilation and an unexpected nonocclusive saddle pulmonary embolism. Corticosteroid-refractory troponin elevation prompted escalation to abatacept, while prednisone was reduced for worsening myasthenic weakness. Follow-up cardiac magnetic resonance during sepsis showed improved left ventricular ejection fraction of 53%, but myocardial T2 remained elevated with a persistent nonischemic pattern of late gadolinium enhancement. Troponin remained elevated, and ventilator dependence persisted.

Discussion

ICI myocarditis may show improving ventricular systolic function while myocardial tissue abnormalities persist, and coexisting MG may limit corticosteroid use.

Take-home messages

Myocarditis and MG may coexist and require multidisciplinary management. Troponin T may remain elevated for months and is not diagnostic of ongoing myocardial inflammation.

title: Deletion of Yes-Associated Protein in Vascular Smooth Muscle Cells Alleviates Atherosclerosis.
authorString: Hou Y, Sun X, Zhang X, Qin Q, Jia M, Su X, Chen Y.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

The migration and proliferation of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) are critical processes in the development of atherosclerosis. YAP (Yes-associated protein) regulates VSMC migration and proliferation. However, its specific role in atherosclerosis remains unclear.

Methods

Atherosclerosis models were generated in mice injected with adeno-associated virus 8-mPCSK9 (murine proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9) or ApoE-/- (apolipoprotein E knockout) mice by being fed a high-cholesterol diet. Primary VSMCs were used to elucidate its mechanism.

Results

YAP expression was elevated in VSMCs within mouse atherosclerotic plaques. Both tamoxifen-mediated YAPΔVSMC or adeno-associated virus-inducible VSMC-specific YAP knockout mice injected with adeno-associated virus 8-mPCSK9 and YAPΔVSMCApoE-/- mice exhibited alleviated atherosclerotic phenotype. Further study found that angiopoietin-2 overexpression induced VSMC phenotypic switching, migration, and proliferation in YAP knockout VSMCs stimulated with platelet-derived growth factor-BB in vitro. Furthermore, the VSMC-specific angiopoietin-2 overexpression could completely reverse VSMC YAP deficiency-alleviated atherosclerotic phenotype and the effect of YAP-mediated VSMC phenotypic switching. Mechanistically, YAP upregulated angiopoietin-2 via TEAD4 (murine TEA domain family member 4) in VSMCs.

Conclusions

In conclusion, our findings revealed that YAP promotes atherosclerosis by inducing angiopoietin-2-mediated VSMC phenotypic switching via TEAD4. Inhibition of VSMC YAP may be an effective therapeutic strategy for atherosclerosis.

title: Metabolic and Renal Dysfunction Are Associated With Intraplaque Lipid Burden Assessed by Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Intravascular Ultrasound: Insights Into the Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Axis.
authorString: Kook H, Kim W, Cho SR, Lim YH.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

The cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic framework emphasizes the interrelated contributions of metabolic and renal dysfunction to cardiovascular risk. Whether these disturbances are reflected in coronary plaque composition remains incompletely understood. We evaluated the association of metabolic and renal dysfunction with intraplaque lipid burden using near-infrared spectroscopy intravascular ultrasound.

Methods

Intraplaque lipid burden was assessed by the maximum lipid core burden index (LCBI) within a 4-mm segment (maxLCBI4mm), and lipid-rich plaque (LRP) was defined as maxLCBI4mm≥324.7. Multivariable linear regression models were constructed with maxLCBI4mm as the dependent variable, and multivariable logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations with LRP.

Results

Among 483 patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention with pre-intervention near-infrared spectroscopy intravascular ultrasound imaging, lower estimated glomerular filtration rate and higher hemoglobin A1c were independently associated with greater intraplaque lipid burden and higher odds of LRP. In analyses standardized per 1 SD, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol showed the strongest association with maxLCBI4mm (β=52.51; 95% CI, 27.49-77.53), followed by estimated glomerular filtration rate (β=33.38; 95% CI, 9.97-56.80) and hemoglobin A1c (β=24.71; 95% CI, 3.71-45.71). Similarly, lower estimated glomerular filtration rate (odds tatio [OR], 1.36; 95% CI, 1.06-1.75) and higher hemoglobin A1c (OR, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.05-1.77) were independently associated with LRP. No significant interaction between estimated glomerular filtration rate and hemoglobin A1c was observed.

Conclusions

Metabolic and renal dysfunction are independently associated with intraplaque lipid burden assessed by near-infrared spectroscopy intravascular ultrasound. These findings provide intracoronary imaging evidence linking the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic framework to plaque-level lipid accumulation.

title: Eight Novel Sonographic Signs
authorString: Ji X.
abstractText: Ultrasound is a widely used imaging modality in clinical practice, and sonographic signs serve as valuable teaching tools that aid in pattern recognition and diagnosis. This review consolidates five novel sonographic signs previously proposed by the author, including the Cracked Earth Sign for subcutaneous edema, the Mushroom Cap Sign for localized gallbladder adenomyomatosis, the LTS Sign for dilated cardiomyopathy, the LTI Sign for endocardial fibroelastosis, and the Three Pipes Sign for the suprasternal long-axis view of the aortic arch. The SFH Sign for advanced cervical insufficiency, the Gentle Upslope Sign for the parvus–tardus waveform, and the Fenestrated Ring Sign for diffuse gallbladder adenomyomatosis are proposed for the first time in this paper. Collectively, these eight signs span the fields of superficial ultrasound, abdominal ultrasound, echocardiography, and obstetric ultrasound. For each sign, its naming logic, definition, clinical implications, and teaching value are described. This review aims to facilitate a better understanding of these signs and to promote their use as teaching aids in ultrasound education.

title: Preclinical testing of a novel tandem endo-Wheat delivery system.
authorString: Pedroza AJ, Vallee A, Ghostine S, Julien M, Fleurot S, Kratzberg J, Fabre D, Guihaire J, Haulon S.
abstractText:
Background

Endovascular repair of pathology affecting the proximal aorta is an area of active innovation. Physician-modified composite valve-graft devices have successfully been implemented to repair the aortic root, but several technical challenges remain. While treatment of aortic root pathology requires complete seal at the level of the sinuses of Valsalva and bridging stents into the coronary arteries ("endo-Bentall"), aortic dissection originating above the sinotubular junction can be addressed in principle via a procedure analogous to surgical aortic valve replacement and separate graft replacement of the ascending aorta ("endo-Wheat"). Here, we report the technical description and preclinical assessment of a novel fenestrated endograft, and delivery system intended for tandem use with a balloon-expandable aortic valve prosthesis.

Methods

A novel endo-Wheat device and sheath system were fabricated following iterative design refinements. Laboratory-based testing was performed using a 3D-printed phantom of a thoracoabdominal aorta with an acute type A aortic dissection.

Results

This endo-Wheat system is designed to enable coronary artery perfusion through via aortic root fenestrations while establishing a seal at the sinotubular junction. We demonstrated techinical feasibility with tandem delivery of the fenestrated endograft and balloon-expandable TEVAR in rapid succession. We identify technical challenges with the implementation of this system and subsequent design modifications.

Conclusions

We conclude that this device may provide a reliable, off-the-shelf solution for treatment of acute type A aortic dissection in poor operative candidates.

title: Longitudinal Endoleak Behaviour Following Complex Aortic Repair With Branched Devices.
authorString: Vuthivanich C, Konstantinou N, Stana J, Hasemaki N, Elkady M, Becker D, Tsilimparis N.

journal.title: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists

abstractText:
Objective

This study aimed to determine the incidence, natural history, outcomes and risk factors of endoleak following branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) for complex abdominal aortic aneurysm (cAAA) and thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs).

Methods

This retrospective, single-centre study enrolled patients with cAAA and TAAA treated with BEVAR. Patients with at least 1 target vessel incorporated using directional branches were included. End points were spontaneous resolution of endoleak detected on completion angiography, 3-year freedom from persistent type I/III endoleak and endoleak-related reintervention. Multivariable Cox regression analyses were performed to identify independent risk factors for type II endoleak (T2EL) and branch-related endoleak (BREL).

Results

In a 6-year period, 298 patients underwent fenestrated/branched endovascular aortic repair (F/BEVAR) of which 129 patients (mean age 72 ± 9 years; 62% male) underwent F/BEVAR for 36 cAAA (27.9%) and 93 TAAA (72.1%) with at least 1 directional branch. In all, 458 reno-mesenteric arteries were incorporated using directional branches. Completion intra-operative angiography detected endoleak in 81 patients (64.8%), of which 43.2% demonstrated spontaneous resolution on postoperative computed tomographic angiography. During a mean follow-up of 20.2 ± 19.9 months, 14 branches (3.0%) in 14 patients (10.9%) developed BREL, predominantly type Ic. Freedom from persistent type I/III endoleak and endoleak-related reintervention were 70.6% and 68.5% at 3 years, respectively. Aneurysm diameter ≥80 mm (hazard ratio [HR] 2.76, 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.54-4.95; P < .001), post-dissection aetiology (HR 1.84, 95% CI, 1.02-3.33; P = .043) and accessory renal artery (ARA) ≥3 mm in diameter that was not incorporated or pre-emptively embolised (HR 2.03, 95% CI, 1.11-3.74; P = .022) were identified as independent risk factors for T2EL.

Conclusion

Immediate endoleak following BEVAR was common, but a substantial proportion were self-limiting. Type Ic endoleak was the most common type of BREL and the most frequent indication for endoleak-related reintervention. Large aneurysm diameter, post-dissection aetiology and ARA increased risk for T2EL.Clinical ImpactEndoleak following branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) was commonly detected on completion angiography; however, immediate intervention was not required after ensuring adequate sealing zones and optimised bridging stent configuration, as 43% demonstrated spontaneous resolution on early postoperative imaging. Type Ic endoleak was the predominant form of branch-related endoleak, highlighting the importance of meticulous attention to target vessel landing zones. When anatomically feasible, incorporation of accessory renal artery ≥3 mm in the repair is recommended; alternatively, pre-emptive embolisation may reduce type II endoleak incidence.

title: Comparison of Prosthetic Valve Deformation and Hemodynamic Performance Between Bicuspid and Tricuspid Aortic Valve Anatomy After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
authorString: Feng D, Zhou Z, Ma H, Niu G, Zhang H, Zhao Z, Zhang E, Zhang B, Ye Y, Li Z, Wang M, Zhao J, Wu Y.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

This study compared prosthetic valve deformation and postprocedural hemodynamic performance between bicuspid and tricuspid aortic valve anatomy after transcatheter aortic valve replacement with the Venus-A prosthesis.

Methods

We retrospectively evaluated patients who underwent transcatheter aortic valve replacement between 2012 and 2022 and underwent postoperative computed tomography within 1 year. Predischarge echocardiographic assessments included the mean transvalvular gradient and paravalvular leak. Computed tomography measurements included expansion ratio, ellipticity, implantation depth, asymmetric leaflet expansion, and hypoattenuated leaflet thickening. The leaflet inflow and valve waist were collectively defined as the functional valve portion.

Results

Among 212 patients (106 bicuspid and 106 tricuspid), the mean age was 74.2±7.6 years, and 43.9% were women. Patients with bicuspid anatomy had a significantly lower oversizing ratio and underwent balloon predilation and postdilation more frequently than those with tricuspid anatomy.
