Residual transvalvular gradients were higher with bicuspid than tricuspid anatomy (12.0 [interquartile range, 8.2-17.0] versus 10.0 [7.2-14.0] mm Hg; P=0.014), whereas moderate to severe paravalvular leak did not differ significantly. Prosthetic ellipticity was greater in bicuspid anatomy, but expansion ratios, including those within the functional valve portion, did not differ significantly. Implantation depth, asymmetric leaflet expansion, and hypoattenuated leaflet thickening incidence also did not differ significantly.

Conclusions

Following Venus-A implantation, bicuspid anatomy was associated with greater prosthetic ellipticity and higher residual gradients, despite no significant difference in prosthetic expansion.

title: NNMT Safeguards Vascular Aging by Modulating an Endothelial LMNA-HSP Stress-Response Axis.
authorString: Guo J, Tu H, Yin J, Gao S, Liu D, Wang M, Lin Y, Zhang X, Meng L, Sun J, Wang D, Li Y, Wang M, Li J.
abstractText:
Background

NNMT (nicotinamide N-methyltransferase) is a pivotal metabolic-epigenetic integrator that regulates cellular methylation balance. Although its expression and function exhibit profound, context-dependent heterogeneity in metabolic diseases and cancer, its role within the vascular system, particularly in aging endothelial cells, remains elusive.

Methods

We examined NNMT expression in a small, pathological, male-only cohort of older versus younger plaque-adjacent human carotid intimal donors, primary mouse aortic endothelial cells, and senescent human umbilical vein endothelial cells. Using endothelial-targeted adeno-associated virus-Tie systems, we assessed the effects of NNMT restoration and knockdown on vasodilation and arterial stiffness in aged mice. Mechanistic insights were obtained through exploratory multiomics integration.

Results

We established that NNMT expression exhibits an exploratory inverse association in a small, pathological, male-only cohort of older versus younger plaque-adjacent human carotid intimal donors, a pattern mirrored by declines observed in primary mouse aortic endothelial cells and senescent human umbilical vein endothelial cells. Functional assays demonstrated that NNMT restoration improves vasodilation and arterial stiffness in aged mice, whereas knockdown exacerbates these deficits. Mechanistically, exploratory multiomics integration, including Cleavage Under Targets and Tagmentation and transcriptomic analyses, suggests that NNMT-associated reduction in histone H3 lysine 27 trimethylation occupancy at the LMNA (lamin A/C) promoter correlates with its transcriptional maintenance, a process influenced by S-adenosylmethionine supplementation. Downstream, we identified that NNMT-induced LMNA stabilization operates in concert with HSF1 (heat shock transcription factor 1) activation and nuclear translocation, a process accompanied by enhanced binding to HSP90 and HSP70 promoters to drive their transcription. Furthermore, we demonstrated that the vascular protective effects of the natural compound Heterophyllin B are mediated, at least in part, by NNMT, as these benefits were partially attenuated after endothelial NNMT knockdown in vivo.

Conclusions

We identify a protective, age-dependent role for NNMT in vascular endothelium. Our findings reveal that NNMT maintains endothelial homeostasis through coordinated regulation of nuclear LMNA and the downstream HSP (heat shock protein) stress response, highlighting the therapeutic potential of this pathway for addressing age-related endothelial dysfunction.

title: Partial reprogramming reveals lineage-specific uncoupling of rejuvenation, function, and recoverability in human cells
authorString: Washizu K, Wang X, Draper JM, Yamanaka S, Kunitomi A.
abstractText: Partial reprogramming is therapeutically useful only if cells keep its benefits while recovering their lineage identity and function after the reprogramming factors are withdrawn. Whether the relationship between reprogramming depth and recovery differs between lineages is unknown. Using reversible, traceable Sendai-OSKM, we prospectively isolated intermediate reprogramming states from primary human fibroblasts, cytotoxic T cells, and aortic endothelial cells and followed their recovery. Outcomes diverged: fibroblasts kept a reduced DNA methylation age but retained stromal remodeling and incomplete proliferative recovery; T cells recovered only from shallow reprogramming, with enhanced effector function; endothelial cells rapidly recovered identity, kept a reduced methylation age, and markedly improved vascular function. None of this tracked iPSC derivation efficiency. Multiome and knockdown analyses identified TOX as a shared progression dependency, whereas its candidate downstream programs were predominantly lineage-specific. Partial reprogramming involves a lineage-specific tradeoff between rejuvenation and recovery that must be optimized one lineage at a time.

title: Transbaffle Transcatheter Valve-in-Valve Implantation for Systemic Atrioventricular Bioprosthetic Stenosis in a Patient With Fontan Circulation.
authorString: Quennelle S, Torras O, Aldebert P.
abstractText:
Background

We report the case of a 29-year-old woman with an atrioventricular canal defect with left ventricular hypoplasia and mitral atresia in the setting of situs inversus and dextrocardia, palliated with Fontan circulation.

Case summary

At 21 years of age, she underwent systemic atrioventricular valve replacement with a 33-mm Hancock II bioprosthesis (Medtronic). Eight years later, she developed progressive bioprosthetic stenosis: mean transvalvular gradient of 11 mm Hg with restricted leaflet motion. Given prohibitive surgical risk, transcatheter valve-in-valve (ViV) implantation using a 29-mm Sapien 3 (Edwards Lifesciences) prosthesis was performed via transbaffle access. The procedure resulted in immediate hemodynamic improvement with reduction of the mean gradient.

Discussion

Only a few cases of transbaffle ViV implantation in the systemic atrioventricular position in patients with a Fontan circulation have been reported.

Take-home message

This case illustrates the feasibility of transbaffle ViV implantation in complex Fontan anatomy and highlights transcatheter therapy as a valuable alternative in high-risk adult congenital heart disease.

title: A novel mouse model recapitulates features of the neurodevelopmental disorder 3p25.3 microdeletion syndrome
authorString: Morgan ST, Vanyai HK, Blewitt ME, Keniry A, Eccles S, Kueh AJ.
abstractText: Neurodevelopmental disorders globally affect approximately 15% of children and adolescents, but many disorders do not have mouse models, thus limiting our ability to further understand them and ultimately develop treatments. In our study, we developed a novel mouse line to model 3p25.3 microdeletion syndrome (  6qE3  del/+ ) that reliably recapitulates key features of the syndrome.  6qE3  del/+ mice display congenital heart defects, craniofacial defects, skeletal anomalies and subtle brain changes. We also generated another neurodevelopmental disorder model for a gene often included in the deleted region,  Brpf1 , and found that congenital heart defects and craniofacial defects may be partly attributable to the heterozygous loss of  Brpf1 in  6qE3  del/+ mice. Together our work offers new neurodevelopment models, and provides evidence that treatments developed for  Brpf1 haploinsufficiency may also benefit 3p25.3 microdeletion syndrome.

title: Delayed Intramyocardial Transplantation of Autologous Cardiac Atrial Stem Cells Attenuates Adverse Remodeling in Chronic Ischemic Cardiomyopathy
authorString: Hendrikx M, Daniels A, Fanton Y, De Bouver C, Jamaer L, Rummens J, Hensen K.
abstractText:
Background:

Cell therapy for chronic ischaemic cardiomyopathy remains limited by poor myocardial retention and uncertain regenerative efficacy. We evaluated the effects of delayed intramyocardial transplantation of autologous cardiac atrial stem cells in a large-animal model of established chronic myocardial infarction.

Methods:

Myocardial infarction was induced in Göttingen minipigs by two-hour left anterior descending coronary artery occlusion. After two months of post-infarction remodeling, animals were randomly allocated to intramyocardial transplantation of autologous cardiac atrial stem cells or control treatment. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and three-dimensional electromechanical mapping were performed before treatment and two months thereafter. Histological and immunofluorescence analyses assessed persistence and phenotype of transplanted cells.

Results:

At follow-up, left ventricular ejection fraction was preserved in treated animals but declined in controls (55 ± 9% versus 41 ± 7%; p = 0.0002). Treatment attenuated adverse ventricular remodeling, with preservation of end-systolic volume and regional wall thickening. Late gadolinium enhancement-defined infarct mass decreased from 6.2 ± 2.0 g to 4.0 ± 1.0 g in treated animals and was significantly lower than in controls at follow-up (p = 0.04). Electromechanical mapping demonstrated improved myocardial electrical viability and regional mechanical function. Transplanted cells persisted within the injured myocardium and exhibited cardiomyocyte-associated structural features.

Conclusions:

Delayed intramyocardial transplantation of autologous cardiac atrial stem cells attenuated adverse remodeling and was associated with improved regional myocardial structure and function in established chronic ischaemic cardiomyopathy.

title: The Burden of Occult Cerebrovascular Disease in CKD: A Scoping Review.
authorString: Vasaghi-Gharamaleki M, Jazayeri SB, Pillai A, Johansen KL, Murray AM, Sedaghat S, Sabayan B.

journal.title: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation

abstractText:
Rationale & objective

Occult cerebrovascular diseases (OCCD) including extracranial and intracranial atherosclerotic disease (ECAD and ICAD) and cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) are asymptomatic cerebrovascular abnormalities associated with future risk of stroke and dementia. Although chronic kidney disease (CKD) is strongly associated with adverse brain health outcomes, the breadth of evidence regarding OCCD in people with CKD has not been comprehensively characterized. This scoping review summarizes the available literature on OCCD among adults with CKD without clinically overt cerebrovascular disease.

Sources of evidence

PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched for studies published between January 2000 and July 2025.

Eligibility criteria

Peer-reviewed studies reporting the frequency or characteristics of OCCD manifestations in adults with CKD without a known history of stroke or transient ischemic attack.

Charting methods

Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data on study characteristics, CKD definitions, neuroimaging modalities, and reported OCCD findings. Methodological quality was assessed using a modified Newcastle-Ottawa Scale.

Results

Forty-six studies comprising 5,153 participants with CKD were included. Study populations varied substantially with respect to CKD stage, dialysis status, study design, and imaging methodology. Two studies evaluating ICAD reported moderate-to-severe intracranial stenosis in approximately one-quarter of participants with CKD. Across studies evaluating ECAD, the frequency of significant extracranial carotid stenosis ranged from approximately 3% in patients with non-dialysis-dependent CKD to 28% among patients receiving dialysis. Thirty-eight studies evaluated manifestations of CSVD, including cerebral microbleeds, silent cerebral infarctions, white matter hyperintensities, and enlarged perivascular spaces. Several studies suggested a greater burden of CSVD manifestations among patients with advanced CKD or dialysis dependence. Reported frequencies varied considerably across studies.

Limitations

Considerable heterogeneity in study populations, CKD definitions, imaging protocols, and outcome ascertainment methods limited direct comparison across studies.

Conclusions

Occult cerebrovascular abnormalities are frequently reported across diverse CKD populations, particularly among patients with advanced kidney disease. Variation in the prevalence of abnormalities may reflect differences in CKD severity, participant characteristics, neuroimaging protocols, and outcome definitions. These findings highlight the need for standardized neuroimaging approaches and prospective studies to better characterize the clinical implications of OCCD in CKD.

title: VEXAS Unraveled: Reversal of Severe Cardiomyopathy in VEXAS With Targeted Immunotherapy.
authorString: Dawamne T, Omega M, Tochtrop A, Grennan K, Acevedo-Monsanto M, White D, Merilan V, Dhungel S, Wilson C, Freeman M.
abstractText:
Background

Vacuoles, E1 enzyme, X-linked, autoinflammatory, somatic (VEXAS) syndrome is an autoinflammatory disorder associated with systemic inflammation. Cardiac involvement is rare (<12%).

Case summary

A 72-year-old man with myelodysplastic syndrome presented with sepsis progressing to shock, despite resolution of prior infection and the lack of a new infection. He developed severe nonischemic cardiomyopathy with a left ventricular ejection fraction decline from 65% to 12% with an unremarkable cardiac angiogram, intermittent fevers, and pancytopenia. Genetic testing confirmed VEXAS syndrome. After multidisciplinary discussions, initiation of corticosteroids, interleukin-1 blockade, and Janus kinase inhibition led to recovery of cardiac function to a 54% left ventricular ejection fraction.

Discussion

This case highlights VEXAS syndrome as an under-recognized inflammatory cause of cardiomyopathy. Restored cardiac function, a rarely reported finding, underscores the role of multidisciplinary management and targeted immunomodulatory therapy.

Take-home messages

VEXAS should be considered in older men with refractory systemic inflammation and new cardiomyopathy. Early immunotherapy may reverse cardiac dysfunction.

title: Adult-like thick-filament protein stoichiometry in immature human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes
authorString: Ventura-Gomes A, Calheiros da Gama M, Furtado M, Carmo-Fonseca M.
abstractText: Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs) retain immature sarcomeric isoforms, raising questions about their ability to recapitulate the protein stoichiometry of adult human myocardium. We integrated two independent quantitative proteomic datasets of iPSC-CMs with published fetal and region-resolved adult human heart proteomes to compare sarcomeric protein abundance. Although iPSC-CMs clustered with fetal heart based on their global shared proteome and retained fetal troponin I expression, key thick-filament protein ratios closely matched those of adult myocardium. Myosin heavy-to-light chain ratios approached the expected 2:4 stoichiometry, while myosin-binding protein abundance relative to myosin heavy chains was comparable across iPSC-CMs and adult cardiac regions. These findings reveal that developmental immaturity in sarcomeric isoform expression does not entail altered thick-filament protein proportions. Preservation of adult-like myosin-binding protein stoichiometry supports the use of iPSC-CMs to investigate sarcomeric diseases associated with altered protein dosage, particularly MYBPC3-associated hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

title: 360° MDL: A Multi-Stream, Multidimensional and Resilience-Tested Methodology for Literature Reviews—Design, Open Toolkit and Demonstration in Two Applied Reviews
authorString: Lytras MD.
abstractText: Literature reviews are among the most read and cited scholarly publications, yet most draw on one or two databases, privilege the most-cited voices and report conclusions without testing whether they depend on the choice of sources. Reporting guidelines secure transparency of searching and selection but do not prescribe how to balance academic, practice, policy and emerging evidence, or how to measure the robustness of conclusions. We present 360° MDL, the Multidimensional Literature Review Model, developed with a design-science approach and released with an open toolkit and a 30-item reporting checklist. It combines five evidence stream families, a three-gate selection process with a six-criterion quality gate and portfolio rules, eight analysis matrices, and indices of stream balance, coverage, method diversity and resilience; each key finding is graded by its Triangulation Strength across stream families and stress-tested by leaving one family out. Two applied reviews, in clinical artificial intelligence and in genetic cardiomyopathy, demonstrate it: non-database streams supplied 60–64% of the core corpora, most key findings were robust across three or more families, and a database-only design would have missed two to three findings per review. 360° MDL complements PRISMA and offers authors, editors and assessors an auditable route from evidence volume to tested synthesis.

title: Ruptured pheochromocytoma during preoperative doxazosin treatment.
authorString: AlMaimoni R, AlFaraj A, AlSaif O, AlWosaibei A, Busbaih A, Hussein S.
abstractText: Rupture of pheochromocytoma is rare but represents a life-threatening complication. A 43-year-old man with episodic hypertension, palpitations, and chest discomfort was incidentally found, during a computed tomography (CT) aortogram performed to rule out aortic dissection, to have a 5.2-cm right adrenal mass suspicious for pheochromocytoma. Biochemical testing confirmed catecholamine excess. He was started on oral doxazosin 1 mg daily, which was titrated to 2 mg daily after 1 week, followed by oral bisoprolol 2.5 mg daily in preparation for surgery. Five weeks later, he presented with severe right-sided abdominal pain and a blood pressure of 215/111 mmHg. Abdominal CT angiography showed interval enlargement of the adrenal mass with posterior rupture and a retroperitoneal hematoma without active bleeding. He was stabilized with conservative management and subsequently underwent robotic right adrenalectomy. Histopathology confirmed pheochromocytoma with necrosis, without angioinvasion or lymphatic invasion, and with negative margins. Pheochromocytoma rupture can occur despite appropriate α-blockade, and spontaneous hemorrhage remains the most likely proposed mechanism, although α-blockade may be a contributing factor in selected cases.

title: Multi-Structure Segmentation of Type B Aortic Dissection from CT Images with U-Net
authorString: Gong R, Chen J, Qian L, Du Y, Leshnower BG, Liu M, Liang L.
abstractText: Type B aortic dissection (TBAD) is a life-threatening condition in which a tear in the intimal layer separates the aortic wall into a true and a false lumen. Assessment of the lumen, the intimal flap, and false-lumen thrombosis from CT images is important for risk analysis and treatment planning. This work applied U-Net-based deep neural networks to the automatic segmentation of these structures in TBAD. We collected 46 CT scans from 20 patients, with voxel-wise annotations of three structures: the aortic lumen, the intimal flap, and the thrombus. We explored four models: two convolutional networks, nnU-Net 2D and 3D, and two transformer-based architectures, TransUNet 2D and 3D. We observed that (1) for both nnU-Net and TransUNet, the 3D models outperformed their 2D counterparts on all three structures. The difference was small for the aortic lumen but large for the thin flap and the thrombus. The best model, nnU-Net 3D, reached a DSC of 93.05% for the lumen, 50.22% for the flap, and 69.94% for the thrombus. (2) The intimal flap was the most difficult structure for all models. Even the best 3D models showed large thrombus boundary errors in a few scans. These results provide a baseline for developing more advanced models for accurate segmentation of these structures in TBAD.

title: Senescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype (SASP) and Atherosclerotic Plaque Inflammation: Natural Product-Based Interventions and Implications for Personalized Therapy.
authorString: Liu D, Kornthong N, Yu S, Tangthianchaichana J, Sobhon P, Yang S.
abstractText: Atherosclerosis underlies most ischemic cardiovascular events, and its prevalence rises with population aging. Cellular senescence is increasingly implicated as a driver of plaque progression, although the causal evidence is largely preclinical. Senescent endothelial cells, smooth muscle cells, and macrophages acquire a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), releasing cytokines, chemokines, proteases, and procoagulant factors. These factors sustain plaque inflammation, weaken the fibrous cap, and increase rupture risk. In this narrative review, we link SASP signaling to plaque instability through NF-κB, p38 MAPK, mTOR, NLRP3, and cGAS-STING signaling. We then evaluate tetramethylpyrazine (ligustrazine), quercetin, fisetin, resveratrol, and curcumin against an operational definition reserving senolytic and senomorphic for effects shown in confirmed senescent cells. On that standard, only quercetin and fisetin qualify; for the other three, the vascular evidence is anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, or senescence-preventive rather than directed at established senescent cells. Tetramethylpyrazine protects the endothelial glycocalyx and reduces plaque area in atherosclerotic rabbits. Dasatinib plus quercetin benefits ApoE-/- mice, whereas the only human evidence comes from quercetin monotherapy, which improved endothelium-dependent vasodilation in vessels from symptomatic male, but not female, bypass patients ex vivo. Because senescence burden varies between individuals, we consider how multiomics profiling might stratify patients. The evidence remains mechanistic and hypothesis-generating, with limited human cardiovascular interventional data: Much of it was recorded in cells never shown to be senescent, and no formulation has been shown to reach the human vessel wall. Targeting the SASP therefore requires trial evidence rather than an established basis for precision medicine.

title: Late Type IIIa Endoleak Despite Adequate Component Overlap after AFX2 EVAR: A Report of Two Cases.
authorString: Yokoyama N, Tatsukawa T, Fuchizawa K, Lee JA, Kagawa K, Kobayashi D, Akasaka N, Harada H.
abstractText: Late type IIIa endoleak is a recognized complication of AFX2 (Endologix, Irvine, CA, USA) endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). We report 2 cases occurring 6 and 7 years after EVAR despite adequate initial overlap. In Case 1, computed tomography angiography (CTA) did not clearly demonstrate component uncoupling, whereas duplex ultrasonography showed bidirectional ("to-and-fro") flow and angiography confirmed a type IIIa endoleak. In Case 2, serial computed tomography (CT) retrospectively demonstrated progressive sideways displacement before complete uncoupling. Focal cuff relining and complete endograft relining were performed, respectively. These cases emphasize the need for lifelong surveillance for sac enlargement and changes in endograft configuration after AFX2 EVAR.

title: NLRP3<sup>+</sup> Macrophages: Central Inflammatory Nodes of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm and Potential Cellular Target of Omega-3 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids.
authorString: Wang Y, Pan H, Rong H, Zeng Y, Li Y, Li X, Liang Z, Wang J, Fang L, Li P, Dai X.
abstractText: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a fatal inflammatory vascular disease without effective clinical treatments. Dietary patterns regulate aortic inflammation, and Mediterranean diet-derived omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (ω-3 PUFA) exert anti-inflammatory effects, yet their cellular targets in AAA remain unclear. We integrated three single-cell RNA-seq cohorts (12 AAA, 3 controls) and constructed a human aortic cell atlas with 64,258 cells. Pseudo-bulk analysis and CoVarNet multicellular network analysis revealed a core remodeling axis: protective FOLR2<sup>+</sup> resident macrophages were depleted, while a unique AAA-enriched NLRP3<sup>+</sup> inflammatory macrophage population (M08_Mph_NLRP3) formed the hub of pathological inflammatory networks. Three bulk transcriptomic cohorts and five complementary enrichment approaches verified this signature. An LPS/OX-LDL/IL-1β-stimulated THP-1 model recapitulated AAA macrophage pathological changes including NLRP3 inflammasome overactivation, enhanced proliferation and migration. Further functional tests demonstrated ω-3 PUFA markedly blocked inflammasome cascade, reduced IL-1β/IL-18 release and reversed all macrophage pathological phenotypes. This study identifies M08_Mph_NLRP3 as the important inflammatory mediator of AAA and provides single-cell and in vitro functional evidence supporting ω-3 PUFA as a candidate nutritional agent targeting NLRP3-driven vascular inflammation.

title: Native Aorta Non-Touch Total Arch Hybrid Repair for Residual Aortic Dissection after Hemiarch Replacement.
authorString: Handa K, Sakamoto T, Ohata T, Nakamura T, Kuratani T.
abstractText: Reintervention for residual aortic arch dissection after hemiarch replacement for acute type A aortic dissection remains technically challenging. A 70-year-old man presented with progressive dissecting arch aneurysmal dilatation 6 years after hemiarch replacement. Native aorta non-touch total arch hybrid repair was performed using the previously implanted hemiarch graft as the inflow source for total supra-aortic debranching and as the site for short elephant trunk placement. Staged thoracic endovascular aortic repair was performed the following day. Postoperative computed tomography showed no endoleak, and the patient remained free from aortic events at 5-year follow-up.

title: Prescription Patterns and Adherence to GOLD 2021 Guidelines for Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Management in Pakistan: A Cross-Sectional Study.
authorString: Kanwal H, Shah SS, Ali AA, Khan A, Umm-E-Kalsoom, Mushtaq S, Rabia M, Fang Y.
abstractText:
Background and aims

Global Initiative for chronic obstructive lung disease (GOLD) offers evidence-based recommendations for the management of COPD, but compliance with the guidelines amongst physicians in LMC countries is varied. The objective of this study was to determine the prescribing pattern of inhaled COPD medications in Pakistan and to evaluate the adherence of pulmonologists with the GOLD 2021 guidelines and to assess all the factors that would affect the adherence.

Methods

This cross-sectional observational study was undertaken at secondary health care facilities Rawalpindi and Islamabad between the period of April-September, 2022. Spirometry, COPD Assessment Test (CAT) and Modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) scores were used to classify outpatients ≥ 40 years old who had COPD confirmed by spirometry into GOLD 2021 ABCD groups. Pharmacological regimens recommended by GOLD were compared with prescribed regimens. Adherence was rated as appropriate, overtreatment or undertreatment. Demographic and clinical variables were correlated with adherence using chi-square and t-test.

Results

Among 400 patients (mean age 61.8 ± 10.0 years; 74.8% male), Group B was most frequent (40.3%), followed by C (24.0%), A (23.8%), and D (12.0%). Overall, 57.0% (228/400; 95% CI: 52.1-61.9%) received guideline-concordant therapy, while 43.0% (172/400; 95% CI: 38.1-47.9%) were inappropriately managed. The 80 patients were considered to be overtreated and 92 patients were considered to be undertreated among the inappropriate prescriptions. Cardiovascular comorbidity was associated with treatment inappropriateness (OR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.05-2.34; p = 0.026), and male sex was also significantly associated with inappropriate prescribing (OR, 2.36; 95% CI, 1.44-3.85; p = 0.001).

Conclusion

More than two-fifths of patients received pharmacological treatment that was not concordant with GOLD 2021 recommendations. Both overtreatment and undertreatment were observed. Strengthening spirometry-based assessment, clinician education, and access to appropriate inhaled therapies may improve guideline-concordant COPD management in Pakistan.

title: Prevalence and factors associated with the development of asthma in a cohort of children who were preterm infants and received passive immunization with palivizumab.
authorString: Manini MB, da Silva NC, Cruz GDAG, Morcillo AM, Ribeiro JD, Toro AADC.
abstractText:
Objective

To assess the prevalence of asthma in a cohort of preterm infants, comparing those who received prophylaxis with palivizumab, a monoclonal antibody against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), with those who did not. That is relevant because RSV infection has been linked to recurrent wheezing and asthma in childhood, but a causal relationship remains unclear.

Methods

This was a prospective cohort study involving children who were preterm infants without congenital heart disease, exposed or not to palivizumab. Parents or legal guardians answered a telephone questionnaire adapted from the International Study of Asthma and Allergies in Childhood, which covers respiratory symptoms, allergy history, and potential risk factors.

Results

Among 292 eligible children, 217 were included (149 in the palivizumab group and 68 in the control group). Of those 217 infants, 25.3% (95% CI:19.9-31.5%) had asthma: 24.2% (95% CI: 17.8-31.5%) in the palivizumab group and 27.9% (95% CI: 18.3-39.5%) in the control group, with no significant difference (p = 0.553). In the bivariate analysis, asthma was significantly associated with a family history of atopy (p < 0.001), parental asthma (p = 0.006), allergic rhinitis in the child (p < 0.001), and atopic dermatitis in the child (p = 0.022). In the multivariate analysis, asthma remained associated with a family history of atopy (adjusted OR = 4.16; 95% CI: 1.77-9.79), allergic rhinitis in the child (adjusted OR = 5.10; 95% CI: 2.59-10.02), and parental asthma (adjusted OR = 2.45; 95% CI: 1.19-5.04).

Conclusions

Palivizumab does not seem to protect against asthma development in preterm infants without congenital heart disease. A family history of atopy, parental asthma, and allergic rhinitis in the child seem to be the primary determinants of asthma risk in such infants.

title: Suspected Clinical Ellis-Yale-Winter Syndrome in an Infant With Unilateral Renal Agenesis, Contralateral Renal Ectopia, Microcephaly, and Congenital Heart Defects: A Case Report.
authorString: Tejeda MC, Garcia Gonzalez CA, Perez Santiago M, Somano Chaviano AD, Nunez Garcia JA.
abstractText: Ellis-Yale-Winter syndrome (EYWS) is an exceptionally rare multiple congenital anomaly syndrome characterized by microcephaly and congenital heart disease, variably associated with unilateral renal agenesis and abnormal pulmonary lobation. Its phenotype derives from a single original sibship, no validated diagnostic criteria exist, and no causative gene has been established. We report a male infant with congenital microcephaly, right renal agenesis with a contralateral ectopic solitary kidney, congenital heart defects, craniofacial dysmorphic features, and neurological abnormalities. The findings showed phenotypic overlap with the original cases, leading a multidisciplinary team to a suspected clinical diagnosis of EYWS. This diagnosis is not molecularly confirmed, as no genetic testing was performed. Pulmonary lobation and segmentation could not be assessed, which is a major limitation; their presence or absence cannot be inferred. The contralateral renal ectopia may represent a coincidental malformation or a hypothetical phenotypic variant. Long-term outcome and vital status are undetermined. This report does not establish new diagnostic features or an expanded phenotypic spectrum. Dedicated pulmonary imaging, exome or genome sequencing, DNA banking, and longitudinal follow-up are recommended in future cases.

title: Situs Inversus Totalis First Detected in the Third Trimester: Diagnostic Pitfalls in Routine Fetal Ultrasonography - A Case Report.
authorString: Malawat E, Setiyanto AB, Pribadi A, Handono B, Anwar AD.
abstractText:
Introduction

Situs inversus is a rare congenital condition characterized by a mirror-image reversal of thoracic and/or abdominal organs, with an estimated incidence of 1 in 10,000 live births. Although many individuals are asymptomatic, the condition is associated with congenital heart disease (CHD), and because a mirror-image heart may appear structurally normal, it can be overlooked at routine prenatal ultrasonography unless fetal laterality is determined first.

Case description

A 25-year-old primigravida was referred at 34-35 weeks of gestation for evaluation of fetal growth restriction; fetal situs inversus had not been identified at previous antenatal examinations. Ultrasonography showed the stomach on the right, the liver on the left, the descending aorta to the right of the spine and the inferior vena cava to the left, with the cardiac apex directed to the right. Fetal echocardiography confirmed atrial situs inversus with mirror-image dextrocardia and normal systemic and pulmonary venous return, without structural cardiac defects or features of heterotaxy. Doppler indices were normal, and the fetus was categorized as small for gestational age. The patient delivered a neonate weighing 2365 grams vaginally at 39 weeks and 4 days, and postnatal echocardiography confirmed mirror-image dextrocardia with normal intracardiac anatomy.

Conclusion

Isolated situs inversus totalis can remain undetected until the third trimester because each standard view of a mirror-image heart appears normal. Determining fetal laterality at the start of every obstetric scan, followed by detailed fetal echocardiography to exclude CHD and heterotaxy, consideration of genetic evaluation, and postnatal follow-up for primary ciliary dyskinesia, allows accurate counseling and appropriate perinatal planning.

title: Treatment of pulmonary hypertension in infants, children and young adults. 2026 consensus statement from the European Pediatric Pulmonary Vascular Disease Network (EPPVDN), endorsed by AHA, AEPC, EACTS, ESPR, PASCAR, PCS, and PICS.
authorString: Hansmann G, Idorn L, Melicoff E, Justino H, Anjos R, Bates A, Bobylev D, Budts W, Diekmann F, Hasan BS, Hasan H, Heath A, Maron BA, Mocumbi AO, Rahkonen O, Sajti E, Lucas SS, Brun H.

journal.title: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation

abstractText: The European Pediatric Pulmonary Vascular Disease Network (EPPVDN) is a registered, non-profit organization dedicated to advancing innovative diagnostic methods and treatment options for all forms of pediatric pulmonary vascular disease, including pulmonary hypertension (PH) related to congenital heart disease (CHD), PH associated with developmental lung disease (DEVLD-PH), persistent PH of the newborn (PPHN), postcapillary PH in left heart disease (PH-LHD), and associated cardiac dysfunction/heart failure. In the past, the EPPVDN has published consensus statements on the diagnosis and treatment of pediatric PH (2016, 2019), which have been endorsed by multiple societies. The executive writing group conducted comprehensive searches of the PubMed/MEDLINE bibliographic database (2000 to 2025) and engaged in multiple web-based and in-person meetings. Thirteen section task forces discussed and created consented recommendations. Prospective clinical studies, clinical trials, meta-analyses, expert consensus guidelines, and other articles with pediatric data were included in the search, using the terms 'pulmonary hypertension' and related keywords. Classes of recommendation (COR) and levels of evidence (LOE) were assigned based on AHA/ESC definitions, pediatric PH studies, adult studies including a minimum N number of 15 children, or studies involving adults with CHD. Classifications and definitions from the 7th World Symposium on Pulmonary Hypertension (WSPH) in 2024 were incorporated and discussed. We produced 6 graded recommendation tables (COR, LOE) and 3 algorithms for the treatment of pulmonary hypertension in infants, children, and young adults. A total of 16 main and 17 supplemental display items cover a range of topics, including risk assessment, pharmacological therapy, transcatheter interventions and surgery, recommendations specific to PH subgroups/special populations and clinical settings. Adaptation of management recommendations for middle-to-low-income regions is provided. Together, these up-to-date guidelines provide a comprehensive, detailed, and practical framework for the treatment of pulmonary hypertension in infants, children and young adults, aiming to improve outcomes and quality of life for affected patients.

title: Treatment of children and young adults with a Fontan circulation and cardiovascular dysfunction. 2026 Consensus Statement from the European Pediatric Pulmonary Vascular Disease Network (EPPVDN), endorsed by AHA, AEPC, EACTS, ISACHD, ISHLT and PICS.
authorString: Opotowsky AR, Allen KY, Chessa M, Crossland D, Grewal J, Hörer J, Karamlou T, Liuba P, Lorts A, Marsden A, Miyamoto SD, Smith CL, Bruaene AV, Voges I, Hansmann G.

journal.title: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation

abstractText: The Fontan operation enables long term survival for many individuals born with single ventricle heart disease, but the resulting circulation imposes a lifelong hemodynamic burden and predisposes to cardiovascular dysfunction and multisystem morbidity. Evidence based guidance for assessment and management of Fontan specific cardiac and vascular dysfunction, however, remains limited. The European Pediatric Pulmonary Vascular Disease Network (EPPVDN) convened an international, multidisciplinary executive writing group to review the available literature and develop consensus recommendations addressing cardiovascular dysfunction in children and young adults with a Fontan circulation. Recommendations were graded using established Class of Recommendation and Level of Evidence criteria adapted to the Fontan specific evidence base. The statement addresses cardiovascular assessment, pulmonary vascular disease and use of pulmonary vasodilator therapy, Fontan pathway obstruction, systemic venous and arterial abnormalities and collateral vessels, lymphatic dysfunction and intervention, myocardial dysfunction and heart failure therapy, and thromboembolic risk and antithrombotic therapy. The focus is on phenotype-guided management, hemodynamically informed treatment decisions, and medical, transcatheter, and surgical approaches tailored to Fontan circulation. Seven graded recommendation tables as well as a flowchart for considerations regarding pulmonary vasodilator therapy are provided to support clinical decision making. Fontan-specific evidence remains limited, so many recommendations necessarily represent expert opinion. This EPPVDN consensus statement, therefore, discusses knowledge gaps and priorities for collaborative research to improve outcomes for individuals living with a Fontan circulation.

title: Transpulmonary Atrial Pacemaker Implantation in Fontan Circulation With Bilateral Glenn.
authorString: Dávila Ruales A, Ramírez Barrera JD, Agudelo Uribe JF, Zapata Sánchez MM, Ocampo Aristizábal LA, Correa Velásquez R.
abstractText:
Background

Patients with Fontan circulation frequently develop atrial arrhythmias and sinus node dysfunction. Atrial pacing is challenging because conventional transvenous access is limited by complex Fontan anatomy.

Case summary

A 20-year-old man with dextroisomerism, bilateral Glenn anastomoses, and Fontan circulation presented with symptomatic sinus node dysfunction and recurrent supraventricular tachycardia. A transpulmonary transvenous approach achieved endocardial atrial lead implantation with excellent pacing parameters. Despite optimized medical therapy, heart failure progressed, and the patient died during transplant evaluation.

Discussion

This case highlights the technical feasibility of transpulmonary endocardial atrial pacing as an alternative to repeat epicardial surgery in selected patients with Fontan circulation. Careful procedural planning, multimodality imaging, and individualized assessment of long-term anticoagulation are important considerations. Despite arrhythmia control, optimized therapy and restoration of atrioventricular synchrony may not prevent heart failure progression, which may be irreversible.

Take-home messages

Transpulmonary endocardial atrial pacing is a feasible alternative in carefully selected Patients with Fontan circulation. Sudden cardiac death risk stratification remains limited in this study group.

title: Recurrent Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis With Aortic Root Abscess in Fontan Circulation: Navigating a Complex Dilemma.
authorString: Wahba A, Said SM.
abstractText:
Background

Prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE) in patients with Fontan physiology represents a formidable challenge, with limited data to guide management.

Case summary

We report a 30-year-old woman with tricuspid atresia status post-Fontan palliation who previously underwent aortic valve replacement for endocarditis. She presented with recurrent PVE complicated by sepsis, multiorgan failure, and embolic stroke. Echocardiography revealed a 2.2-cm mobile vegetation and aortic root abscess. Following completion of antibiotic therapy and neurological recovery, she underwent a fifth redo sternotomy. A Bentall procedure with reconstruction of the aortomitral curtain was performed using a bioprosthetic valved conduit. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 5 and, at 6-month follow-up, echocardiography demonstrated normal prosthetic valve function.

Discussion

This case illustrates the feasibility and efficacy of complex aortic root surgery in patients with Fontan with recurrent PVE. It underscores the critical importance of multidisciplinary planning, individualized surgical strategy, and optimal timing of intervention to achieve favorable outcomes in this high-risk population.

title: Transvenous Coil Implant in a Patient With Lateral Tunnel Fontan: The Route Less Traveled.
authorString: Fuentes Rojas SC, Rothstein PA, Chao MF, Duarte VE, Monteiro GA, Lin CH, Dave AS.
abstractText:
Background

Ventricular arrhythmias occur in approximately 11% of patients who undergo Fontan palliation. Sudden cardiac death, presumably from ventricular arrhythmia, accounts for approximately 10%-20% of the overall mortality among these patients. Implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) implantation in these patients is challenging because of limited transvenous access to the subpulmonary ventricle.

Case summary

A 41-year-old woman who underwent Fontan palliation later developed complete heart block and underwent epicardial pacemaker implantation at the age of 36 years. She developed symptomatic ventricular tachycardia and worsening heart failure with planned heart/lung transplant listing. She was considered to be at prohibitive risk for epicardial defibrillator and failed subcutaneous ICD screening. We describe a transvenous ICD upgrade using a hemiazygos vein coil, inframammary generator, and lead extenders for existing epicardial leads.

Discussion

This case highlights the feasibility of hemiazygos vein coil placement in combination with an inframammary generator pocket in selected patients with Fontan.

Take-home message

The hemiazygos vein may be a viable option for transvenous coil placement in these patients.

title: Global Prognostic Impact of Substance Use in Alcohol-Associated Hepatitis.
authorString: Albhaisi O, Idalsoaga F, Wang W, Araujo RC, Fontanini GM, Valsan A, Nair G, Alcayaga B, Arnold J, Ayala-Valverde M, Ramirez-Cadiz C, Blaney H, Jahagirdar V, Gu H, Rhoads SF, Parraga X, Fakhoury B, Jalal PK, Ibrahim MA, Elfeki MA, Roblero JP, Simian D, Velasco JAV, Córdova J, Higuera-de-la-Tijera F, Silva R, Rocha CM, Pereira GH, Bessone F, Tanno M, Kisch A, Mendizabal M, Marciano S, Perdiguero GG, Montes P, Salazar PG, Ramos G, Carrera E, Haque L, Chacko KR, Skladaný L, Sanyal AJ, Shah VH, Kamath PS, Arrese M, Dunn W, Singal AK, Bataller R, Díaz LA, Arab JP.
abstractText:
Background and aims

Alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) carries high short-term mortality. Although concomitant substance use is common in patients with AH, its impact on clinical outcomes remains unclear. We aimed to determine the prevalence of active substance use and evaluate its association with clinical outcomes in a large, multinational cohort of hospitalized patients with AH.

Methods

We conducted a prospective, multicenter study across 38 centers in 13 countries (2015-2024). Adults meeting National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism (NIAAA) criteria for AH were enrolled. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality stratified by substance use. Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models were used to identify mortality predictors, with liver transplantation (LT) treated as a competing event.

Results

We included 814 patients, with a mean age of 49.5 ± 10.6 years, and 88.8% were male. Active cannabis and cocaine use were reported in 6.1% and 5.5%, respectively. Over follow-up, 210 patients (25.8%) died, and 35 (4.3%) underwent LT. In multivariable analysis, active cannabis use independently predicted higher mortality (sHR 2.49, 95% CI 1.52-4.09; p < 0.001), along with higher MELD scores and ACLF grades 2-3. Corticosteroid therapy (sHR 0.57, 95% CI 0.38-0.85; p = 0.007) and higher educational levels (sHR 0.34 and 0.31 for intermediate and highest categories, respectively) were associated with improved survival.

Conclusions

Active substance use-particularly cannabis use-was independently associated with increased mortality in patients hospitalized with AH, even after adjusting for liver disease severity and accounting for transplantation as a competing event. These findings identify a behavioral dimension of AH severity and highlight the need to integrate addiction medicine and psychiatric care into hepatology practice to improve outcomes.

title: Hemodynamic Challenges After Paraganglioma Resection in Fontan-Palliated Adult With Fontan-Associated Liver Disease.
authorString: Gupta JR, Modi R, Kerling D, Liu B, Subramanyam P, Yuan S, Finnerty B, Dobri G, McDonald D, Brandman D, Singh HS.
abstractText:
Background

Chronic hypoxemia in cyanotic congenital heart disease is associated with increased risk of pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma (PPGL), particularly among patients with single-ventricle physiology.

Case summary

A 26-year-old man with unbalanced atrioventricular septal defect and extracardiac Fontan palliation, and Fontan-associated liver disease presented with hypertensive crisis, with imaging evidence of PPGL. The patient underwent robotic right adrenalectomy and nodule resection complicated by high-volume chylous ascites for several weeks.

Discussion

Chronic hypoxemia in cyanotic congenital heart disease, particularly univentricular physiology, is a well-established driver of PPGL. Existing guidelines mandate preoperative α-blockade and volume expansion for functional PPGL, but this approach is not tailored to Fontan physiology.

Take-home messages

We present a rare case of operative disruption of retroperitoneal lymphatics superimposed on Fontan-associated systemic venous and lymphatic congestion. Right heart catheterization, cautious α-blockade with volume expansion, and multidisciplinary perioperative management are essential to balance catecholamine blockade against the risks of venous congestion, lymphatic failure, bleeding, and thrombosis.

title: Challenges of Fontan Completion in Bilateral Bidirectional Glenn: A Patient-Specific Computational Comparison of Conduit Options.
authorString: Shah I, Natarajan T, Iannucci GJ, John MM, Shashidharan S, Dasi LP, Slesnick TC.
abstractText:
Background

Bilateral bidirectional Glenn (BDG) anatomies present a distinct challenge for Fontan completion, with bilateral superior caval inflow creating competitive flow dynamics that impair balanced hepatic flow delivery.

Case summary

A 3-year-old with hypoplastic left heart syndrome and bilateral BDG underwent patient-specific computational surgical planning before Fontan completion. Six virtual surgical options, including an extracardiac conduit (ECC) and Y-graft variants with and without bilateral superior vena cava (SVC) bridging, were evaluated, with hepatic flow distribution (HFD) and power loss as primary endpoints.

Discussion

Although its baseline HFD was unbalanced, the ECC demonstrated the most consistent HFD response across simulated physiological states. By contrast, Y-graft performance was highly sensitive to arm placement. Bilateral SVC anastomosis improved HFD but introduced low-velocity stagnant flow, raising concerns for thrombosis.

Take-home messages

In bilateral BDG Fontan planning, computational modeling revealed nonintuitive flow interactions not predictable from anatomy alone. The ECC was selected for surgical robustness, whereas SVC bridging warrants further investigation.

title: Fontan-Associated Liver Disease: A Novel Strategy to Assess Hepatic Reserve.
authorString: Zhyvytsia Y, Kurkevych A, Teterin O, Kvilinska O, Moshkivska L, Olkhovich N.
abstractText:
Background

Evaluating Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD) remains challenging, as elastography reflects passive congestion and standard biochemistry often remains normal. We explore transient hepatic metabolic reserve exhaustion during hemodynamic and dietary stress.

Case summary

An asymptomatic 10-year-old boy who had undergone Fontan completion presented for routine evaluation coinciding with an unusually large mixed meal. Dried blood spot amino acid profiling by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry revealed marked hypercitrullinemia (188.9 μmol/L) with elevated ornithine and arginine, whereas shear-wave elastography peaked at 18.1 kPa and systemic ventricular ejection fraction transiently fell to 52%; standard liver biochemistry remained normal. Amino acids normalized within 5 days, with partial recovery of liver stiffness and ejection fraction at 3-month follow-up.

Discussion

Hemodynamic impairment combined with acute dietary stress can transiently exhaust hepatic metabolic reserve before conventional biochemical tests turn abnormal.

Take-home message

Dried blood spot amino acid profiling is a promising noninvasive tool to unmask subclinical metabolic reserve exhaustion in Fontan-associated liver disease when standard liver enzymes are normal.

title: An Acute Coronary Event in a Patient With Fontan Circulation During Pregnancy.
authorString: Freddo AM, Ziadi MC, Ruckdeschel ES, Kim YY, Partington S, Vaikunth SS.
abstractText:
Background

There is a growing number of adults living with Fontan circulation who are pursuing pregnancy.

Case summary

We report a case of a woman with Fontan physiology and pregnancy who had sudden onset chest pain, ST-segment changes, and troponin elevation with coinciding echocardiographic and magnetic resonance imaging changes consistent with myocardial injury from likely paradoxical coronary embolism.

Discussion

Patients with Fontan circulation are at increased thrombotic risk, which is further exacerbated by pregnancy. However, there are limited data regarding appropriate thromboprophylaxis in these patients, especially because there is also a significant bleeding risk.

Take-home message

This case highlights the complexity of decision-making regarding diagnosis of coronary events in patients with Fontan circulation, as well as challenges determining ideal thromboprophylaxis in these patients during pregnancy.

title: Transvenous Atrial Pacing Via Extracardiac Conduit Fenestration of Fontan Patient With Situs Inversus Totalis.
authorString: Nguyen Xuan T, Nguyen Quoc H, Pham Nhu H, Le Van N, Nguyen Van D, Pham Van T, Nguyen The Nam H, Citra I.
abstractText:
Objective

To describe a stepwise technique for transvenous atrial pacing in a patient with situs inversus totalis and a fenestrated extracardiac (EC) Fontan circulation.

Key steps

Preprocedural caval venography to identify the cavopulmonary anastomoses, EC conduit, and fenestration. A telescopic catheter technique using a 7-F peel-away introducer as the outer sheath, the 5-F pigtail catheter as the inner catheter, and a hydrophilic 0.035-inch guidewire to access the fenestration. Advancement of the 7-F introducer across the fenestration and deployment of an atrial lead in the right atrium.

Potential pitfalls

Cavopulmonary anastomoses can be noncoaxial; a femoral snare can help with advancement of the telescopic system. In older Fontan patients, a longer peel-away introducer may be required to reach the EC conduit.

Take-home messages

Preprocedural caval venography helps identify the optimal route for lead delivery. A telescopic catheter technique facilitates fenestration access and advancement of the pacing lead.

title: Imaging-Guided Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation in an Adult Patient With Fontan Circulation.
authorString: Tarantini R, Bosch L, van der Zwaan H, Loh P, Kassenberg W, Fernandez SS, Guglielmo M, Hendriks A.
abstractText:
Background

Ventricular arrhythmias are an emerging cause of late morbidity in adults with Fontan circulation, yet catheter ablation strategies in this anatomically complex population remain poorly defined.

Case summary

A 25-year-old woman with tricuspid atresia palliated by total cavopulmonary connection presented with sustained ventricular tachycardia. Cardiac magnetic resonance showed circumferential subendocardial fibrosis in the right ventricular outflow tract. Imaging-guided catheter ablation was performed. The cardiac magnetic resonance-defined scar was targeted, abolishing local abnormal ventricular activities. The patient remained arrhythmia-free at the 12-month follow-up.

Discussion

Multimodality imaging facilitated a substrate-based ablation strategy by overcoming the anatomical and hemodynamic constraints inherent to single-ventricle physiology.

Take-home messages

Multimodality imaging is essential for ventricular tachycardia substrate characterization in Fontan patients. Right ventricular outflow tract fibrosis may represent the arrhythmogenic substrate even within the rudimentary right ventricle.

title: Refractory Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding as an Unusual Manifestation of Fontan Failure.
authorString: Pomiato E, Mori B, Avesani M, Cuppini E, Prati F, Reffo E, Cerutti A, Castaldi B, Biffanti R, Di Salvo G.
abstractText:
Background

Chronic venous congestion is an expected consequence of Fontan palliation. In rare cases, hemorrhage arises from congested hemorrhoidal or colonic venous plexuses.

Case summary

A 48-year-old man with Fontan palliation presented with massive rectal bleeding causing severe anemia. Colonoscopy and computed tomography angiography excluded malignancy. Repeated mesenteric embolizations provided only transient benefit. As rescue therapy, medical therapy was uptitrated and Fontan fenestration was re-created percutaneously using an atrial flow regulator, preventing further major bleeding at 5 months.

Discussion

As the Fontan population ages, previously underrecognized mechanisms of failure become evident, requiring tailored strategies to restore the "optimal Fontan hemodynamic," the balance between systemic oxygenation and venous congestion being remarkably fragile in advanced Fontan states.

Take-home messages

Fontan failure requires individualized, pathophysiology-driven management. Novel medical and interventional treatments may be useful in selected Fontan patients, as a calibrated fenestration may balance oxygenation against venous decompression and improve end-organ stability.

title: Kidney Transplantation in an Adult With a Fontan Circulation: Targeting Renal Perfusion Pressure.
authorString: Arista P, Busque S, Oakes D, Jackson E, Lui GK, Clark DE, Haeffele C, Romfh A, Mohamed MA, Woo JP.
abstractText:
Background

Dialysis is poorly tolerated in Fontan circulation because of preload-dependent maintenance of cardiac output in the face of passive pulmonary circulation. Evidence that Fontan cardiac output can support kidney-only transplantation remains limited.

Case summary

A 24-year-old woman with situs inversus, congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries, pulmonary atresia, and ventricular septal defect palliated with a fenestrated lateral tunnel Fontan developed stage 5 chronic kidney disease from immune-complex glomerulonephritis. Multidisciplinary evaluation supported preemptive kidney-only transplantation based on preserved ventricular function and stable mixed venous oxygen saturation (60%-63%). She remained dialysis-free with excellent 6-month allograft function (creatinine 1.03 mg/dL).

Discussion

Perioperative management targeting renal perfusion pressure (mean arterial pressure minus central venous pressure ≥55-60 mm Hg), maintaining near-baseline Fontan pressures, and using mixed venous oxygen saturation-guided assessment supported immediate graft function.

Take-home messages

In carefully selected patients with Fontan circulation without evidence of Fontan failure, optimization guided by mean arterial pressure minus central venous pressure may enable kidney-only transplantation, avoiding higher-risk heart-kidney transplantation.

title: Junctional Rhythm and Atrial Ectopy Presenting as Chronic Abdominal Pain in Fontan Circulation.
authorString: Campens L, Schmidt MR, Jøns C.
abstractText:
Background

Rhythm disturbances may contribute to clinically significant hemodynamic compromise in patients with Fontan circulation, even without overt Fontan failure.

Case summary

A 32-year-old woman with double-inlet left ventricle and total cavopulmonary connection presented with years of debilitating abdominal pain resulting in marked functional limitation. Extensive abdominal, hepatic, lymphatic, and cardiac investigations failed to identify a cause. Holter monitoring demonstrated predominant junctional rhythm and frequent atrial ectopy, whereas cardiopulmonary exercise testing revealed heart rate-dependent restoration of sinus rhythm with suppression of atrial ectopy. Invasive assessment showed that temporary atrial pacing suppressed ectopy and improved Fontan hemodynamics. Following AAIR pacemaker implantation, abdominal pain resolved completely and functional capacity improved.

Discussion

This case illustrates that rhythm-related hemodynamic compromise may present with atypical extracardiac symptoms despite reassuring conventional investigations.

Take-home message

Chronic abdominal pain in patients with Fontan circulation may reflect arrhythmia-related hemodynamic compromise despite apparently stable Fontan physiology.

title: Ascending Aorta Dilation in the Fontan: To Intervene or Not.
authorString: Herron C, Hsia TY, Briston D.
abstractText:
Background

Ascending aorta dilation is a known finding in the congenital heart disease population and specifically in patients who have undergone single ventricle palliation.

Case summary

We present 3 patients with single ventricle physiology who underwent single ventricle palliations and had severe ascending aorta dilation.

Why beyond the guidelines

Guidelines for the management of these patients are lacking, and decisions are made on a case-by-case basis.

Discussion

There are case reports of aortic dissection, but true risk remains unknown. Weighing the risks of surgery versus conservative management in patients with single ventricle physiology is challenging.

Take-home message

Surgical intervention on dilated aortas in patients with single ventricle physiology is perilous but possible in the correct circumstances.

title: VA-ECMO Bridge to Transplant in Acute Fontan Circulatory Failure: A Transpulmonary Gradient-Guided Approach to Weaning.
authorString: Joseph A, Tan W, Truby L, Shafer K, Murala J, Brickner ME, Wrobel C, Jawaid A, Peltz M, Kearney K.
abstractText:
Background

Little is known about strategies for managing adults with Fontan circulation who require temporary mechanical circulatory support.

Case summary

A 33-year-old woman with Fontan circulation presented with syncope and was found to have Fontan conduit stenosis with low cardiac output. The patient developed hemodynamic collapse during catheter-based intervention, necessitating veno-arterial extracorporeal circulatory membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) cannulation. She was supported by VA-ECMO and was successfully bridged to heart transplantation after 11 days of support.

Discussion

In a patient with acute Fontan circulatory failure, temporary mechanical support with VA-ECMO and a Fontan-tailored approach to ramp trial and weaning studies ultimately led to informed clinical decision-making and bridge to successful heart transplant.

Take-home messages

VA-ECMO can be used for temporary mechanical circulatory support in acute Fontan failure. Patients with Fontan circulation on VA-ECMO require careful management, with a thoughtful approach to hemodynamics given the circuit's unique physiology.

title: Junctional Rhythm Associated With Multilevel Flow Reversal in a Well-Functioning Fontan Detected by 4-Dimensional Flow.
authorString: Erdem S, Siddiqui S, Gunda R, Thai L, Greil FG, Reddy SV, Bano M, Zou Q, Hussain T, Alsaied T.
abstractText:
Background

Flow reversal in Fontan circulation is highly associated with Fontan circulatory failure and adverse hemodynamics.

Case summary

A 12-year-old boy with hypoplastic left heart syndrome with an extracardiac fenestrated Fontan circuit underwent routine cardiovascular magnetic resonance surveillance. Phase-contrast and 4-dimensional flow imaging demonstrated late-systolic-to-early-diastolic flow reversal throughout the Fontan circuit and across the fenestration. The patient had no Fontan pathway obstruction, significant atrioventricular valve regurgitation, or ventricular dysfunction. Electrocardiography demonstrated a junctional rhythm (JR).

Discussion

JR is common after Fontan palliation and causes atrioventricular dyssynchrony. This case highlights chronic JR as a potential cause of multilevel flow reversal despite otherwise favorable Fontan anatomy and preserved ventricular function, expanding the differential diagnosis of flow reversal in patients with Fontan circulation.

Take-home message

Advanced flow imaging may provide unique mechanistic insights into rhythm-related hemodynamic disturbances and improve the interpretation of Fontan flow patterns.

title: Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection of an Anomalous LAD in an Adult With Fontan Palliation.
authorString: Scandinaro AL, Wang L, Huber M, Rosado M, Smith B, Cox D.
abstractText:
Background

Evaluating chest pain in patients with Fontan palliation can be a daunting task given the spectrum of pathology, surgical history, and multisystem involvement.

Case summary

A 32-year-old man with double inlet left ventricle status post-Fontan palliation was transferred to our facility with 3 days of chest pain, dyspnea, and a sense of impending doom. An electrocardiogram and troponin trend were consistent with an acute coronary syndrome. Coronary angiography revealed 100% occlusion of the mid-left anterior descending with a linear lucency and intramural hematoma consistent with spontaneous coronary artery dissection type IV. He underwent cutting balloon angioplasty and was discharged on antiplatelet therapy and follow-up imaging to assess for fibromuscular dysplasia.

Discussion

Chest pain is common among patients with congenital heart disease (CHD). Knowledge regarding spontaneous coronary artery dissection in the CHD spectrum is limited. Chest pain differentials for patients with CHD should include evaluation for acquired conditions, particularly as this population ages.

title: Recalibration of Invasive Hemodynamic Monitoring Devices on Serial Catheterization in Adults With Fontan Circulation.
authorString: Freddo AM, Salavitabar A, Blais B, Armstrong AK, Daniels CJ, Marshall V WH.
abstractText:
Background

There are limited data on long-term accuracy of invasive hemodynamic monitoring (IHM) in patients with nonpulsatile Fontan circulation (FC).

First-in-human/early reports summary

In a retrospective review of 20 patients with FC and CardioMEMS IHM implanted (2015-2025), simultaneous IHM and invasive mean pulmonary artery pressure measurements were available during 6 repeat catheterizations in 6 patients. IHM readings were nearly all lower than invasive measurements, with the absolute difference ranging from 1 to 10 mm Hg.

Discussion/novelty

There are limited reports of recalibration data with IHM, and to our knowledge this is the first report of simultaneous IHM and invasive measurement in adults with FC. IHM accuracy is important with FC as small pressure differences can greatly affect physiology.

Take-home messages

IHM can provide outpatient pulmonary artery pressure measurements in patients with FC. Because we find discrepancy in device measurements in our cohort, we recommend recalibration with each hemodynamic catheterization in this population.

title: Spontaneous Closure of Pulmonary Arteriovenous Fistulas After a Modified Fontan Surgery.
authorString: Lv R, Dong A, Lin X, Jing X, Zhang X, Tian C, Wei ZA, Qiao B.
abstractText:
Background

This case report discusses a 9-year spontaneous closure of pulmonary arteriovenous fistulas (PAVFs) after a Fontan procedure in a patient with a single ventricle.

Case summary

An 18-year-old female patient developed PAVFs after a Glenn procedure in infancy and underwent a total cavopulmonary connection with a 12-mm conduit at age 9. PAVFs remained evident at 1 year of age postoperatively, but multimodal imaging (catheterization, cardiac magnetic resonance, and echocardiography) at 9 years showed complete resolution, with SpO2 96%, mean pulmonary artery pressure 10 to 11 mm Hg, and normal ventricular function.

Discussion

This is the first case of imaging-documented delayed closure of PAVFs up to 9 years following the Fontan procedure, supporting the hepatic factor hypothesis (hepatic venous flow inhibits angiogenesis). The small conduit may have balanced perfusion and thrombosis risk, allowing adaptive flow optimization.

Take-home messages

Delayed spontaneous closure of PAVFs can occur years after undergoing a Fontan procedure. Comprehensive multimodal imaging is essential for guiding management in patients with congenital heart disease.

title: Incidental Hepatocellular Carcinoma on Explant Pathology in Patients With Fontan Circulation After Heart-Liver Transplantation.
authorString: Farkas IZ, Weinfurtner K, Olthoff KM, Abt PL, Kaldas FM, Rosen MA, Lluri G, Rychik J, Hoteit MA, Kim YY.
abstractText: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is an increasingly recognized complication of Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD), yet diagnosis remains challenging. We describe 4 patients with Fontan circulation in whom HCC was identified incidentally on explant pathology following combined heart-liver transplantation (CHLT). All patients underwent transplantation for Fontan circulatory failure and had hepatic lesions identified on surveillance imaging that were indeterminate for HCC with normal alpha-fetoprotein levels. Explant pathology revealed well- or moderately differentiated HCC in all cases. Among the 3 patients who survived transplantation, none have experienced recurrence to date. These cases highlight the limitations of current surveillance strategies in a subset of patients with FALD referred for CHLT. Further studies are needed to develop imaging criteria and biomarkers specifically validated for FALD-HCC.

title: Hemoptysis After Fontan Palliation: A 32-Year Single-Center Experience.
authorString: Oribe RJ, Marengo AA, Pasinato C, Mouratian DM, Lafuente MV.
abstractText:
Background

Hemoptysis is an uncommon but potentially severe complication after Fontan palliation.

Case summary

We retrospectively reviewed 453 patients with Fontan circulation who were evaluated between 1991 and 2023. Thirteen (2.8%) developed hemoptysis, and 9 of those (69%) had recurrent bleeding, accounting for 45 episodes. Twelve patients underwent 28 catheterizations with embolization of 132 aortopulmonary collaterals. Hemoptysis occurred in 3 of 50 patients with right atrial isomerism (6.0%) versus 10 of 403 without it (2.5%; P = 0.164, Fisher exact test). Four patients received inhaled desmopressin with a clinically observed temporary reduction in bleeding. One patient died from massive hemorrhage.

Discussion

Recurrent bleeding and repeated interventions were common, while right atrial isomerism was not significantly associated with hemoptysis.

Take-home message

Hemoptysis after Fontan palliation may recur despite embolization, supporting repeated evaluation and long-term surveillance.

title: Catheter-Based Selective Pulmonary Artery Digital Subtraction Angiography and Microvascular Reserve Quantification in Fontan Patient.
authorString: Juaneda I, Contreras A, Oyola J, Capdevila MS, Juárez F, Peirone A, Kreutzer C, Tabares A, Juaneda E.
abstractText:
Background

Fontan circulation allows univentricular congenital heart physiology to survive. Pulmonary microvascular images are poorly described in live patients during follow-up.

Case summary

A 25-year-old man with a diagnosis of tricuspid atresia status after extracardiac fenestrated Fontan surgery performed at 3 years of age, followed by fenestration device closure a year later, and with a history of hemoptysis at 9 years of age. Follow-up was performed through cardiac catheterization with selective pulmonary artery (PA) digital subtraction angiography (DSA). A decreased percentage of microvascular reserve associated with increased D-dimer suggested in situ thrombosis, and thromboprophylaxis was switched from aspirin to direct oral anticoagulation.

Discussion

We focus on catheter-based PA DSA microvascular reserve percentage, cardiopulmonary exercise test, and D-dimer quantification to generate evidence of in situ microvascular thrombosis.

Take-home message

Catheter-based PA DSA revealing reduced microvascular reserve may identify in situ microvascular thrombosis and offer a novel pathophysiological insight in patients with Fontan circulation during follow-up.

title: Cardiac CT in a Criss-Cross Heart With Double-Outlet Right Ventricle Guiding Single-Ventricle Palliation.
authorString: Răzvan-Andrei L, Liliana G, Gheorghe-Marian R, Kincső-Zsófia L, Anca-Maria D, Anca B, Sabin-Christoph MG, Liviu M, Marian P.
abstractText:
Background

Criss-cross heart with double-outlet right ventricle (DORV) and dual discordance is a rare phenotype challenging the conventional echocardiographic segmental characterization.

Case summary

An infant with prenatally diagnosed complex congenital heart disease had functionally univentricular physiology, severe pulmonary stenosis, and large septal defects. Echocardiography suggested double-inlet left ventricle with transposed great arteries but incompletely defined segmental anatomy and pulmonary arteries. Electrocardiographically gated cardiac computed tomography (CT) angiography established criss-cross atrioventricular relationships with clockwise ventricular rotation, straddling tricuspid valve, DORV from a mildly hypoplastic morphologic right ventricle, severe subpulmonary/pulmonary annular obstruction, confluent pulmonary arteries, single coronary artery pattern, and patent ductus arteriosus, supporting staged single-ventricle palliation.

Discussion

CT provided the segmental and vascular roadmap for staged palliation.

Take-home messages

Criss-cross heart with DORV and dual discordance frequently precludes biventricular repair, directing single-ventricle planning. CT is pivotal pre and postoperatively, defining pulmonary artery eligibility for cavopulmonary connection and confirming the substrate for Fontan completion.

title: Transvenous Atrial Pacing Using Subclavian 3-Dimensional Electroanatomical Mapping in Lateral Tunnel Fontan With Sinus Arrest.
authorString: John KJ, Quintero E, Thaler C, Lloyd MS.
abstractText:
Background

Bradyarrhythmias are common late complications after Fontan palliation. Transvenous pacing avoids the high-risk redo sternotomy required for epicardial leads but is technically challenging because of extensive surgical atrial scarring and low-voltage tissue.

Case summary

A 39-year-old woman with a lateral tunnel Fontan and severe aortic regurgitation presented with heart failure secondary to bradyarrhythmia and sinus arrest. Using subclavian access, 3-dimensional electroanatomical mapping identified a discrete, viable island of native atrial tissue within an otherwise electrically inert baffle. A transvenous active-fixation pacemaker lead was successfully implanted at this site, restoring stable 1:1 atrioventricular conduction.

Discussion

This case demonstrates that electroanatomical mapping can locate viable atrial tissue and guide lead implantation in complex Fontan atrial substrates. This technique allows for rapid identification of target lead implant sites through a single access point from the pacer pocket.

Take-home messages

Three-dimensional mapping enables successful transvenous pacing in highly scarred Fontan atria. This technique allows for mapping and lead placement via the same surgical site.

title: Fontan Baffle Failure Signaled by Neurologic Events and Worsening Cyanosis: Transcatheter Vs Surgical Repair.
authorString: Bianco C, Abis A, Borzillo I, Micheletti A, Torchio F, Varrica A, D'Aiello F, Giamberti A, Chessa M.
abstractText:
Background

As the Fontan population ages, follow-up care and attention to quality of life become increasingly complex, requiring a multidisciplinary approach. In this context, cyanosis in patients with an intra-atrial Fontan tunnel may be a signal of structural intracardiac baffle failure associated with clinical deterioration.

Case summary

The patients were two 35-year-old adults with fenestrated intra-atrial Fontan circulation in whom neurologic events preceded recognition of worsening desaturation. In the first patient, a focal defect of the inferior caval patch associated with neurologic events, was closed percutaneously with an occluder device. In the second patient, extensive tunnel dehiscence required surgical revision with the creation of a calibrated fenestration.

Discussion

These cases underscore the importance of thoroughly investigating progressive desaturation in patients with Fontan circulation, as identifying and treating the cause is essential to optimize clinical outcomes.

Take-home messages

Late Fontan worsening desaturation requires diagnostic investigation. Discriminating focal leak from dehiscence within the tunnel is crucial for treatment strategies.

title: Successful Repair of Giant Aortic Aneurysm With Severe Aortic Regurgitation in Fontan Patient.
authorString: Mitropoulos F, Zioga A, Vlahos A, Pappas K, Apostolidis C, Tzifa A.
abstractText:
Background

Progressive aortic root dilation in patients with Fontan circulation requires vigilant monitoring to ensure timely surgical intervention.

Case summary

A 41-year-old patient with Fontan circulation (tricuspid atresia, large ventricular septal defect, situs inversus totalis) presented on NYHA functional class II. Echocardiography and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging confirmed severe aortic regurgitation with 8.1-cm ascending aortic aneurysm and impaired function. He underwent a modified Bentall and bilateral Cabrol procedure using 30-mm tube graft, 27-mm mechanical valve, and coronary conduits. Despite a challenging postoperative course requiring temporary intra-aortic balloon pump, he recovered well with improved ventricular function.

Discussion

Aortic root dilation is a recognized late complication in single-ventricle physiology. This is the first report of surgical repair of a giant aortic aneurysm with severe regurgitation and impaired function in mirror-image Fontan anatomy. This case highlights how modified graft techniques overcome extreme surgical constraints.

Take-home message

A modified Bentall-Cabrol procedure can successfully repair giant aneurysms in Fontan anatomy.

title: Emergency Percutaneous Thromboembolectomy in an Adult With Fontan Circulation.
authorString: Vignaud-Marighetto P, Karsenty C, Ly R, Combes N.
abstractText:
Background

Thromboembolic complications remain a major source of morbidity in patients with Fontan circulation, particularly in older atriopulmonary connections with atrial arrhythmias.

Case summary

A 54-year-old man with tricuspid atresia and Fontan circulation presented with acute hypoxemia and chest pain after diagnosis of a large right atrial thrombus. Imaging confirmed embolization into the pulmonary artery. Considering a future heart transplantation strategy, the multidisciplinary team opted for percutaneous thrombectomy rather than surgery. The procedure resulted in rapid clinical improvement without complications.

Discussion

This case highlights the complexity of thromboembolism management in Fontan patients and illustrates the feasibility of percutaneous thrombectomy as a bridge-to-transplant strategy in selected patients.

Take-home message

Percutaneous thrombectomy may represent an effective option for acute pulmonary embolism in selected Fontan patients.

title: Successful Fontan Completion in a 36-Year-Old: A Durable Glenn.
authorString: Gormley M, Allen KY, Monge M.
abstractText:
Background

Fontan palliation is commonly completed at 2-4 years, but delays may occur due to medical optimization and, rarely, loss to follow-up.

Case summary

A 36-year-old woman with tricuspid atresia status post-bidirectional Glenn presented with significant exercise intolerance and hypoxemia. She had lived over 2 decades with Glenn physiology and successfully carried 2 pregnancies. The patient ultimately underwent fenestrated Fontan completion with significant functional improvement.

Discussion

This case represents an exceptionally prolonged duration of Glenn physiology, demonstrating that this palliation can be highly durable in select patients with favorable anatomy and hemodynamics. Fontan completion in this patient resulted in meaningful functional improvement, though it remains a temporizing measure that carries substantial risks and potential long-term morbidity.

Take-home messages

Glenn palliation can be durable in select patients. Fontan completion may meaningfully improve function well beyond the conventional 2-to-4-year age window, and timing should be patient-specific.

title: Mechanical Hemolysis After Fontan Fenestration Closure: An Unrecognized Complication.
authorString: Abed M, Fitzgerald N.
abstractText:
Background

Mechanical hemolysis following transcatheter device closure is uncommon and is typically associated with a residual high-velocity shunt. Hemolysis after Fontan fenestration closure has not been previously reported.

Case summary

A 7-year-old boy with single-ventricle physiology underwent elective transcatheter Fontan fenestration closure, complicated by hematuria the following day. Laboratory evaluation confirmed nonimmune intravascular hemolysis. Echocardiography demonstrated a well-positioned device without residual shunt but with an atrioventricular valve regurgitant jet directed toward the device. Conservative management was pursued, with biochemical surveillance, folic acid, and iron supplementation. Device removal was not required.

Discussion
