Device-related hemolysis is classically attributed to residual shunting. Described herein is hemolysis caused by regurgitant jet collision with a nonendothelialized device. Conservative management is appropriate in stable patients, as given expected resolution with device endothelialization.

Take-home messages

Hematuria after Fontan fenestration closure should raise suspicion for mechanical hemolysis, even without residual shunt. Early recognition is essential in Fontan patients and warrants earlier supportive intervention given limited cardiopulmonary reserve.

title: A Successful Fontan Completion for Asplenia Syndrome Complicated by a Hiatal Hernia.
authorString: Hataoka T, Yamamoto Y, Okamura T.
abstractText:
Background

Hiatal hernia (HH) in patients with a functional single ventricle can increase pulmonary vascular resistance through lung compression and recurrent aspiration.

Case summary

A female infant with asplenia, functional single ventricle, and HH presented with lung compression. We prioritized HH repair and gastrostomy placement at 8 months of age, successfully alleviating compression and preventing aspiration. She subsequently underwent a bilateral bidirectional Glenn procedure at 1 year and an extracardiac Fontan procedure at 2 years, demonstrating excellent postoperative hemodynamics.

Discussion

Prioritizing HH repair in patients with single ventricle optimizes pulmonary compliance, providing a safe bridge to Fontan completion when hemodynamically tolerated.

Take-home message

Early surgical intervention for HH optimizes pulmonary hemodynamics, safely bridging patients with single ventricle to Fontan completion.

title: Systemic Atrioventricular Valve Replacement After Fontan Completion: A Multimodality Clinical Case Series.
authorString: Tao K, Sato M, Ishikita A, Kuraoka A, Nakano T, Ishikawa Y.
abstractText:
Background

Systemic atrioventricular (AV) valve regurgitation contributes to late Fontan failure. However, physiological changes after systemic AV valve replacement remain poorly characterized, and objective criteria for patient selection and intervention timing remain undefined.

Case summary

We reviewed 7 patients after Fontan completion undergoing systemic AV valve replacement, with paired catheterization in all and paired cardiovascular magnetic resonance in 6. Replacement markedly reduced AV valve regurgitation in all patients, with ventricular unloading in evaluable cases and clinical improvement or stabilization. Fontan pressure generally decreased when preoperative central venous pressure was elevated, whereas low-output states, altered loading conditions, collateral flow, and high-output physiology modified the hemodynamic response.

Discussion

Systemic AV valve replacement was associated with favorable hemodynamic and clinical effects, although the pattern and tempo of recovery differed across preoperative physiological stages. These observations suggest that integrated cardiovascular magnetic resonance and catheterization may help characterize disease stage and inform patient selection and intervention timing.

title: Novel Transvenous Approach for Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator Implantation in a Patient With Fontan Circulation: Trans-Left Pulmonary Artery-Left Atrium.
authorString: Karolcik BA, Kherallah RY, Boyd CA, Tucker SE, Ermis PR, Lam WW.
abstractText:
Background

After Fontan palliation, direct venous access to the ventricle is eliminated, complicating implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) placement.

Fih/early reports summary

A 34-year-old status-post lateral tunnel Fontan presented with syncope. He was found to have high-grade atrioventricular block and fractured epicardial leads. He was recommended an ICD with severely depressed single right ventricle function but was not an epicardial candidate because of multiple prior sternotomies and recurrent chest wall abscesses. Despite balloon angioplasty of the transbaffle puncture, a sheath for ICD placement could not be advanced. A trans-left pulmonary artery to left atrial (LPA-LA) puncture was performed at the left pulmonary artery/Fontan conduit junction above the left atrium roof to implant the right ventricle ICD lead.

Discussion

Transpulmonary LPA-LA is a feasible option for ICD lead implantation in patients with Fontan who are not candidates for epicardial leads.

Novelty

This is the first report of transpulmonary LPA-LA puncture for ventricular lead placement in Fontan circulation.

title: Peritoneal Dialysis for Refractory Ascites in Fontan-Associated Liver Disease.
authorString: Durán JH, Camargo Castro JS, Guerrero Chalela CE, Casallas-Gutierrez I.
abstractText:
Background

Fontan-associated liver disease and refractory ascites represent advanced systemic failure in patients with Fontan circulation, with limited therapeutic options.

Case summary

A 38-year-old woman with tricuspid atresia, after a Fontan procedure, developed progressive Fontan-associated liver disease and recurrent refractory ascites. Imaging showed portal hypertension and cirrhosis, and liver biopsy confirmed advanced congestive hepatopathy with stage V fibrosis. She was not a candidate for transplant or further intervention, so a tunneled peritoneal catheter was placed for palliative drainage.

Discussion

Refractory ascites reflects Fontan failure and a worse prognosis. Conventional therapy is insufficient, and diuretic resistance becomes common. Peritoneal dialysis allows gradual decongestion with reduced hemodynamic stress in preload-dependent circulation. Evidence supports decreased hospital admissions in refractory heart failure, although data in Fontan cases remain limited.

Take-home messages

Refractory ascites is a marker for end-stage Fontan failure. Peritoneal ultrafiltration becomes a palliative choice when definitive therapies are not feasible.

title: Massive Right Atrial Thrombus After Fontan Palliation Due to Inadequate Atrial Decompression: The Forgotten Chamber.
authorString: Jain M, Johnson JN, Parkerson S, Reiss UM, Merlocco A, Ryan K, Philip R.
abstractText:
Background

Thromboembolic complications are well recognized after Fontan palliation, typically attributed to low-flow conditions within the pathway. Thrombosis arising from residual native cardiac chambers excluded from the preload circuit is rarely reported.

Case summary

A 4-year-old boy with pulmonary atresia and intact ventricular septum underwent pre-Fontan hemodynamic catheterization demonstrating a restrictive atrial septal communication that was balloon dilated, with perceived elimination of the gradient. Ten months after Fontan palliation, he presented with fever and mild respiratory distress and was found to have a giant right atrial thrombus. Imaging suggested profound right atrial stasis because of inadequate atrial decompression. The patient was managed with anticoagulation.

Discussion

This case highlights thrombosis in a native chamber excluded from the preload circuit. Progressive right atrial isolation likely fulfilled Virchow's triad despite an unobstructed Fontan circulation.

Take-home message

Despite exclusion from the preload pathway, definitive atrial decompression is essential when planning a Fontan procedure in patients with pulmonary atresia/intact ventricular septum.

title: Midodrine for Prolonged Pleural Effusions After Total Cavopulmonary Connection.
authorString: Markiewitz ND, Pinto E, Dewitt AG, Kozyak BW, O'Byrne ML, Maeda K, Goldberg DJ, Gupta M.
abstractText:
Background

Prolonged pleural effusions are a common and frustrating problem after total cavopulmonary connection (TCPC), leading to increased duration of indwelling pleural catheters and prolonged hospital stay. Our center has considered midodrine, a selective alpha-1 receptor agonist with a well-established safety profile, as a potential therapy for post-TCPC effusions.

Case summary

We describe our center's experience using midodrine in refractory cases of prolonged pleural effusion following TCPC. Seven patients who had undergone TCPC were prescribed midodrine for the first time at our center within 6 months post-TCPC. In the 3 patients who underwent TCPC at our center, chest tubes were removed a median of 3 days after starting midodrine compared to 11 days in the 4 patients referred for lymphatic intervention.

Discussion

In this single-center experience of patients with prolonged effusions after TCPC, midodrine demonstrated some promise both immediately after TCPC and after lymphatic intervention.

Take-home messages

Prolonged pleural effusions remain a challenge in caring for patients after TCPC. Although midodrine shows potential benefit, formal testing of its safety and efficacy on pleural effusion duration is needed.

title: Leadless Transatrial or Transconduit Pacing in Fontan Circulation.
authorString: Duncan RK, Faluk M, Weingarten AJ, Frischhertz BP, Kowal J, El-Harasis M, Richardson T, Janssen D, Crossley G, Fish F.
abstractText:
Background

Epicardial or transvenous pacing strategies may be suboptimal in certain patients with Fontan requiring permanent pacing. Leadless pacing offers an alternative, but experience in complex Fontan anatomy remains limited.

Case summary

We report 3 patients with Fontan who underwent transatrial or transconduit leadless pacemaker (LP) implantation. One patient with a lateral tunnel Fontan and sinus node dysfunction underwent successful placement of an AVEIR AR (Abbott) LP in the pulmonary venous atrium. Two patients with Fontan circulation and complete heart block with prior epicardial pacing systems underwent implantation of a Micra AV (Medtronic) LP in the systemic ventricle, with longer follow-up than in prior reports.

Conclusions

This case series demonstrates leadless pacing in the pulmonary venous, atrial, and systemic ventricular chambers in Fontan circulation, including atrial AVEIR AR implantation and extended follow-up of ventricular Micra AV pacing. These approaches may expand pacing options in selected patients with Fontan when conventional strategies are limited, although long-term outcomes remain unknown.

title: Intravascular Lithotripsy to Facilitate Percutaneous Stenting of Obstructed Fontan Circuit.
authorString: Puckett JA, Skelton T, McMullan M, Campbell W.
abstractText:
Background

Fontan circuit obstruction generally presents with progressive fatigue or dyspnea on exertion in adulthood with options for management including percutaneous stenting or surgical revision.

Case summary

We present the case of a 27-year-old with history of Fontan palliation with Fontan obstruction due to a heavily calcified, obstructive thrombus within the Fontan circuit. We used intravascular lithotripsy to facilitate appropriate stent expansion.

Discussion

Consensus guidelines recommend evaluating adults with Fontan circuits and progressive symptoms with a combination of cardiac catheterization and advanced imaging. However, consensus on management of Fontan circuit obstruction does not exist, and clinical practice varies widely. We present a case that broadens percutaneous management options.

Take-home messages

Fontan obstruction presents with progressive dyspnea, and options for management include percutaneous stenting or surgical revision. We present a novel approach to allow stent expansion within a calcified Fontan obstruction using intravascular lithotripsy.

title: Recovery of Postpartum Ventricular Dysfunction in a Fontan Patient Treated With Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy.
authorString: Bartra S, Reid J, Saidi A, Saef J.
abstractText:
Background

Women with Fontan circulation (FC) are vulnerable to heart failure during pregnancy and postpartum.

Case summary

A 25-year-old woman with hypoplastic left heart syndrome palliated to a lateral-tunnel Fontan developed severe systemic right ventricular dysfunction 8 weeks postpartum (fractional area change 24%, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide 5,710 pg/mL) despite preserved function immediately after delivery. Guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) was initiated. Serial imaging demonstrated progressive recovery to baseline ventricular function (fractional area change 39%) by 2 years with marked biomarker improvement and symptom resolution.

Beyond the guidelines

Evidence guiding postpartum heart failure management in patients with FC is limited, and there is also limited data on the role of GDMT in FC.

Discussion

Timely initiation of GDMT may facilitate recovery of postpartum systemic ventricular dysfunction in patients with FC.

Take-home message

This case highlights the potential role of early GDMT initiation in a population lacking disease-specific postpartum management recommendations.

title: Intravascular Lithotripsy in Calcific Fontan Conduit Stenosis: Between a Rock and a Hard Place.
authorString: Pinsker BL, Djomaleu M, Wang D, Lin CH.
abstractText:
Background

Dilation and stenting of stenotic Fontan conduits may be limited by circumferential calcific stenosis. Few options exist for calcium modification in this study group.

Case summary

A 29-year-old woman with an extracardiac Fontan was found to have a severely stenotic, circumferentially calcified Fontan conduit (approximately 8 mm). She was brought to the catheterization laboratory for balloon dilation and stent placement. Calcium modification was performed before stenting using intravascular lithotripsy, allowing restoration of the lumen diameter to 20-22 mm. Hemodynamics following lithotripsy and stent placement confirmed the absence of a gradient across her conduit.

Discussion

High-pressure balloons have traditionally been used to facilitate stent expansion in calcified Fontan conduits. However, circumferential calcification may lead to suboptimal results. This case highlights the efficacy of prestent calcium modification with intravascular lithotripsy in a Fontan conduit.

Take-home message

Intravascular lithotripsy may facilitate optimal dilation and stenting in circumferentially calcified Fontan obstruction.

title: Lower-Extremity Chronic Venous Disease Interventions in Patients with Fontan: A Single-Center Experience.
authorString: Faluk M, Duncan R, Weingarten A, Frischhertz B, Byrne RD, Aday AW, Stokes L.
abstractText:
Background

Lower-extremity chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) affects >50% of adult patients with Fontan circulation, with 25% having severe CVI. CVI has historically been managed conservatively in patients with Fontan circulation, but this may not adequately control symptoms. Minimally invasive procedures for management of symptomatic CVI are widely performed in the general population and may be appropriate for treatment of patients with Fontan circulation as well.

Case summary

We report 5 patients with Fontan circulation with symptomatic CVI who underwent minimally invasive venous procedures targeting CVI.

Discussion

The procedures were performed to manage symptoms that were not adequately controlled with conservative measures and were significantly impacting quality of life. All patients underwent venous ablation, phlebectomy, and/or percutaneous liquid sclerotherapy under general anesthesia, and most were discharged on the same day. Patients reported significant clinical improvement without major complications.

Take-home message

Lower-extremity venous procedures may offer a safe and effective strategy for managing symptomatic CVI in patients with Fontan circulation without major complications.
