title: Single-stage combined cardiac and abdominal wall reconstruction in Pentalogy of Cantrell using a cemented sandwich mesh technique: a case report.
authorString: Zaidi ARZ, Samhan SM, Samhan LM, Alghalyini B, Alanazi FSR, ElMahmoud MH.
abstractText:
Background

Pentalogy of Cantrell (POC) is a rare congenital malformation defined by five midline defects involving the sternum, anterior diaphragm, diaphragmatic pericardium, abdominal wall, and heart. Surgical strategies vary between staged and single-stage approaches, and optimal timing remains debated. We report a case of complete POC managed with a single-stage combined cardiac and abdominal wall reconstruction at six months of age, using a cemented sandwich mesh, previously used by our team after sternal tumor resection, for the lower sternal defect.

Case presentation

A six-month-old Saudi male infant, born at 38 weeks by emergency cesarean section (birth weight 1.99 kg, Apgar 8/9), was diagnosed antenatally with ectopia cordis, ventricular septal defect (VSD), and epigastric omphalocele. Amniocentesis had excluded trisomy. Postnatal echocardiography confirmed a large perimembranous VSD with inlet extension, a mid-muscular VSD, a small atrial septal defect (ASD), and an ejection fraction of 57%. A multidisciplinary team elected to proceed with a single-stage combined operation once his weight exceeded 5 kg (6.2 kg at surgery). Cardiac surgery was performed first through sternotomy (bypass time 150 min; cross-clamp time 124 min), with patch repair of the VSD and ASD and excision of a left ventricular diverticulum. The pediatric surgery team then addressed the omphalocele via midline laparotomy extension, closed the anterior diaphragmatic defect primarily, and reconstructed the lower sternal defect using gentamicin-impregnated bone cement within doubled Gore-Tex mesh (a sandwich mesh configuration). Fascial closure reached the umbilicus without clinical signs of raised intra-abdominal pressure. The patient was extubated on postoperative day three and achieved full oral feeds by day five. Echocardiography before discharge showed no residual shunt and an ejection fraction of 54%. A small incisional hernia was repaired electively about one year later, and the child remained asymptomatic at two years.

Conclusions

This case demonstrates that single-stage combined cardiac and abdominal wall repair in complete POC is feasible and can reduce the burden of repeated surgical interventions. The cemented sandwich mesh achieved stable reconstruction of the lower sternal defect in this patient, offering a potential alternative for centers managing similar complex congenital anomalies.

title: Early epigenetic alterations in cardiac tissue following perinatal sertraline exposure in mice.
authorString: Lu Y, Chimenti MS, Haskell SE.
abstractText:
Introduction

Maternal use of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), including sertraline, has been associated with an increased risk of congenital heart defects, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. SSRIs cross the placenta and may influence cardiac development during sensitive periods. Previous work showed that perinatal sertraline exposure impairs postnatal growth, alters cardiomyocyte calcium handling, dysregulates serotonin signaling genes (Htr2a, Htr2b, and Slc6a4), and chronically reduces left ventricular size. We hypothesized that these effects may involve early epigenetic alterations in cardiac DNA methylation.

Materials & methods

Adult female C57BL/6J mice received daily intraperitoneal injections of sertraline (5 mg/kg) or saline for five days before mating and throughout gestation. Offspring continued to receive 1.5 mg/kg of sertraline until postnatal day 14 (PN14), when hearts were collected. Global DNA methylation (5-methylcytosine, 5-mC) was quantified using a colorimetric ELISA assay. Targeted bisulfite sequencing (TBS-seq) profiled CpG methylation across predefined promoter and regulatory regions of 10 genes involved in serotonin signaling and cardiac function. Regional differential methylation was analyzed across 23 regions using overdispersion-corrected logistic regression with Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) adjustment.

Results

Global 5-mC levels did not differ significantly between sertraline-exposed and control groups. TBS-seq identified 1,941 CpG sites across 25 targeted regions. After coverage and regional quality filtering, 1,411 CpG sites across 23 regions were retained. Regional analysis identified two regions with significant differential methylation after FDR correction: the Htr2a enhancer showed an 8.19% increase in methylation (p < 4.1 × 10-15, q < 9.4 × 10-14), whereas the Tph2-associated region showed a 3.00% decrease in sertraline-exposed animals (p < 0.0020, q < 0.0229). Secondary site-level analyses identified no individual CpG sites that remained significant after multiple-testing correction. Overall methylation profiles were highly correlated across samples, with no significant global difference between treatment groups.

Discussion

Perinatal sertraline exposure was associated with localized regional DNA methylation changes in neonatal cardiac tissue without a global change in 5-mC. The Htr2a enhancer and Tph2-associated region represent candidate regulatory loci linking early-life SSRI exposure with cardiac serotonergic pathways. These findings support further investigation of regional epigenetic alterations using integrated methylation, transcriptomic, and cell-type-resolved approaches to determine their functional significance and potential contribution to later-life cardiovascular outcomes.

title: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: Incidence, Outcomes, and Treatment.
authorString: Herrmann FEM, Taha A, Charitos EI, Wehbe M, Wakili R, Jeppsson A.
abstractText:
Background

Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is the recommended treatment in advanced coronary heart disease. More than 28 000 isolated CABG procedures are performed each year in Germany: almost one-third of patients have transient, new-onset postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) before they are discharged from the hospital. In this narrative review, we outline the detection, incidence, outcomes, and treatment of POAF after CABG on the basis of current evidence.

Methods

This narrative review is based on guidelines and pertinent publications that were retrieved by a selective search in PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov. In the analysis, randomized controlled trials concerning CABG patients were given priority over observational studies and those involving mixed cardiac surgical cohorts.

Results

Nationwide registries have documented a 30-31% incidence of POAF after CABG, but recent data obtained by continuous monitoring indicate a cumulative 1-year incidence of 48% (95% confidence interval [41; 55]). The atrial fibrillation (AF) burden (time in AF divided by the duration of monitoring) after CABG is low (0.07%), and episodes most commonly arise in the first month after surgery. POAF can be treated acutely with either rate or rhythm control, depending on physician preference. The evidence on long-term oral anticoagulation (OAC) for patients with POAF after CABG is mixed; current data suggest it may not be indicated.

Conclusion

POAF often arises shortly after CABG and mainly consists of brief episodes with a low overall atrial fibrillation burden. The role of long-term OAC remains unclear. The guideline recommendations for CABG patients should be reassessed in the light of current evidence.

title: Temporal Effects of Exogenous Testosterone on the Circulating Small Noncoding RNA Landscape in a Placebo‑Controlled Human Study.
authorString: Main AM, Solheim SA, Wagner SP, Albrechtsen HM, Nordsborg NB, Winge SB, Juul A, Mørup N, Almstrup K.
abstractText:
Background

Anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS) are widely misused, but molecular markers serving as physiological readouts as well as biomarkers of misuse remain poorly defined. Circulating small noncoding RNAs (sncRNAs) are plausible endocrine-responsive messengers and candidate biomarkers.

Objective

To determine whether exogenous testosterone administration acutely and persistently alters circulating sncRNAs.

Materials and methods

Randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial in healthy eugonadal men (n = 19; 20-30 years), receiving intramuscular injections of 250 mg mixed testosterone esters as Sustanon 250 or placebo on Day 0 and 21. Serum was collected at Day 0, 1, and 42, and the isolated RNA was subjected to small RNA sequencing using the RealSeq-Biofluids library kit. A link between miR-214-3p and testosterone concentrations was tested on longitudinal serum samples from 29 peri-pubertal boys with RT-qPCR, and its expression in testis tissue was investigated by in situ hybridization.

Results

Twenty-four hours after testosterone administration, we identified a distinct signature of 19 Sustanon-responsive sncRNAs (12 upregulated, 7 downregulated), with piRNAs as the most represented class. One of the Sustanon-specific sncRNAs, miR-214-3p, was found to correlate positively with circulating testosterone in peri-pubertal boys and showed expression in testicular tissue, including testosterone-producing Leydig cells. Despite testosterone having returned to baseline concentrations at Day 42, 160 sncRNAs remained altered, indicating sustained effects of testosterone use. Intersecting short- and long-term analyses revealed 43 Sustanon-specific sncRNAs, including the small nucleolar RNA U3.

Discussion

Despite the modest sample size, this study highlights that multiple sncRNAs respond to testosterone exposure. Further studies are needed to develop a functional, tissue-specific understanding of the identified sncRNAs.

Conclusions

Brief supraphysiological testosterone exposure remodels circulating sncRNAs both acutely and over weeks, implicating androgens in systemic RNA-based communication. Several responsive sncRNAs, notably miR-214-3p and snoRNA U3, show potential as biomarkers of androgen misuse.

title: Correction to "Ephedrine for Reducing Onset Time of Rocuronium in Elderly Patients: A Randomised Study".
A Superior Spermatic Cord Denervation Technique?: A Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Turin D, Shish L, Gagen R, Hubbard L, Bodie J.
abstractText:
Introduction

Chronic orchialgia is a common condition encompassing about 2.5%-5% of urology consults in the United States each year. When conservative treatments fail, spermatic cord denervation is often pursued after a diagnostic cord block. A standard total denervation (SD) of the spermatic cord has been considered the gold standard, targeting all nerves while preserving arteries. Recently, newer methods like targeted complex denervation (TD) and robotic-assisted denervation (RD) have emerged.

Objectives

This study systematically evaluates whether these methods provide improved pain relief over the traditional approach.

Methods

A systematic review evaluating pain improvement in men with chronic orchialgia following SD, TD, and RD was conducted, PROSPERO database (Registration No.: CRD42024540544). A comprehensive literature search was performed using MEDLINE, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov, WHO ICTRP, Global Index Medicus, and Web of Science in May 2024. Articles were evaluated by two independent screeners. Data was analyzed and summarized using odds ratios (ORs) and confidence intervals (CIs) for complete (100%) or significant (> 50%) pain resolution, and continuous variables were compared using inverse-variance weighted means and corresponding 95% CI. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS).

Results

Twenty-three studies were included: 17 on SD, 5 on RD, and 4 on TD. SD was performed on 675 testicular units, RD on 947, and TD on 992. Complete pain resolution was found in 65.8%, 48.6%, and 51.4% of testicular units undergoing SD, TD, and RD, respectively. Significant (> 50%) pain resolution was experienced by 84.9%, 83.8%, and 83.3% of testicular units after SD, TD, and RD, respectively. SD had 1.86-fold higher odds of complete pain relief (OR: 1.86; 95% CI: 1.51-2.29; p < 0.001) and no difference in the odds of significant (> 50%) pain relief (OR: 0.94; 95% CI: 0.72-1.24; p = 0.68) compared to TD. SD had 1.68-fold higher odds of complete pain relief (OR: 1.68; 95% CI: 1.36-2.07; p < 0.001) and no difference in the odds of significant (> 50%) pain relief (OR: 0.98; 95% CI: 0.74-1.28; p = 0.86) when compared to RD. Average operative times were 71.50, 20.89, and 21.25 min per testicular unit for SD, TD, and RD, respectively. Complication rates were similar with 6.1%, 7.0%, and 7.6% for standard, targeted, and robotic approaches, respectively. Of all included and scored studies, 55% (12/22) were categorized as having a NOS score < 7.

Conclusion

SD offers the highest odds of complete pain resolution, although all approaches have similar chances of achieving > 50% pain reduction. The ORs suggest that SD had higher odds of complete pain resolution, but the lack of well-designed comparative studies limits adequate comparison of efficacy.

title: Coronary Risk in Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement, Overview of Data, Challenges, and Best Practices.
authorString: Dandach L, Mahmoudi K, Sfeir M, Masri A.
abstractText: Coronary artery obstruction is a rare complication of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). This risk increases in TAVR-valve-in-valve procedure. Several anatomic risk factors were described in many studies to identify the predictive elements of coronary artery occlusion on computed tomography cardiac scan. Rescue percutaneous coronary intervention was the first approach described to treat this complication with a high mortality rate. Later on, preventive chimney stenting technique was evaluated and results showed that is a safe and effective strategy but it leads to a difficult coronary access later. New preventive techniques are being evaluated recently (Basilica and Shorctut).

title: Coronary Artery Disease and Heart Failure: Medical Management and Future Direction.
authorString: Patel PN, Poliner MC, Bossone E, Baliga RR.
abstractText: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a leading etiology of heart failure (HF) and serves as a significant therapeutic target to ameliorate HF-associated morbidity and mortality. Key management considerations include pharmacologic treatment, electrophysiological devices, and coronary revascularization, aimed toward preventing CAD progression, left ventricular remodeling, sudden death, and reinfarction. The optimal revascularization strategy for patients with CAD and HF who are surgical candidates requires careful assessment of each patients' unique risk/benefit profile and individual preferences. Several novel pharmacologic agents are in development with hopes of adding to the armamentarium of treatment of CAD and HF.

title: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Heart Failure due to Coronary Artery Disease.
authorString: Singh A, Zhang RS, Bangalore S.
abstractText: The role of revascularization and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with acute coronary syndrome is well established. However, the incremental value of revascularization over guideline-directed medical therapy is controversial. Currently available data supports the use of PCI to improve angina and quality of life for chronic coronary disease and heart failure (HF). However, there is insufficient data to support revascularization with PCI to improve mortality, reduce cardiovascular events, or improve ejection fraction over medical therapy alone. Additional trials are necessary to identify HF patients who may benefit from revascularization, and the optimal revascularization strategy for this population.

title: Microglial Transmembrane 119 (Tmem119) is Protective in Ischemic Stroke.
authorString: Misrani A, Xu Y, Wang J, Tanifum EA, McCullough LD, Liu F, Ngwa C.
abstractText: Microglial responses to cerebral ischemia are tightly regulated by inhibitory pathways that limit excessive post-stroke inflammation. Transmembrane protein 119 (Tmem119) has emerged as an important regulator of microglial activation and neuroinflammatory signaling. We investigated the role of microglial Tmem119 during acute ischemic stroke using primary microglia and a young adult mouse model. Primary microglia were transfected with Tmem119-siRNA and subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) alone or combined with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation. In vivo, young adult male mice received stereotaxic injection of lenti-Tmem119 or lenti-GFP for 4 weeks before 60 min of transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO). Tmem119 expression and inflammatory responses were assessed by qPCR, Western blotting, and ELISA at 1 and 3 days after stroke. Infarct volume and neurobehavioral outcomes were also evaluated. Tmem119 silencing significantly increased IRAK4, IRF5, and CD68 mRNA expression in primary microglia. Ischemic injury reduced microglial Tmem119 protein expression and increased IRAK4 signaling in vivo. In contrast, lenti-Tmem119 treatment before MCAO decreased phosphorylated IRAK4 protein expression and increased IL-10 levels in both plasma and ischemic brain tissue compared with lenti-GFP controls. Tmem119 overexpression also significantly reduced infarct volume and improved neurobehavioral outcomes. These findings demonstrate that microglial Tmem119 exerts a protective anti-inflammatory role during the acute phase of ischemic stroke by suppressing IRAK4-mediated inflammatory signaling and enhancing IL-10 production. Collectively, Tmem119 limits microglial activation, reduces ischemic brain injury, and improves functional recovery, identifying Tmem119 as a promising therapeutic target for ischemic stroke.

title: Mapping the Care Literature in Patients With Left Ventricular Assist Device: A Bibliometric Analysis.
authorString: Yıldız GA, Kulaksızoğlu H, Aslan FE.

journal.title: Japan journal of nursing science : JJNS

abstractText:
Background

As left ventricular assist device (LVAD) use expands, multidisciplinary care has become increasingly important. This study aimed to analyze the literature on LVAD patient care using bibliometric methods and identify publication trends, influential contributors, research themes, international collaborations, and future research areas.

Methods and results

Publications indexed in Web of Science up to July 3, 2026, were analyzed using Biblioshiny in the Bibliometrix R package. Based on predefined eligibility criteria, 207 English-language articles published between 1997 and 2026 were included. The annual publication growth rate was 3.86%, with an average of 17.94 citations per article. Publication output peaked in 2024 (n = 20). The most productive journals were ASAIO Journal and Heart & Lung (n = 15 each), while McIlvennan CK, Allen LA, Thompson JS, Matlock DD, and Grady KL were the most prolific authors. Keyword Plus analysis highlighted heart failure, LVAD, quality of life, mechanical circulatory support, and outcomes. Thematic analysis identified mechanical circulatory support and outcomes as well-developed research areas, while quality of life, LVAD, and heart failure formed the field's conceptual foundation. The United States was the leading contributor, followed by Italy, Japan, Germany, and Canada.

Conclusion

LVAD research has evolved from a predominantly device- and outcome-focused approach toward holistic, patient-centered care encompassing caregiver support, self-care, palliative care, and decision-making. Patient experience, communication, decision-making, heart transplantation, and mortality remain areas requiring further research.

title: Evaluation of Coronary Artery Disease and Ischemia by Echocardiography: Advances in Technology and Techniques.
authorString: Hussain K, Shrivastav R, Puthumana JJ.
abstractText: This review describes the role of echocardiography in the diagnosis and prognostication of coronary artery disease (CAD). It describes the diagnostic capabilities of echocardiography using rest and stress imaging, speckle tracking strain imaging with myocardial work index, as well as the use of myocardial perfusion imaging. It also evaluates the use of echocardiography in the assessment of common complications from CAD and the incremental value of incorporating right ventricular, left atrial, and diastolic function assessment in these patients. In addition, the review aims to highlight the prognostic value of echocardiography, especially in the determination of myocardial viability.

title: Valvular Shock in the Cardiac Intensive Care Unit: Perioperative Care for Transcatheter Valve Interventions.
authorString: Prosperi-Porta G, Dahiya G, Hibbert B, Jentzer JC.
abstractText: Valvular heart disease is an uncommon but high-risk cause of cardiogenic shock requiring rapid, multidisciplinary management aimed at bridging patients to definitive surgical or transcatheter valve intervention. Early comprehensive Doppler echocardiography is essential, as clinical signs may be subtle. Distinguishing decompensated chronic valvular disease from acute unstable lesions guides urgency and treatment strategy. Medical stabilization and mechanical circulatory support vary markedly between stenotic and regurgitant lesions, and standard shock therapies may be harmful in specific contexts. Transcatheter approaches are preferred when feasible, though their expanding use introduces added complexity in cardiac intensive care.

title: Electrosurgery in Structural Heart Interventions.
authorString: Kattoor AJ, Iyer V.
abstractText: Electrosurgery has emerged as a groundbreaking tool in the field of structural cardiac interventions, revolutionizing the approach to complex cardiac conditions. This review delves into the core principles, procedural techniques, outcomes, and potential challenges associated with various electrosurgical procedures within the realm of structural cardiology. Five key electrosurgical procedures performed in complex structural interventions are highlighted in this review. They are the Transcaval Access, BASILICA, LAMPOON, ELASTIC/ELASTA-Clip, and SESAME procedures. While these electrosurgery procedures hold promise and have demonstrated positive outcomes, their technical intricacies, patient selection criteria, and the need for further research remain important considerations. As technology continues to evolve and more data becomes available, electrosurgery is poised to continue shaping the landscape of cardiac care, offering minimally invasive alternatives, and improving patient outcomes in complex structural cardiac interventions.

title: Coronary Artery Revascularization in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
authorString: McHugh S, Allaham H, Chahal D, Gupta A.
abstractText: Patients with concomitant severe aortic stenosis and significant coronary artery disease present a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge in clinical practice. There are no clear-cut guidelines as to the timing of revascularization in these patients who are referred for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). This article aims to show that in patients without high-grade proximal coronary artery disease, revascularization after TAVR is safe, feasible, and practical. Additionally, the use of preoperative TAVR computed tomographic angiography might be used in both intermediate and high-risk patients rather than invasive coronary angiography to assess for significant proximal coronary artery disease to help guide the timing of revascularization.

title: Coronary Microvascular Dysfunction: Identification, Special Populations, and Management Strategies.
authorString: Di Carli MF.
abstractText: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is a prevalent and often underdiagnosed condition with significant implications for adverse cardiovascular outcomes. The pathophysiology of CMD includes structural and functional abnormalities in the coronary microvasculature and epicardial atherosclerosis contributes to downstream reduction in myocardial perfusion and symptoms. Diagnosis relies on advanced invasive or noninvasive imaging techniques, such as PET and cardiac magnetic resonance, capable of quantifying myocardial perfusion and myocardial blood flow reserve. Effective management includes optimizing cardiovascular risk factors and symptom control. Novel therapeutic strategies recently approved for management of diabetes, obesity, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction offer potentially powerful options for management of CMD.

title: Coronary Angiography in the Evaluation of Systolic Heart Failure.
authorString: McGee K, Cremer PC.
abstractText: The review discusses angiographic and hemodynamic features of invasive and computed tomography coronary angiography, which inform diagnosis, prognosis, and coronary revascularization in patients with systolic heart failure.

title: IgA nephropathy: evolving treatment strategies.
authorString: Mastroianni-Kirsztajn G, Siliano JM, Luciano EP.
abstractText: IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is the most common primary glomerular disease and is characterized by marked clinical, laboratory, and histopathological heterogeneity, with a variable risk of progression to advanced stages of chronic kidney disease depending on several underlying factors. A better understanding of its pathogenesis, which involves at least a four-hit pathogenic sequence, has enabled the development of novel therapeutic strategies targeting different stages of disease development, including agents directed at specific molecular pathways. Supportive kidney-protective therapy is now well established as the cornerstone of IgAN management and involves lifestyle modifications such as a healthy diet, regular physical activity, weight control, smoking cessation, sodium restriction, optimal blood pressure control, and interventions to reduce cardiovascular risk. Pharmacological measures include renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, as well as mineralocorticoid receptor and endothelin A receptor antagonists. Historically, immunosuppressive treatment relied primarily on systemic corticosteroids, with cyclophosphamide or azathioprine reserved for selected clinical situations. More recently, targeted-release budesonide has emerged as a therapeutic option, followed by the development of agents directed at specific molecular pathways, particularly complement inhibitors and therapies targeting BAFF and/or APRIL signaling, among others. Although this expanding therapeutic armamentarium provides new opportunities to improve patient outcomes, it also introduces uncertainty and complexity into clinical decision-making. Therefore, defining evidence-based parameters to guide the selection and combination of available therapies according to the distinct endotypes of IgAN has become increasingly important.

title: Contemporary Coronary Disease in Interventional Cardiology.
authorString: Eng MH.

title: Challenges of Robot-Assisted Surgery in Reconstructive Microsurgery: A Scoping Review.
authorString: Cai L, Seth I, Ricketts S, Mah E.
abstractText:
Introduction

Robotic platforms have been popularized in reconstructive microsurgery for their ability to enhance precision and dexterity, filter tremor, and reduce surgical fatigue. Nonetheless, implantation challenges compared with conventional methods remain poorly synthesized. This scoping review identifies common barriers to robotic platforms in reconstructive microsurgery.

Method

A literature search was conducted in PubMed (Medline), Embase, and the Cochrane Library for English-language publications between January 1, 2016 and September 30, 2026 reporting clinical challenges in robot-assisted surgical reconstruction. Publications included were primary research. Reviews and preclinical studies were excluded. A total of 726 articles were screened, and 30 met the inclusion criteria.

Results

Thirty peer-reviewed publications were reviewed, predominantly from European and American institutions utilizing the Da Vinci Surgical System, Medical Microinstrument's Symani Surgical System, or MicroSure's MUSA surgical robots. Most consistently reported challenges were prolonged operative and anastomotic times in 83% of studies, increased operative costs in 57% of studies, learning and adaptation to robot-assisted microsurgery, as well as a lack of haptic feedback and complex operating room set-up. Less commonly reported barriers include instrument reliability, physiological motion impairing operative control, large robotic footprint, sustainability of single-use consumables, limited operative field, and magnetic interference. Inconsistent reporting on the learning curve of robot-assisted surgery was noted. Overall, the evidence base is limited by conflicts of interest with robotic manufacturers present within 37% of reviewed studies, small sample sizes, methodological heterogeneity, and paucity of long-term patient outcomes. These limitations may underestimate the challenges surgeons face in adopting robotic platforms in reconstructive microsurgery.

Conclusion

Robot-assisted reconstructive microsurgery is a promising but maturing field. Future research should include manual microsurgical control groups and report long-term clinical outcomes to strengthen the evidence base for robot-assisted reconstructive microsurgery. Randomized controlled trials with manual control groups will help guide the standardization of robot-assisted microsurgery training curricula.

title: Exploring the Implementation Potential of Integrating Diabetes Care Into Tuberculosis Services in Pakistan: A Qualitative Case Study.
authorString: Afaq S, Jamal SF, Rehman A, Ashfaq U, Zala, Asim M, Khan FU, Gill S, Khan HL, Sarfraz M, Khan Z, Siddiqi K, Jennings H.

journal.title: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy

abstractText:
Background

The co-occurrence of diabetes and tuberculosis (TB) worsens outcomes for both conditions, increasing mortality risk and treatment failure. Despite the need for integrated care for the two conditions, evidence on feasible and context-specific implementation strategies remains limited. This study explored the implementation potential of contextually designed implementation strategies to integrate diabetes within TB care in Pakistan, using the Optimised TB and Diabetes (Opt-TBD) package.

Methods

This qualitative case study was conducted from October 2023 to June 2024, across four TB facilities representing primary, secondary and tertiary levels of care in Pakistan. Using a qualitative design, we conducted in-depth interviews with TB patients with comorbid diabetes (n = 12) at 3 and 6 months after implementation, while healthcare providers (n = 6) were interviewed towards the end of the implementation period. We applied the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) alongside Proctor's implementation outcomes framework to explore implementation processes and six implementation outcomes: acceptability, appropriateness, feasibility, adoption, penetration and sustainability.

Results

Several contextually tailored implementation strategies, including structured staff training, standardised screening protocols and strengthened referral mechanisms, were employed to integrate diabetes care within routine TB services. Overall, the intervention aligned well with existing TB workflows, provided that adequate resources, clearly defined referral pathways and ongoing staff training were ensured. Despite logistical challenges-such as delays in obtaining HbA1c test results and patient privacy concerns-healthcare providers reported adopting diabetes screening and counselling practices beyond the initial study participants. Strong leadership engagement and consistent programmatic support facilitated early implementation; however, sustaining these efforts long-term will require securing dedicated financial resources and formal integration into policy frameworks.

Conclusion

This qualitative study indicates promising implementation potential for integrating the Opt-TBD care package within routine TB services in Pakistan. Participants generally perceived the package as acceptable and workable within routine TB services, while laboratory delays, referral challenges and dependence on external financing remained important barriers to wider implementation. These findings informed refinement of the Opt-TBD package and the subsequent broader RE-AIM evaluation.

Lived experience or public contribution

To develop a more inclusive and contextually relevant integrated TB-diabetes care pathway, we gathered input from both service providers and service users, including patients with TB-diabetes multimorbidity. The Opt-TBD care package was co-designed with relevant stakeholders, and this qualitative study was undertaken to capture the experiences and insights of patients and healthcare providers during implementation. Participation was sought across different genders, age groups, provinces and levels of care to ensure a broad range of perspectives. This approach helped ensure that the views of those directly affected by and involved in service delivery informed the refinement of the care package and its implementation strategies.

title: Real-World Comparative Effectiveness and Safety of Prasugrel Versus Ticagrelor After Acute Coronary Syndrome and Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
authorString: Riaz M, Angiolillo DJ, Lee CR, Cavallari LH.
abstractText:
Study objective

To compare the real-world effectiveness and safety of prasugrel versus ticagrelor among patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in the United States.

Design

Retrospective new-user cohort study.

Data source

MarketScan Research Databases, 2017-2023.

Patients

Patients aged 18 years or older with ACS and PCI initiated on either prasugrel or ticagrelor were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) diagnosis codes and prescription records. The prescription fill date was assigned as the index date. Patients were required to have continuous enrollment in their health care plan for 1 year prior to and including the index date.

Measurements and main results

Stabilized inverse probability treatment weighting was applied to balance baseline characteristics between treatment groups. Cox proportional hazards models with adherence adjustment were used to estimate 1 year risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE, composite of myocardial infarction [MI], ischemic stroke, or stent thrombosis), bleeding events, and individual MACE components. The study included 6662 prasugrel-treated and 25,452 ticagrelor-treated patients. Prasugrel was associated with a lower risk of MACE (3.83 vs. 5.61 events per 100 person-years; adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.72, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.65-0.92) and MI (3.43 vs. 4.73 events per 100 person-years; aHR 0.80, 95% CI 0.66-0.97) compared with ticagrelor, respectively. Bleeding risk did not differ between prasugrel versus ticagrelor (2.85 vs. 3.89 events per 100 person-years, respectively; aHR 0.92, 95% CI 0.74-1.13). Sensitivity analyses restricted to patients with high medication adherence and without contraindications to prasugrel showed similar results.

Conclusion

Among commercially insured US patients with ACS undergoing PCI, prasugrel was associated with a lower risk of ischemic cardiovascular events compared with ticagrelor, without an increase in bleeding risk, including in patients with high medication adherence. These findings provide contemporary real-world evidence supporting the preferential use of prasugrel over ticagrelor following ACS and PCI in appropriately selected patients.

title: Gene-Dose Interaction in Low-Dose Irinotecan: A Real-World Cohort Study of the Association Between Adverse Effects and UGT1A1 Polymorphism.
authorString: Zukerman D, Hadad J, Lejbkowicz F, Barnett-Griness O, Gronich N.
abstractText:
Introduction

Exposure to the toxic metabolite of irinotecan is higher in UGT1A1 poor metabolizers (PMs). It is uncertain if there is a higher risk for adverse effects in PMs receiving low-dose irinotecan regimens (< 150 mg/m2). In this retrospective cohort study, we examined in a real-world cohort the interaction between UGT1A1 polymorphism and initial irinotecan dose, with severe adverse effects of irinotecan.

Material and methods

We performed a retrospective cohort study based on Clalit Health Services (CHS) database, including all adults initiating irinotecan, with available UGT1A1 result. Short-term outcomes, within 2 months of first irinotecan dose, were Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia, hospitalization, and mortality. A composite outcome included all of the above. Secondary outcomes were hospitalization due to diarrhea and long-term overall survival. We used logistic regression models and a propensity score that included demographics, cancer-related variables, chronic clinical conditions, and laboratory characteristics at cohort entry.

Result

Of 450 patients initiating irinotecan (2004-2025), 185 (41.1%) were UGT1A1 normal metabolizers (NMs), 211 (46.9%) were intermediate metabolizers (IMs), and 54 (12%) were PMs. Dosing data was available for 260 patients. UGT1A1 PM status was associated with increased risk for Grade-3 neutropenia with an odds ratio (OR) of 4.36 (95% CI 1.29-14.82) in the higher dose group, with a median initial dose (interquartile range) of 107 (100-115) mg/m2. UGT1A1 PM status was not associated with increased toxicity risk in the lower dose group, with a median initial dose (interquartile range) of 80 (66-88) mg/m2. The risk for the composite outcome in PMs receiving the higher dose had an OR of 3.19 (95% CI 0.95-10.72) p = 0.06 (marginally significant). An interaction between UGT1A1 polymorphism and initial irinotecan dose was identified. Propensity-score analysis and sensitivity analyses yielded similar results. There was no increased risk for hospitalizations due to diarrhea in PMs receiving higher doses of irinotecan, and no difference in overall survival was found between the four groups defined by polymorphism and initial dose.

Conclusion

Our data suggest a possible dose-by-genotype interaction within the irinotecan regimens of < 150 mg/m2. The findings may support heightened vigilance and motivate larger prospective studies to establish the recommended initial irinotecan dose with regard to the common UGT1A1 polymorphism.

title: A Murinized Bimagrumab Analogue Increases Skeletal Muscle Mass and Improves Cardiometabolic Remodelling in Experimental Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Baka T, Mirrione SM, Qin F, Gower AC, He H, Haney C, Su KM, Dillon ST, Libermann TA, Heitman K, Ryan AP, Brozinick JT, Seta F, Pimentel DR, Sam F, Luptak I.

journal.title: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle

abstractText:
Background

Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) involves left ventricular hypertrophy and metabolic dysfunction. Given the role of skeletal muscle in systemic metabolism, we investigated whether activin type II receptor inhibition with CDD866, a murinized bimagrumab analogue that induces skeletal muscle hypertrophy, improves physical performance and cardiometabolic remodelling in established HCM.

Methods

Twenty-four-week-old male mice harbouring the cardiac myosin R403Q mutation received CDD866 or isotype antibody (20 mg/kg subcutaneously every 3 days) for 4 weeks; wild-type (WT) littermates received isotype antibody. Assessments included body composition, muscle imaging and histology, grip strength, treadmill exercise, glucose tolerance, echocardiography, cardiac histopathology, myocardial substrate oxidation by 13C nuclear magnetic resonance in isolated beating hearts and cardiac transcriptomics and proteomics. Values are mean ± SEM.

Results

Compared with R403Q placebo, CDD866 increased lean mass (22.5 ± 0.6 vs. 18.7 ± 0.5 g; p < 0.001), grip strength (135.3 ± 3.4 vs. 99.9 ± 4.3 cN; p < 0.0001) and treadmill distance (99.8 ± 1.7 vs. 77.2 ± 3.2 m; p < 0.0001). Hindlimb muscle volume increased by 24 ± 8% (p < 0.05), and individual muscle weights increased by 44%-87% (all p < 0.0001). CDD866 reduced total left ventricular wall thickness (1.80 ± 0.03 vs. 1.98 ± 0.03 mm; p < 0.001) and improved E/A ratio (1.31 ± 0.04 vs. 0.99 ± 0.04; p < 0.001) and early diastolic mitral annular velocity (18.6 ± 0.7 vs. 14.0 ± 0.7 mm/s; p < 0.01). Cardiomyocyte cross-sectional area and myocardial fibrosis decreased by 32 ± 6% (p < 0.0001) and 69 ± 31% (p < 0.01), respectively. Glucose tolerance was impaired in R403Q mice versus WT (p < 0.01), with a nonsignificant reduction in AUC following CDD866 (p = 0.223). CDD866 increased the fractional contribution of fatty acids to myocardial oxidative metabolism (0.66 ± 0.02 vs. 0.38 ± 0.05; p < 0.01) and reduced 13C-lactate output (15.3 ± 2.5 vs. 40.2 ± 3.8 nmol/min; p < 0.001). Consistent with these measurements, cardiac RNA-seq GSEA showed HCM-associated suppression and CDD866-associated enrichment of fatty acid oxidation, pyruvate metabolism, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, oxidative phosphorylation, ATP synthesis and branched-chain amino acid catabolism (all FDR q < 0.05). Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic upstream regulator predictions provided an exploratory regulatory context for these metabolic findings.

Conclusions

CDD866 increased skeletal muscle mass and performance alongside improvements in cardiac remodelling, diastolic function and myocardial metabolism in established experimental HCM. Activin receptor inhibition offers a promising therapeutic avenue for HCM.

title: Day to Day Variability and Effects of Collection Conditions on Urinary Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System Biomarkers in Vervet Monkeys (Chlorocebus aethiops sabaeus).
authorString: Graham ME, Carter K, Gwathmey TM, Cilvik SN.
abstractText:
Background

Dysregulation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) is associated with cardiovascular and renal disease. Our objectives were to determine the daily variability in urinary RAAS biomarkers and differences between non-sedated free catch (FC) and sedated cystocentesis samples in vervet monkeys.

Methods

We performed repeated urine collections (six non-sedated FC, three sedated cystocentesis) from six adult vervets (Chlorocebus aethiops sabaeus). We quantified RAAS components, normalized to urine creatinine. We assessed variability using coefficients of variation (CV) and compared sedation effects using linear mixed-effects models with false discovery rate correction.

Results

Analytes showed high to very high variability (CV 28.17%-103.03%). Angiotensin converting enzyme demonstrated the lowest variability (cystocentesis, CV 28.17% ± 18.28%). Creatinine, Angiotensin-(1-7), Angiotensin II, and aldosterone concentrations differed between non-sedated FC and sedated cystocentesis samples.

Conclusions

Substantial within-animal variability suggests that single-timepoint measurements insufficiently characterize urinary RAAS in vervets. Differences between collection conditions support standardization of collection methods and repeated sampling.

title: Acute Suffering, Act of Togetherness and On-Scene Space: A Concept Synthesis for Caring in Prehospital Emergency Care.
authorString: Holmberg M, Wallinvirta E, Rantala A, Bremer A.
abstractText:
Background

Prehospital emergency care attends to patients experiencing acute suffering; a sudden and profound disruption affecting the person's life, body and existential well-being in the context of illness, injury or crisis. In this unpredictable and vulnerable setting, a central question emerges: how can caring needs be effectively met?

Aim

The aim of this paper is to develop a concept synthesis grounded in a caring science paradigm within the prehospital context, clarifying the nature of caring.

Method

A concept synthesis based on a caring science theoretical framework was conducted using a combined deductive-inductive approach, integrating theory, clinical experience and relevant literature through an abductive and iterative process.

Results

The synthesis introduces three interrelated concepts: acute Suffering (S), act of Togetherness (T) and On-scene space (O), situated within Prehospital emergency care (P). These concepts collectively shape the STOP synthesis. STOP positions caring as the core of prehospital emergency care, emphasizing a holistic perspective that extends beyond a purely biological understanding. It provides a structured framework for understanding and practicing the complexity of caring in this setting.

Conclusion

Using the STOP-sign metaphor, the STOP synthesis highlights the importance of pausing in prehospital emergency care to recognize the patient as a multidimensional human being experiencing acute suffering. By integrating the concepts of acute Suffering, act of Togetherness and On-scene space within the prehospital context, the synthesis promotes a shift beyond a solely biomedical perspective toward a caring science understanding of suffering and care. The synthesis may support prehospital professionals, particularly nurses, in integrating caring and medical knowledge in clinical practice and provides a theoretical basis for future research, education and a holistic prehospital emergency care.

title: Barriers to Addressing Sexual Health Needs of Adults With Chronic Kidney Disease: A Multidisciplinary Survey of Renal Healthcare Professionals.
authorString: McKeaveney C, Sun X, McMahon J, Bonner A, Donald M, Dumanski S, Elliott M, Finderup J.
abstractText:
Background

Sexual dysfunction is common among adults with chronic kidney disease and can significantly affect health and well-being. Understanding healthcare professionals' attitudes, training experiences, and perceived barriers toward discussing sexual health needs with patients is essential to improving patient care.

Methods

A cross-sectional survey was conducted with healthcare professionals involved in the care of adults with chronic kidney disease. The survey comprised four sections aimed to uncover participants' attitudes and beliefs toward sexual health, experience of sexual health training and practice, and barriers to discussing sexual health. Recruitment and data collection were conducted through social media and professional renal networks between December 2022 and April 2023. Descriptive statistics (means, standard deviations, frequencies, and percentages) were employed to summarise responses. Bivariate analyses were conducted to examine differences in sexual health attitude and belief scores across participants' age, sex, and professional experience. Open-ended responses were summarised descriptively.

Results

A total of 135 participants completed the survey. Most were female nurses aged 35-54, working in haemodialysis, with more than 10 years' experience. Almost 80% had not received any sexual health training in their current or previous roles. The average attitude score was 35.49 ± 6.95, suggesting a relatively positive attitude. Ninety percent believed that addressing sexual health is essential for optimising patients' health outcomes. Key barriers included a lack of training, insufficient knowledge, and cultural or religious considerations.

Conclusion

Training for healthcare professionals on addressing sexual health in renal care is limited. Educational initiatives are required to improve professionals' confidence and competence in discussing sexual health.

title: Effect of Field Dimension on Energy Expenditure and Exercise Intensity During Walking Football in Older Adults.
authorString: Varela S, Blanco-Martínez N, Chapela JMR, Ayán-Pérez C.
abstractText: Walking football (WF) is an adapted low-impact form of traditional football designed to promote physical activity and social interaction among older adults. However, evidence on its physiological demands-particularly energy expenditure expressed in metabolic equivalents (METs)-remains limited. This cross-sectional experimental study aimed to estimate the energy expenditure of WF in older adults and to examine whether field dimensions influence the exercise intensity of the game. Twenty recreational male WF players (mean age = 66.8 ± 6.5 years) participated in 6-a-side matches on two official field sizes. Physical activity and accelerometry-derived estimates of energy expenditure and METs were monitored using wrist-worn triaxial accelerometers (Axivity AX3). Subjective enjoyment was assessed using the feeling scale (FS). Mean energy expenditure was 6.79 ± 1.30 kcal·min<sup>-1</sup> (4.81 ± 0.91 METs) on the large field and 6.58 ± 1.36 kcal·min<sup>-1</sup> (4.66 ± 0.91 METs) on the small field, with no significant differences between conditions. Participants spent a greater proportion of time in motion on the larger field (ES: 0.340; p < 0.05), whereas enjoyment (FS) was significantly higher on the smaller field (ES: 0.708; p < 0.05). Walking speed averaged 0.8 m·s<sup>-1</sup> across both formats. Strong correlations were found between steps, cadence, and METs (rho > 0.70, p < 0.01). WF elicits a moderate-intensity physical activity response (≈4.5 METs) in older adults, independent of field size. These findings primarily support the feasibility of WF as a moderate-intensity community-based intervention, while suggesting that field-size manipulation within normative ranges has limited physiological impact.

title: Deuterium-Oxide Labelling Proteomics Illustrates the Importance of Sample Timing and the Limitations of Serial Biopsies.
authorString: O'Reilly CL, Taylor ME, Kobak KA, Chiao YA, Sadygov RG, Kinter MT, Miller BF.

journal.title: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle

abstractText:
Background

Measuring in vivo protein synthesis is important for testing how interventions, disease and ageing remodel the proteome. A limitation of approaches using short-term infusions of labelled amino acids was that long-term changes had to be extrapolated from short-term measurements. Deuterium oxide (D2O) is now widely used because it can measure protein synthesis over periods of days to weeks. We previously showed that the duration of labelling impacts measured protein synthesis, but many still employ repeated tissue sampling during D2O provision. We hypothesized that the timing of tissue sampling alters which proteins contribute to the overall protein fractional synthesis rate (FSR), thereby invalidating comparisons between serial samples collected during continuous labelling.

Methods

To test this hypothesis, we used a five-timepoint (0d, 4d, 15d, 30d and 45d) D2O labelling time course followed by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry proteomics to calculate individual protein synthesis rates and plateau values in mouse gastrocnemius muscle. Individual proteins were stratified into slow and fast groups, such that each group was responsible for the slowest or fastest 20% of total synthesis over the first 4 days of labelling, respectively.

Results

In a 4-day period representing a baseline period, the synthesis rate of summed proteins was 2.09%/day. When the period was extended to 15, 30 or 45 days, the synthesis rates of summed proteins declined to 1.64%, 1.31% and 1.10%/day, respectively. The contribution of slow and fast proteins to these rates changed as a function of time. The fast and slow proteins accounted for 4.3% and 34.0% of measured proteome abundance, respectively. From Day 0 to Day 4, fast and slow proteins contributed 19.8% and 20.2% of the calculated FSR, respectively. By Day 45, these contributions shifted to 6.5% and 28.8%. Further, we demonstrated that the assumption that the fraction new of proteins linearly increases to 100% new is not true for the majority of proteins. Instead, most proteins plateaued at some point less than 100%, which stops their individual contribution to a summed protein synthesis rate.

Conclusions

In continuous long-term labelling studies, biopsy timing changes the measured bulk FSR because the relative contributions of individual proteins to that measurement over time. Fast proteins that plateau early decrease their contribution as labelling time increases. These findings indicate that studies with different labelling periods, or multiple biopsies over time during continuous labelling of days to weeks cannot be compared to biopsies taken at other times in the labelling period.

title: Multi-Omics Mendelian Randomization Prioritizes Candidate Druggable Genes for Major Depressive Disorder.
authorString: Zhou H, Liu Q, Yan H, Jin G, Zhou W, Yin X, Wang N, Zheng M, Zheng H, Wu Y.
abstractText: This study aimed to prioritize candidate druggable genes for major depressive disorder (MDD) using Mendelian randomization (MR) integrated with expression (eQTL) and protein quantitative trait loci (pQTL) data. We conducted a systematic MR analysis combining cis-eQTL and cis-pQTL data from blood and brain tissues to assess the causal effects of druggable genes on MDD, using FinnGen R9 GWAS summary statistics. Bayesian colocalization analysis confirmed shared genetic variants, while sensitivity analyses (MR-Egger, weighted median, MR-PRESSO) tested robustness. A phenome-wide MR (Phe-MR) assessed broader trait associations. To evaluate translational potential, we mapped candidate genes to known drugs using DrugBank, ChEMBL, and ClinicalTrials.gov.Six candidate druggable genes (MAPK3, PSMB9, SIGLEC9, MST1, BTN3A1, and TAPBP) showed significant associations with MDD across multiple eQTL and pQTL datasets. These genes are involved in biological processes related to neuroinflammation, immune regulation, and apoptosis. Colocalization analyses supported shared genetic signals between the identified genes and MDD, while phenome-wide analyses identified associations with additional diseases and traits that may be relevant for future translational research. Through MR analysis, six candidate druggable genes were prioritized from 6889 potential druggable genes as significantly associated with MDD. Among them, MAPK3, MST1, and SIGLEC9 showed consistent evidence across multiple analyses and emerged as genetically supported candidate targets for future investigation.

title: The Association of Early Graft Dysfunction and CYP3A5 Genotype With Tacrolimus Exposure in Adult Kidney Transplant Recipients.
authorString: Zimmerman MS, Pasternak AL, Patil S, Zöllner S, Park JM.
abstractText:
Introduction

The incidence of early graft dysfunction following kidney transplantation is rising due to the expanded use of marginal organs. Prior studies have suggested that acute kidney dysfunction causes renohepatic crosstalk and tacrolimus metabolism may be decreased. It is also well known that tacrolimus metabolism and dosing requirements differ significantly based on a recipient's CYP3A5 genotype. The objective of this study was to investigate the interplay between early graft function and pharmacogenetics on tacrolimus dose requirements in adult kidney transplant recipients.

Methods

This was a single-center, retrospective cohort study of adult kidney transplant recipients who received immediate-release tacrolimus and had CYP3A5 genotypes available. Immediate graft function (IGF) was defined as serum creatinine decrease of ≥ 10% from baseline and urine output ≥ 0.5 mL/kg/h on post-operative day (POD) 1. Tacrolimus dose-normalized trough concentration (C/D) on POD 2 was compared between patients with IGF and non-IGF using Mann-Whitney U test. Patients were then grouped by both IGF and CYP3A5 genotype, and the differences in C/D considering these factors were analyzed by Mann Whitney U test and a multivariable linear regression analysis.

Results

A total of 242 patients were included, 185 with IGF and 57 with non-IGF. The median [IQR: interquartile range] of tacrolimus C/D was higher in non-IGF than IGF (200.0 [129.7-327.1] vs. 134.0 [95.0-197.4] [ng/ml]/[mg/kg/day], p < 0.001). Among CYP3A5 nonexpressers, the median [IQR] of tacrolimus C/D was 73% higher in non-IGF than IGF (263.3 [177.5-390.1] vs. 151.8 [105.1-214.1] [ng/ml]/[mg/kg/day], p < 0.001), and 16% higher in CYP3A5 expressers with non-IGF versus IGF (116.2 [102.3-199.5] vs. 101.1 [72.5-131.0] [ng/ml]/[mg/kg/day], p = 0.01). In the multivariable linear regression model, the effects of IGF and CYP3A5 expression on tacrolimus C/D remained significant.

Conclusion

Patients with early graft dysfunction who were CYP3A5 nonexpressers had the highest tacrolimus exposure. Initial tacrolimus dose reductions may be considered in kidney transplant recipients who are at risk for non-IGF, especially in CYP3A5 nonexpressers.

title: Bioremediation of Chlorpyrifos Contaminated Soil: Microcosm Investigation and 16S rRNA Gene Amplicon Sequencing.
authorString: Nhi-Cong LT, Toan VD, Lam DV, Mai TT, Mai CTN, Anh BTK, Linh DD.
abstractText: This study describes the isolation and characterization of two biofilm-forming bacterial strains, Pseudomonas aeruginosa MD3 and Bacillus toyonensis LD07, capable of degrading chlorpyrifos. These isolates demonstrated remarkable phenotypic plasticity, maintaining biofilm formation across varying pH, temperature and salinity levels. To maximize microbial stability and metabolic efficiency, sugarcane bagasse was utilized as a support matrix. Analytical characterization (EDX, BET and XRD) confirmed that the bagasse possesses a highly porous architecture, serving as a protective scaffold and an auxiliary carbon source for synergistic co-metabolism. A bio-product formulated via solid-state fermentation on this matrix exhibited exceptional bioremediation efficacy, eliminating 99% of chlorpyrifos at an extreme concentration of 4500 ppm within 35 days. Furthermore, 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing of coffee-growing soils across different treatments (natural control, pesticide-stressed and 10% bio-product amended) with accession numbers PRJNA1529359 revealed distinct shifts in microbial community dynamics. While the taxonomic landscape was broadly dominated by Bacillota, Pseudomonadota and Actinomycetota, the bio-product amendment caused P. aeruginosa and B. toyonensis to become the dominant taxa. Ultimately, these insights underscore the viability of cost-effective agricultural by-products for cell immobilization and highlight metagenomics as a powerful predictive framework for monitoring the remediation of anthropogenically stressed ecosystems.

title: Self-Reported Awareness of Periodontal-Systemic Health Associations Among Physicians: A Descriptive Cross-Sectional Study.
authorString: Arpaci A, Lermi AE, Silahtar AN, Meşeli SE.

journal.title: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice

abstractText:
Rationale, aims and objectives

Physicians' recognition of oral-systemic health relationships may support medical-dental communication, although its relationship with clinical practice remains uncertain. This study described overall and disease-specific patterns of self-reported awareness in a convenience sample of physicians in Türkiye and explored differences according to demographic and professional characteristics.

Method

This descriptive cross-sectional online survey included physicians with at least 1 year of clinical experience who were recruited through professional networks. Following ethical approval, responses included in the final dataset were submitted between 17 March and 7 May 2026. Self-reported awareness was assessed using a Turkish-adapted 10-item questionnaire that had not undergone formal cross-cultural validation. The items formed a study-specific summary index ranging from 0 to 40 (Cronbach's α = 0.847). Disease-specific responses were treated as the primary findings, whereas the summary index and subgroup comparisons were secondary and exploratory.

Results

Among 109 physicians, the median summary index score was 34/40 (IQR: 30-38), and the mean was 33.26 ± 6.67. Twenty-five participants (22.9%) attained the maximum score, indicating a substantial ceiling effect and limited discrimination at the upper end. Agreement was highest for the general oral-systemic relationship (98.2%), the impact of oral disease on quality of life (96.3%), and the periodontal disease-cardiovascular disease association (93.6%). Recognition was lower for chronic kidney disease (63.3%) and rheumatoid arthritis (54.1%). Exploratory estimates for sex, specialist status, and graduation year were imprecise, with confidence intervals including zero and allowing potentially meaningful associations in either direction.

Conclusion

In this convenience sample, self-reported awareness was generally high but varied across specific periodontal-systemic associations. The findings represent self-reported recognition rather than objective knowledge, competence, or referral behaviour and should not be generalised to physicians in Türkiye overall. Representative samples, validated instruments, and objective or vignette-based measures are needed to determine whether self-reported awareness is associated with oral-health assessment or dental referral.

title: AHR2 as a Potential Integrator of Eco-Evo-Devo in Non-Mammalian Vertebrates: A Focus on Fishes.
authorString: Lofeu L, Sturmbauer C, Ahi EP.
abstractText: Aryl hydrocarbon receptor 2 (AHR2) is increasingly recognized as a distinctive member of the AHR family in non-mammalian vertebrates, where it acts as a ligand-activated transcription factor linking environmental cues to developmental and physiological outcomes. The most extensive AHR2-specific evidence for these functions currently comes from fishes. Although the AHR pathway has traditionally been framed through responses to environmental contaminants, it also responds to endogenous, dietary, microbiota-derived and other exogenous small molecules. This review focuses on AHR2 because its distinctive evolutionary history and the convergence of receptor-specific evidence across development, chemical responsiveness and adaptation make it a particularly informative candidate interface linking chemical sensing, development and evolution. We first consider the origin and diversification of the AHR2 paralog, its ligand spectrum, signaling partners and regulatory context. Organismal studies, with primary emphasis on fishes, are then used to examine AHR2-dependent roles in craniofacial, cardiac, skeletal, reproductive and behavioral development, as well as variation in chemical sensitivity among paralogs, species and populations. Evidence from pollution-adapted killifish and Atlantic tomcod directly connects heritable AHR-pathway variation with altered chemical responses and local adaptation. By contrast, proposed links among natural ligand variation, AHR2-dependent developmental plasticity and morphological divergence remain incompletely tested. Examples from other vertebrate groups provide comparative context for receptor retention, loss and functional divergence. By expanding the attention on development, ecology and evolution rather than on the toxicological endpoints alone, this fish-centred perspective presents AHR2 as a useful model for testing how chemical environments may influence developmental reaction norms, evolutionary responses and population resilience.

title: Histamine-3 Receptor Activation Reduces Cardiac Fibrosis Through Direct Inhibition of Collagen Processing in Cardiac Fibroblasts.
authorString: Linsky H, Herrnreiter A, Dariano D, Webb B, Campbell WB, Widiapradja A, Levick SP.
abstractText:
Background and purpose

Fibrosis is a major contributor to diastolic dysfunction that underlies cardiac disease, such as heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. We previously established that exogenous histamine-3 receptor activation inhibits cardiac fibrosis in angiotensin II-infused mice. The present study aimed to determine the cellular mechanisms underlying the antifibrotic effect of the histamine-3 receptor, with a focus on cardiac fibroblasts.

Experimental approach

8-week-old male wild-type C57BL/6J mice underwent saline or angiotensin II (Ang II, 1500 ng/kg/min) infusion with or without concomitant treatment with the histamine-3 receptor agonist, imetit dihydrobromide (40 mg/kg/day) for 7 days. Left ventricles were assessed for cardiac function, fibrosis, and hypertrophy. Proteomic analysis was performed to assess proteomic profiles between groups. Primary mouse cardiac fibroblast cultures were treated with TGF-β1 (30 ng/mL) and Imetit (300 nM) to assess collagen transcription, release, retention, and cellular signaling mechanisms.

Key results

Exogenous histamine-3 receptor activation with Imetit inhibited cardiac fibrosis and cardiomyocyte hypertrophy in Ang II-infused mice. Proteomic analysis identified distinct left ventricle proteomic profiles between Saline and Ang II mice. Imetit inhibited collagen I release, while promoting migration and intracellular collagen I retention in TGF-β1-treated mouse cardiac fibroblasts, potentially by inhibiting HSP-47 and reducing the phosphorylation of P38 MAP kinase.

Conclusion and implications

Histamine-3 receptor activation inhibits cardiac fibrosis through a proposed mechanism involving collagen retention by cardiac fibroblasts, thereby, reducing released collagen. This study provides key insights into the histamine-3 receptor as a potential therapeutic target for cardiac fibrosis.

title: Perspectives on Physical Activity in Nephrology: An Explorative Cross-Sectional Survey of Adults With Chronic Kidney Disease and Nephrology Nurses.
authorString: Jakobsen MS, Finderup J, Ml Young H, Pedersen M, Molsted S.
abstractText:
Background

Persons with chronic kidney disease are often physically inactive, despite evidence supporting the benefits of physical activity. However, implementation of physical activity in clinical practice remains limited.

Objectives

To investigate and compare informational needs and priorities regarding physical activity among persons with chronic kidney disease and nephrology nurses.

Methods

This cross-sectional survey included adults with chronic kidney disease and nephrology nurses in Denmark. Participants reported their need for information on physical activity, preferred educational formats and preferred clinical monitoring approaches.

Results

A total of 82 persons with chronic kidney disease and 107 nurses participated. Both groups expressed a need for more information on exercise modalities, safety, and the effects of physical activity. Nurses more frequently requested information on exercise modalities (78.5% vs. 63.4%, p = 0.013) and motivational strategies (79.4%). Patients more often preferred physical activity level as a clinical monitoring parameter (69.5%), whereas nurses preferred physical function (66.4%) (p = 0.013). Audiovisual materials were widely requested by both groups.

Conclusions

Persons with chronic kidney disease and nephrology nurses share substantial informational needs regarding physical activity, although differences exist in preferred monitoring approaches. Developing aligned educational resources and incorporating motivational strategies may support implementation of physical activity in clinical practice. Due to exploratory nature, the findings of this study should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory.

title: Oral Health-Related Quality of Life, Perceived Stress, and Well-Being in Oral Lichen Planus Subtypes.
authorString: Stolte KN, Dogan SS, Attia S, Dommisch H.
abstractText:
Objective

Oral lichen planus (OLP) is a chronic inflammatory mucosal disease with reticular and erosive clinical subtypes. This study aimed to compare oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL), stress, and general well-being between participants with reticular OLP, erosive OLP, and healthy controls.

Material and methods

In this single-center cross-sectional study, healthy controls (n = 20) and patients with reticular (n = 20) or erosive OLP (n = 20) completed the OHIP-G14, PSS-10, and WHO-5-questionnaires, and group differences were evaluated.

Results

Patients with OLP reported significantly poorer OHRQoL than controls (OHIP-G14 total score: 13.18 ± 10.01 vs. 2.85 ± 6.54; p < 0.001). Significant group differences were observed across all OHIP-G14 subdomains. Erosive OLP showed higher scores than reticular OLP across domains, though subtype differences were not significant. In both OLP groups, the highest mean scores were observed for physical pain and psychological discomfort. No significant between-group differences were observed for PSS-10 or WHO-5 (all p ≥ 0.259). Interpretation is limited by differences in baseline characteristics between groups.

Conclusion

Patients with OLP reported poorer OHRQoL than healthy controls, whereas differences between reticular and erosive OLP were not significant. The findings suggest that oral-specific and generic patient-reported outcome measures capture complementary aspects of patient experience, with OHIP-G14 reflecting oral disease-specific burden in OLP.

title: Investigating Causal Relationships Between Major Mental Disorders and Hypertension Subtypes and Their Complications: A Mendelian Randomization Study.
authorString: Su J, Zhang J, Ding Y, Ying Y.
abstractText: The association between major psychiatric disorders (major depression, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia) and hypertension has long been of clinical and research interest. Using publicly available summary data from large-scale genome-wide association studies (GWASs), we selected, quality-controlled, and clustered eligible genetic variants for the three psychiatric disorders and hypertension-related outcomes. The inverse variance weighted (IVW) method was applied as the primary analysis, with a suite of sensitivity analyses including MR-Egger regression, weighted median estimator (WME), and leave-one-out analysis performed to assess result robustness and detect potential horizontal pleiotropy. False discovery rate (FDR) correction was implemented to multiple testing. Bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) identified a reciprocal causal association between major depression and essential hypertension. Genetically predicted major depression was significantly associated with an increased risk of essential hypertension [IVW: odds ratio (OR) 1.247, 95% confidence interval (CI) (1.117-1.393), p < 0.001; WME: OR 1.243, 95% CI (1.127-1.371), p < 0.001]. Conversely, genetic predisposition to essential hypertension also increased the risk of major depression (IVW: OR 1.028, 95% CI (1.007-1.050), p = 0.008), which remained significant after FDR correction. We found that bipolar disorder was causally associated with essential hypertension, hypertensive heart disease, and hypertensive renal disease (p < 0.05). In contrast, no causal associations were observed between schizophrenia and any hypertension subtypes or complications (p > 0.05). All sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the primary effect estimates, with no evidence of significant horizontal pleiotropy or influential outliers. In conclusion, our study, conducted under the MR framework from the perspective of genetic susceptibility, supports a bidirectional causal relationship between major depression and essential hypertension.

title: Prognostic value of right atrial pressure to cardiac output slope in patients undergoing exercise right heart catheterization.
authorString: Müller J, Douschan P, Mayer L, Lichtblau M, Andersen MJ, Barberà JA, Blanco I, Caravita S, Condliffe R, D'Alto M, Egenlauf B, Ewert R, Galiè N, Grünig E, Heine A, Herkenrath S, Herve P, Houston BA, Hsu S, Humbert M, Kasperowicz K, Kurzyna M, Lewis GD, Mak S, Malhotra R, Maron BA, McCabe C, Oliveira RKF, Olschewski H, Rosenkranz S, Savale L, Souza R, Systrom D, Tedford RJ, Tello K, Vonk-Noordegraaf A, Kovacs G, Ulrich S, PEX-NET (Pulmonary Haemodynamics during Exercise Network) ERS Clinical Research Collaboration.

journal.title: Annals of the American Thoracic Society

abstractText:
Background/aims

This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of the right atrial pressure to cardiac output relationship (RAP/CO-slope) from rest to end exercise in patients undergoing exercise right heart catheterization for suspected or confirmed pulmonary hypertension (PH).

Methods

The analysis used data from the retrospective arm of the Pulmonary Hemodynamics during Exercise Network (PEX NET), a multicenter collaboration involving 23 PH centers. Patients were included if resting and exercise measurements were obtained in the same body position and if RAP/CO-slopes were available. Cox proportional hazard models adjusted for age, sex, and hemoglobin were applied. Time dependent ROC curves were used to identify a prognostic cut off.

Results

A total of 856 patients were included (median age 59 years; 67% female), of whom 336 had PH. Over a median follow up of 6.5 years, 114 patients (13%) died. Higher RAP/CO-slopes were independently associated with increased mortality, even after adjusting for established resting and exercise hemodynamics (hazard ratio 1.08, 95%CI: 1.03-1.13, p < 0.001). Among patients with manifest PH at rest, a RAP/CO-slope ≥1.0 mmHg·min·L⁻¹ was linked to a 2.2 fold higher mortality risk (hazard ratio: 2.20; 95% CI: 1.1-4.5; p = 0.032) compared with slopes <1.0 mmHg·min·L⁻¹. In a multivariable model including NT proBNP, 6 minute walking distance, and WHO functional class, the RAP/CO-slope remained the strongest predictor of mortality.

Conclusion

The RAP/CO-slope is a strong, independent prognostic marker across a spectrum of RV afterload stress. A RAP/CO slope ≥1 mmHg·min·L⁻¹ was identified as particularly predictive in manifest PH.

title: Fluorouracil-Associated Coronary Vasospasm and Reversible Cardiomyopathy Mimicking ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction During a First Cycle of FOLFOX: A Case Report.
authorString: Alyacoub R, Veras Victoria A.

journal.title: The American journal of case reports

abstractText: BACKGROUND 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) is a mainstay chemotherapeutic agent for gastrointestinal malignancies but carries a recognized risk of cardiotoxicity, most often manifesting as coronary vasospasm that can mimic acute myocardial infarction. This report describes the case of a 50-year-old woman with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) due to coronary artery vasospasm during continuous infusion of 5-FU as part of the first round of FOLinic acid (leucovorin), Fluorouracil (5-FU), and OXaliplatin (FOLFOX) chemotherapy for colorectal carcinoma. CASE REPORT A 50-year-old woman with colorectal carcinoma receiving her first cycle of FOLFOX developed severe chest pain during a continuous infusion of 5-FU. Initial emergency department evaluation was reportedly unremarkable, and she was discharged after symptomatic improvement with ketorolac. She returned emergently with recurrent crushing chest pain; a repeat electrocardiogram showed hyperacute T waves and ST-segment elevation, prompting ST-elevation myocardial infarction activation and transfer for emergent catheterization. Coronary angiography revealed no obstructive coronary artery disease. Echocardiography demonstrated a severely reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 30% to 35% with apical akinesis, consistent with 5-FU-induced cardiomyopathy. 5-FU was permanently discontinued, and the patient was treated with vasodilator therapy, with complete resolution of symptoms and normalization of ventricular function on follow-up echocardiography. CONCLUSIONS 5-FU can precipitate life-threatening coronary vasospasm and a fully reversible cardiomyopathy even during a first chemotherapy cycle, in the absence of obstructive coronary artery disease. Early recognition, prompt drug interruption, and a multidisciplinary cardio-oncology approach, including an individualized decision between permanent discontinuation and carefully supervised rechallenge, are essential to guide safe oncologic decision-making.
