We delineate how the interconnected signalling networks that govern these pathways are coordinated at the cellular and organismal levels and how their dysregulation drives disease progression. We also emphasise translating mechanistic insights into clinical practice by critically evaluating pharmacological strategies. Furthermore, this review systematically describes how an improved understanding of pathway crosstalk mechanisms, the discovery of predictive biomarkers, and advances in targeted delivery systems collectively drive the development of precision therapeutic strategies. Finally, we discuss current challenges in achieving on-target specificity and minimising off-tumour toxicity, and we outline future directions for integrating these approaches into immunomodulatory and combination frameworks. By bridging fundamental cell biology with translational medicine, this review aims to illuminate both the conceptual foundations and the clinical potential of targeting cell death in human diseases.

title: Prevalence, Clinical Characteristics, and Hemodynamic Impact of Coronary Artery-Ventricular Microfistulas in Patients with Fontan Circulation.
authorString: Higashi K, Nakajima H, Aotsuka H.
abstractText: Coronary artery-ventricular microfistulas (CAMFs), which are defined as diffuse communications between dilated coronary arteries and the main ventricle, are poorly understood in Fontan circulation. We evaluated their prevalence, clinical features, and longitudinal hemodynamics. We retrospectively reviewed 167 Fontan patients undergoing cardiac catheterization between 2005 and 2025. Excluded were sinusoidal communications in PA/IVS, LV fistulas in HLHS, or solitary focal fistulas. Clinical, surgical, and serial hemodynamic parameters, such as the subendocardial viability ratio (SEVR) and aortic regurgitation (AR) index, were assessed. CAMFs were identified in 6 of the 153 eligible Fontan patients (prevalence: 3.9%). Polysplenia was more frequent in the CAMFs group (33% vs. 5%, ). At initial diagnosis, systemic cardiac index (median 3.3 L/min/m<sup>2</sup> [range, 2.2-3.9 L/min/m<sup>2</sup>]) and ejection fraction (median 52% [range, 44%-65%]) were preserved. Notably, resting SEVR (median 91% [range, 85%-156%]) and AR index (median 54% [range, 44%-59%]) remained stable and well-compensated over a decade of follow-up. Late morbidities included protein-losing enteropathy (17%), pulmonary arteriovenous fistulas (17%), esophageal varices (17%), and death (17%). CAMFs occur in 3.9% of Fontan patients and correlate with polysplenia. Although resting SEVR and AR index remain well-compensated over mid-term follow-up, their impact on long-term outcomes beyond two decades post-Fontan remains uncertain. Careful long-term monitoring is necessary for late extra-cardiac complications and hemodynamic changes.

title: Treatment sequencing for intracardiac masses in pregnancy: a 10-year retrospective cohort of 21 patients
authorString: Yang Y, Wang Q, Qiao Z, Ge Y, Li C, Hu H, Zhu J.
abstractText: Background Intracardiac masses during pregnancy are rare, and treatment decisions must balance timely maternal surgery against fetal exposure to cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). We evaluated a 10-year single-center experience, focusing on gestational-age-based treatment sequencing and maternal and pregnancy outcomes. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 21 women who underwent surgery for an intracardiac mass associated with pregnancy between April 2016 and July 2026. Strategies were classified by actual sequence: antenatal surgery with intended pregnancy continuation, delivery followed by cardiac surgery during the same anesthetic session, postpartum cardiac surgery, and concurrent early-pregnancy termination and surgery. Follow-up ended on 31 August 2026. Analyses were descriptive. Results Histopathology showed 19 myxomas, 1 hemangioma, and 1 lipoma. Antenatal surgery with intended pregnancy continuation was performed in 14 women at 15.8 ± 3.4 gestational weeks; delivery-prioritized management in 4 at 35–39 weeks; postpartum surgery in 2 at 49 and 57 days after delivery; and concurrent termination and surgery in 1 at 9 weeks. Mean CPB time was 55.9 ± 17.9 min; mean aortic cross-clamp time was 34.2 ± 16.1 min among 20 patients who underwent cross-clamping. There were 17 live births (81.0%), 3 terminations (14.3%), and 1 ongoing pregnancy (4.8%). No in-hospital maternal death or predefined major maternal perioperative complication occurred. Median maternal follow-up was 23.9 months (range, 1.3–124.1), with no death or tumor recurrence documented. Conclusions Individualized sequencing of cardiac surgery and delivery was associated with favorable observed outcomes in this selected surgical cohort. Antenatal resection may be considered before fetal maturity when maternal risk precludes waiting, whereas delivery before cardiac surgery may be appropriate near fetal maturity. These findings support multidisciplinary planning in experienced centers, while conclusions remain constrained by the observational design and small sample size.

title: <span data-teams="true">Biphasic Digital Twin for Dynamic Coronary Occlusion Risk of TAVR: Beyond Static Anatomical Assessment
authorString: Luo C, Li C, Chen S, Yan C, Li Y.
abstractText: Coronary occlusion (CO) is a lethal complication of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) (incidence, 0.35%–4.0%; in-hospital mortality, approximately 50%). Although static computed tomography thresholds (ostial height >12 mm) remain the assessment standard, CO still occurs in 14.3% of patients meeting them. We developed a biphasic digital twin (BDT) integrating systolic and diastolic electrocardiogram-gated computed tomography angiography to assess dynamic CO risk in a 71-year-old woman with severe aortic stenosis. Biphasic aortic root dynamics and bilateral virtual valve-to-coronary distance (VTC) were evaluated at two implantation depths. Ostial height varied by approximately 5%, whereas leaflet volume increased by 22.0% in diastole. Right coronary ostial displacement (4.28 mm) was 1.74-fold that of the left (2.46 mm), and the sinotubular junction rotated 8.7°. A commissural calcified mass remained stable. Implantation 5 mm deeper reduced diastolic left VTC from 8.96 to 6.54 mm (–27%) but increased systolic right VTC from 4.57 to 5.93 mm (+29%). Delayed CO occurred 30 min after extubation despite patent intra-procedural angiography; surgery confirmed calcified anchoring, stent deflection, and coronary compression. Static coronary height did not capture dynamic CO risk in this patient. BDT may support individualised, biphasic, bilateral assessment by integrating dynamic leaflet expansion, asymmetric root motion, and calcified anchoring.

title: Case Volumes and Outcomes of Early-Career Operators Performing TAVR in the United States.
authorString: Salah HM, Manandhar P, Baron S, Batchelor W, Cohen D, Harrison JK, Hughes GC, Lowenstern A, Pineda AM, Pride YB, Thourani VH, Vekstein AM, Wang A, Wegermann Z, Young MN, Vemulapalli S, Rymer JA.
abstractText:
Background

Operator experience is a key determinant of outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, whether early-career operators achieve comparable results to more experienced peers is unknown. Herein, we evaluate case volumes, patient risk profiles, and 30-day outcomes of early-career versus non-early-career operators performing TAVR in the United States.

Methods

Using the Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapies Registry, we identified isolated TAVR procedures from October 2011 through March 2024. Early-career status was defined as ≤5 years in independent practice (based on board certification or first TAVR date); non-early-career status was >5 years. Multivariable hierarchical models adjusted for patient-, procedural-, operator-, and site-level factors, including annualized institutional TAVR volume, while accounting for clustering of procedures within operators and operators within sites. Primary outcomes were 30-day mortality and a composite of death, stroke, major bleeding, stage III acute kidney injury, or moderate-to-severe paravalvular leak.

Results

A total of 634 723 TAVR procedures were performed by 3126 operators across 847 sites, including 90 376 (14.2%) by early-career operators. Median annualized lifetime volume was lower for early-career operators (13 [interquartile range, 5-31] versus 19 [interquartile range, 7-42] cases per year; P<0.001). After adjustment, 30-day mortality was similar between early-career and non-early-career operators (2.38% versus 2.44%; risk ratio, 0.97 [95% CI, 0.92-1.01]; P=0.293), whereas the composite end point was lower among early-career operators (11.19% versus 11.77%; risk ratio, 0.95 [95% CI, 0.93-0.98]; P<0.001).

Conclusions

In a national TAVR registry, early-career operators performed fewer cases but achieved similar 30-day mortality and a modestly lower adjusted composite event rate relative to more experienced peers. These findings suggest that within the structured, team-based environment of contemporary TAVR programs, early-career status alone is not associated with inferior procedural outcomes and should not be viewed as a barrier to independent practice.

title: How prenatal residential greenness links to congenital heart defects: The role of multi-pollutant mediating pathways and non-linear exposure-response.
authorString: Wang X, Zuo S, Huang Z, Qiu Y, Dai S, Ju J, Chen X, Chu H, Wu J, Chi Y, Liu X, Alemayehu B, Ren Y, Yang X.
abstractText: Background Rapid urbanization has intensified cardiovascular burdens, particularly congenital heart defects (CHDs), a leading cause of neonatal mortality globally. The first trimester is the critical exposure window, which results in the cardiac septation and outflow tract formation. The vegetation may affect air pollutants through processes such as purification, dust retention, and temperature regulation. These pollutants have been linked to disrupted embryonic cardiogenesis. Methods We conducted a case-control study using Xiamen birth records for January 2016 to June 2019, comprising 1785 infants with CHDs and 1848 without. After applying 1:1 propensity score matching, 890 pairs (1780 neonates) were retained. Exposure was quantified as NDVI in 250, 500 and 1000 m buffers and as 23 landscape indices. Multi-pollutant mediation models were fitted for NO<sub>2</sub>, PM<sub>2.5</sub>, SO<sub>2</sub> and O<sub>3</sub>. Results Maternal first-trimester exposure was associated with lower CHD odds. At 1 km, large core patches and high connectivity were associated with lower odds, whereas fragmentation and high edge density were associated with higher odds. Indirect associations appeared through NO<sub>2</sub> and PM<sub>2.5</sub>, largest for NO<sub>2</sub>. The SO<sub>2</sub> pathway was shared with these two and did not persist when all four pollutants were modelled together. The NDVI-NO<sub>2</sub> relation was non-linear, with a population-specific turning point at an NDVI of about 0.46. The inverse association was stronger off-island, during high-temperature periods, and among mothers with shorter gestational periods. The O<sub>3</sub> indirect estimate was positive at 1 km. Conclusions Planning should shift from quantity-based expansion to morphology-oriented strategies prioritising connectivity and vulnerable groups.

title: SUDDEN CARDIAC ARREST IN NEW SOUTH WALES (NSW), AUSTRALIA: A DATA LINKAGE STUDY.
authorString: Sweeting J, Leslie F, Yeates L, Butters A, Brown J, Stafford F, Lawley CM, Shajedur Rahman Shawon M, Vandenberg J, Dennis M, Evens T, Nedkoff L, Paratz E, Ingles J.
abstractText:
Background

Sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) is a global health challenge. Routinely collected health data represents a potential source of data to identify SCA.

Objective

Evaluate whether routinely collected health data can retrospectively identify community-based SCA (1-50 years) in NSW.

Methods

Potential SCA cases (aged 1-50yrs; occurring in NSW; cardiac-related ICD-9/10/SNOMED codes) were identified by the Centre for Health Record Linkage (CHeReL) in the NSW Ambulance OHCA Register (OHCAR) and NSW Emergency Department Data Collection (EDDC). Probabilistic data linkage was undertaken between ambulance, hospital and mortality datasets. External causes were excluded at case identification in ambulance records. Cardiac aetiology was assigned where a cardiac diagnosis appeared in hospital admission or cause of death records.

Results

From 1.7 million linked records, 13,345 presumed SCA cases were identified; 54% had cardiac aetiology and 83% were fatal. Cardiac cases were older than non-cardiac cases (median 42 vs 37 years, p < 0.001) and more likely to be admitted to hospital (58% vs 7%, p < 0.001). Within cardiac cases, rhythm-related and structural diagnoses dominated in 1-11 year olds, while ischaemic disease dominated in 35-50 year olds. Older cardiac cases were more likely to die pre-hospital (adjusted OR 3.56, 95% CI 2.66-4.85, for 35-50 vs 1-11 years).

Conclusionx

Multi-source administrative data linkage identifies age-related patterns in SCA aetiology and clinical trajectory. Findings extrapolated nationally suggest approximately 370 cardiac SCA deaths per year in Australians aged 1 to 35, a substantial burden that could be tracked through routine data linkage.

title: Clinical risk factors associated with acute hypertension-mediated organ damage in patients presenting with severe hypertension: A retrospective cohort study from Qatar.
authorString: Barjas H, Al-Balushi S, Joudeh AI, Alabbas Y, Almzori M, Afzal M, Ata F, Qassim A, Fathi B, Almayoof M, Berjis Z, Faisal M, Alwassiti W, Abdurabu M, Naji D, Alameen O, Sadik N.

journal.title: Clinical and experimental hypertension (New York, N.Y. : 1993)

abstractText: Severe hypertension is a common reason for emergency department (ED) visits and is associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Identifying factors associated with acute hypertension-mediated organ damage (HMOD) may improve risk stratification. A large retrospective cohort study across four hospitals in Qatar (January 2015-January 2020). Adults presenting to the ED with severe hypertension (systolic blood pressure [SBP] ≥ 180 mmHg and/or diastolic blood pressure [DBP] ≥ 110 mmHg) were included. In a cross-sectional primary analysis, the outcome was hypertensive emergency, defined as acute HMOD present at the index presentation, and univariable and multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with acute HMOD at presentation. A separate exploratory longitudinal secondary analysis described cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, and renal complications over three years of follow-up using descriptive statistics was conducted. Discrimination and calibration were assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and Hosmer-Lemeshow test. Of 881 patients (median age 50 years [IQR 43-57]; 68.8% male), 94.7% had severe asymptomatic hypertension and 5.3% presented with hypertensive emergency. Independent factors associated with acute HMOD were higher admission SBP (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.016, 95% CI 1.000-1.033), higher DBP (aOR 1.027, 95% CI 1.006-1.049), chronic kidney disease (aOR 2.38, 95% CI 1.02-5.57), hypertensive retinopathy (aOR 3.82, 95% CI 1.14-12.83), and current smoking (aOR 2.83, 95% CI 1.32-6.06). The model showed good discrimination (AUC 0.77) and adequate calibration. Kidney disease progression was the most common follow-up complication. Elevated admission blood pressure, chronic kidney disease, hypertensive retinopathy, and current smoking were independently associated with acute HMOD. These readily identifiable factors may support ED risk stratification in patients with severe hypertension.

title: Prevalence, Incidence, Clinical Presentation, and Treatment of Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome in Primary Care in the United Kingdom Between 1998 and 2025.
authorString: Shapiro SB, Yu OHY, Dahan MH, Azoulay L.
abstractText: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is a multisystemic disorder with a wide range of health consequences. We sought to describe temporal trends in the prevalence and incidence of PMOS and to characterize its clinical presentation, comorbidity burden, and pharmacological management in primary care in the United Kingdom (UK) between 1998 and 2025. Population-based matched cohort study using primary care records from the UK Clinical Practice Research Datalink. Females newly diagnosed with PMOS between the ages of 15 and 49 matched on age, general practice, calendar year of cohort entry, and duration of medical history to population controls without PMOS. Annual prevalence and incidence of diagnosed PMOS; baseline prevalence and incidence of cardinal PMOS features and various comorbidities; and pre- and post-cohort entry prevalence of hormonal contraceptive, anti-androgen, ovulation-inducing drug, and metformin use. The prevalence of diagnosed PMOS increased from < 0.1% in 1998 to 2.0% in 2025, with incidence rising from 0.1 to 3.6 per 1,000 person-years over the same period. Among 125,482 patients with newly diagnosed PMOS matched with an equal number of controls, patients with PMOS had higher baseline prevalence and incidence of cardinal features of PMOS, as well as diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease, sleep apnea, thyroid disorders, endometriosis, uterine fibroids, chronic pain, depression, and anxiety. Use of anti-androgens, ovulation-inducing drugs, and metformin was substantially higher in patients with PMOS, especially in the year following diagnosis. PMOS is increasingly diagnosed in UK primary care and is associated with substantial multimorbidity and pharmacotherapy.

title: Exploring the Potential Mechanisms Linking Bisphenol A Exposure to Atrial Fibrillation: An Integrated Multi-Dimensional Analysis from Network Toxicology to In Vivo Validation.
authorString: Ning Y, Su Y, Zhong G.

journal.title: Omics : a journal of integrative biology

abstractText: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common clinical arrhythmia with complex pathogenesis and limited therapeutic options. The pro-arrhythmic effect of environmental endocrine disruptor bisphenol A (BPA) remains unclear. This study integrated network toxicology, Mendelian randomization (MR), molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, single-cell transcriptomics and in vivo rat experiments to construct a multi-dimensional evidence chain for exploring BPA-mediated AF mechanisms and key intervention targets. We screened 206 shared targets of BPA and AF, which were enriched in endocrine resistance, phosphoinositide 3-kinase-protein kinase B, and lipid-metabolism pathways. Protein-protein interaction and two-sample MR analyses, supported by genetic evidence, suggested cystatin C (CST3) as a potential risk factor for AF, while glutathione S-transferase A1 (GSTA1) and placental growth factor (PGF) served as potential protective factors. Molecular docking confirmed favorable binding activities between BPA and core targets (binding energy < -5.0 kcal/mol), and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations verified stable complex conformations under physiological conditions. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed cell-type-specific expression of target genes: CST3 in immune and stromal cells, GSTA1 in smooth muscle cells and fibroblasts, and PGF predominantly in smooth muscle cells. Further experiments in Sprague-Dawley rats demonstrated that BPA exposure increased AF inducibility, upregulated atrial CST3, down-regulated GSTA1 and PGF, and aggravated atrial fibrosis and inflammatory infiltration. Collectively, BPA may promote AF by interfering with the functions of CST3, GSTA1, and PGF. This study provides evidence for the pro-arrhythmic effects of environmental pollutants and theoretical references for targeted prevention and treatment of AF.

title: Comparison of outcome in patients with idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) following optic nerve sheath fenestration (ONSF) using a medial transconjunctival approach with dural window or superomedial lid-crease incision approach.
authorString: Maripudi S, Garcia A, Keenum Z, Mei F, Itani K, Mancini R, Tenzel PA.
abstractText: This study compares outcomes and complications of two common optic nerve sheath fenestration (ONSF) approaches for treating vision loss in idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH). This retrospective comparative study included 71 eyes of 48 patients with IIH who underwent ONSF by two oculoplastic surgeons at the University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center from January 2010 to December 2023. Patients were grouped by surgical approach: Group 1 underwent a superomedial lid-crease incision with fenestration, and Group 2 underwent a medial transconjunctival approach with dural window. Outcomes measured included operative time and changes in visual acuity, visual fields, and color vision within a 180-day postoperative period. Complications were also recorded. Fisher's exact test was used to compare favorable outcome rates between groups. Mean operation time was compared using a simple paired t-test. Both surgical approaches were successful in preventing progression of vision loss in patients with IIH. Postoperatively, visual acuity was stable or improved in 97% of Group 1 and 85% of Group 2 patients. Both groups showed stability of visual fields and color vision testing. At 6 months, there was no statistically significant difference in outcome between the groups. Furthermore, mean operation time was approximately 30 min shorter in Group 1 compared to Group 2. Both groups had low complication rates. This study demonstrates that the superomedial lid-crease approach with fenestration and the medial transconjunctival approach with dural window for ONSF are both effective in preventing vision loss in patients with IIH, with similarly low side‑effect profiles.

title: Plasmonically Enhanced Microarray Immunoassay for High-Sensitivity Monitoring of Heart Failure.
authorString: Semeniak D, Acil D, Liu J, Cruz DF, Fontes CM, Li C, Silverstein BE, Felker GM, Hucknall AM, Mikkelsen MH, Chilkoti A.
abstractText: Point‑of‑care testing (POCT) demands diagnostic platforms that pair high analytical sensitivity with compact, low‑cost readout hardware, yet fluorescence‑based immunoassays face a fundamental tradeoff between detector cost and detection performance. Plasmonic nanocavities-such as metal-dielectric-metal nanopatch antennas-offer a powerful signal‑amplification strategy by dramatically enhancing fluorophore emission, enabling sensitive fluorescence detection with inexpensive optics. Here, we introduce a plasmonically enhanced fluorescence microarray immunoassay that integrates nanopatch antennas for high‑sensitivity, low‑cost quantification of key heart‑failure biomarkers, NT‑proBNP, NGAL, and galectin‑3, using a custom smartphone‑based detector. The nanopatch antennas yield up to 485‑fold fluorescence enhancement enabling quantitative and multiplexed detection with limits of detection of 0.055, 3.932, and 0.864 ng/mL, respectively. Analysis of NT‑proBNP-positive human samples shows strong correlation with clinically validated assays, demonstrating the potential of this plasmonically enhanced platform to deliver high‑performance heart‑failure biomarker monitoring at low cost in resource‑limited and point‑of‑care settings.

title: Dsg2 arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy is accompanied by neocortical synaptic changes in adult mice.
authorString: Eichler A, Biermann J, Hemkemeyer SA, Hegermann J, Schinner C, Lenz M.
abstractText: Heart failure is frequently accompanied by cognitive impairment, yet structural correlates in the brain remain incompletely defined. Here, we assessed whether chronic heart failure is associated with synaptic ultrastructural remodeling in the murine neocortex using a mouse model of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy caused by a point mutation in desmoglein-2 (Dsg2-W2A). Brains from aged adult homozygous Dsg2-W2A mice and age-matched wildtype controls were processed for transmission electron microscopy, and excitatory synapses in layer I of the prefrontal cortex were quantitatively assessed, with comparative analyses in the somatosensory cortex. In the prefrontal cortex, presynaptic terminal area and synaptic vesicle number were reduced in mutant mice, whereas postsynaptic measures were not altered. The prevalence of mitochondria and the spine apparatus within synapses was comparable between genotypes, suggesting no major loss of synapse-associated organelles. Finally, synaptic parameters in the prefrontal cortex did not show a systematic dependence on distance to local blood vessels. Together, these findings indicate moderate region- and compartment-specific synaptic ultrastructural alterations associated with Dsg2 cardiomyopathy and chronic heart failure, with predominant effects on presynaptic terminals.

title: Increased prevalence of hypertension in paediatric turner syndrome: a retrospective study.
authorString: Sutherland A, Lucas-Herald AK, Fletcher A, McVey L, Mason A.
abstractText: Girls and women with Turner Syndrome (TS) are known to be at increased risk of aortic dissection, a condition for which hypertension is a modifiable risk factor. Our aim was to determine the frequency of hypertension in girls attending a tertiary paediatric TS clinic and its association with clinical characteristics. Retrospective analysis of clinical data was conducted for girls with TS attending the dedicated paediatric TS clinic at the Royal Hospital for Children Glasgow, between 1976-2023. Blood pressure (BP) was converted to centiles according to age and height. Hypertensive range BPs were defined as BPs ≥ 95<sup>th</sup> centile and pre-hypertensive range BPs were defined as BPs between the 90<sup>th</sup>-95<sup>th</sup> centiles, with measurements on 2 consecutive occasions. 184 girls with TS were included and BP data were available for a total of 172 (93%) with a median (range) age at the time of BP attainment of 12 (4, 18) years. Of these, 38 (22%) had congenital heart disease and 48 (28%) had an existing renal anomaly. The prevalence of hypertensive range BP at clinic within this cohort was 50% (n = 86), with median age of onset at 12 (4, 17) years of age. Pre-hypertensive range BPs were identified in 12 (7%). In total, 14/86 (15%) had ongoing high BP and were prescribed anti-hypertensive treatment. There is an increased prevalence of hypertension within the paediatric TS population compared to the general paediatric population. Early management of blood pressure in this group is likely to reduce cardiovascular disease burden.

title: Pulsed Field or Cryoballoon Pulmonary Vein Isolation for Atrial Fibrillation in Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction.
authorString: Boehmer AA, Zylla MM, Feickert S, Hillmann HAK, Dyrda K, Lussier S, Stangl D, Buia V, Yogarajah J, Kibel S, Berthelsen LF, Brockmueller C, Lemoine MD, Kahle AK, Iliodromitis K, Post F, Gold C, Rothe M, Ruckes C, Ewertsen NC, Ince H, Meyer C, Duncker D, Neumann T, Bogossian H, Rillig A, Wakili R, Andrade JG, Nattel S, Ehrlich JR.
abstractText:
Background

Atrial fibrillation (AF) and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) frequently coexist, worsening prognosis. While catheter ablation confers clinical benefits in this high-risk population, comparative data between novel non-thermal pulsed field ablation (PFA) and established cryoballoon ablation (CBA) for AF-therapy in patients with HFrEF are limited.

Objective

To compare the efficacy and safety of PFA- with CBA-based pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) in patients with AF and HFrEF (left ventricular ejection fraction ≤40%).

Methods

This retrospective, international multicenter study included patients with HFrEF undergoing first-time PVI-only procedures between 2018 and 2025. Propensity-score matching (1:1 ratio) was applied to balance baseline characteristics. The primary efficacy endpoint was the first recurrence of any atrial tachyarrhythmia after a 3-month blanking period. Secondary measures included safety events and procedural efficiency.

Results

A total of 700 patients from 12 German and Canadian centers were included, with 420 patients analyzed following propensity-score matching. At 12 months, freedom from atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence with PFA was comparable to CBA (Kaplan-Meier estimates, 65.0% vs. 67.8%; hazard ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.77 to 1.55; P=0.61). No statistically significant differences in observed safety outcomes were detected. PFA significantly improved procedural efficiency with shorter total procedure duration (58±22min vs. 72±22min; P<0.001), left-atrial dwell time (42±16min vs. 52±17min; P<0.001) and lower contrast dye use (0 ml [IQR 0-15] vs. 47 ml [IQR 30-56], P<0.001).

Conclusions

In patients with AF and HFrEF, PFA-based PVI achieves similar rhythm-control efficacy and safety compared with CBA, while significantly enhancing procedural efficiency.

title: Prenatal melatonin regulates lung prostanoids expression in newborn sheep exposed to chronic hypoxia.
authorString: Figueroa EG, Gonzaléz-Candia A, Villanueva C, Paz AA, Herrera EA.
abstractText: Chronic hypoxia during pregnancy disrupts the balance of pulmonary vasoactive agents, altering prostanoid signaling and increasing the contractility of resistance arteries. This leads to elevated pulmonary arterial pressure and vascular resistance, ultimately resulting in pulmonary hypertension of the neonate (PHN). While prenatal melatonin is known to influence vascular tone, its specific impact on the neonatal pulmonary prostanoid system in hypoxic pregnancies remains unclear. This study aimed to determine the effects of third-trimester maternal melatonin administration on the cyclooxygenase and prostanoid pathways, and to evaluate its efficacy in reversing PHN in a high-altitude ovine model. In-vivo and ex-vivo pulmonary vascular function was evaluated in neonatal lambs gestated and born under chronic hypoxia. Furthermore, lung samples from 12-day-old lambs were analyzed using RT-PCR, Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. The results demonstrate that prenatal melatonin actively modulates the pulmonary vascular function, and the prostanoids system, altering both the transcriptional and translational expression of specific prostanoids, as well as their spatial localization within pulmonary resistance arteries. However, despite this significant molecular and structural modulation, maternal melatonin treatment failed to reverse or clinically improve PHN in the offspring. These findings highlight the complexity of hypoxia-induced vascular remodeling and suggest that melatonin-driven prostanoid modulation alone is insufficient to overcome PHN, although it can improve some pulmonary function in neonates.

title: Metabolic Unloading: How SGLT2i Recalibrate Cell Energetics to Slow CKD Progression.
authorString: Leon VM, Aggarwal S.
abstractText: Kidney outcome trials demonstrate that sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors consistently slow chronic kidney disease progression; however, the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely defined, as benefits extend beyond glycemic control and hemodynamic effects across diabetic and non-diabetic chronic kidney disease. This review advances a unifying framework in which metabolic unloading of the proximal tubule contributes to renoprotection. The metabolic burden of solute reabsorption places the proximal tubule at the center of renal energetics, predisposing it to hypoxia, mitochondrial stress, and maladaptive injury responses. We synthesize evidence that these agents reduce adenosine triphosphate-dependent transport workload, oxygen consumption and may also reduce megalin-dependent endocytosis, with downstream effects on mitochondrial efficiency, redox balance, and autophagy/mitophagy supported by emerging preclinical data. By mitigating energetic stress, these agents divert tubular cell fate away from maladaptive hypertrophy and fibrosis toward adaptive repair. This framework integrates spatial cortex-medulla vulnerability, reconciles early hemodynamic changes with durable slowing of estimated glomerular filtration rate decline, and explores disease-agnostic benefit. We discuss translational implications including early initiation, identification of high workload phenotypes (hyperfiltration, recovery after acute kidney injury), and deployment of energetics associated biomarkers such as ketones, oxidative stress profiles, and estimated glomerular filtration rate slope. This review positions cellular energetics as an important upstream constraint shaping kidney disease progression, offering a foundation for nephroprotective strategies.

title: Association of age at menopause with incident depressive disorders in women: A prospective cohort study.
authorString: Wu N, Wang Z, Zhang H, Liu M, Zhai J, Lyu N, Liu Y, Guo L.
abstractText: This study aimed to examine the association between age at menopause and the subsequent development of depression. This study included 37,754 postmenopausal women from the UK Biobank. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to assess the association between age at menopause and depression risk, and multivariable-adjusted restricted cubic splines (RCS) were used to evaluate the dose-response relationship. Sensitivity analyses evaluated the robustness of the findings. During a mean follow-up of 14.91 ± 3.04 years, 698 participants developed depression. RCS analysis showed a significant linear dose-response relationship between age at menopause and the risk of depressive disorders; each 1-year increase in age at menopause was associated with a 3.5% lower risk of incident depressive disorders (HR = 0.965, 95% CI: 0.947-0.983, P < 0.001). With 50 years as the reference, women who experienced menopause at age 45 years had a 17.3% higher risk (HR = 1.173, 95% CI: 1.031-1.333, P = 0.015), whereas those who experienced menopause at age 55 years had a 20.3% lower risk (HR = 0.797, 95% CI: 0.642-0.989, P = 0.039). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the findings. Stratified analyses showed that the protective association of age at menopause was more pronounced among participants with hypertension, whereas hormone replacement therapy did not significantly modify the association. Age at menopause was significantly associated with the risk of new-onset depression in a linear dose-response manner, with a younger age at menopause associated with a higher risk of depressive disorders.

title: Body composition and blood pressure: Haemodynamic links in young men and women.
authorString: Cseh D, Middlemiss JE, Yu S, Bentley GJ, Williams AR, Yasmin, McDonnell BJ, Pugh CJA, Wilkinson IB, McEniery CM.
abstractText: The aim of this study was to explore the sex-specific haemodynamic links between body composition parameters and systolic and diastolic blood pressure (SBP and DBP, respectively) in adults free of cardiovascular disease and not receiving cardiovascular medications. Body mass index (BMI), fat mass (FM), fat-free mass (FFM), SBP and DBP, cardiac output (CO), peripheral vascular resistance (PVR) and aortic pulse wave velocity (PWV) were determined in 235 men and 192 women aged 18-40 years. Multivariable linear regression and single- as well as multiple-mediator models were used to assess haemodynamic mechanisms underlying the associations between body composition and blood pressure. BMI showed positive associations with SBP and DBP in both sexes (P < 0.001 for all). In men, FFM was the main body composition correlate of SBP (P < 0.001), with the positive association driven in part by CO and partially offset by opposing effects through PVR. FM was the dominant body composition correlate of DBP in men and both SBP and DBP in women (P < 0.001 for all), with the positive associations mediated by PVR and PWV in both sexes, and additionally by heart rate in the FM-DBP association in men. Changes in FFM may affect SBP predominantly through CO in young men. Changes in FM may affect DBP in young men and both SBP and DBP in young women, predominantly through vascular mechanisms. These findings provide important insights into sex differences in the physiology of adiposity-related BP changes in young adults and may help inform sex-specific strategies for the management of adiposity-related hypertension.

title: Peripartum echocardiographic findings in preeclampsia and their association with subsequent hypertension.
authorString: Alhuneafat L, Puttur A, Williams BA, Manalo K, Khan S, Tieliwaerdi X, Arrigo A, Poornima I.
abstractText: Preeclampsia, a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy, predisposes women to long-term cardiovascular risk, especially future hypertension. We examined whether peripartum echocardiographic measures were associated with subsequent hypertension among women with preeclampsia without pre-pregnancy chronic hypertension. Retrospective study of 252 women with preeclampsia and 222 normotensive pregnant controls who underwent echocardiography between 20 weeks' gestation and 30 days postpartum within a single integrated health system (2016-2022). Incident hypertension during follow-up (through mid-2023), defined by a new diagnosis of hypertension, systolic blood pressure (BP) >135 mmHg on a recorded visit, diastolic BP >85 mmHg, or initiation of antihypertensive medication. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify echocardiographic and clinical predictors of subsequent hypertension. Among 474 pregnant women followed for a mean of 2.3 years, 119 of 252 (47.2%) preeclampsia women and 9 of 222 (4.1%) controls met criteria for hypertension. Among women with preeclampsia, 85% had severe features. Eighteen of 26 echocardiographic measures differed significantly between preeclampsia and control groups. In adjusted models limited to women with preeclampsia, both interventricular septal thickness at end-diastole (IVSd) and left ventricular mass index (LVMi) were independently associated with the development of hypertension (IVSd OR = 1.37 per 0.1 cm, p < 0.01; LVMi OR = 1.15 per 10 g/m2, p = 0.04). LVMi greater than 95 g/m2 was associated with a more than threefold higher odds of developing hypertension. Peripartum echocardiography may provide additional insight for identifying women at higher risk for future hypertension, allowing for closer follow-up and early intervention.

title: Horizon-Aware Forecasting of Hypertension Prevalence and Mean Total Cholesterol in Chinese Men: Retrospective Leakage-Controlled Benchmark Study Comparing Statistical, Machine-Learning, and Neural Models.
authorString: Lai W, Subhan F, Zhou N, Khan J.
abstractText: Forecasts of population-level cardiovascular risk factors can support surveillance and planning, but annual country-level health series are often short. With only 30 or 39 annual values per target, model flexibility can outpace the information available for training, making leakage control, repeated temporal evaluation, and comparison with simple baselines essential. The aim of this study is to compare statistical, classical machine-learning, and neural forecasting models for age-standardized prevalence of hypertension (ASPH) and mean total cholesterol (MTC) in Chinese men and to test whether attention or substantially greater neural capacity provides consistent predictive benefit. The authors analyzed 2 officially sourced annual series: ASPH for Chinese men aged 30 to 79 years (1990-2019; 30 observations) and MTC for Chinese men aged 18 years or older (1980-2018; 39 observations). No series was interpolated, extrapolated, imputed, smoothed, spliced, or synthetically extended. Leakage-controlled expanding-window evaluation began after 21 observations and assessed 1-, 2-, and 5-year horizons. Classical machine-learning and neural models used a fixed primary lookback of 3 (L=3), with nested lookback selection disabled; neural models used 10 fixed seeds. Performance was assessed with root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error, mean absolute scaled error, root mean squared scaled error, symmetric mean absolute percentage error, directional accuracy, mean error, median error, diagnostic R², prespecified neural-ablation inference, empirical forecast-interval coverage, and computational-cost reporting. Statistical models had the lowest RMSE in all 6 target-horizon cells. Autoregressive integrated moving average won for ASPH at h=1 (RMSE 0.000178), h=2 (RMSE 0.000578), and h=5 (RMSE 0.004324), and for MTC at h=1 (RMSE 0.000400) and h=2 (RMSE 0.001479); error-trend-seasonal state space won for MTC at h=5 (0.006991). Classical machine-learning and primary neural models won no cells. Removing attention reduced RMSE in 5 of 6 ablation cells, while the compact architecture had lower RMSE than Original23K in 5 of 6 cells; formal differences were detected for both contrasts at ASPH h=1 and h=2, whereas ASPH h=5 (n=5) was descriptive only. Predictive intervals often undercovered. The benchmark completed all 7242 planned output-producing fits. Simple statistical forecasting remained highly competitive in these short, retrospectively estimated annual series. Greater complexity did not ensure better point prediction, and neither attention nor larger capacity conferred a consistent advantage. Point accuracy did not ensure well-calibrated predictive uncertainty; findings were conditional on the 2 targets, target-specific horizons, and small evaluation samples.

title: Variability in non-invasive tests: Challenges and implications for monitoring liver disease.
authorString: Semmler G, Lindvig KP, Simonis L, Embacher J, Hruska P, Andersen P, Marcour Y, Mehl B, Balcar L, Jachs M, Thorhauge KH, Simbrunner B, Hansen JK, Hofer BS, Israelsen M, Hartl L, Haselwanter P, Wunderbaldinger A, Höfinger P, Villesen IF, Winker R, Trauner M, Krag A, Reiberger T, Scherzer TM, Mandorfer M, Thiele M.
abstractText: Diagnostic and prognostic non-invasive fibrosis tests (NITs) are increasingly repurposed to monitor liver disease. However, their reproducibility and the minimal detectable change (MDC, ie, the smallest change that exceeds expected measurement variability) are poorly characterized. We retrospectively assessed variability of blood-based NITs and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) by vibration-controlled transient elastography on the same day (repeatability) and across use-cases when metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, fibrosis, or portal hypertension is suspected. Measurements were done within 90 days. Agreement and variability were quantified using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), Bland-Altman analyses, and MDC on the original (absolute) and relative (MDC%) scales. Across 6 cohorts, ICCs were generally good to excellent, but within-subject variability remained substantial. Same-day LSM had a pooled MDC% of 24% on the m/s scale, corresponding to an asymmetric kPa-equivalent window of -43% to +54%. For longitudinal lab-based NITs, pooled MDC% was 47% for FIB-4 and 56% for APRI, while absolute MDC was 13-17 percentage points for LiverPRO and 3 percentage points for CORE. Optimistic estimates remained substantial after excluding the 10% most extreme paired differences. Variability increased with biomarker level for LSM, FIB-4, and APRI, whereas MDC windows for probability-based scores were strongly baseline-dependent and followed an inverse U-shaped pattern. When repeat testing was triggered by an elevated initial LSM, regression to the mean accounted for most or all of the observed decrease. Good agreement in NITs does not guarantee high precision for disease monitoring. MDC depends on biomarker level, clinical setting, measurement scale, and selection for repeat testing. Universal thresholds should not be applied uncritically, and repeated measurements, baseline-dependent interpretation, and regression to the mean should guide monitoring decisions.

title: Poor sleep quality and anxiety in patients with diabetes mellitus and its association with glycemic control: A cross-sectional study.
authorString: Baghdad W, Satté A, El Harrati O, El Brouzi MY, Bernoussi Z, Raggabi A, Hmamouchi I, El Omri N, Mekouar F, Mesfioui A, Sqalli Houssaini Y, El Hessni A.
abstractText: Sleep is crucial for maintaining physical and mental health, and poor sleep quality is associated with an increased risk of metabolic, cognitive, and cardiovascular diseases. This study aimed to assess sleep quality and factors associated with poor sleep quality, such as mental disorders, especially anxiety, in adult patients with type 2 diabetes in Morocco. A cross-sectional study was conducted on patients with type 2 diabetes, using random selection, aged 39-85, in the clinical neurophysiology and internal medicine department of the Mohammed V Military Instruction Hospital, between 30/09/2024 and 30/12/2024. The questionnaire comprised demographic data, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and the Generalized Anxiety Disorder Scale (GAD-7). Descriptive tests, independent two-sample t-tests, chi-square tests, and logistic regressions were performed using Jamovi version 2.6.2. Out of the 120 participants, the mean age of our patients was 65.4 ± 9.32 years, of whom 66.67% were women. The mean PSQI score was 9.18 ± 3.73, and the mean GAD-7 score was 8.0 ± 6.11. Poor sleep quality was reported in 84.2% of participants, while a binary logistic regression analysis revealed that poor sleep quality was not significantly associated with high HbA1c, but rather was highly significant with age and GAD-7. The study reveals that poor sleep quality is common among type 2 diabetic patients in Morocco, and is strongly associated with generalized anxiety disorders. These findings underscore the crucial role of psychological factors in diabetes management. They highlight the need for a comprehensive and integrated approach that takes into account not only biomedical aspects but also the psychological and behavioral dimensions of patients.

title: Mechanical forces enable human stem cell modeling of protein aggregation cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Kooh YKG, Bahmani B, Zhao C, Malayath G, Khokhlova A, Hayem L, Umuragwa H, Jin H, Ramahdita G, Peng X, Jiang H, Perez JS, Chou HC, Silva JR, Ma X, Genin GM, Rawnsley DR, Diwan A, Huebsch N.
abstractText: Inherited cardiomyopathies are the leading cause of heart failure in young adults, with limited therapeutic options. Desmin-related cardiomyopathy (DRM), caused by mutations to cytoskeletal proteins and their chaperones, exemplifies this challenge: Here, protein quality control is compromised, leading to toxic protein aggregates that destroy cardiomyocyte contractile machinery. One of the deadliest DRM mutations in the chaperone protein αB crystallin (CRYAB-R120G) lacks a genetically matched preclinical model: Mouse models require massive overexpression of mutant CRYAB, raising questions about physiological relevance. Here, we establish a human model of CRYAB-linked DRM, using induced pluripotent stem cells expressing CRYAB-R120G at near-endogenous levels. We show that three-dimensional mechanical loading, but not fatty acid-based metabolic maturation media, is essential for expressing Desmin, whose aggregation defines DRM. Using microengineered heart tissues, we found that contractile deficits are associated with impaired calcium handling, pointing to electromechanical uncoupling in DRM. Treatment with the Janus kinase 1 inhibitor itacitinib partially rescued contractility, providing a functional validation of this emerging therapeutic strategy.

title: Economic evaluations of interventions for the treatment and management of non-communicable diseases in humanitarian contexts: A scoping review.
authorString: Elnajar A, Allsop M, Ba-Break M, Kasasbeh N, Dawkins B.
abstractText: Humanitarian crises profoundly disrupt health systems and limit access to healthcare. People with non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are among the most vulnerable groups affected. As humanitarian interventions often focus on acute health needs, NCDs are often overlooked in financing and service delivery. In such contexts, efficient strategies are crucial for maximising health benefits and ensuring equitable service delivery. Health economic evaluations provide decision-makers with evidence on optimal resource allocation. Given the high burden of NCDs and the uncertainty about the effectiveness of their management in such contexts, this review aims to map available evidence from studies that utilised health economic approaches to assess NCD programmes implemented in humanitarian contexts. Systematic searches were conducted across seven electronic databases: Ovid Medline, Global Health, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CAB, and EconLit, alongside grey literature. Eligible studies were full economic evaluations (cost-effectiveness, cost-utility, and cost-benefit analyses) of NCD interventions in humanitarian contexts. Of the 6911 deduplicated records screened, seven studies met the inclusion criteria; a structured Excel sheet charted key study characteristics. The included evidence comprised four studies from conflict-affected lower-middle-income countries, and three from natural disaster settings in high-income countries. No studies from low-income countries met the inclusion criteria. NCDs addressed included mental health (n = 4), asthma (n = 2), and congestive heart failure (n = 1). One study addressed broader NCD-related public health interventions, including cancer screening and management, and incorporated diabetes into an NCD burden model without cost-effectiveness analysis. Methodological approaches varied, including simulation/microsimulation (n = 3), trial-based economic evaluations (n = 3), and a Markov model (n = 1). The review highlights limited and fragmented evidence to support decision-making and long-term planning, particularly in low-income settings. Further research is needed to understand how health economic evidence for NCDs can be generated, interpreted and used within humanitarian decision-making systems, and to support allocation of scarce resources for people living with NCDs during crises.

title: Training Structure and Satisfaction with Learning in European Vascular Surgery Training: Results from the European Vascular Surgery Training (EVaST) Surveys.
authorString: Wippel D, Schönherr L, Gouveia E Melo R, Heidler J, Wegner M, Kukulski L, Cecere F, Darwish M, Jongkind V, Hakkenbrak N, Zlatanovic P.

journal.title: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery

abstractText:
Objective

This study describes the availability of modifiable structural training elements across European vascular surgery programmes to identify which of these elements are independently associated with trainees' satisfaction with learning and to contextualise them with trainer reported delivery constraints.

Methods

The study comprised two parallel cross-sectional web based European Vascular Surgery Training (EVaST) surveys of trainees and trainers. The main outcome variable was satisfaction with learning (10 point Likert scale). Five modifiable structural elements were identified a priori: structured curriculum; training coordinator; dedicated or protected training time; assigned mentor; and simulation access. Associations were examined using an adjusted linear mixed effects model (LMM), with secondary models for coordinator resourcing and mentorship evaluations. Trainer data were analysed descriptively.

Results

Of 420 trainee responses (32 countries), 273 entered the complete case main LMM. Availability was inconsistent: structured curriculum 56.4%; dedicated or protected training time 34.3%; and simulation access 32.3%. In the adjusted LMM, learning satisfaction was higher with a structured curriculum (= 0.79, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.21 - 1.38; p = .008) and dedicated training time (= 0.62, 95% CI 0.05 - 1.19; p = .035). In secondary models, coordinators with dedicated educational time showed the largest association (= 1.76, 95% CI 1.05 - 2.46; p < .001), and mentorship with regular evaluations was associated with higher satisfaction (= 0.98, 95% CI 0.36 - 1.59; p = .002). Among 659 trainers (37 countries), mentorship importance was rated 8.26 out of 10, yet only 43.4% had dedicated mentorship time; the dominant barrier was clinical workload (84.1%). Desired improvements were dedicated mentorship time (64.4%), formalised programmes (54.3%), and regular feedback sessions (51.6%).

Conclusion

A structured curriculum and dedicated training time were independently associated with higher trainee learning satisfaction across European vascular surgery programmes. Organisational roles such as training coordinators and mentors were associated with higher satisfaction in exploratory secondary analyses, suggesting these roles may be most beneficial when actively resourced with dedicated time and regular evaluations. Trainer constraints converged on protected time for training and mentorship.

title: Mitral valve strain and chordal forces as potential diagnostic parameters in pediatric mitral valve disease.
authorString: Christierson L, Revstedt J, Mertens L, Dragulescu A, Karlsson M, Isaksson H, Hakacova N.
abstractText:
Background

A challenge in pediatric mitral valve disease is the limited understanding of the biomechanical alterations in valvular dysfunction. This complicates decision-making regarding timing and choice of intervention. Fluid-structure interaction (FSI) simulations offer patient-specific insights into valve biomechanics, unattainable by conventional imaging. This study compared healthy, regurgitant, and surgically repaired pediatric mitral valves to determine whether valve strain and chordal forces differ between groups and whether these measures reflect the biomechanical consequences of disease.

Methods

A validated FSI framework was applied to assess valve strain and chordal forces in pediatric healthy valves (N = 6) and regurgitant valves (N = 7). Patient-specific geometries were reconstructed from 3D echocardiography, and flow boundary conditions were derived from left ventricular volume data.

Results

Strain analysis revealed statistically significant differences between healthy (6.6% strain) and regurgitant valves (9.8% strain before and 9.0% after surgery), indicating that repair improves but does not normalize strain patterns. Localized high-strain regions were present in regurgitant valves pre- and postoperatively. Regurgitant valves exhibited elevated diastolic chordal forces compared to healthy valves, indicating pathological loading. No statistically significant differences in strain or chordal forces were observed between pre- and postoperative states.

Conclusions

Valve strain and chordal forces differed between healthy and regurgitant pediatric mitral valves. These biomechanical parameters open the possibility of quantifying mitral valve mechanics and introduce an innovative approach to using valve strain and chordal forces as functional biomarkers, supporting the future clinical integration of patient-specific FSI simulations in the evaluation of pediatric mitral valve disease.

title: B cells dominate the heart immune infiltrate during chronic infectious cardiomyopathy
authorString: Dąbek A, Fortes Francisco A, Khan AA, Ashraf S, Dey S, Van Bocxlaer K, Ashwin H, Parker K, Dey NS, Bayraktar OA, Teichmann SA, Taylor MC, Green EA, Kaye PM, Kelly JM, Lewis MD, Pérez-Mazliah D.
abstractText: Recent advances in single-cell and spatially resolved multi-omics have revolutionised our understanding of the cellular and molecular niches governing cardiac homeostasis and acute injury. However, the immune-stromal networks sustaining long-term, chronic heart pathology remain poorly defined, largely due to a paucity of physiologically relevant experimental models. Here, through a side-by-side multi-omic comparison of Trypanosoma cruzi-infected mouse models displaying contrasting degrees of chronic myocardial pathology and fibrosis, we define the long-term cellular landscape of the inflamed fibrotic heart. We reveal that class-switched, antibody-secreting plasma B cells represent the predominant immune subset infiltrating the fibrotic myocardium. CellChat intercellular communication modelling identifies plasma cell-fibroblast crosstalk as the strongest immune-stromal interaction in the fibrosis-prone heart, driven by predicted matrix anchoring (CD44-collagen/laminin) and molecular survival axes (App-Cd74, C3-Cr2). Supporting these computational predictions, immunofluorescence and spatial profiling confirm close proximity between plasma B cells and fibroblasts, alongside a striking accumulation of B cells embedded within extracellular matrix-rich cardiac scars. This localised B cell response maintains prominent pools of parasite-reactive and heart-autoreactive antibody-secreting cells despite a lack of detectable parasite signal in their immediate micro-vicinity. Together, these findings identify a matrix-associated plasma B cell-fibroblast niche as a central driver of chronic cardiac remodelling, revealing how persistent tissue scarring can become decoupled from direct local pathogen presence.

title: Electromechanical Drivers of Diastolic Dysfunction During Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Progression
authorString: Hasaballa AI, Coleman JAI, Wang ZJ, Doste R, Zhou X, Zingaro A, Vazquez M, Argiro A, Coppini R, Olivotto I, Bueno-Orovio A.
abstractText:
Aims:

: Diastolic dysfunction in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy reflects changes in sarcomeric function, electrophysiology, ventricular structure, and myocardial mechanics. Their effects on filling remain difficult to determine clinically. We sought to dissect these effects in MYH7-related non-obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy progression. Methods and results: We developed a human biventricular electromechanical model linking electrophysiology and calcium handling to contraction, ventricular mechanics, haemodynamics, electrocardiography, and myocardial strain. Stage I represented MYH7 sarcomeric dysfunction before hypertrophy; Stage II added septal hypertrophy; Stage III added increased myocardial stiffness. Secondary ionic remodelling was examined at each stage and severity. Sarcomeric dysfunction alone generated a low-volume hypercontractile phenotype before overt hypertrophy. Septal hypertrophy further constrained chamber filling, whereas myocardial stiffening exacerbated diastolic dysfunction and regional mechanical heterogeneity. Secondary ionic remodelling produced marked repolarisation abnormalities but, importantly, also prolonged calcium-tension dynamics and impaired relaxation, reducing ventricular filling to an extent comparable with structural remodelling in some disease states. Increasing ionic-remodelling severity progressively amplified these effects. Despite preserved ejection fraction throughout progression, ventricular volumes decreased while global and regional myocardial deformation deteriorated.

Conclusion:

Diastolic dysfunction was evident before overt hypertrophy and worsened as structural, mechanical, and ionic abnormalities were added. Preserved ejection fraction did not reflect reduced ventricular filling or deterioration in myocardial strain. Regional mechanical measures may therefore reveal disease burden not captured by ejection fraction alone. By separating individual disease mechanisms, in silico modelling may help link measurable biomarkers to their underlying causes and support mechanism-based patient stratification.

title: TREM2-stimulated, PDGF-dependent macrophage-fibroblast crosstalk induces beneficial plaque remodeling in clonal hematopoiesis
authorString: Liu W, Xue C, Olszewska M, Hsu C, Yalcinkaya M, Xiao T, Schlepckow K, Haass C, Papapetrou EP, Monroe KM, Wang N, Reilly M, Tall AR.
abstractText:
Background:

In Jak2V617F clonal hematopoiesis, inflammatory signaling suppresses macrophage TREM2 and promotes features of plaque instability, while therapeutic TREM2 agonism reverses plaque instability by increasing fibroblasts and fibrous cap formation. We tested whether macrophage-derived PDGFB and stromal cell PDGFR? signaling mediate this response.

Methods:

Low allele burden (LAB) Jak2V617F atherosclerosis models were combined with inducible Pdgfb deletion in CX3CR1-lineage monocytes/macrophages or Pdgfra deletion in Col1a2-lineage fibroblast-enriched stromal cells. Mice were treated with the TREM2 agonist 4D9. Plaque composition, macrophage-fibroblast interactions, and aortic stromal cell populations were analyzed. Human WT and JAK2V617F iPSC-derived macrophages were used for validation.

Results:

TREM2 activation with 4D9 increased macrophage PDGFB production and promoted fibrous cap formation in LAB Jak2V617F atherosclerosis. Deletion of Pdgfb in CX3CR1-lineage cells markedly attenuated the 4D9-mediated increase in fibrous cap area and lesional PDGFR?+ cells, establishing macrophage-derived PDGFB as a key signal for the stromal response. Consistently, Col1a2-lineage Pdgfra deletion abolished the 4D9-induced fibrous cap response without significantly altering lesion or necrotic core area. Single cell RNA-seq identified increased Fmod+ and CD26/Dpp4+ fibroblast populations associated with 4D9 treatment. Fmod+ fibroblasts represented an abundant matrix-associated population, whereas CD26+ fibroblasts showed greatest enrichment, prominent extracellular matrix, collagen organization, and matrix-remodeling programs that were enhanced by 4D9 and attenuated by Pdgfra deletion. The stromal response was also associated with reduced macrophage migration-related programs and predicted chemokine communication from CD26+ fibroblasts to macrophages which was verified by macrophage migration studies. Moreover, stromal Pdgfra deletion increased lesional CCR2+ and CCR5+ macrophages.

Conclusions:

In a CH model of inflammatory atherosclerosis, TREM2 activation promotes a macrophage PDGFB-stromal PDGFR? pathway that expands Fmod+ and CD26+ fibroblast populations and increases fibrous cap matrix formation. CD26+ fibroblasts impair macrophage chemotaxis in a DPP4-dependent manner, suggesting reciprocal macrophage-fibroblast communication that coordinates matrix remodeling and inflammatory cell trafficking in the plaque.

title: Zonulin and the Gut Barrier–Inflammation Axis: From Pathophysiology to Clinical Implications in Inflammatory Bowel Disease and Cardiometabolic Disease
authorString: Mademlis C, Patoulias D, Teperikidis L, Akritidis K, Kotsiou N, Evangelidis P, Kefas A, Koufakis T, Katsaros M, Doumas M, Giouleme O.
abstractText: The intestinal barrier is not a passive membrane but a layered and actively regulated interface. The epithelium and its tight junctions form the physical layer, which is complemented by a chemical layer of mucus and antimicrobial peptides, by the mucosal immune compartment, and by the resident microbiota. Together these layers separate a substantial microbial and dietary antigen load from the systemic circulation. Zonulin, identified as pre-haptoglobin-2, has been implicated in the reversible regulation of intestinal tight junctions while the broader concept of zonulin-related proteins (ZRP) encompasses proteins potentially associated with this regulatory system. Loss of barrier control has an established role in the pathogenesis of inflammatory bowel disease and has also been described in obesity, insulin resistance and atherosclerosis, with emerging evidence of an association with cardiovascular outcomes. Circulating ZRP have consequently attracted interest as potential biomarkers of intestinal barrier dysfunction and associated inflammatory and metabolic disturbances. However, uncertainty regarding the molecular specificity of commercial immunoassays complicates their biological interpretation and warrants further analytical and clinical validation. In this Review, we place zonulin within barrier physiology, appraise the clinical evidence in these disorders, and set out the analytical limitations that constrain its use as a biomarker.

title: Carotid Ultrasound Elastography for Atherosclerotic Plaque Assessment: Correlation with Clinical and Histological Findings
authorString: Dedes A, Demergetzoglou N, Kontopodis N, Charalampopoulos G, Liasis N, Pappas T, Maras D, Mitsias PD, Ioannou CV.
abstractText:
Background:

and Objectives: To investigate whether carotid artery elastography, including strain ratio and elasticity scores, can serve as an effective screening and diagnostic tool for carotid atherosclerosis and whether elastographic parameters correlate with histologic severity and clinical symptoms.

Materials and Methods:

This prospective study included consecutive patients undergoing endarterectomy for carotid artery disease in a single institution from January 2018 to December 2024 and assessed the association between ultrasound elastography parameters and histologically determined plaque severity using VEGF and COX-2 indices. Clinical correlations were also explored using demographic and symptomatic status data. Statistical methods included Spearman correlation, ROC analysis, and multivariate logistic regression.

Results:

In total 101 patients were included. No statistically significant correlations were observed between elastography measures and VEGF or COX-2 histologic indices. ROC analysis showed limited predictive value of elastographic markers (AUC range: 0.534 to 0.611). However, in multivariate analysis, plaque area was significantly associated with histologic severity as per the COX-2 index (OR = 0.14; 95% CI, 0.03-0.70; p=0.016). Symptomatic presentation was also associated with higher COX-2 levels (p=0.037).

Conclusions:

Carotid elastography demonstrates limited utility as an independent screening tool for histologic plaque severity. However, plaque morphology (area) may provide supportive value for identifying high-risk atherosclerotic lesions.

title: Aviation Medicine and Cardiovascular Assessment of Aircrew: A European Society of Cardiology-Aligned Review of Integrating International Civil Aviation Organization, European Union Aviation Safety Agency, Federal Aviation Administration, and Turkish Directorate General of Civil Aviation Aeromedical Standards.
authorString: Aydın S, Ekici B, Yalçın M, Erkan AF, Erdem G, Gümüşer F, Bekler Ö, Şabanoğlu C, Okuyan E, Töre HF, Yıldırır RA, Nakou E, Costantini L, Eren K.
abstractText: Aeromedical certification is based on a safety-first principle: a pilot or other aircrew member must not have a medical disorder that creates an unacceptable risk of sudden or subtle incapacitation during flight. Cardiovascular disease remains one of the most important determinants of flight fitness, as it may impair consciousness, judgment, rhythm stability, exercise capacity, and hemodynamic reserve. Modern aeromedical decision-making therefore requires the integration of aviation law, operational risk, contemporary cardiology guidelines, advanced imaging, biomarkers, and long-term surveillance. The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Annex 1 provides the global licensing framework; the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) Part-MED, together with its Acceptable Means of Compliance and Guidance Material, defines detailed operational standards in Europe; and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) employs a protocol- and special issuance-based system for many cardiovascular and metabolic disorders. This review summarizes the aeromedical assessment of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic and acute coronary syndromes, heart failure, cardiomy-opathies, arrhythmias and conduction disorders, pacemakers and implantable cardiac devices, valvular heart disease, aortic disease, congenital heart disease, venous throm-boembolism, cardiovascular pharmacotherapy, and major respiratory conditions rel-evant to flight certification. The manuscript is aligned with current European Society of Cardiology cardiovascular guidance and with the operational aeromedical principles applied by ICAO, EASA, FAA, and the Turkish Directorate General of Civil Aviation. In general, preserved ventricular function, absence of significant symptoms, low thrombo-embolic and arrhythmic risk, stable treatment, and adequate exercise capacity support certification or restricted certification. In contrast, uncontrolled hypertension, unstable diabetes, significant residual myocardial ischemia, reduced ejection fraction, malignant ventricular arrhythmias, implantable defibrillator therapy, severe valvular disease, significant aortic pathology, major congenital hemodynamic lesions, or poorly controlled sleep apnea usually preclude certification. Final decisions remain individualized and depend on license class, operational role, treatment burden, surveillance data, and the judgment of the aeromedical authority.

title: Transcatheter Mitral Cerclage Ventriculoplasty: 5-Year Outcomes.
authorString: Rogers T, Greenbaum AB, Babaliaros VC, Foerst JR, Khan JM, Bruce CG, Stine AM, Tian X, Lederman RJ.
abstractText:
Background

Transcatheter mitral cerclage ventriculoplasty places a circumferential tensioning loop around the base of the left ventricle to reduce mitral annular dimensions and reshape ventricular geometry in patients with functional mitral regurgitation and heart failure. Early experience demonstrated reductions in mitral regurgitation and improvements in heart failure symptoms.

Methods

The National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute Division of Intramural Research Transcatheter Mitral Cerclage Ventriculoplasty Early Feasibility Study was an investigator-initiated, prospective, multicenter study. Between 1 and 5 years, vital status, serious adverse events, routine clinical documentation, and site-reported transthoracic echocardiography findings were collected.

Results

Nineteen procedures were attempted in 18 participants (63% heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, 37% heart failure with preserved ejection fraction). Median age was 73 years, and 63% were female. Kaplan-Meier estimated 5-year survival was 57%. One participant underwent left ventricular assist device implantation after 2 years, and 1 participant underwent mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair after 3 years; none underwent heart transplantation. The study was suspended after complete heart block developed in 6 participants, including 4 requiring new cardiac implantable electronic devices. Among participants with available follow-up echocardiography, site-reported imaging demonstrated mitral regurgitation reduction and improved left ventricular ejection fraction through 5 years. Symptomatic improvement was most apparent during the first year and attenuated thereafter.

Conclusions

Cerclage ventriculoplasty was associated with mitral regurgitation reduction and improved ventricular function among participants with available long-term follow-up. Symptomatic benefit was greatest during the first year and diminished thereafter, suggesting that favorable remodeling may not fully offset progression of the underlying cardiomyopathy.

Registration

URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT03929913.

title: GLP-1/GLP-1R signalling in infectious diseases: basic biology, immunometabolic mechanisms, and therapeutic translation.
authorString: Yue X, Fu H, Qian H, Zhang B, Xu H, Li D, Chen J, Min X, Yang H, Wu W, Liu Z, Mei A, Chen J.
abstractText: Infectious diseases remain a major global health burden, and metabolic disorders such as diabetes and obesity further increase susceptibility to infection and adverse outcomes. These intersecting metabolic and infectious risks have prompted growing interest in the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)/GLP-1 receptor (GLP-1R) axis beyond its established role in glycaemic regulation. GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) modulate systemic metabolism, neuroimmune signalling, vascular and epithelial homeostasis, and inflammatory responses. Whether their infection-related effects arise from direct immune-cell GLP-1R signalling, improved pathogen control, or indirect host protection remains unresolved. This narrative review critically evaluates GLP-1/GLP-1R signalling in infection. It distinguishes live-pathogen models from endotoxin and sterile-injury models, host resistance from host tolerance, and direct receptor-dependent actions from indirect systemic effects. It also differentiates chronic pre-infection exposure from treatment initiated after infection onset. Across selected preclinical models, GLP-1RAs more consistently attenuate inflammation and tissue injury while preserving organ function, whereas their effects on pathogen burden and clearance remain variable. Receptor-specific evidence for immune-cell-intrinsic GLP-1R signalling remains limited, and many reported immune phenotypes may instead reflect metabolic improvement, neuroimmune regulation, or barrier protection. Human evidence is derived mainly from observational studies and secondary analyses of chronic GLP-1RA exposure, with limited evidence from trials initiating treatment during acute infection. Future translation will require cell-specific receptor validation, live-pathogen models with post-infection treatment, parallel assessment of pathogen control and host protection, clinically relevant standard-of-care comparators, and infection-specific safety evaluation. GLP-1RAs are therefore best regarded as candidate host-directed adjuncts. Current evidence does not establish them as direct anti-infective therapies.

title: Adolescent Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Can Be the First Clue to Multisystem Mitochondrial Disease.
authorString: Ngue H, Perez-Atayde AR, Meka PN.
abstractText: Up to 40% of children with mitochondrial disease develop hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) during their disease course, but HCM is almost never the first presenting manifestation. When it is, the underlying mitochondrial disorder is easily missed: the cardiomyopathy is managed in isolation, and extracardiac findings that emerge later may be dismissed as unrelated. We describe an adolescent whose severe HCM was the first major manifestation of clinicopathologically confirmed multisystem mitochondrial disease with a phenotype consistent with Leber hereditary optic neuropathy. Her cardiomyopathy was managed in isolation for over a year before optic atrophy, primary ovarian insufficiency, osteopenia, and exercise intolerance were ultimately recognized as part of a single mitochondrial process. Endomyocardial and skeletal muscle biopsy confirmed mitochondrial pathology. The diagnosis directly changed management: cofactor supplementation was initiated, her visual acuity stabilized on idebenone, and perioperative planning for transplantation was adapted to prevent catabolic decompensation. Her cardiac disease progressed to heart failure requiring transplantation at age 16 years, but she remains clinically stable with preserved graft function more than 15 years later. This case challenges the assumption that mitochondrial disease should enter the differential only after neurologic dysfunction appears. General pediatricians, who see the whole child longitudinally, are uniquely positioned to recognize when dysfunction in other high-energy tissues points toward a unifying mitochondrial diagnosis in a child with cardiomyopathy.

title: Longitudinal Deployment Balloon Rupture With Uncomplicated Retrieval During TAVR.
authorString: Iwata R, Fukamachi D, Matsumoto N, Okumura Y.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText: Deployment-balloon rupture during balloon-expandable transcatheter aortic valve replacement can impede device retrieval. An octogenarian woman underwent transfemoral implantation of a 23-mm SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA valve. The balloon ruptured at approximately the nominal inflation volume adjacent to focal sinotubular-junction calcification. Immediate aspiration produced complete collapse without residual contrast or abnormal balloon geometry, permitting resistance-free retrieval into the 14-F eSheath. Inspection demonstrated a longitudinal tear involving nearly the entire balloon length without circumferential separation or missing fragments. Tear orientation was identifiable only after retrieval; during the procedure, residual contrast, balloon geometry, response to aspiration, and withdrawal resistance guided management. This case suggests that rupture configuration may influence balloon collapse and retrievability, although the proposed relationship remains hypothesis-generating.

title: Alfred Kocher technique for prevention of patient-prosthesis mismatch in paediatric patients.
authorString: Murin P, Winter M, Werner P, Urganci E, Atteneder C, Andreeva A, Osorio-Jaramillo E, Zimpfer D, Kocher A.

journal.title: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS

abstractText: Aortic valve replacement requires special considerations in paediatric patients, who are not yet fully grown. The Ross procedure remains the gold standard in paediatric patients as it offers growth potential. If the Ross procedure is not feasible, or the size of the aortic annulus precludes placement of an adult-sized mechanical prosthesis, the problem of patient-prosthesis mismatch and subsequent aortic valve reinterventions arises. The standardized option for this patient cohort is the Konno incision and patch ventriculoplasty in combination with an adult-sized mechanical prosthesis, which carries substantial procedural complexity and risk. This video tutorial demonstrates posterior aortic root enlargement using the Alfred Kocher technique in a 7-year-old female with a functionally unicuspid aortic valve and a bicuspid pulmonary valve. The bicuspid pulmonary valve was an unplanned intraoperative finding, making the patient ineligible for a durable autograft transplantation. The technique involves an inverted T-shaped incision in the centre of the non-coronary sinus, and reconstruction with a barrel-shaped patch tailored from a 28 mm Valsalva prosthesis to augment the non-coronary sinus in an anatomical fashion, allowing upsizing by 5 mm in annular diameter. This technique enabled implantation of a 21 mm size mechanical prosthesis (diameter = 24 mm) upsized from a 19 mm annulus.

title: Robotic mini-thoracotomy approach to aortic valve and ascending aorta replacement.
authorString: Grubjesic M, Mitar L, Malas T, Torregrossa G, Bakaeen F, Roselli EE, Svensson L, Gillinov M, Koprivanac M.

journal.title: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS

abstractText: Fully endoscopic robotic-assisted aortic valve replacement has emerged as a safe, reproducible and effective minimally invasive approach with favourable clinical outcomes. In patients undergoing aortic valve surgery, concomitant ascending aortic aneurysms should be addressed whenever indicated, as failure to do so may lead to serious long-term aortic complications. Currently these patients must undergo some form of sternotomy to address both pathologies. The use of a totally robotic minithoracotomy approach for concomitant aortic valve and ascending aortic replacement has not, to our knowledge, been previously reported. This video tutorial highlights a robotic approach for combined aortic valve and ascending aortic replacement, representing a pioneering step in the evolution of complex robotically assisted aortic surgery.
