Our vision is to develop a robotic aortic surgery programme that maintains the safety, efficacy and durability of conventional techniques while significantly expediting postoperative recovery for selected patients.

title: Identification of a novel anti-angiogenic regulatory sequence within the syndecan-3 extracellular core protein.
authorString: Arokiasamy S, De Rossi G, Moseley TC, Ricard-Blum S, Whiteford JR.
abstractText: Syndecans are transmembrane proteoglycans that regulate angiogenesis through their glycosaminoglycan chains and core proteins. We previously demonstrated that the syndecan-3 (SDC3) extracellular core protein possesses anti-angiogenic activity independent of its glycosaminoglycan chains. Here, using recombinant truncation mutants, endothelial migration assays and peptide mapping, we localised this activity and identified a minimal nine amino acid peptide, QM111, that retained full biological activity. QM111 inhibited endothelial cell migration and angiogenic sprouting in rat aortic ring and mouse choroidal explant models. Intrinsic disorder analysis revealed that QM111 resides within a region of comparatively reduced disorder, consistent with other syndecan regulatory sequences. QM111 did not induce inflammatory chemokine production, exhibited no detectable cytotoxicity, and retained substantial stability in human serum and vitreous humour. QM111 displayed anti-angiogenic activity comparable to the previously described syndecan-2-derived peptide QM107, with combination treatment producing robust inhibition of angiogenesis. These findings identify a novel anti-angiogenic regulatory sequence within SDC3 and support the concept that syndecan extracellular core proteins contain biologically active sequences with potential therapeutic utility.

title: Association between fixed orthodontic treatment and pulp stone development: a retrospective study.
authorString: Ratzmann A, Krey KF, Beisser AS.
abstractText:
Objectives

This retrospective longitudinal cohort study aimed to evaluate changes in pulp stone prevalence between pretreatment and post-retention panoramic radiographs and to assess potentially associated factors, including sex and active multibracket treatment duration. Additional objectives were to characterize pulp stone distribution by tooth type, jaw, and side and to quantify changes in the radiographic density and pixel-based size of pre-existing pulp stones.

Materials and methods

This study included 199 patients (117 females and 82 males; mean age at T0, 12.5 years) who underwent fixed multibracket orthodontic treatment. Panoramic radiographs obtained before orthodontic treatment (T0) and after completion of the retention phase (T1) were evaluated for radiographically detectable pulp stones in permanent first and second molars. The interval between appliance removal and T1 imaging varied among patients and was not recorded separately. Patient- and tooth-level prevalence analyses were performed in the full cohort, whereas changes in radiographic density, expressed as the mean grey value, and pixel-based size of pre-existing pulp stones were quantified using ImageJ in the baseline-positive subgroup (n = 38). Statistical analyses included paired and between-group comparisons, correlation analyses, and regression models to evaluate longitudinal changes and potential associations with sex and active multibracket treatment duration.

Results

Patient-level pulp stone prevalence increased significantly from 19.6% at T0​​ to 28.6% at T1 (p < 0.001). The increase was greater in males than in females (17.1 versus 3.4 percentage points; p = 0.001). At the tooth level, descriptive increases were observed in all evaluated first and second molars. Maxillary molars showed higher prevalence at both time points, whereas the descriptive magnitude of change was broadly comparable between the jaws. Active multibracket treatment duration (mean, 16.6 months) was not significantly associated with an increase in the number of pulp stone-positive molars per patient (p = 0.90). Exploratory quantitative analyses showed positive pooled mean changes in radiographic density and pixel-based size, with substantial variability among measurements. No sex-related differences were identified for either quantitative outcome, while analyses of the association between active multibracket treatment duration and pixel-based size yielded inconsistent results.

Conclusions

Patient-level pulp stone prevalence increased between the pretreatment and post-retention radiographs, with a greater increase observed in males. Maxillary molars showed higher prevalence at both time points. Exploratory quantitative analyses showed positive pooled mean changes in radiographic density and pixel-based size; neither outcome showed sex-related differences, and findings regarding the association between active multibracket treatment duration and pixel-based size were inconsistent. In the absence of an untreated comparison group, these findings describe longitudinal changes within an orthodontically treated cohort but do not establish a causal effect of fixed orthodontic treatment.

Clinical relevance

Patient-level prevalence of radiographically detectable pulp stones was higher at the post-retention assessment than at pretreatment. Because pulp stones may complicate access to the root canal system, their recognition and documentation on clinically indicated radiographs may be relevant if endodontic treatment is required later. The present findings do not justify additional radiographic examinations solely for pulp stone detection.

title: Neurodevelopmental Outcomes in School-Age Children with Down Syndrome: A Comparison of Children with Repaired Complete Atrioventricular Septal Defect and Those without Major Congenital Heart Disease.
authorString: Van Rompay MI, Martin CN, Trachtenberg FL, Sharma B, Esbensen AJ, Pawlowski KG, Potvin DC, Pipan ME, Hines AC, Bernhard N, Bainton J, Raghuveer G, Newburger JW, Nathan M, Kasparian NA, Hogan W, Goldberg CS, Russell MW, LaRosa A, Talboy A, Pena SY, Prospero C, Schwartz BN, Miller JE, Baumer NT, Pediatric Heart Network’s CHILD-DS Writing Committee on behalf of the Pediatric Heart Network Investigators.
abstractText:
Objective

To compare neurodevelopmental (ND) and behavioral outcomes in children with Down syndrome (DS) having complete atrioventricular septal defect (CAVSD) repair as infants and those without major congenital heart disease (CHD) requiring surgery and/or annual cardiology follow-up.

Study design

In a multi-center, observational study across North America, 259 children aged 5-12 years with DS (124 CAVSD repair; 135 non-CHD) underwent a standardized ND assessment battery. Co-primary outcomes were cognitive scores through direct child testing of the Stanford Binet Intelligence Scales, 5th Edition (SB-5) and adaptive composite scores from the parent/caregiver-reported Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales, 3rd Edition.

Results

Study groups were comparable across most socio-demographic and medical characteristics; however, the CAVSD group had lower neighborhood socioeconomic status (SES). There was no difference in SB-5 deviation index scores (unadjusted mean ± SD in CAVSD and non-CHD: nonverbal, 41.5 ± 18 vs 43.0 ± 17 and verbal, 37.9 ± 18 vs 38.7 ± 16, respectively). When unadjusted, Adaptive Behavior Composite scores also showed no group difference (CAVSD and non-CHD median (Q1, Q3): 66.5 (57.0, 73.0) vs 69.0 (62.0, 74.0), respectively); however, after adjustment for a priori sociodemographic, baseline neonatal, and medical factors, the CAVSD group scored 3.8 ±1.7 points lower (P=.03). Children with CAVSD were less likely to pass teaching items on the Expressive Vocabulary Test, 3rd Edition, and they had increased social communication challenges on the parent/caregiver-reported Social Communication Questionnaire, Current Version (2.3±1.2, P=.05).

Conclusions

Among school-age children with DS, those with CAVSD repair showed no difference in cognitive scores compared with children without major CHD, but they had lower adaptive skills and greater social communication challenges. Lower SES in the CAVSD group underscores the need to examine how social drivers of health influence ND outcomes. Findings improve our understanding of ND profiles among children with DS having repaired CAVSD, helping identify those in need of greater ND support.

title: Physiology-adapted cardiac CT angiography during veno-arterial ECMO in neonatal and pediatric postoperative congenital heart disease: feasibility and clinical impact.
authorString: Salem Y, Shaffer A, Jacobson J, Giotein O, Mishali D, Hubara E, Tirosh T, Kassif Lerner R, Vazhgovski O, Samara M, Vardi A, Tejman-Yarden S.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiac computed tomographic angiography (CCTA) provides high-resolution anatomical assessment in cases of congenital heart disease (CHD). This is crucial in patients supported by veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO), since the fundamental alteration of systemic hemodynamics and contrast transit kinetics makes conventional CT acquisition strategies unreliable.

Objective

We evaluated the feasibility, diagnostic yield, and clinical impact of a structured CCTA protocol adapted to ECMO-dependent physiology in postoperative neonatal and pediatric CHD patients.

Materials and methods

This retrospective, single-center cohort study (2013-2022) included all consecutive postoperative neonatal and pediatric patients with CHD who underwent clinically indicated CCTA while supported by VA-ECMO subsequent to cardiac surgery. Contrast administration route and scan timing were individualized according to ECMO circuit flow characteristics and clinical indication.

Results

Twenty-six CCTA examinations were performed in 25 patients ranging in age from 3 days to 14.8 years (median age 133 days; median weight 5.1 kg). Contrast was administered via the arterial ECMO limb in 15 cases and intravenously with controlled ECMO flow modulation in 11. In 18 of the 26 examinations (69%), the examination revealed a pathology. CCTA provided anatomical information beyond echocardiography in 22 of 26 cases (85%) and directly informed a surgical or catheter-based intervention in 14 cases (54%), with procedural confirmation in all. No transport-related or CT-related adverse events occurred.

Conclusion

When acquisition protocols are adapted to ECMO-dependent hemodynamics, CCTA is feasible and diagnostically consequential in neonatal and pediatric patients supported by VA-ECMO after congenital cardiac surgery. A physiology-guided strategy enables consistent vascular enhancement and frequently identifies clinically actionable findings not detected by echocardiography which can directly inform therapeutic decision-making in this critically ill population.

title: Postoperative Infection Mediates and Modifies the Effect of Risk Adjustment for Congenital Heart Surgery-1 Category on Hospital Stay in Pediatric Cardiac Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Huang J, Gao J, Shang W, Chen S, Wang H, Jiao X.

journal.title: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies

abstractText:
Objectives

To investigate whether postoperative infection mediates and/or modifies the effect of surgical complexity, as defined by the Risk Adjustment for Congenital Heart Surgery (RACHS-1) category, on hospital length of stay (LOS) in pediatric cardiac surgery patients.

Design

Retrospective cohort study.

Setting

Tertiary pediatric cardiac center at Xinhua Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University.

Patients

A total of 1244 children who underwent congenital heart surgery between October 2020 and July 2024.

Interventions

None.

Measurements and main results

Multivariable regression and causal-mediation analyses were performed to estimate the direct and infection-mediated effects of surgical complexity on LOS. Higher-RACHS-1 categories and postoperative infection were independently associated with prolonged LOS (all p < 0.001). In negative binomial mediation analysis, infection mediated 17.4% of the total RACHS-LOS association for RACHS-1 category greater than or equal to 5 vs. 1, corresponding to an infection-mediated increase of 3.87 expected LOS days (95% CI, 1.70-6.42). Infection also modified the association between surgical complexity and LOS, with infection-associated excess LOS increasing to +16.73 days in RACHS-1 category greater than or equal to 5 vs. 1. Mediation was strongest among infants less than or equal to 1 year (28% for RACHS-1 category 3 vs. 1).

Conclusions

Postoperative infection both mediates and amplifies the impact of surgical complexity on hospital LOS, particularly in high-risk infants. Targeted infection-prevention strategies are essential to reduce postoperative morbidity in this population.

title: Predicting and Mitigating Maternal Risk.
authorString: Blissett S, Siu SC.
abstractText: Rates of maternal cardiac events are increasing, highlighting the importance of identifying people with higher risks of pregnancy. Pregnancy imposes hemodynamic and hormonal changes, which can lead to heart failure, arrhythmias, and other cardiac complications. This review provides an overview of assessing cardiac risks of pregnancy in people with pre-existing acquired and congenital heart disease.

title: Oral anticoagulation with or without antiplatelet therapy for secondary stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation and atherosclerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Lopes VHP, da Silva AMP, Cardoso LJC, de Medeiros GN, de Freitas LGC, Gonçalves OR, Visentini LM, de Lima Loiola J, Azevedo CDS, Ibiapino MK, Telles JPM.
abstractText: Patients with ischemic stroke (IS), atrial fibrillation (AF), and atherosclerosis have an increased risk of recurrent ischemic events. Addition of antiplatelet therapy (APT) to oral anticoagulant therapy (OAC) may offer additional protection against these events, at the cost of an increased risk of bleeding. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of combined antithrombotic therapy versus OAC alone in this population. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception through September 2026 for randomized controlled trials and observational studies comparing OAC plus APT versus OAC alone in adults with IS, AF, and atherosclerosis. Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and ROBINS-I. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251164174). Seven studies (4 retrospective, 2 prospective, 1 randomized trial; n= 9,924) were included. Combined therapy was not associated with a reduction in vascular composite outcome (HR 1.10, 95% CI 0.61-1.96), recurrent IS (HR 1.03, 95% CI 0.91-1.16), major bleeding (HR 1.17, 95% CI 0.86-1.59), or all-cause mortality (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.60-1.36). In the subgroup with intracranial or extracranial atherosclerosis, combined therapy showed no significant difference in vascular composite risk (HR 1.67, 95% CI 0.83-3.33). Combined antithrombotic therapy with OAC plus APT was not associated with a reduction in recurrent IS, vascular composite outcome, major bleeding, or all-cause mortality in patients with IS, AF, and atherosclerosis. In patients with intracranial or extracranial atherosclerosis, combined therapy was not associated with a significant difference in the risk of the vascular composite outcome. These findings suggest that the addition of APT to OAC should be approached with caution in this population, and may be best reserved for select clinical contexts.

title: The effect of carotid atherosclerosis and revascularization on cognition and dementia: a systematic review and meta-analysis
authorString: Box CVJ, Yu Q, Stroom R, Verhagen H, Howard DP, Niehot C, Ikram MK, Wolters FJ, Bos D.
abstractText:
Background:

Carotid artery atherosclerosis may accelerate cognitive decline and increase dementia risk, but evidence is fragmented and inconsistent, and benefit of revascularization on cognitive outcomes uncertain.

Methods:

We systematically searched Medline, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Central Register, and Google Scholar for articles published until 11 November 2024, reporting change in cognition or dementia incidence in relation to carotid artery intima-media thickness, plaque, stenosis, and revascularization procedures. We excluded studies that investigated people with dementia, lacked a reference group, or had post-intervention follow-up <30 days. We additionally included new data from the Rotterdam Study, and results from the recent CREST-2 trial. Two independent reviewers extracted study data. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed if data allowed. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, Cochrane Risk of Bias, and ROBINS-I.

Results:

Of 5592 records identified, 97 studies were eligible, including 43 observational studies (N=100,326) and 54 intervention studies (N=15788, 6 randomized controlled trials). In observational studies, mostly among stroke-free individuals, intima-media thickness was associated with higher dementia risk (hazard ratio per 1-SD increase: 1.07, 95%CI 1.01-1.13; I2=24.8%; 5 studies), as was presence of 50-100% asymptomatic steno-occlusive disease (hazard ratio: 1.48, 95%CI 1.06 -2.07; I2=0.0%, 3 studies). Cognitive outcomes were too heterogeneous for meta-analysis, but 11/20 observational studies reported a significant association between carotid atherosclerosis and global cognition. In non-randomized intervention studies, carotid revascularization improved global cognition (standardized mean difference: 0.73, 95%CI 0.37 -1.09; I2=89.8%), but all studies were at high risk of bias, and heterogeneity was only partially explained by intervention type and study characteristics in meta-regression. Suggested benefit of stenting on cognition among Chinese patients (Standardized effect: 0.86 [0.57-1.16], 197 patients; and 1.09 [0.64-1.53], 90 patients, 2 trials) was not observed in the larger CREST-2 trial (Standardized effect: 0.03 [-0.09 to 0.15] and 0.02 [-0.09 to 0.14]), nor in post-hoc analyses of cognition in the ACAS trial and long-term dementia risk in ACST-1 (HR: 0.98 [0.75-1.28]).

Conclusions:

Carotid atherosclerosis is associated with increased risk of dementia. Current evidence does not support carotid revascularization for prevention of cognitive decline or dementia.

title: Routine Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Versus Conservative Management in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
authorString: Mohamed AA, Alawlaqi B, Ahmed AM, Elhadi A, Galal AS, Mahmoud ES, Shahda IS, Mostafa H, Mohammed KA, Saad YA, Alghzawi HM.
abstractText: Coronary artery disease commonly coexists with severe aortic stenosis in transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) candidates, yet optimal revascularization remains debated. We meta-analyzed randomized controlled trials comparing routine percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) before or concomitant with TAVI versus conservative management. Major databases were searched through May 2026. Random-effects models calculated risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and evidence certainty was evaluated via the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation. Three randomized controlled trials (1156 patients; PCI: n = 579, conservative: n = 577) were included. Routine PCI was not associated with significant reductions in all-cause mortality (RR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.70-1.15; P = 0.40), cardiac death (RR, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.51-1.08; P = 0.12), myocardial infarction (RR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.45-1.64; P = 0.64), stroke (RR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.48-1.03; P = 0.07), or hospitalization (RR, 1.07; 95% CI, 0.87-1.32; P = 0.52). However, PCI significantly increased major bleeding (RR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.06-2.34; P = 0.02) and any bleeding (RR, 1.77; 95% CI, 1.27-2.48; P = 0.0008), while reducing urgent and repeat revascularization. In conclusion, routine PCI before or concomitant with TAVI reduces subsequent revascularization without conferring survival or ischemic benefit, while increasing bleeding complications. Given the moderate-to-low certainty of evidence, limited cumulative sample size, and clinical heterogeneity across trials, these findings warrant cautious interpretation and favor an individualized, Heart Team-guided revascularization strategy over routine PCI.

title: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of Tafamidis-treated ATTR-CM patients in a real-world cohort: Comparison with the results of pivotal trials.
authorString: Gregório C, Agostinho JR, Caldeira D, Vilela M, Abrantes A, Batista M, Abrantes F, Garcia AB, Campos C, Conceição I, Pinto FJ, Brito D.

journal.title: Revista portuguesa de cardiologia : orgao oficial da Sociedade Portuguesa de Cardiologia = Portuguese journal of cardiology : an official journal of the Portuguese Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Introduction and objectives

Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is a progressive and life-threatening disease that leads to heart failure and increased mortality. Pivotal clinical trials - ATTR-ACT, ATTRibute-CM and HELIOS-B - have provided robust evidence supporting the efficacy of TTR stabilizers (Tafamidis and Acoramidis) and the TTR-synthesis inhibitor Vutrisiran in reducing mortality and cardiovascular events. This study aims to compare the clinical characteristics and cardiovascular outcomes of a real-world Portuguese cohort of patients with ATTR-CM treated with tafamidis to those reported in pivotal clinical trials.

Methods

Single-center, observational study including consecutive patients with ATTR-CM treated with tafamidis 61 mg once a day. Clinical, laboratory, and echocardiographic data were collected and compared with published results from the ATTR-ACT, ATTRibute-CM, and HELIOS-B trials. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality at 24 months, assessed by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis. Secondary outcomes included cardiovascular-related hospitalizations and quality of life, assessed by KCCQ-OS during follow-up, both of which were compared across studies.

Results

A total of 89 patients were included (76 males; 39 with hereditary ATTR-CM and 50 with wild-type ATTR-CM). The Portuguese real-world cohort was older than the ATTR-ACT and HELIOS-B study populations (mean age 78.6 vs. 74.5 vs. 77.0 years, respectively; p<0.001) and exhibited better functional capacity as assessed by New York Heart Association class compared to ATTR-ACT, ATTRibute-CM and HELIOS-B (New York Heart Association (NYHA) I: 30 vs. 9 vs. 12 vs. 15%, respectively; p<0.001). Echocardiography showed higher LVEF (55 vs. 48%, p<0.001) and better GLS (-15 vs -9%, p<0.001) compared with ATTR-ACT. NT-proBNP levels were comparable across cohorts (2639 vs. 2996 vs. 2946 vs. 2021 pg/mL, respectively; p>0.05). Hereditary ATTR was significantly more prevalent in the Portuguese cohort (44%) compared to ATTR-ACT (24%), ATTRibute-CM (10%), and HELIOS-B (11%; p<0.001), reflecting the endemic p.Val50Met mutation in Portugal. Over a follow-up of 27.4 ± 19.3 months, seven patients (7.9%) experienced heart failure hospitalizations and five patients (5.4%) died, including three cardiovascular deaths, corresponding to an annualized cardiovascular-related hospitalization rate of 0.034 events per patient-year. The 24-month all-cause mortality of 5.6% was considerably lower than reported in ATTR-ACT (24.2%), ATTRibute-CM (15.9%), and HELIOS-B (11.4%). However, KCCQ-OS scores were lower than in ATTRibute-CM and HELIOS-B (both p<0.001), likely reflecting comorbidities, and neurological involvement in hereditary cases.

Conclusions

Patients receiving tafamidis 61 mg for ATTR-CM in this real-world cohort were older, had a higher prevalence of hereditary ATTR, and demonstrated better baseline functional capacity compared to those enrolled in pivotal clinical trials. These observational data provide valuable real-world evidence complementing clinical trials, supporting the use, and safety of tafamidis in this Portuguese cohort.

title: Moderate-intensity statin and ezetimibe combination therapy versus high-intensity statin on coronary atherosclerotic plaque.
authorString: Lee JM, Lee SY, Choi KH, Park TK, Yang JH, Song YB, Choi SH, Gwon HC, Hahn JY.
abstractText:
Background

Effect of moderate-intensity statin and ezetimibe is known to be non-inferior to high-intensity statin in prevention of adverse clinical events in patients with coronary atherosclerotic disease. However, data regarding regression of coronary atherosclerotic plaque remains limited.

Methods

In this randomized, non-inferiority trial, patients with intermediate coronary artery stenosis were randomly assigned 1:1 to either moderate-intensity rosuvastatin (10 mg) with ezetimibe or high-intensity rosuvastatin (20 mg) group. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) was performed at baseline and after 12 months or longer to quantify the coronary plaque response. Primary end point was absolute changes in percent atheroma volume (PAV) between baseline and follow-up IVUS, and non-inferiority margin was as 2.5%. Secondary end point was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), which was a composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, and unplanned repeat revascularization.

Results

A total of 280 patients underwent randomization. Follow-up IVUS showed absolute changes in PAV were - 1.286 ± 3.704% and - 1.302 ± 3.586%, respectively for moderate-intensity rosuvastatin and ezetimibe group and high-intensity rosuvastatin group. Mean difference between 2 groups (0.017%; 95% confidence interval: -0.957% to 0.991%) did not exceed noninferiority margin (non-inferiority p < 0.001). Both groups showed acceptable side effect profiles without group differences.

Conclusion

Compared with high-intensity rosuvastatin monotherapy, moderate-intensity rosuvastatin and ezetimibe was non-inferior regarding regression of coronary atherosclerotic plaque (Supported by Hanmi Pharmaceutical co., ltd; ROSUZET-IVUS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT03169985).

title: Off-Pump versus On-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting in Prefrail and Frail Patients: 30-Day and 1-Year Outcomes From the FRAGILE Randomized Trial.
authorString: Mejia OAV, Meneghini B, de Freitas FL, Deininger MO, Segalote RC, Cosentino F, Hueb AC, Guerrieri MLJ, Faglioni Ribas F, Jucá FG, Palma Dallan LR, Mioto BM, Hajjar LA, Serrano CV, de Barros E Silva PGM, Lopes RD, Taggart DP, Doenst T, Puskas JD, Lisboa LAF, Jatene FB, FRAGILE Study Group.
abstractText:
Background

Frailty is associated with worse outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). However, the comparative effectiveness of off-pump CABG (OPCAB) versus on-pump CABG (ONCAB) in prefrail and frail patients remains uncertain.

Methods

This multicenter, randomized, open-label trial enrolled patients ≥60 years of age classified as prefrail or frail, randomized 1:1, between January 2018 and December 2024. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of death, myocardial infarction, stroke, renal failure, acute respiratory distress syndrome, or reoperation for bleeding. Secondary outcomes included ventilation time, intensive care unit and hospital stay, transfusion requirements, completeness of revascularization, surgical wound infection at 30 days, and neurocognitive function preoperatively and at 1 year. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle; relative risks with 95% CIs were estimated.

Results

A total of 508 patients were included (OPCAB, n=258; ONCAB, n=250; median age, 68 years [interquartile range, 65.0-73]; 30.5% female). The primary composite outcome occurred in 28 patients receiving OPCAB (10.9%) and 40 patients receiving ONCAB (16.0%; relative risk, 1.47 [95% CI, 0.94-2.31]; P=0.09). Surgical wound infection was more frequent with ONCAB (20 [8.0%] versus 9 [3.5%]; P=0.04). No significant differences were observed in neurocognitive or quality of life outcomes at 1 year. Estimated 1-year survival probabilities were 96.1% and 92.8% in the OPCAB and ONCAB groups, respectively (P=0.099).

Conclusion

In prefrail and frail patients undergoing CABG, OPCAB and ONCAB resulted in similar rates of the primary composite outcome. No significant differences between OPCAB and ONCAB were found in neurocognitive outcomes.

Registration

URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02338947.

title: Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage and myositis complicating eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis: a case report and narrative review.
authorString: Subki AH, Albeity A, Alghamdi MK, Sayes NM, Alsolaimani R, Halabi H.
abstractText:
Background

Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is an uncommon antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis characterized by asthma, eosinophilia, and multisystem involvement. Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage and myositis are both infrequent manifestations of EGPA, and their co-occurrence in the same patient has rarely been reported.

Case presentation

A 46-year-old man with adult-onset asthma, chronic sinusitis, and marked peripheral eosinophilia was diagnosed with EGPA in 2015. Over six years of follow-up, he had recurrent pulmonary relapses with migratory infiltrates and developed gastrointestinal involvement, nondilated cardiomyopathy, coronary artery disease, myositis, and diffuse alveolar hemorrhage; he was positive for myeloperoxidase (MPO)-ANCA. Disease activity persisted despite high-dose glucocorticoids, azathioprine, cyclophosphamide, and mycophenolate mofetil. Because the disease was severe, organ-threatening, and predominantly vasculitic, an anti-interleukin-5 agent was not chosen for remission induction; instead, rituximab was started and induced sustained remission.

Conclusion

This case illustrates that refractory, MPO-ANCA-positive EGPA may respond to B-cell depletion with rituximab. The randomized REOVAS trial did not show rituximab to be superior to conventional remission-induction therapy; however, it was not designed to establish equivalence with cyclophosphamide in severe disease, and the optimal strategy for severe refractory disease remains undefined. ANCA status, together with the pattern and severity of organ involvement, may help individualize treatment in this setting.

title: Mechanism of Sini Decoction and its self-assembled component in improving Doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Liu Y, Pu Z, Chen X, Peng Y, Peng C, Li X.
abstractText:
Ethopharmacological relevance

Sini decoction (SND) is a typical Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) prescription composed of Aconitum carmichaelii Debx, Zingiberis Rhizoma, and Glycyrrhizae Radix et Rhizoma Praeparate cum Melle, used to treat cardiomyopathy in TCM clinical trials. Recent studies have shown that the active ingredients of SND can form self-assembled complexes during decoction, whose bioactivity differs from that of the monomeric compound. However, current research on the active ingredients of SND has not yet included these self-assembled components, and the mechanism by which SND exerts its effects on doxorubicin (Dox)-induced cardiomyopathy remains unclear.

Aim of the study

This study aimed to investigate the underlying mechanisms by which SND and its self-assembled component (SAC) improve Dox-induced cardiomyopathy in mice. The complete isolation of the self-assembled complex component from SND was achieved for the first time, and its activity and mechanism were explored, providing a new perspective for revealing the substance basis of TCM prescriptions.

Materials and methods

SAC and the unassembled component (SMC) were separated from SND by ultrafiltration, and UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS was used to qualitatively analyze their chemical components. Based on the main components of SAC, Benzoylmesaconine-glycyrrhizic acid complex (GBMA) was prepared under simulated decoction conditions of SND. A mouse model of cardiomyopathy was established by intraperitoneal injection of Dox, followed by oral administration of SND, SAC, SMC, and GBMA, to evaluate improvements in cardiac systolic function across treatment groups. The effects of SND and its components on cardiac systolic function were evaluated to reveal the differences in their medicinal effects. The mechanisms by which SND and SAC improve cardiomyopathy were systematically investigated using Seahorse energy metabolism analysis, autophagic flux analysis, and Western blotting, with a focus on the interconnected organelles, mitochondria, and autophagosomes.

Results

A total of 173 compounds were identified in SAC. Among them, molecules with lower hydrophilicity tend to self-assemble in the decoction, while molecules with a molecular weight less than 300 Da participate less in self-assembly. SND, SAC, and GBMA significantly improved abnormal cardiac systolic function in Dox-induced cardiomyopathy mice, while SMC had no such effects. SAC and GBMA inhibited Dox-induced excessive mitophagy by downregulating BNIP3 and MFN2 expression, thereby protecting mitochondria and cardiomyocyte nuclei. SND, SAC, and GBMA all alleviated mitochondrial functional impairment in the cardiomyopathy model. They could trigger energy metabolism reprogramming (reducing the expression of the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex subunits PDC-E2 and PDC-E3, and increasing the expression of OXPHOS-CI and OXPHOS-CIV) to optimize mitochondrial energy supply efficiency. SMC could downregulate CII expression in OXPHOS and exert some mitochondrial protective effects, but failed to significantly improve mitochondrial functional impairment.

Conclusions

SND and SAC administration improve Dox-induced cardiomyopathy. They could protect mitochondria and cardiomyocyte nuclei through optimizing mitochondrial energy metabolism efficiency and inhibiting autophagy, while the specific active constituents and their absorption routes remain to be determined. This study elucidates the molecular mechanism by which the adminstration of SAC in SND improves Dox-induced cardiomyopathy, providing new scientific evidence for the combined clinical application of SND and Dox. It also offers a new approach to the research of the substance basis of TCM prescriptions, namely, focusing on the self-assembled substances present in the decoction, rather than assuming the active components are small molecules, to accurately reveal the overall effects of TCM prescriptions and the scientific connotation of their compatibility. It should be noted that the current findings are based on a single batch of SND, and further validation using multiple batches is required to confirm the consistency of the observed effects.

title: Arrhythmia management in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Yassin AS, Faro D, van der Meer P, Blaauw Y.

journal.title: Netherlands heart journal : monthly journal of the Netherlands Society of Cardiology and the Netherlands Heart Foundation

abstractText: Arrhythmias are common in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) and contribute substantially to morbidity at all disease stages. The arrhythmogenic substrate-reflecting diffuse amyloid infiltration, atrial myopathy, autonomic dysfunction, and conduction system involvement-differs fundamentally from that in other cardiomyopathies. Prospective rhythm monitoring reveals a burden substantially higher than previously recognised and predominantly asymptomatic, with bradyarrhythmias and atrial fibrillation (AF) dominating and sustained ventricular arrhythmias remaining rare.This review examines key aspects of arrhythmia management in ATTR-CM. Conduction system disease is frequently encountered, and pacing strategies-including conduction system pacing-are discussed in the context of progressive infiltrative disease. We address the rationale for lifelong anticoagulation in AF irrespective of CHA2DS2-VA-score, and emerging considerations for anticoagulation in selected sinus rhythm patients with impaired atrial function. Rhythm control strategies are reviewed in light of extensive atrial substrate, high AF recurrence rates, and the absence of randomised trial data. The role of implantable cardioverter-defibrillators is examined, with emphasis on the lack of proven survival benefit for primary prevention. Finally, we explore disease-modifying therapies and their potential to attenuate the arrhythmogenic substrate. Overall, structured surveillance, rhythm control, and individualised device decisions form the cornerstones of modern arrhythmia management in ATTR-CM.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonists for people with type 2 diabetes and peripheral artery disease: reducing uncertainty in clinical practice.
authorString: Giugliano D, Caruso P, Longo M, Scappaticcio L, Bellastella G, Maiorino MI, Esposito K.
abstractText: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) may be the most frequent first manifestation of cardiovascular disease (CVD) in type 2 diabetes (T2D). Management of PAD in T2D aims to improve symptoms and lower the high risk of major adverse cardiovascular (MACE) and limb (MALE) events. Drugs commonly used are lipid-lowering and antihypertensive medicines, antithrombotic and antihyperglycemic agents. The ADA recommends both GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2i) as the first-line therapy to reduce the cardio-renal risk in people with T2D, including those with PAD. Meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) show that semaglutide is better than placebo in reducing by 30% PAD events in people with T2D (with or without PAD at baseline), although no RCT was designed to investigate PAD-related hard outcomes as a primary endpoint; however, both liraglutide and semaglutide may increase walking distance by approximately 25-30 m at six months in people with T2D and PAD. Cohort studies also confirm that GLP-1RA use is better than non-use in reducing by 28% the risk of MALE in individuals with T2D and PAD, although their retrospective design might introduce residual confounding and under-ascertainment of outcomes. Dedicated RCTs will obtain more direct evidence for the promising lower limb benefits of GLP-1RAs, but the scientific outlook of specific RCTs on hard limb events is empty. In the meantime, clinicians should choose a GLP-1RA of proven efficacy in subjects with T2D and PAD to improve their cardio-nephro-metabolic outlook, as well as their walking capacity, limited at present to liraglutide and semaglutide.

title: Pulmonary artery to ascending aorta ratio on pre-procedural computed tomography and pulmonary hypertension after transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
authorString: Santillan PJ, Gatuz M, Okuno T, Yoshida T, Kai T, Sekiguchi M, Kobayashi Y, Tanaka T, Saito A, Shoji T, Oda R, Miyahara D, Harashima Y, Shiokawa N, Sato Y, Kuwata S, Sakamoto M, Izumo M, Akashi YJ.
abstractText: To investigate whether pre-transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) computed tomography (CT)-derived anatomical metrics are associated with post-TAVR pulmonary hypertension (PH) with elevated pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR). In this post-hoc analysis of a prospective single-center registry (Invasive PPM Registry; UMIN-CTR: 000054628), 97 patients undergoing TAVR with complete CT, echocardiography, and invasive hemodynamics were evaluated. Prespecified CT metrics included main, left and right pulmonary artery diameters, right ventricle/left ventricle ratio (RV/LV), right ventricular outflow tract wall thickness, septal deviation, and the pulmonary artery-to-ascending aorta ratio (P​A:​AA). The primary endpoint was post-TAVR PH with elevated PVR (mean pulmonary artery pressure > 20 mmHg and PVR > 2 Wood units). Incremental value beyond right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP) was assessed. PH with elevated PVR occurred in 21 (21.6%) patients. Diastolic PA:​AA showed the best discrimination, although this was modest (AUC 0.664, 95% CI 0.526-0.798), other metrics performed less well (AUCs 0.46-0.60). At the Youden-optimal threshold of ≥ 0.90, sensitivity was 61.9%, specificity 72.4%, positive predictive value 38.2% and negative predictive value 87.3%. RVSP discriminated poorly (AUC 0.558); adding PA:​AA(d) improved discrimination (AUC 0.710; ΔAUC 0.152), model fit (p = 0.015), risk separation (IDI 0.066; p = 0.020) and reclassification (category-free NRI 0.690; p = 0.024). PA:​AA(d) correlated modestly with post-procedural mPAP (Spearman ρ = 0.247; p = 0.015). In this exploratory analysis, a larger pre-TAVR diastolic PA:AA ratio was associated with post-TAVR PH with elevated PVR and improved discrimination when combined with echocardiographic RV​SP.Trial registration: This study was registered with the University Hospital Medical Information Network Clinical Trial Registry and accepted by the International Committee of Medical Journal ​Editors (UMIN ID: 000054628).

title: Rheumatoid factor positivity in ANCA-negative eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis: cardiac mimicry, mononeuritis multiplex, and long-term outcome in a case-based systematic review.
authorString: Alghaithi AD, Saryeddine C, Alghaithi RD, Elghazali G, Alnaqbi KA.
abstractText: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is a rare small- to medium-vessel vasculitis characterized by asthma, eosinophilia, and multisystem involvement. Diagnosis is challenging in ANCA-negative disease, particularly when misleading serology is present. We describe a 42-year-old woman with long-standing asthma and a rheumatoid factor (RF) of 322 IU/mL, who initially presented with myocardial infarction-like cardiac involvement with non-obstructive coronary arteries. Over the subsequent seven months, progressive eosinophilia, chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis, and mononeuritis multiplex emerged. ANCA-negative EGPA was diagnosed after connective tissue disease, infection, malignancy, and other causes of hypereosinophilia were excluded. She was treated with prednisolone and azathioprine and subsequently remained off immunosuppressive therapy for more than nine years without reported relapse. On later clinical reassessment, she remained stable apart from mild residual neuropathic symptoms. We also conducted a case-based review following the CABARET standards, searching PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science up to 15 August 2026. We identified 38 published cases of ANCA-negative, RF-positive EGPA, 36 of them without pre-existing rheumatoid arthritis. In these 36, the median age was 53 years and 69% were female. Peripheral neuropathy was reported in 72% and cardiac involvement in 47%; with both occurring in 25%; two patients died of cardiac causes. Among 12 cases with sufficient data to standardize RF relative to the assay upper limit of normal, 75% had RF levels > 3 × ULN. Reporting was often incomplete: both MPO- and PR3-ANCA were documented in only 42% of cases and anti-CCP in 11%. No included published case reported prolonged treatment-free remission, although follow-up and treatment status were incompletely reported in several cases. Based on these gaps, the authors propose a reporting checklist for future EGPA case reports. RF positivity, even at high titer, should not dissuade clinicians from considering EGPA when asthma, eosinophilia, ENT disease, neuropathy, or other compatible manifestations are present.

title: Systematic Review of Clinical Outcomes With the E-tegra™ Stent Graft System for Endovascular Aneurysm Repair: Endoleaks, Limb Patency, Reinterventions, Aneurysm Sac Behaviour, and Mid-Term Follow-Up.
authorString: de Athayde Soares R.
abstractText:
Objective

To systematically synthesize the published clinical evidence regarding endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) using the E-tegra™ stent graft system, evaluating technical success, endoleaks, limb patency, reinterventions, aneurysm sac behavior, and mid-term follow-up outcomes.

Methods

Conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 framework, systematic searches were performed across PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane databases. Observational studies and registry reports reporting clinical outcomes of adults undergoing EVAR with the E-tegra system were included. Because of cohort overlap and heterogeneous endpoint definitions, data were synthesized narratively and descriptively without formal quantitative pooling.

Results

Three eligible publications were identified, representing 209 unique patients across two underlying cohorts: the multicenter TIGRE registry (147 patients) and an independent single-center series (62 patients). Primary technical success was high, reaching 99.3% in the registry and 100% in the single-center cohort, with zero perioperative mortality across both. At mid-term follow-up (ranging from 18 months to 2 years), type II endoleak and iliac limb occlusion emerged as the primary complications. The TIGRE update reported 16 total complications (10.88%), including 8 type II endoleaks and 6 iliac limb occlusions, with a 2-year reintervention rate of 4.76%. In the single-center series, 1 type IIIa endoleak (1.6%) and 3 clinically significant type II endoleaks requiring embolization were observed. Favorable mid-term sac behavior was noted in the registry, with 72.11% of patients demonstrating >10-mm aneurysm sac shrinkage. Predefined anatomical hostility did not demonstrate a statistically significant association with adverse outcomes or reinterventions in the registry data.

Conclusions

Early and mid-term evidence for the E-tegra stent graft demonstrates high procedural success and acceptable clinical outcomes with competitive mid-term complication and reintervention rates. However, the current literature is strictly limited to single-arm observational data with short-to-medium horizons (18-24 months). Long-term durability and structural performance relative to well-established companion platforms remain unestablished, highlighting the critical need for continued prospective surveillance and comparative, long-term multicenter trials.

title: Fenestrated-Branched Endovascular versus Open Surgical Repair for Elective Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
authorString: Pimentel-Junior D, Mastra MM, Huang Y, Mulatti GC, Oderich GS.

journal.title: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery

abstractText:
Objective

This study compared outcomes between patients undergoing elective open surgical repair (OSR) and fenestrated branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR) for thoraco-abdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs) through a systematic review and meta-analysis.

Data sources

PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane.

Review methods

A total of 5 980 articles were screened following the PRISMA protocol. Primary endpoints were thirty day or in hospital major adverse events (MAEs) and mortality, and late all cause mortality. Secondary endpoints were thirty day or in hospital permanent paraplegia, stroke, bowel ischaemia, and new onset dialysis, as well as late re-interventions. A DerSimonian-Laird random effects model was employed to calculate risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for binary endpoints. Significance was defined as a p value of . Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I and evidence certainty with GRADE.

Results

A total of 1 567 patients from five retrospective observational comparative studies were included. FBEVAR was used to treat TAAA in 824 patients (52.6%). Thirty day MAEs (RR 0.51, 95% CI 0.34 - 0.78; p = .002; I2 = 77.0%), mortality (RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.37 - 0.97; p = .040; I2 = 29.0%), and dialysis (RR 0.18, 95% CI 0.06 - 0.54; p = .002; I2 = 80.0%) were significantly less frequent among patients undergoing FBEVAR. Conversely, late aortic related re-interventions were significantly more common in the elective FBEVAR cohort (RR 1.80, 95% CI 1.04 - 3.13; p = .040; I2 = 18.0%). No statistically significant differences were observed between groups in thirty day or in hospital permanent paraplegia (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.51 - 1.91; p = .96; I2 = 39.0%), bowel ischaemia (RR 0.46, 95% CI 0.09 - 2.33; p = .35; I2 = 81.0%), and stroke (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.37 - 2.06; p = .76; I2 = 0.0%), or late mortality (RR 1.29, 95% CI 0.87 - 1.92; p = .20; I2 = 57.0%). According to GRADE, certainty of evidence was low to very low across outcomes.

Conclusion

Elective FBEVAR was associated with a significantly lower incidence of thirty day MAEs, mortality, and acute kidney injury requiring dialysis compared with OSR. In contrast, elective OSR was associated with a significantly lower incidence of late aortic related re-interventions, whereas overall re-intervention rates were similar between groups.

title: Finerenone ameliorates diabetic cardiomyopathy by modulating inflammation through the FoxO3a/Acod1/MAPK axis.
authorString: Li G, Liu J, Li Z, Wang Y, Wang F, Wang L, Su W, Li D, Han J, Li H, Liu Y, Liu X.

journal.title: Journal of diabetes and its complications

abstractText:
Background

Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is one of the leading causes of death among people with diabetes. However, potential treatment strategies for DCM are limited. As another complication of diabetes, finerenone has been shown to alleviate Diabetic Kidney Disease (DKD), but its ability to improve DCM remains unclear.

Methods

A mouse model of DCM was established using a high-fat diet (HFD) combined with low-dose streptozotocin (STZ). We assessed biomarkers such as body weight, blood glucose, and blood lipids in the mice, and evaluated cardiac function via echocardiography. Histochemical staining was employed to evaluate myocardial tissue structure and the degree of fibrosis, and Western blot analysis was used to detect myocardial protein expression. We investigated the underlying molecular mechanisms through transcriptomic analysis. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) was used to measure Acod1 levels in serum samples from patients with DCM.

Results

Following finerenone administration, DCM mice exhibited alleviated abnormal weight gain (p < 0.01), improved glucose tolerance (p < 0.01), and improvements in lipid metabolism: TG (DCM from 2.49 ± 0.3 to FIN-H 0.59 ± 0.1 mmol/L, mean difference[MD]: -1.9, p < 0.01), TC (DCM from 3.90 ± 0.97 to FIN-H 2.03 ± 0.8 mmol/L, MD: -1.87, p < 0.01), LDL-C (DCM from 1.35 ± 0.14 to FIN-H 0.45 ± 0.15 mmol/L, MD: -0.9, p < 0.01), and HDL-C (DCM from 0.32 ± 0.04 to FIN-H 0.52 ± 0.07 mmol/L, MD: +0.2, p < 0.01). Cardiac function improved significantly: LVEF (DCM from 48.49 ± 7.58% to FIN-H 61.96 ± 7.67%, MD: +13.47%, p < 0.05), FS (DCM from 22.65 ± 6.00% to FIN-H 32.8 ± 4.73%, MD: +10.15%, p < 0.05), and E/e'(DCM from 33.91 ± 5.01 to FIN-H 26.17 ± 3.19, MD: -7.74, p < 0.01). Inflammatory markers decreased: CRP (DCM from 1.12 ± 0.20 to FIN-H 0.65 ± 0.21 mg/L, MD: -0.47, p < 0.01) and IL-6 (DCM from 4.97 ± 2.40 to FIN-H 1.91 ± 0.32 pg/mL, MD: -3.06, p < 0.01). Histological analysis showed reduced myocardial fibrosis (collagen volume fraction: DCM from 0.53 ± 0.09% to FIN-H 0.23 ± 0.10%, MD: -0.30%, p < 0.01). Transcriptomic analysis confirmed elevated Acod1 expression in DCM mouse hearts (p < 0.01), and serum Acod1 levels were significantly lower in patients with DCM (29.93 ± 8.84 ng/mL) compared with healthy controls (37.34 ± 9.88 ng/mL, MD: 7.44, p < 0.01).

Conclusion

In summary, finerenone treatment was associated with improved metabolic parameters, reduced myocardial injury markers, reduced inflammation, attenuated myocardial fibrosis, and improved cardiac function in mice with DCM. Notably, finerenone administration also correlated with modulated expression of Acod1 and proteins within the FoxO3a/Acod1/MAPK pathway.

title: Network pharmacology and machine learning nominate PPARG as a candidates target of <i>Aegle marmelos</i> (L.) Correa phytochemicals in breast cancer.
authorString: Zulfiqar H, Khan H, Haroon, Tasnim J, Ali I, Imran M, Knani S, Khan MU.
abstractText: Breast cancer remains a leading cause of cancer death in women, and toxicity, tumor heterogeneity and acquired resistance sustain the search for multi-targeted agents of natural origin. Aegle marmelos (L.) Correa is a traditional medicinal species whose molecular targets in breast cancer have not been defined systematically. Filtering 138 reported phytochemicals on drug-likeness, oral bioavailability and predicted toxicity left six leads, whose 252 predicted targets yielded ten hub genes by protein-protein interaction degree. Three classifiers trained on GSE42568 (104 tumor, 17 normal) under nested tenfold cross-validation reached pooled areas under the curve of 0.939-0.974, and their marker sets intersected in PPARG and ERBB2; a composite score adding differential expression, network degree and out-of-fold SHAP importance ranked BCL2 a clear second, with EP300, EGFR and ERBB2 clustered within 0.02 of one another for third, too close to call. All compounds were docked with six targets; marmeline was the strongest lead at four of the six receptors. Molecular dynamics and Hartree-Fock-level quantum-chemical characterization, completed for marmeline at PPARG against its own co-crystallized reference ligand, rosiglitazone, found both complexes stable over 200 ns (backbone RMSD 2.4-2.6 Å) with MM/PBSA binding free energies of -26.5 and -29.6 kcal mol-1, and confirmed marmeline's optimized geometry as a genuine minimum (zero imaginary frequencies; HOMO-LUMO gap 9.97 eV). Together, these findings identify PPARG as the best-supported target by almost every measure and marmeline as a structurally supported lead for experimental validation.

title: Light-chain amyloidosis causing left ventricular outflow tract obstruction managed with a dual-chamber pacemaker: a case report.
authorString: Chang MJ, Schonman I, Bhatla A, Gelber AC, Rose MR.
abstractText:
Background

Amyloid light-chain (AL) cardiac amyloidosis can rarely mimic hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy with systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve and resultant left ventricular (LV) outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO). Dual-chamber pacing with a right ventricular (RV) apical lead may be another option for LVOT gradient reduction and symptomatic relief for these patients.

Case summary

A 67-year-old man presented with subacute bilateral lower extremity oedema and syncope. Examination revealed a systolic murmur increasing with Valsalva, bibasilar crackles, and pitting oedema. Electrocardiogram showed low QRS voltage disproportionate to the degree of LV wall thickening. Transthoracic echocardiogram demonstrated severe concentric LV hypertrophy with SAM of the mitral valve and LVOTO (65 mmHg at rest, 100 mmHg with Valsalva). Laboratory tests and renal biopsy confirmed lambda AL amyloidosis, and endomyocardial biopsy confirmed cardiac amyloid infiltration. Medical therapy included cautious beta-blockade and midodrine, but the patient experienced refractory syncope. Septal reduction therapy was not anatomically feasible. Dual-chamber pacemaker implantation with RV apical pacing resulted in an improvement in the LVOT gradient and orthostatic symptoms. At more than 1 year after initiation of dual-chamber pacing and therapy directed at his underlying plasma cell dyscrasia, the patient had no further hospitalizations and endorsed sustained symptomatic improvement.

Discussion

Management of LVOTO in patients with AL cardiac amyloidosis is challenging due to competing restrictive physiology and the absence of guideline-recommended practices. Dual-chamber pacing may reduce LVOT gradients and improve symptoms in cases refractory to medical management.

title: The efficacy of add on cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) to symptomatic patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction on sacubitril/valsartan treatment as regards left ventricle reverse remodeling and functional improvement.
authorString: Nazmy NEDM, Eldamanhory HM, Badran HA, Hassan HS.

journal.title: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background

Heart failure (HF) represents a substantial worldwide healthcare burden, with nearly 26 million people affected. CRT is widely recommended for HFrEF patients with QRS duration > 150 msec, but its role in those with QRS duration of 130-149 msec remains debated. The objective was to evaluate whether adding CRT improves LV reverse remodeling and functional status in symptomatic HFrEF patients receiving maximally tolerated sacubitril/valsartan with QRS duration of 130-149 msec.

Methods

This study included 100 patients with HFrEF (≤ 35%) treated with maximally tolerated sacubitril/valsartan and having LBBB morphology with QRS duration of 130-149 msec. Patients were classified into two groups: those receiving CRT and those maintained on medical therapy without CRT. Clinical status, QRS duration, and echocardiographic findings were reassessed after 6 months and compared between groups.

Results

At 6 months, NYHA class improvement occurred more frequently with CRT than without CRT (37 vs. 20 patients, P = 0.004). The decline in end-systolic volume was greater in the CRT group (mean change, 11.42 ± 7.30 vs. 3.54 ± 6.41, P < 0.001). Ejection fraction also showed greater improvement with CRT (mean change, 4.24 ± 3.17 vs. 1.30 ± 2.35, P < 0.001). Hospitalization occurred less frequently in the CRT group (46% vs. 70%, P = 0.03). No deaths were observed in either group throughout follow-up.

Conclusions

In symptomatic HFrEF patients receiving maximally tolerated sacubitril/valsartan with QRS duration of 130-149 msec, adjunctive CRT was associated with greater LV reverse remodeling, improved functional status, and fewer hospitalizations.

title: Alcoholic cardiomyopathy: Metabolic stress, inflammation, epigenetic reprogramming, and therapeutic strategies.
authorString: Samidurai A, Saravanan PB, Chintkuntlawar P, Kottury N, Gupta G, Xi L, Kukreja RC.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Biochim Biophys Acta Mol Basis Dis
journal.title: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Biochim Biophys Acta Mol Basis Dis

abstractText: Alcoholic cardiomyopathy (ACM) is a major form of non-ischaemic dilated cardiomyopathy characterized by ventricular dilation and impaired systolic function following chronic alcohol exposure. Despite partial reversibility with prolonged abstinence, ACM remains an important cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, while the molecular mechanisms driving disease initiation and progression are incompletely understood. Emerging evidence indicates that ACM is not solely a consequence of direct ethanol toxicity, but rather a complex disorder involving interconnected metabolic, inflammatory, immune, and epigenetic pathways. In this review, we summarize current advances in the pathophysiology of ACM and propose an integrated immunometabolic framework underlying disease progression. Chronic alcohol exposure induces oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, calcium mishandling, and endoplasmic reticulum stress, leading to cardiomyocyte injury and impaired cellular energetics. These disturbances activate pro-inflammatory signaling pathways, including NF-κB and the NLRP3 inflammasome, promoting cytokine production and inflammatory forms of programmed cell death such as pyroptosis. Concurrently, accumulating evidence implicates immune dysregulation as a central contributor to adverse remodeling, characterized by altered T-cell polarization, macrophage phenotypic switching, and dysregulated immune checkpoint signaling that sustain chronic inflammation and fibrosis. In parallel, alcohol-induced epigenetic and post-transcriptional mechanisms, including DNA methylation, histone modifications, and microRNA-mediated regulation, establish persistent transcriptional reprogramming that links transient metabolic stress to long-term alterations in cardiomyocyte function and myocardial structure. Collectively, these pathways form a self-reinforcing network of metabolic injury, immune activation, and maladaptive remodeling that drives ACM progression. A more integrated understanding of these mechanisms identifies oxidative stress, inflammasome activation, immune imbalance, and epigenetic reprogramming as interconnected and potentially targetable processes. Therapeutic strategies combining alcohol abstinence with mechanism-based interventions targeting these pathways may provide new opportunities for precision treatment of ACM.

title: Neuroendocrine activation in the pathophysiology of Chagas cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Rumbo-Romero- JA, Rangel-Flores H, Ramos C, Gutiérrez-Perucho E.
abstractText: Chagas disease is a zoonosis affecting 6 million people across 21 countries in Central and South America. Chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy represents the most severe form of organ involvement in the disease, characterized by a high incidence of arrhythmias, stroke, thromboembolic events, heart failure, and sudden cardiac death. Decades of research have focused on persistent parasitism, parasite-induced autoimmune processes, and inflammatory responses to Trypanosoma cruzi as potential mechanisms contributing to the degeneration of cardiac myofibers. In recent years, neuroendocrine imbalances involving the sympathetic nervous system, the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, and central T-cell tolerance in the thymus have been proposed as significant contributors to the pathophysiology. The roles of pituitary hormones, the pineal hormone, adipose tissue, and testosterone have also been emphasized. Thymic atrophy, mediated through caspase-dependent mechanisms, along with the aberrant migration of immature and autoreactive T cells into peripheral lymphoid tissues and the myocardium, are central features that likely act concurrently or synergistically with the already known mechanisms to drive the progression of the disease to its advanced stages. mecanismos dependientes de caspasas, junto con la migración aberrante de células T inmaduras y autorreactivas hacia los tejidos linfoides periféricos y el miocardio, constituye un conjunto de procesos que probablemente actúan de forma concurrente o sinérgica con los mecanismos ya conocidos, impulsando así la progresión de la enfermedad hacia sus etapas avanzadas.

title: Progress in multimodal imaging assessment of the correlation between perivascular adipose tissue and atherosclerosis.
authorString: Wu T, Wu L, Hu P, Chen A, Ye L, Shi J, Jin L, Li Z, Luo X.

journal.title: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging

abstractText: Cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of death and disability worldwide. Adipose tissue dysfunction is a key driver, and perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) exerts location‑specific effects on the cardiovascular system. This review focuses on PVAT in atherosclerosis, with particular attention to pericoronary PVAT, epicardial adipose tissue (EAT), carotid PVAT, and peri-aortic adipose tissue (PAAT). PVAT homeostasis relies on UCP1‑mediated thermogenesis for metabolic modulation and on paracrine signaling via adiponectin and apelin. Under aging, obesity, or diabetes, PVAT switches from an anti‑inflammatory to a pro‑inflammatory phenotype, accelerating plaque formation through bidirectional inflammatory crosstalk. For clinical assessment, this review highlights progress in multimodal imaging technologies, including CT fat attenuation index, MRI water‑lipid separation, PET/CT, and echocardiography, for noninvasive quantification of PVAT density, composition, and metabolic activity, and compares their advantages and limitations. This review further discusses artificial intelligence (AI)-driven radiomic and radiotranscriptomic approaches that extend PVAT assessment beyond conventional single-parameter metrics. We systematically review the research progress of these techniques in evaluating dynamic PVAT changes and their correlation with atherosclerosis, aiming to clarify the intrinsic correlation between imaging‑derived PVAT functional status and AS development.

title: [Multimodal prevention and risk reduction of cardiovascular diseases with focus on obesity and diabetes].
authorString: Könemann S, Lehnert K.
abstractText: Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of death worldwide. Obesity and diabetes mellitus are among the most important modifiable cardiovascular risk factors, promoting the development of atherosclerosis through chronic inflammation, insulin resistance, dyslipidemia and vascular injury. Effective prevention focuses on lifestyle interventions, including dietary optimization and regular physical activity, supported by digital health applications where appropriate. If conservative measures are insufficient, pharmacotherapy, such as sodium-glucose transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors and incretin-based drugs as well as metabolic surgery, should be considered according to the clinical indications. In addition, optimal blood pressure and lipid control are essential. Long-term cardiovascular risk reduction requires an individualized, interdisciplinary prevention strategy integrating medical, behavioral and societal interventions.

title: Mitochondrial antiviral signalling protein (MAVS) in cardiovascular diseases (CVD): a novel pharmacological target.
authorString: Mayamba BS, Chaurembo AI, Chanda F, Zheng X, Liang YT, Deng WH, Liu Y, Huang ZF, Lin YF, Xing N, Liu PP, Lin HB.
abstractText: Mitochondrial antiviral signalling protein (MAVS), also known as interferon-β (IFN-β) promoter stimulator 1 (IPS-1), virus-induced signalling adaptor (VISA), and CARD adaptor inducing IFN-β (CARDIF), has emerged as a regulatory node linking mitochondrial stress, innate immune signalling, and cardiovascular disease (CVD) pathogenesis. In the cardiovascular system, MAVS is activated not only by viral RNA sensors such as retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I) and melanoma differentiation-associated gene 5 (MDA5), but also by endogenous danger signals. This activation promotes transcription of NLR family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) and pro-inflammatory cytokines, and facilitates NLRP3 inflammasome assembly and cytokine maturation, processes implicated in myocardial inflammation, remodelling, and dysfunction in conditions such as myocardial hypertrophy, atherosclerosis, and cardiomyopathy. Beyond inflammasome activation, MAVS intersects with multiple cell death and homeostatic pathways relevant to CVD, including apoptosis, autophagy, and, potentially, ferroptosis. Preclinical studies show that genetic ablation of MAVS, or pharmacological interventions that limit mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS), mitochondrial double-stranded RNA (mtdsRNA) release, or downstream innate immune signalling, can attenuate MAVS-associated inflammation, oxidative stress, and metabolic remodelling, thereby slowing disease progression in experimental cardiovascular models. MAVS, however, also performs essential protective functions, particularly in antiviral defence and maintenance of cardiac homeostasis, underscoring the need for context-specific, cell-type-restricted, or pathway-selective modulation rather than indiscriminate inhibition. Collectively, these findings position MAVS as a promising therapeutic target in CVD, warranting further investigation into MAVS-associated signalling pathways and their modulation in cardiovascular contexts.

title: Early ambulatory re-evaluation and follow-up of patients admitted in the acute cardiac care unit - Practical aspects on ambulatory follow-up of acute care patients: acute coronary syndromes, heart failure, ventricular arrhythmias, atrial arrhythmias, conductance disorders, myocarditis, pericarditis, other acute cardiac settings A Clinical Consensus Statement of the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care of the ESC.
authorString: Roubille F, Lenz M, Morosin M, Algalarrondo V, Kalmanovich E, Schaubroeck H, Sionis A, Vidal-Perez R, Leonardi S, Delmas C, Imazio M, Ammirati E, Aboyans V, Chapet N, Rosenberg A, Belohlavek J, Pavlov M, Vandenbriele C.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care
journal.title: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care

abstractText: Early, structured ambulatory follow-up after hospitalization for acute cardiac events remains a key unmet need in cardiovascular care. This clinical consensus statement of the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care of the ESC provides pragmatic, condition-specific guidance on post discharge management and (early) ambulatory re-evaluation for patients admitted to an acute cardiac care unit. It complements existing disease-oriented guidelines by focusing on the vulnerable transition from hospital to home rather than on acute in-hospital treatment. The document first defines key concepts and outlines general principles regarding timing, content, and organization of the first post-discharge contacts, including risk stratification, medication reconciliation, symptom assessment, evaluation of psychosocial status and comorbidities, patient and family education, and integration of cardiac rehabilitation. In practice, the consensus statement discusses the patient's path after discharge: how should the follow-up team look like, when should the first and subsequent visits be planned, what should be done at each contact, and how can multidisciplinary teams and hybrid (in-person plus remote) models be implemented according to local resources. Supplementary material highlights major evidence gaps, including the optimal timing and intensity of follow-up, the composition of ambulatory teams, the role of telemonitoring and digital health, and the needs of vulnerable populations. Overall, this consensus aims to support clinicians in designing structured, individualized, and scalable ambulatory pathways after acute cardiac care.

title: Not all endothelium is equal: regional and sex-dependent roles of DDAH1 in regulating endothelial function.
authorString: Flynn A, Riddell A, Gilroy N, Pitman JN, Wu Y, MacInnes CAL, Dougan L, Leiper J, Dowsett L, Miller AA.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
journal.title: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
journal.isoabbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol

abstractText: Asymmetrical dimethylarginine (ADMA), an endogenous inhibitor of nitric oxide synthases (NOS), is primarily metabolized by dimethylarginine dimethylaminohydrolases (DDAH1 and 2). This study used endothelial-specific DDAH1 knockout (DDAH1En-/-) mice to test whether reduced endothelial DDAH1 activity impairs cerebral endothelial function and worsens outcomes after cerebral ischaemia-reperfusion. Using male and female, DDAH1En-/- and control (DDAH1fl/fl) mice, we assessed vasoreactivity of middle cerebral (MCA), common carotid (CCA), and systemic arteries (thoracic aortae and first-order mesenteric arteries) ex vivo; and quantified CCA expression of genes associated with vascular smooth muscle (VSM) contractility. ADMA concentrations, and mRNA expression of protein arginine methyltransferases (PRMT), and DDAH were quantified in human cerebral (hCMEC/D3) and aortic (HAEC) endothelial cells. Outcomes following transient MCA occlusion (tMCAo) were also evaluated in male mice. In male DDAH1En-/- mice, NO-dependent vasodilator responses in MCA and CCA were significantly impaired compared to controls, while responses in systemic arteries were unaffected. Vasoconstrictor responses were paradoxically reduced in CCA from male DDAH1En-/- mice in association with altered expression of genes involved in VSM contractility. In contrast to males, vasoreactivity was unaltered in MCA and CCA from female DDAH1En-/- mice. Both PRMT1 and DDAH mRNA expression were higher in hCMEC/D3 compared with HAEC cells, in association with no change in ADMA concentrations. Lastly, in male DDAH1En-/- mice, infarct volumes and functional outcomes post-tMCAo were comparable with controls. These findings underscore a role for endothelial DDAH1 in maintaining endothelial function in cerebral arteries from male but not female mice. However, endothelial DDAH1 does not influence stroke outcomes.

title: In Vivo Comparison of Algorithms Estimating Left Ventricular Stroke Work From LVAD-Derived Pump Parameters.
authorString: Habigt MA, Hein M, Mechelinck M, Olbrich F, Stemmler M, Schulz A, Hammer B, Billig S.
abstractText:
Background

Accurate assessment of cardiac work during left ventricular assist device (LVAD) therapy is essential for patient management, device explantation timing, and adaptive control algorithm development. While invasive pressure-volume methods provide accurate work and contractility assessment, their clinical applicability is limited. Non-invasive algorithms utilizing inherent pump parameters offer a promising alternative, yet no systematic comparison exists.

Methods

Six non-invasive algorithms for estimating stroke work (SW) were compared in 22 healthy German Landrace pigs (48.9 ± 2.6 kg) with a Deltastream DP3 LVAD: maximal LVAD flow derivative, motor power-LV pressure relationship, pressure head-flow relationship, systolic fraction of pressure-flow area, and total/pulsatile components of pump current and flow. After isoflurane-induced heart failure, four interventions were performed: preload reduction (inferior vena cava occlusion, n = 105), afterload increase (aortic balloon occlusion, n = 97), dobutamine infusion (n = 21), and speed ramps (n = 14). Linear multilevel modeling revealed significant main effects for algorithm (χ2 = 582.38), intervention type (χ2 = 73.77), and their interaction (χ2 = 324.80; all p < 0.001), explaining 54.04% of variability.

Results

The pressure head-flow algorithm demonstrated consistently high correlations across interventions, though requiring semi-invasive pressure measurements. The pump flow area algorithm performed robustly during preload, afterload, and speed ramps but failed to capture SW changes during dobutamine. The systolic fraction algorithm achieved the highest correlations during dobutamine but frequently failed mathematical optimization, limiting applicability.

Conclusion

No single algorithm performed optimally across all conditions, necessitating context-specific selection. Pronounced inter-individual variability underscores the importance of patient-specific factors. These findings provide the first systematic comparison of non-invasive SW algorithms during LVAD therapy, offering guidance for algorithm selection.

title: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation with Vitaflow prosthesis in Latin America.
authorString: Chiabrando JG, González V, Rodríguez A, Cafaro G, Menéndez M, Lazarte J, Hauqui A, Mendiz O, Lamelas P, Sztejfman M.
abstractText:
Background

Robust long-term data on the performance and durability of novel transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) valve designs, especially in Latin America, are lacking and warrant further investigation.

Objectives

To provide a 1 year follow-up data regarding a novel TAVI device.

Methods

A retrospective, multicenter cohort study was conducted in Latin America of patients with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis treated with the Vitaflow prosthesis from June 2022 to June 2023. The clinical endpoints were all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, vascular and bleeding complications, permanent pacemaker implantation (PPM), and heart failure admission. Echocardiographic outcomes were the transvalvular gradient and paravalvular leak at 1 year of follow-up.

Results

A total of 46 consecutive patients were included. The mean age of the patients was 80.9 ± 6.13 years; 50% were men, the mean STS score was 4.64 ± 2.67, and 60.8% were in NYHA class III/IV. The most used valve size was the 27 mm (47.1%). All-cause death at 1-year follow-up occurred in 4 patients (8.7%), of which 3 were cardiovascular (6.5%). There were 2 strokes, 1 vascular event, 2 major bleeding events, 4 new PPMs, and no myocardial infarctions or heart failure admissions. The 1-year mean transvalvular gradient was 7 ± 4 mmHg, and 3 patients (6.4%) had moderate paravalvular leak, with no severe leaks.

Conclusions

In a Latin American population, the Vitaflow TAVI valve has proved good safety and efficacy outcomes at 12 months of follow-up in the treatment of patients with severe aortic stenosis.

title: Hypertension and Blood Pressure Dysregulation in Cancer Survivors: Mechanisms, Management, and Future Directions.
authorString: Daniel L, Hundley WG.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

This review examines the epidemiology, mechanisms, and management of hypertension in patients with cancer, emphasizing treatment-related hypertension, autonomic dysfunction, blood pressure lability, and evolving blood pressure targets in cardio-oncology.

Recent findings

Among cancer survivors both during and after their cancer treatment, hypertension is highly prevalent and is associated with increased cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) inhibitors are one of the most common causes of cancer treatment-induced hypertension, although other cancer treatments also contribute. Emerging evidence highlights the coexistence of orthostatic hypotension and hypertension, likely related to autonomic dysfunction, arterial stiffening, baroreflex impairment, and endothelial dysfunction related to cancer and its treatment. Medical management, intensive blood pressure control, and cardio-oncology rehabilitation may improve blood pressure control while mitigating adverse outcomes. Current hypertension management in cancer survivors largely follows general population guidelines despite the unique pathophysiology of cancer and its therapies. Future research should establish cancer-specific blood pressure targets, optimize antihypertensive strategies, and further investigate management of blood pressure lability, autonomic dysfunction, and cardio-oncology rehabilitation.

title: Acute aortic syndrome rule-out criteria: development and external validation.
authorString: Ohle R, Pai CW, Bima P, Reed MJ, Goodacre S, Wilson S, Morello F, Nazerian P, Roy DC, Savage DW, Deb S, McIsaac S, Woznicki EM, Mehta C, Trahanas J, Jakobsen Ø, Hofmann Bowman M, Eagle KA.
abstractText:
Background and aims

Acute aortic syndrome (AAS) is a rare but catastrophic event, presenting with non-specific symptoms that mimic common conditions, and carries a mortality approaching 80% when missed. Current clinical tools, including the Aortic Dissection Detection Risk Score (ADD-RS) and its refinement, the simplified AORTA score, achieve high sensitivity when combined with D-dimer but fail to identify a population at sufficiently low risk to safely avoid further testing. To address this gap, the Acute Aortic Syndrome Rule-Out Criteria (ARC) were developed and validated, a pragmatic bedside tool designed to safely exclude AAS in low-risk patients without additional testing.

Methods

A retrospective multistep derivation and validation study was conducted. The derivation cohort included patients with confirmed AAS from the International Registry of Acute Aortic Dissection (IRAD). Starting from existing scores, candidate predictors were identified from the IRAD dataset and sequentially added to achieve sensitivity ≥ 99%. External validation was performed in patients with suspected AAS across three prospective multicentre cohorts (ADvISED, PROFUNDUS, and DAShED).
