Multivariable linear regression and proportional odds models determined the link of GPV to both inflammatory markers and established cardiovascular risk factors.

Results

Of the 3471 participants, 58% had SA (GPV >0 mm3) at 6-year follow-up. WBC count had the strongest statistical associations with 6-year SA burden after adjusting for age, sex, baseline LDLc, and mean SBP, with an estimated 32.6% increase in GPV per one standard deviation (SD) increase in WBC (Z = 7.33, P < 1 × 10-10). GPV at 6 years increased 40.9% per one SD increase in baseline LDLc and 42.7% per one SD increase in mean SBP (Z = 8.80 and Z = 7.97, respectively, both P < 1 × 10-10; their SDs were 29.4 mg/dL and 11.5 mmHg, respectively), followed by fibrinogen (16.8% increase in GPV per one SD increase, Z = 3.91, P < .0001). High-sensitivity C-reactive protein was not predictive of greater GPV at 6 years (Z = 1.36, P = .174). For WBC, the marked trend in risk occurred only at levels above its median. Similar patterns were observed for separate analyses of carotid and femoral plaque volumes, and coronary artery calcium. Increasing levels of WBC and fibrinogen were also associated with a greater anatomical spread of disease.

Conclusions

Inflammation contributes to SA burden, as assessed by direct plaque quantification, beyond the effects of LDLc and SBP. These findings indicate that inflammation, captured through the use of systemic inflammatory markers, is a risk factor relevant across the entire continuum of atherosclerosis, exerting a deleterious impact comparable to that of LDLc and SBP.

title: The role of global longitudinal strain change in the assessment of early cardiotoxicity in patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors: a prospective pilot study of 30 patients.
authorString: Korucu C, Gökaslan S.
abstractText:
Background

Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) improve survival in various malignancies but may cause immune-mediated cardiotoxicity. Because left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) typically declines late, more sensitive markers are needed for early detection of subclinical myocardial injury. This study investigated the association between changes in global longitudinal strain (GLS) and early cardiotoxicity in patients receiving ICIs.

Methods

In this prospective, single-center pilot study, 30 consecutive adult patients scheduled for ICI therapy were enrolled. Serial transthoracic echocardiography was performed at baseline, 6 to 8 weeks, and 12 weeks to measure LVEF using the biplane Simpson method and GLS using 2D speckle-tracking echocardiography. Cardiotoxicity was defined as a ≥ 10% absolute reduction in LVEF to < 50% and/or new-onset heart failure, suspected myocarditis, clinically significant arrhythmia, or major cardiovascular events. A relative GLS reduction ≥ 15% was considered indicative of subclinical dysfunction.

Results

During a mean 12-week follow-up, cardiotoxicity occurred in six patients (20.0%). In affected patients, GLS significantly deteriorated early (from - 18.2% ± 2.5% to - 14.1% ± 2.8%, P < 0.001), preceding any significant decline in LVEF. Patients without cardiotoxicity showed stable GLS and LVEF values. A ≥ 15% GLS reduction was associated with cardiotoxicity and showed exploratory discriminatory ability, with 83.3% sensitivity and 91.7% specificity (area under the curve, 0.86; 95% confidence interval, 0.72-0.97).

Conclusions

Early GLS deterioration was associated with cardiotoxicity despite relatively preserved LVEF. Given the temporal overlap between GLS assessment and cardiotoxicity events in several patients, these findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

title: Association of coronary artery calcium with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after catheter ablation according to atrial fibrillation type.
authorString: Terashima R, Enomoto Y, Wada M, Miyake W, Kubota S, Okazaki T, Yamamoto M, Hara H, Hiroi Y.
abstractText:
Background

Coronary artery calcium (CAC) reflects systemic atherosclerosis and inflammation and may contribute to atrial remodeling. Although CAC has been associated with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF), whether this association differs according to AF type remains unclear.

Methods and results

We retrospectively analyzed 202 consecutive patients who underwent first-time catheter ablation for AF and had coronary computed tomography between October 2019 and August 2024. CAC was quantified using the Agatston score. The primary outcome was atrial arrhythmia recurrence beyond a 90-day blanking period. Patients were stratified by AF type, and associations were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Branch-specific CAC was also evaluated in exploratory analyses. During a median follow-up of 617 days (IQR, 457-808), atrial arrhythmia recurrence occurred in 19 of 96 patients with paroxysmal AF (PAF; 19.8%) and 39 of 106 patients with non-PAF (36.8%). In the overall cohort, CAC ≥100 was associated with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after adjustment for age, sex, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, and left atrial volume index (adjusted HR, 2.03; 95% CI, 1.07-3.86; P=0.031). In age- and sex-adjusted analyses stratified by AF type, CAC ≥100 was associated with a higher risk of recurrence in patients with PAF (adjusted HR, 5.59; 95% CI, 2.05-15.27; P<0.001), whereas no significant association was observed in patients with non-PAF (adjusted HR, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.56-2.52; P=0.647). The interaction between CAC ≥100 and AF type was statistically significant in the age- and sex-adjusted model (P for interaction=0.011) and remained significant in the expanded clinically adjusted model including hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, and left atrial volume index (P for interaction=0.005).

Conclusions

CAC ≥100 was associated with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after AF ablation, and this association may differ according to AF type, with a stronger association observed in patients with PAF. Subgroup and interaction analyses were exploratory and limited by the small number of recurrence events. CAC may provide useful information for post-ablation recurrence risk stratification, although these findings require validation in larger prospective studies.

title: Current diagnostic clinical examinations for cardiomyopathies: a nationwide survey of cardiologists in Japan.
authorString: Ohtani T, Yasui H, Sakata Y, research group for the investigative study of the diagnosis, clinical application of genomic information in idiopathic cardiomyopathy, Ministry of Health, Labour, Welfare Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research on Intractable Diseases.
abstractText: Idiopathic cardiomyopathies-including dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), restrictive cardiomyopathy (RCM), and arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC)-are diagnosed after excluding secondary cardiomyopathies caused by systemic diseases or specific etiologies. Although current guidelines recommend several diagnostic examinations to aid in this differentiation, the extent to which these tests are used in routine clinical practice and their associated factors remain unclear. We conducted a nationwide web-based questionnaire survey among physicians of the Japanese Circulation Society. An invitation was sent by email to 25,258 physicians, and responses were collected anonymously between January 10 and February 28, 2024. The questionnaire assessed respondents' characteristics and whether they would perform diagnostic examinations for each cardiomyopathy using a five-point Likert scale. Responses were categorized into two groups ("always/frequently" vs. "sometimes/rarely/never"), and multivariable nominal logistic regression analysis was performed to examine associations between respondent characteristics and reported routine use of diagnostic tests. Adjusted trends were also assessed for clinical experience and hospital bed categories. Among 1103 (4.4%) respondents, the frequency of diagnostic examinations varied by cardiomyopathy type. A high proportion of respondents (95%) reported that they would perform coronary evaluations in DCM, whereas this proportion was approximately 80% for other idiopathic cardiomyopathies. In contrast, the proportion of respondents reporting frequent use of examinations relevant to the differential diagnosis of secondary cardiomyopathies, such as endomyocardial biopsy (EMB), cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and nuclear imaging, was generally low. Multivariable analysis showed that institutional and physician-related factors were associated with reported testing patterns. Respondents working at larger hospitals more frequently reported routine use of most examinations, and those with fewer years of clinical experience more often reported that they would perform MRI in DCM and EMB and MRI in HCM. In addition, respondents reporting less frequent EMB use in DCM also reported less frequent use of MRI and <sup>67</sup>Ga scintigraphy/<sup>18</sup>F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography. In Japan, the proportion of physicians reporting that they would routinely perform several examinations relevant to the differential diagnosis of secondary cardiomyopathies was low, and these responses were associated with physician and institutional characteristics.

title: Large Language Models to Label CT Radiology Reports for Incidental Findings Found in Lung Cancer Screening: A Comparative Analysis
authorString: van der Graaf F, Antonissen N, Scholten ET, Schalkx H, Prokop M, Jacobs C.
abstractText: In this study, LLM and prompting strategies for labeling Specific Incidental Findings (SIFs) occurring during lung cancer screening, in radiology reports were compared. In this retrospective study, 300 CT reports from a Dutch academic hospital were included between 19th March 2003 and 28th December 2020. GPT-5, GPT-4-Turbo, Llama-3.1-8B-INST, MedGemma-4B-IT, a keyword-based search method, and a radiologist labelled the reports for the presence or absence of nine SIFs. The radiologist's scores were the reference standard. Each LLM was evaluated with four different prompting strategies: two without Chain-of-Thought (CoT), and two with CoT (one zero shot, one few shot). The automated labelling methods were evaluated against the radiologist primarily using Cohen's Kappa, and additionally sensitivity, specificity, and F1 scores. GPT-5 achieved substantial or almost perfect agreement for seven out of nine SIFs: aortic valve disease, bronchiectasis, consolidation, coronary artery calcification, emphysema, abnormality in mediastinal lymph nodes, and thyroid abnormalities, with Cohen $\kappa$ values of 0.81 (0.70, 0.93), 0.97 (0.93, 1.00), 0.71 (0.62, 0.82), 0.92 (0.87, 0.96), 0.91 (0.84, 0.97), 0.71 (0.62, 0.80), and 0.92 (0.86, 0.98) respectively. For the remaining two SIFs, moderate LLM agreement was obtained with MedGemma-4B-IT and with GPT-4-Turbo with Cohen $\kappa$ values of 0.48 (0.40, 0.60), 0.42 (0.31, 0.58) for interstitial lung abnormalities and mediastinal mass respectively. The highest agreement was obtained with the non-CoT prompt strategies for most SIFs. This study demonstrated that LLMs can automatically label radiology reports with agreement ranging from almost perfect to moderate, but not one LLM -- prompt combination achieved the highest agreement across all SIFs.

title: Completely extraperitoneal approach via midline incision through the pre-transversalis fascia space for resection of retroperitoneal tumor: a case report.
authorString: Wu J, Yi S, Chen G, Chen J, Jiang J, Yang D.
abstractText: Surgical resection is the mainstay of treatment for retroperitoneal tumors. Conventional surgical approaches include the transperitoneal approach and the extraperitoneal approach via the lateral abdominal wall. We report a 36-year-old male with a left retroperitoneal tumor who underwent tumor resection via a midline incision through the pre-transversalis fascia space using a completely extraperitoneal approach along. Compared with the aforementioned approaches, this new technique avoids division of the abdominal wall musculature while preserving the integrity of the peritoneal cavity. The patient was discharged uneventfully on postoperative Day 3. Histopathological examination revealed Castleman disease. Follow-up computed tomography 3 months postoperatively showed no evidence of tumor recurrence. This approach has not been previously described in the literature. This case suggests that for tumors confined to the unilateral retroperitoneal space, it may serve as a safe and viable surgical alternative.

title: Sternal retraction-induced internal mammary artery graft flow impairment: intraoperative assessment and mechanistic insights: a case report.
authorString: Umeda Y, Inoue Y, Mitta S, Matsuno Y, Azuma K.
abstractText:
Background

The internal mammary artery (IMA) is the primary conduit for coronary revascularization, making reliable intraoperative flow assessment indispensable. We describe a rare case in which left IMA (LIMA) graft flow was compromised not by conduit or anastomotic issues but by sternal manipulation.

Case summary

A 76-year-old man undergoing emergency coronary artery bypass surgery reproducibly demonstrated markedly reduced LIMA flow only during wide sternal retraction. Intraoperatively, pronounced unilateral sternal retraction was noted, and postoperative computed tomography confirmed first- and second-rib fractures.

Discussion

These findings suggest a dynamic, retraction-dependent inflow disturbance, possibly related to deformation of the thoracic outlet and proximal subclavian artery. This case underscores the need for careful sternal manipulation, which may help avoid unnecessary graft revision or conduit replacement.

title: Transventricular and Transseptal Closure of Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Pseudoaneurysms After Mechanical Aortic Valve Replacement: Access-Related and Technical Considerations.
authorString: Ealick W, Clark DE, Kipps AK, McElhinney DB.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText:
Background

Pseudoaneurysms of the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) are a life-threatening entity, typically developing as a complication of infective endocarditis or prior cardiac surgery. They should be repaired to reduce the risk of systemic embolization and the catastrophic risks of rupture. Surgical resection has been the gold standard; however, percutaneous transcatheter closure has emerged as an alternative for patients deemed to be at prohibitive surgical risk. The procedural access routes and technical methods for closure remain variable and patient specific.

Aims

This study aims to describe unique cases of percutaneous LVOT pseudoaneurysm closure in patients with mechanical valves.

Methods

From 2023 to 2026, 4 patients underwent percutaneous transcatheter closure of LVOT pseudoaneurysms at our center after prior mechanical aortic valve or root replacement (AVR).

Results

Case 1 highlights an antegrade transseptal approach to pack a wide-necked post-endocarditis pseudoaneurysm with coils. Case 2 demonstrates the ability of a microcatheter to engage a slit-like orifice and utilization of coil embolization without device closure of the orifice due to proximity to the aortic valve ring. Case 3 illustrates a combined approach using devices to close 2 separate orifices and coils to pack a large aneurysm sac. Case 4 represents the first reported case of an excluded LVOT pseudoaneurysm accessed via a percutaneous, transthoracic puncture of the RV free wall and subsequent traversal of the interventricular septum.

Conclusions

In our experience, percutaneous transcatheter closure is a feasible option in most cases and should be considered prior to operative revision unless there is an unstable valve, active endocarditis, or other complicating circumstance that mandate prosthetic valve removal or a surgical approach for other reasons.

title: Opportunistic abdominal aortic calcification assessment on spine radiographs in women with longstanding rheumatoid arthritis: linking cardiovascular burden and femoral neck bone loss.
authorString: Pinheiro MMC, Ramos FP, Silva LVA, Szejnfeld VL, Castro CHM.
abstractText:
Introduction/objectives

Cardiovascular disease (CVD) and osteoporosis are major comorbidities in rheumatoid arthritis (RA). We assessed abdominal aortic calcification (AAC) opportunistically on spine radiographs and examined its associations with CVD, estimated cardiovascular risk, bone mineral density (BMD), and fragility fractures in women with longstanding RA.

Method

This cross-sectional study included 196 consecutive women with longstanding RA followed at a tertiary hospital. All underwent dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry and conventional spine radiography. AAC was graded using the Kauppila score (KS) and categorized as absent, mild-to-moderate (KS 1-6), or extended (KS > 6). Multivariable models evaluated factors associated with AAC and overt CVD.

Results

Participants had a mean age of 62.8 ± 9.6 years and median RA duration of 21 years. AAC was present in 48 women (24.5%), including extended AAC in 25 (12.7%). Overt CVD was documented in 32 participants (16.3%). Extended AAC was independently associated with hypertension (OR 8.57, 95% CI 1.10-67.02), longer RA duration (OR 1.05 per year, 95% CI 1.004-1.09), and lower femoral neck T-score (OR 0.57, 95% CI 0.35-0.95). AAC of any severity was associated with overt CVD (OR 2.89, 95% CI 1.26-6.63).

Conclusions

AAC detected on routine spine radiographs was common among women with longstanding RA and was associated with cardiovascular burden and lower femoral neck BMD. Opportunistic AAC assessment may complement cardiovascular and skeletal risk evaluation in RA. Larger cohorts are needed to confirm these exploratory associations, and prospective studies are needed to establish predictive value.

title: CCL19 emerges as a regional signal in human abdominal aortic aneurysm through targeted proteomic and transcriptomic profiling of the aneurysmal wall and neck.
authorString: Guo J, Lareyre F, Chinetti G, Clement M, Ivanov S, Neels JG, Raffort J.

journal.title: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology

abstractText:
Background and aim

The molecular mechanisms underlying abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) progression remain incompletely understood and may vary across anatomically distinct regions of the diseased aorta. We hypothesised that the aneurysmal wall and aneurysm neck exhibit distinct molecular profiles, reflecting regional heterogeneity in AAA tissue. To this end, we characterized and compared targeted proteomic and transcriptomic profiles of these two anatomically distinct regions to identify molecular alterations associated with AAA pathology.

Methods

Paired aneurysmal wall and aneurysm neck tissues were obtained from 18 patients with AAA. Inflammatory proteins were quantified using the Olink Target 48 cytokine panel, with 45 proteins retained for analysis after quality-control filtering. Directional RNA sequencing was subsequently performed on matched tissue samples to characterize the expression of genes corresponding to the proteins included in the proteomic analysis and to assess concordance between transcriptomic and proteomic differences.

Results

Proteomic analysis identified three differentially expressed proteins (IL6, IL15, CCL19) between aneurysmal wall and neck. Transcriptomic analysis of the corresponding genes identified three differentially expressed transcripts (CCL19, CCL11, LTA). CCL19 was consistently elevated at both the protein and transcript levels in aneurysmal wall, whereas the remaining molecular alterations were specific to either the proteomic or transcriptomic analysis.

Conclusions

Aneurysm wall and neck tissues showed largely similar inflammatory molecular profiles, with only a limited number of regional differences identified either on the protein or transcript level. CCL19 being the only concordant signal in both proteomic and transcriptomic analysis.

title: Zhenwu Decoction improves myocardial energy metabolism and mitochondrial integrity in pressure overload-induced heart failure partly through AMP-activated protein kinase signaling.
authorString: Liu C, Zhang Z, Wang Y, Sun S, Meng T, Li C, Wang B, Wang H, Fu Q.
abstractText:
Ethnopharmacological relevance

Zhenwu Decoction (ZWD), recorded in the Shang Han Lun, is traditionally used for yang deficiency with fluid retention, a pattern relevant to congestion and impaired cardiac function. Its mitochondrial mechanism in pressure-overload heart failure remains unclear.

Aim of the study

To evaluate the cardioprotective effects of ZWD and the contribution of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK)-related signaling.

Materials and methods

Male C57BL/6J mice subjected to transverse aortic constriction received low-, medium-, or high-dose ZWD (4.32, 8.64, or 17.28 g/kg/day, respectively) or the positive control captopril. Cardiac function, remodeling, oxidative stress, energy metabolites, mitochondrial ultrastructure, transcriptomics, and metabolomics were assessed. In angiotensin II-injured H9c2 cardiomyoblasts, small interfering RNA-mediated AMPK silencing was used to assess pathway dependence.

Results

ZWD improved systolic function and reduced ventricular dilation, injury biomarkers, collagen accumulation, and oxidative imbalance, with the most evident effects at the high dose. It increased adenosine triphosphate and acetyl-coenzyme A, reduced adenosine diphosphate and adenosine monophosphate, and preserved mitochondrial ultrastructure. These changes were accompanied by increased AMPK phosphorylation and sirtuin 1 abundance and reduced dynamin-related protein 1 phosphorylation. Multi-omics analyses identified treatment-associated changes in energy-related pathways. AMPK silencing attenuated, but did not completely abolish, the mitochondrial and metabolic effects of ZWD.

Conclusions

ZWD ameliorated pressure-overload cardiac dysfunction and improved myocardial energy homeostasis and mitochondrial integrity. AMPK silencing partially attenuated the cellular response, supporting AMPK involvement in these protective effects, alongside increased sirtuin 1 abundance and reduced dynamin-related protein 1 phosphorylation.

title: The IMA-PLUS Score for Predicting Type 2 Endoleak After Endovascular Repair: Development and External Validation in European and Japanese Cohorts.
authorString: Hatzl J, El-Sanosy E, Kilian S, Barb A, Bornhak L, Ozawa H, Ohki T, Böckler D, ZEPHYR Study Group collaborators.

journal.title: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery

abstractText:
Objective

Prophylactic embolisation of infrarenal branch vessels has been investigated to prevent type 2 endoleak (EL2) following endovascular repair (EVAR) of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA), but patient selection is poorly defined. In this study, a computed tomography angiography (CTA) based risk score was developed and validated to predict EL2 after EVAR.

Methods

This multicentre, retrospective diagnostic study used prospectively collected data from the Zenith alpha for aneurysm Repair Registry (ZEPHYR) as the development cohort. Eligible patients underwent standard EVAR with pre-operative arterial phase CTA and at least one post-operative delayed phase CTA. The model was converted into a numerical score ("IMA-PLUS Score") and validated in two retrospective cohorts. Discrimination, calibration, and risk group thresholds were assessed. In validation cohorts, freedom from AAA expansion and EL2 associated reinterventions up to 5 years were analysed.

Results

Data from 245 patients of the ZEPHYR registry were included. EL2 occurred in 96 patients (39.2%). The IMA-PLUS Score includes inferior mesenteric artery diameter, number of infrarenal renal pole arteries, number of patent lumbar arteries, and median sacral artery patency, achieving a crossvalidated area under the curve (AUC) of 0.78. Using prespecified thresholds (low < 128, medium 128 - 200, high > 200), observed EL2 incidences in ZEPHYR were 19%, 59%, and 74%. In the Heidelberg cohort (n = 134; EL2 44%), AUC was 0.77 (95% confidence intervals [CI] 0.69 - 0.85) with EL2 incidences of 24%, 60%, and 89% across risk groups with good calibration; interobserver agreement for total score was high (intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.95). In the Tokyo cohort (n = 123; EL2 52.8%) AUC was 0.75 (95% CI 0.67 - 0.84); EL2 incidences were 36%, 76%, and 80%, with higher observed incidence than predicted. In validation cohorts, the IMA-PLUS Score was associated with AAA expansion and reduced freedom from EL2 associated reinterventions.

Conclusion

The IMA-PLUS Score may support selection of patients for future studies on preventive management strategies.

title: Image quality assessment of 40-keV virtual monoenergetic reconstruction in low-contrast lower-extremity spectral CT angiography.
authorString: Augustin AM, Sosa Contreras ME, Grandel A, Klink T.
abstractText:
Introduction

Lower-extremity CT angiography (CTA) is widely used for the assessment of peripheral arterial disease. Reducing iodinated contrast medium is desirable, particularly in patients with impaired renal function. This study evaluated the impact of 40-keV virtual monoenergetic images (VMI) on image quality in low-contrast lower-extremity spectral CTA.

Methods

In this retrospective single-center study, 60 patients who underwent lower-extremity spectral CTA with 40 mL of iodinated contrast medium were included. Conventional reconstructions and 40-keV VMI were compared regarding vascular attenuation, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), iodine concentration, and subjective image quality across predefined arterial segments. Qualitative image quality was independently assessed by two readers using a 5-point Likert scale.

Results

Compared with conventional reconstructions, 40-keV VMI significantly increased vascular attenuation, SNR, and CNR across all arterial segments (all p < 0.001). Subjective ratings for vessel contrast, vessel sharpness, overall image quality, and diagnostic confidence were significantly higher with VMI for both readers across all evaluated arterial segments (all p < 0.05). Iodine concentration decreased progressively from proximal to distal arterial segments, whereas the CNR advantage of VMI remained preserved throughout the arterial tree.

Conclusion

Forty-keV virtual monoenergetic reconstruction significantly improves quantitative and qualitative image-quality parameters in low-contrast lower-extremity spectral CTA compared with conventional reconstructions. These findings suggest that low-keV VMI may improve image-quality characteristics in reduced-contrast CTA protocols, particularly in distal arterial segments.

Implications for practice

Low-keV virtual monoenergetic reconstruction may support reduced-contrast lower-extremity CTA protocols by improving image quality without increasing contrast medium volume. This approach may be particularly valuable for patients in whom minimizing iodinated contrast medium exposure is desirable.

title: TAVR in anomalous origin of the right coronary artery with interarterial course and acute takeoff angle.
authorString: Alanís-Naranjo JM, Granados-Casas OM, Galeana-Abarca C, Mayen-Casas JC, Aragón-Ontiveros KD, Gudiño-Resendez AE, Alcocer-Chauvet A.
abstractText: Anomalous aortic origin of the coronary arteries (AAOCA) is an infrequent finding that may increase the risk of coronary obstruction during transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). We report the case of an 80-year-old woman with severe aortic stenosis and anomalous origin of the right coronary artery (RCA) from the left coronary sinus, with an interarterial course and an acute takeoff angle. Preprocedural coronary angiography showed ostioproximal occlusion. Intravascular ultrasound demonstrated approximately 80% extrinsic compression, and coronary physiologic assessment confirmed hemodynamically significant ischemia. Given the high risk of myocardial ischemia during TAVR, the RCA was treated with drug-eluting stents before valve implantation. Subsequently, transfemoral TAVR with a self-expandable valve was performed successfully, with preserved coronary patency and no complications. At 4-year follow-up, the patient remained asymptomatic, with a normally functioning prosthetic valve and no hospital readmissions. This case underscores the importance of detailed preprocedural imaging, coronary physiology assessment, and individualized planning to minimize the risk of coronary obstruction in patients with high-risk AAOCA undergoing TAVR.

title: Fluid-structure interaction simulation and analysis of the aortic valve under the condition of subaortic stenosis complicated with ascending aortic dilatation.
authorString: Xu X, Su F.

journal.title: Computer methods in biomechanics and biomedical engineering

abstractText: Subaortic stenosis (SAS) and ascending aortic dilatation (AAD) often coexist, and the transitional stage from normal to early lesions is critical for intervention, yet their synergistic effects on the tricuspid aortic valve (TAV) remain unclear. This study used a standardized 3D fluid-structure interaction model to simulate nine cases combining different transvalvular gradients and ascending aortic diameters, in order to analyze leaflet kinematics and hemodynamics. The results showed significant synergistic amplification of flow velocity and wall shear stress (WSS). In severe combined lesions, peak flow velocity increased by 144.8% and peak WSS exceeded the physiological threshold by 42%, leading to premature over-opening and asymmetric leaflet motion. A high-risk reference range was identified: ascending aortic diameter ≥30 mm with transvalvular gradient ≥22 mmHg. These findings reveal the mechanical injury mechanism of early combined lesions and provide theoretical references for risk screening and individualized intervention in SAS-AAD patients.

title: Cannula exchange for refractory cannula infections during Berlin Heart EXCOR support: a case report.
authorString: Kawai S, Kido T, Komori M, Kugo Y, Narita J, Ishida H, Ueno T, Miyagawa S.

journal.title: Journal of artificial organs : the official journal of the Japanese Society for Artificial Organs

abstractText: Infection of the cannulae during Berlin Heart EXCOR (BHE) support is a serious complication, with refractory infections often necessitating surgical intervention to prevent their progression to mediastinitis. However, the treatment options for such infections are limited. We report the case of a 4-year-old girl with truncus arteriosus who developed severe heart failure after palliative right ventricular outflow tract reconstruction and aortic valve replacement. The patient successfully underwent a combined surgical procedure consisting of ventricular septal defect and aortic valve closure, redo right ventricular outflow tract reconstruction, and BHE implantation. However, at 10 months after BHE implantation, the outflow cannula exit site was infected by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis. Gallium-67 scintigraphy revealed tracer uptake along the abdominal outflow cannula tract without mediastinal extension. Because the prior aortic valve closure prevented temporary BHE explantation, surgical cannula exchange was performed together with mediastinal irrigation, omental flap transposition, and negative-pressure wound therapy. The infection resolved completely and no recurrent infection was observed during the 1-year follow-up period. In conclusion, cannula exchange combined with omental flap transposition is an effective surgical option for treating refractory cannula infections during BHE support when device explantation is not feasible.

title: Serum Galectin-3 Levels and Aortic Dimensions in Children with Bicuspid Aortic Valve.
authorString: Sönmez E, Vural Ç, Tangüner İH, Yılmaz CZK, Kazımova Y, Keti DB, Baykan A.
abstractText: This study aimed to compare serum galectin-3 levels between children with bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) and healthy controls and to investigate the association between galectin-3 levels and aortic dimensions in children with BAV. This prospective, single-center, cross-sectional, controlled study included 47 children with echocardiographically confirmed BAV and 43 healthy controls. Echocardiographic aortic dimensions and corresponding Z-scores, anthropometric measurements, and serum galectin-3 levels were assessed. Aortic dilation was defined as an ascending aorta Z-score > 2. Age, body mass index, and cardiac function were similar between groups, whereas sex distribution differed significantly. Ascending aorta diameter and Z-score were significantly greater in the BAV group than in controls (27.94 ± 5.56 vs. 21.52 ± 2.53 mm, p < 0.001; 2.34 ± 1.54 vs. 0.31 ± 0.72, p < 0.001). Aortic dilation was present in 28 (59.6%) BAV patients. Serum galectin-3 levels did not differ between BAV patients and controls [8.70 (7.03-11.38) vs. 8.05 (6.10-13.15) ng/mL, p = 0.566]. No significant correlation was found between galectin-3 levels and aortic dimensions or Z-scores. Galectin-3 levels were also similar in BAV patients with and without aortic dilation [8.80 (6.58-12.30) vs. 8.15 (6.30-10.95) ng/mL, p = 0.537]. Serum galectin-3 levels were not associated with aortic dimensions or aortic dilation in children with BAV. Longitudinal studies incorporating serial assessment of aortic dimensions and complementary markers of aortic disease are warranted.

title: Association of A Body Shape Index, But Not Body Mass Index, with Seated Arterial Stiffness Evaluated by Innovative Cardio-Ankle Vascular Index.
authorString: Shimizu K, Ogawa A, Nagayama D, Yamamoto T, Kawakami S, Iwakawa M, Sato S, Mikamo H, Kinoshita T, Shirai K.
abstractText:
Background

A Body Shape Index (ABSI) reflects abdominal adiposity independent of body size. Although the cardio-ankle vascular index (CAVI) is linked to ABSI, whether this association extends to innovative CAVI (iCAVI) remains unclear. We developed iCAVI, an arterial stiffness index measured from the aortic valve to the right brachial artery in the seated position and examined its association with ABSI.

Methods

This cross-sectional study included 117 individuals undergoing cardiovascular risk assessment. iCAVI, ABSI, body mass index (BMI), and waist circumference (WC) were evaluated. Associations were assessed using Spearman's correlation and multivariable analyses adjusting for age and sex-adjusted analyses, with further adjustment for hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, and coronary artery disease. Adjusted iCAVI values across anthropometric tertiles were compared.

Results

iCAVI was positively correlated with ABSI (ρ = 0.233, 95% CI [0.048, 0.402], p = 0.012), but not with WC (ρ = -0.054, 95% CI [-0.238, 0.134], p = 0.563) or BMI (ρ = -0.162, 95% CI [-0.339, 0.026], p = 0.081). Age- and sex-adjusted iCAVI increased across ABSI tertiles (2.79, 2.96, and 3.14; p for trend = 0.045). The linear contrast estimate was 0.25 (95% CI [0.01, 0.49]) and remained similar after further adjustment for hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, and coronary artery disease (0.23, 95% CI [-0.02, 0.48]; p for trend = 0.067).

Conclusions

ABSI was positively associated with iCAVI, whereas BMI and WC were not, suggesting that ABSI may capture aspects of body shape associated with arterial stiffness that are not reflected by conventional anthropometric indices.

title: Isolated Cephalic Perfusion via Aortic Occlusion for Cervicofacial Simulation: Validation of a High-Fidelity Cadaveric Model.
authorString: Benvegnu V, Guibert A, Lopez R, Bonnecaze G, Chaynes P, Lauwers F, Chantalat E, Carfagna L, Prevost A, Cavallier Z, Danevoy V, Festinger Q, Breque C, Weyl A, Barros A.

journal.title: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery

abstractText:
Objective

High-fidelity simulation may improve surgical training in head and neck surgery, yet validated perfused cadaveric models remain scarce. We evaluated the face, content, and construct validity of a perfused cadaveric model using isolated cephalic perfusion for cervicofacial surgical simulation.

Study design

Prospective validation study of a reperfused cadaveric model using SIMLIFE® technology.

Setting

Institute of Anatomy and Surgical Simulation, Toulouse University Hospital.

Methods

Twenty unilateral levels I to IV neck dissections were performed on 11 body donors using a perfused SIMLIFE® model with isolated cephalic perfusion. Seven experts and 5 residents participated. Face and content validity were assessed using Likert-scale questionnaires, whereas construct validity was evaluated using the Onco-Neck-Score through blinded video assessment.

Results

High face validity was demonstrated across most assessed domains, particularly venous wall consistency, venous coloration, nerve appearance, and bleeding flow following vascular injury. Experts rated the model as highly relevant for resident training and surgical skills acquisition. Construct validity was supported by significantly higher Onco-Neck-Score values among experts compared with residents (70.8 [interquartile range 68.8-71.0] vs 58.2 [interquartile range 53.8-61.9], P < .001).

Conclusion

This study supports the face, content, and construct validity of a cadaveric model using isolated cephalic perfusion for cervicofacial surgical training. It provides a realistic environment for neck dissection simulation and may represent a promising tool for surgical education and competency assessment.

title: Near-infrared spectroscopy reveals asymmetric hemispheric blood supply during aortic arch surgery
authorString: El Mokhtari Y, Schumacher FK, Podlasek J, Meissner F, Hiller A, Damjanovic D, Humburger F, Brizzi F, Kirr H, Berger T, Kreibich M, Maier S, Schimmel M, Gottardi R, Urbach H, Unterrainer JM, Czerny M, Kondov S, Kaller CP.
abstractText:
Objectives:

Bilateral and trilateral selective antegrade cerebral perfusion (SACP) aim to ensure symmetric hemispheric perfusion during aortic arch surgery, which current monitoring cannot directly assess. As a step towards real-time monitoring, we assessed the feasibility of multichannel contrast-enhanced near-infrared spectroscopy (CE-NIRS) using indocyanine green and whether hemispheric bolus timing matched expectations for each perfusion configuration.

Methods:

In this prospective, offline-analysed pilot study, 10 patients undergoing aortic arch surgery (9 frozen elephant trunk) received 94 boluses across 10 perfusion configurations. The interhemispheric difference in time to peak (ΔTTP) was compared with the pre-bypass baseline using a linear mixed model with Holm correction, alongside cerebral oximetry; the relationship to postoperative cerebral injury was explored post hoc.

Results:

92 of 94 boluses yielded a bilateral TTP. Contrary to expectation, the left hemisphere peaked later under bilateral (+7.2 s, 95% CI 3.4-11.0; p = 0.003) and trilateral SACP (+8.7 s, 2.5-14.8; p = 0.031). With both left-sided arch vessels on body perfusion, the asymmetry reversed (-7.0 s, -11.7 to -2.3; p = 0.025). ΔTTP detected 6 of 9 configuration effects, whereas oximetry detected none after correction. The three patients with cerebral injury showed the three most pronounced reversals (exact p = 0.100) but were also those managed trilaterally.

Conclusions:

Multichannel CE-NIRS is feasible during aortic arch surgery, without indicator-related adverse events. Bilateral and trilateral SACP did not secure symmetric indicator delivery; the configuration-dependent asymmetry and its reversal point to two steals within the perfusion circuit that oximetry missed. Their clinical relevance requires prospective confirmation.

title: Instructional Revision, Facilitator-Supported Practice, and Cardiac Auscultation Performance: A Seven-Cohort Observational Study
authorString: Corbin C, Hliebova T, Polykandriotis E, Mehta S, Benjamin L, Calton R.
abstractText: Review of objective structured clinical examination (OSCE) results identified aortic sclerosis as the lowest-performing Harvey simulator station, with faculty reporting that students confused it with aortic stenosis because both present with systolic murmurs. Instruction was revised to emphasize carotid palpation and murmur radiation, the distinguishing finding, but performance did not improve. Facilitator supervision was later added to existing extended-hours practice without increasing simulator availability, allowing supervision to be examined independently of access. We analyzed seven consecutive OSCEs delivered under one curriculum and one machine-scored 14-item instrument (1,121 student-station observations, 2024 to 2026). The revision took effect in Fall 2024; four facilitators joined practice sessions from Summer 2025, intervening only when students encountered difficulty. The primary outcome was performance at the aortic sclerosis station, named in monitoring records before either intervention; mitral valve prolapse, whose diagnostic feature is independent of the revised maneuver, served as a comparison outcome. The revision alone produced no improvement, with performance across the three preceding cohorts flat to declining (83.3%, 82.2%, 81.1%). After facilitators were added, aortic sclerosis rose from 81.7% to 89.9%, a difference-in-differences of 7.87 points (95% CI 3.06 to 12.69, P = 0.001), and students scoring below 70 fell from 25.9% to 12.0%. Overall performance rose from 82.4% to 88.3% (5.65 points, 95% CI 0.87 to 10.43, bootstrap P = 0.016), while the comparison station changed by 0.40 points (P = 0.84). Facilitator-supported practice may provide educational benefit beyond access to simulation resources alone.

title: Sacubitril/valsartan for radiation-induced heart disease in children: preclinical and clinical findings.
authorString: Zhao L, Guo X, Tang Y, Hua Y, Liu X, Yue F, Chen X, Li B, Dai X, Shen C, Gao J, Zhou K, Tang Q, Wang C.
abstractText:
Background and aims

Radiation-induced heart disease (RIHD) is a life-threatening sequela for cancer survivors. A proactive preventive strategy is urgently needed but remains elusive, particularly for the vulnerable paediatric population where prospective data are scarce. To address this gap, this study aimed to evaluate the prophylactic efficacy of sacubitril/valsartan against RIHD in children through a comprehensive translational research pipeline.

Methods

A prospective observational study was first conducted in 40 paediatric solid tumour patients, comparing cardiac function before and 1 week after radiotherapy, with 80 healthy controls. A juvenile rat RIHD model was then established, in which the efficacy of sacubitril/valsartan was assessed and validated through longitudinal echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, histopathology, bulk RNA-seq, and single-nucleus RNA-seq. Finally, a prospective clinical cohort (n = 15 sacubitril/valsartan, n = 15 control) was conducted in paediatric patients post-radiotherapy, with a 12-month follow-up for efficacy and safety.

Results

In paediatric patients, radiotherapy significantly impaired biventricular function, notably reducing left ventricular global longitudinal strain, and mean heart radiation dose was significantly correlated with cardiac function impairment. In juvenile rats, sacubitril/valsartan attenuated pathological ventricular wall thickening, myocardial fibrosis, diastolic dysfunction, and perfusion deficits. Mechanistically, it mitigated endothelial cell damage and immune cell activation, promoted a macrophage phenotypic shift from M1 to M2, suppressed fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition, and broadly attenuated pro-fibrotic and inflammatory cell-cell communication. In the clinical cohort, sacubitril/valsartan significantly improved left ventricular global longitudinal strain and aortic compliance vs controls, with a favourable safety profile.

Conclusions

This first-in-kind translational study demonstrates that early prophylaxis with sacubitril/valsartan is a feasible and effective strategy to mitigate radiation-induced cardiotoxicity in children. These findings, underpinned by multi-modal validation from bench to bedside, challenge the reactive management paradigm in paediatric cardio-oncology and establish a foundational evidence base for a new standard of proactive heart care in childhood cancer survivors.

title: [Isolated persistent left superior vena cava: a rare presentation].
authorString: Ortega-Zhindón DB, García-Montes JA, Arenas-Fabbri V, Hernández-Enciso G, González-Pacheco MG, Cervantes-Salazar JL.
abstractText: Anomalies of systemic venous return represent rare congenital malformations, accounting for approximately 2% of all such cases. The occurrence of congenital heart disease patients exhibiting an isolated persistent left superior vena cava has been observed at a frequency of 0.07 to 0.13%. Due to their rarity, these anomalies are frequently associated with chromosomal abnormalities. These forms may manifest in isolation or in conjunction with other congenital heart conditions. The following report details a case of a patient two-year-old.

title: [Right coronary artery to right atrium fistula treated by percutaneous closure].
authorString: Vargas-Echeverría C, Echeverría-Consuegra R, Carrillo-López I, Vargas-Echeverría L, Da Acosta-Cardona A.
abstractText: Coronary fistulas are rare congenital anomalies defined by an abnormal communication between a coronary artery and a cardiac chamber or great vessel. We report the case of a 5-year-old male patient (17 kg) referred for cardiac catheterization due to echocardiographic suspicion of patent ductus arteriosus. Coronary angiography revealed a fistula originating from the right coronary artery with direct drainage into the right atrium. Percutaneous closure was successfully performed using a COMED PDA 4/6 device. Post-procedural angiography showed complete occlusion without residual shunt. This case highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic role of cardiac catheterization in congenital coronary anomalies.

title: Retrospective Mexican experience in the transcatheter closure of atrial septal defects using different devices.
authorString: Mijangos-Vázquez R, Pérez-Ruíz VM, Hernández-Reyes R.
abstractText:
Background

Over the past decades, significant advancements and innovations have occurred in the field of percutaneous atrial septal defect (ASD) closure using transcatheter-based devices. The Amplatzer septal occluder has been widely used since its Food and Drug Administration approval in 2001. Studies have shown its high success rate in closing ASDs. Since then, many other devices have been developed and used with high technical success and closure rates, with low rates of serious adverse events and device-related complications. When compared to surgery, percutaneous closure provides a less invasive approach with quicker recovery and reduced physical and psychological impact.

Objectives

To demonstrate the effectiveness of using different devices for transcatheter ASD closure, emphasizing the success and complications obtained in our patients.

Methods

Patients with congenital ASDs who underwent transcatheter closure using different devices were included. The primary endpoint was to determine the efficacy and safety of these devices and to determine the incidence of complications at follow-up. Two hundred and eighty-seven patients underwent ASD closure at a median age of 6 years (7 months-70 years).

Results

Only minor complications occurred during catheterization. After a follow-up of 90 ± 67.7 months (up to 96 months), the closure rate was 98.6%, and the absence of atrioventricular block was 100%.

Conclusions

Transcatheter ASD closure using percutaneous devices has proven to be safe and effective in most cases. However, careful patient selection and follow-up are necessary to minimize complications and ensure optimal outcomes.

title: Target-oriented contrast enhancement strategies for pediatric cardiac CT angiography in congenital heart disease: a narrative review.
authorString: Masuda T, Funama Y, Shohji T, Nakaura T.
abstractText: Congenital heart disease (CHD) often requires precise anatomical assessment from the neonatal and infant periods. Although echocardiography remains the first-line imaging modality, cardiac computed tomography angiography (CTA) plays an important complementary role in evaluating complex cardiovascular anatomy, coronary artery origin anomalies, great vessel abnormalities, and postoperative anatomy. However, contrast enhancement behavior in neonates and infants differs substantially from that in adults because of low body weight, high heart rate, small-caliber veins, limited circulating blood volume, and short circulation time. In addition, disease-specific flow patterns such as right-to-left shunting, Glenn circulation, Fontan circulation, and surgically altered pathways further modify contrast arrival, mixing, and washout. This narrative review summarizes practical strategies for optimizing contrast enhancement in pediatric cardiac CTA for CHD. Key considerations include iodine dose, contrast concentration, injection rate, injection duration, venous access, saline flush, timing method, and CT technology. The available literature suggests that contrast protocol design should be individualized according to body size, circulation pattern, target anatomy, and scanner performance. In normal neonatal and infant circulation, reproducible enhancement may be supported by body-weight-based iodine dosing, low-kV imaging, diluted contrast material, and stable low-flow injection. In abnormal circulation, particularly Glenn and Fontan physiology, protocol design should additionally consider access-site selection, delayed arrival, heterogeneous mixing, and bolus shaping tailored to the hemodynamic setting. Because the current evidence base remains heterogeneous and is largely derived from single-center studies, the protocol ranges summarized in this review should be interpreted as a practical framework rather than as formal guideline-level recommendations.

title: Additional pulmonary blood flow strategy at bidirectional Glenn: impact on pulmonary artery growth and long-term Fontan outcomes.
authorString: Orioli V, Careddu L, Berardi M, Mangerini VF, Petridis FD, Egidy Assenza G, Agulli M, Donti A, Gargiulo GD, Angeli E.
abstractText:
Objective

Management of additional pulmonary blood (APBF) flow during staged palliation toward Fontan completion remains debated, however it may influence long-term outcomes. To assess whether APBF promotes pulmonary artery (PA) growth before Fontan completion and whether different APBF strategies correlate with distinct long-term outcomes.

Methods

A retrospective single-center study was conducted on 205 patients undergoing Fontan completion between 1989 and 2024. Of these, 98 had APBF (83 antegrade APBF, 15 persistent mBT-shunt). Long-term outcomes included survival and freedom from PA stenting.

Results

Pre-Fontan PA diameters were larger in patients with APBF than in those without APBF: LPA 10.70 ± 3.76 mm vs 8.80 ± 3.43 mm (p < 0.0001) and RPA 12.18 ± 3.65 mm vs 10.99 ± 3.65 mm (p = 0.032). Within the APBF group, antegrade flow was associated with larger PA diameters than persistent mBT-shunt: LPA 11.12 ± 3.70 mm vs 9.01 ± 3.51 mm (p < 0.0001) and RPA 12.56 ± 3.67 mm vs 11.12 ± 3.59 mm (p = 0.009). Overall survival was higher in patients with APBF at 20 years (97.5% [95% CI, 83.6%-99.6%] vs 88.2% [95% CI, 75.9%-94.4%], p = 0.032). Freedom from PA stenting at 10 years was 98% (95% CI, 81.7%-96.1%) in patients without APBF, 95% (95% CI, 86.3%-98.5%) in those with antegrade APBF, and 78% (95% CI, 45.9%-92.3%) in those with persistent mBT-shunts.

Conclusions

APBF appears to promote PA growth without increasing pulmonary pressures, but both APBF strategies may be associated with branch PA stenosis, with different timing according to flow type.

title: Time-resolved single-cell screening reveals the dynamic regulatory architecture of human cardiogenesis
authorString: Lindenhofer D, Mikulik K, Mantz S, Jung H, Ueltzhoeffer K, Kueblbeck M, Rueda-Gensini L, Munoz-Verdu A, Haas J, Meder B, Schraivogel D, Mall M, Huber W, Pettet A, Reddington J, Clarke B, Stegle O, Steinmetz LM.
abstractText: Congenital heart disease (CHD) originates during early embryogenesis, yet when disease genes act cannot be determined from existing data. Human fetal heart atlases lack critical time points, and perturbation screens that systematically assess gene function currently profile at most a few time points. Here we combined single-cell CRISPR screening of 400 disease-relevant genes in cardioids, sampled daily over seven developmental days (~975,000 cells), with a matched multiome atlas. Perturbation phenotypes were strongly dependent on developmental stage. Perturbations that reshaped cell-fate allocation or gene expression were enriched for CHD-linked genes, and most acted already during progenitor stages. Timing was largely independent of the target gene's own expression, marking instead when a cell state became functionally dependent on it, and some effects persisted after expression declined. Consensus gene regulatory networks integrating perturbation and multiome data recovered stage-specific regulators and nominated HOXB2 and HOXB3 as candidate cardiac regulators. Many perturbations converged on shared downstream programmes, which were reorganised through differentiation. Effects correlated in progenitors were maintained in differentiated cells, split into distinct programmes, converged with other perturbations or disappeared entirely, indicating that gene function is highly context dependent. Beyond advancing our understanding of the developmental regulatory logic underlying CHD, our work provides a resource for developing context-dependent models for in silico prediction of perturbation effects.

title: Pediatric ECG foundation model via adult-to-pediatric fine-tuning: downstream tasks and clinical evaluation
authorString: Cao Y, Xu H, Li X, Yang J, Feng Y, Wang W, Li H.
abstractText: Pediatric electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation is complicated by age-dependent electrophysiological changes that limit direct transfer of adult AI models. We asked whether an adult ECG foundation model could be adapted to pediatric ECGs. Using 339,563 12-lead ECGs from 238,189 children, we compared direct application, pediatric fine-tuning, and training from scratch under an identical architecture. Direct transfer was poor (mean AUC 0.8256). Fine-tuning reached 0.9695, above de novo training (0.9661), and attained 0.9079 using only 1% of training data. On 10,999 external ECGs, fine-tuning achieved a mean AUC of 0.9385 across 30 labels. It generalized to age regression (MAE 1.12 years) and congenital heart disease classification (AUC 0.9562). Across 17 clinicians and 100 cases, diagnostic accuracy rose from 56.8% to 65.4% (p < 0.001) and did not decline when AI erred. Adult ECG foundation models require pediatric adaptation; fine-tuning offers a data-efficient route to scalable pediatric ECG AI.

title: Tricuspid inflow E-wave velocity for the assessment of severe or greater tricuspid regurgitation: derivation and external validation of threshold values.
authorString: Fisicaro S, Moldovan MP, Kawada Y, Penso M, Simonato M, Buta AS, Negru A, Clement A, Springhetti P, Radu N, Heilbron F, Tomaselli M, Rella V, Muraru D, Hahn RT, Badano LP.
abstractText:
Aims

Current guidelines include tricuspid inflow E-wave (>100 cm/s by pulsed-wave Doppler) as a semiquantitative criterion for diagnosing severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR), despite limited supporting evidence. We assessed its diagnostic performance for identifying severe or greater TR, deriving and externally validating practical thresholds.

Methods and results

Tricuspid inflow E-wave velocity was measured by pulsed-wave Doppler in consecutive patients with at least mild TR between December 2024 and February 2026. Among 178 patients (77±13 years, 65% women), TR was mild in 44, moderate in 61, severe in 44, massive in 15, and torrential in 14. Mean tricuspid E-wave velocity was 56±16 cm/s and increased with TR severity: 47±8, 50±10, 62±16, 67±13, and 77±21 cm/s for mild, moderate, severe, massive, and torrential TR. Only three patients had E-wave velocity >100 cm/s (one with severe and two with torrential TR). Using multiparametric echocardiographic grading as the reference standard, the >100 cm/s threshold showed 5.5% sensitivity, 100% specificity, and kappa 0.25 for severe or greater TR. As a continuous variable, E-wave velocity discriminated severe or greater TR with an AUC of 0.81. A lower threshold of 52 cm/s yielded 81% sensitivity and 67% specificity, whereas 47 cm/s provided 90% sensitivity and 43% specificity. External validation resulted in 94% sensitivity and 47% specificity.

Conclusion

The guideline-recommended threshold of >100 cm/s is highly insensitive for detecting severe or greater TR. Lower cut-offs, particularly 47 cm/s, may be useful for screening to trigger a comprehensive multiparametric assessment.

title: Myocardial Responses to Eplontersen in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: The CARDIO-TTRansform CMR study.
authorString: Razvi Y, Solomon SD, Cuddy SAM, Venneri L, Martinez-Naharro A, Cappelli F, Cipriani A, Garcia-Pavia P, Masri A, Sheikh A, Ramos-Lopez N, Sekar P, Conrad T, Claggett B, Kellman P, Sheikh FH, Grodin JL, Manisty C, Thornton GD, Moon JC, Maurer MS, Angeli FS, Chen J, Tsimikas S, Gillmore JD, Fontana M.
abstractText:
Background

Transthyretin-lowering therapies target the underlying cause of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), but their effects on myocardial amyloid burden and cardiac remodelling remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated the myocardial effects of sustained transthyretin suppression with eplontersen using serial multiparametric cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR).

Methods

This CMR study was a pre-specified, international, prospective study embedded within the randomized, placebo-controlled phase 3 CARDIO-TTRansform trial. Participants underwent CMR at baseline and planned assessments at weeks 25, 49, 97, and 140. The primary imaging analysis evaluated longitudinal changes in CMR parameters using mixed models for repeated measures. Myocardial amyloid regression and progression were defined as ≥5 percentage-point decreases and increases in extracellular volume (ECV), respectively. All other patients were considered stable.

Results

We enrolled 120 participants with baseline and ≥1 follow-up CMR assessment (eplontersen, n=58; placebo, n=62; mean age, 76.7±6.5 years; 95% male; baseline stabilizer, 12.5%). At week 140 eplontersen resulted in lower ECV, compared with placebo (least-squares mean difference [95% CI], -6.7 percentage points [ -8.7 to -4.7]; P<0.001) and lower native T1 ( -25.9ms [-41.7 to -10.2 ]; P=0.002) and left ventricular mass (-19.1g [-28.0 to -10.2]; P<0.001). Eplontersen also increased left ventricular ejection fraction (+5.1% [1.8-8.3]; P=0.002), right ventricular ejection fraction (+4.6% [0.6-8.7]; P=0.03), and left ventricular global longitudinal, circumferential, and radial strain and right ventricular longitudinal strain (all P<0.05), compared to placebo. At week-140, myocardial amyloid regression occurred in 12.5% receiving eplontersen versus 0% receiving placebo, whereas progression occurred in 12.5% versus 76%, respectively.

Conclusions

Sustained transthyretin suppression with eplontersen resulted in substantially lower myocardial ECV and favorable changes in cardiac structure, biventricular systolic function, and myocardial deformation compared with placebo in a cohort of patients mostly not on background stabilizer at baseline. These findings provide randomized evidence that lowering circulating transthyretin modifies myocardial disease progression in ATTR-CM and support serial multiparametric CMR for characterizing myocardial treatment response.

title: From Dysbiosis to Vascular Disease: the Gut Microbiota in Type 2 Diabetes and Atherosclerosis.
authorString: Sasidharan Pillai S, Ashraf AP.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

Type 2 diabetes (T2D) and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) are closely linked chronic disorders and leading causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Increasing evidence identifies the gut microbiota (GM), including its microbial genes and metabolites, as potential modifiers of these processes. This narrative review summarizes mechanistic, translational, and clinical evidence linking GM dysbiosis with T2D and atherosclerosis and evaluates microbiota-directed therapeutic strategies.

Recent findings

Converging mechanistic, translational, and clinical evidence supports GM dysbiosis as a plausible shared contributor to T2D and atherosclerosis through interconnected pathways involving impaired intestinal barrier integrity and metabolic endotoxemia, TLR4/NF-κB- and inflammasome-mediated inflammation, and microbial metabolites, including short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), bile acids (BAs), trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), phenylacetylglutamine (PAGln), and tryptophan-derived indoles. These pathways can influence glucose and lipid metabolism, insulin signaling, immune activation, endothelial function, and vascular inflammation, providing a biological framework linking dysglycemia with increased cardiovascular risk and supporting the GM as a potential therapeutic target. However, the field remains limited by predominantly observational and confounded human data, incomplete causal evidence, and heterogeneous responses to microbiota-directed interventions. Dietary modification, prebiotics, probiotics, synbiotics, next-generation probiotics and postbiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation, and microbiota-modulating antidiabetic therapies have shown signals of benefit on metabolic or vascular surrogate endpoints, but evidence for durable clinical benefit remains limited and inconsistent across strains, populations, and study designs. Future progress in GM manipulation to improve cardiometabolic outcomes will require function-focused, causally grounded research and adequately powered, outcome-driven clinical trials incorporating GM-guided patient stratification. Until such evidence is available, the GM should be viewed as a biologically compelling and promising, but not yet clinically actionable, link between metabolic and atherosclerotic disease.

title: Effects of Eplontersen on Cardiac Structure and Function in Patients With Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy: Insights from the CARDIO-TTRansform Trial.
authorString: Jering KS, Skali H, Claggett B, Prasad N, Chen J, Gonzalez-Lopez E, Morbach C, Cuddy SAM, Davis MK, Fernandes F, Mitchell JD, Sarswat N, Urey MA, Platz E, Tsimikas S, Maurer MS, Fontana M, Solomon SD.
abstractText:
Background

In CARDIO-TTRansform, the TTR (transthyretin) silencer eplontersen did not significantly reduce the primary end point of cardiovascular death and recurrent cardiovascular events in patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy, although treatment effects varied by baseline TTR stabilizer use. Whether eplontersen favorably affects cardiac structure and function is unknown.

Methods

CARDIO-TTRansform randomized 1432 patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy to eplontersen (45 mg) subcutaneously every 4 weeks or placebo. Echocardiograms were performed at baseline and weeks 61, 97, and 140. Associations of baseline echocardiographic measures with all-cause mortality and the primary end point were evaluated using Cox and semiparametric proportional rates models. Between-group differences at week 140 were analyzed with mixed models for repeated measures.

Results

Among 1426 participants with baseline echocardiograms (mean age, 76±7 years, 91% men, 85% wild type, 57% receiving stabilizers), baseline measures of left ventricular systolic function (LV ejection fraction, global longitudinal strain, stroke volume, myocardial contraction fraction), diastolic function (E wave deceleration time, septal e', average E/e'), and right ventricular function and hemodynamics were independently associated with all-cause mortality or the primary end point. At week 140 (echocardiograms available in 554 patients in the eplontersen group and 506 in the placebo group), eplontersen attenuated increases in mean LV wall thickness (least-squares mean [LSM] difference, -0.24 mm [95% CI, -0.48 to -0.01]) and declines in LV stroke volume (LSM difference, 1.88 mL [95% CI, 0.07-3.69]), myocardial contraction fraction (LSM difference, 0.88% [95% CI, 0.25-1.57]), average E/e' (LSM difference, -0.71 [95% CI, -1.36 to -0.07]), and right ventricular outflow tract velocity-time integral (LSM difference, 0.42 [95% CI, 0.00-0.85]) versus placebo in the overall cohort. Beneficial effects were driven almost exclusively by patients not receiving stabilizers at baseline. No significant treatment effects were observed in patients receiving stabilizers.

Conclusions

Among patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy, eplontersen modestly attenuated deterioration in prognostically important measures of LV systolic, diastolic and right ventricular function, primarily among patients not receiving stabilizers at baseline. These findings complement the clinical findings of CARDIO-TTRansform and suggest that TTR silencing may attenuate progression of cardiac dysfunction in TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy.

title: Post-approval study preliminary 1-month outcomes of the first 100 patients treated with an off-the-shelf multibranch aortic device.
authorString: Lee JT, Jackson BM, Zimmerman PM, Bath JM, Orion KC, Rossi PJ, Han SM.
abstractText:
Objectives

To report the preliminary 1-month outcomes from the post-approval study of the first 100 patients treated with the GORE® EXCLUDER® Thoracoabdominal Branch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE).

Methods

This multicenter, nonrandomized, prospective study of the TAMBE aortic component included endovascular repair of an aortic disease involving the visceral vessels. Demographics, core-lab adjudicated imaging characteristics, perioperative metrics, and postoperative 1-month outcomes are reported.

Results

The first 100 patients treated were 30% female, 81% white, and the median was age 74 years. Anatomic classifications included 48 patients (49.0%) with Extent I-IV thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA), 21 (21.4%) with pararenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA), 12 (12.2%) with juxtarenal AAA, and 17 patients with post dissection pathology (n=11) or 'other' (n=6). Enrollment and treatment of 45.0% of the patients were at sites without prior TAMBE device experience. Prior aortic surgery was noted in 48.0% of patients treated. For patients with Extent I-III TAAA (n=22), staging of the TAMBE procedure was planned with initial proximal thoracic endovascular aortic repair in 7 patients (31.8%). Median aneurysm diameter was 6.2 cm. The GORE® VIABAHN® VBX Balloon Expandable Endoprosthesis was used in all patients, with additional use of a VIABAHN® self-expanding stent in six patients. Intentional non-use of one or more portals (with planned plug occlusion) was a strategy used in 15 (15.0%) patients. Median procedure time was 280 minutes, and median length of stay was four days with 83 patients (83.8%) discharged to home. Branch target vessel technical success rate was 98.9% (average of 1.39 stents into the celiac, 1.44 superior mesenteric artery, 1.62 right renal, and 1.59 left renal per portal). Three patients (3.0%) died, all were procedure related. Major adverse events in 8 patients (8.1%, 3 had ≥1 event) included 1 (1.0%) respiratory failure, 4 (4.0%) permanent paraplegia, 4 (4.0%) renal function decline, and 1 (1.0%) bowel ischemia. No patient experienced a major stroke, aneurysm rupture, or myocardial infarction. A total of eight Type 1c or Type IIIa/IIIc endoleaks were detected in 6 (6.1%) patients. No conversion to open-surgical repair, rupture, or device migration/integrity issues were reported.

Conclusions

The preliminary analysis of the FDA-mandated post-approval study 1-month outcomes in this prospective multicenter cohort treated with the TAMBE device demonstrates applicability to more extensive thoracoabdominal pathology with similar outcomes to the pivotal trial. Distinct findings for the TAMBE device in the real-world include successful treatment of post-dissection aneurysms, increased staging strategies for spinal cord protection with low paraplegia rates, and rapid adoption by many sites that did not participate in the pivotal trial.

title: Renin Kinetics and Hemodynamic Response During Treatment of Vasoplegic Shock With Angiotensin II (TENSINTEST): Protocol for a Multicenter Observational Study.
authorString: Möller Petrun A, Bajec KB, Chawla L, Zmazek J, Markota A.
abstractText:
Background

Shock is a life-threatening condition that can lead to multiorgan failure and death. Vasopressors are needed for the treatment of vasoplegic (distributive) shock. Angiotensin II (AT II) is a novel vasopressor. Approximately two-thirds of patients respond to AT II, and one-third do not. AT II is part of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS). Renin is the limiting enzyme of the RAAS, and among other mechanisms, its concentration is regulated by AT II concentration through a negative feedback loop. It might be an indicator of response to AT II therapy.

Objective

We designed a study with a primary objective of developing and standardizing an AT II stress test, which could help predict the responsiveness to AT II in patients with distributive shock, regardless of its origin.

Methods

This is an investigator-initiated, multicenter observational clinical study of renin kinetics before and 6 hours after starting an infusion of AT II in patients with vasoplegic shock and adequate fluid resuscitation who are severely ill. Prior to AT II, patients will receive an infusion of norepinephrine base of 0.3 mcg per kilogram per minute or higher, and vasopressin of 0.03 IU per minute according to institutional protocol. Blood samples for serum renin determination will be obtained immediately prior to and after 6 hours of AT II infusion. We hypothesize that patients who demonstrate a negative trend in relative renin ratio (defined as renin plasma concentration at baseline or at 6 hours after treatment with AT II divided by upper normal concentration of plasma renin [50 mU/L]) will have a greater number of 28-day organ failure-free days (days without vasopressors, mechanical ventilation, or renal replacement therapy). The primary analysis will assess the association between early renin reduction and organ failure-free days using an adjusted proportional odds ordinal regression model.

Results

The research was funded in December 2024. After obtaining ethics approval in July 2025, data collection started on August 1, 2025. As of July 2026, a total of 70 patients had been enrolled. Data collection is expected to be completed in 2027, after which the results will be analyzed and published.

Conclusions

The goal of our study is to determine whether renin 0-6 h kinetics (difference between renin levels before and 6 hours after starting an AT II infusion) are associated with clinical outcomes in patients who require AT II. Our study could contribute to the development of a more individualized approach to vasopressor therapy and avoidance of inappropriate use of AT II in patients who are not responders, allowing earlier discontinuation of AT II and consideration of alternative therapies.

title: Evaluation of a therapeutic education program for patients with coronary heart disease in a Tunisian university hospital: A quasi-experimental study.
authorString: Ghali H, Tlili MA, El Hraiech A, Sahli J, Bhiri S, Layouni S, Ben Souda H, Karray M, Pavy B, Ben Cheikh A, Zedini C.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a major public health concern globally, including Tunisia. Therapeutic Patient Education (TPE) plays a crucial role in managing CVD and improving patient outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of a TPE program on the occurrence of major cardiovascular events in patients with coronary heart disease (CHD) in a Tunisian university hospital.

Methods

A quasi-experimental study was conducted over one year, involving 129 patients with CHD. The intervention group (n = 38) received a four-stage TPE program, while the control group (n = 91) received standard care. The control group met the same inclusion and non-inclusion criteria as the intervention group. It was constituted based on a 3:1 ratio. Patients in the intervention and control groups were recruited from the same department and during the same period to ensure comparability. The primary outcome was the occurrence of major cardiovascular events within one year. Secondary outcomes included knowledge, lipid profile, glycated hemoglobin levels, and quality of life.

Results

The occurrence of major cardiovascular events was significantly lower in the intervention group compared to the control group (21.1% vs. 59.3%, p < 0.001). The TPE program was also associated with improvements in knowledge and biological parameters. Knowledge of cardiovascular risk factors increased from 71.1% at baseline to 78.9% immediately post-intervention (p = 0.039), with 60.5% retention at 3 months. The intervention group showed marked improvements in lipid profiles, with LDL cholesterol decreasing from 2.53 ± 1.45 to 1.88 ± 1.11 mmol/L (p < 0.001) and total cholesterol from 4.32 ± 1.47 to 3.75 ± 1.56 mmol/L (p = 0.002) at 3 months. In contrast, the control group demonstrated worsening lipid parameters (LDL: 2.50 ± 1.55 to 2.90 ± 1.60 mmol/L, p = 0.001).

Conclusions

The TPE program was associated with a lower occurrence of major cardiovascular events and improvements in patients' knowledge and lipid profiles. These findings suggest a potential beneficial effect of structured therapeutic education in patients with CHD.

Trial registration

The study was prospectively registered on the Pan African Clinical Trial Registry within the number PACTR202307694422939. The authors confirm that all ongoing and related trials for this intervention are registered.

title: Preclinical characterization of the potent and selective MALT1 inhibitor safimaltib in B-cell lymphoma models.
authorString: Philippar U, Fontan L, Xia M, Vloemans N, Bekkers M, Gaudiano M, Irrechukwu O, van den Biggelaar D, Perova T, Guimerans-Lorenzo I, Wnuk-Lipinska K, Cornelissen I, van Heerden M, van der Leede BJ, Amssoms K, Xu R, Grant J, Trella E, Abraham Y, Kimpe K, Medaer B, Greway A, Snoeys J, Jacobs F, D Cummings M, Sun W, Thuring JW, Wu T, Gaj S, Verbist B, Connolly PJ, Austin N, Balasubramanian S, Kinyamu-Akunda J, Packman K, Edwards JP, Elsayed Y, Fourneau N, Morschhauser F, Gerecitano JF, Bussolari J, Melnick AM, Attar RM.
abstractText: Constitutive activation of the B-cell receptor (BCR) pathway drives non-Hodgkin lymphomas. MALT1 is a key mediator of NF-κB signaling downstream of B- and T-cell receptors. Herein, we report development of safimaltib (JNJ-67856633), a selective, allosteric inhibitor of MALT1 protease. The crystal structure of safimaltib bound to MALT1 was determined, and enzyme kinetic studies were performed to characterize its inhibitory mechanism. Sub-micromolar doses of safimaltib inhibited growth of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) and mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) cell lines with activation of NF-κB signaling and models mimicking BTK inhibition resistance. Notably, activating mutations in BCR-pathway components were strongly associated with safimaltib response in vitro. Safimaltib demonstrated efficacy in DLBCL and MCL mouse models and synergy with a BTK inhibitor. Safimaltib was well tolerated in preclinical immunocompetent animal models with a safety profile supporting MALT1 targeting in humans. Overall, these results provide rationale for the first-in-human MALT1 inhibitor clinical trial.

title: Clinical presentation, management strategies, and mortality outcomes in idiopathic aortitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Hamdan O, Otoom S, Abdaljaleel N, Sandouka A, Alsakarneh H, Al-Ruwaidan N, Qreini S, El Hadid A, Rabi H, Arias F.

journal.title: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Introduction

Idiopathic Aortitis (IA) is defined as inflammation of the aortic wall, in the absence of a systemic disease or an infection. Most cases are found incidentally during repair of thoracic aortic aneurysms. Given the rarity of the disease, data on IA diagnosis and treatment are limited and derived mainly from small observational studies. This study aims to comprehensive and up-to-date synthesis of the available evidence on IA.

Methods

Literature search of the PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases was performed in late September 2025. Data regarding patients' medical history, presentations, complications, diagnostic investigations, management and outcomes were obtained.

Results

A total of 58 studies were included, comprising data from 79 patients with idiopathic aortitis. The mean age was 46 ± 20 years, with a slight male predominance of 53%. Weight loss was the most frequently reported symptom (58%). Regarding management, 44% underwent exclusive surgical treatment, 31% received mixed therapy, and 25% were managed medically. Corticosteroids were utilized in 51% of cases. The overall mortality rate was 20%. Significant predictors of mortality included a younger age at presentation (18 vs. 48 years, P < 0.001) and descending aorta involvement (P = 0.005). Conversely, corticosteroid administration (P = 0.002) and clinical surveillance (P < 0.001) were significantly associated with survival.

Conclusion

This meta-analysis highlights idiopathic aortitis as a severe condition with significant mortality whereas the administration of corticosteroids and clinical surveillance are strongly associated with survival, our findings emphasize the need for standardized, evidence-based management protocols and prospective multicenter studies to optimize patient outcomes.

title: Noninvasive assessments for identifying peripheral artery disease described within guidelines, consensus, and best practice statements: A rapid systematic review.
authorString: Weerasekara I, Askew C, Perrin B, Charles J, Cheong K, Golledge J, Lim P, Parmenter B, Tran M, Tehan P.
abstractText: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) affects approximately 4% of adults and is associated with lower-limb pain, reduced function, ulceration, amputation, and an increased likelihood of cardiovascular events. Noninvasive vascular testing methods are essential for accurate diagnosis to enable clinicians to deliver appropriate management. Clinical guidelines, consensus statements, and best practice documents are commonly used to guide practice. The quality of these documents, how well they specify the populations requiring screening, assessment, and the most appropriate noninvasive tests to use when diagnosing PAD is currently unclear.
