This rapid systematic review identified 37 national and international guidelines, consensus statements, or best practice documents that included information on noninvasive assessments for PAD diagnosis published up to 2025. The quality of these documents was assessed using the Appraisal of Guidelines for Research and Evaluation Instrument 2 or Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) appraisal checklist for textual evidence (policy/consensus guidelines), and scores varied substantially, with contemporary documents generally yielding higher scores. Common reasons for lower scores were a lack of systematic methods used to derive recommendations and inadequate engagement with key stakeholders, such as end-users. Within the documents, signs and symptoms of PAD consistently listed as indicators for further vascular assessment were intermittent claudication, rest pain, gangrene, and nonhealing wounds. Other prompts for vascular assessments were traditional cardiovascular risk factors, with some newer guidelines highlighting additional risk factors such as end-stage renal disease, First Nations ancestry, and lack of physical activity. There was varying guidance on the use and interpretation of the tests. Many documents did not consider the changes in diagnostic performance that occur in noninvasive tests in people with diabetes or renal disease. Some newer documents included clinical assessment pathways, which were considered beneficial in simplifying the assessment and interpretation process for clinicians. Although some high-quality documents with strong evidence-based recommendations were identified, there was a gap in comprehensive guidance that could be applied in a variety of settings and patient cohorts. Therefore, the development of an evidence-based, co-designed comprehensive guidance document for noninvasive vascular assessment is warranted.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Electrocardiography for the Detection of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy in Athletes: A Systematic Review of Diagnostic Accuracy and External Validity
authorString: De Medeiros Quirino L, Duarte K, Pereira S, Leff G, Rafael B, Pinto M, Lopes R, Simões C, Soares J, Kieling G.

title: Memory-guided mutual information optimization in retinal imaging for early stroke detection and subtyping.
authorString: Zhou S, Cao L, Mou L, Wang H, Hao J, Zhang X, Li H, Yuan L, Liao W, Julian TH, Wang M, Liu Y, Kwapong WR, Meng Y, Xie J, Zheng Y, Fu H, Liu J, Sheng B, Frangi AF, Wu B, Zhao Y.
abstractText: Effective stroke prevention relies on identifying at-risk individuals before neurological symptoms arise, yet this is severely limited by the absence of scalable screening tools. To address this, we developed RetCEVD, a diagnostic framework that uses rapid, non-invasive retinal Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography (OCTA) for auxiliary assessment of ICVD. At its core, RetCEVD introduces a memory-guided mutual information optimization strategy that maximizes shared disease-relevant information within the same diagnostic category while suppressing redundant or confounding dependencies across different categories. This dual information constraint encourages compact, discriminative representations of subtle retinal microvascular abnormalities. Trained and validated on a multi-center cohort of 24,438 retinal images, RetCEVD addresses three primary tasks: auxiliary detection of existing ICVD, etiological subtyping (large artery atherosclerosis vs. small vessel disease), and current symptomatic-status classification (asymptomatic vs. symptomatic LAA). The model achieved AUCs of 0.95 internal and 0.94 external for ICVD detection, 0.83 internal and 0.81 external for etiological subtyping, and 0.75 internal and 0.76 external for current symptomatic-status classification. The two-year ALAA follow-up provided supplementary longitudinal validation for subsequent stroke events (AUC, 0.71). By comprehensively evaluating the model's clinical interpretability, including its learned pathological features and alignment with established clinical patterns, we provide novel insights into retina-based stroke evaluation. Ultimately, RetCEVD may serve as an efficient, low-cost screening and triage tool to identify individuals who may benefit from confirmatory neurovascular imaging and specialist assessment.

title: Serum Very-Long-Chain Saturated Fatty Acids and the Mediating Role of Systemic Immune Inflammation in Cardiovascular Disease Risk.
authorString: Chen X, Zhou L, Cheng J.
abstractText: Very-long-chain saturated fatty acids (VLCSFAs) represent a distinct class of saturated fatty acids whose cardiovascular associations remain underexplored and controversial. This study investigated the associations of serum VLCSFAs-C20:0, C22:0, C23:0, and C24:0, and their sum (total VLCSFAs)-with myocardial infarction (MI), heart failure (HF), and stroke in 3456 NHANES 2011-2014 participants. Binary logistic and restricted cubic spline regression models were employed, with mediation analysis examining neutrophil-related inflammatory markers. With the middle tertile as the reference, participants in the lowest tertile had higher odds of MI for C20:0 (OR 2.11, 95% CI: 1.30-3.43, p = 0.003) and C23:0 (OR 2.55, 95% CI: 1.54-4.22, p < 0.001); higher odds of HF for C22:0 (OR 1.77, 95% CI: 1.08-2.90, p = 0.023), C24:0 (OR 2.14, 95% CI: 1.29-3.54, p = 0.003), and total VLCSFAs (OR 2.02, 95% CI: 1.22-3.33, p = 0.006); and higher odds of stroke for C24:0 (OR 1.77, 95% CI: 1.10-2.84, p = 0.019). Conversely, the highest tertile of C24:0 was associated with lower odds of MI (OR 0.49, 95% CI: 0.28-0.89, p = 0.018), whereas the highest tertiles of the remaining VLCSFAs showed no further risk reduction. SII, NER, NHR, and NLR partially mediated the associations of C23:0, C24:0, and total VLCSFAs with HF, and NER, NHR, and NLR partially mediated that of C22:0 with HF. These findings reveal novel associations of serum VLCSFAs with MI, HF, and stroke that were most evident in the lowest tertile of serum concentrations, suggesting that VLCSFA deficiency may contribute to cardiovascular risk, partly through neutrophil-related inflammatory pathways.

title: Clinical and Echocardiographic Predictors of Underutilization of Mitral Valve Intervention in Patients with Significant Mitral Regurgitation
authorString: Davarashvili I, Dvir D.
abstractText:
Background:

Mitral regurgitation (MR) is one of the most common valvular heart diseases and is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality if left untreated. Despite guideline recommendations, many patients with significant MR do not undergo surgical or transcatheter mitral valve intervention. We aimed to identify the clinical and echocardiographic characteristics associated with mitral valve intervention.

Methods:

We retrospectively analyzed 1,637 consecutive patients with moderate-to-severe or severe MR evaluated at Shaare Zedek Medical Center between December 2016 and December 2021. Patients were categorized into an intervention group (n = 191) and a conservatively managed group (n = 1,446). Clinical and echocardiographic characteristics were compared using univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses.

Results:

Among 1,637 patients, only 191 (11.7%) underwent mitral valve intervention. Patients receiving intervention were younger (72.8 ± 12.9 vs. 76.5 ± 14.2 years; p = 0.001), more frequently male (57.6% vs. 48.0%; p = 0.013), and more commonly of Arab ethnicity (22.5% vs. 13.1%; p < 0.001). Severe MR (68.6% vs. 40.1%; p = 0.0004) and prosthetic mitral valve (6.8% vs. 2.3%; p = 0.0004) were more common among treated patients, whereas hypertension, advanced chronic kidney disease, and previous myocardial infarction were less common. Independent predictors of intervention were younger age (OR 0.98, 95% CI 0.97–0.99; p = 0.035), Arab ethnicity (OR 2.02, 95% CI 1.24–3.29; p = 0.005), and severe MR (OR 2.87, 95% CI 1.88–4.35; p < 0.001).

Conclusions:

Only a small proportion of patients with significant MR underwent mitral valve intervention. Older patients and those with ischemic or renal comorbidities were more likely to be managed conservatively. Earlier referral to dedicated Heart Valve Teams may improve access to guideline-directed treatment.

title: Internal Mammary Artery Bypass Graft Dissection Mimicking Atherosclerotic Stenosis: Optical Coherence Tomography to Guide Stent Deferral.
authorString: Borovac JA, Matetic A.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText: Angiographic narrowing of a left internal mammary artery (LIMA) bypass graft does not always reflect atherosclerotic progression. Chronic or spontaneous LIMA graft dissection may be identified using optical coherence tomography (OCT). A patient with severe multivessel coronary disease and a history of coronary stenting and triple coronary artery bypass grafting presented with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction. Coronary angiography demonstrated critical left main-left circumflex disease, extensive left anterior descending artery in-stent restenosis, an occluded venous graft, and eccentric mid-LIMA narrowing. Urgent native-vessel revascularization restored Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) grade 3 flow and relieved the patient's symptoms. During staged LIMA assessment 6 days later, OCT was performed using a Dragonfly OpStar imaging catheter. OCT identified the entry of a longitudinal intimal flap separating the true and false lumens over a long segment, without significant atherosclerosis in the imaged segment. The operators interpreted this "double-barrel" configuration as a nonobstructive dissection of presumed chronicity. Preserved LIMA flow and clinical stability supported stent deferral; the patient remained asymptomatic and with preserved ejection fraction at the 2-month follow-up visit. This report offers important lessons for interventionalists: intravascular imaging can distinguish dissection from apparent atherosclerotic stenosis and significantly drive further management. Inadvertent false-lumen stenting could expand the false channel, compress the true lumen, and compromise graft perfusion. OCT clearly elucidated lesion morphology and supported clinical restraint; however, it did not independently establish dissection age or an exact mechanism of dissection.

title: Association of Adult and Pediatric Cardiac Surgery Volumes with Outcomes of the Ross Procedure in Adults.
authorString: Verma A, Balian J, Coaston T, Sakowitz S, Sanaiha Y, Si MS, Benharash P.
abstractText:
Background

There is growing interest in application of the Ross procedure for treatment of aortic valve disease; however, utilization is restricted to specialized centers. The present study evaluated the differential association of adult aortic valve surgery and pediatric cardiac surgery volumes on outcomes of adults undergoing the Ross operation.

Methods

The 2016-2022 Nationwide Readmissions Database was queried to identify all adults undergoing the Ross procedure. Hospitals were categorized as pediatric high-volume centers (pHVC, ≥75th percentile pediatric cardiac surgery volume), adult high-volume centers (aHVC, ≥75th percentile aortic valve replacement/repair volume among non-pHVC), and low-volume centers (LVC). Major adverse events (MAE) were defined as a composite of mortality, stroke, prolonged ventilation, acute renal failure, pulmonary embolism, cardiac arrest, and reoperation.

Results

Among 1,212 adults undergoing the Ross operation, 37.7% were treated at pHVC, 56.7% at aHVC, and 5.6% at LVC. National utilization increased from 63 cases in 2016 to 385 in 2022, with the number of performing centers rising from 14 to 37. Patients at LVC experienced the highest rates of MAE (42.1% vs aHVC 8.8% vs pHVC 3.8%, p<0.001). After risk adjustment, care at LVC was associated with a 7.7-fold increase in odds of MAE compared to pHVC (95% CI 3.0-19.7, p<0.001). Outcomes at aHVC and pHVC were comparable, although aHVC had higher rates of reoperation (4.5% vs 0.6%, p<0.001).

Conclusions

Adults undergoing the Ross operation at LVC face worse outcomes compared to aHVC and pHVC. These findings support selective referral strategies and regionalization of care.

title: Physical Performance After Acute Myocardial Infarction: Gait, Frailty, and Cardiovascular Prognosis.
authorString: da Luz Goulart C, Franzoni L, Correale L, Peyré-Tartaruga LA.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

Physical performance and frailty have emerged as potential markers of physiological reserve and cardiovascular vulnerability after acute myocardial infarction (AMI). This review examines the prognostic significance of gait speed, lower-extremity physical performance, frailty, and sarcopenia after AMI and acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and discusses their underlying pathophysiological mechanisms and clinical implications.

Recent findings

Slow gait speed, impaired Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) scores, and frailty are associated with mortality, rehospitalization, heart failure, and adverse cardiovascular events after AMI or ACS. Gait speed and SPPB may provide incremental prognostic information beyond conventional cardiovascular risk assessment and established risk scores. These associations may reflect an interconnected cardiac-vascular-muscle axis involving reduced cardiac reserve, vascular dysfunction, impaired skeletal muscle perfusion, sarcopenia, and physical deconditioning. Importantly, emerging evidence suggests that targeted cardiac rehabilitation may improve gait speed, muscle strength, and overall physical performance in vulnerable patients. Physical performance represents a clinically relevant and potentially modifiable dimension of post-AMI cardiovascular vulnerability. Incorporating gait speed, SPPB, and frailty assessment into conventional risk stratification may improve patient phenotyping and identify individuals requiring more intensive rehabilitation and follow-up. Further prospective studies are needed to standardize assessment strategies and determine whether improving physical performance translates into better cardiovascular outcomes.

title: Development and validation of a long-term prognostic prediction nomogram for ICM on the basis of polymorphism and plasma level of Mfn2
authorString: Naman T, Mahemuti A, Aini R, Maihemuti A, Yu D, Guo Zt.
abstractText: Objective To investigate the association between Mitofusin2 (Mfn2) genotype and its plasma levels with long-term prognosis of ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM), and to establish and validate a predictive nomogram for long-term prognosis of ICM, thereby providing a theoretical basis for risk assessment of ICM. Methods This study included 1092 ICM patients who underwent follow-up at 3, 6, 12, 24, 36, 48, and 60 months after first diagnosed with ICM. Based on follow-up outcomes, patients were categorized into survival and death groups. All patients were randomly divided into a training set (n = 764) and a validation set (n = 328). Univariate Cox regression analysis was performed on the training set. Variables with P  < 0.1 in univariate analysis underwent Lasso regression analysis. Multivariate Cox regression models were constructed using selected variables by lasso regression analysis.followed performed model validation. Performance was evaluated using ROC curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results Multivariate Cox regression analysis revealed that plasma Mfn2 levels, heart rate, serum sodium, treatment with PCI or CABG, beta-blocker use, LVDD, and mutations at SNP loci rs1042842, rs2295281, and rs2236054 were independent predictors of long-term ICM prognosis ( P  < 0.05). The nomogram constructed based on these findings demonstrated excellent discriminatory ability in both the training and validation cohorts (AUCs: 0.824 [1 year], 0.809 [3 years], and 0.877 [5 years] in the training set; and 0.808 (1 year), 0.767 (3 years), and 0.790 (5 years) in the validation set). The model demonstrated good consistency between observed and predicted values, indicating strong clinical usefulness. Conclusion Elevated plasma Mfn2 levels and genetic mutations at rs223605 may represent protective factors influencing long-term prognosis in ICM, whereas mutations at rs1042842 and rs2295281 may constitute risk factors for poor long-term outcomes in ICM.

title: Revisiting Mcconnell's Sign: Right Ventricular Infarction in the Absence of Pulmonary Embolism.
authorString: Munekata Y, Saito T, Ishizaka S, Tsuchida T, Takauji S, Shimono Y, Konishi T, Nagai T, Anzai T, Wada T.
abstractText: McConnell's sign, defined as hypokinesis of the right ventricular (RV) midfree wall with preserved apical contractions, was initially considered to be highly specific for acute pulmonary embolism. However, evidence indicates that it may also appear in other conditions involving RV dysfunction. Here, we report a case of McConnell's sign associated with RV myocardial infarction in the absence of pulmonary embolism. A 74-year-old female was successfully resuscitated following cardiac arrest. Echocardiography revealed a dilated RV with moderate tricuspid regurgitation and a regional wall motion pattern characteristic of McConnell's sign. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography excluded a pulmonary embolism. Coronary angiography revealed an occluded right coronary artery, which was identified as the culprit lesion, and a chronically occluded left anterior descending artery with collateral flow. Conservative management led to gradual clinical and echocardiographic improvement. This case underscores that McConnell's sign is not pathognomonic for pulmonary embolism and should be interpreted cautiously.

title: From Catheters to Wearables: Advanced Hemodynamic Monitoring and the Emerging Role of PPG-Based Devices.
authorString: Aliev E, Eisenkraft A, Nachman D.
abstractText: Advanced hemodynamic monitoring, including cardiac output (CO), stroke volume (SV), and systemic vascular resistance (SVR), is important for the management of cardiogenic shock, postoperative patients, and heart failure. Traditional approaches such as pulmonary artery catheterization (PAC) provide comprehensive hemodynamic assessment but are invasive, costly, and associated with procedure-related risks. This review summarizes established invasive and minimally invasive techniques alongside emerging noninvasive approaches, including pulse contour analysis, bioimpedance, pulse wave transit time, and photoplethysmography (PPG)-based systems. Particular emphasis is placed on PPG-based technologies, which combine pulse wave analysis, pulse wave transit time, and advanced signal processing to estimate blood pressure and flow-related parameters. As a representative case study, the clinical development and evaluation of the Biobeat BB-613WP wearable are described, including preclinical swine hemorrhagic shock models, intensive care and perioperative validation against invasive reference methods, and ambulatory blood pressure monitoring studies. Available evidence suggests that PPG-based wearables can achieve clinically acceptable agreement with invasive reference methods in selected populations while offering the potential for continuous, noninvasive, and ambulatory monitoring. However, the available evidence is limited by small sample sizes, single-center studies, controlled conditions, and limited independent validation. Further multicenter, outcome-oriented studies are required to establish the clinical role of PPG-based devices across diverse patient populations and stages of care.

title: Cardiac Endothelial Enhancer RNA Tek-e1 Restores Microvascular Homeostasis After Myocardial Infarction.
authorString: Lyu Y, Yang K, Ling Y, Cheng J, Shi J, Hu S, Zhou C, Wei W, Chen H, Wei X, Wang Z, Xiong Z, Yang C, Zou S, Shen R, Song Y, Zhang G, Gao R, Lin K, Xu Y.
abstractText: Microvascular repair after myocardial infarction involves both angiogenesis and re-establishment of vascular homeostasis. Here, we identify a distinct transcriptionally active state in hypoxic border-zone endothelial cells driven by KDM5A downregulation and biased towards endothelial stabilization and microvascular homeostatic repair. KDM5A loss increases H3K4me3 enrichment at the Tek promoter and an intronic enhancer, enabling ISL1 to coordinately activate transcription of Tek and the enhancer RNA Tek-e1. Tek-e1 acts as an essential cis-regulatory RNA that further amplifies Tek/TIE2 expression through R-loop formation and reinforced enhancer-promoter communication, thereby converting Kdm5a-loss-induced epigenetic activation into persistent transcriptional reinforcement. In mice with endothelial-specific deletion of Kdm5a, this mechanism promotes the maturation and stabilization of nascent-microvascular networks after myocardial infarction. In a clinical cohort, serum soluble TIE2 independently stratified collateral status in 402 patients with chronic total occlusion. To further enable translation, we developed LNP@Tek-e1 modified with a VCAM-1-targeting peptide, combining VCAM-1-directed endothelial enrichment with enhancer-dependent Tek-e1 activity to selectively enhance Tek/TIE2 expression in border-zone endothelium, improving microvascular function and limiting adverse left ventricular remodelling. Together, these findings define KDM5A downregulation as a hypoxia-triggered endothelial repair programme and establish Tek-e1 as an essential cis-regulatory amplifier that can be delivered in vivo to restore post-infarction microvascular homeostasis.

title: Prognosis of Patients with Delayed Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Rupture after Endovascular Aortic Repair: A Multicentre Retrospective Study in France.
authorString: Bartlomiejczyk S, Salomon C, Morin L, Bamdé CC, Steinmetz E, Settembre N, Malikov S.

journal.title: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery

abstractText:
Objective

The majority of patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) undergo endovascular aortic repair (EVAR). Despite its high overall success rate, EVAR does not eliminate the risk of aneurysm rupture. This study aimed to evaluate the prognosis of patients undergoing surgical management for post-EVAR rupture.

Methods

A multicentre retrospective study of patients who presented with ruptured AAA after successful EVAR between 2007 and 2022 at 22 academic hospitals was conducted. The index EVAR procedures were performed between 2002 and 2020. Data were extracted from electronic hospital records and computed tomography scans. Death during follow up was ascertained using the French register of deceased persons. Survival probabilities at 30, 90, and 365 days were estimated with Kaplan-Meier estimators. Cox proportional hazards survival regression was used to identify determinants associated with increased risk of death.

Results

One hundred and nine patients (96 men) were included, with a mean age of 79.1 ± 9 years at the time of rupture. The median time from index EVAR to rupture was 50 months (range 0 - 179 months). Sixty-seven patients had open surgery (of which 37% underwent suprarenal cross clamping), 39 received endovascular treatment, and three underwent hybrid repair. Overall mortality was 26.6% at thirty days, increasing to 33.9% at ninety days, and 41.3% at 1 year. Neither the type of endoleak nor the type of repair was significantly associated with risk of death during follow up. Post-operative complications were frequent, including renal complications (44.0%), major haemorrhage (22.9%), respiratory distress (19.3%), and mesenteric ischaemia (6%).

Conclusion

This study presented a large multicentre series of patients treated for ruptured AAA after EVAR. Despite considerable progress in stent graft technology, EVAR offers little protection in the event of late rupture, even among patients with type II endoleak only. The mortality rate in this study is within the range of those published based on de novo AAA rupture.

title: Revascularization Outcomes in Patients with Femoropopliteal Peripheral Artery Disease Presenting with Claudication.
authorString: Rahgozar S, Zarrintan S, Aarabi S, Menard MT, Farber A, Malas MB.
abstractText:
Objective

Supervised exercise therapy (SET) and optimal medical therapy (OMT), including smoking cessation, are first-line treatments for claudication. Revascularization is reserved for quality-of-life-limiting symptoms refractory to conservative management; however, the optimal revascularization strategy for femoropopliteal disease remains uncertain. We compared outcomes of endovascular therapy (ET) and bypass strategies in patients undergoing revascularization for claudication.

Methods

We analyzed Vascular Quality Initiative data (2016-2024) for patients undergoing first-time elective revascularization for femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease (PAD) presenting with claudication. Three 1:1 propensity score-matched cohorts were constructed: ET vs single-segment great saphenous vein (SSGSV) bypass, ET vs prosthetic graft (PG) bypass, and PG vs SSGSV bypass. The primary outcome was one-year freedom from persistent claudication. Secondary outcomes included one-year loss of patency, reintervention, and all-cause mortality. Outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression.

Results

We identified 27,335 patients (30,483 limbs): ET 27,111 (88.9%), SSGSV 1,399 (4.6%), and PG 1,973 (6.5%). Matching yielded 1,294 ET-SSGSV pairs, 1,801 ET-PG pairs, and 1,242 PG-SSGSV pairs with well-balanced baseline characteristics. At one year, symptom-free rates were 92.0% for SSGSV, 90.0% for PG, and 89.6% for ET. Compared with SSGSV, ET was associated with a higher risk of persistent claudication at one-year (HR 1.48; 95% CI 1.10-2.00; P=0.010). No significant differences in one-year symptom relief were observed between ET and PG or between PG and SSGSV. Across all matched comparisons, loss of patency, reintervention, and mortality did not differ significantly.

Conclusions

SET and OMT should remain first-line therapy for claudication. Among patients proceeding to revascularization after unsuccessful conservative care, SSGSV bypass was associated with greater symptom relief than ET at one year, while all strategies achieved high symptom-free rates (≥89%). ET and PG demonstrated comparable outcomes across symptom relief, patency, reintervention, and survival. There were no significant differences between PG and SSGSV. Given vein-preservation considerations and procedural invasiveness in claudication, strategy selection should be individualized to anatomy, comorbidities and patient goals. Prospective studies are needed to clarify long-term durability, and quality-of-life effects.

title: Echocardiography-led multimodal assessment for pulmonary hypertension in a right heart catheterization-referred cohort: incremental value of ECG and natriuretic peptides.
authorString: Gao Y, Chen W, Ou J, Tao Q, Zhuang W.
abstractText:
Background

Right heart catheterization (RHC) is the reference standard for diagnosing pulmonary hypertension (PH), whereas echocardiography is the primary noninvasive tool for identifying patients who require further evaluation. Whether electrocardiography (ECG) and natriuretic peptides provide incremental diagnostic information beyond echocardiographic assessment in patients referred for RHC remains uncertain.

Methods

This single-center retrospective study included 130 hospitalized patients with suspected PH who underwent echocardiography, 12-lead ECG, B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) or N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) testing, and RHC during the same admission. PH was defined as mean pulmonary arterial pressure > 20 mmHg on RHC. A temporal validation cohort of 42 consecutive eligible patients was used to evaluate the final model without refitting. To reduce collinearity, the final multimodal model included pulmonary artery systolic pressure estimated by echocardiography (PASP ECHO), ECG positivity, and BNP/NT-proBNP positivity. Model discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, areas under the curve (AUCs) were compared using DeLong's test, calibration was assessed using calibration plots and calibration metrics, and internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling.

Results

Among 130 patients in the derivation cohort, 111 had PH and 19 did not. The final multimodal model showed higher discrimination than PASP ECHO alone in the derivation cohort (AUC 0.825, 95% CI 0.722-0.928 vs. 0.730, 95% CI 0.620-0.841; DeLong P = 0.008). At the Youden threshold, the final model showed high specificity but limited sensitivity, whereas a sensitivity-oriented threshold increased sensitivity at the expense of specificity. Bootstrap internal validation yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.811. In the temporal validation cohort, the final model showed an AUC of 0.792, compared with 0.749 for PASP ECHO alone; this difference was not statistically significant. Bland-Altman analysis showed wide limits of agreement between PASP ECHO and invasive systolic pressure estimates, indicating that echocardiographic and invasive pressure estimates are associated but not interchangeable.

Conclusions

In this RHC-referred suspected PH cohort, ECG and natriuretic peptide positivity provided complementary information beyond PASP ECHO. However, because of the small sample size, marked class imbalance, and limited subtype characterization, the proposed multimodal approach should be considered exploratory. Larger prospective studies with subtype stratification and external validation are required before clinical implementation.

title: Prevalence, Clinical Characteristics, and Hemodynamic Impact of Coronary Artery–Ventricular Microfistulas in Patients with Fontan Circulation
authorString: Higashi K, Nakajima H, Aotsuka H.
abstractText: Background: Coronary artery–ventricular microfistulas (CAMFs), which are defined as diffuse communications between dilated coronary arteries and the main ventricle, are poorly understood in Fontan circulation. We evaluated their prevalence, clinical features, and longitudinal hemodynamics. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 167 Fontan patients undergoing cardiac catheterization between 2005 and 2025. Excluded were sinusoidal communications in PA/IVS, LV fistulas in HLHS, or solitary focal fistulas. Clinical, surgical, and serial hemodynamic parameters, such as the subendocardial viability ratio (SEVR) and aortic regurgitation (AR) index, were assessed. Results: CAMFs were identified in 6 of the 153 eligible Fontan patients (prevalence: 3.9%). Polysplenia was more frequent in the CAMFs group (33% vs. 5%, p = 0.03). At initial diagnosis, systemic cardiac index (median 3.3 L/min/m² [range, 2.2–3.9 L/min/m²]) and ejection fraction (median 52% [range, 44%–65%]) were preserved. Notably, resting SEVR (median 91% [range, 85%–156%]) and AR index (median 54% [range, 44%–59%]) remained stable and well-compensated over a decade of follow-up. Late morbidities included protein-losing enteropathy (17%), pulmonary arteriovenous fistulas (17%), esophageal varices (17%), and death (17%). Conclusions: CAMFs occur in 3.9% of Fontan patients and correlate with polysplenia. Although resting SEVR and AR index remain well-compensated over mid-term follow-up, their impact on long-term outcomes beyond two decades post-Fontan remains uncertain. Careful long-term monitoring is necessary for late extra-cardiac complications and hemodynamic changes.

title: Pulmonary arterial hypertension in adult congenital heart disease: prevalence, outcomes and treatment patterns.
authorString: Lloyd LK, Nicholson CA, Strange GA, Celermajer DS.
abstractText:
Background

Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive, life-threatening complication of congenital heart disease (CHD). We aimed to determine the burden of clinically relevant PAH in a well-characterised adult CHD population.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study included 35 235 adult CHD patients from the Australian National CHD Registry, of whom 392 had clinically significant PAH (mean±sd age 43.4±13.9) (prevalence 1.11%). We prospectively defined clinically significant PAH as 1) prescription of PAH-specific therapy and/or 2) known Eisenmenger syndrome. 330 patients (84.2%) received PAH pharmacotherapy during the study period and 193 patients (49.2%) had Eisenmenger syndrome, 62 (32.1%) of whom were untreated.

Results

During the study period, 141 (36.0%) patients died, PAH treatment was associated with a numerically lower risk of mortality (hazard ratio (HR) 0.74, 95% CI 0.49-1.11; p=0.22). Patients with moderate complexity CHD had a significantly higher risk of death than the mild group (HR 1.78, 95% CI 1.08-2.92; p=0.023), whilst severe complexity patients had >2.5 times the risk of death (p<0.001). At last follow-up, 211 (63.9%) of treated patients were prescribed monotherapy, 90 (27.3%) dual and 29 (8.8%) triple therapy. From initial treatment to last follow-up, 123 (37.3%) of the treated group had switched therapy, 100 (30.3%) died, 75 (22.7%) continued their initial pharmacotherapy, 25 (7.6%) added additional drugs and seven (2.1%) underwent transplantation.

Conclusions

Approximately 1.11% of a large adult CHD population had clinically significant PAH. Mortality is high (6.9% at age 30 years, 35.7% at age 50 years) and treatment has shifted towards increased utilisation of combination therapy.

title: Surgical Timing and Physiology-Specific Outcomes in Congenital Heart Disease.
authorString: Joshi SS, Shetty R, Murthy KS, Prabhu S, V SP, Nair H, Sambandamoorthy G, Ramachandra P, Prabhu AS, Maiyya S, Sahu DP, Charles A, Suresha SN, Tambrallimath PR, Hegde R, Mohanty S, Rao S, Shetty D.
abstractText:
Background

In low- and middle-income countries, most children with congenital heart disease reach the operating room after the guideline-recommended window has closed. Existing analyses grade delay by chronological age or a binary early/late split and report outcomes in aggregate, not by physiology.

Methods

All 12,190 consecutive pediatric congenital heart operations at a single Indian tertiary center (2020-2025) were graded against national guidelines using a lesion-normalized Guideline Deviation Score, from G0 (timely) to G4 (critically delayed). Logistic regression and restricted cubic splines assessed operative mortality, morbidity, and resource utilization overall and within seven pre-specified physiological subgroups.

Results

Of 10,187 gradable operations, 73.7% were delayed and 34.8% critically delayed. Operative mortality was 2.1% (adjusted OR per grade, 0.88 [95% CI, 0.81-0.96]; P = .004). Fontan-stage palliation was the only subgroup with progressive morbidity increase (64% at guideline age, 85% at grade 3; P = .002), inflecting near age 12 years. Left-to-right shunt lesions showed forward morbidity accumulation (adjusted OR, 1.05 [1.01-1.09]; P = .03). Resource utilization rose with delay overall (adjusted OR, 1.04 [1.01-1.07]; P = .01) and in left-to-right shunt and transposition physiology, but fell in cyanotic and Fontan-stage groups.

Conclusions

Three in four children missed their guideline window. Operative mortality did not rise with delay, which reflects case-mix confounding rather than evidence that delay is safe, since the youngest and sickest children are operated first. Morbidity rose with delay in Fontan-stage and left-to-right shunt physiology. Physiology-specific grading supports surgical decision-making when a child presents late.

title: A Selenium-Enriched Composite From Edible Mushrooms and Medicinal Plants Ameliorates Metabolic Disorders via Multi-Target Network Modulation.
authorString: Zhou W, Wang F, Duan Y, Jiang X, Xiao H, Yu A, Kuang H, Zhu B, Wang Q, You J.
abstractText: Inspired by the dietary habits of centenarians in Enshi, China, this study developed two selenium-enriched water-soluble powder formulations (OFXBJC and NFXBJC) from edible mushrooms and medicinal plants. Comparison of their active components and metabolomic profiles showed that NFXBJC contained 39.0% higher total flavonoids, 33.4% higher total saponins, and 38.6% higher soluble protein, along with upregulated hypoglycemic metabolites. NFXBJC was therefore selected for subsequent evaluation of its effects on glucolipid disorders, renal injury, and hyperuricemia. In a Type 2 diabetic mouse model, low-dose NFXBJC (80 mg/kg/day) dose-dependently increased serum selenium levels, reduced fasting and postprandial blood glucose by 36.2% and 38.9%, respectively, lowered total cholesterol and triglycerides by 14.8% and 35.6%, respectively, and restored renal function without obvious organ toxicity. Correlation analysis revealed a strong negative association between blood glucose and serum selenium (R 2 = 0.964). Network pharmacology identified 48 candidate compounds and 552 putative targets, with the top 10 hub targets (STAT3, IL6, AKT1, CTNNB1, TNF, EGFR, HIF1A, IL1B, SRC, and BCL2) fully conserved across diabetes, hyperlipidemia, and hyperuricemia, suggesting multi-target modulation of a shared inflammation-metabolism network across these three conditions. Molecular docking further predicted stable binding of core active ingredients (e.g., cryptotanshinone, isorhamnetin, kaempferol) to these hub targets, with binding energies below -5.0 kcal/mol. An exploratory small-scale human observational study suggested that NFXBJC may progressively reduce uric acid (32.2%-39.8%), blood glucose, and total cholesterol. Collectively, NFXBJC exerts beneficial effects on glucolipid metabolism, renal function, selenium status, and uric acid levels via multi-target mechanisms, supporting its potential as a functional food for metabolic health.

title: Andrographolide, A Plant-Based Dietary Bioactive Nutritional Health Compound, Attenuates Hyperoxia-Induced Acute Lung Injury by Inhibiting Ferroptosis Through the STAT3/P53 Signaling Pathway.
authorString: Xia Q, Liu X, Qin S, Feng B, Yu K, Ren Y.
abstractText: Andrographolide (AG) is a plant-derived bioactive diterpenoid compound with potential applications in nutritional science and clinical nutrition. This study investigated whether AG attenuates hyperoxia-induced acute lung injury (HALI) by inhibiting ferroptosis via the signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3)/tumor protein P53 (P53) signaling pathway. Male C57BL/6 mice were used to establish a hyperoxia-induced lung injury model, and the protective effects of AG were compared with those of the ferroptosis inhibitor ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1). Lung histopathological changes, the lung wet-to-dry (W/D) weight ratio, reactive oxygen species (ROS), ferrous iron (Fe<sup>2+</sup>), glutathione (GSH), inflammatory cytokines, and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) expression were assessed. Network pharmacology and functional enrichment analyses were performed to identify potential targets of AG, followed by validation in MLE-12 lung epithelial cells and mouse models. Cell viability was assessed using the CCK-8 assay, and the expression of phosphorylated STAT3 (P-STAT3), total STAT3, P53, and GPX4 was examined by western blotting. Co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) was used to investigate the interaction between STAT3 and P53. Hyperoxia induced marked lung injury, inflammatory cell infiltration, increased pulmonary edema, and alterations in ferroptosis-related indicators. Both AG and Fer-1 attenuated lung injury and reduced ferroptosis-associated changes. Network pharmacology analysis identified 79 potential targets associated with HALI, with STAT3 emerging as a core candidate target. In MLE-12 cells, AG attenuated ferroptosis-associated changes, whereas the STAT3 phosphorylation activator Colivelin TFA attenuated these protective effects. Co-IP confirmed an interaction between STAT3 and P53, and Colivelin TFA also weakened the protective effects of AG in the mouse model. These findings suggest that AG may alleviate HALI by inhibiting ferroptosis through modulation of the STAT3/P53 signaling pathway, providing experimental evidence for its potential as a plant-derived bioactive compound for further investigation in hyperoxia-induced lung injury.

title: Beyond the Infection: The Immunopathological Cascade and Novel Therapeutic Avenues in Viral Myocarditis.
authorString: Chen Y, Liu M, Wu J, Li Y, Wan Z, Cheng S, Chen M, Luo G, Chen H.
abstractText: Viral myocarditis (VMC) is an inflammatory disease of the myocardium induced by infection with cardiotropic viruses. Its pathogenesis encompasses direct virus-induced myocardial injury and excessive host immune-mediated pathological responses. This review systematically delineates the dynamic progression of VMC, from viral invasion and immune activation to chronic myocardial remodeling. Special emphasis is placed on pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) in sensing viral components, and how mechanisms like cytokine storms, autoimmunity, and macrophage polarization imbalances drive myocardial injury and fibrosis. Furthermore, we summarize current and emerging therapeutic strategies-highlighting etiology-guided stratification based on myocardial viral genome status. For virus-positive cases, direct pathogen-targeted antivirals (e.g., interferon-beta [IFN-β], telbivudine), viral entry decoys, mitochondrial protectants, novel antiheart failure agents (SGLT2 inhibitors, ARNI), and blood component apheresis (TPE/IA) offer promising avenues. Conversely, immunosuppressive regimens, CAR-Treg therapies, and cytokine antagonists (e.g., IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-17) are strictly indicated for virus-negative inflammatory cardiomyopathy. The clinical translation potential and challenges in these multitarget interventions are discussed in detail. Despite advances in elucidating VMC immunopathology, precise management remains ch.allenging due to difficulties in balancing antiviral defense and inflammatory injury. Future research should leverage multiomics technologies and personalized multitarget approaches to improve clinical outcomes.

title: Regulatory T Cells in Health and Disease.
authorString: Li M, Zhang S, Wu T, Tang T, Cheng X.
abstractText: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) are central guardians of immune tolerance and tissue homeostasis. Initially defined as suppressors of excessive immune responses, Tregs are now recognized as adaptable cells that integrate antigenic, cytokine, metabolic, and tissue-derived signals to coordinate immune regulation, inflammation resolution, and tissue repair. However, these dimensions are often considered separately, and their interrelationships across physiological and pathological contexts remain insufficiently integrated. Here, we summarize the developmental origin, lineage stability, plasticity, and tissue adaptation of Tregs, and examine how these features shape their context-dependent functions. In lymphoid organs, Tregs maintain systemic tolerance by limiting antigen-presenting cell activation, restraining IL-2 availability, and setting the threshold for T- and B-cell responses, whereas in non-lymphoid tissues, they acquire organ-specific transcriptional, metabolic, and migratory programs that support barrier integrity, metabolic fitness, and regenerative repair. Chronic inflammation, persistent antigenic stimulation, oxidative stress, and metabolic disturbance can in turn disrupt these programs, promoting functional reprogramming or lineage instability, while excessive Treg-mediated suppression may favor pathogen persistence and tumor immune escape. We further discuss Treg alterations across major disease settings and emerging Treg-targeted therapies, providing an integrated framework that links developmental origin, tissue context, and functional state to more precise therapeutic strategies.

title: Clinical and neurohormonal correlates of plasma TNF-α in a Zambian outpatient cohort.
authorString: Kaango A, Chisompola D, Chakulya M, Luwaya E, Sidambi D, Mulamfu S, Hamooya BM, Povia JP, Masenga SK.
abstractText:
Background

Chronic inflammation persists in populations with high HIV and tuberculosis (TB) burden, even during suppressive therapy. Tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) is a key mediator, but its correlates beyond infectious status remain unclear in people living with HIV on stable antiretroviral therapy and who are virologically suppressed. We investigated clinical, metabolic, and neurohormonal correlates of TNF-α in a Zambian cohort.

Methods

This was a cross-sectional study, which included 227 adults recruited from the outpatient medical clinic at Livingstone University Teaching Hospital in the Southern Province of Zambia. Simple and multivariable linear regression analyses were performed to determine independent associations with plasma TNF-α levels. Models were adjusted for HIV serostatus and history of TB. Standardized beta coefficients (β_std) were computed to compare the relative magnitude of associations across predictors measured on different scales.

Results

Among 227 participants, 64.8% were living with HIV (95.3% on integrase strand transfer inhibitor-based ART) and 14.0% had a history of tuberculosis. In multivariable analysis, the strongest independent associations with TNF-α were observed within the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS): angiotensin II (β = 1.18 per pg/mL, p < 0.001; β_std = 0.51) and aldosterone (β = 0.884 per pg/mL, p < 0.001; β_std = 0.47). Living with HIV serostatus was also independently associated with higher TNF-α (β = 2581.1 pg/mL, p = 0.018; β_std = 0.19), while the history of TB was not. Significant metabolic factors associated with TNF-α levels included VLDL (β = 4397.4 per mmol/L, p = 0.038; β_std = 0.16) and triglycerides (β = 1971.6 per mmol/L, p = 0.034; β_std = 0.17). Inflammatory markers sST2 (β = 104.4 per ng/mL, p < 0.001; β_std = 0.31), IL-17 A (β = 1.137 per pg/mL, p = 0.003; β_std = 0.21), and D-dimer (β = 0.037 per pg/mL, p = 0.001; β_std = 0.22) were independently associated, as was plasma potassium (β = 107.3 per mmol/L, p < 0.001; β_std = 0.46). Renin, IL-6, IL-5, hs-CRP, and left ventricular mass were not associated with TNF-α.

Conclusion

In this high-burden population, RAAS activation was an independent correlate of TNF-α, exceeding the effect of HIV serostatus. These findings support the hypothesis that RAAS inhibition may have anti-inflammatory effects; however, this remains to be tested in prospective and interventional studies.

Supplementary information

The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s44337-026-00738-x.

title: Leadless Pacemaker Implantation in Fabry Disease With Permanent Atrial Fibrillation and Bradycardia: Diagnostic and Implantation Guidance by Preprocedural Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
authorString: Saito H, Suzuki Y, Yamada S, Fujii H, Takami K, Takahashi Y, Nishijyo K, Yoshida A.
abstractText: In advanced Fabry cardiomyopathy, preprocedural cardiac magnetic resonance imaging may reveal a lower septal region spared from otherwise extensive septal late gadolinium enhancement. This information, combined with pre-fixation electrical mapping, may help identify an optimal site for leadless pacemaker implantation and minimize repeated fixation attempts.

title: Calpain-1 Deficiency Attenuates Atherosclerosis and Improves Cardiac Function Through Vascular-Cardiac Coupling Mechanisms in ApoE-Deficient Mice.
authorString: Shi Y, Juvenal H, Pan Y, Li S, Gu W, Wei Y, Jiang Y, Shao J, Chen S, Zhao Y, Liu T, Shuai L, Zhang S, Liu J, Zhou X, Tang F.
abstractText: Calpain-1 has emerged as an important regulator of vascular remodeling and inflammation; however, its systemic role in atherosclerosis and cardiac dysfunction remains incompletely understood. This study investigated whether genetic deletion of calpain-1 attenuates atherosclerosis and improves cardiac function in apolipoprotein E-deficient (ApoE KO) mice. ApoE KO mice and ApoE/calpain-1 double knockout (A × C DKO) mice were fed a high-fat diet for 8 weeks, while C57BL/6 mice served as controls. Atherosclerotic lesions, serum lipid profiles, endothelial function, cardiac structure and function, and global proteomic changes were evaluated. A × C DKO mice exhibited significantly reduced atherosclerotic plaque burden and decreased CD68-positive macrophage infiltration compared with ApoE KO mice. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging revealed that ApoE KO mice developed ventricular dilation and systolic dysfunction characterized by increased LVESV and LVEDV and reduced LVEF. Calpain-1 deficiency partially normalized ventricular volumes and significantly improved LVEF, LVSV, and cardiac output. Notably, serum total cholesterol, triglycerides, LDL-cholesterol, HDL-cholesterol, and glucose levels were not significantly altered by calpain-1 deletion, indicating that the protective effects occurred independently of systemic lipid metabolism. Mechanistically, calpain-1 deficiency suppressed foam-cell related pathways by downregulating SR-A and CD36 while restoring cholesterol efflux regulators PPAR-γ and LXR-α. Endothelial function was improved as evidenced by increased eNOS activity and NO bioavailability. Aortic DIA proteomic analysis further revealed that calpain-1 ablation reversed multiple pathogenic pathways including cytoskeletal remodeling, extracellular matrix destabilization, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and endothelial barrier impairment. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that calpain-1 deficiency attenuates atherosclerotic plaque development and improves cardiac function in ApoE-deficient mice through lipid-independent mechanisms involving endothelial protection, reduced foam cell formation, and restoration of vascular homeostasis. Calpain-1 therefore represents a promising therapeutic target linking vascular pathology with cardiac dysfunction in atherosclerosis.

title: Preventive Linear Ablation Strategy for Intra-Atrial Reentrant Tachycardia Following Cardiac Surgery.
authorString: Chen J, Pan T, Liu Y, Chen Z, Zhao Y, Bai J, Shen W, Xu W.
abstractText:
Aims

Intra-atrial reentrant tachycardia (IART) frequently occurs following cardiac surgery due to scar-related conduction abnormalities. While advances in mapping technologies have improved the acute success rate of catheter ablation, arrhythmia recurrence remains a significant clinical concern. This study aimed to evaluate whether a preventive linear ablation strategy guided by voltage mapping improves the long-term success rate of catheter ablation in patients with IART post-cardiac surgery.

Methods and results

A total of 46 consecutive patients following cardiac surgery who underwent atrial tachycardia ablation between 2022 and 2024 were enrolled in the study group. After activation mapping-guided ablation for ongoing IART, preventive linear ablation was performed based on voltage mapping. Fifty consecutive sex- and age-matched patients with cardiac surgery undergoing activation mapping-guided ablation alone served as the historical control group between 2018 and 2021. At a mean follow-up of 21 ± 4.9 months, the rate of freedom from atrial arrhythmias was significantly higher in the study group compared to the control group (82.6% vs. 64.0%; p = 0.019). Despite the improved outcomes, the study group had significantly longer total procedure times (192 ± 37 vs. 126 ± 25 min; p < 0.001) and radiofrequency ablation durations (29 ± 5 vs. 20 ± 6 min; p < 0.001). However, there were no significant differences in complication rates between the two groups.

Conclusions

Preventive linear ablation strategy was associated with improved arrhythmia-free survival in patients with IART post cardiac surgery, but these exploratory findings require confirmation in future prospective studies.

title: Raised Amylase as a Potential Marker of Vascular Dysfunction and Inflammation in Fabry Disease.
authorString: D'Amore S, Cabides M, Ramaswami U.
abstractText: Fabry disease (FD) is a X-linked disorder caused by deficiency of alpha-galactosidase A (AGAL), leading to progressive accumulation of globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) and globotriaosylsphingosine (lyso-Gb3). While renal, cardiac and cerebrovascular complications are well described, pancreatic involvement remains poorly characterised. We retrospectively evaluated the clinical and biochemical features of FD patients with elevated serum amylase levels and explored associations with disease severity, treatment status, inflammation and vascular dysfunction. Sixty-two patients (35 males, 27 females; median age 53.9 years [IQR 42.1-64.5]) showed hyperamylasaemia (> 100 U/L). None had known pancreatic disease or significant alcohol intake. Median amylase levels were 114.5 U/L (IQR 104-137). Seven patients were obese (body mass index ≥ 30 kg/m2). No significant differences in amylase levels were observed according to sex, genotype, treatment status or renal/cerebrovascular involvement. However, patients with cardiac involvement had higher amylase levels than those without cardiac manifestations (median 128 [IQR 104-149] vs. 113 U/L [IQR 104.3-125]; p = 0.039). Amylase levels were not associated with AGAL activity, lyso-Gb3 concentrations, renal function, liver function, d-dimer, lactate dehydrogenase or lipid profile. Significant correlations were observed with age (r = 0.292; p = 0.021), body mass index (r = -0.382; p = 0.003) and lipoprotein(a) levels (r = 0.413; p = 0.004). Notably, elevated amylase occurred in the absence of clinically evident pancreatic disease, significant alcohol consumption or liver dysfunction. These findings suggest that hyperamylasaemia may represent an underrecognised biochemical feature of FD, potentially reflecting vascular and inflammatory mechanisms rather than overt pancreatic disease. Further studies are needed to clarify the pathophysiological significance of hyperamylasaemia in FD.

title: Microfluidics Lab-on-a-Chip Approaches to Decipher Atherosclerosis Pathogenesis.
authorString: Akther F, Ta HT.
abstractText: Atherosclerosis is a complex, multifactorial disease driven by intricate cellular and molecular interactions within the vascular microenvironment. While conventional experimental models have provided important insights into disease progression, they often fail to recapitulate the coupled mechanical and biochemical stimuli that govern vascular pathology in vivo. Lab-on-a-chip technologies offer a powerful platform for reconstructing key cellular and tissue-level features of atherosclerosis within controlled microscale environments, enabling the study of processes such as endothelial dysfunction, inflammatory signaling, cell-matrix interactions, and vascular remodeling. The integration of microfluidics further enhances these models by enabling precise control of flow-derived mechanical cues, including shear stress, vascular geometry, and pulsatile pressure. This review highlights recent advances in microfluidic lab-on-a-chip models for atherosclerosis research, with a focus on their ability to replicate human-relevant pathophysiological conditions. We discuss pioneering studies that have employed these paltforms to investigate endothelial barrier dysfunction, monocyte recruitment, foam cell formation, vascular remodeling, and plaque instability across different stages of disease progression. Collectively, these microfluidic systems provide powerful, physiologically relevant tools for dissecting the mechanisms underlying atherosclerosis and evaluating therapeutic strategies under controlled, biomimetic vascular conditions.

title: Comprehensive geriatric assessment and frailty in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy: toward more individualized and appropriate care.
authorString: van der Heide SI, Drenth-van Maanen AC, Lefeber GJ, Emmelot-Vonk MH, van der Meer MG, Oerlemans MIFJ, Knol W.

journal.title: Netherlands heart journal : monthly journal of the Netherlands Society of Cardiology and the Netherlands Heart Foundation

abstractText: Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), once considered a rare disease, is now an increasingly recognized cause of heart failure. This rise in diagnoses is driven by increased awareness, the availability of non-invasive diagnostics, and the introduction of disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) in an aging population. Available DMTs are costly and may require 12 to 18 months before clinical benefit becomes apparent, making careful assessment of expected treatment benefit essential. Because ATTR-CM predominantly affects older adults, frailty, multimorbidity, and competing health risks are common. Frailty is associated with poorer outcomes and reduced quality of life, yet is not captured by current prognostic staging systems, which primarily reflect cardiac disease severity. Frailty assessment may complement cardiac evaluation by supporting personalized DMT decision-making and identifying modifiable vulnerabilities for targeted interventions. This narrative review integrates cardiology and geriatric perspectives to examine the role of Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment, including frailty assessment, in ATTR-CM. Evidence on frailty prevalence, prognostic significance, and the concept of a disease-specific frailty phenotype is summarized. The role and key components of the CGA are outlined. Additionally, a multidisciplinary care pathway incorporating CGA into clinical practice is proposed to support personalized DMT decisions and targeted interventions.

title: Family experiences with genetic/genomic testing in the pediatric intensive care unit.
authorString: Kim S, Murthy S, Langlois S, Virani A, Osiovich H, GenCOUNSEL Study, Elliott AM.
abstractText:
Genetic testing is increasingly utilized in neonatal and pediatric intensive care units (NICUs and PICUs, respectively) for diagnosis and management. Despite this, research on family experiences and genetic testing is limited, especially in the PICU. Our previous NICU study emphasized the importance of communication in conveying test results. Similar to the NICU, PICU settings raise parental stress and uncertainty. We aimed to identify considerations to increase empowerment for parents undergoing genetic testing in the PICU and compare our results to previous NICU findings. The following mixed-methods study, conducted at BC Children's Hospital in Vancouver, British Columbia, included a demographic and validated empowerment survey (EMPATHIC-38) and semi-structured interviews with caregivers of children who underwent genetic testing in the PICU. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Interviews were analyzed using an interpretive description framework and thematic analysis. Transcripts were coded by two independent coders, and themes were finalized. Eleven semi-structured interviews and 12 empowerment surveys were completed. The organization (Mean = 5.79/6.00 ± 0.16) and professional attitude (Mean = 5.77/6.00 ± 0.17) domains scored the highest. The lowest-scoring domain was parental participation (Mean = 5.43/6.00 ± 0.15), measuring healthcare professionals' attitudes toward parental engagement in care. Identified themes included: preferences for different formats for receiving results, considerations for different languages, understandable language, impact on extended family members, funding for testing, and long-term clinical management.

Conclusion

In contrast to the NICU, PICU parents showed greater consideration for extended family members and long-term management, with a clear preference for educational materials. Parents in both ICUs identified the need for a clear explanation of uninformative and positive results.

What is known

• Despite the growing implementation of genetic testing for critically ill children, the evaluation of caregivers' experiences for those undergoing this process is limited, particularly in the PICU. • Factors affecting parental empowerment for caregivers in the PICU environment are critical to tailor family-centred care.

What is new

• PICU-specific considerations for navigating challenges between healthcare professionals and families were identified, which are in contrast to previous findings in the NICU. • To increase caregivers' empowerment, both genetic and nongenetic healthcare professionals should work together with caregivers to navigate various aspects of genetic testing, including funding, timeline, potential diagnoses, long-term clinical management, and implications for extended family members.

title: Mitral annular calcification.
authorString: Brahier EA, Keen SK, Unai S, Xu B, Desai MY.
abstractText: Mitral annular calcification (MAC) is a chronic, progressive, and degenerative process characterized by calcium deposition along the mitral annulus. This leads to stiffening and distortion of normal mitral annular architecture and ultimately MAC-related valvular dysfunction, which can manifest as mitral stenosis, mitral regurgitation, or mixed valvular disease. Due to its anatomic complexity, transcatheter and surgical interventions for MAC carry significant procedural challenges. As such, multi-modality imaging and multi-disciplinary heart team discussions are critical in MAC evaluation and procedural planning. This review summarizes the epidemiology and pathophysiology of MAC, highlights the critical role of multimodality imaging in the evaluation and procedural planning of MAC, and reviews established transcatheter mitral valve procedures and surgical options for managing MAC, MAC-related valvular dysfunction, and potential complications.

title: Cold septic shock: recognising the low-output phenotype.
authorString: Maan P.
abstractText: Septic shock is commonly taught as a warm, vasodilated state, but the cold, low-output phenotype, in which the underlying process is still sepsis but cardiac output is low and vascular resistance high, is under-recognised. Escalating vasopressors alone in these patients support the blood pressure while leaving the low output untreated. I describe how I separate low from high cardiac output shock at the bedside using peripheries, pulse pressure and central venous oxygen saturation and where cold septic shock and its mechanisms sit within this framework. The phenotype is recognised at the bedside, whereas identifying the underlying mechanism usually requires echocardiography. The central principle is to treat the haemodynamic phenotype, not the label.

title: Genetically Predicted β-Hydroxybutyrate and Coronary Atherosclerosis: Mendelian Randomization and APOE-Associated Transcriptomic Signatures in Human Atherosclerotic Plaques.
authorString: Yang H, Qi W, Liu C, Li Y, Li L, Wu X.
abstractText:
Aims

Ketone bodies are implicated in cardiovascular metabolism, yet the contributions of β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB), acetoacetate and acetone to coronary atherosclerosis remain unclear.

Methods

We integrated Mendelian randomization (MR), cross-trait GWAS analysis, ApoE pQTL-MR and colocalization to investigate genetic associations with coronary atherosclerosis, complemented by bulk transcriptomic analysis, machine learning-based signature construction, immune infiltration analysis and single-cell analysis to characterize APOE-associated molecular features in human atherosclerotic plaques.

Results

Genetically predicted BHB was associated with coronary atherosclerosis risk in univariable MR (OR = 1.59, 95% CI: 1.29-1.95, p = 8.8 × 10-6) and remained significant after mutual adjustment for acetoacetate and acetone (OR = 1.58, 95% CI: 1.14-2.18, p = 0.005), whereas neither acetoacetate nor acetone showed a significant association. Cross-trait gene prioritization highlighted APOE for further investigation. ApoE pQTL-MR supported an association between genetically predicted ApoE and coronary atherosclerosis (OR = 1.23, p = 0.003). Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and machine-learning algorithms, including LASSO, random forest, SVM-RFE and XGBoost, identified an APOE-associated five-gene signature comprising XAF1, CEP128, TMEM106A, VEPH1 and ABCB1. The signature achieved an apparent AUC of 0.956 in GSE43292 and AUCs of 0.974 in GSE100927 and 0.736 in GSE28829. High signature scores were associated with immune-inflammatory changes. Single-cell analysis showed enrichment of the signature in macrophages, endothelial cells and fibroblasts, while CellChat analysis identified a macrophage-centred pattern of inferred cell-cell communication.

Conclusions

These findings identify BHB as the ketone body most strongly associated with coronary atherosclerosis susceptibility and define an APOE-associated multicellular signature in human atherosclerotic plaques with potential value for molecular stratification.

title: Novel Ultrasound Parameters for the Stratification of Femoropopliteal Artery Lesions: A B-Mode and Acceleration Rate Approach.
authorString: Casella IB, Name Villari TF, Françolin PC, Farias C, de Luccia N, Puech-Leão P.
abstractText:
Objective

To identify hemodynamic and morphological parameters on duplex ultrasound (DUS) that may improve the accuracy of differentiating between moderate and severe stenosis of the femoropopliteal arteries.

Methods

Seventy-nine patients (85 limbs) with known peripheral artery disease from two institutions were selected retrospectively and prospectively. Duplex ultrasound (DUS) hemodynamic and morphological (B-mode) parameters were collected at pre-stenotic, stenotic, and post-stenotic segments. Duplex data were compared with contrast-enhanced computed tomography angiography (CTA) or digital subtraction angiography (DSA) as reference standards.

Results

DUS parameters showing the strongest correlations with the reference-standard examinations were direct lesion estimation using B-mode (R = 0.893), post-stenotic acceleration rate (R = -0.733), and the PSV ratio (stenotic/pre-stenotic peak systolic velocity [PSV]) (R = 0.667). For ≥50% stenosis, direct stenosis estimation ≥50% using B-mode, post-stenotic acceleration rate <730 cm/s2, and a stenotic/pre-stenotic PSV ratio ≥1.93 presented sensitivities of 97.1%, 95.7%, and 91.9%, respectively. For ≥70% stenosis, direct stenosis estimation ≥70% using B-mode, post-stenotic acceleration rate <258 cm/s2, and a stenotic/pre-stenotic PSV ratio ≥2.6 presented sensitivities of 95.1%, 80.5%, and 78.8%, respectively.

Conclusion

Among patients with peripheral artery disease, direct lesion estimation using B-mode and post-stenotic acceleration rate emerged as DUS parameters with good sensitivity for detecting moderate and severe stenosis in the femoropopliteal arteries. However, external validation is required before these thresholds can be recommended for clinical use.

title: Is atherosclerosis an autoimmune disease?
authorString: Moutsopoulos HM, Mavragani CP.
abstractText: Atherosclerosis was traditionally viewed as a lipid-storage disorder driven by dyslipidemia and vascular injury. However, accumulating evidence indicates that immune mechanisms are central to disease initiation, progression, and plaque destabilization. Oxidized low-density lipoprotein (oxLDL) and related oxidation-specific epitopes (OSEs), ApoB100 peptides as well as newly identified autoantigens function as modified self-antigens that trigger both innate and adaptive immune responses, linking metabolic stress to chronic vascular inflammation. Innate immune activation is sustained through trained immunity, whereby monocytes and macrophages undergo long-lasting epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming that promotes a persistent pro-inflammatory phenotype. Additional contributors include dendritic cell-mediated antigen presentation, activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome and interleukin-1β signaling pathway, and type I interferon responses, all of which amplify vascular inflammation and plaque progression. Clinical benefits observed with anti-inflammatory therapies targeting these pathways provide evidence for their pathogenic relevance. Adaptive immune responses are characterized by the presence of antigen-experienced T and B lymphocytes within atherosclerotic lesions. oxLDL- and apolipoprotein B (ApoB)-reactive T cells contribute to disease progression through loss of immune tolerance and predominance of pro-inflammatory T helper 1 responses, whereas regulatory T cells exert protective effects. CD8 cytotoxic T cells as well as B cell subsets contribute to the formation of atherosclerotic plaque. Humoral responses against oxLDL generate both atheroprotective and pro-inflammatory antibodies, depending on their specificity and functional properties. Emerging evidence of tertiary lymphoid structures within the arterial wall further supports local antigen-driven immune activation. The accelerated development of atherosclerosis in systemic autoimmune diseases highlights important mechanistic overlap between systemic autoimmunity and vascular pathology. Nevertheless, immune activation in atherosclerosis remains largely initiated by lipid accumulation and vascular injury rather than a primary breakdown of systemic immune tolerance. Atherosclerosis does not appear to require a primary, generalized breakdown of systemic self-tolerance. Nevertheless, ApoB-reactive CD4<sup>+</sup> T cells can lose regulatory features during disease progression, indicating impaired antigen-specific immune regulation. Whether, and to what extent, the local arterial environment drives this change remains to be established. Collectively, current evidence supports the concept that atherosclerosis is a chronic immune-mediated inflammatory disease with prominent autoimmune features, providing a rationale for the development of targeted immunomodulatory therapies.

title: Rheumatic fever: At the interface of autoimmunity and autoinflammation - An overlap hypothesis.
authorString: Parentelli AS, Lopes AA, Levin C, Bertolotti A, Georgin-Lavialle S, Levy Y.
abstractText: Autoinflammatory diseases (AIDs) are disorders of innate immunity characterised by recurrent febrile episodes, systemic inflammation and markedly elevated inflammatory markers. In their classical definition, these diseases occur without pathogenic autoantibodies or antigen-specific autoreactive T and B cells. Many systemic AIDs (SAIDs) involve organs, including the pericardium. Acute rheumatic fever (ARF) is an immune-mediated complication of group A Streptococcus (GAS) infection and remains a global health concern, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Patients with ARF experience inflammatory episodes involving fever, arthralgia, arthritis, chorea, cutaneous features, cardiac complications, all underpinned by a pronounced systemic inflammatory response. Recurrent episodes following further GAS exposure can contribute to rheumatic heart disease (RHD), its chronic valvular sequela. Genetic susceptibility and GAS exposure contribute to disease development. Molecular mimicry is a major proposed mechanism, involving cross-reactive antibodies and T cells that recognise both microbial and host antigens, including cardiac myosin, laminin and tropomyosin. However, recurrent GAS-triggered episodes of ARF are characterised by marked systemic inflammation, raising the possibility that innate immune mechanisms contribute to inflammatory amplification and disease severity. We therefore propose that rheumatic fever (RF) may lie at the interface between autoimmunity and autoinflammation, with established autoimmune mechanisms potentially complemented by dysregulated innate immune responses. This autoimmune-autoinflammatory overlap remains a hypothesis that requires validation through functional immunological studies, particularly those investigating inflammasome pathways.

title: Family screening and genetic testing in transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis : Changing (not only) variant transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis.
authorString: Muller SA, Kieviet LC, van Tintelen JP, Zwetsloot PP, Michels M, Knackstedt C, van der Meer P, van der Meer MG, Meems LMG, van der Zwaag PA, Oerlemans MIFJ, Nienhuis HLA.

journal.title: Netherlands heart journal : monthly journal of the Netherlands Society of Cardiology and the Netherlands Heart Foundation

abstractText: With increasing awareness of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) as a cause of heart failure and the availability of disease-modifying therapies, the importance of early diagnosis has grown. Consequently, greater emphasis has been placed on genetic testing and family screening to identify individuals with variant transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTRv) who are at risk of developing ATTRv cardiomyopathy (ATTRv-CM). To identify individuals with a genetic predisposition to the disease, all individuals with ATTR-CM should undergo genetic testing with subsequent cascade genetic testing in relatives when a genetic variant is identified. In asymptomatic pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) transthyretin (TTR) variant carriers, structured follow-up is recommended to enable early diagnosis, allowing timely initiation of treatment. Additionally, systematic family screening protocols may also help identify and detect ATTR-CM in general, including wild-type ATTR-CM.In conclusion, this narrative review provides clinicians with an overview of how to manage patients with ATTRv-CM and their families. Indeed, comprehensive genetic and cascade screening strategies are essential for early identification and optimal management of ATTR-CM. Future perspectives include refinement of risk stratification, optimization of diagnostic and screening pathways, improved timing of treatment initiation, and addressing health inequalities to ensure equitable access to care.

title: IL23-axis cytokines and C-reactive protein as dissociable biomarkers of vascular recovery in psoriasis: A hypothesis.
authorString: Zhou Y.
abstractText: Biologic therapy has transformed psoriasis into a clinically controllable disease, yet skin clearance does not guarantee resolution of the systemic inflammation and vascular dysfunction that drive cardiovascular risk in this population. We hypothesize that interleukin (IL)-23-axis-proximal cytokines and C-reactive protein (CRP) mark two distinct, dissociable inflammatory compartments in psoriasis: IL23-axis-proximal signaling predominantly governs cutaneous disease activity and microvascular endothelial function, whereas CRP integrates a broader cardiometabolic burden and tracks macrovascular recovery. We distinguish IL23-axis-proximal cytokines (IL23, IL17a, IL22), whose production is largely confined to lesional skin, from shared effector cytokines (TNF-α, IFN-γ, IL1, and IL6), which also arise from adipose tissue and other systemic sources. This model generates two falsifiable predictions: (1) IL23 blockade will improve cutaneous microvascular endothelial function in proportion to suppression of IL23-axis-proximal signaling and out of proportion to any change in CRP, and (2) persistent CRP elevation despite adequate skin clearance will identify patients with blunted macrovascular recovery even when IL23-axis-proximal signaling is suppressed. Because IL6 is a node shared by cutaneous and adipose inflammation, the two compartments are coupled, and we therefore state the model in relative rather than absolute terms: quantitative dissociation, not statistical independence. If confirmed, this compartmentalized model would explain why near-complete skin clearance under biologic therapy, including IL23 blockade, does not uniformly normalize cardiovascular risk, and would offer two complementary, mechanism-specific biomarkers, rather than skin clearance alone, for monitoring vascular recovery after psoriasis treatment. We outline the rationale for this hypothesis and a longitudinal biomarker-imaging design capable of refuting it.

title: The lncRNA SEPT5-GP1BB-encoded peptide ARP, upregulated by 17β-estradiol, retards H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>-induced senescence of human umbilical vein endothelial cells by promoting autophagy.
authorString: Wei W, Song S, Xie L, Wang Y, Zhang Q, Yang S, Ruan Y, Gao M.
abstractText: Vascular endothelial cell (VEC) senescence is a key contributor to vascular aging and atherosclerosis. Increasing evidence suggests that long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) can encode functional micropeptides involved in cellular regulation. In this study, we investigated whether 17β-estradiol (17β-E2) delays endothelial senescence through an lncRNA-encoded peptide associated with autophagy. RNA sequencing was performed in H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>-induced senescent human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) treated with or without 17β-E2, and differentially expressed lncRNAs with coding potential were identified through GO/KEGG analyses and bioinformatics prediction. LncRNA SEPT5-GP1BB was found to encode a 453-amino-acid peptide termed ARP, whose expression was reduced during endothelial senescence but restored by 17β-E2 treatment. Functional experiments demonstrated that 17β-E2 promoted autophagy through ARP rather than through the lncRNA transcript itself. ARP overexpression increased LC3B expression, reduced p62 accumulation, decreased senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity, suppressed SASP-related gene expression, and alleviated oxidative stress in senescent HUVECs. Furthermore, these protective effects were largely abolished by chloroquine treatment, indicating that autophagy mediated the anti-senescent effects of ARP. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that 17β-E2 delays endothelial senescence by upregulating the lncRNA SEPT5-GP1BB-encoded peptide ARP, which promotes autophagy, suggesting that ARP may serve as a potential therapeutic target for vascular aging.

title: Mid to long-term effect of balloon pulmonary valvuloplasty on right ventricle function: a three-dimensional echocardiographic study.
authorString: Elsayegh AT, Elfiky AA, Abdelkader EF, Kamel HM.

journal.title: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background

Right ventricular (RV) remodelling may persist after balloon pulmonary valvuloplasty (BPV) for isolated valvular pulmonary stenosis (PVS). Three-dimensional echocardiography (3DE) enables global RV volumetric assessment beyond conventional 2D indices.

Methods

This cross-sectional observational study included 200 pediatric patients (≤ 18 years) with isolated PVS who underwent successful BPV (post-procedural peak gradient < 36 mmHg) at least 1 year before evaluation. All patients had clinical assessment, ECG, standard 2D/Doppler echocardiography (TAPSE, S', FAC), and ECG-gated 3DE RV quantification to derive RV end-diastolic and end-systolic volume indices and right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF). Patients were classified into 2 groups; group 1 had normal RVEF (≥ 45%) and group 2 had impaired RVEF (< 45%).

Results

RVEF was normal in 71% (n = 142) and impaired in 29% (n = 58). Group 2 was associated with; older age at assessment (median 120 vs. 72 months, p < 0.001), later intervention (median age at BPV 24 vs. 3 months, p < 0.001), and longer time since BPV (96 vs. 68 months, p = 0.004). it also showed association with higher pre-dilatation peak gradients (97.24 ± 26.47 vs. 83.8 ± 24.61 mmHg, p = 0.017) and higher post-dilatation gradients (30.97 ± 9.81 vs. 23.56 ± 8.59 mmHg, p < 0.001). Group 2 also had lower conventional RV function indices: S' 12.64 ± 3.22 vs. 15.01 ± 1.09 cm/s, TAPSE 16.28 ± 2.75 vs. 19.21 ± 1.72 mm, and FAC 39.86 ± 5.21 vs. 49.8 ± 2.62% (all p < 0.001). by using 3DE interrogation, group 2 showed higher RVEDV index (62.0 ± 11.06 vs. 43.14 ± 11.44, p < 0.001) and RVESV index (34.41 ± 8.24 vs. 22.76 ± 6.65, p < 0.001) .

Conclusions
