At ≥ 1 year after successful BPV, nearly one-third of children showed impaired 3DE-derived RVEF, associated with older age at intervention, higher residual gradients, and RV dilatation, patients with RV impairment were underestimated when assessed by 2D vs. 3D echo, supporting the role of 3DE in long-term surveillance.

title: The spectrum of amyloid cardiovascular disease.
authorString: Triposkiadis F, Starling RC, Hanna M, Xanthopoulos A.
abstractText: Cardiac amyloidosis, historically characterized as a restrictive cardiomyopathy, is now understood as a multi-compartmental disorder. Atrial amyloid infiltration-whether ANP-derived isolated atrial amyloidosis secondary to atrial stretch, or primary atrial ATTR infiltration-produces an atrial cardiomyopathy that frequently manifests as atrial fibrillation and a thrombogenic substrate even in sinus rhythm. Cardiac amyloidosis exhibits a high prevalence in heart failure, particularly among elderly patients presenting with preserved ejection fraction. Furthermore, TTR amyloid frequently coexists with degenerative aortic stenosis, and amyloid deposits are also found in the coronary microcirculation and the aorta. Given the current availability of efficacious treatments for amyloidosis, the recognition of these diverse clinical manifestations is paramount for achieving accurate diagnosis, appropriate risk stratification, and timely therapeutic intervention to enhance cardiovascular outcomes. This review frames amyloid cardiovascular disease as a multisystem process affecting the myocardium, atria, valves, and vasculature-often with extracardiac red flags-rather than solely as an infiltrative ventricular cardiomyopathy. Actionable implications currently concentrate on ventricular ATTR/AL cardiomyopathy and concomitant aortic stenosis; coronary and aortic medial deposits remain mechanistically important research targets rather than independently treatable lesions.

title: 293-Day Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump Support as a Bridge to Transplantation in Refractory Heart Failure.
authorString: Bernardes AB, Benedetti H, Hames RL, Galoro VG, Pinheiro Junior JA, Mendonça FCC, Martins SK.
abstractText:
Background

The intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) is widely used as temporary mechanical circulatory support in patients with refractory heart failure complicated by cardiogenic shock. However, its use is generally limited to short-term therapy because of device-related complications.

Case summary

A 57-year-old man with idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy receiving guideline-directed medical therapy and cardiac resynchronization therapy with defibrillation developed cardiogenic shock refractory to inotropic therapy, requiring IABP implantation. Mechanical circulatory support was maintained for 293 days, including 291 days as a bridge to heart transplantation and 2 days after transplantation.

Discussion

This case demonstrates that prolonged IABP support is feasible when combined with transition to a left subclavian approach, serial device replacement, and meticulous multidisciplinary management.

Take-home message

In carefully selected patients, prolonged IABP support, combined with individualized device management and multidisciplinary care, may provide sustained clinical stabilization and serve as an effective bridge to heart transplantation.

title: Butin Ameliorates Atherosclerosis by Regulating the TIMM13-TIMM8A Complex to Alleviate Macrophage Ferroptosis.
authorString: Wang D, Yu X, Xie M, Huang G, Liang Z, Huang C, Liu H.
abstractText: Atherosclerosis (AS) progression is heavily driven by iron dyshomeostasis and oxidative stress, yet current therapies fail to effectively resolve these underlying drivers. Ferroptosis exacerbates plaque vulnerability through macrophage dysfunction, but its regulatory nodes remain elusive. This study aims to investigate the role of the mitochondrial translocase complex TIMM13/TIMM8A in atherogenesis and evaluate the natural flavonoid Butin as a targeted inhibitor of this complex. Transcriptomic profiling and network pharmacology identified key targets. Oxidized low-density lipoprotein (Ox-LDL)-treated macrophages and high-fat diet-fed ApoE<sup>-/-</sup> mice were used for functional validation. Direct target engagement was demonstrated by Cellular Thermal Shift Assay, molecular dynamics simulations, competitive Co-Immunoprecipitation, and site-directed mutagenesis. Ox-LDL promoted aberrant TIMM13 upregulation and TIMM8A suppression, triggering mitochondrial iron overload and lipid peroxidation; this ferroptotic cascade was exacerbated by TIMM13 overexpression or TIMM8A knockdown. We identified Butin as a selective binder of TIMM13 at the Asn34 residue, competitively disrupting the pathological TIMM13-TIMM8A interaction. Consequently, Butin restored the SLC7A11/GPX4 axis and alleviated iron overload and inflammation. In ApoE<sup>-/-</sup> mice, Butin reduced necrotic cores, enhanced plaque stability, and attenuated vascular ferroptosis, whereas in vivo Asn34 mutation abrogated these benefits. This study identifies the TIMM13/TIMM8A complex as a pivotal mitochondrial gatekeeper of ferroptosis in AS, and demonstrates that Butin acts as a targeted natural inhibitor that halts plaque progression by disrupting this complex and restoring iron homeostasis. These findings provide a compelling mechanistic and translational framework for targeting mitochondrial iron handling in cardiovascular disease management.

title: The TET2-H19 axis modulates the osteogenic differentiation of smooth muscle cells and atherosclerotic calcification.
authorString: Zeng Z, Fan XJ, Tao J, Fan SY, Li FF, Yang CB, Li K, Liu YY, Wen Y, Chen HX, Zhang Y, Liu RJ, Zheng JM, Tang WH.
abstractText: Atherosclerotic calcification, which is characterized by the osteogenic differentiation of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), is prevalent in advanced lesions and contributes to increased plaque vulnerability and the likelihood of rupture, but no approved medical therapies are available to effectively prevent this condition. Here, we investigated the effects of ten-eleven translocation-2 (Tet2) deficiency and overexpression on atherosclerotic calcification, as well as the underlying molecular mechanisms. We found that the expression and activity of TET2 were decreased in calcified human coronary arteries, vitamin D3 overload-induced calcified aortas and diet-induced atherosclerotic aortas. The single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that the osteochondrogenic cluster was markedly expanded in VSMC-specific Tet2-deficient mice. Atherosclerotic lesions from VSMC-specific Tet2-deficient mice showed significantly increased calcification and deposition of collagen, whereas VSMC-specific Tet2 overexpression ameliorated atherosclerotic calcification. TET2 knockdown induced the H19-mediated and RUNX2 (runt-related transcription factor 2)-dependent osteogenic differentiation of primary human VSMCs via increased trimethylation of histone H3 lysine 4 at the H19 promoter. Treatment with a calpain inhibitor significantly inhibited calpain activity, attenuated high calcium-induced TET2 destabilization and protected against vascular calcification. Restoring TET2 expression may represent an effective strategy to protect against atherosclerotic calcification.

title: Multi-omics, spatial omics and artificial intelligence in chronic diseases: current applications and future directions.
authorString: Wang Q, Qu H, Jin S, Wang J, Li Z, Zhao G, Liu J, Huang Y, Ji X, Pan X.
abstractText: Chronic diseases exhibit multiscale heterogeneity and spatial organization, yet analytical frameworks often fail to connect molecular perturbations, tissue architecture, and clinical outcomes within a unified evidence framework. Bulk and single-modality approaches can identify regulatory or cellular alterations but provide limited insight into why pathogenic programs emerge in anatomical regions, how they shape disease niches, and how they drive divergent clinical trajectories. Multi-omics partially addresses this gap by resolving interconnected layers of regulation, transcription, protein activity, and metabolism, whereas spatial omics maps these processes within preserved tissue architecture, enabling the delineation of lesion topology, interface states, and multicellular microenvironments. Artificial intelligence (AI) may further extend this framework by integrating molecular, spatial, imaging, and clinical data into disease representations that support disease stratification, the discovery of mechanistic patterns, and clinically testable predictions, provided that models are externally validated, biologically interpretable, and robust to dataset bias and domain shift. In this review, we examine how multi-omics, spatial omics, and AI can bridge the disconnect between molecular profiling, spatial pathology, and clinical translation in chronic disease research. We discuss six representative disease domains before synthesizing insights into how these approaches define molecular endotypes, map pathological niches, identify recurrent mechanistic patterns, and generate interpretable surrogate readouts for diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment stratification. We also highlight limitations, including preanalytical variability, inconsistencies across platforms, limited external generalizability, and the challenges of translating high-dimensional outputs into deployable clinical tools. Finally, we outline priorities for scalable evidence systems, mechanism-guided validation frameworks, multimodal model interpretability, and prospective clinical implementation.

title: Epicardial adipose tissue volume and the Naples Prognostic Score add incremental value to EuroSCORE II for predicting MACE after TAVR: a retrospective cohort study
authorString: Chen B, Li X, Li K, Zhou C, Xia Z, Lian Z.
abstractText: Background Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is a common degenerative valvular disease in the elderly, and transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is now its mainstream treatment. Conventional risk scores based on demographic and comorbidity data do not capture local cardiac inflammation or systemic nutritional status, limiting prediction of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) after TAVR. Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) volume and the Naples Prognostic Score (NPS) reflect these dimensions, but their combined incremental value is unknown. We assessed their independent and incremental value for MACE after TAVR, using EuroSCORE II as reference. Methods In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 427 consecutive patients with severe CAVD undergoing TAVR (January 2020 to July 2025) were enrolled. EAT volume was quantified on computed tomography angiography and dichotomized at the cohort median; NPS was derived from routine laboratory indices and categorized as low (0–2) or high (3–4). The endpoint was MACE after TAVR, defined by Valve Academic Research Consortium 3 criteria. Multivariable Cox regression assessed independent prognostic value; nested models were compared by Harrell’s C-index, time-dependent ROC, net reclassification index (NRI), integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) and decision curve analysis. Proportional hazards were assessed. Results During a median follow-up of 24.51 months, 89 patients (20.8%) experienced MACE. After adjustment, both high EAT and high NPS were independent predictors, with average hazard ratios (HRs) of 3.01 (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.80–5.03; P  < 0.001) and 1.96 (95% CI 1.27–3.04; P  = 0.003). Adding both markers raised the C-index from 0.716 to 0.751 (likelihood-ratio P  < 0.001); the 24-month area under the curve was 0.757. Integrated discrimination improvement was 0.068 (95% CI 0.031–0.134; P  = 0.011) and net reclassification index was 0.075 (95% CI − 0.081–0.239; P  = 0.345). Calibration and sensitivity analyses supported the model; time-varying analysis showed that the effect of high EAT increased over follow-up whereas that of high NPS was confined to the early period. Conclusions Preoperative EAT volume and NPS are independent, complementary predictors of MACE after TAVR. Their combination improves on conventional risk scores and requires only routine preoperative examinations.

title: Immediate Femoral Closure Without Mobility Restrictions: Using the CELT ACD<sup>®</sup> for Neuroendovascular Interventions.
authorString: Sorrentino ZA, Yang W, Saini N, Dagra A, Sarathy D, Lucke-Wold B, Robinson CP, Koch MJ, Hoh BL, Chalouhi N.
abstractText:
Background and objectives

A vascular closure device that provides rapid hemostasis is useful for neuroendovascular patients, especially for those with altered mental status or high intracranial pressure that limits compliance with bedrest. CELT ACD® (arterial closure device) has demonstrated effectiveness and safety in non-neurological cohorts, and thus, the aim of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of CELT in neuroendovascular interventions.

Methods

We conducted a prospective cohort study at our institution, enrolling consecutive patients undergoing neuroendovascular intervention with femoral access and subsequent CELT closure. We used a CELT-first approach for femoral closure during the study period, with all patients undergoing immediate head-of-bed (HOB) elevation postprocedurally. Primary outcomes included immediate device failure, time to hemostasis (TTH), time to HOB elevation, and risk of access-site hematoma 12 hours after hemostasis (delayed hematoma).

Results

Fifty consecutive patients undergoing neuroendovascular interventions were closed with CELT. All patients (n = 50, 100%) underwent immediate postprocedure HOB elevation after a straight-leg test, and there was no immediate device failure or delayed hematoma. The average TTH and HOB/mobility liberalization was 1.1 (±2.2) minutes. There was no lower extremity ischemia attributable to CELT closure.

Conclusion

In this prospective study, we reported the first experience with CELT closure in neuroendovascular interventions and found an excellent safety and efficacy profile. CELT may be considered first line for patients requiring rapid TTH and early HOB elevation, particularly in the context of high intracranial pressure concerns.

title: ALDH2 Deficiency Promotes Mitochondrial Oxidative Stress and Adverse Limb Outcomes via VDAC-HSP60 Signaling.
authorString: Lin YC, Wu NC, Hong CS, Hsu PC, Yang WJ, Chang YC, Chen CH, Chang WT.
abstractText: The ALDH2 rs671 variant, which is frequent in East Asian populations, markedly reduces mitochondrial aldehyde-detoxifying capacity and thereby increases vulnerability to reactive aldehydes, including 4-hydroxynonenal (4-HNE), during ischemic stress. We show that impaired ALDH2 activity perturbs endothelial mitochondrial proteostasis through an ALDH2-4-HNE-HSP60-VDAC1 pathway. In Aldh2 knock-in mice and endothelial cells exposed to oxygen-glucose deprivation, ALDH2 deficiency was accompanied by 4-HNE accumulation, mitochondrial DNA injury, loss of membrane potential, increased mitochondrial ROS, mitochondrial fragmentation, and apoptosis. Analysis of transcriptomic data highlighted HSP60 (HSPD1) as a downstream candidate. LC-MS/MS, covalent docking, co-immunoprecipitation, and proximity ligation analyses supported 4-HNE modification of HSP60, while native electrophoresis indicated disruption of higher-order HSP60 assembly. HSP60 redistribution to the cytosol was predominantly dependent on VDAC1. Activating ALDH2 with AD-5591, or suppressing VDAC1 genetically or pharmacologically, preserved HSP60 homeostasis, mitochondrial integrity, and endothelial function. In a prospective cohort of 227 patients with peripheral artery disease, the rs671 variant was associated with a higher incidence of major adverse limb events. These data position HSP60 proteostasis downstream of ALDH2-dependent aldehyde detoxification and identify the ALDH2-4-HNE-HSP60-VDAC1 pathway as a potential therapeutic target in ischemic vascular disease.

title: Simultaneous Aortic and Mitral Valve-in-Valve Replacement Using Balloon-Expandable MyVal Valves With Bioprosthetic Valve Fracture.
authorString: Bajaj N, Singh N, Gupta A, Pathania S.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText: Valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement and mitral valve replacement have proved to be a viable alternative to redo surgery in patients who have bioprosthetic valve dysfunction. There is a large subgroup of patients who undergo double valve replacement with bioprosthetic valves, especially in patients with rheumatic heart disease. Failure of these bioprosthetic valves would require a transcatheter management strategy. Transcatheter double valve replacement (TDVR) in these complex cases would require careful evaluation and planning of valve sizing, aortomitral interactions, access, and residual gradients. A 73-year-old man with rheumatic heart disease and prior double bioprosthetic valve replacement in 2014 presented with New York Heart Association class (NYHA) III dyspnea and exertional pre-syncope. He had severe stenosis of a 19 mm Perimount Magna aortic bioprosthesis and a 27 mm Perimount Magna mitral bioprosthesis, with pulmonary hypertension. Computed tomography demonstrated suitable anatomy for transcatheter valve-in-valve treatment. He underwent successful TDVR with a 20 mm MyVal balloon-expandable in the aortic position, followed by a post-implantation valve fracture, and a 27.5 mm MyVal transseptally in the mitral position. The final mean gradients were 15 mmHg across the aortic valve and 6 mmHg across the mitral valve at discharge. At 1-year follow-up, the patient remained clinically well without an increase in valve gradients. Simultaneous transcatheter aortic and mitral valve-in-valve replacement can be performed successfully in selected high-risk patients after meticulous multimodality planning. In patients with a small surgical aortic bioprosthesis, intentional bioprosthetic valve fracture may be an important adjunct to optimize post-implantation hemodynamics. This report highlights the complexity of procedural planning for bioprosthetic valve fracture in a small aortic valve, ensuring optimal hemodynamics and the safety and durability of the Myval transcatheter heart valve in challenging and complex procedures like TDVR.

title: Single-port robotic surgery versus laparo-endoscopic single-site surgery for the surgical staging of early-stage endometrial cancer: a sequential-period propensity-score analysis.
authorString: Kim JH, Kim Y, Jo D, Seo H, Shin S, Kim S, Choi MC, Lee SW, Kim DY, Kim JH, Park JY.
abstractText: We compared perioperative outcomes of da Vinci SP robotic surgery and laparo-endoscopic single-site surgery (LESS) for staging early-stage endometrial cancer in a sequential-period cohort. Between 2010 and 2025, 178 women with presumed and final FIGO stage I or II endometrial carcinoma underwent single-port staging with lymph node assessment; LESS was used through 2021 (n = 95), and SP surgery was introduced in 2021 (n = 83). Patients were analyzed by planned approach, including procedures requiring an additional port. The primary outcome was the hemoglobin decline from the preoperative value to the value measured on the day of surgery. The hemoglobin decline was 1.92 ± 1.14 g/dL after LESS and 0.92 ± 0.88 g/dL after SP surgery (p < .001), and estimated blood loss was 205.4 ± 192.4 and 68.5 ± 79.3 mL (p < .001). After inverse probability of treatment weighting, the between-group difference in hemoglobin decline (SP minus LESS) was - 1.06 g/dL (95% CI - 1.42 to - 0.70). This estimate was not materially changed by further adjustment for perioperative fluid volume and sampling time. In a sensitivity analysis restricted to patients with pelvic lymphadenectomy, the difference was attenuated to - 0.72 g/dL (95% CI - 1.21 to - 0.22), and operative time was 25.5 min longer with the SP robot. Overall operative time, hospital stay, conversions, and complications did not differ significantly. SP staging was associated with a smaller hemoglobin decline. Because the 2 approaches were used in largely different calendar periods, these findings do not establish an independent effect of the platform.

title: Mitral annular calcification on routine Non-ECG Gated Chest CT Is associated with advanced atrioventricular block requiring permanent pacing: A case-control study.
authorString: Brodov Y, Massalha E, Kirshenboim Z, Shajrawi R, Sabbag A, Konen E, Goitein O.

journal.title: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging

abstractText: The purpose of this study was to determine whether visual or quantitative mitral annular calcification (MAC) burden on routine non-contrast, non-ECG-gated chest computed tomography (CT) is associated with permanent pacemaker (PPM) implantation for advanced atrioventricular (AV) block. MAC has been linked to conduction disturbances after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Whether MAC visible on routine chest CT is associated with significant AV conduction disease in non-TAVI patients remains uncertain. In this retrospective single-center case-control study, 39 consecutive patients who underwent PPM implantation for symptomatic advanced AV block and had non-contrast chest CT were compared with 39 age- and sex-matched controls without AV block or prior PPM. MAC was graded visually by annular circumference involvement and quantified using an Agatston-based score. Visual MAC was more prevalent in the PPM (+) group than in the PPM (-) group (22 of 39 [56%] vs. 12 of 39 [31%]; P = 0.039). The prevalence of PPM implantation increased across visual MAC categories, from 39% with no MAC and 48% with MAC involving < 1/3 of the annular circumference to 80% with MAC involving 1/3 to 1/2 and 100% with MAC involving > 1/2 of the annular circumference (P = 0.007). Quantitative MAC categories also differed (44%, 33%, and 78% PPM implantation for MAC scores of 0, 1 to 400, and > 400, respectively; P = 0.022). In multivariable analysis, MAC score > 400 remained independently associated with PPM implantation (odds ratio: 24.6; 95% confidence interval: 1.63 to 370.96; P = 0.02).Visual and quantitative MAC burden on routine non-contrast chest CT were associated with PPM implantation for advanced AV block. Structured assessment and reporting of marked MAC may provide a clinically useful marker in patients with suspected AV conduction disease.

title: On-Pump Beating-Heart Redo Mitral Valve Surgery: A Personalized, Risk-Adapted Surgical Strategy for Plug-Induced Hemolysis.
authorString: Pasic M, Shrestha N, Jaber W, Samaras C, Torregrossa G, Duncan A, Gillinov M, Chaubey S.
abstractText:
Background

Severe mechanical hemolysis following the use of a paravalvular leak occluder plug is a challenging complication, particularly for patients with multiple comorbidities who face prohibitive risks with repeat surgery.

Case summary

A 63-year-old multimorbid man with end-stage renal disease presented with severe microangiopathic hemolytic anemia after transcatheter paravalvular leak closure. Ten months earlier, he had undergone aortic and mitral valve replacements and coronary bypass, complicated by a difficult recovery requiring temporary mechanical circulatory support with an Impella. Now, to minimize the operative risk and avoid the difficult postoperative course experienced after the previous surgery requiring mechanical circulatory support, a modified, infrequent surgical strategy was used: On-pump, beating-heart redo mitral valve replacement with extraction of the occluder plug. It successfully circumvented global myocardial ischemia and simplified complex redo surgery. Postoperatively, the hematologic parameters normalized within days.

Discussion

This personalized, risk-adapted surgical strategy mitigates operative risk in a high-risk patient, achieving rapid, definitive resolution of hemolytic anemia.

Take-home messages

Eliminating the source of mechanical hemolysis results in rapid normalization of laboratory parameters within days. On-pump beating-heart surgery is a valuable strategy to simplify complex redo procedures while minimizing high perioperative risk.

title: Risk factors for the recurrence of chronic subdural hematomas in patients undergoing burr-hole drainage.
authorString: Stoessel T, Rasadurai A, Guzman R, Soleman J.
abstractText: Chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH) is a common neurosurgical disease, particularly in the elderly. The recurrence of cSDH remains a clinical challenge, with several risk factors postulated. Although adjunctive treatments to surgery exist, such as steroids, statins, and middle meningeal artery embolization, the number needed to treat is high, and patient selection remains unclear. This retrospective study aimed to identify risk factors for recurrence after burr hole drainage of cSDH. A single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients undergoing burr-hole drainage for cSDH between February 2012 and May 2023. The primary outcome was surgical recurrence, defined as cSDH recurrence requiring reoperation within six months. Clinical characteristics, preoperative radiological findings, comorbidities and medications, and postoperative findings were assessed as potential risk factors using univariate analysis and, after imputation, multivariable analysis.A total of 766 patients with a recurrence rate of 11.2% (86/766) were included. Significant preoperative risk factors for recurrence included subacute and separated hematoma types (p = 0.02), larger hematoma volume (p = 0.004), greater midline shift (MLS) (p = 0.006), lower Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) (p < 0.001) and higher Markwalder score (p = 0.012). Postoperative findings significantly associated with recurrence were larger cavity volume (p = 0.005), greater MLS (p = 0.01), a higher Markwalder score (p = 0.01) and modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score (p < 0.001) at discharge. After multivariable logistic regression, subacute hematoma age (OR 2.097, p = 0.036), absence of hypertension (OR 1.937, p = 0.012), larger postoperative cavity volume (OR 1.012, p = 0.016), greater postoperative MLS (OR 1.179, p < 0.001), and higher mRS at discharge (OR 1.959, p = 0.002) remained independently associated with recurrence. We found subacute hematoma, larger postoperative subdural cavity volume, higher mRS at discharge, greater postoperative MLS, and the absence of hypertension as factors significantly associated with surgical recurrence within six months.

title: Analysis of haemolysis-based injury in immortalised proximal tubule epithelial cells is impaired by haemoglobin interference with bioluminescence assays.
authorString: Trott C, Bennett J, Murray PA, Chadwick A, McWilliam SJ, Wilm B.
abstractText: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a serious complication which is common amongst cardiac and aortic/vascular surgery patients. Although the cause of AKI following cardiac surgery is multifactorial, haemolysis is an increasingly recognised contributing factor caused by the use of cardiopulmonary bypass machines. Haemolysis, the lysis of red blood cells, releases free haemoglobin (fHb) into the bloodstream which is known to cause kidney injury. Currently, the mechanisms of haemolysis-induced kidney injury are not fully understood. In this study, we investigated the injury response to fHb in a human-derived conditionally immortalised proximal tubule epithelial cell line (ciPTECs). Results showed that fHb interference reduces bioluminescence signal output which is considerably mitigated by removing fHb solutions and haemolysed plasma prior to the beginning of the assay. Interestingly, we found that the effect of fHb on ciPTECs was different with haemolysed plasma compared to fHb solutions, potentially due to factors other than fHb within the plasma. In contrast to expectations, haemolysed plasma induced only a marginal increase in NF-ĸB activity and had minimal effect on mitochondrial function. Together, these findings suggest that caution should be applied when using bioluminescent assays with fHb, both in solution and haemolysed plasma, and that fHb may not inflict severe injury on ciPTECs.

title: Postbiotics derived from <i>Latilactobacillus curvatus</i> alleviate alcoholic liver injury by reshaping intestinal microbiota and activating the lysozyme-AHR-IL-22 axis.
authorString: Zhu S, Chen Y, Shi L, Lu H, Gong Q, Wang Y, Yang Y.
abstractText: Long-term alcohol exposure disrupts gut microbiota and mucosal immune homeostasis, promoting the pathogenesis of alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) via the gut-liver axis. Postbiotic intervention has emerged as a potential strategy for alleviating ALD, yet its protective mechanisms within the impaired intestinal microenvironment remain unclear. This study investigated whether postbiotics derived from Latilactobacillus curvatus can alleviate alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) and explored their active components and underlying mechanisms. In two alcohol-exposed mouse models, heat-killed L. curvatus (HKLC) significantly reduced liver injury, steatosis, oxidative stress, and inflammation, while improving lipid metabolic homeostasis. HKLC also restored intestinal barrier integrity by increasing tight junction protein expression and recovering cecal short-chain fatty acids. Microbiota analysis showed that HKLC remodeled both bacterial and fungal communities, suppressing opportunistic pathogens such as Parasutterella excrementihominis and Candida albicans while enriching beneficial short-chain fatty acid-associated bacteria including Phascolarctobacterium faecium. Fractionation experiments further showed that the cell precipitate fraction was the major active component, reproducing most of the protective effects of whole HKLC. Mechanistically, HKLC and its cell precipitate fraction enhanced intestinal lysozyme and Defa5 expression, reactivated the AHR-IL-22 signaling pathway, and increased downstream antimicrobial peptides. These findings demonstrate that L. curvatus-derived postbiotics alleviate ALD mainly through the gut-liver axis by restoring intestinal homeostasis, reshaping gut microbiota, and activating lysozyme-associated mucosal immune signaling. This study provides experimental evidence supporting postbiotic-based strategies for ALD intervention.

title: Left Bundle-Branch Pacing versus Right Ventricular Pacing for Atrioventricular Block.
authorString: Qian Z, Jiang L, Hou X, Xue X, Shen M, Su Y, Chen Y, Cai B, He L, Fan J, Fu F, Jastrzębski M, Yang S, Chan JY, Huang W, Whinnett ZI, Sheng X, Chelu MG, Xu Y, Wang Y, Shu X, Chen H, Zou F, Ellenbogen KA, Gold MR, Wei Y, Liu X, Zou J, OptimPacing Investigators.

journal.title: The New England journal of medicine

abstractText:
Background

Right ventricular pacing is associated with cardiac dyssynchrony and left ventricular systolic dysfunction. Left bundle-branch pacing preserves left ventricular electrical and mechanical synchrony, but its clinical benefits relative to right ventricular pacing in patients with atrioventricular block remain unclear.

Methods

In this investigator-initiated, international, open-label, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned patients with atrioventricular block in a 1:1 ratio to receive left bundle-branch pacing or right ventricular pacing. The primary outcome was a composite of death from any cause, hospitalization for heart failure, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy.

Results

A total of 702 patients underwent randomization, with 348 assigned to receive left bundle-branch pacing and 354 to receive right ventricular pacing; 17 patients (6 in the left bundle-branch pacing group and 11 in the right ventricular pacing group) were excluded before device implantation. A total of 685 patients (342 in the left bundle-branch pacing group and 343 in the right ventricular pacing group) were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis. The mean age of the patients was 68.4 years, and 57.5% were men. At the prespecified interim analysis, the data monitoring committee recommended early termination of the trial. At a median follow-up of 35.1 months (interquartile range, 23.6 to 40.7), a primary-outcome event had occurred in 16 patients in the left bundle-branch pacing group and in 35 patients in the right ventricular pacing group (Kaplan-Meier 4-year cumulative incidence, 8.5% and 19.2%, respectively; hazard ratio, 0.41; 95% confidence interval, 0.23 to 0.75; P = 0.003 by a stratified log-rank test). Serious adverse events unrelated to implantation procedures occurred in 39 patients (11.8%) who had received left bundle-branch pacing and in 33 patients (9.3%) who had received right ventricular pacing (P = 0.32).

Conclusions

Among patients with atrioventricular block, left bundle-branch pacing was superior to right ventricular pacing in reducing the risk of a composite of death from any cause, hospitalization for heart failure, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. (Funded by Project on New Technology of Jiangsu Province and others; OptimPacing ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04624763.).

title: Preventive cardiovascular ultrasound imaging: a strategy for lifelong atherosclerosis control.
authorString: Naqvi TZ.
abstractText:
Introduction

Atherosclerosis develops silently over decades before manifesting as myocardial infarction, stroke, or cardiovascular (CV) death. Carotid and femoral ultrasound can identify subclinical atherosclerosis SA), quantify plaque burden, and refine cardiovascular risk assessment beyond traditional risk factors.

Areas covered

This narrative review synthesizes evidence from population-based cohorts, longitudinal studies, clinical trials, and imaging investigations from 1987-2026 identified through PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar. Carotid and femoral plaque prevalence, associated risk factors, vulnerability, natural history, prediction of CV events across the lifespan, serial ultrasound assessment of plaque progression and regression, including responses to lifestyle modification and lipid-lowering therapy are discussed. Comparisons with other imaging modalities and the importance of primordial prevention to reduce cumulative exposure to CV risk factors are addressed.

Expert opinion

Carotid and femoral plaque ultrasound offers a practical, accessible, radiation-free approach to detecting subclinical atherosclerosis and supporting individualized prevention. Plaque assessment may inform risk discussions, reinforce lifestyle changes, and improve adherence to appropriate lipid-lowering therapy. Standardized acquisition, reproducible measurements, and validated thresholds are needed for broader implementation. Prospective trials should establish whether ultrasound-guided prevention improves clinical outcomes. Integrating plaque imaging with sustained risk factor control and primordial prevention may help reduce the lifetime burden of atherosclerotic CV disease.

title: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial of a Digital Health Intervention for Medication Optimization in Heart Failure: The ENGAGE-HF Trial Outcomes.
authorString: Dorsch MP, Gilotra NA, Spaulding EM, Martin SS, Zhao H, Wilson GA, Poddar M, Verma A, Schmiedmayer P, Kraft P, Rodriguez F, Azizi Z, Hwang PH, Trumpower B, Ganai S, Basu T, Luff E, O'Neill M, Nallamothu BK, Golbus JR, Sandhu AT.
abstractText: Background: Despite clear evidence that guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) significantly reduces mortality and hospitalizations in patients with heart failure (HF) with reduced and mildly reduced ejection fraction, real-world implementation remains suboptimal. Digital health interventions may promote GDMT titration after hospital discharge. Methods: The ENGAGE-HF trial was a multicenter, two-arm, open-label, randomized controlled trial across three academic centers, funded by the AHA Strategically Focused Research Network (SFRN) for Health Technology and Innovation. Patients recently hospitalized with HF, with or without a primary hospital diagnosis of HF, and LVEF <50% receiving suboptimal GDMT were randomized 1:1 to either the ENGAGE-HF app or usual care for 90 days. The ENGAGE-HF intervention consisted of a patient-facing mobile app and a clinician dashboard overseen by study coordinators. The primary outcome was the Medication Optimization Score (MOS, scale 0-100%) at 90 days. Secondary outcomes were individual GDMT therapies and the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score at 90 days. Results: A total of 134 participants were randomized. At 90 days, the adjusted MOS was significantly higher in the ENGAGE-HF group compared to the control group (83.7% vs. 74.0%, p = 0.010). Results remained consistent across multiple sensitivity analyses. Overall prescribing prevalence increased more in the ENGAGE-HF group for MRAs (+15.9 vs. +2.5 percentage points) and SGLT2 inhibitors (+10.9 vs. +2.5 percentage points). Furthermore, the ENGAGE-HF group demonstrated greater increases in achieving target doses for ARNI (+18.8% vs. +6.3%) and beta-blockers (+8.5% vs. +0.6%). KCCQ-23 CSS at 90 days was 75.2 (SE 2.6) in the intervention group versus 72.2 (SE 2.6) in the control group (between-group p = 0.40). Conclusions: ENGAGE-HF, a digital health intervention that integrates remote monitoring, patient engagement, and clinical decision support, significantly improved GDMT optimization at 90 days compared with usual care among patients with HF. Registration: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov Unique Identifier: NCT06750549.

title: From Valve to Spine and Spleen: Multisystem Complications of <i>Gemella haemolysans</i> Prosthetic-Valve Endocarditis.
authorString: Baghdasaryan E, Lada S, Orphali R, Jayswal R, Dutta S.
abstractText: Gemella haemolysans is an uncommon cause of infective endocarditis, yet infection involving a prosthetic valve may be accompanied by extensive extracardiac disease. A 79-year-old man with a history of transcatheter aortic valve replacement presented with fever, rigors, dyspnea, severe low back pain, and inability to walk after a fall. Two sets of blood cultures grew G. haemolysans. Echocardiography demonstrated a 0.6 × 0.6 cm vegetation at the aortic valve annulus. Lumbar magnetic resonance imaging identified discitis and vertebral osteomyelitis at L4-L5 and L5-S1, an anterior epidural abscess, and moderate-to-severe spinal canal stenosis. Abdominal imaging revealed a right psoas abscess and a 6.2-cm splenic infarction. Antimicrobial therapy was narrowed to intravenous ceftriaxone according to susceptibility testing. Fever resolved and inflammatory markers declined during hospitalization; a 6-week course was arranged at discharge without valve surgery. This case highlights the association between endocarditis and vertebral infection, the limitations of vegetation size as a measure of extracardiac disease, and the complexity of treatment decisions following transcatheter valve replacement.

title: Sirtuins in Cellular Senescence and Cardiovascular Diseases: From Mechanistic Basis to Activator Development and Translational Perspectives.
authorString: Deng Y, Cai Y, Wang X, Ge B, Sheng X, Liu T, Song S, Li X.
abstractText: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of mortality worldwide, and cellular senescence serves as a core driving factor in the pathogenesis and progression of cardiovascular degeneration and related diseases. Sirtuins act as a crucial molecular hub linking cellular senescence to CVDs, and their upregulated activity is closely associated with delayed cellular senescence and preserved normal cardiovascular function; therefore, the research and development of small-molecule Sirtuin-activating compounds (STACs) hold important research value and promising translational potential for CVD intervention. This review systematically elucidates the molecular mechanisms by which various Sirtuin subtypes influence senescence-related processes in CVDs through the regulation of biological events such as DNA damage repair, mitochondrial homeostasis, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses. Furthermore, it comprehensively outlines their roles in major cardiovascular conditions, including hypertension, angiogenesis, atherosclerosis, aortic aneurysm and dissection, and heart failure. Finally, this paper summarizes recent advances in the development of Sirtuin activators and, in light of current challenges such as insufficient specificity and hurdles in clinical translation, provides perspectives on the future development of Sirtuin-targeted therapies for the prevention and treatment of CVDs.

title: Ambiguous Familial Loss: Perinatal Experiences of Women Living With Their Children in Daily Life Who Received a Prenatal Diagnosis of Congenital Heart Defects-A Qualitative Evidence Synthesis.
authorString: Maruyama A, Murayama S, Kamibeppu K.
abstractText: This study aimed to examine the perinatal experiences of women who received a fetal diagnosis of congenital heart defects (CHD) and chose to continue their pregnancies. To achieve this, we conducted a qualitative evidence synthesis. Using thematic synthesis following Thomas and Harden, we analyzed 14 qualitative studies published in Japanese or English within a 15-year period starting from 2010. The heart symbolizes the life of the fetus, an ambiguous family member. Following a fetal diagnosis of CHD, women mourned the loss of an imaginary baby or became aware of their child's death while feeling strong fetal movements. This situation of feeling a child's presence while being aware of their absence corresponds to the theory of ambiguous loss. The results showed that health care professionals recognize fetal CHD diagnosis as an external trigger for ambiguous loss in women, suggesting the importance of interventions targeting this unresolved grief.

title: Primary Systemic Carnitine Deficiency Complicated With Severe Cardiomyopathy: A Case Report.
authorString: Luo X, Luo J.
abstractText: We report a 6-year-2-month-old girl with SLC22A5-related PSCD presenting with severe cardiomyopathy, pneumonia, and anemia. Trio-WES confirmed the c.338G>A homozygous variant. L-carnitine replacement, combined with standard heart-failure therapy, was followed by prominent cardiac recovery, alerting clinicians to suspect PSCD in unexplained pediatric cardiomyopathy accompanied by hepatosplenomegaly and anemia.

title: Dual Gut Microbiota-Dependent Mechanisms Underlying the Anti-Atherosclerotic Effect of Tilianin.
authorString: Ruan X, Liu R, Cao W, Wang L, Guo M, He Z, Zhang Y, Luo Y, Gao Y, Huang C, Zhao Y, Yuan Y, Song X, Wang X.
abstractText: Tilianin (Til), a flavonoid from Dracocephalum moldavica L. and Agastache species, exerts potent anti-atherosclerotic effects via gut microbiota-mediated mechanisms. In atherosclerotic mice, Til dose-dependently reduced plaque burden and enhanced plaque stability by reducing necrotic cores and increasing collagen. Til also improved lipid profiles, attenuated inflammation, and lowered trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) levels, accompanied by microbiota remodeling-specifically, enhancing α-diversity and enriching Akkermansia muciniphila. Fecal microbiota transplantation from Til-treated donors successfully transferred these protective phenotypes. Conversely, antibiotic-induced microbiota depletion selectively abrogated the plaque-stabilizing arm of Til's action, leaving its effect on overall plaque burden intact, despite maximized TMAO reduction and increased systemic exposure. This "antibiotic paradox" stemmed from short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) depletion and intestinal barrier breakdown (decreased ZO-1/occludin), triggering metabolic endotoxemia (elevated LPS). Mechanistically, Til directly inhibits microbial trimethylamine monooxygenase (TMM) with nanomolar potency (IC50 = 18.78 nM), blocking local TMA-to-TMAO conversion. Overall, Til's lipid-lowering, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant activities in vivo are gated by a pivotal microbiota-metabolite-barrier axis, acting through dual enzymatic inhibition and homeostasis maintenance, offering novel insights for flavonoid-based multi-target atherosclerosis therapies.

title: Identifying Structural Heart Disease and Prioritizing Echocardiography Through Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Tele-ECG: An External Validation of the PROVAR+ Study.
authorString: Borges E Reges R, Vinhal WC, Pedroso AF, Cardoso CS, Oliveira CR, Brant LCC, Paixão GMM, Sable C, Dhingra LS, Shankar SV, Ribeiro I, Abreu LP, Pires M, Orto FTCD, Sena MD, Souza IS, Dos Santos BAA, de Paula LH, Angelo GR, Gomes PR, Rodrigues SMAF, Lopes RD, Ribeiro ALP, Khera R, Nascimento BR.
abstractText: Structural heart disease (SHD) is underdiagnosed where echocardiography access is limited. We evaluated the role of artificial intelligence-enabled ECG for SHD detection (AI-ECG-SHD) in cardiovascular screening. We prospectively enrolled adults undergoing public-system cardiovascular screening in two Brazilian cities. Participants underwent clinical assessment, digital 12-lead tele-ECG, and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) interpreted by cardiologists. ECG signals were analyzed using a validated AI-ECG-SHD algorithm through an application programming interface. SHD was defined as moderate/severe ventricular dysfunction/hypertrophy, wall-motion abnormalities, moderate/severe valvular disease, congenital heart disease, or pericardial disease. AI-ECG-SHD performance was assessed at a predefined threshold and discrimination compared with a model incorporating clinical variables and major conventional ECG abnormalities. Number needed to screen (NNS) was calculated. Among 3,779 participants (median age 66 years; 56.7% women), 58.7% screened AI-ECG-SHD-positive and 24.2% had TTE-detected SHD. Major ECG abnormalities (OR=3.73), age (OR=1.22/10-years), male sex (OR=1.50), Chagas disease (OR=1.89), coronary disease (OR=3.01), and heart failure (OR=1.33) independently predicted SHD. AI-ECG-SHD probability (each 10% increase) was strongly associated with SHD (OR 1.55, 95%CI 1.51-1.61; p<0.001) and showed superior discrimination versus the conventional model (AUC 0.80, 95%CI 0.78-0.82 vs 0.75, 95%CI 0.74-0.77; p<0.001). AI-ECG-SHD achieved 59.4% accuracy, 87.3% sensitivity, 50.4% specificity, 92.6% negative-predictive value, diagnostic odds ratio 7.00, and NNS 4.7. AI-guided prioritization reduced estimated time to diagnosis of 50% of SHD cases from 407 to 172 days under fixed TTE capacity. In conclusion, AI-ECG-SHD improved SHD detection over conventional prediction and may enable scalable, resource-efficient TTE prioritization in underserved public healthcare systems.

title: Impact of Coexisting Adenomyosis on the Histopathological, Immunohistochemical, and Molecular Features of Endometrial Cancer and on Adjuvant Therapy Allocation: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: D'Asta M, Monaco C, Gulino FA, Ettore C, Incognito GG, Ettore G.
abstractText:
Background and aims

Adenomyosis is frequently found in hysterectomy specimens of women with endometrial cancer (EC), but its relationship with tumor characteristics remains debated. This study aimed to compare the histopathological, immunohistochemical (IHC) and molecular features of EC, and the allocation of adjuvant therapy, between patients with and without coexisting adenomyosis.

Methods

Single-center retrospective cohort study of consecutive women who underwent hysterectomy for EC at ARNAS Garibaldi Nesima, Catania, Italy, between January 2023 and September 2024, with complete IHC and molecular profiling. Adenomyosis was defined histopathologically. FIGO 2023 stage, histotype and grade, myometrial invasion, lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI), nodal status, p53 and p16 expression, POLE, mismatch repair (MMR), KRAS and PIK3CA status, and adjuvant therapy were compared using Fisher's exact and chi-square tests, with odds ratio (OR) and 95% confidence interval (CI).

Results

Of 87 patients, 27 (31.0%) had coexisting adenomyosis. Adenomyosis was associated with FIGO stage I (81.5% vs. 46.7%; OR 5.03, 95% CI 1.68-15.04; p = 0.003), myometrial invasion < 50% (66.7% vs. 35.0%; OR 3.71, 95% CI 1.42-9.70; p = 0.010), absent/focal LVSI (77.8% vs. 50.0%; OR 3.50, 95% CI 1.24-9.89; p = 0.019) and a lower proportion of grade 3 endometrioid tumors (3.7% vs. 26.7%; p = 0.017). No differences were observed in nodal status or in p53, p16, POLE, MMR, KRAS, or PIK3CA status. Fewer patients with adenomyosis received adjuvant therapy (29.6% vs. 58.3%; OR 0.30, 95% CI 0.11-0.80; p = 0.020). Multivariable adjustment was not feasible given the sample size.

Conclusion

In this cohort, coexisting adenomyosis was associated with earlier-stage, less invasive EC and, consistently, with less frequent allocation to adjuvant therapy. These are univariate associations from a small, single-center retrospective series without survival data; they do not establish an independent or causal effect of adenomyosis and require confirmation in larger prospective multicenter studies.

title: CHST3 Skeletal Dysplasia and GRIA3 Neurodevelopmental Disorder: A Dual Diagnosis With a Recurrent Syrian CHST3 Variant.
authorString: Hashemi B, Nkrumah EAF.
abstractText: CHST3-related skeletal dysplasia is a rare autosomal recessive skeletal disorder characterized by disproportionate short stature, progressive skeletal abnormalities, and congenital joint dislocations, typically with preserved cognitive function. We report a Syrian boy presenting with severe skeletal dysplasia, epilepsy, profound developmental delay, and intellectual disability. Clinical evaluation and trio exome sequencing identified a homozygous recurrent pathogenic variant in CHST3 and a de novo likely pathogenic splice-site variant in GRIA3. The skeletal manifestations, including the pattern of dysplasia, were consistent with CHST3-related disease. However, the severity of the neurodevelopmental phenotype and epilepsy were not explained by CHST3 deficiency alone and were more consistent with a GRIA3-related neurodevelopmental disorder. This case illustrates the importance of considering dual molecular diagnoses when a patient's phenotype extends beyond the expected clinical spectrum of a known genetic condition. Furthermore, it provides additional evidence supporting the pathogenicity of a recurrent CHST3 variant observed in individuals of Syrian ancestry, suggesting a possible founder effect. Recognition of blended phenotypes resulting from multiple genetic diagnoses is essential to avoid inappropriate expansion of disease phenotypes and to ensure accurate genetic counseling and clinical management.

title: Automated Prediction of Diabetes-Related Foot Ulcer Healing at Initial Assessment.
authorString: Sari NN, Ngo QC, Ogrin R, Hanna S, Waller K, Polus B, MacIsaac RJ, Ekinci E, Kumar DK.

journal.title: Journal of diabetes science and technology

abstractText:
Background

Diabetes-related foot ulcers (DFUs) that fail to heal within the expected trajectory and become chronic are associated with substantial morbidity. The current clinical standard for identifying chronic DFUs relies on a <50% reduction in wound area over 4 weeks. There is a critical need for tools that can predict wound-healing outcomes at first clinical presentation to enable timely, individualised wound management. We have developed and validated TherMUL, an AI device that analyses the texture of thermal images to predict DFU healing.

Methods

Adults with neuropathic DFUs were recruited from 2 specialist foot clinics in Melbourne, Australia. TherMUL, a software-based device, was used to take thermal images during the initial visit. Texture features were extracted using grey-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) analysis. Wound-healing status at 12 weeks served as the ground-truth label for model training. A support vector machine (SVM) classifier was trained using the images from 44 healed and 24 unhealed DFUs. A separate unseen dataset was used for a preliminary feasibility assessment.

Results

The classifier achieved a mean area under the curve (AUC) of 0.635, with a sensitivity of 75.8% for predicting unhealed DFUs, and a specificity of 53% for identifying healed DFUs. In the preliminary evaluation, 5 of 7 predictions correctly matched the 12-week podiatry outcomes.

Conclusion

This study demonstrated early feasibility of using TherMUL to assist clinicians in predicting 12-week DFU healing outcomes at first clinical presentation, with moderate discriminative performance. This non-contact, point-of-care approach has the potential to support earlier identification of DFUs unlikely to heal and enable more timely, targeted wound management strategies.

title: Thymectomy Extent, Immune Recovery, and Infectious Burden After Neonatal Cardiac Surgery.
authorString: Rojas A, Katasani H, Faateh M, Potter AS, Chappell G, Mantell BS, Morales DLS, Karamlou T, Moore C.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Neonatal cardiac surgery frequently requires thymectomy, but the consequences of extensive thymic removal remain uncertain.

Methods

We retrospectively studied 105 neonates undergoing sternotomy (2015-2024), comparing infections and 6-month lymphocyte recovery after partial versus total thymectomy, with Firth regression adjusted for bypass duration and surgical era. Separate cohorts underwent paired plasma biomarker (n=8) and whole-blood RNA sequencing (n=4) analysis before and after thymectomy.

Results

Among 105 neonates, 27 underwent partial and 78 total thymectomy. Multiple infections occurred in 2 of 27 (7%) after partial and 23 of 78 (30%) after total thymectomy (P=0.02); after adjustment for bypass duration and surgical era, the association was not statistically significant (Firth-adjusted odds ratio, 2.99 [95% CI, 0.82-15.85]; P=0.10). Median lymphocyte count decreased after total but increased after partial thymectomy (change, -0.8 versus +0.9×103/μL; P=0.011). Tumor necrosis factor-α decreased in all 8 biomarker participants (unadjusted P=0.0078). RNA sequencing in 4 patients (2 partial, 2 total thymectomy) identified 835 differentially expressed genes; pre-T-cell receptor α decreased in all 4 pairs (log2 fold change, -2.50; adjusted P=6×10-6).

Conclusions

Total thymectomy was associated with reduced 6-month lymphocyte recovery and higher unadjusted odds of multiple infections. The infection association was not statistically significant after adjustment, and few events (2 of 27 after partial thymectomy) limit precision and cannot exclude a clinically important effect; these findings are hypothesis-generating. Biomarker and transcriptomic findings are exploratory and cannot distinguish thymectomy from surgery, maturation, or postoperative recovery. Prospective studies are underway to evaluate thymic preservation and autologous reimplantation.

title: Investigating Causal Relationships Between Major Mental Disorders and Hypertension Subtypes and Their Complications: A Mendelian Randomization Study

title: Achieved LDL-C Levels and Clinical Outcomes Following Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with Drug-Coated Balloons for De Novo Coronary Lesions.
authorString: Nagasaka T, Ishio S, Taniuchi R, Amanai S, Ishibashi Y, Takama N, Ishii H.
abstractText:
Aim

Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with a drug-coated balloon (DCB) is a coronary revascularization strategy; however, the prognostic impact of achieved low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels after intervention remains unclear. In this study, we aimed to understand the association between LDL-C and the clinical outcomes in patients undergoing PCI with DCB.

Methods

This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients who underwent PCI with DCB (April 2019-March 2023) and had available 6-month LDL-C data. The clinical outcomes were assessed using a 6-month landmark approach. Patients were stratified by LDL-C level (＜70, 70-＜100, and ≥ 100 mg/dL). The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and target lesion revascularization (TLR).

Results

Among 320 patients, 47.8% had LDL-C ＜70 mg/dL, 31.6% had 70-＜100 mg/dL, and 20.6% had LDL-C ≥ 100 mg/dL. The cumulative incidence of MACE and TLR was significantly higher with increasing LDL-C levels (log-rank P = 0.006 and P = 0.023, respectively), whereas all-cause mortality and myocardial infarction did not differ significantly. In a multivariate Cox regression analysis, LDL-C ≥ 100 mg/dL independently predicted TLR (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.31; 95% confidence interval, 1.16-4.61; P = 0.02). In an exploratory subgroup analysis, PCSK9 inhibitor use was associated with lower achieved LDL-C levels and reduced rates of MACE and TLR.

Conclusions

Among patients undergoing PCI with DCB, higher achieved LDL-C levels, particularly LDL-C ≥ 100 mg/dL, were independently associated with an increased TLR risk, which primarily drove the observed difference in MACE. These findings highlight the importance of optimal LDL-C management following PCI with DCB.

title: Predicting prosthetic use and survival following transfemoral amputation for peripheral arterial disease: a retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Smith S, Blackburn L, Shanmugam S.
abstractText:
Objectives

To examine associations between BLARt, CFS, prosthetic use and 24-month survival after unilateral transfemoral amputation for peripheral arterial disease.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study included 168 adults aged ≥65 years who underwent unilateral transfemoral amputation between 2019 and 2023. BLARt was analysed as a continuous score and CFS as an ordinal measure grouped as ≤4, 5 and ≥6. Prosthetic-use analyses excluded participants who had died by the relevant time point. Logistic regression, exact tests, ROC analysis, and Kaplan-Meier analysis were used.

Results

At discharge, 23 of 132 survivors (17.4%) were using a prosthesis; at 24 months, 17 of 80 survivors (21.3%) were using one. Higher BLARt scores were associated with lower odds of prosthetic use at discharge (OR 0.44, 95% CI 0.33-0.60) and 24 months (OR 0.51, 95% CI 0.37-0.69; both p<.001). Prosthetic use differed across CFS groups at both time points (p<.001), with no prosthetic users among participants with CFS ≥6. By 24 months, 88 participants (52.4%) had died. Compared with CFS ≤4, adjusted odds of death were higher for CFS 5 (OR 4.12, 95% CI 1.12-15.20) and CFS ≥6 (OR 8.40, 95% CI 1.97-35.80). CFS and the combined mortality model each had an AUC of approximately 0.71.

Conclusions

BLARt was associated with prosthetic use among survivors, while increasing frailty was strongly associated with both lower prosthetic use and higher 24-month mortality. These measures may support multidisciplinary prognostic discussion but should not be used as rigid thresholds for prosthetic rehabilitation.

title: Integrating polygenic and classical risk factors for cardiovascular risk stratification in a polish primary-care cohort.
authorString: Banach M, Stempor P, Osadnik T, Gach A, Strapagiel D, Słomka M, Skóra M, Fronczek M, Lejawa M, Goc A, Boniewska-Bernacka E, Pańczyszyn A, Lip GYH, Mikhailidis DP, Toth PP, Penson PE, Viigimaa M, Jóźwiak J.
abstractText:
Background

Polygenic risk scores (PRS) promise improved cardiovascular risk stratification, but most validation derives from UK or Nordic biobanks. The transferability of these scores to Central European populations and their incremental value over classical risk factors in routine care remain unestablished.

Objectives

To determine whether a coronary PRS derived from external European data transfers to a Polish primary-care population and adds discrimination for prevalent cardiovascular disease beyond classical risk factors.

Methods

In the nationwide Polish LIPIDOGEN2015 primary-care cohort, we derived PRS for coronary heart disease, myocardial infarction (MI) and stroke from FinnGen data with continuous shrinkage priors and applied them to imputed genotypes. We compared allele frequencies of 1397 unrelated participants with a non-Finnish European (NFE) reference and, in 1328 participants with clinical data, related the PRS to coronary artery disease (CAD), MI and stroke recorded at baseline and to a composite including death during follow-up, with and without classical risk factors or SCORE2.

Results

Allele frequencies correlated with the NFE reference (r = 0.97). Per standard deviation (SD), the coronary PRS was associated with prevalent CAD (odds ratio 1.36, 95% CI 1.11 to 1.67) and the composite endpoint (1.26, 95% CI 1.04 to 1.51), as were two validated genome-wide scores. Adding it to classical risk factors changed the area under the curve (AUC) for the composite endpoint by 0.0017 (95% CI -0.0005 to 0.0076), from 0.860 to 0.861; results with SCORE2 were similar. The study had 80% power for odds ratios per SD of 1.31 (CAD) and 1.27 (composite).

Conclusions

A coronary PRS derived from external European data retains its association with prevalent CAD without re-derivation in this Polish primary-care cohort but, in this cross-sectional, event-limited sample, adds little discrimination to classical risk factors. Its value for predicting future events in this setting remains to be tested against incident outcomes.

title: Current Status and Outcomes of Infective Endocarditis in Adults With Congenital Heart Disease in Japan　- A Nationwide JROAD-DPC Analysis.
authorString: Machino-Ohtsuka T, Osawa T, Yano Y, Kume K, Yano T, Nakai M, Kanaoka K, Sumita Y, Kawamatsu N, Ishizu T.

journal.title: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society

abstractText:
Background

Nationwide data on infective endocarditis (IE) in adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) in Japan are limited.

Methods and results

Using a nationwide Japanese administrative database (2013-2023), we identified 822 ACHD patients (median age 41 years; 32.0% female) hospitalized for IE. In-hospital mortality rate was 4.0%, and cardiac surgery was performed in 38.6%. Older age, severe CHD complexity, and pulmonary hypertension were independently associated with in-hospital death.

Conclusions

This study clarified the clinical characteristics and outcomes of IE in ACHD in Japan.

title: An integrated analytical strategy combining UPLC-QTOF-MS-based metabolomics and 16S rRNA sequencing to explore the mechanism of Shenqi Jieyu decoction in coronary heart disease complicated by depression in ApoE<sup>-/-</sup> mice.
authorString: Lu W, Zhang D, Zhang H, Fu Y, Hei Z, Song L, Wang S, He F, Wang F, Cang S.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: J Chromatogr B Analyt Technol Biomed Life Sci
journal.title: Journal of chromatography. B, Analytical technologies in the biomedical and life sciences
journal.isoabbreviation: J Chromatogr B Analyt Technol Biomed Life Sci

abstractText: Coronary heart disease combined with depression (dual-heart disorder) exhibits high morbidity and poor prognosis, lacking safe unified therapeutic agents. Shenqi Jieyu Decoction (SQJY) relieves depressive and cardiovascular symptoms in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) patients, yet its underlying multiple potential mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, an ApoE<sup>-</sup>/<sup>-</sup> mouse model of dual-heart disorder was induced via high-fat diet combined with chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS). Behavioral testing, aortic pathological staining, hippocampal neurochemistry, and ultra-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC-QTOF-MS)-based untargeted metabolomics of serum and cecal contents were integrated with 16S rRNA sequencing, establishing an integrated multi-omics workflow to examine the potential modulatory effects of SQJY and to explore its possible mechanism. Behavioral and pathological assays indicated that SQJY alleviated atherosclerosis and depression-like phenotypes, elevated hippocampal 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT), dopamine (DA) and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), and suppressed neuroinflammatory cytokines. 16S sequencing suggested SQJY remodeled dysregulated gut microbiota toward a more balanced profile. Metabolomics identified disturbed sphingolipid and glycerophospholipid metabolism as important metabolic signatures that H-SQJY group corrected more extensively in cecal content (68 of 265 metabolites) than in serum (8 of 103). Phylogenetic Investigation of Communities by Reconstruction of Unobserved States 2 (PICRUSt2)-based prediction of microbial functions was integrated, and Spearman correlation analysis showed significant associations between predicted microbial functions, differential gut microbes and lipid metabolites. Collectively, SQJY showed concurrent potential cardioprotective and antidepressant effects, possibly through restoring gut microbial homeostasis and modulating lipid metabolic disorders. These correlative and predicted findings provide preliminary evidence for the potential application of SQJY in dual-heart disorder.

title: Quantification of vortex characteristics and rupture risk assessment in abdominal aortic aneurysms using the liutex method.
authorString: Zhang FN, Cao HY, Wang YQ, Wu P.
abstractText: The blood flow of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs) is characterized by complex vortex interactions. Previous studies have found three flow types in AAAs (Type I: multiple vortices; Type II: non-helical single vortex; Type III: helical main flow channel), and Type III has strong correlation with rupture risk. However, flow pattern classification is subjective and qualitative, hindering further improvements in risk prediction. To enhance the predictive value of vortex-based metrics, three-dimensional models of 40 infrarenal AAAs (22 ruptured and 18 unruptured) were reconstructed from preoperative CTA images for computational fluid dynamics analysis. Flow pattern types and two novel quantitative vortex parameters based on Liutex method (volume vortex fraction (vVF) and directional entropy (H)) were compared between the two groups. A multiparametric rupture risk prediction model was constructed. Receiver operating characteristic curves and the area under the curve (AUC) were employed to evaluate predictive performance. Results demonstrated that vVF in the ruptured group was significantly higher (p = 0.02). Type III AAAs exhibited a median vVF of 15.29 %, significantly surpassing those of Types I and II, and a 12.5 % threshold achieved 80 % accuracy in identifying these high-risk patterns. Ruptured cases exhibited higher entropy, facilitating more granular risk stratification. Ultimately, the integrated model combining maximum diameter, flow pattern, and directional entropy achieved an AUC of 0.86 (p < 0.001). By objectively quantifying vortex structures and establishing a multiparametric prediction model, this study significantly enhances the predictive accuracy for AAA rupture, providing a reference for risk evaluation.
