title: Supradiaphragmatic Epicardial Pacemaker Implantation for Pseudoatrioventricular Block in Neonatal Long QT Syndrome: Genotype-agnostic Anesthetic Strategy Pending Genetic Diagnosis.
authorString: Maddali MM, Al-Yamani MI, Al-Abri IA, Al Aamri I, Fang ZA, Ibla JC, Still B.

journal.title: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia

abstractText: A late-preterm female neonate (35+3 weeks gestation) was delivered via emergency cesarean section due to fetal bradycardia. Electrocardiography revealed a 2:1 pseudoatrioventricular block, a wide QRS complex, and a corrected QT interval of 495 ms, a pattern typically associated with long QT syndrome type 2 (KCNH2) or type 3 (SCN5A). Additional findings included a large patent ductus arteriosus, moderate apical muscular ventricular septal defect, glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency, neonatal hypoglycemia, and hyperbilirubinemia. Following preoperative QT stabilization with intravenous magnesium sulfate, the infant underwent epicardial single-chamber permanent pacemaker implantation (VVI 120 bpm) via lower partial sternotomy, with a supradiaphragmatic pericardial generator pocket, on day of life (DOL) 4, at an operative weight of 2.37 kg. Anesthesia was administered using a genotype-agnostic total intravenous anesthesia strategy, comprising propofol and remifentanil with cisatracurium neuromuscular blockade, while avoiding volatile and QT-prolonging agents, optimizing electrolytes, and maintaining external defibrillator readiness. This approach was designed to be safe irrespective of the underlying channelopathy. No intraoperative arrhythmia was observed. Postoperative genetic testing unexpectedly identified a heterozygous KCNQ1 variant c.1273C>A p.(Leu425Met), confirming LQT1 (a potassium channelopathy), contradicting the preoperative electrocardiography-based assumption of sodium channelopathy. Device interrogation on DOL 14 confirmed satisfactory parameters, and the infant was discharged on propranolol on DOL 15 without further arrhythmic events. This case demonstrates that 2:1 pseudoatrioventricular block, typically associated with LQT2/LQT3, can manifest in LQT1, and that a genotype-agnostic total intravenous anesthesia strategy is an appropriate anesthetic approach when the genetic subtype is unknown prior to urgent neonatal long QT syndrome surgery.

title: Anesthesia Management in Pregnant Women with Cardiac Disease: A Narrative Review.
authorString: Gunaydin DB, Camgoz Eryilmaz N, Inan G.
abstractText: This review addresses the perspective of an obstetric anesthesiologist, focusing on the practical principles of peripartum anesthetic management by integrating current evidence with contemporary guideline recommendations rather than providing a comprehensive overview of cardiovascular disease during pregnancy. It also provides a clinically oriented approach to hemodynamic optimization, delivery planning, neuraxial and general anesthetic management, and the treatment of obstetric cardiac emergencies. Ultimately, this review aims to answer the question every anesthesiologist faces in daily practice: "What should the anaesthesiologist do for cardiac pregnant patient?" Cite this article as: Gunaydin DB, Camgoz Eryilmaz N, Inan G. Anesthesia management in pregnant women with cardiac disease: a narrative review. Eurasian J Med. 2026, 58(4), 1693, doi: 10.5152/eurasianjmed.2026.261693.

title: Analysis of the Routine Use of Factor VIIa in the Neonatal Arterial Switch Operation.
authorString: Jani S, Sinton JW, Nguyen K, Well A, Fraser CD, Gottlieb E.

journal.title: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia

abstractText:
Objectives

Arterial switch operation (ASO) for the correction of d-transposition of the great arteries can be associated with significant postbypass bleeding. Recombinant factor VIIa (rFVIIa) is used off-label to improve hemostasis, yet its effects on intraoperative and postoperative outcomes remain uncertain. The primary objective was to describe the frequency and severity of thrombotic complications among infants receiving rFVIIa at contemporary, lower doses; secondary objectives were to describe present-day dosing practice and to compare perioperative characteristics and postoperative outcomes between infants who did and did not receive rFVIIa.

Design

Retrospective chart review.

Setting

Quaternary Children's Hospital from July 1, 2018, to December 31, 2025.

Participants

Infants undergoing ASO for d-transposition of the great arteries, including intact ventricular septum, ventricular septal defect, and aortic arch repair.

Interventions

Not applicable.

Measurements and main results

A total of 56 patients undergoing ASO were included in the study. Forty-four patients in the cohort were male (78%). Of these, 34 (61%) received rFVIIa during their procedure, while 22 (39%) did not receive rFVIIa. The median first dose of rFVIIa was 50 (interquartile range [IQR]: 49.7-50.1) mcg/kg; 17 (50%) patients received a second dose (median: 50.0 [IQR: 48.8-50.0] mcg/kg), and 8 (23%) patients received a third dose (median: 48.4 [IQR: 27.9-50.0] mcg/kg), corresponding to a mean of 1.7 doses per treated patient. Administration varied from 6% to 84% of cases across the 3 operating surgeons (p < 0.0001). Postoperative outcomes were comparable, including chest tube output (2 v 2 mL, p = 0.511), length of stay (13 v 13 days, p = 0.731), and time to extubation (4 v 3 days, p = 0.089). Thrombotic complications occurred in 12% of patients, with no difference between groups (9% v 14%, p = 0.670). Patients receiving rFVIIa had shorter postoperative prothrombin time and lower international normalized ratio (both p < 0.001), with no difference in partial thromboplastin time.

Conclusions

This study reveals that patients receiving higher amounts of post-bypass transfusion were more likely to recieve rFVIIa, and that receipt of rFVIIa at a median dose of 50.9 mcg/kg, was not associated with additional thrombosis risk. Given the observational design and limited number of thrombotic events, these findings provide preliminary descriptive data on safety and warrant further study in larger cohorts.

title: Against All Odds: Repeated Successful Pregnancies in Two Women with Unrepaired Single-Ventricle Physiology.
authorString: Sugralimova M, Togyzbayeva K, Mukarov M, Talkhatova S, Abbay A.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur J Case Rep Intern Med
journal.title: European journal of case reports in internal medicine
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur J Case Rep Intern Med

abstractText:
Introduction

Pregnancy in women with unrepaired single-ventricle physiology is rare and associated with substantial maternal and foetal risk. Evidence regarding pregnancy outcomes in this population remains limited.

Case description

We report three successful pregnancies in two women with unrepaired double-inlet left ventricle, transposition of the great arteries and valvular/sub-valvular pulmonary stenosis. Both women were classified as modified World Health Organization class IV and received multidisciplinary care throughout pregnancy. Despite complex congenital heart disease, systemic ventricular function and oxygen saturation remained stable. All three pregnancies resulted in live births. However, foetal growth restriction, oligohydramnios, placental insufficiency, prematurity and prolonged neonatal hospitalisation occurred in all pregnancies. One patient successfully completed two consecutive pregnancies without maternal cardiovascular deterioration.

Discussion

Pulmonary outflow obstruction, relatively preserved oxygen saturation and stable systemic ventricular function may have contributed to maternal haemodynamic stability. However, substantial foetal and neonatal morbidity in all three pregnancies underscores that favourable maternal outcomes do not establish pregnancy safety in this population.

Conclusion

Carefully selected women with unrepaired single-ventricle physiology and balanced circulation may tolerate pregnancy better than expected, although foetal complications remain common. Multidisciplinary management in specialised congenital heart disease centres is essential.

Learning points

Successful pregnancy may be possible in selected women with unrepaired single-ventricle physiology and balanced circulation.Favourable maternal outcomes do not preclude foetal complications, including foetal growth restriction, prematurity and prolonged neonatal hospitalisation.Multidisciplinary management in specialised congenital heart disease centres is essential.

title: Risk-adapted first-stage patent ductus arteriosus ligation for an anomalous left brachiocephalic trunk arising from the main pulmonary artery in a critically ill neonate: a case report and literature review.
authorString: Peerapatanapong K, Samankatiwat P.

journal.title: International journal of surgery case reports

abstractText:
Introduction and importance

Anomalous origin of the brachiocephalic trunk from the main pulmonary artery (MPA) is an exceptionally rare congenital vascular anomaly. Management is not standardized, particularly in critically ill neonates.

Case presentation

A female neonate developed acute respiratory distress after birth. Echocardiography showed an atrial septal defect and a patent ductus arteriosus (PDA). Follow-up echocardiography and computed tomography angiography confirmed a right-sided aortic arch, a right-sided PDA, and an anomalous left brachiocephalic trunk arising from the MPA. The course was complicated by active infection, mechanical ventilation, liver cirrhosis, thrombocytopenia, and coagulopathy. After multidisciplinary review, PDA ligation alone was selected as a first-stage stabilization strategy to eliminate the dominant left-to-right shunt. Median sternotomy allowed exposure of the right-sided PDA and great vessels. The PDA was ligated without cardiopulmonary bypass, and the anomalous vessel was preserved. Complete PDA closure and temporary hemodynamic improvement were observed. However, after transfer back to the referring hospital, the patient died before second-stage reconstruction could be performed.

Clinical discussion

Reported strategies include vessel ligation and single-stage anatomical repair. In this neonate, definitive reconstruction was deferred because of severe systemic comorbidities and poor physiological reserve. PDA ligation may provide temporary hemodynamic stabilization in critically ill neonates; however, it did not correct the anomalous vascular anatomy or establish long-term perfusion of the cerebral circulation and the left upper extremity.

Conclusion

Treatment should be individualized according to physiological reserve. PDA ligation alone may be considered as a temporary, risk-adapted first-stage stabilization in selected high-risk neonates when complete correction is unsafe.

title: Whole blood transcriptomics atlas across human diseases.
authorString: Li M, Tatar A, Green E, Simsek E, Kahraman CY, Ceylan M, Laloglu F, Ceviz N, Tatar A, Laloglu E, Akcay G, Cadirci K, Yapca OE, Ozmen HK, Yapanoglu T, Kudas O, Simsek F, Yılmaz EPT, Senocak GNC, Doneray H, Ozden A, Cayir A, Tasar PT, Kara M, Aktaş YE, Karadavut M, Akpinar B, Calik ES, Erkut B, Akcay M, Karadeniz E, Kartal M, Disci E, Yildirgan MI, Atamanalp SS, Peksoz R, Albayrak Y, Eroglu A, Aydın Y, Gur STA, Gul M, Tekin E, Ulas AB, Senocak E, Paksoy AE, Donmez AS, Turgut MC, Ozmen O, Alper F, Guliyev HA, Albayrak B, Cinici E, Kocer I, Aydın EF, Dogan N, Gul Y, Kaya U, Topdagi YE, Kumtepe Y, Dostbil A, Kursat H, Bilge N, Cinici O, Disci E, Cevizli D, Guler MA, Ozcan H, Koca Lacin T, Sari S, Kerget B, Araz O, Tortum F, Altundas N, Aksungur N, Kara S, Ozturk G, Kaya SK, Ulku M, Can FK, Alay H, Albayrak A, Ozden K, Karatas E, Ozen MM, Gur A, Arabaci T, Yilar S, Saritas S, Ozkurt Z, Ceyhun HA, Sevinc C, Sirin MA, Sincan G, Kanjee M, Saruhan B, Eren SO, Utlu B, Tas MH, Tanriverdi E, Álvez MB, Edfors F, Kong X, Song X, Altay O, Yuksel B, Uhlen M, Shoaie S, Zhang C, Turkez H, Mardinoglu A.
abstractText: We present a WBT Atlas, comprising 4444 WBT samples across 98 distinct health conditions, enabling systematic exploration of disease-associated transcriptomic signatures. Health condition-specific profiles are characterized across immune, metabolic, and cell-type specific features at the gene, gene module, and pathway levels. By integrating matched plasma proteomics data from 1280 participants across 28 health conditions, we further assess blood RNA-protein relationships and demonstrate their complementary biological roles. By integrating RNA and protein signatures, we develop multi-class classification models that accurately distinguish among a wide range of health conditions, with integrated models consistently outperforming those based on single-omics data alone. The identified RNA and protein signatures are validated across ten independent WBT cohorts and the UK Biobank. Together, the WBT Atlas provides a genome-wide resource that enables translational discovery in precision medicine.

title: Superiority of magnetic resonance elastography and proton density fat fraction: an umbrella meta-analysis of non-invasive imaging for hepatic steatosis and fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and chronic hepatitis B.
authorString: Li X, Yang D, Yang Z.

journal.title: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery

abstractText:
Background

Various quantitative techniques based on ultrasound (US) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) have been widely used to assess hepatic steatosis and fibrosis. This study thus aimed to synthesize and critically evaluate the evidence derived from systematic reviews on the diagnostic performance of noninvasive imaging techniques including transient elastography (TE), point shear wave elastography (pSWE), two-dimensional shear wave elastography (2D-SWE), magnetic resonance elastography (MRE), controlled attenuation parameter (CAP), and proton density fat fraction (PDFF) for liver fibrosis and steatosis in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and chronic hepatitis B (CHB).

Methods

Searches were performed on PubMed, Embase, the Web of Science, and Cochrane Library from database inception until 2 March 2025, including keywords 'liver diseases', imaging', 'systematic review' and others. We included systematic reviews that comprised studies evaluating the diagnostic performance of non-invasive imaging techniques for liver fibrosis or steatosis in patients with MASLD or CHB.

Results

Thirty-five reviews were included from 3,752 articles. For hepatic steatosis assessment, PDFF demonstrated high diagnostic stability, while CAP showed good screening performance for mild steatosis. For liver fibrosis assessment, MRE exhibited high diagnostic accuracy for significant (≥F2), advanced (≥F3) fibrosis, and cirrhosis (F4). In obese MASLD patients, MRE demonstrated superior specificity compared to TE. Among CHB patients, MRE displayed particularly high diagnostic performance. Other techniques (2D-SWE, TE) remained clinically valuable in specific stages and patient populations.

Conclusions

MRE performance varied between the two etiologies, suggesting liver stiffness is a composite biomarker. PDFF provides precise quantification of steatosis, while CAP is suitable for screening mild cases. The findings emphasize the necessity of developing personalized imaging strategies based on etiology to optimize patient management and reduce reliance on liver biopsy.

title: Postoperative Mortality and Risk Factors in Adults With Congenital Heart Disease Undergoing Cardiovascular Surgery: Insights From the Japanese Registry Data.
authorString: Osawa T, Machino-Ohtsuka T, Kume K, Yano T, Saji M, Kanaoka K, Sumita Y, Yano Y, Numata R, Kawamatsu N, Kuraoka A, Kato H, Hiramatsu Y, Ishizu T.
abstractText:
Background

Patients with adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) are prone to complications and usually require surgical intervention, but the surgical risk factors remain poorly defined.

Methods and results

We analyzed data from April 2013 to March 2023 in the nationwide Japanese Registry of All Cardiac and Vascular Disease-Diagnostic Procedure Combination (JROAD-DPC) to assess postoperative cardiac death and its predictors. This study included ACHD patients aged ≥18 years who underwent cardiovascular surgery, and the primary outcome was in-hospital death. A total of 10,535 patients (median age 53 [interquartile range 36-68] years; 50.4% female) were classified into mild (n=6,831), moderate (n=2,388), and severe (n=1,316) complexity groups. Among the 146 in-hospital deaths (1.4%), the highest mortality rate was observed in patients with severe complexity (2.4%). Multivariable analysis showed that age (hazard ratio [HR] 1.15), severe complexity (HR 1.77), renal disease (HR 1.74), pulmonary hypertension requiring medications (HR 2.01), chromosome abnormality (HR 6.22), and high-risk surgery (Fontan surgery or coronary artery bypass grafting) (HR 1.67) were significantly associated with increased in-hospital deaths. Subgroup analyses showed that age, renal disease, and high-risk surgery were prognostic factors in the mild group. Age was not significant in the moderate or severe groups.

Conclusions

The in-hospital mortality rate after cardiovascular surgery in ACHD was low overall but increased with disease complexity, supporting the need for disease complexity-based, individualized risk assessments in surgical planning.

title: Left Ventricular Torsion Derived From Cardiac Cine Magnetic Resonance: Interventricular Interaction of Transcatheter Pulmonary Valve Implantation for Pulmonary Regurgitation.
authorString: Inoue A, Nagao M, Yamamoto A, Kogure T, Asagai S, Inai K, Ando R, Yamaguchi J, Sakai S.
abstractText:
Background

After tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) repair, pulmonary regurgitation (PR) frequently leads to right ventricular (RV) dilation and heart failure. Transcatheter pulmonary valve implantation (TPVI) reduces RV volume, but its impact on left ventricular (LV) function remains unclear. We hypothesized that LV torsion is a more sensitive indicator than LV ejection fraction (LVEF) and evaluated longitudinal changes in torsion using 3D cardiac cine magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) before and after TPVI.

Methods and results

30 patients with PR (25 with TOF, 4 with pulmonary artery stenosis, and 1 with double-outlet right ventricle; mean age, 42 years) underwent MRI before, 3 months, and 12 months after TPVI. LV time-torsion curves were derived from short-axis cine images using feature-tracking analysis. Torsion, biventricular function, and the PR fraction (PRF) were assessed. Torsion increased progressively (0.82±0.42 vs. 0.98±0.48 vs. 1.18±0.55 degrees/cm; all P<0.01), whereas LVEF showed no significant change (52.1±11.0% vs. 53.7±9.3% vs. 55.3±9.9%). RV end-diastolic volume index and PRF were significantly reduced at 12 months.

Conclusions

Despite unchanged LVEF, torsion improved after TPVI, reflecting LVEF-independent LV pump function and interventricular interaction.

title: Positional Obstructive Sleep Apnea in Children With Down Syndrome: Prevalence, Clinical Characteristics, and Polysomnographic Features.
authorString: Al Dhouyani B, Abu-Hasan M, Toma HM, Abushahin M, Al-Naimi AR.
abstractText:
Background

Positional obstructive sleep apnea (POSA), defined as obstructive events that occur predominantly in the supine position, is considered a phenotype of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) that requires a special diagnostic and therapeutic approach. Children with Down syndrome (DS) are at increased risk of having OSA in general and POSA in particular. However, the clinical and sleep determinants of POSA in DS are not well characterized.

Objective

To determine the prevalence of POSA in children with DS with OSA, compare the clinical and polysomnographic characteristics between POSA and non-POSA phenotypes, and identify predictors of POSA.

Methods

The study is a retrospective evaluation of the entire cohort of children with genetically confirmed DS who completed a diagnostic polysomnography study at the only pediatric sleep lab in Qatar between September 2019 and May 2026. Patients' demographic, clinical, and polysomnographic data were collected from the medical records. Only patients with OSA were included in the analysis. OSA was defined as an obstructive apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) ≥ 1.5 events/hour. OSA was considered positional (POSA) if the ratio of supine to non-supine AHI was ≥2, with at least 20 minutes of sleep recorded in both the supine and non-supine positions. Non-positional (non-POSA) if the ratio was < 2. Comparisons between POSA and non-POSA groups were made using Student's t-test for continuous variables and a chi-square test for categorical variables. Multivariable logistic regression was performed in the study population to identify potential independent predictors of POSA.

Results

A total of 151 children with DS were identified. Only 132 (87%) of the children had OSA. POSA was identified in 61 (46.2%) children and non-POSA in 71 (53.8%) children. There was no significant difference between the two groups in age, gender, weight, height, BMI, or history of snoring or witnessed apnea. There was also no significant difference between the two groups in sleep efficiency, sleep architecture, AHI, OAHI, or OSA severity. Regression analysis showed no significant clinical or PSG predictors of POSA in the study population.

Conclusions

POSA is prevalent in children with DS. However, there are no significant clinical or polysomnographic differences between POSA and non-POSA, suggesting that POSA is not a unique OSA phenotype. Further prospective and interventional studies are needed to confirm the clinical impact of POSA in DS and its treatment.

title: Eighteen Years of Complication-Free Survival Following Inadvertent Left Ventricular Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillator (ICD) Lead Placement via Atrial Septal Defect: A Case Report.
authorString: Elboraey O, Hasan S, Farooq M, Schofield I, Ahmed IM.
abstractText: Implantable cardioverter defibrillators (ICDs) are recommended for primary or secondary prevention in multiple cardiac conditions. One of the recognised complications during implantation of cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) is inadvertent lead malposition in the left heart (ILMLH), which can lead to further thromboembolism and infective endocarditis. In this paper, we present a unique case of a patient who had an accidental ICD lead implanted into the left ventricle via an atrial septal defect (ASD). Evidence on the management of such a complication is rare. A watchful-wait approach with appropriate anticoagulation was adopted here, resulting in an uneventful 18-year survival. We also navigate through the current evidence on the recognition and management of such cases.

title: Exploratory clinical predictors of prolonged hospital stay in patients with patent foramen ovale undergoing transthoracic echocardiography- or X-ray-guided closure.
authorString: Zhang P, Chen M, Dang X, Guo F, Hou X, Zhou G, Yang Y, Wei X, You T.
abstractText: Patent foramen ovale (PFO) can be managed using different image-guided treatment modalities; however, the determinants of prolonged hospitalization remain insufficiently defined. This retrospective study aimed to identify clinical predictors associated with length of hospital stay and to develop a machine learning model for predicting prolonged hospitalization in patients with PFO. Clinical data from 216 patients with PFO treated at Gansu Provincial People's Hospital were retrospectively analyzed. Among them, 106 patients underwent transthoracic echocardiography (TTE)-guided treatment and 110 underwent X-ray-guided treatment. According to the median length of stay, patients were divided into a short-stay group (≤7 days) and a prolonged-stay group (>7 days). Baseline variables were compared between groups. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for feature selection. Five machine learning algorithms were then developed and compared in the training cohort, followed by validation in an independent validation cohort. Thirteen baseline variables showed significant between-group differences. LASSO regression retained 10 candidate predictors for model construction. Among the evaluated models, the random forest model showed the best overall performance. In the validation cohort, the model achieved an accuracy of 0.692, a precision of 0.708, a recall of 0.850, an F1-score of 0.773, and an AUC of 0.711, indicating moderate discrimination. The random forest model demonstrated moderate predictive discrimination for prolonged hospital stay. Given the limited sample size and single-center retrospective design, the model should be considered exploratory and requires external validation in larger independent cohorts before clinical use.

title: Hyperreactivity of Pulmonary Vasculature in Children With Pulmonary Hypertension at Altitude and the Importance of the Prolonged Hyperoxia Test (O<sub>2</sub>Test).
authorString: Diaz G GF, Ruiz-Parra A, Ulrich S, Márquez A.
abstractText: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is defined hemodynamically, but pulmonary vascular reversibility may provide additional prognostic information, particularly in children exposed to chronic hypobaric hypoxia. We retrospectively analyzed 85 patients diagnosed with PH during childhood at high altitude in Bogotá, Colombia (2,640 m). Seventy-seven underwent cardiac catheterization and 78 underwent a prolonged hyperoxia test (O2Test), consisting of supplemental oxygen at FiO2 > 0.80 for 4-24 h with echocardiographic assessment of pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP). A > 20% reduction in baseline PASP was considered a positive response. Seventy-two patients (84.7%) had severe PH. Among the 78 patients undergoing O2Testing, 49 (62.8%) had a positive response. Patients with a positive O2Test were younger at diagnosis than nonresponders (median, 2 vs. 7 years; p = 0.0061), had lower mean pulmonary artery pressure (55 vs. 83 mmHg; p = 0.0047), and were more frequently in World Health Organization functional class I-II. A negative O2Test was substantially more frequent among patients who died than among survivors (74.1% vs. 17.6%; p < 0.001). Patients with the longest follow-up were predominantly diagnosed before 3 years of age and demonstrated preserved pulmonary vascular reactivity. These findings suggest that pulmonary vascular reactivity to prolonged hyperoxia is associated with age at diagnosis, hemodynamic severity, functional status, and long-term outcome in children with PH living at high altitude. The O2Test may provide complementary information to conventional acute vasoreactivity testing in this population.

title: Immediate and long-term outcomes of aortic commissurotomy for severe congenital aortic valve stenosis in infants: a single-center experience.
authorString: Rączka M, Kuźma J, Rudziński A, Weryński P, Kołcz J, Mroczek T, Skalski J, Morka A.

journal.title: Kardiochirurgia i torakochirurgia polska = Polish journal of cardio-thoracic surgery

abstractText:
Introduction

Severe congenital aortic valve stenosis (AVS) in infants constitutes a significant therapeutic challenge. Currently, two methods are mostly used as first-line therapy: balloon aortic valvuloplasty (BAV) and surgical aortic valvotomy (SAV). In critically ill neonates, BAV is preferred as a less invasive procedure. If BAV fails, SAV remains an indispensable option.

Aim

To evaluate retrospectively the immediate and long-term outcomes of SAV as a primary procedure or re-intervention (after BAV) in infants with severe AVS.

Material and methods

SAV results were retrospectively analyzed in 23 children (including 3 born prematurely), operated on in the first year of life. Patients were divided into two groups: Gr-I (n = 9) infants with prior BAV and Gr-II (n = 14) infants who underwent SAV as the primary intervention. BAV was performed at a median age of 4 days, while SAV was performed at a median age of 50 days in Gr-I and 33 days in Gr-II. The mean follow-up period was 12.3 years.

Results

Postoperative echocardiography showed a reduction in transvalvular pressure gradient (TVPG) and an increase in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) in both groups. During hospitalization 10 (43.5%) infants developed various complications, which occurred more frequently in Gr-I. After SAV, 4 children (all from Gr-II) required 5 various re-interventions. One patient (Gr-I) died due to septicemia. In follow-up, 22 children were doing well and remained under outpatient supervision.

Conclusions

SAV as the first-line treatment or re-treatment after BAV in infants with severe AVS was associated with satisfactory outcomes. Both methods may complement each other, potentially delaying definitive aortic valve replacement.

title: Cardiac rehabilitation: from historical milestones to technological integration and global implementation.
authorString: Ibrahimi A, Mulita F, Dogjani A, Androutsopoulou V, Liolis E, Nikolakopoulos K, Schizas D, Papathanasiou J, Baikoussis N, Leivaditis V.

journal.title: Kardiochirurgia i torakochirurgia polska = Polish journal of cardio-thoracic surgery

abstractText: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain the leading cause of death globally, accounting for approximately 20.5 million deaths annually, with a disproportionate burden in low- and middle-income countries. As the prevalence of CVD continues to increase, cardiac rehabilitation (CR) has emerged as a cornerstone of secondary prevention and long-term management. This narrative review examines the historical evolution, current practices, and future directions of CR, with particular emphasis on patients undergoing cardiac surgery - a population with unique recovery challenges and increased vulnerability. Global case studies illustrate the diversity of CR systems, and emerging trends such as telehealth, artificial intelligence, and culturally adapted care are discussed as tools to expand access and personalize care. Barriers to CR implementation - including socioeconomic inequities, referral gaps, and policy limitations - are analyzed, alongside proposed solutions supported by implementation science frameworks. The review concludes that expanding and modernizing CR programs is both a clinical imperative and a global health priority.

title: The GIPMER 3-Method (Blood-Hegar-Silk) Approach for intraoperative localization of apical muscular ventricular septal defects via limited right ventricular apical ventriculotomy: a five-patient case series.
authorString: Singh A, Sharma P, Asati S, Marvania S, Sharma V.

journal.title: Kardiochirurgia i torakochirurgia polska = Polish journal of cardio-thoracic surgery

abstractText:
Introduction

Apical muscular ventricular septal defects (VSDs) are surgically challenging because of their deep location within the trabeculated right ventricle, often resulting in difficult intraoperative localization and residual shunting.

Aim

This study reports the early feasibility of a structured three-step intraoperative localization strategy, termed the GIPMER 3-Method Approach (Govind Ballabh Pant Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education & Research), developed to assist in identifying apical muscular VSDs during surgical repair.

Material and methods

This single-center prospective feasibility case series included 5 pediatric patients with apical muscular VSDs who underwent surgical closure over a one-year period following standard preoperative evaluation. A structured three-step intraoperative localization strategy (the GIPMER 3-Method) was applied via a limited right ventricular apical ventriculotomy. Outcomes were assessed using intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) and postoperative transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) at 48 hours and at 1 month.

Results

Complete closure was achieved in all 5 patients, with no residual VSD detected on intraoperative or early postoperative imaging. Median cardiopulmonary bypass time was 78 minutes (range: 70-90), and median aortic cross-clamp time was 42 minutes (range: 35-50). No major early postoperative complications, including arrhythmias or low cardiac output, were observed.

Conclusions

In this small prospective case series, the GIPMER 3-Method Approach demonstrated technical feasibility for early localization of apical muscular VSDs. While early outcomes were favorable, these results should be interpreted as preliminary, and larger studies with longer follow-up are required to evaluate safety, durability, and comparative effectiveness against established techniques.

title: Exercise capacity in school-aged children after surgical correction of congenital heart defects in infancy.
authorString: Zielińska AK, Wasilewski J, Ewertowska P, Łuszczyk M, Haponiuk-Skwarlińska J, Paczkowski K, Gierat-Haponiuk K, Leszczyńska K, Chojnicki M, Tuptanowski K, Staniak A, Jankowski B, Haponiuk I.

journal.title: Kardiochirurgia i torakochirurgia polska = Polish journal of cardio-thoracic surgery

abstractText:
Introduction

Despite successful early surgical correction of congenital heart defects, reduced exercise capacity may be observed in children. Functional assessment using cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) enables an objective evaluation of cardiovascular and respiratory responses to exercise.

Aim

The aim of the study was to assess the physical performance of children in the long-term period after surgical correction of ventricular and atrial septal defects (VSD/ASD) compared with healthy peers.

Material and methods

The study included 45 children aged 9-11 years: 20 after surgical correction of VSD/ASD and 25 healthy controls. Exercise capacity was evaluated using a modified Godfrey protocol. Parameters analysed included WRpeak, VO2peak, VEpeak, METpeak, VCO2peak, RERpeak, HRpeak, and VO2-pulsepeak. Statistical analysis was performed using Student's t-test or the Mann-Whitney U test, with a significance level of p < 0.05.

Results

Children after surgical correction of congenital heart defects achieved significantly lower WRpeak, VO2peak, VEpeak, and METpeak values compared with controls (p < 0.05). No significant differences were observed in RERpeak, indicating comparable maximal effort levels. When expressed as a percentage of predicted values, the operated group demonstrated lower physical performance and impaired cardiopulmonary adaptation to exercise.

Conclusions

Despite successful early anatomical correction, children after surgical repair of congenital heart defects exhibit decreased exercise capacity compared with healthy peers. These findings emphasize the need for long-term monitoring and the introduction of tailored physical rehabilitation programmes as part of postoperative care to improve physical fitness.

title: Isolated partial anomalous pulmonary venous return with severe mitral stenosis managed successfully by a modified Warden procedure and mitral valve replacement: a rare case report.
authorString: Rizvi SA, Siddique S, Aslam H, Javaid MH, Aminpoor H, Karimi H.

journal.title: International journal of surgery case reports

abstractText:
Background

Partial anomalous pulmonary venous return (PAPVR) is a very rare condition, with an incidence ranging from 0.4% to 0.7% in autopsy series. Isolated PAPVR without autism spectrum disorder is extremely rare, accounting for less than 10% of all PAPVR.

Case presentation

The patient was a 40-year-old female with isolated PAPVR, rheumatic heart disease, and hypertension who presented with New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class IV symptoms 15 years after failed percutaneous transvenous mitral commissurotomy. Multimodality imaging showed anomalous drainage of the right superior pulmonary vein into the superior vena cava (SVC) with aneurysmal dilation (65 × 35 mm), a marked left-to-right shunt (pulmonary blood flow to systemic blood flow ratio of 7.25), and severe mitral stenosis (mitral valve area 0.8 cm2; a Wilkins score of 9/16). She underwent a modified Warden procedure and mechanical mitral valve replacement using a 27 mm bileaflet valve. The postoperative course was uneventful. After 12 months, she improved to NYHA Class I, with a prosthetic mean gradient of 4 mmHg, a normal right ventricular size, and a low systolic pulmonary artery pressure (38 mmHg). No arrhythmias, SVC obstruction, or prosthetic dysfunction were noted.

Conclusion

This is an example of the complicated hemodynamic relationship between PAPVR and severe rheumatic mitral stenosis. The two conditions can be repaired together successfully with careful multimodality imaging assessment and an individualized surgical plan.

title: Delayed presentation of type I jejunal atresia radiologically mimicking malrotation in an infant with Down syndrome and congenital heart disease: a case report.
authorString: Abrishami M, Khanghah AS, Savadi H, Boskabadi A, Sarsarabi AH, Atqiaee K.

journal.title: International journal of surgery case reports

abstractText:
Background

Type I jejunal atresia presenting beyond the neonatal period is exceptionally rare and may mimic other obstructive gastrointestinal pathologies. Concurrent syndromic and cardiopulmonary comorbidities add substantial complexity to diagnosis and perioperative management.

Case presentation

A 2-month-old male infant with Down syndrome and complex congenital heart disease (large patent ductus arteriosus, atrial septal defect, ventricular septal defect, and moderate mitral and tricuspid regurgitation) presented with a 3-week history of progressive bilious vomiting and acute-onset, severe metabolic acidosis. Preoperative upper gastrointestinal contrast study demonstrated delayed transit with proximal dilatation, raising concern for intestinal malrotation. Cardiac surgery had been deferred due to a preceding episode of culture-negative sepsis. Exploratory laparotomy revealed a type I jejunal atresia (intraluminal web) located approximately 20 cm distal to the ligament of Treitz, with no intraoperative evidence of malrotation or volvulus. A short-segment bowel resection with primary end-to-end anastomosis was performed.

Conclusion

Late-presenting type I jejunal atresia can radiologically simulate malrotation, particularly when chronic partial obstruction has produced marked proximal dilatation. In syndromic neonates and infants with significant cardiopulmonary disease, a structured multidisciplinary approach - including aggressive metabolic resuscitation and appropriately timed surgical intervention - is essential for optimizing outcomes.

title: Prognostic Implications of Clinically Attributed Left Atrial Enlargement Subtypes in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
authorString: Sato T, Ito A, Kitagawa Y, Ito S, Yamaura H, Okamoto A, Nomura N, Yamaguchi T, Kagawa S, Ogawa M, Shimada T, Ishikawa S, Hayashi Y, Shibata A, Otsuka K, Fukuda D.
abstractText:
Background

Left atrial enlargement (LAE) is common in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), but its prognostic significance may vary according to the clinical drivers of atrial remodeling. We examined whether prognostic factors differ by clinically attributed LAE subtype in patients undergoing TAVI with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF).

Methods and results

We retrospectively analyzed 317 consecutive patients with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis (AS) undergoing TAVI who had preserved LVEF and LAE. Patients were classified as AS-associated LAE (no atrial fibrillation [AF] and ConclusionsPrognostic markers after TAVI differ by clinically attributed LAE subtype, supporting subtype-informed risk stratification.

title: The palliative care needs of adolescents and young adults with a life limiting condition: a systematic review.
authorString: Linane H, Allen J, O'Reilly M, Sullivan L, Molcho M.
abstractText:
Background

Adolescence and young adulthood is characterised by complex developmental and psychosocial changes. The diagnosis of a life-limiting condition adds complexity and stress to this already turbulent period of life. Provision of developmentally appropriate palliative care to this group necessitates an understanding of the palliative care needs specific to this group. The aim of this study is to identify existing evidence about the palliative care needs of adolescents and young adults with a life-limiting condition (both cancer and non-cancer conditions).

Methods

This systematic review was carried out according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Protocols (PRISMA) guidelines. Six databases were searched from time of inception until 18th December 2025. The databases searched included Pubmed, Scopus, CINAHL (EBSCO), Ovid MEDLINE, PsycINFO (EBSCO) and the Web of Science Core Collection. Articles were screened and extracted. Key themes were identified within and across articles.

Results

In total, twelve articles (nine qualitative and three quantitative studies) were included. Nine of the included studies focused on adolescents and young adults with cancer, while the remaining three studies focused on non-cancer conditions. Analyses generated five themes: (i) Shared core palliative care need domains, (ii) Parent and peer relationships, (iii) Normalcy, (iv) An adapted approach to communication and decision making, and (v) Continuity and coordination of health services.

Conclusions

This systematic review outlines the evidence on palliative care needs specific to adolescents and young adults with a life-limiting condition. These findings will support advancement of developmentally appropriate palliative care supports for this group.

title: Nineteen-year experience with total anomalous pulmonary venous return at a tertiary care hospital in a low- and middle-income country: a single-centre retrospective study.
authorString: Ahmad W, Sadqani SA, Shahid AH, Amir SM, Salman M, Anns KM, Hassan SMD, Malik M, Amanullah M.
abstractText:
Introduction

Total Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Return (TAPVR) is a rare congenital defect requiring surgical correction. Outcomes are influenced by associated anomalies and preoperative pulmonary venous obstruction, which increase morbidity, mortality, and postoperative pulmonary hypertension risk. This study reviews our institutional experience with pediatric TAPVR repair, emphasizing postoperative outcomes and prognostic determinants.

Methodology

This single-centre retrospective cohort (2006-2024) at Aga Khan University Hospital included pediatric TAPVR patients (< 18 years). Preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative data were analyzed. Continuous variables summarized as mean/SD or median/IQR and categorical as frequencies, with appropriate statistical tests applied.

Results

Our cohort included 80 patients (65% male, mean weight 7.6 ± 6.3 kg). Subtypes were supracardiac 43.8%, cardiac 35%, infracardiac 6.3%, and mixed 15%. Mean age at presentation was 20.1 ± 38.5 months, with 55.6 ± 80.5 days to surgery. ASD (86.3%) was most common. Median CPB and cross-clamp times were 90 and 45 min, respectively. Open-chest (23.8%) and extracorporeal support (70%) showed no subtype significance. Median hospital stay was 8 (9) days with CICU stay as 4 (6). Postoperative outcomes included PAH (22.5%), sepsis (18.8%), PVO (6.3%), tracheostomy (7.5%), reoperation (5%) and mortality reported in 17.5% (higher in cardiac TAPVR, p = 0.044). Univariate analysis linked younger age, low weight, TAPVD subtype, postop PVO, and reduced RV function to outcomes; multivariate confirmed only reduced RV function. While preop PVO was significantly associated with postoperative PAH.

Conclusion

TAPVR repair yielded favourable outcomes; however vigilant monitoring of RV function and preoperative PVO is essential to improve survival and reduce complications.

title: Postoperative complications from alcohol use disorder in an adult congenital heart disease patient: a case report emphasizing the role of high-complexity congenital centers.
authorString: Alexander B, Greiten L, Sanders E.
abstractText:
Background

Superior sinus venous atrial septal defect (SVASD) associated with partial anomalous pulmonary venous return (PAPVR) is a rare congenital heart disease that is predominantly diagnosed and surgically treated in childhood; however, sometimes the diagnosis is delayed and requires intervention in adulthood.

Case presentation

A 69-year-old patient presented to the adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) clinic due to shortness of breath and recurrent syncopal episodes and was found to have significant right ventricular enlargement by echocardiogram of undetermined cause. Cardiac CT detected a large SVASD with PAPVR that required surgical intervention. The postoperative course was complicated by delirium tremens.

Conclusions

ACHD patients often have many comorbidities that are not commonly seen in the pediatric population. Because of this, it is of utmost importance that pediatric surgical centers offering procedures for ACHD patients have established protocols to manage these comorbidities postoperatively, including substance withdrawal symptoms.

title: Single-stage repair of tetralogy of Fallot with partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection in an adult: a case report.
authorString: Tang H, Luo J, An Q, Tang M, Ling Y.
abstractText:
Background

Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) with partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection (PAPVC) is rare and may be missed preoperatively, which may produce persistent right heart volume overload and contribute to right ventricular dilatation and dysfunction after TOF repair. Reports of this combination in adults with unrepaired TOF remain limited.

Case presentation

A 24-year-old woman with congenital heart disease diagnosed in childhood presented with exertional fatigue and dyspnea relieved by squatting. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated TOF, a superior sinus venosus atrial septal defect, and incomplete visualization of the pulmonary veins. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) with three-dimensional reconstruction confirmed anomalous drainage of the right upper pulmonary vein into the superior vena cava (SVC). Single-stage repair was successfully performed, comprising TOF repair, a modified Warden procedure, and tricuspid valvuloplasty. Central venous pressure was 9 mmHg postoperatively, with no rhythm disturbance. Short-term follow-up indicated unobstructed venous pathways, with no residual intracardiac shunting, normal left ventricular systolic function, and no rhythm abnormalities.

Conclusion

This case highlights the importance of careful preoperative assessment of pulmonary venous anatomy in TOF. Single-stage repair was feasible and can achieve a favorable short-term outcome.

title: Aberrant cerebrovascular reactivity presents as an early biomarker of psychosis susceptibility in patients with 22q11.2DS.
authorString: Delavari F, Moia S, Forrer S, Sandini C, Kojovic N, Pascucci A, Lacour C, Eliez S, Van De Ville D.
abstractText: The brain's ability to regulate blood flow is fundamental to both its function and development. In the context of neurodevelopmental disorders such as schizophrenia, understanding the complex interactions between cerebrovascular health and brain function is crucial for unraveling the pathophysiology of psychosis. This study investigates the developmental trajectory of cerebrovascular reactivity (CVR) in 22q11 deletion syndrome (22q11.2DS) compared to healthy controls, and its association with psychosis susceptibility. Using one of the largest longitudinal data-set of resting-state fMRI, we mapped for the first time voxel-level CVR across development. We found an early reduction in CVR in 22q11.2DS, and in particular in those who later developed positive psychotic symptoms (PPS + ). These reductions were evident within the anterior cingulate cortex, frontal lobes, and globi pallidi (GP). We propose that the pattern of CVR alterations presenting early during childhood is possibly linked to altered blood-brain barrier integrity or permeability, potentially involving endothelial or tight-junction dysfunction; however, BBB integrity was not directly measured in this study. A decrease in CVR during childhood and within the frontal regions and GP was predictive of subsequent development of positive psychotic symptoms), which often occurs during adolescence in 22q11.2DS patients. These findings suggest that cerebrovascular health is critical for normal brain development, particularly in regions like the striatum, which are vulnerable to vascular damage due to their anatomical features. These results underline the potential of CVR as an early biomarker for psychosis vulnerability, emphasizing the need for targeted interventions to mitigate neurodevelopmental disruptions of cerebrovascular health in 22q11.2DS.

title: Gut microbiome and metabolite profiling in term SGA infants: a multi-omics approach to physical development.
authorString: Li S, Yu Z, Jin Y, Ma K, Sha L, Qian M, Chen X, Han S.
abstractText:
Introduction

Early-life gut microbial composition and fecal metabolic profiles may be altered in infants born small for gestational age (SGA), but evidence specifically concerning term SGA infants remains limited.

Objectives

To characterize gut microbial composition, predicted microbial functions, and fecal metabolite profiles in term SGA infants and explore their associations with early growth.

Methods

This prospective nested case-control study included 62 term infants (31 SGA and 31 appropriate for gestational age [AGA]). Fecal samples were collected at 3 months. Untargeted metabolomics was performed in the full cohort, and shotgun metagenomic sequencing was conducted in a nested subset of 20 infants (10 SGA and 10 AGA). Differential taxa, KEGG orthologs (KOs), metabolites, and cross-omics correlations were analyzed.

Results

Alpha diversity did not differ significantly between groups, whereas microbial composition and species-level abundance patterns differed between SGA and AGA infants. Functional analysis identified 135 differential KOs, including 36 with higher and 99 with lower abundance in the SGA group. These KOs were mapped to 25 metabolic pathways, including galactose, butanoate, D-amino acid, aromatic amino acid, fructose-mannose, pyruvate, propanoate, and lipid metabolism. Twelve fecal metabolite features differed between groups, including 5'-methylthioadenosine, taurocholate, β-alanine, and 17α-hydroxypregnanolone. Exploratory integration identified connections among microbial species, KOs, and metabolites. Several microbial and metabolite features showed nominal associations with 6-month growth indices, but most cross-omics and metabolite-growth associations did not remain significant after false discovery rate correction.

Conclusions

Term SGA infants showed differences in gut microbial composition, predicted metabolic potential, and fecal metabolite profiles at 3 months. Associations with subsequent growth were exploratory and require validation in larger longitudinal studies.

title: Association of maternal serum ferritin stratification with metabolic phenotypes and pregnancy outcomes: a single-center retrospective observational study.
authorString: Wang P, Yao J, Li Y, Zhang Z, Li L, Huang X, Zeng J.
abstractText:
Background

This study aimed to systematically investigate the associations of maternal serum ferritin (SF) stratification with lipid metabolism markers, including triglycerides (TG) and total cholesterol (CH); glucose metabolism markers, including glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) and abnormal glucose tolerance; coagulation/vascular-related markers, including D-dimer and homocysteine (HCY); and vitamin D status, assessed by 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D]. Complete blood count-related parameters and pregnancy outcomes were also incorporated to provide evidence for identifying metabolic phenotypes and supporting risk assessment during pregnancy.

Methods

This retrospective study included 1,606 singleton pregnant women who underwent antenatal care between January 2023 and October 2024. Participants were categorized into three groups according to SF levels: low ferritin group (SF < 15 µg/L, n = 609), intermediate ferritin group (15 ≤ SF < 30 µg/L, n = 422), and relatively high ferritin group (SF ≥ 30 µg/L, n = 575). Between-group differences were assessed using the Kruskal-Wallis test, and correlations among biomarkers were evaluated using Spearman correlation analysis. Multivariable linear regression and logistic regression models were used to adjust for potential confounders, including age, body mass index (BMI), gravidity, and complete blood count-related parameters, including WBC, NLR, PLT, Hb, MCV, and RDW-SD.

Results

The low SF group showed higher levels of TG (2.84 vs. 1.78 mmol/L), CH (5.94 vs. 4.82 mmol/L), D-dimer (1.76 vs. 1.54 mg/L), and HCY (7.31 vs. 6.36 µmol/L), together with lower 25(OH)D levels (15.05 vs. 16.96 ng/mL), compared with the SF ≥ 30 µg/L group. In fully adjusted models, compared with the SF < 15 µg/L group, the SF ≥ 30 µg/L group remained associated with lower TG, CH, D-dimer, and HCY levels and higher 25(OH)D levels. The prevalence of abnormal glucose tolerance increased across SF categories (18.4%, 24.6%, and 32.0%, respectively). After full adjustment, the SF ≥ 30 µg/L group still had a significantly higher risk of abnormal glucose tolerance (OR = 2.13, 95% CI: 1.58-2.87, P < 0.001). Sensitivity analyses using alternative SF cut-offs, excluding participants in the highest 5% of NLR, excluding participants with BMI < 15 kg/m², and applying log-transformation to skewed variables showed generally consistent directions of the main findings. Exploratory analyses of pregnancy outcomes suggested that the SF ≥ 30 µg/L group had higher risks of preterm birth and hypertensive-related diagnoses and slightly lower birth weight, whereas the prevalence of GDM diagnosis and macrosomia did not differ significantly across the three groups.

Conclusions

SF stratification may help identify distinct metabolic phenotypes during pregnancy. Low SF status was more likely to be accompanied by higher lipid, D-dimer, and HCY levels and lower 25(OH)D levels, whereas relatively higher SF status was associated with an increased risk of abnormal glucose tolerance. This retrospective observational study is hypothesis-generating and does not support causal inference or direct intervention recommendations. Future studies incorporating OGTT glucose values at each time point and abnormality patterns, inflammatory markers, comprehensive iron metabolism indicators, and prospective pregnancy outcome data are needed to further validate the clinical value of SF stratification in metabolic risk assessment during pregnancy.

title: Incomplete Shone's complex as a rare cardiac manifestation of Coffin-Lowry syndrome: a case report.
authorString: Gužauskaitė G, Sendžikaitė S, Burnytė B.
abstractText:
Background

Coffin-Lowry syndrome is a rare X-linked genetic disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the RPS6KA3 gene, characterized by distinctive craniofacial features, skeletal abnormalities, and neurodevelopmental impairment. Although cardiac involvement has been reported in Coffin-Lowry syndrome, it most commonly manifests as cardiomyopathy or valvular insufficiency. To the best of our knowledge, Coffin-Lowry syndrome has not been associated with obstructive left-sided congenital heart diseases including an incomplete Shone's complex.

Case presentation

We report a case of a 2-month-old boy who, on cardiac evaluation, was found to have coarctation of the aorta, a bicuspid aortic valve with severe stenosis, a parachute-like mitral valve with mild subvalvular stenosis, consistent with an incomplete Shone's complex, and marked left ventricular hypertrophy. The patient underwent successful corrective surgery for coarctation of the aorta and aortic valve stenosis, with follow-up revealing moderate residual aortic valve stenosis and mild residual valvular dysfunction. Genetic testing identified a maternally inherited microduplication of the X chromosome p22.12 region, encompassing several 5' exons of the RPS6KA3 gene.

Conclusions

This case suggests that obstructive left-sided congenital heart diseases including an incomplete Shone's complex may represent a previously unrecognized cardiac manifestations of Coffin-Lowry syndrome, thereby expanding the cardiovascular phenotype of this rare condition. Recognition of this association may have implications for early diagnosis, genetic evaluation, and long-term cardiac surveillance in affected patients.

title: Targeting PRMT5 alleviates diabetic cardiomyopathy: mechanisms involve Ndufs2 R118 dimethylation-mediated complex I protection and serum PRMT5 as a biomarker.
authorString: Cai S, Su M, Li J, Yu Y, Wu M, Liu M, Wang R, Huang J, Lai Q, Chen C, Yiu KH.
abstractText:
Background

Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is defined by progressive cardiac dysfunction driven by myocardial ATP depletion, where mitochondrial electron transport chain (ETC) Complex I dysfunction acts as a critical factor. Protein arginine methyltransferase 5 (PRMT5) maintains cardiac homeostasis, yet its function in DCM and association with Complex I remain elusive. This study aimed to investigate the function, key substrate, and mechanism of PRMT5 in DCM, and evaluate serum PRMT5 as a potential biomarker for DCM.

Methods

Gain- and loss-of-function experiments of PRMT5 were conducted to explore the function of PRMT5 in DCM. IP-MS proteomics and post-translational modification analysis were applied to identify the substrates of PRMT5 and their modified sites. By employing ELISA assay, serum levels of PRMT5, lactate, and lactate/pyruvate (L/P) ratio were measured in DCM patients, and the association between serum PRMT5 level and hospital readmission risk was analyzed.

Results

PRMT5 overexpression protected against DCM pathogenesis, while its knockdown or inhibition exacerbated disease progression. PRMT5 mediated symmetric di-methylation (SDMA) of Ndufs2 at R118 to prevent its ubiquitin-proteasomal degradation and preserve mitochondrial Complex I function. DCM patients had significantly lower serum PRMT5, which correlated positively with serum lactate and L/P ratio and was associated with higher hospital readmission risk.

Conclusions

Our findings unveil a novel PRMT5/Ndufs2 regulatory axis where arginine methylation maintains bioenergetic capacity of Complex I through methylation-ubiquitination crosstalk. PRMT5 shows potential as a therapeutic target and biomarker for DCM, which may aid the establishment of innovative diagnostic and treatment frameworks for DCM pending further translational validation.

title: Recompensation of decompensated autoimmune hepatitis cirrhosis: a multi-center retrospective analysis.
authorString: Kulkarni AV, Kumar K, Roy A, Priya P, Premkumar M, Sharma M, Alla M, Venishetty S, Ravikumar S, Rao PN, Reddy KR, Reddy DN.
abstractText:
Background and objectives

Recompensation is well known in patients with alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) and viral hepatitis. While there is limited data on patients with autoimmune hepatitis (AIH). The primary objective was to assess the rate of recompensation in AIH-related decompensated cirrhosis; the secondary objectives were to determine predictors of recompensation per Baveno VII criteria, re-decompensation, and further decompensation rates.

Methods

In this multicentre retrospective study from India, we included patients with biopsy-proven AIH-related decompensated cirrhosis from January 2019 to December 2024.

Results

Among 127 patients (aged 48.9±12.8 years; women: 72.4%, Child B: 51.2%; Child C: 48.8%), 77.2% (98/127) patients received immunosuppressive therapy, and 64.3% (63/98) had achieved complete biochemical remission. Forty-four of 127 patients (34.6%, 95% CI, 26.4-43.6) achieved recompensation after a median follow-up of 18 months (0.2-94 months). On competing risk regression analysis, Child Pugh score (sHR, 0.832 [95%CI, 0.7-0.979]; P = 0.02) was the only predictor of recompensation. Of the patients who recompensated, 20.4% (9/44) re-decompensated, and 44.4% (4/9) recompensated again. Of the 83 patients who had not recompensated, 9.6% (8/83) experienced further decompensation; of these, 37.5% (3/8) recompensated later. The transplant-free survival rate among recompensated patients was 97.7% (95% CI, 87.9-99.9) compared with 63.8% (95% CI, 52.5-74.1) among those who did not achieve recompensation (P < 0.001). Twenty-five per cent of patients with AIH-primary biliary cholangitis recompensated, while none with AIH-primary sclerosing cholangitis recompensated.

Conclusions

One-third of patients with AIH-related decompensated cirrhosis recompensate and one in five of such patients re-decompensate again.

title: Loss of FCN3 links cirrhotic matrix stiffness to YAP activation in HCC.
authorString: Luo JM, Xuan W, Qian G, Tao Y, Wang X, Chen Y, Wu J, Zhang ZG, Tian J.
abstractText:
Background

Cirrhosis-associated matrix stiffness is a major biophysical driver of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). How fibrosis-induced stiffness activates oncogenic YAP signaling remains unclear. We investigated the role of ficolin-3 (FCN3) in stiffness-associated regulation of the O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT)-YAP axis in HCC.

Methods

Public transcriptomic datasets comparing cirrhotic and normal liver tissues (GSE114564), as well as HCC tissues from patients with and without cirrhosis (GSE14520), were analyzed. FCN3 protein expression was evaluated in 67 paired HCC and adjacent non-tumorous tissues, and a subset of 20 matched cases was further analyzed by quantitative reverse-transcription PCR and atomic force microscopy. Controlled-stiffness substrates, FCN3 gain- and loss-of-function models, and murine H22 allograft and human HepG2 xenograft models were used for functional validation. Mechanistic studies included RNA sequencing, cycloheximide chase assays, subcellular fractionation, co-immunoprecipitation, structural prediction, YAP-S127A rescue, Thiamet-G treatment, and YAP knockdown.

Results

FCN3 was downregulated in cirrhotic liver and HCC with cirrhosis. In clinical samples, tumor stiffness inversely correlated with FCN3 expression. FCN3 overexpression curtailed proliferation, clonogenicity, migration, and invasion in vitro and suppressed tumor growth in vivo. Transcriptomics revealed YAP pathway inhibition without changes in upstream kinases. FCN3 did not alter YAP mRNA but reduced YAP protein, increased p-YAP(S127), limited nuclear YAP, and shortened YAP half-life. Co-IP showed FCN3 binds OGT and disrupts OGT-YAP association, decreasing YAP O-GlcNAcylation. YAP knockdown partially attenuated FCN3's anti-tumor effects.

Conclusions

These findings support a stiffness-associated FCN3-OGT-YAP regulatory model in HCC, in which FCN3 expression is associated with reduced OGT-YAP interaction, decreased YAP O-GlcNAcylation, and restricted YAP nuclear activity. Further studies are required to establish direct molecular competition and its independence from canonical Hippo-LATS signaling.

Anesthetic management for coarctation of aorta repair in a very low birth weight preterm infant: a case report.
authorString: Sun Z, Ying D, Ye S, Ye Q, Li D.
abstractText:
Background

Anesthetic management for cardiac surgery in very low birth weight (VLBW) preterm infants is highly challenging due to organ immaturity and metabolic vulnerability. Coarctation of the aorta (CoA) requiring early intervention adds further complexity. Reports on anesthesia for CoA repair in VLBW infants remain limited.

Case presentation

A male infant born at 32⁺² weeks gestation with a VLBW of 1360 g underwent CoA repair at 39 days of age (weight 2600 g). Anesthesia was induced with etomidate (0.3 mg/kg) and maintained with sufentanil (2.5 µg/kg/h), propofol (6 mg/kg/h), and low-dose sevoflurane (0.5%). Mechanical ventilation was initiated with a tidal volume of approximately 9.6 mL/kg. Dopamine (5 µg/kg/min) was infused for hemodynamic support.

Intervention

Intraoperative blood glucose was monitored at induction (4.6 mmol/L), 1 h after incision (9.8 mmol/L), and at the end of surgery (significant transient intraoperative hyperglycemia of 15.6 mmol/L). Upon detection of hyperglycemia, which was likely multifactorial and potentially related to exogenous glucose administration, surgical stress, and dopamine infusion, although definitive causality cannot be established due to the absence of endocrine or metabolic assessments, glucose-containing infusions were immediately reduced. Blood glucose normalized spontaneously within 12 h without insulin therapy.

Outcome

The infant remained hemodynamically stable with no seizures, hyperosmolality, or neurological complications. He was extubated on postoperative day 3, discharged on day 26, and showed good catch-up growth at one-month follow-up.

Conclusion

This case highlights the importance of individualized anesthetic regimens and routine, serial perioperative glucose monitoring in VLBW infants undergoing cardiac surgery. Even modest glucose infusion rates may lead to significant hyperglycemia under surgical stress, emphasizing the need for proactive glucose stewardship.

title: Fetal atrial strain: a scoping review of physiology, methods, and clinical applications.
authorString: Kotian N, Vasudeva A, Nayak K, Shivananda RP, Bhalke P, Nayak R, Lakshmi V, Krishnan M, Lewis LES, Nagaraj N.
abstractText:
Background

The evaluation of fetal cardiac function is moving towards the angle-independent myocardial deformation techniques, including the atrial strain obtained with speckle-tracking echocardiography. Angle-independent myocardial deformation techniques are gaining increasing traction and interest, where speckle-tracking-derived atrial strain (AS) has emerged as a potentially sensitive marker of subclinical myocardial dysfunction.

Methods

This scoping review aims to give an overview of the existing evidence regarding fetal atrial mechanics, which covers physiology, methodological aspects, reported reference values, and potential clinical use. Fetal atrial strain assessment is technically challenging. The traditional triphasic atrial cycle tends to be shortened with high fetal heart rate, creating a pattern of predominant reservoir domination. Furthermore, there are no standard acquisition protocols, gating strategies, and software implementations which may restrict the ability to replicate and compare studies conducted by different researchers.

Results

The inclusion criteria were met by only six heterogeneous studies because there is still a limited number of studies in this field. Therefore, the current results should be considered as tentative and exploratory. There is emerging evidence indicating fetal atrial strain varies with clinical circumstances. Lower atrial strain values have been reported in maternal diabetes, which may reflect a change in myocardial function. Placental insufficiency in contrast, however, seems to be accompanied by a relatively preserved atrial strain which may be due to adaptive cardiovascular responses to hypoxic stress. But the observations are based on small sample sizes and need to be validated further.

Conclusions

Fetal atrial strain is a promising quantitative measure of fetal cardiac function overall. Methodological heterogeneity, however, as well as limited reproducibility data and the relative scarcity of studies available suggest the need for standardized acquisition protocols and larger, well-designed studies to determine its clinical usefulness.

title: Prognostic impact of the right-to-left atrial volume index ratio on mortality and length of stay in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting.
authorString: Sevil FC, Siner H, Korucu C, Güme S, Tort M, Aksu U.
abstractText:
Background

Atrial remodeling is a key mechanism influencing prognosis in cardiovascular diseases [1]. This study aimed to investigate the prognostic value of the right-to-left atrial volume index ratio (RAVI/LAVI) for 2-month all-cause mortality and length of hospital stay in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).

Methods

In this single-center retrospective observational study, a total of 267 hospitalized patients were included. Patients were stratified into two groups according to the median RAVI/LAVI ratio (median value = 0.78) (below-median vs. above-median). Clinical, laboratory, and echocardiographic variables were compared between groups. The primary endpoint was 2-month all-cause mortality after CABG, and the secondary endpoint was length of hospital stay. Predictors of mortality were evaluated using logistic regression analysis.

Results

Mortality was significantly higher in the high RAVI/LAVI group (35.2% vs. 12.8%, p < 0.001), and the length of hospital stay was markedly longer (24.9 days vs. 11.4 days, p < 0.001). In multivariable logistic regression analysis, the RAVI/LAVI ratio remained an independent predictor of mortality (OR 6.67; 95% CI 1.96-22.73; p = 0.002).

Conclusion

The RAVI/LAVI ratio demonstrates a strong and independent association with mortality and length of hospital stay. This ratio may represent a practical and robust echocardiographic marker for risk stratification in vascular and cardiac patients.
