title: Impact of Aspirin Use on Mortality and Cardiac Allograft Vasculopathy After Heart Transplantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
authorString: Fournier N, Antiochos P, Gencer B, Nowacka A, Abdurashidova T, Yerly P, Meyer P, Rancati V, Ltaief Z, Muller O, Kirsch M, Hullin R, Lu H.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV) remains a major cause of late graft failure and morbidity among heart transplant (HTx) recipients. Aspirin is currently assigned a Class IIb recommendation for CAV prevention, reflecting the limited evidence supporting its clinical benefit. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the association between aspirin use and clinical outcomes in HTx recipients (PROSPERO ID: CRD420261399873).

Methods

Outcomes of interest included all-cause mortality and CAV-related clinical outcomes (graft dysfunction or CAV-related death). Literature searches were conducted through December 2025 in PubMed and EMBASE. Studies comparing HTx recipients treated with aspirin versus no aspirin were included. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were meta-analyzed across studies.

Results

Five observational studies were included, comprising four adult cohorts and one pediatric cohort. Participants were predominantly male (66.6%), with a mean age of ≈50 years in the four adult studies and 7.4 years in the sole pediatric study. Aspirin use was associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality (four studies, HR 0.31 [95% CI: 0.15-0.67]). No statistically significant association was observed with CAV-related clinical outcomes (HR 0.42 [95% CI: 0.10-1.77]).

Conclusions

In HTx recipients, aspirin use was associated with lower all-cause mortality, while no significant association was observed in the exploratory analysis of CAV-related clinical outcomes. These findings should be interpreted cautiously given the observational design, substantial heterogeneity, and potential residual and time-related biases. Prospective studies are needed to determine the efficacy and safety of aspirin after HTx.

title: Prognostic role of sarcopenia in anal squamous cell carcinoma treated with chemoradiotherapy: systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Socha J, Iwański Ł, Mazur E, Dendek A, Jaśkiewicz J, Kaptacz I, Domański A, Domańska J.

journal.title: Reports of practical oncology and radiotherapy : journal of Greatpoland Cancer Center in Poznan and Polish Society of Radiation Oncology

abstractText:
Background

Sarcopenia is a recognised prognostic factor in cancer patients treated with definitive radiotherapy, but its relevance in anal squamous cell carcinoma (ASCC) is poorly defined. We aimed to evaluate the prevalence of sarcopenia in ASCC and its association with treatment-related toxicity and survival outcomes in patients with ASCC treated with chemoradiotherapy.

Materials and methods

A systematic review and meta-analysis were performed to determine the effect of sarcopenia, defined by skeletal muscle index (SMI), on overall survival (OS) in patients with ASCC treated with chemoradiotherapy. Hazard ratios (HRs) for OS and disease-free survival (DFS) were pooled using an inverse variance random-effects model. Prevalence was estimated using random-effects meta-analysis of proportions with Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation. Toxicity outcomes were synthesised qualitatively due to heterogeneity in outcome definitions and reporting.

Results

Five retrospective cohort studies (n = 426) were included. The pooled prevalence of sarcopenia was 30% [95% confidence interval (CI): 21-41%]. Meta-analysis showed a strong association between sarcopenia and inferior OS (HR = 2.80, 95% CI: 1.59-4.94, p = 0.0004, I2 = 0%). No significant association was found for DFS. Qualitative synthesis indicated that sarcopenia was linked to severe haematological toxicity and to chemotherapy modifications, while no study demonstrated an effect on radiotherapy delivery.

Conclusions

Sarcopenia affects approximately one-third of ASCC patients and is associated with a nearly threefold increased risk of death. Sarcopenia is linked to haematological toxicity and chemotherapy modifications, but not to radiotherapy interruptions. Prospective studies with standardised definitions and functional assessments are needed to clarify its prognostic role in ASCC treated with chemoradiotherapy.

title: The application value of two-dimensional speckle tracking imaging technology in evaluating the functions of the left atrium and left atrial appendage in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation: A comparative cross-sectional study.
authorString: Guan X, Chang Q, Lu L, Wu W, Fang L, Bai C, Feng P.
abstractText: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is associated with increased risk of stroke due to left atrial appendage (LAA) thrombus formation. Two-dimensional speckle tracking imaging (2D-STI) may provide valuable insights into left atrial and LAA functional changes associated with thrombus formation. This study aimed to evaluate the functions of the left atrium (LA) and LAA in patients with non-valvular AF by using 2D-STI and explore echocardiographic parameters associated with the presence of LAA thrombus. In this comparative cross-sectional study, consecutive patients with non-valvular AF who were scheduled for radiofrequency ablation were screened. Finally, 68 eligible AF patients and 30 age-matched healthy controls were included. All AF patients underwent preoperative transthoracic echocardiography, transesophageal echocardiography, and two-dimensional speckle tracking imaging, and were classified according to the presence or absence of LAA thrombus detected by transesophageal echocardiography into the thrombus group (n = 32) and the non-thrombus group (n = 36). The healthy controls were included as a reference group for comparison of echocardiographic parameters. The left atrial appendage emptying velocity (LAAEV), left atrial global longitudinal strain (LAGLS), and LAA global longitudinal strain (LAAGLS) were measured and compared between groups. Compared with the control group, AF patients showed significantly reduced LAAEV, LAGLS, and left atrial appendage global longitudinal strain (all P < .05). In AF patients, the thrombus group had significantly lower LAAEV, LAGLS, and left atrial appendage global longitudinal strain compared to the non-thrombus group (all P < .05). Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that LAAEV and left atrial strain during reservoir phase were significantly associated with the presence of LAA thrombus. 2D-STI can quantitatively evaluate the functional changes of the LA and LAA. LAAEV and left atrial strain during reservoir phase may serve as useful echocardiographic markers for assisting clinical evaluation of LAA thrombus.

title: Beyond anticoagulation: defining the role of left atrial appendage closure in stroke prevention for atrial fibrillation.
authorString: Camm AJ.

journal.title: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText: Oral anticoagulation has a very strong evidence base for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) at elevated thromboembolic risk. Direct oral anticoagulants have improved the safety and convenience of treatment, yet important limitations remain, including residual ischaemic stroke, major bleeding, treatment discontinuation, and patient refusal. Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) offers an alternative strategy for selected patients by excluding the principal anatomical source of AF-related cardiac thrombi. However, the appropriate role of LAAC remains controversial, particularly in patients who can and do tolerate anticoagulation. This viewpoint argues for a more individualized approach that distinguishes absolute contraindications from modifiable bleeding risks, treatment refusal or non-persistence, and stroke occurring despite adequate anticoagulation.

title: Association of Cognitive Reserve and Chronic Disease Comorbidity with the Risk of Progression from Subjective Cognitive Decline to Objective Cognitive Impairment: A Cohort Study Among Chinese Community-Dwelling Older Adults.
authorString: Zhao Y, Wu Y, Yang B, Mao Z, Yu J.
abstractText:
Background

Although cognitive reserve (CR) and chronic disease comorbidity (CDC) are closely related to cognitive trajectories, their independent and combined effects on objective cognitive impairment (OCI) in subjective cognitive decline (SCD) remain insufficiently evidenced.

Objective

This study aimed to investigate the independent effects and interactions between CR and CDC on the risk of OCI in community-dwelling older adults with SCD.

Methods

This prospective cohort study included 605 community-dwelling SCD patients aged ≥60 years from Wuxi City in 2022, with a 3-year follow-up to assess progression to OCI (mild cognitive impairment or dementia). Cox proportional hazards (Cox PH) regression models were used to analyze the associations and interactions between CR, CDC, and OCI risk. Kaplan-Meier curves were employed to compare the probability of remaining free from OCI across different combinations of CR and CDC.

Results

During follow-up, 195 SCD patients progressed to OCI. Cox PH regression identified low CR (LCR) and high CDC (HCDC) as factors independently associated with elevated OCI risk in SCD patients. Compared with the LCR group, the high CR (HCR) group had a significantly lower risk of cognitive progression (HR = 0.473, 95% CI: 0.350-0.640, P < 0.001); in contrast, the HCDC group had a higher risk than the low CDC (LCDC) group (HR = 5.286, 95% CI: 3.772-7.409, P < 0.001). A significant positive additive interaction was observed between CR and CDC. Survival analysis revealed that patients with HCDC combined with LCR exhibited the highest risk of progression, while those with LCDC and HCR demonstrated the highest probability of maintaining normal cognition.

Conclusion

HCR was associated with lower risk of OCI among community-dwelling older adults with SCD, whereas LCR and HCDC showed synergistic association with elevated cognitive progression risk. Moreover, HCR remained independently associated with reduced risk even under HCDC exposure.

title: Use of Ecological Momentary Assessments to Evaluate Alcohol Use With American Indian Women.
authorString: Hanson JD, Gilbertson RJ, Kleffman C, Nowak AV, Charboneau M, Evans MD, Engel S, O'Leary M.
abstractText:
Background

Understanding the factors surrounding alcohol use among American Indian women requires real-time, event-level data collection. Ecological momentary assessment (EMA) offers a promising approach to better understand the context around drinking in this population. The goal of this study was to utilize EMA to track daily alcohol consumption, the setting in which alcohol consumption occurred, and affect among American Indian women over a 30-day period.

Methods

Following formative think-aloud sessions to refine survey instruments, 74 American Indian women (ages 18-50) who reported recent alcohol use completed baseline assessments, including the Timeline Followback (TLFB), the Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test (AUDIT), and measures for depression (CES-D-R-10) and social support (ISEL). Participants were then enrolled in a 30-day EMA protocol receiving three daily text prompts via the ReTAINE system to report on alcohol quantity, beverage type, social contexts, and mood.

Results

Of the 74 American Indian women who completed baseline data, n = 40 participants completed at least 35% of the EMA prompts, yielding 2278 records across 359 drinking days. Binge drinking throughout the 30-day period was significantly associated with higher baseline depression scores and higher baseline risky drinking behaviors. Binge drinking was significantly more likely to occur at someone else's house compared to other locations, though it was not associated with time of day or social group size. Furthermore, lower perceived social support (ISEL appraisal) was significantly associated with a higher likelihood of consuming hard alcohol, and drinking with two or more people significantly increased the odds of hard alcohol use compared to drinking alone.

Conclusion

Utilizing EMA is a feasible method for capturing detailed data on drinking behaviors and context with American Indian women. The findings highlight the critical role of social setting, social support, and underlying depressive symptoms in driving binge drinking and beverage choice, offering valuable insights for the development of tailored interventions.

title: Bibliometric analysis of septic cardiomyopathy: Current status, research hotspots, and emerging trends (2015-2025).
authorString: Xu Y, Yang Z, Zhu L, Ai Q, Guo H, Liu J.
abstractText:
Background

Septic cardiomyopathy (SCM) represents a life-threatening complication of sepsis. This study provides the first systematic bibliometric analysis and visualization of research in this field during the critical decade following the publication of the "Sepsis-3" definition (2015-2025), highlighting the current status, hotspots, and emerging trends.

Methods

Publications related to SCM were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection for the period August 2015 to August 2025. After data cleaning, bibliometric and visualization analyses were conducted using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, Scimago Graphica, and Excel/GraphPad Prism.

Results

The annual number of publications has shown exponential growth since the release of the Sepsis-3 guidelines. China has emerged as the global leader in research output, with Wuhan University identified as the leading institution. The knowledge base is anchored in the Sepsis-3 guidelines and seminal reviews on pathophysiology. Research frontiers have evolved from macro-level concepts such as "inflammation" and "oxidative stress" toward more precise molecular targets, including "ferroptosis," "mitophagy," and the "NLRP3 inflammasome," while "machine learning" has begun to penetrate as an emerging methodological approach.

Conclusion

Over the past decade, research on SCM has shifted from broad pathophysiological concepts toward specific molecular mechanisms. The resulting knowledge map provides a reference for identifying key literature, influential teams, and emerging research directions. Future studies should link mechanistic findings to clinical phenotypes and evaluate diagnostic and therapeutic strategies using patient-centered outcomes.

title: Blood serotonin, ionized magnesium, cardiac troponin I, N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide concentrations, and mitral valve billowing in horses with mitral valve regurgitation.
authorString: Demeyere M, Dufourni A, Verhaeghe LM, Paulussen E, Heirman L, De Baere S, Croubels S, De Backer T, van Loon G, Decloedt A.
abstractText:
Background

Serotonin, ionized magnesium (iMg), cardiac biomarkers, and mitral valve prolapse are extensively investigated in humans and dogs with mitral valve regurgitation (MR), but not in horses.

Hypothesis/objectives

To investigate serotonin, iMg, cardiac troponin I (cTnI), and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) concentrations and degree of mitral valve billowing (MVB) in horses with MR.

Animals

Eighty controls (no/trivial MR), 122 horses with MR (92 mild, 24 moderate, 6 severe).

Methods

Prospective cross-sectional observational study. All horses underwent echocardiography with MVB distance assessment and MR classification. Platelet-poor plasma serotonin and serum iMg, cTnI, and NT-proBNP concentrations were determined. Controls and horses with different MR grades, biomarker concentrations, and MVB distance were compared using (non-)parametric tests.

Results

Ionized magnesium concentration was lower in MR compared to controls (mean difference, 0.03 mmol/L; 95% CI, 0.01-0.05; P = .01), but showed no correlation with billowing distance. The billowing distance was higher in horses with MR than in controls (septal: median difference, 0.2 cm; 95% CI, 0.1-0.3; P < .001; parietal: median difference, 0.3 cm; 95% CI, 0.2-0.3; P < .001), and in horses with a crescendo compared to a holosystolic MR jet (septal: median difference, 0.2 cm; 95% CI, 0.1-0.3; P = .003; parietal: median difference, 0.1 cm; 95% CI, 0.0-0.2; P = .01). No differences in serotonin, cTnI, and NT-proBNP concentrations were detected.

Conclusions and clinical importance

Mitral valve billowing is to some extent likely physiological. The association of serotonin and iMg in MVB and MR requires further investigation. Both cTnI and NT-proBNP showed limited use as biomarkers of MR severity.

Abstract (dutch)

Achtergrondinformatie: Serotonine, geïoniseerd magnesium (iMg), cardiale biomarkers en mitraalklep prolaps werden reeds uitgebreid onderzocht bij mensen en honden met mitraalklep regurgitatie (MR), in tegenstelling tot paarden met MR. Hypothese/Doelstelling: Het onderzoeken van de serotonine, iMg, cardiaal troponine I (cTnI) en N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) concentraties en de mate van bolling van de mitraalklep naar het linker atrium (MVB) bij paarden met MR. Studiepopulatie: Tachtig controle paarden (geen/triviaal MR), 122 paarden met MR (92 mild, 24 matig, 6 erg). Materiaal en methoden: Prospectieve cross-sectionele observationele studie. Alle paarden ondergingen echocardiografie, waarna de mate van MVB gemeten werd en MR classificatie uitgevoerd werd. De concentraties van serotonine in bloedplaatjesarm plasma en van iMg, cTnI en NT-proBNP in serum werden bepaald. Controle paarden en paarden met verschillende MR graden, biomarker concentraties en de mate van MVB werden onderling vergeleken aan de hand van (non-)parametrische testen. Resultaten: De concentratie iMg was lager bij paarden met MR in vergelijking met controle paarden (gemiddeld verschil, 0.03 mmol/L; 95% BI, 0.01-0.05; P = 0.01), maar vertoonde geen correlatie met de mate van MVB. De mate van MVB was hoger bij paarden met MR dan bij controle paarden (septaal: mediaan verschil, 0.2 cm; 95% BI, 0.1-0.3; P < 0.001; pariëtaal: mediaan verschil, 0.3 cm; 95% BI, 0.2-0.3; P < 0.001), en bij paarden met een crescendo MR jet in vergelijking met paarden met een holosystolische MR jet (septaal: mediaan verschil, 0.2 cm; 95% BI, 0.1-0.3; P = 0.003; pariëtaal: mediaan verschil, 0.1 cm; 95% BI, 0.0-0.2; P = 0.01). Er werden geen verschillen gedetecteerd in de concentraties van serotonine, cTnI en NT-proBNP. Conclusies en klinisch belang: De mate van MVB is tot op een bepaalde hoogte waarschijnlijk fysiologisch. De rol van serotonine en iMg in MVB en MR vergt verder onderzoek. Zowel cTnI als NT-proBNP vertoonden een beperkte meerwaarde als biomarkers bij het bepalen van de ernst van MR.

title: Integrated Lipidomic and Energy Metabolomic Analyses Reveal the Cardioprotective Mechanisms of Meconopsis horridula Alkaloids in Heart Failure.
authorString: Zhao Y, Li Y, Liu G, Fu J, Han J, Wang S, Chen X, Yang X, Zhang J, Wang S, Li X, Jia Q.
abstractText: Meconopsis horridula Hook. f. & Thomson (MH) is a traditional Tibetan medicinal herb used to promote blood circulation and treat cardiovascular disorders; however, its active constituents and cardioprotective mechanisms in heart failure (HF) remain poorly understood. In this study, liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry was used to characterize the alkaloid profile of MH, and the cardioprotective effects of its alkaloid fraction were evaluated in a doxorubicin-induced rat model of HF. A total of 26 alkaloids were identified. Treatment with MH alkaloids significantly improved cardiac function and attenuated myocardial injury in HF rats. To elucidate the underlying mechanisms, quantitative lipidomics and targeted energy metabolomics analyses were performed. Compared with the model group, MH treatment altered multiple lipid and energy metabolites associated with ether lipid metabolism, glycerophospholipid metabolism, lipid and atherosclerosis, glyoxylate and dicarboxylate metabolism, and the citrate cycle. Integrated pathway analysis identified NADH/ubiquinone oxidoreductase complex assembly factor 6 (NDUFAF6), AMPK, ACC, GLUT4, ACOT1, and ATP2A as key regulatory nodes. Western blot analysis further supported the involvement of these proteins in MH-mediated metabolic remodeling. Collectively, these findings suggest that MH alkaloids alleviate HF by partially restoring dysregulated glucose and lipid metabolism and provide mechanistic insights into their cardioprotective effects.

title: Endothelial Cell Secretome Alterations Induced by Inflammatory Stress.
authorString: Tang VT, Baid S, Castellanos A, Basrur V, Kretz CA, Nesvizhskii AI, Gao X, Dong Q, Weiss MJ, Abbineni PS.
abstractText: Endothelial cells detect pathogens through pattern recognition receptors, such as Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), which triggers the synthesis and secretion of molecules that initiate the innate immune response. Proteins bearing signal peptides are secreted through the classical endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-Golgi-dependent route, whereas select signal-peptide-lacking proteins are secreted via less well-characterized ER-Golgi-independent mechanisms, collectively termed unconventional protein secretion (UcPS). To systematically characterize the secretome of human umbilical vein-derived endothelial cells (HUVECs) and delineate the contribution of UcPS, we performed deep quantitative proteomics on HUVEC lysates and conditioned medium before and after TLR4 stimulation with lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Of 5205 proteins detected in either fraction, 381 were enriched in the conditioned medium and therefore classified as secreted. Of these, 302 proteins (79.3%) were secreted via the conventional pathway, and 79 (20.7%) lacked a signal peptide and were classified as candidate UcPS cargos. Predicted functions of UcPS-secreted proteins include redox regulation, proteostasis, cytoskeletal remodeling, and innate immune signaling. We confirmed that α-globin (HBA1), which functions as a redox sensor and regulator of nitric oxide in endothelial cells, is secreted constitutively by UcPS and at higher levels following inflammatory activation. Notably, candidate UcPS cargo identity showed poor concordance with current computational predictors, underscoring the need for empirical datasets. Overall, our findings suggest that the HUVEC secretome includes both conventionally and unconventionally secreted proteins that regulate coagulation, angiogenesis, and immune function. Our findings establish a high-quality secretome dataset for HUVECs, providing a novel resource for future efforts to define the molecular determinants governing UcPS cargo selection and trafficking related to endothelial cell function.

title: Clinical Diagnosis Versus Plain Radiography for Diabetic Foot Osteomyelitis: A Prospective Study of Diagnostic Agreement in a Resource-Limited Settings.
authorString: Abbas ZG, Gangji RR, Naemi R.
abstractText: Diabetic foot osteomyelitis (DFO) is a serious complication of diabetic foot ulcers, particularly in advanced infections. In low-resource settings, access to medical imaging may be limited. This study evaluated the diagnostic agreement between a composite clinical approach (clinical assessment plus probe-to-bone test) compared with plain radiography for diagnosing DFO, including performance across ulcer categories. A prospective cohort study was conducted from December 2021 to January 2025 among patients with suspected DFO. Participants underwent clinical evaluation, risk factor assessment, ulcer history, SINBAD classification, probe-to-bone testing and plain radiography. Diagnostic performance measures were calculated. Given the absence of a gold standard reference test (bone biopsy) in this low-resource setting, performance measures represent comparative diagnostic agreement with plain radiography rather than absolute diagnostic accuracy. A total of 166 patients with deep foot ulcers were enrolled. Composite clinical diagnosis identified osteomyelitis in 117 patients and excluded it in 49. Plain radiography was positive in 96 of 117 composite positive cases, while 21 were discordant; all 49 composite negative cases were radiographically negative. The composite approach showed 100% sensitivity, 70% specificity and 87.3% overall agreement. Sensitivity remained 100% across ulcer categories, while specificity increased significantly from 63.8% in SINBAD-4 ulcers to 77.8% in SINBAD-5 ulcers, improving agreement from 86.1% to 89.7%. In conclusion, composite clinical diagnosis demonstrates substantial agreement with plain radiography in this cohort of patients with suspected DFO. This can provide a practical adjunct for clinical assessment in resource-limited settings where imaging is unavailable or difficult to interpret but should not be considered a definitive diagnostic test in the absence of an independent reference standard.

title: Artificial intelligence in cardiology for non-experts: decoding key terms and understanding machine learning methodologies. A Scientific Statement of the ESC Working Group on e-Cardiology, the European Heart Rhythm Association (EHRA), the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care (ACVC), the Heart Failure Association (HFA), the European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging (EACVI), the European Association of Preventive Cardiology (EAPC), and the European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions (EAPCI) of the ESC, the ESC Regulatory Affairs Committee, and the ESC Digital Cardiology and Artificial Intelligence Committee
Exploring time-varying cardiovascular effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists: A multi-state network meta-analysis of cardiovascular outcome trials.
authorString: Wang Z, Zhang P, Zhang Y, Bai J.
abstractText:
Aims

To explore time-varying cardiovascular effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and transition-specific estimates obtainable from published outcome curves.

Methods

Ten placebo-controlled cardiovascular outcome trials included 87,334 participants and eight GLP-1 RA regimens. Reconstructed major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE) data and all-cause mortality data, directly reconstructed for four trials and synthesised for four, informed a three-state model. Two trials contributed MACE data only. The model assumed no treatment effect on death before a first non-fatal MACE. Conventional random-effects meta-analysis provided a comparator.

Results

Conventional meta-analysis yielded a MACE hazard ratio (HR) of 0.856 (95% confidence interval 0.810-0.905). Modelled transition HRs for first non-fatal MACE at 24 months ranged from 0.51 to 1.38; all 95% credible intervals included 1. Semaglutide posterior median curves suggested larger early reductions that attenuated over time. Mortality attribution depended on structural assumptions, and several sensitivity analyses showed incomplete convergence.

Conclusions

Conventional synthesis supported a class-level MACE reduction. Multi-state estimates suggested possible time-varying patterns but remained imprecise and assumption-dependent. These data did not establish a reliable efficacy hierarchy or empirically distinguish event prevention from post-event survival effects.

title: Lactate in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: an evidence synthesis and a hypothesis-generating framework for dynamic assessment.
authorString: Mishra A, Mishra P, Mishra V.
abstractText: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome is staged with measures that capture organ-specific abnormality rather than integrated metabolic reserve under stress. Lactate is a circulating fuel and signal exchanged among every organ the syndrome names. We synthesise the human evidence on lactate handling across adipose tissue, skeletal muscle, kidney, liver and myocardium, and on what resting and dynamic lactate measurement has shown. That evidence contains two negative findings: in ARIC, the association of resting lactate with incident diabetes was lost after adjustment for fasting glucose and insulin, and the only direct comparison with cardiorespiratory fitness in metabolic syndrome found no independent lactate signal. Against this evidence we propose lactate resilience - blood-lactate excursion and recovery relative to standardised external work - as a hypothesis-generating framework only; it is not a biomarker, score, diagnosis or treatment target and does not alter CKM management. The contribution of this framework is not a demonstration of clinical value but a falsifiable specification: prespecified abandonment criteria (redundancy with peak oxygen uptake, ventilatory threshold and measured physical activity) and negative controls (tracking of renal function alone; attenuation after adjustment for glycaemia and fitness) against which the construct can be tested and, if necessary, discarded.

title: Advances in Next-Generation Sequencing and Single-Cell Transcriptomics for Profiling NK Cell Heterogeneity and Functional Diversity in Cancer.
authorString: Ahangarzadeh S, Nakhlband A, Alibakhshi A, Maleki B, Rahimmanesh I, Yaghoobi H, Javanmard SH.
abstractText: Natural Killer (NK) cells, as the prototypic member of innate lymphocytes, play a key role in recognizing and killing malignant cells without the need for prior desensitization. NK cell-based therapies have been considered as a promising approach for the treatment of a wide range of hematological and solid malignancies. However, identification and characterization of highly functional populations of NK cells is essential for the advancement of this field. Recent advances in next-generation sequencing (NGS) and single-cell transcriptomics have enabled high-resolution profiling of NK cell diversity at the molecular level. This review explores methods for assessing NK cell function, including chromium-51 release assays, flow cytometry, impedance-based cell analysis systems, microfluidic platforms, bioluminescence imaging, PET, and multiplex imaging systems. Applications of NGS in NK cell research, including KIR receptor genotyping, exome and genome sequencing, and RNA-seq, are also discussed. Herein we examined the impact of NK cell heterogeneity on cancer treatment strategies and personalized therapeutic approaches, and analyzes the challenges and future directions in this field.

title: Twice the Joy, but Added Risk: Exploring Twin Birth Outcomes at the East Suffolk and North Essex NHS Foundation Trust Maternity Service, England.
authorString: Aakanksha, Mon PE, Sharma A, Sunita F, Mamah JE.
abstractText: Background and aim Twin pregnancy carries higher maternal and neonatal risk than singleton pregnancy, and local data on chorionicity and national benchmarking remain limited. This study primarily aims to describe maternal characteristics, timing and mode of birth, and maternal and neonatal outcomes of twin deliveries in a two-site NHS maternity service. Secondary, hypothesis-generating aims were to explore factors associated with cesarean birth and early delivery and to make an indicative comparison with UK national audit data. Materials and methods We conducted a retrospective, descriptive, and analytical cross-sectional study of 55 women who delivered twins (110 fetuses) between October 2, 2025, and June 18, 2026, following STROBE and RECORD guidance. Key proportions are presented with 95% CIs. Timing of birth was assessed against chorionicity-specific National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) windows. Analyses were exploratory and unadjusted, and no formal comparison with national data was made. Results Mean maternal age was 31.8 ± 5.7 years. Of the 55 pregnancies, 46 (83.6%) were dichorionic diamniotic (DCDA), nine (16.4%) were monochorionic diamniotic (MCDA), and 10 (18.2%) followed assisted conception. Mean gestation at delivery was 36.1 ± 1.6 weeks; 33 women (60.0%) delivered before 37 weeks. Compared with chorionicity-specific NICE windows, 24 of 46 DCDA pregnancies (52.2%) delivered before 37+0 weeks, and seven of nine MCDA pregnancies (77.8%) before 36+0 weeks. Cesarean birth of both twins occurred in 42 women (76.4%; 95% CI 63.7-85.6): 24 (43.6%) elective and 18 (32.7%) unscheduled. Postpartum hemorrhage (≥500 mL after vaginal birth or ≥1000 mL after cesarean) occurred in 19 women (34.5%), and composite maternal morbidity in 18 (32.7%). Mean birthweight was 2417 ± 457 g; nine of 53 pairs (17.0%) had ≥20% birthweight discordance. At least one twin was admitted to the neonatal unit (any level of care) in 20 of 54 pregnancies (37.0%), including four of four (100%) born before 34 weeks. One fetus (one of 110, 0.9%) died in utero at 23+3 weeks; there were no neonatal or maternal deaths. Conclusions Preterm birth, cesarean birth, postpartum hemorrhage, and neonatal unit admission were common in this twin population. With 55 women, CIs were wide, so the study cannot show whether local outcomes differ from national data. Early delivery of MCDA twins relative to the NICE window and the reasons recorded for cesarean birth warrant local review. Structured documentation of the planned mode of birth, the reasons for the decision, cesarean urgency, neonatal level of care, and indications for admission would support more reliable audits.

title: Biomechanical Evolution in the Neuropathic Diabetic Foot: A Scoping Review of Gait and Kinetic-Kinematic-Structural Adaptations in Diabetes.
authorString: Di Stasio G, Colella R, Armstrong DG, Bellingeri A, De Mola A, Montini G, Scotti V, De Silvestri A, Campitiello F.
abstractText:
Background

Gait alterations and biomechanical changes associated with diabetic peripheral polyneuropathy have been described in the literature, but the available evidence remains fragmented. It does not provide a comprehensive overview of how the reported biomechanical patterns differ across clinical stages of the Neuropathic Diabetic Foot (NDF). Mapping these patterns may support an improved understanding of the biomechanical mechanisms underlying increased ulceration risk.

Aim

This scoping review aims to explore and synthesise the existing literature on changes in gait and foot biomechanics in people with diabetes in association with Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy (DPN) and across its reported clinical stages.

Methods

The scoping review was conducted in accordance with the JBI methodology for scoping reviews and in line with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). The population included adults with diabetes and peripheral neuropathy, without active foot ulceration, who were managed in community or outpatient settings. The concept of interest is gait and foot-biomechanical alterations associated with diabetic neuropathy in clinical and biomechanical assessment contexts. A comprehensive search was conducted in PubMed, EMBASE, CINAHL, PEDro, and the Cochrane Library, complemented by grey literature sources including the Trip Medical Database, NICE, and the Guidelines International Network (GIN). Studies published within the last 11 years were considered (2014/12-2026/04). Data were charted and synthesised using a descriptive and narrative approach.

Results

From 2044 initial records, 44 sources met the eligibility criteria. An updated search conducted in April 2026 identified 6 additional eligible sources, resulting in 50 included sources. The evidence mapped across three principal themes: gait and lower-limb kinematic alterations, changes in plantar loading and joint kinetics, and structural or functional changes of the foot. No included study directly evaluated whether the identified biomechanical alterations predicted the subsequent development of Charcot neuro-osteoarthropathy.

Conclusions

To our knowledge, this is the first scoping review to map structural, kinematic, kinetic, and plantar-loading findings within an integrated biomechanical framework of the neuropathic diabetic foot. Because the evidence was predominantly cross-sectional, the proposed relationships should be interpreted as a conceptual synthesis rather than a demonstrated longitudinal progression. These findings highlight the need for longitudinal studies to investigate the temporal evolution of biomechanical alterations in the neuropathic diabetic foot.

title: Metabolic Niches: MALDI Imaging Reveals Lipidomic Heterogeneity in the Human Heart.
authorString: Osumi KM, Kransdorf EP, Manzoor D, Karlstaedt A, Neumann EK.

journal.title: Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry

abstractText: The human heart is characterized by aberrant lipid accumulation and remodeling during periods of stress and disease, yet spatially resolved lipidomic profiling of the human heart remains unreported. Here, we employ matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry imaging (MALDI-MSI) to map lipid distributions across five anatomical regions of healthy human donor hearts (left and right atrium, left and right ventricle, and interventricular septum). Cryosections of donor hearts from healthy subjects were thaw-mounted onto indium tin oxide slides, coated with 2,5-dihydroxyacetophenone, and analyzed on a Bruker timsTOF fleX mass spectrometer in positive and negative ionization modes (m/z 50-1850; 20 μm raster spacing). Serial sections were stained with hematoxylin and eosin to enable histological coregistration with lipid distributions. We identified 150 unique lipid species across four glycerophospholipid classes, including phosphatidylcholine (PC), phosphatidylglycerol (PG), phosphatidylethanolamine (PE), and phosphatidylserine (PS), with abundances and spatial distributions differing significantly between regions. H&E coregistration further resolved epicardial and myocardial compartments, enabling tissue-specific lipid mapping. These findings establish the first spatially resolved lipidomic profiles of the human heart and provide a framework for identifying region-specific lipid biomarkers of cardiovascular disease.

title: Snare-Assisted Traction Technique for Renal Artery Reconstruction in Endovascular Repair of Complex Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
authorString: Wei R, Zhang H, Zhang M, Fan C, Xiong J, Jia X, Guo W.
abstractText: Renal artery (RA) reconstruction during complex endovascular aortic repair often fails in hostile anatomy because of inadequate guidewire support. We describe snare-assisted traction (SAT), a novel endovascular bailout technique using conventional off-the-shelf devices. By combining distal snare traction with a long femoral sheath, SAT shifts target vessel reconstruction from simple wire guidance to sheath-based structural support. This provides robust stability for wire exchange and stent delivery without requiring specialized, unavailable tools or high-morbidity open conversion. Among 12 patients with severe RA angulation, ostial stenosis, or sac origin, SAT achieved 100% technical success without procedural complications. At median 6-month follow-up, all reconstructed RAs remained patent with stable renal function. SAT offers a safe, reproducible, and universally accessible solution for hostile target vessel access, significantly enhancing the feasibility and clinical safety of complex endovascular repair.

title: Tick tock: how the body's circadian clock keeps cardiometabolic rhythm in check.
authorString: Sato M, Alammar AMA, Gachon F, Mauvoisin D, Karunakaran D.
abstractText: The circadian clock orchestrates the internal timing of numerous physiological processes through an approximately 24-h cycle. It comprises a hypothalamic central clock, which responds to light cues and entrains peripheral clocks within individual cells and organs that, depending on the tissue, regulate gene expression across diverse biological functions in a tissue-specific manner. Peripheral clocks are also entrained by feeding and exercise-related cues, enabling their synchronization with feeding rhythm and physiology. Together, these clocks maintain a complex molecular network essential for metabolic homeostasis. Disruption of circadian rhythms, driven by genetic, environmental, or behavioral factors, is increasingly recognized as a major contributor to cardiometabolic disorders. Modern lifestyles, including shift work, irregular sleep, prolonged exposure to artificial light at night, jet lag, and erratic eating schedules, misalign circadian clocks with environmental cues, contributing to disruption of circadian rhythms or chronodisruption. This misalignment alters hormonal regulation, promotes systemic inflammation, and impairs metabolic balance, thereby increasing the risk of cardiovascular disease, obesity, type 2 diabetes, and related complications. The present review examines the mechanistic roles of core circadian clock genes in cardiometabolic health, highlighting their regulation of physiological processes in peripheral organs such as the heart, liver, and adipose tissue. We further discuss how circadian clock disruption accelerates disease onset and progression and explore emerging therapeutic strategies, including pharmacological modulation of the molecular circadian clock components and personalized chronotherapy. These approaches offer promising avenues to restore circadian alignment and mitigate cardiometabolic risk.

title: Tree Shrew as an Emerging Model for Aging Research: Characterization of Senescence and Therapeutic Interventions.
authorString: Luo Q, Xiao W, Dong X, Nisar A, Ma Y, Lai X, Bai R, Zi M, Geng Q, Zhang Q, Zhang C, Wang Q, Gold NM, Zhou Z, Hu L, Zhang A, Zeng Q, Liu J, Khan S, Lv L, He Y.
abstractText: Aging is characterized by progressive physiological decline and increased susceptibility to age-related diseases. Conventional rodent models have contributed significantly to our understanding of aging, yet their translational relevance is limited by substantial evolutionary divergence from humans. Here, we introduce the tree shrew (Tupaia belangeri chinensis) as a novel and biologically relevant model organism for aging research. In vitro, we induced cellular senescence in tree shrew fibroblasts through ionizing radiation, doxorubicin treatment, or replicative exhaustion, all of which consistently triggered robust senescent phenotypes and a pronounced senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), accompanied by upregulation of conserved senescence biomarkers. In vivo, aged tree shrews exhibited progressive physical frailty, metabolic dysfunction, organ fibroplasia, and spontaneous tumorigenesis. Transcriptomic profiling uncovered widespread age-related alterations across multiple tissues, prominently affecting pathways involved in chronic inflammation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and metabolic dysregulation. Further comparative transcriptomic analyses of liver and spleen tissues confirmed that tree shrews recapitulate conserved human aging transcriptional trajectories and core gene expression patterns, whereas mice displayed markedly divergent aging signatures. Notably, senolytic intervention with dasatinib and quercetin (D + Q) effectively reversed key transcriptional changes and ameliorated selected age-related pathologies, including hepatic steatosis. Importantly, the D + Q-induced transcriptomic responses in tree shrews exhibited markedly greater concordance with human aging signatures than did corresponding mouse datasets. Collectively, these findings establish the tree shrew as a translationally relevant aging model that bridges the gap between fundamental discovery and clinical application.

title: Primary Erythrocytosis (Polycythaemia) in a Neutered Male Dog Presenting With Right Hindlimb Lameness.
authorString: Belch R, Henry P, Ferreira M, Padros AA, Munoz ML, Lloyd-Bradley B, Isaac I, Llewellyn E, Nagendran A.
abstractText: A 2-year-old male entire Cocker Spaniel was referred for investigation of progressive right hindlimb lameness and polyuria and polydipsia. Investigations conducted by the primary care veterinary surgeon revealed erythrocytosis (haematocrit of 78%, reference interval: 37%-55%) and urine concentration consistent with polyuria and polydipsia (specific gravity 1.014). Upon referral, physical examination revealed a dark red oral mucosa and right hindlimb lameness, characterised by intermittent non-weight bearing of the limb when standing. Neurological examination only revealed a mild short-strided gait, and orthopaedic examination was unremarkable. Secondary causes of erythrocytosis were excluded by normal arterial blood gas, low erythropoietin levels and normal thoracic and abdominal imaging, resulting in a diagnosis of primary erythrocytosis (PE). Focal ultrasonography identified a right external iliac venous thrombus, suspected to be the cause of the right hindlimb lameness and presumed to be associated with the PE. Initial management involved repeated phlebotomies, followed by long-term treatment with hydroxyurea (31 mg/kg twice weekly) and rivaroxaban (2 mg/kg once daily). At the 5-month recheck, the dog was asymptomatic, with resolution of the iliac thrombus and a normal haematocrit. This case highlights an unusual presentation of PE in a dog, not previously described in the veterinary literature, and re-examines the discussion on the optimal management of this rare condition, with a focus on the necessity of antithrombotic therapy.

title: Walking Capacity and Daily Movement Behaviours After Ischemic Stroke: A Potential Capacity-Performance Gap.
authorString: Ezeugwa JC, Iyizoba M, Shiloff-Rogers A, Chan A, Hayward J, Tuchak C, Yu JC, Buck BH, Manns PJ, Ezeugwu VE.

journal.title: Physiotherapy research international : the journal for researchers and clinicians in physical therapy

abstractText:
Background and purpose

Walking capacity is a common focus of stroke rehabilitation; however, the extent to which walking capacity is associated with daily movement behaviours (primary lying, sedentary time, standing and stepping) during different phases of stroke recovery remains unclear. This study examined the relationship between walking capacity and daily movement behaviours among individuals in the acute and subacute phases of ischemic stroke recovery.

Methods

In this cross-sectional study, adults with ischemic stroke who were ambulatory (able to walk ≥ 5 m with or without a gait aid) were recruited during the acute (≤ 7 days post-stroke; n = 19) and subacute (2 weeks-3 months post-stroke; n = 25) phases of stroke recovery. Movement behaviours were assessed using 24-h activPAL accelerometry, including primary lying time, sedentary time, standing time, stepping time and daily step count. Walking capacity was assessed using the 6-Minute Walk Test, 10-m Walk Test (gait speed) and Timed Up and Go. Between-group differences were analysed using Welch's t-tests or Mann-Whitney U tests, as appropriate, and associations were examined using Spearman correlations and exploratory partial correlations adjusted for stroke severity (NIHSS).

Results

The subacute group demonstrated faster gait speed than the acute group (0.89 vs. 0.71 m/s; p = 0.03), and shorter Timed Up and Go times (median 15.9 vs. 19.0 seconds; p = 0.03), whereas the 6-Minute Walk Test and daily movement behaviours were similar. Both groups accumulated high sedentary time (∼12 hours/day). Gait speed was the only walking capacity measure associated with daily movement behaviours. In exploratory analyses adjusted for stroke severity, gait speed remained associated with sedentary time in both groups, whereas associations with stepping and standing time were attenuated in the acute group.

Conclusions

In this ambulatory sample of adults in the acute and subacute phases of ischemic stroke recovery, participants accumulated approximately 12 hours of sedentary time per day despite walking speeds approaching thresholds associated with community ambulation. These findings are consistent with a potential capacity-performance gap and highlight the importance of assessing daily movement behaviours alongside standardized walking capacity measures.

title: Symptom control in comprehensive conservative care for chronic kidney disease.
authorString: Valverde TL, Abreu PF, Rodrigues CIS, Lotaif L, Ramos CI, Gonçalves JG, Lucena JMDC, Caetano CP, Watanabe R, Sallenave MP, Miranda E, Magalhães T, Magalhães LP, Neiva MAOO.
abstractText: Over recent decades, the prevalence of chronic kidney disease (CKD) has risen markedly. In the terminal stage of the disease, renal replacement therapy (RRT) is traditionally recommended as the standard therapeutic approach. However, in older individuals with a high burden of comorbidities or substantial functional impairment, the benefits of RRT in terms of survival prolongation or improvement in quality of life become uncertain. In this context, comprehensive conservative kidney management (CKM) has emerged as a clinical alternative that is centered on the patient's needs, values, and preferences. CKM entails an active, nondialytic management strategy for CKD that incorporates palliative care principles, with emphasis on kidney supportive care, slowing disease progression, and symptom control. This article discusses the main symptoms experienced by patients with advanced CKD managed conservatively and provides practical recommendations for their clinical management.

title: Inter-Individual Variation in LUNG Mechanics Assessed by the Non-Invasive PEEP-Step Method During Laparoscopic and Robotic Surgery Indicates Need for Individualized Ventilatory Settings.
authorString: Abdulhussein A, Hammarskjöld S, Stenqvist O, Persson P, Hallén K, Jildenstål P, Lindgren S.
abstractText:
Background

During laparoscopic surgery, abdominal carbon dioxide (CO2) insufflation in the supine position and with head-down tilt for robotic surgery increases abdominal pressure and pushes the diaphragm cranially. This causes a decrease in end-expiratory lung volume and in lung and chest wall compliance. These effects can be counteracted by the application of PEEP. Our study aimed to measure lung and chest wall mechanics during laparoscopic surgery using a non-invasive method (PEEP-step method) and to determine the optimal PEEP level for each patient.

Methods

Thirty-two patients scheduled for abdominal surgery participated in this observational study with pneumoperitoneum. Fourteen patients underwent surgery for pelvic conditions in head-down position and 18 in supine position. Data from the ventilator was collected and analysed with a dedicated software, which calculated lung compliance and transpulmonary pressure from a two-step PEEP increase. Measurements were performed after induction, after pneumoperitoneum in supine/tilt head-down and before emergence.

Results

Lung and chest wall compliance decreased during CO2 insufflation with high individual variation, and we observed a≈90% increase in transpulmonary driving pressure. After CO2-desufflation, lung and chest wall compliance returned to near baseline levels on a group level. However, 19 patients had a remaining reduction in lung compliance, six with 20%-50%. Optimal PEEP level calculated by the software was twice the clinical routine level.

Conclusions

The study found substantial individual variation in lung compliance during laparoscopic surgery in patients without evident lung disease. This variability does not align well with respiratory system compliance. The findings highlight the need for individualized ventilator settings based on lung- rather than respiratory system mechanics. The PEEP-step method may be a non-invasive, real-time bedside tool to identify patients who would benefit from higher PEEP to preserve lung volume and possibly prevent postoperative complications.

Editorial comment

Laparascopic surgical conditions can affect lung mechanics, though not always predictably. This study examined how a test of higher or lower PEEP directly after anaesthesia induction might inform PEEP optimization in the same cases undergoing laparoscopic surgery.

Trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04484727, 2022-05-01).

title: Metabolomics Reveals Multiple Metabolic Alterations and Biomarkers of Disease Severity in Facioscapulohumeral Muscle Dystrophy.
authorString: Reynier P, Michel M, Vandeputte P, Albano N, Zoppi D, Gillet C, Pini S, Nuredini A, De Maria M, Blanchet O, Gueguen N, Chao de la Barca JM, Ruggiero L, Tupler R, Spinazzi M.

journal.title: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle

abstractText:
Background

Facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy type 1 (FSHD1) is one of the most common adult-onset myopathies and is causally associated with a contraction of the D4Z4 macrosatellite repeat array on chromosome 4. It presents with a variable pattern of progressive muscle weakness affecting the face, shoulder girdle and lower limbs. Pathophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely understood, and no effective treatments are available. Moreover, the lack of validated biomarkers limits the assessment of disease progression and therapeutic effects in clinical trials. Metabolic dysfunction has been hypothesized as a contributing factor, yet remains poorly explored.

Methods

In this multicentre, observational, cross-sectional case-control study, we performed quantitative plasma metabolomics by mass spectrometry in 57 patients (age: 41.8 ± 11.9; females/males ratio: 1.04) with mild to moderate facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD clinical score 6.4 ± 2.6) and age- and sex-comparable controls (age: 41.1 ± 11.2; females/males ratio: 1.13) recruited from three tertiary neuromuscular reference centres. We restricted inclusion to patients with preserved ambulatory capacity to better capture systemic metabolic alterations not primarily driven by advanced disability. We analysed the data using an integrative framework combining univariate and multivariate analyses with five machine-learning classifiers.

Results

We identified 57 circulating metabolites discriminating patients from controls, suggesting systemic perturbations in nitric oxide, mitochondrial and one-carbon metabolism, as well as oxidative stress, muscle mass maintenance and lipid membrane remodelling. Notably, decreased creatinine (fold change in patients vs. controls: 0.754; FDR-corrected p = 0.000003) and increased asymmetric dimethylarginine (ADMA; fold change in patients vs. controls: 1.168; FDR-corrected p = 0.000704) emerged as the most significantly altered metabolites, both showing strong correlations with clinical neuromuscular functional scores, including muscle strength (creatinine ρ = 0.62, p = 0.0001; ADMA ρ = 0.34, p = 0.0124), facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy severity score (creatinine ρ = 0.53, p = 0.0001; ADMA ρ = 0.32, p = 0.0145) and the daily activity limitation ACTIVLIM scale (creatinine ρ = 0.38, p = 0.0035; ADMA ρ = 0.35, p = 0.008). Plasma levels of GDF15, a biomarker commonly used to support the diagnosis of mitochondrial diseases, were modestly but significantly elevated in patients versus controls (542.3 pg/mL ± 277.2 vs. 444.4 pg/mL ± 164.5, p = 0.043). Further analysis of a predefined mitochondria-related metabolite panel showed coordinated alterations involving mitochondrial metabolic pathways and discriminated FSHD1 patients from controls (best AUC = 0.83).

Conclusions

These findings highlight systemic metabolic disturbances already detectable in mild-to-moderate stages of facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy, identifying creatinine and ADMA as promising biomarkers of disease severity, and expand current knowledge of disease pathophysiology.

Trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06086548.

title: Effects of Combined Blood Flow Restriction and Inter-Effort Recovery Hypoxia On Repeated-Sprint Performance And Physiological Responses: A Randomized And Single-Blinded Crossover Trial.
authorString: Carvalho CD, Putti GM, Ihsan M, Scott BR, Peeling P, Papoti M, Girard O.
abstractText: We investigated the acute effects of local and/or systemic hypoxia on performance and psycho-physiological responses during repeated cycle sprints. Eleven physically active young adults (six men, five women) performed four sessions on separate days, each involving three sets of five 5-s all-out efforts on a cycle ergometer (25 seconds rest between efforts and 5 minutes rest between sets). Sessions were conducted under four conditions, combining blood flow restriction [BFR; 45% of arterial occlusion pressure (AOP)] or control (CON; 5% of AOP) applied bilaterally to the legs during sprints, with inter-effort recovery hypoxia [IEH; inspired oxygen fraction (FiO<sub>2</sub>) = 13.5%] or normoxia (NOR; FiO<sub>2</sub> = 20.9%). Power output decreased across sprints and heart rate increased over sets, with no differences between conditions (Δ = -9.18%). IEH resulted in lower peripheral oxygen saturation (Δ = -8.0%) but higher oxygen uptake (Δ = 6.7 mL·kg<sup>-1</sup> min<sup>-1</sup>) and minute ventilation (Δ = 6.1 L·kg<sup>-1</sup> min<sup>-1</sup>), compared to normoxic conditions. Blood lactate concentration increased (Δ = 6.5 mM) post-session similarly across all conditions. Vastus lateralis muscle oxygenation during sprints and inter-set recovery was comparable across conditions, although the mean tissue saturation index during inter-set recovery was lower in BFR + IEH versus CON + NOR conditions (Δ = -4.0%). Ratings of perceived exertion (Δ = 22.5%), limb discomfort (Δ = 34.2%), and breathing difficulty (Δ = 43.7%) increased throughout the sets, independently of conditions. Despite physiological and perceptual adjustments across sprint repetitions, neither BFR during sprints nor systemic hypoxia during recovery altered mechanical output in physically active individuals.

title: Clinical Services Provided by Pharmacists in Primary Health Care in Latin America: A Scoping Review.
authorString: Barrozo YS, Nascimento BF, Mendonça VS, de Matos GC, Valerio CC, Gomes LR, Torres F, Lima EC, Teixeira CA, Lopes LPN, Ramos-Silva A.

journal.title: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice

abstractText:
Objective

To map and characterise evidence on pharmacist-provided clinical services in primary health care in Latin America, including service types, practice settings, study designs, team integration, populations, outcomes, and equity-related dimensions.

Methods

This scoping review followed JBI methodological guidance and PRISMA-ScR. Bibliographic databases and grey literature sources were searched without language or publication date restrictions according to a prospectively registered protocol. Two reviewers independently screened records and charted data. Multiple classifications per study were permitted when applicable. Findings were synthesised descriptively and narratively.

Results

We included 134 studies from six countries, 107 of which were conducted in Brazil. Among 140 study-design classifications, randomised controlled trials (n = 26), cross-sectional studies (n = 23), mixed-methods studies (n = 21), and qualitative studies (n = 20) predominated. Among 137 study-setting classifications, primary health care units (n = 80) and community pharmacies linked to primary care (n = 29) were most frequent. The 168 study-service entries most commonly represented pharmacotherapeutic follow-up (n = 54), health education (n = 35), medication review (n = 20), and clinically oriented dispensing (n = 19); seven could not be clearly classified. Service, process, or management indicators accounted for 87 of 182 study-outcome classifications. Among 136 team-integration entries, referral-based (n = 54) and isolated (n = 35) models predominated. Only 26 studies reported an equity-related variable.

Conclusions

Most of the mapped studies were conducted in Brazilian primary health care settings, with comparatively few studies from other Latin American countries. Future research should examine service integration, equity, economic outcomes, and sustainability across diverse health-system contexts in the region.

title: 2D U-Net Framework for Multiclass Automated Segmentation of Healthy Structures, Ischemic Stroke, and Glioblastoma in the Rat Brain.
authorString: Ortega-Espina S, Fernández-Rodicio S, Alonso-Alonso ML, García-Acevedo P, Sampedro-Viana A, Bazarra-Barreiros M, Abengoza-Bello MT, Mosqueira AJ, Porto-Álvarez J, Fernández JM, Oblitas CM, Castillo J, Hervella P, Iglesias-Rey R.
abstractText: Rodents are essential for preclinical brain disease research, including stroke, tumors, and neurodegenerative disorders. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) enables longitudinal brain tissue visualization, but accurate segmentation is crucial for meaningful analysis. This study introduces a multitask 2D U-Net, a convolutional neural network designed for automated segmentation and quantification of brain regions, ischemic stroke lesions, and tumors in rats using T<sub>2</sub>-weighted imaging (T<sub>2</sub>-wi) and T<sub>2</sub>-relaxation maps. The model was evaluated on the following three MRI datasets: (i) segmentation of multiple brain regions in healthy rats, (ii) ischemic stroke lesions using T<sub>2</sub>-relaxation maps, and (iii) glioblastoma tumors using T<sub>2</sub>-wi. Performance was assessed using the Dice coefficient (DC), Hausdorff distance (HD), sensitivity (SEN), and volume ratio (VR), comparing network outputs against semiautomatic ground truths and existing models. A total of 1949 images from 111 rats were analyzed, expanded to 5847 through data augmentation. After correcting an animal-level train/test partitioning that prevented data leakage between subjects, the model achieved robust accuracy across all tasks (DC = 0.80-0.96, HD = 0.83-2.16 mm, SEN = 0.75-0.96, VR = 0.89-1.10), showing a strong correlation ( ρ=0.82-0.99 ) with manual annotations. This framework improves segmentation accuracy, robustness, and applicability across different MRI settings and conditions, addressing issues like interrater variability and time inefficiency when analyzing rodent brain MRI data. Datasets are publicly available at https://github.com/NOBEL-MRI/Rat-Datasets.

title: Focus Where It Matters: Design and Implementation of a Physiology-Based Care Pathway for Traumatic Shock.
authorString: Noonan M, Mathew J, Hendel S, Underhill A, Miller JP, Cass A, Thomson H, Bannon-Murphy H, Fitzgerald M.
abstractText:
Objective

Traumatic shock lacks a consensus definition, and in blunt-predominant systems its causes are heterogeneous. Simple physiological parameters remain the most universally available basis for early recognition. We describe the design and staged implementation of a physiology-based care pathway for traumatic shock and evaluate its implementation through staff experience.

Methods

Single-centre quality-improvement and implementation project at an Australian Level 1 trauma centre, reported per SQUIRE 2.0. The pathway comprised physiology-based activation (systolic blood pressure ≤ 90 mmHg, shock index > 1, prehospital blood or senior clinician concern), structured pre-arrival preparation, trauma bay and equipment standardisation, task-based team roles, prioritised life-saving interventions and senior-led disposition, supported by simulation and embedded quality improvement. Components were implemented between June and November 2022. Evaluation comprised pre-intervention (2021) and post-implementation (2025) staff surveys, summarised as top-box favourability, with cross-sectional characterisation of the shocked cohort. Clinical effectiveness was not assessed.

Results

Of 3667 major trauma patients, 324 (8.8%) met shocked trauma criteria; these patients were younger, more severely injured and had markedly higher mortality (emergency department death 6.8% vs. 0.4%). Favourable ratings of trauma bay equipment and environment rose from approximately one-quarter to 87.0%. Post-implementation, staff reported high favourability for timely life-saving interventions (88.9%), pathway embedding (85.2%) and role confidence (86.5%). Leadership clarity, communication and reliable debriefing did not improve and were identified as ongoing targets.

Conclusions

A physiology-based traumatic shock pathway was feasibly implemented and embedded, with high staff-reported readiness and clear targets for refinement. Effectiveness remains to be established.

title: Response to Liu Fangfang on 'Haemostatic Balance and Transfusion Strategies in ALF and ACLF: A Systematic Review'.
authorString: Ferdinande K, Zanetto A, Senzolo M.
