title: Association Between Colchicine Use and Clinical Outcomes Post Cardiac Surgery: A Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
authorString: Jaiswal V, Hanif M, Raja HAA, Khadka S, Deb N, Mashkoor Y, Ahmed A, Rajak K, Jaiswal AK, Gupta M, Hirji S, Fonarow GC, Qamar A.

journal.title: American journal of cardiovascular drugs : drugs, devices, and other interventions

abstractText:
Background

Colchicine has been shown to mitigate inflammation and reduce adverse cardiovascular events. However, evidence from clinical trials has been mixed regarding its efficacy in cardiovascular prevention among patients undergoing cardiac surgery.

Objective

We aimed to evaluate the association between colchicine use and cardiovascular outcomes in patients undergoing cardiac surgery.

Methods

We conducted a systematic literature search on various electronic databases for relevant studies from their inception until July 15, 2025. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) with two arms-one with colchicine as an intervention and the other with placebo-in patients undergoing cardiac surgery were included. Risk ratios (RRs) and weighted mean differences (WMDs), along with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), were pooled using a random-effects model. A p value of < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

Results

Nine RCTs with 2005 patients (990 in the colchicine group and 1015 in the placebo group) were included. The mean age was 62.8 years. Pooled analysis demonstrated that compared with placebo, colchicine was significantly associated with a reduction in the risk of postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) (RR 0.70 [95% CI 0.59-0.83], p < 0.001). However, between the groups, there was no statistically significant difference in the risk of all-cause mortality (ACM) (RR 0.81 [95% CI 0.39-1.69], p = 0.57, I2 = 0%), stroke (RR 1.86 [95% CI 0.48-7.12], p = 0.37), and permanent pacemaker implantation (PPM) (RR 1.36 [95% CI 0.08-22.44], p = 0.83). Length of hospital stay, which was exploratory, was significantly shorter in the colchicine group (WMD - 1.16 [95% CI - 1.89 to - 0.44], p < 0.01) compared to placebo.

Conclusion

This meta-analysis demonstrates that colchicine appears to reduce the risk of POAF. However, it does not significantly affect the risks in terms of PPM, ACM, or stroke.

Registration

PROSPERO identifier no. CRD420251117966.

title: Effect of cardiac-index guided intraoperative haemodynamic therapy on postoperative outcome in non-cardiac surgery patients - a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Omuro PK, Dinges HC, Kammerer T.
abstractText:
Background

Optimal perioperative haemodynamic management is essential to reduce postoperative complications. While multiple technologies allow for advanced monitoring, clear evidence on the effectiveness of Cardiac Index-guided goal-directed therapy (CI-GDT) compared to standard care in non-cardiac surgery is lacking. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to investigate the impact of CI-GDT on postoperative outcome.

Methods

A systematic search using PubMed and Web of Science (2010-2025) identified randomised controlled trials (RCT) comparing CI-GDT to standard care in adult non-cardiac surgery. Study selection and data extraction were conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and registered under PROSPERO (CRD420251058399). Odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) and 95% prediction intervals (PI) were calculated using a random-effects model. Risk of bias was assessed via the RoB 2 tool. Heterogeneity was quantified with I2, τ2, and Cochran's Q. Reporting bias was evaluated by funnel plots, Egger's test, and trim-and-fill method. Sensitivity was assessed by leave-one-out analysis.

Results

Twenty-one RCTs were included, of which 20 contributed data to the meta-analysis of postoperative complications. CI-GDT significantly reduced the incidence of postoperative complications (OR .59 [.45-.78]; PI .20-1.74; I2 = 62.9%). Mortality did not differ significantly between groups (OR 0.77 [.57-1.05]; I2 = 0%). Funnel plot and Egger's test indicated no significant publication bias (p=.15). Leave-one-out analysis confirmed robustness of findings. Trim-and-fill did not suggest missing studies. Certainty of evidence was graded high.

Discussion/conclusion

CI-GDT was associated with a lower incidence of patients experiencing at least one postoperative complication, whereas mortality did not differ significantly. However, substantial heterogeneity and a prediction interval crossing the null indicate that the benefit may not be consistent across clinical settings. These findings do not establish an independent advantage of CI targeting over other GDT strategies.

title: Peripheral Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor Changes and Clinical Response to Electroconvulsive Therapy and Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation in Major Depressive Disorder: A Systematic Review.
authorString: Galindo CD, Jemar G, Osorio IC, Lopez A, Uribe Zapata M, Gonzalez Perez L, Villamil Montejo SD, Carvajal Angarita LA.
abstractText: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a leading contributor to the global burden of disease, and a substantial proportion of patients experience inadequate responses to conventional treatments. Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), a key regulator of neuronal survival and synaptic plasticity, has been investigated as a potential biomarker of antidepressant response. However, its clinical relevance following brain stimulation remains uncertain. This systematic review evaluated changes in peripheral BDNF concentrations and their association with clinical outcomes following electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) and repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) in adults with MDD. The review followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines, and searches were conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE (Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online), PsycINFO, and LILACS (Latin America and the Caribbean Literature on Health Sciences). Study selection and data extraction were independently performed by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved through consensus or consultation with a third reviewer. Eleven studies met the eligibility criteria, including two randomized controlled trials and nine non-randomized investigations. Due to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, a meta-analysis was not performed, and findings were synthesized narratively. Peripheral BDNF responses varied across interventions, biological matrices, and sampling intervals. While many studies reported increased serum or plasma BDNF following ECT, others documented substantial clinical improvement without corresponding biomarker changes. Evidence following rTMS was less consistent, with insufficient data to establish a reliable association between BDNF changes and antidepressant response. Overall, peripheral BDNF changes did not consistently parallel clinical improvement, and current evidence does not support their use as a standalone biomarker of antidepressant response. Further adequately powered studies with standardized biomarker measurements and longitudinal clinical assessments are warranted.

title: Statin Use and Age-related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Disease Outcomes.
authorString: Magalhães PLM, Rassi T, Amaral DC, Veiga DM, Oliveira AKR, Gonzalez JVP, Silva LO, Caixeta GL, Maia M, Louzada RN.
abstractText:
Topic

This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association between statin use and the prevalence, incidence, and progression of age-related macular degeneration (AMD).

Clinical relevance

AMD is a major cause of vision loss in older adults, many of whom receive statins for cardiovascular prevention.

Methods

We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library through October 2025 for randomized trials and cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies with comparators. We assessed risk of bias with tools appropriate to each design and pooled effect measures separately using random-effects models. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO.

Results

Twenty-eight studies included 1,918,120 participants. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) for the prevalence of any, early, and late AMD were 1.03 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.86-1.24), 1.10 (95% CI, 0.92-1.31), and 0.75 (95% CI, 0.46-1.25), respectively. For incidence of any AMD, the pooled hazard ratio (HR) was 1.04 (95% CI, 0.82-1.31) and the OR was 0.76 (95% CI, 0.43-1.34), with substantial heterogeneity. For neovascular AMD incidence, different study subsets suggested lower hazard (HR, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.60-0.85) and higher risk (risk ratio, 1.31; 95% CI, 1.18-1.44); the OR was inconclusive (0.93; 95% CI, 0.82-1.05). Progression evidence was limited and heterogeneous. Ten of 12 longitudinal nonrandomized studies had serious overall risk of bias.

Conclusion

The evidence was of very low certainty and insufficient to establish a protective or harmful effect of statins on AMD. These findings do not support prescribing statins specifically for AMD or discontinuing otherwise indicated therapy.

title: Phase 3 clinical development of semaglutide (2015-2026): a comprehensive evidence-based review of trial designs, therapeutic outcomes and global clinical experience.
authorString: Patel SK, Dubey S, Tiwari A.
abstractText: Semaglutide, a long-acting glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA), has become an important therapeutic agent for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), obesity, and associated cardiometabolic complications. Its prolonged pharmacological activity and availability as subcutaneous and oral formulations have supported extensive clinical development across diverse populations. This review critically evaluates Phase 3, Phase 3a, and Phase 3b clinical trials (CTs) assessing the efficacy, safety and therapeutic utility of semaglutide, with an emphasis on the SUSTAIN, PIONEER, STEP, SELECT, FLOW, SOUL and related programmes. Eligible trials were assessed according to study design, registration, treatment duration, population characteristics, interventions, comparators, primary endpoints, adverse events (AEs) and clinical significance. Collectively, the evidence demonstrates clinically meaningful improvements in glycaemic control and body weight, as well as cardiovascular and renal benefits, in selected populations. Evidence from obesity and post-bariatric studies further supports its expanding therapeutic role beyond conventional glucose management. Gastrointestinal events, particularly nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and constipation, were the predominant adverse effects, while overall tolerability remained consistent with the established GLP-1RA profile. However, differences in populations, treatment duration, comparators and endpoint definitions highlight important evidence gaps. This review synthesises Phase 3 clinical evidence to define the evolving therapeutic position, safety profile and future research priorities for semaglutide.

title: Cangrelor versus crushed ticagrelor in acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (DAPT-SHOCK-AMI): a randomised, double-blind trial.
authorString: Motovska Z, Hlinomaz O, Mrozek J, Akin I, Kala P, Montalescot G, Hromadka M, Geisler T, Precek J, Kettner J, Cervinka P, Katina S, Pudil J, Olivier CB, Bis J, Matejka J, Bartus S, Jarkovsky J, Vodzinska A, Tomasov P, Zohoor A, Andrasova A, Kovarik A, Kochman J, Souckova L, Tousek P, Vulev I, Kubica J, Ostadal P, Ducrocq G, Coufal Z, Rokyta R, Marinov I, Demlova R, Karpisek M, Klimsa Z, Hudec M, Widimsky P, Bhatt DL, DAPT-SHOCK-AMI study group.
abstractText:
Background

Acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) can compromise the administration and absorption of oral P2Y12 inhibitors and carries high ischaemic and mortality risks. This trial assessed whether intravenous cangrelor was non-inferior to crushed oral ticagrelor for short-term clinical outcomes and whether it provided faster and more consistent platelet inhibition in patients with AMI-CS.

Methods

DAPT-SHOCK-AMI was a double-blind trial conducted at 29 hospitals across five European countries (Czech Republic, France, Germany, Poland, and Slovakia). Patients older than 18 years with AMI-CS were randomly assigned (1:1 ratio, stratified by centre, age, sex, presence or absence of ST-segment elevation, and mechanical ventilation) to cangrelor (30 μg/kg bolus followed by an infusion of 4 μg/kg per min for at least 2 h) or crushed ticagrelor (180 mg loading dose). The primary laboratory endpoint was a platelet reactivity index of less than 50% at the end of primary percutaneous coronary intervention. The primary clinical endpoint was death, myocardial infarction, or ischaemic stroke at 30 days. The primary clinical endpoint was analysed for non-inferiority with a prespecified margin of 1 percentage point among all randomly assigned patients who received study treatment. The study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03551964) and EudraCT (2018-002161-19); recruitment and 1-year follow-up are complete, and 5-year follow-up is ongoing.

Findings

Between Aug 1, 2018, and Jan 19, 2024, 605 patients (137 [23%] were female) were randomly assigned to cangrelor (n=298) or ticagrelor (n=307); no surviving patients were lost to the 1-year follow-up. The primary laboratory endpoint was analysed in 56 (19%) patients in the cangrelor group and 68 (22%) in the ticagrelor group, and was achieved in 56 (100%) of 56 patients receiving cangrelor and 15 (22%) of 68 receiving ticagrelor (p<0·0001). The 30-day primary clinical endpoint occurred in 112 (38%) of 298 patients receiving cangrelor and 126 (41%) of 307 receiving ticagrelor; non-inferiority was not demonstrated (difference -4 percentage points [90% CI -10 to 3]; Pnon-inferiority=0·13). Major bleeding at 30 days occurred in 19 (6%) of 298 patients receiving cangrelor and 16 (5%) of 307 receiving ticagrelor.

Interpretation

To our knowledge, this is the first randomised trial to compare P2Y12 inhibitor strategies specifically in patients with AMI-CS. Cangrelor achieved effective platelet inhibition more frequently than crushed ticagrelor at the end of primary percutaneous coronary intervention. Non-inferiority of cangrelor versus crushed ticagrelor was not demonstrated for the primary 30-day clinical endpoint. These trial findings can inform future trials of P2Y12 inhibition strategies in patients with AMI-CS.

Funding

Czech Republic Ministry of Health, Charles University (Czech Republic), and NextGenerationEU.

title: Amrecibart and cenvacibart for the prevention of catheter-related thrombosis (ROXI-CATH): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial.
authorString: Zwicker JI, Kithcart AP, Kaplan J, Banerjee P, Vyas K, Chalothorn D, Raya JG, Li S, Fredenburgh LE, Mocan M, Razboynikov R, Morton LG, Gutstein DE, Musgrave KM, Piazza G, ROXI-CATH Trial Investigators.
abstractText:
Background

Peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs) are often complicated by venous thromboembolism, yet no thromboprophylaxis is approved. Factor XI (FXI) inhibition might prevent catheter-associated venous thromboembolism without increasing bleeding. We evaluated the safety and efficacy of amrecibart and cenvacibart for preventing venous thromboembolism after PICC placement.

Methods

ROXI-CATH is a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial conducted across 12 hospital centres in Bulgaria, Canada, Israel, Romania, the UK, and the USA. Eligible participants aged 18 years or older undergoing PICC insertion, with the PICC expected to remain for at least 14 days, and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 2 or less were randomly assigned (1:1:1) using a permuted block design and stratified by site and diagnosis of active cancer to receive a single intravenous infusion of amrecibart (300 mg; anti-FXI A2 domain monoclonal antibody), cenvacibart (250 mg; anti-FXI catalytic domain monoclonal antibody), or placebo. Participants, principal investigators, and study site staff were masked to treatment assignment. The primary efficacy outcome was adjudicated venous thromboembolism (symptomatic or asymptomatic PICC-associated deep vein thrombosis or superficial vein thrombosis, or pulmonary embolism, including pulmonary embolism-related death) up to day 14. Ultrasounds were performed on days 7 and 14. The key secondary efficacy outcome was adjudicated thrombosis detected by ultrasound in the upper extremity with the PICC up to day 14. The primary safety outcome was site-reported treatment-emergent adverse events up to the end of the study. The key secondary safety outcomes were adjudicated major and clinically relevant non-major (CRNM) bleeding up to day 14. Efficacy analyses were performed in the full analysis set, which consisted of all randomly assigned participants who received any study drug and with any evaluable post-baseline ultrasound or a confirmed episode of venous thromboembolism. Safety analyses were performed in the safety analysis set, which included all randomly assigned participants who received any study drug (as treated). This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06299111 (completed; these analyses were performed after database lock on May 6, 2026).

Findings

Between Sept 20, 2024, and Dec 19, 2025, 240 participants were screened, and 195 were randomly assigned to amrecibart (n=65), cenvacibart (n=66), or placebo (n=64). One participant in the placebo group who did not receive study treatment and had no evaluable ultrasound was excluded from the full analysis set. The median follow-up time was 100 days (IQR 100-103). The median age was 60 years (49-69), and 89 (46%) of 194 participants were female, 105 (54%) were male, and 192 (99%) were White. Adjudicated venous thromboembolism up to day 14 occured in 13 (20%) of 65 participants in the amrecibart group (odds ratio [OR] 0·37 [90% credible interval 0·18-0·65]), 13 (20%) of 66 participants in the cenvacibart group (0·36 [0·17-0·64]) compared with 27 (43%) of 63 participants in the placebo group. Adjudicated PICC-associated venous thromboembolism up to day 14 occurred in 12 (18%) participants in the amrecibart group (OR 0·30 [95% CI 0·14-0·67]), 13 (20%) participants in the cenvacibart group (0·32 [0·14-0·69]), compared with 27 (43%) participants in the placebo group. Site-reported treatment-emergent adverse events up to day 100 occurred in 45 (69%) participants in the amrecibart group, 42 (64%) participants in the cenvacibart group, and 48 (76%) participants in the placebo group. No participants had major bleeding up to day 14. CRNM bleeding up to day 14 occurred in two (3%) participants in the amrecibart group, two (3%) in the cenvacibart group, and two (3%) in the placebo group. Serious adverse events occurred in nine (14%) participants in the ambrecibart group, six (9%) in the cenvacibart group, and ten (16%) in the placebo group. One (2%) participant in the amrecibart group, four (6%) participants in the cenvacibart group, and two (3%) participants in the placebo group died; these deaths were assessed as not related to treatment by the respective investigators.

Interpretation

A single infusion of amrecibart or cenvacibart reduced the incidence of venous thromboembolism following PICC insertion, suggesting FXI inhibition at the A2 or catalytic domain as a promising prophylactic strategy for contact-mediated thrombosis.

Funding

Regeneron Pharmaceuticals.

title: Statin-Ezetimibe Combination Therapy versus Statin Monotherapy in Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: A Prespecified Secondary Analysis of the Randomized Ez-PAVE Trial.
authorString: Lee SH, Byun YS, Kim JW, Park JH, Cho JM, Kang WC, Yoon HJ, Kim WH, Lee SJ, Lee JB, Jang JY, Shin S, Park IH, Kwon SU, Kim S, Lee YJ, Lee SJ, Hong SJ, Ahn CM, Kim JS, Ko YG, Choi D, Hong MK, Jang Y, Kim GS, Kim BK, Ez-PAVE investigators.
abstractText:
Background

In a target-directed low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C)-lowering strategy, the impact of the initial treatment regimen has not been investigated in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. We compared the efficacy and safety of initial statin-ezetimibe combination therapy versus statin monotherapy within intensive or conventional LDL-C-targeting strategies.

Methods

In this prespecified second randomization of the randomized Ez-PAVE trial (Effects of Ezetimibe Combination Therapy for Patients With Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: Randomized Comparison of LDL Cholesterol Targeting <70 versus <55 mg/dL) conducted at 17 centers in South Korea, a total of 3048 patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease were enrolled between January 2021 and July 2022. Following the first randomization to either an intensive (<55 mg/dL) or conventional (<70 mg/dL) LDL-C-targeting strategy, patients underwent subsequent randomization (initial statin-ezetimibe combination therapy [n=1525] versus statin monotherapy [n=1523]) and were followed up for 3 years. Lipid-lowering therapy was adjusted according to a predefined protocol to achieve LDL-C targets. The primary end point was a 3-year composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, any revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina.

Results

The mean±SD age was 64.4±9.0 years, and 638 patients (20.9%) were female. The incidence of the primary end point did not differ between statin-ezetimibe combination therapy (128 patients [8.5%]) and statin monotherapy (119 patients [7.9%]; hazard ratio, 1.07 [95% CI, 0.83-1.37]; P=0.596). Patients who received statin-ezetimibe combination therapy achieved lower median LDL-C levels during follow-up than those who received statin monotherapy in both the intensive-targeting (53 mg/dL [interquartile range, 45-62 mg/dL] versus 62 mg/dL [interquartile range, 53-74 mg/dL]) and conventional-targeting (63 mg/dL [interquartile range, 55-73 mg/dL] versus 70 mg/dL [interquartile range, 62-81 mg/dL]) strategies. During follow-up, ezetimibe was added to the treatment regimen of 241 patients (34.3%) and 177 patients (24.8%) who initially received statin monotherapy in the intensive- and conventional-targeting strategies, respectively. The treatment effect of intensive-targeting versus conventional-targeting strategies was consistent regardless of therapy regimens without significant heterogeneity (Pinteraction=0.583). The safety end points were similar between the groups.

Conclusions

Within a target-directed LDL-C-lowering strategy, cardiovascular efficacy and safety did not differ significantly, whether initiated as statin-ezetimibe combination therapy or as statin monotherapy, but combination therapy facilitated achievement of a lower LDL-C target.

Registration

URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04626973.

title: Multimodality Cardiac Imaging Substudy of the DAPT-SHOCK-AMI Randomized Trial: Echocardiographic and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Assessment of Cangrelor versus Crushed Ticagrelor in Cardiogenic Shock Complicating Acute Myocardial Infarction.
authorString: Motovska Z, Ionita O, Guglielmo M, Hromadka M, Baxa J, Tarantini R, Kotrc M, Panovsky R, Geisler T, Novak M, Weichet J, Kautznerova D, Kuchynka P, Ondrus T, Montalescot G, Jarkovsky J, Lhotsky J, Ajmone Marsan N, Vichova T, Klofac P, Andrasova A, Nijveldt R, Cani M, Precek J, Gajdusek L, Masek M, Penicka M, Bartus S, Tudos Z, Kettner J, Hlinomaz O, Belohlavek J, Kala P, Tomasov P, Bhatt DL, DAPT-SHOCK-AMI Multimodality Imaging Substudy Investigators.
abstractText:
Background

In acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS), the myocardium sustains a dual injury: ischemia of the culprit territory and global hypoperfusion from low cardiac output. Whether platelet inhibition at reperfusion affects the microcirculation, the infarct, the noninfarcted myocardium, and ventricular function, and over what time course, has not been examined with serial imaging. The prespecified multimodality imaging substudy of the randomized DAPT-SHOCK-AMI trial (intravenous cangrelor versus crushed oral ticagrelor) addressed this question.

Methods

Patients at prespecified imaging sites underwent serial echocardiography (208 enrolled; evaluable examinations in 175, 120, and 99 patients in the acute phase, at 1 month, and at 1 year) and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR; 93 enrolled; 73, 68, and 63); 81 patients (40 and 41) underwent both modalities. Blinded core laboratories analyzed all studies. The primary imaging endpoint was microvascular obstruction (MVO) on acute CMR, evaluable in 60 patients; secondary endpoints were infarct size, native T1 of the global, infarcted, and remote myocardium, left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction (LVEF), global longitudinal strain (GLS), E/e', and left atrial volume, and their changes. Comparisons between the cangrelor and crushed ticagrelor arms used covariate-adjusted logistic or linear regression; the substudy was not separately powered.

Results

The odds of acute MVO were lower with cangrelor (adjusted odds ratio 0.27 [95% CI 0.08 to 0.98]; P=0.023). Infarct size did not differ between the arms. At 1 year, native T1 of the remote myocardium was lower with cangrelor (adjusted mean 1114 [95% CI 1057 to 1171] versus 1171 [1115 to 1228] ms; P=0.005). Over 1 year, LVEF increased more with cangrelor on echocardiography (37.9% versus 21.7% of the acute value; adjusted P=0.046) and CMR (15.8% versus 2.1%; P=0.027), with greater improvement in GLS, lower E/e', and less left atrial enlargement; no parameter differed between the arms at 1 month.

Conclusions

In AMI-CS, serial multimodality imaging characterized microvascular, tissue-level, and functional injury over 1 year. Cangrelor was associated with less acute MVO, lower remote native T1, and more complete recovery of LV function than crushed ticagrelor, without a difference in infarct size; these hypothesis-generating findings suggest differences in the microcirculation and non-infarcted myocardial injury but do not establish a treatment mechanism.

title: Long-Term Survival After Initial Invasive or Conservative Management of Stable Coronary Disease in ISCHEMIA-EXTEND.
authorString: Hochman JS, Anthopolos R, Reynolds HR, Bangalore S, Xu Y, O'Brien SM, Boumakis S, Chang M, Rosenberg Y, Senior R, Banfield A, Goodman SG, Lopes RD, Pracon R, Lopez-Sendon J, Steg PG, Maggioni AP, Newman JD, Berger JS, Sidhu MS, White HD, Troxel AB, Harrington RA, Boden WE, Stone GW, Mark DB, Spertus JA, Maron DJ, ISCHEMIA-EXTEND Research Group.
abstractText:
Importance

It is unknown whether routine invasive management of chronic coronary disease improves long-term survival when added to guideline-directed medical therapy.

Objective

To compare the effects of initial invasive and conservative strategies on long-term mortality in patients with chronic coronary disease.

Design, setting, and participants

In this long-term follow-up study of the International Study of Comparative Health Effectiveness with Medical and Invasive Approaches (ISCHEMIA), an international trial of patients with chronic coronary disease, moderate or severe ischemia, left ventricular ejection fraction of 35% or more, and no left main coronary artery disease, unacceptable angina, or recent acute coronary syndrome, participants were randomized at 320 sites in 37 countries beginning August 2012 and followed up through December 2025. Data were analyzed using the intention-to-treat principle.

Intervention

ISCHEMIA randomized patients to an initial invasive strategy of guideline-directed medical therapy plus coronary angiography and revascularization (when feasible) or an initial conservative strategy with guideline-directed medical therapy alone, with invasive management for failure of medical therapy.

Main outcomes and measures

All-cause, cardiovascular, and noncardiovascular mortality were analyzed using cumulative incidence estimates, Cox and Fine-Gray models, bayesian analysis, and restricted mean survival time.

Results

Among 5179 participants, median age was 64 (IQR, 58-70) years; 23% were female, 42% had diabetes, and median ejection fraction was 60% (IQR, 55%-65%). During 9-year median follow-up (range, 1 day to 13.4 years), 1071 deaths occurred (782 during extended follow-up): 672 cardiovascular, 359 noncardiovascular, and 40 unclassified. All-cause 11-year mortality was not significantly different between groups (25.8% invasive vs 26.9% conservative; estimated difference, -1.0 percentage point [95% CI, -4.2 to 2.1 percentage points]; adjusted hazard ratio [AHR], 0.97 [95% CI, 0.86-1.09]). By bayesian analysis, the posterior probability of more than 1 percentage-point survival benefit to invasive vs conservative was low (18%). Cardiovascular mortality at 11 years was 15.8% in the invasive group vs 17.1% in the conservative group (estimated difference, -1.4 percentage points [95% CI, -4.0 to 1.3 percentage points]; AHR, 0.88 [95% CI, 0.75-1.02]). Noncardiovascular mortality at 11 years was 9.1% in the invasive group vs 8.1% in the conservative group (estimated difference, 1.0 percentage point [95% CI, -0.9 to 2.9 percentage points]; AHR, 1.18 [95% CI, 0.96-1.45]). Eleven-year restricted mean survival was not significantly different (estimated difference, 14 days [95% CI, -41 to 70 days]).

Conclusions and relevance

In this study, long-term all-cause mortality in patients with high-risk chronic coronary disease was not significantly different after routine invasive vs initial conservative management.

Trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04894877.

title: Long-Term Survival After Initial Invasive or Conservative Management of Stable Coronary Disease in Patients With Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease: ISCHEMIA-CKD EXTEND.
authorString: Bangalore S, Maron DJ, Anthopolos R, Reynolds HR, Xu Y, Chang M, Boumakis S, Lopez-Sendon J, Senior R, Goodman SG, O'Brien SM, Fleg JL, Hochman JS, ISCHEMIA-CKD EXTEND Research Group.
abstractText:
Background

In the ISCHEMIA-CKD trial (International Study of Comparative Health Effectiveness With Medical and Invasive Approaches-Chronic Kidney Disease), at a median follow-up of 2.2 years, the primary composite outcome of death or nonfatal myocardial infarction was similar between an initial invasive strategy (INV) compared with an initial conservative strategy (CON) in patients with moderate or severe myocardial ischemia and advanced chronic kidney disease. However, the long-term outcomes comparing the 2 strategies are unknown.

Methods

Participants in the ISCHEMIA-CKD trial were randomly assigned to either INV, involving coronary angiography and revascularization when feasible, added to guideline-directed medical therapy or to CON with guideline-directed medical therapy alone and invasive procedures reserved for failure of guideline-directed medical therapy. After the active intervention trial phase, long-term vital status follow-up was conducted through participant contact by participating sites and by health record and centralized death database searches. The primary outcome for the extended follow-up phase was all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes were cause-specific mortality, including cardiovascular and noncardiovascular mortality.

Results

Among the 777 participants randomized (388 to INV and 389 to CON), over a median of 8 years of follow-up, vital status retention among survivors was 95%. There was a total of 429 deaths (55%). Cumulative all-cause mortality (57.4% versus 56.8%; adjusted hazard ratio, 1.05 [95% CI, 0.87-1.28]) or cardiovascular mortality (40.3% versus 38.4%; adjusted hazard ratio, 1.06 [95% CI, 0.84-1.34]) at 8 years did not differ between INV and CON. The restricted mean survival time was 1941 days (1834-2047 days) for INV versus 1990 days (1885-2094 days) for CON, with an adjusted estimated difference of -99 days (-245 to 46). The posterior probability of at least a 1 percentage point lower or higher death with INV at the 8-year median follow-up was 28% and 52%, respectively. Similarly, the posterior probability of at least a 1 percentage point lower or higher cardiovascular mortality with INV was 23% and 56%, respectively.

Conclusions

In patients with at least moderate ischemia and advanced chronic kidney disease, there was no significant long-term benefit of an initial INV at reducing the risk of all-cause or cardiovascular mortality compared with an initial conservative strategy.

URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT01985360.

title: EMAIL-HF: Can Digital Strategies Shorten the Path from Scientific Evidence to Clinical Practice in Heart Failure?
authorString: Albuquerque MTA, Guimaraes PO, Tavares CAM, Madrini V, Martins EB, Keramida K, Ojji D, Hosseini K, Monzo L, Musella F, Sakata Y, Canonico ME, Alexy T, Biegus J, Nodari S, Ambrosy A, Lainscak M.
abstractText: A substantial gap persists between scientific evidence and clinical practice in heart failure (HF). Digital solutions have emerged as promising strategies to accelerate the implementation of evidence-based therapies. This mini-review examines the results of the EMAIL-HF study, a registry-based, randomized, controlled, parallel-group clinical trial conducted in Denmark that included patients aged 20 years or older with a diagnosis of HF irrespective of left ventricular ejection fraction, who were not receiving SGLT2 inhibitors (SGLT2i). Participants were randomized to usual care or a digital strategy consisting of an e-mailed letter with information on SGLT2i, followed by contact with an HF specialist. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients redeeming a prescription for dapagliflozin or empagliflozin within 6 months of randomization and the secondary endpoint was a composite of time to first HF hospitalization or death from any cause. The digital strategy significantly increased SGLT2i initiation within 6 months, although no difference in HF hospitalization or all-cause mortality was observed during the 24-month follow-up. Whether these strategies can translate modest improvements in treatment uptake into sustained, scalable, and cost-effective gains across diverse healthcare systems remains uncertain.

title: Extended Analyses of Pelacarsen and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with High Lipoprotein(a).
authorString: Nissen SE, Cho L, Frndak S, Wolski K, Wang J, Manning B, Leitersdorf E, Landmesser U, McCluskey J, Blaha MJ, Lincoff AM, Zhao Z, Mueller-Edenborn B, Nuehrenberg TG, Tsimikas S, Lesogor A, Cao H, Kalahasti V, Laufs U, Baum S, Stroes ES, Shapiro MD, Nordestgaard BG, Nicholls SJ.
abstractText:
Background

Pelacarsen is an antisense oligonucleotide that reduces serum levels of lipoprotein(a). In a randomized placebo-controlled trial in patients with established cardiovascular disease, pelacarsen did not reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events compared to placebo. We further investigated the association of pelacarsen treatment with cardiovascular outcomes.

Methods

We report the association of pelacarsen treatment with a primary composite end point of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or urgent coronary revascularization. Analyses included on-treatment, uninterrupted treatment, total primary end point events (first and recurrent events), landmark analyses classified by changes in and achieved lipoprotein(a) at 3 months, and key subgroups including baseline lipoprotein(a), low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (CRP), and time from qualifying event to enrollment.

Results

For participants on treatment, a primary end point occurred in 434 participants (10.4%) randomly assigned to placebo and 380 participants (9.1%) assigned to pelacarsen (hazard ratio, 0.98; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.85 to 1.12). When evaluating participants with uninterrupted treatment, a primary end point event occurred in 167 participants (11.0%) in the pelacarsen group and 204 participants (10.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.89 to 1.34). When evaluating total primary end point events, there were 644 events in the pelacarsen group and 646 events in the placebo group (rate ratio, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.87 to 1.14). In landmark analyses evaluating participants alive and free of the composite end point at 3 months, when compared to placebo there was no association between pelacarsen treatment and the primary end point either in participants with reduction in lipoprotein(a) greater than or equal to the median (170 nmol/l) (hazard ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.92 to 1.29) or in participants who achieved lipoprotein(a) lower than or equal to the median (69.5 nmol/l) (hazard ratio, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.93 to 1.29). There was also no association between pelacarsen treatment and the primary end point in any of the evaluated key subgroups including classification by median baseline lipoprotein(a), LDL cholesterol, high-sensitivity CRP, or time from qualifying cardiovascular disease to enrollment.

Conclusions

Pelacarsen was not associated with a reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events when evaluated by treatment exposure, changes in or achieved lipoprotein(a) levels at 3 months, considering total events, or within subgroups of baseline lipoprotein(a), LDL cholesterol, or high-sensitivity CRP levels.

title: Saphenofemoral junction reconstruction and recurrence after the treatment of superficial venous reflux disease with endovenous ablation methods.
authorString: Oztas DM, Akbulut D, Ugurlucan M.
abstractText: BackgroundRecurrence of varicosities and reflux-related symptoms after endovenous ablation of the great saphenous vein (GSV) remains common. Standard ablation is delivered 1.5-2 cm distal to the saphenofemoral junction (SFJ), leaving the junctional tributaries and dilated proximal junction untreated, unlike conventional high ligation and stripping. We compared standard endovenous ablation with a technique combining open SFJ reconstruction and endovenous ablation.MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed patients treated for symptomatic primary GSV reflux. Group 1 underwent standard endovenous ablation (at our institution or referred from elsewhere). Group 2 underwent open SFJ reconstruction - ligation of the junctional tributaries, division of the saphenous vein, and reduction of the dilated common femoral vein - plus endovenous ablation of the GSV trunk. The protocol was introduced during the study period and applied selectively and non-randomly; patients with a body mass index ≥30 kg/m2, those aged ≥70 years and those with groin skin infection received standard ablation. Beyond a 3-month review, duplex follow-up was not standardised and was performed mainly when symptoms recurred. Symptomatic recurrence, recurrent visible varicosities, duplex recurrence patterns, reintervention and complications were reported separately.ResultsGroup 1 included 115 patients (70 treated at our institution and 45 referred after treatment elsewhere) and Group 2 included 203. Mean age was 54.3 ± 10.9 and 48.7 ± 14.8 years, and 62.6% and 71.9% were female, respectively. Group 1 had a higher body mass index and more diabetes, hypertension and smoking (all P ≤ .003). During follow-up, 18 patients in Group 1 (15.7%) returned with symptomatic recurrence, compared with 7 (3.4%) in Group 2 (p < .001; adjusted OR 0.14, 95% CI 0.05-0.40). No Group 2 patient showed a patent refluxing GSV trunk. In Group 2, six patients (3.0%) had groin wound complications, four managed with wound care and two requiring surgical revision, and one had a minor groin hematoma; one Group 1 patient developed deep vein thrombosis. There was no pulmonary embolism and no mortality.ConclusionsIn this selected, non-randomised cohort, adding open SFJ reconstruction to endovenous GSV ablation was associated with an acceptable complication rate, at the cost of reintroducing groin wound morbidity, and with lower symptomatic recurrence than standard ablation. Given the baseline imbalance, potential referral bias and non-standardised follow-up, these findings show an association rather than a preventive effect. Whether patients at particularly high risk of SFJ/anterior accessory saphenous vein-related recurrence benefit from this approach should be tested prospectively.

title: Extended Clopidogrel Monotherapy versus Dual Antiplatelet Therapy in Acute Coronary Syndrome Patients With and Without Heart Failure: A Prespecified Subgroup Analysis of the OPT-BIRISK Trial.
authorString: Jiang Z, Li Y, Li J, Wang B, Jing Q, Wang Z, Zhang P, Chen S, Liu B, Zeng H, Zeng Y, Liu A, Qu P, Zeng C, Qiu M, Wang X, Han Y.
abstractText:
Background

The optimal extended antiplatelet strategy after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) in patients with heart failure (HF) remains uncertain.

Methods

In OPT-BIRISK, patients at high ischemic and bleeding risk who completed 9-12 months of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) were randomized to clopidogrel plus placebo or aspirin for 9 months. This analysis compared treatments by recorded HF history. The primary endpoint was Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) types 2, 3, or 5 bleeding; the key secondary endpoint was major adverse cardiac and cerebral events (MACCE).

Results

Of 7,758 patients, 653 (8.4%) had HF history. Without HF, bleeding occurred in 83/3,565 (2.3%) monotherapy recipients and 118/3,540 (3.3%) DAPT recipients (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.53-0.92). With HF, bleeding occurred in 12/308 (3.9%) and 9/345 (2.6%), respectively (HR 1.49, 95% CI 0.63-3.53). MACCE occurred in 90/3,565 (2.5%) versus 120/3,540 (3.4%) patients without HF (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.57-0.98) and 11/308 (3.6%) versus 16/345 (4.6%) patients with HF (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.36-1.66). Interaction P values were 0.1021 for bleeding and 0.9345 for MACCE.

Conclusions

Extended clopidogrel monotherapy reduced clinically relevant bleeding in patients without a history of HF after PCI for ACS. No statistically significant treatment-by-HF interaction was observed for bleeding or MACCE, although HF-specific treatment effects remain inconclusive because of limited events.

title: Smart Alerting in Smartphone-Based First Responder Systems and Arrival Before Emergency Medical Services:The ALARM Randomized Clinical Trial.
authorString: Ganter J, Gronewald J, Heller AR, Trummer G, Brucklacher T, Schmitz D, Busch HJ, Mueller MP.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Smartphone alerting systems (SAS) aim to increase the proportion of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) cases in which a community first responder (CFR) arrives before emergency medical services (EMS). Many use fixed-radius alerts and ignore estimated arrival times. We compared different alerting strategies to maximize CFR arrival before EMS.

Methods

In a prospective, randomized three-arm trial, smart alerting (SMA) was compared with fixed-radius strategies (600 m and 2500 m). The primary endpoint was the rate of CFR arrival before EMS. In the SMA arm, responders were dispatched based on individually estimated travel times versus expected ambulance time. Binary endpoints were analyzed using chi-square tests, reporting risk differences and 95% confidence intervals; continuous endpoints used non-parametric tests.

Results

Across 823 activations, 1482 CFR were dispatched. CFR arrived before EMS in 31%, 57%, and 58% of missions in the 600 m, 2500 m, and SMA groups, respectively. Compared with the 600 m strategy, SMA increased pre-EMS arrival (risk difference +26.8%, 95% CI 18.6-34.4; p < 0.001), whereas no significant difference was observed compared with the 2500 m strategy (risk difference +1.2%, 95% CI -7.0-+9.3; p = 0.80). Response rates were 56%, 83%, and 87%, respectively. In the SMA group, 31% of accepting CFR were excluded because predicted arrival exceeded EMS arrival. Response times were longer with smart alerting reflecting greater dispatch distances.

Conclusions

Smart alerting increased the likelihood of CFR arriving before EMS while reducing dispatches unlikely to achieve pre-EMS arrival. Further research should evaluate its impact on patient outcomes.

title: Leveraging AI-ECG Technology for Early Notification and Tracking of AF Development (LATENT): A Randomized Controlled Trial.
authorString: Lee CC, Lin WY, Liu WT, Chang CH, Liu YL, Chang DW, Liu PY, Liu WC, Lin Y, Tsai DJ, Chen KC, Lin TC, Chang SC, Chen HH, Fang WH, Lin WS, Cheng CC, Lin KH, Chen TW, Lin CY, Tsai YT, Chen YH, Tsai CS, Lin SH, Lin C, Lin CS.
abstractText:
Background

Electrocardiographic analysis aided by artificial intelligence (AI) may identify atrial electrical vulnerability during sinus rhythm. The objective of this study was to determine whether AI-enabled ECG (AI-ECG) is effective for detecting atrial fibrillation (AF), atrial flutter (AFl), or prespecified pre-AF atrial findings in a randomized trial.

Methods

In this single-center, open-label trial, 14 665 adults 40 to 85 years of age without previous AF/AFl were randomized to an AI-ECG-guided strategy or usual care. Participants randomized to AI-ECG who were then identified by AI as having a high-risk sinus-rhythm ECG in the preceding year were offered Holter monitoring for ≤7 days. Each monitored high-risk intervention participant was paired with an age- and sex-matched control selected before control ECGs underwent AI analysis. Matched controls received identical monitoring to reduce ascertainment bias. Reporting cardiologists were blinded to AI results and randomized assignment. The primary outcome was a composite of newly detected AF, AFl, or pre-AF atrial findings within 90 days. Pre-AF atrial findings comprised frequent premature atrial complexes, short runs of premature atrial complexes, or nonsustained AF/AFl.

Results

Among 7337 intervention and 7328 control participants, 84 (1.1%) and 78 (1.1%), respectively, were classified as high risk. Of the 84 high-risk intervention participants, 48 (57.1%) underwent monitoring, as did 48 matched controls. The primary outcome occurred in 54 intervention participants (0.74%) versus 35 control participants (0.48%; odds ratio, 1.54 [95% CI, 1.01-2.37]; P=0.046). Hypothetical reclassification of 1 intervention event to a nonevent changed the primary analysis P value to 0.057. The intervention effect on detection of the primary composite outcome differed by baseline AI-ECG risk (Pinteraction<0.001): 32.1% versus 2.6% among high-risk participants and 0.4% versus 0.5% among low-risk participants. AF/AFl detection (0.3% versus 0.2%) and antiarrhythmic therapy initiation at 180 days (2.3% versus 2.4%) did not differ significantly between the intervention and control groups. Participant-reported monitoring-related adverse events, including skin reactions and discomfort, occurred in 22.9% of monitored intervention participants versus 18.8% of matched controls.

Conclusions

AI-ECG-guided monitoring resulted in a modest increase in the detection of new AF, AFl, or pre-AF atrial findings. However, these findings were fragile statistically and sensitive to reclassification of 1 event. LATENT (Leveraging AI-ECG Technology for Early Notification and Tracking of AF Development) demonstrates the clinical application of AI-ECG risk stratification to guide targeted rhythm surveillance, providing a foundation for larger trials evaluating its impact on patient outcomes.

title: Colchicine in chronic coronary artery disease: effects on vascular glucose uptake, inflammation, remodeling and blood pressure.
authorString: Baldwin SN, Bastrup JA, Muroke V, van der Horst J, Rainville É, Dubik M, Harel F, Cossette M, Guertin MC, Kudryavtseva OS, Saljic A, Rognant S, Dannesboe J, Mozzicato AM, Rhéaume É, Moeller JB, Thomsen MB, Tardif JC, Jepps TA.
abstractText:
Aims

The mechanisms underlying colchicine's cardiovascular benefits in patients with coronary artery disease remain unclear and warrant further translational investigation.

Methods and results

In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 111 patients with chronic coronary artery disease and aortic or carotid target-to-background ratio ≥1.6 were assigned to colchicine 0.6 mg daily (n=55) or placebo (n=56) for 24 weeks. Arterial inflammation was assessed using 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) of the ascending aorta. The primary endpoint was the change in mean maximum target-to-background ratio over 24 weeks. Secondary and exploratory objectives included evaluation of systemic inflammatory markers and blood pressure. To support interpretation of the clinical findings, a complementary hypertensive rodent model, the spontaneously hypertensive rat (SHR), was treated with colchicine for 4 weeks to explore vascular and inflammatory pathways potentially influenced by colchicine using immunohistochemistry, myography and proteomics.Colchicine did not reduce aortic FDG uptake compared with placebo (adjusted mean change 0.05 [95% CI -0.02 to 0.12] vs 0.01 [95% CI -0.06 to 0.08]; p=0.38). In secondary and exploratory analyses, colchicine was associated with a reduction in neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (adjusted mean change -0.36 vs -0.08; p=0.033), a trend toward lower high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (adjusted geometric mean percentage change -28.2% vs -5.8%; p=0.060) and attenuation of increases in systolic (adjusted mean change 0.88 mmHg vs. 4.94 mmHg; p=0.046) and diastolic (1.41 mmHg vs. 4.35 mmHg; p=0.048) blood pressure. In SHRs, colchicine had no effect on the aorta but attenuated the progression of hypertension and reduced inflammation and extracellular matrix remodelling in mesenteric resistance arteries, while enhancing vasodilator responses. Reductions in CXCL10, CXCL2, NLRP3 and IL-18 expression were observed in mesenteric arteries from the SHR following colchicine treatment.

Conclusions

These findings support the hypothesis that vascular effects of colchicine likely extend beyond large conduit arteries, while the specific pathways and relevance to coronary atherosclerosis require further investigation.

title: Medical Complications of Catatonia and Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome: A Systematic Review.
authorString: Daneshvari NO, Cantos A, Gunther M, Shah D, Punko D, Grossman MN, Feig EH, Rogers JP, Luccarelli J, Huffman JC, Smith FA, Fricchione GL, Beach SR.

journal.title: Journal of the Academy of Consultation-Liaison Psychiatry

abstractText:
Background

Catatonia and neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) are related neuropsychiatric conditions linked to diverse and potentially life-threatening medical complications; however, no large-scale review of existing literature has described the types and rates of such complications.

Objective

We aimed to systematically examine documented medical complications associated with catatonia/NMS, delineate their clinical implications, and inform strategies for monitoring and improving patient outcomes.

Methods

Systematic searches of PubMed and Web of Science were conducted up to February 8, 2025 for articles including patients with catatonia or NMS who experienced medical complications. Reviewers independently performed screening and data extraction. Quality assessment was completed via the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Case data were analyzed using descriptive statistics.

Results

281 articles (11 observational studies and 270 case reports/series) met inclusion criteria. Eleven observational studies examined medical complications in 2,008 patients with catatonia/NMS; study quality was low in 1, moderate in 6, and high in 4. Across studies, pneumonia occurred in 0-64% of patients, rhabdomyolysis in 0-30%, and deep vein thrombosis/pulmonary embolus (DVT/PE) in 0-25%, with these complications reported in both malignant and non-malignant presentations. Comparative studies identified catatonia as a significant risk factor for specific complications including DVT and rhabdomyolysis. Case reports/series (364 patients; mean age 45.7 years) demonstrated widespread complications including rhabdomyolysis (n=178), renal dysfunction (n=105), respiratory dysfunction (n=78), respiratory infections (n=47), aspiration (n=36), pulmonary emboli and infarcts (n=43), cardiac dysfunction (n=37), and malnutrition (n=63). Overall 23.9% (n=87) of case-reported patients experiencing medical complications from catatonia/NMS died. Within this case-report sample, mortality rates appeared lower among those receiving benzodiazepines (n=26, 16.9% vs n=61, 29.1%) and electroconvulsive therapy (n=6, 7.3% vs. n=81, 28.7) compared to those not receiving such interventions.

Conclusions

Catatonia/NMS carries high risks for multisystem complications and mortality, including in non-malignant cases and younger patients. Rhabdomyolysis, renal injury, respiratory compromise, and thromboembolism were particularly common. Among case reported patients, numerically lower mortality rates were seen in those who received benzodiazepines or electroconvulsive therapy. Clinicians should recognize strategies that may reduce risk for certain medical complications.

title: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention and Long-Term Outcomes in Stable Coronary Artery Disease: Extended Follow-Up of the COURAGE Randomized Trial.
authorString: Butala NM, Murali N, Rahman N, Cave S, Ayandeh S, Plomondon ME, Cunningham JW, Weintraub WS, Yeh RW, Waldo SW, Boden WE.

title: From cancer prevention to survivorship: Comprehensive menopause management after risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy.
authorString: da Silva Filho AL, Grandi G, Lopes TL, Pinhati MES, Rodrigues AN, Maluf FC, Cândido EB, Lamaita RM.

journal.title: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics

abstractText: Risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy (RRSO) is the cornerstone of ovarian cancer prevention for women with hereditary cancer predisposition syndromes. When performed before natural menopause, however, RRSO induces immediate surgical menopause, with vasomotor symptoms, sexual dysfunction, accelerated bone loss, and potential long-term cardiometabolic consequences. For eligible women, menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) is the most effective treatment for vasomotor symptoms and prevents estrogen-deficiency bone loss. MHT should not be prescribed solely to prevent cardiovascular disease, and cardiometabolic risk requires standard preventive care. Concerns about breast cancer risk nevertheless limit its use. Recent observational evidence in BRCA1/2 pathogenic variant carriers found that estrogen-only MHT was associated with a lower breast cancer incidence in one prospective matched analysis, whereas combined estrogen-progestogen therapy was not statistically associated with increased risk; residual confounding and limited treatment duration preclude causal conclusions. For women with a personal history of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, systemic MHT remains generally contraindicated, and non-hormonal options, including neurokinin receptor antagonists, selected antidepressants, gabapentin, and cognitive behavioral therapy, can reduce symptom burden. Genitourinary syndrome of menopause and sexual dysfunction require proactive, multidimensional management. This narrative review synthesizes international guidance, cohort studies, trials, and systematic reviews to provide a practical framework for preoperative counseling and long-term survivorship care after risk-reducing gynecologic surgery.

title: MicroRNA-9-5p targets ELAVL1 to regulate NLRP3 inflammasome activation and cardiomyocyte pyroptosis in diabetic hypoglycemic myocardial injury.
authorString: Wei X, Luo S.
abstractText:
Objective

Recurrent hypoglycemia during intensive glycemic control in diabetes is an independent risk factor for cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying its myocardial damage remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the role of post-transcriptional regulatory networks in diabetic recurrent hypoglycemic myocardial injury.

Methods

Type 2 diabetic mouse models were established using a high-fat diet combined with streptozotocin (STZ) injection, and recurrent hypoglycemia was induced by repeated insulin administration. Integrated mRNA-seq and small RNA-seq were performed to screen differentially expressed genes and microRNAs (miRNAs). Key upstream regulators of the NLR family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome were identified via Pearson correlation analysis combined with predictions from the StarBase, TargetScan, and miRDB databases. Direct binding between miRNA and target gene was verified by dual-luciferase reporter assays. Gain- and loss-of-function experiments were conducted in a diabetic hypoglycemic HL-1 cardiomyocyte model by transfection with miR-9-5p mimics/inhibitor and ELAV-like protein 1 (ELAVL1)-targeting short hairpin RNA (sh-ELAVL1). In vivo intervention and rescue experiments were performed via tail vein injection of miR-9-5p agomir/antagomir and sh-ELAVL1 lentivirus. Myocardial structure and function were evaluated using echocardiography, hematoxylin-eosin (HE) staining, immunofluorescence, and Western blot.

Results

Mice with diabetic recurrent hypoglycemia exhibited significant weight loss (p<0.001) and impaired cardiac function. Transcriptome analysis identified 42 differentially expressed genes between the diabetic (DM) and diabetic hypoglycemic (HDM) groups, with specific enrichment of the NOD-like receptor signaling pathway. Protein levels of NLRP3, cleaved caspase-1 (p20), and the N-terminal fragment of gasdermin D (GSDMD-N, p30) in the myocardium were further significantly upregulated in the HDM group compared with the DM group (p<0.001). Correlation analysis combined with StarBase database screening identified ELAVL1 as the key upstream RNA-binding protein regulating NLRP3 (r=0.82, p<0.001). Small RNA sequencing revealed 16 significantly downregulated miRNAs in the HDM group versus the DM group. Intersection with TargetScan and miRDB predictions of ELAVL1-targeting miRNAs identified miR-9-5p as the sole candidate, which was significantly downregulated in the HDM group (p<0.001). Dual-luciferase reporter assays confirmed direct binding of miR-9-5p to the 3' untranslated region (3'UTR) of ELAVL1 (p<0.001). In vitro, transfection with miR-9-5p mimics significantly reduced the protein levels of ELAVL1, NLRP3, and cleaved caspase-1 (p<0.001), increased cell viability, and decreased lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release (p<0.001). Conversely, miR-9-5p inhibitor promoted these pathological changes, which were fully reversed by sh-ELAVL1 (p<0.001). In vivo, miR-9-5p agomir significantly improved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and left ventricular fractional shortening (LVFS) (both p<0.01), inhibited co-localization of NLRP3 with apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a CARD (ASC), and downregulated the protein levels of GSDMD-N, interleukin-1β (IL-1β), and interleukin-18 (IL-18) (p<0.001). miR-9-5p antagomir exacerbated these injuries, which were effectively reversed by co-administration of sh-ELAVL1 (p<0.001).

Conclusion

Our findings demonstrate that miR-9-5p directly targets ELAVL1 to inhibit NLRP3 inflammasome activation and cardiomyocyte pyroptosis, thereby attenuating myocardial injury and improving cardiac function in diabetic recurrent hypoglycemia. The miR-9-5p/ELAVL1/NLRP3 axis may represent a promising therapeutic target for diabetic hypoglycemic myocardial injury, although clinical validation of this axis in patients with diabetes remains to be performed.

title: Cardiomyocyte-derived ACE2/Ang-(1-7) axis mediates DIZE-induced inhibition of TGF-β signaling to attenuate cardiac fibrosis following myocardial infarction.
authorString: Li F, Chen L, Qu S, Liu X, Zhong S, Li Z, Chen Y, Cao Y, Ren J, Tian X, Ling Z.
abstractText: Cardiac fibrosis represents a critical pathological determinant of poor prognosis in coronary artery disease (CAD). Pharmacological activation of the angiotensin-Converting enzyme 2/angiotensin-(1-7) (ACE2/Ang-(1-7)) axis is a promising anti-fibrotic approach for cardiac fibrosis, a condition that currently lacks effective therapies. Diminazene aceturate (DIZE) is recognized as an ACE2 agonist with anti‑fibrotic activity, the molecular mechanism of which has not been fully elucidated. This study demonstrates that the anti-fibrotic effects of DIZE are exerted via a cardiomyocyte-mediated paracrine mechanism, rather than through direct action on fibroblasts. Using a cardiomyocyte-fibroblast co-culture system and transcriptomic analysis, we found that ACE2 activated by DIZE on cardiomyocytes enhances the conversion of Ang II to Ang-(1-7), which subsequently suppresses the pro-fibrotic transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) signaling in adjacent fibroblasts. This effect was partially abrogated by the Ang-(1-7) antagonist A779, confirming Ang-(1-7) as a key paracrine mediator. To exploit this mechanism in vivo, a collagen-binding, low-intensity focused ultrasound (LIFU)-responsive nanoplatform (CNA35-GDP) was developed for specific DIZE delivery. In a rat model of myocardial infarction, LIFU-triggered DIZE release from CNA35-GDP was found to significantly improve cardiac function and attenuate fibrosis. These therapeutic benefits were accompanied by restoration of the ACE2/Ang-(1-7) axis and suppression of TGF-β signaling, thereby validating the proposed mechanism. Collectively, activation of cardiomyocyte-derived ACE2 by DIZE inhibits collagen production in fibroblasts through paracrine Ang-(1-7) and downstream suppression of TGF‑β signaling.

title: Frailty Burden in Patients with HFrEF Undergoing Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation: Clinical Outcomes and Readmissions.
authorString: Bahar AR, Bahar Y, Cangut B, Hasan Jawadi M, Khoury I, Bolaji O, Abidov A.

journal.title: The American journal of the medical sciences

abstractText:
Background

Frailty is common and has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes across cardiovascular populations. However, its prognostic significance, particularly the impact of graded frailty burden, among patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) undergoing catheter ablation for ventricular tachycardia (VT) remains incompletely characterized.

Methods

We evaluated the association between frailty burden and in-hospital outcomes among patients with HFrEF undergoing VT ablation using the Nationwide Readmissions Database. Frailty was defined using the validated Johns Hopkins Adjusted Clinical Groups (ACG) frailty indicator. Cumulative frailty burden was quantified as the number of domains (range: 0-10). Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess associations with outcomes, and in-hospital mortality probabilities were estimated across increasing frailty burden.

Results

Among 17,367 hospitalizations for VT ablation in patients with HFrEF, 7.4% were classified as frail. Frailty was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.59; 95% CI, 1.19-2.13; p<0.001), and increased complication rates. Frail patients had higher 30-day (13.6% vs. 9.1%) and 90-day (33.7% vs. 28.1%) readmission rates compared with non-frail patients. Frailty burden demonstrated a graded association with in-hospital mortality, with estimated mortality increasing progressively with each additional frailty domain.

Conclusions

Frailty is independently associated with worse in-hospital outcomes and higher readmission rates among patients with HFrEF undergoing VT ablation, with a graded increase in risk across increasing frailty domains. These findings suggest that frailty burden may serve as a clinically relevant risk stratification marker in this vulnerable cohort.

title: Segment and side specific determinants of carotid atherosclerotic burden: evidence for a distinct left internal carotid artery phenotype.
authorString: Vinci P, Fiotti N, Pellicori F, Pirulli A, Di Girolamo FG, Altamura N, Puato M, Caruso P, Furlanis G, Naccarato M, Rodinis B, Manganotti P, Biolo G.
abstractText:
Background and aims

Carotid atherosclerosis is an important feature in patients with cerebrovascular events, but its determinants may vary across arterial segments and sides. We assessed segment- and side-specific determinants of carotid atherosclerotic burden.

Methods

We studied 177 patients aged 18-65 years who were hospitalized with acute ischemic stroke or TIA and underwent carotid ultrasonography. Atherosclerotic involvement of bilateral common carotid arteries, carotid bifurcations and internal carotid arteries was assessed using a Burden of Disease (BoD) score. We examined segment-specific associations between BoD, stenosis severity and cardiovascular risk factors.

Results

Plaques were more frequent at the carotid bifurcation and in the internal carotid artery than in the common carotid artery. After Bonferroni correction, age and hypertension were associated with BoD in the carotid bifurcation and internal carotid segments bilaterally; hypertension was also associated with left common carotid BoD (p = 0.003). BMI was associated with right bifurcation and internal carotid BoD (p = 0.007 and p = 0.005), Lp(a) >30 mg/dL with left internal carotid BoD (p = 0.002), and fibrinogen with left common carotid BoD (p = 0.005). The multivariable model for the left internal carotid artery explained the largest proportion of variance (R2 = 0.274), with contributions from hypertension (0.092), Lp(a) >30 mg/dL (0.084), BMI (0.036), fibrinogen (0.035) and atrial fibrillation (0.027). Associations with stenosis severity were less consistent (n = 16-54).

Conclusions

In this symptomatic cohort, carotid atherosclerotic burden showed segment- and side-specific associations with cardiovascular risk factors. The broader range of associations in the left internal carotid artery is hypothesis-generating and requires confirmation in larger prospective cohorts.

title: Relation of advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome with mortality risk in cancer survivors: joint effect and mediating role of PhenoAge acceleration.
authorString: Wu J, Kang Z, Wu D, Wang D.
abstractText:
Aims

We assessed mortality associations of advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome (CKM) and PhenoAge acceleration (PAA), individually and jointly, among cancer survivors. Outcomes were all-cause, cancer-specific, and cardiovascular mortality; mediation by PAA was also evaluated.

Methods

We analyzed 2,781 cancer survivors from NHANES 1999-2010 and 2015-2018 using Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, joint exposure, additive interaction, subgroup, and mediation analyses.

Results

Advanced CKM was associated with all-cause, cancer-specific, and cardiovascular mortality (HRs 2.319 [95% CI 1.926-2.793], 1.627 [1.215-2.181], and 4.469 [2.695-7.410], respectively). After adjusting for continuous age, these associations were attenuated, and the association with cancer-specific mortality was no longer significant. Compared with neither exposure, coexisting advanced CKM and PAA conferred the highest cardiovascular mortality risk (HR 9.026 [95% CI 5.505-14.800]). A positive additive interaction was observed for cardiovascular mortality (RERI 4.36 [1.42-7.30]; AP 0.48 [0.29-0.67]; SI 2.19 [1.38-3.48]). The indirect effects via PAA accounted for 17.0% and 4.7% of the associations of advanced CKM with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, respectively (both P < 0.05).

Conclusions

Advanced CKM and PAA were independently associated with mortality, while their coexistence further increased cardiovascular mortality. Joint assessment may improve cardiometabolic risk stratification and preventive care.

title: Long Term Outcomes After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Patients With Lymphoma: A Propensity-Matched Analysis.
authorString: Reeves IC, Laenger JG, Lewis BR, Lugo-Fagundo N, Ray JC, Herrmann J, McPherson AD, Bianco S, Singh M, El Sabbagh A, Pillai DP, Parikh PP, Reddy P, Sher T, Gharacholou SM.
abstractText:
Background

Patients with a history of lymphoma may develop significant coronary artery disease (CAD), which may be treated by percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), yet long term outcomes are not well characterized.

Methods

We reviewed patients with a history of lymphoma undergoing PCI from our institutional PCI database and compared characteristics and outcomes to a cohort without cancer. Long-term mortality and major adverse cardiac events (MACE) (cardiac death, myocardial infarction (MI), target vessel revascularization (TVR)) were assessed.

Results

Of the 11,953 patients identified, 83 (0.7%) had past or current lymphoma. Most had Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) (n=23; 28.8%) or Hodgkin's Lymphoma (HL) (n=22; 27.%), and 31 (37.3%) presented with acute coronary syndrome. Lymphoma patients, as compared to non-lymphoma patients, were similar with respect to age, sex, hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, prior MI, and prior PCI (all p=ns). The 1, 3, and 5-year survival rates were 90.5%, 69.5 %, and 52.5% in lymphoma patients as compared to 88.0%, 77.1%, and 66.7% in propensity matched non-lymphoma controls. Lymphoma was an independent predictor of mortality (OR 1.59; 95% CI 1.07-2.36, p=0.02) after multivariable adjustment. In propensity matched analysis over a median follow up of 4.2 years (IQR 1.28, 7.73), lymphoma was not independently associated with worse survival or MACE.

Conclusions

Among patients with CAD undergoing PCI, <1% had previous or active lymphoma. Although lymphoma may appear predictive of mortality in regression models with multivariable adjustment, mortality and MACE rates are similar to propensity matched controls.

title: Initial Diabetes Therapy After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting and Long-Term Outcomes.
authorString: Tam V, Schaff HV, Thao V, Van Houten H, Frye RL, Greason KL, AlJamal YN, Spencer PJ, Rowse PG, Crestanello JA.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is common among patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), but optimal post-CABG glucose-lowering therapy remains uncertain.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the OptumLabs Data Warehouse of adults with T2D undergoing isolated CABG from 2012-2024. Follow-up began 30 days after discharge. Glucose-lowering therapy was modeled as a time-varying exposure with patients contributing no-observed-therapy person-time until the first qualifying post-discharge fill. Pairwise comparisons used stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes were heart failure hospitalization, stroke, and repeat coronary revascularization.

Results

Among 19,237 patients, 24.9% had no observed post-discharge therapy, 42.8% received metformin, 22.9% received insulin, and 9.4% received GLP-1RA/SGLT2i therapy. All active therapies were associated with lower mortality compared with no observed therapy, including GLP-1RA/SGLT2i (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.58-0.87), metformin (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.55-0.66), and insulin (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.67-0.84). Among active therapies, metformin was associated with lower mortality than insulin (HR, 0.61 [0.54-0.70]); GLP-1RA/SGLT2i comparisons with metformin and insulin were less precise. Metformin was also associated with lower cumulative incidence of heart failure hospitalization than no observed therapy and insulin, and lower stroke incidence than insulin.

Conclusions

Observed glucose-lowering therapy initiation after CABG was associated with lower mortality compared with no observed therapy across all active treatment groups. These findings highlight a potential care gap and suggest that proper initiation of diabetes therapy after CABG represents an important opportunity to improve long-term outcomes following surgical revascularization.

title: Cerebral Blood Flow-Derived Myogenic Dynamics Reveal Impaired Postischemic Cerebrovascular Recovery in Experimental Stroke.
authorString: Li J, Alavi R, Dai W, Carreno J, Gharib M, A Kloner R, Pahlevan NM.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Restoration of cerebral blood flow (CBF) after ischemic stroke does not necessarily indicate recovery of cerebrovascular regulation. We tested whether myogenic-band dynamics derived directly from CBF signals provide information beyond mean perfusion during cerebral ischemia and after acute stroke.

Methods

Transient focal cerebral ischemia was induced in 29 Sprague-Dawley rats using middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion. Bilateral laser-Doppler flowmetry (LDF)-derived CBF signals were decomposed using empirical mode decomposition and Hilbert transform, and myogenic-band activity (0.15-0.4 Hz) was quantified by absolute and relative power. Cross-validated logistic regression models were used to evaluate whether myogenic-band power provided discriminative information beyond mean CBF alone.

Results

Ipsilateral mean CBF fell from 73.5±51.8 p.u. at baseline to 52.2±38.0 p.u. during late ischemia (P=0.0088), then increased to 126.6±91.5 p.u. after 3 hours of reperfusion (P=0.0050 versus baseline). Relative myogenic-band power decreased from 37.43±14.65% to 13.35±7.51% during ischemia (P<0.0001) and remained below baseline after reperfusion (20.74±12.02%, P=0.00033 versus baseline); contralateral relative power was comparatively preserved. Combining mean CBF and myogenic-band power improved discrimination of baseline from late ischemia (AUC, 0.99 versus 0.70 for mean CBF alone) and late reperfusion (AUC, 0.88 versus 0.70).

Conclusions

Frequency-specific analysis of LDF-derived CBF reveals persistent, lateralized abnormalities in myogenic-band dynamics that are not captured by mean perfusion alone. The persistence of depressed myogenic activity despite restored or elevated mean CBF demonstrates incomplete recovery of frequency-specific oscillatory dynamics after reperfusion. These findings support myogenic-band power as a potential functional measure of persistent postischemic cerebrovascular dysfunction.

title: Treatment Patterns of Oral Glucocorticoids in Patients with IgG4-Related Disease: A Real-World Analysis based on a Japanese Claims Database.
authorString: Kawano M, Sato H, Yamamoto M, Takashima N, Ikawa Y, Hongo Y, Okazaki K.
abstractText:
Objectives

To describe the prescribing patterns of oral glucocorticoid and evaluate flares and glucocorticoid-related complications in patients with immunoglobulin G4-related disease.

Methods

This retrospective observational study used a Japanese hospital claims database. Patients with a prescription for oral glucocorticoids, a diagnosis of immunoglobulin G4-related disease, and having at least two immunoglobulin G4 measurement tests were included. The index date was defined as the first oral glucocorticoid prescription recorded in the database (Day 0). Patients were followed for up to Day 1460 (4 years).

Results

The study included 3,167 patients. The mean dose of oral glucocorticoid was 28.76, 10.71, and 4.12 mg/day on Day 0, 90, and 1095, respectively. At Day 1460, 66.56% of the patients were still receiving oral glucocorticoid therapy and the dose exceeded 5 mg/day in 17.80% of patients. During the follow-up period, 453 patients (14.30%) experienced at least one flare. The incidence rates of hospitalized infections, osteoporotic fractures, and cardiovascular diseases, defined as serious glucocorticoid complications, were 7.46, 0.61, and 1.61 per 100 person-years, respectively.

Conclusions

Over half of the patients continued glucocorticoid therapy at 4 years. Glucocorticoid withdrawal strategies could be associated with reducing the long-term glucocorticoid-related toxicity in patients with immunoglobulin G4-related disease.

title: David vs supracoronary with non-coronary sinus replacement in acute type A aortic dissection: 5-year outcomes.
authorString: Dawoud O, Soliman S, Ali AS, Muhamed MY, Derbala HM.
abstractText: BackgroundAcute aortic dissection complicated by severe aortic regurgitation (AR) requires urgent surgical intervention. The optimal root management strategy remains controversial. This study compared the long-term outcomes of the Tirone David procedure and supracoronary aortic replacement with non-coronary sinus replacement in patients with acute type A dissection.MethodsThis retrospective observational study included 80 consecutive patients with acute aortic dissection type A (AADA) and severe AR who underwent surgery between October 2015 and February 2020 at the University Hospitals, with a 5-year follow-up. Patients were divided into two groups: valve-sparing reimplantation (Tirone David, n=40) and supracoronary repair with non-coronary sinus replacement (n=40). Outcomes included operative data, postoperative complications, mortality, and echocardiographic assessment of AR immediately postoperatively, at 6 months, and at 5 years.ResultsThere were no significant differences in age, cross-clamp time, bypass time, intensive care stay, hospital stay, or early mortality between groups (p>0.05). Immediate postoperative AR occurred significantly more frequently in the supracoronary group (57.5% mild AR) compared with the Tirone David group (5.0% mild AR; p<0.001). At 6 months and 5 years, the incidence of AR remained significantly lower in the Tirone David group (10% and 15%) versus the supracoronary group (65% and 75%, respectively; p<0.001).ConclusionsIn this selected cohort of relatively stable patients with AADA and severe AR, the Tirone David procedure was associated with better long-term aortic valve competence than supracoronary aortic replacement with non-coronary sinus replacement, without an observed increase in major perioperative complications.

title: Development and external validation of an interpretable machine learning model for in-hospital major adverse cardiovascular events after PCI in acute coronary syndrome
authorString: Yan D, Xin E, Wang Y, Tian W, Li W, Li T, Zhang Z.
abstractText:
Background Electronic medical record (EMR) data provide an opportunity to support early risk stratification in acute coronary syndrome (ACS), but models with large predictor sets may be difficult to implement. We aimed to develop and externally validate a parsimonious, interpretable machine learning model for in-hospital major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with ACS undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).

Methods:

This two-center retrospective cohort study included 1,726 patients: 1,218 in the derivation cohort and 508 in an independent external validation cohort. The primary outcome was in-hospital MACE, defined as a composite of death, cerebral hemorrhage, cerebral infarction, cardiogenic shock, cardiac rupture, recurrent myocardial infarction, stent thrombosis, or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium bleeding events. A total of 125 candidate EMR variables were evaluated. LASSO and Boruta-based feature selection, alternative preprocessing strategies including ADASYN, seven machine learning algorithms, and grid-search cross-validation were compared. Discrimination was assessed using AUROC and AUPRC, with calibration and decision-curve analyses used to assess agreement and potential clinical utility.

Results:

In-hospital MACE occurred in 138 of 1,218 patients (11.3%) in the derivation cohort and 15 of 508 patients (3.0%) in the external cohort.
