title: Bibliometric Analysis and Cluster Analysis of Research Trends on Postoperative Cognitive Dysfunction in Elderly Patients After Anesthesia.
authorString: Duan J, Duan X, Zhang H, Chu J.

journal.title: Journal of perianesthesia nursing : official journal of the American Society of PeriAnesthesia Nurses

abstractText:
Purpose

The purpose of this study was to analyze research on postoperative cognitive dysfunction in elderly patients after anesthesia and to identify research hotspots and trends.

Design

A bibliometric analysis.

Methods

We searched the Web of Science Core Collection for English-language publications on postoperative cognitive dysfunction in elderly patients after anesthesia published from 1988 to 2024. The retrieved data were analyzed using VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and R 4.3.3.

Findings

A total of 1,119 articles were included in the analysis. Among countries, China had the highest number of publications. Among institutions, Harvard University ranked first, with 165 publications. Among journals, Anesthesiology had the highest total number of citations, with 3,074 citations and an impact factor of 9.1. Among authors, Xie Zhongcong had the largest number of publications, with 24 articles and 1,045 citations. Keyword cluster analysis identified seven major research themes: anesthesia approach, risk, and clinical management; pathophysiological mechanisms and neuroinflammation; cardiovascular surgery and perioperative monitoring; biomarkers and neurodegeneration; anesthetic drugs and assessment tools; outcomes and neurophysiological responses; and recommendations. High-frequency keywords such as "anesthesia," "surgery," and "dysfunction" reflected the main research hotspots and trends in this field.

Conclusions

This bibliometric study summarizes the research landscape of postoperative cognitive dysfunction in elderly patients after anesthesia and identifies major contributors, research hotspots, and evolving trends. The findings may provide a useful reference for future research in this field.

title: Impact of Statin and Aspirin Use on Dementia Diagnosis Stratified by Cardiovascular Risk.
authorString: Kainat A, Muluk P, Thoma F, Zhu J, Mulukutla S, Lopez O, Karikari T, Pascoal T, Cohen A, Reis S, Saeed A.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) dementia share common risk factors. However, the role of ASCVD prevention therapies in AD dementia prevention is not fully understood. We examined the effect of LLT and antiplatelets with dementia and AD dementia diagnoses across ASCVD risk profiles.

Methods

We used data from primary prevention registry derived from a large healthcare network. Multivariable Cox proportional models were generated to study dementia and AD dementia diagnoses, stratified by ASCVD risk profiles. Impact of aspirin and LLT use on dementia and AD dementia diagnoses was assessed in adjusted models.

Results

Among n= 347,128, 2.4% developed dementia and 2.0% developed AD dementia over a median follow-up of 7.94 years. In adjusted models, dementia (HR, 2.59; 95% CI [2.29-2.92]) and AD dementia (HR, 2.85; 95% CI [2.49-3.25]) was higher in high risk patients. Low and high-dose aspirin among high ASCVD risk had lower dementia (HR, 0.88; 95% CI, [0.77-1.00] and HR, 0.83; 95% [CI 0.77-0.90]) and AD dementia (HR, 0.83; 95% CI [0.77-0.91] and HR, 0.85; 95% CI [0.73-0.97]). Similarly, moderate- to high-dose LLT use among high ASCVD risk groups was associated with lower dementia (HR, 0.85; 95% CI [0.79-0.93]) and AD dementia (HR, 0.85; 95% CI [0.78-0.93]).

Conclusions

Higher baseline ASCVD risk was associated with increased risk of dementia and AD dementia diagnoses. Aspirin and moderate- to high-dose LLT use among patients with high ASCVD risk was associated with lower dementia and AD dementia risk.

title: Housing mice in thermoneutrality causes peripheral tissue-specific changes in the number, identity, and phase of circadian-expressed mRNA transcripts.
authorString: Prabhat A, Naidu S, Stumpf IG, Clemons EJ, Rozmus E, Nwadialo SO, Wen Y, Esser KA, Schroder EA, Delisle BP.

journal.title: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology

abstractText: Laboratory mice are typically housed at room temperature (20-25°C), well below their thermoneutral zone (about 30°C), imposing chronic mild cold stress that increases metabolic rate by 30-40%. Because circadian and metabolic physiology are highly temperature-sensitive, we tested whether this housing condition reshapes rhythmic gene expression in tissues central to cardiovascular and metabolic health. We hypothesized that mild cold stress suppresses circadian gene expression in peripheral tissues. We performed RNA sequencing on hearts, livers, and diaphragms collected every 4 hours over 48 hours in constant darkness from male mice to identify transcripts with approximately 24-hour rhythms. Thermoneutral housing reorganized the circadian transcriptome tissue-specifically. Out of ∼13000 filtered transcripts, the proportion of rhythmic transcripts (q<0.05) in the heart nearly quadrupled, from 11% (1410) at room temperature to 42% (5282) at thermoneutrality, while the diaphragm rose modestly (6% to 9%; 792 vs. 1153). The liver's overall proportion was unchanged (36% vs. 37%; 4041 vs. 4150), yet more than 30% of rhythmic transcripts were unique between housing conditions. Almost 80% of rhythmic genes in the heart under thermoneutrality show acrophase near the subjective activity/rest transition. Gene ontology analysis revealed coordinated changes in the temporal organization of metabolic pathways in the heart and liver but less pronounced in the diaphragm. These changes occurred without detectable changes in core clock expression, implicating regulators acting downstream of, or parallel to, the clock itself. Because room temperature housing is standard across biomedical research, our findings show that this overlooked variable can distort the circadian transcriptome of tissues central to cardiovascular and metabolic disease, with implications for how mouse studies model human physiology.

title: Systemic Inflammation in Bronchiectasis: Data from the EMBARC-BRIDGE Study.
authorString: Hughes C, Long MB, Stobo J, Johnson ED, Viligorska K, Lind H, McIntosh E, Petrou I, Du Q, Hennayake C, Shuttleworth M, New JM, Goeminne PC, Shteinberg M, De Soyza A, Aliberti S, Altenburg J, Haworth CS, Sibila O, Polverino E, Loebinger M, Shoemark A, Ringshausen FC, Lorent N, Dimakou K, Amorim A, Mendez R, McLaughlin AM, Borrill Z, Lord R, Finch S, Blasi F, Khan F, Chalmers JD.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Am J Respir Crit Care Med
journal.title: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
journal.isoabbreviation: Am J Respir Crit Care Med

abstractText:
Background

Neutrophilic inflammation in the airways is associated with exacerbation risk in patients with bronchiectasis. Systemic inflammation and neutrophil function are less characterised. The aim of this study was to investigate the relationship between systemic inflammation and neutrophil function with severity of disease and clinical outcomes.

Methods

Observational international multi-centre study of adults with bronchiectasis (EMBARC-BRIDGE). Serum inflammatory profiling was performed in 487 patients using Olink® proteomics, and associations with key clinical and patient reported outcomes, including severe exacerbations during follow-up, were analysed. In a sub-study, peripheral blood neutrophils from bronchiectasis patients and controls were analysed for surface activation and functional markers, and functional responses including degranulation and neutrophil extracellular trap formation.

Results

Systemic inflammatory profiling revealed a dominant neutrophil-endothelial signature. Several proteins including PR3, AZU1, MPO, the soluble IL-33 receptor ST2, and the cellular stress marker GDF-15 were associated with increased disease severity using the bronchiectasis severity index, lower lung function, increased symptoms and for many markers, higher rates of severe exacerbations during follow-up. Neutrophils from bronchiectasis patients exhibited reduced surface CD11b and increased CXCR2, with lower CD11b correlating with lower lung function. Basal degranulation was reduced in bronchiectasis, whereas responsiveness to LPS stimulation was preserved.

Conclusion

Bronchiectasis is associated with a systemic neutrophil and endothelial inflammatory signature linked to disease severity and risk of severe exacerbations, alongside altered but functionally-responsive circulating neutrophils.

title: Development and internal evaluation of a model combining ECG waveforms with machine reports to identify recorded right ventricular systolic dysfunction in adults
authorString: Li¹ J, Shao¹ Y.
abstractText: Background ECG waveform models can identify structural and functional cardiac abnormalities. Their incremental value beyond jointly modeled machine measurements and interpretation text requires evaluation using the same patients and reference labels. Methods We linked MIMIC-IV-ECG v1.0 with MIMIC-IV-Echo v1.0.1 from a single hospital and selected one index ECG–echocardiography pair per eligible adult. The primary training cohort comprised 25,315 patients, including 3,165 endpoint-positive patients. The primary endpoint was recorded global or unspecified reduction in right ventricular systolic function. A selected machine-feature model (B; XGBoost) was compared with the same configuration refitted with an additional convolutional-network waveform score (BW). Development, calibration and threshold selection were separated from internal testing. The primary comparison was test specificity at model-specific thresholds selected for a 90% validation sensitivity target. Actual test sensitivities were reported separately. Nominal 95% confidence intervals were obtained from 2,000 paired patient-bootstrap resamples of the frozen systems. Results The primary test cohort included 5,505 patients, of whom 703 were endpoint-positive. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) increased from 0.782 (95% CI 0.764–0.798) to 0.850 (95% CI 0.835–0.865), a difference of 0.069 (95% CI 0.057–0.080). Specificity increased from 40.19% to 49.77%, a difference of 9.58 percentage points (95% CI 8.40–10.79), corresponding to 460 fewer false positives (95% CI 403–518). Actual sensitivity was 92.18% versus 91.89%, a difference of − 0.28 percentage points (95% CI − 2.29–1.63). Sensitivity was lower in the operationally complete-measurement subset, and a secondary severity-label scenario showed a sensitivity disadvantage. Conclusions Adding a waveform score improved discrimination and reduced false positives within this frozen internal evaluation. The findings do not establish sensitivity noninferiority, clinical utility or external applicability. Registration: OSF grs6q; stage-specific registration.

title: Novel ABCA1 mutations in Tangier disease associated with early-onset type 2 diabetes: A case report.
authorString: Wada M, Saito-Sato N, Tanaka M, Nomoto J, Watanabe A, Kuroda M, Maezawa Y, Sato T, Yagyu Y, Toriumi S, Kajiyama A, Hashimoto T, Ohtake N, Yamaga M, Yoshida T, Tsuji S, Takemoto M.
abstractText: Tangier disease (TD) is a rare disorder caused by mutations in the ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1) gene with autosomal recessive inheritance and is characterized by extremely low high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) and premature atherosclerosis. Although experimental studies suggest that ABCA1 plays an important role in pancreatic β-cell cholesterol homeostasis, its clinical contribution to diabetes development in humans remains unclear. We report a 69-year-old Japanese man with early-onset type 2 diabetes mellitus, profound hypo-HDL cholesterolemia (HDL-C 5 mg/dL), and severe atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Genetic analysis identified compound heterozygous ABCA1 variants (p.Arg104Cys and the novel p.Asp1706Tyr), both of which were predicted to be potentially pathogenic, although direct functional validation was not performed. Despite a 40-year duration of diabetes, endogenous insulin secretion was partially preserved. This case highlights phenotypic variability in TD and suggests that variant-specific effects on ABCA1 function and polygenic susceptibility may influence diabetes development in humans.

title: Radial Artery Pseudoaneurysm With Individualized Non-Operative Management: A 4-Case Series.
authorString: Ho JK, Tan Z, Tan ASM, Loh S, Lim D, Lew P, Tay HTL, Too CW.

journal.title: The American journal of case reports

abstractText: BACKGROUND Radial artery pseudoaneurysm (RAP) is an uncommon complication of radial arterial access. Although rarely life-threatening, it can cause significant morbidity. With the increasing use of radial access for coronary and endovascular procedures, arterial blood gas sampling, and invasive hemodynamic monitoring, RAP remains a potential access-site complication. Given its rarity, the literature on its management is limited and consists mainly of case reports and small case series. We report 4 cases of iatrogenic RAP with different non-operative management. CASE REPORT Four patients developed RAP following radial arterial access for intra-arterial blood pressure monitoring or coronary angiography. In Case 1, ultrasound-guided compression (UGC) was chosen because of poor collateral hand circulation and concerns for hand ischemia with thrombin injection, resulting in successful thrombosis of the pseudoaneurysm. Cases 2 and 3 underwent ultrasound-guided thrombin injection (UGTI), with Case 3 requiring repeat injection following recanalization. Case 4 had a large, flat-appearing pseudoaneurysm that was unsuitable for direct thrombin injection; balloon-assisted thrombin injection was attempted to preserve the radial artery but was unsuccessful, and a covered stent was deployed for exclusion of the pseudoaneurysm. CONCLUSIONS A range of non-operative approaches can be used in the management of RAP, depending on the clinical and anatomical circumstances. UGC and UGTI can achieve successful thrombosis, while endovascular techniques can provide an alternative when initial treatment is unsuccessful or the anatomy is challenging. Further studies are needed to better define the outcomes of these approaches and to establish a standardized treatment algorithm for RAP.

title: Mucosal-associated invariant T cells promote atherosclerosis through monocyte-driven inflammation.
authorString: Radecke T, Nipoti T, Wang LZ, Mouttoulingam N, Diedisheim M, Chajadine M, Bacquer E, Heron C, Alayrac P, Caër C, Laurans L, Knosp C, Liénart P, Damache K, Al-Rifai R, Camus S, Lemitre M, Piollet M, Soehnlein O, Julia P, Alsac JM, El Batti S, Letourneur F, Cochain C, Tedgui A, Ait-Oufella H, Mirault T, Mallat Z, Lantz O, Silvestre JS, Lotersztajn S, Taleb S.
abstractText:
Aims

Mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells are innate-like T lymphocytes involved in antimicrobial defence and inflammatory regulation, yet their contribution to atherosclerosis remains poorly defined. This study aimed to characterize the distribution, phenotype, and functional role of MAIT cells in human atherosclerotic lesions and complementary murine models.

Methods and results

MAIT cells were identified using MHC class I-related protein 1 (MR1) tetramers loaded with the agonist 5-(2-oxopropylideneamino)-6-D-ribitylaminouracil (5-OP-RU). They were significantly enriched among CD3+ T cells in human carotid atherosclerotic plaques compared with matched peripheral blood. Plaque-resident MAIT cells displayed an activated, exhaustion-prone phenotype and a distinct transcriptional profile characterized by upregulation of inflammatory, stress-response, and chemotactic pathways, as revealed by bulk RNA sequencing of purified cells.In murine models, low-density lipoprotein receptor-deficient (Ldlr-/-) mice carrying the CAST locus, which confers increased MAIT cell frequency, exhibited enhanced MAIT cell accumulation in the liver and aorta under a high-cholesterol diet. We identified mature MAIT in the bone marrow which displayed activated state. Moreover, Bulk RNA sequencing of bone marrow-sorted MAIT cells from these mice revealed transcriptional signatures consistent with immune activation and enhanced myelopoiesis. In contrast, MAIT cell-deficient Ldlr-/-CAST MR1-/- mice showed reduced atherosclerotic burden, decreased liver fibrosis, and smaller myocardial infarcts following coronary artery ligation, without changes in plasma cholesterol levels. These protective effects were associated with reduced myeloid progenitors and bone marrow and circulating monocytes, as well as decreased macrophage accumulation within plaques. Importantly, disruption of monocyte mobilization via CCR2 deficiency abrogated MAIT cell-dependent effects, demonstrating a monocyte-mediated mechanism.

Conclusions

MAIT cells accumulate in human atherosclerotic plaques and acquire a pro-inflammatory, functionally altered phenotype. Experimental evidence demonstrates that MAIT cells promote atherosclerosis and its complications by enhancing myelopoiesis and monocyte-driven vascular inflammation. These findings identify MAIT cells as previously unrecognized regulators of monocytosis and highlight their potential as therapeutic targets in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

title: Mapping and Outcome Implications of Left Atrial Low Voltage Regions as Determined by a Novel 122-electrode Spherical Mapping and Ablation Catheter.
authorString: Verma A, Kottkamp H, Calkins H, Nair DG, Sommer P, Hussein AA, Schumacher B, Dukkipati S, Neuzil P, Oza S, Woods C, Deyell MW, Osorio J, Reddy VY.

journal.title: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Aims

A novel 122-electrode spherical mapping/pulsed field ablation (PFA) device is known to effectively ablate atrial fibrillation (AF). The aim of this study is threshold optimization of LVA for the unique geometry of the Globe electrodes and the prognostic association, to evaluate if the extent of low voltage areas could predict recurrence.

Methods and results

The PULSAR study was an IDE trial of 183 patients undergoing first-time paroxysmal AF ablation with one-year outcomes of any atrial arrhythmia. During this study, a subset of patients (n=82) had detailed pre-ablation voltage maps performed with the catheter. Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) was then performed with PFA. Patients were followed with weekly transtelephonic monitoring, ECG, and Holters at 3, 6, and 12 months. Recurrence was defined as any atrial arrhythmia (AA) > 30 seconds.Receiver operator curve (ROC) analysis revealed that a low voltage threshold of 1.0 mV had the highest value (0.735). The percentage LVA surface area resulting from a threshold of 1.0 mV that predicted AA recurrence was 11.6%. Univariate and multivariate analysis revealed the percentage LVA was the strongest predictor of AA recurrence. The 12-month freedom from AA was 84.6% and 52.9% for subjects under and over the low voltage area threshold respectively.

Conclusions

A voltage threshold of 1.0 mV is proposed as a threshold for defining LVA using the spherical catheter, but a range of approximately 0.5-1.5 mV yielded similar performance. Increased low voltage area in the pre-ablation atrial map was associated with a higher risk of AA recurrence.

title: Pharmacokinetics, tissue residue depletion and withdrawal period estimation for tylosin in geese (Anser anser domesticus) following intravenous, intramuscular, and oral administration.
authorString: Serih F, Łebkowska-Wieruszewska B, Gajda A, Kacperek N, Poapolathep A, Giorgi M.
abstractText: Tylosin, a macrolide antibiotic, is used in poultry to treat Mycoplasma-associated respiratory disease and Clostridium perfringens-associated necrotic enteritis. To the authors' knowledge, no pharmacokinetic or tissue residue data exist for geese, preventing the establishment of a species-specific withdrawal period. This study characterized plasma pharmacokinetics in sixteen healthy adult male Bilgorajska geese (Anser anser domesticus) using a four-period crossover design following intravenous (5 mg/kg), intramuscular (25 mg/kg), single-dose oral (100 mg/kg), and multiple-dose oral (100 mg/kg bw/day for 3 consecutive days) administration. Tylosin concentrations were quantified via validated UHPLC-MS/MS method and analyzed using non-compartmental methods. Tissue residue depletion in muscle, fat, liver, and kidney was assessed in a separate group of sixteen geese at 10, 24, 48, and 72 h post-final oral dose, with withdrawal periods estimated using EMA WT 1.4 (MRL = 100 µg/kg). Systemic clearance was 0.81 ± 0.11 L/h/kg bw, volume of distribution 2.36 ± 0.12 L/kg bw, and terminal half-life approximately 2 h across parenteral routes. Absolute bioavailability was 57 ± 14% and 15-16% after intramuscular and oral dosing, respectively. No accumulation occurred after three days of oral administration. Liver residues were highest and most persistent; muscle and fat were below MRL value by 24 h, while kidney marginally exceeded MRL value at 72 h. Estimated withdrawal periods were 2.91, 4.23, and 7.66 days for muscle, kidney, and liver, respectively, yielding a provisional withdrawal period of 8 days following oral administration of tylosin at 100 mg/kg bw/day for 3 consecutive days. These exploratory findings provide the first species-specific pharmacokinetic and residue data for tylosin in geese, identifying liver as the limiting tissue and demonstrating route-dependent bioavailability.

title: Comparative validation of standard screening tools and an exploratory model for detecting obstructive sleep apnea in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Karim S, Iyyappan BS, Tabraiz S, Rajendran A, Chahal A, Geske JB, Chamberlain AM, Somers VK.
abstractText:
Study objectives

Despite representing a highly prevalent comorbidity, standard screening tools for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) lack validation in the hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) population. We sought to prospectively evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of three widely used screening tools against gold-standard polysomnography in an HCM cohort and to explore the potential for a tailored predictive model.

Methods

In this prospective cohort study, patients with HCM completed the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), Berlin (BQ) and STOP-Bang questionnaires before undergoing inpatient overnight polysomnography.

Results

Of 159 participants (median age 60; 64% male), 90 (57%) had OSA (46% mild, 26% moderate, 28% severe). Standard tools yielded modest performance: STOP-Bang [AUC 0.59 (0.50-0.68), sensitivity 77% (68-86), specificity 40% (28-52)]; ESS [AUC 0.58 (0.49-0.67), sensitivity 24% (15-33), specificity 92% (86-98)]; and Berlin [AUC 0.62 (0.53-0.71), sensitivity 65% (55-75), specificity 57% (45-69)]. In contrast, an exploratory model incorporating age, BMI, and waist-hip ratio showed promising preliminary results [AUC 0.82 (0.74-0.88), sensitivity 60% (48-72), specificity 84% (75-91)].

Conclusions

This study underscores the high prevalence of OSA in patients with HCM and demonstrates that standard screening tools developed for the general population perform poorly in this cohort, complicating clinical triage when polysomnography is delayed. While the derived exploratory model may represent an improvement in risk stratification, these findings require extensive external validation. Targeted screening strategies tailored to the unique pathophysiology of HCM remain necessary to improve OSA identification and management in this high-risk population.

title: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance feature-tracking strain characterization across phenotypic spectrum of danon disease.
authorString: Cao G, Liu N, Li J, Chen Z, Yin G, Yan W, Wang X, Cui C, Lu M.

journal.title: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging

abstractText: To characterize atrial and ventricular strain across the phenotypic spectrum of Danon disease (DD) and explore their relationships with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) extent. This retrospective case-control study included 27 DD patients (median age 17 [range 10-50] years; 15 males) and 32 healthy controls. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging was performed at 3-T with cine and LGE. Structural, functional, and LGE parameters were assessed. Kruskal-Wallis H test with Dunn's test and Bonferroni correction was used for intergroup comparisons; Mann-Whitney U or t-test for two-group comparisons; Spearman's correlation; and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis were used. Left atrial (LA) and right atrial (RA) strain were impaired across all DD subgroups versus controls, with LA strain impairment evident even in the hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) subgroup with preserved LVEF. LV global longitudinal strain (LV-GLS) was reduced across all subgroups, whereas global circumferential strain (GCS) and global radial strain (GRS) impairment were confined to hypertrophic and dilated cardiomyopathy (HCM-DCM) and dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) subgroups. Mid-ventricular longitudinal strain was relatively preserved (P = 0.062). LGE extent correlated with GRS (all P < 0.01). Left atrial conduit strain rate (LASRe) demonstrated the best diagnostic performance (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.981; sensitivity 88.9%, specificity 100%). CMR feature-tracking revealed phenotype-specific bi-atrial and biventricular strain abnormalities in DD. Atrial strain impairment was detectable even in HCM with preserved LVEF, suggesting early mechanical dysfunction. LASRe showed promising discrimination and warrants validation. HCM-DCM may represent a possible transitional phenotype; longitudinal validation is required.

title: Mechanobiology in the Brain: Sensing Your Heartbeats via Mechanosensitive Channels.
authorString: Hu DX, Guan ZT, Zhou WJ, Yuan TF.
abstractText: The brain-heart axis mediates bidirectional communication via neural and humoral pathways and plays a pivotal role in physiological regulation and the pathogenesis of cardiocerebral comorbidities. Mechanobiological studies further suggest that mechanical signaling pathways may serve as the third modality for brain-heart crosstalk. This commentary reviews two distinct mechanical regulatory modalities within the brain-heart axis: periphery-dependent mechanosensation, which acts as an upstream sensory module of classical neural pathways, and central in-situ mechanotransduction, which directly senses mechanical stimuli originating from cardiovascular pulsations in the central nervous system. Cumulative molecular, ex vivo, and in vivo experimental evidence demonstrates that subsets of central neurons can directly respond to arterial pressure pulsations via mechanosensitive ion channels and achieve functional coupling with heartbeat rhythms. Nevertheless, this field faces further evidentiary limitations. This commentary synthesizes current evidence and puts forward a scientific hypothesis that the mechanical microenvironment of brain tissue may modulate central mechanosensation. It also highlights future priorities including verification across broader neuronal cell types and in vivo functional interventions, to further refine the theoretical framework of the brain-heart axis.

title: The impact of maternal cardiovascular risk factors and diseases on offspring cardiovascular health.
authorString: Ceasovschih A, Markos S, Kotlyarov S, Sorodoc V, Banach M, endorsed by the International Lipid Expert Panel (ILEP).
abstractText: The increasing number of pregnancies among women at cardiovascular risk or with established cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) has become a major global health concern because of its lasting influence on the health of their offspring. Maternal heart disease, hypertension, diabetes, obesity, and abnormal lipid levels, including also elevated lipoprotein(a), can disturb fetal growth and development, leading to changes in the heart, blood vessels, and metabolism that raise the risk of CVD problems in childhood and later life. The rising age of pregnant women, especially in the developed countries, also increases this risk. These effects result from a combination of inherited traits and alterations in the intrauterine environment, including impaired blood flow, inflammation, oxidative stress, and disrupted nutrient transfer through the placenta. Such disturbances can modify the structure and function of the developing cardiovascular system and contribute to lifelong vulnerability to CVDs. Studies from large populations show that children born to mothers with cardiovascular conditions have about twice the risk of developing CVD compared with those born to healthy mothers. Good maternal health before and during pregnancy, supported by balanced nutrition, regular physical activity, and effective control of blood pressure, lipids, body weight, and blood sugar, is strongly linked to better outcomes for both mother and child. Although current lifestyle interventions in pregnancy have shown promising effects on maternal wellbeing, their influence on the long-term cardiovascular health of the offspring remains uncertain. Strengthening preconception care, well-designed healthcare education, improving cardiovascular screening in women of reproductive age, and promoting heart-healthy habits across the life course are essential to prevent the transfer of cardiovascular risk from one generation to the next.

title: Factors Associated With Extended Resection (Cecal Resection or Right Hemicolectomy) in Patients With Acute Appendicitis at a Tertiary Private Hospital: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Silva-Ramos CS, Leal-Hidalgo JL, Arechavala-Lopez SF, Ramos-Griera MF, Fuentes-Calvo KJ, Alfaro-Goldaracena A, Díaz Girón-Gidi A, Villegas-Tovar E, Montalvo-Jave EE.
abstractText:
Introduction

Acute appendicitis may require surgical procedures beyond conventional appendectomy, including cecal resection and right hemicolectomy. This study aimed to identify clinical factors associated with extended resection in adults undergoing surgery for acute appendicitis.

Methods

This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 360 adults treated surgically for acute appendicitis at a tertiary care hospital between 2018 and 2023. Extended resection was defined as cecal resection or right hemicolectomy. Associations were assessed using univariate analyses and multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, symptom duration, previous abdominal surgery, diabetes mellitus, and hypertension. Appendicitis severity was evaluated in a secondary model using grouped phases. Missing data were not imputed. The study received ethics committee approval (2024-EXT-871).

Results

Extended resection occurred in 50 of 351 patients with available outcome data (14.2%). Longer symptom duration (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 1.185; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.004-1.398; p=0.045) and older age (aOR 1.022; 95% CI 1.001-1.045; p=0.045) were associated with extended resection in the primary model. In the secondary model, advanced appendicitis phases were strongly associated with extended resection (aOR 10.273; 95% CI 4.694-22.481; p<0.001).

Conclusion

Longer symptom duration was associated with extended resection, including after adjustment for grouped appendicitis severity. These findings warrant cautious interpretation given the retrospective design and limited number of events.

title: Hybrid Osteosynthesis for Septic Humeral Shaft Nonunion in a Patient with Obesity: A Case Report.
authorString: Chiquini-Ramírez P, Villamues-Moreno NL, Ponce-de-Léon-Dominguez J, Moreno-Degante L, Pettet-Ruiz B, Torres-Casado E, Reyes-García HM, Garduza-Leyva N.
abstractText: Septic humeral shaft nonunion represents a complex reconstructive challenge in orthopedic surgery, particularly in patients with obesity, in whom increased lever arms and greater mechanical loading of the upper extremity substantially compromise fixation stability. Recurrent failure of isolated fixation constructs, including intramedullary nails or compression plates, necessitates hybrid strategies that combine enhanced biomechanical stability with effective eradication of microbial infection. This article presents the case of a middle-aged man with obesity and a history of a left humeral shaft fracture initially treated with intramedullary nailing in December 2020 who developed persistent nonunion. Following revision surgery with dynamic compression plating, fixation failure occurred secondary to implant fatigue. A second revision procedure was performed through a posterior approach, including nerve neurolysis, extensive debridement, and hybrid fixation using a 240 x 8 mm Targon™ H intramedullary nail (B. Braun, Melsungen, Germany) combined with a narrow 4.5-mm dynamic compression plate (DCP; DePuy Synthes, Warsaw, IN, USA). Cancellous bone chip grafting was also performed. Intraoperative cultures yielded Staphylococcus epidermidis, establishing the diagnosis of septic nonunion, and targeted oral clindamycin therapy was initiated. Despite transient postoperative radial neuropraxia, which resolved with pregabalin treatment and structured physical rehabilitation, the patient achieved complete osseous union, eradication of infection, and an Upper Extremity Functional Scale (UEFS) score of 69/80, corresponding to 86% of maximal functional capacity. In conclusion, hybrid fixation combining an intramedullary nail with a narrow 4.5-mm DCP, together with pathogen-directed antimicrobial therapy, provides excellent axial and rotational stability and represents an effective salvage strategy for septic humeral shaft nonunion in patients with increased biomechanical demands.

title: Circadian blood pressure adaptation and arterial stiffness in pregnancy: An exploratory study.
authorString: López-Sánchez C, Ayala-Hernández J, Castro S, Barbosa A.
abstractText: Maternal vascular adaptation influences blood pressure (BP) regulation and arterial stiffness. Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) allows calculation of the Ambulatory Arterial Stiffness Index (AASI), a non-invasive surrogate of vascular compliance. Data on these parameters in Latin American populations remain scarce. This exploratory study included 81 women (36 nonpregnant; 45 healthy pregnant). 24-hour ABPM assessed BP, circadian patterns, and AASI. Comparisons were made by pregnancy status and gestational age (<20 vs. ≥20 weeks) using Welch tests and bootstrap confidence intervals. Mean 24-hour BP was comparable between pregnant (111/66 mmHg) and nonpregnant women (115/69 mmHg; p > 0.05). AASI values were also similar between groups (0.33 ± 0.12 vs. 0.31 ± 0.18; p > 0.05), though pregnant women exhibited significantly reduced variability confirmed by bootstrap analysis. After 20 weeks, a significant shift from dipper to non-dipper systolic pattern occurred (p < 0.00001, Cramer's V = 0.703). Circadian patterns and AASI were not significantly associated. Pregnancy involves distinct hemodynamic shifts, specifically a non-dipper pattern after mid-gestation and reduced AASI variability. These exploratory findings provide a physiological baseline for vascular adaptation in this population, informing future research on hypertensive disorders.

title: Single-nucleus cNMF identifies a six-gene classifier predictive of atrial fibrillation recurrence.
authorString: FengHong X.

journal.title: Mammalian genome : official journal of the International Mammalian Genome Society

abstractText: Atrial fibrillation (AF) reflects intertwined immune-stromal remodeling, yet compact and generalizable diagnostic markers remain limited. Left-atrial single-nucleus RNA-seq was analyzed using SCTransform, PCA/UMAP, and lineage-aware cNMF (K = 4-8) to define transcriptional programs. Immune-related genes were filtered via ImmPort and analyzed using clusterProfiler, ReactomePA, and Enrichr. A 16-model benchmarking framework integrating stepwise GLM and LASSO identified a six-gene panel (EXT1, ATG7, PTPRC, MERTK, IRAK3, RORA). Immune infiltration was estimated using CIBERSORTx, and clinical outcomes were assessed using Andersen-Gill and Fine-Gray models. Experimental validation included RT-qPCR, siRNA-mediated knockdown, wound-healing, colony formation, and immunofluorescence assays in AF-mimicking atrial fibroblasts. Docking-guided drug screening and gene-drug interaction assays were performed to evaluate therapeutic targeting. Luciferase assays confirmed miRNA regulation. cNMF revealed lineage-restricted programs enriched in TGF-β, interferon-α, and inflammatory signaling, with macrophage and T cell activation as dominant features. The six-gene panel achieved AUROC = 0.583 (AUPRC = 0.627) with consistent external validation. RT-qPCR confirmed upregulation of all genes under AF-like conditions. Functional assays demonstrated that MERTK and IRAK3 regulate fibroblast activation, migration, proliferation, and extracellular matrix deposition, with MERTK exerting the strongest effect. Docking-guided screening identified MK-2461 as a potent inhibitor of fibrotic remodeling, significantly reducing gene expression, wound healing, and α-SMA/collagen accumulation. Lack of additive effects with MERTK knockdown indicated target dependency. hsa-miR-155-5p directly repressed all six genes. Persistent AF showed increased recurrence and progression risk. This integrative framework links immune-stromal remodeling, miRNA regulation, functional fibroblast activation, and therapeutic targeting, identifying MERTK as a key driver and actionable target in AF progression.

title: Assessing radiology recommendations on neuroimaging reports for patients with idiopathic intracranial hypertension.
authorString: Kamali Zonouzi S, Amadasun A, Suthiphosuwan S, Margolin E, Micieli J.

journal.title: Canadian journal of ophthalmology. Journal canadien d'ophtalmologie

abstractText:
Objective

To characterise the frequency and nature of radiologists' recommendations in magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography reports for patients with papilledema attributable to idiopathic intracranial hypertension.

Design

Retrospective chart review.

Participants

In total, 146 consecutive patients with papilledema secondary to idiopathic intracranial hypertension were included. They were all ≥18 years of age with optic disc edema and preserved visual function or a visual field defect consistent with papilledema and underwent structural neuroimaging.

Methods

Electronic medical records were assessed for clinical and imaging characteristics.

Results

In total, 146 patients (131 female and 15 male) were analysed. The mean age was 32.9 ± 10.8 years. Recommendations were provided in 33 reports (22.6%). Lumbar puncture (LP) was the most common recommendation (72.7%), followed by additional imaging (15.2%), and referral to other providers (9%). Of the 67 radiologists who contributed to the 146 reports, 11 (16.4%) recommended LP in at least 1 of their reports. Incidental findings were characterised in 15 (10.3%) reports.

Conclusions

In this study, radiologists provided recommendations in 22.6% of radiology reports, with LP being the most frequent recommendation. Future studies evaluating the appropriateness and impact of such recommendations are warranted.

title: Tear-fluid glial fibrillary acidic protein combined with optic-nerve ultrasonography for non-invasive assessment of cerebral involvement in severe pre-eclampsia: a cross-sectional study.
authorString: Taskina ES, Tsybikov NN, Mudrov VA, Kibalina IV, Magen E.
abstractText:
Objectives

To determine whether serum and tear-fluid glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), anti-GFAP autoantibodies, and optic-nerve ultrasonography are associated with disease severity in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, and to explore whether their combination adds to the identification of severe pre-eclampsia.

Study design

This prospective cross-sectional study included 184 pregnant women equally allocated to normotensive pregnancy, gestational hypertension, moderate pre-eclampsia, or severe pre-eclampsia (n = 46/group). Serum GFAP and anti-GFAP autoantibodies were measured in all participants, and tear-fluid GFAP in a predefined subgroup (22/group). Standardized optic-nerve ultrasonography assessed optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD), optic disc height (ODH), optic nerve diameter, and scleral canal diameter. Associations were analysed using non-parametric statistics, Spearman correlation, and receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) analysis.

Main outcome measures

Between-group differences in biomarkers and ultrasonographic parameters, correlations with disease severity, and discrimination of severe pre-eclampsia by ROC analysis.

Results

Serum GFAP increased only in severe pre-eclampsia, whereas tear-fluid GFAP increased progressively from moderate to severe disease (both P < 0.001). Anti-GFAP autoantibodies peaked in moderate pre-eclampsia. Tear-fluid GFAP correlated strongly with ODH (r = 0.772) and with clinical severity (all P < 0.001). ONSD (AUC 0.984) and ODH (AUC 0.973) were the most accurate individual markers; tear-fluid GFAP (AUC 0.908) outperformed serum GFAP (AUC 0.744).

Conclusions

Tear-fluid GFAP rises earlier than serum GFAP and tracks ultrasonographic signs of raised intracranial pressure, supporting it as a non-invasive marker of astroglial injury in pre-eclampsia. Optic-nerve ultrasonography provides the strongest discrimination of severe disease. Prospective multicentre studies with neurological outcomes are needed before clinical implementation.

title: GPR146 as a therapeutic target: Linking lipid metabolism with macrophage inflammation in atherosclerosis.
authorString: Liu Q, Wang Y, Geng Y, Xue Y, Lv C, Ren J, Zhao Z, Lv T, Zhang P.
abstractText: Atherosclerosis is driven by dyslipidemia and chronic inflammation. GPR146 has emerged as a regulator of cholesterol metabolism; however, whether GPR146 links lipid metabolism with macrophage inflammation during atherosclerosis remains unclear. Apolipoprotein E-deficient (ApoE<sup>-</sup>/<sup>-</sup>) mice were fed a high-fat diet for 12 weeks, followed by 4 weeks of intervention with adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated hepatic GPR146 knockdown or rosuvastatin treatment. Atherosclerotic lesions and plaque composition were assessed using Oil Red O staining and immunofluorescence. Lipid profiles, oxidized low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL), and inflammatory markers were evaluated using enzymatic assays, ELISA, and qPCR, respectively. In ox-LDL-stimulated THP-1-derived macrophages, GPR146 was silenced to examine lipid accumulation, inflammatory responses, transcriptomic alterations, and the potential involvement of the JAK-STAT signaling pathway. GPR146 expression increased in atherosclerotic lesions, particularly in macrophage-rich regions. Hepatic GPR146 knockdown reduced atherosclerotic lesion burden, circulating total cholesterol and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels, ox-LDL accumulation, and inflammatory activation within plaques. In macrophages, GPR146 silencing suppressed ox-LDL-induced lipid accumulation, accompanied by reduced CD36 expression and decreased foam cell formation. GPR146 silencing also attenuated pro-inflammatory macrophage activation, as evidenced by reduced expression of inflammatory mediators. Transcriptomic analysis implicated JAK-STAT signaling, with reduced JAK2 and STAT3 expression following GPR146 silencing. Pharmacological inhibition of the JAK-STAT signaling partially recapitulated the anti-inflammatory effects associated with GPR146 knockdown. Together, these findings suggest that GPR146 contributes to lipid metabolic regulation and macrophage inflammatory responses during atherosclerosis and may represent a therapeutic target warranting further investigation.

title: Association between biological age acceleration and the risk of aortic valve stenosis: An observational epidemiologic and Mendelian randomization study.
authorString: Zheng Y, Xu X, Li R, Xiong Z, Wen H, Guo Y, Liu M, Zhou H, Xu X, Zhang S, Huang R, Ke Z, Huang Z, Zhang J, Zhuang X, Liao X.

journal.title: The journal of nutrition, health & aging

abstractText:
Introduction

Biological age acceleration (BAA) is thought to be a major risk factor for age-related diseases, but its role in aortic valve stenosis (AVS) remains uncertain. We aimed to assess the associations between biological aging and the risk of AVS.

Methods

This study involved 4526 participants from the Real-world Data of Cardiometabolic Protection (RED-CARPET) study and 5114 participants from the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) study. BAA was assessed using clinical biomarkers through the Klemera-Doubal method (KDM) and the PhenoAge algorithm. We employed multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) regression to examine the association between BAA and AVS risk. Additionally, Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis was conducted to assess causality.

Results

In the RED-CARPET cohort of 4526 participants (mean age 60.93 years, 33.5% female), 113 AVS events were recorded. In the ARIC cohort of 5114 participants (mean age 51.94 years, 56.4% female, 82.3% White), there were 266 AVS events. After fully adjusting for confounding variables, each standard deviation increase in BAA was significantly associated with elevated AVS risk (RED-CARPET: KDM-BA acceleration: OR 1.29, 95% CI 1.07-1.55; PhenoAge acceleration: OR 1.48, 95% CI 1.24-1.77; ARIC: KDM-BA acceleration: OR 1.42, 95% CI 1.24-1.63; PhenoAge acceleration: OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.11-1.51). The RCS regression model revealed significant linear relationships between BAA and the risk of AVS in both cohorts. MR analysis suggested a potential causal relationship between KDM-BA acceleration and AVS risk (OR 1.38, 95% CI 1.21-1.57).

Conclusion

BAA, as derived from clinical biomarkers, is independently associated with an increased risk of AVS. This finding suggests that BAA, as a composite indicator of systemic biological aging, may complement traditional risk factors in the early identification of high-risk populations for AVS, and offer the possibility of early intervention for prevention.

title: Long Non-Coding RNA HIF1A-AS2 Promotes the Progression of Acute Cerebral Infarction with Large Atherosclerosis and Has Clinical Value in Early Diagnosis and Prognosis Assessment.
authorString: Ding T, Zhang L.
abstractText: Acute cerebral infarction (ACI) with large atherosclerosis (LAA) has a poor prognosis. This study evaluated the clinical significance of the HIF1A-AS2/miR-129-5p/HMGB1 axis in diagnosing and assessing prognosis in LAA-type ACI. This study included 150 LAA-type ACI patients and 150 matched healthy controls. The clinical outcomes of the patients were assessed using the GOS score. An in vitro hypoxia model was established using HUVECs. The levels of HIF1A-AS2, miR-129-5p, and HMGB1 were quantified by RT-qPCR, and levels of inflammatory factors were measured by ELISA. Luciferase reporter assays confirmed direct interactions among HIF1A-AS2, miR-129-5p, and HMGB1. Cell viability was assessed using the CCK-8 assay, cell migration was evaluated through Transwell assays, and apoptosis was analyzed by flow cytometry. The diagnostic performance of HIF1A-AS2 was assessed using the ROC curve. Kaplan-Meier curves were used to analyze adverse outcomes in LAA-type ACI, and Cox regression models identified prognostic factors. HIF1A-AS2 expression was significantly upregulated in LAA-type ACI, showing high diagnostic value. Higher HIF1A-AS2 levels were correlated with increased adverse outcomes, elevated inflammatory factors, higher NIHSS scores, and lower GOS scores. Hypoxic conditions upregulated HIF1A-AS2 expression, inhibited cell proliferation and migration, while promoting apoptosis. Conversely, downregulating HIF1A-AS2 reversed these effects. In LAA-type ACI, miR-129-5p was downregulated while HMGB1 was upregulated. Significant negative correlations were observed between HIF1A-AS2 and miR-129-5p and between miR-129-5p and HMGB1. The miR-129-5p inhibitor partially reversed the effects of si-HIF1A-AS2 on cell proliferation, migration, and apoptosis under hypoxia. Functional rescue experiments revealed that miR-129-5p mimic partially reversed the detrimental effects of HIF1A-AS2 overexpression on endothelial cells, as evidenced by enhanced cell proliferation and migration, suppressed apoptosis, and downregulated HMGB1 expression. Conversely, overexpression of HMGB1 partially abrogated the effects induced by the miR‑129‑5p mimic. In human aortic endothelial cells (HAECs) and human aortic smooth muscle cells (HASMCs), knockdown of HIF1A‑AS2 or overexpression of miR‑129‑5p both attenuated cell injury, further validating the extensive role of this regulatory axis in various vascular cell types. HIF1A-AS2 promoted the progression of LAA-type ACI and has clinical value in early diagnosis and prognosis assessment. The HIF1A-AS2/miR-129-5p/HMGB1 axis may serve as a vital factor in the early diagnosis and prognosis evaluation of LAA-type ACI.

title: Silencing the fire alarm: responding to intraoperative blood pressure targets.
authorString: D'Amico F, Landoni G.
abstractText: A meta-analysis in a recent issue of the British Journal of Anaesthesia pools randomised evidence on intraoperative arterial blood pressure targets in nine trials in noncardiac surgery. With a total of 14 658 patients included in the analysis, the authors show that higher mean arterial pressure targets do not reduce 30-day mortality, acute kidney injury, or myocardial injury. These findings reinforce the distinction between low blood pressure as a marker of perioperative vulnerability and low blood pressure as a modifiable therapeutic target. Correcting arterial pressure might normalise a number without removing the underlying physiological vulnerability that drives adverse postoperative outcomes. Therefore, this meta-analysis supports a shift from reflexive increases in blood pressure targets towards attention to the underlying cause of haemodynamic instability.

title: Safety and efficacy of cerebral embolic protection devices during TAVI: a meta-analysis and sequence analysis of trials.
authorString: Costa AJSC, Fernandes MVC, Batista TC, Félix AVJ, Barbosa TLS, Cruz IML, Noleto GS.
abstractText:
Background

Cerebral embolic protection (CEP) devices have been developed to reduce postoperative neurological outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI); however, their effectiveness remains controversial.

Objective

To evaluate the impact of CEP use during TAVI on the occurrence in clinical outcomes.

Methods

Databases were used to search for randomized clinical trials. The occurrence of all strokes, of disabling strokes specifically, transient ischemic attacks (TIAs), all-cause mortality, and vascular complications were analyzed. Conventional meta-analysis was conducted using fixed-effects modeling and trial sequential analysis (TSA: type I error of 5%, power of 90%). The systematic review protocol was registered on the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; CRD420251081075).

Results

In total, eight clinical trials were included, gathering 11,589 patients randomized between those who used the devices (5,943) and those who did not (5,646). The meta-analysis demonstrated no significant association between CEP use and reduced odds of all-cause stroke (OR = 0.92, 95% CI: 0.73-1.15, p = 0.46) and disabling stroke (OR = 0.80, 95% CI: 0.57-1.13, p = 0.20). The sequential analysis identified a lack of evidence for all strokes (required sample size [rSS] = 38,626; 10.53%), disabling strokes (rSS = 59,732; 17.05%). In terms of mortality, there was no significance in the use of devices (OR = 1.09, 95% CI: 0.71-1.69, p = 0.69), reaching evidence for support (rSS = 7,053; 42.25%).

Conclusion

The data on the use of CEP is insufficient to support meta-analytic conclusions regarding cerebrovascular outcomes. Nevertheless, TSA demonstrated evidence supporting futility regarding mortality reduction.

title: Artificial intelligence in dialysis.
authorString: Usvyat LA.

journal.title: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension

abstractText:
Purpose of review

Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning in dialysis have matured beyond the initial phase of algorithm development. Recent work has shifted toward clinical implementation, evaluation, and governance. During the past year, the first randomized trial of AI-guided dosing in maintenance hemodialysis has been published, a meta-analysis of technology-guided dry-weight adjustment has appeared, and the first professional society framework for the responsible use of AI in kidney care has been released.

Recent findings

The Anemia Control Model is now supported by hospitalization outcomes and cost-effectiveness analyses. A randomized trial demonstrated that AI-guided erythropoiesis-stimulating agent dosing achieved outcomes comparable to physician-directed dosing. Technology-guided dry-weight adjustment is supported by a meta-analysis of 21 randomized trials. Machine learning for vascular access is evolving toward preoperative clinical decision support, while peritoneal dialysis is beginning to receive greater attention from the machine learning community. Large language models are entering nephrology along two complementary paths: open generative systems for education and clinical support, and deterministic, protocol-driven frameworks designed for safety-critical bedside applications. At the same time, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has released comprehensive lifecycle guidance for AI-enabled medical devices.

Summary

The major challenge for AI in dialysis is no longer developing accurate prediction models. Instead, success will depend on effective workflow integration, validation across diverse patient populations, ongoing postdeployment monitoring, and demonstrating meaningful improvements in patient outcomes.

title: Efficacy of Nutritional Intervention in Adult Patients With Heart Failure: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Batool M, Duseja N, Mustafa MS, Khan MS, Rasheed T, Abrar M, Ihtasham A.
abstractText: Approximately 50% of heart failure (HF) patients are malnourished, doubling mortality risk; however, interventional evidence remains limited. A previously published meta-analysis found modest weight improvements only in malnourished/cachectic patients (5 studies, n = 275). This review updates the evidence in a broader HF population to evaluate the effect of nutritional interventions on all-cause mortality, hospital readmissions, and body mass index (BMI) in HF, determine whether intervention type moderates effect size, and identify sources of heterogeneity via meta-regression. This PRISMA-compliant, PROSPERO-registered (CRD420261445761) systematic review and meta-analysis searched PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane, and Embase for randomized controlled trials, quasi-randomized, and observational studies evaluating nutritional interventions (supplements, fortification, enteral/parenteral nutrition, counseling, with or without exercise) to increase protein/energy intake in HF, updating a 2021 search. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias (RoB 2.0 for randomized controlled trials; ROBINS-I for observational studies). Random-effects models pooled risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs), with subgroup, meta-regression, and sensitivity analyses. Of 7190 records screened, 23 studies (n = 2240) were included; 18 contributed to meta-analysis. Risk of bias was predominantly low. Nutritional intervention significantly reduced all-cause mortality (RR 0.43, 95% confidence interval: 0.26-0.71, P = 0.001), with no significant effect on readmission or BMI. Exercise capacity improved significantly (6-minute walk distance mean difference 25.01, 95% confidence interval: 5.26-44.76, P = 0.013), while quality of life, creatinine, and B-type natriuretic peptide showed no significant change. Nutritional intervention was associated with reduced mortality and improved exercise capacity in HF, though effects on hospitalization, BMI, and biomarkers were nonsignificant, warranting cautious interpretation.

title: Effects of angiotensin receptor blockers on aortic growth and clinical events in Marfan syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
authorString: Tanriverdi LH, Doğan MM, Barrett A, Zafar MA, Ziganshin BA, Elefteriades JA.
abstractText: Thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA) is a major cause of aortic dissection and premature mortality in Marfan syndrome. Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) may slow aortic enlargement, but their effects on clinical and imaging outcomes remain uncertain. The aim of the study is to evaluate the effects of ARBs on clinical events and aortic growth in patients with Marfan syndrome. We searched the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Ovid MEDLINE, PubMed, and Web of Science through February 1, 2025. Acute aortic dissection and all-cause mortality were the primary outcomes. Binary outcomes were analyzed using both Mantel-Haenszel common-effect (MH-CE) and inverse-variance random-effects (IV-RE) models. For outcomes with an event incidence below 10% in every contributing study, the MH-CE estimate was emphasized and the IV-RE estimate was treated as a sensitivity analysis. Continuous outcomes were analyzed using IV-RE models. All analyses were conducted with the meta package in R (v4.3.2). Seven randomized controlled trials involving 1522 patients with Marfan syndrome were included in the main analysis. For acute aortic dissection, the MH-CE estimate was RR 0·62 (95% CI 0·24-1·59) and the IV-RE estimate was RR 0·62 (95% CI 0·20-1·92). For all-cause mortality, the corresponding estimates were RR 0·53 (95% CI 0·17-1·64) and RR 0·58 (95% CI 0·16-2·07). Confidence intervals were wide and crossed unity. ARBs were associated with less aortic-root growth measured by MRI (MD - 0·48 mm/year, 95% CI - 0·89 to - 0·08) and by echocardiography over 3 years (MD - 0·51 mm/3 years, 95% CI - 0·85 to - 0·17), whereas annual echocardiographic measurement showed no significant difference (MD - 0·06 mm/year, 95% CI - 0·22 to 0·10). No significant effect was observed on ascending-aortic diameter, aortic Z-score at 3 years, aortic surgery, or serious adverse events. No statistically significant effect modification was detected in exploratory subgroup analyses. In patients with Marfan syndrome, ARB therapy was associated with small reductions in aortic-root growth in selected imaging analyses but did not significantly reduce acute aortic dissection or all-cause mortality. Sparse events, wide confidence intervals, and limited follow-up preclude firm conclusions regarding clinical benefit. Adequately powered, long-term trials with standardized imaging and clinical outcomes are required.

title: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke: the BRETIS-TNK2 trial.
authorString: Zhao ZA, Qiu J, Li W, Wei M, Wang SC, Liu L, Zhao YG, Zheng TY, Sun XH, Li XL, Wang J, Liu X, Sun XL, Zhang Y, Zheng B, Cui Y, Nguyen TN, Chen HS.
abstractText: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during endovascular treatment (EVT) may increase first-pass recanalization and dissolve microcirculatory thrombi, but its efficacy and safety are uncertain. We hypothesised that this strategy would improve functional outcomes versus EVT alone. This phase 3, randomised, adaptive-enrichment, open-label, blinded-endpoint multicentre study aims to evaluate whether intra‑arterial tenecteplase improves clinical outcomes for patients with acute ischemic stroke. Patients with large‑vessel occlusion eligible for EVT within 24 hours of symptom onset were randomly assigned (1:1) to the tenecteplase group receiving intra‑arterial tenecteplase during EVT or the control group receiving EVT alone. The primary endpoint was favorable functional outcome. Of 380 randomised patients (192 in the tenecteplase group and 188 in the control group), primary outcome data were available for 190 and 186 patients, respectively. Favorable 90-day functional outcomes (modified Rankin Scale 0-2) occurred in 40.0% of the tenecteplase group versus 46.8% of the control group (unadjusted odds ratio 0.76, [95% CI 0.50-1.14], P = 0.19). This work suggests intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy did not improve 90-day functional outcomes in this population. (Funded by National Science and Technology Major Project and hospital-initiated grants; ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT05657444).

title: PCSK9-Targeted Therapy and Kidney Function in Chronic Kidney Disease: A Systematic Review and Narrative Synthesis.
authorString: Adleh MH, Kassis A.
abstractText:
Purpose

Chronic kidney disease (CKD) increases cardiovascular risk, but renal impairment, proteinuria, dialysis, and transplantation complicate interpretation of lipid-lowering therapy. This systematic review evaluated renal tolerability, kidney-related clinical and biological evidence, and unresolved renal-outcome gaps for proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9)-targeted therapies in CKD.

Methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception and most recently updated on September 19, 2026; ClinicalTrials.gov was additionally searched on September 19, 2026. Eligible evidence included clinical trials and CKD subgroup analyses, renal-impairment pharmacology, observational cohorts, dialysis and transplant reports, pharmacovigilance, case-based evidence, and kidney-specific experimental studies. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted, and appraised reports. Findings were synthesized narratively without quantitative pooling. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261402376).

Findings

One hundred five reports representing 116 underlying studies were included. Evolocumab, alirocumab, and inclisiran consistently lowered low-density lipoprotein cholesterol without a clear short- to medium-term signal for deterioration in creatinine-based kidney function across the CKD strata studied. Evidence for reduced albuminuria or proteinuria was limited to small uncontrolled studies, and mechanistic findings did not establish clinical evidence of renoprotection. Most renal tolerability evidence came from cardiovascular or lipid-efficacy trials dominated by mild-to-moderate non-dialysis CKD; advanced CKD, dialysis, and kidney transplantation were excluded or sparsely represented.

Implications

Current evidence supports lipid-lowering efficacy in mild-to-moderate non-dialysis CKD but does not establish renoprotection or an antiproteinuric effect. Kidney-centered studies are needed in advanced CKD, dialysis, and transplantation.

title: Pharmacotherapy for older adults with cancer: a digest of the Japanese clinical practice guidelines (2nd edition) - lung cancer.
authorString: Kubo T, Shimokata T, Tsukita Y, Nakashima K, Yamamoto S, Takigawa N, Nagashima F, Matsuoka A, Asahina H, JSMO/JSCO Clinical Practice Guideline Committee for Pharmacotherapy in Older Adults with Cancer.
abstractText:
Background

The number of older adults with lung cancer is increasing in aging societies. However, determining optimal pharmacotherapy remains challenging because of heterogeneity in functional status, comorbidities, and the limited representation of older adults in clinical trials.

Methods

This article presents an English digest of the second edition of the Japanese Clinical Practice Guidelines for Pharmacotherapy in Older Adults with Cancer, focusing on lung cancer. The guidelines were developed using the Minds 2020 methodology and incorporated systematic reviews, an evidence-to-decision framework, and multidisciplinary expert consensus.

Results

These guidelines address key clinical questions in small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), including prophylactic cranial irradiation, adjuvant therapy, and immune checkpoint inhibitor-based treatments. Most recommendations were conditional, and no recommendation could be made for several clinical questions because of limited evidence in older populations. Prophylactic cranial irradiation may reduce brain metastases in selected patients with SCLC but requires careful consideration of potential neurocognitive toxicity. In resected NSCLC, tegafur-uracil may be an option for selected older patients; however, evidence supporting platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy remains insufficient. In advanced NSCLC, immune checkpoint inhibitor monotherapy may benefit selected patients, whereas the role of chemoimmunotherapy remains uncertain because of insufficient age-specific evidence.

Conclusions

These guidelines provide practical, evidence-based recommendations for pharmacotherapy in older adults with lung cancer. They emphasize individualized treatment strategies based on patient characteristics, treatment goals, and tolerability. Further research in older populations is required to strengthen the evidence base for geriatric oncology.

title: User Engagement Strategies for Digital Medication Adherence Interventions: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authorString: Thaw-Poon S, Diaz I, Acevedo C, Goyal T, Salinas D, Balakid J, Eaton C.
abstractText:
Background: Medication adherence is critical for chronic disease management, yet poor adherence remains an unsolved challenge. Digital health interventions are promising to support medication adherence but are limited by poor user engagement with the tools. Understanding which strategies effectively support user engagement could improve the efficacy and sustainability of these interventions.

Purpose:

This systematic review and meta-analysis characterized strategies used to support user engagement in digital adherence interventions with the well-established Behavior Change Technique Taxonomy and evaluated whether these strategies were associated with medication adherence and user engagement outcomes.

Methods:

Electronic databases (Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL), Embase via Ovid, MEDLINE, PsycInfo, and Web of Science Core Collection) were searched (4/18/2025) to identify randomized controlled trials of app-based digital adherence interventions for people with chronic medical conditions taking oral medications, published in English between 2020 and 2025. User engagement strategies were characterized with the Behavior Change Technique Taxonomy. Meta-regression models evaluated associations between specific techniques and study outcomes. Risk of bias was characterized with the Risk of Bias-1 measure.

Results:

The 60 studies included for review predominantly included adults with cardiovascular disease, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes (median N=117, IQR=72.0-204.5). All but one included at least one user engagement strategy appropriate to characterize with the Behavior Change Technique Taxonomy. The most common techniques were Prompts/cues (90%), Instruction on how to perform the behavior (70%), Adding objects to the environment (35%), Feedback on behavior (28%), Self-monitoring of behavior (25%), Credible source (22%), Goal setting (behavior) (20%), and Self-monitoring outcome(s) of behavior (20%). Prompts/cues were frequently paired with another behavior change technique (54%). User engagement was rarely measured as an outcome, and thus, it was not possible to evaluate this outcome in the meta-analysis. In the 44 studies included in the meta-analysis of medication adherence outcomes, there were no statistically significant associations with user engagement techniques.

Conclusions:

Digital adherence interventions commonly include strategies to support user engagement, particularly prompts/cues, but it remains unknown whether these strategies translate to actual user engagement. No user engagement strategy was associated with medication adherence outcomes. This may reflect variability across study samples and medication adherence measurement approaches, threats to internal validity, or reliance on ineffective strategies. Further research should continue to evaluate which engagement strategies support sustained digital adherence tool use and improved adherence outcomes.

title: Immunisation and preventive measures against mpox in pregnant women and children: A scoping review.
authorString: Rahman L, Eva FN, Ahsanuzzaman AKM, Monami S, Tabassum A, Nabi MH, Hawlader MDH.
abstractText: Mpox (monkeypox) poses disproportionate risks to pregnant women and children, yet evidence on immunisation and prevention in these groups remains limited. This scoping review mapped and synthesised existing evidence on vaccines and non-pharmaceutical preventive measures for mpox in pregnant women and children, to assess reported effectiveness, and to identify implementation barriers and facilitators. Peer-reviewed and Grey literature were searched in PubMed, Scopus, and Google for records published since 2008; databases were last searched on 19 September 2025. Screening and data extraction followed a pre-specified protocol and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) framework. Key themes included immunisation strategies, preventive measures, effectiveness, barriers, and facilitators. Forty-eight peer-reviewed articles and 16 Grey literature sources were included. Third-generation non-replicating vaccines (MVA-BN/JYNNEOS/Imvanex/IMVAMUNE) were consistently recommended for pregnant women and children because of their favourable safety profiles. Observational and programmatic estimates of vaccine effectiveness (single dose 36-86%; two doses up to approximately 89%) came almost entirely from adults, and no effectiveness estimate specific to pregnant women or children was identified. No source reported vaccine use by trimester, and paediatric data were limited to small studies. Ring vaccination and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) were supported mainly by adult data. Major barriers included limited vaccine supply and cold-chain and logistical constraints in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), vaccine hesitancy driven by safety concerns, particularly in pregnancy, and the absence of randomised trials in pregnant women and children. Few sources were centred on Africa or other LMICs. Facilitators included international coordination, targeted surveillance, flexible delivery strategies such as intradermal dosing, and integration with maternal and child health services. Priorities include prospective safety and immunogenicity studies in pregnancy and childhood, equitable vaccine access in LMICs, and tailored risk communication to address hesitancy.

title: Impact of Food and Beverage on Enlicitide Pharmacokinetics and LDL-C Lowering.
authorString: Johns DG, Skataric M, Zhou S, Gheyas F, Bajwa E, Banka P, Kesisoglou F, Hunt A, Bruce D, Anderson C, Manthos H, Pollock J, Donabella PJ, Thompson C, Freire D, Giang K, Pietrantonio F, Wolford D, Basak P, Pistilli M, Kantesaria B, Kothare P, Younis IR.
abstractText: Enlicitide decanoate is a macrocyclic peptide first-in-class oral PCSK9 inhibitor that lowers LDL-C, with maximal efficacy achieved when administered on an empty stomach. This work characterizes the effects of food, pre-dose fasting duration (2-8 hours), water volume, common beverages (black coffee and plain tea), and other real-world scenarios on enlicitide exposure and predicts the impact on clinical efficacy. Three phase I, open-label, crossover studies in healthy participants evaluated the effects of these conditions on enlicitide exposure following a single 20 mg dose. Enlicitide steady-state exposure and corresponding LDL-C reductions under various conditions were predicted using population pharmacokinetic and exposure-response models. Administration of enlicitide 30 minutes after a high-fat meal resulted in an approximately 48% reduction in steady-state AUC and delayed absorption compared with fasted conditions (median Tmax ~8 hours vs. 0.5-1 hour). Increasing pre-dose fasting duration from 2 to 8 hours increased exposure. Water volume, black coffee or plain tea had no meaningful effect on enlicitide exposure. Model-predicted LDL-C reductions remained robust across various conditions, with LDL-C reductions of approximately 64% under fasted conditions, 62% to 63% when occasionally administered with food or if a dose is occasionally missed, 60% with black coffee or plain tea, and 59% following a 4-hour fast. These data support the recommended dosing and administration instructions for enlicitide, which are expected to provide ~60% LDL-C reduction, as seen in the enlicitide phase III clinical trials. Furthermore, these findings highlight the pharmacokinetic forgiveness potential of enlicitide, suggesting that occasional departures from the recommended dosing or sporadic lapses in compliance may be tolerated with minimal impact on efficacy.

title: The odyssey of inflammation: pericoronary adipose tissue attenuation as a dynamic marker of coronary-specific inflammation.
authorString: Avivi I, Taub PR, Ben-Yehuda O.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

Inflammation drives atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, yet targeted therapies remain scarce, and identifying which patients benefit has been a central challenge. High-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), a systemic marker, has been used to select patients for anti-inflammatory trials but has proven neither sufficient nor necessary: the Ziltivekimab Cardiovascular Outcomes Trial (ZEUS), a recent phase 3 trial of an anti-interleukin-6 agent, lowered hsCRP yet did not reduce events, whereas colchicine reduced cardiovascular events in COLCOT and LoDoCo2 without hsCRP-based selection. Pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) attenuation offers a novel, coronary-specific measure of inflammation; whether it translates into better patient selection for anti-inflammatory therapy remains to be shown.

Recent findings

Measured from routine coronary CT angiography (CCTA), PCAT attenuation reflects inflammation within the coronary wall and, in large observational cohorts, predicts cardiac events independent of plaque burden, traditional risk factors, and hsCRP. Early interventional studies suggest it may also serve as a dynamic endpoint, though this evidence remains preliminary.

Summary

PCAT attenuation could enable precision anti-inflammatory prevention - selecting patients by coronary inflammatory risk rather than nonspecific systemic markers, and serving as a pharmacodynamic endpoint in mechanistic trials. Key gaps remain: randomized evidence that PCAT-guided care improves outcomes, treatment thresholds, longitudinal stability, reproducibility, and contrast-free validation.

title: Intra-arterial tenecteplase for acute basilar artery occlusion with sufficient recanalization after thrombectomy: the INSIST-IT randomized clinical trial.
authorString: Liu L, Li W, Qiu J, Wei M, Wang SC, Zhao ZA, Zhao YG, Sun XH, Liu X, Zheng TY, Wang J, Li XL, Sun XL, Zhang Y, Cui Y, Zheng B, Nguyen TN, Chen HS, INSIST-IT Investigators.
abstractText: The clinical effect of adjunctive intra-arterial tenecteplase after successful recanalization in acute basilar artery occlusion (BAO) remains uncertain. In this prospective, randomized, adaptive-enrichment, open label, blinded-end point, multi-center trial, patients with BAO within 24 h of estimated symptom onset who achieved successful reperfusion after endovascular treatment (EVT) were randomized (1:1) to intra-arterial tenecteplase (n = 75) or control (only received standard medical therapy, n = 69). The primary efficacy outcome was independent ambulation (modified Rankin Scale 0-3) at 90 days; the primary safety outcome was symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH). The trial was stopped early due to safety concerns and lack of efficacy per Data Safety and Monitoring Committee recommendation. Among 144 randomized patients, 143 (99.3%) completed follow-up. At 90 days, independent ambulation was achieved in 40.0% of the tenecteplase group versus 50.0% in the control group (OR 0.67; 95% CI 0.34-1.29; P = 0.23). sICH occurred in 6.2% versus 4.8% (OR 1.31; 95% CI 0.28-6.89; P = 0.73). All-cause mortality at 90 days was 41.3% versus 26.5% (OR 1.96; 95% CI 0.97-4.03; P = 0.063). In this prematurely terminated trial, adjunctive intra-arterial tenecteplase did not improve functional outcomes in patients with BAO.

title: Rescue treatment for medium vessel occlusion by intra-arterial tenecteplase: the RESCUE-TNK randomized clinical trial.
authorString: Zhao ZA, Wang SC, Wei M, Xing GP, Li W, Qiu J, Li XL, Sun XH, Liu L, Zheng TY, Wang J, Yin R, Sun XL, Zhang Y, Cui Y, Nguyen TN, Chen HS.
abstractText: In patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by medium vessel occlusion (MeVO), intra-arterial tenecteplase may offer a targeted strategy to improve recanalization; we hypothesized that intra-arterial tenecteplase would increase successful reperfusion compared with standard care with a comparable safety profile. This phase 2, prospective, randomised, open-label, blinded-endpoint, multicentre study aims to assess the efficacy and safety of intra-arterial tenecteplase for patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by MeVO. Patients with MeVO were randomly (1:1) assigned to receive intra-arterial tenecteplase or standard care. The primary outcome was successful reperfusion of medium vessel occlusion. A total of 80 patients were randomized to either the tenecteplase group (n = 41) or control group (n = 39). Successful reperfusion reached 61.0% (25/41) in the tenecteplase group versus 28.2% (11/39) in the control group (unadjusted odds ratio 3.98, 95% CI 1.56-10.16; P = 0.004). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 24 h was similar between the tenecteplase and control groups. This work suggests that intra-arterial tenecteplase significantly increased the probability of successful reperfusion compared with standard care, with a comparable safety profile in this stroke population. (Funded by Shenyang Science Tech Project and hospital-initiated grants; ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT05657470).

title: A randomized trial to reduce heart disease risk among Yup'ik Alaska native people: the DAiLY study.
authorString: Hopkins SE, Thompson B, Tiwari H, Gittelsohn J, Boyer BB.
abstractText:
Background

Heart disease (HD) is a leading cause of mortality among Yup'ik Alaska Native people, whose prevalence of HD exceeds that of the U.S. population overall. Transition away from traditional subsistence foods and lifestyles toward processed market-food diets and reduced physical activity have contributed to increasing cardiometabolic risk. The Diet and Active Lifestyle-Yuuyaraq (DAiLY) Study was developed in partnership with Yup'ik communities to promote heart health through culturally grounded strategies that support traditional foods, healthy market food choices, and active lifestyles.

Methods

DAiLY is a community-based, cluster-randomized trial conducted in four Yup'ik communities in southwest Alaska. Communities were randomized to immediate or delayed intervention conditions.
