The multilevel intervention integrates home-based workshops, a food store component, community-wide events, and community media messaging, guided by the Warnecke Transdisciplinary Model and community-based participatory research principles. Adults aged ≥18 years who self-identify as Yup'ik are eligible to participate in outcome assessments. The primary outcome is a change in continuous metabolic syndrome (cMS) score, a validated composite indicator of cardiometabolic risk. Secondary outcomes include self-reported dietary intake, physical activity, psychosocial measures, and stable isotope biomarkers of subsistence and market food intake. Process evaluation will assess reach, dose, fidelity, engagement, and implementation context.

Discussion

DAiLY is the first multicomponent, multilevel intervention designed to reduce cardiometabolic risk among Yup'ik Alaska Native communities by integrating Indigenous knowledge, subsistence food practices, and community-driven health promotion strategies. Findings will inform culturally grounded approaches to cardiovascular disease prevention in Indigenous and other rural populations undergoing nutrition and lifestyle transitions.

title: Cardiovascular risk stratification in patients undergoing liposomal anthracycline: Association with cardiovascular outcomes and overall survival.
authorString: Camilli M, Torre I, Viscovo M, Maiolo E, Ballacci F, Leo L, Lamendola P, De Stefano V, Burzotta F, Hohaus S, Lombardo A, Minotti G.
abstractText:
Background

Elderly patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma and cardiovascular disease are frequently treated with regimens incorporating non-PEGylated liposomal anthracycline to mitigate cardiotoxicity while preserving antitumor efficacy. However, considering their unique pharmacokinetics, validation of a cardiovascular risk stratification tool for these patients is much needed.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed patients with newly diagnosed non-Hodgkin lymphoma treated with rituximab, cyclophosphamide, non-PEGylated liposomal doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone (R-COMP) between 2014 and 2025. Baseline demographics, cardiovascular history and medications, echocardiographic and laboratory parameters were recorded. Patients were stratified into risk categories according to the Heart Failure Association International Cardio-Oncology Society (HFA-ICOS) score. Outcomes included overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS) and incidence of cardiovascular events defined as asymptomatic left ventricular dysfunction, new-onset or worsening heart failure and acute coronary syndrome.

Results

The cohort consisted of 265 patients [median age 73 years (69-77); 51% males]; 41% were classified as moderate risk, 55% as high risk, and 4% as very high risk. During a median follow-up of 29 months, 38 patients (14%) died. OS and cardiovascular events occurrence significantly differed across the three HFA-ICOS risk categories; in particular, very high-risk patients exhibited substantially higher hazards of mortality (HR 5.8) and cardiovascular events (HR 40.4). Cardioprotective therapy at baseline appears not influence cardiovascular outcomes.

Conclusions

The HFA-ICOS score effectively stratifies mortality and risk of cardiovascular events among patients treated with R-COMP. Despite the limited number of very-high risk patients and the heterogenous, non-randomized cardioprotective strategies at baseline, our findings may provide evidence supporting its integration into practice.

title: Digital Health Intervention to Optimize Heart Failure Management After Hospital Discharge in Brazil (OPT-HF): A Randomized Clinical Trial.
authorString: Ciminelli ALA, Sandhu AT, Longenecker CT, Rezende LC, Camelo LV, Gonçalves BPA, Lino RZS, Bramucci V, Melo BMH, Siqueira CV, Carvalho APV, Ribeiro EG, Ferreira LB, Beaton AZ, Ribeiro ALP, Brant LCC.
abstractText:
Background

Barriers to optimizing guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) for heart failure include infrequent clinical visits, clinician inertia, and poor patient knowledge. Digital health interventions (DHIs) may mitigate these barriers, but evidence from low- and middle-income countries is limited. We evaluated whether a DHI would improve GDMT use and other outcomes in Brazil.

Methods

We enrolled adults admitted for heart failure with ejection fraction <50% and GDMT gaps (≥1 GDMT class not started or ≥2 classes ≤50% target dose) across 5 Brazilian public hospitals from November 2023 to August 2025. Participants were randomized to usual care or the DHI comprising a patient-facing app linked to a provider dashboard, supporting nurse-led remote monitoring, cardiologist teleconsultations, and self-care education. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in mean heart failure GDMT score (0-12) at 90 days. Secondary outcomes included differences in health status, self-care, hospitalization rates, and all-cause mortality. Intention-to-treat analyses used baseline-adjusted linear regression and estimated risk ratios.

Results

Among 154 randomized patients (DHI: 87; usual care: 67), mean age was 65±14 years; 62% were male, 66% were Black, 44% had ≤4 years of education, and 68% were New York Heart Association class III/IV. Primary outcome data were available for 141 participants (91.6%; DHI: 81; usual care: 60). Mean GDMT scores increased from 7.2 in both groups to 10.5 with DHI versus 7.5 with usual care at 90 days (changes: +3.3 versus +0.3 points; adjusted difference, 3.01 [95% CI, 2.30-3.73]; P<0.001). A borderline difference was observed in health status (7.89; P=0.052). Improvements were observed in self-care (β=14.79 [95% CI, 9.78-19.81]; P<0.001). Fewer participants were hospitalized with DHI than usual care (9/87 [10.3%] versus 15/67 [22.4%]; risk ratio, 0.46 [95% CI, 0.21-0.99]; P=0.048), with no statistically significant difference for deaths.

Conclusions

In patients hospitalized for heart failure in Brazil, a context-adapted DHI improved GDMT use, self-care, and reduced hospitalizations. These findings provide early randomized evidence supporting DHI for GDMT optimization in low-resource settings.

Registration

URL: https://ensaiosclinicos.gov.br/rg/RBR-10vpf9bm; Unique identifier: U1111-1295-1864.

title: Resolving clinical Dilemmas in Hyperkalemia management for chronic heart failure: Current and emerging roles of sodium zirconium cyclosilicate.
authorString: Imamura T.
abstractText: Hyperkalemia, commonly defined as a serum potassium concentration > 5.0 mEq/L, is a frequent and clinically important complication in patients with chronic heart failure (HF), particularly those with chronic kidney disease receiving guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT). Its impact extends beyond the electrolyte abnormality itself because recurrent hyperkalemia may lead to underuse, dose reduction, or discontinuation of prognostically important therapy. The risk is not uniform across GDMT classes: mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists carry the greatest direct risk, angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers, and angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors also increase risk, whereas sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors may reduce serious hyperkalemia. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (SZC) effectively lowers serum potassium and randomized evidence supports its use to maintain normokalemia and facilitate spironolactone optimization. However, a reduction in mortality or HF hospitalization has not been established. Emerging observational data suggest additional potential roles in supporting individualized dietary liberalization, improving gastrointestinal tolerability relative to traditional resins, and preventing recurrent hyperkalemia after treatment withdrawal. These findings should be interpreted cautiously because several supporting studies are small, nonrandomized, and potentially affected by residual confounding. Long-term treatment also requires attention to sodium exposure and edema, particularly in patients with HF or advanced kidney disease. This review integrates class-specific hyperkalemia risk, practical potassium thresholds, efficacy and safety evidence, comparison with patiromer, health-economic considerations, and remaining evidence gaps to provide a clinically applicable framework for individualized potassium management in HF.

title: Female Fingerprint: Sex-Specific Aspects in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and Heart Failure.
authorString: Roth E, Rottner L.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

Atrial fibrillation (AF) and heart failure (HF) frequently coexist and represent a major source of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. This review summarizes current evidence on sex-specific differences in epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, prognosis, and treatment in women with AF and HF.

Recent findings

Emerging evidence indicates that women with AF and HF constitute a distinct clinical and biological phenotype. Women typically develop AF at older age, more commonly present with hypertension and HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), and report greater symptom burden and impaired quality of life. Sex-specific mechanisms including hormonal influences, atrial fibrosis, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, autonomic dysregulation, and microvascular disease contribute to these differences. Population studies further demonstrate sex-related disparities in HF development and outcomes across AF subtypes. Despite increasing awareness, women remain underrepresented in clinical trials and are less likely to receive rhythm-control strategies, catheter ablation, or device therapy. Recognition of the "female fingerprint" in AF and HF is essential for individualized risk stratification and the advancement of precision cardiovascular medicine.

title: Cessation of oral anticoagulation after atrial fibrillation ablation: who and when?
authorString: Lee JG, Verma A, Birnie DH, Ha ACT.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

The ideal long-term oral anticoagulation (OAC) management strategy for patients who have undergone successful catheter-based atrial fibrillation ablation is not well defined. Over the past 20  years, observational studies suggested that OAC could be safely discontinued for patients with intermediate thromboembolic risk, but randomized trial data were lacking to inform clinical practice.

Recent findings

Recently, two randomized clinical trials on this topic have been published: The Optimal Anticoagulation for Enhanced Risk Patients Post-Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation (OCEAN) and Anticoagulation One Year after Ablation of Atrial Fibrillation in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation (ALONE-AF). These trials showed that OAC cessation at 1 year after successful atrial fibrillation ablation was not associated with increased thromboembolic risk for patients with an intermediate stroke risk profile (i.e. CHA2DS2-VASc 1-3 points). In both trials, the annualized rate of thromboembolism was below 1%. Patients with higher thromboembolic risk (i.e. CHA2DS2-VASc ≥4 points or history of stroke/transient ischemic attack) were minimally represented in these trials.

Summary

For patients without high-risk features for thromboembolism, the OCEAN and ALONE-AF trials showed that OAC cessation is a viable option at 1 year after ablation if no atrial fibrillation is documented by routine rhythm monitoring modalities.

title: Early thyroid-stimulating hormone dynamics as an independent predictor of immune-related hypothyroidism during nivolumab therapy.
authorString: Çınaroğlu D, Döngelli H, Ataca E, Güç ZG.
abstractText:
Background

Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment landscape of advanced solid tumors, yet immune-related adverse events remain a major challenge. Thyroid dysfunction is among the most frequent endocrine toxicities associated with programmed cell death-1 (PD-1) inhibitors, often evolving dynamically and remaining early immune-mediated thyroid injury. Identifying an early and reliable biomarker for immune-related hypothyroidism could improve patient monitoring and treatment safety.

Methods

This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 214 adult patients with solid tumors treated with nivolumab between January 2020 and January 2025. Thyroid function tests obtained at baseline and at the first month of treatment were analyzed. Early thyroid-stimulating hormone change (ΔTSH) was defined as change from baseline, calculated as first-month TSH minus baseline TSH. The primary endpoint was the development of de-novo or deteriorated hypothyroidism. Time-to-event analyses were performed using Cox proportional hazards regression. The discriminative performance of ΔTSH was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, with internal validation using 2,000 bootstrap resamples.

Results

During follow-up, nivolumab-related thyroid adverse events occurred in 37 patients (17.3%), with de novo or deteriorated hypothyroidism observed in 27 patients. Median time to hypothyroidism was 12 weeks (IQR: 8-24). In multivariable Cox regression, ΔTSH remained independently associated with subsequent hypothyroidism (adjusted HR per 1 mU/L increase: 1.060; 95% CI: 1.036-1.085; p < 0.001), together with age. Exploratory ROC analysis demonstrated high apparent discrimination of ΔTSH for subsequent hypothyroidism (AUC 0.952, 95% CI 0.925-0.979). Internal validation using 2,000 bootstrap resamples showed a mean AUC of 0.952 (95% bootstrap CI: 0.922-0.976).

Conclusions

Early ΔTSH was associated with subsequent immune-related hypothyroidism in this retrospective cohort. However, the modest sample size of 214 patients and the limited number of hypothyroidism events (n = 27) mean that the observed association and apparent discriminative performance should be regarded as preliminary, exploratory evidence. Bootstrap resampling does not overcome these data limitations. Larger cohorts with more outcome events are needed to confirm predictive performance before clinical application.

Clinical trial number

Not applicable.

title: Blood pressure control assessed by clinic and home blood pressure measurements among hypertensive patients in India: results from the GRAND study.
authorString: Verma N, Matsushita N, Barooah R, Bhat S, Bhavatharini N, Goel A, Gupta AK, Gupta A, Gupta A, Gupta VK, Jagadeesha A, Parashar R, Patni B, Saboo B, Saxena D, Singh NK, Singh R, Singh R, Srivastava S, Ohde S, Imai Y, Maheshwari A, Ohkubo T.

journal.title: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension

abstractText: Hypertension is a prevalent non-communicable disease and a significant cardiovascular risk factor in India, affecting 25% of adults. Among those treated, only 52.5% achieved controlled clinic blood pressure (CBP). We investigated blood pressure (BP) control in India using CBP and home BP (HBP). This multicenter, cross-sectional study across 18 centers in 12 states within 7 regions enrolled hypertensive participants aged 20-70 years receiving antihypertensive medications for ≥3 months who regularly visited their clinic. A background survey and four CBP readings were collected at baseline ("Clinic Visit 1") and Clinic Visit 2. Participants underwent HBP monitoring for seven days. Based on average CBP across the two clinic visits and average HBP, participants were classified as having well-controlled hypertension (CBP < 140/90 mmHg and HBP < 135/85 mmHg), white-coat uncontrolled hypertension (WUCH; CBP ≥ 140/90 mmHg and HBP < 135/85 mmHg), masked uncontrolled hypertension (MUCH; CBP < 140/90 mmHg and HBP ≥ 135/85 mmHg), or sustained uncontrolled hypertension (SUCH; CBP ≥ 140/90 mmHg and HBP ≥ 135/85 mmHg). Among 1920 participants, 1578 with appropriate CBP and HBP readings were analyzed. Of these, 55.9% had well-controlled hypertension, 5.1% had WUCH, 21.8% had MUCH, and 17.2% had SUCH. The proportion classified as controlled was 77.7% using clinic BP alone versus 55.9% using both clinic and home BP, a difference of 21.8 percentage points. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating HBP alongside CBP for comprehensive assessment of BP control and identification of BP control phenotypes. Clinical trial registration: Registered at Clinical Trials Registry-India (CTRI) under CTRI/2023/02/049486 on 06 February 2023.

title: The effect of maternal oxygenation on cardiopulmonary haemodynamics during the transition at birth in preterm lambs.
authorString: Stenning FJ, Gill AW, Kluckow M, Zahra VA, Moxham A, Crossley KJ, Blank DA, Dekker J, Te Pas AB, Polglase GR, Hooper SB.
abstractText:
Background

The cardiovascular transition at birth is a period of instability for preterm infants; however, the impact of fetal oxygen (PaO2) levels on this process is unclear. We hypothesized that increasing maternal, and subsequently, fetal oxygenation will increase pulmonary blood flow (PBF) and improve cardiovascular stability at birth.

Methods

Preterm sheep fetuses (0.9 gestation) were delivered via cesarean section and instrumented to measure carotid pressure and flow, PBF, and cerebral (SctO2) and arterial (SaO2) oxygenation. Ewes were randomized to maternal oxygen supplementation (O2Supp; fetal PaO2 > 20 mmHg, n = 7) or reduction (O2Red; PaO2 < 20 mmHg, n = 8). After reaching target PaO2, lambs underwent immediate cord clamping, with ventilation withheld for 1 min, then maintained for 30 min.

Results

O2Supp increased fetal pH, PaO2, SpO2, SctO2, and PBF (28.5 ± 7.8 vs 4.0 ± 3.2 mL/min/kg), which was maintained during the period between cord clamping and ventilation. Cord clamping increased blood pressure but reduced oxygenation in O2Supp lambs. Ventilation caused marked increases in carotid pressure and flow in O2Red lambs, which were attenuated by prior oxygen supplementation.

Conclusions

Maternal oxygen supplementation enhances fetal oxygenation and PBF before cord clamping and reduces cardiovascular instability, suggesting potential benefits for improving cardiovascular stability in preterm infants.

Impact

The impact of maternal and fetal oxygenation on the cardiovascular transition is not known. We found that maternal oxygen supplementation improves fetal oxygen and increases pulmonary blood flow prior to cord clamping. Maternal oxygen supplementation stabilizes carotid blood pressure and flow during cord clamping and ventilation onset. Our findings suggest that maternal oxygen supplementation may provide cardiovascular stability for preterm infants at birth.

title: In Vivo CRISPR Base Editing of ANGPTL3 for Durable Lipid Lowering.
authorString: Mizoguchi T, DeNizio JE, Chadwick AC, Mazzola AM, Brown MP, Mishra S, Damle M, Matsumoto Y, Neang V, Garrity R, Mantri M, Olorife JO, Hsu HT, Peshdary V, Shabani E, Ganey JD, Santos R, Federico A, Garcia SP, Hao P, Wu Y, Glass Z, Kasiewicz LN, Summers C, Sanjeev A, Wang K, Briscoe SD, Rosenson RS, Cheng CJ, Rohde E, Biedenkapp J, Farutin V, Bellinger AM, Musunuru K, Kathiresan S, Lister T, Rajeev KG, Lee RG, Khera AV.
abstractText: Circulating concentrations of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and triglyceride-rich lipoproteins are leading risk factors for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease<sup>1</sup>. Despite several approved lipid-lowering medications, most patients fail to achieve target lipid levels under the chronic care treatment model<sup>2,3</sup>. Here, we describe a potential single-course treatment in which an infusion of guide RNA and mRNA encoding a CRISPR adenine base editor-encapsulated within a GalNAc-lipid nanoparticle-leads to durable, liver-selective inactivation of angiopoietin-like 3 (ANGPTL3), a known driver of increased LDL-C and triglyceride concentrations. Analyses in human liver cells in vitro confirmed that the base editor introduces a DNA base-pair change at the target ANGPTL3 locus with no detectable off-target editing at any of approximately 3000 candidate sites or treatment-related structural variants. Targeted ANGPTL3 inactivation in nonhuman primates was well-tolerated and led to a > 90% mean reduction in circulating ANGPTL3 protein, with durability confirmed out to 3 years following a single dose. In mouse and nonhuman primate models of hyperlipidemia, gene inactivation was associated with reductions of approximately 40 to 50% in LDL-C and 50 to 70% in triglycerides. These results provided the scientific foundation for initiation of an ongoing first-in-human clinical trial in patients with refractory hyperlipidemia syndromes.

title: Lifestyle counseling including the DASH diet improves multiple metabolomic profiles.
authorString: Mehri Hajmir M, Wang X, van Dam RM.
abstractText:
Background

Lifestyle interventions improve cardiometabolic risk factors, but data from randomized trials on their impact on detailed metabolomic profiles remain limited.

Objectives

Our aim was to evaluate the effects of lifestyle counseling with and without the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet on changes in metabolomic patterns.

Methods

We analyzed data from 690 adult participants of the randomized PREMIER trial. The trial compared three lifestyle interventions: 'Advice-only', 'Established', and 'Established plus DASH'. Fasting plasma metabolites were quantified by NMR spectroscopy at baseline and 6 months, and principal component (PC) analysis was used to identify metabolomic patterns. Multiple linear regression examined the interventions and changes in BMI and heart rate in relation to changes in PC scores and individual metabolites.

Results

Thirteen PCs representing lipoprotein, triglyceride-rich, amino acid, fatty acid, inflammatory, and ketone-related patterns were identified. Compared with Advice-only, the Established intervention reduced PC4 (β = -0.50, P = 0.04), VLDL cholesterol, and saturated fatty acids. Established plus DASH had broader effects, reducing PC9 (β = -0.33, P = 0.01), PC11 (β = -0.28 P = 0.004), and PC12 (β = -0.23, P = 0.02), increasing omega-3 fatty acids, and lowering branched-chain and aromatic amino acids, lactate, citrate, and GlycA. BMI change was associated with multiple PCs, whereas heart rate change showed fewer independent associations.

Conclusions

Lifestyle interventions induce coordinated metabolomic changes across lipid, amino acid, and inflammatory pathways. Weight loss appears to be the primary driver, while adding DASH provides broader metabolomic benefits than standard lifestyle counseling.

Clinical trial registration number

ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00000616 (PREMIER: Lifestyle Interventions for Blood Pressure Control - Full Text View - ClinicalTrials.gov).

title: Effectiveness of a Multicomponent Digital Therapeutic Program on Inhaled Medication Adherence in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
authorString: Wu H, Dong F, Cui Y, Hu D, Zhang Y, Peng T, Peng Y, Li X, Li Y, Li X, Chen Y, Yu Q, Niu H, Yang T.
abstractText:
Background

Poor medication adherence is a critical impediment to effective chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) management and remains challenging to track in routine care. Digital therapeutic interventions may improve chronic disease management through remote monitoring and patient education. However, most existing digital interventions focus on individual components of disease management, and evidence from longer-term pragmatic randomized controlled trials evaluating integrated digital therapeutics in routine clinical practice remains limited.

Objective

This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a multicomponent digital therapeutic program combining electronic inhaler monitoring (EIM) with behavioral support in improving medication adherence and symptom-related outcomes among patients with COPD prescribed pressurized metered-dose inhalers, and to assess patient engagement and implementation in routine clinical practice.

Methods

In this prospective, open-label, unblinded, randomized controlled trial, patients with COPD prescribed pressurized metered-dose inhalers were enrolled and randomized in a 2:1 ratio to either the intervention group or the control group. All participants received an EIM device to objectively record inhaler use throughout the 24-week study period. Patients in the intervention group also received personalized medication reminders from the EIM, adherence feedback, educational content, and clinician-supported follow-up through an integrated digital management platform based on EIM-derived data, whereas the control group received usual care. The primary outcome was medication adherence over 24 weeks. Secondary outcomes included exacerbations, COPD symptoms, quality of life, and lung function.

Results

A total of 158 participants were randomized, including 106 in the intervention group and 52 in the control group. The median monitoring coverage was 161.5 (IQR 86.3-168.0) days during the follow-up period. The self-reported adherence measured using the Test of Adherence to Inhalers showed no significant between-group differences at any follow-up time point. However, the electronically monitored adherence was significantly higher in the intervention group than in the control group (59.5% vs 33.1%, P=.009). Adherence declined over time in both groups, decreasing from 85.3% during weeks 0 to 4 to 43.0% during weeks 12 to 24 in the intervention group and from 76.8% to 11.9% in the control group over the same intervals, resulting in a progressively larger between-group difference over follow-up. No significant differences were observed in exacerbations, health-related quality of life, symptom burden, lung function, or mental health outcomes. In an exploratory analysis, a significantly greater proportion of participants in the intervention group achieved the minimal clinically important difference in the COPD Assessment Test score than in the control group (odds ratio 2.21, 95% CI 1.11-4.41; P=.02).

Conclusions

The multicomponent digital therapeutic program significantly improved objective medication adherence in patients with COPD over 24 weeks. While most clinical outcomes did not differ significantly between groups, the higher proportion of participants achieving a clinically meaningful improvement in the COPD Assessment Test score warrants further investigation.

title: Neuromodulatory effects of audio-proprio-phonatory reinforcement training on subjective tinnitus, a HD-EEG study protocol.
authorString: Marié-Bailly I, Guillard R, Wanneveich M, De Dieuleveult B, Hassan M, Vérin M.
abstractText: Tinnitus affects 14% of the global population, with 2% experiencing a severe form of the condition. Sound therapy using white noise emitted by hearing aids is a common intervention, supported by the phenomenon of residual inhibition observed during tinnitus assessment. This study aims to investigate whether audio-proprio-phonatory reinforcement training can improve the quality of life of patients with chronic subjective tinnitus by enabling them to listen to their own phonation, which may mask the tinnitus or induce residual inhibition. We will conduct a prospective, controlled, monocentric, 2-arm block-randomized study, stratified by the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory (THI) score, involving two groups for two sequential phases (Phase 1 and Phase 2). Fifty-six patients with tinnitus, recruited from the Ear Nose Throat (ENT) Department of Orléans University Hospital, will undergo a five-week training program, randomized into weekly remote group workshops, and daily individual sessions using specially developed videos. Training efficacy will be assessed through self-report questionnaires. The primary endpoint, the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory, will be assessed at three ENT medical visits: at inclusion, end of phase 1 and end of phase 2. Additionally, patients in both groups will regularly complete Visual Analog Scales for Tinnitus and five related questions (noise, cervical, jaw, sleep, stress-anxiety) via a secure digital platform throughout the study. High-density electroencephalograms (HD-EEG) will be performed in a blinded manner before and after Phase 1 at the Neurology Department of Orléans University Hospital. This pilot study aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy of audio-proprio-phonatory training in patients with chronic subjective tinnitus and to objectively measure its effects using HD-EEG. We will explore potential correlations between changes brain activity (such as functional brain connectivity) and clinical responses to the intervention.

title: Efficacy of a Smartphone-Based Virtual Patient in Increasing Clinical Competence Among Primary Health Care Providers: Protocol for a Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial.
authorString: Wang X, Zhang K, Du J, Cai Y, Cao J, Chen Y, Ding L, Fang Y, Gong W, He W, Li J, Liang H, Liao J, Lu Y, Mi B, Pan J, Wang R, Xu DR, Zhang N, Zhao Q, Zhou J, Zhou Z, Wang Z.
abstractText:
Background

Virtual patients (VPs) are considered cost-effective and convenient tools for clinical training. The research team developed a smartphone-based VP tailored to the needs of primary health care physicians in rural China. The VP demonstrated high levels of feasibility and acceptability in this group in a previous study.

Objective

The proposed cluster randomized controlled trial (RCT) will compare the efficacy of clinical training delivered via a smartphone-based VP in increasing diagnosis and treatment competence among primary health care providers in rural China as compared to a waitlist control group.

Methods

This is a partially blinded (outcome assessors and data analysts) and parallel-group cluster RCT conducted in Lintao county, China. All 18 township health centers in Lintao will be randomized evenly into either the intervention or the waitlist control group. The target sample size is 150 physicians per group. Physicians in the intervention group will receive clinical training delivered via the smartphone-based VP. They will be required to complete the diagnosis and treatment plan of 2 conditions randomly assigned by the VP within a 1-month intervention period. The VP will provide detailed feedback on their procedures. The intervention group can also access 9 other conditions in the VP and receive detailed feedback during the intervention period. Participants in the control group will not have access to any clinical training delivered via the VP during the 1-month intervention period. They will gain full access to the VP system after completion of the outcome assessment at T1 (1 month after baseline [T0]). The primary outcome is the score representing overall diagnosis and treatment competence. To measure this outcome, participants will be invited to complete the diagnosis and treatment plan of a condition randomly assigned by the smartphone-based VP at both T0 and T1. Intention-to-treat analysis will be performed.

Results

Study recruitment started on August 1, 2026. By August 15, 2026, a total of 18 township health centers had been randomly assigned to either the intervention (9 centers) or control (9 centers) group. A total of 216 physicians from these centers completed baseline assessment; 56% (121/216) were randomly assigned to the intervention group, and 44% (95/216) were assigned to the control group. Recruitment will be completed by the end of November 2026. The follow-up assessment at T1 will start in September 2026. Data collection is expected to be concluded in January 2027.

Conclusions

The findings will extend the application of smartphone-based VPs in medical training. If the smartphone-based VP is proven effective in increasing diagnosis and treatment competence among primary health care physicians in rural China, it will provide a feasible and effective alternative training tool to address the existing service gaps.

title: Efficacy of diadynamic currents versus transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation for transcutaneous tibial nerve stimulation in subjects with overactive bladder syndrome: A double-blind randomized controlled trial.
authorString: Tedla JS, Lalaji SL, Midde AK, Papalkar NA, Bindhu Priya N, Sangadala DR, Reddy RS, Mukherjee D, Alamri AM, Alzahrani AS, Alhadi NA.
abstractText:
Background

In the traditional treatment of overactive bladder (OAB) with transcutaneous posterior tibial nerve stimulation (TTNS), physical therapists currently use only transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS). However, the literature has commonly replaced TENS with diadynamic currents for various musculoskeletal pain syndromes. Moreover, no literature describes the use of diadynamic currents in the TTNS procedure. Therefore, our study aimed to determine the efficacy of diadynamic currents (DDC) versus TENS for TTNS in OAB Treatment.

Methodology

A randomized controlled trial was conducted among female patients with OAB aged 18-80 years. Subjects were randomly allocated to control and experimental groups. Participants in the control group received TTNS with TENS, and those in the experimental group underwent TTNS using DDC. Both groups received 8 TTNS sessions, two per week for 4 weeks. We measured pre- and post-intervention improvements using the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire (ICIQ) for OAB and the ICIQ OAB Quality of Life (QOL). The study is registered with the Clinical Trials Registry of India under registration number CTRI/2025/12/099269.

Results

The mean age of the included sample was 59.75 years. Pre- and post-intervention ICIQ-OAB and ICIQ-OAB QOL scores showed significant improvements in disease symptoms and quality of life among patients with OAB in both the control and experimental groups. Comparison of improvements between the two groups on the ICIQ questionnaires showed no significant difference (p-values of 0.87 and 0.95). Correlations between patient-related characteristics and improvements in outcome measures were also not significant.

Conclusion

Eight sessions of TENS and DDC, combined with conventional physical therapy, including Kegel and breathing exercises, can reduce OAB symptoms and improve QOL in subjects with OAB syndrome. Diadynamic current can be used as an adjunct to conventional TENS in TTNS for treating OAB syndrome.

title: Micropeptides: challenges and opportunities in cardiovascular pharmacology.
authorString: Biondi-Zoccai G, Giordano S, Corcione N, Booz GW.
abstractText: Micropeptides are small proteins that generally comprise fewer than 100 amino acids and are translated from short or noncanonical open reading frames. They were long overlooked, but their role is being actively explored as biologically active regulators with potential pharmacological relevance. Advances in ribosome profiling, proteogenomics, peptidomics, and computational modelling have enabled the identification and characterization of a substantially larger repertoire of micropeptides. Yet, it is important to focus on rigorous validation of endogenous translation, molecular targets, concentration-dependent activity, and peptide-specific effects. In particular, cardiovascular micropeptides can regulate myocardial calcium handling and contractility, exemplified by DWORF, which activates sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase 2a and has shown therapeutic potential in multiple preclinical models of cardiomyopathy and heart failure. Other candidates, including mitoregulin, mitolamban, BRAWNIN, IAMP, SPAAR, and MFRLP, have been linked to distinct aspects of mitochondrial bioenergetics, inflammatory signalling, ischemia-reperfusion injury, angiogenesis, vascular smooth-muscle phenotypic switching, and arterial remodeling. Collectively, these findings suggest that micropeptides may provide novel therapeutic targets or pharmacological tools across several cardiovascular conditions, including heart failure, ischemia-reperfusion injury, and vascular remodeling. However, clinical translation will require advances in tissue-specific delivery, control of expression and stoichiometry, pharmacokinetic characterization, safety assessment, biomarker development, and demonstration of reproducible effectiveness in human-relevant and large-animal models before evaluation in clinical trials.

title: Thrombotic microangiopathy after kidney transplant: a mechanistic + therapeutic decision tree.
authorString: Chutani A, Francis JM, Mahmoud H.

journal.title: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension

abstractText:
Purpose of review

Posttransplant thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) is classified as de novo or recurrent, with distinct triggers and management implications for kidney transplant recipients. This review provides an etiology-based framework for de novo TMA and the current approach to diagnosis, pretransplant risk assessment, and management of recurrent complement-mediated TMA (atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome).

Recent findings

Complement alternative pathway dysregulation underlies both de novo and recurrent posttransplant TMA, with pathogenic variants in complement regulatory proteins-factor H, complement regulatory proteins-factor I, and membrane cofactor protein identified in a substantial minority of affected recipients and increasingly sought as a second hit alongside calcineurin inhibitor exposure, antibody-mediated rejection, infection, and ischemia-reperfusion injury. Eculizumab, and increasingly ravulizumab, have transformed outcomes in complement-mediated disease, with growing evidence supporting pretransplant prophylactic use in high-recurrence-risk genotypes and protocol-based alternatives in lower-risk settings.

Summary

A systematic, etiology-directed approach-addressing reversible triggers, excluding rejection and infection, and reserving complement blockade for complement-mediated or refractory disease-remains central to managing posttransplant TMA, though randomized trial data to guide optimal prophylactic strategy remain limited.

title: The Art Behind the Algorithm: Hybrid Ablation and the Need for a Lifetime Strategy in Non-Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation.
authorString: Spadaccio C, Schena S, Sherman AJ.

journal.title: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText: The management of persistent and long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation remains highly variable in clinical practice, despite increasingly refined guidelines and an expanding ablation armamentarium. Treatment sequencing is frequently driven by local program infrastructure and institutional culture, and hybrid ablation is often deferred until multiple endocardial procedures have failed, by which point progressive atrial remodeling may have already narrowed the therapeutic window. Randomized and registry data support a meaningful role for hybrid ablation earlier in the disease course of selected patients with non-paroxysmal AF, particularly those with enlarged atria, prolonged AF duration, advanced substrate, or failed prior endocardial ablation. Contemporary pulsed-field ablation technology has improved procedural safety and efficiency, yet freedom from recurrence at one year in persistent AF remains substantially lower than in paroxysmal AF across all current energy platforms, reflecting the complexity of atrial substrate over time. This ongoing myocardial remodeling places non-paroxysmal AF closer to a chronic structural cardiac disease than to a discrete procedural target and demands a lifetime management strategy rather than a sequence of isolated procedural decisions. The mindset for other progressive structural cardiac diseases has already moved in this direction-aortic valve stenosis is now managed through a multidisciplinary team that integrates anatomy, timing, procedural durability, and long-term risk across the full patient trajectory. We propose an AF Heart Team framework for non-paroxysmal AF in which catheter-based, hybrid, and surgical strategies are selected according to disease phenotype and lifetime trajectory, with the goal of intervening before advanced remodeling reduces the likelihood of durable rhythm control.

title: Population-based screening for familial hypercholesterolaemia.
authorString: Schlein C, Piel-Behrendt SYL.

journal.title: Medizinische Genetik : Mitteilungsblatt des Berufsverbandes Medizinische Genetik e.V

abstractText: Familial hypercholesterolaemia (FH) is among the most common monogenic disorders, affecting at least 1 in 250 individuals. Lifelong elevation of LDL cholesterol from birth can cause accelerated atherosclerosis and premature cardiovascular disease. However, the vast majority of affected children (and adults) remain undiagnosed. Population-based childhood screening, combining LDL cholesterol measurement with genetic testing, enables early diagnosis and treatment. This review summarizes evidence on childhood FH screening, including disease burden, treatment efficacy, diagnostic performance, and economic considerations. Although no randomized trial has compared screened and unscreened populations, extensive indirect evidence supports the benefit of early detection and lipid-lowering therapy.

title: Systematic review of pulmonary and cardiovascular disease among asphalt pavers.
authorString: Sandvik A, Bugge MD, Nordby KC, Jørgensen IL, Randem BG, Smedslund G, Vist GE, Brinchmann BC.
abstractText:
Background

Asphalt pavers may be exposed to a wide range of potentially hazardous substances, and an annual decline in lung function among asphalt pavers has been reported. Studies reporting a modest increase in lung cancer mortality among asphalt workers have been thoroughly summarized and reviewed.

Aims

The aim of this paper was to systematically review and meta-analyse mortality from non-malignant pulmonary diseases and cardiovascular disease (CVD) associated with asphalt paving (PROSPERO Nr CRD42022341463).

Methods

A librarian conducted a literature search in February 2024. We included human studies, assessed risk of bias, conducted meta-analysis and assessed confidence in effect-estimates using GRADE. We included cohort studies reporting estimates on mortality from non-malignant pulmonary disease and CVD among asphalt pavers compared with referents.

Results

We included 10 cohort studies (3714 to 248 087 participants). Asphalt paving was associated with standardized mortality ratio (SMR) from all causes of 0.94 (95% CI 0.81-1.07), SMR from non-malignant pulmonary disease was 1.19 (95% CI 0.95-1.42), whereas SMR from CVD was 0.88 (95% CI 0.75-1.02).

Conclusions

Our study gave no support to the hypothesis linking asphalt work to excess mortality from cardiovascular or non-malignant pulmonary disease. The studies were not adequately adjusted for confounders. Healthy worker bias may have affected the results. From the GRADE assessment we are uncertain (very low confidence) about the association between asphalt paving and mortality from cardiovascular or non-malignant pulmonary disease. New studies, especially on non-malignant pulmonary disease with better control of confounding factors are warranted.

title: Sudden Death in Patients with Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Pooled Analysis of Five Randomized Trials.
authorString: Ariss RW, Hamatani Y, Claggett BL, Vaduganathan M, Desai AS, Solbes ASC, Shen L, Jhund PS, Anand IS, Zile MR, Pfeffer MA, McMurray JJV, Solomon SD, Cunningham JW.

title: Cardiovascular disease risk prediction models for people living with HIV in Sub-Saharan Africa: A scoping review protocol.
authorString: Ntiyani N, Letamo G, Keetile M, Disang M.
abstractText:
Background

The landscape of Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) care has dramatically shifted with the advent of effective antiretroviral therapy (ART), transforming HIV from a rapidly fatal illness into a chronic, manageable disease. This success, however, has unveiled new challenges, primarily the increased prevalence of non-AIDS-related comorbidities, with non-communicable diseases (NCDs) such as cardiovascular disease (CVD) emerging as a critical concern for people living with HIV (PLWH). CVD has now become a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in this population, and its risk assessment is imperative. However, there is scanty data on CVD risk prediction models developed and/or applied among PLWH in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). Therefore, this planned scoping review aims to systematically map existing literature on CVD risk prediction models developed and/or used among PLWH in SSA. The review will identify the models that have been developed, used, and validated in the region.

Methods

The scoping review protocol will follow an established framework for conducting scoping reviews. The study will employ the methodological approaches by Arksey and O'Malley and its recent advances, the Joanna Briggs Institute, and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis Protocols. The objective of the scoping review will be achieved through a comprehensive published literature search from 01 January 2000 to 03 June 2026 across five selected databases: PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and CINAHL, based on a predefined strategy. Inclusion criteria will focus on studies written in English that develop, validate, or apply CVD risk prediction models among PLWH in SSA. The screening of search results and data extraction will be conducted by two independent reviewers.

Expected outcomes and conclusions

The review will synthesize and summarize the existing literature on CVD risk prediction developed and used among PLWH in SSA, identify knowledge gaps, and provide insights to inform the development of a novel CVD risk prediction model specific to PLWH in SSA. Registration: Open Science Framework https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/XVFUA.

title: Impact of Particulate Matter Exposure on Neurological Health in Older Adults: A Systematic Review.
authorString: Zaręba M, Pietrzak D, Stolecka A, Zupo R, Castellana FS, Nawrot TS, Lampignano L, Bortone I, Sardone R, Madowicz J, Musioł K, Gruszecka-Kosowska A.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

This systematic review evaluates the current epidemiological evidence on the relationship between particulate matter (PM) exposure and neurological health in older adults, with particular attention to cognitive decline and neurodegenerative disease.

Recent findings

A PRISMA-guided systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect was conducted through January 2026. Twenty-one observational studies met the inclusion criteria. The most frequently studied outcomes were cognitive performance and decline and cognitive impairment, including mild cognitive impairment (MCI), with several studies reporting adverse associations, particularly for long-term PM2.5 exposure. Evidence for dementia and Alzheimer's disease was also provided by several large cohort studies, although findings varied across exposure metrics and clinical endpoints. In contrast, evidence for Parkinson's disease-related hospitalizations, cerebral amyloid burden, retinal neurodegeneration, mental disorder-related hospital admissions, and individual PM constituents was more limited and was often based on one or a few studies. Findings concerning specific PM constituents were heterogeneous and should therefore be considered exploratory. The available evidence suggests an association between PM exposure and adverse neurological health in older adults, with the most substantial evidence concerning long-term PM2.5 exposure and cognitive outcomes. However, the strength and certainty of the evidence vary considerably across pollutants and neurological endpoints. Heterogeneity in study design, exposure assessment, and outcome definitions should be considered when interpreting the overall findings.

title: Revisiting the role of sex in stroke risk stratification in atrial fibrillation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Yeh CY, Lee PH, Wu CS, Chen PH, Chen HH, Chan PK, Yoshimura H, Lin WY, Lee CC.
abstractText:
Background

The 2024 European Society of Cardiology guidelines introduced the CHA2DS2-VA score, omitting female sex from stroke risk stratification in atrial fibrillation (AF). However, evidence on the relative predictive performance of CHA2DS2-VA versus CHA2DS2-VASc across diverse populations remains inconsistent. We therefore conducted a systematic evaluation of their discrimination and reclassification performance.

Methods

We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational cohort studies comparing CHA2DS2-VA and CHA2DS2-VASc for prediction of ischaemic stroke or thromboembolic events in patients with AF. Discrimination was evaluated using the difference in C-statistics (ΔAUC) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), and reclassification using continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI). Pooled estimates were derived using random-effects models.

Results

Seven studies including 250,112 patients were analysed. In the overall population, discriminative performance was comparable between the CHA2DS2-VA and CHA2DS2-VASc scores (ΔAUC 0.00065, 95% CI -0.00288 to 0.00417; IDI 0.00010, 95% CI -0.00063 to 0.00083). Continuous NRI indicated a modest advantage for CHA2DS2-VASc (-0.05615; 95% CI: -0.10350 to -0.00880). Among patients not receiving oral anticoagulation, both discrimination and reclassification were similar between the two scores. Variability in reclassification performance was observed across regions and study periods.

Conclusions

The CHA2DS2-VA and CHA2DS2-VASc scores showed comparable discrimination for stroke risk prediction in patients with AF when evaluated as continuous scores, although reclassification modestly favoured the CHA2DS2-VASc score. The clinical contribution of female sex to risk prediction appears context-dependent and warrants further evaluation.

title: The relationship between cardiac output and postexercise hypotension differs according to resting blood pressure status: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Leme da Silva JCP, Lima da Silva N, Borges JP, Cordeiro R, Rocha J, Rangel M, Brasil I, Farinatti P.
abstractText:
Objective

To examine whether postexercise blood pressure (BP) reductions are associated with changes in cardiac output (CO) and its components and whether these relationships depend on baseline BP status.

Methods

This systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO: CRD42021256569) included studies assessing BP and central hemodynamic responses at least 30 min after aerobic exercise. Random- and mixed-effects models and meta-regression examined associations between BP and CO, stroke volume (SV), and heart rate (HR), stratified by baseline BP status.

Results

Fifty-six trials were included (101 interventions; 1026 participants, 31.2 ± 5.1 years, 120.4 ± 8.9/72.3 ± 7.6 mmHg). Aerobic exercise reduced systolic, diastolic, and mean arterial pressure. Meta-regression analyses revealed that the association between BP reduction and central hemodynamic responses differed according to baseline BP. In individuals with normal BP, no associations between BP and CO, SV, or HR remained significant after correction for multiple testing. In contrast, in individuals with elevated BP, greater reductions in SBP were associated with greater reductions in CO [slope = 0.659; 95% confidence interval (95% CI), 0.268-1.051; P < 0.001], and this association remained significant after false discovery rate and Bonferroni corrections. No other associations between BP and CO, SV, or HR remained significant.

Conclusion

Greater postexercise reductions in SBP were associated with reductions in CO in individuals with elevated BP, whereas no consistent association was observed in individuals with normal BP. These findings indicate that the relationship between postexercise BP and hemodynamic responses differs according to baseline BP status, with a stronger association between SBP and CO responses in individuals with elevated BP, without establishing a causal relationship.

title: Genetic and phenotypic landscape of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in the MENA region: a systematic review.
authorString: Iqbal S, Syauqi K, Alsaiqal A, Hasan A, Aldosari WR, Carlus J, Al-Harbi KM, Al-Haidose A, Abdallah AM.
abstractText:
Background

Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is the most common inherited cardiomyopathy, and it is a leading cause of sudden cardiac death (SCD) in young people. Recessive genetic disorders are especially prevalent in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region due to consanguinity, which affects the genetic landscape of hereditary disorders. Here we conducted a systematic review of mutations in patients with HCM in the MENA and report genotype-phenotype associations to provide an evidence base for personalized diagnostic and therapeutic interventions.

Methods

We systematically searched the PubMed, ProQuest, and Scopus databases from inception until October 2025 to collect all genetic data and phenotypes of patients with HCM in the MENA. Broad search terms were used to capture all relevant literature describing genetic variants associated with HCM in the MENA region including inheritance patterns and genotype-phenotype associations.

Results

The database search returned 448 studies, with 17 meeting inclusion criteria. 14 studies were case series, 2 studies were case reports, and 1 was a case-control study. In 1323 HCM subjects in the MENA, there were 107 genetic variants in 21 genes. The majority of the variants occurred in MYBPC3 and MYH7, consistent with other populations. However, there were also homozygous variants in recessive genes, founder mutations, and novel variants in non-sarcomeric genes in the region, with patients experiencing more severe clinical phenotypes.

Conclusion

To our knowledge, this is the first systematic review on genetic variants associated with HCM in the MENA region. The genetic landscape of HCM is complex and unique in the MENA. The underrepresentation of MENA populations in global genomic resources remains a barrier to variant interpretation. Region-specific gene panels may be required to advance the diagnosis of HCM in the region.

title: Primary repair during the neonatal period for tetralogy of Fallot (RIFAN): a multicentre randomised controlled trial protocol in China.
authorString: Zhongyi H, Yalun Q, Lv L, Hua Z, Li X, Ye M, Luo S, Wu Y, Liu S, Yang S, Yang J, Mo Y, Li W, Li G, Wang Q, RIFAN Trial Collaboration Group.

title: Dilated Virchow-Robin Space and Cognitive Impairment in People With Parkinson's Disease: A Systematic Review.
authorString: Salari M, Mirabedini M, Rezaei K, Etemadifar M.
abstractText: Virchow-Robin space (VRS) is characterized by small cavitary or cystic structures in the brain that represent morphological markers of altered interstitial fluid dynamics within the perivascular (glymphatic) pathway, originating from small vessels in the subarachnoid space and penetrating the brain. Their dilation has been associated with altered clinical status in Parkinson's disease (PD). The present study aims to review the reported relations between dilated VRS (dVRS) and cognitive impairment in patients with PD. A total of 71 articles were identified through database searching, and after reviewing based on the eligibility criteria, 16 studies were selected. Across the directly relevant PD studies, dVRS burden was associated with lower scores on some cognitive tests in some, but not all, cohorts; several studies reported null or only indirect associations. The most commonly used assessment tool was Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA); the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), Frontal Assessment Battery (FAB), Seoul Neuropsychological Screening Battery (SNSB), and Parkinson Neuropsychometric Dementia Assessment (PANDA) were also used across the included studies. Overall, the presence of the dVRS in basal ganglia in patients with PD was frequently associated with the vascular risk factors, and the resulting mechanical mass effect (local compression and displacement of adjacent neural structures by the dilated, fluid-filled spaces), impaired waste clearance, and vascular impact have been proposed as pathways potentially relating dVRS to cognitive status in these patients. Cognitive decline in the case of basal ganglia dVRS is shown to be associated with crossing inferior fronto-occipital and inferior longitudinal fasciculus fibers.

title: Prevalence of low-renin hypertension: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Shah SS, Bhatia R, Chauhan K, Fuller PJ, Yang J.
abstractText:
Background

Current recommendations support measuring plasma renin and aldosterone in all adults with hypertension to detect primary aldosteronism (PA). However, clinical guidelines do not address individuals with low renin (commonly defined as a direct renin concentration <10 mU/l or plasma renin activity <1 ng/ml/h) who do not meet diagnostic criteria for PA and have normal or low aldosterone concentration, a normal aldosterone-to-renin ratio, and/or adequate suppression of aldosterone following salt loading or captopril challenge. This systematic review aimed to estimate the global prevalence of low-renin hypertension, as emerging evidence suggests this group may benefit from treatment distinct from standard antihypertensive therapy.

Methods

The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD42023467251). MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane databases were searched for studies reporting renin measurements in hypertension. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data, with disagreements resolved by consensus. Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute tool. Pooled prevalence estimates and heterogeneity were calculated using random-intercept logistic regression and I2 statistics.

Results

Of 2745 records identified (1968-2024), 56 studies involving 13 210 participants met inclusion criteria. The pooled prevalence of low-renin hypertension was 32% (95% CI 28-35%; I2 =  94%). Prevalence was higher in studies with >70% Black participants (47% vs. 30%, P = 0.034). In studies with confirmatory testing to exclude PA, the pooled prevalence was 27% (95% CI 25-29%; I2 = 0%).

Conclusion

Low-renin hypertension affects a substantial proportion of individuals with hypertension, particularly among Black populations. Further research is necessary to guide optimal management.

title: Acute Kidney Injury in East Africa in an Era of Converging Renal Stressors: A Multiple-Hit Narrative Review.
authorString: Yusuf AA, Abdi DA, Hassan AM, Hirsi AM, Kabayare IA, Mohomed AA, Abdulle AH, Ulusow KH.
abstractText:
Background

Acute kidney injury (AKI) remains an important cause of morbidity and mortality in East Africa, where infectious disease, volume depletion, hemodynamic instability, and nephrotoxic exposure frequently occur in resource-constrained clinical settings. This review aimed to synthesize regional evidence through a multiple-hit framework focused on three modifiable renal stressor domains.

Methods

A structured narrative review of PubMed, Embase, and Scopus was conducted for peer-reviewed human studies published from January 2012 to 18 August 2026 across the 18 Eastern African countries defined by the United Nations M49 framework. Eligible studies examined AKI in relation to volume depletion or hemodynamic compromise, infection or inflammatory illness, and/or nephrotoxic exposure.

Results

Of 902 records identified, 420 duplicates were removed, 482 records were screened, 66 full-text reports were assessed, and 45 studies were included. Evidence originated from only six countries: Ethiopia, Uganda, Tanzania, Kenya, Somalia/Somaliland, and Rwanda. Across adult, pediatric, neonatal, obstetric, infectious-disease, emergency, cardiac, and critical-care populations, AKI was associated with dehydration, hemorrhage, hypotension, shock, malaria, sepsis and other infections, nephrotoxic medications, iodinated contrast, and traditional or herbal medicines. The most consistently documented pattern was cohort-level clustering of more than one renal stressor domain within the same clinical populations. Individual-level coexistence was documented in selected studies, whereas detailed temporal sequencing was uncommon. Most studies assessed exposures separately and rarely examined cumulative effects, exposure timing, or statistical interaction.

Conclusion

The currently available evidence from East Africa supports a multiple-hit perspective as a clinical organizing framework rather than a proven biological or prognostic model. Because the evidence is geographically concentrated, particularly in Ethiopia, Uganda, and Tanzania, these findings should not be interpreted as representative of all East African settings. Recurrent cohort-level clustering of infectious or inflammatory, hemodynamic, and nephrotoxic stressors was well documented, but patient-level coexistence and temporal sequence remain incompletely characterized. Prospective multicountry studies with patient-level temporal data are needed to determine whether the timing, overlap, duration, or combination of these stressors influences AKI severity, recovery, and longer-term outcomes.

title: Development of a novel drowning index using predicted body weight and evaluation of its diagnostic performance.
authorString: Yoshimiya M, Yamamura R, Ueda A, Takeuchi I, Kakimoto Y.
abstractText:
Objective

The aim of this study was to develop a predicted body weight-based drowning index (PBW-DI) and compare its diagnostic performance with that of the conventional drowning index (DI).

Methods

This retrospective study included 46 drowning and 26 acute cardiac death cases. The PBW-DI was calculated by dividing the combined weight of the lungs and pleural fluid by predicted body weight (PBW) derived from height and sex. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis. A secondary analysis was performed to assess the effects of advanced decomposition.

Results

PBW-DI values were significantly higher in drowning than in acute cardiac death cases (median, 27.7 [interquartile range, 25.0-31.4] vs. 18.4 [16.0-20.0] g/kg; p < 0.001). The area under the curve was 0.948 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.888-1.000) for the PBW-DI and 0.893 (95% CI, 0.802-0.984) for the DI, with no significant difference (p = 0.280). In exploratory analyses, PBW-DI also showed higher AUCs than indices normalized to actual body weight (0.901; p = 0.0335) or height (0.906; p = 0.0371). The optimal PBW-DI cutoff was 23.6 g/kg, with 0.935 sensitivity and 1.000 specificity. PBW-DI values were significantly lower with advanced than with mild-to-moderate decomposition (22.9 [17.5-27.4] vs. 27.7 [25.0-31.4] g/kg; p = 0.002).

Conclusions

The PBW-DI showed good diagnostic performance without requiring spleen weight, which may be affected by pathological conditions. However, advanced decomposition should be considered when interpreting results. The PBW-DI may serve as a novel objective adjunct to the postmortem diagnosis of drowning.

title: Development and Validation of a Prediction Model for Recurrent Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease.
authorString: Zhou H, Zhang Y, Zhou MM, Choi SK, Morrissette KL, Reynolds K, Bellows BK, Moran AE, Colantonio LD, Safford MM, Xanthakis V, Isasi CR, An J.
abstractText:
Background

The definition of very high risk from the American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology 2018 and 2026 cholesterol guidelines may oversimplify heterogeneity in recurrent atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk.

Objectives

We developed a prediction model for recurrent ASCVD and compared its performance with the 2018 cholesterol guideline.

Methods

We used electronic health records from Kaiser Permanente Southern California (KPSC) for model development and the REGARDS (Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke) cohort for external validation. We included adults with a prior ASCVD and followed them for recurrent ASCVD or up to 10 years. We used elastic net regularization for predictor selection and a Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards model for model development. Model performance was evaluated using time-dependent area under the curve, sensitivity, and specificity compared with the 2018 guideline.

Results

Among 70,310 and 5,239 adults from KPSC and REGARDS, 17,344 and 1,185 experienced recurrent ASCVD during the median (Q1, Q3) follow-up of 6.1 (2.5, 10) and 8.3 (4.0, 10) years, respectively. Time-dependent area under the curves were 0.68 (95% CI: 0.66-0.69) in KPSC and 0.67 (95% CI: 0.65-0.69) in REGARDS. Compared with the 2018 guideline, using a 5-year 15% risk threshold, the model classified a similar proportion of patients as high risk and improved sensitivity from 64% (95% CI: 62%-66%) to 73% (95% CI: 71%-75%) in KPSC and from 69% (95% CI: 65%-72%) to 73% (95% CI: 69%-76%) in REGARDS; specificity remained similar in KPSC (51% and 52%) and improved in REGARDS (from 45% to 50%).

Conclusions

Compared with the 2018 cholesterol guideline, the new model improves identification of individuals at very high risk of recurrent ASCVD, supporting more personalized treatment decisions.

title: Trends in Care and Outcomes Among Emergency Department Patients With Chest Pain Without Myocardial Infarction.
authorString: Chou SC, Wharam JF, Hsia RY.
abstractText:
Study objective

To characterize trends in hospitalization, downstream care, and outcomes among emergency department (ED) patients with chest pain without acute myocardial infarction (AMI) diagnosis.

Methods

We analyzed claims data from a large national commercial insurer (2007-2021) and identified ED visits with a principal diagnosis of chest pain. We excluded visits with secondary diagnoses of AMI or other significant cardiopulmonary conditions and those preceded by cardiac testing, coronary procedures, AMI admissions, or chest pain ED visits within 6 months. Usage outcomes included index hospitalization (principal), 7-day cardiac testing, and 30-day coronary revascularization. The principal clinical outcome was 180-day postindex AMI hospitalization. Adjusted annual rates were estimated using generalized estimating equations, and trends were assessed using inverse-variance-weighted linear regression.

Results

We included 773,250 index chest pain ED visits (mean age 54.2 years; 54.3% women). Adjusted hospitalization rates declined from 42.7% to 18.6%, and 7-day noninvasive testing decreased from 26.7% to 9.1%. Revascularization within 30 days declined from 5.8% to 3.6%. Overall, 180-day postindex AMI hospitalization showed no significant temporal trend, ranging from 0.8% to 1.2%. However, a modest increasing trend was observed among patients aged 70 years and older.

Conclusion

Among ED patients with chest pain without AMI diagnosis, hospitalization, cardiac testing, and revascularization declined substantially from 2007 to 2021. Overall, downstream AMI hospitalization remained stable, although those in older adults experienced modest rises. Although efforts continue to identify additional low-risk patients for safe discharge, future research should quantify the potential benefits of hospitalization and cardiac testing, particularly for older adults and high-risk patients.

title: Acute Myocardial Injury in Patients Presenting With Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding: Prevalence, Predictors, Troponin Dynamics, and In-Hospital Outcomes.
authorString: Abbas N, Shahid FN, Amjad R, Amjad MW, Arooj SS, Sehrish S, Bashir A, Yusuf M, Shafiq A, Mahmood S.
abstractText:
Background

Upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB) may cause anemia, hypovolemia, and hemodynamic compromise, potentially contributing to myocardial injury during the acute illness. Troponin elevation in this setting requires careful interpretation because an isolated measurement cannot reliably distinguish acute injury from elevation without qualifying change or establish myocardial infarction. The frequency, temporal evolution, and clinical significance of acute myocardial injury in patients with UGIB remain incompletely characterized. This prospective multicenter study evaluated its prevalence, associated admission factors, serial troponin dynamics, and relationship with in-hospital outcomes, including subsequent mortality among patients surviving the first 24 hours.

Methods

This prospective multicenter observational cohort study enrolled 1,000 adults at tertiary care hospitals in Punjab, Pakistan, between January 2025 and August 2026. Cardiac troponin I measurements were scheduled at presentation, 3-6 hours, and 20-24 hours. Acute injury required a concentration above the applicable 99th-percentile reference limit and a serial maximum-minimum range of ≥10 ng/L and ≥20% of the earliest observed concentration, using at least two measurements spanning ≥3 hours. Prevalence was estimated with Wilson confidence intervals (CIs). Multivariable logistic regression examined admission factors associated with injury. A 24-hour landmark analysis evaluated subsequent mortality among patients alive and still hospitalized with classifiable injury status.

Results

Injury status was classifiable in 960 patients; 104 had acute injury, giving a prevalence of 10.8% (95% CI: 9.0-13.0%). A further 131 patients (13.6% of classifiable assessments) had troponin elevation without qualifying change, while 40 assessments were indeterminate. Older age (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) per decade: 1.40; 95% CI: 1.21-1.63), coronary artery disease (aOR: 1.82; 95% CI: 1.06-3.10), and lower hemoglobin (aOR per 1 g/dL decrease: 1.27; 95% CI: 1.06-1.51) were associated with acute injury. Fourteen acute-injury cases (13.5%) first met the classification criterion at the late measurement. Among 810 landmark patients with known outcomes, 34 died. Subsequent mortality was 15.2% with acute injury versus 2.8% without acute injury (aOR: 3.47; 95% CI: 1.58-7.62; p=0.002). An adverse differential assignment of unresolved mortality outcomes attenuated this association (aOR: 1.86; 95% CI: 0.94-3.69).

Conclusions

Acute myocardial injury affected approximately one in 10 classifiable patients with UGIB and was associated with older age, coronary artery disease, lower hemoglobin, and higher subsequent in-hospital mortality. Serial measurements distinguished acute changes from elevation without qualifying change. The mortality association requires cautious interpretation because of limited events, residual confounding, and incomplete follow-up.

title: Posterior Circulation Stroke From Paradoxical Embolism in a Patient With Patent Foramen Ovale Dislodged During Masturbation.
authorString: Saleh A, Brown A, Larkins MC, Tensmeyer M, Merkle F.
abstractText: Diagnosis of stroke in young and otherwise healthy individuals is rare, but early detection and treatment are crucial to patient outcomes. There may be unusual factors that lead to a presentation of stroke as seen in this case.

title: Late-Stage Concentration of Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome Burden in US Adults: Disability-Adjusted Life Years Across AHA Stages, 2005 to 2023
authorString: Wang X, Qiao Y, Sun H, Wang Y, Zhou H, Zhang T.
abstractText:
Background:

Cardiovascular prevention is increasingly prioritised using burden estimates, yet disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) reward late-stage treatment by construction. Whether that bias is large for cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome, and where the population is accumulating relative to where the burden sits, is unknown.

Methods:

We pooled nine National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey cycles (2005-2023) and assigned CKM stages 0-4 from measured blood pressure, adiposity, glycaemia, lipids, kidney function, urine albumin, self-reported cardiovascular disease, and 10-year PREVENT risk. Years lived with disability used GBD disability weights. Years of life lost combined national death counts, stage-specific mortality from linked mortality files (1999-2018), and period life tables. A second aim attributed burden to smoking and physical inactivity, two exposures outside the CKM definition.

Results:

In 2021-2023, 13.8% of adults were stage 0, 21.3% stage 1, 49.1% stage 2, 6.5% stage 3, and 9.3% stage 4. CKM accounted for 20.0 million DALYs annually (7,881 age-standardised per 100,000), of which 4.1 million were YLD and 15.9 million attributable YLL. Stages 3-4, 15.8% of adults, generated 76% of attributable YLL; stage 4 alone generated 65% of YLD and 49% of attributable YLL. Adjusted mortality rose from stage 2 (hazard ratio 1.39) through stage 4 (3.22), while stage 1 did not differ from stage 0 (0.99; 95% CI, 0.78-1.25). Between 2006 and 2016, stage 0 prevalence fell 2.3% per year and stage 1 rose 3.1% per year. Smoking and physical inactivity accounted for 30.5% of burden (95% CI, 25.7-35.1).

Conclusions:

CKM burden is concentrated in stages 3-4, where excess mortality begins, while the population has been shifting into stage 1, where mortality is normal. DALY-based prioritisation will therefore systematically underfund the stage in which the next generation of patients is being created.

title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Added to Statin Therapy and Cardiovascular Outcomes in ASCVD A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study
authorString: Tah S, Cheshire M.
abstractText:
Objective:

To evaluate whether GLP-1 RA use added to statins is associated with lower all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction (MI), and ischemic stroke versus statin monotherapy in ASCVD patients with body mass index (BMI) 30 kg/m2. Approach and Results:Using the TriNetX Research Network (108 U.S. healthcare organizations), we identified ASCVD patients with BMI 30 kg/m2 on statins initiating a GLP-1 RA (n=166,278) versus statin-only controls (n=920,176). Propensity score matching on 34 covariates yielded 119,911 matched pairs followed 3 years. Prespecified analyses included a BMI 35 subgroup (62,385 pairs), four washout sensitivity analyses (30-120 days), and a familial hypercholesterolemia exclusion analysis (161,312 matched pairs). Results. GLP-1 RA use was associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality (4.0% vs. 7.5%; HR 0.479; 95% CI: 0.463-0.496; p<0.001), MI (HR 0.762; 95% CI: 0.737-0.788; p<0.001), and ischemic stroke (HR 0.671; 95% CI: 0.588-0.766; p<0.001). Benefits were consistent across the BMI 35 subgroup and all washout analyses. GLP-1 RA users were more likely to achieve LDL <55 mg/dL by risk analysis (17.1% vs. 15.3%; RR 1.118; p<0.001); the Kaplan-Meier analysis was non-significant (HR 1.007; p=0.538). Mortality benefit was preserved in the FH exclusion analysis.

Conclusion:

ASCVD patients with obesity on statins, GLP-1 RA use was associated with substantially lower mortality, MI, and stroke, suggesting GLP-1 RAs may serve as cardioprotective adjuncts to statin therapy in this population.

title: Short physical performance battery and dementia in adults aged 60 years and older.
authorString: Liang Z, Wang W, Huang L, Chen H.
abstractText:
Background

The Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) is a simple and objective tool for assessing physical performance in older people. Although SPPB scores have been linked to all-cause mortality, their longitudinal association with incident dementia remains unclear.

Methods

We used data from the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA), including 4927 adults aged ≥ 60 without dementia in 2012/2013. Baseline SPPB scores were categorized as high (10-12), moderate (7-9), low (4-6), and very low (0-3). Cox proportional hazards models estimated the association between different levels of physical performance and dementia risk, adjusting for demographic, health behaviors, and health status.

Results

Over a median 8.7-year follow-up, 252 (5.1%) participants developed dementia. Compared with high physical performance, low (HR = 1.71, 95% CI: 1.11-2.62) and very low (HR = 2.45, 95% CI: 1.54-3.89) physical performance were significantly associated with higher dementia risk. Associations remained significant in women and adults aged < 80, although among men and adults aged ≥ 80, only very low SPPB showed significance. Sensitivity analysis showed robust results after excluding cases of dementia diagnosed within two years, reducing the likelihood of reverse causality.

Conclusions

Physical performance assessed by the SPPB was significantly associated with dementia risk. These findings support the potential value of the SPPB in identifying older adults at higher risk of dementia. Future intervention studies are needed to determine whether improving physical performance can reduce dementia risk.

title: The incidence of postoperative hypotension among non-cardiac surgical specialties: A single-centre retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Li JT, Selman CJ, Douglas N.
abstractText: Postoperative hypotension is associated with increased risk of postoperative complications and mortality. There are limited studies quantifying the incidence of this potentially life-threatening condition among different surgical cohorts. We aimed to describe and compare the incidence of postoperative hypotension in the first 48 h after leaving the post-anaesthesia care unit (PACU) across different surgical specialties after non-cardiac surgery. We conducted a single-centre retrospective study at the Royal Melbourne Hospital. The primary outcome was postoperative hypotension (systolic blood pressure (SBP) <90 mmHg) within 48 h after surgery and discharge from PACU, noted on routine blood pressure monitoring or a requirement for postoperative vasopressor or inotropic support. We estimated odds ratios (OR) using mixed-effects logistic regression models to account for multiple surgical procedures within the same patient. We identified 11,634 surgeries from 17 specialties, of which 47.3% were emergency operations. The median age was 53 years (interquartile range 35-68), with 42.2% being female and 42.5% of patients on regular antihypertensive medication. The overall incidence of ward hypotension was 4.4%. Trauma had the highest rate of postoperative hypotension (27.3%), followed by thoracic surgery (11.6%). Surgical specialties that had a higher risk of hypotension included trauma surgery (OR 13.0, 95% confidence interval (CI) 3.7-46.0) and thoracic surgery (OR 3.6, 95% CI 2.3-5.5). Specialties with a lower risk of hypotension included breast and endocrine surgery (OR 0.4, 95% CI 0.2-0.7) and plastic surgery (OR 0.4, 95% CI 0.3-0.6). Postoperative hypotension is relatively common with substantial variation in incidence between surgical specialties. These findings highlight the need for heightened vigilance for hypotension in certain patients.

title: EXPRESS: Air pollution increases cardiometabolic diseases in China: A nationwide longitudinal cohort study.
authorString: Xu M, Han Y, Zhao H, Han W, He M, Fan Y, Liu S.

journal.title: Journal of investigative medicine : the official publication of the American Federation for Clinical Research

abstractText:
Objective

To investigate the associations between long-term exposure to multiple ambient air pollutants (PM1, PM2.5, PM10, O3 and NO2) and the incidence of cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) in middle-aged and older Chinese adults, and to identify potential effect modifiers.

Design

Nationwide longitudinal cohort study.

Setting

The China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), covering 28 provinces in China.

Participants

A total of 8,725 participants aged 45 years and older from the CHARLS 2011 baseline, free of pre-existing CMM, defined as having two or more of the following four conditions: hypertension, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and stroke, with complete follow-up data through 2020.
