Participants with only one of these conditions at baseline were retained.

Primary and secondary outcome measures

The primary outcome was incident CMM. Secondary outcomes included pollutant-specific hazard ratios and effect modification by education level and sleep duration. Sensitivity analyses using multiple imputation were performed to assess the robustness of the associations for all five pollutants.

Results

Long-term exposure to PM1, PM2.5, PM10, O3 and NO2 was significantly associated with an increased risk of incident CMM. Stronger associations were observed among participants with lower educational attainment and shorter sleep duration.

Conclusions

Long-term exposure to ambient air pollutants is associated with a higher risk of CMM in the Chinese middle-aged and older population. These findings highlight the importance of air quality improvement and targeted public health strategies for socioeconomically disadvantaged and sleep-deprived subgroups.

title: [Hypercholesterolemia and lipid profile alterations in Moroccan patients with myocardial infarction: A case-control study].
authorString: Mohammadi K, Jramy C, Adadi W, Mohammadi H, Safi A.
abstractText:
Background

Hypercholesterolemia, particularly elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), is a major risk factor for cardiovascular diseases, including myocardial infarction.

Aims

This study aimed to investigate lipid profile alterations in Moroccan patients with myocardial infarction.

Methods

This case-control study included 104 patients hospitalized for myocardial infarction at the Ibn Rochd University Hospital Center (mean age: 59±11 years; range: 30-82 years) and 79 apparently healthy controls recruited at the Pasteur Institute of Casablanca (mean age: 48±8 years; range: 23-57 years). Serum total cholesterol (TC), triglycerides (TG), LDL-C, and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) were measured using standardized enzymatic methods.

Results

Patients with myocardial infarction exhibited significantly higher levels of TC, TG, and LDL-C compared with controls, with increases of 17.5% (P<0.001), 78.2% (P<0.001), and 27.7% (P<0.001), respectively. In contrast, HDL-C levels were significantly reduced by 22.2% in patients with myocardial infarction (P<0.001).

Conclusion

These findings highlight a strong association between dyslipidemia and myocardial infarction in the Moroccan population, emphasizing the importance of lipid profile monitoring for cardiovascular risk prevention.

title: [Right aortic arch with a true bicarotid trunk and aberrant left subclavian artery in an adult: Value of CT angiography].
authorString: Bouzid I, Touil N, Sakhy Y, Hmada S, Tabakh H, Siwane A, Kacimi O.
abstractText: We report a rare right aortic arch variant detected during neurovascular assessment in a 48-year-old woman. Arch-to-vertex computed tomography angiography showed three consecutive branches: a true bicarotid trunk dividing into both common carotid arteries, a separate right subclavian artery, and an aberrant left subclavian artery with a retroesophageal course. Neither a Kommerell diverticulum nor aortic dissection was identified. Focused questioning disclosed chronic dysphagia, without definitive evidence of vascular esophageal compression. No causal relationship with the presenting stroke could be established. This case underscores the value of multiplanar and three-dimensional imaging in distinguishing a true bicarotid trunk from a common brachiocephalic-carotid origin, identifying aberrant subclavian anatomy, and informing cardiovascular and neuroendovascular procedural planning.

title: Interaction between unhealthy sleep pattern and obesity on cardiometabolic multimorbidity.
authorString: Huang W, Chen B, Chen Y, Lin X, Zhang K, Qiu W, Du S, Ye W.
abstractText:
Objectives

Obesity and unhealthy sleep are established risk factors for cardiometabolic multimorbidity, but their joint effect remains unclear. This study aims to investigate their joint effect on cardiometabolic multimorbidity risk by analyzing data from 2 independent cohorts.

Methods

We analyzed cross-sectional (Fuqing Cohort, N = 34,703) and prospective data (UK Biobank, N = 362,474; 12.3-year median follow-up, 3980 incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity cases). We defined unhealthy sleep (≥3 of 5 traits: late chronotype, sleep <7 or >8 h/day, frequent insomnia symptoms, self-reported snoring, frequent daytime sleepiness), cardiometabolic multimorbidity (≥2 of type 2 diabetes, coronary heart disease, stroke), and obesity (general: BMI ≥25 kg/m²; central: waist circumference ≥80 cm in women, ≥94/90 cm in European/Asian men). The reference group had a sleep score <3 and no corresponding obesity. Logistic and Cox regressions evaluated associations and additive interaction was assessed.

Results

Unhealthy sleep and both obesity types independently increased cardiometabolic multimorbidity risk in both populations. The joint effect was stronger for unhealthy sleep combined with central obesity (FQC adjusted OR = 3.46; UKB adjusted HR = 2.55) than general overweight/obesity (FQC adjusted OR = 2.61; UKB adjusted HR = 2.46). Additive interaction showed stronger effect for unhealthy sleep with central versus general overweight/obesity in Europeans (adjusted RERI: 0.61 vs. 0.32). A similar additive interaction in Asians turned non-significant after covariate adjustment. Insomnia and central obesity showed a significant additive interaction in both cohorts.

Conclusions

Unhealthy sleep and obesity jointly increase cardiometabolic multimorbidity risk, with central obesity having a stronger additive interaction than general overweight/obesity. Integrated public health strategies targeting sleep and weight are warranted.

title: Extrarenal Papillary Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Unique Case With Bilateral Involvement of the Adrenal Glands.
authorString: André M, Cismasiu B, Moreira L, Vasconcelos M, Santos MI, Rodrigues-Alves J, Fernandes E, Rosa JP, Carvalho M, Mansinho H, Luz-Correia C.
abstractText: Primary extrarenal renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is an exceptionally rare malignancy. We report a unique case of bilateral adrenal papillary extrarenal RCC in a 62-year-old man, managed through sequential surgical interventions over a prolonged follow-up. Initial right adrenalectomy revealed a papillary RCC with high-grade oncocytic features; immunohistochemical analysis confirmed PAX8 positivity, supporting a renal-type origin in the absence of a renal primary. Subsequent contralateral adrenal involvement and local recurrence required laparoscopic adrenalectomy and multiorgan resection. Despite complete macroscopic resections, the disease progressed to hepatic, pulmonary, peritoneal, and cerebral metastases, resulting in the patient's death due to postoperative intracranial hemorrhage. No renal involvement was identified throughout the disease course. This case highlights the aggressive behavior of extrarenal RCC and underscores the importance of comprehensive immunohistochemical workup, prolonged surveillance, and multidisciplinary management in the absence of standardized guidelines.

title: Clinical Spectrum of Young-onset Hypertension: Diverse Etiologies, Target-organ Damage, and Diagnostic Challenges - A Seven-case Series.
authorString: Ravichandran AS, Ravichandran PY, Narayanan AR.
abstractText:
Abstract

Young-onset hypertension - defined as sustained blood pressure elevation presenting before the age of 40 years - is increasingly encountered in tertiary care settings in India. Unlike hypertension in older adults, it frequently harbors secondary etiologies, presents with severe target-organ damage, and poses considerable diagnostic challenges. This case series illustrates the clinical heterogeneity of the condition and highlights the importance of systematic evaluation in this population. We report seven cases (age range 19-38 years; six males, one female) presenting to a tertiary care teaching hospital. Secondary etiologies included biopsy-proven focal segmental glomerulosclerosis with nephrotic-range proteinuria (Case 1), bilateral ostial renal artery stenosis complicated by heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (Case 2), and hypertension associated with erythrocytosis under evaluation (Case 6). Hypertensive emergency with acute ischemic stroke and hemorrhagic transformation, complicated by hypertensive dilated cardiomyopathy, occurred in Case 7. Essential hypertension was established in Cases 3-5, with end-organ manifestations including hypomagnesemia-induced ventricular premature complexes (Case 4) and hypertensive retinopathy (Case 5). Diagnostic investigations included renal biopsy, renal Doppler ultrasonography, renal angiography, 24-h Holter monitoring, serum erythropoietin assay, and brain magnetic resonance imaging. Individualized antihypertensive regimens were supplemented by disease-specific interventions. Outcomes ranged from clinical stabilization to partial neurological recovery, reflecting the variable prognosis associated with delayed diagnosis and inadequate treatment. Young-onset hypertension is not a uniformly benign or essential condition. Systematic evaluation for secondary causes and comprehensive assessment of target-organ damage are critical, particularly in resource-limited settings where these steps are frequently deferred.

title: Association of pre-stroke blood pressure with functional outcome after stroke. The PRESS study.
authorString: García-Sánchez SM, Gómez-Choco M, Armario P, Mengual JJ, Avellaneda-Gómez C, Boned S, Montalvo C, de Dios S, Anguita A, Pacheu A, de la Sierra A.
abstractText: The aim of this study was to analyze the association between the mean of available outpatient blood pressure (BP) measurements recorded during the 12 months preceding stroke and functional outcome at 90 days in patients with stroke, adjusting for other established prognostic factors. This was a prospective, observational study including consecutive adult patients admitted with acute stroke between October 2022 and October 2023. Pre-stroke outpatient BP data were obtained from the shared electronic medical record system of Catalonia. All available outpatient systolic blood pressure (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) measurements recorded during the 12 months preceding stroke onset were collected. A total of 187 patients were included. Sixty patients (32.1%) had a poor functional outcome at 90 days, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) ≥ 3 (>3 in those with a previous mRS = 3). In unadjusted models, mean pre-stroke outpatient SBP and DBP and the outpatient SBP measurement closest to stroke were associated with poor functional outcome at 90 days. In the multivariate analyses adjusted for age, baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, pre-stroke mRS, mean in-hospital SBP or DBP, type of stroke and history of atrial fibrillation, pre-stroke SBP (OR 2.52, 95% CI 1.59-4.01, per 1 SD increase, p < 0.001), and pre-stroke DBP (OR 2.78, 95% CI 1.60-4.84, p < 0.001) were associated with a poor outcome. In conclusion, higher mean outpatient BP levels during the year preceding stroke were independently associated with poor functional outcome at 90 days.

title: Volume status of patients with hyponatremia across the age span - results from a large prospective international study.
authorString: Varaldo E, Potasso L, Hoorn EJ, Refardt J, Christ-Crain M, HIT Study Group.
abstractText:
Background and hypothesis

Hypotonic hyponatremia is the most common electrolyte disorder in hospitalized adults and becomes increasingly prevalent with age. However, age-related differences in volume status and underlying etiologies remain poorly characterized. We aimed to assess the distribution of volume status and etiologies of hypotonic hyponatremia across the adult age span.

Methods

This was a secondary analysis of the prospective Hyponatremia Intervention Trial (NCT03557957), including hospitalized adults with chronic moderate-to-severe hypotonic hyponatremia. Patients were stratified into three age groups (<65, 65-79, ≥80 years). Final volume status (hypovolemic, euvolemic, or hypervolemic) was determined at the end of hospitalization based on the complete in-hospital clinical course.

Results

Overall, 1992 patients (F/M 1050/942; median age 73 [63-81] years) were analyzed. Euvolemic hyponatremia (n = 1073) predominated across all age groups and sexes, mainly due to syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis (SIAD; n = 853). In adjusted analyses, patients aged 65-79 years (OR 1.49, 95% CI 1.19-1.88) and ≥80 years (OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.14-1.91) had higher odds of SIAD than patients aged <65 years. Volume status distribution differed across age groups (p = 0.007), driven by a higher prevalence of hypervolemic forms in patients aged ≥80 years; however, the association between age category and volume-status phenotype was attenuated and no longer statistically significant after multivariable adjustment. Hypovolemic hyponatremia (n = 613) was most commonly due to gastrointestinal sodium losses in younger patients, whereas diuretics accounted for nearly 50% of cases in those aged ≥80 years. Among patients with hypervolemic hyponatremia (n = 306), heart failure and liver insufficiency were the leading causes, with heart failure increasing and liver insufficiency decreasing across age groups.

Conclusion

Euvolemic hyponatremia was the predominant form across all age groups and was mainly due to SIAD, with both older age groups showing higher adjusted odds of SIAD compared with patients aged <65 years. Age-related differences were observed in the distribution of etiologies within hypovolemic and hypervolemic hyponatremia.

title: Prevalence, clinical implications and prognostic impact of frailty and other geriatric conditions in patients with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Antúnez-Ballesteros M, Rosende-Celeiro I, Crespo-Leiro MG, Barge-Caballero G, Enríquez-Vázquez D, Couto-Mallón D, Paniagua-Martín MJ, Padilla-Bautista M, Grille-Cancela Z, Riveiro-Rodríguez C, Blanco-Canosa P, Bouzas-Mosquera A, Muñiz J, Manuel García-Pinilla J, Manuel Vázquez-Rodríguez J, Barge-Caballero E.
abstractText:
Introduction and objectives

Frailty in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) remains poorly characterized. The aim of this study was to analyze the prevalence and prognostic influence of frailty and other geriatric conditions such as nutritional risk, cognitive status, depression, and dependence in patients with ATTR-CM.

Methods

We performed an observational, prospective, single-center study of 110 ATTR-CM patients who underwent comprehensive geriatric assessment from October 2024 to April 2025 and were followed up to September 2026. Study endpoints were all-cause death and the combined event of all-cause death or worsening heart failure. Outcomes were assessed by the Kaplan-Meier method and multivariable Cox regression.

Results

The prevalence of frailty, based on 4 different criteria, varied from 32.7% to 62.7%. Dependence, depression, nutritional risk, and cognitive impairment were detected in up to 70.9%, 29.1%, 27.3%, and 15.5% of patients, respectively. Frailty, defined as a Clinical Frailty Scale > 4, a Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe-Frailty Instrument > 2, or a Short Physical Performance Battery < 10, was independently associated with an increased risk of both study outcomes. Dependence (Katz index < 6) and cognitive impairment (Mini Examen Cognitivo score < 23) were also independent predictors of both outcomes. Frailty diagnosis showed incremental prognostic value when added to United Kingdom National Amyloidosis Centre stages.

Conclusions

Frailty is frequent in patients with ATTR-CM and is associated with impaired clinical outcomes.

title: VOLUME ADJUSTED CALCIUM ANALYSIS OF AORTOILIAC ATHEROSCLEROSIS AS A PREDICTOR OF AMPUTATION FREE SURVIVAL.
authorString: Kumar R, Matabele M, Grayzel C, Litvak A, Röder F, Kruger J, Mix D, Doyle A, Stoner M, Newhall K.
abstractText:
Introduction/objectives

Pre-operative cross-sectional imaging guides surgical planning in vascular surgery. Despite the relationship between atherosclerotic burden and surgical success, no studies have adjusted atherosclerotic burden according to lumen volume. Given variability in vessel diameter and significance of aortoiliac disease, we developed a volume-adjusted calcium score (VACS) and evaluated its association with patient outcomes.

Methods

This single-institution retrospective study included 187 patients over nine years who underwent peripheral vascular intervention. Using TeraRecon, calcium and patent lumen volumes were quantified along a contiguous aorto-iliac segment totaling 10 cm generating a VACS. An intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) assessed inter-rater reliability. Patients were stratified into two groups. Primary outcomes were death at one year and amputation-free survival. Secondary outcomes were re-interventions and number of arteries treated.

Results

Intervention type did not differ between the two groups. Patients with higher VACS were more likely older, have CHF, COPD, or hypertension. Patient in the higher VACS group had greater number of arteries treated, subsequent vascular interventions, and one-year all-cause mortality. A Cox-regression model demonstrated a VACSgreater than 0.33 was independently associated with decreased amputation-free survival at one year (HR 2.24, p=0.019).

Conclusion

In patients undergoing intervention for aortoiliac occlusive disease, higher VACS was independently associated with worse one-year amputation free survival. Incorporating patent lumen volume into VACS appears to capture a systemic atherosclerotic burden not fully reflected by traditional lesion-specific assessments.

title: Prognostic Value of Late Gadolinium Enhancement in Non-Ischemic Dilated Cardiomyopathy: A Prospective Observational Study from India.
authorString: Meena AK, Ojha V, Malhi AS, Jagia P, Kumar S, Naik N, Roy A, Gupta AK.
abstractText:
Background

Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (NIDCM) represents a significant cause of heart failure and sudden cardiac death (SCD). Current risk stratification relies heavily on left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), which has limitations in predicting adverse outcomes. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) on cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging may provide additional prognostic information.

Methods

This prospective observational study enrolled 88 consecutive NIDCM patients who underwent CMR imaging at our institution. Patients were followed for a minimum of 6 months and thereafter until a common study closure date, giving a mean follow-up of 337±173 days. The primary endpoint was a composite of major adverse cardiac events (MACE), defined as sudden cardiac death, heart failure death, aborted sudden cardiac death, sustained ventricular tachycardia, and heart failure hospitalization.

Results

LGE was present in 44 patients (50%). The most common pattern was mid-myocardial enhancement (40.9%), followed by a combination of patterns (25.0%) and transmural enhancement (22.7%); the interventricular septum was the most frequently involved segment (81.8%). MACE occurred in 22.7% of LGE-positive patients versus 13.6% of LGE-negative patients. ROC curve analysis identified LGE extent >26% of LV volume as the optimal threshold for predicting MACE (sensitivity 70%, specificity 73.5%, AUC 0.75). Patients with LGE >26% had significantly higher event rates (43.7% vs 10.7%; unadjusted OR 6.48, 95% CI 1.45-28.9; p=0.02).

Conclusions

Greater LGE extent was associated with adverse cardiac events in NIDCM patients. CMR-based risk stratification may help identify high-risk patients who could benefit from ICD, but external validation in larger cohorts is required before using this threshold clinically.

title: Aortic Root Abscess in Infective Endocarditis: Prognostic Impact and Outcomes of Patch Repair.
authorString: Watkins A, Kang N, Dean M, Auclair F, Boodhwani M, Lau L, Messika-Zeitoun D, Toeg H, Voisine P, Rubens F.

journal.title: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery

abstractText:
Objective

Due to discrepancies between guidelines and expert consensus, we examined the perioperative and mid-term outcomes of aortic root abscesses to determine their prognostic significance and optimal surgical management.

Methods

We completed a single-center retrospective study of patients surgically treated for aortic valve infective endocarditis (AV IE) from 2019 to 2024. We compared outcomes in patients with and without root abscess, and among abscess cases, between patch repair and extended surgery (root reconstruction or replacement). The primary outcome was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE, composite of all-cause death, heart failure (HF) readmission, and stroke). Outcomes were analyzed using Kaplan Meier estimators and Cox proportional hazards.

Results

Among 158 patients (57% with abscess) with a median follow-up of 1.22 years (IQR 0.13-2.53), root abscesses were associated with increased MACCE (adjusted HR 3.15 (1.51-6.59), p=0.002) and HF readmission (SHR 4.54 (1.55-13.30), p=0.006). In patients with aortic root abscess, 62 underwent patch repair and 21 underwent extended surgery. Patch repair was associated with decreased MACCE (adjusted HR 0.34 (0.15-0.74), p=0.006), all-cause mortality (p=0.002), and death at 30 days (13% vs 33%, p=0.035) compared to extended surgery.

Conclusions

Aortic root abscess was associated with increased MACCE and HF readmissions compared to AV IE without abscess, identifying root abscess as a marker of adverse prognosis and supporting prompt recognition and referral in aortic valve endocarditis. Patch repair for aortic root abscesses is a safe and reasonable approach in patients with suitable anatomy compared to more extensive surgery.

title: Acute Right Heart Failure Following Left Coronary Myocardial Infarction in Left Ventricular Assist Device-Supported Patients: A Case Series and Mechanistic Insight.
authorString: Fakhreddine O, Liu J, Civitello A, Diakos N.

journal.title: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)

abstractText: Right heart failure (RHF) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in patients supported with durable left ventricular assist devices (LVADs). While right coronary artery infarction is a recognized cause of acute RHF, the ventricular consequences of left coronary system infarction in LVAD-supported patients are not well characterized. We describe two patients supported with HeartMate III LVADs who developed acute RHF within 24-48 hours after successful revascularization of acute left coronary system occlusions (mid-left anterior descending artery and left main coronary artery). Both had previously stable LVAD function and no evidence of advanced RHF. After revascularization, each developed hypotension, rising central venous pressure, reduced LVAD flows, and echocardiographic evidence of severe right ventricular (RV) dilation and dysfunction with septal shift toward the left ventricle. Hemodynamic deterioration reversed with inotropic support, diuresis, and LVAD speed adjustment, without mechanical RV support. These cases suggest left coronary acute myocardial infarction (AMI) may precipitate acute RHF in LVAD-supported patients through septal ischemia with impaired ventricular interdependence, acute increases in RV afterload, and relative RV ischemia despite patent right coronary arteries. Heightened surveillance and early echocardiographic assessment after left-sided AMI in LVAD recipients may enable prompt recognition and timely intervention.

title: Barriers and factors associated with patient-centered communication in oncology inpatients: a cross-sectional study.
authorString: Kiliç B, Korkmaz S, Kurt SE, Çinar Fİ.

journal.title: Revista da Escola de Enfermagem da U S P

abstractText:
Objective

This study aimed to evaluate patient-centered communication barriers in oncology patients and the factors influencing these barriers.

Methods

A cross-sectional study was conducted with 336 hospitalized cancer patients (≥18 years) in the Oncology Clinic of a Training and Research Hospital between February 2022 and March 2023. Patients with dementia or intellectual disability were excluded. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews using a Sociodemographic Form and the Patient-Centered Communication Barriers Scale (PCCBS).

Results

The mean age of participants was 57.5 ± 17.3 years; 68.7% were male, and the mean hospitalization period was 13.4 ± 15.9 days. Regression analysis showed significant relationships between patient characteristics and communication barriers. Higher education increased patients' need for attention and information (β = 0.175, p = 0.001, 95% CI [0.039-0.157]) and curiosity (β = 0.130, p = 0.017, 95% CI [0.024-0.242]). Greater symptom burden reduced the need for attention (β = -0.116, p = 0.031, 95% CI [-0.345, -0.016]). Absence of a caregiver was associated with higher fear and anxiety (β = 0.173, p = 0.001, 95% CI [0.180-0.749]). Education and symptom experience explained 4.5% of the variance in need for attention (R2 = 0.045), 1.7% in curiosity and information needs (R2 = 0.017), and 3% in fear and anxiety (R2 = 0.030).

Conclusion

Patients with higher education reported greater information needs, whereas those with heavier symptom burdens were less likely to seek attention. Lack of caregiver support increased fear and anxiety. These results indicate that communication barriers in oncology are influenced by educational background, symptom experience, and caregiving context. Nurses and clinicians should assess these factors systematically and tailor communication strategies to individual needs. Implementing such interventions and screening for barriers can enhance patient-centered oncology care. However, the cross-sectional, single-center design limits causal inference and generalizability.

title: Calibration of a fully closed-loop lumped-parameter cardiovascular model with baroreflex in response to induced central hypovolemia.
authorString: Tlałka K, Saxton H, Halliday I, Xu X, Narracott A, Taylor DJ, Høiseth LØ, Hisdal J, Hose DR, Malawski M.
abstractText: Calibration of cardiovascular models is essential to their clinical utility. We provide a full description of the calibration of a non-linear, dynamic model using global optimisation methods. Specifically, we consider an experimental cohort response in a closed-loop, baro-regulated cardiovascular model, in the setting of induced central hypovolemia.We propose a framework for simplifying calibration of dynamic, regulated models. We perform global sensitivity analysis and orthogonality analysis of a 58-parameter non-linear cardiovascular model including the baroreflex, to select an optimal subset of parameters for model calibration. We fit the model to relative Lower Body Negative Pressure data, using global optimisation (Differential Evolution method), searching a reduced input parameter space. Global sensitivity analysis and orthogonality analysis revealed multiple higher-order interactions within the model, as well as areas of similar influence of input parameters, on the components of the objective function. The model was fitted using only baroreflex parameters. Relative errors in the estimation of heart rate, mean arterial pressure, and stroke volume were reduced from -15.03%, 1.60% and 42.06% before calibration to 0.42%, -1.37% and 0.61% after the fitting, respectively.

title: Development of a village health worker care model to reduce cardiovascular risk in areas of armed conflict: Qualitative results from a participatory planning process in Myanmar.
authorString: Htoo E, Parmar P, Richards A, Russell T, Lee C, Law SSK, Myint SK, Aung ZYP, Traill T.
abstractText: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death in Myanmar, but care models are lacking to deliver evidence-based treatments to reduce CVD risks in areas of armed conflict. Village health workers (VHWs) play a key role in bridging communities and clinics, but their role in CVD prevention and management in conflict-affected settings has not been clearly defined. This study aimed to describe the system for CVD care and to elicit perspectives on how VHWs might contribute to a village-based care model to overcome structural and behavioral barriers to CVD risk factor control in remote rural areas experiencing active armed conflict in Karen State, Myanmar. We conducted 33 semi-structured key informant interviews with patients, VHWs, clinic staff, ethnic health organization leaders, donors, and non-government organization health experts. Content analysis of participant responses suggested many people were unaware of CVD and its risks, and there were persistent gaps in CVD screening, medication adherence, and referral systems. Transportation costs and hazards, medicine shortages, and security risks made it difficult for patients to visit clinics or achieve continuity of care. Respondents believed VHWs could play an important role in improving CVD care by providing health education sessions, screening for high blood pressure and diabetes, delivering medications and supporting adherence, and facilitating referrals. Respondents reported that expanding VHW roles could make CVD care more accessible, particularly where travel to clinics was unsafe or unaffordable. Respondents perceived that VHWs have the potential to address CVD care gaps, and that targeted training and regular supervision of VHWs, coupled with structured systems for referral and follow-up, could enhance continuity of care, adherence to treatment, and community resilience to acute conflict events.

title: Deep learning optimisation for cardiology: Neural Architecture Search-driven arrhythmia classification with electrocardiograms.
authorString: Vanegas Müller E, Joe-Oshodi A, Banerjee A, Villarroel M.
abstractText: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death worldwide. Sudden cardiac death (SCD) accounts for roughly 50% of all cardiac deaths. The electrocardiogram (ECG) is widely used for diagnosing cardiac disease. However, the complexity of interpretation limits the ECG's efficacy. Modern deep learning methods can assist clinicians in diagnosis. We applied Neural Architecture Search (NAS) to identify optimal deep learning architectures for classifying cardiac arrhythmias with ECGs. We applied the Differentiable Architecture Search strategy to an AutoFormer search and trained, validated, and tested the resulting model on the PhysioNet Challenge 2021 (PC21) dataset (n = 88,253 from three continents). We optimised hyperparameters on the NAS output, exploring input patch size, class weighting, and loss function. The PC21 metric and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) are the performance metrics. The NAS converged towards minimal architectural configurations (embedding dimension: 384, depth: 4, self-attention heads: 4, MLP ratio: 1) with a validation and test PC21 metric of 0.66 (PC21 winner: 0.63). The NAS-created network achieved an AUROC of 0.97 and a PC21 metric of 0.72 during testing (PC21 winner: 0.69). We tested the PC21 winner architecture (1D-convolutional neural network with attention mechanism) without the attention mechanism and with the NAS-suggested architecture of 4 self-attention heads (instead of 8). The architecture without the attention mechanism performed similarly to the one with 8 self-attention heads (AUROC: 0.90, PC21 metric: 0.69). The architecture with 4 self-attention heads scored an AUROC of 0.91 and improved the PC21 metric to 0.71. The attention mechanism visualisation for two SCD-related arrhythmias (premature ventricular contractions and prolonged QT-interval) showed more clinically relevant attention for the 4-self-attention-head architectures. We interpret architectural simplicity as driving performance in arrhythmia classification. The self-attention mechanism can autonomously abstract clinical representations, simplifying clinical deployment by eliminating the need for an explicit feature-extraction pipeline.

title: Ethnic disparities in outcomes of coronary artery bypass grafting in Israel.
authorString: Leviner DB, Ronai T, Abraham D, Erez E, Witberg G, Yishai Y, Haddad J, Sharoni E.
abstractText:
Objective

Ethnic disparities after cardiac surgery are well reported. Israeli Arabs have lower life expectancy and greater frequency of cardiovascular risk factors. We sought to compare long-term outcomes following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) between Arab and Jewish patients in Israel.

Methods

Retrospective study of adult patients with multivessel disease undergoing isolated CABG in three centers between January 1st, 2009, and December 31st, 2023. The primary outcome was a composite of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE). The cumulative incidence of MACCE was plotted using KM curves. The hazard ratio (HR) for Arabs vs. Jewish were calculated using multivariate Cox models.

Results

Our cohort included 6,330 patients, 1,819 (28.74%) and 4,511 (71.26%) patients were Arabs and Jewish, respectively. Median follow-up time was 78.32 months. Arab patients had higher rate of the primary outcome at median follow-up (46.26% vs 40.90%, HR 1.184, 95%CI: 1.09-1.286, P < 0.001) and there was no difference in mortality between the two groups (26.44% vs 26.45%, HR 1.004, 95%CI: 0.901-1.118, P = 0.82). After multivariable adjustment, the risk of MACCE was similar between the groups (adjusted HR 1.073, 95%CI: 0.965-1.193, P = 0.19).

Conclusions

After multivariable adjustment for baseline and socioeconomic factors, ethnicity was not independently associated with worse long-term clinical outcomes in patients undergoing CABG in Israel, while unadjusted disparities remained evident.

title: Exploratory cluster analysis of noninvasive vascular measures reveals heterogeneous vascular profiles after stroke.
authorString: Bartsch BL, Engler AN, Billinger SA.
abstractText: Vascular dysfunction is prevalent after stroke and contributes to elevated cardiovascular risk; however, the extent to which vascular heterogeneity exists in this population remains unclear. This study examined whether distinct multi-domain cluster-derived vascular profiles are present in individuals with chronic stroke and whether these profiles are associated with functional performance. Vascular structure and function were assessed using flow-mediated dilation, carotid intima-media thickness, pulse wave velocity, and augmentation index, with age included in vascular clustering to account for vascular aging. Unsupervised k-means clustering was applied to identify vascular profiles. Functional performance was assessed using gait speed and predicted peak oxygen consumption (VO2peak) derived from a submaximal exercise test. Between-cluster differences were characterized using analysis of variance. Forty-five individuals with chronic stroke (62 ± 12 years; 29 ± 30 months post-stroke) were included. Three vascular profiles were identified (cluster 1: n = 13; cluster 2: n = 11; cluster 3: n = 21), with significant differences across clusters for all vascular measures (p < 0.01). Although age increased across clusters, vascular structure and function did not change uniformly. One profile exhibited elevated arterial wave reflection despite relatively preserved endothelial function and arterial structure, whereas another demonstrated impairment in all vascular variables. Vascular profile was not associated with predicted VO2peak (p = 0.31) or gait speed (p = 0.65). Three exploratory cluster-derived vascular profiles emerged among participants with chronic stroke, and age did not fully account for the observed vascular heterogeneity. Multi-domain cluster-derived vascular profiling revealed heterogeneous vascular profiles in individuals with chronic stroke, providing a basis for future studies to evaluate their relevance to cardiovascular risk stratification and long-term health management. NCT05936008: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05936008.

title: Male breast cancer in Northern Tanzania: Clinicopathology and predictors of two-year survival (2016-2022).
authorString: Emaely TS, Mremi A, Msoka EF, Mutashobya R, Mmbaga BT, Chilonga K.
abstractText:
Background

Male breast cancer (BC) is rare, accounting to approximately 1% of all breast cancers worldwide. Patients often present with advanced disease, contributing to poor outcomes. This study aimed to estimate two-year overall survival (OS) and identify clinicopathological and health-system-related predictors of survival among men with breast cancer treated at Kilimanjaro Christian Medical Centre (KCMC).

Methods

A retrospective cohort study was conducted among 55 histologically confirmed male BC patients managed at KCMC between 2016 and 2022. The primary outcome was two-year overall survival, defined as time from histological diagnosis to death from any cause or censoring at two years. The dependent variables were clinical and pathological factors and the key independent variable was overall survival (OS). Descriptive statistics summarized participants characteristics. Kaplan-Meier curves, log-rank and Cox proportional hazards regression were used to estimate the OS and the factors associated. A p-value <0.05 was considered statistically significant.

Results

The mean age at diagnosis was 62.2 ± 14.3 years, with most patients (54.6%) aged between 50-70 years. Over half (52.7%) presented with stage III or IV disease, and 21.8% had distant metastasis. Invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) was the predominant histological subtype (85.5%), and luminal B was the most common molecular profile (23.6%). Surgery was performed in 60% of patients, chemotherapy in 47.3%, hormonal therapy in 30.9%, and radiotherapy in only 9.1%. The overall two-year survival rate was 67.3%. Independent predictors of poor survival included age > 70 years (p = 0.009), stage IV disease (p = 0.005), delayed receipt of histopathological results (> 2 weeks), delayed surgery (>6 weeks), and non-receipt of hormonal therapy or radiotherapy.

Conclusion

Male BC in Northern Tanzania remains a disease for older who frequently present with advanced-stages. Two-year overall survival remains suboptimal and is strongly influenced by advanced disease stage, older age, diagnostic and treatment delays, and limited access to adjuvant therapies. Strengthening early diagnosis, timely pathology reporting, and access to radiotherapy and hormonal therapy may substantially improve outcomes.

title: Protocol for investigating the association between Helicobacter pylori exposure, antigen-specific serological responses, and resistant versus non-resistant hypertension in a South African cohort.
authorString: Mennen MC, Zulu MZ, Mabatha KC, Baguma R, Skelem S, Mbundwini NN, Aremu OO, Adriaanse M, van Dijk D, Pillay P, Africa S, Jones E, Setshedi M, Brink A, Burgers WA, Ntusi NAB.
abstractText:
Background

Hypertension is a leading contributor to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, with poor control in low- and middle-income countries. Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) has been associated with hypertension through inflammatory, endothelial, metabolic and immune pathways, but data from sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in resistant hypertension, are limited.

Methods

This cross-sectional observational study will enrol 200 adults aged ≥18 at a tertiary academic hospital in Cape Town, South Africa: 80 with resistant hypertension, 80 with non-resistant hypertension and 40 with normotension. Participants will undergo standardised clinical assessment, blood pressure measurement, and collection of blood, urine and saliva. H. pylori exposure will be assessed using the Pylori DuoTect® point-of-care assay, which detects antibodies to CagA and FliD. Laboratory analyses will include lipid profile, inflammatory and nitric oxide-related markers, homocysteine, insulin indices, complete blood count, ghrelin, multiplex cytokine profiling and flow cytometric immunophenotyping. PAXgene® blood RNA samples will be retained for future exploratory analyses. Saliva will undergo exploratory H. pylori antigen testing using CerTest® kits, which are validated for stool rather than saliva. Saliva analysis will be exploratory, and results will not define the primary H. pylori exposure variable. Remaining saliva will be kept for potential future oral microbiome analyses not defined in this protocol. Multivariable logistic regression will evaluate associations between H. pylori exposure and hypertension phenotype, adjusting for demographic, lifestyle, and clinical covariates.

Discussion

To our knowledge, this will be the first African study to integrate point-of-care H. pylori serology with detailed clinical, inflammatory, metabolic, and immunological profiling across resistant hypertension, non-resistant hypertension and normotension. Findings may clarify biological pathways linking H. pylori exposure to blood pressure dysregulation and inform future mechanistic and interventional studies.

title: Changes in left atrial reservoir function and their association with exercise capacity after outpatient cardiac rehabilitation in early-stage heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
authorString: Yanagimoto K, Murayama M, Hioka T, Kimura K, Tanemura A, Kikuchi-Hirano M, Minezaki S, Minagawa N, Tsuda M, Fukushima A, Kaga S.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) improves exercise capacity in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Nonetheless, changes in left atrial (LA) mechanics after outpatient CR and the link between changes in LA function and exercise capacity in early-stage HFpEF remain unclear. Therefore, we aimed to examine changes in LA reservoir function after outpatient CR and its association with exercise capacity in early-stage HFpEF.

Methods

Echocardiography and cardiopulmonary exercise testing were performed pre- and post-CR in 21 patients with early-stage HFpEF without prior HF hospitalization (median age: 80 years; median HFA-PEFF score: 4). Exercise capacity was assessed by peak oxygen uptake (VO2). Left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LV-GLS) and LA reservoir strain (LASr) were derived using speckle-tracking echocardiography. Early diastolic mitral inflow velocity to mitral annular velocity (E/e') ratio was measured. LA stiffness index was calculated as the ratio of E/e' to LASr.

Results

Peak VO2 (13.3 ± 3.7 to 15.0 ± 3.8 mL/kg/min, p < 0.001) and LASr (20.4 ± 7.3 to 24.2 ± 6.9%, p = 0.002) significantly increased after outpatient CR. The peak VO2 change rate correlated with the LASr and LA stiffness index change rates (r = 0.62, p = 0.003; r = - 0.53, p = 0.017, respectively), but not with the LV-GLS change rate (r = 0.08, p = 0.735). LASr change rate continued to be associated with the peak VO2 change rate after multivariable adjustment in exploratory models.

Conclusions

In early-stage HFpEF, LA reservoir function increased after outpatient CR, and changes in LA reservoir function were independently associated with changes in exercise capacity.

title: Reduced diagnostic accuracy of screening questionnaires in older psychiatric patients at risk for obstructive sleep apnea: an observational cohort study.
authorString: Bailer M, Stein EM, Sprügel MI, Mestermann S, Sonnauer F, Schwarz JA, Utz J, Spitzer P, Kornhuber J.
abstractText:
Background

Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is highly prevalent among geriatric patients and is associated with increased mortality, reduced quality of life, depression, and cognitive decline. Early identification and treatment are particularly important in older psychiatric patients, in whom typical OSA symptoms overlap with psychiatric and aging-related symptoms. Screening questionnaires are used to identify patients at risk for OSA, but their performance in older psychiatric populations is largely unknown. This study compared the diagnostic accuracy of screening questionnaires between younger and older psychiatric inpatients at risk for OSA and assessed the discriminative value of chronological age alone.

Patients and methods

Observational study of consecutive admissions to a psychiatric ward at University Hospital Erlangen (June 2016-December 2022). 128 screened patients at risk for OSA with valid overnight polygraphy and questionnaire data were analyzed (72 aged 18-64 years; 56 aged ≥ 65 years). Risk scores were calculated for STOP-Bang, STOP-B28, BOAH, GOAL, NoSAS and No-Apnea questionnaires. The reference standard was apnea-hypopnea-index (AHI) measured by polygraphy. Primary outcome measures were the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity and specificity for any OSA (AHI ≥ 5 events/h). The discriminative value of age and individual questionnaire components was evaluated in the entire cohort.

Results

In the screened cohort of psychiatric inpatients, older patients had higher median AHI (7.7 vs. 1.8 events/h; p = 0.007), greater prevalence of any OSA (AHI ≥ 5: 73.2% vs. 47.2%; p = 0.003), deeper desaturations and longer apneas. In younger patients, questionnaire AUCs ranged 0.61-0.78. In the older subgroup, AUCs were 0.12-0.36 lower; BOAH had the highest AUC (0.59), while the other questionnaires showed AUCs of 0.38-0.49. The lower discrimination was mainly reflected in lower specificity. Chronological age yielded an AUC of 0.70 (95% CI, 0.61-0.80), whereas BMI, neck circumference, and symptom-based items showed poor discrimination.

Conclusions

In our sample of psychiatric inpatients at risk for OSA, commonly used screening questionnaires demonstrated markedly reduced diagnostic performance in patients aged ≥ 65 years, largely reflecting lower specificity. Chronological age demonstrated moderate discriminative value. Further research is warranted regarding the accuracy of OSA screening in older patients, and a lower threshold for device-based diagnostics may warrant consideration.

title: Biomarker-Informed Phenotyping of the Heart Failure Continuum: A Population-Based Evaluation of the Second Universal Definition of Heart Failure
authorString: Chen H, Ye J.
abstractText:
Objective:

To develop and evaluate a biomarker-informed, computable phenotype of the heart failure (HF) continuum, aligned with 2026 AHA/ACC/ESC/WHF Expert Consensus, using NHANES and linked mortality data, and to determine whether this phenotype identifies subgroups with distinct mortality risks.

Methods:

We analyzed 11,477 U.S. adults aged ≥20 years from the 1999-2004 NHANES cycles who participated in the surplus-sera biomarker substudy and were linked to National Death Index follow-up. Participants were classified into four phenotypes according to the 2026 Universal Definition of Heart Failure: no apparent risk, Stage A (at risk), Stage B (elevated NT-proBNP without self-reported HF), and Stage C (self-reported HF). Survey-weighted Kaplan-Meier curves and nested, multiply imputed Cox proportional hazards models, with sequential adjustment for demographic, socioeconomic, and cardiometabolic covariates, were used to estimate associations with mortality. Pairwise phenotype comparisons, standardized adjusted survival estimates, and restricted mean survival times were also calculated. Incremental prognostic value was evaluated by comparing discrimination and reclassification metrics between the full phenotype and a conventional three-level model that excluded NT-proBNP.

Results:

Weighted prevalences were 16.9%, 70.0%, 10.7%, and 2.4% for no apparent risk, Stage A, Stage B, and Stage C, respectively. In fully adjusted models, the hazard ratios (HRs) relative to no apparent risk were 1.58 (95% CI, 1.08-2.30), 2.88 (95% CI, 2.00-4.16), and 2.56 (95% CI, 1.61-4.09), respectively. Stage B was associated with significantly higher mortality risk than Stage A (HR, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.62-2.07), whereas the difference between Stage C and Stage B was not statistically significant (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.71-1.11). The association for Stage B attenuated less across sequentially adjusted models than that for Stage C. Adjusted 10-year mortality risks were 15.2% for Stage B and 14.2% for Stage C. Incorporating Stage B into the conventional model yielded only marginal improvements in discrimination (ΔC-statistic, 0.002; 95% CI, 0.001-0.002).

Conclusion:

A biomarker-informed phenotype of the HF continuum can be operationalized using national survey data and identifies a pre-HF subgroup with an adjusted mortality risk not significantly different from that of individuals with overt HF, despite only marginal gains in prognostic discrimination.

title: Deep Survival Analysis with Temporal Trajectory Embedding for Substandard Life Insurance Pricing: A DeepSurv Modeling Study of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
authorString: Xie Y, Wang Q.
abstractText: Substandard (impaired) lives have long been excluded from commercial health in- surance because conventional actuarial tools fail to capture the nonlinear progres- sion of chronic diseases and the high-dimensional interactions among comorbidities. Taking type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) as a case study, this paper constructs a substandard-life rate-making framework centered on the DeepSurv deep survival model. Using 1,883,235 T2DM inpatient claim records with mini-batch training on the full sample, we first expose the failure boundaries of traditional methods: the extra mortality (EM) model suffers a rate inversion (118.22% for T2S1 com- plicated cases versus 88.87% for T2S2 target-organ-damage cases) driven by age- structure confounding; the generalized linear model (GLM) two-part approach and the Tweedie compound model, while capable of decomposing frequency and severity, remain constrained by the proportional-hazards and linear-additivity assumptions; after incorporating province and year controls, the age coeﬀicient in the Gamma severity regression is corrected from −0.0002 to +0.0028 (the directional bias is re- paired), yet remains far below the Poisson frequency coeﬀicient of 0.031, indicating limited capacity of the linear-additive structure in capturing age effects. Deep- Surv, coupling a deep neural network with the Cox partial likelihood and trained on 1,840,774 records, attains a concordance index (C-index) of 0.695. It should be emphasized that the Tweedie/GLM area under the curve (AUC) for binary dis- crimination of excess events reaches 0.715, but the two metrics are not directly comparable—AUC measures binary classification power for whether out-of-pocket expenses exceed a 10,000 RMB threshold, whereas the C-index measures concor- dance in survival time ranking. The core value of DeepSurv lies not in a dominant single discrimination metric, but in its ability to capture high-dimensional interac- tions among comorbidities through a nonlinear risk surface and to provide premium attribution via SHAP—capabilities beyond the reach of linear models. Bootstrap resampling (B = 50) confirms a C-index standard error of 0.0031 with a 95% con- fidence interval of [0.684, 0.695], confirming robust discrimination. Methodologically, our contributions are fivefold. First, we incorporate Elastic Net regularization—embedding both L1 (Lasso) and L2 (Ridge) penalties into the DeepSurv loss function—so that the L1 component drives weak-signal features to- ward zero while the L2 component assigns similar weights to collinear comorbidities 1 (e.g., heart failure and ischemic heart disease), achieving the ideal “equal within group, sparse across groups” feature selection. Empirical comparison demonstrates that Elastic Net (α = 0.5) preserves the C-index while effectively shrinking re- dundant features, resolving the dilemma where pure Lasso arbitrarily selects one variable from a collinear group and pure Ridge cannot perform variable selection. Second, we introduce a long short-term memory (LSTM) network for independent rate-prediction benchmarking against time-varying health trajectories; empirically, its temporal R2 of 0.391 outperforms the GLM cross-section (R2 = 0.197, +99%) yet trails the lagged-mean benchmark (R2 = 0.455), confirming the incremental predic- tive value of temporal information and its future potential as a feature-embedding module for DeepSurv. Third, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) gradient ap- proximation on the full 1.84 million sample identifies age (mean|SHAP| = 0.269), DX_T2S2 (0.129), chronic ischemic heart disease COMB_I25 (0.123), DX_T2S1 (0.107), and heart failure COMB_I50 (0.107) as the top five risk drivers, with cardiovascular comorbidities approaching or exceeding diabetes staging itself in at- tribution weight. Fourth, we provide a complete mapping from survival probabil- ities to actuarial premiums, introducing a sojourn-time factor A(τ) and a health- management factor H(r) directly into the gross premium formula, and demonstrate SHAP-driven premium attribution with a high-risk case (male, age 65, cardiac co- morbidities, gross premium 14,802 RMB). Fifth, Bootstrap robustness checks con- firm that all key metrics exhibit acceptable standard errors, and the findings are reproducible under repeated sampling. Deep survival analysis with Elastic Net reg- ularization markedly improves the fairness, discrimination, and model parsimony of substandard-life pricing while preserving actuarial interpretability.

title: A Lanyu Pig Model of Ischemia-Reperfusion Myocardial Infarction for Cardiac Regeneration
authorString: Liu Y, Chen T, Fang Y, Chen D.
abstractText: Background Myocardial infarction (MI) remains a leading cause of heart failure worldwide. Robust large animal models that mimic human physiology are necessary to develop regenerative therapies such as cell transplantation. However, conventional porcine models (e.g., Yorkshire and Göttingen minipigs) are limited by high perioperative mortality, primarily from lethal ventricular arrhythmias, and rapid somatic growth, which hinders long-term study. We hypothesized that the Lanyu pig, a genetically distinct miniature breed, would offer a superior translational platform with better survival and physiological stability than do the conventional models. Methods Catheter-based ischemia-reperfusion injury was induced in 17 adult Lanyu pigs through 90-min balloon occlusion of the midsegment of the left anterior descending artery. An insertable cardiac monitor was implanted 3 days before surgery for continuous rhythm tracking. Cardiac function was comprehensively assessed at baseline, immediately after MI, and on Day 14 after MI through transthoracic echocardiography and pressure-volume loop analysis. Intramyocardial injections were administered on Day 14 to simulate the subacute phase and validate the feasibility of therapeutic delivery. Results The Lanyu pig model achieved a procedural survival rate of 94.1% (16/17), significantly higher than the historical rates for other breeds. Post-MI assessments confirmed substantial functional decline: left ventricular ejection fraction decreased from 69.4% to 40.0% ( p  < 0.001), and the slope of end-systolic pressure-volume relationship maximum rate of pressure rise decreased from 5.6 to 1.9 mmHg/mL ( p  < 0.001). Although transient arrhythmias were observed, no sustained malignant arrhythmias occurred. Infarcts were consistent, and the animals tolerated the surgical and follow-up procedures well. Conclusion Our Lanyu pig MI model demonstrated high survival rates, reproducible cardiac dysfunction, and physiological similarity to humans. This model overcomes key limitations of conventional porcine models, offering a robust and ethically refined tool for preclinical evaluation of novel cardiac regenerative therapies.

title: Multivariate study of renal function in hypertensive patients treated at the Amissa Bongo University Hospital Center
authorString: ONDO JP, MBA TN, OBIANG CS, MOUSSAVOU BN, KAYEBEGHE ARE, MOMBO EJM, MISSO RNM, ENGONGA LO.
abstractText: Background Arterial hypertension remains a major public health challenge in sub-Saharan Africa, with inadequate blood pressure control despite available treatments. Objective To describe the epidemiological, clinical, and biological profile of hypertensive patients and assess associations between antihypertensive treatment, blood pressure control, and renal function. Methods A cross-sectional descriptive and analytical study was conducted from October to December 2025 at the Amissa Bongo University Hospital Center, Franceville, Gabon, including 73 hypertensive patients. Sociodemographic, clinical, therapeutic, and biological data were collected using a standardized questionnaire and analyzed with R software (v4.3.1). Results Mean age was 60.9 ± 15.2 years, with a balanced sex distribution (50.7% male). Mean systolic and diastolic blood pressures were 169.1 ± 31.9 and 101.0 ± 24.9 mmHg, respectively; Grade 3 hypertension predominated (35.6%). Major comorbidities included type 2 diabetes (28.8%), stroke history (19.2%), and chronic kidney disease (16.4%). Perindopril/amlodipine (Coveram®) was the most prescribed treatment (61.6%). Only 23.3% achieved blood pressure control (< 140/90 mmHg). Coveram® use was associated with lower serum creatinine (142 ± 89 vs. 218 ± 341 µmol/L; p = 0.042). Age correlated with systolic pressure (r = 0.38; p = 0.001). Multivariate analyses identified distinct renal, blood pressure-glycemic, and hepatic profiles, with age particularly associated with renal parameters. Conclusion Blood pressure control remains suboptimal despite frequent combination therapy. Perindopril/amlodipine use was associated with better renal parameters. Therapeutic education and closer follow-up are warranted.

title: Admission NT-proBNP-to-Albumin Ratio, Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index, and Early Severe Clinical Deterioration in Acute Decompensated Heart Failure
authorString: Kaya MG, Kilinc M.
abstractText: Background Early risk stratification in acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) remains challenging in the emergency department. This study aimed to evaluate the association between admission-based laboratory biomarkers, composite inflammatory indices, and early severe clinical deterioration in patients hospitalized with ADHF. Methods This retrospective single-center cohort study included 1,450 adult patients hospitalized from the emergency department with ADHF between January 2023 and January 2025. Admission laboratory biomarkers and composite indices, including the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR), prognostic nutritional index (PNI), and log10 NT-proBNP-to-albumin ratio, were evaluated. The primary outcome was a composite severe clinical course defined as intensive care unit admission, non-invasive ventilation (NIV), or endotracheal intubation during index hospitalization. Results Severe clinical course occurred in 338 patients (23.3%). In multivariable analysis, the log10 NT-proBNP-to-albumin ratio remained independently associated with severe clinical course in both tested models (Model 1: OR 2.008, 95% CI 1.493–2.701; Model 2: OR 1.988, 95% CI 1.498–2.640; both p < 0.001). In the extended model, SII was also independently associated with severe clinical course (OR 1.179 per doubling, 95% CI 1.075–1.293, p < 0.001). ROC curve analysis demonstrated statistically significant but limited discriminatory performance for both the log10 NT-proBNP-to-albumin ratio (AUC 0.608, 95% CI 0.570–0.646, p < 0.001) and SII (AUC 0.595, 95% CI 0.559–0.631, p < 0.001). Conclusion In patients hospitalized with ADHF, early severe clinical deterioration was associated with higher inflammatory, cardiorenal, and myocardial stress markers. The log10 NT-proBNP-to-albumin ratio showed the most consistent independent association, while SII provided an additional inflammatory risk signal. These routinely available admission-based indices may provide complementary information for early risk assessment but demonstrated only modest discriminatory performance.

title: Ventricular arrhythmia-heart failure interaction and mortality in ICD recipients after myocardial infarction.
authorString: Echivard M, Sellal JM, McMurray JJV, Ziliox C, Monzo L, Lamiral Z, Duarte K, De Chillou C, Baudry G, Girerd N, WICD-MI Registry Group.
abstractText:
Aims

Ventricular arrhythmia (VA) and heart failure (HF) frequently coexist in patients with ischaemic left ventricular (LV) dysfunction. Whether VA and HF events are bidirectionally associated remains unclear. We investigated their bidirectional relationship and associations with mortality.

Methods

We analysed 1014 patients from the multicentre WICD-MI study. All received a wearable cardioverter-defibrillator after acute myocardial infarction (MI) and subsequently underwent implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) implantation, with persistent LV ejection fraction ≤35%. Associations between ICD-treated VA, HF-events (HF hospitalization, heart transplantation, or LV assist device implantation), and all-cause mortality were assessed using time-dependent Cox models.

Results

Over a median follow-up of 2.6 years post-ICD implantation, VA was independently associated with an increased risk of HF events [aHR = 3.50 (1.66-7.38), P = .001], while HF events similarly preceded subsequent VA [aHR = 2.96 (1.59-5.50), P = .0008]. Both were independently associated with all-cause mortality, with a numerically higher aHR for HF events [aHR = 7.96 (4.71-13.47), P < .0001] than for VA [aHR = 4.43 (2.35-8.36), P < .0001]. Sensitivity analyses suggested that the VA-HF association was strongest for shock-treated arrhythmias. In exploratory analyses, VA was strongly associated with subsequent HF events in subcutaneous ICD recipients [aHR = 15.08 (4.62-49.22), P < .0001] but not in transvenous ICD recipients (P for interaction = .0002).

Conclusion

In ICD recipients with persistent LV dysfunction following MI, VA and HF events are bidirectionally associated and independently associated with mortality. The VA-HF association was strongest for shock-treated arrhythmias. These findings highlight the potential value of integrated HF and VA management.

title: Sequential Coronary Obstruction After Native TAVI: Immediate Acute Occlusion and Very Late Stent Compression by Aortic Wall Hematoma.
authorString: Akyüz AR, Yerlikaya MG, Öztürk M, Kul S.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText: Coronary obstruction is a rare but catastrophic complication of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) associated with high mortality. While acute and delayed presentations have distinct pathophysiological mechanisms, their occurrence in the same patient is exceedingly rare. We present a unique case of a 91-year-old female who developed acute left main coronary artery (LMCA) obstruction immediately following native TAVI using a balloon-expandable valve, which was successfully treated with bail-out percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Three months later (> 60 days, classified as "Very Late" coronary obstruction), she presented with severe angina and heart failure. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) revealed extrinsic compression of the previously implanted coronary stent caused by a localized aortic wall hematoma. A repeat PCI with a stent-in-stent technique restored coronary flow, leading to complete clinical recovery. This case expands the known mechanical spectrum of very late coronary obstruction according to recent classification frameworks and highlights the vital role of intravascular imaging and multimodality assessment in diagnosis and management.

title: Successful Management of Infective Native Infrarenal Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Associated With <i>Micrococcus luteus</i> and <i>Streptococcus mitis</i> in a 77-year-Old Man.
authorString: Castro E, Galaz-Alvarez PE, Ramírez-Delgado M, Hinojosa CA, Arzola-Flores LH, Anaya-Ayala JE, Laparra-Escareno H.
abstractText: BackgroundInfected native abdominal aortic aneurysm (INAAA) is a rare but life-threatening condition characterized by rapid progression and high mortality.Case SummaryWe report a 77-year-old male with a history of arterial hypertension, ischemic heart disease, and stage IVB hormone-sensitive prostate adenocarcinoma, presenting with lumbar pain and mild inflammatory activation, including leukocytes 8.8 ×10³/µL and C-reactive protein 3.6 mg/dL (normal <0.50 mg/dL). Computed tomography angiography (CTA) demonstrated a 50-mm infrarenal aneurysm, with periaortic inflammatory changes and a periaortic hematoma. A multidisciplinary decision, made 3 hours after admission, favored urgent open surgical repair with resection and in situ reconstruction. Midline laparotomy with debridement and resection of the affected aorta was performed; in situ reconstruction was carried out using a rifampicin soaked bifurcated Dacron graft covered with bovine pericardium with anastomoses to healthy aortic and iliac segments. Intraoperative cultures identified Micrococcus luteus and Streptococcus mitis, rare pathogens in this context. Targeted therapy included intravenous ceftriaxone during hospitalization, followed by oral amoxicillin-clavulanate and doxycycline for seven weeks. Histopathology confirmed chronic granulomatous abscessed inflammation. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient was discharged home on postoperative day 17. At six months, follow-up imaging demonstrated a patent reconstruction without signs of persistent infection.ConclusionThese findings highlight the importance of early recognition, aggressive debridement, and coordinated multidisciplinary management in achieving optimal outcomes in INAAA, particularly when atypical microorganisms complicate diagnosis and therapeutic decision-making.

title: Healthcare Access, Use, Affordability, and Satisfaction Among Adults With Cardiovascular Conditions After Enrollment in Medicare Advantage Versus Traditional Medicare.
authorString: Oseran AS, Xia K, Tale A, Qian Y, Wadhera RK.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiovascular disease is highly prevalent among older adults and remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in Medicare. Medicare Advantage (MA)-the managed care alternative to traditional Medicare (TM)-offers adults integrated care and supplemental benefits that may improve outcomes and satisfaction for this high-risk population.

Methods

We used longitudinal data from the National Health and Retirement Study (2010-2022) and an event-study, difference-in-differences design to compare changes in self-reported measures of health care access, utilization, affordability, and satisfaction among adults with cardiovascular conditions newly enrolling in MA versus TM (exposure) at 65 years. Eligible adults had a self-reported history of hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, heart disease, or stroke.

Results

A total of 3312 adults with cardiovascular conditions newly enrolled in Medicare, 34.3% in MA (mean age, 63.6 years; 60.5% female) and 65.7% in TM (mean age, 63.5 years; 56.5% female). Following enrollment, there were no differential changes in health care access or utilization between MA and TM at any follow-up time point. However, new MA enrollees experienced relative improvements in affordability compared with their TM counterparts, including greater reductions in trouble affording medical care (difference-in-differences estimate -6.6 percentage points [95% CI, -12.0 to -1.3]) and trouble affording prescription medications (difference-in-differences estimate -4.6 pp [95% CI, -9.2 to -0.2]) by the end of follow-up. Satisfaction with care increased in both groups but with larger gains among MA enrollees (difference-in-differences estimate at the end of follow-up +11.3 pp [95% CI, 5.2-17.4]).

Conclusions

For adults with cardiovascular conditions transitioning into Medicare at 65 years, enrollment in MA was associated with greater improvements in affordability and satisfaction compared with TM. These findings may inform coverage decisions for this high-risk population, though generalizability to older beneficiaries or those with more advanced disease remains uncertain.

title: Comment on "Lymphedema therapy in head & neck cancer with carotid stenosis: a systematic review and care pathway".
authorString: Jeya Beulah D, Nathiya K, Badduri P, Ozukum S.

title: Roles of TRIM proteins in cardiovascular diseases: From pathogenesis to therapeutic targeting (Review).
authorString: Wang F, Xing Z, Gao Y, Gai Y.
abstractText: Cardiovascular diseases are driven by sustained mechanical stress, metabolic derangement, inflammation and oxidative injury, which progressively disrupt cellular homeostasis within the heart and vasculature. Although current therapeutic strategies have substantially improved clinical outcomes, most interventions primarily target downstream pathological manifestations rather than upstream regulatory mechanisms that determine stress adaptation and tissue remodeling. Tripartite motif (TRIM) proteins constitute a large family of E3 ubiquitin ligases characterized by a highly conserved RBCC domain architecture and diversified C‑terminal regions. By catalyzing distinct ubiquitin chain topologies and functioning as molecular scaffolds, TRIM proteins broadly regulate protein turnover, inflammatory signaling, metabolic adaptation and cell fate determination. Emerging evidence identifies TRIM proteins as context‑dependent regulators whose biological effects are shaped by cell type, disease stage and microenvironmental conditions. Multiple TRIM family members have been linked to a wide spectrum of cardiovascular diseases, including atherosclerosis, vascular calcification, myocardial infarction, cardiac hypertrophy and metabolic cardiomyopathy. At the cellular level, TRIM proteins influence disease initiation and progression by modulating endothelial dysfunction, vascular smooth muscle cell phenotypic remodeling, cardiomyocyte survival and metabolic homeostasis, fibroblast activation and immune‑inflammatory responses. The present review summarized the biochemical characteristics and cell‑specific functions of TRIM proteins and delineates their mechanistic roles in cardiovascular pathogenesis. In addition, it discussed their emerging potential as diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets, highlighting both translational opportunities and context‑dependent challenges.

title: Left Subclavian Artery Revascularization and Early Neurological Outcomes After Zone 2 TEVAR.
authorString: Eren Karpuzoğlu O, Karaağaç A, Bozkurt B, Çalişkan R, Kağan Kuş M, Baştopçu M, Karakaya C, Uğur Koçoğullari C.
abstractText:
Background

LSA revascularization is generally favored when intentional LSA coverage is planned during elective zone 2 TEVAR, whereas in urgent settings the decision is individualized according to anatomy, ischemic risk, and clinical urgency. This study evaluated the association between preoperative or concomitant LSA revascularization and early neurological outcomes after zone 2 TEVAR.

Methods

This single-center retrospective study included 32 patients who underwent zone 2 TEVAR with intentional LSA coverage between January 2018 and December 2024. Patients were classified according to whether LSA revascularization was performed before or concomitantly with TEVAR (Rev+, n=21) or not (Rev-, n=11). The primary endpoint was any 30 day neurological complication, including ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), and spinal cord ischemia (SCI). Major neurological events, defined as stroke or SCI, were additionally evaluated.

Results

Early neurological complications occurred in 4/21 patients (19.0%) in the Rev+ group and 3/11 (27.3%) in the Rev- group (p=.667), corresponding to an absolute risk difference of -8.2 percentage points (95% CI, -39.4 to 23.0) and a risk ratio of 0.70 (95% CI, 0.19-2.58). Major neurological events occurred in 3/21 (14.3%) and 2/11 (18.2%) patients, respectively (p=1.000). Stroke occurred in 3/21 (14.3%) Rev+ patients and 1/11 (9.1%) Rev- patients, while SCI occurred in no Rev+ patients and in 1/11 (9.1%) Rev- patients. LSA revascularization was not significantly associated with the primary endpoint (OR, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.12-3.34; p=.582). Results remained similar after separate adjustment for age, dissection, urgency, coronary artery disease, and chronic kidney disease. Sensitivity analyses using major neurological events as the endpoint and including postoperative LSA revascularization in the exposure definition also yielded similar results.

Conclusions

Preoperative or concomitant LSA revascularization during zone 2 TEVAR was associated with a numerically lower rate of early neurological complications, although the difference was not statistically significant. Larger studies are needed to better define the association between LSA revascularization and neurological outcomes after zone 2 TEVAR.

title: Surgical outcomes of infective endocarditis in children and adults with congenital heart disease.
authorString: Schaeffer T, Alaham K, Kienmoser D, Amici A, Palm J, Lemmen T, Ruda C, Piber N, Matsubara M, Heinisch PP, Hager A, Ewert P, Hörer J, Ono M.

journal.title: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery

abstractText:
Objective

Reports describing surgery for infective endocarditis (IE) in children and adults with congenital heart disease (CHD) are limited. This study aimed to determine the patient characteristics, preoperative conditions, surgical outcomes, and risk factors in this cohort.

Methods

All children and adults with CHD who underwent surgical treatment for IE between 2001 and 2024 were reviewed. Patient characteristics and surgical procedures were evaluated; survival, recurrent IE, and risk factors were analyzed.

Results

A total of 96 patients underwent surgical treatment for IE, including 52 children and 44 adults with CHD. Underlying CHD included ventricular septal defect in 31 patients, aortic stenosis/insufficiency in 26, and tetralogy of Fallot in 14. The most frequently infected lesion was the aortic valve in 40 patients, and the most frequently detected organism was Staphylococcus species in 34 patients. Vegetation was observed in 65 patients. Median age at surgery was 17.2 (IQR: 11.7-29.4) years. In-hospital mortality was 6.3%, and survival at 5, 10, and 20 years was 90.6, 88.1, and 80.5%, respectively. Freedom from recurrent IE was 96.4% at 20 years. Number of previous operations (hazard ratio (HR): 1.585, p=0.005), gram-negative bacteria (HR: 11.475, p<0.001), emergency operations (HR: 17.988, p=0.001), and longer aortic cross-clamp time (HR: 1.011, p=0.043) were risk factors for mortality.

Conclusions

In children and adults with CHD, mortality following surgery for IE was low, and recurrent IE was rare. Individualized management based on the patient's preoperative condition and the causative organism appears to be important for improving survival.

title: Predictors of longer recognition time in acute aortic dissection: a retrospective observational study.
authorString: Wang PH, Kao CL, Chien LC, Chuang CC, Huang PC, Hong MY, Chi CH.

journal.title: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care

abstractText:
Background

Acute aortic dissection (AAD) carries a high mortality risk closely tied to diagnostic timeliness. Delays remain prevalent, driven by atypical presentations-particularly in patients without a chief complaint of pain. This study identified predictors of a longer recognition time, as indicated by prolonged door-to-CT times, and developed a cumulative prediction model for patients presenting without pain complaints.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective study of 197 adult patients diagnosed with AAD at a tertiary emergency department (ED) from 2016 to 2023. Patients were classified as having a shorter (< 74 min) or longer (≥ 74 min; cohort median) door-to-CT completion time. Predictors were identified by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-penalized logistic regression and decision tree analysis. A subgroup analysis characterized pain-complaint-free patients using a stepwise identification algorithm.

Results

A longer door-to-CT time was associated with female sex, older age, and physiological instability. The strongest multivariable predictors were absence of abrupt pain (odds ratio [OR] 2.81, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.47-5.46) and non-severe triage classification (OR 4.70, 95% CI 1.71-15.29). Dyspnea (OR 2.14) and elevated diastolic blood pressure (OR 1.02/mmHg) also independently predicted a longer door-to-CT time. Among pain-complaint-free patients (n = 46), a stepwise combination of mediastinal widening on chest radiography, Charlson Comorbidity Index ≥ 3, and Shock Index > 1.0 was present in all identified cases (cumulative case coverage 46/46; 95% CI 92.3%-100%).

Conclusion

This study identifies a high-risk profile for a longer recognition time of AAD, particularly in older female patients and those presenting without sudden pain. For patients unable to report pain, chest radiography, shock index, and comorbidity burden may be considered to help identify atypical presentations warranting urgent evaluation.

title: Digital Twin-Based Risk Stratification Integrating Aortic Shape and Wall Mechanics in Acute Uncomplicated Type B Aortic Dissection
authorString: Liu M, Zhou Z, Du Y, Cebull HL, Dong H, Oshinski JN, Elefteriades JA, Gleason RL, Leshnower BG.
abstractText:
Objective

This study evaluated whether patient-specific digital twins integrating 3D aortic anatomy and structural wall stress could identify patients with acute uncomplicated type B aortic dissection (AUTBAD) at high risk for adverse aortic events.

Methods

We analyzed CTAs from 50 patients extracted from a 400 AUTBAD patient database treated with optimal medical therapy from 1999-2025. Digital twin models were constructed, and statistical shape modeling and reduced-order fluid-structure interaction analysis were performed. Anatomic shape and biomechanical stress data were integrated into models predicting freedom from aortic events, defined as intervention or aortic-related death, using leave-one-out cross-validation. A cross-validated risk score was generated for each patient, with higher scores indicating higher event risk.

Results

At diagnosis, the median descending aortic diameter was 40.61 mm. During follow-up, 35 patients experienced an aortic event: 28 interventions (56%) and 7 aortic-related deaths (14%). Stratification by descending aortic diameter above or below 40.61 mm yielded higher-versus lower-risk aortic event-free survival of 72.0% versus 84.0% at 1 year and 27.8% versus 56.7% at 6 years (p=0.035; C-index=0.590). In the cross-validated multidimensional model combining morphology and structural stress, higher-versus lower-risk event-free survival was 60.0% versus 96.0% at 1 year and 12.5% versus 68.9% at 6 years (p<0.001; C-index=0.792).

Conclusions

Digital twin modeling integrating morphology and wall stress provided greater risk separation than univariable predictors in AUTBAD patients. With independent validation, patient-specific AUTBAD risk stratification using geometric and biomechanical data may ultimately contribute to identification of high-risk patients who may benefit from early endovascular repair.

Central Picture

Multidimensional digital twin model stratifies aortic event-free survival in AUTBAD

Central Message

Combining patient-specific 3D aortic morphology and wall stress may improve identification of medically managed AUTBAD patients at high risk for aortic intervention or aortic-related death.

Perspective
