TBAD geometry is highly patient specific, and one-dimensional measurements may not fully reflect patient risk. Digital twin modeling incorporating 3D morphology and wall mechanics may provide a more complete basis for risk stratification. This study demonstrates the feasibility of integrating multidimensional shape and stress data into a risk-stratification model to identify high-risk AUTBAD patients.

title: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Sudden Cardiac Death: Epidemiology, Mechanisms, Risk Stratification, and Prevention.
authorString: Liu ZY, Qin ZH, Liu YF, Wei HT, Zhang RY.
abstractText: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has emerged as the most prevalent chronic metabolic liver disease worldwide. Cardiovascular adverse events have long been the leading cause of death in the MASLD population, far exceeding liver-related mortality. Sudden cardiac death (SCD) represents the most insidious and rapidly progressing extreme clinical phenotype among these cardiovascular complications. However, the relationship between MASLD and SCD has long received insufficient attention. Accumulating evidence from clinical studies indicates that MASLD is associated with elevated sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) risk independent of conventional cardiometabolic risk factors. Notably, while non-invasive clinical proxies of hepatic steatosis (such as the fatty liver index) identify individuals with heightened susceptibility to SCA, advancing liver fibrosis shows the strongest, gradient-dependent association with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, although its relation to SCA or SCD specifically requires confirmation. Sudden death in MASLD may result from primary ventricular arrhythmias or, in advanced cirrhosis, from non-shockable arrest due to hemodynamic, infectious, or metabolic decompensation. Although shared cardiometabolic risk factors account for a substantial portion of this association, proposed mechanisms include insulin resistance-related myocardial energy disturbances, inflammation-associated myocardial and electrophysiological remodeling, cirrhosis-associated circulatory dysfunction, and gut-derived endotoxemia. In clinical practice, non-invasive fibrosis scores, circulating biomarkers, and imaging parameters represent promising candidate risk markers for evaluating electrophysiological vulnerability, though a validated, MASLD-specific SCD risk prediction model remains to be established. Strategies such as lifestyle intervention, metabolic-targeted pharmacotherapy, and intensive management of cardiovascular risk factors may interrupt the progression from MASLD to SCD. This review summarizes the current evidence to inform cardiovascular risk management across the course of MASLD.

title: Symmetrical Peripheral Gangrene in a Child With <i>Plasmodium falciparum</i> Cerebral Malaria: A Rare but Serious Complication.
authorString: Ahenkan E, Kotoh-Mortty MF, Boateng FO, Donkor KK, Struck NS, May J, Ascofare OM.
abstractText: Symmetrical peripheral gangrene is a rare, limb-threatening complication associated with severe infection and disseminated intravascular coagulation. We report a case of a 6-year-old girl with cerebral malaria who developed gangrene of all toes during treatment. Management included antimalarials, antibiotics, supportive care, debridement, and subsequent skin grafting after adequate wound granulation.

title: Clinically Suspected Tumefactive Demyelination Mimicking a Brain Tumor in a 10-Year-Old Boy: A Case Report.
authorString: Aman F, Ali A, Khan MF, Khan HN, Shah A, Erkin AS, Khan S, Sattar Y, Khalid AA.
abstractText: After cranial surgery, a 10-year-old boy developed hand weakness, numbness, and fatigue. MRI showed frontoparietal lesions; biopsy lacked documented demyelination. Symptoms and lesions reportedly improved after methylprednisolone. Tumefactive demyelination was suspected, but discordant laterality, unavailable antibody testing, and brief follow-up left the diagnosis unclassified.

title: Prescribing, Medication Adherence, and Blood Pressure Goal Achievement Among Middle-to-Older Age Adults in a Primary Care Setting.
authorString: Elhiny R, O'Keeffe LM, Das T, Burton E, Millar SR, Byrne S, Donovan M, Bermingham M.
abstractText:
Background

Blood pressure (BP) control among hypertensive people remains inadequate. This study aims to assess BP goal achievement among people prescribed antihypertensives, to examine medication nonadherence, and to identify demographics associated with goal achievements and medication nonadherence in this population.

Methods

This was a cross-sectional analysis of the Mitchelstown Cohort Study Rescreen data. Goal achievement was assessed in accordance with the 2013 European guidelines, the guidelines in place during data collection. A validated, self-reported 3-item medication nonadherence questionnaire was used, with a mean score ranging from 1 (Perfect Adherence) to 5 (Perfect Nonadherence). Nonadherence was defined as mean score > 1. Multiple imputation was used to impute missing data on covariates and outcomes. A sensitivity analysis was performed to assess the consistency of results by applying the 2024 European guideline recommendations. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to identify the factors associated with BP goal achievements and medication nonadherence.

Results

Antihypertensives were prescribed to 567 participants. Based on imputed data, 63.8% of these achieved 2013 BP goal. Mean medication nonadherence score was 1.6 (SE ± 0.06), with 34.8% participants being nonadherent. Having multiple antihypertensives pills was associated with lower likelihood of achieving BP goals. In the sensitivity analysis, 38.4% achieved 2024 BP goal and in multivariable analysis, being overweight or obese was associated with not achieving the 2024 goals.

Conclusion

The study highlights the gap between guideline BP goals and achieving these goals in real world practice. Key patient and medication factors were identified that could guide efforts to improve BP goal achievement. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03191227.

title: Cerebral Air Embolism Following Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography Stent Removal: A Rare and Fatal Complication.
authorString: Senthuran B, Arulmurali A, Kajendran A, Vijayacumar T, Paramanathan S.
abstractText:
Background

Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) is a generally performed procedure for biliary pathology. Although usually safe, air embolism is an exceptionally rare but potentially fatal complication.

Case presentation

We report the case of a 79-year-old female (ASA II) with a history of dyslipidemia and obesity, who presented for elective ERCP and biliary stent removal. She had previously undergone ERCP and open cholecystectomy for choledocholithiasis. During this time, sedation was administered by using fentanyl, midazolam, and propofol via target-controlled infusion. The procedure was initially uneventful; however, at its conclusion, the patient developed sudden desaturation, bradycardia, and a reduced level of consciousness. Computed tomography (CT) imaging revealed multiple cerebral air emboli. Despite intensive care management and ventilatory support, the patient deteriorated and died 2 days later.

Conclusion

This case highlights the importance of maintaining vigilance for air embolism, even in seemingly straightforward ERCP procedures, especially in elderly patients. Early recognition and immediate management are vital to improving outcomes.

title: Enteric Fever Presenting With Acute Bilateral Lower Limb Weakness due to Para Infectious Myopathy With Elevated Serum Creatine Kinase: A Case Report.
authorString: Khan S, Farooq T, Hussain SF, Rehan R, Usman K, Iftikhar H, Siddiqui HH, Kamal M, Khan H, Sikandar A, Ahmed S.
abstractText: Parainfectious myopathy is a rare complication of Salmonella infection. We report an immunocompetent young patient presenting with acute bilateral lower limb weakness and markedly elevated creatine kinase. Blood cultures confirmed Salmonella sp. Prompt treatment with meropenem and azithromycin resulted in reducing CK level from 1854 to 240 U/L.

title: Astragalus Polysaccharide Exerts a Neuroprotective Effect in a Demyelination Model by Alleviating Oxidative Stress.
authorString: Long Y, Wang L, Hou B.
abstractText: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune disease of the central nervous system characterized by progressive demyelination and neurodegenerative damage. The accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and the resulting oxidative stress are considered key contributors to myelin injury and disease progression. Astragalus polysaccharide (APS), a water-soluble polysaccharide, exhibits multiple pharmacological activities, including immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and anti-apoptotic effects. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects of APS in MS and to explore its potential mechanisms. In vivo, APS was administered intraperitoneally at 50 mg/kg/day in a cuprizone-induced demyelinating mouse model, and its effects were evaluated by immunofluorescence, immunohistochemistry, and Western blotting. In vitro, the regulatory effects of APS on oxidative stress in oligodendrocytes were assessed by immunofluorescence and Western blotting in an H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>-induced oligodendrocyte injury model. APS significantly ameliorated myelin damage and apoptosis in vivo by inhibiting oxidative stress and attenuated oxidative stress and apoptosis in oligodendrocytes in vitro, thereby exerting neuroprotective effects. These findings indicate that APS alleviates demyelination by regulating oxidative stress, suggesting that it may represent a promising therapeutic option for the treatment of multiple sclerosis.

title: A synergistic framework of homotopy perturbation and finite element analysis of electro-osmotic thermo-hydrodynamics for Carreau-Yasuda hybrid nanofluids in composite arterial stenoses.
authorString: Hussain A, Hassan A, Iqbal Z, Naz H.
abstractText: Accurate modeling of hemodynamics is essential for understanding cardiovascular pathologies. In this research, we focus on understanding the thermo-hydrodynamic response of blood, which is modeled as a Carreau-Yasuda non-Newtonian fluid, flowing through an artery with composite trapezoidal/tilted ellipsoidal stenoses. We analyze the transport of Ag-TiO<sub>2</sub> hybrid nanoparticles driven by wall-induced electroosmosis. The governing equations are solved numerically using the Finite Element Method (FEM) in COMSOL Multiphysics, and validated analytically using the Homotopy Perturbation Method (HPM). We evaluate velocity, pressure, and temperature profiles across various rheological parameters, including zero-shear viscosity, infinite-shear viscosity, and relaxation time. Quantitative analysis reveals a peak blood velocity of 0.25m/s at the center of the ellipsoidal stenosis. The pressure profile demonstrates a drop from 12030Pa at the inlet to a minimum of 11991Pa at the second constriction. Thermally, the fluid temperature decays exponentially from 337K at the inlet to 313K at the outlet, alongside a maximum heat flux of 600W/m<sup>2</sup>. Furthermore, the thermal profile demonstrated high stability, showing no shift across zero-shear viscosity variations. Practically, this hybrid nanofluid framework provides a crucial computational tool for predicting complex hemodynamics, thereby optimizing targeted drug delivery mechanisms and localized thermal therapies in cardiovascular disease management.

title: Left Ventricular Aneurysm Associated With Severe Aortic Regurgitation.
authorString: Sa F, Yang K, Chen X, Zhao S, Dai L.
abstractText:
Images

Multimodality imaging findings.

Case summary

A 53-year-old man presented with exertional chest tightness. Transthoracic echocardiography showed severe aortic regurgitation, left ventricular dilatation, basal inferior wall thinning with paradoxical motion, and an eccentric regurgitant jet impinging on the basal inferior wall. Coronary computed tomography angiography excluded obstructive disease. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance demonstrated an inferior aneurysm with near-transmural late gadolinium enhancement. Four-dimensional flow imaging further characterized the regurgitant jet trajectory, with a localized vortex and elevated wall shear stress. He underwent bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement.

Take-home message

Multimodality imaging demonstrated spatial concordance between eccentric regurgitant flow, regional hemodynamic abnormalities, and myocardial injury.

title: Patient-Specific Physical and Computational Models for Replicating Coronary Stent Deployment.
authorString: Ilic M, Utzmann T, Lass A, Häner J, Rüd J, Stark AW, Gräni C, Busch J, Haeberlin A.
abstractText:
Background

Percutaneous coronary intervention with balloon angioplasty and stent implantation is standard therapy for coronary artery disease, but accurate prediction of patient-specific procedural outcomes remains challenging.

Case summary

Patient-derived imaging data were used to reconstruct three-dimensional coronary models, which were further translated into a three-dimensional-printed physical phantom and a finite element digital twin. The identical stent and balloon were deployed in the phantom; stent deployment was computationally simulated, and both were compared with the clinical optical coherence tomography.

Discussion

Both platforms reproduced key procedural features. The phantom moderately underestimated, and the finite element model overestimated, the clinically observed lumen gain. These proof-of-concept findings support the technical feasibility of building patient-specific artificial twins, but quantitative accuracy will require further model refinement and validation before clinical use.

Take-home message

Patient-specific models offer a means to visualize procedural characteristics and test alternative stent designs or deployment strategies outside the patient.

title: Live Versus Delayed Video-Based TEAM Assessment During Real-World Cardiac Arrest: Agreement and Exploratory Differences by Rater Experience.
authorString: Lien CJ, Yu PH, Huang SK, Chang JH, Pei-Chuan Huang E.
abstractText:
Study objective

To evaluate agreement between immediate live and delayed video-based assessment of nontechnical skills during real-world adult cardiac arrest resuscitation, and whether agreement differed by rater experience.

Methods

We conducted a prospective observational study of adult cardiac arrest resuscitations in a tertiary emergency department in Taiwan in 2024. For each event, one trained physician or nurse who participated in the resuscitation completed the Team Emergency Assessment Measure (TEAM) immediately afterward and re-rated the same event from video approximately 30 days later. Live-video agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients and Bland-Altman analysis.

Results

Of 105 recorded resuscitations, 80 had complete paired assessments. Mean global ratings were similar between modalities (8.25 versus 8.22; mean paired difference, -0.03; 95% confidence interval [CI] -0.25 to 0.20), whereas teamwork scores were modestly lower on video review (mean paired difference, -1.00; 95% CI -1.77 to -0.23). Event-level agreement was limited: intraclass correlation coefficients were 0.21 (95% CI 0.00 to 0.41) for total TEAM score and 0.16 (95% CI -0.06 to 0.37) for global rating. Total TEAM video ratings averaged 1.24 points lower than live ratings, with limits of agreement from -12.28 to 9.80. Agreement was higher among senior raters.

Conclusion

Delayed video-based TEAM assessment produced similar group-level scores but limited event-level agreement during real-world cardiac arrest. Agreement appeared higher among senior raters. Video review may support debriefing and monitoring, but appraisal of a specific resuscitation or other higher stakes use likely requires experienced raters and structured safeguards.

title: Cardiac electrophysiology procedures must be performed exclusively by trained electrophysiologists: A statement from the Heart Rhythm Society and Heart Rhythm Advocates.
authorString: Greenberg SJ, Chung MK, Lakkireddy D, Al-Khatib SM, Aryana A, Di Biase L, Ellenbogen KA, Liu CF, Mehta R, Mittal S, Natale A, Reddy VY, Shanker AJ, Hurwitz JL.
abstractText: The exponential growth of clinical cardiac electrophysiology (CCEP) as a subspecialty has created an important unresolved question in contemporary cardiovascular medicine: Who is qualified to perform electrophysiology (EP) procedures? As nonelectrophysiologists increasingly perform procedures that require the nuanced expertise of a trained or board-certified CCEP (eg, permanent pacemaker implantation, implantable cardioverter-defibrillator implantation, cardiac resynchronization therapy, and transvenous lead extraction), the consequences for patient safety, procedural outcomes, and health system efficiency have become impossible to ignore. This article presents a comprehensive, evidence-based argument that cardiac EP procedures must be performed exclusively by physicians who have completed accredited fellowship training in CCEP. We draw upon peer-reviewed outcome data, guideline-derived training standards from the Heart Rhythm Society, the American College of Cardiology, and American Heart Association, including the newly published 2026 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association/Heart Rhythm Society Advanced Training Statement on Clinical Cardiac Electrophysiology, as well as registry analyses spanning hundreds of thousands of patients to substantiate our position. The risks associated with suboptimal operator training are not theoretical; they are measurable, costly, and potentially fatal. The evidence presented demonstrates that operator specialization in EP is among the most powerful independent predictors of procedural safety and long-term outcomes and can be as important as institutional volume in many analyses. We call upon hospital credentialing committees, national medical societies, payers, regulatory bodies, and policymakers worldwide to establish and enforce a definitive standard: only trained CCEPs should implant and manage cardiac implantable electronic devices, perform catheter ablation procedures, execute transvenous lead extraction, and conduct formal EP studies.

title: Objectively Measured Smartphone Use Is Associated With Worse Sleep Health Among Adolescents: The Stony Brook University MEDiA Study.
authorString: Mathew GM, Reichenberger DA, Rodriguez IR, Christakis DA, Hale L.

journal.title: The Journal of adolescent health : official publication of the Society for Adolescent Medicine

abstractText:
Purpose

Screen use among adolescents is ubiquitous and associated with poor sleep health. This study examined gender-specific associations between objectively measured smartphone use (including timing-specific and social-media-specific duration of use) and sleep health among a diverse national sample of adolescents.

Methods

Adolescents (n = 218; 13-18 years old) from across the U.S. were recruited online. Participants (50% F) survey-reported sociodemographic characteristics, sleep timing, and sleep quality, and then installed a passive sensing meter on their personal smartphones (iOS or Android) for ≥3 days (M = 17.5) to objectively monitor smartphone activity, including app use, duration, and timing. Linear regression models assessed gender interactions in associations between timing- (i.e., 24-hour, evening 20:00-23:00, and nighttime 23:00-6:00) and category- (i.e., all-app or social media) specific smartphone use (hours/day) with nighttime sleep onset time, sleep duration, sleep quality, and sleep variability (social jetlag and free night catchup sleep), adjusting for sociodemographic and smartphone characteristics.

Results

Greater smartphone use was associated with later sleep onset time (b = 0.13-1.78 hours, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.07, 0.19-1.06, 2.51, β = 0.27-0.52), shorter sleep duration (b = -1.38 to -0.17 hours, 95% CI = -2.08, -0.72 to -0.25, -0.09, β = -0.48 to -0.36), more social jetlag (b = 0.06-0.43 hours, 95% CI = 0.01, 0.10-0.22, 0.64, β = 0.15-0.29), and longer free night catch-up sleep (b = 0.09-0.88 hours, 95% CI = 0.02, 0.17-0.38, 1.50, β = 0.16-0.29), with the strongest associations for evening, nighttime, and social media use. Several associations with sleep onset time and duration were stronger among females.

Discussion

The association between objectively assessed smartphone use and sleep health differs depending on timing and type of use and gender. Interventions to improve sleep health should consider aiming to reduce screen time around and after bedtime and social media specifically, which may especially benefit females.

title: S100A7 promotes orthodontic tooth movement by enhancing osteoclastogenesis via the receptor for advanced glycation end products.
authorString: Wu S, Sun X, Xu H, Yang F, Zhang H, Yan B.

journal.title: American journal of orthodontics and dentofacial orthopedics : official publication of the American Association of Orthodontists, its constituent societies, and the American Board of Orthodontics

abstractText:
Introduction

Orthodontic tooth movement (OTM) requires coordinated remodeling of the periodontal ligament (PDL) and alveolar bone, but clinically relevant molecular regulators remain incompletely defined. We investigated damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) in human PDL and the mechanism by which a candidate DAMP regulates OTM.

Methods

PDL from premolars exposed or not exposed to 7 days of orthodontic force underwent tandem mass tag-based proteomics. Candidate expression was validated by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction, and immunohistochemistry. Wild-type and mS100a7a15-knockout mouse OTM models, local mS100a7a15 administration, and primary murine osteoclast assays were used to assess function and mechanism.

Results

S100A7 was upregulated in force-loaded human PDL and peaked at day 7; its murine homolog, mS100a7a15, showed a similar pattern and was enriched on the compression side. mS100a7a15 deficiency reduced osteoclastogenesis, alveolar bone resorption, and OTM. Recombinant mS100a7a15 enhanced receptor activator of nuclear factor κB (NF-κB) ligand-induced osteoclast differentiation, ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme E2 N (UBE2N) expression, tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factor 6 (TRAF6) ubiquitination, and NF-κB activation. Receptor for advanced glycation end products antagonism attenuated NF-κB activation and osteoclastogenesis, whereas Ube2n knockdown reduced TRAF6 ubiquitination and osteoclast differentiation. Local mS100a7a15 administration accelerated OTM without further reducing distal alveolar bone height in the 7-day model.

Conclusions

S100A7 promotes osteoclast-mediated OTM through the receptor for advanced glycation end products, UBE2N, TRAF6, and NF-κB axis. This pathway may provide a target for modulating orthodontic treatment rate, although long-term periodontal and root safety requires evaluation.

title: Artificial intelligence in cardiology for non-experts: decoding key terms and understanding machine learning methodologies. A Scientific Statement of the ESC Working Group on e-Cardiology, the European Heart Rhythm Association (EHRA), the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care (ACVC), the Heart Failure Association (HFA), the European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging (EACVI), the European Association of Preventive Cardiology (EAPC), and the European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions (EAPCI) of the ESC, the ESC Regulatory Affairs Committee, and the ESC Digital Cardiology and Artificial Intelligence Committee.
authorString: De Lucia R, Cluitmans M, Ramírez J, Kolossváry M, Climent AM, Millet J, Parollo M, Tubaro M, Volterrani M, Dendale P, D'Ascenzo F, Szymański P, Jensen MT, Dilaveris P, Bernardino G, Duncker D, Rienstra M, Vidal-Perez R, Locati ET, Treskes R, Schuuring M, Vitale C, Aung N, Leeson P, Busnatu S, Koltowski L, Casado-Arroyo R.
abstractText: Evidence-based medicine represents the systematic approach through which physicians today use the best available scientific evidence from clinical research to guide their clinical decision-making process. However, the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI), with its diverse models and potential applications in medicine, is leading to a new form of research driven by 'big data' and heterogeneous datasets, extending beyond conventional statistical analysis and thereby making AI literacy an increasingly essential competence for clinicians. Artificial intelligence applications in cardiology have shown potential to support disease diagnosis, risk prediction, workflow efficiency, and therapeutic decision-making. However, despite these opportunities, AI may also represent a technological barrier for many physicians, due to its mathematical foundations and the speed at which models evolve. A solid understanding of AI concepts is therefore necessary for cardiologists to critically interpret results and engage with this new research landscape. This scientific statement explores AI in cardiology from an educational perspective, outlining the key knowledge required to build adequate AI literacy. The goal is to enable cardiologists not only to avoid reliance on external experts for methodological decisions, but also to collaborate with greater insight and informed judgment.

title: Unexplained Optic Neuritis and New Heart Block: A Diagnostically Challenging Case of Probable Sarcoidosis.
authorString: Kamath C, Al-Qaysi G, Paudel H, Saado J, Nwaonu J.
abstractText: Sarcoidosis is a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown etiology and manifests in multiple forms. It can affect several organs within the body; however, the lungs and intra-thoracic lymph nodes are involved in the majority of cases. Diagnosis can be challenging due to the diversity of presentation and similarities to other systemic diseases. Although biopsy is often used to confirm the diagnosis, areas of disease involvement can be difficult to access. This case involves a patient with 2 years of unexplained recurrent optic neuritis who presented to the emergency room with a new third-degree heart block. Her optic neuritis had previously responded to high-dose prednisone, but she was unable to achieve steroid-sparing disease control with the addition of rituximab despite receiving it for over a year. Imaging identified areas of nervous system and cardiac inflammation. She had elevated inflammatory markers and soluble IL-2 receptor level suspicious for systemic inflammation. Extensive evaluation for infection and other autoimmune disease was negative. A subsequent PET/CT scan was eventually able to identify lymph node involvement. Probable sarcoidosis remained the leading differential, and a bronchoscopy with endobronchial biopsy was performed 2 weeks later. Unfortunately, the yield was insufficient due to immunosuppression from ongoing steroid use. The patient was able to achieve remission after methotrexate and infliximab were added to her prednisone. Her steroids were tapered off without recurrence of disease activity. High-grade heart block is a well-established manifestation of cardiac sarcoidosis. However, the preceding unexplained optic neuritis in the absence of typical pulmonary involvement or histological confirmation complicated the diagnosis of sarcoidosis. This case highlights the importance of considering sarcoidosis in the differential of multisystemic inflammatory disease and the challenges associated with its diagnosis.

title: Recent advances of 4CzIPN in visible-light-mediated ring-formation reactions towards <i>N</i>-heterocycles.
authorString: Manod M, Roy J, H G, Vijayakumar A, Mohan C.
abstractText: Nitrogen-containing heterocyclic compounds are prevalent and play important roles across various fields, including medicine, natural products, agrochemicals, pharmaceuticals, and organometallic chemistry. The ongoing demand for novel techniques to synthesize these compounds has led to the growing popularity of ring-formation reactions, which enhance synthetic efficiency by enabling the simultaneous formation of multiple rings in a single transformation. Recently, visible-light-mediated photoredox catalysis has attracted attention for its clean and efficient approach, particularly in the context of green chemistry. Transition metal-free photoredox catalysis has emerged as a promising area, with the organophotocatalyst 4CzIPN standing out for its excellent redox potential, strong stability, and cost-effectiveness, which make it versatile for various applications. Despite the growing field of research on visible-light photoredox methods and the use of 4CzIPN, there is a lack of comprehensive analysis regarding its role in ring-formation reactions for synthesizing N-heterocycles. This review aims to fill that gap by summarizing recent advancements in 4CzIPN-catalyzed ring-formation reactions from 2020 to the present. It will provide a mechanistic overview, discuss the advantages and disadvantages of various synthetic protocols, and explore new opportunities for sustainable methods to create structurally diverse N-heterocycles. The review is organized into seven sections based on the structural formation of N-heterocycles, including the synthesis of oxindoles, quinolinones/quinolines/isoquinolines, quinazolinones/fused quinazolinones, phenanthridines, indoles/pyrrolo[1,2-a]indoles, indole[2,1-a]isoquinolinones/benzimidazo[2,1-a]isoquinolinones, and miscellaneous compounds.

title: Time From Anaesthetic Start to Surgery Start in Hysteroscopy and Theatre List Overrun in Gynaecology: A Retrospective Observational Study.
authorString: Alhusban F, Al Ajlouni Y, Bashall A, Clabon L, Roche C.
abstractText: Background We evaluated patient-level factors associated with the interval from anaesthetic start to surgery start in hysteroscopy and list-level factors associated with overrun in elective gynaecology lists. Methods This retrospective observational study used 2025 nursing pre-assessment and theatre timing records from two hospitals within one National Health Service (NHS) trust. Duration was analysed using a lognormal mixed model with a theatre-list random intercept, adjusting for recorded pre-assessment characteristics, session, site, and mixed-list status. Body mass index (BMI) was modelled using a four-knot restricted cubic spline. Adjusted mean differences were reported in minutes. Secondary analyses used mixed-effects logistic regression for intervals ≥22 minutes and multivariable logistic regression for list overrun, defined as last-patient departure after the scheduled finish. Sensitivity analyses examined untransformed duration and excluded all-day lists. Results Among 913 hysteroscopies, 890 cases across 491 theatre lists were included in adjusted analyses. BMI was nonlinearly associated with duration (overall p<0.001; nonlinearity p=0.007). Compared with BMI 30 kg/m², adjusted mean intervals were 1.42 minutes longer (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.46-2.43) at 40 kg/m² and 4.67 minutes longer (95% CI 2.56-6.90) at 50 kg/m². These contrasts were similar in sensitivity analyses. Among 611 gynaecology lists, 302 (49.4%) overran. Lists combining minor and major procedures had higher odds of overrun than lists containing only minor procedures (adjusted odds ratio (OR) 3.10; 95% CI 2.00-4.80). Afternoon lists had lower odds than morning lists (OR 0.23; 95% CI 0.15-0.34), while odds were higher at University Hospital Lewisham than Queen Elizabeth Hospital (OR 2.18; 95% CI 1.49-3.20). Lists in which at least half of minor cases had prolonged intervals also had higher odds of overrun (OR 1.52; 95% CI 1.04-2.23), but evidence for this association was less certain after excluding all-day lists (OR 1.40; 95% CI 0.92-2.11). Conclusions Higher BMI was associated with longer intervals from anaesthetic start to surgery start in hysteroscopy. Lists combining minor and major procedures had higher odds of overrun. Prospective studies should evaluate whether accounting for preparation requirements and list composition improves scheduling. These findings do not establish a BMI threshold or booking rule.

title: Identifying Clinical Issues for a Modified Delphi-Based Clinical Guideline on Diagnosis and Treatment of Vertigo/Dizziness in Children: Chinese Practice.
authorString: Wang W, Zhang SL, Duan ML, Zhang J, Jin YL, Yang J.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: World J Otorhinolaryngol Head Neck Surg
journal.title: World journal of otorhinolaryngology - head and neck surgery
journal.isoabbreviation: World J Otorhinolaryngol Head Neck Surg

abstractText:
Objective

The aim was to use a modified Delphi procedure to identify clinical issues to be included in the guidelines on diagnosis and treatment of vertigo/dizziness in children based on Chinese practice.

Methods

Sixty-five experts in the field of childhood dizziness were invited to participate in two-round surveys. The first-round survey (Survey One) was used to collect as many clinical issues as possible. The second-round survey (Survey Two) required the experts to rate the importance of the issues. The final confirmation of the identified clinical issues was completed via a core expert panel voting.

Results

Over 90% of experts responded to both rounds. After Survey One, 27 clinical issues were presented to the expert panel for importance rating in Survey Two. According to the modified Delphi inclusion criteria, 19 clinical issues were selected after the two rounds. In the core expert panel voting session, 12 clinical issues (8 diagnostic issues and 4 treatment issues) were finally identified.

Conclusion

A Chinese expert panel reached consensus on 12 clinical issues that warrant further investigation in the under-researched area of diagnosis and treatment of vertigo/dizziness in children based on Chinese practice.

title: Profound Hyperbilirubinemia During Severe Carbon Monoxide Poisoning and Subsequent Multiorgan Failure: A Case Report.
authorString: Joma M, Zahran A, Karam A, Sawaf B, Sayeh W, Sodeman T, Alastal Y.
abstractText: Carbon monoxide poisoning is classically associated with neurologic and cardiovascular toxicity, while severe exposure may also cause systemic toxic-hypoxic injury. Profound direct-predominant hyperbilirubinemia without mechanical biliary obstruction is rarely described. We report a 55-year-old woman with alcohol use disorder, chronic tobacco use, COPD, and hepatic steatosis who presented with altered mental status and jaundice after suspected household carbon monoxide exposure. Her carboxyhemoglobin level was > 30%, and she required intubation, intensive care, vasopressor support, and three hyperbaric oxygen treatments. Initial testing showed total bilirubin of 23.1 mg/dL and direct bilirubin of 13.1 mg/dL, despite only mild AST elevation and near-normal ALT and alkaline phosphatase. Imaging showed hepatic steatosis and cholelithiasis without convincing biliary obstruction, and the documented workup for viral, autoimmune, metabolic, hemolytic, and vascular causes was unrevealing. Her liver dysfunction was considered multifactorial, with possible carbon monoxide-related toxic-hypoxic injury superimposed on underlying steatotic or alcohol-related liver vulnerability. After transient improvement, she developed coagulopathy, acute kidney injury, recurrent shock with clinical and imaging concern for acute cholecystitis, worsening hyperbilirubinemia peaking near 49-50 mg/dL, encephalopathy, respiratory failure, and multiorgan failure. Cholecystostomy yielded dark green bile without documented purulence, and aspirate cultures showed no growth; biliary sepsis was therefore not microbiologically confirmed. She died in the hospital after goals-of-care discussions. The initial bilirubin-predominant pattern was atypical for classic hypoxic hepatitis and may have reflected overlapping hepatic insults. This case emphasizes broad evaluation and cautious causal interpretation; it does not establish that carbon monoxide exposure alone caused the initial hyperbilirubinemia.

title: Neonatal compressive goiter as the initial presentation of thyroid hormone resistance with dual THRB and TSHR mutations.
authorString: Dubois S, Savagner F, Heneau A, Azar-Kolakez A, Al-Amir I, Carel JC.
abstractText: Resistance to thyroid hormones (RTH) is a rare disorder mostly caused by mutations in the thyroid hormone receptor β gene (THRB). It typically presents in late childhood or adulthood with elevated free thyroid hormone levels, inappropriately normal or high thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), and goiter. We report a case of RTH associated with a compressive neonatal goiter. A preterm newborn presented with respiratory distress due to a large goiter (9.7 mL; normal, <1.53 mL) requiring mechanical ventilation, as well as supraventricular tachycardia. His thyroid hormone profile was consistent with RTH: TSH, 73.8 mIU/L (normal range [NR], 1.5-15.6 mIU/L); free T4, 77.1 pmol/L (59.9 pg/mL; NR, 11.6-36 pmol/L [9.0-28.0 pg/mL]), and free T3, >30 pmol/L (>19.5 pg/mL; NR, 3.5-7.8 pmol/L [2.3-5.1 pg/mL]). Genetic testing and functional analyses identified a de novo heterozygous THRB nonsense mutation and an inherited heterozygous missense activating mutation in the TSHR gene. Treatment with tiratricol reduced TSH levels and goiter size, allowing extubation after 17 days. At 4 years, the patient remains stable on tiratricol. We conclude that the activating TSH receptor mutation is responsible for the neonatal compressive goiter in the context of a loss of function in THRB.

title: Sex-Stratified Transcriptomic Analysis of Cord-Blood Endothelial Colony-Forming Cells from Pregnancies Complicated by Gestational Diabetes.
authorString: Adegbaju MS, Babayeju O, Morenikeji OB, Ojurongbe O, Thomas BN.
abstractText: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and maternal obesity are intrauterine metabolic exposures associated with altered fetal development and increased cardiovascular risk later in life. Increasing evidence suggests that fetal responses to these exposures are sex-dependent; however, the regulatory mechanisms underlying sex-specific vascular programming remain poorly understood. Using purified neonatal endothelial colony-forming cells (ECFCs), a progenitor population of fetal vasculature, we performed a sex-stratified transcriptomic analysis of pregnant mothers classified as lean, overweight, or GDM. Differential expression, pathway enrichment, transcription factor activity inference, kinase network reconstruction, and connectivity mapping were integrated to characterize sex-dependent regulatory responses to maternal metabolic dysfunction. Male and female ECFCs exhibited markedly divergent transcriptomic responses to GDM. Correlation between male and female fold-change estimates was negligible (r = -0.01), and the female-specific signal was not detectable when sex was modeled as a covariate rather than as a stratifying variable. Female GDM-exposed ECFCs demonstrated coordinated enrichment of cell-cycle- and DNA replication-associated pathways together with recurrent prioritization of E2F-family regulators across multiple analytical approaches. In contrast, the male response was comparatively limited and was associated with distinct transcriptional changes, including AKT3-associated pathways. Notably, E2F1 transcript abundance remained relatively stable despite coordinated expression changes among E2F-associated target genes. Independent endothelial transcriptomic datasets, drawn from previously published findings rather than independent reanalysis, provided complementary biological context rather than direct validation, consistent with enrichment of E2F-associated programs in GDM-exposed ECFCs and greater transcriptional responsiveness in female endothelial cells reported elsewhere. These findings indicate that fetal sex is a major determinant of the endothelial progenitor response to maternal metabolic dysfunction and that biologically relevant signals may be obscured in pooled analyses. Our results support the existence of sex-dependent regulatory programs associated with fetal vascular responses to GDM and identify an E2F1-associated regulatory framework as a candidate mechanism warranting further investigation.

title: Delayed recognition of primary thyroid lymphoma with progressive thyroid enlargement and cardiopulmonary symptoms.
authorString: Tovar YE, Elsayed AG, Pragani M, Romanoski PT, Kaur R, Jun JY.
abstractText: Primary thyroid lymphoma (PTL) is a rare thyroid malignancy that may present with respiratory symptoms overlapping with cardiopulmonary disease, contributing to delayed diagnosis. We report a 78-year-old woman with chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, heart failure, and prior lung cancer whose worsening dyspnea was repeatedly attributed to underlying cardiopulmonary conditions. She subsequently developed dysphonia and dysphagia with a rapidly enlarging thyroid mass requiring tracheostomy for airway protection. Prior computed tomography imaging obtained during multiple evaluations for cardiopulmonary symptoms incidentally demonstrated subtle thyroid enlargement with progressive interval growth on retrospective review. Core biopsy confirmed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, and staging established stage IIIE disease. Given her age and comorbidities, a dose-reduced regimen of rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone was initiated. Despite treatment, her condition deteriorated rapidly, and she died shortly thereafter. This case underscores how overlapping comorbidities can obscure PTL presentation until advanced airway compromise develops. In patients with persistent respiratory symptoms despite appropriate cardiopulmonary management, careful review of prior imaging is critical because subtle thyroid enlargement may otherwise be overlooked.

title: Analysis of reproductive traits associated with lipoprotein(a) deficiency in participants from the Pakistan Genome Resource
authorString: Koch C, Dominy JE, Gurtan AM, Khan MZ, Khalid S, Timsit YE, Casas JP, Hache C, Xu H, Mendelson MM, Jones I, Goldfine AB, Saleheen D.
abstractText:
Aims

Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined, independent risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, driving development of LPA-targeting therapies that markedly lower circulating Lp(a). Because LPA —the gene encoding apolipoprotein(a)—is absent in most model organisms, preclinical studies have limited value for assessing effects such as reproductive safety. Therefore, naturally occurring human LPA “knockouts” were analyzed to evaluate reproductive outcomes of on-target Lp(a) lowering.

Methods and Results

Individuals carrying high-confidence LPA loss-of-function (LoF) variants which reduce Lp(a) in a gene-dosage–dependent manner within the Pakistan Genome Resource were identified. LoF variants showed no depletion of homozygotes relative to Hardy–Weinberg expectations. LPA LoF associations with fertility-related traits (ever having a child and number of children) under additive and recessive models were assessed using regenie-based burden testing, including sex-stratified analyses, and no significant associations were observed. A recall-by-genotype study of female LoF homozygotes alongside heterozygous and non-carrier family member controls was performed, surveying reproductive histories and offspring outcomes. Across 107 pregnancies and 87 children in 19 homozygous LoF women, rates of miscarriage, maternal complications (including preeclampsia, hypertension, and gestational diabetes), delivery complications, neonatal intensive care admission, birth defects, and child health problems were comparable across genotypes with no statistically significant genotype–outcome associations.

Conclusions

These genetic and by-genotype analyses indicate that complete lifelong LPA deficiency due to high-confidence LPA loss-of-function variants is not associated with overt adverse maternal fertility, pregnancy or child health outcomes. These findings offer human genetic reassurance regarding reproductive and developmental safety in the context of sustained Lp(a)-lowering, with implications for long-term therapies targeting Lp(a).

Translational Perspective

Despite advances in clinical management of atherosclerosis, cardiovascular event rates remain high and novel therapeutic approaches to reduce residual risk are needed. Lp(a) is an independent, genetic risk factor for atherosclerosis. Lp(a)-lowering therapies are under development. Prior to marketing reproductive safety is typically evaluated. However, rodents do not express apolipoprotein(a), the unique Lp(a) structural protein, rendering them unsuitable for evaluating on-target reproductive safety. This human genetics study provides evidence that lifelong, complete LPA deficiency caused by naturally occurring loss-of-function variants is not associated with reduced fertility, adverse pregnancy outcomes, congenital abnormalities, or impaired child health. These findings provide human genetic support for reproductive and developmental safety of chronic Lp(a)-lowering therapies and the approach may inform evaluations of other therapeutic targets.

title: Routine CBC-Derived Markers of Systemic Inflammation Are Associated With Growth of the Dilated Ascending Aorta During CT Surveillance
authorString: Murad B, Campello Jorge CA, George G, Queiroz Costa Neto I, Karnam Y, Spahlinger G, Hofmann Bowman M, Burris NS.
abstractText:
Background

Ascending aortic surveillance relies on diameter thresholds, yet most dissections occur below them. Inflammation drives aortic wall remodeling independent of diameter. Inflammation drives aortic wall remodeling independent of diameter. Inflammatory indices derived from routine blood counts, such as neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), red cell distribution width (RDW), and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) have been show to predict adverse cardiovascular outcomes, but their association with ascending aortic growth is unclear.

Methods and Results

We retrospectively studied adults with ≥2 computed tomography (CT) scans of the native ascending aorta ≥6 months apart at a single center (2000–2023), excluding those with aortitis or no complete blood count during follow-up. Markers were summarized as 95th percentile values per patient and per scan interval. Growth was defined as a ≥2-mm increase in mid-ascending aortic diameter. Patient-level logistic regression and interval-level generalized estimating equation models were adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, baseline diameter, systolic blood pressure, diabetes, and heritable thoracic aortic disease. Among 3,262 patients, data were available in 1,882 for RDW, 1,471 for NLR, and 1,468 for SII; 192 (10.2%) met criteria for growth. Only RDW was independently associated with growth in the overall cohort (patient level: odds ratio [OR] 1.071, 95% CI 1.002–1.144, p=0.043; interval level: OR 1.075, 95% CI 1.012–1.141, p=0.019); NLR (p=0.080) and SII (p=0.164) were not. Among patients with guideline-defined ascending aortic dilation (≥40 mm), all three markers were associated with interval growth (RDW OR 1.14, NLR OR 1.05, SII OR 1.01 per 100 units; all p≤0.014), whereas none were among aortas <40 mm; effect modification was significant for NLR (p=0.01).

Conclusions

RDW was modestly associated with ascending aortic growth overall, and all three markers were associated with interval growth in patients with guideline-defined aortic dilation, suggesting that systemic inflammation may contribute to progression of aortic dilation. Prospective studies with more specific inflammatory markers are needed.

Clinical Perspective

What Is New?

Among 1,882 patients undergoing serial computed tomography surveillance, higher red cell distribution width was modestly but independently associated with ascending aortic growth, whereas the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio and systemic immune-inflammation index were not associated with growth in the overall cohort. In patients with guideline-defined ascending aortic dilation (≥40 mm), all three inflammatory markers were associated with growth across surveillance intervals, a signal not seen in nondilated aortas.

What Are the Clinical Implications?

Routine blood count markers of inflammation may carry information about disease activity in patients under surveillance for ascending aortic dilation, although effect sizes are too modest for standalone risk stratification. Prospective studies with standardized inflammatory panels obtained at fixed surveillance intervals are needed to test whether inflammation identifies patients with dilated aortas who are at risk of growth.

title: EXPRESS: Associations of the triglyceride/HDL-cholesterol ratio and triglyceride-glucose index with malnutrition risk and other geriatric parameters in older adults: a retrospective cross-sectional study.
authorString: Cicek O, Yilmaz Kars M, Akkar I, Turgut ZI, Dogan MH, Kizilarslanoglu MC.

journal.title: Journal of investigative medicine : the official publication of the American Federation for Clinical Research

abstractText:
Background/objectives

This study aimed to investigate the association of the triglyceride/HDL-cholesterol ratio (THR) and the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index with malnutrition risk and other geriatric parameters among patients attending a geriatric outpatient clinic.

Methods

A total of 355 patients aged ≥65 years who presented to the geriatric outpatient clinic and completed a comprehensive geriatric assessment (CGA) were retrospectively evaluated in this study. Patients were divided into tertiles according to THR and TyG values. Mini Nutritional Assessment-Short Form (MNA-SF) and CGA parameters were recorded and compared between groups. Malnutrition risk was defined as MNA-SF <12.

Results

The median age of patients was 79 years (59.7% female). Regarding comorbidities, TyG and THR values were higher in the presence of diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease, and malignancy (all p<0.05). In unadjusted analyses, gait speed was positively correlated with both TyG and THR (both p<0.05). Higher THR and TyG values were correlated with higher MNA-SF scores, and MNA-SF score remained associated with both indices in multivariable linear regression analyses. In binary logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, and diabetes, both indices were associated with malnutrition risk (MNA-SF <12; present in 69.6% of patients) and with impaired Timed Up and Go test performance; the association with malnutrition risk persisted after additional adjustment for basic activities of daily living, instrumental activities of daily living, depression, and comorbidity burden, in which higher THR was also associated with higher odds of Clinical Frailty Scale >4. After multiple-testing correction, only the association of THR with malnutrition risk remained significant. THR and TyG had limited discriminative power for malnutrition risk (area under the curve 0.601 [95% CI 0.535-0.667] and 0.592 [95% CI 0.526-0.659], respectively).

Conclusion

Within the observed range, higher THR and TyG values were associated with lower malnutrition risk in older outpatients. Because their discriminative power is limited, these indices should not be considered independent screening or diagnostic tools; reverse causality cannot be excluded, and prospective studies are needed.

title: Active Learning and Cascaded nnU-Net v2 for Multi-structure Segmentation of Thoracic CT: A Single-Center Pilot Study.
authorString: Ham S, Hwang I, Kim C, Hwang J.

journal.title: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

abstractText: Accurate segmentation of thoracic structures on chest computed tomography (CT) is important for lung cancer surgery, but manual annotation is labor intensive and particularly challenging for small structures such as pulmonary vessels and nodules. We compared four nnU-Net v2-based segmentation configurations: single-stage full-data training, active learning alone, cascaded segmentation alone, and active learning combined with cascaded segmentation in a retrospective single-center cohort. This retrospective study included chest CT scans from 85 patients. In the cascaded configurations, pulmonary lobes were segmented in the first stage to provide global anatomical context, followed by refinement of the bronchus, pulmonary vessels, and nodules within the constrained region. All four configurations were evaluated using the same fixed patient-level internal test set of 30 patients, with segmentation performance assessed using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and the 95th percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95). The full-data baseline achieved DSCs of 0.92-0.93 for the five pulmonary lobes, with lower performance for the bronchus (0.82), pulmonary vessels (0.67), and pulmonary nodules (0.78). The combined active learning and cascaded configuration improved lobar DSCs to 0.94-0.96. Compared with the baseline, DSC increased to 0.90, 0.77, and 0.86 for the bronchus, pulmonary vessels, and pulmonary nodules, respectively (all p < 0.05), while HD95 decreased from 5.4 to 2.5 mm for pulmonary vessels and from 4.8 to 2.1 mm for pulmonary nodules. In this single-center cohort, cascaded segmentation strategies showed improved internal test performance for small thoracic structures, supporting further evaluation in larger multicenter cohorts.

title: Pregestational maternal diabetes primes neonatal beta cell dysfunction with structural remodelling, impaired calcium buffering and altered mTORC2-Gαq-PKCα signalling in a pig model.
authorString: Valla L, Schwager MF, Cohrs CM, Stoeckl JB, Karampelias C, Shashikadze B, Rathkolb B, Lindner R, Kraetzl M, Renner S, van den Bosch MM, Yang K, Sterr M, Böttcher A, Hrabě de Angelis M, Speier S, Fröhlich T, Theis FJ, Lickert H, Wolf E, Kemter E.
abstractText:
Aims/hypothesis

Offspring of mothers with diabetes are at increased risk of developing type 2 diabetes, and this predisposition is established during fetal life. The aim of this study was to define the functional, morphological and molecular alterations in neonatal pancreatic islets associated with maternal hyperglycaemia, with a particular focus on beta cells, an area that remains poorly understood. Given its similarity to humans in endocrine pancreas development, the pig was used as a translational animal model.

Methods

Using genetically diabetic and beta cell reporter pig models, we performed functional assessments of glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in vivo and in situ using fresh pancreatic tissue slices from neonatal piglets born to hyperglycaemic mothers (PHGs) or normoglycaemic mothers (PNGs). Morphological and molecular profiling, including proteomics and single-cell RNA-seq, were performed to elucidate molecular changes reflecting the developmental impact of maternal diabetes on offspring metabolic health, with a particular focus on neonatal beta cells.

Results

PHGs were born hyperglycaemic, hyperinsulinaemic and insulin resistant, exhibiting markedly delayed glucose and insulin response curves following oral glucose administration, with more pronounced effects in male piglets. Elevated basal insulin secretion and an almost blunted glucose responsiveness of pancreatic tissue slices were associated with increased insulin and somatostatin content, expansion of beta (+35%) and delta (+47%) cell populations, and organisation into larger islet clusters. Neonatal PHG islets exhibited a molecular profile consistent with intrinsic beta cell dysfunction that partially overlapped with type 2 diabetes (e.g. RBP4 upregulation), together with alterations in glucose sensing (near absence of GLUT2), nutrient metabolism resembling congenital hyperinsulinism (HADH downregulation), and cytosolic Ca2⁺ homeostasis (near absence of the Ca2⁺ buffer calbindin D28K). In addition to an ATF4-dominated stress signature, a shift towards a distinct PHG beta cell subcluster characterised by low expression of ribosomal genes was observed, with an adaptive early-response-gene-mediated transcriptional reactivity. In contrast to the Gαs-adenylyl cyclase-cAMP-PKA signalling axis that dominated in PNG beta cells, neonatal PHG beta cells displayed distinct alterations in Gαq-PLC-PKCα signalling components, the mTORC2 target PKCα, and CREB1, suggesting a restructured signalling architecture.

Conclusions/interpretation

Our findings reveal altered islet modelling with a unique beta cell dysfunction profile that partially overlaps with, but differs from, that of type 2 diabetes. A shift towards a beta cell subcluster exhibiting an adaptive early-response-gene-mediated transcriptional reactivity and an ATF4-associated transcriptional stress signature provides insight into molecular alterations associated with fetal exposure to maternal diabetes and may contribute to the increased risk of metabolic disease in offspring.

title: DGKE acts as a negative regulator of podocyte migration and injury in glomerular diseases.
authorString: Zuo F, Wang M, Du J, Wang X, Ding P, Han Q, Liu X, Tang W, Sun Y, Zhang Y, Wang X, Liu M, Wu J, Zhang X, Yu J, Wang Z, Yi F.
abstractText: Podocyte injury is a major determinant of glomerular diseases. Although considerable advances have been made in the understanding of the mechanisms that trigger podocyte injury, effective cell-specific therapies remain clinically unavailable. In particular, recent studies have revealed that podocyte adhesion dysfunction and aberrant migration are pivotal events in the pathogenesis of podocyte loss and injury. Therefore, identifying candidate pathways for therapeutic intervention in podocyte migration has significant clinical importance. Here, we found that diacylglycerol kinase epsilon (DGKE) expression level is reduced in kidney biopsies from patients with glomerular diseases, which correlates with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Moreover, urinary migrasome levels, a marker of migration, were significantly elevated in patients and negatively correlated with DGKE levels. Podocyte-specific overexpression of DGKE attenuated podocyte injury and proteinuria in three independent mouse models, adriamycin (ADR)-, puromycin aminonucleoside (PAN)- and streptozotocin plus high-fat diet (STZ/HFD)-induced nephropathy. Mechanistically, DGKE regulates podocyte migration through the urokinase plasminogen activator receptor (uPAR)/β3 integrin axis and its downstream Rac1/Cdc42 signaling cascades. Collectively, our findings provide new insights into the pivotal role of DGKE in maintaining podocyte function and suggest that DGKE may represent a potential therapeutic target for treating patients with glomerular diseases.

title: Applicability of cognitive decline risk scores in a high socioeconomic preventive medicine cohort.
authorString: Julian A, Lepoittevin M, Balia M, Benani A, Mounier M, Salomon J, Bodard S.
abstractText: BackgroundValidated cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease risk scores (CAIDE, ANU-ADRI, LIBRA, LIBRA2) were developed in general-population cohorts; how they behave in the high-socioeconomic, health-selected populations typical of preventive-medicine programs and over-represented in ageing cohorts is undescribed.ObjectiveLacking a cognitive outcome, we did not test predictive validity but described score distributions, inter-score concordance, the components driving variance, and complementary biological data.MethodsFour scores were computed for 895 participants aged ≥45 years in the Zoī cohort, a self-referred, self-funded preventive-medicine sample. Concordance was assessed by Spearman correlations and, after dichotomization, by pairwise agreement (percentage agreement, Cohen's κ). Principal component analysis identified components accounting for most between-person variance. Complementary data (DEXA body composition, HbA1c, erythrocyte omega-3) were cross-tabulated with score-derived risk categories.ResultsConcordance was moderate (ρ = 0.39-0.60), and dichotomized categories were fairly-to-moderately concordant across families (Cohen's κ 0.33-0.52). Protective variables showed ceiling effects (education ≥10 years, 86%; social/cognitive activity, 100%), leaving cardiovascular factors (BMI, hypertension, coronary heart disease) to account for most variance. Despite 91% having normal BMI (≤30 kg/m<sup>2</sup>), DEXA-measured fat mass showed a dose-response gradient across all scores (CAIDE 4.36-6.26); HbA1c revealed a glycemic gradient invisible to self-reported diabetes.ConclusionsIn this high-socioeconomic cohort, the scores were moderately concordant and varied almost solely by cardiovascular components, protective factors being saturated. Whether this reflects uniformly low risk or reduced ability to separate individuals cannot be determined without a cognitive outcome. Complementary biological measurements added stratification, supporting augmented risk-assessment tools to be validated against cognitive endpoints.

title: Evaluation of PainWaive: a consumer-grade EEG headset for remote EEG monitoring and neurofeedback research in chronic pain.
authorString: Chowdhury NS, Rawsthorne J, Hesam-Shariati N, Quidé Y, Alexander L, Ermolenko E, McIntyre A, Restrepo S, Chen K, Lin CT, Newton-John T, Middleton JW, Craig A, Jensen MP, McAuley JH, Gustin SM.
abstractText: Affordable electroencephalography (EEG) headsets could widen access to EEG-based treatment and assessment, but require rigorous validation. We evaluated PainWaive, a custom-developed 2-channel central scalp EEG headset designed for remote EEG monitoring and neurofeedback research in chronic pain. Eighty participants completed two resting-state EEGs using PainWaive and a research-grade system (LiveAmp). Alpha, beta and theta power, and peak alpha frequency (PAF), were derived from homologous central channels. PainWaive demonstrated good-to-excellent test-retest reliability for alpha power and PAF (ICCs = 0.72-0.93), with beta and theta ranging from moderate-good (ICCs = 0.42-0.76). Across 160 home-based neurofeedback sessions in two chronic pain samples, reliability was good-to-excellent across metrics (ICCs = 0.72-0.88). Spectral-shape correlations between PainWaive and LiveAmp were excellent (r > 0.91). Cross-device agreement was moderate-to-good for alpha power and PAF (ICCs = 0.53-0.74), but weaker for beta and theta (ICCs = 0.16-0.51). Sensitivity analyses showed alpha power and PAF were robust across choices, whereas beta and theta agreement varied by pipeline. Overall, PainWaive demonstrated reliable measurement of central scalp EEG metrics, supporting repeated within-device monitoring. Cross-device findings showed correspondence with research-grade EEG for some measures but should not be interpreted as establishing direct numerical interchangeability between systems. These findings provide a technical foundation for future remote EEG and neurofeedback studies in chronic pain.

title: Sociodemographic and clinical factors associated with comorbid dementia in late-life difficult-to-treat depression: A cross-sectional study using electronic health records.
authorString: Mueller C, Orgeta V, von Gunten A, Vandel P, Ma R, Stewart R, Moyano BP.
abstractText:
Objectives

Late-life difficult-to-treat depression (LL-DTD) is associated with dementia, but the factors associated with comorbid dementia in this population remain unknown. We aimed to identify sociodemographic and clinical factors associated with comorbid dementia in LL-DTD.

Design & setting

Cross-sectional study using electronic mental health records from a south London mental healthcare provider.

Participants

Patients aged ≥ 60 years with a first recorded depressive episode between 2008 and 2023, meeting criteria for LL-DTD (n = 3886).

Measurements

LL-DTD was defined as ≥ 2 antidepressants prescribed or a natural language processing algorithm indicating treatment resistance. Dementia was ascertained using ICD-10 codes. Sociodemographic characteristics, depressive symptoms, and physical health conditions were ascertained from the electronic health record. Multivariable logistic regression was used. A sensitivity analysis restricted dementia to diagnoses recorded more than three months after the index episode.

Results

Of 3886 patients with LL-DTD, 890 (22.9%) had dementia. Older age, female sex, and Black and Asian ethnicity were associated with higher odds of dementia (aOR 1.07, 1.24, 1.83 and 1.73, respectively). Somatic multimorbidity, cardiovascular and cerebrovascular conditions were also associated with higher odds. Anxiety (aOR 1.66) and cognitive problems (aOR 3.98) showed positive associations, while severe or psychotic depression and several ICD-10/11 depressive symptoms showed negative associations. When restricted to dementia recorded after the index episode, the association with cognitive problems halved (aOR 1.93) and those with apathy and ADL problems were lost.

Conclusions

In our analysis, somatic multimorbidity, cardiovascular conditions and anxiety were associated with comorbid dementia in LL-DTD, supporting comprehensive physical and neuropsychiatric assessment.

title: Towards Contact-Free Cardiac Magnetic Resonance: Feasibility of Remote Photoplethysmography for Cardiac Triggering and Gating.
authorString: Doeblin DMP, Carrizosa K, Wuelbern JH, Stehning C, Weiss S, Werhahn SM, Eggers AS, Meuwly C, Köpcke N, Li JJ, Hilgendorf I, Kelle S.

journal.title: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance

abstractText:
Background

Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) sequences necessitate synchronisation with the cardiac cycle. This is routinely obtained through electrocardiographic (ECG) detection of the R-wave with subsequent triggering or gating of the acquisition, depending on the type of sequence. An accepted alternative is the use of transmissive photoplethysmography using a fingerclip (fPPG) to detect the peripheral pulse wave.

Objectives

To assess the feasibility of contact-free remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) for CMR triggering/gating.

Methods

In this prospective study (www.drks.de, DRKS00036686), CMR sequences were triggered/gated by ECG, fPPG and rPPG. The primary endpoint was trigger accuracy, measured by true positive rate (TPR), positive predictive value (PPV), beat detection error rate (BDER) and trigger-latency variability (TLV) in the rPPG and fPPG tracings compared to the ECG tracing. Secondary endpoints were technical success, image quality and quantitative CMR measurements of the acquired CMR sequences. Subsequently, the rPPG algorithm was adjusted to improve pulse wave detection in patients with skin type Fitzpatrick 5-6.

Results

64 subjects were included. rPPG initially provided comparable measures of trigger accuracy to fPPG, with worse performance in subjects with skin type Fitzpatrick 5-6. Adjusting the rPPG algorithm significantly improved trigger accuracy irrespective of skin type: BDER (%) for fPPG 8.5 (0.9-23.0), for rPPG 7.2 (0.3-49.1) and for the adjusted rPPG 1.3 (0.2-11.2). Image quality with both fPPG and rPPG were comparable to ECG. The differences observed in quantitative CMR measurements between fPPG, rPPG and ECG were in the order of inter-observer-variability.

Conclusions

Contact-free rPPG is a viable alternative to standard CMR triggering/gating using ECG or fPPG. Adjustment of our algorithm led to excellent trigger accuracy irrespective of skin type.

title: Esophageal Manometry is Needed for Accuracy in Selected Patients with Postcapillary Pulmonary Hypertension.
authorString: Tonelli AR.
abstractText: Both mean pulmonary artery (mPAP) and pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP) are essential determinations in the hemodynamic evaluation of patients undergoing a right heart catheterization. These pressure determinations are traditionally obtained at end-expiration and reflect the intramural pressure relative to the atmospheric pressure, but not the pressure distending the vessel wall which is the transmural pressure. In conditions in which the intrathoracic pressure is elevated, the intravascular pressure may overestimate the transmural pressure. A relatively simple way to estimate the transmural pressure is to measure the esophageal pressure (Pes). We previously shown that in patient with obesity, this correction decreased the number of patients diagnosed with postcapillary PH. Physicians need to consider the measurement of Pes in patients with increased mPAP and PAWP in the context of conditions known to be associated with high intrathoracic pressure and particularly when a potential increase in Pes may alter the management. As with other hemodynamic determinations, it is essential to understand the technique, limitations and potential errors in Pes measurement. Further research is needed to determine whether the measurement of Pes improves clinical decision-making or outcomes.

title: Anticipatory Cardiac Deceleration Is Related to Cautious Decision-Making after Threat Image Exposure.
authorString: Runkle L, Lauharatanahirun N, Cavigelli S, Spangler DP.
abstractText: Cautious decision-making can be an adaptive tendency in stressful environments and in certain individuals. We hypothesized that cautious decision-making is supported by anticipatory cardiac deceleration (ACD)- a brief cardiac slowing tied to preparation and action readiness. To test this hypothesis, we examined whether individuals with stronger ACD make more economically cautious choices after exposure to threat-depicting images. Participants (N = 97; 65% women, Mean age = 22.4 years) completed a threat priming decision-making task while electrocardiography was collected. To manipulate emotional contexts, every economic lottery choice was preceded by an affective image depicting a neutral, injury threat, or infection threat scene, and choice trials were presented in three separate blocks - one for each image type. Cardiac deceleration was assessed during 10-s countdown periods before each block. Results indicate that individuals with greater ACD before the infection threat block made more cautious choices after exposure to the infection threat images. This association was strongest when the infection block occurred last in the task sequence, i.e., when that image condition was more predictable. No significant relationships emerged for the other image conditions suggesting that anticipatory deceleration might only relate to behavioral caution in certain threat conditions. Results are consistent with the hypothesis that ACD is an autonomic correlate of preparation that is relevant to human performance and fear/anxiety theories.

title: Pregnancy-Induced Hypertension Complicated by Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome: A Case Series of Two Patients.
authorString: Zhao X, Yan M, Long F, Mumdzjans A, Song R.
abstractText: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) is a rare but potentially life-threatening neurological complication associated with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. This report presents two cases of pregnancy-induced hypertension complicated by PRES, both clinically characterized by headache and visual disturbances, with characteristic neuroimaging findings. The clinical manifestations, laboratory findings, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics of two patients are described. Following prompt multidisciplinary consultation and immediate interventions, including strict blood pressure control, seizure prophylaxis, infection prevention, and appropriate obstetric management, both patients achieved favorable clinical outcomes. No significant neurological abnormalities were observed at the 42-day postpartum follow-up. In patients with severe pregnancy-induced hypertension, PRES warrants recognition as a potential complication; management should prioritize rigorous blood pressure control, seizure prophylaxis, alleviation of pregnancy-related physiological stress, and timely neuroimaging to guide treatment, with strategies balancing maternal and fetal safety-early recognition and intervention underpinned by standardized protocols and multidisciplinary collaboration being critical to improving prognosis and reducing complications.

title: Differential recovery of macrophage iron deficiency by oral iron formulations determines inflammation and autocrine hepcidin production in iron-deficiency anemia.
authorString: Antypiuk A, Asperti M, Sharma R, Navaneethabalakrishnan S, Jhita N, Pearce Q, Cox JE, Brilli E, Tarantino G, Vinchi F.
abstractText: Exposure of macrophages to iron has been implicated in sterile inflammation through reactive oxygen species (ROS)-dependent cell pro-inflammatory activation. Here, we compare the effect of the commonly used oral iron salt, iron sulfate (FeSO4), with that of an innovative formulation, sucrosomial® iron (SI), on the iron status and inflammatory activation of tissue macrophages in mice with iron-deficiency (ID) anemia. Despite similar recovery of anemia and tissue ID, FeSO4 treatment, but not SI, elevated transferrin saturation, generated non-transferrin bound iron (NTBI), and quickly corrected macrophage ID compared to SI, with a more pronounced cell transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1) suppression and labile iron pool expansion. In both ex vivo and in vitro ID macrophages, the rapid kinetic of ID correction by FeSO4 was associated with increased ROS and inflammatory cytokine production, whereas these responses were minimally affected by the slower kinetic of SI uptake. Metabolome data suggest that FeSO4 but not SI suppressed lipid metabolism in macrophages, indicating reduced fatty acid β-oxidation and limited reliance on mitochondrial activity, metabolic hallmarks of cell inflammatory skewing. Ultimately, we demonstrate that FeSO4 drives a higher autocrine production of hepcidin compared to SI, via inflammatory cytokine-mediated activation of the STAT3 signaling pathway, further limiting macrophage iron recycling in ID. In conclusion, our data prove that the kinetic of macrophage ID correction by iron formulations determines cell inflammatory activation and modulates hepcidin production. Overall, SI appears a superior formulation than FeSO4 due to its reduced pro-oxidant potential, inflammatory action, and hepcidin induction, with relevance for ID treatment in individuals with pre-existing inflammatory conditions.

title: Cabozantinib Monotherapy for Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Involving Hemodialysis: Two Case Reports.
authorString: Nara T, Furihata K, Sato K, Sato T, Honma N, Horikawa Y, Shimoda N.
abstractText:
Introduction

Data on cabozantinib monotherapy for metastatic renal cell carcinoma in patients requiring hemodialysis are scarce. We present two cases: initiation before hemodialysis with subsequent continuation and initiation during maintenance hemodialysis.

Case presentation

Case 1 was a 77-year-old man with lung metastasis who received cabozantinib after multiple systemic therapies. Cabozantinib was started at 20 mg/day before hemodialysis; hemodialysis began 8 months later, and treatment continued for 59 months with tolerability-guided schedule modification. Case 2 was a 69-year-old man on maintenance hemodialysis who received cabozantinib 20 mg/day for lung and bone metastases. The schedule was changed to alternate-day dosing. Partial response was achieved, but treatment was discontinued after 4 months because of worsening general condition.

Conclusion

Cabozantinib was administered with individualized dose adjustment and careful monitoring; further clinical and pharmacokinetic data are needed to establish optimal dosing.

title: Central Adiposity and Tear Film Instability in Adults With Obesity.
authorString: Li A, Wu Y, Lin R, Wu Y, Nie Q, Tian L, Jie Y.
abstractText:
Purpose

To examine the association between central adiposity, assessed by waist-to-height ratio (WHtR), and tear film stability in adults with obesity.

Methods

This cross-sectional observational study included 269 adults with BMI ≥ 28 kg/m2. WHtR and noninvasive tear breakup time (NIBUT) were the primary exposure and outcome. Models adjusted for age, sex, education, systemic diseases, myopia, display exposure, smoking, alcohol consumption, and sleep problems. Secondary outcomes were Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI) and dry eye disease (DED) status; other adiposity indices were examined in separate models.

Results

Each 1-SD higher WHtR was associated with shorter NIBUT (adjusted β -0.341 s; 95% CI -0.612--0.071; p = 0.014). The highest versus lowest WHtR tertile differed by -0.961 s (95% CI -1.696--0.227). BMI had a numerically larger coefficient (-0.591 s; 95% CI -0.842--0.339). DED was present in 208 participants (77.3%). The WHtR-DED association was nominally significant (OR 1.630; 95% CI 1.072-2.477; p = 0.022) but did not survive false discovery rate correction (q = 0.061).

Conclusions

Higher WHtR was associated with modestly shorter NIBUT among adults with obesity, while BMI showed a numerically larger association. These findings support considering overall and abdominal adiposity in the clinical assessment of ocular surface function.

title: The elusive culprit: a renal neuroendocrine tumor unmasked by ectopic Cushing syndrome.
authorString: Denysova V, Yutkin V, Bel-Angе A, Atlan K, Solomonov E, Grozinsky-Glasberg S.
abstractText: The case provides insight into the diagnostics and management of ectopic Cushing syndrome caused by the ectopic adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) secretion by a primary renal neuroendocrine tumor (RenNET), an exceptionally rare cause of endogenous hypercortisolism.

title: Multimorbidity patterns and disease co-occurrence networks in older adults with diabetes: A national population-based network analysis.
authorString: Sun C, Mao L, Ji D, Si L, Zhang Y, Zhang X, Zhang L, Xie G, Xu X.

journal.title: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association

abstractText:
Aims

This study aimed to characterize multimorbidity patterns and disease co-occurrence networks among older adults with diabetes in China.

Materials

This cross-sectional study analysed data from older adults aged ≥65 years with diabetes from the 2018 Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey. Network and hierarchical clustering analyses were used to examine co-occurrence patterns among 17 chronic physical and mental conditions.

Results

A total of 1408 participants with diabetes were included, comprising 593 male participants (42.1%) and 815 female participants (57.9%). Overall, 91.6% of participants had ≥1 additional chronic condition, and 71.3% had ≥2 additional chronic conditions. Hypertension (75.5%), heart disease (36.7%) and affective disorder (33.7%) were the three most common conditions; the hypertension-heart disease combination was the leading comorbidity pair (31.75%). Arthritis ranked highest for strength, closeness and betweenness in the overall network; epilepsy also ranked highly for strength and betweenness, particularly among participants aged ≥75 years and in the central and western regions. Five comorbidity clusters emerged from hierarchical clustering, with centrality profiles differing by age, sex and region.

Conclusions

Our study indicated that multimorbidity burden was high among people with diabetes aged ≥65 years in China and was characterized by distinct network structures and clustering patterns.
