Arthritis and epilepsy showed high centrality in the comorbidity network, and network characteristics differed across age, sex and regional groups. These findings suggest that health management for older adults with diabetes should address not only common cardiometabolic conditions but also musculoskeletal, neurological and mental health problems.

title: An integrative roadmap for a new era of kidney replacement therapies.
authorString: Winkler MKH, Ash SR, Barraclough KA, Bluechel C, Ferrell N, Fissell W, Freedman BS, Gerritsen KGF, Hassan HA, Hentschel DM, Hestekin J, Hughes A, Johnson DG, Krendel M, Li Z, Locke JE, Montserrat N, Nishinakamura R, Plisiewicz A, Ratner BD, Roberts GV, Roy S, Sirich TL, Subramanya AR, Wasse H, Wiener S, Wieringa F, Wolf K, Himmelfarb J.
abstractText: Innovation in kidney replacement is entering a transformative era. Although precision medicine has driven major breakthroughs in disease-specific therapies, progress in translating next-generation kidney replacement strategies into practice has lagged. This updated Roadmap highlights a shift toward bold, integrative approaches that merge engineering, biology and patient-centred design. Emerging directions include reimagining filtration and tubular function through biomimetic membranes, cellular systems and organ-on-chip technologies, and simultaneously exploring microbiome modulation and sorbent-based strategies to reduce the uraemic toxin burden. Beyond improving survival, new solutions are being shaped by priorities of mobility, sustainability and quality of life, pointing toward wearable and implantable systems that move care beyond the clinic. Biologic frontiers such as xenotransplantation and stem cell regeneration are opening pathways to potentially curative therapies, although challenges in safety, equity and scalability remain. Central to these efforts is the need to embed patient perspectives and ensure that innovations align with lived experiences. This integrative approach calls for renewed investment, regulatory clarity and cross-sector collaboration to accelerate translation of advances into equitable therapies redefining the future of kidney health.

title: A Teleglaucoma Screening System for Individuals at Risk of Open-Angle Glaucoma: Long-Term Clinical Outcomes and Comparative Cost Analysis.
authorString: Olasagasti LG, Acera A, Medina JM, Pinar-Sueiro S, Paraiso T, Rodriguez-Agirretxe I.
abstractText:
Purpose

To evaluate the clinical effectiveness and economic impact of a teleglaucoma screening program for individuals at increased risk of developing open-angle glaucoma (OAG).

Design

Prospective cohort study with retrospective evaluation of long-term clinical outcomes and comparative cost analysis.

Participants

Consecutive individuals with risk factors for OAG enrolled in a teleglaucoma screening program between 2020 and 2022.

Methods

A targeted teleglaucoma screening program was implemented within the Donostialdea Integrated Healthcare Organization (Gipuzkoa, Spain). Consecutive individuals with risk factors for OAG were included. The teleglaucoma assessment included best-corrected visual acuity, non-contact tonometry, pachymetry, and peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer optical coherence tomography (pRNFL-OCT), performed by an optometrist and reviewed asynchronously by glaucoma specialists. Findings consistent with glaucoma or suspicious for glaucoma were considered positive screening results, whereas ocular hypertension (OHT) or the absence of abnormalities were considered negative screening results. Clinical effectiveness was evaluated through analysis of glaucoma-related diagnoses recorded using ICD-10 codes during a five-year follow-up period. A comparative cost analysis was conducted from a societal perspective. Patient satisfaction was assessed using the Client Satisfaction Questionnaire (CSQ-8).

Main outcomes measures

Agreement between teleglaucoma classifications and glaucoma-related ICD-10 diagnoses recorded during follow-up, diagnostic performance indicators, patient satisfaction, and costs.

Results

A total of 1,112 patients were included (mean age 60.2 years), of whom 63.1% were women. Positive screening results were identified in 8.2% of participants. Overall agreement between the teleglaucoma assessment and follow-up ICD-10 diagnoses was 92.6%, with a mean follow-up of 3.7 ± 0.8 years. Sensitivity was 64.5%, specificity 93.4%, and negative predictive value 98.9%. Patient satisfaction was high, with a mean score of 8.5/10. The economic analysis demonstrated a 50% reduction in total costs compared with conventional care, with a cost per patient of €40.7 versus €81.2.

Conclusions

The teleglaucoma system demonstrated a high ability to rule out disease among individuals at risk of glaucoma, reduced costs and achieved high patient satisfaction. However, moderate sensitivity and the use of coded clinical records as the reference standard should be considered.

title: Efficacy and safety of cavo-tricuspid isthmus ablation using the linear-shaped pulsed field ablation catheter: LINEAR study.
authorString: Kawaji T, Yamano S, Naka M, Ishida R, Bao B, Kimura T, Hojo S, Matsuda S, Kato M, Yokomatsu T, Miki S.
abstractText:
Background

Cavotricuspid isthmus(CTI) using pulsed field ablation(PFA) is still challenging.

Methods

We prospectively enrolled 90 consecutive patients with atrial fibrillation(AF) and atrial flutter(AFL), who received CTI ablation using a linear-shaped PulseSelect PFA Loop catheter. Coronary angiography of the right coronary artery was performed before and just after PFA application. During the CTI ablation following PVI, the initial 45 patients did not receive prophylactic nitroglycerin administration (control group), and the latter 45 patients received systemic nitroglycerin administration of 1.5mg before the applications (NTG group).

Results

All patients achieved an acute line of block using only the PFA catheter, with 91.1% requiring two or fewer applications. Operators performed additional "bonus" applications, resulting in an average of 4.4 ± 1.4 applications per patient. After a mean waiting period of 24.7 minutes, high-density mapping revealed a re-conduction gap in 20 patients (22.2%). Of these 20 patients with reconduction, four had an epicardial bridge. Coronary artery spasm was observed in 51.1% of the control group. In contrast, prophylactic nitroglycerin administration significantly reduced the incidence of coronary spasm to 15.6% in the NTG group. No severe spasms were observed in the NTG group. Among nine patients who underwent a repeat ablation procedure due to clinical AF recurrence, CTI reconduction was found in five (55.6%).

Conclusion

Linear-shaped PulseSelect CTI ablation readily achieves acute block, but early reconduction limits long-term durability despite consolidation applications. Without prophylactic NTG, there is a notable risk of coronary spasm, necessitating its routine use. Additionally, systematic postprocedural follow-up is needed to assess delayed coronary safety.

title: Preliminary Experience with a Standardized Perioperative Protocol for Infection Prevention in Inflatable Penile Prosthesis Surgery.
authorString: Carter BB, Swanton AR, Atwater BL, Gross MS.
abstractText:
Objective

To describe a structured, multimodal perioperative protocol for infection prevention in Inflatable penile prosthesis (IPP) surgery and report preliminary outcomes.

Methods

We retrospectively reviewed a prospectively maintained single-surgeon database of all IPP procedures performed at two XXXXXX XXXXXX hospitals between January 2017 and December 2025, classified as primary implants, removal and replacement (R/R), or component revisions (CR). Salvage procedures and explantations were excluded. A structured, protocol-driven perioperative antibiotic regimen individualized by procedure type was employed throughout, using a modified no-touch technique, copious antibiotic irrigation, a compressive mummy wrap dressing, and 23-hour inpatient observation. A Jackson-Pratt drain was placed routinely in primary cases and selectively in R/R and revision cases.

Results

Of 487 procedures (406 primary, 58 R/R, 23 CR), one surgical site infection occurred (primary implant patient, 0.25%; 1/406), for an overall rate of 0.21% (1/487); no infections occurred in the R/R or CR groups. The infected case was managed with malleable salvage and later uncomplicated replacement. Mean age was 62.5, 63.4, and 65.2 years for primary, R/R, and revision patients, respectively. Comorbidities in the primary group included hypertension (64.5%), hyperlipidemia (60.3%), diabetes (32.3%), HIV (1.0%), and preoperative S. aureus/MRSA colonization (16.5%).

Conclusions

A standardized, multimodal perioperative protocol, including MRSA decolonization, chlorhexidine bathing, antimicrobial prophylaxis, no-touch technique, drain usage, and compressive dressing was associated with a very low infection rate across all procedure types, supporting further evaluation of this approach in broader settings.

title: Baseline circulating thrombospondin-1 is associated with recurrence after catheter ablation in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: A retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Liao W, Wang S, Huai W, Zhang L, Yang X, Chen M, Gao Y, Liu X.
abstractText:
Introduction

Recurrence after radiofrequency catheter ablation remains common in patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF), and clinically accessible biomarkers for pre-procedural risk stratification are limited. Thrombospondin-1 (TSP-1) is a circulating matricellular protein implicated in inflammatory and profibrotic pathways.

Methods

We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of 211 patients with paroxysmal AF undergoing first-time radiofrequency catheter ablation. Baseline circulating TSP-1 was measured before ablation and analysed primarily as a continuous (log-transformed) variable, with a pre-specified 75th-percentile threshold used for exploratory subgroups. The primary endpoint was AF recurrence after a 3-month blanking period. Multivariable Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, time-dependent discrimination with bootstrap optimism correction, and propensity score matching (sensitivity analysis) were performed.

Results

During a median follow-up of 700 days, 61 patients (28.9%) experienced AF recurrence. Higher baseline TSP-1 was independently associated with recurrence in the full cohort (adjusted HR per 1-SD of log-TSP-1, 1.54; 95% CI 1.26-1.88; p < 0.001) and persisted after propensity score matching (HR 4.73; 95% CI 2.18-10.29). Adding TSP-1 improved time-dependent discrimination at 700 days (AUC 0.62 to 0.70; optimism-corrected 0.66; Harrell's C 0.627 to 0.705), although reclassification metrics were mixed and the incremental value was exploratory.

Conclusion

Elevated baseline circulating TSP-1 was associated with a higher risk of AF recurrence after first-time radiofrequency catheter ablation in patients with paroxysmal AF. These findings support further evaluation of TSP-1 as a candidate biomarker for pre-procedural risk stratification.

title: Anthraquinone-enriched fraction of Rheum australe D. Don by Bioassay-guided fractionation and synergistic interaction with tetracycline against Bacterial pathogens.
authorString: Rolta R, Salaria D, Soni M, Choudhary G, Lal UR, Prakash A, Behera A, Gautam V, Kaman L, Medhi B.
abstractText:
Ethnopharmacological relevance

Rheum australe is an important medicinal herb known as Himalayan rhubarb. Traditionally used in Ayurveda and Tibetan medicine to treat diabetes, diarrhoea, hypertension, obesity, wounds, backache & gastrointestinal diseases.

Aim of the study

The current study is focused on studying the antibacterial and synergistic potential of the anthraquinone-enriched fraction of R. australe in combination with conventional antibiotics.

Materials and methods

The extract of R. australe was prepared using 70% ethanol with a Soxhlet apparatus, and Bioassay guided fractionation was done. Broth microdilution methods determined antibacterial and Synergistic activity of crude extracts and subfractions. Phytoconstituents were identified by LC-MS, and molecular docking was done to study the interaction with penicillin-binding protein 3, and docking-predicted potential interacting Phytoconstituents were quantified by HPLC.

Results

The extraction yield of the hydroalcoholic extract was recorded as 40.66 ± 3.05%. The chloroform subfraction showed the strongest antibacterial activity among all the subfractions against MRSA (64 μg/ mL), S. aureus (16 μg/mL) &P. aeruginosa (8 μg/mL) mL, and also the strongest synergistic activity with tetracycline against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) (FICI 0.19-0.5), Staphylococcus aureus (FICI 0.0312-0.125), and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (FICI 0.125-0.375). Six phytoconstituents (piceatannol, chrysophanol, rhein, aloe-emodin, physcion & emodin) were identified by LC-MS. Molecular docking and MD simulation data revealed that among all the phytoconstituents, aloe-emodin, chrysophanol, emodin, & rhein indicated favourable interactions. HPLC analysis showed that these four phytoconstituents were enriched in the chloroform subfraction.

Conclusion

The current study suggests that the chloroform subfraction enriched in anthraquinones exhibits strong antibacterial activity and synergistic activity in combination with tetracycline, and the synergistic mechanism of the combination remains to be established.

title: Differential Regulatory Activities of Potassium and Aldosterone in the Distal Nephron: A Resolution to the Aldosterone Paradox.
authorString: Pearce D, Korbmacher C.
abstractText: Aldosterone has long been viewed as a master regulator of fluid and electrolyte homeostasis, acting through the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) to stimulate electrogenic Na+ transport via the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) in the distal nephron. This primary effect is thought to drive both K+ secretion and Cl- reabsorption; however, the underlying mechanism has remained obscure and the dual regulation has generated an enigma often referred to as the aldosterone paradox. Here we propose a model for regulated K+ secretion centered on local regulation of ENaC in the late distal convoluted tubule and early connecting tubule. In this segment, the MR is constitutively activated by glucocorticoids rather than by aldosterone, and yet ENaC activity and K+ secretion through the renal outer medullary K+ channel (ROMK) are not constitutive but, rather, are highly regulated. The model holds that the key regulatory step for K+ secretion involves a cell-autonomous mechanism through which local interstitial [K+] stimulates mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2)-dependent phosphorylation of the ENaC regulatory serum- and glucocorticoid-induced kinase 1 (SGK1); the K+-sensing kinase augments this phosphorylation by serving as a scaffold to enhance the physical interaction of mTORC2 with SGK1. Aldosterone acts further downstream to stimulate ENaC primarily in the late CNT and cortical collecting duct, in which ROMK apical expression is relatively low and Na+-Cl- reabsorption is favored. This revised paradigm resolves the aldosterone paradox and has important implications for hypertension, potassium disorders, and potentially medical therapies.

title: Community health worker-led home blood pressure monitoring in rural sub-Saharan Africa: a diagnostic accuracy study.
authorString: Lucinde RK, Jobe M, Perkins AD, Awori JO, Karia B, Lamin J, Oyando R, Kalu C, Sanneh S, Mwagwabi C, Saru E, Brazeal A, Kinyanjui S, Peck RN, Leon DA, Clayton T, Ogola EN, Ehret G, Schutte AE, Prentice AM, Tsofa B, Shah ASV, Perel P, Etyang AO, IHCoR-Africa collaborators.
abstractText:
Background

Home blood pressure monitoring (HBPM) coordinated by community health workers (CHWs) is a potential strategy to improve hypertension detection in sub-Saharan Africa, yet data on its diagnostic performance in this setting are scarce. We aimed to determine the diagnostic accuracy of CHW-coordinated HBPM in Kenya and The Gambia using daytime ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) as the reference standard.

Methods

In this cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study, we recruited a random sample of representative age-stratified individuals aged 30 years or older from the general population of two health and demographic surveillance systems in Kilifi, Kenya, and Kiang West, The Gambia. We used the latest enumeration lists of the two health and demographic surveillance systems as sampling frames and performed computer-generated random sampling within five predefined age strata (30-39 years, 40-49 years, 50-59 years, 60-69 years, and ≥70 years). Pregnant women were excluded, and participants were eligible to participate irrespective of previous hypertension status. CHWs trained and provided participants with HBPM devices for self-measurement of blood pressure twice a day, for a minimum of 3 days and a maximum of 7 days. For the reference standard measurement, an ABPM device was fitted by CHWs, and ambulatory blood pressure was measured every 15 min during the day and 30 min at night. We used blood pressure cutoffs derived from the European Society of Hypertension to determine the age-standardised measures of accuracy (sensitivities, specificities, positive predictive values [PPVs] and negative predictive values [NPVs], positive likelihood ratios [LR+] and negative likelihood ratios [LR-] and area under receiver operating characteristic curves) of HBPM among participants who had valid HBPM and ABPM measurements.

Findings

Between Aug 18, 2023, and Dec 13, 2024, from 1452 eligible participants, we included 1279 participants with valid HBPM and ABPM measurements (696 in Kenya and 583 in The Gambia). In 1279 participants, the median age was 54 years (IQR 43-66), 805 (62·9%) were women, and 474 (37·1%) were men. The age-standardised prevalence of hypertension on daytime ABPM was 23·1% (95% CI 19·9-26·2) in Kenya and 27·1% (23·6-30·6) in The Gambia while the respective prevalences on HBPM were 32·5% (29·1-35·8) and 31·2% (27·5-34·9). The age-standardised sensitivities and specificities of HBPM were 82·6% (76·2-89·0) and 82·4% (79·0-85·7) in Kenya and 68·7% (61·3-76·1) and 83·5% (79·7-87·2) in The Gambia. The age-standardised PPVs and NPVs were 58·6% (52·0-65·2) and 94·0% (91·6-96·4) in Kenya and 59·9% (52·5-67·2) and 88·1% (84·8-91·4) in The Gambia, respectively. The age-standardised LR+ and LR- were 4·68 (3·67-5·69) and 0·21 (0·13-0·29) in Kenya and 4·15 (3·09-5·21) and 0·37 (0·28-0·46) in The Gambia, respectively. In both countries, the area under receiver operating characteristic curve for HBPM was above 75%.

Interpretation

HBPM showed moderate-to-high sensitivity and high specificity for detecting hypertension in two rural sub-Saharan African communities. HBPM represents a promising alternative for increasing hypertension awareness in rural sub-Saharan Africa.

Funding

The UK National Institute for Health and Care Research, the UK Medical Research Council, and the Wellcome Trust.

title: Managing Abnormal Uterine Bleeding During Anticoagulant Therapy in Clinical Practice.
authorString: Sarlon G, Gendron N, Chauleur C, Zuily-Lamy C, Mahé I, Sevestre-Pietri MA, Tromeur C, Couturaud F, Trillot N, Agostini A, Morange PE.
abstractText: Anticoagulant therapies, including heparins, vitamin K antagonists, and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) such as rivaroxaban, apixaban and dabigatran, are crucial for the treatment and the prevention of venous thromboembolism (VTE). While DOACs offer improved safety profiles, their use, espe-cially in women of reproductive age, increases the risk of abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB), partic-ularly heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB). HMB, defined as blood loss exceeding 80 mL per cycle or causing significant life disruption, is associated with reduced quality of life and substantial economic costs. Women on anticoagulants report higher incidences of HMB, often requiring adjustments in therapy or additional interventions. Management strategies include the referral for a gynecological consultation, the adjustment of hormonal therapy and anticoagulant treatment, the administration of tranexamic acid, and the treatment of iron deficiency. The review underscores the importance of a comprehensive, personalized approach to managing AUB in women on anticoagulants to optimize both anticoagulation effectiveness and patient quality of life.

title: Exercise-Induced Tricuspid Regurgitation: Clinical Predictors and Hemodynamic Implications.
authorString: Baratto C, Mercurio M, Muraru D, Heilbron F, Tomaselli M, Perego GB, Previdi F, Paleari S, Fiocca L, Senni M, Vachiéry JL, Rao VN, Tedford RJ, Fudim M, Parati G, Badano LP, Caravita S.
abstractText:
Background

Exercise-induced preload/afterload changes could affect tricuspid regurgitation (TR).

Objectives

The study aims to assess exercise-induced TR (exTR+), its consequences, and predictors.

Methods

Consecutive patients underwent exercise cardiac catheterization and three-dimensional echocardiography. ExTR+ was defined as a ≥1 grade increase in TR severity.

Results

ExTR+ occurred in 34% of 132 patients. Patients with exTR+ were older, had more atrial fibrillation, higher natriuretic peptides/heart failure with preserved ejection fraction probability scores, higher filling pressures, and lower cardiac output (P < 0.05). ExTR+ displayed greater right ventricular dilation, right atrial pressure rise, lower cardiac output, and lower oxygen consumption (P < 0.05). Exercise rather than resting TR regurgitant volume was more associated with cardiac output and oxygen consumption. Baseline TR, atrial fibrillation, and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (OR: 1.065, 4.97, and 1.0004 per pg/mL, respectively, P < 0.05) predicted exTR+ (area under the curve: 0.91).

Conclusions

ExTR+ is frequent, identifies heart failure with preserved ejection fraction-like phenotypes with a maladaptive exercise response, and adds information beyond resting TR.

title: Association Between Intradialytic Foot Temperature Gradients and Severe Peripheral Artery Disease in Patients Undergoing Hemodialysis: Prospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Lin DS, Wu CC, Yang CW, Lee JK, Hsu CY.
abstractText:
Background

Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is prevalent in hemodialysis (HD) patients but remains difficult to diagnose due to unreliable ankle-brachial index (ABI) measurements caused by vascular calcification. We hypothesized that monitoring foot temperatures and their changes during HD, provoked by hemodynamic shifts, could serve as a novel diagnostic tool for detecting severe PAD.

Objective

This study aims to evaluate the diagnostic utility of intradialytic foot temperature monitoring using wearable mobile health (mHealth) sensors for detecting severe PAD in patients undergoing HD.

Methods

In this prospective observational study, we recruited 109 patients undergoing chronic maintenance HD. Skin temperatures were monitored continuously at the instep and sole during HD sessions using wearable sensors (Temp Pal, iWEECARE Co, Ltd), which are wireless, nanochip-based mHealth thermometers with ±0.05 °C accuracy. The diagnostic performance of temperature parameters, specifically the temperature difference between the wrist and foot at the end of HD, was evaluated against vascular duplex ultrasound (DUS). Severe PAD was defined as abnormal (monophasic or absent) flow in the distal posterior tibial artery (PTA) or anterior tibial artery (ATA).

Results

Patients with abnormal tibial flow on DUS exhibited significantly different temperature gradients between the wrist and foot at the end of dialysis compared to those with normal flow. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis demonstrated that the wrist-foot temperature difference at the sole effectively discriminated abnormal ATA flow (area under the curve [AUC] 64.5%, 95% CI 57.8%-70.9%) and abnormal PTA flow (AUC 62.0%, 95% CI 55.2%-68.5%). Notably, an instep wrist-foot temperature difference cutoff of -2.2 °C or less yielded a specificity of 97.6% (95% CI 94.0%-99.3%) for detecting abnormal PTA flow.

Conclusions

Intradialytic foot temperature monitoring, particularly the temperature gradient between the wrist and foot, significantly correlates with severe tibial artery flow abnormalities. This method offers an accessible, noninvasive screening adjunct to the ABI for detecting severe PAD in the HD population. These findings indicate an association rather than a standalone diagnostic test; given the modest discriminative ability, external validation is warranted.

title: Evaluating the Performance of Large Language Models in Vascular Surgery Cases: Cross-Sectional Study.
authorString: Wijetunga A, Wang Y, Yaghi C, Vicaretti M.
abstractText:
Background

Large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude are increasingly used by clinicians, yet their accuracy, safety, and consistency in clinical cases remain poorly defined. Most studies assess LLMs using multiple-choice questions rather than free-response reasoning.

Objective

The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the performance and safety of 3 widely used LLMs in realistic vascular surgery scenarios in key domains such as diagnosis, investigation, and multidisciplinary and multimodal management. The secondary objective of this study was to evaluate the safety of the models' outputs.

Methods

A total of 42 fictitious vascular cases across 5 major pathologies (acute limb ischemia [ALI], aortopathy, chronic limb ischemia, diabetic foot infection, and extracranial cerebrovascular disease) were independently entered into GPT-5, Gemini 2.5, and Claude Sonnet 4.5 using standardized prompts. Each model answered structured questions covering diagnosis, investigation, and management (both operative and nonoperative). Responses were scored out of 20 by a panel using a predefined rubric. Each plan's overall safety was separately assessed. Comparative analyses used 2-tailed t tests, ANOVA, and multivariable logistic regression.

Results

Mean composite scores by model were 86.5% for ChatGPT, 83.5% for Gemini, and 88.0% for Claude, whereas scores by disease were 82.7% for ALI, 83.8% for aortopathy, 85.9% for chronic limb ischemia, 86.1% for diabetic foot infection, and 80.7% for extracranial cerebrovascular disease (P>.05 in each case). Unsafe plans were generated in 11.9%, 23.8%, and 7.1% of cases by ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, respectively. On multivariable analysis, independent predictors of unsafe outputs were lower composite score (odds ratio [OR] 0.471, 95% CI 0.306-0.722; P=.001), higher word count (OR 1.003, 95% CI 1.001-1.005; P=.001), and ALI (OR 20.9, 95% CI 3.79-61.8; P<.001).

Conclusions

Our findings demonstrate LLMs' promise in managing routine vascular surgery cases. However, their inconsistent safety profiles and ethical limitations preclude unsupervised clinical use. Rigorous specialty-specific validation is essential before they may be integrated into routine practice.

title: Coexistence of AI Nurse and AI-Simulated Patient in Nursing Education Using a Bidirectional Fine-Tuning Pipeline: Development and Content Analysis Study.
authorString: Koike T, Majima Y.
abstractText:
Background

Simulated patient systems are essential in nursing education but face actor scarcity, instructor burden, cost, and disrupted continuity where in-person simulation cannot be sustained. Existing large language model (LLM)-based systems address these issues but treat the dialogic partner-the AI nurse-as a static prompt or unspecialized model, compromising data collection quality and pedagogical applicability.

Objective

We report (1) the construction of 2 specialized fine-tuned models, NURSE-ONE (AI nurse) and PATIENT-ONE (AI-simulated patient), via a 5-step bidirectional fine-tuning pipeline; (2) their evaluation using Berelson content analysis validated by independent human coders; (3) an exploratory third-party evaluation by nursing faculty; and (4) the design of a coexistence simulation ecosystem supporting 3 operating modes, including offline disaster preparedness applicability.

Methods

On a single consumer-grade graphics processing unit (NVIDIA RTX 4090; 24 GB video random access memory), the multimodal base model gemma4-E4B-it was fine-tuned via low-rank adaptation in five steps: (1) a 251-scenario base from 29 institutionally authored nursing care plans and 20 items from the 115th Japanese National Nursing Examination; (2) a provisional dialogue system (AutoGen v18, maxmsg=25) to collect training dialogues; (3) NURSE-ONE fine-tuning across 3 training volume conditions (245, 735, and 1225 cases); (4) 4-condition Berelson comparison; and (5) PATIENT-ONE fine-tuning on NURSE-ONE-generated dialogues with a 3-condition comparison. Interrater reliability was confirmed by 2 independent nursing experts (196 blinded utterances, κ=0.770) and corroborated by 2 LLM raters (κ=0.742). Ten nursing faculty evaluated 3 coexistence modes in a working web user interface (21-item rubric; item-level content validity index=1.00).

Results

Four-condition Berelson analysis (χ215=42.0, P<.001) identified the 735-case nurse-side condition (open question rate=21.5%) as NURSE-ONE; information collection rate reached 15.5% (~4× baseline) at 1225 cases. PATIENT-ONE A/B/C analysis (χ210=11.8, P=.30) showed no significant category shift but the lowest response length variability (SD 24.5) and highest information-providing rate (47.9%) at 735 cases, adopted as PATIENT-ONE. The 2 adapters appeared to operate on different axes-qualitative questioning style on the nurse side and quantitative response stability on the patient side-a preliminary observed pattern we term functional asymmetry, pending replication. Third-party evaluation rated the AI-simulated patient, AI nurse, and dyadic interaction at 90.3%, 69.0%, and 84.8%, respectively, with role maintenance at ceiling (mean 5, SD 0). All 3 modes met the prespecified 3-second latency threshold.

Conclusions

A 5-step bidirectional fine-tuning pipeline produced 2 specialized models whose joint deployment constitutes a design pattern for nursing education simulation. The preliminarily observed functional asymmetry between qualitative nurse-side variation and quantitative patient-side stabilization appears to underwrite the system's coherence, supporting 3 operating modes on consumer-grade hardware and deployable offline in disaster preparedness contexts. Third-party evaluation confirmed exploratory educational applicability, with all evaluators rating the system as usable, providing a foundation for future learner outcome studies.

title: Trends in Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump Technology: Patentometric Analysis.
authorString: Shen H, Li J, Dong X, Tao C.
abstractText:
Background

The intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) remains a commonly used temporary mechanical circulatory support device because it is relatively easy to implant, less invasive, and well established in clinical practice. Previous studies have focused primarily on the physiological mechanisms, indications, clinical outcomes, and complications of IABP, whereas its technological evolution and industrial research have not been systematically examined.

Objective

This study aimed to characterize the global technological and industrial evolution of IABP; identify current research priorities and underdeveloped areas; and relate patent innovation to unresolved needs in hemodynamic support, vascular safety, counterpulsation accuracy, prolonged bridging, and patient transport.

Methods

Patent documents related to IABP were retrieved from the PatSnap database using a combined search strategy based on keywords and International Patent Classification (IPC) codes. The search was limited to documents published by August 18, 2026. After screening and deduplication, simple patent families were used as the unit of analysis. Patentometric analysis and technology function matrix analysis were performed to characterize the technological evolution, geographical distribution, and major innovation directions of IABP technology.

Results

A total of 1235 IABP-related patent families were identified. The United States, China, Japan, and Europe were the principal countries or regions of origin, together accounting for 89.1% (1100/1235) of the included simple patent families. China contributed 326 simple patent families, representing 26.4% of the global total, and showed particularly rapid growth over the past 5 years. IABP technology evolved through an embryonic stage (1968-1985), a steady development stage (1986-2012), and a rapid development stage beginning in 2013. Patent families were mainly classified as balloon components (n=552, 44.7%), catheters and accessories (n=416, 33.7%), and counterpulsation timing and control (n=161, 13%). The technology function matrix indicated that structural optimization and control precision are the current priorities in research and development, while balloon folding and compression, fiber-optic pressure sensing, and adaptive control algorithms have emerged as important hotspots.

Conclusions

IABP innovation has focused on balloon catheter design, pressure sensing, and adaptive control to improve hemodynamic support and counterpulsation accuracy. However, safety and complication reduction remain underdeveloped, particularly for prolonged support and transport. Future systems should integrate durable, low-profile designs with sensing, adaptive timing, and failure monitoring and be evaluated in specific patient populations and clinical settings.

title: BPR-30901649, An Angiotensinogen-Targeting Small Interfering RNA, Achieves Ultra-Durable Target Silencing and Sustained Blood Pressure Reduction Through 20 Weeks in Hypertensive Non-Human Primates.
authorString: Liu W, Pei S, Lu J, Chen Y, Zou K, Duan J, Zang C, Cheng X, Huang H, Chen Y.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Hypertension affects over 1.3 billion adults worldwide, and poor adherence to daily oral therapy contributes to inadequate blood pressure (BP) control. We characterized BPR-30901649, a liver-targeted small interfering RNA (siRNA) against angiotensinogen (AGT), hypothesizing that its optimized design would confer greater potency and durability than an advanced clinical-stage AGT siRNA benchmark.

Methods

BPR-30901649 was selected through in vitro and in vivo screening in HepG2 cells and human AGT (hAGT) transgenic mice. Off-target risk was assessed by RNA sequencing in primary human hepatocytes. Pharmacodynamics were evaluated in hAGT mice after single and repeat subcutaneous (SC) dosing, and in hypertensive cynomolgus monkeys given a single SC dose of 1.5 or 3.0 mg/kg, with serum AGT and systolic BP (SBP) monitored for 20 weeks. Investigational New Drug (IND)-enabling toxicology was conducted in rats and nonhuman primates (NHPs).

Results

RNA sequencing indicated low off-target risk. In hAGT mice, BPR-30901649 produced significantly deeper serum AGT knockdown than the benchmark. In hypertensive NHPs, a single SC injection produced rapid, dose-dependent, and sustained AGT suppression; at week 20, SBP remained reduced by 14.2% (20.3 mm Hg) and 17.3% (25.3 mm Hg) in the low- and high-dose groups, respectively. In repeat-dose toxicology, the no-observed-adverse-effect level was 100 mg/kg in NHPs.

Conclusions

BPR-30901649 surpassed an advanced clinical-stage AGT siRNA benchmark in vivo and showed a wide preclinical safety margin, supporting its clinical development as a potential twice-yearly therapy for hypertension.

title: A transcriptional and cellular exploration of obesity and type II diabetes in human adipose tissues.
authorString: Trim WV, Petrova K, Healy K, Stevens BM, Scanlan JG, Faust HJ, Svensson Akusjärvi S, O'Brien KL, O'Shea D, Brenner MB, Heneghan H, Lynch L.
abstractText: Obesity is tightly linked to metabolic disorders such as type II diabetes mellitus (T2D), although a subpopulation of individuals with obesity do not present with these morbidities. The biological factors conferring T2D vulnerability remain incompletely understood. We recruited 58 individuals with obesity with or without a clinical diagnosis of T2D (Ob + T2D and Ob). We profiled paired samples of omental and subcutaneous adipose by single-cell RNA sequencing (n = 10), flow cytometry under basal and stimulated conditions (n = 42), and histology (n = 17). Flow cytometry and chemokine quantification were also performed in paired whole blood. We identified reprogramming of the omental stromal compartment, centered on mesothelial and endothelial cells, alongside contrasting innate T cell and macrophage phenotypes across depots. Mesothelial and IGFBP2+ cells exhibited a fibrotic, epithelial-mesenchymal transition-like phenotype, while omental endothelial cells exhibited a lipid-overload, inflammatory, antigen presentation profile in T2D. Omental and subcutaneous adipose innate T cells exhibited divergent inflammatory profiles between tissues. These findings reveal previously unidentified insights into the pathophysiology of T2D in adipose tissue and identify compensatory networks within the tissues that could be exploited by targeted therapeutics.

title: Mevalonate pathway regulates double-negative regulatory T cell stability in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
authorString: Jin H, Wang X, Zhou L, Zhong X, Wei Y, Han X, Xu N, Fang P, Zhang Z, Du X, Li M, Wang S, Zhang Z, Sun G, Zhang D.
abstractText: Lipid metabolism dysfunction and immune imbalance are critical pathogenic drivers of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Double-negative regulatory T cells (DNTreg) are important immune regulatory cells that maintain liver immune homeostasis. However, their survival and function are compromised in MASLD. Herein, we found that mevalonate pathway and its rate-limiting enzyme HMG-CoA reductase (HMGCR) were significantly down-regulated in DNTreg from both mice and patients with MASLD, correlating with impaired DNTreg viability and immunosuppressive function. Arachidonic acid is enriched in MASLD liver and inhibits DNTreg HMGCR expression. Geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (GGPP), a downstream product of HMGCR, mediates RAC1 geranylgeranylation, which facilitates its interaction with mitochondrial CLPX protease, thereby enhancing mitochondrial function and immunoregulatory activity of DNTreg. Adoptive transfer of Pggt1b+/- DNTreg into MASLD mice demonstrated significantly diminished therapeutic efficacy compared with wild-type DNTreg. In conclusion, mevalonate metabolism-mediated geranylgeranylation is essential for the suppressive activity and immune homeostasis of DNTreg in MASLD.

title: Reduced apelin expression and atrial fibrosis in postoperative atrial fibrillation following coronary artery bypass grafting.
authorString: Xu Y, Chen Z, Liu P, Wen W, Li X, Wang H.
abstractText: The role of apelin in atrial fibrosis linked to postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is not fully understood. This exploratory study investigated apelin's association with POAF-related atrial fibrosis and its impact on profibrotic signaling. The study included 18 patients: six CABG patients with POAF, six CABG patients without POAF, and six patients with congenital heart disease in sinus rhythm (serving as a secondary reference). Left atrial appendage tissue was analyzed histologically and molecularly, and serum apelin levels were measured on postoperative day 2 in CABG patients. Primary neonatal rat atrial fibroblasts were treated with transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1) both with and without apelin, or subjected to apelin silencing. Compared with CABG patients without POAF, the POAF group exhibited lower atrial apelin expression and serum concentrations, increased collagen deposition, elevated TGF-β1 expression, and enhanced phosphorylation of mothers against decapentaplegic homolog 2 (Smad2), while total Smad2 remained unchanged. Experimentally, apelin attenuated TGF-β1-induced fibroblast activation, collagen expression, and Smad2 phosphorylation. Conversely, apelin silencing increased the expression of fibrosis-associated proteins. These preliminary findings suggest a link between reduced apelin and atrial fibrosis, as well as POAF after CABG. They also indicate antifibrotic effects of apelin, potentially mediated through TGF-β1/Smad2 signaling. Further research with larger clinical cohorts and complementary experimental models is necessary to fully elucidate the pathway mediation and clinical significance of these findings.

title: Intravenous midazolam alters short-interval paired-pulse TMS responses differently in younger and older adults.
authorString: McGregor KM, Safavynia SA, Novak T, Weber AM, Wang J, Nocera JR, Woodbury A, Crosson B, García PS.
abstractText:
Objective

Aging is associated with changes in cortical excitability and altered responsiveness to benzodiazepines, but the effects of benzodiazepine challenge on motor cortical paired-pulse physiology in older adults remain incompletely understood. We examined whether intravenous midazolam differentially modulates corticospinal excitability and short-interval paired-pulse transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) responses in younger and older adults.

Methods

Sixteen younger adults (18-35 years) and sixteen older adults (50-69 years) underwent single-pulse and paired-pulse (conditioning stimulus: 110% motor threshold; test stimulus: 143% motor threshold) TMS of the left primary motor cortex at baseline and during intravenous midazolam administration. Single-pulse motor evoked potential (MEP) amplitude was used to assess corticospinal excitability. Short-interval paired-pulse responses were quantified as the ratio of conditioned to unconditioned MEP amplitude.

Results

At baseline, younger adults showed greater corticospinal excitability than older adults, reflected by larger single-pulse MEP amplitudes (adjusted p = 0.04). Younger adults demonstrated paired-pulse inhibition at baseline, reflected by a conditioned/unconditioned MEP ratio below 1.0 (ratio = 0.73; adjusted p < 0.01), whereas older adults did not show inhibition and instead had a mean ratio above 1.0 (ratio = 1.25). Midazolam reduced single-pulse MEP amplitudes in both groups. During midazolam administration, paired-pulse inhibition was no longer observed in younger adults, and older adults continued to show no evidence of inhibition.

Conclusions

Younger and older adults differed in baseline corticospinal excitability and in short-interval paired-pulse TMS responses. Intravenous midazolam reduced corticospinal excitability and altered paired-pulse response patterns, eliminating baseline paired-pulse inhibition in younger adults while producing little measurable change in older adults. These findings suggest that aging may modify the net motor cortical response to benzodiazepine challenge. The results should be interpreted in relation to the paired-pulse stimulation parameters used and support further studies using complementary approaches to characterize age-related differences in inhibitory and facilitatory motor cortical circuits.

title: Rethinking hypertension in the brain: from blood pressure control to temporal blood pressure stability-a scoping review.
authorString: Chakraborty S, Pai AR.
abstractText:
Background

Temporal blood pressure variability (BPV) may contribute to cerebrovascular injury beyond mean blood pressure (BP), yet the mechanisms linking antihypertensive treatment patterns to temporal BP instability remain incompletely understood. This scoping review synthesised evidence linking treatment instability, pharmacodynamic determinants of BP control, temporal BPV, and cerebrovascular vulnerability.

Methods

PubMed and Embase were searched for studies evaluating antihypertensive medication adherence, pharmacodynamic persistence, BPV, and cerebrovascular outcomes. Data were charted using a standardised form and synthesised narratively according to predefined thematic domains.

Results

The available evidence suggests that inconsistent antihypertensive exposure and reduced pharmacodynamic persistence may contribute to increased temporal BPV. Generally BP fluctuations are associated with cerebral small vessel disease, white matter injury, vascular cognitive impairment, and other manifestations of cerebrovascular vulnerability independent of mean BP. This review investigates the relationship between treatment instability, pharmacodynamic determinants, and temporal BPV and proposes a hypothesis-generating conceptual framework to facilitate future individualised risk stratification and guide prospective investigation.

Conclusions

Current evidence supports expanding hypertension management beyond achieving mean BP targets to include optimisation of temporal BP stability. Recognising treatment persistence and pharmacodynamic coverage as determinants of BP stability provides a clinically relevant framework for improving cerebrovascular protection and individualised risk assessment. These findings support consideration of temporal BP stability as a potential complementary dimension of hypertension management for preventing chronic cerebrovascular injury and vascular cognitive dysfunction.

title: Fruit and vegetable consumption among people living with HIV at a large Urban HIV Clinic in Central Uganda: A cross-sectional study.
authorString: Kasendwa M, Nantale R, Kusolo R, Mayega RW, Ndejjo R, Musinguzi G, Mukunya D, Ssennyonjo A, Murokora D, Ddungu A, Owarwo NC, Nanteza NJ, Asire B, Wanyenze R.
abstractText:
Background

Fruit and vegetable consumption has been shown to effectively reduce the risk of developing non-communicable diseases such as hypertension. This study assessed the prevalence, perceptions and factors associated with fruit and vegetable consumption among people living with HIV (PLHIV) at an Urban HIV clinic in central Uganda.

Methods

This was a cross-sectional study conducted at the Infectious Diseases Institute (IDI) HIV clinic located in Kampala, Uganda. An adapted World Health Organisation STEPwise questionnaire was administered with Open Data Kit (ODK) to a random sample of 431 PLHIV clients aged 18 years and older to obtain data on levels and perceptions of fruit and vegetable consumption. Adequate intake of fruits and vegetables was defined as consumption of five or more servings of fruits and/ or vegetables per day in a typical week. We conducted multivariable robust Poisson regression to determine the independent factors associated with adequate fruit and vegetable consumption. Data were analyzed in Stata version 17.0.

Results

A total of 44 out of 417 (10.6%) respondents met the WHO recommendations of fruit and vegetable consumption. Overall, the perceptions of respondents about consumption of a fruits and vegetables were favourable (mean = 3.7, SD = 0.5), with the construct of perceived barriers to eating fruits and vegetables (mean = 3.2, SD = 1.6) having the least favourable perceptions. Being unemployed (APR: 0.1, 95% CI:0.0-0.8, p = 0.027), having a higher household income (APR:0.99, 95% CI: 0.900-0.998, p = 0.039) and having a longer duration on Antiretroviral Therapy (ART) (APR:0.9, 95% CI:0.89-0.996, p = 0.046) were significantly associated with inadequate consumption of fruits and vegetables.

Conclusions

Fruit and vegetable consumption among PLHIV was low. Our findings underscore the need for targeted strategies and interventions to promote healthy dietary practices, reduce perceived barriers, and improve awareness of hypertension risk among PLHIV.

title: Visual outcomes and headache in intracranial hypertension following cerebral venous sinus thrombosis: A retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Knoche T, Grueninger I, Pietrock C, Jami Z, Danyel LA.
abstractText: Intracranial hypertension is a frequent complication of cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVT), posing a risk for permanent visual impairment. However, long-term visual outcomes have not been systematically assessed using objective neuro-ophthalmic measures. We retrospectively evaluated consecutive adults presenting to a single-center tertiary intracranial hypertension clinic between 2019 and 2025 with intracranial hypertension following CVT. Visual outcomes were assessed using best-corrected visual acuity, automated perimetry, and optical coherence tomography measuring global peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness. Headache phenotype and medication overuse were documented. Nineteen patients (11 female; mean age 33.4 ± 12.1 years) were included, with a mean follow-up of 3.4 ± 2.4 years after diagnosis of CVT-related intracranial hypertension. The transverse sinus was involved in 78.9% of cases, and complete or near-complete recanalization was achieved in 68.4%. Although visual acuity remained normal in most patients (84.2%), 26.3% had severe visual field loss and 15.8% showed retinal nerve fiber layer thinning. Headache persisted in 94.7%, most commonly as tension-type headache (63.2%), and 26.3% fulfilled criteria for medication overuse headache. Despite generally preserved visual acuity, substantial visual field deficits and persistent headache were common in CVT-related intracranial hypertension. These findings support routine neuro-ophthalmic follow-up to facilitate early detection of visual deterioration in CVT-related intracranial hypertension. As this cohort was drawn from a specialized tertiary referral clinic, these findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than representative of the broader CVT population.

title: Predictors of return to work after shoulder injuries: The influence of health perception and job characteristics.
authorString: Nik Asa S, Mirzamohammadi E, Nakhaei Amroodi M, Tabrizian P, Mohammadi S, Asadgol Z, Kassiri N.
abstractText: Shoulder injuries are prevalent among working populations and may significantly delay return to work (RTW). Identifying predictors of successful RTW is crucial for designing effective interventions. This study aimed to assess the RTW status and its determinants among patients with shoulder injuries. In this retrospective cohort study with prospective follow-up, 340 patients with shoulder injuries- such as acromioclavicular joint dislocation, clavicle fractures, and shoulder instability-treated between 2016 and 2020 were included. Data were obtained from medical records and structured telephone interviews. Demographic and clinical variables, health-related quality of life (SF-12), and perceived support from employer and colleagues were assessed. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify predictors of RTW. Among 340 participants, 67.9% returned to their previous job, 14.1% returned with modifications, 14.4% obtained new employment, and 3.5% did not return to work. Multivariate analysis showed that coworker support (OR=1.88, p < 0.001) was positively associated with RTW, whereas lower employer support (OR=0.585, p < 0.001), lower SF‑12 scores (OR=0.895, p = 0.023), and white‑collar occupation (OR=0.015, p < 0.001) were associated with reduced likelihood of RTW. In addition, health insurance coverage and certain injury types were significantly related to RTW outcomes. RTW after shoulder injuries is mainly influenced by multiple occupational, clinical, and psychosocial factors. Workplace support, overall health status, and job characteristics play important roles in facilitating occupational reintegration. Strengthening rehabilitation programs and workplace support systems may improve RTW outcomes among injured workers.

title: Home cardiotocography for high-risk obstetric care: A prospective observational feasibility study.
authorString: Le Vance J, Hodgetts Morton V, Morris RK, Gurney L.
abstractText: Home cardiotocography (CTG) may support remote antenatal surveillance, reduce hospital attendances, and improve patient-centred maternity care. However, United Kingdom (UK) evidence remains limited, and international findings may not be generalisable due to differences in maternity pathways and digital implementation. We therefore evaluated the feasibility, acceptability, usability, and safety of home CTG monitoring in a UK cohort of high-risk pregnant women. In this single-centre prospective feasibility study, 50 English-speaking women with high-risk singleton pregnancies at ≥32 weeks' gestation were enrolled. Participants received a portable CTG device and were advised to complete one hour of home monitoring weekly, for up to six weeks, or until delivery. Recordings were reviewed synchronously. The primary outcome was completion of 20 minutes of continuous, interpretable monitoring per episode. Secondary outcomes included feasibility, anxiety, acceptability, usability, competency, technological issues, and safety. In total, 204 home monitoring sessions were completed. The primary outcome was achieved in 82.4% (95% Confidence interval (CI), 76.5%-87.0%) of sessions (168/204), with a mean continuous monitoring duration of 34.3 ± 16.8 minutes. Session number was not associated with achievement of the primary outcome (Odds Ratio (OR) 1.18, 95% CI 0.93-1.51; p = 0.19) or monitoring duration (p = 0.16). Maternal demographic characteristics showed no statistically significant association with monitoring competency in the exploratory analysis. Anxiety scores decreased significantly following participation (p = 0.0004), including before and after the first (p = 0.01) and fifth sessions (p = 0.007). Usability was rated highly (mean 77.6; grade B + , 80th percentile). Participants were advised to attend maternity triage following 13 sessions (6.4%). No prespecified adverse outcomes related to device use occurred. Overall, 78% would use home CTG instead of hospital attendance in a future pregnancy. Home CTG monitoring for high-risk pregnancies was feasible, acceptable, usable, with no safety concerns identified in this single-arm cohort. These findings support future implementation, pathway integration and development of effectiveness studies.

title: Arabic translation, cross-cultural adaptation, and testing measurement properties of the European heart failure self-care behaviour (EHFScBS-12 and EHFScBS-9).
authorString: Sallam LA, AlOtaibi NG, Alharbi HA, Innab A, Hayajneh A, Al Ghafri AK, Almogbel O.
abstractText:
Background

Enhanced self-care is the primary objective of many heart failure (HF) management programs. The European Heart Failure Self-care Behaviour Scale (EHFScBS), available in 12-item and 9-item versions, is widely used to assess self-care in patients with HF. However, the EHFScBS has not been translated or evaluated its measurement properties in Arabic-speaking populations with HF.

Objective

The objective of this study was to translate, culturally adapt and evaluate the measurement properties of the Arabic version of EHFScBS-12 and EHFScBS-9 followed the COSMIN (COnsensus-based Standards for the selection of health Measurement Instruments) guidelines and to compare both versions regarding structural validity, reliability, and model fit among Arabic-speaking patients with HF.

Materials and methods

A cross-sectional study conducted at a governmental hospital in Riyadh used purposive sampling to recruit participants who met the predefined inclusion criteria relevant to the study objectives:137 patients with HF (mean age = 59 years; 61.3% male). The researchers evaluated the comprehensive measurement properties of the 12- and 9-item (EHFScBS) included forward-backward translation, confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), and reliability testing. In addition, convergent and divergent validity were assessed using the Self-Care Heart Failure Index version 6.2 and the Perceived Stress Scale10-Item.

Results

The scale demonstrated excellent content validity as evidenced by I-CVI of .85 to 1 and S-CVI of .95, and the CFA of the 12-item scale yielded ambiguous fit indices: root mean square error of approximation (RMSEA) =0.084, (90% CI: .059-.108), comparative fit index (CFI) =0.824, and normed fit index (NFI) =0.706 which is low/suboptimal. The CFA of the 9-item scale showed good fit indices (RMSEA = 0.042, (90%CI: .000-.084), CFI = 0.969). The internal consistency was acceptable for both scales at 0.75 and 0.72, respectively. Both the versions demonstrated convergent and discriminant validity.

Conclusions

The EHFScBS as unidimensional showed satisfactory measurement properties in Arabic-speaking HF patients. The 9-item one-factor has demonstrated better fit in the present sample compared to the 12-item version achieved after post-hoc modification, support its use in practice and research. However, future studies should conduct independent cross-validation in separate samples from Saudi Arabia and other Arabic-speaking countries to confirm the generalizability, and cross-cultural validity of the instrument.

title: Neutralization of IL-17A Ameliorates PM2.5-Induced Cardiac Inflammation and Fibrosis in Rats by Suppressing the TXNIP/NLRP3 Signaling Pathway.
authorString: Ba AS, Wu M, Li WC, Li WY, Ma D, Wang Y, Chen ZZ.

journal.title: The Kaohsiung journal of medical sciences

abstractText: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) pollution is a major environmental risk factor for cardiovascular diseases. Exposure can cause cardiac inflammation and fibrosis. However, whether interleukin-17A (IL-17A) contributes to these effects is unclear. Here, a rat cardiac injury model was established by intratracheal instillation of PM2.5, and an IL-17A neutralizing antibody was administered. PM2.5 exposure increased the proportion of splenic CD4<sup>+</sup>IL-17A<sup>+</sup> T cells and IL-17A/TRAF6 expression in cardiac tissue, with impaired cardiac function, myocardial inflammatory infiltration, collagen deposition, and increased expression of α-SMA and Collagen I/III. Cardiac tissue exhibited increased oxidative stress, enhanced NF-κB activation, elevated IL-6 and IL-1β, upregulated TXNIP, and activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome and pyroptosis-related proteins (ASC, cleaved Caspase-1 p20, GSDMD-N, and IL-18). Neutralizing IL-17A reversed these abnormalities and improved cardiac function. In vitro, IL-17A upregulated TXNIP/NLRP3 and increased the expression of inflammatory cytokines and extracellular matrix components in neonatal rat cardiac fibroblasts (NRCFs), whereas TXNIP knockdown reversed these effects. These results identify IL-17A as a key driver of PM2.5-induced cardiac inflammation and fibrosis, and targeting the IL-17A-TXNIP/NLRP3 axis may offer a new approach to treating PM2.5-related cardiac injury.

title: Atorvastatin inhibits PASMC proliferation in pulmonary hypertension via the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3/IL-1β pathway.
authorString: Cai Z, Chen Z, Lian G, Zhang Y, Luo L, Huang B.
abstractText: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a progressive disorder leading to right heart failure. This study explored how atorvastatin (ATO) alleviates PH using a multidisciplinary approach. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and dynamics analysis were employed to identify ATO targets. A PH rat model was established via monocrotaline (40 mg/kg) subcutaneous injection, and animals were divided into CT, PH, and ATO (10 mg/kg/day) groups. Hemodynamics, histopathology, and immunofluorescence were evaluated. In vitro, pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMCs) were exposed to PDGF-BB (20 ng/ml) with or without ATO (10-8 M). Cell proliferation was measured by CCK-8 and PCNA expression, and key proteins in the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3/IL-1β pathway were analyzed via western blot. siRNA-NLRP3 was used to verify NLRP3's role in PASMCs proliferation. Network pharmacology identified 277 common targets, with KEGG analysis linking ATO to the NF-κB signaling pathway. Docking showed strong binding affinity between ATO and TLR4 (-6.3 kCal/mol) through non-covalent interactions with ASN464 and PHE487. In vivo, ATO reduced right ventricular systolic pressure, right ventricular hypertrophy and pulmonary artery thickening. Immunofluorescence confirmed NLRP3 co-localization with α-SMA+ PASMCs. ATO downregulated TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3/IL-1β protein expression in PH rats' lungs and PASMCs, and suppressed PDGF-BB-induced PASMCs proliferation via the pathway inhibition. Direct knockdown of NLRP3 reduced both PDGF-BB-induced and non-PDGF-BB-induced proliferation of PASMCs, and ATO primarily inhibited PASMCs proliferation through NLRP3. These findings demonstrate that ATO directly targets TLR4 to inhibit NF-κB/NLRP3/IL-1β signaling, thereby reducing PASMCs proliferation and suppressing PH progression.

title: Reproductive Health in Monogenic Kidney Disease: Practical Guidance for Fertility, Genetic Counseling, and Pregnancy Care.
authorString: Lobo AS, Norouzi S, Shah S.

journal.title: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN

abstractText: Monogenic kidney diseases, including autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), Alport spectrum disorders, Fabry disease, and monogenic podocytopathies presenting as focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), increasingly affect people of reproductive age. Reproductive care extends beyond pregnancy to fertility, menstrual and sexual health, contraception, assisted reproduction, inheritance counseling, and long-term shared decision-making. This review uses these four disease groups to illustrate distinct counseling challenges arising from autosomal dominant, X-linked, autosomal recessive, and genetically heterogenous inheritance, including the underrecognized disease burden in heterozygous women with X-linked Alport syndrome or Fabry's disease. Across diseases, adverse maternal and fetal outcomes are driven primarily by reduced kidney function, chronic hypertension, proteinuria, prior preeclampsia and major extrarenal disease, whereas genotype, inheritance pattern, and syndromic features further shape counseling and reproductive genetic decisions. Preconception counseling should integrate maternal risk stratification; discontinuation or planned transition of fetotoxic agents, such as renin-angiotensin system inhibitors, tolvaptan, SGLT2 inhibitors, mycophenolate, and migalastat; and genetic counseling that addresses recurrence risk, cascade testing, and reproductive options, including prenatal diagnosis and preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic disorders (PGT-M). During pregnancy, close co-management by nephrology, maternal-fetal medicine, and genetics is essential to control blood pressure, provide low-dose aspirin prophylaxis, monitor kidney function and proteinuria, distinguish preeclampsia from progressive glomerular disease, and anticipate disease-specific complications such as cyst infection, intracranial aneurysm, nephrotic syndrome, and cardiac arrhythmia. Postpartum care should include medication re-optimization, breastfeeding counseling, kidney and cardiovascular surveillance, and revisiting contraception and future reproductive goals. Reproductive decision-making should be nondirective and centered on patient values, access to care, and tolerance for uncertainty. Evidence remains limited, largely retrospective, and enriched for milder disease, particularly regarding fertility outcomes, male reproductive implications, the reproductive safety of emerging targeted therapies, and genotype-specific pregnancy risk, underscoring the need for prospective multicenter studies.

title: Barriers and Facilitators to Technology Use Among Caregivers of Homebound Older Adults: Descriptive Qualitative Study.
authorString: Katigbak C, Shenoy E, Ramaswamy P, Lee J, Milbury K, Scott K.
abstractText:
Background

Homebound older adults (≥60 y) and their informal family caregivers face multiple challenges in meeting their instrumental, emotional, and informational needs, which result in lower functional status, multiple comorbidities, and poorer mental health. Caregivers are tasked with providing uncompensated care for medically complex older adults, often without formal health care training. This circumstance may translate to high levels of burden and greater vulnerability to social isolation and loneliness, which may precipitate chronic stress and compromise caregiver health. In recent years, numerous health-focused technologies assisting with health-promoting behaviors such as physical activity, stress management, and nutritional tracking have emerged. However, little is known about how these tools are adopted by family caregivers of homebound older adults.

Objective

This descriptive qualitative study aimed to explore how caregivers of homebound older adults perceive technology in the context of supporting caregiving and aging in place through focus groups and one-on-one interviews.

Methods

We conducted a descriptive qualitative study using in-person and online video conference focus group methodology with 40 individuals (32 caregivers, 6 clinicians, and 2 additional key informants) to explore perspectives on caregivers' use of technology to support their caregiving activities. Participants completed a brief sociodemographic questionnaire prior to all interviews. Procedures for thematic analysis were used to analyze the data and identify emerging themes.

Results

Three main themes (and related subthemes) emerged from the data: (1) these technologies are not designed for people like us, (2) balancing the scales, and (3) preserving a sense of self. Caregivers' experiences with technology are marked by a paradox: the same technologies that can ease caregiving activities may also impose new burdens through additional costs, uncertainty, learning demands, and emotional strain.

Conclusions

Caregivers should not navigate these technological tensions alone. Realizing the promise of technology requires more than innovative tools-it demands caregiver-centered design, accessible and equitable implementation strategies, and sustained clinical and health system support to ensure that technology alleviates, rather than amplifies, caregiver burden.

title: Pre-pregnancy maternal steatotic liver disease and offspring neurodevelopmental disorders: a nationwide cohort study.
authorString: Chung GE, Cho A, Kim DH, Yu SJ, Kim YJ, Yoon JH, Han K, Cho EJ.
abstractText:
Background/purpose

Maternal metabolic health before pregnancy is increasingly linked to offspring neurodevelopment, but metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), the most common chronic liver disease worldwide, has not been examined in this context. We investigated whether maternal steatotic liver disease (SLD) phenotypes identified before pregnancy are associated with offspring neurodevelopmental disorders.

Methods

In this nationwide Korean cohort of 778,401 mother-child pairs, maternal pre-pregnancy phenotypes (no SLD, MASLD, and alcohol-involved SLD) were defined using the fatty liver index (FLI), cardiometabolic criteria, alcohol intake, and diagnostic codes. Offspring were followed through 2022 for registration-confirmed intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and for claims-based attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Cox regression estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with and without adjustment for body mass index (BMI), diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidemia in addition to other covariates.

Results

Without this adjustment, MASLD was associated with intellectual disability (HR 1.72, 95% CI 1.52-1.96), ASD (1.42, 1.22-1.66), and ADHD (1.22, 1.15-1.30). After this adjustment, HRs were 1.05 (0.89-1.24), 1.18 (0.98-1.44), and 1.09 (1.01-1.17), respectively. The ADHD estimate was smaller when at least two separate claims were required (1.06, 0.98-1.15). Estimates for alcohol-involved SLD were imprecise.

Conclusion

Pre-pregnancy MASLD was associated with higher risks of offspring neurodevelopmental disorders in analyses without adjustment for maternal BMI and metabolic conditions. These associations were substantially attenuated after adjustment; a modest ADHD association remained only under the least stringent claims-based definition and should be interpreted with caution. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant confirmation with pregnancy-specific exposure assessment and sibling-comparison designs.

title: Pharmacological Management of Atrial Fibrillation Across the Heart Failure Ejection Fraction Spectrum: Rate Control, Rhythm Control, and Beyond.
authorString: Barone G, Baldetti L, Falanga U, Pagnesi M, Rienstra M, Voors AA, Metra M.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

To summarise the contemporary pharmacological management of atrial fibrillation (AF) in heart failure (HF), focusing on rate and rhythm control and upstream therapies across the ejection fraction spectrum.

Recent findings

Rate control remains a cornerstone of AF management, particularly in permanent AF or haemodynamically fragile patients, with beta-blockers, digoxin, and non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers selected according to ejection fraction phenotype. Concurrently, increasing evidence supports early rhythm-control strategies because of their prognostic benefits in HF populations, with current guidelines reinforcing a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF)-guided approach to antiarrhythmic drug selection. Beyond conventional drugs, HF guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) is emerging as an important upstream pharmacological strategy for modulation of the arrhythmogenic substrate. AF management in HF requires an integrated, phenotype-oriented approach combining symptom control, thromboembolic prevention, and optimisation of GDMT. LVEF remains a key determinant of pharmacological safety and therapeutic selection, whereas haemodynamic status primarily guides acute management decisions.

title: Digital Health Interventions in Cardiovascular Prevention: Medication Adherence, Risk Factor Management, and Patient Engagement.
authorString: Baggett KH, Yan S, Suresh A, Kodukula SS, Marvel FA, Martin SS, Morgan J, Michos ED.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

Blood pressure (BP) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) are leading cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk factors yet remain suboptimally controlled. Digital health technologies may help bridge the gap between guideline recommendations and improved cardiovascular (CV) outcomes. We review digital health interventions for hypertension and dyslipidemia management.

Recent findings

Mobile health (mHealth) interventions, including Corrie, LINKED-BP, Hello Heart, and Mass General Brigham platforms, demonstrate meaningful improvements in BP and LDL-C, particularly when paired with clinical support. In contrast, low-intensity text messaging alone produces modest or inconsistent benefits. Electronic Health Record (EHR)-based alerts can support therapy intensification but require thoughtful integration and clinician co-design. Artificial Intelligence (AI) may identify nonadherence and automate prescription refills, although further study is needed. Equitable implementation among high-risk and underserved populations remains essential. Digital health can promote treatment adherence, patient activation, earlier intervention, and access to care, with potential to improve CVD prevention at scale.

title: Heart Regeneration: Endogenous and Exogenous Mechanisms and Their Significance for Cyanotic Congenital Heart Disease.
authorString: Deng YS, Sun JS, Zhao QX, Li G.
abstractText: Myocardial remodeling and the limited regenerative capacity of mammalian cardiomyocytes constitute major barriers to heart failure therapy. Current therapies cannot reliably restore lost cardiomyocytes, and advanced heart failure may ultimately require mechanical circulatory support or transplatation. This review synthesizes recent advances in endogenous cardiac regeneration mechanisms, focusing on three key regulatory pathways: intracellular signaling, extracellular matrix (ECM) interactions, and exogenous cell-based therapies. We examine strategies to enhance the reprogramming of non-cardiomyocytes into functional cardiomyocytes, leveraging insights from regeneration-competent animal models including zebrafish and neonatal mice. Additionally, we explore the emerging role of hypoxia as a pro-regenerative signal, particularly in the context of cyanotic congenital heart disease (CCHD) such as tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) and pulmonary atresia (PA) with intact ventricular septum or ventricular septal defects. While stem cell technologies and intrinsic cardiomyocyte proliferative mechanisms have shown preclinical promise, clinical translation remains fraught with challenges. This review aims to provide a comprehensive, integrated perspective on endogenous regeneration pathways and their therapeutic potential to transform heart failure management. We further emphasize the unique therapeutic value of these regenerative mechanisms in CCHD: chronic hypoxia triggers hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α)-mediated metabolic reprogramming and cell-cycle regulation, which paradoxically activates pro-regenerative signaling and establishes a transient myocardial regenerative window. This window can be harnessed via early neonatal surgical intervention to facilitate myocardial repair.

title: Combining shear wave elastography and ultrasound localization microscopy for liver fibrosis staging in a rat model.
authorString: Zhang Y, Lin H, Kong X, Wen H, Ma Z, Chen M, Chen S, Chen X, Liu Z.
abstractText:
Objective

Accurate staging of liver fibrosis (LF) remains a clinical challenge. This study aimed to quantitatively evaluate the diagnostic value of combining shear wave elastography (SWE) and ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) for LF staging across the full disease spectrum. We sought to integrate liver mechanical properties and microvascular structural parameters to build a multiparametric model for fibrosis staging.

Materials and methods

LF was induced in Sprague-Dawley rats and histologically staged according to the METAVIR system. A total of 62 rats were included in the final analysis. Both SWE and ULM were performed in each animal. Liver viscoelastic moduli were estimated from SWE data using SW-VEI-Net, a physics-informed neural network-based approach. ULM data were post-processed to reconstruct super-resolution images of the hepatic microvasculature, followed by quantitative analysis to extract microvascular structural parameters.

Results

Histology revealed fibrosis stages F0 (n = 10), F1 (n = 12), F2 (n = 19), F3 (n = 11), and F4 (n = 10). Compared with the single-modality SWE and ULM models, the multiparametric combined model achieved the highest numerical areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve across the four classification tasks: 0.93 for F0 versus F1-F4, 0.92 for F0-F1 versus F2-F4, 0.90 for F0-F2 versus F3-F4, and 0.89 for F0-F3 versus F4.

Conclusion

Combining SWE-derived viscoelastic parameters with ULM-derived microvascular features enabled multiparametric characterization of LF in this preclinical rat model. Independent validation in larger animal cohorts and, ultimately, human studies is essential before robust clinical conclusions can be drawn.

Key points

Question Can combining shear-wave elastography (SWE) and ULM improve the accuracy of LF staging? Findings By integrating viscoelastic and microvascular features, the SWE-ULM combined model achieved the highest numerical AUCs across all four fibrosis classifications in a rat model. Relevance statement The SWE and ULM combined model suggests potential value for LF staging by integrating viscoelastic and microvascular biomarkers, providing a basis for further investigation toward future clinical translation.

title: Atrial fibrosis, atrial fibrillation susceptibility, and molecular remodeling in female goats with cardiac TGF-β1 overexpression.
authorString: Regouski M, Fillmore J, Larsen R, Marriott C, Patrick T, Sweat A, Stott R, Thomas A, Van Wettere A, Cutler MJ, Rutigliano HM, Polejaeva IA.
abstractText: Atrial Fibrillation (AF) is the most common cardiac arrhythmia in adult humans. Atrial fibrosis plays a primary role in developing and sustaining this disease phenotype. Specifically, TGF-β1, a potent pro-fibrotic molecule, is implicated in cell turnover, increasing the amount of extracellular matrix in the heart. This increase leads to aberrant electrical signaling and can produce AF. In this study, we hypothesized that TGF-β1 modulates AF susceptibility in TGF-β1 transgenic goats and that genes related to TGF-β1 and AF would be differentially expressed when compared to wild-type (WT) controls. Transgenic (TG) female goats expressing the active form of human TGF-β1 under the control of the cardiac-specific α-myosin heavy chain (α-MHC) promoter and age-matched wild-type female goats were utilized in the study. Pacemakers were implanted in all animals for continuous arrhythmia monitoring and AF inducibility, which was evaluated using five separate 10 s bursts of atrial pacing (200-160 ms). Tissue samples were collected from both atria of TG and WT goats. RNA was extracted, and gene expression analyses were run on a selected panel of genes. Immunohistochemistry was performed on atrial tissue to evaluate for the presence of selected inflammatory markers to elucidate AF substrate in these animals. There was a significant increase in AF inducibility in both frequency and duration in TGF-β1 goats compared to their WT counterparts. There was no significant difference in the number of inflammatory cells tested by immunohistochemistry. Differentially expressed genes between the TG and WT groups were found in several functional categories including AF, apoptosis, extracellular matrix, inflammation, and TGF-β1.These data support the hypothesis that fibrosis is an important modulator of AF susceptibility. More specifically, an overexpression of TGF-β1 significantly increases expression levels of ECM proteins and TGF-β1 signaling modulators, adding to elevated AF risk without altering underlying inflammation.

title: Associations between biomarkers of vitamin K and cardiovascular disease risk factors: the role of lipids.
authorString: Michalopoulos V, Bondonno NP, Pokharel P, Lauridsen JA, Jakobsen J, Booth SL, Nielsen CFB, Kårhus LL, Møllehave LT, Jørgensen NR, Bjørnsbo KS, Brøns C, Hansen T, Vaag A, Linneberg A, Bjerregaard AA.
abstractText:
Purpose

Emerging evidence indicates that vitamin K is important not only for its role in blood coagulation activation, but also for cardiovascular health. However, the results are equivocal, and due to the lipophilic nature of vitamin K, adjustment for triglycerides may be important. We investigated the associations between levels of circulating vitamin K vitamers, phylloquinone (PK) and total menaquinones (MK), and dephospho-undercarboxylated matrix Gla protein (dp-ucMGP, a biomarker of functional vitamin K status), with multiple cardiovascular disease risk factors and adjusted for triglycerides.

Methods

From the population-based Inter99 cohort, 2,195 participants had available fasting blood samples from which dp-ucMGP, PK, and MK-4 to MK-10 were analysed (mean age, ± SD: 68, ± 7 years, 48% female). Cross-sectional associations with cardiovascular disease risk factors were examined per doubling of vitamin K biomarkers using multivariable regression models.

Results

Both PK and total MK were positively associated with hypertriglyceridemia: OR (95%CI) 1.91, (1.69, 2.18) and 13.1, (7.55, 23.4), respectively, but not measures of adiposity and diabetes.
