However, after triglyceride adjustment, higher PK and total MK were inversely associated with central obesity: 0.86, (0.79, 0.95) and 0.61, (0.37, 0.98), respectively, and diabetes: 0.81, (0.69, 0.95) and 0.33, (0.13, 0.81), respectively. Higher dp-ucMGP was associated with hypertriglyceridemia: 1.50, (1.08, 2.09). After adjustment for triglycerides, higher dp-ucMGP remained associated with central obesity: 2.81, (2.16, 3.70) and obesity: 3.31, (2.50, 4.42).

Conclusion

After accounting for triglycerides, both PK and total MK were inversely associated with measures of adiposity and diabetes, suggesting that blood triglyceride levels need to be accounted for when considering circulating vitamin K levels. Higher dp-ucMGP, reflecting reduced vitamin K-dependent MGP carboxylation, was associated with adiposity markers independent of triglycerides.

title: Demographic, comorbidity, and temporal trends in anterior (ALIF) versus posterior (PLIF/TLIF) single-level lumbar interbody fusion: a retrospective analysis from 2015 to 2023.
authorString: Champigneulle O, Yusupov D, Johnson M, Budin JS, Mastrokostas LE, Xavier J, Monas A, Baek G, Mastrokostas PG, Oyekan A, Varthi A, Bou Monsef J, Razi AE, Ng MK.

journal.title: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society

abstractText:
Purpose

The aim of this study is to characterize national demographic and comorbidity profiles associated with anterior lumbar interbody fusion (ALIF) versus posterior interbody fusion (PLIF/TLIF) and evaluate temporal utilization patterns.

Methods

Using a commercial insurance database from 2015 to 2023, adults undergoing single-level ALIF or posterior interbody fusion were identified. Univariate tests compared baseline characteristics. Annual utilization trends were estimated with Poisson regression or negative binomial regression if overdispersion was present. Significance was set at P < 0.05.

Results

Among 407,319 patients, 133,323 underwent ALIF and 273,996 underwent posterior interbody fusion. Mean age was higher for posterior interbody fusion (61.8 vs. 59.5 years; P < 0.001), as was mean Elixhauser Comorbidity Index (5.3 ± 3.6 vs. 5.2 ± 3.6; P < 0.001). Sex distribution and rheumatoid arthritis were similar (P > 0.05 for all). Posterior interbody fusion patients more frequently had obesity, diabetes, hypertension, COPD, chronic kidney disease, congestive heart failure, coronary artery disease, osteoporosis, and tobacco use (P < 0.001 for all). ALIF procedures increased at an average annual rate of 6.66% (95% CI, 4.60-8.47; P < 0.001), whereas posterior interbody fusion increased 1.98% per year (95% CI, -0.19-4.19; P = 0.075); the annual growth-rate difference (ALIF - posterior interbody fusion) was 4.68% points (95% CI, 1.71-6.98; P < 0.001).

Conclusions

In this national sample, posterior interbody fusion was more commonly used in older, more medically complex patients, while both approaches grew over time with faster growth for ALIF and increasing ALIF share. These descriptive patterns outline contemporary selection of anterior versus posterior approaches and motivate outcome-focused, risk-adjusted studies in key subgroups.

title: Clinical pharmacology of antidiabetic drugs: an update.
authorString: Wichaiyo S.
abstractText:
Purpose

This review describes the updated pharmacology of antidiabetic drugs and its translation into clinical applications.

Methods

English language literature published from January 1, 1998 to July 25, 2026 was collected using PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Ovid. Research articles, reviews, and clinical practice guidelines were included for discussion.

Results

Currently, ultra-long-acting basal insulins are emerging, allowing less frequent injections. Glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), tirzepatide, and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) have novel pharmacodynamic properties and clinical evidence of cardiorenal and metabolic benefits, supporting their important roles in individuals with type 2 diabetes (T2D) who have high cardiorenal risk. Because of their effects on weight reduction, GLP-1RAs (semaglutide, liraglutide, and orforglipron) and tirzepatide are approved for the treatment of obesity. Furthermore, SGLT2is (empagliflozin, dapagliflozin, and sotagliflozin) provide cardiorenal benefits, with supporting potential mechanisms, in individuals with heart failure and chronic kidney disease. Conventional oral drugs (e.g., metformin, thiazolidinediones, dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors, sulfonylureas, meglitinides, and α-glucosidase inhibitors) lack sufficient pharmacologic and clinical data on cardiorenal benefits, suggesting their roles as adjunctive therapies. Novel candidates, including triple incretin hormone agonists (acting on GLP-1, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide [GIP], and glucagon receptors), GLP-1RA-GIP antagonism-based therapies, amylin analogues, and new dual SGLT1/2 inhibitors, show promising results for glycemic control and weight loss.

Conclusion

Overall, a comprehensive understanding of the pharmacologic characteristics of antidiabetic drugs promotes appropriate drug use for the management of T2D and cardiometabolic diseases and helps avoid undesirable events. Ongoing investigations of novel approaches may contribute to improved patient care in the future.

title: Imaging-based epicardial adipose tissue assessment and serum adipokines in postoperative atrial fibrillation after coronary artery bypass grafting.
authorString: Tekin KA, Yiğit F, Güneş A, Zengin A, Karagöz A, Pençe ME, Hacımustafaoğlu F, Aksoy R, Rabuş MB.

journal.title: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging

abstractText: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is a common complication after cardiac surgery. We evaluated the associations of preoperative epicardial adipose tissue thickness (EATT), measured by transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) and multislice computed tomography (MSCT), and circulating adipokines with POAF after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), and compared the imaging methods. This prospective observational cohort included 96 consecutive eligible adults without prior atrial fibrillation who underwent elective isolated CABG. EATT was measured preoperatively by TTE and MSCT, and serum adiponectin, leptin, and resistin concentrations were determined. POAF was recorded during the first postoperative week. POAF occurred in 26 patients (27.1%). EATT measured by both methods was higher in patients who developed POAF. In multivariable analysis, EATT measured by TTE (odds ratio, 2.05; 95% confidence interval, 1.45-2.89; p < 0.001) and age (odds ratio, 1.08; 95% confidence interval, 1.00-1.156; p = 0.040) independently predicted POAF. The area under the curve was 0.818 for TTE (cutoff, 6.55 mm; sensitivity, 73.1%; specificity, 87.1%) and 0.787 for MSCT (cutoff, 6.22 mm; sensitivity, 80.8%; specificity, 75.7%), with no significant difference (p = 0.127). Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of - 0.016 mm. Serum adipokine concentrations were not associated with POAF. Increased EATT and older age independently predicted POAF after isolated CABG. TTE showed performance comparable to MSCT and may provide a practical, radiation-free approach to preoperative EATT assessment. Larger multicenter studies are needed.

title: Dual-channel surface-enhanced Raman immunoassay for simultaneous determination of atrial-fibrillation-associated NT-proBNP and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I in artificial serum.
authorString: Qin L, Mou Y, Guo Y, Ma Z.

journal.title: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications

abstractText: Atrial fibrillation is associated with myocardial wall stress and low-grade injury, yet parallel measurement of N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) generally requires separate immunoassays. We developed a single-chamber, dual-channel surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) immunoassay that combines antibody-functionalised magnetic capture beads with Au@Ag nanotags encoded by 4-mercaptobenzonitrile at 2227 cm<sup>-1</sup> and 4-mercaptobenzoic acid at 1077 cm<sup>-1</sup>. A 9 × 9 full-factorial calibration design spanning 0-10 000 pg per mL NT-proBNP and 0-500 pg per mL hs-cTnI was executed across three independently prepared tag lots. Ten spatial spectra were aggregated at the sample level, preprocessed and quantified by a batch-grouped partial least-squares model. Limits of detection were 6.30 pg mL<sup>-1</sup> for NT-proBNP and 0.46 pg mL<sup>-1</sup> for hs-cTnI; corresponding limits of quantification were 18.7 and 1.35 pg mL<sup>-1</sup>. Across matrix lots and concentration levels, recoveries were 93.1-107.8% and total coefficients of variation were 4.8-9.4%. Thirty-six independently prepared, blinded artificial-serum specimens representing four dual-biomarker phenotypes were compared with electrochemiluminescence and chemiluminescent microparticle immunoassays. Under an equal-error-variance assumption, Deming slopes were 0.963 and 1.012, concordance correlation coefficients were 0.9951 and 0.9930, and concentration-quadrant agreement was 35/36. Grouped validation and specimen-level comparison assessed the dual readout without treating spatial spectra as independent replicates. This architecture provides a controlled route to simultaneous cardiac-biomarker measurement in artificial serum.

title: Association Between Socioeconomic Status and Dysphagia Among Japanese Adults.
authorString: Kitamura H, Tanaka K, Ihara Y, Kimura E, Kawamoto R, Miyake Y.
abstractText: Socioeconomic status (SES) is a well-established determinant of various health outcomes; however, its association with dysphagia remains poorly understood. We examined the association of household income and educational attainment with the prevalence of dysphagia among community-dwelling Japanese adults. This cross-sectional study included a total of 9,912 adults (4,225 men aged 21-95 years and 5,687 women aged 20-91 years). Dysphagia was assessed using the 10-item Eating Assessment Tool. SES was evaluated by self-reported household income and educational attainment. Logistic regression analysis was performed, stratified by age (younger: <65 years; older: ≥65 years) and sex. Models were adjusted for age, smoking status, alcohol consumption, leisure-time physical activity, living alone, number of medications, toothbrushing frequency, self-reported bilateral posterior occlusal support, hypertension, dyslipidemia, diabetes mellitus, and body mass index. In both sexes, household income was significantly associated with lower odds of dysphagia among participants aged ≥ 65 years, but not among those aged < 65 years. Conversely, an inverse association between educational attainment and the prevalence of dysphagia was consistently observed in men regardless of age, whereas this association was only observed among women aged < 65 years. Higher household income was inversely associated with dysphagia among men and women aged ≥ 65 years. Higher educational attainment was inversely associated with dysphagia among men regardless of age and women aged < 65 years.

title: Shared additive- and variance-associated genetic architecture of cardiac structure and function
authorString: Tsaggaris J, Mimouni N, Judy RL, Xue D, Morley MP, Wang X, Cotney JL, Kelly DP, Day SM, Cappola TP, Penn Medicine BioBank, Damrauer SM, Levin MG.
abstractText: Cardiac remodeling underlies cardiomyopathy and heart failure, yet how common genetic effects are organized across the four chambers, and whether they influence phenotypic variability beyond additive genetic effects, remains unclear. We analyzed 22 cardiac magnetic resonance phenotypes in up to 77,271 UK Biobank participants. Additive mapping identified 748 locus–trait associations across 239 regions. Multivariate fine-mapping revealed that 96% of signals showed effects across multiple cardiac chambers, while resolving independent signals with distinct anatomical profiles, including predominantly atrial and ventricular signals at RBM20. Fine-mapped signal sharing formed three robust communities corresponding broadly to atrial function, chamber remodeling and ventricular systolic function. Variance mapping identified 19 associations, 13 without a nearby additive signal. Individual variance loci and polygenic effects generalized to clinical echocardiographic phenotypes and outcomes in the Penn Medicine Biobank. These findings reveal cardiac common-variant architecture as broadly shared yet locally heterogeneous and identify phenotypic variability as a partly distinct genetic dimension.

title: Hypertension and obstructive sleep apnea among adults with overweight or obesity in Tiko Health District, Cameroon: a community-based cross-sectional study
authorString: Mbapah LT, Salifou AMZ, Toh TF, Shu BN, Tsague MS, Mokossa HO, Etaka ST, Igbokwe E, Nkoke C, Noubiap JJ.
abstractText: Background Hypertension, excess adiposity, and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) frequently coexist and contribute to cardiovascular risk, yet community-based data on their combined burden in Cameroon remain scarce. The study assessed the prevalence of hypertension, adiposity, and OSA risk among adults in the Tiko Health District, Cameroon. Methods This community-based cross-sectional study included adults aged ≥ 18 years who attended a one-week health screening campaign in four health areas of the Tiko Health District, Cameroon, in August 2026. Anthropometric measures, cardiovascular risk factors, blood pressure, and sleep-related symptoms were assessed using standardized procedures. Body mass index (BMI) was categorized according to WHO criteria. Blood pressure was defined as the mean of two seated measurements, and hypertension was defined as a measured blood pressure ≥ 140/90 mmHg or current antihypertensive treatment. OSA risk was assessed with the STOP-BANG questionnaire, and excessive daytime sleepiness with the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS). Associations between adiposity and hypertension were evaluated using modified Poisson regression with robust variance to estimate adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs). Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05. Results Of 304 participants, 221 (72.7%) were female, and the mean age was 43.4 ± 16.2 years. BMI was available for 302 participants; 95/302 (31.5%) were overweight, and 120/302 (39.7%) had obesity. Hypertension was present in 110/304 participants (36.2%, 95% CI 31.0–41.7). Among participants with hypertension, 48/110 (43.6%) were aware, 29/110 (26.4%) were receiving treatment, and 11/110 (10.0%) were controlled. A positive STOP-BANG screen occurred in 115/299 participants (38.5%, 95% CI 33.1–44.1), and ESS > 10 was present in 46/304 (15.1%). After adjustment for age, sex, residence, and diabetes, hypertension prevalence did not differ markedly between overweight (aPR 0.90, 95% CI 0.60–1.33) and obesity (aPR 1.27, 95% CI 0.90–1.79) and BMI < 25 kg/m². Each 5-kg/m² higher BMI was associated with a 13% higher prevalence of hypertension (aPR 1.13, 95% CI 1.03–1.24). Greater waist circumference (aPR 1.10 per 10 cm, 95% CI 1.02–1.20) and waist-to-height ratio (aPR 1.24 per 0.1 unit, 95% CI 1.13–1.37) were similarly associated with hypertension. Obesity was also associated with higher mean systolic blood pressure (β 9.5 mmHg, 95% CI 4.0–15.1) and diastolic blood pressure (β 7.8 mmHg, 95% CI 4.3–11.3) compared with BMI < 25 kg/m². Conclusions Among adults attending community screening, excess adiposity, hypertension, previously undetected high blood pressure, and elevated OSA risk were common. The accompanying gaps in hypertension awareness, treatment, and control underscore the need for community-based detection, confirmatory blood-pressure assessment, cardiovascular risk reduction, and referral for objective sleep evaluation.

title: Background and Behavioral Cue Weighting in Current Versus Age-60 Disease-Risk Judgments: Two Cross-Disease Scenario Studies
authorString: Cao W, Fu M, Luo Y, Lei C.
abstractText: Background Disease-risk judgments combine stable background characteristics with behaviors that may change. We examined whether cue weights differed between judgments of current risk and risk at age 60. Because the age-60 prompt changes both temporal perspective and target age, construal-level theory was treated as one interpretive lens rather than the mechanism tested. Methods We reanalyzed two archived questionnaire data sets. Study 1 included 1,190 undergraduates who evaluated hypertension and osteoporosis; Study 2 included 869 participants who evaluated nasopharyngeal carcinoma and gallstones. Complementary questionnaire forms paired one disease with a current-risk judgment and the other with an age-60 judgment. Random allocation was not documented. Temporal frame was form-defined; sex, ancestry, family history, and behavioral scores were measured characteristics. Perceived likelihood was the primary outcome. Disease-specific linear models used continuous behavioral cues and HC3 robust standard errors; cross-disease models used participant-clustered standard errors. False-discovery-rate correction was applied within defined testing families. Results Guangdong ancestry was more strongly associated with perceived likelihood of nasopharyngeal carcinoma in the age-60 frame than in the current frame ( B  = 0.645, SE  = 0.173, 95% CI 0.305 to 0.985, p  = 0.000197, q  = 0.001577). The frame-by-female-sex interaction for osteoporosis was also supported ( B  = 0.638, SE  = 0.204, 95% CI 0.237 to 1.038, p  = 0.001791, q  = 0.008588), although sample-restriction sensitivity remained. The hypertension frame-by-salt-intake estimate was smaller and did not survive multiplicity correction ( B  = 0.187, SE  = 0.092, 95% CI 0.005 to 0.368, p  = 0.043616, q  = 0.096388). No key gallstone interaction was detected. Most cross-disease three-way interactions were non-significant or multiplicity-sensitive, and outcome components showed different patterns. Conclusions The relative weight of background and behavioral cues differed between current and age-60 disease-risk judgments. Differences were clearest for Guangdong ancestry in nasopharyngeal carcinoma and female sex in osteoporosis; the hypertension pattern was weaker, and no consistent gallstone pattern emerged. The findings suggest that health messages may work better when the age frame matches the risk cue and links it to clear preventive or screening action. Because the age-60 prompt also changes objective age-related risk, direct intervention testing is needed.

title: Neighborhood Disadvantage, Identity-based Resilience, and Hypertension: The Healthy Aging with Resilient Identities (HARI) Study
authorString: Pleasants H, Bey GS.
abstractText: Introduction . Perceived neighborhood problems (PNP), such as safety concerns and limited resources, have been linked to elevated hypertension risk through chronic stress pathways. The Identity Vitality Pathology (IVP) framework captures the extent to which individuals experience threats to identity, belonging, and psychosocial vitality in the face of structural disadvantage, and may modify these pathways. Methods . We conducted logistic regression analyses to estimate the association between PNP and hypertension. Models were stratified by race and gender groups (Black women, Black men, White women, White men). Both main effects models and adjusted models included an interaction term between PNP and Identity Vitality Pathology score (IVPS) to assess effect modification. Adjusted models controlled for age, education, perceived support, financial strain, physical activity, diabetes, smoking status, and self-rated health. Interaction terms were used to evaluate whether the association between PNP and hypertension varied by levels of IVPS within each race/gender group. Results . Higher PNP was associated with increased odds of hypertension among White women and men, but not consistently among Black women and men. Identity state moderated this association only among Black women, such that each 1-SD increase in IVPS score was associated with 59% lower odds of hypertension at the highest level of PNP (aOR-0.41; 95% CI: 0.19, 0.88), with no meaningful moderation observed in other groups. Conclusion . Identity state may moderate the association between subjective neighborhood disadvantage and hypertension, particularly among Black women, representing a potentially novel, modifiable protective factor among multiply marginalized persons living in communities with increased risk for hypertension.

title: Risk of Hysterectomy Following Endometrial Ablation: A 10-Year Retrospective Analysis
authorString: Hackett A, Murphy C, Lundsberg L, Clark M, Johnson-Murray M.
abstractText: Purpose This study assessed indication for hysterectomy following failed endometrial ablation and identified risk factors for therapy failure. Methods A retrospective cohort study of 1054 patients undergoing endometrial ablation from January 1, 2011, to January 1, 2021, within the Yale New Haven Health system was conducted using chi-square and ANOVA tests. No interventions were made in this study. Results The hysterectomy rate amongst endometrial ablation patients was 18% (n = 190). Each additional year post ablation decreased the risk of subsequent hysterectomy by 5% (aHR 0.95, p < .05). Patients with BMI of 30-39.9 had a 61% increased risk of subsequent hysterectomy (aHR 1.61, p = .003), and a BMI ≥ 40 had a 108% increased risk (aHR 2.08, p = .002). A history of diabetes showed a nonsignificant trend toward increased risk of hysterectomy (aHR 1.44, p = 0.09). The primary indication for hysterectomy after ablation was persistent AUB (68.9%). The primary uterine pathology identified at time of hysterectomy was leiomyoma (61.1%). Conclusion Endometrial ablation has become a popular choice for treatment of abnormal uterine bleeding given its minimally invasive nature and cost-effectiveness. This study demonstrated 1 in 5 women will require hysterectomy post ablation. Risk factors including younger age, presence of leiomyoma or adenomyosis, and obesity, can increase patient’s risk of requiring hysterectomy for management. There was no significant difference in parity, race-ethnicity, history of hypertension, diabetes, or smoking, within the two cohorts. These findings can be used to enhance patient counseling and selection of appropriate candidates for endometrial ablation.

title: Diversity and Functionality of the Gut Microbiota in Hypertensive Patients from Different Regions of Peru
authorString: Marcos-Carbajal P, Villegas-Suarez MN, Rafael Ccama VV, Otiniano Trujillo MA, Huancahuire-Vega S, Chambi Quispe MS, Luque Arapa A, Ruiz Panaifo M, Diaz Rengifo PE, Sias Garay CE, Espinoza Rojas R, Tito R, Rohra Benitez S, Tapia Paniagua ST.
abstractText: Introduction Hypertension affects approximately 14.2% of people over 15 years of age in Peru, constituting a major public health issue. Recent evidence highlights the gut microbiome’s role in regulating blood pressure through bioactive metabolites that influence inflammation and metabolism. This study aims to characterize the gut microbiota of hypertensive adults from three Peruvian regions, contributing to the understanding of microbial influences on hypertension. Objective To analyze the composition and functionality of the gut microbiota in hypertensive and normotensive adults from different Peruvian regions, considering age, body mass index (BMI), and geographical location. Methods An observational, cross-sectional, and analytical study was conducted with 84 adults (46 hypertensive and 38 normotensive) from nine regions of Peru. Fecal samples were collected for 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing of the V3–V4 region. Alpha and beta diversity were evaluated using the Shannon index, UniFrac distances, and multivariate analyses. Microbial functional pathways were examined to identify potential metabolic differences between groups. Results The dominant phyla in all groups were Bacillota and Bacteroidota. At the genus level,  Streptococcus was associated with hypertensive patients with BMI ≥25, while  Alistipes appeared only in normotensive individuals with BMI <25. Alpha diversity was greater in hypertensive participants under 50 years and with BMI <25, while lower diversity was seen in normotensive adults over 50 and with BMI ≥25. Beta diversity analyses showed substantial overlap across hypertensive status, age, and regional groups, with no clear separation. Adjusted multivariable models confirmed no significant independent association between hypertension status and either alpha or beta diversity after accounting for age, BMI, and region, with region remaining the strongest independent correlate of community composition (R  2 = 16.3%, p = 0.001). Functional profiles were similar among groups, mainly involving carbohydrate, amino acid, and lipid metabolism, though BMI and age modulated these patterns. Conclusions Gut microbiota composition and diversity in this Peruvian cohort were associated not only with hypertension status but also with anthropometric and geographic factors. Despite similar functional profiles between groups, environmental and nutritional context appeared to have a greater influence than hypertension status alone. These exploratory, hypothesis-generating findings should be confirmed in larger, adjusted, longitudinal studies before informing preventive or therapeutic strategies for local settings.

title: When Less is More: A Physiology-Driven Approach to a 17-Hydroxylase Deficiency Case Series.
authorString: Bastien L, Sasidharan Pillai S, Geller D, Auchus R, Witchel S, Ahmet A.
abstractText:
Background

17-hydroxylase deficiency (17OHD) is a very rare form of congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) caused by autosomal recessive mutations in the cytochrome P450 family (CYP17A1). Despite low cortisol, adrenal insufficiency does not typically manifest because elevated corticosterone, a weaker glucocorticoid (GC), exerts GC effects. Exogenous GC are the foundation of treatment but can be associated with significant side effects. Published literature regarding management strategies is limited.

Case presentations

We describe three female adolescents treated for 17OHD with different GC regimens. All patients presented at age 14 with delayed puberty, hypertension, and primary ovarian insufficiency. Patient 1 was initially treated with physiological hydrocortisone divided three times daily (10 mg/m2/d) and spironolactone 100 mg/d, separately and combined, which did not lower her blood pressure (BP). Eventually, a combination of physiological hydrocortisone once daily (8.8 mg/m2/d) and gradual titration to a higher spironolactone dose (100 mg bid) normalized her BP (115/75 mmHg) with no side effects. Patient 2 was treated with dexamethasone 0.25 mg daily for 10 years with poor follow-up and developed multiple complications related to supraphysiological GC use. She was transitioned and successfully treated with hydrocortisone 10 mg every morning and 5 mg every afternoon with a normal BP and potassium for over a year. Patient 3 was treated with cortisone acetate for 2.6 years and then with dexamethasone for about 10 months before discontinuation of GC and transition to spironolactone monotherapy. Her potassium and BP remained normal.

Conclusion

In conclusion, 17OHD is a rare form of CAH, with about 500 published cases and limited established management guidance. Our cases highlight the importance of considering the pathophysiology of 17OHD when developing a management plan; a supraphysiological GC therapy may not be necessary to manage the hypertension and hypokalemia. Physiological hydrocortisone dosing lowers but does not normalize DOC production allowing DOC to exert GC effects. Physiological hydrocortisone and/or monotherapy with mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists both mitigate GC-related side effects, avoid adrenal suppression, and minimize risk for adrenal crisis in patients with 17OHD.

title: Inadvertent Left Ventricular Pacing Through an Unrecognized Sinus Venosus Atrial Septal Defect.
authorString: Viscogliosi S, Vincent M, Vedrenne G, Mirailles R, Pezel T, Thibault H, Martial PJ.
abstractText:
Background

Inadvertent left ventricular (LV) lead placement is rare but exposes patients to systemic thromboembolism.

Case summary

An 89-year-old man received a dual-chamber pacemaker for atrial fibrillation with paroxysmal complete heart block. Severe right atrial dilatation prevented right ventricular lead placement, and the operator converted to a sheath-delivered "left bundle branch area" approach. Seven months later, imaging unexpectedly showed the lead coursing from the superior vena cava through an unrecognized superior sinus venosus defect into the left atrium, across the mitral valve, into the LV. Transesophageal echocardiography confirmed a 30 × 20 mm superior sinus venosus defect with partial anomalous pulmonary venous return.

Discussion

A paced right bundle branch block pattern is expected during left bundle branch area pacing, and activation-time criteria may be falsely reassuring when the lead paces the LV endocardium directly. Atrial septal defect screening is warranted whenever right-sided dilatation is unexplained.

title: Dynamic Transmitral Gradient From Eccentric Aortic Regurgitation Resolved by Valve-in-Valve TAVR.
authorString: Ray I, Shoura S, Saravanabavanandan R, Coombes K, Sisodia R, Grzeskowiak MZ, Mungee S, Barzallo MA.
abstractText:
Background

Bioprosthetic aortic valve degeneration can present as isolated regurgitant failure, and an eccentric jet may raise the transmitral gradient, mimicking mitral stenosis.

Case summary

An 84-year-old man presented with acute heart failure 12 years after surgical aortic valve replacement. Echocardiography showed a degenerated Trifecta bioprosthesis with an immobile leaflet causing severe eccentric aortic regurgitation, whose jet impinged on the anterior mitral leaflet and produced severe functional mitral stenosis. Given high surgical risk, the heart team performed transfemoral valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement.

Discussion

Trifecta leaflet tear causes regurgitant rather than stenotic failure; an eccentric jet can raise the transmitral gradient independent of the Austin Flint murmur. Valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement eliminated the regurgitation, improved leaflet mobility, and reduced the mean mitral gradient from 17 to 6 mm Hg, with complete symptom resolution.

Take-home message

Eccentric aortic regurgitation can cause a reversible rise in transmitral gradient; treating it can resolve apparent mitral stenosis without mitral intervention.

title: Cost-Minimization and Budget-Impact Analysis of N-Terminal Pro B-Type Natriuretic Peptide Biomarker Assay for the Risk Assessment and Monitoring of Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension in the Australian Healthcare Setting.
authorString: Papadopoulos G, Barman P, Gupta A, Rathi H.
abstractText:
Objectives

N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) is a biomarker for risk stratification in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Published evidence supports NT-proBNP as a complementary parameter within the multiparameter risk stratification framework recommended by the 2022 European Society of Cardiology/European Respiratory Society guidelines, used alongside transthoracic echocardiography (TTE). This study compares the financial implications of a publicly funded NT-proBNP biomarker assay with a TTE-based approach in patients with PAH from the Australian healthcare perspective.

Methods

The cost-minimization analysis estimates the annual per-patient cost of risk assessment in PAH. Additionally, a 6-year budget-impact analysis was conducted using an epidemiological approach. The model compared publicly funded NT-proBNP-guided risk assessment in PAH with a reference scenario using TTE alone, with NT-proBNP estimated to replace 1.5 TTE tests per patient annually. Model inputs were derived from Australian public databases and published literature, with costs adjusted to 2025 Australian dollars.

Results

The unit costs for NT-proBNP and TTE tests were $58.50 and $258.70, respectively. The annual per-patient cost with public funding of NT-proBNP was $880.75 compared with $1034.80 without NT-proBNP, leading to a yearly cost saving of $154.05. The budget-impact model estimated 2450 patients with PAH in year 1, increasing to 3619 by year 6. Assuming 90% uptake rate of NT-proBNP testing, the net savings to the Medicare Benefits Schedule ranged from $288 549 in year 1 to $426 190 in year 6 (85% Medicare Benefits Schedule rebate applied).

Conclusions

Routine NT-proBNP testing for risk assessment and monitoring in PAH could result in considerable cost savings of $2.3 million over 6 years.

title: Clinical Characteristics of Mediastinal Paragangliomas: A retrospective study.
authorString: Li T, Cui Y, Zhou Y, Hu M, Li Z, Chen S, Chang X, Tong A.
abstractText:
Background

Studies focusing on mediastinal paragangliomas are limited. In this study, we describe the clinical, pathological, and genetic characteristics of mediastinal paragangliomas.

Methods

Clinical data from all patients with extrapericardial mediastinal paragangliomas at a single center were retrospectively analyzed. Germline variants were assessed using next-generation sequencing and Sanger sequencing of blood samples. Patients were grouped according to genetic variants and tumor location, and clinical characteristics were compared.

Results

22 patients (male:female ratio, 8:14) were included in the study, with a mean age of 41.4 years. Hypertension was present in 16 patients (72.7%), and 13 (59.1%) exhibited typical catecholamine-related symptoms. Tumors were located in the anterior, middle, and posterior mediastinum in 1 (4.5%), 4 (18.2%), and 17 (77.3%) cases, with an average size of 5.3±1.7 cm. Multiple tumors were identified in 6 patients. Catecholamine-producing tumors were observed in 17/21 (81.0%) patients. Surgical resection was performed in 20 (90.9%) patients. No postoperative local recurrences were observed. Metastasis occurred in 2/18 (11.1%) cases. Eleven patients underwent genetic testing; six harbored SDHx mutations. Compared with anterior and middle mediastinal tumors, posterior mediastinal tumors were associated with higher rates of typical symptoms (12/17 vs. 1/5, p = 0.043) and catecholamine-producing function (17/17 vs. 0/4, p < 0.001), as well as higher levels of 24-hour urinary norepinephrine (5.10 × ULN vs. 0.56 × ULN, p = 0.037).

Conclusion

Mediastinal paragangliomas are rare and are frequently associated with SDHx variants. Posterior mediastinal tumors are predominantly functional and noradrenergic; recognizing these features may facilitate diagnosis.

title: Percutaneous Rescue of Acute Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Obstruction After Mitral Valve-In-Valve Replacement.
authorString: Mangiameli A, Bernardini V, Azzano A, Miccichè E, Brscic E, Cascella A, Mollace R, Cao D.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText:
Background

Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO) is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication of transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR). Mitral valve-in-valve procedures are generally associated with a lower risk of LVOTO because of the predictable geometry provided by the surgical bioprosthesis, yet severe obstruction may still occur and precipitate abrupt hemodynamic collapse.

Case

A 79-year-old woman with a degenerated 27-mm Carpentier-Edwards Perimount mitral bioprosthesis presented with acute decompensated heart failure due to severe bioprosthetic mitral stenosis. Following multidisciplinary Heart Team evaluation, she was considered not a candidate for redo mitral valve surgery and underwent urgent transseptal valve-in-valve TMVR with a 26-mm balloon-expandable SAPIEN valve.

Intervention

Immediately after valve deployment, severe LVOTO developed, with an invasive peak-to-peak LV-aortic gradient of 120 mmHg. A mechanism-guided percutaneous rescue strategy was undertaken. Correction of the structural component of obstruction reduced the gradient to 60 mmHg. Persistent obstruction suggested a significant dynamic contribution, prompting selective septal branch coil embolization, which further reduced the gradient to 20 mmHg and resulted in immediate hemodynamic stabilization.

Conclusion

Severe LVOTO after valve-in-valve TMVR may reflect both structural and dynamic mechanisms. Persistence of significant obstruction after structural correction should prompt consideration of a dynamic component and may guide effective rescue therapy.

title: Cardiometabolic Outcomes in Dahl Salt-Sensitive Rat Pregnancies: Impact of a Maternal Hypertensive High-Fat Diet.
authorString: Gomes VCL, Bailey VN, Kim LG, Lopez KM, Crandell F, Garver H, Mahlmeister M, Borne BM, Lauver DA, Krieger-Burke T, Watts SW, Fink GD.

journal.title: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism

abstractText: Excessive adiposity and chronic hypertension are major risk factors of preeclampsia, a leading hypertensive disorder of pregnancy. Yet, mechanisms underlying the complex interplay between adiposity, chronic hypertension, and preeclampsia remain incompletely understood, partly due to the limited availability of experimental models that capture these interactions. Herein, we explored maternal cardiometabolic adaptations in high-fat diet (HFD)-fed Dahl Salt-Sensitive rats, an established model of HFD-associated chronic hypertension. We hypothesized that HFD-fed dams would display a superimposed preeclampsia-like phenotype compared to control diet (CD)-fed Dahl Salt-Sensitive females. HFD-fed dams exhibited attenuated gestational weight gain, increased ketogenesis, cardiovascular dysfunction and blunted uteroplacental vascular adaptation to pregnancy. HFD feeding was associated with high blood pressure pre-pregnancy and during most of gestation and lactation. Interestingly, however, both groups displayed a drop in blood pressure during late gestation, with lower blood pressure nadir and lower urine protein excretion in HFD-fed dams. Short-term pregnancy outcomes were largely preserved in HFD-fed dams, including litter size, pup viability, and placental efficiency. Long-term, dietary normalization failed to reverse the hypertensive phenotype of HFD-exposed dams, with blood pressure remaining 10-15 mmHg higher than controls for at least 14 weeks post-weaning. In conclusion, HFD-fed Dahl salt-sensitive females developed chronic hypertension and impaired metabolic and cardiovascular adaptations to pregnancy. Yet, neither CD- nor HFD-fed dams exhibited hallmark preeclampsia features, including late-gestation blood pressure rise, proteinuria, and fetal growth restriction. This model therefore provides a valuable platform to investigate adaptive cardiometabolic mechanisms that may attenuate preeclampsia risk in obese and chronic hypertensive patients.

title: Association of decreased serum Netrin-1 with inflammatory markers, neurological severity, and 3-month outcome in hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage.
authorString: Li L, Cheng Y, Tian H, Bai X, Zhang L, Zheng M.
abstractText:
Objective

To compare serum Netrin-1 levels among hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage (HICH) patients, hypertensive patients without cerebrovascular lesions and healthy controls, and analyze its correlations with inflammatory markers, neurological deficit severity and 3-month functional prognosis.

Methods

This single-center retrospective cohort enrolled 294 participants from September 2021 to September 2022, including 98 HICH patients, 92 uncomplicated primary hypertension patients and 104 healthy subjects. Serum samples were collected within routine clinical time windows, yet the intervals from hemorrhage onset and acute treatments to blood collection were inconsistent. Multiple subgroup, correlation and prognostic analyses were conducted with exact p-values presented; p < 0.01 was set as a strict threshold for primary interpretations.

Results

HICH patients had markedly lower serum Netrin-1 than healthy controls (p < 0.001), with no significant difference versus hypertensive patients (p = 0.083). Netrin-1 was negatively correlated with NIHSS, mRS, IL-6 and CRP, and positively correlated with IL-10. Its concentrations declined progressively with aggravated neurological impairment. Multivariate regression identified low Netrin-1, high NIHSS and brainstem hemorrhage as independent predictors of poor 3-month outcome (GOS 1-3). The internal ROC analysis showed an AUC of 0.896 (95%CI 0.817-0.923).

Conclusion

Reduced serum Netrin-1 correlates with severe neurological damage and unfavorable 3-month prognosis in HICH, serving as an independent prognostic indicator after covariate adjustment. Restricted by retrospective single-center design, inconsistent sampling timing, insufficient outcome events and lack of external validation, Netrin-1 is merely an investigational biomarker rather than a validated clinical prognostic assay.

title: Right heart remodeling in Sugen/hypoxia rat model of severe pulmonary hypertension.
authorString: Olejnickova V, Kvasilova A, Naidu P, Perera N, Gregorovicova M, Bartos M, Miklovic M, Melenovský V, Talacko P, Papoušek F, Hrdlička J, Eckhardt A, Kolar F, Sedmera D.

journal.title: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology

abstractText: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) directly impacts the right heart through pressure overload. Unlike well-characterized remodeling of the left ventricle in systemic hypertension, PH-induced changes in the right heart are less understood. Here, we investigate chamber-specific alterations in the right atrium (RA) and right ventricle (RV) in a rat model of PH. PH was induced in 6-week-old male Wistar rats using Sugen/hypoxia (SuHx) treatment. Right heart pressure overload was confirmed by catheterization. Cardiac remodeling was characterized by using confocal microscopy, micro-CT, optical mapping, and proteomic mass spectrometry. The increase in right-heart mass was predominantly attributable to cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, with concomitant extracellular-matrix remodeling. Hypertrophy was associated with significantly elevated right heart pressures after SuHx treatment, further progressing during the subsequent normoxia. At the end of the PH protocol, electrophysiology analysis showed significant prolongation of the action potential in both the RA and RV. Proteomic analysis revealed pronounced alterations in the RV, with substantial overlap with the RA and LV, and more upregulated than downregulated proteins. GO analysis indicated increased expression of sarcomeric and fibrillar proteins and reduced expression of proteins related to oxidative energy production. In conclusion, myocardial remodeling in PH is based on cardiomyocyte hypertrophy rather than cell proliferation. Electrophysiological changes along with increased pressure in the right atrium might contribute to phenotype progression. Changes in proteome show commonalities and differences in RA and RV pressure-induced pathways that that warrant therapeutic exploration.

title: GCN5L1 Depletion Promotes Left Ventricular Fibrosis in Failing Hearts via Upregulation of RAB7A.
authorString: Sharifi-Sanjani M, Zhang M, Thapa D, Stoner MW, Bugga P, Manning JR, Mushala BAS, Bhattarai N, Scott I.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
journal.title: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
journal.isoabbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol

abstractText: Pathologic cardiac fibrosis is one of the key determinants of adverse remodeling and progression to heart failure. Although GCN5-like 1 (GCN5L1) is documented to regulate cardiac metabolic homeostasis, its role in myocardial remodeling and fibrosis is unknown. In a murine transverse aortic constriction (TAC) pressure overload model, GCN5L1 protein abundance was significantly reduced in the left ventricular (LV) tissues from wild type (WT) mice. This finding was concurrent with increased collagen 1α1 expression in the same tissues. Interestingly, LVs from cardiomyocyte-specific GCN5L1 knockout (GCN5L1 cKO) mice showed exacerbated TAC-induced collagen 1α1 expression among profibrotic genes identified by bulk RNA sequencing, when compared with corresponding WT mice. These finding are consistent with our previous report of increased fibrotic tissue and decreased fractional shortening (a marker of contractile function) in GCN5L1 cKO mice under TAC stress. Consistently, analysis of human hearts with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction demonstrated reduced GCN5L1 expression accompanied by increased collagen 1α1, revealing a conserved inverse relationship. In vitro, we further demonstrate that conditioned media collected from GCN5L1-depleted AC16 human ventricular cardiomyocyte-like cells induced upregulation of collagen 1α1 expression in human cardiac fibroblasts. Proteomic profiling of WT and GCN5L1 cKO cardiac tissues aligned with our in vitro findings in WT and GCN5L1 knockout (KO) mouse embryonic fibroblasts, revealing increased expression of lysosomal, endo-lysosomal, and autophagy markers (including RAB7A) in response to GCN5L1 deficiency. In vivo, RAB7A protein was increased following TAC, which was exacerbated in GCN5L1-deficient hearts under the same conditions. Furthermore, in human ventricular fibroblasts, TGF-β1 stimulated RAB7A and collagen 1α1 expression. Importantly, RAB7A knockdown attenuated TGF-β1-induced collagen 1α1, whereas GCN5L1 knockdown altered expression of fibrosis related markers and increased RAB7A without directly altering collagen expression. Collectively, these findings identify GCN5L1 as a negative regulator of pressure overload-induced cardiac fibrosis, and implicate a GCN5L1- RAB7A axis linking lysosomal pathways to collagen deposition in ventricular remodeling. These findings highlight a potential therapeutic target to attenuate LV fibrosis.

title: Elabela in pregnancy: Physiology, associated disorders and translational perspectives (Review).
authorString: Xie Y, Yang S, Meng C, Chen X, Long H, Wu H, Wang T.
abstractText: Elabela (ELA) has emerged as a critical regulator of reproductive success, signaling through the cognate apelin receptor (APJ) (encoded by the APLNR gene) to orchestrate embryonic development and placental function. The present narrative review summarizes evidence spanning from molecular mechanisms to clinical phenotypes, evaluating the role of ELA in both physiological pregnancy and major complications, including preeclampsia, fetal growth restriction and gestational diabetes, as well as emerging associations with placental disorders and early pregnancy loss. The present review addresses three key challenges: i) The receptor paradox in APJ‑low or APJ‑negative contexts; ii) inconsistencies among clinical ELA measurements; and iii) the need to distinguish direct ELA evidence from inference drawn from apelin studies. Current findings position ELA as a candidate biomarker and experimental therapeutic target; however, its clinical utility remains unproven due to pre‑analytical variability across sample types (plasma vs. serum), inconsistencies between detection platforms (ELISA vs. immunohistochemistry), and biological heterogeneity across specific disease subtypes (such as preeclampsia and heart failure). Future work should focus on defining receptor‑ and isoform‑specific signaling, standardizing ELA measurement and establishing pharmacokinetics, dose‑response relationships, delivery strategies and maternal‑fetal safety.

title: Early childhood blood pressure in relation to umbilical cord homocysteine and folate: insights from the ENVIRonmental influence ON AGEing birth cohort Study.
authorString: Shi HZ, Martens DS, Croons H, Verheyen L, Giesberts N, Sleurs H, Renaers E, Wang YC, Yang ZK, Yu YL, An DW, Zhang DY, Li Y, Allegaert K, Verhamme P, Plusquin M, Staessen JA, Nawrot TS.
abstractText:
Background

High blood pressure (BP) tracks from childhood into adulthood, contributing to cardiovascular risk. How the prenatal one-carbon (1-C) metabolism, as reflected by umbilical cord homocysteine and folate, affects BP in early childhood is unknown.

Methods

The prospective population-based birth cohort ENVIRonmental influence ON early﻿AGEing (ENVIRONAGE) comprised 500 mother-offspring pairs. Umbilical cord and maternal homocysteine and folate were measured by electrochemiluminescence immunoassay. The association of the offspring BP and risk of high BP was assessed by linear and logistic regression and by mediation analysis. Association sizes were expressed per doubling of the biomarkers and adjusted for the children's sex, age and weight and maternal age at delivery and parity.

Results

At 4.5  years (median), cord homocysteine was associated with higher diastolic and mean BP (MBP), but not SBP with association sizes of 1.67  mmHg [95% confidence interval (CI), 0.36-2.99] and 1.19  mmHg (0.01-2.38), respectively. The odds ratio for high childhood DBP with normotension as reference was 2.22 (1.34-3.68). Associations of BP with cord folate were not significant. Cord folate had only an indirect effect on DBP and MBP with effect sizes amounting to -3.04 (P = 0.027) and -2.30 (P = 0.061)  mmHg. Maternal biomarkers were not associated with the offspring's BP.

Conclusion

In this prospective birth cohort study, higher cord plasma homocysteine was associated with higher DBP in early childhood, whereas cord folate was only via homocysteine associated with the offspring's BP. The 1-C metabolism provides a mechanism for preventing high BP in childhood, which is a forerunner of hypertension in adolescence and adulthood.

title: Circadian blood pressure dipping patterns, hypertension, and cortisol metabolism across the weight spectrum.
authorString: Kallehauge M, Juhl CB, Glintborg D, Andersen MS, Støving RK, Stolberg CR.
abstractText:
Background

Blood pressure (BP) exhibits a circadian rhythm with a nocturnal decline, dipping. Alterations in cortisol metabolism have been linked to hypertension and nondipping patterns. This study aimed to examine associations between 24-h BP patterns, hypertension, and cortisol levels.

Methods

In this cross-sectional study, 426 participants (329 with BMI ≥30 kg/m2; 97 with BMI 18.5-29.9 kg/m2) underwent 24-h ambulatory BP monitoring and assessments of 24-h urinary cortisol/cortisone ratio (F/E ratio), serum corticosteroid-binding globulin, and serum F/E ratio. Dippers were defined by at least 10% nocturnal BP fall; nondippers as less than 10% BP fall; and risers as a nocturnal BP increase.

Results

Participants with BMI 18.5-29.9 kg/m2 (BMI 24.8 ± 2.7 kg/m2) compared to participants with BMI at least 30 kg/m2 (BMI 40.9 ± 6.8 kg/m2), were older (47.6 ± 8.2 vs. 43.9 ± 10.9, P = 0.002), had lower 24-h mean SBP (119 ± 11 vs. 131 ± 12 mmHg, P < 0.001), and were less frequently nondippers (50.5 vs. 66.6%, P = 0.004). No significant difference was observed in cortisol metabolism when comparing nondippers and dippers (sex-stratified). In a multivariable regression analysis, female sex, BMI at least 30 kg/m2, being normotensive, or receiving antihypertensive treatment were all significantly associated with a lower 24-h urinary F/E ratio. Among nondippers with BMI 18.5-29.9 kg/m2, urinary F/E ratio was positively associated with 24-h mean SBP (r = 0.46, P < 0.001).

Conclusion

Associations between cortisol biomarkers and BP variation were limited in participants with BMI at least 30 kg/m2, but appeared stronger in individuals with BMI 18.5-29.9 kg/m2 with nondipping BP.

title: Multiomics Integration Reveals a Skeletal Muscle Metabolic Myopathy in Cardiometabolic HFpEF.
authorString: Allerton TD, Arabie D, Malone K, Pandit A, Elbatreek MH, Li Z, Noland RC, Doiron J, Kinter M, Loveland B, Javvadi P, Agrawal K, Gartia MR, Guttula PK, Goodchild TT, Shah SJ, Ghosh S, Lefer DJ.
abstractText:
Background

Skeletal muscle dysfunction is a major peripheral determinant of exercise intolerance and physical disability in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Metabolic and mitochondrial dysfunction are considered to be key components of skeletal muscle dysfunction, but comprehensive profiling of metabolic pathways has not been conducted. Elucidation of dysregulated metabolic pathways is essential to determine viable targets for the treatment of exercise intolerance in HFpEF.

Methods

Male ZSF1 Obese rats (HFpEF, n=8) and Wistar Kyoto lean normotensive controls (Control, n=8) were studied at 26 weeks of age. The gastrocnemius was analyzed using bulk RNA sequencing, proteomics, metabolomics, and lipidomics. Differential expression across all omics layers was determined using standard statistical modeling with thresholds of absolute fold‑change >1.5 and FDR <0.05, unless otherwise specified. Additional targeted plasma and skeletal muscle metabolomics and lipidomics were performed in HFpEF and control rats, including analyses of the soleus and the extensor digitorum longus, to validate features associated with predominantly oxidative and glycolytic muscle, respectively.

Results

Pathway-level analysis for RNA sequencing and proteomics revealed significant downregulation of oxidative phosphorylation (natural enrichment score (NES), -2.1; P<0.005), electron transport chain (NES, -2.0; P<0.005), and tricarboxylic acid cycle cycle (-1.8; P<0.05). The most upregulated pathways were PPAR signaling (NES, 2.2; P<0.0001), tryptophan metabolism (NES, 1.8; P<0.005), and amino acid oxidation (NES, 1.8; P<0.005) pathways. Metabolomics revealed an accumulation of tricarboxylic acid cycle cycle intermediate, isocitrate, and phosphate reduction. Branched-chain amino acids were significantly increased, whereas amino acids related to tryptophan metabolism were reduced and shifted towards increased serotonin accumulation. Phospholipid species were differentially regulated with increased palmitoylated phosphatidylcholines but reduced arachidonoyl-phosphatidylcholine species. Phosphatidylethanolamines species (16:0/16:1-18:0/18:2) were increased.

Conclusions

HFpEF skeletal muscle shows signatures of profound mitochondrial and peroxisomal dysfunction with lipid overload, impaired branched chain amino acid and tryptophan metabolism, and a shift in membrane phospholipid composition, supporting an acquired metabolic myopathy in cardiometabolic HFpEF.

title: A practical framework for using GLP-1 RAs, SGLT2i, and MRAs with contemporary immunosuppression in kidney transplant recipients.
authorString: El Essawy B, Muzammil FM, El Essawy I.

journal.title: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension

abstractText:
Purpose of review

Calcineurin inhibitors (CNIs) remain central to kidney-transplant (KTX) immunosuppression (IS) but contribute to nephrotoxicity and cardiometabolic (CM) complications which negatively affect patient and graft survival. This review presents a practical framework for adding glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RA), sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i), and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) to established IS regimens. These agents complement individualized optimization of IS, including CNI-sparing strategies when indicated.

Recent findings

Evidence in KTX recipients remains limited, but available studies suggest that these agents may improve glycemic control, weight, blood pressure, proteinuria, and cardiorenal risk without routinely requiring changes to IS choice or dose. Whether these changes improve patient and graft survival remains unproven. GLP-1 RA related gastrointestinal effects may alter oral IS absorption, warranting continued CNI trough monitoring, particularly when significant gastrointestinal symptoms occur after initiation or dose escalation. SGLT2i require assessment of volume status, renal-function, and infection risk. MRAs may compound CNIs associated hyperkalemia and early eGFR decline, requiring close potassium and renal-function monitoring.

Summary

These therapies may extend cardiorenal benefits observed in nontransplant chronic kidney disease to selected KTX recipients. Their use should be individualized, introduced sequentially, and supported by monitoring of graft function, electrolytes, volume status, blood pressure, and IS exposure. Temporary withholding should follow drug-specific perioperative and sick-day guidance, particularly for SGLT2i.

title: Distinct phenotypes associated with the same homozygous ENPP1 c.26dup variant.
authorString: Yılmaz ZY, Çamtosun E, Elkiran Ö, Eser M, Dündar İ, Alagöz M.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

abstractText:
Objectives

ENPP1 pathogenic variants have been associated with a wide phenotypic spectrum, ranging from generalized arterial calcification of infancy to vascular stenoses and autosomal recessive hypophosphatemic rickets.

Case presentation

This study presents two cases of cousins who are homozygous for the c.26dup (p.Gly10ArgfsTer67) variant in the ENPP1 gene, but who exhibit distinct clinical features. The first patient developed hypophosphatemic rickets in early childhood. He was subsequently diagnosed with hypertension due to multiple arterial stenoses. In the second case, prenatal monitoring revealed generalized vascular calcification of intrauterine onset. Postnatally, the patient was diagnosed with heart failure, for which medical therapy was initiated, and early parenteral pamidronate was administered. However, the infant died during infancy due to a respiratory infection.

Conclusions

These findings suggest that ENPP1 variants may manifest with heterogeneous phenotypes and modifying factors may influence the variant's clinical expression. Case 1 was previously reported with limited clinical information as part of a national Turkish cohort of patients with autosomal recessive hypophosphatemic rickets type 2 caused by ENPP1 deficiency. However, as the study was a cohort analysis, it did not comprehensively describe the patient's clinical course, cardiovascular involvement, long-term follow-up, or the intrafamilial phenotypic variability observed within the affected family. Our report contributes to a better understanding of this rare genetic disorder's clinical spectrum and to clarifying the genotype-phenotype correlation.

title: Phase 4 Atrioventricular Block Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: Unmasking Latent Conduction Disease.
authorString: Reddy S, Lemieux AT, Donsky A, Assar M, Stoler RC.
abstractText: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) carries up to a 15% risk of complete heart block (CHB) within 30 days, but the mechanisms driving recurrent heart block after the apparent initial conduction system recovery post-TAVR remain incompletely understood. Phase 4 atrioventricular block, a pause-dependent phenomenon occurring when supraventricular or ventricular impulses encounter diseased His-Purkinje fibers during diastolic depolarization, may contribute to post-TAVR conduction disturbances. We present an instructive case of a 71-year-old woman with severe aortic valve stenosis who developed CHB in the setting of phase 4 atrioventricular block following TAVR. Despite recovering sinus rhythm with 1:1 atrioventricular conduction within 12 hours post-procedure, she experienced recurrent ventricular standstill upon temporary pacemaker removal, ultimately requiring permanent pacemaker implantation. This case illustrates the multiple mechanisms and temporal patterns of post-TAVR conduction system disorders, the potential unreliability of early apparent conduction recovery as a predictor of durable atrioventricular conduction, and the necessity for careful and more prolonged patient monitoring before and after temporary pacemaker removal.

title: Increased Left Ventricular Wall Thickness without Increased Mechanical Dispersion: A Distinguishing Feature of Transthyretin Amyloidosis Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Ozbay B, Soman P, Wong TC, Akdogan M, Katz WE, Wang Y, Saba SF, Sade LE.

journal.title: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography

abstractText:
Introduction

Life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia (LTVA) is infrequent in patients with transthyretin cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) despite severe cardiac dysfunction. We aimed to assess left ventricular mechanical dispersion (LVMD), as a marker of arrhythmia substrate, in ATTR-CM in comparison to other phenotypes with increased left ventricular (LV) wall thickness and in relation to LTVA occurrence.

Methods

Patients with suspected cardiac amyloidosis (CA) and increased LV wall thickness (septal thickness ≥12 mm) were identified. Patients with other types of CA and obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy were excluded. Data from comprehensive clinical assessments, laboratory tests, echocardiography with speckle tracking, and Tc-99m labeled pyrophosphate scintigraphy (PYP) were retrospectively collected from each patient. Diagnosis of ATTR-CM was established based on current recommendations. Longitudinal follow-up was performed over 5 years for LTVA (ventricular tachycardia and sudden cardiac arrest).

Results

In ATTR-CM group (n=150) lower LV ejection fraction, impaired global longitudinal strain (GLS), higher LV mass index, smaller end-diastolic volume index and higher relative apical sparing (RAS) were observed compared to the non-amyloid LVH group (n=223). Significantly lower mechanical dispersion (LVMD) was a remarkable feature of ATTR-CM, additive to ESC echocardiography parameters for the differential diagnosis (net reclassification improvement: 0.74). Higher LVMD was associated with increased risk of LTVA, whereas ATTR-CM was associated with a lower risk of LTVA. Mediation analysis further supported the mediating role of LVMD in the association between ATTR-CM and LTVA.

Conclusion

Lower LVMD seems to be a distinguishing feature of ATTR-CM in association with infrequent LTVA despite severe increased LV wall thickness.

title: Preoperative high-frequency QRS parameters and left bundle branch area pacing response in non-ischemic left bundle branch block patients: An exploratory study.
authorString: Hou Z, Jiang Z, Xia X, Zhao Z, Bu J, Li C, Yang G, Wang C.
abstractText:
Background

Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBP) has become a preferred as a novel strategy for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). High-frequency QRS (HFQRS) analysis can detect subtle ventricular depolarization abnormalities that are not identifiable on standard electrocardiography and may provide novel markers for predicting response to LBBP.

Methods

We prospectively enrolled 58 consecutive patients with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy and left bundle branch block (LBBB) who underwent guideline-directed LBBP between 2022 and 2025. LBBP response was defined as an absolute increase in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) >10% at 6-month follow-up. Preprocedural HFQRS parameters were quantitatively analyzed, including mean HFQRS amplitude and the high-frequency morphological index (HFMI).

Results

Forty-three patients (74.1%) met the criteria for LBBP response. Responders had significantly lower anterior mean HFQRS amplitude (1.61 ± 0.59 vs. 2.60 ± 1.01 μV, P = 0.002) and higher anterior HFMI (24.7% vs. 16.1%, P = 0.002) than non-responders. Anterior mean amplitude showed the strongest predictive value for LBBP response (AUC = 0.800, 95% CI 0.656-0.944). Patients with lower anterior mean amplitude demonstrated better event-free survival (log-rank P = 0.011). In multivariable analysis, lower anterior mean amplitude independently predicted greater LVEF improvement (β = -0.474, P = 0.003) and was associated with more pronounced reverse remodeling (P = 0.001).

Conclusion

In patients with non-ischemic LBBB undergoing LBBP, reduced anterior mean HFQRS amplitude is independently associated with improved ventricular recovery and a higher likelihood of response to resynchronization therapy. HFQRS analysis may provide a useful noninvasive tool for preprocedural risk stratification and patient selection in LBBP.

title: Targeting phospholipid signaling in arterial diseases: mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities.
authorString: Hu CX, Wang X, Wang M, Zhang Z.
abstractText: Phospholipids are fundamental components of cellular membranes and a major source of bioactive lipid mediators that regulate vascular homeostasis. Emerging evidence links dysregulated phospholipid metabolism to arterial disease progression; however, clinical findings are inconsistent, and the specific roles of individual phospholipid pathways in arterial pathologies remain unclear. The diverse functions and mechanisms of phospholipid signaling in arterial diseases also require further investigation. Integrating these advances is increasingly important for understanding pathological vascular remodeling and identifying new therapeutic opportunities. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview of membrane phospholipid metabolism and phospholipid-mediated signaling, discuss their emerging roles in arterial diseases, particularly atherosclerosis and aortic diseases, and highlight current challenges and future directions for translating phospholipid biology into therapeutic strategies.

title: Combating drug-resistant <i>Aeromonas veronii</i>: Multiomics revealed the antibacterial mechanism of resveratrol.
authorString: Ouyang P, Wang M, Li X, Chen F, Liu B, Yin K, Zhang N, Xiao J, Zhang C, Geng Y, Huang X, Chen D.
abstractText: Aeromonas, widely distributed in aquatic ecosystems, is a prevalent fish pathogen and can cause human infections via contaminated aquatic products, polluted water contact, or tainted food consumption. Escalating antibiotic resistance in Aeromonas strains highlights an urgent need for alternative natural antimicrobial agents. This study investigated resveratrol's antibacterial mechanisms against Aeromonas veronii and evaluated its protective efficacy in hybrid sturgeon. Resveratrol exhibited strong activity [minimum inhibitory concentration: 128 microgram per milliliter (μg/ml), minimum bactericidal concentration: 256 μg/ml], disrupting cell wall/membrane integrity, inducing reactive oxygen species accumulation, inhibiting adenosine 5'-triphosphate synthesis, and down-regulating key metabolic pathways via transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses. In the sturgeon infection model, resveratrol-nanoemulsion notably improved survival, reduced tissue bacterial loads, mitigated oxidative stress and inflammation, and restored intestinal barrier function. These findings confirm resveratrol as a promising antibiotic alternative against A. veronii, with nanoemulsion formulation enhancing its therapeutic efficacy.

title: Magnetic resonance angiography based on iron-coordinated poly(amino acid)s nanoprobes: an in vitro and in vivo experimental study.
authorString: Shen T, Xu S, Li G, Xia J, Han G, Zhang Y, J Wáng YX, Ling J, Sun J.
abstractText:
Objectives

To develop a gadolinium-free T1-weighted magnetic resonance (MR) contrast nanoprobe using Fe(III)-poly(amino acid)s-coordinated complexes (Fe@polyDOPA-b-polysarcosine, Fe@POS) for high-resolution MR angiography (MRA) with an extended imaging window.

Materials and methods

Fe@POS nanoprobes were prepared by the self-assembly of Fe(III) and polyDOPA-b-polysarcosine copolymers. Physicochemical and cytological characterizations were conducted to demonstrate their feasibility for MRA. MRA of the aorta was conducted on New Zealand rabbits, which were divided into one experimental group (n = 3) receiving Fe@POS nanoprobes and one control group (n = 3) receiving Gadolinium diethylenetriamine pentaacetic acid (Gd-DTPA). Cardiac and hepatic MR acquisition were conducted on Bama Swine (n = 3). Long-term biodistribution (n = 3) and biosafety (n = 4) evaluation was performed on BALB/c mice. Short-term and acute toxicity evaluation was conducted on BALB/c mice (n = 5) and Bama pigs (n = 3).

Results

Fe@POS nanoprobes exhibited a regular nanomicelle structure with an average particle size of 25 nm. Compared with Gd-DTPA (r1 = 4.38 mM-1 s-1), Fe@POS nanoprobes exhibited higher longitudinal relaxivity (r1 = 5.74 mM-1 s-1). In rabbit models, significant MR signal enhancement was observed in the abdominal aorta for over 4 h post-injection of Fe@POS. In porcine models, prolonged T1 enhancement was observed on MRA of the cardiovascular system, revealing detailed arterial and venous vasculature system in MR images. The biosafety evaluations demonstrated that the Fe@POS nanoprobes exhibited satisfactory biocompatibility and no prolonged iron accumulation in major organs under the tested conditions.

Conclusion

Fe@POS nanoprobes simultaneously provided high-resolution T1-weighted MRA of the cardiovascular system with an extended imaging window.

Key points

Question Can a gadolinium-free nanoprobe provide prolonged high-resolution T1-weighted magnetic resonance angiography? Findings The use of Fe (III)-based poly(amino acid)s nanoprobes enables high-spatial-resolution magnetic resonance angiography of the cardiovascular system with a long window period.

Critical relevance

The development of this new MRI contrast agent could broaden its clinical applicability and contribute to more precise diagnoses of cardiovascular diseases.

title: Multilayer regulation of osteogenic reprogramming in human aortic valve interstitial cells in calcific aortic valve disease.
authorString: Liang C, Zhu L, Zhou M, Shi H, Shao G.
abstractText: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is an active fibrocalcific disorder in which human aortic valve interstitial cells (hVICs) undergo heterogeneous osteogenic reprogramming. This narrative review provides an hVIC-centered synthesis of four interacting regulatory layers: pathological microenvironmental cues, intracellular signaling, non-coding RNA regulation, and cellular heterogeneity. Lipid dysregulation, inflammation, hypoxia, oxidative and metabolic stress, cellular senescence, and abnormal mechanical loading alter hVIC behavior through interconnected developmental, inflammatory, metabolic, and mechanosensitive pathways. Non-coding RNAs add post-transcriptional and epigenetic regulation, although many proposed axes remain incompletely validated. Single-cell transcriptomic studies further identify distinct disease-associated hVIC states and challenge a universal linear transition from quiescent to myofibroblast-like and osteogenic cells. We compare conventional and advanced experimental models and evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies according to the strength of human, functional, and translational evidence. Current data support a context- and stage-dependent network rather than a single dominant pathway. Integrating human valve tissue, cell-state-resolved analyses, complementary disease models, clinically meaningful endpoints, and targeted delivery may improve biomarker development and support disease-modifying strategies for CAVD.

title: Emodin ameliorates diabetic cardiomyopathy by regulating mitochondrial dynamics of fission and fusion and ferroptosis through the AHR‑Nrf2 pathway.
authorString: Yu X, Lou H, Zhou J, Lin H, Yang J, Chi J.
abstractText: Emodin, a natural anthraquinone with known antioxidant properties, has not been fully investigated in diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM), a condition marked by oxidative stress, ferroptosis and metabolic disturbance, and lacking specific therapies. A DCM model was induced by streptozotocin and a high‑fat diet. Cardiac function after emodin treatment was assessed via echocardiography, while myocardial injury, fibrosis and myocardial iron concentration were evaluated histologically. Mitochondrial fission‑fusion dynamics were examined using transmission electron microscopy and confocal imaging. In vitro functional rescue experiments using Ferrostatin‑1 and aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) knockdown via small interfering RNA or AAV9 was performed to determine its role in emodin‑regulated ferroptosis, lipid peroxidation, mitochondrial dynamics and Nrf2 signaling. Emodin improved left ventricular systolic function, attenuated metabolic disorders, reduced myocardial iron concentration and fibrosis, and suppressed excessive mitochondrial fission and lipid peroxidation in DCM mice. These effects were largely reversed by AHR knockdown. Mechanistically, emodin promoted Nrf2 nuclear translocation and upregulated antioxidant molecules, while AHR silencing abrogated these protective effects, thereby exacerbating ferroptosis and mitochondrial dynamic imbalance. In conclusion, emodin protects against high glucose‑induced cardiac injury and improves mitochondrial function by limiting ferroptosis and restoring mitochondrial fission‑fusion homeostasis, effects that are mediated through the AHR‑Nrf2 pathway. These findings suggest emodin and the AHR‑Nrf2 axis as potential therapeutic targets for DCM.

title: Cedrol mitigates atherosclerosis by inhibiting foam cell formation and inflammatory response via suppression of NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3 inflammasome.
authorString: Cui X, Tian X, Li X, Zhang X, Wu J.
abstractText:
Background

Foam cell formation and inflammation are critical to atherosclerosis development. Cedrol is a well-known natural sesquiterpene with a wide range of pharmacological properties. In this study, we aimed to elucidate the influence of cedrol on foam cell formation and inflammatory reaction during atherosclerosis.

Methods

ApoE-/- mice were fed a high-fat diet and treated with cedrol (60 and 120 mg/kg). Aortic lesions were determined by Oil Red O staining. Inflammation in the aorta was evaluated by ELISA and reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Immunohistochemical staining showed NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) and cleaved caspase-1 expression in aortic roots. RAW264.7 mouse macrophages were stimulated with oxidized low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL; 80 μg/ml) and treated with cedrol (1, 5, and 10 μM). Cholesterol accumulation and foam cell formation were evaluated. Western blotting assessed the levels of macrophage cholesterol efflux and NLRP3 signaling-related proteins. Nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) signaling and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production were examined to explore upstream mechanisms.

Results

Cedrol improved serum lipid profiles and alleviated the pathological features of atherosclerosis in mice. Cedrol inhibited the expression of inflammatory cytokines and inactivated the NLRP3 inflammasome in atherosclerosis mice. In RAW264.7 cells, cedrol significantly suppressed ox-LDL-induced cholesterol accumulation and foam cell formation. Cedrol also inhibited ox-LDL-induced inflammation and NLRP3 inflammasome activation, while the NLRP3 activator nigericin reversed these effects. Mechanistically, cedrol suppressed NF-κB activation and reduced total and mitochondrial ROS production in vitro.

Conclusion

Cedrol alleviated atherosclerosis development by suppressing inflammation and foam cell formation via inactivation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, which was mediated through inhibition of NF-κB signaling and oxidative stress.

title: Early-onset severe dilated cardiomyopathy in a child with <i>COL5A1</i> and <i>ABCC9</i> variants: a possible complex genetic contribution.
authorString: Ercan Bozyer H, Türkmen H.
abstractText: We report a 16-month-old boy presenting with progressive respiratory distress and generalised oedema. Chest radiography revealed pulmonary oedema, and echocardiography demonstrated severe left ventricular dilation with markedly reduced systolic function (ejection fraction ∼ 30%). There was no clinical, laboratory, or cardiac magnetic resonance evidence supporting myocarditis. Cardiac MRI demonstrated a non-ischaemic dilated cardiomyopathy phenotype without evidence of myocardial fibrosis. Despite intensive medical therapy, only partial functional recovery was observed. Aetiological evaluation using clinical exome sequencing identified a heterozygous likely pathogenic ABCC9 variant together with a heterozygous COL5A1 variant of uncertain significance. Although the pathogenic contribution of the COL5A1 variant remains uncertain, its coexistence with the ABCC9 variant may have contributed to the unusually early and severe clinical presentation.

title: Recommendations for the Examination, Processing, and Reporting of Non-neoplastic Pericardial Diseases: A Consensus Statement on Pericardial Disease from the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology and the Association for European Cardiovascular Pathology.
authorString: Tan CD, Preston SD, Basso C, Bois MC, Casimero FVC, de Boer H, de Gaspari M, Fabre A, Fishbein GA, Fyfe BS, Halushka MK, de Gouveia RH, Kholova I, Krywanczyk AR, Maleszewski JJ, Franch NM, Marzullo A, Michaud K, Nair V, Parsons S, Pontinha CM, Rotman S, Rizzo S, Martins CS, Seki A, Sheppard MN, Stone JR, Thomas S, Wang H, Westaby J, von der Thüsen JH, Rodriguez ER.

journal.title: Cardiovascular pathology : the official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology

abstractText:
Background and aim

Recent advances in the evaluation and management of pericardial diseases highlight the importance of accurate pathologic assessment. Despite these current developments, the handling, processing, and reporting of pericardial specimens have not been formally addressed in recent years. This consensus document is intended to enable the pathologist to evaluate the pericardium as a surgical specimen as well as at postmortem examination, with particular emphasis on standardized gross and microscopic assessment of the pericardium.

Methods and results

An international expert panel comprising volunteer members of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology and the Association for European Cardiovascular Pathology was convened to develop consensus recommendations. Strong agreement on best practices was achieved through a series of in-person and hybrid virtual meetings. The document outlines recommendations for the handling and processing of surgical pericardial specimens, including appropriate histochemical and immunohistochemical stains and ancillary diagnostic studies. Guidance for the systematic examination of the pericardium at autopsy is also provided. In addition, a nomenclature for common and well-defined pathologic processes is proposed, together with relevant differential diagnoses. The recommended terminology encompasses the predominant inflammatory cell infiltrates and the spectrum of organization from fibrinous pericarditis to established pericardial fibrosis.

Conclusion

This consensus document provides a standardized framework for the pathologic evaluation of the pericardium with the goal of improving diagnostic consistency, facilitating communication among clinicians and pathologists, and promoting uniformity in clinical practice and research.

title: Pathology of the Parietal Pericardium: A Consensus Statement on Pericardial Disease from the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology and the Association for European Cardiovascular Pathology.
