authorString: Tan CD, Preston SD, Basso C, Bois MC, Casimero FVC, de Boer H, de Gaspari M, Fabre A, Fishbein GA, Fyfe BS, Halushka MK, de Gouveia RH, Kholova I, Krywanczyk AR, Maleszewski JJ, Franch NM, Marzullo A, Michaud K, Nair V, Parsons S, Pontinha CM, Rotman S, Rizzo S, Martins CS, Seki A, Sheppard MN, Stone JR, Thomas S, Wang H, Westaby J, von der Thüsen JH, Rodriguez ER.

journal.title: Cardiovascular pathology : the official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology

abstractText:
Background and aim

Pericardial diseases encompass a broad spectrum of infectious, inflammatory, metabolic, traumatic, iatrogenic, and neoplastic disorders occurring in the setting of both localized and systemic conditions. Advances in understanding of the pathogenesis and diagnosis of pericardial disease have been substantial. Despite extensive literature on the clinical aspects of pericardial disease, relatively few studies have focused on its pathologic features.

Methods and results

An international panel from volunteer members of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology and the Association for European Cardiovascular Pathology conducted a comprehensive review of the literature to develop a consensus document on the recommendations for pathologic evaluation of the parietal pericardium. This first document summarizes our state-of-the-art understanding of the etiological and morphological aspects of pericardial diseases, including pericardial effusions, cardiac tamponade, infectious and non-infectious pericarditis, and constrictive pericarditis, and incorporates updated clinical definitions and diagnostic criteria.

Conclusion

This consensus review highlights the role of pathology in the diagnosis of pericardial disease. Future efforts should explore establishing contemporary reference ranges for normal pericardial fluid volume, refining the pathologic characterization of pericarditis, correlating histopathologic findings with advanced cardiac imaging, and elucidating the molecular mechanisms driving the progression of pericardial fibrosis to constrictive disease.

title: Prevalence of concomitant aneurysms in patients with thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms who underwent Fenestrated/Branched Endovascular Aortic Repair (F-BEVAR).
authorString: Maggiorani Davila LF, Farber MA, Gomes VC, Nunes VA, Theis C, Ohana E, Pascarella L, Benrashid E, Parodi FE.
abstractText:
Objective

To determine the prevalence of synchronous ascending aortic and peripheral arterial aneurysms in patients with Crawford extent I-IV thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAA) undergoing fenestrated/branched endovascular aneurysm repair (F/BEVAR).

Methods

We performed a single-center retrospective review of prospectively collected data from patients with Crawford extent I-IV TAAA treated with F/BEVAR under a physician-sponsored investigational device exemption. The preoperative CTA obtained for device planning was used to measure the ascending aorta and bilateral common iliac (CIA), hypogastric (HA), and common femoral (CFA) arteries using centerline reconstruction. Bilateral popliteal artery (PA) diameters were obtained from preoperative arterial duplex imaging. An aneurysm was defined as a vessel diameter >50% greater than the expected normal diameter for that arterial bed, using references available from literature. Multivariable logistic regression included sex, obesity, race/ethnicity, TAAA diameter ≥7 cm, and prior aortic dissection. A sensitivity analysis was performed after excluding patients with prior aortic dissection.

Results

Among 249 patients (mean age, 70.8±8.6 years; 40.2% women), 177 (71.1%) had at least one concomitant aneurysm. Race/ethnicity was 75.1% NH-White, 21.7% NH-Black, 0.8% Hispanic, and 2.4% Other. Among evaluable patients, aneurysm prevalence was 12.0% in the ascending aorta (29/242), 62.8% in the CIA (140/223), 42.1% in the HA (98/233), 22.2% in the PA (51/230), and 9.6% in the CFA (22/228). On multivariable analysis, CIA aneurysm was associated with obesity, non-White race/ethnicity, and TAAA diameter ≥7 cm; HA aneurysm with male sex, obesity, and prior dissection; CFA aneurysm with male sex; PA aneurysm with male sex and prior dissection; and ascending aortic aneurysm with TAAA diameter ≥7 cm and prior dissection. After exclusion of 46 patients with prior dissection, concomitant aneurysms remained a common occurrence.

Conclusions

Concomitant aneurysms are common in patients undergoing F/BEVAR for Crawford extent I-IV TAAA. Several associations remained significant after multivariable adjustment. These findings should be interpreted in the context of a single-center referral population, variable arterial-bed denominators, possible diffuse arteriomegaly, and residual confounding. The prevalence of PA aneurysm supports further evaluation of selective popliteal assessment; however, this study does not support a universal screening recommendation or establish an effect on management, outcomes, or cost.

title: Repair durability following fenestrated versus chimney endovascular repair for elective juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms: a multicenter cohort study.
authorString: Brinster C, Barber M, Parkerson GR, Speranza G, Maldonado T, Cheung D, Meltzer A, Kruger J, Stoner M, Money SR.
abstractText:
Objective

To compare repair durability following elective fenestrated endovascular aneurysm repair (FEVAR) and chimney endovascular aneurysm repair (ChEVAR) for juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms using complementary procedural, imaging, and clinical outcome measures.

Methods

A retrospective multicenter cohort study was performed across five high-volume aortic referral centers. Consecutive patients undergoing elective FEVAR or ChEVAR for juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms were included. Baseline characteristics, technical success, endoleaks, secondary aortic intervention, aneurysm sac remodeling, and target vessel patency were compared. Repair durability was assessed by integrating proximal seal integrity, longitudinal aneurysm sac remodeling, and freedom from secondary aortic intervention. Continuous variables were compared using Student's t test or the Mann-Whitney U test, and categorical variables using χ2 or Fisher's exact tests. Statistical significance was defined as P < .05.

Results

A total of 130 patients underwent elective repair, including 77 treated with FEVAR and 53 with ChEVAR. Baseline demographic characteristics, aneurysm diameter, and duration of follow-up were similar between groups. Technical success was comparable (98.7% vs 98.1%; P = .76), and target vessel patency exceeded 95% in both cohorts (P = .38). Type Ia endoleak occurred less frequently following FEVAR than ChEVAR (1.3% vs 22.6%; P < .001), with a lower incidence of all Type I endoleaks (Types Ia, Ib, and Ic) (7.8% vs 26.4%; P = .006). Secondary aortic intervention was also less common following FEVAR (10.4% vs 30.2%; P = .006). Progressive aneurysm sac regression was observed following FEVAR, with a mean reduction of 11 mm at 24 months, whereas ChEVAR demonstrated limited early regression followed by late sac re-expansion, resulting in an overall 2-mm reduction. Mean aneurysm sac diameter was significantly smaller following FEVAR compared with ChEVAR at both 12 months (55 vs 59 mm; P = .01) and 24 months (51 vs 63 mm; P < .001).

Conclusions

Elective FEVAR and ChEVAR achieved similarly high technical success and target vessel patency for juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms. During mid-term follow-up, FEVAR was associated with lower rates of proximal attachment-site failure, greater aneurysm sac regression, and fewer secondary aortic interventions. These concordant procedural, imaging, and clinical outcomes suggest that integrated longitudinal assessment provides a more comprehensive evaluation of repair durability following complex endovascular aneurysm repair than technical success alone.

title: Risk Prediction With a Type Ia-Oriented Proximal Neck Anatomic Severity Grading Score After EVAR.
authorString: Işcan HZ, Külahcioğlu E, Aytekin B, Yildiz GT, Altintaş G.
abstractText:
Background

We developed an exploratory Type Ia-oriented proximal neck Anatomic Severity Grading Score (Type Ia-ASGS) and assessed its association with postoperative type Ia endoleak after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR).

Methods

We analyzed 304 elective standard EVAR patients treated during 2016-April 2024 with an Ankura endograft (Lifetech). Neck measurements were proximal diameter (A), distal diameter (B), and centerline length (C). The score assigned 1 point each for C ≤15 mm, max(A, B) >28 mm, and B - A ≥3 mm, and 2 points each for angulation >60° and calcification. The theoretical range was 0-7; weights reflected observed univariable associations.

Results

Mean clinical and imaging follow-up was 27.6 ± 3.2 months, with final follow-up in June 2026. Type Ia endoleak occurred in 14/304 patients (4.6%). Observed event proportions were 1.2%, 2.8%, and 28.1% in exploratory low (0-1), intermediate (2-3), and high (≥4) score categories (p < 0.001). Each point was associated with greater odds of type Ia endoleak (odds ratio, 2.78; 95% confidence interval, 1.80-4.29). Apparent area under the curve was 0.859 (bootstrap 95% confidence interval, 0.750-0.943). Individual event and censoring dates were unavailable for time-to-event analysis.

Conclusions

The Type Ia-ASGS was associated with postoperative type Ia endoleak in this derivation cohort. Its heuristic weights and exploratory categories require independent validation before clinical use.

title: Prophylactic extended-field irradiation versus pelvic radiotherapy in high-risk locally advanced cervical cancer with radiologically negative para-aortic lymph nodes: a retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Shao H, Zhao Y, Cui T, Wang T, Liu Z.
abstractText:
Objective

To compare para-aortic recurrence, survival outcomes, and treatment-related toxicity between prophylactic extended-field irradiation (EFI) and pelvic radiotherapy (PRT) in patients with high-risk locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) who have radiologically negative para-aortic lymph nodes (PALNs).

Methods

We retrospectively reviewed patients with FIGO 2018 stage III-IVA cervical cancer treated with definitive radiotherapy or concurrent chemoradiotherapy between December 2015 and December 2022. Eligible patients had radiologically negative PALNs and at least one high-risk feature: ≥2 positive pelvic lymph nodes, a maximum pelvic nodal short-axis diameter ≥ 1.5 cm, or pelvic sidewall involvement. Patients received EFI (n = 140) or PRT (n = 153). Survival outcomes were compared using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression.

Results

Para-aortic recurrence occurred in 2.1% of patients receiving EFI and 11.1% receiving PRT. Five-year PARFS, PFS, and DMFS were higher with EFI than with PRT (97.8% vs 88.1%, P = 0.002; 70.9% vs 58.8%, P = 0.002; and 83.7% vs 75.2%, P = 0.032, respectively). Five-year OS was 79.1% versus 68.6% (P = 0.052). In multivariable analysis, EFI remained associated with improved PFS (HR, 0.532; P = 0.002), DMFS (HR, 0.554; P = 0.036), and PARFS (HR, 0.178; P = 0.006), but not OS (HR, 0.630; P = 0.054). Grade 3-4 leukopenia was more frequent with EFI, whereas other severe toxicities were similar.

Conclusions

Prophylactic EFI was associated with improved para-aortic control, PFS, and DMFS in high-risk LACC, with acceptable toxicity. These findings support further evaluation of a risk-adapted strategy for selecting patients who may benefit from prophylactic EFI.

title: Association Between Serum FGF21 Levels and Isolated Aortic Valve Calcification.
authorString: Wei C, Zhou Y, Xu X, Shao Z, Li P, Zhang Q, Gou Z, Yan X.
abstractText: Aortic valve calcification (AVC) is a progressive pathological process, eventually leading to valve dysfunction. We aimed to examine the association between fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21) and AVC. Forty-three patients with confirmed isolated AVC (without valve incompetence) and seventeen control individuals were included. Patients with AVC were older (P < 0.001) and exhibited higher serum levels of IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, and IFN-γ (P < 0.05) than the control group did. Importantly, the serum FGF21 levels of the patients with AVC were higher than those of the control individuals (P < 0.001). Linear regression analysis showed that the presence of AVC and the serum IL-4 levels significantly affected FGF21 levels. Multivariate logistic regression revealed that FGF21 levels and age were strong independent factors that influenced AVC. The area under the ROC curve (AUC) of the combined diagnosis of AVC with FGF21 levels and age was 0.941 (95% CI 0.855-0.981; P < 0 .001). Therefore, elevated serum FGF21 levels were robustly associated with the presence of AVC. FGF21 levels showed a positive correlation with IL-4 levels, suggesting possible interactions among FGF21, inflammation, and AVC.

title: Systematic comparison of gliflozins identifies a selective anti-calcifying effect of canagliflozin beyond canonical SGLT2 inhibition
authorString: Fernandez L, Brunet M, Ballongue E, Ducos V, Buléon M, Feuillet G, Galaricha E, Mairal A, Del Bello A, Augé N, Gayrard N, Laget J, Fabrice R, Diaz-Tocados JM, Thomas A, Chabbert M, Arefin S, Kublickene K, Stenvinkel P, Schanstra JP, Klein J.
abstractText:
Background

Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) provide important cardiorenal benefits in chronic kidney disease (CKD), but their effects on vascular calcification remain conflicting. Whether potential anti-calcifying effects are shared across gliflozins or involve mechanisms beyond canonical SGLT2 inhibition is unknown.

Methods

We systematically compared canagliflozin, dapagliflozin and empagliflozin in a high-phosphate diet-induced mouse model of vascular calcification and complementary ex vivo and in vitro models, including rodent and human vascular tissues and vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). Aortic transcriptional response was investigated by RNA sequencing. VSMC calcification, proliferation, migration, viability, glucose uptake and bioenergetics were investigated using complementary cellular assays, including OsteoSense staining, Annexin V/propidium iodide staining, radiolabeled 2-deoxyglucose uptake and Seahorse ATP rate analysis. SGLT2/1 expression was examined by RT-qPCR, Western blotting and immunofluorescence. We also evaluated sotagliflozin, a dual SGLT1/2 inhibitor, and mizagliflozin, a selective SGLT1 inhibitor.

Results

Among the three gliflozins, only canagliflozin significantly reduced aortic calcification in vivo . Its anti-calcifying effect was also observed in rodent aortic rings, human vascular explants, cultured VSMCs and aortic rings from diabetic db/db mice. Aortic RNA-seq revealed that canagliflozin partially reversed HPD-induced transcriptional alterations, including changes in pro-calcific signaling and cellular metabolism, while some endothelial and inflammatory responses were shared among gliflozins. In mouse VSMCs, canagliflozin reduced calcification across all tested concentrations, dose-dependently decreased osteogenic marker expression, and reduced proliferation and migration. Increased apoptotic and damaged cell fractions were observed at higher concentrations, but not at lower concentrations. Canagliflozin also reduced glucose uptake and mitochondrial ATP production, without significantly affecting glycolytic ATP production. Neither dapagliflozin nor empagliflozin reproduced these cellular and metabolic effects at any of the concentrations tested. SGLT2 and SGLT1 expression was low or undetectable in vascular tissues and cells, and neither sotagliflozin nor mizagliflozin reproduced the anti-calcifying effect of canagliflozin in vivo or in vitro .

Conclusions

Canagliflozin exhibits a selective anti-calcifying profile among the gliflozins tested, associated with changes in VSMC responses and cellular metabolism. These findings suggest that its vascular protective effects may involve mechanisms beyond canonical SGLT2 inhibition.

title: First-in-Human Mechanical Bilateral Iatrogenic Coronary Leaflet Obstruction Risk Nullification (BICORN) for Transcatheter Aortic Valve-in-Valve Replacement.
authorString: Al Hennawi H, Mascarenhas V, Dahou A, Akram AS, Ahmad T.
abstractText:
Objectives

We describe mechanical leaflet traversal as an alternative to electrosurgical traversal for BICORN during valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement in a patient with unfavorable cardiac orientation and extreme bilateral coronary obstruction risk.

Key steps

The ShortCut device created targeted basal splits in both coronary leaflets. The left coronary cusp split was crossed using a Pilot 100 guidewire (Abbott) and microcatheter with an EBU 3.5 guide catheter (Medtronic) and Agilis steerable introducer (Abbott) support. After balloon dilation, the left coronary cusp was translocated with an 18-mm True Dilatation Balloon (BD). A 20-mm SAPIEN 3 Ultra transcatheter heart valve (Edwards Lifesciences) was then advanced through the right coronary cusp split and deployed within the pre-existing 23-mm SAPIEN 3 valve (Edwards Lifesciences).

Potential pitfalls

Mechanical traversal requires precise targeting. Leaflet translocation may cause embolization, severe aortic insufficiency, or hemodynamic compromise, requiring readiness for immediate valve deployment.

Take-home message

Mechanical traversal may facilitate BICORN when cardiac rotation, unfavorable catheter trajectory, neosinus malalignment, eccentric coronary takeoffs, or leaflet fibrocalcification make electrosurgical traversal challenging.

title: Percutaneous Transmural Arterial Bypass for Recurrent Superficial Femoral Artery Chronic Total Occlusion.
authorString: Yasir H, Bonaguro AM, Golzar J.
abstractText:
Image

Fluoroscopic angiography and duplex ultrasound.

Case summary

A 73-year-old man with Rutherford class IV chronic limb-threatening ischemia had a recurrent, heavily calcified superficial femoral artery chronic total occlusion despite multiple prior endovascular interventions. After declining surgical bypass, he underwent percutaneous transmural arterial bypass using covered stent grafts routed through the femoral venous pathway. Inline flow was restored without immediate complications. At 3 months, duplex ultrasound demonstrated bypass patency, and rest pain had resolved.

Take-home message

Percutaneous transmural arterial bypass may offer an alternative for carefully selected patients with complex femoropopliteal disease when conventional endovascular treatment has failed, and surgical bypass is declined.

title: MEX3B leads to aberrant expression of VCAN, aggravating the thoracic aortic dissection by contributing to the phenotype transformation of VSMCs.
authorString: Hong J, Xu B, Wang S, He F.
abstractText: Thoracic aortic dissection (TAD) is a lethal condition due to the risk of aortic rupture and malperfusion of arterial branches. Currently, effective treatments are unavailable due to the unclear pathogenic mechanisms; therefore, it is essential to explore the underlying mechanisms of TAD to find novel therapeutic targets. The present study aimed to explore the effects of Mex3 RNA‑binding family member B (MEX3B) on TAD pathogenesis. A murine model of TAD was established with β‑aminopropionitrile monofumarate and angiotensin II. Hematoxylin and eosin and elastic Van Gieson staining were performed to assess the TAD formation and fragmentation of elastic fibers. Echocardiography was applied to measure the diameter of thoracic aorta. RT‑qPCR, western blot, and immunohistochemistry were employed to detect the expression of phenotypic transformation markers of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). mRNA sequencing was performed to further explore the downstream factors of MEX3B. MEX3B was upregulated following TAD induction. Knockdown of MEX3B alleviated TAD formation, as evidenced by decreased diameter and hematomas of thoracic aorta, as well as the enhanced integrity of the aortic structure and decreased thrombi in the false lumens. Loss of MEX3B mitigated the TAD‑induced depletion and fragmentation of elastic fibers. In vitro, small interfering RNA pool‑mediated MEX3B downregulation triggered VSMC switching from a synthetic towards a contractile phenotype. High‑throughput transcriptomics demonstrated that the MEX3B knockdown reduced the expression of versican (VCAN). MEX3B potentiated VCAN mRNA stability by binding to its 3'untranslated region. VCAN downregulation induced a contractile phenotype of VSMCs. In conclusion, the loss of MEX3B protected against TAD, potentially via its contribution to VSMC phenotype switching, which may be associated with the downregulation of VCAN. The present study preliminarily demonstrated the function and mechanism of MEX3B in TAD. These findings provide a theoretical basis for understanding TAD pathogenesis.

title: Left Ventricular Free-Wall Injury During Emergency Pericardial Drainage After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention-Related Coronary Perforation.
authorString: Zuo Q, Ge T, Liu J, Xiao P.

journal.title: The American journal of case reports

abstractText: BACKGROUND Coronary perforation during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) can cause pericardial bleeding and shock. Emergency pericardiocentesis may be lifesaving, but persistent bloody drainage after apparently successful coronary sealing creates a diagnostic trap: clinicians may assume ongoing coronary leakage and miss catheter-related injury. We report a safety lesson from this setting. CASE REPORT A 63-year-old woman weighing 37 kg underwent PCI for a severely calcified right coronary artery lesion. Coronary perforation after stenting was sealed with a covered stent. After transfer to the ward, she developed shock and increased apical pericardial effusion. Our treating team performed real-time echocardiography-guided apical pericardiocentesis, draining 200 mL of bloody fluid with transient improvement. Routine catheter-position checks, including agitated saline injection, contrast fluoroscopy through the catheter, pressure-waveform recording, and blood gas or oxygen saturation testing, were not performed or not documented. Drainage remained bloody, with approximately 1000 mL additional output, recurrent hypotension, and a hemoglobin decrease from 102 to 67 g/L. Repeat coronary angiography showed no recurrent extravasation. Fluoroscopy/digital subtraction angiography showed an abnormal catheter trajectory, with the distal tip projected over the aortic region. Computed tomography was not performed because the patient proceeded directly to emergency surgery. Surgical exploration confirmed left ventricular free-wall penetration. The catheter was removed only after pledgeted repair was secured. The patient recovered well. CONCLUSIONS This case emphasizes a safety message rather than a proven intravascular route. After PCI-related perforation, persistent bloody drainage with shock should prompt immediate drain-position reassessment and controlled removal if intracardiac or intravascular malposition is possible.

title: Dynamic infrared thermography for quantitative assessment of peripheral microcirculation: models, metrics, and clinical translation.
authorString: Ordaz JMB, Kashina S.
abstractText: Peripheral microcirculation assessment is critical for understanding tissue oxygenation, thermoregulation and metabolic function, but conventional techniques such as laser Doppler perfusion imaging and indocyanine green angiography are constrained by contact requirements, invasiveness or limited field of view. Dynamic infrared thermography (DIRT) provides a non-contact method that quantifies microvascular function by analyzing skin temperature recovery following a controlled thermal challenge, thereby offering functional insights into perfusion dynamics beyond static anatomical imaging. This narrative review synthesizes the bioheat models, quantitative metrics and clinical evidence supporting DIRT for peripheral microcirculation assessment. Following PRISMA-adapted searches, 71 studies and key modeling papers with dynamic protocols and perfusion-related quantitative endpoints were included. Bioheat transfer models, from the Pennes formulation to non-Fourier dual-phase-lag extensions, enable inverse estimation of perfusion parameters from temperature time-series. Validated metrics include rewarming rate, thermal time constant, area under the temperature vs time curve, maximum recovery percentage and spatial hotspot detection for perforator mapping. These parameters correlate strongly with laser Doppler and laser speckle contrast imaging, particularly in Raynaud's phenomenon (RP), and achieve high diagnostic performance for preoperative perforator mapping and postoperative flap monitoring in reconstructive microsurgery. Evidence is most mature in surgical applications, supporting DIRT as a repeatable adjunct for planning and surveillance. In RP, peripheral arterial disease and diabetic foot disease, DIRT metrics detect microvascular impairment and show promise for early ulceration risk prediction, although heterogeneity in protocols and scarcity of large-scale outcome data hinder broader adoption. As a conclusion, DIRT offers practical advantages of portability, negligible consumable cost and absence of contrast or ionizing radiation. Its transition to routine quantitative clinical use requires standardized acquisition protocols, integration of advanced signal processing and machine learning, and adequately powered multicenter trials linking metrics to patient-centered outcomes across populations.

title: Neurodevelopmental condition count, functional difficulties, and care-coordination gaps among U.S. children with caregiver-reported congenital heart conditions: a cross-sectional NSCH study, 2020-2024
authorString: Dong W, Xuming M.
abstractText: Background Children with congenital heart disease often receive care across cardiology, primary care, developmental, rehabilitation, and educational services. We examined whether the number of current neurodevelopmental diagnoses and the number of functional difficulties were associated with care-coordination gaps among U.S. children with caregiver-reported congenital heart conditions. Methods We analyzed pooled 2020–2024 National Survey of Children's Health data in a cross-sectional study of children aged 6–17 years. A congenital heart condition was defined by caregiver report of a heart condition that was present at birth. The primary outcome was failure to receive at least one needed element of effective care coordination among children who needed coordination. Survey-weighted modified Poisson models estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) for neurodevelopmental condition count and age-applicable functional difficulty count, each categorized as 0, 1, or 2 or more. Results Among 3,830 children meeting the congenital heart condition definition, 2,788 needed care coordination and had a classifiable outcome. The weighted prevalence of care-coordination failure in this domain was 40.8% (95% confidence interval [CI], 37.1%-44.6%). In separate models, both condition count and functional difficulties were associated with higher failure prevalence. In the joint model, neurodevelopmental estimates included the null, whereas functional difficulties remained associated with failure (one difficulty: aPR, 1.77; 95% CI, 1.37–2.28; 2 or more difficulties: aPR, 2.31; 95% CI, 1.78–3.01). The same pattern was present after restriction to children with a current heart condition. Conclusions Functional difficulties identified children whose caregivers reported more gaps in needed care coordination. Assessment of everyday function may add useful information when services span medical, developmental, rehabilitation, and educational settings.

title: Decreasing Births and NICU Admissions for Congenital Anomalies in the United States, 2016-2023
authorString: Acharya K, Cortezzo D, Rholl E, Fry J, Riddle S, Cabacungan E.
abstractText: Objectives: Evaluate trends in U.S. births and NICU admissions for congenital anomalies Study Design: This population-based, cross-sectional study included all births with congenital anomalies in the U.S. from 2016 to 2023 from CDC WONDER. Trends in anomaly-associated NICU admissions and births were assessed. Results: From 2016-2023, NICU admissions for anomalies decreased from 18.5 to 18 per 10,000 live births (annual percent change (APC), -0.4%; 95% CI, -0.7% to -0.2%). Admissions for gastroschisis showed the greatest decline; admissions for cyanotic congenital heart disease (CCHD) increased. NICU trends approximated birth trends for neonatal surgical anomalies, and not for non-surgical or life-limiting anomalies. Conclusions: Births and NICU admissions for congenital anomalies declined modestly in the U.S. from 2016 to 2023 with births decreasing to a greater degree than NICU admissions. Anomaly-specific considerations such as need for neonatal surgical repair, comorbid diagnoses requiring NICU care, and parental goals of care may explain these differences.

title: Ventricular Fibrillation During Pulsed Field Ablation With Dual-Energy Focal Catheters in Patients With Cardiac Implantable Electronic Devices.
authorString: Kong NW, Gamarra N, Kelly FA, Garcia DV, Alhassan H, Locke A, Ferro EG, Tung P, Zimetbaum P, Maher T, d'Avila A.
abstractText:
Background

Arrhythmia induction during catheter ablation in patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) has been reported, but the risk associated with pulsed field ablation (PFA) remains poorly characterized.

Objective

To estimate the procedural incidence of unexpected ventricular fibrillation (VF) during PFA in patients with CIEDs and describe associated clinical and device findings.

Methods

We performed a retrospective single-center cohort study of consecutive PFA procedures in patients with CIEDs. All procedures were reviewed for unexpected VF.

Results

Among 107 consecutive procedures using PFA energy in patients with CIEDs, 83 were atrial and 24 were ventricular ablations. Unexpected VF occurred in 4 patients (overall incidence 3.7%, 95% CI 1.0% - 9.3%): 1 during left atrial PFA for pulmonary vein isolation and 3 during left ventricular PFA for ventricular tachycardia ablations. VF occurred at ablation sites both near and remote from CIED lead tips. Device electrograms demonstrated prominent ablation artifact with abnormal triggered activity and mode switch behavior. Intra-procedural recordings also demonstrated local capture and R on T mechanisms.

Conclusions

Unexpected VF during PFA in patients with CIEDs occurred in 3.7% of procedures. These results complement prior adverse-event reports and support systematic pre-, intra-, and post-procedure CIED management, with external defibrillation immediately available, whenever PFA or dual-energy ablation is performed in patients with cardiac devices.

title: Early Valve Replacement vs Surveillance in Moderate Aortic Stenosis: Meta-Analysis of Randomized and Observational Evidence
authorString: Majed A, Kmeid P, Safa A, Kahwaji H, Safieddine H, Ghanem G.
abstractText: BACKGROUND: Moderate aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with excess mortality, and 2 randomized trials have tested early transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). OBJECTIVES: The authors sought to estimate the effects of early TAVR vs clinical surveillance and to compare randomized with observational estimates. METHODS: Six databases and registries were searched through November 3, 2026. Adjusted observational studies were synthesized separately from trials. Certainty was rated with GRADE. RESULTS: Two trials (922 patients; TAVR UNLOAD, n = 178, HF with reduced ejection fraction; PROGRESS, n = 744, 96.4% symptomatic) and 7 cohorts were included. Early TAVR did not detectably change death over approximately 2 years (HR: 1.05; 95% CI: 0.74-1.49; low certainty), with one-fifth of the deaths needed to detect a 20% reduction. Heart failure (HF) hospitalization was lower (RR: 0.53; 95% CI: 0.36-0.77; low certainty), or 70 fewer patients per 1,000 at 2 years. New pacemakers were more frequent (PROGRESS: 17.3% vs 9.3%; moderate certainty). About half of surveillance patients underwent valve replacement within 2 years. Observational cohorts estimated a 48% mortality reduction (HR: 0.52; 95% CI: 0.43-0.64; very low certainty), which differed from the randomized estimate (ratio of HRs: 2.01; 95% CI: 1.37-2.95). CONCLUSIONS: In older, predominantly symptomatic patients with moderate AS, early TAVR may make little or no difference to 2-year mortality and may reduce HF hospitalization, at the cost of more pacemakers. Because about half of patients under surveillance receive a valve within 2 years, the decision largely concerns timing. Observational survival estimates should not guide practice.

title: Door-to-Valve Intervention Time and Clinical Outcomes in Acute Decompensated Severe Aortic Stenosis: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authorString: Ma JR, Gerges M, Koshy AN, Wilson W, Taylor AJ, Chan W.
abstractText:
ABSTRACT

Background

Acute decompensated aortic stenosis (ADAS) carries high mortality, but the optimal timing of valve intervention is unknown.

Objective

To assess the association between time to valve intervention (transcatheter aortic valve replacement [TAVR] or balloon aortic valvuloplasty [BAV]) and clinical outcomes in ADAS.

Methods

Embase, Ovid MEDLINE and CENTRAL were searched to May 15, 2026. Hazard ratios (HRs) for delayed versus earlier intervention were pooled using random-effects models with modified Hartung-Knapp inference. Unadjusted short-term mortality risk ratios (RRs) were pooled using the Mantel-Haenszel method.

Results

Eight observational cohort studies (n=6,044) met inclusion criteria: six TAVR (n= 5,986) and two BAV (n=58) studies. Patients were approximately 79 years old, and 63% were male. Early-intervention thresholds ranged from <24-48 hours (BAV) to ≤22 days (TAVR) from admission. Delayed intervention was not significantly associated with long-term all-cause mortality (HR 1.52, 95% CI 0.46-5.00; p=0.269; I 2 =58.2%) or mortality per five-day delay (HR 1.09, 95% CI 0.34-3.43; p=0.530; I 2 =86.7%). Crude short-term mortality was higher with delayed intervention (RR 4.96, 95% CI 1.17-20.92; p=0.029; I 2 =0.0%), although this association was not robust to sensitivity analyses. Most studies were at serious risk of bias, with substantial heterogeneity in clinical severity, intervention timing, and treatment modality.

Conclusion

Point estimates favour earlier intervention, but current observational data do not establish a mortality benefit for an optimal door-to-valve interval, and existing study designs are biased against early treatment. Prospective and randomized-controlled trials on optimal valve intervention timing following ADAS are needed.

title: Risk-benefit assessment of oral anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation using virtual clinical trials
authorString: Cai M, Farahani F, Rienstra M, Severi S, Crijns HJ, Schotten U, Heijman J.
abstractText:
Background

Oral anticoagulation (OAC) reduces stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF), and screening can enable earlier AF detection and OAC initiation. However, the population-level trade-off between stroke prevention and OAC-related major bleeding for different types of AF and OAC therapy remains uncertain, and large randomized trials to resolve this are costly and time-consuming.

Methods

A state-transition Markov-like model was developed to: 1) simulate the lifetime course of AF, stroke, major bleeding, and death in different virtual populations; 2) quantify benefits (stroke reduction) and harms (major bleeding) of systematic AF screening with screening-triggered OAC across CHA 2 DS 2 -VA scores; and 3) compare rhythm-guided, time-delimited (“pill-in-pocket”) OAC with continuous OAC.

Results

The model synthesized information from multiple clinical sources and reproduced stroke and bleeding incidence across clinical scenarios. At CHA₂DS₂-VA=2, long-term continuous rhythm monitoring (LT-CRM) with OAC lowered stroke risk (HR, 0.92 [95%CI, 0.88-0.96]) but raised bleeding risk (HR, 1.17 [95%CI, 1.07-1.27]) versus no screening. Time-to-benefit was shorter than time-to-harm for CHA₂DS₂-VA≥4, but longer for CHA₂DS₂-VA=0. Pill-in-pocket OAC vs continuous OAC showed no difference in stroke/mortality (HR, 1.03, 95%CI [0.91-1.16]) but lower bleeding risk (HR, 0.81, 95%CI: 0.68-0.96]) in patients with elevated bleeding risk, but not at baseline. Sensitivity analyses revealed that the risk-benefit profiles of screening or pill-in-pocket OAC strategy further depend on OAC adherence and bleeding risks.

Conclusions

Our model highlights a trade-off between stroke reduction and bleeding for systematic screening-initiated OAC, with net benefit for CHA₂DS₂-VA≥4. We provide the first virtual implementation of an ongoing rhythm-guided OAC trial, showing that pill-in-pocket OAC may lower bleeding risk compared to continuous OAC, highlighting the potential of virtual clinical trials to guide clinical trial design.

title: Real-World Treatment Patterns, Tolerability, and Outcomes Among Patients With CLL/SLL Treated With First-Line Ibrutinib, Acalabrutinib, or Zanubrutinib in the US Community Oncology Setting: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Burke JM, Zackon I, Wang Y, Aguilar KM, Murphy J, Wayne B, Prescott J, Leng S, Kim I, Chirovsky D, de Nigris E.
abstractText:
Background

Covalent Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitors (cBTKis) are standard first-line (1L) therapies for chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)/small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL). In clinical trials, second-generation (2G) cBTKis demonstrated better tolerability than ibrutinib, particularly regarding cardiotoxicity; however, real-world evidence on their use, discontinuation, and tolerability remains limited. This study examined treatment patterns and outcomes of cBTKis in the US community oncology setting.

Methods

CLL/SLL patients who initiated 1L therapy between November 21, 2019 and July 31, 2023 were identified from electronic health records. Kaplan-Meier methods estimated time to treatment discontinuation (TTD), time to next treatment or death (TTNT-D), real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS), and overall survival (OS). Adverse events (AEs) were reported as proportions and incidence rates. Cox proportional hazards models assessed factors associated with TTD. Correlations between rwPFS and OS were evaluated with Kendall's tau.

Results

Among 584 patients, 384 initiated ibrutinib, 150 acalabrutinib, and 50 zanubrutinib. Median follow-up durations were 35.6, 42.3, and 16.1 months, respectively. Overall, 51.2% discontinued 1L therapy by 24 months and 65.9% by end of follow-up, most commonly due to AEs (38.4%). Most patients who discontinued 1L treatment did not advance to 2L (61.8%; n = 238/385). Rates of AEs varied across cBTKis. Higher comorbidity burden, poorer performance status, del(17p), bleeding or infection, and ibrutinib (vs. acalabrutinib) were associated with shorter TTD. At 24 months, rwPFS and OS were 72.8% and 81.9%, respectively; medians were not reached. Older age (≥ 65 years) was associated with shorter TTD, TTNT-D, rwPFS, and OS. Notable correlations were observed between rwPFS and OS.

Conclusions

In this real‑world study, 1L cBTKi discontinuations occurred more frequently than in clinical trials, primarily driven by AEs. Many patients did not receive subsequent therapy. Tolerability was generally consistent with clinical trials, with variance across cBTKis. These findings highlight the unmet need for more tolerable treatment strategies to improve treatment durability and outcomes in real-world CLL/SLL populations.

Trial registration

The authors have confirmed clinical trial registration is not needed for this submission.

title: The atherosclerotic plaque microenvironment: cellular plasticity, extracellular matrix remodeling, and plaque stability.
authorString: Faa G, Piludu M, Piras M, Faa A, Sanfilippo R, Suri JS, Cau R, Saba L.
abstractText: The plaque microenvironment (PME) integrates systemic lipid exposure with local vascular, immune and stromal responses. Vascular smooth muscle cells, endothelial cells, monocytes, macrophages, fibroblast-like cells and lymphocytes interact within a continuously remodeled extracellular matrix. Their context-dependent states influence inflammation, lipid handling, matrix organization and the balance between plaque stability and vulnerability. This narrative review examines these cellular and extracellular components, with particular attention to phenotypic modulation, endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition and the limitations of inferring cellular origin from shared markers. Human single-cell findings expand the conventional M1/M2 view of macrophages. Therapeutic evidence is considered across experimental models, human pathology, intravascular imaging and randomized clinical outcome trials. Systemic lipid lowering and selected anti-inflammatory interventions can modify atherosclerotic disease, but changes in plaque composition do not by themselves establish reductions in myocardial infarction or stroke. Carotid and coronary findings also require site-specific interpretation. Integrating mechanistic observations with the level and anatomical setting of the evidence provides a framework for evaluating established therapies and developing selective PME-directed strategies.

title: Curcumin in the Treatment of Various Diseases: Mechanism of Action, Bioavailability, Therapeutic Effects, and Current Clinical Trials.
authorString: Wang L, Pan Q, Long W, Li X, Mao J, Zhou S, Wang Z, Zou X, She Y, Shi M, Zhou Y, Du J, Hu Z, Lv X, Chen Y, Qin D.
abstractText: Curcumin is a naturally occurring polyphenolic compound with anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antiapoptotic, and anticancer properties. Numerous studies have demonstrated that curcumin can regulate multiple molecular targets, including signaling pathways such as Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/myeloid differentiation primary response 88 (MyD88)/nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB), Janus kinase (JAK)/signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT), PTEN-induced kinase 1 (PINK1)/Parkin, Parkin, phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (Akt), mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), and nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2)/antioxidant response element (ARE). Notably, curcumin exhibits therapeutic potential in a variety of diseases, including neurological disorders, cardiovascular diseases, cancer, inflammatory diseases, and autoimmune diseases. Its mechanisms of action are associated with the suppression of inflammation, regulation of mitochondrial dysfunction, inhibition of apoptosis, attenuation of oxidative stress, and enhancement of neuroplasticity. However, the extremely low oral bioavailability of curcumin limits its application in disease therapy. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in curcumin research, including its pharmacological properties, molecular mechanisms of action, and nanodelivery systems, such as nanoparticles, liposomes, nanoemulsions, polymeric micelles, and exosomes, which have been developed to enhance curcumin bioavailability. Furthermore, this review provides an in-depth overview of the therapeutic benefits of curcumin in neurological disorders, cardiovascular diseases, cancer, inflammatory diseases, and autoimmune diseases. It focuses on evidence from in vitro studies, in vivo experiments, and potential clinical applications, while also discusses the therapeutic potential, current challenges, and future perspectives of curcumin in disease management.

title: Semaglutide versus diet-based weight loss in obesity and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (FIT-HF): Protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
authorString: El-Sheikh M, Bandholm T, Jørgensen NB, Ulrik CS, Barløse M, Møller S, Siebner HR, Grand J, Barasa A, Petersen M, Madsbad S, Yang Lee MM, Dirksen C, Hove JD.
abstractText:
Background & aims

Obesity is common in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), but the functional, mechanistic, and safety consequences of intentional weight loss remain uncertain. Incretin-based therapies improve symptoms and functional capacity in obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, whereas evidence in HFrEF is limited, and prior glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist trials have raised safety concerns. The FIT-HF trial tests whether semaglutide-based weight loss is superior to intensive diet-based weight loss for improving exercise capacity in adults with obesity and stable HFrEF.

Methods

FIT-HF is an investigator-initiated, randomized, parallel-group, open-label, assessor-blinded, active-comparator superiority trial enrolling 100 adults with body mass index ≥30 kg/m2, left ventricular ejection fraction ≤40%, New York Heart Association class I-III symptoms, and stable guideline-directed heart failure therapy. Participants are randomized 1:1 to once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide, titrated to a target dose of 2.4 mg, or low-calorie total dietary replacement of approximately 800 kcal/day for 8 weeks followed by a dietitian-led weight-maintenance program. Both groups receive lifestyle counseling, heart failure care, and structured physical training from week 16. Follow-up is 52 weeks. The primary endpoint is the adjusted between-group difference in change in weight-indexed peak oxygen uptake (VO2peak) from baseline to week 52, assessed by cardiopulmonary exercise testing. Supportive secondary endpoints include Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score, 6-min walk distance, left ventricular end-systolic volume assessed by cardiovascular magnetic resonance, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide. Exploratory work packages assess safety, cardiac/pulmonary physiology, body composition, physical activity, and metabolic/biomarker responses.

Discussion

FIT-HF is the first direct comparison of these weight-loss strategies in obesity and HFrEF, integrating VO2peak with multimodal phenotyping to interpret physiological profiles alongside achieved weight loss and body composition.

Clinical trial registration

European Clinical Trials Information System: European Union trial number: CT-2023-503753-35-01; ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06423599.

title: Bempedoic Acid in Statin-Intolerant Patients: Real-World Implementation Strategies, Cardiovascular Outcomes Beyond the CLEAR Trial, and Combination Therapy Approaches.
authorString: Vergara Sanchez C, Lopes RA, Shapiro MD.
abstractText:
Purpose of the review

Statin intolerance remains a significant barrier to achieving lipid goals and reducing atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk. Bempedoic acid (BA), an oral ATP-citrate lyase inhibitor activated predominantly in the liver, offers a non-statin lipid-lowering option with a low propensity for muscle-related adverse effects. This review seeks to discuss BA use in real-world practice.

Recent findings

This review summarizes BA pharmacology, cardiovascular outcomes, safety, combination strategies, and real-world implementation in individuals who are either statin intolerant or unwilling to take statins. The CLEAR clinical trial series established BA's lipid-lowering effect and safety profile, culminating in CLEAR Outcomes, which further demonstrated fewer major adverse cardiovascular events among patients with established ASCVD or at high cardiovascular risk. Although these findings are compelling, they are limited to this population, and the impact in low- to borderline-risk populations remains unclear. In practice, clinicians should assess the potential contribution of the nocebo effect, distinguish partial versus complete statin intolerance, preserve any tolerated statin exposure, define the residual lipid-lowering gap, and align treatment intensity with cardiovascular risk and patient preferences. BA may then be considered within a guideline-directed framework that accounts for treatment access, tolerability, and shared decision-making. Combination therapy with BA and ezetimibe represents a practical oral option, whereas PCSK9-targeted therapy may be preferred when the gap to lipid goals is sufficiently large or the patient is at high ASCVD risk. Clinicians should also provide risk-based counseling and monitoring for potential adverse effects, including hyperuricemia, gout, and tendon injury. Overall, BA represents a valuable addition to the lipid-lowering armamentarium.

title: Remimazolam versus Propofol for General Anesthesia in Elderly Patients Undergoing TAVI: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authorString: Jing H, Qin P, Shen X, Zhang H, Song S, Lin H.
abstractText: Background Remimazolam, a novel short-acting benzodiazepine, has emerged as a potential alternative to propofol for anesthesia. This study aimed to examine the effectiveness and safety of remimazolam compared to propofol for anesthesia in elderly patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) procedures. Methods We conducted a single-center, prospective, randomized controlled, non-inferiority trial in elderly patients undergoing TAVI under general anesthesia with a laryngeal mask airway (LMA). The eligibility criterion was age 65 to 80 years. Of 118 patients assessed for eligibility, 76 met the inclusion criteria and were randomized (39 remimazolam, 37 propofol). Patients were blinded to allocation; the treating anesthesiologist, who administered the agents and recorded the emergence times, was not blinded. The primary outcome was time to LMA removal, with a prespecified non-inferiority margin of 2 minutes. Results The remimazolam group demonstrated significantly faster recovery: LMA removal time was 9.7 ± 1.5 minutes versus 20.8 ± 2.0 minutes in the propofol group (mean difference − 11.1 minutes, 95% confidence interval (CI) − 11.9 to − 10.3; p < 0.001), indicating both non-inferiority and, as a post-hoc observation, superiority. Recovery of consciousness (6.7 ± 1.6 vs. 16.6 ± 2.2 minutes, p < 0.001) and time to spontaneous respiration (8.5 ± 1.5 vs. 19.4 ± 2.2 minutes, p < 0.001) were also significantly shorter with remimazolam. Total norepinephrine dose was lower in the remimazolam group (0.06 ± 0.03 vs. 0.17 ± 0.05 mg, p < 0.001), a descriptive finding not interpreted as evidence of hemodynamic superiority given the prophylactic-infusion protocol. Hospital length of stay did not differ significantly (10 [8–12] vs. 11 [10–13] days, p = 0.06). Conclusions In elderly patients undergoing TAVI under general anesthesia, remimazolam was associated with significantly faster recovery than propofol and met the prespecified non-inferiority margin for time to LMA removal; the large observed difference is a post-hoc, hypothesis-generating finding. Because the trial was single-center and retrospectively registered, these results should be interpreted with caution and require confirmation in protocolized, prospectively registered multicenter trials. Trial registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR; https://www.chictr.org.cn/), ChiCTR2500109737. Registered on 24 September 2025; retrospectively registered.

title: Genotype and Phenotype Description in Individuals With <i>GYG1</i> Variants-A Case Report and Systematic Review.
authorString: Schadeck M, Tankeu A, Elmers J, Hewer E, Maurer F, Monney P, Théaudin M, Tran C.
abstractText: Glycogen Storage Disease Type XV (GSD XV) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in GYG1, encoding glycogenin-1. Although primarily a myopathic disease, cardiac involvement is increasingly recognized and overlapping features with other neuromuscular disorders contribute to underdiagnosis. We performed a systematic search of databases without restrictions on publication dates. Twenty-one articles describing individuals with GSD XV were included, providing clinical, histological, and genetic data. In addition to the systematic review, we present an illustrative case of GSD XV diagnosed at our institution. We identified 49 individuals, of whom 98% were symptomatic with onset ranging from childhood to late adulthood; manifestations were isolated neuromuscular (81.6%), cardiac (8.2%), or mixed (8.2%). One case (2.0%) was asymptomatic. Among neuromuscular cases, 12% required a walking aid, while four cardiac patients required implantable cardioverter-defibrillators and two underwent heart transplantation. Muscle biopsy frequently revealed PAS-positive, diastase-resistant polyglucosan bodies, although polyglucosan bodies were not consistently identified by electron microscopy. Molecular diagnosis was confirmed in all cases, with c.143+3G>C in GYG1 being the most prevalent variant, homozygous in 36.7% of patients and associated with both juvenile and adult-onset phenotypes. GSD XV should be considered in cases with unexplained myopathy or cardiomyopathy, regardless of age at onset. Genetic testing remains the gold standard for diagnosis, although muscle biopsy can guide investigations, particularly in atypical cases or when genetic analysis is inconclusive. Further studies are needed to clarify the full clinical spectrum, refine genotype-phenotype correlations, and guide long-term management strategies.

title: Mitral valve disease in rheumatic heart disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, antiphospholipid syndrome, and rheumatoid Arthritis.
authorString: Lucki M, Grygiel-Górniak B, Lucka E, Lesiak M.
abstractText: Mitral valve disease occurs in rheumatic heart disease (RHD) and selected systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases, but similar lesions may have different underlying mechanisms. This structured narrative review examines epidemiological, mechanistic, imaging, and management evidence, distinguishing established pathways from incompletely validated mechanisms and hypotheses. In RHD, post-streptococcal valvulitis leads to fibrotic remodeling, commissural fusion, and chordal shortening, producing mitral stenosis, regurgitation, or mixed disease. A meta-analysis of 215,552 children and adolescents in endemic settings reported echocardiographically detected RHD in 24 per 1000. In systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and antiphospholipid syndrome (APS), typical findings include leaflet thickening, Libman-Sacks vegetations, and regurgitation; embolic complications may occur despite mild valve dysfunction. Among 508 clinically selected patients with SLE undergoing echocardiography, 27.4% had heart valve involvement and 11.2% had mitral involvement. Immunothrombotic mechanisms may contribute to these lesions, but direct validation in human valve tissue remains incomplete. In rheumatoid arthritis (RA), a prospective cohort found an association with incident mitral regurgitation (adjusted hazard ratio 1.54, 95% confidence interval 1.32-1.81), but not mitral stenosis. Myocardial imaging findings do not establish a causal link to regurgitation. These findings support anatomy- and severity-based assessment in RHD, combined valvular and thromboembolic evaluation in SLE/APS, and assessment of conventional regurgitation mechanisms in RA. The framework informs clinical interpretation within existing guidelines, while proposed disease-specific mechanisms require further validation.

title: Closing the loop: a needs-assessment informed model for embedding a non-allergist penicillin allergy de-labelling service in acute medicine, a quality improvement report.
authorString: Toner P, Glass A, Donnelly C, Garnett K, Mchaffie M, Quinn S, Hillen C, Mullan J, Mustafa YH, Maguire C, Faulkner S, Ng B, Brady A.
abstractText:
Objectives

To describe and evaluate a needs-assessment informed model for embedding a non-allergist penicillin allergy de-labelling (PADL) service within an Acute Medical Unit (AMU), including stakeholder experience.

Methods

A four-phase quality improvement project in one UK AMU, reported per SQUIRE 2.0. Phase 1: needs-assessment survey of 124 staff (pharmacists, doctors, nurses, immunology staff). Phase 2: a multidisciplinary team translated Phase 1 barriers into a PEN-FAST-guided direct oral amoxicillin challenge (DOC) protocol delivered by acute medicine consultants and pharmacists; design decisions were retrospectively mapped to the capability, opportunity and motivation model for behavioural change and Behaviour Change Wheel. Phase 3: DOC in 60 adult inpatients penicillin allergy labels. Phase 4: post-implementation survey of 54 patients and staff.

Results

Before implementation, 90% of staff anticipated a service would be useful, but identified time, education, safety concerns and staffing as the main barriers. Fifty-nine of 60 patients (98.3%) were de-labelled, with one mild Type 4 reaction but no anaphylaxis. All 21 (35.6%) who needed antibiotics within six months received a penicillin without reported reaction. All 54 post-implementation respondents rated the service extremely useful and would recommend or refer into it; as Phase 1 and Phase 4 cohorts were non-matched, this comparison is indicative only. Patients described years of unwarranted anxiety about antibiotic use that resolved after de-labelling.

Conclusions

A needs-assessment-informed model translated staff-identified barriers into design decisions and was associated with high stakeholder endorsement, durable penicillin use and an under-recognized psychological benefit for patients. It offers a practical, replicable template for non-allergist PADL in acute medicine.

title: Multivessel Assessment by Angiography-Derived Index of Microcirculatory Resistance in Patients With Nonobstructive Coronary Artery Disease.
authorString: Lui CL, Xuan HC, Huang JY, Zhang JN, Gu WL, Guo R, Ren QW, Li Y, Wong CCY, Yiu KH.
abstractText:
Background

Current guidelines recommend testing for coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) in the left anterior descending coronary artery, and it is unclear whether multivessel assessment can improve the diagnostic yield and prognostic value of CMD.

Objectives

The aim of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic implications of multivessel CMD assessment using angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance (angio-IMR) in patients with nonobstructive coronary artery disease (NOCAD).

Methods

Angio-IMR was measured in all 3 major coronary arteries in 439 patients with NOCAD. Single-vessel assessment was defined as angio-IMR measurement in the left anterior descending coronary artery only. Multivessel assessment was defined as angio-IMR measurement in all 3 major coronary arteries. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events, comprising a composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and hospitalization for heart failure.

Results

Multivessel assessment identified more patients with CMD than single-vessel assessment (46.7% vs 24.1%; P < 0.001). During a median follow-up period of 4.3 years, an increased number of vessels with CMD was associated with a higher risk for major adverse cardiovascular events after adjustment for diabetes mellitus, smoking, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and history of myocardial infarction (adjusted HR: 1.963 per vessel; 95% CI: 1.513-2.548; P < 0.001). Multivessel assessment showed superior prognostic performance compared with single-vessel assessment when added to a clinical risk factor model (area under the curve: 0.751 vs 0.707; P = 0.034).

Conclusions

Multivessel assessment by angio-IMR improved the diagnostic yield of CMD and added incremental prognostic information compared with single-vessel assessment in patients with NOCAD.

title: Multi-omics and Functional Analyses Identify Cancer-associated Fibroblast-derived Insulin-like Growth Factor 1 as a Stromal Mediator of Lung Adenocarcinoma Progression.
authorString: Deng J, Sheng J, You L, Han Q, Wang Y, Pan H, Lu Y, Cai X, Liu H, Han W.
abstractText: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, yet the stromal mechanisms driving rapid disease progression are incompletely understood. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing with exploratory whole-exome sequencing to characterize tumor microenvironment remodeling in a rapidly progressing LUAD patient. Tumor tissue exhibited marked stromal enrichment, with inflammatory cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) constituting a prominent fibroblast subset. Receptor-ligand and cell-type-specific expression analyses identified CAF-derived insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1) as a potential stromal mediator of LUAD progression. This fibroblast-specific IGF1 pattern was corroborated by an external single-cell dataset and by immunofluorescence validation in LUAD tissues with or without bone metastasis. Functionally, recombinant IGF1 enhanced LUAD cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, whereas IGF1 knockdown in CAF-like cells attenuated these malignant phenotypes in co-culture models. In vivo, IGF1 knockdown in CAF-like cells reduced distant metastatic burden, accompanied by alterations in Wnt-related signaling, extracellular matrix organization, and metastasis-associated molecules. These findings indicate that CAF-derived IGF1 contributes to LUAD progression and bone metastatic remodeling through paracrine stromal-tumor communication, highlighting the IGF1/IGF1R axis as a potential stromal-directed therapeutic target in selected LUAD patients.

title: Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease: Epidemiology, Pathogenesis, and Emerging Therapeutic Targets.
authorString: Wang S, Hu Y, Chu H.
abstractText: Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) represents a leading cause of preventable liver-related morbidity and mortality worldwide. Despite its growing global burden, no pharmacological therapies targeting disease progression have achieved clinical approval, with management still centered on alcohol abstinence and supportive care. Classic pathogenic mechanisms, including ethanol metabolism, oxidative stress, innate immune activation, and regulated cell death, are well recognized, yet emerging evidence highlights the gut-liver axis and intestinal dysbiosis as critical, interactive drivers of disease pathophysiology. However, how gut microbial imbalance mechanistically intersects with these canonical pathways to accelerate ALD progression remains insufficiently integrated. This article summarizes the epidemiology, clinical manifestations, and pathogenesis of ALD. Importantly, we focus specifically on changes in the gut microbiota (including bacteria, fungi, and viruses) and microbial metabolites. We further discuss the interactive relationships between dysbiosis and these core mechanisms. Finally, we summarize progress in preclinical and clinical research on targeted strategies such as probiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation, and phage therapy. By synthesizing the research findings, we propose a stage-based, mechanism-oriented framework aimed at advancing the development of safer and more precise therapeutic interventions for ALD.

title: Determinants of cardiovascular disease among people living with HIV on antiretroviral therapy in northern Nigeria.
authorString: Abdulkadir Z, Kwaku AA, Olawumi AL, Suleiman AK, Michael GC, Grema BA, Tsiga-Ahmed FI, Musa BM, Wester CW, Sani MU, Aliyu MH.
abstractText:
Background

People living with HIV (PLWH) exhibit a two-fold higher incidence of cardiovascular disease compared to HIV-negative persons. However, determinants of cardiovascular disease risk in PLWH are still evolving. The objective of this study is to evaluate the determinants of cardiovascular disease among PLWH in Nigeria.

Methods

This cross-sectional study was conducted from 30th September to 11th November 2024 among adult patients attending the HIV clinic of Aminu Kano Teaching Hospital, Kano, ​Nigeria. We used systematic sampling to recruit participants and computed their 5-year projected CVD risk using the Data collection on Adverse effects of Anti-HIV Drugs (DAD) equation. We analysed data collected using IBM SPSS Statistical software for windows, version 26 and binary logistic regression was used to identify the determinants of CVD risk among PLWH.

Results

The majority of participants were female (70.6%). The estimated median 5-year CVD risk was 0.7% (interquartile range, IQR 0.4, 10). The majority of participants (58.9%) had a low risk of developing cardiovascular disease, while 28.9% had a moderate risk. Cardiovascular disease was associated with elevated high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) > 3.03 mg/L [adjusted odds ratio, aOR: 4.58, 95% CI: 2.09-10.05), p = 0.001], increasing age [aOR 2.38, 95% CI (1.48-4.50), p = 0.020], male sex [aOR 2.16, 95% CI (1.03-4.53), p = 0.040] and hypercholesterolemia [aOR 3.03, 95% CI (1.68-4.86), p = 0.005].

Conclusion

The majority of PLWH in our setting have low to moderate risk of developing cardiovascular disease. Cardiovascular disease risk was associated with elevated hsCRP, increasing age, male sex, and hypercholesterolemia. Our findings highlight the importance of integrating CVD screening in HIV care to reduce morbidity and mortality among PLWH.

Supplementary information

The online version contains supplementary material. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12982-026-03262-6.

title: Evaluation of a postpartum cardiovascular risk clinic after hypertensive disorder of pregnancy: First-year experience.
authorString: Ait Ouarab D, Lefebvre J, Côté AM, Cumyn A, Champagne M, Lafrenière K, Malick M, Pesant MH, Roy-Lacroix MÈ, Sauvé N.
abstractText:
Background

Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy increase future cardiovascular risk. The Clinique Santé Globale PostPartum (CSGPP) was created to assess risk, provide lifestyle counseling, and inform primary care providers. This study was meant to assess its relevance, efficacy, and women's satisfaction to optimize the clinic.

Methods

This descriptive, single-center prospective cohort study was conducted at the Centre Hospitalier Universitaire de Sherbrooke. Women were recruited at their first CSGPP visit. Data on attendance, lifestyle behaviors, motivation, follow-up with primary care providers, and satisfaction were collected at baseline and 12 months postpartum.

Results

Of 104 referrals, 84 women (80.8%) attended the first visit, 65 agreed to participate, and 47 completed follow-up. Belief in the health benefits of lifestyle changes increased (P = .007), and satisfaction with the clinic was high.

Conclusion

Given the high adherence and satisfaction with the clinic, these findings support expanding access to the clinic to all conditions increasing CVD in this young population.

title: Hypoxic Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cell-Derived Cardiomyocytes Release Large Extracellular Vesicles That Promote a Pro-Inflammatory Phenotype in Macrophages.
authorString: Viola M, Maas RGC, Lowik JM, Driedonks TAP, Benavente ED, van de Schepop L, Seinen CS, Blok CJBS, de Jager SCA, Vader P, Sluijter JPG.
abstractText: Directly post-infarction, myocardial tissue release signals that trigger an acute inflammatory response to clear debris and initiate cardiac repair. However, prolonged inflammation may drive adverse remodelling and heart failure in the long-term. Therefore, understanding the mechanisms of acute and chronic inflammation after myocardial infarction (MI) is crucial for developing targeted treatments. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) mediate intercellular communication by carrying diverse biomolecules, such as proteins, that influence recipient cell behaviour. Cardiomyocyte-derived EVs (CM-EVs) are known to play a role in both cardiac repair and the progression of heart failure following MI. However, little is known about CM-EV subpopulations and how they modulate post-infarction inflammation. Here, we demonstrate that human CM-EV subpopulations can modulate macrophage phenotype. We identified three EV subpopulations, defined by their sedimentation coefficients, with distinct density and proteome profiles released by human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs). The 2K, 10K and 100K pellets, collected by differential ultracentrifugation of the conditioned medium, are enriched, respectively, in sarcomeric components, metabolic proteins and proteins involved in transport to the plasma membrane. Proteomic analysis revealed that hypoxia changes the proteome of EV-containing pellets, enriching for proteins involved in cellular stress responses, such as chaperones, ribosomal, proteasomal and metabolic proteins. Next, we observed that both normoxic and hypoxic CM-EVs are internalized by macrophages, and the hypoxic 10K pellet induces a pro-inflammatory phenotype in these cells. Future research should elucidate whether CM-EVs contribute to excessive inflammation and adverse cardiac remodelling post-MI in vivo and if this can be modulated by blocking the release of specific CM-EV subpopulations.

title: Associations of Pathogenic Sequence Variants and Copy Number Variants with Cardiovascular and Major Clinical Outcomes in Adults with Congenital Heart Disease
authorString: Youssef P, Broussous F, Alhussain H, Rana K, Al-Najjar M, Islam MM, Kashipovich AX, Dasi HC, Aman MH, Kabul MAK, Chauhan P.
abstractText:
Background

Genetic abnormalities play a role in the phenotypic heterogeneity of congenital heart disease (CHD), but their associations with long-term cardiovascular outcomes in adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) remain inadequately defined. This study examined the correlations between pathogenic sequence variations and copy number variants (CNVs) with cardiovascular and significant clinical outcomes in persons suffering from CHD.

Methods

This prospective observational cohort study included 1,000 adults with structurally confirmed CHD recruited from a tertiary care centre in Noida, India, between January 2022 and January 2026, with follow-up through August 2026. Those who have consented received exome sequencing and chromosomal microarray assessment and were categorized into four distinct, non-overlapping groups: reference, sequence-variant-only, CNV-only, and dual-positive. The primary outcome was the time to the first occurrence of any of the following events: cardiovascular death, unplanned heart failure hospitalization, resuscitated cardiac arrest, qualifying sustained ventricular tachyarrhythmia, heart transplantation or durable mechanical circulatory support. Appropriate statistical analysis was performed and results were obtained.

Results

The results showed that among the participants recruited, 800 were in the reference group, 120 had sequence variants alone, 60 had CNVs alone, and 20 had both sequence variants and CNVs. Over a median follow-up of 4.2 years, the primary outcome occurred in 12.0%, 20.0%, 25.0%, and 30.0% of participants, respectively. In the fully adjusted model, the sequence-variant-only group had an HR of 1.65 (95% CI, 1.01–2.69; nominal p = 0.0455), while the CNV-only group had an HR of 1.92 (95% CI, 1.04–3.52; nominal p = 0.0360), compared with the reference group. After Holm adjustment, neither association reached statistical significance (adjusted p = 0.072 for both comparisons). The dual-positive group had an HR of 2.12 (95% CI, 0.83–5.42; p = 0.1182). Extracardiac congenital anomalies and neurological disorders were more prevalent in those with genetic variations. Nonetheless, the secondary outcomes revealed no statistically significant correlations.

Conclusions

Pathogenic sequence variations and CNVs exhibited a numerically elevated adjusted risk for the primary cardiovascular composite outcome in ACHD, however neither primary association reached statistical significance after multiplicity adjustment. The findings highlight the potential significance of genetic diversity concerning clinical variability in ACHD, however they do not confirm independent prognostic significance.

title: Uncovering Distinct Phenotypes of Early Onset Heart Failure in Women
authorString: Khorsandi J, Yu Y, Tinnium DK, Ganesh S, Alahapphan R, Oyinloye P, Mueller K, Ardekani S, Taylor CO, Greenstein JL, Ndumele CE, Michos ED, Bairey Merz N, Barrett RB, Minhas AS.
abstractText:
Background

Heart failure in younger women is understudied and may reflect heterogeneous pathways and risk not adequately captured by conventional classifications. We aimed to identify clinically distinct phenotypes of early-onset heart failure in women, assess their prognostic significance, and evaluate their transportability in an independent national cohort.

Methods

We identified women aged 18-55 years with heart failure using electronic health record data from a large multi-hospital system. A variational deep embedding model incorporating 283 clinical features was used for unsupervised phenotyping. Associations with subsequent inpatient hospitalization, emergency department utilization, and mortality were evaluated using age-stratified Cox models. Phenotype transportability was assessed by both applying the institutionally trained model and by independent de novo clustering as a replication analysis in the All of Us cohort.

Results

Among 1,407 young women with heart failure (median age, 45 years), four phenotypes were identified: hypertensive pregnancy (n=494), cardiorenal (n=276), autoimmune (n=394), and cardiometabolic-ischemic (n=243), with a bootstrap adjusted Rand index of 0.65 and silhouette score of 0.45. Compared with the hypertensive pregnancy phenotype, risks of inpatient hospitalization were highest for the cardiorenal (HR 2.86 [95% CI, 2.35–3.49]) and autoimmune (HR 2.25 [95% CI, 1.87–2.70]) phenotypes; mortality risks were similarly elevated (HR 4.65 [95% CI, 3.17–6.82] and HR 4.38 [95% CI, 3.03–6.31], respectively) in these two groups. In All of Us participants (n=682), transferred phenotypes retained their principal clinical characteristics and continued to stratify hospitalization risk. Independent clustering most strongly reproduced the cardiorenal phenotype (Jaccard index, 0.744).

Conclusions

Early-onset heart failure in women comprises distinct cardio-obstetric, cardiorenal, autoimmune, and cardiometabolic-ischemic phenotypes with divergent clinical outcomes. These findings support a life-course approach to heart failure classification in women that complements conventional frameworks and incorporates pregnancy history and female-predominant systemic conditions.

Clinical Perspective

What Is New?

Unsupervised machine learning identifies distinct clinical phenotypes of heart failure among young women, highlighting heterogeneity in a population that remains understudied. These phenotypes captured differing cardiometabolic, cardiovascular, and pregnancy-related characteristics, suggesting potentially distinct pathways contributing to heart failure development. External validation in the All of Us cohort supported external validity and demonstrated the potential for identifying these patterns across diverse healthcare populations.

What Are the Clinical Implications?

Heart failure in young women is clinically diverse, underscoring the importance of comprehensive assessment beyond traditional heart failure classifications, including cardiometabolic risk factors and pregnancy history. Recognition of distinct clinical phenotypes may help clinicians identify women with differing risk profiles and inform more individualized approaches to cardiovascular evaluation, risk factor management, and longitudinal follow-up. Further studies are needed to determine whether phenotypes differ in treatment responses and whether phenotype-guided management can improve outcomes.

title: Cardiovascular Disease Subtypes and Osteoporosis: Epidemiological Evidence, Biological Mechanisms, and Clinical Perspectives
authorString: Chazanga L, Shi Z, Dhakal R, Sha Q, Chen Q, Zhou W.
abstractText: Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) and osteoporosis pose major clinical challenges for older adults worldwide. Evidence suggests these diseases are interconnected through shared biological mechanisms and risk factors. However, differences in the associations between specific CVD subtypes and osteoporosis remain incompletely understood. We examine osteoporosis in relation to coronary artery disease (CAD) and myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, atrial fibrillation (AF), peripheral arterial disease (PAD), and heart failure (HF). The review considers epidemiological evidence, shared biological mechanisms, medication effects, and questions for future research on cardiovascular–bone interactions. Studies addressing CVD, bone mineral density (BMD), osteoporosis, or fracture outcomes were identified through PubMed and backward citation searching.Across these cardiovascular conditions, studies report associations with low BMD, osteoporosis, or hip fracture. Their magnitude and consistency vary, however, according to the CVD subtype, study population, and skeletal outcome. Proposed links include chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, vascular calcification, endocrine dysregulation, and changes in RANK/RANKL/OPG and Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Genomic approach, large population-based cohorts, and causal inference methods offer opportunities to improve understanding of the complex cardiovascular-bone interactions. Further research is needed to classify subtype-specific associations and mechanisms, assess potential causal relationships, and determine whether these insights can improve risk prediction, prevention, early detection, and management of CVDs, osteoporosis, and osteoporotic hip fractures.

title: Clinical Phenotype and Outcomes of Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children According to SARS-CoV-2 Laboratory Status During 2020-2021: A Retrospective Observational Study.
authorString: Armin S, Hoseini-Alfatemi SM, Ghanaiee RM, Karimi A, Rahimidanesh N, Ashnaei A, Fakhfouri A, Jafrasteh A, Soleimani Y.
abstractText:
Background and aims

Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) is a post-infectious inflammatory condition associated with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) that can affect multiple organ systems. Data comparing clinical features and outcomes between MIS-C patients with and without laboratory evidence of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) remain limited.

Methods

This retrospective observational study was conducted at Mofid Children's Hospital, a pediatric referral center in Tehran, Iran, between March 2020 and July 2021. Children diagnosed with MIS-C based on World Health Organization (WHO) criteria were included and classified into groups with and without laboratory evidence of SARS-CoV-2 infection according to PCR and/or IgG serology results. Demographic data, clinical manifestations, laboratory and imaging findings, treatments, and outcomes were compared between the groups using univariate and multivariable analyses. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

Results

A total of 121 patients with MIS-C were included, of whom 44 (36.4%) had laboratory evidence of SARS-CoV-2 infection. The mean age was 4.74 ± 3.99 years, and 61.2% were male. ICU admission occurred in 21.5% and mortality was 2.5%. In univariate analysis, fever during the first 24 h of hospitalization and antiviral use were more frequent in the group with laboratory evidence, whereas conjunctivitis and elevated C-reactive protein levels were more common among the group without laboratory evidence; however, CRP did not differ significantly between groups when analyzed as a continuous variable. In multivariable analysis, fever during the first 24 h of hospitalization was the only variable associated with laboratory evidence of SARS-CoV-2 infection (aOR 2.57; 95% CI 1.05-6.30; p = 0.040).

Conclusion
