MIS-C presents with broad and largely overlapping clinical, laboratory, and imaging features regardless of SARS-CoV-2 laboratory status, and the few observed differences were exploratory and of limited discriminative value. These findings highlight the importance of considering MIS-C even in the absence of laboratory confirmation of SARS-CoV-2 infection.

title: Pannexin-1 (PANX1) in Metabolic Diseases: Structural Basis, Molecular Mechanisms, and Pharmacological Significance.
authorString: Fu G, Wang Z, Rao B, Liu J, Ouyang H.
abstractText: Metabolic diseases, including obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), atherosclerosis (AS), and diabetes-related complications, are characterized by disrupted glucose and lipid metabolism, chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, and progressive tissue dysfunction. Pannexin-1 (PANX1), a large-pore membrane channel that mediates regulated ATP release, has emerged as an important interface between metabolic stress and extracellular purinergic signaling. PANX1 influences metabolic homeostasis through ATP-dependent and broader signaling mechanisms that regulate insulin action and secretion, hepatic glucose and lipid metabolism, autophagy, vascular function, inflammatory responses, and regulated cell death. Its effects are highly context dependent. PANX1 can support metabolic homeostasis in adipocytes, pancreatic β cells, hepatocytes, and selected vascular cell populations, whereas sustained or dysregulated PANX1 signaling may promote inflammation, vascular dysfunction, ferroptosis, and pyroptosis under metabolic stress. These divergent actions are shaped by cellular origin, disease stage, and the local metabolic environment. This review summarizes current understanding of PANX1 structure, channel gating, and regulatory mechanisms and integrates predominantly preclinical evidence for its involvement in metabolic homeostasis and related diseases. We further examine the interactions of PANX1 with purinergic signaling, inflammation, oxidative stress, organelle homeostasis, and regulated cell death, together with current pharmacological strategies targeting PANX1. Although most available PANX1 modulators remain primarily mechanistic tools and lack direct evidence of therapeutic efficacy in metabolic disease models, these findings provide a foundation for the future development and evaluation of more selective PANX1-targeted interventions.

title: Comparative outcomes of endovascular versus synthetic bypass for isolated superficial femoral artery lesions: A 3-year single-center cohort study.
authorString: Han C, Kim GM, Choi J, Tak YJ, Lee C, Lee CW, Bae M, Wang IJ, Huh U.
abstractText: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) ranges from intermittent claudication to critical limb‑threatening ischemia (CLTI), with <3% of intermittent claudication cases progressing to CLTI. This study aimed to compare the outcomes of percutaneous transluminal angioplasty with stenting (PTAS) and synthetic graft femoropopliteal bypass (FPB) in a homogeneous PAD cohort. A subgroup analysis of TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus (TASC) B and C lesions, which lack standardized treatment algorithms, was also performed. We retrospectively analyzed 88 patients with no prior history of vascular interventions in the same limb who were treated for isolated superficial femoral artery lesions between 2016 and 2020 (29 underwent PTAS and 59 underwent FPB). Primary outcomes were reintervention, limb amputation, mortality, and vessel patency (primary, assisted primary, and secondary) over a 3‑year follow‑up. Subgroup analysis was performed to assess differences in treatment outcomes. No statistically significant differences were detected in reintervention, limb amputation, mortality, or patency between the two treatments. For loss of primary patency, the hazard ratio (HR) for FPB versus PTAS was 1.89 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.76-4.69; log-rank p = 0.146) and 1.23 (95% CI, 0.45-3.38) after adjustment for lesion length and TASC grade. In the TASC B and C subgroup, no significant differences were observed in primary, assisted primary, or secondary patency (log-rank p = 0.809, 0.302, and 0.135, respectively). The study was underpowered to detect modest effects (post-hoc power for primary patency, 34.4%). In this small single-center cohort, no statistically significant difference in 3-year outcomes was detected between PTAS and FPB for isolated superficial femoral artery lesions; clinically meaningful differences cannot be excluded, and the findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating.

title: Time to Storm the Next CASTLE: Can Atrial Fibrillation Ablation Improve Outcomes in Patients With Heart Failure and Preserved Ejection Fraction?
authorString: Darzi AE, Moersdorf M, Khalil MA, Massad CM, Atasi MM, Menassa Y, Khoury CE, Marrouche NF.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and atrial fibrillation frequently coexist and are linked by shared mechanisms including atrial myopathy, elevated filling pressures, fibrosis, and adverse hemodynamic interactions. The combination of both diseases worsens patient outcomes, and catheter ablation has emerged as a potentially important treatment strategy in this population. This review aims to summarize and highlight the current evidence on ablation in patients with atrial fibrillation and HFpEF.

Recent findings

When examining outcomes of mortality, hospitalization, hemodynamics, and recurrence, ablation appears to be superior to medical treatment with some mixed results. However, no large trials have been conducted on the topic, and no clear guidelines for ablation in HFpEF patients exist. Ablation is promising but not yet definitive for patients with atrial fibrillation and HFpEF. Ongoing trials, including CASTLE-HFpEF should clarify the gaps including patient selection, procedural strategy, and outcome benefit.

title: Advancements in Artificial Intelligence for Enhanced Diagnosis and Prognosis in Cardiac CT: a Comprehensive Review and Future Perspectives.
authorString: Adabifirouzjaei F, Budoff M, Nomeli M.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

Cardiovascular disease, with coronary artery disease (CAD) as its main culprit, remains a leading cause of death worldwide. Traditional diagnostic methods that focus on the degree of arterial narrowing (percent diameter stenosis, or %DS) can miss early signs of disease or the specific plaque features that indicate high risk. The purpose of this review is to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) can enhance the diagnostic and prognostic capabilities of cardiac computed tomography (CCT), and to address where AI can most meaningfully improve diagnostic accuracy, workflow efficiency, and patient care.

Recent findings

AI is transforming cardiac CT across the entire imaging pathway. By applying AI algorithms, recent studies have refined the assessment of coronary artery calcium (CAC), improved plaque characterization, and detected subtle lesions that might evade traditional detection methods. AI further enables non-invasive assessment of ischemia (reduced blood flow), aids in the evaluation of myocardial infarction, analyzes adipose tissue surrounding the heart, improves image quality, and provides valuable prognostic insights for risk stratification. This comprehensive review explores the transformative potential of AI in cardiac CT, highlighting its role in accurate diagnosis, precise risk stratification, and personalized management of cardiovascular disease. Through collaboration between AI technology and clinical expertise, we envision a future where cardiac CT imaging is more powerful, efficient, and patient-centered, ultimately leading to improved outcomes in cardiovascular medicine. Continued standardization, external validation, and clinician education will be essential to realize this impact in routine practice.

title: Efficacy of empagliflozin in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction according to the presence of echocardiographic features of diastolic dysfunction in the EMPEROR-Preserved trial.
authorString: Stewart Coats AJ, Butler J, Zimmet H, Zannad F, Böhm M, Chopra VK, Verma S, Nordaby M, Iwata T, Pfarr E, Zeller C, Ponikowski P, Anker SD, EMPEROR-Preserved Trial Committees and Investigators.
abstractText:
Aims

To define the impact of diastolic dysfunction (DD) on the response to empagliflozin treatment in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.

Methods and results

Diastolic dysfunction was defined by left atrial volume index ≥34 ml/m2, the ratio of early diastolic mitral inflow velocity to early diastolic mitral annular tissue velocity (E/e) ≥ 13 or left ventricular mass index >115 (males) or >95 (females). We created three categories of increasing DD (0, 1, or ≥2 DD criteria at baseline) to describe the effect of DD on response to empagliflozin therapy and adverse effects. Of 5988 patients in the EMPEROR-Preserved trial, 3766 (63%) had no documented baseline DD, 1619 (27%) had one, and 603 (10%) had two or more measures. Baseline DD was associated with sex, race, ethnicity, and region and was more common with lower heart rate, DBP, body weight, and eGFR. Despite baseline DD not being significantly associated with the primary endpoint of hospitalization for heart failure or cardiovascular death within the placebo group, a progressive treatment effect across the three DD categories was seen (trend test P-value .0014), with estimated hazard ratios of empagliflozin vs placebo of 0.91 (none present), 0.64 (1 present), and 0.49 (≥2). A significant treatment-by-subgroup trend test was also observed for the total number of hospitalizations for heart failure. Both Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score improvement at week 52 and safety profile were consistent across DD categories.

Conclusion

Baseline detection of echocardiographic DD predicted improved clinical response to empagliflozin in a graded fashion, but the reasons cannot be reliably determined from this analysis.

title: A multi-center retrospective chart analysis identifying clinical, biochemical, and radiographic signatures of short-chain enoyl-CoA hydratase (ECHS1) deficiency
authorString: Kong C, Alves C, Vogel G, Xiao R, Anselm I, Berry G, Cabello JF, Cornejo V, Cortes Fernandez A, Enns GM, Gomez M, Haldeman-Englert C, Hollander S, Innes AM, Jannotta E, Kochhar A, Kopesky J, Larson A, Lee C, Lezcano M, Li R, Lines M, Morrison J, Muriello M, Null E, Peña-Quintana L, Phelps E, Saifeddine M, Sanabria MC, Saneto RP, Shelkowitz E, Tise CG, Van Hove JL, Elsharkawi I, Ganetzky R.
abstractText:
ABSTRACT

Short-chain enoyl-CoA hydratase (ECHS1) catalyzes the hydration of C4-C6 acyl-CoA molecules to produce ATP in fatty acid β-oxidation. Deficiency of the ECHS1 enzyme, ECHS1D, is a rare autosomal recessive disorder that presents with a large and pleomorphic clinical spectrum. We present the largest comprehensive study of known diagnosed ECHS1D patients to date, reporting 26 new patients and 8 novel variants in conjunction with a literature review of 87 previously reported patients. All patients were categorized into neonatal, infantile, and late-onset groups based on age of onset and clinical course. Neonatal-onset cases were characterized by early and severe multisystem disease, often with lactic acidosis, hypotonia, cardiomyopathy, and high early mortality (62.5%). The infantile-onset group was heterogeneous, but many exhibited hallmark features such as dystonia, developmental delay, and basal ganglia involvement on neuroimaging. Mortality was significantly lower than the neonatal cohort (24.4%). Late-onset patients had more localized neurologic symptoms, particularly dystonia, and significantly lower mortality overall (0%). Moreover, we report a 37.5% survival rate in newly reported neonatal onset patients compared with 18.2% in prior reports, possibly reflective of earlier recognition of ECHS1D and greater utilization of therapies including N-acetylcysteine, sodium dichloroacetate, and valine-restricted diet.

title: One-Year Outcomes of Patients Diagnosed with Peripartum dialted Cardiomyopathy: A 5-Year Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
authorString: Atanfu T, Fentie K, Chinkey F, Neda W, Berassa A, Mekonnen D.
abstractText:
Background: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is an important cause of maternal heart failure associated with variable recovery and significant morbidity and mortality. Outcomes significantly differ from region to region with lower in high-income settings and very high in Africa and Asia. However, data from Ethiopia remain limited, particularly regarding one-year clinical and echocardiographic outcomes.

Objective:

To assess the one-year clinical and echocardiographic outcomes of patients diagnosed with peripartum cardiomyopathy and to identify factors associated with poor outcomes.

Methods:

A multicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted across selected tertiary and private hospitals in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. All women diagnosed with PPCM between January 2020 and December 2024 were included using a census sampling approach. Data were extracted from electronic medical records and supplemented by phone follow-up when necessary. The primary outcomes were one-year mortality, heart failure–related hospital admission, and one-year ejection fraction recovery. A composite poor outcome was defined as death, hospital admission, or non-recovery of left ventricular function.

Results:

A total of 61 patients were included in the analysis. Five patients (8.2%) died within one year of diagnosis. Among patients with available one-year echocardiographic data, 50.8% achieved recovery of left ventricular systolic function. The remaining patients demonstrated either partial recovery or persistent systolic dysfunction. Higher baseline New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class (III–IV) was associated with poorer outcomes, including lower rates of ejection fraction recovery and increased likelihood of adverse clinical outcomes.

Conclusion:

PPCM in this Ethiopia’s associated with measurable mortality, significant morbidity and heterogeneous recovery of left ventricular function at one year. Only about half of patients achieved full recovery, with worse outcomes observed among those presenting with advanced heart failure and severely reduced ejection fraction. Outcomes appear more favorable than those reported in some African settings but remain inferior to those observed in high-income countries.

title: Technical Feasibility and Outcomes of t-Branch Proximal Shortening in Urgent Complex Aortic Repair.
authorString: Torrealba JI, Nana P, Panuccio G, Apostolidis G, Yousef Al Sarhan D, Zabel N, Kölbel T.

journal.title: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists

abstractText:
Introduction

Branched endovascular repair has shown consistently good outcomes, being sometimes the only available endovascular solution for aortic emergencies. However, in cases of limited proximal extension of the disease, such as juxtarenal or pararenal aneurysms, branched endografts usually cover a greater extent of the aorta than needed to establish a seal zone, thus increasing the risk for spinal cord ischemia (SCI) by unnecessarily covering segmental arteries.Our objective is to analyze a series of patients who underwent proximal shortening of an off-the-shelf (OTS) branched endograft to limit aortic coverage and preserve segmental arteries.

Methods

Single-center retrospective study identifying all patients undergoing branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) with a shortened t-Branch, through the removal of the first stent row, from April 2020 to March 2026.Perioperative technical success and complications were evaluated. Primary endpoints were technical success. Secondary endpoints were 30-day mortality, SCI, assessment of number of saved segmental arteries, and endograft migration at follow-up.

Results

Fifteen patients underwent BEVAR with a shortened t-Branch endograft. All were urgencies, 60% being ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs). Thirteen (86%) cases were juxta/pararenal aortic aneurysms, and 3 (20%) had a previous endovascular aortic repair. In all cases, the proximal sealing stent of the t-Branch was removed, whereas in 2 cases, an additional large posterior fenestration at the second sealing stent was created. Technical success was 93%, with 1 severely stenotic renal artery not able to be catheterized and left unbridged. No endograft deployment complication (migration or malrotation) were experienced. There was 1 postoperative mortality in a patient with a ruptured AAA. Major complication rate was 27%, including 2 patients having SCI (one grade 2, one grade 3). A median of 2 segmental arteries were saved through the endograft modification.At a median follow-up of 1 year no endograft migration was observed.

Conclusions

In urgent complex aortic repair for circumscribed anatomies such as juxta/pararenal aneurysms, the use of a modified OTS branched endograft proved to be a reproducible and safe technique, allowing the preservation of segmental arteries and possibly affecting favorably the spinal cord ischemic rates.Clinical ImpactOn-table shortening of the t-Branch endograft, optionally creating a big fenestration at the second sealing stent, is a feasible and reproducible option for urgent juxta/pararenal aortic aneurysm repair when custom-made devices are not available. The modification allowed sparing a median of two segmental arteries otherwise covered with a standard t-Branch, which might help mitigating the risk of spinal cord ischemia.

title: Vascular surgeons have better limb salvage outcomes than non-vascular surgeons in chronic limb-threatening ischemia.
authorString: Recarey M, Li R, Erguven T, Peshel EC, Fealy A, Lala S, Sidawy AN, Nguyen BH.
abstractText: BackgroundWhile the treatment of peripheral artery disease with lower extremity bypass is performed primarily by board-certified vascular surgeons, a subset of non-vascular surgeons continues performing these cases. We investigated differences in practice patterns and surgical outcomes between vascular and non-vascular surgeons for bypass in patients with claudication and chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI).MethodsThe ACS-NSQIP targeted database from 2011 to 2022 was used to select non-emergent claudication and CLTI patients. Propensity matching (3:1) was applied to balance demographics and comorbidities between vascular and non-vascular surgeons. Claudication and CLTI cohorts were analyzed separately. Thirty-day outcomes were examined.ResultsFemoropopliteal bypass was the most common procedure followed by femoral-distal bypass for both vascular and non-vascular surgeons. Vascular surgeons were more likely to perform femoral-distal procedures and use single-segment saphenous vein grafts (SSSV) for both claudication and CLTI. Vascular surgeons were less likely to use other non-SSSV conduits for claudication patients (40.6% vs 54.6%, p < 0.01), but no difference in CLTI (38.9%% vs 40.1%, p = 0.74). There was no significant difference in 30-day mortality/morbidities between surgeons for either claudication or CLTI. However, 30-day major amputation for CLTI was significantly better with vascular surgeons (3.0% vs 7.5%, p < 0.01). In CLTI patients, after correcting for operation type and conduit usage, vascular surgeons continued to be associated with lower major amputation (aOR = 0.46, 95 CI = 0.29-0.72, p < 0.01).ConclusionVascular surgeons have better limb salvage than non-vascular surgeons. This could not be explained by the higher use of SSSV; thus, other factors such as surgical skill may account for better outcomes.

title: Long-term Outcomes After Medical and Surgical Management of Blunt Traumatic Aortic Injury.
authorString: Ayouty M, DuBose JJ, Lu M, Schwieger L, Bahroloomi D, Baril D, Chou EL, Arbabi C, Gupta N, Azizzadeh A, Aortic Trauma Foundation.
abstractText:
Introduction

Blunt traumatic aortic injury (BTAI) is a common cause of morbidity and mortality after blunt force. Management strategies include non-operative management (NOM) and operative management (OM). This study evaluated patterns of follow-up and outcomes using data from the international Aortic Trauma Foundation (ATF) registry.

Methods

The ATF prospective multicenter registry was queried for patients who had subsequent follow-up at participating centers after management of BTAI. Patients were stratified by injury grade. Collected data included demographics, imaging, medical therapy, complications, and need for re-intervention.

Results

227 patients had follow-up data: Grade I (n=45), II (n=31), III (n=124), and IV (n=27). NOM was pursued in 86.7% of GI, 41.9% of GII, 7.2% of GIII, and 0% of GIV injuries while OM was performed in 13.3% of GI, 58.1% of GII, 90.4% of GIII, and 100% of GIV injuries. Anticoagulation was used in 15.7% and anti-platelet therapy in 46.4%. Five (2.2%) patients required re-intervention, mostly in GIII: 1 for failure of NOM, 2 for stent thrombosis, and 1 for subclavian steal. One patient with GII injury had reintervention for lesion progression. Morbidities (3.1%) included ischemia from left subclavian artery (LSA) coverage(n=5), embolic complication (n=1), and infection (n=1). Notably, there were no strokes, re-interventions for endoleak, or stent graft-related complications upon initial deployment.

Conclusion

Both NOM and OM demonstrated favorable outcomes with low rates of treatment failure or re-intervention. TEVAR had low device-related complication rates. However, consistent follow-up remains a challenge in the trauma population.

title: Carotid artery bypass and supraclavicular subclavian artery cannulation for cerebral malperfusion in aortic dissection.
authorString: Fasolt Richard Corvin Meinert É, Arif R, Karck M, Dib B.

journal.title: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS

abstractText: Cerebral malperfusion complicating acute aortic dissection type A is a serious complication associated with markedly increased morbidity, permanent neurological deficit, and mortality. Early cannulation and extended replacement of occluded or dissected carotid arteries is an effective yet underused strategy for improving outcomes in such patients. We present a case of acute aortic dissection type A extending from the aortic root to the right common femoral artery, complicated by an occluded right common carotid artery and a dissected left common carotid artery. The patient was successfully treated with an extensive repair comprising David's procedure, arch repair, frozen elephant trunk implantation, bilateral extended carotid artery bypass and extended left subclavian artery bypass.

title: Common arterial trunk with interrupted aortic arch in a very low-birth-weight infant: hybrid management.
authorString: Padovani P, Laribi J, Baruteau AE.
abstractText: A common arterial trunk with an interrupted aortic arch is a rare and complex CHD. Although single-stage neonatal repair can be performed in term infants, prematurity, low birthweight, and complex/multiple defects are major risk factors for in-hospital mortality. We report the first patient-specific, three-dimensional-modelling-guided, off-pump transaortic ductal stenting combined with bilateral pulmonary artery banding, performed as a bridge to successful complete repair in a very-low-birthweight, extremely premature infant with this anomaly.

title: Comparing the Practice of Routine Postnatal Clinical Examination of Healthy Newborns in Norway, Denmark and Sweden: A Survey.
authorString: Solnes Miltenburg A, Awan LM, Sahlin Torp L, Henriksen TB, Solevåg AL.
abstractText:
Aim

In many countries, all newborns undergo a routine clinical newborn examination before discharge. Key aim of this examination is to detect conditions for which early treatment may improve outcomes. This study aimed to describe variation in the timing, content, professional responsibility and follow-up arrangements for routine clinical newborn examination in Norway, Denmark and Sweden.

Methods

April to September 2024, we distributed a survey to Norwegian paediatricians and to representatives of maternity and paediatric departments in Denmark and Sweden.

Results

We analysed responses from 45 hospitals: Norway (N = 20), Denmark (N = 12) and Sweden (N = 13). In Norway and Sweden, a more comprehensive examination was generally performed by paediatricians within 72 h after birth. In Denmark, midwives typically performed a simplified examination within 12 h, with paediatric assessment when indicated. Examination content was broadly similar in Norway and Sweden but differed in Denmark. All participating hospitals reported routine pulse oximetry screening, but cardiac auscultation and follow-up of heart murmurs differed.

Conclusion

The organisation of routine clinical newborn examination differs across Scandinavia. These differences in care pathways may influence resource use and clinical decision making. Whether they translate into differences in neonatal morbidity or mortality remains unknown.

title: Modifiable cardiovascular health, inflammatory biomarkers, and risk of cardiovascular disease and mortality among Cancer survivors.
authorString: Zhang BY, Kuang L, Chen HJ, Wang YX, Tang XL, Lai SM, Huang HX, Xiong ZY, Chen SQ, Li YX, Zhu H, Zhang YH, Li YS, Huang E, Li ZH.
abstractText:
Background

Cancer survivors are at increased risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and mortality, but the roles of modifiable cardiovascular health (CVH) and systemic inflammation remain incompletely understood. We examined the associations of CVH with incident CVD and mortality and assessed potential mediation by inflammatory biomarkers.

Methods

This prospective cohort study included 11,825 cancer survivors free of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) at baseline. CVH was assessed using the Life's Essential 8 (LE8) score and the number of LE8 components meeting guideline-based thresholds. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for cardiovascular events and mortality. Mediation analyses evaluated the contributions of inflammatory biomarkers.

Results

During a median follow-up of 13.5 years, 1923 MACE events and 2082 deaths occurred. Compared with the lowest CVH tertile, the highest tertile was associated with lower risks of MACE (HR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.54-0.68), coronary heart disease (0.56; 0.48-0.65), heart failure (0.65; 0.52-0.81), stroke (0.60; 0.45-0.80), all-cause mortality (0.72; 0.64-0.80), CVD mortality (0.48; 0.32-0.72), and cancer mortality (0.74; 0.66-0.85). Each additional LE8 component under control was associated with 7%-20% lower risks across outcomes. Among significant mediation effects, C-reactive protein and the INFLA score mediated 9.7%-48.7% and 6.8%-17.9% of the associations, respectively.

Conclusions

Favorable modifiable CVH is consistently associated with substantially lower risks of cardiovascular events and mortality among cancer survivors. Inflammation biomarkers partially mediated these associations, implicating inflammation as a key biological pathway.

title: Practice Patterns and Outcomes of Women Interventional Cardiologists in Treatment of STEMI.
authorString: Shaikh N, Patel R, Wang Y, Wang TY, Curtis JP, Resnic FS.
abstractText:
Background

Women are known to have worse outcomes than men in acute myocardial infarction. There is increasing evidence that gender discordance between patients and physicians may be a contributing factor to poor outcomes. Whether the gender of the interventional cardiologist influences outcomes in STEMI and whether this varies based on patient gender is unknown. We sought to ascertain whether the gender of the interventional cardiologist has an association with patient outcome.

Methods

The NCDR CathPCI registry was queried for cases coded as "Primary PCI for STEMI" between April 2018 and March 2025. These cases were stratified by both patient and cardiologist gender. Logistic regression models were performed and sequentially adjusted for patient and hospital characteristics. Outcomes of interest were door to balloon time (DTB), in-hospital mortality, documented non-system reasons for delay, and door-to-door time (DTD) among transferred- in patients.

Results

Among 834,465 primary PCI procedures for STEMI, only 44,335 (5.3%) were performed by female interventionalists. Male interventionalists were more likely to meet DTB standards. Female interventionalists were more likely to document non-system reasons for delay. There was no evidence of influence of operator gender on the outcomes of patients, when stratified by patient gender.

Conclusions

Female interventionalists performed a small proportion of primary STEMI PCI procedures. Although female interventionalists had lower adjusted odds of achieving DTB < 90 minutes, interventionalist gender was not associated with adjusted in-hospital mortality. These findings were consistent across male and female patient subgroups and highlight persistent differences in selected care-process measures without a corresponding detectable difference in mortality.

title: Long-term safety and efficacy of arrhythmia monitoring with an implantable cardiac monitor.
authorString: Martens E, Eschalier R, Cabanas P, Jesel L, Amellone C, Milliez P, Lau D, Hain A, Mansourati J, Cuenca EG, Erglis A, Cuneo A, Ploux S, Huemer M, Steinborn F, Del Castillo S, Schrader J, Pierre B.
abstractText:
Background

Implantable cardiac monitors (ICMs) provide long-term monitoring for cardiac arrhythmias. This analysis summarizes late diagnoses, patient management and complications until 5 years after implantation.

Methods

The BIO|STREAM-ICM study is an ongoing, prospective registry capturing the real-world application of ICMs at 38 sites across 9 countries. Patients with any ICM indication are followed until device information is no longer clinically utilized. All arrhythmia diagnoses were assessed for relevance to the device indication.

Results

Of 1249 patients included in the present analysis, most received an ICM after syncope (56%) or cryptogenic stroke (30%). Follow-up extended to 5 years, 34% of patients had at least 3 years of monitoring. Kaplan-Meier estimates of the cumulative incidence of indication-related diagnosis were 31%, 36%, and 39% for syncope, and 21%, 24%, and 28% for cryptogenic stroke at 2, 3, and 4 years, respectively. After diagnosis, ICMs were explanted in 46% of cases, continued for monitoring of therapy efficacy in 41%, and inactivated but left in situ in 12%. Explantations needed a median duration of 10 min and were characterized as easy or very easy in 86% of cases. Six device related adverse events occurred later than 180 days after insertion, and none in the context of explantations.

Conclusion

ICMs continue to deliver clinically meaningful arrhythmia diagnoses in the third and fourth year post-implantation, even when the preceding follow-up has been uneventful. Long-term follow-up and explantation have a low risk. Our results affirm the safety and efficacy over the device's lifetime in clinical practice.

title: Delayed High-Output Chylothorax Following Thymectomy for Thymoma.
authorString: Nafaa M, Bencherki R, Ziati J, Noussair M, Lahcen B.
abstractText: Chylothorax is an uncommon complication following thymectomy and results from disruption of the thoracic duct or its tributaries during surgery. We report the case of a 50-year-old man with autoimmune myasthenia gravis who developed a delayed postoperative chylothorax following video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) thymectomy for a type B2 thymoma, Masaoka stage I. On postoperative day 21, the patient presented with acute respiratory distress and severe hypoxemia. Chest computed tomography revealed a large left-sided pleural effusion with extensive passive lung collapse. Thoracentesis in the emergency department evacuated 1.5 L of milky pleural fluid, followed by an additional 4 L after chest tube drainage in the intensive care unit. Pleural fluid analysis revealed a triglyceride concentration of 188 mg/dL, with chylomicrons detected, confirming the diagnosis of chylothorax. The fluid also showed marked lymphocytic predominance (96%). Management included pleural drainage, a strict fat-free diet, and octreotide, administered as a 100 µg slow intravenous loading dose followed by continuous infusion at 50 µg/h. Pleural drainage showed an overall decreasing trend and eventually ceased. Octreotide was discontinued after 13 calendar days, and the chest tube was removed without requiring additional invasive or surgical intervention. The patient was subsequently discharged home. This case illustrates that post-thymectomy chylothorax may present several weeks after surgery and that conservative management may achieve a favorable outcome even in the setting of substantial initial pleural drainage.

title: Routine Versus Clinically Indicated Cerebrospinal Fluid Sampling During Diversion Procedures: A Second-Cycle Audit at a Tertiary Neurosurgical Centre in the United Kingdom.
authorString: Basu Y.
abstractText: Background Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cultures contribute to the investigation of suspected infection associated with CSF diversion procedures. However, routine intraoperative sampling in patients without suspected infection may yield organisms, often skin commensals, of uncertain or insignificant clinical significance. A first-cycle local audit of 172 samples found that most cultures were negative and few led to treatment, and recommended avoiding routine sampling in elective cases where infection was not suspected. The primary objective of this second-cycle audit was to determine whether routine CSF sampling (performed when infection was not suspected) led to culture-driven changes in management, compared with clinically indicated sampling (performed when infection was suspected). Secondary objectives were to compare culture positivity and antibiotic initiation between the two groups and to assess the consistency of documentation of the sampling indication. Methods A retrospective re-audit of all intraoperative CSF specimens from shunt and external ventricular drain procedures at a tertiary neurosurgical centre in the United Kingdom was undertaken (from August 2024 to July 2025). Specimens were classified as routine or clinically indicated using pre-specified criteria applied to operative notes, electronic records, and microbiology request forms. The author classified all specimens and extracted all outcomes; there was no independent second reviewer. The primary outcome was a documented change in management attributable to the culture result. Categorical data were summarised as counts and percentages. No formal statistical testing was undertaken, consistent with the descriptive nature of this audit. Results Of 78 specimens, 60 (76.9%) were routine, and 18 (23.1%) were clinically indicated. Culture positivity was 16.7% (10/60) for routine and 44.4% (8/18) for clinically indicated specimens. None of the 10 routine positive cultures led to a change in management (0/10 positive routine specimens), whereas 7 of 8 indicated positive cultures did (87.5%). Microbiology request wording and clinical documentation were discordant on the indication in 14 specimens (17.9%). Conclusion Routine intraoperative CSF sampling persisted despite first-cycle guidance and, in this cohort, did not change documented management, whereas clinically indicated sampling accounted for all culture-driven management changes. The small number of events limits precision, and the absence of documented harm in a retrospective audit cannot establish that omitting routine sampling is safe. Therefore, a prospective evaluation of an indication-based pathway, with structured documentation of the indication and the missed-infection rate as a balancing measure, is warranted.

title: ABCB4 Deficiency Presenting as a Pruritus-Free Continuous Spectrum From Childhood Cholestasis to Adult Cirrhosis: A Case Report.
authorString: Ma R, Zhang W, Yang X, Zhang H.
abstractText: Progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis type 3 (PFIC3) is caused by biallelic mutations in the ABCB4 gene and typically presents in childhood. However, the full phenotypic spectrum-particularly adult-onset and pruritus-free forms-remains under-recognized. We report the case of a 28-year-old male who presented with pruritus-free decompensated cirrhosis after a 10-year diagnostic delay. Genetic testing revealed compound heterozygous ABCB4 variants [c.249C>A (p.Asp83Glu) and c.1466A>G (p.Asn489Ser)], which were initially classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS). Proactive family screening identified his asymptomatic 14-year-old sister, who carried the same genotype and exhibited significant gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) elevation (142.1 U/L) but no pruritus. Perfect genotype-phenotype cosegregation in the two siblings, combined with the absence of these variants in population databases (PM2 and PP1 criteria per American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics [ACMG] guidelines), provided decisive evidence for reclassifying the VUS as "Likely Pathogenic." This family defines a pruritus-free continuous PFIC3 spectrum and demonstrates that systematic screening of all first-degree relatives upon proband diagnosis is essential for enabling pre-symptomatic intervention. The key learning point is that ABCB4 deficiency should be considered in adults with cryptogenic cirrhosis even without pruritus, and family screening can resolve diagnostic uncertainty while facilitating early therapy.

title: Invasive Rhinoscleroma Mimicking an Aggressive Sinonasal Neoplasm: A Diagnostic Challenge-A Rare Case Report.
authorString: Kahiye MA, Ali SM, Osman FAO, Mohamed YG, Saman J.
abstractText: Rhinoscleroma is a chronic granulomatous infection of the upper respiratory tract caused by Klebsiella rhinoscleromatis. We report, to our knowledge, the first published case from Somalia. A 60-year-old woman presented after two years of progressive right proptosis, nasal obstruction, and headache. Magnetic resonance imaging showed an extensive right nasopharyngeal mass with orbital and intracranial extension, initially raising concern for malignancy. Biopsy demonstrated foamy Mikulicz cells and plasma cells with Russell bodies; periodic acid-Schiff staining highlighted intracytoplasmic organisms. Biopsy culture isolated K. rhinoscleromatis. The patient improved clinically after a two-month antibiotic course, but residual fibrotic disease remained, and planned surgery was not undertaken because of financial constraints. This case illustrates how rhinoscleroma can mimic an aggressive neoplasm and how combined histopathological and microbiological assessment can establish the diagnosis despite resource limitations.

title: Microtubule stability modulates Schlemm's canal cell mechanobiology and outflow facility in glaucoma.
authorString: Li H, Fraticelli-Guzmán NS, Perkumas KM, Chrenek M, Feola AJ, Stamer WD, Ethier CR.
abstractText: The inner wall of Schlemm's canal (SC) is a specialized mechanosensitive endothelium in which pore formation is essential for normal conventional aqueous humor outflow and hence intraocular pressure homeostasis, yet the role of microtubule (MT) stability in this process remains poorly understood. Here, using SC cell primary cultures from normal and glaucomatous human eyes as well as mouse whole eye perfusion, we identify MTs as a key component of the mechanotransduction machinery linking the mechanical microenvironment to SC cell biomechanics and conventional outflow. We show that MT stability is modulated by substrate stiffness and diminished in glaucomatous SC cells. MT stabilization suppresses GEF-H1-dependent actomyosin contractility, reduces cellular stiffness, and promotes transcellular pore formation in both normal and glaucomatous SC cells, whereas MT destabilization elicits opposing effects. Consistent with these cellular responses, pharmacological MT stabilization enhances conventional outflow facility in ex vivo mouse eyes. Together, our findings establish MT-dependent cytoskeletal remodeling as a previously unrecognized mechanism linking extracellular mechanical cues to SC biomechanics and transcellular pore formation and highlight MT-associated signaling as a potential therapeutic target for improving conventional outflow in glaucoma.

title: Diagnostic Challenge of Multivessel Takayasu Arteritis-A Case Report.
authorString: Parvin K, Ziad NM, Khan AT, Nijhum W, Florin AT, Hussen MD, Zeehad MMR.
abstractText: Progressive limb claudication, pulse deficits, marked inter-arm blood pressure differences, and elevated inflammatory markers should prompt evaluation for Takayasu arteritis. Early vascular ultrasound followed by CTA or MRA enables timely diagnosis and treatment in settings with delayed access to specialist services, reducing the risk of irreversible vascular complications.

title: Identification of Neuroinflammation-Related Diagnostic Biomarkers in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis: An Integrated Bioinformatics and Machine Learning Approach.
authorString: Jia Y, Li M, Ga D, Qian X.
abstractText:
Background

Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a liver disease that progresses and may be connected to neuroinflammation, though the specific molecular mechanisms are not yet understood. The objective of this research was to explore candidate diagnostic biomarkers related to neuroinflammation-associated gene programs for MASH through integrated bioinformatics and machine learning, as a hypothesis-generating study.

Methods

Genes with differential expression (DEGs) were pinpointed from the GSE89632 dataset, which includes 39 MASH samples compared with 24 controls. Candidate genes were identified using weighted gene coexpression network analysis (WGCNA) and gene sets related to neuroinflammation. A diagnostic model was constructed using 81 machine learning algorithm combinations (filtered from an initial set of 113 by excluding models with fewer than 2 features) within the training set, and its performance was subsequently evaluated in GSE126848 (31 MASH vs. 26 controls) as an evaluation set. Because the evaluation set contributed to model selection, it does not represent a fully independent validation cohort. Regulatory network construction, drug prediction, and molecular docking were used for further analysis of key genes.

Results

A total of 90 disease-associated neuroinflammation-related candidate genes were identified. Five candidate key genes (IRS1, HBEGF, MYC, CD274, and HMOX1) were screened, and a diagnostic model was constructed. The model achieved an AUC of 0.978 in the training set and 0.823 in the evaluation set; however, because the evaluation set contributed to model selection in the original analysis, the 0.823 estimate should be interpreted with caution. These findings are exploratory and require experimental validation.

Conclusions

This exploratory study identified five neuroinflammation-related candidate genes that may serve as candidate biomarkers for MASH. These findings provide candidate molecular links and potential therapeutic hypotheses, but require experimental validation and should be regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than clinically actionable.

title: Community health workers’ experiences with a digital clinical decision support system for longitudinal hypertension and diabetes care in rural Lesotho: a mixed-methods study
authorString: Gerber F, Raeber F, Moruthoane M, Khaemba A, Bhandari N, Kunwar L, Sanchez-Samaniego G, Gupta R, Williams A, Tahirsylaj T, Mathulise M, Kabi T, Mokaeane M, Maphenchane M, Molulela M, Khomolishoele M, Sematle MP, Sao L, Tlahali M, Shankar U, Basler DB, Kindler K, Grimm P, Labhardt ND, Amstutz A.
abstractText:
Community health workers (CHWs) are increasingly delivering chronic care in resource-constrained settings but require support to manage complex longitudinal clinical workflows. In the Community-Based chronic Care Lesotho (ComBaCaL) project in rural Lesotho, CHWs provide longitudinal hypertension and diabetes care, supported by the ComBaCaL Community Health Toolkit (CHT) application. The application combines longitudinal participant management and task coordination with clinical decision support for screening, diagnosis, treatment initiation and adjustment, cardiovascular risk management, referral, and follow-up for hypertension and diabetes care. This model of care has demonstrated improved or maintained clinical outcomes compared to facility-based care only. We conducted a mixed-methods study among all 103 participating CHWs to evaluate their experiences with the application. All CHWs completed a 38-item questionnaire, and 22 participated in qualitative interviews or focus group discussions. Overall usability was high, with a mean System Usability Scale score of 75.6 (SD 13.0), and 98 (95%) CHWs were satisfied or very satisfied with the application. General application functions and diagnosis and treatment tasks were rated easy or very easy by 98% of participants. The most frequently reported benefits were task reminders (92%), structured clinical guidance (87%), overview of allocated participants (81%), and retention of participant information (81%). Main challenges were lengthy questionnaires, difficulties charging tablets, and limited internet connectivity. Qualitative findings showed that ease of use increased with experience, supported by training and supervision. Participants described how algorithmic guidance and task reminders supported care delivery, while also identifying tensions between standardized workflows and flexibility in day-to-day care. The ComBaCaL CHT application was highly usable and valued by CHWs. High perceived usability extended from general application functions to complex clinical workflows. CHT demonstrated suitability as a configurable framework for implementing such context-specific workflows for hypertension and diabetes care when accompanied by appropriate workflow design, training, and supervision.

Author summary

High blood pressure and diabetes require repeated follow-up and treatment decisions, which is difficult where healthcare professionals are scarce. Community health workers (CHWs) may help expand access to this care, but they need appropriate tools to manage complex clinical tasks. We evaluated a digital application designed to support CHWs in delivering hypertension and diabetes care in rural Lesotho. Overall, 103 CHWs used an application built with the Community Health Toolkit to support hypertension and diabetes care. The application helped manage participants and follow-up tasks and provided step-by-step guidance for screening, diagnosis, treatment, referral, and repeated care visits. All 103 CHWs completed a survey, and 22 participated in interviews or focus group discussions. CHWs found the application easy to use and useful for their work. Frequently reported benefits included reminders, procedural guidance, better participant oversight, and retention of participant information over time. Ease of use improved with experience and was supported by training and supervision. Challenges included lengthy research questionnaires, difficulties charging tablets, limited internet connectivity, and standardized digital workflows that did not fit day-to-day circumstances. Our findings show that a configurable open-source digital application can support CHWs in delivering complex, longitudinal hypertension and diabetes care in a remote rural setting.

title: Conduction System Pacing in Pediatric Patients: Outcomes From a Multicenter International Cohort.
authorString: Cano Ó, Turubayev Y, Žižek D, Ponnusamy SS, Imnadze G, Huybrechts W, Vijayaraman P, Molina-Lerma M, de Wilde H, Nuralinov O, Ruiz E, de Pooter J.
abstractText:
Background

Conduction system pacing (CSP) may be advantageous in children requiring lifelong ventricular pacing, but long-term durability data are limited.

Objectives

The goal of this study was to evaluate the long-term preservation, durability, and safety of CSP in pediatric patients.

Methods

This international, multicenter, retrospective study included consecutive patients aged ≤18 years undergoing His bundle pacing or left bundle branch area pacing at 9 experienced centers. The primary endpoint was long-term preservation of CSP.

Results

Among 120 patients (mean age 12.6 ± 3.7 years), 68 (56.7%) had congenital atrioventricular block, 41 (34.2%) had congenital heart disease, and 12 (10.0%) underwent CSP for heart failure/cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). Acute CSP implantation, defined as achievement of His bundle pacing, left bundle branch pacing, or left ventricular septal pacing, was successful in 116 patients (96.7%). After a median follow-up of 24 months (Q1-Q3: 10-54 months), electrical lead performance remained stable. Among 101 patients with CSP at implantation and follow-up capture assessment, CSP was preserved in 95 (94.1%). Kaplan-Meier-estimated freedom from loss of CSP was 100.0% at 1 year and 98.2% (95% CI: 94.7%-100.0%) at 2 and 3 years. CSP lead-related complications occurred in 10 patients (8.3%), and reintervention was required in 9 (7.5%). In the CRT subgroup, left ventricular ejection fraction improved from 28.8% ± 9.4% to 46.8% ± 12.0% (P < 0.001).

Conclusions

CSP is a feasible, safe, and durable physiological pacing strategy in children, with excellent long-term CSP preservation and stable electrical performance despite ongoing somatic growth. CSP may also provide effective physiological resynchronization in pediatric patients requiring CRT.

title: Ibrutinib-Induced Effusive Constrictive Pericarditis and Acute Atrial Fibrillation.
authorString: Kumi DD, Coombes K, Bastidas Granizo LC, Sarangi S, Barzallo M, Baumann R, Mungee S, Mortoti SS, Bhardwaj C.
abstractText:
Background

Ibrutinib-associated pericardial disease is uncommon, and inflammatory effusive-constrictive pericarditis is rarely reported.

Case summary

A 66-year-old man with recurrent chronic lymphocytic leukemia receiving ibrutinib presented with dyspnea and palpitations. Echocardiography showed a fibrinous circumferential pericardial effusion with constrictive physiology. Simultaneous right and left heart catheterization confirmed ventricular interdependence, and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated diffuse pericardial late gadolinium enhancement consistent with active inflammation. He developed atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. Ibrutinib was discontinued, and anti-inflammatory therapy, rate control, and anticoagulation were initiated. Follow-up imaging showed complete resolution of the effusion and constrictive physiology.

Discussion

Multimodality imaging established the diagnosis and guided conservative management. Complete recovery after ibrutinib withdrawal and anti-inflammatory therapy supports a drug-related inflammatory mechanism and suggests that selected patients may avoid pericardiectomy.

Take-home messages

Ibrutinib may rarely cause inflammatory effusive-constrictive pericarditis with atrial fibrillation. Multimodality imaging and multidisciplinary cardio-oncology care are critical for diagnosis and individualized management. Early recognition and medical therapy may reverse constrictive physiology and avoid pericardiectomy.

title: Very Late Complete Heart Block After Cardiac Transplantation Presenting as Acute Decompensated Heart Failure.
authorString: Tao J, Yong J, Gu P, Zeng L, Yan J, Yao J, Wang Z, Yang Y.
abstractText:
Background

Complete atrioventricular (AV) block is an uncommon late complication after heart transplantation; in the denervated allograft, which depends on rate for output, it may present as heart failure rather than syncope.

Case summary

A 61-year-old man developed complete AV block 22 years after biatrial transplantation, presenting with acute decompensated heart failure and preserved ejection fraction. Serial electrocardiograms over 5 years documented stepwise progression to complete AV block. After conventional septal fixation repeatedly failed, left bundle branch area pacing was delivered via the atrial port with a right ventricular backup lead on the ventricular port; symptoms and function improved at 6 months.

Discussion

Very late allograft conduction disease is rarely documented longitudinally and is easily misattributed to rejection; physiological conduction system pacing was feasible despite failed conventional fixation.

Take-home message

Consider conduction disease in long-term transplant recipients presenting with heart failure, and use serial electrocardiographic surveillance to detect its gradual evolution.

title: Transcatheter Mitral Paravalvular Leak Closure With a Multifunctional Ventricular Septal Defect Occluder.
authorString: Anwar S, Sadiq N, Jain H, Malik T, Brohi F, Kumar A, Shakil R, Khalid AA, Kumar A, Sattar Y.
abstractText:
Background

Paravalvular leak (PVL) after surgical mitral valve replacement is an uncommon but clinically significant complication. Redo surgery carries a high risk, making transcatheter closure a viable and less invasive alternative.

Case summary

We report 2 cases of mitral PVL following prior surgical valve replacement who presented with signs and symptoms of heart failure. After echocardiographic evaluation, a transcatheter approach was undertaken to deploy a Konar-multifunctional (MF) ventricular septal defect (VSD) occluder under fluoroscopic guidance. Following the procedure, both patients showed significant clinical improvement with complete resolution of PVL.

Discussion

This case series emphasizes the feasibility and favorable outcome of transcatheter closure using the Konar-MF VSD occluder, off-label as an alternative to redo surgery in high-risk surgical patients with mitral PVL. Larger studies are warranted to evaluate the safety and efficacy of this off-label approach across a broader patient population.

Take-home messages

New-onset symptoms of heart failure and hemolytic anemia even after years of surgical mitral valve replacement warrant careful and timely evaluation for PVLs. In select high-risk patients who are not ideal candidates for redo surgery, off-label use of the Konar-MF VSD occluder is a feasible alternative for closure of PVLs.

title: Biomarker Testing, Imaging, and Outcomes in Cardiology-Referred Acute Breathlessness: A Retrospective Clinical Audit.
authorString: Mathews J, Riaz RK, Kazi A, Rahman S.
abstractText: Background Breathlessness is a leading cause of emergency hospital attendances, and its multifactorial nature often reflects overlapping cardiopulmonary pathologies such as pulmonary embolism (PE), heart failure (HF), and acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) is frequently used, often without documented pretest probability assessments. This audit primarily assessed the diagnostic yield of CTPA for suspected PE against the Royal College of Radiologists (RCR) standard of ≥15% and secondarily described biomarker testing, imaging, and outcomes across the PE, HF, and ACS pathways in patients referred to cardiology with acute breathlessness. Methods We conducted a retrospective audit of 70 adults referred to cardiology with breathlessness through the electronic patient record or multiprofessional team list (MPTL) referral systems at a district general hospital in the United Kingdom between March 1 and June 30, 2025. Biomarker testing for D-dimer, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and high-sensitivity troponin I (hs-TnI), together with imaging and outcomes, was reviewed and described across the PE, HF, and ACS pathways, with diagnostic yields restricted to CTPA for suspected PE and coronary angiography for suspected ACS. Yields were reported with Wilson 95% CIs and compared using exploratory Fisher's exact tests. Additional analyses examined biomarker concentrations by outcome and overlap in biomarker and imaging use. Results Seventy patients were included (median age, 69.5 years; 52.9% male). D-dimer, NT-proBNP, and hs-TnI were tested in 68.6%, 58.6%, and 81.4% of patients, respectively. Overall, seven of 54 CTPAs performed for suspected PE were positive (13.0%, 95% CI, 6.4-24.4), numerically below the RCR benchmark of ≥15%. A clinically relevant alternative diagnosis was reported in 44.4% (target, ≥50%), and pretest probability was documented in 22.2% (target, 100%). PE yield was 15.0% (6/40) among patients with an elevated D-dimer, 0% (0/4) among those with a normal D-dimer, and 10.0% (1/10) among those without D-dimer testing (p = 1.000 for both comparisons). Left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVSD) was found on transthoracic echocardiography in 40.0% (8/20) of patients with elevated NT-proBNP, 23.1% (3/13) of those with non-elevated NT-proBNP, and 26.3% (5/19) of those without testing (p = 0.456 and p = 0.501, respectively). Of 47 patients with elevated hs-TnI, 10 (21.3%) underwent coronary angiography for suspected ACS, with percutaneous coronary intervention performed in four (40.0%). Overall, 29 of 57 patients tested (50.9%) had hs-TnI levels above the sex-specific 99th-percentile upper reference limit. Conclusions Cardiology-referred breathlessness frequently involved multiple biomarker and imaging pathways during the same admission. CTPA yield, alternative diagnosis rates, and pretest probability documentation fell below RCR standards. LVSD was more frequent with elevated NT-proBNP, although differences were not statistically significant. No hs-TnI comparison was possible because all patients undergoing angiography for suspected ACS had elevated levels. Given the small, single-center sample and selective imaging, these findings do not establish diagnostic accuracy or pathway effectiveness. Larger multicenter studies are needed. The findings support reviewing pretest probability documentation and investigation decisions, followed by reaudit against RCR standards.

title: Transcriptomic Identification of Candidate Biomarkers Associated With Vascular Calcification-Related Signaling Pathways in Immunoglobulin A Nephropathy.
authorString: Cheng L, Xin Z, Zhao X, Wang J.
abstractText:
Background

Immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) is one of the most prevalent primary glomerular diseases globally. This study is aimed at identifying candidate biomarkers associated with vascular calcification-related signaling pathways in IgAN and at investigating their potential biological associations.

Methods

This was an observational bioinformatics study based on public transcriptomic datasets. Vascular calcification-related genes (VCRGs) were defined based on selected KEGG signaling pathways. Data were obtained from public databases. Candidate biomarkers were identified via differential analysis, machine learning, and cross-compartment external expression assessment. Enrichment analysis, immune infiltration, regulatory networks, computational drug prediction, and computational N6-methyladenosine (m6A) site prediction were used to explore the potential biological context of the candidate biomarkers.

Results

Differential analysis identified 348 differentially expressed genes (DEGs). By intersecting these DEGs with VCRGs, 30 candidate genes were obtained. JUN, FOS, and COL1A2 were finally identified as candidate biomarkers, and these genes were mainly associated with the "Nagashima EGF signaling" and "Nagashima NRG1 signaling." Six differential immune cell types (e.g., M2 macrophages) differed significantly between the IgAN and control groups. Spearman analysis showed that COL1A2 was negatively correlated with resting natural killer (NK) cells (cor = -0.57, p < 0.05); and FOS was positively correlated with resting NK cells (cor = 0.72, p < 0.01). BRD4, MAZ, and CTCF were computationally predicted as shared candidate transcription factors (TFs). A regulatory association involving hsa-miR-139-5p and FOS was also predicted. Troglitazone was predicted to target JUN. High-confidence m6A modification sites were computationally predicted in all three candidate biomarkers. These findings were considered exploratory and hypothesis generating.

Conclusion

JUN, FOS, and COL1A2 were identified as IgAN-associated candidate biomarkers linked to vascular calcification-related signaling pathway genes, providing exploratory biological insights into the potential molecular links between IgAN and calcification-related signaling.

title: Targeted Protein Degradation: From Molecular Mechanisms to Emerging Therapeutic Strategies.
authorString: Guo H, Duan H, Liu Y, Fang K, Xiao L, Bai L, Qu X, Yan X, Zhang K.
abstractText: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) redirects endogenous protein clearance pathways to eliminate disease-associated proteins, offering an alternative to conventional occupancy-based inhibition. Advances in TPD have expanded the range of degradable targets from intracellular proteins to cell-surface and extracellular proteins, although these modalities differ in their mechanisms and delivery requirements. Translating these differences into rational degrader design and effective therapeutic strategies remains challenging. This review compares proteasome-dependent degradation, endocytosis-mediated lysosomal degradation, macroautophagy, and chaperone-mediated autophagy, together with representative degrader classes and target scope. We discuss molecular factors influencing degradation efficacy, including target accessibility, selection of degradation machinery, productive complex formation, degradation kinetics, and target resynthesis. We then examine strategies for improving degrader delivery and spatiotemporal control, including local administration, molecular conjugation, conditional activation, and nanotechnology. Particular attention is given to the roles of nanomaterials in improving degrader delivery, controlling drug release, and constructing functional nanoscale degradation systems. Finally, we summarize preclinical evidence and clinical advances in oncology and nononcology indications and discuss limitations and future directions for therapeutic translation. By integrating degradation mechanisms, molecular design, delivery strategies, and pharmacological considerations, this review provides a framework for selecting TPD approaches according to target biology and disease context.

title: A Phase-Based Patient-Safety Approach to Intraoperative Transesophageal Echocardiography in Adult Cardiac Surgery
authorString: Abbay A, Shindauletova A, Lesbekov T.
abstractText: Patient safety remains a major challenge in cardiac surgery, where cardiopulmonary bypass carries risks of residual structural lesions, hemodynamic instability, embolic events, and unrecognized technical complications. This review examines intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography as a patient-safety intervention across the pre-bypass, bypass, and post-bypass phases of adult cardiac surgery, drawing on observational studies, registry analyses, and professional society guidance. Before cardiopulmonary bypass, transesophageal echocardiography establishes baseline ventricular and valvular function, identifies previously unrecognized pathology, and may guide cannulation and operative planning. During bypass, it supports ventricular decompression, myocardial protection, cannula assessment, and the detection and clearance of intracardiac air. After bypass, it evaluates the adequacy of surgical repair and identifies residual valvular lesions, ventricular dysfunction, ischemia, intracardiac air, and aortic complications while immediate corrective intervention remains possible. Although associated changes in surgical or anesthetic management are consistently reported, their frequency varies according to procedure type, patient risk, institutional practice, and study design. Furthermore, management change is a process outcome and does not, by itself, establish improvement in patient-centered outcomes. Serious complications related to transesophageal echocardiography are uncommon, but safe use requires appropriate patient selection, contraindication screening, careful probe manipulation, standardized examination and communication, and operator competence. A phase-based approach may help surgical teams connect imaging findings with time-sensitive hazards and corrective actions. Further prospective evidence is needed to identify the procedures and patient-risk profiles in which routine rather than selective intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography provides clinically meaningful benefit.

title: Network Pharmacology, Machine Learning, and Molecular Docking Analysis of Changluo Tiaogan Dinghun Decoction for Coronary Heart Disease with Anxiety.
authorString: Ning B, Wang K, Lv C, Kou L, Zheng Z, Jia W, Jia L, Luo C, Zhang Z, Lei Y, Ge T, Yang L, Zhao M, Wang Y.
abstractText: Coronary heart disease (CHD) and anxiety disorder frequently coexist, highlighting the need to investigate their potentially shared molecular mechanisms. Conventional therapeutic approaches have limitations, while traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) offers a potential multitarget strategy. Changluo Tiaogan Dinghun decoction (CLTGDHD) was developed for qi stagnation and blood stasis. This computational study integrated network pharmacology, machine learning, and molecular docking to investigate the potential compounds and molecular targets of CLTGDHD relevant to CHD with anxiety disorder. Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets GSE100927 and GSE61672 were analyzed separately to identify disease-associated genes. GSE100927 comprises peripheral-artery atherosclerosis samples and was used as a surrogate for atherosclerosis-related processes relevant to CHD, whereas GSE61672 represents an anxiety disorder cohort. The resulting candidate genes were evaluated using a machine-learning prioritization workflow, which identified protein tyrosine phosphatase receptor type C (PTPRC) as the sole retained gene. Molecular docking using the AlphaFold-predicted PTPRC structure (AF-P08575-4-F1) yielded predicted binding affinities ranging from -5.985 to -6.827 kcal/mol for five selected compounds. These findings suggest potential molecular interactions relevant to the investigated disease processes but do not establish therapeutic efficacy or a CHD-specific mechanism. Because the transcriptomic datasets represent separate populations rather than a clinically defined cohort with both CHD and anxiety disorder, the findings remain exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Further validation using appropriately defined clinical datasets and experimental models is required.

title: Claudin-1 as a potential marker of stress-induced premature senescence in vascular smooth muscle cells.
authorString: Gadecka A, Janiszewska D, Dudkowska M, Koblowska M, Buko T, Iwanicka-Nowicka R, Kossowska H, Bojakowski K, Mosieniak G, Bielak-Zmijewska A.
abstractText: Cellular senescence, a permanent state of cell cycle arrest, can result either from external stress and is then called stress-induced premature senescence (SIPS), or from the exhaustion of cell division potential giving rise to replicative senescence (RS). Despite numerous biomarkers, distinguishing SIPS from RS remains challenging. We propose claudin-1 (CLDN1) as a potential cell-specific marker of SIPS in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). In our study, VSMCs subjected to RS or SIPS exhibited higher levels of CLDN1 mRNA when compared with control cells. ChIP-seq results demonstrated a more open chromatin state, as evidenced by a broader H3K4me3 peak in the gene promoter region, in both SIPS and RS. However, only in SIPS did the broad H3K4me3 peak and increased mRNA level translate into higher protein level, which implies a different regulatory mechanism in RS. Moreover, nuclear accumulation of this protein was also characteristic solely for prematurely senescent cells. Elevated CLDN1 levels were also observed in VSMCs isolated from atherosclerotic plaques, although this was highly donor-dependent. These findings indicate that increased CLDN1 levels in prematurely senescent cells could serve as a promising cell-specific marker of SIPS in VSMCs, both in vitro and ex vivo. We discussed the potential mechanisms that could lead to claudin-1 upregulation and cause the difference observed between SIPS and RS. Identifying new markers specific to different senescence types might be helpful in recognizing conditions that promote accelerated aging and thus the development and progression of age-related diseases.

title: PRKAG2 Cardiac Syndrome: A Comprehensive Review of Clinical Manifestations, Pathophysiological Mechanisms, and Precision Medicine Frontiers.
authorString: Nogueira YAC, Martins MB, de Abreu Oliveira AL, Façanha AR, Sternick EB, Dias GM.
abstractText: PRKAG2 cardiac syndrome (PCS) is a metabolic storage cardiomyopathy caused by pathogenic variants in the PRKAG2 gene encoding the γ2-subunit of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK). It is defined by left ventricular hypertrophy, ventricular preexcitation and progressive conduction system disease accompanied by early-onset atrial arrhythmias. This review systematically evaluates PCS, outlining its clinical manifestations, genotype-phenotype spectrum, and diagnostic clues that distinguish it from sarcomeric hypertrophy. It explores underlying pathophysiological mechanisms, detailing how chronic AMPK activation drives glycogen accumulation via allosteric G6P activation of glycogen synthase, following a biphasic temporal model from early GLUT4-mediated glucose flooding to late metabolic feedback suppression. It further examines how Akt-mTOR hyperactivation fosters hypertrophy and how activated fasciculoventricular pathways mediate preexcitation. Finally, it reviews current supportive clinical management and highlights emerging precision medicine frontiers-including RNA-based silencing, pharmacological pathway inhibitors, and CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing-that aim to shift PCS care toward targeted disease modification.

title: Association of the new atherogenic index non-high-sensitivity C-reactive protein/HDL with significant coronary artery disease in patients with suspected coronary artery disease.
authorString: Vallejo-Garcia V, Fabregat-Ándres Ó, Sargues FJF, Valtueña-Gimeno N, Cejalvo-Lapeña D, Gumbau GV, Tormos JM.
abstractText:
Introduction

Atherosclerosis is the main cause of coronary heart disease (CHD). Atherogenic indexes (AI) are used to stratify cardiovascular risk. The aim of this study is to evaluate the association with significant CHD of a novel AI that includes parameters of both inflammatory residual risk and lipidic residual risk.

Methods

203 patients with suspicion of coronary heart disease were included. The new AI was established as the ratio between CRP (mg/dL) multiplied by 100, and HDL-C (mg/dL). It was compared with traditional AI Castelli I and II, and atherogenic index of plasma (AIP).

Results

The mean age was 53.9±7.34 years. 114 patients (55.9%) had significant CHD. The ratio PCRx100/HDL had the highest values of sensibility and specifity and was the only predictor of CHD with OR 1.59 (CI 95% 1.2-2.1, p = 0.001) and multivessel disease with OR of 1.45 (CI 95% 1.2 - 1.7, p < 0.001).

Conclusions

The new ratio PCRx100/HDL shows the best association with significant CHD.

title: Beyond edge-to-edge repair for the percutaneous treatment of mitral valve disease.
authorString: Pensotti F, Amat-Santos IJ.
abstractText: Mitral regurgitation (MR) is one of the most prevalent valvular heart diseases worldwide. Mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) has become the cornerstone percutaneous treatment for both primary and secondary MR; however, its efficacy remains highly anatomy-dependent, with a substantial proportion of patients deemed unsuitable and others experiencing residual or recurrent MR at follow-up. Looking beyond M-TEER, a growing armamentarium of alternative transcatheter strategies has emerged, including transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) platforms direct and indirect annuloplasty systems, and, more recently, percutaneous chordal replacement/leaflet-based technologies. This review discusses the current evidence supporting TMVR, transcatheter annuloplasty, and emerging leaflet-based strategies, focusing on those technologies most likely to redefine the treatment algorithm for mitral regurgitation over the coming years.

title: Multicentre study of activity quantification methods for 99m-Tc-pyrophosphate SPECT/CT in cardiac amyloidosis.
authorString: Torres LA, Ljungberg M, Brink A, Paez D, Peix A, Jimenez-Heffernan A, Mut F, Dorbala S, Knoll P.

journal.title: Physica medica : PM : an international journal devoted to the applications of physics to medicine and biology : official journal of the Italian Association of Biomedical Physics (AIFB)

abstractText:
Objective

99mTc-PYP SPECT/CT imaging is used for diagnosis of transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CA). The calculation of quantitative metrics allows assessment of the myocardial amyloid burden and supports therapy response evaluations. This study explores the implementation of reliable metrics and the validation of activity quantification methods in a multicentre study.

Methods

As part of the IAEA Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy (iTAC) project, a multicentre phantom study was conducted at 10 institutions using 12 hybrid SPECT/CT systems. Standardized acquisitions consistent with clinical protocols were used to compute the activity calibration factors (ACF). Absolute activity verifications were based on cardiac insert measurements with known activity distributions. Multiple reconstruction/quantification approaches (RecMethod) were evaluated, including the institution method (SiteProc) and four alternative ones; results of the computed activity were compared with the true activity meter measurements. Accuracy was assessed using RecMethod-to-True activity ratios, summarized by median, interquartile range (IQR) and coefficient of variation (CV).

Results

Most institution ACF values (ACFSiteProc) ranged 75-105 cps/MBq and were consistent with reference CoreLab estimates. Agreement between ACFSiteProc and reference CoreLab values showed a median ratio of 99.6 %, IQR 5.8 %, and CV 9.4 %, indicating no systematic bias. For activity quantification, median RecMethod-to-True ratios were 100.1 % for the SiteProc reconstructions and 97.8 %, 94.1 %, 95.6 % and 96.0 % for the alternatives.

Conclusion

The evaluated quantification methods demonstrated good median accuracy across institutions providing reliable activity estimates, essential for a robust implementation of quantitative metrics for ATTR-CA. The obtained inter-site variability indicates that precision remains a challenge at the multicentre quantitative imaging studies.

title: Polysomnography harmonization schemes: A multi-institutional sleep research resource.
authorString: Han Y, Ryu G, Kim Y, Shin H.
abstractText: Sleep disorders are associated with cardiovascular diseases and cognitive decline worldwide, highlighting the need for effective therapeutic strategies. Polysomnography (PSG) is the gold standard diagnostic tool for sleep disorders. However, long examination times, high costs, specialized biosignal equipment and controlled settings requirements hinder large-scale data collection. As artificial intelligence applications in sleep research expand, structural heterogeneity in PSG data across institutions complicates multi-center integration, increases preprocessing burden, and limits reproducible large-scale algorithm validation. We investigated biosignals, sleep parameters, and demographic features from eight publicly available PSG datasets. A set of schemas for PSG harmonization is proposed to formalize unified structural specifications aligned with established clinical guidelines. These schemas systematically integrate heterogeneous biosignals, derived sleep parameters, and demographic features to achieve consistent attribute selection and uniform preprocessing across datasets. When applied to construct an integrated dataset, the schemas demonstrated stable demographic and clinical distributions through repeated sampling. By addressing schema-level interoperability, the proposed framework facilitates consistent algorithm evaluation and comparison and provides a structured reference for reproducible, large-scale sleep research.

title: Harpagide alleviates neuroinflammation and cognitive dysfunction in sepsis-associated encephalopathy: Association with the MMP9/NF-κB signaling pathway.
authorString: Lou F, Deng G, Chen J, Jing Y, Wang A, Zhang M, Zhang Y, Wang B.
abstractText:
Background

Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is a severe neurological complication of sepsis, characterized by uncontrolled neuroinflammation and cognitive decline, yet no specific therapy is currently available. Harpagide, a naturally occurring iridoid glycoside, has been reported to possess anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective activities; however, its therapeutic potential in SAE remains unexplored. This study aimed to investigate whether Harpagide exerts neuroprotective effects in SAE and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms.

Methods

A mouse model of SAE was established by intraperitoneal injection of lipopolysaccharide (LPS, 18 mg/kg). Cognitive performance was assessed using behavioral assays. Brain tissue morphology and neuronal survival were evaluated through histopathological examination. Glial cell activation and the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6) were measured. Network pharmacology was employed to predict potential targets, followed by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to predict binding interactions with core targets. Western blotting was performed to determine the expression levels of key proteins involved in the MMP9/NF-κB signaling pathway.

Results

Treatment with Harpagide significantly improved behavioral performance, ameliorated brain pathological changes, preserved hippocampal neurons, suppressed glial activation, and reduced the levels of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 in SAE mice. Network pharmacology analysis predicted four core targets: GAPDH, CASP3, MMP9, and ICAM1. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations suggested stable binding between Harpagide and MMP9. Western blot analysis further showed that Harpagide treatment was associated with reduced expression of MMP9 and phosphorylated NF-κB p65 in both hippocampal and cortical tissues.

Conclusions

The present study demonstrates that Harpagide exerts neuroprotective effects in SAE, which are associated with mitigated neuroinflammation and reduced MMP9/NF-κB signaling, supporting its potential as a promising therapeutic candidate for this devastating condition.

title: Lean MAFLD as an independent risk factor for carotid plaque: The value of FIB-4 index in subgroup analysis.
authorString: Chao G, Lin A, Mai T.
abstractText:
Objective

This study aimed to investigate the associations between different subtypes of Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) and carotid plaque, and to evaluate the independent association of the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index with carotid plaque risk.

Methods

Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess associations of MAFLD subtypes and the FIB-4 index with carotid plaque.
