Two covariate‑selection strategies were adopted: confounders for MAFLD‑subtype analyses were chosen based on clinical considerations, while subgroup‑analysis confounders were screened using a univariable p < 0.10 threshold. Separate adjusted models were constructed disentangle the independent association of the composite FIB-4 score from its individual components.

Results

A total of 15,544 participants were included. After multivariable adjustment, lean MAFLD demonstrated an independent association with carotid plaque (OR=1.444), and its point estimate was numerically higher than those for diabetes-related MAFLD (OR = 1.354) and overweight/obesity-related MAFLD (OR = 1.172), although the confidence intervals overlapped. The FIB-4 index demonstrated a significant association with carotid plaque across all MAFLD subtypes (all p < 0.05) in models excluding its individual constituent components (OR range: 1.401-2.227).

Conclusion

Lean MAFLD is independently associated with carotid plaque. The FIB-4 index, a readily accessible noninvasive marker, shows consistent associations with carotid plaque across all MAFLD subtypes.

title: Atherosclerotic plaque healing: mechanisms and clinical relevance.
authorString: Buonpane A, De Caterina AR, Porto I, Crea F, Vergallo R.
abstractText: Atherosclerotic plaque healing is a dynamic biological mechanism that occurrs after plaque disruption and represents an endogenous reparative response within the atherosclerotic lesion. This process unfolds through three partially overlapping phases: endogenous thrombus lysis, granulation tissue formation, and re-endothelialization. Through the coordinated interaction of circulating cells, vascular wall components, and soluble mediators, plaque healing promotes fibrous repair and structural stabilization of the disrupted plaque. For many years, plaque healing remained primarily a histopathological observation described in post-mortem studies. The advent of high-resolution intracoronary imaging, particularly optical coherence tomography, has enabled in vivo visualization of the characteristic layered morphology of healed plaques, providing direct clinical confirmation of these early pathological findings. These observations have significantly improved our understanding of the clinical significance of plaque healing. Healed plaques are more frequently observed in patients with chronic coronary syndromes, supporting the concept that healing contributes to plaque stabilization. At the same time, recurrent cycles of plaque disruption followed by repair may lead to progressive luminal narrowing, thereby contributing to the long-term progression of coronary atherosclerosis. This review provided an updated overview of the clinical significance and implications of healed plaques in coronary artery disease, the mechanisms underlying plaque healing, and examines emerging intracoronary and non-invasive imaging modalities that allow their in vivo identification.

title: Impact of Air Quality Index on Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease Risk in South Asians: A Narrative Review.
authorString: Siddiqui F, Irfan M, Fayyaz M, Waqar A, Fatmi Z, Das JK, Al-Kindi SG, Deo S, Baumgartner J, Virani SS, Khoja A.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

This review examines whether worsening air quality, as represented by the Air Quality Index (AQI), and its constituent pollutant exposures, is associated with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk in South Asia. South Asian populations have a genetic predisposition to cardiovascular disease and several modifiable risk factors; however, research examining the interaction between air quality and these factors remains understudied.

Recent findings

Large population-based health studies consistently demonstrate a positive correlation between elevated levels of air pollutants, including PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, NO₂, CO, O₃, and NO, and ASCVD risk. Poor air quality may compound traditional ASCVD risk factors. Policy and pollution-reduction efforts may help, but evidence for South Asia-specific interventions remains limited. This review synthesizes evidence from population studies to establish air quality as a potentially modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease and stresses the need for improved surveillance and targeted risk-mitigation strategies to address the ASCVD burden in South Asia.

title: Serum Perfluorooctanoic Acid and Elevated Atherosclerosis Index: NHANES Associations and Exploratory Ceramide-Related Analyses.
authorString: Hong Q, He Y, Feng Y, Wang C, Lin D, Huang S.
abstractText: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) exposure has been associated with lipid abnormalities, but its potential links to ceramide-related processes in atherosclerosis remain incompletely characterized. This study examined the association between serum PFOA and atherosclerosis-related lipid status and explored candidate molecular links. Survey-weighted cross-sectional analyses of National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data evaluated the atherosclerosis index (AI) as the primary outcome. AI was analyzed continuously and as elevated AI, defined as AI ≥ 4. Complementary analyses integrated network toxicology, machine learning, and bulk and single-cell transcriptomics. When serum PFOA was modeled continuously, higher concentrations were associated with elevated AI, and this association persisted after adjustment for confounders. After further adjustment for survey cycle, the association with elevated AI remained, whereas the association with continuous AI was attenuated. Integrative analyses prioritized candidate genes involved in lipid regulation and inflammatory signaling, with APOE showing prominent expression in macrophages and foam cells. Cell-cell communication analysis identified stronger inferred macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) signaling from APOE-low macrophages to foam cells. An independent PFOA-exposure dataset further showed APOE upregulation in macrophages. Together, these findings suggest that higher serum PFOA concentrations are associated with an adverse atherogenic lipid profile, as reflected by greater odds of elevated AI. They also highlight ceramide-related molecular candidates and APOE-associated communication patterns for further mechanistic investigation.

title: Incident generalized anxiety and common mental disorders in rheumatoid arthritis: a 12-year case-cohort analysis from ELSA-Brasil.
authorString: Estrada PF, Cavalcante MRN, de Souza Santos I, Brunoni AR, Meneghini V, Tebar WR, Lotufo PA, de Carvalho Goulart A, Bensenor IJM.
abstractText: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with mental health disorders, but longitudinal evidence remains limited. To examine the association of RA with depressive episode, generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), and common mental disorders (CMD) in the Brazilian Longitudinal Study of Adult Health (ELSA-Brasil). This case-cohort analysis included 1,795 participants: 252 in the RA case group and 1,543 in a randomly selected reference sample. For each incident outcome, participants with the condition at baseline or without follow-up information were excluded. Outcomes were assessed over 12 years of follow-up. Logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), adjusted for sociodemographic and clinical covariates. At baseline, depressive episode was present in 19 (7.5%) participants in the RA group and 60 (3.9%) in the reference sample, GAD in 45 (18.1%) and 186 (12.2%), and CMD in 92 (36.5%) and 411 (26.6%), respectively. Fully adjusted ORs for the association of RA with depressive episode, GAD, and CMD were 1.52 (95% CI 0.85-2.74), 1.30 (0.89-1.90), and 1.41 (1.04-1.90), respectively. During follow-up, depressive episode occurred in 24 (14.4%) participants in the RA group and 94 (9.4%) in the reference sample, GAD in 37 (25.2%) and 120 (13.3%), and CMD in 43 (36.4%) and 164 (20.9%), respectively. Corresponding fully adjusted ORs were 1.41 (0.84-2.36), 2.04 (1.30-3.18), and 2.06 (1.33-3.18), respectively. RA was associated with baseline CMD and incident GAD and CMD, but not with baseline depressive episode, baseline GAD, or incident depressive episode after adjustment.

title: Inherited cardiovascular risk and its impact on healthspan and lifespan.
authorString: Li L, Schunkert L, Schunkert H.
abstractText: Genetic disposition for cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a major determinant of aging-related traits, such as healthspan, dementia, and frailty. While rare monogenic disorders provide important mechanistic insights, most CVDs and aging-related traits are driven by the cumulative effects of numerous common genetic variants, resulting in a polygenic risk architecture. Analyses of genes and pathways affected by these variants revealed significant correlations in the genetic architectures of CVD and aging, which appear to promote each other bidirectionally. Thus, CVD and aging share common genetic mechanisms, linking inherited cardiovascular risk to frailty, dementia, reduced healthspan, and shortened lifespan-and, conversely, explaining why aging is the strongest risk factor for atherosclerosis. Advances in genome-wide association studies have also enabled the construction of a polygenic risk score (PRS), which quantifies inherited CVD risk and facilitates early risk stratification beyond conventional clinical assessment. Importantly, individuals at high polygenic risk for CVD derive greater benefit from preventive strategies, which reduce their lifelong burden of CVD risk and ultimately promote healthy aging. Therefore, personalizing clinical risk assessment by integrating genetic testing for both CVD and aging-related traits may be of clinical importance. Specifically, lifestyle modification and preventive therapies based not only on conventional risk assessment, but also on polygenic risks may offer an individualized life-course approach for precision prevention, shifting cardiovascular care from reactive disease management toward the promotion of healthy aging.

title: Gene-metabolite-cardiac associations in the Chronic Kidney Disease in Children (CKiD) study.
authorString: Lee AM, Mitsnefes MM, Wong CS, Roem J, March ME, Hakonarson H, Xiao R, Flynn JT, Furth SL, Warady BA, Vasan RS, Kimmel PL, Surapaneni A, Rhee EP, Schlosser P, Grams ME, Denburg MR, CKiD Study Investigators.
abstractText:
Background

Characterizing gene-metabolite-cardiac associations in childhood chronic kidney disease (CKD) has the potential to identify new research directions or therapeutic targets for mitigating the excessive cardiovascular risk in childhood CKD.

Methods

The Chronic Kidney Disease in Children (CKiD) is a prospective cohort that recruited children with eGFR 30-90 ml/min/1.73 m2 across 54 North American centers. Predictor and outcome variables included genotypes, metabolite levels, left ventricular mass index (LVMI) z-score, and left ventricular filling pressure (E/e'). Multivariable linear regression analyses assessed metabolite associations with either LVMI z-score or E/e', adjusting for age, sex, CKD duration, glomerular etiology, renin-angiotensin-aldosterone-system blockade, hypertension, anemia, dyslipidemia, eGFR, and proteinuria. Significance was based on the Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate <0.05. Metabolites associated with cardiac markers were carried forward for a metabolite-genome-wide association study (mGWAS). Linear regression calculated the residual metabolite variability not explained by age, sex, and eGFR. Linear regression assessed metabolite residual variability versus genetic variant dosage at the Bonferroni-corrected genome-wide significance threshold (corrected for number of metabolites assessed).

Results

556 unique participants with 574 metabolites and ~8.4 million SNPs were included. Sphingomyelin (d18:2/d18:1) and hypotaurine were associated with LVMI z-score. Isobutyrylglycine and 3beta-hydroxy-5-cholestenoate were associated with E/e'. Multiple genetic variants associated with these metabolites at p < 1.25E-8 (p < [5E-8]/4, Bonferroni-corrected genome-wide significance threshold).

Conclusions

We identified metabolites associated with cardiac markers in children with CKD. We identified genetic associations with variability in these metabolites. Collectively, these gene-metabolite associations suggest roles for inflammation, increased oxidative stress, mitochondrial and energy dysmetabolism, and gut microbial dysbiosis in mediating cardiac pathology in childhood CKD. A higher resolution version of the Graphical abstract is available as Supplementary information.

title: Novel Metabolomic Signature as a Biomarker to Detect Subclinical Atherosclerosis in Individuals Traditionally Classified as Low Risk.
authorString: Xue Y, Vescovi J, Chan AS, Vernon ST, Tang O, Zhu D, Bate KA, Brieger D, Gray MP, Quek LE, O'Sullivan JF, Grieve SM, Patrick E, Yang JYH, Figtree GA.
abstractText:
Background

Standard modifiable risk factors such as age, hypertension, diabetes, cholesterol, and smoking contribute to coronary artery disease risk. However, up to 27% of first-time heart attacks occur in individuals without standard modifiable cardiovascular risk factors. As medical management can stabilize coronary atherosclerosis, there is a need for biomarkers to identify disease before symptoms or a heart attack.

Methods

We performed targeted metabolomics, identifying 54 metabolites in 1212 adults undergoing coronary artery calcium score (CACS) from the BioHEART-CT Study. Individuals were classified as having clinically actionable CACS positive or not (clinically actionable CACS negative). Metabolite-to-metabolite ratios were then calculated to identify transferable biomarkers. Logistic regression models incorporating age, sex, and metabolite ratios were developed and classified as low risk by traditional scoring. The BioHEART Metabolite Risk Score (BioHEART-MRS) was derived from the best-performing model, trained in a Discovery cohort (n=635), adapted using transfer component analysis (n=266), and validated in an independent External cohort (n=311).

Result

A model including age, sex, and 5 metabolite ratios: histidine-kynurenic acid, histidine-riboflavin, citrullin-proline, kynurenic acid-phosphocholine, and arginine-dimethylguanidino valerate, referred to as BioHEART-MRS, demonstrated the best performance in younger individuals for predicting CACS. In the External cohort, BioHEART-MRS outperformed the traditional risk score (area under the curve=0.67 versus 0.55). The traditional risk score underperformed in the under-60 cohort, misclassifying 62% of those with clinically actionable CACS as low risk. Within this group, BioHEART-MRS identified 46 additional cases among low-risk individuals (n=495). As a triage tool, BioHEART-MRS reduced the number needed to scan to detect one true positive case to 7, compared with scanning all low-risk individuals.

Conclusions

In the External validation cohort, BioHEART-MRS showed greater discrimination than Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis risk score among traditionally low-risk individuals and enriched for clinically actionable CACS positive among those selected for imaging. These findings support prospective evaluation of metabolite-based triage for CACS, particularly in younger and SMuRFless individuals.

title: Symptomatic Vertebral Artery Loop Formations: A Scoping Review of Epidemiology, Pathogenesis, and Treatment.
authorString: Tiangco DAL, Sih IMY.
abstractText:
Background and objectives

Vertebral artery loop formations (VALFs) are under-reported yet treatable causes of cervical radiculopathy. Incidence varies between 2% and 7.5%. Exact pathogenesis is unclear. Literature is sparse, and optimal treatment remains controversial. This review aims to collect all available literature describing symptomatic VALFs.

Methods

We performed a scoping review in PubMed, Ovid Medline, Cochrane Library, British Medical Journal, and Google Scholar. Full-text original, descriptive, and analytical studies were collated. Data from retrieved articles were collaboratively reviewed, tabulated, and synthesized. Clinical features, diagnosis, and treatment outcomes were discussed.

Results

A total of 31 articles and 33 patients found to have symptomatic VALFs were included. The mean age of patients was 52 years, 17 (53%) of whom were females. Tortuosity was more apparent on the left, with C4-C5 and C5-C6 (28%) being the most common levels affected. Neck (13%) and shoulder pain (26%) were the most common left- and right-sided presenting symptoms. In the 31 treated patients, 71% (n = 22) underwent surgery, whereas the remaining 29% (n = 9) were treated conservatively. There was complete resolution of symptoms in 54% of patients who underwent surgery and in 75% of patients who were treated conservatively.

Conclusion

Vertebral artery loops are understudied yet clinically significant causes of radiculopathy. Believed to arise from various etiologies, it can be tricky to diagnose and manage, necessitating a high index of suspicion and prompt clinical recognition. When conservative management fails, a patient-tailored surgical approach may provide the most direct decompression with the least associated surgical risks.

title: Manual Brachial Artery Compression as an Adjunct for Intraoperative Hemostasis During Carpal Tunnel Release.
authorString: Yazaki S, Sato M, Uchida M, Takasuna H, Matsumori T, Kushiro Y, Hidaka G, Tanaka T, Fukuyama R, Tenjin K, Murata H.
abstractText:
Background and objectives

Carpal tunnel release (CTR) is typically a straightforward procedure, and major bleeding is uncommon. However, minor oozing may occasionally interfere with visualization during critical steps. We describe a simple adjunctive maneuver using manual brachial artery compression for temporary control of arterial inflow during CTR.

Methods

This retrospective study describes a consecutive series of 55 patients who underwent CTR under local anesthesia with epinephrine. Manual compression of the brachial artery was applied intermittently to modulate arterial inflow during critical surgical steps. Operative findings and postoperative complications were evaluated. Intraoperative discomfort was retrospectively assessed from nursing records. In a subset of 26 cases with operative video recordings, compression duration and intraoperative bleeding control were evaluated using video review and a 5-point Likert scale by 2 surgical team members.

Results

Manual brachial artery compression was applied without interrupting the surgical workflow and provided temporary control of arterial inflow during critical surgical steps. Among the 26 video-analyzed cases, the median total compression time was 23 minutes (range, 13-38 minutes) and the median maximum continuous compression interval was 13 minutes (range, 8-23 minutes). No evaluations were rated ≤3 on the 5-point Likert scale by either evaluator. No documented intraoperative discomfort, distal ischemia, vascular injury, postoperative hematoma, or other complications were identified.

Conclusion

Manual brachial artery compression is a simple and reproducible adjunctive maneuver that may be useful for temporary control of bleeding during CTR when additional intraoperative hemostatic control is desired.

title: Normative Measures of Colon Length in Children With Inflammatory Bowel Disease, Aged 11-17 Years, Based on MRI.
authorString: Jonker CAL, Gorter RR, Benninga MA, Koppen IJN, de Jonge CS, de Jong JR, van Schuppen J.
abstractText: To better understand (abnormal) colonic anatomy on imaging, data on normal colonic anatomy in the unaffected population are crucial. We assessed colon lengths in children without constipation on MRI. This retrospective study included patients (< 18 years), who underwent MRI-enterography between 2016 and 2020 for suspected inflammatory bowel disease, and did not meet Rome-IV criteria for functional constipation. Patients with colonic inflammation were excluded. Primary outcome was the mean total colon length/BSA (cm/m<sup>2</sup>) (95% CI; ±2SD), and the secondary outcomes were total colon length (cm), rectosigmoid length/BSA (cm/m<sup>2</sup>), and rectosigmoid length (cm). Colon segments were independently measured on coronal T2-weighted MRI using 3D multiple-point measurements. Linear regression was used to evaluate associations between total colon length and sex, age, height, weight, body surface area (BSA). Eighty-one patients (median age 15 years; range 11-17; 53% male) were included. The mean total colon length/BSA was 72.9 ± 21.0 cm/m<sup>2</sup>. Mean total colon length was 115.8 ± 13.8 cm, mean rectosigmoid length/BSA was 24.2 ± 12.3 cm/m<sup>2</sup>, and mean rectosigmoid length was 38.2 ± 7.9 cm. Additionally, we assessed colonic segments per age group. Colon length significantly correlated with age (p = 0.03), height (p < 0.001), weight (p < 0.001), and BSA (p < 0.001). In a multivariable linear regression analysis, BSA was significantly correlated with total colon length (95% CI 21.4-49.4; p < 0.0001). This study provides data on colon and rectosigmoid lengths in children, aged 11-17 years, without constipation measured on MRI-enterography. This knowledge can be used for the identification of abnormal colonic anatomy in children with therapy-resistant constipation on imaging.

title: Links between chronic health conditions and sexual dysfunction in men: insights from a German population-based study.
authorString: Kronthaler SM, Oesterling CF, Tissen-Diabaté T, Beier KM, Schlomm T, Neymeyer J, Hatzler L.
abstractText:
Background

Sexual dysfunction (SD) is common among men and significantly impacts quality of life. Chronic health conditions (CHC), particularly with comorbid mental health (MH) issues, may be associated with increased risk of SD, yet large-scale population data are limited.

Objective

This study examined the prevalence and associations of sexual problems (SP), ICD-11-defined SD, and sexual distress among men with and without CHC in a representative German sample.

Methods

From a cross-sectional online survey, data from N = 1742 cisgender men (unweighted sample size) were included in the analysis. Participants reported on CHC status (i.e., cardiovascular, urological, mental health, cancer), SP, SD, and sexual distress (SDS-DAO). Regression models assessed associations between CHC and SD. Network analyses explored interrelations between CHC subgroups and SD domains.

Results

CHC were reported by 50.8% of participants. Men with CHC had higher rates of SP (79.2%) and SD (23.2%) than those without CHC (66.7% SP, OR 1.90, 95% CI 1.52-2.37; 9.1% SD, OR 3.00, 95% CI 2.24-4.07). SD was most prevalent in men with urological disorders, cancer, pain-related, mental health and cardiovascular conditions. Among men with CHC, comorbid MH conditions were substantially associated with sexual distress (β = 3.4, 95% CI 1.3-5.4, p = .001). Regression models demonstrated strong associations between CHC, comorbid MH conditions, and SD, with network analysis revealing strong links between erectile dysfunction with hypoactive sexual desire dysfunction and delayed ejaculation dysfunction, and conditions such as urological disorders, mental health conditions, cancer and cardiovascular disease.

Conclusion

CHC, especially mental health conditions, urological disorders, cancer and cardiovascualr disease, are strongly associated with SD and sexual distress in men. Integrated care approaches that include routine sexual health screening and address mental wellbeing may thus be essential to improving outcomes for men with chronic illness.

title: The Para-ISS Dural Space Enhancement Sign: A Novel MRI Finding Independently Associated With Intracranial Atherosclerotic Burden
authorString: Zeng S, Lin D, Tang K, Zeng F, Zheng X, Li M, Lin J, Huang B, Zhan S, Chen S, Dai Z.
abstractText:
Background

No dural enhancement sign centered on the inferior sagittal sinus (ISS) has been characterized. We observed a frequent, previously undescribed finding—para-ISS dural space enhancement (PISE)—at the free inferior margin of the falx cerebri.

Objective

To define PISE, determine its detection rate in a large cross-sectional cohort, and characterize its correlates, in particular whether the pattern of association is compatible with an atherosclerosis-related dural mechanism.

Methods

Consecutive contrast-enhanced intracranial vessel-wall MRI (VWI) examinations (May 2015–December 2025) were reviewed; 835 of 875 examinations were evaluable, corresponding to 811 patients. The first outcome-evaluable examination for each patient was used for all primary analyses. PISE was defined as dural enhancement strictly at the falx free margin adjacent to the ISS, exceeding the ISS vascular lumen. Forty-seven demographic, clinical-history, and imaging variables were tested univariately with Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction; multivariable logistic regression with patient-grouped 5-fold cross-validation was triangulated with LASSO and random forest. Dose–response across plaque grades was assessed with the Cochran–Armitage trend test, and circulation-specific associations were compared in models adjusted for age and sex (inter-reader Cohen’s κ=0.93).

Results

PISE was detected in 609/811 patients (75.1%); detection rose from 50.0% (<40 years) to 81.7% (>70 years; trend p=5.6×10⁻⁶). The strongest univariate correlate was vulnerable intracranial plaque (OR=8.29, 95%CI 5.54–12.40). Detection increased across plaque grades 0/1/2 (38.7%→77.2%→90.3%; Z=11.09). Anterior-circulation plaque showed a stronger association than posterior-circulation plaque (OR=4.42 vs 2.76). Vulnerable plaque (OR=2.37), plaque grade (OR=2.84 per grade), age (OR=1.38 per SD), and inpatient status (OR=3.18) remained independently associated (patient-grouped cross-validated AUC=0.755). Moyamoya disease was inversely associated (OR=0.25). Findings were consistent across imputation and all-examination sensitivity analyses.

Conclusions

PISE is a frequently detected novel dural enhancement sign whose independent, graded, anatomically concordant association with intracranial atherosclerotic burden supports an atherosclerosis-related dural mechanism and warrants prospective validation.

title: Meningioma Resection in a Patient with High-Risk Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Preoperative Mavacamten Optimization and Multidisciplinary Management
authorString: Chen C, Song Y, Cao S, Sun D, Wang L, Zhou S.
abstractText: Background The clinical presentation of meningioma combined with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HOCM) is extremely rare, and perioperative management is exceptionally challenging. High-risk HOCM without optimization is generally regarded as an absolute contraindication for craniotomy, and there is a profound lack of established experience regarding its successful management. Case presentation: A 50-year-old man presented with headache and dizziness. Magnetic resonance imaging showed a large anterior skull base meningioma abutting the internal carotid and anterior cerebral arteries. Preoperative cardiac evaluation diagnosed obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with a resting left ventricular outflow tract gradient of 133 mm Hg and a right ventricular ejection fraction of 28%. After multidisciplinary team discussion, mavacamten was started. The gradient fell to 79 mm Hg after 5 days. The tumor was then completely resected under goal-directed hemodynamic management. The perioperative course was uneventful. Postoperative brain swelling resolved with conservative treatment. At 1-month follow-up, the patient had recovered well without cardiac or surgical complications. Conclusions Unoptimized obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is an absolute contraindication to craniotomy. However, selected patients whose hemodynamics are stabilized by medical therapy can undergo surgery safely within a multidisciplinary framework. Maintaining preload, avoiding tachycardia, and preserving afterload are essential for perioperative safety.

title: A Single Smart Nanomaterial for Near-Infrared-Switchable Theranostics of Hemorrhage and Thrombosis via Photoacoustic Imaging.
authorString: Ye Y, Sun Z, Wu D, Lai J, Yang M, Luo Z, Cheng S, Yang S, Zeng H, Li Y, Kuang F, Sun B, Zhang W, Tang X, Luo H, Wu G.
abstractText: The clinical management of hemorrhagic patients remains a significant challenge, as current therapeutic approaches lack real-time diagnostic capability and spatiotemporal precision. Conventional materials (e.g., hydrogels) require surgical intervention, while molecular targeting strategies are limited by slow kinetics and uncontrollable thrombotic risks. To address these limitations, we developed a smart nanomaterial based on a NiFe-layered double hydroxide decorated with both Ag single atoms and nanoparticles (Ag<sub>SA + NP</sub>/NiFe-LDH). This platform can bind plasminogen activators, achieving rapid hemostasis with approximately 30% reduced fibrinolysis in vitro and approximately 50% reduced blood loss in vivo in models of intracranial and abdominal hemorrhage. Under pulsed near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, the dominant photoelectric effect enhances hemostatic efficacy, reducing blood loss by about 50% compared to the unexposed part; under sustained NIR exposure, strong photothermal effects inactivate clot-enriched thrombin and alter fibrin structure, thereby promoting controlled thrombolysis. This dual functionality is consistently demonstrated in arterial models and in cryopreserved human blood samples from healthy individuals and hemorrhagic patients. Moreover, the material enables real-time visualization of active bleeding (as low as 3 μL) via photoacoustic imaging, as validated in an intracranial hemorrhage model. Our work demonstrates a proof-of-concept NIR-based strategy for externally modulated management with potential applications in dynamic vascular emergencies.

title: Passive Sealing Stent-Grafts for Chimney Endovascular Repair: <i>In Vitro</i> Examination and a Japanese Single-Centre Retrospective Study.
authorString: Kaneko K, Ohki T, Ito E, Ozawa H, Omori M, Murakami Y.

journal.title: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists

abstractText:
Purpose

Juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms (JAAAs) present with a short infrarenal neck that does not permit standard endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). The AFX VELA cuff extension with its endoskeletal architecture may reduce type Ia endoleak (TIaEL) through passive sealing. We examined this hypothesis using a double-chimney benchtop model and a clinical cohort treated with VELA-based chimney EVAR (ChEVAR).

Materials and methods

A benchtop model compared gutter leakage volumes among VELA, Endurant II and Excluder C3 (5 trials per device). A retrospective single-centre cohort (January 2018-April 2024) included consecutive JAAA patients undergoing VELA-based ChEVAR with ≥12-month follow-up. Postoperative computed tomographic (CT) morphometry compared seal-zone geometry across the 3 platforms.

Results

In the benchtop model, VELA showed a median gutter leakage of 5.0 mL/min (interquartile range [IQR], 4.0-11.0), whereas both comparators exceeded 500 mL/min and were right-censored. In the clinical cohort, 20 patients (55% male; median age 80.0 years) underwent ChEVAR for JAAAs with a median diameter of 53.5 mm and infrarenal neck length of 5.0 mm. Clinically successful sac exclusion was achieved in 19 of 20 patients (95%). Intraoperative TIaEL occurred in 5 patients: 1 major endoleak was sealed with adjunctive gutter coil embolisation, and 4 minor endoleaks resolved spontaneously on the 1-month CT angiogram. Over a median follow-up of 36.5 months, no persistent TIaEL was detected on follow-up imaging, and no chimney stent-graft (SG) occlusion occurred. One patient (5%) required an aortic-related reintervention for a type Ib endoleak. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decreased by ≥20% in 9 patients (45%), and 1 started dialysis at 4 years. On postoperative CT morphometry, relative gutter area was lowest with VELA, intermediate with Endurant II and highest with Excluder C3; circumferential apposition followed the inverse pattern.

Conclusion

In the benchtop model, VELA produced consistently lower leakage than both comparators, with concordant CT morphometric evidence consistent with a passive sealing mechanism. In this cohort, VELA-based ChEVAR achieved clinically successful sac exclusion in 19 of 20 patients (95%) with no persistent TIaEL and no chimney SG occlusion. These findings support the feasibility of VELA-based ChEVAR when FEVAR is unavailable; multicentre prospective validation is required.

Clinical impact

Persistent type Ia endoleak (TIaEL) is a principal limitation of chimney EVAR (ChEVAR) compared with fenestrated EVAR (FEVAR). We report short-to mid-term outcomes of ChEVAR using the AFX VELA cuff extension, whose endoskeletal architecture is designed to promote passive sealing. Postoperative CT morphometry comparing the 3 devices (VELA, Endurant II and Excluder C3) showed a smaller relative gutter area and higher circumferential apposition with VELA, paralleling the benchtop pattern. VELA-based ChEVAR achieved clinically successful sac exclusion in 19 of 20 patients (95%), without persistent TIaEL detected on follow-up imaging. VELA-based ChEVAR appears feasible when FEVAR is unavailable; however, multicentre validation is required.

title: Pharmacogenomics guided clopidogrel utilization in veterans undergoing peripheral arterial intervention with vascular surgery compared to usual care.
authorString: Bridge L, Kujath S, Weatherall T, Keller J, Neu D, Marler J.
abstractText: After revascularization, patients with peripheral arterial disease (PAD) are at risk for ischemia. CYP2C19 variants may impact outcomes in those receiving clopidogrel but data is limited in PAD. This pilot study evaluated pharmacogenomic (PGx) guided care in 146 adult patients who underwent revascularization and were prescribed P2Y12 inhibitors. PGx testing was compared to no testing, with 61 patients in the PGx group vs 85 in control (clopidogrel only group). Clopidogrel was used in 97% of patients at baseline. Use of aspirin (64.7% vs 85.2%; p < 0.01) as well as stent interventions (44.7% vs 80%; p < 0.01) were less frequent in the control group, but P2Y12 inhibitor therapy duration was longer (10.2 ± 3.4 vs 8.0 ± 4.0 months; p < 0.04). Roughly one-third of patients were switched from clopidogrel based on PGx. Overall, in the control group, the composite of major adverse limb and cardiovascular events (45.9% vs 32.8%; p = 0.11), as well as bleeding events (14.1% vs 9.8%; p = 0.43) were non-significantly higher. At 7-12 months after revascularization, ischemic events were significantly lower in the PGx group (21.3% vs 4.7%; p = 0.01). A majority of ischemic events in the PGx group occurred within 90 days, and timely PGx testing was found to be delayed.

title: Variations in Access to Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Versus Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement by Socioeconomic Factors: A Retrospective Population-Level Study in New South Wales, Australia.
authorString: Shawon MSR, Ryan JB, Jorm L.
abstractText:
Background

Despite increasing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) activity in Australia in recent years, patient access to TAVI remains limited and is often more complex than access to surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR). The aim of this study was to identify socioeconomic factors associated with the likelihood of receiving TAVI versus SAVR in New South Wales (NSW), Australia.

Methods

Data from the NSW Admitted Patient Data Collection were used to compare the clinical and socioeconomic profiles of patients aged ≥65 years who underwent either TAVI or SAVR between 1 November 2017 and 28 February 2022. Multiple logistic regression analyses were performed on the overall patient cohort and on subgroups defined by age groups, hospital type and funding type.

Results

The study included 6,493 patients (mean age: 79.1 years, 35.5% female) who underwent aortic valve replacement (SAVR=3,294; TAVI=3,199). The odds of receiving TAVI versus SAVR increased significantly with age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] for patients aged 85 years and older versus those aged 75-84 years: 12.3, 95% CI: 9.99-15.2). Patients from the most disadvantaged socioeconomic areas had lower odds of receiving TAVI than those from the least disadvantaged areas (aOR:0.58, 95% CI: 0.47-0.73). Patients with private health insurance/Department of Veterans Affairs (PHI/DVA) funding were more likely to receive TAVI than SAVR (aOR: 3.29, 95% CI: 2.61-4.14), with this finding consistent across age groups and even more pronounced in patients treated in public hospitals (aOR: 5.82, 95% CI: 4.40-7.70).

Conclusions

Our study highlights significant variations in TAVI access based on age, socioeconomic status of area of residence, and funding type. These findings underscore the need for policy settings that promote equitable access and ensure that procedural choices for aortic valve replacement reflect clinical needs.

title: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance findings in His-bundle pacing: Insights to pacing threshold rise.
authorString: Meier C, Soutodeh R, Deelawar S, Kazlauskaite M, Hoyer A, Stoye FV, Eisenblätter M, Israel C, Gielen S.

journal.title: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance

abstractText:
Background

The mechanisms underlying pacing threshold elevation in His bundle pacing (HBP) despite an electrically intact lead remain poorly understood. This can compromise long-term battery life and increase the need for generator replacement or lead revision, adding procedural risk for patients and costs for healthcare systems. Using multiparametric cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR), this proof-of-concept study examined whether the myocardium at the lead tip can be visualised with conventional CMR sequences, whether imaging remains safe despite elevated pacing thresholds, and whether fibrosis at the implantation site can be identified.

Methods

We prospectively enrolled 16 patients with HBP systems, of whom 9 had an increased pacing threshold. A significant increase was defined as a rise of ≥1.0V/1.0 ms. All scans were performed on a 1.5T scanner using standard bSSFP cine imaging and IR TFE late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging in atrial-focused short-axis, long-axis, and modified aortic valve (AV) views to optimally visualise the HBP insertion site. LGE was assessed visually in different views.

Results

All MRI images were evaluable and showed no visual artefacts. The tip of the HBP lead was best visible on short-axis and AV planes. No periprocedural safety issues occurred, in particular pacing thresholds remained unaffected, demonstrating that CMR is feasible even in patients with elevated pacing thresholds, a scenario often considered a relative contraindication. In the case-control comparison, the presence of LGE at the His lead implantation site was associated with increased pacing thresholds, although our small cohort showed no association with clinical markers. Given the limited sample size, these findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

Conclusions

This proof-of-concept study shows that the HBP lead implantation site can be visualized with conventional CMR sequences, and that MRI can be performed safely even in patients with elevated pacing thresholds. Pacing threshold rises were associated with LGE at the implant site, suggesting a mechanistic link and traction-related micro-injury. These findings highlight that local tissue remodeling should be considered when selecting and optimizing His-bundle implantation techniques.

title: Associations between Antidiabetic Drug Classes and Aortic Aneurysm Risk in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
authorString: Lu YW, Joni Shao YH, Hsu CY, Hsiao CY, Chen WT, Shih CC, Lip GYH, Huang PH.

journal.title: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery

abstractText:
Objective

Aortic aneurysm (AA) is a potentially life threatening condition that often remains asymptomatic for prolonged periods. Although type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) increases cardiovascular risk, epidemiological studies have paradoxically reported a lower incidence of AA in patients with T2DM. Antidiabetic therapies may contribute to this inverse association, but class specific effects remain unclear. This study evaluated associations between antidiabetic drug classes and incident AA.

Methods

This was a nationwide, population based, retrospective cohort study of adults with T2DM in Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database between 2009 and 2022. Associations between antidiabetic drug classes and incident AA were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models with time varying medication exposure, adjusted for demographic characteristics, diabetes severity, comorbidities, tobacco related diagnoses, and concomitant medications. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were considered exploratory.

Results

Among 3 295 564 adults with T2DM (mean age 60.0 years; 52.8% men) followed for 8.5 ± 4.7 years, 45.5% received at least three antidiabetic drug classes. In multivariable time varying Cox models, metformin (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.78, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.75 - 0.82), thiazolidinediones (aHR 0.71, 95% CI 0.65 - 0.77), sulfonylureas/meglitinides (aHR 0.82, 95% CI 0.78 - 0.85), and α-glucosidase inhibitors (aHR 0.83, 95% CI 0.77 - 0.89) were associated with lower AA risk. DPP-4 inhibitors (aHR 0.95, 95% CI 0.90 - 1.00), sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors (aHR 0.90, 95% CI 0.81 - 1.00), and glucagon like peptide 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) (aHR 0.69, 95% CI 0.50 - 0.95) also showed inverse associations, whereas insulin use was associated with higher AA risk (aHR 1.14, 95% CI 1.08 - 1.20). The inverse associations of conventional oral antidiabetic agents remained robust across sensitivity analyses. In contrast, the inverse associations for DPP-4 inhibitors, SGLT2 inhibitors, and GLP-1RAs were attenuated and no longer statistically significant in patients with an index date from 2011 onward.

Conclusion

In this nationwide T2DM cohort, conventional oral antidiabetic agents were consistently associated with a lower observed AA risk. Although newer glucose lowering therapies showed similar inverse associations, these findings were less robust and warrant cautious interpretation and prospective confirmation.

title: Modelling Medial Degenerative Features by Enzymatic Digestion to Evaluate Disease-Relevant Structure-Function Relationships in the Thoracic Aorta.
authorString: Eliathamby D, Ung L, Yap H, Elbatarny M, Ouzounian M, Bendeck M, Seidman MA, Simmons CA, Chung JC.
abstractText:
Background

To clarify aortic microstructure-function relationships, we used improved, disease-motivated enzymatic digestion models of medial degeneration to evaluate individual extracellular matrix (ECM) components (i.e., elastin, collagen, and proteoglycans) and their influence on biomechanical properties of ascending aortic tissue.

Methods

Thin, 200 µm medial porcine ascending aortic sections were progressively digested with elastase or collagenase for selective degradation of these ECM components. Full thickness human aortic tissues were treated with chondroitinase, hyaluronidase, and heparinase to completely remove proteoglycans. Low- and high-strain modulus, transition-zone behaviour, strain-energy density, and energy loss were derived from planar biaxial tensile testing. Degradation of elastin was captured with two photon excitation fluorescence imaging. Degradation of collagen was captured with picrosirius red staining and polarized light microscopy. Proteoglycan content and organization was confirmed by Alcian blue staining.

Results

Degradation of elastin fibers reduced low-strain modulus, strain-energy density, transition zone stress, and energy loss. Collagen degradation similarly reduced strain-energy density and decreased strain at the onset of transition, with reductions in high strain modulus and energy loss with increased degradation. Proteoglycan removal decreased energy loss and reduced strain-energy density and strain at onset of transition, and increased high strain modulus.

Conclusions

Through targeted modelling of ECM degenerative features, we have delineated the overlapping effects of major matrix constituents, underscoring the complex, multifactorial nature of structure-function relationships in aortic disease. We also identified multiple microstructural pathways to increasing energy loss and the vulnerability of aortic tissue to failure.

Statement of significance

Thoracic aortic dissection results from the progressive degeneration of the aortic wall extracellular matrix, yet the contributions of individual matrix constituents to this mechanical failure remain understudied. To address this gap, we developed a disease-motivated enzymatic model that enables controlled, graded modification of key extracellular matrix constituents in aortic tissue, better replicating the partial degeneration observed in vivo than existing approaches. Using this framework, we systematically evaluated the biomechanical consequences of elastin, collagen, and proteoglycan degeneration. Here, we revealed multiple microstructural pathways to altered viscoelastic behaviour, which is associated with increased susceptibility to aortic failure. These findings provide new mechanistic insight into structure-function relationships in aortic disease and help explain how matrix degeneration contributes to tissue vulnerability and dissection risk.

title: Vasodilatory and antihypertensive effects of sotagliflozin: Ex vivo evaluation in isolated rat aortic rings and an in vivo assessment in spontaneously hypertensive rats.
authorString: Ge D, Tew WY, Xu X, Loh HW, Zhang R, Xu W, Yam MF.
abstractText: Sotagliflozin, a dual SGLT1/2 inhibitor, is noted for its cardioprotective and antihypertensive effects, yet its direct vascular action remains unclear. This study investigated its ex vivo vasodilatory effects in isolated rat thoracic aorta and in vivo antihypertensive effects in non-diabetic Spontaneously Hypertensive rats (SHRs), with subchronic safety assessment. Aortic rings were pre-contracted with phenylephrine or potassium chloride, and underlying mechanisms were studied using pathway-specific inhibitors against matched vehicle controls. Blood pressure and heart rate were measured weekly over 28 days of oral treatment, and safety assessed through body weight, organ weight, biochemistry and hematology. Sotagliflozin induced a concentration-dependent, predominantly endothelium-dependent vasodilation. Cyclooxygenase-derived prostanoid signaling coupled to the AC/cAMP/PKA axis contributed most consistently. In contrast, attenuation by L-NAME and ODQ was surmounted at higher concentrations, indicating a supplementary role for the NO/sGC/cGMP pathway. Vasodilation persisted under KCl-induced depolarization and was unaffected by potassium channel blockers, arguing against a requirement for potassium channel-mediated hyperpolarization. Sotagliflozin also blunted vasoconstriction mediated by voltage-operated calcium channels and inositol triphosphate receptors. In vivo, 200 mg/kg significantly reduced systolic blood pressure relative to baseline and vehicle control, comparably to propranolol and without reflex tachycardia, whereas diastolic and mean arterial pressures were unaltered. Body and organ weights were unaffected, serum uric acid was lower at 50 and 100 mg/kg, urea was higher at the upper doses, and hematology was unremarkable. These findings indicate that sotagliflozin exerts direct vasodilatory activity in the rat thoracic aorta and lowers systolic blood pressure at supratherapeutic doses, warranting further investigation.

title: Pearls & Oy-sters: Trace Visualization of the Central Retinal Artery: A Favorable Sign for Late-Window Endovascular Therapy in Central Retinal Artery Occlusion.
authorString: Du Y, Qi Z, Cong L, Wang D, Liu W, Zhang S.
abstractText: In acute central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO), vessel stenosis and hemodynamic impairment significantly affect visual prognosis. We report a 69-year-old man who presented with 18 hours of acute, severe right eye blurred vision. Fundus examination and optical coherence tomography confirmed central retinal artery (CRA) occlusion with inner retinal edema. Digital subtraction angiography revealed an aortic arch variation and severe C1 segment stenosis of the right internal carotid artery (ICA), accompanied by delayed ophthalmic artery filling and faint visualization of the CRA. After multidisciplinary consultation, the patient underwent ICA stenting. Postoperative imaging showed resolved stenosis and improved retinal perfusion; the patient's vision subsequently improved and stabilized. This case suggests that revascularization can facilitate visual recovery even beyond the traditional window. Furthermore, faint CRA visualization on digital subtraction angiography indicates residual flow, providing a potential rationale for recanalization therapy.

title: Clinical Protocols and Guidelines for Hypertension and Diabetes in Incarcerated Populations: A Scoping Review.
authorString: Alves de Oliveira R, Oliveira Teles D, Gomes Ribeiro S, Amorim Lessa PR, Oliveira Nicolau AI, Freitas Nunes S, Nascimento da Silva K, Biazus Dalcin C, Bezerra Pinheiro AK.
abstractText:
Introduction

Incarcerated populations have a disproportionate burden of acute and chronic conditions, including hypertension and diabetes. We aimed to identify and describe clinical protocols and guidelines for managing hypertension and diabetes in the incarcerated population.

Methods

We conducted a scoping review in July 2025 of clinical protocols and guidelines that address the prevention, promotion, screening, diagnosis, and treatment of hypertension and diabetes in the incarcerated population. We searched electronic databases (Medline/PubMed, Embase, the Virtual Health Library, EBSCOhost, Scopus, Cochrane, and Web of Science), gray literature repositories, and websites of governmental and international organizations. We used the AGREE II instrument to assess document quality.

Results

Three documents met the inclusion criteria; they were published in 2021, 2022, and 2024 and originated from high-income countries. Methodological appraisal showed heterogeneity in guideline development, with consistently low scores in the domains of stakeholder involvement and rigor of development. Existing protocols encompass health education and self-management support, multidisciplinary care, universal screening at intake, evidence-based and individualized treatment, and intersectoral collaboration to ensure health care delivery in correctional settings.

Conclusion

The small number of clinical protocols addressing hypertension and diabetes management in the incarcerated population reflects a critical normative gap in correctional health systems. Strengthening the scientific rigor of these protocols and ensuring their implementation are essential to standardize care, reduce clinical variation, and promote health equity, both within correctional settings and in the transition back to the community.

title: Coronary angiography in heart transplants from donors older than 40: a Eurotransplant study.
authorString: Aliabadi-Zuckermann AZ, Kaider A, De Pauw M, Rega F, Milicic D, Gummert J, Berchtold-Herz M, Schulze PC, Warnecke G, Hartyansky I, Erasmus M, Caliskan K, Knezevic I, Smits J, Strelniece A, Laufer G, Zuckermann AO, ETHAC Committee, Eurotransplant.
abstractText:
Background and aims

The increasing age of heart donors in Europe raises concerns about undetected coronary artery disease (CAD), a contributor to early graft dysfunction and long-term complications. This study examined the association between donor coronary angiography (CA) and heart transplant utilization, particularly in donors aged >40 years.

Methods

A total of 20 681 donor heart offers reported to Eurotransplant between 2004 and 2020 were analysed. The use of CA, donor characteristics, and acceptance rates were assessed. CAD status was imputed for donors without angiography using logistic regression based on clinical risk factors. Transplantation probabilities were modelled using observed and imputed CAD severity to explore potential differences under a scenario of broader CA availability.

Results

CA was performed in 23.5% of cases, predominantly in older donors and those with cardiovascular risk factors. Among donors with CA, 37.5% had CAD, which was significantly associated with age, male sex, hypertension, and smoking. Donors with normal CA findings had lower odds of rejection compared with those without CA (odds ratio 0.36, P < .0001). In a counterfactual model, broader CA availability in donors aged >40 years was associated with a higher estimated transplant utilization (56.4%-67.1%), corresponding to a model-based increase of ∼535 transplants.

Conclusions

In this observational cohort, CA availability was associated with differences in donor heart utilization, particularly when findings were normal or showed non-significant CAD. These findings suggest that angiographic information may reduce diagnostic uncertainty and support clinical decision-making in older donors. A risk-adapted, resource-sensitive approach to CA use is warranted.

title: Dopaminergic neurons linking threat processing to cardiac modulation and locomotor responses.
authorString: Tsuji M, Jinkoma D, Uemura Y, Ogasawara A, Emoto K.
abstractText: Heartbeat and behavior are tightly coordinated during defensive states, yet the neuronal mechanisms linking threat processing to cardiac modulation-and the potential contribution of cardiac dynamics to behavioral output-remain poorly understood. Here, using simultaneous recordings of heartbeat and behavior in tethered Drosophila, we show that mechanical threat triggers locomotion together with rapid cardiac deceleration. We identify two pairs of dopaminergic neurons, termed DA-WED neurons, that mediate this cardiac response. Silencing these neurons markedly attenuates threat-induced cardiac deceleration, whereas optogenetic activation induces cardiac deceleration in the absence of threat. Two-photon calcium imaging further shows that DA-WED neurons are activated by mechanical threat, and manipulating their activity bidirectionally modulates threat-induced locomotion. Linking cardiac dynamics to behavior, direct optogenetic manipulation of cardiomyocytes that quantitatively reproduces threat-evoked cardiac deceleration is accompanied by increased locomotion. Together, these results identify a dopaminergic descending pathway that links threat processing to cardiac modulation and suggest that cardiac dynamics may contribute to shaping defensive behavior.

title: Descending aortic replacement after frozen elephant trunk: graft clamping and true-lumen anastomosis.
authorString: Shimano R, Nakahara Y, Iwakura T, Marui A.

journal.title: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS

abstractText: Second-stage descending aortic replacement after arch replacement with a frozen elephant trunk requires proximal control at a site that is often hostile to cross-clamping. The conventional elephant trunk technique was introduced to avoid cross-clamping the vulnerable proximal aorta; the previously implanted graft, left hanging in the descending aorta, is grasped and clamped directly, and the new graft is sutured to it. This video tutorial demonstrates the manoeuvre in the current era of the frozen, stented elephant trunk. In a patient with a frozen elephant trunk, computed tomography confirmed complete circumferential thrombosis of the false lumen around the stented graft. Through a left thoracotomy the distal aorta was clamped, and the completely thrombosed false lumen was opened without a proximal cross-clamp. The previously implanted stented graft was exposed and clamped directly, providing proximal control without dissecting or cross-clamping the densely adherent native aorta and without damaging the stent. The new graft was anastomosed proximally to the unstented distal cuff, and distally to the true lumen only, avoiding leak into the false lumen and limiting late aortic enlargement. The imaging that makes the approach safe, the step-by-step conduct, and the pitfall of identifying the graft within the walled-off true lumen are described.

title: Off-pump subtotal pericardiectomy using ultrasonic aspirator in constrictive pericarditis
authorString: Srivastava I, Yildiz M, Veit M, Reineke D, Siepe M, Schoenhoff F.

journal.title: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS

abstractText: A subtotal pericardiectomy was performed without the use of extracorporeal circulation due to the patient's advanced age and underlying liver cirrhosis. After exposure of the heart, both phrenic nerves were identified and carefully preserved. The pericardium was found to be massively calcified, with extensive involvement extending to the base of the aorta and the diaphragm. The pericardium was divided into multiple diamond-shaped sections, allowing controlled, stepwise resection and facilitating safe handling of the rigid, calcified tissue. Decortication was initiated at the right ventricle and proceeded gradually. The calcified pericardium was removed using a combination of an ultrasonic aspirator, a rongeur and electrocautery. Careful, controlled separation of the pericardium from the epicardium was performed throughout, addressing dense adhesions while preserving the underlying myocardium and epicardial vessels. The ultrasonic aspirator facilitated resection of the calcified tissue without harming the underlying structures. Resection was extended over the right atrium, right ventricle and anterior wall of the left ventricle up to the level of the phrenic nerves. Complete pericardiectomy was not achievable due to extensive adhesions and proximity to critical structures. Intraoperative echocardiographic imaging demonstrated immediate improvement in cardiac filling and function.

title: The H<sub>2</sub>S-releasing metformin hybrid Met-ITC protects against diabetes-associated vascular dysfunction preserving glycaemic control.
authorString: Spezzini J, Piragine E, Flori L, Citi V, Brogi S, Testai L, Barresi E, Taliani S, Da Settimo F, Calderone V, Martelli A.
abstractText:
Background and purpose

Patients undergoing metformin (Met) therapy for the treatment of type 2 diabetes remain at high cardiovascular risk. Hydrogen sulphide (H2S)-releasing molecules offer antioxidant, anti-senescence and vasoactive properties that may complement Met activity. This study investigated whether metformin-isothiocyanate (Met-ITC), a H2S-releasing metformin hybrid, preserves the antidiabetic activity of Met while providing H2S-derived vascular protection.

Experimental approach

The predicted Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism and Excretion (ADME) properties of Met and Met-ITC were evaluated in silico. Maintenance of Met antidiabetic properties was assessed in vitro by evaluating glucose uptake in HepG2 cells and in vivo through oral glucose tolerance tests in db/db mice. The ability of Met-ITC to release H2S and its ability to preserve cell viability and contrast ROS formation and cellular senescence were evaluated in human aortic endothelial cells (HAECs) and smooth muscle cells (HASMCs) exposed to hydrogen peroxide, homocysteine or high-glucose concentrations. The hyperpolarizing effect of Met-ITC was tested on HASMCs and its direct vasorelaxing effect as well as its ability to inhibit noradrenaline-induced vasoconstriction were tested on endothelium-intact or -denuded rat aortic rings.

Key results

Met-ITC showed a more favourable permeability profile than Met and maintained its antidiabetic profile. It provided better protection against oxidative stress, loss of cell viability and senescence compared with Met. Moreover, Met-ITC produced a concentration-dependent hyperpolarization of HASMCs, restricted noradrenaline-induced contraction and induced vasodilatation in endothelium-denuded and -intact rat aortic rings.

Conclusion and implications

These findings identify Met-ITC as a potential candidate for the treatment of diabetes-associated vascular dysfunction.

title: Molecular MRI Reveals Macrophage-Enriched Peritumoral Immune Remodeling After Incomplete Ablation in Liver Cancer.
authorString: He Y, Xu H, M M Rogasch J, Berndt N, Guo J, Schellenberger E, Häckel A, Heidemann L, Hesse F, Liu Y, Ramtke J, Beindorff N, Hofheinz F, Kader A, Mülleder M, Textoris-Taube K, Hamm B, Müller DN, Schmidt R, Hauptmann R, Traub H, Schannor M, Savic LJ.
abstractText: Incomplete image-guided ablation can promote local tumor progression by reshaping the residual tumor microenvironment toward immunosuppression, yet noninvasive biomarkers of this process remain limited. Here, a translational multiparametric PET/MRI strategy was developed to monitor macrophage-associated microenvironmental remodeling after incomplete microwave ablation (iMWA) in orthotopic VX2 liver tumors. Twenty-four tumor-bearing rabbits were assigned to untreated control, early post-iMWA (short-term), or late post-iMWA (long-term) groups and underwent clinical 3 T PET/MRI, including diffusion-weighted imaging, dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI, [<sup>1</sup> <sup>8</sup>F]FDG PET, and T2-weighted MRI before and after administration of Eu-VSOP. Eu-VSOP-enhanced MRI revealed a hypointense peritumoral rim after iMWA, with the largest rim-to-liver signal decrease and rim thickness observed in the long-term group. Prussian blue staining and LA-ICP-ToF-MS demonstrated preferential iron and europium enrichment in macrophage-rich, CD206-associated peritumoral regions. Histology and proteomics further demonstrated increased CD206 and MMP-9 expression, extracellular matrix remodeling, immunosuppressive myeloid-associated changes, and metabolic reprogramming in viable residual tumors, accompanied by altered [<sup>1</sup> <sup>8</sup>F]FDG uptake. Together, these findings indicate that incomplete ablation induces a temporally evolving, macrophage-rich immunosuppressive peritumoral niche and support the potential of Eu-VSOP-enhanced multiparametric PET/MRI for noninvasive monitoring of post-ablation microenvironmental remodeling.

title: Emergent Roles of RVLM<sup>C1</sup> Neurons in Cardiovascular Homeostasis and Systemic Physiological Regulation.
authorString: Souza GMPR, Faborode OS, Omoto ACM.
abstractText:
Purpose of the review

Adrenergic C1 neurons in the rostral ventrolateral medulla (RVLMC1) have long been recognized for their role in regulating sympathetic activity and arterial blood pressure (BP). However, novel approaches such as genetic targeting, optogenetics, fiber photometry, among others, allowed us to study the biology of these neurons in deeper detail and in non-anesthetized preparations, unraveling previously underappreciated or unrecognized functions. Here we will discuss recent studies that explored the function of RVLMC1 neurons for the sympathetic regulation of BP and also the emergent roles of these cells for other processes involved in systemic physiological regulation.

Recent findings

Using selective methods of manipulation and recording of neuronal activity in conscious animals, it was demonstrated that RVLMC1 neurons play a critical role in BP stability across multiple behaviors, including sleep-wake state and postural changes. Besides cardiovascular control, recent evidence shows that these neurons play a critical role in different homeostatic functions such as thermoregulation, immune response, glycemia and in complex behaviors such as anxiety. RVLMC1 neurons are a key hub that integrates interoceptive signals from peripheral systems to regulate BP and other basic physiological functions. Along with their role in cardiovascular regulation, these emergent roles of RVLMC1 neurons may also need to be considered when explaining the complex and multifactorial pathophysiology of cardiometabolic diseases associated with hypertension.

title: Could obinutuzumab be the new therapy for adults with primary membranous nephropathy?
authorString: Juanet C, Venda J, Yandian F, Caravaca-Fontán F, Fervenza FC.
abstractText:
Introduction

Membranous nephropathy (MN) is the most common cause of nephrotic syndrome in adults. Anti-CD20 therapy is first-line when immunosuppression is indicated. However, a non-negligible proportion of patients fails to respond to rituximab, through mechanisms that include urinary drug loss and escape of tissue-resident B cells or long-lived plasma cells. Obinutuzumab, a glycoengineered humanized type II anti-CD20 antibody producing deeper, more sustained B-cell depletion, is a candidate to overcome these limitations.

Areas covered

We review the treatment landscape and unmet needs in primary MN; the chemistry, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics and rationale of obinutuzumab; its clinical efficacy, including the MAJESTY trial; its safety profile; the competitive environment; and its regulatory status. PubMed was searched without date restrictions up to October 2026.

Expert opinion

Obinutuzumab is effective in primary MN, with the clearest indications being high anti-phospholipase A2 receptor (anti-PLA2R) titers, high-risk disease, severe rituximab hypersensitivity and rituximab-refractory disease. Key questions concern how best to use it: its pharmacokinetics in the nephrotic state are uncharacterized, and response-adapted dosing instead of the fixed four-dose regimen requires prospective validation. Persistent immunologic activity despite confirmed depletion argues for plasma cell-directed therapy. Standardized definitions of immunologic remission and resistance remain essential to generate better comparative evidence.

title: Ablation of Twin Atrioventricular Node-Mediated Macroreentrant Tachycardia in a Patient With Complex Heterotaxy Syndrome.
authorString: Robledo-Nolasco R, Hernández-Urquieta L, Andrade-Cuellar EN, Solís-Gómez JC, Muñoz-López VA, Martínez-Galindo M, González-Silva EF, Elorreaga-Camacho H, Ramírez-Martínez B, Oliver-Mayorga LC, Villatoro-Gúzman KI, Niño-Nájera AG, Santiago-González ML, Jaime-Ruíz NG.
abstractText: Twin atrioventricular (AV) nodes constitute a rare and highly complex electrophysiological substrate for tachycardia in heterotaxy syndrome (complex cardiac heart disease). We present the case of an 18-year-old male with right atrial isomerism, asplenia, univentricular physiology, and a Glenn shunt, who presented with a regular wide-QRS tachycardia associated with severe hemodynamic decompensation. High-density electroanatomical mapping identified two distinct His bundle recordings separated by 20.3 mm. Together with two non-preexcited QRS morphologies and different conduction properties, these findings supported suspected twin AV node-mediated macroreentry, with proposed anterograde conduction via the inferior-posterior system and retrograde conduction through the superior-anterior system; complete circuit mapping and entrainment were not possible. Following an initial procedure complicated by pulseless electrical activity clinically attributed to post-cardioversion myocardial stunning, a second electrophysiological study prioritized functional characterization during sinus rhythm and atrial pacing without preablation reinduction of the clinical tachycardia. Selective ablation of the superior-anterior His region preserved AV conduction and was followed by noninducibility of the clinical tachycardia. A separate isthmus-dependent flutter was also ablated. At two months, clinical assessment, ECG, and 24-hour Holter monitoring showed no documented recurrence or new AV block.

title: Relationship Of Facial Pattern and Smile Features in Patients with Dentofacial Deformities.
authorString: Fontan C, de Andrade Silva V, Siqueira R, Celestino J, Cimões R.

journal.title: The international journal of esthetic dentistry

abstractText:
Purpose

To evaluate the association between smile characteristics and facial patterns in patients with dentofacial deformities.

Methods

Records of patients with dentofacial deformities were retrospectively analyzed. Electronic health records and standardized photographs were assessed to classify gender (male or female), skeletal facial pattern (Pattern II, Pattern III, Long Face, Short Face, dolichocephalic, brachycephalic, and mesocephalic), and smile characteristics, including smile line, smile arc, smile design, upper lip curvature, lip-tooth relationship, and number of teeth displayed during smiling.

Results

Data from 187 individuals were included. Pattern III was the most prevalent skeletal pattern (48.1%), with a higher proportion of female patients (62.6%). Most Pattern II (94.9%) and Pattern III (82.2%) individuals were classified as mesocephalic. Smile line height showed a significant association with the vertical facial dimension, being higher in patients with vertical excess and lower in those with vertical deficiency. Smile arc and smile design demonstrated similar distributions among facial patterns presenting comparable occlusal plane inclinations. No statistically significant differences among smile characteristics were observed within the Short Face group.

Conclusion

Smile line height was associated with vertical skeletal discrepancies, whereas smile arc and smile design were more consistent among facial patterns with similar occlusal plane inclinations. These findings emphasize the role of facial morphology in smile characteristics and support the inclusion of smile analysis in orthodontic and orthognathic treatment planning.

title: Functional Assessment and Extended Culture of Human Pediatric Cardiac Tissue Slices for Preclinical Testing
authorString: Guerrelli D, McLean K, Freeman A, Pressman J, Bruce A, Desai M, d’Udekem Y, Posnack NG.
abstractText:
ABSTRACT

Background

Living human myocardial slices preserve native tissue architecture, but their application to pediatric cardiac physiology or prolonged functional testing remains limited. We adapted a passive culture method for small surgical myocardial specimens obtained from patients with congenital heart disease (CHD).

Methods

Atrial and ventricular specimens were obtained from 41 cardiac surgery patients (7.7±11.1 years; 1 day – 49 years). Myocardial tissue was sectioned into slices and studied acutely, or maintained under free-floating, rocking cell culture conditions without electrical or mechanical stimulation. Calcium transients were recorded in response to external pacing (0.2–2 Hz) at baseline, and after isoproterenol or norepinephrine exposure. Selected preparations underwent viability, histological, and gene-expression analyses.

Results

Pacing-evoked calcium transients were recorded from all four cardiac chambers, exhibiting expected frequency-dependent shortening. Mean interslice and intraslice coefficients of variation were 11.1% and 7.6%. Viability was 85.8 ± 5.6% post-slicing and 78.8 ± 5.0% after 3–5 hours. Calcium transients remained detectable through 178 days in atrial and 119 days in ventricular slices. Calcium transient durations were relatively stable during extended culture. Beta-adrenergic agonists shortened calcium transient durations (isoproterenol: 32% atrial, 25% ventricular at 0.3 Hz); responses to isoproterenol persisted to approximately 120 days in selected atrial slices and 60 days in ventricular slices. Selected histological features were preserved, although some extracellular-matrix and apoptosis-related transcripts changed.

Conclusions

Small surgical specimens support repeated physiological measurements and pharmacological testing during extended passive culture, providing a platform for human developmental and disease-specific cardiac research.

title: Normative Values for QRS Duration in Athletes aged 12-35 years undergoing Pre-participation Exams.
authorString: Montalvo S, Tso JV, Ferrari F, Ashley E, Wheeler M, Froelicher VF.
abstractText:
Background

Due to limited data on athletic QRS duration, this cross-sectional study aims to establish normative digital reference values in asymptomatic, apparently healthy athletes ages 12 to 35 undergoing pre-participation examinations.

Objectives

We hypothesized that QRS duration of athletes would be longer in males, increase with age, and rarely exceed 120 ms in the absence of a bundle branch block.

Methods

We analyzed QRS duration from standardized digital ECG recordings in 9,084 athletes (58% male, age 12-35 years, mean age 18) obtained during pre-participation examinations. Sex-stratified 99th-percentile quantile-regression equations were developed and applied in an APP to demonstrate that QRS duration outliers could be easily identified.

Results

Females had shorter QRS durations than males (88.5 +/- 8.3 ms vs. 97.3 +/- 9.1 ms; mean difference 8.9 ms, 95% CI: 8.5-9.2 ms). QRS duration demonstrated a positive cross-sectional association with age and was greater in men than women. Female 97.5th and 99th percentile QRS duration were 106.0 ms and 108.0 ms, respectively, with range 62-130 ms. Male 97.5th and 99th percentile QRS duration were 116.0 ms and 118.3 ms, respectively, with range 70-132 ms. 7(0.2%) females and 55 (1.0%) males had QRS duration >120 ms. 99th percentile quantile regression equations were derived (Female: QRS=99.6 + 0.56 x age; Male: QRS = 104.7 + 0.74 x age).

Conclusions

Our results indicate that defining prolonged QRS criteria necessitates adjustments according to age and sex. To facilitate future prospective research, we offer specific regression models to detect outliers.

title: Association of preoperative quantitative flow ratio with 1-year graft patency after coronary artery bypass grafting: A two-center retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Iwakura T, Nakayama M, Mizukami T, Takanashi S, Nakahara Y, Tanigaki T, Kawase Y, Matsuo H, Koyama Y, Sumi K, Yano A, Takeda K, Hagiya K, Okada Y, Marui A, Takamisawa I, Nanasato M, Shimokawa T, Isobe M.
abstractText:
Background

Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) targets are selected by angiographic stenosis, whereas percutaneous coronary intervention increasingly relies on functional assessment. Whether quantitative flow ratio (QFR), a wire-free angiography-derived index, relates to graft outcomes is unclear. We examined preoperative QFR and 1-year graft patency.

Methods

We retrospectively studied 491 patients undergoing isolated CABG at two heart centers, 2006-2019. Investigators blinded to bypass design and outcome measured preoperative QFR in all analyzable major vessels. Protocol angiography assessed 1-year graft status. Generalized estimating equations accounting for within-patient clustering related QFR (per 0.1-unit increment) to graft occlusion, unadjusted and adjusted for target vessel, graft type, age, sex, diabetes, and ejection fraction. Linearity and effect modification by graft type and target territory were assessed.

Results

Median QFR among 1161 analyzable vessels was 0.66 (interquartile range, 0.48-0.80); among 1036 bypassed vessels, higher QFR was associated with greater 1-year graft occlusion risk (unadjusted odds ratio [OR], 1.27; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.15-1.42; adjusted OR, 1.15; 95% CI, 1.04-1.27; p = 0.008). The association was linear (standardized occlusion probability, 8.2% at QFR 0.50; 13.1% at 0.90). Effect modification by target territory was borderline (joint interaction p = 0.025; Holm-adjusted p = 0.050); this exploratory finding requires confirmation. Graft type did not modify the association (p = 0.28).

Conclusions

Higher preoperative QFR, indicating functionally less significant stenosis, was associated with greater 1-year graft occlusion risk. This hypothesis-generating, group-level association establishes neither causation nor predictive utility for individual grafts. Prospective validation is needed.

title: Impact of Infarct Type on Serious Arrhythmic Event Detection and Cardiovascular Outcomes During Telemedical Monitoring After Myocardial Infarction: A SMART-MI substudy.
authorString: Dolejsi T, Schreinlechner M, Hofer F, Pavluk D, Klimovskis N, Kindl B, Boehmer AA, von Stuelpnagel L, Zabel M, Ehrlich JR, Freyer L, Massberg S, Rizas KD, Bauer A.
abstractText:
Background

Patients with LVEF 36-50% and cardiac autonomic dysfunction remain at risk after myocardial infarction (MI) despite not qualifying for primary-preventive defibrillator therapy. Implantable cardiac monitor (ICM)-based telemonitoring facilitates early detection of serious arrhythmic events (SArE), however it remains unclear whether infarct type modifies the detection and prognostic significance of SArE.

Objective

To compare the effect of ICM monitoring on SArE detection by infarct type and explore associations with subsequent major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE).

Methods

SMART-MI randomized MI survivors with LVEF 36-50% and cardiac autonomic dysfunction to ICM-based telemonitoring or conventional follow-up. Cox models assessed effects on SArE detection and treatment-by-infarct-type interaction. Exploratory analyses modeled detected SArE as a time-dependent covariate, stratified by arm, for subsequent MACCE.

Results

400 patients were randomized to ICM implantation (n=201, 122 STEMI) or conventional follow-up (n=199, 114 STEMI). Telemedical monitoring increased SArE detection in STEMI (HR 11.99, 95% CI 3.67-39.17) and NSTEMI (HR 4.44, 95% CI 2.09-9.43; both p<0.001). Although the effect was numerically greater in STEMI, clinically relevant effect modification cannot be excluded (p for interaction=0.154). Detected SArE were associated with subsequent MACCE in both, STEMI and NSTEMI with HR of 7.77 (95% CI 3.20-18.86) and 4.26 (95% CI 1.44-12.58), respectively.

Conclusion

ICM-based telemonitoring increased SArE detection in both STEMI and NSTEMI patients and detected SArE were associated with subsequent MACCE in both infarct types. These findings support further investigation of intensified rhythm-surveillance strategies in high-risk STEMI and NSTEMI patients.

title: Acute and 6-month vascular effects of a multi-component nutritional supplement: a randomized controlled trial.
authorString: Piercy C, Harris J, Sackho K, Campagnolo P, Barardo D, Creagh-Brown B, Heiss C.
abstractText:
Aims

To evaluate 6-month effects of a multi-ingredient nutritional powder formulation targeting complementary pathways relevant to vascular ageing on endothelial function and other vascular ageing markers in apparently healthy adults.

Methods and results

The effects of a supplement to target ageing mechanisms on vascular function study was a double-blind, randomized, controlled trial. Participants received a multi-ingredient nutritional powder formulation comprising vitamins/minerals, amino acids, and plant-derived bioactives, or control for 6 months. Vascular assessments were performed at baseline and after 6 months (with an acute post-dose assessment). The primary outcome was change in brachial artery flow-mediated dilation (FMD). Secondary outcomes included pulse wave velocity (PWV), peripheral and central blood pressure, augmentation index, lipid profile, and estimated 10-year cardiovascular risk (SCORE2/SCORE2-OP). Sixty-one participants (baseline SCORE2/SCORE2-OP 3.6 ± 2.9%) were randomized (33 actives; 28 controls); 43 completed both visits (24 vs. 19).
