Compared with control, the supplement improved endothelial function (ΔΔFMD at 6 months +2.9% [95% CI 2.1-3.8]) and reduced arterial stiffness (ΔΔPWV -1.18 m/s [95% CI -2.00 to -0.36]). Peripheral systolic blood pressure (SBP) decreased (ΔΔSBP -6.1 mmHg [95% CI -10.9 to -1.3]). Lipids were unchanged. Estimated 10-year cardiovascular risk decreased (ΔΔSCORE2/SCORE2-OP -0.45% [95% CI -0.86 to -0.03]).

Conclusion

Daily intake of a multi-ingredient nutritional powder formulation was associated with sustained improvements in endothelial function, arterial stiffness, and systolic blood pressure, with a modest reduction in estimated 10-year cardiovascular risk primarily attributable to lower systolic blood pressure rather than lipid change.

Registration

clinicaltrials.gov NCT06145087.

title: Index of microcirculatory resistance-guided management in angina: design and rationale of the DECISIONING trial.
authorString: Caullery B, Marzouki IE, Popovic B, Meneveau N, Dérimay F, Servoz C, Rioufol G, Teiger E, Gallet R, Morelle JF, Sideris G, Didier R, Pommier T, Van Belle E, Adjedj J, Leroy C, Bosson JL, Giai J, Barone-Rochette G, DECISIONING Investigators.
abstractText:
Rationale

Coronary microvascular dysfunction may contribute to persistent angina after fractional flow reserve (FFR)-guided coronary management. Whether disclosure of the index of microcirculatory resistance (IMR) and personalized management improve angina-related health status remains unknown.

Primary hypothesis

Among participants with initial IMR ≥25, disclosure of IMR with protocol-guided personalized management will improve the baseline-adjusted 12-month Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ) Summary Score compared with concealed IMR and usual care.

Design

DECISIONING is an investigator-initiated, 16-center French randomized trial (planned n=280). All participants have angina and at least one angiographic lesion ≥50%; FFR and initial IMR are measured before randomization. FFR ≤0.80 guides percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), whereas PCI is deferred when FFR >0.80. Participants are randomized 1:1, stratified by center and initial IMR (<25 or ≥25), to IMR disclosure with individualized treatment or IMR-concealed usual care. Participants and treating clinicians are aware of allocation; the initial IMR value remains concealed from control participants and their treating clinicians. Centralized follow-up and outcome assessment are blinded. Coronary flow reserve (CFR) is collected for exploratory secondary physiologic characterization but does not guide randomization or treatment. Enrollment and status Enrollment began on March 31, 2022. As of September 19, 2026, 275 participants had been randomized; enrollment toward 280 was ongoing, with final follow-up expected in october 2028.

Conclusions

DECISIONING will test the clinical benefit of IMR-informed management while characterizing complementary CFR/IMR physiology in exploratory analyses. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov; NCT05178914; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05178914.

title: Prediction models for venous thromboembolism in pediatric patients: A protocol for systematic review and critical appraisal.
authorString: Liu H, Zhou X, Li Z, Lu W, Ding Q, Xi Z, Yang J.
abstractText: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) in children is a severe disease with high mortality rates. It is also gradually recognized as a major source of morbidity in hospitalized children, leading to increased length of hospital stay, higher mortality, and increased costs. The majority of pediatric subjects with VTE present inherited or acquired risk factors,such as the use of a central venous catheter (CVC), which accounts for more than more than 90% of neonatal VTE and 50% of pediatric VTE. Clinical studies on predictive models for VTE in children have shown inconsistent results. This systematic review aims to evaluate published prediction models for pediatric VTE, analyzing their characteristics, predictors, efficacy, and the methodological quality and applicability. The protocol has been prepared using the Preferred Items for Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Protocols (PRISMA-P) guidelines. The systematic review protocol for VTE prediction in pediatric patients has been registered on PROSPERO (PROSPERO 2025CRD420251231316. Available from https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/vi-ew/CRD420251231316.) A comprehensive search across five major databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, and Wanfang) will be conducted for studies on prediction models of VTE among pediatric patients. Two researchers will independently screen literature, extract data, and evaluate the bias risk and applicability of included studies using prediction modelling study tools. This systematic review will provide critical insights into the efficacy and quality of reporting of the VTE model in pediatric patients. This will guide clinical physicians in selecting the most appropriate VTE prediction model and inform future research endeavors in pediatric VTE prediction.

title: CT-Based Deep Learning Assessment of Aortic Valve Fibrosis and Calcification: Development and Multicenter External Validation Against Experts, Histology, and Outcomes.
authorString: Grodecki K, Manral N, Kwiecinski J, Lenell J, Cadet S, Zuhair Kassem T, Geers J, Park C, Xing E, Tomasino GF, Olasinska-Wisniewska A, Wolny R, Dabrowski M, Protasiewicz M, Chmielak Z, Wojakowski W, Niemierko J, Fijalkowska J, Rymuza B, Parma R, Scislo P, Grabowski M, Jagielak D, Walczak A, Hajder A, Grodecka M, Gocol R, Urbanowicz T, Perek B, Jemielity M, Reczuch K, Grygier M, Ruile P, Schoechlin S, Elzomor H, Williams MC, Dweck MR, Berman DS, Newby DE, Kochman J, Jilaihawi H, Makkar R, Slomka PJ, Witkowski A, Huczek Z, Dey D.
abstractText:
Background

Computed tomography angiography (CTA) enables assessment of aortic valve tissue composition, providing insights into disease progression and helping predict outcomes in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis (AS). The authors aimed to develop a deep learning system for CTA-based quantification of aortic fibrotic and calcific tissue, validate its agreement with expert manual analysis and histopathology, and evaluate its value for outcome prediction.

Methods

This international, multicenter study included 1,674 patients who underwent CTA at 9 sites. A deep learning model based on the nnU-Net architecture was trained in 468 patients and applied to an external test set of 1,206 patients, including 29 with valve histology and 12 with serial CTA. In 1,165 patients with clinical outcomes, prognostic value was assessed adjusting for clinical, echocardiographic, and procedural covariates.

Results

Deep learning-enabled tissue composition analysis was rapid (1.35 ± 0.4 min vs 7.2 ± 1.2 min for experts) with excellent agreement vs expert assessment (r = 0.915; intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] = 0.913), histology (r = 0.909; ICC = 0.905), and scan-rescan reproducibility (r = 0.999; ICC = 0.999). In the external cohort, 469 patients (40%) died over 4.1 ± 1.1 years of follow-up. Fibrotic tissue volume (adjusted HR [aHR] 1.42 per IQR increase; P < 0.001), calcific tissue attenuation (aHR 1.02 per 25 HU increase; P = 0.005), left ventricular ejection fraction (aHR 1.10 per 5% decrease; P < 0.001), life-threatening bleeding (aHR: 1.96; P = 0.003), major vascular complication (aHR: 1.51; P = 0.042) and postprocedural peak pressure gradient (aHR 1.03 per 1 mm Hg increase; P < 0.001) independently predicted mortality. Patients in the highest tertile of fibrotic tissue volume (>0.940 cm3) had a 2-fold higher risk of death (aHR: 2.0; P < 0.001), whereas patients with dense calcific tissue attenuation (>885 HU) had a 1.5-fold higher risk of death.

Conclusions

Deep learning enables rapid quantification of aortic valve fibrotic and calcific tissue from CTA, demonstrating excellent agreement with both expert CTA and histological assessments. Quantitative analysis of aortic tissue composition provides additional prognostic value for all-cause mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement in multicenter external evaluation.

title: Clinical and Epidemiological Characteristics of Stroke in North Sumatra: A Multicenter Hospital-Based Study.
authorString: Fitri FI, Kadri A, Batubara CA, Nainggolan PH, Novita O, Ekayana E, Sastrawan MG, Nurchalida N, Gultom IM, Puspitasari CS, Sembiring S, Putra A, Ginting PN, Nasution IK, Ismira A, Sitanggang LM, Keliat M, Aritonang M, Dachi OA, Damanik ET, Arina CA, Rambe AS, Indonesian Neurological Association Medan Chapter, Medan, North Sumatra, Indonesia.
abstractText:
Background

Stroke remains a major cause of mortality and disability worldwide, with a disproportionate burden in low- and middle-income countries. In Indonesia, multicenter epidemiological data from regions outside Java remain limited. This study describes the clinical and epidemiological characteristics of stroke in North Sumatra using a multicenter hospital-based dataset.

Methods

This multicenter cross-sectional study analyzed medical record data of patients diagnosed with stroke between January and December 2024 across 25 hospitals in North Sumatra, Indonesia. Participating hospitals included public and private facilities with head computed tomography capability. Data included demographics, vascular risk factors, stroke subtype, clinical presentation, treatment patterns, complications, and in-hospital outcomes. Descriptive analyses were performed using frequencies, percentages, means, and medians.

Results

A total of 2862 patients were included. Mean age was 61.2 ± 11.4 years, with the largest proportion aged 55-64 years (35.3%); 52.5% were male. Ischemic stroke predominated (84.6%), whereas hemorrhagic stroke accounted for 15.4%. Hypertension was the most common risk factor (80.5%), followed by dyslipidemia (32.6%) and diabetes (29.8%). Hemiparesis was the most frequent presenting symptom (63.5%). Only 11.3% of patients arrived within 4.5 h of symptom onset, whereas 45.2% arrived more than 24 h after symptom onset; arrival time was undocumented or unclassified in 20.4% of patients.

Conclusion

Stroke in North Sumatra is strongly associated with modifiable vascular risk factors and delayed hospital presentation. Strengthening prevention, acute stroke care systems, and regional stroke surveillance is urgently needed.

title: Valvular Heart Disease and the Importance of Inspiratory Muscle Training in Cardiovascular Rehabilitation.
authorString: Bordoni B, Morabito B, Pianese L, Cannadoro G, Escher AR.
abstractText: Valvular heart disease (VHD) is a major cause of global cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Treatment is either surgical or transcatheter, as there is currently no conservative pharmacological approach. Cardiovascular rehabilitation (CR) is indicated before or after invasive medical interventions to facilitate the patient's functional recovery. While CR is common practice for many cardiovascular conditions, guidelines specifically addressing VHD are lacking. Another gap concerns the use of inspiratory muscle training (IMT). This narrative review discusses the importance of routinely incorporating IMT into CR programmes, offering hypotheses and recommendations for setting IMT parameters from the perspective of the Italian Association for Cardiovascular Rehabilitation (AIRC). Further research is needed to improve our understanding of rehabilitation and VHD.

title: Absence of Documented Standard Modifiable Cardiovascular Risk Factors Among Catheterized Admissions in Bangladesh: Frequency and Coronary Angiographic Phenotype in a 20-Year Registry Study.
authorString: Hasan MM, Haq MM, Kabir CS, Chowdhury MZ, Khan SR, Rahman MH, Nasrin S, Ali IA, Siraj KMF, Rahman A, Latif SB.
abstractText:
Background and aims

Coronary artery disease may occur without standard modifiable cardiovascular risk factors (SMuRFs), but the frequency and angiographic phenotype of such presentations in South Asian catheterization cohorts remain uncertain. We estimated registry-defined SMuRF-less frequency, tested alternative dyslipidaemia definitions, and compared angiographic phenotypes by SMuRF status.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective, single-centre, registry-based cross-sectional analysis of 51,864 admissions with matched catheterization records at a Bangladeshi tertiary cardiac centre from 2005 to 2024. Admissions were classified as SMuRF-less when no qualifying hypertension, diabetes, smoking, or dyslipidaemia was documented or identified; dyslipidaemia reflected a documented diagnosis or qualifying lipid measurement. Documented-only and statin-inclusive definitions were sensitivity analyses. We calculated unadjusted prevalence ratios (PRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

Results

Under the primary definition, 3172 admissions (6.1%) were SMuRF-less, compared with 6.5% under the documented-only definition and 1.6% under the statin-inclusive definition. Among admissions with a classifiable angiographic phenotype, SMuRF-less admissions more frequently had normal coronary arteries (24.9% vs. 10.7%; PR, 2.34; 95% CI, 2.18-2.50) and less frequently had obstructive coronary artery disease (56.6% vs. 71.2%; PR, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.77-0.82). Among admissions with obstructive disease, multivessel disease was less frequent (49.6% vs. 57.8%; PR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.82-0.90), whereas recorded intracoronary thrombus was more frequent (5.3% vs. 3.2%; PR, 1.65; 95% CI, 1.33-2.04). Of 6635 ST-elevation myocardial infarction admissions, 355 (5.4%) were SMuRF-less; 318 (89.6%) had obstructive disease.

Conclusion

Registry-defined SMuRF-less admissions, reflecting absence of documented qualifying factors rather than prospectively verified biological absence, were uncommon, and their estimated frequency depended on risk-factor ascertainment. Although their recorded angiographic burden was generally lower, obstructive disease remained common, particularly in ST-elevation myocardial infarction. The absence of documented SMuRFs should not provide clinical reassurance. Prospective patient-level studies with standardized risk-factor assessment and longitudinal follow-up are needed.

title: Intergenerational educational attainment and risk for incident dementia in a U.S. community-based cohort study: Findings from the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Neurocognitive Study.
authorString: Gupta S, Morrill V, Groechel RC, Kucharska-Newton A, Mosley TH, Lutsey PL, Meza E, Gottesman RF.
abstractText: BackgroundIndividuals with higher educational attainment have a lower risk for dementia, including Alzheimer's disease, but it is less clear how the educational attainment of an individual's parents may influence dementia risk, particularly in diverse populations.ObjectiveThis study examined whether intergenerational educational attainment for two adjacent generations was associated with incident dementia risk.MethodsIndividuals from the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities study were asked about their own educational level (at study baseline, 1987-1989; ages 44-66 years) and, several years later, that of each parent. Dementia status was ascertained from baseline through 2020 using expert committee diagnoses from in-person and telephonic neuropsychological assessments, informant interviews, hospitalization codes, and death certificates. Individuals without dementia at baseline, and with non-missing covariates/ educational history, were included. Educational level was classified (for individuals and the highest-educated parent) as less than high school, completed high school or GED, or more than high school. Cox proportional-hazard models were used to evaluate the association between intergenerational educational attainment and incident dementia risk.ResultsAmong 10,626 individuals (21.8% Black; 55.9% female), models showed that high parental education level and individual education level were each significantly and independently associated with a lower hazard of dementia, although associations were strongest and most consistent for individual education. Individuals whose educational attainment surpassed that of their parents, compared to those with comparable levels, exhibited a significantly lower dementia risk.ConclusionsAn individual's own educational attainment may exert a more significant influence in lowering dementia risk, even when parental education is considered.

title: Wearable E-Textiles for Cardiovascular Monitoring: Materials, Devices, and Integrated Systems.
authorString: Khan B, Tavakoli M, Radacsi N, Khoo BL.
abstractText: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, highlighting the need for continuous, non-invasive, and reliable physiological monitoring beyond conventional clinical assessments. Smart textiles have emerged as a promising platform for personalized cardiovascular healthcare by combining wearability, mechanical comfort, and seamless integration into everyday garments. This review examines recent advances in conductive materials, textile manufacturing technologies, and system-level device integration for cardiovascular sensing applications. Metallic fibers, carbon nanomaterials, and conducting polymers are evaluated for electrical conductivity, stretchability, mechanical durability, and wash stability. Furthermore, textile fabrication approaches, including weaving, knitting, embroidery, printing, and electrospinning, are analyzed for their ability to translate material properties into scalable, manufacturable sensing architectures. Recent developments in textile-integrated electrocardiography, pulse-wave, blood pressure, and hemodynamic monitoring demonstrate performance approaching clinical standards, with high signal fidelity and strong agreement with conventional medical devices. Key challenges related to long-term stability, power autonomy, signal reliability, and large-scale manufacturing are discussed alongside emerging solutions, including MXene-based electrodes, self-powered sensing systems, and edge artificial intelligence. Finally, future perspectives are outlined for developing clinically validated, scalable, and intelligent smart textile platforms that enable continuous cardiovascular monitoring and next-generation personalized healthcare.

title: Global, regional, and national burden of gallbladder and biliary diseases in 204 countries and territories, 1990-2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
authorString: GBD 2023 Gallbladder and Biliary Disease Collaborators.
abstractText:
Background

Gallbladder and biliary diseases-including cholelithiasis, cholecystitis, cholangitis, and other non-malignant biliary tract disorders-are important contributors to the global digestive disease burden, but a global, comprehensive, and systematic estimation of their burden is absent. We aimed to quantify long-term trends and current patterns in prevalence, mortality, and disability associated with gallbladder and biliary diseases across geographies, sexes, and ages.

Methods

We used estimates from the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2023 to assess the burden of gallbladder and biliary diseases in 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023. Mortality was modelled with the Cause of Death Ensemble model and prevalence with the Disease Modelling Meta-Regression tool (DisMod-MR 2.1). Years of life lost (YLLs) were calculated as the number of deaths for each age-sex-location-year multiplied by the standard life expectancy at each age. Severity-specific prevalence values were multiplied by their respective disability weights (with asymptomatic cases assigned zero disability) to estimate years lived with disability (YLDs). Disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) were computed by summing YLDs and YLLs. We report prevalence, mortality, YLDs, YLLs, and DALYs as counts and age-standardised and age-specific rates per 100 000 population with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs), stratified by sex, GBD region, and Socio-demographic Index (SDI).

Findings

In 1990 and 2023, the global counts for prevalence attributable to gallbladder and biliary diseases were 157·4 million (95% UI 134·0 to 183·3) and 264·4 million (226·0 to 309·9), for deaths were 65 800 (95% UI 53 000 to 78 800) and 146 700 (121 800 to 171 300), and for DALYs were 4·8 million (95% UI 3·5 to 6·2) and 8·2 million (6·3 to 10·6), representing substantial increases. However, age-standardised rates declined over the same period, from 3573·2 (95% UI 3045·5 to 4159·1) per 100 000 population to 2990·1 (2561·5 to 3492·5) per 100 000 population for prevalence, from 1·95 (1·58 to 2·31) per 100 000 population to 1·67 (1·39 to 1·95) per 100 000 population for mortality, and from 111·5 (84·1 to 143·3) per 100 000 population to 92·3 (70·9 to 119·6) per 100 000 population for DALYs. Over the past three decades, females had higher age-standardised prevalence and DALY rates than males, while sex differences in mortality rates were smaller. In 2023, age-standardised prevalence and DALY rates were lowest in south Asia and highest in central and western Europe, central Asia, and many regions in Latin America. By contrast, several regions in sub-Saharan Africa had relatively low prevalence and DALY rates but comparatively high mortality rates. National patterns broadly mirrored these regional profiles. In 2023, prevalence and DALY counts peaked in middle to early-older adulthood (ages 55-69 years), but age-specific rates continued to rise into the oldest age groups, with DALYs dominated by YLDs in midlife and early-older adulthood and by YLLs at older ages (≥80 years). The number of deaths peaked in the ninth decade of life, but age-specific rates also peaked in the oldest age groups. Across GBD regions, the association between SDI and age-standardised prevalence and DALY rates generally followed a reversed U-shaped pattern, with the lowest rates at low SDI, peak rates at intermediate SDI, and declining rates at the highest SDI levels. The association between SDI and mortality rate was less clear.

Interpretation

The global burden of gallbladder and biliary diseases is rising in absolute terms despite declining age-standardised rates, underscoring the importance of population growth and ageing. Health systems, particularly in settings with rapidly ageing populations and intermediate SDI levels, will need to expand diagnostic, elective, and emergency surgical capacity while investing in prevention of obesity and metabolic risk factors. Marked regional and national heterogeneity, as well as differences in risk factors, might reflect variance in health-system capacity and access to care, including timely diagnosis, availability of surgical services, and perioperative care. The predominance of non-fatal disability in midlife and rising mortality in older age groups indicates that integrated strategies spanning risk-factor control, early diagnosis, elective management, and robust acute care for older adults are essential to reduce both YLDs and YLLs.

Funding

Gates Foundation.

title: Multiparametric Extracellular Vesicle Profiling Identifies a Distinct Circulating Signature of Bicuspid Aortic Valve Disease
authorString: Weiss L, Harrison A, Chelvanambi S, Kasai T, Turner ME, Blaser MC, Billaud M, Aikawa M, Singh SA, Aikawa E.
abstractText:
Background

Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) resulting in life-threatening aortic stenosis, heart failure and death, develops earlier and progresses more rapidly in patients with bicuspid aortic valves (BAV) than tricuspid aortic valves (TAV), yet the circulating molecular drivers remain poorly understood. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) capture disease-relevant cellular activation and offer a powerful window into a BAV-specific pathophysiology.

Methods

Circulating large extracellular vesicle (LEV) abundance and morphology were characterized by complementary single-vesicle nano-flow cytometry and super-resolution microscopy. Proteomic profiling further delineated LEV molecular cargoes and associated biological pathways between patients with BAV and TAV.

Results

We demonstrate that patients with BAVs exhibited fundamentally altered circulating LEV profiles compared to TAVs. Super-resolution imaging revealed BAV-specific organization of platelet- and leukocyte-associated adhesion molecules into discrete EV membrane microdomains. Proteomic profiling identified distinct LEV cargoes between BAV and TAV, including a BAV-specific, previously unrecognized neutrophil-associated signature enriched for proteins involved in neutrophil degranulation and innate immunity. Consistent with this phenotype, BAV displayed alterations in platelet- and neutrophil-associated LEV populations, suggesting enhanced (thrombo-)inflammatory activity. Lastly, distinct associations between LEV populations and clinical parameters in BAV and TAV suggest that LEV profiles reflect morphology-specific aspects of disease severity.

Conclusions

Comprehensive single-vesicle analysis and bulk proteomic profiling identified a distinct circulating LEV signature in BAV-associated CAVD, characterized by endothelial activation and reciprocal platelet-neutrophil interactions. These findings reveal previously unrecognized differences in circulating LEVs between BAV and TAV and highlight their potential as biomarkers of valve morphology-specific pathophysiology.

title: Lack of Association between the Prothrombin gene rs1799963 G/A polymorphism and atherosclerosis risk in non-smokers from Sargodha, Pakistan
authorString: Abbas FA, Batool S, Hina M, Aman A, Khalid T, Awan FR, Hussain M.
abstractText: Background Atherosclerosis is a leading cause of cardiovascular related morbidity and mortality worldwide. Although smoking is a well-established risk factor, the genetic and environmental factors contributing to atherosclerosis in non-smoking populations remain less understood. This study aimed to investigate the association between the prothrombin F2 gene rs1799963 G/A polymorphism and atherosclerotic risk in non-smoking Pakistani adults. Results Family history of cardiovascular diseases (p < 0.001), high stress level (p = 0.001) and low physical activity (p = 0.002) showed significant association with atherosclerosis. The rs1799963 GG genotype (90% vs. 74%, p = 0.213) and G allele (95% vs 85%, p = 0.126) were more prevalent in patient group as compare to healthy controls. However, association between atherosclerosis and rs1799963 G/A in non-smokers was not significant. Discussion The findings suggest that family history, stress level, and lifestyle-related factors may contribute more strongly to atherosclerotic risk in non-smoking individuals than the studied F2 rs1799963 polymorphism. Although a higher frequency of the GG genotype and G allele was observed among patients, the lack of statistical significance may be due to the small sample size. Further studies with larger cohorts and multiple genetic markers are required to better understand genetic and environmental interactions in non-smoking populations. Conclusion In summary, risk of atherosclerosis increases in subjects with family history of cardiovascular diseases, high stress level and low physical activity. However, no influence of F2 rs1799963 polymorphism for the risk of atherosclerosis was found in non-smokers in the studied cohort.

title: CTHRC1 mitigates dystrophic aortic valve calcification by suppressing foamy macrophage-mediated inflammatory remodeling
authorString: Sakaue T, Sakamoto H, Hamaguchi M, Nakao Y, Kurata M, Iwase A, Kurihara H, Kiriyama Y, Fukunishi T, Hirotsugu K, Nishimura T, Uchita S, Shiokawa D, Kubota Y, Yamaguchi O, Izutani H.
abstractText: Although aortic stenosis (AS) represents a major cardiovascular burden, the molecular mechanisms underlying aortic valve calcification remain unclear. Spatial transcriptomic analysis of injured valve leaflets identified Cthrc1 (collagen triple helix repeat containing 1) as a prominently induced factor within the valvular interstitium. CTHRC1 elevation in expanded valvular interstitial cells (VICs) of thickened murine valve leaflets was validated by immunohistochemistry, and similar CTHRC1 upregulation was confirmed in human stenotic aortic valves. Lineage-tracing analyses demonstrated that the expanded VIC population in thickened murine valve leaflets following wire injury was derived predominantly from PDGFRβ-positive interstitial cells, with little contribution from endothelial cells. Although hemodynamic alterations were comparable between Cthrc1 −/− and wild-type AS mice, Cthrc1 deficiency markedly exacerbated valvular calcification during the chronic phase. Further spatial transcriptomic analyses of Cthrc1 −/− AS mice revealed extensive accumulation of Galectin-3-positive foamy macrophages within the interstitial space of stenotic valves in Cthrc1 −/− mice compared with wild-type controls. Moreover, stenotic valves from Cthrc1 −/− mice exhibited depletion of respiratory-chain signatures and upregulation of cell death–associated pathways, suggesting that CTHRC1, transiently induced during the acute phase following valvular endothelial injury, protects against subsequent dystrophic calcification.

title: Molecular Findings, Clinical Severity, and Transplant-Free Survival in Pediatric Cardiomyopathy: A Prospective Indian Cohort
authorString: Raj S, Deshpande S, Gajarski R, Cabrera A, Das B.
abstractText: Background The relationship between molecular findings, clinical disease severity, and heart failure (HF) outcomes in pediatric cardiomyopathy remains uncertain. Objectives To evaluate genetic diagnostic yield and the relative associations of clinical severity, biomarkers, and multimodality imaging with death or heart transplantation in children with cardiomyopathy. Methods This prospective single-center study included 235 children younger than 18 years at a South Indian referral center. Genetic testing, HF functional class, biomarkers, echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), and longitudinal outcomes were evaluated. Transplant-free survival was assessed using Kaplan–Meier analysis and Cox regression. Hierarchical models evaluated incremental prognostic discrimination using Harrell's C-index. Results Genetic testing was performed in 112 children (47.7%), of whom 54 (48.2%) had reported pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants. During a median follow-up of 15 months, 63 children (26.8%) died or underwent heart transplantation. Transplant-free survival did not differ significantly between P/LP-positive and genetic-negative groups (log-rank P = 0.058). Reduced ventricular function and late gadolinium enhancement were associated with adverse outcomes in univariable analyses. Among complete cases, the apparent C-index increased from 0.527 for demographics and cardiomyopathy phenotype to 0.813 after adding HF functional class and 0.842 after biomarkers, with limited additional discrimination from imaging measures. Conclusions Genetic testing demonstrated substantial laboratory-reported P/LP yield, although its effects on clinical management, family screening, and costs were not evaluated. HF functional severity and biomarkers provided the greatest apparent prognostic discrimination for death or transplantation, supporting an integrated clinical approach to pediatric cardiomyopathy assessment.

title: Diabetes and all-cause mortality in hemodialysis: A comparative survival analysis with complementary machine-learning methods.
authorString: Aylı BI, Ikhlef Ç, Gök Oğuz E, Paksoy N.
abstractText:
Background

Diabetes mellitus is the leading cause of end-stage renal disease and confers excess mortality in patients on hemodialysis. However, which diabetes-specific clinical parameters best predict survival remains insufficiently explored.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study followed 252 patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis (126 with diabetes, 126 without) from three centres in Ankara, Turkey, over 68 months (January 2020-September 2025; 66 deaths). Mortality predictors were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models, propensity score-weighted regression, and gradient-boosted machine-learning survival analysis. Eleven diabetes-specific parameters were examined within the diabetes subgroup.

Results

Diabetes was associated with reduced survival (log-rank p = 0.038) and a 68% higher mortality hazard (HR 1.68, 95% CI 1.02-2.75). After multivariable adjustment, the association was attenuated but directionally consistent across all specifications (HR 1.52-1.66). Within the diabetes subgroup, HbA1c was the strongest modifiable predictor (adjusted HR 1.43 per 1%, 95% CI 1.17-1.76, p < 0.001), improving model discrimination (C-index 0.679 vs. 0.652). No other diabetes-specific parameter, including retinopathy, diabetic foot, and diabetes duration, independently predicted mortality.

Conclusion

In this Turkish hemodialysis cohort, diabetes showed a consistent adverse trend toward higher mortality. HbA1c was the dominant modifiable predictor, supporting the integration of structured glycaemic monitoring into routine hemodialysis care.

title: Reduced desaturation-based detection of sleep apnea events in self-identified Black individuals across two cohorts.
authorString: Azarbarzin A, Sands SA, Messineo L, Esmaeili N, Vena D, White DP, Redline S, Wellman A.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Am J Respir Crit Care Med
journal.title: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
journal.isoabbreviation: Am J Respir Crit Care Med

abstractText:
Rationale

Pulse oximetry may overestimate oxygen saturation in individuals with darker skin pigmentation, potentially reducing detection of desaturation during sleep-disordered breathing.

Objectives

To assess racial/ethnic differences in desaturation-based obstructive event detection and cardiovascular risk, and evaluate heart-rate response as an oximetry-independent marker for risk stratification.

Methods

We analyzed participants without cardiovascular disease in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis(MESA) and Sleep Heart Health Study(SHHS). We modeled desaturation-based AHI relative to airflow-defined AHI and examined AHI-ΔHR6, defined by respiratory events with a heart-rate increase ≥6 beats/min. Adjusted Cox models evaluated associations with a composite outcome, major adverse cardiovascular events or all-cause mortality(MACE/mortality).

Measurements and main results

Black participants had 21% and 20% lower proportions of airflow-defined events meeting the ≥4% desaturation criterion than White participants in MESA (ratio 0.79[95% CI,0.68-0.93]; p = 0.003) and SHHS (0.80[0.68-0.94]; p = 0.008), respectively. No other racial/ethnic group showed a lower proportion of airflow-defined events meeting desaturation criteria than White participants. AHI-ΔHR6 event detection was similar between Black and White participants in both cohorts. In Whites participants, desaturation-based events were associated with MACE/mortality in MESA but not in SHHS, while desaturation-based AHI measures were not significantly associated with MACE/mortality in Black individuals in either cohort. In contrast, AHI-ΔHR6 was associated with MACE/mortality in MESA (HR 1.33[1.09-1.63];p=0.006) and SHHS (1.26[1.02-1.55]; p = 0.033).

Conclusions

Desaturation-based scoring identified a lower proportion of reduced flow events in Black than White participants, whereas heart-rate-response-based event detection was similar across groups, suggesting oximetry-related under-detection in individuals with darker pigment.

title: Association of HIV infection with short-term major adverse cardiovascular events among Chinese patients with carotid atherosclerosis: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Zhang W, Li Q, Deng C, Liu M, Yuan J.
abstractText:
Background

People living with HIV (PLWH) suffer accelerated atherosclerotic injury, but real-world Chinese cohort data excluding patients with pre-existing cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases remain scarce regarding HIV-related incident major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). This study aimed to explore the independent associations between HIV infection and 2-year incident MACE among Chinese patients with carotid atherosclerosis free of prior cardiovascular events, and identify correlated metabolic and renal factors.

Methods

A retrospective single-center cohort design was adopted. We enrolled patients with ultrasound-confirmed carotid atherosclerosis from January 2020 to June 2023, excluded individuals with prior coronary heart disease, ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack, and conducted standardized 2-year follow-up for all eligible participants. Univariate statistical tests screened variables correlated with MACE; variables with univariate p < 0.05 plus core clinical confounders (age, sex, hypertension, diabetes) were incorporated into multivariate binary logistic regression to identify independent correlates of new-onset MACE.

Results

Patients with HIV infection showed significantly younger age compared with HIV-negative counterparts (63.55 ± 10.81 years vs 70.61 ± 9.75 years, p < 0.001). The cumulative 2-year occurrence rate of MACE was markedly higher in the HIV-positive group (40.4% versus 22.9%, p = 0.023). Multivariate regression analysis verified four independent risk markers for incident MACE: HIV seropositivity (OR = 2.24, 95%CI 1.19-4.22, p = 0.012), baseline active smoking (OR = 1.98, 95%CI 1.07-3.66, p = 0.028), reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) (OR = 2.15, 95%CI 1.15-4.02, p = 0.017) and hyperuricemia (OR = 1.89, 95%CI 1.02-3.51, p = 0.043).

Conclusion

Chinese people living with HIV (PLWH) combined with carotid atherosclerosis develop atherosclerotic lesions at an earlier age and carry elevated short-term MACE risk. Integrated intervention strategies covering HIV viral control, smoking cessation, renal function protection and serum uric acid management can effectively improve cardiovascular long-term prognosis for this special population.

title: Postoperative spontaneous coronary artery dissection after major abdominal oncological surgery: a case report.
authorString: Alsubaie LS, Saida H, Alzahrani N.
abstractText: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is an uncommon non-atherosclerotic cause of acute coronary syndrome that can present as ST-elevation myocardial infarction (MI) and is particularly challenging because postoperative thrombosis and bleeding risks coexist. We report the case of a 44-year-old woman who underwent major abdominal oncologic surgery and developed a minor pulmonary embolism treated with anticoagulation. On postoperative day 4, she developed acute chest pain with ST-segment elevation. Emergency coronary angiography showed a long lesion involving the second diagonal branch, consistent with SCAD, with otherwise normal coronary arteries. She was managed conservatively. Her course was complicated by right JP drain-site bleeding, which required permanent heparin discontinuation and blood transfusion. This case illustrates SCAD as a cause of postoperative ST-elevation MI and the difficulty of balancing thrombosis and bleeding risk after major surgery.

title: Age-specific prognostic value of 1-year changes in cardio-ankle vascular index.
authorString: Kabutoya T, Hoshide S, Kario K.

journal.title: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension

abstractText: The prognostic significance of longitudinal changes in the cardio-ankle vascular index (CAVI) remains unclear. We investigated the association between 1-year changes in CAVI and subsequent cardiovascular events according to age. A total of 4032 participants with cardiovascular risk factors who were enrolled in the prospective multicenter Coupling Registry and had undergone CAVI measurements at baseline and 1 year were classified into four groups using a CAVI cutoff of 9: good ( < 9 at both time points, n = 1841), improved ( ≥ 9 to <9, n = 268), worsened ( < 9 to ≥9, n = 408), and persistently high ( ≥ 9 at both time points, n = 1515). The primary outcome was a composite of stroke, coronary artery disease, sudden cardiac death, heart failure, and aortic dissection. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models assessed associations between CAVI changes and outcomes. CAVI increased from 8.80 ± 1.34 at baseline to 8.88 ± 1.35 at 1 year (P < 0.001). During a median 60-month follow-up (49-63 months), 155 cardiovascular events occurred. In the overall cohort, neither the worsened group (HR, 1.56; 95% CI, 0.93-2.62) nor the persistently high group (HR, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.72-1.68) was significantly associated with cardiovascular events compared with the good group. Among participants aged <65 years, the worsened group (HR, 3.36; 95% CI, 1.18-9.58) and persistently high group (HR, 2.68; 95% CI, 1.11-6.50) had higher cardiovascular risk. No significant associations were observed among participants aged ≥65 years. In conclusion, among patients aged <65 years with cardiovascular risk factors, both worsening and persistently elevated CAVI were independently associated with increased cardiovascular risk.

title: Transapical mitral valve-in-ring implantation: Results of the real-world European Tendyne valve-in-ring registry.
authorString: Maier J, Ruge H, Krane M, Bleiziffer S, Friedrichs KP, Charitos EI, Schönburg M, Kuhn EW, Giannini C, De Carlo M, Teles RC, Nolasco T, Andreas M, Zillner L, Blessberger H, Lambert T, Damian I, Grund M, Zierer AF, Steinwender C, Kellermair J.

journal.title: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society

abstractText:
Objectives

Mitral regurgitation (MR) is commonly treated with ring-based annuloplasty. In case of recurrent MR, re-do operations are often denied due to high risk. Transcatheter valve-in-ring (V-i-R) procedures offer an alternative. This study assessed the feasibility and outcomes of using the transapical, repositionable Tendyne valve for off-label mitral V-i-R procedures, as an alternative to balloon-expandable valves like SAPIEN, which face limitations such as paravalvular leakage and LVOT obstruction.

Methods

The TEND-RING registry is a retrospective, international study with prospective follow-up, including 16 high-risk patients from eight European centers who underwent Tendyne V-i-R procedures between 2017 and 2024. Procedural, 30-day, and long-term outcomes were analyzed.

Results

Patients were elderly (median age 79.5), predominantly male (81%), with significant comorbidities (STS Risk of Mortality 5.6%, 4.4-7.2%) and severe MR (3 + /4 +). Procedural success was 100%, with no LVOT obstruction or device embolization. MR was reduced to mild or none in all patients. 30-day mortality was 6.3%. Over a median 11-month follow-up, five deaths occurred (31.3%), three from cardiovascular causes (18.75%). Surviving patients showed sustained MR reduction and improved symptoms (89% in NYHA I/II). Ring size analysis suggested a minimum of 36 mm for rigid/semi-rigid rings, while flexible bands allowed successful implantation in sizes as small as 30 mm.

Conclusions

Tendyne V-i-R procedures are technically feasible, effective, and safe in selected high-risk patients with recurrent MR. Ring size thresholds identified may guide patient selection and procedural planning in future interventions.

title: Childhood and Adolescent Cancer Burden in 2024 and Projections to 2050.
authorString: Tawfiles D, Jain U, Lam CG, Chan JSK, Feliciano EJG, Moraes FY, Bounedjar A, Willmann J, Wu JF, Pramesh CS, Magsanoc-Alikpala MJK, Mutebi M, Iyengar P, Buchmiller TL, Wolden SL, Ginsburg O, Dee EC.
abstractText:
Background

In recent decades, significant improvements have been made in the treatment of many childhood and adolescent cancers (patients ages 0-19 years), yet outcomes remain strikingly inequitable worldwide. We quantified the 2024 global burden of childhood and adolescent cancer by Human Development Index (HDI) and projected trends to 2050.

Methods

We used GLOBOCAN 2024 to estimate numbers of children and adolescents diagnosed with cancer and who died from cancer in 186 countries, overall and for four key cancer types (leukemia, brain and central nervous system [CNS] tumors, non-Hodgkin lymphoma [NHL], and kidney cancer). Age-standardized incidence and mortality rates (ASIR, ASMR) were calculated using the Segi-Doll world standard and stratified by sex, UN region, and four-tier HDI. Projections to 2050 applied 2024 age-specific rates to UN World Population Prospects demographic estimates, assuming constant rates over time.

Results

In 2024, excluding non-melanoma skin cancer, an estimated 277,023 children and adolescents were diagnosed with cancer and 102,056 died from cancer. Leukemia accounted for 27.8% of diagnoses and 33.9% of deaths, followed by CNS tumors (11.1% of diagnoses; 17.3% of deaths), NHL (8.2%; 6.9%), and kidney cancers (4.7%; 2.5%). Hematological malignancies represented the largest diagnostic category across all HDI levels, accounting for 36.8-46.4% of incident cases and 35.9-49.5% of deaths. Very high-HDI countries had the highest ASIRs but the lowest ASMRs, whereas low- and medium-HDI settings accounted for 57% of deaths in 2024. By 2050, incident cancers are projected to increase by 35.2% and deaths by 34.8% in low-HDI countries, while very high- and high-HDI countries are projected to experience relative declines in both incidence and mortality. Approximately 52% of diagnoses and 65% of deaths are expected in low- and medium-HDI countries, with more than 35% of deaths occurring in low-HDI settings alone.

Interpretation

Although significant advances have improved outcomes of many childhood and adolescent cancers, substantial global disparities in cancer burden persist. Underdiagnosis, limited diagnostic infrastructure, constrained workforces, and weak cancer registration systems likely lead to underestimation of the true burden. Under the assumption of constant incidence and mortality rates, an increasing share of childhood and adolescent cancer cases and deaths is projected to occur in low- and medium-HDI countries, underscoring the need for equitable investments in diagnosis, treatment, survivorship, and cancer registration. Contextualized implementation of the WHO Global Initiative for Childhood Cancer, including earlier diagnosis, reliable access to essential therapies, survivorship care, and strengthened registries, is essential to ensure that all children, regardless of geography, have a chance to survive cancer and thrive.

title: Anesthetic and Sedative Effects on Echocardiographic Parameters in Rat Models of Cardiomyopathy: A Critical Review
authorString: Pajović V, Kosić M, Jovanović M, Japundžić-Žigon N.
abstractText: Cardiomyopathies represent a heterogeneous group of diseases that lead to functional and structural impairment of the myocardium, frequently culminating in heart failure. Due to ethical and technical constraints inherent to human studies, rat models have become indispensable in experimental cardiology. Transthoracic echocardiography represents one of the most commonly used methods for assessing cardiac structure and function in experimental rat models of cardiomyopathy, due to its accessibility, non-invasiveness, ease of use, safety and cost-effectiveness. Almost all echocardiographic examinations in rats require a certain level of pharmacological sedation or general anesthesia to immobilize the animal and reduce motion-induced artifacts. A review of the literature reveals that only a few anesthetics are used in experimental practice. By far the two most prevalent choices are isoflurane and the ketamine-xylazine combination. Less frequently used are pentobarbital, the tiletamine-zolazepam combination, sevoflurane, and acepromazine. However, the interpretation of echocardiographic findings in experimental animals can be significantly biased by the effects of anesthesia primarily on the autonomic nervous system and cardiac contractility. Therefore the choice of anesthetic or sedative protocol represents an important, yet insufficiently standardized, methodological variable in the echocardiographic assessment of rat models of cardiomyopathy. Here we discuss the bias introduced by the use of sedatives/anesthetics when performing echocardiography in different rat models of experimental cardiomyopathy.

title: Phenytoin Toxicity Presenting With Ataxia and Nystagmus: A Case Report.
authorString: Elashmawy S, Kingston K.
abstractText: Phenytoin has a narrow therapeutic window, and elderly patients with multiple comorbidities are more susceptible to developing toxicity. This report details a patient who developed cerebellar symptoms during admission. Elevated phenytoin levels were identified and were higher still when corrected for low serum albumin. Structural, central infective, and epileptic causes were excluded. Despite repeated dose adjustments, therapeutic levels could not be maintained. Establishing therapeutic levels may have been further complicated by declining renal function and concurrent infection, and phenobarbitone levels were also supratherapeutic. He deteriorated and subsequently died. This case highlights the need for early phenytoin level monitoring when toxicity is suspected, particularly in frail patients with hypoalbuminemia, renal impairment, or acute illness, where dose titration is challenging.

title: A Race Against Time: Contralateral Acute Limb Ischemia During Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis for Peripheral In-Stent Thrombosis-A Case Report.
authorString: Madishetty V, Singh A, Sojitra B, Yaylayan A, Schneider K, Krolick M.
abstractText:
Background

Acute limb ischemia (ALI) from peripheral in-stent thrombosis is a vascular emergency requiring urgent revascularization. Catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) is an established treatment option in selected patients, but development of contralateral ALI during active thrombolysis is rarely described.

Case summary

A 70-year-old man with severe peripheral arterial disease, prior bilateral lower extremity stenting, coronary artery disease, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, and active tobacco use presented with acute left lower extremity pain, coolness, and absent pulses with preserved motor function most consistent with Rutherford Class IIa ALI. Imaging demonstrated extensive thrombosis involving previously placed left iliac and femoropopliteal stents. The patient underwent mechanical aspiration thrombectomy, balloon angioplasty, and left-sided CDT. During ongoing thrombolytic therapy, he developed new right lower extremity discoloration and absent pulses with preserved motor and sensory function-also most consistent with Rutherford Class IIa ALI. Repeat angiography demonstrated restored left-sided perfusion but new occlusion involving the right common femoral and superficial femoral arterial stents. Mechanical aspiration thrombectomy followed by right-sided CDT restored bilateral limb perfusion.

Discussion

Contralateral ALI developing during CDT may have multifactorial causes, including underlying thrombotic susceptibility as well as local access or sheath-related thrombosis. This case highlights the importance of bilateral vascular surveillance during thrombolytic therapy and prompt evaluation of new ischemic findings.

title: Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging in the Diagnosis and Management of Postpartum Choriocarcinoma With Cardiopulmonary Complications.
authorString: Lutay N, Castiglione A, Ahmed S, Koul A, Rådegran G, Ostenfeld E.
abstractText:
Background

Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (choriocarcinoma) may be associated with substantial diagnostic delay because of nonspecific symptoms and the rarity of this malignancy.

Case summary

A young postpartum woman presented with progressive dyspnea, fever, and chest pain. Delayed diagnosis led to clinical deterioration with severe pulmonary hypertension (PH), right ventricular (RV) dysfunction, culminating in cardiac arrest with successful resuscitation. Ultrasound demonstrating uterine lesions and markedly elevated β-human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) levels established the diagnosis of gestational choriocarcinoma. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) precisely assessed RV function and PH-related cardiac involvement. Chemotherapy normalized β-hCG levels and resolved PH and RV dysfunction.

Discussion

This case illustrates the diagnostic challenges of unclear dyspnea and choriocarcinoma complicated by PH and the value of CMR.

Take-home message

CMR plays an important role in the assessment of cardiopulmonary complications of choriocarcinoma, although a structured evaluation of dyspnea, including β-hCG, is essential for the early diagnosis.

title: Emotional stress-induced hot phases in a patient with a desmoplakin-associated arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy: a case report.
authorString: Caputo A, Birtolo LI, Canuti ES, Scoccia G, Vizza CD.
abstractText:
Background

Desmoplakin (DSP) mutations are a common cause of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM), frequently presenting with recurrent myocarditis-like 'hot phases' that contribute to myocardial injury and increased arrhythmic risk.

Case summary

A 40-year-old woman presented with acute chest pain and marked troponin elevation following emotional stress. Her history was notable for recurrent stress-related myocarditis episodes and a diagnosis of biventricular arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy due to a pathogenic DSP mutation. Cardiac magnetic resonance demonstrated diffuse myocardial oedema and a characteristic circumferential subepicardial ring-like pattern of late gadolinium enhancement, consistent with an active hot phase. Given the high-risk pathogenic DSP mutation with multiple high-risk features, including documented non-sustained ventricular tachycardia, frequent ventricular ectopy, and mild left ventricular disfunction (resulting in a calculated 5-year arrhythmic risk of 12% according to the novel DSP risk score)-and the presence of frequent hot phases recurrences and high burden of late gadolinium enhancement-a primary prevention implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was implanted after clinical stabilization. Medical therapy was optimized with β-blocker up-titration and low-dose selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor therapy targeting recurrent stress-related triggers. At follow-up, the patient reported sustained clinical well-being with no recurrence of hot phases or arrhythmic events.

Conclusion

This case exemplifies DSP-related arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy marked by recurrent, stress-triggered 'hot phases,' highlighting the pivotal interplay between inflammation and arrhythmic risk, and underscoring the need for refined, disease-specific risk stratification and targeted management strategies.

title: Illuminating metabolic disorders with engineered fluorescent carbon dots: advances in biosensing to therapeutics.
authorString: Prasad G, Srivastava M, Devi S, Tripathi P, Singh V.
abstractText: Metabolic diseases, including diabetes, obesity, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, dyslipidemia, and hyperuricemia, represent a major global health challenge, necessitating early diagnosis and effective therapeutic strategies. Conventional approaches may face limitations in sensitivity, specificity, and targeted delivery. In this context, carbon dots have attracted considerable interest as versatile nanoplatforms for metabolic biomarker detection, bioimaging, and potential therapeutic applications. Carbon dots are carbon-based, quasi-spherical nanomaterials characterized by tunable photoluminescence, relatively low toxicity, ease of synthesis, and promising biocompatibility. These properties support their investigation for detecting metabolic biomarkers, including uric acid, glucose, and cholesterol, through sensitive and selective fluorescence-based approaches. Their demonstrated sensing capabilities in controlled environments and spiked biological samples provide a foundation for further investigation toward clinical applications. Similarly, carbon dot-based bioimaging of metabolically relevant organs, such as the pancreas and liver, and their antioxidant and drug-delivery properties highlight their potential for advancing future diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. Advances in surface engineering and heteroatom doping (e.g., nitrogen, sulfur, and phosphorus) have expanded the potential biomedical applications. CDs are also being investigated as carriers for antidiabetic and lipid-regulating agents, with the potential to improve drug loading, delivery, and release. Furthermore, certain CDs exhibit antioxidant activity that may help mitigate oxidative stress associated with metabolic disorders. These developments highlight the emerging potential of CDs in integrated diagnostic-and-therapeutic, or theranostic, platforms. This review critically examines the applications of CDs in acquired metabolic disorders, emphasizing sensing mechanisms, analytical performance, biological validation, and emerging therapeutic strategies. It also discusses key challenges, including biosafety, biodistribution, pharmacokinetics, long-term toxicity, reproducibility, scalable production, and the gap between laboratory-based findings and clinical translation. Further validation in appropriate biological models and clinical samples is essential before their diagnostic and therapeutic efficacy can be established.

title: Impact of Anti-drug Antibodies in Patients with Fabry Disease under Enzyme Replacement Therapy: Long-Term Outcomes.
authorString: Lenders M, Rudolph E, Radke R, Nordbeck P, Brand E.

journal.title: BioDrugs : clinical immunotherapeutics, biopharmaceuticals and gene therapy

abstractText:
Background

Neutralizing anti-drug antibodies (ADAs) against enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) in Fabry disease (FD) are associated with disease progression despite therapy in affected male patients.

Objective

The aim of this study was to assess the long-term effects of ADAs on clinical outcomes.

Methods

We analyzed the long-term outcomes of ADA-positive (n = 24) and ADA-negative (n = 28) male patients under agalsidase alfa or beta. The assessment included Fabry-associated clinical events (FACEs), determination of cardiac and renal function, evaluation of FD-related symptoms, and the analysis of plasma globotriaosylsphingosine (lyso-Gb3) values.

Results

Median observation time was 10 years. ADA-positive and ADA-negative patients presented with comparable disease burden at baseline. Although there were no significant differences in the overall event rate of FACEs (p = 0.114), ADA-positive patients had an increased risk of ischemic cardiac events, an increase in interventricular septum thickness in diastole (median difference 0.25 mm per year; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.06-0.42; p = 0.0053), and a steeper decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) (median difference -0.39 ml/min/1.73 m2 per year; 95% CI -2.40 to 0.25; p = 0.0554). Macroalbuminuria and high-risk patients according to Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) guidelines at baseline resulted in an accelerated yearly eGFR decline of -6.5 in ADA-positive patients (p < 0.001) versus -2.1 ml/min/1.73 m2 in ADA-negative patients (p = 0.0177; comparison: p = 0.0079). The lyso-Gb3 decrease was more pronounced in ADA-negative patients (p = 0.0407).

Conclusions

Compared to ADA-negative patients, ADA-positive male patients with FD show significantly worse clinical long-term outcomes under ERT. They should be classified as high-risk patients, undergo close monitoring, and receive intensive treatment. Immune tolerance induction to prevent ADAs might be considered to improve the therapeutic efficacy in future.

title: Exercise exposure and arrhythmic patterns in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Aaserud LT, Five CK, Haugaa KH, Lie ØH.
abstractText:
Background

Exercise is associated with ventricular arrhythmias (VA) in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC), but relationships with atrial fibrillation (AF) and arrhythmic patterns are less established.

Objective

To assess prior exercise intensity and dose in relation to AF, VA, and combined arrhythmic patterns across the ARVC diagnostic spectrum.

Methods

Genotype-positive probands and relatives were included. Exercise during the three years preceding diagnosis was assessed retrospectively by structured interview. Intensity was defined by the primary activity's Metabolic Equivalent of Task (MET) and dose as MET-hours/week across activities. AF and VA were assessed at first visit and last follow-up.

Results

We included 122 individuals (49% women; mean age 39±17 years), with a median follow-up of 13.5 years. AF prevalence increased from 5% to 21% and VA from 26% to 37%. Median onset ages were 55 years for AF and 36 years for VA. Both exercise measures were associated with VA at both time points. Exercise dose was associated with AF at first visit and intensity at last follow-up. Median exercise dose increased across groups with no arrhythmia, AF only, VA only, and both. The association between AF and VA at last follow-up was attenuated after adjustment for exercise intensity (adjusted OR 2.43, 95% CI 0.85-6.97, p=0.10).

Conclusions

Associations with exercise was consistently associated with VA, but varied for AF by measure and time point. The graded distribution does not establish thresholds or sequential progression. Co-occurrence may reflect shared exercise history, disease susceptibility, and differential surveillance rather than a direct relationship.

title: Microgravity and Cardiac Electrophysiology: Autonomic Remodeling, Arrhythmogenesis, and Implications for Long-Duration Spaceflight.
authorString: Ciaccio EJ, Talke M, Peters NS, Schwartz SM, Coromilas J, Yarmohammadi H, Biviano AB.
abstractText:
Background

In microgravity, the human heart undergoes significant geometric and functional remodeling due to the removal of gravity-dependent hydrostatic gradients. These adaptations include a transition from an elliptical to a more spherical shape configuration. Furthermore, cephalad fluid shifts trigger an early spaceflight diuresis, inducing a stable reduction in circulating plasma volume.

Objective

To describe resulting electrophysiologic alterations and arrhythmia promotion.

Method

While most spaceflight arrhythmias are transient and non-lethal, they remain a concern for long-duration missions. Frequently reported irregularities include isolated premature atrial and ventricular complexes. Other events, including non-sustained ventricular tachycardia during spaceflight, the possibility of early-onset atrial fibrillation, and atherosclerosis in former astronauts following exposure to high-energy ionizing radiation have been documented, though the association is still being evaluated. The underlying arrhythmogenic substrate is driven by autonomic resetting, spatiotemporal heterogeneity, and QTc interval prolongation.

Results

The National Aeronautics and Space Administration utilizes a multi-faceted approach to maintain electrical stability, incorporating high-intensity interval training and electrolyte monitoring and supplementation. Real-time monitoring of wearable technology enables continuous telemetry of the heart. Recently, automated chest compression devices have been shown to significantly outperform manual cardiopulmonary resuscitation in microgravity environments.

Conclusion

Although structural changes typically revert to baseline upon return to Earth gravity, deep-space missions present some risks. Astronauts exposed to ionizing radiation beyond Earth's magnetic field may face risk of long-term cardiovascular disease. Design of personalized nutrition to mitigate electrolyte loss and development of advanced screening tools for cardiac risk assessment are essential to improve the safety of future planetary missions.

title: Targeting the PI3K/Akt/eNOS pathway in atherosclerosis: From mechanotransduction to emerging therapies.
authorString: Li L, Li L, Gao M, Wu H, Wu Y, Xiao F.

journal.title: The international journal of biochemistry & cell biology

abstractText: Atherosclerosis (AS) is the primary underlying cause of the majority of severe cardiovascular diseases (CVDs), including coronary heart disease (CHD), ultimately resulting in myocardial ischemia and hypoxia. Endothelial dysfunction is universally acknowledged as the initiating event in atherogenesis. In a healthy vasculature, laminar shear stress (LSS) exerted by flowing blood acts as the paramount physiological stimulus for maintaining endothelial homeostasis by triggering sophisticated mechanotransduction cascades. At the molecular apex of translating this physical force into protective biochemical signals is the phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/Akt) signaling axis. Upon activation by LSS or protective biochemical ligands, Akt directly phosphorylates its pivotal downstream effector, endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS). This specific post-translational modification catalyzes the sustained biosynthesis of physiological nitric oxide (NO). As a highly potent atheroprotective molecule, NO mediates vasodilation, suppresses vascular inflammation, and inhibits aberrant cellular proliferation. Conversely, the impairment of this signaling axis under conditions of disturbed flow or metabolic stress accelerates AS progression. This article comprehensively reviews the molecular architecture of the PI3K/Akt/eNOS signaling pathway, its mechanosensitive regulation by LSS, and its pleiotropic roles in combating atherogenesis, thereby providing novel mechanistic insights and therapeutic strategies for the prevention and treatment of atherosclerosis.

title: Hypoxia alters the synthesis and post-translational modification of collagens in human coronary artery smooth muscle cells.
authorString: Jørgensen SM, Yang-Jensen KC, Lorentzen LG, Yeung K, Eiberg JP, Davies MJ, Chuang CY.
abstractText: Considerable data support the hypothesis that hypoxia plays a central role in the development of atherosclerotic plaques and cardiovascular disease. Hypoxia may modulate the pool of proteins within cells, including vascular smooth muscle cells of the artery wall, and drive phenotypic changes. Here we report a detailed liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) study of changes induced in human coronary artery smooth muscle cells (HCASMC) on transfer from an atmosphere of 20 to 1% O<sub>2</sub> (hypoxia) for 1 and 7 days. Exposure to 1% O<sub>2</sub> resulted in marked changes in the HCASMC proteome with 755 proteins (of 5,842 total) altered in abundance after 1 day, and 2874 (1234 up, 1640 down) after 7 days of hypoxia. Significant changes in specific collagens, and collagen-modifying hydroxylases and cross-linking enzymes were detected (lysyl oxidases and related species, prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases), with most of these upregulated by hypoxia. These data are consistent with significant extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling under hypoxia and increased collagen synthesis, processing, secretion and incorporation into ECM. Analysis of protein post translational modifications (hydroxylations) indicates enhanced hydroxylation of multiple collagen peptides, particularly within the helical coil regions. Immunoblotting and ELISA data support these ECM changes. Comparison with proteomic data obtained from advanced symptomatic human carotid artery atherosclerotic plaques and control artery samples, provides evidence for a similar pattern of changes, particularly with regard to collagen-modifying and processing enzymes, consistent with the presence of hypoxic regions within human plaques. Together, the data indicate that hypoxia plays a significant role in collagen-focused ECM remodeling.

title: PANI/CMWCNTs immunosensor with KNN-ridge for high-throughput COX-2 screening.
authorString: Sun B, Fu J, Sun Y, Zhang Y, Dong Y, Qin C, He H, Kang J, Yang L, Wu Y, Ma X, Liang D.
abstractText: Chronic inflammation is tightly linked to atherosclerosis and malignancies. Cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) is a pivotal target for anti-inflammatory drug discovery. However, conventional screening approaches for natural products are limited by low throughput, insufficient precision, and prolonged assay durations. Herein, a high-performance COX-2-targeted electrochemical immunosensor was constructed with polyaniline/carboxylated multiwalled carbon nanotube (PANI/CMWCNTs) nanocomposite as conductive sensing interface. Benefiting from the synergistic electron-transport network of dual nanomaterials, this sensor delivers distinct quantitative advantages over traditional single-carbon-material and bare glassy carbon electrode sensors, including greatly boosted detection sensitivity and superior signal stability. Fabrication parameters were systematically optimized using the Box-Behnken response surface methodology coupled with cyclic voltammetry (CV) and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). Under optimized conditions, the developed immunosensor exhibited a low limit of detection (LOD) of 76 pg/mL. By combining electrochemical response signals with K-nearest neighbor-ridge regression (KNN-Ridge) machine learning, an intelligent screening platform was further built. The integrated system achieves 60% classification accuracy for discriminating herbal active ingredients, with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.71 for concentration trends. This approach captures the rough variation trend of analyte concentration, significantly shortening screening duration and meeting the demand for qualitative preliminary screening that traditional assays cannot satisfy. This work establishes an integrated "sensing-intelligent trend analysis" strategy for rapid, preliminary screening of COX-2-targeted anti-inflammatory components from natural products, facilitating intelligent auxiliary analysis and traceability assessment of bioactive constituents in traditional herbal medicines.

title: Urinary oxidative DEHP metabolites and advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: Evidence from NHANES and mechanistic insights into MECPP-related macrophage inflammatory-glycolytic activation.
authorString: Liang L, Su S, Niu Q, Rao K, Zhang Y, Chen N, Wang L, Chen Y, Yao P.
abstractText:
Background

Phthalates are ubiquitous environmental contaminants, yet their relevance to advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome remains unclear. We examined the associations between urinary phthalate metabolites and advanced CKM syndrome, and explored the potential mechanisms linking di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP)-related exposure to macrophage inflammatory-glycolytic activation.

Methods

We analyzed 4236 adults from seven cycles (2005-2018) of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). A total of ten urinary phthalate metabolites were quantified, and advanced CKM syndrome was defined as CKM stages 3-4 using an NHANES-adapted American Heart Association framework. Survey-weighted logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, and weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression were used to assess single-metabolite, dose-response, and mixture associations. Mono(2-ethyl-5-carboxypentyl) phthalate (MECPP) was further evaluated using network toxicology, molecular docking, Mendelian randomization, single-cell RNA sequencing, and macrophage reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR).

Results

Among 4236 participants, 648 had advanced CKM syndrome. In fully adjusted models, oxidative DEHP metabolites were positively associated with advanced CKM syndrome. Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest quartile was associated with higher odds for mono(2-ethyl-5-oxohexyl) phthalate (MEOHP; odds ratio [OR], 1.64; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.12-2.42), mono(2-ethyl-5-hydroxyhexyl) phthalate (MEHHP; OR, 1.60; 95% CI, 1.05-2.42), and MECPP (OR, 1.84; 95% CI, 1.26-2.68), with significant trends. Restricted cubic spline analyses suggested non-linear associations. WQS regression indicated a positive mixture association, with MECPP receiving the highest weight. Network toxicology identified 33 overlapping genes enriched in pathways related to the renin-angiotensin system, insulin resistance, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor signaling, and diabetic cardiomyopathy. Among the candidate hub genes, tumor necrosis factor (TNF) and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARG) were further examined using molecular docking and Mendelian randomization. Single-cell analyses of public mouse heart and kidney datasets localized Tnf mainly to macrophages and Pparg to cardiac endothelial cells and renal monocytes. In RAW 264.7 macrophages, MECPP potentiated palmitic acid-induced expression of inflammatory and glycolysis-related genes.

Conclusions

Urinary oxidative DEHP metabolites, particularly MECPP, were positively associated with advanced CKM syndrome in US adults. These findings support MECPP as a potential biomarker of DEHP-related exposure and generate mechanistic hypotheses involving macrophage-centered inflammatory and glycolytic transcriptional activation. Prospective and experimental studies are warranted to clarify causality and to determine whether DEHP-related exposure contributes to the development and progression of CKM syndrome.

title: NNMT modulates macrophage polarization and atherosclerosis through AMPKα and HIF1α pathways.
authorString: Wu X, Wang J, Mi Y, Huang R, Peng L, Ren J, Zhuo R, Zhou Y, Huang X, Cai P, Qiu Y, Zhao Y.
abstractText:
Background

Macrophage polarization and inflammatory responses play a pivotal role throughout all stages of atherosclerosis. Wedelolactone (WDL), a naturally occurring coumestan derivative, exhibits potent inhibitory activity against nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT). This study aims to clarify the role of NNMT in macrophage polarization and explore the anti-atherosclerotic effects of WDL together with its molecular mechanisms linked to NNMT inhibition.

Methods

Immunofluorescent staining was performed on high-fat-diet (HFD) fed apoE-deficient (apoE-/-) mice to localize NNMT and determine its abundance within atherosclerotic lesions. In cultured macrophages, expression levels of polarization markers and NNMT were examined following transfection with/without NNMTsiRNA and/or intervention with WDL. In vivo, HFD-fed apoE-/- mice were treated with WDL, and atherosclerotic lesions were comprehensively assessed using ultrasound imaging, histological staining, and immunological labeling.

Results

NNMT expression was markedly elevated in macrophages of atherosclerotic plaques, and its abundance correlated tightly with macrophage polarization status. Accordingly, WDL remodels macrophage polarization to M2 phenotype through activating AMPKα and depressing HIF1α pathway in an NNMT-dependent manner. Thereby, WDL significantly alleviated atherosclerosis in apoE-/- mice.

Conclusion

The results demonstrate that NNMT modulates macrophage polarization and its inhibition with WDL alleviates atherosclerosis, which delineates the functional cascade connecting NNMT suppression with macrophage phenotypic remodeling, and offers novel therapeutic strategies for clinical atherosclerosis management.

title: ZeXieYin formula attenuates trimethylamine N-oxide- induced atherosclerosis and cognitive impairment by regulating microglial-neuronal signaling and autophagy.
authorString: Wu W, He Y, Zhang X, Zhou S, Song Z, Hu Y, Wang M, Zhu B.
abstractText:
Ethnopharmacological relevance

ZeXieYin Formula (ZXYF), a classic traditional Chinese medicine decoction first documented in the Huangdi Neijing (an ancient Chinese medical text), traditionally used to treat patterns of internal accumulation of phlegm turbidity and deficiency of healthy qi-a pathogenesis closely associated with atherosclerosis and cognitive impairment, and which is composed of three medicinal herbs-Alisma plantago-aquatica L. (Zexie, Water Plantain Rhizome, dried tuber), Atractylodis macrocephala Koidz. (Baizhu, Largehead Atractylodes Rhizome, dried rhizome), and Pyrola calliantha Andres. (Luxiancao, Chinese Pyrola Herb, whole herb)-in a 2:2:1 ratio. For the preparation of ZXYF decoction, Zexie (200 g), Baizhu (200 g), and Luxiancao (100 g) were accurately weighed. ZXYF has been observed in our previous studies to reduce trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) levels, exert anti-inflammatory and lipid-lowering effects and alleviate atherosclerosis (AS) while improving cognitive function.

Aim of the study

To investigate whether ZXYF ameliorates TMAO-induced AS with concurrent cognitive impairment (AS-CI) by modulating microglia-mediated paracrine signaling and subsequent neuroinflammation.

Materials and methods

To create an AS-CI model in vivo, Apolipoprotein E-deficient mice(ApoE-/- mice) were given a high-fat diet (containing the TMAO precursor choline) for 8 weeks. ZXYF (6.5, 13 g/kg) was administered via gavage. Aortic plaques were evaluated by Oil Red O staining, cognitive function was detected by behavioral tests (Y-maze, Morris water maze, and novel object recognition), and TMAO levels in brain tissue and serum were examined by Ultra-performance liquid chromatography-electrospray ionization tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-ESI-MS/MS). Immunofluorescence, immunohistochemistry, and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) were used to evaluate microglial activation, C-C chemokine receptor type 5 (CCR5) expression, microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 (LC3) expression, toxic proteins deposition, and autophagic ultrastructure in the hippocampus. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and Western blot were performed to detect the protein expression of chemokines, factors that promote inflammation, and related signaling pathways. In vitro, a paracrine model of BV2 microglia and HT22 neurons was established, and autophagic flux was detected by transfection with green fluorescent protein-red fluorescent protein-LC3 (GFP-RFP-LC3) lentivirus. CCR5 antagonist maraviroc, mTOR inhibitor rapamycin, and ZXYF-containing serum were used for intervention to verify the signaling pathway mechanism.

Results

ZXYF treatment significantly reduced aortic plaque area, enhanced working, spatial, and recognition memory (p < 0.05), and concurrently lowered TMAO levels in both brain tissue and serum. ZXYF prevented hippocampus microglial activation and the MAPK/NF-κB inflammatory cascade, and downregulated the release of proinflammatory factors. Mechanistic studies showed that ZXYF markedly reduced the expression of chemokines C-C motif chemokine ligand 3 (CCL3), C-C motif chemokine ligand 4 (CCL4) and C-C motif chemokine ligand 5 (CCL5) in the brain, inhibited the expression of their receptor CCR5 and downstream mTOR phosphorylation, thereby restoring neuronal autophagy (increasing the number of autophagosomes, upregulating LC3-II and Beclin1, and downregulating sequestosome 1 (p62)) and reducing the deposition of amyloid-beta (Aβ) and phosphorylated Tau (p-Tau) proteins. In vitro experiments supported that the conditioned medium of activated microglia induced autophagy inhibition and neuroinflammation through the CCL3/4/5-CCR5-mTOR axis, while maraviroc, rapamycin and ZXYF-containing serum could block this effect and restore autophagic flux.

Conclusion

ZXYF ameliorates AS-CI by reducing TMAO levels, inhibiting microglial activation and the release of CCL3/4/5, thereby blocking the neuronal CCR5-mTOR signaling axis, restoring autophagic function and alleviating neuroinflammation.

title: Interpretable ECG manifolds link longitudinal electrical phenotypes to heart-failure risk in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
