title: Coronary artery calcification is not associated with survival in advanced gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer: a secondary analysis of the EXPAND trial.
authorString: Meyer HJ, Dermendzhiev T, Jacobs PP, Romeo D, Stocker G, Denecke T, Lordick F, Hacker UT.

journal.title: Journal of cancer research and clinical oncology

abstractText:
Purpose

Computed tomography (CT) is the clinical standard for staging of gastrointestinal cancer. Previous studies have highlighted the prognostic significance of coronary artery calcification (CAC) detected by CT in various types of cancer. However, the prognostic role of CAC scoring in gastrointestinal cancers is still unclear. The aim of this study was to investigate the impact of CT-defined CAC on overall survival (OS) in patients with advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer.

Methods

CAC was semiquantitatively measured using the visual Weston method on baseline CT scans in 785 patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer from the phase III EXPAND trial. This present study is a secondary analysis of the base line CT images. In the original analysis patients were randomly assigned to first-line treatment with cisplatin/capecitabin ± cetuximab. The primary endpoint of the current subanalysis is the OS. For statistical analysis group differences were calculated using the Mann-Whitney-U test and ANOVA test. Kaplan-Meier curves and multivariable Cox regression analysis were used to test the effect of CAC on mortality.

Results

The median CAC score was 1 (IQR 0; 3). A total of 337 patients (42.9%) had no visible CAC (CAC score 0). Male patients had statistically significant higher CAC score compared to female patients (median 1 versus 0, p < 0.0001). In univariable Cox regression CAC showed no significant association with survival when analysed as a continuous value (HR: 0.99, 95% CI: 0.96-1.02, p = 0.74), and when dichotomized for absence and presence of calcification (HR:1.08, 95% CI: 0.92-1.26, p = 0.34). Similar results were identified in further subgroup analyses.

Conclusion

CT-defined CAC scoring has no relevant prognostic impact in advanced gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer undergoing first-line chemotherapy. The present study cannot confirm the promising results for CAC scoring in lung cancer patients.

title: Clinical and Economic Impact of Nirsevimab and Bivalent Maternal Vaccine Against RSV Infections in Infants in Italy.
authorString: Bini C, Marcellusi A, Muzii B, Soudani S, Trotta S, Parisi S, Bozzola E, Bonanni P, Boccalini S.
abstractText:
Objective

This study aimed to estimate the potential clinical and economic impact of nirsevimab and of a maternal vaccine in the prevention of medically attended (MA) RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) in the entire cohort of newborns entering their first RSV season in Italy compared with the absence of prevention strategies.

Methods

A cost-consequence analysis using a static decision tree model previously published was conducted to estimate the RSV-MA-LRTIs and associated mid-long-term complications avoided with each immunization strategy during a single RSV epidemic season. Nirsevimab efficacy was derived from the pooled analysis of Phase 3 MELODY and Phase 2b clinical trials and a protection of 6 months with constant efficacy was considered. For maternal immunization (MI), the efficacy for term infants was derived from MATISSE clinical trial and it was considered until 6 months of age. Zero efficacy was assumed starting from the seventh month for both preventive strategies. The time horizon of the analysis corresponding to one RSV epidemic season. National Health Service (NHS) perspective was considered in the base-case.

Results

From the NHS perspective, over the first RSV season, the immunization strategy with MI compared with no preventive strategies could lead to a reduction of 68,358 RSV-MA-LRTIs and 6,417 associated mid-long-term complications. These reductions in terms of RSV‑related health events can be translated into economic savings of about € 24.5 million. The immunization strategy with nirsevimab compared with no preventive strategies could lead to a reduction of 118,123 RSV-MA-LRTIs, 8,480 associated mid-long-term complications. The economic saving associated with these reductions in terms of RSV-related health events was estimated equal to € 34.2 million.

Conclusion

Both preventive strategies represent effective measures for the prevention of RSV infections in infants. The organizational impact of these two strategies should also be assessed, in addition to ensuring appropriate counselling for pregnant women and the parents of infants, to avoid missing these immunization opportunities against RSV. These findings may support public health decision-making and inform future policy strategies.

title: Single vs Double ProGlide Devices for Access Site Closure after Transfemoral Aortic Valve Replacement: The SINGLE-CLOSURE Trial.
authorString: Liu X, Guo Y, Song G, Chen T, An G, Wang L, Guo Y, Zhou H, Jiang L, Chen X, Cheng B, Niu G, Xu K, Shao Y, Chen Z, Yang Y, Fang Z, Liu J, Xiu J, Chen J, Bai Y, Zhuang X, Cheng Z, Wang L, Xu J, Liang X, Han K, Hu H, Liu Q, Leon MB, Wang J.

journal.title: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background

Despite advances in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), access-site vascular complications remain an important source of procedural morbidity. The conventional double-ProGlide strategy may increase the risk of access-site stenosis and other vascular complications, particularly in patients with challenging iliofemoral anatomy. Retrospective studies have suggested that a single-ProGlide strategy may offer an effective alternative, but this strategy has not yet been evaluated in a randomized trial.

Objectives

This trial aimed to determine whether a single-ProGlide strategy could offer a simpler alternative to the conventional double-ProGlide strategy without increasing vascular complications.

Methods

The SINGLE-CLOSURE trial was a prospective, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 25 centers in China. Patients aged ≥65 years scheduled for transfemoral TAVR were assigned 1:1 to single-ProGlide or double-ProGlide closure for the main access site. The primary endpoint was the in-hospital composite of Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC)-3-defined access-site or access-related major and minor vascular complications.

Results

A total of 876 patients were randomized. In the modified intention-to-treat population, the primary endpoint occurred in 57 of 436 patients (13.1%) in the single-ProGlide group and 65 of 430 patients (15.1%) in the double-ProGlide group, meeting the prespecified criterion for noninferiority (risk difference: -2.2%; 95%: -7.0% to 2.6%; P = 0.013; noninferiority margin: 3.19%). Access-related major vascular complications occurred in 2 patients (0.5%) in the single-ProGlide group and 6 patients (1.4%) in the double-ProGlide group. Among the secondary endpoints, individual components of the primary endpoint, access-related bleeding, time to hemostasis, and all-cause mortality were similar between groups. Access-site stenosis was numerically less frequent with the single-ProGlide strategy (5.0% vs 7.9%), whereas additional closure devices might be used more often (2.5% vs 0.9%).

Conclusions

A single-ProGlide strategy was noninferior to conventional double-ProGlide closure for the composite of VARC-3-defined access-site or access-related vascular complications after transfemoral TAVR. Primary endpoint events were predominantly minor vascular complications.

title: Radiomics performance to identify high-risk carotid artery plaques: a systematic review.
authorString: D'lima J, Rheault F, Beaudoin AM.
abstractText:
Background

Stroke is a leading cause of mortality worldwide, with 15-20% of ischemic strokes caused by extracranial carotid atherosclerotic disease. Risk stratification has traditionally relied on luminal stenosis severity, which inadequately reflects plaque vulnerability. Radiomics offers an emerging solution by extracting high-dimensional quantitative data from standard medical images. This systematic review evaluated the performance of radiomics-based models for identifying high-risk carotid plaques.

Materials and methods

A systematic search was conducted across multiple databases. Studies were included if they developed or validated radiomics-based models for carotid plaque assessment and reported performance metrics, specifically the area under the curve (AUC). Data were extracted on study design, imaging modalities, segmentation methods, and modeling techniques.

Results

Twenty-eight studies involving 6,108 patients (72.4% male) were included. Computed tomography angiography was the most commonly used imaging modality (n = 16), and manual region-of-interest segmentation was performed in 27 of 28 studies. Radiomics models showed strong predictive performance. Internal validation AUCs were as high as 0.984, whereas combined models incorporating radiomics with clinical and/or conventional radiological features achieved the best predictive accuracy, often exceeding 0.90. However, only four studies included external validation cohorts.

Conclusion

Radiomics is a powerful, non-invasive tool for identifying high-risk carotid plaques, offering superior discriminative power over conventional stenosis-based assessments. Despite these promising results, the field faces significant hurdles, and future research must prioritize prospective multicenter trials, the development of automated segmentation workflows, and the correlation of radiomic features with histopathological findings to ensure clinical reproducibility and transition into routine stroke prevention.

Key points

Question Standard carotid atherosclerotic disease assessments fail to capture biological plaque complexity and vulnerability, necessitating objective, reproducible, and non-invasive methods to improve stroke prevention. Findings Radiomics and combined models demonstrate superior capability in identifying high-risk carotid plaques compared to traditional assessments. With four external validations, the field remains exploratory. Relevance statement Radiomics offers a non-invasive tool for personalized stroke prevention. However, technical barriers currently prevent its transition to routine clinical use, including reliance on manual segmentation and low compliance with international standardization guidelines.

title: Cerebral Small Vessel Disease and Its Associations with Cognitive Impairment, Gait Disturbance, and Europsychiatric Symptoms: A Narrative Review.
authorString: Wang S, Zhu J, Sun J, Liu G.
abstractText: Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) encompasses a heterogeneous group of pathological processes affecting the small arteries, arterioles, capillaries, and venules of the brain. Beyond its well-recognized role in lacunar stroke and intracerebral hemorrhage, CSVD is increasingly understood as a major contributor to cognitive decline, gait impairment, and mood disturbances in older adults. These non-stroke manifestations often coexist and share common pathophysiological substrates, including endothelial dysfunction, blood-brain barrier disruption, chronic hypoperfusion, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and disruption of structural and functional brain networks. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the epidemiology, neuroimaging markers, and pathophysiological mechanisms of CSVD, with particular attention to its associations with cognitive impairment (predominantly executive dysfunction and slowed processing speed), gait abnormalities (reduced walking speed, increased stride variability, and elevated fall risk), and europsychiatric symptoms (vascular depression, apathy, and anxiety). The interactive relationships among these clinical phenotypes and the amplifying effects of comorbidities such as diabetes are also discussed. Finally, we review existing intervention strategies, particularly blood pressure control, and highlight emerging therapeutic targets and unresolved questions that warrant further investigation.

title: Hydroxychavicol-Rich <i>Piper betle</i> Extracts Attenuate TNFα-Driven Endothelial Inflammatory Response by Modulating Adhesion Molecules and Cytokine Release.
authorString: Jasni SM, Suffian Y, Zamakshshari NH, Dayang EZ.

journal.title: Advances in pharmacological and pharmaceutical sciences

abstractText: Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammatory disorder that involves endothelial dysfunction and accumulation of inflammatory cells in the vessel intima. Approximately 32% of global mortality is attributed to cardiovascular diseases, with atherosclerosis playing a major role. Endothelial dysfunction is a key hallmark of atherosclerosis, with key mediator tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) driving endothelial-monocyte interactions that further lead to adverse cardiovascular events. Hydroxychavicol, a phenolic compound enriched in Piper betle (PB), methanolic and chloroform extracts, has demonstrated anti-inflammatory activity, yet its effects on endothelial activation remain insufficiently characterized. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the endothelial-protective effects of hydroxychavicol-rich PB methanol (PB-M) and chloroform (PB-C) extracts by evaluating their impact on the expression of adhesion molecules and proinflammatory cytokines in TNF-α-induced human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs). HPLC was performed to confirm the presence and determine the amount of hydroxychavicol in both PB-M and PB-C. The cytotoxicity effects of both extracts were first assessed by MTT assay. HUVECs were pretreated with NF-κB inhibitor BAY11-7082, PB-M, or PB-C before being exposed to TNF-α for 4 h. Adhesion molecules and cytokines expression were measured by Western blot and ELISA, respectively. Both PB-M and PB-C were shown to contain hydroxychavicol, yet PB-C has about 3.8 times higher levels. MTT assays yielded IC50 values of 128.9 µg/mL for PB-M and 18.59 µg/mL for PB-C, while HUVEC morphology remained normal at 100 µg/mL PB-M and 20 µg/mL PB-C. Both extracts displayed dose-dependent suppressing effects on TNF-α-induced E-selectin, VCAM-1, and ICAM-1 expression. PB-M resulted in a pronounced inhibition of IL-6, IL-8, and MCP-1, while PB-C displayed cytokine-selective suppressive effects. In conclusion, both PB-M and PB-C attenuated TNF-α-induced endothelial inflammation, with PB-C acting at lower effective doses but PB-M providing broader anti-inflammatory suppression, suggesting that their different phytochemical compositions and possible synergistic interactions beyond hydroxychavicol may contribute to their distinct bioactivities, warranting further investigations.

title: Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage Associated with Diabetic Ketoacidosis in a Patient with Insulin-Dependent Diabetes: An Autopsy Case Report.
authorString: Cao C, Herath J.
abstractText:
Introduction

Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is a well-known complication in diabetic patients, especially those who rely on insulin to maintain physiologic blood glucose levels, and allow for normal cellular uptake of glucose. While an uncommon cerebrovascular complication of DKA, there have been reported cases of subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) occurring in episodes of DKA. DKA is more prevalent in patients with insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus, particularly in younger patients under the age of 50.

Methods

A medicolegal autopsy was performed on a 19-year-old woman with a history of type 1 diabetes mellitus as well as prior episodes of DKA, who was found unresponsive in bed and did not survive resuscitation.

Results

The cause of death was found to be DKA on a background of elevated vitreous glucose and post-mortem serum β-hydroxybutyrate. Additionally, a mild recent SAH was found on post-mortem internal examination. Two aneurysms were identified in both the right ascending communicating artery (RACA) and right middle cerebral artery, and the SAH was found to originate from the RACA. There were other findings supportive of DKA, such as gastric erosions, pale kidney cortices, and fatty changes in the liver.

Discussion

DKA is a fatal complication of untreated diabetes mellitus, and the risk of mortality and morbidity increases with subsequent episodes. Diabetes can also predispose an individual to vasculopathies such as aneurysm formation, and subsequent SAH may be identified on post-mortem exam. While the SAH may not be the immediate cause of death, it is a rare finding in post-mortem examination of diabetic decedents, and the risk of aneurysm rupture may be the result of derangements such as increased intracranial pressure during DKA.

title: Percutaneous Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement for Symptomatic Mitral Regurgitation: 2-Year Outcomes From the ENCIRCLE Trial.
authorString: Webb J, Guerrero ME, Muhammad KI, Greenbaum AB, Vasquez A, Oldemeyer JB, Dahle TG, O'Neill BP, Rihal C, Morse M, Rodriguez E, Russo M, Makkar RR, Whisenant B, Yadav P, Thourani V, Inglessis-Azuaje I, Langer N, Kapadia S, Stinis C, Price M, Summers M, Chehab BM, Grizzell B, Foerst J, Yaryura R, Castellanos J, Wang J, Zorn G, Tadros P, Alli O, Pu D, Garcia S, Mullen MJ, Boone R, Blanke P, Pham M, Baran DA, Asch FM, Daniels DV, ENCIRCLE trial Investigators.

journal.title: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background

Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) is an approved treatment option for select high-risk patients with symptomatic mitral regurgitation (MR). The main cohort of the ENCIRCLE trial, evaluating fully percutaneous transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system, demonstrated 13.9% mortality, significant MR reduction, and improved functional and health status outcomes at 1 year.

Objectives

We report 2-year outcomes from the main cohort of the ENCIRCLE trial.

Methods

Eligible symptomatic patients with ≥3+ MR who were not suitable for surgery or transcatheter edge-to-edge repair underwent TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system. Independent study oversight included an echocardiographic core laboratory and a clinical events committee. Endpoints included the nonhierarchical composite rate of all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization (HFH) as well as clinical, echocardiographic, functional, and health status outcomes.

Results

A total of 299 patients were treated, with 2-year follow-up data available for 202 of 210 eligible patients (96.2%). Mean age was 75.5 ± 9.3 years, 50.8% were men, and the mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score for mitral valve replacement was 6.6% ± 4.1%. At 2 years, MR reduction was sustained, with MR ≤1+ in 97.0% patients (P < 0.001). The 2-year composite rate of all-cause mortality or HFH was 35.6% (25.1% all-cause mortality, 23.0% HFH). In a 365-day landmark analysis, 1- to 2-year rates were 13.0% for all-cause mortality and 10.6% for first HFH. At 2 years, the rates of disabling stroke, clinically significant valve thrombosis, and hemolysis requiring intervention were 6.6%, 7.1%, and 7.6%, respectively. There were no instances of clinically significant left ventricular outflow obstruction. Improvements in functional and health status outcomes were sustained with 87.0% of patients in NYHA functional class I/II (P < 0.001) and a mean Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire overall summary score increase of 17.2 points (P < 0.001). The 6-minute walk distance increased by +9.0 ± 97.3 m compared to baseline (P = 0.246).

Conclusions

The 2-year results of the ENCIRCLE trial demonstrated durable near MR elimination with sustained improvements in functional and health status outcomes in surviving patients. These findings support transseptal TMVR as a therapeutic option for carefully selected patients with symptomatic MR. (The ENCIRCLE Trial [ENCIRCLE]; NCT04153292).

title: Transient Atrioventricular Block Secondary to Coronary Artery Embolism From Infective Endocarditis Following CAR T-Cell Therapy.
authorString: Kito K, Tsutsui K, Matsuyama T, Ban A, Kobayashi K, Hatsuno M, Haga T, Sasajima Y, Kozuma K.
abstractText: Silent infective endocarditis after CAR-T therapy caused septic embolic occlusion of a septal coronary branch, producing localized myocardial infarction involving the His bundle region and transient complete atrioventricular block. This case highlights a rare, pathologically confirmed mechanism of conduction disturbance.

title: Metabolomic Analysis of Patients with Coronary Artery Disease and Acute Myocardial Infarction by Using Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy.
authorString: Pagonas N, Dammermann W, Siasos G, Kostin S, Sasko B, Sotiriou P, Strathmeyer S, Heelemann S.
abstractText: This cross-sectional exploratory study investigates the potential of metabolomics to differentiate between stable coronary artery disease (CAD) and acute myocardial infarction (AMI) through Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopic analysis. The study identifies distinct metabolic profiles for each condition, revealing significant variations in metabolite levels, particularly lactic acid, which is a key metabolic product of anaerobic glycolysis, emerges as a prominent marker in AMI patients, reflecting acute ischemic stress and providing insight into adverse outcomes associated with high lactate levels. Another metabolite found in the present study was hypoxanthine, which is key biomarker for myocardial ischemia. These findings underscore the potential of metabolomics in combination with pathway analysis in distinguishing between CAD and AMI and highlight the metabolic dysregulation that occurs in these diseases. Our results suggest that these metabolites could serve as potential biomarkers, paving the way for personalized prognostic and diagnostic strategies. Further large-scale studies are necessary to validate these findings and incorporate them into clinical practice.

title: Rare Sites of Metastases to the Breast and Integumentary System in Advanced Cervical Cancer at Initial Presentation in Eastern Uganda: A Case Report.
authorString: Nteziyaremye JG, Akandwanaho D, Adong LL.
abstractText:
Background

Cervical cancer (CC) is the leading Gynaecological cancer in Uganda with an estimated 6959 women diagnosed, and 4607 annual deaths. About 60-80% of CC patients present with advanced stage disease with either local spread or with distant metastases. For those with distant metastases, the most common sites of spread are the lungs and supraclavicular lymph nodes. Breast and integumentary system metastases are very rare. We present a case with such metastases managed in eastern Uganda.

Case presentation

A 72 years old, Ugandan black African female, came in with a 13 months history of intermittent postmenopausal bleeding and associated abnormal vaginal discharge. She had repeatedly been managed from the nearest health facility for recurrent urinary tract infection and sexually transmitted diseases with no improvement. On examination at Mbale Regional Referral Hospital, she had poor performance status, cachexic, with bilateral pitting, tender poedal oedema, left breast masses and cutaneous nodules on the anterior aspect of the left thigh. Abdominal exam revealed a bulky uterus. On vagina examination, a large easily bleeding cervical tumour measuring about 8 cm × 7 cm and involving the upper 1/3 of the vagina was found. Bimanual pelvic exam revealed bilateral parametria involvement and bilateral pelvic side wall extension. Biopsies of the cervical, breast and the cutaneous masses were positive for high grade adenocarcinoma. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) for breast and cutaneous biopsies was positive for 16-kilodalton protein (P16), and negative for Oestrogen receptors (ER) and Progesterone receptors (PR). A diagnosis of cervical adenocarcinoma stage IVB (with breast and integument system metastases), with obstructive uropathy and probable deep venous thrombosis was made. She was offered total palliation and unfortunately succumbed on day 3 of admission.

Conclusion

Cervical adenocarcinoma stage IVB with breast and integumentary metastases portends poor prognosis. Gynaecologic Oncologists and other service providers need to do thorough exam and investigations to rule out metastases to rare sites. This will aid appropriate counselling during care.

title: Association Between the HbA1c-To-HDL-C Ratio and Female Infertility Among Reproductive-Aged Women: Evidence from NHANES.
authorString: Wang X, Luo S, Cheng H.
abstractText:
Background

Metabolic abnormalities have been increasingly implicated in female reproductive dysfunction. The HbA1c-to-HDL-C ratio may reflect the combined burden of chronic glycemic exposure and lipid-related metabolic status; however, its relationship with female infertility remains insufficiently understood. This study investigated the association between the logarithmically transformed HbA1c-to-HDL-C ratio [Log (HbA1c/HDL-C)] and infertility among reproductive-aged women.

Methods

This cross-sectional study included women aged 18-45 years from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) conducted between 2013 and 2018. After applying the exclusion criteria, 2452 participants were included, comprising 329 women with infertility and 2123 without infertility. Log (HbA1c/HDL-C) was analyzed as both a continuous variable and quartiles. Weighted multivariable logistic regression models were used to estimate the association between Log (HbA1c/HDL-C) and infertility. Restricted cubic spline analysis was performed to evaluate the dose-response pattern, and subgroup analyses were conducted to assess potential heterogeneity across population characteristics.

Results

Compared with women without infertility, those with infertility were older and had higher BMI, HbA1c, and Log (HbA1c/HDL-C) levels. In the primary multivariable model, higher Log (HbA1c/HDL-C) was associated with greater odds of infertility (OR = 1.93, 95% CI: 1.03-3.60). Women in the highest quartile had higher odds of infertility than those in the lowest quartile (OR = 1.90, 95% CI: 1.13-3.22), with a significant trend across quartiles. The association was more apparent among women younger than 35 years. After additional adjustment for BMI, the association was attenuated (OR = 1.64, 95% CI: 0.85-3.16).

Conclusion

Higher Log (HbA1c/HDL-C) was associated with greater odds of self-reported female infertility in models without BMI, but the association was attenuated after BMI adjustment. These findings suggest that adiposity may partly account for the observed relationship and require confirmation in prospective studies.

title: Extracellular Vesicles in Periodontitis: Bidirectional Crosstalk Between Periodontal Inflammation and Systemic Diseases.
authorString: Qu R, Wang F.
abstractText: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease that leads to the destruction of tooth supporting tissues, including gingival inflammation, periodontal attachment loss, and alveolar bone resorption. Increasing evidence suggests that periodontitis also increases susceptibility to a range of systemic conditions and there is a reciprocal communication between the periodontum and systemic organs. Extracellular vesicles (EVs), as key mediators of intercellular communication, can transport proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids across biological barriers and may play an important role in this crosstalk. In this review, we synthesize current evidence for the involvement of EVs in communication between periodontitis and distant organs. Compared with previous reviews that mainly focus on Porphyromonas gingivalis EVs or one-way effects, we synthesize evidence across multiple EV sources (bacterial, host periodontal, and circulating biofluid EVs) and explicitly review both directions of signaling. At present, the evidence is considerably stronger for periodontal-to-systemic EV effects, particularly in endothelial dysfunction, metabolic reprogramming, osteoclastogenic signaling, and barrier disruption in distant organs, whereas the evidence of systemic EVs on periodontitis remains limited, fragmented, and largely preclinical. This marked imbalance identifies the systemic-to-oral EV pathway as a major knowledge gap in the field. Further studies are needed to define the sources, cargoes, and functional significance of EVs in oral-systemic crosstalk and to clarify their translational potential as biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

title: Preoperative CALLY Index and Quantitative Left Atrial Low-Voltage Burden are Associated with Documented Recurrence After First Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Chen S, Zhang Z, Cai B, Wang H, Ma J, Ge G, Liu H.
abstractText:
Background and objectives

We assessed whether preoperative C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte (CALLY) index and intraoperative left atrial low-voltage area (LVA) burden provide complementary prognostic information after first ablation for persistent atrial fibrillation.

Materials and methods

This retrospective cohort included 259 patients. The endpoint was first documented atrial fibrillation, flutter, or tachycardia lasting ≥30 s after a 60-day blanking period. ln(1/CALLY) and LVA burden were modeled with natural cubic splines in landmark Cox models; diagnostics prompted an extended model allowing LVA effects to vary with log time.

Results

There were 114 recurrences. Both exposures showed nonlinear associations (overall P<0.001; P for nonlinearity=0.011 and 0.004). Relative to the median, the 75th percentile of ln(1/CALLY), where higher values correspond to lower CALLY and a less favorable systemic profile, had HR 1.99 (95% CI 1.47-2.70). Corresponding LVA HRs were 2.41, 4.78, 7.36, and 10.21 at days 90, 150, 240, and 364, although late high-LVA support was sparse. Harrell C increased from 0.648 to 0.819 after adding both markers. Near-12-month performance was similar across fixed Cox, time-varying Cox, and fixed-horizon logistic models.

Conclusion

CALLY and LVA burden provided complementary systemic-host and electroanatomic information. Findings are prognostic within the observed operator-directed pathway and require external validation.

title: Key Genes Related to the Integrated Stress Response Identified Through Bioinformatics and Clinical Experiments in Ovarian Aging.
authorString: Xian Y, Huang Y, Chen X, Lin D, Ou Y, Guo X.
abstractText:
Background

Ovarian aging (OA) compromises female fertility, but its relationship with the integrated stress response (ISR) remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify ISR-related genes associated with OA and assess their expression through experimental validation.

Methods

Differentially expressed genes from an OA-related transcriptomic dataset were intersected with ISR-related genes to identify candidates. Machine learning and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis were used to prioritize key genes. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) and immune cell enrichment analysis were performed to explore associated biological features. Gene expression was assessed using reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR).

Results

BAG2, BLVRB, PHB2, and STC1 were identified as key genes, with individual areas under the ROC curve (AUCs) ranging from 0.73 to 0.77 in the discovery dataset. All four genes were downregulated in OA samples in the transcriptomic analysis. GSEA revealed enrichment of ribosome-related pathways in gene expression profiles correlated with BAG2, BLVRB, and PHB2 (adjusted P < 0.05). BLVRB expression was positively correlated with the estimated regulatory T-cell enrichment score (cor = 0.42, P = 0.013). RT-qPCR supported the downregulation of BAG2, BLVRB, and PHB2 in the OA group (P < 0.05), whereas the decrease in STC1 expression was not statistically significant (P = 0.0811).

Conclusion

These findings identify four candidate ISR-related genes associated with OA, with experimental expression support for three genes. Their biological roles and clinical relevance require further investigation in independent cohorts and functional studies before diagnostic or therapeutic applications can be considered.

title: Identifying potential targets in endothelial to mesenchymal transition-mediated atherosclerosis using bioinformatics and machine learning.
authorString: Hou Z, Chen S, Cui Y, Ma Q, Chen J, Shu K.
abstractText:
Background

Endothelial to mesenchymal transition (EndMT) is a key driver of atherosclerosis (AS). This study integrated multiple RNA transcriptomic and single-cell transcriptomic datasets to identify shared gene expression signatures between EndMT and AS.

Methods

GEO expression profiles were analyzed via differential expression, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and functional enrichment analyses. A Random Forest model evaluated key genes, validating their expression and diagnostic performance. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) further assessed their expression patterns, and a Transcription Factor (TF)-mRNA-miRNA regulatory network.

Results

Fifteen overlapping genes were identified, from which six candidates were screened through a Protein-Protein Interaction (PPI) network and validated in vitro. The application of a Random Forest model identified two key hub genes, CCL5 and IL1B, which were significantly upregulated. Their diagnostic Area Under the Curve (AUC) was >0.7 when assessed separately and increased to >0.85 in a combined model. Three shared TFs (NFKBIA, NFKB1, RELA) of the Nuclear Factor-kappa B (NF-κB) pathway were identified, highlighting its central role in disease progression.

Conclusions

CCL5 and IL1B are key genes potentially regulating EndMT-mediated AS via inflammatory pathways including Nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain-like (NOD-like) receptor, Tumor Necrosis Factor (TNF), and NF-κB signaling, offering promising diagnostic and therapeutic targets for AS.

title: Orchestrating adaptive homeostasis on bioprosthetic valves: a metal-polyphenol hydrogel armor for integrated immunomodulation and endothelialization.
authorString: Huang X, Feng Y, Jiang D, Chen L, Li G, Zheng C, Wang Y.
abstractText: With the advancement of transcatheter valve replacement technology, bioprosthetic heart valves (BHVs) are being increasingly used in the clinical treatment of valvular diseases. However, current BHVs fail to concurrently resist thrombosis, modulate the immune and redox homeostasis in response to complex host-biomaterial interactions, leading to premature degeneration and shortened lifespan. Herein, we constructed an endothelial layer-inspired armor for BHV by fusing metal-polyphenol drug network (MPN) nanoparticle with immune/redox regulation functions and vascular endothelial glycocalyx-like layer that serve as passive defense and endothelialization scaffolds. The coating established a biomimetic endothelial defense barrier that resisted the deposition of blood components on BHVs while acting as a scaffold for endothelialization. The MPN nanoparticle fabricated through the self-assembly of Epigallocatechin-3-gallate, curcumin, and Cu<sup>2+</sup> was anchored to endow the BHV with free-radical-scavenging capability, immunomodulatory activity and endothelialization-promoting potential. The overexpressed reactive oxygen species were scavenged and the local inflammation responses were downregulated through immune and inflammatory response pathways. This not only maintained homeostasis at the BHV bio-interface but also created a pro-endothelialization microenvironment that favors the adhesion and growth of endothelial cells. Additionally, the coating catalyzed the releasing of NO to promote the endothelialization through PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway. The combined advantages of nanoparticles and glycocalyx-like hydrogel, which integrate antithrombotic, immunomodulatory, antioxidant, endothelialization-promoting, and anti-calcification effects, provided a promising strategy to address the critical challenge of BHV degeneration.

title: Effects of Tea Polyphenols on the Pharmacokinetics of Atorvastatin and Underlying Mechanisms in Hyperlipidemic Rats.
authorString: Feng C, Zhao F, Zuo D, Pang G, Ma Y.
abstractText: This study systematically explored the impact of tea polyphenol (TP) on the pharmacokinetics of atorvastatin (ATV) and underlying mechanisms in male Sprague-Dawley rats with hyperlipidemia induced by high-fat diet. The study was conducted using UHPLC-MS/MS, Western Blot, and in situ single-pass intestinal perfusion experiments. Pharmacokinetic analysis revealed that high-dose TP administration (200 mg/kg, 7 days) significantly reduced the C max and AUC0-t of ATV by 43.83% and 43.38%, respectively, while increasing CLz/F by 85.04%. Similar reductions were observed for statin metabolites 2-hydroxy atorvastatin (o-ATV) and 4-hydroxy atorvastatin (ρ-ATV). Western blot results showed that 7-day TP treatment downregulated CYP3A4 expression but upregulated intestinal P-gp expression to 1.37-fold (LDTP) and 1.84-fold (HDTP). Intestinal perfusion experiments further confirmed that TP decreased the cumulative intestinal absorption amount (M) of ATV by 40%. EGCG and ECG exhibited significant inhibitory effects to ATV intestinal absorption, reducing the M by 44% and 48%, respectively. In contrast, EGC and EC showed a nonsignificant trend toward slightly increased absorption of ATV. In summary, TP may lower ATV bioavailability through P-gp-mediated efflux induction and potential physicochemical interactions, implying caution for long-term high-dose intake of TP or supplements.

title: Adipose-Derived Mesenchymal Stem Cells: Isolation, Origin, Phenotype Applications, and Challenges.
authorString: Liu Z, Tu G, Wang C, Zhao H, Wu Z, Li W, Chen L, Niu B.
abstractText: Traditional adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (AD-MSCs) research has relied on unfractionated bulk populations, whose therapeutic efficacy is constrained by cellular heterogeneity, culture-induced phenotypic drift, and rapid postengraftment functional exhaustion, resulting in inconsistent outcomes and impeding clinical translation. This review systematically examines AD-MSC developmental origins, tissue niches, isolation and purification strategies, functional phenotypes, and biomanufacturing bottlenecks. It integrates preclinical and clinical evidence for AD-MSCs and their extracellular vesicles (EVs) in bone and cartilage regeneration, chronic cutaneous diseases, neurological disorders, cardiovascular diseases, and other conditions. These therapies remodel injured microenvironments through immunometabolic reprogramming, antifibrotic signaling, angiogenesis, mitochondrial transfer, and paracrine regulation rather than direct tissue replacement. Major translational barriers include cellular heterogeneity, safety concerns, the transdifferentiation controversy, nonstandardized preconditioning, culture-induced phenotypic drift, and low cell retention after transplantation. We propose that clinical translation should be based on prospective isolation of functional subpopulations, coupled with tailored preconditioning, precision gene editing, three-dimensional biomaterials, EV engineering, and automated closed-system biomanufacturing. This framework aims to preserve potency, phenotypic stability, and paracrine function, transforming AD-MSCs and their bioactive derivatives from variable, unfractionated preparations into well-characterized, standardized, highly potent precision biologics. More broadly, it offers a mechanism-driven, function-defined, engineering-enabled, and clinically accessible roadmap for next-generation regenerative medicine.

title: Cellular and spatial continuum of TAM functional states governs immune exclusion and dictates immune checkpoint resistance in melanoma.
authorString: Chakraborty S, Corrales E, Godbole I, Madkhali N, Das T, Krolla C, Nystrom A, Meiss F, Rafei D, Bengsch B, Andrieux G, Boerries M.
abstractText:
Background

Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy has transformed melanoma treatment, yet many patients either fail to respond or develop resistance after an initial response. The cellular and spatial determinants within the tumor microenvironment (TME) that underlie these divergent ICI therapy outcomes remain poorly defined. Here, we aimed to characterize the immune composition and spatial organization of the TME associated with ICI response and resistance.

Methods

We integrated public scRNA-seq data (N = 32) with in-house spatial transcriptomics and imaging mass cytometry from an independent melanoma cohort (N = 6) to achieve high-resolution spatial profiling of the TME. This multimodal approach allowed us to map cellular heterogeneity within discrete spatial neighborhoods. To validate our findings, we constructed a scRNA-seq derived signature-matrix and deconvoluted a bulk RNA-seq cohort (N = 334). Clinical associations were assessed using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, Cox hazard models, and a machine-learning classifier.

Results

We identified a distinct tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) state, termed lipid-associated TAMs (LA-TAMs), characterized by conserved lipid metabolic programs and tumor-specific adaptations in glycolysis under hypoxic conditions. Deep spatial multi-omics profiling revealed divergent immune architectures associated with treatment outcomes. In non-responder patients, LA-TAMs colocalized with sparsely distributed TIM3⁺ exhausted CD8⁺ T cells within an immune-excluded TME. In contrast, responder patients harbored interferon-primed CCL4+ TAMs (IFN-TAMs) spatially associated with Granzyme B⁺ activated CD8⁺ T cells, reflecting an immune-active microenvironment. These findings define contrasting macrophage-centered immune neighborhoods linked to ICI response. Interestingly, patients with LA-TAM-enriched neighborhoods were consistently non-responders or progressed during follow-up, irrespective of the presence of IFN-TAM neighborhoods. Lastly, we constructed a single-cell-derived signature matrix that estimates TAM fractions from bulk RNA-seq data and revealed LA-TAM abundance as a robust, independent predictor of poor ICI response and survival in a validation cohort.

Conclusions

Our study defines the spatial landscapes of TAM-heterogeneity in melanoma and identifies LA-TAM neighborhoods as an important feature of ICI resistance. Although patients span a continuum of TAM-centered immune states, the presence of LA-TAM is likely to diminish the beneficial effects of IFN-TAM-associated immune activation. Finally, our proposed Melanoma-TME-derived signature-matrix provides a translatable framework to robustly predict ICI response and resistance.

title: The Bicuspid Aortic Valve Within the Therapeutic Window of Cannabis, Tryptamines, and Novel Neuroplastogen Analogs: A Mechanistic Risk Analysis Anchored to a Reconstructed openSNP Genotype Cohort
authorString: Henry P.
abstractText: Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) is the most common congenital cardiac malformation and converts the aortic valve and proximal aorta into unusually vulnerable target tissues: a calcification-prone valve seated in front of an aneurysm-prone media governed by transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) signalling and nitric oxide (NO) homeostasis. We ask where the therapeutic windows of three expanding drug classes — cannabis, tryptamines (psilocybin/psilocin, DMT, 5-MeO-DMT), and non-hallucinogenic neuroplastogen analogues — sit relative to that vulnerability. We integrate receptor pharmacology (CB1/CB2; 5-HT2A/5-HT2B; biased agonism), exposure patterns separating macrodose from microdose regimens, and the convergent effector pathways through which each class could plausibly interact with BAV disease, and we anchor the analysis to a reconstructed genetic resource: the complete archived openSNP phenotype-361 (“Bicuspid aortic valve”) cohort (22 members; 19 with recoverable genotypes across a 17-SNP panel), rebuilt from Internet Archive holdings after the platform closed in April 2025. We propose that the three classes threaten BAV through separable doors — cannabis hemodynamically and vasculopathically, tryptamines through 5-HT2B-mediated valvular fibrosis, and neuroplastogen analogues, by medicinal-chemistry design, through neither — and that cumulative 5-HT2B receptor occupancy above endogenous tone, not binding affinity, is the operative risk variable. Descriptively, most genotyped cohort members carry at least one TGFB1 −509 variant allele and five of eight covered members carry a NOS3 −786C allele, demonstrating that the substrate for pharmacogenomic interaction is common rather than rare. We close with an exposure × phenotype risk-stratification matrix and six falsifiable hypotheses for a registry-scale test. This is a hypothesis-generating mechanistic analysis, not clinical guidance.

title: A Network Pharmacology-Based Computational Workflow for Investigating Gut Microbiota Metabolites Associated with Coronary Atherosclerosis.
authorString: Li CH, Huang HQ, Chen XY, Chen XD, Xiao N, Yang YT, Shen XJ, Pan Y, Zhang L.
abstractText: The gut microbiota and its metabolites are closely associated with the pathogenesis of coronary atherosclerosis (CAS). However, a standardized computational pipeline for systematically integrating microbial, metabolite, and host target information remains lacking. Here, we established an integrative workflow combining multi-database mining, network pharmacology, and molecular docking to explore potential molecular links between gut microbial metabolites and CAS. Gut microbial metabolites and host target genes were retrieved from gutMGene, with additional metabolite targets predicted using SEA and SwissTargetPrediction. CAS-related targets were compiled from GEO, GeneCards, CTD, OMIM, and Open Targets. Multi-level intersection analysis yielded candidate targets, followed by construction of a GUT-TARGET-CAS network. Protein-protein interaction networks were analyzed via STRING and Cytoscape, and a Microbiota-Substrate-Metabolite-Target (M-S-M-T) network was built. Functional and disease enrichment analyses (GO, KEGG, and Disease Ontology) were performed, and drug-likeness and toxicity of candidate metabolites were assessed using SwissADME and ADMETlab 3.0. Finally, CB-Dock2 was employed to evaluate predicted structural compatibility between candidate metabolites and highly connected targets. Representative analysis identified 226 gut microbial metabolites, 1,518 predicted metabolite targets, and 2,462 CAS-related targets, from which 52 candidate targets were prioritized. The PPI network prioritized TNF, IL6, AKT1, TP53, IL1B, and PPARG as highly connected targets. The M-S-M-T network linked these targets with 53 metabolites, 33 substrates, and 82 gut microbial taxa; all edges represent database-derived associations rather than proven causal regulatory relationships. Lipinski-type physicochemical criteria and ADMET (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity) predictions were used as a developability-oriented prioritization step, whereas docking scores were used only for internal candidate ranking. This computational framework enables systematic integration of gut microbiota-metabolite-host target information and prioritizes candidate metabolites and molecular targets for subsequent experimental validation.

title: ALDH4A1 and anti-ALDH4A1 emerge as a novel antigenic axis linked to atherosclerosis in rheumatoid arthritis.
authorString: Miranda-Prieto D, Alperi-López M, Pérez-Álvarez ÁI, Coras R, Alonso-Castro S, Amigó N, Guma M, Suárez A, Rodríguez-Carrio J.
abstractText:
Objective

Cardiovascular risk excess in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) cannot be explained by traditional risk factors alone. Recent experimental data have identified ALDH4A1 as a mitochondrial self-antigen implicated in atherosclerosis, yet its clinical significance in human autoimmunity remains unexplored. We aimed to characterize ALDH4A1 and anti-ALDH4A1 antibody levels in early RA, and evaluate their associations with atherosclerosis burden and lipoprotein traits.

Methods

ALDH4A1 and anti-ALDH4A1 antibodies (IgM, IgG, IgA, and IgG subclasses) were measured in early RA (n = 82), clinically suspect arthralgia (n = 14), healthy controls (n = 70), and a validation cohort of established RA. A prospective cohort (n = 13) explored therapeutic modulation under TNF blockade. Associations with atherosclerosis burden, lipid/lipoprotein profiles, oxylipin signatures, proteomics, and cell-free DNA were assessed.

Results

ALDH4A1 serum levels were associated with apoptotic-related proteomic pathways, cell-free DNA and lipidomic signatures in early RA. Reduced anti-ALDH4A1 antibodies were found, although divergent patters were noted across isotypes. These differences were confirmed in a validation cohort. IgG (predominantly IgG3) anti-ALDH4A1 correlated with favourable lipoprotein traits and cardiometabolic risk factors. Increased ALDH4A1 and reduced IgM/IgG anti-ALDH4A1 antibodies independently predicted atherosclerosis and improved risk stratification beyond mSCORE, most notably for IgG. ALDH4A1 tracked with TNF dynamics under TNF blockade, whereas increases in IgG antibodies occurred in responders and paralleled changes in lipoprotein features.

Conclusions

The ALDH4A1/anti-ALDH4A1 axis emerges as a novel player bridging lipid disturbances and atherosclerosis along the whole RA continuum, hence highlighting the involvement of mitochondrial targets. These components hold promise as functional players, clinical tools and therapeutic targets.

title: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy With Superimposed Pre-Eclampsia in a Grand Multiparous Woman.
authorString: Boahene PY, Ampofo BK, Gyabaah S, Tembila RN, Opare-Addo KA, Akowuah EA, Appiah LT, Kokuro C.
abstractText: This case report highlights the importance of clinical vigilance, the role of echocardiography, and the benefits of guideline-directed multidisciplinary management of pregnant women with HCM in resource-limited settings. Advocating for comprehensive multidisciplinary care models is essential in optimizing maternal and fetal health outcomes among pregnant women with cardiac pathologies.

title: GATA2 Deficiency Presenting With a WHIM-Like Phenotype and Subsequent Development of Monosomy 7-Associated Myelodysplastic Syndrome in an Adolescent Female: A Case Report.
authorString: Eghbali A, Poortavakol M, Mirmohammadi HS.
abstractText: We report an 18-year-old female with GATA2 deficiency presenting with a WHIM-like phenotype, including pancytopenia, monocytopenia, CD19<sup>+</sup> B-cell depletion, sensorineural hearing loss, and cutaneous warts. Subsequent cytogenetic evaluation revealed monosomy 7 and 7q22 deletion, with bone marrow progression to MDS. She was treated with azacitidine and referred for allogeneic HSCT.

title: Coinfections With Respiratory Syncytial Virus in a Cohort of Adults With High-Risk Conditions, 2015-2020: A Retrospective Observational Study.
authorString: Alonge OD, Sundaram ME, Nguyen HQ, King JP, Stefanski E, Allmon AG, Pirçon JY, Saeedi P.
abstractText: Coinfections may influence the clinical outcome of respiratory illness. Data are limited regarding RSV coinfections in adults with high-risk conditions. Residual respiratory specimens from community-dwelling adults (≥ 18 years) with ≥ 1 high-risk condition were retested using a multiplex panel for multiple viral pathogens. We compared demographic and clinical characteristics between those with RSV coinfection versus RSV single infection. RSV coinfections comprised 5.9% of all RSV infections among adults with ≥ 1 high-risk condition. No statistically significant differences were observed between those with RSV coinfections and single infections according to presence of specific high-risk conditions or clinical disease presentation.

title: Rapidly Progressing Interstitial Fibrosis and Glomerulonephritis due to Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis Presenting With Calf Pain.
authorString: Gupta Allison L, Wang Y, Chen E.
abstractText: We describe a 51-year-old male presenting with bilateral calf pain and found to have rapidly progressing pulmonary-renal syndrome due to GPA vasculitis, despite completing an empiric course of steroids for a gout flare. This case underscores the heterogeneous nature of GPA and the importance of early strong immunosuppressive therapy.

title: Evaluation of Mitral Regurgitation: Comparison of Ultrafast and Focused Ultrasound in an In-Vitro Pulsatile Flow Phantom.
authorString: Buffle E, Ouaret RA, Leroy H, Zhang G, Caudoux M, Baranger J, Baron I, Esclozas G, Stucki M, Papadacci C, Messas E, Puscas T, Aissaoui N, Houdouin A, Mousseaux E, Soulat G, Pernot M.
abstractText:
Objective

Mitral regurgitation (MR) severity is assessed by measuring the regurgitant volume (RVol) with echocardiography using the proximal iso-velocity surface area (PISA) method. The low temporal resolution of focused ultrasound, the assumption of hemispheric iso-velocity contours, and the use of a single point to assess the velocity are the pitfalls of this method. This study evaluates a novel method using ultrafast ultrasound, and multiple points for velocity assessment without the aforementioned geometrical assumption to provide a more accurate RVol measurement.

Methods

A left heart mock system, comprised of an orifice simulating MR, was filled with water mixed with cellulose. RVols from 20 mL to 70 mL with increments of 10 mL, were delivered by a pulsatile pump which was the reference. Data were acquired at 6000 frames/s by a cardiac phased array probe emitting ultrafast diverging waves, connected to an ultrafast scanner as well as a clinical system emitting focused waves. RVols were computed with the surface integral of the velocity through a planar disk at the input of the orifice with ultrafast transmission (u-PD) and PISA method with focused waves (f-PISA). The error of the two methods was compared.

Results

u-PD showed a significant lower error values than f-PISA (18.6 ± 11.5% and 56.5 ± 4.9%, respectively, p < 0.001).

Conclusion

This study demonstrates that ultrafast ultrasound can provide accurate multi-point estimates of RVol in a model of MR by leveraging the complete axial velocity mapping at high temporal resolution. Its complementary role to PISA method will be evaluated in future clinical studies.

title: Aromatic profiles and 15-LOX inhibitory effects of Australian and New Zealand Manuka honeys.
authorString: Moore G, Boufridi A, Russell F, Brooks P.
abstractText: Manuka (Leptospermum) honeys from Australia (Aust) and New Zealand (NZ) contain high levels of aromatic compounds, though only a subset are true phenolics in that they contain a hydroxyl group attached to an aromatic ring. Consequently, the traditional Folin-Ciocalteu Total Phenolic Content (FC-TPC) assay fails to detect many non-phenolic aromatic compounds that may confer health benefits. This paper quantified both phenolic and non-phenolic aromatic compounds in monofloral manuka honeys using high-performance liquid chromatography with diode array detection (HPLC-DAD) and the FC-TPC assay. In addition, this study evaluated the capacity of the honeys to inhibit 15-lipoxygenase (15-LOX), an enzyme that causes peroxidation of long chain polyunsaturated fatty acids. Australian (n = 7) and New Zealand (n = 6) Leptospermum scoparium (L. scoparium) honeys showed the highest total aromatic concentrations by HPLC-DAD (>2100 mg/kg), significantly exceeding those of L. liversidgei (n = 5), L. whitei (n = 5), and L. speciosum (n = 3) honeys. The FC-TPC assay identified higher phenolic levels in L. scoparium and L. polygalifolium honeys than in the other species studied. Sugar free Australian and New Zealand manuka honey aromatic extracts were potent inhibitors of 15-LOX enzyme, with IC50 values recorded at <15% of stock solutions (total extractables from 20.0 g of honey dissolved in 1.0 mL of 50% aqueous ethanol). Australian (IC50, 13.2 ± 0.7%) and New Zealand (13.1 ± 1.9%) L. scoparium honeys were more potent in inhibiting 15-LOX than L. liversidgei (IC50, 37.5 ± 6.3%) and L. speciosum (IC50, 36.6 ± 10.5%). Overall, this study demonstrates that HPLC-DAD provides a more comprehensive assessment of aromatic compounds in manuka honey than the FC-TPC assay and highlights the potential contribution of these compounds to anti-inflammatory activity.

title: Unveiling the neuroinflammatory potential of aspartame in Alzheimer's disease: A comprehensive network toxicology and experimental validation approach.
authorString: Li D, Weng X, Huang Y, Yang D, Yao S, Zheng W, Jiang X, Wei Y, Xu S, Wei C.
abstractText: Aspartame, a widely used artificial sweetener, has raised significant concerns regarding its safety, especially in light of the rising incidence of Alzheimer's Disease (AD). However, systematic investigations into aspartame's potential neurotoxicity and its role in AD pathology remain limited. In this study, we employed an integrated approach combining network toxicology predictions, molecular docking, and in vitro validation to explore the neurotoxic mechanisms of aspartame in AD. By analyzing multiple public databases through network toxicology, we identified 185 common targets between aspartame and AD. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis further highlighted 10 core hub genes, including KDR, CCNE1, and GSK-3β. Molecular docking predicted favorable interactions for key targets such as GSK-3β (-5.002 kcal/mol) and KDR (-5.613 kcal/mol), with other hubs showing moderate binding affinities. In vitro experiments demonstrated that aspartame dose-dependently reduced BV2 microglial cell viability and triggered a pro-inflammatory response. Specifically, aspartame increased the production of nitric oxide (NO) and pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6), while upregulating the expression of GSK-3β, iNOS, TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6, similar to LPS-induced inflammation. These findings suggest that aspartame may induce a pro-inflammatory response in BV2 microglial cells through multiple signaling pathways, although the relevance of these findings to human neurological safety remains to be established. This study provides a basis for further investigation into the neurological safety of aspartame and proposes a novel paradigm for evaluating the neurotoxic potential of food additives using an integrated systems toxicology approach.

title: Complete Surgical Resection of Rare Solitary Anterior Mediastinal Metastasis From Ovarian Clear Cell Carcinoma.
authorString: Chiba T, Yano K, Imoto T, Suzuki M, Shimizu R, Hishima T, Nakagawa K.
abstractText: Epithelial ovarian cancer typically spreads via transcoelomic dissemination and lymphatic pathways. Extra-abdominal metastases presenting as solitary anterior mediastinal lesions are rare. Ovarian clear cell carcinoma (CCC) is characterized by aggressive local behaviour but has a lower propensity for distant metastasis than serous carcinoma. Furthermore, it is less sensitive to platinum-based chemotherapy than other epithelial ovarian cancers. Here, we report a rare case of ovarian CCC with a solitary anterior mediastinal metastasis after primary surgery. A woman in her 50s had a 2.6-cm anterior mediastinal mass during postoperative surveillance. Considering progressive lesion enlargement and increased 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose uptake on positron emission tomography-computed tomography, complete surgical resection via median sternotomy was performed. Histopathological and immunohistochemical findings confirmed the presence of metastatic ovarian CCC. The patient remained disease-free for 6 months postoperatively. Complete surgical resection may represent an effective treatment option for isolated recurrence of chemoresistant histological subtypes.

title: Knockdown of fibrillarin reveals cell- and virus-dependent restriction of henipavirus replication and enhanced antiviral immune signalling
authorString: Sathiqu RM, Rootes CL, Brice AM, Caputo AT, Williams SM, Rodrigues CHM, Farr RJ, Alexander MR, Stewart CR.
abstractText:
ABSTRACT

The henipavirus genus includes several highly pathogenic zoonotic viruses that lack medical countermeasures. The 2’-O-methyltransferase fibrillarin (FBL) has been identified by genome-wide functional genomics studies as a henipavirus pro-viral factor. While FBL is a potential target for host-directed antiviral therapeutics, its impact on henipavirus replication in cell types relevant to henipavirus disease has not been explored. Here we demonstrate that depleting cellular FBL using short interfering RNAs (siRNAs) has varying impacts on henipavirus replication, depending on cell type and virus. FBL depletion in small airway epithelial cells (HSAEC1-KT) significantly impaired viral gene transcription for Hendra virus (HeV) genotypes 1 and 2 (HeV-g1, HeV-g2), and Nipah virus (NiV) Bangladesh strain (NiV-B), but not NiV Malaysia (NiV-M) strain or Cedar virus (CedV). Conversely, reduced FBL expression in bronchial epithelial (NuLi-1) cells, aortic endothelial (Telo HAEC) cells or neuroblastoma (BE(2)-M17) cells did not inhibit HeV-g1 replication. Transcriptomic analyses revealed that impaired virus replication in FBL knockdown cells was associated with enhanced activation of innate immune pathways and robust upregulation of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs). Together, these findings demonstrate a virus- and cell-type dependent impact of FBL on henipavirus replication and support a role for FBL in modulation of the antiviral innate immune response.

title: Severe Doxycycline-Induced Oesophagitis With Granulomatous Inflammation Managed in a Rural Australian Hospital: A Case Report.
authorString: Zou MHT, Chin X, Ng JY.
abstractText: Pill-induced oesophageal injury or pill oesophagitis typically presents with acute retrosternal pain, odynophagia, and dysphagia. While often self-limiting, cases may mimic acute coronary syndrome, food bolus, oesophageal perforation, and mediastinitis. Doxycycline is among the most commonly implicated medications. We report the case of a 32-year-old woman with severe mid-oesophageal ulceration secondary to doxycycline commenced for rosacea, managed at a rural Australian hospital. The histopathology finding of granulomatous inflammation was deemed reactive and secondary to severe ulceration, in the absence of infection or sarcoidosis. The patient was treated supportively with complete clinical and endoscopic resolution. Clinicians should consider pill oesophagitis in patients with acute retrosternal pain and odynophagia after starting doxycycline, and conservative management can be successful.

title: Click-chemistry targeting of inflammation using NIR-emitting lanthanide nanoparticles with preserved optical functionality.
authorString: Didonè L, Qiu D, Gutiérrez González P, Román-Carmena M, Martín Rodríguez E, Rubio Retama J, Iglesias-de la Cruz MC, Ortgies DH, Jaque D, Granado M, Artiga Á.
abstractText: Bioorthogonal click chemistry was employed for the selective detection of VCAM-1 overexpression on inflamed endothelial cells using lanthanide-doped nanoparticles as near-infrared (NIR) probes. Neodymium/Ytterbium co-doped nanoparticles exhibited efficient and specific targeting following bioorthogonal conjugation, while preserving their characteristic NIR emission profile and thermal sensing capabilities. These results demonstrate the potential of this strategy for the selective recognition of inflammatory biomarkers without compromising the optical performance of the nanoprobes, paving the way for multifunctional platforms for inflammation imaging and nanothermometry.

title: Magnetically Actuated Continuum Robots: From Engineering to Clinical Translation.
authorString: Yang Z, Jiao Y, Niu M, Cui Y, Yang L, Xu Q, Zhang L.
abstractText: Magnetically actuated continuum robots (MACRs) have emerged as a promising approach for minimally invasive surgery. By using external magnetic fields to apply torques and forces at the instrument tip, MACRs move actuation outside the patient, thus reducing the mechanical complexity of the robot. This architecture enables miniaturization, improved compliance, and improved steering capabilities, especially for navigating intricate intravascular or endoluminal pathways. Despite substantial progress in functional materials, robotic archetypes, and magnetic field generation platforms, effective clinical translation requires holistic consideration of surgical workflows, intraoperative localization, and operator interaction. Integrating these engineering advances into routine clinical practice remains an ongoing challenge. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of recent advances in MACRs from a clinical perspective, highlighting technologies that accelerate their translation into minimally invasive surgery. The fundamental working principles of MACRs are first outlined, followed by a task- driven categorization of robotic designs. The emerging strategies for intraoperative localization and motion control at varying levels of autonomy are then evaluated. Furthermore, representative applications across physiological systems are summarized. Finally, key challenges are highlighted to elucidate current technological boundaries and provide a roadmap for future research.

title: Vasomechanic treatment is associated with increased efflux of human brain proteins.
authorString: Tuunanen J, Hautamäki K, Väyrynen T, Järvelä M, Korhonen V, Huotari N, Kaakinen M, Kananen J, Helakari H, Raitamaa L, Jukkola J, Herukka SK, Laurén K, Salmi U, Eklund L, Nikkinen J, Nedergaard M, Kiviniemi V.
abstractText: An age-related neurovascular impairment in nitric oxide (NO)-mediated vasodilation and reciprocal Piezo1-dependent vascular vasoconstriction may precede the accumulation of soluble brain proteins such as amyloid-β (Aβ) and disruption of brain fluid homeostasis in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Preclinical studies suggest that restoring these pathways can enhance neurofluid transport and improve cognitive outcomes. In this study (EudraCT 2021-000625-27), we investigated the effects of sublingual NO and Piezo1-targeted whole-body vibrations (WBV<sub>p</sub>) in healthy adults (n = 29) using multimodal neuroimaging and blood biomarker analysis. The combined intervention (NO+WBV<sub>p</sub>) was associated with correlating changes in brain fluid dynamics and increased blood levels of soluble brain-derived proteins (Aβ<sub>40&42</sub>, GFAP). These effects increased with age and the magnitude of NO-induced hypotension. The interventions were well tolerated under controlled experimental conditions. Overall, the findings are consistent with transient redistribution of brain-derived proteins toward circulation, suggesting a potential non-invasive approach to increase neurofluidic solute efflux in humans. Pre-specified primary endpoints, changes in circulating brain-derived protein concentrations, brain fluid imaging and brain pulsation measures, were met. Secondary outcomes included physiological analyses.

title: Maternal cardiac and perinatal outcomes among pregnant individuals with tetralogy of Fallot.
authorString: Patel R, Singer A, Gentile B, Kovell L, Wilkie G.
abstractText:
Background

Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) is associated with maternal-fetal risks during pregnancy, particularly in those with uncorrected or residual defects.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study identified pregnancies with TOF and compared them with pregnancies with other congenital heart diseases (CHDs) using ICD-10 codes, between 5/23/22 and 5/22/25. Demographic and clinical characteristics were analyzed using analysis of variance or Student's t-tests for continuous variables and chi-square tests for categorical variables.

Results

There were 1574 women (1961 pregnancies) with TOF compared to 37,899 women (47,239 pregnancies) with other CHD. Significant differences in cardiac outcomes were observed in arrhythmias (32.9% vs. 18.3%), particularly ventricular arrhythmias (6.8% vs. 2.1%) and endocarditis (2.4% vs. 1.5%). Significant perinatal outcomes included preterm delivery (17% vs. 14.1%) and earlier gestational age at delivery (37.4 ± 3 vs. 38.9 ± 1.7).

Conclusions

Pregnancies with TOF have a greater occurrence of adverse cardiac outcomes, particularly arrhythmias and endocarditis, and obstetric outcomes, including preterm delivery.

title: FGFBPs in health and tumors: emerging prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic implications.
authorString: Xia J, Xiao Y, Li Y, Zhao H.
abstractText: The fibroblast growth factor (FGF)/FGF receptor (FGFR) signaling pathway is essential for maintaining physiological homeostasis, and its dysregulation is implicated in the pathogenesis of numerous diseases. FGF-binding proteins (FGFBPs) constitute a family of secreted proteins that modulate the bioavailability of FGF ligands, thereby fine-tuning FGF signaling output in a context-specific manner. Emerging evidence indicates that FGFBPs regulate diverse physiological processes, including embryonic development, tissue repair, and metabolic homeostasis, while dysregulation of these members is closely associated with various diseases, particularly malignancies. Nevertheless, their precise functional roles in physiological homeostasis and oncogenesis, as well as the underlying molecular mechanisms governing these functions, remain incompletely characterized. This review systematically summarizes the physiological functions of FGFBPs, with a focused analysis of their context-dependent roles in diverse types of cancer. We further discuss their emerging potential as prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic implications. A deeper mechanistic understanding of FGFBPs is expected to advance insights into the molecular underpinnings of both physiological homeostasis and tumorigenesis, thereby informing the rational development of novel diagnostic biomarkers and precise therapeutic intervention strategies.
