title: The Latest Progress in the Application of Tofacitinib in Rheumatic Diseases--A Narrative Review.
authorString: Liu B, Liu Q, Zhao X.
abstractText: Tofacitinib is an oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor that modulates cytokine-dependent JAK/STAT signaling and has been extensively investigated in rheumatic diseases. This narrative review provides an updated synthesis of the pharmacological characteristics, mechanisms of action, clinical efficacy, safety, drug-drug interactions and dosing considerations of tofacitinib in special populations. The relevant literature published from January 2013 through December 2025 was identified through searches of MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar, supplemented by manual screening of reference lists. After screening and eligibility assessment, 89 clinical publications were included in the disease-specific evidence synthesis, and the strength of clinical evidence across disease indications was evaluated qualitatively. The most robust evidence is available for rheumatoid arthritis, with randomized trials, long-term extension studies, and real-world investigations demonstrating improvements in disease activity and physical function and inhibition of radiographic progression. Clinical evidence also supports therapeutic benefit in psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, and juvenile idiopathic arthritis, whereas evidence for Takayasu arteritis, polymyalgia rheumatica, systemic lupus erythematosus, and anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis-associated interstitial lung disease remains limited or exploratory. Long-term integrated safety analyses in RA have reported incidence rates of serious adverse events of approximately 9.0-9.4 per 100 patient-years and serious infections of approximately 2.5-2.7 per 100 patient-years, while herpes zoster, major adverse cardiovascular events, venous thromboembolism, and malignancy remain clinically important safety considerations. Potential drug-drug interactions and dose adjustment in patients with renal or hepatic impairment and other special populations further require individualized assessment. Overall, tofacitinib has a well-established role in RA treatment and potential therapeutic value in several other rheumatic diseases; however, its use should be guided by disease-specific evidence, previous treatment exposure, comorbidities, concomitant medications, and individual safety risks. Further prospective and long-term studies are needed to better define its role in less well-established indications and special populations.

title: Paradoxical ethnic differences in prevalence of vascular risk factors versus extracranial atherosclerotic disease in TIA/stroke patients in the United Kingdom: Population-based study and meta-analysis.
authorString: Kamtchum-Tatuene J, Li L, Rothwell PM.
abstractText:
Background

Studies in Northern America report a lower prevalence of coronary artery disease (CAD) in Black than White people despite higher prevalence of vascular risk factors. However, it remains unclear to what extent these differences are driven by biology or reflect ethnic disparities in smoking, socioeconomic deprivation, healthcare access, and health-seeking behaviour. We aimed to determine if ethnic differences in coronary and peripheral artery disease persist in people with stroke living in the United Kingdom (UK), considering that most people with stroke seek medical attention and the National Health Service provides equitable access to care.

Methods

In a prospective population-based cohort of all patients with suspected TIA or stroke in Oxfordshire, UK (Oxford Vascular Study, OxVasc, April 2002 to March 2023), we fitted multivariable logistic regression models to quantify the association of ethnicity and extracranial atherosclerotic disease (coronary or peripheral) while adjusting for age, sex, vascular risk factors, and socioeconomic deprivation. We verified our findings in a systematic review of UK-based studies reporting prevalence of extracranial atherosclerotic disease and associated vascular risk factors across ethnic groups. Prevalence estimates were pooled by random-effects meta-analysis.

Results

In 7297 OxVasc participants (52.6% women, 71.0 ± 15.5 years), non-White people (n = 335) had a higher prevalence of diabetes mellitus (OR = 3.26, 2.55-4.16). However, Black people had a lower prevalence of CAD (OR = 0.31, 0.10-0.98, p = 0.046) or any extracranial atherosclerotic disease (OR = 0.42, 0.18-0.96, p = 0.04) than White people. After adjustment for age, sex, vascular risk factors, and deprivation, the difference was attenuated both for CAD (aOR = 0.50, 0.18-1.41, p = 0.19) and any extracranial atherosclerotic disease (aOR = 0.43, 0.18-1.04, p = 0.06). Asian and White people had similar prevalence of CAD and extracranial atherosclerotic disease. Among UK-based studies of patients with stroke, Black and Asian people were more likely than White people to have diabetes (pooled OR: 2.78, 2.40-3.22, n = 3 studies; 4.15, 3.11-5.53 n = 6), hypertension (1.95, 1.47-2.60, n = 3; 1.47, 1.02-2.12, n = 6), and obesity (1.52, 1.27-1.83, n = 1; 1.2, 0.66-2.29, n = 3) but less likely to be smoking (0.70, 0.50-0.97, n = 2; 0.57, 0.44-0.74, n = 5). Yet, Black people had less CAD than White (0.48, 0.31-0.76, n = 3) and Asian (0.30, 0.10-0.80, n = 2) people.

Interpretation

We confirm the existence of a coronary artery disease paradox in Black but not Asian people with TIA or stroke, which is likely independent of biases in healthcare access or health-seeking behaviour, and may suggest different biological susceptibilities.

title: Structural and Process Factors Associated with 30-Day Postoperative Complication Severity After Open-Heart Surgery: A Single-Center Observational Study.
authorString: Nakkhamhaeng S, Utriyaprasit K, Tankumpuan T, Wanitkun N, Tocharoenchok T.
abstractText:
Background

Open-heart surgery is associated with substantial postoperative morbidity. Guided by the Nursing Role Effectiveness Model, this study focused on the severity of 30-day postoperative complications rather than only the presence or absence of complications.

Purpose

The study examined structural factors (health literacy, nutritional status, severity of comorbidities, anemia, and surgical mortality risk) and process factors (perception of patient-centered care, type of surgery, and cardiopulmonary bypass time) associated with complication severity after open-heart surgery.

Patients and methods

A prospective, single-center observational prognostic factor study with medical record review was conducted from June 2022 to July 2023 among 136 adult patients undergoing open-heart surgery at a tertiary hospital in Thailand. Data were collected from patient questionnaires and medical records. The primary outcome was 30-day complication severity measured using the Comprehensive Complication Index. Bivariate analyses and multiple linear regression were performed, with prespecified covariates selected based on clinical relevance.

Results

Participants had a mean age of 61.32 years (SD = 13.09), and 61.8% were male. The mean Comprehensive Complication Index score was 37.25 (SD = 14.70). In the adjusted model, surgical mortality risk (standardized beta = 0.345, p < 0.001), anemia (standardized beta = 0.224, p = 0.018), nutritional status (standardized beta = -0.218, p = 0.011), and cardiopulmonary bypass time (standardized beta = 0.198, p = 0.034) were independently associated with complication severity. Health literacy, comorbidity severity, and perceived patient-centered care were not statistically significant.

Conclusion

Surgical mortality risk, anemia, nutritional status, and cardiopulmonary bypass time were key factors associated with 30-day complication severity. These findings support preoperative optimization of hematological and nutritional status and careful intraoperative management to reduce postoperative morbidity; however, interpretation should consider the single-center design and available covariates.

title: Ischemic Stroke as the Initial Presentation of an Underlying Neuroinfectious Disease.
authorString: Sehmbi G, Abbas M, Patel M, Hassan A, Jamali R.
abstractText: Neuroinfectious cerebral vasculitis is a rare but potentially underrecognized cause of ischemic stroke. Its clinical and neuroimaging features may closely mimic those of common cerebrovascular disorders, posing a diagnostic challenge. We describe two patients who presented with ischemic stroke, one with an atypical presentation and the other with recurrent episodes, in whom advanced neuroimaging and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis were pivotal in establishing the diagnosis. A 55-year-old man presented with a two-month history of nonfocal symptoms and was found to have a right posterior cerebral artery infarct with multifocal intracranial stenoses. Syphilis serology was positive in both blood and CSF. High-resolution magnetic resonance vessel wall imaging (HR-VWI) demonstrated multifocal vessel irregularities suggestive of inflammatory vasculopathy, although the initial clinical suspicion was ischemic stroke. A 48-year-old woman presented with recurrent posterior circulation strokes and progressively worsening neurological symptoms. HR-VWI again revealed vessel irregularities, prompting further investigation with CSF analysis, which identified herpes simplex virus 2 (HSV-2). These cases highlight the importance of considering neuroinfectious etiologies in patients presenting with unexplained, multifocal, or recurrent ischemic strokes. Advanced neuroimaging techniques, such as HR-VWI, may help identify intracranial vasculitic changes and prompt further targeted investigations, including CSF analysis, which is essential for establishing a neuroinfectious diagnosis. Given the potentially treatable nature of these conditions, early recognition and initiation of pathogen-specific therapy, supported by a multidisciplinary approach, are essential to optimizing clinical outcomes.

title: Angina in the young: a right coronary artery malignant course-a case report.
authorString: Omodara AB, Dawood K, Darwin S, Khokar A, Qureshi A.
abstractText:
Background

Coronary artery anomalies are rare congenital defects that often remain undetected due to their asymptomatic nature. However, in certain cases, they represent an important cause of sudden cardiac death, particularly among younger individuals with low to intermediate risk factors for coronary artery disease.

Case summary

We report the case of a 35-year-old woman who presented to the cardiology outpatient clinic with intermittent typical anginal chest pain. Despite having a low-to-moderate risk profile for ischaemic heart disease, limited to well-controlled hypertension and hypercholesterolaemia, further evaluation with computed tomographic coronary angiography revealed an anomalous right coronary artery originating from the left coronary sinus with a malignant course. An exercise stress echocardiogram demonstrated ischaemic electrocardiographic changes in the absence of physical symptoms. Her cardiovascular risk factors were managed with medications; however, due to evidence of inducible ischaemia, she was referred to a tertiary adult congenital heart disease centre for ongoing surveillance and consideration of appropriately timed surgical intervention.

Conclusion

Although rare, anomalous coronary artery disease may represent a significant cause of angina in younger patients. A thorough clinical history remains essential in identifying this condition and facilitating potentially life-saving management.

title: Drug Therapies and Incidence of Dementia Among Adults With Overactive Bladder.
authorString: Sheyn D, Rhodes S, Mohamed Z, Hijaz A.
abstractText:
Importance

Concern that anticholinergic medications for overactive bladder (OAB) are associated with increased dementia risk has encouraged a shift toward β3 adrenergic agonists, which are presumed cognitively safer. Whether this presumption is justified is uncertain.

Objective

To compare the risk of incident dementia among adults initiating high-risk anticholinergic, low-risk anticholinergic, or β3 agonist therapy for OAB and to evaluate the association of treatment duration with risk.

Design, setting, and participants

This retrospective cohort study used Epic Cosmos electronic health record data from 2012 to 2025. Adults aged 40 to 90 years newly treated for OAB within 1 year of diagnosis without preexisting dementia were included.

Exposures

First prescribed medication class: high-risk anticholinergics (oxybutynin, tolterodine, or solifenacin), low-risk anticholinergics (darifenacin, trospium, or fesoterodine), or β3 agonists (mirabegron or vibegron).

Main outcomes and measures

Incident dementia by diagnosis code or dementia-specific medication. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and Cox proportional hazards models were used, with analyses stratified by age and sex and an exploratory landmark duration-response analysis.

Results

Among 830 393 patients (585 198 female [70.5%]; median [IQR] age, 67 [57-76] years), incident dementia occurred in 65 134 patients, with a median (IQR) follow-up ranging from 1046 (571-1809) days for β3 agonists to 1568 (857-2614) days for high-risk anticholinergics. After IPTW, high-risk anticholinergics were associated with a lower hazard of dementia than β3 agonists (hazard ratio [HR], 0.90; 95% CI, 0.87-0.93) and low-risk anticholinergics (HR, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.90-0.96); low-risk anticholinergics did not differ from β3 agonists (HR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.93-1.01). Weighted 10-year dementia risk was highest for β3 agonists (20.0%; 95% CI, 18.8%-21.2%) and lowest for high-risk anticholinergics (18.1%; 95% CI, 17.9%-18.3%). E-values of 1.29 (high-risk anticholinergics vs β3 agonists) and 1.20 (high-risk vs low-risk anticholinergics) suggested that observed differences could be explained by a modest amount of unmeasured confounding. Longer anticholinergic duration was not associated with increased risk.

Conclusions and relevance

In this cohort study of patients undergoing treatment for OAB, β3 agonists were not associated with a lower dementia incidence compared with anticholinergics. These findings suggest that previously reported increases in risk may reflect residual confounding rather than a pharmacological effect.

title: NT-proBNP levels and arrhythmias in adolescents with chronic upper gastrointestinal diseases.
authorString: Shevchenko N, Krutenko N, Zimnytska T, Voloshyn K, Holovko T.

journal.title: Revista paulista de pediatria : orgao oficial da Sociedade de Pediatria de Sao Paulo

abstractText:
Objective

To assess plasma N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels in adolescents with chronic upper gastrointestinal diseases and investigate their association with 24-hour Holter electrocardiographic findings.

Methods

This cross-sectional study included 104 adolescents with endoscopically-verified chronic upper gastrointestinal diseases and 58 comparison adolescents without clinically-documented chronic gastrointestinal or cardiovascular disease. Both groups underwent 24-hour Holter electrocardiographic monitoring. NT-proBNP was measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay in 60 patients and 28 controls. Receiver operating characteristic analysis explored the ability of this biomarker to identify positive Holter findings, defined as rhythm, conduction, or repolarization abnormalities exceeding age-related physiological limits or requiring further cardiological evaluation.

Results

Positive Holter findings were observed in 71 patients (68.3%). Most findings were benign; potentially clinically significant abnormalities occurred in 11 patients (10.6% of all patients; 15.5% of those with positive Holter findings). Median NT-proBNP levels did not significantly differ between patients and controls but were higher in patients with cardiovascular complaints (53.0 42.5-85.0 versus 22.6 12.4-41.4 pg/mL; p=0.001) and positive Holter findings (50.0 32.2-70.5 versus 27.8 10.7-41.4 pg/mL; p<0.05). According to the receiver operating characteristic analysis for identifying positive Holter findings, we observed an area under the curve of 0.779 (95% confidence interval 95%CI: 0.726-0.833; p<0.001). An NT-proBNP cutoff value of ≥43.2 pg/mL showed 66.7% sensitivity and 90.9% specificity for identifying positive Holter findings.

Conclusions

Higher NT-proBNP levels were associated with positive Holter findings. Given the cross-sectional design and limited monitoring period, this association requires prospective validation.

title: Triple Total Coronary Occlusions in a Young Adult: Looking Beyond Conventional Atherosclerotic Risk Factors.
authorString: Naeem J, Begum NM, Amjad F.
abstractText: Severe coronary artery disease is uncommon in young adults, particularly when conventional cardiovascular risk factors are limited. We describe a 26-year-old man who presented with exertional chest pain and was found to have total occlusions affecting all three major coronary arteries. Extensive investigation for inherited, metabolic, autoimmune, and inflammatory causes did not identify a definitive aetiology. His history of heavy electronic-cigarette use and a prolonged febrile illness in childhood were considered potentially relevant but could not be established as causal. He ultimately underwent successful three-vessel coronary artery bypass grafting. This case highlights the importance of investigating unusual causes of severe premature coronary disease while avoiding over-attribution to unconfirmed risk factors.

title: Suspected Endomyocardial Fibrosis With Extensive Left Ventricular Thrombus: A Diagnostic Dilemma.
authorString: Mano Geran S, Burhani S, Sharma S, Hline AT.
abstractText: We report a case of a 64-year-old man with biventricular dysfunction and a large left ventricular (LV) thrombus in whom endomyocardial fibrosis (EMF) was suspected. Despite extensive evaluation for eosinophilic, autoimmune, infective, and haematological causes, no secondary aetiology was identified. He was managed with guideline-directed heart failure therapy and anticoagulation. His condition progressively deteriorated, and he died within a year, highlighting the diagnostic challenge of suspected EMF when characteristic imaging findings coexist with atypical features and definitive histological confirmation cannot be obtained, as well as the therapeutic challenges of this rare cardiomyopathy.

title: Pulmonary Vein Anatomy, Cooling Kinetics, and Recurrence After Cryoballoon Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation.
authorString: Yang KM, Hsiao HC, Yeh TC, Chiou CW, Hung JF, Chiang CH.
abstractText:
Background

Cryoballoon pulmonary vein isolation depends on balloon-to-ostium contact. We assessed whether computed tomography-derived pulmonary vein ostial area (OA) and ovality index (OI) were associated with cooling after accounting for pulmonary vein (PV) branch and within-patient clustering, and whether PV anatomy was associated with recurrence.

Methods

We retrospectively studied 120 patients with symptomatic atrial fibrillation undergoing second-generation cryoballoon ablation. Vein-level associations with nadir temperature, 1 min temperature, and time to isolation were assessed using linear mixed-effects models with a patient random intercept and PV branch as a fixed effect; generalized estimating equations served as sensitivity analyses. Given 23 post-blanking recurrences, logistic models were limited to left atrial volume index (LAVI) and one clinically selected covariate, with Firth-penalized regression as a sensitivity analysis.

Results

All patients achieved acute PV isolation. Larger OA was associated with lower nadir temperature (β = -0.583°C per 50 mm2; 95% CI, -0.910 to -0.257; p < 0.001) and 1 min temperature (β = -0.441°C per 50 mm2; 95% CI, -0.764 to -0.118; p = 0.008) after branch and clustering adjustment. OI was not associated with either temperature outcome. Twenty-three patients (19.2%) developed recurrent atrial arrhythmia. LAVI was associated with recurrence (adjusted OR, 1.659 per 10 mL/m2; 95% CI, 1.250-2.201; p < 0.001), whereas persistent AF was not.

Conclusions

OA showed a modest association with cryoballoon temperatures but should not be used as a stand-alone prognostic marker. LAVI remained associated with recurrence in parsimonious patient-level analyses.

title: Scimitar Syndrome in Adolescence.
authorString: Ing SK, Lee YH, Yip JMJ, Tan JGL, Ngu NH.
abstractText: Scimitar syndrome has infantile and childhood/adult variants. We describe an adolescent girl with recurrent wheeze in whom chest radiography and multimodality CT demonstrated the characteristic scimitar vein and associated bronchovascular abnormalities, with normal right ventricular function and no pulmonary hypertension.

title: Durable Complete Response to Pembrolizumab for Postoperative Nodal Recurrence of Lynch Syndrome-Associated Upper Tract Urothelial Carcinoma: A Case Report.
authorString: Atagi K, Yamamoto S, Shimizu N, Iguchi M, Shigehisa R, Nao T, Shimamoto T, Fukuhara H, Fukata S, Inoue K.
abstractText:
Introduction

Germline mutations in mismatch repair genes cause Lynch syndrome and are associated with upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC). Tumors with deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) or microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) may respond favorably to immune checkpoint inhibitors.

Case presentation

A 54-year-old woman with Lynch syndrome and a germline MSH2 mutation developed right renal pelvic carcinoma. The tumor was diagnosed as a pT3 high-grade urothelial carcinoma, and the patient underwent laparoscopic nephroureterectomy. She was subsequently administered adjuvant gemcitabine and carboplatin due to a contraindication for cisplatin. Due to nodal recurrence, pembrolizumab was initiated at 200 mg every 3 weeks, achieving a complete radiological and metabolic response after five cycles. The course was complicated by immune-related adrenal insufficiency, which was managed with corticosteroid replacement therapy.

Conclusion

Pembrolizumab may achieve a durable complete response in Lynch syndrome-associated UTUC. MSI screening should be considered in UTUC to guide decision-making.

title: Lycopene-loaded albumin nanoparticles developed by an ultrasound-driven assembly-emulsification method for parenteral nutrition.
authorString: Żółnowska I, Krajka-Kuźniak V, Adamek G, Belka M, Jadach B, Stawny M.
abstractText: Intestinal failure-associated liver disease (IFALD), a severe complication of parenteral nutrition (PN), remains difficult to prevent and treat. We hypothesized that the bioactive carotenoid lycopene could alleviate hepatocellular signaling disturbances involved in its pathogenesis. However, IFALD patients require intravenous nutrient administration; therefore, potential lycopene treatment would necessitate an appropriate delivery system to overcome its poor water solubility. In this study, we evaluated the biological activity of free lycopene in THLE-2 hepatocytes under IFALD-like conditions and developed lycopene-loaded human serum albumin nanoparticles (Lyc@AlbNPs) for PN supplementation. Lycopene attenuated MAPK- and NF-κB-related inflammatory signaling and modulated the expression of genes involved in cholesterol metabolism, including ABCA1, CYP7A1, and SREBF2. Lyc@AlbNPs were prepared by adding lycopene directly to the albumin solution rather than first dissolving it in an organic solvent, as required in typical methods for producing albumin nanoparticles. Initial lycopene-albumin assemblies formed during bath sonication; subsequent ultrasonic emulsification promoted their reorganization into smaller particles, yielding Lyc@AlbNPs with a mean size of 72.2 ± 3.1 nm, a polydispersity index of 0.265 ± 0.013, and lycopene loading of 9.42 ± 0.22 %. Thermal and diffraction analyses indicated disruption of the crystalline structure of lycopene during initial assembly formation. Lyc@AlbNPs were nonhemolytic and cytocompatible in THLE-2 cells. Five ready-to-use three-chamber PN bags were supplemented with Lyc@AlbNPs to assess potential interactions; all admixtures met the predefined compatibility criteria and remained stable for 24 h. These findings indicate that free lycopene modulates inflammatory and metabolism-related signaling in an in vitro IFALD model, while the albumin-based nanoformulation enables its addition to PN admixtures. The study also demonstrates an alternative formulation approach to incorporating poorly soluble compounds into albumin nanoparticles.

title: Vitamins E and C supplementation reduces hepatic lipid peroxidation and steatosis in neonatal Yucatan piglets receiving prolonged parenteral nutrition.
authorString: Kumarasinghe T, Khaled AS, Bertolo RF, Brunton JA.
abstractText: Parenteral nutrition (PN) is essential in neonatal care for many infants born prematurely or with impaired gastrointestinal function. However, prolonged PN use is associated with complications such as PN-associated liver disease and intestinal atrophy, potentially related to oxidative stress. Commercial PN lipid emulsions with fish oil are used to counteract PN-associated liver damage but may also contribute to oxidative stress due to their high content of long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids. Using neonatal Yucatan miniature piglets as an established animal model for investigating PN-associated complications in neonates, this study investigated whether co-supplementation of vitamins E and C could reduce oxidative stress-related injury in the liver and small intestine during PN. The objective of this study was to determine whether supplementing a mixed-lipid emulsion (SMOFlipid®) with vitamins E and C would attenuate hepatic oxidative damage and enhance intestinal perfusion and morphology in neonatal piglets. Neonatal Yucatan piglets were surgically fitted with intravenous catheters and an indwelling blood flow probe around the superior mesenteric artery (SMA). Piglets received either standard PN (Control; n = 10) or PN supplemented with vitamins E (10 mg/kg/d) and C (100 mg/kg/d) (Vit E&C, n = 10) for ten days. Vitamin supplementation was associated with lower hepatic lipid accumulation and lipid peroxidation (P < 0.05 for both), compared with the control group. Plasma and liver vitamin E concentrations were markedly higher in the Vit E&C group (P < 0.001 and P < 0.01, respectively). No differences were determined between groups in liver or plasma triglyceride and cholesterol levels, SMA blood flow, intestinal villus height, crypt depth, or overall intestinal morphology. Hepatic and intestinal protein synthesis rates and in vivo bile acid clearance were also not significantly different between groups. Co-supplementation of PN with vitamins E and C was associated with lower hepatic oxidative stress and steatosis in neonatal piglets. Although no improvements were measured in intestinal structure or perfusion, these findings support the potential of antioxidant-enriched PN formulations to mitigate PN-associated liver complications.
