title: Apigenin: Antihypertensive Effects and Underlying Mechanisms - A Comprehensive Review.
authorString: Liao X, Huang H, Cai J, Lu H, Li J, Li H, Jiang Y.
abstractText: Apigenin, a ubiquitous dietary flavone from vegetables, fruits and herbal teas, exhibits multi-target hypotensive effects, yet its poor water solubility limits oral bioavailability and industrial translation. Previous reviews only summarized its general bioactivities and anti-atherosclerotic effects, without comprehensively analyzing its antihypertensive mechanisms. Most evidence derives from preclinical studies; human trials merely use crude celery seed extracts instead of purified apigenin, lacking reliable clinical proof for its antihypertensive efficacy. This review summarizes apigenin's sources, chemical properties, safety and solubility-enhanced delivery systems to support functional food exploitation. We elaborate four core antihypertensive pathways, and also point out translational bottlenecks and propose strategies including food-grade nanoformulation and standardized clinical trials. This work links preclinical mechanisms to food industry application, providing theoretical evidence for developing apigenin-enriched functional foods for hypertension adjuvant intervention.

title: State of Art of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation for the Treatment of Aortic Stenosis in Low-Risk Patients: A Perspective on Brazilian Contributions and Implementation Challenges.
authorString: Saadi EK, Saadi RP, Tagliari AP.
abstractText: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has profoundly changed the management of severe aortic stenosis (AS), evolving from a treatment reserved for inoperable and high-risk patients to an established therapeutic option across a wide surgical risk spectrum. Although the expansion of TAVI indications has been largely supported by randomized clinical trials conducted in high-income countries, real-world experience and technological contributions from distinct healthcare systems are increasingly relevant. Brazil has played a significant role in the early adoption, structured implementation, and clinical evaluation of TAVI in Latin America. Since the first procedures performed in 2008, Brazilian centers have developed Heart Team models, contributed to national and regional registries, and generated real-world evidence demonstrating procedural safety and effectiveness comparable to international benchmarks, despite the presence of resource limitations and a higher prevalence of complex clinical and anatomical scenarios. The incorporation of TAVI into the Brazilian public health system in 2022 marked a major milestone in expanding access to minimally invasive therapy for patients with severe AS. In parallel, Brazilian scientific societies have adapted international guideline recommendations to local practice, supporting evidence-based patient selection across different surgical risk categories. Notably, Brazil has also emerged as a developer of locally engineered transcatheter valve technologies, highlighting its transition from a technology consumer to an active contributor in the field of structural heart disease. This review summarizes the historical evolution, national experience, clinical outcomes, guideline integration, technological innovation, and health economic considerations of TAVI in Brazil.

title: Comparison of anticoagulation efficacy and safety of different heparin dosages in cardiogenic shock patients supported by intra-aortic balloon pump: A retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Li Y, Yang W, Yu Y, Fan B, Dong H, Wang Y, Nie H, Hao Z, Wang Z, Niu X, Zhang D.
abstractText: The study aimed to evaluate whether a half-dose heparin flush strategy during intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) support improves safety compared with the standard-dose strategy in patients with cardiogenic shock (CS). In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 128 CS patients who received IABP support between January 2023 and December 2024 were included. Sixty-eight patients received a standard-dose heparin flush, and 60 received a half-dose flush. The primary endpoints were clinically relevant bleeding (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium 2, 3, or 5) and thrombocytopenia (platelet count < 100 × 109/L). Multivariable logistic regression was conducted, adjusting for dual antiplatelet therapy and renal dysfunction. The incidence of clinically significant bleeding events and thrombocytopenia was significantly lower in the half-dose group than in the standard-dose group (P < .05). Compared with the standard-dose group, the half-dose heparin flush strategy was significantly associated with a lower risk of clinically significant bleeding (odds ratio = 0.15; 95% confidence interval = 0.03-0.68). Among the secondary outcomes, the half-dose group had a significantly lower transfusion requirement than the standard-dose group (P < .001). No significant differences were observed between the 2 groups in activated partial thromboplastin time, activated clotting time, in-hospital mortality, or catheter-related occlusion events. In patients with CS receiving IABP support, the half-dose heparin flush strategy was associated with lower incidences of thrombocytopenia, clinical bleeding, and transfusion requirements. No device-related thrombotic events were observed in either group, suggesting that the half-dose heparin flush strategy may contribute to optimizing anticoagulation management during the peri-support period.

title: Coronary artery disease and cardiac pathology in cerebral small vessel disease and post-stroke dementia: Implications for Alzheimer's disease.
authorString: Hase Y, Polvikoski T, Jobson D, Premarion K, Tutter E, Kitajima E, Kalailingam P, Gallart-Palau X, Sze SK, Allan L, Kalaria RN.

journal.title: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association

abstractText:
Background

The relationships between coronary or cardiac pathology, cerebral small vessel disease (SVD), Alzheimer's disease pathology, and vascular cognitive impairment and dementia (VCID) remain unclear.

Methods

We performed a clinicopathological study in 75 stroke patients enrolled in the prospective Cognitive Function After Stroke (CogFAST) cohort. Comprehensive histopathological examination was performed to characterize the spectrum of pathologies in samples of the main coronary arteries (CorA), and cardiac and brain tissues from stroke survivors diagnosed with post-stroke dementia (PSD; mean age, standard deviation, range, % sex; 88 ± 8 years, 65-99, 55% female) or without dementia (PSND; 86 ± 4 years, 79-94, 45% female).

Results

All subjects exhibited occult or obstructive CorA disease with > 50% clinically defined stenosis in at least one of the main coronary arteries. Linear correlation analysis showed that CorA stenosis was positively related to internal carotid artery stenosis (P < 0.03). CorA stenosis was not associated with pathological measures of cerebral SVD per se or neurodegenerative disorders. Cardiac pathology was highly prevalent, with ≈ 80% of the subjects having at least one feature of cardiac pathology including fibrosis, disarray, and myocyte damage and 62% exhibiting myocardial infarcts. CorA stenosis was associated with higher cardiac pathology score, which was also related to cardiac sympathetic denervation and α-synuclein accumulation in the stellate ganglia. We noted low heart weights (P < 0.001), greater myocardial infarcts (P < 0.001), and greater general cardiac atrophy (P = 0.024) in the PSD compared to the PSND group.

Conclusions

Our findings suggest there is a relationship between CorA disease and carotid artery disease and that cardiac pathology in elderly stroke survivors may be a factor in the development of delayed dementia after the stroke injury and VCID.

title: Bloodstream Infections After Cardiac Surgery: Pathogen Distribution, Antimicrobial Resistance, and a Nomogram Prediction Model.
authorString: Miao S, Lu Y, Wang J, Zhang W, Xia W, Xu Y.
abstractText:
Background

Postoperative bloodstream infection (BSI) is a severe complication following cardiac surgery, associated with significant mortality. This study aims to characterize pathogen profiles, antimicrobial resistance and independent risk factors for BSI in a Chinese cardiac surgery cohort.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study of postoperative BSI in patients who underwent cardiac surgery at the First Affiliated Hospital of Nanjing Medical University from January 2019 to December 2024. Patients who developed postoperative BSI were identified and a 1:1 propensity score matched analysis were performed to adjust for baseline characteristics of patients. Univariate and multivariate analysis were applied to identify independent risk factors for postoperative BSI. R software was used to construct a prediction nomogram, followed by internal validation.

Results

During the study, a total of 10,007 patients underwent heart surgery, and 164 pairs of patients were successfully matched using propensity score matching. Gram-negative bacteria were the most common pathogens (64.1%), followed by Fungi (18.2%) and Gram-positive bacteria (17.6%). Among Enterobacterales, 33.8% were carbapenem-resistant, with carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) accounting for 63.6% of K. pneumoniae isolates. Meanwhile, 85.0% (17/20) of A. baumannii isolates were multidrug-resistant A. baumannii (MDRAB). The 90-day mortality rate in the BSI group was 39.0%, significantly higher than that in the non-BSI group (4.9%, P < 0.001). Multivariate logistic regression identified impaired cardiac function (New York Heart Association II-IV, NYHA II-IV) (OR=5.583, 95% CI:2.681-11.627), pulmonary infection (OR =4.053, 95% CI:1.692-9.710), emergency surgery (OR=9.629, 95% CI:2.962-31.301), coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) (OR=2.796, 95% CI:1.096-7.134), continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT Postoperative ICU stay ≥ 14 d) (OR=4.758, 95% CI:1.854-12.211) and postoperative ICU stay ≥14 d (OR=14.616, 95% CI:6.765-31.577) as independent risk factors for postoperative BSI. The nomogram showed good discrimination and calibration after internal validation, with an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.913 and a mean absolute calibration error of 0.026.

Conclusion

Postoperative BSI in cardiac surgery patients is associated with high mortality. A nomogram based on impaired cardiac function (NYHA II-IV), pulmonary infection, emergency surgery, CABG, CRRT and postoperative ICU stay ≥14 d displayed high accuracy and consistency in predicting the risk of postoperative BSI. These results facilitate early risk stratification and guide preventive strategies in high-risk cardiac surgical patients.

title: Improved Programs for Injury Categorization Using ICD-10.
authorString: Clark DE.
abstractText:
Background

Among the many efforts to convert International Classification of Diseases (ICD) codes into useful categories and scores for injury research has been the "ICD Programs for Injury Categorization" (ICDPIC).

Methods

Data from the American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Program (TQP) and US National Inpatient Sample (NIS) were used to develop Version 2 of ICDPIC for the R language (ICDPIC-R2). Programming efficiency was increased and new injury categorizations were added. Effect estimates for each ICD-10 Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) code were derived using logistic ridge regression with hospital mortality as the outcome. These estimates were converted to Abbreviated Injury Scale (AIS), Maximum AIS (MAIS), Injury Severity Score (ISS), and New Injury Severity Score (NISS). ICD-based Injury Severity Score (ICISS) was also calculated using TQP, NIS, and previously published data from an International Collaborative Effort for Injury Statistics (ICE-ICISS). Mortality predictions from ICDPIC-R2 were compared to those from ICDPIC Version 1 for R (ICDPIC-R1). Predictions derived from TQP data were partially validated using NIS data, and vice versa.

Results

Among 1,178,107 patient records in TQP or NIS, there were 8,427 distinct ICD-10-CM anatomic injury diagnosis codes. Regression results or predictions of mortality derived from AIS in ICDPIC-R2 were satisfactory measures of severity (evaluated using area under a Receiver Operating Characteristic curve or mean square error) and improved slightly on predictions obtained with ICDPIC-R1. ICISS methods (new in ICDPIC-R2) were also quite accurate, including ICE-ICISS. Predictions derived from TQP data performed well with NIS data, and vice versa. Runtimes were much faster with ICDPIC-R2. Effect estimates from ICD-10-CM codes and ICE-ICISS were applied to an additional 12,124 possible ICD-10 codes, including all those published by the World Health Organization.

Conclusion

ICDPIC remains reasonably accurate for categorizing injured patients, especially when only ICD codes are available. ICDPIC-R2 adds features and may extend applicability, especially for international data.

title: RV-LV volumetric relationship during graded supine exercise in healthy adults assessed by cardiovascular magnetic resonance.
authorString: Ikeda M, Hieda M, Yoshida K, Imabayashi M, Toyomura D, Izumi R, Nishizaki A, Wada T, Saito Y, Tokunaga C, Nishikawa K, Kurokawa S, Fukudome Y, Hino T, Yamasaki Y, Hosokawa K, Fukata M, Ishigami K, Abe K, Akashi K.
abstractText: Exercise cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging (exCMR) enables quantitative assessment of biventricular responses during physiological stress. We aimed to characterize right ventricular (RV)-left ventricular (LV) volumetric relationships in healthy adults using exCMR. Eighteen healthy adults (9 males, 9 females) underwent exCMR. Electrocardiography-gated short-axis cine and phase-contrast flow images were obtained at rest, at a target heart rate of 100 beats/min (Ex1), and at 40% of peak work rate determined by cardiopulmonary exercise testing (Ex2). The RV-LV volumetric relationship was operationally represented by the RV/LV end-diastolic and end-systolic volume ratios derived from simultaneous cine volumetry. All participants completed the protocol, and all cine and phase-contrast datasets were analyzed. During exercise, stroke volume increased in both ventricles predominantly through a reduction in end-systolic volume (ESV), whereas end-diastolic volume (EDV) changed little. Cine-derived LV and RV stroke volumes showed internal concordance with phase-contrast flow-derived measurements. The RV/LV EDV ratio (1.03, 1.03, and 1.03 at rest, Ex1, and Ex2, respectively) and RV/LV ESV ratio (1.09, 1.09, and 1.08 at rest, Ex1, and Ex2, respectively) remained stable across stages. Healthy adults maintained a stable relative RV-LV volumetric relationship during low-to-moderate intensity supine exercise. These findings provide quantitative physiological reference data for future disease-focused studies.

title: [Successful Hybrid Treatment of Crawford Type IV Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysm:Report of a Case].
authorString: Ueda D, Niwa K, Nishikawa H, Taniguchi T, Yamashita K.

journal.title: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery

abstractText: Thoracolaparotomy remains the first-line surgical approach for thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms. However, there is still room for improvement with regard to mortality and the incidence of postoperative complications, including paraplegia. In this context, hybrid treatment strategies that allow preservation of organ blood flow have gained increasing attention. We report a case of a Crawford type IV thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm that was successfully treated using a hybrid approach. The patient was an 87-year-old man. Computed tomography (CT) at admission revealed a thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm. Given the patient's advanced age and severe frailty, thoracolaparotomy was considered high risk. As the primary surgery, abdominal total debranching with thoracic endovascular aortic repair was performed. Bypasses from the right external iliac artery to visceral arteries were made, and stent graft was deployed in the thoracic artery. Anastomosis to the left renal artery was technically impossible. On postoperative day two, endovascular abdominal aortic stent graft was implanted. The patient was extubated on postoperative day 4, and was transferred to a rehabilitation hospital on postoperative day 29.

title: [Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting for Coronary Arteritis Induced by Myeloproliferative Neoplasms:Report of a Case].
authorString: Yu Z, Watanabe S, Murata K, Imamura Y, Minakawa M.

journal.title: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery

abstractText: In a 60-year-old man with a history of stroke, coronary angiography revealed triple vessel disease, comprising left anterior descending artery (LAD) #6-7 with 99% diffuse stenosis within the stent, #11 and #12 with 90% stenosis, and right coronary artery (RCA) #1 stent with 50% stenosis. Cardiac ultrasonography showed 34% left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) without mitral regurgitation (MR) or tricuspid regurgitation (TR). Following median sternotomy, the bilateral internal thoracic artery (BITA) was harvested by skeletonization;however, dissection was confirmed at the distal end of the right internal thoracic artery (RITA). Owing to severe apical adhesions, we decided to perform on-pump beating coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) for this patient. Cardiopulmonary bypass was initiated via proximal aortic arch inflow and bicaval drainage without left ventricule (LV) venting. Subsequently, a left internal thoracic surgery (LITA)-free RITA composite Y-graft was prepared. On-pump beating CABG was performed in the graft design of the LITA-LAD (onlay patch, 4.5 cm), LITA-free RITA composite Y-graft to the obtuse marginal (OM) artery, and AO-saphenous vein graft (SVG)-4 posterior descending artery (PD)-4AV by sequential anastomosis. Many inflammatory cells invaded the RITA and coronary artery, and distal vessel thickening was confirmed but not in the ascending aorta. Coronary arteritis induced by myeloproliferative neoplasms was diagnosed based on pathology. Coronary computed tomography (CT) revealed the patency of all grafts.

title: Shikonin: From Biosynthesis and Pharmacological Mechanisms to Translational Safety and Drug Delivery.
authorString: Joshi N, Semwal P, Rawat B, Kumar R, Oliveira MS, Rai N, Rawat JM.

journal.title: Chembiochem : a European journal of chemical biology

abstractText: Shikonin (SHK) is a red naphthoquinone produced mainly in the roots of Boraginaceae species and has been investigated for anticancer, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, neuroprotective, cardioprotective, hepatoprotective, and wound-healing activities. This review critically integrates botanical sources and biosynthesis with pharmacological mechanisms, preclinical evidence, safety, and delivery strategies. Across cancer models, SHK converges on redox imbalance and regulated cell-death programmes, including apoptosis, cell-cycle arrest, autophagy, necroptosis, ferroptosis, and immunogenic cell death, while modulating NF-κB, MAPK, PI3K/Akt, and related signalling networks. However, the evidence is dominated by heterogeneous in vitro experiments and small-animal studies, with limited pharmacokinetic standardisation, incomplete assessment of selectivity toward diseased versus normal tissues, and almost no robust clinical evaluation. Poor aqueous solubility, chemical and photochemical instability, rapid metabolism, route-dependent exposure, and a context-dependent therapeutic window remain central translational barriers. Liposomes, polymeric micelles, nanoparticles, nanogels, nanoemulsions, and ligand- or stimulus-responsive systems can improve dispersion, tissue accumulation, controlled release, and combination therapy; nevertheless, their long-term safety, manufacturing reproducibility, and comparative advantage over free SHK require rigorous validation. SHK should therefore be regarded as a mechanistically versatile therapeutic lead rather than a clinically established treatment. Translation will depend on exposure-response studies, standardised formulations, clinically relevant models, and well-designed human trials.

title: Association of CT-Based Sarcopenia, Clinical Frailty, and Nutritional Status With Mortality After Aortic Valve Replacement for Severe Aortic Stenosis.
authorString: Park JH, Zhang HS, Lee S, Soh S, Suh YJ.
abstractText:
Objective

This study investigated the association between multiple frailty-related markers-Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score, and computed tomography (CT)-based sarcopenia-and overall survival after aortic valve replacement (AVR) for severe aortic stenosis (AS), with particular emphasis on the first year after AVR.

Materials and methods

A total of 407 patients with severe AS who underwent surgical or transcatheter AVR at a tertiary center between November 2020 and December 2022 were retrospectively included. Three frailty-related markers were analyzed: CFS score for functional frailty, CONUT score for nutritional status, and CT-defined sarcopenia for structural muscle depletion. The CONUT score was calculated using serum markers, and sarcopenia was defined according to cohort-specific tertiles of the paravertebral muscle index quantified at the 12th thoracic vertebra (T12) vertebral level using CT. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis was performed to assess the prognostic associations of the Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) score and the three frailty-related markers with all-cause mortality after AVR.

Results

Within 1 year after AVR, 32 patients (7.9%) died. In the overall multivariable analysis, higher CFS scores and CT-defined sarcopenia were independently associated with mortality, with hazard ratios (HRs) of 1.82 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.40-2.38; P < 0.001) and 2.63 (95% CI, 1.22-5.67; P = 0.014), respectively. The STS score and CONUT scores were not associated with survival, with HRs of 1.00 (95% CI, 0.95-1.06; P = 0.883) and 1.05 (95% CI, 0.90-1.22; P = 0.563), respectively. A significant interaction was observed between the CONUT score and sarcopenia.

Conclusion

Among patients with severe AS undergoing AVR, higher CFS scores and CT-based sarcopenia were independently associated with survival after adjustment for the STS score. The prognostic association of the CONUT score differed according to sarcopenia status. These findings support the incorporation of functional and structural vulnerabilities into risk assessment for patients undergoing AVR for AS; however, the role of nutritional status requires further investigation.

title: Prevalence and clinical associations of age-related clonal haematopoiesis in SSc.
authorString: Maachi H, Fenwarth L, Duployez N, Ternynck C, Collet A, Dubucquoi S, Terriou L, Sanges S, Sobanski V, Hachulla E, Launay D.
abstractText:
Objectives

SSc is an autoimmune disease involving both innate and adaptive immunity, characterized by progressive organ fibrosis. Age-related clonal haematopoiesis (ARCH) results from somatic mutations in haematopoietic progenitors and is increasingly implicated in inflammation and autoimmunity. We aimed to assess the prevalence of ARCH in patients with SSc and its association with disease characteristics.

Methods

Targeted myeloid next-generation sequencing (NGS) was performed in 196 patients with SSc and 392 age- and gender-matched individuals without SSc and referred for NGS without a final diagnosis myelodysplastic syndrome. Variants with variant allele frequency (VAF) ≥ 0.8% were considered for ARCH analysis. Clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) was defined as ARCH with a VAF ≥2%.

Results

The prevalence of ARCH and CHIP was similar between SSc patients and the control group: 32.7% vs 37.2% (P = 0.25) and 23.5% vs 28.8% (P = 0.15), respectively. Among patients with SSc, ARCH was associated with higher NT-proBNP levels and higher prevalence of progressive interstitial lung disease (39.1% vs 15.7%, P = 0.026), pulmonary hypertension (23.4% vs 11.4%, P = 0.028), valvular heart disease (23.4% vs 11.4%, P = 0.028), ACAs (65.1% vs 49.6%, P = 0.043) in our cohort. After adjustment to age and gender, only NT-proBNP levels remain significantly higher in SSc patients with ARCH. These associations were not observed when restricting the analysis to CHIP except for valvular heart disease (26.1% vs 11.4%, P = 0.019) and higher NT-proBNP levels.

Conclusion

The prevalence of ARCH and CHIP was 32.7% and 23.5%, respectively, in our cohort of patients with SSc presence of ARCH was associated with more severe pulmonary involvement, a higher frequency of pulmonary hypertension, valvular heart disease and ACAs. After adjustment to age and sex, ARCH was associated with a higher NT-pro BNP levels.

title: Comparison of different radiotherapy planning techniques in breast cancer using active breathing coordinator.
authorString: Farid YG, Ibrahim MS, Shafaa MW, Rahmoun NA, Khalil MM, Khalil KA.

journal.title: Reports of practical oncology and radiotherapy : journal of Greatpoland Cancer Center in Poznan and Polish Society of Radiation Oncology

abstractText:
Background

To identify the optimal radiotherapy planning technique that provides the best dosimetric outcomes in terms of target coverage and sparing of organs at risk (OAR) when using deep inspiration breath-holding (DIBH) for early left-sided breast cancer treatment.

Materials and methods

Thirty patients with early-stage left-sided BC had previously been simulated and treated with DIBH using the active breathing coordinator (ABC) system. Each patient underwent replanning using 3D conformal radiotherapy (3DCRT), intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT), and volumetric-modulated arc therapy (VMAT) techniques with a prescription dose of 40.05 Gy over 15 fractions. The planning target volume (PTV) and OARs were evaluated using dose-volume histograms (DVH). Dosimetric parameters [V95, D98, D50, D2, V107, conformity index (CI), homogeneity index (HI)], and OAR metrics for the heart, left anterior descending artery (LAD), lungs, and contralateral breast were analysed statistically.

Results

VMAT achieved the best PTV coverage and homogeneity (HI = 0.1). The mean heart dose was lowest for 3DCRT (1.9 Gy) and VMAT (2 Gy), whereas for the LAD VMAT achieved the lowest doses (Dmean = 5.2 Gy; Dmax = 17.3 Gy; p < 0.001). For the ipsilateral lung, 3DCRT offered superior low-dose sparing, while VMAT minimised high-dose exposure. Contralateral lung and breast doses were lowest with 3DCRT.

Conclusions

VMAT offers superior target conformity and cardiac sparing specifically for the LAD, whereas 3DCRT minimises contralateral organs and low-dose lung exposure. These findings highlight the necessity for personalised treatment, whether the priority is to limit cardiac toxicity or reduce low-dose exposure to the patient.

title: Comparison of extended kV-CBCT image quality between conventional and O-ring linear accelerators.
authorString: Gazdag-Hegyesi S, Gáldi Á, Major T, Pesznyák C.

journal.title: Reports of practical oncology and radiotherapy : journal of Greatpoland Cancer Center in Poznan and Polish Society of Radiation Oncology

abstractText:
Background

In cases of non-central or large tumours, the use of an extended field of view is important for patient positioning or adaptive treatment. The aim of our study was to investigate the longitudinal and lateral consistency of extended kilovoltage cone-beam CT (kV-CBCT) image quality over the entire scan length.

Materials and methods

The study compared extended kV-CBCT image quality between conventional and O-ring linear accelerators (LINACs) using image quality phantoms. The impact of lateral and longitudinal phantom offsets was analysed across the reconstruction algorithms [filtered back projection - Feldkamp-Davis-Kress (FDK) and iterative cone-beam computed tomography (iCBCT)] and imaging protocols.

Results

The CT calibration curves showed consistent alignment across LINACs, imaging protocols, longitudinal displacements, and reconstruction algorithms. The average mean difference in the CT numbers measured during longitudinal shifts, averaged over the other material inserts, was 37 ± 15 Hounsfield units (HU). In the homogeneity examination, the lateral inserts displayed signal reductions as they moved away from the isocentre. For an imaging protocol on a ring accelerator, the central insert remained near 8 HU, while the signal of lateral inserts located 20 cm from the isocentre decreased from 0 HU to -160 HU.

Conclusions

Our results show that the longitudinal extension does not affect image linearity, making extended CBCT protocols suitable for long target volumes. CBCT-based adaptation may be unsuitable for large lateral or peripheral tumours due to poor image quality. Consequently, the generation of synthetic CTs from peripheral regions of CBCT images should be approached with caution.

title: Early Post-operative Fracture of Titanium Cementless Tibial Baseplate: Case Report and Review of the Literature.
authorString: Jubril A, Denasty A, Krishnan R, Kaplan N, Ricciardi B.
abstractText:
Introduction

Modern improvements in design and materials have led to a recent resurgence in the popularity of cementless total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Although early catastrophic failure is known to infrequently occur in cemented constructs, it is uncommon in modern designs of cementless knee systems.

Case report

Here, we report a 70-year-old female with a case of early fracture of the tibial component in a cementless, highly porous titanium-coated baseplate (Triathlon Tritanium, Stryker Orthopaedics), occurring within 20 months of the index procedure. Our case was successfully managed with a cemented tibial cone and stem construct; however, the etiology of failure remains uncertain.

Conclusion

Tibial baseplate fracture following TKA with modern cementless titanium three-dimensional -printed porous implants is scarcely reported in the literature, and a high index of suspicion should be maintained in the setting of unexplained pain even at short-term follow-up.

title: Radiotherapy for Cervical Cancer: Technical Advances, Clinical Applications, and Future Perspectives.
authorString: Maemoto H, Toita T, Nishie A.

journal.title: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research

abstractText: Radiotherapy is an essential treatment modality for cervical cancer and has evolved substantially with advances in image guidance and treatment delivery. This review summarizes recent technological developments in external beam radiotherapy and brachytherapy, their clinical applications, and future directions, with particular consideration of Japanese practice in an international context. In external beam radiotherapy, conventional techniques incorporating central shielding are increasingly being replaced by intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) and volumetric-modulated arc therapy (VMAT). Daily three-dimensional image-guided radiotherapy (3D-IGRT) is essential for the safe implementation of these techniques because of substantial uterine motion and deformation. In brachytherapy, the transition from two-dimensional point-based prescription to three-dimensional image-guided treatment has enabled individualized assessment of target coverage and doses to organs at risk. Although magnetic resonance imaging-based brachytherapy is internationally recommended, computed tomography-based planning predominates in Japan and has achieved favorable outcomes, despite some studies reporting lower cumulative target doses than those recommended internationally. Intracavitary/interstitial brachytherapy (IC/IS BT) further improves dose distribution by combining intracavitary applicators with interstitial needles, particularly when adequate target coverage cannot be achieved with standard intracavitary brachytherapy alone. Future advances may include artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted treatment planning and adaptive workflows, tissue spacers to overcome anatomical constraints, and the incorporation of genomic, multi-omics, and radiomics information. Integrating these approaches may enable cervical cancer radiotherapy to progress beyond increasingly safe and precise treatment toward personalized care tailored to individual patient and tumor characteristics.

title: Machine Learning-Based Clustering of Clinical Phenotypes in Adults With Bicuspid Aortic Valve: A Large Single-Center Study.
authorString: Zhang X, Chen Z, Xu Z, Liu T, Zhang L, He Y, Gu X.
abstractText:
Objective

Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) is clinically heterogeneous, and the relationships among valve morphology, valvular dysfunction, and aortic involvement remain incompletely understood. We aimed to identify clinical phenotypes of adults with BAV by clustering multidimensional clinical data, primarily echocardiographic parameters.

Methods

We retrospectively included adults with echocardiographically confirmed BAV at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2016 and December 2024. Data from the first echocardiographic examination and contemporaneous clinical records were extracted, and nine continuous and three categorical variables were entered into a two-step clustering model. Continuous and categorical variables were compared across clusters using the Kruskal-Wallis H test and chi-square test, respectively, followed by pairwise comparisons. The stability of the four-cluster solution was assessed using 100 bootstrap resamples; agreement was quantified with the adjusted Rand index (ARI) and Jaccard coefficients. Clustering was also repeated after separately excluding sex and valve dysfunction to assess the influence of these key variables on cluster structure.

Results

A total of 6977 patients with echocardiographically diagnosed BAV were included. The median age was 53.0 years (interquartile range, 40.0-61.0), and 70.0% were men. Two-step clustering identified four clinical phenotypes that differed significantly in valve morphology, valvular dysfunction, aortic dimensions, left-heart remodeling, cardiac function, and surgical interventions (all p < 0.001): Cluster 1, a predominantly male, regurgitation-predominant phenotype with left ventricular dilatation; Cluster 2, a predominantly male, stenosis-predominant phenotype with concentric hypertrophy; Cluster 3, a male phenotype with no or mild valve dysfunction; and Cluster 4, a female phenotype characterized mainly by no or mild valve dysfunction with a tendency toward stenosis. The proportion undergoing subsequent surgery after the baseline echocardiographic assessment was highest in Cluster 2 (40%) and lowest in Cluster 3 (14%). Left ventricular end-systolic diameter, left ventricular end-diastolic diameter, aortic root diameter, valve dysfunction, and sex were the principal drivers of clustering. Across bootstrap resamples, the mean ARI for the four-cluster solution was 0.696. In sensitivity analyses, exclusion of either sex or valve dysfunction reduced the optimal solution from four clusters to two.

Conclusions

Machine learning-based two-step clustering identified four baseline clinical phenotypes among adults with BAV, revealing multidimensional combinations of valve morphology, valvular function, aortic dimensions, and left-heart remodeling. This classification is intended primarily to characterize the clinical heterogeneity of adult BAV; its longitudinal clinical value requires confirmation in independent prospective cohorts.

title: Untargeted Plasma Metabolomics Reveals Molecular Subtypes Associated with Reintervention Risk in Peripheral Artery Disease after Revascularization.
authorString: Zhang B, Cao Y, Zhao W, Luo J, Li X, Zhang X, Xu Z, Wang J, Chen Z, Chen L, Diao Y, Li Y.
abstractText: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) shows substantial outcome heterogeneity after revascularization that is incompletely explained by conventional severity indicators. We performed untargeted plasma LC-MS metabolomics in 175 PAD patients undergoing revascularization and applied variability-based feature selection, unsupervised clustering, pathway and chemical-class analyses, survival modeling, and metabolite prioritization. Three metabolically defined molecular subtypes were identified: redox protective (n = 93), metabolic burden (n = 72), and renal dysfunction (n = 10). Compared to the redox-protective subtype, the metabolic-burden subtype showed higher risks of composite adverse outcomes, reintervention, and major adverse cardiovascular events, accompanied by acylcarnitine accumulation, fatty-acyl enrichment, and COX-prostaglandin-related inflammatory signaling. Secondary clustering of high-risk patients identified a subgroup with increased reintervention risk, despite no corresponding increase in Rutherford classification or ankle-brachial index severity, characterized by sphingomyelin, diglyceride, and thromboxane/leukotriene-related lipid mediator signatures. A five-metabolite score was associated with reintervention risk and showed numerically higher apparent discrimination than the original and expanded clinical models. These findings establish an untargeted metabolomics framework for molecular subtyping of PAD after revascularization and nominate metabolic phenotypes for future validation.

title: A Qualitative Study of Preventive Behaviors Among Patients Considered at High Risk of Lower Limb Lymphedema After Gynecological Cancer Surgery Using the Theoretical Domains Framework.
authorString: Wang Y, Zhang Y, Wu Y, Xu C.
abstractText:
Purpose

To explore experiences, barriers, and facilitators related to preventive behaviors among patients considered at high risk of lower limb lymphedema (LLL) after gynecological cancer surgery, using the Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF).

Methods

Eighteen patients considered at high risk of LLL and assessed as having no clinically apparent LLL at enrollment were purposively recruited. Semi-structured interviews were conducted between March and July 2026. The 14-domain TDF informed the interview guide and initial deductive coding. Directed content analysis was used to develop subthemes and overarching themes. Reporting followed the Standards for Reporting Qualitative Research (SRQR).

Results

Three overarching themes and nine subthemes were identified: (1) everyday activities and practical constraints: access to and understanding of preventive practices, role-driven activity, and changes in activity after role disruption; (2) emotional responses in the context of daily activity and preventive practices: anxiety alongside differing levels of engagement, fear and limited enactment of preventive intentions, distress around illness-related events, and acceptance, optimism, and everyday activity; and (3) following advice and remembering preventive practices: willingness to follow advice and remembering practices through everyday cues.

Conclusion

Participants described practical constraints, family roles, emotional responses, and reliance on advice or everyday cues in relation to daily activity and preventive practices. The findings may inform context-sensitive nursing support before clinically apparent LLL develops. However, any resulting intervention requires prospective evaluation of its acceptability, feasibility, and effects.

title: Lipoprotein(a), Endothelial Dysfunction and Cardiovascular Disease.
authorString: Zhou X, Fang X, Zhou X, Zhang Z, Hu Y, Cheng Z.

journal.title: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine

abstractText: Lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) is a particle similar to low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and is associated with apolipoprotein (A). High Lp(a) levels are a genetic, independent risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). Endothelial cells, which form the continuous lining of the cardiovascular system, are crucial for vascular function and represent the primary target of Lp(a)-mediated injury. Lp(a) penetrates the endothelial barrier and undergoes oxidative modification, triggering endothelial dysfunction, which is characterized by inflammation, oxidative stress and impaired nitric oxide bioavailability. These disruptions promote monocyte recruitment, foam cell formation and atherosclerosis development. Currently, various drugs that can reduce Lp(a) levels are also involved in regulating endothelial cell function, ultimately reducing the risk of ASCVD. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying Lp(a)-mediated endothelial injury and the extent to which Lp(a) lowering improves endothelial function remain incompletely defined. Clarifying these issues may inform cardiovascular risk stratification and the clinical development of Lp(a)-targeted therapies. This review seeks to consolidate the understanding of the link between Lp(a) levels and endothelial dysfunction, highlighting its pivotal role in cardiovascular disease progression.

title: Mitochondrial Dysfunction as a Context-Dependent Driver and Amplifier of the SASP: Targeting the mtDNA-cGAS-STING Axis for Next-Generation Senotherapeutics.
authorString: Hama HK, Hama MA, Zorab MM, Gholami A, Al-Farga AM.

journal.title: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine

abstractText: Cellular senescence combines stable cell-cycle arrest with mitochondrial and innate immune remodelling that shapes the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). This narrative review evaluates mitochondrial dysfunction as a context-dependent initiator or amplifier of senescence and examines mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) sensing through cGAS-STING as a driver of SASP regulation. We distinguish mitochondrial damage, cytosolic mtDNA exposure, pathway activation, SASP transcription, secretion, paracrine activity and tissue outcomes as separate levels of evidence. The strongest mechanistic studies link BAX/BAK-mediated minority mitochondrial outer-membrane permeabilization, VDAC1 oligomerization, defective mitophagy or abnormal mtDNA composition to cytosolic mtDNA, cGAS-STING activation and SASP modulation through genetic or pharmacological perturbation. However, pathway architecture varies across cell types, tissues and senescence triggers, and nuclear DNA, micronuclei, retroelements and mitochondrial RNA can activate overlapping inflammatory programmes. Preclinical evidence therefore supports STING inhibition primarily as a senomorphic, anti-inflammatory and tissue-protective strategy rather than a senolytic intervention. Mitophagy enhancement, inhibition of mtDNA release, targeted protein degradation and precision delivery offer complementary approaches, but human efficacy remains unestablished. Clinical translation will require standardized biomarkers, biologically informed patient selection, pharmacodynamic confirmation, tissue-restricted or reversible modulation and prospective assessment of antiviral, antitumour and long-term safety. Overall, the mitochondrial dysfunction-mtDNA-cGAS-STING axis is a mechanistically credible but context-dependent therapeutic framework whose clinical value will depend on validated pathway engagement and appropriately timed clinical intervention.

title: Alterations in the Immune-Fibrotic Axis Are Spatially Localized in the Aging Heart.
authorString: Aljakna Khan A, Sintou A, Zhao Y, Somarakis A, Chandok H, Diniz JA, Ramasamy R, Clark GT, Frommer L, Hayat S, White BS, Robson P, Korstanje R, Mahoney JM, Rosenthal NA.
abstractText: The immune-fibrotic axis functions as a vicious feedback loop where age-related chronic, low-grade systemic inflammation (inflammaging) drives maladaptive tissue repair and fibrosis, while senescent fibrotic cells in turn amplify systemic inflammation. In the aging heart, immune dysregulation and fibroblast activation drive tissue scarring and stiffening and a higher risk of heart failure and vascular disease. To identify cardiac regions and cell types affected with age, we monitored transcriptional changes across whole hearts of 6- and 24-month-old male and female mice. Spatially resolved signatures of macrophages and fibroblasts, non-cardiomyocyte populations highly involved in inflammaging, were enriched predominantly in the valves and aorta. With age, two cell types simultaneously adopted maladaptive programs: Macrophages displayed reduced immune homeostasis together with increased chemotactic and stromal programs, while more widely distributed fibroblast-lineage cells displayed alterations in extracellular matrix organization and intercellular signals, as well as upregulation of senescence-associated Cdkn1a (encoding p21) and other activated features shared with human cardiac fibroblasts. The major biological significance of these findings is that cardiac immune-fibrotic remodeling is not a uniform, heart-wide process. Instead, it varies with cell type, with valves and aorta emerging as major sites where age-associated programs converge to progressively compromise cardiac structure and function.

title: Chemodectoma Arising From the Abdominal Aorta in a 9-Year-Old Female Dog: Clinical, Histopathological and Immunohistochemstric Study.
authorString: Boskabadi SA, Nikroo KS, Mirshahi A, Nourani H, Hadiyan SS.
abstractText:
Background

Chemodectomas are uncommon, typically benign neoplasms derived from paraganglionic chemoreceptor tissues, most frequently arising in the heart base or carotid bodies of brachycephalic dogs. This report documents a detailed pathological description of a chemodectoma originating from the abdominal aorta in a non-human species, representing, to our knowledge, the first case specifically characterized by its origin at the aortic trifurcation, thereby expanding the recognized anatomical spectrum of this tumour entity.

Case presentation

A 9-year-old spayed female terrier was presented with persistent panting, recent-onset obesity following previous cachexia, and a complex clinical history including polyuria/polydipsia and pyoderma. Haematological and biochemical analyses revealed a regenerative anaemia, leucocytosis, and biochemical indicators suggestive of cholestasis and potential endocrinopathy. Advanced imaging identified a solitary, well-demarcated, highly vascular abdominal mass closely associated with the aortic trifurcation. Given the tumour's inaccessibility and pronounced vascularity, cytological confirmation via fine needle aspiration was precluded due to haemorrhagic risk, necessitating exploratory laparotomy.

Management and outcome

Intraoperatively, the mass was unresectable because of its anatomical relationships and the prohibitive risk of catastrophic haemorrhage. Humane euthanasia was subsequently elected. Histopathological evaluation demonstrated a lobulated neoplasm composed of pleomorphic neuroendocrine cells, with low mitotic activity and an absence of necrosis or haemorrhage. Immunohistochemistry confirmed strong, diffuse synaptophysin reactivity and focal neuron-specific enolase positivity, while chromogranin A and S100 protein were negative, underscoring immunophenotypic variability.

Conclusion

This case illustrates the diagnostic complexity and therapeutic limitations posed by extra-cardiac chemodectomas in veterinary species, especially when located in unconventional anatomical sites. Limitations included the unavailability of computed tomography and lack of postoperative follow-up. This report expands the recognized clinico-pathological spectrum of chemodectomas and highlights the necessity for multidisciplinary diagnostic strategies and further research aimed at defining optimal management protocols for such rare and challenging presentations.

title: Rethinking Left Ventricular Diastolic Dysfunction in Hypertension: The Interplay of Arterial Stiffness, Ventricular-Arterial Coupling, and Pulse Wave Velocity in HFpEF.
authorString: Palmiero P, Amati F, Bombini L, Ciccone MM, Maiello M, I.C.I.S.C.U. (Italian Chapter of the International Society of Cardiovascular Ultrasound).
abstractText: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) accounts for approximately half of heart failure cases and is closely associated with hypertension and left ventricular diastolic dysfunction (LVDD). This narrative review examines the relationship between diastolic function, arterial stiffness, and ventricular-arterial coupling in hypertensive heart disease. We summarize ventricular relaxation and filling and discuss echocardiographic measures, including E/e', left atrial volume, and left atrial reservoir strain, for assessing diastolic function and filling pressures. We then examine how aortic stiffening may increase late systolic load and contribute to ventricular remodeling and impaired relaxation. This review addresses four central questions: whether arterial stiffness represents an independent component of hypertensive left ventricular diastolic dysfunction; whether pulse wave velocity (PWV) is primarily a marker of vascular aging, ventricular afterload, or HFpEF risk; whether PWV provides incremental information beyond established echocardiographic markers; and how arterial stiffness could be integrated into contemporary HFpEF assessment. The available evidence supports arterial stiffness as a biologically plausible contributor to hypertensive ventricular remodeling and impaired diastolic reserve. However, current evidence does not establish echocardiographic global PWV (PWVg) as an independent diagnostic criterion or validated prognostic marker of clinical HFpEF. We therefore propose PWVg as a complementary, hypothesis-generating measure for vascular and ventricular phenotyping, to be interpreted alongside clinical assessment, natriuretic peptides, multiparametric echocardiography, and exercise or invasive hemodynamic testing when indicated.

title: [Non-anatomic Bypass for Severe Brachiocephalic Artery Stenosis due to Dissecting Aneurysm After Total Arch Aortic Replacement for Stanford Type A Acute Aortic Dissection:Report of a Case].
authorString: Fukuta H, Ushioda R, Narita M, Setogawa Y, Miyamoto H, Okubo R, Takahashi S, Takeyoshi D, Kunioka S, Tsutsui M, Kamiya H.

journal.title: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery

abstractText: Dissecting brachiocephalic artery aneurysm after total arch aortic replacement poses a risk of postoperative cerebral infarction, yet no consensus exists regarding optimal management. Treatment decisions rely on the patient's condition, degree of true lumen stenosis, and lesion characteristics. We report a case of a dissecting brachiocephalic aneurysm with severe true lumen stenosis following surgery for Stanford type A acute aortic dissection. A 70-year-old man was transferred to our hospital with acute aortic dissection and multiple right-hemispheric cerebral infarctions and underwent emergency total arch replacement. On postoperative day nine, contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) revealed progressive false lumen expansion with significant true lumen compression. To prevent further cerebral ischemia, a left axillary-right common carotid artery non-anatomic bypass was performed. The patient gradually recovered left upper limb function and was transferred for rehabilitation on postoperative day 27.

title: [Aortic Root Replacement for a Left Sinus of Valsalva Aneurysm Complicated by Ascending Aortic Dissection:Report of a Case].
authorString: Matsuda Y, Sakata J, Yanase Y, Nakamura M.

journal.title: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery

abstractText: We report a case of a left sinus of Valsalva aneurysm (SVA) complicated by ascending aortic dissection (AAD). A 37-year-old man presented to our hospital with worsening leg edema and was diagnosed with heart failure due to severe aortic regurgitation (AR). Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) and transesophageal echocardiography revealed the presence of an AAD and a left SVA. After medical treatment for heart failure, the patient underwent aortic root replacement. The postoperative course was favorable. The combination of SVA and AAD in a young patient is extremely rare and may lead to delayed diagnosis. Therefore, thorough investigation of the underlying cause is essential, particularly in young patients presenting with heart failure or AR.

title: [Left Coronary Sinus of Valsalva Aneurysm with Infective Endocarditis:Report of a Case].
authorString: Konegawa Y, Kyo S, Doi K, Ueyamaya K, Nagato H.

journal.title: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery

abstractText: Sinus of Valsalva aneurysm is an uncommon cardiac anomaly, either acquired or congenital. Left sinus aneurysm is extremely rare. A 60-year-old man with chest discomfort initially presented to an outside facility. Computed tomography (CT) revealed a left sinus of Valsalva aneurysm with thrombus. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated a bicuspid aortic valve with moderate aortic insufficiency. Based on blood culture tests and images, he was diagnosed with sinus of Valsalva aneurysm with infective endocarditis. Immediately, antimicrobial therapy was initiated, and then, he underwent elective surgical repair. After four weeks of treatment with post-operative antibiotics, he was discharged uneventfully. Left sinus of Valsalva aneurysm with infective endocarditis is rare and fulminant. Optimal medical treatment followed by aortic root replacement using rifampicin-bonded graft is one of the options for the resolution of this pathology.

title: [Efficacy of Inhaled Nitric Oxide Therapy During the Perioperative Period of Cardiac and Aortic Surgery:a Four-case Report Featuring Reactive and Prophylactic Initiation Strategies].
authorString: Ohkawa A, Miki K, Yasuda N, Koshima R, Hashiguchi H.

journal.title: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery

abstractText: Inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) is a selective pulmonary vasodilator that reduces pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) without compromising systemic blood pressure, making it useful in perioperative management during cardiac and aortic surgery. We report four cases in which iNO was administered either therapeutically or prophylactically according to intraoperative or postoperative hemodynamic and respiratory conditions. Therapeutic use improved pulmonary artery pressure and oxygenation during cardiopulmonary bypass weaning and extubation. Prophylactic administration before separation from cardiopulmonary bypass was effective in a patient with severe preoperative pulmonary hypertension, allowing stable weaning. iNO also contributed to hemodynamic and oxygenation improvement in extracorporeal membrane oxygeration (ECMO)-managed cases. These findings suggest that iNO, when used according to pathophysiology, is a valuable adjunctive therapy in high-risk perioperative settings.

title: [Taping the Trachea at Aorto-pulmonary Window].
authorString: Tsubota N.

journal.title: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery

abstractText: Key technique encircling the trachea at aorto-pulmonary (A-P) window is described. A lesion around the left main bronchus and the lower end of the trachea is approached through left or right thoracotomy, or median sternotomy. When left thoracotomy is selected, taping the trachea at A-P window under the aortic arch moves the lesion closer and yields better surgical view, which makes bronchoplastic procedure easier. Two cases are presented, in which preoperative bronchoscopy revealed the left main bronchus totally occluded at its origin. In the first case, total length of the left main bronchus including lateral portion of the tracheal end was resected with the nonfunctioning left upper lobe. The reconstructed left lower lobe recovered its function after collapsing for one year and half. In the second case, deep wedge resection of the left main bronchus at its origin with tumor was performed. The lung parenchyma was preserved. Postoperative bronchoscopy showed the successfully reconstructed air way in both cases.

title: Inflammatory and Insulin Resistance Indicator for Predicting Repeat Revascularization and In-Stent Restenosis in Patients With Chronic Coronary Syndrome Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
authorString: Jiale W, Longcheng L, Peipei L, Lihong M.
abstractText:
Objective

The C-reactive protein-triglyceride glucose index (CTI) has been associated with cardiovascular risk. This study evaluated its prognostic value for repeat revascularization and in-stent restenosis (ISR) in patients with chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).

Methods

A total of 2147 CCS patients undergoing PCI were stratified into CTI tertiles. The primary endpoint was a composite of repeat revascularization and ISR. Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank tests was used to compare event rates. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models and restricted cubic spline analyses were applied to assess associations. Predictive performance was evaluated using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves.

Results

During a median follow-up of 60 months, 992 patients (46.2%) experienced the primary endpoint. Event rates increased progressively across CTI tertiles. After multivariable adjustment, CTI remained independently associated with the primary endpoint (HR 1.11; 95% CI 1.01-1.22; p = 0.028). Compared with the lowest tertile, the highest CTI tertile was associated with a 31% higher risk (HR 1.31; 95% CI 1.10-1.55; p = 0.002). A linear dose-response relationship was observed (p for non-linearity = 0.172; p overall = 0.040). The multivariable model incorporating CTI showed modest discrimination, with AUCs of 0.627 (95% CI 0.602-0.651) at 3 years and 0.651 (95% CI 0.627-0.674) at 5 years.

Conclusions

CTI is independently associated with increased risks of repeat revascularization and ISR after PCI in patients with CCS. However, its incremental predictive value beyond conventional risk factors appears limited and requires further validation.

title: Nomogram for Postoperative Permanent Neurologic Dysfunction Following Acute Type A Aortic Dissection Surgery: A Multicentral Retrospective Study.
authorString: Chen J, Li J, Yu J, Dai M, Wang C, Zhu J, Wang J.
abstractText:
Background

Permanent neurologic dysfunction (PND) often complicates following surgery for acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) and is strongly correlated with unfavorable outcomes. Consequently, developing an effective diagnostic method to identify high-risk patients is of considerable importance.

Methods

This retrospective study, covering 2022 to 2024 across two centers, ultimately included 117 ATAAD patients with Supra-Aortic Branch Vessel (SABV) dissection from our center (2022-2023) as the training set and 52 ATAAD patients with SABV dissection from a secondary center (2024) as the validation set. We used logistic regression to identify predictors and developed a nomogram, which was assessed using the area under the ROC curve, calibration and decision curve analysis. External validation was conducted using the validation set.

Results

In this study, 169 cases were finally collected (117 in the training set and 52 in the validation set), of whom 64 patients developed postoperative PND. Four risk factors were identified: brachiocephalic trunk dissection at the bifurcation plane, chronic kidney disease, age over 50, and cross-clamp duration over 168 min. The AUC was 0.809 for the training set and 0.736 for the validation set. The nomogram model demonstrated acceptable predictive performance, and decision curve analysis potential clinical utility for predicting postoperative PND risk for thresholds of 1%-90% in the training set and 3%-75% in the validation set.

Conclusions

This study developed and validated a predictive model for assessing the risk of postoperative PND in patients undergoing ATAAD surgery, which may assist clinicians in individualized risk assessment.

title: Study on Wall Shear Stress Changes in the Aortic Arch and Isthmus in Fetuses With Aortic Coarctation Using Vector Flow Mapping.
authorString: Xu Z, Zeng S, Tong X, Aboubacar Hamidou AR, Liu Y, Liu B.
abstractText:
Objective

To evaluate segmental peak systolic wall shear stress (WSSmax) in the aortic arch and isthmus of fetuses with coarctation of the aorta (CoA) and to explore its relationships with conventional anatomical and hemodynamic parameters.

Methods

This prospective study included 58 CoA fetuses and 58 gestational age-matched normal controls. Vector flow mapping measured WSSmax at the inner and outer curvatures of the aortic arch and isthmus. Within the CoA group, Spearman correlation was used to assess relationships between isthmus WSSmax and the isthmus Z-score, PA/AO, TV/MV, isthmus Vmax, and RV/LV. Multivariable linear regression was performed using the isthmus Z-deficit (-Z), PA/AO, and isthmus Vmax.

Results

Arch WSSmax did not differ between groups (all p > 0.05). Isthmus WSSmax (general, inner, and outer curvature) was significantly higher in the CoA group than in controls (all p < 0.05). Within the CoA group, isthmus WSSmax was lower than arch WSSmax (all p < 0.05). Isthmus WSSmax was correlated with the isthmus Z-score, PA/AO, and isthmus Vmax. In multivariable regression, isthmus Z-deficit (B = 0.271, 95% CI 0.031-0.510, p < 0.05) and isthmus Vmax (B = 0.01, 95% CI 0.001-0.020, p < 0.05) were independently associated with isthmus WSSmax, whereas PA/AO was not significant (p > 0.05).

Conclusion

Isthmus WSSmax is elevated in fetuses with CoA and is independently associated with greater isthmus hypoplasia and higher isthmus flow velocity, suggesting a role in CoA pathophysiology. Its incremental diagnostic value could not be assessed because the control group consisted of normal fetuses. WHAT IS ALREADY KNOWN ABOUT THIS TOPIC?: Prenatal diagnosis of aortic coarctation (CoA) has a high false‑positive rate. Hemodynamic changes in CoA include increased velocity and turbulence, but biomechanical assessment in fetuses is limited. WHAT DOES THIS STUDY ADD?: This study uses VFM to quantify WSSmax in the fetal aortic arch and isthmus. Isthmus WSSmax is significantly elevated in fetuses with CoA and is independently associated with greater isthmus hypoplasia and higher isthmus flow velocity, providing mechanistic insights into the biomechanical alterations of fetal CoA.

title: Impact of micro-mobility-induced step reduction in healthy adults on vascular and glycemic health: A real-world investigation.
authorString: Reidy PT, Betz AC, Yeager JP, Liu Y, Binion RA, Ayton S, Lefkowitz L, Slattery E, Skujins RJ, Walsh A, Scerbo M, Timmerman KL, Ballard KD.
abstractText: We investigated the effects of a 7-day e-scooter-induced step reduction followed by 7 days of recovery on vascular function, body composition, and glycemic control in healthy adults. Longitudinal time series. Twelve adults (5 male and 7 women; 20.3 ± 1.8 years) completed a three-week study: (1) baseline, (2) 7-day step reduction via e-scooter, and (3) 7-day recovery. Assessments included daily steps (accelerometry), glycemic control (continuous glucose monitoring), body composition (bioelectrical impedance), and arterial stiffness (pulse wave velocity [cf-PWV]). Steps decreased by ~33% during Reduced Activity (10,466 ± 2872 to 6965 ± 3408 steps/day; p < 0.05) and returned to baseline (9103 ± 2896) during Recovery. Step reduction decreased lean mass and increased glycemic variability. While some lean mass recovered, glycemic variability remained elevated during Recovery. cf-PWV was unchanged during step reduction but decreased by 0.4 m/s after Recovery. Short-term, modest physical activity reduction impairs glycemic control and reduces lean mass. Rapid recovery of lean mass contrasts with persistent increases in glycemic variability, suggesting residual metabolic impacts. Resuming normal activity may improve vascular function via reduced arterial stiffness.

title: Development of Aortic Stents from Open Surgery to Endovascular Therapy: A Brazilian Contribution to the Treatment of Aortic Diseases.
authorString: Fonseca JHAPD, Maia ADS, Fonseca GDPD, Ribeiro BS, Moura Filho AA.
abstractText: The treatment of aortic diseases has undergone profound transformation over the last decades, with the progressive incorporation of endovascular techniques either replacing or complementing conventional open surgical repair. The development of aortic stents represents one of the most significant milestones in this transition. This article reviews the historical, experimental, and clinical evolution of aortic stents, with emphasis on pioneering Brazilian contributions, including the experimental phase in animal models, the first clinical applications in aortic dissection, and the role of the national industry in the development and dissemination of these technologies. The impact of these innovations on contemporary cardiovascular surgical practice and future perspectives are also discussed.

title: Tips and Tricks of Aortic Valve Reimplantation to Treat Aortic Root Aneurysms.
authorString: David TE.
abstractText: This article summarizes the author's experience with aortic valve reimplantation, focusing on technical errors that may adversely affect outcome. This is a complex surgical procedure that requires detailed knowledge of the functional anatomy of the aortic valve and how disease affects its components. The procedure was developed to correct abnormal components of the aortic root in patients with aortic root aneurysms, both sporadic and associated with genetic syndromes, with the aim of restoring the native aortic valve anatomy and function. When applied to properly selected patients and performed correctly, the very long-term outcomes are gratifying for both the patient and the surgeon.

title: Liver Injury Repair and Regeneration: Molecular Mechanisms and Therapeutic Targets.
authorString: Pan M, An N, Feng Y, Hu Y, Pan C, Su Y, Huang Y, Long T, Wang Q, Song Q, Li P, Li X, Yin W, Hu Z, Liu X, Liu J.
abstractText: The liver possesses a remarkable regenerative capacity to restore tissue integrity and physiological function following acute injury. However, this endogenous repair potential is gradually impaired in chronic liver diseases, including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and hepatic fibrosis. These disorders frequently lead to persistent inflammation and progressive hepatic dysfunction. Our incomplete understanding of the mechanisms behind pathological liver regeneration limits the development of new regenerative therapies. This review summarizes recent advances in liver regeneration across temporal, cellular, metabolic, and interorgan communication aspects. It describes the dynamic features of different regenerative phases and emphasizes the regulatory roles of non-parenchymal cells within the regenerative niche. We also outline promising translational strategies, including molecular-targeted therapy, cell-based therapy, liver tissue engineering, and nanocarrier delivery systems. This review links basic mechanistic findings to clinical translation, discusses key existing research challenges, and offers useful insights for developing precision therapeutics for liver regeneration.

authorString: Gierlinger G, Srivastava I, Seeber F, Mair R, Kreuzer M, Prandstetter C, Wichert-Schmitt B, Tulzer A, Tulzer G, Mair R, Sames-Dolzer E.
