authorString: Aydin MI.

title: Cerebral near infrared spectroscopy - clinical use in the neonatal intensive care unit.
authorString: de Crescenzo S, Austin T, Martini S.
abstractText: Preventing brain injury and optimising neurodevelopmental outcome are central goals of neonatal intensive care, yet routine cerebral monitoring remains uncommon. Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) offers a continuous, non-invasive, cot-side measure of cerebral oxygenation and perfusion, and has been investigated in the newborn for nearly forty years. The introduction of spatially resolved spectroscopy enabled absolute measurement of regional tissue oxygen saturation (rStO<sub>2</sub>), bringing the technology from the research laboratory into routine bedside use. Abnormal cerebral oxygenation patterns are associated with intraventricular haemorrhage in preterm infants, with injury severity in hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy, and with adverse events in congenital heart disease, although signals are strongly influenced by systemic factors and are best interpreted within the broader clinical context. The landmark SafeBoosC and COSGOD randomised trials confirmed that NIRS-guided care is feasible and safe but did not demonstrate reductions in death or severe brain injury, exposing the limitations of single-threshold approaches. Measures of cerebral autoregulation, cerebrovascular reactivity, and neurovascular coupling, alongside emerging techniques such as multiscale entropy and AI-driven multimodal integration, offer richer physiological insight. Future progress lies in dynamic, individualised, brain-oriented monitoring rather than reliance on absolute saturation thresholds alone.

title: Development and Validation of a Logistic-Bayes Method for In-Hospital Mortality Discrimination in Neonatal Heart Failure: A Real-World Study.
authorString: Zhang X, Wei M, Yang H, Wu J, Liu B, Lu Y, Tang B.
abstractText:
Background

Neonatal heart failure is a severe condition with high mortality, posing a significant burden on families and healthcare systems. Accurately discriminating whether a neonate with heart failure will die in hospital is essential for improving outcomes.

Objective

To develop and validate a discriminant model for identifying neonates with heart failure who will experience in-hospital death.

Methods

This real-world study included 600 neonates with heart failure treated at the First Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University between 2012 and 2025. Demographic, clinical, perinatal, laboratory, and first-24-hour medication data were extracted. Candidate variables were screened by LASSO regression and between-group comparisons; eight discriminators retained by multivariable logistic regression were used to construct the Logistic-Bayes model, and the cohort was randomly split in a 7:3 ratio into training and internal validation sets.

Results

The final discriminators were urea, fibrinogen, poor postnatal response, oliguria, cedilanid use, dopamine use, epinephrine use, and digoxin use. The model achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.87 (95% CI 0.82-0.91) in the training set and 0.86 (95% CI 0.78-0.92) in the internal validation set, with accuracy of 0.87 in both.

Conclusion

On internal validation, the model demonstrated high specificity and high negative predictive value, supporting early identification of low-risk neonates with heart failure; prospective multicenter validation is required before routine clinical use.

title: High-Resolution Mapping of Healthcare Pathways in Autism
DUF6383-domain containing protein from <i>Parabacteroides distasonis</i> predicts survival in patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis.
authorString: Kreimeyer H, Gonzalez C, Fondevila MF, AlcHepNet Investigators, Canbay A, Stärkel P, Gonzalez DJ, Schnabl B.
abstractText: Intestinal dysbiosis is a hallmark of alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) characterized by a higher abundance of unfavorable species and a reduction of beneficial species. In this study, we aimed to analyze the bacterial proteome of stool samples from patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) (n = 80), alcohol use disorder (AUD; n = 20), and controls (n = 19) from an international multicenter cohort using quantitative tandem mass tag (TMT)-based metaproteomic profiling. We validated our results in an independent multicenter cohort of 72 patients with AH at the genomic level using qPCR. We detected 2,364 bacterial proteins and identified distinct metaproteomic signatures separating controls, patients with AUD, and AH. Patients with AUD and AH were characterized by depletion of Firmicutes-derived proteins and enrichment of proteins from Bacteroidetes, Proteobacteria, and Actinobacteria. Eighteen bacterial proteins increased with disease severity, many with multifunctional "moonlighting" roles, including enolase and hexokinase. DUF6383 domain-containing protein from Parabacteroides distasonis is correlated with histological injury, inflammatory cell infiltration, and is linked to neutrophil degranulation in the host. Patients with a high abundance of DUF6383 domain-containing protein had significantly lower 90-day survival, and this association was validated by qPCR at the genomic level in a second cohort. Our findings show that microbial proteins are associated with disease severity and progression, and that DUF6383 domain-containing protein from P. distasonis is a potential prognostic biomarker for AH.

title: <i>Schaalia odontolytica</i> causing <i>primary</i> intraventricular brain abscess in a child- A case report.
authorString: Acquah F, Semevor GO, Aggrey I, Okrah OA, Abdullah HM, Mbiriba Labi JE, Labi AK.
abstractText: Primary intraventricular abscesses are very rare and may be mistaken for intraventricular tumors or other lesions with very few cases reported in literature. Although organisms from the oral cavity are recognized pathogens for brain abscess formation, reports of abscesses caused by Schaalia odontolytica previously known as Actinomyces odontolyticus remain uncommon. This is a case report of a 6-year-old boy with a congenital heart disease (ventricular septal defect and pulmonary atresia) who presented with headaches, fever, neck stiffness and vomiting. Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain showed central T1W hypointense, T2/FLAIR hyperintense collection in the dilated left lateral ventricle with associated periventricular vasogenic oedema indicating a primary intraventricular abscess. The main abscess was drained via a burr hole with persistent small abscesses in the occipital and temporal horns. A second burr hole attempt at draining the occipital and temporal lobe abscesses failed. Cultures of the pus yielded Schaalia odontolytica a known flora of the mouth. No oral lesions were observed in the patient. The patient was managed on 61 days of amoxicillin-clavulanic acid, with erythrocyte sedimentation rate falling from 6 mm/h to 1 mm/h after 2 months of therapy. Primary intraventricular abscess is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition that can present with nonspecific neurological symptoms. In children with cyanotic congenital heart disease, an intracranial abscess should be considered when compatible clinical and neuroimaging findings are present. This case highlights the importance of MRI for diagnosis and microbiological examination of drained material for identification of unusual pathogens such as Schaalia odontolytica.

title: Clinical outcomes with initial oral triple and dual therapy in echocardiography-defined connective tissue disease-associated pulmonary hypertension: a retrospective single-center cohort study.
authorString: Shen X, Chen Q, Ren M, Wang L, Wu J, Cao J, Yin Y, Ren T, Zhou X, Cheng T, Wang M.
abstractText:
Background

Connective tissue disease-associated pulmonary hypertension (CTD-PH) is a serious complication, but evidence on early oral treatment intensification in patients followed primarily by echocardiography is limited. We evaluated outcomes associated with initial selexipag-containing oral triple therapy vs. dual therapy in echocardiography-defined CTD-PH.

Methods

This single-center retrospective cohort included consecutive adults who initiated PH-targeted therapy between April 2020 and June 2025. Treatment was selected by treating physicians in routine care and was not randomized: dual therapy comprised macitentan plus tadalafil, whereas triple therapy additionally included selexipag. Baseline clinical, laboratory, and echocardiographic variables were obtained from standardized institutional assessments and reassessed at week 26. The primary endpoint was the change in the number (0-3) of European Society of Cardiology/European Respiratory Society (ESC/ERS) noninvasive low-risk criteria met: World Health Organization functional class (WHO-FC) I-II, 6-minute walk distance (6MWD) >440 m, and B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) <50 ng/L or N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) <300 ng/L. Complete cases with all three components available at both time points were analyzed without imputation. Disease-progression events were recorded through 30 weeks, and adverse events were assessed during follow-up.

Results

Of 119 patients, 59 received triple therapy and 60 received dual therapy. The groups had similar baseline functional and biomarker profiles (6MWD, 290.0 vs. 286.9 m; NT-proBNP, 1,455 vs. 1,473 pg/mL); mean age was 45.5 vs. 47.2 years in the triple and dual therapy group respectively, and 93% vs. 83% were women. At week 26, the change in low-risk criteria differed between groups (P=0.003), with 57.6% vs. 33.3% meeting all the three criteria. Mean 6MWD increased by 156 vs. 104 m (adjusted difference, 52 m; 95% confidence interval (CI): 29-78; P<0.001), and WHO-FC distributions differed at week 26 (P=0.007). Exploratory analysis yielded an hazard ratio (HR) of 0.75 (95% CI: 0.39-1.43) for the first disease-progression event. At least one adverse event occurred in 53/59 (89.8%) vs. 47/60 (78.3%) patients; diarrhea occurred in 24/59 (40.7%) vs. 19/60 (31.7%), nausea in 21/59 (35.6%) vs. 16/60 (26.7%), and jaw pain in 16/59 (27.1%) vs. 11/60 (18.3%), with no significant between-group differences.

Conclusions

In this real-world cohort of patients with echocardiography-defined CTD-PH, initial selexipag-containing oral triple therapy was associated with greater improvement in noninvasive ESC/ERS risk status and functional outcomes than dual therapy over 26 weeks, supporting further evaluation of noninvasive risk-guided oral treatment intensification in CTD-associated pulmonary vascular disease. However, given the small, single-center, nonrandomized retrospective design, these findings cannot establish superior efficacy or safety and require prospective multicenter confirmation with systematic hemodynamic assessment.

title: Danon disease due to a <i>de novo</i> LAMP2 variant in a girl with d-transposition of the great arteries and a maternally inherited GDF1 variant: a case report.
authorString: Ahamed H, Hari A, Kumar RK, Jha V.
abstractText:
Background

Danon disease, caused by loss-of-function variants in LAMP2, is an X-linked cardioskeletal disorder with cardiac manifestations in heterozygous females that are often underrecognized. The co-occurrence of surgically corrected dextro-transposition of the great arteries (d-TGA) and subsequent Danon cardiomyopathy in a patient carrying a maternally inherited GDF1 variant of uncertain significance has not previously been reported.

Case summary

We describe a girl with d-TGA repaired in the neonatal period who later presented at 12 years of age with progressive dyspnoea on exertion (New York Heart Association class III). She was found to have severe left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH), biventricular outflow tract obstruction, myocardial fibrosis, and non-sustained ventricular tachycardia on ambulatory electrocardiographic (ECG) monitoring. Whole-exome sequencing revealed a de novo pathogenic LAMP2 variant, c.98del (p.Leu33Ter), predicted to disrupt all LAMP2 isoforms, establishing the diagnosis of Danon disease. A maternally inherited GDF1 in-frame deletion, c.651_656del (p.Ala218_Leu219del), was also identified and classified as a variant of uncertain significance; while its clinical significance remains unresolved, it is biologically plausible that the GDF1 variant may have contributed to the congenital heart disease substrate.

Discussion

This case highlights two mechanistically distinct genetic events operating across different developmental windows: a likely susceptibility allele for congenital heart disease and a de novo lysosomal cardiomyopathy causing Danon disease. In patients with repaired congenital heart disease who subsequently develop an otherwise unexplained hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) phenotype, comprehensive cardiomyopathy-focused genetic evaluation may reveal a second diagnosis with major prognostic, therapeutic, and family-screening implications.

title: Temporal patterns of melanopsin-evoked calcium signaling engage NF-κB-associated transcriptional and phosphoproteomic responses.
authorString: Nikpour P, Varas-Godoy M, Tenghamn J, Uhlén P, Smedler E.
abstractText: Cells use oscillatory calcium (Ca2+) signals to regulate diverse biological processes, with temporal dynamics providing a potential layer of intracellular information. We used optogenetic activation of the Gαq-coupled photoreceptor melanopsin to impose defined slow or fast temporal stimulation patterns in human non-excitable cells, evoking oscillatory Ca2+-associated signaling while preserving receptor-proximal signaling. Fast, regular melanopsin stimulation induced stronger nuclear factor κB (NF-κB)-associated tumor necrosis factor (TNF) and interleukin-8 (IL8) expression than temporally irregular stimulation, while TNF and IL8 showed partly distinct responses to stimulation frequency. Transcriptomic analysis identified an MYC-associated gene expression program despite unchanged MYC transcript levels. Integration of transcriptomic and phosphoproteomic datasets identified candidate kinase networks involving PRKDC, CHEK2, and ATM, potentially linking temporally patterned signaling to cell-cycle and stress-response pathways. Together, these findings show that distinct temporal patterns of melanopsin-evoked signaling are associated with distinct transcriptional and phospho-signaling responses, highlighting temporal dynamics as a feature of intracellular information processing.

title: Left bundle branch-optimized cardiac resynchronization therapy in a dextrocardia patient: a case report.
authorString: Aiyasiding X, Yang J, Chen Z, Dai Y, Chen K.
abstractText:
Background

Mirror-image dextrocardia presents unique challenges for cardiac device implantation. Here, we report a case of left bundle branch-optimized cardiac resynchronization therapy (LOT-CRT) for a patient with dextrocardia and heart failure with mid-range ejection fraction (HFmrEF).

Case summary

A 69-year-old woman with mirror-image dextrocardia was electively admitted to our hospital with a complaint of chest distress and shortness of breath. Twenty-four-hour Holter showed sinus arrest with junctional rhythm, intermittent first-degree atrioventricular block with complete left bundle branch block (QRS 154 ms). Echocardiography revealed a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 46%. In contrast to previous research utilizing the modified C315 sheath, the LOT-CRT implant was successfully achieved using a standard-curve C315 delivery sheath. At the 9-month follow-up, the patient demonstrated a significant improvement in LVEF compared with baseline (60% vs. 46%).

Discussion

This case demonstrates the clinical viability of LOT-CRT as a physiologic pacing strategy in patients with congenital heart disease. By directly targeting the conduction system, this approach may circumvent the anatomical challenges posed by traditional biventricular pacing in complex cardiac anatomies, offering a promising therapeutic alternative for resynchronization in select populations.

title: Successful ablation of lower loop re-entry after Starnes procedure in an infant with severe tricuspid valve dysplasia: a case report.
authorString: Hayashi K, Aoki H, Ishii Y, Tanimoto K, Tsumura S.
abstractText:
Background

Tricuspid valve dysplasia (TVD) is a rare right-sided congenital heart disease characterized by severe tricuspid regurgitation and right atrial enlargement, which may predispose to atrial arrhythmias. In severe neonatal cases, the Starnes procedure can be life-saving, but postoperative anatomical alterations may complicate subsequent arrhythmia management.

Case summary

A 2-month-old female infant with TVD and pulmonary atresia developed drug-refractory atypical atrial flutter after the Starnes procedure. Three-dimensional electroanatomical mapping identified lower loop re-entry involving the cavotricuspid isthmus (CTI). Radiofrequency catheter ablation across the CTI successfully terminated the tachycardia. However, atypical flutter recurred 1 week later. During subsequent systemic pulmonary shunt surgery, additional surgical ablation was performed using the prior catheter ablation site as an anatomical landmark. After detaching the tricuspid valve patch, the CTI line was extended to the tricuspid annulus, resulting in complete arrhythmia control.

Discussion

The outcome of this case suggests that foetal-onset volume overload from severe tricuspid regurgitation may promote early atrial remodelling and arrhythmogenic substrate formation in TVD. Although CTI ablation after the Starnes procedure may be feasible in a small infant, patch-related anatomic barriers may prevent complete lesion formation. Prior catheter ablation sites may be useful intraoperative landmarks for successful surgical ablation.

title: Impact of sampling site on Activated Clotting Time (ACT) during cryoballoon ablation: Left atrium vs femoral sheath.
authorString: Margolis G, Berezhnoi K, Goldhaber O, Kobo O, Kazatsker M, Shapira M, Abu-Fanne R, Roguin A, Leshem E.

journal.title: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice

abstractText:
Background

Activated clotting time (ACT) is used to monitor unfractionated heparin (UFH) during left atrial (LA) ablation procedures. Inadequate anticoagulation increases thromboembolic risk, while excessive UFH may increase bleeding. ACT can be sampled from a femoral venous sheath (ACTFV) or from oxygenated blood within the LA (ACTLA). The influence of sampling site on ACT values during atrial fibrillation ablation is unknown.

Methods

In this prospective observational study, consecutive patients undergoing cryoballoon pulmonary vein isolation received intravenous UFH. ACT was sampled sequentially from the LA and from a femoral venous sheath. All samples were analyzed on the same point-of-care ACT machine. Non-inferiority of LA relative to femoral venous sampling was tested against a 30-s margin, with agreement assessed by Cohen's kappa at 300 s and Bland-Altman analysis.

Results

Sixty-two patients were recruited (42% female; CHA2DS2-VASc 3.1 ± 1.8); 61 had paired samples. Mean ACTLA was 365 ± 83 and ACTFV was 359 ± 65 s (p = 0.455). The mean paired difference (ACTLA - ACTFV) was +6.1 s (upper one-sided 97.5% confidence limit +22.4 s), below the 30-s non-inferiority margin (p = 0.002). Bland-Altman limits of agreement were - 119 to +131 s, with significant proportional bias (β = 0.288, p = 0.017). Dichotomized at 300 s, Cohen's kappa was 0.586 (moderate concordance).

Conclusions

ACT sampling from the LA was non-inferior to femoral venous sampling within a 30-s margin, supporting the use of either sampling site during LA ablation. Despite notable variability between paired measurements, unexpected ACT values should prompt repeat testing rather than be attributed to the sampling site.

title: Aborted sudden cardiac death in children and adolescents-from acute management to diagnosis.
authorString: Kwok SY, Webster G.
abstractText: Aborted sudden cardiac death (SCD) in children and adolescents is terrifying for patients and families. Inherited arrhythmia syndromes, cardiomyopathies, and coronary anomalies are the most common associations. This review provides a comprehensive framework for diagnostic evaluation in survivors of resuscitated sudden cardiac arrest. After hemodynamic stabilization and neuroprotection, evaluation often requires data retrieval, structured cardiac phenotyping, and obtaining samples to assess for molecular, metabolic or toxicology analysis. A tiered approach is essential. A surface electrocardiogram (ECG) and echocardiography remain first line investigations. Primary electrical diseases may be evident on a standard and modified ECG, including Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome, conduction abnormalities, myocardial ischemia, and some cardiac channelopathies. Early echocardiography assesses structural heart disease, cardiomyopathies and myocarditis. Special attention should be paid to anomalous origin of the coronary arteries and recent work has emphasized the importance of mitral annular disjunction. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, exercise stress testing, and drug provocation testing can be useful supplements to reveal concealed substrates. Genetic testing is vital for precision medicine and cascade family screening, often requiring a multidisciplinary team to assess variants of uncertain significance (VUS) and complex genomic findings. Ultimately, the critical step is genotype-phenotype correlation, where the team determines whether the genetic and clinical data reinforce one another to provide a diagnosis, refine treatment, and prevent future tragedies within affected families.

title: Growth trajectories in exclusively breastfed infants with clinically diagnosed food allergy: a prospective longitudinal cohort study.
authorString: Fang J, Zhang Z, Zhong Y, Wan Y, Chen Q, Xia X, Zhang X.
abstractText:
Background

Food allergy (FA) in infancy may be accompanied by feeding difficulties and dietary modifications during breastfeeding, which may influence early growth. However, longitudinal growth patterns in exclusively breastfed infants with clinically diagnosed FA remain incompletely characterized.

Methods

In this prospective longitudinal cohort study, 73 exclusively breastfed infants (30 with FA and 43 without FA) were enrolled at 4-6 months of age and followed through infancy. A total of 268 anthropometric observations were included in the longitudinal analysis. Weight-for-length Z-score (WLZ), weight-for-age Z-score (WAZ), length-for-age Z-score (LAZ), and head circumference-for-age Z-score (HCZ) were calculated according to the WHO Child Growth Standards. Growth trajectories were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models with infant-specific random intercepts. Age was modeled continuously and centered at 5 months. Sensitivity analyses examined nonlinear age effects and group-by-sex interactions.

Results

Maternal dietary avoidance was substantially more common among mothers of infants with FA than among those without FA (83.3% vs. 18.6%, p < 0.001). In the longitudinal WLZ model, the estimated difference between the NFA and FA groups at 5 months was 0.423 Z-score units (95% CI 0.036 to 0.811, p = 0.035), with lower estimated WLZ in the FA group. There was no evidence of a group-by-age interaction (estimate = -0.011, 95% CI - 0.086 to 0.063, p = 0.763), indicating no detectable difference in the linear rate of WLZ change between groups. Sensitivity analysis did not support a nonlinear WLZ trajectory, and no group-by-sex interaction was detected.

Conclusion

Infants with clinically diagnosed FA had lower estimated WLZ around 5 months of age than infants without FA, but the longitudinal analysis did not provide evidence that WLZ changed at a different linear rate between groups over time. Maternal dietary avoidance was substantially more common among mothers of infants with FA, underscoring the importance of appropriate nutritional counseling and growth monitoring in this population.

title: Effects of early cardiac exercise rehabilitation on the recovery of cardiac function in patients following open heart surgery.
authorString: Cai H, Cai L, Ding M, Li H, Chen S.
abstractText:
Introduction

This study aims to investigate the short-term effect of early cardiac exercise rehabilitation on the recovery of cardiac function in patients who have undergone open heart surgery.

Methods

A total of 120 patients who performed open heart surgery from January 2019 to December 2021 were divided into an experimental group (n = 60) and a control group (n = 60). The control group received standard nursing by nurses while the experimental group participated in early cardiac exercise rehabilitation training. The postoperative cardiac function (at discharge and 3 months after operation), gastrointestinal peristalsis recovery, infection rate, readmission rate, and patient satisfaction of both groups were assessed.

Results

The experimental group demonstrated lower infection rate, reduced readmission rate, higher patient satisfaction, and better postoperative cardiac function at 3 months after operation than the control group (P < 0.05). There was no significant difference in the postoperative cardiac function at discharge and the recovery time of gastrointestinal peristalsis between two groups (p > 0.05).

Discussion

In conclusions, early cardiac exercise rehabilitation training during the perioperative period can help to improve the recovery of cardiac function in a short term for patients who have undergone open heart surgery. At the same time, early cardiac exercise rehabilitation also helped to reduce postoperative infections and readmission, and improve patient satisfaction..

title: Highly vascularized left atrial myxoma mimicking a cardiac haemangioma: a case report.
authorString: Pérez Barrios S, Aragón González JM, Fajardo Perdomo HN, Rodríguez Mora F, González Calle A.
abstractText:
Background

Primary cardiac tumours are rare; atrial myxomas predominate, while haemangiomas represent only 1%-2.8%. Differentiating them is challenging when hypervascular features overlap.

Case summary

An 81-year-old woman presented with a large, hypervascular left atrial mass supplied by the circumflex artery. Following uneventful surgical resection, histopathology confirmed a cardiac myxoma despite imaging suggesting a haemangioma.

Discussion

Hypervascularity cannot reliably distinguish myxomas from haemangiomas. Although multimodal imaging is important for surgical planning, definitive diagnosis relies strictly on histopathological evaluation.

title: SHROOM3 promotes leading-edge protrusion stability and Wnt/planar cell polarity-mediated migration in breast cancer cells

journal.title: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

title: Hemorrhage distribution, imaging-defined post-hemorrhagic ventricular dilatation, and clinical outcomes in neonates with intraventricular and cerebral parenchymal hemorrhage: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Zhang X, Cai Y, Huang S, Shi H, Chen L, Wu S, Xiang Y.
abstractText:
Objective

Neonatal intracranial hemorrhage contributes substantially to neonatal mortality and neurodevelopmental impairment. This retrospective single-center cohort study aimed to investigate associations between hemorrhage anatomical distribution, post-haemorrhagic ventricular dilation severity, and clinical outcomes among neonates with intraventricular and/or cerebral parenchymal hemorrhage, and to identify factors associated with mortality and Neurodevelopmental abnormality.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study included 109 neonates with intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) and/or cerebral parenchymal hemorrhage (CPH) hospitalized at Hunan Children's Hospital from 2015 to 2018. Patients were classified into isolated IVH, isolated CPH, and combined IVH with parenchymal involvement groups. Clinical characteristics, systemic comorbidities, PHVD severity, treatment interventions, and follow-up outcomes were analyzed. MRI findings were additionally evaluated in infants who underwent examination. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with clinical outcomes.

Results

Among the 109 neonates, 44 (40.4%) had isolated IVH, 41 (37.6%) had isolated CPH, and 24 (22.0%) had combined IVH and parenchymal involvement. Imaging-defined post-hemorrhagic ventricular dilatation (PHVD) severity differed significantly among groups (P < 0.001), with moderate-to-severe imaging-defined PHVD occurring in 61.4%, 24.4%, and 70.8% of patients, respectively. Overall outcomes included 41 deaths (37.6%), 21 cases of Neurodevelopmental abnormality (19.3%), and 47 favorable outcomes (43.1%), with no significant difference among hemorrhage groups (P = 0.693). MRI provided additional identification of deep, posterior fossa, subarachnoid, and small focal hemorrhagic lesions. Lower gestational age and higher clinical severity scores were independently associated with mortality, whereas cerebrospinal fluid drainage or neurosurgical intervention was associated with lower odds of Neurodevelopmental abnormality (OR = 0.115, 95% CI: 0.022-0.595, P = 0.010). This observed association cannot be interpreted as causal or preventive therapeutic effect owing to inherent selection and survivorship bias in a retrospective observational study.

Conclusion

Hemorrhage distribution was associated with PHVD severity but not independently with mortality or Neurodevelopmental abnormality. Ventricular involvement identifies infants at higher risk of significant hydrocephalus, while gestational maturity and systemic disease burden remain important determinants of outcome. Ultrasound and MRI provide complementary information for clinical assessment. The observed association between cerebrospinal fluid-directed drainage or neurosurgical intervention and favourable neurological outcomes should be interpreted cautiously. Given the retrospective non-randomized nature of this cohort, causal inference regarding preventive benefit of these interventions is not feasible.

title: Challenging the guidelines: longitudinal trends in left ventricular diameter and function in severe aortic regurgitation.
authorString: Schwartzenberg S, Berkowitz A, Lerman TT, Bental T, Vaturi M, Goldberg Y, Shapira Y.
abstractText:
Background

Guidelines recommend aortic valve replacement (AVR) in patients with severe aortic regurgitation (AR) based on progressive changes in left ventricular (LV) function or size. We aimed to reassess the clinical relevance of current guideline recommendations pertaining to traditional echocardiographic measurements in routine practice.

Methods

Retrospective analysis of patients with severe AR who underwent serial echocardiographic follow-up over at least 18 months. The composite outcome was symptom-driven AVR, acute heart failure hospitalization, or death. We used a joint modelling approach to handle within-subject correlation and censoring.

Results

The cohort consisted of 140 patients, with a median follow-up of 93 months (interquartile range 58-130). LV end-systolic (LVESD) and fractional shortening (FS) showed a small but statistically significant longitudinal trend, while LVEDD did not. In three separate joint models adjusted for age at onset and sex, higher LVESD and LVEDD and lower FS were each associated with increased risk of the composite event. Each 1 mm increase in LVESD and LVEDD was associated with a 6% in risk; each 1% decrease in FS corresponded to a 12% increase in risk. Only 8 (5.7%) of patients were predicted to exceed the guideline-recommended LVEDD threshold of 65 mm over 10 years. Age at onset was also a significant risk factor, with each decade increasing risk by 65% for each of the three parallel joint models.

Conclusion

LV parameters show modest changes over time, despite holding strong prognostic value in patients with severe AR. LVEDD, while associated with overall risk, does not predictably or significantly dilate over time in most patients. AVR decisions should be based on comprehensive clinical and volumetric assessment rather than waiting for simple linear progression to guideline cutoffs.

title: Clinical Correlates and Prognostic Value of Low QRS Voltages in Non-Ischemic Dilated Cardiomyopathy: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Li T, Tian T, Zhang X, Gao Z, Zhang L, Gong S, Deng X, Qin M, Zhang Y, Qin Z, Luo X.
abstractText:
Background

Data on the prognostic significance of low QRS voltage (LQRSV) in non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (NIDCM) are limited. Therefore, this study aimed to determine whether LQRSV is associated with a composite endpoint of all-cause mortality or heart failure (HF) re-hospitalization in patients with NIDCM.

Methods

Patients with NIDCM who met predefined criteria were retrospectively enrolled and divided into LQRSV and non-LQRSV groups based on electrocardiographic findings. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality or HF re-hospitalization. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, cardiovascular (CV) death, and HF re-hospitalization. The prognostic significance of LQRSV was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) functions were applied to examine potential nonlinear relationships between continuous QRS voltage and the primary outcome. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were used to assess predictive performance. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to balance baseline characteristics, and sensitivity and subgroup analyses were conducted to test the robustness of the findings.

Results

The overall cohort included 784 consecutive patients with NIDCM (median age 56 years; 30% female). During a median follow-up of 1079 days, 335 primary outcome events occurred. After PSM, 463 patients were matched, with 186 in the LQRSV group and 277 in the non-LQRSV group. In the matched cohort, Kaplan-Meier analysis with the log-rank test showed that the LQRSV group had a significantly worse long-term prognosis than the non-LQRSV group (p < 0.001). Multivariable Cox analyses demonstrated that LQRSV was significantly associated with the composite of all-cause mortality or HF re-hospitalization (hazard ratio, (HR) 2.048, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.519-2.760; p < 0.001), all-cause mortality (HR 2.526, 95% CI 1.660-3.844; p < 0.001), and CV death (HR 2.820, 95% CI 1.776-4.476; p < 0.001). RCS analyses showed a linear association (p for nonlinearity > 0.05), with the highest risk observed at the lowest QRS voltage amplitudes. ROC analysis revealed that incorporating LQRSV into the clinical model significantly increased the area under the curve (0.808 vs. 0.723; p < 0.001).

Conclusions

LQRSV is associated with poor prognosis in NIDCM. Routine electrocardiographic assessment of QRS voltage may provide valuable information for risk stratification.

title: Case Report: Familial <i>TBX4</i>-related developmental lung disease: two siblings with fatal neonatal respiratory failure.
authorString: Thiruvenkataramani RP, Mohamed T, Pugmire MV, Omar SA.
abstractText:
Background

T-box transcription factor 4 (TBX4) is a critical regulator of lung and pulmonary vascular development. Pathogenic TBX4 variants are associated with developmental lung disease, pulmonary hypertension, and neonatal respiratory failure.

Case presentation

We report two siblings with lethal neonatal respiratory failure. The first, a term female infant, died at 11 h of life, and her late-preterm male sibling died at 9 h despite maximal intensive care. Both developed severe hypoxemia and pulmonary hypertension. Autopsy demonstrated marked pulmonary hypoplasia. Whole-exome sequencing identified a novel heterozygous TBX4 variant, c.741G>C (p.Lys247Asn), inherited from their unaffected father. Preimplantation genetic testing detected the variant in seven of 10 embryos.

Conclusion

These cases expand the spectrum of TBX4-associated developmental lung disease and support consideration of TBX4 testing in neonates with unexplained respiratory failure and pulmonary hypertension.

title: Frontal QRS-T angle in patients with Graves' disease: association with thyroid function and cardiovascular parameters.
authorString: Kłosowicz M, Urbańczuk M, Burbelka A, Gala-Błądzińska A, Balawender K.
abstractText:
Introduction

Thyroid hormone excess may alter ventricular electrophysiology, affecting both depolarization and repolarization. The frontal QRS-T (fQRS-T) angle reflects the directional relationship between these processes and may provide information on ventricular electrical heterogeneity. However, data on the fQRS-T angle in overt hyperthyroidism (OHT) remain limited. We evaluated the fQRS-T angle in patients with Graves' disease presenting with OHT compared with euthyroid controls.

Materials and methods

This retrospective single-center study included 55 patients with Graves' disease and biochemically confirmed OHT and 42 euthyroid controls. Frontal QRS and T axes were calculated from ECG measurements in leads I and aVF. Between-group comparisons, multivariable regression adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, and heart rate, sensitivity analyses, ROC analysis, and correlations with thyroid function parameters were performed. Results: The median fQRS-T angle was greater in patients with OHT than in controls (21.89° [12.37-44.09] vs. 17.36° [9.02-27.29], p = 0.006), with a rank-biserial correlation of 0.328 (95% CI 0.106-0.535). An fQRS-T angle >45° occurred in 23.6% of patients with OHT and in none of the controls (p < 0.001), whereas the QRS and T axes did not differ significantly between groups. After adjustment for age, sex, body mass index, and heart rate, OHT remained associated with a greater fQRS-T angle (β = 9.00°, 95% CI 1.77-16.22; p = 0.015), with consistent findings in sensitivity analyses. Discriminatory performance was modest (AUC 0.664, 95% CI 0.552-0.768). No significant associations were observed between fQRS-T angle and FT3, FT4, TSH, or heart rate.

Discussion

Patients with Graves' disease and OHT exhibited greater discordance between ventricular depolarization and repolarization despite similar individual QRS and T axes. This association persisted after adjustment for heart rate and other potential confounders, suggesting that fQRS-T widening may reflect electrophysiological alterations associated with OHT rather than tachycardia alone.

Conclusion

Overt hyperthyroidism due to Graves' disease is associated with a wider fQRS-T angle independently of age, sex, body mass index, and heart rate. Larger prospective, multicenter studies with longitudinal ECG assessment are needed to determine the reversibility and prognostic significance of these alterations.

title: Partial trisomy 19p13.3-p13.2 from antenatal diagnosis to 7-year follow-up: case report and literature review.
authorString: Abualnaja R, Azher Z, Alkhaifi S, Alkharouby R.
abstractText: Partial trisomy of the short arm of chromosome 19 (19p) is a rare chromosomal abnormality with significant clinical implications. We report the prenatal diagnosis and 7-year follow-up of a boy with partial trisomy 19p13.3-p13.2 and multiple congenital anomalies including microcephaly, unilateral hydronephrosis, mild bilateral hearing loss, failure to thrive, and global developmental delay. The pregnancy was complicated by antenatal findings of severe oligohydramnios and severe intrauterine growth restriction. Amniocentesis with chromosomal microarray analysis identified a 6.8 Mb copy number gain involving chromosome 19p13.3-p13.2, arr [GRCh37] 19p13.3-p13.2 (260,911_7,089,557)x3. Maternal cytogenetic analysis revealed an apparently balanced reciprocal translocation involving chromosome 13 and 19, supporting inheritance through unbalanced chromosomal segregation. The cytogenetic and clinical findings of our patient are discussed in this report. To our knowledge, this is the first report of partial trisomy 19p13.3-p13.2 as a result of maternal reciprocal translocation in the Middle East.

title: PIK3R2-related megalencephaly syndrome: expanded phenotypic spectrum associated with craniosynostosis.
authorString: Digkas E, Körberg IB, Mourtos E, Nowinski D, Aravidis C.
abstractText:
Background

Megalencephaly-polymicrogyria-polydactyly-hydrocephalus (MPPH) syndrome is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder caused by activating variants in the PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling pathway, most frequently in PIK3R2. The recurrent variant c.1117G > A (p.Gly373Arg) has been associated with classical MPPH features including megalencephaly, bilateral polymicrogyria, hydrocephalus, and polydactyly. However, the phenotypic spectrum is still expanding.

Methods

We describe a 7-year-old girl with developmental delay, epilepsy, and structural brain anomalies. Trio-based whole exome sequencing followed by Sanger validation was performed. Clinical and radiological evaluations were conducted, including brain MRI, CT, and ophthalmological assessment.

Results

The patient exhibited congenital megalencephaly, bilateral perisylvian and parietotemporal polymicrogyria, and hypotonia. She lacked polydactyly but presented with complex bicoronal and sagittal craniosynostosis, representing a potential novel association with this variant. Imaging revealed signs of chronic intracranial hypertension, including optic nerve tortuosity, papilledema, pituitary flattening, and gyral impressions. A heterozygous de novo PIK3R2 c.1117G > A (p.Gly373Arg) variant was identified and classified as pathogenic.

Conclusion

This report broadens the phenotypic spectrum of PIK3R2-related MPPH syndrome by describing a potential novel association with craniosynostosis, accompanied by radiologic signs of intracranial hypertension. The findings support the inclusion of PIK3R2 in genetic work-ups for patients with cortical malformations, megalencephaly, and syndromic presentations-even in the absence of polydactyly.

title: Spatial profiling of Kawasaki disease cardiac inflammation identifies STING as a therapeutic target

title: The Temporal Investigation of Multimodal Elements (TIME) Study: protocol for an observational, longitudinal study to characterize the dynamic structure of molecular and digital data in older adults in stable health.
authorString: Yurkovich JT, Glass E, Nash AN, Levine N, Lee S, Ehlen K, Hernandez E, Gharti P, Senadheera C, Fernando A, Witherington D, Pflieger L, Erram J, Rappaport N, Le A, Newman JC, Stubbs BJ.
abstractText:
Background

Biological systems exhibit dynamic patterns over multiple temporal scales-from minutes to months-that are poorly captured by conventional cross-sectional or low-frequency longitudinal studies. These patterns, including diurnal variations and underlying continuous rhythms, may be critical determinants of health, resilience, and disease risk in aging. Existing longitudinal studies in older adults lack high-frequency, multimodal measurements that integrate molecular, physiological, and digital health data streams.

Objectives

The TIME Study aims to: (i) Characterize temporal patterns in molecular, physiological, and digital health measures in healthy older adults; (ii) determine how these patterns vary across biological domains and relate to each other; and (iii) assess how physiological systems respond to defined perturbations (oral glucose tolerance and maximal exercise).

Methods

TIME is a single-site, observational, longitudinal study enrolling up to 150 adults aged ≥55 years. Over an 11-week main phase, participants complete seven weekly low-frequency visits, two perturbation challenge visits, and two, two-day high-frequency sampling epochs. Biospecimens, clinical measures, cognitive and physical performance tests, and continuous digital health data are collected. Follow-up visits occur at 6 and 12 months.

Expected impact

By integrating multimodal, temporally resolved data, TIME will provide a foundational dataset for understanding the role of biological rhythms in aging and inform future precision health strategies.Clinical Trial Registration: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07107386, identifier NCT07107386.

title: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance-derived hemodynamics predict adverse outcomes after Fontan palliation.
authorString: Platnick C, Frank B, Romanowicz J, Gonzalez De Alba C, Chase M, Umer A, Chaudhuri NR, Awori J, Chauhan D, Mascio CE, Udassi JP, Hedjazi Moghari M.
abstractText:
Background

Long-term outcomes following the Fontan procedure remain heterogeneous, and robust imaging-based predictors of adverse events are limited. Patients residing at moderate-altitude may experience additional pulmonary vascular stress; however, the prognostic value of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived flow parameters in this population are not well defined.

Methods

We performed a retrospective cohort study of Fontan patients followed at a single moderate-altitude center who were ≥5 years post-Fontan and had undergone comprehensive CMR exams. Demographic, anatomic, and surgical data were collected. CMR-derived variables included indexed ventricular volumes and function, systemic arterial dimensions, and flow indices in the ascending and descending aorta, superior vena cava (SVC), inferior vena cava, and branch pulmonary arteries.The primary composite outcome was death or referral/listing for heart transplantation. Time-to-event analyses from the time of CMR were performed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and Cox proportional hazards regression.

Results

A total of 182 Fontan patients were included (median age at Fontan 3.2 years [interquartile range (IQR) 2.6-3.9]; median time from Fontan to CMR 10.9 years [IQR 7.7-14.2]). Over a median follow-up of 4.7 years following CMR (IQR 3.1-6.6), 14 patients (7.7%) experienced the primary outcome. In univariable Cox regression, a higher SVC flow index was significantly associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome [hazard ratio [HR] 0.70 per 0.1 L/min/m2 increase; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.50-0.92; p = 0.008].

Conclusions

In this moderate-altitude Fontan cohort, reduced CMR-derived SVC flow index was significantly associated with the primary outcome. This finding suggests that systemic venous flow merits further investigation as a prognostic marker in the Fontan population.

title: Divergent PICU lengths of stay despite identical phoenix sepsis scores: heterogeneity in pediatric sepsis outcomes according to system involvement profiles.
authorString: Jiang Z, Wu L, Zhou X, Xu J, Xiong X, Chen J, Hu Y.
abstractText:
Objective

This study examined how different subsystem involvement patterns in the Phoenix Sepsis Score relate to PICU length of stay among children with sepsis, focusing on patients with identical total scores, and explored clinical factors associated with these differences.

Methods

We retrospectively included 107 children with sepsis admitted to a single PICU (2024-2025). Patients were grouped by the number of affected Phoenix subsystems (respiratory, coagulation, circulatory, neurological): single-system (n = 37), dual-system (n = 62), and multi-system (n = 8). We further compared the largest subgroups with identical total scores of 2-isolated respiratory involvement (n = 29) versus respiratory-coagulation involvement (n = 59). Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of prolonged PICU stay (≥10 days), and the association between IMV and PICU length of stay was further explored.

Results

Respiratory and/or coagulation involvement accounted for 89.7% (96/107) of cases, with the respiratory-coagulation combination being most frequent (55.1%). The multi-system group had the highest total scores, lactate levels, and mortality (37.5%, all P < 0.05). Despite identical total scores [2 (2, 2), P = 0.457], the isolated respiratory group had significantly prolonged PICU stay [10 (9, 12) vs. 6 (4, 8) days, P < 0.001], higher ventilation rates (100% vs. 25.4%, P < 0.001), and longer ventilation duration [6 (4, 7) vs. 0 (0, 0) days, P < 0.001]. Invasive ventilation was the strongest risk factor for prolonged stay (OR=18.80, 95% CI: 3.78-123.24, P < 0.001). Adjusting for ventilation attenuated the group effect from OR=6.92 (P < 0.001) to OR=1.27 (P = 0.739), suggesting that the subgroup difference in PICU length of stay was largely explained by the higher IMV use in the single-respiratory group. Since IMV is part of the Phoenix respiratory subscore, this attenuation likely reflects shared information rather than formal mediation.

Conclusions

In septic children with the same Phoenix total score, different system involvement patterns yield substantially different outcomes and resource use. A respiratory subsystem score ≥2 signals high risk of prolonged PICU stay, largely explained by the greater need for invasive ventilation. The total Phoenix score alone is insufficient for resource planning; the respiratory component may provide additional information beyond the total score.

title: Integrated clinical and laboratory assessment for severity classification in pediatric pertussis.
authorString: Wang X, Zhu X.
abstractText:
Background

Early identification of children with severe pertussis is essential for timely intervention and improved clinical outcomes.

Objective

To assess clinical and laboratory characteristics associated with severe pertussis and to evaluate their ability to classify severe disease at admission among hospitalised children.

Methodology

This retrospective cohort study included 722 children aged 1 month-13 years with laboratory-confirmed pertussis admitted from January 2020 to December 2025. Clinically diagnosed, laboratory-unconfirmed cases were excluded. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, radiological, and outcome data were extracted from electronic medical records. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with severe pertussis, with model performance assessed by AUC. Because several predictors contributed to the definition of severe disease, the integrated model was interpreted as a concurrent classification model. A second model using demographic, historical, and admission laboratory variables was interpreted as an admission-time severity classification model. Bootstrap internal validation and calibration were performed.

Results

Severe pertussis occurred in 157 children (21.7%). In the concurrent model, apnea and respiratory distress were strongly associated with severe disease but were not interpreted as independent predictors because they formed part of the severity definition. Age <6 months, prematurity, incomplete-for-age or absent vaccination, radiological pneumonia, marked leukocytosis, hypoalbuminemia, and low immunoglobulin G (IgG) levels were also independently associated with severe disease (all p < 0.05). The apparent AUC was 0.89 (sensitivity 83.4%, specificity 82.1%, accuracy 82.4%), although this performance may be overestimated because of outcome-information leakage. In the admission-time model, age <6 months, incomplete-for-age or absent vaccination, higher white blood cell and absolute lymphocyte counts, and lower albumin and IgG levels were independently associated with severe pertussis. For the admission-time model, AUC was 0.961 (95% CI 0.947-0.975), with an optimism-corrected figure of 0.957, an apparent measure of discrimination that should not be taken as a measure of prediction of clinical deterioration.

Conclusion

Severe pertussis was associated with distinct demographic and laboratory abnormalities, with admission-time variables showing strong discrimination for severe disease. Given that many severe cases met severity criteria at the index event, the admission-time model should not be interpreted as prognostic for subsequent deterioration.

title: Overexpression of TUBA1A suppresses bladder cancer progression with potential modulation of autophagic activity and macrophage polarization.
authorString: Song DM, Lu H, Shu YC, Xu JJ, He YB, Duan H, Jin YY, Chen SL, Duan SC, Jing GH, Wen JM, Tong M.
abstractText:
Background

Bladder urothelial carcinoma (BUC) exhibits high recurrence and poor prognosis, with limited efficacy of current immunotherapies. The role of the aggrephagy-related gene TUBA1A in the BUC immune microenvironment remains unclear.

Methods

Single-cell transcriptomic data from public repositories were analyzed to characterize the immune microenvironment. Non-negative matrix factorization identified aggrephagy-related immune-stromal subtypes, and CellChat mapped intercellular interactions. TIDE validation and KEGG enrichment defined functional modules. TUBA1A expression and function were evaluated through qRT-PCR, Western blot, proliferation, migration, apoptosis assays, and transmission electron microscopy. THP-1-derived macrophages were treated with conditioned medium from control or TUBA1A-overexpressing bladder cancer cells in the presence or absence of the autophagy inhibitor chloroquine (CQ), and polarization markers were assessed by flow cytometry and qRT-PCR. In vivo xenograft models verified tumor growth effects.

Results

Single-cell analysis identified a TUBA1A-high macrophage subset with strong immune communication and immune activity. TUBA1A was significantly downregulated in BUC tissues and cell lines. TUBA1A overexpression inhibited proliferation, migration, and invasion, promoted apoptosis, and enhanced autophagic activity (increased LC3-II and ATG5, reduced SQSTM1/p62, and elevated autophagic vesicles). Conditioned medium from TUBA1A-overexpressing cells promoted M1-like polarization; CQ abolished the induction of the M1 markers IL-12 and CD86. In vivo, TUBA1A overexpression significantly suppressed xenograft tumor growth and reduced Ki-67 expression.

Conclusion

TUBA1A is downregulated in BUC and acts as a candidate regulator of autophagic activity and macrophage polarization. TUBA1A overexpression is associated with inhibition of BUC progression, and its promotion of M1-like macrophage polarization appears to require autophagic activity. TUBA1A may represent a promising biomarker and therapeutic target for BUC.

title: Prevalence of iron deficiency anaemia and associated factors among preterm infants aged 3-6 months attending clinics in Dodoma, Tanzania: a facility-based cross-sectional study.
authorString: Mchwampaka C, Mahamba D, Jumanne S, Msuya MA, Matovelo S.
abstractText:
Background

Iron deficiency anaemia (IDA) among preterm infants is a global public health problem due to its effects on development, immunity and general growth that may be irreversible. Despite the high burden of preterm births in Tanzania the prevalence and factors associated with Iron deficiency anaemia (IDA) among preterm infants remain relatively understudied. Therefore, the study aimed to determine the prevalence of iron deficiency anaemia and associated factors among preterm infants aged 3-6 Months attending clinics in Dodoma, Tanzania.

Methods

A hospital-based analytical cross-sectional study was conducted from 1st August, 2023 to 1st January, 2024, among 190 preterm infants who attended clinics in Dodoma. A structured questionnaire adopted from previous study was used to collect data from study participants. A univariable and multivariable binary logistic regression analyses were used to assess the strength of association between variables. The final results from the binary logistic regression model were presented using Adjusted Odd's Ratio (AOR), 95% Confidence Interval (CI), p < 0.05. The data were analyzed using the Statistical Package of Social Science IBM SPSS version 26.

Results

The prevalence of IDA among preterm infants was 11.58%. Factors significantly associated with IDA included very low birth weight (<1.5 kg) (AOR = 6.91, 95% CI: 1.47-32.36, p = 0.014), lack of iron supplementation (AOR = 6.28, 95% CI: 1.05-37.76, p = 0.045), multiple pregnant (AOR = 6.85, 95% CI: 1.69-27.71, p = 0.007), and maternal haemoglobin before delivery (AOR = 12.00, 95% CI: 2.70-53.34, p = 0.001).

Conclusion

IDA remains an important concern among preterm infants in Dodoma. Strengthening iron supplementation and early identification of high-risk infants, particularly those with very low birth weight, multiple gestation, or maternal anaemia, may help reduce the burden of IDA.

title: Case Report: Genetic diagnosis and counseling for recurrent holoprosencephaly: a case of parental balanced translocation.
authorString: Ge T, Zhang C, Hao Y, Cheng S, Zhou B, Wang X, Cao Y, Lin X.
abstractText:
Introduction

Holoprosencephaly (HPE) is a severe developmental anomaly of the brain, resulting from the failure of forebrain vesicle division during fetal development. Chromosomal abnormalities, such as trisomy 13 and trisomy 18, along with copy number variations (CNVs), are implicated in the pathogenesis of HPE. Furthermore, over 20 genes have been implicated in the pathogenesis of HPE, with SHH (MIM: 600725), ZIC2 (MIM: 603073), TGIF (MIM: 602630), and SIX3 (MIM: 603714) identified as the primary causative genes. This study aims to investigate the genetic causes underlying recurrent holoprosencephaly in a specific couple and to offer genetic counseling and reproductive guidance.

Case presentation

A 31-year-old woman with a history of 9 naturally conceived pregnancies, all ending in first-trimester miscarriage or fetal structural abnormalities. She is a balanced translocation, characterized by a chromosomal karyotype of 46,XX,t(3; 13)(q27; q31). In three instances, pregnancies advanced beyond 12 weeks and were complicated by fetal nuchal cystic hygroma and holoprosencephaly. In this study, prenatal diagnostic procedures were conducted on the last two pregnancies, identifying a duplication of approximately 12.74 Mb in the q27.2q29 region of chromosome 3 and a heterozygous deletion of approximately 21.78 Mb in the q31.3q34 region of chromosome 13 in the fetuses.

Conclusion

In cases of recurrent miscarriages and abnormal fetal structures, it is imperative to perform karyotype analysis and related genetic tests. Upon elucidating the etiology, genetic counseling and reproductive interventions should be offered to mitigate the risk of chromosomally abnormal fetuses during pregnancy and to safeguard the physical and mental wellbeing of pregnant women.

title: Hemodynamic and biomechanical impact of proximal aortic surgery on the cardiovascular system: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: van Sambeeck PS, Hermans BP, Nauta FJH, Hasami NA, Saouti N, Verkroost MWA, Trimarchi S, Czerny M, Heijmen RH.
abstractText:
Background

The consequences of proximal aortic (PA) replacement with a stiff vascular prosthesis remain insufficiently understood. This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to consolidate evidence regarding the hemodynamic and biomechanical effects of PA surgery on the cardiovascular system.

Methods

Four databases were searched on April 16th, 2025. Clinical and experimental studies reporting hemodynamic or biomechanical outcomes after PA compliance alterations were included. Exclusion criteria comprised non-original work, computational models, acute procedures, interventions beyond the PA, and PA constriction surgeries. Primary outcomes reflected cardiac functioning, hemodynamics, and aortic biomechanics.

Results

Thirteen studies (six clinical, seven experimental) were included. Six studies measured changes pre- and post-intervention, seven studies compared changes to a control group. Pulse pressure (investigated in four studies) significantly increased in one experimental study (37.7±5.9 vs. 49.2±6.9 mmHg, P=0.01). Left ventricular mass (one study) increased significantly following stiff prosthetic replacement versus optimal medical therapy (+3.67±4.1 vs. +0.62±4.4 g/m², P<0.001). Blood flow velocity of the PA (two studies) showed significant increases in both studies. Two (of five) studies reported significant increases in aortic wall mechanics parameters including mean wall shear stress (WSS) (0.31 vs. 0.82 Pa, P=0.04) and maximal WSS (0.55 vs. 1.11 Pa, P=0.04). Meta-analysis (four studies) found increased distensibility [standardized mean change score (SMCC) 0.50, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.24-0.76, k=3] and circumferential strain (SMCC 0.55, 95% CI: 0.00-1.10, k=3) of the descending aorta. Ejection fraction (SMCC 0.08, 95% CI: -0.29-0.45, k=3) and pulse pressure (SMCC 0.47, 95% CI: -0.36-1.31, k=3) remained unchanged. Certainty of evidence was very low, and risk of bias was moderate.

Conclusions

PA stiffening due to a vascular prosthesis appears to have limited systemic hemodynamic effects, likely due to compensatory mechanisms (e.g. increased left ventricular mass and distal aortic adaptation). Local distensibility, WSS and flow dynamics are adversely affected.

title: Multicenter experience of hybrid transcatheter pulmonary valve implantation in patients with a large right ventricular outflow tract.
authorString: Dong J, Su J, Liu A, Wen S, Fan T, An Q, Jia B, Ye M, Zhang G, Jin Y, Li Y, Zhou C, Zheng B, Xu J.
abstractText:
Background

Management of pulmonary regurgitation (PR) in patients with a large and dysplastic native right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) remains a significant challenge for percutaneous intervention. Given the limitations of percutaneous intervention in patients with a large and morphologically complex RVOT, this study aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of a hybrid transcatheter pulmonary valve implantation (TPVI) strategy using a self-expanding valve in this patient population.

Methods

Between June 2021 and December 2023, 102 patients with moderate-to-severe PR and dilated RVOT from 11 centers underwent hybrid TPVI with the Salus transcatheter pulmonary valve (TPV). Procedural strategies, including surgical access and concomitant procedures, were tailored based on comprehensive preoperative assessment.

Results

The mean age was 22.37 ± 11.15 years (range, 9-66), and 56.9% were male. The most common RVOT morphologies were pyramidal (37.2%) and tubular (30.4%). All procedures were successful. Twenty cases required cardiopulmonary bypass support. There were no intraoperative deaths. One in-hospital death occurred on postoperative day 12 in a high-risk patient with severe preoperative right ventricular dysfunction. All patients completed at least 1 year of follow-up, with a median follow-up duration of 1 year. During this period, significant improvements in right ventricular volumes (RVEDVI and RVESVI) and QRS duration were observed, whereas RVEF did not change significantly. There were no instances of coronary artery compression, valve embolization, or stent fracture. One suspected case of endocarditis was reported.

Conclusions

In patients with a large and morphologically complex RVOT, hybrid TPVI with the Salus TPV is a safe and effective therapeutic strategy, associated with high procedural success and encouraging short-term outcomes. A patient-specific approach, guided by meticulous preoperative imaging to determine the optimal access and the need for concomitant procedures, is key to minimizing complications. This hybrid technique offers a valuable alternative for patients who are not candidates for percutaneous intervention.

title: Three distinct trajectories of early oral feeding ability in preterm infants and their associated clinical factors.
authorString: Tang X, Zhu Y, Wu Y, Sun S, Zhou M, Yu X.
abstractText:
Background

Globally, approximately 13.4 million infants are born preterm each year, and difficulties during the transition to oral feeding are common among preterm infants during NICU hospitalization. Existing studies on oral feeding ability in preterm infants are predominantly cross-sectional, failing to identify underlying heterogeneity. This study used latent class growth modeling (LCGM) to identify trajectories of oral feeding ability during the first 14 days after oral feeding initiation and examine clinical characteristics associated with trajectory membership.

Methods

This prospective cohort study enrolled preterm infants (gestational age 28-32 weeks) from a tertiary hospital neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) between May 2025 and April 2026. Oral feeding ability was assessed at Days 1, 3, 7, 10, and 14 using the Oral Feeding Ability Scale for Preterm Infants. LCGM identified trajectories; multinomial logistic regression examined factors associated with trajectory membership.

Results

Of the 245 enrolled infants, 213 (86.9%) completed all five scheduled assessments. Scores increased significantly from 22.03 ± 2.95 on Day 1 to 34.41 ± 3.67 on Day 14 (p < 0.001). Three trajectories were identified: high-start rapid-rise (31.5%), moderate-start accelerated catch-up (44.6%), and low-start slow-rise (23.9%). Variables associated with trajectory membership included gestational age, birth weight, postmenstrual age (PMA) at oral feeding initiation, mechanical ventilation, illness severity (Neonatal Medical Index, NMI), and pre-feeding behavioral state.

Conclusions

Significant heterogeneity was observed in the developmental trajectories of early oral feeding ability. In this exploratory single-center cohort of formula-fed preterm infants, clinical characteristics were associated with trajectory membership; these findings should be considered associative and hypothesis-generating rather than predictive.

title: Neutrophil extracellular traps in neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis: from developmental maturation to immunothrombotic injury.
authorString: Chen Y, Zhu M.
abstractText: Neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is best understood as a syndrome of intestinal necrosis arising in a developmentally susceptible host, with overlapping inflammatory, ischemic, infectious, cardiac-related, and transfusion-associated triggers. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) are extracellular DNA networks decorated with histones, neutrophil elastase, myeloperoxidase, and other granule proteins. They may limit pathogen dissemination, yet persistent NET formation or impaired NET clearance can injure epithelium and microvascular endothelium and amplify immunothrombosis. This review focuses specifically on NETs in NEC. We first condense the general NEC background and then appraise human, animal, and mechanistic evidence with explicit attention to model system, intervention timing, NET detection method, infection burden, and NEC subtype. The neonatal NET-inhibitory factor (nNIF)/NET-maturation window is presented as a testable developmental hypothesis rather than an established quantitative rule. We synthesize biomarker and intervention literature and conclude that the translational question is not simply whether NETs are "good" or "bad", but which infants, at which disease phase, defined by which combination of formation, clearance, platelet, endothelial, microbial, and imaging signals, may benefit from inhibition, clearance, or preservation of NET function.

title: Predictive modelling to differentiate possible bacterial and viral cases of childhood pneumonia in Kilifi, Kenya using protein markers and clinical data.
authorString: Matuli C, Waeni JM, Gicheru ET, Sande CJ, Gallagher K.
abstractText:
Background

To date, accessible diagnostic tools to identify whether a patient's pneumonia is a bacterial, or viral infection, are not accurate or timely enough to prevent preemptive antibiotic administration. Relying on single biomarkers or clinical presentations has been insufficient. We aimed to incorporate a wide range of novel biomarkers and clinical presentations into a multivariable model and to validate its ability to differentiate bacterial from viral pneumonia.

Methods

A total of 457 children aged 2-59 months, admitted to the Kilifi County Referral Hospital, Kenya, with WHO defined pneumonia were classified using gold standard laboratory diagnostics as possible bacterial (i.e., bacterial/ unknown cases, n = 229) or possible viral (n = 228) infections. Clinical and laboratory data, and levels of CRP, PCT and 6 novel protein biomarkers were used to develop and validate a predictive multivariable Poisson regression model to differentiate pneumonia etiology. The Receiver Operating Characteristic curve was used to assess biomarker performance and validate the model internally.

Results

In age-adjusted analyses, chest-wall indrawing, cough, convulsions, crackles, angiotensinogen (AGT), and Serpin Family A Member 1 (SERPINA1) were significantly associated with pneumonia etiology, controlling for age. However, only chest-wall indrawing remained significant in multivariable analyses after controlling for age. The model demonstrated fair, but inadequate, discrimination, with an Area Under the Curve of 0.61. In a separate analysis excluding the unknowns from the bacterial group, chest-wall indrawing, crackles, cough, AGT (>=7.9144MFI), were significant predictors of pneumonia etiology, adjusting for age. This model demonstrated good discrimination, with an Area Under the Curve of 0.78 on the validation dataset.

Conclusion

Among children admitted to the hospital with WHO-defined pneumonia, modelling a wide range of biomarkers and clinical presentations still failed to distinguish bacterial from viral pneumonia with enough accuracy to guide clinical management. Further research addressing some of the limitations we encountered in outcome classification, stratifying by disease severity and potentially accounting for variation in biomarker performance by age, may improve predictions.

title: An ultrasound-based nomogram for predicting early neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis.
authorString: Ruan J, Su H, He Y, Lin W.
abstractText:
Objective

To develop and validate an ultrasound-based nomogram prediction model for the early diagnosis of neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC).

Methods

This is a retrospective cohort study. A total of 500 preterm infants admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) of our hospital from January 2023 to June 2024 were enrolled. They were stratified by NEC status and randomly assigned to a development cohort and a validation cohort at a ratio of 7:3. According to whether NEC occurred, infants were further categorized into an NEC group and a non-NEC group. General clinical data, including gestational age and birth weight, were collected. Laboratory inflammatory markers included C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), and interleukin-6 (IL-6). Ultrasound parameters included bowel wall thickness, intestinal peristalsis, gastric antral area, gastric antral peristalsis, and bowel wall blood perfusion. Logistic regression analysis was performed in the development cohort to identify independent risk factors and construct a nomogram prediction model. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis were used to evaluate model discrimination, calibration, and clinical net benefit in the development cohort. The validation cohort was used to verify model performance.

Results

Univariate analysis in the development cohort showed that gestational age, birth weight, CRP, PCT, IL-6, bowel wall thickness, intestinal peristalsis, gastric antral area, gastric antral peristalsis, and bowel wall blood perfusion differed significantly between groups (P < 0.05). Multivariable logistic regression further identified gestational age, CRP, PCT, IL-6, bowel wall thickness, intestinal peristalsis, bowel wall blood perfusion, gastric antral area, and gastric antral peristalsis as independent factors associated with early NEC (P < 0.05). On this basis, a nomogram prediction model was established. The areas under the ROC curve (AUCs) in the development and validation cohorts were 0.88 and 0.85, respectively, indicating good discriminative ability. The optimal risk cut-off of 0.18 was determined by Youden index solely from the development cohort. At this fixed threshold, sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV were 82.4%, 81.2%, 51.4%, and 95.0% for the development cohort; the corresponding performance in the validation cohort was 77.2%, 76.0%, 43.8%, and 92.4%. Goodness-of-fit testing of the calibration curves showed chi-square = 1.235 and P = 0.998 in the development cohort, and chi-square = 1.642 and P = 0.995 in the validation cohort, suggesting favorable agreement between predicted probabilities and observed risks. Decision curve analysis showed that when the risk threshold was greater than 0.05, the nomogram provided significant clinical net benefit.

Conclusion

The nomogram prediction model constructed from inflammatory and multiparametric ultrasound indicators demonstrates favorable predictive performance for the early diagnosis of neonatal NEC. It may provide clinicians with a noninvasive and repeatable auxiliary diagnostic tool, facilitating early intervention for NEC and improving prognosis.

title: Case Report: Refractory childhood-onset takayasu arteritis with digital clubbing and extensive supra-aortic and lower-limb arterial disease.
authorString: Abunejma FM, Jabari LM, Hamad MN, Tamimi TO, Bseiso O, Dweik HA, Isayed RMA, Qunibi H, Alzaro W, Alhroub W.
abstractText: Childhood-onset Takayasu arteritis is rare, and its early picture is often too vague to point at a large-vessel vasculitis. We report a 12-year-old girl who presented with 13 days of recurrent severe retrosternal chest pain and diffuse colicky abdominal pain, on a background of six months of exertional fatigue and painful swelling of the right fingertips, without fever, weight loss or night sweats. Examination showed bilateral digital clubbing, a right arm blood pressure below the 5th percentile with left arm and lower limb readings between the 50th and 90th percentiles, an absent right radial pulse, and weak brachial and right posterior tibial pulses. The erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 110 mm/h and C-reactive protein 82 to 93 mg/L. Computed tomography angiography showed mild concentric mural thickening of the aortic arch with severe stenosis of the right common and internal carotid arteries, near-occlusion of the right subclavian artery, moderate to severe brachiocephalic stenosis, moderate narrowing of the left common carotid and left subclavian arteries, and moderate stenosis of the right common and superficial femoral arteries. The abdominal aorta and its visceral branches were spared. She met the EULAR/PRINTO/PRES (Ankara 2008) classification criteria for childhood Takayasu arteritis, and the arterial distribution corresponds to Numano type IIa, together with peripheral lower-limb involvement that the Numano scheme does not cover. Disease progressed on intravenous methylprednisolone, oral prednisolone, methotrexate, aspirin and low-molecular-weight heparin, culminating in an 80% stenosis of the right common femoral artery. Adalimumab was started and later replaced by tocilizumab, after which the femoral peri-arterial inflammatory changes resolved on imaging and acute-phase reactants normalized. Blood pressure asymmetry, pulse deficits and the established stenoses persisted. This case suggests that normal inflammatory markers in childhood-onset Takayasu arteritis can coexist with fixed arterial damage, and that judgements about disease activity are better based on clinical findings and serial imaging together than on acute-phase reactants alone.

title: Beyond eosinophil depletion: long-term clinical trajectory and durability of response to benralizumab in patients with severe eosinophilic asthma and CRSwNP: an 18-month real-world study (the BANDOR study).
authorString: Bizzi E, Marra AM, Manzotti G, Gidaro A, Ortolani V, Iemoli E, Borgonovo L, Asperti C, Modica S, Greco E, Rotunno S, Yacoub MR, Ministrini S, Bini F, Germinario C, Mauro A, Paciullo F, Damanti S, Casarin F, Sculco M, Rovere Querini P.
abstractText:
Background

The management of patients with severe eosinophilic asthma and chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps requires therapies capable of inducing stable remission. While benralizumab is an established treatment for severe asthma, randomized controlled trials in nasal polyposis have failed to reach primary clinical endpoints or showed inconsistent results. Consequently, there is a lack of evidence regarding its performance in clinical practice. The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the kinetics of response across different symptom domains and to identify predictors of clinical improvement in a Real-World setting in patients affected by severe eosinophilic asthma and chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps.

Methods

This retrospective observational study analyzed a cohort of patients with a United Airways Disease phenotype treated with benralizumab for a continuous period of 18 months. We mapped the longitudinal trajectory of specific SNOT 22 subdomains and lung function. Patients were stratified into early and late responders based on the timing of clinical improvement to identify baseline predictors of rapid versus gradual response.

Results

Analysis revealed that SNOT 22 subdomains exhibit distinct recovery patterns. Nasal and physical symptoms showed a significant improvement within the first months of therapy despite the limited success reported in previous clinical trials. In contrast, functional and emotional domains required a longer period of treatment to reach a stable plateau. Early responders were characterized by a significantly higher baseline eosinophil count (median 885 vs 530 cells per microliter) and greater bronchial obstruction at baseline compared to late responders. Functional stability in FEV1 and a reduction in oral corticosteroid use were maintained throughout the observation.

Conclusions

The BANDOR study demonstrates that benralizumab can induce durable clinical remission in a specific subset of patients who maintain treatment adherence. The speed of response is domain specific, with physical symptoms improving before emotional and functional ones. A high initial eosinophilic burden is the primary determinant of a rapid response. These findings suggest that while randomized trials showed limited efficacy, Real-World data identifies a high disease burden phenotype that derives significant long term benefit from receptor targeted eosinophil depletion.

title: Myocardial Bridge in High School Athlete With Exertional Symptoms: Innocent Bystander or Major Player?
authorString: Langan A, Segal V, Cattani M, Cao L, Sachdeva S, Reaves-O'Neal D, Schellhaas J, Qureshi AM, Brenes J, Molossi S.
abstractText:
Background

Myocardial bridge (MB) is largely considered a benign condition, though it may lead to myocardial ischemia because of coronary vessel compression. It is a known cause of sudden cardiac arrest/death in young athletes.

Case summary

A 16-year-old boy athlete with asthma presented with exertional dyspnea, chest tightness, and tachycardia following 3-mile races. Echocardiography showed a small atrial septal defect and normal coronary artery origins. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated a left anterior descending MB. Stress cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging showed no inducible perfusion defects. Cardiac catheterization for intracoronary flow assessment demonstrated compromised coronary flow distal to the MB, with compression on intravascular ultrasound. Surgical unroofing of the MB allowed a safe return to competition.

Discussion

Exhaustive workup and invasive assessment of intracoronary flow are invaluable to determine significant compression of a MB causing ischemia in athletes with exertional symptoms.

Take-home message

Exertional symptoms in athletes should be considered for advanced imaging to exclude significant lesions that compromise coronary flow.
