title: Do We Still Need Conventional Holter ECGs in the Era of Smart Devices?
authorString: Stump R, Brügger J, Badertscher P.
abstractText: Wearable devices for rhythm monitoring are increasingly available and are being used by patients across a broad spectrum of technologies, including smartwatches with electrocardiogram (ECG)-recording functions and ECG patch systems. Early development of automated rhythm classification algorithms using artificial intelligence primarily focused on atrial fibrillation (AF), although indications and validated use cases differ substantially between device types and continue to evolve. This review aims to provide an overview of contemporary smart devices, their capabilities in arrhythmia care, and future perspectives. Currently, two main technologies are used for rhythm assessment: photoplethysmography (PPG) and single- or multi-lead electrocardiography. PPG enables continuous monitoring of heart rate and pulse regularity, whereas ECG acquisition is typically user-initiated. The use of a 30-second single-lead ECG (SL-ECG) strip with physician confirmation for the diagnosis of AF is supported by current ESC AF guidelines. Systematic screening approaches using wearables have demonstrated higher AF detection rates compared with standard diagnostic pathways; however, whether this translates into improved stroke prevention remains to be proven. Beyond AF, wearables may be particularly useful for infrequent symptomatic arrhythmias, such as supraventricular tachycardias, by enabling SL-ECG recording during symptoms and thereby supporting diagnosis and management. Additional applications include monitoring of QT prolongation, conduction disturbances, and rhythm surveillance following interventions. As an established alternative to user-dependent ECG acquisition, ECG patches provide continuous rhythm recording for up to 30 days and are generally more user-friendly than conventional Holter monitoring. A key challenge remains automated rhythm detection for non-AF arrhythmias, as well as a relevant proportion of inconclusive tracings in real-world populations, for example in the presence of conduction abnormalities or frequent premature atrial or ventricular complexes. From a physician's perspective, clear workflows and dedicated technical solutions are essential to manage the growing volume of data, and reimbursement mechanisms for analysis of these recordings must be established. Ultimately, the future of wearable-based rhythm monitoring lies in its structured integration into clinical workflows, enabling more individualized and optimized arrhythmia care. In parallel, combining rhythm information with additional health metrics may facilitate a more holistic approach to prevention and management of cardiovascular disease. Despite all technical advances, traditional Holter ECG still has irreplaceable value in patients with frequent arrhythmia symptoms or when coronary vasospasms or Brugada syndrome are suspected.

title: Clinical manifestations of resistance to thyroid hormone beta (RTHβ) syndrome in children - multicenter case series.
authorString: Fedorczak A, Sokół M, Beń-Skowronek I, Mierzwa M, Zachurzok A, Bogusz-Wójcik A, Przybylak-Ortega J, Moszczyńska E, Berezowiec P, Bossowski A, Dąbek N, Mazur A, Dyrka K, Niedziela M, Makowiecka-Wołek M, Śmigiel R, Ulenberg A, Myśliwiec M, Stawerska R.
abstractText:
Introduction

Resistance to thyroid hormone (TH) β (RTHβ) is a rare genetic disorder caused by mutations in the TH receptor β gene (THRB) and characterized by elevated TH levels with non-suppressed thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and variable clinical presentation. The aim of the study was to characterize the clinical and biochemical features of children with RTHβ, correlate them with genetic findings and therapeutic management, to raise clinicians' awareness of the specific characteristics of the condition.

Material and methods

This retrospective multicenter case series included 15 children with genetically confirmed THRB variants. Clinical, laboratory, imaging, and treatment data were analyzed retrospectively.

Results

All the patients demonstrated elevated free thyroxine and free triiodothyronine concentrations with detectable, non-suppressed TSH serum level. Common findings included tachycardia (73%), neurodevelopmental disturbances (60%), and a lean phenotype (BMI <10th percentile, 53%). Misdiagnosis of primary hyperthyroidism occurred in 20% of cases. Most patients did not require pharmacological treatment or were managed with beta-blockers alone for symptomatic tachycardia control.

Discussion

Pediatric RTHβ shows consistent biochemical features but marked clinical heterogeneity. Awareness is essential to ensure accurate diagnosis and avoid unnecessary therapy.

title: Preliminary experience with controlled hypothermic storage of donor heart in combined heart transplantation.
authorString: Argaw ST, Lora Ronco L, Frering A, Kloeckner M, Coutance G, Coilly A, Vibert E, Snanoudj R, Genty T, Achouh P, Belli E, Guihaire J.
abstractText: While studies have demonstrated improved clinical outcomes with the use of controlled hypothermic storage (CHS) devices in isolated heart transplantation, it has not been evaluated in combined heart transplantation. In this small retrospective study (n=17), we evaluate clinical outcomes after combined heart-liver and heart-kidney transplantation in recipients of donor hearts preserved with conventional ice cold storage (ICS, n=10) versus CHS (n=7). The study found severe early graft dysfunction (EGD) occurred more frequently in the ICS cohort when compared to the CHS cohort (70% vs 0%, respectively). In addition, the CHS cohort had shorter median intensive care unit length of stay (7 days compared to 15.5 days, respectively) as well as fewer post-transplant complications, including sepsis (60% in ICS and 28.6% in CHS), pneumonia (40% in ICS and 14.3% in CHS), stroke (30% in ICS and 0% in CHS), and acute kidney injury requiring dialysis (60% in ICS and 28.6% in CHS). These preliminary findings suggest CHS may improve outcomes in combined heart transplantation.

title: Advances in Mechanisms and Management Strategies of Pulmonary Hypertension: A Review.
authorString: Liu A, Xi L, Du J, Guo Y, Yu H, Zhang S, Xie W, Liu M.
abstractText: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) encompasses a heterogeneous group of disorders characterized by persistently elevated pulmonary artery pressure and driven by diverse etiologies and intersecting pathological mechanisms. In recent years, substantial advances have clarified key contributors to PH pathogenesis, including pulmonary vascular remodeling, immune-inflammatory dysregulation, and genetic predispositions. Concurrently, diagnostic and therapeutic approaches tailored to different PH subtypes have evolved, incorporating targeted pharmacological treatments, interventional procedures, and lung transplantation. This review summarizes recent advances in elucidating the mechanisms underlying PH and outlines clinical management strategies across the major etiologic categories. Particular emphasis is placed on developments in PH-specific therapies and on emerging therapeutic targets to provide a coherent mechanistic framework and practical guidance for clinicians involved in the diagnosis and treatment of this challenging disease.

title: Breakthroughs in the Pathological Mechanism and Comprehensive Management of Pulmonary Hypertension.
authorString: Zhou K, Gong Y, Zhang J, Chen D, Liu Y, Xu Z.
abstractText: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a rare and life-threatening vascular disorder characterized by complex and multifactorial pathogenesis. Emerging evidence indicates that pulmonary vascular remodeling is driven by coordinated abnormalities in genetic susceptibility, epigenetic regulation, metabolic reprogramming, immune-inflammatory crosstalk, and DNA damage repair. Recent advances in multi-omics profiling, single-cell technologies, and high-resolution imaging have substantially improved the understanding of PH pathobiology and disease heterogeneity. Current therapeutic strategies mainly target the three classical vasoactive pathways to alleviate vasoconstriction and improve hemodynamics. Notably, (bone morphogenetic protein) BMP/transforming growth factor‑β1 (TGF-β) pathway-targeted therapy, represented by sotatercept, has initiated a new era of disease-modifying treatment aimed at reversing pulmonary vascular remodeling. In addition, emerging therapies targeting immune, hormonal, and metabolic pathways have demonstrated promising therapeutic potential. Despite significant progress in both basic and clinical research, major challenges remain, including precise phenotypic stratification, long-term therapeutic safety, and individualized treatment optimization. This review summarizes recent advances in the molecular mechanisms and comprehensive management of PH and highlights future directions for translational research and precision medicine.

Waitlist mortality risk (US-CRS score) distribution among status 1 and 2 adult heart transplant candidates with exceptions.
authorString: Fatma N, Patel SS, Lyden GR, Moazami N, Wayda B, Parker WF, Gentry SE.
abstractText:
Background

The US-candidate risk score (US-CRS) predicts waitlist mortality among heart transplant candidates using 7 laboratory, cardiovascular, and cardiac device usage variables on a 50-point scale, with higher scores indicating greater mortality risk. We assessed whether US-CRS accurately assigns mortality risk for exception candidates, and whether the alignment of allocation priority with waitlist mortality risk (US-CRS) differs between candidates with and without exceptions.

Methods

We compared the performance of US-CRS in candidates with and without exceptions using receiver operating curves. We compared US-CRS distributions using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) test and examined the proportion of candidates below specific score thresholds in each group. We also compared candidates with and without exceptions using Wilcoxon Rank-Sum test for continuous variables and Pearson's Chi-squared test or Fisher exact test for categorical variables.

Results

US-CRS is accurate for measuring mortality risk among exception candidates as it is among non-exception candidates. Patients with higher waitlist status had higher median US-CRS. However, the median US-CRS of Status 1 candidates without exceptions (50 [IQR 48-50]) was significantly higher than for candidates with exceptions (45 [36-48]; [ p≤0.05 ]), and similarly for Status 2 (46 [41-49] vs. 42 [32-47]; [ p≤0.05 ]). Notably, 33.13% of Status 1 and 41.28% of Status 2 candidates with exceptions had US-CRS below 40, compared to only 1.84% and 19.20% of candidates without exceptions, respectively. Conversely, among candidates in Status 3 and 4, candidates with exceptions generally had higher US-CRS than candidates without exceptions.

Conclusions

Allocation priority under the status system does not align with estimated mortality risk; misalignment is greater for candidates with exceptions. While some exception candidates in Status 1 and 2 do have high estimated mortality risk and legitimately need exceptions, many of these exceptions appear to have been granted to candidates with relatively low medical urgency.

title: Mitral regurgitation and left atrial phasic function and atrioventricular coupling in patients with myocardial infarction: a cardiac magnetic resonance imaging study.
authorString: Wen XL, Guo YK, Gao Y, Yang ZG.

journal.title: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery

abstractText:
Background

Mitral regurgitation (MR) after myocardial infarction (MI) may increase left atrial (LA) pressure and contribute to cardiac dysfunction. This study evaluated the incremental association of MR with LA phasic function and strain and identified independent factors associated with LA deformation in patients with MI.

Methods

This retrospective study included 189 patients with MI (111 without MR and 78 with MR: mild, 27; moderate, 33; severe, 18) and 86 normal controls who underwent 3.0-T cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR). MR severity was graded by the CMR-derived MR fraction: mild <30%, moderate 30% to <50%, and severe ≥50%. CMR-derived LA phasic function and strain (reservoir strain, epsilon-s; booster strain, epsilon-a; conduit strain, epsilon-e), left ventricular (LV) function and strain, infarct size, and MR fraction were measured. Between-group comparisons were performed using one-way analysis of variance or the Kruskal-Wallis test with post hoc correction, and multivariable linear regression was used to identify independent factors associated with LA strain. A two-sided P<0.05 was considered statistically significant.

Results

Patients with MI and MR had lower LA reservoir strains [22.14%±10.91% vs. 28.65% (22.78%, 38.30%) vs. 41.70% (36.15%, 53.15%)], booster strains [11.52%±6.19% vs. 13.80% (10.20%, 19.80%) vs. 19.25% (15.10%, 24.05%)], and conduit strains [9.40% (6.03%, 14.85%) vs. 14.60% (9.60%, 20.50%) vs. 22.55% (17.75%, 30.43%)] than patients with MI without MR and controls (all P<0.05). They also had higher LA maximum volume [68.43 (57.44, 91.51) mL] and minimum volume [35.93 (24.43, 61.15) mL] and lower LA total ejection fraction (45.39%±14.97%) than the other groups (all P<0.05). In multivariable analysis, MR degree was independently associated with reservoir strain (β=-0.194, P=0.048) and conduit strain (β=-0.208, P=0.038). Anterior wall MI (reservoir strain: β=-0.245, P=0.014; booster strain: β=-0.231, P=0.028; conduit strain: β=-0.224, P=0.027) and posteromedial papillary muscle infarction (reservoir strain: β=-0.329, P=0.004; booster strain: β=-0.370, P=0.003) were also independently associated with LA strain.

Conclusions

MR was associated with further deterioration of LA myocardial strain in patients with MI. Posteromedial papillary muscle infarction, anterior wall MI, beta-blocker use, and dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin plus clopidogrel were independently associated with LA strain. CMR-derived functional and strain parameters may help characterize LV-LA coupling and support risk stratification in this population.

title: Ventricular tachycardia ablation in late-onset phenotype Fabry disease: a case report.
authorString: Tran KD, Lim H, Nguyen PH, Lin CY.
abstractText:
Background

Fabry disease is an X-linked lysosomal storage disorder that can cause progressive cardiomyopathy, myocardial fibrosis, conduction disease, and malignant ventricular arrhythmias. Ventricular tachycardia (VT) ablation in advanced Fabry cardiomyopathy is challenging, particularly in patients with extensive scar and left ventricular assist device (LVAD) support.

Case summary

A 71-year-old man with late-onset Fabry disease, confirmed by endomyocardial biopsy showing myelin body accumulation, reduced α-galactosidase A activity, and elevated plasma Gb3, developed severe left ventricular dysfunction, extensive late gadolinium enhancement, LVAD implantation, and complete atrioventricular block requiring dual-chamber pacemaker implantation. He presented with recurrent palpitations and near-syncope. Device interrogation revealed multiple VT episodes, including one episode degenerating into ventricular fibrillation, and surface electrocardiography documented wide-complex tachycardia with right bundle branch block morphology and an inferior axis. An electrophysiological study was performed using an antegrade transseptal left ventricular approach. Intracardiac echocardiography was used to delineate the LV cavity and LVAD position, facilitating safe catheter navigation and mapping while avoiding interference with the LVAD. Endocardial mapping demonstrated diffuse late potentials, low-voltage substrate, and deceleration zones involving the basal-to-mid-inferolateral left ventricle. Substrate modification targeting these abnormal electrograms eliminated inducible ventricular premature complexes. No recurrent VT episodes were detected on subsequent pacemaker interrogation.

Discussion

This case highlights the complex arrhythmogenic substrate of late-stage Fabry cardiomyopathy and the utility of intracardiac echocardiography-guided mapping in patients with LVAD support. Catheter ablation may provide short-term arrhythmia control, but in advanced Fabry disease, its role remains largely palliative.

title: Anesthetic Management of Pregnant Patients With Cardiovascular Disease: A Practical, Lesion-Based Clinical Review.
authorString: Iosovich A, Ronenson A, Guasch E, Brogly N, Aljuba Y, Shatalin D.
abstractText: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a major cause of maternal morbidity and mortality and increasingly complicates pregnancy as more women with congenital and acquired heart disease reach reproductive age. Anesthetic management of these patients requires integrating lesion-specific cardiovascular physiology, pregnancy-related hemodynamic changes, obstetric considerations, and the anticipated effects of labor, anesthesia, delivery, hemorrhage, and the postpartum transition. Despite contemporary cardiovascular and obstetric guidelines, translating lesion-specific physiology into practical anesthetic decisions remains challenging. This narrative review provides a practical framework for the peripartum anesthetic management of pregnant patients with CVD. We discuss contemporary risk assessment using the modified World Health Organization 2.0 classification and the Cardiac Disease in Pregnancy II risk model, followed by principles of Pregnancy Heart Team planning, labor analgesia, cesarean delivery, monitoring, anticoagulation, uterotonic therapy, and postpartum surveillance. Lesion-specific considerations are reviewed for mitral stenosis, aortic stenosis, aortic disease and coarctation, pulmonary hypertension, pregnancy-associated myocardial infarction, peripartum cardiomyopathy, congenital heart disease, and Fontan circulation. Particular attention is given to maintaining appropriate preload, ventricular filling, systemic vascular resistance, cardiac rhythm, and oxygenation while avoiding abrupt changes in vascular resistance or cardiac loading conditions. The review emphasizes individualized anesthetic planning rather than universal preferences for a particular anesthetic technique or mode of delivery. Neuraxial anesthesia can be advantageous in selected patients but should be considered in the context of ventricular function, pulmonary pressures, anticoagulation, urgency, and the expected hemodynamic response. General anesthesia remains an important option when neuraxial anesthesia is contraindicated or inadequate, rapid delivery is required, airway or ventilatory control is necessary, or maternal or surgical circumstances dictate. Uterotonic therapy should similarly be individualized according to cardiovascular physiology, with careful attention to dose, route, and hemodynamic effects. Close multidisciplinary planning and coordinated postpartum care are particularly important for women with pulmonary hypertension, ventricular dysfunction, complex congenital heart disease, and Fontan circulation.

title: Sex-specific association between body mass index and mortality after heart transplantation: A nationwide KOTRY Cohort Study.
authorString: Lee Y, Kim K, Kim AR, Hong JA, Hyun J, Lee SE, Kim MS, Jeon ES, Choi JO, Oh J, Kang SM, Kim MS, Kim JJ, Lee HY, Jung SH, KOTRY Study Group.
abstractText:
Background

Body mass index has paradoxical associations with outcomes in advanced heart failure, but whether its relationship with survival after heart transplantation differs by sex remains uncertain.

Methods

We analyzed 1059 adult heart transplant recipients enrolled in the Korean Organ Transplantation Registry from 2014 through 2023. Body mass index was assessed using Asian-specific BMI categories and 3-knot restricted cubic splines. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Multivariable Cox models adjusted for prespecified clinical characteristics and pretransplant support. Sex differences in the body mass index-mortality association were evaluated using restricted cubic spline modeling.

Results

The cohort included 304 female patients, and 217 deaths occurred during a median follow-up of 3.6 years. The body mass index-mortality association differed by sex in the pooled spline model (P for interaction=0.041). In male patients, the association was nonlinear and U-shaped (P for overall association=0.031; P for nonlinearity=0.017). Underweight was associated with higher mortality than normal weight (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.97; 95% confidence interval, 1.17-3.33). In female patients, the fitted association was inverse, without evidence of nonlinearity (P for overall association=0.030; P for nonlinearity=0.302). Obesity class I was associated with lower mortality than normal weight (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.24; 95% confidence interval, 0.08-0.73), although this estimate was based on few events.

Conclusions

The association between body mass index and mortality after heart transplantation may differ by sex. The apparent lower mortality among female patients with obesity class I is hypothesis-generating and requires external validation.

title: A Giant Atherosclerotic Ascending Aortic Aneurysm (13.5 cm) With Arch Involvement Successfully Managed by Valve-Sparing Total Arch Replacement: A Case Report.
authorString: Tabbah RN, Irani J, Barbar S, Khattar M, Karam K.
abstractText: Giant ascending aortic aneurysms (AscAAs), conventionally defined as aneurysms exceeding 10 cm in diameter, are exceedingly rare in contemporary practice due to earlier diagnosis and prophylactic surgical intervention. AscAAs of atherosclerotic origin are particularly uncommon because proximal thoracic aortic aneurysms are typically associated with medial degeneration, connective tissue disorders, or bicuspid aortic valve disease rather than advanced atherosclerosis. Reports of aneurysms exceeding 13 cm remain exceptional in the literature. We report the case of a 70-year-old woman with multiple cardiovascular risk factors, including heavy tobacco exposure and type 2 diabetes mellitus, who presented with progressive dyspnea, constitutional symptoms, and hemodynamic compromise. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated a giant AscAA measuring 13.5 cm with extension into the aortic arch (8.7 cm), associated with periaortic fluid and imaging features suggestive of impending rupture. The aortic root and descending thoracic aorta were spared. Emergency open surgical repair was successfully performed using supracoronary ascending aortic replacement, total arch replacement under deep hypothermic circulatory arrest, and separate supra-aortic branch reconstruction with a branched Dacron graft. Histopathology confirmed an atheromatous aneurysm with thrombotic degeneration, while microbiological studies excluded infection. This case highlights the extreme rarity of massive atherosclerotic AscAAs and demonstrates that successful treatment is achievable through advanced, anatomy-driven open surgical reconstruction. Complete valve-sparing total arch replacement with separate branch vessel reconstruction provided durable exclusion of extensive disease while preserving native root structures. This report adds to the limited literature on extreme-diameter ascending aneurysms and underscores the importance of prompt diagnosis and individualized operative planning.

title: Ebstein Anomaly Associated With Primary Lymphedema: A Case Report and Literature Review of a Rare Anatomical Combination.
authorString: Dimakakos E, Toumanidou MG, Cholidou K, Papapanagiotou I, Psarogiorgos K, Toilos S, Adonatou F, Mariolis-Sapsakos T, Troupis T.
abstractText: A 15-year-old male patient with a congenital heart disease known as Ebstein anomaly presented with edema of the right leg. The patient underwent lymphoscintigraphy, which revealed bilateral hypoplasia of the lower-extremity lymphatic system. The coexistence of these conditions may represent a previously unrecognized syndromic association. Physicians should be aware of the possible coexistence of these conditions and investigate patients with Ebstein anomaly in order to minimize physical and psychological complications.

title: Incidental Diagnosis of Heterotaxy Syndrome With Left Isomerism in a Postpartum Woman Presenting With Dyspnea and Cyanosis.
authorString: Sharma K, Sharma S, Gupta A, Prakash A.
abstractText: Heterotaxy syndrome (situs ambiguus) is a rare congenital disorder characterized by abnormal thoracoabdominal organ positioning. Left isomerism (polysplenia syndrome) is a subtype associated with bilateral left-sided morphology, multiple spleens, and complex cardiovascular anomalies. Most cases present in childhood, but adults may rarely remain undiagnosed until acute illness unmasks the condition. Timely recognition through cross-sectional imaging is critical, as delayed diagnosis in adulthood is associated with high morbidity and mortality, particularly during physiological stress, such as pregnancy and the postpartum period. We present a case of a 25-year-old postpartum woman who presented with shortness of breath, cough, and cyanosis seven days after delivery. Evaluation revealed an oxygen saturation of 70% on room air and a markedly elevated D-dimer level. Contrast-enhanced CT of the chest and abdomen demonstrated left atrial isomerism, double superior vena cava, interrupted infrahepatic inferior vena cava with azygos continuation, polysplenia, a midline liver, a right-sided stomach, dorsal pancreatic agenesis, and bilateral bilobed lungs. Cardiac anomalies included an atrial septal defect, a ventricular septal defect, discordant ventriculoarterial connections, and pulmonary arterial hypertension. This case highlights that heterotaxy with left isomerism may first present in adulthood during physiological stress, such as pregnancy and the postpartum period, and that CT plays a crucial role in defining the full spectrum of anomalies.

title: Technical limitations and error propagation in the 3D printing pipeline for congenital heart disease: an integrative review-a narrative synthesis.
authorString: Balaji A, Yu ST, Hussein N, Ramcharan T, Pinkey B, Fratini A, Crucean A.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur Heart J Imaging Methods Pract
journal.title: European heart journal. Imaging methods and practice
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur Heart J Imaging Methods Pract

abstractText: Three-dimensional (3D) printing has gained prominence in the management of congenital heart disease (CHD) by augmenting spatial understanding, facilitating preoperative planning, and supporting education for clinicians and families. The clinical validity of printed models, however, is contingent upon accuracy maintained across a multistage pipeline that spans image acquisition, segmentation and modelling, printer-specific processing, and post-processing with subsequent clinical interpretation. Technical and human factors introduce discrepancies at each stage; these inaccuracies may accumulate and propagate, thereby altering the geometric and qualitative fidelity of the final model. This integrative review examines the principal sources of error across the pipeline, outlines mechanisms of propagation, and considers implications for decision-making in CHD, with particular emphasis on paediatric applications where permissible tolerances are narrow. Drawing upon contemporary literature, we provide recommendations for protocol standardization, validation procedures, operator training, and transparent documentation. An inter-observer experiment is proposed to quantify segmentation-induced variability using similarity and surface distance metrics, linking measurable divergence to potential clinical impact. A pragmatic error-minimizing pipeline is also described to improve reliability and promote reproducibility in clinical practice.

title: [Surgical Case of Posterior Transposition of the Great Arteries with Bilateral Conus].
authorString: Kaneko M, Oka N, Matsunaga Y, Moriyama W.

journal.title: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery

abstractText: A two-month-old girl presented with hyperpnea, a significant cardiac murmur, and severe hypoxemia. Transthoracic echocardiography at the referring hospital suggested congenital heart disease with highflow pulmonary hypertension, and she was referred to our institution for further evaluation. At our hospital, echocardiography demonstrated transposition of the great arteries (TGA) with a small ventricular septal defect (VSD), atrial septal defect, and patent ductus arteriosus. Detailed echocardiography revealed that the aorta was positioned slightly posterior and to the right of the pulmonary artery, with the presence of both subpulmonary and subaortic conus. The subaortic conus represented an atypical anatomical feature of posterior TGA. Based on these findings, a diagnosis of posterior TGA with bilateral conus was established. Aortic angiography demonstrated a Shaher type 9 pattern, in which the right coronary artery courses anterior to the aorta and the left coronary artery passes posterior to the pulmonary artery. At three months of age, she underwent an arterial switch operation. The Lecompte maneuver was not performed because the aorta was positioned posterior and to the right of the pulmonary artery (original Jatene procedure). An autologous pericardial patch was interposed along the left margin of the pulmonary artery bifurcation stump to shift the anastomotic site of the neo-pulmonary artery rightward, thereby preventing compression of the transferred coronary arteries. A small VSD intentionally left open as a fenestration in anticipation of a postoperative pulmonary hypertensive crisis. The postoperative course was uneventful.

title: The ligament of Marshall as a therapeutic target in atrial fibrillation: from anatomy to catheter-based and surgical management-a narrative review.
authorString: Juárez Del Río JI, Kowalewski M, Stec S, Farkowski M, Kwaśniak E, Smoczyński R, Brączkowski J, Buczma K, Urso S, Torrón FP, Suwalski P.
abstractText:
Background and objective

Long regarded as an inconsequential embryological remnant, the ligament of Marshall (LOM) is now recognized as a treatable component of the atrial fibrillation (AF) substrate. This review synthesizes the anatomical, electrophysiological and clinical evidence behind that shift and compares the two routes to the LOM: percutaneous retrograde ethanol infusion into the vein of Marshall (EIVOM) during catheter ablation, and direct division during thoracoscopic surgery. Both act on the same epicardial structure; only the route of access differs.

Methods

A structured literature search of PubMed, Embase and Web of Science covered the embryology, anatomy, histology and electrophysiology of the LOM and clinical studies of both routes. Two authors screened and selected records independently. Given the heterogeneity of study designs, findings were synthesized narratively.

Key content and findings

The LOM is a neuro-muscular remnant of the embryonic left superior vena cava that contributes to AF through three mechanisms: triggers arising from insulated myocardial "Marshall bundles", autonomic modulation via adjacent ganglionated plexi, and preferential conduction across the mitral isthmus. Five randomized trials of EIVOM-based strategies have enrolled more than 1,100 patients; pooled analysis shows improved 12-month freedom from any atrial arrhythmia (risk ratio 1.16, 95% confidence interval: 1.04-1.29; number needed to treat 10) and less repeat ablation, without excess major complications (2.5% vs. 2.8%) but with more overall complications and longer fluoroscopy. Crucially, no trial has tested ethanol infusion in isolation; the observed benefit reflects composite lesion sets. Thoracoscopic division interrupts the entire ligament independent of venous anatomy but has never been a randomized variable; randomized evidence for thoracoscopic and hybrid strategies overall ranges from neutral (CASA-AF) to positive (CONVERGE, HARTCAP-AF). Guidelines recognize both as options in selected patients without mandating routine LOM division.

Conclusions

The LOM is a reproducible, anatomically defined target reachable percutaneously or by surgical division within a comprehensive AF ablation strategy. The supporting evidence is markedly asymmetric: randomized data exist for EIVOM-based strategies but never for ethanol infusion alone, none at all for surgical division, and the two routes have never been compared head-to-head. Its incremental benefit beyond pulmonary vein and posterior wall isolation remains undefined.

title: The platelet count combined with activated partial thromboplastin time as predictive marker for predicting surgical necrotizing enterocolitis.
authorString: Zhu K, Wang Y, Zheng X, Lu Y, Wang X.
abstractText:
Background

The platelet count to activated partial thromboplastin time ratio (PAR) is a validated laboratory marker that reflects the severity of systemic inflammatory responses and coagulation dysfunction. However, the predictive value of PAR for surgical necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) remains poorly defined. The study aimed to investigate clinical value of PAR in predicting surgical NEC.

Methods

The retrospective study was conducted on 112 very low birth weight (VLBW) infants diagnosed with NEC during the hospitalization at The First Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University from March 2016 to February 2026. Clinical baseline data, laboratory parameters, treatment strategies and prognostic outcomes of all enrolled infants were systematically collected and treated. The included population was stratified into surgical and non-surgical groups according to surgical intervention or conservative treatment. Univariate logistic regression analyses were used to identify risk factors for NEC surgical intervention. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was applied to assess the predictive markers for surgical NEC.

Results

Among the 112 enrolled NEC infants, 21 cases (18.75%) ultimately received surgical treatment. Baseline laboratory tests at NEC diagnosis revealed significant differences in predictive indicators. The surgical group exhibited significantly lower platelet count (PLT) and lymphocyte count (LY), as well as markedly prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) compared with the non-surgical group. Multivariate regression analysis confirmed that PAR [odds ratio (OR) =0.561, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.395-0.798, P=0.001] and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) (OR =1.008, 95% CI: 1.003-1.014, P=0.002) were independent risk factors for surgical NEC. ROC analysis showed that PAR possessed predictive efficacy for high-risk factor of surgical NEC, with a sensitivity of 75.7% and specificity of 74.3%, and the area under the curve (AUC) was 0.729. PLR predictor demonstrated a sensitivity of 71.4% and specificity of 73.2%, and the AUC was 0.722. A decreased PAR value and increased PLR levels at the onset of NEC were significantly associated with adverse clinical outcomes.

Conclusions

PAR and PLR are reliable, simple, and accessible prognostic biomarkers for early prediction of surgical intervention in NEC which have the potential to become reference indicators for clinical decision-making.

title: Predictive value of novel inflammatory markers for post-infectious pulmonary embolism in children.
authorString: Kuang X, Shu C.
abstractText:
Background

Pulmonary embolism (PE) is an increasingly recognized life-threatening condition in children, characterized by aberrant thrombo-inflammatory responses. New inflammatory markers such as systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), neutrophil to lymphocyte ratio (NLR), monocyte to lymphocyte ratio (MLR), and platelet to lymphocyte ratio (PLR) are associated with the prediction and prognosis of PE. This study aimed to investigate the expression levels of biological markers such as D-dimer in acute PE of varying severity, and to discuss their correlations, thereby providing a reference for the early clinical identification of children with infection-associated acute PE.

Methods

A retrospective analysis was performed on data from 28 inpatients diagnosed with PE on imaging, including 24 with infection-related PE (post-infectious PE) and 4 with non-infectious PE (all with tumors), and 43 controls without PE on computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) (control group), all of whom were admitted to the Children's Hospital of Chongqing Medical University from January 2010 to June 2024. The study aimed to compare the levels of novel inflammatory indicators between the groups and to evaluate their predictive value for diagnosing PE.

Results

There were 24 cases in the PE group, 9 men and 15 women, with a mean age of 94.42±43.76 months; 43 cases in the control group, 19 men and 24 women, with a mean age of 90.95±44.95 months. The differences in sex composition ratio and age between the two groups were not statistically significant (P>0.05). The values of NLR, MLR, SII, SIRI, and AISI in the PE group were higher than those in the control group (all P<0.05), and multifactorial logistic regression analysis revealed that patients with high levels of NLR, SIRI, and AISI had a higher risk of morbidity. The receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves showed that the values of NLR [area under the curve (AUC): 0.794; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.682 to 0.905], SIRI (AUC: 0.861; 95% CI: 0.772 to 0.951) and AISI (AUC: 0.859; 95% CI: 0.766 to 0.953), and AISI had a higher specificity, and the combination of the three had a higher sensitivity.

Conclusions

Elevated NLR, SIRI, and AISI levels were significantly associated with the presence of PE in children with infections, suggesting their utility as adjunctive biomarkers for the early identification of children with PE. NLR emerged as the most robust independent predictor. Given the cross-sectional design and limited sample size, the predictive value for disease severity or prognosis was not evaluated.

title: Metabolic abnormalities in pediatric pulmonary arterial hypertension: a narrative review of direct evidence, mechanistic boundaries, and a validation-focused research agenda.
authorString: Sui K, Jia X, Wang S, Li Z.
abstractText:
Background and objective

Metabolic reprogramming has been proposed as a major mechanism of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), but evidence from adult patients, experimental models, and children is uneven. This distinction is especially important in pediatric disease because congenital heart disease (CHD), developmental syndromes, identifiable genetic disorders, and treatable metabolic conditions are more prominent than in adult-onset PAH. This narrative review evaluates what has been measured directly in children, defines the boundaries of extrapolation from adult and experimental studies, and identifies priorities for pediatric validation.

Methods

PubMed-indexed literature and reference lists were searched from database inception through July 2026 using terms related to pediatric PAH, metabolomics, proteomics, biomarkers, mitochondria, glycolysis, pyruvate dehydrogenase, right-ventricular metabolism, CHD, genetics, and cobalamin C deficiency. Priority was given to original pediatric cohorts and biospecimen studies, followed by adult human mechanistic studies with perturbation or rescue and experimental studies that directly measured metabolic function.

Key content and findings

Direct pediatric studies document severe and heterogeneous disease, a substantial burden of genetic diagnoses, clinically informative but mechanistically nonspecific circulating biomarkers, and exploratory serum and bronchoalveolar-lavage metabolomic signatures in CHD-associated PAH. These studies do not establish a shared pulmonary vascular metabolic mechanism. Cobalamin C (cblC) deficiency provides the clearest evidence that a defined metabolic disorder can cause severe pediatric pulmonary hypertension and that targeted biochemical treatment can normalize pulmonary pressure in many affected children. Adult human and experimental studies support candidate roles for pyruvate dehydrogenase regulation, mitochondrial redox signaling and fission, endothelial and fibroblast glycolysis, inflammation, and right-ventricular lipid handling, but these pathways remain candidates for pediatric testing rather than established pediatric targets.

Conclusions

No metabolism-directed therapy has demonstrated efficacy and long-term safety in children with idiopathic, heritable, or CHD-associated PAH. Clinical practice should prioritize phenotype-directed screening for defined metabolic or nutritional disorders. Research should use pediatric subgroup-specific sampling, direct flux measurements, causal perturbation and rescue, independent replication, and prospective linkage to clinical outcomes.

title: Prenatal multimodal ultrasound assessment of a fetal hepatic artery-umbilical vein fistula with an atypical Sylvian fissure appearance: a case description.
authorString: Niu KX, Yue ZC, Zhang WD, Li TG.

journal.title: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery

title: Genetic primary adrenal insufficiency in children: a narrative review.
authorString: Dai L, Bao Y, Hu L.
abstractText:
Background and objective

Pediatric primary adrenal insufficiency (PAI) beyond common 21-hydroxylase deficiency comprises rare monogenic disorders affecting adrenal development, steroidogenesis, adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) signaling, or cellular stress responses. Clinical overlap is substantial, but associated features such as disorders of sex development, hypogonadism, alacrima and achalasia, neurologic disease, growth restriction, or immunodeficiency can guide etiologic testing. This review summarizes the molecular basis, genotype-phenotype relationships, diagnostic approach, and emerging therapies for these disorders.

Methods

Literature from 2015 to 2025 was retrieved from PubMed using keywords: pediatric adrenal insufficiency; non-congenital adrenal hyperplasia; monogenic endocrine disorders; steroidogenesis; next-generation sequencing. Papers were filtered by pre-set inclusion and exclusion criteria. This review synthesizes current diagnostic algorithms, highlighting the critical integration of baseline biochemical profiling with high-throughput next-generation sequencing (NGS) and whole-exome sequencing (WES) to achieve precise molecular characterization and mitigate missed diagnoses.

Key content and findings

Severe loss-of-function variants in genes required for adrenal development or steroidogenesis generally present early with combined glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid deficiency, whereas hypomorphic variants may cause later-onset or isolated glucocorticoid deficiency. Extra-adrenal findings narrow the differential diagnosis and should determine the first genes analyzed. Biochemical phenotyping remains essential, but targeted panels or WES improve diagnostic yield when presentations overlap. Hormone replacement prevents mortality but does not reproduce physiologic cortisol exposure or treat the neurologic, reproductive, or immune components of syndromic disease.

Conclusions

Diagnosis should integrate the age at onset, pattern of steroid deficiency, associated phenotype, and molecular testing rather than rely on a single clinical feature. Current limitations include incomplete genotype-phenotype prediction, variants of uncertain significance, uneven access to functional testing, and limited pediatric outcome data for modified-release or infusion-based hydrocortisone. Near-term priorities are prospective registries, standardized variant interpretation, and genotype-stratified studies. Gene editing, gene replacement, and cell-based adrenal restoration remain experimental and should be matched to the affected tissue and mutation mechanism; hematopoietic transplantation can treat selected immune or neurologic complications but does not restore adrenal steroidogenesis.

title: Risk factors and day-14 prediction models for bronchopulmonary dysplasia and coexisting retinopathy of prematurity in very-low-birth-weight or very preterm infants.
authorString: Fan Y, Ge H, Li S, Han X, Huang X, Wu W, Wang Y, Zhang Y, Liu J, Zou L, Ren C, Li H.
abstractText:
Background

Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) and retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) share developmental, oxygen-related, and inflammatory susceptibility. We examined factors associated with BPD and with ROP among infants with BPD and developed prediction models restricted to information available by postnatal day 14.

Methods

This retrospective two-center study included 437 infants born before 32 weeks of gestation or weighing less than 1,500 g at birth. Conventional logistic regression evaluated mutually adjusted associations. For prediction, 15 prespecified variables available by day 14 were entered into elastic-net logistic regression. Preprocessing and hyperparameter selection were confined to the training data after an outcome-stratified 8:2 split. The classification threshold was selected from training-set out-of-fold predictions; the held-out test set was used once. Discrimination, calibration, Brier score, and repeated nested cross-validation were assessed.

Results

Among 437 infants, 172 (39.4%) had BPD; among those with BPD, 89 of 172 (51.7%) had ROP. In the association analysis, lower gestational age, longer invasive ventilation and oxygen therapy, and later first feeding were associated with BPD. Among infants with BPD, longer cumulative respiratory support, lower platelet distribution width (PDW) at 24 hours and day 14, male sex, and shorter birth length were associated with ROP. The day-14 BPD model yielded a held-out area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.789 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.688-0.880], a Brier score of 0.199, and an accuracy of 0.739. The ROP model yielded an AUC of 0.690 (95% CI: 0.500-0.859), a Brier score of 0.235, and an accuracy of 0.629. Mean AUCs across repeated nested cross-validation were 0.846 and 0.752, respectively.

Conclusions

Routinely available information through day 14 provided moderate internal discrimination for BPD and for ROP among infants with BPD. The models define a transparent prediction landmark and avoid use of later cumulative treatment variables, but require external and prospective validation before clinical use.

title: Mitral annular disjunction associated with myxomatous mitral valve disease, infundibular pulmonic stenosis and ventricular septal defect in a dog: a case report.
authorString: Tavares LCJ, Santos BA, Goldfeder GT.

journal.title: Journal of veterinary cardiology : the official journal of the European Society of Veterinary Cardiology

abstractText: Mitral annular disjunction is an abnormality of the mitral valve characterized by a displacement of the mitral annulus in which the annulus is functionally decoupled from the left ventricle and moves toward the atrium during systole. In human medicine, it is commonly associated with an increased risk of mitral valve prolapse, cardiac arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death but rarely described in veterinary medicine. This article describes a case report of a six-year-old male Shih tzu dog with signs of frequent syncope episodes diagnosed by echocardiography with mitral annular disjunction associated with myxomatous mitral valve disease, infundibular pulmonic stenosis, and perimembranous ventricular septal defect with bidirectional shunting. Due to the patient's congenital heart defects, clinical signs, and laboratory results, the hemodynamic profile was determined to be functionally analogous to the Tetralogy of Fallot. Conservative drug therapy with β-blocker propranolol was chosen rather than a surgical approach. Short-term follow-up showed initial improvement of clinical signs, followed by progressive worsening. The total survival time was 19 months from the initial diagnosis and the conservative palliative therapy. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first report of mitral annular disjunction associated with congenital abnormalities in dogs.

title: [Long-term Outcomes and Treatment Strategies for Minimally Invasive Mitral Valve Repair].
authorString: Yamamoto M, Hiraoka A, Totsugawa T, Sakaguchi T.

journal.title: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery

abstractText: We have actively adopted minimally invasive mitral valve plasty (MICS-MVP) since the early phase of its introduction. Between October 2012 and March 2021, we performed MICS-MVP in 264 patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation. The mean age was 58.5 (range, 18~82) years;104 patients (39 %) were female, and 60 patients had concomitant atrial fibrillation. Concomitant procedures were performed in 150 patients, including tricuspid valve surgery in 56 patients, arrhythmia surgery in 59, left atrial appendage procedures in 58, and congenital heart disease surgery in 39. The mean operative time was 254 minutes. Regarding repair techniques, artificial chordae were used in 139 cases;annuloplasty was performed using a full ring in 101 cases and a partial band in 162 cases. The 5-year survival rate was 98.1%, and the 5-year freedom from major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) was 92.8%. There were no cardiac deaths, and 7 readmissions for heart failure. Compared with the fullring group, the partial-band group showed a significantly lower mean mitral valve pressure gradient (p<0.001). By multivariable analysis for MACCE incidence and readmission for heart failure, none of the factors-including surgical technique and choice of annuloplasty device-were detected as significant predictors. In recent years, annuloplasty with partial band and artificial chordae has become our standard procedure to prevent functional mitral stenosis. Further standardization of surgical techniques may contribute to improve long-term outcomes.

title: Harmony™ Valve Implantation in the Right Pulmonary Artery in a Patient with Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot and Left Pulmonary Artery Occlusion: A Case Report.
authorString: Yabusaki M, Hasegawa S, Nakano S, Kojima T.
abstractText:
Transcatheter pulmonary valve implantation using the Harmony™ valve (Medtronic, Minneapolis, MN, USA) has expanded treatment options for pulmonary regurgitation in patients with enlarged right ventricular outflow tracts. However, complex pulmonary artery anatomy may preclude standard implantation in the main pulmonary artery. We report a 41-year-old woman with repaired tetralogy of Fallot and complete left pulmonary artery occlusion who developed severe pulmonary regurgitation and advanced biventricular dysfunction. Implantation in the main pulmonary artery was not feasible because of unfavorable anatomy and a significant pressure gradient. A 25-mm Harmony™ valve was therefore successfully implanted in the proximal right pulmonary artery, preserving branch perfusion and without creating additional pressure gradients. The patient's clinical condition stabilized without procedural complications. This case suggests that right pulmonary artery implantation of the Harmony™ valve may be a viable alternative in carefully selected patients with unilateral pulmonary artery occlusion when standard implantation is not feasible.

Learning objectives

This case highlights that the Harmony™ valve can be implanted in the proximal right pulmonary artery when standard main pulmonary artery implantation is not feasible. In patients with complex pulmonary artery anatomy, careful anatomical and hemodynamic assessment may enable alternative implantation strategies that preserve branch perfusion without creating additional pressure gradients.

title: Feasibility and acceptability of prenatal parental palliative care in congenital heart disease: a pilot study.
authorString: Hock KM, Dodenhoff E, Clark MG, Patrician PA, Landier W, Rice M, Shan L.
abstractText:
Background

Ductal dependent congenital heart disease (ddCHD) is associated with significant parental anxiety, yet palliative care (PC) support is rarely offered in the prenatal period. While prior studies have evaluated PC postnatally, little is known about feasibility and acceptability of prenatal PC interventions for this population. The purpose of this study is to assess feasibility and acceptability of prenatal PC support sessions (PCSS) for parents whose fetus has been diagnosed with ddCHD requiring neonatal cardiac intervention.

Methods

This prospective single-center feasibility study enrolled English-speaking parents referred to a pediatric cardiology clinic after fetal echocardiographic diagnosis of ddCHD. Eligible participants were offered monthly prenatal PCSS, in person or via videoconference, led by a dual-certified pediatric critical care and hospice/palliative medicine physician. Feasibility was defined as ≥75% session attendance and very/extremely easy scheduling and attendance ratings; acceptability was defined as ≥75% satisfied/very satisfied ratings.

Results

Of 26 eligible parents, 15 (58%) (10 mothers, 5 fathers) consented to participate. Sixteen sessions were scheduled; 14 (87.5%) were attended, with median duration of 42 min. Most sessions (75%) occurred via videoconference. Thirteen participants (86.7%) rated scheduling and attendance as "very easy" or "extremely easy." All attendees rated the sessions as "satisfied" or "very satisfied."

Conclusion

Prenatal PC support for families facing a ddCHD diagnosis may be feasible and acceptable, with high rates of participation and satisfaction at a single tertiary care hospital. Larger, multi-center studies are warranted to assess outcomes and develop sustainable models for integrating prenatal PC into congenital heart disease care pathways.

title: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in pediatric cardiac surgery: retrospective survival analysis.
authorString: Abdelrehim AR, Elhady M, Alnajjar AA, Allugmani M, Benouadah D, Sabtirul M, Wally A, Alothmali A, Qawalh A, Elsayed MS, Alabsi FA, Elderie A, Alashwal M, Al-Muhaya MA, Salem SS.
abstractText:
Background

Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is a life-saving therapeutic modality in children. Outcome is multifactorial with debates regarding predictors of weaning success and mortality.

Objective

To explore predictors of ECMO outcome in children with surgically corrected congenital heart disease (CHD).

Method

This single-center retrospective cohort study included children with operated CHD who were admitted to a tertiary-care cardiac center in Saudi Arabia during 2022-2025. Demographic data, clinical characteristics, as well as operative and ECMO details were recorded. Predictors of weaning failure and overall mortality during follow-up were analyzed.

Results

Thirty children aged 15 days to 12.8 years were included. ECMO connection was applied in day zero in 23 patients (76.6%). ECMO duration ranged between 1 and 15 days. Successful ECMO weaning was achieved in 56.7%. ECMO complication included renal injury in 36.7%, neurological complications in 16.7% and wound infection in 10%. The overall mortality rate was 46.7%. Residual cardiac lesions (OR 20; 95%CI:2.037-196.37 and OR 25.6; 95%CI:2.544-257.566) and ECMO complication (OR 5.4; 95%CI:1.12-26.044 and OR 7.5.6; 95%CI:1.484-37.905) were associated with ECMO failure and mortality during follow-up.

Conclusion

Residual cardiac lesions and ECMO-related complications were associated with poor outcome in children with surgically corrected CHD who require ECMO. The complexity of cardiac surgery and delayed initiation of ECMO are associated with prolonged ECMO stay duration. Proper timing of ECMO Initiation may reduce complications and improve survival.

title: Impact of timing on outcomes following redo-sternotomy after initial CABG or valvular surgery.
authorString: Yan J, McKinnerney J, Al Janabi T, Vranian MN, Kashyap R.
abstractText:
Objective

The optimal timing of reoperation for those who need repeat coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and valve surgery is not well established. Early re-entries may be technically challenging due to adhesions and incomplete healing, while delayed interventions may expose patients to progressive cardiac disease.

Methods

Patients undergoing redo-sternotomy for CABG and valve surgery were identified from the TriNetX database and categorized into three cohorts based on the interval from their initial sternotomy: <1 year, 1-5 years, and > 5 years. Redo-sternotomies performed < 30 days after the initial procedure were excluded, as these typically represent early interventions for acute complications rather than planned reoperations. Two independent propensity score-matched analyses compared < 1 year vs. 1-5 years and 1-5 years vs. > 5 years, with separately matched 1-5 years cohorts for each comparison. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed based on demographics, comorbidities, prior cardiac procedures, medications, and laboratory parameters including BMI. Primary outcomes included all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), and emergency department or hospital readmissions. Secondary outcomes included postoperative infection, atrial fibrillation, acute kidney injury, dialysis, cardiogenic shock, respiratory failure, and cerebrovascular events.

Results

After PSM in the < 1 year vs. 1-5 years analysis (N = 305 in each group), redo-sternotomy within 1 year showed no significant differences in mortality, MACCE or readmissions. Combined cerebrovascular events were significantly reduced in the < 1 year group. In the 1-5 years vs. > 5 years analysis (N = 439 in each group), outcomes were similar between groups, with no significant differences in mortality, MACCE, or readmissions. Atrial fibrillation was significantly higher in the 1-5 years group. All other secondary outcomes, including combined cerebrovascular events, were comparable.

Conclusion

Redo-sternotomy within 1 year appears to be equally safe compared to later intervals, with comparable rates of adverse events, including mortality, MACCE, readmissions, postoperative infection, or AKI.

title: Preliminary experience of mechanical thrombectomy treatment in pediatric arterial ischemic stroke: a retrospective case series.
authorString: Zhou Y, Li S, Zhuang Y, Li Z, Yang K.
abstractText:
Objective

To evaluate the feasibility and efficacy of mechanical thrombectomy in the treatment of pediatric acute ischemic stroke (AIS).

Methods

The clinical data, radiographic results and management outcomes of children diagnosed with AIS and treated at our hospital between 2016 and 2021 were retrospectively analyzed.

Results

A total of 8 patients (4 male and 4 female) were included, with a mean age of 7.8 ± 2.8 years. All patients presented with focal neurological deficits at onset, including hemiplegia, facial deviation, mild limb weakness, dizziness, and headache, with Pediatric National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (PedNIHSS) scores ranging from 4 to 12 on presentation. Six patients had isolated middle cerebral artery occlusion, one bilateral posterior cerebral artery occlusion, and one had combined middle cerebral and anterior cerebral artery occlusion. Half of the patients underwent two mechanical thrombectomy procedures. After treatment, all patients achieved a modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (mTICI) score of ≥2b. The median follow up duration was 20.13 months (range, 6-32 months). At the 6-month follow-up, all patients had the pediatric modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores of 0 to 1.

Conclusion

Our preliminary experience suggests that mechanical thrombectomy is technically feasible and may be associated with favorable short- to medium-term functional outcomes in carefully selected pediatric patients with large vessel AIS. However, due to the retrospective design, small sample size, and lack of a control group, further multicenter prospective studies are warranted to better evaluate the safety and clinical outcomes of this procedure in pediatric patients.

title: Comparison of lung ultrasonography and chest radiography in detecting neonatal respiratory distress as a composite clinical condition: a prospective cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study at Muhimbili National Hospital.
authorString: Dadi HK, Baraka BM, Mhalu IH, Mkony MF.
abstractText:
Background

Neonatal respiratory distress (RD) is a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality. While chest radiography (CXR) is the traditional modality of diagnosis, lung ultrasound (LUS) has emerged as a bedside, radiation-free alternative for evaluating neonatal respiratory conditions.

Aim

To determine the diagnostic performance of lung ultrasonography (LUS) compared to chest radiography (CXR) in detecting neonatal respiratory distress (RD) as a composite clinical condition at Muhimbili National Hospital (MNH).

Methods

A prospective cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study was conducted at Muhimbili National Hospital (MNH) between June and December 2022. A total of 179 neonates with clinical signs of respiratory distress were consecutively enrolled. All neonates underwent both LUS and CXR within 6 h. Demographic and clinical data were collected using a structured tool. Diagnostic performance was assessed for overall respiratory distress rather than individual disease etiologies. Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), and diagnostic accuracy (DA) were calculated using a composite clinico-radiological reference standard. Agreement was assessed using Cohen's kappa with 95% confidence intervals and significance set at p < 0.05.

Results

Among 179 neonates (mean gestational age: 32 ± 4 weeks; mean birth weight: 1,769 ± 856 g), LUS demonstrated high diagnostic performance in this setting, with higher sensitivity (95.1% vs. 90.3%), specificity (94.7% vs. 89.5%), positive predictive value (PPV) (96.1% vs. 92.1%), negative predictive value (NPV) (93.5% vs. 87.2%), and diagnostic accuracy (95% vs. 90%) compared to chest radiography (CXR). We observed almost perfect agreement between lung ultrasonography and the reference standard (κ = 0.898) and substantial agreement between lung ultrasonography and chest radiography (κ = 0.806).

Conclusion

Lung ultrasonography demonstrated high diagnostic performance in this setting for detecting neonatal respiratory distress as a composite clinical condition. However, interpretation should consider the use of a composite reference standard that included chest radiography, which may have introduced incorporation bias. Additionally, the composite outcome limits interpretation for individual respiratory conditions. Despite these limitations, LUS appears to be a useful adjunct imaging modality in resource-limited settings, where access to radiography may be constrained.

title: Risk factors for pulmonary consolidation in 316 pediatric cases of chlamydia pneumoniae pneumonia: a single-center retrospective study.
authorString: Wang P, Ma R, Ba C, Zhang F, Hu D, Zhang Y.
abstractText:
Background

Chlamydia pneumoniae (CP) infection in children is increasingly recognized, with a growing proportion developing pulmonary consolidation. Early identification of risk factors is critical for timely intervention, yet systematic pediatric studies remain limited. We aimed to identify independent predictors of pulmonary consolidation and develop a nomogram for individualized risk assessment.

Methods

This retrospective study enrolled 316 children with Chlamydia pneumoniae pneumonia (CPP) at Hebei Children's Hospital (Jan-Dec 2025), divided into consolidation (n = 79) and non-consolidation (n = 237) groups. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and imaging data were compared between the two groups. Multivariable logistic regression was used to screen for independent predictors, which were then incorporated into a nomogram. Model discrimination was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and calibration was evaluated using the Hosmer-Lemeshow test and a calibration curve with 1000 bootstrap resamples.

Results

Multivariable analysis identified age, pre-admission illness duration, peak temperature, platelet count (PLT), C-reactive protein (CRP), and D-dimer as independent predictors (all P < 0.05). A nomogram was constructed based on peak temperature, PLT, CRP, and D-dimer. The nomogram showed good discriminative ability, with an AUC of 0.868 (95% CI: 0.823-0.912). Calibration was satisfactory: the bias-corrected curve closely followed the 45-degree ideal reference line, with a mean absolute error of 0.022, indicating excellent model calibration, and the Hosmer-Lemeshow test confirmed good fit (χ² = 9.736, df = 8, P = 0.284). At the optimal cutoff, the model yielded a sensitivity of 79.7% and a specificity of 79.7%.

Conclusions

The combined model (peak temperature, PLT, CRP, and D-dimer) demonstrated promising discrimination for identifying pulmonary consolidation in children with Chlamydia pneumoniae pneumonia. The identified cutoffs may indicate increased risk of existing consolidation and could support early risk stratification. However, given the retrospective cross-sectional design, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than prospective predictions; external validation in prospective studies is required before clinical application.

title: Quality assessment of primary health care for infants and young children in Hunan Province of China.
authorString: Li T, Zhang S, Jia N, Dai Y.
abstractText:
Objective

To comprehensively evaluate the service quality of primary health care (PHC) for children aged 0-3 years in healthcare facilities of China, and to identify strengths and existing gaps to provide evidence for optimizing regional child health service policies.

Methods

A multi-stage stratified random sampling method was used to select 35 healthcare facilities from 4 geographical regions in Hunan province of China. Data were collected using the WHO Western Pacific Regional Office Primary Health Care Quality Improvement Guide, which included facility assessments, medical record reviews, and caregiver interviews. All indicators were assessed against China national basic public health service standards and WHO PHC quality benchmarks. Chi-square test was used for comparative analysis between sick and healthy children.

Results

The overall PHC foundation was sound: 85.0% of service rooms had qualified handwashing facilities, 92.0% were equipped with alcohol rub, and over 97% of facilities had standardized protocols for breastfeeding screening and infection control. The key basic medicines and routine growth monitoring supplies achieved an availability rate above 91.4%. The under-6-month exclusive breastfeeding rate was 38.9%, and National Immunization Programme (NIP) vaccine coverage remained over 90% for most routine vaccines. However, significant gaps existed. Well children showed far higher health screening rates than sick children, with growth measurement completion rates of 93.9% vs. 72.2% for weight and 92.1% vs. 9.0% for height; respiratory rate screening remained extremely low at around 17% in both groups. Non-NIP vaccine coverage was only 28.5%-47.1%. The availability of therapeutic food, special vaccines and essential emergency medicines was below 30%, and only 45.8% of rooms were equipped with sharps containers and merely 28.6% of facilities had child abuse and neglect management protocols. Additionally, the staff IMCI training rate was only 54.2%, and patient-staff ratios ranged from 48.6% to 65.9% across clinics.

Conclusion

Child PHC services in Hunan Province perform well in basic infrastructure, routine health management and national immunization, but have prominent deficiencies in standardized clinical assessment for sick children, breastfeeding promotion, non-NIP vaccine accessibility, child protection system construction, essential drug supply, and human resource allocation. Targeted interventions on clinical standardization, material guarantee, professional training and child protection mechanism improvement are needed to further elevate the overall quality and equity of early childhood PHC services.

title: Infective endocarditis due to a novel <i>Gemella</i> species revealed by metagenomic sequencing.
authorString: Sekikawa Y, Horiba K, Hashino M, Soneda K, Kato T.
abstractText:
Background

Gemella species are rare causes of infective endocarditis, and accurate species identification can be challenging with routine diagnostic methods. We report infective endocarditis caused by a novel Gemella species, highlighting the diagnostic value of sequencing-based approaches for bacteria not registered in public databases and the risk of misclassification when novel species are not represented in reference databases.

Case summary

A 55-year-old Japanese man presented with fatigue, anorexia, and altered mental status. Echocardiography revealed vegetations on the mitral and tricuspid valves with severe mitral regurgitation, and imaging demonstrated multiple systemic embolic events. Blood cultures grew gram-positive cocci that were initially identified as Gemella bergeri by matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry. The patient received antimicrobial therapy and underwent mitral valve replacement and tricuspid valve repair. Culture of the excised valve tissue was negative. Metagenomic sequencing of the valve vegetation detected a Gemella species distinct from G. bergeri. Genome assembly from sequencing data showed 94.5% average nucleotide identity with a reference G. bergeri genome, supporting classification as a novel species. Whole-genome sequencing of the blood culture isolate demonstrated near-complete concordance with the organism detected in the valve tissue. The patient recovered with a 6-week course of intravenous penicillin G after blood cultures became sterile.

Conclusion

This case demonstrates that rare Gemella infections may be misidentified by routine mass spectrometry. It underscores the importance of sequencing-based methods for accurate pathogen identification and highlights a diagnostic pitfall associated with database-dependent identification in infective endocarditis.

title: Isolated systemic arterial supply to the normal lung presenting with massive hemoptysis in a child: CT angiographic diagnosis and endovascular management.
authorString: Singh R, Gupta V, Yadav R, Ghasi RG.
abstractText: Isolated systemic supply to normal lung (ISSNL) is an uncommon bronchopulmonary vascular abnormality in which a section of normally ventilated lung gets arterial blood from the systemic circulation, without accompanying bronchial or pulmonary abnormalities. We discuss a case of a 12-year-old boy who had a single episode of significant hemoptysis. Computed tomographic angiography (CTA) identified a significant convoluted anomalous artery originating from the mid-descending thoracic aorta, supplying the left lower lobe, with no evidence of fistulous connection to pulmonary arteries. The diagnosis of ISSNL was confirmed, and the patient was effectively treated with endovascular embolization with a vascular plug. At the 3-month follow-up, no recurrence of hemoptysis was seen. While often asymptomatic, ISSNL may manifest as hemoptysis or signs of volume overload. CTA is essential for diagnosis, anatomical characterization, and treatment strategy formulation. Timely identification of this condition is crucial, since endovascular embolization provides a safe and effective alternative to surgical intervention with less morbidity.

title: Risk factors for post-extubation stridor in pediatric cardiac intensive care unit: a single-center retrospective study.
authorString: Saengsin K, Wongyikul P, Phinyo P, Borisuthipandit T, Sittiwangkul R, Silvilairat S, Makonkawkeyoon K, Sethasathien S, Ayurag T, Wiwatkamonchai N, Sunkonkit K.
abstractText:
Background

Post-extubation stridor (PES) is a frequent and clinically significant complication among pediatric cardiac intensive care unit (PCICU) patients, particularly those with congenital heart disease (CHD). This study aimed to determine the incidence, associated risk factors, and outcomes of PES in this population.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study included children aged 1 month to 18 years who underwent planned extubation after more than 24 h of mechanical ventilation in the PCICU at Chiang Mai University Hospital between July 2016 and June 2024. Demographic, clinical, and ventilatory variables were retrieved from electronic medical records. Univariable and multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of PES.

Results

Among 494 extubation episodes from 380 children, PES occurred in 25.5% of attempts. Patients who developed PES were younger, low body weight, and had longer ventilation duration compared with those without PES. In multivariable analysis, lower body weight (OR 0.84; 95% CI, 0.73-0.97) and mechanical ventilation exceeding 7 days (OR 1.83; 95% CI, 1.04-3.23) remained significant independent predictors.

Conclusions

PES was common among pediatric cardiac patients and was independently associated with lower body weight at extubation and prolonged mechanical ventilation. Recognition of children at higher risk may support targeted preventive strategies and improve post-extubation outcomes.

title: A case of mucopolysaccharidosis I with severely increased albuminuria and Graves' disease, and functional analysis of previously uncharacterized variant.
authorString: Dong K, Peng JJ, Zhou X, Zhu Q, Li C, Yang Y.
abstractText:
Background

Mucopolysaccharidoses (MPS) are a group of inherited lysosomal storage disorders which results in accumulation of glycosaminoglycans throughout the body. MPS I is a subtype characterized by mutations in the α-L-iduronidase (IDUA) gene with subsequent multiorgan dysfunction.

Case description

Here, we describe an adult patient with MPS I who presented with anasarca, as well as severely increased albuminuria, and was initially diagnosed with hyperthyroidism. Subsequent testing revealed clinical characteristics and deficient IDUA enzyme activity consistent with MPS I. Genetic testing identified two variants of interest in the IDUA gene: IDUA c·265C > T (p.R89W) and IDUA c.1403-2A > G.

Methods

IDUA enzymatic activity was measured in HEK293T cells transfected with wildtype or p. R89W mutant IDUA expression constructs using the fluorogenic substrate 4-methylumbelliferyl-α-L-iduronide (4MU-iduronide). A minigene splicing assay was performed using IDUA exon 9-11 (including intron 9 and 10) DNA fragments cloned into the pMini-CopGFP vector, with the mutant plasmid containing the IDUA c.1403-2A > G variant generated using site-directed mutagenesis. HEK293T cells were transfected with either the wildtype or mutant plasmids, and splice products were separated by gel electrophoresis with distinct bands excised for Sanger sequencing.

Results

The IDUA c·265C > T (p.R89W) mutant construct was cloned into HEK293T cells and showed significantly decreased intracellular (10.86 ± 0.36%, p < 0.01) and extracellular (1.18 ± 0.09%, p < 0.01) enzymatic activity compared to wild type. A minigene splicing assay of the previously uncharacterized IDUA c.1403-2A > G splice site variant found retention of intron 9 between exon 9 and 10 leading to a premature termination codon.

Conclusion

This manuscript describes a unique clinical presentation of MPS I with simultaneous Graves' disease and severely increased albuminuria. Functional analysis of the IDUA variants identified in our patient adds to the current understanding of genetic variants implicated in the disease.

title: Integrated bioinformatics analysis and mouse validation identify C7 and MFAP4 as candidate genes associated with type 2 diabetes and atherosclerosis.
authorString: Wang L, Chen Y, Ding P, Wang H, Wu C, Li P, Ou C, Xie Z, Jin J, Hu J, Yu J, Wang Y.
abstractText:
Background

Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is closely associated with accelerated atherosclerosis (AS), but the molecular features linking these two conditions remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify candidate genes associated with T2DM and AS and to explore their potential biological relevance.

Methods

Public GEO transcriptomic datasets were analysed. GSE38642 and GSE100927 were used as T2DM and AS training datasets, while GSE41762 and GSE57691 were used for validation. Differentially expressed genes were identified using limma, and disease-associated modules were screened by weighted gene co-expression network analysis. Candidate genes were obtained by intersecting differentially expressed genes with module genes, followed by protein-protein interaction analysis, cytoHubba-MCC, and MCODE screening. Expression validation, receiver operating characteristic analysis, cross-validation, permutation testing, GeneMANIA, GSEA, ssGSEA-based immune infiltration analysis, regulatory network construction, and exploratory drug-gene enrichment analysis were performed. Selected genes were further examined in mouse models.

Results

21 overlapping genes were identified, and six candidate hub genes were further screened. Among them, C7 and MFAP4 showed reproducible but disease-context-dependent expression patterns and exploratory discriminatory performance across the training and validation datasets. Functional analyses suggested that C7 and MFAP4 were associated with inflammatory response, complement activation, TNF-α/NF-κB signaling, oxidative phosphorylation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and immune-related alterations. Additional robustness analyses supported the exploratory relevance of these two genes, particularly MFAP4, while also indicating that the findings should be interpreted cautiously. In mouse models, C7 and MFAP4 showed disease-associated expression changes, supporting their potential relevance to metabolic stress and vascular remodeling.

Conclusion

This integrated bioinformatics and experimental validation study identified C7 and MFAP4 as exploratory candidate genes associated with T2DM and AS.

title: Cardiovascular effects of methylphenidate, risperidone, and their combination in children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a prospective 3-month observational study.
authorString: Oveisi S, Jafari E, Bahari MM, Farshidgohar M.
abstractText:
Background

We aimed to evaluate changes in hemodynamic parameters and electrocardiographic (ECG) indices related to ventricular arrhythmia risk after three months of treatment with methylphenidate (MPH), risperidone (RIS), or their combination in children and adolescents with ADHD.

Methods

A total of 150 children and adolescents with DSM-5-diagnosed ADHD were prospectively enrolled at Qods Hospital. Participants received methylphenidate (n = 50), risperidone (n = 50), or combination therapy (n = 50). Cardiovascular outcomes were assessed using age- and weight-adjusted two-way repeated-measures ANCOVA to evaluate changes over time and differences among treatment groups.

Results

Significant group × time interactions were observed for systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, heart rate, and QTc interval after adjustment for baseline age and weight. After three months, systolic and diastolic blood pressure increased in the methylphenidate and combination therapy groups, while heart rate showed an overall increase, with the greatest rise observed in the methylphenidate group.
