QTc interval increased over time across all treatment groups, with the largest prolongation observed in the combination therapy group (377.9 ± 25.4 to 424.5 ± 24.9 ms). However, mean QTc values remained below commonly accepted thresholds for clinically significant QT prolongation, and no significant longitudinal changes were observed in QRS duration or PR intervals.

Conclusion

Treatment with methylphenidate, risperidone, and combination therapy was associated with modest changes in heart rate, blood pressure, and QTc interval over three months. These findings highlight the importance of baseline and follow-up cardiovascular monitoring in children and adolescents receiving ADHD medications.

title: The Italian Spina Bifida registry: insights from the first 1,000 patient data.
authorString: Salvatore M, Rocchetti A, Buoncuore G, Rendeli C, Capriati M, Taverna M, Redaelli T, Leo A, Bruno R, Dieci MC, Torreri P, Spina Bifida registry group.
abstractText:
Background

Spina bifida (SB) results from failure of fusion of the caudal neural tube leading to complications in several organ systems and considerable disability. The causes of this disorder are heterogeneous and multifactorial. Medical and surgical management is a lifelong necessity for people with SB (pwSB) and should be provided by a multidisciplinary team. Standardized collection of data in ad hoc registries represents an important tool to (i) collect clinical and epidemiologic data, (ii) assess the clinical management including the diagnostic delay, (iii) improve patients' care and (iv) foster research to identify new therapeutic solutions. The present study aimed to shed light on the analyses from the first 1.000 patients included in the Italian SB registry (period 2020-23) thus boosting the contribution of registries of pathology in the improvement of knowledge and research.

Methods

The Italian SB registry was established in 2020 to (i) describe the natural history of the disease, (ii) determine the clinical effectiveness of health care services, (iii) measure and monitor the quality of care of patients. It is based on a web-customizable-based system for the collection of demographics, diagnosis and genetics, patient status, therapy, quality of life and mortality data. Clinical data are updated annually during follow-up visits. Data quality is ensured by an automatic check performed by the system enabling a constant longitudinal and vertical control of data included in the registry. Descriptive statistics, including absolute and relative frequencies, mean, standard deviation, median, and percentiles, were used to summarize the quantitative variables of interest. the Pearson's Chi-Square Test was conducted to study the association between the qualitative variables under study.

Results

A total of 1.000 pwSB were enrolled in the first 36 months after registry establishment (period: October 2020 to October 2023) from 15 Referral paediatric and adult Italian Centres; 66,8% and 33,2% of patients were enrolled in a paediatric and an adult Centre respectively (53% female versus 47% males). Forty-point-4% (40,4%) of patients was characterized by open spina bifida (OSB) while 59,6% by a closed spina bifida (CSB). Diagnoses were performed during the prenatal period (26,6%), at birth (41,7%) and within the first year of life (15%), most of these latter cases being characterized by a CSB. Associated primary malformations were reported in 57.4% of patients; among these, Arnold-Chiari II malformation was significantly associated with OSB (p < 0.001). Lesions were mainly localized in the lumbosacral region (82.3%). Plastic surgery was performed in 549 patients, predominantly among OSB cases (73.5%).

Conclusions

The analyses of our data form, allowed to highlight important demographic and clinical aspects of SB useful to inform future actions to be taken by national health care services and health professionals. The present study represents the first report describing the Italian Spina Bifida Registry, aiming at demonstrating the feasibility and successful implementation of a national registry, which may serve as a foundation for future studies with direct implications for patient care.

title: Microbiota in liver carcinogenesis: Illuminating the complex relationship.
authorString: Chuaypen N, Dissayabutra T, Bajaj JS.
abstractText: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) develops predominantly in patients with cirrhosis, yet the biological mechanisms underlying the transition from cirrhosis to malignancy remain incompletely understood. Increasing evidence suggests that the oral-gut-liver axis contributes to this process through coordinated interactions among oral and intestinal microbiota, the epithelial barrier, the immune system, and the liver. While previous reviews have primarily focused on gut dysbiosis in cirrhosis and its complications, emerging evidence indicates that microbiome-associated alterations actively contribute to hepatocarcinogenesis. In this review, we propose a transition-state model in which disruption of the oral-gut-liver axis promotes progression from cirrhosis to HCC through functional microbiome insufficiency, epithelial barrier dysfunction, microbial translocation, inflammatory remodeling, and immune dysregulation. We emphasize that disruption of microbial metabolic functions, including reduced butyrate biosynthesis, bile acid remodeling, altered tryptophan metabolism, and enrichment of virulence-associated pathways may be more biologically relevant than taxonomic changes alone. We further discuss emerging biomarkers representing distinct domains of the gut-liver axis, including butyryl-CoA:acetate CoA-transferase (BCoAT) as a marker of microbial function, intestinal fatty acid-binding protein (I-FABP) as a marker of epithelial injury, and lipopolysaccharide-binding protein (LBP) as a marker of microbial translocation and endotoxemia. Finally, we discuss the translational implications of integrating microbiome-derived functional biomarkers with immune and clinical profiling for biological risk stratification, early detection, and precision hepatology as well as therapeutic strategies based on microbiome modulation. This framework shifts the focus from descriptive dysbiosis toward mechanistic host-microbiome interactions, highlights the oral-gut-liver axis as an active contributor to hepatocarcinogenesis, and provides a conceptual foundation for future microbiome-informed surveillance, risk stratification, and therapeutic strategies.

title: Cardiac Organoids Uncover an Association of CHD7 Deficiency with Congenital Heart Disease.
authorString: Sun S, Feng Z, Na W, Gao Y, Min S, Zhuang Q, Lin S, Zhao Q, Huang X, Song H, Sheng W, Huang G.
abstractText:
CHD7 (Chromodomain helicase DNA-binding protein 7) encodes an ATP-dependent chromatin remodeler, and pathogenic disruption of CHD7 underlies CHARGE syndrome(Coloboma, Heart defects, Atresia choanae, Retarded growth and development, Genital abnormalities, Ear abnormalities syndrome), a congenital disorder frequently accompanied by complex cardiac malformations. However, how CHD7 contributes to human cardiogenesis remains poorly defined. Here, we use multi-chamber cardiac organoids derived from human embryonic stem cells, which capture key features of early cardiac morphogenesis and regional lineage patterning, to interrogate CHD7 function. CHD7 loss leads to attenuation of cardiac progenitor gene programs, disrupted chamber organization, reduced efficiency of cardiomyocyte differentiation, and markedly impaired contractile function. Bulk RNA sequencing further reveals broad misregulation of transcriptional modules involved in cardiogenic signaling, regional progenitor patterning, and myocardial maturation. Together, these data establish a human organoid framework for modelling CHD7-associated congenital heart disease and identify CHD7 as a key regulator of cardiac morphogenesis and the acquisition of functional cardiomyocyte properties.

Graphical abstract

Supplementary information

The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s43657-026-00319-z.

title: The Effect of Adding Dexmedetomidine to Modified Del Nido Cardioplegia Solution on Myocardial Protection in Children Undergoing Congenital Heart Defect Surgery - A Prospective, Randomized, Triple-Blind, Controlled Trial.
authorString: Samadieh F, Maleki MH, Razeghian M, Izanlou T, Sistani MN, Fazli B, Yaghubi M.
abstractText:
Introduction

The myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) is an indispensable factor in pediatric congenital heart defect (CHD) surgery. Although effective myocardial protection strategies are crucial, the issue remains a dilemma. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of adding dexmedetomidine to modified Del Nido cardioplegia on myocardial protection in children undergoing CHD surgery.

Methods

This was a prospective, randomized, triple-blind, controlled clinical trial. A total of 60 pediatric patients were enrolled and randomized 1:1 into two groups - an intervention group that received dexmedetomidine-enriched modified Del Nido cardioplegia and a control group that received standard modified Del Nido cardioplegia with normal saline. Primary outcomes included serum troponin I and creatine kinase-MB levels, as well as coronary sinus lactate levels. Secondary outcomes were the vasoactive-inotropic score, weaning time from mechanical ventilation, and intensive care unit length of stay.

Results

Adding dexmedetomidine to modified Del Nido cardioplegia significantly improved myocardial protection in children undergoing CHD surgery. The intervention group showed significantly lower troponin I levels at all postoperative time points compared to the control group (P < 0.001). Similarly, the dexmedetomidine group had significantly lower vasoactive-inotropic score at all time points (P < 0.001). Patients in the intervention group also experienced a significantly shorter mean ventilator weaning time (P < 0.001) and intensive care unit stay duration (P < 0.001). The overall distribution of postoperative morbidities did not differ significantly between the groups (P = 0.059).

Conclusion

Adding dexmedetomidine to modified Del Nido cardioplegia significantly improved myocardial protection in children undergoing corrective CHD surgery.

title: Double-Inlet single ventricle associated with transposition of the great arteries, <i>situs inversus</i>, and criss-cross heart in an unrepaired adult: A case report.
authorString: Vargas-Lucio B, Bravo-Alvarado J, Gaibor-Gaibor S, Vargas-Lucio E, Almache-Palacios A.

journal.title: Archivos peruanos de cardiologia y cirugia cardiovascular

abstractText: The single ventricle represents a group of complex congenital heart diseases characterized by the mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, chronic cyanosis, and ventricular volume overload. The combination of a double-inlet single ventricle with transposition of the great arteries, situs inversus, and a criss-cross heart is extremely rare, reported only in isolated cases in the literature. Most of these patients require early palliative interventions, such as the bidirectional Glenn procedure and eventual Fontan circulation, to optimize oxygenation and reduce ventricular overload. We present the case of a 26-year-old man with a history of cyanotic congenital heart disease, scheduled for surgery at age 12 but managed conservatively due to high surgical risk. Survival into adulthood without definitive surgical correction is likely due to a favorable hemodynamic balance conferred by pulmonary stenosis, which limits pulmonary overcirculation and protects the dominant ventricle. Currently, the patient remains clinically stable, classified as New York Heart Association functional class II, with no recent episodes of cardiovascular decompensation, hospitalizations, or documented thromboembolic events. This case highlights the anatomical rarity and underscores the importance of specialized follow-up in adults with complex univentricular congenital heart disease who have not undergone corrective surgery.

title: Heart transplant in an adult patient with dysfunctional Fontan circulation at a high-complexity cardiovascular center in Peru: A case report.
authorString: Conde Moncada RY, Robles Velarde V, Zamudio Silva R, Masabel Chicoma EA, Zavala Castillo SM, Soplopuco Palacios FR.

journal.title: Archivos peruanos de cardiologia y cirugia cardiovascular

abstractText: Fontan circulation failure represents a progressive condition associated with multiorgan dysfunction and increased morbidity and mortality. In this context, heart transplantation has become the definitive treatment for this subgroup of patients. Reported survival rates after heart transplantation in patients with Fontan circulation are approximately 80% at 1 year, 74% at 5 years, and 59% at 10 years. We present the case of a 46-year-old patient with a history of Ebstein anomaly who underwent intracardiac Fontan surgery, which progressed to progressive Fontan circulation failure, and who underwent orthotopic heart transplantation with reconstruction of the pulmonary branches.

title: Acute cardiac failure in pregnancy: diagnosis and treatment.
authorString: Muñoz-Ortiz E, Gándara-Ricardo JA, Holguín-González É, Velázquez-Penagos JA, Flórez-Muñoz JP, Giraldo-Serna MB, Arana-Escandón YI.

journal.title: Archivos peruanos de cardiologia y cirugia cardiovascular

abstractText: Heart disease affects approximately 4% of pregnancies and is the leading non-obstetric cause of maternal death during pregnancy in many countries. The physiological hormonal and haemodynamic changes that occur during this period can unmask previously undiagnosed cardiac disease and destabilise pre-existing cardiovascular conditions. Acute heart failure during pregnancy is uncommon; however, it can lead to severe maternal and fetal complications. Although the diagnostic criteria are the same as those used in the general population, diagnosis can be challenging because the cardinal signs and symptoms of heart failure overlap with several symptoms and clinical findings that commonly occur during pregnancy. A comprehensive clinical history therefore remains fundamental to the diagnostic approach, enabling the rational use of complementary investigations and, in many cases, guiding treatment. Management of acute heart failure during pregnancy must be highly individualised and may involve decisions regarding continuation of the pregnancy and the optimal mode of delivery. Care should therefore be led by an experienced multidisciplinary team with expertise in the diagnosis and management of cardiovascular disease during pregnancy, with the aim of achieving the best possible outcomes for both the mother and the fetus.

title: Neurologic presentation unmasks arrhythmogenic channelopathy: KCNH2 variant Long-QT syndrome managed with subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator. A case report.
authorString: Vallejos-Barrientos A, Centeno-Araujo A, Soto-Becerra R, Cabrera-Saldaña M, Guevara-Caicedo C, Gonzales-Luna AC, Payano-Rojas M, Cueva-Parra Á, Calle-García R, Ramos-Godoy C, Zelaya-Castro P.

journal.title: Archivos peruanos de cardiologia y cirugia cardiovascular

abstractText: A previously healthy 10-year-old boy developed febrile seizure-like episodes after an appendectomy, which were diagnosed as epilepsy despite a normal electroencephalogram. He later presented with dyspnea and palpitations and was prescribed propafenone for frequent premature ventricular complexes. The electrocardiogram showed a markedly prolonged QTc interval of 550 ms with a notched T wave in lead V2. Phenytoin and propafenone were discontinued, and propranolol was initiated, but QTc prolongation persisted. The combination of severely prolonged QTc, characteristic T-wave morphology, and absence of structural heart disease redirected the diagnosis toward a repolarization channelopathy; genetic testing confirmed long-QT syndrome type 2 due to a pathogenic KCNH2 c.1814C>T variant. β-blocker therapy was optimized, QT-prolonging triggers were avoided, and a subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was implanted. Cascade genetic screening identified no additional KCNH2 carriers. One variant-negative sister had frequent idiopathic right ventricular outflow tract premature ventricular complexes and was referred for catheter ablation.

title: Feasibility and Early Outcomes of Intraoperative Extubation in Pediatric Atrial and Ventricular Septal Defect Repair via Axillary Thoracotomy.
authorString: Seçici S, Terkanlıoglu S.
abstractText:
Introduction

This retrospective study evaluated the feasibility, safety, and early recovery outcomes of intraoperative extubation combined with minimally invasive axillary thoracotomy for atrial septal defect (ASD) and ventricular septal defect (VSD) repair in pediatric patients.

Methods

Sixty-one consecutive pediatric patients who underwent ASD (n = 43) or VSD (n = 18) repair via axillary thoracotomy between March 2017 and December 2023 were included. Patients were categorized by extubation timing into intraoperative (operating room [OR] group) and postoperative (intensive care unit [ICU] group). Baseline characteristics, operative variables, and postoperative outcomes were compared.

Results

In the ASD cohort, patients extubated intraoperatively had a shorter hospital stay compared with those extubated in the ICU (2.78 ± 1.24 vs. 3.60 ± 0.99 days, P < 0.001). In the VSD cohort, the OR group included younger and lower-weight patients yet demonstrated a significantly shorter hospital stay (3.56 ± 0.73 vs. 5.78 ± 3.35 days, P = 0.013). Across the entire cohort, on-table extubation was associated with reduced hospital stay (P < 0.001), with no increase in reintubation or major complications.

Conclusions

Intraoperative extubation following axillary thoracotomy for ASD and VSD repair in pediatric patients appears safe and feasible and was associated with a significantly shorter hospital stay, even in lower-weight patients. These findings suggest that intraoperative extubation may be considered as part of enhanced recovery strategies in pediatric congenital heart surgery.

title: Camptodactyly and Early-Onset Scoliosis in Snijders Blok-Campeau Syndrome.
authorString: Miura M, Kobayashi Y, Hojo M, Yamada K, Fujii H, Eimori K, Yanagi K, Kaname T, Nagasaki K, Nyuzuki H, Ikeuchi T, Tohyama J.
abstractText: Snijders Blok-Campeau syndrome is caused by a heterozygous CHD3 pathogenic variant, and characterized by features including macrocephaly, speech delay, hypotonia, and joint laxity. In the hereby-presented case, a Japanese girl with Snijders Blok-Campeau syndrome displayed bilateral middle finger camptodactyly and early-onset scoliosis, beyond the characteristic symptoms such as intellectual disability, facial abnormalities, macrocephaly, and hypotonia due to a recurrent CHD3 pathogenic variant. This case expands our knowledge of the phenotypic spectrum of Snijders Blok-Campeau syndrome.

title: Clinical study on feasibility and repeatability of left ventricular systolic function assessment in patients with chronic kidney disease using artificial intelligence-based automatic strain technique.
authorString: Tian F, Wu Z, Zhong L, Qiu J, Tang H.

journal.title: Malawi medical journal : the journal of Medical Association of Malawi

abstractText:
Background

Cardiovascular damage is a common complication in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), and left ventricular longitudinal strain (GLS) is superior to LVEF in evaluating systolic function. However, it has not been widely adopted clinically because it requires proficiency and is time-consuming. This study aimed to investigate the feasibility, reproducibility, and predictive value of automated GLS compared with manual GLS, providing a reference for clinical evaluation and reduction of cardiovascular events in CKD patients.

Methods

A total of 285 CKD patients (aged 52 ± 12.85) without dialysis were enrolled from Hainan Provincial People's Hospital. GLS was measured using three methods on identical apical three-, two-, and four-chamber views: (1) fully automatic GLS analyzed by machine functions, (2) semi-automatic GLS corrected by researchers, and (3) manual GLS measured by experts. Five cases were excluded due to poor image quality. Clinical outcomes were followed up by telephone and outpatient visits.

Results

About 35% of automatic GLS results required manual correction, with significant differences among the three methods (P < 0.01). The correlation and consistency between semi-automatic and manual GLS were higher than those of automatic GLS (P < 0.01). During 2-year follow-up, 55 patients (19.6%) experienced cardiovascular events. Automated GLS predicted events but with lower accuracy than semi-automatic GLS. The analysis time for automatic (15.23 ± 0.75 s) and semi-automatic GLS (75.06 ± 19.01 s) was markedly shorter than manual analysis (236.81 ± 45.41 s, P < 0.01).

Conclusions

Automated GLS assessment in CKD patients is feasible and reproducible. As some images still require manual correction, the semi-automated approach currently offers the optimal balance between efficiency and predictive value.

title: Prenatal diagnosis of agenesis of the portal system type II Abernethy malformation associated with trisomy 21.
authorString: Mendes Ribeiro AC, Araújo M, de Nazaré Miziara A, de Figueiredo LRAS, de Abreu YR, Araujo Júnior E, Peixoto AB.
abstractText: Congenital agenesis of the portal vein (CAPV) is a rare vascular anomaly characterized by absence of the portal vein, resulting in abnormal shunting of splenic and mesenteric blood directly into the systemic circulation without adequate hepatic perfusion. This case report describes a fetus diagnosed prenatally with CAPV associated with trisomy 21 (Down syndrome), confirmed postnatally. Detailed ultrasonographic and Doppler findings revealed a porto-caval shunt and vascular abnormalities, while genetic analysis confirmed the chromosomal anomaly. The newborn presented with moderate pulmonary hypertension and mild congenital heart defects, requiring multidisciplinary management. This report highlights the importance of early prenatal diagnosis through imaging, enabling appropriate obstetric planning and postnatal care. The association between CAPV and trisomy 21, although rare, underscores the need for genetic investigation in fetuses with vascular malformations. Follow-up demonstrated persistence of the porto-caval shunt - type II Abernethy malformation, reinforcing the pathological nature of the condition and necessity for specialized monitoring. This case contributes to the understanding of the clinical spectrum and embryological origins of CAPV and its syndromic associations.

Preoperative Lower Respiratory Tract Infection and Postoperative Mortality in Elderly Hip Fracture Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study
authorString: Chu L, Chen X, Liu W, Zhang S, Wang X, Liu Z, Xi C.
abstractText: Background Preoperative lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) is common in elderly hip fracture patients, but its prognostic significance remains understudied. We aimed to investigate whether preoperative LRTI is independently associated with postoperative mortality in this population. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 1,922 elderly patients (≥ 60 years) who underwent hip fracture surgery at a single Level I trauma center between 2015 and 2021. Preoperative LRTI was identified from medical records according to European guidelines. The primary outcomes were 30-day and 1-year all-cause mortality. Hierarchical Cox regression models (Models 1–5) were used to sequentially adjust for demographics, nutritional and inflammatory status, comorbidities, surgical factors, and postoperative complications. Subgroup analyses were performed. Results Preoperative LRTI was present in 319 patients (16.6%). In fully adjusted models, preoperative LRTI was independently associated with increased 30-day mortality (HR 2.68, 95% CI 1.67–4.33) and 1-year mortality (HR 1.71, 95% CI 1.30–2.26). Patients with preoperative LRTI also had significantly higher rates of postoperative cardiac events (8.8% vs. 2.9%) and new-onset pneumonia (21.6% vs. 6.8%). In exploratory subgroup analyses the association appeared stronger in patients with low neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), although this finding requires validation in future studies. Conclusions Preoperative LRTI is an independent risk factor for both short- and medium-term mortality in elderly hip fracture patients. Preoperative LRTI should be actively screened for and incorporated into preoperative risk stratification. Future multicenter prospective studies are needed to validate these findings and determine whether preoperative optimization can improve outcomes.

title: Association of the admission albumin–bilirubin score with long-term major adverse cardiovascular events among patients who survived to discharge after percutaneous coronary intervention for non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction: a single-center cohort study
authorString: Lin Y, Yao J, Lin C, Wu J, Li S.
abstractText: Objective To investigate the association of admission albumin–bilirubin (ALBI) score with long-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) among patients who survived to discharge after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), and to assess whether ALBI provides prognostic information beyond the admission GRACE score. Methods We retrospectively included 681 patients hospitalized between January 1, 2023, and September 1, 2025, who survived to discharge after PCI for NSTEMI. Patients were categorized into ALBI tertiles (T1, T2 and T3). Kaplan–Meier analysis, multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and restricted cubic spline analysis were used to evaluate the association between ALBI and long-term MACEs. Missing data were handled using predictive mean matching, generating 50 imputed datasets. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed. The discriminatory performance of the admission GRACE-based model was compared before and after ALBI was added. Follow-up continued through September 6, 2026. Results Among 681 patients, the median follow-up duration was 585 days, during which 186 MACEs occurred, representing 27.3% of the cohort. The cumulative proportions of MACEs in T1, T2 and T3 were 18.1%, 29.1% and 34.8%, respectively, differing significantly among groups (all P < 0.001). After adjustment, each 1-standard-deviation (1-SD) increase in ALBI was associated with a 25% higher risk of long-term MACEs (HR = 1.25, 95% CI: 1.06–1.46, P = 0.007). Compared with T1, the corresponding HRs were 1.59 for T2 and 1.60 for T3. Restricted cubic spline analysis showed no evidence of a significant nonlinear association. The results were therefore compatible with an approximately linear association within the observed ALBI range. The direction of association remained positive in sensitivity analyses, although the complete-case estimate was less precise and was not statistically significant. Adding ALBI produced small, statistically nonsignificant increases in the GRACE model’s C-index and 365-day time-dependent AUC. Conclusion Among patients who survived to discharge after PCI for NSTEMI, a higher admission ALBI score was independently associated with increased risk of long-term MACEs, with an approximately linear pattern across the observed range. ALBI may serve as a simple marker of long-term risk. Its incremental predictive value beyond the GRACE score requires validation in multicenter prospective studies.

title: An Efficient Microfluidic Platform for Organ-Specific Cyclic Multiaxial Loading and Differentiation of Progenitor Cells
authorString: Murugesan N, Arkat S, Aristotle D, Saha S, Paul A, Guhathakurta S, Mullasari A, Shah P, Kamath SR, Mahapatra NR, Das SK.
abstractText: Mechanical loading is a fundamental regulator of tissue development, maturation, and function, yet existing  in vitro systems predominantly apply uniaxial load/strain to cell-laden hydrogels, limiting their ability to reproduce physiologically relevant multiaxial on-chip tissue mechanics. Here, we present an engineered system to apply controlled multiaxial mechanical loading to real scaffolds with undifferentiated cells. The system enables programmable cyclic stretching and relaxation at the cell scaffold level and is compatible with both cell-laden native scaffold and engineered soft tissues. We have quantified the strain field experienced by the tissue with distinct mechanical loading periods using computation simulations and validated these with systematic experiments, demonstrating reproducible and various organ-relevant multiaxial strain profiles. As proof of concept, we applied the approach to human cardiac tissues, where cyclic multiaxial mechanical loading of mononuclear cells laden native tissue scaffold promoted cardiac structural organization and supports the emergence of spontaneous contractile activity. This approach provides a generalizable method for reproducing physiologically relevant tissue mechanics  in vitro and enables systematic investigation of mechano-regulation across a plethora of human tissues.

title: Submembrane geography dictates GPCR signalling compartmentation and physiological function
authorString: Froese A, Qi B, Feng M, Böer G, Morhenn K, Kupsch S, Sun X, Subramanian H, Sanchez-Alonso JL, Medvedev R, Wright PT, Gallego M, Revuelta D, Beck NI, Molina CE, Miragoli M, Rossi S, Ehmke H, Gorelik J, Parak WJ, Feliu N, Nikolaev VO.
abstractText: G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are key mediators of intercellular signalling and targets for the vast majority of current therapeutics. Numerous biochemical and biophysical studies have uncovered that individual GPCRs activated at different subcellular locations can mediate distinct functional effects due to compartmentalization of the downstream second messengers in subcellular nanodomains. However, the reasons why a single receptor subtype activated at the same subcellular compartment such as plasma membrane leads to various functional responses have remained poorly understood. Here, we used β  1 -adrenergic receptor and cardiomyocytes as classical examples of a therapeutically relevant GPCR and highly compartmentalized cell, to study communication between membrane receptors and subcellular cAMP nanodomains based on a combination of nanoscale scanning ion conductance microscopy assisted local receptor activation with Förster resonance energy transfer based live cell imaging of the cAMP pathway. Unexpectedly, this approach revealed that β  1 -adrenoceptors located in cardiomyocyte T-tubular membrane are strongly coupled to the regulation of cardiac contractility, whereas receptors residing in the outer non-tubular membrane preferentially engage nuclear nanodomains linked to hypertrophy. This unique mechanism of spatially segregated signalling was maintained in failing rodent and human hearts, indicating that it is conserved across species and preserved in disease. Finally, we explored potential therapeutic targeting of this mechanism by generating submembrane-specific beta-blockers acting exclusively at the outer non-tubular membrane. These improved compounds could ameliorate hypertrophy and cardiac remodeling without reducing contractility  in vitro and  in vivo . Together, these findings uncover an unexpected level of spatial organization of GPCR signaling within the same subcellular compartment and show that not only its identity but also its submembrane location determines cellular signaling and functional response engaged by the same GPCR.

title: Symptom-Demand journey map for patients with cardiometabolic multimorbidity undergoing the periprocedural pathway of percutaneous coronary intervention: A qualitative study
authorString: Shi Y, Li T, Li Y, Wang Z, Cai Z, Zhou J, Tao J.
abstractText: Background Patients with cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) face complex physical, psychosocial, and self-management demands, yet their stage-specific symptoms and care needs across the PCI pathway remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to map these stage-specific experiences and construct a patient journey map to inform tailored nursing care. Methods Guided by the Timing It Right (TIR) framework, we conducted a qualitative descriptive study using maximum-variation purposive sampling. Sixteen patients with CMM undergoing PCI were recruited from the Department of Cardiology at a tertiary hospital in Wuhan, China, from June to July 2026 and participated in 20 semi-structured interviews. Qualitative content analysis used four prespecified journey-map domains with inductive development of subthemes, which were synthesized into a patient journey map. Results The PCI pathway was represented by three phases: preprocedural preparation, postprocedural recovery, and transition. Forty-eight subthemes were identified across four domains: symptoms, care needs, emotions, and pain points. Preprocedural accounts emphasized symptom recognition, gaps in chronic disease self-management, and needs for procedural information and reassurance; postprocedural accounts centered on symptom burden, prognostic uncertainty, and rehabilitation support; before discharge, patients anticipated difficulties coordinating multimorbidity self-management and expressed needs for structured, multidisciplinary continuity of care. Conclusions The journey map identified distinct stage-specific patterns in symptoms, emotions, care needs, and pain points among patients with CMM undergoing PCI. These findings may help align nursing support with preprocedural information and reassurance needs, postprocedural symptom and rehabilitation needs, and pre-discharge preparation for coordinated multimorbidity self-management.

title: Native-to-fibril structural remodelling reveals an amyloid-selective transthyretin epitope for AI-guided binder design
authorString: Lomoio U, Carbonari V, Roncada P, Urbani A, Lio' P, Veltri P, Guzzi PH.
abstractText: Transthyretin (TTR) amyloidosis involves conversion of the native tetramer into cross-$\beta$ fibrils, creating potential targets for conformation-selective binders. Full-assembly solvent-accessibility analysis of 30 patient-derived fibril structures, spanning wild-type TTR and ten hereditary variants, identifies increased exposure of an N-terminal region adjacent to Cys10. Using a common normalisation reference, mean relative solvent accessibility for residues 11--15 is 0.089 in native TTR and at least 0.168 in fibrils. Modification mapping, saturation-mutagenesis stability predictions and steric PTM models provide molecular context. BoltzGen and RFAntibody generate candidate binders, and sequence-only Boltz-2 counter-predictions place selected nanobodies at the Pro11/Met13/Lys15 region in fibril-derived constructs but at distal surfaces in native-state constructs. Vitreous-fibril designs also engage cardiac-fibril constructs, suggesting cross-tissue epitope recognition. These results support structure-guided candidate prioritisation, while fibril geometry, binding affinity and disease-state selectivity require experimental validation.

title: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome and reproductive factors in postmenopausal Chinese and United States women: a cross-sectional analysis of two national survey cohorts
authorString: Chen C, Wen Y, Huang W, Yang L, Huang X, Zhang Z, Lin X.
abstractText: Background Whether female reproductive history is associated with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome staging and cardiometabolic multimorbidity, and whether such associations differ between populations, is unclear. We examined age at menarche, parity, and age at first birth in relation to these outcomes in two national cohorts of postmenopausal women in China and the United States. Methods We analyzed 3,876 women in China postmenopausal at the 2011 examination and 4,357 naturally postmenopausal United States women. Using harmonized definitions, including a modified CKM staging based on the American Heart Association framework, we estimated prevalence ratios (PRs) by modified Poisson regression for CKM stage ≥ 2 (primary), CKM stage ≥ 3, and cardiometabolic multimorbidity, and tested whether PRs differed between cohorts. Results Later menarche was associated with lower CKM stage ≥ 2 prevalence in both cohorts (China PR 0.985/year [95% CI 0.974–0.996]; United States 0.982 [0.969–0.995]), but survived correction in the United States only. Later age at first birth was associated with lower CKM stage ≥ 2 prevalence in the United States (0.991 [0.985–0.996]) but not in China (0.997 [0.992–1.003]). For multimorbidity, later menarche was associated with lower prevalence in the United States (0.919 [0.873–0.967], survived correction), whereas age at first birth showed only a nominal association in China (0.967 [0.940–0.994], not surviving correction). Parity was not associated with any outcome. Conclusions Later menarche was associated with lower CKM stage ≥ 2 prevalence in both cohorts, with similar magnitude, although this survived correction in the United States only; later age at first birth was associated with lower prevalence in the United States only. For multimorbidity, only later menarche in the United States survived correction. Parity was not associated with any outcome, and no cross-cohort difference survived correction. In these cross-sectional analyses, reproductive history appears to be a life-course marker of modest effect size, warranting prospective evaluation rather than causal or clinical use.

title: Targeting Ferroptosis-Inflammation Crosstalk: A Novel Strategy for the Prevention and Treatment of Myocardial Ischaemia Reperfusion Injury
authorString: Zhang¹ M, Ji¹ X, Wan¹ L, Wang¹ B, Deng¹ L, Xing¹ Z, Fan¹ G, Wang¹˒² Y.
abstractText: Myocardial ischaemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI) is a major cause of residual myocardial damage following coronary revascularisation. Unfortunately, effective mechanism-based pharmacological interventions that can be translated into clinical practice remain limited. Emerging evidence indicates that ferroptosis and inflammation mutually reinforce each other and constitute a critical pathological process responsible for the amplification of myocardial injury during the early phase of reperfusion. Upon myocardial reperfusion, ferroptotic cardiomyocytes release damage-associated molecular patterns and disrupt tissue barriers, thereby activating the innate immune system and initiating inflammatory responses. In turn, inflammation promotes oxidative stress, dysregulation of iron metabolism and lipid peroxidation through the activation of inflammatory signaling pathways and the release of pro-inflammatory mediators, ultimately exacerbating ferroptosis. This reciprocal interaction establishes a self-perpetuating vicious cycle that contributes to the progression of MIRI. Encouragingly, several Western medicines and bioactive compounds derived from traditional Chinese medicine have shown therapeutic potential in modulating MIRI. This review systematically summarizes the molecular mechanisms underlying the bidirectional interaction between ferroptosis and inflammation in MIRI and discusses emerging pharmacological strategies targeting this pathological network. Collectively, the available evidence suggests that future therapeutic approaches to MIRI should extend beyond reperfusion therapy, antioxidant treatment, or anti-inflammatory intervention alone and instead consider combined strategies that simultaneously suppress inflammation and ferroptosis. Such an integrated approach may provide a novel translational framework for early risk assessment, therapeutic response prediction and targeted intervention in patients with MIRI.

title: Deceleration Capacity of the Heart Rate: Measurement Characteristics and Biological Determinants
authorString: de Ven Sv, Gevonden MJ, Noordzij ML, de Geus EJ.
abstractText: Purpose Deceleration capacity is becoming a more widely used predictor for health outcomes and cardiac autonomic dysfunction, but its measurement characteristics and biological determinants remain insufficiently understood. This study examined these factors in a large population-based sample (n = 1291) from the Netherlands Twin Register. Methods Participants wore an physiological monitoring device for 24 hours, and deceleration capacity was computed through phase-rectified signal averaging. To test whether short recordings might suffice, deceleration capacity estimates derived from 5-minute segments were compared with estimates obtained from full 24-hour ambulatory recordings. Temporal stability was examined in a subsample of participants measured again roughly three years later, and twin modeling was used to determine how much of the individual variance was explained by environmental and genetic factors. Results The results indicated that short-term deceleration capacity derived from 5-minute segments can deviate substantially from those derived from the full 24-hour recording, and that these deviations vary systematically across the day. It showed moderate to strong temporal stability across two measurement occasions roughly three years apart (r = .74, ICC(A,1) = .74). In addition, deceleration capacity was negatively associated with age (β = -0.04, R² = .14) and BMI (β = -0.04, R² = .03), and was higher in males than females (M = 4.70 vs M = 4.12). We further found substantial heritability of deceleration capacity (h 2 = .62). Conclusions Together, these findings establish that 24-hour DC reflects a stable biological trait, which is in line with its prognostic potential for health outcomes.

title: Bupivacaine induces cardiotoxicity in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes through mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress-associated apoptosis: attenuation by Intralipid
authorString: Jiang T, Zhao Z, huang W, Wang M, Wang N, Song W, Zhang S, Miao Y.
abstractText: Bupivacaine is a widely used local anesthetic, but its cardiotoxicity during local anesthetic systemic toxicity (LAST) remains incompletely characterized in human-relevant cardiac models. In this study, human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs), generated using the GiWi monolayer differentiation protocol, were exposed to bupivacaine for 24 or 48 hours. Cell viability, cytotoxicity, spontaneous beating activity, mitochondrial function, oxidative stress, and apoptotic signaling were evaluated. Bupivacaine reduced cell viability in a dose- and time-dependent manner, with estimated IC₅₀ values of approximately 550 µM at 24 hours and 312 µM at 48 hours, and significantly impaired spontaneous beating rate and rhythm regularity at concentrations ≥ 100 µM. Mechanistically, bupivacaine induced mitochondrial membrane depolarization and mitochondrial fragmentation, accompanied by increased expression of the fission-related proteins DRP1 and FIS1 and decreased expression of the fusion-related proteins MFN2 and OPA1. These changes were associated with increased intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS), an elevated BAX/BCL2 ratio, increased cytochrome c expression, and enhanced caspase-3 cleavage, indicating activation of the intrinsic mitochondrial apoptotic pathway. Co-treatment with Intralipid significantly restored cell viability, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential, reduced oxidative stress, and attenuated apoptotic signaling in bupivacaine-exposed hiPSC-CMs. These findings suggest that bupivacaine induces cardiotoxicity through a mitochondria–ROS–apoptosis cascade involving dysregulated mitochondrial dynamics, and provide mechanistic cellular evidence supporting Intralipid as a rescue agent for LAST-associated cardiotoxicity.

title: Formononetin as a Natural Product-Derived Candidate for Diabetic Microvascular Complications: Mechanistic Evidence, Pharmacokinetics, Formulation Strategies, and Translational Barriers.
authorString: Gao X, Zhang Y, Zheng Y, Qiao L, Liu X, Yang S, Chen X, Xiao Y, Wang X, Liu R, Dong Z, Wang Q, Chen X, Hong Q.
abstractText: Diabetic microvascular complications (DMCs) mainly affect the kidneys, retina, and peripheral nerves. Their treatment remains challenging because these complications involve overlapping metabolic, inflammatory, vascular, and neurodegenerative changes. Formononetin, an isoflavone derived from Astragalus membranaceus, has shown protective effects in several preclinical models of microvascular injury. This review summarizes the current evidence on formononetin in DMCs, with attention to proposed mechanisms, pharmacokinetic features, formulation strategies, and barriers to clinical translation. In diabetic kidney disease models, preclinical studies suggest that formononetin may reduce oxidative stress through pathways related to SIRT1/PGC-1α and Nrf2. It may also lessen mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, and fibrotic remodeling. In retinal hypoxia and oxygen-induced retinopathy models, formononetin has been reported to modulate HIF-1α/VEGF-related angiogenic responses. However, whether these findings apply directly to diabetic retinopathy, especially proliferative diabetic retinopathy, still needs to be examined in diabetes-specific models. Evidence for diabetic neuropathy, diabetic cardiomyopathy, and diabetic wound healing is more limited and is mainly based on preclinical findings or indirect mechanistic evidence. Overall, formononetin should be considered a preclinical candidate for DMC-related research rather than a clinically established intervention. Further translation will require human PK/PD studies, standardized formulations, rational dose-conversion analysis, GLP-compliant toxicology, reproductive and endocrine safety evaluation, and assessment of CYP-mediated drug interactions.

title: Mechanisms, Impact, and Clinical Management of Cancer-Related Anorexia: A Narrative Review.
authorString: Fang X, Wang X, Qian X.
abstractText: Cancer-related anorexia (CRA) is a common and distressing symptom in patients with cancer. It affects nutritional status, treatment tolerance, and quality of life. This narrative review examines the molecular mechanisms, clinical manifestations, risk factors, and current management of CRA from a clinical perspective. Existing interventions include nutritional counselling, oral nutritional supplements, and enteral or parenteral nutrition when indicated. Pharmacological options such as megestrol acetate and low-dose olanzapine have shown benefit in appetite stimulation, though their use requires careful patient selection. Several therapeutic approaches are under active investigation, including anamorelin, a ghrelin receptor agonist, and agents targeting the growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF-15) pathway. Melanocortin-4 receptor antagonists have also emerged as candidate treatments in preclinical and early-phase studies. Multimodal strategies combining nutritional support with pharmacological and exercise-based interventions are increasingly recognised as the most practical framework for clinical care. This review summarises the molecular basis, clinical features, risk factors, and contemporary treatment strategies for CRA, with particular emphasis on evolving pharmacological and multimodal strategies. The goal is to give clinicians a practical reference to improve patients' nutritional status and overall well-being during cancer treatment.

title: Mechanism Study of Ginsenoside Rd in the Prevention and Treatment of Post-Myocardial Infarction Heart Failure: Network Pharmacology Combined with in vivo and in vitro Experiments Verification.
authorString: Zhao T, Liao H, Wang R, Xiao B, Li Z, Qu F, Lu M, Yang Z, Ni S, Wang X.
abstractText:
Purpose

This study aims to investigate the immunoprotective mechanisms of GSRd, an active ingredient of Panax ginseng C.A. Mey (P. ginseng C.A. Mey), against post-MI HF, with particular focus on its regulatory effects on regulatory T cells (Tregs) and Monocytes/macrophages (Mos/Mφs).

Materials and methods

UPLC-MS/MS was used to identify GSRd. A mouse post-MI HF model was established by LAD ligation to observe GSRd-mediated changes in Tregs, IL-10 and Mos/Mφs. Network pharmacology predicted GSRd core targets against post-MI HF. Single-cell virtual knockout evaluated target function, while protein-protein docking predicted IL-10-core target binding regions. In vitro, LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages were applied for inflammatory modeling, with exogenous IL-10 as positive control and Stattic for functional reverse validation of GSRd.

Results

UPLC-MS/MS confirmed GSRd in P. ginseng C.A. Mey. GSRd ameliorated cardiac function and alleviated myocardial fibrosis in post-MI HF mice. Immunologically, GSRd facilitated the recruitment of Tregs in failing myocardium and peripheral circulation and elevated IL-10 expression. Furthermore, GSRd promoted the polarization of Mos/Mφs toward anti-inflammatory Ly6Clow phenotype (with upregulated CD206 and Arg1), suppressed pro-inflammatory Ly6Chigh polarization, and reduced the secretion of TNF-ppressed pro-inflammatory Ly6Cin post-MI HF mice. Immunologically, GSRd facilitated the recruitment of Tregs in failing myocardium and peripheral ci of STAT3 in cardiac monocytes/macrophages predicted that STAT3 acts as a critical regulator maintaining cardiac inflammatory balance and immune homeostasis. Protein-protein interaction analysis predicted the binding domains between IL-10 and STAT3; molecular docking predicted that ginsenoside Rd can stably bind to Foxp3, IL-10 and STAT3. In vitro experiments revealed that GSRd promotes STAT3 phosphorylation to induce RAW264.7 macrophage polarization toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype, and Stattic attenuates the protective effects of GSRd.

Conclusion

The present study demonstrates that GSRd confers therapeutic benefits against post-MI HF via modulating the cardiac immune microenvironment.

title: Development and Validation of a Machine Learning Model for Predicting Three-Month Unplanned Readmission in Patients with Moderate-to-Severe Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Yu S, Wei H, Chen Q, Li N, Jiang Z, Ma H.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Int J Chron Obstruct Pulmon Dis
journal.title: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Int J Chron Obstruct Pulmon Dis

abstractText:
Purpose

Patients with moderate-to-severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) face a high risk of three-month unplanned readmission after discharge, yet early identification of high-risk patients remains challenging in clinical practice. This study aimed to develop and validate machine learning (ML) models for predicting the risk and providing a reference for the subsequent development and updating of predictive tools.

Methods

This single-center retrospective cohort study involved individuals with moderate-to-severe COPD from Tianjin Chest Hospital (January 2023 to January 2026). Participants were randomly split into a 70% training set and a 30% validation set. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression identified candidate predictors for model development. Six models were constructed: logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), Backpropagation Neural Network (BPNN), and Naive Bayes (NB). Model performance was assessed through the area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC), sensitivity (SEN), and specificity (SPE). Calibration was evaluated through calibration curves, and clinical utility via decision curve analysis (DCA).

Results

299 patients with moderate-to-severe COPD were enrolled, and 59 (20%) experienced unplanned readmission within three months after discharge. Six ML models were compared, and the XGBoost model exhibited the best performance in the validation cohort, with an AUC of 0.809 (95% CI: 0.690-0.927), SEN of 0.750, and SPE of 0.826. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis ranked the key predictive factors in descending order: history of hospitalization in the past year, FEV1, history of coronary heart disease, and smoking history.

Conclusion

XGBoost model showed promising performance in internal validation for predicting the risk of unplanned readmission among patients with moderate-to-severe COPD. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample size, single-center design. Future studies should use prospective, multicenter data from diverse geographic regions to externally validate and update the model.

title: Mimicking in vivo Inflammation: A New in vitro Model of Endothelial Inflammation to Advance the Study of IMID-Associated Cardiovascular Diseases.
authorString: Parra P, Mas B, Marchand F, Chatelais M, Floris I.
abstractText:
Background

Patients with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs), such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA), inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), face a markedly increased risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD). This is mainly driven by chronic systemic inflammation, which in turn triggers endothelial activation and dysfunction.

Objective

We aimed to establish a pathophysiologically relevant in vitro endothelial activation model using sub-nanogram concentrations of cytokines to mimic the low-grade systemic inflammatory milieu observed in active IMIDs.

Methods

Human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) were exposed to a combination of three key proinflammatory cytokines at circulating pathophysiological concentrations, representative of active clinical disease -interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β) at 20 pg/mL, tumor necrosis factor (TNF-α) at 50 pg/mL, and interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) at 100 pg/mL- referred to as the MIX. Each individual cytokine was also tested, and a high-dose IL-1β control (10 ng/mL) was included as a standard supra-physiological positive control. Surface marker expression was analyzed by flow cytometry, and cytokine/chemokine release was quantified by multiplex assay.

Results

At 24 h, the MIX triggered a particular endothelial activation state. Notably, it significantly upregulated key immunological surface markers, including vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (VCAM-1), and intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1), compared to the untreated control. Furthermore, the MIX significantly increased the release of key chemokines, such as IL-8, interferon-gamma inducible protein-10 (IP-10), and monocyte chemotactic protein-1 (MCP-1), displaying a distinct cooperative profile compared to individual low-dose cytokines.

Conclusion

Our study demonstrates that the combination of IL-1β, TNF-α, and IFN-γ at pathophysiologically relevant, sub-nanogram concentrations, can successfully model key features of IMID-associated endothelial activation by driving immune marker upregulation and secretory activity, opening new avenues towards the development of physiologically relevant in vitro system for future research into IMID-associated CVD.

title: Poor R-wave progression and long-term outcomes in the multi-ethnic study of atherosclerosis (MESA).
authorString: de Alencar JN, Trindade JVG, Dos Santos Filho CA, Felicioni SP, De Marchi MFN.
abstractText:
Background

Poor R-wave progression (PRWP) has been interpreted as a marker of anterior myocardial injury since the 1970s, but its temporal stability, substrate, and independent prognostic value in a CAD-free cohort remain uncertain.

Methods

We studied 6323 MESA participants free of clinical cardiovascular disease with standardized 12‑lead ECGs at baseline (Exam 1, 2000-02) and after a median of 10 years (Exam 5, 2010-12). PRWP was defined as R-wave amplitude ≤3 mm in V3 with RV3 > RV2. We assessed 10-year test-retest stability (Cohen's κ), pulmonary/thoracic correlates, mechanistic substrate via cardiac magnetic resonance, high-sensitivity troponin T, NT-proBNP, and polysomnography, and long-term outcomes (all-cause death, cardiovascular death, MACE) over median 14 years using Cox and Fine-Gray models.

Results

PRWP prevalence was 3.2% at Exam 1 and 6.2% at Exam 5. Binary test-retest agreement was limited (κ = 0.344; 95% CI 0.283-0.406) despite good continuous R-V3 reliability (ICC = 0.73); only 52% of baseline PRWP persisted at 10 years. Self-reported emphysema (OR 4.48; 2.30-8.22) and current smoking (OR 1.77; 1.14-2.73) were the strongest PRWP predictors. PRWP was not associated with RV volumes, RV ejection fraction, NT-proBNP, or sleep apnea. After adjustment for smoking and emphysema, PRWP was not independently associated with all-cause mortality (HR 1.19; 0.90-1.58), cardiovascular death (HR 1.02; 0.67-1.57), or MACE (HR 0.89; 0.54-1.47). Time-updated and Fine-Gray models confirmed null associations.

Conclusions

In a CAD-free multi-ethnic cohort, isolated PRWP is an ECG pattern with limited binary reproducibility, linked to pulmonary exposure and thoracic habitus rather than myocardial substrate, and carries no independent cardiovascular prognostic value.

title: Clinical Characteristics and Comprehensive Management of Multimorbidity in Older Adults with Diabetes: A Narrative Review.
authorString: Wu M, Zhang C, Wang Y, Zhao Y.
abstractText: With the acceleration of population aging and the progressive decline in physiological function, older adults with diabetes frequently present with multiple chronic conditions. This not only increases the complexity of clinical management but also adversely affects disease prognosis, quality of life, and the efficient allocation of healthcare resources. Traditional single-disease-centered management models are increasingly inadequate for addressing the complex and heterogeneous healthcare needs of these patients. Consequently, there is an urgent need to shift toward personalized and integrated management strategies guided by patients' overall health status and functional needs. A literature search was conducted in PubMed and Web of Science for studies published from 2014 to 2026, using combinations of keywords related to diabetes, older adults, multimorbidity, comorbidity, polypharmacy, comprehensive geriatric assessment, and multidisciplinary management. Inclusion criteria encompassed original studies, clinical trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, clinical guidelines, and consensus statements focusing on multimorbidity and its management in older adults with diabetes. Studies unrelated to the target population or research topic were excluded. The available evidence indicates that multimorbidity in older adults with diabetes is characterized by complex interactions across multiple organ systems and presents substantial challenges in therapeutic decision-making, polypharmacy, and treatment adherence. Comprehensive geriatric assessment, individualized treatment targets, shared decision-making, medication optimization and deintensification, and multidisciplinary collaboration represent important approaches to addressing these challenges. Emerging technologies, including real-time continuous glucose monitoring, electronic health records, digital health platforms, and integrated data analytics, may further facilitate dynamic risk monitoring, coordinated decision-making, and continuity of care. Overall, management should progressively shift from a disease-centered paradigm toward personalized, integrated, and function-oriented care, with greater emphasis on preserving functional independence, minimizing treatment burden, and improving quality of life in older adults with diabetes and multimorbidity.

title: Clustering of Electrocardiographic Atrial Cardiomyopathy Markers and Risk of Cardiovascular Mortality.
authorString: Mohsen AM, Cheon P, Boursiquot BC, Bhave PD, Soliman EZ.
abstractText:
Background

ECG markers of atrial cardiomyopathy (AtCM) are individually associated with morbidity and mortality; however, whether they cluster within individuals and confer incremental risk when present in combination remains unclear.

Objective

This study aimed to examine ECG markers of AtCM co-occurrence and their cumulative association with cardiovascular (CVD) mortality.

Methods

We analyzed 7326 adults (mean age 59 ± 13.4 years) without cardiovascular disease from the Third National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey with available ECGs. AtCM markers included: (1) prolonged P-wave duration ≥120 ms in lead II; (2) abnormal P-wave axis outside 0°-75°; and (3) deep terminal negativity of the P wave in lead V1 (DTNPV1) < -100 μV. Marker burden (0-3) was evaluated in relation to CVD mortality using Cox proportional hazards models.

Results

AtCM markers were present in 44.6% of participants: 1 marker (37.9%), 2 markers (6.4%), and 3 markers (0.3%). Prolonged P-wave duration and abnormal P-wave axis most co-occurred, whereas combinations involving DTNPV1 were less frequent. Over a median follow-up of 13.8 years, 979 CVD deaths occurred. CVD mortality increased progressively across marker burden categories. In fully adjusted models, each additional marker was associated with a higher risk of CVD death (hazard ratio [HR] 1.16, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.06-1.28; p = 0.002). When modeled categorically, higher marker burden was associated with increased CVD mortality risk (overall p = 0.010). The association did not differ by sex or race and ethnicity.

Conclusion

ECG markers of AtCM cluster within individuals, and increasing marker burden is associated with progressively higher CVD mortality risk.

title: Septal Reduction Therapy: Thinking Beyond the Conventional.
authorString: da Motta PAM, Motta BD, de Oliveira CGC, Caied F, Osterne EMC, Osterne TEC, Osterne ECV, de Oliveira DC.
abstractText: For patients with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy who are refractory to medical treatment, the surgical myectomy is the treatment of choice, but for some patients, alcohol septal ablation (ASA) is an alternative. In the following case report, we described a patient that underwent ASA, but during the follow-up, the gradient came back. This patient did not have septal branches from left anterior descending artery; therefore, she underwent ablation of a marginal branch of the left circumflex artery using an ethylene-vinyl alcohol copolymer guided by evaluation of the invasive gradient (echocardiogram was not performed during the procedure). One year later, the patient presented with refractory symptoms, and color Doppler echocardiography revealed a mean resting left ventricle outflow tract (LVOT) gradient of 72 mm Hg, a basal septum thickness of 21 mm, and a mid- and apical-septal thickness of 10 mm. Coronary angiography showed a pattern similar to that observed at the end of the marginal branch occlusion procedure. A transcatheter treatment attempt was proposed to identify the vessel supplying the basal septum for potential ablation; however, the patient opted for surgical myomectomy, which was performed successfully and without complications. She was discharged on the fifth day of hospitalization. Based on this case, we conclude that septal ablation should not be performed without an echocardiographic assessment during the procedure, other branches than the septal branches may supply the interventricular septum (if ablation of these branches is performed, it must be as selective as possible), and the reduction of the invasive LVOT gradient should not be used as the sole criterion for deciding which branch to occlude.

title: Multimodal photoacoustic arthroscopy for quantitative morphomechanical assessment of articular cartilage.
authorString: Li R, Xin H, Zeng F, Chen W, Zheng X, Chen H, Ma Z, Wang E, Gao H, Shen T, Guo T, He C, Xu J, Zhang Z, Hu J.
abstractText:
Background

Osteoarthritis (OA) involves progressive cartilage degeneration, while conventional white-light arthroscopy mainly provides surface morphological information and lacks quantitative functional contrast. Multimodal photoacoustic arthroscopy (MMPA) may strengthen intraoperative cartilage assessment by enabling earlier identification of matrix, collagen, and biomechanical alterations that are not readily visible under white light.

Methods

We developed a preclinical multimodal photoacoustic arthroscopy (MMPA) prototype integrating photoacoustic imaging, polarization-resolved photoacoustic imaging, and photoacoustic elasticity imaging to enable label-free, in situ microscopic-resolution assessment of cartilage composition, collagen-related structural anisotropy, and biomechanical response. Validation was performed on 300 human cartilage regions spanning multiple degenerative grades. A feature-based machine-learning classifier was developed mainly using cartilage regions with Mankin scores from 2 to 9, and an independent external validation cohort including 120 cartilage regions was used to assess model generalizability. Longitudinal in vivo monitoring was conducted in a large-animal model. MRI and white-light arthroscopy were used as comparative imaging modalities, whereas histopathological grading served as the reference standard.

Results

MMPA provided additional visualization of microscopic morphomechanical changes that were less apparent on conventional white-light arthroscopy. The multimodal machine-learning model achieved AUCs of 0.93 (95% CI: 0.91-0.95) internally and 0.89 (95% CI: 0.87-0.90) externally. MMPA detected 81% of lesions, compared with 78% for MRI and 72% for white-light arthroscopy, with a significant overall difference (Cochran's Q=21.00 , p=2.75×10-5 ) and significant pairwise differences (MMPA vs MRI, p=0.0313 ; MMPA vs white-light arthroscopy, p=0.000831 ). MMPA-derived scores most closely tracked histopathological severity.

Conclusion

This study establishes a preclinical multimodal photoacoustic arthroscopy framework for quantitative intraoperative morphomechanical assessment of articular cartilage degeneration. MMPA has potential to serve as a quantitative upgrade to conventional white-light arthroscopy, assisting surgeons in earlier recognition of degenerative cartilage changes from Mankin score 2 onward, lesion evaluation, and intraoperative decision-making. The translational potential of this article : This study presents a preclinical multimodal photoacoustic arthroscopy platform that provides quantitative intraoperative assessment of cartilage composition, structural anisotropy, and biomechanical properties. Rather than replacing MRI, MMPA is intended to complement preoperative MRI by offering real-time functional assessment during arthroscopy.

title: Reduced bi-atrial reservoir strain in patients with cardiac amyloidosis: a cardiac magnetic resonance feature-tracking study.
authorString: Kato R, Iwakawa H, Yoshida H, Sasaki Y, Miura C, Suzuki N, Kaimori R, Watanabe H.

journal.title: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature

abstractText:
Background

Although heart strain analysis is useful for diagnosing cardiac amyloidosis (CA), it remains unclear which chamber best distinguishes CA from hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). This study analyzed strain in all four cardiac chambers in patients with CA and HCM using cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) feature-tracking.

Methods

We enrolled 30 patients with left ventricular hypertrophy (15 with CA and 15 with HCM) and 17 healthy volunteers as a reference. Participants underwent 1.5-Tesla CMR to assess volume, function, and strain parameters in both ventricles and atria. The primary analysis comprised four comparisons between CA and HCM, one representative parameter per chamber (bi-ventricular longitudinal strain and bi-atrial reservoir strain), with Bonferroni correction (P < 0.0125). Additionally, exploratory analyses of the other parameters were conducted comparing patients with CA to HCM.

Results

Left atrial (LA) and right atrial (RA) reservoir strain were lower in CA than in HCM (LA: 7.1 ± 4.1% vs. 10.3 ± 3.9%, P = 0.035; RA: 10.8 ± 6.9% vs. 22.1 ± 12.9%, P = 0.005), whereas ventricular longitudinal strain did not differ. After Bonferroni correction, only RA reservoir strain remained significant. In an exploratory receiver operating characteristic analysis, the areas under the curve for LA and RA reservoir strain were 0.73 and 0.78, respectively, and did not differ significantly.

Conclusion

Bi-atrial reservoir strain was lower in CA than in HCM, and the difference in RA reservoir strain remained significant after accounting for multiplicity. Atrial reservoir strain may provide adjunctive, contrast-free functional information to help differentiate CA from HCM.

title: Circulating Interleukin-36 Alpha, Beta, Gamma, and Interleukin-37 Levels in Patients With Chronic Coronary Syndrome.
authorString: de Oliveira DC, Barboza S, Oliveira C, Osterne E, Osterne T, Osterne E, Motta P.
abstractText:
Background

The aim of this study was to assess whether circulating interleukin (IL)-36α, IL-36β, IL-36γ, and IL-37 levels were higher in patients with chronic coronary syndrome compared with healthy controls.

Methods

This was a cross-sectional, descriptive, and analytical study, with recruitment conducted from August 2022 to February 2023. After undergoing coronary angiography, patients were assessed in the hemodynamics laboratory according to the inclusion and exclusion criteria. For those who met these criteria, the study was explained, and they were invited to participate. Clinical characteristics were collected via interview, followed by a blood sample for the measurement of ILs. Serum IL levels were quantified using a sandwich ELISA assay (R&D Systems, USA), according to the manufacturer's recommendations. The present study was submitted to and approved by the institutional research ethics committee.

Results

A total of 100 patients were recruited (mean age: 58 ± 6.2 years; 59% male, 41% female) along with 100 healthy controls (mean age: 56 ± 4.6 years, 59% male, 41% female). Comparative analyses of circulating IL-36 family levels between patients and healthy controls revealed the following: IL-36α, 6.25 pg/mL (2.25-81.68) vs. 6.25 pg/mL (6.25-127.6) (P = 0.6); IL-36β, 9.68 pg/mL (6.25-36.39) vs. 6.25 pg/mL (6.25-6.25) (P = 0.006); and IL-36γ, 3,212 pg/mL (2,091-5,761) vs. 89.1 pg/mL (30.98-145.29) (P < 0.001), respectively.

Conclusions

Circulating IL-36α and IL-36β levels were higher in patients with chronic coronary syndrome compared with healthy controls. These ILs may be involved in the development of coronary atherosclerosis. However, further studies are needed to clarify the role of these ILs.

title: Arginine and homoarginine as predictors of cardiovascular mortality in chronic coronary syndrome.
authorString: Storesund SK, Karaji I, McCann A, Svingen GFT, Ueland PM, Lønnebakken MT, Nygård O, Pedersen ER.
abstractText:
Background and aims

Arginine (Arg) and homoarginine (hArg) are related to the nitric oxide pathway, which is important for vascular function. We investigated if serum concentrations of Arg and hArg predicted long-term cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality in patients with chronic coronary syndrome (CCS), and whether associations differed between non-obstructive coronary artery disease (NOCAD) and obstructive coronary artery disease (OCAD).

Methods and results

We included 4164 patients undergoing invasive coronary angiography for suspected CCS. Associations with CVD mortality were assessed using multivariable Cox regression, reporting hazard ratios (HRs) per standard deviation increase in log-transformed concentrations. During a median follow-up of 14.1 years, 586 (14.1%) patients died from CVD. Serum hArg was inversely associated with CVD mortality [HR (95% CI): 0.81 (0.74-0.88)] as was serum Arg [HR (95% CI): 0.90 (0.83-0.98)]. However, in Fine-Gray competing risk analyses, the association of serum Arg with CVD mortality was no longer statistically significant, whereas the inverse association for serum hArg persisted. Addition of serum hArg to the clinical model increased the C-statistic from 0.771 to 0.776, indicating a modest improvement in discrimination. In exploratory subgroup analyses, the association between serum hArg and CVD mortality was stronger in NOCAD than OCAD [0.54 (0.40-0.73) vs. 0.84 (0.77-0.92); P for interaction = 0.037].

Conclusion

Serum Arg and hArg were inversely associated with long-term CVD mortality in patients with CCS. However, the association of serum hArg was more robust than that of serum Arg. The stronger association observed in NOCAD requires independent validation.

title: Qishen Yangxin Granule ameliorates cardiac function and ventricular remodeling in dilated cardiomyopathy by attenuating inflammation and myocardial fibrosis.
authorString: Tao S, Yu L, Li J, Zhang Z, Liu Y, Wu J, Xia X, Xie Z, Tan Y.

journal.title: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology

abstractText:
Background

Qishen Yangxin Granule (QSYX), a clinically utilized traditional Chinese medicinal formula, has demonstrated therapeutic efficacy for cardiovascular diseases. However, its cardioprotective mechanism in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) remains incompletely defined.

Purpose

To evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of QSYX against DCM and the associated anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic mechanisms.

Methods

Cardioprotective effects of QSYX were assessed both in vivo using a doxorubicin-induced DCM rat model and in vitro using rat cardiac fibroblasts stimulated with lipopolysaccharide. Evaluations included cardiac function, histopathological analysis, levels of inflammatory factors, and myocardial fibrosis markers. Single-cell RNA sequencing was employed to explore the potential mechanism of QSYX-mediated improvement in cardiac structure and function. Modulation of the toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (p38 MAPK)/nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) pathway was examined via western blot, immunohistochemistry, confocal laser scanning microscope, and real-time reverse transcription-PCR. The specific p38 MAPK agonist LY188011 was used to verify the dependence of QSYX effect on the TLR4/p38 MAPK/NF-κB signaling pathway.

Results

QSYX administration improved cardiac function in DCM rats, accompanied by significant attenuation of cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, apoptosis, inflammatory cell infiltration, and collagen deposition. Comparable protective effects were observed in lipopolysaccharide-treated cardiac fibroblasts. Mechanistically, QSYX suppressed lipopolysaccharide-induced upregulation of TLR4, p38 MAPK, and NF-κB p65 and downregulated the expression of inflammatory factors and myocardial fibrosis markers. Furthermore, intervention with LY188011 confirmed that the cardioprotective effects of QSYX are mediated through suppression of the TLR4/p38 MAPK/NF-κB signaling pathway.

Conclusion

QSYX attenuates myocardial inflammation and fibrosis primarily through inhibition of the TLR4/p38 MAPK/NF-κB signaling pathway, thereby exerting cardioprotective effects against DCM-induced cardiac injury.

title: Inhibition of asparagine endopeptidase extends the lifespan and improves health span during aging.
authorString: Yang M, Meng X, Xie Z, Wang M, Qian Z, Ye K.
abstractText: Asparagine endopeptidase (AEP), also known as legumain, is a lysosomal cysteine protease whose activity increases with age and contributes to age-related tissue dysfunction. We tested whether chronic AEP inhibition could slow aging phenotypes in naturally aged mice. Here, we show that chronic treatment with the AEP inhibitor #11a extended lifespan and improved health span in aged C57BL/6 mice, together with reduced frailty and improved physical and cognitive performance. #11a treatment also attenuated several senescence- and inflammation-associated readouts in multiple organs. Mechanistically, #11a treatment suppressed AEP-dependent cleavage of nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT), accompanied by an increased NAD<sup>+</sup>/NADH ratio and higher SIRT1 levels. These findings support further investigation of pharmacological AEP inhibition as a strategy to promote healthy aging.

title: Deep protease profiling deconvolutes protease signatures released from activated neutrophils.
authorString: Yu E, Holding ML, Huang R, Chan A, Teney C, Desch KC, Kretz CA.
abstractText: Dysregulated protease activity drives the progression of cancer, cardiovascular, and inflammatory diseases. Current substrate-based detection methods lack specificity, breadth, and require prior knowledge of protease content. We have advanced deep protease profiling, through differential enrichment, substrate motif, and deconvolution analyses, to provide comprehensive, unbiased, and scalable characterizations of protease activity. Phage libraries were screened against neutrophil serine proteases or activated neutrophils, and high-throughput sequencing determined cleaved peptides. Cathepsin G, neutrophil elastase, and proteinase 3 (PR3) cleaved 5,985, 5,325, and 1,285 peptides, with substrate recognition motifs that align with natural substrates. Activated neutrophil supernatants cleaved 5,166 peptides, and inhibition of serine proteases caused 95% reduction in signal. Deconvolution algorithms identified protease signatures for elastase, cathepsin G, and PR3 proportional to their levels in neutrophils. This approach enables systematic functional analysis of proteolysis, adaptable across proteases, samples, and scenarios to advance disease understanding, diagnosis, and management.

title: Personalized Prevention of Cardiovascular Diseases Through Measurement of Plaque Burden in the Carotid Artery.
authorString: Adams A, Romanens M.
abstractText:
Background

This study provides an overview of the results of carotid screening for the prevention of cardiovascular disease.

Methods

Between 2009 and 2026, 11,540 individuals, 45% of whom were women, aged 20-65 years without clinical signs of cardiovascular disease, underwent carotid ultrasound examinations. Over 8,800 follow-up examinations were also performed. The total plaque area (TPA) and maximum plaque thickness were measured.

Results

TPA was presented as percentile curves according to age and sex. In a second cohort, age-related TPA thresholds for coronary stenosis ≥ 50% were determined. Advanced atherosclerosis (type III/IVb) is associated with a high risk of cardiovascular disease. Early treatment with statins improves the prognosis of these patients. The individual course of the disease with rapid progression of plaque burden could not be predicted based on classic risk factors. Of 75 patients with advanced atherosclerosis who suffered a myocardial infarction or ischemic stroke, 35% had a low PROCAM risk (< 10%) and only 27% had a high PROCAM risk. Mortality (from any cause) was significantly lower in men treated with statins.

Conclusions

Measuring plaque burden in the carotid artery allows for a good estimation of an individual's risk of a cardiovascular event. In this non-randomized observational study, statin treatment significantly improved the prognosis in subjects with advanced carotid artery atherosclerosis (type III-IVb findings on ultrasound).

title: A Study on the Mechanism of Medicinal cyathula Roots in the Treatment of Diabetic Nephropathy Based on Network Pharmacology.
authorString: Nazir MM, Farzeen I, Muzammil S, Nazir S, Nazir MM, Ashraf A.
abstractText:
Introduction

Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is one of the leading causes of chronic kidney disease and end-stage renal failure worldwide, highlighting the urgent need for effective multitarget therapeutic strategies.
