title: Clinical Application of Hemadsorption in Maintenance Hemodialysis Patients: An Adapted English Republication of the Chinese HA-MHD Consensus.
authorString: Sheng X, Lu W, Guo Z, Mou S, Ni Z, Ding X, Deng Y, Li G, Liu J, Luo P, Sun S, Wang H, Wei J, Xu X, Yang X, Yang Z, Zhang W, Zhao J, Zhou X, Zhou X, Zhou Z, Jiang G, Wang N, Nephrology Branch of the Shanghai Medical Association and the 2025 HA–MHD Consensus Working Group.
abstractText: The accumulation of protein-bound uremic toxins and middle- to large-molecular-weight toxins in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) results in long-term complications. Hemadsorption (HA) can efficiently remove these uremic toxins and reduce the risk of long-term complications in MHD patients. The Chinese HA-MHD Consensus Working Group has revised and updated the 2021 Shanghai Expert Consensus on the Clinical Application of Haemoadsorption in Maintenance Haemodialysis Patients to further standardize clinical application of HA and reflect the latest evidence. Based on an extensive literature search, the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation framework, and the modified Delphi method, the working group formulated 27 evidence-based recommendations regarding patient populations, session frequency, treatment modalities, precautions, and adverse reactions. This consensus systematically delineates the clinical thresholds and rationales for utilizing HA across three core dimensions: routine treatment regimens, intensive treatment regimens, and long-term complication risk management to provide comprehensive guidance. Furthermore, the consensus provides detailed guidance on individualized operational parameters to maximize both safety and treatment efficacy. This consensus aims to provide the latest guiding opinions for the rational and standardized application of HA therapy in patients receiving MHD.

title: Endovascular Stroke Thrombectomy for Patients With Concomitant Head Trauma: A Propensity Score-Matched and Machine Learning Study.
authorString: Chen H, Colasurdo M, McIntyre MK, Awad A, Lakhani DA, Malhotra A, Gandhi D.
abstractText:
Background

The safety and efficacy of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for patients with large vessel occlusion stroke presenting with concomitant head trauma is unclear.

Methods

Using the Nationwide Readmissions Database in the United States (2016-2022), we identified adults with nonelective admissions for large vessel occlusion stroke and concurrent head trauma. Patients who underwent EVT were compared with patients who did not undergo EVT using 1:1 propensity score matching. A causal forest machine learning model was deployed to estimate individual-level conditional average treatment effects for excellent neurological outcomes, with Shapley Additive Explanation values quantifying variable importance.

Results

Of 15 527 patients with large vessel occlusion stroke large vessel occlusion stroke with concomitant head trauma (median age, 78 years; 52.6% female; 51.6% with superficial injury), 2750 (17.7%) received EVT; propensity score matching yielded 2616 balanced pairs. After matching, EVT was associated with significantly higher rates of excellent outcomes (19.0% versus 13.7%; P=0.002) with no difference in mortality (14.6% versus 14.7%; P=0.93). In causal forest analysis, younger age, higher National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, lack of intravenous thrombolysis, and lack of altered mental status emerged as the strongest drivers of larger treatment benefit, and patients were dichotomized into EVT-favorable (n=8097) and EVT-unfavorable (n=7430) subgroups. In the favorable subgroup, EVT was associated with higher routine discharge (25.7% versus 21.5%; P=0.01); in the unfavorable subgroup, EVT conferred no benefit in routine discharge (10.0% versus 11.7%; P=0.26) but was associated with higher mortality (19.0% versus 14.0%; P=0.004).

Conclusions

EVT is overall associated with higher rates of favorable discharge outcomes; however, treatment effect heterogeneity is substantial.

title: Left Main Coronary Artery Atresia: Chest Pain From an Uncommon Cause.
authorString: Balmaceda P, Anderson T, Wang L, Wilson BD, Lu D.
abstractText:
Background

Angina is commonly associated with atherosclerotic epicardial coronary artery disease, but it could be the presenting symptom of a coronary structural anomaly or even a noncoronary cardiac structural pathology.

Case summary

A 40-year-old man with obesity, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia presented with exertional chest pain and dyspnea. Coronary computed tomographic angiography showed no coronary atherosclerosis. However, there was an absence of a direct left main coronary artery connection to the aortic root, and retrograde filling of the left coronary system from right coronary collateral vessels. Stress echocardiography demonstrated no wall motion abnormality or ventricular arrhythmia. Medical management, including beta-blockade, aggressive risk factor modification, and surveillance, was pursued through shared decision-making.

Discussion

Left main coronary artery atresia is an exceedingly rare congenital anomaly that may present as exertional angina mimicking atherosclerotic coronary artery disease. Coronary computed tomographic angiography provides precise anatomical information for the diagnosis, and functional testing helps guide individualized management.

title: Association of older age with outcomes of retrograde chronic total occlusion percutaneous coronary interventions.
authorString: Sural S, Aslan V, Yıldırım A, Uluganyan M, Avci G, Duzel B, Brilakis ES, Gorgulu S.

journal.title: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology

abstractText:
Introduction

The association of older age with collateral characteristics, retrograde crossing success, and procedural outcomes in chronic total occlusions-percutaneous coronary intervention (CTO-PCI) remains poorly understood.

Aim

To investigate the association between older age and collateral characteristics, retrograde crossing success, and procedural outcomes.

Material and methods

Among 2,077 CTO-PCI procedures performed between January 2019 and April 2026 at four experienced CTO centers, 564 procedures with complete datasets and at least one attempted retrograde approach were included. Procedures were stratified according to age (< 65 vs. ≥ 65 years). Collateral assessment, collateral crossing, retrograde lesion crossing, and procedural outcomes were analyzed. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify predictors of successful retrograde crossing.

Results

A total of 201 of 564 procedures (35.6%) were performed in patients aged ≥ 65 years. Elderly patients were more likely to have moderate/severe calcification (58.7% vs. 43.3%, p < 0.001), and had higher J-CTO scores (3.3 ±1.0 vs. 3.0 ±1.0, p = 0.004) and more difficult J-channel collateral anatomy (38.8% vs. 30.3%, p = 0.020). In the unadjusted analysis, successful retrograde CTO crossing was significantly lower in elderly patients (61.7% vs. 73.0%, p = 0.007). Technical success (74.6% vs. 83.7%, p = 0.009) and procedural success (73.1% vs. 82.1%, p = 0.013) were also lower in elderly patients. After IPTW adjustment, age ≥ 65 years remained independently associated with lower odds of successful retrograde crossing (OR = 0.64, 95% CI: 0.41-0.99; p = 0.039). Continuous age analysis demonstrated a progressive decrease in retrograde crossing success with increasing age (OR/year = 0.969, p = 0.001). Vascular access-site complications were more frequent in elderly patients (4.5% vs. 1.7%, p = 0.046).

Conclusions

Older age remained independently associated with lower retrograde CTO crossing success after IPTW adjustment.

title: Changes in the institutional treatment of severe aortic stenosis following the introduction of transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
authorString: Rojko M, Kocjancic E, Kodra M, Pleskovic A, Reschner H, Span M, Danojevic N, Ðordevic M, Radovanovic N, Zorc M, Susak S, Noc M.

journal.title: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology

abstractText:
Introduction

Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has transformed the treatment of severe aortic stenosis.

Aim

To investigate the association of TAVI introduction on institutional volume and characteristics of patients treated for aortic stenosis either by surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) or TAVI.

Material and methods

A single-centre retrospective observational study of consecutive patients treated only with SAVR (SAVR-only period, 2004-2017) and with either SAVR or TAVI (SAVR + TAVI period, 2017-2025).

Results

During the SAVR-only period, 1011 patients underwent SAVR, and during the SAVR + TAVI period, 685 patients underwent SAVR and 824 underwent TAVI. The total number of aortic valve interventions increased annually by 9% (95% CI: 1.08-1.10; p < 0.001), while SAVR decreased by 15% during the SAVR + TAVI period (95% CI: 0.82-0.89; p < 0.001). Cumulative 30-day mortality was 2.8% during the SAVR-only period and 1.5% during the SAVR + TAVI period (p = 0.021). Patients undergoing SAVR during the SAVR + TAVI period were younger (68 vs. 70 years; p < 0.001), had a lower Logistic EuroSCORE (4.52 vs. 6.33; p < 0.001) and less often underwent concomitant revascularization (29% vs. 35%; p = 0.013). Patients undergoing TAVI compared to SAVR were older (80 vs. 68 years; p < 0.001), had a higher Logistic EuroSCORE (11.39 vs. 4.52; p < 0.001), and had comparable 30-day mortality (1.0% vs. 2.0%; p = 0.083). The difference in 5-year mortality in favour of SAVR (13.8% vs. 27.4%) was not significant after adjustment for age, sex and Logistic EuroSCORE (HR = 0.794; 95% CI: 0.550-1.147; p = 0.22).

Conclusions

Introduction of TAVI was associated with increased institutional volume of aortic valve interventions despite a concomitant decrease in the number of SAVR procedures. TAVI appears to have expanded treatment to previously undertreated high-risk elderly patients while also being used in a sizable proportion of patients who previously underwent SAVR.

title: Prognostic value of preprocedural neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio for in-hospital and overall mortality in patients with reduced ejection fraction undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
authorString: Biyikli K, Keten MF, Danısman N, Ceneli D, Erdem C.

journal.title: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology

abstractText:
Introduction

Patients with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) represent a particularly vulnerable subgroup with elevated perioperative and long-term mortality. The neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio (NPAR), an integrated marker of systemic inflammation and nutritional status, has not been specifically evaluated as a prognostic marker in this population.

Aim

To examine the prognostic value of preprocedural NPAR for in-hospital and overall (all-cause) mortality in patients with reduced LVEF undergoing TAVI.

Material and methods

This retrospective single-centre study enrolled 169 consecutive patients with severe aortic stenosis and LVEF < 50% undergoing TAVI between June 2020 and January 2026. Preprocedural NPAR was derived from blood samples obtained within 24 h before the procedure. In-hospital and overall mortality were assessed using logistic and Cox regression models with limited covariate adjustment.

Results

Using an NPAR cut-off of 20.74, patients with elevated NPAR exhibited higher rates of chronic kidney disease, acute kidney injury, and both in-hospital and overall mortality, along with higher C-reactive protein and BNP levels and lower haemoglobin, albumin, postprocedural LVEF, and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE) values. NPAR remained associated with in-hospital mortality after adjustment for chronic kidney disease or TAPSE and was also associated with overall mortality in multivariable Cox regression analyses. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly reduced survival among patients with elevated NPAR.

Conclusions

After limited multivariable adjustment, preprocedural NPAR was associated with both in-hospital and overall mortality in patients with reduced LVEF undergoing TAVI. As a simple marker of inflammatory and nutritional burden, NPAR may provide additional prognostic information and complement preprocedural risk assessment, although its incremental value beyond established risk models and other biomarkers remains uncertain.

title: Apelin signaling controls neuroendocrine homeostasis via Atoh8-dependent transcriptional regulation
authorString: Menard R, Neog A, Halluin C, Bonnet F, Madelaine R.
abstractText:
ABSTRACT

Apelin is a pleiotropic peptide hormone with established roles in cardiovascular function, angiogenesis, and metabolism, but its contribution to neuroendocrine development and function remains poorly understood. Here, using genetic loss-of-function and inducible gain-of-function approaches in zebrafish, we show that Apelin signaling is dosage-sensitive and required for normal development, reproductive capacity, and physiological homeostasis. Both apelin deficiency and apelin overexpression disrupted embryonic development and reduced adult lifespan, while exhibiting markedly reduced fertility in both sexes. Transcriptomic profiling revealed broad changes in neuroendocrine, hormonal, stress-response, and inflammatory genes with young adult mutant expression profiles resembling those of aged wild-type fish. Both loss and excess of Apelin also disrupted hypothalamic–pituitary–thyroid (HPT) axis development, reducing hypothalamic thyrotropin-releasing hormone-expressing cells, pituitary gonadotropic cell populations, and thyroid gland volume. Transcriptomic analyses identified atoh8 , encoding a basic helix–loop–helix transcription factor, as a candidate effector of Apelin signaling. Apelin expression increased atoh8 expression during early embryogenesis, whereas atoh8 mRNA partially rescued developmental defects in apelin mutants, including hypothalamic and pituitary markers, and thyroid volume. Conversely, atoh8 crispants displayed thyroid and pituitary abnormalities, supporting a role for Atoh8 in neuroendocrine development. Together, these findings establish Apelin signaling as a dosage-sensitive regulator of zebrafish development and tissue homeostasis and identify Atoh8 as a functional downstream effector that partially mediates Apelin-dependent HPT axis formation. This work links peptide hormone signaling to neuroendocrine development and provides a framework for investigating its broader contributions to vertebrate physiology, reproduction and aging.

title: Embodied Dynamic Causal Modelling: Brain and Cardiac Effective Connectivity
authorString: Levy A, Zeidman P, Allen M, Friston K.
abstractText: Brain-body interactions underpin embodied inference and interoception, and are central to both general health and the pathophysiology of mental health disorders. These interactions are orchestrated across a hierarchy extending from the cortex, through the brainstem, to peripheral autonomic effectors. Existing methods either reduce this communication to scalar summaries or lack an invertible biophysical model, and so cannot resolve where in this extended architecture an observed effect originates. To address this, we introduce Embodied Dynamic Causal Modelling, an extension of the generative causal modelling framework that formalises hierarchical message passing across the full brain-body axis. We instantiate the framework for brain-heart interactions with the Brainstem Cardiac Network, a closed-loop neural mass model of brainstem autonomic circuitry and sinoatrial node dynamics. By incorporating five brainstem nuclei, a viscerosensory thalamic relay and the cardiac pacemaker, the network enables estimation of directed effective connectivity across the cortical-brainstem-cardiac axis. As an illustrative case study, representative of the experiments and extended physiological systems that Embodied DCM and the BCN can now interrogate, we applied the framework to simultaneously recorded electroencephalography and electrocardiography during an auditory Go/No-Go paradigm. A multimodal observation model permits joint inversion of electrophysiological and cardiac responses, so that neural and bodily measurements together constrain an account of central and peripheral dynamics. The case study shows how the framework can arbitrate between competing hypotheses about functional cytoarchitecture, distinguishing granular from agranular microcircuits within the viscero-sensorimotor hierarchy. It also shows how time-varying estimates of synaptic efficacy can be recovered alongside continuous latent neuronal dynamics, over extended windows spanning anticipation, target processing and motor inhibition. By linking neural and cardiac signals to a single generative architecture, this work moves the study of brain-heart interactions beyond correlation, providing a framework for testing theories of embodied inference and for identifying circuit-level disruptions in disorders of interoceptive and autonomic regulation.

title: A Systems Theory of Cardiac-Autonomic Trajectories and Equilibria
authorString: Castillo-Aguilar M, Mabe-Castro D, Núñez-Espinosa C.
abstractText: Heart rate variability (HRV) is conventionally summarized with static indices computed over fixed windows, which cannot show how cardiac autonomic regulation persists, transitions, responds to perturbation, and recovers. We develop the Systems Theory of Cardiac-Autonomic Trajectories and Equilibria (STATE), in which autonomic regulation is a low-dimensional latent stochastic dynamical system observed only through RR intervals, and we derive what the theory can and cannot claim. First, we prove that for isotropic linear dynamics the sympathetic and parasympathetic coordinates are not separately identifiable from a scalar RR signal, whereas distinct time scales or coupling restore observability. Second, we derive exact properties of a minimal bistable system (stationary law, mean escape time, critical forcing), and a Monte Carlo simulation agreed with the exact escape time within 6%. Third, in 2000 simulated replicates of a monostable and a bistable system that share the same linearization at rest, baseline variability (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUC, 0.56) and peak displacement at the pulse used (AUC 0.42) did not discriminate the systems, yet sustained return after an identical pulse differed: 100% versus 7%. We define resilience as a multidimensional response profile, show that recovery descriptors depend on analyst-chosen tolerances that must be fixed a priori, and state four falsifiable hypotheses with the result that would refute each. The work is theoretical and computational; no empirical recordings were used.

title: American Indian and Alaska Native Patients Undergoing Hip Fracture Surgery: A National Retrospective Cohort Study Between 2016 and 2022.
authorString: Grellinger ED, So A, Keeley T, Ward D, Wong SE.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: J Am Acad Orthop Surg Glob Res Rev
journal.title: Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons. Global research & reviews
journal.isoabbreviation: J Am Acad Orthop Surg Glob Res Rev

abstractText:
Introduction

Racial and ethnic disparities have been reported in the treatment of hip fractures; however, American Indian and Alaska Native (AI/AN) patients are often excluded. No existing racial disparity studies have evaluated the management and outcomes of hip fractures among AI/AN patients. We aim to assess whether there are disparities in risk factors, management, and complications in the surgical treatment of hip fractures among AI/AN patients.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study used the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (NSQIP) database to analyze AI/AN and White patients undergoing surgical treatment of hip fractures between 2016 and 2022. Descriptive statistics, t-tests, chi-squared tests, and multiple regression models were used to assess differences in patient demographics, preoperative comorbidities, time to surgery (TTS), and postoperative complications.

Results

AI/AN patients were significantly younger than White patients yet had higher rates of preoperative comorbidities (diabetes [P < 0.001], smoking [P < 0.001], dialysis [P < 0.001], anemia [P = 0.007], and delirium [P < 0.001]). When controlling for patient characteristics, TTS and mortality were similar between AI/AN and White patients (P = 0.31, P = 0.38, respectively). However, AI/AN patients had significantly more postoperative complications including stroke (P = 0.04) and pneumonia (P < 0.01), had a shorter length of stay (LOS) (P < 0.001), and were less likely to be discharged to a facility (P < 0.001).

Discussion

AI/AN patients with hip fractures had a higher burden of preoperative comorbidities and postoperative complications when compared with White patients. Reassuringly, AI/AN and White patients had similar TTS and 30-day mortality. When controlling for patient characteristics, AI/AN patients had a shorter LOS and were more likely to be discharged home. This may be inferred as a lack of access to rehabilitation facilities on discharge or more support from patient families and communities at home. Overall, AI/AN patients should be included in current and future research to better assess disparities in orthopaedic care.

title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Analyses Identify Shared Inflammation-Related Candidate Genes in Psoriasis and Acute Myocardial Infarction.
authorString: Fang RN, Shen Y, Li JH, Zhu BC, Jia N, Chen Y, Feng HS, Zhang WT.
abstractText:
Background

Psoriasis and acute myocardial infarction (AMI) are both closely associated with immune-inflammatory dysregulation; however, the shared molecular features of psoriasis-AMI comorbidity remain incompletely characterized. To address this gap, this study aimed to identify novel shared inflammation-related candidate genes between psoriasis and AMI and to characterize their cellular expression patterns using public transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing data. The main finding was the identification of shared inflammation-related candidate genes and their cell-type-specific expression patterns in psoriasis-AMI comorbidity.

Methods

Transcriptomic datasets related to psoriasis and AMI were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. GSE30999 and GSE66360 were used as discovery cohorts. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified using limma with adjusted P value < 0.05 and |log2FC| ≥ 1.0. Shared DEGs between the two diseases were extracted. GO and KEGG enrichment analyses were performed, and a PPI network was constructed using STRING and Cytoscape. Consensus hub genes were selected using six cytoHubba algorithms. Candidate gene expression differences were evaluated in the external validation datasets GSE201827 and GSE59867, and ROC curve analysis assessed their discriminatory performance. Finally, scRNA-seq datasets GSE220116 and GSE269269 were analyzed to characterize the cell-type distribution of the final candidate genes.

Results

A total of 57 shared DEGs were identified in the psoriasis and AMI discovery cohorts, including 51 commonly upregulated and 6 commonly downregulated genes. Enrichment analysis showed that these genes were mainly involved in processes related to cellular response to lipopolysaccharide, chemotaxis, cytokine activity and chemokine activity, and were significantly enriched in the IL-17, NF-κB, TNF and chemokine signaling pathways, as well as lipid and atherosclerosis-related pathways. PPI network and cytoHubba analyses identified 9 consensus hub genes. External validation and ROC analyses showed that S100A9, S100A12 and CXCL1 were significantly upregulated in both psoriasis and AMI validation datasets and showed moderate discriminatory performance between groups. Single-cell analysis showed that S100A9 and S100A12 exhibited prominent myeloid inflammation-related expression profiles in psoriatic lesions and AMI peripheral immune cells, whereas CXCL1 expression was relatively restricted, suggesting that it may primarily reflect chemokine-mediated inflammatory cell recruitment.

Conclusion

This study identified S100A9, S100A12 and CXCL1 as candidate genes potentially associated with shared inflammatory features of psoriasis-AMI comorbidity. These findings suggest that myeloid cell activation and chemokine-mediated recruitment of inflammatory cells may contribute to the molecular link between the two diseases; however, further clinical and experimental validation is required.

title: MHR and AIP as Differential Predictors of 1-Year Major Adverse Cardiovascular and Cerebrovascular Events After Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Combined Model Study.
authorString: Liang Z, Hu W, Xu C, Wang H, Li F.
abstractText:
Objective

To evaluate the predictive value of monocyte-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (MHR), plasma atherogenic index (AIP), and baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score for 1-year major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) after acute ischemic stroke, and to explore potential differences in their predictive patterns across endpoint subtypes.

Methods

This retrospective study enrolled 429 elderly patients (≥65 years) with acute ischemic stroke admitted to Lu'an People's Hospital (Anhui, China) between January 2020 and September 2023. Clinical and laboratory data were collected; MHR and AIP were Z-standardized. Patients were followed for 1 year for MACCE (stroke recurrence, all-cause mortality, non-fatal myocardial infarction/angina). Independent predictors were identified using multivariable logistic regression (Enter method: full model, then parsimonious model). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and DeLong tests compared individual and combined (MHR+AIP+baseline NIHSS) models. Endpoint-specific analyses were exploratory. Bootstrap resampling was performed for internal validation.

Results

MACCE occurred in 115 patients (26.8%), comprising 58 stroke recurrences, 41 deaths, and 17 coronary events. MHR (per 1-SD increase: OR=2.765, 95% CI: 2.062-3.707, P<0.001), AIP (per 1-SD increase: OR=1.682, 95% CI: 1.289-2.193, P<0.001), and Baseline NIHSS score (OR=1.170, 95% CI: 1.108-1.235, P<0.001) were independent predictors of MACCE. In exploratory endpoint-specific analyses, MHR was associated with all three subtypes, while AIP was associated with stroke recurrence and coronary events but not all-cause mortality. However, formal interaction tests were underpowered. AUCs were 0.731 (MHR), 0.628 (AIP), 0.646 (NIHSS), and 0.810 (combined); the combined model outperformed all individual markers (all P<0.05 by DeLong test).

Conclusion

MHR and AIP independently predict 1-year MACCE in elderly stroke patients. The observed differences in their associations across endpoint subtypes are exploratory and hypothesis-generating; formal interaction tests or adequately powered prospective studies are required. The combined model may improve risk stratification, but requires prospective validation.

title: Cardiovascular Events Among Female Users of Osteoporosis Treatments: A Cohort Study in United Kingdom Primary Care Data.
authorString: Persson R, Yang TH, Jafry Z, Vasilakis-Scaramozza C, Hagberg KW, Jick SS.
abstractText:
Background

Information on cardiovascular disease (CVD) safety of osteoporosis treatments is important for patients and clinicians choosing between treatment options.

Methods

We conducted a cohort study in the United Kingdom Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum and linked inpatient data (2000-2020). We selected two cohorts of female patients aged 40-89 with no history of CVD: (1) treated cohort: new users of study drugs (alendronate, ibandronate, risedronate, zoledronic acid, etidronate, denosumab, raloxifene, teriparatide, and calcitonin); (2) common reference cohort: prescription vitamin D users with a diagnosis or monitoring for osteoporotic disease. We followed patients from first prescription through censor date (event, major comorbidity, age 90, or end of record) and estimated adjusted incidence rate ratios (aIRRs) of atrial fibrillation (AFib), myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, and fatal stroke, by study drug compared to vitamin D-only. We assessed aIRRs compared to the common referent across all osteoporosis treatments.

Results

Among 226,484 (74%) patients in the treated cohort and 79,973 (26%) in the vitamin D-only referent cohort, there were 4313 AFib, 7312 stroke, and 3846 MI outcomes. AFib rates were highest in zoledronic acid users (13 outcomes; aIRR 1.87; 95% CI 1.08-3.24). MI incidence was highest among ibandronate users (63 outcomes; aIRR 1.50; 95% CI 1.16-1.95). There were no differences in rates of AFib or MI across other study drugs or for stroke or fatal stroke for any study drug.

Conclusion

Rates of AFib, MI and stroke were similar across most osteoporosis treatments, including between various types of bisphosphonates. However, the rate of AFib was increased among zoledronic acid users and rate of MI was somewhat increased among ibandronate users. However, findings were generally limited by small numbers of exposed outcomes.

title: Effect of Preoperative Intranasal Dexmedetomidine on Postoperative Myocardial Injury in Patients Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
authorString: Li Q, Hu S, Fu Y, Shen L, Xiong B, Qi D.
abstractText:
Purpose

To evaluate the effects of preoperative intranasal dexmedetomidine on postoperative myocardial injury biomarkers in patients undergoing on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).

Patients and methods

In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 70 patients undergoing on-pump CABG were assigned to receive intranasal dexmedetomidine (1 μg/kg) or saline 30 min before bedtime on the night before surgery and again 30 min before anesthesia induction. The primary outcome was serum high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) at 24 h after surgery. Secondary outcomes included perioperative cardiac biomarkers, preoperative sleep quality, postoperative delirium, and adverse events.

Results

For the prespecified primary outcome, hs-cTnT concentrations at 24 h after surgery were significantly lower in the dexmedetomidine group than in the control group (estimated marginal means, 170.29 vs 357.29 ng/L; P < 0.001). Postoperative creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB) concentrations were also lower in the dexmedetomidine group (all P < 0.05). N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide showed a significant group-by-time interaction (P = 0.030), although between-group differences at individual postoperative time points were not significant. The dexmedetomidine group had higher Leeds Sleep Evaluation Questionnaire scores (62 [60-64] vs 44 [41-50]; P < 0.001) and a lower incidence of postoperative delirium (14.3% vs 37.1%; P = 0.029). Adverse events, mechanical ventilation duration, and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay did not differ significantly between groups.

Conclusion

In this single-center trial, two-dose preoperative intranasal dexmedetomidine was associated with lower postoperative hs-cTnT and CK-MB concentrations, better subjective preoperative sleep quality, and a lower observed incidence of postoperative delirium. These findings are preliminary and require confirmation in larger, adequately powered multicenter randomized trials to determine whether the biomarker reductions translate into clinically meaningful cardiovascular benefits.

Trial registration

Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2500111431.

title: Anatomical Risk Factors for Technical Failure of the Perclose Vascular Closure Device: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
authorString: Jinno H, Kikuchi S, Doita T, Fukii I, Fuchizawa K, Uramoto T, Ohira S, Kamada K, Kuriyama N, Azuma N.
abstractText:
Objectives

Percutaneous large-bore femoral closure with the Perclose device is widely used, but technical failure remains clinically important. We identified anatomical risk factors for technical failure.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed endovascular aortic repair and endovascular therapy procedures using the Perclose device at the common femoral artery (CFA) between April 2020 and March 2025. Preoperative computed tomography (CT) measured CFA diameter, puncture depth, and a calcification score (0-4). Technical failure was defined as failure to achieve hemostasis with the intended deployment. Independent predictors were identified using patient-clustered generalized estimating equations.

Results

Among 300 patients (485 limbs), technical failure occurred in 52 limbs (10.7%), of which 75.0% required surgical repair. Independent predictors were a higher calcification score (odds ratio [OR] 2.13 per 1-point increase; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.37-3.31), an emergency procedure (OR 3.77; 1.55-9.14), a smaller CFA diameter (OR 1.16 per 1-mm decrease; 1.01-1.32), and a shallower puncture depth (OR 1.22 per 5-mm decrease; 1.01-1.47); the area under the curve was 0.72.

Conclusions

Technical failure was driven by unfavorable CFA anatomy-heavy calcification, a small diameter, and a shallow puncture depth-and by emergency procedures. Preprocedural imaging assessment is essential; alternative closure or surgical cutdown should be considered in unfavorable or emergent cases.

title: Integrating Systemic Inflammation, Nutrition and Skeletal Muscle into a Composite Score (the HALP-Sarcopenia Combined Index) for Preoperative Risk Stratification of Lymph-Node Metastasis and Recurrence in Endometrial Carcinoma: A Single-Centre Retrospective Study.
authorString: Zhang Q, Guo D, Li D.
abstractText:
Background

Lymph-node metastasis and recurrence dominate outcomes in endometrial carcinoma, yet the strongest predictors are recovered only from the hysterectomy specimen, whereas systemic inflammation, nutritional reserve and skeletal-muscle mass are measurable before surgery. We investigated whether a preoperatively obtainable composite-the HALP-Sarcopenia Combined Index (HS-index)-is associated with nodal metastasis and recurrence.

Methods

We retrospectively studied 195 consecutive women undergoing primary surgery for endometrial carcinoma. The HS-index was specified a priori from the standardised HALP score and skeletal-muscle index (SMI). Nodal metastasis, assessable in the 181 women who underwent lymph-node evaluation, was modelled with logistic regression; recurrence was modelled with Cox proportional-hazards regression. Restricted cubic splines, decision-curve analysis and bootstrap-validated C-statistics were used to characterise the shape and clinical usefulness of the associations.

Results

Nodal metastasis occurred in 30 of 181 women (16.6%) and recurrence in 43 of 195 (22.1%; median follow-up 34 months). Per standard deviation, a higher HS-index was independently associated with lower odds of nodal metastasis (adjusted odds ratio 0.48, 95% CI 0.27-0.85; P = 0.012) and a lower hazard of recurrence (adjusted hazard ratio 0.37, 95% CI 0.25-0.55; P < 0.001) after adjustment for grade, myometrial invasion, lymphovascular space invasion, histological type and adjuvant therapy. Adding the HS-index to a clinicopathological model raised the area under the curve from 0.853 to 0.870, a non-significant increment.

Conclusions

A preoperatively available composite of nutrition, inflammation and muscle mass was independently and monotonically associated with nodal metastasis and recurrence. It is best positioned as an exploratory adjunct to, not a substitute for, surgical-pathologic staging, and requires external validation before clinical use.

title: Global Landscape of Telehealth Interventions for Type 2 Diabetes Self-Care: A Scoping Review of Nursing Roles, Care Models, and Outcomes.
authorString: Rahayu YSE, Pramukti I, Kurniawan T, Ibrahim K.
abstractText:
Background

Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) requires ongoing self-care support to minimize preventable complications. Telehealth interventions have the potential to extend diabetes self-management education and support beyond conventional face-to-face care. However, the specific contributions of nursing roles, conceptual frameworks, and digital care architectures have not been comprehensively synthesized.

Objective

This scoping review aimed to map global evidence on telehealth interventions for T2DM self-care.

Methods

The review was conducted in accordance with Arksey and O'Malley's framework, JBI scoping review guidance, and the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews. Electronic databases including PubMed/MEDLINE, EBSCOhost, Scopus, Taylor AND Francis Online, ScienceDirect, and Sage Journals, were systematically searched for empirical studies published between January 1, 2021, to June 26, 2026, examining telehealth, mHealth, telenursing, or digital self-care interventions for adults with T2DM involving nursing or nursing-relevant digital care component. Data were charted using the systematic table and synthesized through descriptive and thematic analysis.

Results

A total of 26 studies were included, representing diverse models such as app-based self-management, messaging platforms, telemonitoring, virtual education, EHR-supported discharge pathways, virtual group visits, and comprehensive telehealth. Nursing roles were categorized as digital education, clinical monitoring, care coordination, behavioral coaching, medication and follow-through support, peer-support moderation, and digital onboarding. Of the 26 included studies, nine (34.6%) were classified as nurse-led, five (19.2%) as nurse-supported, seven (26.9%) as multidisciplinary/team-based, and five (19.2%) had insufficient reporting to isolate a nurse-specific intervention role. Interventions featuring structured nurse involvement, individualized feedback, theory-informed behavior-change strategies, and escalation pathways demonstrated the most consistent improvements in self-care behaviors and selected glycemic outcomes, particularly HbA1c and fasting blood glucose.

Conclusion

Telehealth interventions for T2DM self-care should be regarded as hybrid care models rather than solely technology-based tools. The synthesized evidence supports nurse-mediated, theory-informed, and equity-sensitive digital diabetes care, while underscoring the need for improved reporting on nursing scope, digital engagement, clinical escalation, fidelity, cost, and implementation context.

title: Jejunal B-Cell Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma Presenting with a Long Stenosing Lesion in an Adolescent: A Case Report.
authorString: Deeb AS, Nasra AB, Alkaraa J, Alashkar M, Wassouf AAA.
abstractText:
Background

Jejunal involvement by pediatric B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) can be difficult to diagnose when the lesion lies beyond conventional endoscopic reach.

Case presentation

A previously healthy 15-year-old boy presented with 2 weeks of postprandial vomiting, periumbilical pain, weight loss, peripheral lymphadenopathy, and a palpable abdominal mass. CT identified a large segment of jejunal thickening. Enteroscopy showed approximately 12 cm of ulcerated, friable stenosis with contact bleeding; the endoscope could traverse the affected segment. Biopsies demonstrated an atypical lymphoid infiltrate, and immunohistochemistry supported CD20-positive B-cell NHL without a definitive subtype. Persistent vomiting led to surgical exploration, which showed extensive abdominal disease considered unresectable. A palliative gastrojejunostomy was performed. Further molecular and formal staging investigations were not completed, and the patient died before planned chemotherapy.

Conclusion

This case highlights the complementary diagnostic roles of CT and enteroscopy in jejunal lymphoma and the need to coordinate gastrointestinal palliation with prompt pathological and oncologic assessment. The available findings do not establish a specific lymphoma subtype or verifiable pediatric stage.

title: Nurse-Led Longitudinal Screening and Care Transitions for Post-Traumatic Stress Symptoms After Acute Type A Aortic Dissection: A 12-Month Retrospective Longitudinal Cohort Study.
authorString: Tang H, Wang Y, Jia T, Ma M, He F.
abstractText:
Objective

To identify longitudinal trajectories of post-traumatic stress symptoms (PTSS) after acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) and to examine baseline and time-varying psychological factors associated with subsequent symptom burden in a nurse-led follow-up cohort.

Methods

This single-center retrospective longitudinal cohort study included 278 ATAAD survivors discharged from Henan Provincial Chest Hospital between 1 August 2023 and 30 July 2024. Clinical and nurse-led follow-up records through 1 August 2025 were reviewed for assessments at discharge and at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. The primary trajectory analysis used PCL-5 scores from 1 to 12 months among participants with at least two valid assessments. One- through four-class latent class mixed models were compared according to convergence, Bayesian information criterion, classification quality, and minimum class size. Baseline correlates were examined with multinomial regression. Lagged models separated between-person means from within-person changes in illness threat, insomnia, and repetitive negative thinking; social support was examined across the 3-to-6-month interval.

Results

A three-class solution was selected: low-decreasing (n=153, 55.0%), recovering (n=77, 27.7%), and persistent-high (n=48, 17.3%). Within-person increases in illness threat, insomnia, and repetitive negative thinking were associated with higher subsequent PCL-5 scores, whereas higher social support was associated with a lower subsequent score. Baseline associations were attenuated after multiplicity correction.

Conclusion

The model identified three PTSS trajectories during the first year after ATAAD discharge. Repeated nurse-led assessment may help identify survivors with a persistent symptom burden, and changes in illness threat, insomnia, repetitive negative thinking, and social support may inform the timing and focus of transitional care. The effectiveness of screening or targeted care was not tested.

title: Tuberculous Cervicitis Mimicking Cervical Malignancy: A Diagnostic Challenge.
authorString: Zulfa F, Tjahyadi D, Djuwantono FW, Abdullah AR, Suardi A, Dewi OM.
abstractText:
Introduction

Tuberculous cervicitis is a rare form of female genital tuberculosis that can closely resemble cervical cancer both clinically and radiologically. Its nonspecific manifestation often leads to diagnostic challenges, delayed recognition, and the risk of unnecessary oncologic management. We report two cases of tuberculous cervicitis presenting with cervical lesions highly suggestive of cervical cancer.

Case illustration

A 42-year-old multiparous woman presented with vaginal discharge, amenorrhea, fever, and unintentional weight loss. Gynecological examination revealed extensive inflammatory involvement of the ectocervix, raising suspicion of cervical cancer. Cervical cytology was inconclusive. Histopathological examination demonstrated granulomatous inflammation with caseous necrosis and Langhans giant cells, supporting the diagnosis of tuberculous cervicitis in the context of patient's clinical presentation. Chest radiography showed right pleural effusion; however, microbiological confirmation of pulmonary or pleural tuberculosis was not available. The patient was treated with anti-tuberculosis therapy. A second case involved a 24-year-old nulliparous woman with a six-year history of infertility, secondary amenorrhea, chronic vaginal discharge, and postcoital bleeding. Pelvic examination revealed a friable and irregular cervical lesion. Imaging demonstrated a necrotic cervical mass with associated lymphadenopathy, highly suggestive of advanced cervical cancer. However, cervical biopsy revealed caseating granulomatous inflammation consistent with tuberculosis. The patient also received anti-tuberculosis treatment.

Conclusion

Tuberculous cervicitis should be considered in the differential diagnosis of cervical cancer, particularly in women presenting with abnormal cervical lesions, persistent vaginal discharge, menstrual abnormalities, or infertility. Histopathological examination remains the cornerstone of diagnosis when cytological and radiological findings are inconclusive. Early recognition is essential to prevent misdiagnosis and avoid unnecessary invasive or oncologic treatment, especially in regions with a high burden of tuberculosis.

title: Société de Biomécanique Senior Researcher Award 2025: Challenges in multiscale modeling and homogenization for integrative arterial biomechanics and mechanobiology
authorString: Sauty B, Morin C, Marino M, Avril S.

title: Digoxin Revisited: An Updated Review in the Light of Recent Trials.
authorString: Saad M, Abdullah M, Yelamarthy A, John K, Mallick AH, Khan B, Tahir H, Krishnamani R.
abstractText: Isolated from Digitalis species following William Withering's 1785 work on foxglove, digoxin inhibits myocardial Na+/K+-ATPase, raising intracellular calcium and vagal tone to produce inotropic, rate-controlling, and neurohormonal-deactivating effects. The foundational DIG trial (1997) showed no mortality benefit but reduced heart failure hospitalizations, prompting a progressive guideline downgrade. Three decades later, DIGIT-HF (2025, digitoxin) and DECISION (2026, low dose digoxin) retested cardiac glycosides atop modern four pillar guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT). DIGIT-HF significantly reduced the composite of death or worsening heart failure (hazard ratio (HR), 0.82), while DECISION showed a numerical but nonsignificant benefit. A pooled meta-analysis of DIG, DIGIT-HF, and DECISION (9,013 patients) confirmed a consistent 15% reduction in worsening heart failure events across three decades of changing background therapy, without a significant mortality effect. The Dig-RHD trial addressed an unstudied population: symptomatic rheumatic heart disease (RHD), a chronic valvular heart disease that results from permanent damage to cardiac valves due to group A streptococcal infection. RHD affects roughly 40 million people and causes approximately 300,000 deaths annually, disproportionately in low- and middle-income countries. In 1,769 patients randomized across 12 Indian centers, digoxin significantly reduced the composite of death or new-onset/worsening heart failure (31.4% vs. 35.5%; HR, 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.70 to 0.97; P = 0.02), with greater benefit in atrial fibrillation, women, and patients with low body mass index (BMI), and a number needed to treat of approximately 14 over 2 years. Digoxin is not a mortality-reducing drug, but pooled contemporary evidence establishes it as a reproducible, low-cost tool for reducing heart failure events, now supported for the first time by high-quality randomized data in RHD, a population with substantial global burden and no prior evidence-based medical therapy. These findings warrant reconsideration of digoxin's guideline status and development of RHD-specific recommendations.

title: Warfarin After Seven Decades: Persistent Value and the Contemporary Role of Vitamin K Antagonism.
authorString: Leite WF, Ribeiro WN, Povoa RMDS, de Almeida DR, Hemerly DFA, Luna Filho B, Moises VA, Ramires JAF.
abstractText: Warfarin is one of the most enduring drugs in cardiovascular medicine. Although direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) have transformed anticoagulation, especially in atrial fibrillation (AF) eligible for DOAC therapy, their success cannot be extrapolated to every thrombotic substrate. This review examines the contemporary boundaries of warfarin and vitamin K antagonist (VKA) therapy. Mechanical heart valves remain the clearest setting in which lifelong international normalized ratio (INR)-guided VKA therapy is required; randomized attempts to substitute dabigatran or apixaban have failed. In rheumatic heart disease-associated AF, INVICTUS favored VKA therapy over rivaroxaban, supporting the VKA class rather than warfarin specifically. High-risk thrombotic antiphospholipid syndrome, particularly triple-positive disease, is another VKA-preferred setting. Left ventricular thrombus (LVT) occupies an evolving position in which warfarin remains established, while randomized evidence supports rivaroxaban as a potential alternative in selected acute post-myocardial infarction LVT. Pregnancy with mechanical valves requires dynamic maternal-fetal risk balancing, whereas advanced chronic kidney disease and dialysis represent areas of uncertainty rather than intrinsic indications for warfarin. The global relevance of warfarin also depends on total anticoagulation burden, including INR monitoring, travel, treatment continuity, quality of anticoagulation, and reversal capacity. The persistence of VKA efficacy in selected highly thrombogenic environments raises a biologically plausible hypothesis that broader suppression of vitamin K-dependent factors may matter, but this mechanism is not established by clinical trials. Contemporary anticoagulation should therefore be substrate-centered: VKA therapy remains necessary in some conditions, preferred in others, increasingly replaceable in several, and uncertain in a few.

title: False patency, true occlusion: perfusion imaging and dual stent-retriever thrombectomy for a calcified carotid terminus embolus.
authorString: Huang M, Gan S, Miao J, Zhu R, Chen J, Chen W.
abstractText: Calcified cerebral emboli are an uncommon cause of acute ischemic stroke and may produce a false-patency sign on computed tomography angiography because their high attenuation can mimic intravascular contrast material. We report the case of a 77-year-old woman who presented with a wake-up stroke approximately 14 hours after she was last known well, with right hemiplegia and global aphasia. Noncontrast computed tomography showed a markedly hyperattenuating intraluminal focus at the left carotid terminus and proximal M1 segment, suggesting a calcified cerebral embolus. Computed tomography angiography appeared to show severe stenosis with residual luminal patency, whereas computed tomography perfusion demonstrated extensive hypoperfusion involving the left middle cerebral artery and bilateral anterior cerebral artery territories. Because the severe neurologic deficit and perfusion abnormality were discordant with the apparent patency on computed tomography angiography, cerebral angiography was performed. Digital subtraction angiography demonstrated complete occlusion of the left M1 origin and near-complete occlusion of the left A1 segment; the right A1 segment was congenitally hypoplastic. A rigid calcified embolus spanning the carotid-terminus bifurcation was retrieved using a balloon guide catheter-assisted dual-stent technique under proximal flow arrest, achieving complete reperfusion in a single pass. Histopathologic examination confirmed calcified embolic material. This case highlights the value of multimodal imaging and confirmatory angiography when clinical and imaging findings are discordant. In this patient, balloon guide catheter-assisted dual-stent retrieval was a tailored and feasible strategy; however, a single case cannot establish its superiority over other thrombectomy approaches.

title: The lungs in Alström syndrome: a retrospective analysis.
authorString: Madathil SC, Zhang Q, Geberhiwot T.
abstractText:
Background

Alström syndrome (AS) is a rare multisystemic disorder frequently associated with respiratory complications, which are a major cause of premature death. While fibrosis in multiple organs has been historically suggested as a hallmark of AS, including the lungs, definitive evidence in adult patients remains limited.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective study of adult patients diagnosed as AS seen in our National Multidisciplianry AS clinic from 2010 to 2024. Lung function test and high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of the thorax was performed in a subset of patients. Postmortem lung tissue analysis was available from four patients.

Findings

A total of 25/41 (61%) of the patients were unable to complete full lung function testing. Among those who did, 67% exhibited reduced lung volumes, with 47% showing decreased diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide but normal or elevated transfer coefficient for carbon monoxide, indicating extrapulmonary restrictive physiology. HRCT scans in 39 patients showed no evidence of diffuse interstitial lung fibrosis; however, breathing artefacts were common. Historical infantile cardiomyopathy was identified as a risk factor for adult pulmonary dysfunction. Post-mortem pathology reports were obtained from four patients and no diffuse fibrosis in the lung tissue was identified in any of the patients. Pulmonary hypertension and Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome were identified as potential causes of respiratory morbidity and mortality, despite the absence of intrinsic interstitial lung disease.

Interpretation

This is the first large cohort study to depict the lung in adult patients with AS. This study provides no evidence for diffuse interstitial lung fibrosis in adult patients with AS, challenging prior assumptions. Pulmonary dysfunction appears mainly due to extrapulmonary restrictive physiology, with infantile cardiomyopathy as a possible risk factor. Pulmonary hypertension and acute respiratory distress syndrome, rather than intrinsic lung disease, likely underlie respiratory morbidity and mortality, highlighting the need for focused cardiopulmonary care. Although this study represents one of the largest single-centre cohorts of patients with AS reported to date, the overall sample size remains limited due to the ultra-rare nature of the disease and findings should be interpreted with caution.

Funding

This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

title: Clinically Actionable Prevention and Management of Major Complications During Durable Left Ventricular Assist Device Support: A Contemporary Narrative Review.
authorString: Sheng WY, Tang TS, Wu YS, Asif H, Zakaria S, Zhang DF.
abstractText: Durable left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) have become an established therapy for selected patients with advanced heart failure as bridge-to-transplant or destination therapy. Despite major progress in continuous-flow pump design and perioperative care, long-term benefit remains constrained by a recurrent burden of right heart failure, aortic regurgitation, pump thrombosis, stroke, bleeding, infection, and end-organ dysfunction. Because these events often arise from the interaction of altered hemodynamics, hemocompatibility-related injury, chronic antithrombotic exposure, and the practical complexity of longitudinal device care, a complication-centered management framework is clinically useful. This contemporary narrative review focuses on actionable prevention, surveillance, and treatment strategies for the major complications encountered during durable LVAD support. Rather than providing a broad device-oriented overview, we emphasize clinically relevant decision points across the perioperative and long-term course, including right ventricular protection, antithrombotic balance, structured monitoring for aortic regurgitation and hemolysis, prevention of driveline infection, and multidisciplinary outpatient follow-up. By organizing current evidence around practical management pathways, this review aims to support earlier recognition of adverse events and more durable long-term support.

title: Prognostic Value of Serum Albumin in Elderly Cardiovascular Disease Management.
authorString: Liu YY, Zheng HQ, Guan FL, Han SS, Huang SW, Ye FH, Jiang WB.
abstractText: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide and represents a major contributor to disability and poor health among elderly individuals, particularly those aged ≥ 65 years. Age-related physiological changes, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and oxidative stress play critical roles in the development and progression of CVD. Identifying reliable prognostic biomarkers is therefore essential to improve risk stratification and clinical management in this vulnerable population. Serum albumin (SA), the most abundant plasma protein, has emerged as a potential prognostic marker in elderly patients with CVD. Accumulating evidence from observational studies indicates that hypoalbuminemia is associated with increased all-cause mortality across a wide spectrum of CVDs, including coronary artery disease, heart failure, hypertension, atrial fibrillation, stroke, peripheral artery disease, and in patients undergoing various cardiovascular interventions. Importantly, low SA levels have been shown to remain an independent prognostic marker of adverse outcomes in observational studies after adjustment for confounding factors, such as malnutrition, inflammation, and comorbid conditions, although these associations may partly reflect underlying disease burden and other clinical factors. Proposed mechanisms linking hypoalbuminemia to poor outcomes include impaired antioxidant capacity, increased inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and altered fluid balance. This review also highlights substantial heterogeneity in SA threshold values reported across studies, which may limit its standardized application in clinical practice. Although albumin supplementation has been suggested as a potential therapeutic strategy, current evidence regarding its clinical benefit remains inconclusive. SA may provide additional prognostic information in elderly patients with CVD and may support improved risk stratification across diverse clinical settings. At present, management strategies should prioritize identifying and addressing the underlying causes of hypoalbuminemia rather than routine albumin supplementation. Further well-designed studies are needed to establish standardized SA cut-off values and to clarify its role in guiding clinical decision-making in elderly cardiovascular populations.

title: Outcomes After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Using the Self-Expanding Allegra Valve in Daily Practice.
authorString: Zemaite J, Erler S, Schafer U, Vormfelde S, Remppis BA, Bohmann K, Januszewski BM, Burgdorf C.
abstractText:
Background

Limited data are available of the self-expanding Allegra transcatheter heart valve (THV). The aim of this study was to investigate the safety and outcome of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) using the Allegra THV in daily practice.

Methods

Between February 2018 and September 2024, 142 consecutive patients underwent Allegra TAVI at the Heart and Vascular Center, Bad Bevensen, Germany, either for native aortic stenosis (AS) (n = 117, median 82 (interquartile range 80-86) years) or degenerated aortic bioprostheses (n = 25, 80 (73-84) years) as valve-in-valve (ViV) procedures. Endpoints were defined according to Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 criteria.

Results

The logistic EuroSCORE II was significantly higher in the cohort of patients with degenerated aortic bioprostheses than in those with native AS (14.4% (6.6-25.3%) versus 3.3% (2.5-5.7%), P < 0.01). Technical success was nearly identical in both cohorts (91.5% of patients with native AS and 92.0% of patients with ViV TAVI). Postinterventional aortic regurgitation ≥ moderate was found in 4.5% of patients with native AS and was not present in any patient with ViV TAVI. In the native AS cohort, mean and maximal aortic pressure gradients decreased from 44 (36-54) mm Hg and 72 (60-87) mm Hg before the intervention to 6 (5-9) mm Hg and 12 (9-15) mm Hg after Allegra TAVI. In the ViV cohort, mean and maximal transvalvular pressure gradients decreased from 34 (27-43) mm Hg and 59 (44-70) mm Hg to 9 (7-11) mm Hg and 16 (14-23) mm Hg, respectively. Periprocedural mortality rates (≤ 30 days) were 6.8% and 12.0% in the native AS and ViV cohorts, respectively. One-year and 3-year survival rates were 87.2% and 73.2% in the native AS cohort and 89.8% and 75.1% in the ViV cohort, respectively.

Conclusions

TAVI using the self-expanding Allegra THV system is safe and leads to acute hemodynamic improvements in patients with native AS or degenerated aortic bioprostheses.

title: Association Between Hepatitis C Virus Infection and Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
Association Between Changes in Paravalvular Leakage After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation and Serum Lactate Dehydrogenase.
authorString: Ikuta A, Bando G, Oka S, Matsushita S, Inoue N, Hirao S, Abe M, Kadota K, Komiya T, Fuku Y.
abstractText:
Background

The association between changes in paravalvular leakage (PVL) and serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is unexplored. We aimed to investigate the short-term changes in PVL after TAVI and their association with LDH elevation.

Methods

A total of 550 consecutive patients underwent TAVI from 2020 to 2024. Of these, 313 receiving SAPIEN 3 (S3) or SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA (S3UR) valves were included in this study. Patients were categorized into two groups based on whether their PVL severity worsened by at least one grade from immediately after the procedure to hospital discharge.

Results

PVL deterioration was observed in 16.3% of patients. The incidence of moderate or greater LDH elevation was significantly higher in the PVL deterioration group than in the non-PVL deterioration group at 7 days (17.6% vs. 8.4%; P = 0.04) and 1 month (29.4% vs. 8.8%; P < 0.01) after the procedure. The area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve for predicting PVL deterioration using the sizing index (SI) was 0.84, with an optimal cut-off value of 96.5% (odds ratio (OR): 13.6; 95% confidence interval (CI): 6.55-31.1; P < 0.01). Multivariable analysis showed that an aortic valve calcium score ≥ 1,435, use of the S3UR valve, and an SI < 96.5 were independently associated with PVL deterioration.

Conclusion

Early PVL deterioration after TAVI with a balloon-expandable valve may be associated with LDH elevation. These findings highlight the importance of selecting a prosthetic valve with an appropriate sizing ratio to minimize PVL deterioration after TAVI.

title: Virtual Assessment of Coronary Microcirculation Before and After Rotational Atherectomy.
authorString: Kone G, Baala B, Canville A, Godin M, Landolff Q.
abstractText:
Background

Calcified coronary lesions remain a major challenge during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Rotational atherectomy (RA) (Boston Scientific) is a well-established tool used to modify calcified plaques and facilitate stent delivery. Despite its mechanical benefits, RA may adversely affect coronary microcirculation through distal plaque debris embolization. Angiography-derived microvascular resistance (AMR) (Pulse Medical) is a wire-free index correlated with invasive indices such as the index of microcirculatory resistance (IMR), which allows assessment of microcirculatory resistance directly from angiographic images, without a pressure wire or adenosine. The objective of this study is to evaluate changes in AMR before and after RA and to identify clinical, angiographic, and procedural predictors of postprocedural coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD).

Methods

We performed a retrospective single-center observational study including all patients who underwent RA between January 2023 and December 2024 at Clinique Saint-Hilaire in Rouen, France. AMR was measured before and after RA using the AngioPlus software (Pulse Medical). CMD was defined as postprocedural AMR > 250 mm Hg·s/m.

Results

Of 49 RA procedures, 40 patients were included. AMR increased in all cases but CMD occurred in 42.5% of patients (n=17). Diabetes mellitus and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) were significantly more prevalent in the CMD group. Long coronary artery lesions (> 20 mm), larger plaque burden, and prolonged burr run time were associated with higher AMR values. Mean AMR rose from 176 to 315 mm Hg·s/m in the CMD group, versus 177 to 201 mm Hg·s/m in the non-CMD group.

Conclusions

Performing RA affects the coronary microcirculation, especially in cases of diabetes mellitus and reduced LVEF.
