title: Resistance Training and Respiratory and Immune-Related Outcomes in Older Adults: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
authorString: Silva-Reis A, de Oliveira RAC, Moura-Maia MS, Rachid-Wolpp ET, Moreira-Silva NN, de Oliveira LVF, Bachi ALL, Aprigliano V, Salehian O, Albertini R, Furtado GE, Sá Filho AS, Stolz D, Vieira RP.
abstractText: Age-related declines in pulmonary function and immune regulation increase morbidity and mortality in older adults. Physical activity mitigates these effects, but the isolated impact of resistance training (RT) on lung function and immune responses remains unclear. Sixty-nine older adults without participation for at least one year in structured exercise programs (aged 60-85 years) were recruited from a community extension program at a Brazilian university and randomized into an RT group (n = 31) or a control group (n = 38). This randomized controlled trial evaluated the effects of a 12-week supervised RT program performed three times per week. Primary outcomes included spirometry parameters (FVC, FEV1, FEV1/FVC, PEF, and FEF25-75%), respiratory muscle strength (MIP and MEP), and inflammatory biomarkers (IL-6, IL-10, TNF-α, and Klotho) in plasma and exhaled breath condensate. Secondary outcomes included handgrip strength, sit-to-stand performance, oxygen saturation, and body composition. Normally distributed outcomes were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVA, whereas non-normally distributed longitudinal outcomes were analyzed using the Brunner-Langer approach for factorial longitudinal data. Between-group differences in pre-to-post changes were additionally estimated using bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. No significant Group × Time interactions were observed for spirometric parameters. Significant Group × Time interactions were observed for MIP and MEP; however, significant pre-to-post changes were observed in the control group but not in the RT group. A significant Group × Time interaction was also observed for sit-to-stand performance, with improvement in the control group but not in the RT group. No significant Group × Time interactions were observed for handgrip strength or oxygen saturation. Significant Group × Time interactions were observed for plasma IL-6, IL-10, and Klotho (all p < 0.001), as well as exhaled breath condensate IL-6 (p = 0.006) and Klotho (p = 0.003). In contrast, no significant interactions were observed for plasma TNF-α, exhaled breath condensate IL-10, or exhaled breath condensate TNF-α. Twelve weeks of supervised RT were associated with differential changes in respiratory muscle strength, functional capacity, and selected systemic and airway biomarkers in older adults. Significant Group × Time interactions were observed for MIP, MEP, the 1-min sit-to-stand test, and selected inflammatory and aging-related biomarkers, but not for pulmonary function. These findings indicate that the effects of RT varied across outcomes, rather than demonstrating consistent improvement across all assessed measures. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06682221.

title: Differentiated effect of hypothermia versus normothermia after cardiac arrest by neurological status and clinical correlates of ischemic burden.
authorString: Lileikyte G, Marinho LL, Lu Y, Boileau P, Moseby-Knappe M, Spicer A, Dankiewicz J, Lilja G, Wise MP, Schrag C, Aneman A, Haenggi M, Grejs AM, Horn J, Stammet P, Jakobsen JC, Kjaergaard J, Rylander C, Harhay MO, Churpek MM, Nielsen N, Lawler PR.
abstractText:
Introduction

The optimal temperature target after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains uncertain, as major randomized trials have not demonstrated a clear benefit of lower-target hypothermia compared with normothermia. Despite this, patients with differing degrees of ischemic burden or early neurological injury may hypothetically respond differently to temperature targets, raising the possibility of heterogeneous treatment effects. This study aimed to determine whether outcomes differ after OHCA with 33 °C versus controlled normothermia (36.0-37.7 °C) according to correlates of ischemic burden and neurological findings at hospital admission.

Methods

This secondary analysis of the TTM and TTM2 trials employed effect-based machine learning to probe for heterogeneous treatment effects. Causal forests and Bayesian additive regression trees (BART) estimated individualized treatment effects (ITE) based on ischemia duration, prehospital factors, and neurological examination findings at hospital admission. Treatment effect modifier variable importance parameter (TEM-VIP) analysis ranked the baseline variables most likely to modify effect. The primary outcome was six-month all-cause mortality, and the secondary outcome was poor functional outcome (modified Rankin scale score 4-6). Primary analyses evaluated potential heterogeneity within each trial, while secondary analyses pooled all participants.

Measurements and main results

All 2789 adult OHCA patients from the trials' primary analyses were included (median age 65 years (IQR 56-73), 79.9% male). Death occurred in 49.4% of patients in the 33 °C group, and in 47.9% in the controlled normothermia group. Variation in six-month mortality ITEs estimated from ischemic burden correlates and initial neurological findings was minimal, and no significant heterogeneity of treatment effect was identified across all methods and analysis populations. In the pooled analysis, estimated conditional mean mortality risk difference ranged from - 1.2% to 2.1% in causal forest (p = 0.99), and from - 0.5% to 1.5% in BART, with posterior probabilities for hypothermia benefit ranging from 42% to 53%. Absolute subgroup estimates in TEM-VIP analysis were small and non-significant. Results were consistent for the six-month functional outcome.

Conclusions

Among TTM and TTM2 participants randomized to 33 °C versus controlled normothermia post-OHCA, no evidence of detectable heterogeneity of treatment effect based on available clinical correlates of ischemic burden or initial neurological findings was identified, with minimal estimated variation in treatment effect.

title: A Randomized Factorial Trial of Varenicline, Nicotine Lozenges, and Smartphone Medication Adherence Reminders for Smoking Cessation: Protocol for the COMBO II Study.
authorString: Machado NM, Ahluwalia JS, Businelle MS, Frank-Pearce SG, Baranskaya I, Hébert ET, Sifat MS, Gwin SH, Thakur R, Glassman S, Kinnard HW, Kumar G, Gupta D, Kendzor DE.
abstractText:
Background

Smoking remains the leading preventable cause of cancer mortality in the United States. Varenicline is the most effective monotherapy for smoking cessation, and combining it with nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) may further improve cessation rates. Smartphone-based medication adherence interventions could enhance pharmacotherapy adherence and cessation outcomes.

Objective

This trial will evaluate the efficacy of varenicline plus nicotine lozenges and a smartphone adherence intervention for promoting smoking cessation.

Methods

This fully remote, 2 × 2 factorial randomized controlled trial will enroll 496 adults from Oklahoma who smoke cigarettes daily. Participants will be randomized to 1 of 4 conditions: (1) varenicline (VAR) + nicotine lozenges (NRT) versus VAR alone and (2) a smartphone-based smoking cessation app with adherence components (COMBO-A [adherence]) or without adherence components (COMBO-B [basic]). The primary outcomes are biochemically verified 7-day point prevalence abstinence at 26 weeks post quit date and medication adherence during the treatment period. Secondary outcomes include withdrawal symptoms and medication side effects over the 12-week treatment period.

Results

Study recruitment began in July 2026. As of the date of this paper's submission, 8 participants have been enrolled. Enrollment is expected to be completed by December 2028, with primary data collection and follow-up completed by June 2029. Primary study results are anticipated later in 2029.

Conclusions

If effective, VAR+NRT would offer a new evidence-based cessation treatment option. If the smartphone adherence intervention improves medication adherence and cessation, it could be adapted for other pharmacotherapies and widely implemented. Ultimately, this research aims to enhance cessation efforts and reduce cancer risk among adults who smoke.

title: Leadless Cardiac Resynchronization Results in Left Ventricular Reverse Remodeling: A Randomized Substudy of the SOLVE-CRT Study.
authorString: Sanders P, Ariyaratnam JP, Rinaldi CA, Kubo SH, Thiyagarajah A, James S, Niazi IK, Betts T, Butter C, Biffi M, Zaidi A, Alison J, Rovaris G, Rao A, Ghani A, Piot O, Chow A, Singarayar S, Auricchio A, Gold MR, Lindenfeld J, Walsh MN, Singh JP, SOLVE-CRT Investigators.

title: Real-World Comparison of Cardiorenal Outcomes With SGLT-2 Inhibitors Versus GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Type 2 Diabetes.
authorString: Huang CH, Wu JL, Ling TC, Yang AS, Wu SH, Huang CC, Lai EC, Chang YT.
abstractText:
Aims

To compare cardiorenal outcomes, mortality and safety between sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2i) and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RA) in adults with Type 2 diabetes (T2D).

Materials and methods

We conducted a retrospective, new-user cohort study using the TriNetX global federated health research network. We identified 249 237 propensity score-matched pairs (498 474 total patients) who initiated SGLT-2i or GLP-1 RA between 2018 and 2023. The primary outcome was a kidney failure/death composite, defined as kidney failure, dialysis, kidney transplantation or all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included composite cardiovascular events, mortality and safety profiles.

Results

SGLT-2i initiation was associated with a lower risk of the kidney failure/death composite compared with GLP-1 RA (HR: 0.87, 95% CI: 0.85-0.89). For the kidney-specific component, SGLT-2i initiation was associated with a lower risk of kidney failure, dialysis or kidney transplantation (HR: 0.74, 95% CI: 0.71-0.78), while all-cause mortality was also lower (HR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.88-0.93). The composite cardiovascular outcome (myocardial infarction, stroke, acute heart failure, cardiogenic shock, cardiac arrest or death) was broadly comparable between groups (HR: 0.98, 95% CI: 0.97-1.00).

Conclusions

SGLT-2i initiation was associated with lower risks of kidney failure-related outcomes and all-cause mortality compared with GLP-1 RA initiation, while cardiovascular outcomes were broadly comparable. These findings may inform individualized treatment selection in adults with T2D.

title: Congestion, Inflammation, and Renal Impairment Mediate the Association Between Cardiac Troponin and Mortality in Acute Heart Failure.
authorString: Scicchitano P, Iacoviello M, Ricci G, De Feo D, Di Rienzo G, Bonfantino VM, Massari F.
abstractText:
Introduction

Cardiac troponin is recognized as a strong predictor of mortality in patients with acute heart failure (AHF). The aim of this study was to evaluate the prognostic impact of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) on mortality risk in patients with AHF in relation to inflammatory, congestion, and renal indices.

Methods

We enrolled 431 patients (79 ± 10 years, 51% male) with AHF. At admission, hemodynamic congestion, inflammatory status, and renal function were assessed by means of brain natriuretic peptide (BNP, ng/l), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP, mg/l), and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR, ml/min), respectively. Mediation analyses were performed to assess the presence and magnitude of these components.

Results

The cumulative incidence of mortality at 180-day follow-up was 36%. hs-cTnI significantly correlated with BNP (r = 0.28), hs-CRP (r = 0.31), and eGFR (r = - 0.23); these variables explained 18% of the overall variability in hs-cTnI. In univariate Cox regression analysis, hs-cTnI, hs-CRP, BNP, and eGFR were predictors of all-cause death. The association between hs-cTnI and mortality was largely mediated by inflammation, congestion, and renal function, which collectively explained 69% of the total effect. In multivariate analysis, only ln hs-CRP (HR: 1.21; 1.08-1.37), ln BNP (HR: 1.37; 1.09-1.74), and eGFR (HR: 0.99; 0.98-1.00) remained independent predictors of mortality.

Conclusions

Elevated troponin levels in AHF might be influenced by the coexistence of systemic inflammation, hemodynamic congestion, and renal dysfunction. Therefore, circulating troponin in AHF may be considered an integrated biomarker reflecting multiple pathophysiological processes.

title: Immuno-Proteomic Age of Cardiovascular Etiology (iPACE) Signature Predicts Cardiovascular Risk in Elderly Patients
authorString: Baechle JJ, Arthur J, Nguyen K, Wu F, Fuentealba M, Knowlton KU, Knight S, Horne B, Sayed N, Maecker H, Winer DA, Barzilai N, Davis MM, Haddad F, Furman D.
abstractText: Despite advances in clinical care, cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of disability and mortality worldwide. While age alone is a primary risk factor for CVD, accumulating evidence suggests the immune system influences the initiation and progression of CVD pathophysiology, particularly in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and atherosclerotic CVD (ASCVD). Here, using two independent cohorts of older adults, we develop a thirty-protein signature of age based on serum immune proteomics, which correlates with HFpEF and ASCVD risk and mortality (Immuno-Proteomic Age of Cardiovascular Etiology, iPACE). We find aging-related circulating immune proteins associated with ASCVD and HFpEF-specific resilience and susceptibility that may be used as potential prognostic, diagnostic, or therapeutic targets.

title: Bioresorbable, Injectable In Situ-Formed Electroactive mRNA-Delivering Device for Precision Gene Therapy after Myocardial Infarction
authorString: Aydemir U, Sahoglu Göktas S, Dasmahapatra U, Yadav AS, Hellman K, Sumit S, Ek F, Arner A, Meissner A, Hjort M, Olsson R.
abstractText: Myocardial infarction (MI) causes irreversible cardiomyocyte loss and triggers inflammatory and fibrotic remodeling that promote the progression to heart failure. Although regenerative gene therapy offers a promising route to cardiac repair, clinical translation has been limited because of the lack of targeted, minimally invasive, and clinically scalable delivery strategies. Here we report an injectable, bioresorbable in situ-formed electroactive device that enables local mRNA delivery through the pericardial space, a clinically established route of access. Following administration, the formulation self-assembles into a transient conductive mRNA-carrying drape electrode over the injured heart, enabling in vivo electrotransfection, and is then bioresorbed, eliminating the need for retrieval. In animal models, the formulation was well tolerated, did not disrupt cardiac contractile activity, and enabled targeted mRNA transfer. In a mouse model of MI, localized delivery of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF-A) mRNA attenuated adverse remodeling, improved cardiac function (e.g., stroke volume and ejection fraction were fully recovered), and established a minimally invasive strategy for localized regenerative gene delivery to the injured heart.

title: Validation of Modified Albumin-Bilirubin-Tumor Stage as a Prognostic Model in Early-Stage Hepatocellular Carcinoma Treated With Radiofrequency Ablation.
authorString: Hsieh CY, Yeh WS, Yen YH, Kuo YH, Tsai MC, Lu SN, Hung CH, Wang JH, Chen CH, Kee KM.

journal.title: The Kaohsiung journal of medical sciences

abstractText: Survival after radiofrequency ablation (RFA) for very early- or early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains heterogeneous because prognosis depends on both tumor burden and hepatic reserve. We retrospectively evaluated treatment-naive patients with Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) Stages 0 or A HCC treated with RFA as initial therapy from January 2002 to September 2016. Patients with Child-Pugh class A or B and complete ablation were included. Four prespecified total scores, Child-Pugh-tumor (CP-T), albumin-bilirubin-tumor (ALBI-T), modified ALBI-tumor (mALBI-T), and platelet-ALBI-tumor (pALBI-T) were compared using the Akaike information criterion (AIC), Harrell concordance index (C-index), time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, calibration, and subgroup analyses. Of 1238 patients screened, 950 were included; 831 (87.5%) were Child-Pugh class A. During a median follow-up of 5.44 years, 417 deaths occurred; 5- and 10-year overall survival rates were 58.0% and 35.8%, respectively. The American Joint Committee on Cancer eighth-edition T stage illustrated the best tumor-stage performance and was used in the total scores, while mALBI-T had the lowest AIC (5052.2) and highest Harrell C-index (0.628; 95% confidence interval, 0.601-0.655). Paired bootstrap differences versus CP-T, ALBI-T, and pALBI-T were statistically significant, but modest, while mALBI-T performed best at 5 years and in Child-Pugh class A patients, whereas all models showed limited discrimination in Child-Pugh class B patients. Apparent calibration was generally close, and mALBI-T also had the best fit for recurrence-free survival. mALBI-T provides a simple prognostic model for long-term survival stratification after complete ablation in early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma, especially in Child-Pugh class A patients.

title: Implications of SGLT2 Inhibitors, GLP-1RAs, and Nonsteroidal MRAs on the Anticipated Burden of Heart Failure.
authorString: Sayed A, Vasan RS, Harrell FE, Butler J.
abstractText:
Background

Several treatments that reduce the risk of heart failure (HF) have been introduced recently. Their impact on the future burden of HF in the U.S. has not been well characterized.

Objectives

This study aims to estimate the potential impact of recently approved cardiometabolic medications on the future burden of HF in the United States.

Methods

Using a nationally representative sample of persons in the United States 30-79 years of age without cardiovascular disease at baseline, we used the PREVENT (Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events) equation to estimate the 10- and 30-year burden of HF and the projected impact of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists on these estimates. The authors estimated the total number of HF cases that could be averted with risk-based treatment and calculated the number needed to treat to prevent HF.

Results

An estimated 5.5 million (95% CI: 5.1-5.8 million) U.S. adults 30-79 years of age without established cardiovascular disease will develop HF over 10 years. It is estimated to decrease to 5.1 million (95% CI: 4.7-5.4 million) with indicated treatment with a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor, 5.2 million (95% CI: 4.8-5.6 million) with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, 5.4 million (95% CI: 5.0-5.7 million) with nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, and 4.8 million (95% CI: 4.4-5.2 million) with the use of combination therapy. The use of combination therapy in eligible persons with an estimated 10-year HF risk of ≥10% would result in 6.8 million (95% CI: 6.1-7.5 million) eligible participants, and 498,000 (95% CI: -663,000 to -319,000) fewer cases of HF, with a number needed to treat of 14 (95% CI: 10-22) to prevent 1 incident case.

Conclusions

The projected burden of HF in the U.S. is substantial. A risk-based approach to preventive treatment may help reduce this considerably. The feasibility of such an approach deserves further investigation.

title: Dynamics of the Prevalence of Non-communicable Diseases in the Urban Double Cotonou - Abomey-Calavi (South of Benin).
authorString: Tranquillin YF, Azouma KH, Justin D, Fanès AT.
abstractText:
Background

The on going demographic transition in African countries like Benin is promoting changes in lifestyle and intensifying the emergence of non communicable diseases (NCDs), a marker of the epidemiological transition.

Objective

This research aims to analyse the influence of demographic dynamics on NCDs in Cotonou and Abomey Calavi.

Material and methods

The methodological approach is based on documentary research and interviews with stakeholders. Technical and general documents were consulted throughout all phases of the research. In total, 58 semi structured interviews were conducted with medical practitioners identified through purposive sampling, as well as 761 questionnaires addressed to heads of households (409) and individuals diagnosed with NCDs (352). The sample size was determined according to the principle of empirical saturation and the Cochran formula. The prevalence of each pathology is obtained based on the variables provided in the survey questionnaires. The prevalence of a disease is the proportion of people affected by that disease observed at a given point in time. The analysis of multiple correspondence and multinomial logistic regression allowed for the assessment of interrelations and the contribution of variables to the prevalence of NCDs.

Results

The results show that the gender structure of the population in the pair shows a slight predominance of women. The indicators of youth and old age show a significant young population, still marked by gradual aging, but which bodes well for the prospects of a demographic dividend. Similarly, the results show that hypertension is the most prevalent condition at 48.1%, followed by diabetes (14.6%), chronic respiratory diseases (10%) and cancers (2.5%). Research into risk factors proves that age, gender, place of residence education level, size of siblings and household and marital status significantly influence the risk of NCDs. Thus, the probability of having an NCD increases with age. A higher level of education is associated with a lower risk of diabetes and chronic kidney disease. Married individuals or those in a monogamous partnership have a lower risk of hypertension, which could be related to better social support. Urban living is associated with a higher risk of hypertension and cancers, probably due to environmental and lifestyle factors. Similarly, physical activity is associated with a reduced risk of NCDs. A higher intake of fruits and vegetables is linked to a reduced risk of diabetes, whereas alcohol consumption is inversely associated.

Conclusion

Demographic dynamics and lifestyle changes in the Cotonou-Abomey-Calavi urban area contribute significantly to the increase in non-communicable diseases, highlighting the need to strengthen prevention policies and promote healthy lifestyles.

title: Radiographic manifestations of pneumatosis intestinalis and construction of an AI-assisted diagnostic system.
authorString: Zhang X.
abstractText: Pneumatosis intestinalis (PI) has a wide range of etiologies, and the imaging differentiation between benign and ischemic PI is difficult, leading to a high risk of missed diagnosis. This study systematically summarizes the CT (Computed Tomography) imaging manifestations of PI and constructs an AI (Artificial Intelligence)-assisted diagnostic model that integrates multidimensional features. This study retrospectively collected CT and x-ray data from 612 patients with PI (398 benign and 214 ischemic cases) from three tertiary hospitals, and included an external validation set of 106 cases. Imaging analysis established a five-level PI-CT severity scoring system based on gas morphology, distribution, portal venous gas (PVG), intestinal wall enhancement, mesenteric edema, and ascites. The AI system adopted a two-level architecture: The first level used EfficientNet-B3 for rapid screening on x-ray films; the second level used 3D nnU-Net (No-new-Net) to segment intestinal wall gas, and then fused the data through a three-branch network (gas morphology, accompanying signs, and clinical metadata) via cross-attention to output the probability of ischemic PI. In the internal test set, the model achieved an AUC (Area Under the Curve) of 0.947 for ischemic PI (sensitivity 91.3%, specificity 93.6%), significantly outperforming senior radiologists (AUC = 0.876); the AUC on the external validation set was 0.931. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis showed that PVG and blood lactate were the most important predictors. This two-tiered AI system can significantly improve the early identification of the causes of critical PI, providing a reliable method for intelligent diagnosis of emergency imaging.

title: A Rare Endobronchial Lipoma of the Right Middle Lobe Causing Middle Lobe Syndrome and Recurrent Post-Obstructive Infection in a Patient With Interstitial Lung Disease, Managed by Lung-Sparing Bronchoscopy.
authorString: Palamidas A, Papatheodosiou K, Karagianni E, Daglis F, Bouros D.
abstractText: Endobronchial lipomas are rare benign tumours that can cause airway obstruction and recurrent infection. A 70-year-old smoker with combined pulmonary fibrosis and emphysema presented with recurrent right middle lobe infections and declining pulmonary function. Computed tomography revealed a fat-density lesion obstructing the middle lobe bronchus, with atelectasis and consolidation. Bronchoscopy and histology confirmed lipoma. Given limited respiratory reserve, lung-sparing flexible bronchoscopy with snare electrocautery and argon plasma coagulation restored airway patency; retained purulent secretions were drained and infection treated. At 2 months, the patient was asymptomatic with radiological resolution; FVC improved from 75% to 83% predicted and DLCO from 35% to 50% predicted. Recovery followed concurrent recanalization, drainage and antimicrobial treatment, whose individual contributions cannot be separated. This case highlights bronchoscopic diagnosis and treatment of benign obstruction in persistent middle lobe disease. Longer surveillance is needed to assess durability.

title: 6-min walk test reveals early physiological impairment in fibrotic interstitial lung diseases.
authorString: Ogura T, Okuda R, Kuwahira I, Nishikiori H, Chiba H, Takeda Y, Suda T, Fujisawa T, Abe M, Tomioka H, Sakamoto S, Zaizen Y, Ohkubo H, Yamauchi H, Kawamura T, Kimura M, Sakamoto K, Koga Y, Nishiyama O, Nakagawa H, Yatera K, Usui K, Matsushima H, Hashimoto D, Handa T, Kishaba T, Ichiyasu H, Oyamada Y, Matsuda T, Ishimoto H, Narumoto O, Nukiwa T, Kobayashi K, JIPS Registry collaborators, JIPS Registry collaborators .
abstractText:
Rationale

Early prediction of lung function decline remains challenging in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and fibrotic interstitial lung diseases (ILDs). We evaluated whether oxygen desaturation during the 6-min walk test (6MWT) predicts forced vital capacity (FVC) decline and long-term outcomes.

Methods

We analysed data from two independent cohorts: the nationwide Japanese Idiopathic Interstitial Pneumonias (JIPS) Registry and an external IPF cohort (K-Junko Study). Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated for each 6MWT parameter to identify variables associated with FVC decline and to determine optimal thresholds. Sensitivity analyses were conducted using Fine-Gray models. The performance of the predictive model was assessed using calibration plots and the concordance index (C-index).

Results

In the JIPS IPF (n=457) and K-Junko IPF (n=318) cohorts, a peripheral oxygen saturation (S pO2 ) change of ≤-6 percentage points during the 6MWT independently predicted a decline in FVC of ≥5 percentage points in both cohorts (JIPS HR 1.292; K-Junko HR 1.480). Moreover, S pO2 change during the 6MWT was significantly associated with FVC change in the subsequent year, and this association persisted over 5 consecutive years in JIPS IPF cohort. The nomogram demonstrated moderate discrimination (C-index: 0.619 (training) and 0.632 (validation)) and fair calibration. A composite profile meeting all three criteria (FVC ≥80%, S pO2 change >-6 percentage points, 6-min walk distance (6MWD) ≥420 m) identified patients with favourable transplant-free survival. In the JIPS non-IPF fibrotic ILD cohort (n=387), S pO2 change remained the sole independent predictor of an FVC decline of ≥5 percentage points (HR 1.350).

Conclusion

S pO2 change during the 6MWT predicts FVC decline and outcomes across fibrotic ILD; its incorporation into routine assessment may enable earlier risk stratification and facilitate timely intervention.

title: D-dimer/NT-proBNP ratio in acute pulmonary embolism patients stratifies risk of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension.
authorString: Spychalska K, Jermakow M, Kucharska J, Dzikowska-Diduch O, Perzanowska-Brzeszkiewicz K, Dudzik-Niewiadomska I, Łabyk A, Ou-Pokrzewińska A, Wiśniewska M, Roik M, Michał C, Pruszczyk P.
abstractText:
Background

There are ongoing efforts to identify patients at risk of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) during acute pulmonary embolism (APE). Lower D-dimer levels and right heart overload at APE diagnosis were reported to predict CTEPH. We hypothesised that plasma D-dimer to N-terminal pro-B type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) ratio assessed during APE may be useful for early CTEPH screening.

Methods

We followed 342 APE survivors (median age 64.5 years, female 56.1%), for a median of 39 (25-64) months.

Results

Despite ≥3 months anticoagulation CTEPH was diagnosed in 22 (6.4%) patients (CTEPH(+)). At APE diagnosis, CTEPH(+) compared with subjects without this sequela (CTEPH(-)) presented with advanced right ventricular overload: increased tricuspid regurgitation peak gradient (TRPG) (46.5 mmHg versus 32.0 mmHg; p<0.001) and NT-proBNP (1860 ng·L-1 versus 515 ng·L-1; p=0.02). Despite no differences in plasma D-dimer (4210 μg·L-1 versus 5330 μg·L-1; p=0.10), the ratio of D-dimer to NT-proBNP (DD/NT-proBNP) was significantly lower in the CTEPH(+) cohort versus the CTEPH(-) cohort (2.89 μg·ng-1 versus 12.0 μg·ng-1; p<0.001). In patients with DD/NT-proBNP≤10 CTEPH was diagnosed in 20 cases (11.7%), whereas in the group with DD/NT-proBNP> 10 CTEPH could only be detected in 2 of 171 cases (1.2%) with an OR 0.09 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.02-0.38; p=0.0013), a sensitivity of 90.9% (95% CI 70.8-98.9%), a specificity 52.8% (95% CI 47.2-58.4%), a negative predictive value 98.8% (95% CI 95.8-99.9%), a and positive predictive value of 11.7% (95% CI 7.3-17.5%). Combination of DD/NT-proBNP≤10 with TRPG≥36 mmHg detected in 87 patients, including 17 patients with CTEPH (19.5% CTEPH incidence).

Conclusion

DD/NT-proBNP>10 μg·ng-1 identifies patients with a low risk of subsequent CTEPH diagnosis, whereas DD/NT-proBNP≤10, especially presenting TRPG≥36 mmHg at echocardiography, forms a high risk group at follow-up.

title: Botox Injection Combined With Partial Arytenoidectomy: A Novel Approach for Treatment of Episodic Laryngeal Breathing Disorders.
authorString: Zhou Z, Wu JH, Yan PK, Li XX, Kang J, Ge PJ.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: World J Otorhinolaryngol Head Neck Surg
journal.title: World journal of otorhinolaryngology - head and neck surgery
journal.isoabbreviation: World J Otorhinolaryngol Head Neck Surg

abstractText:
Objective

The aim of this study was to develop effective treatments for episodic laryngeal breathing disorders (ELBD), a series of diverse obstructive respiratory disorders with an unknown pathogenesis. The diseases include paradoxical vocal fold motion/movement disorder (PVFMD), vocal cord dysfunction (VCD), irritable larynx syndrome (ILS), exercise-induced laryngeal obstruction, and laryngospasm.

Methods

Five patients with ELBD were involved in this study (60-81 years, average of 70 years), including three men and two women, who visited the otolaryngology outpatient department suffering from dyspnea several times. Bilateral vocal fold paralysis and asthma were excluded. An injection of initial botulinum toxin into the vocal cords was treated for each patient. If recurrence were to take place within 3 months after injection, a vocal cord process resection would be performed. The visual scale of perception was used for assessing preoperative and postoperative dyspnea.

Results

All patients experienced symptoms of recurring dyspnea for a duration of 1-120 months. The average follow-up duration was 14 months (6-24 months) after treatment. Dyspnea was relieved in two patients after the Botox injection alone. Three patients found relief after unilateral vocal cord process resection. All patients showed a significant reduction in postoperative dyspnea scale in VAS score.

Conclusion

This study preliminarily explores the efficacy of combined Botox injection and partial arytenoidectomy as a therapeutic option for ELBD.

title: Compressive Goiter Hiding Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma Metastases to the Thyroid Gland-Report of a Rare Case and Literature Review.
authorString: Ying C, Messias H, Zagalo C, André S, Gomes P.
abstractText: Thyroid gland metastases should be considered in a patient presenting with thyroid disease and a history of cancer, particularly clear cell renal cell carcinoma. These may present many years after primary tumor resection and coexist with goiter or thyroid tumors. Early detection can significantly impact the patient's treatment and prognosis.

title: From Sedation to Injury: Isoflurane-Associated Hepatic Dysfunction: A Series of 3 Intriguing Cases.
authorString: Syed MNA, Qaiser F, Makhdoomi FH, Shaikh MTA, Aisha S, Hayder T.
abstractText: Hepatitis occurring post-induction of general anesthesia remains a perplexing conundrum of medicine. Isoflurane, one of the most commonly employed drugs in the maintenance of anesthesia worldwide, has succeeded outdated agents such as halothane. Despite its widespread and high frequency of usage, there exist unanticipated and undesirable side effects and toxicity that are usually overlooked, as the symptoms are mostly generic and insidious. It is reported that isoflurane causes acute liver injury ranging from mild transaminitis to fulminant hepatic failure. This case series discusses patients who have been unfortunate victims of this situation, developing severe transaminitis after exposure to isoflurane during general anesthesia induction and maintenance for surgical interventions for their respective ailments in the absence of any other relevant causal links. Every patient presented with postoperative jaundice and markedly elevated liver enzymes, which were treated conservatively, resulting in full recovery. In the absence of more specific therapies, conservative management remains the cornerstone of treatment. In this article, 3 intriguing cases have been described. These cases highlight the need for more research and greater awareness of isoflurane-induced hepatotoxicity, especially given its non-specific presentation.

title: Salt-Sensitive Hypertension and Vascular Dysfunction.
authorString: Zheng X, Li Z, Friberg L, Sabouri M, Gong YD, Machin DR, Wainford RD.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
journal.title: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
journal.isoabbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol

abstractText: The salt-sensitivity of blood pressure (SSBP) affects 50% of hypertensive individuals and ∼25% of normotensive individuals (increasing their hypertension risk) and is a risk factor for cardiovascular disease independent of blood pressure (BP). When consuming a high-salt (HS) diet ∼90% of U.S. consume excess salt), individuals with the SSBP develop salt-sensitive hypertension (SSH). Historically, the SSBP is thought to be mainly determined by neural and renal mechanisms. In salt-sensitive (SS) individuals, the brain fails to suppress sympathetic outflow in response to a HS diet and renal sodium handling is impaired, contributing to SSH. During HS-intake salt-resistant (SR) individuals suppress sympathetic outflow maintain sodium balance, and normotension. Recently, this classic theory was challenged due to its lack of consideration for vascular dysfunction as a contributing mechanism for the SSBP. Growing evidence shows a HS diet induces vascular dysfunction, including endothelial dysfunction and arterial stiffening, that may contribute to SSH. Furthermore, the endothelial glycocalyx is proposed to impact how the vasculature responds to a HS diet, the so-called 'vascular salt-sensitivity'. In this review, we summarize recent evidence on the pathophysiology of SSH with an emphasis on mechanisms regarding vascular dysfunction. HS diet-induced vascular dysfunction occurs regardless of changes in BP but may be exacerbated in SS phenotypes. Future studies are warranted to further delineate the causes for SSH and vascular dysfunction through stratification of SS/SR and normotensive/hypertensive to provide mechanistic insights into the relationship between the SSBP and vascular salt-sensitivity to promote precision medicine for cardiovascular disease management in those populations.

title: Postpartum Placental Ischemic Dams Display an Increase in Kidney Cortex TNF-α and Kidney Medulla Nitric Oxide Bioavailability with High Blood Pressure.
authorString: Smith SL, Smith J, Jones K, Castillo A, Burkes A, Howard A, Ma R, Cunningham M.

journal.title: American journal of physiology. Renal physiology

abstractText: Women who experience a placental ischemic (PI) pregnancy, such as preeclampsia, have an increased risk of developing chronic kidney disease (CKD) as early as 5-20 years postpartum. The underlying mechanisms leading to this increased risk for CKD are unknown. Mechanisms that contribute to the development of CKD are hypertension and changes in renal molecular factors such as inflammation, oxidative stress, and nitric oxide (NO) bioavailability. To determine the relationship between blood pressure, renal molecular factors, and CKD in women after a PI pregnancy, we used the reduced uterine perfusion pressure model of preeclampsia in rats. In this study, two groups were utilized: normal pregnant (NP) and PI dams. At 6 weeks postpartum (∼2-3 human years), we examined the dams' blood pressure via carotid catheterization, collected the plasma to measure creatinine, and obtained the kidneys to evaluate the abundance and concentrations of renal molecular factors. PI dams exhibited an increase in blood pressure (125±3vs111±3 mmHg, p=0.002), TNF-α in the kidney cortex (81.38±1.1vs67.48±0.58 pg/mL / mg Protein, p<0.0001), and increased NO bioavailability (0.64±0.08vs0.41±0.05 µmol NO<sub>3</sub>/mg Protein, p=0.03) in the kidney medulla. However, serum creatinine, renal KIM-1, eNOS, NGAL, and oxidative stress did not have significant changes. In summary, PI dams have alterations in kidney inflammation and NO bioavailability, with no indications of renal dysfunction or injury. Thus, suggesting that changes in renal molecular factors may precede the onset of CKD. This study is clinically relevant, because it highlights the potential contributions of altered renal molecular factors in development of CKD postpartum.

title: Residual Symptoms and Quality of Life in Female Patients with Hypothyroidism and Cardiovascular Disease
authorString: Gonzales CS, Theisen E, Sarau A, Kim J, Landek DC, Bianco AC, Volgman AS.
abstractText:
Background

Current clinical management of patients with hypothyroidism emphasizes thyroid hormone replacement at doses that normalize serum thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels. However, biochemical correction does not always translate into symptom resolution or restored health-related quality of life (QoL). We evaluated whether higher TSH levels within the reference range would be associated with worse Thyroid-Related Patient-Reported Outcome (ThyPRO)-39 scores, reflecting greater symptom burden.

Objective

The objective of this study was to assess residual symptoms and health-related quality of life in women with normal TSH levels in patients with cardiovascular disease being treated for hypothyroidism.

Materials and methods

We prescreened 96 participants who completed study assessments. Following the TSH obtained at the study visit, 14 participants were excluded due to TSH values falling outside the predefined euthyroid range (0.35-4.94 μIU/mL), resulting in a final cohort of 82 women. We also investigated whether comorbidities contributed to symptom burden.

Results

Although mean composite scores were numerically higher in the upper TSH quartiles, neither multivariable regression nor ordered trend testing demonstrated a significant association between increasing TSH and overall symptom burden (Jonckheere-Terpstra p = .333). Notably, major depressive disorder (MDD) (β=16.93, 95% CI 8.22–25.65; p<.001) and hypertension (HTN) (β=12.45, 95% CI 2.24–22.66; p=.018) were independently associated with greater Thy-PRO-39 scores.

Conclusions

MDD and HTN were independently associated with higher Thy-PRO-39 scores, suggesting that comorbidities may be more strongly related to persistent symptoms than modest variation in TSH within the euthyroid range. Our results suggest that in patients with hypothyroidism and cardiovascular disease, comorbidities may be particularly important when interpreting residual symptoms in biochemically euthyroid patients.

title: Electronic Health Record–Based Machine-Learning for Cardiac Arrhythmia Identification in Adults with High-Risk Chronic Disease: Model Development and Validation Study
authorString: Goel M, Matlock S, Karasu Benyes Y, Narayanan N, Howard J, Brazeal TG, Cogan C, Navarro E, Petrus A.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiac arrhythmias may remain unrecognized in adults with chronic disease. Established risk scores primarily address atrial fibrillation.

Objective

To develop and internally evaluate an electronic health record (EHR)–based machine-learning model to identify patients more likely to receive a documented cardiac arrhythmia diagnosis.

Methods

We retrospectively evaluated EHR data (2018–2025) from one healthcare organization among adults with type 2 diabetes, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chronic kidney disease, or coronary artery disease. Logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost were compared. XGBoost was selected using internal validation, reduced to 30 features using Shapley additive explanations, and evaluated in a holdout set with data ending one day before the index date. Sensitivity analyses excluded information recorded within 30, 90, or 180 days before the index date. An atrial fibrillation/flutter-specific analysis compared XGBoost with CHARGE-AF and HARMS 2 -AF.

Results

Among 30,356 patients, 6,835 (22.5%) had a qualifying arrhythmia diagnosis. In 3,051 holdout patients, XGBoost achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.894 (95% CI 0.879–0.908) and an area under the precision-recall curve of 0.792 (95% CI 0.763–0.822). At a 0.5 threshold, sensitivity was 0.564, specificity 0.971, and precision 0.857. AUROC remained 0.896–0.897 across earlier cutoffs. In the common score-calculable atrial fibrillation/flutter subset ( n = 2,436), AUROCs were 0.883 for XGBoost, 0.712 for CHARGE-AF, and 0.554 for HARMS 2 -AF.

Conclusions

XGBoost demonstrated strong internal discrimination for documented arrhythmias. External validation and prospective evaluation are needed to assess generalizability and clinical utility.

title: Association between pancreatic ectopic fat deposition and QCT-assessed bone mass status in patients with chronic kidney disease: a cross-sectional study.
authorString: Yang J, Wang R, Xue G, Wei J, Wang L.
abstractText:
Background

Patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) are at increased risk of bone abnormalities. Beyond disturbances in mineral metabolism, ectopic fat deposition may also be associated with skeletal abnormalities in CKD. However, the relationship between pancreatic fat and bone mass status remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between mean pancreatic fat fraction and quantitative computed tomography (QCT)-assessed bone mass status in patients with CKD.

Methods

This retrospective cross-sectional study included 327 patients with CKD. Vertebral volumetric bone mineral density was measured using QCT to classify bone mass status as normal bone mass, osteopenia, or osteoporosis. Mean pancreatic fat fraction was quantified from CT images. Ordinal logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS), subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses were performed to evaluate its association with bone mass status.

Results

Mean pancreatic fat fraction was highest in patients with osteoporosis (p < 0.001). In the fully adjusted model, each 5-percentage-point increase in mean pancreatic fat fraction was associated with higher odds of a more severe bone mass category (OR = 1.481, 95% CI: 1.152-1.905, p = 0.002). RCS analysis showed a significant overall association (p = 0.009), with no evidence of nonlinearity (p = 0.290). No statistically significant interactions were detected for sex, age, diabetes status, or CKD stage.

Conclusion

A higher mean pancreatic fat fraction was associated with more severe bone mass categories in patients with CKD after adjustment for the measured covariates. QCT-based pancreatic fat assessment may provide additional information on metabolic features associated with bone mass abnormalities in CKD.

title: Late rupture of a myelomeningocele sac devoid of neural placode associated with good functional outcome 2 years after postnatal repair: illustrative case.
authorString: Lam J, Guberman G, Sahlas E, Veilleux L,  MScA , Altuhayni KS, Cattani A, Farmer DL, Farmer JP.
abstractText:
Background

Neurological deficits in myelomeningocele are driven by a three-hit paradigm: primary myelodysplasia, intrauterine chemotoxic amniotic fluid exposure, and mechanical traction on the neural placode. How sac integrity and rupture timing influence these progressive pathophysiological hits remains poorly understood.

Observations

A neonate presented with a prominent S1 myelomeningocele sac that remained intact until approximately 35 weeks' gestation. Rather than a distinct neural placode, postnatal repair at 36+3 weeks revealed a hairpin loop of functional nerve roots within the myelomeningocele sac that entered and exited via the dorsal defect. A mild Chiari type II malformation was identified only on postnatal imaging. Following postnatal repair, the child demonstrated not only excellent lower extremity motor function as expected, but also excellent urinary sphincter function with no hindbrain herniation or ventriculomegaly 2 years postrepair.

Lessons

This case illustrates a possible "best of both worlds" clinical scenario in which the persistent hydrostatic pressure of the intact sac protected against early hindbrain herniation and direct toxicity, while the structural absence of a neural placode within the sac reduced mechanical stretch injury. Finally, rupture of the myelomeningocele sac only in late gestation minimized chemical toxicity to neural elements. Overall, this case highlights the multifaceted and varied nature of myelomeningocele pathophysiology. https://thejns.org/doi/abs/10.3171/CASE26739.

title: Health Dataspace Technology Acceptance Model (HDS-TAM): Development and Case Evaluation Study of Patient Acceptance of Germany's Electronic Patient Record.
authorString: Vasileva V, Wolf E, Riediger V, Ahmadian AS, Buschmann D, Jürjens J.
abstractText:
Background

The European Health Dataspace (EHDS) expands health data sharing beyond direct care and introduces governance, transparency, trust, and secondary-use considerations that are not fully captured by established technology acceptance models such as the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT). To address this gap, we developed the health dataspace technology acceptance model (HDS-TAM) and evaluated it using the German electronic patient record (ePA) as an illustrative health dataspace (HDS) application.

Objective

This study aimed (1) to derive an HDS-oriented technology acceptance framework from the literature and (2) to assess its applicability in explaining acceptance of the ePA from a patient perspective.

Methods

A structured literature review screened 1788 records, reviewed 134 full-text papers, and retained 68 studies for model development. HDS-TAM was subsequently applied in a scenario-based online survey conducted between March and April 2025. Of 235 questionnaire accesses and 163 submitted responses, 149 valid responses were analyzed. Data were analyzed using multiple imputation, exploratory factor analysis, and partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The association between behavioral intention and actual ePA use was examined using logistic regression.

Results

The model explained 75.9% of the variance in behavioral intention to use (BI, R²=0.759), 67% in perceived usefulness (PU, R²=0.670), and 54% in perceived risk (PR, R²=0.540). PU showed the strongest positive association with BI (β=.670, P<.001, f²=0.457), whereas PR showed a small negative association (β=-.149, P=.04, f²=0.034). Transparency was positively associated with PU (β=.220, P=.001) and perceived ease of use (PEOU; β=.454, P<.001) and negatively associated with PR (β=-.594, P<.001). Perceived need (PN) showed a strong positive association with PU (β=.567, P<.001) but no significant direct association with BI (β=.071, P=.35). Eight of 20 hypotheses were supported. Only 23.5% (n=35) of participants reported actual ePA use. BI showed a positive but imprecise and nonsignificant association with self-reported actual use (OR 1.37, 95% CI 0.89-2.11, P=.15). Measurement quality was mixed: reflective constructs generally showed satisfactory reliability and convergent validity; however, discriminant validity between PU and BI was poor (heterotrait-monotrait ratio of correlations [HTMT]=0.981).

Conclusions

PU showed the strongest association with behavioral intention in the ePA case evaluation, while transparency and PN were mainly associated with behavioral intention through indirect pathways. The findings suggest potential value in extending traditional acceptance models with governance-related constructs relevant to HDSs. However, the severe overlap between PU and behavioral intention, low actual ePA uptake, and the young, highly educated convenience sample limit confidence in the magnitude and distinctiveness of the observed effects. HDS-TAM should therefore be regarded as a promising but preliminary framework requiring further refinement and validation.

title: Cardiometabolic risk burden and associated behaviours in schoolchildren aged 7-10 years from public urban schools in the Federal District, Brazil.
authorString: Diogo SS, Gubert MB, Gonçalves VSS, do Carmo AS, Melo GRDAE, Oliveira GAL, Toral N.
abstractText:
Objective

To assess cardiometabolic risk burden among schoolchildren aged 7-10 years attending public urban elementary schools in the Federal District, Brazil, and examine its association with health behaviours and socioeconomic characteristics.

Methods

This population-based cross-sectional study included 978 children, with a subsample of 315 undergoing biochemical assessment. Data were collected on dietary intake, eating and sedentary behaviours, physical activity, anthropometry, blood pressure, and biochemical markers. A composite cardiometabolic risk outcome was constructed and assessed only in the biochemical subsample. Analyses accounted for the complex sampling design.

Results

Among children included in the biochemical subsample, 89.9% presented at least one cardiometabolic risk factor and dyslipidaemia was present in 72.0%. In the full sample, overweight was observed in 30.2% of the children. Eating with distractions was associated with higher odds of cardiometabolic risk burden, increasing the likelihood of one to two risk factors (odds ratio = 2.98; 95% confidence interval: 1.62-5.47) and three or more risk factors (odds ratio = 2.52; 95% confidence interval:1.08-5.90). Consuming snacks or treats, compared with a homemade meal, was associated with lower odds of presenting one to two risk factors (odds ratio = 0.32; 95% confidence interval: 0.10-0.99), but no association was observed with three or more risk factors.

Conclusions

Within the non-random biochemical subsample of morning-shift students, a high burden of cardiometabolic risk factors was observed, and eating with distractions was associated with greater cardiometabolic risk burden. Early preventive strategies targeting modifiable behaviours are needed.

title: Online co-care management and glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: A propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Sun S, Yang G, Tong H, Zhao H, Liu Q, He Y, Zhang Z.
abstractText:
Objective

This study aimed to investigate the association of an Online Co-care Management (OCCM) model with changes in glycemic control and metabolic indicators among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).

Methods

Based on clinical follow-up records, we conducted a retrospective cohort study with a propensity score (PS)-matched control group.The OCCM group included patients enrolled in the integrated care clinic from 2022 to 2025 (n = 406). Among patients who did not participate in OCCM (n = 199) during the study period, PS-matched controls were selected at a 1:1 ratio.The PS model included age, sex, diabetes duration, smoking, drinking, medication use, and follow-up duration.After matching, 240 patients were included in the final analysis, with 120 patients in each group. Follow-up data were collected at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months. Longitudinal data on anthropometrics, glycemic indices, blood pressure, lipid profiles, and organ function were analyzedusing repeated measures ANOVA.

Results

Over a 6-month follow-up period, HbA1c levels decreased more markedly in the OCCM group compared with the usual-care group. In the OCCM group, HbA1c declined from 7.403 ± 1.748% at baseline to 6.591 ± 0.871% at 3 months and 6.593 ± 1.056% at 6 months, while in the usual-care group, it changed from 6.310 ± 1.277% to 6.225 ± 1.017% and 6.534 ± 1.598%, respectivelyRepeated-measures ANOVA revealed significant time, group, and time × group effects for HbA1c (F = 10.608, P < 0.001; F = 16.748, P < 0.001; F = 14.546, P < 0.001). BMI, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, and lipid profiles, also showed greater improvements in the OCCM group than in controls.

Conclusion

The OCCM model was associated with short-term improvements in glycemic and metabolic indicators among T2DM patients, suggesting it may be an effective approach for structured chronic disease management.

title: Clinical and laboratory determinants of treatment response and rifampicin resistance among Xpert MTB/RIF-confirmed extrapulmonary tuberculosis patients: A prospective study from Central India.
authorString: Bhagwat G, Kanthali M, Chauhan S, Julka A, Chauhan DS, Purohit M.
abstractText: Extrapulmonary tuberculosis (EPTB) contributes significantly to the global tuberculosis burden, yet treatment response and drug resistance remain poorly characterized. India, a high- tuberculosis burden country, faces growing challenges of delayed diagnosis, treatment and drug-resistant tuberculosis, particularly in extrapulmonary forms. This study evaluated early clinical response to therapy and identified factors associated with rifampicin resistance among patients with EPTB. A prospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary care centre in central India between 2018 and 2024. A total of 532 patients with microbiologically confirmed EPTB, based on the Xpert MTB/RIF assay, were included. The study collected baseline demographic, clinical, and laboratory data. Clinical response at 8 weeks was assessed using standardized criteria. Multivariable logistic regression analysis identified factors associated with slow clinical response and rifampicin resistance. A total of 5,764 presumptive EPTB samples were tested using the Xpert MTB/RIF assay. Among these, 532 patients had confirmed EPTB. Rifampicin resistance was detected in 36 patients (6.7%), while 496 patients had rifampicin-sensitive disease and were included in the response analysis. Among these patients, 113 (22.8%) demonstrated slow clinical response. Slow response showed independent association with HIV co-infection, diabetes mellitus, malnutrition, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, prolonged symptom duration, and non-lymph node disease, particularly abdominal and genitourinary tuberculosis. Socioeconomic factors, such as rural residence and lower educational status, also showed independent association. Elevated inflammatory markers, including erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein, showed independent association with slow clinical response. Rifampicin resistance showed independent association with previous tuberculosis, HIV infection, male sex, and disseminated disease. A significant overlap existed between delayed clinical response and drug resistance, as rifampicin resistance occurred more frequently among slow responders than among responders (12.3% vs. 4.1%, p = 0.002). Nearly one-quarter of patients with EPTB demonstrated delayed clinical response at 8 weeks. Both host-related and disease-related factors showed association with treatment response, while rifampicin resistance showed strong association with prior tuberculosis and immunosuppression. The overlap between slow clinical response and drug resistance highlighted the importance of early molecular diagnostics and targeted clinical monitoring in high-risk patients.

title: Female sexual dysfunction in premenopausal women with diabetes mellitus in northern Nigeria: A cross-sectional study from two tertiary hospitals examining associations with glycaemic control and reproductive hormones.
authorString: Damagum FM, Hassan AH, Uloko AE, Habeeb HA, Damagum HB, Umar ZA, Murtala HA, Abdulkadir Z, Ibrahim IY, Ibrahim ZU, Abdullahi UF, Salihu HM, Aliyu MH, Kanki PJ, Musa BM.
abstractText:
Background

Female sexual dysfunction (FSD) is a recognised complication of diabetes mellitus (DM), but evidence on its clinical and biological correlates in sub-Saharan Africa remains limited. FSD is defined as a disorder characterized by disturbances in sexual desire, arousal, orgasm, and/or pain that causes interpersonal difficulty or distress. This study examined associations between glycaemic control, reproductive hormonal status, and FSD among premenopausal women with diabetes in northern Nigeria.

Methods

We conducted a cross-sectional study among 180 premenopausal women aged 18-45 years attending diabetes clinics at two tertiary hospitals in Kano, Nigeria. Sexual function was assessed using the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI), with scores ≤26 indicating FSD. Glycaemic control was measured using glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), categorised as optimal (≤7.0%) or suboptimal (>7.0%). Reproductive hormones (FSH, LH, Oestrogen, testosterone, prolactin, and progesterone) were measured at phase-specific points of the menstrual cycle. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to assess associations with FSD, and linear regression models were used to examine associations with FSFI domain scores.

Results

Overall, 51.7% of participants screened positive for FSD. Suboptimal glycaemic control was associated with higher odds of FSD (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 2.80; 95% CI 1.05-7.72). It was also associated with lower orgasm (β -0.77; p = 0.032) and satisfaction (β -0.88; p = 0.003) scores. No statistically significant associations were observed between reproductive hormonal imbalance (including FSH, LH, Oestrogen, testosterone, prolactin, and progesterone) and FSD or FSFI domain scores.

Conclusions

FSD was common among premenopausal women with diabetes in this setting. Suboptimal glycaemic control was associated with FSD and with lower orgasm and satisfaction scores, while reproductive hormonal measures were not associated with FSD. These findings provide evidence on clinical correlates of FSD in a sub-Saharan African population.
