title: Plasma Osteoprotegerin and Cardiovascular Mortality During the First Two Years of Maintenance Hemodialysis: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study.
authorString: Nguyen HD, Hoang AT, Nguyen TK, Le VT.
abstractText:
Aim

We performed this study to determine the cardiovascular-cause mortality rate and the predictive value of the plasma osteoprotegerin (OPG) concentration for cardiovascular-cause mortality in patients with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) undergoing maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) during the first 2 years.

Methods

We performed a prospective observational cohort study of 218 ESKD patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis from September 2021 to September 2025. Plasma OPG concentrations were quantified using a colorimetric measurement method based on ELISA method. Cardiovascular-cause mortality data were collected over 2 years of follow-up. All patients were divided into 2 groups: the survival group (n = 187) and the mortality group (n = 31).

Results

The incidence of cardiovascular-cause mortality was 14.2% over 2 years of follow-up. Compared with survivors, patients who died from cardiovascular causes had significantly lower HDL-C levels and higher PTH, hs-CRP, and OPG levels (p < 0.001). In multivariable Cox regression analysis, higher OPG levels were independently associated with increased cardiovascular mortality (HR = 1.050, p < 0.001). OPG showed good discriminatory performance for cardiovascular mortality (AUC = 0.828, p < 0.001), and Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly higher mortality among patients with OPG levels > 47.95 pmol/L (log-rank p < 0.001).

Conclusion

The cardiovascular-cause mortality rate during the first 2 years of maintenance hemodialysis was 14.2%. Plasma OPG levels are associated with cardiovascular mortality, suggesting its potential as a useful biomarker for risk stratification in ESKD patients.

title: Prognostic Value of the Frailty Index in Patients with Severe Aortic Regurgitation Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
authorString: Yu Q, Fu Q, Cheng Z, Feng J, Huang X, Gong R, Xu H, Wu Y, Wu Y.
abstractText:
Background

Frailty represents a multidimensional vulnerability that predicts poor outcomes in cardiovascular disease. Its prognostic value in patients with severe native aortic regurgitation (AR) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is not well defined.

Objective

To determine whether an abbreviated cumulative deficit frailty index predicts one-year all-cause mortality and to explore its interaction with N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide in this population.

Methods

In this post hoc analysis of the prospective China DVD2 multicenter cohort, 298 patients with isolated severe AR who underwent TAVR were included. Frailty was assessed preprocedurally using an abbreviated 8-9-item cumulative deficit frailty index (FI) encompassing functional, cognitive, nutritional, and clinical domains. The primary endpoint was one-year all-cause mortality. The cohort-derived FI threshold for mortality was derived using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis. Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, atrial fibrillation, and NT-proBNP were applied. Subgroup and interaction analyses were performed.

Results

The cohort-derived FI threshold was 0.407, classifying 32 patients as high frailty. High-FI patients exhibited greater symptom burden, higher prevalence of atrial fibrillation, larger left atrial diameter, and elevated NT-proBNP. One-year mortality was significantly higher in the high-FI group compared with low-FI patients (15.6% vs 3.4%, P = 0.010). High FI was associated with higher one-year mortality in Model 3 (HR 4.00, 95% CI 1.18-13.50; P = 0.026). No significant multiplicative or additive interaction with NT-proBNP was observed.

Conclusions

Among patients undergoing TAVR for severe native aortic regurgitation, a high FI was associated with higher one-year mortality. These findings extend prior evidence on the prognostic implications of frailty to this understudied population.

title: Extracellular ATP Signaling as a Proposed Mechanistic Link to Cellular Senescence in Cardiovascular Diseases.
authorString: Liu X, Zhang J, Lu J, Hu Z, Wei H, Li L, Yang Y, Liu J, Li Z, Zhang H, Zhang W.
abstractText: Cellular senescence represents a critical pathological process involved in the progression of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). Senescent endothelial cells, cardiomyocytes, vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), and immune cells can promote inflammatory responses, oxidative stress, extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation, and fibrotic remodeling through the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Beyond its fundamental role in intracellular energy metabolism, adenosine triphosphate (ATP) can also be released into the extracellular environment under conditions such as ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI), mechanical stress, inflammatory stimulation, and cellular damage, where it participates in cellular stress responses through P2X/P2Y purinergic receptors. This article proposes the hypothesis that ATP-induced cellular senescence (AICS) contributes to CVD progression, suggesting that sustained or abnormally enhanced extracellular ATP signaling may promote cardiovascular cell senescence through disruption of Ca<sup>2</sup>⁺ homeostasis, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, activation of DNA damage response (DDR) pathways, NLRP3 inflammasome activation, enhanced NF-κB signaling, and persistent maintenance of the SASP. However, ATP signaling is highly dependent on its concentration, exposure duration, receptor subtype, and cellular context, and therefore cannot be simply regarded as a pro-senescence signal. Further studies using CVD-specific models and human pathological samples are required to establish the causal relationship among ATP/P2 receptor activation, cellular senescence burden, and disease progression.

title: Predictive Value of P-Wave Dispersion Combined with Left Atrial Reservoir Strain for Incident Atrial Fibrillation in Patients with Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Yu L, Zhang Y, Sun D, Hou A, Xia F.
abstractText:
Purpose

Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common arrhythmia in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). This study aimed to investigate the associations of P-wave dispersion (PD) and left atrial reservoir strain (LASr) with incident AF.

Methods

This single-center retrospective cohort study included 165 consecutive patients with HCM who were diagnosed at Liaoning Provincial People's Hospital from January 2018 to January 2026. Independent predictors of incident AF were identified using multivariable Cox regression. Model performance was assessed using a nomogram, time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis.

Results

During a median follow-up of 1.79 years, 56 (33.9%) patients developed incident AF. PD (P=0.025) and LASr (P=0.028) were independently associated with incident AF. The combined PD + LASr model showed AUCs of 0.766, 0.764, and 0.823 at 1, 2, and 3 years, respectively. The model showed good calibration at 3 years and positive net benefit across clinically relevant threshold probabilities. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed a significantly higher cumulative incidence of AF in the high-risk group than in the low-risk group (log-rank P<0.001).

Conclusion

PD and LASr are independently associated with AF risk in patients with HCM, and their combination may improve AF risk assessment.

title: Pregnancy after transcatheter closure of atrial septal defects: safety and clinical outcomes.
authorString: Trojanowicz K, Prochownik P, Tworek M, Sachajko Z, Bielecka K, Gancarczyk U, Sobień B, Bielecka L, Komar M.

journal.title: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology

abstractText:
Introduction

In recent years, there has been rapid development of minimally invasive cardiovascular procedures, such as atrial septal defect (ASD) transcatheter closure. Many female patients of reproductive age have undergone this procedure, but evidence regarding pregnancy outcomes after transcatheter closure of ASD remains limited.

Aim

Our aim was to assess maternal and fetal outcomes and investigate the magnitude and determinants of obstetric complications in patients after transcatheter closure of an ASD.

Material and methods

We analyzed 130 women with an average age of 28.6 ±9.1 years (19-44) who underwent ASD transcatheter closure using the Amplatzer Septal Occluder. Detailed records of each pregnancy (n = 130), occurring an average of 18.2 ±4.1 months (11-35) after transcatheter closure, were analyzed. Cardiac events were defined as heart failure exacerbation, stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), arrhythmias, or endocarditis; obstetric events as pregnancy-induced hypertension (PIH), preeclampsia, HELLP syndrome, premature labor, or postpartum hemorrhage; neonatal events as premature delivery, small-for-gestational age, or fetal or neonatal morbidity or mortality.

Results

Cardiac events were observed during 20.8% (n = 27) of pregnancies and included supraventricular arrhythmias (n = 24, 18.5%) and severe peripheral edema (n = 3, 2.3%). Obstetric events occurred in 22 (16.9%) patients. Neonatal events complicated only 2 (1.5%) pregnancies.

Conclusions

Most pregnancies after transcatheter ASD closure with the Amplatzer Septal Occluder were completed successfully, with favorable obstetric and neonatal outcomes. Maternal complications were more common among women aged over 30 years.

title: Neonatal Mortality in a High-Risk Tertiary Referral Center in Southern Turkiye: A 5-Year Retrospective Descriptive Study.
authorString: Gulasi S, Coskun H, Cekinmez EK.
abstractText:
Objective

To evaluate neonatal mortality rates and causes of death and describe the clinical and demographic characteristics of non-surviving infants admitted to a tertiary referral neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) in southern Türkiye.

Materials and methods

This retrospective descriptive study included all neonates admitted to the NICU who died between January 2019 and August 2024. Demographic characteristics, perinatal and maternal risk factors, neonatal morbidities, severity scores (Score for Neonatal Acute Physiology, Score for Neonatal Acute Physiology with Perinatal Extension II, and Vasoactive-Inotropic Score [VIS]), and causes of death were analyzed.

Results

During the study period, 4339 infants were admitted to the NICU, and 631 deaths were recorded, corresponding to an overall mortality rate of 14.5%. The majority of deaths occurred in preterm infants (83%), particularly those born at <26-week gestation (39%). Most deaths (61.8%) occurred within the first 7 days of life. Major congenital anomalies were present in 27.7% of infants, and severe congenital heart disease in 8.3%. The most common causes of death were severe congenital malformations (27.7%), extreme prematurity (11.8%), and early-onset sepsis (12%). Among infants receiving inotropic support, 32.8% had a VIS > 20, indicating significant hemodynamic instability. Exclusion of infants with conditions incompatible with life reduced the mortality rate to 13.8%.

Conclusion

Neonatal mortality was primarily driven by extreme prematurity, major congenital anomalies, and sepsis. Elevated disease severity scores, particularly VIS, reflected substantial hemodynamic burden among non-survivors. Mortality rates in referral NICUs may be influenced by patient complexity, referral burden, and treatment limitation practices.

title: Tricuspid valve leaflet multiplicity and Doppler-derived right-heart hemodynamic trajectories after surgical repair.
authorString: Iwakura T, Kitamura M, Nakahara Y, Kishiki K, Izumi Y, Ono M, Yano A, Sumi K, Marui A, Noack T, Takamisawa I, Nanasato M, Shimizu J, Isobe M.
abstractText:
Objective

To determine whether tricuspid leaflet multiplicity is associated with divergent postoperative hemodynamic trajectories after surgical repair.

Methods

One hundred seventeen patients undergoing tricuspid valve surgery (January 2023 to March 2025) were prospectively enrolled, with leaflet morphology classified by intraoperative visualization and serial echocardiography over 1 year. The prespecified primary end point was a Doppler-derived tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient (TRPG) increase, defined as a 5-mm Hg-or-greater increase in TRPG from discharge to 1 year.

Results

Among 100 patients with paired data, the primary end point occurred more frequently in the 4/5-leaflet group despite similar residual tricuspid regurgitation (TR) and discharge TRPG (48.5% vs 26.9%; odds ratio, 2.56; 95% CI, 1.07-6.12; P = .034); the age-adjusted association was borderline (aOR, 2.39; P = .054) and the within-group rise significant only in that cohort (P = .024). Severe-or-greater TR recurrence was rare (3.0% vs 0.0%; P = .327). Discharge tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion was lower in the 4/5-leaflet group (0.96 ± 0.36 vs 1.15 ± 0.36 cm; P = .010) but converged by 1 year (P = .585).

Conclusions

Tricuspid leaflet multiplicity was associated with a subphenotype showing preserved early TR reduction, lower discharge tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion, and a greater 1-year frequency of Doppler-derived TRPG increase. Morphology-based stratification may refine postoperative surveillance pending external validation.

title: Two decades of targeted pulmonary artery banding in pediatric dilated cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Logeswaran T, Steinbrenner B, Schranz D, Recla S, Klingel K, Müller M, Gummel K, Rüblinger L, Reich B, Farr M, Jux C, Akintürk H.
abstractText:
Objectives

Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) with severe left ventricular (LV) dysfunction in infants and young children is a life-threatening condition and carries a high risk of mechanical circulatory support and heart transplantation (HTx). Pulmonary artery banding (PAB) has been proposed as a recovery strategy, but data on medium- and long-term outcomes remain limited.

Methods

This retrospective, single-center observational study included infants and young children who underwent surgical PAB between 2006 and 2024. Inclusion criteria were ROSS functional class (FC) III/IV, spherical left ventricular-dilated cardiomyopathy (LV-DCM) with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) <35%, and left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD) z-score >+4 with preserved right ventricular function. Primary endpoints were overall survival and transplant-free recovery, defined as sustained normalization of LV systolic function with reverse remodeling.

Results

Fifty patients (27 female) met the inclusion criteria and underwent PAB at a median age of 188 days, 70% were in ROSS FC IV, and 42% were listed as urgent for HTx. DCM etiology was idiopathic in 42%, genetic in 22%, and myocarditis-associated in 36%. There was no procedural mortality. Overall survival was 90% and 72% achieved transplant-free functional recovery. Following PAB, magnetic resonance imaging-derived LVEF improved from 19% ± 7% to 56% ± 11%, and LVEDD z-scores decreased from +6.3 to +1 (P < .001). In 33 patients, recovery was sustained over a median follow-up of 7 years, including 15 patients with stable LV function for over 10 years.

Conclusions

In infants and young children with severe LV-DCM, PAB is associated with high long-term survival, sustained transplant-free recovery, and durable reverse cardiac remodeling.

title: Impact of nocturnal oxygen saturation on sleep quality and exercise performance in adult Fontan patients.
authorString: Schön P, Boyle KGPJM, Beltrami FG, Greutmann M, Spengler CM.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Int J Cardiol Congenit Heart Dis
journal.title: International journal of cardiology. Congenital heart disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Int J Cardiol Congenit Heart Dis

abstractText:
Introduction

A decreased peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2) is common in Fontan patients. We aimed to determine whether these patients experience greater nocturnal desaturation (ΔSpO2,noct), and to which extent this may impact sleep quality and exercise performance, compared to healthy controls.

Methods

16 adult Fontan patients and 16 healthy, individually matched controls completed questionnaires on quality of life, sleep quality, and daytime sleepiness, performed measurements of lung function and diffusion capacity (DLCO), and cycled in a cardiopulmonary exercise test to volitional exhaustion. Sleep quality was assessed with a wrist-worn actigraph and nocturnal SpO2 was measured with a pulse oximeter during six nights.

Results

Fontan patients experienced greater ΔSpO2,noct (-3.4 ± 0.8%-points, n = 14) compared to their controls (-2.5 ± 0.6%-points, n = 14, p = 0.001). In patients, ΔSpO2,noct correlated with baseline SpO2, DLCO, and exercise performance. Fontan patients had a longer sleep onset latency (22.8 ± 9.6 vs. 10.8 ± 6.0 min, p < 0.001) and lower self-perceived physical functioning (91 ± 7 vs. 100 ± 0 points, p < 0.001), but similar subjective sleep quality (4.2 ± 1.5 vs. 3.4 ± 1.4 points, p = 0.121) and daytime sleepiness (6.1 ± 4.3 vs. 6.3 ± 2.8 points, p = 0.884) compared to controls. In patients, daytime sleepiness correlated with the total number of desaturation events (r = 0.74, p = 0.003).

Conclusion

Indices of nocturnal SpO2 were related to daytime sleepiness and reduced exercise performance, and may therefore be a contributing factor to exercise limitation in adult Fontan patients. Enhancing nocturnal SpO2 may thus be a promising target to improve daytime sleepiness and exercise performance in adult Fontan patients.

title: Atrioventricular septal defect and aortic arch obstruction: A challenging combination.
authorString: Villar S, Lu A, Wu TT, Doan TT, Olarinde T, Cho J, Clunie SK, Imamura M, Heinle JS, Orr Y.
abstractText:
Objective

The combination of atrioventricular septal defect and aortic arch obstruction (AVSD-AAO) is rare and associated with significant morbidity and mortality. We characterized our institutional experience to identify variables influencing the surgical strategy and outcomes in this heterogeneous patient population.

Methods

A retrospective review was performed on all patients undergoing biventricular AVSD repair at Texas Children's Hospital between January 1995 and August 2024. Patients with AVSD-AAO were identified and stratified by age at first intervention (neonates vs infants) and surgical strategy (staged vs concurrent repair). Kaplan-Meier survival estimates, competing risks analysis, and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests were employed in statistical analysis.

Results

Of 790 AVSD patients, 33 (4.2%) had concurrent AAO. Compared to AVSD without AAO, AVSD-AAO patients had significantly higher cumulative incidence of a left atrioventricular valve reoperation (32.2% vs 14.4%, P = .0006), left ventricular outflow flow tract obstruction repair (18% vs 4.7%, P = .0015), and the mortality (15-year survival, 77.6% vs 94.2%, P < .0001). Staged repair with an initial arch repair followed by AVSD repair trended toward improved survival compared to concurrent repair (87.8% vs 67.0%, P = .13). Survival was not different between patients who underwent an initial intervention as neonates versus infants (81.9% vs 73.3%, P = .50).

Conclusions

AVSD-AAO carries substantially higher rates of reoperation and mortality compared with AVSD alone. AAO is the primary driver of surgical timing due to the frequent duct-dependent systemic blood flow; however, neonatal AVSD repair is challenging. Temporizing surgical interventions that optimize systemic and pulmonary blood flow may allow for somatic growth, the valve maturation, and the normalization of pulmonary vascular resistance prior to definitive repair.

title: The interaction of age and time on durable left ventricular assist device and its effect on heart transplant outcomes.
authorString: Sollie ZW, Kwon JH, Miller CC, Zhang J, Welch BA, Inampudi C, Kilic A.
abstractText:
Objective

This study aims to assess the interaction between age and left ventricular assist device duration on heart transplant outcomes in the modern era.

Methods

All heart transplantation in adults with a fully magnetically levitated centrifugal flow left ventricular assist device between October 2018 and June 2025 were identified from the United Network for Organ Sharing database. Groups were stratified primarily by age less than 55 years and 55 years or more and secondarily by age less than 2 years and 2 years or more of left ventricular assist device support. The primary outcome was post-heart transplant survival.

Results

A total of 1005 patients were aged less than 55 years, with 608 having a left ventricular assist device for less than 2 years and 397 having a left ventricular assist device for 2 years or more. There was no significant difference in post-heart transplant survival between left ventricular assist device duration groups at 90 days (95.3% vs 94.4%, P = .57), 1 year (93.7% vs 90.2%, P = .07), or 3 years (88.0% vs 83.9%, P = .061). A total of 1411 patients were aged 55 years or more, with 935 having a left ventricular assist device for less than 2 years and 476 having a left ventricular assist device for 2 years or more. Patients having a left ventricular assist device for less than 2 years exhibited improved survival at 90 days (92.4% vs 89.2%, P = .046), 1 year (87.8% vs 81.9%, P = .0051), and 3 years (81.4% vs 72.7%, P = .0011). Multivariable adjustment showed a significant impact of age 55 years or more on post-heart transplant mortality (hazard ratio, 1.96; 95% CI, 1.34-2.86; P < .001); however, having a left ventricular assist device for 2 years or more showed no significant impact (hazard ratio, 1.47; 95% CI, 0.91-2.36; P = .116). Formal testing revealed no significant interaction of age and left ventricular assist device duration (hazard ratio, 1.1; 95% CI, 0.63-1.91; P = .735).

Conclusions

Although there is a lower observed post-heart transplant survival in patients aged 55 years or more and supported by a left ventricular assist device for 2 years or more, formal testing reveals no significant interaction of these variables on mortality.

title: Risk factors and outcomes of tricuspid valve surgery in hypoplastic left heart syndrome patients with tricuspid regurgitation.
authorString: Cordoves EM, Ramos-Lemos G, LaSala VR, Beqaj H, Trackey P, Goldstone AB, Levasseur S, Shah A, Krishnamurthy G, Bacha EA, Kalfa DM.
abstractText:
Objective

The management of patients with hypoplastic left heart syndrome with tricuspid regurgitation remains controversial. We evaluate risk factors for mortality/transplant/Fontan takedown in patients with hypoplastic left heart syndrome with tricuspid regurgitation and the effect of tricuspid valve surgery on clinical trajectories.

Methods

A retrospective chart review was performed for all hypoplastic left heart syndrome primary surgical Norwood recipients at our center who had moderate or greater tricuspid regurgitation (2006-2023). Freedom from a primary outcome of combined mortality/transplant/Fontan takedown was compared between those who underwent tricuspid valve surgery (N = 30, 67%) and those who did not (N = 15, 33%; Cox regression, log-rank). Among those who developed tricuspid regurgitation anytime post-Norwood (N = 37), tricuspid valve repair efficacy was assessed (Wilcoxon signed-rank, McNemar's test). Cumulative incidence of recurrent tricuspid regurgitation and right ventricle dysfunction was estimated (Aalen-Johansen estimator, death/transplant as competing risks).

Results

Patients with pre-Norwood tricuspid regurgitation experienced a mortality-dominated trajectory (5-year freedom from mortality 37.5%), whereas patients with post-Norwood/pre-Glenn tricuspid regurgitation experienced a transplant-dominated trajectory (5-year freedom from mortality 88.5%, composite outcome 55.9%). On univariable Cox regression, pre-Norwood right ventricle dysfunction (hazard ratio, 9.75, P < .001) was associated with the primary outcome; pre-Norwood tricuspid regurgitation tended toward association (hazard ratio, 2.40, P = .10). On multivariable analysis, pre-Norwood right ventricle dysfunction (hazard ratio, 12.79 [3.16-51.80], P < .001) and pre-Norwood tricuspid regurgitation (hazard ratio, 3.10 [1.03-9.31], P = .04) were both independently associated with the primary outcome. Among those with post-Norwood tricuspid regurgitation who underwent tricuspid valve surgery, tricuspid regurgitation severity decreased, with 43% achieving preserved freedom from moderate or greater tricuspid regurgitation.

Conclusions

Pre-Norwood right ventricle dysfunction and pre-Norwood tricuspid regurgitation were found to be associated with the primary outcome. In those with post-Norwood tricuspid regurgitation, tricuspid valve repair reduced tricuspid regurgitation but was not associated with improved survival.

title: Compliments to the surgeon: An artificial intelligence-based analysis of online patient reviews on cardiac surgical care in the United States.
authorString: Dogan MM, Sears SF, Sarrazin V, Dejanovic D, Sargeant MM, Oehlert J, Taylor JG, Kilic A, Akhter SA, Bates MJ, Boyd WD, Nifong WL, Degner BC.
abstractText:
Objective

Patients increasingly describe care in their own words on public review platforms, but this evidence has been too large and unstructured to use. We aimed to develop and validate a reproducible artificial intelligence (AI)-based method to make this source usable and apply it to cardiac surgery.

Methods

Patient comments on online platforms (2020-2026) were collected. Cardiac surgery comments were identified by registered specialty or, where absent, by key word filtering and AI classification (Claude API [Anthropic], validated by physician, 95% sensitivity, and 85% specificity). Sentiment and praise and complaint themes were classified by the same approach and validated by a psychologist (91% accuracy). Cardiac surgery was compared against 4 noncardiac surgery groups, and 6 cardiac surgery subgroups were compared using Wilcoxon rank-sum tests for comment ratings and χ2 tests for theme comparisons.

Results

Of 28.8 million comments, 14,678 cardiac surgery comments were identified. Sentiment was positive in 82%. Cardiac surgery rated higher than every noncardiac comparator, including clinically comparable specialties (4.31 vs 4.13; P < .001). The most common complaints were interpersonal (unprofessionalism, coldness, dismissiveness, and poor communication), whereas surgical complications ranked sixth. Among subgroups, aortic surgery alone rated significantly higher; transplant patients showed uniquely lower praise across themes, whereas congenital surgery combined elevated gratitude with the only elevated complaint theme.

Conclusions

Patients describe cardiac surgical care with overwhelming gratitude and rate it above every comparator group examined. Where they voice dissatisfaction, it centers on how patients are treated as people rather than on the surgical outcomes, identifying communication as the principal target for improvement.

title: Right Atrial Cardiac Fibroma Mimicking Eustachian Valve Endocarditis in Neutropenic Sepsis: A Diagnostic Challenge.
authorString: Prescott M, Zwischenberger BA, Bloomfield GS, Alenezi F, Demis J, Cosiano M, Hitt A, Lushniak L, Shah NP.
abstractText:
Background

Management of an undifferentiated right atrial (RA) mass in a septic, immunocompromised patient is challenging when imaging and microbiologic data are discordant.

Case summary

A 51-year-old kidney transplant recipient presented with neutropenic sepsis and a newly identified RA mass. Transesophageal echocardiography suggested eustachian valve endocarditis, whereas cardiac magnetic resonance imaging favored thrombus. Percutaneous aspiration, performed for therapeutic debulking, incidentally failed to mobilize the mass, suggesting firm adherence and low embolic potential. This informed discontinuation of poorly tolerated anticoagulation and deferral of high-risk surgery. Elective resection 2 months later revealed a cardiac fibroma.

Discussion

Evidence guiding management of indeterminate RA masses is limited. Resistance to aspiration may provide functional information about embolic risk.

Take-home messages

RA fibromas can mimic thrombus or endocarditis, particularly in septic, immunocompromised patients. In select patients already undergoing percutaneous aspiration, incidental procedural resistance may indicate stability and lower embolic risk.

title: Postoperative chylothorax following congenital heart surgery: Incidence, risks, therapy, and possible mechanisms.
authorString: Schaeffer T, Kunke V, Palm J, Amici A, Lemmen T, Ruda C, Piber N, Matsubara M, Heinisch PP, Hager A, Ewert P, Hörer J, Ono M.
abstractText:
Objective

To determine the incidence, risks factors, outcomes, and mechanisms of postoperative chylothorax (PCT) following congenital heart surgery.

Methods

Among all patients who underwent congenital heart surgery between 2001 and 2024, those who developed PCT during the same hospitalization were identified. The prevalence of chylothorax was analyzed, along with associated procedures, risk factors, and hemodynamics.

Results

Among 9892 congenital heart surgeries performed during the study period, 312 patients (3.2%) developed PCT. Patients with PCT had a higher proportion of males (64% vs 56%; P = .009), younger age at surgery (median, 0.6 years vs 1.2 years; P < .001), and lower weight at surgery (median, 6.1 kg vs 8.6 kg; P < .001) compared to those without PCT. Regarding surgical types, the most frequently performed operation was the Fontan procedure (20.5%), followed by repair of tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) with atrioventricular septal defect (11.8%), arterial switch operation (ASO), ventricular septal defect (VSD) closure, and aortic arch repair (10.0%). Younger age at operation (P < .001; hazard ratio [HR], 0.745), the Fontan procedure (P < .001; HR, 16.198), ASO, VSD closure, and aortic arch repair (P < .001; HR, 2.835) were strong risk factors for PCT. Postoperative lower mean arterial pressure and higher central venous pressure were associated with PCT in patients following the Fontan procedure and TOF repair.

Conclusions

This large, single-center study of approximately 10,000 congenital heart surgeries reported a 3.2% incidence of PCT. The Fontan procedure had the highest incidence of PCT, followed by complex biventricular repair in neonates and young infants. Early postoperative lower mean arterial pressure and higher central venous pressure may trigger PCT.

title: Health-Related Quality of Life and Psychiatric Morbidity at Follow-up After Catheter Ablation in Children with Supraventricular Tachycardia.
authorString: Doğaç T, Elkıran Ö, Maraş SA, Öncül M, Doğan Ö.
abstractText: Background: This study aimed to evaluate health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and psychiatric outcomes in children and adolescents with supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) during the post-ablation follow-up period. Methods: This retrospective-prospective observational cohort study included pediatric patients who underwent successful catheter ablation for supraventricular tachycardia. Clinical and procedural data were collected retrospectively. Pre-ablation HRQoL data were obtained from either documented pre-procedural assessments or caregiver recall when records were unavailable. Psychiatric interviews and post-ablation HRQoL assessments were conducted prospectively during a single follow-up evaluation. Results: A total of 59 pediatric patients participated in the follow-up evaluation and were included in the study; the median age was 13.0 years (Q1-Q3, 10.0-15.0). Depending on the HRQoL domain, paired pre- and post-ablation data were available for 53 or 54 participants. Follow-up scores for physical, emotional, social, and school functioning were higher than the retrospectively obtained pre-ablation reference scores (all p < .001; Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold, p < .0125). At follow-up, at least 1 DSM-5 psychiatric diagnosis was identified in 18 participants (30.5%), most commonly anxiety and depressive disorders. Seven of these participants had 2 or more concurrent psychiatric diagnoses. Conclusion: Pediatric patients had higher HRQoL scores at post-ablation follow-up, and 30.5% met criteria for at least 1 psychiatric diagnosis. The HRQoL comparisons should be interpreted cautiously because baseline data were obtained from a combination of medical records and caregiver recall, informants were not fully standardized across assessment periods, and the exact interval between ablation and follow-up could not be reliably reconstructed.

title: Clinical characteristics and risk factors for poor prognosis of RSV lower respiratory tract infection: a two-center study.
authorString: Chen T, Guo X, Tang W, Liu F, Jv J, Sun H.
abstractText:
Objective

Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) in children under five years of age. In this study, we investigated the value of simple and readily available clinical indicators in predicting poor prognosis in children with RSV-LRTI.

Methods

This was a retrospective cohort study of children with RSV-LRTI admitted to Children's Hospital of Nanjing Medical University (April 2023-May 2024) and Gaoyou People's Hospital (December 2024-June 2025). Demographic and clinical data were collected from patient records, and patients were stratified based on three adverse prognostic events: admission to Intensive Care Unit (ICU), prolonged hospital stay, and severe pneumonia.

Results

A total of 257 eligible children were enrolled, of whom 254 (98.8%) exhibited cough, 144 (56.0%) presented with wheezing and 194 (75.4%) developed febrile symptoms. 220 (85.6%) cases of RSV-LRTI occurred in winter and spring, with a higher proportion of cases occurring in infants under 1 year of age. A higher respiratory rate at admission was independently associated with ICU admission (Firth regression: OR 1.132, both P < 0.05), though this finding was limited by the small number of ICU cases. The presence of three concave sign was independently associated with prolonged hospital stay (OR 5.242, 95% CI 1.360-19.951, P = 0.017). Procalcitonin (PCT) was an independent risk factor for severe pneumonia (OR 1.616, 95% CI 1.074-2.837, P = 0.020).

Conclusion

Higher respiratory rate at admission was independently associated with ICU admission, and the presence of three concave sign was independently associated with prolonged hospital stay. PCT was an independent risk factor for severe pneumonia. These simple clinical indicators facilitate early identification of children at risk of adverse outcomes.

title: Parental experiences of death preparedness at the end of life of their children: a qualitative meta-synthesis.
authorString: Li X, Yang L, Feng Z, Ma Y.
abstractText:
Objective

This study aimed to synthesize existing qualitative evidence on how parents experience and navigate death preparedness when facing the impending loss of a child, and to identify key challenges and support needs relevant to clinical practice.

Methods

A qualitative meta-synthesis was conducted using Thomas and Harden's thematic synthesis approach. Databases including PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, PsycINFO, CNKI, and VIP were systematically searched from inception to May 28, 2026.

Results

Seventeen studies were included. Eleven descriptive subthemes were identified and further organized into five analytical themes. (1) Oscillation Between Awareness and Avoidance, (2) Forced Urgent Preparation Crises, (3) Needs for Prognostic Information on the Dying Trajectory, (4) Rejection of Preparation Alone, (5) Construction of Meaning in the Face of Inevitable Loss.

Conclusion

Death preparedness among parents is a dynamic, nonlinear, and relational process. Clinical support should move beyond promoting acceptance alone and instead focus on reducing decisional burden, improving communication, providing practical guidance, and supporting relational and meaning-making processes.

title: The prescription profiles of Chinese patent medicine in Internet hospitals in China: a retrospective cross-sectional study.
authorString: Hu J, Zuo JX, Zhou TT, Meng RG, Zhuo L, Liu GZ, Wang D, Wang SF, Liao X.
abstractText:
Background

Chinese patent medicine (CPM) is widely used in China's rapidly expanding Internet hospital system, yet its prescribing profiles in this setting remain uncharacterized.

Methods

Prescription data were collected from 87 enterprise-led Internet hospitals between January 1, 2018, and March 31, 2021. Visits involving at least one prescribed CPM were included. Descriptive analyses characterized the top 20 most frequently prescribed CPMs overall, with stratification by gender and age groups. The top three CPMs for diseases with over 20,000 visits were identified, and the results were visualized using a sunburst chart.

Results

Among 2,065,486 eligible visits, the respiratory diseases category was the most prevalent (26.29%), with acute upper respiratory tract infection (n = 319,772) as the top diagnosis, commonly treated with CPMs like Niuhuang Jiedu Tablet. Genitourinary diseases (23.43%) were also prominent, with Honghe Fujie Cleansing Lotion being the most prescribed CPM overall (3.77%), accounting for 15.2% of prescriptions for adult females. For chronic disease management, digestive (19.12%) and circulatory system (13.14%) diseases were common. Elderly patients (≥ 60 years) frequently received CPMs for cardiovascular conditions (18.9%, e.g., Wenxin Granule, Suxiao Jiuxin Pill). Age stratification showed pediatric patients (< 18 years) were primarily prescribed CPMs for respiratory infections (48.0%), while patients in the 18-44 years age group commonly used CPMs for gynecological and dermatological conditions.

Conclusions

Among visits that included at least one CPM prescription, CPM was extensively prescribed via Internet hospitals in China for acute respiratory infections, urogenital, and chronic conditions, with notable coverage also observed among pediatric and elderly populations. Our findings suggest that this model may enable contactless care, provide discreet consultation channels for urogenital conditions, and facilitate medication access for patients with stable chronic diseases.

title: Prevalence, patterns, and correlates of non-communicable disease multimorbidity among healthcare workers: a multicenter study from Bangladesh.
authorString: Haque MA, Basher AK, Yeamin A, Islam MT, Siraj MS, Chowdhury F, Hassan MZ.
abstractText:
Background

Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are an increasing public health concern in low- and middle-income countries, including Bangladesh. Limited data exist on NCD prevalence and multimorbidity among HCWs in Bangladesh. This study aimed to assess the prevalence, patterns, and factors associated with multimorbidity among Bangladeshi HCWs.

Methods

We conducted a cross-sectional study (July 2021-March 2024) among HCWs in purposively selected 13 primary, 2 secondary, and 5 tertiary healthcare facilities across 4 administrative divisions in Bangladesh. HCWs were interviewed using a structured questionnaire covering socio-demographics, NCDs, and anthropometric measurements. Data were summarized using frequencies and percentages, and the factors associated with multimorbidity were assessed with two separate multivariable binary logistic regression models.

Results

We enrolled 2,881 HCWs, of whom 63% were female. Almost half of the respondents were aged 30-44 years, and the median age was 36 years (IQR 30-46 years). The overall prevalence of having at least one NCD was 1,162 (40%), with multimorbidity in 708 (25%) of the respondents. The most prevalent NCDs among HCWs were hypertension at 612 (21%), followed by diabetes at 409 (14%), chronic lung disease at 323 (11%), dyslipidemia at 160 (6%), and heart disease at 111 (3%). However, multimorbidity was derived from both objectively measured and self-reported conditions, which should be considered in interpreting prevalence estimates. Factors associated with multimorbidity included age ≥ 45 years (AOR: 35.2, 95% CI: 22.3-55.7) compared to individuals without NCDs (Model 1) and (AOR: 5.5, 95% CI: 3.2-9.6) compared to individuals with a single NCD (Model 2). Other associated factors, compared with individuals without NCDs (Model 1), included female (AOR: 1.8, 95% CI: 1.3-2.4), central obesity (AOR: 2.8, 95% CI: 1.9-4.0), higher education (AOR: 1.9, 95% CI: 1.1-3.2), and employment at tertiary healthcare facilities (AOR: 1.9, 95% CI: 1.4-2.7).

Conclusion

Our study highlights a high burden of NCDs among HCWs in Bangladesh, with one in four HCWs experiencing multimorbidity. Older age (≥ 45 years), female, central obesity, higher education, and employment in tertiary healthcare facilities were associated with increased odds of multimorbidity. These findings underscore the need for targeted interventions, including workplace health programs, routine health screenings, and strategies to promote healthier lifestyles, to improve HCWs' health and ensure a resilient healthcare system.

title: Emanuel syndrome: a physiotherapy overview.
authorString: Ansari SF, Mohamed MA, Panattuparambil AD, Sasidharan AP, Rahma A.
abstractText:
Background

Emanuel syndrome is a rare chromosomal disorder arising from an unbalanced translocation between chromosomes 11 and 22, leading to severe developmental delays, and multisystem impairments. Physiotherapy supports motor function in affected children.

Case report/results

An 8-year-old boy with Emanuel syndrome, received five physiotherapy sessions targeting strengthening, trunk control, and balance, with exercises also engaging lower-limb flexibility as part of functional movement practice. Improvements were observed in dynamic sitting balance, calf flexibility, and hand function, before therapy was discontinued.

Conclusion

Individualized physiotherapy can provide meaningful gains, though limited adherence restricts long-term assessment. Greater awareness and timely multidisciplinary care remain important for optimising functional outcomes.

title: Genetic diagnostic yield of prenatal testing for fetal central nervous system abnormalities: a phenotype-driven study in a large single-center cohort.
authorString: Fu X, Zhong W, Yao Z, Gao H, Wang F, Liu Y, Liu Y, Yang K, Yan Y, Yin C.
abstractText:
Objective

To evaluate the diagnostic yield and clinical value of a phenotype-driven genomic testing strategy in fetuses with central nervous system (CNS) abnormalities.

Methods

In this retrospective single-center study, 966 fetuses with CNS abnormalities detected by prenatal ultrasound and/or fetal magnetic resonance imaging were included. All cases underwent copy number variation sequencing (CNV-seq), while karyotyping and trio exome sequencing (trio-ES) were performed based on clinical indications and parental preference. Fetuses were stratified into isolated-single, isolated-complex, and non-isolated subgroups according to CNS involvement and extracranial abnormalities. Diagnostic yields were compared across phenotypic subgroups and common CNS phenotypes.

Results

Among 966 fetuses with prenatal CNS abnormalities, pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants were identified in 12.63% of cases. CNV-seq had a diagnostic yield of 8.07% (78/966), while trio-ES had a diagnostic yield of 16.32% (70/429) and provided an additional 10.92% yield (44/403) following negative CNV-seq results. Diagnostic yield varied significantly across phenotypic subgroups, with a higher CNV-seq yield in non-isolated cases than in isolated cases (15.41% vs. 4.25%, P < 0.001), and a higher ES yield in isolated-complex cases than in isolated-single cases (32.56% vs. 9.20%, P < 0.001). After excluding mild isolated CNS anomalies, diagnostic yields increased to 15.60% for CNV-seq and 26.67% for ES. In the adjusted cohort, differences among the three subgroups remained significant for CNV-seq (P < 0.001) but not for ES (P = 0.156). Across phenotypes, major structural abnormalities demonstrated substantially higher diagnostic yields than mild or soft markers, with a clear severity-dependent increase observed in ventriculomegaly and head circumference reduction.

Conclusion

Fetal CNS abnormalities show substantial genetic heterogeneity, and diagnostic yield is closely associated with prenatal imaging phenotypes. A phenotype-driven testing strategy may help prioritize genetic evaluation and improve prenatal counseling for fetuses with CNS abnormalities.

title: B‑lines on lung ultrasound: a non‑invasive marker for short‑term outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting.
authorString: Afrakoti NM, Khani M, Hemmati S, Ebrahiminasab A, Yekta RA, Rabi SHM, Pagard E, Marashi M.
abstractText:
Background

Postoperative pulmonary complications increase morbidity and mortality after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Lung ultrasound detection of B-lines is an established method to quantify pulmonary congestion, and while B-lines have been studied as predictive markers in heart failure and general critical care settings, their role in predicting outcomes specifically for post-CABG patients remains inadequately defined. This study aimed to evaluate the association between B-lines detected on postoperative lung ultrasound and 30-day mortality and hospital length of stay in patients undergoing isolated CABG.

Methods

This prospective cohort study was conducted in a single-center intensive care unit between 2023 and 2024. A total of 148 adult patients scheduled for elective CABG were enrolled. Lung ultrasound was performed on postoperative days 1 (POD1) and 3 (POD3) using a standardized 8-zone protocol to quantify B-lines. The primary outcomes were all-cause 30-day mortality, assessed via hospital records and telephone follow-up, and total hospital length of stay. Univariate and multivariate logistic and linear regression analyses were used to identify predictors.

Results

The mean patient age was 60.15 ± 9.8 years, and 57% were male. Within 30 days, 22 patients (15%) died. In the multivariate logistic regression, the number of B-lines on POD1 was an independent predictor of 30-day mortality (Adjusted Odds Ratio: 1.090, 95% CI: 1.018-1.167, p = 0.013), indicating a 9% increase in the odds of death for each additional B-line. In contrast, the B-line count on POD3 was not significantly associated with mortality. B-line counts on both days were also not associated with hospital length of stay. Instead, higher body mass index (β = 0.22, p = 0.022) and a history of smoking (β = 2.20, p = 0.020) were independently associated with longer hospitalization.

Conclusions

Early postoperative pulmonary congestion, as quantified by B-lines on POD1 lung ultrasound, is an independent predictor of 30-day mortality after CABG. Routine bedside lung ultrasound on the first day after surgery can serve as a non-invasive tool to stratify high-risk patients, potentially allowing for earlier intervention to optimize fluid status and improve outcomes.

title: Neurodevelopmental sequelae in paediatric pneumococcal meningitis: a call for strengthened surveillance and follow-up care.
authorString: Miraclin T A, Oommen SP, Cruz SD, Gunasekaran K, Inbaraj MJ, Verghese VP, Neeravi A, Varghese R, Ezekiel F, Thomas M, George L, Gupta N, Veeraraghavan B.
abstractText:
Background

Pneumococcal meningitis remains a significant cause of morbidity and mortality in children, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Despite widespread use of pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCVs), limited data exist from India on the long-term neurodevelopmental sequelae among survivors. This study aimed to characterise the clinical profile, microbiological features, and neurocognitive outcomes of children diagnosed with pneumococcal meningitis over a 15-year period at a tertiary care centre in South India.

Methods

This cross-sectional study included children admitted with microbiologically confirmed pneumococcal meningitis between January 2007 and January 2022. Clinical, laboratory, radiological, and microbiological data were retrieved retrospectively. Survivors were contacted for follow-up; consenting families underwent structured neurodevelopmental screening and in-person evaluations by a developmental paediatrician and psychologist. Outcomes were assessed using the Modified Rankin Scale (mRS) and domain-specific neuropsychological assessments. Statistical analyses were conducted using SPSS software.

Results

A total of 48 children were included, of whom 70.8% were male and under 12 months of age. The in-hospital case fatality rate was 10.4%, while 25.7% of children died post-discharge. At follow-up, only 57.2% achieved favourable functional outcomes (mRS 0-2), and 17.2% had moderate-to-severe disability (mRS 3-5). Long-term sequelae included learning difficulties (54.2%), behavioural disturbances (37.5%), intellectual disability (37.5%), hearing impairment (28.0%), and drug-refractory epilepsy (25.0%). Language impairments, sensorimotor delays, executive dysfunction, and cortical visual impairment were also observed. Serotype 14 was the most prevalent (20.8%), with 23 unique serotypes identified. Post-vaccine trends showed a decline in the prevalence of vaccine-protected serotypes, such as 6B and 23 F, and the emergence of 19 A and 7 F. Penicillin resistance was high (79.2%), including 14.6% with high-level resistance (≥ 1 µg/mL). Cefotaxime susceptibility remained favourable in 81.3% of isolates; however, increasing resistance is alarming.

Conclusion

Pneumococcal meningitis in children is associated with substantial mortality and a high burden of long-term neurodevelopmental sequelae, particularly in low-resource settings. Survivors experience persistent deficits across cognitive, motor, sensory, and behavioural domains, warranting structured post-discharge neurodevelopmental follow-up. The evolving serotype landscape and antibiotic resistance patterns underscore the need for continuous surveillance and tailored vaccine strategies, with particular emphasis on PCV13. Public health efforts must integrate early rehabilitation and school-based support to optimise outcomes for children affected by this disease.

title: Predictors and outcomes of early left ventricular dysfunction in paediatric patients postoperative for ventricular septal defect: a retrospective cohort study based on myocardial strain and work.
authorString: Zhao W, Li W, Wang T, Gao L, Zhang J, Guo Q, Zhang Y, Zhang L, Yu S, Dong X, Wang J, Luo Z.
abstractText:
Background

Early postoperative left ventricular (LV) dysfunction commonly occurs after ventricular septal defect (VSD) repair in paediatric patients. This study aimed to investigate its risk factors and impact on follow-up cardiac functional status.

Methods

We retrospectively enrolled patients with preserved LV ejection fraction (LVEF) ≥ 55% undergoing isolated surgical VSD repair. Early postoperative LV dysfunction was defined as LVEF < 55% during hospitalisation. LV function parameters including myocardial strain and work were obtained. Cardiac functional recovery was assessed at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months post-discharge based on Ross Classifications.

Results

The cohort comprised 409 patients (3.00 [1.00-5.75] years; 50.4% male), with 82 (20.05%) developing postoperative LV dysfunction. Multivariate analysis showed that preoperative LV global longitudinal strain (LV GLS), global work index (LV GWI), global work efficiency (LV GWE), LV end-diastolic volume index (LVEDVi), moderate-to-severe sPAP, and large VSD size, as well as prolonged cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) time, were significantly associated with postoperative LV dysfunction (all p < 0.05). ROC analyses found that integrating LV GWI and GWE with clinical parameters (LVEDVi, VSD size, or sPAP) enhanced prediction (AUC 0.848-0.883, P < 0.001). During follow-up, patients with postoperative LV dysfunction exhibited less favourable Ross classification recovery at 12 months after surgery.

Conclusions

Myocardial strain and work indices were related to early postoperative LV dysfunction in paediatric patients after isolated VSD repair, which was correlated with persistent symptoms and cardiac dysfunction at 12-month follow-up. Pre- and postoperative LV function assessment may offer useful information for managing this patient population.

title: Weekend versus weekday cardiac surgery: A comprehensive meta-analysis of more than 500,000 cases with meta-regression.
authorString: Santos K, Belen Kim Kim JY, Fárez CC, Hakkeem B, Habiyambere GI, Lira-Castañeda MS, Płonek T.
abstractText:
Objectives

The "weekend effect" describes worse outcomes with weekend hospital care, but its impact on cardiac surgery remains unclear. We performed a comprehensive meta-analysis and meta-regression to assess whether weekend cardiac surgery is associated with poorer perioperative outcomes than weekday procedures.

Methods

PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched for studies comparing weekend versus weekday cardiac surgery outcomes. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) and mean differences with 95% CIs were calculated using a random-effects model. Subgroup analyses were performed by procedure type (emergent, coronary artery bypass grafting, acute type A aortic dissection) and geographic region. Meta-regressions explored effects of mean age, percentage of female patients, proportion of emergent cases, and publication year. A day-by-day mortality heat map was constructed to assess daily trends.

Results

Seventeen studies comprising 527,195 patients were included; 7.4% underwent surgery on weekends. Weekend surgery was associated with significantly greater mortality (OR, 1.5; 95% CI, 1.2-1.8; P = .001) and longer stay in the intensive care unit (mean difference, 0.4 days; 95% CI, 0.1-0.7; P = .01). No significant differences were found for acute kidney injury, stroke, aortic crossclamp time, reoperation for bleeding, or total hospital stay. The incidence of transient ischemic attack was slightly lower on weekends (OR, 0.8; 95% CI, 0.6-1.0; P = .02). Subgroup analyses showed consistently elevated mortality in weekend cases across emergent, coronary artery bypass grafting, and acute type A aortic dissection subgroups, and in studies from Asia and the United States but not Europe. Meta-regression showed no significant effect of age, sex, emergent case proportion, or publication year on mortality differences.

Conclusions

Weekend cardiac surgery is associated with greater mortality and longer stay in the intensive care unit, independent of case mix. The absence of patient-level effect modification suggests that systemic or institutional factors, rather than patient acuity, underlie the weekend effect, supporting the need for policies ensuring consistent care across all days.

title: Single-center clinical analysis of anomalous aortic origin of a coronary artery (AAOCA) in children: a multimodal imaging approach to risk stratification.
authorString: Wang T, Qi H, Xie Y, Feng X, Gong L.
abstractText:
Objective

This study aimed to analyze the clinical characteristics of pediatric patients with Anomalous Aortic Origin of a Coronary Artery (AAOCA), explore the application of multimodal imaging in risk stratification, and establish individualized diagnosis and treatment protocols for this population.

Methods

A retrospective observational study was performed on children diagnosed with AAOCA at Wuhan Children's Hospital between January 2015 and April 2026. Clinical manifestations, multimodal imaging findings, therapeutic strategies, and long-term outcomes were comprehensively analyzed.

Results

A total of 58 AAOCA patients confirmed by coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) were enrolled. Initial transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) yielded false-negative results in 24 patients (41.4%). Twenty-seven patients underwent single-photon emission computed tomography myocardial perfusion imaging (SPECT-MPI, MPS), among whom 6 had normal perfusion and 21 showed perfusion defects. Seven patients with positive MPS findings received surgical correction, including 2 patients with L-AAOCA( 1 coronary angioplasty and 1 coronary unroofing) and 5 patients with R-AAOCA; all treated with coronary unroofing. No patients with negative MPS results underwent surgery, indicating that negative MPS findings perhaps provide limited valuable evidence to avoid unnecessary coronary revascularization. Two patients developed massive postoperative pericardial effusion and recovered after pericardiotomy and drainage; the remaining 5 surgical patients experienced no perioperative complications. All surgical patients were discharged after full recovery and received 3 months of aspirin antiplatelet therapy. Non-surgical patients were instructed to restrict strenuous physical activity and followed up for 3 months to 3 years. Follow-up CCTA or TTE revealed normal coronary ostia without stenosis in all patients.

Conclusion

Clinical manifestations of pediatric AAOCA vary widely across age groups, ranging from asymptomatic presentation to sudden cardiac arrest (SCA), leading to marked discrepancies in risk evaluation and therapeutic decision-making. Multimodal imaging including TTE, CCTA and SPECT-MPI facilitates risk stratification and guides personalized clinical management of children with AAOCA.

title: Extracardiac conduit versus lateral tunnel: Exploring the optimal surgical approach in the EUROFONTAN experience.
authorString: Bergonzoni E, Cao I, Vedovelli L, Hazekamp M, Hörer J, Protopapas EM, Ono M, Sames-Dolzer E, Gierlinger G, Rijnberg FM, Galletti L, Butera G, Meyns B, Van Puyvelde J, Yemets L, Bairamov E, Kansy A, Nosal M, Lenoir M, Gargiulo G, Angeli E, Martens T, Bove T, Napoleone CP, Lo Rito M, Giamberti A, Dimopoulos K, Montanaro C, Marianeschi S, Rocafort AG, Castaldi B, Gregori D, Di Salvo G, Meliota G, Scalzo G, Scrascia G, Michielon G, Vida V, Sarris G, Constantine A, Padalino MA.
abstractText:
Objective

The Fontan procedure is a crucial surgical intervention for single-ventricle physiology, with the extracardiac conduit (ECC) and lateral tunnel (LT) techniques being the predominant approaches. This study aimed to compare early and late clinical outcomes of ECC and LT, using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) to ensure robust assessments.

Methods

A retrospective analysis of 3300 patients from the EUROFONTAN registry was conducted, with data collected from 21 European centers. The cohort included 3010 patients who underwent the ECC technique and 290 patients who underwent the LT technique. IPTW was used to balance baseline characteristics. Primary outcomes were early and late mortality, Fontan failure, and adverse events. Secondary outcomes included postoperative complications and nonsurgical adverse events.

Results

Propensity-matched analysis showed significantly better outcomes for ECC. Early mortality was lower for ECC (1.2% vs 3.9%, P = .003), whereas late mortality at 20-year follow-up was 8.6% in LT versus 3.2% in ECC after IPTW (P = .003). Patients who underwent the ECC technique experienced fewer postoperative complications (47% vs 66%, P = .025) and less frequent Fontan failure (12% vs 19%, P = .032). Kidney-related events were more frequent in patients who underwent the LT technique (3% vs 0.6%, P = .004). The development of arrhythmia initially appeared greater in the LT group but equalized after matching. Long-term complications, such as protein-losing enteropathy and hepatic issues, showed no significant differences.

Conclusions

ECC was associated with better early and intermediate outcomes than LT in this multicenter European registry. However, surgical era and hospital center explain a substantial part of the observed difference. Continued long-term surveillance of the Fontan pathway is essential to optimize lifelong outcomes.

title: Atrial septal defect associated with suspected left ventricular non-compaction supported by histopathological findings in a child.
authorString: Osama MA, Malick SK, Sargunan BB, Varghese MB, Rajashekar P, Arava S, Ray R.

journal.title: Indian journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery

abstractText: Left ventricular non-compaction (LVNC) is a rare cardiomyopathy characterized by excessive trabeculation of the left ventricular myocardium. The debate over whether LVNC is a distinct disease entity limits the estimates on its prevalence and incidence as there is a significant overlap with other known cardiomyopathies like hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, apical hypertrophy, and dilated cardiomyopathy. This condition is defined by excessive trabeculation of the myocardium, with deep intertrabecular recesses that communicate directly with the ventricular cavity. We report an 11-year-old boy with ostium secundum atrial septal defect (ASD), unexplained left ventricular dysfunction, and intraoperative findings suggestive of LVNC, in whom histopathological examination provided supportive evidence for the diagnosis. The decision for fenestrated ASD closure was based on reduced left ventricular compliance demonstrated during preoperative assessment. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of LVNC when classical echocardiographic criteria are not fulfilled and emphasizes the complementary role of histopathological findings in selected cases.

title: Improvement in health-related quality of life after complex biventricular repair.
authorString: Stack KO, Gauvreau K, Campos S, Bamgbose MS, Blume ED, Emani SM, Kobayashi RL, Beroukhim RS.
abstractText:
Objective

Complex biventricular (BiV) and one-and-a-half ventricle (1.5V) repairs are alternatives to single ventricle palliation. We describe 1 domain of the health-related quality of life of patients undergoing BiV and 1.5V repairs.

Methods

This single-center study included children (≤ 18 years) who underwent BiV or 1.5V repairs between October 1, 2022, and July 7, 2024. Parents completed Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory Infant Scales or Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory 3.0 Cardiac Modules; physical function and physical symptom scores for patients younger than 2 years and heart problems and treatment scores for patients 2 years and older were evaluated.

Results

Seventy-three patients, 36 younger than 2 years and 37 ages 2 years and older, were included. Forty-one patients (56%) underwent BiV surgery, and 32 (44%) underwent 1.5V surgery. Preoperatively, patients younger than 2 years had a mean physical symptom score of 76 ± 14 and a mean physical function score of 70 ± 20; patients ages 2 years and older had a mean heart problems and treatment score of 64 ± 20. Thirty-six patients, 10 younger than 2 years and 26 ages 2 years and older, had paired pre- and postoperative health-related quality of life data. Following repair, physical symptom scores improved among infants ages 0 to 12 months (mean, 67 vs 79; P = .033), and heart problems and treatment scores improved (ages 2 to 4 years, 69 vs 84; P = .002; ages 5 to 7 years, 57 vs 86; P = .044). For patients ages 2 years and older, 5 symptoms drove score improvement: exertional dyspnea, chest pain, tachycardia, cyanosis, and fatigue.

Conclusions

Six months after surgery, parents reported improvement in children's health-related quality of life following complex BiV or 1.5V repairs. Further work is needed to better understand long-term outcomes in this vulnerable population.

title: Tricuspid aortic valve morphology predicts favorable midterm outcomes after aortic valve neocuspidization in children.
authorString: Wang G, Zhang S, Ma K, Pang K, Zhang B, Yang K, Li S.
abstractText:
Objective

To evaluate the midterm outcomes of the aortic valve neocuspidalization (AVNeo) procedure for aortic valve reconstruction in 83 pediatric patients with complex aortic valve disease and to identify risk factors associated with the outcomes.

Methods

A retrospective analysis was conducted on pediatric patients who underwent the AVNeo procedure between January 2017 and June 2025. The composite primary end point included all-cause mortality, reoperation, or moderate-to-severe aortic valve dysfunction (regurgitation or stenosis). Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify risk factors.

Results

Among the 83 patients (mean age 7.0 ± 3.7 years; 67.5% male) included in the analysis, the predominant preoperative pathology was moderate-to-severe aortic regurgitation (88.0%). Single-leaflet reconstruction (65.1%) using autologous pericardium (94.0%) was the most common surgical approach. Over a mean follow-up of 28.4 ± 23.9 months, 27 patients (32.5%) met the composite end point, including 2 late deaths, 18 cases of moderate-to-severe regurgitation, and 9 cases of moderate-to-severe stenosis; 10 patients underwent reoperation. The probability of freedom from the primary end point was 83.6%, 64.5%, and 54.4% at 1, 3, and 6 years, respectively. Multivariable analysis identified tricuspid aortic valve morphology as an independent protective factor against the primary end point (hazard ratio, 0.408; 95% CI, 0.178-0.935, P = .034), whereas the use of autologous pericardium showed a strong protective trend (hazard ratio, 0.284; 95% CI, 0.078-1.037, P = .057).

Conclusions

AVNeo provides midterm outcomes that support its use as an alternative strategy. Tricuspid aortic valve morphology is a strong predictor of favorable outcomes, and the use of autologous pericardium demonstrates significant potential as a protective factor.

title: Reprogramming gut microbiota and targeting CXCL1: The multifaceted mechanism of PLP1 in ameliorating alcohol-induced liver disease.
authorString: Yang Z, Lv Q, Xu Q, Chen Y, Yang Y, Li Z, Che H, Wang G, Wei W, Wu J, Han J.
abstractText: Hepatic inflammation and gut barrier dysfunction are core pathologies of alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD), yet effective therapies remain limited. Pueraria lobata polysaccharide (PLP1), a key active constituent of P. lobata Radix, has demonstrated hepatoprotective potential; however, its underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, we sought to elucidate the therapeutic mechanism of PLP1 against experimental ALD by integrating proteomics, metabolomics, and gut microbiota analyses. We demonstrated that PLP1 initially functions through a microbiota-dependent pathway, transferable by fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), to restore gut barrier integrity and suppress the gut‒LPS‒TLR4 inflammatory axis. Furthermore, PLP1 exerted a direct, microbiota-independent effect, maintaining its therapeutic efficacy in antibiotic-depleted mice. Mechanistically, PLP1 directly and specifically targets CXCL1, promoting its ubiquitin-mediated proteasomal degradation as confirmed by biophysical assays. The functional necessity of this interaction was definitively established via comprehensive genetic manipulation of CXCL1 in vitro and in vivo. Specifically, CXCL1 overexpression reversed PLP1's benefits, whereas CXCL1 knockdown mimicked its effects and occluded any additional benefit from PLP1. Overall, PLP1 ameliorates ALD by independently targeting both extrinsic and intrinsic inflammatory triggers. This study reveals the multifaceted pharmacology of a natural polysaccharide and validates a dual-pronged therapeutic strategy for ALD.

title: Postoperative root size predicts regurgitation in supravalvular aortic stenosis repair.
authorString: Recco DP, Marshall L, Schildmeier M, Gauvreau K, Confessore J, Quinonez LG, Del Nido PJ, Baird CW, Hammer PE, Hoganson DM.
abstractText:
Objective

Supravalvular aortic stenosis (SVAS) repair carries a moderate risk for postoperative aortic regurgitation (AR). This may be related to the targeted sinotubular junction diameter z score (STJDZ) at reconstruction, traditionally sized to zero. We investigated relationships between achieved STJDZ and aortic valve function after repair.

Methods

Sixty-six children underwent patch repair from 2010 to 2024 at a median age of 1.2 years (interquartile range [IQR], 0.4, 3.5 years) via Brom (n = 53), Doty (n = 9), and McGoon (n = 4) techniques. Relationships between STJDZ and aortic valve function were assessed via Jonckheere-Terpstra nonparametric test for trend over median follow-up of 5.6 years (IQR, 2.4, 8.4 years).

Results

Preoperatively, AR was none/trivial in 52 (79%), left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO) moderate or greater in 54 (82%), and median STJDZ -3.8 (IQR, -4.4, -2.9). At discharge, AR and LVOTO were mild or greater in 45 (68%) and 18 (27%), and median STJDZ was -0.3 (IQR, -1.3, -1.1). STJDZ increased by a median of 3.0 (IQR, 1.6, 4.4) preoperatively to postoperatively. Discharge AR was none/trivial at median STJDZ -1.3 (IQR, -1.8, -0.1) and worsened with increasing diameters (mild: 0.4 [IQR, -1.0, 1.8], mild+: 0.0 [IQR, -1.2, 1.5]; P = .038), with similar results at follow-up (P = .048). LVOTO worsened with lower median STJDZ (none/trivial: 0.2 [IQR, -1.2, 1.5], mild: -1.3 [IQR, -3.2, -0.1]; P = .015). Subanalysis of those with none/trivial preoperative AR (n = 52) showed that increase in STJDZ by ≥4 demonstrated worse follow-up AR (P = .016).

Conclusions

Achieving STJDZ zero using patch repair techniques to relieve SVAS obstruction demonstrated mild or greater postoperative AR compared with none/trivial regurgitation at median z score -1.3. Mild LVOTO was noted with median z score -1.3. Targeting STJDZ of -1 in pediatric SVAS repair appears appropriate to balance residual regurgitation and LVOTO. Further follow-up is required to understand the long-term impact of this target on aortic growth.

title: Descending aortic translocation for aerodigestive vascular compression.
authorString: Tsou S, Chiu P, Benavente R, Castellanos D, Brown J, Cole L, Zendejas B, Baird CW.
abstractText:
Objective

Patients with complex vascular ring anomalies can present with symptoms of esophageal and airway compression, occasionally persisting despite relief of the vascular ring, due to residual compression from the aorta. We report our early experience with descending aortic translocation to address aerodigestive vascular compression.

Methods

This is a retrospective single-center review of patients undergoing descending aortic translocation. The operation involves dividing the distal aortic arch on cardiopulmonary bypass, relocating the descending aorta beneath the carina and right pulmonary artery, and anastomosis to the posterior aspect of the ascending aorta, thereby entirely relieving compression on the aerodigestive tract. Concomitant esophageal mobilization and tracheopexies are performed as needed.

Results

From 2020 to 2023, 15 patients underwent descending aortic translocation. Anatomic variants included hairpin aorta (n = 2), circumflex aorta (n = 4), midline descending aorta (n = 7), and bowstring aorta (n = 2). Median age was 2 years. Preoperatively, most patients (80%) had mixed esophageal and airway symptoms and had undergone at least 1 prior operation (60%). Intraoperative bronchoscopy revealed improved airway patency for all patients. Postoperatively, 93% of patients had relief of respiratory symptoms, and 79% of patients had improved dysphagia. Postoperative complications included neurologic event (n = 1) with full resolution, right pulmonary artery compression requiring stenting (n = 1), and need for reoperation (n = 2).

Conclusions

Descending aortic translocation is a novel approach that can provide symptomatic relief of aerodigestive compression related to complex aortic anomalies. For patients with persistent symptoms after initial vascular ring repair, ongoing aortic compression may need to be addressed, thus also raising the question of whether descending aortic translocation should be considered as a first-line therapy.

title: Psychological Impact of Fetal Echocardiography Referral on Pregnant Women With a Normal Routine Morphologic Ultrasound.
authorString: Dufour C, Roy LO, Taillefer V, Duclos M, Raiche E, Cavallé-Garrido T, Mansukhani G, Brown R, Thakur V, Ferland-Dorval A, Al-Amir-Dach R, Hall M, Vaujois L, Dallaire F, Canadian Congenital and Pediatric Cardiology Research Network.

journal.title: CJC pediatric and congenital heart disease

abstractText:
Background

Fetal echocardiography (FE) is widely recommended in pregnancies at increased risk of congenital heart defects. Although FE is a safe diagnostic tool, its psychological impact on expectant pregnant women remains poorly understood.

Methods

We conducted a prospective observational study in 8 Canadian centers. Women aged ≥18 years with a normal second-trimester ultrasound between 18 and 26 weeks' gestation referred for an FE were compared with women who were not. Anxiety was assessed using the Spielberger State-Trait Anxiety Inventory. The primary outcome was the difference between state and trait anxiety (net situational anxiety) after morphologic ultrasound but before FE (T0). Secondary outcomes included the proportion of participants with significant anxiety (State-Trait Anxiety Inventory ≥40) and anxiety trajectories after FE among referred participants.

Results

Eighty-four women were included, of whom 38 were referred for FE. At T0, women referred for FE showed slightly higher median net situational anxiety compared with controls. In multivariable analyses, FE referral was associated with a modest increase although estimates were imprecise. A higher proportion of referred women reached a state anxiety score ≥40, though this association was weak after adjustment. Among the 14 women who completed post-FE questionnaires, anxiety trajectories were heterogeneous, with both increases and decreases observed after FE.

Conclusions

Referral for FE after a normal second-trimester ultrasound is associated with a small and variable increase in maternal anxiety. These findings suggest that FE referral may not be psychologically neutral and highlight the importance of considering maternal psychological responses as referral criteria broaden.

title: Acute Kawasaki Disease With Concomitant Adenovirus Infection.
authorString: McCrindle BW, Rahman R, Gangemi D, Farid P, Butris N, Chahal N, O'Shea S, Collins T, Runeckles K, Guerra V, Manlhiot C.

journal.title: CJC pediatric and congenital heart disease

abstractText:
Background

Adenovirus infection is the most common condition in the differential diagnosis of acute Kawasaki disease (KD), but it may also occur as a concomitant infection, the relevance of which has been incompletely defined.

Methods

A prospectively maintained, single-center database of all presenting patients with acute KD was queried. Patients with laboratory evidence of adenovirus infection were compared with patients with no laboratory evidence of any concomitant infection of any type. We sought to determine differences in demographics, clinical and laboratory features, treatment received, and coronary artery (CA) outcomes.

Results

From 1997 to 2023, a total of 1442 patients who had no laboratory evidence of concomitant infection and 39 patients positive for adenovirus were compared. There were no differences regarding demographics and few differences regarding clinical features at presentation, with 72% in each group meeting guideline criteria for a diagnosis of complete KD. Patients positive for adenovirus were less likely to have rash (69% vs 88%; P < 0.001), were more likely to have respiratory (61% vs 20%; P < 0.001) and gastrointestinal symptoms (47% vs 27%; P = 0.007), and had less severe laboratory abnormalities. Adenovirus positivity was not associated with an increased risk of resistance to intravenous immunoglobulin. CA involvement was not observed in any patient in the adenovirus group (P = 0.049).

Conclusions

The presence of positive evidence of adenovirus in the setting of acute KD does not appear to confound the diagnosis of KD, the response to which should be prompt initiation of immunomodulatory treatment. CA outcomes appear to be excellent.

title: Atrial Flow Regulator Bridging to Heart Transplantation in Congenital Heart Disease With Severe Combined Pulmonary Hypertension.
authorString: Albertini M, David P, Nougué H, Cholley B, Waldmann V, Chamandi C, Chaussade AS, Du Puy-Montbrun L, Coutance G, Iserin L.
