title: Early Outcomes of Harmony Transcatheter Pulmonary Valve Implantation in the Middle East: A Single-Center Experience From Saudi Arabia.
authorString: Dowaikh AM, Arafat AA, Ahmed SF, Ismail AA, Alsahari AH, Alotay AA, Momenah TS.

journal.title: CJC pediatric and congenital heart disease

abstractText:
Background

Significant pulmonary regurgitation (PR) is a common late complication after repair of right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) lesions, potentially leading to right ventricular failure. The Harmony transcatheter pulmonary valve (TPV) was developed for large, native, or patched RVOTs. Although multicenter studies have shown favorable results, regional single-center data, particularly from the Middle East, are scarce. This study reports our initial single-center experience with Harmony TPV implantation, focusing on procedural success, safety, and 1-year outcomes.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective analysis of 10 consecutive patients who underwent Harmony TPV implantation at our institution. Data were collected on baseline characteristics, procedural details, and outcomes. Procedural success, complications, and hemodynamic performance were assessed.

Results

The median age of our population was 15.5 years, and 70% of patients were male. The most common underlying diagnosis was post-tetralogy of Fallot repair (50%). All patients had severe PR at baseline. Technical success was achieved in all patients. There was no mortality. Minor periprocedural complications occurred in 4 patients, including minor femoral vein avulsion, fever, ecchymosis, and frequent premature ventricular contractions, all managed conservatively. At 1-year follow-up, freedom from death, moderate/severe PR, mean RVOT gradient >40 mm Hg, or reintervention was 100%. No endocarditis, valve thrombosis, or stent fracture was observed.

Conclusions

This single-center experience from the Middle East demonstrates that Harmony TPV implantation is a feasible and safe procedure with excellent early clinical and echocardiographic outcomes. These findings are consistent with previously published international series and support the adoption of this technology in specialized centers for managing severe PR in patients with complex RVOT anatomy.

title: Assessment of the Variability of an Echo-Doppler Method for Measurement of Aortic Pulse Wave Velocity.
authorString: Massarotto RJ, Bradley TJ, Potts JE, Mah K, Sandor GG, Cote AT.

journal.title: CJC pediatric and congenital heart disease

abstractText:
Background

Pulse wave velocity (PWV) is an indirect measure of elastic arterial stiffness. Although various methods have been established to measure PWV, the Echo-Doppler method for measuring thoracic aortic PWV (a-PWV) is a highly available and cost-effective technique within the cardiology clinic. The purpose of this study was to assess the variability of a-PWV using the Echo-Doppler method and identify the optimal number of measurements providing the least variability of a-PWV in paediatric patients and healthy controls.

Methods

Eighteen patients with a dilated proximal aorta and 21 healthy controls with a normal-sized proximal aorta (10-18 years) were evaluated. Imaging was performed in 4 studies across 2 visits. Variability comparisons were performed for short-term, medium-term, intra-reviewer, inter-reviewer, and inter-sonographer variability and analysed via intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and Bland-Altman plots.

Results

The ICCs were highest for 10 beats. The combined group ICCs for the variability comparisons for 10 beats were short-term (0.743), medium-term (0.723) intra-reviewer (0.978), inter-reviewer (0.729), and inter-sonographer (0.823). Bland-Altman plots showed good agreement for all variability comparisons.

Conclusions

This study has established that the measurement over 10 beats produces the lowest variability and is recommended when assessing a-PWV in both patients with a dilated proximal aorta and controls. Further, reproducibility remains high, even when accounting for sources of measurement variation, such as differences between sonographers, reviewers, and study visits.

title: Exercise Limitations in Fontan Circulation: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Peak Oxygen Uptake.
authorString: Weeldreyer NR, Shewman A, Waldron M, Hewitt D, Schmid V, Weinkauf C, Pagano J, Tomczak CR, Niederseer D, Vontobel J, Angadi SS, Foulkes SJ, Haykowsky MJ.

journal.title: CJC pediatric and congenital heart disease

abstractText:
Background

The degree to which individuals with Fontan circulation (FC) experience exercise limitations and the underlying physiological mechanisms remains unclear. Thus, we sought to quantify the magnitude of peak oxygen consumption ( V˙ O2peak) impairment and its determinants in individuals with FC and age-matched healthy controls (CON).

Methods

PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched from January 1980 through July 2025. Studies were included if they reported V˙ O2peak or its Fick determinants derived from a cardiopulmonary exercise test and compared FC with CON. Random-effects models were used for pooled data analysis, and meta-regressions were used to explore key moderators of age and time after Fontan surgery.

Results

Pooled analysis demonstrated significantly reduced V˙ O2peak in FC vs CON (19 studies, n = 893; weighted mean difference: 17.2 mL/kg/min, 95% confidence interval: -20.9 to -14.3 mL/kg/min). Meta-regressions revealed that age significantly moderated the weighted mean difference for relative V˙ O2peak (β = -5.77 mL/kg/min; 95% confidence interval: -11.27 to -0.27; P = 0.041). Peak exercise oxygen pulse, heart rate, systolic blood pressure, and arterial oxygen saturation were significantly lower in FC compared with CON, whereas peak exercise stroke volume did not differ significantly between the groups.

Conclusions

Exercise capacity is markedly impaired in individuals with FC due to central and peripheral limitations, and the magnitude of this decline accelerates with time after surgery. These findings highlight the importance of early identification and targeted (exercise) intervention to mitigate long-term functional decline.

title: Association Between a Novel Adult Congenital Heart Disease Patient-Reported Outcome Metric and New York Heart Association Functional Classification.
authorString: Amir R, Ko JM, Kutty S, Van Bulck L, Jackson JL, Caruana M, Jameson SM, Mahadevan VS, Moons P, Cedars A, APPROACH-IS II consortium, International Society for Adults Congenital Heart Disease (ISACHD).

journal.title: CJC pediatric and congenital heart disease

abstractText: Patient-reported outcomes (PROs) are important for clinical care. As part of the Adults with Congenital Heart Disease International Study-II, we included an English language version of the novel adult congenital heart disease (ACHD)-specific PRO metric, the ACHD PRO, for distribution at English-speaking sites. We found that ACHD PRO scores correlate with New York Heart Association functional class, with an 11-point change in summary score reflecting a 1-category change in New York Heart Association class. These results provide further validation of the ACHD PRO as a tool and suggest clinically meaningful thresholds for differences in the ACHD PRO summary score.

title: Systematic Review and Meta-regression of Longitudinal Outcomes of Pulmonary Valve Replacement in Tetralogy of Fallot.
authorString: Roy LO, Watelle L, Champagne PA, Blais S, Dallaire F.

journal.title: CJC pediatric and congenital heart disease

abstractText:
Background

Despite excellent survival after tetralogy of Fallot repair, pulmonary regurgitation (PR) is common. Pulmonary valve replacement (PVR) is frequently performed, but its long-term efficacy remains uncertain. We conducted a meta-regression to assess the impact of PVR on key cardiac outcomes over time.

Methods

We included studies reporting PR, right ventricular (RV) and left ventricular volumes, QRS duration, RV ejection fraction, peak VO2, or New York Heart Association class before and after PVR in patients with tetralogy of Fallot. A multilevel random-effects meta-regression was performed using time since PVR as a covariate. Cubic splines were used to explore temporal trends and meta-analysis to quantify the impact of PVR over time.

Results

Sixty-nine studies were included. Compared with pre-PVR values, PVR yielded substantial absolute reductions in PR fraction and RV end-systolic and end-diastolic volume. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume increased slightly. New York Heart Association class also improved. The median follow-up was 14.4 months (interquartile range: 10.3-31.1 months) with only 1 study extending beyond 10 years. Estimated annual changes after PVR were minimal for all parameters and negligible for key parameters such as PR fraction (0.36%, 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.05% to 0.77%), RV end-systolic volume (-0.58 mL/m2, 95% CI: -1.62 mL/m2 to 0.45 mL/m2), and RV end-diastolic volume (-0.49 mL/m2, 95% CI: -0.72 mL/m2 to 1.72 mL/m2).

Conclusions

The long-term impact of PVR remains uncertain. Although short-term improvements are clear, insufficient long-term data preclude firm conclusions on sustained benefits.

title: The Fontan Conundrum: Rarity, Complexity, and the Research Gap.
authorString: Shah AH, Krasuski RA, Grewal J, Opotowsky AR, Ramakrishnan S.

journal.title: CJC pediatric and congenital heart disease

title: Prognostic Value of N-Terminal Pro-B-Type Natriuretic Peptide for Risk Stratification in Adults With Fontan Palliation.
authorString: Abozied O, Miranda WR, Reddy YVN, Kholeif Z, Connolly HM, Jaffe AS, Egbe AC.

journal.title: CJC pediatric and congenital heart disease

abstractText:
Background

There are limited data about the prognostic role of N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) in adults with Fontan palliation. The purpose of this study was to determine the correlates and the prognostic value of serial NT-proBNP assay for risk stratification in adults with Fontan palliation.

Methods

This is a retrospective cohort study of adults with Fontan palliation who had ≥1 NT-proBNP measurement in the outpatient clinic (2003-2023). In patients with ≥3 NT-proBNP measurements, serial NT-proBNP was calculated as the mean of the first 3 measurements. The study outcome was death/transplant.

Results

Of 369 patients (age 27 ± 8 years; 55% male) with NT-proBNP, 214 (58%) had serial measurements. The baseline level was 217 (82, 562) pg/mL, whereas the serial value was 261 (98, 715) pg/mL. The correlates of higher NT-proBNP levels were older age, atriopulmonary connection, atrial fibrillation, hepatorenal dysfunction, systemic ventricular dilation and systolic dysfunction, and higher Fontan pressures and pulmonary artery wedge pressure. Baseline and serial NT-proBNP levels were associated with death/transplant independent of anatomic indices, comorbidities, and hemodynamic indices. Serial NT-proBNP levels had superior prognostic value to single (baseline) NT-proBNP measurements, echocardiographic indices, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging indices, and cardiac catheterization indices.

Conclusions

These findings have important clinical implications in the management of adults with Fontan palliation because NT-proBNP assay is inexpensive, readily available, and noninvasive, and hence ideal for longitudinal assessment. Further studies are required to determine whether NT-proBNP can be used as a surrogate marker to monitor response to therapeutic interventions in this population.

title: Modeling the potential clinical and economic impact of clesrovimab for the prevention of RSV in infants in England and Wales.
authorString: Kura K, Burgess C, Matthews IR, Garba SM, Wang D, Lang JC, Ntais D, Chen YH.
abstractText:
Background

Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infects nearly all children under two years, causing mild lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) although serious disease, mortality and long-term recurrent wheezing can also occur.

Objectives

This study evaluates the health and economic impact of various RSV prevention strategies (monoclonal antibodies [mAb] such as clesrovimab, nirsevimab, palivizumab [high risk infants only] or maternal vaccination) in infants in England and Wales.

Design

A previously published decision tree model was adapted to estimate RSV LRTIs and associated costs over one year among a cohort of infants entering their first RSV season in England and Wales.

Methods

Clinical trial data were used for efficacy inputs alongside country-specific epidemiology and costs to assess the impact of year-round and seasonal mAb programs (without and with catch-up [for infants born out of season]) alongside maternal vaccination. Deterministic sensitivity analyses of incremental treatment costs and QALYs were performed.

Results

Seasonal administration of clesrovimab with and without catch-up led to fewer RSV-associated LRTI cases and lower treatment costs compared to other RSV intervention strategies. Without catch-up, clesrovimab reduced RSV-LRTI cases by 18%-27% versus palivizumab, 3%-4% versus nirsevimab and 2%-13% versus maternal vaccine. With catch-up, RSV-LRTI outcomes reductions by clesrovimab were greater: 60%-70% versus palivizumab, 14%-20% versus nirsevimab, and 43%-54% versus maternal vaccination. It also reduced treatment costs by £37.0 million compared to palivizumab, £4.0 million compared to nirsevimab, and £26.0 million compared to maternal vaccination. Coverage and efficacies were the most influential parameters.

Conclusions

Clesrovimab is projected to substantially reduce RSV-associated clinical outcomes and costs compared to both standard of care and potential new RSV prevention measures in England and Wales.

title: Serum magnesium levels and the risk of acute viral cardiomyopathy in children: A case-control study.
authorString: Doost-Mohammadi F, Anjomshoaa F, Derakhshan R.
abstractText:
Background

Acute viral cardiomyopathy is a leading cause of heart failure in children. Although magnesium is essential for myocardial electrophysiology, its potential association with pediatric viral cardiomyopathy remains poorly characterized.

Methods

This hospital-based frequency-matched case-control study (1:1 ratio, balanced for age) included 73 children with confirmed acute viral cardiomyopathy and 73 non-cardiac hospitalized controls at Afzalipour Hospital, Kerman, Iran (2023-2024). Serum total magnesium was measured on admission (reference 1.7-2.3 mg/dL); hypomagnesemia was defined as <1.7 mg/dL. Groups were compared using an independent-samples t-test and a χ² test. Multivariable logistic regression has been used to assess associated factors for acute viral cardiomyopathy.

Results

Mean serum magnesium level was significantly lower in the cardiomyopathy group than the control group (1.80 ± 0.31 vs. 1.98 ± 0.31 mg/dL; P = 0.003). Hypomagnesemia prevalence was significantly higher in the cardiomyopathy group (39.7% vs. 9.6%; unadjusted OR (95% CI): 5.80 (2.28-14.75); P < 0.001). After adjustment for sex, BMI, fever, and underlying chronic disease, each 0.1 mg/dL decrease in serum magnesium was associated with 1.38-fold higher odds of cardiomyopathy (adjusted OR (95% CI): 1.38 (1.11-1.72); P = 0.004). Hospital stay was longer in cases (7.77 ± 2.42 vs. 5.39 ± 2.20 days; P < 0.001). In-hospital mortality was higher among the cardiomyopathy group (6.8% vs. 1.4%), though the difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.209).

Conclusion

Children with acute viral cardiomyopathy seem to have significantly lower serum magnesium compared with matched controls. Routine admission magnesium screening could be considered in management protocols.

title: Mental Health Staff Capability and Practice for Promoting Physical Activity: Evidence From a Mental Health Community-Managed Organisation.
authorString: Lamble R, Wirtu G, Watkins A, Orr M, Curtis J, Gagnon L, Ryall J, Fibbins H, Haywood D, Caperchione CM, Simmons D, Fletcher T, Hart NH, Rosenbaum S, Lederman O.

journal.title: Health promotion journal of Australia : official journal of Australian Association of Health Promotion Professionals

abstractText:
Issue addressed

People with complex mental health conditions experience substantial reductions in life expectancy, largely due to preventable chronic disease. Mental health community-managed organisations (CMOs) are well placed to support physical health, yet little is known about staff capability to promote physical activity (PA).

Methods

A cross-sectional survey was administered to staff at a CMO in Sydney. Staff barriers, attitudes, confidence and knowledge relating to PA and physical health were assessed using the Physical Activity Attitudes Confidence Knowledge (PACK) and modified Metabolic Barriers Attitudes Confidence Knowledge (mM-BACK) questionnaires. PA promotional practices and personal PA behaviours were also assessed and relationships between these factors explored.

Results

Fifty-six of 78 eligible staff (72%) completed the survey. Mean scores were 34.8/45 (SD = 3.6) on PACK and 43.8/65 (SD = 6.7) on mM-BACK. Perceived barriers were generally low; workload was among those most commonly identified. Across both tools, attitudes scored highest, while confidence and knowledge scored lower. Only 23% reported familiarity with PA guidelines. Although 82% discussed PA with clients in the previous five workdays, 63% made no formal referrals. In correlation analyses, PA conversations were associated with mM-BACK attitudes (ρ = 0.43, p < 0.001) and PACK confidence (ρ = 0.34, p = 0.011), while capability was not associated with referrals.

Conclusions

CMO staff held positive attitudes towards PA promotion and commonly discussed PA with clients, but gaps remain in confidence, knowledge and referral practices. SO WHAT?: Building workforce capability, clarifying referral pathways and embedding organisational support for PA promotion within mental health CMOs may help reduce preventable health inequities in this population.

title: Complaint Driven Clinical Guidance and ICD Chapter Suggestion: An AI-Based Text Classification Tool.
authorString: Duru A, Sehirli E, Turan MK, Demiral E, Tankul M, Coskun M.

journal.title: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice

abstractText:
Rationale, aims and objectives

Accurate routing of patients to appropriate clinical departments is essential for timely diagnosis, effective treatment, and efficient use of hospital resources. However, hospital statistics and feedback from patients and healthcare staff indicate that many patients select clinics that are not appropriate for their presenting complaints. This mismatch unnecessarily occupies appointment slots, limits access to appropriate care, and increases the operational burden on healthcare systems. To address this problem, a complaint-driven clinical guidance framework was developed to map patient complaints to suitable clinical departments and corresponding International Classification of Diseases (ICD) chapters.

Method

A 7-year electronic health record dataset comprising 1,795,645 patient complaints was used to train and evaluate conventional machine learning algorithms and BERT-based language models. The final classification tasks included 15 clinical departments for department recommendation and 12 ICD chapters for suggestion.

Results

For clinical department recommendation, Turkish BERT achieved the best performance, with a mean accuracy of 92.02%, precision of 92.91%, and F1-score of 92.08%. McNemar's test confirmed that its improvement over multilingual BERT-based alternatives was statistically significant. Error analysis indicated that most department-level misclassifications occurred between clinically related or symptomatically overlapping departments, including Internal Medicine-Cardiology, Neurosurgery and Physical Therapy, and Cardiovascular Surgery-Cardiology. For ICD chapter suggestion, Turkish BERT achieved the best performance among the evaluated models, with a top-1 accuracy of 66.7%, top-3 accuracy of 82.9%, top-5 accuracy of 85.4%.

Conclusion

Although exact ICD chapter prediction remained challenging, the substantially higher top-3 and top-5 accuracies indicate that the model may be useful for generating ranked candidate ICD chapters. Confusion analysis showed that errors were mainly concentrated between clinically overlapping ICD chapters, particularly neoplasms/blood and immune disorders, endocrine/metabolic diseases, circulatory system diseases, and symptom-based chapters. These findings suggest that artificial intelligence-based systems can effectively support clinical department recommendation to improve hospital workflow efficiency, whereas ICD chapter suggestion may serve as a preliminary ranked decision-support tool.

title: From Static Choices to Navigating Clinical Trajectories: Reframing Therapeutic Reasoning in Medical Education.
authorString: von Kodolitsch Y, Dreyer T, Wick T, Harendza S.

journal.title: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice

abstractText:
Problem

Therapeutic reasoning is central to clinical practice and informed by established frameworks such as evidence-based medicine and shared decision-making. In educational settings, however, therapeutic decision-making is frequently taught and assessed as a discrete choice among predefined treatment options. This static framing - commonly structured through decision trees and guideline algorithms- emphasizes treatment selection under uncertainty but may insufficiently reflect the temporally evolving and regulatory nature of patient care.

Conceptual shift

We propose that therapeutic reasoning can be more fully understood as the navigation of clinical trajectories rather than the selection of isolated choices. Drawing on complex adaptive systems theory, we conceptualize disease, resilience, and health as dynamically interacting functions evolving through feedback loops and shifting stability. Therapeutic reasoning is the anticipatory and interpretive process that guides the adaptive regulation of evolving clinical trajectories across coupled systems of organism and pathology. This perspective complements established decision-making models by making the temporal and systemic dimensions of therapeutic practice explicit.

Framework

We operationalize this reframing through a phase-based model distinguishing disease-dominant decline, therapy-dominant modulation, and resilience-dominant recovery. Using severe pneumonia as an illustrative case, we demonstrate how inflection points and destabilizing events reveal the dynamic cognitive work underlying therapeutic practice and provide a conceptual scaffold for structuring therapeutic thinking.

Implications

Reframing therapeutic reasoning as trajectory navigation enriches the teaching of therapeutic decision making by providing a conceptual scaffold for curriculum design, clinical supervision, and assessment.

title: Bexagliflozin: pharmacological profile and clinical applications of a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor.
authorString: Gars A, Khan A, Kim S, Dodge C, Tinna H, Li Z, Gupta A.

journal.title: Journal of basic and clinical physiology and pharmacology

abstractText: Bexagliflozin, approved in the United States in 2023, is the fifth selective sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Unlike other class members, it lacks an event-driven cardiovascular outcomes trial (CVOT) and trials with hard kidney or heart failure endpoints. This narrative mini-review separates bexagliflozin-specific evidence from class benefits. PubMed and Google Scholar were searched for English-language articles (January 2009-June 2026) using "bexagliflozin," "Brenzavvy," and "SGLT2 inhibitor," plus prescribing information and pivotal class trials. Randomized trials and meta-analyses were prioritized. Bexagliflozin reduced glycated hemoglobin (HbA<sub>1c</sub>), body weight, and systolic blood pressure vs. placebo and was noninferior to sitagliptin, glimepiride, and, in one 24-week trial, dapagliflozin for HbA<sub>1c</sub>. In stage 3a/3b chronic kidney disease, it reduced albuminuria by 20.1 % vs. placebo, a surrogate finding. A cardiovascular safety trial and meta-analysis excluded excess cardiovascular risk but were not powered for benefit. Adverse events were consistent with the class. Bexagliflozin is an effective glucose-lowering drug, but its cardiovascular, kidney, and heart failure benefits remain unproven and cannot be assumed from class data. Outcome-proven agents are preferred for cardiorenal protection. An adequately powered CVOT and hard kidney endpoint trials are the key research priorities.

title: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate in chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: the H-HeFT trial.
authorString: Køber L, Skak-Hansen KW, Larsen AH, Vraa S, Schou M, Høfsten DE, Refsgaard J, Steffensen F, Hassager C, Parner E, Møller J, Eiskjær H, Bøtker HE, Serup-Hansen K, Madsen JS, Kristensen SL, Poulsen MK, Holst-Hansen C, Hollingdal M, Hove JD, Barasa A, Wolsk E, Buch NPG, Bruun NE, Bøttcher M, Dodt K, Brogaard V, Nielsen G, Ryde H, Mikkelsen KV, Wang Y, Madsen EH, Poenaru MP, Raymond I, Mahboubi K, Petersen M, Tønder N, Gislason G, Mellemkjær S, Gustafsson F, Wiggers H, DANHEART Investigators.
abstractText: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate (H-ISDN) has shown benefit in earlier randomized trials of patients with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and chronic heart failure. This trial tested if H-ISDN could reduce worsening heart failure or mortality in patients with chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) receiving contemporary treatment. The Hydralazine-Isosorbide Dinitrate in Patients With Chronic Heart Failure Trial (H-HeFT) was a multicentre, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in patients with HFrEF at 23 Danish hospitals (New York Heart Association class II-IV, elevated N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide and LVEF ≤40%). Target treatment was hydralazine 75 mg/isosorbide dinitrate 40 mg three times a day (t.i.d). The primary endpoint was a composite of hospitalization with worsening heart failure, an urgent outpatient visit resulting in intravenous/metolazone therapy for heart failure, heart transplantation, left ventricular assist device implantation, or death. Secondary endpoints included components of the primary outcome. Overall, 592 predominantly White patients (median age 72 years, 18% women) were randomized with a mean follow-up of 3.7 years. The primary outcome occurred in 90 of 294 patients (30.6%) in the H-ISDN group and in 91 of 298 patients (30.5%) in the placebo group [hazard ratio (HR) 0.90; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.67-1.21; P = .48]. There were 57 deaths in the H-ISDN group vs 72 in the placebo group (HR 0.72; 95% CI 0.51-1.02); worsening heart failure events occurred in 52 vs 47 patients (HR 1.01; 95% CI 0.68-1.50). Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate did not change the incidence of the composite endpoint of heart failure events or death in patients with heart failure and LVEF ≤40%.

title: Remnant Cholesterol Inflammatory Index and its Association With Cardiometabolic Multimorbidity in Middle-Aged and Advanced-Aged Individuals: Evidence From the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study.
authorString: Wang Y, Dong Q, Wang W, Tang S, Yu N, Wang Y, Zou C.

journal.title: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research

abstractText: BACKGROUND The association between remnant cholesterol inflammatory index (RCII) and cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) remains unclear. RCII is defined as: {Total Cholesterol - (High-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol + Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol)] × High-Sensitivity C-Reactive Protein/10}. This study examined the association between baseline RCII and CMM among middle-aged and older adults in China. MATERIAL AND METHODS This study analyzed data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), including 6173 participants. CMM was defined as the coexistence of at least 2 of 4 conditions: hypertension, diabetes, heart disease, or stroke. Participants were grouped according to the quartiles of natural log-transformed RCII (lnRCII) values. Modified Poisson regression models, restricted cubic splines, and receiver operating characteristic curves were used to examine the relationship between lnRCII and CMM outcomes. RESULTS In the cohort, 1832 cases of CMM occurred, and the incidence of CMM was highest in the lnRCII highest-quartile group (P<0.001). In the fully adjusted model, each unit of increase in lnRCII was associated with a higher risk of CMM (RR=1.13, 95% CI: 1.09-1.16), and participants in the highest quartile had a higher risk than those in the lowest quartile (RR=1.69, 95% CI: 1.50-1.90). The area under the curve for lnRCII was 0.607 (95% CI: 0.592-0.622), indicating modest discriminatory ability. CONCLUSIONS Higher baseline lnRCII was associated with an increased risk of incident CMM in middle-aged and older Chinese adults. Although RCII may capture combined information on remnant cholesterol and inflammation, its clinical predictive value requires further validation.

title: Long-term Prognostic Value of Sequential Coronary CT Angiography and Quantitative PET in Suspected Chronic Coronary Syndromes: A Multicentre study.
authorString: Hoek R, Rasmussen LD, Maaniitty T, Jukema RA, Søby JH, Twisk JW, van Diemen PA, Saraste A, Bøttcher M, Danad I, Knaapen P, Knuuti J, Winther S, Driessen RS.
abstractText:
Background and aims

The long-term prognostic value of a guideline-recommended selective sequential anatomical-functional imaging strategy using coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) followed by quantitative [15O]H2O positron emission tomography (PET) remains uncertain. We evaluated its long-term prognostic value in patients with first symptoms suggestive of obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD).

Methods

In this multicentre European cohort, symptomatic patients first underwent CCTA and were selectively referred to quantitative [15O]H2O PET in case of suspected obstructive stenosis (≥50%). Patients were stratified according to CCTA findings and PET-derived ischaemia (normal CCTA; non-obstructive CAD on CCTA; obstructive CAD on CCTA without ischaemia; obstructive CAD on CCTA with ischaemia). The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), and hospitalization for unstable angina (UA). Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) were calculated.

Results

Among 3,918 patients (61.0±9.8 years; 54.3% female) with a median follow-up of 5.1 [3.8-8.0] years, 278 (7.1%) experienced the primary endpoint. aHRs increased stepwise across CCTA-PET categories. Compared to normal CCTA, non-obstructive CAD and obstructive CAD without ischaemia were associated with a higher risk of the combined primary endpoint (aHR 1.89, [95%CI: 1.23-2.91], p=0.004; aHR 3.20, [95%CI: 1.95-5.25], p<0.001). Among patients with obstructive CAD on CCTA, PET-derived ischaemia further increased the risk of the primary endpoint (aHR 1.55, [95%CI: 1.05-2.30]; p=0.029), but not when excluding UA from the composite endpoint (aHR 1.37, [95%CI 0.90-2.07]; p=0.141). PET-derived ischaemia primarily predicted events within the first year, while obstructive CCTA findings remained associated with long-term hard outcomes.

Conclusions

A sequential strategy combining CCTA and quantitative [15O]H2O PET provides robust and incremental long-term risk stratification. While PET-derived ischaemia refines prediction of short-term and symptom-driven events, CCTA-derived CAD remains the principal determinant of long-term hard outcomes.

title: Sex-based differences in the atrial fibrillation care pathway and outcomes: an ITHACA-database analysis.
authorString: Coleman KM, Bekiaridou A, Miller L, Gianos E, Parikh N, Brennan C, Roswell RO, Woods B, Smith K, Cohn E, Rosen SE, Mieres JH, Mountantonakis SE.
abstractText: To characterize sex-specific differences in clinical presentation, evaluate progression through the atrial fibrillation (AF) care pathway from diagnosis to catheter ablation (CA) and assess long-term outcomes. This was a retrospective cohort study of patients with incident AF at Northwell Health between 2015 and 2024 from the ITHACA-database. Sex-specific differences in clinical presentation were examined. The AF care pathway was operationalized as a stepwise cascade, modelling conditional drop-off to identify care gaps. Sex-specific CA risk ratios were assessed via Poisson regression. Incident AF was identified among 165 563/655 459 patients (71.4 ± 11.6 years, 32% non-white, 45% female) with a recorded diagnosis of AF. Women were older (73.3 ± 10.6 vs. 69.8 ± 12.1 years, P < 0.001), had higher rates of dementia (9.1% vs. 5.2%), stroke (8.6% vs. 7.4%) and congestive heart failure (21.5% vs. 20.8%) at diagnosis. Transfer-of-care gaps [median 3.6 years follow-up, 96% retention] were identified at every level: 31.5% of women vs. 35.3% of men were evaluated by cardiology, 16.2% vs. 21.6% by electrophysiology, and 3.5% vs. 5.7% underwent CA (all P < 0.001). Women were 16% less likely to receive CA (RR 0.84 95% CI 0.77-0.91). In cause-specific Cox models, female sex was associated with incident stroke (aHR 1.24, 95% CI 1.18-1.30) and dementia (aHR 1.30, 95% CI 1.24-1.35), but modestly lower mortality after adjustment (aHR 0.96, 95% CI 0.94-0.99). In this real-world analysis, significant sex-specific differences in clinical phenotype at presentation, progression through the AF care pathway and clinical outcomes were observed.

abstractText: National Healthcare Safety Network cardiac Current Procedural Terminology codes incompletely capture Society of Thoracic Surgeons index procedures, especially in infants. Adding 62 pediatric codes increased validation-period sensitivity from 77.0% to 97.4%. Most additional captures were STS index procedures, although some non-index operations appeared potentially relevant to surgical site infection surveillance.

title: The interplay of insulin resistance and systemic inflammation on cancer history: a nationally representative cross-sectional study from NHANES.
authorString: Wang X.
abstractText:
Aim

To investigate whether systemic inflammation, measured by the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), modifies the cross‑sectional association between insulin resistance (IR, assessed by HOMA-IR) and overall cancer history in a nationally representative population.

Methods

We conducted a cross-sectional analysis utilizing data from the 2017-2018 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), which employs a complex, multistage probability sampling design. All analyses accounted for the complex survey design and sampling weights to ensure national representativeness. Weighted multivariable logistic regression was used to assess the cross‑sectional association, with an interaction term between HOMA-IR and NLR.

Results

Among 3,746 adults, after adjusting for age, sex, and BMI, HOMA-IR was not independently associated with cancer history (OR = 1.00, 95% CI 0.98-1.02). The HOMA-IR × NLR interaction term was not statistically significant (P for interaction = 0.359), indicating no significant effect modification by NLR.

Conclusion

In this nationally representative sample, we found no evidence that systemic inflammation, as measured by NLR, amplifies the cross‑sectional association between IR and overall cancer history. The potential synergistic effect may be confined to specific high-risk subgroups or inflammatory pathways.

title: Exploration of various administration routes for the nitric oxide donating organic nitrite, nitrosooxypropanol, in a porcine model.
authorString: Stene Hallerbäck A, Edström M, Agvald P, Nilsson KF.
abstractText: Organic nitrites are restricted to intravenous or inhaled administration. The aim was to explore novel administration routes for an organic nitrite, previously demonstrated to have pulmonary selectivity, in normal and elevated pulmonary vascular resistance. Hemodynamic and respiratory variables, including fraction of exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO), were measured in 13 anesthetized pigs. In naïve conditions, nitrosooxypropanol (PDNO) was given subcutaneously (100-1600 nmol/kg/min; 5 min/dose, 30 min interval), intramuscularly (50-400 nmol/kg/min; 5 min/dose, 30 min interval), intravenously (5-80 nmol/kg/min; 30 min infusion), intranasally (500-2000 nmol/kg boli), and sublingually (80-16,240 nmol/kg boli). In pulmonary hypertension (intravenous infusion of U46619), PDNO was given intravenously (5-45 nmol/kg/min; 15-20 mins infusion/dose) and subcutaneously (200-1800 nmol/kg/min; 5 min/dose at 20 min interval). Recovery was calculated using FeNO. PDNO, given by all administration routes, dose-dependently decreased systemic blood pressure and increased FeNO. Subcutaneous and intramuscular administration induced slow-onset (9 min to maximum effect) and long-lasting effects (~30 min). Intravenous administration induced rapid effects (1-2 min to steady state) and prompt decline after infusion cessation. The proportion of PDNO reaching exhaled gas (intravenous administration as reference; FeNO-based recovery) was 17% (intramuscularly) and 9% (subcutaneously). In pulmonary hypertension, intravenous and subcutaneous administration decreased the pulmonary/systemic vascular resistance-ratio. In this exploratory proof-of-concept study evaluating novel administration routes for organic nitrites, PDNO demonstrated measurable biological effects and acceptable FeNO-based recovery following intramuscular and subcutaneous administration. Furthermore, intranasal and tentatively sublingual administration showed biological effects. Future work on formulation and investigations into relevant disease models is warranted.

title: Maternal Ascites as an Atypical Presentation of Severe Preeclampsia: A Case Report.
authorString: Rayburn K, Cottrell J, Pauley A.

journal.title: The American journal of case reports

abstractText: BACKGROUND Preeclampsia is a multisystem hypertensive disorder of pregnancy associated with significant maternal and fetal morbidity. Although third spacing and fluid accumulation may occur in severe disease, maternal ascites is an uncommon manifestation. Recognition of this atypical presentation is important to facilitate timely diagnosis and appropriate management. CASE REPORT We present the case of a 23-year-old woman at 30 weeks and 2 days of gestation who developed severe preeclampsia superimposed on chronic hypertension, complicated by marked maternal third spacing and large-volume ascites while admitted for fetal growth restriction with intermittent absent end-diastolic flow on umbilical artery Doppler. Her clinical course was notable for profound capillary leak syndrome with significant fluid accumulation, including ascites (1.8 L) and pleural effusions. The extent of third spacing represented an unusual manifestation of severe hypertensive disease and created additional diagnostic and management considerations. Careful clinical assessment and recognition of the relationship between her fluid accumulation and severe preeclampsia were essential to guiding management and determining the need for delivery in the setting of maternal and fetal risk. CONCLUSIONS Severe preeclampsia may present with atypical manifestations beyond the classic features of hypertension and proteinuria. Profound capillary leak with marked third spacing, large-volume ascites, and pleural effusions can occur and may complicate the clinical evaluation of affected patients. Awareness of the uncommon presentation may facilitate earlier recognition of disease severity and prevent delays in management. In patients with severe hypertensive disease and unexplained fluid accumulation, preeclampsia should remain an important consideration. Prompt recognition of maternal or fetal deterioration and timely escalation of care are critical to optimizing outcomes and expediting delivery when clinically indicated.

title: Clinical characteristics of paediatric-onset type 2 diabetes: a comparison by weight status in the Hong Kong childhood diabetes registry 2008 to 2023.
authorString: Chan SS, Tung JY, Chan KT, But BW, Wong SM, Yam WI, Cheung PT, See WS, Yu GC, Chan KY, Yau HC, Wong WY, Wong LM, Chan CS, Fu AC, Kwan EY, Lai TS, Lo PW, Lam YY, Yuen HW, Wong SW, Ying-Ki Chung J, Tay MK, Poon SW.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

abstractText:
Objectives

Although obesity is a major risk factor for paediatric type 2 diabetes (T2DM), many Asian youths present without obesity. This phenotype remains under-recognised and poorly described. This study aimed to compare the clinical and metabolic characteristics of children newly diagnosed with T2DM, stratified by weight status, in Hong Kong.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study using data from the Hong Kong Childhood Diabetes Registry (2008-2023). We compared the clinical and metabolic features of children with and without obesity who were newly diagnosed with T2DM.

Results

A total of 689 children (96 % Chinese) were included and 35 % were children without obesity. While age at diagnosis was similar between groups, children without obesity exhibited a higher prevalence of family history of T2DM (80.6 % vs. 67.5 %; p<0.0001), more frequent presentations of classical symptoms and diabetic ketoacidosis with or without hyperosmolar hyperglycaemia state (4.6 % vs. 1.6 %, p=0.0262), and higher HbA1c and blood glucose levels at diagnosis, with lower HOMA-%B, suggesting greater β-cell dysfunction. Conversely children with obesity had higher insulin resistance. They also had higher prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), hypertension, hyperuricaemia, obstructive sleep apnoea, and polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Insulin therapy was more frequently required at diagnosis in children without obesity (16.3 % vs. 8 %, p=0.001).

Conclusions

These results highlight a distinct T2DM phenotype in Chinese children without obesity, marked by severe hyperglycaemia and a higher rate of insulin requirement at diagnosis. Increased clinical vigilance for this under-recognised group is warranted to optimise management at diagnosis, with long term outcomes to be address in future longitudinal studies.
