title: Association Between Weight Loss on Incretin-Based Therapy and Cardiovascular Outcomes and Mortality: A Systematic Review and Meta-Regression.
authorString: Skelin M, Perkov-Stipičin B, Bračić V, Škugor ZM, Krečak I.
abstractText: The primary aim was to evaluate, using aggregate-data meta-regression, whether body weight loss induced by incretin mimetic therapy is associated with reductions in three-point major adverse cardiovascular events (3P-MACE), individual cardiovascular outcomes and mortality. A secondary aim was to estimate the overall cardiovascular effects of incretin mimetics compared with placebo. A systematic review of placebo-controlled randomized trials was conducted using MEDLINE, EMBASE, CENTRAL and ClinicalTrials.gov. Eligible trials reported cardiovascular hazard ratios (HRs) and weight changes. The primary analysis was an aggregate-data meta-regression, with the prespecified moderator defined as the placebo-adjusted percentage weight difference at the latest reported follow-up time point. Standard meta-analysis was performed to estimate overall treatment effects. Sixteen randomized trials including 97 199 participants with and without diabetes were analysed. Meta-regression showed no statistically significant association between greater body weight loss and treatment HRs for 3P-MACE, cardiovascular or all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke and hospitalization for heart failure (HHF). These findings do not establish an individual-level or causal relationship. Meta-analysis showed significant reductions in 3P-MACE (15%), cardiovascular mortality (13%), all-cause mortality (12%), myocardial infarction (14%), stroke (13%) and HHF (10%). Greater trial-level placebo-adjusted body weight loss was not significantly associated with lower treatment HRs for the cardiovascular and mortality outcomes examined, including 3P-MACE and HHF. These findings do not exclude an individual-level contribution of weight loss to cardiovascular benefit or establish causality. Individual-participant-level analyses are needed to clarify the relationship between weight loss and cardiovascular outcomes.

title: Choosing Between On-Pump and Off-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: Contemporary Evidence for Patient Selection and Clinical Decision-Making.
authorString: Zhang Y, Ren C.
abstractText: On-pump (ONCAB) and off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OPCAB) remain established approaches to surgical myocardial revascularization, but contemporary evidence does not support a universal preference for either technique. The clinically relevant question is which patient and operative setting are most likely to benefit from each strategy. We performed a contemporary narrative evidence synthesis of landmark randomized trials, long-term follow-up studies, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, observational cohorts, graft-patency studies, and major coronary revascularization guidelines. MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched for studies published from 2009 through 2025. Evidence was organized around perioperative neurologic, renal, bleeding, and respiratory outcomes; completeness of revascularization; graft patency; conversion to cardiopulmonary bypass; surgical experience; and long-term survival. No de novo meta-analysis was performed, and all pooled estimates reported in this review are explicitly attributed to previously published evidence syntheses. Randomized evidence indicates broadly similar long-term mortality between OPCAB and ONCAB, whereas OPCAB may reduce selected perioperative complications, particularly stroke, transfusion, acute kidney injury, and respiratory morbidity in appropriately selected patients. Conversely, complex coronary anatomy may favor ONCAB because a stable operative field can facilitate complete revascularization. Conversion from OPCAB to cardiopulmonary bypass is consistently associated with worse outcomes, underscoring the importance of surgeon and institutional experience. Graft-patency differences are most evident for saphenous vein grafts and technically challenging territories. Anaortic or no-touch OPCAB may be particularly valuable in patients with extensive ascending-aortic atherosclerosis. ONCAB and OPCAB should therefore be viewed as complementary strategies. Selection should integrate aortic pathology, ventricular function, renal and bleeding risk, coronary complexity, the probability of complete revascularization, and local OPCAB expertise. A patient-tailored framework can help translate heterogeneous comparative evidence into practical clinical decision-making.

title: Percutaneous coronary intervention or medical therapy alone before transcatheter aortic valve replacement: insights from a meta-analysis of randomized trials.
authorString: Mohamed AE, Abomohsen M, Maqsood MH, Almakadma AH, Kholeif Z, Gadelmawla AF, Harari R, Kodali SK, Elgendy IY, Bangalore S.
abstractText:
Background

Coronary artery disease frequently coexists in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), yet the benefit of routine percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) before TAVR remains uncertain.

Objectives

To evaluate the efficacy and safety of routine PCI before TAVR compared with conservative or deferred revascularization.

Methods

We pooled randomized clinical trials comparing PCI before TAVR versus no/deferred PCI in patients with concomitant coronary artery disease. Random-effects models estimated pooled relative risks (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Bayesian sensitivity analyses and trial sequential analysis were performed.

Results

Three trials included 1156 patients (PCI, n = 579; no/deferred PCI, n = 577). In comparator arms reporting postrandomization PCI/revascularization, 72 of 461 patients (15.6%) underwent subsequent PCI/revascularization. PCI did not significantly reduce major adverse cardiac events (RR: 0.91, 95% CI: 0.70-1.18; I2 = 36.9%), myocardial infarction (RR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.45-1.63; I2 = 49.8%), all-cause death (RR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.70-1.15; I2 = 0.0%), or stroke (RR: 0.70, 95% CI: 0.48-1.03; P = 0.069; I2 = 0.0%). In two trials, PCI reduced urgent revascularization (RR: 0.33, 95% CI: 0.13-0.87; I2 = 54.5%) but increased major bleeding (RR: 1.57, 95% CI: 1.07-2.32; I2 = 37.9%) and any bleeding (RR: 1.77, 95% CI: 1.27-2.47; I2 = 66.7%). Bayesian analyses were directionally concordant. Trial sequential analysis was inconclusive for all efficacy outcomes.

Conclusion

Routine PCI before TAVR reduced urgent revascularization but increased bleeding, without significant differences in other outcomes. Current evidence remains underpowered to rule out benefit for other ischemic outcomes; larger trials are needed.

title: Effect-site concentrations of remifentanil to suppress coughing during emergence from general anesthesia in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Kim N, Park JH, Kim S, Lee JW, Kim MS.

journal.title: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie

abstractText: Remifentanil infusion titrated to effect-site concentration (Ce) is commonly used to suppress coughing during emergence from general anesthesia; nevertheless, the optimal Ce range remains unclear. We aimed to conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis to synthesize the existing evidence on the optimal Ce values of remifentanil for cough suppression during emergence. We performed a comprehensive literature search using PubMed®, Embase®, Web of Science™, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar on 27 February 2025. We included prospective studies that used the up-and-down method to estimate the effective concentrations of remifentanil in 50% of patients (EC50) and 95% of patients (EC95) for suppressing coughing during emergence from general anesthesia with tracheal intubation in adult patients. We excluded studies in children or patients undergoing cardiac surgery, as well as those that only compared predefined Ce targets of remifentanil to determine optimal dosing. We obtained pooled estimates using a random-effects model with inverse-variance method, and heterogeneity was quantified using the I2 statistic. We assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias 2 tool for randomized trials and the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies for nonrandomized comparative or single-arm studies. The primary outcome was EC50 estimated using the up-and-down method, with secondary outcomes including model-based EC50 and EC95 estimates. We included 22 prospective studies comprising 857 adult participants, and none were assessed as being at a high risk of bias or of low methodologic quality. Based on 28 groups and 653 participants across 17 studies, the pooled mean EC50 from the up-and-down method was 2.0 ng·mL-1 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.8 to 2.3), with considerable heterogeneity (I2 = 74.5%). Based on 29 groups and 693 participants across 18 studies, the model-based EC50 was 1.9 ng·mL-1 (95% CI, 1.6 to 2.1), with considerable heterogeneity (I2 = 96.1%). Based on 31 groups and 809 participants across 20 studies, the model-based EC95 was 2.7 ng·mL-1 (95% CI, 2.5 to 3.0), with considerable heterogeneity (I2 = 99.5%). Subgroup analyses revealed higher mean EC50 values in male individuals (2.6 ng·mL-1) and the highest mean EC50 in patients undergoing video-assisted thoracic surgery (2.6 ng·mL-1). Using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation framework, the certainty of evidence was rated as very low for all outcomes. The identified EC50 and EC95 values of remifentanil for suppressing coughing during emergence from general anesthesia in adults were 2.0 and 2.7 ng·mL-1, respectively. Patient sex and surgical type may influence the required Ce. Careful dose adjustment is recommended to avoid delayed awakening and hypoventilation, especially in cases requiring higher concentrations. PROSPERO ( CRD42024623581 ); first submitted 20 December 2024.

title: Safety and Tolerability of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitors: A State-of-the-Art Narrative Review.
authorString: Kunutsor SK, Seidu S.
abstractText: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2is) have evolved from glucose-lowering agents to foundational therapies for the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease, with substantial benefits for cardiovascular, kidney, and survival outcomes. As their indications continue to expand, a comprehensive understanding of their safety and tolerability has become increasingly important for optimizing patient care. Building on our recent state-of-the-art review of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, this review provides a contemporary synthesis of the evidence on the safety and tolerability of SGLT-2is. We critically appraise data from randomized controlled trials, cardiovascular and kidney outcome trials, pharmacovigilance databases, large observational studies, and systematic reviews and meta-analyses. The available evidence demonstrates that SGLT-2is have a favorable overall safety profile, with genital mycotic infections representing the most consistently observed adverse event. Volume depletion and euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis remain clinically important but are uncommon and are largely preventable through appropriate patient selection, patient education, and temporary treatment interruption during high-risk clinical situations. Fournier's gangrene should be regarded as a very rare but serious complication requiring prompt recognition and treatment. In contrast, randomized trials and meta-analyses generally indicate a reduced risk of acute kidney injury, while evidence concerning fracture, lower-limb amputation, hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis, and cancer is less definitive. Although consistent class-wide increases in these latter outcomes have not been established, uncommon or agent-specific risks cannot be excluded, particularly where event numbers are small or follow-up is limited. Overall, treatment discontinuation because of adverse events is low across major cardiovascular, heart failure, and kidney outcome trials, supporting the excellent tolerability of this therapeutic class. Comparative evidence suggests only modest differences among individual SGLT-2is, although definitive conclusions remain limited by the absence of direct, large, randomized head-to-head trials. We also summarize practical strategies for adverse-event mitigation, monitoring, temporary treatment interruption, and individualized patient selection. As the clinical applications of SGLT-2is continue to broaden, ongoing pharmacovigilance, inclusive clinical trials, and comparative safety studies will be essential to further refine their benefit-risk profile and optimize their safe use across diverse patient populations.

title: Management of established bronchopulmonary dysplasia after 36 weeks' postmenstrual age: an evidence-informed review.
authorString: Brumer E, Sanders MR, Sheehan J, Loechner K, Collins MS.

journal.title: Journal of perinatology : official journal of the California Perinatal Association

abstractText: To review available evidence in the management of established bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD). We conducted a structured, domain-specific narrative review of PubMed (MEDLINE) from 2000 to 2025, including randomized trials, cohort studies, systematic reviews, and clinical guidelines in preterm infants with established BPD, with qualitative synthesis across predefined management domains. Published studies support oxygen saturation targets of 90-95% for most infants, with slightly higher targets used for those with pulmonary hypertension. Chronic-phase ventilation strategies accommodating heterogeneous lung mechanics are associated with improved synchrony and gas exchange. Diuretics provide only a transient benefit and are associated with growth and electrolyte disturbances. Systemic corticosteroids may facilitate extubation in selected infants, while inhaled corticosteroids and bronchodilators lack evidence for routine use. Chronic management of established BPD is supported by limited data. Current evidence for infants after 36 weeks' PMA favors careful oxygen titration, chronic-phase ventilation strategies, and selective pharmacologic therapy.

title: Effectiveness of home-based exercise interventions on cardiorespiratory fitness and cancer treatment-related cardiovascular toxicity in cancer survivors exposed to cardiotoxic therapies: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
authorString: Wang W, Lee GA, Zhang W, Liu X.

journal.title: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer

abstractText: To evaluate the effectiveness of home-based exercise (HBE) interventions on cardiorespiratory fitness and cancer treatment-related cardiovascular toxicity (CTR-CVT) in cancer survivors. A comprehensive search of seven electronic databases was conducted for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published from January 2000 to October 2025. The participants were cancer survivors who had received cardiotoxic therapies. The interventions were structured HBE programmes. Eligible studies were those that reported on any outcomes related to CTR-CVT. The primary outcomes included direct cardiotoxicity parameters (e.g., left ventricular ejection fraction [LVEF] and global longitudinal strain [GLS]) and cardiac biomarkers (e.g., troponins and B-type natriuretic peptide); clinical cardiovascular events (e.g., heart failure and arrhythmias); cardiorespiratory fitness (e.g., peak oxygen uptake [VO2 peak]); and (d) functional capacity (e.g., the six-minute walk test [6MWT]). Two researchers independently performed the study selection, data extraction, and methodological quality assessment. Meta-analyses were conducted using R software. Ten RCTs involving 851 participants were included. The meta-analysis demonstrated that the HBE interventions significantly improved VO2 peak (MD = 2.35 mL/kg/min, 95% CI: 1.26 to 3.43, p < 0.001), which indicated improved cardiorespiratory fitness. Subgroup analysis found larger effects for longer-duration interventions (24 to 52 weeks), mHealth use, and cancer Stage III/IV. Evidence on direct cardiotoxicity parameters and biomarkers was limited, as only one study assessed these outcomes. No significant improvements were found in the 6MWT or health-related quality of life (HRQoL). While HBE improved cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2 peak) and mitigated functional decline in cancer survivors, its ability to prevent CTR-CVT was unproven. Future adequately powered trials should incorporate direct cardiotoxicity assessments to establish true cardioprotective efficacy and implementation studies to optimise real-world delivery. not applicable.

title: Haemorrhagic Transformation in Breakthrough Ischemic Stroke: Clinical Characteristics, Outcomes, and Anticoagulation Resumption Timing-Insights from the ASPERA-R Study.
authorString: D'Anna L, Foschi M, Gabriele F, Ornello R, Zini A, Paolucci M, Forlivesi S, Gentile M, Urbinati G, Cascio Rizzo A, Sessa M, Schwarz G, Tortorella R, Prandin G, Miserocchi LM, Balducci G, Desai G, Pantoni L, Mele F, Scopelliti G, Cova I, Valente M, Merlino G, Maisano D, Antonelli L, Bagnato MR, Di Mauro G, Bernocchi F, Di Donna MG, Casolla B, Mbakop-Noukoua S, Arnoffi P, Bun SS, Gonzalez-Martín L, Rigual R, Fuentes B, Hervás C, Candelaresi P, Andreone V, De Mase A, Spina E, Aguiar de Sousa D, Almudi Souza M, Fior A, Serôdio M, Caliandro P, Zauli A, Reale G, Abdelalim A, Ahmed SM, Ismail SA, Zhang L, Latimer T, Elboghdany M, Elbassiouny A, Roushdy T, Shokri HM, Ferrari F, Loizzo N, Mazzacane F, Guarino M, Barone V, Forti P, Rinaldi G, Rossi M, Laterza V, Frisullo G, Rizzo PA, Broccolini A, Mannino M, Terruso V, Caggiula M, Scalise S, Fonseca ACG, Antunes B, Budinčević H, Crnac P, Viticchi G, Silvestrini M, Musienko V, Abu-Rumeileh S, Barba L, Otto M, Lochner P, Landau B, Buddha S, Khalil R, Piscaglia MG, Zedde M, Nasreldein A, Vinciguerra L, Costa LR, Elsayed A, AlBanna M, Tudisco L, Mosconi MG, De Santis F, Sacco S.

journal.title: International journal of stroke : official journal of the International Stroke Society

abstractText: The timing of anticoagulation resumption in patients who experience ischemic stroke despite ongoing anticoagulation and develop haemorrhagic transformation (HT) remains uncertain. We aimed to describe the characteristics and outcomes of patients with HT after a breakthrough ischemic stroke and to explore the association between anticoagulation resumption timing and the model-predicted balance of recurrent ischemic and bleeding risks in this high-risk population. We analysed data from patients with breakthrough ischemic stroke receiving anticoagulation therapy from the multicentre ASPERA-R registry. Analyses focused on patients with HT. HT was defined according to the Heidelberg Bleeding Classification based on brain imaging within 24 hours and categorized as haemorrhagic infarction (HI) or parenchymal hematoma (PH). Anticoagulation resumption and its timing were determined by treating clinicians and were not randomized. Landmark Cox regression models were used to evaluate recurrent ischemic events and moderate-to-severe bleeding after anticoagulation resumption. Restricted cubic spline models and exploratory net clinical benefit analyses integrating ischemic and bleeding risks were used to assess the relationship between anticoagulation resumption timing and model-predicted combined risk, overall and across clinically relevant subgroups. Among 1,555 patients with breakthrough ischemic stroke, 269 (17.3%) developed HT, of whom 170 (63.2%) resumed anticoagulation and contributed to the restart-timing analyses. At 90 days, patients with HT had higher crude rates of recurrent ischemic events (27.1% vs 13.8%), moderate-to-severe bleeding (7.4% vs 2.8%), and mortality (34.2% vs 17.7%) compared with patients without HT. In landmark analyses, HT was not associated with recurrent ischemic events (HR 1.42, 95% CI 0.85-2.37) but remained strongly associated with moderate-to-severe bleeding (HR 3.39, 95% CI 1.61-7.13). Exploratory net clinical benefit analyses showed that the model-predicted combined risk reached its nadir at approximately 10 days after stroke in the overall HT population, with substantial uncertainty around this estimate. HT is a marker of poor prognosis in patients with breakthrough ischemic stroke, with an increased risk of bleeding after anticoagulation resumption. Among selected patients who resumed anticoagulation, exploratory modelling suggested that the combined predicted ischemic and bleeding risk reached its nadir at approximately 10 days after stroke. Given the non-randomized treatment timing and potential for treatment-selection bias, this estimate is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective validation.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Cardiovascular Health Behavior Change: A Narrative Review of Patient-Facing Tools.
authorString: Wu CF, Hernandez R, da Cruz Souza F, Yang F, He J.

journal.title: Health education & behavior : the official publication of the Society for Public Health Education

abstractText: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death in the United States and disproportionately affects racial/ethnic minoritized populations, low-income communities, older adults, and rural residents. Behavioral interventions can reduce cardiovascular risk, yet traditional programs face scalability barriers, including high costs and limited reach. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on the efficacy and equity of patient-directed AI tools that support health education and behavior change for cardiovascular health. Using PRISMA-ScR elements, we searched 10 databases (January 2010 to December 2025), yielding 19 empirical studies evaluating Generation 2.0 AI systems aligned with the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (LE8) framework. Of these, five were randomized controlled trials (RCTs), and 14 were nonrandomized (quasi-experimental, observational, or early-stage) studies. AI-enabled interventions such as conversational agents, machine-learning models, and reinforcement-learning systems addressed hypertension, diabetes, heart failure, and related conditions. Among the RCTs, one demonstrated superiority of an AI-powered program over usual care (AI-delivered Diabetes Prevention Program), whereas the remaining four reported outcomes equivalent or non-inferior to standard behavioral care. Effects were most apparent in high-intensity interventions that paired machine learning-based personalization with structured behavioral curricula, although the multi-component nature of these programs limits inference about AI-specific contributions. Across nonrandomized studies, greater engagement intensity was consistently associated with improved cardiometabolic outcomes, although causal attribution to AI-specific mechanisms remains limited. Most studies had small samples, short follow-up, and limited reporting on safety and equity. Technology-intensive interventions were concentrated in higher-resourced settings, and populations with limited health literacy showed reduced engagement. Overall, evidence supports cautious optimism that AI can meaningfully scale personalized cardiovascular prevention; however, realizing that equitable and clinically meaningful impact will require rigorous trials with longer follow-up, explicit behavioral science integration, safety-conscious governance, and equity-centered strategies addressing digital determinants of health.

title: Decoding Stroke-Heart Syndrome: A Translational Framework Linking Cerebral Injury to Cardiovascular Dysfunction.
authorString: Ahad A, Hullon D.
abstractText: Acute ischemic stroke can trigger cardiac injury independent of primary coronary disease, producing manifestations ranging from troponin elevation and electrocardiographic abnormalities to arrhythmias, left ventricular dysfunction, Takotsubo syndrome, and sudden cardiac death, collectively termed stroke-heart syndrome. Cardiac complications affect roughly a quarter of patients within the first month, cluster in the first days, and are the second most frequent cause of death after stroke; older patients, those with severe or insular strokes, those with cardiometabolic comorbidity, and women are disproportionately affected. We propose the Neurocardiac Injury Cascade, an eight-stage framework comprising brain lesion, central autonomic network disruption, catecholamine storm, immune activation, coronary microvascular dysfunction, myocardial injury, electrical instability, and cardiac remodeling. Stages three to five are explicitly modeled as a concurrent, mutually reinforcing module rather than as sequential steps, and each stage is given a definition, an expected time window, and a measurable signature. By organizing these events sequentially, the model links mechanisms with biomarker evolution, imaging findings, and stage-specific therapeutic opportunities. We further propose that chronic comorbidity, principally hypertension and diabetes, does not add stages but sets the gain at existing ones, which has direct consequences for the design of preclinical models and clinical trials. We highlight the role of the insular cortex and lateralized autonomic output, position Takotsubo syndrome as the severe phenotype of the cascade, and address the heterogeneity of post-stroke troponin elevation. This framework integrates diagnosis, risk stratification, and mechanism-based therapies to advance precision neurocardiology and guide future translational and clinical research.

title: Dapagliflozin vs. Acetazolamide in Patients With Acute Heart Failure: A Randomized Controlled Trial (CHOICE-AHF).
authorString: Sharaf H, Wadie M, Mansour NO, Shams MEE.
abstractText: Early adjunctive therapies may improve decongestion and symptoms in acute heart failure. This trial compared dapagliflozin with acetazolamide when initiated early, focusing on dyspnea relief as the primary outcome and decongestive, diuretic, natriuretic, and safety outcomes. In this randomized, active-controlled trial, 108 adults hospitalized with acute heart failure, dyspnea, and objective evidence of congestion requiring intravenous loop diuretics were randomized to receive dapagliflozin 10 mg (N = 55) or acetazolamide 500 mg (N = 53) once daily for 3 days alongside standard care. The primary endpoint was the between-group difference in 72-hour dyspnea visual analog scale area under the curve. Secondary endpoints included successful decongestion within 3 days, diuretic and natriuretic responses, the relative change in N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels from baseline to day 3, and safety. Acetazolamide produced a significantly lower 72-hour dyspnea area under the curve than dapagliflozin (2647.9 ± 1213.8 vs. 2988.7 ± 1196.7 mm × hour; P = 0.048). It increased cumulative urine output over 72 hours (12,200 vs. 10,000 mL; P = 0.019) and total natriuresis over 48 hours (824.7 vs. 547.9 mmol; P = 0.001). Dapagliflozin achieved a larger reduction in N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide at 72 hours (-34.2% vs. -25.0%; P = 0.003). Safety events were infrequent and similar. In conclusion, acetazolamide provided greater dyspnea relief, diuresis, and natriuresis, whereas dapagliflozin produced a larger short-term reduction in N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide. Further studies are needed to validate these findings. Trial registration: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06783166.

title: Dose-Exposure-Response Analysis of Finerenone on Serum Potassium and Cardiovascular Outcomes Among Patients With Heart Failure: Insights From FINEARTS-HF.
authorString: Eissing T, Mc Causland FR, Vaduganathan M, Goulooze SC, Marostica E, Berkhout J, van den Berg P, Snelder N, Garmann D, Lippert J, Brinker M, Claggett BL, McMurray JJV, Solomon SD.
abstractText: Finerenone reduces the risk of heart failure and cardiovascular (CV) death among patients with heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction (HFmrEF/HFpEF). Whether the effects of finerenone to reduce CV risk are dose/exposure dependent is not clear. In FINEARTS-HF, 6001 participants were randomized to finerenone or placebo, where the initial and target dose of finerenone was titrated according to the baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR; 10- > 20 mg if baseline eGFR ≤ 60; 20- > 40 mg if > 60 mL/min/1.73 m2) and by serum potassium and changes in eGFR during the trial. We fitted non-linear mixed-effects population pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic and parametric repeated time-to-event models to explore the effect of finerenone dose on exposure (n = 6658 plasma concentration measurements) and exposure on serum potassium (n = 123 720 measurements), NT-proBNP (n = 16 971 measurements) and the primary composite outcome of total heart failure events and CV death (n = 2366 events). The mean eGFR in those with an initial dose of 10 mg and 20 mg was 46 ± 12 and 76 ± 14 mL/min/1.73 m2, respectively. The frequency of hyperkalemia (> 5.5 mmol/L) was 4.3% in patients taking 10 mg finerenone, 2.7% among those taking 20 mg and 1.5% among those taking 40 mg. Simulated PK/PD data produced higher serum potassium with higher finerenone exposure in a hypothetical scenario without dose titration; however, when simulating the protocol-guided dose titration strategy implemented in the trial, the lower observed frequency of hyperkalemia at higher finerenone exposure was explained. For the efficacy exposure-response analyses, while higher finerenone exposure was non-significantly related to a lower frequency of CV composite events (p = 0.55), higher exposure did result in a significantly greater reduction in NT-proBNP concentrations (p < 0.001). Among participants of FINEARTS-HF, finerenone dose titration was effective in managing serum potassium concentration. Although FINEARTS-HF was not designed to test a randomized comparison of dose or exposure, the PK/PD model suggests that higher achieved exposure is associated with improved CV efficacy.

title: Beyond Weight Loss: A Scoping Review and Thematic Analysis of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Across the Neurosurgical Landscape.
authorString: Diamandi J, Aydin S, Chomelawala TF, O'Rourke E, Sen B, Zeeshan Q, Maroon JC.
abstractText: GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are increasingly used for diabetes and obesity. Literature spans spinal fusion, idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH), and cerebrovascular disease, but has not been systematically mapped. We aimed to map literature on GLP-1RA exposure in neurosurgical landscapes by characterizing study design, drug class, disease-specific outcomes, and safety considerations. This scoping review was conducted per the PRISMA-ScR guideline. Eligible studies reported GLP-1RA exposure in adults with spinal, intracranial, or cerebrovascular disease, recording clinical, perioperative, or imaging outcomes. Two reviewers screened independently with third-reviewer adjudication. Extracted variables included country, design, agent, timing, indication, neurosurgical and metabolic outcomes, and adverse events. Of 1342, 48 were included, predominantly from the United States (US) (34/48, 71%). Most were retrospective (43/48, 90%); 31/48 (65%) used propensity score matching; 5/48 (10%) were randomized. Three themes dominated: spinal fusion (24/48, 50%), IIH and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dynamics (14/48, 29%), and cerebrovascular and neurointerventional disease (10/48, 21%). In spinal fusion, perioperative GLP-1RA exposure was repeatedly associated with lower pseudarthrosis, although some studies reported increased postoperative complications. In IIH, GLP-1RAs were associated with lower papilledema, fewer CSF leaks, reduced acetazolamide requirement, and lower shunt placement. Cerebrovascular reports described lower intracerebral hemorrhage, subarachnoid hemorrhage, and post-stroke mortality, mostly in observational studies. GLP-1RA neurosurgical literature is dominated by US-based retrospective, propensity-matched analyses. Benefit signals are most consistent in spinal fusion and IIH, but perioperative adverse effects and overlap among database cohorts limit causal interpretation. Adequately powered prospective trials with standardized endpoints are needed to confirm results.

title: SGLT2 Inhibitors in Geriatric Heart Failure: Evidence, Safety, and Clinical Implementation.
authorString: Tokcan M, Hohl M, Altmayer LA, Kulenthiran S, Kessler T, Böhm M.
abstractText: This review summarizes the rationale, efficacy, safety, and implementation of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) in older adults with heart failure (HF). SGLT2i have become an integral part of contemporary HF therapy, with benefits demonstrated across the ejection fraction spectrum. Age subgroup analyses from randomized trials, frailty analyses, meta-analyses, and real-world cohorts suggest that benefits on HF hospitalization and cardiovascular outcomes are largely preserved in older and frail patients. Observational data in patients aged  ≥ 75 and > 80 years further support potential effectiveness in very old and multimorbid populations. However, geriatric vulnerability modifies clinical implementation, particularly regarding volume status, renal function, risk of falling, genitourinary infections, nutritional status, cognition, polypharmacy, and self-care capacity. Available evidence suggests that SGLT2i remain effective and are generally well tolerated in older patients with HF. Older age alone should therefore not preclude SGLT2i therapy. In geriatric HF, treatment decisions should be individualized according to frailty, comorbidity burden, safety risks, functional status, self-care capacity, and goals of care.

title: Cardiometabolic benefits of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and dual agonists: from obesity and diabetes to heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
authorString: Chotalia R, Ghias O, Shah MU, Hills CE, Ward JK, Squires PE, Andrews R, Venugopal V, Lee K, Gulsin G.
abstractText:
Introduction

Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) accounts for over half of all heart failure hospitalisations and is increasing in prevalence, largely driven by obesity and Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM). Glucagon-like-peptide receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and the dual GLP-1/GIP agonist, tirzepatide, have been shown to be safe and effective medications in the treatment of T2DM and obesity as well as in obesity-related HFpEF.

Areas covered

This review summarises the pathophysiology of obesity-related HFpEF, mechanisms by which GLP-1 RAs and tirzepatide may improve symptoms and outcomes, and summarise evidence from recent randomised controlled and observational trials across the disease spectrum they have been studied in. Therapeutic implications and future research directions are also discussed. A structured literature search was performed using PubMed/MEDLINE and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) up to August 2025.

Expert opinion

GLP-1 receptor agonists and tirzepatide represent a promising therapeutic advance for obesity-related HFpEF. Benefits are likely mediated through weight loss dependent and weight-loss independent mechanisms. Important uncertainties remain regarding their role in non-obese HFpEF, optimal patient selection, and their safety in HFrEF.

title: Endovascular Therapy in Intracranial Atherosclerotic Stenosis-Related Large Vessel Occlusion Stroke: A Brief Practice Update and Consensus Statement From the SVIN.
authorString: Al Kasab S, Abu Qdais A, Yaghi S, Guerrero WR, Majidi S, Abdalkader M, Limaye K, Zaidat OO, de Havenon A, Liebeskind DS, Chaudhari A, Kass-Hout T, Siddiq F, Kenmuir CL, Hassan AE, Spiotta AM, Czap AL, Samaniego EA, Jumaa M, Nguyen TN.
abstractText: Intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis-related large vessel occlusion (ICAS-LVO) represents a distinct subset of acute ischemic stroke with unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges during endovascular therapy. Compared with embolic LVO, ICAS-LVO is associated with higher rates of reocclusion and the frequent use of adjunctive interventions. This Brief Practice Update summarizes current evidence and expert consensus to guide the identification and management of ICAS-LVO during endovascular therapy. The Society of Vascular and Interventional Neurology Guidelines and Practice Standards committee convened a multidisciplinary writing group of neurointerventionalists to review available literature and define key clinical questions on ICAS-LVO and endovascular therapy. Evidence was appraised using the Society of Vascular and Interventional Neurology framework for Class of Recommendation and Level of Evidence, adapted from the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association. Draft statements were iteratively refined and approved by the Society of Vascular and Interventional Neurology Guidelines and Practice Standards Quality Committee for adherence to internal standards and endorsed by the Society of Vascular and Interventional Neurology Board of Directors. Evidence was derived from randomized trials, multicenter registries, cohort studies, post hoc analyses, and meta-analyses addressing diagnostic features, first-line thrombectomy strategies, and adjunctive therapies in ICAS-LVO. Both stent retriever and direct aspiration approaches are acceptable initial strategies; however, durable recanalization is only achieved in about half of patients. Adjunctive use of intravenous or intra-arterial glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitors, balloon angioplasty, and rescue stenting has demonstrated improved recanalization rates and favorable functional outcomes in observational studies, without increased hemorrhagic complications. However, the quality of evidence remains weak. A summary of recommendations is provided to guide practice in common procedural scenarios. This Brief Practice Update provides evidence-based and expert consensus recommendations for the diagnosis and endovascular treatment of ICAS-LVO. Management should be individualized by incorporating the clinical presentation, imaging characteristics, and operator expertise. While adjunctive therapy may be beneficial in select cases, high-quality randomized trials are needed to define optimal strategies and establish standardized algorithms for this challenging stroke subtype.

title: Forgotten electrolytes: magnesium and calcium flux during dialysis.
authorString: Hinojosa S, Ravi KS.

journal.title: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension

abstractText:
Purpose of review

Calcium and magnesium remain incompletely individualized in contemporary dialysis prescriptions despite growing evidence linking their concentrations to cardiovascular outcomes, vascular calcification, mineral metabolism, and mortality. The 2025 Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Controversies Conference report on chronic kidney disease (CKD)-mineral and bone disorder (MBD) and recent kinetic studies of intradialytic ion fluxes make a focused review of these "forgotten" divalent cations timely.

Recent findings

Intradialytic calcium mass transfer is influenced by patient- and prescription-level factors, and total serum calcium incompletely reflects biologically relevant calcium flux; ionized calcium may decline during dialysis as hemoconcentration increases albumin concentration and alkalosis increases albumin-bound calcium. Small randomized trials show that raising dialysate magnesium improves serum resistance to calcification, but whether higher dialysate magnesium improves clinical outcomes remains unknown. The 2025 KDIGO report retains the 1.25-1.50 mmol/l dialysate calcium range and identifies individualized calcium mass-transfer assessment as a research priority. Dial-Mag, a large pragmatic trial comparing higher versus conventional dialysate magnesium concentrations, is ongoing.

Summary

Recent evidence challenges the assumption that standardized dialysate calcium and magnesium prescriptions are optimal for all patients. Future studies should define patient-specific targets, validate practical methods to assess peridialytic calcium and magnesium levels and intradialytic flux, and determine whether individualized dialysate prescriptions improve clinical outcomes.

title: Impact of Low-Intensity Occlusive Cardiorespiratory Training on Office Blood Pressure and Physical Fitness in Adults with Hypertension
authorString: María MS, Minetto J, Cerri G, Collado S, Barreda¹ M, Staropoli F, Espeche W.
abstractText: Background Hypertension is the leading modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, underscoring the need for non-pharmacological strategies such as exercise to optimize blood pressure control. Although moderate-intensity continuous training (MICT) and high-intensity interval training (HIIT) are supported by substantial evidence, blood flow restriction (BFR) combined with low-intensity cardiorespiratory training (LICT) has emerged as a promising alternative because it imposes a lower workload. Objective To compare the effects of three cardiorespiratory training modalities—high-intensity interval training (HIIT), moderate-intensity continuous training (MICT), and low-intensity continuous training with blood flow restriction (LICT-BFR)—with those of a control group on office blood pressure and physical fitness in patients with hypertension. Methods This randomized controlled clinical study was conducted at the Cardiometabolic Diseases Unit of Hospital Interzonal General de Agudos San Martín in La Plata, Argentina. Sixty participants were assessed (mean age, 60 ± 6 years). After eight participants were excluded for clinical reasons, 52 participants remained: a control group (n = 15) and three exercise groups—HIIT (n = 10), MICT (n = 13), and LICT-BFR (n = 14). The intervention comprised 36 sessions, three times per week for 12 weeks. Results Loss to follow-up was 26.9%, and 38 participants completed the study. Compared with the control group, the exercise groups combined showed significant improvements in physical fitness and office blood pressure (p < 0.05), with no changes in body weight or waist circumference. All three protocols improved physical fitness; however, only LICT-BFR produced a statistically significant reduction in office diastolic blood pressure (DBP; p = 0.044). Conclusion Cardiorespiratory training is important for improving functional capacity and hemodynamic control in people with hypertension. LICT-BFR provided functional benefits comparable to those of traditional aerobic training and was associated with a statistically significant reduction in office DBP.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Routine Postdilation in Balloon-Expandable Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Platform: The DUOTAP Randomized Clinical Trial.
authorString: Autherith M, Singer K, Hauptmann L, Torrefranca C, Jantsch C, Koschatko S, Röglsperger EM, Halavina K, Heitzinger G, Dannenberg V, Palaparti R, Längle S, Mahr S, Demirel C, Coti I, Zimpfer D, Hengstenberg C, Nitsche C, Bartko PE.
abstractText:
Importance

In patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), asymmetric valve expansion can estimate prosthetic dysfunction and death. Postdilation has shown promising results in optimizing valve geometry in observational studies; however, randomized evidence is currently lacking.

Objective

To determine the efficacy of routine postdilation on transcatheter heart valve (THV) geometry and hemodynamic performance, and associated safety outcomes.

Design, setting, and participants

DUOTAP was a single-center, single-blinded randomized clinical trial. Recruitment took place from January 2025 to April 2026 and end points were assessed periprocedurally (fluoroscopy) at 30 days (adverse events) and at 3 months (computed tomography [CT]). The trial was conducted at a high-volume tertiary referral center, the Medical University of Vienna, Austria. Included patients had severe AS suitable for transfemoral TAVI with a balloon-expandable THV and without high-risk features on preprocedural CT or coronary angiography and were randomized in a 1:1 ratio, stratified by THV size, to routine postdilation vs no postdilation. These data were analyzed from July 2026 to September 2026.

Intervention

Routine postdilation using the original delivery balloon at the identical filling volume. A sham procedure was performed in the control group.

Main outcomes and measures

The fluoroscopic THV asymmetry index served as primary end point. Further fluoroscopic and CT-derived measures of valve geometry, hypoattenuated leaflet thickening (HALT), paravalvular leak (PVL), and THV hemodynamics on echocardiography, and freedom from major procedural adverse events served as secondary end points.

Results

Overall, 148 patients (median [IQR] age, 81 [77-85] years; 69 female [46.6%] and 79 male [53.4%]; median EuroSCORE-II, 2.3%) underwent randomization (n = 74 intervention vs n = 74 control). Intervention yielded a 70% lower THV asymmetry index compared with control (median: 1.2% vs 2.8%; geometric mean ratio: 0.30; 95% CI, 0.18-0.47; P < .001), with consistent effects across prespecified subgroups, induced by frame height reduction across the outer curve. Additionally, intervention yielded numerically larger THV diameters on fluoroscopy and significantly larger THV areas at the inflow, midframe, and outflow level on CT. HALT and mild or worse PVL were significantly less frequent and the Doppler Velocity Index was significantly higher in the intervention group. No differences in procedure-related adverse events between groups were recorded (χ2 test: P = .36).

Conclusions and relevance

In this randomized clinical trial, postdilation led to reduced THV asymmetry, optimized geometry, and improved hemodynamic performance, without increasing procedure-related adverse events. These results support the use of routine postdilation to optimize THV geometry and hemodynamics in suitable patients.

Trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07477002.

title: Next-generation incretin therapeutics for polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: navigating current pipeline and clinical considerations.
authorString: Ozgen Saydam B, Yıldız BO.
abstractText: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), formerly known as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is a complex metabolic-reproductive disorder managed with lifestyle interventions, metformin, and symptom-directed therapies. Incretin-based therapies offer substantial metabolic benefits, but their reproductive efficacy, durability, and phenotypic safety remain incompletely defined. This narrative review examines the therapeutic evolution from single glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists to dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 receptor agonism with tirzepatide and triple GIP/GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonism with retatrutide. A structured PubMed search of studies published from January 2023 to October 2026 was supplemented by ClinicalTrials.gov and reference-list screening. Evidence was evaluated across metabolic, hormonal, and reproductive outcomes. Single GLP-1 receptor agonists, particularly semaglutide, improve weight, adiposity, and insulin resistance, with emerging evidence of reproductive benefits. Multi-incretin therapies may provide greater reductions in body weight, visceral and ectopic fat, and insulin resistance. However, PMOS-specific reproductive evidence remains limited. Whether reproductive benefits are independent of weight loss, persist after treatment withdrawal, or differ across PMOS phenotypes is uncertain. Phenotype-stratified randomized trials with standardized reproductive, metabolic, cardiovascular and safety endpoints are needed to determine whether multi-incretins provide durable benefits beyond weight control while maintaining reproductive safety and accessibility.

title: Giving young patients with ADPKD a voice: preliminary validation of the 'Symptom and impact scale for adolescents with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease' (SAIL-ADPKD).
authorString: Willem L, Gimpel C, Vanmeerbeek L, Trouet D, Janssens P, Voets T, Vennekens R, Schaefer F, Mekahli D, Luyckx K.
abstractText: Unpredictable pain and reduced quality of life are common in adults with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) and occur even before gross kidney enlargement or markedly decreased kidney function. Very little is known about pain in adolescents with ADPKD, and there are no patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) in youth. An age-appropriate questionnaire on pain, impact, symptoms, and worries was created by pediatric nephrologists, clinical psychologists, pain specialists, patient representatives, and external reviewers. Self- and proxy-reported versions exist in English and Dutch. Psychometric validation included exploratory factor analysis for scale construction, assessment of internal consistency, test-retest reliability, and evaluation of content validity through correlations with established generic instruments. The validation cohort consisted of 46 patients with ADPKD aged 12-25 years (mean 19.3 ± 3.6 years). Subscores created according to factor analysis showed good internal consistency, especially for fatigue-, pain-, worry-, and disruption of everyday activities scores. Fatigue and total pain & fullness scores correlated well with the PedsQL physical functioning score (both r = -0.65, p < 0.0001). Disruption of everyday life converged with the PROMIS pain interference T-score (r = 0.76, p < 0.0001) and PedsQL scores, and total worry score with PedsQL emotional functioning score (r = -0.57, p = 0.0001). Repeatability was assessed with test-retest correlations after a median of 1.7 months (n = 35), and convergence of subjective and parental assessment with self-proxy correlations (n = 20). This initial validation of an age- and disease-specific PROM capturing pain, impact, symptoms, and worries in youth with ADPKD supports its suitability for further studies and clinical trials.

title: Intra-Prostatic Epinephrine injection in Bipolar Transurethral resection of large prostate: Exploring Its Role in Optimizing Surgical Outcomes
authorString: ALhefnawy MA, Mohamed SA, Abdelraouf A, Elbashir SEM, Fattah AAEA.
abstractText: Background Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is a common condition in aging men, with transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) remaining the gold standard surgical intervention. Perioperative bleeding represents one of the most significant complications, particularly in large prostates. Intraprostatic epinephrine injection has been proposed as a hemostatic adjunct. This study evaluates the efficacy of intraprostatic epinephrine injection during bipolar TURP in reducing blood loss and improving surgical outcomes. Methods In this single-center randomized controlled trial, 80 men with symptomatic BPH and prostate volumes of 80–100 mL were allocated equally to bipolar TURP with intraprostatic injection of either epinephrine (200 mcg in 20 mL saline) or saline alone. Patients with cardiovascular comorbidities were excluded. Perioperative blood loss (irrigation-fluid hemoglobin method), transfusion requirement, resection time, operative vision, complications, and follow-up functional outcomes were compared. Results Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. Epinephrine reduced perioperative blood loss (median 87.5 vs 132.5 mL, p < 0.001) and eliminated blood transfusion (0% vs 12.5%, p = 0.021). Operative vision was rated excellent or good in 97.5% versus 85% (p = 0.048). Resection time was shorter (50.9 vs 77.6 minutes, p < 0.001) despite greater resected tissue weight (81.6 vs 71.4 g, p < 0.001), and postoperative hemoglobin decline was smaller (p < 0.001). Postoperative serum sodium and creatinine remained comparable between groups. Hospital stay was shorter with epinephrine (p = 0.004). Hypertension and arrhythmia occurred in 5% of epinephrine patients versus none of the controls (p = 0.494), other early complications were comparable. At follow-up, the epinephrine group showed a smaller residual prostate volume (7.6 vs 16.9 mL, p < 0.001) and a lower post-void residual volume (p = 0.015), with comparable symptom scores, flow rates, retrograde ejaculation, and re-operation rates. Conclusions Intraprostatic epinephrine during bipolar TURP significantly reduces bleeding and transfusion requirements, improves visualization, and enables faster, more complete resection without increasing cardiovascular risk. It is a simple, inexpensive, and readily available adjunct that merits routine use for large-volume prostates.

title: Risk of cardiovascular events and mortality associated with LDL and non-HDL cholesterol levels after statin initiation for primary prevention: A multiregional cohort study.
authorString: Blais JE, Akyea RK, Harrison W, Chan AHY, Zhong W, Weng SF, Beyene KA, Lau WCY, Man KKC, Qureshi N, Chan EWY, Wong ICK, Harrison J.
abstractText: The cardiovascular and mortality benefits of achieving guideline-recommended concentrations of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) and non-high-density lipoprotein (non-HDL) cholesterol with statins in primary prevention remain uncertain. In this new-user cohort study, we used electronic healthcare databases from Hong Kong (HK), New Zealand (NZ) and the United Kingdom (UK) to identify 185,237 patients initiating statins between 1 January 2007 and 31 December 2012 (with follow-up to 31 December 2017) without atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure, or chronic kidney disease. Associations between LDL and non-HDL cholesterol measured within 2 years post-initiation with the outcomes of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) or all-cause mortality were assessed in landmark analyses using multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, hypertension, atrial fibrillation, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidaemia, obesity, smoking, alcohol misuse, rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus and connective tissue disorders, severe mental illness, antihypertensive drugs, antidiabetic drugs, antiplatelet drugs, and anticoagulant drugs. Estimates were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. At 2 years, LDL cholesterol was <1.4 mmol/L in 7,084 (3.8%), 1.4-1.7 mmol/L in 21,893 (11.8%), 1.8-2.5 mmol/L in 81,941 (44.2%) and ≥2.6 mmol/L in 74,294 (40.1%) patients. Mean duration of follow-up for the primary outcome of MACE was 6.5 years in HK, 5.6 years in NZ and 5.4 years in UK. versus an LDL cholesterol ≥2.6 mmol/L, adjusted hazard ratios (HR) for MACE were 0.80 (95% CI [0.77,0.83]) for 1.8-2.5 mmol/L, 0.79 (0.66,0.94) for 1.4-1.7 mmol/L and 0.82 (0.60,1.12) for <1.4 mmol/L. Non-HDL cholesterol showed similar estimates for MACE (e.g., HR 0.75, [0.72,0.79] for 2.6-3.3 mmol/L versus ≥3.4 mmol/L). In continuous analysis, the association with MACE was approximately log-linear across achieved LDL and non-HDL cholesterol in HK and the UK, whereas in NZ estimates were less consistent and imprecise at the lowest concentrations. After adjustment for confounding factors, very low LDL (HR 1.06, [0.96,1.16]) and non-HDL cholesterol (HR 0.98, [0.84,1.14]) were not associated with all-cause mortality. Limitations include heterogeneity across cohorts, which may reflect confounding by indication where treatment intensity was guided by cardiovascular risk, and residual confounding from comorbidities, lifestyle interventions and disease severity. Estimates are also conditional on patients having initiated statins, survived to the landmark, and undergone follow-up lipid testing. Lower achieved LDL and non-HDL cholesterol after statin initiation was associated with a reduction in MACE, with limited evidence of an increase in all-cause mortality at very low concentrations after adjustment for confounding. Additional reductions in cardiovascular events could be obtained by achieving guideline-recommended non-HDL cholesterol levels of at least <3.4 mmol/L after statin initiation for primary prevention.

title: Prior Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting and Its Impact on Lesion Complexity, Procedural Characteristics, and Outcomes in Chronic Total Occlusion Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Azam H, Alam B, Javaid SS, Janjua H, Hasan SU, Lal R, Saad R, Shuja H, Pandey RK, Riaz A, Pooja L, Kiani SS, Zahid A, Haq A, Shah MN.
abstractText: Prior coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is associated with accelerated native vessel atherosclerosis and more complex chronic total occlusion (CTO) anatomy, rendering CTO-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) more challenging despite contemporary technical advances. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to compare CTO lesion characteristics, procedural demands, and in-hospital outcomes according to prior CABG status. PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar were systematically searched from inception through May 15, 2026, for studies comparing CTO-PCI outcomes in patients with and without prior CABG. Data were pooled using odds ratios (ORs) and standardized mean differences (SMDs). Twelve studies enrolling 47,434 patients, including 10,354 with prior CABG, were included. Compared with patients without prior CABG, those with prior CABG had higher rates of blunt stump morphology (OR 1.51 [1.42-1.61]), proximal cap ambiguity (OR 1.55 [1.45-1.66]), calcification (OR 2.49 [2.22-2.79]), vessel bending (OR 2.27 [1.27-4.05]), distal cap bifurcation (OR 1.73 [1.51-1.98]), and higher Multicenter CTO Registry of Japan scores (SMD 0.48 [0.40-0.56]). Procedural burden was greater, with higher contrast use, longer fluoroscopy time and procedure duration, and greater stent use. Technical success (OR 0.63 [0.43-0.92]) and procedural success (OR 0.60 [0.53-0.69]) were lower in the prior CABG group. In-hospital mortality (OR 2.19), myocardial infarction (OR 2.29), and contrast-induced nephropathy (OR 1.97) were higher, whereas cardiac tamponade was less frequent (OR 0.37). Prior CABG is associated with substantially greater CTO complexity, procedural burden, and in-hospital risk, underscoring the need for careful procedural planning and individualized risk stratification in this population.

title: Treatment Strategies and Outcomes of Aneurysms Affecting Small and Medium Arteries in Neurofibromatosis Type 1. A systematic review.
authorString: Sibiriu V, Lodico T, Borghese O, Pedicelli A, Tshomba Y.
abstractText:
Objective

Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1)-associated arterial aneurysms are rare and characterized by vessel fragility and heterogeneous presentation. Evidence guiding optimal management remains limited. This systematic review aimed to evaluate treatment strategies and outcomes in NF1-related arterial aneurysms.

Methods

A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251169825). PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for studies reporting management and outcomes of NF1-associated arterial aneurysms. Case reports, case series, and observational studies were included. Data were independently extracted by two reviewers. Primary outcomes included treatment strategies, technical success, complications, and mortality. Isolated aortic aneurysms or aortic dissections were not considered the primary target of the review. However, studies reporting concomitant aortic disease and aneurysmal involvement of non-aortic arteries were retained when relevant data on NF1-associated vasculopathy and its management were available.

Results

Eighty-six studies including 99 patients (mean age 42 years; 44.4% male) were analyzed. Aneurysms were most frequently located in cervico-vertebral (45.2%) and visceral arteries (24.0%). Multifocal disease was present in 12.1% of patients. Overall, 65.7% of patients presented with aneurysm rupture or acute hemorrhage. This high proportion should be interpreted cautiously because of the substantial publication bias inherent to a literature predominantly based on case reports and small case series. Endovascular therapy was the most frequently used approach (68.7%), followed by open surgery (19.2%), hybrid repair (5.0%), and conservative management (9.1%). Endovascular treatment showed a reported technical success rate exceeding 90%. Recanalization (6.3%), delayed thrombosis (4.2%), and new aneurysm formation (5.3%) were observed. Open repair was mainly used for anatomically complex or endovascularly inaccessible lesions. Overall mortality was 8.1%, primarily in patients presenting with rupture.

Conclusions

NF1-associated aneurysms require an individualized, anatomy-driven management strategy. Endovascular therapy was the most frequently reported treatment and appears to be a viable option in anatomically suitable patients, while open and hybrid techniques remain important for selected complex lesions. However, the available evidence is derived predominantly from case reports and small case series and does not permit comparative assessment of treatment strategies. Lifelong imaging surveillance is mandatory due to the risk of recurrence and new aneurysm formation.

title: Kidney Allograft Rupture Following Transplantation: A Scoping Review.
authorString: Bosire HM, Chothia MY.
abstractText: Kidney transplantation is the preferred therapy for kidney failure; however, complications still occur, among which kidney allograft rupture (KAR) is rare but potentially life-threatening. This scoping review aimed to map our current understanding of KAR, focusing on clinical presentation, causes of KAR, management strategies and patient and allograft outcomes. The review was guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews methodology. Eligible studies included case reports, case series and observational studies, including retrospective consecutive series, reporting case-level or aggregate data on KAR in adults. We searched Medline (PubMed), Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection from database inception to 5 March 2025 and re-ran all three searches without a study-design filter between 13 August and 4 September 2026. A total of 86 articles were included. One hundred and two cases of KAR were analysed at the individual-patient level, and 34 consecutive series or cohort studies, comprising 367 ruptures among 20 202 transplants, contributed aggregate data; 36 of the 102 individually reported cases were drawn from six of these series and are therefore common to both strands. The mean recipient age was 35 years, and 65% were male. Chronic glomerulonephritis (33%) and hypertension (18%) were the leading reported causes of kidney failure. Acute allograft rejection was the most common precipitating factor for rupture (58%), followed by renal vein thrombosis (14%) and acute tubular necrosis (13%). Clinical presentation was dominated by graft pain or tenderness (88%), a fall in haemoglobin (62%) and hypotension (57%). The allograft was preserved in 49 of 102 cases (48%) and 53 (52%) underwent nephrectomy. Across the 33 single-centre consecutive series, the pooled incidence of KAR was 1.84% (366/19 922; range between series 0.25%-10.75%), falling from 4.7% in series published before 1990 to 1.5% in those published from 1990 onwards, and 55% of ruptured grafts were preserved. Patient survival was 94%. KAR is a rare complication of kidney transplantation, occurring in approximately 2% of transplants in consecutive series and most often precipitated by acute allograft rejection. Its reported incidence has fallen roughly threefold since 1990. Just under half of ruptured allografts were preserved and half required nephrectomy. Graft preservation was reported in 62% of the standalone case reports that made up the original version of this review but in only 39% of cases described within consecutive series, indicating that the case-report literature materially overstates the likelihood of successful salvage. Patient survival was high.

title: Association Between Cardiovascular Disease and Cataracts: Protocol for a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Yap JF, Heng PP, Wan Mohamad Darani WNS, Mat Rifin H, Muhamad NA, Pong MY, Mohd Yusoff MF.
abstractText:
Background

There is emerging evidence suggesting shared pathophysiological mechanisms between cataracts and cardiovascular disease (CVD), indicating a potential link between these 2 prevalent noncommunicable diseases. Oxidative stress, resulting from an imbalance between reactive oxygen species production and the body's antioxidant defenses, contributes to lens protein aggregation in cataracts and lipid oxidation in atherosclerosis, a key feature of several CVD subtypes. This shared pathophysiology implies that systemic vascular health may influence cataractogenesis. However, the epidemiological evidence supporting this relationship remains inconclusive.

Objective

The main objective of this systematic review is to synthesize existing evidence on the odds or risk of developing cataracts in adults with underlying CVD.

Methods

This systematic review will adhere to the PRISMA-P (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Protocols). Using the population, exposure, comparator, and outcome framework, this review will identify the association between established CVD and the risk of cataract development or needing cataract surgery. Systematic literature searches will be conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase using MeSH terms from database inception to December 31, 2024. Original research articles involving adults (aged ≥18 years) that assess the statistical relationship between CVD and cataracts will be included. Two independent reviewers will screen studies, extract data, and appraise the studies' quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. If deemed feasible, meta-analyses will be conducted using random-effects models to calculate pooled effect estimates, with heterogeneity assessed using the I2 statistic.

Results

This study did not receive any external funding. The literature search, study screening, and data extraction will be conducted in 2026, and data analysis will be performed accordingly. The findings are anticipated to be published in 2027.

Conclusions

This systematic review will provide a consolidated and up-to-date evaluation of the relationship between CVD and cataracts. The findings will highlight the potential importance of integrating cardiovascular risk assessment into routine ophthalmologic care. Continued refinement of study methodologies and standardization of outcome measures may be needed to address observed heterogeneity and strengthen future evidence, ultimately supporting more holistic management of patients with coexisting cardiovascular and ocular conditions.

title: Molecular biomarkers associated with progression and adverse outcomes in human ascending thoracic aortic aneurysm: a systematic review protocol.
authorString: D'Anna T, Belmonte B, Mangogna A, Orlandi A, Balistreri CR.
abstractText:
Objective

This systematic review will identify, classify, and synthesize evidence on molecular biomarkers (circulating, tissue, genetic, epigenetic, proteomic, metabolomic, and inflammatory) associated with the progression and outcomes of ascending thoracic aortic aneurysm (ATAA) in human populations.

Introduction

ATAA is a heterogeneous condition driven by genetic, epigenetic, inflammatory, proteolytic, and metabolic alterations that are not completely understood. Current management relies mainly on aortic diameter and does not incorporate molecular data. Emerging evidence suggests that circulating, tissue, genetic, epigenetic, metabolic, and proteomic biomarkers may support diagnosis, improve prognostic assessment, identify high-risk patients, and clarify mechanisms of medial degeneration. Existing studies are fragmented and inconsistent, and are based on small observational cohorts, highlighting the need for a rigorous synthesis.

Eligibility criteria

This review will include observational studies that quantify molecular biomarkers in blood or biopsy samples from adult populations with ATAA.

Methods

We will search PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Scopus, Web of Science, trial registries, dissertations and theses databases, preprint repositories, and other gray literature sources for eligible evidence from 2015 to the present. Study selection, critical appraisal, and data extraction will follow the JBI methodology. A narrative synthesis will summarize the findings. Where sufficient clinical and methodological homogeneity exists, meta-analysis will be conducted using random-effects models. The certainty of evidence will be assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach adapted for prognostic and etiological research.

Review registration

PROSPERO CRD420251237933.

title: Correction to 'Effect of Medications for Type 2 Diabetes on Cardiovascular Events and Mortality: A Comprehensive Pairwise and Network Meta-Analysis'.
Primary Prevention ICD in a Contemporary Underserved Population: Factors Associated With Underutilization and Mortality.
authorString: Song JJ, Xu S, Gidon A, Matos C, Kallash M, Apple SJ, Jayant G, Marhaba R, Borck J, Zhang S, Kalani S, Yuan Y, Rodriguez CJ, Biase LD, Guttenplan NA, Fisher JD, Ferrick KJ.
abstractText:
Background

Registry studies from 2000-2010 demonstrated underutilization of primary prevention ICD therapy. As heart failure therapies have reduced sudden cardiac death, investigators have questioned guidelines derived from trials conducted two decades prior, particularly in non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) and elderly subgroups. We characterized contemporary referral determinants, decision-making processes, and outcomes of primary prevention ICD therapy in a diverse, under-represented population.

Methods

In this retrospective single-center cohort study, we reviewed records of all patients meeting Class I criteria for primary prevention ICD in 2019. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with ICD referral, and time-varying Cox models compared all-cause mortality by implantation status through 2022.

Results

Of 559 eligible patients, 345 (62%) were referred and 227 (41%) underwent implantation. Referral was associated with male gender, care coordination by a cardiologist rather than a generalist, and lower social vulnerability index (SVI) score. No decision-making rationale was documented for a plurality of non-referred and non-implanted patients; documented rationales identified potential intervention targets. ICD implantation was not associated with all-cause mortality (aHR 0.74, 95% CI 0.49-1.12). In exploratory analyses stratified by cardiomyopathy type, implantation was associated with lower mortality in ischemic cardiomyopathy (aHR 0.51, 95% CI 0.27-0.95) but not in NICM (aHR 1.11, 95% CI 0.63-1.95).

Conclusion

Many eligible patients are never referred for ICD therapy. Female gender, generalist care coordination, and high SVI were associated with non-referral. The exploratory association of implantation with lower mortality in ischemic cardiomyopathy was not significant in propensity score overlap-weighted analyses. The NICM estimate was imprecise.

title: A Pharmacist-Led Antiplatelet Therapy Stewardship Initiative in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation Receiving Concomitant Oral Anticoagulants and Single Antiplatelet Therapy.
authorString: Kido K, Sokos G.
abstractText: Concomitant therapy with anticoagulants and antiplatelets in patients with atrial fibrillation and chronic coronary syndrome significantly increases the risk of bleeding with no added reduction in cardiovascular disease risk over anticoagulation alone. The primary objective was to evaluate an evidence-based antiplatelet stewardship service designed to deprescribe single antiplatelet therapy in patients with atrial fibrillation receiving oral anticoagulants and a single antiplatelet therapy for both primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease. This retrospective study included adult patients aged older than 18 years with atrial fibrillation who were seen at a tertiary academic heart failure center and received therapeutic oral anticoagulants and single antiplatelet therapy for any cardiovascular secondary or primary prevention. The primary outcome was the acceptance of the antiplatelet deprescribing intervention by both providers and patients. The secondary outcomes included provider- or patient-accepted antiplatelet deprescribing intervention. A total of 71 patients were included in the final cohort of this study. The most common indication for the antiplatelet therapy was chronic coronary disease at 69.0 % followed by primary prevention at 14.1% and stroke at 11.3%. The most common antiplatelet therapy was aspirin 81 mg once daily (83.1%), followed by clopidogrel 75 mg once daily(16.9%). Among the 71 patients, 54 (76.1%) were on non-guideline directed antiplatelet therapy. Of the 54 recommendations, 50 (92.6%) were accepted by the providers, and 43 of the 50 provider-accepted recommendations (86.0%) were accepted by the patients. Conclusion: A pharmacist-led antiplatelet deprescribing service is feasible in a tertiary heart failure cardiology outpatient setting. Most recommendations were accepted by the providers and patients.

title: Risk Factors for Reoperation and Outcomes Following Repair of Atrioventricular Septal Defects.
authorString: Ho YL, Hew CC, Yaakub A, Sirisani JD, Basran NF, Sivalingam S.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
journal.title: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
journal.isoabbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg

abstractText: IntroductionReoperations following atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD) repair remain an important cause of late morbidity. This study aimed to evaluate long-term survival and identify risk factors associated with reoperation following AVSD repair.MethodsA total of 395 patients underwent definitive AVSD repair between January 2010 and December 2021. The primary outcome was freedom from reoperation and identification of predictors of reoperation following index repair. Secondary outcomes included actuarial long-term survival and outcomes following reoperation.ResultsThe median age at repair was 1.3(IQR 0.7-6.2) years. Complete AVSD repair accounted for 64.0% (253/395) of cases, while transitional and partial AVSD comprised 19.5% (77/395) and 16.5% (65/395), respectively. Freedom from reoperation was 95.8%, 92.9% and 86.8% at 1, 5 and 10 years, respectively. Twenty-eight of 395 patients(7.1%) underwent reoperation, including left atrioventricular valve (LAVV) repair in 14/28 (50.0%), LAVV replacement in 4/28 (14.3%), right atrioventricular valve (RAVV) repair in 6/28 (21.4%) and left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO) resection in 5/28 (17.9%). Independent predictors of LAVV reoperation were age <3 months at initial repair (OR 4.03, 95% CI: 1.55-10.51, P = .004), double-orifice LAVV repair (OR 6.85, 95% CI: 2.59-18.12, P < .001) and residual moderate or greater LAVV regurgitation at discharge (OR 8.20, 95% CI: 3.59-21.76, P < .001). No significant predictors were identified for RAVV or LVOTO reoperation. Actuarial survival at 1, 5 and 10 years was 98.6%, 97.2% and 95.2%, respectively. No early or late mortality occurred among patients undergoing reoperation.ConclusionAVSD repair provides excellent long-term survival and low reoperation rates. Residual moderate LAVV regurgitation at discharge is the strongest predictor of reoperation. Durable cleft repair remains critical for long-term valve function. Most patients requiring LAVV reoperation are amenable to re-repair.

title: EXPRESS: Age, Insurance, and Social Vulnerability as Determinants of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitor After New-Onset Heart Failure: Insights from Epic Cosmos.
authorString: Shukla K, Sinha M, Potlach T, Baskaran N, Ruzieh M.

journal.title: Journal of investigative medicine : the official publication of the American Federation for Clinical Research

abstractText: Social determinants of health contribute to inequities in heart failure (HF) management, yet how age, insurance status, and social vulnerability index (SVI) jointly influence sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) use remains poorly understood. To evaluate how SVI and key demographic and system-level factors impact SGLT2i initiation following new-onset HF. This retrospective cohort study used the Epic Cosmos, a national, de-identified electronic health record repository. Adults aged ≥18 years hospitalized with a new HF diagnosis between 2021 and 2024 were included, excluding those with prior SGLT2i use, dialysis-dependent kidney disease, or hospice enrollment. SVI was categorized into quartiles from least vulnerable (Q1) to most vulnerable (Q4). The primary outcome was SGLT2i initiation following index HF hospitalization stratified by SVI, age, and insurance types. Secondary outcomes included crude and age-adjusted mortality. Among 389,986 patients hospitalized with new HF, 81,387 patients (20.9%) were started on SGLT2i. Higher social vulnerability was inversely associated with initiation (Q4 vs Q1 adjusted OR 0.96, 95% CI 0.93-0.98). Younger age was the strongest predictor of initiation (<45 vs 65-74 years: adjusted OR 1.53, 95% CI 1.48-1.59). Commercial insurance was independently associated with higher initiation odds (adjusted OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.18-1.22; p<0.001), as was Medicaid beneficiaries (adjusted OR 1.06, 95% CI 1.02-1.11; p=0.006). In patients with new HF diagnosis, a persistent disadvantage in SGLT2i initiation exists in high-SVI communities. Age and insurance, not social vulnerability alone, are the dominant determinants, highlighting the need for targeted strategies in older adults and payer-level reform.

title: Ruptured INfrarenal abdominal AneurySm: aortiC repair using the ENduranT Endograft. The R.IN.AS.C.ENT.E. Study.
authorString: Lorido A, Mirabella D, Orellana B, Chisci E, Esposito A, Chegai F, Dinoto E, Accarino G, Bruno S, Pecoraro F.

journal.title: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists

abstractText:
Background

Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA) represents a vascular surgical emergency with high mortality. Endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) using the bifurcated Endurant stent graft system is widely employed; however, data specifically addressing its performance in infrarenal rAAA remain limited.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective, multicenter study including 121 patients with confirmed infrarenal rAAA treated exclusively with bifurcated Endurant II or IIs (Medtronic Inc., Minneapolis, Minnesota) devices across 5 Italian tertiary vascular centers from January 2014 to October 2024. Primary endpoints were technical success and 30-day all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included long-term survival, incidence of endoleaks, and reintervention rates. Patients receiving alternative stent grafts or hybrid procedures were excluded to ensure cohort homogeneity.

Results

A total of 121 patients were enrolled during the study period. The cohort had a mean age of 75.3 ± 8.2 years, with 91.7% male predominance. Technical success was achieved in 96.7%. The 30-day mortality rate was 15.7%.
