Multivariate logistic regression identified abdominal compartment syndrome (ACS) (odds ratio [OR], 29.8; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.8-317.7; P = .005) and use of an aortic occlusion balloon (AOB) (OR, 16.4; 95% CI, 2.5-106.2; P = .003) as independent predictors of early mortality. At a median follow-up of 33.6 months (interquartile range, 4.9-72.3), 5-year survival was 65.4%, freedom from any endoleak was 92.6%, and freedom from reintervention was 91.6%. Late type Ia endoleaks occurred in 2.5% of patients.

Conclusions

In this large, strictly defined infrarenal rAAA cohort, bifurcated Endurant stent grafts demonstrated high technical success and favorable early and mid-term clinical outcomes, including in patients with hostile neck anatomy. Early identification and management of ACS and judicious use of AOBs may improve survival. These findings reinforce current EVAR-first guidelines and emphasize the importance of device-specific outcome assessment in emergent rAAA repair.Clinical ImpactThis multicenter study provides one of the largest device-specific evaluations of bifurcated Endurant stent grafts for infrarenal ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms in a rigorously defined Italian cohort, demonstrating high technical success (96.7%) and low 30-day mortality (15.7%) despite a high prevalence of hostile neck anatomy (54.5%). Abdominal compartment syndrome and the use of an aortic occlusion balloon emerged as independent predictors of early mortality, highlighting the critical role of perioperative management. Mid-term outcomes were favorable, with a 5-year survival rate of 65.4%, a low incidence of type Ia endoleak (2.5%), and high freedom from reintervention (91.6%). Overall, these findings support the use of Endurant devices in emergent settings for anatomically suitable patients and reinforce EVAR-first strategies in the management of ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms.

title: Women-Focused and Sex/Gender-Related Cardiovascular Research Funding under Canada's Sex- and Gender-Based Analysis Policy from 2000 to 2024.
authorString: Chen N, Kendall T, Zhang W, Ahmed SB, MacMaster FP, Parekh RS, Brotto LA.
abstractText: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death among women, yet women have historically been underrepresented in cardiovascular research. Whether Canada's sex- and gender-based analysis (SGBA) policies have shifted funding toward women-focused and sex/gender-related cardiovascular research remains unclear. To examine time trends in Canadian Institutes of Health Research (CIHR) investment in women-focused cardiovascular research and assess changes associated with milestones for CIHR SGBA policy implementation, including mandatory application-level requirements in 2010 and grant criteria assessed by reviewers in 2018. We conducted a longitudinal study using CIHR funding data from fiscal years (FYs) 2000 to 2024. Women-focused cardiovascular research projects were identified through terminology searches in titles, keywords, and abstracts. Annual FY funding proportions were analyzed using interrupted time series segmented regression with interruption points in 2010 and 2018. Among 17,168 cardiovascular research grant records, 11.3% were women-focused research. These grants received 11.9% of total funding over the 25-year period. Funding increased before 2010, declined during 2011 and 2017, and accelerated after 2018. Segmented regression showed a small immediate increase in 2010, followed by a negative post-2010 trend and a significant positive quadratic trend after 2018. Application-level SGBA requirements had limited influence on national health research investment patterns, yet more recently reviewer-level assessment aligned with increased investment in women-focused research. Strengthening SGBA implementation will require consistent monitoring of sex- and gender-disaggregated data to assess patient outcomes and impact.

title: The law of surprise: temporal variation and seasonality of acute aortic syndromes: a single-centre epidemiologic cohort analysis spanning 20 years.
authorString: Groß R, Elbayomi M, Harig F, Mellert F, Cesnjevar R, Pathare P.
abstractText:
Background and aims

Acute aortic syndromes (AAS) represent life-threatening cardiovascular emergencies characterized by high mortality rates despite rapid intervention. Global epidemiological data indicate substantial variance in incidence. Longitudinal single-centre data over extended periods are limited but crucial for understanding diagnostic, demographic, and systemic factors influencing admission trends.(1). This study aimed to analyze annual and seasonal variation trends of AAS over a 20-year period in a single maximal care centre and explore potential chronological and environmental contributors to this variation.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study evaluated 403 patients admitted with a confirmed diagnosis of AAS between 2005 and 2025 at the University Hospital Erlangen, Germany. All diagnoses were established via computed tomography angiography (CTA) and confirmed intraoperatively. Annual, quarterly, and monthly surgical volumes were calculated, and temporal trends were analyzed using Poisson and negative binomial regression models. Admission rates during public holidays and school vacations were also evaluated.

Results

Over the 20-year observation period, a steady increasing trend in the annual number of AAS cases was observed, peaking in 2017. Analysis of quarterly distributions revealed a statistically significant dominance of cases in the fourth quarter (Q4: October-December; p < 0.05) compared to the second (Q2) and third (Q3) quarters. Monthly analysis demonstrated a prominent peak in October (incidence rate ratio [IRR] = 1.85 vs. June, p < 0.05). Conversely, fixed public holidays and school vacations were associated with statistically significant reductions in daily admission counts (p < 0.05), with the lowest relative case counts observed during the Christmas vacation period (IRR: 0.40-0.50).

Conclusion

The case counts of acute aortic syndromes exhibits significant temporal and seasonal variation, characterized by a distinct late-autumn and early-winter peak, alongside significant declines during institutional vacation periods. These findings suggest that acute cardiovascular events are heavily modulated by cyclical environmental and socio-systemic factors.

title: Age-stratified clinical phenotypes of cardiac implantable electronic device infections: a 20-year retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Al-Maisary S, Mustafi M, Romano G, Karck M, Arif R, Kraft P, Guzman-Ruvalcaba MJ.
abstractText: The widespread adoption of cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) has been accompanied by a parallel increase in severe CIED infections. Traditional risk stratification frequently relies on binary age cutoffs, which can obscure how infection phenotypes evolve across a patient's lifespan. This study evaluated how advancing age-analyzed across ordered chronological strata-correlates with anatomical infection site, device hardware type, microbiology, and in-hospital mortality in patients with CIED infections. In this retrospective cohort study of 383 patients treated for CIED infections between 2002 and 2022, patients were categorized into five sequential age brackets (< 50 to 80-90 years). Age was modeled both categorically across these strata and continuously to estimate per-decade odds ratios (ORs) for clinical presentation, hardware type, and microbiological findings. The cohort was predominantly male (75.2%) with a mean age of 67.4 years. Pacemaker involvement increased significantly with age (p < 0.001), whereas implantable cardioverter-defibrillator use declined (p = 0.036). Localized generator pocket infections demonstrated a pronounced age-dependent gradient, rising from 19.4% in patients under 50 years to 73.0% in octogenarians (p < 0.001; OR 1.43 per decade, 95% CI: 1.21-1.69). Conversely, systemic presentations-including bacteremia and lead endocarditis-showed no age-dependent trend. In-hospital mortality remained low and stable across age groups (p = 0.452) but was markedly higher in patients presenting with bacteremia or sepsis compared to those without systemic involvement (16.7% vs. 1.6%, p < 0.001). Analyzing age as a continuous spectrum reveals a distinct clinical phenotype dominated by localized pocket infections and low-power devices, an insight obscured by standard binary age cutoffs. Crucially, mortality risk was driven by systemic bloodstream infection rather than patient age itself, emphasizing that clinical surveillance should prioritize infection phenotype over chronological age alone. Not applicable.

title: Racial and Ethnic Disparities in Stroke Among Hypertensive Adults by Antihypertensive Medication Use in the United States.
authorString: Akomaning E, Baah BA, Asaithambi G.

journal.title: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities

abstractText: Despite improvements in hypertension management, racial and ethnic disparities in stroke persist. Whether intervention intensity modifies stroke disparities remains unclear. We analyzed 10,005 adults aged ≥ 20 years with hypertension in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey from March 2013 to March 2020. Stroke history was self-reported. Antihypertensive therapy was categorized as untreated, monotherapy, or combination therapy. Multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical variables and included a race/ethnicity × medication group interaction term. Outcomes were reported as odds ratios (OR) and accompanying 95% confidence intervals (CI). 5% of the studied population reported a history of stroke. After full adjustment, current smoking (OR = 1.80, 95% CI 1.27-2.56), history of cardiovascular disease (OR = 2.38, 95% CI 1.70-3.35), and Medicaid insurance (OR = 3.06, 95% CI 1.40-6.68) were independently associated with stroke. Descriptive differences in stroke prevalence varied across race/ethnicity and antihypertensive medication categories; however, the race/ethnicity x medication interaction was not statistically significant (p = 0.346). Among untreated participants, predicted stroke prevalence was 3.5% in Black participants and 2.8% in White participants, compared to 7.0% and 6.8%, respectively, among those receiving combination therapy. Compared with White participants, Asian participants demonstrated lower odds of stroke on combination therapy (adjusted OR 0.23, 95% CI 0.06-0.96) compared with untreated individuals (adjusted OR 0.49, 95% CI 0.22-1.09). Hispanic participants demonstrated lower odds of stroke relative to White participants across medication categories (adjusted OR = 0.57, 95% CI 0.37-0.90 combination therapy vs. adjusted OR = 0.66, 95% CI 0.48-0.92 untreated). Stroke prevalence differed by race/ethnicity and antihypertensive medication category; however, no statistically significant evidence was found that treatment intensity modified racial/ethnic disparities. Larger longitudinal studies incorporating blood pressure control, medication adherence, and hypertension severity are needed to better understand the relationship between antihypertensive treatment intensity and racial/ethnic differences in stroke risk.

title: Hematopoietic loss of KDM6A impairs cardiac recovery in heart failure via epigenetic reprogramming of myeloid cells.
authorString: Solomonidis EG, Hecker D, Shumliakivska M, Leberzammer J, Fischer A, Katschke MT, Bendel M, Korth L, Schuhmacher B, Rumpf L, Glaser SF, Schmitz K, Luxán G, Frenz S, Pennoyer P, Wilken-Schmitz A, Rasper T, Zimmermann S, Ganß F, Ullrich E, John D, Guenther S, Pálfi K, Weiss LM, Leisegang MS, Brandes RP, von Scheidt M, Leistner DM, Zeiher AM, Abplanalp WT, Looso M, Schulz MH, Dimmeler S, Cremer S.
abstractText: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH), the expansion of blood cell clones carrying acquired mutations, is an independent risk factor for cardiovascular disease. Although mutations in DNMT3A and TET2 are well studied, the cardiovascular consequences of KDM6A mutations remain unclear. KDM6A is an X-linked histone demethylase that is commonly mutated in patients with heart failure (HF). Here we performed multiomics profiling and functional characterization of mouse models and patient-derived data to show that hematopoietic KDM6A loss impairs cardiac recovery after myocardial infarction (MI). KDM6A deficiency increases myeloid cell recruitment to the injured heart and reprograms monocytes, macrophages and neutrophils toward inflammatory, migratory and glycolytic states. Patients with HF and KDM6A-driven CH show similar pro-inflammatory monocyte signatures. KDM6A-silenced macrophages promote cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and cardiac fibroblast activation. Notably, IL-1β blockade after MI rescued the adverse cardiac phenotype of hematopoietic KDM6A loss. These findings identify KDM6A-driven CH as a driver of immune dysregulation and IL-1β signaling as a potential therapeutic target in CH-associated HF.

title: Hypoxia-induced platelet activation and pulmonary platelets are increased in a murine model of neonatal chronic lung disease and pulmonary hypertension.
authorString: Archambault JL, Posey JN, Jordan M, Roberts DS, Olsen-Dufour AM, Sola-Visner MC, Davenport P, Wright CJ, Nozik ES, Delaney CA.
abstractText: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia-associated pulmonary hypertension (BPD-PH) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in preterm infants, yet available therapies lack mechanistic diversity and can be ineffective, highlighting an urgent need for novel therapeutic targets. Platelets are increasingly recognized as immune cells capable of driving pulmonary vascular inflammation, but their role in neonatal PH remains undefined. Neonatal mice were exposed to 12% hypoxia beginning at 12-24 h of life until postnatal day 8 (P8) or 15 (P15). Cardiopulmonary phenotype and markers of platelet activation were quantified using histology, flow cytometry, ELISA, and immunohistochemistry. Hypoxia produced a BPD-PH phenotype, including alveolar simplification, pulmonary vessel muscularization, elevated right ventricular systolic pressure, and right ventricular hypertrophy. Hypoxia disrupted the postnatal decline in pulmonary platelets and the platelet α-granule stored protein, platelet factor 4, resulting in increased pulmonary platelet accumulation at P15. Circulating platelets from hypoxic mice demonstrated increased activation, with higher P-selectin and activated αIIbβ3 expression at P8 and P15, enhanced agonist-induced P-selectin expression at P8, and increased leukocyte-platelet aggregation at P8. Postnatal hypoxia induces a robust, biologically meaningful platelet activation phenotype, supporting a previously unrecognized association between platelet activation and BPD-PH and identifying platelet activation pathways as potential therapeutic targets warranting further mechanistic investigation. Postnatal hypoxia drives persistent pulmonary platelet accumulation in a neonatal model of bronchopulmonary dysplasia-associated pulmonary hypertension. Hypoxic neonatal platelets exhibit increased P-selectin expression and αIIbβ3 activation, enhanced agonist responsiveness, and early leukocyte-platelet aggregation, indicating a shift toward a pro-inflammatory phenotype. These findings demonstrate that, despite developmental hyporesponsiveness, neonatal platelets are dynamically activated by hypoxia and may contribute to pulmonary vascular remodeling. This work identifies platelet activation pathways as potential circulating biomarkers and clinically relevant targets in neonatal pulmonary hypertension, expanding beyond current vasodilator-based therapies.

title: Cardiovascular disease in diabetes mellitus: beyond atherosclerosis and heart failure.
authorString: Gong JY, Fourlanos S, Butler J, Kistler PM, Reid CM, Magliano DJ, Shaw JE.
abstractText: The global burden of diabetes mellitus continues to grow, now affecting one in nine adults. In people with diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, and considerable focus has been placed on reducing the incidence of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and heart failure over the past few decades. Due to reductions in the prevalence of some major risk factors, improved control of other risk factors and improved therapeutic agents, mortality attributed to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease has declined. Meanwhile, the decline in mortality attributed to heart failure has stalled. However, beyond atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and heart failure, many other cardiovascular diseases are responsible for morbidity and mortality. We provide a comprehensive narrative summary of the association between diabetes mellitus and the most common cardiovascular diseases as reported by the 2023 Global Burden of Disease study. The evidence indicates that diabetes mellitus is a risk factor for atrial fibrillation, infective endocarditis, hypertensive heart disease, intracerebral haemorrhage and aortic stenosis. We also discuss the available evidence for the effects of incretin hormone mimetics, such as glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists, and of sodium/glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors for each of these cardiovascular diseases. This Review underscores the multifaceted link between cardiovascular disease and diabetes mellitus, highlighting that integrated strategies are required to effectively reduce the global burden of both conditions.

title: Bleeding and Thromboembolic Outcomes Following GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Initiation in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Atrial Fibrillation Receiving Direct Oral Anticoagulants: A Target Trial Emulation.
authorString: Du F, Cicali B, Singh Ospina NM, Ruzieh M, Schmidt S, Jiao T.
abstractText: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and Type 2 diabetes (T2D) require coordinated stroke prevention and metabolic risk management. Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are standard for stroke prevention, while glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are increasingly used in T2D. In DOAC users, GLP-1RA initiation may alter body weight and gastrointestinal physiology, potentially increasing DOAC exposure and thereby elevating bleeding risk. We aim to investigate the impact of GLP-1RA initiation on risks of thromboembolic disease and bleeding in patients with T2D and AF receiving DOACs. We emulated a target trial comparing GLP-1RA versus dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor initiation. We identified Medicare beneficiaries aged ≥ 65 years with T2D and AF receiving DOACs. Randomization was emulated using 1:1 propensity score matching. Primary outcomes include thromboembolic disease and bleeding. Per-protocol effects were estimated using inverse-probability-censoring-weighted Cox proportional hazards models. After matching, 930 patients were included in each group, with mean follow-up of 1 year. Mean age was 74.7 vs. 74.2 years, and 47.1% vs. 44.2% were women in the GLP-1RA vs. DPP-4 inhibitor groups. GLP-1RA initiation was associated with higher bleeding risk (HR 1.18, 95% CI: 1.03-1.36), lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.58, 95% CI: 0.36-0.95), and similar thromboembolic risk (HR 1.50, 95% CI: 0.22-10.43). Among DOAC-treated patients with T2D and AF, GLP-1RA initiation was associated with a less favourable bleeding profile but no evident increase in thromboembolic risk. These findings support careful clinical monitoring and further studies incorporating body weight and renal function to inform individualized treatment.

title: Single-cell profiling reveals monocyte mitochondrial dysfunction in patients with cirrhosis progressing to acute-on-chronic liver failure.
authorString: Wirtz TH, Palomino-Echeverria S, Pollmanns MR, Huergo E, Schreibing F, Reißing J, Sánchez-Garrido C, López-Vicario C, Aransay AM, Baldassare M, Zaccherini G, Pompili E, McCoy MS, Uschner FE, Klein S, Gu W, Schierwagen R, Valainathan S, Verbeeck A, Campion D, Giovo I, Schneider KM, Koch A, Kramann R, Bruns T, Kiani N, Stiles L, Caraceni P, Alessandria C, Moreau R, Trebicka J, Clària J, Planell N, Rautou PE, Trautwein C, Gomez-Cabrero D.
abstractText: Patients with acute decompensation (AD) of cirrhosis are at a high risk of developing acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF), a syndrome characterized by multi-organ failure and high short-term mortality. Prospective studies addressing the cellular mechanisms that drive the transition from AD to ACLF are lacking. In this study, we aimed to determine whether peripheral immune cell subsets at hospital admission predict the progression from AD to ACLF and to delineate underlying molecular mechanisms. We prospectively enrolled 63 patients with AD and 15 healthy donors across five European centres, with a 90-day follow-up. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed on peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from 16 patients with distinct trajectories and 4 controls. Progression to ACLF was associated with expansion of classical monocytes, particularly subcluster "C2", which specifically displayed impaired energy metabolism with reduced oxidative phosphorylation (p<0.001). A C2-derived gene signature (18 genes) was enriched in two large international whole-blood cohorts (PREDICT, n=689; ACLARA, n=521), particularly in patients with bacterial infections, those developing ACLF, and non-survivors (p<0.001). Functional validation by respirometry in an independent AD cohort confirmed declining monocyte Complex IV-dependent oxygen consumption in patients with pre-ACLF (p<0.05). We identified and validated a distinct monocyte subpopulation with defective energy metabolism in patients with AD with poor outcomes, supporting a link between monocyte bioenergetic dysfunction and ACLF development. Impact and Implications:The cellular mechanisms that drive progression from acute decompensation (AD) to acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) remain poorly understood, limiting the development of effective strategies for therapeutic intervention. By integrating prospective single-cell transcriptomics, functional bioenergetic analyses, and validation in independent multicentre cohorts, we identified a distinct monocyte subset characterized by impaired oxidative phosphorylation that is associated with subsequent ACLF development. These findings are relevant to clinicians and researchers because they suggest that immune-metabolic dysfunction emerges before overt ACLF and may contribute to disease progression. While further mechanistic and prospective validation studies are required, our results provide a framework for the investigation of monocyte bioenergetics as a potential therapeutic target in patients with decompensated cirrhosis.

title: Lipoprotein(a) and an aggressive coronary disease phenotype: Association with multivessel disease and recurrent coronary events in the CERES study.
authorString: Gómez-Barrado JJ, Porras-Ramos Y, Camacho-Alcalá JA, Gómez-Turégano P, Gómez-Turégano M.
abstractText:
Background

Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established genetically determined risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Whether elevated Lp(a) identifies a broader phenotype of aggressive coronary disease, integrating anatomical disease burden and recurrent clinical manifestations, remains incompletely characterised.

Methods

We analysed 1892 patients with coronary artery disease from the multicentre CERES cohort after exclusion of myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA). Lp(a) was analysed continuously, after natural-log transformation, and categorically using >50 mg/dL. Multivariable logistic regression models were adjusted for age, sex, hypertension, diabetes, smoking, and historical maximum LDL cholesterol (LDL-C).

Results

Lp(a) was available in 1833 patients; median concentration was 24.7 [9.1-63.7] mg/dL, and 33.2% had Lp(a) >50 mg/dL. Multivessel disease was present in 50.4% and recurrent coronary events in 19.5%. Lp(a) was independently associated with multivessel disease (OR, 1.004; 95% CI, 1.001-1.006; p = 0.002) and recurrent coronary events (OR, 1.004; 95% CI, 1.001-1.006; p = 0.003). Lp(a) >50 mg/dL was associated with multivessel disease (OR, 1.406; 95% CI, 1.144-1.730; p = 0.001) and recurrent events (OR, 1.504; 95% CI, 1.166-1.942; p = 0.002).

Conclusions

Elevated Lp(a) was independently associated with greater anatomical coronary disease burden and recurrent coronary events, supporting its role as a marker of an aggressive coronary disease phenotype.

title: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair for mitral valve regurgitation: insights from a 5-year prospective multicenter registry.
authorString: Giordano S, Sorrentino S, De Rosa S, De Carlo M, Adamo M, Pezzola E, De Felice F, Pennacchi M, Villa E, Maffeo D, Ferraro P, Morello A, Cimmino M, Albanese M, Biondi-Zoccai G, Giordano A, Corcione N.
abstractText: Long-term data on transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) for significant mitral regurgitation (MR) remain limited. We aimed to evaluate long-term clinical outcomes and functional and echocardiographic findings during follow-up after MitraClip in a long-term subanalysis of the prospective multicenter GIOTTO registry. We included 406 consecutive patients undergoing MitraClip implantation for significant MR from 6 Italian centers contributing long-term follow-up. Baseline, procedural, in-hospital, and long-term follow-up data were compared according to MR etiology. Predictors of all-cause death were assessed using Cox regression analysis. Mean follow-up was 56.4±27.2 months. The cohort included 257 (63.3%) patients with functional or mixed MR and 149 (36.7%) with degenerative MR, who were older, more often female, and had smaller ventricles and higher LVEF, whereas functional or mixed MR patients had greater ischemic burden, conduction disease, prior revascularization, pacemaker implantation, and ventricular remodeling. During the overall observation period, crude all-cause death occurred in 161 patients (39.7%) and MVARC-style cardiovascular death in 98 (24.1%), without significant differences between groups. Mitral surgery, repeat TEER, endocarditis, and stroke occurred in 2.2%, 0.7%, 1.5%, and 3.5%, respectively. Among patients with available follow-up assessment, 77.5% were in NYHA class I/II. At the actual 5-year landmark echocardiographic assessment, 82.9% had none or mild MR and 97.1% had no more than moderate MR. Independent mortality predictors were older age, lower body mass index, right bundle branch block, MR etiology, larger LV end-systolic diameter, higher systolic pulmonary artery pressure, and longer index hospitalization (all p <0.05). In conclusion, in this prospective multicenter cohort, TEER with MitraClip in high-risk patients was associated with high procedural success and favorable long-term clinical and echocardiographic findings among patients with available follow-up. Mortality appeared to be associated with patient vulnerability, MR etiology, ventricular remodeling, pulmonary hypertension, and the early post-procedural course.

title: UBAP2L O-GlcNAcylation contributes to DDX21-associated stress granule formation and suppression of trophoblast pyroptosis in preeclampsia.
authorString: Liu R, Wei J, Wang Z, Wu Z, Sun Q, Jin X, Li X, Zhang H, Kong Y.
abstractText: Preeclampsia (PE) is a severe pregnancy disorder characterized by hypertension and multi-organ dysfunction. Impaired trophoblast function and defective spiral artery remodeling are considered the central pathological features of PE, leading to placental ischemia/hypoxia and a subsequent inflammatory cascade. Increasing evidence has demonstrated that pyroptosis contributes to placental dysfunction and the establishment of a pro-inflammatory microenvironment in PE; however, the mechanisms remain largely unclear. O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc) modification is a reversible post-translational modification (PTM) that plays critical roles in maintaining cellular homeostasis and regulating multiple forms of programmed cell death (PCD), yet its role in pyroptosis during PE has not been elucidated. In the present study, we found that O-GlcNAcylation was markedly reduced in placental tissues from patients with PE and negatively correlated with pyroptosis. In both an LPS-induced PE-like mouse model and trophoblast cells, enhancement of O-GlcNAcylation significantly suppressed pyroptosis and ameliorated PE-like phenotypes. IP-MS identified UBAP2L as a critical O-GlcNAcylated protein. Mechanistically, T446, an O-GlcNAcylation site of UBAP2L, contributed to maintaining its protein stability by preventing ubiquitin-mediated proteasomal degradation and promoted its interaction with DDX21, thereby promoting stress granule assembly. This process suppressed inflammasome activation and pyroptosis, improved trophoblast function, and ameliorated PE-like phenotypes. Collectively, our findings define an O-GlcNAcylation-UBAP2L-DDX21-stress granule-pyroptosis axis in PE and nominate O-GlcNAc signaling as a therapeutic target.

title: Medicinal Plants and Fungi of the Sikkim Himalaya for Hypertension and Cardiovascular Disorders: Ethnopharmacology, Mechanisms, and Cardiovascular Relevance.
authorString: Kattel A, Sharma A, Chutia D.
abstractText: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are the leading cause of global mortality, driven by mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, and dysregulated cellular signaling. Despite extensive use of plant-based therapies for circulatory disorders, many ethnomedicinal claims lack molecular validation. In the biodiversity-rich Sikkim Himalaya, India, traditional medicinal plant use by Lepcha, Bhutia, and Nepali communities remains unsystematically integrated with cardiovascular evidence, with limited classification into three evidence tiers: Tier I (mechanistically validated), Tier II (mechanistically suggestive), and Tier III (pharmacologically divergent). To critically assess the extent to which the traditional cardiovascular uses of medicinal plants and fungi from the Sikkim Himalaya, India, are supported by experimental pharmacological and molecular evidence, and to classify the available evidence according to its mechanistic strength. A PRISMA 2020-guided narrative review was conducted to identify, screen, and report the available literature using predefined procedures. The retrieved evidence was synthesized qualitatively to integrate ethnopharmacological, pharmacological, phytochemical, and molecular mechanistic findings. Literature from Jan 1950 to March 2026 was retrieved from PubMed, Embase, and Google Scholar. Studies were screened using predefined inclusion criteria focusing on Sikkim-based ethnomedicinal use and cardiovascular indications. Data were extracted on species identity, traditional use, phytochemistry, and molecular mechanisms, followed by qualitative synthesis. Fifteen medicinal plant and fungal taxa were identified. Five taxa, including Rhododendron arboreum Sm., Centella asiatica (L.) Urb., Nardostachys jatamansi (D.Don) DC., Oroxylum indicum (L.) Kurz, and Ophiocordyceps sinensis (Berk.) G.H.Sung, J.M.Sung, Hywel-Jones & Spatafora, demonstrated cardioprotective effects in myocardial injury models via modulation of mitochondrial stability, inflammatory signaling, and PI3K/Akt and AMPK pathways. Evidence was stratified into three tiers: Tier I, mechanistically validated; Tier II, mechanistically suggestive; and Tier III, pharmacologically divergent. Stress-adaptive Himalayan phytochemistry converges with conserved cardiovascular signaling pathways, supporting their potential as candidates for further preclinical cardiovascular investigation. However, integration of metabolomics, pharmacokinetics, disease-relevant models, and clinical studies is required to establish therapeutic efficacy and enable clinical translation.

title: Clinical outcomes and coronary complication risk after transcatheter tricuspid annuloplasty with cardioband: a 12-month single-center cohort study.
authorString: de Almeida Mussons HS, Sánchez-Recalde Á, Domínguez Rodríguez LM, Salinas JA.
abstractText: To evaluate the clinical and echocardiographic outcomes of transcatheter tricuspid annuloplasty using the Cardioband system in a single-center cohort of high-risk patients with severe functional tricuspid regurgitation. This single-center prospective cohort study included 64 consecutive patients with severe functional tricuspid regurgitation undergoing transcatheter tricuspid annuloplasty with the Cardioband system. Clinical and echocardiographic data were collected at baseline, discharge, 6-months, and 12-months. Primary endpoints included changes in tricuspid regurgitation severity, annular dimensions, and clinical status, as well as all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization. Outcomes were analyzed using available-case data. At 12-months, among patients with available echocardiographic data (n = 44), tricuspid regurgitation severity was reduced compared with baseline (p < 0.001); 15.9% had trace or mild TR, 45.5% had moderate TR, 27.3% had severe TR, and 11.4% had massive or torrential TR. All-cause mortality at 12-months was 6.3% (4/64 patients). According to TVARC criteria, intraprocedural success was achieved in 81.3% of patients, while a more stringent definition yielded a success rate of 65.6%. In this single-center cohort of high-risk patients with severe functional tricuspid regurgitation, transcatheter tricuspid annuloplasty using the Cardioband system was associated with reductions in tricuspid regurgitation severity and improvements in selected clinical parameters at 12-months. However, these findings should be interpreted with caution given the observational design, incomplete follow-up, and the absence of a control group, as well as the observed rate of procedural complications. Further studies, ideally including larger multicenter cohorts and controlled comparisons, are needed to better define the role of this therapy in the management of tricuspid regurgitation.

title: Increasing Cardiovascular Disease-Related Mortality Burden in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) in the United States: A Nationwide Analysis (1999 to 2024).
authorString: Singh C, Sampada, Tembhare A, Sohal A, Sandhu S.
abstractText: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a complex multisystem disorder, with cardiovascular disease (CVD) representing the most common cause of mortality. This study aims to analyze trends in MASLD and CVD-related mortality in the United States. Mortality data for individuals aged 25 years and older from 1999 to 2024 were obtained from the CDC WONDER database. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 population were calculated among patients with MASLD and CVD. Temporal trends were assessed using Joinpoint regression analysis to estimate the annual percent change (APC) and average annual percent change (AAPC) in mortality rates. Between 1999 and 2024, a total of 55,788 deaths were identified related to MASLD and CVD among adults aged 25 years or older. The number of deaths increased from 1044 in 1999 to 5216 in 2024, reflecting a 400% increase in mortality. The most common causes of CVD-related mortality were hypertension and ischemic heart disease. The total number of deaths among men was higher compared to women (30,201 vs. 25,587), and the rate of increase in mortality was higher among women (7.60, 95% CI: 7.07-8.35 vs. 3.42, 95% CI: 2.78-4.17). Our analysis highlights acceleration in CVD-related mortality among MASLD patients with widening disparities. These findings highlight MASLD as a growing contributor to cardiovascular mortality, and targeted prevention, along with reduction strategies, are urgently needed to mitigate this rising burden.

title: Toward detection of heart failure: development of a sensitive fluorescent kit for clinical sST2 detection.
authorString: Ping Z, Chen M, Jin Y, Gu M, Pan L, Zang J, Nai S, Song T, Liu M, Ren K, Zhao H, Yang Y.
abstractText: Heart failure, the terminal stage of various cardiovascular diseases, typically presents with subtle early symptoms that are difficult to detect. Consequently, developing fast and accurate diagnostic tools is essential for effective early diagnosis and disease management. Soluble suppression of tumorigenicity 2 (sST2) is recognized as a valuable biomarker for predicting disease severity and mortality in cardiovascular disease, making it a promising target for developing a detection kit for early heart failure diagnosis. Recently, the CRISPR-Cas12a system has been increasingly used for quick and sensitive nucleic acid detection. However, its application in protein detection remains limited. In this study, we combined nanotechnology-mediated protein capture with the CRISPR-Cas12a system and developed a fluorescence-based method for rapid and sensitive detection of sST2. The presence of sST2 triggers the formation of a ternary complex, which can activate the trans-cleavage activity of Cas12a, resulting in cleavage of the response DNA single strand and the production of a fluorescent signal. Importantly, when tested on serum samples, this method can effectively distinguish patients with heart failure from healthy controls. This method offers a promising alternative to traditional enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs), with potential advantages in operational simplicity and detection speed. Therefore, this innovative fluorescence-based sST2 detection technique has significant potential for the clinical diagnosis of heart failure.

title: Accelerated aortic stenosis progression is associated with greater CT-derived extracellular volume.
authorString: Lobo A, Cavadas J, Almeida MC, Brandão M, Teixeira R, Castro C, Dias Ferreira N, Braga P, Sampaio F, Fontes-Carvalho R.

journal.title: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging

abstractText: Rapid progression of aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with adverse outcomes, yet the myocardial changes accompanying faster progression remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated the association between the rate of AS progression and myocardial fibrosis assessed by computed tomography (CT)-derived extracellular volume fraction (ECV), and the impact on clinical outcomes. We studied 134 patients with classical high-gradient severe AS who underwent pre-transcatheter aortic valve implantation cardiac CT with a delayed dual-energy acquisition for ECV quantification and had at least two echocardiograms ≥ 6 months apart. Progression was defined as the annualized change in peak aortic jet velocity. Rapid progression was defined as an increase > 0.30 m/s/year. Patients were followed for a composite of cardiovascular hospitalization, urgent aortic valve replacement, or death. ECV correlated with progression rate (Spearman ρ = 0.33, p < 0.001). In multivariable linear regression, faster progression remained independently associated with ECV (β = 2.52, p = 0.001). Rapid progressors had higher ECV than slow progressors (31.5% vs. 28.3%, p < 0.001). Over a median follow-up of 16.2 months, 36 patients (26.9%) reached the composite outcome. Patients with both rapid progression and high ECV had an event rate of 69 versus 11 per 100 patient-years in those without (adjusted HR 6.22, 95% CI 3.13-12.32). Faster AS progression is independently associated with greater diffuse myocardial fibrosis, irrespective of stenosis severity, and their combination identified patients at higher risk of adverse events. These findings suggest that AS progression rate and myocardial tissue characterization carry complementary prognostic information in severe AS.

title: A Mortality Risk Prediction Score for Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Wirawan MT, Arafuri N, Martelina Y, Noormanto, Nugroho S, Murni IK.
abstractText: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a leading cause of pediatric heart failure and carries a substantial risk of death or heart transplantation. In low- and middle-income countries, limited access to advanced heart failure therapies and transplantation highlights the need for simple, reliable tools to identify children at highest risk. Therefore, this study aimed to identify independent predictors of mortality and develop a practical bedside risk score for mortality prediction in children with DCM. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of children with DCM treated at Dr. Sardjito Hospital, Indonesia, between 2016 and 2025. Clinical, electrocardiographic, and echocardiographic variables were evaluated for association with mortality. Independent predictors were incorporated into a point-based risk score using the Spiegelhalter-Knill-Jones method. Discriminative performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic analysis and internal validation. Among 109 children with DCM, mortality was 33.9%. Seven independent predictors of mortality were identified: age ≥ 2 years at diagnosis, New York Heart Association/Ross functional class IV heart failure, malnutrition, requirement for vasoactive support, low-voltage electrocardiography, left ventricular end-diastolic diameter z-score > + 4, and left ventricular ejection fraction ≤ 30%. The derived score ranged from - 25 to + 28 points. A threshold score ≥ 11 accurately identified high-risk patients, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.932 (95% CI 0.886-0.977), with 73.0% sensitivity and 95.8% specificity. Internal validation demonstrated sustained performance (AUC 0.921). We developed and validated a simple, bedside mortality risk score with excellent discriminative ability for children with DCM. By relying on routinely available clinical and echocardiographic parameters, this tool enables early identification of high-risk patients and may support timely clinical decision-making and resource allocation, particularly in resource-constrained settings.

title: Association Between Pituitary Adenoma Excision and Risk of Cerebrovascular Disease and Mortality in Patients With Cushing's Disease: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
authorString: Chung RS, Zeng W, Cote DJ, Kang KM, Lin M, Shah I, Gomez D, Dallas J, Briggs RG, Sisti J, Omotosho YB, Carmichael JD, Mack WJ, Zada G.
abstractText:
Background and objectives

Cushing's disease (CD) is a hypercortisolemic state resulting from an adrenocorticotropic hormone-secreting pituitary adenoma (PA). Cerebrovascular disease (CeVD) is a dangerous sequela of CD, yet few studies have characterized its risk in CD. This study aimed to report the risk of CeVD in CD patients with and without surgical treatment.

Methods

This retrospective multicenter study from the TriNetX database included 20 years of data from 69 healthcare organizations. TriNetX was searched to identify adults in the United States with CD. We used 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) for demographic characteristics and tobacco use to identify a matched non-CD group. Risk ratios were calculated to identify the risk of CeVD. Among patients with CD, we identified those who underwent PA excision after diagnosis and determined associations with CeVD. We used 1:1 PSM matching for demographic characteristics and comorbidities (hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia) to identify a matched non-PA excision CD group.

Results

The CD group (n = 4265) was 78.4% female with a mean age at CD diagnosis of 45.7 years. After PSM, patients with CD had a significantly higher risk of any CeVD (risk ratio [RR] = 1.97, 95% CI: 1.70-2.29), ischemic stroke (RR = 2.35, 95% CI: 1.83-3.01), and hemorrhagic stroke (RR = 1.75, 95% CI: 1.22-2.49). Stratification by sex identified similar associations. One thousand three hundred seventy-seven patients with CD who underwent PA excision were identified after matching. PA excision was associated with lower risk of any CeVD (RR = 0.68, 95% CI: 0.55-0.86, number needed to treat [NNT] = 25.6), ischemic stroke (RR = 0.50, 95% CI: 0.35-0.72, NNT = 33.3), and mortality (RR = 0.52, 95% CI: 0.35-0.77, NNT = 40.0) compared with those who did not have excision. Sensitivity analyses using medication-based proxies for biochemical remission showed similar trends between curative and noncurative resection but were not statistically significant.

Conclusion

This study demonstrated that patients with CD are at an increased risk of CeVD, including ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke. PA excision for patients with CD may reduce lifetime CeVD risk and mortality.

title: Depression among patients with recurrent <i>Clostridioides difficile</i> infection: a nationwide inpatient analysis.
authorString: Chaar A, Sehgal K, Abboud Y, Rizwan R, Nawaz A, Patel S, Feuerstadt P.
abstractText:
Background

Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) frequently recurs and impacts quality of life, yet its relationship with mental illness remains understudied.

Methods

Using the National Inpatient Sample (2018-2019), we calculated depression rates among adults with recurrent CDI (rCDI) and assessed the odds of codiagnosed depression compared to other chronic medical conditions.

Results

Among 84,055 hospitalizations with rCDI, 21.5% had a codiagnosis of depression. In a population without CDI, depression prevalence was 14.2%. CDI patients had a 56% greater chance of having a diagnosis of depression compared with the general population (odds ratio [OR] 1.56, 95% confidence interval 1.5-1.6). When compared to those with common chronic medical comorbidities, patients with CDI had significantly higher odds of having depression than those with heart failure (OR 1.4), diabetes (OR 1.3), end-stage kidney disease (OR 1.5), and metastatic cancer (OR 1.9). Patients with fibromyalgia, multiple sclerosis, and alcohol-related disorders had higher rates of depression compared with those with CDI.

Conclusion

Patients with rCDI appear to have remarkably high depression rates, higher than those of patients with many other common chronic medical conditions. Further studies are needed to evaluate the causation of this potential association and to consider the benefit of implementing depression screening programs in this vulnerable population.

title: Short 3-month telemedical monitoring is associated only with partial maintenance of functional performance 12 months later: a single-arm study in patients with heart failure in underserved areas.
authorString: Wańczura P, Rodzoń-Wańczura U, Wiśniowski M, Stecko W, Bukowski H, Aebisher D, Zalewski J.
abstractText:
Introduction

A 3-month telemedical care model under specialist supervision was associated with an improvement in New York Heart Association (NYHA) class and quality of life in heart failure (HF) population from underserved areas.

Objectives

This study sought to investigate whether the effects of a 3-month telemonitoring intervention (3m-INT) were maintained 12 months later.

Patients and methods

In this prospective study, HF patients were enrolled in 5 rural voivodeships and were evaluated after completion of a 3m-INT and 12 months later using the NYHA scale, the Chronic Heart Failure Questionnaire (CHFQ) and the EuroQol Visual Analogue Scale. The clinical composite endpoint (CCE) was death, hospitalization for HF decompensation, stroke, or myocardial infarction.

Results

Of 429 HF patients who completed 3m-INT, 320 (74.6%) were reevaluated 12 months later. Within the 3m-INT, 1 patient died and 6 more during the following 12 months. After 12 months follow-up, CCE occurred in 23 (7.2%) patients while the NYHA class improved in 42 (13.4%) patients, remained unchanged in 131 (41.7%), and deteriorated in 141 (44.9%). Finally, the distribution of NYHA classes at 12 months remained significantly better than at baseline (P <0.001). Atrial fibrillation was independently associated with the occurrence of CCE (P = 0.005). EuroQol Visual Analogue Scale-assessed quality of life did not change (P = 0.36), while CHFQ-measured dyspnea measured by CHFQ deteriorated (P <0.001) after a 1-year observation.

Conclusions

After 3m-INT followed by 12 months of observation, only partial maintenance of functional performance of HF patients in underserved areas was observed. Atrial fibrillation was associated with an unfavorable clinical effect.

title: Predicting Outcomes in Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage Using Clinical and Computed Tomography Markers: A Prospective Study.
authorString: Jain A, Sharma SR, Synmon B, Lynser D, Thakre M.
abstractText:
Background

Spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) represents a disproportionately high stroke burden (20%-30%) in low- and middle-income countries like India, necessitating accurate, early risk stratification using readily available clinical and radiographic features.

Materials and methods

This prospective observational study included 185 patients with spontaneous ICH at a tertiary care center. Baseline clinical severity was assessed using the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) and the ICH score. Radiographic markers included hematoma volume, intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH), and radiographic signs (swirl, blend, black hole, satellite, and spot signs). The primary outcome was unfavorable functional status (modified Rankin scale: 4-6, including mortality) at 90 days. Univariate analyses focused on identifying predictors associated with a poor outcome, followed by multivariable logistic regression.

Results

The mean age was 56.0 ± 12.4 years, with 72.4% prevalence of hypertension. The unfavorable outcome rate was 37.3% (N = 69), with 22.2% mortality. Univariate analysis (P < 0.05) revealed strong associations between poor outcome and greater hematoma volume, lower GCS score, higher ICH score, IVH, swirl sign, blend sign, satellite sign, hydrocephalus, herniation, and ≥2 multiple noncontrast computed tomography (NCCT) signs. Multivariable analysis identified hematoma volume, GCS score, ICH score, herniation, satellite sign, and male gender as independent predictors.

Conclusion

Clinical severity indicators and multiple NCCT signs in univariate analysis serve as robust markers of poor functional outcome. The independent prognostic value of the satellite sign and herniation highlights the utility of readily available radiographic features for immediate risk stratification.

title: Investigating the Distinctive Clinical and Genetic Landscape of <i>PPA2</i> Deficiency.
authorString: Low BSH, Corver ME, Lipov A, Wardle JPR, Mazzarotto F, Bezzina CR, Behr ER, Jurgens SJ, Carroll CJ, Walsh R.
abstractText:
Background

PPA2 encodes for inorganic pyrophosphatase 2, a mitochondrial enzyme that hydrolyzes inorganic pyrophosphates into orthophosphate. Biallelic loss-of-function variants cause PPA2 deficiency, an emerging recessive cardiac condition that causes heart failure and sudden cardiac death in infants and young people.

Methods

Using published case reports and large-scale genomics resources, we defined the clinical and molecular spectrum of this disease, classified variants using a customized American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics pipeline, assessed genotype-phenotype correlations, calculated predicted prevalence using the gnomAD GenIE tool, and investigated monoallelic associations in the UK Biobank.

Results

A total of 63 cases from 37 families were identified from 12 publications. The natural history of this disease is characterized by clinical heterogeneity and high mortality (79% by 20 years of age), typically presenting as a highly arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy with 2 distinct risk periods: in infancy, where viral infections can lead to heart failure, and in adolescence, where minimal alcohol exposure can trigger sudden cardiac death. The disease is genetically heterogeneous, with 29 distinct variants described (18 of which were classified as [likely] pathogenic), usually in compound heterozygosity. As complete gene knockout appears to be incompatible with life, PPA2 deficiency is caused by biallelic variants within a particular loss-of-function window, with deficiency mitigated by hypomorphic effects, variants in nonconstitutive exons, and particular compound heterozygous combinations. The spectrum of phenotypic effect extends to monoallelic carriers of pathogenic variants, which demonstrate an apparent mitohormesis-like compensatory protection from heart failure. The disease has an estimated prevalence of at least 1/135 000 in European ancestry populations.

Conclusions

PPA2 deficiency is a genetically complex and clinically severe disease. Given the potential for effective life-saving interventions, PPA2 may warrant inclusion in emerging newborn genomic screening programs.

title: The American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association classification of chronic hypertension in pregnancy has better clinical applicability and risk assessment than the traditional severe and mild hypertension approach - lessons from a population-based study.
authorString: Rabinovich A, Dar Diab S, Shiloh A, Speigel E, Erez O.

journal.title: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians

abstractText:
Background

Chronic hypertension (CHTN) increases the risk of superimposed preeclampsia, contributing to maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality. Accurate hypertension classification is therefore essential for risk stratification, antenatal surveillance, prevention, and outcomes. The clinical impact of applying the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) classification, compared with the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) criteria, in pregnancy remains uncertain.

Objective

To determine the impact of ACC/AHA versus ACOG hypertension classifications on the prevalence of CHTN and pregnancy outcomes.

Study design

This population-based retrospective cohort study used a computerized maternity database from a tertiary hospital. All parturients with singleton gestations initiating prenatal care in the first trimester were included (n = 136,606). CHTN was categorized according to ACOG and ACC/AHA criteria. Maternal, fetal, and neonatal outcomes were assessed. Statistical analyses were performed using R-Studio, with ANOVA and Poisson regression models evaluating associations between CHTN severity and outcomes.

Results

The prevalence of CHTN was 2.9% (4,127/137,606) by ACOG criteria and 3.9% (5,424/137,606) by ACC/AHA criteria (p < 0.001). Under ACOG classification, both mild and severe range CHTN were independently associated with preeclampsia or eclampsia (RR 4.15, 95% CI 3.69-4.65; and RR 3.19, 95% CI 2.82-3.59, respectively). Using ACC/AHA criteria, elevated blood pressure (EBP), stage 1 CHTN (S1CHTN), and stage 2 CHTN (S2CHTN) were each independently associated with preeclampsia or eclampsia (EBP: RR 2.34, 95% CI 2.04-2.65; S1CHTN: RR 4.00, 95% CI 3.56-4.50; S2CHTN: RR 3.32, 95% CI 2.88-3.80). Mild CHTN, S1CHTN, and S2CHTN were independently associated with small-for-gestational-age neonates, while both ACOG-defined CHTN and ACC/AHA-defined EBP, S1CHTN, and S2CHTN were associated with preterm birth.

Conclusion

Application of the ACC/AHA classification identifies a larger proportion of pregnant individuals as having CHTN. Notably, even those with elevated blood pressure had a two-fold increased risk of preeclampsia compared with the general obstetric population. These findings support the clinical relevance of the ACC/AHA classification in pregnancy and suggest that its implementation may improve identification of patients who may benefit from targeted preeclampsia prevention strategies.

title: Long-Term Impact of Vutrisiran in Patients With TTR Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy: 1-Year Efficacy and Safety Outcomes From the HELIOS-B Open-Label Extension.
authorString: Garcia-Pavia P, Witteles R, Morbach C, Delgado D, Kitaoka H, Maurer MS, van der Meer P, Yilmaz A, Algalarrondo V, Solomon SD, Cappelli F, Azevedo O, Tang WHW, Lairez O, Boyle KL, Eraly SA, Bao Y, Bender S, Vest J, Fontana M.
abstractText:
Background

In HELIOS-B (A Study to Evaluate Vutrisiran in Patients With Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy), vutrisiran reduced the risk of all-cause mortality (ACM) and recurrent cardiovascular events and slowed disease progression measures versus placebo in patients with TTR (transthyretin) amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy after 33 to 36 months. We report the long-term efficacy and safety of vutrisiran from an ongoing open-label extension of HELIOS-B.

Methods

Patients who completed HELIOS-B could enroll in the open-label extension, continuing with vutrisiran 25 mg every 3 months (continuous vutrisiran) or, if previously receiving placebo, initiating vutrisiran 25 mg every 3 months (placebo/vutrisiran). Prespecified end points assessed in the open-label extension are the composite of ACM and cardiovascular events, ACM, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary score, New York Heart Association class, and NT-proBNP (N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide) and troponin I levels. Outcomes were assessed through month 48 in this analysis.

Results

Of 654 participants in HELIOS-B (vutrisiran, n=326; placebo, n=328), 478 completed double-blind treatment and 466 (vutrisiran, n=243; placebo, n=223) entered the open-label extension. In the continuous vutrisiran group, the risk of first cardiovascular event or ACM was reduced by 37% (hazard ratio, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.51, 0.79]; P=0.0001) and ACM by 37% (hazard ratio, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.46, 0.84]; P=0.0023) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Through month 48, patients in the continuous vutrisiran group had preserved health status and quality of life per Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary score (least squares mean difference, 9.0 [95% CI, 5.3, 12.6]; P<0.0001) and more patients had improved or stable New York Heart Association class (odds ratio, 1.6 [95% CI, 1.1, 2.2]; P=0.0084) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Benefits in the continuous vutrisiran group were maintained for NT-proBNP and troponin I levels (adjusted geometric mean fold change ratios, 0.66 [95% CI, 0.58, 0.74]; P<0.0001; and 0.71 [95% CI, 0.64, 0.79]; P<0.0001, respectively) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Similar benefits were observed in the vutrisiran monotherapy population. No new safety signals were observed.

Conclusions

Long-term vutrisiran resulted in clinically meaningful benefits across mortality, cardiovascular events, cardiac biomarkers, functional status, and quality of life in patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy through month 48. Patients initially treated with vutrisiran had better outcomes than those first receiving placebo, highlighting the importance of early diagnosis and treatment in TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy.

Registration

URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04153149.

title: Association Between Hypoperfusion Intensity Ratio and Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy in Posterior Circulation Stroke: A Retrospective Study.
authorString: Mo M, Tao CR, Yu CY, Chen ZJ, Hu W.
abstractText:
Background

The prognostic utility of the hypoperfusion intensity ratio (HIR) in posterior circulation stroke is undefined. We investigated the association between pretreatment HIR and outcomes after mechanical thrombectomy for acute posterior circulation large vessel occlusion.

Methods

This post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION (Endovascular Treatment for Acute Basilar Artery Occlusion)/ATTENTION-IA (Intra-Arterial Tenecteplase After Successful Endovascular Recanalisation in Patients With Acute Posterior Circulation Arterial Occlusion) trials included patients with posterior circulation occlusion who underwent mechanical thrombectomy and had baseline computed tomography perfusion. HIR (Tmax>10 s/ Tmax>6 s volume) was analyzed. Functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score, 0-2) at 90 days was the primary outcome.

Results

Among 139 patients, higher HIR (per 0.1 increment) was independently associated with lower odds of 90-day modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 2 (adjusted odds ratio, 0.643 [95% CI, 0.422-0.979]; P=0.039). However, its discriminative ability was the modest (area under the curve, 0.617 [95% CI, 0.521-0.712]). The established anterior circulation cutoff (HIR<0.4) did not predict outcomes (P=0.115).

Conclusions

Elevated HIR is independently associated with worse 90-day outcomes after posterior circulation mechanical thrombectomy, but its overall prognostic utility is limited, and the anterior circulation threshold (0.4) could not be validated in this underpowered analysis, highlighting circulation-specific pathophysiological differences.

title: Uncovering cardiac molecular remodelling in racing Thoroughbreds with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.
authorString: Edling CE, Arevalo-Turrubiarte M, Moller-Levet C, Forbes B, Kemp V, Weir J, Tse G, Marr C, Lewis R, Jeevaratnam K.
abstractText:
Background

Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common arrhythmia in both humans and horses, with a comparable prevalence of ~2%. In horses, AF is a major cause of poor athletic performance and linked to sudden cardiac death, yet its underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood.

Objective

To investigate transcriptomic remodelling associated with spontaneous paroxysmal AF (PAF).

Study design

Case-control study.

Methods

We performed RNA sequencing on left atrial (LA) tissue from three Thoroughbred racehorses with PAF and four matched controls. All horses were euthanised due to musculoskeletal reasons. Cell type deconvolution was performed with BayesPrism. The differential expression analysis was performed with EdgeR. Alternative splicing analysis was performed with SUPPA2.

Results

Cell-type deconvolution revealed a modest, non-significant shift towards increased fibroblast and immune cell proportions in PAF, but not enough to account for widespread transcriptional changes. 1400 of the 12,012 included genes were considered significantly differentially expressed (Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value <0.05). These genes included ion channels, calcium-handling proteins, and conduction-related genes. In addition, several genes directly involved in cardiac muscle contraction and mitochondrial energy metabolism were differentially expressed. Alternative splicing analysis revealed over 20 significantly altered events, including skipped exons in genes with potential relevance to cardiac function and remodelling.

Main limitations

The number of biological replicates was modest.

Conclusions

Overall, despite no major changes in cell composition, the findings highlight intrinsic structural and molecular changes in the LA of PAF-affected horses. This study provides the first transcriptomic and splicing analysis of atrial tissue in racehorses with PAF, revealing molecular remodelling consistent with mechanisms of arrhythmia maintenance and suggesting potential targets for further functional investigation.

title: Wearable Arrhythmia Detection: Moving from your Watch to your Shirt?
authorString: Beermann JL, Duncker D.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

Digital devices play an increasingly important role in the detection and screening of cardiac arrhythmias. Atrial fibrillation (AF), the most common arrhythmia, is associated with an increased risk of stroke, heart failure, and mortality. This review summarises the current evidence on wearable devices for screening and diagnosing atrial fibrillation.

Recent findings

Numerous studies have demonstrated the value of wearables for AF detection and diagnosis. In addition, artificial intelligence enhances automated rhythm analysis and signal processing, supporting the increasing clinical implementation of digital technologies in outpatient care. Single-lead ECG devices provide the strongest evidence for AF detection, with smartwatches representing one of the most extensively investigated wearable technology. Limitations include motion artefacts and predominantly semi-continuous monitoring. Future research should focus on integrating artificial intelligence to improve signal analysis and artefact reduction, and on evaluating the impact of wearable-based strategies on clinically relevant outcomes, including stroke and heart failure.

title: Distinct Sex-Associated Phenotypes of Sudden Cardiac Arrest Across Clinical, ECG, and Echocardiographic Domains: Replication in Two Communities and Comparison with the Framingham Heart Study
authorString: Truyen TTTT, Chugh H, Nguyen D, Nakamura K, Uy-Evanado A, Benjamin EJ, Reinier K, Chugh SS.
abstractText:
Background

Sex differences in sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) incidence and outcomes are well established, but risk stratification underperforms in women. It is important to delineate sex-specific patterns in SCA across clinical, electrocardiographic, and echocardiographic domains.

Methods

We studied out-of-hospital SCA cases from the Oregon Sudden Unexpected Death Study (ORSUDS; Portland, 2002–2020; discovery) and Prediction of Sudden Death in Multi-Ethnic Communities (PRESTO; Ventura County, 2015–2024; external replication). Sex differences in 38 comorbidities, 19 ECG and 12 echocardiographic measures were estimated using multivariable-adjusted logistic regression. Female sex was the modeled dependent measure (male as reference). ORSUDS estimates were compared with those in the Framingham Heart Study (FHS), a community-based reference cohort, using FDR-adjusted Cochran Q tests.

Results

Among 5130 ORSUDS cases, 1715 (33.4%) were women (median age, 70.4 years [IQR, 58.7–81.8]) and 3415 (66.6%) were men (65.6 [55.0–76.8]). Compared with men, women had higher BMI (per 5 kg/m², 1.11 [1.08–1.15]) and higher odds of thyroid disease (2.56 [2.17–3.13]), asthma (2.33 [1.92–2.86]), mood disorder (2.17 [1.85–2.50]), dementia (1.27 [1.02–1.56]), and left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH, 3.13 [2.44–4.00]). Women also had lower odds of coronary artery disease (0.61 [0.52–0.71]), atrial fibrillation (0.67 [0.56–0.79]), prolonged QTc (0.45 [0.35–0.57]), prolonged PR (0.53 [0.41–0.68]), premature contractions (0.77 [0.60–0.98]), sleep apnea (0.53 [0.43–0.65]), and reduced LVEF (0.40 [0.29–0.54]). Most findings were replicated in PRESTO (n=2719). In contrast, several of these differences were reversed in the community (FHS, n=3539;FDR-significant): prolonged QTc was more common in women, whereas LVH, dementia, heart failure, and higher BMI were more common in men.

Conclusions

Sex differences among SCA cases were mostly reproducible in SCA cohorts, and distinct from sex-related patterns in the community. These results have implications for development of sex-specific SCA risk assessment and prevention strategies.

Clinical Perspective

What is new?

This study is the first community-based analysis to comprehensively characterize pre-arrest sex-associated profiles across clinical, ECG, and echocardiographic domains, externally validate them, and compare them with a community reference population. Women with SCA were more strongly associated with non-cardiac comorbidities, LVH, preserved LVEF, and mitral valve abnormalities, whereas male cases were characterized by coronary and peripheral vascular disease, atrial fibrillation, prolonged PR and QTc intervals, premature contractions, and reduced LVEF. Several sex associations, including QTc prolongation, LVH, body mass index, heart failure, and dementia, differed in magnitude or direction from patterns in the community reference population.

What are the clinical implications?

Our findings suggest candidate features for future sex specific risk factor analyses and potential components for sex-specific risk models for SCA. Clinicians may need to recognize the critical need to extend beyond dependence on just the value of the left ventricular ejection fraction for SCA risk prediction, especially in women.

title: Latent Transforming Growth Factor Binding Protein-2 promotes microfibrillar TGF-β bioavailability to drive pathologic fibrosis in remote regions of infarcted hearts
authorString: Ehsan F, Di Paola M, Dewar MB, Zhang H, Kuzmanov U, Zhou Y, Reitz CJ, Shah H, Wang T, Liu J, Izumi A, Hu R, Hendy J, Younesi FS, Friedberg M, Billia F, Nakamura T, Hinz B, Mecham RP, Gramolini AO, Heximer SP.
abstractText:
Background

Myocardial infarction (MI) initiates ventricular remodeling that extends beyond the infarct into remote, viable myocardium, where diffuse extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and stiffening contribute to progressive dysfunction and heart failure. Latent transforming growth factor binding protein 2 (LTBP2) is an injury-induced, microfibril-associated ECM glycoprotein that, uniquely among the LTBP family, does not covalently bind latent TGF-β. We asked whether LTBP2 regulates remote remodeling after MI, and how a protein lacking latent TGF-β–binding capacity could influence TGF-β–dependent fibrosis.

Methods

Wild-type and Ltbp2 -null mice underwent permanent coronary ligation or sham surgery and were followed for 28 days by echocardiography and speckle-tracking strain analysis. Remote myocardium was assessed by histology, atomic force microscopy, and quantitative proteomics. Cellular mechanism was interrogated in primary cardiac fibroblasts (CFs) using a TGF-β reporter assay and quantitative imaging of LTBP1 and LTBP2 matrix incorporation. Sufficiency was tested with a minimal fibrillin-1–binding module of LTBP2 delivered as purified protein or by lentiviral expression.

Results

LTBP2 was induced in injury-activated CFs and localized to infarct and remote myocardium by 7 days post-MI. Ltbp2 deletion improved 28-day survival (P=0.0272) without altering infarct size or early post-infarct function. By 28 days, Ltbp2 -null hearts showed improved ejection fraction and faster diastolic strain rates, with protection concentrated in segments remote from the infarct. Remote myocardium contained less interstitial collagen and was significantly less stiff, while cardiomyocyte hypertrophy was unaffected. Proteomic profiling showed enrichment of ECM organization and TGF-β–responsive programs in wild-type hearts that was attenuated in knockouts. In fibroblasts, loss of LTBP2 increased LTBP1 matrix incorporation and shifted TGF-β from the soluble to the matrix-bound compartment; conversely, the minimal LTBP2 module bound fibrillin-1 directly and mobilized latent TGF-β from established matrix within 20 minutes.

Conclusions

LTBP2 drives maladaptive remodeling of remote myocardium after MI by limiting matrix sequestration of latent TGF-β and expanding the activatable pool, resolving how an LTBP that does not bind latent TGF-β amplifies TGF-β–dependent fibrosis. LTBP2 and its fibrillin-1 interaction surface may be tractable targets.

Graphical Abstract

LTBP2 remodels microfibrillar composition to enhance TGF-β bioavailability and profibrotic signaling. Under homeostatic conditions (left), latent TGF-β is sequestered within the extracellular matrix (ECM) as part of the large latent complex (LLC), in which TGF-β is covalently associated with LTBP1 or LTBP4 and tethered to fibrillin-1 microfibrils. This matrix sequestration maintains a balanced distribution between bound and soluble pools of latent TGF-β, thereby limiting ligand activation and downstream signaling. During fibroblast activation (right), LTBP2 expression is upregulated and incorporated into newly assembling fibrillin-1 microfibrillar networks. Although LTBP2 does not covalently bind latent TGF-β, it competes with TGF-β–binding LTBP isoforms for fibrillin-1 binding sites, reducing LLC deposition within the matrix. This competitive remodeling shifts the equilibrium from matrix sequestration toward an expanded soluble LLC pool. Soluble latent complexes are more readily activated through integrin-mediated mechanical stress or proteolytic processing, increasing local active TGF-β levels. This model provides a mechanistic framework whereby LTBP2 indirectly amplifies TGF-β signaling by altering microfibrillar composition and competitive binding dynamics within the ECM, promoting enhanced TGF-β bioavailability and sustained profibrotic remodeling in the remote myocardium.

title: Chronic hypertension disrupts the blood-brain barrier in the ventral hippocampus in females but not males in a rat model of vascular cognitive impairment
authorString: Luchetta J, DeMarco GM, Thaqi A, Bernstein GA, Chavara SE, Schellinger ED, Chen D, Chapman AC.
abstractText:
Background:

Chronic hypertension is a leading cause of cerebrovascular disease, ischemic stroke, and cognitive impairment. In addition, anxiety and hypertension often co-exist, however, little is known about the relationship between the two. Understanding how chronic hypertension impacts limbic brain regions such as the ventral hippocampus may provide insight into how cerebrovascular contributes to altered emotional behavior.

Methods:

An open field task was used to quantify locomotion, exploratory behavior, thigmotaxis, rearing and risk assessment behaviors in adult (7-month-old) male and female normotensive Wistar rats and spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR; n=8/group). Blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability was assessed by measuring extravasation of sodium fluorescein, 3 kDa Texas red dextran and 10 kDa cascade blue into the ventral hippocampus. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays were used to measure markers of vascular signaling, inflammation, and central nervous system-specific proteins indicative of neuroaxonal and glial injury in serum from separate groups of male and female SHR (n=6/group). Main effects and interactions between two independent variables (sex and hypertension) were determined using two-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) with Tukey's post-hoc tests. Circulating factors were compared using a Welch's t-test. Relationships between BBB permeability and anxiety-like behavior were determined using Pearson's correlations.

Results:

Chronic hypertension increased circulating inflammatory factors and BBB permeability in female but not male rats. BBB permeability did not differ by sex in male and female normotensive rats. There was an anxiolytic effect of chronic hypertension on exploratory-related anxiety-like behavior, including less thigmotaxis, lower latency to cross through the center of the arena, and increased unsupported rearing. Risk assessment behavior, quantified as stretch-attend posture, was increased in female SHR. BBB permeability in the ventral hippocampus was correlated with anxiety-like behavior in females, but not in males, suggesting sex-dependent mechanisms of hypertension-induced changes in emotional behavior.

Conclusions:

These findings implicate a role for chronic hypertension-induced BBB disruption in neuropsychiatric disorders in the female sex and advances our understanding of cerebrovascular vulnerability in deep limbic brain regions.

title: Prevalence and Clinical Characteristics of Renal Disease in Hiv Patients at a Tertiary Care Hospital
authorString: Jain V, Ahmad F, Shetty MS, kelur kK.
abstractText: Background Renal disease is a significant comorbidity among people living with HIV (PLHIV), contributing to morbidity and mortality despite antiretroviral therapy (ART). Limited data exist regarding the prevalence and clinical characteristics of renal disease in HIV-positive patients in India. Objectives To determine the prevalence of renal disease among HIV-positive patients at a tertiary care hospital and to identify risk factors associated with renal involvement, including the correlation between CD4 + count and renal dysfunction. Materials and Methods This prospective cross-sectional study was conducted at JSS Medical College and Hospital, Mysuru, from September 2023 to March 2025. A total of 147 HIV-positive patients aged 18–70 years were enrolled. Renal disease was defined as serum creatinine > 1.3 mg/dL or urine albumin ≥ 2 + on dipstick. Data collected included demographics, clinical parameters, CD4 + count, ART regimen, comorbidities, and renal function tests. Statistical analysis included chi-square test, correlation analysis, and multivariate logistic regression. Results The mean age was 45.7 ± 12.8 years with male predominance (65.3%). The overall prevalence of renal disease was 21.1% (95% CI: 14.6–28.6%). Among affected patients, 48.4% had elevated creatinine only, 32.3% had significant albuminuria only, and 19.4% had both. Hypertension was significantly associated with renal disease (OR 2.76, p = 0.031). CD4 + count showed a significant inverse relationship with renal disease (p = 0.032). Multivariate analysis identified hypertension (adjusted OR 3.12, p = 0.022) and CD4 + count per 100 cells/µL decrease (adjusted OR 1.28, p = 0.041) as independent predictors. Conclusion Renal disease affects approximately one in five HIV-positive patients. Hypertension and low CD4 + count are significant independent risk factors, underscoring the importance of systematic renal screening, blood pressure management, and early ART initiation.

title: Prognostic factors associated with In-Hospital Mortality Among Heart Failure Patients in a Private Tertiary Hospital in Sierra Leone: A Five-Year Cohort Study
authorString: Russell JBW, Smith M, Alhassan Y, Coker JM, Tejan EA, Bharat K, Kumari M, Ireland PZ, Mahdi OZ, Lisk DR.
abstractText: Background Evidence on in-hospital mortality among adults with heart failure (HF) in Sierra Leone is limited. We evaluated prognostic factors associated with all-cause in-hospital mortality and described mortality patterns during admission over five years. Methods This retrospective study analysed decompensated HF patients admitted to a private hospital in Sierra Leone from 2021 to 2025. Only the index admission per patient was included to summarize baseline characteristics, estimate in-hospital survival, and examine associations with mortality using Cox regression. Covariates violating the proportional hazards assumption were modelled with linear time interactions. Results Among the 765 patients studied [median age 53 years (IQR 42–61); 55.3% male], all 88 deaths occurred within the first week of admission, resulting in a mortality rate of 11.5% (95% CI 9.3–13.9). The annual mortality rate decreased from 19.7% in 2021 to 7.1% in 2025 (overall heterogeneity p = 0.008). A cold-wet haemodynamic profile was present in 77.3% of patients who died and 6.4% of survivors (unadjusted comparison, p < 0.001). In the final model, underweight [aHR = 2.44, (95% CI 1.46–4.07)], overweight [aHR = 1.93, (95% CI 1.05–3.57)], recurrent HF [aHR = 1.71, (95% CI 1.14–2.58)], and dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) in women [aHR = 15.25, (95% CI 6.66–34.93)] were associated with higher mortality, whereas hypertensive heart disease (HHD) was associated with a lower hazard [aHR = 0.20, (95% CI 0.07–0.52)]. Baseline anaemia, chronic kidney disease (CKD) and Atrial Fibrillation (AF) showed non-proportional associations with mortality. Estimates from the complex final model are exploratory because 88 deaths supported 22 model degrees of freedom. Conclusions The in-hospital mortality rate among HF patients was relatively high but gradually decreased over the study period. Most deaths were reported within the first seven days and were associated with several comorbidities. These findings underscore the importance of early risk assessment and targeted management to reduce mortality in under-resourced settings.

title: Association Between the Endothelial Activation and Stress Index and All-Cause Mortality in Critically Ill Patients with Stage 4 Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome: A Retrospective Cohort Study Based on MIMIC-IV and External Validation in eICU-CRD
authorString: lu q, Liu J, Luo Y, Wan J, Liao B.
