This narrative review synthesises current knowledge on the pathophysiology, imaging and treatment of lymphatic complications in the Fontan circulation. Lymphatic involvement is frequent, under-diagnosed, and prognostically important; the integration of advanced lymphatic imaging and the consolidation of expertise in specialised percutaneous lymphatic intervention represent the most relevant advances of the last decade.

title: Prediction of Bailout Mechanical Circulatory Support Use for Hemodynamic Collapse During PCI: The ORACLE Score.
authorString: Poletti E, Seth M, Ng P, Chung CJ, Elison D, Steinberg ZL, Lombardi WL, Cantey E, Hamilton DE, Gurm HS, Azzalini L.
abstractText: Background: Bailout mechanical circulatory support (MCS) may be used in the setting of intraprocedural hemodynamic collapse during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). We developed and externally validated a simple risk prediction model for bailout MCS use for hemodynamic collapse during PCI. Methods: Consecutive patients undergoing PCI at a tertiary hospital between 2018 and 2025 were included in the derivation cohort (n=6,931), after excluding cases of salvage PCI and procedures performed with pre-existing or prophylactic MCS. The primary endpoint was bailout MCS use for hemodynamic collapse. A multivariable Firth logistic regression model was developed, internally validated, and translated into a simplified integer-based risk score (ORACLE). External validation was performed in 214,877 PCIs from the Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan Cardiovascular Consortium (BMC2) registry. Results: The incidence of bailout MCS was 1.4% in the derivation cohort. Six variables (non-elective presentation, systolic blood pressure, chronic heart failure, prior PCI, rotational/orbital atherectomy, and left main PCI) independently predicted the primary endpoint. The regression model demonstrated good discrimination both in the derivation (area under the curve [AUC] 0.817; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.774-0.860) and external validation (AUC 0.761; 95% CI 0.753-0.770) cohorts. The simplified ORACLE score preserved most of the discriminatory performance of the full model (AUC 0.791 in the derivation cohort and 0.718 in the external validation cohort) and effectively stratified patients, with observed bailout MCS rates ranging from 0.4% in the low-risk category to 8.7% in the high-risk group, with similar findings in the external validation cohort. Discrimination was consistent across clinically relevant subgroups. Negative predictive value was >99% in both the derivation and external validation cohorts. Conclusions:: ORACLE is a simple score to estimate the risk of bailout MCS use for hemodynamic collapse during PCI, which may support preprocedural risk assessment.

title: Type I IFN autoantibodies in three of seven Europeans with life-threatening Usutu virus infection.
authorString: Gervais A, Bastard P, Bizien L, Trespidi F, Angelini M, Rossini G, Lazzarotto T, Baldanti F, Rovida F, Ferrari A, Mancon A, Mileto D, Cassaniti I, Conti F, Schmidt-Chanasit J, Cadar D, Florian DM, Borghesi A, Puel A, Delifer C, Tiberghien P, de Lamballerie X, Durand GA, Aberle JH, Nagy A, Simonin Y, Cobat A, Zhang SY, Casanova JL.
abstractText: We previously reported that two of three patients with severe Usutu virus (USUV) disease carried circulating autoantibodies (auto-Abs) neutralizing type I IFNs (AAN-I-IFN). Here, we studied four additional patients, bringing the total number of European patients with life-threatening USUV infection to seven (Austria, n = 1; France, n = 1; Hungary, n = 4; Italy, n = 1). Three of these patients (all male, aged 43, 77, and 78 years, one French and two Hungarian) had blood auto-Abs neutralizing at least 10 ng/ml IFN-α2 and IFN-ω and at least 1 ng/ml IFN-β. They suffered from meningitis (n = 1), meningoencephalitis (n = 1), or myocarditis (n = 1). The other four patients were similar demographically and clinically but had no detectable AAN-I-IFN. No AAN-I-IFN were found in the 63 individuals with silent USUV infection tested (P = 6.4 × 10-4, Fisher's exact test). These AAN-I-IFN increased the risk of life-threatening USUV disease by 98.8-fold (95% CI: 4.12-2,369; P = 0.0046, Firth's bias-corrected logistic regression) and, thus, account for almost half the cases of life-threatening USUV infection in Europe.

title: Early and persistent blood pressure dysregulation in individuals with subacute motor incomplete spinal cord injury.
authorString: van Oort MJ, Langerak NG, Hopman MTE, Thijssen DHJ, van Nes IJW.

journal.title: The journal of spinal cord medicine

abstractText:
Context

Blood pressure (BP) dysregulation after spinal cord injury (SCI) may disrupt circadian BP rhythms, including absent nocturnal dipping, high BP variability, and hypertension. These disturbances are independent predictors of cardiovascular disease, yet evidence in older adults with subacute motor incomplete SCI is limited.

Objective

To characterize nocturnal dipping status, BP variability, and daytime and nighttime hypertension at admission to inpatient rehabilitation, and to assess changes during rehabilitation.Observational cohort study.

Setting

Primary inpatient rehabilitation center.

Participants

Individuals with motor incomplete SCI who completed 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring shortly after admission and before discharge.

Interventions

Not applicable.

Outcome measures

Nocturnal dipping (% reduction from nighttime to daytime systolic BP), BP variability, and hypertension defined using general population thresholds.

Results

Participants with motor incomplete SCI were included (n = 34, mean age 61 years, 82% male, 44% cervical injury). At admission, 82% were classified as non-dippers or reverse dippers. High BP variability was present in 59% for systolic BP and 29% for diastolic BP. Hypertension occurred in 21% during daytime and 59% during nighttime. All but one participant exhibited at least one BP-related risk factor. No changes were observed in dipping status, BP variability, and mean BP levels between admission and discharge (all p > 0.05).

Conclusion

Marked BP dysregulation is evident early after motor incomplete SCI, including absent nocturnal dipping, high BP variability, and nocturnal hypertension, despite daytime BP appearing within normal limits in most participants. These disturbances persisted throughout rehabilitation, indicating ongoing autonomic dysregulation that may contribute to long-term cardiovascular risk.

title: Does reading patient information leaflets influence adherence and adverse drug reactions in arterial hypertension? A cross-sectional study.
authorString: Tyjas K, Polaczyk M, Chudy R, Zuwała M, Hońdo Ł, Rajzer M, Stolarz-Skrzypek K.
abstractText:
Introduction

Most patients after receiving pharmacotherapy prescription read patient information leaflets (PILs). Many studies highlight the role of the nocebo effect, whereby information on adverse drug reactions (ADRs) increases symptom reporting.

Objectives

The aim of this study was to assess the association between reading PILs, adherence to pharmacotherapy, and the frequency and types of reported ADRs.

Patients and methods

This cross-sectional questionnaire-based study included patients receiving inpatient or outpatient care at a hypertension clinic. The analysis included data from 949 individuals (529 female, 420 male) diagnosed with arterial hypertension.

Results

Approximately 60% of patients reported reading PILs. Compared with non-readers, they were younger (median age 63 vs 67 years), had a shorter duration of hypertension (median duration 10 vs 11.5 years), and fewer cardiovascular comorbidities, while the prevalence of non-cardiovascular comorbidities and the number of medications prescribed did not differ between groups. PILs readers more frequently reported adherence to medical recommendations (98% vs 61%), although 11% reported self-discontinuation at least once after reading the leaflet. They also reported a lower overall frequency of ADRs (38% vs 57%), mainly driven by fewer allergic and idiosyncratic reactions (23% vs 40%), while pharmacologically predictable ADRs did not differ between groups.

Conclusions

Reading PILs was positively associated with self-reported adherence to medical recommendations and with a lower frequency of reported ADRs. These findings suggest that the beneficial effect of improved adherence associated with reading PILs may outweigh the potential negative impact of the nocebo effect.

title: Early recognition of paediatric kidney disease in low- and middle-income countries: Clinical red flags and referral strategies for primary care.
authorString: Prakash TS.
abstractText: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) in children is an important but often under-recognized cause of long-term morbidity, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) where delayed diagnosis is common. Early manifestations are frequently subtle and include oedema, haematuria, proteinuria, recurrent urinary tract infections, growth failure, hypertension, and unexplained anaemia. This review highlights practical clinical red flags that should prompt evaluation for kidney disease, outlines low-cost investigations feasible in primary care, and summarizes indications for timely nephrology referral. Emphasis is placed on careful history-taking, targeted physical examination, blood pressure measurement, urinalysis, serum creatinine estimation, and renal ultrasonography where indicated. Strengthening awareness among frontline healthcare providers and caregivers, together with structured referral pathways, may facilitate earlier diagnosis, preserve kidney function, reduce preventable complications, and improve long-term outcomes for children with kidney disease in resource-limited settings.

title: Targeting ALDOA Lactylation Reverses Vascular Remodeling in Pulmonary Hypertension by Disrupting Actin Polymerization and YAP Activation.
authorString: Huang X, Zhang J, Zeng Q, Lin M, Bai J, Feng H, Liu J, Sha Z, Peng T, Lv Y, Zhang X, Li S, Li T, Qu J, Shao S, Liu Q, Liang S, Yang K, Tang H, Zhang Z, He Y, Duan Z, Kong D.
abstractText:
Background

Maladaptive vascular remodeling is a hallmark of pulmonary hypertension (PH), and therapeutic strategies directly targeting the pathological activity of smooth muscle cells remain limited. Metabolic and epigenetic dysregulation are established drivers of PH, and lysine lactylation has emerged as a novel posttranslational modification implicated in diverse diseases; however, its direct contribution to PH progression remains undefined.

Methods

Integrated lactylomic and proteomic profiling was performed in hypoxic human pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells. The functional role of ALDOA (aldolase A) lactylation at lysine 42 (K42) was assessed using site-specific mutant virus and smooth muscle cell-specific inducible ALDOA knockout mice in 2 established PH models: SU5416+hypoxia in mice and monocrotaline in rats.

Results

We identified ALDOA as a prominent lactylation target in hypoxic pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells, with K42 lactylation consistently elevated in primary pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells derived from PH rodent models and human PH tissues. Mechanistically, AARS1 (alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1)-mediated ALDOA K42 lactylation enhanced its binding to γ-actin, independent of glycolytic activity. This lactylation-enhanced interaction promoted F-actin polymerization and activated YAP (Yes-associated protein) signaling via LATS1 (large tumor suppressor kinase 1) inhibition, thereby driving pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cell proliferation and phenotypic switching. Moreover, YAP/TEAD4 (TEA domain transcription factor 4)-mediated transcriptional upregulation of AARS1 established a positive feedback loop reinforcing ALDOA K42 lactylation under hypoxia. In vivo, ALDOA inducible knockout or reconstitution with the lactylation-deficient K42R (lysine 42 mutant to arginine) mutant attenuated experimental PH progression, with suppressed F-actin/YAP activation and reduced vascular remodeling. Furthermore, competitive inhibition of lactylation through β‑alanine reduced ALDOA K42 lactylation and ameliorated vascular remodeling in ALDOA-overexpressing rodent PH models. Translationally, pharmacological disruption of the ALDOA/γ-actin interaction by raltegravir suppressed cytoskeletal reorganization and YAP signaling, mitigating PH progression in both mouse and rat models.

Conclusions

AARS1-mediated ALDOA K42 lactylation drives pulmonary vascular remodeling through a mechanism independent of ALDOA's catalytic activity, promoting F-actin polymerization and YAP activation. Precision targeting of this modification selectively inhibits pathological signaling while preserving metabolic homeostasis, highlighting a translational potential for precision intervention in PH.

title: CD36 Gates Nocturnal Hypertension via the Renal AMPK/HDAC5/PER1 Axis.
authorString: Chen M, Zhang Y, Fu S, Chen M, Li X, Wang Z, Zhang M, Li D, Luo S, Wei L, Li S, Chen L, Chen Y, Ruan XZ.
abstractText:
Background

Nocturnal hypertension is a strong predictor of cardio-cerebrovascular disease, yet its underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. In this study, we identified CD36 as a key regulator of blood pressure (BP) rhythms and as a gatekeeper of nocturnal hypertension. Its deficiency disrupts circadian BP rhythms.

Methods

We continuously monitored 48-hour BP using telemetry in CD36 global knockout mice and renal proximal tubule-specific CD36 knockout mice. We also collected serum samples and ambulatory BP monitoring data from patients with nocturnal hypertension to assess the relationship between CD36 expression and nocturnal hypertension. A comprehensive screening of various factors affecting BP and circadian rhythms was conducted to explore the molecular mechanisms.

Results

Our telemetry data revealed significantly elevated BP during the daytime (inactive period) in both CD36 global knockout and renal proximal tubule-specific knockout mice compared with their control counterparts. Furthermore, levels of platelet CD36 were negatively correlated with the severity of nocturnal hypertension in humans. Mechanistically, CD36 modulates BP rhythms through the AMPK (AMP-activated protein kinase)/HDAC5 (histone deacetylase 5)/PER1 pathway: its deficiency activates phosphorylated AMPK, leading to the dissociation of the HDAC5-PER1 complex, enhancing PER1 nuclear accumulation, and desynchronizing the oscillations of intrarenal renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system genes and clock-controlled genes, ultimately disrupting BP rhythm.

Conclusions

Our findings highlight CD36 as a critical integrator that links renal clocks to BP homeostasis, establishing it as a potential predictor and therapeutic target for nocturnal hypertension.

title: Management of dialysis catheter-related thrombus.
authorString: Allon M.

journal.title: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension

abstractText:
Purpose of review

The goal of this review is to provide a comprehensive update on the clinical manifestations and medical management of intraluminal hemodialysis catheter thrombosis and central vein stenosis and thrombosis related to hemodialysis catheters.

Recent findings

The two thrombolytic agents used most frequently to treat dialysis catheter dysfunction, alteplase and urokinase, have a similar immediate efficacy of about 80%. A 2 mg per lumen dose of alteplase is superior to a 1 mg per lumen dose, and a 30-min instillation is as effective as a longer instillation time. Restoration of catheter function after instillation of a thrombolytic agents is often short-lived. Catheters with intra-luminal thrombosis frequently require repetitive thrombolytic instillation, and many patients ultimately require catheter exchange when instillation of a thrombolytic agent is no longer effective. Central vein stenosis and thrombosis are seen in about 25% of patients with a hemodialysis catheter. They are often recurrent, and the role of anticoagulation is uncertain.

Summary

Clinicians should recognize the clinical manifestations and medical management of hemodialysis catheter-related thrombosis and its management. We need more research to better understand whether anticoagulation is indicated in central vein thrombosis.

title: Transcatheter ventricular septal shunt creation in end-stage paediatric pulmonary arterial hypertension: lessons from a rescue decompression strategy.
authorString: Torun EG, Bagrul D, Ece İ.
abstractText: A 12-year-old girl with end-stage suprasystemic pulmonary arterial hypertension and progressive right ventricular failure underwent transcatheter ventricular septal shunt creation after deterioration despite targeted therapy and prior atrial septostomy. Right-to-left shunting was established, but haemodynamic improvement was limited; pulmonary pressures remained suprasystemic, persistent pericardial effusion developed, and the patient died despite intensive treatment, illustrating the complexity of rescue decompression in advanced disease.

title: Integrated survey of Taenia solium endemicity, schistosomiasis, scabies, and Guinea-worm disease in northern Namibia.
authorString: Katokele S, Kaura U, Hailu S, Soroses WF, Nairenge R, Juma E, Abela B, Garba Djirmay A, Shikwambi HM, Amaambo M, Wangui N, Mutono N, Gass K, Donadeu M, Mwinzi P.
abstractText:
Background

During a Mass drug administration (MDA) campaign for schistosomiasis using praziquantel in Namibia in 2019, three cases of serious neurological adverse events were observed due to neurocysticercosis caused by the parasite Taenia solium. To have a better understanding of T. solium endemicity, and to prevent and minimize adverse events in future disease control campaigns, the Ministry of Health and Social Services of Namibia decided to conduct field surveys, and take the opportunity to integrate schistosomiasis, scabies, and Guinea-worm disease (GWD) surveillance.

Methods

In July 2024, ten survey teams were deployed to the five regions selected as high-risk (Kavango West, Ohangwena, Omusati, Oshana and Oshikoto), using the World Health Organization (WHO) Risk Classification tool for T. solium. Stool and urine samples were collected and analyzed using Kato-Katz and urine filtration, interviews were undertaken relating to GWD and clinical assessments conducted for scabies. Geographical variations in parasite distribution were evaluated for each species using the design-adjusted Rao-Scott second-order chi-square test of independence.

Results

Roaming pigs and deficient sanitation were confirmed in all regions (61% of the households reported not having a latrine). Laboratory analysis of 4880 stool samples confirmed the presence of T. solium in all regions except Oshana. Only Ohangwena, with a positivity rate of 0.6%, reached the threshold suggested by the WHO to trigger a public health program. However, T. solium was also present in another three regions below the WHO threshold, and while it was not detected in Oshana, it was detected in nearby villages in Ohangwena and Oshikoto. The analysis of 4876 urine samples showed the prevalence of schistosomiasis was only above the threshold to trigger MDA in Kavango West (9.98% for Schistosoma haematobium, and 1.65% for S. mansoni). The overall prevalence of scabies was 1.9% and below the suggested level to justify MDA in all regions. Three households in Ohangwena, near the border with Angola, reported having seen GWD in humans or dogs.

Conclusions

The results provide updated information on T. solium and schistosomiasis endemicity and will guide future disease control efforts, including the prevention, early identification and management of praziquantel-related adverse events.

title: Differential effects of chronic hypertension and sex on vascular density along the septotemporal axis of the hippocampus in a rat model of VCID
authorString: Luchetta J, Schellinger ED, Bolton Z, DeMarco GM, Chapman AC.
abstractText:
Background

Chronic hypertension is a major modifiable risk factor for vascular contributions to cognitive impairment and dementia (VCID), yet vascular changes that precede cognitive dysfunction remain poorly understood. This is particularly relevant for the hippocampus, a deep brain structure critical to memory function, which differs along its septotemporal axis functionally and in its susceptibility to hypoxic/ischemic injury. The impacts of hypertension and sex on hippocampal vascularization remains unclear and could contribute to the development/progression of VCID.

Methods

In this study, adult male and female Wistar and spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR) were used at 5 months old, an age before memory impairments. Vascular density and morphometric parameters in dorsal and ventral hippocampus were quantified using high-resolution confocal microscopy and 3D vascular reconstruction.

Results

In SHR, vascular density was increased in the dorsal hippocampus in males and across dorsal and ventral hippocampus in females compared to normotensive rats. Diameter and length of the microvasculature shifted to be smaller and longer during hypertension in males, but not females.

Conclusions

These findings demonstrate chronic hypertension increases vascular density differentially by sex along the septotemporal axis of the hippocampus in mid adulthood that may increase vascular resistance and potentiate perfusion deficits or increase sites of blood-brain barrier disruption and contribute to VCID.

title: Acute Reversible Posterior Encephalopathy Triggered by Sheath Removal Pain After Coronary Angiography: A Case Report
authorString: Zhang¹ X, Yu¹ J, Zhao¹ W.
abstractText: Background When acute neurological symptoms appear after coronary angiography, contrast-induced encephalopathy (CIE) and posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) are key differential diagnoses. Yet the role of acute peri-procedural pain as a potential trigger has received little attention. Case presentation A 77-year-old man with hypertension and stage 3 chronic kidney disease developed severe pain during radial sheath removal three hours after coronary angiography. Within seconds, he lost consciousness and had generalized tonic-clonic seizures. Blood pressure rose from 136/70 mmHg to 160/90 mmHg. CT perfusion imaging showed hypoperfusion in the left temporal and bilateral occipital lobes, with relatively preserved cerebral blood volume and cerebral blood flow, and prolonged mean transit time and time-to-peak. A second seizure occurred later that evening, without a clear pain trigger, suggesting a persistent process with a tendency for spontaneous recurrence. The patient recovered completely within four days with conservative management and remained symptom-free at six-month follow-up. CIE and PRES could not be definitively diagnosed because MRI and EEG were not performed. Conclusions This case suggests that acute peri-procedural pain may trigger acute reversible posterior encephalopathy. The temporal association—measured in seconds—between pain and neurological symptom onset is exceptionally rare. Clinicians should recognize the potential value of peri-procedural pain management in preventing such complications.

title: Influence of Blood Pressure Change on Cerebral Perfusion During Interventional Embolization of Intracranial Aneurysm
authorString: Liu Y, Ma H, Wu P, Su X.
abstractText: Background : Rupture and hemorrhage of intracranial aneurysms constitute the leading cause of spontaneous subarachnoid hemorrhage. Endovascular embolization is the primary treatment for intracranial aneurysms, where intraoperative blood pressure management is critical to prevent aneurysm rupture and cerebral hypoperfusion. However, unified optimal intraoperative and postoperative blood pressure control standards remain undefined due to insufficient clinical evidence. Methods: This study aimed to explore risk factors for cerebral hypoperfusion during intracranial aneurysm embolization and provide evidence for precise anesthetic management. Results Of the 89 patients included, 55 (61.8%) developed postoperative PI > 1.1. The hypoperfusion group had a higher proportion of hypertension (60.0% vs. 32.4%, P = 0.021) and greater intraoperative SBP variance (median 652.82 vs. 373.19 mmHg², P = 0.009). Multivariable analysis identified hypertension (a OR 2.72, 95% CI 1.09–6.81, P = 0.033) and SBP variance (a OR 1.02, 95% CI 1.00–1.04, P = 0.009) as independent predictors of PI > 1.1. A significant interaction was found between hypertension and SBP variance ( P = 0.022); the effect of hypertension was strongest in patients with above-median SBP variance (aOR 20.68, 95% CI 2.25–190.49, P = 0.007). The nomogram integrating these two predictors showed moderate discrimination (AUC 0.706, 95% CI 0.599–0.813). Conclusions: In conclusion, intraoperative systolic blood pressure variability and a history of hypertension are independently linked to postoperative cerebral hypoperfusion following endovascular embolization of intracranial aneurysms. Hypertensive patients are particularly sensitive to blood pressure changes. A baseline diastolic blood pressure of 96 mmHg appears to have a threshold effect. A straightforward nomogram based on these factors could aid in personalized blood pressure control and risk assessment during and after endovascular aneurysm interventions. Further validation in larger cohorts is necessary.

title: GLP-1 Receptor agonist use and attempted access in individuals with and without lifetime eating disorders: The role of diagnostic history, BMI, and medication motivation
authorString: Mantilla EF, Hog L, Dinkler L, Lu Y, Bulik CM, Thornton LM, Birgegård A.
abstractText: Background Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist medications (GLP-1RAs) have revolutionized management of type-2 diabetes and obesity and are increasingly widespread. In eating disorders (ED), where dietary restriction is a triggering and maintaining factor, concerns have been raised regarding risks related to GLP-1RAs. Methods We studied self-reported prescribed, unprescribed, and attempted use in 5882 individuals with various lifetime EDs compared to 1322 controls, stratified by highest lifetime body mass index (BMI) following drug indication thresholds (above 30 or above 27 with complications, e.g. hypertension). Logistic regression models using single-diagnosis- and mutually adjusted models was used, and prescription for T2D was used as a covariate to control for purely medically motivated use. Results Lifetime atypical anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, and binge eating disorder were generally associated with higher engagement compared to controls. Anorexia nervosa was associated with lower engagement in participants with lifetime BMI above 30, but higher engagement in BMI strata below 30 and below 27. Sex-separated analyses suggested higher engagement in males with lifetime anorexia nervosa also in higher-weight strata. Avoidant-restrictive food intake disorder did not differ from controls on any outcome. While weight loss was the primary motivation for engagement, a notable proportion cited management of binge eating even though that is not among the approved indications. Conclusions Findings suggest that lifetime ED is associated with heightened drug-seeking and inappropriate use in some individuals, and support recent calls for increased monitoring of ED history and symptoms in relation to GLP-1RA treatment.

title: Awareness of Feeding Habits Nutritional Status and Nutrition-Related Health Problems Among Elderly Persons in Agbor Delta State Nigeria
authorString: Ebie CV.
abstractText: Background Population ageing is accompanied by increasing nutritional challenges, including inadequate dietary intake, malnutrition, overweight and nutrition-related chronic diseases. However, limited information is available on feeding habits, nutritional status and awareness of nutrition-related health problems among older persons in Delta State, Nigeria. Objectives This study assessed the awareness of appropriate feeding habits, nutritional status, dietary practices and nutrition-related health problems among older persons in Agbor, Delta State, Nigeria. Methods A cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted among 392 older persons in eight communities in Agbor, Delta State. Data were collected using a structured interviewer-administered questionnaire covering sociodemographic characteristics, awareness of appropriate feeding habits and nutrition-related health problems, dietary practices and a 24-hour dietary recall. Anthropometric measurements were obtained to determine body mass index (BMI) and waist-to-hip ratio (WHR). Data were analysed using descriptive statistics. Results Participants were predominantly aged 65–74 years (65.0%), and 53.0% were female. Awareness of appropriate feeding habits was variable. While 65.0% recognised the importance of regular meals and 65.1% understood that feeding habits influence health and nutritional status, awareness was low regarding dietary variety (30.0%), adequate protein intake (35.0%), limitation of fatty or fried foods (31.1%) and consumption of whole grains and fibre (12.0%). Awareness of nutrition-related health problems was also inconsistent. Most participants recognised that inadequate food intake could cause malnutrition (83.5%) and that inadequate nutritious food could result in underweight (80.5%), while awareness of the relationships between excess salt and hypertension (23.0%), iron-rich foods and anaemia (22.5%), and dietary variety and micronutrient deficiency (24.3%) was poor. Dietary practices showed that 56.0% ate twice daily, 54.3% skipped meals and 48.0% reported that they did not eat enough food. Among those who skipped meals, lack of strength to prepare food (51.0%) and inability to afford food (49.0%) were major reasons. Anthropometric assessment revealed a substantial burden of malnutrition: 27.0% were underweight, while 24.0% were overweight and 30.6% had obesity. Overall, 54.6% were overweight or obese, and 51.5% had an elevated waist-to-hip ratio. Conclusion Older persons in Agbor experience a substantial double burden of malnutrition characterised by the coexistence of undernutrition, overweight/obesity and central adiposity. Gaps in awareness of healthy feeding practices and nutrition-related health risks were accompanied by frequent meal skipping and inadequate food intake. Community-based nutrition education, improved access to affordable nutrient-dense foods, routine nutritional screening and nutrition counselling should be integrated into healthcare and social support services for older persons in Agbor.

title: Cohort dependent associations between gut Bacteroides and circulating sphingolipid balance
authorString: Song H, Yu DJ, Go Y, Oh C.
abstractText: Taxonomic and gene-level measurements offer complementary views of microbial contributions to host lipid metabolism. We examined gut Bacteroides abundance, bacterial serine palmitoyltransferase (SPT) gene read abundance and circulating sphingolipids in heart failure and MetaCardis. In 58 patients, the Bacteroides association with the lactosylceramide(16:0)-to-ceramide(16:0) ratio persisted across 85 observations (β = 0.296, P = 0.007). Bacteroides abundance correlated with SPT read abundance (ρ = 0.389, P = 0.0026), but SPT did not improve the adjusted lipid model (likelihood-ratio P = 0.828). The primary MetaCardis analysis did not reproduce the ratio association (n = 544; permutation P = 0.127). An exploratory analysis identified an inverse Bacteroides –lactosylceramide association (n = 972; P = 0.0029). These findings establish a framework for distinguishing cohort-specific taxonomic associations from measured microbial gene abundance and prioritise direct functional validation of microbiome–sphingolipid relationships.

title: Temporal Validation of Machine-Learning Models for Predicting Postoperative Atrial Fibrillation After Valve or Coronary Artery Bypass Surgery
authorString: Yu Y, Xia J, Yang C, Jiang Q.
abstractText: Background Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is common after valve or coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery, but prediction models often lack temporal validation and calibration assessment. We hypothesized that left atrial volume index (LAVI), as a marker of chronic atrial substrate, would be more transportable than perioperative stress variables and that regularized models would generalize better than complex algorithms under temporal shift. Methods We used a case-enriched retrospective development cohort of 347 patients (189 POAF events; May 2022–May 2025) and a prospective temporal cohort of 167 consecutive patients (44 events; June–December 2025). Eleven classifiers were assessed by repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation with fold-contained preprocessing, then frozen and applied to the temporal cohort. We evaluated discrimination, calibration, decision-curve net benefit, explainability, independent predictors, and six-month prognosis. Results LAVI was the strongest perioperative predictor (adjusted odds ratio per SD, 3.19; 95% CI, 1.66–6.12; P < 0.001). Random forest had the highest internal AUROC (0.827; 95% CI, 0.783–0.870), whereas the frozen preoperative ridge model performed best temporally (AUROC, 0.723; 95% CI, 0.639–0.808). The case-enriched development sample caused absolute-risk overprediction (mean predicted 0.442 vs observed 0.263; integrated calibration index [ICI], 0.173); intercept-only recalibration improved ICI to 0.048. Platt scaling fitted in the temporal cohort yielded an apparent ICI of 0.009 and was treated as exploratory updating. DCA indicates that within the decision threshold range of 0.10–0.50, the clinical benefit is greater than that of the "all-treatment/no-treatment" strategy. POAF was associated with six-month AF recurrence (7/43 vs 1/112; odds ratio, 21.58) and a higher composite-event hazard (adjusted hazard ratio, 3.22; 95% CI, 1.00–10.34; P = 0.050). Conclusions LAVI captured a transportable atrial-substrate signal, while the internally best nonlinear model did not retain superiority under temporal shift. The preoperative ridge model requires recalibration and independent multicenter validation before deployment. POAF identified persistent arrhythmic vulnerability through six months.

title: FAK- and TGF-β1-dependent biomechanical alterations in microvascular endothelial cells exposed to fluid shear stress gradients.
authorString: Sánchez-Rendón JC, Keskin E, Oder N, Reuss A, Michalaki E, Fuller GG, Dunn A, Bastounis EE.
abstractText: Endothelial cells (EC) form a dynamic monolayer barrier that regulates vascular permeability and is highly sensitive to mechanical cues, including shear stresses (SS) generated by blood flow. While spatial shear stress gradients (SSG) are linked to vascular pathologies such as atherosclerosis, their direct effects on cellular biomechanics across EC subtypes remain underexplored. Here, using an impinging flow device compatible with videomicroscopy, we demonstrate that exposure of two EC types to SSG causes an immediate and sustained two-fold decrease in migration speed, accompanied by enhanced coordination of collective motion and directional migration against the flow. Concurrently, EC traction and monolayer stresses increase acutely upon flow onset and continue to rise linearly over time. Mechanistically, FAK-mediated mechanotransduction governs flow-opposed migration, whereas the time-dependent increase in traction depends on TGF-β1 signaling and actomyosin contractility. Together, these findings identify SSG as key regulators of EC mechanics, collective dynamics, and signaling, with important implications for vascular disease diagnostics and therapeutics.

title: Sleep Architecture, Glucose Regulation and Subclinical Cardiovascular Risk in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus: A Wearable Sleep Tracking and Continuous Glucose Monitoring Study.
authorString: Marhefková N, Mikušová V, Roland R, Pazderník M, Wohlfahrt P, Novodvorský P, Sládek M, Sumová A, Haluzík M, Dubský M.
abstractText:
Objective

To investigate the associations of wearable-derived sleep architecture with CGM-derived glucose metrics, HbA1c and markers of subclinical atherosclerosis in adults with Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) in the CORDIA study.

Study design and methods

One hundred and seventy-nine adults (79 women) with long-standing T1DM wore an Apple Watch for 14 nights; glycaemia was assessed from routine 14-day CGM reports (FreeStyle Libre 2, Dexcom G6/G7 or Guardian 4) and HbA1c. Carotid plaques were assessed by ultrasound and coronary artery calcium (CAC) by computed tomography. Participants also completed the Munich Chronotype Questionnaire (MCTQ). Spearman correlations with false discovery rate (FDR) correction and multivariable linear regression were used.

Results

Shorter REM sleep correlated with higher HbA1c (ρ = -0.24; padj = 0.011) and, with borderline significance after FDR correction, with higher GRI, TAR2, mean sensor glucose and glucose SD and lower TIR (|ρ| 0.17-0.21; padj = 0.052). REM sleep expressed as a proportion of total sleep correlated with GRI, TIR, mean glucose and glucose SD (|ρ| 0.18-0.20; padj = 0.044). In adjusted models, REM duration was associated with all glycaemic metrics; the association with glucose SD persisted after additional adjustment for HbA1c and after exclusion of nights with less than 4 h of recorded sleep. After adjustment for age and sex, participants with two or more carotid plaques had 9.4 min shorter REM sleep (p = 0.034); associations with CAC and deep sleep were attenuated. Older age was associated with lower social jetlag (ρ = -0.20; p = 0.010).

Conclusions

In adults with T1DM, shorter REM sleep was modestly associated with worse glycaemia, most consistently with glucose variability and HbA1c, and with carotid plaque burden. These cross-sectional findings generate hypotheses for longitudinal studies combining sleep tracking with CGM.

title: Inclisiran attenuates myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury by inhibiting macrophage M1 polarization.
authorString: Shi DY, Li ZZ, Bai JQ, Dong XP, Zhang W, Wang HY, Huang XR, Dong ZC, Guo L, Lin QY, Zhang B.

journal.title: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death

abstractText: Macrophage polarization is pivotal in myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury. Inclisiran is a small interfering RNA agent that lowers low-density lipoprotein cholesterol by targeting proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9). However, whether Inclisiran exerts LDL-C-independent cardioprotective effects within the acute I/R window remains unclear. In this study, wild-type C57BL/6J mice were pretreated with Inclisiran before I/R surgery. Myocardial injury was assessed by echocardiography, laser speckle contrast imaging, and TTC/Evans Blue staining. Macrophage polarization and its direct impact on cardiomyocytes or fibroblasts were investigated in co-culture system in vitro. Target gene screening was performed by chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP)-sequencing, and transcriptional regulation was validated by dual-luciferase assay and ChIP-qPCR. Protein interaction was confirmed by molecular docking, surface plasmon resonance, and co-immunoprecipitation. Our results demonstrated that Inclisiran significantly attenuated myocardial injury and dysfunction, inhibited macrophage M1 polarization, reduced cardiomyocyte apoptosis, and suppressed fibroblast activation. Mechanistically, Inclisiran disrupted the direct interaction between PCSK9 and JNK, thereby blocking the HIF-1α-mediated transcriptional regulation of Myo1d, and ultimately suppressing macrophage M1 polarization. In conclusion, Inclisiran alleviates myocardial I/R injury by targeting the JNK-HIF-1α-Myo1d signaling axis. These findings identify a previously unrecognized cardioprotective mechanism that is LDL-C-independent within the acute I/R window, suggesting Inclisiran as a promising therapeutic strategy for ischemic cardiomyopathy.

title: The interplay of fibrinogen and lipoprotein(a) with 20-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk: a path analysis within the ATTICA study (2002-2022).
authorString: Giannakopoulou SP, Chrysohoou C, Antonopoulou S, Barkas F, Liberopoulos E, Sfikakis PP, Pitsavos C, Tsioufis C, Panagiotakos D.
abstractText:
Aims

Elevated levels of lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] and fibrinogen are known risk factors for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), and their combined elevation in high-risk individuals may amplify risk. However, the long-term impact of this combination on ASCVD incidence in a primary prevention setting remains unclear. This study sought to examine the association between the combination of Lp(a) and fibrinogen with long-term ASCVD risk, in apparently healthy adults from the general population.

Methods and results

A cohort of 3042 CVD-free adults residing in greater Athens, Greece, was recruited in 2002. A 20-year follow-up was conducted in 2022, comprising n = 2169 participants, of which n = 1988 had complete data for cardiovascular disease incidence. Participants were divided into four groups, using a recommended threshold of 30 mg/dL for Lp(a) and the median value of 303 mg/dL for fibrinogen. In the overall cohort, fibrinogen was associated with higher ASCVD risk [hazard ratio (HR) per 10 mg/dL: 1.040, 95%CI:1.009-1.072]. Upon stratification by Lp(a) levels, the significant association was retained and amplified only in individuals with elevated Lp(a) levels (HR 1.083, 95%CI:1.009-1.162) (P for interaction=0.041). Participants with both elevated Lp(a) and fibrinogen levels demonstrated the highest 20-year ASCVD risk (HR 1.904, 95%CI [1.023, 3.547]). Path analysis revealed a mediating role of fibrinogen in the inflammation [i.e. interleukin-6 (IL-6)]-ASCVD risk association, which become more pronounced at higher Lp(a) concentrations.

Conclusion

In this general population study, elevated levels of Lp(a) and fibrinogen jointly conferred a higher long-term risk of ASCVD than either marker alone, potentially through the complex involvement of inflammation.

title: Association between carotid intima-media thickness and preeclampsia: Prospective observational comparative study.
authorString: Sarikaya S, Uysal E, Toprak E, Gunenc O.

journal.title: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics

abstractText:
Objective

Preeclampsia is associated with widespread endothelial dysfunction and shares several pathophysiological mechanisms with atherosclerosis. Carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) is a well-established marker of subclinical atherosclerosis and may reflect early maternal vascular remodeling. This study aimed to compare CIMT between pregnant women with and without preeclampsia and to evaluate the association between CIMT and preeclampsia.

Materials and methods

In this prospective observational cohort study, pregnant women with singleton pregnancies who attended the outpatient obstetrics clinic between 24 and 37 weeks of gestation and met the eligibility criteria were prospectively enrolled. Participants diagnosed with preeclampsia formed the study group, and pregnant women who were not diagnosed with preeclampsia during the evaluation phase and during pregnancy formed the control group. CIMT measurements were performed at the time of evaluation for all patients, concurrently with the clinical and laboratory assessment used for diagnosis. Demographic characteristics, routine laboratory parameters, and CIMT measurements were compared between groups. Correlation analyses and receiver operating characteristic curve analysis were performed to evaluate the association between CIMT and preeclampsia.

Results

Women with preeclampsia had significantly greater CIMT than pregnant women without preeclampsia. Maternal age, body mass index, serum uric acid, urea, and creatinine levels were significantly higher, whereas serum albumin levels were significantly lower in the preeclampsia group. CIMT demonstrated significant correlations with several biochemical parameters related to renal function and systemic vascular involvement. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, median CIMT remained independently associated with preeclampsia after adjustment for maternal age, body mass index, and gestational age at CIMT measurement (adjusted odds ratio 2.53 per 0.1 mm increase; 95% confidence interval 1.36-4.71; P = 0.003). Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed that CIMT had a moderate ability to discriminate women with and without preeclampsia (area under the curve 0.75).

Conclusion

Women with preeclampsia exhibited significantly increased CIMT compared with pregnant women without preeclampsia. Median CIMT demonstrated moderate discriminatory performance for distinguishing women with and without established preeclampsia; however, the clinical utility of CIMT for preeclampsia screening remains to be established. Larger prospective studies are required to validate the observed association and determine the clinical utility of CIMT in preeclampsia assessment.

title: The role of T-peak to T-end, T peak-to-end/corrected QT ratios, and index of cardiac electrophysiological balance in the differential diagnosis of myocarditis.
authorString: Tanyeli Z, Ozer U, Çınıçev Ş, Atmış A, Sarı Gökay S.
abstractText:
Aim

Paediatric myocarditis, a rare inflammatory cardiomyopathy (incidence 1-2/100,000 annually), challenges emergency diagnosis due to nonspecific symptoms mimicking common illnesses. This study assessed electrocardiographic markers of ventricular repolarisation heterogeneity-T-peak to T-end interval, T-peak to T-end/QT, T peak-to-end/corrected QT ratios, and index of cardiac electrophysiological balance-for diagnosing myocarditis and predicting ventricular arrhythmia risk in children aged 0-18 years.

Methods

Retrospective case-control study of 76 myocarditis patients (diagnosed by clinical, laboratory, echocardiographic, and cardiac MRI criteria) presenting to our paediatric emergency department from January 1, 2024, to May 30, 2025, versus 75 age-matched healthy controls. Electrocardiographic parameters were measured in leads DII and V5. Receiver operating characteristic analysis evaluated the diagnostic performance of T-peak to T-end and T peak-to-end/corrected QT (Lead II (Derivation II)). Myocarditis cases stratified by arrhythmia development (with: n = 28; without: n = 48); groups compared via t-tests, Mann-Whitney U, and chi-square (p < 0.05 significant).

Results

Myocarditis group: 23 females (30.2%) and 53 males (69.8%); mean age 12.0 ± 4.7 years. Controls: 39 females (52.0%), 36 males (48.0%); mean age 10.3 ± 4.9 years (p = 0.03). Receiver operating characteristic (Lead II (Derivation II)): T-peak to T-end cut-off 62 ms (sensitivity 69.3%, specificity 78.9%, area under the curve 0.725, p < 0.001); T peak-to-end/corrected QT cut-off 0.19 (sensitivity 50.7%, specificity 78.9%, area under the curve 0.625, p < 0.05).The arrhythmia subgroup showed corrected QT prolongation (470 vs. 435 ms, V5; p < 0.001), T-peak to T-end (110 vs. 90 ms, V5; p < 0.001), higher T peak-to-end/corrected QT, and index of cardiac electrophysiological balance (both p < 0.05).

Conclusion

The T-peak to T-end interval, T peak-to-end/corrected QT ratio, and index of cardiac electrophysiological balance provide high-specificity, noninvasive electrocardiographic biomarkers for paediatric myocarditis diagnosis in the ED. Corrected QT and T-peak to T-end prolongation signals repolarisation heterogeneity and arrhythmia risk, supporting routine triage integration for early risk stratification.

title: Shared and divergent features of the immune response to acute and chronic Trypanosoma cruzi infection in mice revealed by cardiac transcriptomics
authorString: Olmo F, Jayawardhana S, Taylor MC, Kelly JM, Francisco AF.
abstractText: Chagas disease is caused by infection with  Trypanosoma cruzi and can result in chronic cardiomyopathy. However, the molecular programmes that define infected cardiac tissue, and how they change as the host-parasite relationship moves from acute pathogenic infection to long-term persistence, remain incompletely understood. Here, we used RNA sequencing to characterise host transcriptional responses in cardiac tissue during both acute and chronic infection in a mouse model. Cardiac parasite distribution was defined using bioluminescence imaging and histology, and RNA sequencing was performed on anatomically standardised cardiac tissue samples collected at both stages. Acute infection was associated with a broad interferon-driven immune activation, whereas during chronic infection this network contracted, with preservation of a tightly connected antigen presentation core centred on major histocompatibility complex genes and immunoproteasome components. Genes associated with extracellular matrix remodelling and fibrosis were not broadly activated. These findings indicate that reduced, but sustained immune activation, rather than widespread fibrotic transcriptional remodelling, represents a prominent feature of cardiac tissue in chronically infected mice. They identify a transition from an overtly inflammatory, pathogen-driven acute response to a more restricted chronic host-parasite equilibrium in which immune surveillance remains transcriptionally active despite very low and spatially intermittent cardiac infection. We identified a conserved 20-gene signature shared between acute and chronic stages. This overlap is consistent with continued or episodic parasite-derived stimulation and/or intrinsic host mechanisms that maintain cardiac immune surveillance. Thus, chronic  T. cruzi infection can be viewed as a persistent host-parasite association in which biological coexistence does not imply benignity: immune containment and parasite persistence can occur alongside cumulative cardiac injury.

title: LplA-mediated rescue of lethal myopathy and cardiomyopathy in mitochondrial lipoylation-deficient mammalian caused by Lipt1
authorString: Yu J, Hu Z, Liu Z, Yang R, Zeng A.
abstractText: Inherited mitochondrial metabolic disorders impair cellular energy generation and often lead to fatal metabolic crises. Mitochondrial lipoylation defects represent a severe case of such disorders that can lead to lethality but lacks effective treatment so far. In this study, we generated a viable mouse model with muscle-specific deficiency of the lipoyltransferase coded by Lipt1 to provide an in vivo preclinical model that overcomes embryonic lethality. Using this model, we examined a bacterial lipoate protein ligase A (LplA)-mediated gene therapy via adeno-associated virus (AAV) delivery. By introducing LplA alongside lipoic acid supplementation, we reconstituted a salvage pathway that bypasses the mammalian endogenous lipoylation pathway. The intervention rescued premature lethality, recovered motor function and reversed hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in the Lipt1-deficient mouse model. Mechanistically, AAV-LplA reconstitutes mitochondrial protein lipoylation and oxidative phosphorylation in situ. This energetic rescue suppresses phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)-Akt hyperactivation, thereby restoring autophagic clearance and subsequently contributing to the recovery of the pathological phenotype. This study established AAV-LplA as a promising gene-delivery strategy for rescuing lethal mitochondrial lipoylation disorders.

title: AI-based structural modelling and pathogenic variant mapping across the human protein interactome
authorString: Ille AM, Ille AL, Lamont HH, Holyoak T.
abstractText: Spanning the complex landscape of the human proteome, physical interactions between proteins coordinate cellular organization, signaling, regulation, and homeostasis. Yet the three-dimensional structures of most of these interactions remain unresolved. Here, we performed AI-based modelling of 109,282 human protein interaction structures, generating a structural resource for large-scale analysis. The predicted structures were systematically characterized through analysis of interface residue involvement, buried surface area, intermolecular bonding, and energetic properties. Additionally, we mapped pathogenic variant data onto the predicted structures, identifying interface-localized mutations for over 4,000 annotated disease categories. Acute myeloid leukemia, Alzheimer's disease, and cardiomyopathy were examined as representative disease contexts for exploring the distribution of interface mutations within disease-associated protein interaction networks. Strengths and limitations of predictive capabilities were also assessed, including through experimental structure comparisons. Collectively, this structural resource and accompanying analyses offer a basis for developing novel hypotheses and informing experimental studies involving human protein interactions in physiological and disease contexts.

title: CardioJEPA: A Framework for Holistic Cardiac Representations Through Predictive Multimodal Alignment with ECG-Preservation
authorString: Uyterlinde D, Alvarez-Florez L, Ruipérez-Campillo S, Arts LPA, Asselbergs FW, Bekkers EJ, Išgum I, Tjong FVY.
abstractText: The electrocardiogram (ECG) is the most widely used cardiac diagnostic tool, but it reflects cardiac structure and function only indirectly. Aligning ECG and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) representations offers a way to transfer imaging-derived structural knowledge into the ECG encoder without compromising the electrophysiological information it already carries. Contrastive learning has become the predominant approach for ECG--CMR alignment, yet the quality of the learned representation is jointly determined by the CMR target representation, the alignment objective, and the preservation of electrophysiological information unique to the ECG. We propose CardioJEPA, a predictive alignment framework built on frozen cardiac foundation models that addresses all three: a target that separates static anatomy from cardiac motion, a predictive objective that maps ECG representations onto a fixed CMR target without instance discrimination, and a preservation term that retains nearly all pre-alignment electrophysiological information. On 63,193 paired ECG--CMR recordings from the UK Biobank, CardioJEPA outperforms previous ECG--CMR alignment methods across structural, electrical, and diagnostic tasks, retains 98.6% of the ECG-unique information present before alignment, substantially reduces the modality gap relative to matched contrastive alignment, and transfers to external cohorts for structural heart disease and Chagas cardiomyopathy without task-specific training, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

title: The Lost Kidney: Ultrasound Diagnosis of Adult Bochdalek Hernia With Renal Herniation and Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.
authorString: Li GY, Liu J, Wang TY, Liu ZH, Hu P.
abstractText: Adult Bochdalek hernia (BH) with left renal herniation is clinically rare and has an insidious onset, rendering it prone to misdiagnosis. We report a case of a 77-year-old male patient who presented with an abdominal pulsatile mass in the absence of respiratory symptoms. Ultrasonography revealed a giant abdominal aortic aneurysm and additionally identified renal echogenicity on the left side of the heart, with a normally positioned spleen. Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated herniation of the left kidney and a portion of the bowel into the thoracic cavity, along with a giant abdominal aortic aneurysm and multiple atherosclerotic ulcers of the iliac arteries. Ultrasonography is valuable for initial screening, while contrast-enhanced CT defines diaphragmatic defect, ectopic-kidney rotational malformation, and elongated renal pedicle, providing critical evidence for definitive diagnosis.

title: Early and six-month ventricular remodeling after aortic valve surgery for aortic regurgitation: Predictive value of preoperative static exercise cardiovascular magnetic resonance. A prospective pilot study.
authorString: Alegret JM, Ligero C, Montiel J, Gómez-Llorente M, Montero M, Pujadas S.
abstractText:
Background

Little is known about the timing and trajectory of reverse remodeling after aortic valve surgery (AVS) in severe aortic regurgitation (AR), and better predictors of postoperative ventricular function are needed. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) with static exercise (SE) testing may help anticipate the ventricular response to AVS, but its predictive value has not been established.

Methods

In this prospective pilot study, 20 patients with severe AR referred for AVS underwent CMR, including assessment during SE, with follow-up CMR at 14 days and 6 months. Repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) characterized the time course of each parameter, decomposing the time effect into linear and quadratic components.

Results

Left ventricular (LV) end-diastolic volume decreased progressively, mainly following a linear pattern (η2 0.795), with most of the reduction by 14 days. LV end-systolic volume declined continuously through 6 months (linear component only, η2 0.711). LV ejection fraction (LVEF) described a V-shaped curve, falling at 14 days before recovering above baseline by 6 months (quadratic component predominant, η2 0.358). Right ventricular parameters remained stable. SE-induced changes mirrored the early postoperative response and correlated strongly with 14-day LVEF (r up to 0.87), with good agreement between SE-LVEF and 14-day LVEF (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] 0.76-0.86); no baseline or SE parameter predicted LVEF at 6 months.

Conclusions

AVS for severe AR induces early, heterogeneous LV reverse remodeling, with an initial LVEF dip followed by recovery by 6 months. Preoperative CMR with SE reproduces the early postoperative hemodynamic response and predicts short-term but not mid-term ventricular recovery.

title: Beyond Risk Scores: Concordance of a Multidisciplinary Decision Support Instrument with Real Life Treatment Decisions for Patients with Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.
authorString: Hijkoop LF, van Veldhuizen WA, Keller BPJA, van Leeuwen BL, Schuurman SN, Dijkstra ML, Kropman RHJ, de Vries JPM.

journal.title: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery

abstractText:
Objectives

Treatment decisions for patients with ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA) are ethically complex and must be made under time pressure. This prospective observational study assessed how a previously developed decision support instrument (DSI) for rAAA aligns with real life treatment decisions and determined a reference threshold for interpreting its output. The DSI estimates the proportion of experts from the original multidisciplinary expert panel who would be expected to favour operative treatment (OT) for a given patient profile.

Methods

Consecutive rAAA patients were included between March 2024 and January 2026 from two Dutch hospitals. Treating vascular surgeons completed the DSI after the actual treatment decision (OT or palliative care). DSI outputs were analysed in relation to observed treatment decisions. A threshold sweep analysis was performed to identify a contextual reference threshold reflecting the level of DSI estimated expert support at which OT was generally pursued. Post-operative outcomes were assessed in OT patients for clinical context.

Results

Fifty patients were included; OT was chosen in 43 patients (86%). DSI estimated expert support was higher for patients receiving OT compared with palliative care (median 98% [interquartile range 97, 99%] vs. 83% [59, 89%]; p < .001). The contextual reference threshold was 93%, with concordance of 94% (95% confidence interval 83.8 - 97.9%). Case analysis highlighted challenges in capturing unresponsiveness due to profound hypovolaemic shock and assessing cardiac burden acutely Among patients surviving OT, relatively high health related quality of life was observed.

Conclusions

The DSI shows concordance with real life treatment decisions for rAAA. A contextual reference threshold above which operative treatment was generally pursued could be empirically derived. Although refinement is needed to better identify certain high risk patients, these findings represent an important first step in the validation pathway and provide proof of concept for behavioural artificial intelligence technology methodology.

title: Accuracy of Virtual Circle Method and Valve-to-Aorta Distance Change After Redo-TAVR: Multicenter Paired CT Analysis.
authorString: Fukui M, Sellers SL, De Backer O, Garcia SA, Goel SS, Meier D, Kobari Y, Khokhar A, Ono S, Mendez Hirata G, Kritya M, Webb JG, Reardon M, Bapat VN.
abstractText:
Background

The virtual circle method is currently used in preprocedural computed tomography planning for Redo-transcatheter aortic valve (TAV) replacement to simulate the predicted outer boundary of the index TAV and the valve-to-aorta distance for coronary risk assessment, yet its accuracy against postprocedural observations has not been evaluated. This study aimed to assess the accuracy of the virtual circle method in predicting index TAV expansion and coronary risk following a second TAV implantation using paired preprocedural and postprocedural computed tomography in patients undergoing Redo-TAV replacement.

Methods

This multicenter retrospective study included 58 patients who underwent Redo-TAV replacement at 5 sites with paired preprocedural and postprocedural cardiac computed tomography. Three valve combinations were analyzed: Evolut-in-SAPIEN (n=17), SAPIEN-in-SAPIEN (n=13), and SAPIEN-in-Evolut (n=28). Index TAV frame expansion was quantified by area- or perimeter-derived diameter change. Accuracy of the virtual circle method was defined as a diameter difference within ±1 mm between predicted and observed index TAV frame diameter.

Results

In the Evolut-in-SAPIEN combination, meaningful index SAPIEN frame expansion occurred only with effective pre/postdilatation, whereas in both the SAPIEN-in-SAPIEN and SAPIEN-in-Evolut combinations, consistent frame expansion was observed regardless of dilatation. Changes in index frame diameter corresponded inversely to changes in valve-to-aorta distance. In the SAPIEN-in-Evolut combination, expansion was governed chiefly by implant position and sizing strategy. Across all combinations in which the virtual circle method was applicable (n=53), accurate prediction was achieved in 31 patients (58.5%), with overestimation in 14 (26.4%) and underestimation in 8 (15.1%).

Conclusions

The virtual circle method provided an accurate or conservative (overestimating) estimate of index TAV expansion and coronary risk in the majority of patients (85%), supporting its clinical utility for Redo-TAVR planning. The remaining 15% showed underestimation of modest magnitude (median, 1.3 mm), occurring predominantly in patients who underwent predilatation and postdilatation, warranting heightened caution in borderline coronary anatomy when dilatation strategies are employed.

title: Diagnostic Value, Sonographic Features, and Factors Associated with Misdiagnosis by Color Doppler Ultrasound for Abdominal Aortic Pseudoaneurysms in Patients With Abdominal Aortic Aneurysmal Dilatation.
authorString: Wei Y, Fu J, Xing Y, Liu D, Niu H, Wang L, Chen J.

journal.title: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine

abstractText:
Objectives

To investigate the clinical, anatomical, and sonographic features of abdominal aortic pseudoaneurysms (AAP), evaluate the real-world diagnostic performance of color Doppler ultrasound for AAP in patients with abdominal aortic aneurysmal dilatation, and analyze factors associated with misdiagnosis.

Methods

This single-center retrospective diagnostic accuracy study followed STARD 2015. We included 520 consecutive patients with abdominal aortic aneurysmal dilatation detected by color Doppler ultrasound between January 2018 and January 2025. Using surgical findings, computed tomography angiography, or magnetic resonance angiography as the reference standard, we analyzed AAP features, evaluated ultrasound diagnostic performance, and reviewed misdiagnosed cases.

Results

A total of 393 patients were included, 25 (6.36%) were confirmed as AAP. Focal wall disruption most frequently occurred in the distal abdominal aorta (64.00%), predominantly on the left and posterior walls. Abdominal or back pain was the most common presenting symptom, with 76.00% of patients having elevated D-dimer levels. The characteristic sonographic findings of AAP were focal aortic wall disruption with a cystic lesion communicating with the aortic lumen. Ultrasound demonstrated 84.00% sensitivity (95% CI: 63.92-95.46), 100.00% specificity (95% CI: 99.00-100.00), and 98.98% overall accuracy (95% CI: 97.41-99.72). In all correctly diagnosed cases, the site of focal wall disruption was 100% concordant with the reference standard. Four cases (16.00%) were misdiagnosed as eccentric true abdominal aortic aneurysms. A retrospective imaging review revealed that these misdiagnoses may be associated with three imaging findings: broad focal wall disruption with absent neck, secondary loss of the typical pseudoaneurysmal to-and-fro flow signature, and coverage of the focal wall disruption by organized thrombus.

Conclusions

Color Doppler ultrasound demonstrates favorable diagnostic performance for AAP in real-world clinical practice and can serve as a reliable first-line non-invasive modality for early screening and diagnosis. Recognition of characteristic features and avoidance of common diagnostic pitfalls can further improve diagnostic accuracy.

title: Autologous pulmonary artery flap repair for aortopulmonary window with interrupted aortic arch and anomalous origin of the right coronary artery from the pulmonary artery.
authorString: Kumae M, Masaki N, Sai S.
abstractText: We describe a surgical technique using a pedicled autologous pulmonary artery wall flap for repair of aortopulmonary window in association with interrupted aortic arch and anomalous origin of the right coronary artery from the pulmonary artery. A 29-day-old infant underwent definitive repair in which the pulmonary artery flap was used to close the defect and to achieve wide rerouting of the right coronary artery to the reconstructed ascending aorta. The pulmonary artery was reconstructed with a fresh autologous pericardial patch, and the aortic arch was repaired by direct anastomosis. Postoperative CT demonstrated patency of the right coronary artery and satisfactory aortic configuration. This anatomical repair using autologous tissue may reduce the risk of coronary distortion and provide a favourable coronary geometry in selected patients. However, further follow-up is required to evaluate coronary growth and the long-term durability of the reconstructed vessels.

title: Fibromuscular Dysplasia in Acute Type A Aortic Dissection: A Common yet Underrecognized Vascular Phenotype in Women
authorString: Weustink AC, Keijzer AR, Budde RPJ, Versmissen J, Galema TW, Veen KM, Takkenberg JJ, Arabkhani B, Coenen A.
abstractText:
Objectives:

Fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) is a non inflammatory, non atherosclerotic arterial disease characterized by multifocal arterial beading that predominantly affects women. Although FMD commonly involves the renal and carotid arteries, its relationship with acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) remains poorly understood. We investigated the proportion of patients with FMD among patients with ATAAD, focusing on sex based differences.

Materials and Methods:

Patients aged below 70 years with ATAAD and ECG triggered aortic CT angiography (CTA) were consecutively included in this retrospective single-center study. FMD was defined as multifocal arterial beading (string-of-beads appearance) in at least one vascular territory, according to international consensus criteria. The highest-quality CTA examination was evaluated by an experienced cardiovascular radiologist. All suspected FMD cases were independently reviewed by a second experienced cardiovascular radiologist, with the final diagnosis established by consensus. Proportions were reported with 95% confidence intervals and compared between sexes .

Results:

Of 214 patients screened, 200 were included (138 men and 62 women). FMD was confirmed in 18/200 patients (9%; 95% CI, 6 till 14%), none of whom had a prior FMD diagnosis. FMD was more frequent in women (12/62, 19%; 95% CI, 11 till 31%) than men (6/138, 4%; 95% CI, 2 till 9%; P<0.001). FMD predominantly involved the renal arteries. Additional carotid CTA was available in 49/200 patients (25%) and in 7/18 patients with FMD (39%); three of these seven patients had carotid FMD.

Conclusion:

FMD was observed in a substantial proportion of patients presenting with ATAAD, particularly women. These findings suggest that FMD is an underrecognized vascular phenotype in patients with ATAAD.

title: External validation of the ARISCAT, Gupta Respiratory Failure, and Gupta Pneumonia risk scores in patients undergoing open abdominal aortic surgery: a single-center retrospective cohort study
authorString: Jasińska KW, Polok K, Chwała M, Sładek K, Szczeklik W, Studzińska D.
abstractText: Background. The ARISCAT, Gupta Respiratory Failure, and Gupta Pneumonia scores predict postoperative pulmonary complications, but their validity in open abdominal aortic surgery — a high-risk population — is unestablished. We aimed to externally validate all three scores in this population. Methods. Single-center retrospective cohort study of 693 adults undergoing open abdominal aortic surgery for infrarenal aortic aneurysm and/or peripheral arterial and aortic disease, at a tertiary center in Krakow, Poland, 2015–2023. Discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve) and calibration (calibration-in-the-large, slope, observed-to-expected ratio, calibration belt) of the three scores were assessed for their respective endpoints — composite pulmonary complication, respiratory failure, and pneumonia. Net clinical benefit was assessed by decision curve analysis, per the TRIPOD + AI 2024 statement. Results. The cohort was predominantly male (85.1%), median age 68 years (interquartile range, 64–73), and high surgical risk (73.0% American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status III). Postoperative pulmonary complication incidence was 19.5% (n = 135), respiratory failure 8.7% (n = 60), and pneumonia 9.1% (n = 63). All three scores showed poor discrimination: ARISCAT area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.563 (95% confidence interval, 0.512–0.615), Gupta Respiratory Failure 0.573 (0.516–0.631), Gupta Pneumonia 0.604 (0.536–0.672). All scores systematically underestimated risk (calibration-in-the-large, + 0.426, + 0.369, and + 0.837; observed-to-expected ratios, 1.38, 1.40, and 2.17; calibration belt P < 0.001, P = 0.010, and P < 0.001). Originally proposed cut-offs classified 75%–83% of patients as high-risk. Decision curve analysis showed net benefit over a treat-all strategy only for ARISCAT, within a narrow band near a 20% threshold; the Gupta scores showed no net benefit at any threshold. Conclusions. The ARISCAT, Gupta Respiratory Failure, and Gupta Pneumonia scores provide insufficient pulmonary risk stratification for patients undergoing open abdominal aortic surgery. Systematic underestimation of risk, combined with limited net clinical benefit at their original cut-offs, underscores the need for an aortic-specific pulmonary risk prediction model. Trial registration. Open Science Framework (OSF), https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/349UR. Registered 9 June 2026.
