journal.title: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
journal.isoabbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg

abstractText: Objective(s)Patients with Turner syndrome (TS) and hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) undergoing single-ventricle palliation represent a challenging cohort. We examined birth admission outcomes in TS/HLHS patients, comparing Norwood and hybrid palliation strategies.MethodsThe pediatric health information system (PHIS) database was queried for neonates with a diagnosis of TS and HLHS. Cohort was divided into Norwood procedure, hybrid, or nonoperative, and outcomes were divided into three time eras (Era 1: 2004-2011, Era 2: 2012-2018, Era 3: 2019-2025).ResultsA total of 157 infants were identified: 27/157 (17%) received no operative intervention, 24/157 (15%) underwent hybrid palliation, and 106/157 (68%) underwent the Norwood procedure only. Overall Stage-1 palliation (S1P) hospital survival was 75% (98/130) for both operative cohorts. Hybrid palliations trended upward over time, while Norwood volumes remained stable. In-hospital survival improved across eras for hybrid palliation (75% vs 87%) and the Norwood procedure (71% vs 89%), although neither reached statistical significance. Of 45 PHIS hospitals performing the Norwood, 38 performed S1P for TS patients; 60% (23/38)used the Norwood exclusively, 8% (3/38) used hybrid exclusively, and 32% (12/38) employed both approaches.ConclusionsOutcomes appear satisfactory with either the hybrid or Norwood strategy, with current survival rates ≥87%, although hybrid palliation was associated with a higher rate of subsequent transplantation. However, 17% of (27/157) TS/HLHS neonates were not offered surgical intervention, presumably because they were deemed to be at higher risk. Given demonstrably improving outcomes among selected TS patients undergoing either procedure, offering S1P more broadly, including to higher-risk TS/HLHS patients, may be worthwhile.

title: In Silico Insights into Device-Artery Interactions in Endovascular Pulmonary Flow Restrictors for Neonates with Congenital Heart Defects.
authorString: Bonfanti S, Cetatoiu MA, Di Vincenzo P, Gasparotti E, Fanni BM, Kizilski SB, Recco DP, Del Nido P, Hoganson D, Celi S, Pennati G, Berti F.
abstractText:
Introduction

Transcatheter pulmonary flow restriction using a modified Medtronic Vascular Plug (MVP™) has recently emerged as a promising alternative to surgical pulmonary arterial banding in neonates with complex congenital heart defects. However, clinical outcomes remain variable, and the underlying biomechanical mechanisms are poorly understood. This study aims to exploit in silico modeling to improve the understanding of device-artery interactions following the deployment of modified MVP™ in neonatal pulmonary arteries. To this end, we (i) developed and validated a high-fidelity digital twin of an MVP™ device, and (ii) used clinical imaging data from a retrospective cohort of seven neonates treated at Boston Children's Hospital to reproduce in silico the in vivo device-artery interaction in both the right and left pulmonary arteries.

Methods

The digital twin was reconstructed from high-resolution optical measurements and mechanically characterized under both local and global compression. Idealized artery geometries were generated based on pre-procedural angiographic measurements. For each patient, wall thickness was varied within a size-adjusted range derived from the literature, while Young's modulus was calibrated to reproduce the post-implantation arterial diameters, thereby quantifying the vessel's stiffness in response to device expansion.

Results

Case-specific simulations revealed marked variability in pulmonary artery effective stiffness across patients and between arterial branches. While identical post-implantation diameters could be reproduced through different thickness-stiffness combinations, these generated substantially different local contact pressure distributions.

Conclusions

This study demonstrates the feasibility of a patient-specific computational framework for simulating the deployment of endovascular pulmonary flow restrictors using a validated MVP™ digital twin.

title: Semi-automated Generation and Hemodynamic Assessment of Surgical Baffle Geometry for Biventricular Repair.
authorString: Martinez ES, Kaiser AD, Reed AK, Stocker SW, Sharir A, Choi PS, Maskatia SA, Ma MR, Marsden AL.
abstractText: Patient-specific computational modeling has emerged as a powerful tool for surgical planning in complex congenital heart disease. One promising application is complex biventricular repair, which often requires construction of a custom intraventricular baffle to establish a physiologic left ventricle-to-aorta outflow pathway. In current practice, baffle geometry is designed and shaped intraoperatively. While existing preoperative modeling tools increasingly support visualization and virtual baffle design, the design process remains predominantly manual, and watertight models for quantitative hemodynamic assessment remain limited. We present a semi-automated computational framework for the design and assessment of patient-specific intraventricular baffles. The method constructs an explicit ventricular septal defect (VSD)-to-aorta flow pathway that preserves native right ventricular myocardial and VSD geometry while reshaping the baffle region to satisfy patient-specific, section-wise area constraints. We retrospectively applied this framework to four patients with double outlet right ventricle (DORV) who had previously undergone biventricular repair. Each generated pathway was evaluated with pulsatile computational fluid dynamics (CFD), producing peak-flow pressure differences of 1.58-5.94 mmHg under the prescribed flow conditions. All modeled pressure differences remained below the 10-mmHg planning benchmark across mesh resolutions and under elevated flow. The current implementation preserves the native VSD and does not model VSD enlargement or conal resection; however, it provides a computational framework through which these interventions could be evaluated in silico. By translating a surgeon-defined baffle boundary into a physiologically constrained, simulation-ready model, this approach enables quantitative preoperative design and CFD-based evaluation of candidate baffle geometries, advancing patient-specific computational planning for biventricular flow restoration in heterogeneous anatomies.

title: Neonatal Teeth in Patau Syndrome: A Rare Oral Phenotype and Bedside Surgical Management.
authorString: Franco JB, Curi FR, Peleteiro PV, Caetano ADS, Delgado RZR, Vieira WR.

journal.title: The Cleft palate-craniofacial journal : official publication of the American Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Association

abstractText: This report describes the first cytogenetically confirmed case of complete trisomy 13 associated with a highly mobile mandibular neonatal tooth and a contralateral eruption cyst associated with an unerupted tooth, managed by bedside surgery in the neonatal intensive care unit. A late-preterm newborn with trisomy 13, unilateral complete cleft lip and palate, and congenital heart disease presented with a highly mobile mandibular neonatal tooth and a contralateral eruption cyst associated with an unerupted tooth. Following multidisciplinary evaluation, both teeth were extracted at the bedside under local anesthesia and cardiorespiratory monitoring, without complications. This case expands the oral phenotypic spectrum of trisomy 13 and underscores the importance of early recognition, individualized management, and Hospital Dentistry in preventing airway-related complications in medically complex newborns.

title: Mid-term outcomes of a catheter-based right ventricular decompression strategy for pulmonary atresia with intact ventricular septum and critical pulmonary stenosis
authorString: Sano K, Toda K, Nabeshima T, Nagaoka K, Kojima T, Hirano A, Hosoda R, Hoashi T.
abstractText: Pulmonary atresia with intact ventricular septum (PAIVS) and critical pulmonary stenosis (cPS) span a spectrum of right ventricular hypoplasia in which the optimal initial pathway remains uncertain. We describe mid-term outcomes of an anatomy-guided percutaneous transcatheter pulmonary valvuloplasty (PTPV)-first strategy. We retrospectively reviewed 24 patients treated invasively from 2007 through 2025; three lacked measurable right ventricular end-diastolic volume (RVEDV) and were excluded, leaving an analytic cohort of 21 patients (PAIVS, n = 9; cPS, n = 12). Fifteen patients with a tripartite right ventricle and no major sinusoidal communication underwent PTPV first; six with an absent outlet component or major sinusoidal communication entered a single-ventricle pathway. All 15 PTPV-first patients achieved biventricular circulation; all three PAIVS patients in this group required subsequent, elective surgical right ventricular decompression, consistent with staged rather than failed decompression. All six single-ventricle patients completed Fontan circulation, and no PTPV-first patient required one-and-a-half ventricular repair or crossed over to Fontan. All 21 patients were alive after a median follow-up of 8 years [interquartile range, 6–11]. One patient with borderline RVEDV and tricuspid valve Z-score developed protein-losing enteropathy 11 years after Fontan completion. PTPV-first patients tended to have higher RVEDV and less negative tricuspid valve Z-scores than single-ventricle patients, reflecting selection criteria rather than validated thresholds. PTPV first permitted staged right ventricular recruitment and biventricular circulation with favorable mid-term outcomes, with surgical decompression as an effective subsequent step. Given the small, retrospective, single-center design, these findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant prospective reassessment of borderline right ventricles.

title: Distinct soft plaque morphology on coronary computed tomography angiography in non-culprit lesions among patients with acute coronary syndrome.
authorString: Hatakeyama H, Kato T, Tanba Y, Fujikura Y, Miura K, Kaimori R, Wakaki T, Watanabe H.
abstractText:
Background

Major adverse cardiovascular events arising from non-culprit lesions (NCLs) remain relevant in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS), highlighting the need for more effective identification of vulnerable plaques. Although several coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-derived high-risk features are recognized as markers of plaque vulnerability, the significance of soft plaque morphology remains unclear. This study investigated whether ACS is associated with soft plaque morphology in NCLs on CCTA.

Methods and results

Overall, 174 NCLs from 69 patients with ACS or chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) who underwent CCTA within 1 month of percutaneous coronary intervention were analyzed. Soft plaques were classified according to the presence or absence of focal soft plaque thickening (FSPT), defined as localized thickening of the soft plaque component measuring ≥500 μm in at least one cross-sectional slice. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) was co-registered with CCTA in 49 lesions. The soft plaque burden did not differ significantly between NCLs in patients with ACS and CCS, whereas FSPT was more frequently observed in NCLs in patients with ACS (56.4% vs. 18.8%; p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis accounting for within-patient clustering, ACS was independently associated with FSPT (odds ratio, 6.09; 95% confidence interval, 2.72-13.60; p < 0.001). On co-registered IVUS, lesions with FSPT showed larger attenuation arcs and more frequent superficial attenuation.

Conclusions

ACS was independently associated with CCTA-derived FSPT in NCLs. These exploratory findings suggest that morphological assessment of soft plaques on CCTA may provide complementary information for the characterization of NCLs. Further validation in independent cohorts is warranted.

title: 3-Year Comparison of Sirolimus- Versus Paclitaxel-Coated Balloon Angioplasty in Femoropopliteal Artery Disease: The SIRONA Trial.
authorString: Teichgräber U, Ingwersen M, Lehmann T, Platzer S, Kunstmann I, Steiner S, Schmidt A, Wittig T, Zeller T, Thieme M, Krankenberg H, Werner M, Brodmann M, Malyar N, Müller-Hülsbeck S, de Paoli L, Schlager O, Austermann M, Tepe G, Erbel C, Ito W, Waßmer R, Maiwald L, Aschenbach R, Wissgott C, Andrassy M, Wolf F, Beschorner U, Pech M, Katsanos K, Scheinert D, SIRONA Trial investigators.
abstractText:
Background

Sirolimus-coated balloons (SCBs) have emerged as alternatives to paclitaxel-coated balloons (PCBs), but randomized comparative data beyond 2 years are lacking.

Objectives

The aim of this study was to compare patient-reported outcomes, effectiveness, and safety through 3 years in symptomatic femoropopliteal artery disease.

Methods

SIRONA was a prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial comparing SCB angioplasty with a PCB strategy. Patients were randomized 1:1 after successful predilation. Prespecified 3-year outcomes included walking capacity, health-related quality of life, clinically driven target lesion/vessel revascularization (cdTLR/cdTVR), mortality, major amputation, and amputation-free survival.

Results

Among 482 randomized patients (SCB, n = 238; PCB, n = 244), 96.3% had intermittent claudication; 3-year follow-up was completed by 76.5% and 79.6%, respectively. Changes in patient-reported walking distances did not differ between-groups. Three-year freedom from cdTLR was 88.2% (95% CI: 83.1%-91.9%) versus 80.2% (95% CI: 74.1%-85.0%; HR: 0.60, 95% CI: 0.36-0.97; nominal log-rank P = 0.03). Post-hoc analysis suggested time-varying treatment effects (treatment-by-period interaction P = 0.006), with separation after the first year. Freedom from cdTVR (HR: 0.78, 95% CI: 0.50-1.21; nominal P = 0.27) and amputation-free survival (HR: 1.09, 95% CI 0.57-2.09; nominal P = 0.79) did not differ.

Conclusions

Through 3 years, no between-group differences were observed in walking capacity and health-related quality of life or clinical safety outcomes between SCB angioplasty and the PCB strategy. Three-year freedom from cdTLR was higher with SCB angioplasty, with treatment effect that varied over time. Given the exploratory, nonmultiplicity-adjusted 3-year analysis, the cdTLR difference requires confirmation.

title: Prognostic value of Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio after percutaneous coronary intervention.
authorString:
Zhang R, Xu J, Guan C, Jiang Y, Shi Y, Tu S, Yu B, Fu G, Zhou Y, Wang J, Chen Y, Pu J, Dou K, Yang W, Wu Y, Qiao S, Stone GW, Song L, 
                    on behalf of the FAVOR III China study group
                .

journal.title: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background

Post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) physiological indices have prognostic relevance. Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (μQFR) enables wire-free, rapid, single-view functional assessment, yet its long-term prognostic value after PCI remains incompletely established.

Aims

We sought to evaluate the prognostic value of post-PCI μQFR for long-term adverse outcomes.

Methods

This prespecified subgroup analysis of the FAVOR III China trial included 3,825 patients. All PCI-treated vessels with a reference diameter ≥2.5 mm and 50-90% diameter stenosis were analysed for offline post-PCI μQFR. The primary endpoint was 5-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; including death from any cause, myocardial infarction, or ischaemia-driven revascularisation).

Results

Post-PCI μQFR was successfully analysed in 4,196 vessels from 3,455 patients, with similar distributions between the randomised treatment groups. At 5 years, a low post-PCI μQFR was associated with a higher incidence of MACE compared with the intermediate and high post-PCI μQFR tertiles (23.1% vs 19.0% vs 17.2%; p=0.001). Using the highest tertile (μQFR>0.95) as a reference, adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) were 1.08 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.87-1.34) for the intermediate tertile (0.92-0.95) and 1.30 (95% CI: 1.06-1.60) for the lowest tertile (μQFR ≤0.91). Using a receiver operating characteristic-derived cutoff, MACE occurred more frequently in patients with post-PCI μQFR <0.94 (22.3% vs 17.4%, aHR 1.23, 95% CI: 1.04-1.47; p=0.02) than in those with post-PCI μQFR ≥0.94. No significant interaction was observed between treatment strategy and post-PCI μQFR (p for interaction=0.23).

Conclusions

Post-PCI μQFR distributions were similar between treatment groups, but lower values were associated with higher 5-year adverse event risk without significant treatment interaction. Its limited binary discrimination supports use as a continuous metric for post-PCI physiological risk stratification. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT03656848).

title: A randomised non-inferiority trial of CCTA guidance versus IVUS guidance for PCI: rationale and design of the P4 clinical trial.
authorString: Tajima A, Arai T, Ohashi H, Bouisset F, Belmonte M, Stalikas N, Ali Z, Amano T, Biscaglia S, Bagnall A, Tanaka K, Engstrøm T, Fairbairn T, Good R, Jones DA, Makkar RR, Jilaihawi H, Szilveszter B, Mæng M, Støttrup NB, Nørgaard BL, O'Kane P, Olsen NT, Perera D, Mushtaq S, Pontone G, Purcell I, Sandoval Y, Wilgenhof A, Sonck J, Spratt JC, Mincione G, Stefanini G, Van Belle E, Zivelonghi C, Munhoz D, Sakai K, Miyazaki Y, Brugaletta S, Ihdayhid A, Leipsic J, Ko B, Bartorelli A, De Bruyne B, Malhotra G, da Costa BR, Mizukami T, Andreini D, Collet C.

journal.title: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText: Intravascular imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves clinical outcomes compared with angiography-guided PCI. Contemporary coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides comprehensive assessment of coronary anatomy, plaque characteristics, vessel dimensions, calcification, and lesion-specific physiology, enabling detailed procedural planning before catheterisation. The Precise Procedural and PCI Plan (P4) trial is a prospective, international, multicentre, randomised, open-label trial with blinded endpoint adjudication designed to determine whether a comprehensive CCTA-guided PCI strategy is non-inferior to intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided PCI with respect to clinical outcomes. Approximately 1,100 patients with chronic coronary syndromes or stabilised acute coronary syndrome, at least one coronary stenosis >70%, and fractional flow reserve derived from CCTA ≤0.80 are enrolled. Following central core laboratory confirmation of anatomical and physiological eligibility, patients are randomised 1:1 to CCTA-guided or IVUS-guided PCI. Patients assigned to CCTA-guided PCI undergo standardised procedural planning and virtual PCI simulation, with CCTA integrated into the catheterisation laboratory using computed tomography-fluoroscopy synchronisation for intraprocedural guidance. In the IVUS-guided arm, PCI is performed with mandatory pre- and post-PCI IVUS assessment. The primary endpoint is target vessel failure at 12 months, defined as the composite of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction, or ischaemia-driven target vessel revascularisation. P4 will determine whether comprehensive, non-invasive CCTA-guided PCI planning is non-inferior to IVUS-guided PCI regarding 12-month target vessel failure while potentially improving procedural efficiency and standardisation. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05253677).

title: Spousal Traumatic Brain Injury and Risk of Mortality, Dementia, and Cardiovascular Events.
authorString: D'Alonzo BA, Law CA, Pike JR, Stulberg EL, Walter AE, Diaz-Arrastia R, Gottesman RF, Ornstein KA, Palta P, Coresh J, Schneider ALC.
abstractText:
Importance

Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is highly prevalent in older adults. While there is strong and growing evidence that TBI is associated with caregiver burden and psychological health, it remains unclear whether a spouse's TBI is associated with the long-term health of the uninjured partner.

Objective

To evaluate whether having a spouse who sustains an incident TBI is associated with risk of mortality, dementia, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and to assess whether associations differ by sex or survival of the injured spouse after TBI.

Design, setting, and participants

This prospective community-based cohort of married couples was performed at 4 US centers in North Carolina, Mississippi, Minnesota, and Maryland as part of the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Study. Of 4506 baseline spousal pairs, 3281 were retained for mortality and dementia analyses and 2740 of these for MACE analyses. Participants contributed person-time from baseline (1987-1989) until incident outcome, death, loss to follow-up, divorce or separation, or administrative censoring on December 31, 2022. Analyses were conducted from November 24, 2025, through August 25, 2026.

Exposure

Incident spousal TBI (ascertained using self-report, hospitalization surveillance, and linked Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services data), modeled as a 2-category time-varying exposure (spousal TBI vs no spousal TBI) and 4-category exposure incorporating spousal death.

Main outcomes and measures

Incident all-cause mortality, dementia, and MACE. Cox proportional hazards regression shared frailty models were used to estimate associations adjusted for demographic, clinical, and behavioral characteristics.

Results

Among 3281 married pairs included in mortality and dementia analyses (among whom, 2740 pairs were included in MACE analyses), the mean (SD) age at baseline was 54.5 (5.5) years, with 3281 female and 3281 male spouses (for a total of 6562 participants). The median follow-up was 19.5 (IQR, 10.6-29.0) years. Spousal TBI was associated with increased risk of mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 1.24 [95% CI, 1.07-1.43]; P = .004) but not dementia (HR, 1.17 [95% CI, 0.88-1.56]; P = .28) or MACE (HR, 1.15 [95% CI, 0.84-1.57]; P = .40). In sex-stratified analyses, associations were similar among males and females. In models incorporating spousal death, mortality risk was higher among individuals whose spouse was alive with a TBI (HR, 1.22 [95% CI, 1.05-1.41]; P = .008), higher among those whose spouse was deceased without a TBI (HR, 1.48 [95% CI, 1.36-1.61]; P < .001), and higher among those whose spouse was deceased with a TBI (HR, 1.27 [95% CI, 1.07-1.52]; P = .006) compared with those whose spouse was alive without a TBI. Results were similar, but less precise, for dementia and MACE.

Conclusions and relevance

In this cohort study of married pairs of participants in the ARIC Study, having a spouse who sustained a TBI was associated with a modest but significantly higher risk of mortality in the uninjured partner, whereas findings for dementia and major adverse cardiovascular events were less consistent. These findings suggest that the consequences of TBI may extend beyond injured individuals and support family- and care partner-centered approaches to care.

title: Cardiovascular Disease in Women the Two Decades Following Uteroplacental Disorders: A Population-Based Data-Linkage Study.
authorString: Burger RJ, Kalkman DN, Gordijn SJ, Abu-Hanna A, Henriques JPS, Ganzevoort W, Ravelli ACJ.

journal.title: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology

abstractText:
Objective

Uniform recommendations on cardiovascular follow-up after complicated pregnancies are lacking, partly due to limited evidence. This study aimed to investigate the incidence and timing of premature cardiovascular disease (CVD) after different uteroplacental disorders, to inform the timing and content of cardiovascular follow-up.

Design

Population-based cohort study, linking data from the Dutch perinatal registry with national hospital admissions data.

Setting

Netherlands, 2000-2022.

Population

1 669 681 nulliparous women, with a singleton pregnancy.

Methods

Cox regression was used to estimate hazard ratios for overall CVD and specific cardiovascular conditions after uteroplacental disorders, adjusted for confounders. Time-dependent Cox regression and interaction analyses for education attainment, income, and migration background were performed.

Results

Risks of premature hypertension, atherosclerosis, ischaemic heart disease, cardiac arrest, cardiomyopathy, heart failure, and cerebrovascular disease were significantly increased among women with a history of a uteroplacental disorder, adjusted for confounders (overall CVD: aHR 1.70, 95% CI 1.67-1.74; median follow-up time 11 years, IQR 6-17 years). Hazard ratios were similar after pregnancy induced hypertension (PIH), preeclampsia (PE), fetal growth restriction (FGR), or fetal death, while risks after spontaneous preterm birth (sPTB) were less elevated. Most relative CVD risks were highest shortly after pregnancy but remained elevated more than 10 years postpartum. After hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), hypertension risk was most pronounced, whereas after FGR the increased risk of atherosclerosis was most notable. Socioeconomic factors had limited impact on these associations.

Conclusions

All uteroplacental disorders-not only PE-serve as women-specific markers of CVD risk, shortly after pregnancy and later in life, highlighting the need for early cardiovascular screening. Pathological processes contributing to the increased CVD risk might differ across uteroplacental disorders.

title: Resuscitation and 30-day postoperative mortality in acute type A aortic dissection: A cohort study.
authorString: Kageyama S, Ohashi T, Kuinose M, Yamatsuji T, Kojima T.
abstractText:
Objectives

Patients with acute type A aortic dissection who experience cardiopulmonary arrest require cardiopulmonary resuscitation before definitive repair, but the prognostic relevance of its duration is unclear. We evaluated the association between resuscitation duration and early mortality after emergency surgery.

Methods

In this retrospective two-centre study, we included all adults who underwent emergency surgery for acute type A aortic dissection. The exposure was the combined preoperative and intraoperative duration of resuscitation until return of spontaneous circulation or initiation of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation or cardiopulmonary bypass, categorised a priori as none, <15 min or ≥ 15 min. Multilevel proportional hazards models and competing-risks regression, with multiple imputation of missing covariates, were used.

Results

Of 880 patients, 815 (92.6%), 13 (1.5%), and 52 (5.9%) received no resuscitation, resuscitation for <15 min and resuscitation for ≥15 min, respectively (median recorded duration 29 min, interquartile range 15-43). Thirty-day mortality was 81/815 (9.9%), 3/13 (23.1%) and 42/52 (80.8%), respectively. Resuscitation for ≥15 min was associated with higher 30-day mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 9.59, 95% confidence interval 4.28-21.45; P < 0.001), whereas the estimate for resuscitation for <15 min was imprecise (adjusted hazard ratio 1.68, 95% confidence interval 0.46-6.13; P = 0.43).

Conclusions

Among patients selected for emergency surgery for acute type A aortic dissection, combined preoperative and intraoperative resuscitation for ≥15 min was associated with higher 30-day mortality, and the risk increased with resuscitation duration. These findings provide prognostic information rather than a criterion for withholding surgery.

title: Guided P2Y12 inhibitor selection after rapid CYP2C19 genotyping in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention.
authorString: Thomas CD, Malave JG, Laudani C, Ortega-Paz L, Rollini F, Cavallari LH, Angiolillo DJ, Franchi F.

journal.title: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background

Dual antiplatelet therapy remains the standard treatment following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). While prasugrel and ticagrelor offer consistent antiplatelet effects, they increase bleeding risk compared with clopidogrel, which requires CYP2C19 bioactivation.

Aims

This study aimed to evaluate the impact of rapid CYP2C19 genotyping at the time of PCI on P2Y12 inhibitor selection and clinical outcomes in real-world patients.

Methods

A total of 974 patients who underwent PCI and rapid CYP2C19 genotyping and received P2Y12 inhibitor treatment were included. P2Y12 inhibitor selection, P2Y12 inhibitor switching, major atherothrombotic events (MAE; a composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, stent thrombosis, or unstable angina requiring revascularisation), and bleeding events were assessed throughout the first year post-PCI. Time-varying Cox regression analysis was performed to assess event risk in patients treated with clopidogrel (reference) versus prasugrel/ticagrelor after stratifying by loss-of-function (LOF) status and adjusting for stratum-specific confounders.

Results

Clopidogrel was prescribed more frequently at discharge among CYP2C19 non-LOF versus LOF carriers (43% [296/691] vs 31% [87/283]; p<0.001). The median duration of follow-up was 359 days (interquartile range [IQR] 190-362 days). Among LOF allele carriers de-escalating to clopidogrel, the median de-escalation time was 180 days (IQR 92-354 days). MAE were not significantly different between P2Y12 inhibitor regimens after stratifying by LOF status (LOF-prasugrel/ticagrelor [n=147] vs LOF-clopidogrel [n=136]: adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0.87 [95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.36-2.10]; non-LOF-prasugrel/ticagrelor [n=272] vs non-LOF-clopidogrel [n=419]: adjusted HR 1.26, 95% CI: 0.67-2.36). No significant differences in Bleeding Academic Research Consortium bleeding events were observed.

Conclusions

This real-world study shows that, among LOF carriers managed with rapid CYP2C19 genotyping and delayed de-escalation, ischaemic and bleeding event rates were not significantly different between those taking clopidogrel versus those taking prasugrel/ticagrelor, though findings should be interpreted cautiously.

title: Prediction of coronary events by computed tomography-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio.
authorString: Gim DH, Lee SH, Ding D, Wang Z, Shin D, Kim SM, Lee SY, Choi KH, Park TK, Yang JH, Song YB, Hahn JY, Choi SH, Choe YH, Gwon HC, Tu S, Lee JM.

journal.title: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background

Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (CT-μFR) provides a non-invasive measure of vessel-level ischaemia but may not capture local haemodynamic abnormalities reflected by the longitudinal pressure gradient across the lesion (CT-μFR gradient).

Aims

We aimed to evaluate the association of CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient with 3-year vessel-level subsequent coronary events and to determine the incremental prognostic value of their combined assessment.

Methods

Our study included a total of 885 vessels from 312 patients who underwent invasive coronary angiography for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or stable angina and had prior CCTA performed 6 months to 3 years earlier. CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient were assessed by an independent core laboratory blinded to the clinical data. The primary outcome was 3-year subsequent coronary events (a composite of vessel-specific myocardial infarction or urgent revascularisation for ACS). The discrimination ability of predictive models was assessed using Harrell's C-index.

Results

Vessels with CT-μFR ≤0.80 or a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm had a higher risk of events than those with CT-μFR>0.80 (79.1% vs 20.4%, adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 6.87, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.26-8.96; p<0.001) or a CT-μFR gradient <0.004/mm (72.6% vs 27.4%, adjusted HR 4.08, 95% CI: 3.15-5.28; p<0.001), respectively. Among vessels with CT-μFR>0.80, a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm remained associated with increased risk (adjusted HR 2.59, 95% CI: 1.63-4.11; p<0.001). Adding the CT-μFR gradient to CT-μFR improved discrimination in the overall cohort (C-index 0.700 to 0.755; p<0.001) as well as the subgroup with CT-μFR>0.80 (C-index 0.575 to 0.655; p<0.001).

Conclusions

Both CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient are independently associated with 3-year subsequent coronary events. Their combined assessment improves risk stratification beyond CT-μFR alone. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04794868).

title: Multimodality Imaging Across the Lifespan in Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot: Current Evidence and Future Directions.
authorString: Friedberg MK, Jolley MA, Mercer-Rosa L, Nyrnes SA, Olivieri L, Van De Bruaene A, Villemain O, Wald RM.
abstractText: Repaired tetralogy of Fallot (rTOF) is a common condition encountered across pediatric and adult congenital heart disease clinics. Although childhood survival is excellent, patients remain at risk for late complications, including exercise intolerance, arrhythmias, heart failure, and sudden death. Residual lesions, most notably pulmonary regurgitation and right ventricular outflow tract obstruction, drive progressive right and secondary left ventricular remodeling, often necessitating repeat interventions such as pulmonary valve replacement. Multimodality imaging is central to management, enabling risk stratification and informing the optimal timing of reintervention. This State-of-the-Art Review summarizes the current state of the art in multimodality imaging for rTOF across the lifespan, highlighting established and emerging techniques. The authors discuss the roles of 2- and 3-dimensional echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance, strain and exercise imaging, ultrafast ultrasound, and advanced cardiac magnetic resonance methods in characterizing ventricular function, remodeling, mechanics, flow dynamics, fibrosis, stiffness, and electromechanical interactions. The authors explore developments in image-based machine learning and computational modeling that support patient-specific intervention planning and personalized care.

title: Assessing the toxicological effects of di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate on vascular diseases: Insights from network toxicology, Mendelian randomization, single-cell RNA sequencing, and experimental validation.
authorString: Li X, Xu H, Zhang S, Chen S, Liu Z, Liu Z, Guo R.
abstractText: Phthalates have caused serious environmental and health problems worldwide due to their widespread use and potential toxicity. However, their effects on vascular diseases, particularly abdominal aortic aneurysms, carotid plaque, and vascular remodeling, remain unclear. This study systematically explored the molecular mechanisms by which di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) induced vascular toxicity. Multiple databases and PPI networks were used to identify and screen potential molecular targets. Mendelian randomization analysis based on expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) data was employed to investigate possible causal links between potential targets and diseases. Finally, our study identified a common core network consisting of 23 genes shared across three diseases. At the hub of this network were TLR4, PARP1, and MMP9 - genes consistently identified as hub nodes across multiple network analyses. Together, this core gene cluster constituted a molecular "stress intersection" that integrated inflammatory, metabolic, and cellular fate-related signaling. GO and KEGG analyses revealed that DEHP exposure was associated with the Toll-like receptor signaling pathway, lipid and atherosclerosis signaling pathway, and apoptosis pathway. Molecular docking validated the stable interaction of DEHP with key targets. Virtual knockout and gene perturbation analyses based on single-cell RNA sequencing prioritized TLR4 and PARP1 as candidate regulators for experimental validation. In vitro experiments showed that DEHP (25, 50, and 100 μM for 24 h) concentration-dependently inhibited vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) proliferation, induced mitochondrial oxidative stress and membrane potential depolarization, and increased TLR4 and PARP1 expression, which may be linked to the activation of TLR4 inflammatory signaling pathway and increased ROS production.

title: A Scoping Review of Deep Learning Methods for Photoplethysmography Data.
authorString: Nie G, Zhu J, Tang G, Zhang D, Geng S, Zhao Q, Hong S.
abstractText: Background: Photoplethysmography (PPG) is a noninvasive optical sensing technique widely used to capture hemodynamic information, with broad deployment in both clinical monitoring systems and wearable devices. In recent years, the integration of deep learning has substantially advanced PPG signal analysis and expanded its applications across healthcare and nonhealthcare domains. Methods: We conducted a comprehensive literature search for studies applying deep learning to PPG data published between 2017 January 1 and 2025 December 31, using Google Scholar, PubMed, and Dimensions. The included studies were analyzed from 3 key perspectives: tasks, models, and data. Results: A total of 460 papers applying deep learning techniques to PPG signal analysis were included. These studies span a wide range of application domains, from traditional physiological monitoring tasks such as cardiovascular assessment to emerging applications including sleep analysis, cross-modality signal reconstruction, and biometric identification. Conclusions: Deep learning has substantially advanced PPG signal analysis by enabling more effective extraction of physiological information. Compared with traditional machine learning approaches reliant on handcrafted features, deep learning methods generally achieve improved performance and offer greater flexibility in model development. Nevertheless, several challenges remain, including limited availability of large-scale high-quality datasets, insufficient validation in real-world environments, and concerns over model interpretability, scalability, and computational efficiency. Addressing these challenges and exploring emerging research directions will be essential for further progress in deep learning-based PPG analysis.

title: Hydroxychloroquine-Associated Renal Phospholipidosis: A Forgotten Complication of a Common Drug.
authorString: Tsao YC, Wu CH.
abstractText: Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) treatment in systemic lupus erythematosus can induce drug-induced phospholipidosis mimicking Fabry disease. A 32-year-old woman with lupus nephritis developed podocyte "zebra bodies" on electron microscopy. Normal lyso-Gb3 excluded Fabry disease, confirming HCQ toxicity. Discontinuation and immunosuppression yielded stable renal function and improved proteinuria.

title: circCRIM1 inhibits endothelial cell ferroptosis in atherosclerosis via regulating miR-567/PRDX3 pathway.
authorString: Yue Y, Xu G, Li B, Peng J.
abstractText:
Endothelial dysfunction is an initiating event of atherosclerosis (AS). Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have been implicated in endothelial injury. This study aimed to investigate the function and mechanism of circCRIM1 (hsa_circ_0007386) in AS-related endothelial injury. GSE152280 and GSE115733 datasets were acquired to identify differentially expressed circRNAs in AS. circCRIM1 expression was validated in serum from 30 AS patients and 30 healthy controls. An in vitro AS model was established by exposing human coronary artery endothelial cells (HCAECs) to 50 µg/mL oxidized low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL) for 24 h. The subcellular localization of circCRIM1 were measured by Fluorescence in situ hybridization. Cell injury was evaluated by detecting cell viability, proliferation, LDH release, inflammation, and ferroptosis after circCRIM1 overexpression or knockdown. The underlying mechanism was explored through bioinformatics analysis, dual-luciferase reporter assay, RT-qPCR, Western blot, and rescue experiments. circCRIM1 expression was decreased, whereas miR-567 was increased, in AS and ox-LDL-treated HCAECs. circCRIM1 was mainly localized to the cytoplasm. circCRIM1 overexpression conferred protective effects against ox-LDL-induced injury in HCAECs, as manifested by enhanced cell viability and EdU-positive cell number, attenuated LDH release, reduced secretion of inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α and IL-6), and mitigation of ferroptosis characterized by decreased Fe2+, MDA, and lipid ROS levels, increased SOD activity, downregulated ACSL4, and upregulated GPX4. Conversely, circCRIM1 knockdown aggravated ox-LDL-induced cellular damage. miR-567 mimic exacerbated, whereas miR-567 inhibitor alleviated ox-LDL-induced injury of HCAECs. PRDX3 was identified as a direct target of miR-567, and circCRIM1 served as a miR-567 sponge to regulate PRDX3. Both miR-567 mimic and PRDX3 siRNA partially abrogated the protective effects of circCRIM1 upregulation. circCRIM1 relieves ox-LDL-induced endothelial inflammation and ferroptosis by regulating the miR-567/PRDX3 axis in AS.

Supplementary information

The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s10616-026-01096-3.

title: Pharmacological activation of mitophagy prevents calcific aortic valve disease by targeting dysregulated mitochondrial-to-nuclear communication
authorString: Zhou D, Dai H, Qiu J, Pan Y, Hu W, Lu H, Xue J, Hu H, Xu D, Dai J, Lu J, Yang S, Qian N, Li Y, Cheng S, Mai Z, Fan J, Zhu Q, Guo Y, He Y, Chen J, Xia H, Wang J, Liu X.
abstractText:
Background and Aims

Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) lacks pharmacologic therapy. Mitophagy impairment contributes to various degenerative diseases, but whether it occurs in calcified aortic valves and during human valvular interstitial cell (hVIC) osteogenic differentiation remains unknown. We therefore investigated the role of mitophagy in CAVD and whether its pharmacological treatment prevents disease progression.

Methods

Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed on human aortic valves and hVICs. TJ0113, a novel orally available mitophagy activator from our previous screening, was tested in two CAVD mouse models. Multi-omics analyses and functional rescue experiments were performed to elucidate the mechanism.

Results

Mitophagy was impaired in calcified human aortic valves and during hVIC osteogenic differentiation. TJ0113 activated MCL1-mediated mitophagy and attenuated disease progression in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, the mitophagy receptor MCL1 anchors a fraction of PRMT3 on mitochondria. During osteogenic differentiation, a dysregulated mitochondrial-to-nuclear communication is initiated by the increased release of PRMT3 into the cytosol, where it interacts with BACH1 and impairs BACH1 nuclear translocation. This leads to a widespread loss of BACH1 genomic occupancy, relieving BACH1-mediated transcriptional repression of the pro-osteogenic factor PARM1 and promoting hVIC osteogenic differentiation. Mitophagy activation by TJ0113 restored MCL1-PRMT3 binding and reversed these alterations.

Conclusions

Mitophagy impairment drives CAVD through dysregulated mitochondrial-to-nuclear communication mediated by the MCL1-PRMT3-BACH1-PARM1 axis. Pharmacological mitophagy activation by TJ0113 corrects this communication and attenuates disease progression, representing a promising therapeutic strategy for CAVD.

title: SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complexes in metabolic disorders: integrating tissue-specific epigenetic mechanisms.
authorString: Rahman FU, Wei Z.
abstractText: Metabolic disorders are increasingly linked to epigenetic alterations. SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complexes have emerged as critical modulators of metabolic homeostasis. In this review, we focus on the tissue-specific biological function of SWI/SNF complexes in the pancreas, liver, adipose tissue, and heart, and highlight the dysregulation of chromatin remodeling in metabolic disease progression. Lastly, we discuss therapeutic opportunities targeting chromatin remodeling mechanisms in metabolic disorders.

title: Salivary microbiome, socioeconomic status, and cognitive performance: Triangulating the relationship.
authorString: Naumova OY, Dobrynin PV, Litwin G, Rychkov SY, Milham MP, Grigorenko EL.
abstractText: Research increasingly demonstrates that endogenous bacterial communities (microbiomes) are associated with both cognitive functioning and socioeconomic status (SES). In this study, we used a metagenomics approach to characterize oral microbiome diversity in Hispanic and African American children aged 6-16 years. We examined how microbiome composition and SES were related to cognitive performance, as assessed by the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children (WISC). Our findings indicate that SES and the microbiome contributed complementary, comparably sized influences on cognitive functioning. Together, variability in conventional SES indicators and microbiome composition accounted for approximately 10% of the variability in WISC scores. These results highlight the importance of integrating both social and biological determinants of health when studying cognitive performance and other psychological outcomes.

title: Orthoplastic Limb Salvage Using Transtibial Transport and Free-Flap Reconstruction in Patients With Diabetes-Related Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
authorString: Boey J, Wen J, Zhou Z, Zhou Z.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: J Am Acad Orthop Surg Glob Res Rev
journal.title: Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons. Global research & reviews
journal.isoabbreviation: J Am Acad Orthop Surg Glob Res Rev

abstractText: Early revascularization-through endovascular or open surgery-is the cornerstone of treatment for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). However, some patients are deemed "no-option" because of diffuse infrapopliteal disease, poor distal runoff, or failed previous interventions, leaving limited limb-salvage strategies. We report an orthoplastic limb-salvage case in a 56-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes, severe peripheral arterial disease, and a chronic foot ulcer complicated by toe gangrene after unsuccessful revascularization. After urgent radical débridement, ray amputation, culture-directed antibiotics, and negative-pressure wound therapy, transtibial transport (TTT) was done to improve microcirculation. After infection control and wound stabilization, definitive reconstruction was achieved using a large anterolateral thigh perforator free flap with a flow-through microsurgical technique to provide durable coverage while preserving distal perfusion. At 12-month follow-up, the flap remained viable with complete epithelialization, no ulcer recurrence, preserved foot architecture, and independent ambulation with protective footwear, indicating meaningful functional recovery. This case highlights the potential role of combining TTT with microsurgical reconstruction in orthoplastic management of "no-option" CLTI. Enhancing microcirculation alongside robust soft-tissue coverage may expand limb-salvage possibilities when traditional revascularization is not feasible.

title: Biomedical properties and emerging translational potential of bovine milk extracellular vesicles.
authorString: Guan X, Hou X, Meng W, Guo HD.
abstractText: Extracellular vesicles have garnered significant attention in the biomedical field due to their potential as therapeutic agents and diagnostic tools. Bovine milk extracellular vesicles (BMEVs), in particular, have emerged as a promising tool in biomedical research due to their unique biocompatibility, stability, and ease of isolation. As an alternative to extracellular vesicles sourced from human cells, such as stem cells or blood, these naturally occurring nanovesicles are increasingly recognized for their dual role as potential therapeutic carriers and diagnostic candidates. To map the evolution and knowledge structure of the field, we conducted a CiteSpace analysis that reveals how BMEVs research has expanded beyond nutritional science to emerge as a versatile biomedical platform with rapidly broadening applications. Also, this review systematically examines the biogenesis, isolation techniques, and structural features of BMEVs, while highlighting their applications in drug delivery, disease therapy, and diagnostics. Current preclinical studies provide preclinical evidence supporting potential therapeutic applications. However, clinical safety, therapeutic efficacy, reproducibility, dosing, biodistribution, immunogenicity, large-scale manufacturing, and regulatory acceptance remain to be established. Future research should focus on optimizing drug-loading strategies, enhancing targeted delivery, and exploring novel biomedical applications.

title: Akutt perikarditt ved primær binyrebarksvikt.
authorString: Svendsen M, Comi KM, Rutherford OW.

journal.title: Tidsskrift for den Norske laegeforening : tidsskrift for praktisk medicin, ny raekke

abstractText:
Background

Pericarditis is a common cause of chest pain.

Case presentation

A young man presented with acute chest pain, nausea and vomiting. He reported progressive lethargy, an episode of syncope and orthostatic hypotension. During a recent consultation with a dermatologist, hyperpigmentation had been noted. He had COVID-19 during the pandemic and had been vaccinated. Tests revealed hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia and fever. After admission, the chest pain worsened, and the ECG showed global ST elevations. Cardiac troponins were normal, and coronary angiography showed no signs of occlusion. Pericarditis was assumed, and colchicine treatment was initiated. Based on his medical history and clinical findings, primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease) was suspected. He was treated successfully, with rapid recovery.

Interpretation

To our knowledge, autoimmune primary adrenal insufficiency is a rare cause of pericarditis that may have a potentially fatal outcome. Early investigation and treatment are crucial.

title: Advances in therapeutic oligonucleotide conjugates.
authorString: Zheng YY, Xue Y, Hou X, Dong Y.
abstractText: Oligonucleotide therapeutics (ONTs) have revolutionized the medical landscape by enabling the precise modulation of genetic pathways. This perspective highlights the major conjugation strategies for ONTs, using antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) and small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) as representative modalities. We describe diverse classes of targeting ligands, including small molecules, cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs), antibodies, and aptamers. For example, triantennary N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc) conjugation has enabled a number of approved oligonucleotide therapeutics. Meanwhile, other emerging conjugation technologies have expanded oligonucleotide delivery to extrahepatic tissues to address a broader range of diseases. We further summarize the clinical translation of these delivery platforms, highlighting approved therapeutics alongside emerging clinical candidates. Finally, we provide an outlook on challenges and opportunities for the next generation of oligonucleotide therapeutics.

title: Covered-Stent Migration During Same-Session Aortic Isthmus Repair and Bicuspid Aortic Valve TAVR.
authorString: Papadopoulos GE, Ninios I, Ninios V.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText: Fixed obstruction at the aortic isthmus may preclude transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Covered-stent implantation can restore large-bore access, but immediate passage of balloons and delivery systems through a newly implanted stent may expose it to longitudinal traction. Secondary stent migration during withdrawal of a valvuloplasty balloon and its intraluminal balloon-assisted rescue have not been well characterized. An 87-year-old man with New York Heart Association class III symptoms had severe bicuspid aortic stenosis (peak velocity, 4.4 m/s; mean gradient, 48 mmHg; valve area, 0.65 cm2; left ventricular ejection fraction, 55%) and a focal juxtaductal aortic-isthmus stenosis with a peak-to-peak gradient of 32 mmHg. Because of high surgical risk and unfavorable alternative access, same-session covered-stent treatment followed by transfemoral TAVR was selected. A 12 × 29-mm Advanta V12 covered stent was deployed and flared using an 18-mm noncompliant balloon. After aortic-valve predilation with a 23-mm noncompliant balloon, the stent migrated distally during balloon withdrawal. Guidewire access was preserved, and the stent remained coaxial. The balloon was recentered within the migrated stent and partially reinflated, allowing the balloon and stent to be advanced proximally as a single unit. After restoration and re-expansion of the stent, a 23-mm Myval valve was implanted successfully. Final transvalvular and isthmic gradients were 8 and 5 mmHg, respectively, with trivial paravalvular regurgitation and no aortic injury. The patient was discharged on day 3 and remained in NYHA class I at 6 months. Withdrawal of a large valvuloplasty balloon may cause secondary migration of a newly implanted aortic-isthmus stent. When guidewire access, coaxial alignment, and structural integrity are preserved, controlled intraluminal balloon-assisted repositioning may provide an effective bailout while maintaining transfemoral access.

title: Global thickness for accurate and precise evaluation of post-intervention remodelling in left ventricular hypertrophy
authorString: Khor LJ, Shiwani H, Thornton GD, Bennett J, Aziminia N, Shetye A, Topriceanu C, Captur G, Davies RH, Moon JC, Swoboda P, Chin CW, Treibel TA, Kozor R, Ugander M, PRECISION-HCM Collaborative.
abstractText:
Structured abstract

Background

Cardiovascular interventions may impact both left ventricular mass (LVM) and end-diastolic volume (EDV), but the net effect on wall thickness has been difficult to accurately evaluate. Global average left ventricular end-diastolic wall thickness (GT) relates non-linearly to LVM and EDV. We hypothesized that if GT is independent of EDV in health, then GT will be an ideal measure of post-intervention change in left ventricular hypertrophy.

Methods

GT [mm] was calculated using LVM and EDV by cardiovascular magnetic resonance as previously validated. The correlation between GT and EDV was evaluated in healthy volunteers. Change in GT following intervention was evaluated for aortic stenosis undergoing valve replacement, hypertension commencing antihypertensive medications, athletes undergoing forced detraining, and aortic regurgitation undergoing valve replacement. The performance of GT was compared to LVM/EDV.

Results

Among healthy volunteers (n=4461, mean±SD age 59±10 years, 50% female), EDV correlated with LVM/EDV but negligibly with GT (R 2 >0.16 vs R 2 <0.02, p<0.001 for both sexes). GT and not LVM/EDV changed after intervention in all conditions (p≤0.02 for all). Post-intervention changes in GT varied by condition (mean±SEM aortic stenosis [n=102]: -1.75±0.13mm, hypertension [n=78]: -0.66±0.08mm, athletes [n=28]: -0.29±0.09mm, aortic regurgitation [n=58]: +0.50±0.11 mm, p≤0.02 for all comparisons).

Conclusions

In health, GT, unlike LVM/EDV, remains effectively unchanged across EDV values, indicating that GT is a physiological constant in health and can track pathological changes. After intervention, only GT and not LVM/EDV consistently changed. Instead of LVM/EDV, GT should be used to quantify remodelling after interventions in left ventricular hypertrophy.

title: Perforated Gangrenous Appendicitis Despite a Normal Leukocyte Count and Nondiagnostic Ultrasonography in a 5-Year-Old Child A Case Report.
authorString: Karki I, Jha SK, Poudel S, Thapa S, Giri L, Ajay KC.
abstractText: A 5-year-old girl with prior patent ductus arteriosus device closure presented with abdominal pain, vomiting, and fever. Despite a normal leukocyte count and nonvisualization of the appendix on ultrasonography, computed tomography identified perforation. Emergency appendectomy confirmed gangrenous appendicitis. This case underscores the importance of serial examination and timely diagnostic imaging.
