title: Burden of newly diagnosed hypertension and potential 10-year cardiovascular risk in Burundi: A Bayesian logistic regression and Framingham score-based study
authorString: IRADUKUNDA A, Ineza C, Kwizera A, Taha R, O'Connell P, Akineza AD, Odjidja EN, NIZIGIYIMANA E, BARANSAKA E.
abstractText: Introduction: Arterial hypertension is a major global public health concern. In Burundi, it coexists with other non-communicable and communicable diseases, contributing to a complex and evolving health burden that poses substantial challenges for prevention, diagnosis, and management. We aimed to assess the burden of newly diagnosed hypertension, identify associated risk factors, and assess 10-year cardiovascular risk among hypertensive and non-hypertensive patients. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study of 714 patients admitted to Kamenge Teaching Hospital between January 2018 and January 2023. Retrospective data were extracted from medical records. Bayesian belief updating was used to estimate the prevalence of newly diagnosed hypertension, while Bayesian logistic regression with bootstrapping was used to identify associated risk factors. Bayesian linear models were used to assess the association between diastolic blood pressure and cardiovascular risk level. Potential 10-year cardiovascular risk was estimated using the Canadian Framingham Risk Score. Results The prevalence of newly diagnosed hypertension was 16.9% (95% CrI: 14.2–19.7%). Higher prevalence was observed among women (18.0%), patients aged 40–59 years (21.3%) and ≥ 60 years (33.9%), those with higher educational attainment (up to 28.9%), and individuals who were overweight or obese or had a family history of hypertension. Predictors of hypertension included age ≥ 40 years, tobacco use, education level, and excess weight. Moderate or severe 10-year cardiovascular risk was present in 24.9% of patients, with more than 60% of patients with hypertension classified as high risk. Diastolic blood pressure was positively associated with cardiovascular risk among both hypertensive and non-hypertensive patients. Conclusion Newly diagnosed hypertension and its association with elevated cardiovascular risk highlight potential missed opportunities for early diagnosis and prevention. Targeted screening and management of modifiable risk factors may help reduce cardiovascular risk in Burundi.

title: Net Clinical Benefit of Continuing vs Discontinuing Anticoagulation After Atrial Fibrillation Ablation: Results from a 280,000-Patient Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Koolaji S, Gorog DA, Leader JH, Markides V.
abstractText: Background Oral anticoagulation (OAC) in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) reduces ischaemic stroke (IS), but increases bleeding, including intracranial haemorrhage (ICH). As catheter ablation reduces AF burden and IS risk, we evaluated the net clinical benefit (NCB) of continuing versus discontinuing OAC after AF ablation. Methods We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and cohort studies comparing OAC continuation versus discontinuation after AF ablation. NCB was calculated as the reduction in IS with continued OAC minus 1.5 × the increase in ICH. Results Thirty-eight studies were included (3 RCTs, 35 cohort studies), enrolling 280,415 patients, with 2.7 years' follow-up. In RCTs, there was no difference between patients on-OAC vs. off-OAC for IS, major bleeding, ICH, or NCB. In cohort studies, IS was similar, but major bleeding (OR, 3.02; 95%CI, 2.06-4.42, p<0.001) and ICH (OR, 3.65; 95%CI, 2.31-5.77, p<0.001) increased, with net clinical harm (NCB -0.46; 95% CI, -0.82 to -0.10, p=0.012). Combining all studies, IS was similar, but major bleeding (OR, 2.93; 95% CI, 2.08-4.14, p<0.001) and ICH (OR, 3.63; 95% CI, 2.34-5.63, p<0.001) were increased with continued OAC, with NCB favouring discontinuation (NCB -0.46; 95% CI, -0.77 to -0.14, p=0.004). Conclusion The benefit of OAC thromboprophylaxis is attenuated after AF ablation but contributes to bleeding, supporting consideration of OAC discontinuation post-ablation. However, this cannot be extrapolated to the highest ischaemic risk patients and, as risks are dynamic and sinus rhythm maintenance is not guaranteed, close surveillance would be essential if considering this approach.

title: Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Death: a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Cardioprotective Efficacy of Semaglutide.
authorString: Marino G, Aquilani S, Di Fusco SA, Concistrè A, Nardi F, Gabrielli D, Imperoli G, Colivicchi F.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiovascular death (CVD) remains a leading cause of global mortality. Although semaglutide reduces major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), the consistency and exact magnitude of its standalone effect on CVD across various patient phenotypes require comprehensive evaluation. This meta-analysis systematically evaluated the clinical efficacy of semaglutide on CVD risk across randomized controlled trials (RCTs).

Methods

PubMed, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched up to July 2026 to identify RCTs comparing semaglutide with placebo in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), overweight or obesity, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) or chronic kidney disease, reporting CVD as a primary, secondary or exploratory outcome. Pooled hazard ratio (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using a random-effects restricted maximum likelihood (REML) model. Publication bias and study robustness were assessed via Egger's test, Begg's test, and trim-and-fill analysis.

Results

Seven high-quality RCTs comprising 38412 patients were included. Semaglutide significantly reduced the risk of CVD by 17% compared with placebo (pooled HR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.72-0.95; P = 0.01). Inter-study heterogeneity was low-to-moderate (I 2= 27.44%, P = 0.18). Subgroup analyses confirmed uniform benefits across different clinical phenotypes (T2DM; overweight or obesity without diabetes; and obesity-related HFpEF, with or without T2DM; P = 0.63) and administration routes (oral versus subcutaneous; P = 0.74). Meta-regression identified trial duration as a key moderator (R 2 = 85.27%, P = 0.089), whereas sex, age, BMI, HbA1c and concomitant SGLT2i therapy did not modify the treatment effect. Publication bias tests were non-significant, and trim-and-fill simulations confirmed the stability of the primary pooled estimate.

Conclusion

Semaglutide delivers a robust and consistent 17% reduction in CVD across diverse cardiometabolic populations, including patients with T2DM, overweight or obesity without diabetes, and obesity-related HFpEF. These findings strongly support its role as a foundational cardioprotective intervention, independent of baseline glycemic status or the administration route.

title: Controversy: Anticoagulants need to be maintained after catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation in patients at risk of stroke-Pro and Contra.
authorString: Boriani G, Boveda S, Mei DA, Fauchier L, Imberti JF, Providencia R, Lip GYH.

journal.title: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText: The pillars of atrial fibrillation (AF) management include stroke prevention, patient-centred symptom directed decisions on rhythm or rate control, and the proactive management of comorbidities and lifestyle changes. These pillars are not in isolation; they are complementary to each other. While oral anticoagulants (OACs) are highly effective for reducing stroke and all-cause mortality in patients with AF, these drugs confer a risk of major bleeding, including intracranial bleeding. Evidence from clinical trials and observational data shows that early rhythm control, especially with catheter ablation, results in a reduction in stroke risk and/or the reduction in AF burden. The question arises therefore, whether in patients with intermediate or low stroke risk after successful catheter ablation, whether or not to continue or discontinue OAC. Recent randomized trials and observational data have created some debate about whether OAC can be routinely stopped after a successful catheter ablation procedure, without a higher risk of thromboembolism. In this pro/contra article, we will debate the arguments for and against the cessation of anti-coagulation after catheter ablation, in the context of recent evidence from clinical trials, observational data, and meta-analysis.

title: PCSK9-Targeting Therapies and Mortality: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
authorString: Navarese EP, Ruscio E, Zheng H, Andreotti F, Aboyans V, Kubica J, Grzelakowska K, Henry TD, Brouwer M, Stone GW, Kereiakes DJ.
abstractText:
Aims

To evaluate the association of PCSK9-targeting therapies with mortality and cardiovascular events in stable or clinically stabilized randomized trial populations.

Methods

We systematically reviewed randomized trials comparing alirocumab, evolocumab or inclisiran with placebo or active control. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261395609). Treatment effects were pooled as incidence rate ratios (IRRs) using random-effects models. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Prespecified subgroup analyses were based on trial-level known atherosclerosis status, as defined by enrollment criteria.

Results

Thirty-two trials enrolled 77,178 participants. Individual atherosclerosis status could not be determined beyond trial-level eligibility criteria. Mortality estimates were predominantly informed by large cardiovascular outcome trials. All-cause mortality was lower with PCSK9-targeting therapy (IRR 0.88, 95% CI 0.82-0.95). Estimates favored PCSK9-targeting treatment in both trials requiring known atherosclerosis for enrollment (IRR 0.90, 95% CI 0.83-0.98) and trials without such an enrollment requirement (IRR 0.78, 95% CI 0.62-0.97; interaction p = 0.21). PCSK9-targeting treatment additionally reduced myocardial infarction, stroke, and coronary revascularization rates. Leave-one-out estimates remained directionally consistent.

Conclusion

PCSK9-targeting therapies were associated with lower all-cause mortality and fewer ischemic events across trial populations. The predominant contribution of large cardiovascular outcome trials enrolling populations with known atherosclerosis and using PCSK9 antibodies limits the ability to infer a survival benefit in populations not selected on the basis of atherosclerosis status and across individual therapies, particularly inclisiran.

title: The efficacy of additional atrial driver ablation in persistent and long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
authorString: Bramantyo BB, Firdaus DH, Aditya J, Vianne A, Mulia RH, Baravia PA, Rizal A.

journal.title: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Objective

Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) remains the primary ablation strategy for atrial fibrillation (AF), yet its success in persistent (PeAF) and long-standing persistent AF (LS-PeAF) is suboptimal. Adjunctive ablation targeting atrial drivers has been proposed to enhance outcomes. This systematic review and meta-analysis compared PVI alone with PVI plus atrial driver ablation in PeAF and LS-PeAF.

Methods

Comprehensive searches of PubMed, Scopus, Europe PMC, and Cochrane Library identified randomized controlled trials (RCTs) enrolling adults with PeAF or LS-PeAF undergoing first-time ablation. Eligible studies compared PVI alone versus PVI plus driver ablation and trials utilizing other adjunctive ablations were excluded. Outcomes included recurrence of AF and any atrial tachyarrhythmia (ATA) beyond the blanking period, procedural parameters, and complications. Pooled analyses employed random-effects models to measure risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

Results

Seven RCTs met inclusion criteria. Adjunctive driver ablation modestly improved freedom from AF (RR 1.16; 95% CI, [1.03, 1.31]; p = 0.01; I²=61%). However, this finding was accompanied by substantial heterogeneity and was not robust to leave-one-out sensitivity analysis. Driver ablation failed to elevate freedom from any ATA (RR 1.09; 95% CI, [0.98, 1.20]; p = 0.11; I²=47%). Procedure duration (MD 37.81 min; 95% CI, [4.42, 71.20]; p = 0.03; I²=96%), fluoroscopy time (MD 4.25 min; 95% CI, [2.83, 5.67]; p < 0.00001; I²=0%), and ablation time (MD 10.01 min; 95% CI, [0.25, 19.77]; p = 0.04; I²=95%) were significantly longer with adjunctive driver ablation. Procedural complication rates were comparable among both groups (RR 1.65; 95% CI, [0.80, 3.43]; p = 0.18; I²=20%).

Conclusion

Additional atrial driver ablation modestly improves freedom from AF but does not reduce ATA recurrence, prolonging procedure time without increasing complications.

title: Neoadjuvant concurrent or sequential anthracycline-containing chemotherapy and HER2-targeted agents for HER2-positive breast cancer: a randomized phase 2 study (METIS).
authorString: Zheng Q, Wang S, Wu Z, Zhong M, Xu F, Ma S, Zhang Y, Zhang L, Shi Y, Wang Y, Huang H, Ma X, Xu X, Li H, Li J, Bi X, Huang J, Jiang K, An X, Hong R, Chen M, Xue C, Zhong Y, Yuan Z, Xia W.
abstractText: The integration of anthracyclines with HER2-targeted agents in neoadjuvant therapy for HER2-positive breast cancer has been limited by cardiotoxicity concerns. This randomized phase II METIS trial (NCT04172259) assessed whether concurrent pegylated liposomal doxorubicin (PLD)-containing chemotherapy plus dual HER2 blockade (trastuzumab/pertuzumab) could improve efficacy without increasing cardiac risk. A total of 156 patients with stage II-III HER2-positive breast cancer were randomized to a PLD-based concurrent regimen or an epirubicin and cyclophosphamide (EC)-based sequential regimen. The PLD-based concurrent group achieved a higher pathological complete response (pCR) rate (67.5% vs. 48.7%; difference, 18.8%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 3.6-34.0; P = 0.033) compared with the EC-based sequential group, with greater benefit in hormone receptor-positive disease (58.7% vs. 36.7%) and stage II tumors (82.1% vs. 48.0%). After a median follow-up of 37.5 months, fewer event-free survival (EFS) events occurred in the PLD-based concurrent group (3 vs. 8), yielding a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.35 (95% CI, 0.09-1.32; P = 0.105). The estimated 3-year EFS rates were 96.0% (95% CI, 88.1-98.7) versus 90.7% (95% CI, 81.5-95.6). Achieving pCR was significantly associated with improved EFS (HR = 0.15; 95% CI, 0.03-0.71; P = 0.006). Cardiac safety was comparable, with no symptomatic cardiac dysfunction and only one grade ≥3 cardiotoxicity in the EC-based sequential group. These findings support PLD-based concurrent therapy with trastuzumab and pertuzumab as an effective and safe neoadjuvant option for high-risk HER2-positive breast cancer, warranting further evaluation in phase III trials.

title: Impact of CKD and Hemodialysis on Treatment of Severely Calcified Lesions: The ECLIPSE Trial.
authorString: George P, Vemuri KS, Shlofmitz RA, Dohad S, Dahle T, Pineda AM, Shunk KA, Kraemer C, Généreux P, Kirtane AJ, Stone GW.
abstractText: Background: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) and coronary calcification increase risk for adverse events following drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation. We evaluated whether outcomes following vessel preparation with orbital atherectomy (OA) versus balloon angioplasty (BA) vary according to CKD. Methods: This pre-specified CKD sub-analysis of the prospective, multicenter ECLIPSE trial evaluated 2,001 patients with severely calcified lesions randomized to OA versus BA prior to DES. Independent predictors of two-year target-vessel failure (TVF)-a composite of cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction (TV-MI), or ischemia-driven target-vessel revascularization (ID-TVR)-were determined using multivariable Cox proportional hazards modeling. Results: CKD (eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73m² or hemodialysis) was present in 694 (34.7%) patients; 112 required hemodialysis. Two-year TVF was significantly higher with versus without CKD (21.2% vs. 11.6%; p<0.001), driven by increased cardiac death and ID-TVR. Hemodialysis independently predicted TVF (adjusted HR 2.14, 95% CI 1.30-3.53; p=0.003), whereas reduced eGFR alone did not (p=0.070). In patients on hemodialysis, OA versus BA was associated with higher rates of TVF (52.3% vs. 30.7%; adjusted HR 2.50, 95% CI 1.16-5.41; P=0.020), driven by higher rates of TV-MI and ID-TVR, whereas TVF was similar after OA versus BA in patients not on hemodialysis (13.5% vs. 13.1%; adjusted HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.81-1.35; P=0.730); however, the interaction between treatment assignment and hemodialysis status was not significant (Pint=0.244). Conclusions: CKD remains a major predictor of adverse outcomes after DES implantation in severely calcified lesions, with the highest risks in patients on hemodialysis. In the ECLIPSE trial, higher two-year rates of TVF were observed after vessel preparation with OA compared with BA in patients on hemodialysis but not in patients with CKD not on hemodialysis or in those without CKD. Given the modest hemodialysis subgroup size and non-significant interaction testing, confirmation of these findings in additional studies is warranted.

title: The lipoprotein-immune checkpoint axis: Linking cardiovascular toxicity and antitumor immunity during immune checkpoint therapy.
authorString: Liang S, Wang X, Zhang J, Tao C, Gan W.
abstractText: Immune checkpoint inhibitors(ICIs) improve cancer outcomes but may also perturb vascular immune homeostasis and increase atherosclerotic cardiovascular risk. Clinical cohorts and imaging studies associate ICI exposure with atherosclerotic events, plaque progression, and arterial inflammatory changes, although causality and the relevant vascular phenotype remain incompletely defined. This Review examines a lipoprotein-immune checkpoint interface linking plaque inflammation with antitumor immunity. We focus on low-density lipoprotein(LDL) and oxidized LDL(oxLDL), lipoprotein(a)[Lp(a)] and oxidized phospholipids (OxPLs), statin-related regulation of ubiquitin-like 3(UBL3)-dependent programmed death-ligand 1(PD-L1) sorting into small extracellular vesicles(sEVs), and proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9(PCSK9). Lp(a) and OxPLs are established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease(ASCVD) mediators but unvalidated ICI-specific biomarkers. Statins have proven cardiovascular benefit and emerging mechanistic links to PD-L1 trafficking, whereas oncologic associations remain observational. PCSK9 inhibition combines established lipid lowering with preclinical enhancement of antigen presentation and checkpoint response, but randomized ICI-specific evidence is lacking. Current evidence therefore supports a testable translational framework rather than a validated causal axis. Guideline-directed cardiovascular prevention remains the clinical standard while biomarker and therapeutic hypotheses require prospective validation.

title: Residual physiological profiles in patients with CABG- or PCI-Favored coronary anatomy: A post hoc analysis of the PANDA III randomized clinical trial.
authorString: Hu K, Xu H, Li B, Wang H, Yuan S, Wu S, Guan C, Song C, Gao G, Yang M, An T, Zhao Z, Wang H, Zhao Y, Liu W, Jia L, Liu Q, Wang C, Wu C, Song W, Wang H, Song L, Feng L, Zhu C, Yin D, Zhang R, Dou K.
abstractText: Patients with anatomically complex coronary artery disease may be considered more suitable for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) than percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), but some undergo PCI because of clinical constraints and experience higher long-term cardiovascular risk. The physiological rationale underlying this excess post-PCI risk remains unclear. From the perspective of post-PCI revascularization completeness and physiological results, we sought to explain the drivers of excess long-term adverse risk among patients with Favor CABG anatomy undergoing PCI. Coronary physiology based on quantitative flow ratio (QFR) was retrospectively evaluated in the randomized PANDA III trial in which all patients underwent PCI. Patients were stratified into 2 predefined groups by baseline SYNTAX score: Favor PCI or Favor CABG. Functional revascularization completeness was assessed using classic residual functional SYNTAX score (c-rFSS). Final physiological results were quantified by post-PCI QFR. Causal mediation analyses used 2-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) excluding periprocedural MI as the outcome to estimate the proportion of the group-outcome association statistically accounted for by residual coronary physiological profiles. The primary endpoint was 2-year MACE, defined as the composite of all-cause death, all MI, or any ischemia-driven revascularization. A total of 1555 patients with complete post-PCI physiological assessment constituted the final study cohort, among whom 269 (17.3%) individuals were stratified to Favor CABG group by baseline SYNTAX score. The 2-year MACE rate was significantly higher in the Favor CABG than the Favor PCI group (18.6% vs 9.2%; adjusted HR: 1.78; 95% CI: 1.27-2.50). Functional incomplete revascularization (c-rFSS >0) was substantially more prevalent among patients in the Favor CABG group (53.2% vs. 15.1%, P < 0.001). Suboptimal post-PCI physiology defined by QFR <0.90 was more frequent in Favor CABG cohort (32.0% vs 11.8%, P < 0.001). In analyses using MACE excluding periprocedural MI, the estimated proportions mediated by functional incomplete revascularization and suboptimal post-PCI physiology were 49.4% and 47.8%, respectively, and their estimated joint proportion mediated was 79.8%. Integrating c-rFSS or post-PCI QFR into clinical-anatomic risk models significantly improved discrimination and reclassification capacity for 2-year MACE (all P < 0.05). In this post hoc analysis of an all-comers PCI trial, approximately one-fifth of patients presented with anatomic complexity warranting CABG as the preferred revascularization strategy. Favor CABG anatomy was associated with higher 2-year MACE than Favor PCI anatomy. This association may be partly explained by the higher prevalence of residual functional incomplete revascularization and suboptimal post-PCI physiology. These findings between Favor CABG and Favor PCI anatomy do not represent a head-to-head comparison and should not be interpreted as a direct comparison of revascularization modalities. URL: https://www. gov; Unique Identifier: NCT02017275.

title: Long-Term Survival Following Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation: A Two-Center Five-Year Analysis.
authorString: Alexy T, Beery J, Gottula AL, Daniel R, Svitekova K, Sumzin N, Kalra R, Bruen C, Elliott A, Gurevich S, Yannopoulos NJ, Bartos JA, Belohlavek J, Yannopoulos D.
abstractText: Randomized trials have shown short-term benefit of extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) for refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), but the long-term durability of survival and neurological recovery after hospital discharge remains poorly defined. We performed a retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients discharged alive after ECPR for refractory VT/VF OHCA from two academic centers (University of Minnesota, USA, and Charles University, Prague) from January 2013 through December 2022. The primary outcome was 5-year survival. Secondary outcomes included neurological status by Cerebral Performance Category (CPC) and associations of age and discharge disposition with long-term outcomes. Among 728 patients treated with ECPR, 211 (29.0%) survived to discharge; 138 from Minnesota and 73 from Prague. Median follow-up was 3.9 years; 68 patients (32%) completed 5 years. No patients were lost to follow-up. Among hospital survivors, 76.9% and 67.2% were alive at 1 and 5 years, respectively, with most deaths occurring within 90 days of discharge. CPC 1-2 was present in 78.7% at discharge and remained high among survivors beyond 1 year (93.4%-94.2%). Five-year survival declined by age from 91.6% for those between 18-39 years to 52.9% for >70 years. Discharge disposition also strongly stratified long-term prognosis. Among patients discharged alive after ECPR for refractory OHCA, long-term survival was substantial, with approximately two-thirds alive at 5 years with favorable CPC in most. Younger age and discharge home or to acute rehabilitation identified subgroups with particularly favorable prognosis. These findings support the long-term durability of benefit among selected patients treated within established ECPR systems of care.

title: Kidney Endpoints in ANCA-Associated Vasculitis - Position Report from the European Vasculitis Society Focus Group Meetings.
authorString: Brix SR, Uzzo M, Kronbichler A, Sanchez-Alamo B, Chalkia A, Odler B, Karras A, Mohammad AJ, Neumann I, Flossmann O, Parodis I, Szpirt WM, Bruchfeld A, Vaglio A, Westman K, Jayne D, Bajema I.
abstractText: Anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitides (AAV) often affect the kidneys, driving morbidity and mortality in AAV. Clinical trials have investigated kidney outcomes using a variety of definitions. The standardization of kidney disease response criteria in AAV remains an unmet need, with an urgency to define kidney endpoints for daily clinical practice and new drug development to optimize patient management. A European Vasculitis Society (EUVAS) Focus Group was formed to review the literature and discuss the wide range of definitions used. The group involved nephrologists, pathologists and rheumatologists who met four times over a time frame of two years with the objective of formulating a consensus proposal for standardized kidney endpoint definitions for AAV. The group investigated the terminology and outcome relations of active kidney disease, treatment response and refractory kidney disease, remission and relapse, kidney function recovery and kidney failure requiring kidney replacement therapy. The group reviewed and discussed measurable parameters used for the assessments, such as kidney biopsy, hematuria and proteinuria, serum creatinine and estimated glomerular filtration rate and novel biomarkers. Here, we report on the current variability in terminology, present an expert proposal for kidney endpoints with a research agenda and outline the future strategy for a Delphi consensus.

title: TAVR in Patients with Moderate Aortic Stenosis with At-Risk Features.
authorString: Généreux P, Makkar RR, Pibarot P, Bax JJ, Lindman BR, Muhammad K, Oldemeyer JB, Pirwitz M, Barker CM, Thourani VH, Yadav PK, Rodriguez R, Strote J, Sakhuja R, Khalil R, Sharma R, Chhatriwalla A, Mishell JM, Kar B, Gafoor S, Walsh J, Spoon D, Frutkin A, Pop A, Van Mieghem NM, Satpathy R, Ando K, Montarello J, Webb J, Vemulapalli S, Cohen DJ, Gupta A, Park B, Prince H, Blanke P, Mack M, Leon MB, PROGRESS Trial Investigators.

journal.title: The New England journal of medicine

abstractText:
Background

For patients with moderate aortic stenosis, current guidelines recommend clinical surveillance with echocardiographic assessment every 1 or 2 years. Whether transcatheter aortic-valve replacement (TAVR) will improve outcomes in these patients remains unknown.

Methods

We conducted an international, open-label, randomized trial to evaluate whether TAVR will result in better outcomes than clinical surveillance among patients with moderate aortic stenosis with at least one at-risk feature (i.e., a symptom or structural or functional abnormality that has been shown to be associated with faster disease progression or adverse cardiovascular outcomes). The patients were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo transfemoral TAVR with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance. The primary effectiveness end point was a composite of death from any cause or a heart-failure event with or without hospitalization at 2 years. Superiority testing was performed in the intention-to-treat population.

Results

A total of 744 patients underwent randomization: 373 patients were assigned to the TAVR group and 371 to the clinical-surveillance group. The mean age of patients was 78 years, 39.1% were women, and 45.6% were at low surgical risk. The mean aortic-valve area was 1.2 cm2, and the mean aortic-valve peak velocity was 3.3 m per second. At 2 years, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients with a primary effectiveness end-point event was 16.7% in the TAVR group and 23.9% in the clinical-surveillance group (risk difference, -7.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -13.1 to -1.3; P = 0.02 for superiority). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients who died from any cause was 8.4% in the TAVR group and 7.3% in the clinical-surveillance group; the estimates for a heart-failure event were 10.8% and 19.0%, respectively. The incidence of procedure-related adverse events did not differ meaningfully between the patients in the TAVR group and those in the clinical-surveillance group who underwent aortic-valve replacement.

Conclusions

Among patients with moderate aortic stenosis and at-risk features, a strategy of TAVR was superior to clinical surveillance in lowering the incidence of death or a heart-failure event at 2 years. (Funded by Edwards Lifesciences; PROGRESS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04889872.).

title: Antithrombotic Therapy After Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: The SIMPLAAFY Randomized Clinical Trial.
authorString: Reddy VY, Saliba WI, Waggoner T, Nair DG, Weiner S, Evonich R, Hoskins M, Dublin A, Rinaldi M, Gandhi G, Dukes JW, Reddy M, DeLurgio D, Iyer VR, Venkataraman G, Sadhu A, Yaganti V, Trulock K, Gibson DN, Alkhouli M, Shah M, Doshi SK, Natale A, Coylewright M, Gibson CM, Kolkailah AA, Jaber WA, Leger K, Matznick E, Christen T, Sutton BS, Stein KM, Kar S.
abstractText:
Importance

Following a left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) procedure, antithrombotic therapy is administered to safely allow time for device endothelialization. However, the optimal postimplant antithrombotic regimen is unknown.

Objective

To determine if either reduced-dose non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants (NOACs) or aspirin alone are noninferior to dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) for the composite clinical end point of death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding through 6 months post LAAC.

Design, setting, and participants

This open-label, 3-group, multicenter clinical trial randomized 1857 patients between October 2024 and December 2025 at 87 US investigational sites, with the final 6-month follow-up in July 2026. Enrolled patients had nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, underwent successful LAAC, and were eligible for all 3 regimens.

Interventions

Patients were randomly allocated 1:1:1 to DAPT for 6 months followed by aspirin (n = 624), a reduced-dose NOAC for 3 months followed by aspirin (n = 620), or aspirin alone for 12 months (n = 613).

Main outcomes and measures

The primary outcome was the 6-month composite of all-cause death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding. Noninferiority was tested in the primary analysis population with a 1-sided Farrington-Manning test (α = .025). Bleeding and 45-day device-related thrombus rates were exploratory without multiplicity adjustment.

Results

The cohort had a mean age of 76 (SD, 8) years, 42.9% were female, the mean CHA2DS2-VASc score was 4.2 (SD, 1.3), and 68.0% had paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. The primary outcome occurred in 41 patients (6.9%) with DAPT vs 31 (5.1%) with a reduced-dose NOAC (risk ratio, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.48-1.18]; risk difference, -1.7 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, 1.2) and 20 (3.3%) with aspirin alone (risk ratio, 0.49 [95% CI, 0.29-0.82]; risk difference, -3.5 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, -0.8). Both monotherapy strategies met noninferiority criteria (P < .001 for noninferiority for both). Major bleeding was 4.5% with DAPT, 2.7% with reduced-dose NOACs, and 1.7% with aspirin alone; clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was 8.7%, 4.8%, and 3.8%, respectively. Device-related thrombus was observed in 3.4%, 0.9%, and 2.7%, respectively.

Conclusions and relevance

Both reduced-dose NOACs and aspirin alone were noninferior to DAPT for 6-month outcomes after uncomplicated LAAC.

Trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06521463.

title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Versus Empagliflozin or Dapagliflozin in the MASLD-Heart Failure Phenotype: An Exploratory Propensity-Matched Cohort Study.
authorString: Gautam N, Huynh TM, Truong HH, Duong N.
abstractText:
Background

Treatment selection may confound observational comparisons of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) in adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and heart failure (HF).

Aims

To compare recorded outcomes between treatment groups and examine whether the associations persisted after restricting the analysis by agent and diabetes status and separating early and later outcome windows.

Study design

Retrospective, initiation-based, active-comparator cohort study (new-user design not verified).

Methods

We used the TriNetX US Collaborative Network and a common index eligibility period from January 1, 2018, through June 2, 2026. The revised analyses were performed on September 12, 2026. An additional sensitivity analysis of acute HF excluded patients with this outcome before the start of the day 1-1825 window. The primary analysis compared semaglutide, liraglutide, or dulaglutide with empagliflozin or dapagliflozin using 1:1 propensity score matching and assessed outcomes during days 1-1825. Separate analyses of the broader GLP-1 RA group examined outcomes during days 1-90 and 91-1825 and among patients with type 2 diabetes and no recorded type 1 diabetes. We report endpoint-specific event proportions, risk differences, hazard ratios (HRs), 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and proportionality test results.

Results

The primary analysis included 8,550 patients per group after matching. Mortality occurred in 599/8,514 (7.0%) versus 861/8,509 (10.1%); the HR was 0.607 (95% CI, 0.546-0.673). Coded acute HF diagnoses occurred in 1,217/8,550 (14.2%) versus 2,525/8,550 (29.5%); the HR was 0.398 (95% CI, 0.372-0.427), with evidence of non-proportional hazards. In separately matched descriptive interval analyses (8,489 patients per group), the HR for coded acute HF was 0.262 (95% CI, 0.236-0.291) during days 1-90 and 0.507 (95% CI, 0.469-0.548) during days 91-1825. The HR for acute kidney injury during the later interval was 0.740 (95% CI, 0.650-0.842). Among 5,709 matched pairs with type 2 diabetes and no recorded type 1 diabetes, the HR for coded acute HF was 0.431 (95% CI, 0.397-0.468), whereas the HR for ketoacidosis was 0.683 (95% CI, 0.455-1.025). No advantage was observed for acute pancreatitis in any analysis. In a separate analysis excluding patients with prior acute HF, the HR was 0.421 (95% CI, 0.362-0.489), with evidence of non-proportional hazards. Albumin and bilirubin remained imbalanced in a direction favoring the GLP-1 RA group; body mass index also remained imbalanced.

Conclusion

GLP-1 RA exposure was associated with lower observed hazards for several outcomes, and the association with coded acute HF was weaker after day 90. The early concentration and magnitude of this association make treatment channeling a plausible explanation, although this analysis cannot establish that explanation. These exploratory findings do not support causal inferences or treatment-preference conclusions and do not challenge randomized evidence supporting SGLT2i use in HF.

title: Dapagliflozin attenuates progression from prefrailty to frailty in patients with hypertension and chronic kidney disease.
authorString: Mone P, Viggiano D, Pansini A, Soldovieri MV, Sabatelli G, Visco V, Macina G, Boccalone E, Ciccarelli M, Martinelli G, Di Mauro M, Vecchione C, Morgante M, Varzideh F, Guerra G, Santulli G.
abstractText: BACKGROUNDChronic kidney disease (CKD) and hypertension share common pathophysiological pathways contributing to vascular damage, endothelial dysfunction, and physical decline, particularly in older adults with prefrailty. To evaluate the relationship among renal injury, physical performance, and frailty progression in hypertensive older adults with CKD and assess whether dapagliflozin associates with reduced frailty progression, we designed the study DAPA-FORTRESS (DAPAgliflozin and Frailty prOgression in hypeRTension and chRonic kidnEy diSeaSe).METHODSWe enrolled 135 prefrail hypertensive patients with CKD aged >65 years and followed them for 1 year. After coarsened exact matching, our balanced cohort had 105 patients (52 dapagliflozin). Associations between albuminuria, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and physical performance were analyzed using correlation and regression models. Effect of dapagliflozin on frailty progression was evaluated using multivariable logistic regression.RESULTSA significant inverse association between gait speed and albuminuria (r2 = 0.48, P < 0.0001) and significant positive linear association between gait speed and eGFR (r2 = 0.18; P < 0.0001) were observed. Patients with eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2 exhibited significantly worse physical performance than those with higher eGFR (P = 0.0003). In adjusted analyses, receiving dapagliflozin was independently associated with lower odds of progressing to frailty at 1 year (OR = 0.130; CI 0.045-0.381; P < 0.001).CONCLUSIONIn older hypertensive patients with CKD, greater renal injury is associated with worse physical performance, while dapagliflozin use reduces the risk of frailty progression. These findings indicate a potential protective role of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibition in mitigating functional decline in this high-risk population.FUNDINGNIH: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (R01-HL146691), National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (R01-DK123259); American Heart Association (AHA- 24IPA1268813, AHA-22-915561, AHA-24-1195524).

title: Targeted Metabolites Associated with the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) Diet and Blood Pressure Changes in the DASH and DASH-Sodium Feeding Trials.
authorString: Yang J, Sullivan VK, Kim H, Evans AM, Rebholz CM.

journal.title: The journal of applied laboratory medicine

abstractText:
Background

Blood pressure decreases in response to the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet. Previous studies have identified metabolites associated with DASH diet and blood pressure reduction. Yet, these metabolites were quantified in relative units using untargeted approaches, which is not directly translatable to clinical use. The extent to which these diet-related metabolites correlate with absolute measures from targeted assays remains poorly characterized.

Methods

We measured serum concentrations of 15 metabolites previously identified as key differentiators between the DASH and control diets using targeted assays in the DASH (n = 216) and DASH-Sodium (n = 345) randomized controlled feeding trials. Spearman correlation coefficients were calculated to assess pairwise correlations between targeted and untargeted measurements. Multivariable linear regression was used to assess associations between targeted and untargeted measurements of DASH-related metabolites, to assess associations between metabolites and changes in blood pressure, and test for interactions by diet assignment.

Results

In the DASH trial, relative and absolute concentrations of 7 serum metabolites were strongly correlated (r = 0.91 to 0.99). The DASH diet intervention increased absolute serum concentrations of N-methylproline the most, and significantly decreased theobromine. Absolute concentrations of 12 metabolites in the DASH trial and 10 in the DASH-Sodium trial were significantly different between DASH vs control diet interventions. Eight significant metabolite-diet interactions were observed for changes in systolic and diastolic blood pressure in both trials (all P for interaction <0.05).

Conclusion

Targeted metabolomics confirmed key DASH-related biomarkers and enhanced the reproducibility of identified mechanisms through which the DASH diet lowers blood pressure.

title: Behavior-Based Electrogram Mapping Identifies Potential Functional Substrates in Atrial Fibrillation: The KSP-AF Randomized Study.
authorString: Zhou M, Li L, Wu L, Ruan Z, Zhu G, Zhang L, Duan Y, Xu C, Chen P.

journal.title: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background and aims

Conventional substrate mapping during atrial fibrillation (AF) may fail to capture dynamic electrogram behavior. Key spatiotemporal potentials (KSPs) are electrogram patterns identified by their temporal behavior during AF. We evaluated whether KSP-guided ablation improves outcomes beyond pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) and characterized their short-term frequency consistency.

Methods

In this single-center randomized study, 100 patients with paroxysmal or persistent AF undergoing first-time ablation were assigned to PVI plus KSP-guided ablation or PVI alone. The primary endpoint was 24-month single-procedure freedom from documented AF recurrence without antiarrhythmic drugs. Dominant frequency (DF) analysis included 93 KSP regions from 18 patients, assessed across four consecutive 5-second epochs.

Results

Acute AF termination occurred in 68% of patients with PVI + KSP versus 26% with PVI alone (P < 0.001). At 24 months, freedom from AF recurrence was 74% versus 48% (HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.18-0.79; P = 0.010), and freedom from AF/atrial tachycardia recurrence was 68% versus 46% (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.25-0.97; P = 0.040). Within-recording temporal DF variability was low (coefficient of variation, 4.8 ± 1.2%).

Conclusion

Adding KSP-guided ablation to PVI improved acute and 24-month rhythm outcomes in this single-center trial. These findings support further evaluation of behavior-based mapping to identify potential functional AF substrates and require multicenter confirmation.

title: Wearable-based automated cardiac arrest detection and alerting: A systematic review.
authorString: Jansen CE, Pol LR, Edgar R, Cetinyurek-Yavuz A, Beukema RJ, Brouwer MA, Allaart CP, van Royen N, Bonnes JL.
abstractText: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains a leading cause of death worldwide, with survival strongly dependent on rapid recognition and timely emergency care. Wearables capable of automated cardiac arrest detection and alerting may reduce delays to treatment, particularly in unwitnessed arrests.Therefore, this review aims to systematically evaluate the existing evidence on the performance of wearable sensors and algorithms designed for OHCA detection. A systematic search was performed using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, the Cochrane Libraries, forward citation and backward citation to identify all eligible studies up to 22 September 2026. Studies describing non-invasive, intended wearable systems designed to detect OHCA and reporting on their detection performance were included. The methodology and report of the present review are based on recommendations of the PRISMA statement and Cochrane Collaboration. Primary outcome is the sensitivity for cardiac arrest detection. Secondary outcomes include false positives cardiac arrest alerts and specificity. Studies were evaluated using the QUADAS-2 tool. From 6,344 records screened, 13 publications were included with the number of participants ranging from 18 to 1,423. Wristbands were the most prevalent device type (n=9). Nine studies used photoplethysmography as primary sensor type, with accelerometry as additive sensor modality (n=2). Other sensors used were mechanical plethysmography (n=1), electrocardiography (n=1), sound-based (n=1) and a nonlinear resonant circuit (n=1). Sensitivity ranged between 43.8 and 100%, with ten studies reporting a sensitivity of ≥ 90%. False positives ranged between multiple per day and one per twenty-one user-years. Wearable devices have demonstrated promising sensitivity for detecting cardiac arrest. However, (external) validation and real-life data are scarce, and the sensitivity-false alarm trade-off requires further investigation. OSF, doi: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/AEPF8.

title: Machine learning for predicting mortality in patients with sepsis and its associated complications: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Lv H, Gao Y, Yu A.
abstractText:
Background

Sepsis remains a leading cause of death in intensive care units worldwide and may be accompanied by complex complications, including encephalopathy, coagulopathy, acute kidney injury, myocardial dysfunction, and delirium, each of which substantially increases the risk of poor outcomes. Machine learning, a promising approach for prognostic prediction, can capture complex nonlinear relationships among clinical risk factors. However, its predictive performance in sepsis and its specific complications remains unclear.

Method

We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for relevant literature through April 2026. Studies that aimed to develop or validate machine learning models to predict mortality in adult patients with sepsis and its associated complications were included. The random-effects or bivariate model was used to calculate the AUC, sensitivity, and specificity.

Results

Overall, machine learning models show moderate predictive performance for short-term mortality in sepsis, with a combined AUC of 0.82 for the training set (46 studies, 15 models) and 0.79 for the validation set (50 studies, 25 models). Logistic regression is the most widely evaluated model, demonstrating stable performance (validation AUC = 0.81). Integrated methods, including random forest and XGBoost, performed equally well, with AUCs between 0.81 and 0.83 in both groups. Although LightGBM and DL-CMT achieved the highest AUCs in the training and validation sets, respectively, both estimates were based on a single study. Among the complications, the evidence for sepsis-associated encephalopathy (AUC = 0.81, 3 studies) and sepsis-induced coagulopathy (AUC = 0.80, 4 studies) is the most conclusive and best demonstrated. Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury showed moderate and stable performance (validation AUC = 0.79, 4 studies). Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy showed significant attenuation from training to validation (AUC 0.84 vs 0.78, all from a single study), and random forest performed well in training (AUC = 0.98) but was not widely reported. Septic shock reached the highest AUC (0.95), but this was based on a single study. The predictive utility of sepsis-associated delirium is limited (AUC = 0.67, 1 study), and sepsis-induced myocardial injury is moderate (AUC = 0.77, 1 study).For long-term mortality, evidence is extremely lacking. Only SAE (AUC 0.88 during training and 0.86 during validation) and SCRS (combined AUC 0.76) provided single study estimates, ruling out reliable conclusions.

Conclusion

In this meta-analysis, machine learning models showed moderate predictive performance for short-term mortality in sepsis. Among complications, SAE and SIC had the strongest evidence and best performance, whereas SAD showed limited utility. Evidence for long-term mortality was extremely scarce. These findings support the potential role of machine learning in early prognostic risk stratification, yet they also highlight the urgent need for rigorous external validation and higher-quality studies, particularly for under-investigated complications.

title: Effect of omeprazole on platelet reactivity in patients with diabetes mellitus and coronary artery disease receiving aspirin and clopidogrel: a randomised, placebo-controlled crossover trial (POC-DM).
authorString: Thungthienthong M, Kluntang S, Khopanlert W, Kaewkan P, Meemook K, Likittanasombut K, Chandanamattha P, Vathesatogkit P.

title: Prevalence of Angiographic Coronary Artery Disease in Systolic Heart Failure Without Infarct-Pattern Late Gadolinium Enhancement: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
authorString: Grafton-Clarke C, Farooq M, Gall A, Sawh N, Dinescu C, Berry C, Petrie MC, Greenwood JP, Garg P, Swoboda PP.
abstractText:
Aims

Rest late gadolinium enhancement cardiovascular magnetic resonance (LGE-CMR) identifies infarct-pattern scar but does not assess coronary anatomy. We estimated the prevalence of angiographic coronary artery disease (CAD) among adults with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) or otherwise unexplained left ventricular systolic dysfunction without infarct-pattern LGE.

Methods and results

MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched to 27 July 2026. Eligible studies provided separable scar-negative denominators and corresponding angiographic CAD counts from invasive coronary angiography (ICA). Scar-negative was defined as the absence of subendocardial or transmural LGE in a coronary distribution. Random-effects logit meta-analysis used restricted maximum likelihood and Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals. Twenty-two reports representing 20 studies included 2,236 paired LGE-CMR and ICA. 818 patients had infarct-pattern scar, and 1,418 were scar-negative. Eight studies contributed 44 CAD cases among 468 scar-negative patients for ≥50% stenosis, giving a pooled prevalence of 10.8% (95% confidence interval [CI] 7.4-15.4). Five studies contributed 19 CAD cases among 271 scar-negative patients for ≥70% stenosis, giving a pooled prevalence of 7.6% (95% CI 4.4-12.6). Seven studies contributed 33 CAD cases among 679 scar-negative patients for high-risk-pattern CAD, giving a pooled prevalence of 4.9% (95% CI 2.2-10.6) and a 95% prediction interval of 0.8-24.8%. These strata represented different study subsets and were not nested.

Conclusion

Among selected adults with HFrEF or otherwise unexplained LVSD who underwent paired LGE-CMR and ICA, absence of infarct-pattern LGE did not exclude angiographic CAD. Further coronary assessment should be considered when resolving that uncertainty would alter diagnosis or management.

title: Measurement of left atrial appendage blood transport in patients with atrial fibrillation using dynamic contrast 4DCT.
authorString: Severance L, Contijoch F, Mahmud I, Buchalla T, Han F, Gonzalo A, Maidu B, Bargellini C, Ledesma-Carbayo MJ, Montalvo-García D, Del Alamo JC, Kahn AM, McVeigh ER.
abstractText:
Background

Current stroke risk stratification in atrial fibrillation (AF) relies on clinical factors with known limitations. Blood stasis in the Left Atrial Appendage (LAA) promotes thrombus formation, contributing to embolic stroke. Our objective is to map contrast transport throughout the LAA volume with 4DCT.

Methods

Patients being treated for AF underwent dynamic contrast 4DCT. Hounsfield unit (HU) vs. time curves were fitted voxel wise using gamma-variate models. Three LAA blood transport metrics were extracted: (1) increase in residence time between distal LAA voxels and the LA/LAA orifice (ΔRT); (2) ratio of peak HU enhancement in distal LAA voxels to peak HU in the LA/LAA orifice (ΔHU); and (3) total volume of delayed filling (Vstasis) in the LAA. A composite "LAA Transport Index" (LAATI) was computed using principal component analysis.

Results

Among all 93 patients, a wide range of delayed transport in the LAA was observed with: 0 ​< ​ΔRT ​< ​30 ​s, 0.02 ​< ​ΔHU ​< ​1, 0 ​< ​Vstasis ​< ​13 ​mL. Patients imaged during sinus rhythm (n ​= ​26) had rapid filling of the entire LAA with 0 ​< ​ΔRT ​< ​4.7 ​s, 0.65 ​< ​ΔHU ​< ​1, 0 ​< ​Vstasis ​< ​1.0 ​mL. In comparison, patients in AF had values over the entire range ΔRT, ΔHU and Vstasis. For patients imaged in sinus the mean LAATI ​= ​-1.06 ​± ​0.4, and for those imaged in AF the mean LAATI ​= ​0.43 ​± ​1.7. LAATI did not correlate with CHA2DS2-VASc (p ​= ​0.44) or chicken wing morphology (p ​= ​0.21).

Conclusions

4DCT-based voxel-wise quantification of LAA contrast transport using gamma-variate modeling is technically feasible. Further studies are required to determine its potential value for personalized stroke-risk assessment.

title: Quantifying benefit and cost-effectiveness of additional investment in community health workers for people with cardiovascular risks in New York City.
authorString: Frechette JM, Morse M, McNatt ZZ, Eyssallenne AP, Parrott J, Cabrera R, Zhou Q, Allen B, Braithwaite RS.
abstractText:
Introduction

To estimate the life expectancy gains, cost effectiveness, and impact on life expectancy inequality achieved by additional investment in community health worker (CHW) programs in New York City Methods: Using a state-transition model of mortality-driving conditions adapted to New York City anchored to 2021, we examined the impact of additional investment in CHWs for people with obesity, hypertension, and diabetes on (1) change in life expectancy, (2) health-inclusive (lifespan) return on investment (LROI), and (3) change in inequality of life expectancy distribution between neighborhoods. Inequality analyses included neighborhood-level baseline life expectancy, median income, and plurality race or ethnicity. Analyses were conducted in 2026.

Results

Scaling up CHWs results in a 0.13-year life expectancy gain on the citywide level, with favorable LROI of 14.72 years per $100,000 invested. Neighborhood-level gains range from 0.05 years to 0.33 years, while LROI ranges from 11.76 to 29.62 life-years/$100,000. In general, life expectancy gains and LROI were higher for lower-income, lower life expectancy, and minoritized race neighborhoods.

Conclusions

Additional investment in CHW programs in New York City has the potential to cost-effectively raise the citywide life expectancy while reducing inequalities between neighborhoods.

title: Heart Failure Care in Greece: A Call for Action.
authorString: Xanthopoulos A, Alkagiet S, Nikolaou M, Stavrati A, Chalikias G, Naka KK.

journal.title: Hellenic journal of cardiology : HJC = Hellenike kardiologike epitheorese

abstractText: Heart failure (HF) remains a major public health challenge in Greece, affecting an estimated 300,000 individuals and imposing a substantial burden through high mortality, recurrent hospitalizations, impaired quality of life, and escalating healthcare costs. Although significant advances in pharmacological therapies, device-based interventions, and multidisciplinary care have improved outcomes in recent years, important gaps persist in the implementation of evidence-based HF care across the country. This viewpoint from the Heart Failure Working Group of the Hellenic Society of Cardiology (HCS) highlights five strategic priorities for the development of a comprehensive national HF strategy. First, improving the recognition and diagnosis of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), an increasingly prevalent and frequently underdiagnosed condition, through greater awareness, structured diagnostic pathways, and the adoption of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence. Second, strengthening the national advanced HF network by establishing coordinated referral pathways and equitable access to advanced therapies such as heart transplantation and durable left ventricular assist devices. Third, integrating palliative care into routine HF management to address symptom burden, psychosocial needs, and advance care planning throughout the disease trajectory. Fourth, expanding access to cardiac rehabilitation through hospital-based, community-based, and home-based programs capable of overcoming geographical disparities and improving functional outcomes. Fifth, developing a specialized HF nursing workforce through structured education and certification programs aligned with European standards. Collectively, these interconnected priorities provide a framework for advancing and modernizing HF care in Greece. A national HF registry is proposed as the foundational infrastructure supporting all five priorities.

title: Cardiac lymphatic modulation in myocardial repair: from lymphangiogenesis to microsurgical reconstructive strategies.
authorString: Fabi A, Melcher S, Wendelspiess SR, Boeddinghaus J, Salikhanov I, Kutschka I, Baraki H, Mueller C, Kappos EA.
abstractText: The cardiac lymphatic system is increasingly recognized as a regulator of myocardial fluid homeostasis and tissue remodeling following myocardial injury. Experimental evidence suggests that impaired lymphatic drainage contributes to persistent edema, chronic inflammation and functional deterioration after myocardial infarction and other acute and chronic cardiovascular conditions. However, the translational relevance of pharmacological and microsurgical reconstructive strategies remains largely unexplored. A literature review was performed using PubMed/MEDLINE to identify studies addressing the anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, and potential therapeutic strategies addressing the cardiac lymphatic system. This study finds that cardiac lymphatics drain myocardial interstitial fluid and immune cells toward mediastinal pathways. Across various disease models, cardiac lymphatic dysfunction contributes to prolonged edema, inflammation, and adverse fibrotic remodeling. In preclinical models, pro-lymphangiogenic strategies have increased lymphatic growth and transport and have been associated with more favorable remodeling. By contrast, lymphovenous anastomosis and vascularized lymph node transfer remain largely untested concepts in cardiac disease; their ability to improve myocardial lymphatic drainage or clinical outcomes has not been demonstrated. Consequently, cardiac lymphatics may become an important therapeutic target in myocardial repair. Preliminary evidence supports the pharmacological promotion of lymphangiogenesis as a promising strategy for myocardial regeneration, but further research is necessary to explore the safety, feasibility and effectiveness of surgical cardiac lymphatic modulation.

title: Saturated and Trans Fatty Acids Were Not Associated with All-Cause or Cause-Specific Mortality in a Japanese Population with Relatively Low Intakes: The Japan Public Health Center-Based Prospective Study.
authorString: Kito K, Ishihara J, Kotemori A, Nakadate M, Yamagishi K, Maruyama K, Miyazaki S, Okada C, Yamaji T, Iwasaki M, Inoue M, Tsugane S, Sawada N, JPHC Study Group.
abstractText: World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines recommend that saturated fatty acids (SFAs) and trans fatty acids (TFAs) should comprise ≤10% and ≤1% of total energy intake, respectively. However, evidence of the mortality risk associated with increased TFA and SFA intake in populations with a relatively low fat intake is limited. To examine the association between total fat, SFA, TFA, monounsaturated fatty acid (MUFA), and polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) intake and all-cause and cause-specific mortality in a Japanese population. We included 90,807 participants aged 45-74 years with no history of cancer or cardiovascular disease (CVD). Dietary assessment was performed using a validated food frequency questionnaire. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models for each quintile of dietary fat intake: total fat, SFA, MUFA, PUFA, TFA, industrially-derived TFA (i-TFAs), and ruminant-derived TFA (r-TFA). During a mean follow-up of 18.9 years, 22,618 deaths occurred. None of the analyses of fat intakes in quintiles showed a positive association with all-cause mortality for higher intakes of all fats, even for i-TF. In females, a nominally significant association was observed for all-cause mortality with PUFA (HR, Q5 vs. Q1 = 0.92 [0.84-0.997]) and cancer mortality with MUFA (HR, Q5 vs. Q1 = 0.84 [0.73-0.97]).In females, higher intakes of total fat and MUFA were nominally associated with higher respiratory disease mortality, whereas a higher SFA intake showed a suggestive association (P for trend <0.05). In this study, neither SFA nor TFA intake was positively associated with all-cause mortality, and higher PUFA intake was inversely associated with all-cause mortality in females.

title: Eicosapentaenoic acid in adipose tissue is associated with a lower risk of hemorrhagic stroke: A Danish case-cohort study.
authorString: Thygesen JH, Hesislev VB, Czerwonka P, Lundbye-Christensen S, Dahm CC, Olsen A, Halkjær J, Schmidt EB, Venø SK, Bork C.
abstractText: Omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) have been linked to a lower risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, however, their association with hemorrhagic stroke remains uncertain. We investigated associations between adipose tissue content of individual omega-3 PUFAs (α-linolenic acid (ALA), eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), docosapentaenoic acid (DPA), docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), the sum of EPA+DHA), and the risk of hemorrhagic stroke and its subtypes intracranial and subarachnoid hemorrhage. This case-cohort study based on the Danish Diet, Cancer and Health Cohort included 54,546 men and women aged 50 to 65 years at baseline (1993-1997). Adipose tissue composition of omega-3 PUFAs was determined by gas chromatography for all hemorrhagic stroke cases and within a randomly drawn subcohort of 4,615 participants. Cases were identified by linkage to the Danish National Patient Register. Hazard ratios (HR) were obtained by weighted Cox regression. During a median of 21 years follow-up, we identified 729 hemorrhagic stroke cases. In multivariable analyses, a significant inverse association between the content of EPA in adipose tissue and the risk of total hemorrhagic stroke was found. Thus, the HR for hemorrhagic stroke was 0.64 (95% CI: 0.50-0.82) when comparing the highest quintile of EPA content in adipose tissue with the lowest. Associations were similar when stratified according to sex and when investigating subtypes of hemorrhagic stroke, although findings were not statistically significant for subarachnoid hemorrhages. No statistically significant associations were observed between adipose tissue content of DHA, DPA and EPA+DHA and hemorrhagic strokes. A high content of ALA in adipose tissue was associated with a higher risk of hemorrhagic stroke (HR for quintile 5 vs. 1: 1.32, 95% CI: 1.01-1.72). A high content of EPA in adipose tissue was associated with a lower risk of hemorrhagic stroke, while a high content of ALA was associated with a higher risk in this cohort.

title: Aortic Valve Replacement in Patients 50-65 Years: A Target Trial Emulation.
authorString: Mehaffey JH, Wolfe SB, Strobel RJ, Hayanga JWA, Mascio CE, Yarboro LT, Daggubati R, Price BS, Badhwar V.
abstractText:
Background

Guidelines favor surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) in patients aged 65 years or younger with aortic stenosis, yet many receive transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) without supportive data. We performed a target trial emulation of SAVR versus TAVI in this population.

Methods

Using the all-payer Premier Healthcare Database (2016-2024), patients aged 50 to 65 years undergoing isolated SAVR or TAVI within 90 days of an aortic stenosis diagnosis were evaluated. After trial exclusions, frailty and predicted risk were incorporated into a clone-censor-weight framework with inverse probability weighting. Reporting adhered to TARGET guidance. The primary outcome was the 5-year composite of all-cause mortality, stroke, valve reintervention, or heart failure rehospitalization.

Results

The clone-censor-weighted analysis included 18,549 SAVR and 18,549 TAVI patients, balanced across all covariates (standardized mean difference <0.10). Mean age was 60 years, and many were of low surgical risk <4% (SAVR 69.5% vs TAVI 49.7%). In-hospital mortality (0.41% vs 0.31%; odds ratio, 0.61; p<0.001) and periprocedural stroke (0.31% vs 0.28%; odds ratio, 0.67; p<0.001) favored TAVI. At 5 years, risk-adjusted freedom from the primary composite outcome (87.5% vs 77.8%; hazard ratio, 1.87; p<0.001), heart failure rehospitalization (92.9% vs 88.2%; subdistribution hazard ratio, 1.72; p<0.001), and all-cause mortality (93.6% vs 85.6%; hazard ratio, 2.34; p<0.001) favored SAVR.

Conclusions

For contemporary patients aged 50 to 65 years, the primary composite outcome favored SAVR over TAVI at 5 years, most markedly at centers with high young TAVI utilization. These data may guide heart team decision making and future trial design.

title: Statewide Trends in Morbidity and Mortality in Octogenarians Undergoing Isolated Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
authorString: Weissman C, Clark MJ, He C, Zimmer T, Willekes C, Fanning J, Murphy ET, Nemeh HW, Schwartz CF, Pruitt AL, Timek TA.
abstractText:
Background

We sought to determine whether advanced age modifies the association between established preoperative risk factors and 30-day outcomes following isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), compare temporal trends between octogenarians and younger patients, and characterize differences in perioperative outcomes between the two groups.

Methods

Using the Michigan Society of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgeons Quality Collaborative (The Society of Thoracic Surgeons Adult Cardiac Surgery Database), we identified 105,445 patients undergoing isolated CABG from 2006-2024. Outcomes and case volumes were assessed across four eras. Operative mortality was evaluated using mixed-effects logistic regression with hospital as a random effect. Secondary analyses used multiple imputation with hospital-clustered multivariable logistic regression to evaluate age-related effect modification for short-term mortality and morbidity.

Results

Octogenarians comprised 8.1% of cases (8,563/105,445). Operative mortality was higher in octogenarians (4.8%; n=413) than patients <80 (1.8%; n=1,710). Operative mortality rates were stable over the study period for both patient groups. In multiple-imputation models, octogenarian status was independently associated with higher odds of operative mortality, stroke, reoperation for bleeding, and renal failure. Age-dependent effect modification was observed for select outcomes. In octogenarians, hypertension was more strongly associated with postoperative atrial fibrillation, diabetes with renal failure, and cerebrovascular disease with discharge to extended care.

Conclusions

In octogenarians, CABG remains associated with higher morbidity and mortality than in younger patients, with minimal changes in 30-day outcomes over the last 20 years. Most traditional risk factors demonstrated similar relative associations across age groups, with age-specific effects in select postoperative domains.

title: Trends and Disparities in Mortality Related to Cardiac Arrest and Cardiogenic Shock: A 1999-2024 United States Analysis.
authorString: Jain H, Cheema MRS, Soni K, Sklar MA, Saad MS, Abbott JD, Vallabhajosyula S.
abstractText: Cardiac arrest (CA) complicating cardiogenic shock (CS) identifies a high-risk phenotype, but population-level mortality trends among patients with both conditions are not well described. Using the CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death database, we identified deaths among US adults aged ≥25 years from 1999 to 2024 in which both CA (ICD-10 I46) and CS (R57.0) were recorded on the same death certificate and compared them with all CS-related deaths. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 population were calculated, and temporal trends were assessed using Joinpoint regression. Overall, 98,531 CA+CS deaths occurred, compared with 577,658 CS-related deaths. The AAMR for CA+CS declined from 1.3 in 1999 to 0.9 in the mid-2000s, rose by 10.1% per year between 2009 and 2021 (95% CI 9.8 to 10.5) to a peak of 2.9, and declined modestly to 2.7 by 2024. The share of CS deaths that also listed CA increased from 12.4% to 18.9%. Men had consistently higher AAMRs than women (3.6 vs 1.9 in 2024), and adults aged ≥65 years accounted for 71.3% of deaths. Non-Hispanic Black adults had the highest rates from 2016 onward and the steepest increase, while the West had the highest and the Midwest the lowest rates among census regions. CA+CS mortality in the United States has roughly doubled since 1999, with persistent differences by sex, race and ethnicity, age, and region that warrant study with clinically detailed data.

title: Influence of the PROFUND index on the effectiveness of SGLT2 inhibitors in elderly pluripathological patients with acute heart failure: PROFUND-IC registry.
authorString: Guzmán-Carreras A, Bernabeu-Wittel M, Sánchez-Del Hoyo R, Muñoz-Rivas N, Sánchez-Sauce B, Aguilar-Rodríguez F, Cabeza-Osorio L, Andrès E, Lorenzo-Villalba N, Méndez-Bailón M, all the researchers from the PROFUND-IC registry.
abstractText:
Background and aims

The PROFUND index is a useful tool for estimating one-year mortality in pluripathological patients with heart failure, although its influence on the treatments administered remains unknown. The objectives of the present study were to evaluate whether the PROFUND index influences the effectiveness of sodium-glucose cotransporter type II inhibitors (SGLT2i), and to describe the differential characteristics of pluripathological patients with acute heart failure (AHF) according to this scale.

Methods

Retrospective study of 880 pluripathological patients with AHF from the PROFUND-IC registry, divided into three groups according to PROFUND index: low (0-2 points), medium (3-6) and high/very high mortality risk (≥7). A descriptive and comparative analysis was performed using the Chi-square test for qualitative variables and ANOVA for quantitative ones, (Fisher and Kruskal-Wallis, when indicated). Propensity Score Matching (PSM) was applied to minimize confounding factors. Kaplan-Meier curves were constructed analysing readmissions and mortality according to SGLT2i administration.

Results

880 patients were included, 16.3% with low risk; 39.7% with medium risk and 44.1% with high/very high risk. Those with PROFUND index≥7 were predominantly women (61.3%, p=0.006), older, with worse functional class, lower Barthel index, and higher one-year mortality (p<0.001). SGLT2i administration appears to reduce readmissions among patients with PROFUND index between 3 and 6 (25.5% vs. 38.3%, p=0.02). After PSM, this trend persisted (24.1% versus 36.1%), without reaching statistical significance (p=0.065).

Conclusions

SGLT2i appear beneficial in pluripathological patients with AHF, although the greatest impact is observed in PROFUND 3-6. Further studies are needed to clarify how comorbidity and functionality influence the effectiveness of these drugs.

title: Global burden of chronic kidney disease attributable to hypertension due to high body mass index: projections to 2050.
authorString: Li L, Zhu G, Wang KK, Maimaiti S, Wang S, Lu C.
abstractText: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects approximately 9.1% of the global population, equivalent to approximately 843 million individuals as of 2021, with hypertension (HTN) as a major contributor. High body mass index (BMI) exacerbates HTN-related kidney injury, but the global burden of HTN-related CKD attributable to high BMI remains poorly characterized. Using data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 study for 1990-2021, we estimated attributable deaths, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), the age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR), and the age-standardized disability-adjusted life-year rate (ASDR). Temporal trends were assessed using the estimated annual percentage change (EAPC), and a Bayesian age-period-cohort model was used to project rates to 2050. Attributable deaths increased from 36,476 in 1990 to 179,788 in 2021, and DALYs increased from 1.01 million to 4.26 million. ASMR increased from 1.09 to 2.19 per 100,000 (EAPC, 4.22%), and ASDR increased from 26.04 to 50.11 per 100,000 (EAPC, 3.63%). Central Sub-Saharan Africa had the highest ASMR (7.66 per 100,000), whereas High-income North America had the fastest increase in ASMR (EAPC, 5.63%). ASMR and ASDR were higher in men than in women. Death counts peaked at ages 85-89 years in both sexes, whereas DALYs peaked at ages 60-64 years in men and 65-69 years in women. Crude rates were higher in populations with a higher sociodemographic index (SDI), whereas the relative burden became more concentrated in lower-SDI populations; concentration indices changed from -0.10 to -0.17 for deaths and from -0.06 to -0.08 for DALYs. By 2050, ASMR is projected to reach 4.44 per 100,000 (95% credible interval [CI], 3.70-5.20), and ASDR is projected to reach 77.15 per 100,000 (95% CI, 1.81-152.49). The high BMI-attributable burden of HTN-related CKD is increasing and remains unequally distributed. These findings support integrated obesity prevention and hypertension control, with priority given to high-risk regions and older adults.

title: Proliferative Glomerulonephritis With Monotypic Immunoglobulin Deposits of IgG1 Subclass: A Case Series.
authorString: Bu L, Vaughan LE, Said SM, Zhu Y, Chen C, Abdalla M, Buglioni A, Zhang P, Hernandez LH, Sethi S, Larsen CP, Leung N, Nasr SH.

journal.title: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation

abstractText:
Rationale & objective

Most cases of proliferative glomerulonephritis with monotypic immunoglobulin deposits (PGNMID) are associated with IgG3. The characteristics of IgG1 deposits within PGNMID have not been well defined and are the focus of this study.

Study design

Retrospective case series.

Setting & participants

Forty-six PGNMID cases with granular monotypic IgG1 deposits (PGNMID-IgG1) identified in nephropathology archives.

Findings

57% of cases were male and 78% had hematuria. The median age was 57 years, the median proteinuria level was 4.8 g/day, and the median eGFR level was 52 mL/min/1.73 m2. Hypocomplementemia was uncommon (12%). Kidney biopsy revealed MPGN (54%) or mesangial proliferative GN (33%), with membranous features in nearly half (43%). A nephropathic clone or monoclonal Ig (mIg) was detected in 19 of 42 patients with PGNMID-IgG1 who underwent evaluation, including 10 with chronic lymphocytic leukemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL/SLL). Among patients >50 years, the detection rate was 72% (18/25) vs. 6% (1/17) among younger patients. SPEP/SIF detected the nephropathic mIg in 13 of 40, and bone marrow biopsy done in 25 detected clonal B-cells in eight and clonal plasma cells in two patients. Follow-up (median 27 months) was available for 37 patients. Ten (83%) of 12 patients with an identifiable clone or mIg responded to clone-targeted (anti-plasma or B- cell) therapy, whereas 4 of 8 patients without an identifiable clone or mIg responded to anti-plasma cell therapy. At 60 months, the overall cumulative incidence of kidney failure requiring dialysis or death was 31.1% (7.9% to 48.5%). Four patients underwent kidney transplantation and three with transplant biopsies exhibited recurrent disease.

Limitations

Retrospective, single-center study, non-standardized hematologic workup and management.

Conclusions

Nearly 75% of PGNMID-IgG1 cases >50 years of age have a clonal population detected and nearly a quarter have CLL/SLL. Response to anti-B-cell therapy may be greater in those with an identifiable clone or mIg. These data may inform treatment strategies for people with PGNMID-IgG1.

title: Clinical profile, risk factors, and one-year outcomes of atrial fibrillation in a native West African setting: Insights from the Ibadan atrial fibrillation registry.
authorString: Ogah OS, Orimolade OA, Makinde OZ, Alabi OG, Akinyemi JO, Akunwata CU, Ogah CM, Ademowo-Olusanya OO, Aje A, Adebayo OM, Adeoye AM, Adebiyi AA, Oladapo OO, Shokunbi WA, Owolabi MO, Falase AO.

journal.title: Journal of the National Medical Association

abstractText:
Background

We sought to describe the clinical profile, risk factors, management, and one-year outcomes of atrial fibrillation in a tertiary hospital in Nigeria METHODS: The Ibadan AF registry enrolled consecutive patients with AF from January 1, 2016, to September 30, 2023, at Nigeria's oldest and largest tertiary hospital. The CHA2DS2VASC score was used for stroke risk classification. The participants were followed up for 12 months (at one month, 6 months, and 12 months) after enrolment through clinic visits or telephone calls, and supplementary data were obtained from medical notes. Stepwise multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to identify independent predictors of each of the study outcomes from the variables that were significant in univariable analyses.

Results

Three hundred and fifty-seven patients were enrolled; median age was 65 years (25th and 75th percentiles = 61.6 and 64.6 years; minimum and maximum years = 19 and 95 years), and 52.9% were male. Hypertension was the most common risk factor (80.7%), and heart failure was the most common mode of presentation (70%). Sixty-one percent of patients had permanent AF, 25.0% had persistent AF, and 14% had paroxysmal AF. Most patients (78.4%) were on oral anticoagulants. Most received rate control with beta-blockers (75%) and/or digoxin (44%), and 70% achieved adequate rate control. At the end of one-year follow-up, 251 (70.3%) were alive, 31(8.7%) were hospitalized, and 88(24.6%) died. The independent predictors of composite outcomes (rehospitalization and/or all-cause mortality) were the Kanofsky score (aHR. 0.44, [95% CI: 0.21-0.92, p = 0.028] for score of 50-70 and (aHR. 0.26, [95% CI: 0.12-0.58, p = 0.001] for score of 80-100(Reference. 0-40), socioeconomic class (aHR. 0.54 [95% CI: 0.30-0.98),p = 0.041]) for middle socioeconomic class (Reference- low socioeconomic class) and use of amiodarone (aHR.1.77 [95% CI:1.00-3.13),p = 0.049]) CONCLUSION: Hypertension is the commonest risk factor for AF in this cohort, and >80% of study participants with AF require anticoagulation. Mortality at 12 months is high due to severe structural disease and high comorbidity burden. Efforts are needed to control and treat risk factors, heart failure, and comorbidities in AF management in our setting.

title: Electroactive Gel-MA hydrogels delivering sustained puerarin for myocardial infarction treatment.
authorString: Yue Y, Li B, Xu G, Ren L.
abstractText: Myocardial infarction (MI) remains a major cause of heart failure and mortality worldwide. Herein, an electrically conductive hydrogel was developed by incorporating puerarin-functionalized carbon nanotubes (CNT-Pu) into a gelatin methacryloyl (Gel-MA) matrix for potential MI repair. CNT-Pu was dispersed in the Gel-MA precursor solution, followed by photo-crosslinking to form the Gel-MA/CNT-Pu hydrogel. The resulting hydrogel exhibited a porous microstructure, enhanced electrical conductivity, favorable mechanical properties and elastic recovery, and sustained puerarin release over 28 days. In vitro, the Gel-MA/CNT-Pu hydrogel exhibited favorable cytocompatibility with both L929 fibroblasts and H9c2 cardiomyoblasts, supporting its preliminary biological compatibility for myocardial applications. In a rat MI model, Gel-MA/CNT-Pu treatment was associated with reduced inflammatory cell infiltration and attenuation of fibrotic scar formation.
