Quantitative histological analysis demonstrated a significantly smaller fibrotic area and greater left ventricular wall thickness in the Gel-MA/CNT-Pu group than in the control group, suggesting that Gel-MA/CNT-Pu provided a multifunctional biomaterial strategy combining mechanical support, electrical conductivity, and localized drug delivery to attenuate adverse structural remodeling after MI. Further investigations were required to establish its functional cardiac benefits and long-term safety.

title: Effect of Home Blood Pressure Monitoring on Blood Pressure Control in Post Ischemic Stroke Older Adults.
authorString: Jaipong S, Srithumsuk W, Tongma S, Pattayakorn P, Podimuang K, Ortiz T.
abstractText: Hypertension is a major modifiable risk factor for recurrent stroke in Thailand. This study examined whether home blood pressure monitoring (HBPM) improved short-term blood pressure (BP) control after ischemic stroke. A non-equivalent control group quasi-experimental study was conducted at Phrachomklao Hospital, Thailand. Sequential allocation assigned 130 older adults to standard care and 130 to standard care plus HBPM. The primary outcome was BP control 1 week after discharge based on national guidelines. Multiple logistic regression adjusted for demographic and clinical factors. Of 260 participants, 215 completed the study (HBPM, n = 114; control, n = 101). After adjustment, the HBPM group had significantly greater odds of achieving BP control than the control group (OR = 22.656, 95% CI [9.494-54.066], p < .001). Smoking, diabetes, and lower discharge systolic BP were also associated with BP control, although these findings should be interpreted cautiously. HBPM was associated with improved short-term BP control in older adults following ischemic stroke. HBPM may be a useful addition to post-discharge care, but the single-center design and short follow-up limit generalizability. Further research should examine long-term effects and stroke recurrence.

title: Venous thromboembolism after breast cancer surgery: incidence, predictive factors and outcomes in 270,564 patients.
authorString: Knoedler SA, Fabi A, De Silva P, Sy S, Elfgen C, Heidinger M, Griewing SR, Sofo G, Schmauss D, Tausch C, Montagna G, Hofer SOP, Falkner F, Kappos EA, Orgill DP, Momeni A.
abstractText: Breast cancer surgery is generally considered to be low risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE). However, when VTE occurs, it may lead to severe complications and increased mortality. This study aimed to determine the incidence, predictors, and clinical impact of postoperative VTE following breast cancer surgery using a large, multicenter surgical database. The American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP) database (2008-2023) was queried to identify female patients undergoing surgery for breast cancer without concurrent reconstruction. Patients were stratified according to postoperative VTE occurrence. Demographics, comorbidities, laboratory values, operative characteristics, and 30-day outcomes were compared. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of VTE and to construct a predictive model, which was internally validated using bootstrap resampling. Among 270,564 patients included, 465 (0.2%) developed postoperative VTE. Of these, 247 (53.1%) had deep vein thrombosis, 177 (38.1%) pulmonary embolism, and 41 (8.8%) both. Patients who developed VTE were older, had higher body mass index (BMI), greater comorbidity burden, and longer operative times (all p < 0.001). They also demonstrated lower preoperative serum albumin, hematocrit, prothrombin time, and albumin-to-creatinine ratio. VTE was associated with significantly longer hospital stays, increased rates of reoperation and readmission, and a more than 20-fold higher crude 30-day mortality (1.9% vs. 0.1%) (all p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, increasing age (OR 1.26 per 10 years), BMI (OR 1.17 per 5 kg/m²), congestive heart failure (OR 2.43), metastatic cancer (OR 2.05), lower serum albumin (OR 0.63 per 1 g/dL), and longer operative duration (OR 1.09 per 30 min) were independently associated with postoperative VTE. Compared with partial mastectomy, total mastectomy (OR 2.58), modified radical mastectomy (OR 2.22), and radical mastectomy (OR 2.80) were associated with significantly higher odds of postoperative VTE. The predictive model demonstrated acceptable discrimination (AUC 0.717; optimism-corrected 0.700) and good calibration. Age, BMI, congestive heart failure, metastatic cancer, mastectomy and operative time remained associated with VTE in all sensitivity analyses. Postoperative VTE following breast cancer surgery is uncommon but associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Advanced age, obesity, cardiac comorbidity, metastatic disease, hypoalbuminemia, longer operative duration, and greater surgical extent were independently associated with increased thromboembolic risk. Awareness of these risk factors may support individualized perioperative risk assessment and thromboprophylaxis decisions, as recommended by current consensus guidance, and facilitate earlier recognition of postoperative VTE. Not applicable.

title: Diagnosis of pseudoxanthoma elasticum following genomic re-analysis in a patient with chronic kidney disease: a case report
authorString: Bagkatzounis T, Mabillard H, Sayer JA.
abstractText: Purpose To describe a diagnosis of pseudoxanthoma elasticum following genomic re-analysis and to illustrate the challenge of determining whether chronic kidney disease represents an atypical manifestation of ABCC6-associated disease. Methods Following re-analysis of whole-genome sequencing data, historical renal, vascular, ophthalmic, laboratory and imaging records were reviewed. Reverse phenotyping was undertaken to assess the extent to which the patient’s multisystem features were consistent with pseudoxanthoma elasticum and to examine possible explanations for his chronic kidney disease. Results An older man with progressive chronic kidney disease, low-grade proteinuria, severe visual impairment and extensive large-vessel peripheral arterial disease was found to have compound heterozygous pathogenic ABCC6 variants, NM_001171.6 c.1741C>T; p.(Gln581Ter) and c.2787+1G>T. The diagnosis of pseudoxanthoma elasticum had not been recognized during life. His ocular and vascular disease were compatible with the phenotype of pseudoxanthoma elasticum; however, the renal phenotype was atypical. Renal ultrasonography and computed tomography showed chronic kidney disease without nephrolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis or renal calcification. Long-standing hypertension, severe vascular disease and a possible renovascular component remained plausible alternative explanations for renal impairment. Renal biopsy was not performed, and the diagnosis was made after the patient’s death, preventing targeted clinical reassessment. Conclusions Genomic re-analysis can identify previously unrecognized rare diseases and should prompt careful reverse phenotyping. In this case, the diagnosis of pseudoxanthoma elasticum explained important ocular and vascular features, but a direct causal relationship between ABCC6 deficiency and chronic kidney disease could not be established. This case supports further characterization of kidney phenotypes in individuals with biallelic ABCC6 variants.

title: Rising Inequity in Hypertension Prevalence: Results of a Survey in Sorocaba-SP, Brazil, 2022
authorString: Gianini RJ, Nanartonis MJ, de Carvalho BV, Caneto NF, Junqueira NM, Gammal DF, Rezende CMS, Rodrigues CIS.
abstractText:
Background: Arterial Hypertension (AH) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Its prevalence among adults and the elderly is high globally and between 30-35% in Brazil. It is a primary reason for healthcare consultations, hospital admissions, and mortality.

Objectives:

This study aimed to evaluate the AH prevalence and to investigate its association with sociodemographic factors.

Methods:

A population-based, cross-sectional study on a cluster sample of 1,080 individuals. The analysis evaluated age, gender, education level, income. The statistical model estimated prevalence ratios (PR), 95% confidence intervals, while a concentration curve assessed sociodemographic inequalities.

Results:

An overall prevalence of 38.39% was observed, along with a significant association between AH and gender, age, education level, and income. The concentration curve revealed a distribution of AH higher among men and the elderly, concentration index = -0.31.

Conclusions:

These findings underscore the need for public policies aimed at reducing health inequalities and strategies for prevention, diagnosis, and control of AH for populations facing greater social vulnerability.

title: The association between venous thromboembolism during pregnancy and low birth weight: A retrospective cohort study
authorString: Moradi A, Norouzi M, MosaFarkhani E.
abstractText: Background Among the causes of maternal morbidity and mortality worldwide, venous thromboembolism (VTE) also impacts long-term effects on some organs beyond physical harm of pregnancy. Evidence on the effect of VTE on neonatal outcomes, especially low birth weight (LBW), is still insufficient and contradicting. The objective of this study was to assess the relationship between maternal VTE during pregnancy and LBW in a large national cohort. Methods In a retrospective cohort study, we used data from the Sina Health Information System covering 21094 pregnant women who had received standard prenatal care in Mashhad, Iran from March 2017 to September 2025. The exposed group included 10547 women with VTE confirmed that were each individually matched (1:1) to non exposed pregnant women without a record of VTE. The analysis was performed in Stata version 16. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was used to calculate adjusted odds ratios (AORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for LBW (< 2500 g) confounders such as mothers education, parity, hypertensive disorders, antepartum haemorrhage and previous miscarriage were considered. Results Low birth weight was significantly more frequently recorded in a group of infants whose mothers had VTE compared to a group of infants whose mothers did not have VTE (59% compare to 41%, P < 0.001). Even after the adjustment for confounders, VTE remained a powerful independent factor for LBW (AOR = 2.28, 95% CI: 2.08–2.50, P < 0.001). Besides VTE, maternal hypertension was one of the independent predictors included maternal hypertension (AOR = 1.74, 95% CI: 1.50–2.03), vaginal bleeding during pregnancy (AOR = 1.45, 95% CI: 1.15–1.87) and history of recurrent miscarriage (≥ 3 abortions; AOR = 2.22, 95% CI: 1.72–2.86). Conversely, higher maternal education was associated with a protective effect against LBW. Conclusion Maternal VTE during pregnancy is a significant and independent risk factor for low birth weight likely mediated through impaired placental perfusion and inflammatory pathways. These findings underscore the need for early risk assessment, timely diagnosis and optimized management of thromboembolic disorders during pregnancy to improve neonatal outcomes. Further studies are warranted to explore mechanistic pathways and evaluate the impact of preventive anticoagulant interventions.

title: A Virtual Pulmonary Rehabilitation Program to Address Gaps in Pulmonary Rehabilitation: Retrospective Observational Study.
authorString: Beschloss A, Ostrovsky A.
abstractText:
Background

Traditional brick-and-mortar pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) programs remain substantially underused, with only 2.7% of Medicare beneficiaries completing PR within 12 months following hospitalization for a COPD exacerbation. Given the critical role of PR in improving exercise tolerance, quality of life, and reducing readmissions, innovative delivery models are needed to address this massive utilization gap. Virtual PR platforms have emerged as a potential solution, offering scalable, and home-based rehabilitation.

Objective

This study aimed to evaluate the impact of a novel virtual PR program on functional, psychosocial, and cardiometabolic outcomes among adults with COPD.

Methods

This retrospective observational study analyzed outcomes among patients enrolled in a structured, multidisciplinary virtual PR program between 2022 and 2024. Participants completed individualized exercise and education sessions remotely, supported by a multidisciplinary team including Physicians and Clinical Exercise Physiologists. Baseline and postprogram measures were compared using Cohen d to assess effect sizes across clinical domains. Primary outcomes included changes in maximum metabolic equivalents (METs), Duke Activity Status Index (DASI), and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) scores. Other measures included changes in blood pressure (systolic and diastolic), smoking status, and prevalence of hypertension.

Results

Among 2444 patients completing the program, the largest effect size improvements were observed in maximum METs achieved, DASI, and PHQ-9 scores. The program was also associated with decreased smoking rates and a lower prevalence of hypertension post intervention. Notably, 91% of the studied population self-identified as having a "fixed income," underscoring the potential for virtual PR to extend access to patients with lower incomes in the United States.

Conclusions

Virtual PR appears to be a promising and potentially more scalable alternative to traditional facility-based PR for patients with COPD. Significant improvements in exercise capacity, mood, and cardiovascular parameters suggest clinical benefit, while reductions in smoking and hypertension further highlight potential for broader health impact. Given the high proportion of participants on fixed incomes, virtual PR may represent an effective strategy to expand access and equity in chronic respiratory care delivery across the United States.

title: Association between urine protein-to-creatinine ratio and postpartum resistant hypertension in patients with severe preeclampsia: A retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Annicchiarico W, Gutiérrez Marin JH, Posada RAG, Castro DPC, Blair JES, Campo MNC.

journal.title: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics

abstractText:
Objective

Our objective was to investigate the association between elevated urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) and resistant hypertension during postpartum hospitalization in patients with severe preeclampsia at a tertiary care center in Colombia.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study was conducted in Medellín, Colombia. Patients aged >18 years diagnosed with severe preeclampsia who underwent UPCR assessment were included. Associations between elevated UPCR (≥0.3) and resistant hypertension during postpartum hospitalization were evaluated using robust Poisson regression models.

Results

A total of 261 patients were included in the study. Bivariate analysis showed that resistant hypertension in the postpartum period was more frequent in the UPCR ≥0.3 group than in the UPCR <0.3 group (43.2% vs. 12.7%; risk ratio 3.69; 95% confidence interval 1.92-7.07). After adjustment for maternal age, body mass index, and gestational age at diagnosis, elevated UPCR remained independently associated with resistant hypertension (adjusted risk ratio 4.87; 95% confidence interval 1.86-12.76). Earlier gestational age at diagnosis was also independently associated with resistant hypertension.

Conclusion

The UPCR is independently associated with the development of resistant hypertension during postpartum hospitalization in patients with severe preeclampsia.

title: Antecedent Kidney Function and Cardiovascular Mortality in Over 300 000 Patients With Incident Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
authorString: Karnib M, Selvaganesan P, Helmy I, Zakeri R, Saeed YB, Osman MN, Sahadevan J, Vest AR, Reddy YNV, Sundaram V.
abstractText:
Background

Chronic kidney disease is a frequent comorbidity in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and has been proposed as a contributor to its development. However, the spectrum of antecedent kidney function before incident HFpEF and its association with subsequent cardiovascular outcomes remains unclear.

Methods

We conducted a multicenter cohort study across 170 US Veterans Affairs hospitals, including patients with incident HFpEF diagnosed between January 1, 2000, and June 30, 2025. HFpEF was ascertained using natural language processing-derived left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50% closest to the incident HF date and a validated HFpEF algorithm incorporating loop diuretic use, elevated natriuretic peptide levels, and an HFpEF-age, body mass index, and atrial fibrillation score >0.5. Antecedent kidney function was classified using 2 estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) measurements obtained ≥90 days apart before incident HFpEF and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio. We characterized antecedent kidney function, including albuminuria (urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥30 mg/g), and examined its associations with 5-year cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization. Competing-risk analysis was performed accounting for noncardiovascular death as a competing event for cardiovascular death.

Results

Of 304 712 patients meeting HFpEF ascertainment criteria, 236 910 comprised the final cohort; 51% had antecedent eGFR ≥60 mL/min per 1.73m2. Overall, 15% had an eGFR ≥90 mL/min per 1.73m2. Patients with eGFR <60 mL/min per 1.73m2 were older and had more diabetes and hypertension. 51% of the patients with eGFR <60 mL/min per 1.73m2 had body mass index <30 kg/m2, including 20% with body mass index <25 kg/m2. Progressively lower antecedent kidney function was associated with graded increases in cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization. Among decedents, the proportion of deaths attributed to cardiovascular causes increased from 25% in the preserved eGFR (≥90 mL/min per 1.73m2) without documented albuminuria to 32% with albuminuria and 38% with advanced kidney dysfunction (P<0.001).

Conclusions

In this nationwide study of patients with incident HFpEF, antecedent kidney dysfunction was common but not uniformly present before HFpEF onset. Furthermore, among patients who developed HFpEF, antecedent kidney dysfunction identified a higher-risk phenotype, with progressively greater cardiovascular mortality and heart failure hospitalization with declining kidney function.

title: Exercise Right Atrial Stiffness From Pressure-Volume Loops and Prognosis in Pulmonary Hypertension.
authorString: Thal BR, Kremer NC, Janetzko P, Douschan P, Rako ZA, Bußmann L, Yogeswaran A, Alipour Symakani RS, Merkus D, Ghofrani HA, Seeger W, Olschewski H, Borlaug BA, Tello K.
abstractText:
Background

In pulmonary hypertension (PH), risk assessment focuses on right ventricular function and may overlook exercise-related right atrial (RA) functional limitation. We investigated whether RA stiffness during exercise reflects impaired right-heart filling reserve and is associated with prognosis beyond conventional measures.

Methods

We prospectively enrolled 68 participants in this observational study, including 42 with precapillary PH. Participants who had PH ruled out and patients with postcapillary PH formed reference groups. Participants underwent 3-dimensional echocardiography, right heart catheterization, and invasive RA pressure-volume loop analysis at rest and during standardized semisupine exercise. RA filling stiffness was derived from the reservoir phase. Patients with precapillary PH were stratified by median exercise RA filling stiffness.

Results

At rest, high- and low-stiffness groups had comparable right ventricular function, afterload, and cardiac index, but the high-stiffness group exhibited impaired phasic RA strain and venous congestion (median [interquartile range] liver stiffness, 7.1 [6.0-8.8] versus 5.2 [4.8-5.8] kPa; P=0.021). During exercise, mean RA pressure increased similarly, but the high-stiffness group had impaired peak cardiac index (3.3±1.0 versus 4.1±0.9 L/min per m2; P=0.015) and RA strain. Unlike resting RA stiffness, high exercise RA stiffness was independently associated with mortality (adjusted hazard ratio, 4.37 [95% CI, 1.20-15.96]). A model including RA conduit strain and right ventricular functional reserve discriminated high RA stiffness (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.90).

Conclusions

RA stiffness during exercise integrates resting congestion with limited cardiac reserve and unmasks mortality risk missed by resting metrics. RA conduit strain and right ventricular functional reserve noninvasively identify the high-stiffness subgroup.

title: Sleep and Cardiometabolic Disease: A Wearable-Electronic Health Record Study in the US All of Us Research Program.
authorString: Tran AK, Nguyen MTV.
abstractText: Background: Sleep health spans duration, quality, regularity, and timing, yet Life's Essential 8 scores sleep by duration alone, and regularity studies used about 1 week of data. How these dimensions, measured over months, relate to incident cardiometabolic disease is unknown, as is whether nightly sleep-cycle structure adds information. Methods: This cohort study included US adults in the All of Us Research Program with linked Fitbit and electronic health records (2009-2023). We derived 11 sleep metrics over a 180-day baseline (≥90 valid nights). Incident diagnoses, grouped into phecodes, were counted after a 180-day washout to limit reverse causation. Primary analyses related these metrics to prespecified endpoints, including a CVD composite (myocardial infarction, heart failure, cardiomyopathy, or ischemic stroke), heart failure, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes. Cox models adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, lifestyle, and comorbidity factors. Exploratory analyses examined wearable-estimated sleep cycles (7,199 participants; 1,017,812 sleep-stage nights). Results: Among 10,362 participants (median age, 53 years; 70% female), 230 developed the CVD composite (median follow-up, 3.7 years). Each 1-SD (29-minute) higher night-to-night variability in sleep duration was associated with higher CVD composite risk (hazard ratio, 1.24 [95% CI, 1.09-1.41]), as was higher variability in bedtime (1.23 [1.10-1.37]), waketime (1.20 [1.09-1.32]), and midpoint (1.21 [1.09-1.35]); mean sleep duration was not (0.96 [0.85-1.08]). Variability in sleep duration was also associated with heart failure (1.32 [1.13-1.55]), hypertension (1.16 [1.08-1.25]), and type 2 diabetes (1.20 [1.07-1.35]). More sleep cycles were associated with lower atrial arrhythmia risk (0.72 [0.58-0.89]), independent of sleep duration, regularity, and timing (0.58 [0.44-0.77]). Conclusions: Night-to-night irregularity in sleep duration and timing was associated with the CVD composite, heart failure, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes; mean duration was not associated with the CVD composite. More wearable-estimated sleep cycles were associated with lower atrial arrhythmia risk beyond conventional sleep metrics, a novel finding requiring confirmation.

title: Qi-Blood Harmony Formula mediates post-MI cardioprotection via FTO-driven dual modulation of energy metabolism and fibrosis: a multi-omics validation.
authorString: Xie X, Wang Y, Dong X, Yuan R, Miao Y, Li P, Wang Z, Zhu C, Zhao H, Hu L, Liu M, Li Z, Huang M, Ma S, Xin Q, Cong W, Chen K.
abstractText: Myocardial infarction (MI) remains a leading cause of death worldwide. Persistent myocardial fibrosis and dysregulated energy metabolism following MI contribute to adverse cardiac remodeling and are associated with poor clinical prognosis. Currently, no guideline-recommended therapy provides effective long-term intervention simultaneously targeting both of these core pathological mechanisms. The Qi-Blood Harmony Formula (QBHF), a classical Chinese herbal prescription, has demonstrated cardioprotective potential on attenuating fibrosis, preserving mitochondrial integrity, and restoring myocardial ATP levels in MI, yet its underlying mechanisms and therapeutic targets remain unclear. Using an integrated multi-omics approach in a mouse MI model, we showed that QBHF reactivated genes related to energy metabolism while suppressing pro-fibrotic pathways, as revealed by bulk RNA-sequencing. Non-targeted metabolomics further confirmed its efficacy in counteracting metabolic dysregulation. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing revealed that QBHF altered cardiac cellular composition characterized by reducing a major profibrotic fibroblast subpopulation and expanding a metabolically robust cardiomyocyte subset. Integrative multi-omics analysis identified the fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO) as a central regulatory hub modulated by QBHF across bulk heart tissue, fibroblasts, and cardiomyocytes. Crucially, heterozygous knockout of FTO in mice abolished QBHF-mediated improvements in cardiac fibrosis, ATP level and heart function. Consistently, FTO knockdown in cardiomyocytes blunted QBHF-induced ATP restoration. Together, these findings demonstrate that QBHF confers post-MI cardioprotection via FTO-driven dual modulation of energy metabolism and fibrosis. Our findings highlight FTO as a promising therapeutic target and provide novel mechanistic insights into traditional Chinese medicine-based interventions for post-MI injury.

title: Protective effect of gossypin against high-fat diet-induced atherosclerosis in rats: Role of the phosphoinositide 3-kinase/AKT/mechanistic target of rapamycin pathway and gut microbiota.
authorString: Wang Y, Kumar A, Lu F.
abstractText:
Background

Over the last decade, there has been a global prevalence of high morbidity and mortality associated with atherosclerotic disease. Gossypin exhibits the anti-inflammatory and protective effect against various disease. The current protocol demonstrated the antiatherosclerotic effect of gossypin against high-fat diet (HFD)-induced atherosclerosis (AS) in rats and explored the underlying mechanism.

Materials and methods

HFD and Vitamin D3 (600,000 IU/kg) were used to induce AS in rats, and the rats were treated with different doses of gossypin and rosuvastatin, respectively. Body weight, organ weights, inflammatory, cardiac, and lipid parameters, as well as micro-RNA (mRNA) expression, were estimated. The rat faces were collected for the determination of gut microbiota.

Results

Gossypin treatment markedly reduced body weight and altered organ weights. Gossypin treatment Remarkably modulated the level of cardiac parameters such as creatine kinase (CK), CK myocardial band, lactate dehydrogenase, cardiac troponin I, thromboxane B2, endothelin-1; lipid parameters such as total cholesterol (TC), triglycerides (TG), high density lipoprotein (HDL), low density lipoprotein (LDL), very LDL, TC/HDL, TG/HDL, free fatty acid; hepatic parameters, namely, alanine aminotransferase, aspartate aminotransferase, alkaline phosphatase; inflammatory parameters such as cyclooxygenase-2, inducible nitric oxide synthetase, C-reactive protein, prostaglandin E2, nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-κB); inflammatory cytokines include interleukin (IL)-1β, 6, 5, 10, 17, tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), C-X-C Motif chemokine ligand 1 (CXCL1), respectively. Gossypin treatment also altered the mRNA expression of intercellular adhesion molecule-1, vascular cell adhesion molecule-1, monocyte chemoattractant protein-1, ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA-1), liver X receptor-α, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ, toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3, NF-κBp65, myeloid differentiation primary response 88, IL-1 β, IL-6, IL-17, TNF-α, phosphorylated AMP-activated protein kinase, phosphorylated mechanistic target of rapamycin (p-mTOR), phosphorylated phosphoinositide 3-kinase (p-PI3K), and phosphorylated protein kinase B (p-AKT), respectively. Gossypin treatment remarkably modulated the abundance of Firmicutes, Bacteroidetes, F/B ratio, deferribacteraceae and cyanobacteria.

Conclusion

Gossypin exhibited the anti-AS effect through alteration of PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway and gut microbiota.

title: Respiratory self-similarity is a sleep apnea endotype that predicts cardiovascular disease related mortality.
authorString: Ni YN, Oppersma E, Ganglberger W, Thomas RJ.
abstractText:
Study objectives

Pathological respiratory chemoreflex activation (high loop gain) in sleep apnea may activate the carotid body and induce excessive sympathetic nerve output, and independently add to the risk of adverse outcomes. This study aims to determine whether a high loop gain of the respiratory control system during sleep, estimated by respiratory self-similarity (SS) and the algorithm-derived central respiratory event index (CREI), is associated with new-onset cardiovascular disease (CVD) and CVD-related mortality.

Methods

A secondary analysis of The Sleep Heart Health Study (SHHS) and Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA). High SS% and CREI were defined as the highest quartile. Lasso regression and restricted cubic spline assessed the relationship between SS%, CREI and CVD, CVD-mortality and all-cause mortality. A cumulative incidence function and a Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard model were used to evaluate this outcome accounting for competing risks.

Results

In adjusted models with age as a categorical variable divided by 65 years old, the highest quartile of SS% (HR 1.693, p: 0.017 in MESA and HR 1.240, p : 0.009 in SHHS) was associated with the incidence of CVD and was more prominent in males. A positive relationship between SS% (MESA: HR 1.429, p: 0.039; SHHS HR1.176, p:0.018 ) for the continuous metrics and CVD mortality in both cohorts was more apparent in men than in women. The categorical high-exposure association with CVD mortality was not consistent across cohorts.The associations were significantly attenuated when adjusted by age as a continuous metric.

Conclusions

An endotype of sleep apnea reflecting high loop gain is associated with CVD and CVD mortality, especially in males.

title: Nanoparticle-Mediated Therapies for Atherosclerosis: A Novel Approach to Targeted Treatment.
authorString: Rangnekar T, Londhe V.
abstractText:
Introduction

Atherosclerosis(AS) remains a leading cause of global cardiovascular mortality due to the formation of lipid rich plaques and chronic vascular inflammation. Conventional therapies, including statins, antiplatelet agents and surgical interventions, primarily control risk factors by preventing new plaque deposits but show limited ability to selectively target inflamed vascular sites.

Objective

This review critically evaluates current advances in nanoparticle mediated drug delivery for atherosclerosis, with emphasis on mechanistic targeting of inflamed plaques, modulation of macrophage driven inflammatory and oxidative pathways within the diseased vascular microenvironment. This review also highlights comparative analysis of major nanoparticle systems, integration of theranostic functionalities for simultaneous molecular imaging and therapy. The translational barriers are also addressed to enable clinical implementation.Significance of Review: Despite advancements in lipid-lowering and anti-inflammatory drugs, current atherosclerosis treatments are limited by inadequate plaque specificity, rapid systemic clearance, off-target toxicity, and persistent cardiovascular risk. Nanoparticle based systems can solve these problems with simultaneous diagnosis and therapy, thereby addressing major unmet clinical needs.Key Findings: Different types of nanoparticles demonstrate promising therapeutic outcomes by modulating macrophage activity, reducing oxidative stress, enabling controlled drug release and improving plaque imaging. Theranostic nanoparticles further allow simultaneous diagnosis and treatment. However, large-scale manufacturing, nanotoxicology and regulatory constraints continue to hinder clinical translation.

Conclusions

Nanoparticle-mediated therapies represent a transformative approach for atherosclerosis by enabling precision, targeted and multifunctional treatment. Continued optimization of safety, scalability and regulatory compliance will be essential for successful clinical adoption and improved patient outcomes.

title: Urinary Metals, Soluble Urokinase Plasminogen Activator Receptor, and Outcomes in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
authorString: Ghazzal BZ, Ismail A, Farhat T, Huang Y, Blakely P, Schilling K, Glabonjat R, Sanchez TR, Martinez-Morata I, McGraw K, Domingo-Relloso A, Navas-Acien A, Heckbert SR, Hayek SS.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Environmental metal exposure is associated with cardiovascular disease (CVD) and mortality, potentially through inflammation. Soluble urokinase plasminogen activator receptor (suPAR), a stable marker of immune activation associated with CVD and death, may capture this pathway. We examined associations of urinary metals with suPAR and whether suPAR-associated components were present in cadmium-outcome associations.

Methods

In the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis, we studied 5,148 adults free of clinical CVD (2000-2002). We estimated associations of 11 creatinine-standardized urinary metals with serum suPAR by linear regression (per interquartile-range [IQR] increase), compared associations across suPAR, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and D-dimer, and used VanderWeele 4-way decomposition to estimate suPAR-associated indirect components of cadmium associations with all-cause mortality and four adjudicated cardiovascular outcomes.

Results

Of 11 metals, 7 were associated with suPAR; cadmium showed the strongest association (7.99% higher suPAR per IQR; 95% CI, 6.14-9.87) followed by cobalt, copper, molybdenum, tungsten, and zinc, whereas barium was inversely associated. The association was monotonic and persisted among never-smokers (5.54%; 95% CI, 3.03-8.11). Over a median 14.7 years, higher urinary cadmium was associated with all-cause mortality (Q4-vs-Q1 hazard ratio, 1.43; 95% CI, 1.18-1.74); the suPAR-associated proportion was 0.30 (95% CI, 0.13-0.47).

Conclusions

Cadmium showed a larger association with suPAR than with hs-CRP, IL-6, or D-dimer. An exploratory decomposition identified a suPAR-associated component of this association. Findings for cardiovascular outcomes were directionally consistent but not definitive. suPAR-related immune activation is a candidate pathway linking cadmium to mortality, warranting longitudinal and mechanistic confirmation.

title: Evaluating the SVS 90-Minute Door-to-Intervention Target for Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm: A Single-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Narayanan N, Horne SJ, Seeburrun R.
abstractText:
Introduction

Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms (rAAAs) are a life-threatening condition requiring rapid surgical intervention for survival. Guidelines from the Society of Vascular Surgery in 2018 advised a door-to-intervention time of ≤90 minutes. We hypothesised that door-to-intervention time would not predict outcomes following rAAA repair, as treatment timelines may reflect differences in physiological severity, diagnostic assessment and operative modality, including the use of EVAR.

Methods

This was a retrospective cohort study of 29 patients presenting to University Hospitals Plymouth (UHP) who underwent surgical intervention for rAAA between February 2018 and December 2024. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients achieving the SVS-recommended door-to-intervention time of ≤90 minutes. Secondary outcomes were the rates of endovascular repair (EVAR) compared to open repair and the associated mortality and morbidity.

Results

Twenty-nine patients were included, of whom only three (10.3%) met the SVS target. Median door-to-intervention time was 182 minutes. Arrival-to-diagnosis time was associated with the greatest delay, with a median time of 84 minutes. Twenty-three patients (79.3%) underwent open repair, with a 60.9% (14/23) mortality rate compared to 16.7% (1/6) for EVAR cases. Shorter door-to-intervention time was associated with higher 30-day mortality, although no association was observed with overall mortality. Morbidity rates were 95.6% (22/23) for open cases and 50.0% (3/6) for EVAR cases. No statistically significant association was identified between overall morbidity rates and door-to-intervention time. However, higher grade complications were statistically significantly associated with both shorter arrival to diagnosis time (p=0.011) and shorter arrival to knife-to-skin time (p=0.039).

Conclusions

89.7% (26/29) of rAAAs presenting to UHP between February 2018 and December 2024 exceeded the recommended SVS door-to-intervention target of <90 minutes. Shorter timelines were observed among patients with higher grade complications and who subsequently died. Mortality was higher following open repair.

title: The Impact of Clinical and Biochemical Frailty on Outcomes following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
authorString: Butala AD, Hogarty J, Nanayakkara S, Bloom J, Palmer S, Noaman S, McGaw D, Blusztein D, Johnston R, Gardner E, Gartner E, Pedetti J, Htun NM, Kaye DM, Walton AS, Stub D.
abstractText:
Background

Frailty results from declining reserve and function and is a modifiable cardiovascular risk-factor. Despite this, there is limited evidence surrounding its role in lower-risk TAVR cohorts.

Objectives

This study aimed to evaluate frailty among contemporary TAVR patients, delineate the impact of biochemical and clinical frailty, and understand its additive value to existing risk-prediction tools.

Methods

Analysis of a multicenter Australian registry. Biochemical frailty (BF) was defined as serum albumin <35 g/L and clinical frailty (CF) as a Rockwood Clinical Frailty Scale ≥5. Patients meeting BF or CF criteria were categorized as frail.

Results

Of the 2,661 patients, the median age 82 (IQR: 77-86), 60% male, and median STS 3.3 (2-5.2), 920 patients (35%) were considered frail. A total of 171 (19%) of frail patients fulfilled both BF and CF criteria. The frail group was older (83 vs 81, P < 0.001), more females (43% vs 38%; P = 0.016) with higher STS scores (4 vs 3, P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed a stepwise increase in 12-month mortality with increasing frailty (no frailty 4% vs BF or CF 7% vs BF + CF 16%, Log-rank P < 0.001). In Cox proportional hazards regression BF or CF (adjusted HR: 1.6; 95% CI: 1.0-2.4; P = 0.033) and BF + CF (adjusted HR: 3.3; 95% CI: 1.9-5.6; P < 0.001) independently predicted 12-month mortality. Addition of frailty to STS Score improved mortality prediction (area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve: 0.608 vs 0.664; DeLong's P = 0.021), with Shapley analysis demonstrating significant contribution from frailty.

Conclusions

Frailty is common with significant implications in TAVR. Patients with biochemical and clinical frailty criteria are highest risk. Development of strategies to address frailty is critical.

title: Clinical and economic burden of major lower-limb amputations attributable to peripheral artery disease in Italy: A nationwide analysis.
authorString: Scortichini M, Gargiulo M, Manzi M, Uccioli L, Sciattella P.
abstractText: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) represents a major cause of non-traumatic lower-limb amputation and is associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Despite advances in medical and revascularization therapies, major amputations remain frequent, and comprehensive nationwide estimates of their clinical and hospital-related economic burden within the Italian National Health Service (SSN) are limited. The objectives of this study were to estimate the hospital-related economic burden of major lower-limb amputations attributable to PAD in Italy and to assess revascularization patterns and in-hospital mortality within the SSN. We conducted a nationwide observational study using the Italian National Hospital Discharge Database. Acute hospital discharges between 2015 and 2021 with a major lower-limb amputation and Diagnosis Related Group 113 were identified. Inpatient volumes, length of stay, and costs were estimated by amputation level. A longitudinal cohort of patients amputated between 2015 and 2017 was followed for two years before and after the index hospitalization to assess prior revascularization and in-hospital mortality using age- and sex-adjusted Cox models. A total of 26,417 PAD-attributable major amputations were identified, 75.6% of which were above-knee procedures. Cumulative inpatient expenditure reached €294 million, corresponding to over 511,000 hospital days. Only 46.0% of patients underwent revascularization before amputation. In-hospital mortality increased steeply within the first six months post-amputation and remained higher after above-knee procedures and among patients with diabetes, reaching 16-25% at 180 days and 23-34% at two years. Major lower-limb amputation remains a severe and costly outcome of PAD in Italy. Improved implementation of guideline-recommended PAD management is needed to reduce avoidable amputations and their economic burden on the SSN.

title: Acquired Gerbode Defect After TAVR Presenting With Severe Acute Liver and Kidney Injury.
authorString: Jadav RS, Tuttle M, Neerukonda S, John A.
abstractText:
Background

Acquired Gerbode defects after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) are rare and may present atypically, delaying diagnosis.

Case summary

A 71-year-old man presented 15 days after TAVR with severe acute liver and kidney injury despite preserved ventricular systolic function and normal prosthetic valve function on transthoracic echocardiography. Right heart catheterization revealed elevated filling pressures, an oxygen saturation step-up from the superior vena cava (51%) to the pulmonary artery (79%), and a pulmonary/systemic flow ratio of 2.9. Transesophageal echocardiography identified a high-pressure left ventricular-to-right atrial shunt through the membranous septum. Residual shunting after transcatheter closure caused severe intravascular hemolysis and necessitated surgical salvage. The postoperative course was complicated by multiorgan failure and death.

Discussion

This case highlights an atypical presentation of an acquired Gerbode defect. Complementary transesophageal echocardiography and invasive hemodynamic assessment were essential for diagnosis.

Take-home message

Occult intracardiac shunting should be considered after TAVR when severe end-organ dysfunction is discordant with reassuring transthoracic echocardiographic findings.

title: Transcatheter coil embolization for proximal thoracic aortic pseudoaneurysms: a case series with mid-term clinical and imaging follow-up.
authorString: Di Marco L, Piperata A, Snaidero S, Cocozza MA, Attinà D, Deniku M, Lovato L, Pacini D, Buia F.
abstractText:
Objectives

Proximal aortic pseudoaneurysms represent a life-threatening complication of cardiac surgery. Traditional redo surgery is associated with substantial operative risk, while conventional endovascular stenting is often precluded by complex anatomy. We evaluated the clinical feasibility, safety, and durability of transcatheter coil embolization for proximal aortic pseudoaneurysms in a high-risk cohort.

Methods

Between September 2020 and February 2024, nine consecutive high-risk patients with proximal aortic pseudoaneurysms underwent transcatheter coil embolization at our institution. Preoperative risk profiles, procedural characteristics, intra-hospital outcomes, and serial computed tomography angiography follow-up datasets were retrospectively analyzed.

Results

The cohort was predominantly male (88.9%), with a mean age of 69.1±13 years and a mean Logistic EuroSCORE of 22.82%±18.76%. Patients had undergone a mean of 2.56 previous aortic procedures. Access routes included transfemoral (n = 6), transapical (n = 3), axillary (n = 1), and transbrachial (n = 1) approaches. Stent-assisted embolization was deployed in two cases. Technical success was achieved in all cases, with a median post-procedural stay of six days. Mean follow-up was 16±14.8 months. Serial imaging demonstrated stable sac dimensions in all patients, with no local recurrences. All-cause mortality was 33.3% (n = 3), and all deaths were attributed to sudden systemic events unrelated to target lesion failure or rupture.

Conclusions

Transcatheter coil embolization appears to be a safe, technically feasible, and durable alternative for the exclusion of proximal aortic pseudoaneurysms. In this small high-risk cohort, the technique achieved excellent local control and mid-term structural stability in fragile, multi-operated patients who were not candidates for conventional open surgery.

title: Restitution properties during ventricular fibrillation and the effects of cardiac pacing location on ventricular electrophysiology in the rabbit heart.
authorString: Roper-Jones B, Allen E, Sutcliffe RL, Ng GA, Chauhan RA.
abstractText: Sudden cardiac death is a cause of mortality due to malignant arrhythmias such as ventricular fibrillation (VF). Although action potential duration (APD) restitution is a method to assess arrhythmic susceptibility, repolarisation may depend on prior activation history, a phenomenon known as cardiac memory. Cardiac memory describes the persistence of repolarisation effects from previous beats, such that APD reflects not only the immediately preceding diastolic interval (DI) but also earlier activation effects. This may be relevant during VF, where continuously varying activation patterns prevent a steady electrophysiological state. This study investigated how pacing location affects ventricular electrophysiology and whether repolarisation during VF exhibits short-term cardiac memory. Langendorff-perfused rabbit hearts were used to record monophasic action potentials from the left ventricular apex and base. Pacing was conducted from five sites. Steady-state APD was assessed during constant pacing. Effective refractory period (ERP), APD restitution and conduction time restitution (CTR) were assessed using an S<sub>1</sub>-S<sub>2</sub> extra-stimulus protocol (S<sub>1</sub>, conditioning stimuli; S<sub>2</sub>, premature extra-stimulus). Additionally, APD-DI and APD-APD relationships were analysed during early VF. Pacing location significantly influenced S<sub>1</sub> and S<sub>2</sub> conduction delays, consistent with site-dependent activation timing. However, steady-state APD, ERP and CTR were not significantly affected by pacing location. In contrast, during VF, APD exhibited a significant dependence on preceding DI and preceding APD over approximately the first 30 beats, with these relationships progressively deteriorating thereafter. These findings demonstrate that while pacing location alters activation timing, repolarisation dynamics under stable activation histories are robust. During VF, continuously changing activation patterns unmask short-term cardiac memory.

title: Flow dynamics and systemic arterial stiffness distinguish bicuspid aortic valve aortopathy from heritable thoracic aortic disease.
authorString: Segura-Rodríguez D, Morales-García M, Moreno-Escobar E, Martín de la Fuente P, Burillo Gómez F, Miras Gómez JA, Pérez Cuenca E, Uribe I, García-Orta R.
abstractText:
Aims

Bicuspid aortic valve-associated aortopathy (BAVA) and heritable thoracic aortic disease (HTAD) share clinical manifestations but may represent distinct pathophysiological entities. We aimed to compare morphological and haemodynamic profiles between both groups using cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) and non-invasive systemic haemodynamic assessment.

Methods and results

A total of 185 patients (111 BAVA, 74 HTAD) were prospectively enrolled. CMR 4D-flow assessed aortic distensibility (ADCMR), pulse wave velocity (PWVCMR), global wall shear stress (WSSCMR) and energy loss (ELCMR). Oscillometry assessed systemic PWVM, augmentation index (AIxM) and systemic vascular resistance (SVRM). Composite adverse aortic events (AAE) comprised acute aortic syndrome, cardiovascular death or guideline diameter-based indication for surgery over 42.1±17.6 months. BAVA showed greater tubular ascending aorta and sinotubular junction dilation, ascending aorta WSSCMR (0.42±0.18 vs 0.28±0.12 Pa, p=0.020), ELCMR (19.8±8.4 vs. 12.3±6.1 mW, p<0.001) and ADCMR (6.1 ± 3.5 vs. 4.8 ± 2.9 ×10-3 mmHg-1, p=0.023), yet lower systemic stiffness than HTAD (PWVM 6.2±1.7 vs 7.8±2.1 m/s; AIxM 12.1±7.6 vs 18.4±9.2%; both p<0.001). AAE rates were similar. In exploratory aetiology-specific analyses, ascending aorta WSSCMR was associated with events in BAVA (HR 8.92, 95% CI 2.85-27.95) and systemic PWVM in HTAD (HR 2.16, 95% CI 1.30-3.57).

Conclusion

BAVA and HTAD show distinct morphological and haemodynamic phenotypes: BAVA with focal dilation, elevated WSSCMR/ELCMR and preserved systemic function; HTAD with reduced local distensibility and greater systemic stiffness. These aetiology-specific predictors are exploratory and require external validation.

title: ACHD Care Wheel: A Stakeholder- and Theory-Driven Framework to Improve Specialized Adult Congenital Heart Disease Care.
authorString: Agarwal A, Macholl K, Qian A, Mehta J, Ahuja P, Buenrostro K, Sun K, Dohan D, Gurvitz M, Okumura MJ.
abstractText: Background: Patients with adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) experience significant gaps in guideline-recommended care, associated with higher morbidity and mortality compared to those without care gaps. We evaluated barriers and facilitators to specialized care to inform patient-centered solutions. Methods: We purposively sampled ACHD patients and clinicians from UCSF and across the United States and conducted semi-structured interviews in 2023-2024. Patients were ≥18 years, spoke English or Spanish, and could provide informed consent; clinicians were cardiologists or other staff involved in ACHD care. Zoom interviews were conducted using Capability, Opportunity, Motivation, and Behavior (COM-B)-informed guides and were recorded, professionally transcribed, and translated when applicable. Data were analyzed using inductive coding and rapid qualitative analysis, with independent dual coding, consensus resolution, concurrent analysis, and member checking. Identified categories were subsequently mapped to the Theoretical Domains Framework and COM-B. Results: We interviewed 54 participants (37 patients, 17 clinicians). For patients, the median age was 32 years; 57% were women, 62% were people of color, and 35% had gaps in care of ≥3 years. Findings were organized into six interdependent categories: healthcare system and institutional structure; knowledge and education; sources of support; personal development; identity and personal resources; and ACHD's placement in one's life. Two novel findings emerged: a paradoxical facilitating role of parental language barriers and the complex impact of caregiver support on patients' independent care skills. We developed the ACHD Care Wheel, a theory-guided framework to support the design and evaluation of future interventions. Conclusions: The ACHD Care Wheel is a stakeholder-derived, theory-grounded framework for developing and evaluating interventions to improve ACHD care. Interventions targeting the three priority categories (healthcare system and institutional structure, knowledge and education, and sources of support) are likely to produce effects across multiple domains simultaneously, offering a theoretically grounded path forward for this growing population.

title: Sustained Improvement in Interstage Survival and Outcomes Within the National Pediatric Cardiology Quality Improvement Collaborative.
authorString: Van Bergen AH, Kuhnell P, Brown DW, Lannon CM, Rudd NA, Anderson JB, Bates KE.
abstractText:
Background

Infants with hypoplastic left heart syndrome remain at high risk during the interstage between stage 1 and stage 2 surgical palliations. As a multicenter Learning Health Network, the National Pediatric Cardiology Quality Improvement Collaborate uses collaborative research and improvement to improve hypoplastic left heart syndrome outcomes for infants. We evaluated whether our previously reported improvement in interstage survival from 90.5% to 94.8% was sustained over time.

Methods

Infants enrolled in the National Pediatric Cardiology Quality Improvement Collaborate clinical registry who underwent stage 1 surgical palliation and were discharged home during the interstage period were included. Patient demographics, hypoplastic left heart syndrome anatomic type, and neonatal hospitalization data in phase 1 (2008-2016) and phase 2 (2016-2025) were compared. Statistical process control was used to analyze rates of interstage survival, major adverse event readmissions, and growth failure.

Results

A total of 5495 patients (phase 1-2199, phase 2-3296) were enrolled from 77 centers, of which 38.7% were female and 11.2% had a major syndrome. The phase 2 cohort had a higher prevalence of RV-PA conduit (phase 1: 55.2% versus phase 2: 64.3%; P<0.001), lower median NEONATE score (9 versus 3; P<0.001), higher digoxin prescription (28.9% versus 74.7%; P<0.001), and longer median length of stay compared with phase 1 (28 versus 34 days; P<0.001). Improvement in interstage survival noted in phase 1 was sustained throughout phase 2 at 94.8%. Major adverse event readmissions declined early in phase 2 and were maintained (1.74 versus 0.9/100 interstage patients). Adequate growth was statistically different but clinically stable over time (mean weight Z score at stage 2 admission -1.5 versus -1.42; P<0.019).

Conclusions

National Pediatric Cardiology Quality Improvement Collaborate sustained significant improvements in interstage outcomes through continued adherence to improvement processes, collaborative learning, and promoting best practices over time, including utilization of digoxin and NEONATE score.

title: Long-term follow-up of adolescents with white coat hypertension: a preliminary exploratory study.
authorString: Mitoraj K, Koziej J, Pilip J, Sikorski M, Pac M, Skoczyński K, Podymniak-Grzeszykowska M, Wierzbicka-Rucińska A, Lewandowska W, Dereziński T, Świąder-Leśniak A, Świderska M, Feber J, Litwin M, Obrycki Ł.
abstractText: White coat hypertension (WCH) in youth has traditionally been considered benign, but it may precede sustained hypertension (SH) and cardiovascular remodelling. We evaluated long-term blood pressure (BP) outcomes and hypertension-mediated organ damage in adolescents with WCH. This preliminary exploratory cohort study included 34 adolescents with WCH and 24 normotensive controls followed for median periods of 8.5 and 7.7 years. Clinical, biochemical, echocardiographic, vascular, and ambulatory BP monitoring (ABPM) assessments were performed at baseline and follow-up. At follow-up, 13 participants with WCH (38.2%) progressed to SH, 2 (5.9%) maintained WCH, and 19 (55.9%) became normotensive; no control developed SH. Participants who progressed had higher baseline ambulatory systolic BP (SBP; 124 vs 119 mmHg, p = 0.004) and pulse pressure (PP; 55 vs 49 mmHg, p = 0.01), while office BP was similar. At follow-up, office BP, ambulatory SBP (131 vs 118 mmHg, p = 0.001), PP (60 vs 45 mmHg, p = 0.003), central SBP (126 vs 121 mmHg, p = 0.032), and augmentation pressure (7 vs 4 mmHg, p = 0.009) were higher in the SH group. Most biochemical parameters, carotid intima-media thickness, and pulse wave velocity were similar between groups. More than one-third of adolescents with WCH progressed to SH. Higher baseline ambulatory SBP and PP may identify those at greater risk. These preliminary findings support individualized, risk-stratified surveillance, with closer ABPM follow-up for adolescents with higher-normal ambulatory BP, wider PP, excess adiposity, persistent office BP elevation, or other cardiovascular risk factors.

title: Challenges and innovations in cardiac AAV gene delivery as a platform for cardiac regeneration.
authorString: Kabboul G, Izurieta Muñoz A, Bishawi M, Doering CB, Levit RD.
abstractText: Gene therapies are at the forefront of potential treatments for cardiovascular diseases, but clinical translation remains limited by poor myocardial access and retention, systemic distribution, and immune-mediated toxicities. Heavily underexplored, the route of administration dictates efficacy and safety, ultimately influencing therapeutic outcomes. This review addresses the role of delivery in overcoming these challenges in cardiac adeno-associated viral therapies. Emphasis is placed on biomaterial-based delivery approaches to improve therapeutic outcomes.

title: Real-time XR-based 6-DOF catheter tracking enhances cardiac intervention navigation efficiency and depth perception.
authorString: Annabestani M, Sriram S, Kuzemczak A, Wong SC, Sigaras A, Mosadegh B.
abstractText: Despite advances in 3D ultrasound, most percutaneous cardiac interventions still rely on 2D visualization, limiting depth perception and spatial understanding. To address this challenge, we developed an Extended Reality (XR)-based platform that enables real-time six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) catheter tracking and visualization within a patient-specific 3D heart model. The system combines a custom machine-vision algorithm for 5-DOF catheter tracking with a 3D-printed electromechanical encoder that measures catheter roll, providing complete 6-DOF motion reconstruction. In a proof-of-concept study, 20 novice medical students navigated an intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) catheter to six anatomical targets using either immersive 3D visualization or a conventional 2D cathlab-style view. Participants in the 3D condition completed the task in 54.6 seconds and traveled 1939 mm on average, compared with 263.5 seconds and 7854 mm in the 2D condition. The ratio of cohort means was 4.8× for completion time and 4.1× for travel length (means of subject-level ratios: 5.1× and 4.9×). The 3D mode also produced more direct and less variable approach trajectories. Participants consistently rated immersive visualization higher for accuracy, speed, usability, and clinical value. Exploratory kinematic analysis suggested that 3D users distributed motion more evenly along the depth axis, whereas 2D users relied more on lateral and vertical adjustments. These findings demonstrate that XR-based visualization can substantially improve procedural training efficiency and motor control.

title: [Continuous glucose monitoring in diabetes: Clinical practice guidelines for primary care from SEMERGEN, RedGDPS, semFYC, SEMG and FAECAP].
authorString: Cebrián Cuenca AM, Barrot de la Puente J, Álvarez Hermida ÁB, Egocheaga Cabello MI, Cuatrecasas Cambra G, Arranz Martínez E, Mingorance Cruz N, Navarro Pérez J, de la Cuadra-Grande A, Grupo de Consenso.
abstractText: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) is a key tool for diabetes management in primary care (PC), as it provides dynamic and detailed information on glycemic control. This document summarizes scientific evidence and formulates clinical practice recommendations to optimize the use of CGM in people with diabetes (PwD) managed in PC. The recommendations are based on a Delphi involving 58 PC professionals representing SEMERGEN, redGDPS, semFYC, SEMG and FAECAP; and address the management of GCM within a framework of shared decision-making with PwD, including its indication, prescription, initiation, monitoring, and discontinuation. The integration of CGM into clinical practice in PC, along with adequate training for healthcare professionals and structured PwD education, can improve clinical, PwD-centered outcomes and the efficiency of the healthcare system.

title: Complementary Yield of Gene Panel Testing and ACMG SF v3.3 Screening for Cardiovascular Disease in a Korean Cohort.
authorString: You J, Jung LY, Lee SH, Park J.
abstractText: Inherited arrhythmia syndromes and cardiomyopathies are genetically heterogeneous, and clinical exome sequencing (CES) for unrelated indications increasingly yields cardiovascular secondary findings (SFs) under the ACMG SF v3.3 list. We compared, at a single Korean centre, phenotype-directed cardiac gene panel testing with opportunistically ascertained cardiovascular SFs. Forty patients with suspected inherited arrhythmia or cardiomyopathy underwent a 19-gene arrhythmia or 173-gene cardiomyopathy panel with AI-assisted, manually reviewed variant classification; separately, 288 patients undergoing CES for unrelated indications were screened for ACMG SF v3.3 cardiovascular pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants. A phenotype-concordant pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant was found in 8/40 patients (20.0%), including a recurrent KCNQ1 p.Arg231His variant in two unrelated infants and a MYBPC3 variant upgraded to pathogenic by co-segregation in a mother-son pair. Among the 288 exome-sequenced patients, 17 reportable cardiovascular SFs occurred in 16 (5.6%), predominantly dilated cardiomyopathy (n = 7, mostly TTN) and familial hypercholesterolaemia (n = 6, including a recurrent PCSK9 p.Glu32Lys variant in three patients). The two approaches sampled largely non-overlapping gene categories and are complementary rather than competing; recurrent, population-specific variants underscore the need for population-informed interpretation and structured counselling in cardiovascular genetic diagnosis.

title: Clinical and Genetic Characterization of a Patient With EED-Related Overgrowth Syndrome.
authorString: Shahilooy A, Gibson WT, Heydari S, Kiani M, Roshanaie AM, Moazzeni HR, Chaleshtori ARS.
abstractText: Cohen-Gibson syndrome (COGIS) is a rare genetic disorder caused by heterozygous pathogenic variants in EED. As the COGIS phenotypic spectrum remains incompletely characterized, additional cases help refine understanding of the condition. We evaluated a 37-year-old man with EED-related COGIS features, including overgrowth and intellectual disability. Genetic workup included karyotyping, FMR1 CGG-repeat expansion testing, whole-exome sequencing, and a familial segregation analysis, which identified the previously reported heterozygous pathogenic variant NM_003797.5:c.772C>T:p.His258Tyr. Clinical findings and medical history were recorded; birth parameters were obtained retrospectively from parental report due to lack of official documentation. Echocardiography revealed mild mitral valve regurgitation, alongside features uncommon in previously reported patients-normal adult weight, a long face, normal head circumference, normally spaced eyes, camptodactyly, no history of cryptorchidism, and a normal gait. Notably, the patient's father carried the same variant with reduced Sanger peak height, suggesting possible mosaicism. This case highlights potential phenotypic variability in COGIS, including the cardiac finding warranting further study, and underscores the implications of suspected paternal mosaicism for genetic counseling. Further quantitative assessment of mosaicism and cardiac evaluation in future studies could help better define the clinical spectrum of COGIS.

title: China-PAR-based cardiovascular risk assessment in East Shenzhen using Biossays homocysteine and lipid assays: A prospective cross-sectional and retrospective study.
authorString: Chen L, Zhang B, Xie G, Chen C, Shi M, Fan R, Chen Y, Zhang L, Zhang L, Chen S, Fang Z, Yang S.

journal.title: The Journal of international medical research

abstractText: ObjectiveHypertension and dyslipidemia are two well-established risk factors for cardiovascular disease. This study aimed to evaluate the analytical performance of homocysteine and lipid assays, estimate the 10-year cardiovascular disease risk among individuals with hypertension, and determine the proportions of hyperhomocysteinemia-type hypertension and dyslipidemia in a hospital-based population in East Shenzhen, China.MethodsThe analytical performances of the Biossays homocysteine, total cholesterol, triglycerides, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol assays were evaluated according to the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute documents. A cross-sectional hypertension cohort comprising 400 eligible participants was recruited from Pingshan People's Hospital between April 2024 and April 2025 to assess the risk of cardiovascular disease and prevalence of hyperhomocysteinemia-type hypertension. Additionally, a retrospective analysis was performed involving 55,575 unique individuals with complete lipid data identified from the hospital laboratory database in 2024, following the exclusion of participants with incomplete and duplicate records, to assess the proportion of participants with dyslipidemia.ResultsThe Biossays homocysteine and lipid assays demonstrated satisfactory precision, trueness, sensitivity, and linearity. The 10-year cardiovascular disease risk, based in the Prediction for Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease Risk in China, differed across ages but not across sexes. The proportions of individuals with hypertension and hyperhomocysteinemia, defined as homocysteine levels ≥10 μmol/L and ≥15 μmol/L, were 85.50% (342) and 33.75% (135), respectively, with no difference in the risk distribution between the two criteria. At least one abnormal lipid parameter was observed in 68.00% (272) of the participants in the hypertension cohort and in 62.35% (34,651) of individuals from the annual laboratory dataset.ConclusionsThe Biossays homocysteine and lipid assays demonstrated satisfactory analytical performance. Among individuals with hypertension, the estimated 10-year cardiovascular disease risk differed across ages but not between sexes, and hyperhomocysteinemia was frequently observed. Lipid abnormalities were also common in the hospital-based population. These findings may support cardiovascular risk assessment and preventive management in similar clinical populations.

title: Dynamic Fractional Myocardial Blood Volume Mapping Using Ferumoxytol-enhanced CMR Multitasking with Subspace Dose Harmonization.
authorString: Coudert TA, Pogosyan A, Ming Z, Finn JP, Christodoulou AG, Nguyen KL.

journal.title: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance

abstractText: Fractional myocardial blood volume (fMBV) represents the vascular compartment within myocardial tissue and may reflect changes in microvascular status and health. Conventionally derived from multi-dose Modified Look-Locker Inversion (MOLLI) recovery T1 mapping with ferumoxytol, MOLLI-based fMBV requires repeated breath-holds, inter-dose image registration, and static end-diastolic estimates. CMR Multitasking enables free-breathing, non-electrocardiogram (ECG)-gated imaging and offers a subspace that captures shared motion and contrast dynamics. This subspace representation can be exploited to harmonize multi-dose acquisitions directly in parameter space, enabling motion-resolved dynamic fMBV mapping while reducing reliance on post-hoc image-space registration. Thirteen healthy volunteers (11 females, 28.2±10.0 years) and twelve ischemic heart disease (IHD) patients (1 female, 67.2±7.1 years) underwent multi-dose ferumoxytol imaging at 3.0T using both breath-held ECG-triggered 5(3)3(3)3 MOLLI and free-running 2-dimensional Multitasking T1 mapping sequences. MOLLI-Multitasking agreement was assessed in healthy volunteers; patient data were used for exploratory dynamic fMBV analysis. Multitasking data were harmonized across respiratory- and cardiac-motion subspace dimensions for cross-dose alignment. Pixel-wise fMBV was estimated using a two-compartment water exchange model. fMBV agreement with MOLLI was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis. Dynamic fMBV changes were also evaluated from the Multitasking data. In IHD patients, fMBV kinetic metrics (upslope and diastolic-to-systolic distribution) for cycle-dependent variation in dynamic fMBV were computed to assess systolic compression and diastolic recoil. Cardiac positron emission tomography (PET) derived perfusion and CMR-derived strain and late gadolinium enhancement served as references. In healthy volunteers, Multitasking produced motion-resolved fMBV maps with strong MOLLI agreement (bias -0.11%, p=0.84). Subspace harmonization reduced cross-dose variability and aligned cardiac phases. Healthy subjects showed significant diastolic-to-systolic variation (10.55±2.12% vs. 7.73±2.76%, p=0.0004). In IHD patients, ischemic segments exhibited elevated diastolic fMBV with significant systolic compression (16.36±3.44% vs. 10.01±2.24%, p=0.013), remote myocardium showed similar phasic variation (11.16±0.68% vs. 7.98±0.57%, p<0.0001). At the same time, scar demonstrated reduced fMBV with attenuated modulation (7.74±1.95% vs. 5.59±1.97%, p=0.099). Abnormal dynamic fMBV regions corresponded to PET defects and impaired circumferential strain. Ferumoxytol-enhanced Multitasking with subspace harmonization enables free-breathing, cardiac-resolved dynamic fMBV mapping, overcoming practical limitations of MOLLI-derived fMBV. This approach enables non-invasive assessment of dynamic myocardial blood volume across the cardiac cycle, with potential utility for characterizing microvascular function in ischemic heart disease.

title: The retinal microvasculature as a predictive window for systemic vascular health in CKM syndrome: A narrative review.
authorString: Chowdhury D, Singh G, Bodakhe SH.
abstractText: The cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome is a pathophysiologic continuum resulting from the synergistic interactions between metabolic dysregulation, chronic kidney disease and cardiovascular disease. The syndrome progresses insidiously, initiating a cascade of systemic microvascular injury, oxidative stress, and inflammation, often preceding apparent, permanent multiorgan failure. Traditional systemic markers often do not detect early endothelial dysfunction and there is an unmet clinical need for non-invasive biomarkers to detect subclinical damage. In this narrative review, we explore the emerging field of oculomics which considers the retina as an easily accessible living biopsy of the systemic micro-circulation. The retinal vascular network, nephrons and myocardium have common embryological origins and similar anatomical characteristics, so that changes in the retinal vascular network are a direct manifestation of pathological changes occurring in the nephrons and heart at the same time. Modern ultrahigh resolution imaging modalities such as optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) enable physicians to quantify subclinical parameters such as capillary depletion, arteriolar constriction, and neural layer atrophy. These dynamic retinal fingerprints can be identified to aid in early risk stratification of the CKM continuum, including hypertension, diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and atherosclerosis. Furthermore, these eye measures are sensitive pharmacodynamic endpoints that allow for real-time in vivo monitoring of systemic microvascular responses to novel cardiometabolic drugs. Oculomics, through the integration of portable imaging technologies, algorithms for deep learning, and multi-omics circulating biomarkers, has the ability to translate CKM risk assessment into primary care settings.

title: Validation of senescence as a therapeutic target in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) through navitoclax delivery.
authorString: Jiang Y, Li S, Liehn EA, Chan CS, Tan JX, Phua TX, Chan SL, Lee CK, Lin X, Soh NJH, Grassi G, Wang JW, Wang T, Singh BK, Tripathi M, Toh WS, Yu VC, Pastorin G.

journal.title: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society

abstractText: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a chronic liver disease characterized by steatosis, inflammation, and progressive fibrosis. Increasing evidence suggests that cellular senescence contributes to MASH progression by promoting lipid accumulation, inflammatory signaling, and fibrogenic responses, highlighting hepatic senescent cells as a potential therapeutic target. Senolytics selectively eliminate senescent cells, but their application in MASH remains insufficiently explored. In this study, we developed in vitro models integrating hepatic lipid accumulation and hepatocyte-macrophage inflammatory crosstalk to facilitate investigation of the contribution of cellular senescence to MASH pathology and to evaluate senescence-targeted interventions. Senescent hepatic cells showed enhanced lipid accumulation and amplified inflammatory signaling with macrophages. Natural Extracellular Vesicles (EVs) derived from adipocytes reduced senescence-associated phenotypes but exhibited context-dependent biological effects, highlighting the limited control over their intrinsic bioactivity. Navitoclax, a senolytic targeting anti-apoptotic BCL-2 family proteins, reduced senescence-associated phenotypes, but its clinical use is limited by its dose-dependent toxicity. Hence, we conceived nano-Cell Vesicle Technology Systems (nCVTs), a biohybrid-based platform combining cell-derived membranes with synthetic lipids for controlled delivery of navitoclax. Navitoclax-loaded nCVTs retained senolytic activity and reduced inflammatory signaling and fibrotic activation in vitro. Importantly, in a Western diet- and fructose-induced (WDF) MASH mouse model, navitoclax-loaded AML-12-derived nCVTs alleviated hepatic lipid accumulation while reducing histopathological activity score and fibrotic profiles. Neither navitoclax formulation reduced platelet counts or hemoglobin concentrations at the tested dose. Collectively, these findings support cellular senescence as a therapeutically relevant target for MASH and identify nCVTs as a promising engineered platform for controlled senolytic delivery.

title: Multi-target phosphodiesterase inhibition overcomes adipose catecholamine resistance and ameliorates systemic lipotoxicity.
authorString: Fujiki T, Takami J, Ihara K, Kawajiri K, Ishida R, Nagaoka K, Mori Y, Waseda Y, Yoshida S, Mandai S, Mori T, Susa K, Sato S, Kajimura S, Kagechika H, Sasano T, Fujii Y, Sohara E, Uchida S, Arita M, Ando F.
abstractText: Obesity-related adipose tissue dysfunction is characterized by reduced β3-adrenergic receptor (β3AR) expression, resulting in impaired catecholamine-dependent lipolysis and limiting the efficacy of β3AR agonists. The discovery of impaired β3AR/cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) signaling caused by concurrent β3AR downregulation (limiting cAMP production) and phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE4) upregulation (enhancing cAMP degradation) necessitated the development of TMDU-3 as a multi-isoform PDE inhibitor targeting PDE4, PDE1, PDE3, and PDE10. TMDU-3 robustly restored downstream cAMP-mediated phosphorylation events, including lipolytic activation, and concomitantly increased upstream β3AR expression in white adipose tissue (WAT) from obese mice. Despite a 5-fold increase in WAT mass, TMDU-3 normalized the WAT lipid composition. Moreover, TMDU-3 enhanced thermogenesis in brown adipose tissue, corrected serum accumulation of various lipids, and more effectively reduced circulating monounsaturated fatty acids than the β3AR agonist mirabegron. These findings demonstrate that multi-target PDE inhibition represents a β3AR-independent strategy superior to β3AR agonism in ameliorating obesity-associated metabolic dysfunction.

title: The Hypothalamic Paraventricular Nucleus as an Integrative Hub of Circadian Regulation and a Therapeutic Target in Disease.
authorString: Yao LJ, Qi T, Li X, Huang TX, Xiao JS, Ren SY, Wen ZY, Chen Z, He ZP, Wang YF.
abstractText: Circadian rhythms are endogenous, approximately 24-hour oscillations that align physiology and behavior with the environmental light-dark cycle and support homeostasis. In mammals, the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) serves as the central circadian pacemaker, but its neuronal projections are restricted to a relatively small set of hypothalamic targets. The hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus (PVN) is an important downstream integrative node that receives direct and indirect temporal signals from the SCN and integrates them with metabolic, visceral, stress-related, and limbic inputs. Through functionally distinct neuroendocrine, autonomic, and central-projecting neuronal populations, the PVN contributes to the temporal regulation of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis activity, glucose metabolism, feeding behavior, nociceptive sensitivity, and cardiovascular function. Cell-type-specific genetic and transcriptomic studies further indicate that PVN neuronal populations exhibit distinct clock-related molecular programs. Studies predominantly in nocturnal rodent models have linked disruption of PVN clocks or rhythmic output to aging-associated decline, metabolic dysfunction, altered tumor immunity, neurodegenerative disease, and pain-related phenotypes. Human post-mortem studies have reported heterogeneous PVN changes in Alzheimer's disease, but direct evidence of PVN clock or SCN-PVN circuit dysfunction in humans remains limited. This review integrates circuit-, cellular-, and molecular-level evidence for the PVN's role in circadian regulation, evaluates interventions spanning timed drug delivery, meal timing, light exposure, and PVN-focused experimental manipulation, and outlines the challenges of translating preclinical findings into clinical practice.

title: Paternal Preconception EGCG Exposure is Associated with Reduced Heart Weight, Altered Cardiac Morphology, and Changed Cardiac CREG1/ERK1/2 Levels in Adult Female Mouse Offspring.
authorString: Huang Y, Yang Y, Huang R, Zhang H, Ye X, Yang X, Ke L, Shi Y, Wang C, Wang Q.
abstractText: Epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), the major bioactive polyphenol in green tea, exhibits broad bioactivities. Existing research has uncovered diverse regulatory effects of EGCG on cardiac tissue. Nevertheless, whether paternal preconception EGCG exposure reshapes cardiac structural characteristics in offspring remains largely uncharacterized. In the present work, adult male C57BL/6J mice received 10 mg/kg/day EGCG via drinking water over a 60-day preconception period prior to mating. We observed that paternal EGCG treatment coincided with lower heart weight and heart-to-body weight ratios in adult female offspring, while no comparable shifts were detected in male littermates. Subsequent fluorescent TUNEL and WGA staining revealed unaltered cardiomyocyte apoptosis in female offspring, yet the cross-sectional area of ventricular cardiomyocytes was substantially diminished. This reduced cardiomyocyte cross-sectional area may have contributed to the decreased heart weight, and this structural phenotype was associated with upregulated cellular repressor of E1A-stimulated genes 1 (CREG1) protein abundance and attenuated extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 (ERK1/2) phosphorylation in cardiac tissue. Collectively, these observations suggest that paternal preconception EGCG exposure is associated with reduced cardiomyocyte cross-sectional area and reduced heart weight selectively in adult female mouse offspring.

title: A multilevel circuit gating framework for transforming sexual motivation into sexual action: Insights from mouse models.
authorString: Tao R, Lu X, Tang L, Kang X.
abstractText: Sexual behaviour consists of a appetitive phase and a consummatory phase.
