Based primarily on research evidence from rodents (particularly male mice), this paper presents a multi-level gate model that explains how the transition between these two phases occurs. In this model, the processing of cues associated with a potential mate is initiated in the main olfactory bulb (MOB) and the accessory olfactory bulb (AOB) systems. These cues are then transmitted through limbic circuits, such as the medial amygdala (MeA) and the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNST), where they are encoded as valuable mating information. Subsequently, these cues are integrated with internal motivational states, including social cues, hormonal status, Sexual reward experience, and sexual satiety, within cell-type-specific circuits centred on the preoptic area (POA). This integration process results in the generation of a motivational gain. When intrinsic motivational states are integrated with somatosensory inputs related to the partner, a state-dependent sensory contact gating mechanism facilitates the transition from exploratory contact to mating behaviours (e.g. mounting). In the downstream process, theperiaqueductal gray (PAG), brainstem, spinal cord, and mesolimbic reward circuits coordinate the sequence of intromission and ejaculation behaviours. During the process of mating, feedback mechanisms such as reward reinforcement and sexual reward modulate future motivational states and action thresholds. Finally, we discuss sex differences in the neural mechanisms underlying the transition from appetitive to consummatory. This conceptual model provides a testable hypothesis regarding the neural mechanisms underlying sexual dysfunction caused by insufficient sexual motivation or disrupted action gating thresholds.

title: Identification of substrates for the skeletal muscle-specific lysine methyltransferases METTL21C and METTL21E.
authorString: Nygård K, Małecki JM, Davydova E, Nolte JL, Ramirez-Garrastacho M, Bengtsen M, Gundersen K, Tellkamp F, Krüger M, Falnes PØ.
abstractText: Protein lysine methylation, catalyzed by S-adenosylmethionine (AdoMet)-dependent methyltransferases (MTases), plays important roles in regulating and fine-tuning protein function. The related mammalian lysine-specific MTases METTL21C and METTL21E are predominantly expressed in skeletal muscle, but their substrates have remained unclear and controversial. Here, we found that METTL21C methylated only a single protein, namely fast myosin-binding protein C (fMyBPC; gene: MYBPC2), in METTL21C-deficient mouse skeletal muscle extracts. METTL21C also showed strong activity on recombinant fMyBPC in vitro, introducing trimethylation at Lys-242. This methylation event was also observed in vivo, and abolished by Mettl21c knockout (KO). The observed in vitro activity of METTL21C on fMyBPC was >100-fold stronger than that observed on AARS1 (alanine-tRNA ligase), a previously reported METTL21C substrate. Interestingly, the two other MyBPC paralogs, which are expressed in cardiac and slow skeletal muscle, were not methylated by METTL21C. For METTL21E, we could not detect in vitro activity. However, we found that monomethylation of Lys-35 (K35) in myosin heavy chain (MYH), a methylation event previously reported in various vertebrate muscles, was abolished by Mettl21e KO in mouse muscle, but not by Mettl21c KO. In human muscles, we detected MYH-K35 methylation at a level similar to that observed in mice, suggesting that the current annotation of human METTL21E as a pseudogene (METTL21EP) may be re-evaluated. Taken together, our results provide new insights into protein methylation in skeletal muscle by identifying fMyBPC as a bona fide muscle-specific substrate of METTL21C, and demonstrating that METTL21E is required for MYH-K35 methylation, thus likely representing the responsible MTase.

title: Post-resuscitation ST-segment elevation and coronary angiographic phenotypes in angiography-evaluable survivors of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest with presumed coronary lesion-related arrest.
authorString: Kurosaka E, Matsuda J, Kato S, Hada Y, Negi K, Morita H, Inaba O, Matsumura Y.
abstractText: The clinical meaning of post-resuscitation ST-segment elevation in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients with suspected coronary etiology remains uncertain. We aimed to describe coronary angiographic phenotypes and clinical outcomes according to post-resuscitation ST-segment findings in an angiography-evaluable subset of OHCA survivors with presumed coronary lesion-related arrest. We retrospectively analyzed 149 successfully resuscitated OHCA patients admitted to our institution between January 2015 and December 2023, who underwent post-resuscitation coronary angiography and had presumed culprit lesions, defined by integrating angiographic findings with electrocardiographic, echocardiographic, and biomarker data in the clinical context. Patients were classified according to the presence or absence of post-resuscitation ST-segment elevation. ST-segment elevation was associated with a more acute occlusive coronary phenotype, with more impaired culprit-vessel flow and greater myocardial injury. In contrast, patients without ST-segment elevation more frequently had multivessel disease and chronic total occlusion, suggesting more complex coronary artery disease. Favorable neurological outcome was less frequent with ST-segment elevation in unadjusted analyses, but this association was not independent of pre-hospital factors. In this selected OHCA subset, post-resuscitation ST-segment elevation was associated with an acute occlusive coronary phenotype and greater myocardial injury, as in non-arrest acute coronary syndromes. However, the absence of ST-segment elevation did not exclude a coronary culprit lesion, so comprehensive coronary assessment is essential. ST-segment elevation was not independently associated with clinical outcomes after adjustment for pre-hospital factors. These findings should be interpreted considering substantial selection inherent to the study population.

title: Prevalence of metabolic syndrome and classification performance of triglyceride-glucose-derived indices in people living with HIV in Spain.
authorString: Corral-San Miguel R, Tomás-Jiménez C, García-Villalba E, Valero-Cifuentes S, Gómez-Verdú JM, Alcaraz-García A, Martínez-Rodríguez R, Hernández-Lorente MD, González-Hipólito R, Guijarro-Westerneyer E, Muñóz-Pérez Á, Bernal-Morell E.
abstractText:
Objectives

Estimate the prevalence and predominant phenotypic patterns of metabolic syndrome (MetS) in people living with HIV receiving contemporary antiretroviral therapy (ART) in southeastern Spain, identify independently associated factors and evaluate the classification performance and clinical utility of triglyceride-glucose (TyG)-derived indices relative to a multivariable logistic regression (MLR) model.

Methods

Cross-sectional study of 287 people living with HIV on stable ART for ≥6 months. MetS was defined by National Cholesterol Education Program Adult Treatment Panel III (NCEP-ATP III) criteria. MLR identified factors independently associated with MetS. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC), DeLong pairwise comparisons and decision curve analysis (DCA) compared the TyG, TyG-waist circumference (TyG-WC) and TyG-waist-to-height ratio (TyG-WHtR) against the MLR model.

Results

MetS prevalence was 30.3% (95% CI 25.1%-36.0%), with hyperglycaemia, hypertension and increased waist circumference (G-B-W) as the predominant three-component cluster (16.1%, adjusted residual 3.67). Independently associated factors were body mass index (BMI) (aOR 1.44; 95% CI 1.28-1.64; p < 0.001), age >50 years (aOR 5.02; 95% CI 1.94-13.03; p = 0.001) and lower CD4 nadir (aOR 0.997; 95% CI 0.995-1.000; p = 0.032); neither ART regimen nor prior protease inhibitor (PI) exposure was associated. AUCs were 0.876 for MLR, 0.864 for TyG, 0.901 for TyG-WC and 0.912 for TyG-WHtR (all p < 0.001) without significant pairwise differences. DCA showed net benefit for TyG-WHtR comparable to the MLR model.

Conclusions

MetS affects nearly one-third of people living with HIV on contemporary ART in southeastern Spain, driven primarily by BMI, advanced age and lower nadir CD4, with a predominant G-B-W phenotype. TyG-WHtR offers classification performance comparable to a full multivariable model using routine parameters, supporting its use as a low-burden MetS screening tool in HIV care.

title: Adverse Childhood Experiences screening in pediatric primary care and concurrent health.
authorString: Negriff S, Sarfan LD, Koebnick C, Sidell MA, Barton L, DiGangi MJ.
abstractText:
Objectives

Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs) are linked with a number of chronic health conditions. However, there are no large-scale data examining whether ACEs screening is also associated with these higher rates. The current study examined the rates of chronic health conditions for children with and without ACEs screening, and those with and without positive screens.

Methods

Data from a large integrated healthcare system captured 684,887 youth age 2-18 years old eligible for ACEs screening between June 2023 and August 2025. Chronic physical and mental health conditions from the electronic health records at the same visit as the ACEs screening included: abdominal pain, ADHD, anxiety, asthma, depression, headache, hypertension, and obesity. Logistic regression estimated the odds of each health condition for: 1) screened versus not screened, 2) positive versus negative screen, and 3a) Total score, 3b) Part 1 score (10 original ACEs), and 3c) Part 2 score (7 additional adversities), adjusting for covariates.

Results

ACEs screening (versus not screened) was associated with elevated odds for ADHD, asthma, and obesity but lower odds of anxiety and hypertension. Among the screened cohort (n=599,989), positive ACEs screening was associated with higher odds of every health condition except hypertension. For those with a positive screen (n=178,214), both Part 1 and Part 2 scores were significantly associated with 5 out of 8 health conditions, with Part 2 generally demonstrating larger effects than the Part 1.

Conclusions

ACEs screening in pediatric primary care is a critical component to assess health risks and address early intervention and treatment.

title: Making diagnostic recommendations when evidence is lacking: A proposed framework.
authorString: Khawandi J, Brignardello-Petersen R, Falcone EL, Santesso N, Azzam M, Kawtharany H, Wiercioch W, Schunemann H, Nieuwlaat R, Mustafa RA.
abstractText: Developing recommendations about test strategies is believed to be challenging, especially when there is no data about the accuracy of the test to diagnose the condition or longitudinal evidence about the effects of the tests on patient important outcomes. We therefore developed a framework to facilitate the discussions of a guideline panel to make diagnostic recommendations. This framework was used when making recommendations for the use of diagnostic tests for post-COVID-19 Condition (PCC) (also known as Long Covid). The framework includes six questions. Four questions address desirable effects: Does a test 1) increase/decrease suspicion of PCC, 2) increase/ decrease suspicion of comorbidities associated with PCC, 3) confirm/ rule out other diagnoses, and 4) change the management. Two questions address undesirable effects: Does a test 1) increase the risk of healthcare overuse, and 2) cause important harm. Answers inform the final judgments about desirable and undesirable effects of a test and are incorporated in the Evidence to Decision Framework to make the recommendation. The proposed framework has been used to make 15 recommendations in one condition and therefore, additional research is needed to assess its application in other conditions and to validate it. Such a framework could play a major role in assisting panels to navigate the tradeoffs between the benefits and harms of tests; enhance transparency in what may have driven the decision; and, help users to better understand how conclusions were reached to make a recommendation. Plain language Summary: When making recommendations for the use of diagnostic tests for post-COVID-19 Condition (PCC), the Canadian Testing, Identification & Diagnosis Related to PCC guideline group members struggled with making judgments on the benefits and harms of the tests. Therefore, a group of guideline methodologists and clinical experts created a framework to help the guideline panel make judgments about whether using a test to diagnose PCC or PCC-related comorbidities would lead to benefits or harms. The framework guided discussions to make recommendations. This framework was used during the development of tests in one guideline only, and it will need further validation. However, the framework could help other guideline panels make recommendations where there is a similar lack of evidence about the effects of the tests.

title: Effects of insulin resistance on pregnancy outcomes and complications in women with polycystic ovary syndrome.
authorString: Hua Z, Shen L, Chen WN.

journal.title: The Journal of international medical research

abstractText: ObjectiveTo investigate whether early-pregnancy insulin resistance in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is associated with adverse maternal pregnancy complications and neonatal/perinatal outcomes after adjustment for common metabolic confounders.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included 168 pregnant women diagnosed with PCOS who were consecutively enrolled at Tongren Hospital from July 2023 to December 2024. Of these, 52 patients with insulin resistance (homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance ≥ 2.77) were assigned to the PCOS with insulin resistance group, whereas 116 patients without insulin resistance were assigned to the PCOS without insulin resistance group. Multivariable binary logistic regression was performed to estimate adjusted associations between insulin resistance and gestational diabetes mellitus, adjusting for age, body mass index, family history of diabetes, and conception mode.ResultsBody mass index was significantly higher in the PCOS with insulin resistance group (p = 0.02). No significant differences were found in thyroid function indices or blood lipid levels across trimesters, neonatal birth weight, or perinatal outcomes (all p > 0.05). The incidence of gestational diabetes mellitus was higher in the PCOS with insulin resistance group than in the PCOS without insulin resistance group (30.77% vs. 17.24%, p = 0.04). After adjustment for potential confounders, insulin resistance (adjusted odds ratio = 2.09, 95% confidence interval: 1.02-4.28, p = 0.044) and higher body mass index (odds ratio = 1.19 per kg/m2, p = 0.038) remained independently associated with increased odds of gestational diabetes mellitus. No significant differences were observed in gestational hypertension, polyhydramnios, or premature rupture of membranes.ConclusionsIn this observational cohort, early-pregnancy insulin resistance was associated with a higher incidence of gestational diabetes mellitus after adjustment for body mass index and other confounders. These findings do not establish a causal relationship. Early standardized screening and targeted metabolic management of insulin resistance may help reduce gestational diabetes mellitus incidence; however, prospective studies are warranted to confirm this association.

title: Barriers and Facilitators of Hypertension and Diabetes Screening in Primary Healthcare Facilities in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia: A Mixed-Methods Study.
authorString: Sendo EG, Bekele BA, Rhodes EC, Johnson LCM, Gary R, Hassan S, Aga F, Tadesse Mengistu Y, Urbanski M.

journal.title: Journal of primary care & community health

abstractText: Introduction/ObjectivesTo identify health-system and provider-level barriers and facilitators influencing hypertension and diabetes screening in public primary health care (PHC) facilities in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.MethodsWe conducted a qualitatively dominant convergent mixed-methods study from May to December 2025 in 10 public PHC facilities. Facility readiness was assessed using a checklist adapted from the WHO Service Availability and Readiness Assessment and analyzed descriptively. Semi structured interviews with 21 clinical staff were analyzed thematically using the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation-Behavior (COM-B) model and Theoretical Domains Framework.ResultsOverall readiness was 82.3%, but only 4.6% of clinical staff had received NCD-related training and 4.2% of the workforce was dedicated to NCD care. Stock-outs of glucose test strips and HbA1c reagents, limited HbA1c availability, inadequate equipment maintenance, and duplicate documentation constrained screening. Providers described limited refresher training, selective age- or symptom-based diabetes screening, heavy workload, and burnout as barriers. Peer learning, supportive supervision, NGO assistance, community-based health insurance, teamwork, and professional commitment were facilitators.ConclusionsScreening was constrained by interacting capability, opportunity, and motivation barriers rather than by the absence of guidelines alone. Priorities include competency-based in-service training, reliable diagnostic supplies and equipment maintenance, reduced documentation burden, and protected provider motivation. Transfer to similar settings requires contextual adaptation.

title: Outcomes Associated With a WhatsApp-Based Telehealth Education Program and Remote Follow-Up on Blood Pressure, Medication Adherence, and Self-Care: Formative Quasi-Experimental Pilot Study.
authorString: Salhab D, AlALi NM, Al-Naamani ZY, AlJarrah A.
abstractText:
Background

Hypertension is a common chronic condition associated with substantial morbidity globally. In Jordan, many patients struggle with sustained medication adherence and self-management, highlighting a need for accessible care strategies. Low-cost platforms such as WhatsApp may support telehealth education and remote follow-up, although formative pilot data are needed to assess feasibility in this context.

Objective

This study aimed to evaluate within-participant changes in blood pressure, medication adherence, self-care behaviors, and hypertension-related knowledge from baseline to postintervention among adults with primary hypertension who participated in a formative WhatsApp-based telehealth education program with structured remote follow-up in Jordan.

Methods

A quasi-experimental, single-group pretest-posttest pilot study was conducted. In total, 40 adults (aged 28-60 years) with primary hypertension were recruited from a university hospital. The 8-week hybrid mobile health (mHealth) intervention involved training participants in home blood pressure monitoring, delivering daily educational multimedia messages via WhatsApp (covering diet, exercise, and medication), and conducting biweekly structured telephone consultations with a nurse and dietitian. Validated tools (Hill-Bone Scale, Blood Pressure Self-Care Scale, and Blood Pressure Knowledge Scale) and electronic sphygmomanometers were used at baseline and after the intervention. Data were analyzed using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.

Results

All 40 participants completed the 8-week pilot and contributed paired baseline and postintervention outcome data. Postintervention scores were higher for hypertension knowledge (r=0.840; P<.001) and self-care behaviors (r=0.524; P=.001); medication adherence scores were lower, indicating better adherence (r=0.805; P<.001); and systolic (r=.434; P=.006) and diastolic blood pressure (r=.684; P<.001) were lower than those at baseline.

Conclusions

This formative single-group pilot identified favorable pre-post differences in blood pressure, medication adherence, self-care behaviors, and hypertension-related knowledge among a selected sample of adults with primary hypertension. Because there was no control group, the findings do not establish intervention effectiveness or causality and should be interpreted as preliminary evidence supporting further controlled evaluation.

title: Sickness Absence in Primary Aldosteronism and References: a Longitudinal Cohort Study.
authorString: Ragnarsson O, Bore A, Alexanderson K.
abstractText:
Objective

Primary aldosteronism (PA) is a common cause of hypertension and is associated with increased cardiovascular morbidity. However, its impact on work capacity remains unknown. We investigated sickness absence and disability pension among patients with PA and in matched reference groups with and without hypertension.

Methods

A nationwide eight-year longitudinal cohort study based on linked register data, including 838 individuals with PA aged 18-67 in 2019 and two matched reference cohorts with and without hypertension. Outcomes included annual proportions of individuals with sickness absence (in spells >14 days) or disability pension, mean annual net days, and trajectories of absence days.

Results

Patients with PA had a higher mean annual proportion with sickness absence than individuals with hypertension (21% (range: 18-23%) vs 17% (range: 17-19%) and those without hypertension (10% (range: 9-12%)). Mean annual sickness absence days were 27, 20, and 9, respectively. The combined mean annual number of sickness absence and disability pension days was similar in PA and hypertension (54 (range: 40-66) vs 53 (range: 50-57), and higher than in those without hypertension (25 (range: 22-29)). Trajectory analysis identified four patterns of absence days; 12% of patients with PA had persistently high absence, significantly associated with female sex, higher age, lower education, unmarried status, rural residence, cardiovascular disease, and treatment with mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists.

Conclusion

PA is associated with substantial and sustained sickness absence and disability pension, comparable to that observed in hypertension and higher than in individuals without hypertension. These findings extend the clinical impact of PA beyond cardiovascular morbidity and highlight the importance of considering work capacity in clinical management.

title: Prevalence, associations and sex-related disparities of hypertension in South Asians: Evidence from a national survey of Sri Lanka.
authorString: Mettananda C, Premaratna R, Mallawa R, Fernando U, Senaratne A, Perera U, Wickramasinghe C.
abstractText:
Background

Blood pressure(BP) control remains suboptimal worldwide. Sex-related disparities in hypertension have been reported, but data from South Asia are limited. Understanding the epidemiology and sex-related differences is essential to improve BP control.

Objectives

To assess the prevalence, associations and sex-related disparities of hypertension among Sri Lankans.

Methods

We analysed secondary data from the Sri Lanka STEPS Survey 2021, a nationally representative, community-based, cross-sectional study. Hypertension was defined as BP ≥ 140/90 mmHg or current antihypertensive use; controlled BP as BP < 140/90 mmHg. Prevalences, associations, and sex-related disparities in hypertension, undiagnosed hypertension, and BP control were assessed using logistic regression.

Results

Data from 4,634 adults(mean age 43.5(weighted CI 43.0-44.1) years; female 54.8 (53.1-56.5)%) were analysed. Overall, 37.2(35.5-38.9)% had hypertension, of whom 60.0(58.1-63.4) % were previously undiagnosed. Among those previously diagnosed, 73.6 (73.6, 69.6-77.2)% were on treatment, but only 38.0(33.0-44.20)% achieved BP targets. The rates of hypertension prevalence (p = 0.600), treated hypertension (p = 0.398), and controlled blood pressure (p = 0.819) in females and males did not differ significantly by sex. However, undiagnosed hypertension was significantly higher in males (69.4%, 65.3-73.1) than in females (53.6%, 50.1-57.0) (p < 0.001). Differences in the associations of hypertension by sex were noted; diabetes was associated only in females (p < 0.001), while wealth quintile (p < 0.001) and 24-hour urinary salt excretion (p = 0.011) were associated only in males. Overweight/obesity was shown to have a significant association with undiagnosed hypertension only in males (p = 0.017) in stratified analyses.

Conclusions

More than half of the hypertensives in this South Asian population were previously undiagnosed. Of hypertensives, ¾ were treated, but only 1/3 achieved treatment goals. Prevalence, treatment and control rates of hypertension were not different between females and males, but undiagnosed hypertension was more common in men. Therefore, the emphasis should be on improving the detection of hypertension, especially in men, and on treating to targets in both sexes.

title: Compare 30-minute automated office blood pressure vs 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring: A prospective study.
authorString: Bui ACM, Nguyen QTN, Bui ANM, Ha MVP, Nguyen NP, Nguyen THA, Dang NQ, Tran PM, Kha TV, Nguyen NDP, Le LDB, Tran HH, Bui DT, Nguyen NP.
abstractText:
Background

Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) is the reference standard for diagnosing hypertension (HTN), but its use in routine practice remains limited because of cost, availability, and patient burden. Automated office blood pressure (AOBP) has been proposed as a practical alternative, although its performance relative to ABPM remains uncertain.

Objectives

To evaluate the agreement and diagnostic performance of 30-minute AOBP compared with 24-hour ABPM and to identify optimal cut-off values for detecting ambulatory hypertension.

Methods

In this prospective cohort study, 79 adults undergoing ABPM also underwent 30-minute AOBP measurement with automated readings every 5 minutes. The mean of the final six measurements was analyzed. Agreement was assessed using paired comparisons and Bland-Altman analysis. Diagnostic performance using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and agreement statistics.

Results

Thirty-minute AOBP values were consistently higher than ABPM measurements. Mean differences were +6.59/ + 7.27 mmHg for systolic/diastolic BP versus 24-hour ABPM and +3.73/ + 5.16 mmHg versus daytime ABPM (all p < 0.001). Bland-Altman analysis showed acceptable group-level agreement but wide limits of agreement. Sensitivity ranged from 84% to 96% and specificity from 28% to 79%. ROC analysis demonstrated good discrimination (AUC 0.77-0.87). The highest agreement with overall ABPM occurred at a cut-off of ≥140/84 mmHg (κ = 0.624).

Conclusions

Thirty-minute AOBP showed good discrimination for elevated ambulatory blood pressure but systematically overestimated BP relative to ABPM. It may serve as a practical screening tool, although normal AOBP values cannot reliably exclude ambulatory HTN and confirmation with 24-hour ABPM remains necessary.

Central illustration

Diagnostic Performance of 30-Minute Automated Office Blood Pressure Compared With 24-Hour Ambulatory Monitoring.

title: Prognostic Significance of Early Donor-derived Cell-free DNA Trajectories After Kidney Transplantation.
authorString: Sureshkumar K, Klein JA, Kumar D, Costa N, Glehn-Ponsirenas R, Chuang P, Shen L, Lu J, Wojciechowski D, Jain P, Huang Y, Wiseman A, Huang E, Knechtle S, Bunnapradist S, Villicana R, Sood P, Paramesh A, Choudhury RA, Piper J, Xue J, Qazi Y, Jain D, Parajuli S, Leca N, Mandelbrot DA, Bromberg J, Maw TT, Brennan DC, Alhamad T, KOAR Investigators.
abstractText:
Background

Early post-transplant elevations in donor-derived cell-free DNA are often attributed to ischemia-reperfusion injury, with uncertain prognostic significance. We assessed whether donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) results during the first 4 mo post-transplantation are associated with long-term graft outcomes.

Methods

We analyzed 1137 kidney transplant recipients enrolled in the prospective multicenter Kidney Outcomes AlloSure Registry. Recipients were categorized into 4 trajectory groups based on dd-cfDNA measurements obtained within the first 4 mo post-transplant: consistently low, transient-elevation, late-elevation, and persistent-elevation. Associations with donor-specific antibody (DSA) development, rejection, graft dysfunction, and graft loss were evaluated over 3 y using hazard regression, with multivariable models adjusted for calculated Panel Reactive Antibody (cPRA) and retransplant.

Results

Among the 1137 recipients, 83.7% exhibited consistently low dd-cfDNA, 9.8% transient-elevation, 3.2% late-elevation, and 3.3% persistent-elevation. Late elevation was associated with the highest cumulative incidence of DSA development, whereas persistent-elevation had the highest incidence of rejection, graft dysfunction, and graft loss. Graft loss occurred in 20.0% of recipients with persistent-elevation and 8.8% with late-elevation and was uncommon among consistently low (2.2%) and transient (2.9%) groups. On multivariable analysis, late elevation was independently associated with DSA development, rejection, and graft loss, and persistent-elevation with rejection, graft dysfunction, and graft loss, regardless of prior transplantation or sensitization status.

Conclusions

Early dd-cfDNA trajectories stratify kidney transplant recipients into clinically meaningful risk phenotypes. Persistent or late-emerging elevation identifies patients at independently increased risk of rejection and graft loss, with persistent-elevation also associated with graft dysfunction, supporting serial dd-cfDNA monitoring as a tool for early post-transplant risk stratification.

title: Attenuation of Angiotensin II- Induced Cardiomyocyte Hypertrophy by <i>Moringa oleifera</i> Lam. extract, Fractions and Bioactive Constituents: Cell Size Analysis and Molecular Docking.
authorString: Chin WK, Husain K, Fauzi NM, Jasamai M.

journal.title: Journal of the American Nutrition Association

abstractText:
Objective

Moringa oleifera Lam. leaves are valued for their rich nutritional profile and traditional use in treating various ailments, including hypertension. However, research focusing on their mechanism of action, particularly their interactions with angiotensin (Ang) II receptors remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of M. oleifera leaves extract, fractions and bioactive compounds (kaempferol, chlorogenic acid, gallic acid, and vicenin-2) on Ang II induced H9c2 cells and their binding affinities toward Ang II receptors.

Method

The crude extract was fractionated into hexane, dichloromethane, ethyl acetate, acetone and methanol fractions. Cell viability test was carried out and concentrations that maintained cell viability at 80% and more were selected for further study. Hypertrophic model was simulated by inducing H9c2 cells with Ang II (1 µM) and the antihypertrophic effect was assessed by measuring changes in the cell size.

Results

Ang II significantly doubled the cell size compared to normal control groups. Results showed that the crude extract, its ethyl acetate, acetone, and methanol fractions, and bioactive compounds significantly reduced Ang II-induced cell hypertrophy (p < 0.05) in H9c2 cells compared to the Ang II untreated group. Furthermore, bioactive compounds tested also showed significant dose-dependent (10, 20, and 40 µM) reduction in cell size compared to the Ang II group. Gallic acid demonstrated the highest potency by reducing the size the most at the highest dose tested (40 µM), followed by quercetin, chlorogenic acid, vicenin and kaempferol. In molecular docking studies, binding energies of -5.5 kcal/mol and lower were recorded for all bioactive compounds indicating their strong binding affinities toward Ang II receptor.

Conclusion

This work provides an evaluation of Ang II-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy attenuation activity of bioactive compounds identified in the M. oleifera leaves extract. These findings serve as a foundation for future studies aimed at developing therapies for cardiovascular diseases from natural resources.

title: Age-specific respiratory support and monitoring for acute respiratory distress syndrome: a narrative review.
authorString: Chao KY, Yokoyama T, Wang CY, Chien YH, Mu SC, Chen CY, Chu YZ, Liu WL.
abstractText:
Introduction

Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) causes inflammatory alveolar-capillary injury at different ages. Age-related differences in respiratory mechanics, airway anatomy, pulmonary vascular physiology, and disease etiology limit extrapolation of diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. This review compared respiratory monitoring and support strategies across adult, pediatric, and neonatal ARDS.

Areas covered

We searched PubMed for English-language human studies published from database inception through 14 August 2026 and reviewed major society guidelines. This review covers age-specific ARDS definitions, epidemiology, pathophysiology, respiratory support, adjunctive therapies, and liberation from mechanical ventilation. Adult-derived evidence supports low-tidal-volume ventilation, prolonged prone positioning for severe ARDS, selective higher positive end-expiratory pressure, and early extracorporeal membrane oxygenation for refractory disease. Recommendations for pediatric ARDS often rely on consensus or observational evidence. Neonatal ARDS management remains largely extrapolated from neonatal respiratory disorders and must account for gestational age, surfactant biology, pulmonary hypertension, and etiology.

Expert opinion

Respiratory support should be age-calibrated, phenotype-informed, and reassessed for gas exchange, respiratory effort, mechanics, hemodynamics, device performance, and clinical trajectory. Physiological improvements may not translate into positive outcomes. Noninvasive support should not delay intubation in cases of failure. Standardized interventions and prospective studies must be tailored to pediatric and neonatal populations.

title: Pharmacist-led remote monitoring for hypertension management: A longitudinal descriptive study of patient and pharmacist experiences.
authorString: Yuen J, Sugiarto E, Bleik A, Van MT, Reardon J.

journal.title: Canadian pharmacists journal : CPJ = Revue des pharmaciens du Canada : RPC

abstractText:
Background

Over 50% of patients with hypertension are suboptimally managed, offering the opportunity for pharmacists to leverage technology to support monitoring. The objective of this study was to evaluate patient and pharmacist attitudes, experiences, and perspectives of a remote, pharmacist-led hypertension management program that incorporated a mobile health (mHealth) application into routine care.

Methods

This was a 6-month longitudinal descriptive feasibility study using A&D Heart Track to monitor home blood pressure (BP) alongside pharmacist consultation. A mixed-methods approach was used, combining facilitated patient and pharmacist surveys administered at multiple time points with qualitative interviews. This paper reports the quantitative survey findings, with qualitative interview findings reported separately. Survey responses were analyzed using descriptive statistics.

Results

The study enrolled 17 patients, and 8 pharmacists were involved in their care. At 6 months, 94% of patients reported satisfaction with the mHealth application and 88% felt better cared for knowing a pharmacist was monitoring their readings. Patients reported sustained comfort with the technology and consistently positive perceptions of pharmacist accessibility. At 6 months, all pharmacists agreed or strongly agreed that the application would help them provide better care and increase their involvement in patients' care.

Conclusion

This study provides descriptive evidence that a pharmacist-led, remote monitoring approach for hypertension management was feasible from the perspectives of patients and pharmacists in a Canadian primary care setting, based on patient satisfaction and comfort with technology and pharmacist-reported manageability of mHealth application use. These findings may help inform the expansion of telehealth services and their application to other chronic conditions, such as type 2 diabetes.

title: Echocardiographic phenotypes of opioid-induced cardiotoxicity: a narrative review.
authorString: Żerdziński K, Janiec J, Suchodolski A, Szulik M.
abstractText: Opioid cardiotoxicity is an increasing clinical concern, yet its echocardiographic manifestations are heterogeneous and poorly characterized. This narrative review synthesizes available evidence, maps the principal echocardiographic phenotypes of opioid-related cardiac injury, and identifies major knowledge gaps. A structured PubMed search (January 2014-December 2024) combined opioid and echocardiographic terms without language restriction. Human and animal studies of any design assessing cardiac structure or function by echocardiography after acute or chronic opioid exposure were eligible. Of 209 records, 41 were included and grouped by dominant phenotype. No formal protocol (e.g., PRISMA) or risk-of-bias appraisal was applied. Five distinct-and often conflicting-phenotypes emerged: (1) severe, potentially reversible global left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVEF as low as 20%), sometimes progressing to cardiogenic shock yet normalising within 48-72 h; (2) Takotsubo cardiomyopathy, classic after withdrawal and predominantly reverse after intoxication; (3) right ventricular dysfunction with pulmonary hypertension, usually secondary to hypoxia or left-sided failure but occasionally isolated; (4) consistent cardioprotection in animal ischaemia-reperfusion models, unsupported by any prospective human echocardiographic study; and (5) a mechanically normal profile despite QTc exceeding 610 ms and torsades de pointes. Phenotypes 1-3 rest largely on case reports, and many studies are confounded by co-administered cocaine, benzodiazepines or α2-adrenoceptor agonists. Opioid cardiac effects are context-dependent, and mechanical toxicity diverges from electrical toxicity: a normal echocardiogram does not exclude lethal arrhythmia, so echocardiography and serial QTc assessment are complementary rather than interchangeable. Prospective studies with advanced imaging are needed to establish phenotype frequency and determinants.

title: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic outcomes in women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy at 12 months postpartum : The PreCareFem Cohort.
authorString: Findl K, Halmer S, Klee S, Busvine C, Renner-Sebek M, Wiesholzer M, Schubert S, Eiwegger T, Wichert-Schmitt B, Pfaller B.
abstractText: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy are risk factors for later cardiovascular and chronic kidney disease. Early postpartum trajectories of blood pressure and metabolic recovery in this high-risk population are still insufficiently defined. A prospective, single-center, observational cohort study was conducted in the Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Women's Healthcare Prevention Program (PreCareFem) at the University Hospital St. Pölten, Austria. Participants were enrolled on presentation between 1 June 2023, and 31 March 2025. Cardiovascular and metabolic surrogate parameters, including automated blood pressure measurement, anthropometric evaluation, cardiovascular, kidney and metabolic parameters, lifestyle assessment following the components of the "Life's Essential 8", and urine albumin-creatinine ratio were assessed peripartum and at 3-6 and 12 months postpartum. A total of 91 women with preeclampsia (PE; n = 66) and gestational hypertension (GH; n = 25) were enrolled. At 12 months postpartum, 31% met the diagnostic criteria for arterial hypertension (PE 29%, GH 36%), 18% for prediabetes and 3% for diabetes. More than half (52%) had LDL levels > 100 mg/dL and 32% had low HDL levels. Obesity was diagnosed in 24% of participants, 8% of women were diagnosed with CKD 12 months postpartum. Low-grade albuminuria (uACR 10-30 mg/g) was observed in 21% of women with PE compared to 8% in women with GH. A significant number of women were diagnosed with arterial hypertension, early kidney impairment and/or metabolic abnormalities 1 year following hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. These findings highlight the need for a structured, multidisciplinary postpartum follow-up to address an underutilized opportunity for prevention of cardiovascular and chronic kidney disease.

title: Early real-world use of acoramidis for transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy in Germany: results from StarTTR.
authorString: Morbach C, Ohlmeier C, Trenkwalder T, Aus dem Siepen F, Kruppert S, Keuken G, Evers T, Pfister R, Herrmann S, Störk S.

journal.title: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society

abstractText:
Background

Acoramidis, a selective transthyretin stabilizer, received EU approval in February 2025 for the treatment of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM). We describe patient characteristics and comedication patterns in German routine care.

Methods

Adults with ≥ 1 acoramidis dispensation between April and September 2025 were identified from the IQVIA™ Longitudinal Prescription database, which covers 82% of reimbursed prescriptions. Sociodemographic data, comorbidities, prescribing setting, and comedications were analyzed overall and by pretreatment status (treatment-naïve vs. tafamidis switchers).

Results

A total of 289 patients were identified; median age was 82 (interquartile range 77-85) years; 15% were female and 86% were treatment-naïve. Acoramidis initiation occurred predominantly in hospital outpatient departments (87%). In the year preceding initiation, the most common comedications were renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibitors (76%), sodium glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors (74%), and beta-blockers (71%). Between 12 and 10 months and 3 and 1 months before initiation, use of mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs), loop diuretics, direct oral anticoagulants, and SGLT2 inhibitors increased markedly, whereas RAS inhibitors, beta-blockers, and calcium channel blockers remained unchanged.

Conclusion

This real-world analysis showed that acoramidis was predominantly prescribed as first-line therapy for older, mainly male patients with ATTR-CM; switching from tafamidis was comparatively infrequent. The increasing use of MRAs, loop diuretics, direct oral anticoagulants, and SGLT2 inhibitors prior to acoramidis initiation is consistent with active therapeutic optimization in specialist centers. These data provide an early benchmark for monitoring acoramidis adoption and will inform future comparative effectiveness research.

title: Uncovering disease progression trajectories across multiple timescales with hybrid ODE-mixture models
authorString: de Rooij M, Quadt JD, van Riel NA, O'Donovan S.
abstractText: Biological systems are capable of evolving across multiple timescales, yet most modeling approaches capture either short-term physiological responses or long-term disease progression. Additionally, methods that combine these time scales either struggle with inter-individual variation, or require large volumes of data to work. We present Latent Class Parameter Trajectory Analysis (LCPTA), a hybrid framework that combines mechanistic ordinary differential equation (ODE) modeling of short-term dynamics with latent class trajectory modeling of long-term parameter evolution. To support this approach, we developed TemporalMixtureModels.jl, a Julia package for univariate and multivariate temporal mixture modeling. We evaluated LCPTA in two synthetic longitudinal studies, covering a simulation of a heterogeneous population developing hypertension, as well as a synthetic longitudinal study of 75 virtual individuals followed over 30 years, representing muscle insulin resistance, liver insulin resistance, and healthy trajectories. We compared LCPTA with a conditional neural ODE and a conditional neural network for reconstruction of long-term parameter trajectories and subgroup separation. In both studies LCPTA recovered relevant subgroup structure and trajectory patterns. In the cardiovascular study, the neural approaches were able to distinguish inter-individual differences, but in the insulin sensitivity study, neural approaches failed to represent parameter trajectories faithfully, primarily separating individuals along a single dominant parameter and showing weaker multivariate trajectory reconstruction. In additional experiments with sparse and irregularly sampled unseen individuals, LCPTA maintained strong classification performance. We show that LCPTA is an efficient and interpretable strategy for multiscale modeling of heterogeneous metabolic disease progression, with potential utility for data-efficient digital twin applications.

title: Species-Dependent Limitations of Murine Myocardium for Investigating the Combined Inotropic Effects of SERCA2a Stimulation and Myofilament Ca2+ Sensitization
authorString: Misitano F, Giacomelli N, Maniezzi C, Dente M, Scardigli M, Poggesi C, Pioner JM, Malfatto G, Zaza A, Ferrantini C, Lodola F.
abstractText: Impaired sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ handling and myofilament function both contribute to contractile dysfunction in heart failure. A previous study in failing human myocardium showed that combining the SERCA2a activator istaroxime (ISTA) with the Ca2+ sensitizer levosimendan (LEVO) produces greater positive inotropy than either drug alone. However, human multicellular preparations did not allow comprehensive investigation of the underlying cellular mechanisms. We therefore assessed contractile performance and Ca2+ dynamics in murine multicellular myocardial preparations and ventricular cardiomyocytes treated with ISTA (20 μM), LEVO (0.5 μM), or their combination. ISTA improved developed force, contraction–relaxation kinetics, and mechanical restitution. These effects were associated with increased Ca2+ transient amplitude, accelerated Ca2+ rise and decay, and enhanced sarcoplasmic reticulum reloading. Adding LEVO produced no further mechanical benefit and only minor changes in Ca2+ handling. LEVO alone elicited heterogeneous contractile responses and increased myofilament Ca2+ sensitivity in only a minority of cardiomyocytes, while consistently accelerating Ca2+ transient decay. This effect was reproduced by the phosphodiesterase-3 inhibitor cilostamide, after which LEVO caused no significant additional change, consistent with a contribution of downstream cAMP-PKA signaling to the acceleration of Ca2+ removal. Thus, limited murine responsiveness to LEVO-mediated myofilament sensitization prevented mechanistic reconstruction of the additive inotropic effect observed in human myocardium, highlighting a species-dependent limitation of the mouse model for studying this combined therapy.

title: Modality-agnostic late fusion of electrocardiogram, phonocardiogram and photoplethysmogram signals for cardiovascular disease detection
authorString: Alam MT, Hossain MZ, Moni MA.
abstractText: Cardiac monitors rarely record every signal, and adding one is seldom evaluated. We asked when decision-level (late) fusion of the electrocardiogram (ECG), phonocardiogram (PCG) and photoplethysmogram (PPG) improves cardiovascular disease detection, and why, using one model for any signal combination. One expert per signal was trained in nested, subject-grouped cross-validation, Platt-calibrated and combined by seven rules, each fitted once and applied to any available signals. Three studies: abnormal heart sounds (PhysioNet/CinC 2016, ECG+PCG, 329 recordings), atrial fibrillation (AF; MIMIC-III-Ext-PPG, ECG+PPG, 40,792 segments, 5,642 patients) and a synthetic tri-modal (ECG+PCG+PPG) benchmark. PPG failed quality checks 3.7 times more often in AF, so complete-case fusion could not score 43.9\% of AF segments; the modality-agnostic model scored every segment, raising the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) over ECG alone from 0.923 to 0.938 (+0.015, 95\% confidence interval 0.012--0.018), but only with calibrated experts (uncalibrated: 0.847). With both signals, PPG raised AUC from 0.910 to 0.931 (+0.021, 0.017--0.026). PCG added nothing (\textit{p}\,=\,1.00), consistent with published gains (0.004--0.023). Synthetic data favoured all three signals (AUC 0.984; best pair 0.976). Soft voting nearly matched the best rule; hard voting lost because two votes give three scores. Correlated expert errors, not the combiner, bounded the gain: the best rule nearly matched an oracle combination. Expected Gradients explained the ECG and PCG experts faithfully. Calibrated, modality-agnostic late fusion scores every record from its usable signals; its gain is bounded by expert redundancy, measurable before adding sensors.

title: Epidemiological Analysis of Co-morbidities of Patients with Metabolic Associated Fatty Liver Disease (MAFLD): A Dual-Center Study
authorString: q m, zh l, F G, Zh W, W Z, H Z, Zh H.
abstractText: MAFLD is a multisystem metabolic liver disease with an increasing global prevalence and is frequently accompanied by metabolic co-morbidities. Background/Objectives : To characterize comorbidities in patients with MAFLD and compare their prevalence between MAFLD without cirrhosis and MAFLD with cirrhosis. Methods : Clinical data from patients diagnosed with MAFLD between January and December 2025 were retrospectively collected from the Third People's Hospital of Shenzhen and the Ninth People's Hospital of Dongguan. Inpatient and outpatient records from the Hepatology Department and other clinical departments were reviewed. Demographic characteristics, department visited, and comorbidities were analysed. Results : A total of 25,089 patients were included; 70% were men, and the mean age was 46.2 ± 11.2 years. MAFLD without cirrhosis accounted for 23,952 cases (95.46%), and MAFLD-related cirrhosis for 1,137 cases (4.54%). Male sex, older age, and comorbidities were significantly associated with cirrhosis ( P < 0.01). The most common comorbidities were hyperlipidaemia (41.63%), type 2 diabetes mellitus (34.57%), and hypertension (28.19%). Compared with cirrhosis, MAFLD without cirrhosis was more frequently associated with hypertension, coronary heart disease, hyperlipidaemia, hyperuricemia, and tumours, whereas cirrhosis was more commonly associated with colonic polyps and malignant tumours (all P < 0.01). Comorbidity patterns also differed significantly by age and sex. Conclusions : Comorbidity profiles vary according to MAFLD subtype, age, and sex. MAFLD without cirrhosis is more closely associated with cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, whereas MAFLD related cirrhosis is associated with a higher prevalence of colonic polyps and malignant tumours, providing important implications for screening and clinical management.

title: Association between caregiver burden and quality of life among family caregivers of patients with heart failure: a cross-sectional study
authorString: Aghajanloo A, Heydari E, Vaezi A, Fallah R.
abstractText: Background Heart failure is a common and growing public health problem and a leading cause of recurrent hospital admission among adults aged 65 years and older. Family members are central to the provision of long-term care, but caregiving may impose a substantial burden and affect caregivers’ quality of life. This study aimed to determine caregivers’ quality of life and examine its association with caregiver burden among family caregivers of patients with heart failure. Methods This descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted in Zanjan, Iran. The study population comprised family caregivers of patients with New York Heart Association functional class III or IV heart failure who were admitted to Ayatollah Mousavi Teaching Hospital. A convenience sample of 176 caregivers completed a demographic questionnaire, the Novak and Guest Caregiver Burden Inventory, and the World Health Organization Quality of Life–BREF questionnaire. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, independent-samples t tests, one-way analysis of variance, and multiple linear regression. Results The mean caregiver quality-of-life score was 63.3 ± 19.8, and the mean caregiver burden score was 46.34 ± 10.16. The multiple linear regression model was statistically significant (R = 0.475, R² = 0.226, F = 8.007, p < 0.001). Caregiver burden was the only significant independent predictor of quality of life (B = − 0.652, β = −0.335, p < 0.001); after adjustment for the other variables, each one-point increase in caregiver burden was associated with a 0.652-point decrease in quality of life. Conclusions Caregiver burden was independently and inversely associated with quality of life among family caregivers of patients with heart failure. Early identification of caregivers at risk and the provision of effective supportive, educational, and psychological interventions may help reduce caregiver burden and preserve caregivers’ quality of life.

title: Advanced ECG Signal Analysis for Atrial Fibrillation Detection Using an LSTM Network
authorString: Borghi PH, Teixeira JP, Freitas DR.
abstractText: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a heart rhythm disturbance affecting approximately 1% of the global population, being the most common cardiac anomaly. Visual inspection of extensive electrocardiograms (ECGs), patient variabilities, and long-term dependencies make manual AF diagnosis difficult and heavily reliant on a cardiologist’s expertise. Aiming to aid medical diagnosis, this study develops: an innovative R-peak detector to correct database annotation inaccuracies, and machine learning classifiers to enhance AF detection from long-term raw ECGs. The R-peak algorithm combines self-convolved windows filtering, signal derivatives, Shannon energy, and the Hilbert transform. Using the MIT-BIH Atrial Fibrillation database, extracted ECG features included RR intervals (RRi) durations, Jitter and Shimmer disturbances, Shannon and logarithmic energy entropies, instantaneous frequencies, spectral entropy and Wavelet Scattering Transform (WST) coefficients. These were evaluated using Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. To our knowledge, this is one of the first times that acoustically inspired parameters, Jitter and Shimmer, have described ECG signals. The proposed R-peak algorithm achieved a high accuracy of 98.95%. For AF classification, the best accuracy results were 91.96% for MLP and 98.17% for LSTM, which matches typical state-of-the-art values (≈ 98.00%). Findings indicate that RRi remained the most discriminatory feature, while incorporating P- and T-waves entropies and Jitter significantly enhances performance. Besides LSTM’s superior performance, MLP approaches validate that precise feature engineering allows simpler models to approach state-of-the-art results, highlighting their potential on times of deep learning overuse and of searching for explainable AIs in clinical practice.

title: Dissecting the Role of the Homebox Transcription Factor Pitx2 in Cardiac Development, Regeneration and Disease
authorString: Jaimes-Granados J, Caño-Carrillo S, Lozano-Velasco E, Franco D.
abstractText: The paired-like homeobox transcription factor Pitx2 is a highly conserved master regulator of embryogenesis, primarily recognized for its critical role in the establishment of left-right asymmetry and cardiovascular morphogenesis. This review provides an in-depth analysis of the diverse roles of Pitx2 in cardiac development, adult pathophysiology and tissue regeneration. During embryonic development, the asymmetric expression of the Pitx2c isoform is essential for the proper alignment of the outflow tract, the development of endocardial cushions and the patterning of the atrioventricular conduction system. Crucially, Pitx2 represses the default sinoatrial pacemaker genetic program in the left atrium, thus preventing the formation of ectopic electrical tissue. As a result, genetic alterations or the loss of Pitx2 function directly cause severe congenital heart diseases such as transposition of the great arteries (TGA), double outlet right ventricle (DORV) and Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF). Beyond early development, Pitx2 is indispensable for maintaining electrical and metabolic homeostasis in the adult heart. Genome-wide association studies established the 4q25 locus, containing the PITX2 gene, as the primary global genetic risk factor for atrial fibrillation (AF). The deficiency of this gene in the adult myocardium triggers profound structural and electrical remodeling, arrhythmogenesis and oxidative stress. Furthermore, recent investigations highlight a cardioprotective role for Pitx2 following ischemic injury. By interacting with stress response and cell preservation signaling pathways, Pitx2 mitigates the production of mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS), attenuates apoptosis and fibrosis and promotes myocardial repair. Collectively, this review synthesizes the complex genomic, developmental and pathological regulatory networks of Pitx2, underscoring its evolution from a essential developmental gene into a promising therapeutic target for congenital heart diseases, atrial arrhythmias and cardiac regeneration strategies.

title: Shock With Acute Myocardial Dysfunction in Stercoral Colitis: Diagnosis and Management.
authorString: Parsa S, Mohty R, Pepin ME, Petropoulos T, Gerber D, Witteles R, McAvoy J.
abstractText:
Background

Shock in sepsis is predominantly vasodilatory; however, concomitant myocardial dysfunction may result in superimposed cardiogenic shock and a mixed shock state.

Case summary

A 75-year-old man with Parkinson disease, severe constipation, and stercoral colitis presented with profound shock after an enema. Echocardiography showed new biventricular dysfunction with regional wall-motion abnormalities. Invasive hemodynamic assessment demonstrated elevated filling pressures, low cardiac index, and low systemic vascular resistance despite substantial vasoactive and inotropic support, consistent with a mixed vasodilatory and cardiogenic shock. He improved after antibiotics and vasoactive support, but manual disimpaction after stabilization was followed within minutes by recurrent/similar shock.

Review summary

This case illustrates a practical approach to mixed shock with acute myocardial dysfunction. Treatment of underlying infection should occur in parallel with characterization of the hemodynamic phenotype. Serial echocardiography and invasive hemodynamic assessment can identify concomitant vasodilatory and cardiogenic shock and guide circulatory support as shock physiology evolves.

Take-home messages

Shock physiology is dynamic. In patients with sepsis, serial clinical, echocardiographic, and hemodynamic reassessment can identify concomitant cardiogenic shock and guide circulatory support.

title: Staged sternal distraction for early thoracic expansion in Shwachman-Diamond syndrome.
authorString: Jarrin Lopez A, Zhao A, Darawsheh R, Kephart D, Sebastian VA, Idowu O, Babbitt C, Kim S.

journal.title: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England

abstractText: Shwachman-Diamond syndrome (SDS) is a rare inherited multisystem disorder with variable skeletal involvement; severe neonatal thoracic dystrophy is uncommon but can cause thoracic insufficiency and mimic Jeune syndrome. We report staged sternal distraction in a 5-month-old infant with a severely constricted thorax, pulmonary hypoplasia, refractory pulmonary hypertension, tracheostomy-dependent respiratory failure and an iatrogenic posterior tracheal wall injury. Subsequent trio long-read genome sequencing identified compound heterozygous pathogenic variants in SBDS, c.183_184delinsCT (p.Lys62Ter), inherited paternally, and c.258+2T>C, inherited maternally, establishing a molecular diagnosis of SDS. At presentation, the chest circumference measured 36cm, compared with an age-expected value of 41cm. The patient underwent staged median sternotomy distraction followed by stabilisation with custom fibular allograft struts. At approximately 3 months, chest circumference had increased to 41cm, peak inspiratory pressures had decreased from 40-50cm H2O to the mid-20cm H2O range, pulmonary hypertension was no longer evident on echocardiography, and the tracheal injury had healed. At 6 months, he remained on home mechanical ventilation, with peak inspiratory pressures in the upper 20cm H2O range. To our knowledge, operative thoracic expansion specifically for SDS-associated thoracic insufficiency has not previously been described. In carefully selected infants with severe thoracic insufficiency who are not yet candidates for conventional thoracic reconstruction, staged sternal distraction may serve as an interim strategy to achieve meaningful thoracic expansion.

title: Brain sites involved in endogenous analgesia.
authorString: Henderson LA, Crawford LS, Kang JWM, Keay KA.
abstractText:
Abstract

Pain modulation is a fundamental survival mechanism that prioritises, shapes, and suppresses nociceptive inputs to optimise behaviour. Although acute pain signals potential or actual tissue damage, sustained pain can impair essential behaviours, necessitating modulatory circuits that dynamically regulate nociception according to context and motivational state. These systems are deeply conserved, embedded within primitive spinal and brainstem structures, and capable of powerful modulation independent of cortical input, although higher regions such as the prefrontal cortex can influence their function. Decades of work have sought to identify these core modulatory circuits to advance basic understanding and develop strategies for clinically meaningful hypoalgesia. More recently, dysfunction within these circuits has been implicated in chronic pain, driving efforts to characterise how their organisation and function change during persistent pain states. Although most mechanistic insights come from animal studies, human neuroimaging, particularly since the advent of functional magnetic resonance imaging, has begun to map their location and engagement during pain modulation. Early work focused on forebrain regions due to the limited spatial resolution of standard MRI, but ultra-high-field functional magnetic resonance imaging now enables mm3-scale investigation of brainstem nuclei. This review synthesises evidence from animal and human studies to outline the best-characterised modulatory pathway, consisting of projections from the midbrain periaqueductal gray to the rostral ventromedial medulla and onward to the dorsal horn/spinal trigeminal nucleus, and highlights recent work detailing its organization.

title: Joint associations of handgrip strength and chair-stand performance with motoric cognitive risk syndrome in older adults.
authorString: Li Y, Wang X, Wang S, Liu F, Zhang Z, Zhu M, Li R, Liu R, Wang F, Li L, Yu Y, He C, Luo L, Fu C, Wei Q.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci
journal.title: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
journal.isoabbreviation: J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci

abstractText:
Background

Motor dysfunction is associated with cognitive vulnerability, but whether impairments across body regions jointly contribute to motoric cognitive risk syndrome (MCR) remains unclear. We examined the independent and joint associations of handgrip strength and chair-stand test (CST) with MCR.

Methods

This cross-sectional study included 6258 dementia-free older adults (mean age 71.5 ± 6.6 years; 63.1% women) from a community-based cohort. Handgrip strength and CST performance were used to define upper- and lower-extremity motor impairment. Participants were classified as normal, handgrip weakness only, CST impairment only, or combined motor impairment. Multivariable logistic regression was performed with adjustment for demographic, socioeconomic, lifestyle, and clinical factors. Additive and multiplicative interactions were assessed.

Results

MCR was present in 10.4% of participants. Using the A/B CST cutoff as the primary definition, adjusted odds ratios (95% confidence intervals) for MCR, compared with normal function, were 1.84 (1.14-2.97) for handgrip weakness only, 4.17 (2.97-5.85) for CST impairment only, and 9.17 (6.56-12.81) for combined motor impairment. Associations were directionally consistent across alternative CST cutoffs. A positive additive interaction was observed at the A/B CST cutoff (relative excess risk due to interaction = 3.48; attributable proportion = 0.40; and synergy index = 1.83), whereas multiplicative interaction was not positive.

Conclusions

Combined handgrip weakness and poorer CST performance were strongly associated with prevalent MCR. A positive additive interaction at the primary CST cutoff suggests that joint motor impairment may help characterize MCR-related vulnerability in older adults.

title: Digital Health Literacy in Adults With Heart Failure: Cross-Sectional Study.
authorString: Queiroz GCL, Nolêto AF, de Cassia Gengo E Silva Butcher R, de Sousa MM.
abstractText:
Background

Digital technology is increasingly used in heart failure (HF) management. Deficiencies in digital health literacy (DHL) may hinder the delivery of digitally mediated nursing care. Investigating sociodemographic and clinical factors associated with DHL in middle-income countries could inform targeted interventions to reduce disparities in HF management.

Objective

To examine associations between DHL and sociodemographic and clinical factors in adults with HF.

Methods

Descriptive, cross-sectional, and correlational study. The sample consisted of adult outpatients with HF from a cardiology clinic in João Pessoa, Brazil. Individuals with a clinical diagnosis of HF confirmed in the medical record, regardless of left ventricular ejection fraction, aged ≥18 years, were included. We obtained sociodemographic and clinical data through self-report. We assessed DHL using the eHealth Literacy Scale. We examined associations between sociodemographic and clinical variables and the digital literacy score using the Mann-Whitney or Kruskal-Wallis test and Spearman's correlation.

Results

The study included 109 participants (mean age, 59.1 years; 60% female). DHL was predominantly low. Age, education, and number of comorbidities were significantly associated with DHL.

Discussion

Age, education, and comorbidity burden may affect patients' ability to engage with digital technologies used in HF management in middle-income countries. Supporting patients' technological competencies may expand opportunities for digitally mediated caring relationships, enabling nurses to better understand and support individuals with HF in increasingly digital health care environments.

title: Pulmonary arterial hypertension-associated cerebellar impairment extends evidence linking cardiometabolic and neurodegenerative diseases.
authorString: Schwartz MW, Bornfeldt KE.
abstractText: Growing evidence shows that the risk of cognitive impairment is increased across a range of metabolic and cardiovascular diseases, but underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. One possibility involves activation of microglia, a glial cell type of the central nervous system with morphological and transcriptional features comparable to resident macrophages in other tissues that plays specialized roles in supporting neuronal and brain function. Combining clinical investigation in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) cohorts with mouse model and microglial cell culture studies, a study by Okawa, Shi, and colleagues in this issue of the JCI adds compelling, albeit indirect, evidence linking impaired lysosomal lipid handling in both endothelial cells and microglia to a specific neurological disorder associated with PAH. The findings open opportunities for understanding how cardiopulmonary disease predisposes to neurodegeneration.

title: A single liver-sparing myotropic AAV ameliorates muscular dystrophy in humanized mice by base editing.
authorString: Pien YC, Li H, Bulliard G, Liu H, Durbacz MZ, Xu Z, Chai AC, Chemello F, Sanchez-Ortiz E, Zabaleta N, Vandenberghe LH, Liu N, Olson EN.
abstractText: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is caused by mutations in the DMD gene, most of which are large exon deletions that result in loss of dystrophin protein. Adenine base editing (ABE) enables permanent gene correction by modifying splice sites to cause exon skipping and restoration of the DMD open reading frame. We previously demonstrated that adeno-associated virus 9-mediated (AAV9-mediated) delivery of adenine base editors allows efficient gene editing in mouse models of DMD. However, conventional AAV-based gene delivery approaches are complicated by their limited packaging capacity and high-dose-related toxicity. Here, we describe a single AAV vector encoding a compact adenine base editor, SlugABE8e, and a single-guide RNA, which enable efficient editing in a humanized DMD mouse model at a lower dose using the muscle-tropic MyoAAV4 capsid. Systemic MyoAAV4A delivery in juvenile DMD mice efficiently restored dystrophin expression in the heart and skeletal muscles. This molecular rescue was accompanied by reduced serum creatine kinase activity and diminished muscle pathology. A liver-detargeted MyoAAV4E-off capsid eliminated viral entry and editing in the liver. We also explored a high-fidelity base editor, SlugHF-ABE8e(V106W), which showed similar on-target and off-target editing to SlugABE8e. Together, these findings establish an all-in-one AAV strategy that efficiently mitigates DMD disease progression.

title: Cerebellar and frontal lobe alterations in pulmonary hypertension implicate an inflammatory lung vascular/brain axis.
authorString: Okawa S, Shi Y, Banerjee S, Tai YY, Nabhanizadeh J, Guenther S, Shah AN, Jiang S, Kim T, Al Aaraj Y, Pidro C, Aytekin M, Fatukasi O, Kalepalli N, Mettenburg J, Girard TD, Becker JT, Kaliyappan K, Song S, Breuils-Bonnet S, Provencher S, Bonnet S, Huppert T, Harvey LD, Nouraie SM, Savai R, Sun D, Umar S, Pullamsetti SS, Chan SY.
abstractText: Connections between vascular and neurocognitive diseases are emerging but remain poorly defined. Cognitive impairment is increasingly recognized in pulmonary hypertension (PH), a disease traditionally viewed as limited to the heart and lungs. Given that inflammation is shared by PH and neurodegenerative diseases, we investigated its role in driving brain and cognitive deficits in PH. Using structural and functional MRI data from UK Biobank (N = 248 PH) and a prospective validation cohort, we identified reduced cerebellar white matter volume, thinner frontal gyri, and weakened cerebellar-frontal connectivity in patients with PH but not in other heart or lung diseases. These changes were accompanied by worsened executive function and processing speed. Olink proteomics and targeted genomics linked inflammatory plasma proteins and a PH-associated nuclear receptor coactivator 7 (NCOA7) single nucleotide polymorphism, rs11154337, to these deficits. PH cerebellum showed increased microglial activation and white matter derangement. In PH mice, Ncoa7 deficiency worsened cerebellar inflammation and atrophy. Microglial functional assays, cerebellar single-nucleus RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomic analyses further implicated Ncoa7-dependent lysosomal, inflammatory, and cell-specific mechanisms of cerebellar pathobiology. These findings identify NCOA7-linked inflammatory dysfunction in the cerebellar-frontal axis in PH, redefining this disease with neurologic consequences and thus offering neural targets for diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic development.

title: Performance of the PREVENT-HF Equations Across Heart Failure Subtypes in Community-Based and Ambulatory Healthcare Samples.
authorString: Mounsey LA, Wang D, Ribeiro PH, Nemeth SM, Parekh JK, Strom JB, Ndumele C, Allen NB, Psaty B, Kizer JR, Levy D, de Boer RA, Maddah M, Khurshid S, Ellinor PT, Lau ES, Cunningham J, Khan SS, Ho JE.
abstractText:
Background

The PREVENT-HF equations estimate 10-year risk of overall heart failure (HF), inclusive of both HF with preserved and reduced ejection fraction (HFpEF; HFrEF). Given differential risk factor profiles, pathophysiology, and therapeutic strategies for each HF subtype, we sought to examine the performance of PREVENT-HF for subtype-specific risk assessment.

Methods

We included data from five pooled longitudinal cohort studies (baseline exam 1989 to 2013) and two longitudinal primary-care electronic health record-based samples (Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center [BIDMC], baseline 2004 to 2014; Mass General Brigham [MGB], baseline 2001 to 2018). We assessed the performance of the PREVENT-HF equations in predicting 10-year incident HFrEF and HFpEF, including model discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC]; average precision [AP]/event rate) and calibration (integrated calibration index [ICI]), in adults aged 30-79 years without prevalent cardiovascular disease or HF.

Results

The pooled cohort studies included 23,652 (55% women, age 60 ± 13 years), of whom 1,232 developed HF (432 [35%] HFpEF, 522 [42%] HFrEF). The BIDMC sample included 29,815 (55% women, 50 ± 13 years), of whom 259 (1%) developed HF (133 [51%] HFpEF, 101 [39%] HFrEF). MGB included 138,999 (62% women, 52 ± 13 years), of whom 1050 developed HF (586 [56%] HFpEF, 381 [36%] HFrEF). PREVENT-HF demonstrated better discrimination for HFpEF than HFrEF across all samples: in the pooled cohorts, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.824 (95% CI 0.807, 0.839) versus 0.789 (95% CI 0.770, 0.807) for HFrEF; in BIDMC, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.897 (95% CI 0.874, 0.918) versus 0.833 (95% CI 0.791, 0.869) for HFrEF; in MGB, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.864 (95% CI 0.848, 0.880) versus 0.797 (95% CI 0.771, 0.820) for HFrEF. Similar results were reflected in the AP/event rate ratios: 2.92 (95% CI 2.47, 3.54) for HFpEF compared to 2.66 (95% CI 2.33, 3.14) for HFrEF in the pooled cohorts; 8.08 (95% CI 6.12, 12.30) for HFpEF compared to 5.12 (95% CI 3.84, 8.17) for HFrEF in BIDMC; and 6.84 (95% CI 5.66, 8.28) for HFpEF compared to 4.12 (95% CI 3.37, 5.16) for HFrEF in MGB. Calibration was similar for HFpEF and HFrEF across samples. For example, in the pooled cohorts, the ICI for HFpEF was 0.041 (95% CI 0.039, 0.043) and for HFrEF was 0.038 (95% CI 0.036, 0.040).

Conclusions

PREVENT-HF demonstrated excellent discrimination for both HF subtypes across community-based cohorts and real-world samples, with consistently better discrimination for HFpEF as compared to HFrEF. Given PREVENT-HF was developed to estimate overall HF risk rather than subtype-specific risk, future studies are needed to establish subtype-specific risk thresholds.

title: Incidence of Cardiovascular Risk Factors, Physical Activity, and Diet in Law Enforcement Officers: A 6-Year Prospective Study.
authorString: Sire T, Gendron P, Poirier S.
abstractText:
Background

Law enforcement officers (LEOs) often display poor cardiovascular health, which can impair job performance and increase cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. While many cross-sectional studies have documented these issues, few have examined the progression of CVD risk factors over time, and none appear to have used a longitudinal design assessing incidence in relation to healthy lifestyle behaviors within a sex-representative sample of this occupation.

Methods

This prospective study followed 228 LEOs (28% women) over 6 years using online questionnaires assessing CVD risk factors, physical activity, and fruit and vegetable intake. Incidence of CVD risk factors was analyzed according to baseline physical activity (active vs. inactive), fruit and vegetable intake (≥5 vs. <5 servings/day), and their combined adherence.

Findings

Over time, participants showed significant increases in weight (p < .001, Cohen's d = .49), body mass index (p < .001, Cohen's d = .53), and prevalence of most CVD risk factors. Physically inactive LEOs demonstrated higher incidence of dyslipidemia (7% vs. 0%, p = .04, Cramer's V = .15) compared to active counterparts. Those consuming <5 daily servings of fruits and vegetables were more likely to develop hypertension (7% vs. 0%, p < .01, Cramer's V = .19) and dyslipidemia (8% vs. 1%, p = .01, Cramer's V = .18). The lowest cumulative incidence was observed among participants meeting both lifestyle recommendations.

Conclusions/application to practice

CVD risk factors increased over time in this LEO sample, with baseline physical inactivity and poor diet tending to predict greater incidence. These findings suggest the need for workplace health promotion programs targeting physical activity and healthy eating to reduce long-term CVD risk in this population.

title: Blood and urinary NT-proBNP: atrial fibrillation-associated patterns and cardiac dysfunction in acute chest pain.
authorString: Lang FI, Hupf J, Schlossbauer M, Staudner S, Leininger S, Vogel M, Allgaier R, Wallner S, Burkhardt R, Zimmermann M, Hubauer U, Luchner A, Maier L, Jungbauer C.
abstractText:
Introduction

NT-proBNP is the gold-standard biomarker for diagnosing and monitoring congestive heart failure (CHF); however, its role in detecting atrial fibrillation (AFib) is gaining attention. This study assessed the influence of aberrant cardiac rhythms on plasma NT-proBNP (pNT) considering urinary NT-proBNP (uNT) as a noninvasive alternative in selected clinical scenarios.

Methods

In 824 patients presenting with chest pain at the emergency department of the University Hospital of Regensburg, pNT was assessed. A subset of 355 patients additionally provided uNT.

Results

Both pNT and uNT were significantly increased in AFib, and lesser in atrial flutter (AFlut) and right ventricular (RV) pacing compared to SR (each p < 0.05). A pNT cutoff of 900 pg/mL yielded 74% sensitivity and 83% specificity for discriminating AFib from SR (AUC = 0.85). In multivariate regression, pNT or uNT and history of AFib were independent predictors of AFib (p < 0.05).

Conclusion

Both pNT and uNT are significantly elevated in AFib, and to a lesser extent AFlut, and RV pacing independently of heart failure. These findings align with prior observations and provide further evidence supporting adequately powered prospective studies to evaluate rhythm-adjusted diagnostic thresholds for CHF in AFib. In addition, uNT may complement pNT when venous access is difficult or serial remote monitoring is required.

title: Role of reverse remodelling in recurrence of atrial fibrillation after patient-tailored catheter ablation.
authorString: Obada GT, Ogbomo-Harmitt S, Deprez M, Vandersickel N, Aslanidi O.

journal.title: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background and aims

Catheter ablation (CA) is a curative treatment for atrial fibrillation (AF), yet success rates remain sub-optimal, with ∼50% of patients with persistent AF experiencing recurrence after 1 year. This may be due to the self-perpetuating nature of AF, which remodels atrial structure and cellular properties, while successful treatment can induce reverse remodelling (RR). This study develops a patient-specific CA strategy to directly target re-entrant drivers (RDs) and investigates the role of RR in AF recurrence.

Methods

Left atrial (LA) models were reconstructed from LGE-MRI scans of AF patients (n = 15) and coupled with the Courtemanche-Ramirez-Nattel (CRN) electrophysiology model. RDs were induced via pacing, identified using DGM analysis, and targeted ablation was performed in-silico. Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) was applied as a reference.
