Following termination, AF recurrence was tested under three levels of electrical reverse remodelling (ERR: 0%, 50%, and 100%), with and without structural reverse remodelling (SRR).

Results

Targeted ablation acutely terminated AF in all patient-specific models. After the first procedure, AF recurrence decreased progressively from 55% at 0% ERR to 36.7% at 50% ERR and 5% at 100% ERR; with additional SRR, recurrence was further reduced to 46.7%, 26.7%, and 0%, respectively. After the second CA procedure, AF recurrence rate was 42.9%, 17.9%, and 0% without SRR and 25%, 14.3%, and 0% with SRR.

Conclusion

This study highlights the importance of RR for therapy success, with a novel targeted CA technique ensuring <5% AF recurrence in patient-specific simulations. After clinical validation, this approach can help improve long-term patient outcomes.

title: Remote activity and rhythm monitoring using patient-owned consumer devices after first-time pulmonary vein isolation.
authorString: Lachmann K, Jaeckle S, Al-Taie C, Rieß JL, Lemoine MD, Schenker N, Nies M, van Elferen S, Baumbach J, Kas M, Reißmann B, Ouyang F, Fabritz L, Blankenberg S, Rillig A, Metzner A, Kirchhof P, Obergassel J.

journal.title: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background and aims

Passively collected physical activity data from consumer devices could provide a scalable, objective measure of functional status in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). This study assessed the feasibility of remotely collecting activity and rhythm data from patients undergoing index pulmonary vein isolation (PVI).

Methods

AF patients enrolled in the prospective TRUST registry who underwent index PVI and reported owning an eligible smartphone were re-contacted to provide informed consent and share their smartphone- and smartwatch-generated data. Pre-specified feasibility criteria were participation rate, technical success, and temporal data coverage. The primary functional outcome was the mean daily step-count change between the one-year pre-PVI and two-year post-PVI windows. Exploratory analyses examined associations of daily activity with AF recurrence and AF burden.

Results

Of 280 eligible patients, 172 (61%) attempted and 154/172 (90%) completed data transfer, of whom 123 met pre-specified completeness criteria. Median monitoring duration was 6.0 [3.6, 6.6] years, with 98% [77, 100] coverage. Mean daily step count increased from 5731±2808 to 6220±2816 steps/day after PVI (+488 steps/day [187, 789]; p=0.002). In 35 smartwatch users, AF burden decreased from 3.6% [1.6, 10.8] to 0.0% [0.0, 0.3] after PVI (p<0.001). Baseline AF burden was inversely correlated with daily step count (ρ=-0.36, p=0.035).

Conclusion

Remote collection of activity and rhythm data from consumer smartphones and smartwatches is feasible, yielding high-coverage, multi-year research data. This enables scalable, objective quantification of longitudinal functional outcomes. Daily step count increased after PVI in this exploratory cohort and was inversely related to baseline AF burden.

title: Selective Electrical Muscle Stimulation of the Vastus Medialis in a Patient With Knee Osteoarthritis, With Changes in Muscle Quality, Symptoms, and Physical Activity: A Case Report.
authorString: Tanino Y, Fukumoto Y, Kono T, Yoshida T.

journal.title: The American journal of case reports

abstractText: BACKGROUND Fat accumulation in the vastus medialis has been associated with the progression of knee osteoarthritis. Electrical muscle stimulation may reduce intramuscular fat accumulation by inducing contractions of the targeted muscle. We hypothesized that electrical stimulation of the vastus medialis would be associated with a reduction in intramuscular fat and improvement in self-reported symptoms during the observation period in a patient with knee osteoarthritis. CASE REPORT The patient was a 77-year-old man with Kellgren-Lawrence grade 2 right knee osteoarthritis. Because he also had hypertension and hyperlipidemia, he had maintained regular exercise habits, including aquatic walking; however, he discontinued these activities because of knee pain. Electrical stimulation was applied to the vastus medialis for 30 minutes per session, 3 times per week, for 4 weeks. Ultrasound echo intensity, an indirect indicator of intramuscular fat, and the Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score were assessed before and after the intervention. Compared with the pre-intervention value, vastus medialis echo intensity decreased by 13.7 arbitrary units (25.3%), and knee symptoms improved during the observation period. He resumed aquatic walking 2 weeks after electrical stimulation was initiated. CONCLUSIONS During the observation period, vastus medialis echo intensity decreased, Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score scores improved, and he resumed aquatic walking. However, because this was a single uncontrolled case and physical activity resumed during the intervention, these changes cannot be attributed to electrical stimulation alone; spontaneous improvement, behavioral reactivation, or a combination of these factors remain plausible. Controlled studies across different levels of disease severity are needed.

title: Ultrasound-based assessment of cardiac and hepatic dysfunction: current status and future directions.
authorString: Li YX, Chen L, Chen P, Wang YS, Shen R.
abstractText: Heart failure (HF) is a systemic syndrome in which venous congestion and impaired perfusion can produce clinically important hepatic dysfunction. The term cardiohepatic syndrome (CHS) describes this bidirectional interaction, but cardiac and hepatic abnormalities are still often evaluated in parallel rather than as a connected hemodynamic process. Ultrasound is uniquely suited to an integrated assessment because it can characterize cardiac structure and function, systemic venous congestion, hepatic hemodynamics, tissue stiffness, and treatment-related change at the bedside. Conventional transthoracic echocardiography remains the foundation of evaluation, while three-dimensional echocardiography and speckle-tracking techniques improve quantification of right ventricular, atrial, and subclinical myocardial dysfunction. Abdominal Doppler ultrasound, venous congestion scoring, and liver elastography add complementary information, although liver stiffness must be interpreted cautiously because congestion, inflammation, cholestasis, and fibrosis can produce overlapping signals. Artificial intelligence may improve acquisition, measurement reproducibility, and multimodal data integration, but external validation and transparent reporting remain essential. This review summarizes contemporary evidence and proposes a practical, sequential pathway that combines echocardiography, venous Doppler findings, liver stiffness, laboratory biomarkers, and dynamic reassessment after decongestion. The central clinical principle is that CHS should be evaluated as a time-varying cardiohepatic phenotype rather than diagnosed from a single cardiac, hepatic, or biochemical measurement.

title: TMT-based quantitative proteomic analysis of vitreous humor in proliferative diabetic retinopathy.
authorString: Xiong X, Zhou Q, Cao Y, Tang M, Xie L, Lv H.
abstractText:
Objective

To study the changes in vitreous humor protein profile of proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) and macular hole (MH)/epimacular membrane (EMM), and to identify potential candidate biomarkers for PDR by screening differentially expressed proteins (DEPs).

Methods

This study used tandem mass tag (TMT) combined with liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) to identify DEPs in vitreous samples from PDR patients and MH/EMM control patients. The identified DEPs were analyzed via bioinformatics methods to screen candidate proteins with research potential. Parallel reaction monitoring (PRM) technology was used to perform targeted validation of 30 proteins with potential regulatory effects in PDR.

Results

A total of 4812 peptides and 877 proteins were isolated and identified via TMT combined with LC-MS/MS proteomic analysis, including 59 DEPs (fold change > 1.2, P < 0.05). Bioinformatics analysis showed that DEPs were mainly involved in critical biological processes including cellular process, stimulus-response, biological regulation, localization, immune system process and metabolic process. A total of 23 proteins were successfully quantified via PRM validation, and the overall expression trends were consistent between TMT-based quantification and PRM results. Among them, coagulation factor V (FV), profilin-1 (PFN1), thioredoxin (TXN), ferritin light chain (FTL) and selenoprotein P (SeP) not only showed consistent and significant quantitative trends, but also reached statistical significance (P < 0.05) in both discovery and validation cohorts.

Conclusion

This study revealed significant alterations in the vitreous humor protein profile of PDR patients. The five identified candidate proteins (FV, PFN1, TXN, FTL, SeP) may serve as potential candidate biomarkers for PDR, providing new research directions and therapeutic targets for exploring the pathogenesis of PDR.

title: Integrative single cell and machine learning analysis identifies fibroblast centric hub genes and therapeutic candidates in lung adenocarcinoma and ischemic cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Pu Z, Liu Z, Zhang H, Han Y.
abstractText:
Background

Ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) are distinct diseases but may share fibroblast mediated mechanisms involving tissue remodeling and inflammation. However, their common molecular features at single cell resolution remain insufficiently defined.

Methods

We integrated single cell RNA sequencing datasets from ICM and LUAD with bulk transcriptomic profiles from TCGA LUAD, GSE18842, and GSE48166. Differential expression analysis identified 36 shared core genes. A total of 127 combinations of machine learning algorithms and feature selection methods were benchmarked to identify six hub genes: KRTCAP3, RUNX2, DBF4B, C11orf80, COL3A1, and ZFP64. UCell, scMetabolism, SCISSOR, Monocle 3, CellChat, scTenifoldNet/scTenifoldKnk, virtual drug screening, and molecular docking were used for functional characterization.

Results

Fibroblasts were the dominant cellular source of the six hub genes in both ICM and LUAD. COL3A1 progressively increased along fibroblast pseudotime trajectories. Virtual overexpression and knockout analyses showed convergence on extracellular matrix organization, inflammatory response, and immune regulation. Cell communication analysis identified fibroblasts as major senders of COLLAGEN signaling, with recipient cells shifting from inflammatory monocytes under normal conditions to proliferating macrophages in ICM and tumor cells in LUAD. Molecular docking nominated Digoxin, Ergotamine, and Ledipasvir as candidate RUNX2-binding compounds with favorable predicted docking scores.

Conclusions

This study provides a single cell framework linking ICM and LUAD through fibroblast driven extracellular matrix remodeling and inflammation, and identifies potential molecular targets and therapeutic candidates for further validation.

title: TREM2 encodes plaque macrophage plasticity to mediate atherosclerosis regression
authorString: Hillman H, Stuttgen GM, Lee S, Patterson MT, Chang MD, Zhou Y, Kennedy AE, Schrank PR, Mitha O, Barrett TJ, Colonna M, Williams JW.
abstractText: Cholesterol lowering therapies stabilize atherosclerotic plaque and reduce ischemic events, but the molecular mechanisms governing plaque remodeling or regression remain poorly defined. The lipid sensor TREM2 is a key modulator of plaque-associated foam cell development and was upregulated by plaque macrophages in atherosclerosis regression. We examined macrophage- or monocyte-specific  Trem2 deletion during regression in mice and found that TREM2 expression on plaque macrophages, not newly recruited monocytes, was required for plaque regression.  Trem2 deletion impeded necrotic core resolution, leading us to interrogate the efferocytic capacity of TREM2  + cells during lipid lowering. An  in vitro model of cholesterol-experienced ex-lipid associated macrophages “Ex-LAMs” demonstrated that prior lipid priming enhanced efferocytic ability after unloading lipids and maintained expression of lysosomal and cytoskeletal remodeling genes. Augmented TREM2 signaling through genetic models or agonist treatment accelerated efferocytic ability in vitro and plaque regression in vivo. Thus, we posit that a TREM2-dependent ExLAM programming drives atherosclerosis resolution and facilitates beneficial plaque remodeling through enhanced efferocytosis. Overall, targeting the TREM2 pathway may be a viable strategy for stabilizing atherosclerotic plaques in patients treated with aggressive cholesterol control.

title: Advanced Cardiovascular Disease in Marbach-Rustad Progeroid Syndrome (LEMD2 p.Ser479Phe).
authorString: Delamain TRB, Casarini G, Delamain JHH, Boya C, Correia EB, Salvador P, Siqueira D, Della Togna D, Feres F, Franchini KG.
abstractText:
Background

Marbach-Rustad progeroid syndrome results from the recurrent heterozygous LEMD2 c.1436C>T (p.Ser479Phe) variant. Four cases have been reported, with cardiac involvement absent or only qualitatively described.

Case summary

A 30-year-old man with short stature, skeletal fragility, and facial dysmorphism presented with syncope from high-grade atrioventricular block. Echocardiography showed premature severe calcific aortic stenosis and mild mitral stenosis. Cardiac magnetic resonance showed preserved biventricular function with no late gadolinium enhancement; computed tomography confirmed valvular calcification but no coronary calcium. Chagas serology was negative. Whole-genome sequencing confirmed the p.Ser479Phe variant. He received a permanent pacemaker and, 6 months later, transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Evaluation also revealed overt type 2 diabetes, severe hypertriglyceridemia, and nephropathy: the most advanced metabolic phenotype reported.

Discussion

This case shows that the p.Ser479Phe variant can cause advanced, intervention-requiring cardiovascular disease (objectively quantified and, to our knowledge, the first in vivo characterization by cardiac magnetic resonance). These findings support routine cardiac and metabolic surveillance in LEMD2-associated progeroid syndromes.

title: Blueberry phytochemicals modulate the gut-vascular axis through microbiome-metabolome interaction.
authorString: Satheesh Babu AK, Petersen C, Robeson MS, Iglesias-Carres L, Paz HA, Ratliff JG, Zhong Y, Bell R, Shankar K, Wankhade UD, Neilson AP, Anandh Babu PV.
abstractText: Dietary phytochemicals are metabolized by gut microbes into bioactive metabolites that mediate their physiological effects. This study investigated whether microbiome-metabolome interactions contribute to the vascular benefits of blueberry phytochemicals via the gut-vascular axis. Both conventionally raised and germ-free mice received freeze-dried blueberries via oral gavage, and plasma metabolites were analyzed at multiple time points. In other cohorts, mice were fed a standard or high-fat diet (HFD) with or without freeze-dried blueberry powder (∼1.5 human servings) and treated with or without antibiotics (Abx; to deplete gut microbes) for 12 weeks. Metabolic parameters, vascular endpoints, plasma metabolites, and the gut microbiome were assessed. Blueberry intake increased plasma blueberry-derived metabolites in conventionally raised but not germ-free mice, indicating that gut microbes are essential for metabolizing phytochemicals. This was also confirmed in Abx-treated mice. Blueberries reduced HFD-induced vascular inflammation. However, microbial depletion reduced plasma blueberry metabolites and abolished the benefits of blueberries in reducing vascular inflammation. HFD-enriched genera such as Faecalimonas were positively associated, whereas blueberry-derived metabolites (hippuric acid and 3-hydroxy hippuric acid) were negatively associated with vascular inflammation. Furthermore, Turicibacter and Clostridia UGC-014 (incertae sedis), which are enriched by dietary blueberries, were positively associated with hippuric acid. These findings provide insight into the importance of the interaction between the microbiome and metabolome in regulating the benefits of dietary phytochemicals on vascular inflammation via the gut-vascular axis.

title: Carotid Intima-Media Thickness and Plaque Burden in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Hospital-based Case-Control Study.
authorString: Patil H, Vaithinathan P, Babu P, Vaithiyanathan S.
abstractText:
Background

Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) accelerates atherosclerosis, and carotid ultrasonographic assessment of intima-media thickness (IMT) and plaque offers a noninvasive method to detect subclinical vascular disease and stratify cardiovascular risk.

Objective

To evaluate and compare the IMT of the common and internal carotid arteries between patients with T2DM and age- and sex-matched healthy individuals.

Materials and methods

This single-center, hospital-based analytical case-control study included 40 patients with T2DM and 40 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Participants underwent clinical and biochemical assessment, and carotid IMT (common and internal carotid arteries) and plaque were measured using high-resolution B-mode ultrasonography.

Results

Among 80 participants (40 T2DM cases and 40 controls), the groups were comparable in age (52.4 ± 14.9 vs. 51.7 ± 18.7 years; P = 0.843), sex and lifestyle factors. Body mass index was slightly higher in cases (26.9 ± 4.9 vs. 25.1 ± 3.0 kg/m2; P = 0.052). Cases had significantly higher systolic blood pressure/diastolic blood pressure (142.6 ± 11.4/87.3 ± 4.6 vs. 127.4 ± 7.2/84.1 ± 5.6 mmHg) and markedly higher glycemic indices (fasting blood sugar 160.9 vs. 90.1; postprandial blood sugar 224.9 vs. 109.9 mg/dL; all P ≤ 0.006). Triglycerides, very-low-density lipoprotein and total cholesterol were higher in cases, while high-density lipoprotein and low-density lipoprotein were similar. Mean carotid IMT was greater in cases (0.72 ± 0.17 vs. 0.61 ± 0.19 mm; P = 0.006) and plaque was more frequent (50% vs. 17.5%; P = 0.002). IMT was not significantly associated with age or lifestyle factors. Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed fair discrimination (area under the curve 0.686; P = 0.004); IMT >0.62 mm yielded 70% sensitivity and 65% specificity.

Conclusion

Patients with T2DM had significantly higher carotid IMT and plaque prevalence than controls, supporting carotid ultrasonography as a useful tool for detecting subclinical atherosclerosis and aiding cardiovascular risk stratification.

title: Influence of Geometry, Class Imbalance and Alignment on Phantom Reconstruction Accuracy - A Micro-CT Phantom-Based Evaluation.
authorString: K M AK, Raut SS.
abstractText: The accuracy of the 3D models created from medical scans depends on every stage of the pipeline - segmentation, alignment, and surface extraction. Although segmentation algorithms are well established, the effects of the type of geometry, class imbalance and voxel and point cloud alignment on accuracy remain to be sufficiently explored. This work evaluates the reconstruction accuracy and also studies the effect of voxel alignment on overlap accuracy metrics using controlled perturbation analysis. A sphere, a facemask, and an abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) were printed using the stereolithography technique and scanned using a micro-CT machine. Segmentation was performed using Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM), Otsu thresholding and region-growing (RG) based methods. Segmented and reference models were aligned using the Kabsch-Umeyama (KU) algorithm to evaluate Dice and Jaccard scores, precision, among others. A sensitivity analysis quantified the effect of controlled translational (±5 voxels) and rotational (±5°) perturbations on post-KU-aligned voxel grids. Surface meshes, generated using the marching cubes algorithm, were registered with reference meshes using RANSAC and ICP alignment process. Otsu thresholding yielded highest accuracy for all the geometries. The sphere, with uniform curvature and no thin-walled regions, showed the lowest sensitivity to alignment error. AAA yielded low overlap scores due to its small wall thickness and sensitivity to misalignment. AAA model was most sensitive to misalignment, with Dice and Jaccard scores decreasing by more than 90% under 5° rotation and by over 60% due to just 1°. The facemask surface was most error-prone, possibly due to misalignment during the ICP process. The Jaccard index yields numerically lower values and larger relative changes under perturbations than the Dice score, making alignment sensitivity more apparent for thin-walled structures. Even a sub-millimetre error in voxel alignment adversely affects accuracy. Surface-based accuracy metrics differed from the voxel-based trends, and this divergence carries diagnostic value.

title: Association of Central Arterial Stiffening with Myocardial Oxygen Supply-Demand Indices in Healthy Adults.
authorString: Sakamoto R, Taniai N, Hayashi K, Tanaka H, Sugawara J.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
journal.title: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
journal.isoabbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol

abstractText: Central arterial stiffening may increase systolic aortic impedance and reduce diastolic perfusion pressure, thereby impairing myocardial oxygen supply-demand balance. We tested the hypothesis that longitudinal changes in proximal aortic stiffness are more closely associated with changes in subendocardial viability ratio (SEVR) and its constituent systolic and diastolic pressure-time indices than changes in overall aortic stiffness. We investigated 10-year longitudinal changes in central arterial stiffness in 64 adults spanning a wide age range (19-73 years at pre-measurement). Carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cfPWV) was measured as the reference standard for aortic stiffness, whereas heart-brachial PWV (hbPWV) was used as an index of aortic stiffness for more proximal segment. Aortic pressure waveform was derived from carotid arterial pressure, and SEVR was calculated as the ratio of diastolic to systolic aortic pressure-time integrals. cfPWV and hbPWV increased, whereas SEVR decreased over the follow-up period in all age groups (p<0.01). Although changes in hbPWV were positively associated with changes in both systolic and diastolic pressure-time indices (r=0.41 and r=0.55, respectively; both p<0.01), they were not associated with changes in SEVR (r=0.02, p=0.87). Changes in cfPWV were not significantly associated with changes in either pressure-time index or SEVR. These results suggest that longitudinal changes in proximal aortic stiffness are associated with changes in the individual pressure-time indices of myocardial oxygen demand and supply, but not with changes in their balance as assessed by SEVR.

title: Maternal exposure to extreme temperatures and congenital heart disease: Assessing independent effects and interaction with residential green space.
authorString: Gao W, Pan L, Zhang H, Sun H, Yang Y, Wang Z, Li Y, Yang H, Li W, Chang Y, Li W, Zhang W, Tang NJ, Leng J.

journal.title: International journal of hygiene and environmental health

abstractText: Research on the association between temperature and congenital heart disease (CHD) is relatively limited. This study aims to evaluate the effects of extreme temperature events on CHD morbidity, utilizing apparent temperature data. We conducted a 1:1 matched case-control study in Tianjin, China, including 1540 mother-infant pairs with CHD and their corresponding controls. We calculated maternal exposure to apparent temperature and Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) exposures during weeks 3 to 8 of gestation. Conditional logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between extreme temperature events and CHD, and to assess their additive interactive effects with NDVI. Maternal exposure to extreme cold events during pregnancy significantly increased the risk of CHD in offspring (moderate extreme cold event: OR = 3.11). Pregnant women exposed to low NDVI levels (≤0.25) exhibited consistently higher CHD risks. Notably, the risk of CHD increased sharply during exposure to extreme cold events (OR up to 7.32), and a suggestive positive interactive trend was observed between severe extreme heat and low NDVI (RERI = 1.60), though it did not reach statistical significance. Furthermore, pregnant women whose last menstrual period (LMP) occurred during the cold season exhibited greater susceptibility to extreme cold, whereas those with an LMP in the warm season were more vulnerable to the adverse effects of extreme heat. Maternal exposure to extreme temperature events during weeks 3 to 8 of gestation significantly increases the risk of CHD in offspring.

title: Non-Invasive Markers of Liver Fibrosis in Patients After Fontan Surgery: A Case Series
authorString: ALVARENGA LR, MÖLLER PR, OLIVEIRA CP, BELLOMO-BRANDAO MÂ.
abstractText: Background Fontan circulation predisposes patients to Fontan-Associated Liver Disease (FALD), characterized by chronic congestion and progressive hepatic fibrosis. Although liver biopsy is the gold standard for fibrosis assessment, its use is limited owing to the risk of complications in these patients. In this context, liver elastography and non-invasive serum markers of fibrosis, such as APRI and FIB-4, have been proposed as alternatives for liver monitoring; however, their applicability and correlation with the progression of FALD in pediatric patients remain uncertain. Methods This was an observational case series cohort with both retrospective and prospective components, including patients with univentricular congenital heart disease who underwent the Fontan procedure and had liver elastography performed during follow-up. Liver stiffness was assessed using the 2D-SWE method. Clinical and laboratory data (AST, ALT, and platelets count) were collected to calculate APRI and FIB-4. Spearman correlation and partial correlation analyses were performed to identify factors associated with liver elastography. In the subgroup with longitudinal assessments, paired tests were applied. Results A total of 32 patients (62.5% male) were included with a mean age of 3.75 ± 1.77 years at the time of Fontan surgery and 13.83 ± 8.18 years at the time of elastography evaluation. The mean liver stiffness was 12.05 ± 2.49 kPa. No significant correlation was found between liver elastography and APRI or FIB-4, nor was there any association with sex, age at surgery, or age at elastography evaluation. In the longitudinal subgroup (N = 22), no significant variation was observed between LE1 and LE2, nor were there relevant changes in APRI and FIB-4 over time. Conclusions In pediatric post-Fontan patients, liver elastography did not correlate with APRI or FIB-4, nor with the clinical variables analyzed, in both cross-sectional and longitudinal assessments. The findings suggest limitations of serum markers and reinforce the need for specific and validated strategies for liver monitoring in this population.

title: Noninvasive Insights: Magnetic Resonance Elastography and Ultrasound Liver Elastography for the Assessment of Liver Fibrosis in Fontan-Associated Liver Disease: A Comparative Study with Histology.
authorString: Sethasathien S, Sittiwangkul R, Leerapun A, Kongkarnka S, Inmutto N, Prasankittirach P, Wongyikul P, Phinyo P, Silvilairat S.
abstractText: The diagnostic performance of ultrasound (U/S) elastography and magnetic resonance elastography (MRE) of liver relative to histological assessment in Fontan patients remains uncertain. This study sought to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy and agreement of MRE and U/S elastography compared with histological congestive hepatic fibrosis score (CHFS) staging. We conducted a cross-sectional study in Fontan patients. Patients were categorized into non-significant fibrosis (≤ 2 A) and advanced fibrosis (≥ 2B) groups according to the CHFS scoring system. This study included 34 Fontan patients with a mean age of 20.2 ± 6 years, 23 (67.6%) had fibrosis ≥2B. The majority of whom had undergone an extracardiac conduit Fontan procedure. Hemodynamic parameters were similar between groups. MRE values were significantly higher in the fibrosis group (5.0 ± 0.9 vs. 4.1 ± 1.1 kPa, p = 0.018), whereas U/S elastography values did not differ significantly (p = 0.568). MRE demonstrated fair agreement with biopsy (quadratic-weighted κ = 0.468), while ultrasound showed no meaningful agreement (κ=-0.057). MRE demonstrated acceptable discriminative performance (AUC 0.77; 95% CI: 0.57-0.97), whereas ultrasound elastography showed poor discrimination (AUC 0.44; 95% CI: 0.21-0.66), both estimated from the continuous liver stiffness value in kilopascals; the two areas under the curve differed by 0.33 (95% CI: 0.06-0.60; DeLong p = 0.018). MRE demonstrates better agreement with histology and higher diagnostic performance compared with U/S elastography in Fontan patients. However, its discriminatory capacity, as reflected by AUC, remains lower than that reported in other chronic liver diseases. These findings highlight the unique pathophysiological substrate of Fontan-associated liver disease and underscore the need to establish disease-specific MRE cut-off values for each staging system to achieve more accurate fibrosis stratification and meaningful clinical application.

title: MicroRNA expressions in right ventricular outflow tract myocardium correlate with pulmonary valve size in patients with tetralogy of Fallot.
authorString: Suzuki H, Kotani Y, Kasahara S, Shimizu S.
abstractText:
Objectives

Although microRNAs are critical regulators of mRNA, and dysregulation may contribute to the development of tetralogy of Fallot (TOF), the precise mechanism remains unknown. We aimed to compare microRNA expressions in the right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) myocardium between patients with different surgical repair types to evaluate the impact on disease severity.

Methods

RVOT myocardial tissues were collected from patients at definitive surgery for TOF. Patients who underwent transannular patch or infundibular patch repair were classified as the infundibular repair group, and others as the non-infundibular repair group. MicroRNA expression levels in these tissues were measured quantitatively using microarray. MicroRNA expression levels were compared between the two groups, and the correlations between microRNA expression levels and pulmonary valve diameter indexed to body surface area were analyzed.

Results

948 microRNAs were identified out of 2,632 available sequences from 21 patients. The expression levels of 48 microRNAs differed between the infundibular repair and non-infundibular repair groups (p < 0.05 before false discovery rate correction). Forty-four microRNAs were upregulated, and four were downregulated in the non-infundibular repair group compared to the infundibular repair group. Furthermore, among these 48 microRNAs, 11 microRNAs demonstrated significant correlations with pulmonary valve size in both Pearson's and Spearman's analyses. Four of these microRNAs showed strong correlation coefficients greater than 0.50 across both analyses.

Conclusions

Differential expression of several microRNAs in RVOT myocardium was significantly associated with pulmonary valve size. These identified microRNAs may provide molecular pathways for future studies investigating the mechanisms underlying RVOT development.

title: Potent P2Y<sub>12</sub> inhibitor monotherapy versus dual antiplatelet therapy in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention: Rationale and design of the STARS DAPT randomized pilot trial.
authorString: Iglesias JF, Stähli B, Heg D, Candreva A, Garin D, Muresan M, Valgimigli M, Roffi M.
abstractText:
Background

Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) for 12 months is the current standard of care for patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Recent evidence indicates that potent oral P2Y12 inhibitor-based single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT) after 1 to 3 months of DAPT following drug-eluting-stent (DES) implantation reduces major bleeding events without increasing the risk of major ischemic outcomes in patients with acute coronary syndrome. However, the optimal timing of aspirin discontinuation in STEMI patients treated with P2Y12 inhibitor-based SAPT remains uncertain.

Design

STARS DAPT is an investigator-initiated, prospective, multicenter, open-label, precision-based, randomized controlled pilot trial with a blinded outcome assessment. Patients with STEMI who underwent successful primary PCI of the culprit lesion with a newer-generation polymer-free DES will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to potent P2Y12 inhibitor-based SAPT (with aspirin discontinued after an initial period of DAPT during the index hospitalization and before hospital discharge) for 12 months vs. standard DAPT for 12 months. The primary efficacy endpoint is the rate of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), defined as the composite of all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial re-infarction, non-fatal stroke, urgent target vessel revascularization, or definite/probable stent thrombosis, at 12 months. The primary safety endpoint is Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) class 3 or 5 major bleeding at 12 months. The study is designed to provide estimates of treatment effects and their precision to inform the design of a subsequent larger randomized trial.

Enrolment status

The trial aims to recruit a total of 350 patients. The first patient was enrolled on December 1, 2025.

Conclusion

STARS DAPT is a randomized pilot study assessing the safety and efficacy of a potent oral P2Y12 inhibitor-based SAPT strategy, with aspirin discontinued after an initial period of DAPT during the index hospitalization and before hospital discharge, following primary PCI with a newer-generation polymer-free DES in patients with STEMI. The findings will inform future large-scale trial design and may help optimize antiplatelet strategies and guide clinical decision-making after primary PCI.

Trial registration

Clinicaltrials.gov: Identifier, NCT05785897.

Funding source

Unrestricted research grant from Concept Medical (Tampa, FL, USA) to Geneva University Hospitals, Switzerland.

title: Intravascular Lithotripsy for Severely Calcified Coronary Lesions: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
authorString: Campane RZ, Kuniyoshi GM, Ujjawal A, Taghizade N, Hoffman Filho CR, Mukhtar N, Piovesan A, Silva WC, Abizaid A, Stone GW.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Evogliptin in Mild to Moderate Calcific Aortic Valve Stenosis: The EVOID-AS Trial Rationale and Study Design.
authorString: Padang R, Hodara R, Jan MF, Jain R, Postalian A, Zweig BM, Naqvi TZ, Levine RA, Dal-Bianco JP, Argulian E, Pressman GS, Sengupta PP, Abbas AE, Cheng W, Patel AK, Bhave NM, Chung ES, Sanchecirf CE, Barrett TC, Kort S, Sohn J, Pollak P, Ali MT, Chadderdon S, Zhao Q, Gill E, El Sakr F, Pereira NL, Vella A, Schulte PJ, Bailey KR, Song JK, Oh JK.
abstractText: The only treatment of severe aortic stenosis (AS) is aortic valve replacement. No medical therapy has been proven effective for preventing or delaying AS progression despite several clinical trials. The EVOID-AS trial is designed to evaluate the efficacy of evogliptin, a dipeptidyl peptidase 4 inhibitor, at retarding the progression of aortic valve calcification and AS hemodynamic severity in patients with mild to moderate AS. In this trial, 580 patients with mild or moderate native calcific AS at 40+ clinical sites across the United States and Canada will be randomized in a 1:1 allocation to receive either evogliptin 10 mg or placebo once daily orally for 2 years. Clinical follow-up visits are scheduled at 3-month intervals; transthoracic echocardiography, aortic valve computed tomography calcium score, and laboratory testing are obtained at baseline, 1-year, and 2-year study visits. The primary end point is change in aortic valve calcification as measured by cardiac computed tomography at 2 years of therapy. Secondary end points are progression of AS hemodynamic severity by echocardiography during 2 years of therapy and time to aortic valve intervention. Secondary safety end points include incidence and severity of treatment-emergent or serious adverse events. Enrollment began in June 2022, and the study is expected to be completed in 2028. EVOID-AS is a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized medical trial to modify the progression of calcific AS. This trial will contribute to the critical unmet clinical need of identifying an effective medical therapy to prevent or to delay the progression of AS. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05143177.
