title: How Does Place of Residence Influence the Experience and Management of Chronic Non-Malignant Pain? A Systematic Review.
authorString: Stylianou C, Adam R, Kwushue F, Nicholl BI.
abstractText:
Background and objective

Chronic non-malignant pain (CNMP) affects up to half of the UK population and one third of adults globally. Rural populations experience poorer health outcomes across several chronic conditions; however, the influence of place of residence on CNMP management, outcomes and experiences remains unclear. This systematic review examined how place of residence (urban or rural) impacts CNMP management, outcomes and experiences.

Methods

PubMed, psycINFO, Medline, Embase and CINAHL databases were searched for qualitative and quantitative studies. Dual title/abstract screening and full-text review were undertaken against pre-defined inclusion/exclusion criteria. A narrative synthesis was performed.

Results

Of 2341 titles screened, 16 studies were included (12 observational, three qualitative and one mixed-methods study). Most studies were rated as fair quality, with limitations including unsatisfactory response rates and non-validated outcome measures. Rural residents were more likely to use primary care and opioid-based treatments, whereas urban residents had greater access to specialist pain services. Outcomes were less consistent; several studies reported poorer pain-related outcomes among rural residents, although some identified no significant differences compared with urban populations. Long travel distances, prolonged waiting times and limited specialist and non-pharmacological services were barriers to care.

Conclusions

This review highlights geographic inequalities in CNMP management and experiences. Findings should be interpreted in light of methodological limitations and study heterogeneity. Targeted approaches are needed to improve equitable access to pain management across settings.

Significance statement

This systematic review synthesises evidence on how geographic location influences the management, outcomes and experiences of people with chronic non-malignant pain. The findings identify consistent rural-urban disparities in access to evidence-based pain care and highlight important gaps in the current literature, including the limited availability of high-quality comparative studies. These findings provide a foundation for future research and inform the development of more equitable pain services.

Trial registration

PROSPERO number: CRD42024522734.

title: Prevalence of Diabetes in Low- and Middle-Income Countries' Incarcerated Populations: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Wasti SA, Wasti A, Ahmed A, Sabir B, Asif A, Qayyum SN, Naveed H, Saleem NUA, Iqbal MU, Saeed H, Woldu D, Ahmad SA, Saddique MN.
abstractText:
Background and aims

Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a major global health concern, particularly in resource-constrained settings. Incarcerated populations in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) face increased health risks and limited care access, yet remain understudied. No prior systematic review has synthesized prevalence data for this group. This review aims to estimate diabetes prevalence among incarcerated individuals in LMICs.

Methods

We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis per PRISMA and GATHER guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science and regional databases were searched till May 2025. Random-effects models with Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation were applied in R (version 4.5.1). Publication bias was assessed using DOI plots. Study quality was evaluated with the Joanna Briggs Institute tool, and certainty of evidence was appraised using an adapted GRADE approach.

Results

Twenty-three studies (107,473 participants) were included. Mean participant ages varied from 29 ± 9.6 to 40.5 ± 9.8 years. The tentative pooled estimate of diabetes prevalence was 3.7% (95% CI: [2.5%-5.1%], Prediction Interval [0%-12.2%]), with high heterogeneity (I2 = 95.4%). The pooled prevalence estimate was highest in Asia (5.2%), particularly Pakistan (9.8%), and lowest in South America (2.3%). The DOI plot revealed major asymmetry, indicating a high possibility of publication bias. Overall certainty of evidence was rated as very low for diabetes prevalence due to risk of bias and publication bias. Interpretation of the pooled estimate is limited by substantial heterogeneity and limitations in the primary studies, including differences in diabetes ascertainment methods.

Conclusion

Diabetes is an important health concern among incarcerated populations in LMICs. Differences in diabetes ascertainment methods, participant characteristics and correctional healthcare systems may have potentially contributed to the variability of the pooled estimates. A hypothesis is that there may also be potentially limited detection or underdiagnosis which possibly could have contributed to the observed prevalence estimates.

title: [Aortic root replacement with a stentless xenograft (Freestyle®) in Iceland - indications and outcome].
authorString: Gunnarsson HI, Vidisson KO, Gudbjartsson T.
abstractText:
Introduction

Aortic root replacement (ARR) can be performed with a stentless porcine xenograft (Freestyle®) as an alternative to the conventional Bentall-procedure, where mechanical or stented bioprosthetic are sewn into a wov-en tube-graft. We examined early and late outcomes of Freestyle®-ARR in a whole-nation cohort, focusing on indications and surgical outcomes.

Materials and methods

A retrospective analysis that included 44 consecutive Freestyle®-ARR performed at Landspitali 2002-2018. Primary outcomes were 30-day and long-term survival (Kaplan-Meier), with a median follow-up of 111 months. Secondary outcomes included early postoperative complications and late reoperations.

Results

A median of three cases was performed per year (range 0-5). The most common indication was dilated aortic root (70%), followed by Type-A aortic dissection (9%) and small aortic annulus during aortic valve replacement (9%). Average age was 62 years and 65% were male. Median EuroSCORE-II was 11% (range 3-71%), cardiopulmonary bypass time 234 min. and cross-clamp time 157 min. The most common postoperative complications were new-onset atrial fibrillation (51%) and perioperative myocardial infarction (14%). Postoperative length of stay was 12 days median and 30-day mortality 14% (n=6). At follow-up, 1- and 5-year survival rates were 81% and 74%, respectively. For patients surviving the first 30 days, 5-year survival was 86%, and at long-term follow-up only three patients (7%) had undergone reoperation.

Conclusions

Freestyle®-ARR is a technically challenging operation and is associated with high short-term mortality rates compared with regular AVR. However, long term survival was favourable, and reoperations were uncommon in those surviving to discharge.

title: 1-Year Safety and Effectiveness of a Next-Generation Dual-Seal Left Atrial Appendage Occluder.
authorString: Lakkireddy D, Makkar A, Alkhouli M, Freixa X, Manoukian G, Agarwal H, Abuissa H, Awad K, Cuoco F, Dohadwala M, Ellis CR, Shah D, De Backer O, Chinitz L, Nielsen-Kudsk JE, Horton RP, Schmidt B, Natale A, Reddy VY, Sabir SA, Weiler C, Nair D, VERITAS Investigators.
abstractText:
Background

Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is a stroke prevention alternative for patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) intolerant to long-term oral anticoagulation (OAC). The next-generation dual-seal device was designed to improve operator ease of use while maintaining effective LAAO of the predicate device.

Objectives

The purpose of this analysis was to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of a next-generation device through 1 year.

Methods

VERITAS is a single-arm, prospective, global, multicenter study. Patients with nonvalvular AF with an increased thromboembolism risk seeking a nonpharmacologic alternative to OAC were enrolled. One-year descriptive endpoints are provided, including mortality, neurological events, major bleeding, and device-related complications. One-year cardiac imaging was assessed for peridevice leak and device-related thrombus (DRT).

Results

Complete left atrial appendage (LAA) closure (0 mm leak) was observed in 91.1% (95% CI: 87.9%-93.7%) of patients by either transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) or cardiac computed tomography and 96.3% (95% CI: 93.2%-98.2%) by TEE alone. The cumulative DRT rate was 3.3% (95% CI: 2.0%-5.3%) with only 0.4% (95% CI: 0.1%-1.5%) deemed clinically relevant. One-year key clinical outcome rates are as follows: all-cause mortality: 3.9% (95% CI: 2.4%-6.3%); cardiovascular mortality: 1.9% (95% CI: 0.9%-3.8%); major bleeding: 6.6% (95% CI: 4.5%-9.2%); ischemic stroke or systemic embolism: 1.8% (95% CI: 0.8%-3.3%); pericardial effusion requiring intervention: 0.9% (95% CI: 0.3%-2.1%). No (0%) device embolization occurred. Median follow-up was 365 days (IQR: 349-380 days).

Conclusions

The VERITAS study results support the 1-year safety and effectiveness of the next-generation device. (Abbott Medical-VERITAS Study; NCT06707688).

title: Functional outcomes and quality of life after endovascular thrombectomy in large and extensive infarcts (ASPECTS 0-5): a multicentre registry study.
authorString: Asperger H, Bode FJ, Ebrahimi T, Klehr L, Layer J, Meißner J, Nitsch L, Shirvani O, Thielscher CS, von Danwitz NM, Odensaß S, Stösser S, Dorn F, Petzold GC, Weller J, GSR-ET Investigators.
abstractText:
Introduction

Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) is established for large infarcts, but remains cautiously applied in extensive infarcts with an Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) of 0-2. Real-life outcome data remain limited.

Patients and methods

Retrospective analysis of the German Stroke Registry-Endovascular Treatment comparing extensive (ASPECTS 0-2) and large infarcts (ASPECTS 3-5) in patients with anterior-circulation occlusion and EVT. The primary outcome was the ordinal 90-day mRS distribution; secondary outcomes were mRS 0-3, survival, quality of life (3-level European Quality of Life-5 Dimensions) and living condition.

Results

Of 18,069 screened patients, 889 were analysed (ASPECTS 1-2, n = 89; ASPECTS 3-5, n = 800); none had ASPECTS 0. With ASPECTS 1-2, 20.2% achieved mRS 0-3 and 55.1% died within 90 days. In the model including successful reperfusion, no statistically significant association was detected between infarct group and the 90-day mRS distribution (common odds ratio [cOR] 0.80; 95% CI, 0.53-1.23) or mRS 0-3 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.89; 95% CI, 0.64-1.25), whereas successful reperfusion was associated with both (cOR 3.68; 95% CI, 2.31-5.85 and aOR 4.10; 95% CI, 2.45-6.86). Among survivors, median European Quality of Life-5 Dimensions utility index was 0.445 vs 0.541 (n = 27/324), and 51.5% vs 50.9% lived at home (n = 33/411).

Discussion

An extensive infarct carried a challenging prognosis, yet acceptable outcome and non-institutional living remained achievable in a relevant minority. An independent association of infarct group with outcome was not detected.

Conclusion

An acceptable outcome remained attainable in selected patients with extensive infarction, particularly after successful reperfusion. Lacking a medically managed comparator, these data describe prognosis rather than treatment effect.

title: Serum brain-derived tau in lacunar stroke and cerebral small vessel disease.
authorString: Gattringer T, Haidegger M, Tafrali C, Martinez-Serrat M, Pinter D, Fandler-Höfler S, Kneihsl M, Seiler S, Eppinger S, Kiss C, Bichler R, Haindl MT, Ropele S, Enzinger C, Khalil M.
abstractText:
Introduction

Brain-derived tau (BD-tau) selectively quantifies tau of central nervous system origin in blood and has demonstrated strong correlations with infarct volume and functional outcome in general ischaemic stroke, but data in lacunar stroke and cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) are lacking.

Patients and methods

In a prospectively collected cohort of 101 lacunar stroke patients with an MRI-confirmed recent small subcortical infarct (RSSI) and 47 controls, we measured serum BD-tau using the HD-X SIMOA platform at baseline and 3 and 15 months after stroke. We examined associations of BD-tau with infarct size, chronic CSVD neuroimaging features (white matter hyperintensities [WMHs], lacunes, microbleeds, total SVD score), CSVD progression on follow-up MRI and functional outcome.

Results

Baseline serum BD-tau was higher in RSSI patients than controls (median 9.54 [7.32-12.20] vs 7.75 [6.18-9.44] pg/mL; P = .003) and correlated with infarct diameter (rs = 0.222, P = 0.039). Brain-derived tau did not correlate with time from stroke symptom onset to blood sampling (rs = 0.150, P = .179). Brain-derived tau was not associated with chronic CSVD neuroimaging features (WMHs, lacunes, microbleeds, SVD score; all P > .05) at any timepoint. Longitudinally, BD-tau returned to control levels by 3 months (P = .374) and remained stable at 15 months (P = .985). Brain-derived tau was neither associated with new vascular MRI lesions on follow-up nor functional neurological outcome.

Conclusion

Serum BD-tau is elevated acutely in CSVD-related RSSI, correlates with infarct size and normalises by 3 months. Brain-derived tau was not associated with chronic CSVD neuroimaging features or disease progression, suggesting sensitivity to acute neuronal injury rather than chronic or progressive CSVD.

title: Recurrent Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection.
authorString: Nguyen H, Sharma P, Berg N, Uppal S.
abstractText: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is a rare but increasingly recognized cause of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and sudden cardiac death. It has been associated with several predisposing factors, including hormone replacement therapy, autoimmune disorders, fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD), connective tissue diseases, atherosclerosis, migraine, pregnancy, and the postpartum period. SCAD most commonly affects young to middle-aged women who present with acute myocardial infarction (MI) despite the absence of traditional atherosclerotic risk factors. Coronary angiography remains the gold standard for diagnosis, allowing visualization of the characteristic dissection patterns within the coronary vessel wall. Management is typically conservative as spontaneous healing of the dissection is common; however, revascularization with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) or coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) may be necessary in patients with hemodynamic instability, ongoing ischemia, or failure of medical therapy.

title: From ER and mitochondria to contact sites: integrated regulation of ferroptosis in cardiovascular diseases.
authorString: Leo S, Mollica F, Pedriali G, Morciano G, Colarusso EN, Tremoli E, Pinton P.

journal.title: Redox report : communications in free radical research

abstractText: Iron is a central regulator of cellular redox homeostasis, supporting essential physiological processes. Given its critical biological importance, iron homeostasis is tightly regulated at both the systemic and cellular levels. Ferroptosis is a metabolically regulated, iron-dependent form of cell death characterized by the accumulation of phospholipid hydroperoxides driven by iron-catalyzed redox reactions, ultimately leading to oxidative membrane damage. Accumulating evidence indicates that ferroptosis emerges from the coordinated activity of multiple subcellular organelles rather than from isolated pathways. In this context, the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and mitochondria have recently been established as key regulators of ferroptotic signaling. Notably, mitochondria-associated membranes (MAMs), by spatially coordinating redox signaling and lipid peroxidation, calcium fluxes, mitochondrial metabolism and lipid remodeling, are increasingly recognized as central hubs within the ferroptotic cascade, acting as modulators of cellular susceptibility to ferroptosis and as key sites of its execution. Owing to its strong dependence on mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, the heart is particularly sensitive to perturbations in iron homeostasis. Notably, growing evidence supports a pathogenic role for ferroptosis in cardiovascular diseases (CVDs), linking iron-dependent oxidative stress to cardiomyocyte dysfunction and tissue injury. Accordingly, ferroptosis has emerged as a potential therapeutic target in cardiovascular pathology. This review examines how ER and mitochondrial dysfunction contribute to ferroptotic signaling in CVDs and discusses the hypothesis that MAMs may function as central regulatory interfaces coordinating these processes. Elucidating these mechanisms is essential for the development of novel therapeutic strategies aimed at modulating ferroptosis and limiting CVDs progression.

title: National Trends, Disparities, and Inpatient Outcomes of Cardiac Amyloidosis Hospitalizations in the United States During the Era of Disease-Modifying Therapy.
authorString: Ahmed Farooqi H, Alam B, Mohammed Khan T, Talhaa A, Haider A, Muhammad Umar Hayat H, Hicazi Ş, Fatima H, Babar F.
abstractText:
Background

Tafamidis, approved in 2019, was the first disease-modifying therapy for transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy. Disparities in cardiac amyloidosis outcomes remain incompletely characterized.

Objectives

To characterize US trends in cardiac amyloidosis hospitalizations, subtypes, and risk-adjusted mortality from 2017 to 2022, including changes around tafamidis approval.

Methods

We analyzed the 2017-2022 National Inpatient Sample, defining cases by an amyloidosis code (E85.x) paired with a heart failure or restrictive cardiomyopathy code. Survey-weighted regression assessed outcomes; Joinpoint and segmented regression tested for a 2019 trend inflection.

Results

Of an estimated 111,450 hospitalizations, 83% were coded as Other/Unspecified amyloidosis. In-hospital mortality was 7.1%, highest in light-chain (AL) amyloidosis (9.4%) and lowest in wild-type transthyretin amyloidosis (4.9%; adjusted odds ratio 0.48 vs AL). The age-standardized hospitalization rate nearly doubled, from 4.2 to 8.0 per 100,000 adults, with no inflection detected at 2019. Private and "Other" payer status were associated with higher adjusted mortality than Medicare, the mortality difference for uninsured patients increased over time, and Black patients had lower adjusted odds of pacemaker implantation. Black patients accounted for a larger share of hereditary ATTR admissions than of other subtypes in every year.

Conclusions

Cardiac amyloidosis hospitalizations rose steadily from 2017 to 2022, and no inflection was detected at the 2019 approval of tafamidis. Because the NIS lacks data on treatment exposure, diagnostic testing, and disease severity, these findings cannot establish whether tafamidis influenced hospitalization trends. Differences in in-hospital mortality by payer and in pacemaker implantation by race persisted and warrant investigation with patient-level clinical data.

title: Transvascular neurosurgery.
authorString: Savastano LE.
abstractText: Major advances in cerebrovascular neurosurgery have repeatedly emerged from the convergence of a transformative idea with enabling technology. The introduction of the operating microscope and microsurgical instrumentation in the late 1960s redefined the limits of safe access to deep cerebrovascular structures and gave rise to microneurosurgery. The advent of catheter-based intracranial navigation in the late 20th century created the field of endovascular neurosurgery, transforming the management of aneurysms, arteriovenous malformations, dural arteriovenous fistulas, atherosclerosis, and large-vessel occlusion stroke. Throughout this evolution, the vessel wall has been treated as an inviolable barrier; the cardinal rule of endovascular practice has been to avoid perforating it. Herein, it is argued that the deliberate and controlled crossing of the vessel wall-transvascular neurosurgery-represents a third paradigm shift, whereby the neurovascular arterial and venous networks are repurposed as a natural operative corridor to access the subdural, subarachnoid, parenchymal, and ventricular compartments of the brain without a craniotomy or burr hole. Early clinical work has shown that controlled transvascular exit from the meningeal vasculature is feasible and can enable a range of intracranial procedures, from implantation of biomimetic shunts and combined middle meningeal artery embolization with transarterial evacuation of nonacute subdural hematoma. The authors review the historical arc that brought us to this point, summarize the technical and biological rationale for meningeal-vascular access, and outline a roadmap by which a broad ecosystem of transvascular neurosurgical procedures could be performed through rapid, outpatient, catheter-based workflows.

title: Porphyromonas gingivalis and Ferroptosis: Evidence, Limitations, and Significance.
authorString: Fang X, Xu X, Wei T, Lu S, Qin G, Chen H.
abstractText: Porphyromonas gingivalis (P. gingivalis) is a keystone pathogen in periodontal dysbiosis and has been linked to multiple systemic diseases. Ferroptosis is a form of regulated cell death driven by iron-dependent lipid peroxidation, and accumulating evidence implicates it in P. gingivalis-associated tissue injury. This review examines the mechanisms and disease contexts linking P. gingivalis to ferroptosis across experimental models. In inflammatory and tissue-injury models, P. gingivalis exposure is associated with disrupted iron homeostasis, increased lipid peroxidation, and impaired antioxidant defenses. In contrast, tumor models show reduced ferroptotic sensitivity associated with P. gingivalis. These findings support a context-dependent model in which P. gingivalis may alter host-cell susceptibility to ferroptosis through direct bacterial effects and indirect changes in the microbial, inflammatory, and redox environment. This framework highlights how bacterial exposure, host-cell state, and the disease microenvironment shape ferroptotic responses and provides a basis for evaluating the mechanistic and translational significance of ferroptosis in P. gingivalis-associated diseases.

title: Residual Shunt at 6 Months Follow-up After Percutaneous Patent Foramen Ovale Closure in CAHAL: A Comparison of Occlutech and Amplatzer.
authorString: Nieuwendijk JD, Bouziani AE, Witte LS, Robbers-Visser D, Bouma BJ, Straver B, Amri IA, Coutinho JM, Delewi R, de Winter RJ, Beijk MAM, van der Kley F, Grundeken MJ.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText:
Background

Residual shunt is a known complication in percutaneous patent foramen ovale (PFO) closure, and moderate to large residual shunt has been associated with an increased risk of recurrent stroke. Device-related factors, such as device size, have been associated with residual shunt, but comparative data per device type are scarce.

Aims

We compared the prevalence of moderate to large residual shunt at 6 months between the Amplatzer and Occlutech devices.

Methods

In this retrospective cohort study, patients undergoing successful percutaneous PFO closure with an Amplatzer or Occlutech dedicated closure device within the CAHAL centers Amsterdam UMC and Leiden UMC between 2018 and 2024 were included. The study population was divided into patients treated with an Occlutech and an Amplatzer device. The prevalence of moderate/large residual shunt at 6 months of follow-up was compared between the two groups. As a sensitivity analysis, a logistic regression was conducted to determine the association between the treatment groups and moderate/large residual shunt. The logistic regression was conducted in a weighted population using inverse probability weighting (IPTW), correcting for age, sex, smoking status, shunt size at baseline, device size, and atrial septal aneurysm.

Results

A total of 413 patients were included with an average age of 45.8 ± 11.3 years and 51.6% were male. Of the included patients, 279 were treated with an Amplatzer- and 134 with an Occlutech device. In the group treated with an Amplatzer, 22.2% of the patients had a moderate or large residual shunt at 6 months compared to 14.9% in the Occlutech group (p = 0.11). The sensitivity analysis did not show an association between device type and moderate/large shunt OR 0.71 (95% CI: 0.39-1.28, p = 0.25).

Conclusion

In this study, no significant difference was observed in moderate/large residual shunt prevalence at 6 months of follow-up between the Occlutech and Amplatzer devices.

title: Sociodemographic and Clinical Factors Associated With Nirsevimab Receipt Among Children Aged Younger Than 20 Months in the New Vaccine Surveillance Network in 2023 to 2025.
authorString: Teoh Z, Tannis A, Sullivan E, Boom JA, Halasa N, Michaels MG, Payne DC, Sahni LC, Schuster J, Selvarangan R, Staat MA, Stewart LS, Szilagyi PG, Weinberg GA, Williams JV, Dawood FS, Klein EJ, Moline H, Englund JA, Zerr DM.
abstractText:
Objectives

We aim to evaluate the association of sociodemographic and clinical factors with nirsevimab receipt among children with medically attended acute respiratory illness (ARI) across multiple seasons and beyond birth hospitalization.

Patients and methods

We included nirsevimab-eligible children aged younger than 8 months and 8 to 19 months with ARI enrolled in the New Vaccine Surveillance Network during the 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025 respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) seasons (October 1 to March 31). A mixed-effects logistic regression model was used to evaluate the association between sociodemographic and clinical factors with the likelihood of nirsevimab receipt among enrolled children aged younger than 8 months.

Results

Of the 2151 nirsevimab-eligible children with ARI enrolled in the 2023 to 2024 RSV season and 1819 in the 2024 to 2025 RSV season, 96% were aged younger than 8 months and in their first RSV season. Fourteen percent and 36% of eligible children aged younger than 8 months received nirsevimab in the 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025 seasons, respectively. Among infants aged younger than 8 months, those born during the RSV season and those with an underlying medical condition were more likely to receive nirsevimab in both RSV seasons; infant female sex and maternal education were also associated with nirsevimab receipt during 2023 to 2024 but not 2024 to 2025.

Conclusion

Most nirsevimab-eligible children with medically attended ARI in this analysis did not receive nirsevimab during the first 2 seasons of nirsevimab availability. Factors such as birth before the RSV season were associated with a decreased likelihood of nirsevimab receipt, emphasizing the need for tailored interventions following birth hospitalization to increase nirsevimab uptake for this group of children.

title: Cumulative Opioid Exposures in the First Year of Life and Cognitive Neurodevelopment in High-Risk Infants.
authorString: Keane OA, Ourshalimian S, Lakshmanan A, Ross P, Kim E, Lee HC, Hintz SR, Nguyen N, Ing M, Kaplan C, Mirzaian CB, Vanderbilt D, Anand KS, Kelley-Quon LI.
abstractText:
Background

High-risk infants with significant neonatal-perinatal morbidities often require opioids, but prolonged exposures can impair neurodevelopment. We evaluated the effect of cumulative opioid exposures in the first year of life, measured by morphine milligrams equivalents (MME), on neurodevelopment.

Methods

A retrospective cohort of high-risk infants younger than 1 year admitted to a tertiary children's hospital from 2010 to 2020 was identified. International Classification of Diseases, Ninth and Tenth Revisions (ICD-9/ICD-10) codes for congenital heart disease surgery, medical and surgical necrotizing enterocolitis, extremely low birth weight, very low birth weight, hypoxemic ischemic encephalopathy, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, and thoracoabdominal surgery identified high-risk infants. Cumulative MME received over all hospitalizations in the first year of life were calculated alongside benzodiazepine dosing and neurodevelopmental scores at 18 months or older. Neurodevelopmental impairment was defined as a score more than 1 SD from the standardized mean. Multivariable linear regressions adjusted for demographics and comorbidities.

Results

Overall, 330 high-risk infants were identified, and 70.6% demonstrated neurodevelopmental impairment. Cumulative MME negatively correlated with cognitive (P < .001), motor (P < .001), and language (P = .004) scores. On multivariable linear regression, increasing MME was significantly associated with decreasing cognitive (P < .001) scores but not motor or language scores.

Conclusion

Higher cumulative opioid exposure in the first year of life was associated with reduced cognitive scores at 18 months or older, independent of comorbidities. Opioid stewardship initiatives extended to high-risk infants may further optimize long-term neurodevelopment.

title: Extending Problem and Solution Trees: A Participatory Method for Community Partnership Development
authorString: Sesay NA, OoNorasak K, Bawa MS, Haskins D, Hughes K, White BM.
abstractText:
Background:

Problem and solution trees (PASTs) are a participatory method for understanding complex environmental and systemic health problems and incorporating community input in appropriate solutions. While PASTs have been applied in international contexts to examine critical health concerns (e.g., hand-washing behaviors and malnutrition), their use in the United States (US) is limited.

Objectives:

Together with a Project Advisory Board (PAB), identify barriers to DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) eating plan adoption and co-develop actionable solutions to low adherence for a historically marginalized community in the U.S.

Methods:

PASTs are visual tools. Over virtual and in-person meetings, we constructed and refined five distinct trees to address each core barrier to DASH adherence. We made real-time edits to trees in PowerPoint and engaged in group discussion to reach consensus on barriers and solutions. Supporting material included a project workbook distributed to the PAB. Meetings were audio-recorded, and transcripts were reviewed following each meeting to ensure the accuracy of each tree. The PAST method aided collaboration with the PAB by allowing members to identify additional barriers and refine the trees based on their knowledge and experience. PASTs additionally supported the community-engaged partnership by identifying the interconnectedness of core problems (i.e., limited supply of healthy foods and preference for salty foods).

Conclusions:

PASTs showed their relevance as tools for community-engaged research and responsive program planning. Challenges in creating and presenting intricate trees via online format highlight considerations for virtual facilitation and real-time documentation. Adaptations to the method are described for future use.

title: Subclinical Cerebral Lesions in Migraine: A Proof-of-Concept Study on Platelet Aggregation.
authorString: Maestrini I, Curreli M, Puma M, Giannì C, Schiera E, Giuliani G, Toscano M, Altieri M, Pantano P, Pulcinelli F, Di Piero V.
abstractText:
Background

Migraine patients exhibit cerebral white matter lesions (WMLs) more frequently than the general population, with a potential micro-ischemic origin. Although platelet function in migraine patients has been extensively studied, no previous research has evaluated platelet function in those with WMLs. Our aim was to assess platelet aggregation in migraine patients with WMLs, to investigate their potential correlation with ischemic pathophysiology.

Methods

We enrolled consecutive 34 patients diagnosed with episodic or chronic migraine, with or without aura (ICHD3 criteria), out of attacks, including 20 with WMLs and 14 without lesions. Patients on antiplatelet therapy, or those with inherited platelet disorders or thrombophilia, were excluded. All patients underwent MRI to identify and quantify WMLs in mm3. Platelet aggregation was assessed in response to various agonists (ADP, collagen, epinephrine, and arachidonic acid) and compared to a group of matched healthy volunteers (HV).

Results

Platelet aggregation in response to epinephrine was lower in migraine patients compared to HV. Among migraine patients, those with a lesion load ≥ 146.25 mm3 (forth quartile of the WMLs total volume) showed significantly higher platelet aggregation in response to epinephrine (1.25 and 2.5 μM), compared to those with a lesion load < 146.25 mm3 or no lesions (p = 0.043 and p = 0.0047, respectively).

Conclusions

Migraine is associated with reduced platelet aggregation compared to HV, which may serve as a protective mechanism. However, in patients with a higher burden of WMLs, platelet aggregation levels were comparable to those of HV, raising the possibility of an ischemic contribution to WMLs in migraine patients.

title: Integrated Multi-Omics Analysis of Human Cerebrospinal Fluid in Traumatic Spinal Cord Injury: An Exploratory Pilot Study.
authorString: Jiang W, Wang Y, Miao W, Liu H, Qiao Q, Jiang T, Shen C, Zhou Z, Cheng H, Li N.
abstractText:
Objective

Acute traumatic spinal cord injury (TSCI) is a devastating neurological disorder with limited therapeutic options. We aimed to characterize the human cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) microenvironment to identify novel multi-omics signatures and potential mechanistic hypotheses.

Methods

CSF from 13 acute cervical TSCI patients and 13 controls was prospectively collected. A discovery cohort (n = 10) underwent untargeted proteomics and metabolomics. Following differential and functional enrichment analyses, sequential multi-omics integration was applied to extract cross-omics features. Prioritized candidates were subsequently validated via ELISA and targeted metabolomics in an independent validation cohort (n = 16).

Results

We identified 216 differentially expressed proteins and 26 metabolites, highlighting extensive extracellular matrix remodeling alongside profound purine and amino acid metabolism dysregulation. Integrated analyses converged on downregulated mitochondrial aspartate aminotransferase (GOT2) as a candidate marker. Targeted correlation analysis revealed that GOT2 selectively associated with specific co-mapped metabolites that were concurrently downregulated, notably methionine and 4-acetamidobutanoic acid. The GOT2-associated metabolic signature was experimentally validated in the independent cohort.

Conclusions

This exploratory multi-omics study unveils the acute human TSCI molecular landscape, nominating a novel GOT2-associated metabolic signature that warrants further mechanistic investigation regarding its pathogenic implications and potential therapeutic relevance.

title: Association of Thyroid Autoimmunity With Age-Related Macular Degeneration in U.S. Adults.
authorString: Chen X, Zhang J, Wong TY, Huang L, Wang YX.
abstractText:
Purpose

To investigate the associations of thyroid autoimmunity, assessed by thyroid peroxidase antibody (TPOAb) and thyroglobulin antibody (TgAb), with prevalent age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in U.S. adults, and to explore whether genetic liabilities to Hashimoto thyroiditis (HT) and Graves' disease (GD) were associated with AMD risk using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR).

Methods

This cross-sectional study included 2967 adults aged 40 years or older from the 2007-2008 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. Survey-weighted logistic regression models included TPOAb and TgAb positivity simultaneously. Two-sample MR analyses were exploratory.

Results

Among 2967 participants, 234 had AMD, corresponding to a weighted prevalence of 6.6% (95% confidence interval [CI], 5.6%-7.9%). In the mutually adjusted observational model, TgAb positivity was associated with higher odds of prevalent AMD (odds ratio [OR], 2.02; 95% CI, 1.13-3.61; P = 0.022), whereas TPOAb positivity was not associated with AMD (OR, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.63-1.37; P = 0.676). Exploratory MR analyses suggested a possible association between genetic liability to HT and AMD (OR, 1.14; 95% CI, 1.01-1.29; P = 0.033), whereas evidence for GD was less consistent.

Conclusions

TgAb positivity was associated with prevalent AMD. The cross-sectional design and the nonidentical exposures assessed in the observational and MR analyses preclude causal inference.

Translational relevance

Thyroglobulin antibody positivity was associated with prevalent AMD and may reflect a systemic immune phenotype warranting prospective investigation.

title: Successful Medical Management of Obstructive Mechanical Mitral Valve Thrombosis Using Low-Dose, Ultraslow Infusion Thrombolytic Therapy: A Case Report.
authorString: Nguyen KM, Huynh HH, Tran LNM, Phan LT, Hoang SV.
abstractText: Obstructive mechanical valve thrombosis is a life-threatening complication that requires emergent diagnosis and intervention. We report the case of a 61-year-old man who presented with dyspnea. He had undergone mechanical aortic and mitral valve replacement in 2010. Admission laboratory results revealed subtherapeutic anticoagulation with an international normalized ratio of 1.09. Transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography confirmed obstructive mechanical mitral valve thrombosis, with a 17 × 25 mm mass showing imaging features consistent with subacute thrombus and suggestive of concomitant pannus, which restricted the motion of one leaflet and increased the mean transmitral pressure gradient to 23 mmHg. Because of the patient's substantial surgical risk and the family's refusal of surgical intervention, the patient received low-dose, ultraslow thrombolytic therapy with alteplase administered as a continuous intravenous infusion of 25 mg over 25 h. The patient tolerated the regimen well, with no hemorrhagic or systemic embolic complications. Postintervention echocardiographic evaluation showed hemodynamic recovery (mean pressure gradient decreased to 3 mmHg). The patient was discharged on vitamin K antagonist therapy with planned close international normalized ratio monitoring. This case demonstrates that low-dose, ultraslow alteplase infusion may be a feasible treatment option for carefully selected patients with obstructive mechanical prosthetic valve thrombosis when surgery is considered high risk or declined.

title: Posttranslational Modification Cross-Talk in Vascular Cells: Molecular Mechanisms and Therapeutic Implications for Atherosclerosis.
authorString: Jiang W, Du H.
abstractText: Atherosclerosis is driven by coordinated changes in endothelial cells (ECs), macrophages, and vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). Post-translational modifications (PTMs), phosphorylation, acetylation, ubiquitination, SUMOylation, O-GlcNAcylation, palmitoylation, ISGylation, and ADP-ribosylation, integrate metabolic, inflammatory, and mechanical inputs at a limited number of signaling nodes. This review argues that these modifications interact according to four definable relationships rather than merely co-occurring. In competitive cross-talk, two marks contest one acceptor residue, as when O-GlcNAcylation displaces phosphorylation at the Akt site of endothelial nitric oxide synthase. In hierarchical cross-talk, one modification licenses another, as when Ser536 phosphorylation of NF-κB p65 recruits p300 and permits Lys310 acetylation. In enzyme-directed cross-talk, a modification acts on the writer or eraser of a different system, as HDAC9 does on IκB kinases. In cofactor-coupled cross-talk, sirtuin-dependent deacylation and PARP1-dependent ADP-ribosylation draw on one limiting NAD<sup>+</sup> pool. We rank nodes against four stated criteria, grade every finding on a five-level evidence scheme, and apply the framework to phosphorylation-O-GlcNAcylation, ubiquitination-SUMOylation, and acetylation-ubiquitination interactions across the three vascular cell types. Of the cross-talk relationships invoked, five are supported at residue resolution by a substitution experiment, and two of these were obtained in vascular cells; the remainder are inferred from enzyme-level regulation or from pathway convergence. Candidate intervention points include HDAC9, SENP3, OGT, UBA1, and the NAD<sup>+</sup> pool, none of which has been evaluated in a cardiovascular outcome trial.

title: Myeloid-Derived Growth Factor Alleviates Diabetic Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease by Up-Regulating ABCA1 and ABCG1 Expression via the AMPK/PPARγ/LXRα Pathway.
authorString: Chen Z, Meng B, Wang B, Ding Y.

journal.title: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine

abstractText: The regulatory role of bone marrow in systemic metabolic processes remains incompletely characterized. Myeloid-derived growth factor (MYDGF) is a myeloid cell-secreted factor with emerging metabolic functions, but its action in diabetes-associated non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (DM NAFLD) is undefined. To investigate the influence of myeloid cell-derived MYDGF on DM NAFLD, both loss- and gain-of-function approaches were applied in vivo. DM NAFLD models were established in Mydgf-knockout (KO) mice, Pparg<sup>ΔLyz2</sup> mice and Pparg<sup>ΔLyz2</sup>/KO (DKO) mice. For in vitro studies, primary Kupffer cells (KCs) were stimulated with high glucose and recombinant MYDGF (rMYDGF) and bone marrow cells (BMCs) were co-cultured with KCs via a transwell system. Protein levels related to DM NAFLD pathology and signalling pathways were quantified. In this study, we found that MYDGF was significantly downregulated in DM NAFLD mouse liver. Myeloid MYDGF deficiency exacerbated hepatic inflammation, lipogenesis, steatosis and macrophage infiltration, while reconstituting myeloid MYDGF reversed these phenotypes. rMYDGF attenuated inflammation, reduced macrophage foaming, decreased cholesterol content and increased efferocytosis. Mechanistically, MYDGF induced AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) phosphorylation, which subsequently activated the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ)/liver X receptor α (LXRα) pathway in KCs and upregulated downstream ABCA1 and ABCG1 expression. These results identify the AMPK/PPARγ/LXRα-ABCA1/ABCG1 cascade as the core signalling axis mediating MYDGF's metabolic regulatory effects, which bridges the previously unrecognized functional linkage between myeloid cell function and hepatic lipid homeostasis, and explains the protective phenotype observed in MYDGF-reconstituted DM NAFLD mice. In conclusion, myeloid cell-derived MYDGF ameliorates DM NAFLD, decreases cholesterol content in macrophages and reduces lipid accumulation via the AMPK/PPARγ/LXRα pathway. MYDGF serves as a key mediator for bone marrow-liver metabolic crosstalk, indicating that the bone marrow may act as a potential endocrine target for the prevention and treatment of diabetes-related metabolic disorders.

title: A Scalable, Traceable Computational-to-Experimental Pipeline for Activity-Guided Identification of Bioactive Constituents: A Case Study in Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge.
authorString: Wang X, Tan Z, Jin X, Hai J, Pei D, Di DL.
abstractText: Systematic identification of bioactive constituents from complex natural products remains challenging. Here, a scalable and traceable integrated workflow was developed and validated in Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge (SMB) for anti-Parkinson's disease (PD) constituent discovery. Network pharmacology first identified four candidate compounds, which were quantified and dynamically tracked during X-5 macroporous resin enrichment and fractionation using a validated HPLC method. Transfer rates exceeded 80% for all candidates, confirming efficient enrichment and chemical traceability. Bioactivity was then evaluated in MPP<sup>+</sup>-induced PC12 cells and a rotenone-induced PD mouse model. SMB-2 showed the strongest neuroprotective activity and was subjected to spectrum-effect relationship analysis, which identified five activity-associated compounds. Integration of pharmacological validation, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations progressively narrowed the candidate space and identified cryptotanshinone as a major bioactive constituent. Cryptotanshinone exhibited favorable predicted binding affinity and stable interactions with key residues in the monoamine oxidase B binding pocket, supporting its potential MAO-B inhibitory activity. It also restored intracellular ATP levels and superoxide dismutase activity, indicating improved energy metabolism and antioxidant defense. Overall, this workflow enables stepwise convergence from complex natural matrices to experimentally supported bioactive constituents and provides a broadly applicable strategy for natural-product-based drug discovery.

title: Positive-call rates and agreement of two artificial intelligence electrocardiogram models for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and cardiac amyloidosis in competitive athletes.
authorString: de Sousa Barzon Serra V, Zanco J, de Souza BL, Crystal OR, Nabi HA, Ibrahim R, Shamoun F, Ayoub C, Arsanjani R, Farina JM, Scott LR.
abstractText:
Background

Artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) models detect hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and cardiac amyloidosis in clinical populations; whether two independently developed models agree in athletes is unknown.

Methods

We applied two independently developed AI-ECG models to the screening electrocardiograms (ECGs) of 716 competitive athletes aged 40 years or younger, screened by ECG alone and presumed free of structural heart disease. The RST algorithms return per-condition probabilities dichotomized at published operating points; the AZ model, a four-class ECG-image classifier, assigns one class per ECG. The primary outcome was each model's positive-call rate (proportion of athletes flagged) for HCM and cardiac amyloidosis; agreement was described with Cohen kappa and positive agreement. Because the cohort was presumed disease-free, sensitivity was not assessed.

Results

Median age was 22.1 years; 86.0% were men. The RST algorithms flagged HCM in 13 athletes (1.8%; 95% CI, 1.0-3.1) and cardiac amyloidosis in 2 (0.3%; 0.0-1.0); the AZ model flagged HCM in 29 (4.1%; 2.7-5.8) and cardiac amyloidosis in 18 (2.5%; 1.5-3.9). Of 60 athletes flagged by either model, 2 were flagged by both (kappa 0.07 and - 0.01; positive agreement 0.10 and 0.00); continuous outputs were uncorrelated for HCM (Spearman rho 0.00). Of 59 flagged athletes with a stored cardiologist interpretation under the international criteria, 39 had a normal ECG. All 18 AZ amyloidosis calls occurred in men.

Conclusions

The two models flagged different athletes at different rates. Without verified cases these rates describe referral burden, not accuracy; whether either detects disease requires validation against verified diagnoses.

title: Establishing a Biophotonic Signature of Brain Ageing.
authorString: Slayo M, Vocale L, Xavier S, Singhaarachchi P, Quinn KM, Del Rosal B, Spencer SJ.
abstractText: Ageing-associated inflammation ("inflammaging") is characterised by chronic microglial priming or overactivity that elevates neurodegeneration risk. Microglia also accumulate autofluorescent lipofuscin as they age-aggregates of oxidised lipids, misfolded proteins and metals that generate reactive oxygen species. Characterising age-related changes in brain autofluorescence could provide insight into brain ageing dynamics and could identify associations with potential biomarkers in accessible tissues such as blood. We hypothesised that the ageing-related increase in microglial autofluorescent material produces a spectral signature that makes ageing autofluorescence distinct from that in young brains. To test this, we examined autofluorescence profiles in the hippocampus and arcuate nucleus (ARC) of young (3 months) and aged (21 months) female C57BL/6 mice. We found that ageing significantly increased the volume of the autofluorescent material in microglia, including driving an abundance of extra-large aggregates. In the ARC, larger aggregates-present only in aged brains-exhibited stronger far-red emission than the autofluorescence seen in young brains. Fluorescence lifetime imaging analysis indicated specific ageing-related molecular changes in brain autofluorescence. Lipidomic analysis from the plasma of these mice indicated 22 lipids that were differentially concentrated with age and one (sphingomyelin 32:2) that was significantly associated with the ageing brain spectral profile after controlling for multiple comparisons and validating in a separate cohort. These findings demonstrate that autofluorescent material aggregates with age in microglia and that brain autofluorescence undergoes a spectral red-shift associated with ageing and lipid alterations. Brain autofluorescence may thus reflect brain ageing with potential translational relevance for non-invasive monitoring.

title: Prevalence and Specificity of Red Blood Cell Alloimmunization Among Transfusion Recipients in a Portuguese Hospital.
authorString: Sousa ALM, Silvestre-Ferreira AC, DE Barros Sanches FMF, Queiroga FL, Costa JJ.
abstractText:
Background/aim

The transfusion of red blood cells (RBCs) is a vital and widely used support therapy. Although often lifesaving, it carries certain risks, as it exposes the patient to alloimmunization due to exposure to various antigens. Despite its importance, the relative frequency of RBC alloantibodies within the general patient population in Portugal has not been extensively studied. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence of RBC alloimmunization in patients attending a Northern Portuguese Hospital Center.

Patients and methods

We conducted a 3-year retrospective study to investigate the incidence of RBC alloimmunization in patients who received RBC transfusion at a hospital center in Northern Portugal and characterized the target population according to demographic data; ABO, Rh, and Kell blood groups; associated pathology; hospital department; and number of RBC transfusions.

Results

The alloimmunization rate was 1.3% in the study population of 4,079 patients who received RBC transfusion, with the most common antibody being anti-K (18.5%), followed by anti-Lua (13.0%), and anti-E (11.1%). Among the 54 patients that developed alloimmunization, 75.9% developed only one alloantibody, 9.3% presented two alloantibodies, and only 1.9% of the cases developed three alloantibodies; specificity was not identifiable for the remainder. Hematological malignancies were the most frequently observed pathology in the alloimmunized population (25.9%), with myelodysplastic syndrome being the most common (13.0%).

Conclusion

This study demonstrates the importance of characterizing alloimmunized populations to identify high-risk groups. Based on this understanding, it becomes feasible to implement targeted preventive measures to reduce alloimmunization rates and optimize the use of available resources.

title: Bilateral Iliac Branch Endoprosthesis Deployment With IVUS-Guided Contrast-Sparing Technique: A Complex Case Report.
authorString: Al Haj B, Koehler CE, Austermann MJ.

journal.title: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists

abstractText:
Background

Preserving internal iliac artery (IIA) patency during endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) for aortobiiliac aneurysms typically requires substantial contrast volume, posing risk to patients with renal insufficiency.

Case description

We present the case of an elderly female with chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 3b (baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate 35 mL/min/1.73 m², serum creatinine 1.5 mg/dL) and an aortobiiliac aneurysm who underwent complex bilateral iliac side-branch (iliac branch endoprosthesis [IBE]) deployment. The procedure used intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) as the primary guidance to minimize contrast exposure. A notable intraoperative challenge arose on the left side, where retrograde cannulation was unsuccessful due to anatomical tortuosity and sheath dislodgement. We therefore performed a left axillary cut-down, which facilitated successful IIA reconstruction and resolved a type 1b endoleak. The total contrast volume employed was approximately 38 mL. Incidental findings included hyperthyroidism and suspected lymphoproliferative disorder.

Conclusion

Intravascular ultrasound-guided bilateral IBE is feasible and substantially reduces contrast exposure in patients with renal impairment, though technical flexibility is essential for complex anatomy.Clinical ImpactIVUS-guided bilateral iliac branch endoprosthesis deployment may offer a contrast-sparing option for patients with chronic kidney disease undergoing endovascular repair of complex aortobiiliac aneurysms. Using IVUS for vessel identification, sizing, landing-zone selection, and stent-apposition assessment can reduce reliance on iodinated contrast while preserving internal iliac artery perfusion. This case shows that bilateral reconstruction is feasible with only 38 mL of contrast, even when complex anatomy requires axillary access. Its innovation is using IVUS as the primary guidance modality, with angiography reserved for confirmation and troubleshooting.

title: Exercise and physiological monitoring in isolated, confined and extreme environments and space analogues: A scoping review.
authorString: Lima GSO, Dinis KVF, Silva LP, Sousa NB, Silva MKFS, Talhari DC, Almeida JS, Moraes MM, Arantes RME, Nascimento MA, Mendes TT.
abstractText: This scoping review synthesized evidence on physical activity/exercise and physiological monitoring in isolated, confined and extreme (ICE) environments, with emphasis on Antarctic missions and space analogues. ICE exposures combine cold stress, confinement, disrupted light-dark cycles and psychosocial strain, which can challenge musculoskeletal integrity, cardiovascular regulation, sleep/circadian function and cognition. Following Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidance, we searched Web of Science, Embase, Scopus and PubMed/Medline, complemented by grey literature and AI-assisted citation chasing. Eligible reports included human studies in ICE/analogue settings that implemented or quantified physical activity/exercise and/or physiological monitoring. Seventeen studies published between 2003 and 2025 met inclusion criteria and were mapped across ICE characteristics, exercise protocols, monitoring technologies, outcomes and research gaps. Exercise was reported as a potential countermeasure to attenuate selected aspects of deconditioning and support sleep and psychophysiological adaptation, particularly in bed rest and simulated confinement studies. Antarctic field studies more often characterized spontaneous physical activity, sleep/activity rhythms and field-adapted monitoring. Assessment strategies varied, ranging from self-reported logs and actigraphy in operational field settings to laboratory-grade measures in bed rest and simulated confinement studies. Overall, exercise emerged as a pragmatic, domain-specific countermeasure against deconditioning in ICE settings, with effectiveness varying by modality and physiological target. However, heterogeneity in exposure characterization, exercise dose and monitoring methods, despite feasible wearable-based capture of behavioural and physiological signals, limited comparability and mechanistic inference. Future ICE research should prioritize harmonized reporting, standardized monitoring and longitudinal designs linking exercise exposure to physiological, behavioural and operational outcomes.

title: Frailty Assessment and Treatment Effects in Clinical Trials of Disease-Modifying Therapies for CKD.
authorString: Yang C, Chen D, Chepulis L, Nair D, Vart P.

journal.title: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation

abstractText: Frailty is common in chronic kidney disease (CKD) and is independently associated with disability and mortality. However, evidence on the optimal treatment of frail adults with CKD remains limited. Consequently, regulators have encouraged routine assessment of frailty and the reporting of outcomes stratified by frailty in clinical studies. In this narrative review, we found that several recent clinical trials of disease-modifying therapies for CKD evaluated treatment effects across frailty strata and reported consistent benefits, with potentially greater benefits in the highest frailty subgroup. However, frailty was not formally assessed in any of these trials, and the proxy measures used may not have fully captured the multidimensional aspects of frailty needed to inform treatment decisions.

title: Cognitive impairment in uncontrolled vs controlled hypertension - systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Tyjas K, Rusinek-Glück J, Ziółek W, Rajzer M, Gruszka-Gosiewska A, Stolarz-Skrzypek K.
abstractText: Hypertension is a well-recognized risk factor for the development of cognitive impairment (CImp) and brain vasculogenic lesions. The aim of this systematic review was to assess whether adequate blood pressure control, compared with ineffective treatment, reduces the risk of CImp and brain structural abnormalities. Between June and July 2024, three databases (MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO) were screened for studies comparing cognitive performance or brain damage in hypertensive adults. 2,613 unique records were identified, and ultimately 18 predominantly cross-sectional studies were included. Meta-analyses using a random-effect model were performed for CImp prevalence in 5 studies, for Mini-Mental State Examination and Montreal Cognitive Assessment scores in 3 studies, for verbal fluency outcomes in 3 studies, and for white matter hyperintensities assessed in magnetic resonance imaging in 4 studies. The prevalence of CImp was lower in the group with well-controlled hypertension (OR 0.32, 95% CI: 0.13, 0.80), but the result was significant only among individuals ≥65 years of age. Similarly, white matter hyperintensities (WMH) tended to be less advanced among patients with controlled hypertension (SMD: 0.58, 95% CI: 0.08, 1.08). However, the individual neuropsychological tests analyzed (verbal fluency, delayed word recall, digit symbol substitution, and digit span) did not reveal significant differences between these groups. Adequate control of hypertension may be associated with a lower prevalence of CImp and less advanced WMH. However, the association with CImp was confined to older adults (≥65 years) and was based on a small number of studies with considerable between-study heterogeneity.

title: Leveraging immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry and neuropathology to identify the clinical value of different blood tau species in Alzheimer's disease.
authorString: Labonte J, Miner AE, Groh JR, Montoliu-Gaya L, Tripodis Y, Aparicio HJ, Turk KW, Budson AE, Farrer L, Goldstein LE, Qiu WQ, Mez J, McKee AC, Zetterberg H, Stein TD, Gobom J, Ashton NJ, Alosco ML.
abstractText:
Introduction

Advances in plasma-based assays have allowed for the study of several tau and p-tau epitopes. P-tau217 has emerged as one of the most robust markers of Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology. Despite their strong diagnostic performance, plasma tau biomarkers require further validation to clarify their clinical utility.

Objective

To investigate the associations between a panel of phosphorylated and non-phosphorylated tau species measured in antemortem plasma and clinical features of autopsy-confirmed AD.

Methods

Cross-sectional data from 123 participants from the BU ADRC who had antemortem blood draws and brain donation following death. Participants completed neuropsychological testing during life as part of their National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center-Uniform Data Set (NACC UDS) evaluation. AD neuropathology was diagnosed using NIA-Reagan criteria. Time interval between testing at last visit and autopsy ranged from 0 to 12 years, mean = 5.54 years. Raw neuropsychological test scores were used for analysis. Sample size ranged from 65 to 91 across the tests. Plasma samples were analyzed using immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry (IP-MS) for phosphorylated tau species (p-tau-181, 199, 202, 205, 217, 231) and non-phosphorylated tau (195-209, 212-221) peptides. Two ratios were analyzed, p-tau217/tau212-221 and p-tau205/tau195-209.

Results

123 participants took part in this study, 55 (44.7%) female, and 6 (4.9%) Black/African American. The mean (SD) age at blood draw was 78.17 (8.55). The strongest association between plasma biomarkers with neuropsychological test outcomes was observed with the ratio p-tau217/tau212-221 (b = - 0.564-0.404, plow-high = 0.00-0.18), followed by p-tau217 (b = - 0.478-0.377, plow-high = 0.00-0.28), both significantly correlating with six of the eight neuropsychological measures (p < 0.05). Followed by the ratio p-tau205/tau195-209 (b = - 0.513-0.356, plow-high = 0.00-0.55), p-tau205 (b = - 0.365-0.226, plow-high = 0.00-0.44), then p-tau231 (b = - 0.319-0.237, plow-high = 0.02-0.62). Fewer significant relationships and weaker effect sizes were observed among the other biomarkers. The effect sizes of the ratio p-tau217/tau212-221, followed closely by p-tau217 on neuropsychological test outcomes, were observed to be the most similar to the effect sizes of autopsy-confirmed AD (b = - 0.564-0.393).

Conclusions

Plasma p-tau217 and p-tau ratios were comparable to autopsy-confirmed AD in predicting clinical outcomes of AD. This study highlights the promise and potential utility of plasma biomarkers for symptom monitoring.

title: Imaging-Based Assessment of Plaque Modification Following Intravascular Lithotripsy in Femoropopliteal Disease: A Prospective Single-Centre Observational Study.
authorString: Sidiropoulou K, Saratzis A, Karkos C, Tigkiropoulos K, Saratzis N, Karamanos D.

journal.title: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery

abstractText:
Objective

Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is designed to treat calcified peripheral arteries with steno-occlusive disease; however, its effect on plaque morphology remains incompletely understood in vivo. This study evaluated plaque modification and luminal changes following IVL in femoropopliteal disease using computed tomography angiography (CTA) and intravascular ultrasound (IVUS).

Methods

This was a prospective single centre observational study. Consecutive patients with symptomatic femoropopliteal disease undergoing IVL between December 2024 and October 2025 underwent pre- and post-procedural (within five days) CTA with quantitative plaque analysis. IVUS was performed before and immediately after IVL, prior to drug coated balloon angioplasty (applied in all patients) or stenting (used only as bailout). The primary endpoint was change in calcified plaque volume on CTA. Secondary endpoints included luminal gain, haemodynamic changes, procedural success, and 6 month clinical outcomes.

Results

Thirty nine patients were included; median age was 71 years. Calcified plaque volume showed a modest reduction (median proportional reduction 12.2%, p < .001) on post-procedural CTA. IVL resulted in luminal expansion, with IVUS measured lumen area increasing from 5.78 to 16.11 mm2 (p < .001) immediately after IVL alone and CTA intraluminal volume increasing 52.7% (median). Haemodynamic improvement was observed (ankle brachial index: 0.80 to 1.00 (median); toe brachial index: 0.40 to 0.62 (median); p <.001) between baseline and 30 days. Intra-procedural dissections were detected in 18% of cases on IVUS; only two lesions (5%) were flow limiting and required stenting. At 30 days, no mortality or target lesion revascularisations were observed, while restenosis at 6 months occurred in 5% of cases. Chronic total occlusion was associated with residual stenosis in multivariable analysis (OR 6.2, 95% CI 1.11 - 34.48, p = .038).

Conclusions

IVL was associated with modest apparent plaque modification and significant luminal gain in calcified femoropopliteal lesions. Combined CTA and IVUS imaging suggest luminal expansion is primarily driven by plaque fracture, altered vessel compliance, and remodelling rather than debulking.
