title: The State of Health in Jordan, 1990-2023: A Systematic Analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study.
authorString: Al-Ajlouni YA, Alawa J, Al-Shamari A, Hazra A, Khoshnood K, Shamieh O, Makarem N, Al Ta'ani O, Zubi SA, Coutts A, Njei B.
abstractText:
Background

Jordan's health system has evolved amid rapid urbanization and the strain of hosting one of the world's largest refugee populations per capita. This study comprehensively evaluates national disease burden trends in Jordan from 1990 to 2023 to inform health priorities.

Methods

Using the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 framework, we analyzed age-standardized rates of disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), years lived with disability (YLDs), and years of life lost (YLLs) across 370 diseases and 88 risk factors. Data were derived from national censuses, health surveys, disease registries, and hospital records, and harmonized using standardized GBD modeling and estimation procedures. Analyses were stratified by age, sex, and cause.

Results

Between 1990 and 2023, age-standardized DALYs declined by 33.88% (95% UI: -37.38 to -30.59), with greater reductions in males (-38.83%; -42.22 to -35.60) than females (-27.22%; -31.33 to -23.58). YLLs decreased by 49.38% (-50.93 to -47.68), while YLDs remained comparatively stable (2.49%; -2.37 to 7.47). Using mutually exclusive GBD Level 3 causes, ischemic heart disease and diabetes mellitus were the two leading causes of DALYs in 2023. Diabetes mellitus rose from 7th place in 1990 to 2nd place in 2023, while neonatal disorders declined from 1st to 7th place. Metabolic risks remained important contributors to the overall disease burden. Jordan's age-standardized diabetes DALY rate in 2023 was approximately 1.56 times the global rate.

Conclusion

Jordan's health profile has shifted toward a greater burden from noncommunicable diseases, while age-standardized health loss and premature mortality have declined substantially. In contrast, nonfatal disability changed comparatively little. These findings provide an evidence base for primary prevention of NCDs and for long-term strategies addressing the country's evolving health challenges.

title: CT-based anatomical and clinical characteristics associated with gastroparesis following cryoballoon ablation for atrial fibrillation.
authorString: Shimosato H, Sasaki T, Usui A, Funayama R, Tahara T, Hayashi K, Nozaki S, Toya C, Hayasaka K, Doi J, Watanabe K, Yamashita S, Shirai Y, Sasano T.
abstractText: Periesophageal vagal nerve injury-induced gastroparesis is a rare but significant complication of cryoballoon ablation (CBA) for atrial fibrillation (AF). Data on the utility of pre-procedural computed tomography (CT) imaging for identifying patients at risk remain limited. We retrospectively analyzed 265 consecutive patients with persistent or long-standing persistent AF who underwent pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) and left atrial roof ablation (LARA) using a cryoballoon system. Symptomatic gastroparesis occurred in 5 patients (1.9%). Patients with gastroparesis had a significantly lower body mass index (BMI; 20.0 ± 3.3 vs. 23.8 ± 3.5 kg/m², P = 0.008). During LARA, the number of cryoballoon applications with esophageal temperature < 25 °C was higher (1.0 ± 0.6 vs. 0.3 ± 0.5, P = 0.004) and the nadir temperature was lower (21.3 ± 7.7 vs. 28.2 ± 6.3 °C, P = 0.01). CT analysis showed a longer left atrium (LA)-esophagus contact length and shorter distances between the esophagus and adjacent structures (spine and aorta) in patients with gastroparesis. All cases recovered with conservative treatment. Lower BMI, wider atrial-esophageal contact on CT, and lower esophageal temperature during LARA were associated with gastroparesis following CBA. Pre-procedural CT imaging may help identify patients at higher risk and inform procedural strategies to minimize periesophageal nerve injury.

title: Current Challenges and Future Directions in US Maintenance Dialysis Care: A Policy-Innovation Perspective.
authorString: Shah AD, Watnick SG.

journal.title: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation

abstractText: Dialysis care for patients with End-Stage Kidney Disease (ESKD) has seen minimal improvement in outcomes over the past decade, despite substantial advancements in other chronic disease fields. This article explores enduring challenges and future opportunities in outpatient dialysis care from a policy-innovation perspective. The current landscape is defined by clinical limitations and a profound economic strain on the healthcare system. However, a period of cautious optimism may be emerging. This is driven by promising innovations, including the development of wearable and implantable artificial kidneys, advanced hemodiafiltration techniques, biologically inspired therapies like bioartificial kidneys, and the integration of artificial intelligence for personalized care. Realizing the full potential of these advancements requires a multi-pronged approach involving a greater emphasis on the patient's voice, payment reforms that incentivize value over volume throughout a person's journey with kidney disease, and supportive policy changes. Yet, hurdles remain, including supply chain vulnerabilities, a growing nephrology workforce crisis, and the need to ensure equitable access to new technologies to avoid amplifying existing health disparities. A collaborative effort is essential to move toward a future where dialysis is less burdensome and facilitates a better quality of life for all people with kidney diseases.

title: Pharmacological activation of sigma-1 receptor by clinically approved drugs enhances K<sub>V</sub>1.5 channel activity in the pulmonary circulation.
authorString: Villegas-Esguevillas M, Barreira B, Hernández-García A, Gibello LJ, Morales-Cano D, Adão R, Sancho M, Moreno L, Navarro-Dorado J, Pérez-Vizcaino F, Climent B, Cogolludo A.
abstractText: Sigma-1 receptor (S1R) is a ligand-operated chaperone involved in the modulation of ion channel function, including the voltage-gated potassium (KV) channels such as KV1.5. KV1.5 channel dysfunction is a characteristic feature of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), and its pharmacological modulation represents an attractive strategy in this context. Here, we investigated whether pharmacological activation of S1R by clinically approved drugs, such as dimemorfan and fluoxetine, enhances KV1.5 channel activity in pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMCs). KV currents were recorded using whole-cell patch-clamp in freshly isolated PASMCs from rats, humans, and rats with experimental PAH induced by SU5416 plus hypoxia (SuHx). Pulmonary vascular reactivity was assessed was assessed in isolated pulmonary arteries using wire myography, and protein expression was analysed by Western blot. Dimemorfan and fluoxetine significantly increased DPO-1-sensitive KV currents, corresponding to the KV1.5 component, without affecting DPO-1-insensitive currents. These effects were abolished by pharmacological blockade of S1R, supporting a S1R-dependent mechanism. Increased KV1.5 activity was associated with reduced pulmonary vasoconstrictor responses. The KV1.5-enhancing effects of both compounds were also observed in PASMCs from PAH rats. The ability of dimemorfan to enhance KV currents was also confirmed in freshly isolated human PASMCs. Overall, these findings support a role of S1R as a pharmacological regulator of KV1.5 channel function and provide evidence that clinically approved S1R-active drugs can enhance KV1.5 activity in pulmonary vascular smooth muscle. This pharmacological approach may provide a basis for further investigation of drug repurposing strategies targeting KV1.5 channel dysfunction in PAH.

title: Title: Impact of Coexisting Gout on Disease Activity in Rheumatoid Arthritis: Data from the Ontario Best Practices Research Initiative (OBRI).
authorString: Kwok TS, Movahedi M, Cesta A, Akhavan P, Carter Thorne J, Pope J, Lau A, Mirza R, Hepworth E, Chow A, Aydin SZ, Kuriya B, OBRI Investigators.
abstractText: To determine the prevalence and factors associated with coexisting gout in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and evaluate whether concomitant gout is associated with worse RA disease activity. We conducted a retrospective study of RA patients enrolled in the Ontario Best Practices Research Initiative, a multicentre real-world cohort across Ontario, Canada. Coexisting gout was defined by patient- or physician-reported diagnosis or xanthine oxidase inhibitor use. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with coexisting gout and the impact of gout on oral glucocorticoid (GC) use. The association between baseline gout and longitudinal RA disease activity (Clinical Disease Activity Index, CDAI ≤10) was examined using mixed-effects logistic regression at 24-months, adjusting for prespecified confounders. Among 3,703 RA patients, 113 (3.1%) had coexisting gout with mean (SD) age of 66.1 (8.7) years and 52.2% were female. Coexisting gout was associated with older age (OR 1.05 per year), obesity (OR 1.67), cardiovascular disease or hypertension (OR 1.95) and diuretic use (OR 1.68), while female sex was inversely associated (OR 0.31). CDAI scores were similar between patients with and without gout at baseline (18.3±12.5 vs 20.2±13.5) and at 12-months (10.9±9.8 vs 11.0±10.4). After adjustment, baseline coexisting gout was neither significantly associated with oral GC use at 12-months (OR 1.73, 95% CI: 0.96-3.13) or the attainment of CDAI low disease activity/remission by 24-months (OR 1.19, 95% CI: 0.72-1.97). In this large real-world RA cohort, coexisting gout was uncommon and associated with traditional gout risk factors but did not statistically influence oral GC use or RA treatment target attainment.

title: The Adolescent Indication for Buprenorphine: What It Is, What It Is Not, and Why It Matters.
authorString: Babul A, Mahdavi P.
abstractText: Adolescents with opioid use disorder remain the group least likely to receive medication treatment despite facing the most severe risks in the current fentanyl landscape. Recent discussions in the clinical literature highlight persistent gaps in treatment initiation and engagement among young people, yet many analyses rely on age classifications and regulatory interpretations that do not align with established pediatric drug development standards. In the United States, buprenorphine carries no formal approval for individuals younger than 18 years, even though international authorities recognize adolescent indications and multiple federal bodies support its use in youth. Long‑standing misconceptions about an age‑16 approval, combined with the common practice of merging adolescents and young adults into broad "youth" categories, contribute to structural and epistemic barriers that restrict access to evidence‑based care. Clarifying regulatory terminology and correcting these entrenched misunderstandings are essential steps toward improving buprenorphine access for adolescents in the fentanyl era.

title: ABCA1 deficiency exacerbates diet-induced atherosclerosis and hepatic xanthomatosis in knockout hamsters.
authorString: Chen J, Zhang W, Shi S, Wang Y, Fan J, Yang X.
abstractText: ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1) is a critical transmembrane protein that mediates the cellular efflux of cholesterol and phospholipids to extracellular acceptors. Lipid metabolism dysfunctions caused by ABCA1 deficiency in humans have been closely linked to atherosclerotic disease. However, ABCA1 deficient mouse models reported so far are inadequate for faithfully recapitulating the characteristics of dyslipidemia and atherosclerotic pathology seen in ABCA1 deficient patients. To overcome this problem, we attempted to use a golden Syrian hamster model because of its lipid metabolism similarities to humans, and generated ABCA1 knockout (KO) hamsters using the CRISPR/Cas9 technique and examined the pathophysiological consequences of ABCA1 deficiency. On a normal chow diet, ABCA1 KO hamsters exhibited significantly lower levels of plasma total cholesterol (TC) but higher levels of plasma triglycerides (TG) compared with the wild-type (WT) controls. Nevertheless, plasma HDLs were nearly undetectable in KO hamsters. On a high-cholesterol high-fat diet, male KO hamsters displayed more pronounced hyperlipidemia with increased levels of plasma TC and TG compared with those in WT controls, a change attributable to a remarkable increase in TC contents in VLDLs and in TG contents in all apoB-containing lipoproteins, whereas cholesterol in IDLs and large LDLs was reduced. Female KO hamsters, in contrast, showed consistently lower plasma TC levels than WT controls. Pathological analysis showed that ABCA1 deficiency not only promoted aortic atherosclerosis but also caused massive hepatic xanthomatosis in KO hamsters. These results indicate that ABCA1 KO hamsters may become a useful model for the study of human dyslipidemia and atherosclerosis.

title: Neutrophils: Heterogeneity, Biology, Diseases, and Therapeutic Strategies.
authorString: Zhang Y, Wu S, Wang Y, Hu D, Yang L.
abstractText: Neutrophils are the most abundant circulating leukocytes and are essential components of innate immunity, contributing to host defense, inflammation, tissue remodeling, and disease progression. Increasing evidence has revealed substantial neutrophil heterogeneity and functional plasticity, which enable distinct neutrophil populations to exert protective or pathogenic effects depending on the tissue and disease context. These properties have attracted growing interest in neutrophils as therapeutic targets and as vehicles for targeted drug delivery. This review summarizes the biological characteristics and functional heterogeneity of neutrophils, with particular emphasis on their recruitment, phagocytosis, oxidative responses, extracellular trap formation, and interactions with the tissue microenvironment. We further discuss the diverse roles of neutrophils in cancer, inflammatory diseases, infectious diseases, and other pathological conditions, highlighting their context-dependent functions. Building on these insights, we review current and emerging therapeutic strategies, ranging from broad neutrophil modulation to precision targeting and neutrophil-based drug delivery. Living neutrophil carriers, neutrophil membrane-coated nanoparticles, and neutrophil-derived vesicles are comparatively evaluated in terms of preparation, cargo loading, targeting properties, advantages, limitations, and translational potential. Finally, we discuss key challenges in the development and clinical translation of neutrophil-based therapies, including manufacturing, quality control, safety, and therapeutic precision, and highlight future opportunities for their clinical application.

title: Phototherapy for Psoriasis in Contemporary, Biologic-Focused Practice.
authorString: Fadel S, Feldman SR.
abstractText: Phototherapy has been a cornerstone of psoriasis management since before the biologic era, and despite being eclipsed by systemic agents, it retains meaningful clinical utility. Narrowband ultraviolet B (NB-UVB) achieves clinically significant clearance rates, has been associated with greater improvement in overall health-related quality of life compared to adalimumab, and is effective across all skin tones. NB-UVB is associated with spatially distinct transcriptomic changes within plaques and downregulation of HLA-C-mediated antigen presentation on melanocytes. Home-based phototherapy, assessed in the LITE trial, performs non-inferiorly to office-based UV and is an accessible alternative. Coverage for home phototherapy is improving. Access barriers, insurance structure, and limited familiarity by prescribers remain obstacles to wider adoption. Addressing these through policy reform, expanded phototherapy coverage, and implementation science may represent an actionable path forward.

title: Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation With Ventricular Unloading in Fulminant Influenza A (H1N1) Perimyocarditis: A Case Report.
authorString: Marchetti MF, Frau F, De Candia G, Cirio EM, Cadeddu M, Porcu M, Montisci R.
abstractText:
Background

Fulminant perimyocarditis is an uncommon cause of cardiogenic shock and refractory cardiac arrest. We describe Influenza A (H1N1)-associated perimyocarditis managed with a stepwise extracorporeal resuscitation strategy.

Case

A 54-year-old woman presented with chest pain, hypoxemia, and cardiogenic shock. Electrocardiography (ECG) showed diffuse ST-segment elevation. Echocardiography revealed severe biventricular dysfunction and a fibrinous pericardial effusion and coronary angiography excluded obstructive disease. Despite vasoactive support and mechanical circulatory support with microaxial flow pump Impella CP (flow 2.7 L/min.), she deteriorated to Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) Stage E with pulseless electrical activity (PEA). During automated chest compressions, mechanical circulatory support with femoral Impella CP was rapidly escalated to venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO). Respiratory polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was positive for Influenza A (H1N1) virus. Antiviral therapy, heparin anticoagulation, ventilation, and organ support were instituted. Hemodynamics stabilized, lactate cleared, and neurological examination after decannulation was intact. Progressive myocardial recovery permitted VA-ECMO explant on Day 3 and Impella CP removal 24 h thereafter. She was extubated on Day 6 and discharged from intensive care unit (ICU) on Day 10. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging confirmed myocarditis; echocardiography at follow-up showed preserved biventricular function.

Conclusion

In fulminant perimyocarditis with refractory arrest, rapid activation of an extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) pathway with early VA-ECMO-combined with ventricular unloading-can bridge to myocardial recovery and favorable neurological outcome. Regional systems enabling safe transfer under continuous cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) are critical.

title: Application of Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy to discriminate serotypes of Streptococcus suis.
authorString: Massacci FR, Cordovana M, Albini E, Cucco L, Piersanti F, Russo E, Leo P, Baldaccini A, Luppi A, Vio D, Paniccià M, Pezzotti G, Magistrali CF.
abstractText: Streptococcus suis is a major swine pathogen and is considered an emerging zoonotic agent. Serotyping plays a crucial role for epidemiological investigations, pathogenicity assessment, and vaccine strategy. The present study evaluated the applicability of Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy, using the IR Biotyper system, for the serotype discrimination of 94 S. suis isolates belonging to 13 distinct serotypes. Analysis of the 1300-800 cm<sup>-1</sup> spectral region demonstrated the highest discriminatory power. Principal component analysis (PCA)/linear discriminant analysis (LDA) showed clear separation among the tested serotypes, except for serotypes 1/2 and 2. The classifier achieved overall accuracy of 90%, which increased to 96.7% when serotypes 2 and 1/2 were considered as a single category. These findings demonstrate that FT-IR spectroscopy represents a promising, rapid, and cost-effective tool for S. suis serotype discrimination. Its performance, ease of use, and compatibility with machine learning approaches support its potential implementation in routine diagnostic and epidemiological workflows. As previously reported for other clinically relevant bacteria, FT-IR spectroscopy may serve as a valuable complementary method to molecular typing, particularly in settings requiring rapid decision-making and high-throughput analysis.

title: Sarcocystis sp. infection associated to encephalomyelitis and myositis in a Brazilian dog.
authorString: do Nascimento Iara ÍH, Martins AFG, de Sousa Ribeiro L, Boabaid FM, de Oliveira LGS, da Silva EMS, Driemeier D, Torres BBJ.
abstractText: Sarcocystis sp.-induced disease is known especially in horses, in which S. neurona is the primary causative agent of Equine Protozoal Myeloencephalitis in the Americas. While horses are aberrant hosts, the range of susceptible species includes marine mammals, raccoons, and cats. Reports of clinical disease in dogs are rare, remaining unreported in South America. This study describes the clinical, pathological, and immunohistochemical findings of a naturally occurring, fatal case of meningoencephalomyelitis and myositis caused by Sarcocystis sp. in a dog in Brazil. A 5-year-old mixed-breed bitch presented with acute non-ambulatory tetraparesis, generalized muscle atrophy, and blindness. Despite supportive therapy, the patient deteriorated and was euthanized. Gross findings included enlarged lymph nodes, moderate splenomegaly and hepatomegaly, with multifocal mild fibrin deposition on the liver capsule, accompanied by multifocal mild hemorrhages in the pancreas. Histopathology demonstrated severe, multifocal necrotizing meningoencephalomyelitis, myositis, splenitis, lymphadenitis and interstitial pneumonia, associated with intralesional protozoal schizonts. Immunohistochemistry supported immunolabelling consistent with Sarcocystis sp. while excluding Toxoplasma gondii and Neospora caninum. To the authors' knowledge, this represents the first report of clinical canine sarcocystosis with this severity in South America supported by histopathological and immunohistochemical findings. These findings support that Sarcocystis sp. should be considered a differential diagnosis for canine progressive neurological disease, highlighting the potential role of wildlife reservoirs in the disease's epidemiology.

title: Hastatoside ameliorates alcohol-associated liver disease, potentially involving ATF4-regulated PANoptosis signaling cascades.
authorString: Cao S, Yuan SY, Jiang YH, Cai WY, Guo X, Sheng Y, Shi LQ.
abstractText: This study aimed to elucidate the therapeutic efficacy of Hastatoside (Has) against alcohol‑associated liver disease (ALD) and characterize the molecular mechanisms underlying its hepatoprotective effects. For in vivo studies, mice were fed a Lieber‑DeCarli ethanol diet for 28 days to establish ALD models, followed by ATF4 silencing via lentiviral shRNA. In vitro experiments involved exposing HepG2 cells to Has and ethanol, followed by transfection with ATF4 siRNA. The interaction between ATF4 and the ZBP1 promoter was verified using a dual‑luciferase reporter assay. Additionally, to investigate mouse bone marrow‑derived macrophages (BMDMs) and hepatocyte crosstalk in ALD, primary hepatocytes isolated from normal mice were first exposed to conditioned media-the culture supernatants of BMDMs stimulated with LPS/ATP, and were subsequently subjected to LPS/ATP stimulation in the presence or absence of Has. Our data revealed that Has downregulated ATF4 expression as well as levels of PANoptosis‑related receptors in ALD models. Silencing of ATF4 via shRNA notably reduced ZBP1 levels and ameliorated liver injury accompanied by global PANoptosis. Hepatocyte‑specific ATF4 deficiency potentiated Has‑mediated inhibition of PANoptosis pathways. Moreover, Has suppressed pyroptosis in BMDMs, thereby mitigating inflammatory responses. Collectively, these results show that Has may alleviate ALD by modulating the ATF4‑driven PANoptosis axis. In summary, our findings highlight Has as a promising candidate for therapeutic interventions against ALD.

title: Comparing BREAST-Q Scores by Race Among Patients Who Underwent Breast Reconstruction: A Global Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Mah AE, Razeghi P, Datta S, Chai B, Hardy J, Snell L.
abstractText:
Background

Breast reconstruction (BR) is an important component of comprehensive breast cancer care. Racial minorities often face barriers to BR access and worse clinical outcomes versus White counterparts. We sought to (1) compare BREAST-Q scores by race among BR patients at least one year post-reconstruction; (2) synthesize mean BREAST-Q scores by race; and (3) summarize reconstruction characteristics.

Methods

In this systematic review and meta-analysis, MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to August 13, 2025 for studies comparing postoperative BREAST-Q outcomes by race globally. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-E. Primary outcomes were the literature-pooled mean differences (MD) in satisfaction with breasts, and psychosocial, sexual, and physical (chest) well-being domains among White versus non-White patients, evaluated with a random-effects meta-analysis. We secondarily pooled mean BREAST-Q outcomes by race and described reconstruction characteristics.

Results

Eleven studies were included, encompassing 8108 White, 702 Black, 1037 Asian, 0 American Indian or Alaska Native, and 0 Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander BR patients. White patients reported significantly higher satisfaction with breast scores compared to Black patients (MD = 5.25; 95% CI [2.90, 7.59]; I2 = 0%; p < .0001), exceeding the minimal important difference. No significant difference was found in BREAST-Q scores of White and Black patients for psychosocial, sexual, and physical (chest) well-being.

Conclusion

White patients reported higher postoperative breast satisfaction than Black patients. Future research should use standardized, race-specific BREAST-Q reporting, while validating the measure across diverse populations to clarify and address structural causes of satisfaction disparities.

title: Non-HDL cholesterol as a lipid control target in severe hypercholesterolemia in primary care: a sex-stratified analysis.
authorString: Gijón-Conde T.
abstractText:
Background and aims

Non-HDL cholesterol (non-HDL-C) is recognized as a co-primary lipid target by the 2019 ESC/EAS guidelines, yet its attainment in patients with severe hypercholesterolemia (SH) in primary care remains poorly characterized. We aimed to assess non-HDL-C goal attainment in SH, examine LDL-C/non-HDL-C discordance, and evaluate sex differences in treatment and lipid control.

Methods

Cross-sectional, multicenter study using electronic health records from 156,082 adults attending 69 primary care centers in Madrid (2018-2021). SH was defined as total cholesterol ≥300 mg/dL or LDL-C ≥220 mg/dL. Non-HDL-C goal was <100 mg/dL per ESC/EAS 2019. Discordance was defined as LDL-C <70 mg/dL with non-HDL-C ≥100 mg/dL. Sex-stratified multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of goal attainment.

Results

Of 6071 patients with SH, only 228 (3.8%) achieved non-HDL-C <100 mg/dL. Men received high/very high intensity lipid-lowering therapy (LLT) more often than women (34.1% vs 26.0%; p < 0.001), yet non-HDL-C levels were higher in men across all treatment categories except very high intensity. Among patients with established ASCVD, men achieved the target more often than women at both the <100 mg/dL (13.9% vs 6.1%; p = 0.001) and <85 mg/dL thresholds (7.8% vs 2.6%; p = 0.022). LDL-C/non-HDL-C discordance was identified in 21.3% of patients with LDL-C <70 mg/dL, more frequently in men (31.8% vs 13.8%; p = 0.006), and increased with triglyceride levels. LLT intensity was not independently associated with goal attainment; diabetes, age, obesity, and ASCVD were the main predictors.

Conclusions

Non-HDL-C goal attainment is critically low in SH patients in primary care, independently of treatment intensity. Sex disparities were significant, particularly in secondary prevention. Systematic non-HDL-C monitoring via electronic records and greater use of combination LLT are needed.

title: Determinants of alcohol use disorder among adults in Rolpa Municipality, Nepal: a community-based cross-sectional study.
authorString: Gharti Magar N, Shrestha G, Kandel B, Badal S, Sah JK, Chiluwal S, Poudyal AK.
abstractText:
Introduction

Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a major global public health concern, with wide-ranging physical, psychological and social consequences. Socioeconomic challenges, family dynamics and harmful cultural and behavioural factors might play critical roles in the onset and progression of AUD in rural Nepal, such as Rolpa Municipality. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of AUD and identify its sociodemographic, economic, cultural and behavioural determinants among adults in Rolpa Municipality.

Methods

A community-based quantitative cross-sectional study design was carried out among 456 participants residing in Rolpa Municipality. Data were collected through an interview schedule using structured questionnaires. A stratified proportionate simple random sampling technique was used to select the participants. The Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test was used to assess AUD, the Family Adaptability and Cohesion Evaluation Scale III to evaluate family dynamics and a validated financial well-being scale to measure the economic status of the participants. Bivariable and multivariable logistic regression were conducted to determine the association of problematic drinking with independent variables.

Results

The prevalence of problematic drinking was 46.7%, with 22.4% identified as hazardous drinkers and 24.3% as alcohol-dependent. Participants with extreme family types (adjusted OR (AOR)=4.55, 95% CI 1.84 to 11.26, p=0.001) and financial difficulties (AOR=2.47, 95% CI 1.10 to 5.54, p=0.027) were more likely to have problematic drinking. Similarly, participants from households that brewed alcohol (AOR=5.25, 95% CI 2.23 to 12.32, p<0.001) and those with poor self-rated health (AOR=2.44, 95% CI 1.49 to 4.02, p<0.001) were also at higher risk of problematic drinking.

Conclusions

This study found a considerable prevalence of AUD in Rolpa Municipality, with nearly half of the respondents classified as problematic drinkers. These findings highlight the significance of addressing family support, socioeconomic stability and awareness and health education programmes in reducing alcohol-related problems in this community.

title: Familial Hypercholesterolemia Screening: From Pediatric Detection to Life-long Management.
authorString: Inoue T, Tada H, Minamino T.
abstractText: Familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) is a common autosomal dominant disorder characterized by elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels from birth and an increased lifetime risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). Early identification and treatment are therefore essential to reduce cumulative LDL-C exposure. Several approaches to FH screening have been proposed, including cascade, reverse cascade, opportunistic, selective, and universal screening, each with distinct advantages, limitations, and implementation requirements. In particular, pediatric screening provides an opportunity for early diagnosis and treatment while also facilitating the identification of affected family members. Screening programs have been implemented differently across countries and regions according to healthcare systems and existing screening infrastructure, with regional universal screening programs also emerging in Japan.However, the value of FH screening extends beyond case detection. Individuals identified through screening should be linked to a definitive diagnosis, risk assessment, treatment, family-based management, and life-long follow-up. This review summarizes current FH screening strategies and their international implementation, with particular emphasis on pediatric detection, and discusses subsequent clinical management and future approaches to sustainable life-long care. Integrating effective screening with coordinated healthcare delivery systems is essential to translate early detection into long-term ASCVD prevention.

title: Transverse Cervical Vessels: A Viable Option for Microsurgical Reconstructions in Vessel-Depleted Necks.
authorString: Torres Gonzalez JC, Rojas Gómez MC, Álvarez Tamayo AA, Baquero RL, Torres Pabón ML, Olaya Osorio JC, Mallarino Restrepo G.
abstractText: Transverse cervical vessels are a safe and reliable recipient alternative for microvascular reconstruction in vessel-depleted necks. In three complex head and neck cases, all anastomoses succeeded, with 100% flap survival, no re-exploration, and no airway or swallowing sequelae at a minimum 2-month follow-up.

title: Inflammation factors mediate association of muscle mass and erectile dysfunction: NHANES 2001-2004.
authorString: Wang Z, Zheng X, Wang H, Liu C, Chen M, Sun C.
abstractText:
Background

Erectile dysfunction (ED) constitutes a global male health issue. Current evidence indicates that low muscle mass may exacerbate insulin resistance and vascular endothelial damage via inflammatory cascades, both of which are established determinants of ED. The relationship between muscle distribution and its effect on ED remains unclear.

Aim

This study aimed to examine the association between muscle mass and ED prevalence and evaluate potential mediation by inflammatory biomarkers.

Methods

The study analyzed data from 2217 participants in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). Appendicular lean mass (ALM) is the total lean mass of the limbs. The Appendicular Skeletal Mass Index (ASMI) is calculated as ALM divided by height in meters squared. The association between ASMI and ED prevalence was evaluated through weighted logistic regression and subgroup analyses. Mediation analyses were conducted to examine the potential mediating roles of inflammatory markers in the relationship between ASMI and ED prevalence.

Outcomes

Compared with the non-ED group, patients with ED exhibited significantly lower ASMI; Monocytes mediated the association between ASMI, vigorous activity, and ED.

Results

Patients diagnosed with ED exhibited significantly lower ALM compared to those in the non-ED group (25.27 ± 4.87 kg vs 27.35 ± 4.52 kg, P < .001). Participants in the highest ASMI tertile (Q3) had a 39.6% lower ED risk compared with those in Q1 (OR = 0.606, 95% CI, 0.396-0.925, P = .033). Restricted cubic spline analysis showed that there was a nonlinear relationship between ASMI and ED in the fully adjusted model 3 (P = .047). Except for drinking status, no statistically significant interactions were observed in any subgroup (P > .05). Vigorous activity showed a significant negative correlation with ED prevalence (OR = 0.604, 95% CI, 0.418-0.873, P = .013). Monocytes mediated 1.76% and 2.01% of the association between ASMI, vigorous activity, and ED, respectively.

Clinical implications

Early screening for sarcopenia and ED, followed by resistance training and anti-inflammatory interventions, may provide a comprehensive approach to protecting muscle mass and erectile health.

Strengths and limitations

Studies utilizing nationally representative databases to investigate the association between muscle mass and ED remain insufficiently explored, a gap that this research aims to fill. The diagnosis of ED relied on participant self-report via questionnaire, which may lead to underreporting or misclassification bias due to psychological factors.

Conclusion

Current research suggests that increased muscle mass is associated with a reduced risk of ED, and that systemic inflammation mediates this relationship to some extent.

title: An efficient hypochlorous acid fluorescence imaging strategy based on toehold-mediated strand displacement for distinguishing cancer cells from normal cells.
authorString: Duan Q, Xu A, Han R, Xu G, Wang Q, Ma C.
abstractText: Cancer is among the most significant diseases endangering global public health. Early detection has been demonstrated to markedly improve prognoses and increase cure rates. Hypochlorous acid (HClO) is a pivotal reactive oxygen species, frequently manifesting elevated levels in cancer cells. Herein, a highly sensitive, highly specific, and efficient HClO detection method was established based on the toehold-mediated strand displacement (TMSD). This method employs a duplex complex (TN) formed from three single-stranded DNAs to carry a fluorescent group (FAM), and introduces a hairpin DNA (HP) with a phosphorothioate (PS)-modified site for specific recognition of HClO. Under the action of HClO, the short fragment bearing FAM group is eventually released from TN, resulting in a significant increase in the system fluorescence. After optimization, the method achieves excellent HClO detection performance, with a detection range of 0.01-7 µM (LOD: 12.9 nM). Analysis of real samples, including tap water, serum and cell lysate, also confirms its good stability and accuracy. Most importantly, the method enables imaging of intracellular HClO, thereby effectively distinguishing cancer cells from normal cells. Overall, this method offers various advantages, including excellent detection performance, fast response times, ease of use, and readily available materials, making it promising for application in early diagnosis of cancer.

title: Association of non-methane volatile organic compound emission burden with chronic kidney disease: integrated epidemiological, transcriptomic and in vitro analyses.
authorString: Yan C, Zhao Y, Chen G, Wu J, Zhang L, Wang T, He Y, Zhang L, Liu P.
abstractText:
Background

Environmental exposure to non-methane volatile organic compounds (NMVOCs) may contribute to chronic kidney disease (CKD), but the underlying molecular pathways remain unclear. We integrated epidemiological, transcriptomic, single-cell, and experimental analyses to identify candidate mechanisms linking NMVOCs to kidney injury.

Methods

Province-level NMVOC emission burden was linked to residential province for 3,472 participants in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). CKD was defined as an eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2. Associations were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Putative NMVOC-CKD targets, kidney transcriptomic datasets, 113 machine-learning models, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to prioritize biomarkers. Single-cell transcriptomics, cell-communication analysis, virtual knockout, and hydroquinone-treated cell experiments were used to investigate candidate pathways.

Results

Among 3,472 participants, 417 had CKD. In the fully adjusted model, higher province-level NMVOC emission burden was associated with greater odds of prevalent CKD (OR = 1.05). The best transcriptomic classifier achieved areas under the curve of 0.964 and 0.836 in the training and validation sets. Integrated analyses prioritized SLC9A3 and localized its expression to proximal tubular cells. Single-cell analysis predicted SPP1-ITGAV/ITGB1 signaling between proximal tubular cells and fibroblasts. In a benzene-metabolite model, hydroquinone increased tubular SLC9A3 and SPP1 expression; conditioned medium increased fibroblast ITGB1 and α-smooth muscle actin expression and migration.

Conclusions

Province-level NMVOC emission burden was associated with CKD. The findings nominate proximal-tubule SLC9A3/SPP1-integrin signaling as a candidate link between NMVOC emission burden and fibroblast activation, warranting validation through individual-level exposure assessment and targeted perturbation studies.

title: Small-Bowel Obstruction due to AA Amyloidosis in Presumed Extrapulmonary Tuberculosis.
authorString: van Wees J, Yan T, Sia R, Moir D, Lu I, Lewis D.
abstractText: AA amyloidosis is rare in resource-rich settings, but remains prevalent in regions with untreated infection, particularly tuberculosis. We describe a case in Australia of a 68-year-old Somali-born woman with recurrent small-bowel obstruction, weight loss, and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy. While colonoscopy was macroscopically normal, small-bowel biopsies revealed Congo red-positive AA amyloidosis. Lymph-node biopsy showed histiocytes with granulomatous inflammation, and tuberculosis testing was negative. Given epidemiologic factors and chronic inflammation, culture-negative tuberculosis with AA amyloidosis sequelae was presumed. Empirical tuberculous treatment led to clinical improvement and resolution of PET-avid lymphadenopathy, highlighting an unusual case of infiltrative small-bowel disease.

title: Abdominal cocoon syndrome presenting with high-grade small bowel obstruction and postoperative intra-abdominal collection: a case report from Saudi Arabia.
authorString: Binmoieql LY, Alomayyer A, Alotaibi S, Alshalfan RI, Almuqbil MS, Alsaab BA.
abstractText: Abdominal cocoon syndrome, also called idiopathic sclerosing-encapsulating peritonitis, is a rare cause of intestinal obstruction in which bowel loops are enclosed by a fibrocollagenous membrane. Diagnosis is often delayed because symptoms are nonspecific and many cases are confirmed only at operation. We report a case of a 65-year-old man in Saudi Arabia who presented with vomiting, abdominal distension, anorexia, constipation, and colicky epigastric and periumbilical pain. Computed tomography showed high-grade small bowel obstruction at the distal ileum with features of encapsulating peritoneal sclerosis. Diagnostic laparoscopy was converted to open laparotomy because of complex adhesions and a mass involving the distal ileum, right colon, sigmoid colon, and bladder. He underwent adhesiolysis, right hemicolectomy, and ileocolic anastomosis. Recovery was complicated by intra-abdominal collections requiring image guided drainage. He recovered clinically and remained well at follow-up.

title: Diffusion-weighted imaging reversal after reperfusion therapy in acute ischemic stroke: associations with white matter hyperintensities and cerebral microbleeds.
authorString: Bannert N, Klassen P, Krijatov R, Dooat A, Nosanova A, Dreyhaupt J, Müller HP, Haeusler KG, Laible M.
abstractText:
Background

White matter hyperintensities (WMH) and cerebral microbleeds (CMBs) are common MRI markers of chronic small-vessel brain injury and have been associated with adverse outcomes after ischemic stroke. However, whether these markers influence early ischemic tissue reversibility following reperfusion therapy remains unclear. We therefore investigated their associations with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) lesion reversal, hemorrhagic complications, and short-term functional outcome after MRI-guided reperfusion therapy.

Methods

In this retrospective single-center study, consecutive patients with acute ischemic stroke undergoing MRI-guided intravenous thrombolysis, with or without additional mechanical thrombectomy, were included. According to the institutional protocol, follow-up MRI was planned 24 ± 6 h after treatment to assess DWI lesion evolution, WMH volume, and CMBs. DWI reversal was defined as a reduction of ≥ 25% in baseline DWI lesion volume. Multivariable regression analyses were performed to identify predictors of DWI reversal, intracerebral hemorrhage, and functional outcome at hospital discharge.

Results

Among 345 patients (median age 74 years [IQR 63-82], 48.1% female), 45 (13%) additionally underwent mechanical thrombectomy. DWI reversal occurred in 76 patients (22.0%) and was not associated with baseline WMH volume, CMBs, initial infarct volume, treatment modality, or thrombolysis time window. Higher baseline NIHSS and modified Rankin Scale scores were associated with lower odds of DWI reversal, whereas hypercholesterolemia was independently associated with increased odds of DWI reversal. We found no evidence of an association of WMH burden or CMB presence with intracerebral hemorrhage or of an independent association with functional outcome. Fourteen patients (4.1%) developed new CMBs on follow-up MRI.

Conclusions

We found no evidence of an association between baseline WMH volume or CMB presence and early DWI lesion reversal or hemorrhagic complications following reperfusion therapy in this cohort. These findings provide no evidence that these two chronic MRI markers are major determinants of early infarct tissue reversibility. Larger multicenter studies incorporating comprehensive small-vessel disease phenotyping and long-term follow-up are warranted.

title: High Rates of Atrial Fibrillation among Inpatients with Heart Failure or Ischemic Stroke in Southwestern Uganda.
authorString: Olds PK, Twesigye P, Nakawesa L, Kasomba I, Haberer JE, Fardous A.
abstractText: Background: Atrial fibrillation (AF) affects over 37 million people worldwide, and its prevalence is projected to increase by 60% by 2050. Addressing AF is critical in Uganda and elsewhere in sub-Saharan Africa, where data are lacking despite the high prevalence of AF risk factors, comorbidities, and sequelae. Objectives: To evaluate AF prevalence among inpatients with acute heart failure or acute ischemic stroke in Uganda. Methods: Between November 4, 2024 and November 30, 2025, we recruited a cohort of inpatients at the Regional Referral Hospital in Mbarara, Uganda with either acute heart failure or acute ischemic stroke. We collected baseline clinical data and hospital outcomes, performed a transthoracic echocardiogram, and equipped participants with a 24-hour Holter monitor. A multivariable logistic regression model was fitted for a primary outcome of AF detection. Results: Among 250 individuals, mean age was 61.7 years (SD 20.5), of whom 175 (70.0%) were women. 123 (49.2%) had acute heart failure; 127 (50.8%) had acute ischemic stroke. Holter monitors detected AF in 105 (42.0%), with a mean AF duration of 11.0 hours (IQR 1.0-21.9) with a bimodal distribution. Mean stroke risk (CHA2DS2VA) was 3.5 (SD 1.6). Factors associated with AF included increasing age in years (OR 1.04, 95% CI 1.02-1.06) and left atrial volume index (mL/m2) (OR 1.02, 95% CI 1.01-1.03). Conclusions: We found high rates of AF among inpatients with acute heart failure or acute ischemic stroke, comparable to studies from the United States and Europe. These findings highlight the need to address AF in Uganda, with improved screening using long-term monitors, updated treatment protocols, and broadened access to cardiac care.

title: Alterations in oral microbiome and salivary metabolome profiles associated with myocardial infarction: a case-control study.
authorString: Lei S, Chen T, Xie X, Zhang X, Song T, Khan I, Li Z.
abstractText:
Background

Few studies have comprehensively profiled both the salivary microbiome and metabolome in myocardial infarction (MI). This case-control study therefore characterized microbial and metabolic alterations in MI patients and identified potential diagnostic signatures.

Methods

Seventy participants (35 MI patients and 35 matched healthy controls) were enrolled. Salivary microbiota were profiled via 16S rRNA (V3-V4) sequencing, and metabolites were analyzed using untargeted LC-MS. Microbial diversity, taxonomic composition, and predicted functional pathways were assessed. Diagnostic performance was evaluated by ROC analysis, and microbiota-metabolite correlations.

Results

Significant differences in oral microbial diversity were observed between MI patients and controls. MI patients exhibited significantly higher alpha diversity and a distinct community structure, with beta diversity separating between groups. Enriched taxa included Bacteroidota, Veillonella, and Prevotella_7, while Streptococcus and Porphyromonas were depleted in MI patients. A four-metabolite panel comprising elevated L-2-aminoadipic acid and reduced thromboxane B2, 4-oxo-2-nonenal, and arginyl-glutamate distinguished MI from controls with high diagnostic accuracy (AUC = 0.92-0.94). Pathway analysis implicated ferroptosis and arginine/proline metabolism as candidate mechanisms. Correlation analysis revealed a significant positive association between Streptococcus and L-2-aminoadipic acid.

Conclusion

MI is associated with distinct oral microbial and salivary metabolomic signatures. A four-metabolite panel shows promise as a potential non-invasive biomarker signature, though external validation is required. Given the cross-sectional design, causality cannot be established.

title: Aggressive Hepatic AL Amyloidosis Encountering Therapeutic Frailty: Rapid Organ Reversal With Tailored Daratumumab-Based Therapy and Low-Dose Corticosteroids in a Patient With Steroid-Induced Psychosis.
authorString: Ceccarelli R, Offidani M, Morsia E, Poloni A, Mandolesi A, Goteri G, Valente M, Ranghino A, Morè S.
abstractText: Hepatic AL amyloidosis can cause severe cholestasis independent of marrow tumor burden. In patients with absolute contraindications to high-dose steroids-such as steroid-induced psychosis-tailored daratumumab regimens with low-dose corticosteroids can drive rapid, life-saving organ reversal. However, intensive antimicrobial vigilance remains mandatory.

title: Evolving Systemic Intensification Strategies Beyond CCRT in Locally Advanced Cervical Cancer.
authorString: Cheng T, Niu R, Li X, Gao X, Chen J.
abstractText: Concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) remains the standard of care for locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC); however, 30-40% of patients experience recurrence, prompting evaluation of systemic treatment intensification to improve outcomes over CCRT alone. This critical review synthesizes evidence from PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library up to January 2026, evaluating clinical trials of intensification strategies categorized by treatment timing: neoadjuvant, concurrent, and adjuvant modalities. Historical attempts to intensify treatment through adjuvant chemotherapy have failed to confer survival benefits with the regimens studied, often increasing toxicity without efficacy (OUTBACK). However, recent Phase III trials have reported survival benefits with specific treatment regimens. Specifically, induction chemotherapy followed by CCRT (INTERLACE) and pembrolizumab with CCRT followed by maintenance (KEYNOTE-A18) have demonstrated significant improvements in overall survival, whereas additional concurrent cytotoxic agents have not consistently improved outcomes and may increase toxicity. CCRT remains the cornerstone; intensification should follow the tested regimen, eligibility criteria, and toxicity profile. PD-L1-based selection and the independent benefit of adjuvant immunotherapy require further validation.

title: Selection of Genetic Conditions for Multi-State Genomic Newborn Screening in BRIDGES-NBS.
authorString: Gold NB, Johnson BA, Somanchi H, Minten T, Coury SA, Zawatsky CB, Begtrup A, Butler E, Langley KG, Zimmerman R, McLaughlin HM, Ellefson T, Kern A, Rehm HL, Bick D, Brenner SE, Kasperaviciute D, Abraham RS, Aksentijevich I, Babinski M, Billington CJ, Butte MJ, Canna SW, Caron M, Chan YM, Chandrakasan S, Chiang SCC, Delmonte OM, Diller LR, Downie L, Fleischer J, Fulton A, Ganetzky RD, Gold J, Goldbach-Mansky R, Grunebaum E, Hale RC, Hamosh A, Hildebrandt F, Holtz AM, Jacobsen C, Kan MJ, Kitcharoensakkul M, Kodyte V, Kreienkamp RJ, Lennerz BS, Lin AE, Madduri AV, Majzoub JA, Marsh RA, Miller DT, Milner JD, Mitchell DM, Murray B, Notarangelo LD, Peng XP, Place EM, Platt CD, Plon SE, Plotkin SR, Powell CM, Puck JM, Roberts AE, Sankaran VG, Schwartz DM, Seroogy CM, Srinath S, Strong A, Sullivan KE, Tan W, Tarrant TK, Thiagarajah JR, Walker MA, Wassner AJ, Bolanos HZ, BRIDGES-NBS team, Gaviglio AM, Bonhomme N, Ojodu J, Singh S, Zarbalian G, Pereira S, Goldenberg AJ, Holm IA, Wasserstein MP, Green RC.

journal.title: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics

abstractText:
Purpose

BRIDGES-NBS is a feasibility study evaluating the integration of genome sequencing into newborn screening (NBS) across multiple U.S. states and territorial public health laboratory programs (PHLPs). We developed a list of conditions for screening.

Methods

We designed inclusion criteria and assembled an initial condition list from published resources. The list was revised by clinical experts, molecular geneticists, genetic counselors, PHLPs, rare disease advocacy organizations, the BRIDGES-NBS Community Advisory Board, and project leadership from the National Institutes of Health. For each condition, we provided a rationale for early detection, diagnostic signs or biomarkers, and treatments or surveillance strategies.

Results

The BRIDGES-NBS condition list includes 777 condition entries associated with 743 genes, one copy number variant, and two aneuploidies and is larger than those used in other genomic NBS research studies in the U.S. and United Kingdom. Most condition entries are inborn errors of immunity (37.2%), inherited metabolic disorders (18.7%), or endocrine conditions (18.1%). Nearly all condition entries (93.3%) can be confirmed using a non-genetic test.

Conclusion

BRIDGES-NBS has established a condition list for implementation across multiple state and territorial PHLPs, enabling the prospective evaluation of feasibility of population-wide genomic NBS.

title: Recognizing Arterial Tortuosity Syndrome in Adulthood: A Case Unveiled by Stress Echocardiography.
authorString: Asachi P, Gandhi AR, Halpern D, Vainrib AF, Sarić M.
abstractText:
Background

Arterial tortuosity syndrome (ATS) is a rare autosomal recessive connective tissue disorder characterized by arterial elongation, tortuosity, and stenosis.

Case summary

A 31-year-old woman with childhood peripheral pulmonary artery stenosis was referred for preconception counseling. Examination revealed a high-arched palate, narrow facies, dolichostenomelia, and joint hypermobility. Stress echocardiography demonstrated exercise-induced right ventricular systolic hypertension and incidental carotid tortuosity. Computed tomography angiography revealed tortuosity of the aortic arch, celiac trunk, and pulmonary artery branches. Genetic testing confirmed ATS. Pulmonary artery balloon angioplasty and stenting were performed. She was initiated on metoprolol and referred to maternal-fetal medicine.

Discussion

ATS in adulthood may be identified following incidental findings of arterial tortuosity on imaging. ATS should be considered in patients with these findings and syndromic connective tissue features.

Take-home messages

Imaging is crucial in diagnosing ATS. Echocardiographic findings of right ventricular systolic hypertension and arterial tortuosity should prompt consideration of ATS in the right clinical setting.

title: Clinical Symptom Burden and Its Association With Echocardiographic Parameters and Comorbidities in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Retrospective Study.
authorString: Athisivam RA, Nagajothi Shanmugasundaram V, Syed Javid Hasan SAH, Ramkumar MK, Damodar NV, Gopalakrishnan N, N S D, H H, Pandian Jeyamurugan HV, Srinivasan H.
abstractText:
Introduction

Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous clinical syndrome in which substantial symptoms may occur despite preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Echocardiographic abnormalities involving ventricular filling, left atrial remodeling, diastolic function, and pulmonary pressures may contribute to symptom burden. This study evaluated the association between clinical symptom severity, echocardiographic parameters, and comorbidities in patients with HFpEF.

Study

This retrospective observational cross-sectional study was conducted at the Government Peripheral Hospital, Periyar Nagar, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, from March 2025 to March 2026. A total of 216 patients aged ≥18 years with HFpEF and LVEF ≥50% were included. Clinical symptom burden was assessed using New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class and categorized as I-II or III-IV. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, and echocardiographic parameters, including LVEF, left ventricular mass, left atrial volume index (LAVI), E/e' ratio, diastolic dysfunction grade, and estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP), were evaluated. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with NYHA III-IV symptoms.

Results

The mean age was 67.8 ± 10.4 years, and 53.7% were female. Hypertension was the most prevalent comorbidity (80.6%), while 76.9% had ≥2 major comorbidities. Fifty-five patients (25.5%) had NYHA III-IV symptoms. Compared with NYHA I-II, the severe symptom group had higher E/e' (17.4 ± 5.0 vs. 12.6 ± 4.0), LAVI (44.5 ± 12.1 vs. 34.2 ± 9.1 mL/m²), LV mass, and PASP (43.9 ± 12.4 vs. 36.8 ± 8.7 mmHg), with significantly more advanced diastolic dysfunction. On multivariable analysis, E/e' (adjusted OR 1.18), LAVI (adjusted OR 1.05), and PASP (adjusted OR 1.04) were independently associated with severe symptoms.

Conclusion

Symptom severity in HFpEF was associated more strongly with abnormal filling pressures, left atrial remodeling, and pulmonary hemodynamics than with preserved systolic function alone. E/e', LAVI, and PASP may provide useful complementary markers of symptomatic burden and support a multidimensional echocardiographic assessment of HFpEF.

title: Impact of malnutrition and nutritional support on infectious complications in critically ill infants and children.
authorString: Kerstein JS, Weld JK, Mulhall DT, Lee JJ, Allfather AE, Morton SU, Martinez EE, Mills KI.
abstractText: Children with critical illness are vulnerable to nutritional deficits, which may contribute to increased susceptibility to infection, impaired immune function and delayed recovery. Optimizing nutritional support during acute illness is therefore essential to improving clinical outcomes. The complex interplay between critical illness, nutrition and infection is nuanced and requires careful consideration to minimize morbidity and mortality. In this narrative review, we synthesize current evidence and considerations regarding optimizing nutritional management to minimize infectious complications across neonatal and pediatric intensive care settings.

title: Cervical spinal cord compression in children and adolescents with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome.
authorString: Boxem JA, Houben ML, Ecker ML, Schwartz ES, Schlösser TP, Zackai E, Crowley TB, Mink van der Molen AB, McDonald-McGinn DM, Tucker AM.
abstractText:
Introduction

Cervical spine anomalies are common in patients with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22q11DS), but the clinical course and risk of spinal cord compression remain poorly defined in this population. Current guidelines recommend radiographic cervical spine screening for cervical instability around 4 years of age, yet cases of compression are often detected later. This study aims to characterize the clinical and radiological presentation of patients with 22q11DS who develop cord compression to aid early recognition and to improve awareness.

Research question

What are the clinical trajectories and radiological features of 22q11DS patients who develop cervical spinal cord compression?

Methods

This is a retrospective multicenter case-series of patients with 22q11DS and cervical spinal cord compression requiring surgery. Clinical and radiological findings were reviewed of routine screening and pre-operative assessment. All 22q11 patients older than four years underwent routine cervical spine screening, in accordance with current clinical guidelines for 22q11DS.

Results

5 patients were identified with cervical spinal cord compression. Three presented with neurological symptoms, two of which could be attributed to cord compression, while two patients were asymptomatic. Four of five patients demonstrated no evidence of cervical instability on cervical lateral radiographs at their initial evaluation (age ranged 2-13 years).

Discussion and conclusion

Most patients with 22q11DS and cervical myelopathy presented in adolescence and did not show signs of instability during initial evaluation for cervical instability. These findings suggest that continued vigilance beyond childhood is warranted, with particular attention to signs of cervical myelopathy during adolescence to facilitate timely diagnosis and intervention.

title: Left Ventricular Myocardial Deformation Abnormalities in Ankylosing Spondylitis (Radiographic Axial Spondyloarthritis): Association With Disease Severity Assessed by Two-Dimensional Speckle-Tracking Echocardiography.
authorString: Saad Reihan M, Mohyeldin MMM, Al-Habbaa A, Bashandy MS, Thalib HI, Ezz IF, Al-Adl Ali Ali M, Bayoumy AN, Ali MA.
abstractText:
Background

Ankylosing spondylitis (AS), also termed radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (r-axSpA) under current Assessment of SpondyloArthritis international Society (ASAS) nomenclature, is a chronic inflammatory disorder associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular involvement, including subclinical myocardial dysfunction. Conventional echocardiography often fails to detect early myocardial abnormalities despite preserved left ventricular systolic function. Two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography (2D-STE) enables sensitive assessment of myocardial deformation through global longitudinal strain (GLS), facilitating the early detection of subclinical cardiac involvement. This study aimed to evaluate left ventricular myocardial deformation in patients with AS using 2D-STE and investigate its relationship with disease severity and duration.

Methods

This cross-sectional observational study included 35 patients with AS diagnosed according to the Modified New York criteria. All participants underwent comprehensive clinical evaluation, laboratory investigations, conventional transthoracic echocardiography, and 2D-STE. Disease activity was assessed using the Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index (BASDAI) and Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Score (ASDAS). Radiographic disease severity was determined using the modified New York sacroiliitis grading system. Correlations between myocardial deformation parameters, radiographic severity, and disease duration were analyzed using Pearson's correlation coefficient.

Results

The study population had a mean age of 33.9 ± 7.3 years, and 68.6% were male. Conventional echocardiography demonstrated preserved left ventricular systolic function, with a mean left ventricular ejection fraction of 65.6±5.0%. The mean GLS was -17.92±4.80%. Radiographic sacroiliitis grade demonstrated a significant positive correlation with global longitudinal strain (r = 0.345, P = 0.046), apical two-chamber longitudinal strain (r = 0.455, P = 0.008), and apical four-chamber longitudinal strain (r = 0.392, P = 0.022), whereas no significant association was observed with apical three-chamber strain, aortic root diameter, or valvular abnormalities. Disease duration showed a moderate negative correlation with GLS (r = -0.544, P = 0.001), indicating greater impairment of myocardial deformation in patients with longer-standing disease.

Conclusions

Patients with AS demonstrated evidence of subclinical left ventricular myocardial dysfunction despite preserved conventional systolic function. Greater radiographic disease severity and longer disease duration were significantly associated with impaired myocardial deformation assessed by speckle-tracking echocardiography. These findings support the potential role of GLS as a sensitive imaging biomarker for the early detection of cardiac involvement in AS and highlight the importance of cardiovascular surveillance in patients with advanced or longstanding disease.

title: Transcatheter closure of a quadriform atrial septal defect with a custom double-fenestrated occluder: A case report.
authorString: Utamayasa IKA, Putri AY, Kartikasari DP, Zuhra Z.
abstractText:
Background

Quadriform atrial septal defect (ASD) is a rare anatomical and functional variant of ASD. Its rarity and complex morphology pose significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, distinguishing it from more common forms of ASD. Although surgical closure has traditionally been the standard treatment, this case demonstrates the feasibility and efficacy of a minimally invasive transcatheter approach.

Case report

A 71-year-old woman presented with shortness of breath. Physical examination and transthoracic echocardiography revealed an interatrial septal defect. Right heart catheterization combined with transesophageal echocardiography confirmed a complex ostium secundum ASD with a cribriform morphology resembling a quadriform ASD and associated high-flow, low-resistance pulmonary hypertension. Device deployment required additional manual modification and manipulation by the operators. Successful ASD closure was achieved using a single 40-mm occluder with double fenestrations. The patient remained asymptomatic at the 3-month follow-up.

Conclusion

Transcatheter device closure may be an effective treatment option for quadriform ASD, although close follow-up is required to ensure proper device positioning. The increasing complexity of ASD presentations, particularly secundum defects, underscores the importance of continued discussion and experience sharing within the cardiovascular community.

title: Early Cardiotoxicity in Pediatric Patients with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia and Hodgkin Lymphoma: Incidence, Risk Factors, and Clinical Implications.
authorString: Meyer R, Dewein L, Baumann T, Rais K, Steinbach D, Kaestner M, Apitz C.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiotoxicity is a major adverse effect of antineoplastic therapy in pediatric oncology, potentially leading to long-term morbidity. This study aimed to evaluate the incidence, spectrum, and risk factors of early cardiovascular (CV) complications in children treated for acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and Hodgkin lymphoma (HL).

Methods

In this retrospective cohort study, 109 patients diagnosed with ALL or HL between 2013 and 2019 were analyzed. All patients were under 18 years at diagnosis. CV assessment included electrocardiography, echocardiography, blood pressure and Holter monitoring, and additional imaging where available. Early cardiotoxicity was defined as CV events occurring during or shortly after therapy, including echocardiographic abnormalities, arrhythmias, arterial hypertension, and other CV complications. Descriptive and exploratory statistical analyses were performed to identify potential risk factors.

Results

Early CV events occurred in 69% of ALL patients and 68% of HL patients. Multiple CV events were observed in 32% of ALL and 36% of HL patients. Most cardiotoxic effects were subclinical or transient; clinically significant CV complications were rarely detected. These comprised treatment-requiring heart failure, arterial hypertension, and thromboembolic events. Persistent CV abnormalities were also observed, including subclinical cardiac dysfunction, arterial hypertension, and cardiac arrhythmias. The majority of CV complications occurred within the first 500 days after therapy initiation. Increased cardiotoxicity was associated with older age, higher treatment risk groups, and disease relapse, while no significant sex differences were identified.

Conclusions

CV abnormalities were frequent in children and adolescents receiving treatment for ALL or HL, although most were subclinical or transient. Clinically significant CV complications were uncommon. These findings support systematic CV surveillance during and after pediatric cancer therapy, with particular attention to persistent abnormalities and potentially treatable complications.

title: Low-Dose CT in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Techniques, Evidence, and Clinical Impact.
authorString: Qurashi AA.
abstractText: Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) is essential for reducing potential radiation-associated risks, but increased noise and artifacts can compromise diagnostic confidence. This review examines how AI is reshaping LDCT by improving reconstruction, denoising, protocol optimization, and workflow integration. It outlines the evolution from FBP to IR and then to deep learning methods that better preserve anatomical detail while reducing noise. The review also considers emerging applications in photon-counting CT (PCCT) and discusses clinical use in screening, pediatric imaging, oncology, cardiac imaging, and emergency care. These developments may support safer imaging, improve consistency across studies, and reduce the need for repeat examinations. However, important challenges remain, including limited generalizability across scanners and patient populations, the potential loss of subtle findings, changes in quantitative imaging features, and the need for careful validation before widespread clinical adoption. Further research should focus on multicenter validation, task-based performance assessment, and integration into routine clinical workflows.

title: Evaluating the 2023 safety-net kidney policy: Eligibility and outcomes of heart transplant recipients in the United States.
authorString: Zappacosta H, Daniel M, Tan N, Cho PD, Song J, White JP, Ardehali A.
abstractText:
Objectives

In 2023, a safety-net kidney policy granting priority kidney allocation to heart transplant (HT) recipients with persistent renal dysfunction was implemented. We aim to compare early outcomes of safety-net kidney-eligible HT recipients and simultaneous heart-kidney transplant (SHKT) recipients.

Methods

Adults in the United Network for Organ Sharing database between July 2023 and November 2025 were stratified into isolated heart or SHKT groups. Isolated HT recipients were further categorized by safety-net kidney eligibility, as defined by the Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network Policy. The primary outcome was 1-year survival for safety-net kidney-eligible and simultaneous heart-kidney recipients. Secondary outcomes included 6-month mortality and acute cardiac rejection within 1 year.

Results

During the study period, there were 309 SHKT recipients and 181 isolated HT recipients who were safety-net kidney-eligible, 67 of whom received a kidney transplant within the study period. One-year survival was similar for safety-net kidney-eligible and SHKT recipients (96.7% vs 93.5%, P = .46). Mortality at 6 months did not differ between groups (2.2% vs 3.2%, P = .51). Acute cardiac rejection within 1 year was higher among safety-net kidney-eligible recipients (17.4% vs 8.1%, P = .01).

Conclusions

The safety-net kidney pathway yields comparable 1-year survival compared with SHKT. However, in this early analysis, staged transplantation is associated with higher rates of acute cardiac rejection. Further studies are needed to validate the incidence and persistence of acute cardiac rejection and ascertain longer-term outcomes to better inform timing of renal transplantation for HT recipients.

title: Incidence and prevalence of cerebral hemorrhage in patients with bicuspid aortic valve.
authorString: Ibrahim R, Albdour K, Pham HN, Omar MA, Lester SJ, Alsidawi S, Ayoub C, Arsanjani R.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Int J Cardiol Congenit Heart Dis
journal.title: International journal of cardiology. Congenital heart disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Int J Cardiol Congenit Heart Dis

abstractText:
Importance

Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) is associated with aortopathy and an increased prevalence of intracranial aneurysms, but the burden of clinically recognized nontraumatic intracranial hemorrhage in this population is not well characterized.

Methods

Retrospective descriptive cohort study using deidentified electronic health record data from the TriNetX Research Network. The study window extended from January 1, 2015, through December 31, 2024. The source query identified 48,582 patients with BAV and no prior aortic valve replacement across 54 health care organizations. The platform returned 45,802 patients for the prevalence analysis and 45,724 patients for the incidence risk set after excluding 78 patients with a prior recorded hemorrhage. The primary outcome was nontraumatic intracranial hemorrhage, defined by ICD-10-CM codes I60, I61, or I62. Incident cases were first recorded events during follow-up among patients without a prior event in the maximum available pre-index lookback. Incidence proportion, incidence rate per 1000 person-years, and period prevalence were estimated. Unadjusted sex-specific risk and rate ratios were calculated.

Results

Hypertensive disease was documented in 26,120 patients (54%) and coarctation of the aorta in 3552 (7%). Total of 579 incident nontraumatic intracranial hemorrhages occurred, corresponding to an incidence proportion of 1.27% and an incidence rate of 1.68 per 1000 person-years. There were 657 prevalent cases (1.43%). Incidence was higher in males than females (1.44% vs 0.94%; risk ratio, 1.53 [95% CI, 1.27-1.84]; P < .001), and the male-to-female incidence rate ratio was 1.61 (95% CI, 1.34-1.94; P < .001). Incidence rates increased across older age strata.

Conclusions and relevance

Nontraumatic intracranial hemorrhage represented a measurable component of morbidity among patients with BAV. These findings support further patient-level studies rather than causal attribution or routine neurovascular screening based on BAV alone.

title: Evaluation and Management of Modified WHO I and II Lesions in Pregnancy.
authorString: Zayat N, Mendoza L, Gupta M, Wolfe DS.

journal.title: Obstetrics and gynecology clinics of North America

abstractText: The modified World Health Organization (mWHO) risk classification provides a practical framework to stratify maternal cardiovascular risk in pregnancy. For general obstetric providers, particularly those practicing outside tertiary centers, this tool can guide management decisions across different health care settings, both urban and rural. The result is the opportunity for early identification of patients who will benefit from multidisciplinary input and require transfer of care. It also provides reassurance when routine obstetric care is appropriate. A structured yet flexible approach that combines mWHO classification, clinical judgment, and multidisciplinary collaboration is recommended to optimizing outcomes in this population.

title: Utilization of Preventive Single-Inflow Cannula Left Atrial Veno-Arterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Cardiogenic Shock.
authorString: Shih YT, Jong HC, Lin CC, Hsiao BY, Tu CM, Hsu JC, Wang TJ.

journal.title: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions

abstractText:
Background

Left ventricular/left ventricle (LV) overload remains a major limitation of veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) in patients with cardiogenic shock. Left atrial veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (LAVA-ECMO) has been proposed to facilitate LV unloading; however, data regarding its optimal timing and clinical role remain limited.

Methods

This single-center retrospective cohort study evaluated the efficacy and safety of a preventive single-inflow cannula LAVA-ECMO strategy, defined as an a priori LV unloading approach implemented at extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) initiation, either through primary LAVA-ECMO implantation or planned early conversion from VA-ECMO within 60 minutes. Between January 2020 and July 2025, eligible patients supported with VA-ECMO or LAVA-ECMO were screened. After predefined exclusions, 42 patients managed with preventive LAVA-ECMO were compared with 64 contemporaneous patients receiving conventional VA-ECMO.

Results

Thirty-day all-cause mortality was lower in the LAVA-ECMO group than in the VA-ECMO group (47.6% vs 76.6%; adjusted hazard ratio, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.31-0.95). Failure to wean from ECMO tended to occur less frequently with LAVA-ECMO (31.0% vs 56.3%; adjusted odds ratio, 0.43; 95% CI, 0.18-1.01). Signs of LV overload during ECMO support were significantly reduced in the LAVA-ECMO group (47.6% vs 82.8%; adjusted odds ratio, 0.19, 95% CI, 0.08-0.49). Overall complication rates were comparable between groups.

Conclusions

In this retrospective cohort, preventive LAVA-ECMO was associated with lower short-term mortality and a reduced incidence of LV overload without an apparent increase in complications. Preventive LAVA-ECMO may represent a feasible mechanical circulatory support strategy in carefully selected patients with cardiogenic shock.

title: Development and internal validation of a Septic Shock Clinical Score System (SCSS) for predicting 28-day mortality in pediatric patients: a single-center retrospective study.
authorString: Ma W, Du C, Li X.
abstractText:
Background

Predicting short-term mortality in pediatric septic shock is difficult due to the variability of the condition and the restricted practicality of current severity scoring frameworks. This study was conducted to determine predictors of 28-day mortality in children with septic shock. The study developed the Septic Shock Clinical Score System (SCSS) and performed internal validation of the score.

Methods

This single-center retrospective observational study included pediatric patients (0-16 years) with septic shock admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit of Shanxi Children's Hospital between January 2020 and December 2024. Clinical variables, including mechanical ventilation and vasoactive medication use, and laboratory parameters obtained within the first 24 h after PICU admission were collected. Univariable logistic regression and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression were used for predictor selection. A multivariable logistic regression model was constructed, and a point-based Septic Shock Clinical Score System (SCSS) was derived. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration plots with bootstrap resampling, and decision curve analysis. The primary outcome was 28-day mortality.

Results

A total of 123 children with septic shock were included, of whom 83 (67.5%) died within 28 days. Four variables were independently associated with mortality: mechanical ventilation (OR 23.95, 95% CI 6.97-100.54), use of ≥ 2 vasoactive agents (OR 6.95, 95% CI 2.08-26.59), prolonged prothrombin time (PT > 18 s; OR 5.33, 95% CI 1.82-17.05), and elevated troponin T (TnT > 40 ng/L; OR 6.70, 95% CI 1.93-28.69). SCSS scores ranged from 0 to 5 points, with higher scores associated with an increased risk of 28-day mortality. The model demonstrated favorable apparent discrimination within the study population (AUC 0.902, 95% CI 0.839-0.965) and apparent calibration based on internal bootstrap validation with 1,000 resamples. SCSS-based risk stratification demonstrated significant differences in 28-day mortality across low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups (23.8%, 90.0%, and 90.9%, respectively; log-rank P < 0.001). Decision curve analysis demonstrated considerable clinical utility across a wide range of threshold probabilities.

Conclusions

The SCSS may represent a simple tool for early risk stratification in pediatric septic shock using variables available within the first 24 h of Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) admission. Although the model demonstrated encouraging apparent predictive performance in this single-center study population, the internal validation was performed on the final fitted model after predictor selection and may therefore provide optimistic performance estimates. Accordingly, the results should be interpreted with caution, and external validation in larger multicenter studies is required to confirm model performance and further optimize clinically meaningful risk stratification before broader clinical application.
