title: Intestinal Failure-Associated Liver Disease: Current Understanding and Recent Advances.
authorString: Abi-Aad SJ, Bapatla A, Khalaf RT.
abstractText: Intestinal failure (IF) can result from diverse etiologies, including surgical interventions and congenital defects, often leading to parenteral nutrition dependence. IF-associated liver disease (IFALD) is a serious and life-threatening complication of IF. IFALD is multifactorial leading to cholestasis during phase I, and steatosis and fibrosis during phase II. Diagnosis and screening remain challenging due to the lack of consensus criteria, and management requires a multidisciplinary intestinal rehabilitation approach. Despite these challenges, outcomes including survival and quality of life of patients with IF have improved over the past decade leading to lower rates of liver and small bowel transplants.

title: Fontan-Associated Liver Disease.

Guidelines for monitoring for progression of disease and risk factors for more severe disease are not well described. Collaboration between cardiologists, hepatologists and surgeons from both pediatric and adult medicine backgrounds in the management of these patients are necessary to provide the best care for these complex patients.

title: Single- and Dual-Colour In Vivo Ca<sup>2+</sup> Imaging in Oligodendrocyte Precursor Cells and Neurons in Zebrafish.
authorString: Bispo P, Czopka T.
abstractText: In vivo time-lapse microscopy of genetically encoded biosensors allows for the optical interrogation of cell physiology. Here, we describe a protocol for single- and multi-channel imaging and analysis of Ca<sup>2+</sup> signalling dynamics in oligodendrocyte precursor cells and surrounding neurones using cell type-specific expression of genetically encoded Ca<sup>2+</sup> indicators. With this method, we can simultaneously investigate the spatiotemporal signalling activity in up to two cell types.

title: Fontan-related protein-losing enteropathy: A comprehensive review of pathophysiology and current therapies.
authorString: Al Atrash E, Zourob D, Alghfeli H, AbdelMassih A.
abstractText: Protein-losing enteropathy (PLE) is a condition characterized by the abnormal loss of serum proteins into the intestinal lumen, and it is one of the most challenging complications in individuals with Fontan circulation. It affects approximately 5%-12% of Fontan patients and is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. As these patients age and milder or transient forms of PLE are more frequently recognized, its incidence is expected to rise. Although early detection and recent advances in treatment have improved quality of life, the risk of death remains significant. This review explores the pathogenesis of PLE in Fontan patients and discusses current management strategies. Treatment options are diverse and include medical therapies such as pulmonary vasodilators to reduce pulmonary vascular resistance, alpha-adrenergic agents to enhance lymphatic tone and promote lymphatic peristalsis and interventional procedures such as widening the fenestration to decongest the inferior vena cava. Additionally, lymphatic embolization guided by liver lymphangiography has emerged as a promising therapeutic approach in refractory cases. This strategy reflects a shift from palliation toward targeted, pathophysiology-driven interventions that aim to improve outcomes and potentially delay the need for transplantation.

title: Letter to the Editor: Coronavirus disease 2019, multisystem inflammatory syndrome, and children's hearts: Finding answers with cardiac magnetic resonance imaging.
authorString: Bregel LV, Efremova OS, Kostik MM.
abstractText: The article refers to "Persistent long-term subclinical myocardial changes in multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children revealed by cardiac magnetic resonance and galectin-3" by OV et al published in the World Journal of Clinical Pediatrics, multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) associated with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and its cardiovascular complications. MIS-C frequently causes cardiovascular complications, including coronary artery dilatation, low left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction, diastolic dysfunction, myocarditis, and pericardial effusion, decreases over time, usually resolving within 6-9 months after the disease onset. Echocardiographic evaluations reveal mild to moderate LV dysfunction, resolving within two weeks. Severe dysfunction normalizes after approximately 1.5 months. Global longitudinal strain proves valuable for detecting subclinical myocardial damage. Long-term effects based on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMRI) data indicate the persistent myocardial edema and/or fibrosisupto12 months after the initialevent. Signs of interstitial fibrosis were found in 7.7% of patients during a one-year follow-up period. CMRI is an important additional method in the assessment of children who have experienced multisystem inflammatory syndrome in COVID-19, especially in patients with persistent symptoms or abnormal data from other cardiac findings.

title: Auxological and pubertal outcomes of children with Kawasaki disease: Experience from Chandigarh, India.
authorString: Thakur S, Kaur H, Pilania RK, Kabeerdoss J, Singh S.
abstractText:
Background

Kawasaki disease (KD) is an acute childhood vasculitis with potential long-term cardiovascular sequelae. However, data regarding auxological and pubertal outcomes in children with KD, particularly from developing countries, remain limited.

Aim

To study physical and pubertal growth patterns in male and female children with KD. We also aimed to examine lipid profiles and their relationship with fat distribution in KD patients at higher risk for coronary abnormalities.

Methods

The research employed a cross-sectional approach and incorporated anthropometric evaluations, puberty assessment, and analyses of lipid profiles. 47 children with KD (32 boys and 15 girls) who were over 8 years old and had been diagnosed at least 5 years prior to the study, along with 54 healthy control participants (35 boys and 19 girls) matched for age, gender, and socioeconomic background were included in this cross-sectional study.

Results

Male patients with KD demonstrated significantly higher height-for-age Z-scores, while weight-for-age Z-scores and body mass index Z-scores were numerically higher compared to controls. Female patients with KD exhibited increased height-for-age Z-scores, skinfold thickness, as well as waist and hip circumferences in comparison to the control group. KD patients demonstrated normal pubertal development, with no signs of delayed or early pubertal onset. Thirteen KD subjects (27.6%) had coronary artery abnormalities.

Conclusion

The study's findings have implications for the long-term follow-up and management of KD in pediatric populations, suggesting that children with KD generally demonstrate normal growth and pubertal development comparable to healthy controls.

title: Does Takayasu arteritis differ between children and adolescents? Insights from a Russian multicenter cohort.
authorString: Podzolkova VA, Geppe NA, Glazyrina AA, Valieva SI, Avrusin IS, Kurbanova SK, Vakhlyarskaya SS, Kostina YO, Yudina VT, Lagutina EA, Osminina MK, Zholobova ES, Podchernyaeva NS, Turginekova EP, Sorokina LS, Davtian SA, Kostik MM.
abstractText:
Background

Takayasu arteritis (TA) is a chronic large-vessel vasculitis with significant age-related heterogeneity. Global data highlight differences between adult and pediatric TA, as well as among different pediatric age groups. However, the epidemiology and clinical features of childhood-onset TA in the Russian population are largely unknown.

Aim

To characterize the clinical and laboratory features, age-related differences, and long-term outcomes of TA in a Russian pediatric cohort.

Methods

A retrospective multicenter cohort study included 79 patients aged under 18 years with TA, diagnosed according to EULAR/PRINTO/PRES criteria, from four centers in the Russian Federation. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and instrumental data were collected. Patients were stratified into two age groups according to WHO definitions: Children (aged less than 10 years, n = 25) and adolescents (aged 10 years to 17 years inclusive, n = 54). Disease activity was assessed using ITAS2010 and ITAS.A. Statistical analysis was performed using StatTech v.4.12.2.

Results

The median age at onset was 11.0 (8.0-14.0) years, and the time before diagnosis was 8.0 (2.0-17.5) months; females were 78.5%. The most common clinical manifestations were malaise (84.8%), fever (54.4%), and vascular bruits (54.4%). Children under 10 years had a lower proportion of girls (P = 0.016), lower erythrocyte sedimentation rate, C-reactive protein, and platelet levels (P < 0.05), ITAS.A scores (8.9 ± 4.3 vs 12.0 ± 4.4, P = 0.005), required more surgical interventions at diagnosis (32% vs 7.4%, P = 0.008) compared to adolescents. At follow-up, 34.4% of patients had persistent vascular imaging activity despite normalized laboratory parameters. Biological drugs were used in 50.6% of patients. Three patients died, all due to postoperative complications.

Conclusion

This pioneer Russian cohort study of childhood-onset TA reveals a unique clinical phenotype. Younger children show lower levels of inflammation than adolescents, yet they still require more surgical intervention.

title: Deciphering Kawasaki disease genetics through next-generation sequencing: A scoping review.
authorString: Kumar A, Thakur V, Dhaliwal M, Kaur T, Raj K, Kabeerdoss J, Rawat A, Pilania RK.
abstractText:
Background

Kawasaki disease (KD) is an acute self-limiting childhood vasculitis. KD is considered the most common cause of acquired heart disease in children worldwide. Despite being the leading cause of acquired heart disease in children, its etiology remains poorly understood. Several epidemiological studies reveal a strong genetic predisposition to KD susceptibility, underlying coronary artery abnormalities (CAAs) and treatment resistance to intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG).

Aim

To evaluate the current literature on the roles of targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS), whole-exome sequencing (WES) and/or whole-genome sequencing (WGS) in identifying genetic susceptibility loci, immunopathogenic pathways, and mechanisms of IVIG resistance in KD.

Methods

We performed a literature search to identify key genes and pathways associated with genetic susceptibility, IVIG resistance, and CAAs development in KD. Our search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar. Studies investigating these features using targeted NGS, WES or WGS were included in this review. Studies employing other methods to investigate genetic susceptibility, IVIG resistance, and CAA among KD patients were excluded.

Results

Targeted NGS, WES and WGS studies of the KD cohort across different regions have identified both rare and common variants associated with KD-related phenotypes. Genes with these variants were linked to immune regulation and vascular biology. Genes linked with innate and adaptive immune responses included TLR6, MEF2A, HLA-DRB1, IL6ST, MYH14, RBP3, EFCC1, FCRLA, PTGER4, IL17F, CARD11, and SIGLEC10. Studies have also revealed genes associated with CAA. These genes were IL17RC, FGFR4, IL31RA, FNDC1, MMP8, and FOXN1, all of which were implicated in inflammatory and vascular remodelling processes. WGS studies also identified novel loci associated with IVIG resistance. These were FANK1, MAP2K3, KCNJ12, CA10, CWH43, EDN1, PPP2R5E, and SFMBT2, as well as previously established genes such as ITPKC, CASP3, FCGR2A, CD40, and IL1B. Many of these genes have known or proposed functions in biological pathways potentially relevant to KD, including TLR and NF-κB signalling, IL-17-mediated cytokine pathways, calcium/NFAT signalling, MAPK signalling, vascular remodelling, and endothelial dysfunction. Moreover, sex-biased variants (EFCC1, LMO7, CEMIP, and USH2A) also revealed gender-based differences in KD susceptibility, indicating a higher risk of KD in boys.

Conclusion

Studies using NGS-based approaches have significantly advanced understanding of KD by identifying key candidate genes and pathways associated with disease susceptibility, CAAs, and IVIG response, and IVIG resistance. These findings support a multi-pathway immunovascular model of KD. Future studies involving larger, ethnically diverse cohorts and functional validation are essential for clinical translation.

title: Primary Liver Cancer and Other Malignancies in Alcohol Use Disorder and Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease.
authorString: Pizarro G, Alcayaga B, Rama K, González-Montero J, Arrese M, Arab JP, Díaz LA.

journal.title: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

abstractText: Excessive alcohol consumption is a significant global health concern, causing over 200 adverse health outcomes, including liver disease, cardiovascular disease, neuropsychiatric disorders, and malignancies. Among these, alcohol-related liver disease (ALD) stands out as a leading contributor to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) worldwide. Moreover, alcohol accounts for 27% of deaths from cirrhosis and chronic liver disease, with 30% of HCC-related mortality attributed to alcohol use. Despite its severity, abstinence from alcohol markedly improves survival, even in advanced stages of ALD, highlighting the centrality of cessation efforts in disease management. HCC represents a major global health challenge, especially in individuals with ALD. Unfortunately, HCC often presents at an advanced stage, limiting treatment efficacy and resulting in a dismal 5-year survival rate of 3.3%. Beyond HCC, alcohol use is linked to an elevated risk of other malignancies, such as cancers of the oral cavity, pharynx, larynx, oesophagus (squamous cell), liver (hepatocellular), colorectum, and female breast; compounding the disease burden. This review explores the intricate relationship between alcohol exposure, primary liver cancer, and other alcohol-related malignancies. It highlights the pathophysiological mechanisms, epidemiological trends, and the importance of alcohol abstinence in mitigating disease progression. Future research must focus on innovative approaches to improve prevention, surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment in this high-risk population.

title: Conservative Management of Presumptive Free Flap Pedicle Compromise on Postoperative Day 6: Report of Two Cases and Literature Review.
authorString: Perozzo FAG, Phuyal D, Ting J, Gaston JO, Levin LS, Franchi A.
abstractText: Pedicle compromise after free tissue transfer typically mandates urgent surgical re-exploration, as flap viability is considered entirely dependent on an intact vascular supply before inosculation is achieved. Whether selective conservative management can be considered in selected cases remains an open question. We report two cases of lower extremity free flap reconstruction in which presumptive late pedicle compromise-occurring on postoperative day 6 in both patients-was managed conservatively with full flap survival. Case 1 was a 71-year-old non-smoking woman with hypertension who underwent coverage of a traumatic pretibial bone-exposing defect (measuring approximately 9 × 5 cm) with a free superficial circumflex iliac artery perforator (SCIP) flap (approximately 10 × 6 cm) anastomosed to the posterior tibial perforator and a deep vein. Case 2 was a 33-year-old moderate smoker who underwent deep inferior epigastric perforator (DIEP) flap reconstruction (approximately 15 × 9 cm) for tibial plate exposure following a fracture fixation and wound dehiscence, anastomosed to the posterior tibial perforator and deep vein. In both cases, loss of Doppler signal and clinical ischemia on postoperative day 6 were accompanied by bedside indocyanine green (ICG) imaging demonstrating peripheral perfusion originating from the flap margins distant from the anastomosis, consistent with early neovascularization. Re-exploration was deferred in both cases. Both flaps developed minor marginal epidermal loss without full-thickness necrosis, and achieved complete healing within 6 weeks. Follow-up was 6 months in both cases. These cases suggest that, in carefully selected patients with multimodal evidence of peripheral flap perfusion, conservative management of presumptive late pedicle compromise may be considered. The accompanying literature review is subject to publication bias, as only cases with successful outcomes are systematically reported; the true failure rate of conservative management cannot be estimated from available evidence. These findings are hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as a new standard of care; prospective validation is required before definitive recommendations can be made.

title: Identifying Iron Deficiency and Opportunities for IV Iron Supplementation in Patients with Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Pryjma M, Buchkowsky S, Feng J, Masoudi S, Barry AR.

journal.title: The Canadian journal of hospital pharmacy

abstractText:
Background

In the AFFIRM-AHF trial, IV administration of iron reduced total hospitalizations due to heart failure in patients with acute heart failure and iron deficiency.

Objectives

To identify what proportion of patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) had iron deficiency and to compare their rate of hospitalization due to heart failure with that of patients in the AFFIRM-AHF trial.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study involved patients with HFrEF seen at a specialized heart failure clinic. Data were collected between February 2021 and August 2022. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients with iron deficiency, with comparison of the rate of hospitalization due to heart failure in this study relative to the AFFIRM-AHF trial.

Results

A total of 284 patients were screened to generate the pre-specified sample of 100. Of these, 73% had iron deficiency. After clinic attachment, the rate of hospitalization due to heart failure among patients with iron deficiency was 21.6 per 100 patient-years, compared with 43.2 in the AFFIRM-AHF trial.

Conclusions

Although more than two-thirds of patients with HFrEF in the study clinic had iron deficiency, their rate of hospitalization due to heart failure was markedly lower than that reported in the AFFIRM-AHF trial. Therefore, the need for routine IV iron repletion in these patients is questionable.

title: Glucosuria as a Marker of Adherence to Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors and Clinical Outcomes in Real-World Practice.
authorString: Li Z, Surapaneni A, Charytan DM, Horwitz LI, Blecker S, Shin JI, Thorpe LE, Melamed ML, Grams ME.

journal.title: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN

abstractText:
Key points

Glucosuria is a proxy for adherence to sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors. Patients with glucosuria during SGLT2 inhibitor prescriptions have lower risk of mortality, heart failure, and kidney failure.

Background

Medication nonadherence contributes to the efficacy-effectiveness gap in real-world practice. Glucosuria, routinely measured on urinalysis, may serve as an objective proxy for assessing medication adherence to sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, a class of medications that reduce the risks of kidney disease, heart failure, and mortality.

Methods

We leveraged 2 cohorts from the Optum Labs Data Warehouse real-world data (2014-2023): cohort 1 included 3987 patients with SGLT2 inhibitor pharmacy claims and a urinalysis performed both before and during active fill periods; cohort 2 included 45,711 patients prescribed SGLT2 inhibitors with urinalysis performed within 6 months after initiation. Glucosuria was defined as urine glucose 2+ or greater. Cohort 2 was followed for a mean of 3.3 years for all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, and kidney failure; fractures were used as a negative control outcome.

Results

In cohort 1, SGLT2 inhibitor use (versus no use) was associated with 18.1-fold higher odds of glucosuria (95% confidence interval [CI], 16.4 to 20.0), adjusted for diabetes status. In cohort 2, 26,657 (58%) had glucosuria within 6 months of SGLT2 inhibitor initiation, suggesting adherence. After inverse probability of treatment weighting, glucosuria was associated with lower risks of all-cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.78; 95% CI, 0.73 to 0.83), heart failure hospitalization (HR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.78 to 0.98), and kidney failure (HR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.91) compared with no glucosuria. No association was observed with fractures (HR, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.95 to 1.06).

Conclusions

Glucosuria was associated with SGLT2 inhibitor adherence and, among patients prescribed SGLT2 inhibitors, is associated with reductions in risks of all-cause mortality, heart failure, and kidney failure.

title: Preoperative cardiopulmonary variability assessment for predicting postoperative adverse events following thoracic surgery: A systematic review
authorString: Aggarwal I, Singh R, Scales N, Herry C, Seely AJ, Jones DG.
abstractText:
Objectives: Postoperative adverse events (AEs) remain a major source of morbidity and mortality following thoracic surgery. Current preoperative risk assessment tools have limited ability to predict individual postoperative complications. Cardiopulmonary variability assessment (CPVA), including heart rate variability (HRV) and respiratory rate variability (RRV), has emerged as a potential biomarker of autonomic function and physiologic reserve. This systematic review evaluated the role of preoperative CPVA in predicting postoperative AEs following thoracic surgery.

Methods:

A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. MEDLINE and Embase were searched from inception to identify studies evaluating preoperative HRV and/or RRV as predictors of postoperative AEs in adults undergoing thoracic surgery. Eligible study designs included randomized controlled trials, cohort studies, case-control studies, and diagnostic accuracy studies. Study characteristics, CPVA methodology, comparator assessments, postoperative outcomes, and risk of bias were extracted and evaluated using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale and QUADAS-2.

Results:

Five cohort studies comprising 693 patients met the inclusion criteria. Four studies evaluated pulmonary resection for non-small cell lung cancer and one evaluated esophagectomy. Three studies assessed HRV directly, while two evaluated functional measures of cardiopulmonary reserve. Reduced preoperative HRV, particularly lower root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD) and high-frequency power (HFP), was associated with postoperative pneumonia, atrial fibrillation, and delirium. Lower RMSSD (OR 0.812, 95% CI 0.720–0.912) and HFP (OR 0.990, 95% CI 0.983–0.996) independently predicted postoperative pneumonia, with good discrimination (AUC 0.867). Risk of bias was low to moderate.

Conclusions:

Preoperative CPVA, particularly HRV, is a promising non-invasive biomarker for predicting postoperative AEs following thoracic surgery. Reduced HRV was consistently associated with pulmonary, cardiac, and neurologic complications. Larger prospective multicentre studies using standardized acquisition and analysis protocols are required to establish the incremental value of CPVA beyond current preoperative risk assessment tools.

title: Fluid Resuscitation Volume After Early Echocardiography and Mortality in Sepsis: Target Trial Emulations With Strictly Pre-Exposure Confounder Measurement in MIMIC-IV
authorString: Ye H, Zhang Q, Chen S, Li P, Wan J, Hao Y.
abstractText: Background Whether echocardiographic phenotypes modify the association between early fluid resuscitation volume and mortality in sepsis is unknown. We emulated three target trials within a single cohort of Sepsis-3 patients with early transthoracic echocardiography (TTE), measuring every confounder strictly before the start of the exposure window. Methods Using MIMIC-IV v3.1 (2008–2022), we identified Sepsis-3 stays with TTE within ± 24 h of ICU admission (first stay per patient; n = 7,819). Emulation 1 (primary) compared post-TTE 24-h fluid volume ≥ 30 vs < 30 mL/kg with a landmark at TTE + 24 h (n = 7,398). Emulation 2 (secondary) compared dobutamine new-users versus non-users within the LVEF < 40% stratum (n = 1,201; 100 new-users). Emulation 3 (secondary) compared vasopressin new-users versus non-users (n = 6,474; 360 new-users). All adjustment covariates—including SOFA components, vasopressor exposure with norepinephrine dose, Sepsis-3 septic shock status, fluid balance and urine output—were measured strictly before the echocardiogram. Overlap weighting was used throughout; propensity scores were re-estimated within phenotype strata. The outcome was 28-day all-cause mortality from each landmark. Effect modification was assessed with formal interaction tests on multiplicative and additive scales. Bias analyses included E-values with hazard-to-risk-ratio conversion, tipping-point grids, and negative control outcomes restricted to diagnoses from prior admissions. Results Post-echocardiography fluid volume ≥ 30 mL/kg was associated with higher 28-day mortality (HR 1.74, 95% CI 1.54–1.97; weighted risk 38.7% vs 24.8%; risk difference + 13.9%, 95% CI 10.8–17.0). The association was similar across LVEF strata (< 40%: HR 1.63, 1.26–2.10, n = 1,361; 40–54%: 2.02, 1.47–2.79, n = 1,180; 55–69%: 1.88, 1.51–2.34, n = 2,752; ≥70% hyperdynamic: 1.39, 1.02–1.89, n = 896) and across RV strata (normal: 1.67, 1.42–1.97, n = 4,814; dysfunction: 1.77, 1.43–2.18, n = 1,979). No formal interaction test supported effect modification (LVEF: multiplicative p = 0.44, additive p = 0.56; RV: multiplicative p = 0.65, additive p = 0.16; LVEF modelled continuously: p = 0.82). A previously observed protective association in hyperdynamic hearts without cardiac disease was not confirmed when cardiac disease was ascertained from pre-admission diagnoses (HR 1.33, 0.90–1.97). The association persisted within pre-TTE SOFA tertiles and septic-shock strata, at 20 and 40 mL/kg thresholds, per 10 mL/kg as a continuous exposure (HR 1.14, 1.11–1.17), with a 6-h exposure window (HR 1.43, 1.27–1.60), and after excluding pre-ICU echocardiograms (HR 1.64, 1.44–1.87). Dobutamine initiation (Emulation 2) was imprecisely estimated (HR 1.57, 0.95–2.60); vasopressin initiation (Emulation 3) was strongly associated with mortality (HR 2.55, 2.13–3.06) without phenotype interaction (multiplicative p = 0.23). The E-value was 2.60 (2.29 for the confidence bound); prior-admission negative control outcomes indicated residual bias acting, if anything, toward the null. Conclusions After strict temporal alignment of confounder measurement, exposure and follow-up, higher fluid volume in the 24 h after early echocardiography was consistently associated with higher 28-day mortality in sepsis, but we found no statistically supported evidence that LVEF or RV phenotype modifies this association. These results do not support phenotype-guided fluid restriction derived from observational subgroup patterns; adequately powered randomised trials with protocolised echocardiography remain necessary.

title: Blood pressure control transitions and subsequent reported stroke among Chinese adults with hypertension in a landmark cohort study
authorString: Zhang B, Shinge SAU, Zheng B, Qiang Y, Liu Z, Zhang L, Gao M, Li B, Zeng K, Yang Y.
abstractText: Background Blood pressure measured at successive visits may identify different subsequent stroke risks, but changes in measured control should be distinguished from treatment effects. We examined blood pressure control transitions from 2011 to 2013 in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). Methods This landmark analysis included adults aged at least 45 years with baseline hypertension, valid blood pressure measurements at both visits, and no reported stroke before the landmark. Control was defined as systolic pressure below 140 mmHg and diastolic pressure below 90 mmHg. Subsequent first reported physician-diagnosed stroke through the 2020 survey was analysed with an interval-censored Weibull model and community-clustered uncertainty. The primary comparison was uncontrolled-to-controlled versus uncontrolled-to-uncontrolled pressure among initially uncontrolled participants. Covariates included baseline demographic and clinical characteristics and continuous blood pressure. Results The complete-case stroke sample comprised 2902 participants with 256 events. Among 2126 initially uncontrolled participants, 190 events occurred. In the primary Weibull model, transition to control was associated with a lower modelled stroke hazard than uncontrolled pressure at both visits (hazard ratio [HR], 0.68; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.49–0.95). Multiple imputation gave an HR of 0.70 (95% CI, 0.51–0.97). A semiparametric interval-censored model gave an HR of 0.69 (community-bootstrap 95% interval, 0.46–0.96). Several exposure-definition analyses could not exclude no association. A lognormal model had a lower Akaike information criterion than the Weibull model and yielded an uncertain time ratio of 1.22 (95% CI, 0.97–1.53). Conclusions In the primary Weibull model, transition to measured control was associated with a lower modelled hazard of subsequently reported stroke. The evidence depended on distributional assumptions and exposure definitions. Death-related underascertainment, measurement error, and selection limit interpretation; these estimates do not establish a treatment effect. Clinical trial registration Clinical trial number: not applicable. This study was an observational secondary analysis of existing CHARLS cohort data and did not involve the assignment of any healthcare intervention to participants.

title: Sustained blood pressure control and rebound hypertension after acute antihypertensive therapy for severe preeclampsia: A multicenter randomized trial of intravenous labetalol versus nicardipine
authorString: Wibowo A, Irianti S, Mose JC, Pribadi A, Krisnadi SR, Handono B, Anwar AD, Siddiq A, Pramatirta AY, Setiawan D, Puspita DA, Fatati I, Primantara D, Gurnadi JI, Kharismawati N, Aziz MA.
abstractText: Background: Severe preeclampsia is an obstetric emergency requiring rapid and safe blood pressure control to reduce maternal and fetal complications. Although intravenous labetalol and nicardipine are used for acute antihypertensive therapy, studies comparing the two first-line agents in severe preeclampsia are limited. This study aimed to compare the effectiveness and safety of intravenous labetalol and nicardipine in pregnant women with severe preeclampsia. Methods: This multicenter, outcome-assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial was conducted in ten hospitals in West Java, Indonesia. One hundred and twenty-three pregnant women with severe preeclampsia were included. The primary outcome was time to target blood pressure (BP). The secondary outcomes included minimum-dose response, dose-escalation response, rebound hypertension, sustained blood pressure control, exploratory (ROC)-derived systolic BP (SBP) cut-off for rebound hypertension, adverse events. Results : Of 123 randomized women, three women allocated to labetalol were excluded due to infusion preparation or dilution error leaving 120 patients for modified intention-to-treat analysis. Labetalol achieved target blood pressure faster than nicardipine [15.50 vs 30.00 min; p = 0.002]. Labetalol was also faster with the minimum dose [11.00 vs 22.00 min; p = 0.003] and after dose escalation [21.00 vs 30.00 min ; p = 0.013]. Rebound hypertension was lower with labetalol [8.3% vs 20.0%; p = 0.067] and sustained blood pressure control was higher [91.7% vs 80.0 %; p = 0.067]. Exploratory ROC analysis identified an SBP cut-off of ≥193 mmHg for rebound hypertension in both groups. Among women with baseline systolic blood pressure ≥193 mmHg, rebound hypertension occurred less frequently with labetalol than nicardipine [17.6% versus 45.5%]. Baseline SBP showed good discrimination in the nicardipine group [AUC 0.839 ; p < 0.001], but not in the labetalol group [AUC 0.644 ; p = 0.291]. No hypotension, tachycardia, headache, nausea/vomiting, or fetal bradycardia was observed. Dizziness occurred in one labetalol recipient and two nicardipine recipients. Conclusions : Intravenous labetalol achieved faster target BP control than nicardipine, with comparable short-term maternal and fetal safety. Women with systolic blood pressure ≥193 mmHg, particularly those receiving nicardipine, may require closer post-target blood pressure monitoring. Trial registration : ISRCTN registry, ISRCTN76310309, registered on 16 September 2026. Retrospectively registered.

title: Assessing EHR Cohort Fitness With Partially Paired Registry Data: A New Statistical Approach Applied to Maternal Health in OneFlorida.
authorString: Harrall KK, Muller KE, Louis-Jacques AF, Barrow SB, Li Q, Shenkman EA.
abstractText: Cohort discovery using electronic health records (EHR) supports research recruitment and pragmatic clinical trials; however, the validity of EHR-derived cohorts depends on whether patient characteristics recorded in EHR are representative of the target population. While methods exist for assessing internal validity, no published methods address continuous outcomes when EHR and reference population data partially overlap at the individual level. We present a novel statistical approach for assessing EHR data cohort fitness when partially overlapping data are available from an EHR and a registry. For continuous outcomes, we derived an explicit test accommodating unequal variances and correlation between paired records. For binary outcomes, we recommend generalized linear mixed models with a binomial distribution and logit link. We demonstrate the new approach using maternal health data from the OneFlorida+ Data Trust (n = 37,200) and Florida birth certificate records (n = 210,910) from 2021. OneFlorida+ EHR had higher rates of Black race identification, residence in areas of higher social deprivation, and pre-existing diabetes or hypertension, while showing lower probabilities of gestational complications. Maternal age, height, and cesarean delivery rates were not meaningfully different between data sources. Observed differences may reflect the academic health center composition of OneFlorida+ partner sites; however, substantially higher missingness in OneFlorida+ EHR than birth certificate records for race, ethnicity, and location of residence suggests that data capture differences play a role. This replicable statistical method provides researchers with quantitative tools to assess cohort fitness and is applicable to other clinical research networks where EHR and registry data overlap.

title: Elevated Lipoprotein(a) Predicts Recurrent Myocardial Infarction in Diabetic Patients Following Acute Coronary Syndromes.
authorString: Echeverria-Ortegon E, Torres-Chávez MC, Tejeda AP, Caballero-Osorno P, Pastor-Cervantes J, Laviada-Molina H.
abstractText:
Background

Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) who experience acute coronary syndromes (ACS) remain at high risk for recurrent ischemic events despite secondary prevention. Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] contributes to residual cardiovascular risk, but its prognostic impact on recurrent myocardial infarction (MI) and repeat revascularization in diabetic patients after ACS or percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains unclear.

Hypothesis

We hypothesized that elevated Lp(a) is associated with increased risk of recurrent MI and repeat coronary revascularization in patients with diabetes after ACS or PCI.

Methods

We conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review and meta-analysis. PubMed, EBSCOhost, and Cochrane Library were searched for studies evaluating Lp(a) and recurrent cardiovascular outcomes in patients with diabetes after ACS or PCI. Observational studies reporting hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were included. Pooled HRs were calculated using random-effects models.

Results

Seven studies comprising 7887 patients with diabetes and prior ACS or PCI were included. Elevated Lp(a) was associated with increased risk of recurrent MI (pooled HR 2.17, 95% CI 1.02-4.62; I2 = 75%) but not repeat coronary revascularization (pooled HR 1.68, 95% CI 0.79-3.57; I2 = 78%).

Conclusions

Elevated Lp(a) was associated with increased risk of recurrent MI in patients with diabetes after ACS or PCI. Findings should be interpreted considering the observational study designs, substantial heterogeneity, and limited evidence for repeat revascularization. These findings support Lp(a) as a contributor to residual cardiovascular risk and its potential role in post-ACS risk stratification.

Trial registration

This study was prospectively registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; registration number CRD420261296821).

title: Prognostic Value of Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SIII) in Predicting Major Adverse Cardiac Events (MACE) in Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI): An Observational Study
authorString: Gambhire S, Agrawal R, Washimkar S, Deshmukh P.
abstractText: Background Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) continue after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) despite advances in revascularisation. Systemic inflammation contributes to atherosclerosis and plaque instability. The Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII) is an inexpensive, easily calculated biomarker derived from routine blood counts that integrates inflammatory and immune pathways. This study evaluated its prognostic value for MACE after PCI. Methods This single-center retrospective observational study included 400 consecutive adults undergoing PCI for stable angina or acute coronary syndromes over 1 year. Pre-procedural complete blood counts were used to calculate SII [(platelet × neutrophil)/lymphocyte]. The primary outcome was in-hospital MACE, comprising all-cause mortality, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and ischemic stroke. Patients were stratified by SII quartiles. ROC analysis and multivariable logistic regression assessed predictive performance and independent associations. Results MACE occurred in 6.8% (n = 27). SII was significantly higher in patients with MACE than without (1127.19 ± 335.99 vs. 599.92 ± 324.55 ×10⁹/L; p < 0.001). High SYNTAX scores (> 27) occurred in 72% of the highest versus 1% of the lowest SII quartile (p < 0.001). Increasing SII was associated with higher troponin positivity and lower discharge left ventricular ejection fraction (p < 0.01). ROC analysis showed excellent predictive ability (AUC 0.886; 95% CI 0.827–0.945), with an optimal cut-off ≥ 776 ×10⁹/L. Multivariable analysis identified SII (adjusted OR 5.36 per quartile increase; p = 0.001) and diabetes mellitus (adjusted OR 4.41; p = 0.024) as independent predictors of MACE. Conclusion Elevated SII independently predicts MACE after PCI and may serve as a simple, cost-effective risk-stratification tool in routine clinical practice.

title: Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio as an independent risk factor for slow flow/no-reflow after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with acute myocardial infarction: a single-center retrospective cohort study
authorString: Li H, Yang M, Wang F, Chen C, Ran B.
abstractText: Background Slow flow/no-reflow after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is a common complication of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and is associated with larger infarct size and worse outcomes, yet simple tools for pre-procedural risk estimation remain limited. We investigated whether the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) independently predicts slow flow/no-reflow after PCI in patients with AMI, and whether adding high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) and culprit-vessel location improves prediction. Methods This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients with AMI who underwent PCI between January 2023 and December 2025. Slow flow/no-reflow was defined as a post-procedural Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) flow grade of 2 or less in the culprit vessel. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent risk factors. Discrimination was assessed with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC); the combined model was compared with NLR alone using paired bootstrap testing of the AUC difference and a nested likelihood-ratio test. Internal validation used bootstrap optimism correction and 10-fold cross-validation. Results Of 305 patients, 53 (17.4%) developed slow flow/no-reflow. Log-transformed NLR (odds ratio [OR] 1.88, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.22–2.88, P = 0.004) and log-transformed hs-cTnI (OR 1.24, 95% CI 1.01–1.53, P = 0.043) were independent risk factors, whereas a left anterior descending culprit vessel, including the left main, was inversely associated with slow flow/no-reflow (OR 0.44, 95% CI 0.22–0.86, P = 0.016). The combined model achieved an AUC of 0.735 (95% CI 0.659–0.805) versus 0.674 for NLR alone (ΔAUC 0.061, 95% CI 0.003–0.123, P = 0.039); the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.719 and the 10-fold cross-validated AUC 0.722, and calibration was good (Hosmer–Lemeshow P = 0.101). Adding thrombus burden, left ventricular ejection fraction, AMI type, age, or sex did not improve discrimination (ΔAUC ≤ 0.002). Conclusions NLR is an independent risk factor for slow flow/no-reflow after PCI in patients with AMI. Combining NLR with hs-cTnI and culprit-vessel location adds discriminative value that is retained after internal validation. NLR is easy to obtain at admission and may support pre-procedural risk stratification, but external validation is needed before clinical use.

title: Machine Learning and Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Predicting 10-Year Mortality after Cardiac Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study
authorString: Jiao¹ R, Zhou C.
abstractText: Background Preoperative neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) is associated with short-term outcomes after cardiac surgery, but its value for long-term mortality prediction remains unclear. We developed a machine learning model incorporating NLR to predict 10-year all-cause mortality after cardiac surgery, and used explainable artificial intelligence to interpret the role of NLR. Methods We included adult patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery from the MIMIC-IV database. The primary outcome was 10-year all-cause mortality. Six machine learning models were compared using grid search, stratified 5-fold cross-validation, and bootstrap internal validation. The best model was interpreted using SHAP on the test set. The NLR cutoff was identified by piecewise regression on the training set. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis were used to evaluate model performance. Results Among 4,891 patients (median age 68 years), 222 (4.54%) died within 10 years. After tuning, XGBoost performed best (optimism-corrected AUC = 0.815; 95% CI: 0.758–0.861), outperforming LASSO regression (AUC = 0.780). NLR alone had an AUC of 0.709, similar to APACHE III (0.732; P = 0.630). Combining NLR with APACHE III improved the AUC to 0.761 (P = 0.002). SHAP analysis identified APACHE III (0.371) and NLR (0.291) as the top two predictors. Piecewise regression identified an NLR cutoff of 6.5. At a 15% risk threshold, the positive predictive value was 23.3% (5.1-fold enrichment). Decision curve analysis showed net benefit across thresholds of 5%-30%. Conclusions Preoperative NLR is an independent predictor of 10-year mortality after cardiac surgery, with performance comparable to APACHE III. The tuned XGBoost model showed good overall performance. An NLR threshold of 6.5 was identified and supported by SHAP analysis. NLR may complement existing risk scores for long-term risk stratification, but should not be used as a standalone tool.

title: Timing of intra-aortic balloon pump support and early mortality after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting in patients with preserved ejection fraction: a single-centre retrospective cohort study
authorString: Rum M, topcu ac, hançer h, bayıcı bb.
abstractText: Background. An intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) is sometimes needed after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), but it is unclear what the timing of that need says about the patient with preserved left ventricular function. Most published series mix different open-heart operations, and the chance of needing support depends partly on the operation. We studied IABP use and timing in one homogeneous group, comparing support already running when the patient left the operating room with rescue support started in the intensive care unit (ICU). Methods. We reviewed consecutive adults who had elective or urgent isolated on-pump CABG with cross-clamping between July 2024 and December 2025, all with a preoperative ejection fraction (EF) of at least 50%. The primary outcome was operative mortality: death during the index stay, or within 30 days. Patients given an IABP were grouped by when it went in and by where support was running: OR-IABP if the balloon was working as the patient came off bypass, ICU-IABP if it started later in the ICU. Results. Of 1224 patients, 57 (4.7%) received an IABP. Operative mortality was 49.1% with IABP and 2.3% without (p < 0.001), and rose across the preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative groups (18.8%, 38.5% and 71.4%; p = 0.002). It was 32.0% for OR-IABP (n = 25) and 71.4% for ICU-IABP (n = 28; p = 0.004); 30-day mortality was 24.0% and 67.9% (p = 0.001). Urgent surgery was more common in the OR-IABP group (76.0% versus 50.0%; p = 0.051). Crude odds of death were higher with ICU-IABP (odds ratio 5.31, 95% CI 1.64–17.19; p = 0.005); after adjustment for age, sex, renal function and urgency the estimate was 4.54 (0.84–24.46; p = 0.078). Conclusions. Needing an IABP after elective or urgent isolated CABG with preserved EF marks a very high early risk. Rescue support started in the ICU carried much higher crude mortality than support established before the patient left the operating room, even though the former group was less acutely ill. These findings raise a hypothesis; they do not show that earlier support saves lives.

title: Older Adults With Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Stage 2: Six-Year Risk Stratification Using NT-proBNP and TNFR1
authorString: Sun S, Zhang J.
abstractText: Background Many older adults without cardiovascular disease meet criteria for CKM stage 2, but their near-term risk may differ substantially. We examined whether NT-proBNP and TNFR1 could distinguish six-year cardiovascular and mortality risk within CKM stage 2. Methods We used data from the 2016 Health and Retirement Study Venous Blood Study with follow-up through 2022. Participants were adults aged 50 years or older with measured CKM stage 0–2 and no cardiovascular disease at baseline. The main analysis focused on participants with measured CKM stage 2. NT-proBNP was evaluated using the commonly used clinical cutoff of 125 pg/mL. Among participants with NT-proBNP < 125 pg/mL, TNFR1 was further assessed using threshold analysis, restricted cubic splines, bootstrap validation, decision curve analysis, survey-weighted models, and competing-risk analysis. Results Among 6,488 eligible participants, 6,205 (95.6%) were classified as measured CKM stage 2. Within this group, participants with NT-proBNP < 125 pg/mL had lower six-year risk of cardiovascular disease or death than those with NT-proBNP > = 125 pg/mL (15.9% vs 44.0%). Among participants with NT-proBNP < 125 pg/mL, higher TNFR1 identified a subgroup with greater risk (27.5% vs 13.5%; adjusted HR 1.68 (1.37–2.05)). Risk increased stepwise across biomarker-defined groups, and sensitivity analyses showed similar patterns. Conclusions In older adults with CKM stage 2, NT-proBNP and TNFR1 identified marked differences in six-year cardiovascular and mortality risk. These biomarkers may help refine risk assessment within CKM stage 2.

title: Navigating the Challenges of Refractory Heart Failure with atrioventricular and biventricular dyssynchrony: Clinical Reflections and Lessons Learned
authorString: Li L, Yang Y, Peng C, Luo Y.
abstractText: Introduction Heart failure (HF), a complex clinical syndrome arising from structural or functional cardiac impairment, carries substantial morbidity with 30% early readmission rates within three months post-discharge and strong mortality associations (1) . The pathophysiological interplay between atrial fibrillation (AF) and HF presents particular clinical challenges, as their concomitant presence portends worse prognoses than either condition in isolation (2) . Moreover, biventricular dyssynchrony emerges as a critical pathophysiological determinant of impaired ventricular filling and reduced cardiac output (3) . The tripartite convergence of these conditions creates a high-risk clinical scenario requiring sophisticated therapeutic strategies. Here we present a therapeutic paradigm employed sequential interventions, highlighting clinical reflections and lessons learned from a staged interventional approach. Methods A therapeutic paradigm employed sequential interventions: initial atrioventricular node ablation (AVNA) with BiV-CRTD implantation, followed by delayed AF radiofrequency ablation 18 months later. Results The patient experienced relief from dyspnea, accompanied by enhanced performance on the 6MWT. The postoperative ECG demonstrated narrowed QRS complex duration,alongside improvements in LVEF and cardiac chamber dimensions. Near 100% biventricular pacing capture was achieved, with progressively optimized left ventricular lead parameters, dynamically decreasing pro-BNP levels and the maintenance of sinus rhythm one year after the AF ablation, collectively confirming the therapeutic benefits. Conclusion Correcting AV, interventricular, and intraventricular dyssynchrony is crucial. The efficacy of CRT varies individually due to myocardial viability, target vessel anatomy, and patterns of delayed cardiac activation. Reducing RV lead output to minimize pacemaker battery consumption in pacemaker-dependent patients with suboptimal LV lead parameters carries substantial risks. Although AVNA can achieve near-complete biV pacing in patients with persistent atrial fibrillation, this approach should be exercised with caution. For future management, Bachmann's bundle pacing may be considered, while left bundle branch area pacing represents a viable alternative when LV lead parameters remain unsatisfactory.

title: Propensity score matched analysis of 5-year outcomes of transcarotid revascularization, transfemoral carotid artery stenting, and carotid endarterectomy
authorString: Cho ES, Ishida AH, Lun Z, Neves PJF, Malgor RD, Malgor EA.
abstractText: Background Prior studies show variable perioperative mortality after transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR), transfemoral carotid artery stenting (TFCAS), and carotid endarterectomy (CEA), but data beyond the first postoperative year are limited. This study evaluated 5-year mortality and perioperative neurological complication rates after TCAR, TFCAS, and CEA. Methods A retrospective analysis of patients undergoing carotid artery stenting and CEA from 2016 to 2022 was performed using the Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database. Patients were propensity score matched using clinically relevant baseline characteristics. Bivariate analysis, Kaplan–Meier survival, and Cox proportional hazards regression were used to evaluate 1- and 5-year mortality, with subgroup analyses based on symptomatic status and perioperative stroke. Results In 2,394 matched CEA–TCAR pairs, 1-year mortality was comparable (2,027 vs 1,923 at risk, p = 0.41), with no difference at 5 years (513 vs 51, p = 0.21). In 2,862 matched CEA–TFCAS pairs, CEA was associated with lower 1-year mortality (2,406 vs 2,397, p < 0.0001), and this difference persisted at 5 years (598 vs 284, p < 0.0001). In 1,758 matched TCAR–TFCAS pairs, TCAR was associated with lower 1-year mortality (1,401 vs 1,468, p = 0.0055), but this difference was no longer significant at 5 years (39 vs 165, p = 0.11). Perioperative stroke rates were low and similar across all comparisons; however, perioperative stroke was associated with significantly higher mortality at both 1 and 5 years. Higher mortality risk was associated with symptomatic status, age ≥ 70 years, diabetes, coronary artery disease, congestive heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and end-stage renal disease. Prior percutaneous coronary intervention was associated with lower mortality only in the TCAR–TFCAS comparison. Conclusions CEA and TCAR demonstrated comparable mortality outcomes at 1 and 5 years. In contrast, TFCAS was associated with significantly higher 1-year mortality than both CEA and TCAR, with this difference persisting through 5 years when compared with CEA. Although TCAR showed a 1-year mortality advantage over TFCAS, this difference attenuated over time and was no longer significant at 5 years. These findings support TCAR as a safe and durable alternative to CEA and suggest a less favorable early survival profile with TFCAS.

title: Association of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic multimorbidity with clinical outcomes and guideline-directed medical therapy response in patients with heart failure: a multicentre prospective study
authorString: Li H, Chen W, Su H, Long M, Zeng H, Shi Y, Li Q, Zhao Y, Liu H, Gui C, Liu Y, Wei D, Tang S, Guo Q, Zhao C, Liao C, Liang C, Ji Q, Zhong Y.
abstractText: Background Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) multimorbidity is common in patients with heart failure (HF), but its clinical impact on the Chinese population remains poorly characterized. This study aimed to evaluate the association of CKM multimorbidity with clinical outcomes and the response to guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT). Methods Based on the GREAT study, this study included 7,339 HF patients from 32 hospitals in an underdeveloped region of China. CKM conditions included atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and type 2 diabetes. The primary outcome was a composite of 1-yeah cardiovascular death and HF hospitalizations. Secondary outcomes included the individual components of the primary outcome and all-cause death. Competing-risk and Cox models were used to evaluate the association between CKM multimorbidity and clinical outcomes. We also assessed the efficacy of GDMT and the heterogeneity of its benefit across CKM burden strata. Results Overall, 72.1% had ≥ 1 CKM condition and 9.2% had all three. Higher CKM burden was associated with stepwise increased risks of the primary composite endpoint (3 vs. 0 CKM: adjusted Hazard Ratio [aHR] 1.73, 95% CI 1.45–2.07), cardiovascular death (aHR 1.66, 1.26–2.18), HF hospitalization (aHR 1.67, 1.33–2.09), and all-cause death (aHR 2.06, 1.63–2.61) (all p for trend < 0.05). The CKM-associated risk gradient for 1-year outcomes was attenuated by quadruple GDMT (p for trend ≥ 0.05). Although GDMT benefit exhibited no significant heterogeneity across CKM strata, the strongest signal was seen in patients with two CKM conditions (aHR 0.69, 95% CI 0.52–0.91). Conclusions CKM multimorbidity is highly prevalent in this underdeveloped Chinese region and predicts a graded increase in adverse outcomes. Quadruple GDMT attenuated the CKM-related prognostic risk gradient, with the greatest relative benefit in patients with two CKM conditions.

title: Heterogeneity in multimorbidity patterns and chronic disease association rules among middle-aged and older adults with cognitive impairment: A dual-cohort analysis of community and hospital real-world data
authorString: Zhang M, Ling Y, Pan J, Xu X, Li Y, Tu Y, Peng J, Zhong J, Wang H.
abstractText: Objective To compare chronic disease multimorbidity characteristics and association patterns in cognitively impaired middle‑aged and older adults across community and clinical settings, and to provide evidence for stratified chronic disease management. Methods A dual-database parallel controlled design was adopted, uniformly referencing the 15 categories of chronic diseases from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) database. After homogenization of the two datasets, descriptive statistics, independent sample t-tests, and chi-square tests were used to compare baseline characteristics and comorbidity burden between the two groups. The Apriori association rule algorithm was employed to mine comorbidity association patterns and core disease clusters in both populations. Results This study included 796 community-dwelling older adults with physician-diagnosed memory disorders and 543 inpatients with confirmed cognitive disorders hospitalized from 2019 to 2025. Significant inter-group differences existed in sociodemographics, sleep quality and chronic disease counts. The community group showed left-skewed distribution: 32.91% had no somatic chronic conditions, mild-to-moderate multimorbidity dominated with a balanced middle-peaked pattern. The hospital group had a right-skewed distribution, with over 85% having three or more somatic chronic conditions. Association analysis identified 46 community rules forming an inflammation-related respiratory-digestive-joint-cardiac cluster. A total of 170 hospital rules indicated severe multisystem multimorbidity with renal, hepatic and pulmonary target organ damage, including 44 rules with 100% confidence. Conclusion Cognitively impaired populations exhibit prominent setting-specific multimorbidity heterogeneity. Early screening for inflammatory risks is essential for community residents, while hospitalized patients require standardized lipid management and targeted organ damage prevention.

title: Comparative Effectiveness of Cardiac Rehabilitation on Functional Capacity and Physical Activity Duration among Post-Revascularization Patients in a Tertiary Care Setting in Pakistan
authorString: Hashmi FA, Ansari B, Hashmi M, Waseem SF, Khan MA.
abstractText: INTRODUCTION Cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, with revascularization procedures such as coronary artery bypass grafting and percutaneous coronary intervention being commonly performed interventions. Despite these procedures, patients frequently experience diminished functional capacity and quality of life. Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) is a proven strategy for improving post-surgical outcomes, yet participation remains notably low in low-resource settings such as Pakistan. METHODS This comparative study enrolled 501 post-revascularization patients at a tertiary cardiac care center in Karachi, Pakistan between January 2020 and December 2022. Participants were categorized into attenders (n = 250) who completed ≥ 15 structured CR sessions within 8 weeks, and non-attenders (n = 251) who attended fewer sessions. Exercise capacity was measured using peak metabolic equivalents, while exercise duration was assessed as moderate-to-vigorous physical activity in minutes per week. Assessments were conducted at baseline, 8-week follow-up, and one-year follow-up. Non-parametric statistical tests including Wilcoxon signed-rank and Mann-Whitney U tests were employed for analysis. RESULTS Both groups demonstrated improvements in peak metabolic equivalents and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity from baseline to follow-up. However, CR attenders showed significantly greater median improvements in peak metabolic equivalents (1.41 vs 0.76, p < 0.001) and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (175.0 vs 35.0 minutes/week, p < 0.001) compared to non-attenders. Baseline characteristics including age, gender, and blood pressure were comparable between groups. CONCLUSION Structured CR significantly enhances exercise capacity and physical activity duration in post-revascularization patients, with attenders demonstrating substantially greater improvements than non-attenders. These findings underscore the vital role of organized CR in optimizing recovery outcomes in low-resource settings and support the expansion of such programs in Pakistan.

title: Timing of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor/angiotensin receptor blocker restart after cardiac surgery and postoperative outcomes: a target trial emulation
authorString: lu q, Liu J, Luo Y, Wan J, Liao B.
abstractText: Objective Restarting angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEI)/angiotensin receptor blockers (ARB) after cardiac surgery is associated with better in-hospital outcomes, but evidence on when to restart after surgery is lacking. This study takes "restart timing" itself as an intervenable treatment strategy and compares the effects of four restart strategies on postoperative outcomes. Methods A target trial emulation was conducted based on the MIMIC-IV 3.1 public critical care database. Inclusion criteria: adult open cardiac surgery, preoperative use of ACEI/ARB, postoperative admission to the intensive care unit (ICU), no ACEI/ARB order in use at ICU admission (t0), and restart before discharge. Four strategies were compared: restart within 24 h, restart within 48 h, restart within 72 h, and restart from 72 h to before discharge. Twelve outcomes were analysed: all-cause death at 30, 90 and 365 days, and 9 in-hospital complication outcomes. Results Among 10 939 open cardiac surgeries, 5 496 patients used ACEI/ARB before surgery, and 1 420 patients restarted before discharge (median restart time 53.9 h). The four strategies contained 259, 664, 872 and 548 patients, respectively. There were 51 deaths within 1 year, 24 within 90 days and 12 within 30 days. Weighted mortality in the four strategies was 4.90%, 2.76%, 3.05% and 4.57% at 1 year, 1.57%, 1.32%, 1.78% and 1.80% at 90 days, and 0.40%, 0.59%, 1.13% and 0.79% at 30 days; at the two earlier time points the intervals of all 6 pairwise comparisons included 0. Compared with restart within 48 h, restart within 24 h had higher 1-year mortality (RD +2.14 percentage points, 95%CI 0.05～4.27; relative risk 1.78, 1.02～2.67; hazard ratio 1.70, 1.01～2.55; E-value 2.95), but this comparison was no longer significant after correction for 6 comparisons within the mortality family (q = 0.23). Among the 15 comparisons whose uncorrected confidence intervals did not cross 0, 8 had q values below 0.05, 3 were 0.054～0.060, and 4 were 0.09～0.23. The risk of reintubation with restart within 24 h was lower than in those restarting at other times. The risk of hyperkalaemia and liver injury was highest with restart at 72 h and later. The risk of infection, pulmonary complications and cardiovascular or cerebrovascular complications with restart within 48 h was higher than with restart at 72 h and later. Conclusions ACEI/ARB restart timing did not differ across the four strategies with respect to 30-day and 90-day mortality; the association with 1-year mortality was not robust after correction for multiple comparisons; the risk of reintubation with restart within 24 h was lower than in those restarting at other times. The risk of hyperkalaemia and liver injury was highest with restart at 72 h and later. The risk of infection, pulmonary complications and cardiovascular or cerebrovascular complications with restart within 48 h was higher than with restart at 72 h and later.

title: Social and Environmental Exposures and the Developing Gut of Newborns With Congenital Heart Disease.
authorString: John AS, Bai J, Calamaro C, Brown AM, Keiffer R, Huang H, Gillespie S, Denning PW, Sanders-Lewis K, Fundora MP.

journal.title: American journal of critical care : an official publication, American Association of Critical-Care Nurses

abstractText:
Background

Dysbiotic gut microbiomes are linked to morbidity, mortality, and poor outcomes, so it is critical to understand their influencing factors.

Objectives

To investigate the impact of nosocomial and socioecological factors on the gut microbiome in newborns with congenital heart disease (CHD).

Methods

This was a secondary analysis of a prospective cohort of newborns with CHD matched to healthy newborns by age, sex, and race and ethnicity. Data on feeding type and routes and disease-related factors were collected from electronic medical records. Stool samples were collected at 3 perioperative time points. Gut microbiome diversity and abundance were analyzed using QIIME 2.

Results

Newborns with CHD (n = 41) showed higher alpha diversity (P = .007) and dissimilar beta diversity (P = .001) versus controls (n = 40). Beta diversity was dissimilar between those receiving human milk versus formula (P = .05), between those receiving fortified versus nonfortified human milk (P = .04), and between those receiving naso-orogastric tube feeds versus other routes (P = .02). Newborns with CHD fed only human milk had higher relative abundance of Haemophilus (P = .04), those with longer duration of aortic cross-clamping had lower relative abundance of Streptococcus (P = .10), and those of higher socioeconomic deprivation had higher relative abundance of Enterococcus (P = .03).

Conclusions

Feeding tubes, formula exposure, aortic cross-clamp, and socioeconomic status were associated with altered gut microbiome diversity. Further study is needed to determine the causal relationships leading to gut microbial dysbiosis in newborns in the cardiac intensive care unit.

title: Timing of Cardiac Contractility Modulation Therapy Implementation.
authorString: Yuecel G, Yildirim G, Schreiner K, Hetjens S, Giannakopoulos K, Kodeih A, Khalil M, Yazdani B, Husain-Syed F, Duerschmied D, Abraham WT, Akin I, Kuschyk J.
abstractText:
Aims

Symptomatic chronic heart failure (HF) despite medical treatment can be addressed with cardiac contractility modulation (CCM) therapy, which has yet to have been investigated regarding outcome differences between early versus late implementation.

Methods and results

CCM recipients from the Mannheim Cardiac Contractility Modulation Observational Registry (MAINTAINED) aged ≤ 70 years at implantation were grouped with regard to implantation time after the first diagnosis of CCM indicating HF (New York Heart Association classification (NYHA) ≥ 2 and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) = 25%-45%) into either Early- (EC, n = 50, implantation < 13 months after diagnosis) or Late-Implantation Group (LC, n = 81, implantation ≥ 13 months after diagnosis). Both groups were compared regarding survival, NYHA, LVEF, and HF-related hospitalizations for up to 60 months. The mean implantation time after the first diagnosis were 5.85 ± 3.1 versus 92 ± 70.2 months (first values EC, p < 0.05). Mean survival was better for EC (55.2 ± 1.7 vs. 52.8 ± 1.6 months, p < 0.05). Improvements in NYHA (2.98 ± 0.47 to 2.0 ± 0.73 vs. 3.01 ± 0.46 to 2.25 ± 0.8, both p < 0.05) and LVEF (23.2 ± 7.5 to ± 38.82 ± 12.85 vs. 23.9 ± 7 to 29.92 ± 8.9%, each p < 0.05) were comparable, with differences in terms of grouping. Hospitalizations due to HF were more frequent to LC patients (39 vs. 110 events, Odds Ratio 2.1).

Conclusions

Heart failure patients might experience improvements in functional status and left ventricular reverse remodeling following CCM therapy, regardless of the timing of implantation. Early implementation of CCM within the first year of CCM suitable HF might provide additional benefits regarding survival, left ventricular systolic recovery and protection against heart failure hospitalizations.

title: Right Ventricular Dysfunction and Ventriculo-Arterial Uncoupling in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Phenotype-Specific Review of Mechanisms, Diagnosis, and Therapeutic Strategies.
authorString: Chamoun A, Farooq T, Batool S, Tameez-Ud-Din S, Yousaf M, Memon P, Ali M, Maloth AK, Sawaira FNU, Khan MT, Ali ME, Khalid M, Pandit M, Kamil KA.
abstractText:
Background

Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) accounts for nearly half of all global heart failure cases. Historically viewed as a left-centric diastolic disorder, emerging evidence identifies right ventricular (RV) dysfunction and impaired ventriculo-arterial (RV-PA) coupling as central drivers of exercise intolerance, functional decline, and adverse clinical outcomes.

Objectives

This review synthesizes current evidence on the pathophysiological mechanisms, advanced diagnostic modalities, prognostic implications, and phenotype-specific therapies for RV dysfunction in HFpEF, advocating for a transition to systematic biventricular evaluation.

Methods

A structured, PRISMA-informed search of PubMed and Scopus (2015-2024) identified 74 eligible studies evaluating RV structure, function, and hemodynamics in HFpEF cohorts.

Results

RV dysfunction is prevalent in 19% to 33% of HFpEF patients and independently predicts all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalizations. Key pathophysiological drivers include post-capillary pulmonary hypertension, impaired RV lusitropy, systemic inflammation, and inter-ventricular dependence. Non-invasive markers notably speckle-tracking echocardiography, 4D-flow cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), and the TAPSE/PASP ratio enable early identification of subclinical RV-PA uncoupling. While traditional heart failure therapies show limited efficacy, emerging options including SGLT2 inhibitors, interatrial shunt devices, GLP-1 receptor agonists, and targeted pulmonary vasodilators demonstrate potential to preserve RV strain and restore hemodynamics across distinct clinical phenotypes.

Conclusions

RV dysfunction is a major prognostic marker in HFpEF. Routine inclusion of RV-PA coupling indices in diagnostic and risk-stratification algorithms is essential to guide precision-based, phenotype-guided management and improve clinical trajectories.

title: Cost-effectiveness analysis of nurse practitioner-led care for patients with heart failure in Japan
authorString: Ueta K, Saito E, Saito S, Ohde S.
abstractText: Background Heart failure (HF) is a leading cause of hospitalization and mortality in Japan. As its population ages rapidly, Japan is projected to experience an “HF pandemic” by 2030, placing an unprecedented burden on health care systems. Owing to increasing physician shortages and regional disparities in access to care, nurse practitioner (NP)-led care has been proposed as a promising strategy for sustainable HF management. However, no cost-effectiveness analysis of NP-led care for patients with HF has been conducted in Japan. Methods We developed a monthly cycle microsimulation Markov model over a 10-year horizon to compare NP-led care plus usual care versus usual care alone for hospitalized patients with HF in Japan (mean age: 76.5 years) from a health care payer perspective. The primary outcome was the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) per quality-adjusted life year (QALY) gained, with a willingness-to-pay (WTP) threshold of JPY 5,000,000. A 2% annual discount rate was applied to both costs and outcomes. Deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were performed. Results NP-led care yielded 3.54 QALYs versus 3.19 for usual care at costs of JPY 2,836,905 versus JPY 2,737,740, respectively. The base-case ICER was JPY 278,680 per QALY, which was below the WTP threshold. Under a conservative scenario in which the effect of NP-led care on readmission was reduced by 50%, the ICER was JPY 676,239 per QALY. Conclusion NP-led care for patients with HF was cost-effective across a range of sensitivity analyses, supporting its potential as a cost-effective strategy to support HF management in Japan.

title: Pulmonary Embolism as a Risk Factor for Necrotizing Pneumonia in Mechanically Ventilated Patients With Severe COVID-19: A Matched Case–Control Study
authorString: Hidrón A, Agudelo C, Ramirez I, Moncada D, Penagos S, Albarracin J, Villa P, Rosa GDl.
abstractText: Background Necrotizing pneumonia (NP) is an uncommon but life-threatening complication of pulmonary infection characterized by parenchymal liquefaction and cavitation. During the COVID-19 pandemic, we observed a high incidence of NP among mechanically ventilated patients (MVP) with severe disease. We sought to identify risk factors associated with NP in this population. Methods We conducted a retrospective matched case–control study including adult ICU patients with laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 requiring invasive mechanical ventilation between March 2020 and June 2021. Cases were patients who developed NP based on radiologic or surgical findings. Controls were matched 3:1 by duration of mechanical ventilation (± 2 days). Conditional logistic regression was used for univariate and multivariate analyses. Results Among 936 mechanically ventilated patients, 42 (4.5%) developed NP. Mortality was significantly higher in patients with NP compared with those without NP (71% vs 44%). Thirty-seven cases were matched to 111 controls. In univariate analysis, male sex, lower body mass index, hypertension, elevated D-dimer levels, pulmonary embolism (PE), pulmonary infarction, and repeated isolation of the same bacterial species were associated with NP. In a multivariable model adjusting for a pre-specified set of clinically relevant covariates, PE during hospitalization remained associated with NP (adjusted OR 5.45; 95% CI 1.85–16.06; P = .002). Conclusions Pulmonary embolism is associated with the development of necrotizing pneumonia in mechanically ventilated patients with severe COVID-19, consistent with a potential thrombotic-ischemic mechanism underlying lung necrosis with subsequent infection. Trial registration Not applicable. This was a retrospective observational study, not a healthcare intervention trial.

title: Association between Admission Total Cholesterol and In-Hospital Mortality in Acute Decompensated Heart Failure: A Prospective Cohort Study from Syria
authorString: Diab QM, Al-Khatib MA, Bakkar B.
abstractText: Background An apparent inverse relationship between cholesterol levels and mortality — the "cholesterol paradox" — has been described in chronic heart failure, but data from Middle Eastern patients with acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) are scarce. This study evaluated the association between admission lipid profile and in-hospital mortality in Syrian patients with ADHF. Methods A prospective cohort study was conducted at two tertiary university hospitals in Damascus, Syria (Al-Mouassat and Al-Watani) from March 2025 to March 2026, enrolling 166 consecutive adult patients with ADHF (2021 European Society of Cardiology [ESC] criteria). Lipid profiles were measured within 24 hours of admission. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, bivariate, and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed; Firth's penalized likelihood regression was used as a sensitivity analysis given the limited number of events. Results In-hospital mortality was 15.1% (25/166). Non-survivors had significantly lower total cholesterol (TC) (142.8 ± 38.4 vs. 168.5 ± 42.6 mg/dL, P = 0.005) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) (78.4 ± 28.2 vs. 96.6 ± 32.8 mg/dL, P = 0.009). TC showed moderate discrimination (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.712; optimal cutoff ≤ 130 mg/dL); LDL-C showed fair discrimination (AUC = 0.632; optimal cutoff ≤ 88 mg/dL). In multivariate analysis, TC < 150 mg/dL was independently associated with mortality (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 2.38, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.12–5.06, P = 0.024); LDL-C was significant in bivariate analysis (P = 0.009) but did not retain independent significance after adjustment for TC and other covariates (AOR = 1.89, P = 0.069). Five independent predictors were identified: oxygen saturation < 90%, TC < 150 mg/dL, age ≥ 70 years, New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class IV, and sodium < 135 mEq/L (model AUC = 0.827). Firth's sensitivity analysis yielded consistent estimates. Conclusions Lower admission TC is independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality in Syrian ADHF patients, supporting the cholesterol paradox in this previously understudied population. LDL-C was associated with mortality only at the bivariate level. The cutoffs of 130 mg/dL (ROC-derived) and 150 mg/dL (multivariate-derived) should be externally validated in larger multicenter studies that include natriuretic peptides and apply propensity score methods.

title: Renal Dysfunction Predicts Adverse Clinical Outcomes Independent of Arrhythmic Control After VT Ablation in Structural Heart Disease
authorString: Nesapiragasan V, Khalaph M, Trajkovska N, Lucas P, El-shirbiny H, Jurisic S, Sciacca V, Fink T, Akkaya E, Moersdorf M, Hamriti ME, Imnadze G, Guckel D, Sohns C, Sommer P, Darma A.
abstractText: Background The prognostic significance of renal dysfunction (RD) in patients undergoing catheter ablation for ventricular tachycardia (VT) in structural heart disease (SHD) remains incompletely defined. Whether RD reflects a marker of arrhythmia-independent disease severity or also compromises ablation efficacy is unknown. Objective To evaluate the association between RD and outcomes after VT ablation, focusing on whether RD affects arrhythmic efficacy (VT recurrence) independently of the composite endpoint of left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation, heart transplantation (HTx), or death. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 499 consecutive patients with SHD undergoing index VT ablation (2019–2025) at a tertiary center, stratified by RD status. The primary composite endpoint comprised LVAD, HTx, or death; VT recurrence was analyzed separately. Multivariable Cox regression assessed the independent association between RD and outcomes, adjusting for age, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), sex, and cardiomyopathy etiology. Results Of 499 patients, 109 (21.8%) had RD. Patients with RD were older, had lower LVEF, and greater comorbidity burden (all p < 0.005). Procedural characteristics and VT recurrence were comparable between groups (47.7% vs. 47.9%, p = 1.00). The composite endpoint occurred more often with RD (48.6% vs. 21.3%, p < 0.001), with diverging event-free survival (log-rank p < 0.001). RD remained an independent predictor of the composite endpoint (HR 1.77, 95% CI 1.22–2.58, p = 0.003), consistent across LVAD (HR 1.79, p = 0.036), HTx (HR 2.22, p = 0.046), and death (HR 1.76, p = 0.022). Conclusion RD is associated with worse clinical outcomes after VT ablation despite preserved arrhythmic efficacy, and should be integrated into post-ablation risk stratification.

title: miR-195-3p alleviates atherosclerosis by regulating VSMC functions through JNK2/NF-κB pathway
authorString: Hou P, Lv T, Lu Q, Zhao X, Ding S.
abstractText: Background and Aim: Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammatory vascular disease and the primary pathological driver of life-threatening cardiovascular diseases. Vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) contribute critically to vascular remodeling; their aberrant proliferation, migration, phenotypic switching and inflammatory activation promote atherosclerotic lesion development. miR-195-3p is a potential vasculo-protective microRNA, yet its exact functions and downstream mechanisms in VSMC-related atherosclerosis remain poorly defined. This study investigated the biological role of miR-195-3p in VSMCs and its molecular regulatory axis.
