Methods and Results miR-195-3p expression was measured in plasma from patients with coronary artery disease, atherosclerotic aortas from high-fat diet-fed ApoE⁻/⁻ mice, and pathologically stimulated VSMCs. miR-195-3p was significantly downregulated under atherosclerotic conditions. Gain- and loss-of-function assays showed that miR-195-3p overexpression suppressed VSMC proliferation, migration and inflammation while preserving the contractile phenotype, whereas miR-195-3p inhibition induced pathological VSMC dysfunction. Transcriptomic, bioinformatic and dual-luciferase assays identified JNK2 as a direct target of miR-195-3p. Rescue experiments confirmed JNK2 mediates miR-195-3p’s protective effects, and JNK2 aggravates VSMC dysfunction partly through activating the NF-κB inflammatory cascade. In ApoE⁻/⁻ mice, AAV-mediated miR-195-3p overexpression reduced plaque burden, repressed JNK2/NF-κB signaling, restored VSMC homeostasis and mitigated vascular inflammation. Conclusions miR-195-3p maintains VSMC homeostasis and alleviates atherosclerosis by directly targeting JNK2 and inhibiting the NF-κB cascade. The miR-195-3p/JNK2/NF-κB axis enriches our understanding of atherosclerosis pathogenesis and offers candidate molecular targets for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease therapy.

title: Senescence-associated KRAS upregulation in peripheral T cells links to premature coronary artery disease
authorString: Sun Z, Yang Z, Wang X, Zhang M, Gao R, Yang M, Li Y, Liu Q, Hou J.
abstractText: Aims Premature coronary artery disease (PCAD) lacks specific molecular drivers, and the role of immunosenescence is unclear. We investigated whether aging-related gene dysregulation in T cells contributes to PCAD. Methods We combined bulk transcriptomics of PBMCs from 12 PCAD patients and 21 controls, single-cell RNA sequencing of PBMCs and human atherosclerotic plaques, weighted gene co‑expression network analysis, gene perturbation network analysis, and molecular docking. Results KRAS was identified as a hub gene intersecting PCAD-associated genes and aging-related genes. Single-cell analysis showed KRAS upregulation predominantly in effector CD8 + T cells, which exhibited the highest senescence scores that were further elevated in disease. Network perturbation of KRAS strongly impacted the cell killing pathway. KRAS-high effector CD8 + T cells were detected in coronary and carotid plaques, displaying enhanced cytotoxicity, exhaustion, and senescence features. Additionally, a candidate small molecule was computationally predicted to bind inactive KRAS. Conclusions Elevated KRAS expression in senescent, cytotoxic CD8 + T cells is associated with PCAD, bridging immunosenescence and premature atherosclerosis. This finding provides a novel biomarker candidate and potential therapeutic entry point, awaiting further functional validation.

title: Evaluation of Vena Cava Inferior Collapsibility Index With Ultrasonography in Children Undergoing General Anesthesia and Regional Anesthesia for Lower Abdominal and Urogenital Surgery
authorString: SANDIKÇI E, IŞIK PDB.
abstractText: Background: Pediatric anesthetic management requires careful hemodynamic monitoring due to limited cardiovascular reserve and age-dependent physiological differences. Neuraxial anesthesia may affect hemodynamics differently from general anesthesia. Caudal anesthesia produces sympathetic blockade that may increase venous capacitance and alter venous return, potentially influencing intravascular volume distribution and preload. This study compared inferior vena cava (IVC) diameters and IVC distensibility (IVCDI) in children receiving general anesthesia alone versus combined general and caudal anesthesia. Methods: In this prospective observational study, 100 children aged 1–8 years scheduled for lower abdominal or urological surgery were enrolled. Patients were allocated based on parental consent: general anesthesia with caudal anesthesia (Group I, n=50) or general anesthesia alone (Group II, n=50). Induction was with sevoflurane in patients without intravenous access and propofol in those with access, followed by laryngeal mask airway placement and controlled mechanical ventilation. In Group I, caudal anesthesia was administered with 0.2% bupivacaine (0.8 mL/kg). IVC maximum (IVC max) and minimum (IVC min) diameters were measured, and IVCDI calculated using M-mode ultrasonography via a subxiphoid approach immediately after induction (T 0 ) and 20 minutes later (T 1 ). Results: Group I showed significant increases in IVC max and IVC min at T 1 , with a non-significant trend toward increased IVCDI, without adverse hemodynamic effects. No significant changes were observed in Group II. Heart rate remained stable and comparable between groups. Conclusion: In this study, caudal anesthesia combined with general anesthesia, at the doses used in our protocol, increased IVC diameters without significant changes in IVCDI or heart rate in mechanically ventilated children. These findings indicate increased venous capacitance without impaired preload responsiveness, supporting caudal anesthesia as a hemodynamically stable adjunct to general anesthesia in pediatric patients.

title: Pain and Anxiety During Intravascular Lithotripsy-Assisted Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Compared with Conventional PCI: A Prospective Single-Center Observational Study
authorString: Cetiner MA, Gjapi A, Özderya A, Vorpahl M, Seyfarth M, Turan RG.
abstractText:
Background: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is an effective treatment for severely calcified coronary lesions during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). However, data regarding patient-reported pain and anxiety during IVL are limited.

Objective:

To compare pain and anxiety levels in patients undergoing IVL-assisted PCI with those undergoing conventional PCI. Methods In this prospective single-center observational study, 100 patients with chronic coronary syndrome undergoing PCI between 2024 and 2025 were enrolled. Fifty patients underwent IVL-assisted PCI and 50 underwent conventional PCI. Pain was assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) and Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale, while anxiety was assessed using the Subjective Units of Distress Scale (SUDS). Results Baseline demographic characteristics were similar between groups. The IVL group had more complex coronary artery disease, including a higher prevalence of three-vessel disease (70% vs. 38%, p  = 0.001), more previous coronary angiographies ( p  = 0.007), and higher radiation exposure ( p  = 0.018). Despite greater lesion complexity, no significant differences were observed in pain or anxiety scores between groups. The number of IVL pulses was not associated with pain or anxiety. Conclusions IVL-assisted PCI was not associated with increased pain or anxiety compared with conventional PCI despite greater procedural complexity. These findings support IVL as a well-tolerated strategy for the treatment of severely calcified coronary lesions.

title: Effects of Perioperative Beta-Blockers on Postoperative Major Adverse Cardiovascular and Cerebrovascular Events in Patients with Colorectal Cancer : a propensity score matching analysis
authorString: Li X, Guo Q, Lin H, Yan T, Huang Y, Li F.
abstractText: Background Patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) undergoing surgical resection face a high risk of perioperative adverse events, and the relationship between perioperative use of beta-blockers and major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) after surgery remains unelucidated. Methods Consecutive patients newly received radical surgery for CRC between 1 September 2019 and 30 September 2021 were identified through the research database and electronic medical records of the Union Hospital of Fujian Medical University. Patients were categorized into two groups based on the use of perioperative beta-blockers, and a 1:2 propensity-score matching (PSM) analysis was conducted to balance confounding factors. The primary outcome was the incidence of MACCE within 30 days postoperatively. Results A total of 1859 patients with complete medical records were included in the study. Among these, 80 patients developed MACCE, resulting in an overall incidence rate of 4.3%. Prior to PSM, the MACCE incidence was significantly higher in the beta-blockers group compared to the non-beta-blockers group (12.7% vs. 3.8%, OR 3.72, 95% CI 2.02 to 6.86, P < 0.001). After 1:2 PSM, MACCE incidence which 108 patients in the beta-blockers group and 216 patients in the non-beta-blockers group were included, remained higher in the beta-blockers group (13.0% vs. 4.6%, OR 3.07,95% CI 1.32 to 7.16, P = 0.007). There was no significant difference in total morbidity between the groups (38.9% vs.44.4%, OR 1.26, 95% CI 0.79 to 2.01, P = 0.34). Sensitivity analyses further supported these findings. Conclusions Perioperative use of beta-blockers in patients with CRC is independently associated with an increased risk of postoperative MACCE; however, this association may not be purely causal but rather reflects the generally poorer overall health status and higher invasiveness of surgery in the group of patients receiving these medications.

title: Characterization and classification of clinical outcomes among ambulatory gynecologic surgery recipients at Kyabirwa Surgical Center, Budondo Sub-County, Jinja City: A Retrospective Chart Review
authorString: Oleo C, Masembe J, Nanyiri J, Azirembuzi J, Wandira EG, Dillon J, Emoru A, Damoi JO, Nuwahereza A, Zhang L, Kalumuna AT, Marin M.
abstractText: Background The global burden of gynecological diseases is increasing, along with challenges in accessing necessary prophylactic and curative surgery due to high costs, especially in sub-Saharan Africa. Ambulatory gynecologic surgery offers a potential solution however; its adoption depends on evidence of a low rate of adverse outcomes. Objective To characterize and classify the clinical outcomes of ambulatory gynecological surgery at Kyabirwa Surgical Center, Budondo Sub-county, Jinja City, Uganda. Method A retrospective chart review of 112 women who underwent major ambulatory gynecologic surgery between April 2023 and October 2025 was conducted. A census was conducted and medical record abstraction was used to collect data, which were analyzed using descriptive statistics, principal component analysis, cluster analysis, and the Kruskal-Wallis test for variance analysis. Result The prevalence of adverse clinical outcomes was 2.7%. Nine principal outcomes were identified among women who underwent major ambulatory gynecological surgery, including cardiac arrest, nausea, vomiting on postoperative days 4 to 7, febrile morbidity, vaginal discharge, superficial thrombophlebitis, intestinal injury, incisional hernias, peripheral nerve injuries, and superficial surgical site infections (grade 1). In the cluster analysis, class 2 superficial SSIs were the most prevalent (16.2%), whereas the prevalence of all other outcomes was less than 1%. The Kruskal-Wallis test showed no statistically significant differences (p > 0.05) in the incidence of surgical site infections or adverse outcomes between or within groups of women based on their intrapersonal and clinical characteristics. Conclusion Only three of 112 patients undergoing major ambulatory gynecologic surgery experienced adverse outcomes, which was significantly lower than the reported global rate at non-ambulatory facilities, ranging from 3.7 to 10.8%, a testament to the safety of this mode of care. Surgical site infections, all superficial (grade 1), were the primary postoperative outcomes of ambulatory gynecology surgery. They were classified as Clavien-Dindo class 2 and managed with oral antibiotics and analgesics, making them negligibly threatening. The incidence of surgical site infections did not differ significantly by any clinical or personal patient characteristics, suggesting that over three years of surgery, patients did not have an intraoperative, clinical, or personal trait that increased the risk of developing infections.

title: A disproportionality analysis of dual bronchodilators based on the FAERS
authorString: Peng Y, Cui W, Xia T, An J, Xiang J, Zhong Y.
abstractText: Objective To detect adverse event (AE) signals for dual bronchodilators using the Food and Drug Administration(FDA) Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS), assess their potential safety risks, and inform pharmacovigilance. Methods AE reports pertaining to dual bronchodilators were retrieved from the FAERS for the period covering the fourth quarter of 2013 through the fourth quarter of 2025. Signal detection was subsequently conducted using both the Reporting Odds Ratio (ROR) and the Multi‑Item Gamma Poisson Shrinker (MGPS) method. Results From the FAERS database, the numbers of AE reports with umeclidinium/vilanterol, indacaterol/glycopyrronium, tiotropium/olodaterol, glycopyrronium/formoterol, and aclidinium/formoterol as primary suspected drugs were 1,674, 674, 572, 102, and 52, respectively; the corresponding numbers of detected AE signals were 140, 111, 64, 30, and 10; and the numbers of involved system organ classes (SOCs) were 19, 16, 15, 12, and 7, respectively. Conclusion The AEs of dual bronchodilators were predominantly observed in the SOCs of respiratory, thoracic and mediastinal disorders, cardiac disorders, and infections and infestations, etc. The distribution of AE signals and serious adverse events(SAEs) varied across the five drugs. Accordingly, individualized drug selection is advised in clinical practice, with special attention to early risk monitoring in elderly patients and those with compromised baseline cardiopulmonary function.

title: Dissociating Early Heartbeat-Evoked Afferent Gating From Late Associative Failure in Post-Anoxic Coma
authorString: Machado¹ C, Sánchez² JJ, Schiff³ A, Sániová⁴ BD, Drobný⁴ M, Mualem⁵ R.
abstractText: Objective Following cardiac arrest and cardiopulmonary resuscitation, standard clinical EEG often fails to differentiate reversible metabolic depression from structural cortical necrosis. We evaluated whether the Heartbeat-Evoked Response (HER) can dissociate viable subcortical-cortical primary interoceptive afferent gating from non-viable distributed cortico-cortical networks in acute post-anoxic coma. Methods Continuous 19-channel EEG and synchronized Lead-II ECG recordings were analyzed across a harmonized multicenter cohort of 150 comatose post-cardiac arrest patients (discovery cohort: n = 100; independent validation cohort: n = 50; 58 Good Outcome [CPC 1–2] and 92 Poor Outcome [CPC 3–5]). Standardized Low-Resolution Electromagnetic Tomography (sLORETA) and non-linear Hilbert–Huang Transform (HHT) with Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) were applied to evaluate early (150–300 ms) versus late (350–500 ms) post-R-peak windows. Results Favorable recovery was associated with a preserved frontocentral negative deflection peaking at ~ 200 ms (-1.18 µV at electrode Fz), localized via sLORETA strictly to the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC; BA 24/32) and anterior insula. EMD isolated this early component into intermediate intrinsic modes (IMF 2–3; 8–16 Hz), yielding a sharp surge in instantaneous Hilbert energy (Et = 1.85 a.u.) and robust phase alignment (IPLV = 0.95). Non-survivors showed an anomalous positive shift (+ 1.45 µV), energy collapse (Et < 0.40 a.u.), and phase desynchronization (IPLV ≈ 0.18). In the late window (350–500 ms), both groups exhibited diffuse spatial dissipation and loss of discrete cortical generators. Conclusion Preserved early primary interoceptive afferent gating to the ACC/insula—rather than late associative network reverberation—serves as an objective electrophysiological biomarker of viable cortical microcircuitry in post-anoxic coma.

title: Left Ventricular Air Embolism and Cardiac Arrest following Percutaneous Needle Biopsy of a Pulmonary Nodule: A Case Report
authorString: Massion SP, Beagle AJ, Frank JA.
abstractText: Background Left ventricular air embolism is a rare yet potentially fatal complication of percutaneous lung needle biopsies. They can precipitate cardiac arrest when air enters the pulmonary veins and obstructs forward blood flow through the left ventricle. We report a case in which intraprocedural imaging enabled recognition of left-sided intracardiac air during cardiac arrest and highlight management strategies that contributed to successful resuscitation. Case Presentation: A 78-year-old man underwent an elective computed tomographic (CT)-guided biopsy of a left upper lobe lung nodule. After core biopsy was obtained, he complained of sudden-onset chest pain followed by unresponsiveness and loss of palpable pulses. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation was initiated following Advanced Cardiac Life Support guidelines. Intraprocedural CT imaging revealed an air embolism within the left ventricular apex without involvement of the right heart or pulmonary circulation. The patient was placed in a modified right lateral decubitus and Trendelenburg position utilizing hospital bed wedges and an automatic mechanical chest compression device. The trachea was intubated, and he was ventilated with 100% FiO2. Hyperbaric oxygen facilities were unavailable. He was resuscitated with interval resolution of intracardiac air and discharged three weeks later. Conclusion Physicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for left ventricular air embolism as a potential cause of cardiac arrest after percutaneous lung biopsy. Prompt recognition, supplemental oxygen therapy, and standard resuscitation measures remain the mainstay of treatment for hemodynamic collapse due to air embolism. Future study is needed to define optimal positional management based on the site of air embolism; venous versus arterial, or right versus left heart chambers.

title: Comprehensive review of the genotype-phenotype spectrum and treatment for biallelic insulin receptoropathy based on 259 affected people
authorString: D'Silva S, Donadille B, Xu J, Bellanné-Chantelot C, Aslanzadeh V, Collin-Chavagnac D, Jubeh JA, Amin R, Beltrand J, Beressi J, Beziaud F, Bismuth E, Bolli G, Carel J, Chandler K, Cochran E, de Kerdanet M, Deodati A, Grasso V, Greeley S, Gueorguieva I, Guran T, Kanthimathi S, Lebreton L, Martino M, Mohan V, Moreau B, Ng SM, Nicolino M, Niedziela M, Perge K, Polak M, Venkatesan R, Reynaud R, Startzell M, Topaloglu AK, Desojo AV, Villanueva C, Williams R, Witsch M, Hussain K, Stears A, Savage D, Dattani M, Marcovecchio L, O'Rahilly S, Vatier C, Jéru I, Colclough K, Barbetti F, Vigouroux C, Brown R, Semple R.
abstractText: Background Biallelic deleterious variants in the insulin receptor gene ( INSR ) cause severe insulin resistance (IR), historically partitioned into Donohue syndrome, Rabson–Mendenhall syndrome and type A IR. Case literature is scattered, and clinical management rests on uncontrolled case series. Genotype–phenotype relationships, natural history, prognosis and optimal management are only partially established. Methods We reviewed reports of biallelic INSR variants published over 40 years and supplemented these with cases from international referral centres, abstracting clinical, biochemical and genetic data from 259 affected individuals (226 unrelated probands; 210 distinct INSR variants). Variant burden was compared with the general population using gnomAD, and a Random Survival Forest-based prognostic model was developed, with cross-validation of feature importance. Results Complete loss-of-function (KO) variants affected 33.3% of patients vs 12.6% in gnomAD (p = 2.5×10⁻¹²), with no domain clustering. All biallelic KO patients presented in the first month of life. Disease was multi-system, encompassing profound IR with fasting hypoglycaemia, hyperglycaemia without dyslipidaemia, pre-/postnatal growth failure with soft-tissue overgrowth, cholestatic liver disease, nephrocalcinosis, cardiac hypertrophy, ovarian enlargement, coagulopathy and colonic overgrowth. Seventy-two individuals (28%) died at a median 0.36 years, most commonly from sepsis; all KO patients were deceased or censored by 36 months. The prognostic model discriminated survival beyond 2 years, stratifying the cohort into tertiles with 2-year survivals of 89.8%, 83.3% and 39.5%. Biallelic KO variants and low birthweight standard deviation score were the strongest negative predictors, with male sex also adverse. Evidence guiding therapy is weak: insulin and metformin remain pragmatic mainstays, SGLT2 inhibitors show encouraging benefit, and rhIGF-1, used in a third of cases, yielded mixed outcomes. Conclusions Biallelic insulin receptoropathy forms a clinical continuum. Routinely available presentation features permit data-driven prognostication, facilitating individualised risk assessment. Several stereotyped tissue-specific features remain poorly understood mechanistically. Strengthening of the therapeutic evidence base is urgently required.

title: Association Between MIA3 and Coronary Collateral Circulation Formation in Patients with Chronic Total Occlusion
authorString: Zhao F, Wu Y, Liu F, Yang Y, Li X, Luo J.
abstractText:
Objective: To investigate the correlation between melanoma inhibitory activity 3 (MIA3) and coronary collateral circulation (CCC) formation in patients with coronary chronic total occlusion (CTO).

Methods:

A total of 489 patients with CTO admitted to the First Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University from January 2021 to July 2022 were enrolled as study subjects. According to the Rentrop classification system, patients were divided into a poor CCC group and a good CCC group. Baseline clinical data were collected, and plasma levels of MIA3 and vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA) were quantitatively measured. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was used to identify independent factors correlated with good CCC formation. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were plotted to evaluate the clinical value of predicting good CCC formation. The net reclassification index (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) were calculated to assess the incremental predictive performance of MIA3 when added to traditional risk models. Clinical subgroup and interaction analyses were also performed.

Results:

Compared with the poor CCC group, patients in the good CCC group showed significantly higher plasma MIA3 levels (1280.87 pg/ml vs.1041.30 pg/ml, P < 0.001), with Rentrop grade 0 patients exhibiting the lowest MIA3 levels. Systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, body mass index (BMI), fasting plasma glucose, and hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) levels were significantly lower in the good CCC group than in the poor group, and the proportions of patients with hypertension and diabetes mellitus were also lower. After adjusting for confounding factors using multivariate logistic regression, a high level of MIA3 (>1462.24pg/ml) was identified as an independent related factor for good CCC formation (OR= 3.152, P < 0.001). ROC curve analysis showed that the area under the curve (AUC) of plasma MIA3 in predicting good CCC was 0.630 (P < 0.001). NRI and IDI analyses demonstrated that adding MIA3 to traditional risk factors significantly improved the predictive efficiency of the model for CCC formation (both P < 0.05). Subgroup analysis revealed a significant interaction between MIA3 and dyslipidemia; among patients with dyslipidemia, higher MIA3 levels were associated with better CCC formation.

Conclusion:

MIA3 is an independent protective factor for good CCC formation in patients with CTO. Higher MIA3 levels are correlated with better collateral development, and this association is particularly prominent in patients with dyslipidemia. Incorporating MIA3 into traditional clinical models significantly enhances the predictive performance for good CCC formation in CTO patients.

title: Acute hyperglycaemia is associated with a left ventricular mechanical phenotype resembling acute myocardial ischemia: a comparative speckle- tracking echocardiography study
authorString: Krljanac G, Ašanin M, Bogdanović J, Savić L, Lukač SS, Stanković S, Rasulić I, Popović L, Polovina M, Petakov A, Lukić D, Avramović J, Jotić A, Lalić NM, Lalić K.
abstractText: This study was aimed to compare LV structural, functional, and mechanical characteristics of acute hyperglycaemia (≥ 11.1 mmol/L) in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM) without cardiovascular diseases (CVD) (group A, n = 52) and of acute myocardial ischemia (AMI) in patients without DM (group D, n = 55) using two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography (2D-STE). Comparison groups included patients with well-controlled DM without complications (Group B, n = 20) and healthy controls (Group C, n = 20). We found that LV global longitudinal strain (GLS), as well as global circumferential strain (GCS) was comparably reduced in both groups A (-18.47+/-1.50% and − 19.86 ± 2.80%) and D (-17,21+/-3,35% and − 18.79 ± 3.40%) being significantly lower in comparison to groups B and C. Longitudinal mechanical dispersion index (LMDI) was highest in Group D and was significantly increased compared with Group A while circumferential MDI was equally increased in both groups A and D in comparison to control groups. Similar deterioration in peak apical rotation, LV twist and torsion were observed in both groups A and D. Simultaneously, AMI was associated with more pronounced LV remodelling in comparison to other three groups. In conclusion, acute hyperglycaemia alone induces LV mechanical dysfunction resembling AMI, affecting myocardial deformation and rotational mechanics despite the absence of overt CVD.

title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Cardiorenal Outcomes in Non-Obese, Non- Diabetic MASLD: A Propensity Score-Matched Study
authorString: Nguyen AT, Hamad YH, Prateek R, Imam D, Gopalakrishna H, Luthra G.
abstractText: Purpose Non-obese individuals account for up to 30% of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) cases yet are routinely excluded from glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) outcome trials. Because MASLD is increasingly recognized as the hepatic component of a systemic cardiometabolic disorder, we evaluated the association between sustained GLP-1 RA use and cardiovascular, renal and hepatic outcomes in non-obese, non-diabetic adults with MASLD. Methods Using the TriNetX federated health research network, we identified non-obese (body mass index ≤ 27 kg/m²), non-diabetic adults with MASLD and at least one cardiometabolic risk factor. Sustained GLP-1 RA users, defined by a second prescription within three months of an initial prescription started within three months of diagnosis, were matched 1:1 to non-users on 38 demographic, comorbidity, medication and laboratory covariates. Cox models estimated five-year hazard ratios (HR) for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), heart failure, major liver outcomes (MALO), acute kidney injury (AKI), and atrial fibrillation/flutter (Afib). Sensitivity analyses excluded baseline metformin, substance use, and tirzepatide. Results Among 1,261 matched pairs, sustained GLP-1 RA use was associated with lower rates of MACE (HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.33–0.87), heart failure (0.34, 0.19–0.59), AKI (0.46, 0.26–0.81) and Afib (0.64, 0.42–0.97). MALO did not differ (1.16, 0.59–2.28). Associations persisted after excluding baseline metformin use and were directionally consistent after excluding tirzepatide. Conclusion In non-obese, non-diabetic MASLD, sustained GLP-1 RA use was associated with lower cardiovascular and renal event rates but not with hepatic events. These findings support prospective evaluation of GLP-1 RA therapy in this understudied phenotype.

title: Clinical Characteristics and Genetic Analysis of MYH7-Related Pediatric Cardiomyopathy—A Multicenter Cohort Study
authorString: Yang Y, Gu Y, Wang Z, Lyu Z, Zhen Z, Li Z, Tian J, Ding W, Jiang X, Wang J, Zhang Y, Peng H, Sun L, Fu L, Yang S, Han L, Xiao Y.
abstractText: Objective The clinical phenotypes of MYH7-related pediatric cardiomyopathy are diverse.This study aims to analyze the clinical characteristics, prognosis, and domain-associated genetic characteristics of MYH7-related pediatric cardiomyopathy. Methods This was a multicenter retrospective cohort study. Children with MYH7 gene mutations who first or revisited ten domestic tertiary pediatric cardiovascular hospitals from January 2020 to December 2025 were enrolled. Based on the initial echocardiogram, the patients were divided into three groups: dilation phenotype group, hypertrophy phenotype group, noncompaction cardiomyopathy(NCM) phenotype group. General clinical data, laboratory test, echocardiogram and genetic results were collected from the medical record system. All children were followed up until December 2025, and follow-up echocardiogram results and occurrence of endpoint events were recorded. Log-rank test was used to assess differences in follow-up outcomes among groups. Spearman correlation analysis was used to examine the relationship between clinical phenotype and functional domain, and multiple logistic regression analysis was used to analyze the association between clinical phenotype and genetic functional domain. Results A total of 75 children with MYH7 gene mutations were enrolled, including four families. The median age at first diagnosis was 20.0 (3.0, 80.0) months, with 47 males (62.7%). Based on echocardiogram, there were 34 cases (45.3%) in dilation phenotype group, 16 (21.3%) in hypertrophy phenotype group, and 25 (33.3%) in NCM phenotype group. Significant differences were found among the three groups in age, creatinine, and BNP levels (p < 0.05). A total of 51 mutation sites were identified in the 75 patients, of which 50 were point mutations and one was a deletion mutation (c.2563_2565delGAG). Among the 51 point mutations, nine sites were recurrent. The most frequent recurrent mutation was c.2710C > T (6 cases), followed by c.602T > C, c.1357C > T, c.1106G > A, c.2711G > A, c.2513C > T, c.4498C > T, c.5401G > A, and c.848A > T. Sanger validation was performed in 72 cases. Among them, 21 cases (28.0%) had maternal inherited variants, 19 cases (25.3%) had paternal inherited variants, and 32 cases (42.6%) had de novo variants. Mutation sites in the three phenotype groups were distributed throughout the entire length of the MYH7 gene without significant enrichment in any region. Although mutations in the head region (S1) were more frequent than in the neck region (S2) or tail region (S3), there was no statistically significant difference among the groups (p = 0.369). Spearman correlation analysis showed no correlation between genetic functional domain and clinical phenotype, but a correlation was observed between functional domain and prognosis (p = 0.034, r=-0.281), indicating that mutations in the head region were associated with worse prognosis. Conclusions Children with MYH7 gene mutations exhibit diverse clinical phenotypes with no significant enrichment of mutation sites. In this cohort, no correlation was found between functional domain and clinical phenotype, but mutations located in the head region were associated with poorer prognosis. Molecular-level genetic profiling can offer crucial clues for clinical outcome prediction.

title: De-escalation of Treatment of HER2 Positive Breast Cancer after Pathological Complete Response to Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy; a Retrospective Analysis
authorString: Khaled E, Shams S, A.M.Abdelhafeez A, Lashin S.
abstractText: Background The teatement of choice for the neo-adjuvant treatment of HER2-positive early breast cancer includes trastuzumab–pertuzumab (TP) with chemotherapy. For those achieving pathological complete response (pCR), the optimal adjuvant strategy remains less clearly defined. Method We retrospectively included patients with HER2-positive early or locally advanced breast cancer who achieved pCR after neo-adjuvant TP-based chemotherapy between January 2021 and December 2023. Disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and cardiac dysfunction were assessed. Results A total of 356 patients were included: 86 (24.2%) received adjuvant trastuzumab and 270 (75.8%) received adjuvant trastuzumab–pertuzumab. After a median follow-up of 24.8 months, the estimated 3-year DFS for the overall cohort was 89.8%. DFS did not significantly differ between the trastuzumab arm (87.7%) and the dual blockade arm (90.5%) (log-rank p = 0.2213).In subgroup analyses, clinical N3 disease and younger patients less than 40 years derived a significant benefit from dual blockad.No other significant differences in DFS were detected across subgroups defined by clinical T stage, hormone receptor status, HER2 IHC score, tumor grade, or Ki-67 index.Cardiac safety was consistent with previous reports, with no significant difference in dysfunction between trastuzumab (23.8%) and trastuzumab–pertuzumab (18.1%) (p = 0.922). Conclusions Among patients who achieved pCR following neo-adjuvant TP-based chemotherapy, de-escalation to adjuvant trastuzumab monotherapy appears to be a safe strategy that does not compromise DFS in most cases.

title: Comprehensive echocardiographic assessment of the left atrium in daily practice: a practical guide.
authorString: Anwar AM, Ali MAM.
abstractText: The left atrium (LA) is a crucial component of cardiovascular performance. A thorough understanding of LA anatomy, physiology, and pathology is necessary for diagnostic and prognostic purposes in daily clinical practice. LA volume is widely recognized as a novel biomarker for cardiovascular risks in the general population. Furthermore, it has been shown to be a significant prognostic factor in various cardiac conditions, such as atrial fibrillation, ischemic heart disease, valvular heart disease, and heart failure. The assessment of LA function in physiologic and pathologic states has gathered interest with expanding research supporting its utility as a biomarker for outcomes in different cardiovascular abnormalities. Utilizing basic and advanced echocardiographic modalities and integrating multiple parameters helps in both qualitative and quantitative assessment of LA size and function. This is a narrative review provides a comprehensive approach to assessing LA size and function by interpreting existing English-language literature, including landmark studies, reviews and consensus documents from leading echocardiography societies. The literature search focused on key terms, such as LA size, phasic function, strain, and Doppler hemodynamics. By collecting, analyzing, and grouping the echocardiographic parameters, we introduce a simplified approach to guide clinicians through a comprehensive LA assessment ranging from standard 2D dimensions to advanced deformational tracking tailored to specific clinical indications.

title: [Electrocardiographic signs of coronary occlusion not meeting STEMI criteria].
authorString: Tomcsányi J, Tomcsányi K, Csákányi M, Arabadzisz H, Kántor Z, Jávor K, Kollár L, Marosi A, Papp E, Frész T.
abstractText: The authors describe the electrocardiographic signs of coronary occlusion that do not fall within the STEMI category. Since immediate coronary angiography is required for these patients as well, the ECG signs being presented have great clinical significance. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(44): 1759-1763.

title: Chronic disease burden and health-related quality of life among missouri adults.
authorString: Lima Dos Santos SP, Schmaltz CL, Jackson-Thompson J, Simões EJ.

journal.title: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation

abstractText: This cross-sectional study examined associations between chronic disease burden, specific chronic conditions, and Short Form 36 (SF-36) health-related quality of life (HRQoL) scores among Missouri adults 18 years of age or older. We analyzed survey-weighted data from the 2024 Center for Medical Epidemiology and Population Health Adult Health Survey (N = 547). The primary chronic condition count included cardiovascular disease, chronic respiratory disease, arthritis, diabetes, depressive disorder, non-skin cancer, and kidney disease and was categorized as zero, one, or two or more conditions. Obesity was examined as a condition-specific exposure and in sensitivity analyses. Survey-weighted linear regression models adjusted for age, sex, race/ethnicity, educational attainment, employment status, and rurality. The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure was used to control the false discovery rate across the 10 HRQoL outcomes. Overall, 30.0% of Missouri adults had two or more of the seven selected chronic conditions. Compared with adults with no chronic conditions, adults with two or more conditions had lower scores for nine of the 10 HRQoL outcomes after false discovery rate correction. The largest adjusted differences were observed for Role-Physical (β = -30.65; 95% CI, -46.56 to -14.74), Physical Functioning (β = -28.70; 95% CI, - 38.60 to -18.81), Bodily Pain (β = -28.28; 95% CI, -38.96 to -17.59), Social Functioning (β = -26.18; 95% CI, -35.43 to -16.92), and General Health (β = -24.18; 95% CI, - 30.75 to - 17.62). Physical Component Summary (PCS) was 12.82 points lower (95% CI, -16.98 to -8.66), and Mental Component Summary (MCS) was 6.10 points lower (95% CI, -9.47 to -2.73). Arthritis and cardiovascular disease had the strongest associations with lower PCS, while depressive disorder had the strongest association with lower MCS. In supplementary continuous-count models, each additional condition was associated with a 4.57-point lower PCS score and a 2.20-point lower MCS score. Greater chronic disease burden was associated with poorer physical and mental HRQoL among Missouri adults. Adding HRQoL assessment to chronic disease surveillance and clinical follow-up may help identify functional limitations and mental health needs that are not apparent from diagnoses alone.

title: A Structured Approach to Teaching Volumetric Fetal Echocardiography Using Fetal Intelligent Navigation Echocardiography (FINE).
authorString: Giubilato AF, Bravo-Valenzuela NJ, Albrecht MEM, Malho AS, Araujo Júnior E.
abstractText: Fetal volumetric echocardiography using Fetal Intelligent Navigation Echocardiography (FINE) enables automated reconstruction of standardized echocardiographic views from a cardiac volume dataset. However, automation of navigation does not eliminate dependence on technically adequate acquisition or the need for operator quality control. We describe the PROBE Educational Workflow, a structured educational approach comprising five sequential steps-Position, Refine, Obtain, Build and Evaluate-designed to organize the teaching of the process from preparation of the two-dimensional image and acquisition of the Spatio-Temporal Image Correlation (STIC) volume to construction of the navigation and systematic assessment of the reconstructed views. PROBE was conceived as an iterative workflow: when the quality of a step is considered insufficient, the operator should identify the probable origin of the problem and return to the corresponding step before proceeding. The workflow does not modify the FINE algorithm and does not constitute a diagnostic protocol; its purpose is to provide a simple and reproducible cognitive framework for technical training in volumetric fetal echocardiography. Future studies should assess its impact on competency acquisition, volume quality, reproducibility and training efficiency.

title: Neurophysiological and Behavioural Effects of Combined Cannabis Concentrates and Alcohol Among People Who Regularly Use Alcohol and Cannabis.
authorString: Hetelekides EM, Davies PL, Prince MA, Gavin WJ, Karoly HC.
abstractText: Increasingly potent concentrated cannabis products containing high levels of Δ<sup>9</sup>-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) are being consumed with alcohol. This combination is known to acutely impair cognitive and psychomotor abilities, although few studies have evaluated alcohol and cannabis co-use using neural measures. This naturalistic feasibility study explored the acute effects of co-intoxication on behavioural performance and brain activity, measured via electroencephalography (EEG), during a performance monitoring task administered three times over a 4.5-h period. Participants (N = 17, 65% male) were heavy drinking community members (age M = 31.7 years; SD = 10.27) who regularly use cannabis. EEG was recorded while participants completed a speeded visual-flanker task at baseline (sober) before consuming a standardized dose of alcohol and a cannabis concentrate product, followed by EEG recordings 1-h (intoxicated) and 4-h post co-consumption (recovery). Recordings were processed to obtain six event-related potential components: the stimulus-locked N1, P2, N2 and P3 and response-locked error-related negativity (ERN) and error positivity (Pe). Repeated measures ANOVAs revealed that behavioural measures at the intoxicated timepoint showed an increase in errors (p < 0.005; η<sup>2</sup> <sub>p</sub> = 0.35) and significant decrease in response time (RT) (p < 0.001; η<sup>2</sup> <sub>p</sub> = 0.50) compared to sober and recovery periods. Measures of brain activity also demonstrated significant change across time with largest amplitudes when sober, smaller amplitudes when intoxicated, then an increase in amplitude to near sober levels at recovery for stimulus-locked (P2, N2 and P3) and response-locked components (ERN and Pe). Thus, compared to sober and recovery periods, the behaviour at the intoxicated timepoint revealed significantly greater impulsivity (RT) leading to significantly higher error rates, while measures of cognitive processing (i.e., decision-making, error detection, performance monitoring/adaptation) showed significantly diminished levels of brain activity. Performance and neurophysiology measures remained diminished at recovery compared to baseline. Understanding neurocognitive functioning during co-intoxication may provide insights into specific cognitive processes that may impact function in everyday activities such as driving. Trial Registration: NCT06259916.

title: Airway Fire During Left Pneumonectomy: A Case Report
authorString: Zhang Y, Meng T, Gao J.
abstractText: Background. Intraoperative airway fire is extremely rare yet potentially fatal, and an oxygen-filled tracheal tube is a major risk factor. Fire during pneumonectomy—in which the airway is simultaneously the operative field, the sole ventilatory route, and the conduit for combustion—is uniquely hazardous. We describe such a case and analyze its mechanism, management, and prevention. Case presentation. A 70-year-old man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and a long history of smoking underwent thoracoscopic resection of a centrally located left-lower-lobe squamous cell carcinoma. During left pneumonectomy, while the left main bronchus was being divided with monopolar electrosurgery, sudden flame and smoke indicated combustion of the double-lumen tube, which was judged nonventilatable and urgently changed to a single-lumen tube. Before chest closure, bronchoscopy showed red, edematous mucosa with diffuse black carbonized deposits over the carina and both main bronchi; four intraoperative lavage passes were performed, and three further passes were carried out intermittently while the patient remained intubated in the intensive care unit. He was extubated on the first postoperative day, developed transient atrial fibrillation on the second, and was discharged on the seventh. Histopathology confirmed keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma (pT4N2M0, stage IIIB). Conclusions. Recognition of the fuel–oxidizer–ignition triad, and preventive measures adopted before and during bronchial division, are essential. Once a fire occurs, immediate cessation of oxygen, rapid re-establishment of a ventilatable airway, aggressive bronchoscopic saline lavage, glucocorticoid pulse therapy, and supportive postoperative care together supported a favorable outcome; at follow-up the patient had completed five cycles of chemotherapy, with intermittent cough and sputum production and hoarseness attributed to unilateral vocal cord paralysis, but remained able to carry out the activities of daily living without clinically significant laryngotracheal stenosis.

title: Association of the Systemic Inflammation Response Index With Atrial Fibrillation Recurrence After Catheter Ablation
authorString: Farooq S, Mpofu TL, SHAHNAWAZ S, Du M, Hu X, Li F, Ge L, Zhang C, Zhang Z, Yang Y, Chen W.
abstractText: Background Systemic inflammation contributes to atrial remodeling and may influence atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence after catheter ablation. The systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), calculated as neutrophil count × monocyte count / lymphocyte count, integrates inflammatory activity and immune status. We investigated the association between baseline SIRI and AF recurrence after catheter ablation. Methods This retrospective cohort included 504 adults with paroxysmal or persistent AF who underwent catheter ablation between July 2023 and December 2024. The primary outcome was atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence lasting at least 30 seconds after a 3-month blanking period during 12-month follow-up. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, receiver operating characteristic analysis, DeLong testing, integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), and category-free net reclassification improvement (NRI) were performed. Results AF recurrence occurred in 140 patients (27.8%). Each 1-standard deviation increase in SIRI was associated with recurrence in univariable analysis (odds ratio [OR], 1.35; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.10–1.65; P = 0.003) and remained independently associated after adjustment for relevant variables (adjusted OR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.00–1.54; P = 0.045). Restricted cubic spline analysis suggested a nonlinear association. Adding SIRI to the base clinical model increased the area under the curve from 0.704 to 0.713 without a significant DeLong difference, although IDI and NRI improved. Adding SIRI and C-reactive protein increased the area under the curve to 0.732 and significantly improved DeLong, IDI, and NRI results. Conclusions Higher baseline SIRI was independently associated with AF recurrence after catheter ablation. Its incremental value alone was modest, whereas combining SIRI with C-reactive protein provided greater improvement.

title: Anterior Scleritis in the Setting of Multiple Autoimmune Disorders: A Rare Case Report and Literature Review
authorString: Shih C, Lin I, Tsai T.
abstractText:
Background: Scleritis is an uncommon inflammatory ocular disorder with heterogeneous etiologies. Although scleritis has occasionally been reported in association with Sjögren's syndrome and antiphospholipid syndrome, its occurrence in patients with multiple concomitant autoimmune diseases is exceedingly uncommon. This is also the first case suggesting a possible association between polymyositis and anterior scleritis. This case may serve as a useful reference for clinicians in managing similar conditions with multiple concomitant autoimmune diseases. Case presentation: A 65-year-old woman with long-standing polymyositis, Sjögren’s syndrome, and antiphospholipid syndrome developed severe left ocular pain following treatment for suspected polymyositis-related pulmonary hypertension with prednisolone and mycophenolate mofetil. Ophthalmic examination revealed mild ptosis, eyelid swelling, diffuse bulbar conjunctival injection with prominent corkscrew vessels, and superficial keratopathy in the left eye. A diagnosis of anterior scleritis was made. Initial treatment with topical fluorometholone and supportive therapy resulted in resolution of ocular pain and improvement of inflammation within one week. However, recurrence with superimposed conjunctivitis occurred one week later. Oral diclofenac, topical levofloxacin, frequent preservative-free artificial tears, and carbomer gel were subsequently administered. The ocular inflammation gradually resolved over three weeks.

Conclusion:

This case highlights a rare occurrence of anterior scleritis in the setting of multiple coexisting autoimmune diseases and suggests a potential association between polymyositis and scleritis that warrants further investigation. Scleritis may develop despite ongoing systemic immunosuppressive therapy, emphasizing the importance of prompt ophthalmic evaluation in patients with autoimmune diseases who develop ocular pain or inflammation.

title: The Perceived Stress Scale-10 as a screening tool for impaired atrial fibrillation-specific quality of life: Identification of an optimal cut-off value and incremental screening value
authorString: Ye H, Li X, Hong J.
abstractText: Background To determine the optimal cutoff of the 10-item Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10) for screening impaired atrial fibrillation (AF)-specific quality of life (QoL), and evaluate its incremental value beyond routine clinical variables. Methods We performed a secondary analysis of a publicly available cross-sectional dataset of 196 community-dwelling adults with AF (Rush et al., PLoS One 2023). Impaired QoL was defined as an AFQoL-16 score at or below the 25th percentile (57.41 points). Associations were assessed by Spearman’s correlation and multivariate logistic regression. ROC analysis identified the optimal cutoff. Incremental value over a base model (age, sex, time since last AF episode, self-rated overall health) was evaluated by DeLong test, net reclassification improvement (NRI), integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results Forty-nine patients (25.0%) had impaired QoL. PSS-10 was inversely correlated with AFQoL score (rs=-0.385, P < 0.001), with each 1-point increase conferring 11.3% higher odds of impaired QoL. The AUC was 0.701 (95%CI 0.617–0.784); the optimal cutoff was ≥ 16 points (sensitivity 57.1%, specificity 78.2%). Adding PSS-10 to the base model increased AUC from 0.769 to 0.827 (NRI 0.490, P = 0.005; IDI 0.062, P = 0.006), with DCA confirming greater net benefit across clinically relevant thresholds. Conclusions PSS-10 is independently associated with AF-specific QoL impairment. A cutoff of 16 points offers acceptable screening performance and significant incremental value beyond routine variables, supporting its use as a simple first-line screening tool, though external validation in independent cohorts is needed.

title: AHNAK2 Polymorphisms rs2582513 and rs10145032 Are Associated with Rivaroxaban Pharmacodynamics and Bleeding Risk: A Two-Stage Multicenter Cohort Study
authorString: Liu Z, Mu G, Tan Y, Wang W, Cao Y, Wei X, Cui Y, Xiang Q.
abstractText: Purpose Existing studies have investigated how genetic variations in drug- metabolizing enzymes and transporters affect rivaroxaban concentrations, but the relationship between these variants and bleeding events is unclear. Moreover, other genes related to pharmacodynamics and bleeding risks need further investigation. Additionally, identifying specific genetic loci in healthy populations and validating their clinical impact are key challenges this study faces. Method A multicenter prospective cohort study was conducted to detect genetic polymorphisms and analyze their pharmacodynamic effects on rivaroxaban in healthy individuals. The study then validated these findings by examining clinical outcomes in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF). Results The findings revealed that specific mutations in the AHNAK nuclear protein 2 (AHNAK2 ) gene, notably rs2582513 and rs10145032 , were correlated with a blunted prolongation of prothrombin time (PT) in healthy individuals undergoing rivaroxaban treatment (p = 0.0003, 0.0004). The ROC curve was employed to assess the predictive capacity of these two single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) for prothrombin time, yielding an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.93. Additionally, these mutations were associated with an elevated risk of bleeding events in clinical patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). When compared to GA/GC and AA carriers, subjects with the GG genotype for AHNAK2 rs2582513/rs10145032 exhibited a statistically significant increase in bleeding events, with a p of 0.03. The ROC curve's AUC for these two SNPs, rs2582513 and rs10145032 , on the AHNAK2 gene in forecasting bleeding events was 0.85. Combined analysis with ABCB1 rs1045642 and CYP3A5 rs776746 improved the AUC for bleeding event prediction to 0.89. Conclusion This study reveals for the first time that mutations in the AHNAK2 gene represent a hypothesis-generating predictive biomarker candidate for anticoagulation therapy. Individuals carrying the GG genotype exhibited weaker PT prolongation after receiving rivaroxaban, yet were associated with higher bleeding risks in clinical patients. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and warrant further validation in independent cohorts and functional studies before clinical application.

title: Prevalence and Factors Associated With Incidental Prostate Cancer After Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia Surgery: A Five-Year Retrospective Study in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
authorString: Tilahun E, Nigusse M, Yeta D, Zereai K, Ashagre C, Zeleke B, Zelalem A, Demissie S.
abstractText: Background Incidental prostate cancer (IPC), defined as cancer unexpectedly identified on histopathology after surgery for presumed benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), has been widely studied internationally, but data from sub-Saharan Africa remain scarce, and none exist from Ethiopia. This study examined the prevalence, predictors, clinicopathological features, and management of IPC among patients undergoing transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) or transvesical prostatectomy (TVP) for presumed BPH. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study included 239 patients who underwent TURP or TVP for presumed BPH at MCM Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, between January 2021 and December 2025. Sociodemographic, clinical, laboratory, and procedural data were abstracted from medical records. Bivariable comparisons used chi-square or Fisher's exact tests and t-tests or Mann–Whitney U tests, as appropriate; univariable and multivariable logistic regression estimated crude and adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Model fit and discrimination were assessed, and sensitivity analyses examined robustness to prostate-specific antigen (PSA) transformation and influential observations Results IPC was identified in 23 of 239 patients (9.6%), with no significant difference by procedure (TURP 11.1% vs. TVP 8.2%, p = 0.445). Patients with IPC had significantly higher rates of hypertension (47.8% vs. 26.4%, p = 0.030), hydronephrosis (39.1% vs. 14.4%, p = 0.006), acute kidney injury (39.1% vs. 8.3%, p < 0.001), and higher PSA and PSA density (both p < 0.001). On multivariable analysis, preoperative PSA (AOR = 1.25 per ng/mL, 95% CI: 1.14–1.38), diabetes mellitus (AOR = 5.28, 95% CI: 1.64–16.95), and hydronephrosis (AOR = 3.92, 95% CI: 1.29–11.94) were independently associated with IPC; age was not (AOR = 1.19 per decade, p = 0.459). The model showed good discrimination (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.838) and calibration (Hosmer–Lemeshow p = 0.162), with findings robust across sensitivity analyses. Among IPC cases, 95.7% had International Society of Urological Pathology (ISUP) Grade Group ≥ 2, yet no patient received active surveillance, radical prostatectomy, radiotherapy, or documented staging investigation; management was uniformly based on androgen deprivation. Conclusions IPC affected nearly 1 in 10 men undergoing BPH surgery, with PSA, diabetes mellitus, and hydronephrosis independently associated with it; PSA density > 0.15 had 90% specificity but only 48% sensitivity. Most cases were clinically significant, yet none received staging or definitive local therapy, highlighting the need for structured incidental-cancer care pathways in similar resource-limited settings.

title: Two decades of presumed Liddle syndrome: biochemical reverse phenotyping reveals apparent mineralocorticoid excess despite a coexisting SCNN1B variant: a case report
authorString: AlHassan HM, Hubail ZAA, AlRashidi A, Elhassan EAM.
abstractText: Background Apparent mineralocorticoid excess (AME) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by deficiency of 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2, in which cortisol activates the mineralocorticoid receptor. AME is clinically and biochemically near-identical to Liddle syndrome, yet the two differ in mechanism and in optimal targeted therapy. The growing use of multigene panels increasingly yields variants of uncertain significance in genes with overlapping phenotypes, creating diagnostic ambiguity that genetic testing alone cannot resolve. We report how targeted biochemical phenotyping adjudicated a genuinely conflicting panel result. Case presentation A woman in her early thirties had been managed since childhood under a presumptive diagnosis of Liddle syndrome, with longstanding hypertension, recurrent symptomatic hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, and renal potassium wasting despite amiloride and potassium supplementation. Multigene panel testing identified a homozygous likely pathogenic HSD11B2 variant (p.Ala237Val) together with a heterozygous SCNN1B variant of uncertain significance (p.Met395Ile) — two findings pointing to the two overlapping disorders. Twenty-four-hour urinary steroid profiling demonstrated a urinary free cortisol-to-cortisone ratio of 20.2 (normal approximately 0.54), providing direct biochemical evidence of impaired 11β-HSD2 activity and establishing AME as the dominant mechanism. The SCNN1B variant lay outside the PY motif where pathogenic Liddle-associated mutations cluster, arguing against Liddle syndrome. Addition of spironolactone to existing therapy was followed by normalization of serum potassium over three months of follow-up, consistent with the biochemical diagnosis. Conclusions This case demonstrates that biochemical reverse phenotyping remains essential for interpreting multigene panels when variants are found in genes with overlapping phenotypes. Urinary steroid profiling distinguished a causative HSD11B2 variant from an incidental SCNN1B variant of uncertain significance, illustrating a diagnostic principle of broad relevance as genomic testing becomes routine in the evaluation of monogenic hypertension.

title: Atherosclerosis and Diabetic Foot Share a Common Molecular Signature of Cellular Senescence: A Multi-Omics and Machine Learning Study
authorString: Zhang F, Wang H, Yang Y, Li C, Weng X, Zhang T, Chen J.
abstractText: Atherosclerosis (AS) and diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) are two major vascular complications of diabetes that frequently co-exist, yet whether they share a common molecular basis remains unclear. Here, we tested the hypothesis that AS and DFU share a common senescence-related molecular signature. We integrated transcriptomic datasets GSE134431 (DFU) and GSE163154 (AS), identified differentially expressed genes common to both diseases, and intersected them with the CellAge senescence-associated gene set to obtain senescence-related DEGs (SR-DEGs). Three machine learning algorithms—LASSO, random forest, and SVM-RFE—were applied to prioritize core feature genes, which were subsequently validated at the single-cell (GSE245703), tissue, and in vitro levels. We identified 72 SR-DEGs shared by AS and DFU, from which three core feature genes—CALCOCO1, CCND2, and FUCA1—were selected by cross-algorithm consensus. A multi-gene nomogram incorporating these genes achieved excellent discriminative performance in both diseases (AUC: 0.96 for DFU, 0.90 for AS). Single-cell analysis revealed cell type–restricted expression patterns of these genes, with fibroblasts emerging as a key senescent cell type in the DFU microenvironment. Clinical validation in an independent cohort of 22 patients (11 DFU vs. 11 non-diabetic foot ulcer) confirmed significant accumulation of senescent cells and dysregulated feature gene expression in DFU tissues. Moreover, metformin treatment effectively attenuated hydrogen peroxide- and high-glucose/high-lipid-induced fibroblast senescence in vitro, partially reversing the expression changes of the three feature genes. These findings demonstrate that AS and DFU share a common senescence-associated molecular signature, identify CALCOCO1, CCND2, and FUCA1 as potential diagnostic and therapeutic targets, and suggest that metformin may exert protective effects through modulation of this senescence-related gene network.

title: Endovascular Closure of Aortic Pseudoaneurysm Following Pulmonary Artery Vegetectomy for Residual Patent Ductus Arteriosus Endarteritis- a case report
authorString: Jhalani I, Gupta A, Meena D, Starlet AR, Rawat SS, Thakur J.
abstractText: Background: Residual patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) following surgical ligation is an uncommon occurrence that may predispose to infective endarteritis at the pulmonary artery end. Surgical vegetectomy may be required when antibiotic therapy fails. The development of an aortic pseudoaneurysm at the isthmus–descending thoracic aorta junction following trans-pulmonary artery vegetectomy and residual PDA closure is an extraordinary complication rarely documented in the literature. Case Presentation: A 2-year-old female underwent surgical ligation of a large PDA via left thoracotomy. Postoperative echocardiography revealed a 1 mm residual shunt. Six months later, she presented with high-grade fever and echocardiography demonstrated a 6 × 8 mm vegetation at the left pulmonary artery end of the residual PDA, which had enlarged to 3 mm. After failure of prolonged intravenous antibiotic therapy, surgical intervention was performed via sternotomy. Due to dense adhesions precluding external re-ligation, vegetectomy and PDA closure were accomplished from within the pulmonary artery using low-flow cardiopulmonary bypass under deep hypothermia. On subsequent follow-up, chest radiography revealed superior mediastinal widening, and CT angiography confirmed a pseudoaneurysm (5.5 × 3.8 × 3.7 cm) with eccentric thrombosis at the aortic isthmus–descending thoracic aorta junction, causing compression of adjacent structures. The pseudoaneurysm was successfully occluded percutaneously using an 8 mm Amplatzer plug via right femoral artery access, with post-deployment angiography confirming complete exclusion of the sac. Conclusion: Even trivial residual PDA shunts carry a lifelong risk of infective endarteritis. Post-discharge surveillance imaging is essential to detect occult complications following complex re-operations in infected fields, and multidisciplinary collaboration is critical to optimizing outcomes.

title: Coronary Intravascular Lithotripsy in the Cardiac Catheterization Laboratory.
