title: Stent Configurations in Aortoiliac Occlusive disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Sivaharan A, Ugwumba L, El-Sayed T, Nandhra S, Configurations In Aortoiliac Occlusive Disease S.

journal.title: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR

abstractText:
Purpose

To evaluate which endovascular stent configuration at the aortic bifurcation offers superior outcomes for aorto-iliac occlusive disease (AIOD).

Methods

Studies reporting outcomes for endovascular reconstruction for AIOD, for TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus (TASC) C and D lesions were included in the review. Data for primary, primary-assisted and secondary patency were extracted (full-text articles or reconstructed from published Kaplan Meier curves).

Results

This review included 12 studies, including 1027 patients (177 Covered Endovascular Reconstruction of the Aortic Bifurcation (CERAB), 850 kissing stent). Most studies were retrospective cohort studies with moderate methodological quality. Median follow-up was 20 months for primary patency, and 48 months for assisted and secondary patency. CERAB and kissing stent techniques showed similar primary patency (p=0.24). Primary-assisted patency was slightly lower for CERAB but not statistically significant (p=0.051). Secondary patency favored CERAB (p=0.045). At two years, CERAB had primary patency of 90%, primary-assisted patency of 87%, and secondary patency of 100%. Kissing stents showed primary patency of 91%, primary-assisted patency of 92%, and secondary patency of 96%.

Conclusion

Both stent types yielded positive results, but current data does not favor one configuration. Current studies on this topic are low quality. At present, the method of endovascular intervention for AIOD could be left to clinical expertise, although hemodynamic studies may provide insights. Randomized trial data or post-market registries are needed to ascertain superiority of any stent configuration in this disease process.

title: Hemodynamic Effects of Reducing LV Afterload With Impella or Intra-Aortic Balloon Counterpulsation During Veno-Arterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Cardiogenic Shock: HERACLES Trial.
authorString: Ezad SM, Panoulas VF, Li Kam Wa ME, Sinha A, Rahman H, Ryan M, Bogerd M, Morgan H, Al-Khayatt B, Poprijan L, Rosenberg A, De Silva K, Meadows C, Sherren P, Ioannou N, Akhtar W, Camporota L, Barrett NA, Perera D.
abstractText: Background: Veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) provides organ support in cardiogenic shock but increases left ventricular (LV) afterload, potentially impairing cardiac recovery. LV unloading with an intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) or micro-axial flow pump (mAFP) may mitigate this effect. HERACLES compared their effects on myocardial oxygen supply and demand. Methods: Patients receiving VA-ECMO for cardiogenic shock were randomized to LV unloading with IABP or mAFP, stratified by ischemic/non-ischemic etiology. Distal coronary, aortic and LV pressures and coronary flow (inverse mean transit time, Tmn) were measured with and without unloading. Myocardial oxygen demand was estimated as the area under the LV pressure curve in systole (TTI) x heart rate (HR). The primary endpoint was the change in myocardial oxygen supply-demand ratio calculated as [(Tmn * TTI*HR)off / (Tmn * TTI *HR)unload]. Secondary endpoints included changes in coronary flow [device flow ratio (DFR) =(Tmn)off/ (Tmn)unload], oxygen demand per beat (DTTI), contractility (DdP/dtmax) and filling pressure (DLVEDP). Results: Twenty-four patients were enrolled (age 51 [46-57]; 46% male; 96% SCAI D/E; 38% ischemic). At randomization, lactate was 4.3 mmol/L [IQR 2.5 to 8.4], LV ejection fraction 10% [10 to 17], LVEDP 18 mmHg [14 to 24]. The myocardial oxygen supply-demand ratio improved with IABP but not mAFP (1.48 [1.23 to 2.10] vs 0.97 [0.92 to 1.39]; P=0.036), driven predominantly by differential reduction of TTI. Coronary pressure increased but flow was unchanged with mAFP (DFR 1.00 [0.86 to 1.13]). Coronary flow increased marginally with IABP (DFR 1.16 [1.00 to 1.51]). LV pressures decreased with both devices and contractility with IABP only, with no between-group differences. Thirty-day mortality was similar (38% vs 45%, p=0.84). Conclusions: In VA-ECMO supported SCAI D/E cardiogenic shock, IABP improved myocardial oxygen supply-demand balance, whereas mAFP did not. Further research is needed to determine whether these mechanistic differences translate to clinical outcomes.

title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Pure Aortic Regurgitation: The Randomized SEASON-AR Clinical Trial.
authorString: Gao XF, Wang Y, Jiang H, Li B, Shao YB, Luo J, Ren FX, Ouyang F, Chen ZK, Yuan HT, Wang C, Han B, Xiao PX, Yuan YQ, Yang ZW, Miao L, Ma X, Yang J, You DF, Chen SL, Zhang JJ, SEASON-AR Trial Investigators.
abstractText:
Background

For patients with severe pure aortic regurgitation (AR) at high surgical risk, guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) is often the only available option. Transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is an established treatment for aortic stenosis and has also been evaluated in patients with pure AR. However, no adequately powered randomized trial has compared TAVR with GDMT alone in this population.

Methods

We conducted a prospective, investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized, open-label trial in China. Patients with severe pure AR for whom surgery was considered difficult or unacceptable by the local heart team or who persistently declined surgery were randomly assigned at a 1:1 ratio to receive transfemoral TAVR with the VitaFlow system plus GDMT or GDMT alone. The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year.

Results

We assigned 210 patients with severe pure AR to the TAVR group (n=109) or GDMT group (n=101) at 18 centers. At 1-year follow-up, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the primary end point was significantly lower in the TAVR group than in the GDMT group (8.3% vs 24.8%; hazard ration [HR], 0.31 [95% CI, 0.14-0.66]; P=0.001), driven primarily by a reduction in heart failure rehospitalization (3.7% vs 21.3%; HR, 0.16 [95% CI, 0.06-0.47]; P < 0.001). TAVR was associated with higher rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation, most of which occurred within 30 days after the procedure.

Conclusions

Among patients with severe pure AR, TAVR plus GDMT significantly reduced the rate of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year compared with GDMT alone despite higher 30-day rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation.

Registration

URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04864145.

title: Bivalirudin With a High-Dose Post-PCI Infusion Versus Heparin During Primary PCI in STEMI: One-Year Results From the BRIGHT-4 Trial.
authorString: Liang Z, Qin L, Wang M, Wang X, Zhang H, Liu Y, Li Y, Liu L, Luo J, Dong S, Guo J, Zhu H, Li S, Zheng H, Liu L, Wu Y, Zhong Y, Qiu M, Li Y, Han Y, Stone GW.
abstractText:
Background

The BRIGHT-4 trial (Bivalirudin With Prolonged Full-Dose Infusion During Primary PCI Versus Heparin Trial-4) demonstrated that procedural anticoagulation with bivalirudin plus a high-dose postprocedure infusion reduced the 30-day composite end point of all-cause death or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium types 3 to 5 bleeding compared with heparin monotherapy in patients with ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with radial artery access. We now report the 12-month follow-up results to evaluate the long-term outcomes of primary PCI with these 2 anticoagulation regimens.

Methods

In this multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial, 6016 patients with ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary PCI with radial artery access were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive bivalirudin with a high-dose post-PCI infusion for 2 to 4 hours (n=3009) or heparin monotherapy (n=3007). The primary outcome of interest was the composite of all-cause death or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium types 3 to 5 bleeding at 12 months.

Results

At 12 months, the primary outcome occurred in 124 (4.1%) patients in the bivalirudin group and 169 (5.6%) patients in the heparin group (hazard ratio, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.58-0.92]; P=0.007). Bivalirudin resulted in lower 12-month rates of Bleeding Academic Research Consortium types 3 to 5 bleeding (0.6% versus 1.2%; hazard ratio, 0.49 [95% CI, 0.28-0.87]; P=0.01) and stent thrombosis (0.8% versus 1.3%; hazard ratio, 0.60 [95% CI, 0.36-0.99]; P=0.045), with nonsignificant differences in all-cause death (3.8% versus 4.8%; hazard ratio, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.63-1.02]; P=0.08), cardiovascular death, reinfarction, ischemia-driven target vessel revascularization, and stroke between the 2 groups.

Conclusions

Among patients with ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary PCI with radial artery access, the benefits of bivalirudin with a high-dose post-PCI infusion in reducing the composite end point of all-cause death or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium types 3 to 5 bleeding at 30 days compared with heparin monotherapy are maintained through 12-month follow-up. These findings support the use of bivalirudin with a post-PCI high-dose infusion as an alternative to heparin to reduce mortality and major bleeding in patients with ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction.

Registration

URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT03822975.

title: Updates in cardiovascular CT imaging in 2025: A year in review.
authorString: Nagpal P, Priya S, Bluemke DA, Garcia-Garcia HM, Alfaddagh A, Andreini D, Baggiano A, Canan A, Chelliah A, Chen MY, Conte E, De Cecco CN, Fairbairn T, Ferencik M, Feuchtner G, Föllmer B, Hamdan A, Han BK, Ko B, Leipsic JA, Madan N, Michallek F, Mushtaq S, Ng MY, Nicol E, Niinuma H, Pontone G, Pourmorteza A, Reid A, Weir-McCall JR, Whelton S, Yu J, Williams MC, Chow BJW, Fuss C, Arbab-Zadeh A.
abstractText: The year 2025 brought long-term outcome data supporting coronary CT angiography (CCTA)-guided management of stable chest pain, a proposed reframing of coronary artery disease around atherosclerosis rather than ischemia, and the first large-scale real-world evaluation of a national artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled CT-derived fractional flow reserve (FFR-CT) program. This review summarizes selected advances in cardiovascular computed tomography (CCT) published in print or online during 2025. The studies span coronary artery disease outcomes and prevention, quantitative plaque analysis, photon-counting detector CT, coronary artery calcium scoring, pericoronary inflammation imaging, AI and machine learning, structural and congenital heart disease, and consensus and training documents. For each study we summarize the design, principal findings, limitations, and likely clinical implications, and we close with the barriers, including technical standardization, vendor-specific thresholds, equitable access, and the need for randomized outcome trials, that must be addressed before many of these advances can be implemented broadly.

title: Improvement in mitral regurgitation after alcohol septal ablation in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy: a retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Damlin A, Rück A, Mustafic M, Jandér R, Rickenlund A, Eriksson MJ, Saleh N, Marlevi D.
abstractText:
Background

The primary mechanism of mitral regurgitation (MR) in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral leaflets due to septal hypertrophy narrowing the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT), influencing leaflet movement and closure. Among patients undergoing alcohol septal ablation (ASA), the impact on- and underlying mechanism of MR remains less studied. The aim was to determine the prevalence of MR and changes in MR severity after ASA and analyze echocardiographic (ECHO) parameters associated with MR changes.

Methods

All patients who underwent ASA at Karolinska University Hospital in Sweden, 2009-2021 (follow-up until 2025), were included in this retrospective cohort study. ECHO parameters were collected before ASA, at 1-year follow-up and at the latest follow-up registered. To evaluate differences in continuous values, Kruskal-Wallis test was used, and for categorical values, Fischer's exact test was used.

Results

154 patients were included (mean follow-up 4.0 ± 3.9 years). 14% (n = 21) had at least moderate MR at baseline, of which 90% (n = 19) improved to mild MR or less. The patients with improved (n = 19, 12%) or unchanged (n = 128, 83%) grade of MR showed greater reduction of LVOT peak pressure gradients (improved MR: 137.5 to 4.8 mmHg, unchanged MR: 57.0 to 25.0 mmHg) between baseline and last follow-up, compared with patients with increased MR grade (n = 7, 4.5%, 57.0 to 51.0 mmHg, p = 0.003).

Conclusions

Among patients with at least moderate MR before ASA, MR severity generally improved at follow-up, potentially due to septal reduction and LVOT enlargement, which may have reduced SAM.

Clinical trial number

Not applicable.

title: HELLP (Hemolysis, Elevated Liver Enzymes, and Low Platelets)-Associated Subcapsular Hepatic Hematoma Presenting as Postoperative Hemorrhagic Shock: A Case Report.
authorString: Grossi Diaz J, Vale de Sá K, Tanios Daneluzzi S, Saddi Nascimento Cavalcante Peres B, Mazzetti AC, Nascimento Motta Spaleta B, Casella Szuster F, Monteiro Klock JC.
abstractText: Subcapsular hepatic hematoma is a rare and life-threatening complication of HELLP (hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelet count) syndrome associated with substantial maternal morbidity and mortality. We report the case of a 23-year-old primigravida at 27 weeks and 3 days of gestation who presented with severe frontal headache, nausea, vomiting, and hypertension and was initially diagnosed with preeclampsia with severe features. On hospital day three, clinical deterioration prompted emergency cesarean delivery, and postoperative laboratory findings confirmed HELLP syndrome. On the first postoperative day, the patient developed hypovolemic shock and signs of acute abdomen. Point-of-care ultrasonography revealed free intra-abdominal fluid, prompting urgent surgical re-exploration. An extensive subcapsular hepatic hematoma with active bleeding was identified, and damage control surgery with hepatic packing and temporary abdominal closure was performed. After 48 hours of clinical stabilization, planned re-exploration with pack removal and definitive abdominal wall closure was completed. Liver enzymes subsequently showed progressive normalization through hospital discharge. This case highlights the importance of recognizing hepatic complications of HELLP syndrome in patients with abrupt postoperative deterioration and demonstrates the role of coordinated multidisciplinary management in severe hemorrhagic presentations. In hemodynamically unstable patients with evidence of ongoing intra-abdominal hemorrhage, the absence of definitive cross-sectional imaging may not preclude urgent surgical exploration.

title: Associations Between Self-Reported Experiences of Racial Discrimination and Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy among Black and White Women in the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults Study.
authorString: Dodds LV, Feaster DJ, Kiefe CI, Gunderson EP, Kershaw KN, Rundek T, Paidas M, Elfassy T.

journal.title: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities

abstractText: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) are major contributors to maternal morbidity, mortality, and long-term cardiovascular risk. Perceived experiences of racial discrimination (EORD) have been associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes. This study investigates the association between EORD and incident HDP among Black and White women. The Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults study is a prospective cohort of 5,115 Black and White adults aged 18 to 30 years at baseline (1985-1986), followed for over 30 years. EORD was analyzed as a continuous proportion, a three-category variable (no discrimination, overall proportion < 33%, and 33% or greater), and dichotomously (none vs. ever). HDP was self-reported in pregnancies lasting at least 23 weeks. Logistic regression assessed the association between EORD and HDP among 1,184 parous women, adjusting for age, race, education, income, cardiovascular risk factors, and parity. At baseline, the mean age was 24.1 years; 48.1% were Black, 72.3% were nulliparous, and 19.7% had an income less than $16,000. Overall, 60.6% reported EORD (86.0% of Black and 37.1% of White women). Those reporting EORD were more likely to be Black, unmarried, have higher BMI, and have had one birth at baseline (p < 0.001). EORD was associated with increased odds of HDP (OR: 1.73 [1.20-2.48]) among both Black and White women. EORD < 33% (OR: 1.75 [1.20-2.55]) and 33% or greater (OR: 1.65 [1.04-2.64]) were significantly associated with HDP. EORD, regardless of race, is significantly associated with increased odds of HDP. The disproportionate burden among Black women highlights the need for targeted interventions.

title: Uqcrc2 lactylation promotes sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy by targeting the mitochondrial respiratory chain.
authorString: Lin SP, Shi H, Mo J, Lian C, He Z, Xie Y, Ji Y, Rao B, Wei J, Li Y, Jiang H, Chen XH.
abstractText:
Background

Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy (SIC) markedly increases the overall mortality among patients with sepsis. The pathogenesis of SIC remains incompletely elucidated; specifically, the role of protein lactylation in the onset and progression of SIC awaits further investigation.

Methods

Using lactylome profilinganalysis, bioinformatics and molecular biology methods, the key proteins and lactylation sites involved in the development of SIC were identified. Amino acid point mutations, molecular dynamic simulation, and biochemical experiments were performed to investigate their biological roles and underlying mechanisms.

Results

The lactylome analysis revealed 439 differentially lactylated sites in the myocardium of septic mice compared with control group.Through integrated bioinformatic analysis and molecular validation, we demonstrated that lactylation of ubiquinol-cytochrome c reductase core protein 2 (Uqcrc2) plays a pivotal role in SIC, andidentified K109 as the critical lactylation site. Mechanistically,Uqcrc2 K109 lactylation disrupts mitochondrial respiratory chain function and exacerbates cardiomyocyte apoptosis. Importantly,inhibition of Uqcrc2 K109 lactylation attenuates this apoptotic process. Furthermore, we identifiedlysine acetyltransferase 6A (KAT6A) as a novel lactyltransferase, mediating Uqcrc2 lactylation.

Conclusions

Our study reveals that the lactate-KAT6A-Uqcrc2 lactylation-mitochondrial apoptosis axis plays a pivotal role in SIC.

title: Temporal trends and projections of hypertension with hyperlipidemia-related mortality among US adults, 2000-2035: Insights from CDC WONDER database.
authorString: Khan S, Vazaym M, Jawad M, Khalid N, Kotak P, Hassan M, Hussain M, Devi M, Mubashir M, Naz A, Fatima I.

journal.title: Journal of the National Medical Association

abstractText:
Background

Hypertension and hyperlipidemia are highly prevalent cardiometabolic disorders and major contributors to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. These conditions frequently coexist and synergistically increase cardiovascular risk through mechanisms including endothelial dysfunction, vascular inflammation, and atherosclerosis. Despite advances in treatment, many individuals remain inadequately controlled. This study evaluated temporal trends in mortality associated with hypertension and hyperlipidemia in the United States from 2000 to 2035.

Methods

A retrospective population-based analysis was conducted using the CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death database. Adults aged ≥25 years with hypertension (ICD-10: I10-I15) or hyperlipidemia (ICD-10: E78) listed on death certificates were included. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 population were calculated using the 2000 U.S. standard population. Temporal trends were assessed using Joinpoint regression to estimate annual percent change (APC) and average annual percent change (AAPC). Analyses were stratified by sex, age, race/ethnicity, region, and urbanization.

Results

From 2000 to 2023, 1,156,335 deaths were recorded. AAMRs increased from 5.86 (95% CI: 5.74-5.97) to 37.28 (95% CI: 37.05-37.51), with a significant overall rise (AAPC: 8.34; p < 0.001). Mortality was consistently higher in males than females (AAPC: 8.50 vs. 7.93; both p < 0.001). All racial and ethnic groups showed increasing trends, with the highest mean AAMR among non-Hispanic Black individuals (AAPC: 8.21; p < 0.001). Older adults (≥65 years) had the greatest mortality burden (AAPC: 8.82; p < 0.001). The South (AAPC: 8.84; p<0.001) and non-metropolitan areas (AAPC: 9.76; p < 0.001) demonstrated the fastest-rising mortality rates.

Conclusion

Hypertension- and hyperlipidemia-related mortality rose substantially with marked disparities, highlighting the need for improved prevention and equitable care.

title: Surgery of retrosternal thyroid: evaluation of 82 cases.
authorString: Gülmez E, Özdemir AÇ, Al EA, Vural A, Kara İ, Yüce İ, Çağlı S.

journal.title: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery

abstractText:
Introduction

Retrosternal goiter (RSG) remains one of the most challenging conditions in thyroid surgery because of its variable mediastinal extension, close relationship with vital mediastinal structures, and occasional need for extracervical surgical approaches. Although advances in perioperative management have improved surgical outcomes, contemporary long-term single-center experiences remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical characteristics, surgical management, postoperative outcomes, and histopathological findings of patients with retrosternal goiter treated over a 13-year period at a tertiary referral center.

Methods

A retrospective cohort study was performed including consecutive patients who underwent surgery for retrosternal goiter at Erciyes University Faculty of Medicine between January 2012 and June 2025. Demographic characteristics, presenting symptoms, thyroid function, operative procedures, postoperative complications, and histopathological findings were retrospectively reviewed.

Results

A total of 82 patients were included. The mean age was 55.0 ± 13.0 years, and 59.8% were female. Cervical swelling was the most common presenting symptom, while nearly one-third of patients were diagnosed incidentally. 91% of patients were euthyroid preoperatively. Total thyroidectomy was the predominant surgical procedure. A transcervical approach was sufficient in 80 patients (97.6%); one patient required partial sternotomy for deep anterior mediastinal extension with fibrous adhesions to the brachiocephalic vessels, and one underwent thoracotomy for posterior retroesophageal extension with subcarinal involvement. Temporary hypocalcemia was the most frequent postoperative complication, whereas permanent hypocalcemia and permanent recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy occurred in 3.7% and 1.2% of patients, respectively. No postoperative hematoma requiring reoperation, tracheomalacia, or perioperative mortality occurred. Benign multinodular or nodular colloid goiter was identified in 79.3% of patients, whereas follicular adenomas and other benign lesions accounted for 10.9%, and malignant lesions comprised 9.8% of the cohort.

Conclusion

In experienced hands, over 97% of retrosternal goiters can be successfully resected via a transcervical approach. Extracervical procedures are reserved for deep posterior retroesophageal extension or extensive mediastinal involvement below the aortic arch. Comprehensive preoperative CT planning and multidisciplinary care in high-volume tertiary referral centers ensure minimal morbidity.

title: Occlusive Multivessel Coronary Vasospasm Causing Cardiac Arrest and ST-Segment Elevation in Nonobstructive Coronaries.
authorString: Nicolela GB, Ferro de Brito PH, Mekhitarian HN, Soares PR, Campos CM, de Brito Júnior FS, Antônio da Cunha Abizaid A, de Melo PHMC.
abstractText:
Background

Coronary vasospasm is an uncommon but potentially fatal cause of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA), and is easily missed when structural disease coexists.

Case summary

A 63-year-old man with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, chronic atrial fibrillation, Stanford type B aortic dissection, and nonobstructive coronaries 3 months earlier presented with decompensated heart failure. Peri-Valsalva, he sustained ventricular fibrillation arrest requiring prolonged resuscitation; post-return of spontaneous circulation electrocardiogram showed inferior ST-segment elevation. Aortography excluded retrograde flap extension; angiography revealed right coronary occlusion with left-system spasm, all reversed by intracoronary nitroglycerin (600 μg, TIMI flow grade 3). Cardiac magnetic resonance confirmed transmural inferior infarction; calcium-channel blockade followed.

Discussion

Coronary vasospasm is an under-recognized, potentially fatal functional cause of MINOCA; registries show vasospastic arrest survivors face high recurrence. A recent nonobstructive angiogram excludes neither spasm nor infarction, and coexisting aortic dissection mandates ascending aortography first.

Take-home message

Consider occlusive vasospasm in ST-segment elevation with previously nonobstructive coronaries; exclude aortic causes, then use intracoronary nitroglycerin diagnostically and therapeutically.

title: Prevalence of many comorbidities is similar irrespective of the time since HIV diagnosis in persons ageing with HIV who have survived to age 65 years.
authorString: Zhabokritsky A, Lovblom LE, Boyachuk B, Falutz J, Klein M, Loutfy M, Smith G, Tan D, Harris M, Guillemi S, Adany N, Verway M, Arbess G, Guaraldi G, Walmsley S.
abstractText:
Objective

To compare the prevalence of comorbidity in persons with HIV ≥65 years of age based on the time from HIV diagnosis.

Design

Cross-sectional observational cohort study.

Methods

Data was collected from 540 participants in the CHANGE HIV (Correlates of Healthy Aging in Geriatric HIV) study, a longitudinal study of HIV in persons aged 65 years and older from seven primary and tertiary care centres in Canada between 2019 and 2026. We compared the baseline prevalence of comorbidities stratified by the cumulative time since known HIV diagnosis (<20 years, 20-30 years and >30 years) and controlled for demographic, HIV and lifestyle factors.

Results

The cohort was 90% male, median age 69 years, 76% white, median CD4 561 cells/mm3 and 92% with an undetectable viral load. They had a median of 3 (range 0-12) comorbid conditions. There was no difference in prevalence of coronary artery disease, dyslipidaemia, peripheral artery disease, stroke, chronic obstructive lung disease, asthma, arthritis, Parkinson's disease, HIV-associated neurocognitive dysfunction, chronic kidney disease, diabetes or liver disease based on time since HIV diagnosis. After accounting for confounders, longer time since HIV diagnosis was associated with higher prevalence of cancer, diabetes and peripheral neuropathy. Of the comorbidities only peripheral neuropathy, dyslipidaemia and Kaposi's sarcoma occurred at a younger age.

Conclusions

Prevalence of many comorbidities was not increased in those with longer time since HIV diagnosis. Lifestyle factors (smoking, substance use and diet) are important contributors to non-infectious comorbidities in this population, and increased prevalence of cancer reinforces the importance of preventative screening.

title: Atrial Distensibility Predicts Short-Term Prognosis in Fetal Single Ventricle-Type Congenital Heart Disease with Atrioventricular Valve Regurgitation.
authorString: Akazawa Y, Yonehara K, Obinata H, Numata R, Shibuya Y, Takei K, Takigiku K.
abstractText: We aimed to determine whether the assessment of atrial distensibility helps predict perinatal outcomes in fetuses with a prenatal diagnosis of single ventricle-type congenital heart disease (SVCHD) with atrioventricular valve regurgitation (AVVR). We retrospectively identified 76 consecutive fetuses with SVCHD who were examined between 2011 and 2023. Atrial distensibility and conventional echocardiographic parameters used to assess the severity of fetal heart failure were measured retrospectively. Fetuses with SVCHD were divided into two groups according to AVVR severity: no-to-mild or ≥moderate. The primary endpoint was a composite of fetal demise, neonatal death from any cause, or early infantile atrioventricular valve surgery. The prognostic value of atrial distensibility was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Of 76 fetuses diagnosed prenatally with SVCHD, nine terminations and eight fetuses with chromosomal abnormalities were excluded. Of the remaining 59 fetuses, 48 had no-to-mild AVVR, and 11 had ≥moderate AVVR. Atrial distensibility was significantly lower in fetuses with SVCHD and ≥moderate AVVR than in those with no-to-mild AVVR (p = 0.0002). Among fetuses with SVCHD and ≥moderate AVVR, atrial distensibility was lower in fetuses with adverse events than in those without (p = 0.011). ROC analysis indicated that atrial distensibility had significant predictive value for composite adverse outcomes in fetuses with SVCHD with ≥moderate AVVR (area under the curve [AUC], 0.93; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.78-1.00). Quantitative assessment of atrial distensibility may have clinical utility in predicting the perinatal outcomes of fetuses with SVCHD and significant AVVR.

title: Sex-Specific Coronary Plaque Characteristics and Risk of Cardiovascular Events: Insights from ISCHEMIA.
authorString: Lakshmanan S, Wang Y, Chen YQ, Mancini GJ, Leipsic J, Budoff M, Hague C, Min JK, Stone GW, Boden WE, Spertus JA, Bangalore S, Hochman JS, Reynolds HR, Maron DJ, ISCHEMIA Research Group.
abstractText: Among the highly diseased population of participants with chronic coronary syndromes and obstructive coronary artery disease enrolled in the ISCHEMIA trial, women had lower burden of total, calcified, non-calcified plaque and adverse plaque characteristics on CCTA compared with men. However, the risk associated with greater atherosclerotic burden was higher among females for the composite outcome of CV death or MI than males. These findings highlight important sex-specific differences in the prognostic value of coronary atherosclerotic burden and support the need to explore differential approaches to cardiovascular risk stratification in men and women.

title: Surgical management of Marjolin's ulcer secondary to chronic burn scar: a case report.
authorString: Zhang Y, Wang J, Jin S.
abstractText: Marjolin's ulcer is a rare malignancy originating from chronically injured skin with a prolonged latency period. We report a 71-year-old male with a 34-year history of a chronic burn scar ulcer in the left popliteal fossa that underwent malignant transformation. Histopathology confirmed moderately-to-well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. His comorbidities included stage 4 chronic kidney disease and hypertension. Following multidisciplinary assessment, wide local excision combined with punch skin grafting was performed. The grafts took well, and no recurrence was noted at short-term follow-up. Chronic post-burn scar ulcers require long-term surveillance, early biopsy, and individualized surgical planning, especially in patients with multiple comorbidities.

title: Renin-angiotensin system inhibitors and arterial stiffness in chronic kidney disease: results from the chronic renal insufficiency cohort.
authorString: Shulman R, Cohen DL, Townsend R, Cohen JB, CRIC Study Investigators.
abstractText: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with accelerated arterial stiffness, which contributes to its high burden cardiovascular disease. There is conflicting evidence on whether renin-angiotensin system inhibitors (RASIs) prevent arterial stiffness. We investigated the association between RASIs versus non-RASI antihypertensive medications and yearly changes in carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cfPWV) - a measure of arterial stiffness -using a linear mixed-effects model among participants in the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) Study. As a secondary analysis, we restricted the cohort to participants on one antihypertensive medication at baseline. Lastly, we used a linear mixed-effects model to evaluate the relationship between RASI use and systolic blood pressure over time. Of the 1 201 participants who met inclusion criteria, 982 were on RASI and 219 were on a non-RASI medication. Individuals on RASI had a non-significant increase in cfPWV (adjusted cfPWV 0.19 m/s per year, 95% CI 0.14 to 0.25) compared to non-RASI users (adjusted cfPWV 0.15 m/s per year, 95% CI 0.00 to 0.30; p = 0.61). In the monotherapy cohort (N = 283), there was no difference in adjusted yearly change in cfPWV between RASI (0.11 m/s per year, 95% CI 0.02 to 0.21) and non-RASI users (0.03 m/s per year, 95% CI -0.14 to 0.20; p = 0.41). In both cohorts, there was no significant difference in systolic blood pressure over time between RASI and non-RASI users. Future research to mitigate the accelerated large artery stiffness in patients with CKD should focus on targetable mechanisms beyond the renin-angiotensin system.

title: Carotid and femoral plaque burden in patients with early coronary artery disease events: Prevalence, extent and relationship to risk phenotypes.
authorString: López-Melgar B, Jiménez-Borreguero LJ, Roquero P, de la Fuente H, Cecconi A, Montes N, Acedo N, Pascual N, González-Juanatey C, Sánchez-González J, Sanz de Benito MÁ, Sánchez-Madrid F, Alfonso F.
abstractText:
Background

Early coronary artery disease events (eCAD) are increasing, occasionally occurring in individuals with minimal atherosclerosis, suggesting heterogeneous underlying mechanisms. We report, for the first time, carotid and femoral plaque burden in eCAD patients, relate it to underlying phenotypes, and compare it with the PESA reference cohort to explore preventive implications.

Methods

eCAD patients (<60 years) were consecutively and prospectively enrolled at a tertiary hospital. Conventional and non-conventional cardiovascular risk factors (CVRF) and blood biomarkers were assessed, and global atherosclerosis plaque burden (GPB) was quantified as total carotid and femoral plaque volume by 3-dimensional vascular ultrasound (3DVUS).

Results

Among 231 eCAD patients (53 ± 5 years old; 14% women; 23% with a prior event; 52% presented with STEMI) conventional CVRF were frequent but prevalence of non-conventional CVRF was high (28% elevated lipoprotein a, 25% family history of premature CVD, 25% hyperuricemia, and 14% hyperhomocysteinemia). Underlying GPB was high (268.7 mm3 [IQR75.2-509.9]), being higher in the femoral than the carotid territory (200.6 mm3 [IQR51.7-420.7] vs 35.2 mm3 [IQR7.9-96.2], p < 0.001), and increased with age. Compared with age-matched asymptomatic individuals (PESA study), eCAD patients had markedly higher GPB (284.1 mm3 [IQR110-546.8] vs 50.8 mm3 [18.7-121.5]). However, GPB in eCAD patients varied widely. Severe GBP (percentile≥75th) identified a subgroup with predominantly conventional CVRF and prior CVD, with marginal presence of non-conventional factors, compared with those with no-or-mild GPB (percentile≤25th).

Conclusion

Carotid and femoral PB by 3DVUS identifies distinct pathophysiological phenotypes in eCAD, underscoring the value of atherosclerosis assessment for individualized management and prevention.

title: Swimming exercise protects against diabetic cardiomyopathy through suppression of FABP4-associated CTRP3 degradation.
authorString: Yue B, Xu F, Jiao X, Wang B, Xu H, Ou S, Chen K, Xu H, Guo X.
abstractText:
Background

Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a major cardiovascular complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D) characterized by metabolic dysregulation, oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and progressive cardiac dysfunction. Although swimming exercise has been recognized as an effective non-pharmacological intervention for DCM, the molecular mechanisms underlying its cardioprotective effects remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify the key exercise-responsive molecular targets involved in DCM and elucidate the mechanisms by which swimming exercise attenuates diabetic cardiac injury.

Methods

Bioinformatic analyses were performed using public transcriptomic datasets to identify hub genes associated with swimming exercise-mediated protection against DCM. A streptozotocin/high-fat diet-induced T2D mouse model was established and subjected to low- or high-intensity swimming exercise interventions. Cardiac function, histopathology, metabolic parameters, oxidative stress markers, and inflammatory cytokines were evaluated. Gain-of-function experiments using AAV9-mediated cardiac fatty acid-binding protein 4 (FABP4) overexpression and C1q/TNF-related protein 3 (CTRP3) mutant constructs were conducted in vivo and in vitro. Protein-protein interactions were investigated using co-immunoprecipitation, molecular docking, thermal shift assays, and ubiquitination analyses.

Results

Bioinformatic screening identified FABP4 as the top-ranked exercise-responsive hub gene associated with metabolic pathways in DCM. Swimming exercise dose-dependently improved glucose homeostasis, insulin sensitivity, oxidative balance, systemic inflammation, and anxiety-like behaviors in diabetic mice. Concurrently, swimming exercise markedly alleviated myocardial fibrosis, cardiac dysfunction, and myocardial injury while suppressing cardiac FABP4 expression. FABP4 overexpression markedly attenuated the favorable cardiac and metabolic phenotypes observed in swimming-trained diabetic mice, resulting in impaired mitochondrial respiration and glycolysis, enhanced oxidative stress, exaggerated inflammatory responses, and aggravated cardiac remodeling. In vitro, FABP4 interacted with CTRP3 and promoted CTRP3 ubiquitination-associated proteasomal degradation. AICAR treatment weakened the FABP4-CTRP3 interaction and preserved CTRP3 protein stability in vitro. Furthermore, N63 of CTRP3 was identified as an important residue contributing to FABP4 interaction and CTRP3 protein stability. The N63A mutation reduced CTRP3 stability and attenuated AICAR-associated metabolic, antioxidative, and anti-inflammatory protection in vitro, while in vivo expression of CTRP3-N63A was associated with impaired cardiac protection during swimming intervention.

Conclusions

These findings identify FABP4 as an exercise-responsive regulator associated with diabetic cardiac injury and reveal a potential FABP4-CTRP3 protein-stability mechanism supported by cellular experiments and CTRP3 functional manipulation. Swimming exercise attenuates the development of diabetes-associated cardiac dysfunction and remodeling by suppressing FABP4, whereas the cellular mechanistic findings suggest that regulation of the FABP4-CTRP3 protein-stability axis may contribute to these cardioprotective effects. However, whether swimming exercise directly regulates endogenous myocardial CTRP3 stability in vivo remains to be established.

title: Childhood Food Insecurity and the Development of Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: Dietary, Metabolic, and Psychosocial Pathways.
authorString: Lewis K, Wilson D.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

Food insecurity affects 18.4% of US households with children and disproportionately impacts racial and ethnic minority and single-parent households. This review examines the association between childhood food insecurity and the development of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), the pathways through which food insecurity may accelerate cardiovascular risk, and the role of nutrition assistance programs and interdisciplinary teams in mitigating that risk.

Recent findings

Children with food insecurity demonstrate lower Life's Essential 8 cardiovascular health scores, primarily driven by higher body mass index, compared to food-secure peers. Food insecurity is cross-sectionally associated with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome stages 1 and 2 among adolescents, with food-secure adolescents having 40% lower odds of CKM stages 1 to 2 in fully adjusted models (OR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.44 to 0.82). Food insecurity is associated with adverse cardiometabolic markers including lower HDL cholesterol, higher triglycerides, and elevated fasting glucose. Non-dietary mechanisms, including chronic psychosocial stress, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis dysregulation, gut dysbiosis, and epigenetic modifications, further contribute to cardiovascular risk. Participation in federally funded nutrition assistance programs is associated with improved cardiovascular health metrics and cardiometabolic profiles. Childhood food insecurity is associated with the accelerated development of ASCVD risk factors through dietary, metabolic, and psychosocial pathways. Early identification of food insecurity and coordinated interdisciplinary intervention represent critical strategies for cardiovascular risk reduction in vulnerable pediatric populations.

Key points

• Food insecurity affects 18.4% of US households with children and is cross-sectionally associated with CKM syndrome stages 1 and 2 among adolescents. • Non-dietary pathways including chronic stress, gut dysbiosis, and epigenetic changes contribute to ASCVD risk. • Nutrition assistance programs improve cardiovascular health metrics. • Evidence supporting food insecurity screening tools for improving health outcomes remains insufficient.

title: An unusual case of adenovirus meningoencephalitis in an immunocompetent adolescent girl.
authorString: Bansal A, Singh H, Prabhakar A, Dhibar DP, Suri V, Bora I, Bhalla A.
abstractText: Human adenoviruses can cause infections at any age, but most commonly involve the paediatric population. Adenoviruses may cause a wide spectrum of diseases depending on the infecting serotype. The various clinical entities include respiratory illnesses, conjunctivitis, gastroenteritis, myocarditis, cardiomyopathy, cystitis, and meningo-encephalitis. Here we present an uncommon case of the latter in an adolescent girl, diagnosed by cerebrospinal fluid RT-PCR. These include mild aseptic meningitis, subacute focal encephalitius, myelitis, Reye syndrome and potentially fatal acute necrotizing encephalopathy, but are all rare in an immunocompetent host.

title: Assessing Hemodynamic Impact of Tissue-Engineered Vascular Graft Displacement: Combining Postoperative In Vivo Results and Computational Modeling to Improve Surgical Planning.
authorString: Aslan S, Chen E, Mese-Jones M, Contento J, Hayashi H, Kawaji K, Huddle J, Johnson J, Loke YH, Fuge M, Olivieri L, Nguyen TD, Hibino N, Krieger A.
abstractText:
Purpose

Tissue-engineered vascular grafts (TEVG) have shown promise in advancing vascular reconstructions. However, precise in vivo implantation is challenging, and it is unclear how deviations in location and size affect hemodynamics. This study aims to 1) compare preoperative designs and postoperative anatomies of TEVG in an in vivo study to evaluate discrepancies and 2) investigate the impact of graft displacement and size on hemodynamics by virtually simulating implantation scenarios that are informed by in vivo postoperative results.

Methods

Designed and postoperative geometries of four porcine aortas were compared to measure the mismatch in implantation location and graft shape. These results informed a virtual TEVG implantation study. TEVG location, orientation, and size were varied to investigate the effects on the final aorta shape and hemodynamics. Anastomosis of TEVG was simulated using finite element modeling. Key hemodynamic metrics were obtained from virtual implantations and actual postoperative anatomies using computational fluid dynamics.

Results

Our in vivo study showed that TEVGs can experience up to 6.9 mm displacement and a 38° rotational shift post-implantation, leading to discrepancies in pressure drop (2.5 mmHg, 50%) and time-averaged wall shear stress (7.2 Pa, 72%) compared to predictions. Virtual TEVG implantation showed that peak systolic pressure drop (PSPD) was most sensitive to translation in the inferior-superior direction and rotation about the anterior-posterior axis. Size mismatch had a greater impact on time-averaged wall shear stress (TAWSS) (85%) than PSPD (23%). Additionally, virtual anastomosis simulations improved aortic shape predictions by 27.5%.

Conclusion

Our results highlight the sensitivity of key hemodynamic metrics to graft implantation location and size mismatch. By quantifying displacement ranges and their impacts during surgery, surgeons can make informed decisions.

title: Ascending Aortic Pseudoaneurysm Near the Right Coronary Ostium: Predicting Occluder Disc Footprint on CT.
authorString: Saeed M, Sabanci R, Saeed Z, Taleb M, Noman A.
abstractText:
Background

Ascending aortic pseudoaneurysm is a rare late complication of aortic surgery. Transcatheter closure is an option for patients at prohibitive surgical risk, but when the neck lies near a coronary ostium, device sizing alone does not predict the final position of the expanded disc.

Case summary

An 82-year-old woman with prior type A dissection repair and subsequent root replacement developed an enlarging ascending aortic pseudoaneurysm with a 15.8 × 13.1 mm neck adjacent to the right coronary ostium. Before intervention, the anticipated footprint of a 12-mm septal occluder was projected geometrically onto 3-dimensional computed tomography reconstruction using the intended working projection; the ostium remained just outside the predicted disc margin. The coronary artery was wired prophylactically, the device seated as predicted, and angiography and echocardiography confirmed sac exclusion with an unobstructed vessel.

Discussion

Projecting the expanded occluder footprint onto computed tomography settled device selection, working projection, and coronary protection preprocedurally rather than by intraprocedural assessment.

title: Concomitant Transcatheter Aortic and Tricuspid Valve Replacement.
authorString: Niamat J, Ren C, De Assis LU, Kostea A, Wilschut J, Nuis RJ.
abstractText:
Background

Severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is associated with adverse outcomes.

Case summary

A 65-year-old man with advanced right heart failure symptoms and torrential TR was accepted for transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR). After an unforeseen treatment delay, reassessment demonstrated progression of concomitant mild-to-moderate aortic stenosis (AS) to severe AS. He underwent successful TAVR and TTVR during 1 procedure with an excellent clinical outcome.

Discussion

Given the sequence of disease progression with symptomatic torrential TR preceding the development of severe AS, an indication for TAVR and TTVR was established. A single-procedure strategy was favored over a staged approach based on the assumption that TAVR alone could increase forward flow and right-sided loading conditions, potentially worsening right heart failure.

Take-home messages

Concomitant TAVR and TTVR may benefit selected patients. Pre-TAVR identification of patients requiring adjunctive TTVR and determination of the optimal timing (concomitant or staged) remain challenging.

title: Mitochondrial Metabolism-Related Candidate Signatures in Calcific Aortic Valve Disease Spectrum: An Exploratory Integrative Bioinformatics Study.
authorString: Yang M, Gui Y, Qian H, Zhang D.
abstractText: ​Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is a progressive valvular disorder in which the role of mitochondrial metabolism remains incompletely understood. This exploratory study aimed to identify mitochondrial metabolism-related genes (MIMMRGs) associated with CAVD-spectrum valve remodeling. GSE83453 was used as the training dataset, and GSE51472 was used for expression-direction validation. Both datasets contain biologically and phenotypically heterogeneous groups of diseased valves. CAVD-associated differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were integrated with MIMMRGs, followed by functional enrichment analysis, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), and support vector machine-recursive feature elimination (SVM-RFE), expression validation, immune infiltration analysis, transcription factor analysis, drug and compound prediction, and molecular docking. A total of 909 DEGs and 1,234 MIMMRGs were identified, yielding 67 candidate genes enriched in metabolic and biosynthetic processes. ACADL and TDO2 were identified as candidate biomarkers and exhibited consistent expression differences between CAVD and normal samples in both datasets. Gene set enrichment analysis indicated the involvement of chemokine-related and immune-regulatory pathways. Four immune cell types differed between the CAVD and normal groups, and ACADL and TDO2 exhibited opposite correlations with naive B cells. HNF4A, STAT3, and AR were predicted to be common transcriptional regulators. Molecular docking indicated favorable in silico interactions between doxorubicin and ACADL and between dexamethasone and TDO2. In conclusion, ACADL and TDO2 are candidate biomarkers associated with mitochondrial metabolism and immune-related processes in heterogeneous CAVD-spectrum valve lesions. These findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating and require independent clinical and experimental validation.

title: Paraparesis and left upper extremity weakness after total arch replacement with frozen elephant trunk: possible contributions of spinal cord ischaemia and cervical radiculopathy.
authorString: Ishihama T, Yokawa K, Shimatani Y, Uesugi K, Ishimoto K, Higuma T, Yoshida K, Obo H, Wakiyama H.
abstractText: An 82-year-old man underwent total arch replacement with the frozen elephant trunk technique for an aortic arch aneurysm. Upon awakening 3 hours postoperatively, the patient exhibited flaccid paralysis of both lower extremities and left upper extremity weakness, whereas the right upper extremity was largely preserved. Cerebrospinal fluid drainage and blood pressure augmentation were initiated for suspected spinal cord ischemia. Lower-extremity motor function partially recovered, but left upper-extremity weakness persisted. Spinal magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated intramedullary T2 hyperintensity at T2/3 and bilateral neural foraminal stenosis from C3/4 to C6/7. Neurological examination revealed predominant weakness in the left C7 myotome with an absent left triceps reflexes, suggesting concomitant C7 radiculopathy. This case demonstrates that neurological deficits after aortic arch surgery may be multifactorial and highlights the value of detailed neurological examination and spinal imaging when upper extremity weakness is disproportionate.

title: Index Below-Knee Endovascular Intervention for Intermittent Claudication Is Associated with Increased Amputation Risk.
authorString: Suri G, Jethmalani N, Chan P, Agrusa C, Connolly PH, Ellozy SH, DeRubertis B, Stern JR.
abstractText:
Introduction

Guidelines advise against infrapopliteal peripheral vascular intervention (PVI) for intermittent claudication (IC) due to potential harm with unclear benefit. We hypothesized that below-knee intervention at index PVI for IC confers higher future amputation risk than above-knee-only treatment.

Methods

From the VQI PVI registry (2015-2025), we identified elective, initial PVIs for IC and compared those patients undergoing above-knee-only treatment (AK) to those having any below-knee intervention (BK). Using our previously described methodology, long-term amputation data were obtained by linking the PVI and amputation registries via unique patient identifiers. Demographic and procedural data were analyzed descriptively. Kaplan-Meier Analysis estimated risk of major and any (major+minor) amputation, with independent predictors of amputation identified by multivariable Firth logistic regression.

Results

Among 92,899 treated limbs (81,338 AK; 11,561 BK), BK patients had increased rates of diabetes (54% vs. 41%), CHF (18% vs. 13%), and ESRD/dialysis (4.7% vs. 1.7%, p<0.001). BK patients were more likely to be Black (21% vs. 13%, p<0.001), Hispanic (8.8% vs. 4.3%, p<0.001), and Asian (1.5% vs. 1.0%, p<0.001). Smoking history predominated in AK (89% vs. 67%, p<0.001). 16,086 limbs required repeat PVI, 13,831 (17%) in the AK group vs. 2,255 (20%) in the BK group (p<0.001). At reintervention, BK patients were more likely to have progressed to CLTI (41% vs. 25%; p<0.001) and undergo ≥2 repeat interventions (32% vs. 27%; p<0.001). Initial below-knee intervention was associated with greater ipsilateral major (OR 2.39;1.70-3.35) and any (OR 2.36;1.75-3.18) amputation. Kaplan-Meier showed increased major [1-year (0.3% vs 0.1%);5-years (0.4% vs 0.1%)] and any amputation risk [1-year (0.5% vs 0.1%); 5-years (0.7% vs 0.2%).

Conclusions

Index below-knee intervention for IC portends greater risk of progression to CLTI, repeat PVI, and ipsilateral amputation, highlighting the potentially dangerous treatment trap of infrapopliteal intervention in patients with intermittent claudicants.

title: Cellular senescence in calcific aortic valve disease: are we ready for senolytic therapy?
authorString: Simonini L, Foffa I, Esposito A, Vecoli C.
abstractText: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is the most prevalent valvular heart disease in the Western countries and carries significant morbidity and mortality, yet no pharmacological therapy has demonstrated efficacy in modifying its natural history. Once regarded as a passive degenerative process, CAVD is now recognized as an actively regulated disease driven by endothelial dysfunction, chronic inflammation, dysregulated mineral metabolism, and cellular senescence, which collectively drive progressive fibrotic remodeling and calcification of the valve leaflets through both dystrophic and osteogenic mechanisms. This review examines the pharmacological strategies that have been investigated or are currently under evaluation to slow CAVD progression, encompassing lipid-lowering agents, renin-angiotensin system inhibitors, bone resorption inhibitors, vitamin K supplementation, and nitric oxide pathway modulators. Despite strong biological rationale and encouraging observational or preclinical data, each of these approaches has thus far failed to demonstrate consistent disease, modifying efficacy in prospective randomized trials, reflecting the complexity of CAVD pathophysiology and the historical lack of mechanistic precision in patient selection and trial design. Emerging evidence suggests that cellular senescence may represent a unifying and potentially actionable therapeutic target, bridging endothelial dysfunction, chronic inflammation, and active calcification within a single pathophysiological framework. Preclinical studies demonstrate that senolytic clearance of senescent cells reduces calcification in atherosclerosic and hypercholesterolemic vascular models provide a compelling rationale for extending this approach to valvular targets.

title: Systematic review of the current landscape and imaging-based definition of septic cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Sivapathan S, Gerhardy B, Pathan F, Thomas L, Orde S, Negishi K.

journal.title: Journal of the Intensive Care Society

abstractText:
Background

Septic cardiomyopathy (SCM) has no current unified definition, although it can be associated with significant mortality. It encompasses a wide spectrum of cardiac dysfunction ranging from mild to severe systolic and/or diastolic dysfunction of the left and/or right ventricle. The objective of this review is to evaluate the imaging modalities and parameters used to define SCM and the clinical outcomes.

Methods

We conducted a systematic review of the literature, including studies up to August 2025, examining the impact of cardiac dysfunction, specifically related to the systolic and/or diastolic dysfunction of the left or right ventricle. We focussed on mortality and comparable phrases as the primary outcome. We considered all cardiac imaging methods. All relevant studies were identified in a search strategy including MEDLINE, Embase and Scopus.

Results

About 2669 articles were identified, of which 142 full-text publications were evaluated. Final analysis included 87 publications. Forty five articles provided a definition of SCM. Seventy studies used TTE. Eighteen studies associated LV dysfunction to mortality. Thirteen studies found an association between diastolic dysfunction or RV dysfunction and mortality. About 64% of the studies assessed cardiac function within 24-h of admission. Twenty eight studies re-assessed reversibility of cardiac dysfunction.

Interpretation

Cardiac dysfunction is commonly reported in the critically ill septic population. There was considerable heterogeneity with regards to the diagnostic criteria of SCM, parameters used to determine cardiac dysfunction, outcomes evaluated, timing of study or assessing reversibility. Given the high prevalence of cardiac dysfunction in sepsis, a unified assessment and definition of SCM is needed.

title: Protective effects of oligomeric bioactive peptides against atherosclerosis in an atherogenic diet-induced mouse model.
authorString: Marasinghe CK, Dayarathne LA, Je JY.
abstractText: This study investigated the anti-atherosclerotic potential of two blue mussel-derived bioactive peptides, PIISVYWK (P1) and FSVVPSPK (P2), using an atherogenic diet (AD)-induced mouse model. Administration of both peptides significantly attenuated atherosclerotic lesion development and markedly improved serum lipid profiles, as evidenced by reductions in low-density lipoprotein (LDL), total cholesterol (TC), and triglyceride (TG) levels, along with an increase in high-density lipoprotein (HDL) concentrations. Mechanistic investigations revealed that P1 and P2 upregulated ATP-binding cassette transporters A1 (ABCA1) and G1 (ABCG1) expression, consistent with enhanced cholesterol efflux while downregulating of cluster of differentiation 36 (CD36) and scavenger receptor class A1 (SR-A1) suggesting reduced cholesterol uptake. Furthermore, both peptides were associated with reduced lectin-like oxidized low-density lipoprotein receptor-1 (LOX-1) expression and increased endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) expression which is responsible for endothelial protection. The peptides also reduced intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1) and vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (VCAM-1) consistent with attenuated vascular inflammation. In addition, treatment with P1 and P2 improved hepatic function, as demonstrated by reduced serum levels of aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT). Collectively, these findings highlight the therapeutic potential of P1 and P2 as promising bioactive agents for the prevention and management of atherosclerosis.

title: Evaluation of an Echocardiography-Based Artificial Intelligence Algorithm for Early HFpEF Detection: A HeartShare/AMP-HF Cohort Study.
authorString: Ahmad FS, Usman MS, Karnik A, Segar MW, Subramanian V, Upton R, Akerman AP, Keshvani N, Freed BH, Shah AM, Patel RB, Chandra A, Willett D, Bertoni A, Butler J, Shah S, Luo Y, Shah S, Pandey A.
abstractText:
Background

Early heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is difficult to identify because of nonspecific symptoms and subtle echocardiographic abnormalities. EchoGo HF, an FDA-cleared artificial intelligence (AI) model, estimates HFpEF probability from a single apical 4-chamber echocardiographic clip, but has been validated only in patients with clinically adjudicated HFpEF.

Objectives

This study aims to evaluate whether AI-HFpEF can detect early HFpEF in community-dwelling adults without a clinical heart failure (HF) diagnosis and predict incident clinical HFpEF in patients within a health system.

Methods

The authors included 2 community cohorts (the MESA [Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis] Early HF study and the DHMS [Dallas Hearts and Minds Study]). Early HFpEF was defined by impaired exercise capacity or health-related quality of life with objective evidence of elevated cardiac filling pressures in patients without clinically diagnosed HF. The AI-HFpEF model was applied to resting echocardiograms, and the diagnostic performance was assessed. Multivariable models examined associations between AI-HFpEF output and early HFpEF phenotype. Separately, we included adults in the UTSW (University of Texas Southwestern) Health System with structurally normal echocardiograms and no prior HF (2018-2024) and assessed the association of AI-HFpEF output with incident HFpEF (adjudicated using a validated registry) using Cox regression.

Results

In MESA (N = 2,544; 8.3% early HFpEF), AI-HFpEF outperformed H2FPEF for detecting early HFpEF (area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve [AUROC]: 0.77 vs 0.70). AI-HFpEF diagnostic positivity was associated with higher odds of early HFpEF (OR: 3.26; P < 0.001), lower 6-minute walk distance, and lower Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-12-Clinical Summary Score. Similarly, in DHMS (N = 624; 18.6% early HFpEF), AI-HFpEF outperformed H2FPEF (AUROC: 0.83 vs 0.77), and diagnostic positivity was associated with early HFpEF (OR: 6.76; P < 0.001), shorter exercise duration, and lower peak oxygen uptake. In the UTSW cohort (N = 6,876; median follow-up = 33 months; incident HFpEF = 3.4%), an AI-HFpEF diagnostic positive result was associated with >2-fold higher incident HFpEF risk (aHR: 2.08; P < 0.001). This association persisted across all conventional diastolic dysfunction grades.

Conclusions

AI-HFpEF identified the early HFpEF phenotype in community-dwelling adults and independently predicted incident clinical HFpEF among patients in a health system.

title: Acute-on-Chronic Upper Limb Ischemia Precipitated by Critical Right Brachiocephalic Stenosis.
authorString: Jha A, Etta I, Burnette S, Ali M, Buhari C, Punnam S.
abstractText:
Background

Brachiocephalic artery stenosis is an uncommon cause of upper extremity ischemia and cerebrovascular insufficiency. Diagnosis may be delayed because of subtle clinical manifestations, particularly in patients with established atherosclerotic risk factors.

Case presentation

A 73-year-old woman with diabetes, dyslipidemia, and active tobacco use presented with progressive bluish discoloration and pain of the right-hand digits. The primary care physician initially misattributed the presentation to Buerger disease. Angiography revealed critical ostial brachiocephalic artery stenosis, and prompt endovascular stenting showed improvement in digital perfusion and eventual resolution of symptoms.

Discussion

This case highlights the potential for isolated upper extremity digital ischemia to represent proximal great vessel disease, especially among high-risk smokers. Careful examination and imaging are important for avoiding a missed diagnosis. Smoking cessation remains essential for long-term protection.

Take-home message

Detailed examination and interarm blood pressure measurement should be routinely performed in patients with unexplained upper-extremity ischemia to identify potential proximal great-vessel disease.

title: Mechanisms of Resistance and Immune-Related Adverse Events Associated with Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Narrative Review.
authorString: Li J, Zhou JY, Yu Y, Chen XM, Luo WL, Lakang Y, Zuo JX, Yang ZS, Xu HB, Liang YB, Wang QB, Li YK, Shang LM, Ke Y.
abstractText: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but their clinical benefits are constrained by primary and acquired resistance and immune-related adverse events (irAEs). Understanding the biological processes underlying these outcomes is essential for improving treatment efficacy and safety. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on ICI resistance and irAEs in HCC across tumor-intrinsic, microenvironmental, and systemic dimensions. Primary resistance involves impaired tumor antigen presentation, dysregulated oncogenic signaling, limited immune-cell infiltration, metabolic immunosuppression, and systemic immune dysfunction, with additional influences from the gut microbiota and underlying liver disease. Acquired resistance may involve immunoediting and clonal escape, compensatory inhibitory checkpoint signaling, and treatment-associated immunosuppressive remodeling of the tumor microenvironment. Mechanisms potentially contributing to irAEs include loss of peripheral immune tolerance, T-cell-mediated tissue injury, dysregulated inflammatory cytokine production, antigenic cross-reactivity, and autoantibody-associated immune dysregulation. The strength of evidence varies substantially across these mechanisms: several are supported by experimental HCC models and clinical observations, whereas others remain largely extrapolated from non-HCC settings or lack causal validation. Future priorities include integrating baseline and longitudinal tumor and host immune profiling to develop predictive biomarkers, detect emerging resistance, and identify patients at increased risk of severe toxicity. Prospective HCC-specific studies are needed to determine whether mechanism-guided interventions can improve outcomes. A more precise understanding of antitumor immunity and tissue tolerance may inform individualized strategies that sustain tumor control while preserving liver function and minimizing immune-related toxicity.

title: Mapping the Intellectual Architecture of Inflammation-Centered Macrophage Research in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Dual-Database Bibliometric and Scientometric Analysis, 2005-2025.
authorString: Chai K, Chen C, Wu K, Zhao X.
abstractText:
Background

Chronic liver inflammation provides a major biological context for hepatocarcinogenesis, and macrophages link innate immune sensing, fibrogenesis, immune suppression and therapeutic resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), Kupffer cells and inflammation-associated myeloid populations have been extensively investigated in HCC; however, the intellectual structure and thematic connectivity of this inflammation-centered research field remain incompletely defined.

Objective

This study aimed to map the intellectual architecture, evolutionary trajectory and inter-module connectivity of inflammation-centered macrophage research in HCC using bibliometric and scientometric methods.

Methods

A total of 9218 English-language articles and reviews on macrophage-related HCC from 2005 to 2025 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus after systematic deduplication. CiteSpace, VOSviewer and bibliometrix were used to perform co-citation clustering, reference historiographic mapping, keyword co-occurrence analysis, publication-volume-adjusted keyword correlation analysis, citation burst detection, journal dual-map overlay and multi-level collaboration profiling.

Results

Annual publication output increased from 84 articles in 2005 to 1129 in 2025. Co-citation analysis resolved 13 well-defined clusters (modularity Q = 0.744; mean silhouette S = 0.884), and historiographic mapping identified four sequential stages: foundational inflammation and hepatocarcinogenesis, mechanistic expansion of TAM function, immune-regulatory convergence and spatial immunology. Keyword dynamics showed a transition from viral hepatitis, innate immunity, Kupffer cells and fibroinflammatory terminology toward TAM-mediated immune suppression, immunotherapy, single-cell analysis, SPP1-positive macrophage-associated spatial immune barriers and computational precision oncology. After annual publication-volume adjustment, the foundational viral-innate module and the contemporary computational-precision oncology module showed a negative inter-module Pearson correlation (mean r = -0.383), lower than expected under label-permutation and temporal-succession null models (both p < 0.001). Three low-connectivity literature interfaces emerged: etiology-immunotherapy, TAM-organized spatial immune exclusion and TAM-MDSC shared myeloid biology.

Conclusion

Macrophage-related HCC research has evolved from inflammation-centered hepatocarcinogenesis toward spatially resolved and computationally assisted immunology. The low-connectivity interfaces identified in this study should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating bibliometric signals rather than as evidence of biological or clinical disconnection or as stand-alone research priorities derived from network structure alone. Their potential translational relevance should be considered alongside published mechanistic and clinical evidence and requires future mechanistic, spatial and prospective clinical validation.

title: Addressing the burden and associated factors of undernutrition in under-five children with congenital heart disease in Pakistan: evidence from a multicenter cross-sectional study.
authorString: Khan MI, Haq IU, Awais M, Zakki SA, Akhtar S, Nabi MAG, Aboagarib EAA, Kolhar M, Huang X, Hu X.
abstractText:
Background

Children with congenital heart disease (CHD) are at heightened risk of undernutrition due to elevated metabolic demands, feeding intolerance, and growth failure. This study aimed to identify the associated factors of undernutrition among children under 5 years with CHD in Pakistan.

Methods

A hospital-based study was carried out among 197 confirmed CHD across three tertiary hospitals in Bannu, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP). WHO-recommended standards and structured questionnaires were used. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of undernutrition.

Results

Overall, 58.9% were male, 40.1% were stunted, 44.2% were underweight, and 35.5% were wasted. Ventricular septal defect was the most common CHD (34.5%), followed by patent ductus arteriosus (23.4%). Infants aged 6-11 months had the most severe deficits. Male children had significantly higher odds of wasting than female children (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 2.10, 95% CI: 1.10-3.98), whereas children from households with a monthly income of ≥ PKR 40,000 had lower odds of wasting (aOR = 0.45, 95% CI: 0.24-0.84) and underweight (aOR = 0.52, 95% CI: 0.29-0.94). Similarly, children whose fathers were government employees (aOR = 0.30, 95% CI: 0.09-0.98) also had lower odds of being underweight. No sociodemographic or clinical variables were significantly associated with stunting (all p > 0.05).

Conclusion

Undernutrition exhibits a high distribution and severity among young CHD children. Multiple associated factors of undernutrition based on wasting and underweight were identified. Timely referrals for nutritional support are of great significance in preventing nutritional deterioration.

title: Maladaptive Liver Regeneration in Chronic Liver Disease: Cellular Mechanisms Linking Ductular Reaction, Parenchymal Extinction, and Extracellular Matrix Remodelling.
authorString: Szymonik M, Krasucka N, Krupa M, Małek D, Płaza-Kościańczuk J, Kleinrok J, Pająk W, Rusztyn K, Mazur M, Korolczuk A.
abstractText: Chronic liver disease is characterised not only by persistent injury and fibrosis, but also by a progressive shift from adaptive hepatocyte-driven repair toward maladaptive tissue remodelling. Although liver regeneration is often discussed as a compensatory response, chronic injury may render this process structurally and functionally dysregulated, thereby promoting architectural distortion, fibrosis progression, and a microenvironment permissive for hepatocarcinogenesis. In this narrative review, we propose that this transition can be interpreted through three interconnected, histopathology-anchored endpoints: ductular reaction, extracellular matrix remodelling, and parenchymal extinction. We discuss ductular reaction as a progenitor niche phenotype that emerges when effective hepatocyte regeneration is impaired and becomes increasingly linked to portal inflammation, fibrogenic signalling, and altered cell-matrix interactions. We then examine extracellular matrix remodelling as a central tissue-level process involving activated stellate cells, portal fibroblasts, macrophages, cholangiocytes, and dysfunctional endothelial cells, resulting in collagen accumulation, increased stiffness, fibrous septa formation, and progressive reorganization of the hepatic microenvironment. Finally, we address parenchymal extinction as a morphological endpoint of often-irreversible or incompletely reversible hepatocyte loss accompanied by microvascular injury, ischaemia, and fibrotic replacement, contributing directly to architectural collapse and disease advancement. Rather than representing isolated phenomena, these three processes form a biologically integrated remodelling axis that links failed regeneration with fibrosis progression and malignant transformation. By framing chronic liver disease through these assessable histologic endpoints, this review aims to provide a more coherent pathology-oriented model of progression and to highlight mechanisms that may improve tissue-based risk stratification and future translational research.

title: Proton Pump Inhibitors and the Gut Microbiota: From Mechanisms to Clinical Implications.
authorString: Deutschbein F, Severino A, Ferrari M, Capuano E, Fusco W, Varca S, Rondinella D, Galasso T, Porcari S, Gasbarrini A, Ianiro G.
abstractText: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are among the most widely used drugs in clinical practice. Although generally effective and well tolerated, their widespread and frequently prolonged use has raised concerns about both gastrointestinal and systemic adverse effects. Some of these effects may be directly or indirectly mediated by proton-pump-inhibitor-induced alterations of the gut microbiota. Proton pump inhibitors can reshape gastrointestinal microbial communities through multiple mechanisms, including gastric acid suppression, impaired barrier function, and modulation of the immune and metabolic pathways. The resulting dysbiosis promotes oral-to-gut microbial translocation, reduces microbial diversity, and favors the expansion of potentially pathogenic taxa. These alterations have been associated with several gastrointestinal disorders such as small intestinal bacterial overgrowth, enteric infections, and disturbances of the gut-liver axis, while emerging evidence suggests broader implications for carcinogenesis and the response to immune checkpoint inhibitors. In this context, microbiota-modulating interventions, including probiotics, may provide clinical benefits; however, the current evidence remains limited and inconsistent, precluding their routine use. By integrating mechanistic and clinical evidence, this review aims to clarify the role of the gut microbiota in proton-pump-inhibitor-related adverse effects and to assess the potential of microbiota-targeted strategies to mitigate their clinical consequences.

title: Fontan-associated liver disease: a Croatian national experience and current clinical practice.
authorString: Šeša V, Marić Bešić K, Ćutić B, Domislović V, Ivanac Vranešić I, Košuta I, Martinčić P, Miličić D, Sremac M, Mrzljak A.
abstractText:
Aim

To assess the characteristics of patients with Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD) and its clinical correlates within contemporary multidisciplinary practice at the national tertiary referral center in Croatia.

Methods

This cross-sectional study included all adult patients with Fontan circulation followed at University Hospital Centre Zagreb between 2023 and 2025. Data from the most recent comprehensive cardiology and hepatology evaluation were analyzed. Liver assessment included laboratory testing, transient elastography, and structured imaging surveillance with alternating ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging. Advanced FALD was defined as liver stiffness measurement (LSM)>22 kPa combined with indirect markers of portal hypertension.

Results

The study enrolled 37 adults (median age 24 years; 64.9% male), with a median of 21 years since Fontan completion. The median LSM was 18.5 kPa (interquartile range 14.6-23.1), and 27% of participants had LSM>22 kPa. Thrombocytopenia was present in 40.5% of patients. LSM was moderately negatively correlated with platelet count (Spearman's ρ=-0.490, P=0.0038). Conventional liver biochemistry was only mildly abnormal in most patients. One patient (2.7%) was diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma during surveillance and treated with locoregional therapy.

Conclusion

FALD is common and clinically heterogeneous in adults with long-standing Fontan circulation, frequently affecting young patients decades after surgery. Conventional laboratory markers alone may underestimate disease severity. These findings support structured, multidisciplinary surveillance in this complex population. This first national experience from Croatia contributes region-specific data to the growing body of evidence on FALD.

title: Complete Heart Block in Young Patient With Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Case Report.
authorString: Sok S, Meth L, Phum C, Nhem S, Sok P, Chan S, Sok C.
abstractText: Complete heart block is a rare but serious cardiac complication of systemic lupus erythematosus. Most reported cases present with symptoms such as syncope. In this report, we describe the case of a 33-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus who was diagnosed with asymptomatic Complete heart block. This case highlights the importance of proactive cardiac evaluation, including a baseline electrocardiogram, in systemic lupus erythematosus patients to detect clinically silent conduction defects that may carry a risk of sudden cardiac death.

title: Effects of strength training on isometric muscle strength and muscle cross-sectional area in adults with a Fontan circulation: a pilot study.
authorString: Wikner A, Bergman F, Rinnström D, Johansson K, Ljungberg J, Johansson B, Sandberg C.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Int J Cardiol Congenit Heart Dis
journal.title: International journal of cardiology. Congenital heart disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Int J Cardiol Congenit Heart Dis

abstractText:
Background

Adults with complex congenital heart disease, particularly those with a Fontan circulation, often have impaired muscle strength and reduced muscle mass from early age. Despite these concerns, data regarding the effects of strength training in this population is limited.

Aim

To evaluate the impact of a 10-week strength training intervention on muscle strength and muscle cross-sectional area (CSA) in adults with Fontan circulation, compared to age- and sex matched controls.

Methods

Nine adults with a Fontan circulation (median age 28.9 [IQR: 23.4-35.0], 4 women) underwent a gym-based strength training program.
