Isometric muscle strength (elbow flexion, knee extension, grip strength), radial and tibial muscle CSA and density, and habitual physical activity (accelerometer-based and self-reported data) were measured pre- and post-intervention. Within-group changes were analysed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test; between-group differences were assessed using the Mann Whitney U test.

Results

Both patients and controls demonstrated improvements in isometric elbow flexion strength (Patients: +6.2% [IQR: 2.8-17.7], p = 0.02, r = 0.77; Controls: +8.4% [IQR: 2.9-16.0], p = 0.012, r = 0.84) and tibial cross-sectional area (Patients: +5.0% [IQR: 2.7-11.4], p = 0.011, r = 0.85; Controls: +4.0% [IQR: 1.4-7.4], p = 0.018, r = 0.89). No changes were observed in isometric knee extension or grip strength. There were no differences between groups, and no adverse events occurred.

Conclusion

This pilot study supports that strength training is safe and effective in improving muscle strength and muscle CSA in adults with a Fontan circulation. Despite the small sample size these findings are reassuring. However, confirmation in larger prospective trials is warranted.

Clinicaltrialsgov id

NCT05454254, https://clinicaltrials.gov.

title: Procedural Sedation in Pediatric Gastroenterology: A Narrative Review from the Shared Perspective of Pediatric Gastroenterology and Anesthesiology.
authorString: Cesur S, Uyar Aksu N, Uncuoğlu A, Çardaközü T, İçli D.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Endoscopic and interventional procedures in pediatric gastroenterology are increasing in number and complexity, and most require sedation or, in selected cases, general anesthesia (GA); children face a higher risk of serious sedation-related adverse events than adults. Written jointly by pediatric gastroenterologists and anesthesiologists, this review provides a practical, evidence-referenced framework for procedural sedation across pediatric gastrointestinal procedures. Methods: We performed a narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE (inception to 20 June 2026, the date of the final search), prioritizing society guidelines, systematic reviews, randomized controlled trials, and large registries on pediatric procedural sedation, sedative agents, capnography, and high-flow nasal oxygen (HFNO). Results: Sedation should be matched to the procedure and to a structured risk tier, targeting the lightest depth that allows safe completion. Propofol-, ketamine-, and dexmedetomidine-based regimens dominate; remimazolam and esketamine are emerging, but pediatric data are limited. Capnography detects hypoventilation before desaturation, and HFNO reduces hypoxemia in adults, whereas pediatric-specific evidence remains limited and the pediatric subgroup analysis did not reach statistical significance. Higher-risk groups require tailored planning, monitoring, and rescue readiness; most evidence is observational or extrapolated from adults. Conclusions: Safe pediatric gastrointestinal sedation combines structured risk assessment, rational drug combinations, capnography-supported monitoring, and consistent complication reporting. Who administers deep sedation, and whether general anesthesia is preferred, should depend on patient and procedural risk together with local regulations, institutional policy, training and credentialing, and rescue capability, within a shared gastroenterology-anesthesiology framework. Adequately powered pediatric trials of HFNO and of remimazolam/esketamine, and long-term neurodevelopmental follow-up, are priorities.

title: Development of a Nomogram Model for Predicting Mortality Risk in Critically Ill Children with Influenza.
authorString: Ye Y, Zhang Z, Chen J, Sun H, Bai Z, Zhou W, Jiang Y.
abstractText:
Background

Influenza virus commonly infects children. Children with critical infection may develop influenza-associated encephalopathy or encephalitis, conditions rarely seen in adults and associated with high mortality. This results in growing healthcare resource consumption and family burden.

Objective

This study aimed to identify the predictors for death in critically ill children with influenza, so as to facilitate early recognition of high-risk patients, guide clinical interventions, and reduce mortality.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed the clinical data of critically ill children with influenza admitted to the Children's Hospital of Soochow University between January 2018 and January 2026. L1-penalized binomial logistic regression (LASSO) was used for variable selection. Variables selected by LASSO were entered into a Firth penalized logistic regression model to identify independent predictors of mortality, based on which a nomogram was constructed to estimate mortality risk. Model discrimination was assessed using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and area under the curve (AUC). Bootstrap resampling was performed for internal validation and optimism correction. Model calibration was assessed using calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA) was performed to evaluate the clinical net benefit of the model.

Results

A total of 113 critically ill children with influenza were included, of whom 34 died, corresponding to a mortality rate of 30.1%. LASSO regression was used for variable selection, followed by Firth penalized logistic regression to develop a mortality risk prediction model. The final model included five variables: Hgb, PLT, UREA, ALB, and confusion. A mortality risk nomogram was developed based on these five predictors and internally validated using bootstrap resampling. The ROC curve showed good discrimination of the nomogram in internal validation. The calibration curve demonstrated good agreement between the predicted probabilities and observed outcomes. DCA showed that the nomogram provided a higher net benefit across a certain range of threshold probabilities, indicating its potential clinical utility.

Conclusions

Hgb, PLT, UREA, ALB, and confusion are important predictors of mortality in critically ill children with influenza. The nomogram developed based on these predictors showed good discrimination and calibration, as well as potential clinical net benefit, and may serve as an adjunctive tool for early identification of mortality risk and clinical decision-making in critically ill children with influenza.

title: Altered Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cell (PBMC) Mitochondrial Coupling and Complex IV Respiration in Severe Aortic Stenosis Before and After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR).
authorString: Marchandot B, Charles AL, Demir K, Momas C, Talha S, Kindo M, Ohlmann P, Giannini M, Meyer A, Morel O, Geny B.

journal.title: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease

abstractText:
Background

Circulating peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) mitochondrial respiration is impaired in heart failure and transplanted patients. Severe aortic stenosis (AS), characterized by pressure overload leading to cardiac mitochondrial dysfunction, might also be associated with PBMC mitochondrial respiration alterations, likely related to systemic inflammation and left heart hypertrophy and diastolic dysfunction.

Population and methods

We determined PBMC mitochondrial respiration by high-resolution respirometry (Oroboros Instruments) in 9 healthy subjects and 25 AS patients before and until 30 days after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and investigated potential correlates with the clinical, biological and echocardiographic characteristics of the patients.

Results

AS patients with a transaortic valvular gradient of 45 mm Hg were older and demonstrated slightly impaired renal function, inflammation markers, increased brain natriuretic peptide, left ventricular hypertrophy, and impaired diastolic function. PBMC mitochondrial coupling was decreased in the AS patients compared to controls (2.12 ± 0.10 vs. 2.76 ± 0.17, p = 0.003) and mitochondrial complex IV respiration was increased (31.07 ± 2.84 vs. 18.69 ± 2.09, p = 0.017). TAVR did not modify the alterations. Interestingly, increased complex IV mitochondrial respiration was associated with reduced mortality (p < 0.01).

Conclusions

Severe aortic stenosis is associated with bioenergetic remodeling of circulating mononuclear cells that were not significantly associated with valvular hemodynamic impairment and ventricular function, before and after the mechanical relief of afterload. Nevertheless, future studies will be useful to determine whether such systemic immuno-metabolic phenotype, particularly PBMC mitochondrial complex IV respiration stimulation, may contribute to reduce the risk following TAVR.

title: The Intersection of Psychological Distress, Cardiovascular Health, and Allostatic Load in Occupational Settings: Implications for Preventive Medicine, Occupational Health, and Clinical Management.
authorString: Park EKC, Park WH, Jeon EY.
abstractText: Background: The clinical and epidemiological literature establishes a clear link between modern occupational environments and human health, highlighting a significant intersection between psychological distress, ethical dilemmas, and physiological dysregulation. This review evaluates the biological, psychological, and occupational pathways linking workplace distress to Cardiovascular Disease (CVD) through a multidisciplinary preventive medicine lens, while also emphasizing its relevance for occupational health, public health policy, and clinical management. Methods: To achieve this, a comprehensive narrative literature search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases to identify relevant peer-reviewed studies published up to August 2026. By utilizing the allostatic load model, this paper explores how chronic activation of the Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Adrenal (HPA) axis and persistent systemic inflammation serve as primary biological mediators bridging psychological exposure and physical disease. Attention is given to how sociodemographic vulnerabilities-including racial and gender disparities-exacerbate these risks. We concurrently examine the lived experiences of patients navigating chronic cardiac disease and the distinct ethical burdens faced by healthcare professionals and medical trainees. Results: This synthesis holds significant clinical value by supporting a potential shift from reactive CVD treatments toward comprehensive preventive strategies that address the psychosocial components of physiological wear-and-tear. Specifically, we emphasize targeted health education and cognitive-behavioral interventions integrated within comprehensive clinical and organizational frameworks. By elucidating the molecular mechanisms, broader clinical realities, and structural implications of occupational stress, this comprehensive review informs proactive clinical and occupational interventions. Conclusions: Ultimately, addressing psychological distress within the workplace is essential for mitigating the global burden of cardiovascular morbidity. This approach narrows persistent health disparities and advances the integration of psychology and public health into modern clinical practice.

title: Transcatheter atrial septal defect closure in infants weighing 3 to 6 kg with clinically significant bronchopulmonary dysplasia.
authorString: Mejia E, Taylor AC, Bocks ML, Berman DP.

title: Unhealthy Digital Marketing Among Aboriginal People in Australia: Findings From the #DigitalMob Pilot Study.
authorString: Browne J, Lister N, Backholer K, Hill K, Crocetti A, Walker T, Atkinson-Briggs S, Pathirana NL, Cubillo B, Martino F, Sherriff S, Yeomans L, Mitchell F, Thow S, Nguyen P, Ananthapavan J, Allender S, Paradies Y.

journal.title: Health promotion journal of Australia : official journal of Australian Association of Health Promotion Professionals

abstractText:
Issue addressed

This study aimed to quantify Aboriginal adults' exposure to digital marketing of unhealthy food and beverages, alcohol, gambling, tobacco and e-cigarettes; analyse demographic differences in marketing exposure; and describe the nature of digital marketing reaching Aboriginal audiences, including brands, platforms and marketing tactics.

Methods

Thirty-one Aboriginal adults were asked to record their screens, capturing approximately one-third of their usual daily screen time (maximum 60 min). Recordings were analysed using SCANNER, an automated system trained to detect unhealthy commodity marketing. Demographic data and usual online behaviours were collected via an online survey. Descriptive statistics, a post hoc Mann-Whitney U test and a Fisher-Freeman-Halton extension of Fisher's Exact test were used to analyse differences in marketing detections.

Results

Most participants (n = 29/31, 94%) were exposed to unhealthy digital marketing. Of the 587 marketing instances detected, unhealthy food brands were most common (47%), followed by gambling (28%), alcohol (15%), sweetened beverages (9%) and tobacco (1%). No e-cigarette marketing was detected. Estimated daily exposure to unhealthy digital marketing was 40.4 (IQR: 11-92) instances per day. Male participants, aged 30 years and under, recorded significantly more marketing detections overall and for unhealthy food, alcohol and gambling brands.

Conclusion

Findings highlight the pervasiveness of unhealthy food and beverage, gambling and alcohol marketing in the everyday digital lives of Aboriginal participants. SO WHAT?: Comprehensive regulation of unhealthy digital marketing is urgently required to advance Aboriginal health.

title: Effect of Blonanserin on Neurotrophic Factors in Patients With Non-Responsive First-Episode Schizophrenia Treated With Early Risperidone Monotherapy-A Randomized Controlled Trial.
authorString: Wei Y, Liu Y, Cai L, Li J, Zheng D, Fu H, Wang S, Huang G.

journal.title: International journal of methods in psychiatric research

abstractText:
Objective

To investigate the efficacy of Blonanserin in patients with schizophrenia who were refractory to Risperidone monotherapy and its effects on various neurotrophic factors.

Methods

A total of 120 patients with first-episode schizophrenia who were hospitalized in our hospital from January 2022 to December 2023 and did not respond to early Risperidone monotherapy were selected as the study participants. They were randomly divided into a control group and a research group, with 60 cases in each group. The control group was treated with Clozapine, and the research group was treated with Blonanserin for 3 months. The scores of the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS), the scores of the Generic Quality of Life Inventory (GQOLI-74), the serum brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), the serum S100β protein, the neuron-specific enolase (NSE), and the Neuregulin-1 (NRG1) levels of the two groups were compared, and the adverse drug reactions of patients were recorded.

Results

After 3 months of treatment, the PANSS scores of both groups decreased compared with those before treatment, and the PANSS scores of the research group were lower. The scores of physical function, social function, and psychological function of the two groups were higher than those before treatment, and the scores of the research group were higher than those of the control group. The differences were statistically significant (p < 0.05 for all). The serum BDNF and NRG1 levels of the two groups were higher than those before treatment, and those of the research group were higher than those of the control group. The S100β and NSE levels of the two groups were lower than those before treatment, and those of the research group were lower than those of the control group. The differences were statistically significant (p < 0.05 for all). No serious adverse reactions occurred in both groups. Most patients with adverse reactions could tolerate them or improved after symptomatic treatment.

Conclusion

Blonanserin can effectively relieve the symptoms of schizophrenia and improve the quality of life of first-episode schizophrenia patients who have failed to respond to Risperidone monotherapy in the early stage. Due to the short follow-up time and small sample size of this study, further prospective multicenter studies should be carried out in the future to observe the long-term treatment effect and provide more favorable reference for clinical practice.

title: The Patient Perspectives of Clinical Pharmacist Services in Hospitals and Clinics: A Focused Narrative Review of Qualitative Studies.
authorString: Henriksen BT, Gillespie U, Mathiesen L, Andersson Y.
abstractText: Patient perspectives are highly important to ensure optimal patient care in hospitals or primary care settings. Clinical pharmacy services, in which clinical pharmacists provide direct patient care, are a relatively recent addition to healthcare and are increasing in scope and availability. In this focused narrative review, relevant qualitative studies describing patients' perspectives after the integration of clinical pharmacists into healthcare services were included. Patients described predominantly positive feedback, presented as facilitators. The facilitators described in studies were that patients felt safe, experienced clear communication and collaboration with pharmacists, increased their knowledge of medications, and appreciated pharmacists' time and availability. Occasionally, patients described challenges with the pharmacist or service, presented as barriers. The barriers were that patients were unfamiliar with the clinical pharmacists' role and services, lacked trust or experienced conflicting information, experienced a lack of patient-centredness, and some disagreed or had challenges with elements of the intervention. In conclusion, most perspectives represented positive facilitators that should be kept and protected in the future, with some barriers that can be overcome in the future for optimal patient care and development of clinical pharmacy services.

title: Cutaneous Adverse Events With Semaglutide: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
authorString: Ganjre S, Borah L, Khardenavis A.

title: MicroRNAs, Nut Consumption, Cardiovascular Risk Factors, and Coronary Artery Disease: A Narrative Review.
authorString: Stein E, Duarte GBS, Bersch-Ferreira AC, Weschenfelder C, Figueiro MF, Rogero MM, de Abreu-Silva EO, Marcadenti A.
abstractText: Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide and has a multifactorial etiology involving genetic, metabolic, and behavioral factors. Hypertension and dyslipidemia contribute significantly to atherosclerosis progression, and these conditions may be influenced by microRNAs (miRNAs), which act as post-transcriptional gene expression regulators. In turn, miRNA expression can be modulated by nutrient-dense dietary patterns or cardioprotective foods, such as nuts. Despite growing interest in miRNAs and cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk, few reviews have specifically addressed the unique role of nuts in modulating miRNA expression, particularly regarding gaps in secondary prevention of CAD. This study summarizes the main miRNAs associated with blood pressure, lipid metabolism, and atherosclerotic disease, as well as the current evidence on how nut consumption influences their expression. Several miRNAs, including miR-1, miR-21, the miR-29 family, miR-30a/b, miR-133, miR-143, miR-145, and miR-221/222, are dysregulated in hypertension and associated with circadian blood pressure patterns, left ventricular hypertrophy, and antihypertensive response. Others, such as miR-122, miR-33a/b, miR-148a, miR-483-5p, and miR-145, are linked to lipid metabolism, plaque instability, and ischemic outcomes. Nut-rich diets, particularly the Mediterranean diet, seem to modulate miRNAs associated with pathways involved in lipid homeostasis, endothelial function, and inflammation. Data from clinical trials conducted in primary CVD prevention setting have shown changes in circulating miRNAs in response to diets rich in nuts. Additional studies with Brazil nuts, pistachios, almonds, and walnuts supplementation also reported modulation of miRNAs involved in lipid homeostasis, inflammation, and insulin resistance, including significant changes in expression of miR-15a, miR-21, miR-328, miR-454-3p, miR-29a-3p, miR-192, miR-330-3p, miR-32-5p, miR-29b-3p, and miR-551a. Nonetheless, it appears no studies have yet evaluated the effect of nut supplementation on miRNAs in secondary prevention of CAD. Although the evidence is promising, more research is needed to clarify the impact of nut consumption on miRNA modulation, particularly in secondary prevention of CVD.

title: Eltrombopag during induction chemotherapy in older patients with newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia is safe and reduces platelet transfusion requirements: The EPAG-2015 French Innovative Leukemia Organization phase 2 randomized trial.
authorString: Pigneux A, Dumas PY, Bernard M, Vey N, Bidet A, Mineur A, Schmidt A, Carré M, Ojeda M, Bertoli S, Banos A, Peterlin P, Guièze R, Desbrosses Y, Guepin GR, Simand C, Leguay T, Gyan E, Jourdan E, Vial JP, Marchand T, Hicheri Y, Béné MC, Hamel JF, Récher C.
abstractText:
Background

Elderly patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) treated with intensive chemotherapy are at risk of developing thrombopenia, which requires platelet transfusions. It would be interesting to provide them with thrombopoietin receptor agonists such as eltrombopag.

Methods

The EPAG-2015 multicenter phase 2 trial (18 French hospitals from October 2018 to June 2021) blindly randomized elderly patients (aged ≥60 years) with placebo or eltrombopag administered on Day 11 after induction chemotherapy and continued until AML response evaluation (Day 45) or a platelet count of >100 × 109/L. A cohort of 110 patients with a median age of 70 years was included and randomized (55 per arm) to receive placebo or eltrombopag.

Results

After induction, 90 patients (81.8%) achieved complete response (CR) or CR with incomplete reconstitution (CRi) (45 in each group), including 74 patients with CR (38 with eltrombopag and 36 with placebo). With a median follow-up for alive patients of 20.9 months the primary objective was not reached, given that there was no difference in overall survival (hazard ratio, 1.59; 95% CI, 0.65-3.89; p = .31). Eltrombopag, however, did not lead to increased grade 3/4 adverse events, and was associated with a lower median number of platelet transfusions (eight; interquartile range [IQR], 6-14; vs. 10; IQR, 7-14; i.e., a 20% benefit).

Conclusions

This study failed to demonstrate a survival advantage after eltrombopag addition, at variance with previous reports, but shows that initiating eltrombopag after chemotherapy washout is feasible and safe, and resulted in a decreased need for platelet transfusions.

title: Effects of a Nurse-Led Multicomponent Exercise Intervention for Haemodialysis Patients With Possible or Confirmed Sarcopenia: A Cluster Randomised Trial.
authorString: Cai G, Zhang L, Zhang Y, Zhang J, Zhou J, Zhan B, Guo Q, Ying J.
abstractText:
Aims

To assess the potential effects, safety and feasibility of a nurse-led multicomponent exercise intervention on skeletal muscle function and quality of life in haemodialysis patients with possible or confirmed sarcopenia.

Design

A cluster randomised trial with clusters defined by fixed haemodialysis schedules.

Methods

A total of 56 eligible participants were enrolled and allocated through cluster randomisation. The intervention group (n = 28) received a 12-week nurse-led multicomponent exercise intervention in addition to standard care, whereas the control group (n = 28) received standard care. The primary outcomes included skeletal muscle mass index (SMI), handgrip strength, gait speed and short physical performance battery (SPPB) scores. Secondary outcomes included scores on the Kidney Disease Quality of Life 36-Item Short-Form Survey (KDQOL-36) and C-reactive protein levels. Handgrip strength, gait speed, SPPB scores and KDQOL-36 scores were assessed at baseline and at Weeks 4, 8 and 12 during the intervention period, whereas SMI and C-reactive protein were assessed at baseline and Week 12. An intention-to-treat analysis was employed, and the effects of the intervention were evaluated using linear mixed models.

Results

Of the 56 participants, 50 completed the study. The intervention group showed favourable trends in handgrip strength, gait speed and SPPB scores, with moderate-to-large effect sizes; however, these differences were not statistically significant after Bonferroni correction. Furthermore, no significant between-group differences were found in skeletal muscle mass index, health-related quality of life, or C-reactive protein levels. No serious intervention-related adverse events were reported.

Conclusions

The nurse-led multicomponent exercise intervention was safe and feasible and showed favourable trends in muscle strength and physical function, although statistically significant between-group differences were not retained after correction for multiple comparisons.

Implications for patient care

A nurse-led, multicomponent exercise intervention may have the potential to increase muscle strength and physical function in haemodialysis patients with possible or confirmed sarcopenia.

Impact

What problem did the study address? This study assessed the potential effects, safety, and feasibility of a nurse-led, multicomponent exercise intervention designed for haemodialysis patients with possible or confirmed sarcopenia. What were the main findings? A nurse-led exercise intervention appeared safe and feasible and may help to improve muscle strength and physical function in haemodialysis patients with possible or confirmed sarcopenia. However, future studies with larger sample sizes and longer follow-up periods are needed to assess the long-term effects. Where and on whom will the research have an impact? The results of this study may inform the development and future implementation of nurse-led exercise interventions for haemodialysis patients with sarcopenia.

Patient and public contributions

Patients and family members were invited to collaborate with healthcare professionals in designing a nurse-led, multicomponent exercise intervention programme. Their contributions helped improve the feasibility and practicality of the exercise intervention.

Reporting method

The CONSORT 2025 checklist was used in the reporting of the study.

Trial registration

This trial was registered at www.chictr.org.cn (registration number: ChiCTR2200065863).

title: The Effect of Implementing Orem's Self-Care Model on Balance and Fatigue in Patients With Diabetic Neuropathy: A Clinical Trial.
authorString: Sadeghi A, Malekzadeh M, Dehbanizadeh A, Sadat SJ.
abstractText:
Aim

This study aims to determine the effect of applying Orem's self-care model on balance and fatigue in patients with diabetic neuropathy.

Design

Randomized clinical trial.

Methods

Seventy diabetic neuropathy patients referred to Shahid Mofateh Clinic, affiliated with Yasuj University of Medical Sciences (YUMS), were chosen for this clinical trial study via convenience sampling and randomly assigned to an intervention group (n = 35) or a control group (n = 35). The intervention group received care based on Orem's self-care model from a graduate nursing student over 2 months, followed by 1 month of self-care at home. The control group received no intervention. Both groups completed the research questionnaires (the Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory and the Berg Balance Test) at pretest and posttest. Data were analysed in SPSS version 27 using an ANCOVA test.

Results

Before the intervention, there were no significant between-group differences (p > 0.05). After the intervention, fatigue was significantly lower in the intervention group, with an adjusted mean difference of -9.40 points (95% CI: -11.09 to -7.71; p < 0.001; partial η2 = 0.647). Balance scores were significantly higher in the intervention group across low, mean, and high baseline levels, with adjusted mean differences of 7.01, 5.77, and 4.52 points, respectively (all p < 0.001). The group × baseline balance interaction was significant (F(1,66) = 5.69, p = 0.020; partial η2 = 0.079).

Implications for nursing

Nurses are recommended to apply Orem's self-care model as an effective structured intervention to reduce fatigue and improve balance in patients with diabetic neuropathy.

Patient or public contribution

Patients with diabetic peripheral neuropathy (diagnosed by an internist using TCSS) who participated in this randomized clinical trial evaluating Orem's self-care model effects on balance and fatigue.

title: Consequences of opioid exposure in disease-free cancer survivors: A systematic literature review.
authorString: Truong AM, Hong S, Brody ER, Pham D, Aduse-Poku L, Pontinha VM.

journal.title: Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy

abstractText:
Background

Chronic pain affects a substantial proportion of cancer survivors, and opioid therapy is commonly used to manage persistent symptoms. However, as survivors transition from active treatment to disease-free survivorship, the long-term consequences of persistent opioid exposure remain poorly characterized.

Objectives

To characterize the consequences of opioid exposure after curative-intent treatment in disease-free cancer survivors, focusing on outcomes including survival, recurrence, opioid-related harms, opioid use disorder (OUD), and health care resource use (HRU).

Methods

A systematic literature review was conducted, and MEDLINE and Embase were searched (January 2009-October 2024) for studies evaluating opioid exposure in cancer survivors and its association with survival, recurrence, opioid-related harms, OUD, and HRU.

Results

Thirteen observational studies were included, with substantial variation in definitions of cancer survivorship and persistent opioid use. Findings regarding the association between survival and opioid exposure were mixed. Although some studies reported modest association with cancer recurrence among persistent opioid users, others reported no association at all. Opioid-related harm and health care use were the most frequently reported outcomes, which generally indicate higher risk among persistent opioid users. Only one study assessed association between persistent opioid exposure and OUD, which found no statistically significant association after adjustment for confounders.

Conclusions

Only 13 studies were reviewed, underscoring the limited and heterogeneous evidence on opioid use in disease-free cancer survivors and reflecting a high-priority knowledge gap. Although opioid exposure was consistently associated with higher risks of adverse drug events and greater HRU, findings for survival were mixed, including for cancer recurrence and OUD.

title: Identification of Issues Contributing to Longer Length of Stay and Higher Readmission Rates for Parkinson's Patients Admitted to Hospital.
authorString: Williams S, Dinh HM, Imbriotis V, Sargeant C, Lubomski M, Silberstein P, Prior SJ.
abstractText:
Background

People with Parkinson's disease (PD) are a vulnerable cohort of people, more likely to suffer serious health-related problems when admitted to hospital. Literature suggests that health service improvement utilising a robust health care redesign framework, can improve local service delivery and outcomes for hospitalised PD patients.

Aim/objectives

This healthcare redesign project aims to identify the issues that contribute to PD patients experiencing a longer length of stay (LOS) and (re)admitting to a tertiary hospital in Sydney, Australia. Quantitative analysis of hospital data previously identified comorbidities present on admission that impact LOS and acquired complications that significantly extend LOS. This paper demonstrates the benefits of utilising mixed methods to provide a comprehensive picture of the PD patient's inpatient experience.

Methods

Mixed-methods healthcare redesign diagnostic tools were used to gather evidence and understand the issues.

Results

Seventy-eight percent (n = 831) of PD patients admitted to the emergency department were triage category 1, 2 or 3. 58.5% of PD patients have their PD medications charted within 4 h of admission. Their average LOS was 13 days. Data triangulation identified several barriers to optimal care, with prioritisation activities identifying three high-impact, feasible targets for improvement: PD medication management during nil-by-mouth periods, timely medication charting and timely discharge planning. Root causes (lack of formalised care pathways, limited access to resources and poor coordination of PD services) were identified as contributing to PD patients experiencing a longer LOS and higher readmission rates. Poor communication between clinicians within the hospital, fragmented transitions between hospital and community services and limited access to specialist resources were identified as key system-level barriers requiring prioritisation in the subsequent redesign phase.

Conclusions

The use of mixed methods provided a rich understanding of the PD patient experience of a hospital admission and prolonged length of stay. This study identified system-level barriers to optimal Parkinson's disease care, providing clear targets for service redesign to improve patient outcomes and hospital efficiency. Addressing gaps in Parkinson's disease medication management, discharge planning and interdisciplinary communication may improve inpatient outcomes, reduce avoidable complications and decrease hospital length of stay and readmissions.

Implications for nursing practice

Nurses play a critical role in advocating for and leading improvements in the quality, safety and efficiency of care for PD patients. This subsequently improves the PD patient's hospital experience. Nursing practice should focus on prioritising accurate and timely medication management, strengthening communication between clinicians to expedite discharge planning and advocating for PD-specific knowledge and education to improve patient outcomes, reduce length of stay and service efficiencies.

Patient and public contribution

Patients and members of the public were not involved in the design, conduct, analysis, reporting or dissemination of this healthcare redesign project.

title: LILRB4 Attenuates Ischemic Brain Injury by Inhibiting Microglial Necroptosis via a RIPK3-Dependent Mechanism.
authorString: Hu J, Zhang M, Liu P, Chen Y, Meng H, Xia S, Bao X, Xu Y, Chen Y.
abstractText: Microglia are central mediators of neuroinflammation following ischemic stroke. Our previous multi-omics data revealed significant upregulation of leukocyte immunoglobulin-like receptor subfamily B member 4 (LILRB4) in microglia after transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO), but its functional role remains unclear. This study demonstrates that LILRB4 expression peaks at 3 days post-tMCAO and is predominantly localized to microglia. Microglia-specific Lilrb4 knockout (Lilrb4-cKO) displayed worse neurological functions, larger infarct volumes, and more significant microglial activation. Transcriptomic analysis in vitro and functional experiments further revealed that microglial LILRB4 knockdown promoted the release of proinflammatory factors and enhanced necroptosis. Mechanistically, deletion of LILRB4 mainly drives receptor-interacting protein 3 (RIPK3) and mixed lineage kinase domain-like (MLKL) expression and phosphorylation, without affecting receptor-interacting protein 1 (RIPK1). Pharmacologic inhibition of RIPK3 can relieve the brain damage caused by LILRB4 knockout after stroke. Additional analysis showed that LILRB4 negatively regulates the stimulator of interferon genes (STING)/RIPK3 axis to limit microglial necroptosis. STING suppression blocked the hyperactivation of RIPK3 induced by LILRB4 deficiency. In conclusion, LILRB4 attenuates ischemic brain injury by suppressing STING/RIPK3-mediated microglial necroptosis and neuroinflammation, emphasizing its significance as a potential neuroprotective therapy.

title: Explainable temporal machine learning of multimorbidity trajectories after acute myocardial infarction: complementing clinical risk scores with mechanistic phenotypes.
authorString: Onoja A, Elomaa K, Whetton AD, Geifman N.

journal.title: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA

abstractText:
Objective

This study aimed to identify trajectories of multimorbidity following acute myocardial infarction (AMI), using explainable temporal machine-learning methods, and assess their clinical, prognostic, and biological significance.

Materials and methods

Dynamic Time Warping k-means clustering was applied to post-AMI diagnostic sequences from 12 701 UK-Biobank participants. Latent Dirichlet Allocation characterised cluster themes. Multiclass classifiers (CatBoost, XGBoost, random forest, logistic regression) trained on pre-AMI diagnoses and demographics predicted trajectory membership, with SHAP interpretability. SMART scores and Cox models evaluated 5-year mortality; Phenotype-Wide Association (PheWAS) and Reactome pathway enrichment were used to identify associated biological mechanisms.

Results

Three trajectories of multimorbidity were identified: acute cardiorenal-respiratory with metabolic disease (ACUTE-CARD; 63.4%), cardiometabolic disease with arrhythmic-ischemic burden (CARDIOMIX; 13.5%), and smoking-related multisystem multimorbidity (SMO-CARD; 23.1%). XGBoost achieved the highest discrimination (AUC-ROC 0.906; 95% CI, 0.895-0.916), with CatBoost showing comparable performance (AUC-ROC 0.900; 95% CI, 0.889-0.910). SMO-CARD had the highest 5-year mortality (43.9%). The established SMART cardiovascular risk score remained the dominant predictor of mortality while the identified trajectories provided complementary prognostic signals; these associations were weaker after full adjustment for potential confounders with each profile displaying distinct genetic and pathway signatures.

Discussion

The SMART score outperformed in capturing mortality risk, whereas the trajectories complement it by revealing nuanced clustering of risk factors across organ systems and in identifying trajectory-specific intervention priorities.

Conclusion

Explainable temporal modeling of EHR data reveals clinically interpretable, biologically grounded multimorbidity trajectories after AMI that complement established risk scores and provide a reproducible approach to mechanistic phenotyping and precision care.

title: Association of Age at Type 1 Diabetes Onset With Survival, Cardiovascular, and Kidney Outcomes: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
authorString: Rawshani A, Eliasson B, McGuire DK, Sattar N, Gerstein HC, Isufi J, Zaccai J, Mahieu A, Rawshani A.
abstractText:
Objective

To investigate the association of age at type 1 diabetes diagnosis with incident mortality, cardiovascular, and kidney outcomes.

Research design and methods

In this retrospective cohort study, individuals ≥18 years of age with type 1 diabetes with one or more entries in the Swedish National Diabetes Register (from January 1998 to December 2019) were followed from the date of first registration up to December 2020. Cox proportional hazards models were used to examine risk per 1-year increase in age at type 1 diabetes diagnosis and excess risk relative to comparator individuals from the Swedish Total Population Register.

Results

Cohorts consisted of 34,155 individuals with type 1 diabetes and 150,026 comparator individuals. The hazard ratio (HR) per 1-year increase in age at type 1 diabetes diagnosis was 0.98 (95% CI 0.98, 0.99) for all-cause mortality, indicating a 1.7% lower probability per 1-year increase in age at type 1 diabetes diagnosis (8.2% lower probability per 5-year increase). Corresponding HRs per 1-year increase in age at diagnosis were 0.97 (0.97, 0.98) for cardiovascular mortality and 0.99 (0.98, 0.99) for noncardiovascular mortality. Excess risk relative to comparator individuals was greatest when type 1 diabetes diagnosis occurred from 0 to 10 years of age, with HRs of 3.23 (2.92, 3.58) for all-cause mortality, 5.73 (4.32, 7.59) for cardiovascular mortality, and 3.01 (2.70, 3.36) for noncardiovascular mortality.

Conclusions

Younger age at type 1 diabetes diagnosis is associated with greater risk of mortality and complications, with each additional year delay in onset being significantly associated with lower risk.

title: Evaluating retrieval-augmented generation versus long-context input for clinical reasoning over electronic health records.
authorString: Myers S, Dligach D, Miller TA, Barr S, Landefeld J, Gao Y, Churpek MM, Mayampurath A, Afshar M.

journal.title: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA

abstractText:
Objective

To evaluate whether retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can serve as an efficient alternative to long-context prompting for clinical reasoning over electronic health records (EHRs).

Materials and methods

We defined 3 EHR-based tasks that are replicable across health systems and vary in reasoning complexity: (1) extracting imaging procedures (modality, date, and anatomic site), (2) generating timelines of therapeutic antibiotic use, and (3) identifying the key diagnoses for a hospitalization. Using real inpatient clinical notes from a US academic health system, we evaluated 3 large language models (GPT-5.4-mini, Mistral Medium 3, DeepSeek V3.1) with varying amounts of provided context, comparing targeted retrieval to using the most recent clinical notes.

Results

For Imaging Procedures, RAG strongly outperformed recent-note inputs and exceeded long-context performance (by 0.17-9.83 F1 across all models) using fewer than 8K tokens. Similar benefits were observed for Antibiotic Timelines, where <8K of retrieved tokens matched long-context recent-notes performance (between -3.26 and +3.24 Jaccard). Error analysis revealed that missing information in the clinical notes-often due to inter-hospital transfers-limited performance to some extent. However, performance on the Diagnosis Generation task remains largely static across methods and models.

Discussion

RAG demonstrated strong token efficiency across tasks, with the clearest and most consistent gains observed for imaging extraction and antibiotic timeline reconstruction. Diagnosis generation proved the most challenging task, suggesting ceiling effects imposed by documentation variability and evaluation constraints.

Conclusion

Our results suggest that RAG remains a competitive and efficient approach for clinical tasks over large amounts of EHR, even as newer models become capable of handling increasingly longer amounts of text.

title: Male mice are more susceptible than females to obesity-induced muscle atrophy when fed a high-fat, high-cholesterol diet.
authorString: Mo T, Wang S, Li Z, Xu H, Liufu X, Wang Y, Qayyum N, Guo H.
abstractText: Obesity-related skeletal muscle atrophy poses a significant health burden, with marked sex differences in this condition. However, the mechanisms underlying these sex differences remain poorly understood. This study investigated whether and to what extent skeletal muscle quality was impaired in C57BL/6 mice fed a high-fat, high-cholesterol (HFHC) diet, focusing on sexual dimorphism. Male and female mice were assigned to control or HFHC groups for 40 weeks. The results showed that both sexes fed the HFHC diet developed obesity and dyslipidemia, with males exhibiting a more severe phenotype. Notably, males experienced more pronounced obesity-induced muscle atrophy than females. This study further revealed that HFHC feeding disrupted physiological homeostasis in both sexes, leading to sexual dimorphism in gut microbial composition and short-chain fatty acid levels, with males displaying a diminished capacity to maintain metabolic homeostasis. Furthermore, males exhibited more severe mitochondrial dysfunction and higher oxidative stress levels compared to females, manifesting as reduced muscle strength and upregulated atrophy-related gene expression. Collectively, these findings indicate that long-term HFHC feeding disrupts gut microbiota and glucolipid metabolic homeostasis, further impairing mitochondrial function and exacerbating muscle atrophy preferentially in males, whereas females are relatively protected through superior maintenance of physiological homeostasis, resulting in milder muscle atrophy.

title: Functional Network Organization Underlying Individual Differences in False Feedback Susceptibility: A Graph Theoretical Analysis.
authorString: Patchitt J, Karapanagiotidis T, Garfinkel SN, Miller M, Tsakiris M, Clark A, Critchley HD.
abstractText: Individual differences in susceptibility to somatosensory false physiological feedback reflect variations in interoceptive processing, yet the underlying neural network mechanisms remain unclear. We analyzed resting-state functional connectivity using graph theoretical approaches in 41 healthy adults who completed a somatosensory false feedback paradigm. Nine regions of interest were defined from previous activation analyses, and network topology metrics including local efficiency, clustering coefficient, centrality measures, and path length were calculated across multiple thresholds. Three distinct patterns of network organization predicted false feedback susceptibility. Individuals more susceptible to false feedback showed: (1) increased posterior insula eccentricity, indicating network peripheralization of this key interoceptive region; (2) consistent orbitofrontal cortex segregation across multiple metrics including increased path length and decreased centrality measures; and (3) cerebellar network reconfiguration with reduced local efficiency but increased betweenness centrality. Somatosensory false feedback susceptibility reflects specific alterations in functional network topology, particularly reduced integration of interoceptive regions (posterior insula) and emotional appraisal systems (orbitofrontal cortex). These findings support a network-based model where interoceptive processing depends on efficient integration between visceral sensation, emotional evaluation, and cognitive control systems. Understanding these network properties may inform interventions targeting interoceptive awareness and emotional regulation.

title: Antimicrobial Resistance in Periodontal Disease: Rethinking Adjunctive Therapy in the Metagenomics Era, the Pressing Need for Precision Treatment and Periodontal Resistome Mapping.
authorString: Alghafri M, Edwards L, Moyes D, Nibali L.

journal.title: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine

abstractText: Systemic antibiotics are effective when used as adjunctive therapy in the treatment of periodontitis; however, their use must be balanced against antimicrobial resistance, which is a major threat to global public health. This review provides an expert synthesis of the literature and a field-level overview of antimicrobial resistance in periodontal therapy, highlighting current knowledge and emerging directions, while examining how adjunctive antibiotic protocols may contribute to resistance within the periodontal microbiome through emerging metagenomic insights. To provide this synthesis, the PubMed database was searched for English-language publications using combinations of the terms periodontitis, systemic antibiotics, antimicrobials, resistance, resistome, therapeutic adjuncts, resistance genes, susceptibility, antibacterial and drug resistance, and the findings are presented as a narrative review. The evidence indicates that a substantial proportion of patients with periodontitis harbour subgingival microbiota that are non-susceptible to at least one antibiotic used in periodontal therapy. Across the included studies, antimicrobial resistance was most frequently reported in Prevotella and Porphyromonas species, while some studies also identified virulence-associated factors in Staphylococcus aureus, a non-classical periodontal organism detected within the subgingival microbiota. Overall, current evidence indicates a high prevalence of antibiotic resistance genes in the subgingival microbiota of patients with periodontitis and highlights the ecological consequences of adjunctive antibiotic use. These findings reinforce the need to optimize antibiotic prescribing protocols within an antibiotic stewardship framework and support further metagenomic investigations to refine understanding of resistance patterns, gene-transfer mechanisms and microbiome disruption, with the aim of advancing precision-based periodontal care.

title: The use of triptans, opioids, and other rescue medications among patients with migraine prescribed calcitonin gene-related peptide inhibitors for migraine prophylaxis.
authorString: Nguyen JL, Lee T, Swart ECS, Peasah SK, Ineh A, Patel U, Good CB.

journal.title: Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy

abstractText:
Background

Migraine attacks can be prevalent and debilitating, affecting 40 million adults in the United States. Patients can be prescribed prophylaxis (eg, β blockers, anticonvulsants, antidepressants) and rescue medications (eg, triptans, opioids [which are not recommended for use to treat migraine]) to treat and/or relieve migraine. Calcitonin gene-related peptide inhibitors (CGRPi) are the newest class of drugs approved for migraine prophylaxis. Patients taking CGRPi report reduced migraine frequency and severity, which should result in lower use of rescue migraine medications.

Objective

To compare the use of triptans, rescue medications, and opioids for patients with migraines prescribed preventive CGRPi (pCGRi) and patients who are not prescribed pCGRPi.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study used Komodo Health medical and pharmacy claims data from 2018 to 2023. Adults aged 18 to 60 years with a chronic migraine diagnosis and continuous enrollment for 12 months before and after index were included if they initiated a migraine medication (pCGRPi or non-CGRPi) during the index period. Outcomes included use of triptans, opioids, and other rescue medications in the post-index period compared with the pre-index period. Propensity score-matched cohorts were analyzed using adjusted logistic regression models with a treatment-by-time interaction term to estimate relative changes over time between cohorts.

Results

In adjusted analyses, compared with the non-CGRPi cohort, the pCGRPi cohort experienced lower odds in triptan use (interaction odds ratio [OR] = 0.57; 95% CI = 0.53-0.61; P < 0.001) and in opioid use (interaction OR = 0.92; 95% CI = 0.85-0.99; P  =  0.033). Although rescue medication use increased over time, the relative pre-post change did not differ significantly between cohorts (interaction OR = 0.96; 95% CI = 0.89-1.04; P = 0.28). Sensitivity analyses restricted to neurologist-prescribed index medications showed consistent findings for triptans, but not for use of opioids or rescue medications.

Conclusions

In the cohort prescribed pCGRPi, there was a statistically significant association with decreased of triptan use over time. Comparatively, the non-CGRPi cohort had statistically significant increases in the use of triptans, opioids, and other rescue medications over time. These findings support that prophylactic use of pCGRPi may be associated with a reduced reliance on migraine-specific rescue medications.

title: Precision targeting using machine learning to optimize medication therapy management delivery in value-based care: A quasi-experimental study using real-world evidence.
authorString: Zamran M, Kirkham H, Henschel T, Witt EA, Wonders P, Gill NW.

journal.title: Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy

abstractText:
Background

Medication therapy management (MTM) is a core component of managed care pharmacy that improves medication safety, adherence, and clinical outcomes in high-risk populations. However, traditional eligibility criteria lack precision, limiting scalability and impact.

Objective

To provide real-world evidence of how machine learning (ML) integration into pharmacy workflows can improve MTM delivery by identifying patients most likely to engage.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study using a de-identified pharmacy dataset. MTM-eligible patients in 2025 were assigned to centralized or community pharmacists via an ML-based precision-targeting model, whereas a 2024 cohort was assigned using traditional eligibility-based assignment. The propensity score matching model incorporated demographics, medication patterns, social determinants of health, engagement history, and plan-level/store-level characteristics. The primary outcome was the call favorability rate (acceptance of a pharmacist consultation).

Results

After propensity score matching, 183,888 matched patient pairs were analyzed. The ML cohort showed a 21.2% call favorability rate vs 12.6% in the historical cohort, an 8.6% absolute increase and 68% relative improvement (risk ratio = 1.68). Results were robust to moderate unmeasured confounding (E value = 2.75). Results were statistically significant (P < 0.001) and remained stable with checks for bias.

Conclusions

ML-based precision targeting was associated with higher MTM call favorability compared with traditional eligibility-based approaches. These findings support integrating ML into pharmacists' workflows to improve patient engagement and resource use amid evolving reimbursement structures. The results were robust to potential hidden bias, suggesting that this approach could be scaled for use in managed care MTM programs.

title: Predicting for Malignancy in Congenital Lung Malformations: A Single-Center Study of the "At Risk" Pediatric and Adult Population.
authorString: Rao MS, Bradley E, Haddad A, Lawther S, Dick A, Doherty G, Boyd C, Shields M, Eastwood MP.
abstractText:
Introduction

Congenital lung malformations (CLMs) are often identified on antenatal scanning and malignant transformation is cited as an indication for early resection. Long-term follow-up of asymptomatic lesions managed nonoperatively is lacking. Herein, we prospectively follow up children with antenatally identified CLMs and reviewed adult patients diagnosed with adenocarcinoma to look for background CLM changes.

Methods

This is a single-center cohort study of pediatric patients with antenatal or early postnatal diagnosis of CLMs and a retrospective review of adult patients with lung adenocarcinoma. In children, data collected included type or location of CLMs and subsequent follow-up. In adult patients, we reviewed radiology for background CLMs.

Results

One hundred and twenty-nine pediatric patients diagnosed with CLMs: congenital pulmonary airway malformations (n = 79; 61%), bronchopulmonary sequestrations (n = 26; 20%), congenital lobar emphysema (n = 11; 9%), resolved lesions (n = 10; 8%), bronchogenic cysts (n = 2; 2%), and an unknown lesion (n = 1; 1%). The patients were followed up for 6.7 (IQR: 3.4-10.5; range 0.08-20.6) years. No pediatric patient was subsequently identified on the Northern Ireland Cancer Registry. Three hundred and twenty-three adult patients were diagnosed with lung carcinoma: 37 (11%) were mucinous adenocarcinomas and 21 (57%) had a KRAS mutation. No CLMs were identified on review of radiological imaging in adult patients presenting with malignancy.

Conclusion

In children with CLMs, no resected malignant lesions could be identified on medium-term follow-up. Furthermore, no CLMs were identified in adult patients presenting with resected mucinous adenocarcinoma. Prospective collaborative databases are needed to determine true malignancy risk in asymptomatic CLM lesions and CPAMs.

title: Analgesic Efficacy of Ropivacaine-P407 Gel vs. Bupivacaine in Single-Port-Assisted Hysterectomy: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
authorString: Kim JC, Lee YJ, Nam EJ, Kim S, Lee JY, Kim YT, Kim SW.
abstractText:
Purpose

To compare the postoperative analgesic efficacy of ropivacaine-poloxamer 407 (P407) gel injection with that of bupivacaine injection in patients undergoing single-port assisted hysterectomy.

Materials and methods

This retrospective study reviewed medical records from January to December 2023 at Severance Hospital, Yonsei University. A total of 209 patients undergoing minimally invasive hysterectomy with or without adnexal procedures were analyzed. Patients were divided into two groups: 42 received ropivacaine-P407 gel (Welpass), and 167 received bupivacaine alone. Demographic variables, intraoperative parameters, and postoperative pain scores were collected. Propensity score matching was applied to control for surgical complexity and baseline imbalances, yielding 31 matched pairs. Pain levels were assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) at multiple time points up to 48 hours postoperatively.

Results

Before matching, the ropivacaine-P407 gel group demonstrated significantly lower pain scores starting at 12 hours postoperatively compared to the bupivacaine group (NRS difference p=0.005 at 24 hours, p=0.020 at 48 hours). After propensity score matching, this difference remained significant: patients in the ropivacaine-P407 gel group continued to report reduced pain intensity at 24 hours [mean NRS±standard deviation (SD): 1.96±0.35 vs. 2.86±1.35, p=0.003] and 48 hours (1.88±0.49 vs. 2.65±1.12, p=0.014). Both groups showed similar safety profiles, with no severe adverse reactions related to the anesthetic agents reported.

Conclusion

Ropivacaine-P407 gel injection provides superior early postoperative analgesia compared to bupivacaine alone in minimally invasive hysterectomy.

title: Clinical events and health care costs among pediatric and young adult patients with generalized myasthenia gravis in the United States.
authorString: Pesa J, Liu Z, Jackson L, Govindarajan R.

journal.title: Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy

abstractText:
Background

Management of children and young adults with generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) is currently informed by research conducted largely in older adults.

Objectives

To (1) describe sociodemographic/clinical characteristics and disease burden (treatments, occurrence of acute events [myasthenia gravis (MG) exacerbation or myasthenic crisis], and health care costs) for pediatric/young adult patients with gMG in the United States and (2) estimate the incremental health care cost burden of gMG for this group compared with controls without MG. A secondary objective was to explore the relationship between selected variables-including prior acute events-and the occurrence of subsequent acute events.

Methods

Longitudinal, retrospective cohorts of pediatric/young adult patients were identified from the Merative MarketScan Commercial Claims and Encounters Database (CCAE) and the Multi-State Medicaid Database (MDCD). Patients in the gMG cohort had at least 1 qualified MG event (January 1, 2010-June 30, 2025) and were aged from 2 to 25 years. Patients in the control cohort were selected at random from patients without MG (0.2% of patients with no MG diagnosis codes during study period; index dates from patients with gMG were randomly assigned) and had at least 6 months of continuous health plan enrollment and age range corresponding to the gMG cohort. Baseline characteristics, treatments during follow-up, and rates of acute events during follow-up were reported for each age category. Health care costs from the payer perspective per person per month (PPPM; following inverse probability of treatment weighting) for patients with gMG were compared with those for patients without MG. The association between selected variables of interest on the occurrence of acute events during follow-up was assessed using case controls with regression models.

Results

In the CCAE population with gMG (aged 2-11, 12-17, and 18-25 years, respectively [n = 226, n = 282, n = 853]), 25.2%, 34.8%, and 23.9% of patients had at least 1 MG exacerbation and 15.5%, 16.7%, and 13.6% had at least 1 myasthenic crisis (rates 18.2, 22.8, and 19.3/100 person-years [PY] and 9.3, 7.3, and 8.7/100 PY, respectively). Mean total health care costs were $6,104 PPPM for patients with gMG vs $257 PPPM for non-MG controls (n = 14,632)-a difference (95% CI) of $5,847 ($4,875-$6,819) PPPM. Mean costs were $13,401 PPPM for patients with MG exacerbation (vs $3,715 PPPM with no MG exacerbation) and $15,565 PPPM for those with myasthenic crisis (vs $4,734 with no myasthenic crisis). In the MDCD population with gMG (aged 2-11, 12-17, and 18-25 years, respectively [n = 218, n = 179, n = 284]), 29.8%, 40.8%, and 34.5% of patients had at least 1 MG exacerbation, and 13.3%, 23.6%, and 22.5% had at least 1 myasthenic crisis (rates 13.3, 26.9, and 30.1/100 PY and 5.8, 12.0, and 15.8/100 PY, respectively). Mean total health care costs were $2,605 PPPM for patients with gMG vs $162 PPPM for non-MG controls (n = 6,908)-a difference (95% CI) of $2,443 ($1,713-$3,172) PPPM. Mean costs were $4,934 PPPM for those with MG exacerbation (vs $1,535 with no MG exacerbation) and $5,538 PPPM for those with myasthenic crisis (vs $2,045 with no myasthenic crisis). In both populations, previous MG exacerbation was associated with recurrence of acute events during follow-up.

Conclusions

For pediatric and young adult patients with gMG in the United States, health care costs were higher than in controls. Many patients experienced acute events, health care costs were higher for patients with acute events, and the occurrence of acute events was strongly associated with prior events. There is a need for improved gMG management to reduce the frequency of costly acute events.

title: Serum albumin oxidation and inter-alpha-trypsin-inhibitor heavy chain-4 abundance correlate with the dystropathology in the rat model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
authorString: Bautista APR, Lafoux A, Tsioutsias I, Terrill JR, Le Guiner C, Huchet C, Arthur PG.
abstractText: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is a fatal X-linked genetic disease caused by the absence of functional dystrophin, resulting in muscle membrane fragility, chronic inflammation, and progressive muscle wasting. The lack of effective treatments is further compounded by the slow onset of measurable changes in clinical outcomes, such as muscle strength, which often take a year or longer to become evident. Blood-based biomarkers that can predict treatment efficacy and monitor disease progression would significantly accelerate therapeutic development. We propose that oxidative modifications to proteins in blood, a consequence of muscle inflammation, could be used to monitor disease progression in DMD. Using the DMDmdx rat, a model with more severe dystropathology than the mouse model of dystrophy (mdx), we assessed inflammation and oxidative stress in muscle and blood across disease stages. DMDmdx rats aged 1.5-12 months showed sustained immune activation, as indicated by elevated circulating leukocytes and increased myeloperoxidase content in dystrophic muscle compared with wild type. Oxidative protein modifications, including carbonylation, tyrosine chlorination, and thiol oxidation, were significantly elevated in serum and tissues of dystrophic rats. Two proteins showed distinct disease-associated oxidative changes: albumin, which exhibited consistently increased thiol oxidation across ages, and inter-alpha-trypsin inhibitor 4 (ITIH4), which showed elevated chlorination between 1.5 and 4.5 months. Notably, serum ITIH4 abundance correlated with markers of muscle inflammation and oxidative stress. These findings identify serum albumin thiol oxidation and serum ITIH4 abundance as promising blood-based biomarkers for monitoring inflammation-associated dystropathology in DMD.

title: Lysine Lactylation Modifies Cryab-Hspa1b Interactions and Prevents MAPK Signaling to Slow Diabetic Cardiomyopathy Progression.
authorString: Ma D, Liang X, Jing H, Liu X, Liu P, Cai W, Zhong X, Li X, Dong S, Tian Y, Wei C.
abstractText:
Protein posttranslational modifications, including lactylation, have been intimately associated with myocardial energy metabolism. In this study, we investigated the role of Cryab in diabetic cardiomyopathy (DbCM) and its lysine lactylation (Kla). A spontaneous DbCM mouse model in db/db mice and a high-fat diet combined with i.p. streptozotocin injection mouse model were used. Primary cardiomyocytes were subjected to liposome-mediated transfection, followed by exposure to high glucose and palmitate. Cryab exhibited reduced Kla modification in myocardial tissue from DbCM mouse models and in damaged cardiomyocytes, while protein expression remained unchanged. Kla modification site mutation at K90R worsened cardiac systolic and diastolic dysfunction, myocardial hypertrophy, fibrosis, and apoptosis in vivo and in vitro. Cryab modulated the Hspa1b protein in a Kla-dependent manner and enhanced the stability of the Hspa1b protein. In DbCM mouse models or cardiomyocytes, Hspa1b protein expression was reduced, and the MAPK pathway was activated, which was further exacerbated following mutation at K90R. These findings demonstrate that reduced Kla modification in Cryab accelerated degradation of Hspa1b and activation of the MAPK pathway, thereby contributing to cardiac dysfunction associated with DbCM. These findings suggest that novel therapeutic strategies targeting protein Kla modification could be significant in the clinical management of DbCM.

Article highlights

Cryab lysine lactylation (Kla) modification in myocardial tissue is reduced in db/db mice with diabetic cardiomyopathy (DbCM). Mutations in the Cryab Kla site exacerbate DbCM damage in vivo and in vitro. Cryab Kla enhances the stability of the Hspa1b protein by interacting with Hspa1b. Cryab blocks DbCM-induced MAPK signaling in an Hspa1b-dependent manner. Cryab/Hspa1b/MAPK signaling influences DbCM-associated cardiac dysfunction.

title: Inulin- and Butyrate-Mediated HIF-1α Butyrylation Prevent Diabetic Ferroptosis and Cardiomyopathy by Maintaining Iron Homeostasis.
authorString: Yang G, Tian Y, Sun R, Dong C, Li Y, Li S, Zhang H, Xin Y.
abstractText:
Abnormal iron metabolism and ferroptosis contribute to diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM); however, the regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. Inulin improves systemic metabolism and cardiac function, but whether it alleviates myocardial ferroptosis and DCM is unknown. Using two distinct type 2 diabetes (T2D) mouse models-the high-fat diet combined with streptozotocin-induced T2D model and the db/db mouse model-in combination with an iron chelator, we found that imbalanced iron homeostasis and ferroptosis drive DCM. Inulin restored cardiac iron homeostasis, inhibited ferroptosis and DCM, and promoted short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs). Treatment with an SCFA inhibitor confirmed that SCFAs mediate the cardioprotective effects of inulin, with butyrate exerting the most potent antiferroptotic effect. Hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α) expression was decreased in DCM, and bioinformatic analysis identified HIF-1α as a hub gene in ferroptosis. Interference with HIF-1α in the two distinct T2D mouse models and in vitro weakened the antiferroptotic effect of butyrate. Mechanistically, butyrate inhibited HIF-1α ubiquitination by inducing HIF-1α butyrylation at lysine 190, which upregulated transcription of ferritin heavy chain (FTH) and mitochondrial ferritin (FTMT) to enhance the storage of unstable iron. HIF-1α acts as a critical regulator of myocardial iron homeostasis through transcriptional upregulation of FTH/FTMT. Inulin-fermented butyrate prevents ferroptosis-driven DCM, and its protective effect depends on the HIF-1α-FTH/FTMT axis via butyrylation. These findings highlight the therapeutic potential of using inulin or targeting HIF-1α in the management of DCM and diseases associated with aberrant iron metabolism.

Article highlights

Dysregulated iron metabolism and ferroptosis contribute to diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM); however, the regulatory mechanisms and effective therapeutic strategies remain elusive. We sought to identify the role of hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α) in regulating myocardial iron homeostasis and ferroptosis in DCM, as well as evaluate the preventive effects of inulin on ferroptosis-induced DCM and elucidate its mechanism. Inulin-fermented butyrate activates the HIF-1α-ferritin heavy chain (FTH)/mitochondrial ferritin (FTMT) axis, alleviating cardiac ferroptosis and DCM, and stabilizes HIF-1α by promoting K190 Kbu modification and inhibiting ubiquitin-dependent degradation. Targeting the HIF-1α-FTH/FTMT axis via inulin, butyrate, or alternative approaches may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for alleviating DCM and other diabetes complications.

title: Exploring the Mechanism of Zhigancao Decoction in the Treatment of Chronic Heart Failure via Modulation of Oxidative Stress.
authorString: Luo Z, Huang Y, Tian Y, Huang S, Li F.

journal.title: Rapid communications in mass spectrometry : RCM

abstractText:
Background

Zhigancao decoction has shown therapeutic potential in the management of chronic heart failure (CHF); however, the molecular mechanisms underlying its pharmacological effects remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate its potential mechanisms, with a particular focus on oxidative stress-related pathways.

Methods

The chemical profile of Zhigancao decoction was characterized by LC-MS/MS, and putative targets were predicted using SwissTargetPrediction. A protein-protein interaction (PPI) network was established using the STRING database and Cytoscape software, followed by Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses. Differentially expressed genes from two GEO datasets (GSE9128 and GSE84796) were integrated with reactive oxygen species (ROS)-related genes to identify candidate targets. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were subsequently performed to investigate compound-target interactions.

Results

A total of 66 chemical constituents and 818 putative targets were characterized and collected, respectively. Among these targets, MMP9 emerged as a central candidate associated with the therapeutic effects of Zhigancao decoction. GO and KEGG enrichment analyses demonstrated that the core targets were significantly enriched in oxidative stress-related pathways, inflammatory signaling cascades, and cell fate regulatory pathways. Computational deconvolution of bulk transcriptomic data suggested marked alterations in the estimated immune cell composition of the CHF microenvironment. Network pharmacology analysis further indicated that multiple chemical constituents of Zhigancao decoction converge on MMP9 and its associated pathways. Molecular docking analysis demonstrated favorable binding affinities between 10 representative compounds and MMP9, with binding energies below -7.0 kcal/mol.

Conclusions

In silico predictions suggest that Zhigancao decoction may exert potential therapeutic effects against CHF through computationally predicted targeting of MMP9 and associated oxidative stress- and immune-related pathways. These computational findings provide a theoretical foundation for future experimental investigations into the mechanisms of Zhigancao decoction in CHF, though clinical application would require confirmation through rigorous in vivo and clinical studies.

title: Longitudinal Repeated Protein Measurements in a Multiethnic Cohort Identify Novel Diabetes Biomarkers That Reveal Unique Disease Pathways.
authorString: Chen ZZ, Mi MY, Barber J, Tiwari G, Adams CD, Deng S, Shin CY, Farrell L, Rao P, Cruz DE, Wilson JG, Sevilla-Gonzalez M, Chen YI, Guo X, Goodarzi MO, Taylor KD, Tahir UA, Rich SS, Wood AC, Gerszten RE, Rotter JI.
abstractText:
Circulating diabetes biomarkers have been identified with proteomics measured at a single time point, but what is additionally provided by longitudinal repeated measurements in the same individuals, over many years, is unknown. We studied participants in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA; n = 5,322; mean baseline age, 61.7 years) at exams 1 (2000-2002), 5 (2010-2012), and 6 (2016-2018) profiled with the Olink Explore (3 K) platform. Associations with incident diabetes, mostly of type 2, were modeled using Cox proportional hazards with exam 1 proteins (i.e., single time point) and time-updating Cox with proteins from all three exams (i.e., longitudinal repeated) adjusted for clinical risk factors. We identified 27 novel single time point associations and up to a fourfold increase in longitudinal associations (false discovery rate < 0.05), with a proportional increase in the number consistent with causality via cis-Mendelian randomization (∼5%) and a smaller overlap in MESA longitudinal versus single associations with UK Biobank single time point findings (42% vs. 87%, respectively). Compared with small-molecule metabolism pathway enrichment among the shared proteins, proteins unique to the longitudinal analyses enriched for protein and cellular processing pathways. We conclude that longitudinal repeated measurements identify a number of distinct disease biomarkers, in part by revealing the progression of relevant biological processes within an individual closer to a clinical diabetes diagnosis versus single measurements.

Article highlights

There is up to a fourfold increase in diabetes biomarkers identified with longitudinal repeated versus single time point proteomic measurements. The increase in biomarkers identified with longitudinal repeated measurements is supported by a similar proportion being nominated as causal for type 2 diabetes with Mendelian randomization. Proteins unique to the longitudinal repeated analyses highlighted biological pathways (e.g., posttranslational protein modification and cellular structure and cycle regulation) that were distinct from pathways enriched among the shared proteins (e.g., small-molecule metabolic and catabolic processes). Longitudinal protein measurements identify additional novel disease biomarkers and disparate biological pathways compared with single measurement analyses.

title: Chemical Profiling by UHPLC-MS/MS and In Vitro Antioxidant, Antimicrobial, and Cytotoxic Properties of Lepidoceras peruvianum Kuijt Leaves and Fruits.
authorString: Jara MRA, Bautista KG, Pérez FIO, Landeo EC, Cáceres EEC, Molero HRL, Segovia JCP, Choque JSC, Rashid A, Prado MSA.

journal.title: Rapid communications in mass spectrometry : RCM

abstractText:
Rationale

Lepidoceras peruvianum Kuijt is an understudied hemiparasitic species endemic to the Peruvian Andes that lacks comprehensive phytochemical characterization. Investigating its metabolome is important for understanding its chemotaxonomic relevance and potential as a source of bioactive compounds.

Methods

Leaves and fruits of L. peruvianum were subjected to untargeted metabolomic profiling using high-resolution UHPLC-ESI-Orbitrap-MS/MS in positive and negative ionization modes. Metabolites were annotated based on accurate mass measurements, isotopic patterns, collision-induced dissociation (CID) fragmentation data, and spectral matching with the Global Natural Products Social Molecular Networking (GNPS), METLIN, and MassBank databases. Structural elucidation employed diagnostic fragmentation pathways, including retro-Diels-Alder (RDA), heterocyclic ring fission (HRF), quinone methide (QM), and benzofuran-forming (BFF) cleavages. Antioxidant activity was evaluated using DPPH●, ABTS●+, and FRAP assays, while antimicrobial activity and toxicity were assessed through antibacterial testing and the Artemia salina lethality assay.

Results

Leaves contained 34 metabolites, mainly flavan-3-ols, proanthocyanidins, flavonols, lignans, and isoquinoline alkaloids, whereas fruits were characterized by anthocyanins, organic acids, and polar lipids. Total phenolic content was higher in leaves (292.4 mg GAE/g) than in fruits (216.8 mg GAE/g), corresponding to stronger antioxidant activity. Leaves extracts exhibited greater antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus, while fruit extracts showed stronger effects against Gram-negative bacteria. LC50 values in the A. salina assay were 181.8 μg/mL for leaves and 475.9 μg/mL for fruits.

Conclusions

This study provides the first comprehensive metabolomic characterization of L. peruvianum, revealing organ-specific chemical diversity and notable bioactive properties. The findings demonstrate the utility of HRMS/MS fragmentation analysis for metabolite annotation and identify this endemic species as a promising source of bioactive natural products.

title: <b>Associations between inflammatory markers and myocardial injury in patients treated with pitavastatin</b> : <b>A retrospective clinical study</b>.
authorString: Mao Y, Zhou W.
abstractText:
Background

Inflammation drives atherosclerosis and myocardial injury; pitavastatin's effect on related markers lacks research.

Objectives

For the purpose of ascertaining the link between inflammatory marker levels and myocardial injury indices in patients undergoing pitavastatin treatment.

Methods

A retrospective study screened 105 pitavastatin-treated patients at the Affiliated Hospital of Guizhou Medical University (January 2022-December 2024). After exclusion criteria application, 100 patients were recruited and stratified into the myocardial injury group (n=32) and non-myocardial injury group (n=68). The primary outcome measures included inflammatory markers, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1) and fibrinogen (FIB). The secondary outcome measures included lipid profiles such as total cholesterol (TC), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE); as well as myocardial injury indices: cardiac troponin I (cTnI), creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB), lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and myoglobin (Mb). Spearman's correlation analysis was executed to assess the correlation between baseline inflammatory markers and myocardial injury indices. Logistic regression analysis was adopted to pinpoint independent risk factors for myocardial injury.

Results

Logistic regression analysis indicated that the baseline characteristics of the two groups were well matched (all P>0.05). Hs-CRP, IL-6, TNF-α, MCP-1, FIB, cTnI, CK-MB, LDH, Mb, TC and LDL-C in the myocardial injury group were higher than those in the non-myocardial injury group (all P<0.05). The incidence of MACE in the myocardial injury group was higher than that in the non-myocardial injury group (P=0.002). Spearman's correlation analysis revealed that hs-CRP, IL-6, TNF-α, MCP-1 and FIB suggested positive correlation with cTnI, CK-MB, LDH and Mb (all P<0.001). Logistic regression analysis suggested that elevated hs-CRP, IL-6 and TNF-α levels are independent risk factors for myocardial injury in patients receiving pitavastatin treatment.

Conclusion

In pitavastatin-treated patients, inflammatory markers correlate with myocardial injury; monitoring hs-CRP, IL-6, TNF-α improves prognosis.

title: Robot-assisted Partial Nephrectomy with the new HugoRAS System: single center matched-pair analysis.
authorString: Gonçalves GG, Vinagre N, Magalhães M, Fraga A, Silva-Ramos M.

journal.title: International braz j urol : official journal of the Brazilian Society of Urology

abstractText:
Purpose

Robotic-assisted surgery represents a leading innovation in kidney-sparing procedures across specialized urology centers.
