As new robotic platforms continue to emerge, comparisons with conventional laparoscopy remain necessary. This study focuses on comparing oncological, perioperative and functional outcomes of robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) with the Hugo™ RAS system and laparoscopic partial nephrectomy (LPN) within a tertiary institution.

Materials and methods

A retrospective single-center study included 165 patients who underwent LPN (n=95) or RAPN (n=70). Perioperative clinical data, tumor characteristics, oncological and functional outcomes were obtained. Propensity score matching (1:1) was implemented to mitigate selection bias. Trifecta and pentafecta were assessed as composite surgical success endpoints. Multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify the predictive factors for each.

Results

Following propensity score matching, 70 patients were included in each group. Operative time, WIT and estimated blood loss did not differ significantly. RAPN was associated with a shorter length of stay (3 days vs 5 days, p<0.001) without increased complication rate. Renal functional outcomes, including ≥90% eGFR preservation and CKD upstaging, were similar. Trifecta (LPN 84.3% vs. RAPN 85.7%) and pentafecta (LPN 48.6% vs. RAPN 57.4%) achievement were comparable. On multivariate analysis, higher RENAL score was the only independent predictor of trifecta failure (OR 1.410, p=0.027). For pentafecta, higher RENAL score (OR 1.396, p=0.030), older age (OR 0.929, p=0.001), and lower pre-operative eGFR (OR 0.981, p=0.049) were independent predictors of failure.

Conclusions

The study reinforced the effectiveness and safety of the new Hugo™ RAS platform for partial nephrectomy, without compromising oncological and functional success.

title: Utility of Pancreatic Perivascular Adipose Tissue as a CT Imaging Biomarker for Diagnosing Type 2 Diabetes.
authorString: Prasad AV, Mathai TS, Balamuralikrishna PTS, Batheja V, Suri A, Mukherjee P, Liu J, Summers RM.
abstractText:
Intrapancreatic fat deposition is a well-established biomarker for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), but little is known about the role of pancreatic perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT), fat surrounding blood vessels supplying the pancreas. The objectives of this study were to develop a fully automated pipeline to derive imaging biomarkers of pancreatic PVAT from abdominal computed tomography (CT) scans and evaluate their utility for diagnosing T2DM. Contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) scans (n = 1,350) from the public PANORAMA data set were used to train a three-dimensional deep neural network to segment pancreatic anatomy (parenchyma, vasculature, ducts) and extrapancreatic structures. The model was applied to an internal data set containing 615 CECT scans. Intrapancreatic, extrapancreatic, and PVAT biomarkers were derived from these segmentations. Logistic regression with feature selection identified optimal biomarker subsets for classifying T2DM. All PVAT biomarkers differed significantly between individuals with diabetes and those without. The best multivariate model for T2DM achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.93, sensitivity of 0.73, and specificity of 0.91. Exploratory analyses for incident diabetes (developed within the following 4 years) showed similarly high discrimination (AUC 0.93). Automated CT-derived PVAT biomarkers are associated with existing and future T2DM and may enable opportunistic identification of undiagnosed or high-risk individuals undergoing routine abdominal CT.

Article highlights

Pancreatic perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) is a potentially important but understudied fat depot surrounding vessels supplying the pancreas, and its role in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remains unclear. We aimed to quantify pancreatic PVAT automatically on routine abdominal computed tomography (CT) scans and assess whether PVAT-derived imaging biomarkers are associated with T2DM and future T2DM risk. PVAT biomarkers were associated with T2DM and were informative predictors in multivariable models. Exploratory analyses showed similar findings for incident T2DM (disease onset within 4 years of follow-up). PVAT may represent a novel CT-based biomarker for early metabolic dysfunction and T2DM risk stratification.

title: Hypofractionated Total Marrow and Lymphoid Irradiation for Relapsed/Refractory Leukemia Using Helical Tomotherapy: Workflow and Dosimetric Analysis.
authorString: Ni W, Wang X, Yang H, Zhao J, Li D, Song L, Sun B, Mu X.
abstractText:
Purpose

To report the workflow optimization, dosimetric characteristics, and clinical outcomes of hypofractionated total marrow irradiation (TMI) and total marrow and lymphoid irradiation (TMLI) as part of conditioning regimens for patients with relapsed or refractory leukemia undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT).

Materials and methods

Ninety-two patients treated between December 2024 and October 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Prescription doses ranged from 10.5 to 15.0 Gy, delivered in once-daily fractions of 3.0-4.0 Gy. Patients were grouped by prescription dose (10.5-12.0 Gy, n=72 vs. 14.0-15.0 Gy, n=20). Dosimetric parameters of planning target volumes and organs at risk (OARs) were extracted. Survival outcomes were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier analysis.

Results

Adequate target coverage was achieved in both dose groups, with median planning target volume D95% values of 100.0% and 99.5% for the 10.5-12.0 Gy and 14.0-15.0 Gy groups, respectively. Lung mean doses were limited to 6.2±0.7 Gy and 6.6±0.8 Gy, and mean oral cavity doses were 6.2±1.5 Gy and 5.6±1.0 Gy, respectively. Mean rib doses were intentionally reduced to approximately 10 Gy to prioritize lung sparing. Eighty-seven out of 92 patients successfully underwent HSCT (94.6%), and 8 died of transplant-related causes (8.7%). The overall incidence of chronic graft-versus-host disease was 62.0%. One-year disease-free survival and overall survival were 78.4% and 87.0%, respectively.

Conclusion

Hypofractionated TMI and TMLI are feasible and efficient conditioning approaches for relapsed or refractory leukemia, providing adequate target coverage with effective OAR sparing. The toxicity and clinical outcomes were acceptable.

title: Beyond Traditional Glycemic Measures: CGM Glycemic Profiles Reveal Associations With Cardiometabolic Risk in Individuals Without Diabetes.
authorString: Bakhshi B, Lin H, Sultana N, Healey E, Queen H, Gao G, Claudel SE, Minetti ET, Mitchell GF, Murabito JM, Lloyd-Jones DM, Cheney MC, Steenkamp DW, Nayor M, Xanthakis V, Walker ME, Spartano NL.
abstractText:
Objective

Fasting plasma glucose (FPG) and hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) may not fully capture the heterogeneity underlying dysglycemia or its associations with cardiometabolic risk factors (CMRFs). We cross-sectionally investigated whether continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) measures and glycemic profiles could reveal 10-year cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk and individual CMRFs among individuals without diabetes.

Research design and methods

We included 1,356 participants without prevalent diabetes or CVD from the Framingham Heart Study, who wore a blinded Dexcom G6 Pro CGM for up to 10 days. CGM glycemic profiles were characterized using 1) binary classification of glycemic burden and variability and 2) unsupervised clustering of CGM measures. We performed multivariable-adjusted linear and logistic regression models to examine associations of CGM measures and profiles with 10-year CVD risk estimates (PREVENT equations) and individual CMRFs.

Results

Participants' mean was age 59.3 years; 55.8% were women, and 92.6% were non-Hispanic White. CGM measures were positively associated with 10-year CVD risk estimates and CMRFs. For example, 1 SD higher % time >140 mg/dL (15.4%) was associated with 2% higher 10-year CVD risk estimates and 21-26% higher odds of hypertension and dyslipidemia, even after adjusting for FPG. Glycemic profiles representing higher CGM dysglycemia revealed discordance with traditionally defined glycemic status (FPG and HbA1c). Although 48.1-84.2% of individuals with traditionally defined prediabetes were included in CGM profiles representing higher dysglycemia, such profiles were associated with 6-7% higher 10-year CVD risk estimates, in addition to worse CMRFs.

Conclusions

Glycemic measures reflective of continuous glucose dynamics may provide additional insights into cardiometabolic risk beyond traditional measures.

title: Clinical association between fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) levels and the severity of vascular calcification and cardiovascular event risk in peritoneal dialysis patients.
authorString: Meiyang Z, Haole H, Canxin Z.
abstractText:
Background

Fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) is a phosphaturic hormone increasingly recognized as a potential contributor to cardiovascular complications in chronic kidney disease (CKD). This study investigated the association between circulating intact FGF23 levels and the severity of vascular calcification and cardiovascular event risk in peritoneal dialysis (PD) patients.

Materials and methods

In this retrospective cohort study, we enrolled 150 PD patients treated at our center between January 2020 and January 2025. All biomarker measurements and vascular imaging data were extracted from clinically indicated chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder (CKD-MBD) and cardiovascular risk assessments documented in the medical record; no additional blood sampling or CT radiation exposure was performed solely for research. FGF23 testing was clinician-initiated rather than routine, so analyses incorporated prespecified approaches to evaluate potential selection bias. Vascular calcification was assessed using complementary modalities: simple vascular calcification score (SVCS) on plain radiographs, coronary artery calcification (CAC) by computed tomography, and abdominal aortic calcification (AAC) by computed tomography. Cardiovascular events were recorded during a median follow-up of 36 months. Associations between log-transformed FGF23 and outcomes were evaluated using multivariable regression with events-per-variable monitoring, and incremental predictive value was assessed with bootstrap-validated discrimination and reclassification metrics.

Results

FGF23 levels were significantly and positively correlated with all three vascular calcification scores. Patients in higher FGF23 tertiles demonstrated greater vascular calcification burden and a higher cumulative incidence of cardiovascular events. In fully adjusted Cox models, each unit increase in log-transformed FGF23 was associated with a higher hazard of cardiovascular events (HR 1.74, 95% CI: 1.18 - 2.56, p = 0.005). Addition of FGF23 to a base model improved bootstrap-corrected discrimination (optimism-corrected area under the curve increment 0.024) and reclassification (category-free net reclassification improvement 0.16, p = 0.002). Attenuation of the FGF23-event association after adjustment for vascular calcification scores was consistent with partial mediation through the calcification pathway, although formal causal mediation was not performed.

Conclusion

Elevated FGF23 levels are independently associated with greater vascular calcification burden and higher cardiovascular event risk in PD patients. FGF23 may contribute to refined cardiovascular risk stratification in this population, though prospective validation and formal mediation analyses are needed to clarify the underlying pathways.

title: The role and clinical significance of the miR‑378a‑3p/MAPK1 axis in hypertensive vascular remodeling.
authorString: Wang S, Hu S, Liu L, Li L.
abstractText:
Background

Primary hypertension is a prevalent cardiovascular disease contributing to a heavy global health burden. To investigate serum miR‑378a‑3p expression in hypertensive patients and its mechanism in OX‑LDL‑mediated vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) dysfunction.

Methods

Two hundred eighty-six primary hypertension patients and 132 healthy controls were enrolled, and serum miR‑378a‑3p levels and clinical parameters were detected. ROC curve and multivariate logistic regression were applied for diagnostic and risk factor analyses. In vitro cultured human aortic VSMCs were used to assess cell function, and phenotypic transformation via qRT‑PCR, CCK‑8, Transwell, and Western blot. Target gene binding was verified by bioinformatics and dual‑luciferase assay.

Results

miR‑378a‑3p was significantly downregulated in hypertensive patients and identified as an independent protective factor, whereas LDL‑C, PRA, Ang II, and ALD were independent risk factors. OX‑LDL downregulated miR‑378a‑3p and promoted VSMC dysfunction, while miR‑378a‑3p overexpression alleviated these injuries by directly targeting MAPK1.

Conclusions

miR-378a-3p shows potential as an auxiliary screening biomarker for hypertension risk stratification and may serve as a promising therapeutic target by regulating VSMC function via MAPK1.

title: Robot-Assisted Radical Cystectomy: Recommendations from Latin American Experts Consensus on Surgical Strategy, Urinary Reconstruction, and Oncological and Func-tional Outcomes.
authorString: Faria EF, Rodriguez A, Pompeo A, Fazoli A, Vaz C, Watanabe C, Fraga C, Chade D, Brazão E, Bodden E, Korkes F, Cárcano F, Hidelbrando F, Almeida G, Guimarães G, Zampoli H, Palou J, Pedrosa JA, Fornazieri L, Kerkebe M, Moschovas M, Tobias-Machado M, Nister M, Paiva M, Luz M, Jorge N, Melo P, Romanelli P, Wiklund P, Coelho R, Rocha R, Sotelo R, Mehrazino R, Machado R, Borges R, Valente R, Kool R, Zequi S, Zacchi S, Patel V, Villamil W, Gualberto R.

journal.title: International braz j urol : official journal of the Brazilian Society of Urology

abstractText:
Purpose

To develop contemporary evidence-informed recommendations for robot-assisted radical cystectomy (RARC), urinary reconstruction, and perioperative management, integrating current evidence with the experience of Latin American experts in uro-oncology and robotic surgery.

Materials and methods

A modified Delphi consensus process was conducted involving 42 experts with extensive experience in RARC. Topics included patient selection, perioperative optimization, enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS), lymph node dissection, urinary reconstruction, functional preservation, perioperative systemic therapy, complex clinical scenarios, and emerging robotic technologies. A comprehensive literature review was performed using Medline, Scopus, and Web of Science through November 2025, following PRISMA principles and incorporating recommendations from EAU, AUA/ASCO/SUO, and NCCN guidelines. Consensus was defined as ≥75% agreement.

Results

Consensus supported routine implementation of ERAS protocols, structured frailty and nutritional assessment, extended pelvic lymph node dissection, and perioperative systemic therapy in eligible patients. Intracorporeal urinary diversion was associated with improved recovery and lower wound-related morbidity. Nerve-sparing and organ-preserving approaches were recommended in selected patients to optimize continence, sexual function, and quality of life. Orthotopic neobladder reconstruction should be individualized according to oncologic safety, functional status, renal function, and patient preference. RARC was considered feasible in complex settings, including obesity, bulky lymphadenopathy, locally advanced disease, and salvage surgery, when performed in experienced high-volume centers. Areas without consensus included urinary drainage strategies and antibiotic prophylaxis duration.

Conclusions

This expert consensus provides recommendations for RARC and urinary reconstruction, aiming to standardize practice, optimize perioperative care, and improve oncological and functional outcomes. Future prospective studies are needed.

title: Vertebral computed tomography attenuation to case-find low bone density in people undergoing lung cancer screening.
authorString: Patel N, Dahl K, O'Rourke R, Williamson A, Lee JC, Fong KM, Yang IA, Marshall HM.
abstractText:
Objective

Lung cancer screening (LCS) participants are "high-risk" for osteoporotic fracture. We compared lumbar vertebral Hounsfield unit CT-attenuation (VHU) from LCS images with standard dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), quantitative CT (QCT) and clinical fracture risk tools to identify participants with low bone mineral density (BMD), prevalent vertebral fracture (VF) and incident osteoporotic fracture.

Methods

LCS participants were cross-sectionally analyzed at a 2-year follow-up time point. BMD was assessed from paired LCS chest low-dose CT (VHU and spine QCT) and DXA scans (T-scores). FRAX and Garvan 10-year fracture risks were calculated from questionnaires. VFs were assessed semi-quantitatively from CT scans; 2-year incident VFs were identified by comparing baseline and 2-year follow-up CT scans. Participants self-reported 2-year incident osteoporotic fractures. Method discrimination for low DXA-BMD (T-score < -1), prevalent VFs and incident fractures was compared.

Results

In 91 participants (M:F = 0.75), VHU moderately discriminated low DXA-BMD moderately (AUC, 0.74), similar to QCT (AUC, 0.73), FRAX (AUC, 0.82) and Garvan (AUC, 0.78) (P > .05). VHU performed similarly to DXA spine T-score, QCT, FRAX, and Garvan in discrimination for both prevalent VF (AUC, 0.71) and incident fractures (AUC, 0.71). Correlation and inter-method reliability between VHU and DXA-T-scores were fair (R = 0.42, ĸ < 0.3).

Conclusion

In LCS, VHU is a convenient alternative to case-finding screenees with occult osteoporosis, having comparable discrimination to standard methods for low BMD and osteoporotic fractures.

Advances in knowledge

Within-population comparison of osteoporosis assessment methods, shows that VHU can comparably "case-find" LCS participants with occult osteoporotic disease and incident fractures, warranting larger prospective studies.

title: SEVERE RETINAL NONPERFUSION IS ASSOCIATED WITH FEWER RETINAL LESIONS ON ULTRAWIDE-FIELD FUNDUS PHOTOGRAPHY IN PROLIFERATIVE DIABETIC RETINOPATHY.
authorString: Torres-Villaros H, Lachiver L, Fajnkuchen F, Morel JB, Arsalane M, Giocanti-Aurégan A.
abstractText:
Purpose

To explore the relationship between the number of retinal lesions observed on ultrawide-field fundus photography (UWF-FP) and the nonperfusion index (NPI) quantified on UWF fluorescein angiography in patients with proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR).

Methods

The NPI was measured on early-phase UWF fluorescein angiography in 100 eyes from 100 patients with PDR, including both type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Eyes were divided into quartiles based on NPI values. Red dots (microaneurysms, retinal hemorrhages, and intraretinal microvascular abnormalities), venous beading, cotton-wool spots, and white thread-like arterioles were counted on UWF-FP.

Results

The mean NPI values for quartiles one to four were 2.8 ± 1.1%, 8.5 ± 2.1%, 17.3 ± 4.5%, and 42.8 ± 12.2%, respectively. Eyes in the highest NPI quartile (quartile 4) had significantly fewer retinal lesions on UWF-FP (76.1 ± 50.6) and fewer cotton-wool spots compared with those in the lowest NPI quartile, which showed 253.0 ± 165.5 retinal lesions ( P < 0.001). White thread-like arterioles were present in 80.0% of eyes in quartile four and none in quartile 1. Patients in quartile four were predominantly type 2 diabetics with higher rates of end-stage kidney disease, peripheral neuropathy, lower-extremity peripheral artery disease, and prior limb amputation or revascularization.

Conclusion

In patients with poorly controlled, long-standing type 2 diabetes complicated by renal failure, peripheral neuropathy, peripheral arterial disease, or lower-limb amputation, fluorescein angiography should be considered when highly ischemic PDR is suspected, particularly in the presence of white thread-like arterioles, as it may otherwise appear milder on color fundus photography.

title: Dissociation of unfolded protein response signaling and endoplasmic reticulum ultrastructure during 4-PBA therapy in shunt-driven pulmonary hypertension.
authorString: Xu X, Chen L, Sun K, Qin X, Zhang C, Li J, Tang B, Li F, Wang J.
abstractText:
Background

Pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with congenital heart disease (PAH-CHD) arises from chronic left-to-right shunting and high-flow exposure, leading to pulmonary vascular remodeling and right-heart dysfunction. Whether high-flow shunting induces branch-selective unfolded protein response (UPR) activation and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) structural adaptation in pulmonary vascular smooth muscle remains incompletely defined.

Methods

Rats underwent right pulmonary artery ligation combined with left common carotid artery-external jugular vein shunting (RPAL/LCS), with or without 4-phenylbutyric acid (4-PBA) treatment. Hemodynamics, right-heart function, vascular remodeling, UPR signaling, transcriptomic profiles, apoptosis, and ER ultrastructure were assessed in vivo or in HPASMC gain- and loss-of-function experiments.

Results

RPAL/LCS increased RVSP from 22.46 ± 1.68 to 59.66 ± 7.06 mmHg, whereas 4-PBA reduced RVSP to 38.24 ± 1.71 mmHg. The wall area/total vessel area ratio increased from 46.88 ± 1.69% to 77.89 ± 3.08% after RPAL/LCS and decreased to 47.19 ± 2.00% after 4-PBA treatment. Lung immunoblotting showed increased p-IRE1α/IRE1α, whereas p-PERK/PERK and ATF6N/ATF6 did not differ significantly; these proximal UPR markers were not reduced by 4-PBA at the endpoint. In HPASMCs, ATF4 and ATF6N overexpression enriched apoptosis-related programs and induced ER swelling and fragmentation, whereas XBP-1s overexpression maintained organized ER cisternae and XBP-1s knockdown disrupted ER ultrastructure with increased Annexin V-positive apoptotic cells.

Conclusions

This study suggests that the IRE1α-XBP1s axis supports adaptive ER proteostasis and structural organization in shunt-driven pulmonary hypertension, whereas 4-PBA improves disease features without measurable suppression of canonical UPR branch activation markers.

title: "Okay, you're moving to the adult world": perspectives on transitioning users of home mechanical ventilation to adult care.
authorString: Friesen JMR, Koke K, Wright MFA.

journal.title: Annals of the American Thoracic Society

abstractText:
Rationale

Children requiring long-term home mechanical ventilation (HMV) increasingly survive into adulthood. However, structured processes to support their transition from pediatric to adult care are lacking. Understanding the perspectives of patients, caregivers, and health and social care providers (HSCPs) is critical to improving transition experiences and outcomes.

Objectives

To explore the experiences, perceptions, and priorities of patients, caregivers, and providers involved in the transition of young people using HMV from pediatric to adult care, and to identify practical targets for improvement.

Methods

We conducted semi-structured interviews and focus groups with the following participant groups: pediatric and adult HSCPs (n = 14) and patients aged 17 to 21 years with experience of HMV (n = 7) and their caregivers (n = 9). Iterative inductive thematic analysis was performed. Patient partners with lived experience contributed to study design, development of data collection tools, and analysis.

Results

Four key themes emerged: (1) The absence of a formal transition framework left patients and caregivers unclear about expectations, timelines, and responsibilities; (2) care continuity and coordination were often disrupted, with prolonged gaps between pediatric and adult care and confusion over roles of providers; (3) patients were insufficiently prepared for differences in adult care, including greater self-management expectations; and (4) providers reported systemic barriers, including lack of institutional support, insufficient resources, and overreliance on individual "transition champions" to drive processes. These challenges were consistently reported across participant groups.

Conclusions

Young people using HMV face significant challenges during and after their transition to adult care. Priorities for improvement include the need for structured transition protocols, early planning, education about adult care expectations, and formalized handovers between services. Sustainable improvements require operational support and integration of transition planning into routine care from early adolescence. Future research should evaluate the impact of formalized transition models on patient experiences and outcomes.

title: Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells-derived exosomes ameliorate doxorubicin-induced nephrotoxicity via the modulation of pyroptosis-associated signaling.
authorString: Shahin RK, Elazazy O, Wahdan SA, AbdelHamid SG.
abstractText: Doxorubicin (DOX) remains a cornerstone chemotherapeutic agent whose clinical application is constrained by nephrotoxicity, with no therapeutic interventions currently available. This study aimed to delineate the ameliorative potential of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs) derived exosomes (EXO) in an experimental model of DOX-induced acute kidney injury (AKI). Twenty-four rats were divided into 4 groups: Control, DOX intoxicated, DOX + EXO, and EXO only groups. Nephrotoxicity was induced in the DOX and DOX + EXO groups using a single dose of DOX (15 mg/ kg i.p.). After 24 h, DOX + EXO and EXO only groups were given BM-MSCs-derived exosomes (100 μg i.v.). DOX was associated with a decline in renal function, activation of oxidative stress, inflammation, and modulation of pyroptosis-associated inflammasome-related signaling. BM-MSCs-derived exosomes significantly improved renal function, as evidenced by histopathological examination, reduction in KIM-1, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), serum creatinine, and renal somatic index (RSI). Exosomes mitigated oxidative stress by enhancing endogenous antioxidant catalase activity and reducing the lipid peroxidation marker MDA, while also suppressing inflammatory mediators, as shown by a reduction in IL-18 and IL-1β. Furthermore, exosomal treatment attenuated the expression of NLRP3, caspase-1 (CASP-1), and gasdermin-D (GSDMD), reduced ELAVL1, IRAK1 and NF-κB levels, while upregulating miR-146a-5p. In Silico analysis identified multiple putative molecular targets for miR-146a-5p, revealing strong interconnection among key targets, including ELAVL1, NF-κB, and IRAK1. These findings provide evidence to support the ameliorative role of BM-MSC-derived exosomes in mitigating DOX-induced AKI, associated with upregulation of miR-146a-5p and concurrent modulation of ELAVL1, IRAK1, and NF-κB, as well as NLRP3-associated inflammatory signaling, supporting the biological plausibility of a candidate miR-146a-5p/ELAVL1/IRAK1/NF-κB/NLRP3 regulatory network in AKI pathogenesis. Harnessing the reno-protective properties of exosomal therapy, as well as targeting the inflammasome-related signaling pathways, represents a compelling therapeutic paradigm warranting further mechanistic validation.

title: Clinical outcomes and midterm durability of the preloading coil-in-plug technique in various arterial territories.
authorString: Nakai T, Iwakoshi S, Iwata M, Kishida H, Oshima K, Ichihashi S, Tanaka T.
abstractText:
Background

Conventional coil embolization of large or high-flow arteries may require multiple coils and a long embolization segment. The Amplatzer Vascular Plug (AVP) enables controlled deployment and repositioning; however, complete occlusion partly depends on thrombus formation, and residual flow or recanalization may occur. The preloading coil-in-plug (P-CIP) technique combines the positional stability of an AVP with internal coil packing. This study evaluated its technical feasibility, procedural characteristics, safety, and mid-term imaging outcomes across different arterial territories.

Methods

This retrospective single-center study evaluated consecutive patients who underwent P-CIP embolization between April 2018 and April 2026. Before insertion, a microcatheter was passed through the nitinol mesh into the internal space of an AVP I outside the patient. The plug and microcatheter were advanced together and deployed at the target site before plug detachment. Coils were then packed within the expanded plug through the preloaded microcatheter. Technical success, AVP-to-vessel diameter ratio, coil use, coil-packing time, procedure-related complications, target-vessel recanalization, and reintervention were evaluated. Imaging follow-up was based on contrast-enhanced computed tomography.

Results

The study included 34 patients, of whom 21 were men, with 40 embolized vessels. The target vessels were the celiac artery in 6 procedures, internal iliac artery in 25, superior or inferior gluteal artery in 8, and external iliac artery in 1. Technical success and final angiographic occlusion were achieved in all 40 vessels. The mean AVP-to-vessel diameter ratio was 1.44, corresponding to 44% oversizing. The mean number of coils used per AVP was 3.13, and the mean coil-packing time was 10.7 min. During a mean imaging follow-up of 619 days, no procedure-related complications, target-vessel recanalization, device migration, or reintervention occurred. Ten patients died during follow-up, but none of the deaths was related to embolization.

Conclusions

P-CIP embolization was technically feasible across multiple arterial territories and achieved sustained target-vessel occlusion during mid-term imaging follow-up. The technique may be useful when controlled short-segment embolization is required. Comparative studies are needed to determine whether P-CIP provides advantages over conventional coil embolization or AVP placement alone.

title: Dose-Response Relationship Between Triglyceride Glucose-Waist Height Ratio Index and Cardiometabolic Multimorbidity Among Chinese Middle-Aged and Older People.
authorString: Li L, Yu Z, Feng Y, Sun C, Hu L, Liu X, Li L, Wu M, Liu L.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) is a growing public health challenge. The triglyceride glucose-waist height ratio (TyG-WHtR) is a novel index linked to metabolic disorders. This study explores the dose-response relationship between TyG-WHtR and CMM.

Methods

Data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), including the 2011 baseline survey and the 2018 follow-up survey with an average follow-up duration of 7.0 years, were analyzed. Multivariate logistic regression and restricted cubic spline models assessed the TyG-WHtR-CMM relationship, adjusting for covariates.

Results

The study enrolled 6674 individuals, and 1140 patients with cardiometabolic multimorbidity and 5534 patients with non-cardiometabolic multimorbidity were documented over an average follow-up duration of 7.0 years. The fourth TyG-WHtR quartile group (Q4) had the highest CMM risk, with an odds ratio of 1.23 and a 95% confidence interval of 1.20-1.26. The restricted cubic spline regression model showed a nonlinear (p < 0.001) association between TyG-WHtR and CMM. Subgroup analyses showed that the positive association between TyG-WHtR and CMM was evident among females and ex-smokers. A notable interaction was observed between TyG-WHtR and variables like age and marital status.

Conclusion

TyG-WHtR is a potential CMM predictor, and maintaining it within a moderate range may help prevent CMM.

title: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation for refractory arrhythmia in a neonate carrying an SCN5A variant: a case report.
authorString: Yixian C, Yuan G, Senxiong Z, Xianqiang L, Yongjiang J, Mingyun T, Yunzhi L, Yanxing L, Yijun W.

journal.title: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background

Neonatal malignant arrhythmias refractory to conventional antiarrhythmic therapy are life-threatening and pose a major therapeutic challenge, particularly in premature infants.

Case presentation

We report a premature infant born at 36 + 2 weeks of gestation who developed ventricular tachycardia and cardiac arrest following resuscitation for perinatal asphyxia. As lidocaine and amiodarone failed to control the rhythm, veno‑arterial ECMO was initiated shortly thereafter. After ECMO support, the rhythm converted to sinus and cardiac function improved, allowing successful weaning. Electrocardiography subsequently revealed a prolonged QT interval, which responded to oral mexiletine. Whole‑exome sequencing identified a heterozygous SCN5A c.1960G > A (p.Glu654Lys) variant inherited from the father, classified as a variant of uncertain significance (VUS).

Conclusions

This case suggests that this specific VUS may be a candidate pathogenic variant, and that early ECMO can be an effective salvage therapy when conventional drugs fail. Additionally, when genetic testing yields a VUS, the clinical phenotype and treatment response appear valuable for assessing pathogenicity in neonatal cases.

title: AnySleep: a channel-agnostic deep learning system for high-resolution sleep staging in multi-center cohorts.
authorString: Grieger N, Raskob J, Mehrkanoon S, Bialonski S.
abstractText: Sleep is essential for health, yet studying its dynamics requires manual sleep staging, a labor-intensive step in research and clinical care. Across centers, polysomnography (PSG) recordings are traditionally scored in 30-s epochs for pragmatic, not physiological, reasons and vary in electrode count, montage, and subject characteristics. These constraints challenge harmonized multi-center studies and the discovery of robust biomarkers on shorter timescales. We present AnySleep, a deep neural network that scores sleep from any electroencephalography (EEG) or electrooculography (EOG) data at adjustable temporal resolutions. We trained and validated the model on over 20,000 overnight recordings (>200,000 h of EEG and EOG) from 28 datasets across multiple clinics to promote robust generalization across sites. The model attains state-of-the-art performance and surpasses or equals established baselines at 30-s epochs. Performance improves with more channels, yet remains strong when EOG is absent, or only EOG or single EEG derivations (frontal, central, or occipital) are available. On sub-30-s timescales, the model captures short wake intrusions consistent with arousals and improves the prediction of pathophysiological conditions (obstructive sleep apnea, narcolepsy type 1, insomnia) over 30-s scoring. We make the model publicly available to facilitate large-scale studies with heterogeneous electrode setups and accelerate biomarker discovery in sleep.

title: Metabolic reprogramming in macrophages: the central role of lipid metabolism in bone homeostasis.
authorString: Li L, Zhang Y, Huang S, Xiao Y, Liu G, Wu Z, Hu Y, Gong S, Mao J, Song K, Li Q.
abstractText: Macrophage lipid metabolism is a pivotal regulator of bone homeostasis. Macrophages orchestrate the balance between bone resorption and formation primarily through their M1/M2 polarization states, with M1 macrophages promoting resorption and M2 macrophages supporting formation. This review comprehensively describes how key lipid metabolic pathways, such as fatty acid oxidation (FAO) and cholesterol metabolism, govern this polarization and subsequent bone remodeling. It integrates the core mechanisms by which lipid metabolism drives M1 and M2 polarization, and highlights that targeting macrophage lipid metabolism represents a promising therapeutic strategy for bone diseases. Finally, we identify emerging frontiers, including the "gut-bone axis" and epigenetic regulation, as critical directions for future research.

title: Association between coronary artery calcium score and myocardial ischemia assessed by stress perfusion cardiac magnetic resonance imaging.
authorString: Kaolawanich Y, Meechuen M, Laohabut I, Ruengchaisiwawaith T, Boonyasirinant T.
abstractText:
Background

Coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring effectively stratifies cardiovascular risk, and stress perfusion cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) accurately detects myocardial ischemia. We aimed to investigate the prevalence and factors associated with myocardial ischemia on CMR in patients with CAC, and to assess the clinical impact of myocardial ischemia following CMR.

Methods

This study included 215 patients aged ≥18 years who underwent CAC scoring for risk stratification, followed by stress CMR between 2013 and 2026. The prevalence and predictors of myocardial ischemia were investigated. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to assess the association between CAC scores and myocardial ischemia. Additionally, subsequent clinical management following CMR was determined.

Results

The mean age was 69.3 ± 9.1 years (60.9% male). The average 10-year PREVENT risk score was 18.6 ± 8.7%. Overall, myocardial ischemia was present in 26.0% of patients (56/215): 17.1% in the CAC 300-999 Agatston units (AU) group (14/82) and 41.6% in the CAC ≥ 1,000 AU group (42/101). CAC score was the only independent predictor of myocardial ischemia (adjusted OR 1.07, 95%CI 1.03 - 1.10; p < 0.001 per 100 AU). Across clinical risk score categories and diabetes status, CAC score was consistently associated with myocardial ischemia, with no significant interactions observed (all p for interaction >0.05).The number of ischemic segments increased with increasing CAC scores (p < 0.001). ROC analysis demonstrated an optimal cutoff threshold of CAC ≥ 1,093 AU for detecting myocardial ischemia (AUC 0.75, p < 0.001). The clinical impact of stress CMR included medication changes in 37.2% of patients, while 18.1% underwent invasive procedures.

Conclusions

In patients with CAC scores undergoing stress CMR, the prevalence of myocardial ischemia was approximately one-fourth and was associated with higher CAC scores. Stress CMR may influence clinical management in this population. Larger or prospective studies validating these findings and evaluating prognosis are warranted.

title: Augmenting intercellular mitochondrial transfer for tissue repair and rejuvenation.
authorString: Soukar J, Jones K, Garza NM, Duran Salas V, Roy S, Gohil VM, Gaharwar AK.
abstractText: Cells exhibit innate reparative communication, enabling the exchange of bioactive molecules and, in some cases, entire organelles. Harnessing this endogenous process of intercellular organelle transfer represents an emerging therapeutic paradigm for restoring cellular function in diseases driven by organelle dysfunction. Mitochondrial transfer has gained prominence for its ability to restore bioenergetic capacity, mitigate oxidative stress, and rescue metabolic function in cells with impaired mitochondrial activity. Given that genetic or acquired defects in mitochondrial function are associated with diverse pathologies, including neurodegeneration, cardiovascular diseases, metabolic disorders, skeletal muscle defects, immune dysregulation, and age-associated decline, mitochondrial transfer offers broad therapeutic potential. Mitochondrial transfer seeks to deliver functional mitochondria to injured cells to reestablish metabolic competence. However, insufficient organelle trafficking and limited control over transfer dynamics remain critical barriers to clinical translation. Recent biotechnological developments aimed at enhancing donor-recipient connectivity, increasing mitochondrial availability, and modulating transfer machinery have begun to address some of these key challenges. This review highlights recent advances in mitochondrial transfer bioengineering, emerging therapeutic applications, and key challenges that must be resolved to enable clinical deployment.

title: Extracellular vesicle-mediated restraint of hepatic CD74-NF-κB repairs diabetic neuropathy.
authorString: Yang H, Miao Y, Meng P, Niu J, Xi J, Zou Z, Hei Y, Zhao J, Luo Q, Huang S, Hu M, Zhang L, Baskys A, Wang Y, Li X, Long Q.
abstractText: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) affects up to half of people with diabetes and lacks disease-modifying therapy. Here, we profiled MSC-EV biodistribution and multiomic programs across diabetic models, with key nerve repair established in db/db mice and corroborated in high-fat diet/streptozotocin- and methionine-choline-deficient mice. Systemically administered EVs predominantly accumulated in the liver and improved peripheral nerve structure and function, with benefits supported by glycemia-controlled or glycemia-adjusted analyses rather than being fully explained by systemic glycemic changes. EV treatment was associated with reduced circulating injury markers, attenuated spinal inflammatory responses, and improved endothelial junction integrity. Mechanistically, EV-encapsulated miR-24-3p repressed hepatic CD74, coinciding with reduced MHC II/NF-κB activity in macrophages. Hepatic CD74 overexpression promoted systemic inflammation and peripheral nerve injury, whereas pharmacologic NF-κB inhibition recapitulated EV-associated benefits. Together, these data define a liver-to-nerve causal axis and support EV-mediated restraint of hepatic CD74-NF-κB signaling as a cross-organ strategy for DPN repair.

title: Advancing Perioperative Medicine With AI: Current Landscape and Research Priorities.
authorString: Rohatgi N, Mathur P.
abstractText:
Unlabelled

AI is increasingly being applied across the perioperative continuum. AI should be viewed as a technology that can reduce cognitive burden, collate fragmented data into clinically meaningful information, support decision-making, and extend precision education to clinicians and patients. This editorial accompanies the JMIR Perioperative Medicine webinar held in May 2026 and presents our perspectives-informed by our clinical experience-on where AI can assist perioperative clinicians and surgical patients, the evidence available today, what is still needed, and how clinicians can prepare to practice alongside AI tools. We consider opportunities in preoperative risk assessment and optimization; intraoperative intelligent decision support; emerging technologies, such as surgical digital twins; and postoperative recovery, monitoring, and prediction of clinical deterioration. Most AI applications remain early and require large-scale, prospective validation across diverse populations and resource settings. Realizing their potential also requires confronting substantial challenges, including limited and fragmented training data, the specialized models needed to interpret the large volumes of data captured in operative videos and during physiological monitoring, biases embedded in data and algorithms or biases inherent in human-AI interactions, and the determination of where human oversight is essential and where it is not feasible. When used responsibly, with human judgment remaining paramount, AI offers an unprecedented opportunity to advance perioperative care.

title: A soft wireless bioelectronic patch for noninvasive modulation of cavernosal microenvironment in diabetic erectile dysfunction.
authorString: Wu H, Chen Y, Tong Y, Tang W, Li J, Jiang X, Zheng Z, Wang Y, Yin D, Dong Z, Chen Q, Yang K, Liu F, Fang Y, Chen D, Yan M, Song T, Chen X, Jiao Y, Hong K, Chang L, Lin H.
abstractText: Diabetes mellitus-induced erectile dysfunction is difficult to reverse due to long-term impairment of cavernosal microenvironment. Conventional oral or intracavernosal injection therapies suffer from poor targeting, uneven drug distribution, and potential complications. Here, we propose a soft, wireless electronic patch for treating erectile dysfunction (SWEED) in diabetes mellitus, which enables safe, noninvasive, and controllable modulation of penile microenvironment. With its "microelectrode-drug reservoir-nanopore" configuration, SWE intensifies local electrical field nanoscopically and achieves uniform transdermal drug delivery. Through the enhanced local delivery of prostaglandin E1 (PGE1), SWEED demonstrates high efficiency in promoting the expression of vascular factors for endothelial repair and enhancing cavernosal blood perfusion. In both in vitro and in vivo settings, the platform achieves vascular regeneration and functional recovery comparable to clinical intracavernosal injection therapy. Moreover, it activates proerectile signaling pathways (EP2/PKA/CREB) and suppresses the TGF-β/Smad pathway, markedly alleviating cavernosal fibrosis. This work presents a paradigm for noninvasive diabetes mellitus-induced erectile dysfunction therapy.

title: Isolated Disturbance of Consciousness as Initial Presentation of Staphylococcus aureus Endocarditis: A Case Report With Brief Literature Review.
authorString: Zhong W, Huang S, Jiang J, Tan Z.

journal.title: The American journal of case reports

abstractText: BACKGROUND Infective endocarditis (IE) typically presents with fever, a heart murmur, or constitutional symptoms, making diagnosis challenging when neurological manifestations predominate. We report an atypical case of IE in which disturbance of consciousness was the initial manifestation. CASE REPORT A man in his 50s was admitted to our hospital with isolated disturbance of consciousness and no history of fever; a temperature of 38°C was recorded on admission. Investigations confirmed an extensive acute right hemispheric watershed (border-zone) infarction involving the right temporoparietal lobe, without evidence of hemorrhagic transformation or intracranial hemorrhage. Subsequent workup identified Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia, mitral valve vegetation, and multiple organ dysfunction syndrome. The absence of classic IE risk factors contributed to a delayed diagnosis. Guideline-concordant clinical management was implemented. Long-term outcome data were unavailable because of patient transfer; only in-hospital mortality (after transfer) was confirmed. We discuss the application of the 2023 Duke criteria to this case and examine factors contributing to the delayed diagnosis of IE. Disturbance of consciousness as the predominant initial manifestation of S. aureus IE is rare and frequently results in diagnostic delay. This case underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for IE in patients with sepsis complicated by acute cerebral infarction, particularly among critical care and neurology clinicians. CONCLUSIONS This case highlights isolated disturbance of consciousness as an atypical initial presentation of IE. Although IE is frequently complicated by acute cerebral infarction, clinicians may not routinely consider IE in the differential diagnosis of patients presenting with disturbed consciousness.

title: Fundamental Strategies and Technical Perspectives in Bile Duct Anastomosis for Living Donor Liver Transplantation: Growth From Novice to Maturity.
authorString: Kim SM, Kang WH, Hwang S, Moon DB, Ahn CS, Kim KH, Ha TY, Song GW, Jung DH, Park GC, Yoon YI, Lee SG.
abstractText: BACKGROUND Biliary reconstruction is the most technically demanding step in living donor liver transplantation (LDLT), yet how a single surgeon's technique matures in the early career, and how this relates to clinical outcomes, remains incompletely characterized. This study evaluated whether the stepwise evolution of surgical technique was associated with a lower anastomotic biliary stricture (BS) rate. MATERIAL AND METHODS We retrospectively analyzed 382 consecutive right-lobe LDLTs with single-surgeon duct-to-duct biliary anastomosis performed between April 2020 and April 2024. Cases were grouped into 3 equal, consecutive time intervals (approximately 16 months each), and cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis was applied to the learning trajectory. Independent risk factors for BS were identified by multivariable logistic regression, with separate models for surgical period and post-transition-point status. RESULTS BS rates decreased across periods from 14.4% to 10.1% to 5.1% (P trend=0.016). CUSUM identified a primary transition at case 33, ending the initial trial-and-error phase and coinciding with adoption of well-vascularized distal recipient duct selection, and a secondary inflection at case 210 coinciding with eversion-overlap anastomosis with hilar plate anchoring. Portal vein stenting (OR 6.515, P=0.004) and ABO-incompatible transplantation (OR 2.462, P=0.016) were independent risk factors. After adjustment, surgical period (OR 0.596, P=0.027) and post-case-33 status (OR 0.291, P=0.010) remained associated with lower BS odds. CONCLUSIONS In this single-surgeon cohort, the stepwise evolution of surgical technique was associated with a progressive reduction in BS rates, alongside the cumulative standardization of fundamental principles, but a concurrently evolving case mix precludes attribution to technique alone.

title: Anticoagulation management and valve-related outcomes after mechanical valve implantation in patients with Fontan palliation.
authorString: Bankes AC, Majdalany DS, Jokhadar M, Dearani JA, Egbe AC.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Int J Cardiol Congenit Heart Dis
journal.title: International journal of cardiology. Congenital heart disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Int J Cardiol Congenit Heart Dis

abstractText:
Background

Valvular dysfunction is a major contributor to morbidity in adults with Fontan palliation. Mechanical valve replacement offers superior durability compared with bioprostheses but requires lifelong anticoagulation, raising concern in the prothrombotic and low-flow Fontan circulation. Data on long-term outcomes after mechanical valve implantation in this population remains limited.

Objectives

To evaluate long-term bleeding, thromboembolic, valve-related, and cardiovascular outcomes after mechanical valve replacement in adults with Fontan palliation.

Methods

We retrospectively studied 26 adults with Fontan circulation who underwent mechanical aortic or atrioventricular valve replacement between 2003 and 2024. Outcomes included (1) major bleeding/thromboembolic complications, (2) valve-related complications, and (3) composite cardiovascular events (valve-related complications, death, or transplant). Events were analyzed as time-to-event endpoints. Anticoagulation control was assessed by time in therapeutic range (TTR).

Results

Median age at valve implantation was 21 (15-28) years. Fifteen prostheses were implanted in the atrioventricular position and 11 in the aortic position. Median follow-up was 14.3 years (364 patient-years). TTR was 71% for atrioventricular and 79% for aortic prostheses. Four patients experienced major bleeding/thromboembolic events. Ten- and 20-year cumulative incidences of major bleeding/thromboembolism were 9% and 22%, respectively. Valve-related complication rates were 13% and 28% at 10 and 20 years. Composite cardiovascular event rates were 31% and 60% at 10 and 20 years, driven primarily by progressive Fontan failure rather than prosthetic dysfunction.

Conclusions

Mechanical valve replacement in selected Fontan patients provides durable valve performance with acceptable long-term complication rates. Outcomes appear largely determined by the natural history of Fontan physiology rather than prosthesis-related failure.

title: Different concentrations of atropine in children with high myopia: a 2-year multicenter double-blind, randomized controlled trial.
authorString: Du L, Liu Z, Cheng T, Yan W, Ke B, Yuan Y, Li X, Zhou J, Chen J, Wang J, Pang CP, Zou H, Gao W, Xu X, He X.
abstractText: High myopia in children risks irreversible visual impairment, yet optimal interventions remain debated. This multicenter double-blind, randomized-controlled trial aims to evaluate the effect and safety of different atropine eyedrops for myopia control in children with high myopia, conducted in Shanghai Eye Diseases Prevention and Treatment Center, Shanghai General Hospital and Shanghai Ninth People's Hospital. Recruitment started on July 4<sup>th</sup>, 2021 and final follow-up was August, 21<sup>st</sup>, 2024. 219 children aged 6-12 years with myopia of at least -5.0 diopter (D) were recruited and randomly assigned to use either 0.01%(N = 76), 0.04%(N = 72), or 0.10%(N = 71) atropine eyedrops once nightly for both eyes over 24 months, and 182 participants completed trial; 219 (76:72:71) randomized cases were analyzed. Main outcome was cycloplegic spherical equivalent (SE) change from baseline over 24 months. After 24 months, mean SE progression was -0.92 D, -0.78 D and -0.56 D for 0.01%, 0.04% and 0.10% atropine, respectively. The 0.10% atropine significantly reduced myopia progression by 0.35 D (95%CI: 0.12 D, 0.58 D) versus 0.01%, while 0.04% atropine did not show significant difference; however, at 12 months, both higher concentrations demonstrated significantly greater reductions (0.16 D and 0.30 D for 0.04% and 0.10%, respectively). Photophobia was the most common adverse event, reported by 9.0%, 10.6% and 18.8% in 0.01%, 0.04% and 0.10% atropine respectively in 12 months and 7.8%, 8.1% and 21.1% in 24 months. These results demonstrated that in children aged 6-12 years with high myopia, nightly use of 0.10% atropine for 24 months effectively and safely attenuated myopia progression. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04699357.

title: [KASID Guidelines for Sexuality, Fertility, Pregnancy, and Lactation in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: 2026].
authorString: Song EM, Yoon J, Kim SE, Kim DH, Yang YJ, Shin SY, Kim JE, Bae JH, Hong SM, Kang SB, Kim ES, Kim SJ, Lee J, Na SY, Park SJ, Park SH, Yun H, Kim TH, Lee YJ, Kim MH, Choi M, Moon W, Jung SA, Guidelines Committee of the Korean Association for the Study of Intestinal Diseases (KASID).

journal.title: The Korean journal of gastroenterology = Taehan Sohwagi Hakhoe chi

abstractText: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is commonly diagnosed during the reproductive years, making sexuality, fertility, pregnancy, and lactation central to long-term care. Misconceptions about heritability, fertility, and medication safety contribute to voluntary childlessness and discontinuation of effective therapy during pregnancy. Accumulating evidence indicates that disease activity, rather than IBD itself or most maintenance therapies, is the major determinant of adverse maternal and fetal outcomes, supporting a paradigm centered on remission before and throughout pregnancy. Meanwhile, newer biologics and small molecules have been incorporated into clinical practice despite limited human reproductive safety data. Uncertainties persist regarding drug continuation, disease monitoring, mode of delivery, breastfeeding, and live vaccination in infants exposed to biologics in utero, highlighting the need for guidance tailored to the Korean national immunization program. The Korean Association for the Study of Intestinal Diseases therefore developed the first guideline in Korea addressing sexuality, fertility, pregnancy, and lactation in patients with IBD. Recent international guidance informed the scope and key questions; however, all evidence was independently reviewed and synthesized, and all recommendations were developed de novo using the GRADE methodology. Given limited randomized trial evidence in pregnancy, evidence synthesis relied primarily on systematic reviews, pregnancy registries, and large cohort studies. Consequently, the certainty of evidence for all recommendations was low or very low. All statements underwent a modified Delphi consensus process. The final guideline comprises 40 statements across 11 chapters: 23 recommendation statements, 9 evidence statements, and 8 expert consensus statements. This guideline supports individualized care throughout the reproductive continuum.

title: Inclusive Time in Assessment: A Universal Design for Learning Perspective.
authorString: Murphy L, Escudero Fontan B, McVicker C, Kenna T.

journal.title: Studies in health technology and informatics

abstractText: The provision of extra time in assessment and formal examinations has long been administered as an individualised accommodation in higher education, a reactive measure granted only to students who can demonstrate the presence of a recognised disability or learning difference. While well-intentioned, this model is increasingly challenged by scholars and practitioners working within the Universal Design for Learning (UDL) framework, who argue that the gatekeeping structure of accommodations is a source of inequity and is not inclusive. UDL contends that learning environments should be proactively structured to reduce barriers and support the widest possible range of learners from the outset, rather than retrofitting adjustments. Based on empirical evidence of staff and student perceptions of additional time, a term we coin "inclusive time", we reveal the discourses that both enable and constrain the potential implementation of inclusive time and UDL principles for assessment more broadly.

title: Chronic Cardiac Conduit Masses in an Adolescent With a Right Ventricle-to-Pulmonary Artery Conduit.
authorString: Huynh G, Burton C, Coe Y, Robinson J.

title: Clinical, Immunological, and Environmental Determinants of Pediatric Respiratory Disorders: A Comprehensive Review of Long-Term Health Outcomes.
authorString: Sharma J, Kumar KS, Sharma A, Sheikh MK, Shukla AK, Shaikh SS.
abstractText: Pediatric respiratory disorders remain a major source of childhood morbidity, healthcare utilization, impaired quality of life, and long-term pulmonary vulnerability. The background of this review centers on the complex interaction between early-life clinical susceptibility, immune maturation, environmental exposure, respiratory infections, and social determinants in shaping pediatric airway health. The objective was to synthesize evidence on clinical, immunological, infectious, environmental, and social determinants relevant to pediatric asthma, recurrent wheeze, and associated long-term respiratory outcomes, including disease persistence, impaired lung-function trajectories, and later respiratory vulnerability. The methodology involved a structured literature search of studies published from 2015 to 2025 in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and Google Scholar, including observational studies, clinical studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and high-quality narrative reviews focused on infants, children, and adolescents. The evidence indicates that early-life respiratory vulnerability, recurrent viral infections, atopic and inflammatory pathways, microbiome alterations, environmental exposures, and social disadvantage may interact across childhood and contribute to heterogeneous long-term respiratory trajectories. Longitudinal cohort findings further show that some children maintain persistent airflow impairment into adulthood, whereas others demonstrate partial improvement over time. Because the available evidence is stronger for associations and prognostic trajectories than for intervention efficacy, preventive and clinical strategies should be interpreted cautiously, with emphasis on appropriate diagnosis, phenotype- and severity-based management, reduction of avoidable exposures, age-appropriate pulmonary-function monitoring, and equitable access to follow-up.

title: Serious Adverse Events in Adult ICU Patients: A Substudy of the PATIENCE Cohort.
authorString: Crone V, Møller MH, Granholm A, Perner A, Alhazzani W, Al-Fares A, Hästbacka J, Ostermann M, Pfortmueller CA, Ferrer R, Blaser AR, Keus E, Szczeklik W, Krag M.
abstractText:
Introduction

Prokinetic agents are used to enhance upper gastrointestinal motility, but adverse events related to these agents are poorly described. We aimed to provide detailed epidemiological data on predefined serious adverse events (SAEs) in a cohort of adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients with and without prokinetic treatment. We hypothesised that all predefined SAEs would occur in both patients treated and those not treated with prokinetic agents, and that a higher number of SAEs would occur among patients treated with prokinetic agents for more than three consecutive days.

Methods

This substudy of the inception cohort study "Prokinetic agents in adult intensive care unit patients" included acutely admitted adult ICU patients. The prokinetic agents assessed (exposures) were erythromycin, metoclopramide, domperidone, and prucalopride. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients experiencing at least one episode of five pre-specified SAEs during ICU stay (cardiac arrhythmias, cardiac arrest, vomiting with aspiration, diarrhoea, extrapyramidal symptoms). Secondary outcomes were (1) proportion of patients experiencing each SAE, (2) the proportion of patients experiencing any of the SAEs after prokinetic treatment stratified by longest consecutive treatment duration, (3) time from index ICU admission to first SAE and (4) time from prokinetic initiation to first SAE. All analyses were descriptive, summarising SAE proportions and timing overall and according to prokinetic exposure.

Results

Among 1440 adult ICU patients, 710 SAEs occurred in 354 patients (24.6%), most commonly cardiac arrhythmias (199/1440, 13.8%). Across the exposure groups, the proportion of patients experiencing one or more SAEs ranged from 23.0% to 42.5%. Among patients treated with prokinetic agents for > 3 consecutive days, 14/59 (23.7%) experienced a SAE, which was similar to the proportion observed among patients not receiving prokinetic agents (291/1.253, 23.2%). Most SAEs occurred on median Day 2 after ICU admission and on median Day 3 after prokinetic initiation.

Conclusion

One in four adult ICU patients experienced at least one SAE, with cardiac arrhythmias being the most frequent. Among patients receiving prokinetic agents, the proportion experiencing one or more SAEs ranged from 23.0% to 42.5% across treatment groups. The findings from this study may help inform the design of a future clinical trial.

Editorial comment

This analysis presents reported serious adverse event observed in an ICU trial cohort assessing gastrointestinal prokinetic drug effects. Serious adverse events were reported frequently in both the drug treatment groups and the comparison (no prokinetic drug) group. Types of serious adverse events reported are presented.

title: Characteristics and Outcomes After General Anaesthesia in Elderly Patients: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
authorString: Risager BH, Mortensen SØ, Pælestik MB, Stankovic N, Lind PC, Andersen LW.
abstractText:
Background

Elderly patients are more frail and have a higher burden of comorbidity, which could influence the risk of complications after anaesthesia. The aim of this study was to describe the elderly patient population undergoing general anaesthesia in Denmark.

Methods

This was a national registry-based observational cohort study of adult patients (≥ 18 years) undergoing general anaesthesia in Denmark in 2020 and 2021, with a primary focus on patients 80 years and above. Patient and procedure characteristics of interest were age, sex, BMI, ASA classification, Elixhauser Comorbidity Index, comorbidities, type of procedure, and class of priority. The primary outcome of interest was 30-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included acute kidney injury within 7 days, length of hospital stay, and number of days in the ICU.

Results

A total of 453,133 cases of general anaesthesia in 328,951 unique patients in Denmark during 2020 and 2021 were included in this study. Of these, 25,955 (8%) patients were 80 years of age and above. Elderly patients undergoing general anaesthesia were of higher ASA classification, suffered from a higher degree of comorbidity measured by Elixhauser Comorbidity Index, had a lower proportion of elective procedures and a higher proportion of expedited and urgent procedures. Mortality for all patients at 30 days was 1.5% (n = 4814). While mortality was low for cases aged between 18 and 65 years, 30-day mortality increased for each year after 65 years of age even after adjusting for covariates. Mortality was especially high for patients with high Elixhauser Comorbidity Index, high ASA classification, and for non-elective procedures.

Conclusion

In this nationwide registry-based cohort study, we described the elderly patient population undergoing general anaesthesia in Denmark. We found that 30-day mortality increased for each year after 65 years of age even after adjusting for covariates.

Editorial comment

This large cohort study from Denmark assesses perioperative case factors including age, comorbidity and more, then describing different risk levels for 30 day mortality, particularly with advanced age.

title: Naming What Cannot Be Named: Discourse, Power, and the Erosion of Equity Language in Professional Nursing Standards-A Case Study of AACN's 2026 Essentials Revision.
authorString: Ballout S, McKinley Yoder C.
abstractText: Professional nursing standards documents codify what a discipline holds itself accountable to know and act on, and they face increasing political pressure to narrow their equity commitments. In April 2026, the American Association of Colleges of Nursing (AACN) released a revised edition of The Essentials: Core Competencies for Professional Nursing Education, originally approved by member vote in 2021, without a member vote or documented evidence base. This study examined how this revision reconstituted equity-related discourse and what it makes sayable and unsayable in professional nursing education. Using a Foucauldian critical discourse analysis integrated with comparative document analysis. We treated the revision as an instrumental case study and compared both editions line by line. Of 76 document elements compared, 40 were revised, 6 removed, and 27 unchanged; the ten-domain competency architecture remained intact. The terms structural racism, social justice, health equity, and diversity, equity, and inclusion, which appeared 20, 21, 9, and 17 times, respectively, in the 2021 edition, are absent from the 2026 edition except for a single retained reference to diversity, equity, and inclusion. Analysis identified two distinct mechanisms: substantive rollback, in which requirements such as holistic admissions were withdrawn, and discursive retrenchment, in which competencies were retained but their named equity terms were replaced with generalized, outcome-neutral language. We argue that discursive retrenchment is especially consequential because it escapes standard accreditation review. We call for transparent, evidence-driven governance of the profession's foundational educational documents, wherever they are produced.

title: Effects of Participation in a Community-Based Food Cooperative on Food Security and Dietary Behaviours: A Pre-Post Study.
authorString: Hliounakis H, Kent K, Brooks C, Scavera J, Fleming C, Morrison N, Si L, Simmons D, Wu JHY, Chapman L, MacMillan F.

journal.title: Health promotion journal of Australia : official journal of Australian Association of Health Promotion Professionals

abstractText:
Introduction

Community-based food cooperatives have shown potential in addressing food insecurity, but longitudinal evidence assessing their impact is limited. This study evaluated the effects of participating in a community-based food cooperative on food insecurity, dietary behaviours, and physical health outcomes among Australian adults.

Methods

A pre-post survey of new cooperative members measured demographics, household food insecurity status (United States Department of Agriculture 6-item Household Food Security Survey Module (HFSSM)), dietary behaviours (servings/day of core food groups), and objective physical health indicators (weight, waist circumference, and blood pressure). Participants were classified as secure (HFSSM score = 0) or insecure (HFSSM score ≥ 1). A McNemar's test assessed the change in proportion of participants classified as food insecure from baseline to follow-up, and paired t-tests or non-parametric equivalents compared other outcomes.

Results

At baseline, 58 participants completed surveys, and 25 completed physical data collection. Participants were primarily female (93.1%), 18-33 or 35-44 years old (37.9% each), and of European background (81.0%). The proportion of participants reporting food security improved from baseline (54.2%) to follow-up (66.7%) (p = 0.041). Importantly, participants who were food secure remained so at follow-up. Those who were food insecure also reported more favourable improvements in dietary behaviours and meal preparation habits, though many of these did not reach statistical significance.

Conclusion

Participation in a community-based food cooperative was associated with improved food security among Australian adults. SO WHAT?: These findings highlight the potential of community-based food cooperatives to reduce food insecurity and support their integration into broader health promotion and food security strategies.

title: Cardiac Arrhythmias and Sleep Disorders.
authorString: Heinzinger CM, Mehra R.
abstractText: Sleep disordered breathing (SDB), periodic limb movements of sleep, insomnia, sleep curtailment, and sleep architectural changes are associated with cardiac arrhythmias in community-based and clinical cohort studies. Findings appear to be strongest in magnitude and most consistent for SDB and atrial fibrillation (AF). The mechanisms most consistently identified in animal experimental models include autonomic nervous system fluctuations and intrathoracic pressure alterations, the latter resulting in direct mechanical effects on the thin-walled atria. Other studies point toward intermittent hypoxia. Nonrandomized interventional studies suggest that the treatment of SDB reduces AF recurrence after ablation or cardioversion.

title: Nursing Student Led Blood Pressure Education in a Community Mental Health Setting: A Pre Post Test Study.
authorString: Stephen C, Yousiph T, Halcomb E, Jay EK, Smith B, Patterson C, Curtis E, Mullan J, Moxham L.

journal.title: International journal of mental health nursing

abstractText: People living with mental illness have greater cardiovascular risk, more lifestyle risk factors and lower health literacy than the general population. The high prevalence of hypertension among people living with mental illness places them at a significantly higher risk of premature morbidity and mortality. Identifying hypertension and empowering consumers to understand its significance are key to controlling elevated blood pressure. Student nurse led blood pressure education in community mental health settings may improve hypertension awareness while building nursing students' confidence and competence. This study sought to evaluate the impact of a preregistration nursing student led blood pressure education activity on consumer blood pressure knowledge and nursing students' health education competence. A single group pre post test intervention study was undertaken during a community mental health clinical placement (Recovery Camp, New South Wales, Australia). Nursing students delivered a brief blood pressure education activity to consumers living with mental illness. Consumer knowledge was assessed using the Hypertension Evaluation of Lifestyle and Management (HELM) scale, and student competence was assessed using the Nurse Health Education Competence Instrument (I-CEpSE). Twenty-one consumers completed paired assessments. Mean HELM scores increased from 5.0 (SD 2.65) pre activity to 6.9 (SD 2.69) post activity (p < 0.001). Forty-four students completed paired assessments, with I-CEpSE total scores increasing from 210.95 (SD 28.81) to 257.27 (SD 30.22) (p < 0.001). This study has demonstrated that a structured, student led blood pressure education activity embedded within a community mental health placement improved both consumer hypertension knowledge and student reported health education competence.

title: Defibrillation in the Cardiac Arrest Patient.
authorString: Dreyfuss A, Carlson GK.
abstractText: Defibrillation is one of the few interventions known to favorably impact survival in cardiac arrest. In witnessed arrest, survival improves with defibrillation as early as possible, whereas it may improve outcomes to administer high-quality chest compressions for 90 seconds before defibrillation in unwitnessed arrest. Minimizing pre-, peri-, and post-shock pauses has been shown to have mortality benefits. Refractory ventricular fibrillation has high mortality rates, and there is ongoing research into promising adjunctive treatment modalities. There remains no consensus on optimal pad positioning and defibrillation energy level, however, recent data suggest anteroposterior pad placement may be superior to anterolateral placement.

title: Management of Patients After Cardiac Arrest.
authorString: Smith D, Kenigsberg BB.
abstractText: Cardiac arrest remains a significant cause of morbidity and mortality, although contemporary care now enables potential survival with good neurologic outcome. The core acute management goals for survivors of cardiac arrest are to provide organ support, sustain adequate hemodynamics, and evaluate the underlying cause of the cardiac arrest. In this article, the authors review the current state of knowledge and clinical intensive care unit practice recommendations for patients after cardiac arrest, particularly focusing on important areas of uncertainty, such as targeted temperature management, neuroprognostication, coronary evaluation, and hemodynamic targets.

title: Arrhythmias in Adult Congenital Heart Disease Heart Failure.
authorString: Dodeja AK, Upadhyay S.
abstractText: Heart failure and arrhythmias represent 2 major causes of mortality and morbidity in adults with congenital heart disease. Arrhythmias and heart failure are interdependent, and one may exacerbate the other. Treatment of one also has a positive impact on the other. Management approaches need to be multifaceted, including pharmacotherapy, optimization of hemodynamic status with catheter-based or surgical interventions, and specific management of arrhythmia with device or catheter ablation therapy.

title: Cardiac Implantable Electronic Devices in Ischemic Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Kamani Y, Peigh G, Verma N, Wasserlauf J.
abstractText: This review discusses the range of device therapy for ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM). This article will review the primary data supporting guideline indications for cardiac implantable electronic devices in patients with ICM, with a focus on primary/secondary prevention transvenous implantable cardioverter defibrillators (ICDs), cardiac resynchronization therapy, and subcutaneous/extravascular ICDs. In addition, this review discusses emerging device therapy for ICM including left bundle area pacing/defibrillation, cardiac contractility modulation and baroflex activation therapy. Device therapy for ICM continues to evolve to incorporate diverse modalities across the spectrum from prevention of sudden cardiac death to modifying cardiac remodeling and recovery.

title: Evaluation and Management of Arrhythmias in Ischemic Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Sehgal A, Peigh G, Wasserlauf J, Verma N.
abstractText: Atrial and ventricular arrhythmias are highly comorbid with ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) and are associated with worsening symptoms, morbidity, and mortality. This review will discuss the pathophysiology, evaluation, and treatment of each arrhythmia in ICM with a focus on novel evaluation strategies and catheter-directed interventions. For atrial fibrillation /atrial flutter, recent studies have demonstrated mortality and symptom benefit with early rhythm control with catheter ablation. With respect to ventricular tachycardia, scar characterization is being investigated to change primary prevention and novel ablation technologies and strategies are being explored.

title: Modulating Perioperative Ventricular Excitability.
authorString: Howard-Quijano K, Kuwabara Y.
abstractText: Cardiac arrhythmias are associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Ventricular arrhythmogenesis is a dynamic interplay among an arrhythmogenic substrate, myocardial electrophysiologic properties, modifying factors, and triggering factors. Imbalances in the autonomic nervous system can lead to increased myocardial excitability, which is a major contributor to the pathophysiology of ventricular tachyarrhythmias. Myocardial excitability and ventricular arrhythmogenesis are modulated perioperatively through hemodynamic and physiologic management, anesthetic agents, or regional anesthetic and surgical techniques.

title: The Pharmacologic Management of Cardiac Arrest.
authorString: Singh A, Heeney M, Montgomery ME.
abstractText: The effectiveness of pharmacologic management of cardiac arrest patients is widely debated; however, several studies published in the past 5 years have begun to clarify some of these issues. This article covers the current state of evidence for the effectiveness of the vasopressor epinephrine and the combination of vasopressin-steroids-epinephrine and antiarrhythmic medications amiodarone and lidocaine and reviews the role of other medications such as calcium, sodium bicarbonate, magnesium, and atropine in cardiac arrest care. We additionally review the role of β-blockers for refractory pulseless ventricular tachycardia/ventricular fibrillation and thrombolytics in undifferentiated cardiac arrest and suspected fatal pulmonary embolism.

title: Perioperative Care of Heart Failure, Arrhythmias, and Valvular Heart Disease.
authorString: O'Glasser AY, Manjarrez EC.
abstractText: Frequently, the question of whether or not a patient is stable for surgery boils down to the question, "Does this patient need a preoperative stress test?" However, coronary artery disease and ischemic heart disease are only some of the many cardiac conditions that patients present with preoperatively-and that can negatively impact their intraoperative management and postoperative outcomes. This article will explore the evidence based, patient centered best practices surrounding the perioperative evaluation and management of heart failure, arrhythmias, and valvular heart disease.

title: Fascial Patch Reconstruction of a Gastric Conduit Defect Using an Anterolateral Thigh-Vastus Lateralis Composite Free Flap: A Case Report.
authorString: Lin FW, Yen CH, Lin YC, Hsieh CH, Wee SJ.
abstractText: Gastric conduit defects are difficult to manage when primary repair fails and the residual wall becomes friable, particularly in the setting of chronic infection and chest-wall tissue loss. We report a 71-year-old man with a retrosternal gastric conduit who sustained a full-thickness rupture during median sternotomy for coronary artery bypass grafting. Primary repair failed, resulting in chronic recurrent dehiscence and sternal wound infection. Debridement and partial resection of infected sternum and manubrium left a 3 × 2 cm noncircumferential conduit defect with adjacent presternal and mediastinal dead space. A 25 × 8 cm anterolateral thigh-vastus lateralis composite free flap was harvested with a thin fascial extension contiguous with the vastus lateralis muscle. The fascia was sutured around the entire defect perimeter as a tension-free primary patch. The vastus lateralis muscle was positioned over the repair for vascularized reinforcement and dead-space obliteration, while the skin paddle provided external coverage and flap monitoring. The flap was transferred to the right transverse cervical artery and branches of the internal jugular vein. No flap-related complications occurred. Esophagography at 4 weeks showed no leakage; full oral feeding was achieved by 6 weeks.
