At 10 months, swallowing symptoms remained at the preoperative post-esophagectomy baseline, with smooth contrast passage and no functional obstruction on videofluoroscopy. This case shows the feasibility of component-specific composite free-flap reconstruction for a limited gastric conduit defect.

title: Vaping and E-Cigarettes: An Emergency Department Survey.
authorString: Lycett C, Jagarlamudi B, Moore A, Minhas S, Briggs N, Chiew A.
abstractText:
Objective

To characterise vaping practices and perceptions in a non-consecutive cohort across four Sydney Emergency Departments (EDs) prior to 2024 Australian legislative changes restricting disposable vapes.

Methods

An anonymous digital survey of up to 40 questions was conducted from May 2023 to January 2024 in patients and visitors aged > 14 years. It assessed demographics, vaping and smoking practices, perceived addiction, side effects and attitudes. Participants were recruited via posters and distribution of linked QR codes.

Results

Of 1263 surveys initiated, 1049 (83.1%) were completed. Among respondents who answered the vaping-status question 51.1% (614/1202) reported ever vaping with 34.4% (211/614) vaping daily. Respondents were more often able to report the puff count and duration of their most recently purchased device (> 85%) than puffs per day or sessions per day (≈60%). Disposable vapes and fruit/candy flavours were most reportedly used. Addiction and anxiety relief were frequently selected reasons for vaping, and daily vapers reported higher perceived addiction scores. Symptoms occurring during or shortly after vaping were commonly reported, most frequently cough (174/308, 56.5%), breathlessness (165/308, 53.6%) and chest pain (98/308, 31.8%). Daily vapers more commonly perceived vaping as safer than cigarettes (101/198, 51.0% vs. 88/568, 15.5% in never vapers) and as an effective smoking cessation aid (105/197, 53.3% vs. 83/571, 14.5%).

Conclusion

In this multicentre, non-consecutive survey, vaping was commonly reported, particularly among younger respondents, with frequent daily use and perceived addiction. These findings highlight the importance of asking about vaping and awareness of patterns of use, perceived addiction and reported symptoms.

title: How to … Do Feasibility, Acceptability and Potential Effectiveness Studies in Health Professions Education Research.
authorString: Sandars J.
abstractText: New interventions in health professions education (HPE) are often widely disseminated before their feasibility, acceptability and potential effectiveness have been adequately evaluated. This creates uncertainty for educators and curriculum decision-makers about whether these interventions have promise for progression, with adoption or adaptation and further evaluation into their own educational setting. This How to … article provides a practical guide to designing and reporting feasibility, acceptability and potential effectiveness studies for early-stage evaluation of new interventions in HPE.

title: The Place of Therapeutic Apheresis in Severe Immune-Related Adverse Events: A Scoping Review of Literature.
authorString: Vuillet C, Moranne O, Daubin D, Quantin X, Palassin P, Kanouni T, Maria ATJ, MonRIO network (Montpellier Réseau Immuno‐Oncologie).
abstractText: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized the management of patients with cancer. However, they can induce breakdowns in immunologic tolerance, leading to autoimmune diseases, or immune related adverse events (irAEs). These irAEs can sometimes be life threatening, requiring aggressive management, such as immunosuppressant (IS) or even therapeutic apheresis (TA). TA, an extracorporeal circulation technique, may represent a therapeutic option for severe irAEs, reducing their severity and duration by removing ICIs, pathogenic antibodies or inflammatory cytokines, although its role in this situation remains underreported. We made scoping review to better identify the use of TA for managing severe irAEs. From January 2022 to August 2025, three databases were reviewed, for articles mentioning the use of TA in the event of immunotoxicity. Only case reports or case series were retained. A descriptive summary was produced in table forms. Between 2022 and 2025, 162 articles were identified, 34 articles concerning 42 patients treated for severe irAE via TA were included. The underlying cancers were mainly non-small cell lung cancer and melanoma, and 78% of patients were treated with monotherapy anti-PD(L)1. The main indications for TA were neurological (40.6%), overlap manifestations (23.8%), and hepatitis (21.4%), mainly highly severe. TA was most often used in rescue situations, that is, after failure of several lines of IS. Complications of TA were rare. Clinical improvement was reported in most patients, usually within days of TA, with 24% complete resolution, and 45% partial resolution. Despite revolutionizing cancer treatment, ICIs induce severe irAEs, with poorly defined therapeutic options. TA may be a therapeutic option for life threatening irAEs, with data in the literature assuming its effectiveness. However, details on its use remain poorly defined. Further studies are required to emphasize its use as in irAEs.

title: Accessing and Navigating Gender-Affirming Hormone Therapy and Perspectives on Inclusive Pharmacy Care Among Transgender and Gender Diverse People: A Qualitative Study.
authorString: McCann J, Wilcock S, Dominy I, Davison K, Sharman S, Robinson-Barella A.

journal.title: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy

abstractText:
Introduction

Transgender and gender diverse (TGD) people continue to experience inequities in access to gender-affirming care, including stigmatisation, delayed treatment and non-inclusive healthcare encounters. Community pharmacies may represent an accessible setting to support inclusive and affirming care; however, lived experiences of engaging with community pharmacy services in the context of gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT) remain underexplored, particularly among younger people who represent the greatest proportion of the TGD community. This study aimed to explore the lived experiences of accessing, navigating and receiving GAHT, alongside participants' perspectives on barriers and facilitators to accessing inclusive and affirming care within community pharmacy.

Methods

Semi-structured interviews were conducted between October and November 2025. Interviews explored participant experiences of accessing GAHT and perspectives on inclusive and affirming pharmacy practice. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. NVivo (Version 15) facilitated data management, and the COREQ and CCRF checklists informed reporting. Ethical approval was obtained from the Newcastle University Research Ethics Committee (reference: 66105/2023).

Results

Ten participants, representing a range of gender identities, were interviewed. Three overarching themes were developed: (1) reflecting on the challenges of navigating gender-affirming hormone therapy; (2) exploring the impact of healthcare barriers upon an individual and (3) accessing and receiving inclusive and affirming pharmacy care. Participants viewed community pharmacies as accessible and supportive environments for affirming care when underpinned by respectful communication, visible inclusivity, appropriate staff training and partnership working with TGD communities.

Conclusion

In this study, TGD individuals described significant structural and interpersonal barriers when accessing GAHT in the United Kingdom, negatively influencing trust, wellbeing and engagement with healthcare services. Community pharmacies may represent an underutilised, yet important, setting for inclusive and gender-affirming support. Embedding gender-affirming training and co-designed approaches within pharmacy services may strengthen accessibility, trust and equity in care for TGD communities.

Lived experience or public contribution

A person with lived experience from the TGD community (ID) acted as a co-author and patient champion in this study; they supported the design and conduct of the research, advised on inclusive and non-stigmatising approaches and supported preparation of the manuscript, contributing a lived-experience perspective throughout.

title: Age- and Sex-Specific Optimal Cutoffs for Obesity Indices for Early Detection of Metabolic Syndrome Risk in Taiwanese Adults.
authorString: Hsu CY, Guo JW.
abstractText: Age- and sex-specific obesity index cutoffs may improve the early identification of individuals at risk for metabolic syndrome. This study determined optimal cutoff points for body mass index (BMI), triglyceride glucose index (TyGI) and Chinese visceral adiposity index (CVAI) to predict MetS risk in Taiwanese adults. This retrospective study using the Mei Jau Health Database, spanning 2008 to 2013, included 30 382 adults (76% females) aged 18 years or older. Subjects free of metabolic syndrome in 2008 had additional data recorded from 2009 to 2013. Approximately 8.5% developed MetS after baseline (2008). Significant differences in BMI, TyGI and CVAI between sexes (p < 0.001) were observed, with females exhibiting lower values than males. The optimal cutoff values for obesity-related indices were determined, stratified by age groups (≤ 29, 30-39, 40-49, ≥ 50) and sex. BMI cutoffs: 22.14-23.14 (females), 23.54-24.94 (males); TyG: 4.44-4.63 (females), 4.55-4.69 (males); CVAI: 10.70-77.11 (females), 67.02-82.23 (males). Most of these age- and sex-specific cutoff values exhibited AUCs and sensitivity values greater than 0.70 and demonstrated acceptable to excellent predictive performance. In summary, CVAI cutoffs showed greater accuracy and sensitivity than BMI and TyGI for identifying MetS risk in Taiwanese adults without baseline MetS.

title: Hypothalamic Neurochemical and Microglial Suppression in Long-Standing Human Hibernation-Like Syndrome.
authorString: Jiang W, Kalsbeek A, Hut RA, Swaab DF, Yi CX.
abstractText: Seasonally recurring hibernation-like states are exceptionally rare in humans, and their neural substrates remain unknown. We investigated the brain of a 57-year-old woman with a > 30-year history of winter-associated hypothermia, neuroendocrine instability, psychomotor suppression and circannual rhythmicity. Postmortem neuropathological analysis revealed preserved hypothalamic and basal forebrain anatomy but profound neurochemical abnormalities. Key peptidergic neuronal populations involved in circadian and neuroendocrine regulation, including arginine vasopressin (AVP), oxytocin (OXT), corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH) and thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH) neurons, showed near-complete loss of immunoreactivity in the SCN, SON and PVN. Immunoreactivity for vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) and neurotensin (NT) in the SCN was markedly reduced. These changes were accompanied by markedly reduced synaptophysin immunoreactivity in all hypothalamic regions examined, whereas catecholaminergic neurons were relatively preserved in the PVN and SON. Beyond the hypothalamus, cholinergic neurons in the NBM showed a moderate reduction without evidence of Alzheimer-related pathology. Microglial immunoreactivity was nearly absent in the hypothalamic and extrahypothalamic regions examined, contrasting with preserved GFAP and AQP4 immunoreactivity. Moreover, myelination and microvascular architecture also remained intact. These findings identify a selective hypothalamic and microglial suppression associated with a rare human hibernation-like phenotype and indicate markedly reduced output of core neuroendocrine and circadian circuits during long-standing hypometabolic states. The case also illustrates that recurrent, profound hypothermia can be tolerated over decades without systemic organ failure, highlighting an unexpected degree of human metabolic resilience.

title: Reductions in Advanced Chronic Liver Disease Among People Who Inject Drugs: The ETHOS Engage Study.
authorString: Conway A, Valerio H, Payne J, Silk D, Marshall AD, Martinello M, Tillakeratne S, Dharmayani PNA, Milat A, Amin J, Read P, Degenhardt L, Stevens A, Hayllar J, Christmass M, Cock V, Doumany J, Grebely J, Dore GJ, ETHOS Engage Study Group.

journal.title: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

abstractText:
Background and aims

Liver disease is a significant risk for people who inject drugs due to the high burden of hepatitis C virus (HCV). There is limited data on the impact of the direct-acting antiviral (DAA) therapy era on liver disease among people who inject drugs. This study evaluated baseline and longitudinal liver disease in a national cohort of people who inject drugs recruited over three Waves: 2018-2019, 2019-2021, and 2023-2025.

Methods

The ETHOS Engage Study is an observational cohort of people who inject drugs attending drug treatment clinics and needle and syringe programs in Australia. Participants completed a questionnaire and underwent point-of-care HCV RNA testing (Xpert HCV Viral Load Fingerstick) and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) by vibration-controlled transient hepatic elastography (FibroScan). Advanced chronic liver disease was defined by LSM of 10 kPa or above.

Results

Among all enrolments with a valid LSM (n = 3126, 79% recruited at drug treatment clinics), 11% had advanced chronic liver disease, decreasing from 12.0% (154/1287) in 2018-2019 to 7.9% (66/839) in 2019-2021, and 6.4% (62/967) in 2023-2025. In adjusted analyses, participants recruited between 2019-2021 and 2023-2025 were less likely to have advanced chronic liver disease (vs. 2018-2019; aOR 0.66, 95% CI: 0.48-0.90 and aOR 0.56, 95% CI: 0.40-0.77, respectively). Current HCV infection declined from 24% in 2018-2019 to 10% in 2023-2025. Among participants with LSM in more than one wave and current HCV infection at first visit and no current HCV infection at second visit (n = 44), advanced chronic liver disease declined from 19% to 5%.

Conclusions

Unrestricted access to DAA therapies in Australia has been associated with reduced liver disease burden among people who inject drugs. Monitoring of liver health in this population is important, given potential ageing and non-HCV liver disease impacts.

title: Research Priorities for Preconception Health in Scotland: A Multidisciplinary Call to Action.
authorString: Currie S, Brough EJ, Ryan L, Renwick K, Rose B, Ganguly A.

journal.title: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy

abstractText:
Introduction

Health and behaviours prior to conception influence reproductive outcomes, lifelong health, and health inequalities across generations. While international attention to preconception health has increased, context-specific evidence to inform effective practice and policy in Scotland remains limited. This gap is concerning given declining birth rates, widening inequalities, and increasing prevalence of adverse maternal and infant outcomes.

Methods

A research prioritisation project was undertaken to identify key areas for preconception health research in Scotland. A narrative review of published literature reviews and relevant Scottish policy and public health guidance was conducted to identify evidence gaps and preliminary research themes. These informed a national online survey that captured views from members of the public and stakeholders with an interest in preconception health. Survey findings were subsequently refined through an in-person, multi-stakeholder workshop involving members of the public, researchers, healthcare professionals, third sector representatives, and policy stakeholders.

Results

Four overarching research priority themes were identified: (1) adopting a life-course approach to preconception health; (2) reducing neurodevelopmental risks and improving awareness of preconception behaviours; (3) addressing health inequalities and ensuring equitable access to care; and (4) enhancing the involvement of men, partners, and shared responsibility for preconception health. Cross-cutting principles emphasised the need for inclusive and consistent messaging, improved healthcare professional training, integration of preconception care within existing services, stakeholder involvement, and robust data collection.

Conclusion

This co-designed research prioritisation project identifies clear and actionable priorities for advancing preconception health research in Scotland. Addressing these priorities will support evidence-based policy and practice, improve reproductive and long-term health outcomes, and contribute to reducing health inequalities for current and future generations.

Public contribution

Members of the public and individuals with lived experience of preconception health were actively involved throughout this research prioritisation project. Public contributors participated in a national survey to identify and rank priorities for preconception health research in Scotland and attended a multi-stakeholder workshop to refine and finalise research themes and questions. The workshop included members of the public alongside researchers, healthcare professionals, third sector representatives, and policy stakeholders, ensuring that priorities reflected lived experience as well as professional perspectives. Public input directly informed the identification of research priorities, the interpretation of findings, and the development of future research directions (See the GRIPP2 short form checklist in the supplementary files).

title: Multidisciplinary Perspectives in Cardiac Electrophysiology-Part II.
authorString: Koneru J, Lloyd M.

title: Hypoxia-activated microglia promote pathological angiogenesis <i>via</i> an FN/ITGB3/FAK/Akt pathway.
authorString: Hao LC, Li DH, Zhang K, Liu CZ, Sun MH, Gao XX, Zhu SQ.
abstractText:
Aim

To investigate whether hypoxia-activated microglia drive pathological neovascularization through extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and endothelial integrin signaling, a mechanism that may function in parallel with vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) signaling.

Methods

The oxygen-induced retinopathy (OIR) mouse model was used. Retinal phenotypes were assessed by flat mounts, histology, and vascular leakage assays. Key pathways were screened by transcriptomics and validated via Western blot, immunofluorescence, and quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR). In vitro, brain microvascular endothelial cells were treated with conditioned medium from hypoxic microglia (Hyp-CM), with cell migration and tube formation assessed. Interventions employed the integrin β3 (ITGB3) inhibitor cilengitide, the focal adhesion kinase (FAK) inhibitor PF-573228 and a neutralizing anti-VEGF antibody. In vivo, cilengitide was administered by intravitreal injection to evaluate its therapeutic effect on neovascularization.

Results

OIR retinas showed significant avascularity, pathological neovascularization, and barrier disruption. Transcriptomics revealed activation of ECM-receptor interaction and focal adhesion pathways, with upregulation of Fn1 and Itgb3. Increased protein levels of fibronectin (FN) and ITGB3, alongside elevated phosphorylation of FAK and protein kinase B (Akt), were confirmed in vivo. Activated microglia co-localized with upregulated FN and ITGB3. Conditioned medium from Hyp-CM activated the ITGB3-FAK-Akt pathway in endothelial cells and promoted their migration and tube formation. These effects were nearly abolished by cilengitide or PF-573228. VEGF neutralization partially reduced Hyp-CM-induced migration and tube formation. Intravitreal injection of cilengitide significantly reduced retinal neovascularization in OIR mice.

Conclusion

Hypoxia-activated microglia promote pathological angiogenesis, and the FN/ITGB3/FAK/Akt axis is identified as a key mediator of this process, revealing a novel mechanism that operates in parallel with VEGF signaling. Targeting this "hypoxia-microglia-ECM-integrin" axis represents a promising therapeutic strategy to overcome anti-VEGF resistance in ischemic retinopathy.

title: Compatibility of 24-2C central extra test points with OCT and OCTA parameters in early-stage glaucoma.
authorString: Kaderli A, Camcıoğlu Ş, Tamer Kaderli S, Sül S.
abstractText:
Aim

To facilitate structure-function analysis by evaluating the compatibility of newly added 10 extra test points in early-stage glaucoma cases with optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT-angiography (OCTA) glaucoma parameters in clinical practice.

Methods

Cases diagnosed with primary open angle glaucoma underwent Humphrey 24-2C visual field (VF) test, OCT, and OCTA tests on the same day. The arithmetic average of the central 10 extra points in the 24-2C VF was calculated, and its compatibility with OCT and OCTA parameters was assessed. Patients with low signal strength OCT and OCTA images, high fixation losses in VF, intraocular pressure of 25 mm Hg and above, systemic vascular diseases [diabetes mellitus (DM), hypertension (HT)] were excluded from the study.

Results

Totally 68 early-stage glaucoma cases (68 right eyes, 37 males) were included with the mean age of 64.52±8.89y. In the Spearman correlation test, all OCT and OCTA parameters except inside disc vascular density showed a positive correlation with the mean of additional VF test points (P<0.05 for all parameters, P=0.114 for inside disc vascular density). In multiple linear regression analysis, superior hemifield vessel density and whole image vessel density percentages were found to be significantly associated with additional points (P=0.029, 0.039, respectively).

Conclusion

It is known that specific regions of the macula may be sensitive to early-stage glaucomatous damage. This suggests that in early-stage glaucoma, attention should be paid to central points in addition to peripheral findings on VF. The compatibility of the mean of 24-2C SITA-Faster VF central extra points with the defined OCTA parameters may demonstrate the value of OCTA in diagnosis and follow-up in early stages for clinics without access to the new software VF devices.

title: Baseline gradient, valve morphology and left ventricular recovery and survival after TAVR in reduced-ejection-fraction aortic stenosis: a retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Li F, Pan W, Zhou D, Zhao Y, Luo W, Zhou J, Xiao C, Ge J.

title: Nanofiber Density Is a Higher-Order Architectural Regulator of Multidimensional Cardiomyocyte Maturation.
authorString: Xiao Q, Yu F, Xiang L, Cheng L, Xu T, Tang H, Liu M, Wang X, Zhang H, Zhang Y, Feng B.
abstractText: Insufficient maturation of cardiomyocytes (CMs) remains a major challenge in cardiac tissue engineering. While electrospun nanofibers offer biomimetic topographical and mechanical cues, conventional high-density fiber architectures impose excessive mechanical constraints that restrict mechanotransduction and limit CM maturation. Here, we employed a suspended, aligned electrospun polycaprolactone (PCL) nanofiber platform to investigate how fiber density-categorized as low (LD; 15.89 ± 1.84 μg/cm2), medium (MD; 85.81 ± 12.74 μg/cm2), and high (HD; 404.90 ± 59.10 μg/cm2)-modulates the maturation of neonatal rat cardiomyocytes (NRCMs). The MD substrate was identified as the optimal configuration, effectively balancing topographical guidance with a permissive mechanical microenvironment for NRCM maturation. Compared with the HD substrate, NRCMs on MD substrates exhibited enhanced structural maturation, with a greater aspect ratio (5.65 ± 1.15) and sarcomere length (1.92 ± 0.17 μm). These structural improvements were accompanied by enhanced gap junction formation and improved electromechanical function, including a 4.03-fold higher contraction displacement and a 4.01-fold faster calcium decay rate. Furthermore, the MD substrate promoted metabolic maturation, evidenced by a 2.08-fold increase in mitochondrial membrane potential and a 2.42-fold higher ATP production. The LD substrate exhibited an intermediate maturation phenotype between MD and HD groups. Mechanistically, the maturation-promoting effects of the MD substrate were associated with increased YAP phosphorylation and cytoplasmic retention, together with enhanced PI3K-Akt signaling, all of which were attenuated by high-density fiber packing. This "Goldilocks effect" establishes fiber density as a critical architectural determinant of CM maturation and highlights optimization of this parameter to regulate mechanosignaling as an effective strategy for engineering functionally mature cardiomyocytes.

title: Semaglutide and Panic Attacks: Active-Comparator Disproportionality Analysis, Temporal Assessment of Notoriety Bias and Evidence Triangulation in Post-Marketing Pharmacovigilance.
authorString: Melamed B, Parsi-Zahabi M, Omrani MA, Baskaran BS, Eddin LE, Kermanshahi N, Chalabianloo N, Muanda FT.
abstractText:
Purpose

To evaluate how confounding by indication and notoriety bias shape the apparent semaglutide-panic attack signal in the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) and to interpret this signal using an evidence-triangulation framework integrating randomized and observational studies.

Methods

We conducted an active-comparator restricted disproportionality analysis of FAERS (2018Q1-2024Q4), including individual case safety reports in which semaglutide, dulaglutide or empagliflozin was the primary suspect drug. Panic attack was identified using the MedDRA preferred term. Crude and adjusted reporting odds ratios (RORs, aRORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using logistic regression, adjusting for age, sex and indication (Type 2 diabetes, obesity/weight management). Notoriety bias was assessed using prespecified temporal analyses (analyses restricted to reports received before July 1, 2023 and a drug-by-period comparison of 2018-2022 with 2023-2024) and reporting proportions per 10 000 reports. A sensitivity analysis used all other primary-suspect drugs in FAERS as the reference set. In parallel, we conducted a systematic review (MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL to November 24, 2025) of randomized trials, cohort and cross-sectional studies, pharmacovigilance analyses and case reports reporting panic attacks or acute anxiety outcomes with semaglutide.

Results

Among 33 267 semaglutide, 54 282 dulaglutide and 25 380 empagliflozin reports, panic attacks were recorded in 87 (0.26%), 28 (0.05%) and 13 (0.05%) cases, respectively. Crude RORs were 5.08 (95% CI 3.32-7.78) versus dulaglutide and 5.12 (95% CI 2.86-9.17) versus empagliflozin, attenuating after adjustment to 2.82 (95% CI 1.74-4.56) and 2.75 (95% CI 1.41-5.36). In the pre-warning period crude RORs were 2.24 (95% CI 1.23-4.07) and 2.15 (95% CI 1.00-4.58), attenuating to 1.38 (95% CI 0.69-2.75) and 1.14 (95% CI 0.48-2.68) after adjustment. Panic-attack reports per 10 000 semaglutide reports rose from 6.7 in 2018-2022 to 42.0 in 2023-2024 (drug-by-period interaction p = 0.007). Against all other primary-suspect drugs, the aROR was 1.48 (95% CI 1.18-1.87) overall and 0.76 (95% CI 0.48-1.18) before July 1, 2023. Across 12 studies, randomized trials and active-comparator observational cohorts did not show a consistent increase in panic attacks or anxiety-related outcomes.

Conclusions

Crude FAERS analyses suggested a semaglutide-panic attack signal that attenuated after adjustment was no longer significant before the July 2023 regulatory communication and rose sharply thereafter in a pattern consistent with notoriety bias. Triangulation with randomized trials and active-comparator observational studies does not support a consistent pharmacological association. Disproportionality analyses are hypothesis-generating and cannot estimate incidence or establish causality. This case study illustrates how active-comparator design, temporal assessment of notoriety bias and evidence triangulation can improve the interpretation of post-marketing safety signals.

title: Metformin at the Time of COVID-19 Infection and Risk of Long COVID: A Target Trial Emulation Study.
authorString: Bramante CT, Stürmer T, Huling JD, Buse JB, Lindsell C, Stewart T, Rothman RL, Sahner D, Dunsmore SE, Topol E, Wiggen TD, Makkar S, Toler A, Estepp T, Johnson SG, N3C Consortium.
abstractText:
Our objective was to evaluate metformin prescribed at the time of SARS-CoV-2 infection on the risk of developing Long COVID (LC) in electronic health record data. We conducted a new user analysis of metformin prescribed within 6 days of documented infection with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) versus experimental control: prescription for fluvoxamine, fluticasone, ivermectin, or montelukast.

Inclusion criteria

a clinic visit in the 0-6 months and the 6-12 months before infection.

Exclusion criteria

metformin or control within 12 months.

Primary outcome

LC or death (LC/D), to address death as a competing risk, among patients prescribed drug within Days 0-6 of infection. LC was defined by diagnosis code or computable phenotype. We used entropy balancing to estimate the average treatment effect with a weighted log-linear model. After weighting, there were 248 in the metformin and control groups; the average age was 53 (16); 16% were Black; and 16% were Hispanic. In the primary analysis, 10/248 (4.0%) in the metformin group developed LC/D versus 21/248 (8.5%) in the control group, adjusted risk ratio (aRR) 0.47 (95% CI 0.25-0.89, p = 0.02). For prescriptions on Days 0-1 relative to infection, aRR was 0.39 (95% CI 0.12-1.24); for prescriptions on Days 0-14, the aRR was 0.75 (95% CI 0.52-1.08). In this observational analysis, metformin prescribed within a week of documented SARS-CoV-2 infection was associated with a 53% lower risk of LC over 6 months than comparator medications. With the aRR of 0.47 (95% CI 0.25-0.89), any risk reduction between 75% and 11% is highly compatible with our data. This analysis of electronic health record diagnoses is important for the reproducibility of clinical trial results that ascertained the same outcome but via participant-report.

title: The Effects of Force-Velocity Profile-Based Load Prescription on Muscle Power and Functional Performance in Velocity-Deficient Older Adults.
authorString: Deboutte J, Delecluse C, Thomis M, Van Roie E.

journal.title: Scandinavian journal of medicine & science in sports

abstractText: Muscle power is essential for functional capacity in older adults and can be improved through power-focused resistance training (PRT). PRT adaptations are load- and velocity-specific, yet optimal load prescription remains unclear. As force and velocity capacities vary between individuals, this 12-week intervention compared two force-velocity (F-V) profile-guided loading strategies: training at loads matched versus not matched to the F-V deficit. F-V profiles of 80 adults ≥ 65 years were assessed on a pneumatic leg press, with maximal force (F<sub>0</sub>) and velocity (V<sub>0</sub>) expressed as z-scores relative to a younger reference group (n = 60, 20-35 years). A difference ≥ 1 between z-scores was considered indicative of a deficit, with the direction determining a force- or velocity-deficit profile. As force deficits were rare (n = 4), the intervention only included participants with a velocity deficit (n = 59), of whom 57 initiated the intervention. Participants were randomly assigned to train at loads matched to their deficit (individualized; IND) or at loads deliberately not matched to their deficit (non-individualized; NON-IND). Maximal power, F-V profile parameters and functional performance were assessed at baseline, 6 and 12 weeks. From baseline to 12 weeks, F<sub>0</sub> increased more in NON-IND than IND (p = 0.040), while V<sub>0</sub> increased more in IND than NON-IND (p = 0.009). Changes in power and functional performance did not differ between groups (all p ≥ 0.065). In velocity-deficient older adults, differences in F-V-guided load prescription led to distinct F-V adaptations but did not lead to differences in power or functional performance. Trial Registration: The study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06449716).

title: Real-World Use of Rezafungin for the Treatment of Challenging Aspergillus Infections.
authorString: Stone N, Bachiller-Luque P, Giuliano S, Pai S, Pernas B, Garcia-Vidal C, Tyler N, Ferin S, Tascini C, Cruz AF.
abstractText:
Background

Aspergillus infections can pose significant treatment challenges, due in part to increasing triazole resistance. Clinical insight is needed to understand the potential for rezafungin, a next-generation echinocandin with once-weekly dosing, to address some limitations of current treatments for Aspergillus infections.

Methods

This retrospective case series collected anonymized real-world data from eight adults who received once-weekly rezafungin for difficult-to-treat Aspergillus infections. The cases were provided by clinicians in Spain, the UK, and Italy with considerable experience in treating challenging fungal infections.

Results

Most patients had pulmonary aspergillosis, nearly all had failed or were intolerant to triazole-based regimens, and half had prior echinocandin or amphotericin B exposure. Rezafungin was used primarily to enable outpatient parenteral antimicrobial therapy (OPAT), avoiding the need for daily IV echinocandin in settings of azole resistance or intolerance. About half received rezafungin as monotherapy; others had combination regimens. Clinical and/or radiological improvement or disease stabilization was observed in most cases, including in patients with azole-resistant infections. Notably, one patient achieved resolution of chronic otitis media, and others had negative cultures or sustained clinical benefit. Rezafungin was well tolerated, including in patients with renal impairment. One patient with chronic aspergilloma did not achieve adequate symptomatic control with rezafungin and required surgery.

Conclusions

This report provides initial clinical insights on rezafungin as a potential option for difficult-to-treat Aspergillus infections. In this limited group of patients, rezafungin enabled OPAT, facilitated hospital discharge, and provided clinically meaningful improvements, including prolonged disease stabilization and resolution, which merit further investigation in clinical trials.

title: The impact of patient weight status on healthcare students' attitudes: Two experimental studies in midwifery and dental students.
authorString: Sehrawat A, Aslan A, Aldam EL, Wood C, Buckland NJ.
abstractText:
Background

Weight stigma refers to prejudice and discrimination based on body weight. Healthcare professionals often hold negative attitudes towards patients with overweight, which can negatively affect patient care and health outcomes. However, weight stigma is yet to be explored in midwifery and dental students.

Methods

Two online experimental studies using hypothetical patient vignettes were conducted in midwifery (n = 281; Study 1) and dental and non-dental students (n = 528; Study 2). Participants were randomly assigned to view a healthy-weight, overweight or obese patient vignette and then reported their attitudes, predicted time, advice they would provide and beliefs about obesity. Data were analysed using ANOVA and logistic regression.

Results

In Study 1, midwifery students held significantly more stigmatizing attitudes towards patients who were overweight than healthy-weight patients; however, there was no significant difference in attitudes towards patients with obesity. Predicted time spent with patients did not significantly differ as a function of patient weight status. In Study 2, dental and non-dental students reported more stigmatizing attitudes towards overweight and obese patients compared to healthy-weight patients. Predicted time spent with patients did not differ significantly. Dental and non-dental students were more likely to offer lifestyle-related advice to overweight and obese patients. There was no significant relationship between beliefs about obesity and attitudes towards treating patients.

Conclusions

Weight stigma is evident among healthcare students and can affect healthcare advice. Increased awareness of potential biases in midwives and dental students is needed and should form formal training to improve equitable healthcare delivery.

title: Fecal Microbiota Transplantation: A Promising Therapeutic Strategy Targeting the Microbiota-Gut-Brain Axis in Anorexia Nervosa.
authorString: Kwok SL, Xiao YC, Cai XB.
abstractText:
Purpose

Anorexia nervosa (AN) is a complex psychiatric disorder characterized by self-starvation, body-image disturbance, and serious medical complications. Because current treatments have variable outcomes and relapse is common, the microbiota-gut-brain axis has been investigated as a possible contributor to disease persistence. This review evaluates fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) as an experimental microbiota-directed strategy for AN.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for relevant studies published from January 1990 to October 2025. Eligible evidence included human reports, animal studies, and mechanistic studies examining FMT or gut-microbiota alterations in AN and related pathways.

Findings

Individuals with AN have been reported to show altered microbial diversity and changes in taxa associated with short-chain fatty acid production and inflammation. These findings are heterogeneous and may reflect starvation, diet, medication exposure, or illness-related physiology. Human evidence for FMT in AN is limited to small, uncontrolled studies and case reports, while most mechanistic support comes from animal models or indirect evidence from other conditions.

Conclusion

Evidence for FMT in AN remains preliminary and is largely based on uncontrolled human observations and preclinical studies. FMT may alter gut microbial composition and gastrointestinal or metabolic measures, but controlled efficacy data are absent and psychiatric benefits remain unconfirmed. Well-designed controlled trials are needed to establish its safety and clinical efficacy.

title: Accelerated Preoperative Wound Bed Preparation Using Negative Pressure Wound Therapy With Instillation and Dwell Time: A Comparison With Conventional Negative Pressure Wound Therapy in Necrotic Wounds.
authorString: Ohura N, Nakayama D, Kinoshita M, Shiraishi T, Morishige Y, Murai S, Ozaki M.
abstractText: Negative pressure wound therapy with instillation and dwell time (NPWTi-d) and conventional NPWT are established treatments for complex wounds, yet direct comparative evidence remains limited. This retrospective observational study evaluated the clinical effectiveness of NPWTi-d for hard-to-heal necrotic wounds using standardized parameters from our previous research. We included 116 patients (50 NPWTi-d; 66 conventional NPWT). The primary endpoint was the time from therapy initiation to achieving a 'reference wound' suitable for definitive closure, defined in accordance with clinical trial guidance from the Japanese Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (PMDA). The NPWTi-d group achieved reference wound status in a median of 14 days versus 22 days for the conventional NPWT group-a statistically significant 8-day reduction. Furthermore, whereas conventional NPWT typically requires a prolonged debridement phase prior to application, NPWTi-d can be initiated earlier, even in the presence of residual necrotic tissue. Ultimately, NPWTi-d provides a synergistic clinical advantage by both shortening active treatment duration and bypassing pre-initiation delays, enabling clinicians to achieve surgical readiness significantly faster than with standard modalities.

title: Liquid Compared to Solid Oral Formulations of the Thyroid Hormone Receptor Agonist Elunetirom Under Fasted and Fed Conditions in Healthy Participants.
authorString: Harris JR, van Haarst AD, Baccei J, Franey B, Everett J, George K, Paglialunga S, Webster K, Hillstrand M, Banfield C, Scanlan TS, Davar G.
abstractText: Elunetirom (ABX-002) is a brain-targeted, oral prodrug being developed for the adjunctive treatment of major depressive disorder and bipolar depression. The active moiety, LL-340001, is a thyroid hormone receptor agonist with modest selectivity for beta over alpha thyroid hormone receptors. Upon entering the brain, the intended site of action, elunetirom is hydrolyzed by fatty acid amide hydrolase to LL-340001. In this 3-way randomized, crossover, bioequivalence study, the pharmacokinetics (PK) and safety of an oral liquid formulation used in early clinical development were compared with those of an oral solid formulation intended for later-stage development and potential commercialization, under fasted and fed conditions. Healthy adult participants received single doses of elunetirom (45 μg) as a liquid formulation under fasted conditions and as a solid formulation under fasted conditions and 30 min after consumption of a high-fat meal. Administration of the solid formulation under fasted conditions resulted in elunetirom and LL-340001 exposures similar to those observed with the liquid formulation and is therefore considered to have comparative bioavailability. Food intake increased elunetirom total exposure (AUC) compared with the fasted state but did not affect maximum exposure (C<sub>max</sub>). In contrast, administration with food reduced LL-340001 C<sub>max</sub> compared with the fasted state but did not affect AUC. Food intake delayed the time to reach C<sub>max</sub> (T<sub>max</sub>) for both elunetirom and LL-340001. Elunetirom, administered orally as a liquid and as a solid formulation, was safe and well tolerated under fed and fasted conditions.

title: Phase 1 Study of Safety and PK With A Combination of Omeprazole and Trimetazidine for Fatty Acid Oxidation Inhibition in Patients With Advanced Solid Tumors.
authorString: Choi W, Chun JW, Sim SH, Han SS, Lee WJ, Kang JH, Kim HC, Lee S, Lee JH, Yoo HJ, Kim SY, Woo SM.
abstractText: Fatty acid oxidation (FAO) is a metabolic vulnerability in cancer cells, making pharmacologic FAO inhibition a promising therapeutic strategy. This Phase I, open-label, 3 + 3 dose-escalation study evaluated the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary antitumor activity of two oral FAO inhibitors-omeprazole (KN510), a carnitine-acylcarnitine translocase inhibitor, and trimetazidine (KN713), an acetyl-CoA acyltransferase inhibitor-given once daily in combination to patients with advanced solid tumors. Twelve patients were enrolled across four dose cohorts (omeprazole and trimetazidine, each 60-120 mg/day). The maximum tolerated dose was not reached; the recommended Phase 2 dose was set at 120 mg once daily for each agent. Treatment was generally well tolerated, with most adverse events Grade 1-2; the most common were flu-like symptoms (25.0%), constipation (16.7%), nausea (16.7%), and dizziness (16.7%). Omeprazole showed time-dependent pharmacokinetics consistent with auto-inhibition of its own metabolism, whereas trimetazidine showed dose-proportional pharmacokinetics across the studied range. The best response was stable disease in five patients (disease control rate 41.7%). Median progression-free survival was 1.66 months (95% CI, 1.18-3.55) and median overall survival was 9.13 months (95% CI, 3.29-not reached). Dual pharmacologic FAO inhibition with oral omeprazole and trimetazidine was feasible and well tolerated, supporting the mechanistic rationale for combination dosing. Disease stabilization observed in this heavily pretreated population warrants further clinical evaluation, particularly in combination with standard chemotherapy regimens. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06012708; registered August 25, 2023.

title: International Collaboration in Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia.
authorString: Pennekamp P, Manion M, Omran H.
abstractText: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia (PCD) exemplifies how international collaboration can transform the study of a rare disease. Since the identification of the first PCD-associated genes in 1999-2002, parallel developments in Europe and North America, driven by patient organizations, academic investigators, and coordinated funding initiatives, have progressively converged into a unified global research infrastructure. Early milestones included the founding of patient advocacy groups, the NIH-funded Genetic Disorders of Mucociliary Clearance Consortium, and European projects such as EUCILIA and SYSCILIA, which respectively established coordinated clinical research infrastructure and advanced ciliary systems biology. The 2012 EU-funded BESTCILIA project formalized transatlantic collaboration, establishing the International PCD Registry and iPCD Cohort, generating the first robust diagnostic evidence base, and enabling the first multinational randomized controlled trial in PCD. This infrastructure was subsequently sustained and expanded through the BEAT-PCD COST Action and its successor ERS Clinical Research Collaboration, the ERN-LUNG PCD Core Network, and the PCD Clinical Trial Network, alongside parallel North American developments including the PCD Foundation Clinical and Research Centers and PCDF Network for Clinical Trials. Together, these initiatives have harmonized diagnostic pathways, produced joint ERS/ATS diagnostic guidelines, and created durable platforms for multinational trials and registries. Dedicated scientific meetings, culminating in the planned 2026 Global PCD Congress, further embody this convergence. Despite this progress, disparities in global representation and diagnostic access remain, underscoring the need for continued international coordination as the field moves toward precision medicine approaches.

title: DBT Modulates Copper-Dependent Cuproptosis-Related Injury in Experimental Alcoholic Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Pan Z, Gao L, Ling Y, Cen X.

journal.title: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine

abstractText: Alcoholic cardiomyopathy (ACM) is a severe cardiovascular complication of chronic alcohol consumption, but its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Cuproptosis is a recently identified copper-dependent form of regulated cell death; however, its role in ACM remains unclear. In this study, male C57BL/6 mice were fed an ethanol-containing Lieber-DeCarli liquid diet to establish an ACM model, and RNA sequencing combined with bioinformatics analysis was performed to identify cuproptosis-related genes. Among the candidate genes, dihydrolipoamide branched-chain transacylase E2 (DBT) showed a consistent trend of downregulation across both independent RNA-seq cohorts, and was further validated by qRT-PCR and Western blotting. ACM mice exhibited increased serum and cardiomyocyte copper content, altered cuproptosis-related markers and impaired cardiac function. In AC16 cells, DBT knockdown induced copper overload, cuproptosis-related molecular alterations and mitochondrial dysfunction, which were markedly alleviated by the copper chelator tetrathiomolybdate. Conversely, DBT overexpression attenuated EtOH-induced copper overload, cuproptosis-related molecular alterations and mitochondrial dysfunction, with effects similar to those of tetrathiomolybdate. These findings suggest that DBT regulates ACM-related cardiomyocyte injury through cuproptosis-associated processes at the cellular level and may represent a potential therapeutic target for alcohol-induced myocardial injury.

title: Barriers to Proactive Health Management Among Elderly Patients With Coronary Heart Disease in Rural Areas: A Qualitative Study.
authorString: Tan J, Liu Q, Sun L.
abstractText:
Aim

To explore the lived experiences, perceived barriers, and internal unmet needs related to proactive health management among rural elderly patients with coronary heart disease (CHD).

Design

Descriptive qualitative study.

Methods

Using purposive maximum variation sampling, we recruited participants from rural elderly inpatients. All subjects were diagnosed with CHD and hospitalized at Shenyang Fourth People's Hospital between May and July 2025. Seventeen eligible participants completed face-to-face interviews lasting 40-60 min each. All interviews were audio-recorded and transcribed verbatim. Inductive descriptive thematic analysis was applied for data coding and to summarize content derived from the interviews. Data collection stopped once data saturation was reached.

Results

Multiple challenge domains with three main themes encompassing eight subthemes were extracted. First, barriers related to individual cognition and behavioural management, including limited disease awareness and pathogenic misconceptions, poor adherence to health-promoting behaviours, and impaired psychological adaptation; Second, barriers and trust deficits in healthcare system interactions, characterized by conflicts between medical decision-making and livelihood needs, as well as insufficient trust in primary healthcare services; and Third, limited family-social care support, encompassing impaired family caregiving function, disconnection of social support networks, and limited resources for health literacy empowerment.

Conclusion

Rural elderly patients with CHD self-reported a range of challenges hindering their proactive health management, including cognitive limitations, low trust in primary care, insufficient intergenerational care, and weak community support networks. Age-appropriate health education and county-level remote medical services are proposed as potential strategies to address these self-reported challenges, which may facilitate patients' proactive health engagement, though improvements in patients' long-term quality of life remain to be further investigated.

Implications for the profession and/or patient care

Nurses caring for rural elderly patients with CHD should provide age-appropriate, simplified health education to counter disease misconceptions and unsafe self-help behaviours, alongside individualized dietary and physical activity guidance. Nurses should identify and relieve patients' fear of acute CHD-related symptom episodes and guilt over burdening their families and offer simplified home-medication-management guidance for patients and their family caregivers.

Impact

The findings highlight patients' cognitive limitations, real-world family-care circumstances, and negative perceptions of grassroots healthcare as key considerations when delivering proactive health-management support for this population.

Patient and public contribution

No patients or members of the public were involved in the study design, recruitment, study conduct, interpretation of findings, or manuscript preparation.

Reporting method

The study report was guided by the COREQ checklist.

title: Changes in Long-Term Care Needs, Healthcare Costs, and Mortality Risk After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Japan: The Longevity Improvement & Fair Evidence Study.
authorString: Sassa T, Maeda M, Oda F, Sakamoto T, Fukuda H.
abstractText:
Aim

Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is increasingly performed in older adults with severe aortic stenosis, but there is limited evidence on their post-procedure changes in care needs, healthcare costs, and mortality risk.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study used linked medical and long-term care (LTC) insurance claims data from 1361 patients aged ≥ 75 years who underwent TAVI in 13 Japanese municipalities. Patients were stratified into four groups by baseline certified care needs level: Independent (n = 725), Support Level 1-2 (n = 321), LTC Level 1-2 (n = 208), and LTC Level 3-5 (n = 107).

Results

Among 532 patients in the 36-month observation cohort, 53% were independent at baseline, and approximately half of those remained independent at 36 months. Monthly total medical and LTC costs at 36 months were approximately 5 times higher in the LTC Level 3-5 group than the Independent group. The LTC Level 3-5 group also showed significantly higher all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 3.19, 95% confidence interval 2.18-4.67).

Conclusions

Higher baseline care needs are associated with poorer outcomes and higher costs after TAVI. Incorporating care needs levels into clinical assessments may inform clinical decision-making and resource planning in older populations.

title: Respirasome Persistence Without Efficient Electron Channeling in Cardiac Mitochondria From an Animal Model of Hypertension.
authorString: Glogowski PA, Algieri C, Cugliari A, Cotugno M, Trombetti F, Fabbri M, Cicero AFG, Rubattu S, Nesci S.

journal.title: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences

abstractText: Cardiac mitochondrial dysfunction contributes to hypertensive remodeling, but whether respiratory supercomplex organization preserves electron transfer efficiency during disease progression remains unresolved. Here, we examined the structural and functional organization of the respiratory complexes in cardiac mitochondria from stroke-resistant and stroke-prone spontaneously hypertensive rats exposed to normal or Japanese diet regimens. In both models, supramolecular analyses revealed the persistence of N-respirasome and Q-respirasome assemblies, indicating that major respiratory supercomplex species are maintained during sustained hypertension and in the pre-stroke state. However, metabolic flux control analysis consistently showed that cytochrome c oxidase or Complex IV exerted only limited control over respiratory flux, with control coefficients below those expected for tightly channeled nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH)-dependent electron transfer. Thus, structural preservation of respirasomes was not matched by evidence of kinetically optimized coupling. These findings uncouple supercomplex detectability from functional electron channeling and suggest that, in the hypertensive heart, respiratory performance is constrained by qualitative defects in supercomplex organization rather than by their overt loss.

title: Plasma Interleukin-10 Levels and IL10 Genetic Variants Are Associated With Clinical Outcomes in Patients With Severe COVID-19 Treated With Corticosteroids.
authorString: Fricke-Galindo I, Ortega-Villafuerte FM, Pérez-Rubio G, Buendía-Roldán I, Ramírez-Bello J, Castillo Morales AA, Chávez-Galán L, de Jesús Hernández-Zenteno R, Ramos-Martínez E, García-Carmona S, Cataneo-Piña DJ, Bautista-Félix NE, Falfán-Valencia R.
abstractText: We aimed to evaluate the association between IL10 variants and plasma IL-10 levels and clinical outcomes in patients with severe COVID-19 treated with corticosteroids. We studied 944 patients with severe COVID-19 who were treated with corticosteroids. The clinical outcomes evaluated were in-hospital mortality and the requirement of invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV). The variants IL10 rs1800872, rs1554286, rs3024505, and rs3122605 were determined using TaqMan SNP assays, and IL-10 levels were measured by ELISA at the start of corticosteroid treatment (T1) and after 8 days (T2). The rs1800872-TT (p = 0.035, OR = 1.55, 95% CI = 1.03-2.33) and the rs1554286-AA genotypes were associated with IMV (p<sub>adj</sub> = 0.036, OR = 2.42, 95% CI = 1.12-5.95). IL-10 levels were higher at T1 than at T2. At T2, IL-10 levels were higher in non-survivors (15.9 vs. 7.0 pg/mL, p < 0.001) and in patients requiring IMV (9.9 vs. 5.5 pg/mL, p < 0.001). Among non-survivors, IL-10 plasma levels did not decrease at T2. The alluvial plot revealed that 51.9% of patients in the highest IL-10 tertile at T1 remained in the highest tertile at T2, with a mortality rate of 50%. IL10 rs1800872 and rs1554286 contribute to the risk of requiring IMV. Elevated IL-10 levels after corticosteroid treatment were linked to in-hospital mortality and IMV.

title: γ-T3 Increases the Sensitization of Gastric Cancer Cells to OXA by a Regulation of ARHGAP29.
authorString: Zhu H, Wang FL, Zhang S, Yang TT, Gao GQ, Tian H, Xue L, Dong HW, Wang Q, Zhang SJ, Liu M, Liu JR.

journal.title: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

abstractText: γ-Tocotrienol (γ-T3) exhibits potent anti-cancer effects in vitro and in vivo. Our previous study demonstrated that γ-T3 modulates autophagy activity in gastric cancer (GC) cells via the GSK-3β/β-Catenin pathway. In this study, we further explored whether γ-T3 also enhances the chemosensitivity of GC cells to oxaliplatin (OXA) by regulating ARHGAP29, and verified the direct binding between γ-T3 and ARHGAP29 as well as the physical interaction of ARHGAP29 with GSK-3β. We employed cell viability assays, flow cytometry, tumor cell spheroid formation assays, RT-qPCR, Western blot analysis, and stable overexpression transfection. Additionally, cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP), and chloroquine (CQ) rescue CCK-8 assays were performed for molecular interaction and autophagy function verification; we established a xenografted tumor model using MKN45 cells in BALB/c nude mice (nu/nu). γ-T3 and OXA inhibited GC cell proliferation in vitro and in vivo, with a synergistic effect when combined (CI = 0.55 in MKN45 cells). In a mouse model, intraperitoneal injection of γ-T3 (20 mg/kg b.w.) and OXA (2.0 mg/kg b.w.) suppressed MKN45 cell xenograft growth. This was related to cell cycle arrest and inhibition of cancer stem cells (CSCs). γ-T3 alone or combined with OXA altered autophagy-related protein levels after 48 h treatment, with elevated LC3-II/LC3-I ratio and Beclin1 expression, and reduced p62 abundance, functional rescue with autophagy inhibitor CQ confirmed that the changed autophagy contributes to drug-induced cell death, and this phenotypic change was accompanied by suppressed GSK-3β/β-Catenin pathway activity. ARHGAP29 was inversely correlated with GC prognosis; CETSA results validated the direct intracellular binding between γ-T3 and ARHGAP29, and Co-IP assays confirmed physical interaction between ARHGAP29 and GSK-3β. γ-T3 inhibited the expression of ARHGAP29 at protein and mRNA levels in a time- and dose-dependent manner, whether alone or with OXA. Overexpression of ARHGAP29 reversed the synergistic effects of γ-T3 and OXA in GC cells, further supporting the regulatory linkage between ARHGAP29 and the GSK-3β/β-Catenin axis. The combination of γ-T3 and OXA represents a promising therapeutic strategy to elevate oxaliplatin sensitivity and alter autophagy-related marker expression in GC, at least partially via the ARHGAP29-associated modulation of GSK-3β/β-Catenin signaling.

title: <sup>15</sup>O-water PET-detected myocardial ischaemia and CT-derived FFR: Predicting the functional significance of anatomical stenosis.
authorString: J V, M O, A-P R, Tm L, Tp L, M H.
abstractText:
Aims

Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. While coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides anatomical assessment of coronary stenoses, its ability to determine their functional significance is limited. Computed tomography-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) has emerged as a non-invasive method for lesion-specific ischaemia assessment. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of CT-FFR using 15O-water positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging as the reference standard.

Methods and results

We retrospectively reviewed 193 patients who underwent hybrid CCTA and 15O-water PET at Kuopio University Hospital between 2017 and 2022. Patients with low-to-moderate pretest probability of CAD in whom CAD could not be ruled out by CCTA were eligible. After exclusions, 165 patients were included. CT-FFR values were calculated using a research prototype algorithm and compared with PET-derived perfusion abnormalities. In the overall cohort, CT-FFR showed moderate diagnostic performance, with area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.672-0.740. In a subgroup of 83 patients with high-quality CCTA and stenosis >50%, diagnostic performance improved substantially (AUC 0.836). Using a CT-FFR threshold of 0.80, sensitivity and specificity were 85% and 87%, respectively.

Conclusion

In an unselected clinical population referred for PET perfusion imaging after CCTA, CT-FFR did not significantly improve diagnostic performance compared with CCTA alone. However, in patients with high-quality CCTA and obstructive coronary stenoses, CT-FFR demonstrated good accuracy for identifying functionally significant disease, supporting its role as a complementary non-invasive diagnostic tool.

title: LncRNA A1BGAS1 Serves as a Tumor Suppressor in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer by Modulating the Expression of miR-3942-5P.
authorString: Du J, Li Z, Wang C, Zhang X.

journal.title: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

abstractText: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), the leading contributor to global cancer mortality, is associated with a notably unfavorable prognosis. This study aims to explore the regulatory interaction between A1BG-AS1 and miR-3942-5p and its molecular mechanisms. The level of A1BG-AS1 and miR-3942-5p in both tumor tissues and cell lines (BEAS-2B, A549, H226) were measured using qPCR. Functional effects of A1BG-AS1 overexpression in NSCLC cells were evaluated through CCK-8, flow cytometry, and Transwell assays. The interaction between A1BG-AS1 and miR-3942-5p was validated through dual-luciferase reporter assays and rescue studies. A1BG-AS1 expression was markedly reduced in both NSCLC tissues and cell lines. A1BG-AS1 expression was significantly associated with various clinical parameters. Overexpression of A1BG-AS1 suppressed NSCLC cell function. Mechanistically, A1BG-AS1 interacted with and negatively regulated miR-3942-5p, and the antitumor effects of A1BG-AS1 overexpression were reversed by miR-3942-5p mimics.A1BG-AS1 inhibits NSCLC tumor progression by targeting miR-3942-5p.

title: "Life and Lower Limb Threatening Condition" Clinical Features, Management and Outcomes of Diabetic Foot Ulcers Complicated by Gas Gangrene: A Prospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Abbas ZG, Gangji RR, Naemi R.
abstractText: Diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) is a common complication of diabetes in low- and middle-income countries and may be complicated by gas gangrene (GG), a rapidly progressive, life-threatening infection. This prospective study assessed whether GG can be diagnosed clinically in low-resource primary care and explored factors associated with wound-healing outcomes in DFU complicated by GG. From December 2021 to June 2025, consecutive patients with diabetic foot infection and clinically active GG were enrolled. Data included demographics, ulcer history and examination, SINBAD classification, GG signs, sepsis status, comorbidities, management, and outcomes. All participants had classical clinical features of GG and were admitted for urgent surgical treatment. Ninety-nine patients (58 male) with classical GG were admitted for urgent surgery. Initial amputation was required in 18% (major 12%, minor 6%). Ten patients were lost to follow-up; that included six who died from foot-ulcer-related causes. Of 89 followed, 30 (33.7%) healed in 225.5 ± 126.9 days, while 59 remained unhealed after 146.1 ± 175.4 days; major amputations during treatment were more frequent in the healed group. Having a previous history of ulcer showed to increase the time to heal by 136 days. A one-day increase in treatment duration was associated with a 1% decrease in both the chance of healing or risk of amputation. Early diagnosis, aggressive medical and surgical intervention are the keys to decreasing morbidity and mortality of diabetic patients with gas gangrene; and remain the mainstay treatment of this dangerous condition globally. Patient's with previous ulcer history were found to need longer time to heal. Increasing treatment duration seems to be a double-edged sword, as while it is associated with reduced risk of amputation, it also decreases the chance of ulcer healing.

title: A Comparative Analysis of Deaths Due to Drug-Related Causes Between Rural and Urban Areas in the United Kingdom, 1997-2026.
authorString: Roberts E, Rehm J, Copeland C.
abstractText:
Introduction

Multiple jurisdictions report disproportionately elevated rates of drug-related harm in urban settings, alongside unique treatment needs in rural populations. We examined differences in case characteristics, circumstances of death and implicated drugs among individuals dying from drug-related causes, stratified by rural or urban setting, and determined changes in the proportion of deaths between settings over time.

Methods

Retrospective registry-based analysis of coronial records of individuals who died from drug-related causes, submitted to the National Programme on Substance Use Mortality in the UK, 1997-2026. UK Government Rural-Urban Classification methodology dichotomised cases using postcode at date of death.

Results

Overall, 39,975 decedents died, 36,350 (90.9%) in urban settings. The urban percentage decreased significantly over the study period from 96.6% in 1999 to 92.3% in 2025 (AAPC -0.34%, 95% CI -0.47% to -0.15%, p = 0.002). Accidental poisoning was the most common direct cause of death in both rural (45.5%) and urban (54.8%) settings, while intentional self-poisoning was more common rurally (17.3% vs. 9.5%). Opioids were the most frequently implicated drug group in both rural (61.1%) and urban (65.4%) settings. The median number of drugs implicated did not differ significantly between settings (both 2, IQR 1-3), but rural decedents had a significantly higher median number of prescribed implicated drugs (1, IQR 0-2 vs. 0, IQR 0-2).

Discussion and conclusions

Over three decades, approximately one in 11 UK drug-related deaths occurred rurally. Intentional self-poisoning was substantially more common in rural fatalities, and opioids were the leading implicated drug group across both settings.

title: Clinical Impact of Haemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis Among Patients With HIV/AIDS and Disseminated Histoplasmosis in a Hyperendemic Region of Northeastern Brazil.
authorString: Mota MAL, Sousa MM, Souza JVM, Moura IO, Oliveira JMS, de Mesquita JRL, Damasceno LS, Leitão TDMJS, Meneses GC, Daher EF.
abstractText:
Background

Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome that may occur in people living with HIV/AIDS (PLWHA), often triggered by opportunistic infections such as disseminated histoplasmosis (DH). The substantial overlap in clinical and laboratory features between HLH and DH complicates timely diagnosis.

Objectives

To describe HLH among PLWHA with DH and compare clinical, laboratory and outcome characteristics between patients with and without HLH.

Patients/methods

A retrospective observational study was conducted at São José Hospital of Infectious Diseases, Fortaleza, Brazil, between March 2023 and June 2024. Hospitalised PLWHA with DH were evaluated for HLH based on the presence of ≥ 3 HLH-2004 criteria and an H-Score ≥ 169. Baseline clinical, laboratory and outcome parameters were compared between patients with and without HLH.

Results

Among 61 patients diagnosed with DH, 11 (18.0%) met the study criteria for HLH. Patients with HLH were more likely to present with hepatomegaly (p = 0.036), haemoptysis (p = 0.030) and lower platelet counts (p = 0.029). In-hospital mortality was significantly higher among patients with HLH (54.5% versus 18.0%; p = 0.019). These patients more frequently required renal replacement therapy (p = 0.028) and intensive care unit admission (p = 0.048). Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank testing demonstrated significantly reduced in-hospital survival among patients with HLH (p = 0.015).

Conclusions

HLH represents a severe complication in PLWHA with DH and is associated with increased mortality and greater need for intensive care. Early recognition and use of adjunctive diagnostic tools may facilitate timely management and improve clinical outcomes.

title: RSV Disease Among Hospitalized Children: Second vs. First Year of Life Multicenter Study.
authorString: Armoni Domany K, Golan-Tripto I, Burrack N, Masarweh K, Gur M, Rochman M, Be'er M, Prais D, Mor M, Weinberger Opek M, Nasrallah E, Megged O, Shatzman Steuerman R, Stein M, Steinberg Z, Shehadeh S, Glatman-Freedman A, Tasher D.
abstractText:
Background

Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of pediatric hospitalization, yet data on children hospitalized with RSV in their second year of life are limited.

Objective

To compare clinical characteristics and management practices of children hospitalized with RSV during their second versus first year of life.

Methods

This retrospective multicenter study included children aged 0-23 months hospitalized with RSV infection across 11 medical centers between 2017 and 2021. We compared demographics, outcomes (length of stay [LOS] > 3 days, and pediatric intensive care unit [PICU] admission), and systemic corticosteroid and antibiotic use between the second and first years of life, adjusting for prematurity, comorbidities, and the COVID-19 pandemic.

Results

Among 6260 children hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed RSV infection, 1321 (21%) were hospitalized during their second year of life. Compared with first-year admissions, second-year patients had higher rates of prematurity (18.0% vs. 13.4%) and comorbidities (6.3% vs. 2.6%) (both p < 0.001). They more frequently received corticosteroids (53.5% vs. 23.2%) and antibiotics (63.4% vs. 45.9%) (both p < 0.001) and had lower PICU admission rates (4.6% vs. 7.0%; p < 0 0.001) and similar rates of prolonged LOS (35.0% vs. 35.6%; p = 0.64). In adjusted analyses, second-year hospitalization was associated with increased corticosteroid use (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 4.28; 95% CI, 3.67-4.99) and antibiotic use (aOR, 2.09; 95% CI, 1.80-2.43), and lower odds of PICU admission (aOR, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.40-0.79).

Conclusions

RSV hospitalization in the second year of life carries a significant burden, with higher antibiotic and corticosteroid use despite lower PICU rates and similar LOS. These findings highlight the need for better characterization of this age group to optimize future immunoprophylaxis strategies.

title: Genomic and Clinical Analysis of Influenza A in Hospitalized Adults, 2019-2024: Exploratory Evidence on Neuraminidase and Polymerase Acidic Protein Mutation-Outcome Associations From a Single Center.
authorString: Feng A, Tan W, Xu W, Zhang X, Wei D, Yang Z.
abstractText:
Background

Antivirals are widely used to treat influenza, but potential resistance mutations remain a major challenge, and clinical data on key resistance mutations are limited.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 765 adults with RT-PCR-confirmed influenza A admitted to Ruijin Hospital, Shanghai, between 2019 and 2024 to determine whether specific NA/PA mutations are associated with severe outcomes or prolonged length of stay (LOS) when analyzed alongside key host factors. PA and NA sequences were obtained and linked to the clinical cohort for mutation-clinical outcome analyses. Multiple testing was addressed by controlling the false discovery rate using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure.

Results

Among 765 inpatients with influenza A virus infection, the median age was 68 years; 5.0% were severe disease and 9.9% died. Older age, higher CURB-65 score, and bacterial/fungal co-infection were the main correlates of mortality, whereas antiviral regimen and Ct value were not independently associated with mortality or severe outcomes. Adjusted observational analyses showed a lower estimate for severe disease with baloxavir but no association with in-hospital death. Major high-level resistance mutations were absent; detected NA/PA mutations showed no robust association with severe disease or mortality. PA-F105L showed an exploratory association with longer LOS, but this finding was attenuated after adjustment and was confounded by clade and calendar period.

Conclusions

Clinical outcomes were driven mainly by host factors and admission severity. Detected NA/PA mutations were not robustly associated with severe outcomes, while high-level resistance could not be assessed; PA-F105L-LOS association requires phenotypic and external validation.

title: Swallowing-Related Time Measured by a Neck-Worn Electronic Stethoscope and Its Associations With Age, Sex, and Masticatory Function in Community-Dwelling Older Adults.
authorString: Shirobe M, Iwasaki M, Motokawa K, Gomi T, Okamura T, Sasai H, Suzuki K, Hirano H.
abstractText:
Introduction

Objective assessment of swallowing function in community-dwelling older adults remains challenging. A neck-worn electronic stethoscope (NWES) can measure swallowing-related time noninvasively. This study aimed to examine age- and sex-related differences in NWES-derived swallowing-related time metrics and their relationship with masticatory function.

Methods

Older adults from the Itabashi Longitudinal Study on Aging in 2024 were included. Swallowing-related time was measured using NWES as pharyngeal clearance time (PCT), representing the duration of pharyngeal swallowing during water swallowing, and oral processing and swallowing time (OPST), reflecting the duration from oral processing to swallowing completion during cracker ingestion. Masticatory function was assessed using a gummy jelly test.

Results

Four hundred and sixty-two participants (mean age 76.1 ± 3.4 years) were included. Median (interquartile range) PCT was 0.88 (0.70-1.01) s in men and 0.75 (0.61-0.92) s in women; corresponding OPST values were 34.51 (28.89-42.93) and 43.46 (34.33-54.09) s, respectively. PCT was significantly longer in men, whereas OPST was significantly longer in women. OPST correlated with age in men (r = 0.17) and women (r = 0.20). Masticatory function was not significantly associated with PCT in either sex. After adjustment for age, body mass index, number of functional teeth, stroke history, and PCT, higher masticatory function scores were significantly associated with shorter OPST only in men (B = -0.67).

Conclusion

NWES-derived PCT and OPST showed different associations with age and masticatory function, with OPST associated with age in both sexes and with masticatory function in men. PCT and OPST may offer practical approaches for evaluating oral processing performance in older adults.

title: Is SARS-CoV-2 Infection (COVID-19) Associated With Congenital Anomalies? A Population Study of Congenital Anomaly Surveillance Data and Maternal SARS-CoV-2 Infection in Wales.
authorString: Fisher SR, Maddison-Jarvis R, Cresswell-Jones P, Tucker D, Davies L.
abstractText:
Objectives

Explore the relationship between maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection and congenital anomalies in Wales.

Study design

Mixed observational epidemiological cross-sectional and cohort.

Methods

Congenital anomaly prevalence data were provided by the Congenital Anomaly Register and Information Service. Two comparisons were made using these data: firstly, congenital anomaly subgroup prevalence prior to and during the pandemic at population level, and in a cohort of women with laboratory-confirmed maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection compared with the population trend.

Results

Prevalence of congenital anomalies in Wales was lower during the pandemic (mean 365 per 10,000 in 2020-22 vs. 454 per 10,000 in 2009-19) showing stable trends. However, the mean for abdominal wall defects increased from 9.8 per 10,000 births between 2009 and 2019 to 13.9 per 10,000 births in 2020-2022, largely attributed to an increase in omphalocele. A cohort of 486 confirmed maternal SARS-CoV-2 infections led to 181 births affected by congenital anomalies, and the trimester of infection did not impact the adjusted odds of this occurring. Circulatory anomalies were most frequently reported, consistent with pre-pandemic population-level data. Urinary and cardiac anomalies were more prevalent in this cohort group than at population level.

Conclusions

There was no clear evidence at population-level of an association between congenital anomalies and maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection in Wales. However, a potential association with specific congenital anomalies cannot be excluded. Increased omphalocele is consistent with a Europe-wide trend that pre-dated COVID-19. National surveillance registries should remain vigilant.

title: Anxiety and Mindfulness in the Relationship Between Stress and Depression in Patients With Coronary Artery Disease: A Parallel Mediation Analysis.
authorString: Song Y, Lee Y, Lim HA, Lee J.
abstractText:
Aim

To examine the indirect effect of anxiety and mindfulness on the relationship between stress and depression in patients with coronary artery disease.

Design

A correlational, cross-sectional design was used.

Methods

Participants of this study comprised 112 patients with coronary artery disease recruited from a general hospital in South Korea between January and September 2021. The Korean versions of the Depression Anxiety Stress Scale-21 and Mindful Attention Awareness Scale were used. Data were analysed using parallel multiple mediation analysis (PROCESS macro Model 4).

Results

Stress, anxiety, mindfulness and depression were significantly correlated. The total indirect effect through anxiety and mindfulness on the relationship between stress and depression was significant (B = 0.37, 95% CI [0.200, 0.592]). The specific indirect effect through mindfulness was significant (B = 0.26, 95% CI [0.122, 0.423]), whereas the indirect effect through anxiety was not statistically significant (B = 0.11, 95% CI [-0.003, 0.268]).

Conclusion

Mindfulness may be an important psychological factor associated with the relationship between stress and depression in patients with coronary artery disease. Further research is needed to clarify the role of anxiety in this relationship.

Implications for the profession and patient care

Mindfulness-based approaches may be considered as complementary strategies for managing psychological distress and depressive symptoms in patients with coronary artery disease. Anxiety should also be assessed as part of comprehensive psychological care.

title: A Novel Peptide Targeting the USP25-SIRT1 Interaction Activates SIRT1 to Suppress Cell Senescence.
authorString: Zhou Y, Wang X, Zhang J, Qiang H, Zhao X, Luo J, Ji Y, Yao J, Zhai L, Zhang T, Li K, Chen Y, Yuan J, Li L, Li Y.
abstractText: The deacetylase SIRT1 is a critical regulator of cellular senescence, and the excessive accumulation of senescent cells can further drive the onset of organismal aging. SIRT1 activity is tightly governed by posttranslational modifications, including ubiquitination. While ubiquitination has been well documented to control SIRT1 protein stability, the precise regulatory pathway underlying SIRT1 activity remains poorly understood. Here, we identify the deubiquitinase USP25 as a central regulator of cellular senescence. Specifically, USP25 deficiency in mice mitigates age-related phenotypes and improves overall physiological function. Mechanistically, USP25 directly interacts with SIRT1 and mediates its deubiquitylation via K63-linked polyubiquitination, specifically targeting SIRT1 lysine residues K506 and K513, which ultimately suppresses SIRT1 deacetylase activity. Reduced SIRT1 deacetylase activity, in turn, increases P53 or PGC1α acetylation, which further increases the transcriptional activation of downstream target genes and consequently accelerates cellular senescence.
