Furthermore, we developed a cell-penetrating peptide, pSirt1-4, that efficiently disrupts the USP25-SIRT1 interaction, increases SIRT1 deacetylase activity, and attenuates cellular senescence. Collectively, our findings establish USP25 as a critical regulator of aging and highlight the USP25-SIRT1 axis as a promising therapeutic target for treating senescence-related diseases.

title: Exercise-Based Management of Diabetic Cardiomyopathy: Preclinical Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence, and Translational Strategies.
authorString: Li X, Wang Z, Liu J.
abstractText: Diabetic cardiomyopathy is characterized by progressive metabolic dysfunction, myocardial fibrosis, impaired calcium handling, and ventricular remodeling, yet effective strategies for reversing established cardiac injury remain limited. Exercise training has emerged as a promising non-pharmacological approach, although its clinical application is constrained by heterogeneous intervention protocols, inconsistent dose reporting, and limited evidence from well-characterized diabetic cardiomyopathy populations. This narrative review synthesizes current preclinical and clinical evidence on exercise-based management of diabetes-associated myocardial dysfunction, with particular emphasis on underlying mechanisms, exercise prescription, and translational implementation. Experimental studies indicate that exercise may improve myocardial function through enhanced mitochondrial biogenesis and metabolic flexibility, attenuation of oxidative stress and inflammatory-fibrotic signaling, restoration of calcium homeostasis, and regulation of apoptosis, pyroptosis, and microRNA-related pathways. Clinical evidence, derived predominantly from individuals with Type 2 diabetes and subclinical or early cardiac abnormalities, suggests that combined aerobic and resistance training can improve cardiorespiratory fitness, insulin sensitivity, vascular function, and selected indices of left ventricular performance. High-intensity interval training may provide additional benefits in appropriately selected patients, but its safety and effectiveness require individualized assessment. To improve translation, exercise intensity should be reported using physiologically comparable metrics, while treatment response should be evaluated through integrated measures of cardiac imaging, functional capacity, biomarkers, glycemic control, and adverse events. Overall, exercise represents a biologically plausible and clinically relevant adjunctive strategy for diabetic cardiomyopathy, particularly in early-stage disease; however, adequately powered trials in clearly defined patient populations are still needed to establish optimal dose, safety, and long-term cardiovascular benefit.

title: Janus Kinase Inhibitor Use Among People With Inflammatory Disease in Australia.
authorString: Deakin CT, Falster MO, Littlejohn GO, Youssef P, Liew D, Pratt NL, Pearson SA.
abstractText:
Aim

To describe Australian trends in JAKi uptake, where there are no restrictions on the sequence of their use in clinical practice.

Methods

We included all people aged 18 years and over initiating a JAKi between 1 October 2015 and 31 August 2022. We used national dispensing claims data for a random 10% sample of Australians to: describe the number of people initiating JAKi per quarter; the characteristics of new JAKi users including demographics, use of other medicines to manage cardiovascular comorbid disease; and use of prior targeted therapy (biologics or small molecule inhibitors). We used Kaplan-Meier analysis to estimate the proportion of initiators who were persistent on their initial JAKi to 365 days.

Results

We identified 2904 people initiating JAKi treatment between 1 October 2015 and 31 August 2022; new use increased consistently during the study period. 45% of initiators had not been dispensed a prior subsidised targeted therapy in 365 days prior to JAKi initiation; 72% of new users were female and 62% were aged 55 years or older. Almost half of people initiating JAKi had at least one marker of higher cardiovascular risk, with 30% dispensed medicines to treat or prevent cardiovascular disease in the year prior to initiation; and 34% being aged 65 years or older. 60% of people persisted on their initial JAKi therapy to 365 days. Of those who stopped, 51% switched to a biologic and 15% switched to a different JAKi.

Conclusion

In a setting where JAKi are permitted to be used in any line of therapy, 45% of new users of JAKi were naïve to targeted therapy and half had at least one marker of cardiovascular risk. Continued monitoring is required to understand the risk profile of JAKi, particularly in those with high baseline cardiovascular disease risk.

title: PTGS1 Regulates Macrophage Polarization Through PPARγ Nuclear Translocation to Affect Oxidative Stress Injury in Chronic Prostatitis.
authorString: Song J, Li W, Han S, Song W, Liang C, Liu Y, Zhang K, Chen X.

journal.title: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine

abstractText: Chronic Prostatitis/Chronic Pelvic Pain Syndrome (CP/CPPS) is a condition marked by persistent inflammation of the prostate, whose underlying mechanisms remain poorly defined. This study aimed to investigate the role of prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 1 (PTGS1) in macrophages and in a mouse model of experimental autoimmune prostatitis (EAP). Using multiple experimental methods, we found that PTGS1 was induced during IL-4-mediated M2 macrophage polarization, whereas PTGS1 silencing further enhanced M2 polarization. Mechanistically, PTGS1 functioned as a feedback regulatory checkpoint by interacting with PPARγ in the cytoplasm and restraining its nuclear translocation; PTGS1 silencing released this constraint, enhanced PPARγ nuclear accumulation, and promoted M2 macrophage polarization. In EAP mice, PTGS1 knockdown alleviated disease progression and reduced oxidative stress injury, accompanied by increased M2 macrophage polarization and reduced iNOS-positive pro-inflammatory macrophage accumulation. Furthermore, PTGS1 silencing diminished the PTGS1-PPARγ interaction, thereby enhancing PPARγ nuclear translocation and strengthening the M2 polarization program. In summary, our findings show that PTGS1 knockdown attenuates F4/80<sup>+</sup>/iNOS<sup>+</sup> pro-inflammatory macrophage accumulation, mitigates prostatic inflammation and oxidative stress, and offers a potential immunomodulatory strategy for CP/CPPS.

title: Opioid Modulation of Major Neurotransmitter Systems: Acute, Chronic, and Withdrawal Effects.
authorString: Novakova D, Pritulova E, Novotny J.
abstractText: Opioids are widely used in clinical practice for the management of moderate-to-severe acute and chronic pain. However, their use is associated with the development of tolerance and physical dependence, often followed by a withdrawal syndrome upon discontinuation. The mechanisms underlying opioid dependence and withdrawal are highly complex and remain incompletely understood. These processes involve multiple regions of the central nervous system and are accompanied by widespread alterations in neuronal signaling pathways. Neurotransmitters, which are essential for communication between neurons, play a critical role in opioid addiction and withdrawal. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview of the major neurotransmitter systems, their involvement, and the changes that occur during acute and chronic opioid exposure. Particular attention is also given to the consequences of opioid discontinuation. Overall, this review summarizes current knowledge of the molecular mechanisms underlying both the acute and long-term effects of opioids on key neurotransmitter systems in the brain.

title: Skin-Protective Effects of Marinophyll, a Carotenoid From Marine Erythrobacter sp. SDW2.
authorString: Kim H, Kyung S, Lee KE, Nho YH, Ryu J, Park M, Choi YJ, Kang S.

journal.title: Skin research and technology : official journal of International Society for Bioengineering and the Skin (ISBS) [and] International Society for Digital Imaging of Skin (ISDIS) [and] International Society for Skin Imaging (ISSI)

abstractText:
Background

Previous studies have highlighted that marine organisms, such as microalgae and marine bacteria, exhibit significantly higher and more sustainable biosynthetic yields of unique carotenoids compared to terrestrial sources. These advantages in production efficiency have sparked significant interest in developing materials derived from marine origins. Marinophyll, natural carotenoids extracted from marine sources, have demonstrated potential in managing oxidative stress and inflammation linked to various skin conditions.

Materials and methods

HaCaT keratinocytes were treated with various concentrations of Marinophyll and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) to assess cell viability and intracellular ROS production. Antioxidant enzyme expression, including Nrf2, HO-1, and SOD2, was evaluated using RT-PCR and immunocytochemistry. The anti-inflammatory effects of Marinophyll were investigated in HaCaT cells treated with IL-4 and Poly I:C, and skin barrier repair was assessed in human skin explants using immunofluorescence staining. The skin explants were obtained from healthy adult donors (aged 43-57 years) undergoing elective breast reduction or abdominoplasty surgery, with informed consent and approval from the relevant ethics committee. All tissues were provided by Seoul National University Bundang Hospital.

Results

The results showed that Marinophyll reduced intracellular ROS production in H2O2-exposed HaCaT cells. Additionally, Marinophyll significantly upregulated the mRNA and protein expression of Nrf2, HO-1, and SOD2 in HaCaT cells. Pretreatment with Marinophyll reduced the levels of inflammatory cytokines IL-1α and IL-1β induced by IL-4 and Poly I:C. In human skin explants, Marinophyll enhanced filaggrin expression, contributing to improved skin barrier function.

Conclusion

Marinophyll demonstrates significant antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and skin barrier-enhancing properties, making it a promising candidate for therapeutic applications in managing oxidative stress and inflammation-associated skin disorders.

title: Preparation, Spectroscopic Elucidation, Antioxidant Potential, Enzyme Inhibition, and Molecular Docking Studies of Novel Schiff Base-Derived Thiosemicarbazones.
authorString: Yakan H, Muglu H, Yenigun S, Ozen T.
abstractText: New thiosemicarbazones bearing Schiff base (1-7) were prepared from 4-(dimethylamino)benzaldehyde and thiosemicarbazides. The reaction of various isothiocyanates with hydrazine monohydrate resulted in the thiosemicarbazides. The structural frameworks of the newly developed derivatives were confirmed by elemental analysis and conventional spectroscopic methods, namely, FT-IR, <sup>1</sup>H, and <sup>13</sup>C NMR. The in vitro antioxidant activity of the synthesized series was evaluated using the DPPH<sup>•</sup> (1,1-diphenyl-2-picrylhydrazyl) scavenging method. The results indicated that the inhibitory concentrations (IC<sub>50</sub>) of the compounds ranged from 8.50 ± 0.14 to 31.44 ± 1.39 µg/mL, with compound 6 exhibiting the most potent antioxidant activity. Additionally, the inhibitory activities of urease and xanthine oxidase (XO) were assessed, and the interactions of the compounds with these enzymes were also analyzed. Molecular docking was performed to assess the interactions between each molecule and the active sites of urease and XO.

title: A Six-Day High-Intensity Interval Training Microcycle Improves Selected Indicators of Endurance Performance in Well-Trained Female Cross-Country Skiers and Biathletes.
authorString: Sørensen A, Odden IU, Rustaden AM, Nygaard H, Hansen J, Sandbakk Ø, Odden TU, Rønnestad BR, Mølmen KS.
abstractText: We compared the effects of a 6-day high-intensity interval training (HIT) microcycle followed by a 5-day active recovery period (HIT<sub>block</sub>) with a time-matched period of continued regular training (REG) on endurance performance in well-trained female cross-country skiers and biathletes. Seventeen athletes (maximal oxygen consumption ( V˙O2max ): 55.1 (5.2) mL·min<sup>-1</sup> kg<sup>-1</sup>) were assigned to either HIT<sub>block</sub> or REG. No differences in training volume or intensity were observed between the groups during the 4 weeks preceding the intervention. During the intervention, HIT<sub>block</sub> completed five HIT sessions over 6 days (6 × 5-min work intervals; target rate of perceived exertion:17-18), with increased HIT replacing part of their habitual training and thereby reducing overall training load, whereas REG continued habitual training, including 3-4 moderate- or high-intensity interval sessions. Endurance performance was assessed during roller ski skating and included 15-min time-trial average velocity (velocity<sub>15-min</sub>), velocity at 4 mmol·L<sup>-1</sup> blood lactate (velocity<sub>4mmol</sub>), and velocity during the final minute of incremental V˙O2max testing ( velocityV˙O2max ). HIT<sub>block</sub> demonstrated greater improvements than REG in velocityV˙O2max (3.6 (2.1)% versus 1.2 (1.6)%, p = 0.024) and velocity<sub>4mmol</sub> (4.4 (2.9)% versus 0.0 (4.4)%, p = 0.023), whereas changes in velocity<sub>15-min</sub> did not differ between groups (5.4 (5.0)% versus 1.3 (3.4)%, p = 0.083). An exploratory composite performance index combining these outcomes demonstrated superior improvements in HIT<sub>block</sub> compared with REG (4.5 (2.8)% versus 0.9 (2.6)%, p = 0.017). These findings indicate that a 6-day HIT microcycle followed by a 5-day active recovery period is associated with greater improvements in selected endurance performance indicators compared with continued regular training in well-trained female cross-country skiers and biathletes.

title: Hookworm Parasitism Shapes Energy Status and Cardiovascular Disease Risk in Northeast Madagascar.
authorString: Kolinski L, Titcomb G, Kauffman K, Rabezara JY, Rahary P, Pender M, Solis A, DeSisto CMM, Soarimalala V, Kramer RA, Moody JM, Nunn CL.

journal.title: American journal of human biology : the official journal of the Human Biology Council

abstractText:
Objective

Cardiometabolic diseases are rising in low- and middle-income countries, which also bear high burdens of helminth infection and malnutrition. Untangling the relationships among helminth infection, energy status, and cardiovascular disease is important for reducing these burdens.

Methods

We investigated the interacting risks and moderating variables associated with cardiometabolic health using demographic, health, and hookworm infection data from 874 participants in rural northeast Madagascar.

Results

We observed wide variation in body-mass index (BMI) and blood pressure, alongside high prevalences of two helminth infections: the human hookworm Necator americanus (53.6%) and the zoonotic hookworm Ancylostoma ceylanicum (20.4%). We hypothesized that hookworm infections would be associated with reduced BMI and lower blood pressure through energetic and immunomodulatory pathways. Yet, the two hookworm species showed different associations, with N. americanus infection negatively associated with BMI and A. ceylanicum infection positively associated with blood pressure. Wealthier individuals had higher BMI, but this positive effect was attenuated if they were infected with A. ceylanicum. Coinfection with both hookworms did not significantly modify these associations with BMI or blood pressure. Structural equation modeling indicated that N. americanus infection was associated with reduced blood pressure both directly and through its negative association with BMI, while A. ceylanicum infection was associated with increased blood pressure independent of BMI.

Conclusions

Our findings shed new light on the interacting burdens of malnutrition, parasitism, and chronic diseases with implications for public health, highlighting that these associations are dependent on parasite species.

title: Calcium dysregulation in small animals: When is it an emergency?
authorString: Lum J, Thomovsky EJ, Rincon AA, Johnson PA, Brooks AC.

journal.title: The Canadian veterinary journal = La revue veterinaire canadienne

abstractText: Calcium is essential for neuromuscular signaling, cardiovascular stability, and metabolic regulation. Disturbances in calcium homeostasis can exacerbate critical illness in small animal patients, whereas more profound abnormalities are associated with life-threatening complications. Although not frequently encountered, both hypocalcemia and hypercalcemia require rapid recognition and targeted therapy in an emergency setting. This article reviews the fundamental principles of calcium regulation, outlines the major etiologies and clinical features of disordered calcium balance, and provides an evidence-based approach to acute management. Practical considerations for monitoring, fluid and drug therapy, and supportive care are emphasized. Finally, we present novel and experimental interventions under evaluation in both veterinary and human medicine, highlighting areas in which future research may improve treatment options for animals.

title: A Versatile, Patient-Centred Approach to Surgical Wound Closure: A Single-Centre Case Series on the Use of a Synthetic Electrospun Fibre Matrix in Vasculopathic Patients.
authorString: Dudkiewicz M.
abstractText: Patients with vascular disease often suffer from lower extremity ulcerations that may require surgical intervention to remove non-viable or infected tissues. Post-operatively, these patients still present with a high risk of non-healing due to poor blood flow and chronic inflammation. Advanced wound healing matrices may be considered to support tissue regenerative and reduce the risk of further wound complications. A synthetic electrospun fibre matrix (SEFM) (Restrata, Acera Surgical Inc.) is a fully synthetic, extracellular matrix that encourages cellular infiltration and neovascularization with minimal inflammatory response. In the present study, a single vascular surgeon retrospectively reviewed data of vasculopathic patients treated with SEFM during surgical management of various wound aetiologies. Ten patients were identified and data on time to closure, closure approach and post-operative complications were collected and analysed. SEFM was utilized to either support neo-vascularization for subsequent autografting or re-epithelialization through secondary intention healing. All patients in this series achieved either definitive closure or complete re-epithelialization in an average of 6.8 weeks. One instance of superficial infection was successfully managed with antibiotics. No instances of unplanned re-operation or other wound complications were observed. Early experience suggests practical application of SEFM for surgical wound management in vasculopathic patients.

title: Further Insights Into the Mechanisms of Lymph Node Metastasis.
authorString: Nathanson SD, O'Melia MJ, Rosso KC, Wood IS, Lall D, Bui JT.
abstractText: Metastasis of malignant tumors arising from epithelial organs to sentinel lymph nodes has important implications for prognosis, staging, and therapeutic decision-making. Recent insights into anatomic pathways, pathogenesis, molecular interactions, and genetic factors have encouraged scientists and clinicians to develop drugs that target mechanisms of lymph node metastasis. We summarize important aspects of the vast literature that pertains to these mechanisms, focusing on five phases that implicate invasion through the epithelial basement membrane and tumor microenvironment, into initial lymphatics, and, after flow through lymphatic trunks, into the sentinel lymph node. Valuable information regarding tumor cell-directed motility, lymphangiogenesis, host cells that enhance metastasis, immune responses to tumor antigens, and tumor-induced changes in sentinel lymph node(s) provides a promising avenue for the continued development of new therapeutic approaches to prevent and treat metastasis. This article reviews these aspects by synthesizing current scientific and clinical advances and translating them for medical professionals.

title: Pharmacogenomics in Cancer Treatment: Challenges and Opportunities in African Settings.
authorString: Maphumulo NF, Rebello G, Ramsuran V.
abstractText:
Background

Cancer incidence in Africa is projected to reach 2.1 million new cases annually by 2040. Current treatment guidelines remain largely based on pharmacogenomic data predominantly from European and Asian genetic profiles, potentially compromising safety and efficacy in African patients. However, limited clinical validation data, extreme intra-population genetic diversity, and significant healthcare infrastructure barriers constrain the translational application of pharmacogenomics in Africa.

Objective

This review critically examines pharmacogenomic variants with established clinical actionability in cancer treatment, focusing on those with differential frequencies or African-specific alleles, and evaluates the evidence base for their implementation in African healthcare settings.

Methods

We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, PharmGKB, dbSNP, and Google Scholar for peer-reviewed studies reporting pharmacogenomic variants in African or African-ancestry populations relevant to cancer therapeutics. We synthesised evidence from recent African and global studies on pharmacogenomic variants affecting commonly used chemotherapy agents.

Results

Several variants show marked frequency differences between African-ancestry reference populations and European populations, including DPYD rs115232898 (2.06% vs. 0.00%), CYP2D6*17 (18.76% vs. 0%), and CYP3A5*6 (12.82% vs. 0%). However, many of these estimates derive primarily from African-American datasets and should not be interpreted as representative of continental African populations. African-specific variants such as CYP2D6*17 and DPYD rs115232898 are underrepresented in guideline development datasets. Intra-African genetic diversity is the highest globally, with Khoi-San populations harbouring extensive private variation, suggesting that no single pharmacogenomic panel will be universally applicable across the continent.

Conclusion

While pharmacogenomics holds substantial promise for personalising cancer treatment in Africa, its current translational readiness is limited by a critical lack of African-specific clinical validation data. Priorities include multi-site validation studies, development of African-enriched genotyping panels, and integration of pharmacogenomic education into oncology practice. Implementation must be accompanied by ethical frameworks ensuring data sovereignty and equitable benefit-sharing.

title: Adapting an Interprofessional Medication Adherence Program for Gout (IMAP-Gout): A Theory-Informed Pre-Implementation Analysis Using the Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF).
authorString: Tahir F, Gul H, Bossina S, Rezae F, Martens D, Rickard H, Kelly A.
abstractText:
Introduction

Adherence rates to urate lowering therapy in gout remain low. Successfully implemented in Switzerland, the Interprofessional Medication Adherence Program (IMAP) supports medication adherence through an ambulatory-based model of care that includes pharmacists, motivational interviewing, and electronic adherence monitoring. We aimed to determine the facilitators and barriers to implementing IMAP for patients with gout in a hospital in Australia.

Methods

Multi-stakeholder, semi-structured interviews were analyzed using the Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF) for each stakeholder group and Implementation Mapping was used to identify target behaviors.

Results

A total of 51 interviews were conducted with patients (n = 8), a general practitioner (n = 1), pharmacists (n = 8), rheumatologists (n = 21), nurses (n = 4), and decision/policy makers (n = 9). Patients identified their health-reducing gout flares and improving function-as key facilitators, while barriers included environmental context and resources, such as time constraints. Pharmacists and nurses were motivated by professional role and identity, particularly the opportunity to extend their skillsets. However, pharmacists faced barriers related to environmental context and resources, including insufficient funding or managerial support. Nurses were keen to improve their knowledge and skills, such as training in motivational interviewing. Rheumatologists were driven by their goals of improving patient outcomes, but expressed concerns about ensuring governance over a pharmacist-led program. For general practitioners, behaviors were facilitated by environmental context and resources, such as remuneration. Finally, decision/policy makers identified improving health system outcomes as key enablers, but emphasized the importance of program reach and cost-effectiveness.

Conclusion

For successful implementation within our context, IMAP-Gout needs to be adapted from a pharmacist-led model to a nurse-led model.

title: Changes in Post-Transplant Vaccine Coverage After Implementing Structured Vaccine Reviews in Pediatric Solid Organ Transplant Recipients in British Columbia, Canada: A Canadian Immunization Research Network Study.
authorString: Barbey FA, Sadarangani M, Burton C, Urschel S, MacDonald SE, McConnell A, Morin E, Meesters K, Blydt-Hansen T, Yong E, Mitchell H, Special Immunization Clinic Network Investigators.
abstractText:
Background

Children with solid organ transplants (SOT) are at increased risk of infections but may be under-vaccinated. In 2021, our center implemented structured post-SOT vaccine reviews. We conducted a single-center, pre-post observational study with a repeated cross-sectional design to assess changes in vaccine coverage from 2020 to 2024.

Methods

We performed a chart review of SOT recipients aged 2-18 years who were ≥ 1 year post-transplant and followed at our clinic on March 1, 2020, and/or March 1, 2024. Patients eligible at both time points (repeat participants) were included in both cohorts; those eligible once (single-time-point participants) were included in the respective cohort. We assessed individual and overall vaccine coverage, defined as receipt of all recommended non-live, non-seasonal vaccines. Comparisons used the chi-square and paired McNemar's test (two-sided p < 0.05).

Results

Overall vaccine coverage increased from 33% in 2020 to 51% in 2024. The most prominent changes were observed for 23-valent pneumococcal polysaccharide (PPV23) and human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines, with significant improvements among both single-time-point (PPV23: 58%-88%, p < 0.001; HPV: 32%-81%, p = 0.003) and repeat participants (PPV23: 52%-76%, p = 0.008; HPV: 20%-53%, p = 0.008). Overall vaccine coverage among patients transplanted at age < 2 years was significantly lower compared to older children in 2020 but not in 2024.

Conclusions

Structured post-transplant vaccine reviews were associated with an increase in coverage across most vaccines and all organ subgroups, supporting its integration into routine post-transplant care and prospective, multicenter evaluation.

title: Cargo Stability of Extracellular Vesicles Derived From Non-Diseased Sources: Effects of Storage and Handling Conditions.
authorString: Abbasi K, Mohammadinasr M, Motavalli R, Arianfar N, Toofani-Milani A, Shirzad M, Hosseini V, Darabi M.

journal.title: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine

abstractText: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are nanoscale, membrane-enclosed particles that transfer proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, and other bioactive molecules between cells. Their cargo-bearing capacity supports applications in drug delivery, regenerative medicine, and biomarker development, but ex vivo handling can alter vesicle recovery and cargo readouts. Storage temperature, pH, freeze-thaw exposure, storage duration, and buffer composition differentially affect EV-associated proteins and nucleic acids. This review evaluates preservation studies using EVs from non-diseased cells, tissues, and biological fluids, with emphasis on the distinction between EV recovery, cargo abundance, molecular integrity, and functional preservation. Across the available literature, optimal conditions depend on EV source, biological matrix, isolation method, storage duration, cargo class, and analytical endpoint. Standardized protocols that separately measure vesicle recovery, cargo abundance, molecular integrity, and biological activity are required to define source- and application-specific preservation strategies and resolve the mechanisms of storage-associated cargo alteration.

title: Knockdown of Smurf1 Promotes Autophagy-Dependent Ferroptosis in Acute Liver Failure by Inhibiting Ubiquitin-Mediated Ulk1 Degradation.
authorString: Shi P, Tao M, Zeng Y, Peng Y, Wu X.

journal.title: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine

abstractText: Treating acute liver failure (ALF) relies on rescuing dying hepatocytes and restoring liver regeneration. Ferroptosis contributes to ALF development, so regulating iron homeostasis or lipid peroxide production may be an effective treatment strategy. Ubiquitination can modify ferroptosis and is involved in liver diseases. The study aims to explore the mechanism of E3 ubiquitin ligase Smurf1 regulating ferroptosis in acute liver failure. Screened using proteomics, bioinformatics and experimental verification, we identified Smurf1, a ubiquitin-related protein associated with ferroptosis. Functional experiments were used to verify that Smurf1 regulates hepatocyte ferroptosis and acute liver failure. Furthermore, ubiquitination assays, western blotting and Co-IP experiments were applied to identify Ulk1 as a substrate of Smurf1. Further, we constructed the cell and animal models with silencing or overexpression of Smurf1 and Ulk1 to clarify the potential mechanism of Smurf1 on ferroptosis in ALF. Knockdown or overexpression of Smurf1 promoted or inhibited hepatocyte ferroptosis, respectively. In the animal model, knockdown of Smurf1 significantly aggravated the progression of ALF, suggesting that Smurf1 knockdown exacerbated liver failure by promoting hepatocyte ferroptosis. In conclusion, Smurf1 interacted with the new substrate Ulk1 and promoted its ubiquitin-mediated degradation at the post-translational level, and Smurf1 knockdown promotes ferroptosis in hepatocytes in a manner dependent on Ulk1-mediated autophagy activation.

title: Huaier Attenuates Renal Injury in Type 2 Diabetic Nephropathy by Ameliorating Mitochondrial Dysfunction and Inhibiting Tubular Epithelial Cell Apoptosis.
authorString: Guan Y, Bai X, Wei X, Ding T, Luo P, Nie P.
abstractText:
Background

Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a major microvascular complication of Type 2 diabetes, with renal tubular epithelial cells (RTECs) apoptosis playing a pivotal role in its progression. The aqueous extract of Trametes robiniophila Murr. (Huaier) has shown renoprotective effects, but its specific molecular mechanisms in DN remain to be fully elucidated.

Objective

This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects of Huaier aqueous extract on DN and verify whether its anti-apoptotic mechanism is mediated through the Wnt/β-catenin pathway using the pathway activator SKL2001.

Methods

In vivo, KKAy Type 2 diabetic mice were treated with Huaier (5 g/kg/day) for 12 weeks to evaluate renal function and histopathology. In vitro, HK-2 cells were treated with high glucose and palmitate (HG + PA) to induce injury. The Wnt/β-catenin pathway activator SKL2001 was employed to determine if activating this pathway could abolish the protective effects of Huaier.

Results

Bioinformatics analysis indicates that the regulation of apoptosis is the primary mechanism by which Huaier improves DN. In vivo, Huaier reduced UACR and improved renal histopathology in KKAy mice. Consistently, TUNEL staining and molecular analysis confirmed that Huaier significantly suppressed RTECs apoptosis within the renal tissues. In vitro experiments demonstrated that Huaier significantly inhibited HG + PA-induced oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and RTECs apoptosis. Notably, the administration of SKL2001 effectively reversed these protective effects, leading to increased β-catenin expression and elevated apoptosis levels despite Huaier treatment.

Conclusion

Huaier aqueous extract mitigates RTECs apoptosis and renal injury in Type 2 diabetic nephropathy by suppressing the Wnt5a/β-catenin signaling pathway.

title: Long-term Patency of Venous Stent After Sharp Recanalization for Benign Superior Vena Cava Occlusion.
authorString: Shima R, Fujimori M, Yamanaka T, Matsushita N, Kokawa T, Kato H, Fukui H, Omori Y, Yamaoka Y, Sakuma H.
abstractText:
Background/aim

The incidence of benign superior vena cava syndrome (SVCS) is increasing due to the widespread use of central venous catheters and cardiac devices. Endovascular therapy is a first-line treatment option; however, recanalization of a completely occluded SVC remains technically challenging, and long-term stent patency data are limited. We report a case of central venous catheter-related benign SVCS treated with stent placement using a sharp recanalization technique and present the resulting 10-year patency outcome.

Case report

A male patient in his 50s presented with facial and upper extremity edema secondary to benign SVCS caused by repeated central venous catheter placement for short-bowel syndrome. Venography revealed complete SVC occlusion (modified Stanford type 4). Sharp recanalization using a trans-septal needle was performed under biplane fluoroscopy and cone-beam computed tomography guidance, followed by placement of a self-expanding bare-metal stent (14 × 40 mm). Symptoms resolved the following day. In-stent re-stenosis occurred at 10 months and was successfully managed with balloon dilatation, after which the stent remained patent with no recurrence of SVCS on annual follow-up. Long-term patency of the stent was achieved for the next 10 years.

Conclusion

Sharp recanalization using a trans-septal needle enabled safe and effective stent placement for completely occluded benign SVC. Long-term stent patency of 10 years was achieved with a single re-intervention, demonstrating that this technique is a viable treatment option for benign SVCS.

title: Predictors of Cardiovascular Events in Patients Undergoing Maintenance Hemodialysis for Diabetic Kidney Disease: A Two-year Prospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Nakamura N, Osawa H, Tsutaya C, Saitoh H, Suzuki T.
abstractText:
Background/aim

Patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis (HD) for diabetic kidney disease (DKD) have a high risk of cardiovascular (CV) events. This study aimed to identify predictors of CV events in these patients, focusing on the prognostic significance of plasma docosapentaenoic acid (DPA).

Patients and methods

This prospective study enrolled 255 patients on maintenance HD between May 2019 and May 2020. Of these, 123 patients whose underlying disease was DKD were analyzed in this study. Baseline clinical parameters, lipid profiles, plasma fatty acids, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) were measured. Patients were followed for two years to monitor CV events.

Results

During follow-up, 28 CV events occurred. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that a history of CV disease, high hs-CRP, and low plasma DPA levels were significantly associated with CV events. Multivariable Cox regression identified a history of CV disease [hazard ratio (HR)=4.86, p<0.001] and elevated hs-CRP (HR=2.80, p=0.035) as independent predictors of CV events. The association of lower DPA with CV events in univariate analysis was not retained after multivariable adjustment.

Conclusion

A history of CV disease and elevated hs-CRP are independent predictors of future CV events in patients on maintenance HD for DKD. While lower DPA levels were associated with CV risk in univariate analysis, larger multicenter studies are needed to fully clarify its prognostic significance.

title: A Comparative Exploratory Study of Cognitive and Functional Outcomes by Sex and Age in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Atrial Fibrillation.
authorString: Militaru M, Lighezan DF, Tudoran C, Cimpean AM, Berzescu N, Militaru AG.
abstractText:
Background/aim

Atrial fibrillation (AF) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are associated with cognitive decline, but possible sex-related differences in cognitive and functional outcomes remain uncertain. This exploratory study evaluated sex-stratified associations of clinical factors, depressive symptoms, and functional independence with severe cognitive impairment in patients with T2DM, AF, and newly identified cognitive decline.

Patients and methods

The study included 140 patients with T2DM, AF, and a Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score <27, comprising 68 men and 72 women. Cognitive performance, depressive symptoms, and functional status were assessed using the MMSE, Montreal Cognitive Assessment, 15-item Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS-15), Activities of Daily Living (ADL), and Instrumental Activities of Daily Living scales. Logistic regression was used to evaluate factors associated with severe cognitive impairment, defined as MMSE <24, in the overall cohort and separately in male and female patients.

Results

Severe cognitive impairment was present in 32/68 men (47.06%) and 36/72 women (50.00%), with no significant difference between sexes. Increasing age and higher diastolic blood pressure were associated with higher odds of MMSE <24 in the overall cohort and in sex-stratified analyses. Higher GDS-15 scores were associated with increased odds of severe cognitive impairment in both sexes, whereas greater functional independence, reflected by higher ADL scores, was associated with lower odds of MMSE <24.

Conclusion

Age, higher diastolic blood pressure, and greater depressive symptom burden in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus were associated with increased odds of severe cognitive impairment, whereas greater functional independence was associated with lower odds in both sexes. These exploratory findings support cognitive, cardiovascular, psychological, and functional assessment in patients with T2DM and AF.

title: Prognostic Value of Histology-specific Ki-67 Labeling Index Cutoffs in Stage I-III Non-small Cell Lung Cancer.
authorString: Kameda Y, Woo T, Matsumura M, Sawazumi T, Arai H, Okudela K, Saito A.
abstractText:
Background/aim

Although the Ki-67 labeling index (LI) is widely used as a marker of tumor proliferative activity, its prognostic utility in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains uncertain because of heterogeneous study populations and the lack of standardized, histology-specific cutoff values.

Patients and methods

We retrospectively analyzed 1,245 patients with completely resected pathologic stage I-III NSCLC. Time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis for postoperative recurrence within 5 years was used to determine Ki-67 LI cutoff values. Associations between Ki-67 LI status and recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models.

Results

Ki-67 LI was significantly higher in squamous cell carcinoma than in adenocarcinoma (median, 40.0% vs. 15.0%; p<0.001). Time-dependent ROC analysis yielded a cutoff value of 21.0% for the overall NSCLC cohort and histology-specific cutoff values of 13.0% for adenocarcinoma and 40.5% for squamous cell carcinoma. The corresponding 5-year area under the curves (AUCs) were 0.656 for the overall NSCLC cohort, 0.691 for adenocarcinoma, and 0.607 for squamous cell carcinoma. After multivariable adjustment, high Ki-67 LI was independently associated with poorer RFS in the overall NSCLC cohort [hazard ratio (HR)=1.40; 95% confidence interval (CI)=1.11-1.77; p=0.005], adenocarcinoma cohort (HR=1.57; 95%CI=1.15-2.16; p=0.005), and squamous cell carcinoma cohort (HR=1.82; 95%CI=1.22-2.73; p=0.004). High Ki-67 LI was also independently associated with poorer OS in the overall NSCLC and adenocarcinoma cohorts, but not in the squamous cell carcinoma cohort.

Conclusion

High Ki-67 LI was independently associated with an increased risk of postoperative recurrence in both adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma. Histology-specific cutoffs derived by time-dependent ROC analysis may support Ki-67-based postoperative risk stratification in resected NSCLC.

title: Renal and Vascular Effects of Selective FGFR4 Inhibition in Folic Acid-induced Kidney Injury in Rats.
authorString: Rumanli Z, Avci E, Yilmaz ÜI, Baykal B, Yildirim BK, Aksoy OA, Göksel BA, Vural IM.
abstractText:
Background/aim

Fibroblast growth factor-23 (FGF-23) has been implicated in chronic kidney disease (CKD)-associated cardiovascular dysfunction, potentially through fibroblast growth factor receptor 4 (FGFR4). This study investigated renal and vascular alterations in folic acid-induced CKD and evaluated the effects of selective FGFR4 inhibition.

Materials and methods

Male Sprague-Dawley rats were assigned to healthy control, CKD control, vehicle, and roblitinib-treated groups. CKD was induced by a single intraperitoneal dose of folic acid. Serum creatinine, FGF-23, tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin-1β, and asymmetric dimethylarginine levels were measured. Vascular reactivity was evaluated in isolated aortic rings using phenylephrine, carbachol, and sodium nitroprusside. Renal fibrosis, carotid calcification, and medial thickness were assessed histologically.

Results

Folic acid administration increased serum creatinine and relative kidney weight and impaired both endothelium-dependent and endothelium-independent vascular relaxation. Relative kidney weight was lower in the roblitinib-treated group than in the CKD control group. However, changes in vascular responses observed in both the treatment and vehicle groups prevented these effects from being attributed specifically to FGFR4 inhibition. FGF-23 and inflammatory marker levels did not differ significantly among the groups. Carotid medial thickness was significantly greater in the treatment group than in the CKD-control group (p<0.05), whereas no other significant between-group differences were detected.

Conclusion

Folic acid-induced renal injury was associated with early functional vascular impairment despite limited structural and inflammatory alterations. Selective FGFR4 inhibition did not demonstrate a clear therapeutic effect. Further in vivo studies using complementary CKD models, direct assessment of FGFR4 signaling, and vehicle formulations without intrinsic vascular activity are required to validate these findings.

title: Machine Learning and Structural Analysis for Generation-Wise Selection of Perylene Diimide Dendrimers Based on Topological Compatibility With Drug Molecules.
authorString: Bibi Z, Ali J, Irshad S, Ghafar MS, Ali Y, Shang Y.
abstractText: Machine learning is increasingly used to explore structure-property relationships in dendrimer-drug systems; however, its integration with topology-based structural compatibility analysis remains limited. This study presents a learning-driven framework to evaluate the topology-based structural compatibility of perylene diimide core dendrimers with antiviral, antioxidant, and imaging agents. Within a quantitative structure-property relationship framework, linear regression, Gaussian process regression (GPR), and artificial neural networks are employed to identify dominant graph-theoretic topological indices and to capture linear and nonlinear structure-property relationships. These insights are combined with a structure-based compatibility analysis that ranks dendrimer generations without altering drug identity or ordering. Generation-wise compatibility is computed using standardized Euclidean distance after global normalization, and ranking stability is assessed through monotonic and magnitude analysis. Results show class-dependent descriptor relevance, with GPR achieving test-set R<sup>2</sup> values above 0.94 for molecular weight, exact mass, monoisotopic mass, and heavy atom count. The generation-wise compatibility analysis further reveals distinct topology-based structural compatibility patterns across the investigated drug classes, highlighting the value of integrating machine learning with graph-theoretic analysis for rational nanocarrier design and the computational assessment of potential encapsulation suitability.

title: Chronic Intermittent Hypoxia Aggravates the Pyroptosis of Renal Tubular Epithelial Cells Through Regulating Mitophagy-Mediated NLRP3 Inflammasome Activation.
authorString: Zhang Y, Tai H.

journal.title: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

abstractText: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA)-induced renal injury is triggered by chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH). Our previous article has revealed that CIH triggers the pyroptosis of renal tubular epithelial cells through the activation of NLRP3 inflammasome, whereas the mechanism by which CIH activates NLRP3 inflammasome remains elusive. Rats and HK-2 cells were exposed to CIH to establish CIH models. Histopathological staining, blood urea nitrogen (BUN) and serum creatinine (Scr) levels were examined to assess renal injury. Western blot and immunofluorescence assay were used to assess proteins related to NLRP3 inflammasome, pyroptosis and mitophagy. Mitochondrial membrane potential and production of ROS and ATP were examined to evaluate mitochondrial function. CCK-8, LDH release and ELISA assays were performed to assess cell injury and inflammation. Mitochondrial division inhibitor 1 (Mdivi-1) was applied for a rescue assay. CIH induced renal injury and suppressed mitophagy in vivo, evidenced by worsening pathological features, elevated Scr and BUN levels, reduced colocalization of Tom20 with LC3B, and downregulated expression of LC3-II/I ratio, Atg5, PINK1 and Parkin. PINK1 overexpression restored mitophagy by enhancing colocalization of mitochondria with LC3B, upregulating LC3-II/I ratio and Atg5, and restored mitochondrial function of CIH-exposed HK-2 cells through enhancing mitochondrial membrane potential, reducing ROS production and increasing ATP content. PINK1 overexpression alleviated cell viability, inflammation and NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated pyroptosis in CIH-exposed HK-2 cells, which were partly abolished by Mdivi-1. PINK1 attenuated NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated pyroptosis in CIH-exposed HK-2 cells partially through restoring mitophagy and mitochondrial function, providing potential therapeutic strategies for OSA-related kidney diseases.

title: Levodopa and Subthalamic Nucleus Deep Brain Stimulation Modulate Excitation/Inhibition Balance and the Neural Encoding of Isochronous Sequences in Persons With Parkinson's Disease.
authorString: Criscuolo A, Schwartze M, Schwarz J, Strecker K, Hesse S, Kotz SA.

journal.title: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences

abstractText: Temporally regular auditory stimuli, as found in isochronous sound streams, metronome beats, or music, are often used in rhythmic auditory stimulation (RAS) interventions to initiate and stabilize the temporal coordination of motor plans in persons with Parkinson's disease (pwPD). Research suggests that RAS promotes the recruitment of a cerebellar-prefrontal network and recalibrates abnormal β-band synchronization in the striato-thalamo-cortical pathway. These cuing effects can resemble those observed via dopaminergic treatments (e.g., levodopa) and deep brain stimulation (DBS) targeting the subthalamic nucleus (STN). Here, we investigated the influence of both levodopa administration and STN DBS on the neural encoding of isochronous auditory sequences in pwPD. A comprehensive analysis of electroencephalography (EEG) data revealed changes in β-band event-locked neural responses, as well as event-related potentials, neural tracking of rhythm (δ-band inter-trial phase coherence), and excitation/inhibition balance (E/I) as a function of these treatments. Furthermore, we characterized the link between changes in E/I and motor symptom severity (UPDRS-III) with levodopa administration. We suggest that characterizing individual responses to specific treatments is a fundamental step in tailoring rehabilitation protocols and optimizing intervention efficacy.

title: Bacterial sialidases subvert the complement system through desialylation.
authorString: Kurniyati K, Clark ND, Fu Q, Zhang S, Qiu W, Malkowski MG, Li C.

journal.title: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society

abstractText: Bacterial sialidases (neuraminidases) are widely studied virulence factors, yet their impact on the complement system, a central component of innate immunity, remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the effects of six sialidases from five human pathogens, including Bacteroides fragilis, Clostridium perfringens, Tannerella forsythia, Treponema denticola, and Vibrio cholerae on complement immunity using an integrated approach combining genetics, biochemistry, glycobiology, mass spectrometry, and structural biology. We show that major complement proteins, including C1q, C4, and C5, as well as complement regulators Factor I, Factor H, and C4BP, are modified by terminal sialic acids (sialylation) and undergo terminal desialylation by all six sialidases. Using the oral pathogen T. denticola and its sialidase NanH as a representative model, we demonstrate that sialidase-mediated desialylation suppresses complement activation and surface deposition, promoting complement evasion. Structural analyses of T. denticola NanH in complex with an inhibitor, sialic acid, and native glycans, together with comparisons to other sialidase structures, reveal the molecular basis of substrate recognition and catalysis. Despite substantial sequence diversity, all six exo-α-sialidases share a conserved six-bladed β-propeller catalytic domain and cleave both N-acetylneuraminic acid and N-glycolylneuraminic acid, the predominant mammalian sialic acids. Together, these findings establish a conserved structural and functional mechanism by which diverse bacterial pathogens desialylate complement components to impair innate immune defense.

title: Endoplasmic Reticulum Autophagy Enhancement Alleviates Synaptic Plasticity Dysfunction and Ameliorates Cognitive Impairment in SAE Mice by Relieving STING-Associated Inhibition of PKM2 Activity.
authorString: Guo X, Yin D, Zhang Z, Zhao Y, Zhang Y, Jiang Y, Zhao Z, Sun T, Zhou F, Zhang X.
abstractText:
Background

The pathogenesis of cognitive impairment in patients with sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) remains unclear. This study investigated whether enhancing micro-endoplasmic reticulum autophagy (micro-ER-phagy) could alleviate synaptic dysfunction and improve cognitive impairment in SAE mice models by relieving stimulator of interferon gene (STING)-associated inhibition of pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2) activity.

Methods

Male wild-type and neuron-specific PKM2 conditional knockout mice (PKM2fl/fl; hSyn-Cre+) were used. Cognitive function in SAE mice models was assessed using the Y-maze and contextual fear conditioning tests. Neuronal plasticity was examined using transmission electron microscopy and Golgi staining, whereas immunofluorescence staining and Western blotting were employed to determine the temporal and spatial expression patterns of related proteins.

Results

Septic mice developed cognitive impairment. Hippocampal tissues of SAE mice exhibited synaptic plasticity dysfunction and glycolysis enhancement. Meanwhile, the hippocampus showed increased PKM2 expression and an altered ratio of PKM2 tetramers and dimers. In addition, phosphorylated STING significantly increased in concentration in hippocampal neurones and its knockdown improved cognitive function. However, this cognitive rescue failed in PKM2 conditional knockout mice treated with SAE. Finally, Sec62-mediated micro-ER-phagy promoted lysosomal degradation of STING, which relieved STING-mediated inhibition of PKM2 and improved synaptic plasticity and cognitive dysfunction in SAE mice.

Conclusions

Elevated micro-ER-phagy may relieve the STING-associated inhibition of PKM2 activity, improve neuronal glycolysis and synaptic plasticity, and alleviate cognitive dysfunction in SAE mice.

title: Associations Between Parity and Parasympathetic Regulation in Response to Infant Crying.
authorString: Gemignani M, Sinisalo H, Peltola MJ.
abstractText: Research suggests that women's parasympathetic response to infant crying reflects regulation of arousal and is associated with caregiving behaviors. In particular, respiratory sinus arrhythmia (RSA) withdrawal in response to infant cry stimuli has been associated with maternal sensitivity. However, the ways in which multiple reproductive and caregiving experiences (in terms of giving birth and raising a child) can modulate women's RSA in response to infant crying are still unknown. Our aim was to test whether women's RSA in response to infant crying is associated with parity. Participants included 184 women (62 nulliparous women; 86 primiparous women; 36 multiparous women). RSA was measured while women were watching a neutral video, followed by videos of crying infants. Analyses revealed that perception of infant crying was associated with a significant RSA withdrawal, compared to the baseline condition, in both multiparous and nulliparous women. A statistically significant RSA withdrawal was absent among primiparous women, possibly reflecting a more sustained physiological arousal to infant crying. We discuss the potential challenges in physiological regulation, indexed by RSA withdrawal, among primiparous women in response to infant crying. More sustained arousal may support an increased focus on infant signals but also predispose new mothers to perceive greater stress.

title: Development of Highly Efficient Lysosome-Targeting Peptide Ligands for the Internalization of Extracellular Proteins.
authorString: Zhao Y, Liao Y, Chen X, Cai D, Gonzalez RS, Tang H, Brunel FM, Cox N, Stock J, Fu G, Zaykov AN, Tang W.

journal.title: Chembiochem : a European journal of chemical biology

abstractText: Lysosome-targeting chimeras (LYTACs) induce the internalization of extracellular and membrane-associated proteins by routing them to lysosomes via endogenous receptors, such as the insulin-like growth factor-2 receptor (IGF2R), also known as cation-independent mannose-6-phosphate receptor. While current IGF2R ligands are effective, expanding the LYTAC toolkit with structurally simple and synthetically accessible ligands remains a practical necessity. Here, we first validated that previously reported dimeric and monomeric peptides induce robust internalization, establishing them as effective IGF2R-targeting LYTAC ligands. To further optimize the peptide architecture, we performed systematic mutational scanning on its monomeric sequence to simplify the peptide architecture. We identified the L4 variant, which features a single leucine substitution at the fourth position. This optimized monomer induces greater internalization efficiency than the previously reported wild-type monomeric peptide ligand. To demonstrate its utility, we conjugated the L4 recruiter to a specific PCSK9 binder. The resulting bifunctional molecule successfully induced the dose- and time-dependent internalization of PCSK9. Collectively, these findings establish several peptide variants as practical and highly effective building blocks for the development of extracellular protein internalization platforms.

title: Combined Use of Adhesive Mesh Closure and Closed-Incision Negative Pressure Therapy for High-Risk Surgical Wounds: A Proof-Of-Concept Study.
authorString: Sanz-Ruiz P, Marquez-Gomez M, Peinado LP, Ayuso AB, Bueno JD, Vaquero J.
abstractText: Surgical wound complications remain a major challenge, particularly in high-risk patients. Closed-incision negative pressure wound therapy (ciNPWT) and adhesive mesh closure systems have shown benefits independently, but their combined use has not been previously evaluated. This single-centre prospective proof-of-concept study included consecutive patients at extremely high risk of wound complications undergoing complex surgical procedures. All patients were treated with adhesive mesh closure (Dermabond Prineo) and ciNPWT (PICO) using a standardized protocol. Outcomes were compared with a historical cohort treated with conventional skin closure. Primary outcomes were wound healing and surgical site complications; secondary outcomes included persistent drainage, delayed healing, readmissions and duration of therapy. Seventeen surgical procedures (16 patients) were included in the prospective cohort and 39 in the historical cohort. The combined strategy achieved consistent wound healing without device-related or allergic complications. Compared with controls, no significant difference was observed for the composite outcome of surgical site complications (17.6% vs. 23.1%), although lower rates were observed for persistent drainage (0 vs. 23.1%, p = 0.045), delayed healing (5.9% vs. 20.5%) and readmissions (0 vs. 20.5%); only persistent drainage reached statistical significance. ciNPWT duration was shorter (12.3 vs. 17.3 days; p = 0.006). This combined approach appears feasible and safe in a highly selected cohort of high-risk patients, with preliminary findings suggesting potential reductions in wound-related complications.

title: Senescent Mesenchymal Stromal Cells Drive Stem Cell Aging Through Dysregulated Chemokine Synthesis.
authorString: Stein SN, Braid LR.
abstractText: Aging is accompanied by a progressive decline in tissue regenerative capacity, driven by intrinsic stem cell dysfunction and age-associated deterioration of the surrounding stem cell niche. Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) are ubiquitous components of stem cell niches, where they integrate structural, metabolic, inflammatory, and paracrine cues to regulate stem cell quiescence, activation, and differentiation. With age, MSCs undergo functional decline and senescence, altering their secretory and signaling profiles. Across tissues, MSC senescence emerges as an intermediate amplifier of aging: molecular, metabolic, epigenetic, and inflammatory stressors promote the senescent state, which converts these upstream insults into chemokine imbalance, chronic inflammation, and progressive loss of stem cell support. Here, we synthesize classical and emerging literature to examine how age-associated changes in MSC chemokine synthesis contribute to stem cell aging, and we propose a synthesis-based model in which MSCs translate age-associated stressors into altered chemokine repertoires that disrupt stem cell-supportive signaling. We also discuss therapeutic strategies, including chemokine-directed therapies, senolytics, and MSC rejuvenation, that may restore regenerative capacity by normalizing MSC-derived signals. Together, the evidence identifies dysregulated chemokine synthesis as a conserved mechanism linking tissue-resident MSC aging to declining regenerative capacity.

title: Voluntary exercise mitigates the effects of peri-adolescent social isolation on emotion recognition and the oxytocinergic system in male mice.
authorString: Van Loveren E, Alfos S, Guu SF, Ducroix-Crepy C, Hernández-Ramírez S, Ferreira G, Lafenetre P.
abstractText: Social isolation, particularly during adolescence, is known to affect cognitive, emotional, and social behaviors as well as brain modulatory systems such as the hypothalamic oxytocinergic system. Interestingly, recent evidence indicates that exercise can exert beneficial effects on behaviors through the activation of the oxytocinergic system. Weaned male mice were either singly- or group-housed and were exposed to either an igloo or a running wheel until the end of the experiment. After 12 weeks in these experimental conditions, they were subjected to various behavioral tests to assess different dimensions of social behaviors (sociability, social recognition and emotion discrimination), anxiety levels, and spatial memory. The impact of peri-adolescent social isolation and of voluntary running activity on the oxytocinergic system was also evaluated. We found that peri-adolescent social isolation enhanced social investigation (social rebound) and impaired emotion discrimination in male mice, without affecting social novelty recognition, spatial memory or anxiety-like behavior. Social isolation also decreased the number of oxytocinergic neurons in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus, but not in the supraoptic nucleus, and did not affect circulating OXT levels. Voluntary exercise protected against social isolation-induced deficits in affective state discrimination and enhanced OXT plasma levels without altering the number of oxytocinergic neurons. Our results indicate that peri-adolescent isolation particularly alters socio-affective discrimination and the oxytocinergic system, that are mitigated by voluntary exercise. This suggests that exercise could alleviate emotion discrimination deficits induced by isolation, possibly through the improvement of oxytocinergic signaling.

title: Airborne and Surface Bacteria in ORs: Integration of ASHRAE-Compliant Ventilation and Active UV-C Air Treatment.
authorString: Lee LD, Clark I, Toldy M, Donnelly C, Hatfield H, Metzger K, Necaise K, Cleveland-Hall LM, Bomgaars S, Nemeth L, Smith JM, Olmsted RN.
abstractText: Bacteria in ORs increase surgical site infection risk. The American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers Standard 170 defines OR ventilation standards, but the added benefit of in-room supplemental ultraviolet C air treatment remains uncertain. We compared bacterial counts before and after installing active ultraviolet C air treatment in an OR with Standard 170-compliant ventilation, using a similar OR as a control with Standard 170-compliant ventilation alone. After installation, the intervention OR showed 80% fewer airborne bacteria and 61% fewer settled surface bacteria. The control OR showed a 219% increase in airborne colony-forming units per cubic meter and a 24% increase in settled surface bacteria over the same period, reflecting potential confounders. Although the intervention was associated with lower bacterial levels in two assays, more evidence is needed given the limited number of ORs tested and the variation in the control OR.

title: Technical development and implementation of 3D-QALAS on a 1.5T MR-Linac for the brain: A prospective R-IDEAL stage 0/1 technology development report.
authorString: McCullum L, Harrington A, West N, Nehring G, Fu Z, Subashi E, Taylor BA, Hwang KP, Fuller CD.

journal.title: Journal of applied clinical medical physics

abstractText:
Background

Quantitative relaxometry of the brain on the integrated MRI / linear accelerator (MR-Linac) at high isotropic reconstructed resolution is currently limited due to prohibitively long scan times and limited field-of-views.

Purpose

The purpose of this study was to assess the technical feasibility of the 3D-QALAS technique on the 1.5T MR-Linac which can acquire whole-brain 1 mm isotropic quantitative T1, T2, and PD maps along with multiple synthetic images in a 7-minute acquisition time.

Methods

A 1 mm isotropic 3D-QALAS acquisition was scanned in both phantoms and five healthy volunteers on the 1.5T Elekta Unity MR-Linac device with scan times around seven minutes. A test-retest protocol across five independent sessions for the phantom was conducted. The Lin's Concordance Correlation Coefficient (LCCC), repeatability, and reproducibility between measured and reference quantitative T1, T2, and PD values were determined in the phantom. Distortion was also studied. Vendor-provided reconstruction through SyMRI was performed to extract synthetic images and brain volume metric assessments in the healthy volunteers.

Results

The slope and LCCC between the measured and phantom reference values was 1.02 (1.00), 1.09 (0.90), and 0.99 (1.00) for T1, T2, and PD, respectively. Median distortion across the phantom remained below 2 mm. The repeatability and reproducibility coefficient-of-variation (CoV) was under 8% for all measured values. The measured brain volumes in the healthy volunteer was within expected age-adjusted reference values.

Conclusions

The technical feasibility of using 3D-QALAS on the integrated 1.5T MR-Linac was confirmed. Applying this technique to the adaptive radiation therapy workflow of the brain will provide new opportunities to integrate quantitative imaging relaxometry biomarkers at 1 mm isotropic reconstructed resolution.

title: A Species-Dependent Spatial Patterning of FOXP1 and nNOS Protein Expression in the Adult Mammalian Subthalamic Nucleus.
authorString: Medenica T, Bokulić E, Judaš M, Sedmak G.
abstractText: The subthalamic nucleus (STN) is a key component of basal ganglia circuitry involved in motor, cognitive, and limbic functions. While the transcription factor FOXP1 has been implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders and basal ganglia function, its expression in the adult STN remains insufficiently characterized. Our study investigated the expression and distribution of FOXP1 protein and its colocalization with neuronal nitric oxide synthase (nNOS) and a pan-neuronal marker (HuC/HuD) in the adult STN across three mammalian species: mouse, rat, and human. Using immunofluorescent double-labeling and quantitative analysis, we examined their spatial organization and relative proportions within the neuronal population. FOXP1 was identified as a substantial neuronal subpopulation, comprising approximately 40%-45% of STN neurons across all species. In contrast, nNOS-positive neurons showed marked interspecies variation, increasing from ∼32% in mice to ∼68% in humans. Notably, the spatial distribution of these markers differed significantly between species. In rodents, FOXP1+ and nNOS+ neurons were largely segregated along the dorsoventral axis, forming visibly distinct subdomains. Conversely, in the human STN, these populations were diffusely intermixed with a higher degree of colocalization. Additionally, both markers exhibited species-specific antero-posterior gradients. These findings provide the first evidence of FOXP1 protein expression in the adult rat and human STN and highlight fundamental interspecies differences in neuronal organization. The expanded nNOS+ population and increased FOXP1/nNOS colocalization in humans suggest evolutionary divergence in the mammalian STN cytoarchitecture. Overall, the results challenge simplified models of STN subdivision in mammals, primates especially, and underscore the need for caution when extrapolating rodent data to human neurophysiology.

title: Identification of a Glycosylation-Related Gene Prognostic Signature for Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
authorString: Zhao Q, Zhang X, Duan G.
abstractText:
Purpose

A prognostic signature for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) was developed through identification and integration of glycosylation-related genes (GRGs).

Methods

TCGA RNA-seq data for LUAD and LUSC were analyzed. GRGs were intersected with differentially expressed genes; prognostic GRGs were selected via Cox and LASSO regression to construct a risk model. The immune microenvironment and immunotherapy responses were compared between risk groups. An miRNA-mRNA-transcription factor (TF) network was built and potential drugs were predicted. ADAMTS15 expression was verified by RT-qPCR in NSCLC tissues and cell lines; functional assays (CCK-8, wound healing, Transwell) were performed after ADAMTS15 knockdown in A549 (LUAD) and NCI-H520 (LUSC) cells.

Results

A total of 134 differentially expressed GRGs were identified. Ten genes (ADAMTS15, PCSK9, MUC2, B3GNT3, etc.) were selected for the prognostic model, which functioned as an independent prognostic factor. High-risk patients showed poorer immunotherapy response. The regulatory network included 30 TFs and 142 miRNAs, with 107 drug-target pairs predicted. ADAMTS15 was elevated in NSCLC; its knockdown inhibited proliferation, migration, and invasion in both LUAD and LUSC cell models.

Conclusion

A 10-gene prognostic signature derived from GRGs was identified. Functional validation affirmed ADAMTS15's tumor-promoting role, offering insights for NSCLC prognosis and targeted therapy.

title: Oral Frailty Is Associated With the Physical Component of Health-Related Quality of Life in Middle-Aged and Older Japanese Master Athletes.
authorString: Nakata E, Yamamoto K, Mitamura S, Oda N, Niina H, Nohara A, Hibi Y, Uemura A, Takezawa K, Fujibayashi M.
abstractText:
Background

The association between health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and oral health remains unclear, especially in physically active adults. This study aimed to examine the association between HRQoL and oral frailty in middle-aged and older Japanese master athletes.

Methods

In this cross-sectional study, 197 Japanese master athletes aged ≥ 35 years participated. HRQoL was assessed using the Short Form-8, from which physical (PCS) and mental (MCS) component summary scores were derived. Oral frailty was assessed using the Oral Frailty 5-Item Checklist. Multivariate regression analyses were conducted to adjust for potential confounders.

Results

Of the participants, 195 individuals (median age: 59.0 years [interquartile range: 53.8-68.0], 41.0% women) were included in the analysis. The prevalence of oral frailty was 37.5% in PCS Tertile 1, compared with 16.9% in Tertile 2 and 16.7% in Tertile 3, while the prevalence was similar across MCS tertiles. Multivariate regression analysis revealed that oral frailty was independently and inversely associated with PCS (standardized β = -0.20, p = 0.006), but not MCS (standardized β = -0.12, p = 0.090). In the sub-analysis, difficulty chewing (standardized β = -0.15, p = 0.034) and swallowing (standardized β = -0.26, p < 0.001) were associated with PCS, whereas fewer teeth (standardized β = -0.15, p = 0.035) and dry mouth (standardized β = -0.21, p = 0.004) were associated with MCS.

Conclusion

Oral frailty was significantly associated with physical HRQoL in Japanese master athletes. These findings suggest that incorporating oral frailty assessment into health promotion strategies may enhance HRQoL in physically active adults.

title: PIH1D2 Loss-of-Function Directs Ciliary and Cell Cycle Defects Resulting in Left Isomerism With or Without Biliary Atresia.
authorString: Kurolap A, Chai Gadot C, Shalata A, Eshach Adiv O, Amir Y, Lando BL, Stehling F, Hershkovitz T, Osman K, Habib C, Mintz H, Steinberg R, Hochberg A, Hamiel U, Mory A, Marom D, von Hardenberg S, Singer A, Auber B, Baris Feldman H.

journal.title: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

abstractText:
Background & aims

Laterality disorders are rare congenital conditions caused by disruption of left-right embryonic patterning, often associated with ciliary dysfunction. Despite the identification of numerous causative genes, the molecular basis remains unresolved in many patients. We aimed to identify the genetic cause of left isomerism heterotaxy in two unrelated patients, and investigate the functional consequences of the implicated gene.

Methods

Genome sequencing was performed in both patients. Candidate variants were validated by RNA and protein analyses in patient-derived fibroblasts. To study the functional consequences, we conducted RNA-seq, cell cycle assays (flow cytometry, EdU incorporation, Ki-67 staining), rescue experiments with the wild-type gene, and primary ciliogenesis studies.

Results

Both patients harboured biallelic loss-of-function variants in PIH1D2, a gene not previously associated with human disease. Transcript analyses confirmed aberrant splicing, and immunofluorescence staining revealed loss of PIH1D2 expression in Patient 1's primary fibroblasts. RNA-seq demonstrated dysregulation of pathways related to cell cycle regulation and developmental signalling. Patient fibroblasts showed impaired cell cycle re-entry from G0 following serum starvation and reduced S-phase progression. Wild type PIH1D2 overexpression partially rescued these defects. Furthermore, patient cells exhibited significantly reduced primary ciliogenesis compared to controls.

Conclusions

Our findings establish PIH1D2 as a novel disease gene for left isomerism heterotaxy, with biliary atresia observed in one of the patients. Loss of PIH1D2 impairs ciliogenesis and cell cycle progression, providing a mechanistic link between ciliary defects and abnormal left-right patterning. These results expand the spectrum of cilia-related laterality disorders and identify PIH1D2 as a critical regulator of human development.

title: Conventional and Emerging Protein Ingredients in Farinaceous Products: Amino Acid Quality, Digestibility, Biological Value, and Functional Performance.
authorString: Álvarez-Arteaga P, Lazo-Vélez MA, Mateo Cordero-Clavijo L, Paterson S.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Compr Rev Food Sci Food Saf
journal.title: Comprehensive reviews in food science and food safety
journal.isoabbreviation: Compr Rev Food Sci Food Saf

abstractText: The increasing demand for protein-enriched foods has renewed interest in farinaceous products as widely consumed and technologically adaptable matrices for nutritional improvement. However, protein enrichment cannot be evaluated solely by increases in crude protein content, as nutritional value depends on essential amino acid (EAA) balance, digestibility, biological quality, technofunctional performance, bioactive potential, and interactions within the food matrix. This review critically examines the incorporation of conventional and emerging protein ingredients from animal, plant, insect, microalgal, and macroalgal sources into farinaceous systems, including flours, powders, concentrates, isolates, and hydrolysates. This review synthesizes current evidence through comparative analyses of protein content, EAA profiles, digestibility, protein digestibility-corrected amino acid score (PDCAAS), digestible indispensable amino acid score (DIAAS), technological functionality, and bioactive properties. Particular attention is given to formulation and processing strategies that improve protein quality while preserving dough or batter performance and consumer-relevant attributes. In general, the literature indicates that effective protein enrichment requires an integrated approach that combines amino acid complementation, digestibility enhancement, reduction of antinutritional constraints, technological compatibility, and sensory feasibility. This review highlights the need to move beyond protein quantity as the primary benchmark and toward multidimensional quality frameworks for designing nutritionally improved, functional, and acceptable farinaceous foods.

title: The Estimated Health System Cost Impacts of Interventions to Reduce Alcohol Harm in New Zealand: A Modelling Study.
authorString: Mizdrak A, Davies A, Cobiac L, Chambers T.
abstractText:
Introduction

Alcohol is responsible for substantial health loss and economic costs. This study aimed to estimate the health gains and health system costs of reducing alcohol consumption in Aotearoa New Zealand (A-NZ).

Methods

This study used the New Zealand Alcohol Intervention Model (NZ-AIM) to estimate the impacts of: (i) a 30% reduction in alcohol consumption from a comprehensive intervention package; and (ii) the elimination of alcohol use. NZ-AIM uses an open cohort approach that replicates the 2018 population by ethnicity (Māori/non-Māori), age and sex.

Results

Both elimination of alcohol consumption and a comprehensive intervention package result in large health gains for our open cohort over the next 60 years: 876,000HALYs (95% UI 432,000 to 1,233,000) and 512,000 HALYs (95% UI 358,000 to 637,000), respectively. With no discounting, the health system cost savings over 60 years are substantial: 2018NZ$3694million (95% UI -$1059m to $8682m) for elimination and $13million (95% UI -$1345m to $1606m) for the intervention package. In the first decade, the intervention package accrues NZ$552m (95% UI 362m to 737m) savings to the health system. Health system cost savings are sensitive to the discount rate and to whether costs associated with increased longevity are included.

Discussion and conclusions

The potential health gains and health system cost savings from the elimination or a reduction of alcohol consumption in Aotearoa New Zealand are large. The health system cost savings are substantial in the first few decades and then increase due to increased longevity. The findings provide additional evidence to support implementation of alcohol interventions aligning with the World Health Organization's SAFER framework.

title: Do Adverse Intrauterine Environments Affect Body Mass Index in Infants and Preschool Children?
authorString: Koglin G, da Silva CH, Bandeira DR, Valentini NC, Goldani MZ, Bernardi JR.

journal.title: American journal of human biology : the official journal of the Human Biology Council

abstractText:
Introduction

Exposure to adverse intrauterine environments resulting from different maternal clinical conditions may alter childhood growth patterns. This study investigated the influence of such environments on body mass index-for-age (BMI-for-age) trajectories from birth to preschool age.

Methods

A total of 342 mother-child dyads recruited from three hospitals in southern Brazil were allocated into five groups: diabetes mellitus (DM), systemic arterial hypertension (SAH), maternal smoking, small for gestational age (SGA, used here as a proxy for impaired fetal growth), and a control group. Children were assessed at seven time points from birth to preschool age using anthropometric measurements to calculate BMI-for-age z-scores.

Results

Generalized estimating equations (GEE) identified a significant interaction between group and time (p < 0.001). Among girls, at birth, the DM group presented higher BMI-for-age z-scores than the smoking group and reached elevated BMI-for-age z-scores at preschool age, differing from the control group. At 6 months of age, girls in the SGA group showed a marked increase in BMI-for-age. Among boys, the SGA group reached higher BMI-for-age values at preschool age than the DM and control groups. Differences were observed across time, group, and sex in the SGA and control groups (p < 0.001).

Conclusion

These findings suggest that adverse intrauterine environments may influence BMI-for-age trajectories during early life, with greater variability and evidence of catch-up growth among children exposed to maternal DM and SGA. Results should be interpreted cautiously due to unequal subgroup sizes and substantial loss to follow-up at preschool age.

title: The novel role of T2R14 antagonism, by LW129, on VEGF-induced lung endothelial neovascularisation processes in vitro.
authorString: Spurrier-Best L, Harrington EO, Chichger H.
abstractText: Pulmonary vascular remodelling, driven by dysregulated angiogenesis, is a hallmark of several cardiopulmonary diseases, yet the molecular pathways regulating endothelial responses remain incompletely understood. Bitter taste receptors (T2Rs), traditionally recognised as chemosensory receptors, have emerged as important modulators of vascular function. However, the contribution of T2Rs to pulmonary angiogenesis remains unexplored. Here, we investigated the role of T2R14 in vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-mediated angiogenic responses in human pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells (HPMECs).
