Using the selective T2R14 antagonist LW129, we examined the effects of T2R14 inhibition on key endothelial angiogenic processes, including VEGF-induced proliferation, migration and capillary-like tube formation in vitro. Pharmacological antagonism of T2R14 significantly attenuated VEGF-driven endothelial proliferative, migratory and morphogenic responses, revealing a novel contribution of T2R14 signalling to pulmonary microvascular angiogenesis. Proteome Profiler analysis identified a range of molecular regulators of angiogenic processes which were dysregulated by LW129 and VEGF exposure, suggesting a potential role for CXCL16, endoglin, FGF-7, and VEGF-C. These findings identify T2R14 as a novel regulator of VEGF-dependent endothelial activation and suggest that targeting T2R14 signalling may represent a therapeutic strategy to limit pathological pulmonary vascular remodelling associated with aberrant angiogenesis.

title: Toward a digital urinary biopsy for early risk stratification in diabetic kidney disease: Anchoring shed cells, vesicles, and cell-free DNA to spatial kidney cell states.
authorString: Wu J, Sheng P, Lu Y, Chen K.
abstractText:
Background

Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is the leading cause of end-stage kidney disease worldwide. However, albuminuria and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), which define and stage DKD, report established injury and do not resolve the cellular heterogeneity underlying variable progression. Urine, the only biofluid to traverse every nephron segment, carries shed cells, extracellular vesicles (EVs) and cell-free DNA (cfDNA), each retaining information about its cell of origin.

Main body

This review develops the concept of a digital urinary biopsy, in which the three compartments are read together against spatial single-cell kidney atlases to infer non-invasively which cell states are active and whether niche-associated programs are engaged, an approach we term atlas-anchored molecular profiling. For each compartment, we tabulate study population, sample size, processing, assay, performance and validation status. Because shed-cell RNA, selectively sorted vesicle cargo and cfDNA methylation differ in origin, measurement scale and bias, each requires its own reference matrix, sampling function and background terms. All three carry renal information in feasibility studies, yet none is a validated clinical assay in DKD. Moreover, a cfDNA methylation reference at the required resolution is lacking, and no named computational method has been tested on urine.

Conclusion

We therefore present the framework as a structured research hypothesis and define the required validation, from analytical and clinical validity to prospective demonstration of utility, with non-albuminuric DKD, which albuminuria-based screening misses, as the index use case. It offers a testable route to cell-resolved, non-invasive staging of DKD rather than a demonstrated capability.

title: Sedative Potential of L (+)-Tartaric Acid: Behavioral Evidence With In Silico Insights Into Possible GABAergic Interaction.
authorString: Bithi SA, Chakrabarty A, Akter K, Saha CK, Alshahrani MY, Hossain MA, Mia E, Yana NT, Ajmee A, Mandal P, Al Hasan MS, Islam MT.
abstractText:
Purpose

Insomnia is a prevalent neurological disorder often caused by stress, anxiety, and imbalances in the GABAergic system. Although benzodiazepines like diazepam (DZP) are commonly prescribed, their long-term use is associated with adverse effects, including dependence and impaired coordination. Therefore, there is growing interest in natural alternatives with safer pharmacological profiles.

Method

This study aimed to investigate the sedative-like potential of L (+)-tartaric acid (LTA), a naturally occurring organic acid, through both in vivo and in silico approaches targeting the γ-aminobutyric acid A (GABAA) receptor. Sedative-like activity was evaluated in Swiss albino mice using thiopental sodium-induced sleeping time, open-field, and rotarod tests.

Findings

LTA significantly reduced sleep latency and prolonged sleep duration in a dose-dependent manner, with the higher dose (240 mg/kg) producing a more pronounced effect. Co-administration of LTA with DZP further enhanced thiopental-induced hypnosis. In the open-field test, LTA reduced locomotor and exploratory activities, as evidenced by decreases in square crossings, rearing, and grooming behaviors. Rotarod assessment demonstrated a dose-dependent reduction in motor coordination and neuromuscular performance, although the impairment remained less pronounced than that produced by DZP at the lower tested dose. Molecular docking revealed lower binding affinity than DZP but demonstrated multiple hydrogen-bond (HB) interactions with key amino acid (AA) residues of the GABAA receptor, suggesting a potentially stable receptor interaction.

Conclusion

Collectively, the behavioral and computational findings indicate that LTA possesses sedative-like properties and may modulate GABAergic neurotransmission. Further mechanistic, pharmacokinetic, and electrophysiological studies are required to clarify its precise mode of action and therapeutic potential.

title: Development and Validation of an Early Postoperative Risk Stratification Model for Hydrocephalus Following Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
authorString: Li F, Fu K, Zhou S, Gong Z, Du C, Zhao Y, Yang W, Zhang C, Zhou W, Li W.
abstractText:
Background

Hydrocephalus is a common complication after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). This study aimed to identify perioperative risk factors and develop an early postoperative risk stratification model to support postoperative monitoring rather than purely preoperative prediction.

Methods

Employing a retrospective case-control design, clinical data from 331 patients with aSAH treated at the First Affiliated Hospital of Henan Medical University between August 1, 2018, and December 31, 2024, were collected and analyzed. The primary endpoint was postoperative hydrocephalus occurring within 3 weeks after aneurysm treatment, diagnosed according to combined radiological and clinical criteria. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression method was employed to screen risk factors. Multiple machine-learning models were compared, and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis was used for individualized model interpretation.

Results

The admission Glasgow Coma Scale score, intraoperative external ventricular drainage/lateral ventricular drainage, and intraventricular hemorrhage were identified as key variables associated with postoperative hydrocephalus. The logistic regression model emerged as the optimal model; locked test set area under the curve (95% CI): 0.891 (0.739-1.000); accuracy: 0.720 (0.688-0.775); sensitivity: 0.899 (0.823-0.987); specificity: 0.683 (0.635-0.740).

Conclusion

The logistic regression model with SHAP-based interpretation may support early postoperative risk stratification for hydrocephalus after aSAH. Given its modest positive predictive value, the model should be used to triage patients for intensified monitoring and timely reassessment.

title: Ursodeoxycholic Acid Confers Neuroprotection in Rats With Acute Cervical SCI and Attenuates NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD Pyroptotic Signaling.
authorString: Song H, Hu X, Liu D, Wang L, Zhu L, Wang W, Hu R, Zhong J, Liu J, Pang R, Zhang A.

journal.title: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

abstractText: Spinal cord injury (SCI) leads to significant and enduring functional limitations for patients. Secondary injury is a pivotal determinant of functional recovery after SCI, with pyroptosis driven by the NLRP3 inflammasome and its downstream inflammatory cascade representing a crucial contributor to this process. Ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA), an endogenous secondary bile acid, displays neuroprotective activity through antioxidant and anti-inflammatory actions and may suppress pyroptosis. This study aimed to explore the neuroprotective effects of UDCA against SCI and its underlying mechanisms. BV2 microglia were treated with LPS and UDCA, either individually or concurrently. Cell viability and NLRP3 inflammasome protein expression were evaluated by CCK-8 assay and immunofluorescence, respectively. Additionally, following establishment of a rat model of C5 cervical SCI, UDCA was administered by oral gavage for 7 days. Functional recovery, histopathological damage, key protein expression in the NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD pyroptosis pathway, and downstream inflammation were analyzed using various techniques, including behavioral evaluation (Cylinder Rearing test), HE staining, Western blot, immunofluorescence, and ELISA. Results showed that appropriate concentrations of UDCA improved BV2 cell viability and inhibited LPS-stimulated NLRP3 upregulation. Oral gavage of UDCA was associated with better forelimb motor function and attenuated spinal histopathological injury in rats with acute C5 cervical SCI. Furthermore, this treatment correlated with altered abundance of key components within the SCI‑activated NLRP3/Caspase‑1/GSDMD pathway, lower Iba‑1 expression, and diminished serum concentrations of IL‑18, IL‑1β, and TNF‑α, suggestive of attenuated neural pyroptosis and dampening of excessive postinjury inflammation. Collectively, UDCA mitigates secondary injury and improves forelimb function in an acute C5 cervical SCI model, alongside attenuation of NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis and subsequent inflammation. Targeting pyroptosis, UDCA holds promise as a novel therapeutic candidate for SCI.

title: The effect of biphasic cuirass ventilation on peripheral lymphatic function in young adults.
authorString: Nilsson CN, Thorup L, Kelly B, Schmidt JF, Seltz M, Hjortdal V.
abstractText: Positive pressure ventilation increases the intrathoracic pressure and the central venous pressure, impeding venous return to the heart. Likewise, both central and peripheral lymphatic function is haltered during positive pressure ventilation, presenting as a possible explanation for fluid retention and edema in post-operative and intensive care unit patients. We aimed to examine the effects of biphasic cuirass ventilation on the peripheral lymphatic system. Peripheral lymphatic function was examined in twenty healthy, young adults during spontaneous breathing and during biphasic cuirass ventilation. The peripheral lymphatic function was assessed with near-infrared fluorescence imaging, and the microvascular circulation was assessed with strain gauge plethysmography. Mean peripheral lymphatic contraction frequency (mean ± SD) was 1.46 ± 0.73/min at baseline and 1.43 ± 0.76/min during biphasic cuirass ventilation. There was no significant difference (mean difference = 0.03, 95% CI: -0.23-0.29, p = 0.81, n = 19). Capillary filtration rates did not differ between baseline and biphasic cuirass ventilation across all pressure levels (F(1,18) = 1.13, p = 0.30). Likewise, there were no significant differences in isovolumetric pressures (mean difference = -2.61, 95% CI: -8.92-3.71, p = 0.39, n = 15), or capillary filtration coefficients (mean difference = 1.21 × 10<sup>-4</sup>, 95% CI: -4,87 × 10<sup>-4</sup> - 7.29 × 10<sup>-4</sup>, p = 0.68, n = 19). We observed no changes in peripheral lymphatic activity in awake, healthy, young adults during BCV.

title: Endothelial ADRB3 protects the heart from myocardial infarction by suppressing endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition.
authorString: Zhang Z, Chen X, Chen X, Li J, Zhai Y, Guzik T, Zheng Y, Gao P, Lin J.
abstractText: β3 adrenergic receptor (ADRB3) has recently emerged as an important regulator of cardiovascular homeostasis. However, the role of endothelial ADRB3 in cardiac repair after myocardial infarction (MI) remains unclear. As endothelial dysfunction critically drives post-MI remodeling, we hypothesized that ADRB3 preserves endothelial integrity and protects the heart from ischemic injury. Endothelial cell-specific ADRB3 knockout mice and adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (AAV9)-mediated endothelial ADRB3 overexpression mice were subjected to MI. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed to characterize cellular heterogeneity and endothelial phenotypic changes. scRNA-seq revealed enhanced EndoMT and activated TGFβ signaling in ADRB3-deficient hearts, accompanied by accelerated fibrotic remodeling and exacerbated ischemic injury. In contrast, endothelial ADRB3 overexpression suppressed EndoMT, reduced fibrosis, and improved cardiac function following MI. In vitro, ADRB3 knockdown induced EndoMT and endothelial dysfunction, whereas ADRB3 overexpression attenuated hypoxia-induced mesenchymal activation. Mechanistically, proximity ligation assay, co-immunoprecipitation, and mass spectrometry identified TGFβ receptor 2 (TGFβR2) as an endogenous binding partner of ADRB3. ADRB3 interaction with TGFβR2 prevented SMAD2 recruitment to TGFβR1 and inhibited downstream SMAD2 phosphorylation. Moreover, endothelial-specific TGFβR2 knockdown using AAV9 mitigated cardiac injury in ADRB3-deficient mice following MI. These findings demonstrate that endothelial ADRB3 protects against ischemic heart injury by limiting TGFβR2-SMAD2-dependent EndoMT, highlighting its role as a critical endothelial regulator and a potential therapeutic target for myocardial repair.

title: LncAAT-mediated decline in energy metabolism is essential for vascular endothelial senescence in advancing age.
authorString: Qiu Y, Liu Z, He J, Chen L, Huang H, Zhang J, Liu X, Liu Z, Zhou Z, Wang Z, Zhu Q, Qiu Y, Chen X, Tang J, Xia W, Qian X, Cao F, Tao J.
abstractText: Vascular endothelial senescence is a critical contributor to the development of cardiovascular disease and energy production deficiency plays a pivotal role in cellular senescence. Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) are increasingly recognized as key regulators in biological aging processes. However, their involvement in energy metabolism and its relationship with endothelial senescence remains poorly understood. LncRNA microarray analysis was performed to profile lncRNAs using young and aged human aortas, and we identified a novel lncRNA, Aging Associated Transcript (lncAAT), which was predominantly localized in the nucleus of vascular endothelial cells and exhibited age-dependent increase. Endothelial-specific knockout of lncAAT in mice delayed vascular aging, enhanced endothelial-mediated vasodilation, and improved angiogenesis in a hindlimb-ischemia model. RNA-sequencing showed that lncAAT knockdown upregulated genes associated with energy metabolism including glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation. LncAAT overexpression mediated fall in energy production led to endothelial senescence in vivo and in vitro. Mechanistically, lncRNA pulldown in combination with liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry analysis found that AAT interacted with pyruvate kinase isozyme type M2 (PKM2) located at the nucleus. The lncAAT-PKM2 complex competitively blocked the interaction between PKM2 and STAT3, impairing energy metabolism gene transcription and ultimately leading to endothelial senescence. Our current findings firstly reveal the essential role of lncAAT in promoting vascular endothelial senescence through defective energy metabolism. Inhibition of lncAAT expression presents a promising therapeutic strategy for alleviating vascular aging and reducing the burden of cardiovascular diseases in humans.

title: Dietary patterns and cardiovascular risk in adult survivors of childhood cancer: findings from the SCCSS-Nutrition Study.
authorString: Li R, Revuelta Iniesta R, Barker AR, Chatelan A, Leuenberger LM, Shoman Y, Spycher BD, Belle FN.

journal.title: Journal of cancer survivorship : research and practice

abstractText: To identify dietary patterns among adult childhood cancer survivors (CCSs), examine their determinants, and assess whether they differ according to cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk profiles. CCSs from the Swiss Childhood Cancer Survivor Study diagnosed before age 21 years (1976-2005), surviving ≥ 5 years and aged ≥ 18 years in 2017, completed a food frequency questionnaire (SCCSS-Nutrition). Factor and hierarchical cluster analyses of 52 food groups identified dietary patterns. We categorised CCSs as having CVD, CVD risk factors (obesity, hypertension, diabetes, high cholesterol), or being CVD risk-free. Multinomial logistic regression assessed associations between dietary patterns and CVD risk profiles. Among 802 CCSs (median age: 35 years; IQR: 29-41; 50% male), we identified five dietary patterns: Mediterranean-inspired diet (22%), Western indulgence diet (38%), Western sweet & fatty diet (26%), restrained indulgence diet (9%), plant-based & alcohol-rich diet (6%). Male sex, younger age, German-speaking region, smoking, and living with others were associated with Western indulgence, Western sweet & fatty, and restrained indulgence diets. Higher Swiss socioeconomic position (Swiss-SEP) and education, and not having children, were associated with the plant-based & alcohol-rich diet, higher Swiss-SEP was also associated with the Western indulgence diet. No associations were observed between dietary patterns and CVD risk profiles. Dietary patterns among adult CCSs were socially patterned and differed according to sociodemographic and lifestyle characteristics, but were not associated with CVD risk profiles. Dietary counselling and broader lifestyle support should be considered as part of long-term survivorship care for CCSs.

title: Regional Divergence in Infective Endocarditis Prophylaxis: A Multi-center Analysis of Clinical Practice vs. International Guidelines from the Pan Arab Congenital Heart Disease Association (PACHDA).
authorString: Al Akhfash A, Dahdah N, El-Segaier M.
abstractText: Current infective endocarditis (IE) prophylaxis guidelines recommend a restrictive approach, excluding low-risk lesions such as patent ductus arteriosus, isolated ventricular septal defect, and valvular stenosis. In many countries, delayed cardiac defect repair and a high prevalence of dental disease may create a distinct risk profile that warrants further investigation. The Pan Arab Congenital Heart Disease Association (PACHDA) conducted a multinational cross-sectional online survey targeting cardiovascular specialists to evaluate perceptions of IE prophylaxis guidelines, adherence patterns, and the influence of oral health and socioeconomic factors on clinical decision-making. Statistical analyses included Spearman rank correlation, Chi-square testing, Fisher's exact test, and qualitative thematic synthesis. The questionnaire was completed by 72 specialists, of whom only 25% reported strict adherence to restrictive international guidelines for isolated simple congenital heart defects. Respondents who identified socioeconomic barriers (e.g., poverty and limited access to dental care) as a primary concern were more likely to deviate from restrictive guideline recommendations than their peers (83.7% vs. 41.4%; p = 0.001). Clinicians with higher IE case exposure (> 5 IE cases in the preceding 5 years) also demonstrated significantly greater rates of guideline deviation (p = 0.047). Fewer than 50% of respondents considered current AHA/ESC guidelines "fit for purpose" in their local practice. Many cardiovascular specialists across the Arab/MENA region perceive current international IE prophylaxis recommendations as insufficiently reflective of local clinical and socioeconomic realities. However, these findings represent clinician perceptions and practice patterns rather than patient-level outcomes and should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating. The observed divergence between guideline recommendations and clinical practice highlights the need for regional epidemiological and outcome-based studies to determine whether local factors influence IE risk and whether adaptation of current prophylaxis strategies is warranted.

title: Empagliflozin's role in cardiometabolic disease treatment: an Egyptian expert's view.
authorString: Assaad-Khalil SH, Elmessallamy F, Elhadidy KE, El Hefnawy MH, Halawa MR, Zeitoun M, Hussein S, Elebrashy I.
abstractText:
Background

Given the expanding therapeutic indications of empagliflozin (EMPA) beyond glycemic control and the growing burden of cardiometabolic diseases, this review evaluated its efficacy, safety, and cost-effectiveness in the Egyptian population within the global context.

Methods

A comprehensive literature review of PubMed and Google Scholar identified clinical trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and clinical guidelines published in English up to July 2025. We included studies reporting EMPA's pharmacological profile, mechanisms of action, and clinical outcomes on diabetes mellitus, cardiometabolic diseases, renal and hepatic functions, safety during Ramadan fasting, and cost-effectiveness.

Results

EMPA, as monotherapy or combination therapy, improves glycemic control in type 2 diabetes through Sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 (SGLT-2) inhibition. For type 1 diabetes mellitus, despite improving glycemic control as an adjunct therapy, it is not recommended due to the increased risk of diabetic ketoacidosis. EMPA reduces major cardiovascular events, heart failure hospitalization, and chronic kidney disease progression, with modest weight loss and blood pressure reduction, in patients with or without diabetes. Emerging evidence suggests benefits in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), although it is not approved for this indication. EMPA demonstrates a favorable safety profile and low hypoglycemia risk during Ramadan fasting. It enhances patients' quality of life and is considered cost-effective.

Conclusions

EMPA extends beyond glucose-lowering by reducing cardiorenal morbidity and mortality in patients with or without diabetes. It shows a favorable safety profile, even during Ramadan fasting, supporting its suitability for the large Muslim population. Further research should evaluate its role in MASLD and assess cost-effectiveness in Egypt.

title: Association of Long-acting Bronchodilator Use with Cardiovascular Adverse Events in Patients with Asthma: A Population-based Cohort Study.
authorString: Bai L, Xiao N, Zhao Q, Wang Z, Xu Y, Zhou X.

journal.title: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice

abstractText: A recent meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials found that long-acting bronchodilator use was associated with cardiovascular adverse events (AEs) leading to treatment discontinuation in asthma, although the certainty of evidence was low. To evaluate the cardiovascular safety of long-acting bronchodilators in a real-world asthma population. This population-based cohort study used UK Biobank data from patients with asthma (2006-2010). Exposure was categorized into three mutually exclusive groups: LABA alone, LAMA alone, or combined LABA/LAMA therapy. The primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular AEs, including coronary heart disease, arrhythmia, hypertension, heart failure, and cerebrovascular disease. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Pre-specified subgroup analyses and interaction tests were performed. A total of 14,677 patients were included (median follow-up 14.68 years). Long-acting bronchodilator use was associated with an increased risk of total cardiovascular AEs (HR: 1.08, 95% CI: 1.02-1.15). This was primarily driven by arrhythmia (HR: 1.23, 95% CI: 1.06-1.42), heart failure (HR: 1.30, 95% CI: 1.02-1.65), and cerebrovascular disease (HR: 1.35, 95% CI: 1.02-1.79). When stratified by regimen, the association was confined to the LABA group (HR: 1.07, 95% CI: 1.001-1.13) and the combined group (HR: 1.32, 95% CI: 1.09-1.59). The association was more pronounced in patients using short-acting bronchodilators (HR: 1.15, 95% CI: 1.07-1.23; interaction P = 0.004). The observed positive associations are more plausibly attributable to confounding rather than to a causal drug effect. Future research should prioritize new-user designs to clarify whether these signals are drug-specific or confounded by disease severity.

title: Short and long-term outcomes after gestational diabetes diagnosis using different glycemic criteria: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Liu Q, Mayer DFR, Harding JE, Gamble GD, Dawes L, Crowther CA, Lin L.

journal.title: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

abstractText: Lower gestational diabetes (GDM) diagnostic criteria on an oral glucose tolerance test are widely recommended, but their impacts on maternal, neonatal, long-term and economic outcomes remain uncertain. To compare outcomes after GDM diagnosis using lower versus higher diagnostic strategies. We searched for randomized controlled trials (RCT) and prospective cohort studies comparing outcomes following assessment for GDM and treatment if indicated, using lower versus higher glycemic diagnostic criteria or thresholds in four databases and four trial registries (PROSPERO registration CRD420251183179) to 27th July 2026. Two reviewers independently assessed risk of bias, conducted random-effects meta-analyses and evaluated GRADE certainty. Seventeen studies were included, with nine RCTs and one cohort study contributing to the meta-analysis (81,528 women). Lower diagnostic criteria or thresholds, compared with higher diagnostic criteria or thresholds, doubled GDM diagnosis and pharmacotherapy use, increased neonatal hypoglycemia (RCTs: 18 more per 1,000; 95% CI 11 to 25 more) and maternal-neonatal separation (RCTs: 6 more per 1,000; 95% CI 1 to 12 more), but had little to no effect on other short-term outcomes. Longer-term evidence was limited to follow-up of one RCT reporting reduced maternal hypertension and child neurodevelopmental impairment but increased subsequent GDM at five-year follow-up with use of lower criteria or thresholds. Findings on GDM-related healthcare costs were inconsistent, with no long-term economic data. Lower diagnostic criteria increased the diagnosis of GDM and some aspects of healthcare utilization, without improving short-term outcomes. Limited evidence suggested possible longer-term benefits, warranting further long-term follow-up from high-quality RCTs.

title: Preoperative Imaging-Derived Factors Associated With Spinal Cord Ischemia After Fenestrated and Branched Endovascular Aortic Repair-A Scoping Review.
authorString: Kappe KO, To K, Cherchi M, Yeung KK, Jongkind V.

journal.title: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists

abstractText:
Background

Spinal cord ischemia (SCI) after fenestrated and branched endovascular aortic repair (F/B-EVAR) is a devastating complication with a non-negligible incidence, and better risk prediction is necessary. Preoperative imaging allows assessment of anatomical and morphological characteristics that may predispose to SCI. This scoping review aimed to systematically search the literature and provide an overview of the current evidence on the association of preoperative imaging-derived factors with SCI after F/B-EVAR.

Methods

This scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines. A systematic literature search of PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane, and Web of Science was performed from database inception to October 21, 2025, to identify studies that reported on the association of preoperative imaging-derived factors with SCI following F/B-EVAR. Only studies published in English were included. Studies were screened by 2 reviewers, and data were charted using a standardized data-extracting form. Identified factors were categorized as aortic-related, aortic side-branch-related, thrombus-related, and miscellaneous factors.

Results

A total of 2231 studies were identified, and 45 were included in this scoping review. Included studies consisted of observational cohort studies and nonrandomized investigational device exemption studies, with all studies using univariable and multivariable analyses. A total of 18 imaging-derived factors were identified and categorized into aortic-related (33 studies), aortic side-branch-related (17 studies), thrombus-related (5 studies), and miscellaneous (psoas muscle parameters, median arcuate ligament [MAL]) (6 studies). Aneurysm extent, maximum aortic diameter, and rupture were the most frequently reported investigated factors. Most (n = 39, 87%) studies were performed in cohorts of less than 400 patients. Definitions of similar investigated factors varied, and associations found were variable across studies. Only a limited number of included studies performed a multivariable analysis.

Conclusion

This scoping review provides a categorized overview of preoperative imaging-derived factors and their associations with SCI after F/B-EVAR. Identified factors showed heterogeneous associations and inconsistent definitions across studies limited comparability. Large prospective cohort studies, including standardized definitions of parameters, are needed to investigate the influence of preoperative imaging-derived factors on the risk of SCI.Clinical ImpactSpinal cord ischemia (SCI) after fenestrated and branched endovascular aortic repair remains a significant complication despite continual advancements in preventive strategies and identification of clinical risk factors. Preoperative imaging allows assessment of anatomical and morphological characteristics that may predispose to SCI. This scoping review provides a categorized overview of preoperative imaging-derived factors and the evidence on their association with SCI. Identified factors had varying definitions and showed heterogeneous associations with SCI. Recommendations for future research are outlined to further optimize SCI risk prediction using preoperative imaging-derived factors.

title: Efficacy and safety of oral orforglipron in Japanese participants with obesity disease (ATTAIN-J): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 trial.
authorString: Yokote K, Yamauchi T, Shingaki T, Chin R, Oura T, Nagai Y, Shimomura I, Kadowaki T.
abstractText: Orforglipron, a small-molecule, non-peptide, oral GLP-1 receptor agonist, has shown bodyweight reduction and cardiometabolic benefits in adults with obesity across phase 3 trials globally. We aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of orforglipron versus placebo for treating obesity disease in Japanese adults. ATTAIN-J was a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 trial conducted across 16 medical research centres and hospitals in Japan and included adults aged 18 years or older with a BMI between 27 kg/m2 and less than 35 kg/m2 and two or more obesity-related health disorders, or a BMI of 35 kg/m2 or higher and one or more obesity-related health disorder, with one or more of the obesity-related health disorders being hypertension, dyslipidaemia, or type 2 diabetes (targeted at about 25% of participants), consistent with Japanese indications for tirzepatide and semaglutide for obesity disease; and at least one unsuccessful dietary attempt to lose weight. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) via a computer-generated sequence to once-daily oral orforglipron (6 mg, 12 mg, or 36 mg) or placebo. Co-primary endpoints were mean percentage change in bodyweight and percentage of participants with at least 5% bodyweight reduction from baseline to week 72. Efficacy endpoints were primarily evaluated by the treatment regimen estimand in all randomly assigned participants. Safety was assessed in participants who received at least one dose of study treatment. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05931380 (completed). Between July 31, 2023, and June 19, 2025, 291 participants were screened, of whom 238 (144 [61%] males and 94 [39%] females; mean age 54·1 years [SD 11·2]) were randomly assigned to receive orforglipron 6 mg (n=61), 12 mg (n=57), or 36 mg (n=60), or placebo (n=60); 214 (90%) participants completed the study. At week 72, mean percentage change in bodyweight was -5·9% (95% CI -7·6 to -4·2) with orforglipron 6 mg, -8·7% (-10·9 to -6·5) with 12 mg, and -7·9% (-10·0 to -5·8) with 36 mg, compared with -0·6% (-2·1 to 0·8) with placebo (all p<0·0001 vs placebo). At week 72, a bodyweight reduction of at least 5% was seen in 15·2% (SE 4·8; nine of 60) of participants in the placebo group compared with 45·6% (6·1; 28 of 61; p=0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 6 mg group, 60·8% (6·4; 35 of 57; p<0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 12 mg group, and 58·8% (6·5; 35 of 60; p<0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 36 mg group. Adverse events with orforglipron were mostly mild-to-moderate gastrointestinal symptoms. Across all orforglipron groups, treatment-emergent adverse events that most frequently led to study treatment discontinuation were nausea (one [2%] of 61 in the 6 mg group, one [2%] of 57 in the 12 mg group, and five [8%] of 60 in the 36 mg group vs none with placebo) and vomiting (none in the 6 mg group, two [4%] in the 12 mg group, and one [2%] in the 36 mg group vs none in the placebo group). In Japanese adults with obesity disease, once-daily orforglipron resulted in statistically superior reductions in bodyweight versus placebo, with a safety profile consistent with that of other GLP-1 receptor agonists. Eli Lilly and Company. For the Japanese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

title: Heterogeneity of Treatment Effect of ABC Pathway-Based Care in Older Atrial Fibrillation: Insights from the mAFA-II and MIRACLE-AF Trials Using a Causal Machine Learning Approach.
authorString: Chen Y, Yu Q, Gue Y, Meng Y, Zheng Y, Li M, Guo Y, Chen M, Lip GYH.
abstractText:
Background

Integrated care based on the Atrial fibrillation Better Care (ABC) pathway improves outcomes in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF), but whether treatment effects differ across older patients remains unclear.

Objectives

To evaluate heterogeneity of treatment effect (HTE) of ABC pathway-based care and assess its transportability across healthcare settings using causal machine learning (ML).

Methods

Individual participant data from the cluster-randomised mAFA-II and MIRACLE-AF trials were analysed, including 3,209 patients aged ≥65 years. Three causal ML models were developed in mAFA-II and externally validated in MIRACLE-AF. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, ischaemic stroke, intracranial haemorrhage, heart failure, acute coronary syndrome, or major bleeding.

Results

The uplift random forest demonstrated the best performance and identified meaningful HTE. In the mAFA-II testing cohort, ABC pathway-based care was associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome in patients predicted to benefit, whereas no benefit and possible harm were observed in those predicted to derive harm (P-interaction=0.002). In external validation, benefit was preserved in the predicted benefit group but not in the predicted harm group, although treatment discrimination was attenuated. Patients predicted to derive limited benefit had greater clinical complexity, including higher comorbidity burden and CHA2DS2-VASc scores. Sex, heart failure, and hypertension were the strongest predictors of treatment effect.

Conclusions

ABC pathway-based integrated care demonstrates clinically meaningful treatment heterogeneity among older patients with AF. These findings support more personalised implementation of integrated care and highlight the potential of causal ML to guide precision management in AF.

Clinical trial registration

MAFA-II trial (ChiCTR-OOC-17014138 || http://www.chictr.org.cn/, registered on 26 December 2017), MIRACLE-AF trial (NCT04622514 || https://clinicaltrials.gov/, registered on 10 November 2020).

title: Patient-Reported Outcomes with High-Volume Hemodiafiltration Versus High-Flux Hemodialysis Across Clinical Subgroups: Results from the CONVINCE Trial.
authorString: Cromm K, Fischer F, Pellegrino G, Vernooij RWM, Riazy L, Barth C, Blankestijn PJ, Bots ML, Canaud B, Davenport A, Hegbrant J, Woodward M, Rose M, Strippoli GFM.

journal.title: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN

abstractText: High-volume hemodiafiltration (HDF) improves survival and attenuates decline in selected patient-reported outcome (PRO) domains versus high-flux hemodialysis (HD). Whether benefits differ across clinically relevant subgroups remains uncertain. We conducted a prespecified subgroup analysis of the multicenter CONVINCE randomized controlled trial comparing high-volume post-dilution HDF (≥23 L/session) with high-flux HD in adults receiving maintenance dialysis. Eight PROMIS domains were assessed quarterly over a median follow-up of 30 months. Linear mixed-effects models evaluated longitudinal PRO changes and treatment-by-subgroup interactions by prespecified baseline characteristics: age, sex, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, dialysis vintage, vascular access type, and residual urine volume. Joint-model sensitivity analyses of all eight longitudinal PROMIS trajectories and time to death assessed informative dropout due to death. Of 1360 randomized participants, 1211 with baseline and follow-up PRO assessments were included. PRO treatment effects were broadly consistent across prespecified clinical subgroups, without evidence of clinically meaningful heterogeneity. Models adjusted for baseline sociodemographic and clinical characteristics showed nominal treatment-by-subgroup interactions for dialysis vintage and physical function (P = 0.03), age and pain interference (P = 0.02), and dialysis vintage and sleep disturbance (P = 0.04). Joint-model sensitivity analyses accounting for informative dropout due to mortality reproduced the first two interactions and identified nominal interactions for vascular access type and sleep disturbance (P = 0.03) and cardiovascular disease status and cognitive function (P = 0.05). Interactions were modest in magnitude, exploratory, unadjusted for multiple comparisons, and not consistently observed across related PROMIS domains. This prespecified exploratory subgroup analysis found no convincing evidence of clinically meaningful treatment-effect heterogeneity across baseline characteristics examined. Nominal interactions were unadjusted for multiple comparisons and should be regarded as hypothesis-generating. Findings should not guide selection or exclusion of patients for high-volume HDF based on patient-reported outcomes.

title: Assessment of Ototoxicity in Patients With Heart Failure Receiving High-Dose IV Loop Diuretics.
authorString: Cox ZL, Rao VS, Ivey-Miranda JB, Myers S, Manning K, Imhoff B, Jenkins CA, Shotwell MS, Miller KF, Storrow AB, Watson P, Rivera-Sanchez A, Wilson FP, Yamamoto Y, Siddiqi H, Schlendorf KH, Stevenson LW, Lindenfeld J, Rybak LP, Collins SP, Testani JM.
abstractText: Concern for ototoxicity hinders loop diuretic (LD) dosing in heart failure (HF); given the mechanism by which LDs affect the ear, high-dose LDs should produce transient, not permanent, hearing changes. To measure the association of LD dose with permanent and temporary ototoxicity. Cohort 1 received a randomized sequence of LD doses (bumetanide, 1.25-10 mg) across study visits with serial audiometry assessments. Cohort 2 received serial LD up to furosemide 500-mg doses during a HF hospitalization with audiometry at baseline and prior to discharge. Cohort 3 retrospectively characterized clinically diagnosed ototoxicity in HF hospitalizations was defined using International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) codes. Cohorts 1 and 2 were single center, while cohort 3 was multicenter. Cohort 1 studied outpatient participants with stable HF, while cohort 2 (n = 40) and cohort 3 studied hospitalized patients with acute HF. Intravenous LD. The primary outcomes were clinically diagnosed ototoxicity and hearing changes via audiometry. Cohort 1 contained 50 participants, cohort 2 contained 40 participants, and cohort 3 contained 22 656 participants. In cohort 1, mean (SD) participant age was 63.2 (10.4) years, and 21 of 50 participants (42%) were women. In cohorts 1 and 2, clinically diagnosed ototoxicity was not observed. In cohort 1, at peak diuretic concentration, worsening hearing shifts were infrequent (24 ears of 400 doses [6%]) but were more common with higher doses (odds ratio [OR], 1.99; 95% CI, 1.21-3.28 per doubling dose; P = .007). Within hours, hearing shifts largely resolved and were absent in 98% of measurements (393 ears of 400 doses). No significant association between LD dose and hearing shifts was present at any time aside from peak LD concentration. In cohort 2, hearing shifts were not different across groups divided by the median daily LD dose and were not associated with LD dose (OR, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.71-1.98 per doubling dose; P = .52). In cohort 3, 608 HF hospitalizations (2.7%) had clinically diagnosed ototoxicity. In multivariable analyses, peak dose of 160 mg furosemide equivalents or greater (OR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.52-1.31; P = .43) and 400 mg furosemide equivalents or greater (OR, 1.28; 95% CI, 0.71-2.31; P = .41) were not associated with greater clinically diagnosed ototoxicity risk relative to less than 160 mg. In this analysis of 2 small HF cohorts, short-term exposure to high-dose LD was not associated with permanent ototoxicity, although concomitant ototoxin use was excluded. Future studies are needed to understand the risk of ototoxicity with repeated LD exposure and in broader HF populations. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifiers: NCT04481919 and NCT05323487.

title: Automated Versus Conventional Annular Suturing in Totally Endoscopic Aortic Valve and Ascending Aorta Replacement: A Prospective Randomized Trial
authorString: Hamiko M, Rogaczewski J, Salamate S, Bayram A, Piekarski F, Eghbalzadeh K, Silaschi M, Kruse J, Velicki L, Ibrahim ME, El-Sayed Ahmad A, Bakhtiary F.
abstractText:
Background

Totally endoscopic aortic valve replacement (AVR) combined with ascending aorta replacement (AAR) remains technically demanding, with prolonged CPB and ischemic times. Annular suturing is a principal technical limitation; automated devices aim to simplify this step and improve efficiency. This study compared early clinical outcomes between automated and conventional annular suturing in totally endoscopic AVR with concomitant AAR.

Methods

Between August 2023 and February 2026, 86 patients undergoing totally endoscopic AVR with concomitant AAR via right anterior minithoracotomy (RAMT) were randomized 1:1 to automated annular (RAM group; n=43) or conventional suturing (conventional group; n=43) in this single-center trial. Primary endpoints were technical success and procedural times; secondary endpoints included complications and 30-day mortality.

Results

Baseline characteristics were comparable, bicuspid aortic valve morphology was more frequent in the RAM group (74.4% vs. 53.5%; P = 0.043). Automated suturing was associated with shorter median procedure (120.8 vs. 144.0 minutes; P = 0.004), CPB (90.0 vs. 105.0 minutes; P = 0.005), and aortic cross-clamp times (62.0 vs. 74.0 minutes; P = 0.003), respectively. No stroke, conversion to sternotomy, paravalvular leakage, or 30-day mortality occurred in either group. Hospital stay was shorter with automated suturing (6.0 vs. 7.0 days; P = 0.037), while total treatment cost, accounting for incremental device cost, did not differ significantly (P = 0.421).

Conclusions

Automated annular suturing appears to be a safe, efficient alternative to conventional suturing in totally endoscopic AVR with AAR, associated with reduced operative and ischemic times and shorter hospital stay without compromising early outcomes.

CLINICAL PERSPECTIVE

What Is New?

In this randomized trial of totally endoscopic aortic valve replacement with ascending aorta replacement (n=86), automated annular suturing with the RAM device was associated with shorter procedure, cardiopulmonary bypass, and aortic cross-clamp times and a shorter hospital stay (6 vs 7 days) than conventional suturing. Earlier evidence for automated annular suturing came mainly from observational series in isolated valve replacement, and this trial extends the observation to combined aortic valve and ascending aorta surgery. No stroke, conversion to sternotomy, paravalvular leakage, or 30-day mortality occurred in either group, and total treatment cost did not differ significantly because the incremental device cost offset the savings from the shorter hospital stay.

What Are the Clinical Implications?

Automated annular suturing may be a safe and efficient option to reduce ischemic and bypass times in technically demanding totally endoscopic aortic procedures at experienced centers. Centers considering adoption should expect cost neutrality rather than cost savings during the index hospitalization. Larger multicenter trials with longer follow-up, including centers earlier in their learning curve, are needed to confirm generalizability and valve durability.

title: N-Acetylgalactosamine-Conjugated Small Interfering RNA Targeting Hepatic Angiotensinogen in Hypertension: A Phase I Clinical Trial With Randomized Part A and Open-Label Part B.
authorString: Zhang J, Wu J, Liu Q, Kong L, Li X, Gao Q, Yin H, Li J, Shi A, Zhang L, Shen A, Liang X, Wang Y, Dong R.
abstractText: Angiotensinogen (AGT) is the precursor of angiotensin peptides and a key determinant of renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system activity. ART101 is an investigational N-acetylgalactosamine-conjugated small interfering RNA (GalNAc-siRNA) designed to durably suppress hepatic AGT synthesis. To evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of single ascending doses of the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA in healthy volunteers and to provide an initial exploratory assessment of blood pressure effects in patients with hypertension. This phase I study was conducted from January 2025 to April 2026 with 24-week follow-up. Part A was a double-blind, placebo-controlled, single ascending-dose trial; part B was an open-label, single-dose study. The study took place at Beijing Friendship Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing, China. Part A enrolled 40 healthy adults randomized 6:2 to receive the GalNAc-siRNA (25-600 mg) or placebo; 39 completed the study. Part B enrolled 8 patients with hypertension receiving the GalNAc-siRNA, 600 mg; all completed the study. A single subcutaneous injection of the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA (25, 75, 150, 300, or 600 mg) or placebo in part A; a single open-label subcutaneous injection of GalNAc-siRNA, 600 mg, in part B. The primary outcome was safety and tolerability; secondary outcomes included pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, exploratory blood pressure assessments, and renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system biomarkers. Among 40 healthy volunteers (27 [67.5%] male; mean [SD] age, 40.4 [7.8] years) and 8 patients (6 [75.0%] male; mean [SD] age, 47.3 [10.3] years) with hypertension, the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA was well tolerated. In part A, treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) occurred in 23 of 30 active-treatment participants (76.7%) vs 7 of 10 placebo recipients (70.0%); in part B, 6 of 8 patients (75.0%) had TEAEs. No serious adverse events, injection site reactions, or hyperkalemia were observed; all TEAEs were mild to moderate. Plasma exposure (maximum plasma concentration [Cmax] and area under the plasma concentration-time curve [AUC]) increased with dose over the wide dose range from 25 mg to 600 mg. Mean maximum serum AGT reductions of 93% (at 600 mg) in healthy volunteers and 90% (at 600 mg) in patients with hypertension were observed. At 24 weeks after a single 600-mg dose, the placebo-corrected 24-hour ambulatory systolic blood pressure decreased by 12.9 mm Hg in healthy participants. In this phase I study, no serious treatment-related safety signals were identified. Sustained, dose-dependent AGT reductions and exploratory blood pressure lowering were observed. These findings support further investigation of the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA as a potential long-acting therapeutic for hypertension. China Drug Clinical Registry Identifiers: CTR20250041 (part A) and CTR20253973 (part B).

title: Intensive vs More Intensive Lipid-Lowering Therapy and Plaque Regression in Statin-Naive Patients: Prespecified Analyses From the FLOWPROMOTE Randomized Clinical Trial.
authorString: Mortensen MB, Iraqi N, Sand NPR, Busk M, Jensen JM, Madsen KT, Grove EL, Dey D, Kanstrup H, Pedersen K, Mathiassen ON, Hosbond S, Bøtker HE, Narula J, Nørgaard BL.
abstractText:
Importance

Prior imaging studies (predominantly using intravascular ultrasound) have demonstrated modest plaque regression with lipid-lowering therapy in stable coronary artery disease (CAD). The effect of initiating intensive lipid-lowering therapy on coronary plaque regression across the entire coronary tree in treatment-naive patients remains uncertain.

Objective

To report the prespecified secondary imaging end points of the FLOWPROMOTE trial by comparing the effects of intensive vs more intensive lipid-lowering therapy on plaque regression in statin-naive patients with stable CAD and to assess the association between achieved low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels and plaque regression.

Design, setting, and participants

FLOWPROMOTE was a multicenter randomized clinical trial enrolling statin-naive patients with newly diagnosed stable CAD, defined by a coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA) stenosis greater than 50% and fractional flow reserve CT less than or equal to 0.80. Coronary CTA was performed at baseline and repeated at 9 and 18 months. Study data were analyzed from February 2025 to January 2026.

Interventions

Patients were randomized to intensive lipid-lowering therapy (atorvastatin 40 mg) or more intensive lipid-lowering therapy (rosuvastatin 40 mg plus ezetimibe 10 mg) for 18 months.

Main outcomes and measures

Prespecified secondary end points included changes in total plaque volume (TPV), noncalcified plaque volume (NCPV), and calcified plaque volume (CPV) across all coronary vessels at 9 and 18 months compared with baseline.

Results

A total of 104 patients (mean [SD] age, 64 [9] years; 82 male [79%]) were included in this analysis, with 52 patients in the intensive group and 52 patients in the more intensive group. LDL-C levels decreased from 119.7 to 69.5 mg/dL (-38%) with intensive therapy and from 127.4 to 42.5 mg/dL (-65%) with more intensive therapy (between-group P < .001). At 18 months, both TPV and NCPV decreased in both groups, with significantly greater regression in the more intensive-therapy group. TPV was reduced by -69.8 mm3 (-21.1%) with more intensive therapy vs -39.0 mm3 (-13.6%) with intensive therapy (between-group difference, -30.9 mm3; 95% CI, -57.2 to -4.5 mm3; P = .02), and NCPV was reduced by -82.3 mm3 (-28.2%) vs -53.5 mm3 (-20.0%), respectively (between-group difference, -28.9 mm3; 95% CI, -53.2 to -4.6 mm3; P = .02). CPV increased similarly in both groups. Regression of TPV occurred in 90% of patients receiving more intensive therapy compared with 76% receiving intensive therapy (47 of 52 [90%] vs 38 of 51 [75%]; P = .05), and regression of NCPV was observed in 98% vs 77% (51 of 52 [98%] vs 39 of 51 [77%]; P =.001). Lower achieved LDL-C levels were linearly associated with greater regression of TPV and NCPV.

Conclusions and relevance

This secondary analysis of the FLOWPROMOTE randomized clinical trial demonstrated that in statin-naive patients with CAD, more intensive lipid-lowering therapy was associated with significantly greater regression of total and noncalcified coronary plaque burden compared with intensive therapy. The extent of plaque regression was related to achieved LDL-C levels, supporting the potential for partial reversal of coronary atherosclerosis with intensive lipid reduction.

Trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04737408.

title: Context-specific effects of CCM2 on atherosclerosis
authorString: Fang S, Schnitzler GR, Vromman A, Jiang J, Maurya M, Kamanu FK, Park JJ, Cui R, Mitra R, Gabbert A, Zheng C, Widdup L, Rao JS, Pham N, Chen M, Zandavi SM, Engreitz JM, Taylor MS, Marston NA, Schmaier AA, Sabatine MS, Libby P, Ruff CT, Gupta RM.
abstractText:
Genetic variants in the Cerebral Cavernous Malformation 2 ( CCM2 ) locus are associated with coronary artery disease (CAD), but the role of CCM2 in atherosclerosis is unknown. We previously identified CCM2 through endothelial cell (EC) Perturb-seq as a regulator of transcriptional programs enriched for CAD risk genes, and predicted that reduced CCM2 function would be athero-protective. Here, we integrated human genetics, functional studies in human aortic ECs, and single cell profiling with mouse models of atherosclerosis to define the effects of reduced CCM2 signaling across disease stages. Ccm2 +/- mice developed less atherosclerosis after 12 weeks of high-fat, high-cholesterol diet. At baseline, aortic ECs from Ccm2 +/- mice exhibited reduced inflammatory transcriptional programs, and CCM2 knockout in human aortic ECs increased KLF2 expression and reduced monocyte adhesion and procoagulant activity. However, this protective phenotype was not sustained during disease progression. After 12 weeks of high-fat, high-cholesterol diet, Ccm2 +/- mice exhibited increased circulating TNFα and increased inflammatory programs in aortic ECs and T cells. Consistent with this transition, Ccm2 +/- showed increased atherosclerotic burden after 20 weeks of atherogenic diet. Human genetic analyses showed a similar context-dependent association. The lead variant in the CCM2 locus (rs2107732, a missense V53I coding variant in CCM2 ) was associated with lower CAD risk in the general population but higher CAD risk in clinical trial cohorts enriched for cardiometabolic disease. These results demonstrate how the phenotypic consequences of a CAD-associated gene can depend on disease context and stage.

One Sentence Summary

CCM2 heterozygosity reduces endothelial inflammation and early atherosclerosis but worsens late-stage disease, consistent with human genetics.

title: Efficacy of Stellate Ganglion Block for Preventing Postoperative Atrial Fibrillation After Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
authorString: Zhang J, Chen Y, Li N, Ai Z, Liang J, Chen Y, Lv H, Sayer S, Cao Y, Li J, Yu X, Chen G.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Stellate ganglion block (SGB) may reduce postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) by modulating the autonomic nervous system. This study evaluated the efficacy of preoperative SGB in preventing POAF following cardiac surgery.

Methods

In this single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 140 patients undergoing valve surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass were assigned (1:1) to ultrasound-guided right SGB with 7 mL of 0.5% ropivacaine or 7 mL of normal saline. The primary outcome was the incidence of POAF from postoperative day 0 to day 7 or until discharge.

Results

A total of 132 patients completed the study and were included in the modified intention-to-treat population (SGB group: n=65; saline group: n=67). POAF occurred in 43% of the SGB group and 40% of the saline group (odds ratio [OR], 0.99 [95% CI, 0.46-2.15], adjusted P=0.989). The SGB group demonstrated a lower incidence of intraoperative ventricular fibrillation/ventricular tachycardia requiring defibrillation after aortic cross-clamp release (6% versus 19%; OR, 0.21 [95% CI, 0.06-0.80]; adjusted P=0.022), lower postoperative high-sensitivity troponin I levels (median difference: -2562 ng/L [95% CI, -4301 to -45]; P=0.045), and a reduced risk of postoperative acute kidney injury (5% versus 18%; OR, 0.24 [95% CI, 0.06-0.98]; adjusted P=0.046).

Conclusions

While preoperative SGB did not reduce the incidence of POAF, it was associated with potential benefits, including a lower requirement for intraoperative defibrillation attributable to ventricular arrhythmias, attenuated myocardial injury (as indicated by lower high-sensitivity troponin I levels), and a decreased risk of postoperative acute kidney injury.

title: Contralateral Major Amputation Following Diabetes- and Peripheral Artery Disease-Related Limb Loss: A Systematic Review and Pooled Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Han K, Muro A, Sun K, Tackett C, Manzur M, Shih CD, Armstrong DG, Tan TW.
abstractText:
Background

Major amputation remains a devastating and understudied outcome in patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD), chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), and diabetes mellitus (DM)-related limb disease. Although modern vascular care emphasizes index and symptomatic limb surveillance, the population-level risk of non-index limb (NIL) major amputation remains incompletely defined. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to quantify NIL major amputation incidence and evaluate factors associated with contralateral limb loss.

Design/method

A systematic search of PubMed (MEDLINE), Embase, and Scopus through January 2026 was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Studies reporting contralateral above- or below-knee amputation in adults with PAD, CLTI, DM-related limb disease, or prior ipsilateral major amputation were included. Single-arm random-effects meta-analysis using the restricted maximum likelihood (REML) estimator was performed with log-transformed effect sizes. Subgroup analyses were conducted by clinical phenotype, geographic location, study era, and DM prevalence. Secondary outcomes included overall mortality, bilateral major amputation, NIL minor amputation, NIL revascularization, and development of NIL CLTI.

Results

Seventeen cohorts encompassing 30,359 patients were included. The pooled incidence of NIL major amputation was 6 per 100 person-years (95% CI, 3-9), with substantial heterogeneity (I2=98.93%). Meta-regression showed no significant differences by clinical phenotype (P=.622), geographic region (P=.662), study era (P=.893), or DM prevalence (P=.127). Clinical phenotypes included CLTI versus non-CLTI PAD or DM versus post-ipsilateral major amputation. Geographic region was divided into United States and international studies. Study era was divided into modern (2010-2025) and legacy (pre-2010) studies. Longer follow-up duration was inversely associated with reported incidence (P<.001). Pooled mortality rate was 38% (95% CI, 30-47%), and the pooled rate of bilateral major amputation was 12% (95% CI, 8-18%). Other secondary outcomes included a pooled NIL minor amputation rate of 11% (95% CI, 3-37%), NIL revascularization rate of 19% (95% CI, 6-47%), and NIL CLTI development rate of 32% (95% CI, 11-64%).

Conclusions

NIL major amputation remains a persistent risk in PAD and DM-related limb disease. These findings support the need for structured bilateral limb surveillance and early NIL risk stratification to inform comprehensive limb preservation care.

title: Outcomes of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in the Middle East and North Africa: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Bastan MM, Siami S, Jodeiri F, Kazemian S, Ebrahimzade M, Seighali N, Maleki S, Anaraki N, Abdelhamid M, Abdel-Rahman SE, Hosseini K.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Data on transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) outcomes in the Middle East and North Africa region are limited. We synthesized available evidence on post-TAVR clinical outcomes in the Middle East and North Africa region.

Methods

We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Scopus from inception through May 2025 for studies reporting TAVR outcomes in this region. Outcomes included device success, all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, new-onset atrial fibrillation, moderate to severe paravalvular leak, and permanent pacemaker implantation. Overall incidence rates were pooled via Poisson analysis and reported per 100 person-years with 95% CIs.

Results

Forty-eight studies encompassing 7331 patients (mean age, 76.9±8.5 years; 52.4% women) were included. Pooled device success rate was 96.4% (95% CI, 95.8%-97.0%). At latest follow-up, pooled incidence rates per 100 person-years were 13.7 for all-cause death (95% CI, 12.9-14.6), 4.8 for cardiovascular death (95% CI, 4.1-5.7), 1.0 for myocardial infarction (95% CI, 0.7-1.4), 1.6 for stroke (95% CI, 1.3-1.9), 2.7 for moderate to severe paravalvular leak (95% CI, 2.2-3.4), 6.5 for new-onset atrial fibrillation (95% CI, 5.5-7.7), and 10.0 for permanent pacemaker implantation (95% CI, 9.2-10.9). Post hoc exploratory meta-regression identified significant study-level modifying effects, with higher mean age and greater use of first-generation versus second-generation valves associated with higher overall all-cause mortality incidence following TAVR. Certainty of evidence was low or very low across all outcomes.

Conclusions

TAVR in the Middle East and North Africa region was associated with high device success rate and relatively low cardiovascular death. Permanent pacemaker implantation was the most prevalent post-TAVR complication. Further studies are warranted to optimize TAVR practice in this region.

title: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Determinants of Bowel Ischemia and Associated Risk After Elective Endovascular Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair.
authorString: Pivoto N, Jaldin RG, Sembenelli M, Bertanha M, Malgor RD, Sobreira ML.

journal.title: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists

abstractText:
Objective

Bowel ischemia (BI) is an uncommon but devastating complication of elective endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR). We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to identify patient- and procedure-related risk factors for BI after elective EVAR.

Methods

We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature, Cochrane Library, Scielo, and Lilacs from database inception through March 31, 2024, without language or date restrictions. We included observational studies of adults who underwent elective EVAR and reported postoperative BI and extractable risk-factor data. Two reviewers independently screened titles, abstracts, and full texts, extracted data, and assessed study quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. For factors reported in multiple sufficiently homogeneous studies, random-effects meta-analysis was used to pool risk ratios (RRs) or mean differences (MDs), with heterogeneity assessed using I2.

Results

Twenty-three retrospective cohort studies, including 306 344 elective EVAR procedures, met the inclusion criteria, and 10 provided sufficient data for quantitative synthesis. Across all studies, 1535 patients developed postoperative BI, corresponding to an overall incidence of approximately 0.5%. Female sex was associated with increased BI risk (RR, 2.66; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.06-3.43; I2 = 0%). Larger aneurysm diameter was also associated with increased risk (MD, 4.05 mm; 95% CI, 0.09-8.02; I2 = 0%). Renal dysfunction was a consistent predictor, with chronic kidney disease (RR, 2.93; 95% CI, 1.01-8.47; I2 = 29%) and dialysis dependence (RR, 5.35; 95% CI, 2.38-12.05; I2 = 0%) associated with BI. Major intraoperative blood loss >1 L conferred the highest relative risk among pooled factors (RR, 7.45; 95% CI, 2.80-19.85; I2 = 0%). Age, systemic arterial hypertension, and active smoking were not significantly associated with BI in pooled analyses.

Conclusions

Bowel ischemia after elective EVAR is uncommon but clinically important because delayed recognition carries substantial morbidity and mortality. Female sex, larger aneurysm diameter, chronic kidney disease, dialysis dependence, and major blood loss identify patients who may warrant heightened perioperative vigilance. The certainty of evidence remains very low, and future studies should standardize reporting of bowel segment, mesenteric vessel involvement, inferior mesenteric artery and internal iliac artery status, endograft configuration, and overlapping registry populations.Clinical RelevanceBowel ischemia after elective endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR) is rare, but its low incidence should not be interpreted as low clinical importance because delayed diagnosis is often catastrophic. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesizes the largest available elective EVAR evidence focused on bowel ischemia and identifies reproducible risk signals, including female sex, aneurysm size, renal dysfunction, dialysis dependence, and major blood loss. The practical gain for readers is not a definitive prediction score, but a clearer framework for perioperative judgment: recognize vulnerable patients, avoid overinterpreting weak or non-poolable associations, and apply heightened postoperative vigilance when embolic, hypoperfusion, pelvic collateral, or renal-risk features coexist.

title: Comparative treatment effects of direct oral anticoagulants versus warfarin for nonvalvular atrial fibrillation in clinical practice vary over time due to channelling.
authorString: van den Hemel RBLJ, Fiolet ATL, Gamba MA, Souverein PC, Klungel OH, Bloem LT, Bots SH.
abstractText: Temporal shifts in patient characteristics can influence comparative treatment effects within a certain indication. We investigated patient characteristics and comparative effectiveness and safety for direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) and warfarin over the time period where DOACs replaced warfarin as preferred stroke prophylaxis in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF). We applied the cohort design to the Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum and created 12 sequential subcohorts of patients with NVAF between 2011 and 2023. Patients with a DOAC or warfarin prescription following a 1-year prescription-free period were included. Baseline characteristics were compared between subcohorts. Survival analysis was used to evaluate the risk of ischaemic stroke (effectiveness outcome) and major bleeds (safety outcome). We included 207 393 patients with NVAF (45% women, 77% DOAC users, mean age 76 years). In early subcohorts, a history of stroke/transient ischaemic attack was more common among DOAC users. In later subcohorts, diabetes, deep venous thrombosis/pulmonary embolism and antihypertensive use were more common among warfarin users. History of other cardiovascular disease, renal failure and diuretic use were consistently higher among warfarin users. Over time, the crude stroke hazard ratio for DOAC users compared with warfarin users shifted from 2.66 (95% CI 2.00-3.52) to 0.62 (0.23-1.67). This trend was attenuated in adjusted analyses. No such trends were seen for major bleeds. DOACs had unfavourable effectiveness estimates in earlier subcohorts, potentially due to preferential prescribing to higher risk patients. Early observational studies may encounter initial biases, underscoring the need for robust methodological approaches when evaluating newly introduced medicines.

title: Types of adult intensive care units and admissions in Türkiye between 2018 and 2023: a nationwide cohort study.
authorString: Yildirim M, Halacli B, Gemcioglu E, Baser S, Kaya EK, Bozkus R, Ata N, Birinci S, Topeli A.

journal.title: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie

abstractText: Türkiye has one of the highest intensive care unit (ICU) bed capacities among middle-income countries but also globally. Nevertheless, little is known about the characteristics of ICUs in Türkiye, their temporal trends, and ICU admissions and readmissions. We sought to analyze the structural characteristics of all adult ICUs and the clinical profiles of ICU admissions across Türkiye. We conducted a retrospective nationwide cohort study using data from the Turkish Ministry of Health National Electronic Database. We analyzed adult ICU admissions across all levels and types over 6 years (2018-2023) and documented patient demographics, comorbidities, admission diagnoses, and ICU outcomes. We retrieved data on 3,362,539 ICU admissions. Among 22 ICU types, mixed ICUs accounted for the highest proportion of admissions (31.4%), followed by coronary (23.7%), anesthesiology (14.3%), medical (6.1%), and surgical (6.0%) ICUs. The proportion of mixed ICU beds decreased from 44.0% in 2018 to 25.1% in 2023. Most ICU beds were in state (public) hospitals (50.8%), followed by private hospitals (34.8%). The number of ICU beds increased from 2019, with a notable rise in state hospitals after 2020. The average number of ICU admissions was 659 per 100,000 population annually. The median patient age was 65 [interquartile range, 39-91] yr, and the ICU mortality was 15.5%. The leading admission diagnoses were respiratory failure (10.1%), cerebrovascular disease (7.1%), and acute kidney injury (5.2%). Hypertension (67.5%) and coronary artery disease (44.8%) were common comorbidities, particularly in nonsurvivors. The 7-day ICU readmission rate was 3.0%. The present comprehensive analysis of ICU admissions in Türkiye between 2018 and 2023 highlights a shift toward specialization with a decrease in mixed ICUs. The impact of ICU diversity on resource use and patient outcomes requires further evaluation.

title: Activities of daily living and health status benefits of semaglutide in very old patients with heart failure, type 2 diabetes, and obesity: Real-world practice study.
authorString: Pérez-Velasco MA, Trenas A, Padilla-Leiva C, Pérez-Ruiz JM, Ruíz-Rodríguez FI, Gómez-Huelgas R, Bernal-López MR, Pérez-Belmonte LM.
abstractText:
Introduction and objectives

The role of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists in patients with heart failure has not been widely described. We aimed to analyze the efficacy of once-weekly semaglutide in very old patients with type 2 diabetes, obesity, and heart failure in terms of activities of daily living performance and health status.

Patients and methods

This real-world observational study included patients ≥80 years with heart failure, diabetes, and obesity treated with semaglutide (Sema-Old Group) and patients not treated with glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists (Control-Old Group). The co-primary outcomes were improvement in activities of daily living performance (measured using the Barthel Index) and health status (measured using the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire) at 24 months.

Results

After propensity score matching, 232 patients were included in each group. The use of once-weekly semaglutide was associated with greater improvement in activities of daily living performance and health status in the Sema-Old Group compared to the Control-Old Group (Odds Ratio: 4.03; 95% Confidence Interval: 1.82-7.31; p<.01; Odds Ratio: 4.65; 95% Confidence Interval: 1.92-7.71; p<.01; respectively). There were also reductions in heart failure and all-cause hospitalizations, and cardiovascular death. Semaglutide use was associated with improved glycemic control and reduced body weight. Negative correlations were observed between activities of daily living performance and heart failure health status with the body weight and NT-proBNP levels.

Conclusions

Once-weekly semaglutide use was associated with improvements in activities of daily living performance and heart failure health status in very old patients with type 2 diabetes, obesity, and heart failure.

title: Atrial Leadless Pacemaker Implantation at the Superior Right Atrial Site.
authorString: Ogano M, Tanabe J, Kimura K, Kokubun H, Matsuda RS, Asai K, Iwasaki YK.
abstractText:
Background

Right atrial appendage (RAA) pacing may produce nonphysiological atrial activation.

Objectives

To evaluate the feasibility, safety, and electrocardiographic characteristics of atrial leadless pacemaker implantation at the superior right atrium (RA).

Methods

Sixty-eight consecutive patients undergoing dual-chamber leadless pacemaker implantation were studied. Procedural, device, electrocardiographic, and clinical outcomes were compared between superior RA and RAA base pacing.

Results

Superior RA implantation succeeded in 26/46 attempts (56.5%), increasing from 27.8% to 60.0% and 92.3% across sequential periods. In noncrossover cases, procedure (72.7±16.4 vs 76.8±27.2 minutes; P=0.533) and fluoroscopy times (15.4±5.8 vs 18.6±11.9 minutes; P=0.249) were comparable. P-wave duration remained unchanged with superior RA pacing (99.7±29.9 to 98.1±25.6 ms; P=0.543) but increased with RAA pacing (106.7±23.1 to 134.9±25.6 ms; P<0.001); P-wave terminal force in V1 changed from 3.6% to 3.6% versus 10.0% to 45.0%, respectively (P<0.001 for RAA). PR intervals increased from 228.4±72.8 to 229.7±77.5 ms (P=0.038) and from 205.5±72.0 to 234.4±72.6 ms (P<0.001), respectively; the increase was smaller with superior RA pacing (+5.7±11.7 vs +38.6±31.3 ms; P<0.001). At 3 months, sensing amplitudes (3.4±1.5 vs 2.4±1.1 mV; P=0.091) and pacing thresholds (0.8±0.5 vs 0.8±0.3 V; P=0.785) were comparable. No pericardial tamponade occurred. During 10.4±4.6 months, mortality, heart failure events, and atrial fibrillation incidence did not differ significantly.

Conclusions

Superior RA pacing was feasible, showed a marked learning curve, and better preserved intrinsic atrial activation than RAA pacing.

title: Guideline-directed medical therapy implementation and its association with cardiac adverse events across cardiac and noncardiac risk domains.
authorString: Higuchi S, Shiraishi Y, Kohno T, Kobayashi M, Kitamura M, Nagatomo Y, Gatate Y, Sakamoto M, Miyamoto K, Saji M, Goda A, Shoji S, Kohsaka S, Yoshikawa T, West Tokyo Heart Failure (WET-HF) Registry Investigators.
abstractText: Guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) improves prognosis in heart failure (HF), but its implementation remains suboptimal, particularly in patients with multiple risk domains. We analyzed the association between GDMT achievement and the 2-year composite endpoint of cardiac death or HF hospitalization across cardiac and noncardiac risk domains using the WET-HF2 registry, a prospective multicenter Japanese registry. GDMT achievement was quantified using a dose-weighted GDMT score (0-12). Cardiac and noncardiac risk domains were assessed using MAGGIC risk score components. Among 2,702 patients, median GDMT and MAGGIC risk scores were 5 (3-6) and 23 (18-27), respectively. Each 1-point increase in noncardiac risk domain was associated with lower GDMT achievement (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.93; 95% CI 0.90-0.95), whereas each 1-point increase in cardiac risk domain was associated with greater GDMT achievement (aOR, 1.08; 95% CI 1.06-1.10). Among patients in the highest tertile of noncardiac risk, no documented reason for non-prescription of renin-angiotensin system inhibitors or mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists was identified in 11% and 16%, respectively. During 2-year follow-up, 652 patients (24%) experienced the composite endpoint. A higher GDMT score was associated with lower risk of the composite endpoint (adjusted hazard ratio per point, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.91-0.98), consistently across tertiles of cardiac and noncardiac risk (P for interaction=0.784 and 0.359). Higher cardiac risk was associated with greater GDMT achievement, while higher noncardiac risk was associated with lower achievement. The favorable association between GDMT achievement and clinical outcomes was observed across both risk domains.

title: Pulmonary function impairment, exercise intolerance, and clinical outcomes in symptomatic patients with HFpEF undergoing exercise stress echocardiography.
authorString: Kuno T, Kagami K, Harada T, Yamaguchi K, Yuasa N, Murakami F, Saito Y, Murakami T, Wada N, Ito I, Ishii H, Obokata M.
abstractText: Pulmonary function impairment is common in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). However, its relationships with exercise capacity, cardiovascular reserve capacity, and prognosis in HFpEF remain uncertain. We retrospectively studied symptomatic patients undergoing exercise stress echocardiography with simultaneous expired gas analysis. Cross-sectional analyses were performed to compare pulmonary function in patients with HFpEF and symptomatic controls in the cohort with available data on percent predicted vital capacity (%VC) and forced expiratory volume in 1 s (%FEV₁). Outcome assessment was also performed in a subset of patients. Among 486 patients in the cross-sectional cohort, 178 had HFpEF and 308 were symptomatic controls. Patients with HFpEF had lower %VC and %FEV₁ than controls. After adjustment for age, sex, and body mass index, lower %VC and %FEV₁ were consistently associated with reduced exercise capacity, higher echocardiographic estimates of left ventricular filling pressure (E/e') and reduced right ventricular systolic function during exercise. Prognostic analyses were performed in the HFpEF cohort with follow-up data (N = 148). There were 37 primary composite events of all-cause death or worsening heart failure over a median follow-up of 935 days. Lower %VC was associated with a higher risk of the primary composite endpoint and remained associated in multivariable models. The %FEV₁ showed a weaker but concordant association. Lower %VC and %FEV₁ were associated with reduced exercise capacity and hemodynamic derangements in the overall cohort and with worse clinical outcomes in patients with HFpEF.

title: Prevention of Abdominal Compartment Syndrome in Acute Care Surgery: A Scoping Review of Risk Factors and Management Strategies.
authorString: Othman Y, Kasabwala D, Jayagopi K, Kata A, Bundschu I, Haddadi M, Zito T, Smith CP, Elkbuli A.
abstractText: Abdominal compartment syndrome (ACS) is a life-threatening complication of sustained intra-abdominal hypertension (IAH) that can lead to organ dysfunction and substantial morbidity and mortality. Early identification and prevention are critical to limiting progression. This scoping review evaluates risk factors and preventive and therapeutic strategies for ACS in acute care surgical populations. This scoping review systematically searched PubMed, Cochrane, and ProQuest, supplemented by a search of the ScienceDirect full-text platform, to identify studies evaluating preventive and early-intervention strategies for ACS in acute care surgery populations through April 2026. Twelve studies were included. Preventive surgical strategies were associated with decreases in intra-abdominal pressure (IAP) and ACS progression. Percutaneous catheter decompression reported a statistically significant decrease in IAP (P = 0.001), whereas prophylactic decompressive laparotomy was associated with a decrease in IAP from 24.4 ± 8.5 mmHg to 13.4 ± 4.0 mmHg (P < 0.0001). Reduced crystalloid resuscitation was associated with a lower incidence of ACS (7.4% in 2006 versus 0% in 2011, P < 0.001) and lower mortality (22.8% versus 10.6%, P < 0.001). Independent risk factors for the development of ACS included abdominal distention (odds ratio [OR]: 4.951, P < 0.001), obesity (body mass index >30; OR: 3.413, P < 0.001), positive fluid balance, and elevated base deficit. Age was the only independent predictor of mortality (OR: 1.09, P = 0.017). Limited evidence suggested early enteral nutrition may reduce the progression of IAH without increasing IAP.
