Cox models and trend tests estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs.

Results

Among 9816 participants, 3836 were included in baseline CKM analysis and 1891 in transition analysis. Both RCF (HR=2.74, 95%CI:2.25-3.34) and PRCF (HR=2.51, 95%CI:1.96-3.21) were associated with increased CKM risk (both P < 0.001). Cognitive status provided additional risk stratification beyond physical frailty. RCF-to-Robust improvement reduced CKM risk by 56% (HR=0.44, 95%CI:0.23-0.85, P = 0.015), while deterioration markedly increased risk (HR≈5.3, P < 0.001). The Δscore trend test showed a significant dose-response relationship (P < 0.001). Substantial improvement (Δscore=-3) significantly reduced risk, whereas minor improvements showed protective trends without statistical significance.

Conclusions

Cognitive frailty is independently associated with CKM multimorbidity progression. Within each direction of cognitive change, the magnitude of change provided additional prognostic information beyond direction alone. These findings support the brain-CKM interconnection framework and suggest cognitive screening should be considered in CKM prevention strategies.

Lay summary

Cognitive frailty-a condition where physical decline and memory problems occur together-is common in older adults. In this study, we analysed data from nearly 10,000 middle-aged and older adults in China to understand whether cognitive frailty increases the risk of developing cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) multimorbidity, a cluster of conditions including heart disease, kidney disease, and diabetes. We found that people with cognitive frailty had significantly higher risks of developing CKM multimorbidity. More importantly, we found that the magnitude of change in cognitive function added prognostic information on top of its direction-greater worsening tracked with higher CKM risk. These findings suggest that monitoring changes in cognitive function over time could help identify individuals at high risk of CKM multimorbidity, and that interventions aimed at improving cognitive health may need to achieve meaningful improvement to reduce this risk.

title: Towards modeling the hemodynamic impact of mitral and aortic valve repair in patients with left ventricular assist devices.
authorString: Bonini M, Ferguson M, Hirschvogel M, Balmus M, Tang PC, Pagani F, Nordsletten D.
abstractText: Valve dysfunction is a major threat to long-term success in left ventricular assist device (LVAD) therapy, with direct implications for right heart performance. In this study, we apply a patient-specific, image-based computational modeling framework to evaluate the hemodynamic impact of simulated mitral and aortic valve repair in five LVAD-supported patients. Each patient was modeled under four conditions: (patient-specific LVAD-supported state), simulated mitral valve (MV) repair, simulated aortic valve (AV) repair, and simulated combined MV&AV repair. Because validation data for valve repair were unavailable, the simulated repair scenarios are exploratory in silico interventions based on clinically validated patient-specific models. The models integrate dynamic CT imaging, echocardiography, catheterization data, and device-specific LVAD parameters into a coupled 3D-0D simulation pipeline. Valve dynamics are governed by transvalvular pressure and flow, allowing physiological modeling of regurgitant lesions and surgical repair. The right ventricular (RV) was assessed using a combination of model-derived metrics, including right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF), pulmonary artery pulsatility index (PAPi), and RV-PA coupling. In addition, we performed blood residence time (RT) analysis to evaluate blood stasis within the left heart and aorta. The simulations suggest that valve repair improved cardiac output, reduced pulmonary congestion, and enhanced right ventricular loading conditions. Notably, mitral valve repair restored aortic valve opening during the cardiac cycle, which improved sinus washout and reduced blood residence time within the aortic root-factors associated with lower thrombotic risk. Overall, these findings suggest a potential role for valve repair in LVAD-supported hearts, though larger, validated patient cohorts are needed to confirm these results.

title: Remodeling of Failed Pulmonary Valve Autografts After the Ross Procedure.
authorString: Stejskal V, Sokolova T, Sagat J, Vasova B, Hrnciarova L, Smolak P.
abstractText: The Ross procedure utilizes a pulmonary autograft for aortic valve replacement, but late autograft failure remains a clinical challenge. In this exploratory study, we characterized structural alterations in failed pulmonary autografts using digital morphometric analysis. Five autografts explanted because of regurgitation were compared with six autopsy control pulmonary valves using special stains and alpha-smooth muscle actin immunohistochemistry. One histologically most affected section per valve was evaluated using QuPath. Failed autografts showed leaflet thickening, elastosis, fibrosis, and myxomatous matrix accumulation. Compared with controls, autografts had greater maximum leaflet thickness (1.540 vs. 0.447 mm; P = 0.004), cross-sectional area (8.730 vs. 3.045 mm²; P = 0.004), α-SMA-positive area (0.707 vs. 0.046 mm²; P = 0.008), and α-SMA-positive area fraction (0.069 vs. 0.016; P = 0.017). The findings demonstrate extracellular matrix alterations and increased α-SMA immunoreactivity in hotspot regions, suggesting a myxomatous-like remodeling pattern.

title: The impact of leaflet thrombosis on transcatheter aortic valve degeneration: a narrative review.
authorString: van Nuland PJA, Overduin DC, van Ginkel DJ, Jacobsen MR, Swaans MJ, Timmers L, Rensing BJWM, Geisler T, Ten Berg JM.
abstractText: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has expanded into younger and lower-risk patients, making long-term valve durability increasingly important. Leaflet thrombosis, most commonly identified on computed tomography as hypoattenuated leaflet thickening (HALT), is common after TAVI. Whether leaflet thrombosis contributes to structural valve deterioration (SVD) remains incompletely understood. To summarize the current evidence on the relationship between leaflet thrombosis and SVD after TAVI, with a focus on clinical outcomes, imaging findings, antithrombotic therapy, and pathophysiological mechanisms. This narrative review synthesizes available clinical, imaging, mechanistic, histopathological and antithrombotic literature addressing leaflet thrombosis and valve durability after TAVI. CT studies show that leaflet thrombosis occurs in 13-32% of patients within the first post-procedural year. Although some lesions resolve spontaneously, longitudinal imaging studies demonstrate persistence in a substantial proportion of patients, supporting the presence of an underlying valve-related substrate. HALT has not consistently been associated with adverse valve hemodynamics during the first year after implantation. Long-term TAVI durability studies report low rates of severe SVD (0.8-1.5% up to 10 years), although outcomes vary according to valve generation and study population. The 10-year NOTION and PARTNER 2A data provide important long-term durability information, but neither study included systematic longitudinal CT assessment of leaflet thrombosis. Observational studies linking early HALT to subsequent hemodynamic valve deterioration have yielded conflicting results. Indirect evidence from anticoagulation studies and histopathological investigations supports biological plausibility for a relationship between leaflet thrombosis and progressive leaflet injury, but does not establish causality. Leaflet thrombosis is a frequent imaging finding after TAVI and may persist over time, but its contribution to long-term SVD remains uncertain. Current evidence supports a potential biological relationship between leaflet thrombosis and valve degeneration but does not demonstrate that HALT is a causal precursor of clinically relevant SVD. Prospective studies combining serial CT imaging with long-term, standardized assessment of structural valve outcomes are required to resolve this question.

title: Histologically Confirmed Myxedematous Myocardial Involvement in Severe Hypothyroidism With Concomitant Bicuspid Aortic Stenosis.
authorString: Sharma-Sharma S, Galindo-Uribe J, Gutiérrez-Alanís S, Cázares-Diazleal AC, Vásquez-Ortiz ZY, Rosales-Uvera SG, Pérez-Enríquez B, Martínez-Benítez B.
abstractText:
Background

Histologically confirmed myxedematous myocardial involvement is rare and may be difficult to recognize when another cause of ventricular hypertrophy and fibrosis coexists.

Case summary

A 40-year-old man with longstanding, inadequately treated primary hypothyroidism presented with exertional dyspnea and a large goiter. Echocardiography showed severe bicuspid aortic stenosis, moderate aortic regurgitation, marked concentric left ventricular hypertrophy, preserved ejection fraction, and severely reduced global longitudinal strain. Cardiac magnetic resonance demonstrated extensive late gadolinium enhancement involving approximately 26% of myocardial mass. After thyroid optimization, he underwent aortic valve replacement. Myocardial biopsy showed severe cardiomyocyte atrophy, interstitial mucin deposition, and extensive replacement fibrosis; Congo red staining was negative.

Discussion

Severe aortic stenosis provided an alternative explanation for the myocardial phenotype, and multimodality imaging alone could not distinguish pressure-overload remodeling from hypothyroidism-related myocardial injury.

Conclusion

Histopathology established concomitant myxedematous myocardial involvement, highlighting the diagnostic value of tissue characterization in severe hypothyroidism.

title: Simplify AVR with da Vinci using the RAM and the SEW-EASY systems.
authorString: Benedik J, Tymochko Y, Kritek J, Rzyman R, Kohut M.

journal.title: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS

abstractText: Robotic aortic valve replacement using the da Vinci surgical system is a technically demanding procedure. In this video tutorial, we demonstrate the use of the RAM and SEW-EASY systems (LSI Solutions), which substantially facilitate the surgical technique and simplify the performance of the procedure.

title: Effect of Endostaple Configuration and Oversizing on Endograft Displacement Force: An In Vitro Evaluation of the Aortoseal Endostapling System.
authorString: Pierie SLR, Ligtenberg LW, David DB, Khalil ISM, de Vries JPM.

journal.title: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists

abstractText:
Background

Proximal endograft fixation remains a key determinant of long-term durability of endovascular aortic repair (EVAR). The Aortoseal Endostapling system consists of a nitinol frame with 6 welded endostaples at the proximal end, intended to enhance fixation and seal of an endograft by mimicking the hand-sewn anastomosis of open aortic repair. This study evaluates the effect of different distributions of activated endostaples on endograft displacement force (EDF), while considering various endograft oversizing options.

Methods

An in vitro silicone tube model was used to assess EDF at 2 mm endograft displacement and pull-out force across 11 activated staple configurations of the Aortoseal Endostapling system with 10%, 20%, and 30% endograft oversizing. Interobserver agreement was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), based on a 2-way mixed-effects model for absolute agreement.

Results

Intraclass correlation coefficient for interobserver agreement was 0.987. Endograft displacement force ranged from 8.8 N ± 0.15 N to 39.6 N ± 2.96 N across all configurations and oversizing conditions. Incorporation of the Aortoseal frame alone, without staple activation, substantially increased EDF compared with no Aortoseal frame at 10% and 20% oversizing. Furthermore, EDF was mostly influenced by the number of activated staples and the maximum unstapled circumferential angle (MUCA). The 6-activated-staple configuration consistently yielded the highest EDF. The effect of oversizing on EDF was inconsistent across configurations at 10% and 20%, whereas 30% oversizing was associated with lower EDF in most configurations. Pull-out force exceeded EDF in all tested configurations except the 1-activated-staple configuration.

Conclusion

In this in vitro study, Aortoseal frame incorporation alone substantially increased EDF relative to the graft-only configuration at 10% and 20% oversizing. Ten percent endograft oversizing yielded EDF values comparable with 20% oversizing across most configurations. Circumferential staple distribution was the primary determinant of EDF in the Aortoseal Endostapling system, with EDF decreasing with increasing MUCA and increasing with staple number across all endograft oversizing conditions, consistent with circumferential load sharing as a potential underlying mechanism. These findings may serve as a mechanistic reference framework for preoperative planning in anatomically challenging cases and warrant further experimental and clinical evaluation.Clinical ImpactThe Aortoseal Endostapling system (Endoron Medical Holdings Ltd., Dublin, Ireland) represents a novel approach to proximal endograft fixation, enabling simultaneous circumferential single-stage activation of 6 nitinol endostaples via balloon activation, providing a uniform and reproducible fixation pattern intended to mimic the longitudinal and radial anchoring of a surgical anastomosis. To support clinical implementation, this study systematically evaluated endograft displacement force across a range of activated staple configurations, including suboptimal deployment scenarios. The findings provide physicians with a mechanistic reference framework for preoperative planning, supporting procedural decision-making in anatomically challenging cases.

title: Comprehensive hemodynamic assessment of the Fontan pathway using four-dimensional flow magnetic resonance imaging.
authorString: Matsubara M, Schaeffer T, Palm J, Lemmen T, Ruda C, Stern H, Shehu N, Miyazaki S, Suzuki K, Nishino T, Itatani K, Meierhofer C, Hörer J, Ono M.
abstractText:
Objectives

Conventional hemodynamic assessment of Fontan circulation relies on limited quantitative measurements. We evaluated the feasibility and clinical value of comprehensive flow visualization using four-dimensional flow magnetic resonance imaging to characterize patient-specific hemodynamic patterns in extracardiac total cavopulmonary connection.

Methods

Eight patients with extracardiac total cavopulmonary connection underwent four-dimensional flow magnetic resonance imaging at a median of 13.7 years postoperatively (interquartile range: 9.0-16.4 years). The Fontan pathway was segmented into five regions: extracardiac conduit, superior vena cava, central confluence, left pulmonary artery, and right pulmonary artery. Energy loss, maximum velocity, and kinetic energy were quantified for each segment using iTFlow software. Clinical outcomes were assessed during follow-up.

Results

Median age at total cavopulmonary connection was 1.8 years (interquartile range: 1.5-3.5), with 18 mm conduits in seven patients and 22 mm conduit in one patient. During a median follow-up of 17.3 years, two patients underwent re-operation after magnetic resonance imaging evaluation (tricuspid valve replacement and ascending aortic reconstruction); all remained alive without Fontan failure. Energy loss differed significantly across segments (p = 0.011), being highest in the conduit and central confluence, with remarkable inter-patient variability superimposed (conduit values varying 35-fold from 0.025 to 0.887 mW). Maximum velocity strongly correlated with energy loss (r = 0.92, p = 0.001), suggesting velocity may serve as an accessible surrogate. Atrioventricular valve regurgitation severity did not consistently correlate with energy loss.

Conclusions

Four-dimensional flow magnetic resonance imaging with iTFlow software enables comprehensive hemodynamic assessment throughout the Fontan pathway, revealing substantial patient-specific heterogeneity in energy efficiency. With larger cohorts and correlation with clinical outcomes, this technique may become a valuable screening tool for post-Fontan evaluation and long-term surveillance.

title: IVUS-Guided Dobutamine Challenge to Guide Anomalous RCA PCI: An Interesting Case Report.
authorString: Votsis S, Cilingiroglu M, Iliescu C, Boudoulas KD, Marmagkiolis K.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText: Congenital coronary artery anomalies are quite uncommon-they are observed in 1.3% of the coronary angiograms. Although most of them are benign, some coronary anomalies are associated with poor clinical outcomes. The exact mechanism of these outcomes in patients with anomalous RCA from the left aortic cusp with interarterial course is hypothesized to be either compression of the coronary artery during its course between the aorta and the pulmonary artery, or obstruction of the coronary flow during exercise due to the acute angulation of the RCA ostium. We present the case of a 54 y/o patient with NSTEMI, who, after a diagnostic coronary angiogram and coronary CT, was found to have complex coronary artery disease, including an anomalous RCA from the left aortic cusp with "malignant" interarterial course. In order to determine the optimal treatment, we proceeded with IVUS assessment of the ostial and proximal RCA with dobutamine challenge, which showed significant stenosis of both the RCA ostium and the interarterial segment at the peak dose of the dobutamine challenge. As a result a decision was made to treat both the RCA ostium and its interarterial segment with PCI, producing an excellent final result. Our case underscores the importance of the combination of IVUS and dobutamine challenge in order to answer the ever-important pathophysiologic mechanism of a lesion and accordingly provide tailor-made treatment for anomalous coronary arteries.

title: Two polymorphs of an independent amyloid core in medin’s C-terminal region
authorString: Pradhan B, Rousseau F, Schymkowitz J.
abstractText: Medin, a 50-residue fragment of lactadherin (MFG-E8), forms aortic medial amyloid, the most common localized amyloid in humans, and co-deposits with vascular amyloid-β (Aβ) in Alzheimer’s disease. In the full-length medin fibril the N-terminal half forms the entire protofilament interface, yet the strongest predicted amyloidogenic determinants lie in the C-terminal region. Here we show that this region aggregates on its own. The isolated C-terminal aggregation-prone region (medin C-APR, medin 31–53) begins to aggregate with the same lag time as full-length medin and assembles into two coexisting polymorphs, determined here by cryo-EM at 2.71 and 2.91 Å. Both are built from the same two-stranded β-arch and a pseudo-2₁ protofilament pair closed by an aromatic–aliphatic zipper, and differ only in how many accessory chains the exposed hydrophobic face recruits. The medin C-terminus therefore carries an amyloid core of its own, unrelated to that of the full-length fibril: medin has more than one aggregation-prone region, and the structural contribution of each region depends on sequence and assembly context.

title: Cross study transfer of vascular transcriptomic classifiers in seven public cohorts
authorString: You L, Guo Y, Zhong X, Peng Z, Wang W, Shen L, Ge J.
abstractText:
Abstract

Strong discrimination within a vascular transcriptomic study may not transfer across clinical endpoints, tissue compartments or assay processing. We evaluated seven public Gene Expression Omnibus datasets containing 294 deposited observations, including repeated lesion segments. Four conventional classifiers and a prior-only control underwent nested validation in 48 abdominal aortic aneurysm samples, followed by external evaluation under three preprocessing configurations. Source-rank L1 logistic regression achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.947; external values were 0.753 and 0.667 in two carotid cohorts and 1.000 in 11 macrophage plaque samples. The latter value fell to 0.367 under a separately source-tuned common-gene pipeline. In 126 plaque donors with censored follow-up, Harrell concordance was 0.565 (95% interval 0.444–0.678) and 0.524 after a 30-day landmark. Processing-incompatible blood data served as a stress control; 43 correlated plaque segments were analysed descriptively. A matched permutation test supported source separation without testing generalisation. These results show that internal discrimination and isolated external success do not establish stable panvascular risk prediction. The benchmark supplies code, per-sample outputs and provenance for scrutinising pipeline sensitivity, endpoint mismatch and observation dependence.

title: Sex-based differences in fibrosis markers in human abdominal aortic aneurysms
authorString: Elizondo-Benedetto S, Wahidi R, Arif B, Rusconi B, Braasch MC, Ibrahim D, Zaghloul MS, Soltan O, Engles N, Kuziez I, Ohman JW, Sanchez LA, Zayed MA.
abstractText:
Background

Abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA) are a complex degenerative vascular disease. The role of fibrosis in AAA progression is unclear. Our study evaluated the impact of fibroblast activation protein (FAP), collagen, and vimentin on AAA fibrosis and progression. We hypothesized that FAP may influence fibrosis and disease severity in AAA, with potential sex-specific differences.

Study Design

Multi-centered transcriptomic analysis of aortic samples from 15 human AAA and 5 non-AAA was performed to evaluate cell-specific fibrosis gene expression profiles. Histopathological and molecular analysis of 26 male and female AAA samples (mAAA and fAAA) and 29 male and female normal abdominal aortas (mNAA and fNAA) was performed to assess whole-tissue fibrosis markers and signaling.

Results

Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis identified eight major cell clusters with distinct sex-based distributions. Although vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) and fibroblast clusters had reduced counts in both male and female AAAs, they more highly expressed FAP and COL1A1 genes, particularly in females. Whole-tissue analysis demonstrated elevated extracellular matrix deposits with markedly increased collagen type 1 in both mAAA and fAAA. Alpha-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA)-positive VSMCs were also reduced in mAAA and fAAA, but FAP was notably elevated, and robustly in fAAA. FAP-positive fibroblasts in fAAA exhibited increased expression of fibrosis markers, suggesting a unique pro-fibrotic phenotype.

Conclusion

Our study reveals a sex-based difference in AAA tissue, with elevated fibrosis markers and increased FAP levels in females, suggesting its significant role in disease progression. These findings underscore the potential of FAP as a unique tissue biomarker for AAAs and warrants further investigation into novel targeted therapies that aim to stabilize AAAs, particularly in female patients.

title: AI-Enabled Digital Stethoscope for Early Detection of Congenital Heart Disease: Prospective Study.
authorString: Karandikar N, Kachappilly A, Kadarge A, Rumane A, Ansari S, Bhaskaran S, Karande T, Bobhate P.
abstractText: Early detection of congenital heart disease (CHD) is critical, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where access to congenital cardiac services is limited. While auscultation remains a first-line screening tool, its accuracy is operator dependent. Advances in digital stethoscopes and artificial intelligence (AI) may enhance diagnostic performance. To evaluate the accuracy of an AI-based algorithm integrated with a digital stethoscope for detecting CHD in children and young adults, using echocardiography as the reference standard. In this prospective single centre study, heart sounds were recorded from 721 subjects (382 with CHD, 339 controls) using the digital stethoscope at four standard auscultatory sites. Of these, 301 recordings were used for algorithm training and 420 for blinded forward testing, which was divided temporally with the data collected in first 5 months used for training and the data collected after that used for forward testing. Recordings were denoised, transformed into mel-spectrograms, and analyzed using a convolutional neural network (CovNN) to classify CHD probability. A threshold probability of > 0.5 across > 2 sites was used to predict CHD. Performance was compared against echocardiography. In forward testing, the AI algorithm correctly identified 222 of 233 CHD cases and 171 of 187 controls, yielding a sensitivity of 95.2% and specificity of 91.4%. The algorithm remained effective in noisy environments and in uncooperative children, where conventional auscultation is challenging. An AI algorithm integrated with a digital stethoscope demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity for CHD detection in children and young adults. By leveraging mel-spectrogram features, it overcomes key limitations of isolated time-domain or frequency domain analysis and shows promise as a scalable, non-invasive screening tool for early CHD detection, particularly in resource-limited settings.

title: Community Health Worker Interventions Addressing Social Determinants of Health in Chronic Disease: A Systematic Review.
authorString: Wilder M, Degtyar A, McKay J, Mavuri S, Bolton M, Richardson LD, Souffront K.
abstractText:
Introduction

Chronic diseases disproportionately affect people facing social and economic adversity. Community health workers (CHWs) are increasingly recognized as a key workforce for addressing social determinants of health (SDOH). However, evidence for the effect of CHW-led interventions on social and clinical outcomes among US adults with chronic disease is limited. This systematic review evaluated the effects of CHW-led interventions on SDOH and health outcomes.

Methods

Following PRISMA guidelines and a registered Prospero protocol, we searched PubMed, Scopus, and Embase (Ovid) in April 2024 for US-based randomized or quasi-experimental studies involving adults with chronic disease and a patient-facing CHW intervention addressing at least 1 SDOH domain. Eligible studies were required to have a comparator group and report social or health outcomes. We used standardized forms to extract data and assess quality.

Results

We identified 1,939 records and screened 1,058 abstracts. We reviewed 110 full-text articles; 7 studies met inclusion criteria. All were randomized controlled trials addressing at least 1 SDOH domain. Interventions most commonly targeted health care access, housing stability, or care coordination among adults with diabetes, HIV, asthma, hepatitis C, or hearing loss. CHW interventions demonstrated improvements in several condition-specific clinical outcomes, but overall effects on major clinical indicators were modest and inconsistent.

Conclusion

CHW-led interventions show promise for addressing social needs and improving engagement in care among adults with chronic disease, but evidence of meaningful clinical benefit is still limited. The lack of large, well-powered trials underscores the need for more rigorous research to strengthen the evidence base for CHW-driven SDOH interventions in US health systems.

title: Phytochemicals at the PPAR-NF-<i>κ</i>B Interface: A Structured Narrative Review of Receptor Pharmacology, Inflammatory Signaling, and Translational Barriers.
authorString: Rehman SU, Rehman FU, Khan SU, Zeb A, Ashfaq S, Khan SU, Hafiz WU.
abstractText:
Background

The peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPARs) and nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) signaling axis serves as master molecular interface governing metabolic homeostasis and inflammatory resolution. Dysregulated reciprocal repression between PPAR-α/γ and NF-κB contributes to chronic inflammatory diseases, metabolic syndrome, and malignancy. Synthetic full agonists (e.g., thiazolidinediones and fibrates) are associated with clinical liabilities including adipogenesis, fluid retention, hepatotoxicity, and cardiovascular adverse effects, underscoring the need for safer modulators.

Objective and rationale

This structured narrative review provides a rigorous mechanistic synthesis of plant derived phytochemicals with selective PPAR modulator (SPPARM) like pharmacology. We elucidate how distinct chemical classes may achieve targeted NF-κB transrepression with reduced transcriptional liability, summarize available ligand receptor binding data, and critically evaluate translational hurdles.

Methods

A structured narrative review was conducted using a systematic style literature search across PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science from January 2000 through March 2026. In line with PRISMA 2020 principles for transparent reporting, original research articles were prioritized according to evidence type (clinical, preclinical, in vivo, and in vitro/in silico), with emphasis on pharmacodynamic metrics, binding kinetics (Ki, EC50, and IC50), receptor dependency validation (knockout, antagonism), and pharmacokinetic data.

Results

Chemically diverse phytochemicals including flavonoids, neolignans, stilbenoids and terpenoids exhibit partial or subtype selective PPAR agonism in reporter and binding assays. Mechanistically, many favor anti-inflammatory transrepression over full coactivator-dependent transactivation, with evidence for corepressor recruitment and inhibition of NF-κB nuclear translocation in selected models. However, integrated analysis reveals a persistent disconnect between submicromolar in vitro potency and negligible systemic exposure of free parent compound (low Cmax, extensive glucuronidation/sulfation), compounded by frequent reliance on unvalidated docking simulations and PPAR-independent NF-κB inhibition.

Conclusion

Phytochemicals with SPPARM-like pharmacology represent a promising but unvalidated paradigm for nonsteroidal inflammation control. Realizing their potential will require next-generation delivery systems (e.g., liposomes, nanoemulsions, and cyclodextrin complexes), mandatory genetic or pharmacological receptor validation, and biomarker-driven clinical trials that document target engagement at achievable human exposure levels.

title: Electrophysiology Team-Administered Conscious Sedation for Pulsed-Field Versus Radiofrequency Ablation in Atrial Fibrillation.
authorString: Cheng L, Xia Y, Hu Z, Zhang T, Li L, Meng X, Xiong Y, Xu Q, Zhang Z, Chen G, Ding L, Yao Y.
abstractText:
Background

Pulsed-field ablation (PFA) is emerging as a novel nonthermal alternative. However, PFA is commonly performed under general anesthesia or deep sedation requiring anesthesiologists, which increases resource utilization and limits its widespread application. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility of conscious sedation for PFA administered by the electrophysiology (EP) team, using radiofrequency ablation (RFA) as a comparator.

Methods

A total of 120 patients with symptomatic, drug-refractory atrial fibrillation were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to the PFA group or the RFA group. We evaluated three key outcomes: (1) intraoperative patient tolerance, assessed using validated scales (Faces Pain Scale-Revised [FPS-R], Likert Scale Questionnaire [LSQ]) combined with intraoperative body movement and cough reactions; (2) procedural efficiency; and (3) procedural safety.

Results

The incidence of pain during pulmonary vein isolation was comparable between the two groups (all p > 0.05), whereas FPS-R scores were significantly lower in the PFA group (p < 0.05). No significant difference was observed in movement scores between the two groups (p = 0.452). According to the LSQ analysis, only 1 patient (1.7%) in the RFA group reported dissatisfaction with intraoperative pain management. Cough incidence during PVI was higher with PFA (21.7% [13/60] vs 6.7% [4/60]; p = 0.018). Both total procedure time and left atrial dwell time were shorter in the PFA group. Furthermore, no serious complications were directly related to conscious sedation.

Conclusion

In selected low-risk patients, EP team-administered conscious sedation is feasible for PFA, with acceptable intraoperative tolerance and safety while preserving procedural efficiency.

title: Atherosclerosis: From Pathogenesis to Therapeutic Interventions.
authorString: Zhou E, Zhan C, Li Y, Zeng Y, Luo R, Ouyang X, Liu S, Yang R, Yan N, Jiang L.
abstractText: Atherosclerosis is no longer viewed solely as a lipid-storage disorder but rather as a complex multisystem inflammatory disease driven by interactions among the vascular, immune, metabolic, and nervous systems. This review integrates recent concepts, including trained immunity, the neuroimmune cardiovascular interface, vascular cell plasticity, and the microbiome-vascular axis, that reshape the understanding of plaque initiation, progression, and instability. We summarize how established lipid-lowering, antidiabetic, antihypertensive, and revascularization strategies influence atherosclerotic disease and discuss emerging interventions, including RNA therapeutics, anti-inflammatory agents, gene therapy, and cell-based approaches. Key ongoing clinical trials that may clarify the cardiovascular benefits and safety of these strategies are also reviewed. Despite therapeutic advances, residual cardiovascular risk persists because of limitations in animal models, sex-related differences in plaque phenotype, and the lack of clinically applicable biomarkers. Nanotechnology, human microphysiological systems, spatial multiomics, and artificial intelligence may help bridge these translational gaps. Successful clinical implementation will nevertheless require biomarker-guided patient selection, rational combination therapy, validated surrogate endpoints, long-term safety assessment, and attention to health economics. In summary, these advances will shape future translational research and clinical trial design, ultimately advancing personalized management of atherosclerosis.

title: Short-Term Effects of Golden Rice Cookies Enriched With <i>Piper crocatum</i> Extract on Lipid Profiles in Adults With Diabetes: A Quasi-Experimental Study.
authorString: Abram AS, Setyawati A, Irwan AM.
abstractText:
Background

Diabetes mellitus (DM) commonly coexists with dyslipidemia and elevated cardiovascular risk. Food-based interventions containing antioxidants and polyphenols may support lipid metabolism. This study evaluated the short-term effects of Golden Rice cookies enriched with active Piper crocatum extract on lipid profiles in adults with DM.

Methods

This quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group study included 102 adults with DM assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention or control group. The intervention group received Golden Rice cookies enriched with P. crocatum extract, while the control group received similar cookies without the extract for 28 days. Total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), and triglycerides were measured before and after the intervention. Bivariate analyses were performed in the full sample, whereas analysis of covariance was performed among non-statin participants, adjusting for baseline lipid values, age, body mass index, diabetes duration, carbohydrate intake, and protein intake.

Results

In the unadjusted analysis, total cholesterol and LDL-C increased significantly in the intervention group, whereas total cholesterol decreased significantly in the control group. Between-group analysis showed a significant difference only in total cholesterol. Among non-statin participants, an exploratory adjusted analysis showed a significant between-group difference in total cholesterol (p = 0.016; adjusted mean difference = -12.55 mg/dL; 95% confidence interval [CI] = -22.74 to -2.36). No significant adjusted differences were observed for LDL-C, HDL-C, or triglycerides.

Conclusion

A 28-day intervention with Golden Rice cookies enriched with active P. crocatum extract was associated with a limited exploratory adjusted between-group difference in total cholesterol among non-statin adults with DM. These preliminary findings require confirmation in longer randomized controlled trials with stronger dietary control and mechanistic biomarker assessment.

Trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov number: NCT07268781.

title: Associations of Coexisting Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Sarcopenia-Related Abnormalities With Adverse Clinical Outcomes Across Obesity States.
authorString: Fan H, Mao X, Yan T, Barnett S, Zhang J, Cheung R, Zhang X, Nguyen MH.
abstractText: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is associated with adverse liver and non-liver outcomes, but the impact of coexisting sarcopenia-related abnormalities (e.g., low muscle strength [MS], muscle mass, and physical performance) remains unclear. In a prospective UK Biobank cohort (n = 438,748), we evaluated their joint associations with incidence and risks of all-cause mortality, cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), cardiovascular disease (CVD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), non-liver cancers, and obesity-related cancers across MASLD and sarcopenia-related abnormality status. Over a median follow-up of 13.8 years, 401 HCC, 1714 cirrhosis, 39,534 CVD, 19,637 CKD, 38,240 non-liver cancers, 12,536 obesity-related cancers, and 34,801 deaths occurred. A stepwise increase in both incidence and adjusted risk of liver and non-liver outcomes was observed across MASLD and sarcopenia strata. Within the coexistence group, the obesity (vs. non-obesity) subgroup generally had higher risks. For example, for cirrhosis, adjusted hazard ratios increased from 3.93 to 7.36 then 8.48 with MASLD alone, coexisting MASLD with low MS overall and coexisting MASLD, low MS and obesity, respectively. Similar findings were observed in external validation analyses using the 2011-2018 US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey cohort. Together, these observations inform risk stratification strategy and management of MASLD to include sarcopenia assessment.

title: A Rare Case Report of Type II Kounis Syndrome With Literature Review: Acute Anterior ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction Following Bee Sting.
authorString: Tarkiani S, Ghajar M, Fard MHS, Palangi MG, Bordbar A, Ahangar H, Ramezani A.
abstractText: Kounis syndrome (KS), also known as allergic angina, is a rare but serious condition defined by acute coronary syndrome occurring alongside a hypersensitivity reaction. We report the case of a 42-year-old male smoker who developed Type II KS after a hymenoptera sting. The patient came to the emergency department with a sudden decreased level of consciousness and retrosternal chest pain. Electrocardiography showed ST-segment elevation in the anterior leads, and coronary angiography revealed total proximal left anterior descending artery occlusion. Primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) was performed successfully. Echocardiography documented a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 35% with regional wall motion abnormalities, indicating significant myocardial injury. The patient was discharged with a treatment plan that included valsartan, spironolactone, bisoprolol, ticagrelor, acetylsalicylic acid, and atorvastatin. This case highlights the diagnostic and treatment challenges of KS and stresses the need for early recognition and a team-based approach to achieve better clinical results.

title: Quantification of NLRP3-caspase-1 complex assembly reveals a non-linear association with 30-day mortality in sepsis: a proof-of-concept pilot study.
authorString: Mehl F, Chedjou WJ, Witowski A, Rump K, Dyck B, Bergmann L, Putensen C, Henzler D, Adamzik M, Koos B, Thon P, Rahmel T.
abstractText:
Background

Direct, cell-resolved quantification of NLRP3 inflammasome activation in clinical patients has not been feasible. Previous studies have relied on indirect surrogates such as downstream cytokines, which are influenced by inflammasome-independent pathways and systemic clearance kinetics, potentially explaining the inconsistent prognostic findings reported in the literature. We applied a proximity ligation assay (PLA) to directly visualise NLRP3-caspase-1 complex formation in peripheral blood mononuclear cells of septic patients, providing a cell-specific, in situ readout of inflammasome assembly at the single-cell level.

Methods

In this prospective, multicentre proof-of-concept pilot study, 78 patients fulfilling Sepsis-3 criteria were enrolled across three university hospitals. The PLA was validated in THP-1-derived macrophages against established readouts of canonical inflammasome activation prior to clinical application. Patients were stratified into low (n = 28), intermediate (n = 23), and high (n = 27) NLRP3 inflammasome activity groups.

Results

Median age was 64 years (IQR: 56-78), 63% were male, and median Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score was 8 (IQR: 4-12). Baseline characteristics, disease severity scores, and routine inflammatory biomarkers did not differ across activity groups. Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed a non-linear pattern of 30-day survival, with the most favourable outcomes in the intermediate activity group. Both low and high activity were associated with increased mortality (log-rank p = 0.003). In adjusted Cox regression, low inflammasome activity (HR 7.88, 95% CI 1.79-34.65; p = 0.006) and high inflammasome activity (HR 4.35, 95% CI 1.01-19.88; p = 0.048) remained associated with 30-day mortality. Modelling PLA activity as a continuous variable using restricted cubic splines confirmed a significant non-linear association with 30-day mortality, independent of the tertile-based categorisation (p for non-linearity = 0.015).

Conclusions

This proof-of-concept pilot study demonstrates that direct in situ quantification of NLRP3-caspase-1 complex assembly is feasible in septic patients and reveals a non-linear association with 30-day survival. These findings indicate that PLA-based profiling captures immune heterogeneity beyond routine inflammatory biomarkers. Larger independent cohorts are needed to validate these findings before clinical application or patient stratification can be considered.

title: Retroperitoneal and Lateral Pelvic Lymph Node Dissection for Colorectal Cancer Metastases.
authorString: Olson KA, Maniskas SA, Marty M, Labadie K, Nguyen J, Zhumkhawala A, Lai LL, Fong Y, Kaiser AM.
abstractText:
Background

Colorectal cancer (CRC) metastases to retroperitoneal (RP) and lateral pelvic (LP) lymph nodes are functionally classified as stage IV disease. While metastasectomy is established for select hepatic and pulmonary metastases, the role of lymphadenectomy for nodal disease remains uncertain. This study evaluates the safety, indications, and oncologic outcomes of RP/LP lymph node dissection in CRC.

Methods

A single-center retrospective review identified patients undergoing RP or LP lymphadenectomy for CRC between 2011 and 2024. Patients with peritoneal metastases or incomplete data were excluded. Demographic, operative, and outcome data were analyzed. Associations with nodal positivity, recurrence-free survival (RFS), and overall survival (OS) were assessed using Fisher's exact test and univariate Cox regression.

Results

Forty-nine patients underwent lymphadenectomy, 45% for synchronous and 55% for metachronous nodal metastases. Dissection was selective in 61% and formal in 39%, with 86% undergoing concurrent major abdominal procedures. There was no perioperative mortality and dissection-specific morbidity was low (two lymphatic leaks, both after multivisceral resection). Pathologic nodal metastases were confirmed in 59% of cases. Median RFS and OS were 30.2 and 104.9 months, respectively. Node positivity was associated with initial N2 stage but did not affect RFS or OS. Formal lymphadenectomy was associated with shorter RFS, likely reflecting higher disease burden.

Conclusions

RP and LP lymphadenectomy can be safely performed, even with multivisceral resection. Pathologic nodal status did not predict survival, suggesting potential benefit to lymphadenectomy irrespective of final pathology. These findings support its use in carefully selected patients with controlled systemic disease and isolated nodal recurrence.

title: Electrical Storm in Advanced Chagas Cardiomyopathy Treated With Stereotactic Arrhythmia Radiotherapy After LVAD Implantation.
authorString: Bhagirath P, Antelo G, Pittorru R, Castel MA, Gonzalez ES, Cases C, Victor-Baldoma A, Pierucci N, Kukavica D, Romero Otero JM, Porta-Sanchez A, Roca-Luque I.
abstractText:
Background

Refractory ventricular tachycardia (VT) in advanced Chagas cardiomyopathy remains challenging after prior ablation and mechanical circulatory support.

Case summary

A 40-year-old man with advanced Chagas cardiomyopathy and prior endo-epicardial VT ablation developed electrical storm during influenza A infection and underwent left ventricular assist device implantation as a bridge to transplantation. Despite unloading, antiarrhythmic therapy, overdrive pacing, and stellate ganglion modulation, monomorphic VT persisted. Repeat ablation was unfavorable because of frailty and extensive residual lateral scar. Targeting for stereotactic arrhythmia radiotherapy (STAR) integrated late gadolinium enhancement cardiac magnetic resonance, clinical VT morphology, prior electroanatomic mapping, and planning computed tomography. A single 25-Gy fraction was delivered without acute complications. No sustained VT or implantable cardioverter-defibrillator shocks occurred during follow-up.

Discussion

Multimodality-guided STAR was feasible in this critically ill left ventricular assist device-supported patient. Although stabilization cannot be attributed to STAR alone, radiotherapy was delivered without observed acute radiotherapy- or device-related complications.

Take-home message

STAR may offer a noninvasive substrate-targeted option when repeat ablation is limited.

title: HADHA <sup>K406</sup> Lactylation Regulates Metabolic Reprogramming and Suppresses Immune Responses in Gastric Cancer.
authorString: Feng M, Jiao Q, Zhu J, Ren Y, Teng X, Su X, Li Z, Cai Y, Liu X, Wang Y, Zhang G.
abstractText: Gastric cancer (GC) represents a substantial global health challenge and is among the most prevalent and deadly malignancies worldwide. Emerging evidence suggests that protein lactylation plays a pivotal role in the progression of various cancers. However, the specific levels and regulatory mechanisms of protein lactylation in GC remain poorly understood. In this study, we detected elevated pan-lactylation modification levels in GC tissues. Notably, lactylation at the K406 site of hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase (HADHA) was significantly upregulated in GC tissues. This site-specific lactylation modification enhanced GC progression. Disrupting lactylation at the HADHA <sup>K406</sup> site markedly reduced its enzymatic activity, thereby mitigating GC progression by impairing fatty acid β-oxidation and glycolysis. Furthermore, inhibiting HADHA <sup>K406</sup> lactylation (HADHA K406la) suppressed the HMG-CoA reductase (HMGCR)-mediated cholesterol synthesis pathway, which, in turn, improved the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment in GC. Finally, combining an HMGCR inhibitor with a lactate dehydrogenase A (LDHA) inhibitor effectively enhanced the immune response against GC and inhibited tumor progression. In conclusion, this study demonstrated that HADHA K406la regulates GC progression through its impact on metabolic pathways, suggesting its potential as a therapeutic target for GC treatment.

title: Caregivers perspectives on multidisciplinary clinic visits for Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy.
authorString: Haynie C, Duvuru R, Akmyradov C, Boyd T, Wagner E, Schrader R, Stefans V, Willis E, Veerapandiyan A.
abstractText: BackgroundA multidisciplinary team (MDT) care model has been advocated for patients with Duchenne and Becker Muscular dystrophy (DBMD) to provide comprehensive care. We aimed to study the perspectives of parents and/or caregivers of individuals with DBMD on MDT clinic visits.MethodsA survey via non-personalized REDCap link was emailed to registered parents/caregivers through the Duchenne Registry provided by Parent Project Muscular Dystrophy (PPMD). The survey contained questions concerning individuals' demographics, and medical information, as well as knowledge and perspectives on MDT visits. Descriptive and association statistics were utilized.ResultsOf the 186 respondents, 166 cared for individuals with Duchenne and 20 for Becker. 117 of the respondents noted that their children receive care from one of the PPMD Certified Duchenne Care Centers. Average travel distance to the care site was 228.37 miles. 75% had their visits within 1 day, 19 % had 2 days visit, and 6% had more than 2 days. Majority (89%) preferred to have MDT appointments with all of their care providers at once and 89.4% commented that they had enough time with each of the providers. 77% noted that the duration of MDT visits was just right. 86.1% were satisfied with the care received from MDT visits. Participant comments underscored concerns regarding travel inconveniences, visit duration, standardization of care, and transition of care.DiscussionOur findings support continued implementation of MDT care and visits for individuals with DBMD, with an emphasis on optimizing visit efficiency and accommodating patients with complex medical needs.

title: Same-Day Discharge After Percutaneous Transaxillary Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Using Self-Expanding Valve.
authorString: Trivilou P, Stewart D, Reicher J, Edwards R, Alkhalil M.
abstractText:
Background

The safety of same-day discharge (SDD) following transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a well-established strategy in patients undergoing the transfemoral approach. The feasibility of SDD in patients undergoing transaxillary TAVI has not been reported.

Case summary

We present a 76-year-old male patient who underwent successful elective transaxillary TAVI. He had severe aortic stenosis, normal left ventricular function, and a background of diabetes, chronic liver disease, and right above-knee amputation. The access site was managed with 2 ProGlide devices with excellent hemostasis. There were no significant electrocardiogram changes postprocedure. Comprehensive postdischarge surveillance was provided, including a welfare telephone call on the following day.

Discussion

To our knowledge, this is the first case in the literature of SDD following transaxillary TAVI. Such a strategy requires appropriate patient selection, meticulous procedural planning, rigorous postdischarge monitoring strategy, and can only be considered in highly selected cases.

title: Echocardiographic Fusion Imaging to Guide LLAMACORN and Prevent Coronary Obstruction With Self-Expanding Valve-in-Valve TAVI.
authorString: Maaroufi A, Streukens SAF, Schreurs RHH, IJsselmuiden AJJ, Kats S, Timmers L, Akodad M, Vriesendorp PA.
abstractText:
Background

Coronary obstruction is a catastrophic complication of transcatheter valve-in-valve procedures, as the prosthesis frame can form a neo-skirt compromising coronary perfusion.

Case summary

A 79-year-old woman presented with a degenerated 23-mm balloon-expandable transcatheter valve, heart failure, and reduced left ventricular function. Computed tomography showed high-risk anatomy for right coronary obstruction: valve-to-right coronary artery distance 3.1 mm and valve-to-sinotubular junction distance 1.3 mm. Multimodality fusion imaging-guided electrosurgical leaflet modification using the leaflet laceration with balloon-mediated annihilation to prevent coronary obstruction with radiofrequency needle (LLAMACORN) technique, followed by implantation of a 26-mm self-expanding valve, achieved excellent hemodynamics and preserved coronary perfusion.

Discussion

This case shows how computed tomography planning and multimodality imaging enable safe management of complex transcatheter aortic valve-in-transcatheter aortic valve anatomies. When conventional coronary protection is not feasible, LLAMACORN leaflet modification offers a safe alternative to mitigate obstruction risk.

Take-home messages

Recognize anatomical predictors of coronary obstruction in transcatheter aortic valve-in-transcatheter aortic valve. Understand multimodality imaging's role in guiding leaflet modification. Describe LLAMACORN as a leaflet-modification strategy when a self-expanding valve is preferred.

title: Cation substitution and oxygen vacancies engineering in ZnNi<sub>0.1</sub>Co<sub>1.9</sub>O<sub>4</sub> spinel oxide for sensitive electrochemical detection of lead(ii) ions in environmental water and soil samples.
authorString: Lan Huong PT, Huong Mai VT, Huyen NN, Liem LT, Van Hoang O, Pham-Cong, Nhung PT, Phan VN, Dinh NX, Le AT.
abstractText: In this study, ZnNi<sub>0.1</sub>Co<sub>1.9</sub>O<sub>4</sub> spinel oxide structures were synthesized and used to modify screen-printed electrodes (SPEs) for sensitive Pb(ii) detection. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirmed that the Ni incorporation significantly modulates the electronic structure and enhance the electrical conductivity of ZnCo<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> structure, thereby accelerating interfacial electron transfer kinetics and improving Pb(ii) adsorption. Benefiting from oxygen vacancies and active redox pairs (Co<sup>2+</sup>/Co<sup>3+</sup>), the ternary ZnNi<sub>0.1</sub>Co<sub>1.9</sub>O<sub>4</sub> structure demonstrated excellent electrocatalytic performance towards Pb(ii) sensing. Under optimized conditions, the advanced ternary ZnNi<sub>0.1</sub>Co<sub>1.9</sub>O<sub>4</sub> spinel oxide-based electrochemical sensor achieved a low detection limit of 0.021 µg L<sup>-1</sup> and a wide linear range of 0.1-1000 µg L<sup>-1</sup> for Pb(ii) detection. Furthermore, the proposed electrochemical sensor also demonstrated excellent potential for the reliable determination of Pb(ii) in environmental water and soil samples. This study demonstrates that ternary ZnNi<sub>0.1</sub>Co<sub>1.9</sub>O<sub>4</sub> structure are promising spinel oxide electrode materials for high-performance electrochemical sensors, highlighting its potential for the rapid detection of heavy-metal ions in environmental water and soil matrices.

title: Disseminated Nocardiosis With Perimyocardial Involvement.
authorString: Jaamour D, Patel M, Horowitz JM, Al-Kazaz M, Cremer PC, Guenette A, Pastapur A, Catania R.
abstractText:
Background

Nocardia pseudobrasiliensis causes opportunistic infection in immunocompromised hosts. Cardiac involvement is rare and may mimic malignancy or inflammatory disease.

Case summary

A 44-year-old woman with prior liver and kidney transplantation on immunosuppressants presented with pleuritic chest pain, cough, and subcutaneous nodules. Electrocardiogram showed diffuse ST-segment elevation and PR depression. Cardiac magnetic-resonance imaging revealed a heterogeneously enhancing left ventricular apical and anterior septal mass with extension into the right ventricle, along with pericardial thickening, and chest computed tomography demonstrated cavitary pulmonary nodules and a periscapular abscess. Aspiration of the periscapular abscess confirmed disseminated nocardiosis. She was treated with intravenous imipenem and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole with a steroid taper, resulting in clinical and radiographic improvement.

Discussion

This case illustrates a rare infectious cause of a myocardial mass and perimyocarditis identified through multimodality imaging, highlighting the importance of maintaining a broad differential diagnosis in transplant recipients presenting with infectious symptoms.

Take-home message

Nocardiosis and infection with other atypical organisms should be considered in immunosuppressed patients with cardiac masses to elucidate etiology early and target antimicrobial therapy to improve patient outcomes.
