title: Quercetin and Cardiovascular Health: An Evidence-Based Review of Risk Factors and Treatments.
authorString: Khazdair MR, Jafari S, Shoghi M.
abstractText: Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) encompass a variety of conditions, including coronary heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, cerebrovascular disease, rheumatic heart disease, and venous thromboembolism. Natural products exhibit a range of pharmacological activities, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and immunoregulatory effects. This review evaluates the potential therapeutic effects of quercetin on factors contributing to cardiovascular disease risk. Quercetin, a flavonoid recognized for its strong antioxidant capabilities, has demonstrated beneficial effects in alleviating pathological cardiac conditions such as hypertrophy and ischemia across multiple in vitro and in vivo experimental models. This review compiles evidence demonstrating quercetin's ability to reduce cardiac hypertrophy and apoptosis in cardiomyocytes through modulation of key signaling pathways. Specifically, quercetin treatment resulted in significant upregulation of protective proteins such as silent information regulatory factor 1 (SIRT1), peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ coactivator-1α (PGC-1α), and Bcl-2, coupled with downregulation of pro-apoptotic Bax. Quercetin improved calcium channel function, enhanced myocardial contractility, and decreased oxidative stress markers, leading to improved survival rates of cardiomyocytes under ischemic conditions. Quercetin administration has been shown to lower systolic and diastolic blood pressure and reduce cardiac hypertrophy. Additionally, quercetin positively influences lipid profiles by decreasing total cholesterol, triglycerides, and low-density lipoprotein while enhancing overall lipid metabolism. Collectively, these findings highlight quercetin as a promising candidate in preclinical models of cardiac hypertrophy and ischemia. However, further research-particularly well-designed clinical trials-is essential to validate these findings and determine the translational potential through dietary interventions of quercetin in human cardiovascular health.

title: Nodal T Follicular Helper Cell Lymphoma With Epstein-Barr Virus-Positive Neoplastic T Cells Derived From Clonal Hematopoiesis.
authorString: Kishi D, Hiramoto N, Yamashita D, Maruoka H, Shiroishi Y, Nishikubo M, Shimomura Y, Yamamoto R, Nagai Y, Torii Y, Kimura H, Nannya Y, Ogawa S, Kondo T.
abstractText:
Introduction

Nodal T follicular helper cell lymphoma (nTFHL) with Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-positive neoplastic T cells is rare.

Methods

We report a woman with nTFHL and analyzed EBV-infected cells using an immunobead-based method and assessed somatic mutations in lymphoma and lymphoma-uninvolved bone marrow by targeted sequencing.

Results

EBV DNA was enriched in the CD4-positive fraction containing neoplastic T cells. Shared TET2 mutation was identified in both lymphoma and bone marrow, whereas additional TET2 and RHOA G17V mutations were restricted to the lymphoma.

Conclusion

These findings support a stepwise model of EBV-positive nTFHL arising from TET2-mutated clonal hematopoiesis with subsequent acquisition of a RHOA mutation.

Trial registration

The authors have confirmed clinical trial registration is not needed for this submission.

title: Evaluating the Association Between PPI Use and Dementia Risk Considering Methodological Choices: An Updated Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Ha H, Lee HW, Park JE, Ye BS, Yu YM, Ah YM.
abstractText: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), commonly prescribed for gastrointestinal disorders, have been investigated for their association with the risk of dementia. We aimed to assess the association between PPI use and dementia risk in older adults and examine the influence of methodological choices on this association. We conducted a meta-analysis of longitudinal observational studies, including subgroup analyses to address time-related biases and comparator selection. Relevant studies were systematically searched in the MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL databases from their inception to January 25, 2026. Twenty-three studies of older adults without dementia at baseline, reporting adjusted estimates for PPI users versus a comparator group, met the inclusion criteria. The pooled hazard ratio (HR) indicated a modest association between PPI use and dementia (HR = 1.18, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.02-1.37). Dementia risk did not differ significantly between PPI users and users of histamine-2 receptor antagonists (H2RAs) (HR = 1.04, 95% CI 0.89-1.20). In a post hoc analysis, H2RA use itself was associated with dementia (HR = 1.44, 95% CI 1.07-1.93), whereas excluding H2RA-treated patients strengthened the PPI estimate (HR = 1.75, 95% CI 1.38-2.22). Estimates also differed according to how time-related bias was handled: lag time, HR = 1.25, 95% CI 1.07-1.46; time-varying exposure, HR = 1.38, 95% CI 1.16-1.64. PPI use was modestly associated with incident dementia. However, the strength and specificity depended substantially on comparator selection and handling of time-related bias. Well-designed, long-term studies using active comparators are needed to clarify whether this effect is PPI-specific.

title: Renal vein thrombosis with inferior vena cava extension and pulmonary embolism in a patient with acute pyelonephritis: a case report and updated literature review.
authorString: Sutanto R, Koesbandono, Masui M, Octavius GS.
abstractText: Renal vein thrombosis (RVT) is a rare and underrecognized complication of acute pyelonephritis, with nephrotic syndrome and malignancy remaining the predominant causes of RVT. Because its clinical features overlap with those of the underlying infection, the diagnosis is often delayed until thrombus propagation or embolization occurs. A previously healthy 29-year-old man presented with a two-week history of left flank pain and fever. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated acute left pyelonephritis with extensive renal vein thrombosis extending into the suprarenal inferior vena cava. Despite initiation of anticoagulation, pulmonary embolism developed during hospitalization. Cultures did not identify a causative organism; a low-count Staphylococcus haemolyticus isolate was considered a contaminant. Thrombophilia screening was negative. The patient improved with antimicrobial therapy and anticoagulation alone, requiring no invasive intervention. A PubMed search identified 23 previously published cases of acute pyelonephritis-associated RVT, pooled with the present case (n = 24) and analyzed separately from five xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis-associated cases. Three cases were excluded for systemic or multifactorial thrombosis, and one case of RVT radiologically mimicking pyelonephritis. Gram-negative organisms predominated (78.3%), diabetes mellitus was present in fewer than half of patients, and outcomes were favorable with antimicrobial therapy and anticoagulation alone in most cases, while invasive interventions were reported selectively in cases with extensive thrombus burden or uncontrolled infection. RVT should be considered in patients with suspected pyelonephritis who deteriorate despite appropriate therapy or present with atypical clinical or imaging features. In cases where infection and RVT coexist, the temporal relationship and causality may remain uncertain, and diagnosis and management should be individualized according to the clinical presentation, thrombus extent, severity of infection, and imaging findings.

title: Photoacoustic phase and intensity dual-modality imaging for characterization of plaque viscoelasticity and lipid composition: a feasibility study.
authorString: Liang Y, Tan Y, Jiang A, Zhang H, Wang P.
abstractText:
Significance

Rupture of atherosclerotic plaque is the most important cause of sudden death in acute myocardial infarction. Plaque stability is closely related to mechanical characters and histological composition. A dual-modality technique, combining photoacoustic phase imaging (PPI) and intensity imaging (PAI), was developed providing viscoelasticity and lipid component of plaques simultaneously.

Aim

We aimed to investigate the feasibility of PPI to identify thin-cap fibrous plaques by detecting viscosity-elasticity ratio (VER), to further examine the correlation between VER and the major components of plaque, and ultimately to verify the accuracy of PPI-PAI in assessing plaque types.

Approach

PPI-PAI experiments were performed on the aortas of 18 Apolipoprotein E-knockout (ApoE) mice fed with high-fat/high-cholesterol diet. After each experiment, the plaques at the target sites were stained with Oil Red O, Masson, and F4/80 staining to verify the accuracy of the imaging and to further investigate the correlations between VER and lipid core area, fibrous cap thickness, and macrophage content. Finally, conventional statistical methods, such as linear analysis, were used to summarize the experimental data and draw general conclusions.

Results

PPI enables quantitative VER detection of plaques, with thin-cap fibrous plaques exhibiting the highest VER ( 3.77×10-5∼4.68×10-5  s ). There is a high positive correlation between VER and lipid cross-section area ( R2=0.81 , p<0.0001 ) and macrophage content ( R2=0.75 , p<0.0001 ) in lipid plaque lesions. Likewise, in fibrous plaques, a strong negative correlation ( R2=0.71 , p<0.0001 ) is demonstrated between VER and fibrous cap thickness; and a high positive correlation ( R2=0.12 , p=0.02 ) between VER and macrophage content. As lipid plaques and thick-cap fibrous plaques may have the same VER values, the combination of PPI and PAI can effectively identify plaque types.

Conclusions

PPI facilitates the characterization of thin-cap fibrous plaques by VER measurements, and further combination with PAI can improve the detection rate of distinct plaque types.

title: Right Atrial Repair of Basal Ventricular Septal Rupture with Long-Term Follow-Up: A Case Report.
authorString: Yoshikai M, Sato H, Hayashi N.
abstractText:
Introduction

Ventricular septal rupture (VSR) remains a life-threatening mechanical complication of acute myocardial infarction. Basal VSR is particularly challenging because of its deep location and close proximity to the atrioventricular valves. We report a case of successful repair of basal VSR through a right atrial approach using a double-patch sandwich technique.

Case presentation

An 88-year-old woman developed an 18-mm basal VSR following inferior myocardial infarction despite successful percutaneous coronary intervention. Mechanical circulatory support with an Impella CP (Abiomed, Danvers, MA, USA) was instituted; however, worsening pulmonary congestion and device-related hemolysis necessitated surgical intervention. Through a right atriotomy, the defect was directly exposed. After debridement of necrotic tissue, full-thickness sutures were placed through the ventricular septum, and the defect was closed using bovine pericardial patches on both the left and right ventricular aspects. Because the subvalvular apparatus of the septal leaflet was incorporated into the repair, concomitant tricuspid valve replacement was performed. Postoperative echocardiography demonstrated complete closure of the defect without residual shunt or deterioration of mitral valve function. The patient was discharged 7 weeks after surgery and remains free from recurrent heart failure, with no evidence of residual shunt at 5.5 years postoperatively.

Conclusions

The right atrial approach combined with a double-patch sandwich technique provides excellent exposure of basal VSR and facilitates secure closure while avoiding ventriculotomy. This technique may represent a useful surgical option for selected patients with basal VSR.

title: Why does apical periodontitis persist? A shotgun metagenomic survey of the microbial community in primary and persistent periapical granulomas.
authorString: Shen Y, Yang Y, Sun J, Han Z, Sun Y, Li R, Zhang Y, Yu Y.
abstractText:
Objective

This cross‑sectional observational study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare the microbiomes of periapical granulomas from primary and persistent apical periodontitis to identify microbial taxa and functional pathways associated with persistent lesions.

Methods

Seventeen patients with untreated primary apical periodontitis (UA), 19 with persistent apical periodontitis (PA), and 19 healthy gingival reference samples (HC) were enrolled. Periapical granuloma and healthy gingival samples were collected during tooth extraction for whole-metagenome shotgun sequencing. Alpha diversity was assessed by the Shannon and Chao1 indices. Beta-diversity was evaluated using PERMANOVA based on Bray‑Curtis distances. Differential abundance analysis of species and predicted functional pathways between UA and PA was performed using the Mann‒Whitney U test with Benjamini‒Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Clinical associations were examined using Spearman's correlation. The HC group served as a descriptive reference.

Results

Alpha diversity showed a significant difference in species richness (Chao1, p < 0.05) but not overall diversity (Shannon, p > 0.05). Beta diversity revealed a trend toward separation but did not reach statistical significance (PERMANOVA, R2  = 0.05085, p = 0.051). Metagenomic sequencing revealed differences in species composition and functional potential between UA and PA. Taxonomic profiling identified 503 species in UA versus 255 in PA. At the species level, several taxa showed nominal differences between UA and PA (p < 0.05), but none remained significant after FDR correction (q > 0.05). Functionally, several KEGG pathways showed nominal differences between UA and PA (p < 0.05, q > 0.05), with the top three pathways all below 3% relative abundance. Swelling duration correlated negatively with several taxa and pathways (p < 0.05), while lesion diameter showed little association with microbial abundance.

Conclusions

Persistent apical periodontitis granulomas showed lower species richness and abundance, but similar predicted functional capacity, compared with primary infections. Further longitudinal and multi‑omics studies are needed to investigate the associations.

title: Comprehensive Echocardiographic Assessment of Right Ventricular Afterload and Right Ventricular-Pulmonary Arterial Coupling in the Intensive Care Unit.
authorString: Mirrakhimov AE.
abstractText: Right ventricular (RV) dysfunction is common in critical illness, yet RV afterload cannot be adequately characterized by pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP) alone. Bedside echocardiography can estimate right atrial and pulmonary artery pressures, suggest increased pulmonary vascular resistance, and assess RV-pulmonary arterial coupling while simultaneously evaluating RV size, systolic function, septal interaction, and forward flow. Peak tricuspid regurgitation velocity combined with right atrial pressure estimates RV systolic pressure and, in the absence of outflow obstruction, approximates PASP. Pulmonary regurgitation velocities provide complementary estimates of mean and end-diastolic pulmonary artery pressure, whereas pulmonary artery acceleration time, RV outflow tract velocity-time integral, and systolic notching provide information regarding pulmonary vascular load and forward flow. A multiparametric assessment of RV systolic performance is essential because tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion, tissue Doppler systolic velocity, fractional area change, RV free-wall strain, and three-dimensional RV ejection fraction assess different aspects of contraction. The tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion/PASP ratio relates longitudinal systolic performance to pulmonary pressure but remains a surrogate of coupling, without a universal intensive care threshold. These measurements depend on image quality, loading conditions, and ventilatory support and may differ substantially from invasive hemodynamics in individual patients. Their greatest value lies in integrated physiologic assessment and serial reassessment after treatment. Echocardiography complements right heart catheterization, which remains necessary when precise hemodynamic classification or measurement of pulmonary artery wedge pressure, cardiac output, or pulmonary vascular resistance will change management.

title: External validation of multitask deep learning for carotid plaque detection: anatomical auxiliary tasks shape performance trade-offs.
authorString: Shi H, Lai Z, Shen F, Du P, He H.
abstractText:
Purpose

Carotid plaque screening using ultrasound is challenged by class imbalance and ambiguous lesion boundaries. However, how different anatomical auxiliary tasks influence carotid plaque detection performance and clinical operating characteristics remains insufficiently investigated. We aimed to externally evaluate multitask deep learning models with different anatomical auxiliary tasks and investigate their effects on clinical performance profiles.

Methods

We developed a multitask network incorporating three anatomical auxiliary segmentation targets (vessel lumen, intima-media thickness (IMT), and plaque), together with a classification-only baseline. The model was developed on 1297 images from 262 patients and evaluated on an external cohort of 1091 images from 263 patients. To ensure fair comparison, we froze the encoder of each variant and retrained an identical classification head on the internal training set, and then applied a fixed threshold determined via Youden index maximization for each model on the internal validation set to the external cohort.

Results

In external validation (263 patients, 94 plaque-positive), all multitask models outperformed the classification-only baseline (AUC 0.615, p < 0.0001), while showing comparable AUCs among themselves (lumen-guided 0.852, IMT-guided 0.853, plaque-guided 0.858; all p > 0.76). Despite comparable discrimination, they exhibited distinct clinical profiles: the IMT-guided model achieved the highest sensitivity (SEN 0.830), the lumen-guided model achieved the highest specificity (SPE 0.864), and the plaque-guided model offered more balanced performance (SEN 0.723, SPE 0.822). Radiofrequency balloon ablation significantly reduced external AUC for the lumen-guided (0.852 vs 0.790; p=0.0145) and plaque-guided (0.858 vs 0.796; p=0.0091) models, but not for the IMT-guided model (p=0.2171), indicating task-dependent effects.

Conclusion

The choice of auxiliary task does not confer universal superiority in discrimination but instead determines the model's clinical orientation, allowing task-specific adaptation to different screening or confirmatory scenarios.

title: FOSL1-associated condensates modulate superenhancer-mediated selected IL-1 family gene activation in psoriasis.
authorString: Qiu Y, Sun K, Yu Y, Hou H, Wu R, Lu Q, Zhao M.
abstractText: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease involving abnormal keratinocyte gene expression, yet the upstream epigenetic mechanisms driving these alterations remain unclear. Here we performed multiomics analyses (chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing, CUT&Tag, ATAC-seq, and RNA sequencing) on psoriatic lesions, perilesional skin, healthy skin, and M5-stimulated HaCaT cells. Functional validation was performed using CRISPR-mediated superenhancer (SE) editing, epigenetic modulation, circular chromosome conformation capture sequencing, assay for chromatin-bound condensates by exploratory sequencing, coimmunoprecipitation, and fluorescence recovery after photobleaching. We found widespread activation of enhancers and SEs in lesions, including an interleukin 1 (IL-1)-SE regulating IL1A, IL1B, and IL36G transcription. BET inhibition reduced SE activity, repressed IL-1 cytokines, and relieved psoriasis-like inflammation in vivo. Fos-like antigen 1 (FOSL1) was identified as a key transcription factor enriched in active SEs and associated with condensate formation, contributing to the maintenance of EP300 occupancy and histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation deposition. Macrophage-derived IL-1 up-regulated FOSL1 through mitogen-activated protein kinase/ERK signaling, forming a positive feedback loop that amplified inflammation. This study revealed an FOSL1-SE-centered regulatory network driving keratinocyte inflammatory responses, providing previously unknown therapeutic targets for psoriasis.

title: Elucidating the toxicogenomic mechanisms of DBP exposure on Hepatocellular carcinoma through network toxicology and molecular docking analysis.
authorString: Dai D, Yang N, Liu F, Chen X.
abstractText:
Backgroud

This study explored the molecular mechanisms by which dibutyl phthalate (DBP) contributes to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) pathogenesis using integrated network toxicology and bioinformatics.

Methods

DBP's carcinogenic potential was evaluated with ADMETLAB 3.0 and ProTox3. DBP-related targets were obtained from ChEMBL, SwissTargetPrediction, and PharmMapper; HCC-related targets from GeneCards and OMIM. Overlapping genes were identified by Venn analysis. A protein-protein interaction (PPI) network was constructed using STRING and analyzed with Cytoscape to identify hub genes. Functional enrichment analysis (GO/KEGG) was performed with DAVID. Expression validation and survival analysis used TCGA-LIHC and GEO (GSE39791) data. A prognostic nomogram integrating gene expression and clinical variables was developed. Single-cell RNA sequencing (GSE299340) was analyzed with Seurat to examine hub gene expression. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations investigated DBP interactions with core targets.

Results

A total of 242 overlapping genes between DBP-associated and HCC-associated targets were identified. PPI network analysis revealed seven hub genes: KRAS, GRB2, ESR1, HSP90AA1, SRC, EGFR, and TP53. Enrichment analysis indicated significant involvement in cancer-related pathways. Expression analysis in TCGA and GEO datasets confirmed significant dysregulation of GRB2, ESR1, HSP90AA1, and SRC in HCC tissues, which correlated with patient survival outcomes. The prognostic model incorporating these genes showed good predictive accuracy. Single-cell analysis indicated distinct expression patterns of ESR1 (hepatocytes) and HSP90AA1 (immune cells) in HCC. Molecular docking demonstrated stable binding of DBP to ESR1 and HSP90AA1 with favorable binding energies (-6.8 and -6.1 kcal/mol, respectively). Molecular dynamics simulations supported the stability of these complexes, with van der Waals interactions being the primary binding force.

Conclusions

This integrative analysis suggests that DBP exposure may contribute to HCC pathogenesis by modulating core genes and pathways, although these findings are associative and require experimental confirmation. Hub genes, especially ESR1 and HSP90AA1, are potential biomarkers and targets. Direct DBP-protein interactions provide mechanistic insights into HCC etiology.

title: DUSP26 Regulated by YY1 Lactylation Couples Osteogenesis and Angiogenesis by Dephosphorylating PMPCB at Y141 and Activating Mitophagy in BMSCs.
authorString: Lv Y, Wu F, Liang X, Liu C, Guo W, Zhang K, Niu J, Jiang W, Xu H, Jiang A, Zheng Y, Yu E, Wang X, Yan J, Xia J, Song C.
abstractText: Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) support bone formation through osteogenic differentiation and pro-angiogenic paracrine activity, but the mechanisms coordinating these functions remain incompletely understood. Here, we identified dual-specificity phosphatase 26 (DUSP26) as a regulator of BMSC osteogenesis and mitochondrial homeostasis. DUSP26 expression increased during osteogenic differentiation and was reduced in osteoporotic femoral tissues. p300 gain- and loss-of-function experiments, together with analysis of the Yin Yang1(YY1) K183R mutant, supported the conclusion that p300-regulated YY1 lactylation contributes to DUSP26 transcriptional activation. DUSP26 interacted with the mitochondrial processing peptidase subunit beta(PMPCB) and reduced its tyrosine phosphorylation, with mass spectrometry and mutational analyses implicating Y141 as involved in this regulation. Functional assays supported a model in which DUSP26 limits mitochondrial processing peptidase (MPP)-mediated PTEN-induced kinase 1 (PINK1) processing and promotes PINK1-dependent mitophagy, thereby supporting mitochondrial homeostasis. DUSP26 enhanced osteogenic differentiation and the pro-angiogenic activity of BMSC-conditioned medium(CM), whereas its knockdown impaired bone formation and reduced type H vessels in vivo. Furthermore, BMSC-derived exosomes carrying a runt-related transcription factor 2 (RUNX2) promoter-driven DUSP26 plasmid produced preferential transgene expression in osteogenic-lineage cells and attenuated ovariectomy-induced bone loss in mice. These findings link lactylation-associated transcriptional regulation to mitochondrial protein processing and support further preclinical evaluation of DUSP26-directed approaches for osteoporosis.

title: Effects of segment chemistry on mechanical performance and hemocompatibility in polyurethane heart valve scaffolds.
authorString: Sadeghi F, Zamani Y, Tacklind M, Edwards R, Simionescu D, Kheradvar A.
abstractText: Polycarbonate-based and polysiloxane-modified thermoplastic polyurethanes (TPUs) are promising candidates for cardiovascular implants because of their tunable mechanical properties and favorable biocompatibility. In this study, we established comparative formulation-property-hemocompatibility criteria for polymeric heart valve scaffolds through a systematic evaluation of five commercial TPU formulations: carbothane AC-4095A (CB95-AC), carbothane AC-4075A (CB75-AC), carbothane PC-3575A (CB75-PC), chronoflex C65D (CF), and quadrasil ARCS 90A (Qsil). This comparative analysis provides practical material-selection criteria based on the balance between elastic recovery, tear resistance, oxidative stability, and hemocompatibility. CF and CB95-AC exhibited the highest stiffness and tensile strength, whereas CB75-AC and CB75-PC demonstrated greater elasticity and lower residual strain during cyclic loading. CB75-AC exhibited the lowest hysteresis and best elastic recovery; however, it also exhibited low tear resistance and slightly elevated hemolysis (∼4%), highlighting the tradeoff between elastic recovery and mechanical robustness. All TPU materials maintained platelet counts and partial thromboplastin time values within ASTM-defined acceptable ranges. FTIR analysis revealed formulation-dependent differences in urethane carbonyl hydrogen bonding and hard-domain association that were associated with differences in mechanical behavior and surface characteristics. DSC revealed formulation-dependent differences in thermal transitions, whereas WAXD showed broadly similar, predominantly amorphous structures with diffuse scattering centered at approximately 20-21° 2θ and no distinct crystalline reflections. Preliminary short-term implantation of a CB95-AC polymeric mitral valve in an ovine model showed no gross thrombotic attachment on the leaflet surfaces after 22 days. Overall, the results demonstrate formulation-dependent tradeoffs among elastic recovery, tear resistance, oxidative stability, and hemocompatibility in TPU-based heart valve scaffolds. These findings provide practical material-selection criteria for future polymeric heart valve scaffold development.

title: A Fatal Case of Pulmonary Tumor Thrombotic Microangiopathy Originating From Primary Bladder Adenocarcinoma.
authorString: Kodani H, Sekii Y, Inoguchi Y, Tomiyama E, Takayama H, Yasuhara Y.
abstractText:
Introduction

Pulmonary tumor thrombotic microangiopathy is a rare, fatal complication of malignancy, with few reports involving bladder cancer.

Case presentation

An 81-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease presented with hematuria and progressive exertional dyspnea. Imaging showed an invasive bladder tumor with lymph node metastases. Echocardiography suggested pulmonary hypertension, although invasive confirmation was unavailable. Recurrent perioperative oxygen desaturation preceded fatal deterioration 2 days after transurethral resection. Autopsy revealed primary bladder adenocarcinoma, signet ring cell subtype, and microscopic pulmonary tumor emboli with fibrin thrombi, fibrous intimal thickening, and recanalization. These findings supported pulmonary tumor thrombotic microangiopathy. Distinct gastrointestinal tumors and matching bladder and metastatic morphology supported a bladder origin.

Conclusion

Pulmonary tumor thrombotic microangiopathy should be considered in patients with bladder tumors and progressive dyspnea. Recurrent desaturation and right heart abnormalities warrant reassessment despite preserved oxygen saturation. Autopsy vascular findings were essential to distinguish this condition from simple pulmonary tumor embolism.

title: Red Light Therapy and Mitochondrial Rejuvenation in Age-Related Disorders.
authorString: Iglewska M, Flis KA, Kołakowska M, Hryniewicz WW, Pluto-Prądzyńska A.
abstractText: Aging is associated with mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired ATP production, and a decline in tissue regenerative capacity, leading to the development of age-related diseases. This review summarizes current evidence regarding the effects of photobiomodulation (PBM) on mitochondrial function and age-related disorders. PBM using red and near-infrared light may enhance proper mitochondrial function by acting on cytochrome c oxidase (CCO) and other signaling pathways, including the transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) channel, leading to increased ATP production, modulation of ROS signaling, and improved cellular homeostasis. We review in vitro, animal, and clinical studies investigating PBM in metabolic, neurodegenerative, hepatic, cardiovascular, age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and skeletal muscle disorders associated with aging, as well as its application in the management of cancer therapy-related oral mucositis. Current studies demonstrate beneficial effects on glucose metabolism, cardiovascular function, neuronal function, lipid metabolism, liver function, muscle regeneration, and visual function in AMD, as well as the safety and efficacy of PBM in the management of cancer therapy-induced oral mucositis. The therapeutic effects of PBM appear to be dose-dependent and influenced by treatment parameters including wavelength, fluence, irradiance, and exposure protocol. Although photobiomodulation still lacks standardized treatment protocols and differences exist in the wavelengths used, dosage, and frequency among studies, it represents a promising therapeutic approach for the treatment of age-related diseases.

title: Malignant Perivascular Epithelioid Cell Tumor Originating from the Transverse Mesocolon.
authorString: Yokota R, Ohta R, Takeda K, Sekiguchi K, Shimizu T, Motoda N, Taniai N, Matsuda A.
abstractText:
Introduction

Perivascular epithelioid cell tumors (PEComas) are rare mesenchymal neoplasms with melanocytic and smooth muscle differentiation. Primary mesenteric PEComas are exceptionally uncommon and usually cannot be diagnosed from imaging alone. We report a case of malignant PEComa arising from the transverse mesocolon.

Case presentation

A 34-year-old woman was referred to our department after abdominal ultrasonography showed a large intra-abdominal mass. Contrast-enhanced CT revealed a 15-cm heterogeneous, hypervascular mesenteric tumor with internal necrosis and feeding vessels from the superior mesenteric artery. MRI showed no continuity with the uterus or ovaries. Because percutaneous biopsy was considered to carry a substantial risk of bleeding and dissemination, the tumor was resected for diagnosis and treatment. Laparotomy demonstrated a transverse-mesocolic tumor directly invading the transverse colon; transverse colectomy with en bloc tumor resection was performed. Histopathological evaluation showed pleomorphic epithelioid cells, marked nuclear atypia, coagulative necrosis, vascular invasion, and frequent mitoses. The tumor was positive for HMB-45, Melan-A, and smooth muscle actin and negative for TFE3, supporting malignant PEComa. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient remained free of recurrence 4 months after surgery.

Conclusions

Malignant PEComa of the transverse mesocolon is extremely rare. This tumor should be considered among large, hypervascular mesenteric tumors, although imaging is not specific. Complete resection with negative margins is the principal treatment for localized disease. High-risk pathological features justify prolonged cross-sectional imaging surveillance and multidisciplinary, molecularly informed management if recurrence develops.

title: Multi-omics, multi-tissue analysis reveal role of extracellular matrix remodeling and sphingolipid homeostasis in edematous malnutrition (kwashiorkor).
authorString: Nackers F, Polnay K, Almey R, Daled S, Djibo AD, Saeger S, Deforce D, Dhaenens M, Gansemans Y, Glorieux G, Guindo O, Jenkins B, Koulman A, Lang HJ, Langendorf C, Laukens D, Mambula C, Mukagatare I, Parkington D, Tassiou EI, Biesen WV, De Wiele TV, Massenhove JV, Nieuwerburgh FV, Adehossi I, Briend A, Gonzales GB.
abstractText:
Background

Edematous malnutrition, aka kwashiorkor, is a phenotype of severe malnutrition whose pathophysiology remains poorly understood.

Methods

In this case-control study, we employed plasma lipidomics, metabolomics, and proteomics, urine metabolomics and gut microbiome profiling to delineate molecular features specific to kwashiorkor in 60 children aged 6-59 months from Niger compared to marasmus (n = 60) and non-malnourished children (NAM) (n = 60) matched by age, sex, and clinical triage score. Features were defined as kwashiorkor-specific if they also correlated with edema severity and normalized following nutritional rehabilitation.

Results

We identified a plasma proteomic factor featuring lumican, gelsolin, and tetranectin and a lipidomic factor enriched in sphingolipids. Both differed in kwashiorkor compared to marasmus and NAM, were associated with edema grade, and trended towards normalcy after nutritional treatment, which are consistent with ECM remodeling and sphingolipid dysregulation. In contrast, neither (plasma and urine) metabolomic profiles nor gut microbiome composition showed kwashiorkor-specific signatures, although our urine and gut microbiome analyses may be underpowered.

Conclusion

These findings advance understanding of kwashiorkor pathophysiology beyond nutrient deficiency and highlight ECM and sphingolipid features associated with its distinct clinical and molecular characteristics compared to marasmus.

title: Organ size in small infants (The OSSI Study): are sonographic reference intervals applicable in preterm infants small for gestational age?
authorString: Klischke L, Renz DM, Müller T, Brodowski L, Franke D, Rahn A.
abstractText:
Sonographic reference intervals for liver, spleen, and kidney size in preterm infants below 40 cm body length were recently established in an appropriately grown (AGA) neonatal cohort. Whether these intervals apply to infants born small for gestational age (SGA) remains unexamined. In this cross-sectional study, 20 preterm SGA infants below 40 cm body length (mean gestational age 29 1/7 weeks, median birth weight 695 g) underwent standardized abdominal ultrasound, measuring craniocaudal liver length in three planes, splenic length, and renal volume. Measurements were compared with published reference intervals, and z-scores assessed systematic deviation. Weight and length at examination were comparable between the SGA and AGA cohorts. The mean z-score was significantly below zero only for liver length in the midclavicular line (- 0.79, p = 0.014). The proportion of infants outside the reference interval exceeded the expected 5% for liver length in the midclavicular line (25%, p = 0.003) and anterior axillary line (20%, p = 0.016) and for spleen length (20%, p = 0.016), but rested on 4 to 5 infants each, and several values lay within 1 mm of the limit. Kidney measurements did not differ from the reference. Organ size correlated most strongly with body weight, and the deviations persisted at equal weight (post hoc).

Conclusion

Abdominal organ dimensions in SGA preterm infants frequently fall outside AGA-derived reference intervals, particularly for liver and spleen size, suggesting that these intervals cannot be reliably applied to this population. Prospective studies establishing reference values for SGA infants are warranted.

What is known

• Sonographic reference intervals for abdominal organ size in preterm infants below 40 cm exist only for appropriately grown (AGA) infants; their applicability to infants small for gestational age (SGA) has not been examined.

What is new

• In 20 preterm SGA infants, the mean z-score for liver length (midclavicular line) was below the AGA reference, and liver and spleen lengths fell outside the intervals more often than the expected 5% (exploratory). • AGA intervals should not be assumed to apply to SGA infants.

title: Endoscopic hemostasis using a narrow-caliber endoscope for a bleeding duodenal ulcer in a 7-month-old infant: A case report.
authorString: Hayashi S, Yamazaki K, Tanaka H, Yamashita K, Ozawa N, Shimizu S, Shimizu M.
abstractText: Duodenal ulcers are rare in infants, and their endoscopic management is challenging because of anatomical factors and limited availability of hemostatic devices compatible with narrow-caliber endoscopes. Here, we present the case of a 7-month-old female infant who developed upper gastrointestinal bleeding 9 days post-cardiac surgery while receiving aspirin therapy. Emergency esophagogastroduodenoscopy revealed a bleeding duodenal ulcer with an exposed vessel. Because of the inability to advance a standard-diameter endoscope, a narrow-caliber endoscope was used. Hemostasis was achieved using scissors-type hemostatic forceps with soft coagulation. The patient recovered without bleeding recurrence. This case highlights the importance of individualized endoscopic strategies in infants and urgent need for therapeutic devices that are compatible with narrow-caliber pediatric endoscopes.

title: Geographic proximity to Down syndrome specialty clinics for individuals born with Down syndrome, 1999-2020 in Texas.
authorString: Gandhi HA, Betancourt D, Shumate C, Allred R, Dixon A, Kilburn M, Singletary C, Riconda D, Agopian AJ.
abstractText:
Background

While effective national clinic networks exist for a select few conditions, the availability and use of multidisciplinary specialty care for most genetic or congenital conditions, including Down syndrome (DS), remain uneven. This uneven distribution creates significant geographic and social gradients in healthcare access. To understand these differences within a geographically expansive and socio-demographically diverse setting, this study quantified travel burden to pediatric DS specialty clinics in Texas, identifying differences based on key maternal socio-demographic and geographic factors.

Methods

A cross-sectional analysis of 8,201 individuals with DS presumed living and 477 deceased individuals with DS born between 1999-2020 from the Texas Birth Defects Registry was performed. One-way driving time and distance along the road networks from the maternal residence to the nearest seven pediatric DS specialty clinics were calculated using ArcGIS Pro. Travel burden was analyzed by maternal race/ethnicity, education, age and residence at delivery. Travel burden measures were categorized as low, moderate to high, and very high.

Results

Among 8,678 live‑born individuals with DS, 45% resided over 90 miles from the closest in-state DS specialty clinic, and 41% faced one‑way driving times exceeding two hours. Those born to mothers in border counties experienced the greatest travel burden, with median one-way driving times exceeding 7 hours. Rural residents had a four times greater travel burden than urban residents. Individuals born to Hispanic mothers traveled twice as far as those born to non-Hispanic mothers. Residents of high‑poverty tracts had a median one-way distance of approximately 150 miles, triple the 35 miles seen in low‑poverty tracts.

Conclusion

Our findings suggest that substantial travel burden to DS specialty clinics exists in Texas, affecting individuals with DS born to Hispanic and younger mothers, as well as those in rural, border, and concentrated-poverty regions. Further research is needed to explore life course residential history and clinic utilization to address these differences.

title: Endovascular management of acute and chronic arterial mesenteric ischaemia: A narrative review of evidence informing interventional radiology treatment

Data-driven reweighting of the Charlson and Elixhauser comorbidity indices using German claims data: development for in-hospital mortality only, external validation across clinical and health-economic outcomes.
authorString: Kaier K, Hazard D, Heidenreich A, Maier A, Westermann D, von Zur Mühlen C, Oettinger V.
abstractText:
Background

Comorbidity scores such as the Charlson and Elixhauser indices are widely used for risk adjustment in health-economic and clinical outcomes research. Yet the existing weighting schemes, originally designed for mortality prediction, may no longer reflect today's patient populations or perform equally well across diverse outcomes. This study aimed to reweight both indices using a data-driven approach and to evaluate their predictive validity for multiple clinical and health-economic outcomes.

Methods

Using administrative data from a large tertiary care teaching hospital in Germany (N = 198,819 hospitalizations), we applied adaptive lasso regression to recalibrate the Charlson (Deyo weights) and Elixhauser (van Walraven weights) comorbidity indices. Reweighting was performed for in-hospital mortality as the development endpoint. Penalized coefficients were converted into integer-based weights. Model performance was assessed for three dichotomous endpoints (in-hospital mortality, severe bleeding, prolonged mechanical ventilation) and two continuous outcomes (length of hospital stay, total reimbursement). External validation was performed in three independent cohorts: Elective endometrial cancer (N = 85,204), interventional left atrial appendage closure (N = 28,039), and emergency ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI; N = 248,062). AUC, R², and RMSE were used as complementary measures of discrimination and predictive accuracy. Pooled relative improvements of AUC, R², and RMSE across the three validation cohorts was calculated using random effects meta-analyses.

Results

Reweighting consistently improved predictive performance across endpoints and cohorts, with modest absolute gains for in-hospital mortality and more pronounced gains for severe bleeding and continuous outcomes. When analysing in-hospital mortality in the three validation cohorts, the reweighted Charlson improved AUC from 0.679 to 0.714 in left atrial appendage closure, 0.588 to 0.594 in STEMI, and 0.798 to 0.810 in endometrial cancer (pooled relative increase: 2.05% [95% CI 0.56-3.53]); the reweighted Elixhauser showed larger gains, particularly in STEMI (0.708 to 0.766) and left atrial appendage closure (0.780 to 0.818; pooled relative increase: 4.86% [0.07-9.65]). The Elixhauser reweighting demonstrated consistently larger gains for severe bleeding (pooled AUC increase: 6.57% [4.23-8.92]). For continuous outcomes, the reweighted Elixhauser index yielded the largest gains in explained variance, with a pooled relative R² increase of 39.66% [33.72-45.60] for total reimbursement. Corresponding reductions in RMSE were modest and often not statistically significant.

Conclusions

Adaptive lasso reweighting consistently enhances the predictive validity of the Charlson and Elixhauser indices across both clinical and health-economic endpoints. Our multi-endpoint evaluation shows consistent performance gains across the three examined German validation cohorts, offering a practical basis for risk adjustment in health-economic studies using German claims data. Because development and validation were based exclusively on German data and a single coding system (ICD-10-GM), international validation across other coding systems and healthcare systems is required before broader applicability can be assumed.

title: The role of microbial enzymes in intervention strategies for metabolic diseases targeting the gut microbiota.
authorString: Gao Y, Gao X, Wang K, Qiao J, Jiang C.
abstractText: Metabolic diseases-including obesity, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), atherosclerosis (AS), and polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)-pose a significant global health crisis due to their rapidly increasing prevalence. The therapeutic potential of the gut microbiota and its metabolites is gaining recognition, with microbial enzymes playing a pivotal role. These enzymes catabolize dietary fibers into mono- and oligo-saccharides, ultimately yielding beneficial short-chain fatty acids, while concurrently converting phytochemicals into absorbable, bioactive small molecules. An increasing array of small-molecule agonists and inhibitors has been developed to target microbial pathways, such as bile acid metabolism and trimethylamine formation. Furthermore, engineered bacteria and fecal microbiota transplantation are gaining traction as promising therapeutic strategies. This review synthesizes evidence on how microbial enzymes underpin these diverse interventions, aiming to advance the development of microbial enzyme-based management strategies for metabolic diseases.

title: Anaesthetic Considerations for Twin Delivery in a Patient With Osteogenesis Imperfecta Type III: A Case Report.
authorString: Eapen SE, Jong BBT, Loh LWW.
abstractText: Osteogenesis imperfecta is an uncommon, inherited connective tissue disease, which is rare in pregnancy and presents multiple challenges to perinatal and anaesthetic care. Caesarean section in these patients is complex, often performed preterm and demands careful coordination between multiple disciplines. A 27-year-old woman at 26 weeks' gestation of a spontaneous twin pregnancy presented for elective caesarean section for worsening respiratory failure. General anaesthesia with total intravenous anaesthesia was used in view of anticipated prolonged surgery and difficult regional anaesthesia. The delivery was largely uneventful, and the patient recovered without major complications. The twins experienced multiple complications of prematurity. This case highlights the importance of multidisciplinary planning in achieving favourable maternal and foetal outcomes in high-risk pregnancies.

title: Iron-Based Contrast for the Heart: Clinical Promise of Ferumoxytol-Enhanced CMR.
authorString: Pogosyan A, Liu Y, Patel JA, Mahmoudi M, Xu H, Finn JP, Nguyen KL.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

Ferumoxytol is an ultrasmall superparamagnetic iron oxide (USPIO) nanoparticle that was originally approved by the U.S. FDA for treating iron deficiency anemia in patients with chronic kidney disease. It has since emerged as an off-label, versatile intravascular contrast agent for cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging, and in 2025, received FDA approval for brain imaging. This review provides an overview of ferumoxytol-enhanced CMR applications primarily focused on the heart, outlines its key imaging and pharmacokinetic properties, and summarizes its diagnostic safety profile.

Recent findings

Unlike gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCAs), which rapidly wash out from the circulation, ferumoxytol has high r1 and r2 relaxivities and remains confined to the intravascular compartment for prolonged periods. Once metabolized by the reticuloendothelial system, its iron core is incorporated into the body's hematopoietic pathways. These unique properties enable steady-state and delayed-phase imaging, simplify complex imaging workflows, and facilitate accelerated multidimensional cardiac imaging methods. Emerging applications for ferumoxytol-enhanced CMR include myocardial perfusion assessment, multidimensional imaging, vascular and hemodynamic evaluation, and comprehensive structural heart disease imaging.

Summary

Ferumoxytol expands the clinical applications of CMR by enabling imaging techniques that are not feasible with conventional GBCAs and broadening imaging options for patients in whom GBCA administration may be less desirable based on individualized clinical risk-benefit assessment, including selected patients with renal insufficiency, very young children, and pregnant women.

title: USP25 promotes ferroptosis in diabetic retinopathy by deubiquitinating p53 and suppressing the GPX4/SLC7A11 axis.
authorString: Gao Y, Zhao W, Chai Q, Ye C.
abstractText:
Objective

To explore the expression of the deubiquitinase (DUB) USP25 in diabetic retinopathy (DR) and its mechanistic role in regulating ferroptosis.

Methods

Bioinformatics was used to screen for DR-related DUB candidate genes. USP25 expression was validated in a streptozotocin-induced diabetic mouse model and high glucose (HG)-treated ARPE-19 cells. Loss- and gain-of-function approaches for USP25 were employed to assess retinal structural damage, tight junction proteins, cell viability, and TUNEL positivity. Ferroptosis-related changes were evaluated by measuring iron content, Fe2+ fluorescent signals, lipid peroxidation levels, and antioxidant enzyme activities. The molecular mechanism underlying USP25-mediated ferroptosis was elucidated through bioinformatics prediction, co-immunoprecipitation, and protein stability assays, followed by rescue experiments with p53 knockdown.

Results

USP25 was upregulated in the retinas of diabetic mice. USP25 knockdown ameliorated retinal structural damage and restored the expression of tight junction proteins (ZO-1 and occludin) in DR mice. USP25 exacerbated HG-induced cellular injury and ferroptosis by promoting iron accumulation, enhancing lipid peroxidation, suppressing the antioxidant defense system, and downregulating the ferroptosis suppressors GPX4 and SLC7A11. Mechanistically, USP25 stabilized p53 protein by reducing its ubiquitination. Rescue experiments further demonstrated that p53 knockdown significantly reversed ferroptosis-related alterations in the context of USP25 overexpression, mitigating ferroptosis-related damage in ARPE-19 cells and retinal tissues of diabetic mice.

Conclusion

USP25 is aberrantly upregulated in DR and promotes ferroptosis by deubiquitinating and stabilizing p53, thereby exacerbating retinal damage. The USP25-p53-ferroptosis axis may represent a potential therapeutic target for DR intervention.

title: ABO blood groups in relation to biomarkers of vascular structure and function in young, healthy adults - the LBA study.
authorString: Stefansson K, Chahal G, Hultdin J, Nilsson TK, Pettersson-Pablo P.
abstractText:
Background

In the elderly, ABO blood groups influence the risk of cardiovascular and thrombotic events, with blood group O consistently showing a more favorable risk profile. However, whether these differences affect physiological markers of vascular structure or subclinical metabolic traits in early adulthood remains poorly studied.

Methods

In this cross-sectional study, cardiovascular disease-related biomarkers in serum, measures of vascular structure and function, pulse-wave velocity (PWV), augmentation index (AIx), carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT), and ABO blood groups were assessed in a sample of young, healthy subjects aged 18-26 years.

Results

No statistically significant differences in PWV, AIx, or cIMT were identified across the different ABO blood groups. Conversely, the serum biomarkers showed distinct profiles. Individuals with blood group O presented with lower plasma concentrations of von Willebrand factor (vWF) compared to all non-O carriers (0.84 kIE/L vs. non-O, 1.09 kIE/L, p < 0.05). Furthermore, blood group O carriers demonstrated significantly lower fasting plasma glucose levels (4.96 mmol/L vs. 5.02 mmol/L, p = 0.02) and a trend toward lower fasting serum insulin levels (p = 0.07).

Conclusion

ABO blood groups were not associated with measures of vascular structure and function in young, healthy adults. Non-O blood groups were associated with higher vWF levels and altered glucose metabolism, suggesting that circulating cardiometabolic risk markers vary by blood group early in life.

title: Association of Blood Heavy Metal Concentrations with Angiographic Coronary Artery Disease in a Consecutive Single-Center Cardiac Catheterization Cohort.
authorString: Taylor JD, Shah P, Specht A, Shah M, Duckett M, Locquiao C, Lizama K, Salem E, McKown H, Glynn P, Vidovich MI.
abstractText: Environmental heavy metal exposure is increasingly recognized as a potentially important but underappreciated contributor to cardiovascular disease, yet its relationship to directly observed coronary artery disease (CAD) remains poorly defined. In this single-center cohort of 52 consecutive adults undergoing cardiac catheterization at an urban Chicago tertiary care center, we paired elemental exposure profiles with direct angiographic assessment in a racially diverse, socioeconomically vulnerable population. While no individual metal independently explained obstructive CAD, circulating metal exposure patterns were more revealing: Bayesian Kernel Machine Regression demonstrated that increasing overall metal burden was associated with worse coronary phenotypes, suggesting that environmental exposures may act collectively rather than in isolation. Lead and mercury emerged as the strongest contributors and were enriched relative to National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) reference populations. Taken together, these findings offer early but meaningful evidence that environmental toxicant burden may represent an underrecognized layer of cardiovascular risk, particularly in urban communities where industrial history, aging infrastructure, and socioeconomic disadvantage intersect. This work highlights the importance of viewing cardiovascular disease not only through the lens of traditional risk factors, but also through the environments in which patients live.

title: Protein-losing enteropathy as a rare presentation of small bowel T-cell post-transplant lymphoproliferative disease.
authorString: Au-Yang W, Chan HY, Kung KSK, Cheuk W, Cheung CY.
abstractText: Posttransplant lymphoproliferative disorders (PTLD) represent a heterogeneous group of lymphoproliferative lesions in patients who have solid organ or bone marrow transplantation. While majority of PTLD are of B-cell origin, T-cell PTLD is extremely rare. Monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal T-cell lymphoma (MEITL) is a rare primary intestinal lymphoma which most commonly involves the small bowel. Since the symptoms at presentation are often vague, the diagnosis is frequently delayed until acute complications such as intestinal perforation or obstruction occur. Here we report a very rare case of posttransplant small bowel MEITL in a kidney transplant recipient presenting with protein-losing enteropathy (PLE) as the initial manifestation. Our patient initially presented with episodic diarrhea but early investigations failed to identify any bowel pathology. Subsequently she developed hypoalbuminemia-related fluid retention and Tc-99 m HSA scintigraphy confirmed the presence of PLE. Even though the upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, colonoscopy and abdominal computed tomography did not show any significant lesions, the patient developed sudden bowel perforation and histologic examination of the resected tissue confirmed the diagnosis of posttransplant MEITL. She developed severe sepsis postoperatively and finally passed away despite aggressive supportive treatment. Our case shows that early diagnosis and prompt treatment is critical to potentially improve the patient outcomes.

title: Effectiveness of Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator Therapy for Primary Prevention in Patients with Nonischemic Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction.
authorString: Rohde LE, Zimerman LI, Moura LZ, Danzmann LC, Martins SM, Colpani V, Zucatti K, Figueiredo-Neto JA, Marcondes-Braga FG, Mourilhe-Rocha R, Albuquerque DC, Oliveira-Júnior MT, Simões MV.
abstractText:
Background

Primary prevention with an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) has become an increasingly debated strategy, with its role in patients with nonischemic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) undergoing continued reassessment.

Objective

To summarize the available scientific evidence on the effectiveness of ICD therapy for primary prevention in patients with nonischemic HFrEF.

Methods

A rapid systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the recommendations of the Cochrane Rapid Reviews Methods Group and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses statement. Statistical significance was defined as a two-sided p-value < 0.05. Searches were performed in the MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL databases. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating ICD implantation for primary prevention were included, with sudden cardiac death (SCD), cardiovascular mortality, and all-cause mortality as the primary outcomes.

Results

A total of 18 publications reporting daata from six pivotal RCTs were included. ICD therapy was associated with a statistically significant reduction in SCD (relative risk [RR] 0.41; 95%CI 0.26-0.65; high-certainty evidence) and cardiovascular mortality (RR 0.75; 95%CI 0.59-0.95; high-certainty evidence). For all-cause mortality, the primary analysis showed no statistically significant difference between groups (RR 0.88; 95%CI 0.72-1.07; moderate-certainty evidence). In the subgroup analysis, studies with shorter follow-up (< 6.8 years) demonstrated a significant reduction in all-cause mortality (RR 0.69; 95%CI 0.52-0.92).

Conclusion

In patients with nonischemic HFrEF, ICD therapy reduced SCD and cardiovascular mortality but did not significantly reduce all-cause mortality in the primary analysis. These findings support the use of ICD therapy when guided by individualized clinical assessment.

title: Percutaneous Axillary Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump Implantation in Patients Hospitalized with Heart Failure: Initial Brazilian Experience.
authorString: Rocha BADM, Melo PHMC, Mapa L, Oliveira RN, Freire AF, Mejía HPG, Bellini VC, Kopel L, Lage SG, Marcondes-Braga FG, Mangini S, Ávila MS, Campos IW, Bacal F, Brito FS, Abizaid AA, Nicz PFG.
abstractText:
Background

The intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) is the most widely used mechanical circulatory support device for patients with advanced heart failure (HF) in our setting. However, femoral implantation restricts patient mobility during support.

Objective

To report the initial experience of a Brazilian advanced HF referral center with percutaneous axillary IABP implantation.

Methods

Consecutive patients hospitalized for HF who underwent percutaneous axillary IABP implantation at a tertiary cardiology referral center were included. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

Results

Between December 2020 and December 2023, 22 patients underwent percutaneous axillary IABP implantation. The mean age was 53 ± 10.7 years. All patients were hospitalized with refractory HF and were listed for heart transplantation. The procedure was successfully performed in all patients selected for the axillary approach. The median duration of support was 15 days (interquartile range: 7-28 days). Observed complications included device migration (18.2%), limb ischemia (9.1%), and isolated infectious and neurological events. Half of the patients either underwent heart transplantation or were successfully weaned from mechanical support.

Conclusion

The initial experience with percutaneous axillary IABP implantation demonstrated that the technique is feasible, safe, and reproducible. Further studies are needed to establish the role of this strategy within the continuum of care for patients hospitalized with advanced HF while awaiting heart transplantation.

title: Characterisation of the patient-specific induced pluripotent stem cell line UKEi075-A carrying the heterozygous PRKAG2 frameshift variant c.769_770del (p.E257Kfs*15).
authorString: Hoffmann B, Knochenhauer T, Schlobohm J, Stathopoulou K, Ulmer BM, Shibamiya A, Laufer SD, Schäfer S, Krämer E, Fuchs S, Augustin C, Girdauskas E, Demal TJ, Klaassen S, Zeller T, Blankenberg S, Eschenhagen T, Cuello F.
abstractText: Missense variants in PRKAG2, the gene encoding for the γ2-subunit of adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK), can cause hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, cardiac conduction defects and glycogen storage disorders. Clinical consequences evoked by truncating PRKAG2 variants are poorly understood. Dermal fibroblasts of a male dilated cardiomyopathy-patient carrying the truncating PRKAG2 variant c.769_770del (p.E257Kfs*15) at a heterozygous state were reprogrammed by Sendai virus-mediated expression of OCT-4, SOX2, c-Myc and KLF4 to human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs). HiPSCs displayed a normal karyotype, high pluripotency, mycoplasma-absence and were successfully differentiated into three primary germ layers. This hiPSC-line will enable analysing molecular pathomechanisms underlying PRKAG2-cardiomyopathy.

title: Association between the Inflammatory Atherosclerosis Index and Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease: NHANES 2017-2020.
authorString: Jiang Y, Xie J, Dong Y.
abstractText:
Background

The Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) prevalence is increasing globally and is closely associated with dysregulated lipid metabolism and inflammation. However, the relationship between NAFLD and the inflammatory atherosclerosis index (IAI), which reflects these processes, is unclear.

Objectives

To investigate the association between IAI and NAFLD in a representative sample of U.S. adults.

Methods

This cross-sectional study included 5,309 adults from the U.S. NHANES database. Multivariate weighted logistic regression was used to assess the association between IAI and NAFLD. Restricted cubic splines explored nonlinear relationships, and ROC analysis evaluated diagnostic performance.

Results

A total of 5,309 participants were included, of whom 37.6% had NAFLD. Obesity and metabolic abnormalities were more pronounced in the NAFLD group, and IAI levels were significantly higher (P < 0.001). Multivariate analysis demonstrated that IAI was independently and positively associated with NAFLD (OR = 1.538, 95% CI: 1.421-1.665). RCS analysis indicated a nonlinear relationship (P for nonlinearity = 0.0473), with an inflection point at IAI = 0.145. When IAI < 0.145, the risk increased steeply (OR = 2.341, 95% CI: 2.037-2.690), whereas when IAI ≥ 0.145, the increase was attenuated (OR = 1.399, 95% CI: 1.263-1.548). Subgroup analyses showed consistent results, with no significant interactions across subgroups. ROC analysis showed that IAI exhibited the best diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.722), significantly outperforming other indicators (all P < 0.001).

Conclusions

Among U.S. adults, IAI demonstrates a strong, positive, and nonlinear association with NAFLD. These findings suggest IAI is a promising population-level marker for NAFLD, though prospective studies are required for validation.

title: Pan-genome insights into the evolutionary dynamics and functional diversification of genes in monkeypox virus.
authorString: Liu Y, Tang Y, Xu Y, Long X, Zhu Z.
abstractText: Monkeypox virus (MPXV) continues to emerge as a global health threat. While genetically diverse, its genomic structure and evolution remain undercharacterized. This study analyzed 157 non-redundant MPXV genomes (subtypes Ia, Ib, IIa, IIb), identifying 183 core and 222 non-core genes via pan-genome analysis-indicative of an open pan-genome. Over half (55.8%) of MPXV genes show gene number variation. Non-core genes exhibit a higher ratio of insertions/deletions compared to core genes. Additionally, selection pressure analysis indicated that non-core genes are more prone to positive selection. Furthermore, interaction analysis revealed that core viral proteins target immune-related human pathways, while non-core proteins engage with viral infection-associated proteins. These results deepen our understanding of MPXV evolution and inform future research directions.

title: Erratum: [Corrigendum] Fisetin ameliorates atherosclerosis by regulating PCSK9 and LOX-1 in apoE<sup>-/-</sup> mice.
authorString: Yan L, Jia Q, Cao H, Chen C, Xing S, Huang Y, Shen D.
abstractText: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.3892/etm.2020.9457.].

title: Securing Maternal Identity: Halachic Concerns in the Age of Mitochondrial Replacement Therapy.
authorString: Loike JD, Flaum RT, Kadish A.
abstractText: Mitochondrial replacement therapy (MRT) encompasses assisted reproductive technologies designed to prevent the transmission of pathogenic mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) mutations by combining the DNA in the nucleus (nuclear genome) of the intending parents with another woman's enucleated egg that provides healthy donor-derived mtDNA. The use of advanced genomic engineering in MRT raises distinct ethical and halachic considerations regarding the ontological status of embryos containing genetic material from more than two individuals. This paper advances an original theoretical protocol, termed biparental mitochondrial replacement therapy (Bi-MRT), that mitigates the central halachic concerns associated with multi-parent embryos. In this protocol, future advances in stem cell technology could be employed to generate an enucleated gamete-like cell containing healthy mitochondria from the husband. The meiotic spindle-chromosome complex from the wife's oocyte could then be transplanted into this reconstituted gamete, which could be subsequently fertilized with the husband's sperm for IVF. If technically feasible and developmentally competent, the resulting embryo could potentially be transferred to the wife for gestation. By combining the wife's nuclear genetic contribution, gestation, and parturition with the husband's paternal DNA, this framework isolates the third-party mitochondrial contribution as a non-maternal factor, thereby reinforcing the wife's singular claim to halachic maternity. Biparental MRT therefore represents a theoretical framework that could potentially reduce some halachic concerns associated with conventional MRT, but substantial scientific and safety barriers remain before any clinical application could be contemplated.

title: ROR2 Drives Right Ventricular Heart Failure Through Disruption of Proteostasis.
authorString: Hartman H, Uy G, Uchida K, Scarborough EA, Yang Y, Barr EW, Williams S, Santilli RT, Kavari SL, Brandimarto J, Li L, Lai L, Griffin J, Yucel N, Shewale S, Rajagopal H, Eaton DM, Dorwart T, Bedi KC, Conn CS, Margulies KB, Prosser BL, Arany Z, Edwards JJ.
abstractText:
Background

No therapies exist to reverse right ventricular failure (RVF), and the molecular mechanisms that drive RVF remain understudied. We recently reported that the developmentally restricted noncanonical WNT receptor ROR2 (receptor tyrosine kinase-like orphan receptor 2) is upregulated in human RVF in proportion to severity of disease. Here we test the mechanistic role of ROR2 in RVF pathogenesis.

Methods

ROR2 was overexpressed or knocked down in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes and then characterized using confocal microscopy, RNA sequencing, proteomics, proteostatic functional assays, and pacing to assess contractile properties. The impact of cardiac ROR2 expression was evaluated in mice by AAV9-mediated overexpression and by AAV9-mediated delivery of short hairpin RNA to knockdown ROR2 in a pulmonary artery banded pressure overload model of RVF. ROR2-modified mice were evaluated by echocardiography, histology, and right ventricle protein synthesis and proteasome capacity.

Results

In neonatal rat ventricular myocytes, we find that ROR2 profoundly dysregulates the coordination between protein translation and folding. This imbalance leads to excess protein clearance by the ubiquitin proteasome system with dramatic impacts on sarcomere and cytoskeletal structure and function. Inhibiting the ubiquitin proteasome system or restoring chaperone expression is sufficient to partially rescue ROR2-induced structural and contractile deficits in cardiomyocytes. In mice, forced cardiac ROR2 expression is sufficient to disrupt proteostasis and drive RVF, whereas conversely Ror2 knockdown partially rescues proteostasis and right ventricle structure and function in a pressure overload model of RVF.

Conclusions

In sum, ROR2 is a key driver of RVF pathogenesis through proteostatic disruption and thus provides a promising target to treat RVF.

title: National Policy on Congenital Heart Disease: Reflections and Proposals for Strengthening Care in Brazil.
authorString: Miana L, Zheleva B, Passos JPU, Mattos R, Damiano AP, Afiune JY, Horowitz ESK, Jatene MB.
abstractText:
Background

In Brazil, more than 20,000 children are born annually with congenital heart disease, and a significant proportion require surgical or interventional treatment within the first year of life. Despite advances in medical care, substantial inequalities persist in access to timely diagnosis and treatment.

Objectives

To describe the evolution of national policies related to congenital heart disease care in Brazil and to discuss strategies for improving the organization and delivery of care within the national public health system.

Methods

This is a narrative and documental review based on the analysis of publicly available data, official health policies, and previously published literature addressing congenital heart disease care and health system organization in Brazil.

Results

The analysis identified that although multiple national initiatives have been implemented over time, they remain fragmented and have not fully addressed disparities in access to care. Key gaps include deficiencies in regionalization, data collection, workforce training, and system coordination.

Conclusions

Congenital heart disease care in Brazil remains marked by structural inequalities and fragmentation of health policies. Strengthening regionalized networks, improving financing strategies, enhancing data systems, and optimizing referral pathways are essential to ensure timely and equitable access to diagnosis and treatment.
