title: Cardiovascular Risk of Conventional Synthetic, Biologic and Targeted Synthetic Disease-Modifying Antirheumatic Drugs in Common Rheumatic Diseases: A Narrative Review of Current Evidence.
authorString: Nian F, Chen Z, Qian Y, Yang M, Zhang B.
abstractText: Rheumatic diseases, including those with an autoimmune etiology (including rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, spondyloarthropathies and systemic vasculitis) represent an independent risk factor for coronary atherosclerosis and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). Systemic inflammation plays a multidimensional role in cardiovascular disease (CVD) pathogenesis, and patients with rheumatic diseases face elevated CVD risk and mortality compared with the general population, driven by both traditional cardiovascular risk factors and systemic immune dysregulation. Adequate management of inflammation will be accompanied by improved cardiovascular risk. In 2010, rheumatology introduced the "targeted therapy" strategy, and around the same time, cohort studies showed a significant decrease in cardiovascular mortality. A comprehensive literature search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to June 2026. Studies were included if they evaluated the cardiovascular effects of disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) in patients with the aforementioned rheumatic diseases. These diseases were selected based on their high prevalence, well-established cardiovascular risk, and availability of comparative evidence across DMARD classes; systemic sclerosis was excluded due to its distinct pathophysiology and limited published data on DMARD-related cardiovascular outcomes. We still need to deepen our understanding of the precise pathophysiological mechanism of autoimmune mediated acceleration of atherosclerosis and its clinical manifestations, to enable more appropriate selection of immunotherapies and biological agents for patients with rheumatic diseases, including those with an autoimmune etiology, and ultimately reduce the cardiovascular risk of this population, thereby improving prognosis and quality of life. The aim of this narrative review was to synthesize available evidence regarding the cardiovascular effects of three major classes of DMARDs: conventional synthetic disease‑modifying antirheumatic drugs (csDMARDs), biologic disease‑modifying antirheumatic drugs (bDMARDs), and targeted synthetic disease‑modifying antirheumatic drugs (tsDMARDs), across a stratified spectrum of cardiovascular endpoints ranging from hard clinical outcomes to subclinical surrogate markers. The main findings indicate that different DMARDs classes exhibit heterogeneous effects on cardiovascular outcomes, with csDMARDs such as methotrexate and hydroxychloroquine generally associated with favorable cardiovascular profiles, whereas the cardiovascular safety of certain biologic and targeted synthetic agents remains a subject of ongoing investigation. Limitations of this review include the observational nature of most included studies, heterogeneity across study designs and populations, and the lack of head-to-head randomized trials comparing different DMARDs classes with respect to cardiovascular outcomes. Collectively, these findings underscore the need for individualized cardiovascular risk assessment and tailored DMARDs selection in patients with rheumatic diseases, thereby optimizing both rheumatic and cardiovascular prognosis.

title: Social and clinical determinants of liver transplant evaluation in hepatocellular carcinoma: A multicenter cohort study.
authorString: Tincopa M, Bridi L, Vodkin I, Yilma M, Zhou K, Kwong A, Singh J, Mehta N, Kuo A, Hirose R, Wisel SA, Steggerda JA, Freise C, Ajmera V.
abstractText:
Background

Liver transplantation (LT) is curative for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) but requires timely referral. Comprehensive data on factors impacting LT referral and outcomes for HCC are limited. We evaluated social, system, and clinical factors associated with listing, LT, mortality, HCC stage at referral, and time from HCC diagnosis to referral.

Methods

The California Liver Network is a consortium of 6 LT centers comprising >75% of adult LTs in California. Demographic, clinical, psychosocial, and social determinants of health and outcome data were collected for adults referred for LT. Multivariable regression identified factors associated with outcomes.

Results

Of 9987 adults referred, 1573 (15.7%) had HCC. Median age was 63.3 years; 73% males, 40% Hispanic, and 26.1% Medicaid insurance. Median MELD was 12.7 (IQR 8-16), and median time from HCC diagnosis to LT referral was 124 days (IQR 32-410). In all, 10% were T1 and 70.5% were T2 at referral. Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) (OR 0.99), HCC stage, Medicaid insurance (OR 0.55), LT site, and marital status (OR 1.90) were associated with listing. Transplantation was associated with HCC stage (OR 0.42) and LT site. Mortality was associated with MELD (OR 1.02), hypertension (OR 1.44), dialysis (OR 2.48), hepatic encephalopathy (OR 1.54), and portal vein thrombosis (OR 1.44). Referral at more advanced HCC stage was associated with male sex (OR 1.55), AFP (OR 1.01), Medicaid insurance (OR 1.40), primary language (OR 0.70), and prior HCC treatment type. Longer time to referral was associated with HCV/alcohol liver disease and prior HCC treatment type.

Conclusions

In this multicenter study of adults with HCC, Medicaid insurance, LT site, HCC treatment history, and psychosocial factors were key determinants of HCC care cascade progression, identifying targets to improve LT access.

title: The Duke Clinically Linked Electrocardiogram and Arrhythmia Repository.
authorString: Masroor K, Daries S, Nenadic I, Lin A, Piccini JP, Loring Z.
abstractText: Artificial intelligence-electrocardiogram (ECG) algorithms are becoming increasingly powerful tools in the clinical world, allowing for earlier and subclinical detection of ubiquitous and harmful pathologies. However, the strength of these algorithms is directly informed by the strength of the data sets on which they are trained, and there is a growing need for large-scale, diverse, publicly available ECG repositories. The Duke Clinically Linked ECG and Arrhythmia Repository is a large-scale ECG database containing over 5 million clinically acquired ECGs linked to longitudinal clinical data. Its strengths-including demographic diversity, large sample size, linked clinical databases, breadth of represented conditions, access to linked procedure codes, various options for data export, and ease in creating targeted subcohorts-position it as a significant tool in the artificial intelligence-ECG research landscape. This Methods paper outlines the demographics and structure of this database and explores promising research applications of this resource.

title: A computational framework for modeling fluid and solid stresses in porous tissues with application to the trabeculated embryonic heart.
authorString: Buffinton CM, Baish JW.
abstractText: This study provides a framework for efficient solutions of computational fluid-solid interaction models of porous tissue, with a focus on blood flow through the developing heart wall in the critical chamber and valve formation stages, when trabeculation fills much of the ventricles. This porous, trabeculated tissue is the site of complex mechanotransduction processes, but accurately estimating solid and fluid stresses within such intricate geometries is difficult. We addressed this with three levels of modeling and verification. Images of E12.5 mouse ventricles were first obtained through confocal microscopy and 3D reconstruction. These guided creation of explicit pore-scale finite element simulations with fluid-solid interaction. Idealized and image-derived unit cells were analyzed to determine hydraulic permeability. Next, a multi-pore representation of the ventricular wall was solved with full fluid and solid equations. A continuum model based on Brinkman equations then replaced the explicit pore structure, and sensitivity to permeability was evaluated in terms of fluid flow in the open channel and porous region. Permeabilities obtained from unit-cell simulations followed trends from Kozeny-Carman solid-pore and fiber theory for the rigid case, while simulations for hyperelastic unit-cell material quantified the effects of tissue elasticity. Comparison of continuum and explicit model results showed the Brinkman equation, which incorporates the diffusion of shear stress from flow in the free fluid into the porous media, but not explicitly inertial effects, could significantly improve the accuracy of continuum models compared to Darcy's law. A 3D model of blood flow through the ventricles of the developing mouse heart demonstrated the application of the technique to more realistic geometry, showed locations of peak solid and shear stress, and produced physiologically reasonable flow. Furthermore, we developed methodologies to estimate local wall shear and solid stress from continuum-based calculations. This approach can enable efficient, whole-organ parametric analyses of fluid flow, circumventing the need for computationally expensive explicit pore modeling.

title: Complete transcatheter closure of residual aortopulmonary window in an elderly patient allowing optimization of refractory pulmonary arterial hypertension therapy.

title: Predictors of Blood Culture Ordering and Results for Febrile Infants Aged 91 to 365 Days in the Emergency Department.
authorString: Florio CJ, Hatch MM, Somers MJ, Greenhow TL, Reed ME, Ballard DW, Vinson DR, Casey SD.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: J Am Coll Emerg Physicians Open
journal.title: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open
journal.isoabbreviation: J Am Coll Emerg Physicians Open

abstractText:
Introduction

The risk of invasive bacterial infections has dropped significantly among febrile infants due to widespread vaccination efforts. In older infants (age 91 days and older), diagnostic guidance is limited, and blood culture ordering is based on clinical judgment. We sought to evaluate blood culture ordering practice, bacteremia incidence, and the patient characteristics of true positive blood culture results.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study of febrile pediatric patients aged 91 to 365 days who presented to Kaiser Permanente Northern California emergency departments (EDs) between January 1, 2018, and December 31, 2019, who had blood cultures drawn. We identified variables related to blood culture ordering using a generalized linear mixed model and adjudicated all positive results to determine rates of true bacteremia or contamination, as well as clinical characteristics of children with true positive bacteremia.

Results

Among 5543 febrile infants, 611 (11.0%) underwent blood culture testing. After adjustment for covariates, higher ED temperature (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.40, 95% CI, 1.30 to 1.50), presence of comorbidities (aOR 2.55, 95% CI, 2.00 to 3.25), and younger age (aOR 0.996, 95% CI, 0.995 to 0.998, P < .001) were associated with blood culture ordering. Of the 37 (6.1%) positive blood cultures, only 16 (2.6%) were true positives. All true positives occurred in infants with either an identifiable risk factor or a clinically evident source of infection. There were no cases of occult bacteremia identified.

Conclusion

In febrile infants aged 91 to 365 days, true bacteremia was rare and associated with significant comorbidities or an obvious infectious source. Our findings suggest a more directed approach to ED blood culture ordering.

title: Angiotensinogen as a molecular hub in interorgan communication.
authorString: Zhou J, Ye X, Wang Y, Hong M, Rong J, Wang J, Xu Y.
abstractText: Angiotensinogen (AGT) is the sole precursor of angiotensin peptides, its physiological relevance is not determined solely by precursor abundance. Although the liver supplies the bulk of circulating AGT, the protein detected in peripheral tissues may arise from local synthesis, vascular retention, glomerular filtration, barrier crossing, or receptor-mediated uptake. Moreover, the molecular form in which AGT exists carries functional implications: intact AGT and des(Ang I)AGT produce effects that are distinct from-and under certain conditions, opposing to-those of angiotensin II (Ang II). This review repositions AGT as a context-sensitive mediator of interorgan crosstalk, with a clear demarcation between preclinical models and human data. Studies using source-specific knockout and lineage tracing in mice offer the strongest causal evidence for liver-to-kidney AGT trafficking; most other proposed axes lack such granular resolution. Human genetic loss-of-function studies have definitively established AGT's indispensability for renal morphogenesis and blood-pressure regulation, while observational cohorts and biomarker studies rarely determine its tissue origin or delivery route. Ultimately, the functional output of AGT across organ systems depends on its source, molecular state, local accessibility, enzymatic processing, and the receptor environment. Therapeutic agents that target hepatocytes, such as zilebesiran and tonlamarsen, produce durable AGT suppression and could potentially ease treatment burden relative to conventional daily angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs). Their slow offset of action, combined with a current lack of solid cardiovascular and renal outcome data, raises an unresolved but critical question: what is the safety margin for AGT reduction before renal self-regulation, fluid-electrolyte balance, or pressor responses to physiological stress become compromised? Overall, AGT does not function as a ubiquitous interorgan signaling molecule; instead, it functions as an upstream determinant whose impact is highly context-dependent, shaped by its site of production, route of dissemination, and mode of processing. This review systematically differentiates experimentally established source-to-target circuits from plausible but as-yet-unconfirmed pathways and outlines the mechanistic and clinical benchmarks that must be met for the safe, tissue-selective application of AGT-targeted therapy.

title: Rationale and design of RECOVER - a prospective, longitudinal cardiac rehabilitation registry.
authorString: Riess J, Schmidt EA, Petrasch G, Brito Da Silva H, Sichler S, Sartori P, Carluccio ED, Haberfellner C, Senftinger J, Albus M, Bieri K, Rhyner C, Hametner G, Prechtl LM, Distler M, Jellestad L, D'Ascenzi F, Sokolowska M, Rodriguez Cetina Biefer H, Dzemali O, Von Moos R, Twerenbold R, Loidl M, Tanner FC, Lustenberger C, Eijsvogels TMH, Bakker EA, Tomczak CR, Baggish A, Kraler S, Aigner E, Carter AW, Bauer N, Röösli M, Haddad IE, Häuptli D, Latshang TD, Steffel J, Haykowsky MJ, Blankenberg S, Vontobel J, Ziegler A, Niederseer D.

journal.title: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice

abstractText:
Background

Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) has been performed in a structured manner since the 1970s, supported by a substantial body of evidence demonstrating its benefits across the heterogeneous pool of cardiac patients. Although therapeutic interventions, pharmacological options, and patient-centered recommendations keep emerging, the majority of CR programs have not changed accordingly. Hence, they are becoming less capable of accounting for an increasingly diverse patient cohort. With a prospective long-term cohort, we aim to achieve an in-depth characterization of CR patients, enabling the delivery of more personalized care in the contemporary era.

Methods

In this non-interventional, monocentric, prospective cohort study named RECOVER (Cardiac REhabilitation COhort at the Medicine Campus DaVos to invEstigate Recovery), we plan to include 10,000 patients over 10 years across a broad spectrum of cardiovascular conditions (e.g., cardiac surgery, myocardial infarction, heart failure) with data collected across the full spectrum of inpatient CR. Data acquisition is complemented through extensive biobanking allowing detailed phenotyping and biomarker profiling of patients. Follow-up assessments are conducted at 3 and 6 months, and yearly thereafter, up to 10 years. By harnessing novel devices, digital monitoring is employed to continuously capture a wealth of health-related parameters, such as blood pressure and accelerometry-based physical activity.

Addition to the field and limitations

Given the substantial research gap in personalized CR, the RECOVER study provides the opportunity to systematically evaluate recovery patterns and treatment response across distinct cardiovascular subgroups. Due to the unique and highly innovative infrastructure available at the recruiting site, the monocentric design enables performance of an extensive standardized assessment. By incorporating digital technologies in conjunction with deep phenotypic and biomarker data, RECOVER holds promise to enable tailored CR strategies.

title: Mosaic RASopathies: comprehensive genetic and clinicopathological analysis for diagnosis and management.
authorString: Belysheva T, Nasedkina T, Zelenova E, Semenova V, Semenova N, Sagoyan G, Kletskaya I, Vishnevskaya Y, Sharapova E, Kulikova K, Vlasov P, Botkina A, Belogurova M, Dorofeeva M, Valiev T, Varfolomeeva S.

journal.title: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

abstractText:
Introduction

Mosaic RASopathies are rare conditions caused by postzygotic mutations arising during embryonic development in genes of the RAS/MAPK signaling pathway. They are mainly characterized by a combination of epidermal nevi and extracutaneous manifestations. Distinguishing between different entities can be challenging because of their substantial clinical and genetic overlap. Our aim was to demonstrate the importance of genetic background for accurate diagnosis and further prognostic assessment of disease progression by analyzing genotype-phenotype correlations within this clinical group.

Methods

The study enrolled 18 patients (10 male and 8 female patients) ranging in age from 1 month to 21 years with congenital craniofacial nevi and variable extracutaneous abnormalities. DNA isolated from peripheral blood leukocytes and affected tissues (nevus and tumor) was analyzed using a targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) panel covering RAS/MAPK pathway genes, followed by Sanger sequencing.

Results

Eight patients were diagnosed with Schimmelpenning-Feuerstein-Mims syndrome caused by postzygotic pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in the HRAS (n = 4) or KRAS (n = 4) genes. Seven patients were clinically diagnosed with phacomatosis pigmentokeratotica (PPK), and mosaic genetic variants were identified in the HRAS (n = 4), KRAS (n = 2), or BRAF (n = 1) genes. In two additional patients with similar phenotypes, somatic mutations in PIK3CA (n = 1) and FGFR2 (n = 1) were identified in affected skin, while in one further case, no clinically significant variant was detected.

Discussion

We compared the spectrum of extracutaneous anomalies according to the affected gene by combining our data with data from other clinical cases of mosaic RASopathies described in the literature. In summary, 53 cases with HRAS postzygotic variants and 41 cases with KRAS variants were included in the analysis of genotype-phenotype correlations. Hypophosphatemic rickets (HR) and malignant tumors were associated with pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in the HRAS gene, while ophthalmological, neurological, cardiovascular, and renal disorders were more common in KRAS-mutant patients.

Conclusion

Thus, genetic testing of affected tissue in comparison to normal tissue (peripheral blood) is essential for accurate diagnosis of these mosaic disorders. Consideration of clinical manifestations and the identified genotype-phenotype correlations may further assist in determining prognosis and guiding patient management.

title: Case Report: Prenatal and postnatal clinical manifestations of 15q duplication syndrome: a single longitudinal case combined with pooled analysis of 35 prenatal cases.
authorString: Xu Z, Ufei M, Chen H, Yang S, Zou P, Lu Y, Xiong F, Li J.
abstractText:
Background

15q duplication (Dup15q) syndrome is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by early-onset hypotonia, developmental delay, intellectual disability, symptoms related to autism spectrum disorder and epilepsy. In the absence of specific treatment, prenatal diagnosis is of important clinical significance. However, most reported cases are postnatal cases, whereas prenatal cases are limited and often lack detailed clinical information, making prenatal recognition of this disorder challenging. In this study, we integrated prenatal and postnatal clinical information from the present case with a pooled analysis of published prenatal Dup15q syndrome cases, providing additional insights into the prenatal-to-postnatal phenotypic spectrum of Dup15q syndrome.

Case presentation

We report a case of Dup15q syndrome with both prenatal and postnatal clinical data. Although prenatal ultrasound showed polyhydramnios, an abdominal circumference below the 10th percentile, and mild tricuspid regurgitation, no further prenatal genetic testing was performed. After birth, the patient presented with early hypotonia and developmental delay, and the diagnosis was established by genetic testing after a poor response to rehabilitation. We collected 34 prenatal Dup15q syndrome cases through literature review. The results showed that non-invasive prenatal screening (NIPS) may facilitate the prenatal identification of Dup15q syndrome. Prenatal ultrasound findings included polyhydramnios, fetal growth restriction (FGR), cardiac abnormalities, dysmorphic features, and abnormal ultrasound soft markers. The pooled analysis further provided an overview of the prenatal phenotypic spectrum of Dup15q syndrome and suggested that FGR and polyhydramnios, particularly in the presence of additional ultrasound abnormalities, positive NIPS results, or a positive family history, may warrant further etiological evaluation.

Conclusions

Dup15q syndrome exhibits prominent clinical heterogeneity with nonspecific prenatal manifestations, predisposing patients to missed or delayed diagnosis. By integrating prenatal and postnatal clinical information with pooled prenatal cases, this study provides a broader understanding of the phenotypic spectrum of Dup15q syndrome and may facilitate prenatal counseling and early clinical recognition.

title: Nursing radiation-protection compliance and 30-day wound and pin-site adverse events after supracondylar humerus fracture fixation in children.
authorString: Huang Y, Huang Z, Jin W.
abstractText:
Background

Fluoroscopy is integral to operative fixation of supracondylar humerus fractures in children, but case-level nursing radiation-protection compliance (NRPC) has not been well characterised as a potential marker of broader perioperative process quality. We examined the association between NRPC and early wound- and pin-site-related outcomes.

Methods

We conducted a single-centre retrospective cohort study of children aged <14 years who underwent fluoroscopy-assisted operative fixation for supracondylar humerus fractures at The Second Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University, China, between 2018 and 2023. NRPC was assessed using three binary components reflecting recent formal radiation-protection training, absence of radiation-protection-related quality-control deductions, and documented implementation of radiation-protection measures during the index procedure. Components were summed to a 0-3 score and categorised as Low (0-1) or High (2-3) NRPC. The primary outcome was any wound- or pin-site-related adverse event within 30 days. The primary multivariable logistic regression model adjusted for calendar year, Gartland classification, operative duration, and emergency surgical status. Firth penalized regression, ordinal-score analyses, and separate nurse- and surgeon-clustered mixed-effects models were performed as sensitivity analyses.

Results

Of 360 children identified, 256 children met the eligibility criteria and had ascertainable NRPC and primary-outcome data; 164 (64%) were classified as High NRPC and 92 (36%) as Low NRPC. Overall, 37/256 children (14.5%) experienced the primary outcome. The observed event rate was 11.0% (18/164) in the High NRPC group and 20.7% (19/92) in the Low NRPC group, corresponding to a crude OR of 2.11 (95% CI 1.04-4.27; p = 0.037) for Low versus High NRPC. In the primary adjusted model, the association was attenuated and imprecise (adjusted OR 1.70, 95% CI 0.80-3.57; p = 0.165). Firth penalized regression yielded OR 1.67 (95% CI 0.80-3.49; p = 0.168), while separate mixed-effects models yielded OR 1.65 (95% CI 0.76-3.58; p = 0.205) for nurse clustering and OR 1.68 (95% CI 0.77-3.66; p = 0.190) for surgeon clustering. Per 1-point increase in the NRPC score, the adjusted OR was 0.70 (95% CI 0.48-1.02; p = 0.061).

Conclusion

Higher NRPC was associated with lower unadjusted rates of 30-day wound- and pin-site-related adverse events, but the association was attenuated and statistically imprecise after temporal and clinical adjustment. Similar directional estimates across sensitivity analyses support NRPC as an exploratory marker of broader perioperative process quality rather than as an independently established predictor or causal determinant of wound outcomes.

title: Animation-assisted psychological intervention in pediatric care: mechanisms, clinical applications, and emerging evidence.
authorString: Dongxian W, Zeqi Y, Qi S, Shutong W.
abstractText: Children frequently experience fear, anxiety, and pain during medical encounters, and this distress can lead to poor cooperation, longer procedures, and lasting avoidance of care. Animation, delivered as cartoons, preparation films, applications, serious games, and virtual reality (VR) scenes, has become one of the most widely deployed non-pharmacological adjuncts in pediatric settings because it is inexpensive, non-invasive, and easily standardized. Drawing on a structured search of six databases through July 2026, this mini-review synthesizes randomized and meta-analytic evidence across perioperative anxiety, procedural pain, pediatric dentistry, chronic-disease self-management, and mental health promotion. It organizes the evidence around five psychological pathways: attentional competition, observational learning, exposure and inhibitory learning, narrative-affective processing, and self-efficacy. Additionally, it examines a sixth, non-psychological use in which animation is used to provide therapeutic visual stimulation. Evidence supports moderate short-term benefits for anticipatory anxiety and for needle- and dentistry-related distress, with weaker and less consistent effects for high-intensity procedures and physiological outcomes. We argue that the field's core issue is conceptual rather than empirical: animation refers to a delivery medium, not a treatment, and trials have compared media rather than mechanisms. This obscures three unresolved problems: discordance between self-reported and autonomic outcomes; an untheorized moderating role of the developmental stage; and a theoretical tension between distraction, which withdraws attention from the feared stimulus, and exposure, which requires engagement with it. Mechanism-matched comparators, core outcome sets, developmentally stratified designs, transparent intervention reporting, and follow-up across repeated procedures are prerequisites for cumulative progress.

title: Pulmonary hypertension in a patient with HHV-8-negative multicentric castleman disease and epstein-barr virus co-infection: a case report.
authorString: Yan X, Xie L, Li H, Tang J, Wang M, Wang L.
abstractText: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) seems to be a rare but severe complication of Castleman disease (CD), especially the multicentric type (MCD). We report a case of recurrent fever, anemia and progressive dyspnea. She was finally diagnosed with pre-capillary PH in the setting of MCD and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) co-infection after right heart catheterization and lymph node biopsy. After receiving siltuximab, an anti-interleukin-6 monoclonal antibody along with diuretic agent, the symptoms were relieved. However, the patient died 8 months after diagnosis due to a pulmonary hypertensive crisis secondary to clinically diagnosed bacterial pneumonia presenting with severe dyspnea, refractory hypoxemia, and acute right ventricular failure. This rare case improves recognition of this infrequent etiology of PH.

title: Effects of chronic alcohol consumption on gene expression in the rat left ventricle: a transcriptomic analysis.
authorString: Ai W, Casey CA, Rasineni K, Saraswathi V.
abstractText:
Objective

Chronic alcohol consumption is one of the leading causes of dilated cardiomyopathy. Alcohol-associated cardiomyopathy (ACM) is characterized by impaired cardiac function and ventricular dilation in individuals with a history of long-term alcohol consumption. Alcohol exerts adverse effects on the myocardium via mitochondrial dysfunction and chronic inflammation. However, the broader transcriptional changes associated with chronic alcohol exposure remain poorly understood.

Methods

A chronic ethanol feeding model was utilized, in which male Wistar rats were fed a Lieber-Decarli ethanol diet containing 6.7% (v/v) ethanol (ET) or an isocaloric control (CONT) diet for 6 weeks. Left ventricular tissues were collected from ET-fed and CONT-fed rats. Differential gene expression was assessed using bulk RNA sequencing, followed by Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA).

Results

Transcriptomic analysis identified 194 upregulated and 199 downregulated genes in the left ventricles of ET-fed rats compared with CONT-fed rats. IPA revealed downregulated pathways related to the circadian clock and interferon signaling in the myocardium of ET-fed rats. In particular, the differentially altered genes included regulators of the circadian clock (Bmal1, Npas2, Per1, Per2) and interferon signaling (Ifit2, Ifit3, Irf6, Irf9). In contrast, pathways associated with mitochondrial RNA degradation, sheddase signaling, and neutrophil extracellular traps were upregulated in the myocardium following chronic ethanol exposure.

Conclusion

Chronic ethanol exposure is associated with dysregulation of circadian rhythm and immune-related signaling pathways in the rat myocardium. These findings highlight molecular pathways that may contribute to the development of ACM and warrant further mechanistic investigation.

title: Coagulation and fibrinolysis biomarkers associated with gastrointestinal bleeding in children with immunoglobulin A vasculitis: a retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Chen F, Shen H, Shao X, Wei J.
abstractText:
Objective

This study aimed to explore alterations of soluble thrombomodulin (sTM), thrombin-antithrombin complex (TAT), plasmin-α2-plasmin inhibitor complex (PIC), tissue plasminogen activator-inhibitor complex (t-PAIC), and D-dimer in children with immunoglobulin A vasculitis (IgAV). We further evaluated the associations of these hemostatic biomarkers and clinical features with gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding in this cohort of patients.

Methods

A retrospective cohort study was conducted at our hospital between September 2021 and April 2025, enrolling 126 consecutive children diagnosed with IgAV. Among these, 44 children presented with GI bleeding and 20 developed overt GI bleeding. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify associated factors for GI bleeding in IgAV children. Moreover, the threshold values were assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.

Results

There were no significant differences in age, gender, sTM and t-PAIC between GI bleeding and no-GI-bleeding groups in children with IgAV. Among IgAV children, those with GI bleeding had significantly higher neutrophils, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), fibrinogen (FIB), TAT, PIC and D-dimer levels than those without GI bleeding, along with decreased serum immunoglobulin G (IgG). Children with overt bleeding had prolonged hospital stay, higher dose of methylprednisolone administration and elevated serum IgM than those with occult bleeding. Multivariate regression analysis revealed that PIC (odds ratio [OR] = 1.888, 95% confidence intervals [CI] 1.013-3.518, P = 0.045; area under the curve [AUC] = 0.687) was independently associated with higher odds of GI bleeding with IgAV in childhood, and serum IgG (OR = 0.843, 95%CI: 0.737-0.965, P = 0.013). The AUC of combined model was 0.737.

Conclusion

Increased PIC levels and decreased serum IgG are closely correlated with GI bleeding in children with IgAV.

title: Post-cardiopulmonary bypass colloid osmotic pressure and creatinine-defined acute kidney injury in infants undergoing cardiac surgery: an age-modified association.
authorString: Zhou Y, Gui W, Zhang X, Chen J, Xie J, Liu K, Yi S, Ma R.
abstractText:
Background

Acute kidney injury (AKI) is common after infant cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). Colloid osmotic pressure (COP) changes during CPB in response to hemodilution, albumin administration, ultrafiltration, and hemoconcentration, but its association with postoperative AKI in infants remains incompletely defined. Because renal physiology matures rapidly during the first year of life, the clinical meaning of COP may also vary across infancy.

Methods

We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of 230 infants aged ≤12 months and weighing ≤10 kg who underwent cardiac surgery with CPB between May 2020 and September 2022. The primary exposure was COP measured immediately after CPB, and the primary outcome was creatinine-defined postoperative AKI based on KDIGO thresholds within a prespecified 48-hour postoperative window. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated the covariate-adjusted association between post-CPB COP and AKI. Restricted cubic splines assessed dose-response form, and a generalized additive model (GAM) with a tensor-product smooth of COP and age was used to explore age-related heterogeneity. Time-specific analyses additionally evaluated pre-CPB, intra-CPB, and post-CPB COP.

Results

AKI occurred in 57 infants (24.8%). After adjustment for covariates, for every 1 mmHg increase in post-CPB COP, the risk of AKI increased by 16% (OR = 1.16; 95% CI: 1.04-1.28; P = 0.004). The dose-response relationship was broadly linear. The GAM curve combining age and COP suggested age-related heterogeneity (P = 0.022); in an exploratory age-stratified analysis, the estimated odds ratio was highest in the group of infants aged 10-12 months (OR per 1 mmHg increase: 1.79; 95% CI: 1.09-3.64; P = 0.048); however, due to the small number of events in this subgroup, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory. There was no significant association between pre-CPB or during-CPB COP and AKI, whereas post-CPB COP exhibited the strongest time-specific signal. Incorporating COP into the clinical model resulted in only a slight, non-statistically significant improvement in discrimination performance (AUC: 0.701 vs. 0.723; P = 0.324); no significant improvement was observed in NRI, and the overall net benefit was minimal.

Conclusions

Higher post-CPB COP was associated with creatinine-defined AKI after infant cardiac surgery, with the clearest risk information observed at the end of CPB. COP is better interpreted as a peri-CPB physiologic risk marker that should be considered alongside age and perfusion context, rather than as an independent prediction tool or a fixed therapeutic target.

title: Correlations between children's Wushu participation, posture, physical fitness, and visual indicators.
authorString: Wang H, Feng X, Li G.
abstractText:
Inroduction

At present, school‑aged children face three common public‑health concerns: functional postural abnormalities, poor physical fitness, and visual fatigue accompanied by early refractive changes. Targeted exercise programmes that simultaneously mitigate all three health problems remain scarce. This study aimed to examine associations between long‑term participation in a comprehensive standardized Wushu programme containing embedded visual‑relaxation exercises and children's postural, physical‑fitness, and ocular indicators.

Methods

This retrospective analysis extracted school physical‑and‑vision screening archives of 196 primary‑school students collected between July‑December 2025. According to after‑school activity records, participants were divided into an experimental group (n = 98, receiving consistent standardized Wushu training) and a control group (n = 98, routine physical education without systematic Wushu practice). Researchers did not provide additional training for participants. Data covering a unified 16‑week observation period were extracted following national standard assessment protocols. Linear mixed‑effects models, partial correlation analysis and forward‑stepwise regression were used, with adjustment for age, gender and daily screen‑reading time.

Results

After 16 weeks of observation, the experimental group demonstrated better body alignment and decreased postural anomalies including uneven shoulder height and trunk tilt (p < 0.01). Significantly higher scores for cardiorespiratory endurance, core strength, flexibility and balance were also observed, alongside significant group‑by‑time interactions (p < 0.01). Compared with the control group, children participating in the Wushu programme achieved better uncorrected distance visual acuity, ciliary‑muscle accommodation capacity and visual‑fatigue recovery performance (p < 0.01). Wushu‑participation frequency and duration were independent positive correlates of improved posture, physical fitness and visual function (p < 0.01). Notably, improvements in visual function may partly derive from embedded visual‑relaxation drills rather than Wushu movements alone.

Discussion

Given its retrospective archival design, causal inferences cannot be established. These real‑world correlational findings provide evidence to support school‑sport planning targeting children's physical and visual health.

title: The correlation between epicardial adipose tissue thickness and left ventricular systolic function in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus.
authorString: Lin S, Zhang S, Zhou H.
abstractText:
Background

Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) can cause myocardial damage and left ventricular dysfunction in patients. Abnormal deposition of epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) can promote the occurrence and development of cardiovascular diseases. The aim of this study was to investigate changes in EAT thickness in patients with SLE and apply two-dimensional speckle tracking echocardiography (2D-STE) to study the correlation between EAT and left ventricular systolic function.

Patients and methods

This case-control study recruited a total of 67 SLE patients as the case group and 31 healthy individuals as the control group. Left ventricular systolic function parameters were measured using 2D-STE. Changes and correlations in laboratory indicators, EAT, and left ventricular systolic function parameters were compared between groups.

Results

Compared with the control group, the case group showed significantly increased EAT and diastolic left ventricular posterior wall thickness (LVPWD) (P<0.05). High-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), apical two-chamber longitudinal strain (AP2C LS), apical three-chamber longitudinal strain (AP3C LS), apical four-chamber longitudinal strain (AP4C LS), and global longitudinal strain (GLS) were significantly reduced (P < 0.05). The 18-segment left ventricular longitudinal strain was further grouped according to coronary artery supply; the LAD, RCA, and LCX groups in the patient cohort all showed reductions compared with the healthy control group (P < 0.05). Spearman correlation analysis revealed that EAT was negatively correlated with GLS (r = -0.39, P < 0.05), LAD group (r = -0.26, P < 0.05), RCA group (r = -0.47, P < 0.05), and LCX group (r = -0.29, P < 0.05), and positively correlated with duration of illness (DT) (r = 0.41, P < 0.05) and age (r = 0.45, P < 0.05). Multiple linear regression analysis confirmed that EAT is an important influencing factor of left ventricular longitudinal strain function (P < 0.05).

Conclusion

Increased epicardial adipose tissue thickness is negatively correlated with left ventricular systolic function. EAT can effectively reflect changes in left ventricular systolic function in SLE patients, providing a basis for clinical management and early intervention.

title: Combination of serum AIM2 and caspase-5 as a predictor of unfavorable prognosis in children with lobar pneumonia: a prospective cohort study.
authorString: Liu L, Qi X, Zhang L, Jiang J, Lyu W, Hu Y, Huo P.
abstractText:
Objective

To validate whether serum levels of absent in melanoma 2 (AIM2) and caspase-5 can serve as early combined biomarkers of unfavorable prognosis in children with lobar pneumonia.

Methods

From February 2022 to June 2025, 475 children aged 1-14 years with first-episode lobar pneumonia were prospectively enrolled at Hebei Children's Hospital. Patients were divided into a favorable-prognosis group (n = 395) and an unfavorable-prognosis group (n = 80) based on treatment outcomes assessed during outpatient follow-up visits conducted 4-6 weeks after discharge. Fasting venous blood was drawn within 24 h of admission, and levels of AIM2 and caspase-5 were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Co-infection, symptom duration, antibiotic duration, hospital stay, C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) were recorded. Prognostic associations were examined using Pearson correlation, multivariable logistic regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Multicollinearity was assessed; a tolerance > 0.1 and a variance inflation factor (VIF) < 10 were considered acceptable.

Results

Serum AIM2 and caspase-5 levels were significantly higher in the unfavorable-prognosis group than in the favorable-prognosis group (both P < 0.001), and the two markers were positively correlated (r = 0.241, P < 0.001). Multivariable analysis identified co-infection and elevated levels of CRP, PCT, AIM2, and caspase-5 as independent risk factors for unfavorable prognosis. The VIF ranged from 1.047 to 1.131, indicating no multicollinearity. The combination of AIM2 and caspase-5 yielded an AUC of 0.839 (95% CI 0.798-0.879) for predicting unfavorable prognosis, with a sensitivity of 75.70% and a specificity of 78.75%, which was significantly superior to either biomarker alone (DeLong test: Z = -4.248, P < 0.001; Z = -2.998, P = 0.003). Nested model analysis demonstrated that adding AIM2 and caspase-5 to conventional variables (co-infection, CRP, PCT, and LDH) improved the AUC from 0.855 to 0.893 (DeLong test P = 0.047), indicating significant incremental predictive value.

Conclusion

Elevated serum AIM2 and caspase-5 are independent risk factors for unfavorable prognosis in children with lobar pneumonia. Their combination shows favorable predictive performance and may help identify high-risk children early.

title: Case Report: Concurrent maternal uniparental disomy-type Prader-Willi syndrome and X-linked G6PD deficiency-an area of focus on multi-gene screening for imprinting disorders.
authorString: Zhou Q, Yuan JM, Zou CC.
abstractText:
Background

Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS) is a rare imprinting disorder caused by functional impairment of imprinted genes within the paternal 15q11.2-q13 region. Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency is an X-linked hereditary disorder. Cases describing the coexistence of maternal uniparental disomy (UPD)-type PWS and G6PD deficiency are extremely scarce in global clinical reports. This article summarizes three male infant cases from our center and further sorts out previously published literature on PWS combined with other genetic disorders to analyze shared genetic characteristics and clinical phenotypes of such combined genetic conditions.

Methods

We performed retrospective sorting and analysis on three male infants simultaneously diagnosed with maternal UPD-type PWS and G6PD deficiency between August 2022 and December 2024 at the Children's Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine. Meanwhile, systematic retrieval of published literature from 1956 to 2025 was carried out across PubMed, Scopus Preview, Cochrane Reviews, Ovid and Semantic Scholar, and 28 documented PWS patients complicated by other single-gene or chromosomal genetic disorders were collated for comparative analysis. Genetic variant pathogenicity was judged against the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) genetic variant classification criteria.

Results

All three enrolled infants presented typical core manifestations of PWS, including neonatal hypotonia, feeding difficulties, and cryptorchidism, without jaundice, anemia, dark urine or other G6PD-related symptoms. Genetic testing confirmed maternally inherited hemizygous G6PD variants: one case carried c.152C >T classified as likely pathogenic, and two carried c.1388G >A classified as pathogenic. Literature collation identified 14 PWS patients complicated with sex chromosome abnormalities and 15 patients with autosomal chromosomal/genomic or monogenic disorders.

Conclusions

To our knowledge, this is the first case series reporting maternal UPD-type PWS combined with X-linked G6PD deficiency; it supplements novel clinical observations of this rare dual diagnosis and expands the recognized spectrum of PWS comorbid genetic disorders. For maternal UPD-PWS patients, expanded trio-whole exome sequencing (trio-WES) or trio-whole-genome sequencing (trio-WGS) is worth clinical consideration even without atypical phenotypes, to screen for hidden maternal multi-locus pathogenic variants. Given the small sample size of only three patients, additional multi-center data are needed to validate the clinical and genetic patterns of this combined phenotype. Keywords: Prader-Willi syndrome; Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency; Uniparental disomy; Comorbid genetic disorders; X-linked hereditary disease.

title: B-cell receptor repertoire remodeling in Kawasaki disease is associated with clonal expansion and distinct repertoire features in coronary artery lesions.
authorString: Xu Y, Lin X, Chen Y, Zhang X, Ma L, Yao X, Li J.
abstractText:
Background

Kawasaki disease (KD) is an acute systemic vasculitis in children, but the characteristics of the B-cell receptor (BCR) repertoire during acute disease and their association with coronary artery lesions (CALs) remain poorly understood.

Methods

High-throughput sequencing of BCR heavy-chain (BCR-H) CDR3 regions was performed in 22 children, including 9 healthy controls and 13 patients with KD, of whom 9 had no CAL and 4 had CAL. Repertoire diversity, clonal expansion, immunoglobulin isotype distribution, V-J gene usage, CDR3 characteristics, and inter-individual and cross-isotype repertoire sharing were systematically evaluated.

Results

KD exhibited reduced BCR repertoire diversity, with a significant decrease in IgM diversity. The repertoire showed increased contributions of high-frequency and hyperexpanded clonotypes, with the most pronounced expansion in patients with CAL. IgM displayed the strongest clonal remodeling, characterized by reduced low-frequency and increased highly abundant clonotypes. KD also showed selective alterations in IGHV usage and V-J gene pairing. CAL was associated with increased IGHA usage and changes in CDR3 amino acid composition. Substantial inter-individual CDR3 sharing was observed among KD patients, and 20 recurrent clonotypes absent from healthy controls were identified as candidate KD-associated sequences. Cross-isotype CDR3 sharing also tended to be higher in KD, particularly among patients with CAL.

Conclusions

Acute KD is characterized by substantial BCR repertoire remodeling, marked by selective IgM clonal expansion, repertoire convergence, and CAL-associated IgA-biased remodeling. These findings provide new insights into humoral immune dysregulation in KD and identify candidate B-cell clonotypes for further investigation of disease pathogenesis and coronary involvement.

title: Case Report: Discordant hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in monozygotic twins with LEOPARD syndrome and an identical PTPN11 c.1391G > C (p.Gly464Ala) mutation.
authorString: Xue X, Ning Y, Yao F, Zhang X, Song X.
abstractText: LEOPARD syndrome (LS; Noonan syndrome with multiple lentigines) is a rare autosomal dominant RASopathy in which PTPN11 mutations cause hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) with highly variable expressivity. We report adolescent monozygotic twin brothers carrying an identical PTPN11 c.1391G > C (p.Gly464Ala) mutation that arose de novo, who developed discordant cardiac phenotypes despite sharing a genome and an intrauterine and postnatal environment. The younger twin developed obstructive HCM with systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve and left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (peak resting gradient 36 mmHg, peak Valsalva gradient 61 mmHg), together with pectus excavatum and macroglossia; the older twin had non-obstructive HCM (maximal septal thickness 12 mm) with a patent foramen ovale. Both twins had multiple lentigines, facial dysmorphism, and sensorineural hearing loss requiring cochlear implantation. The younger twin was treated with a beta-blocker and activity restriction, whereas the older twin was managed with surveillance alone. This case demonstrates that an identical RASopathy mutation can produce divergent forms of HCM, supports a role for non-genetic modifiers in cardiovascular expression, and underscores the need for hemodynamics-guided, individualized cardiovascular management in LS.

title: The impact of heatwaves on maternal, neonatal and child health outcomes in Western Australian climate zones: A protocol paper for a retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Kelty E, Gebremedhin A, Mengersen K, Maloney SK, Le Souef P, Kearney M, Larcombe A, Rhaman A, Judge M, Price A, Wild K, Vardoulakis S, West M, Western Australian Healthy Environments And Lives Aboriginal Steering Group (WA HEAL ASG), Wyrwoll C.
abstractText:
Background

Rising global temperatures have resulted in an increase in the frequency and severity of heatwaves. Pregnancy is a time of substantial physiological change and thus maternal and neonatal health outcomes are susceptible to adverse effects of heat. There is a lack of knowledge about thermoregulation in pregnancy, including how effectively pregnant people adapt in different climate contexts and what specific environmental conditions present the largest thermoregulatory challenges. The primary aim of this study is to examine the associations between exposure to heatwaves during pregnancy and maternal, neonatal, and child health outcomes in Western Australia climatic regions.

Methods

All neonates born in Western Australia between 1991 and 2023 will be identified from perinatal records (~960,000 neonates). Perinatal records will be linked to weather data from the ERA5 database using Statistical Area 2 geocoding to identify heatwave exposed pregnancies. Commonly used definitions of heatwave exposure will be tested against three neonatal outcomes (pre-term birth, low birth weight, and congenital anomalies). From this, a single or small number of definition will be selected to examine maternal, neonatal, and child health outcomes using linked hospital, emergency department, and education assessment data, as well as data from the Western Australian congenital anomalies and death register. The association between heatwaves during pregnancy and health outcomes will be performed using generalised estimating equations, adjusting for covariates including, but not limited to, cigarette smoking, parity, maternal age, socio-economic status, and Aboriginality where appropriate. Stratification by socio-economic status and geographic region will also be carried out.

Discussion

Examining the association between exposure to heatwaves in pregnancy and maternal, neonatal and child outcomes is important given the increasing frequency of heatwaves. The study will highlight which heat definitions confers the highest vulnerability as well as demographic and geographic subgroups who are particularly vulnerable to the effects of heatwaves. It will provide valuable information for future public health planning, including targets for intervention.

title: Pulmonary arterial hypertension before closure of a persistent arterial duct (PDA) in children <12 months: clinical implications and outcome.
authorString: Callegari A, Meot M, Bonnet D, Malekzadeh-Milani S.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Int J Cardiol Congenit Heart Dis
journal.title: International journal of cardiology. Congenital heart disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Int J Cardiol Congenit Heart Dis

abstractText:
Background

The management of patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) in infants with pulmonary hypertension (PH) remains controversial due to concerns regarding irreversible pulmonary vascular disease and post-closure hemodynamic deterioration. Evidence in children <12 months is limited. We aim to describe the hemodynamics and outcomes of infants with isolated PDA and PH undergoing invasive evaluation and to identify clinical factors associated with PH persistence after closure.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed infants <12-months with isolated PDA and mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) > 20 mmHg who underwent right heart catheterization. Hemodynamics, procedural strategy, and clinical outcomes were assessed at 6-/12-months, and last follow-up.

Results

A total of 220 patients were included (mean age 154 ± 87 days; weight 5.7 ± 1.7 kg). mPAP was 36.5 ± 12.8 mmHg and Qp/Qs 1.9 ± 1.0. PDA closure was performed in 214 patients (186 transcatheter, 28 surgical). Cumulative mortality was 1.8%, occurring exclusively in patients with severe comorbidities. Persistent PH was noted in 8 patients (3.6%) at 6-months and 2 patients (0.9%) at 12-months and long-term follow-up. No cases of PH relapse were observed after successful closure. All persistent PH cases were associated with developmental lung disease or severe syndromic conditions. Infants without major comorbidity demonstrated resolution of PH after closure.

Conclusions

In infants with isolated PDA and PH, ductal closure within the 1 year is associated with near-universal normalization of pulmonary pressures. Persistent PH is uncommon and primarily confined to patients with developmental lung disease. Clinical and echocardiographic assessment combined with invasive hemodynamic should guide operability decisions.

title: Video laryngoscopy versus direct laryngoscopy for pediatric emergency tracheal intubation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Couto TB, Acworth J, Rech L, Katzenschlager S, Myburgh M, Scholefield BR, de Caen A, International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation ILCOR Pediatric Life Support Task Force.
abstractText:
Aim

To compare video laryngoscopy with direct laryngoscopy for pediatric intubation during cardiac arrest and peri-arrest scenarios.

Methods

This systematic review (PROSPERO CRD420251081694) searched MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane from inception to May 1, 2026. Two authors independently screened studies; data were extracted by one and independently verified by a second reviewer. Eligible studies compared video versus direct laryngoscopy in pediatric acute care; emergency department, intensive care, and prehospital settings. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and RoB2. Critical outcomes were survival to hospital discharge, first-pass intubation success, overall intubation success, and severe tracheal intubation-associated events. Additional data included study design, setting, age, operator type, and device. Meta-analyses used random-effects Mantel-Haenszel models reporting risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals. Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE.

Results

Eighteen studies (17 observational, 1 RCT). First-pass success was higher with video laryngoscopy (72.2% vs 69.0%; RR 1.11, 95% CI 1.06-1.16; very low certainty). Severe adverse events were less frequent with video laryngoscopy (7.7% vs 11.8%; RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.62-0.93; very low certainty). Overall success (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.99-1.01) and desaturation (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.77-1.01) were similar. No studies reported survival outcomes or data specific to cardiac arrest.

Conclusion

Among children undergoing emergency tracheal intubation, video laryngoscopy may be associated with improved first-pass success and fewer adverse events, although the certainty of evidence is very low and causal inferences are limited. No data were available for survival outcomes and cardiac arrest.

title: Discussing Future Treatment and Care in the ICU: Perspectives From Patients.
authorString: Smith MA, Zwisler AD, Nissen A, Michelsen J, Olsen HT, Wichmann S, Hansen PM, Walther LH, Le Greves S, Westergaard B, Jensen HI, Nystrup KB.
abstractText:
Introduction

Treatment in the intensive care unit (ICU) is usually predicated on curative treatment, but continuing all available treatment options may not always be beneficial for the patient or in line with their wishes. However, patients admitted to the ICU are often assessed as incapable of making decisions regarding their care; hence conversations about wishes for treatment are postponed. This study aimed to investigate the experiences of patients who participated in a conversation concerning treatment and care following ICU discharge based on the Danish version of the Recommended Summary Plan for Emergency Care and Treatment (ReSPECT) form.

Method

Semi-structured telephone interviews were conducted with patients who had a conversation about future treatment and care with an intensivist using the ReSPECT form during an ICU admission between November 2024 and July 2025. Relatives who participated in the conversation and were present during the interviews were asked to elaborate on their experiences of the conversation's timing and how they felt about participating in the conversation. Data was analysed using content analysis.

Results

Nineteen patients were included in the study, of whom 15 patients (83%) participated in a telephone interview. Two themes were identified: Timing of the conversation and Clarifying goals of care and options. Based on these, four sub-themes were identified, two for each theme: Too soon, but not much later; Wishes in accordance; Hard, but necessary and Communicating in an understandable manner. Most patients were satisfied with having had a conversation about future treatment and care. Patients found the conversation relevant and necessary. The intensivists were praised for their communication skills and their ability to know and explain recommendations for future treatment and care. However, most patients believed that the conversation was conducted too soon after recovering from intensive care. They would have preferred to have had the conversation later during their admission.

Conclusions

Most participating ICU patients found a conversation about future treatment and care relevant but preferred it to be held after ICU discharge. Future research should investigate the benefits of incorporating intensivists in these conversations in general wards.

Editorial comment

In this prospective study, former ICU patients were interviewed and asked about their experiences and opinions regarding a structured ReSPECT discussion that had been conducted in the end of their ICU stay. The goal of that interview was advance care planning, involving the patients and their family members. This study reports a qualitative analysis of interviews conducted at least 4 weeks later. Two main themes and four subthemes were identified. Almost all patients remembered having had the discussion, but the content was less clearly remembered. ICU physicians' communication skills were appreciated. The study assesses a function of our daily work from patient and family perspective, and discusses important issues such as optimal timing of the advance care planning.

authorString: Karpova OB, Blinkova LN.

abstractText: The diseases of the circulatory system (DCS) rank first in general structure of morbidity and are leading cause of adult mortality worldwide. The actuality of the study is related to prevalence of DCS in Russia and to trend of its increase in younger population. According to forecasts of the WHO experts, the rate of occurrence of DCS will continue to rise due to increasing of percentage of elderly people in society, intensive pace of life and impact of harmful behavioral habits on health. This analytical review covers the adult morbidity data published in 2024 by the Federal State Statistics Service as well as the results of the study "Sample Survey of Behavioral Factors Affecting Public Health and Behavioral Risk Factors for Diseases (VNSZN-2024)". The authors assume that comprehensive approach to lifestyle modification and medical control of behavioral risk factors remains crucial for reducing risk of development of DCS and improving their prognosis.
