title: Frailty Rather Than Sonographic Muscle Measurement Predicts Outcome in Liver Cirrhosis.
authorString: Kremer WM, Schwarz A, Dumont MC, Gairing SJ, Sivanathan V, Galle PR, Sprinzl MF, Schleicher EM, Labenz C.

journal.title: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle

abstractText:
Background

Sarcopenia and frailty are frequent in patients with liver cirrhosis and are associated with morbidity and mortality. Given the limitations of computed tomography (CT) for routine assessment of muscle loss and the need for practical bedside assessment, we aimed to compare sonographic muscle thickness measurement and the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) for their prognostic value in patients with liver cirrhosis.

Methods

In this study, data of prospectively recruited patients with liver cirrhosis (both in- and outpatients) treated at a tertiary care centre were retrospectively analysed. Sonographic muscle thickness measurement was used to calculate the feather thigh muscle thickness index (fTMTI) and the compression thigh muscle thickness index (cTMTI). Frailty was assessed using the Clinical Frailty Scale. Patients were followed for liver transplantation or death.

Results

In total, 153 patients were included with a median Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) of 18 (Interquartile range (IQR) 10; 24). Ninety-five patients (62.0%) were male, and 70 patients (46%) were recruited in the outpatient setting. During the 90-day follow-up period, 71 patients (46.4%) either died or underwent liver transplantation. Outpatients had more muscle mass than inpatients and a lower CFS (fTMTI 19.1 mm/m vs. 12.1 mm/m, p < 0.001 and CFS 3 vs. 5, p < 0.001). In multivariable Cox-regression models adjusted for age and MELD score, a higher CFS remained independently associated with mortality and liver transplantation (LT) (HR 1.25 (1.14; 1.63), p < 0.001), whereas fTMTI and cTMTI were not consistently associated with a poorer prognosis (fTMTI HR 1.52 (0.68; 3.42), p = 0.300; cTMTI HR 1.01 (0.61; 1.68), p > 0.9). Subgroup analyses in men confirmed a superior prognostic value of CFS (HR 1.51 (1.17; 1.94), p = 0.001) over sonographic muscle thickness measurement (cTMTI HR 0.94 (0.84; 1.04), p = 0.200; fTMTI HR 0.93 (0.88; 1.00), p = 0.039).

Conclusion

CFS is robustly associated with poorer prognosis in patients with liver cirrhosis and seems to be superior to sonographic muscle thickness measurement of the thigh.

title: Can Spleen T1 Mapping Be Used as a Marker of Adenosine Response in Cardiac MRI?
authorString: Solis-Barquero SM, Ezponda A, Aramendía-Vidaurreta V, Vidorreta M, Pascual M, Bastarrika G, Fernández-Seara MA.
abstractText: Splenic switch-off, defined as the visible reduction in splenic perfusion during adenosine stress, can be used as a marker of adequate adenosine response in cardiac stress MRI studies, which can be assessed after the study. Moreover, there is some evidence regarding the use of T1 mapping for the evaluation of splenic switch-off during the study. The aim of this work is to further investigate splenic T1 mapping as a method for quantitatively assessing splenic switch-off, given the limited existing data. Patients with suspected coronary artery disease were scanned at 1.5 T with the routine clinical protocol for stress perfusion cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), including a T1 mapping sequence at rest and during adenosine stress. Visual assessment of first-pass images was used as the reference standard for detecting splenic switch-off. Semi-quantitative analysis of splenic perfusion was performed based on the signal intensity curves and signal changes (ΔSI) were calculated. T1 maps were used to obtain T1 value changes in the spleen from rest to stress (ΔT1<sub>spleen</sub>). Statistical analysis was assessed using an align rank transform followed by a mixed analysis of variance, with Bonferroni corrected post hoc tests. A total of 74.5% (n = 35/47) of analyzed patients experienced splenic switch-off according to the visual assessment. Statistically significant differences were found in splenic T1 between rest and stress only in the switch-off group (p < 0.001), with lower T1 values during stress. There was significant positive weak correlation (ρ<sub>s</sub> = 0.37, p = 0.01) between splenic ΔT1 and ΔSI based on first-pass. ROC curves demonstrated that ΔT1<sub>spleen</sub> classified the failed switch-off and positive switch-off groups with a specificity of 75% and a sensitivity of 80% (AUC: 81.2%, 95% CI: 66.7%-95.8%). This work indicates that the splenic T1 value change has the potential to identify splenic switch-off during adenosine stress CMR in a clinical population.

title: Deep learning and dual-domain fusion of temporal and spectrotemporal SCG for valvular heart disease classification.
authorString: Kim J, Choudhary T, Hassanuzzaman M, Kamaleswaran R.
abstractText: Heart valve disease (HVD) is a growing cause of cardiovascular morbidity, yet accessible screening tools remain limited. Tri-axial seismocardiogram (SCG) signals capture mechanical signatures of both stenosis and regurgitation, but their non-stationary nature and subtle inter-lesion morphological differences challenge robust classification from a single representation. This study proposes an electrocardiogram (ECG)-free dual-domain deep learning framework that combines a 1D convolutional-recurrent encoder of raw SCG waveforms with a 2D EfficientNet encoder of continuous wavelet transform scalograms, integrating temporal and spectrotemporal representations through feature-level fusion. The framework was evaluated on primary valve lesion classification in 94 patients, with an additional exploratory analysis of multi-valvular, aortic-stenosis-dominant disease. Under patient-level stratified group cross-validation, the fused model achieved the highest mean accuracy (65.3%; 95% CI, 59.8%-70.7%), exceeding both unimodal encoders and the majority-class (35.2%) and covariate-only (39.1%) baselines. The same mean performance ordering was preserved when the image backbone was replaced, although the confidence intervals overlap at this cohort size. Under the segment-level protocol used in prior studies, the framework achieved 99.63% accuracy, with faster training convergence and more compact, separable feature clusters than either unimodal encoder. These findings support the value of combining temporal and spectrotemporal SCG representations and demonstrate its potential for ECG-free HVD classification under patient-independent evaluation.

title: Corrigendum to "Comparison of far-field and peak frequency electrogram characteristics at the earliest activation sites during idiopathic ventricular arrhythmias: A novel index to predict ablation success" Heart Rhythm, Volume 23, Issue 3, pp 645- 653, March 2026.
A Novel Resource-Adapted Neurocritical Care Education Program in Tanzania: Implementation, Outcomes, and a Framework for Sustainable Training.
authorString: Rajagopalan S, Koffman L, Rincon F, Puri N, Moledina S.
abstractText:
Importance/objective

Neurologic emergencies contribute disproportionately to morbidity and mortality in sub-Saharan Africa, yet structured neurocritical care training remains limited. Emergency Neurologic Life Support (ENLS) standardizes early management of neurologic emergencies, but implementation in resource-limited settings requires contextual adaptation. Limited access to neuroimaging and monitoring compounds diagnostic uncertainty. Portable neuroultrasound (NeuroUS) offers a feasible bedside adjunct. We developed, implemented, and evaluated Tanzania's first resource-adapted neurocritical care educational program, including hands-on NeuroUS training in a low- and middle-income country (LMIC) setting.

Design setting participants main outcomes and measures

We conducted a prospective observational study during a 2-day in-person training program (October 2025). Multidisciplinary healthcare professionals caring for neurocritical care patients completed pre- and postcourse assessments evaluating medical knowledge, self-reported knowledge, and confidence across ENLS and NeuroUS domains (5-point Likert scale). Ordinal Likert outcomes were summarized using median and interquartile range (IQR) and compared using two-sided Mann-Whitney U tests. Correct-response proportions were compared using Fisher exact tests. Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate adjustment was applied within each outcome family.

Results

Twenty-two participants completed precourse assessments; 17 completed postcourse assessments. Self-reported medical knowledge improved across 15 of 16 domains. The largest effects were observed for NeuroUS knowledge, which increased from a median of 1.5 (IQR, 1-2) to 4 (IQR, 4-5; rank-biserial, r = 0.85; 95% CI, 0.64-1.00; q < 0.001); Broad-Reaching Acute Interventions in Neurocritical Care, from 3 (IQR, 2-3) to 4 (IQR, 4-5; r = 0.73; 95% CI, 0.48-0.93; q < 0.001); and intracranial hypertension and herniation, from 3 (IQR, 3-4) to 5 (IQR, 4-5; r = 0.70; 95% CI, 0.45-0.89; q < 0.001). Confidence scores were higher in eight of 16 domains after adjustment. Both NeuroUS diagnostic-application items demonstrated large postcourse differences (q < 0.001). Correct-response proportions increased across all six exploratory knowledge items, but none remained statistically significant after adjustment for multiple comparisons. Ninety-four percent found the program relevant to their practice.

Conclusions and relevance

Implementation of resource-limited ENLS integrated with structured neuroultrasound is feasible and significantly improved knowledge and confidence. This hybrid approach represents a scalable education model for LMICs.

title: Decitabine plus busulfan-cyclophosphamide versus busulfan-cyclophosphamide myeloablative conditioning before allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation for reducing risk of relapse in adult KMT2A‑rearranged leukaemia in China: an open-label, multicentre, randomised phase 3 trial.
authorString: Hu Z, Fan Z, Dai M, He H, Jin H, Sun Z, Huang F, Xu N, Liu Q, Li Y, Dong Y, Zhu P, Liu C, Zeng Y, Sun J, Sun R, Xuan L, Liu Q.
abstractText:
Background

An unmet need persists for optimal myeloablative conditioning before allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) in adult KMT2A‑rearranged leukaemia. We investigated whether decitabine plus busulfan-cyclophosphamide (DAC-BuCy) conditioning reduced the risk of relapse compared with busulfan-cyclophosphamide (BuCy) conditioning.

Methods

In this open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial at eight transplantation centres in China, eligible patients were aged 14-65 years, had morphologically confirmed KMT2A-rearranged leukaemia, and had an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-2. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) before HSCT to DAC-BuCy (intravenous decitabine 20 mg/m2 once a day on days -14 to -10, intravenous busulfan 3·2 mg/kg once a day on days -7 to -4, and intravenous cyclophosphamide 60 mg/kg once a day on days -3 to -2) or BuCy (same dose and duration of busulfan and cyclophosphamide). Randomisation was done with permuted blocks (block size four) with no stratification and was implemented through an independent, interactive, web-based response system. The primary endpoint was 2-year cumulative incidence of relapse in the intention-to-treat population. Safety was assessed in all patients who received treatment. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03596892) and is complete.

Findings

Between May 1, 2019, and Jan 31, 2023, 130 patients were randomised to receive a DAC-BuCy (n=65; 34 [52%] female and 31 [48%] male) or BuCy (n=65; 29 [45%] female and 36 [55%] male) regimen. Median follow-up was 34·7 months (IQR 30·2-52·5). 2-year cumulative incidence of relapse was 12% (95% CI 6-22) in the DAC-BuCy group and 29% (19-41) in the BuCy group (hazard ratio 0·41 [0·20-0·87]; p=0·017). The most common grade 3-5 adverse events were infections or infestations (DAC-BuCy group 27 [42%] and BuCy group 25 [38%]), acute graft-versus-host disease (DAC-BuCy group 23 [35%] and BuCy group 22 [34%]), and gastrointestinal disorders (DAC-BuCy group 14 [22%] and BuCy group 15 [23%]). Four (6%) patients in the DAC-BuCy group and five (8%) patients in the BuCy group died from adverse events, of which two were due to regimen-related toxicities: one nervous system disorder in the DAC-BuCy group and one cardiac disorder in the BuCy group.

Interpretation

The addition of decitabine to BuCy conditioning reduced the risk of relapse with an acceptable safety profile in adult patients with KMT2A‑rearranged leukaemia and could be a suitable therapeutic option for this population.

Funding

The National Natural Science Foundation of China, the National Key Research and Development Program of China, the Science and Technology Program of Guangdong Province, the Non-communicable Chronic Diseases-National Science and Technology Major Project, the Natural Science Foundation of Guangdong Province, the Science and Technology Planning Project of Guangzhou, and the Outstanding Youth Cultivation Program of Nanfang Hospital, Southern Medical University.

Translation

For the Chinese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

title: The impact of defects of the atrial septum on procedural complexity, complications, and outcomes of transvenous lead extraction.
authorString: Nowosielecka D, Jacheć W, Starck C, Polewczyk A, Mościcka D, Kutarski A.
abstractText:
Background

Patients with defects of the atrial septum (DAS) undergoing transvenous lead extraction (TLE) may be at increased risk of systemic embolism due to transient right-to-left shunting. However, data on the prevalence and clinical relevance of DAS in patients undergoing TLE remain limited.

Methods

This retrospective study included 3637 patients undergoing TLE between 2006 and 2024 with complete preprocedural assessment of the atrial septum and at least 3 years of follow-up. We evaluated the prevalence of DAS and its association with procedural complexity, major complications, and survival.

Results

DAS was identified in 3.71% of patients. Patent foramen ovale was present in 2.45%, secundum atrial septal defect in 1.15%, and both defects in 0.08%. Most defects were small, with predominant left-to-right shunting. Patients with DAS more frequently had lead-related infective endocarditis and vegetations on transesophageal echocardiography (p < 0.001). TLE procedures in patients with DAS were more complex, with longer extraction times and more frequent use of advanced extraction tools. Despite higher predicted procedural risk, the incidence of major complications, including stroke, was low. DAS was not associated with increased in-hospital, 30-day, 1-year, or 3-year mortality.

Conclusions

In this large TLE cohort, DAS was uncommon and associated with greater procedural complexity, but not with a higher incidence of major complications or worse long-term survival. Clinically apparent systemic embolic events were rare.

title: Prognostic Impact of Late Gadolinium Enhancement on Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events and Time-Varying Attenuation of Risk in Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Ma L, Li Y, Zhang H, Zheng Y, Wang P, Niu Y, Zhu L.
abstractText:
Objectives

To investigate the prognostic value of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) extent for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) patients and characterize the dynamic pattern of its risk effect over time.

Methods

We retrospectively enrolled patients who underwent Cardiac Magnetic Resonance (CMR) between 2020 and 2024, with MACE (cardiac death, heart failure re-hospitalization, or sustained ventricular arrhythmia) as the endpoint. Patients were stratified by MACE occurrence. Schoenfeld residual testing showed borderline deviation of the proportional hazards (PH) assumption for LGE extent (LV mass percentage). Thus, a time-dependent Cox model (Extended Cox PHs Model) with an LGE extent × follow-up time interaction term was built to assess dynamic hazard ratio changes, and independent MACE risk factors were identified.

Results

Among 173 DCM patients (age 47 ± 15 years, 105 males), 46 (26.6%) experienced MACE after a mean follow-up of 27 ± 16 months. The time-dependent Cox model identified LGE extent (baseline HR: 1.243, 95% CI: 1.162-1.329, p < 0.001), the LGE extent × time interaction (HR: 0.993, 95% CI: 0.989-0.997, p = 0.001), and LV end-diastolic volume index (LVEDVi; HR = 1.008, 95% CI: 1.003-1.014, p = 0.001) as independent MACE predictors. Notably, the risk effect of LGE extent demonstrated time-dependent attenuation.

Conclusion

LV LGE extent and LVEDVi independently predict MACE in DCM patients. The early prognostic value of LGE extent suggests a critical time window for early fibrosis intervention.

title: Natural Is Not Necessarily Safer: A Probabilistic Assessment of Risk-Risk Trade-Offs Between Cardiovascular and Genotoxic Effects of Food Preservatives.
authorString: Ling MP, Lee YH.

journal.title: Risk analysis : an official publication of the Society for Risk Analysis

abstractText: To extend product shelf life, it is especially important to prevent foods from deteriorating. Apart from the traditional methods of adding salt or sugar in large amounts, other additives, such as food preservatives, can also be applied to achieve the aim of food preservation. This study employs probabilistic risk assessment (PRA) to quantify human health impacts associated with exposure to sodium chloride, sucrose, benzoic acid (BA), and sorbic acid (SA), utilizing cardiovascular disease (CVD) prevalence and micronuclei (MN) induction frequency as dual epidemiological and toxicological endpoints. We evaluated the risks of natural and artificial preservatives in products, such as pickled vegetables, fermented vegetables, candied fruits, and preserved fruits, with the same antibacterial efficiency and under controlled pH and water activity conditions. The results revealed a significant risk trade-off: Although the CVD prevalence associated with natural preservatives reached 16.2%-18.2% across different food categories, the MN frequency induced by artificial preservatives remained comparatively lower at 7.4%-11.6%. The results suggest that combining natural and artificial preservatives may reduce sodium chloride or sucrose intake and the associated cardiovascular health risks compared with using natural preservatives alone. These findings indicate that although limiting high-sodium and high-sugar foods is crucial for cardiovascular health, dietary exposure to artificial preservatives, such as BA and SA, was associated with relatively low estimated genotoxic risks, though potential hepatic or renal impacts warrant further investigation.

title: PAK4 as a cardiometabolic node: tissue-specific metabolic control, cardiovascular remodeling, and therapeutic trade-offs.
authorString: Nguyen THT, Tran KD, Pham TK, Seol JE, Shimizu I, Kim HK, Han J.

journal.title: The Korean journal of physiology & pharmacology : official journal of the Korean Physiological Society and the Korean Society of Pharmacology

abstractText: Cardiometabolic disease reflects interdependent dysfunction across adipose tissue, liver, skeletal muscle, vasculature, and heart. p21-activated kinase 4 (PAK4), a group II serine/threonine kinase controlling cytoskeletal organization and development, has emerged as a nutrient-responsive regulator in metabolic tissues. We position PAK4 as a candidate cardiometabolic node rather than a proven master regulator or direct energy sensor. Established mechanisms include suppression of adipocyte lipolysis and browning, hepatocyte NCoR1-PPARα-dependent fattyacid oxidation and ketogenesis, skeletal-muscle AMPKα2-GLUT4 signaling, together with promotion of hepatic stellate-cell activation via YAP phosphorylation at Thr428. These programs could alter the substrate, inflammatory, redox, and endocrine environment encountered by the cardiovascular system. We refine the hepatic ketone deficiency concept into a PAK4-ketone supply-demand mismatch hypothesis: reduced hepatic ketogenesis may limit adaptive ketone availability when myocardial demand rises, though inter-organ causality remains unproven. PAK4 is essential for embryonic cardiac morphogenesis, and limited adult endothelial studies suggest stress-protective roles in ischemic and inflammatory settings, whereas functions in adult cardiomyocytes, fibroblasts, and vascular smooth muscle cells remain largely undefined. An exploratory scan of Gene Expression Omnibus datasets identified recurrent nominal increases in PAK4 mRNA in selected failing or remodeled human myocardium and steatotic liver, but no universal cardiometabolic signature. These findings define a tissue-dependent therapeutic dilemma in which peripheral metabolic benefits of PAK4 inhibition or degradation may coexist with uncharacterized cardiac, isoform, and exposure-related risks. Resolving this paradox will require adult inducible cell-specific models, inter-organ flux studies, cardiac proteomics and phosphoproteomics, and comparison of catalytic inhibitors, degraders, and tissuedirected delivery systems.

title: In Silico Molecular Docking and SwissADME Prediction of Cinnamaldehyde Protection Against the PbO Ps-Induced Morphological and Histopathological Teratogenicity.
authorString: Qadeer S, Ashraf A, Awan S, Akram S.
abstractText:
Background

This study investigated the antiteratogenic effects of cinnamaldehyde against lead oxide nanoparticulate (PbO-Ps)-induced developmental toxicity in chick embryos.

Methods

PbO-Ps were synthesized using a chemical method and characterized by UV-Vis spectroscopy, FTIR, and SEM. Fertilized Gallus gallus domesticus eggs (n = 56) were randomly assigned to four experimental groups: procedural control (sterile normal saline), PbO-Ps (33 μg/egg), PbO-Ps plus low-dose cinnamaldehyde (33 + 33.2 μg/egg), and PbO-Ps plus high-dose cinnamaldehyde (33 + 66.4 μg/egg). Morphological and histopathological outcomes were assessed. ANOVA was performed to compare outcomes among groups. Molecular docking using AutoDock 4.2 evaluated interactions of cinnamaldehyde with apo p110α/p85α, apo p110δ/p85α, and PTEN. Drug-likeness and pharmacokinetic properties were evaluated using SwissADME.

Results

PbO-Ps characterization revealed a characteristic absorption peak at 236 nm, Pb-O vibrations at 450-550 cm-¹, and irregular plate-like particles with apparent sizes of approximately 100-400 nm. On Day 14, PbO-Ps exposure caused growth retardation, limb and craniofacial deformities, and poor feather development. Persistent morphological abnormalities, impaired movement, and poor coordination were observed after Day 21 in the PbO-Ps group compared with controls. Cinnamaldehyde ameliorated these effects, with significantly greater protection observed at the higher dose (p < 0.05). Severe hepatic, neuronal, and cardiac tissue damage was observed following PbO-Ps exposure, whereas cinnamaldehyde reduced histopathological abnormalities in a dose-dependent manner. Molecular docking showed that cinnamaldehyde interacted with all three target proteins, with the strongest binding affinity observed for apo p110α/p85α.

Conclusions

The findings indicate that high-dose cinnamaldehyde significantly mitigated PbO-Ps-induced developmental toxicity and teratogenicity in chick embryos. Further studies, including molecular dynamics simulations and long-term in vivo investigations, are warranted to clarify the underlying protective mechanisms and evaluate post-hatch effects.

title: Vascular Abnormalities in the Hand and Wrist: State-of-the-Art Multimodality Imaging.
authorString: Bretzman J, Bookwalter C, Bendel E, Bjarnason H, Rajiah PS.

journal.title: Radiographics : a review publication of the Radiological Society of North America, Inc

abstractText: Vascular abnormalities are less common in the hand and wrist than in the lower extremities but can result in significant morbidity if unrecognized or untreated. The unique vascular architecture of the hand and wrist, with a dense network of arterial anastomoses, confers resilience to ischemia, but the superficial location makes them vulnerable to trauma and occupational injury. The authors describe and illustrate a comprehensive multimodality imaging approach to the diagnosis and evaluation of vascular abnormalities of the hand and wrist. They begin with an overview of vascular anatomy and normal variants, including a persistent median artery. Multimodality imaging, including US, CT angiography, MR angiography, and digital subtraction angiography, is reviewed with a focus on strengths, limitations, and clinical utility. Dynamic imaging techniques and photon-counting CT are highlighted for their evolving roles. A wide spectrum of vascular diseases, including atherosclerosis, trauma, iatrogenic injury, embolism, hypothenar hammer syndrome, hand-arm vibration syndrome, vasculitis, and frostbite, as well as their imaging appearances, are discussed. Vascular anomalies, including vascular malformations and vascular neoplasms, are also reviewed. The role of imaging in hand transplantation is addressed. The authors provide a framework for recognizing vascular diseases in the hand and wrist and selecting the appropriate imaging modality. Familiarity with vascular anatomy, imaging findings, and clinical context is essential for timely diagnosis, guiding management, and preserving limb function.

title: The Relationship Between Skeletal Muscle Mitochondrial Function and Cardiac Workload During Exercise in Young Healthy Subjects.
authorString: Jeskanen T, Ylinen VP, Valtonen RIP, Stenbäck V, Mäkelä KA, Kerkelä R, Junttila JM, Pöllänen N, Kivelä R, Kolari K, Pirinen E, Herzig KH, Tulppo MP.
abstractText: Exaggerated cardiac workload responses to incremental exercise are associated with the development of hypertension and future cardiovascular events. We hypothesized that skeletal muscle mitochondrial function is associated with cardiac workload, quantified as Rate Pressure Product (RPP), during exercise. Healthy adults (n = 18; 9 females; age 25 ± 4 years) performed a maximal exercise test on a cycle ergometer. The test began at 0 W and followed an incremental protocol starting at 40 W, with load increases every 2 minutes until exhaustion. Breath-by-breath gas exchange was measured to determine peak oxygen uptake and the respiratory compensatory point (RCP). Heart rate (HR) and systolic blood pressure (BP) were recorded at each load to calculate RPP. The cardiac workload response to exercise was defined as the change in RPP from 0 W to the intensity corresponding to RCP (ΔRPP). Muscle biopsies from the vastus lateralis were collected on separate days to assess mitochondrial respiration. ΔRPP from 0 W to RCP intensity was 18181 ± 2147 mmHg·bpm and Complex I mediated respiration was 31.9 ± 13.7 pmol·mg<sup>-1</sup> s<sup>-1</sup>. ΔRPP was correlated only with Complex I (r = -0.69, p = 0.002) and sex (r = 0.50, p = 0.035). In a forward stepwise linear regression analysis with ΔRPP as the dependent variable and baseline RPP, sex, and complex I mediated respiration as predictors, complex I mediated respiration was the only variable significantly associated with ΔRPP (adjusted R<sup>2</sup> = 0.44; unstandardized β = -107; 95% CI:-167 to -47; p = 0.002). The cardiac workload response to exercise is strongly associated with skeletal muscle mitochondrial function in young normotensive individuals.

title: UCHL1 as a Biomarker of Brain Injury in Neonates and Infants Undergoing Cardiac Surgery: An Exploratory Study.
authorString: Swangwong S, Alhamdan F, Nishiori H, Maisat W, Odegard KC, Soriano S, Koutsogiannaki S, Ishibashi N, Yuki K.

journal.title: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology

abstractText: As survival rates following pediatric cardiac surgery have improved, neurodevelopmental impairment has emerged as a significant long-term comorbidity. Neonates and infants are particularly vulnerable and are at the highest risk for neurodevelopmental impairment. Imaging study has identified new white matter injury in up to 20%-50% of this cohort postoperatively. Currently there is no clinical modality to accurately detect neurological events in real time during cardiac surgery. Brain imaging remains the gold standard for identifying cerebral injury, but it is only feasible postoperatively. In this study we intended to determine a plasma marker suitable to detect intraoperative brain injury by examining infant piglets undergoing cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) and neonates/infants undergoing cardiac surgery on CPB. We compared two different CPB strategies; full-flow bypass alone and bypass involving circulatory arrest (CA) in infant piglets where CA was associated with post CPB neurodevelopmental impairment in our previous study. We found that ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCHL1), a protein abundantly expressed in the neuronal body, was elevated in the blood after CA in infant piglets. CA group showed more proinflammatory profiles than full-flow bypass group. Histological analysis of piglet brain demonstrated that neurons underwent more apoptosis after CA, along with lower UCHL1 expression. Plasma proteomics analysis in infant piglets suggested the disruption of blood brain barrier (BBB) after CA compared to full-flow bypass. We hypothesized that UCHL1 could serve as a promising neurological injury marker in patients, too. We compared neonates and infants who underwent full-flow bypass alone and bypass involving CA/regional perfusion (RP) groups. Neonates and infants subjected to CA/RP had higher odds of having neurodevelopmental impairment compared to full-flow bypass group. CA/RP group showed more proinflammatory profiles than full-flow bypass group. Plasma proteomics analysis in neonates and infants also demonstrated similar findings in CA/RP arm compared to full-flow arm as we observed in piglets. UCHL1 level at the rewarming during CPB showed highest area under the curve (AUC) value of 0.7022 (95% CI 0.5692-0.8287). Overall, this study suggested UCHL1 to be a promising biomarker of brain injury associated with neurodevelopmental impairment following pediatric cardiac surgery involving CPB.

title: Nanozyme-Driven Next-Generation miRNA Biosensing.
authorString: Deshwal A, Tripathi RM.

journal.title: Wiley interdisciplinary reviews. Nanomedicine and nanobiotechnology

abstractText: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are small, noncoding RNA molecules nearly 22 nucleotides in length that contribute significantly to regulating gene expression. Their aberrant expression patterns are associated with disease progression, including cardiovascular and neurological disorders and cancer. However, the rapid detection of miRNAs remains challenging due to their low abundance, sequence similarity, and degradation. Conventional methods of detecting miRNAs, such as Northern blotting, microarray analysis, quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), and next-generation sequencing (NGS), offer significant benefits for miRNA profiling, though they have drawbacks, including limited specificity, complex workflows, relatively high cost, and specialized equipment requirements. Advanced methodologies driven by nanotechnology, especially those that combine clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)/Cas approaches, provide revolutionary developments. Nanozymes enhance the stability and biocompatibility of catalytic amplification, while CRISPR technologies enable real-time, multiplex, and ultrasensitive miRNA detection with accurate sequence recognition. The rapidly expanding field encompasses diverse nanozyme architectures, recognition mechanisms, amplification strategies, and signal-transduction platforms, providing a broad basis for critically assessing advances, limitations, and emerging opportunities in nanozyme-enabled miRNA biosensing. Nanozyme-enabled miRNA detection has evolved across diverse sensing platforms, such as colorimetric and optical assays, sophisticated photoelectrochemical (PEC) and electrochemiluminescence (ECL) biosensors, and portable and paper-based diagnostic technologies. The convergence of nanozyme catalysis, CRISPR-based recognition, and advanced sensing strategies holds promise for sensitive, selective, and portable miRNA diagnostics.

title: The Same Gain for Less Pain When Using Rating of Perceived Exertion Instead of Maximal Aerobic Speed to Prescribe High-Intensity Interval Training.
authorString: Bok D, Gulin J, Miklić D, Foster C.
abstractText: The purpose of the study was to investigate if rating of perceived exertion (RPE) is superior to maximal aerobic speed (MAS) for maximizing time spent ≥ 90% of maximal oxygen uptake (t ≥ 90% VO<sub>2max</sub>) during high-intensity interval training (HIIT). Thirteen male physical education students volunteered to perform maximal incremental exercise test and two HIIT sessions. The HIIT sessions included three 3-min intervals prescribed at either RPE 5 (HIIT<sub>RPE</sub>) or 85% MAS (HIIT<sub>MAS</sub>) interspersed with 2-min passive rest. Borg's category-ratio-10 (CR-10) scale was used for RPE-based HIIT prescription. Heart rate (HR), respiratory gas exchange and running speed were continuously monitored during testing and training sessions. Blood lactate concentration was assessed within the first minute after concluding the HIIT bout. Peak HR (183.7 ± 11 vs. 187.9 ± 9 bpm, p = 0.028), peak respiratory frequency (ƒ<sub>R</sub>) (56.7 ± 5.5 vs. 59.8 ± 6.4 bpm, p = 0.046), blood lactate concentration (9.6 ± 2.8 vs. 11.7 ± 2.3 mmol/L, p = 0.049) and session RPE (5.1 ± 0.6 vs. 6 ± 0.9 au, p = 0.021) were all significantly lower during HIIT<sub>RPE</sub> when compared to HIIT<sub>MAS</sub>. Peak and average speed, VO<sub>2</sub>, carbon dioxide output, minute ventilation, tidal volume, and respiratory exchange ratio, average HR and average ƒ<sub>R</sub>, and t ≥ 90% VO<sub>2max</sub>/HR<sub>max</sub> were not significantly different between sessions. RPE-based prescription enables accumulation of similar t ≥ 90% VO<sub>2max</sub>/HR<sub>max</sub> with lower peak cardiorespiratory, metabolic and perceptual strain in comparison to MAS-based HIIT prescription. This prescription strategy can be used to alleviate physiological stress while still acquiring the same t ≥ 90% VO<sub>2max</sub>/HR<sub>max</sub>.

title: An Australian Narrative Review of Adoptive Cellular Therapies in Malignancy: Expanding Indications, Referral Pathways and Safety Beyond Specialist Centres.
authorString: Childs S, Ma D, Rodrigues A, Massey J, Cosman R, Chin V, Girgis L, Lynam J, Lau P, Withers B, Joshua AM, Tran B, Desai J, Harrison SJ, Moore J, Liu J.
abstractText: Adoptive cellular therapies (ACT), including tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL), T-cell receptor-engineered T (TCR-T) cell and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapies, represent an evolving class of immunotherapies with established efficacy in selected haematological malignancies and emerging applications in solid tumours. Additional platforms under investigation include virus-specific T cells, tumour-associated antigen-specific T cells, natural killer (NK) cell therapies and dendritic cell-based therapies. The therapeutic scope of ACT is expanding beyond oncology into autoimmune and fibrotic diseases, infectious diseases and inherited metabolic and immune disorders, highlighting the broad potential of cellular immunotherapy platforms. In solid tumours, efficacy remains limited by tumour antigen heterogeneity, immunosuppressive tumour micro-environment and impaired immune cell trafficking and persistence. These barriers are driving development of next-generation cellular products and combination strategies. Characteristic immune-mediated toxicities, particularly cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS), remain important considerations. Although potentially severe, these toxicities are generally manageable with early recognition, multidisciplinary care and prompt specialist intervention. As ACT indications expand in Australia, clinician familiarity with indications, mechanisms of action and toxicity profiles is essential to support informed patient discussions, appropriate patient selection, timely referral and prompt toxicity recognition and management. Non-oncology specialists have an important role in shared care, including patient identification, referral coordination, monitoring for delayed or late toxicities and provision of ongoing survivorship and supportive care. Achieving equitable national access to ACT will require streamlined health technology assessment processes, coordinated reimbursement and delivery funding models and structured referral networks with cross-institutional collaboration to support the specialised infrastructure required for their delivery.

title: Prepregnancy Prediabetes and Large-for-Gestational-Age Birth Independent of Gestational Diabetes Among Asian Women.
authorString: Inamura T, Tano S, Fujito S, Fuma K, Matsuo S, Nozaki Y, Katsuki S, Yoshihara M, Yoshida S, Yamashita M, Kajiyama H, Ushida T.

journal.title: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research

abstractText:
Aim

Prediabetes may increase the likelihood of adverse perinatal outcomes, but evidence regarding prepregnancy prediabetes remains limited. This study examined its associations with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and the delivery of a large-for-gestational-age (LGA) infant.

Methods

This multicenter retrospective study included women who delivered at 12 obstetric facilities in Japan between January 1, 2014, and December 31, 2024, and had undergone hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) measurement within 1 year before conception. The primary maternal and fetal outcomes were GDM and LGA birth, respectively. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to evaluate each outcome, with adjustment for maternal age, assisted reproductive technology, prepregnancy body mass index, and primiparity.

Results

A total of 282 pregnancies were included, of which 19 (6.7%) were complicated by prepregnancy prediabetes. Prepregnancy prediabetes showed a more than twofold increase in the estimated odds of GDM (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.15; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.53-8.66), although the association was not statistically significant. In contrast, it was significantly associated with the delivery of an LGA infant (aOR, 3.48; 95% CI, 1.14-10.66). After women who developed GDM were excluded, 262 women remained, including 16 (6.1%) with prepregnancy prediabetes. In this subgroup, prepregnancy prediabetes remained significantly associated with the delivery of an LGA infant (aOR, 3.49; 95% CI, 1.09-11.57).

Conclusion

Prepregnancy prediabetes was independently associated with higher odds of delivering an LGA infant among Asian women, including those without a diagnosis of GDM. These findings suggest that preconception dysglycemia may help identify women at increased risk of excessive fetal growth beyond GDM diagnosis and warrant further evaluation in larger studies.

title: Outcome-specific risk factors for dehydration and acute kidney injury readmission after ileostomy: A US National Cohort Study, 2016-2022.
authorString: Nigam A, Onongaya C, Meshram P, Harmon JV.

journal.title: Colorectal disease : the official journal of the Association of Coloproctology of Great Britain and Ireland

abstractText:
Aim

Single-centre pathways have reduced dehydration and acute kidney injury (AKI)-specific readmission after ileostomy from 17%-28% to single-digit rates, but whether these gains translated nationally is unknown. We examined how discharge destination relates to outcome-specific readmission, quantified 30-day readmission rates and encounter costs from 2016 to 2022 and identified risk factors at the population level.

Method

Retrospective cohort study using the United States Nationwide Readmissions Database (NRD, 2016-2022). Adults undergoing ileostomy creation were included. The primary outcome was 30-day readmission for dehydration or AKI. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression identified risk factors for composite readmission, with home-discharge effects compared between dehydration- and AKI-specific outcomes. Inflation-adjusted encounter costs were calculated.

Results

Among 189,829 patients (176,150 discharged alive), 24,024 were readmitted within 30 days (13.5%, 95% CI 13.3-13.7). Home discharge had opposing associations by outcome subtype. Dehydration-specific readmission increased (aOR 1.25) and AKI-specific readmission decreased (aOR 0.92, p < 0.001 for interaction). The strongest risk factors were extended length of stay >7 days (aOR 1.48), complicated diabetes (aOR 1.46) and age ≥ 65 years (aOR 1.46). Annual rates were stable (p for trend = 0.826). Readmission encounters totalled $1.51 billion in inflation-adjusted dollars. The principal-diagnosis lower-bound estimate was $0.40 billion.

Conclusion

Home discharge had divergent associations by outcome subtype, identifying the post-discharge transition as a candidate for prospective intervention testing. Stagnant national rates over 7 years despite established prevention evidence, an income-dependent gradient and a graded rate across cumulative risk-factor burden together motivate prospective evaluation of risk-stratified discharge protocols incorporating community stoma-output monitoring.

title: Characterizing bone metastases and skeletal-related events in patients with well-differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasms utilizing <sup>68</sup>Gallium-DOTATATE positron emission tomography.
authorString: Coston TW, Mahadevia HJ, Plante MM, Hochwald A, Accurso JM, Sharma A, Johnson GB, Ashman JB, Kendi AT, Sonbol MB, McGarrah PW, Hobday TJ, Halfdanarson TR, Starr JS.
abstractText: Tumors of neuroendocrine origin are a heterogenous group of related neoplasms which can arise from anywhere in the body. Neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) are categorized by site of origin, differentiation status and grade (Ki-67 expression and/or mitotic rate), with significant prognostic variability accordingly. Historically, the prevalence of bone metastasis is reported to be 6%-12% based on "first generation" (i.e., <sup>111</sup>Indium pentetreotide [Octreoscan®]) somatostatin receptor imaging (SSRI). We conducted a retrospective cohort study including patients with well-differentiated NENs to determine the clinical and imaging characteristics of osseous metastases when evaluated with higher-sensitivity <sup>68</sup>Gallium-DOTATATE positron emission tomography (PET) scans, as well as determining fracture prevalence in selected sub-cohorts. We also developed a risk score analysis to assess risk of fracture in this cohort. Four hundred twenty-four patients were identified for inclusion. The median age was 61 years. Most patients were asymptomatic (64%), had sclerotic lesions (77%), Krenning 4 (71%), and had >3 sites (69%) of osseous disease. A high proportion of patients had osseous metastases at sites with high risk for fracture, including vertebra (82%), pelvis (63%), and peri-trochanteric femur (34%). Fifty-seven patients (13%) in the entire cohort suffered a fracture. Fracture prevalence was significantly lower in small bowel neuroendocrine tumors (NETs, 7%) and Grades 1 and 2 disease (8% and 9%, respectively), with higher prevalence in pancreatic NETs, paragangliomas/pheochromocytomas, lung carcinoid, and Grade 3 disease (≥20% for each; p-values <.05). Our study showed that the rate of osseous metastatic disease approximates 20% in well-differentiated NENs. Most bone metastases are asymptomatic and the risk of fracture is variable based on the primary site of disease and tumor grade. Our novel risk score analysis for fracture was designed to assist clinician decision making as to management of bone metastasis in this patient population.

title: Histone Modifications at the Intersection of Aging, Neuroinflammation and Metabolism in Alzheimer's Disease.
authorString: Liang J, Cao H, Ren X, Sha N, Han X, Jiang L, Liu B, Zhao W.
abstractText: Aging, neuroinflammation and metabolic dysfunction are tightly intertwined in Alzheimer's disease (AD), but how transient pathological signals become persistent cellular states remains poorly understood. Histone post-translational modifications (PTMs) provide a dynamic interface between extracellular stimuli, cellular metabolism and chromatin state. This Review examines how canonical histone modifications and emerging metabolite-derived acylations regulate inflammatory and stress-responsive programmes across microglia, astrocytes and neurons during aging and AD. We discuss how amyloid-β, tau pathology, metabolic dysfunction and innate immune signaling converge on histone-modifying machinery, and how reciprocal interactions between metabolism and chromatin may stabilize disease-associated cell states. Particular attention is given to cellular senescence and neuroimmune memory, while emphasizing the context dependence of individual histone marks across cell types, genomic regions and disease stages. We further evaluate evidence for causality using three criteria: perturbation, persistence and reversibility. This framework distinguishes chromatin states that accompany ongoing pathology from those capable of sustaining pathological cell states beyond their initiating signals. Finally, we consider therapeutic strategies targeting histone-modifying enzymes, chromatin readers and metabolic inputs to restore chromatin plasticity and promote resolution of chronic neuroinflammation.

title: Compression Stockings as Core Therapy for Symptomatic Orthostatic Hypertension in an Older Male: A Case Report.
authorString: Li J.
