title: Citrulline Supplementation Improves Aortic Vasodilation and Prevents Aortic Thickening Only in Female Rats.
authorString: Martinez-Gonzalez K, Campos-Bedolla P, Patlán-Lozano C, Almeida-Gutierrez E, Serrano-Cuevas L, Palma-Guzman A, Arellano-Escudero O, Garcia-delaTorre P.

journal.title: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists

abstractText:
Background

Aging is associated with endothelial dysfunction and vascular remodeling, partly due to reduced nitric oxide (NO) bioavailability. l-citrulline, a precursor of l-arginine and NO synthesis, has been proposed as a therapeutic strategy to improve vascular function. This study evaluated the effects of chronic citrulline supplementation on aortic structure and vasodilatory function in adult male and female rats.

Methods

Eight-month-old male and female Sprague-Dawley rats were randomly assigned to control or treatment groups. The treated animals received oral malate citrulline (1 g/kg/d) for 12 weeks. We isolated thoracic aortas for histological and morphometric analyses, including tunica media thickness and intima/media ratio. We assessed vascular reactivity in vitro using isolated aortic rings in an organ bath system, measuring acetylcholine (ACh)-induced relaxation following phenylephrine-induced contraction.

Results

Citrulline supplementation significantly improved ACh-induced vasorelaxation in female rats compared with female controls (55.14% ± 4.8% vs 42.4% ± 4.3%, P < .05. No differences in vasorelaxation were observed in males between the treated and control groups. Histological analyses showed that treated females had less disruption of elastic fibers and a thinner minimal intima than controls, whereas males showed no structural differences.

Conclusions

Citrulline supplementation improves endothelium-dependent vasodilation and may preserve aortic structural integrity in female rats but not in males. These findings suggest a sex-dependent vascular response to citrulline, potentially mediated by differences in NO signaling and hormonal regulation. Citrulline may represent a therapeutic strategy to improve vascular function during aging, particularly in females.

Clinical impact

The findings may guide clinical trials investigating how hormonal status and nitric oxide signaling affect the efficacy of citrulline supplementation in female patients. Ultimately, these insights could establish citrulline as a targeted, preventive intervention to preserve aortic structural integrity and reduce cardiovascular disease risk in the aging female population.

title: Effect of Atorvastatin and Rosuvastatin on Lipid Parameters and Inflammatory Biomarkers in Patients with Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Sohail A, Khurshid M, Khurshid A, Khalid M, Raza A, Shah MUFA, Khan H.
abstractText: Statins produce marked reductions in total and LDL cholesterol, C-reactive protein (CRP), and help prevent stroke, re-infarction, and subsequent risk of death. We conducted a meta-analysis to assess the role of atorvastatin in comparison with rosuvastatin in lowering levels of inflammatory biomarkers and lipid parameters in patients with ACS. Online databases were searched, and results from random-effects meta-analysis are presented as weighted mean differences (WMDs) and corresponding 95% confidence intervals. The outcomes were assessed at the short-term (≤1 month) and long-term (>3 months) follow-up. A total of 15 studies (13 RCTs and 2 observational studies) were included. The level of erythrocyte sedimentation rate (P = 0.13), oxidized LDL (P = 0.94), and long-term HDL-C (P = 0.28) showed no significant difference between the two statin groups. No significant differences were observed between atorvastatin and rosuvastatin in total cholesterol and LDL-C at short-term or long-term follow-up. A significant decrease in CRP levels (WMD 4.08; 95% CI 1.53-6.63; P = 0.002; I2 = 98%) and a significant rise in HDL-C (WMD -1.15; 95% CI -1.99 to -0.32; P = 0.007; I2 = 39%) was reported in the rosuvastatin group compared to the atorvastatin group in the short-term. Atorvastatin was associated with a significant reduction in triglycerides at short-term follow-up (WMD -8.69; 95% CI -14.97 to -2.40; P = 0.007; I2 = 35%), while the overall long-term comparison was borderline and did not reach conventional statistical significance. Our findings suggest that rosuvastatin may provide greater short-term reductions in CRP and modest increases in HDL-C compared with atorvastatin; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of substantial heterogeneity and the absence of significant differences at longer follow-up.

title: Influence of Cardiac Phase on Valve-to-Coronary Ostia Distance in Valve-in-Valve Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
authorString: Cadour F, Castillo F, Pakkal M, Soares Torres F, Halankar J.

journal.title: Canadian Association of Radiologists journal = Journal l'Association canadienne des radiologistes

abstractText:
Purpose

No consensus exists on which cardiac phase to use for virtual valve-to-coronary ostium (VTC) distance measurement to predict risk of coronary obstruction in valve-in-valve (ViV). Our study aimed to investigate whether cardiac phase influences VTC measurements in ViV for failing stented surgical heart valves (SHV).

Methods

All adult patients with stented SHV referred for a pre-planning CT for ViV between 2020 and 2025 were retrospectively eligible. For each patient, VTC was measured for two transcatheter heart valve options at both the right and left coronary ostia. VTC measurements were compared between systole, diastole, and phase with best image quality (best phase). Prevalence of changes in coronary obstruction risk (based on 4-mm cutoff) depending on the phase was assessed. Inter- and intraobserver reliability was evaluated.

Results

A total of 398 VTC measurements derived from 116 included patients (69 male, 71 ± 13 years) were evaluated. Best phase was more often diastolic. Median VTCs differed between systole and diastole (P < .001), and systole and best phase (P < .001), but not between diastole and best phase (P = .47) (systole 4.8 [3.1-6.5] mm vs diastole 4.6 [3.1-6.2] mm vs best phase 3.9 [2.5-6.2] mm). Measurements were slightly higher in systole than in diastole (mean difference +0.24 mm, [95% CI: 0.16, 0.32]; P < .001), but similar between diastole and best phase (P = .47). Risk of coronary obstruction changed between systole and diastole in 41 coronary arteries (41/398, 10%). Intra- and interobserver reliability was good-to-excellent.

Conclusions

VTC measurements differed and were slightly higher in systole than in diastole, which may influence the coronary obstruction risk classification.

title: Photobiomodulation as a contemporary antioxidant intervention in myocardial infarction.
authorString: Batista GMDS, Teixeira ILA, Antonio EL, Serra AJ.
abstractText: Myocardial infarction (MI) triggers a complex cascade of structural and functional alterations that frequently culminate in adverse cardiac remodelling and heart failure. Central to this process is the excessive production of reactive oxygen species (ROS), which disrupt mitochondrial function, impair calcium handling, and activate pro-apoptotic and pro-fibrotic pathways. Photobiomodulation (PBM) has emerged as a non-invasive therapeutic approach capable of modulating several key biological processes involved in post-infarction remodelling. Preclinical studies consistently demonstrate that PBM reduces infarct size, attenuates ventricular dilation, and improves both systolic and diastolic function. Through the absorption of red to near-infrared light by mitochondrial chromophores, particularly cytochrome c oxidase, PBM enhances cellular bioenergetics, modulates ROS production and activates redox-sensitive signalling pathways. These effects promote a shift from detrimental oxidative stress toward controlled ROS signalling and, in turn, facilitate cytoprotective, anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic responses. In addition, PBM promotes the mobilization of progenitor cells, contributing to tissue repair and microvascular restoration. Although still limited, the available clinical evidence suggests that PBM may confer modest improvements in cardiac function. However, variability in treatment protocols, delivery methods and study designs currently precludes definitive conclusions regarding its clinical efficacy. In summary, PBM represents a promising strategy for modulating oxidative stress after MI, integrating metabolic, redox and signalling pathways to attenuate cardiac remodelling. Further well-designed clinical studies are required to establish standardized protocols and to clarify its therapeutic potential in cardiovascular medicine.

title: Analysis of early surgical outcomes in adolescent and adult patients undergoing repair for tetralogy of Fallot.
authorString: Das D, Barsainyan KP, Sarkar T, Malladi V, Das S, Sharma MK, Gajpal S, Chattopadhyay A.
abstractText:
Background

Tetralogy of Fallot is the most common cyanotic CHD and is ideally repaired during infancy. However, delayed diagnosis and limited access to congenital cardiac care may result in presentation during adolescence or adulthood. This study evaluated outcomes of tetralogy of Fallot repair in patients aged ≥ 13 years.

Patients and methods

This retrospective cohort study included patients aged ≥ 13 years undergoing primary tetralogy of Fallot repair between June 2016 and June 2025. Demographic, operative, and post-operative data, including early mortality and reintervention, were analysed.

Results

Ninety-four patients underwent repair at a median age of 15 years (interquartile range: 3) and weight of 36.5 kg (interquartile range: 12.2). Pre-operative coil embolisation of aortopulmonary collaterals was required in 26.6%. Mean cardiopulmonary bypass and aortic cross-clamp times were 114.8 ± 49.8 and 82.4 ± 35.6 minutes, respectively. Mean ventilation duration was 7.7 ± 7.1 hours, ICU stay 3.9 ± 1.0 days, and post-operative hospital stay 4.6 ± 1.3 days. Transannular patch repair was performed in 65 patients (69%), while 29 (31%) underwent pulmonary valve-preserving repair, with comparable early outcomes. Thirty-day mortality was 1.06%, and reintervention occurred in 2.1% during a mean follow-up of 38.4 months.

Conclusions

Primary repair of tetralogy of Fallot in late-presenting adolescents and adults can be performed with low early mortality and acceptable morbidity. Careful pre-operative assessment, including identification and management of significant aortopulmonary collaterals, and individualised right ventricular outflow tract reconstruction are important components of management. These findings support definitive repair in appropriately selected late-presenting patients.

title: Derivation of Pulse Wave Velocity from Arterial Waveforms in Children.
authorString: Billa RD, Dagle JM, Schmelzel M, Johnson K, McNamara PJ, Badheka AV, Tomasson MH, Chegondi M, Haskell SE, Vasileva A, Stauss HM, Bates ML.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
journal.title: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
journal.isoabbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol

abstractText: Aortic stiffness can be assessed using aortic pulse wave velocity (PWV), which can be estimated from peripheral arterial waveforms in adults. However, this method has not been validated in children. We sought to determine whether PWV could be feasibly measured by tonometry and accurately derived from arterial waveforms available in critically ill infants and children. Applanation tonometry was used to measure brachio-femoral or carotid-femoral PWV (b/cfPWV) in hospitalized, hemodynamically stable, prepubertal children with an indwelling arterial catheter. Peripheral arterial line waveforms were converted to ascending aortic waveforms using a model-based transfer function. PWV was estimated from the time delays (Δt<sub>f-b</sub>) between forward and backward wave forms of the ascending aortic waveforms and effective reflecting distance (EfRD). We found that the effective reflecting distance (EfRD) calculation used in adults overestimated b/cfPWV in children. We derived a new EfRD equation that yielded better agreement between measured and estimated PWV (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.30, p < 0.05). Estimating PWV from arterial waveform data eliminates the need for tonometry, allowing larger samples of infants and children to be included in future studies of cardiovascular disease and development.

title: Left Ventricular Noncompaction Cardiomyopathy and Thromboembolic Complications: A Case Report and Focused Review of the Literature.
authorString: Almaguer Gongora LA, Shimon S, Remedios Carbonell LE, Gonzalez G, Acosta-Batista C, Velasquez JC.
abstractText: Left ventricular noncompaction cardiomyopathy (LVNC) is a rare myocardial disorder characterized by prominent trabeculations and deep intertrabecular recesses. Thromboembolic complications represent a major source of morbidity and mortality, yet optimal risk stratification and anticoagulation strategies remain poorly defined. The authors have reported the case of a patient with previously undiagnosed LVNC who presented with rapidly progressive heart failure and developed acute, recurrent cardioembolic strokes. Cardiac imaging revealed extensive left ventricular trabeculations, a severely reduced ejection fraction, and bilateral atrial appendage thrombi. Despite systemic anticoagulation, the patient experienced rapid respiratory and hemodynamic decompensation resulting in death. LVNC is associated with a substantial chance of thromboembolic events, particularly in patients with ventricular dysfunction. This case highlighted the crucial importance of early recognition and the need for individualized anticoagulation strategies in patients at high risk.

title: TNF signaling at the brain-heart interface: neurovascular injury and cardiovascular vulnerability in epilepsy.
authorString: Sha A, Wu Y, Peng HR, Jin B, He B, Zhao ZK, He F, Cao Y, Gan L.
abstractText: Epilepsy is increasingly viewed as a systemic disorder in which recurrent seizures intersect with vascular, autonomic, respiratory, and cardiac processes to influence cardiovascular vulnerability. Seizure-related neuroinflammation involves multiple interacting mediator pathways, including HMGB1/TLR4-RAGE signaling, inflammasome/IL-1β activation, IL-6/IL-6R-gp130 signaling, albumin/TGF-β signaling following blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption, and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α)/TNF receptor (TNFR) signaling. Within this inflammatory network, TNF/TNFR signaling represents a mechanistically distinct and translationally relevant framework for examining how immune activation intersects with endothelial-barrier dysfunction, neurovascular unit injury, autonomic disturbance, inflammatory communication across neural and cardiovascular compartments, and cardiac vulnerability. This review integrates direct evidence from epilepsy studies with mechanistic insights from related experimental studies of BBB injury, myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury, cardioprotection, and brain-heart communication. TNF biology is determined by ligand form, receptor subtype, cellular compartment, and disease context. Soluble TNF preferentially engages TNFR1-associated inflammatory and injury-amplifying pathways, whereas transmembrane TNF/TNFR2 signaling may support regulatory or reparative responses in selected settings. In epilepsy, seizure-associated inflammation, BBB dysfunction, glial activation, and autonomic imbalance may interact to increase susceptibility to arrhythmogenic stress, myocardial injury, adverse cardiac remodeling, and cardiorespiratory instability relevant to sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP). However, epilepsy-specific evidence directly linking TNF/TNFR signaling to cardiovascular outcomes remains limited, and many mechanistic connections currently rely on converging evidence from neurovascular and cardiovascular research. Future studies should integrate compartment-resolved inflammatory profiling with autonomic, respiratory, electrocardiographic, and cardiac phenotyping to distinguish inflammatory signatures of disease severity from modifiable contributors to cardiovascular risk. Such approaches may enable phenotype-specific strategies to better understand and ultimately mitigate the brain-heart consequences of epilepsy.

title: Potassium and Cardiovascular Disease.
authorString: Manolis AA, Manolis TA, Vouliotis A, Manolis AS.
abstractText: Hyperkalemia (potassium levels >5.5 mEq/L) or hypokalemia (potassium < 3.5 mEq/L) may incur potentially serious cardiovascular (CV) complications. Hyperkalemia is most commonly encountered in renal failure, K+ oversupplementation for diuretic therapy, use of potassium-sparing diuretics, therapy with angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers in cardiorenal disease (chronic kidney disease [CKD] and/or heart failure-HF), digitalis toxicity, massive hemolysis, or muscle trauma. For patients with hyperkalemia, potassium binders (sodium zirconium cyclosilicate, patiromer, and sodium polystyrene) are guideline-recommended for patients with CKD. Importantly, proactive potassium control via routine use of potassium binders in hyperkalemia may incur cost reduction in acute care while simultaneously supporting optimization of medications for comorbid conditions. Hypokalemia can occur in response to diuretic therapy (7-56%), following renal dialysis, or during recovery from endurance exercise and can be equally detrimental as it may raise the risk of ventricular arrhythmias and cardiac arrest. Its diagnosis depends on the level of serum potassium. An ECG is useful in identifying the more severe consequences. Hypokalemia occurs in up to 20% of hospitalized patients and incurs an increased incidence of ventricular and atrial fibrillation. Importantly, "you cannot eat your way out of hypokalemia," i.e., by adding bananas and/or other potassium-providing fruit or juices, hence one needs to provide the patient with K+ supplements in tablet or liquid form or in more serious cases via slow (10 mmol/h) IV supplementation in highly controlled, strict hospital protocols and with continuous ECG monitoring. All these issues of serum potassium disturbances and their CV effects are herein reviewed.

title: Offered Deceased Donor Kidneys With Little or No Chance of Being Transplanted.
authorString: Chiang TP, Husain SA, Ali NM, Berger JC, Orandi BJ, Massie AB, Segev DL, Lonze BE, Stewart DE.
abstractText: With a broadening deceased donor pool and recent allocation policy changes, US transplant programs have reported challenges managing an influx of suboptimal kidney offers. We hypothesized that the number of offered kidneys with a minuscule chance of being transplanted has risen. If so, targeted innovations may be needed to reduce administrative burden and improve system efficiency. Using Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network data on kidneys offered in 2016-2024, we developed a multivariable model to predict the probability that an offered kidney was transplanted (PrTx). We examined trends in the number and proportion of offered kidneys having PrTx ≤2%, ≤5%, and ≤10%. Donor factors most predictive of PrTx were age, donation after circulatory death, serum creatinine (terminal, peak, nadir), presence and duration of diabetes and hypertension, infectious disease test results, and body mass index. From 2016 to 2024, the annual number of kidneys offered with PrTx ≤2%, PrTx ≤5%, and PrTx ≤10% increased 13-fold (from 18 to 236), 12-fold (84 to 1055), and 10-fold (299 to 2856), respectively. Of the 236 offered kidneys with PrTx ≤2% in 2024, none was transplanted. The 2856 kidneys with PrTx ≤10% accounted for 7.9% (n = 1 208 883) of manually refused offers but just 1.1% (n = 239) of transplanted kidneys. Organ procurement organizations and centers varied substantially in offering and transplanting low-PrTx kidneys. The number of offered kidneys with extremely low predicted transplant probability has risen sharply, most notably in 2024. Innovations, such as improved offer filtering capabilities and standardized expedited allocation pathways, are needed to improve kidney placement efficiency.

title: ENdb 2.0: an updated database of experimentally supported enhancers.
authorString: Xu M, Zhang G, Wang Q, Chen Y, Song C, Liu J, Guo B, Zhou J, Li C.
abstractText: Enhancers are cis-regulatory elements that control gene expression during development, cell differentiation, and disease. Genome-wide studies have mapped large numbers of candidate regulatory elements, but experimentally supported enhancer information remains dispersed across primary studies and experimental systems. Here, we present ENdb 2.0 (http://www.licpathway.net/ENdb/index.php), an updated, manually curated database of experimentally supported enhancers. Compared with ENdb 1.0, the major updates are (i) literature coverage through 2026 and five species: Homo sapiens, Mus musculus, Drosophila melanogaster, Danio rerio, and Rattus norvegicus; (ii) 4831 enhancer evidence records, including 2793 enhancer-TF-target-gene records involving 496 TFs and 1070 target genes; (iii) expanded curation of genomic coordinates, experimental evidence, enhancer type, regulatory state, biological condition, tissues, cell sources, cell types, and diseases, covering 169 tissues, 1255 cell sources, 415 cell types, and 226 diseases; and (iv) biological search, genome browsing, pathway enrichment analysis, agent-assisted query, and structured data download. ENdb 2.0 links experimentally supported enhancer regions with regulatory factors, target genes, biological conditions, and supporting experiments across physiological and disease states.

title: NAD+ replenishment reduces cardiomyocyte senescence and improves diastolic function in the aged male heart.
authorString: Huang Q, Wang Y, Farias K, Zeng X, Chen Q, Cheng H, Baki VB, Gross SS, Geri J, Sauve AA, Yang Y.
abstractText: Cardiomyocyte senescence is a hallmark of cardiac aging and closely associated with diastolic dysfunction and heart failure in older adults. Strategies to effectively delay or reverse cardiomyocyte senescence in the aged heart remain limited. We investigated whether NAD+ replenishment regulates cardiomyocyte senescence and cardiac function in aging. Ventricular NAD+ metabolism, senescence markers, and cardiac function were assessed in young and aged mice of both sexes. Aged male mice exhibited reduced cardiac NAD+ levels due to impaired biosynthesis, limited mitochondrial mobilization, and increased consumption, leading to suppressed SIRT1 and SIRT6 activity and accumulation of senescent cardiomyocytes. These changes were accompanied by diastolic dysfunction, myocardial hypertrophy, and fibrosis. In cultured cardiomyocytes, NAD+ depletion induced cellular senescence, which was reversed by supplementation with the NAD+ precursors nicotinamide riboside (NR) and dihydronicotinamide riboside (NRH). In aged male mice, two months of NR or NRH treatment suppressed senescence markers, improved diastolic function, and reduced hypertrophy and fibrosis. Mechanistically, both NR and NRH activated SIRT1 and suppressed cell cycle arrest markers. NRH induced more robust SIRT1 activation, which deacetylated SIRT6, promoting its binding to histones and enhancing DNA damage repair. In contrast, aged female mice exhibited diastolic dysfunction without significant decline in cardiac NAD+ levels and did not respond to NR or NRH treatment. NAD+ is a critical regulator of cardiomyocyte senescence in aging male hearts. NAD+ replenishment, particularly with NRH, reverses senescence-associated cardiac dysfunction through coordinated activation of SIRT1 and SIRT6. The sex-specific differences observed highlight distinct mechanisms underlying cardiac aging and emphasize the importance of considering biological sex in the development of NAD+-based therapeutic strategies.

title: Dysphagia and feeding outcomes in paediatric patients with major aortopulmonary collateral arteries undergoing pulmonary artery intervention.
authorString: Momin NH, Steiden C, Bagwell K, Liu KK.
abstractText: Major aortopulmonary collateral arteries represent a complex subgroup of CHD with unique cardiopulmonary physiology. While surgical outcomes have been well described, feeding and swallowing outcomes remain poorly understood. This study aimed to characterise dysphagia prevalence and functional feeding outcomes in these paediatric patients undergoing pulmonary artery intervention. We conducted a retrospective chart review of paediatric patients with major aortopulmonary collateral arteries at a tertiary paediatric cardiac centre between January 1, 2020, and December 31, 2025. Swallowing outcomes were assessed using the Penetration-Aspiration Scale, and functional feeding outcomes were measured using the Pediatric Functional Oral Intake Scale. Descriptive statistics were used to summarise patient characteristics and feeding outcomes. Pre- and post-intervention outcomes were compared among patients with paired data. Nineteen patients were included. Genetic diagnoses were present in 58% of the cohort, most commonly 22q11.2 deletion syndrome. Prolonged intubation occurred in 53% of patients, and vocal fold motion impairment and necrotising enterocolitis were each observed in 42%. Among patients with paired data, median Penetration-Aspiration Scale increased from 3 pre-operatively to 6 post-operatively, and aspiration was observed in 50% post-operatively. Enteral tube use increased from 57% pre-operatively to 79% post-operatively among patients with paired data. Persistent oral aversion at six months was documented in 26% of the cohort. Patients with major aortopulmonary collateral arteries demonstrate high rates of dysphagia and enteral feeding dependence across the perioperative period. Preliminary findings highlight the need for early, multidisciplinary feeding evaluation to optimise developmental outcomes in this high-risk population.

title: Left ventricular geometry as a risk factor for recurrent subaortic stenosis after primary resection.
authorString: Felimban AA, Mohamed HAH, Ismail M, Alibrahim IJ, Ardah HI, Alhabshan F, Kabbani MS.
abstractText:
Background

Discrete subaortic stenosis is a progressive cause of left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in children, and recurrence after surgical resection is not uncommon. We evaluated echocardiographic and morphologic factors associated with reintervention after primary subaortic membrane resection.

Methods

We conducted a single-centre retrospective cohort study of paediatric patients (0-14 years) who underwent primary surgical resection of subaortic membrane stenosis between 2002 and 2019. Demographic, clinical, and echocardiographic variables were compared between patients requiring reintervention and those requiring a single operation. Independent predictors were assessed using multivariable logistic regression.

Results

Seventy-seven patients were included; 16 required reintervention and 61 did not. On univariate analysis, the reintervention group had higher preoperative left ventricular outflow tract peak and mean gradients and shorter membrane length. In multivariable analysis, shorter membrane length independently predicted reintervention (adjusted odds ratio 0.677 per 1-mm increase, 95% confidence interval 0.487-0.941; p = 0.020), as did higher preoperative left ventricular outflow tract peak gradient (adjusted odds ratio 1.066 per 1-mmHg increase, 95% confidence interval 1.023-1.111; p = 0.002). A smaller aorto-septal angle showed a trend towards increased risk but did not reach statistical significance (adjusted odds ratio 0.933, 95% confidence interval 0.866-1.005; p = 0.067). Aortic regurgitation was significantly worse at follow-up in patients requiring reintervention.

Conclusion

Shorter subaortic membrane length and higher preoperative left ventricular outflow tract peak gradient were independent predictors of reintervention after primary resection. These findings may improve risk stratification and support closer echocardiographic surveillance of patients at increased risk of recurrence.

title: Tumour-anchored Purkinje-mediated ventricular tachycardia in a child with cardiac rhabdomyoma.
authorString: Izumi G, Sasaki D, Temma T.
abstractText: Cardiac rhabdomyomas are associated with ventricular arrhythmias, but mechanisms remain uncertain. A 10-year-old boy with tuberous sclerosis complex developed verapamil-sensitive fascicular ventricular tachycardia adjacent to a residual cardiac rhabdomyoma. Electrophysiological mapping demonstrated Purkinje-mediated reentry. Catheter ablation at a tumour-adjacent site eliminated the arrhythmia, suggesting that residual rhabdomyoma may anchor a localised reentrant substrate.

title: Nonlinear Dynamics of Collagen Turnover Reveal Distinct States of Fibrosis and Regeneration After Cardiac Injury.
authorString: Yadav S, Chakraborty S, Dutta A, Das M, Basak T.

journal.title: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology

abstractText: Replacement cardiac fibrosis is accompanied by extensive extracellular matrix remodeling, which can lead to either irreversible fibrosis or functional regeneration. Here, experimental measurements are integrated with nonlinear dynamic modeling to characterize how the temporal coupling between collagen synthesis and deposition contributes to divergent remodeling outcomes. Using an acute β-adrenergic receptor agonist-induced cardiac injury model in mice, we quantified temporal changes in the most abundant fibrillar collagens and the total deposited collagens during inflammatory, proliferative, and reparative phases. Complementarily, proteomic data from zebrafish ventricular amputation were used to map collagen turnover during regenerative healing. Ordinary differential equation-based models were developed to represent collagen mRNA synthesis, protein deposition, and their coupling across time to interpret fibrosis in mice. The model exhibited steep collagen accumulation followed by saturation, reflecting a stable fibrotic fixed point. In contrast, zebrafish exhibited early collagen degradation and subsequent restoration toward baseline levels, consistent with regenerative remodeling. Phase-space and stability analyses revealed distinct steady-state behaviour, where identical initial conditions diverged toward either a fibrosis-dominant or regeneration-dominant attractor state for two different systems, concurring with similar non-linearity observed in gold-standard ligation-mediated fibrosis and cryoinjury-mediated regenerative models. Coupled dynamics in mice further revealed nonlinear, history-dependent relationships between collagen synthesis and deposition. Together, these findings identify collagen turnover as a key driver of emergent tissue-level states, providing a unified quantitative framework that links cellular signaling to the macroscopic outcomes of cardiac repair.

title: Dual-Modal Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance Biosensor for Rapid Bacterial Gram-Typing and Species Identification in Bronchoalveolar Lavage Fluid.
authorString: Xu B, Jing L, Hou H, Sun L, Yue H, Zhang Z, Gao W, Sun D, Xin J, Gui T, Visentin M, Chen Q, Gai Z.
abstractText: Rapid pathogen identification is critical for timely antibiotic therapy in patients with pneumonia, yet current methods remain too slow or complex for routine clinical use. Here, we describe a localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR)-based biosensor platform that detects Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria directly in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) without nucleic acid extraction or amplification. Gold nano-islands (AuNIs) functionalized with antibodies against lipoteichoic acid (LTA) or lipopolysaccharide (LPS) enabled selective bacterial capture. The sensor achieved a refractive index resolution of 8.52 × 10-8 RIU with good reusability and dynamic range. Detection limits reached the concentration of 0.027 μM for purified LTA and 0.208 endotoxin units (EU) for LPS. When tested with Escherichia coli in artificial samples, the LPS sensor showed a reproducibility standard deviation (RSD) of 3.14%, detecting bacterial growth significantly earlier than conventional OD600 measurement. In 33 clinical BALF samples, sensor results correlated strongly with standard diagnostics (Pearson r = 0.963) and distinguished infected from noninfected cases using cutoff values of 0.060 rad (Gram-positive) and 0.083 rad (Gram-negative). The platform detects polymyxin B susceptibility 8 h earlier than conventional OD600 measurements, and a proof-of-concept sandwich immunoassay enables species-level discrimination between E. coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae. With excellent reproducibility (RSD = 3.14%), reusability over six cycles (84.21% ± 2.03% signal retention), and four-week storage stability (98.63% ± 5.42%), this LSPR platform offers a practical, rapid approach for frontline bacterial screening and accelerated antibiotic stewardship in pneumonia.

title: Still's disease and malignancies: insights into the balance between inflammatory enhancement and immune control. Data from the International AIDA Network Still's Disease Registry.
authorString: Gavioli F, Sbalchiero J, Caggiano V, Hinojosa-Azaola A, Torres-Ruiz J, Martín-Nares E, Lopalco G, Morrone M, Del Vescovo S, Suzon B, Donat S, Giardini HAM, Ciccia F, Iacono D, Ruscitti P, Cipriani P, Almaghlouth IA, Sfriso P, Bindoli S, Kasapcopur O, Akay N, Konte EK, Batu ED, Ozen S, Bilginer Y, Ragab G, Mahmoud AAA, Sfikakis PP, Laskari K, Sota J, Tufan A, Erden A, Cakir IY, Emmi G, Fotis L, Kourtesi K, Karamanakos A, Dimouli A, Dagna L, Campochiaro C, Giacomelli R, Berardicurti O, Barone P, Papa S, Conti F, Gattamelata A, Thabet M, Frassi M, Crisafulli F, Direskeneli H, Alibaz-Oner F, Conforti A, Makowska J, Bugatti S, De Stefano L, Boyarchuk O, Pucino V, Govoni M, Rigante D, Al-Mayouf SM, Iagnocco A, Gicchino MF, Gaggiano C, Chimenti MS, Maiolini F, La Torre F, Hernández-Rodríguez J, Lo Gullo A, Moshrif A, Maggio MC, Conti G, Del Giudice E, Carubbi F, Guggino G, Ogunjimi B, Feist E, Balistreri A, Frediani B, Fabiani C, Cantarini L, Vitale A, From the International AIDA (AutoInflammatory Diseases Alliance) Network, from the Autoinflammatory Diseases Working Group of the Italian Society of Rheumatology (SIR).
abstractText: Still's disease is an autoinflammatory condition marked by excessive activation of the innate immune system, resulting in intense and persistent systemic inflammation if left untreated. Chronic inflammation is recognized as both an initiator and promoter of carcinogenesis, although growing evidence suggests it may act against cancer development. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the cancer risk in patients with Still's disease. Data were obtained from the international Autoinflammatory Diseases Alliance (AIDA) Network registry for Still's disease. Statistical analysis included a machine learning-based approach to evaluate associations between independent variables and malignancy. A total of 626 patients with Still's disease were included, of whom 14 (2.2%) developed 15 malignant neoplasms. Patients with malignancy history exhibited higher age at disease onset and diagnosis, as well as longer duration of fever during flares. Machine learning-based analysis, including Elastic Net and Firth's penalized likelihood logistic regression, identified an association between cancer development and fever duration (relative risk = 1.002, 95% confidence interval 1.000-1.004, p = 0.01). Despite being a severe systemic inflammatory condition, Still's disease appears to be associated with a relatively modest prevalence of cancer. However, uncontrolled systemic inflammation, as reflected by prolonged fever duration, may contribute to carcinogenesis in these patients.

title: Timing of the Adrenaline Administration in Witnessed Pediatric Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: Retrospective, National Cohort Study in Japan, Using a 2014-2020 Dataset.
authorString: Okajima K, Amagasa S, Kashiura M, Yasuda H, Kishihara Y, Uematsu S.

journal.title: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies

abstractText: We evaluated the association between the timing of initial adrenaline administration and outcomes in witnessed pediatric out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). A multicenter, retrospective cohort study addressing resuscitation time bias by performing a risk-set matching analysis using time-dependent propensity scores. Analysis of data from the Japanese Association for Acute Medicine OHCA (JAAM-OHCA) registry, which is a nationwide, multicenter, prospective collection of prehospital and in-hospital data involving Japanese patients with OHCA. Pediatric patients (< 18 yr) with witnessed OHCA who received adrenaline, during the period June 2014 to December 2020. None. We compared patients who received adrenaline in specific time intervals (1-10, 11-15, 16-20, 21-25, or 26-30 min) after first contact with emergency medical services with those who still had not received adrenaline during the same time. The primary and secondary outcomes were survival and favorable neurologic outcome at one month, defined as a Pediatric Cerebral Performance Category score of 1-3. We identified a total of 259 OHCA patients who had received adrenaline at 1-10, 11-15, 16-20, 21-25, 26-30, and 31 minutes or later; at each respective time point, there were 15, 39, 62, 55, 37, and 51 patients. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs for 1-month survival at each time group compared with patients at risk were: 1-10 minutes, RR, 2.94 (95% CI, 0.38-22.81); 11-15 minutes, RR, 0.97 (95% CI, 0.30-3.12); 16-20 minutes, RR, 1.00 (95% CI, 0.29-3.48); 21-25 minutes, RR, 1.35 (95% CI, 0.54-3.40); and 26-30 minutes, RR, 1.71 (95% CI, 0.27-10.78). We failed to identify an association between time interval and greater or lesser probability of survival or neurologic outcome. In the JAAM-OHCA registry, with pediatric data from 2014 to 2020, we failed to identify an association between earlier adrenaline administration and greater probability of 1-month survival or favorable neurologic outcomes.

title: Comparison of 3 guideline lipid emulsion regimens for local anesthetic systemic toxicity: an in silico study of bolus duration, total dose, and treatment delay in intravenous bupivacaine overdose.
authorString: Lim S, Cho S, Cho E.
abstractText: Lipid emulsion is the only specific antidote for local anesthetic systemic toxicity, but no dose-finding study has been conducted. We compared 3 published regimens and alternative schedules that deliver the same dose in different ways using a human model of intravenous bupivacaine overdose. A 14-compartment human bupivacaine model was independently reimplemented without fitted parameters, replacing first-order lipid elimination with a saturable term. Toxicity was modeled as 112.5 mg administered intravenously over 3 minutes. Benefit was defined as the predicted maximum decrease in myocardial bupivacaine within 30 minutes, and harm as the predicted relative lipid load, indexed by peak plasma triglyceride concentration. Neither measure is a validated surrogate. The 3 guidelines specify the same doses but different bolus durations: 1 minute versus 2-3 minutes. At a matched dose of 12 mL/kg, myocardial bupivacaine decreased by 30.5% with the 1-minute bolus and 24.9% with the 2.5-minute bolus, with the same lipid load. The completed American Society of Regional Anesthesia and Pain Medicine regimen (7.64 mL/kg) achieved a 24.6% decrease versus 24.9% with 12 mL/kg; thus, complete regimens differ in schedule as well as dose. Repeating the 1-minute bolus twice, for a total of 4.5 mL/kg, achieved a 31.9% decrease with 62% less emulsion. Start time had the greatest effect: the best regimen achieved a 41.8% decrease when started at the end of the injection, but only 9.6% when started at 10 minutes. In this bupivacaine model, bolus duration distinguished the regimens more than dose did, and delay had a greater effect than either, eliminating most of the benefit without changing the lipid load. Treatment should begin at the first signs of toxicity, and 20% lipid emulsion should be immediately available wherever local anesthetics are used.

title: Polygenic Risk Scores: Towards Clinical Application.
authorString: Schumacher J, Koch V, Maj C, Nöthen MM.
abstractText:
Background

Common diseases are largely caused by the combined contributions of genetic and environmental risk factors. On the genetic side, numerous variants contribute to disease susceptibility, resulting in a substantial polygenic component of disease risk. Many such variants have already been identified. Polygenic risk scores (PRS), which aggregate the effects of these variants, enable more precise estimation of an individual's disease risk. We review the current state of bench-to-bedside translation of PRS.

Methods

This review is based on publications retrieved by a selective PubMed literature search using predefined search terms relevant to PRS.

Results

Studies across a range of diseases have shown that PRS can markedly influence the assessment of disease risk, enabling the identification of individuals at high risk. The predictive value of PRS can be improved by integrating them into established clinical risk models; this is the area of application in which the implementation of PRS in clinical practice is currently most advanced. For example, studies on coronary heart disease (CHD) and on breast and pancreatic cancer have shown that integrating PRS into clinical risk models changes personalized recommendations for primary and secondary prevention. Depending on the study, this affects 24% (CHD) to 25% (breast cancer) of individuals in the respective clinical risk groups. A major limitation is that most PRS are based on data from European populations, and their predictive value may be lower in individuals of other ancestral backgrounds. Moreover, quality standards must be established to ensure that the potential of PRS can be effectively translated into routine clinical practice.

Conclusion

As genetic data continue to grow, the predictive value of PRS is expected to increase further. PRS are therefore likely to become an integral component of risk prediction in preventive and precision medicine.

title: Glymphatic Dysfunction as a Multisystem Pathway Linking Systemic Health Conditions to Alzheimer's Disease: Mechanisms, Risk Factors, and Therapeutic Opportunities.
authorString: Abaresh S, Ivantsova E, Parmar MS.
abstractText: The glymphatic system is a glia-associated perivascular pathway involved in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)-interstitial fluid (ISF) exchange and the transport and clearance of neurotoxic metabolites, including amyloid-β (Aβ) and tau, from the central nervous system. Growing evidence suggests that alterations in glymphatic and perivascular clearance are associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology and may contribute to the accumulation of neurotoxic proteins and neurodegeneration. This review examines the role of the glymphatic system in AD and explores how aging, sleep disturbances, hypertension, ischemic heart disease, high-fat diet, diabetes, and gut microbiome dysbiosis impair glymphatic transport. A recurring mechanism across experimental models is the loss of perivascular AQP4 polarization, while vascular, metabolic, and inflammatory conditions may converge on related perivascular and neurovascular processes that impair CSF-ISF exchange and solute handling. Neuroimaging studies using markers such as DTI-ALPS, perivascular space burden, and free-water measurements provide evidence of alterations in glymphatic-related and perivascular processes in AD and demonstrate associations with amyloid deposition, neurodegeneration, and cognitive decline. Furthermore, glymphatic dysfunction may interact with neuroinflammation and tau pathology, creating a self-reinforcing cycle that accelerates disease progression. Emerging therapeutic strategies, including continuous theta-burst stimulation, positive airway pressure therapy for obstructive sleep apnea, pharmacological enhancement of AQP4 function, and nutritional interventions, have shown potential in experimental and early translational studies to influence glymphatic-related processes and may mitigate AD-related pathology. Collectively, current findings suggest that glymphatic and perivascular clearance pathways may represent an important link between systemic health conditions and AD. Because related pathways are implicated across multiple systemic conditions, interventions targeting glymphatic and perivascular dysfunction may have broader relevance to brain health, but their clinical effects remain to be established.

title: Exercise attenuates hypertension-induced renal dysfunction alongside changes in purine metabolism and A2A and P2X7 receptor expression.
authorString: Cardoso AM, Manica A, Morsch VM, Sévigny J, Chitolina MR.
abstractText:
Background

Hypertension-induced renal dysfunction is associated with endothelial dysfunction and changes in purinergic signaling. Exercise training can attenuate hypertension-related disturbances in purinergic pathways, but its effects on renal purine metabolism and purinergic receptor expression remain poorly understood. We investigated these responses in L-NAME-induced hypertensive rats.

Methods

Male Wistar rats were assigned to Control, Exercise, L-NAME, and Exercise L-NAME groups ( n  = 10/group). Hypertension was induced by chronic Nω-nitro- L -arginine methyl ester (L-NAME) administration, and exercise consisted of 6 weeks of swimming training. Blood pressure, renal nitric oxide metabolites (NOx), renal function, serum ATP, renal ATP, ADP, and AMP hydrolysis, ADA activity, and renal expression of purinergic enzymes and P1, P2X, and P2Y receptors were evaluated.

Results

L-NAME increased blood pressure, serum ATP, urea, and creatinine and reduced renal NOx concentrations. Hypertensive animals showed increased CD39 and ADA expression, increased ATP hydrolysis and ADA activity, reduced A1 and A2A receptor expression, and increased P2X4 and P2X7 expression. Exercise attenuated serum ATP accumulation, changes in renal purine-metabolizing enzyme activities, and ADA expression; preserved A2A and P2X1 expression; and attenuated increases in P2X4 and P2X7 expression. Significant correlations among serum ATP, creatinine, A2A, and P2X7 expression occurred exclusively in L-NAME-treated animals.

Conclusions

L-NAME-induced hypertension is associated with renal dysfunction, changes in renal purine metabolism, and selective changes in purinergic receptor gene expression. Swimming training attenuated several of these responses and improved renal function. These findings identify renal purine metabolism and A2A and P2X7 receptor expression as potential pathways associated with exercise-induced protection that warrant further mechanistic investigation.

title: Transcription factor EB as a novel target for dimethyl fumarate to restore endothelial function in diabetes.
authorString: He L, Tan RM, Wu L, Chen Q, Yang J, Han Z, Zhang Y, Fan G, Huang Y, Zhang CL.
abstractText: Diabetes mellitus-associated endothelial dysfunction represents a pivotal early event in diabetic vasculopathy, linking metabolic derangements to vascular injury. Dimethyl fumarate (DMF), an FDA-approved drug for multiple sclerosis and psoriasis, exhibits potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, yet whether it protects against diabetic endothelial dysfunction and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Here, diabetic db/db mice and the non-diabetic db/m<sup>+</sup> littermates were treated with DMF (100 mg·kg<sup>-1</sup>·d<sup>-1</sup>) or vehicle for 4 weeks, and vascular function in aortic and mesenteric artery rings was assessed by wire myography. Human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) and endothelial cell (EC)-specific Tfeb knockout (Tfeb<sup>ECKO</sup>) mice were employed to investigate the target of DMF in vitro and in vivo. DMF restored the impaired endothelium-dependent relaxations (EDRs) in db/db mouse aortas and insulin-induced relaxations in mesenteric arteries, improved glucose tolerance, reduced aortic endothelial mitochondrial ROS (mito-ROS) accumulation, and lowered the expression of inflammatory markers. IL-1β induced phosphorylation and cytoplasmic retention of TFEB (indicative of TFEB inhibition), mito-ROS production, and inflammatory responses in HUVECs and mouse aortas, all of which were reversed by DMF pretreatment. These protective effects of DMF were largely reversed by TFEB knockdown in HUVECs or in aortas of Tfeb<sup>ECKO</sup> mice. RNA sequencing data analysis revealed a substantial overlap between DMF-regulated and TFEB-overexpression transcriptional profiles, implicating a role of TFEB in DMF-induced suppression of inflammatory and oxidative pathways. Together, DMF ameliorates endothelial dysfunction in diabetes by inhibiting TFEB phosphorylation and restoring TFEB nuclear activity. Endothelial TFEB represents a critical mediator responsible for the vaso-protective effects of DMF and a promising therapeutic target for the treatment of diabetic vascular complications.

title: When the skin speaks but the heart remains silent: acute rheumatic fever with three major Jones manifestations without carditis.
authorString: Singhi AK, Paul P.
abstractText: Acute rheumatic fever is classically associated with carditis, particularly when erythema marginatum and subcutaneous nodules are present. We report a 13-year-old boy who fulfilled three major Jones manifestations-migratory polyarthritis, erythema marginatum, and subcutaneous nodules-supported by evidence of recent streptococcal infection, yet had no clinical, electrocardiographic, or echocardiographic evidence of carditis on serial assessment over three months. Serial photographs documented the evolving morphology of erythema marginatum in dark skin. A transient ocular inflammatory episode occurred during convalescence. This case highlights an uncommon phenotype of acute rheumatic fever and underscores the importance of recognising major extracardiac manifestations even when the heart remains unaffected.

title: Aortic valve replacement and concomitant coronary artery bypass grafting: technical considerations in the era of sutureless and rapid-deployment aortic valves.
authorString: Karangelis D, Stougiannou TM.
abstractText:
Introduction

Coexistence of severe aortic stenosis (AS) and coronary artery disease (CAD) is frequently encountered in contemporary practice, particularly amongst elderly patients with multiple comorbidities. Although transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) combined with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) has emerged as an alternative strategy, surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) with concomitant coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains the reference treatment for these patient groups. The introduction of sutureless and rapid-deployment aortic valves (RDAV) has considerably expanded the surgical armamentarium by facilitating implantation and reducing cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) and aortic cross-clamp times. Appropriate application of these technologies requires specific technical considerations that ultimately influence operative planning and execution.

Areas covered

This review summarizes contemporary evidence associated with the use of sutureless and RDAVs in combined CABG and SAVR procedures. To ensure relevant literature is included, a literature search across PubMed and ScienceDirect has been carried out, spanning the last 20 years, utilizing relevant medical subject headings (MeSH) terms and keywords.

Expert opinion

As evidence on sutureless and RDAVs technologies continues to accumulate, with associated advancements in perioperative planning, these valves are expected to become valuable adjuncts in combined procedures, by minimizing operative burden while also allowing for robust, aortic valve pathology correction.

title: Performance of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways in patients with suspected myocardial infarction: a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
authorString: Boeddinghaus J, Kunz M, Lopez-Ayala P, Khand A, Inoue K, Hatherley J, Miller J, Lambrakis K, Emakhu J, Cook B, Collinson P, Papendick C, Kasim S, Salleh FM, Wiencierz A, Bima P, Crisanti L, Koechlin L, Christ M, Miró Ò, Morello F, Nazerian P, Abubakr M, Roth D, Mahfoud F, Riley R, McCord J, Chew DP, Mueller C, Global 0/1 h Consortium.
abstractText: In patients with suspected myocardial infarction, the 0/1 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 1 h) is recommended in current guidelines for early risk stratification. However, individual trials used different safety outcomes, and efficacy outcomes were inconclusive or not assessed. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of all randomised controlled trials to synthesise the totality of the evidence, assess heterogeneity across trials, and evaluate clinically relevant outcomes using harmonised definitions across trials. In this systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, and the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform from inception to July 6, 2026, without language restrictions, for randomised trials comparing the safety and efficacy of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways (blood draws at 0 h and 3 h, ie, standard care). Individual participant data were obtained and outcome definitions were harmonised. The primary analysis used a two-stage random-effects meta-analysis. After receipt of the individual participant data but before data harmonisation or analysis, the primary safety outcome was refined to a composite of all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction within 30 days, from the originally specified composite of all-cause death or any new myocardial infarction. The primary efficacy outcomes were emergency department length of stay and direct discharge from the emergency department. This meta-analysis is registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261383452). Our systematic review identified five randomised trials, all of which provided individual participant data. Among these, the definition of the primary safety outcome varied, and in four trials emergency department length of stay was not reported for the whole analysis population. We included 110 933 patient presentations (55 489 managed with the 0/1 h pathway and 55 444 managed with the 0/3 h pathway). Within 30 days, all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction occurred in 446 patient presentations (0·8%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 562 patient presentations (1·0%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled odds ratio [OR] 0·83 [95% CI 0·45-1·53]; I2=62·9%; τ2=0·143). Emergency department length of stay was 314 min (IQR 211-481) in the 0/1 h pathway group versus 308 min (209-453) in the 0/3 h pathway group (random-effects pooled geometric mean ratio 1·03 [95% CI 0·85-1·25]; I2=99·2%; τ2=0·024). Direct discharge from the emergency department occurred in 37 190 patient presentations (67·0%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 36 485 patient presentations (65·8%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled OR 1·31 [95% CI 0·79-2·16]; I2=97·8%; τ2=0·156). Across the available randomised trials, short-term adverse event rates were low with both pathways, but the pooled safety estimate remained imprecise. On average, earlier cardiac troponin retesting did not reduce emergency department length of stay or clearly increase direct discharge, and substantial between-study heterogeneity indicates that treatment effects might not translate uniformly across health-care systems. For hospitals considering transitioning from a 0/3 h to a 0/1 h pathway, implementation decisions should take broader diagnostic and organisational considerations into account. Swiss National Science Foundation, Swiss Heart Foundation, University Hospital Basel, University of Basel, and Foundation for Cardiovascular Research Basel.

title: Comparative Effects of Pharmacological Treatment on Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
authorString: Zhang J, Wang Y, Li J, Chen Y, Peng X, Thabane L, Lip GYH, Li G.
abstractText: The comparative efficacy and safety of the new drugs (including sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors [SGLT-2Is], glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists [GLP-1RAs], non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists [nsMRAs], and soluble guanylate cyclase stimulators [sGCs]) for heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved (HFmrEF/HFpEF) ejection fraction remains largely unclear. We conducted a systematic review and network meta-analysis to evaluate their comparative effects on HFmrEF/HFpEF, aiming to provide evidence-based guidance for treatment selection. MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were comprehensively searched. We included randomized controlled trials that compared nsMRA, sGC, SGLT-2I, and GLP-1RA with placebo for patients with HFmrEF/HFpEF. Primary efficacy outcomes were cardiovascular (CV) death, hospitalization for heart failure (HF hospitalization), and all-cause mortality, while primary safety outcomes were adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs). The main analysis was conducted to compare the effects on HFmrEF/HFpEF between individual drugs. A frequentist network meta-analysis with random-effects models was used to calculate risk ratios (RRs) for dichotomous outcomes and standardized mean differences (SMDs) for continuous outcomes. A total of 20 randomized controlled trials (RCTs, including 10 drugs from 35 publications) were included for analyses, but none provided head-to-head direct comparisons. No significant differences among all the individual drugs were found in risks of CV death or all-cause mortality. Compared with exenatide, low or moderate certainty evidence showed that dapagliflozin (RR 0.57, 95% CI 0.36-0.91), empagliflozin (RR 0.54, 95% CI 0.34-0.86), and semaglutide (RR 0.43, 95% CI 0.20-0.91) were related to decreased risk of HF hospitalization. No significant differences in the risk of SAEs were found among the individual drugs. Compared with empagliflozin, very low certainty evidence showed that tirzepatide (RR 1.17, 95% CI 1.04-1.32) was related to increased risk of AEs. When comparing the four drug classes (nsMRA, sGC, SGLT-2I, and GLP-1RA), no significant differences in efficacy outcomes were found, while SGLT-2I (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.78-0.96) was associated with a decreased risk of AEs compared with GLP-1RA. No significant differences among the individual SGLT-2I, GLP-1RA, nsMRA, and sGC drugs were found in risks of CV death, all-cause mortality or SAEs in patients with HFmrEF/HFpEF. Further evidence is needed to support these comparative effects and update guidance on medication choice for HFmrEF/HFpEF. PROSPERO identifier number CRD420251143542.

title: Comparative Safety and Efficacy of Oral Anticoagulants in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and Prior Ischemic Stroke: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized-Controlled Clinical Trials.
authorString: Papageorgiou NM, Palaiodimou L, Theodorou A, Stefanou MI, Panagiotopoulos E, Katsanos AH, Safouris A, Kargiotis O, Sacco S, Turc G, Fischer U, Khatri P, Yaghi S, Tsivgoulis G.
abstractText: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and prior ischemic stroke represent a high-risk population facing competing risks of recurrent thromboembolism and hemorrhagic complications. Although direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are recommended over vitamin K antagonists for stroke prevention in AF, no randomized controlled clinical trial has directly compared individual DOACs to each other in this population. We conducted a systematic review and frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis of randomized-controlled clinical trials enrolling patients with AF and prior ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack. MEDLINE, Scopus, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception until May 2026. The primary outcome was any stroke. Secondary outcomes included ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, major bleeding, intracranial hemorrhage (ICH), cardiovascular mortality, and all-cause mortality. Treatment effects were expressed as risk ratios (RR) with 95% CIs. The evidence network comprised 6 trials (18 395 patients) in a star-shaped structure. Each DOAC was informed by a single warfarin-controlled trial, and 2 trials used aspirin as the comparator. All between-DOAC comparisons were indirect. In the network meta-analysis, compared with warfarin, apixaban was the only agent to significantly reduce both any stroke (RR, 0.72 [95% CI, 0.53-0.97]) and major bleeding (RR, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.54-0.99]). Dabigatran, apixaban, and edoxaban each significantly reduced hemorrhagic stroke and ICH versus warfarin, whereas rivaroxaban did not reach significance for any bleeding outcome. Edoxaban was the only agent associated with significantly lower cardiovascular (RR, 0.79 [95% CI, 0.65-0.97]) and all-cause mortality (RR, 0.84 [95% CI, 0.72-0.99]). Based on indirect comparisons only, no differences between individual DOACs were observed. In patients with AF and prior ischemic stroke, individual DOACs reduced intracranial and systemic bleeding relative to warfarin, although not uniformly across agents. Apixaban alone significantly reduced both any stroke and major bleeding versus warfarin, but differences between individual DOACs could not be established given the small number of trials. URL: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/; Unique identifier: CRD420261404062.

title: Effects of exogenous ketones on post-exercise recovery: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Bomans S, Jimenez Garcia B, Leemans L, Mohib O, El M'Rabet I, De Waele E, Janssens P, Beckwée D.
abstractText: Exogenous ketone supplementation has gained attention as a potential strategy to enhance post-exercise recovery. This systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis evaluated its effects on recovery outcomes in adults. PubMed, Embase and Web of Science were searched for randomized controlled and cross-over trials investigating exogenous ketone supplementation. Sixteen studies met the inclusion criteria, of which seven were included in the meta-analysis. Meta-analyses showed no significant effects on muscle soreness (SMD = 0.39, 95% CI [-0.29 to 1.07], p = 0.26, I2 = 0%) or muscle glycogen resynthesis (SMD = 18.21, 95% CI [-19.15 to 55.56], p = 0.34, I2 = 30%). A small effect on post-exercise lactate concentrations (mmol/L) favored the control condition (MD = 0.34, 95% CI [0.02-0.66], p = 0.04, I2 = 0%), although its clinical relevance appears limited. No consistent improvements were observed across physical recovery outcomes. Evidence for cognitive recovery was mixed, with isolated improvements in reaction time, while most outcomes remained unaffected. Creatine kinase concentrations were not significantly affected. Overall, current evidence suggests limited benefits of exogenous ketones for post-exercise recovery and is largely restricted to physically active male adults, limiting generalizability. Further well-powered studies in more diverse populations and recovery contexts are needed.

title: Economic Evaluations of Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction: A Systematic Review
authorString: Acabchuk RL, Larbi NAO, Herman PM, Vieira Neves VV, Goldberg S, Sun S, Haygood LN, Gregory R, Johnson BT, Eric LB.
abstractText: ObjectiveAs healthcare systems increasingly emphasize value-based care, evidence regarding the economic implications of nonpharmacologic interventions is needed to inform implementation and reimbursement decisions. This study aimed to assess the economic value of Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction, identify clinical populations in which economic evaluations have been conducted, and assess the strength of the available economic evidence.DesignSystematic review of economic evaluations.Setting and ParticipantsAll clinical populations and healthcare settings. InterventionsMindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR).Evidence Review MethodsThis systematic review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses 2020 guidelines and was prospectively registered. Nine databases, including MEDLINE, Embase and Scopus, were searched from inception through March 2026 without language restriction, with reference-list screening and citation tracking. Eligible studies evaluated Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction and at least one economic outcome. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed quality using the Quality of Health Economic Studies instrument and the Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards 2022 checklist.ResultsAmong 468 identified records, 12 economic evaluations met inclusion criteria. Studies included 8 randomized clinical trials, 2 Markov models, and 2 prospective cohort studies, conducted in North America (6) and Europe (6). Chronic pain conditions were most frequent (6), followed by mental health disorders (3), breast cancer survivorship (2), and pulmonary arterial hypertension (1). Across these populations, reductions in healthcare utilization and productivity losses generally offset delivery costs, resulting in lower overall costs with equivalent or improved health outcomes for Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction compared with treatment-as-usual. Results were also favorable or comparable relative to active comparators including cognitive behavioral therapy. Despite intervention costs of $195 to $866 per participant (mean, $461), all cost-utility analyses comparing Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction with treatment-as-usual over at least 6 months reported lower costs with equivalent or improved outcomes. Methodological quality was high, with 10 of 12 studies meeting above 80% quality criteria and 5 achieving 100% adherence. Reporting transparency was generally strong.ConclusionsMindfulness-Based Stress Reduction was associated with favorable economic outcomes across chronic pain, mental health, and breast cancer survivorship populations. Current evidence suggests that MBSR may represent a high-value nonpharmacologic intervention, with reductions in healthcare utilization and productivity losses frequently offsetting intervention costs. Additional economic evaluations are needed in underrepresented populations, healthcare settings, and delivery models.

title: Absence of Hepatobiliary Toxicity in Large Animal Species Dosed with AAV8 Gene Therapy for X-linked Myotubular Myopathy.
authorString: Chen CW, Sato T, Crudele JM, Buj-Bello A, Lawlor MW, Mack DL, Fonck C.

journal.title: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy

abstractText: X-linked myotubular myopathy (XLMTM) is caused by mutations in the MTM1 gene that encodes the myotubularin protein, essential for normal muscle development and function. XLMTM manifests as profound muscle weakness and hypotonia at birth, leading to severe respiratory insufficiency, and in many cases, early death. Resamirigene bilparvovec (rAAV8-Des-hMTM1) is a muscle-directed, adeno-associated virus (AAV)-based gene therapy in clinical development for the treatment of XLMTM. In the first-in-human clinical trial (ASPIRO; NCT03199469), rAAV8-Des-hMTM1 was associated with reduced ventilator dependence and unprecedented improvements in motor function in boys with XLMTM. However, four of the 24 participants who received rAAV8-Des-hMTM1 died after developing cholestatic liver failure. Safety results from large-animal studies of rAAV8-Des-MTM1 are presented herein and discussed retrospectively in the context of the adverse events observed in the clinical trial. Healthy infant cynomolgus monkeys and juvenile XLMTM dogs received relatively high doses of rAAV8-Des-hMTM1, or its canine version (rAAV8-Des-cMTM1), respectively. In both species, vector genomes were highest in liver, while myotubularin expression was highest in cardiac or skeletal muscle. rAAV8-Des-MTM1 was generally well-tolerated; importantly, there was no evidence of hyperbilirubinemia or other liver-associated toxicity following rAAV8-Des-MTM1 administration to cynomolgus monkeys or XLMTM dogs.

title: Chlorhexidine within a standardized oral-care bundle for the prevention of ventilator-associated pneumonia: a pragmatic cluster-randomized crossover trial in six medical intensive care units.
authorString: Anushapreethi S, Chhotray P, Samal S, Panda S, Patnaik R, Mishra SB.
abstractText: Chlorhexidine (CHX) has been a long-standing component of oral-care bundles for preventing ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP), but recent evidence has questioned its benefit in non-cardiac-surgery ICU. We evaluated whether adding 0.12% CHX to standardized oral-care bundle provides incremental benefit in a mixed medical ICU. We conducted a prospective, pragmatic cluster-randomized crossover (AB/BA) trial in six adult medical ICUs of a single tertiary-care academic hospital in Bhubaneswar, India. ICUs were randomized as three ICUs of two Period of 9 months with the multicomponent oral-care bundle without chlorhexidine and three with the same bundle plus 0.12% chlorhexidine with a 1-month wash-in and re-training interval. Consecutive adults ventilated for ≥ 48 h were included. The primary outcome was VAP incidence density (Clinical Pulmonary Infection Score (CPIS) > 6) as per 1,000 ventilator-days. Secondary outcomes were 28-day all-cause mortality, duration of mechanical ventilation, ICU length of stay, 28- day ventilator-free days, Beck Oral Assessment Scale (BOAS) and Critical-Care Pain Observation Tool (CPOT) scores. The primary model was a population-averaged Poisson generalized estimating equation (GEE) and adjustment for treatment, period, sequence, age, sex, APACHE II, and SOFA. A total of 1,035 patients (637 No CHX, 398 CHX) accrued 10,024 ventilator-days (5,918 vs. 4,106). Groups were well balanced at baseline (mean age ≈ 55 years; APACHE II ≈ 19.6; SOFA ≈ 13.4). VAP occurred in 100/5,918 ventilator-days (16.9 per 1,000) vs. 77/4,106 (18.8 per 1,000) (No CHX vs. CHX). The adjusted Poisson incidence rate ratio was 1.08 (95% CI 0.84-1.38; p = 0.56). 28-day mortality was 28.7% vs. 26.4% (no CHX vs. CHX) (adjusted OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.65-1.15; p = 0.33). ICU length of stay was longer in the CHX arm (adjusted mean difference + 0.89 days, 95% CI + 0.19 to + 1.58; p = 0.013). BOAS and CPOT scores did not differ. In this trial, adding 0.12% chlorhexidine to a standardized oral-care bundle did not reduce VAP incidence density or 28-day mortality and was associated with a modest increase in ICU length of stay. Routine CHX use provided no clear incremental benefit in a mixed medical ICU population. Clinical Trials Regisrty- India (CTRI) identifier [CTRI/2024/02/062201], registered [01 February 2024].

title: Are Injectable Antihypertensives the Answer to Improving Blood Pressure Control: SiRNAs and Antisense Oligonucleotide Agents.
authorString: Sabouret P, Giamundo DM, Ibrahim A, Calabro P, Ando G, Pathak M, Atar D, Pathak A.
abstractText: Hypertension remains the leading modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide, yet blood pressure control rates remain suboptimal despite the widespread availability of effective antihypertensive therapies. Poor long-term adherence, therapeutic inertia, and the need for lifelong daily treatment continue to limit the effectiveness of current pharmacological strategies. This review examines the biological rationale, available clinical evidence, and potential role of long-acting RNA-based therapies targeting hepatic angiotensinogen synthesis in hypertension. Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) and antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) targeting angiotensinogen represent a novel therapeutic approach that suppresses production of the unique precursor of the renin-angiotensin system. Zilebesiran has demonstrated sustained reductions in circulating angiotensinogen and ambulatory blood pressure following infrequent subcutaneous administration in phase 1 and phase 2 clinical trials. Antisense strategies have provided additional clinical validation of sustained angiotensinogen inhibition, although their antihypertensive efficacy has been less consistent. Ongoing clinical development is addressing long-term cardiovascular outcomes, safety, and optimal patient selection. RNA-based antihypertensive therapies may represent an important evolution in hypertension management by combining upstream renin-angiotensin system inhibition with prolonged pharmacological activity and reduced dependence on daily medication adherence. However, their future clinical role will depend on evidence regarding long-term safety, cardiovascular outcomes, reversibility, cost-effectiveness, patient selection, and integration with conventional antihypertensive therapy.

title: Effect of home blood pressure monitoring on major adverse cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality: results from the VA HOMESTEAD study
authorString: Birkelo B, Velusamy K, Rai NK, Taylor BC, Abdalla M, Margolis K, Shimbo D, Munter P, Nelson D, Kaplan A, Cutting A, Drawz PE, Ishani A.
abstractText:
Importance: Home blood pressure monitoring (HBPM) has been shown to lower blood pressure (BP) in randomized trials, however its real-world effect on clinical outcomes is not known.

Objective:

To determine the association between HBPM and clinical outcomes including cardiovascular events and mortality.

Design:

Target trial emulation employing matched cohorts with index-date follow-up.

Setting:

Veterans Health Administration (VHA) telehealth program. Participants: Eligible Veterans had uncontrolled BP (defined as a systolic BP >140 mmHg) at a primary care visit within VHA, with a systolic BP >140 mmHg at the prior primary care visit or average systolic BP >140 mmHg over the year prior. The HBPM (intervention) group included eligible Veterans who were enrolled in a HBPM program for hypertension between January 1, 2013 and December 31, 2019. Individuals in the control group (usual care) were selected from eligible Veterans who were not enrolled in HBPM. Controls were matched with those in the intervention, in part, on demographics, baseline blood pressure and antihypertensive medication use, baseline frailty, mortality risk, and selected comorbidities. Exposure: HBPM in the VHA telehealth program Main Outcomes: All-cause mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as the first occurrence during follow-up of acute myocardial infarction, stroke, acute heart failure, or unstable angina.

Results:

Among 30,203 Veterans enrolled in HBPM and 30,096 non-enrolled controls, with a median duration of 202 days of HBPM and 6.4 years of follow-up, HBPM was associated with 8.3% lower risk of mortality (hazard ratio 0.92; 95% confidence interval 0.89, 0.95) and a 4.1% higher risk of MACE (HR 1.04; 95% CI 1.01, 1.08). In analyses calibrated for negative control outcomes, there was no longer a statistically significant association between HBPM and MACE. Conclusions and Relevance: HBPM as utilized in routine clinical care among a large national cohort of adults with uncontrolled hypertension was associated with reduced risk of mortality. The association between HBPM with increased risk of MACE may have been due to ascertainment differences between those enrolled and not enrolled in HBPM.

title: <i>F2R</i> Polymorphisms and Efficacy of Clopidogrel Initiated Within 72 Hours for Ischemic Stroke.
authorString: Zhu Y, Gao Y, Chen W, Yan H, Jiang L, Wang T, Yang Y, Pan Y, Wang Y.
abstractText:
Background

The aim of this study was to investigate the association between PAR-1 (protease-activated receptor-1) gene F2R polymorphisms and the efficacy of clopidogrel therapy initiated within a time window extended to 72 hours for mild ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack with intracranial or extracranial atherosclerosis.

Methods

This was a secondary analysis of the INSPIRES trial (Intensive Statin and Antiplatelet Therapy for Acute High-Risk Intracranial or Extracranial Atherosclerosis), a randomized clinical trial conducted at 222 centers across China between September 2018 and October 2022. Four single-nucleotide polymorphisms (F2R [IVSn-14 A/T, rs168753], CYP2C19*2 [681G>A, rs4244285], CYP2C19*3 [636G>A, rs4986893], and CYP2C19*17 [-806C>T, rs12248560]) were genotyped among 5791 patients treated with clopidogrel plus aspirin (n=2894) or aspirin alone (n=2897). The primary efficacy outcome was new stroke, and the safety outcome was moderate-to-severe bleeding within 90 days. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate the interaction between treatment assignment and F2R polymorphisms for the primary outcomes.

Results

Among 5791 patients, 1698 (29.3%) were AA homozygotes, and 4093 (70.7%) were the T-allele carriers (AT/TT) for F2R IVSn-14 polymorphisms. Compared with aspirin alone, clopidogrel-aspirin reduced the rate of new stroke in patients with AT/TT genotype (7.1% versus 9.2%; hazard ratio [HR], 0.77 [95% CI, 0.62-0.95]; P=0.02) but not in carriers of the AA genotype (7.7% versus 8.1%; HR, 0.95 [95% CI, 0.67-1.33]; P=0.75; P=0.30 for interaction). For the safety outcome, the risk of moderate-to-severe bleeding between the clopidogrel plus aspirin group and aspirin group was not significant in patients with AT/TT genotype (HR, 1.91 [95% CI, 0.85-4.29]; P=0.12) or AA genotype (HR, 1.97 [95% CI, 0.59-6.55]; P=0.27; P=0.97 for interaction). Moreover, the presence of CYP2C19 loss-of-function allele carrier status did not alter the effect of the F2R polymorphisms on clinical outcomes, although a marginally reduced risk of stroke with clopidogrel-aspirin versus aspirin alone was observed only among carriers of at least 1 F2R IVSn-14 T allele without CYP2C19 loss-of-function allele (HR, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.52-1.01]; P=0.06).

Conclusions

With the treatment initiated within a time window extended to 72 hours after mild ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack onset, we found that clopidogrel plus aspirin may reduce the occurrence of new stroke specifically in F2R IVSn-14 T-allele carriers. This finding suggests that the clopidogrel-aspirin treatment may appear more beneficial among carriers of the F2R IVSn-14 T allele.

Registration

URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT03635749.

title: Clopidogrel Versus Aspirin Monotherapy According to Atherothrombotic Risk Profile.
authorString: Lee JM, Gim DH, Park YH, Lee JY, Jeong JO, Kim CJ, Yun KH, Lee HC, Chang K, Park MW, Bae JW, Doh JH, Cho BR, Kim HY, Kim W, Kim U, Rha SW, Hong YJ, Lee HJ, Ahn SG, Kim DI, Cho JH, Her SH, Jeon DS, Han SH, Lee JB, Lee CW, Kang D, Choi KH, Park TK, Yang JH, Lee SY, Choi SH, Gwon HC, Song YB, Hahn JY, SMART-CHOICE 3 Investigators.
abstractText:
Background

Clopidogrel monotherapy has shown superior efficacy compared with aspirin after completion of dual antiplatelet therapy following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). However, whether treatment effects differ according to overall atherothrombotic risk integrating clinical and angiographic factors remains unclear.

Methods
