This post hoc analysis of the SMART-CHOICE 3 (Smart Angioplasty Research Team: Choice of Optimal Anti-Thrombotic Strategy in Patients Undergoing Implantation of Coronary Drug-Eluting Stents 3) randomized trial included patients who completed guideline-directed dual antiplatelet therapy after PCI. Atherothrombotic risk was defined using the a Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction Risk Score for Secondary Prevention and complex PCI. Patients with Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction Risk Score for Secondary Prevention ≥3 or complex PCI were classified as higher risk, and those with a Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction Risk Score for Secondary Prevention <3 without complex PCI were classified as lower risk. The primary end point was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (death, myocardial infarction, or stroke). Bleeding was defined as Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type 2, 3, or 5.

Results

Among 5506 patients, 4486 (81.5%) were at higher risk and 1020 (18.5%) were at lower risk. Over a median 2.3 years, the incidence of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events was higher in the higher-risk group (6.1% versus 3.1%; hazard ratio, 1.83 [95% CI, 1.17-2.78]; P=0.007). In higher-risk patients, clopidogrel reduced major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events compared with aspirin (4.6% versus 7.4%; hazard ratio, 0.67 [95% CI, 0.50-0.89]; P=0.006), with no difference in lower-risk patients (3.0% versus 3.2%; hazard ratio, 1.03; P=0.945; interaction P=0.242). Bleeding was similar between groups.

Conclusions

After completion of dual antiplatelet therapy following PCI, clopidogrel monotherapy was associated with lower ischemic risk than aspirin in patients with higher atherothrombotic risk, without increased bleeding.

Registration

URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04418479.

title: The Effects of Cannabinoids in Cardiovascular Disease: A Comprehensive Review.
authorString: Lopez A, Haas MJ, Mooradian AD.
abstractText: Expanded Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and cannabidiol (CBD) use have prompted increasing interest in their risk for cardiovascular complications. This narrative review synthesizes mechanistic, experimental, and epidemiologic evidence on the relationships between cannabinoid exposure and cardiovascular disease, summarizes acute and chronic outcomes, evaluates therapeutic potential of non-psychoactive cannabinoids, and identifies future research priorities. Cannabinoid type 1 receptors in cardiovascular tissues promote sympathetic activation, tachycardia, and endothelial dysfunction, while cannabinoid type 2 receptor activation exerts anti-inflammatory and athero-protective effects. Acute THC exposure in humans produces tachycardia, increased myocardial oxygen demand, vascular stiffness, and transient blood-pressure alterations. Recent large observational studies and meta-analyses suggest associations between cannabis/cannabinoid use and increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular events. While causality has not yet been definitively established, the accumulation of in vitro and in vivo evidence indicates potentially significant cardiovascular risks associated with frequent and/or heavy cannabinoid use, particularly in individuals with underlying cardiovascular disease or other risk factors. In the future, clinicians should screen for cannabinoid use, and standardized exposure metrics, longitudinal studies and randomized controlled trials are urgently needed.

title: Transient Lung-Volume Reduction Improves First-Shock Cardioversion Success by Reducing Transthoracic Impedance in Patients With Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
authorString: Yildirim O, Şahin BK, Kaplan HS, Akincioğlu B, Şahan HF, Özdemir Ö.
abstractText: Transthoracic impedance (TTI) is an important determinant of the efficacy of direct-current cardioversion (DCCV), as increased impedance may reduce myocardial current delivery. Because lung volume influences thoracic electrical properties, transient lung-volume reduction (TLVR) may represent a simple strategy for acutely lowering TTI and improving cardioversion efficacy. This study evaluated the effect of a standardized TLVR maneuver on TTI and first-shock cardioversion success in patients with persistent atrial fibrillation (AF). This prospective, randomized study included 116 patients with persistent AF scheduled for first-time radiofrequency ablation. Patients were randomized 1:1 to conventional mechanical ventilation (standard CV group, n = 58) or a standardized TLVR maneuver immediately before cardioversion (TLVR CV group, n = 58). Baseline TTI was measured before the intervention, and post-TLVR TTI was additionally measured in the TLVR group. All patients underwent anterior-posterior cardioversion with an initial 200 J shock. First-shock success was defined as maintenance of sinus rhythm for at least 1 min. Multivariable linear and hierarchical logistic regression analyses were performed to investigate determinants of impedance reduction and first-shock success. First-shock cardioversion success was significantly higher in the TLVR CV group than in the standard CV group (53.4% vs. 29.3%, p = 0.008), whereas cumulative success after up to three shocks was similar (96.6% vs. 91.4%, p = 0.242). The impedance reduction rate was significantly higher among patients with successful first-shock cardioversion (9.09% vs. 5.00%, p < 0.001). In multivariable linear regression, TLVR independently increased the impedance reduction rate by 1.75 percentage points (B = 1.751, p = 0.001), while a higher Body Roundness Index was associated with a lower reduction (β = -0.468, p < 0.001). In the mechanistic logistic regression model, each 1% increase in impedance reduction was associated with a 2.23-fold higher likelihood of first-shock success (OR = 2.226, p < 0.001). Model explanatory power increased from 56.3% to 74.9% after the incorporation of impedance reduction. A standardized TLVR maneuver immediately before cardioversion was associated with greater TTI reduction and an approximately twofold increase in first-shock cardioversion success in patients with persistent AF. The impedance reduction rate emerged as a strong independent predictor of successful initial cardioversion, supporting a potential physiological mechanism linking acute lung-volume reduction to improved electrical cardioversion efficacy.

title: Balneotherapy in knee osteoarthritis: a review of therapeutic efficacy and inflammatory cytokine regulation.
authorString: Lai X, Ji L, Zou Y, Wang J, Zhan Y, Yao L, Yang X.
abstractText: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a common degenerative joint disease with an inflammatory component. Balneotherapy has been used for KOA, but its clinical efficacy and mechanisms remain uncertain. This narrative review summarizes clinical evidence and proposes a hypothesis-generating mechanistic framework. PubMed and CNKI were searched up to June 2026. Interventions were categorized as mineral-water bathing, aquatic exercise/hydrotherapy, mud therapy/pelotherapy, or multimodal spa programmes, and clinical studies were assessed for risk of bias. Randomized trials and meta-analyses suggest that balneotherapy may improve short-term pain and function, with benefits reportedly persisting for 3-9 months in some studies; however, most trials had high risk of bias, heterogeneous protocols, small samples, and short follow-up. Mechanistic evidence is largely preclinical or indirect. H₂S has the most consistent anti-inflammatory and anti-catabolic rationale, acting via NF-κB and MMP-13 inhibition. Calcium and magnesium may modulate TRPV4/NLRP3 and NF-κB signaling, but human balneotherapy evidence is lacking, and mineral synergy remains unverified. A three-tier "heat-mineral-signal" framework is proposed, but target engagement after bathing and causality between biomarker changes and clinical improvement have not been established. Overall, balneotherapy may offer symptomatic benefits in KOA, but current evidence is limited and heterogeneous. The proposed mechanistic model is hypothesis-generating; higher-quality trials with standardized protocols, long-term follow-up, and integrated clinical and mechanistic outcomes are needed.

title: Mechanical stress-induced release of mitochondrial double-stranded RNA activates RIG-I to drive osteogenic differentiation in aortic disease
authorString: Graef M, Bender F, Dudek S, Vasileiadou P, Soler S, Schlee-Guimaraes T, Steinheuer LM, Spitzer J, Thurley K, Nowak RP, Maser K, Schmidt S, Goody PR, Schlee M, Zimmer S, Nickenig G, Zillinger T, Bartok E, Hartmann G.
abstractText:
Background

Gain-of-function mutations in RIG-I and MDA5 (RIG-I-like receptors, RLR) cause Singleton-Merten syndrome, an interferonopathy with early aortic calcification. Here we set out to study a possible involvement of RIG-I-like receptor signaling in the formation of aortic valve stenosis in general. Methods and results: We investigated whether mechanical stress-induced RLR activation promotes osteogenic differentiation and calcification of primary human aortic cells, whether such RLR activation drives the development of aortic valve stenosis in vivo, and whether inhibition of downstream JAK/STAT activation ameliorates aortic valve stenosis. We found that activation of primary human aortic interstitial cells by exogenous RIG-I- and MDA5 agonists induced a type I interferon response and an osteogenic program including increased expression of BMP-2 and BSP2, and promoted calcification. These effects were RIG-I/MDA5 or MAVS-dependent, as assessed by CRISPR/Cas9 knockouts. The stress-granule protein G3BP1 and the Wnt receptor FZD5 were induced downstream of RLR activation and were required for osteogenic gene expression and calcification. To assess a potential endogenous source of RIG-I activation, mechanical stretch mimicking valvular tissue stress was applied in cell cuture, which induced a significant RIG-I-dependent interferon response. Sequencing of highly purified preparations of double-stranded RNA from stretched cells demonstrated a predominant mitochondrial origin of double-stranded RNA, and depleting mitochondrial RNA abolished the stretch-dependent response. The JAK/STAT inhibitor ruxolitinib suppressed the RIG-I-induced response including the expression of osteogenic factors in vitro . In a murine wire-injury model of aortic stenosis, MAVS deficiency attenuated valvular morphological changes and improved hemodynamic parameters. Ruxolitinib attenuated hemodynamic progression, prevented aortic stenosis development, and improved survival.

Conclusions:

Altogether, our results demonstrate that the mechanical-stress-induced release of mitochondrial double-stranded RNA activates RIG-I signaling in aortic interstitial cells, thereby driving osteogenic differentiation and calcification via a MAVS- and G3BP1-dependent pathway. JAK/STAT inhibition with ruxolitinib mitigates this process in a mouse model of aortic valve stenosis, identifying a candidate therapeutic strategy.

Translational Perspective

Aortic valve stenosis is a common and progressive disease, with no approved drug treatment. The only effective intervention is surgical or transcatheter valve replacement. This study shows that mechanical stress on human aortic interstitial cells leads to the leakage of mitochondrial double-stranded RNA, mistakenly recognized by the antiviral sensor RIG-I as foreign viral RNA, triggering a type I interferon response and osteogenic differentiation. Ruxolitinib, an oral Janus kinase inhibitor already approved for other conditions, reduced this response in cell culture and the development of disease in a mouse model of aortic valve stenosis. The results highlight the therapeutic potential of a ruxolitinib-based drug-repurposing strategy for aortic valve stenosis, a clinical strategy to be confirmed in clinical trials.

title: Postoperative Vocal fold mobility impairment after thoracic aortic surgery: A systematic review and meta-analysis of incidence, anatomy, and ascertainment.
authorString: Farooq O, Jamileh E, Muhammad F, Nawaz A, Abbas Z, Layton G, Zakkar M, Antoun I.
abstractText:
Objectives

Postoperative vocal fold mobility impairment (VFMI) after thoracic aortic surgery is reported inconsistently because operative anatomy, outcome definitions and postoperative ascertainment vary substantially. We evaluated variation in observed VFMI, its relationship with anatomical exposure and ascertainment, and its reported clinical consequences.

Methods

PubMed, Embase and MEDLINE (Ovid) were searched from inception to July 2026 for adult studies reporting VFMI after open or hybrid thoracic aortic surgery. Random-effects meta-analysis was restricted to symptom-triggered, instrumentally confirmed cohorts undergoing direct open thoracic-aortic reconstruction. Risk of bias was assessed using QUIPS and JBI guidance, and certainty using GRADE.

Results

Thirty-nine observational studies were included. Eleven symptom-triggered, instrumentally confirmed cohorts (2,082 patients; 263 events) contributed to the primary synthesis. Pooled observed VFMI was 14.9% (95% CI 9.4-21.5%), but heterogeneity was substantial (I² 92.7%, 95% CI 89.7-94.6%) and the 95% prediction interval was 0.3-43.3%. Study-level incidence ranged from 4.0% to 38.8%. Greater anatomical extent, particularly distal arch or descending exposure, was consistently associated with higher observed VFMI, whereas specific left-subclavian-proximate estimates were based on limited observational evidence. VFMI was also associated with pulmonary morbidity, airway intervention and prolonged hospitalisation.

Conclusion

A single pooled incidence does not adequately describe postoperative VFMI after thoracic aortic surgery. Observed risk varies markedly with anatomical exposure and ascertainment strategy. The evidence supports targeted postoperative laryngeal assessment in symptomatic patients and highlights the need to evaluate routine screening in selected high-risk distal arch and descending procedures.

title: Portable ultra-low field MRI in neurocritical care and intensive care units: A systematic review of diagnostic performance and feasibility.
authorString: Mulhall CB, O'Kelly R, Temperley HC, O'Loughlin C, McDonnell J, Doyle RS, Ho J.
abstractText: To synthesise evidence on the diagnostic performance, safety, feasibility and clinical impact of ultra-low-field portable magnetic resonance imaging (pMRI) in adult neurocritical care and intensive care unit (ICU) populations. PubMed, Scopus and Embase were searched from inception to 6 February 2026 and supplemented by grey literature and citation searching. We included original English-language studies of adult ICU, neurocritical care or emergency department patients undergoing pMRI at ≤ 0.1 T. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Risk of bias in diagnostic comparisons was assessed with an adapted QUADAS-2 framework, and feasibility and safety outcomes were appraised narratively. Because of heterogeneity, findings were synthesised narratively. The review was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261302014). Eleven studies published between 2020 and 2024 were included, comprising 694 patient participants and 715 patient examinations, plus 40 healthy controls. Cohorts overlapped substantially: six studies came wholly and one partly from a single institution, and one ECMO study was a subset of another. The number of unique patients is therefore estimated at 281 to 677. In the multicentre ECMO study, adverse events occurred in 3 of 50 patients (6%). One was serious: an intra-aortic balloon pump malfunction attributed to electrocardiographic artefact. No adverse events were reported in the other seven independent cohorts that reported safety outcomes, and two studies did not report safety outcomes. For ischaemic stroke, pMRI detected infarction in 45 of 50 patients (90%). By sequence, sensitivity was 100% for FLAIR, 98% for T2-weighted imaging and 86% for diffusion-weighted imaging. Visual DWI-FLAIR mismatch identified patients scanned within 4.5 h with 60% sensitivity, 82% specificity and a 93% negative predictive value. Sensitivity for intracerebral haemorrhage was 80.4% (specificity 96.6%) on initial blinded evaluation. It was 92.1% (specificity 99.3%) in a later cohort in which raters had clinical context and images used deep-learning reconstruction, with lower sensitivity for infratentorial haemorrhage (75.0%). Only one subdural haemorrhage and no extradural haemorrhages were reported. Midline-shift detection showed 93% sensitivity, 96% specificity and a kappa of 0.87. pMRI detected hypoxic-ischaemic brain injury in 12 of 12 affected post-cardiac-arrest patients. In ECMO patients, pMRI detected 8 of 8 ischaemic events, compared with 4 of 8 on head CT, but only 1 of 2 haemorrhages. Up to 28% of examinations were nondiagnostic, mainly because of motion. Ultra-low-field pMRI is a feasible bedside neuroimaging adjunct with a low but non-zero adverse-event rate. It is of particular value for ischaemic injury, midline shift and serial monitoring. Lower and variable sensitivity for haemorrhage, the nonspecificity of FLAIR hyperintensity, overlapping single-institution cohorts and small samples mean that larger multicentre validation studies are needed.

title: Utilization of Microaxial Mechanical Circulatory Support Among the Pediatric Population: A Systematic Review.
authorString: Jones AJ, Rahimov D, Smoot D, Mustafa M, Mallur K, Rajab TK, Hoopes CW, Tchantchaleishvili V.
abstractText:
Background

Utilization of microaxial pumps for temporary mechanical circulatory support in children has increased in recent years. However, data on patient selection, implantation techniques, and outcomes remain limited.

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted in July 2025 to identify case reports and case series reporting the use of microaxial pumps in patients aged 18 years or less. Forty-four studies comprising 100 patients were identified, and patient-level data were extracted for analysis.

Results

The median age of the patients was 14 [IQR, 11.5-16] years, with a median weight of 52 [40-73] kg and median body surface area of 1.59 [1.35-1.85] m2. The most common diagnoses were cardiomyopathy (29%), heart allograft rejection (26%), and myocarditis (21%). Impella CP was the most frequently used device (48%), followed by Impella 2.5 and Impella 5.5 (each 21%). Access was predominantly obtained via the femoral artery (47%). Percutaneous implantation was performed in 47% of patients. Patients were weaned from microaxial support for cardiac recovery (42%) or heart transplantation (31%). Fourteen patients (14%) died prior to discharge, with significantly higher mortality among patients supported with ECPella (29%) compared with microaxial pump alone (6%; p = 0.01). The median duration of support was 6 [4-13] days. At the median follow-up of 119 [23-180] days overall survival was 84%.

Conclusion

Microaxial pumps represent an important addition to temporary mechanical circulatory support in pediatric patients and can serve as an alternative to VA-ECMO in selected cases. Outcomes were less favorable when used in tandem configurations such as ECPella, reflecting the greater severity of illness in these patients.

title: Exercise Capacity in Chronic Respiratory Diseases in the Context of Multimorbidity: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
authorString: Marinho MFD, Schafauser-Segundo NS, Hurst JR, Mendes RG.
abstractText: Chronic respiratory diseases (CRD) are accompanied by coexisting chronic conditions, which may occur individually or as multimorbidity burden or patterns. These conditions may contribute to exercise intolerance, a determinant of prognosis. However, their association with exercise capacity remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate, in individuals with CRD, the association between one or more other chronic conditions (multimorbidity) and exercise capacity and to quantify this relationship through meta-analysis. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, Virtual Health Library, and CINAHL until July 2025. Observational studies evaluating exercise capacity in adults with CRD, with coexisting chronic conditions, using field- or laboratory-based tests were included. Methodological quality was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute checklists. Meta-analyses were performed using random-effects models. A total of 49 studies were included in the qualitative synthesis (n=28,972 participants), and 23 contributed to the quantitative synthesis. Most studies involved individuals with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Sensitivity analyses excluding outliers yielded clinically meaningful reductions in six-minute walk distance for metabolic (MD -34.26 m; 95% CI -46.98 to -21.53; I2=5.91%), cardiovascular (MD -27.18 m; 95% CI -39.59 to -14.78; I2=16.19%), and mental health conditions (MD -29.52 m; 95% CI -54.89 to -4.15; I2=0%). In individuals with CRD, multimorbidity is associated with reduced exercise capacity, with clinically meaningful reductions particularly in the presence of metabolic and cardiovascular conditions. Although the certainty of evidence is very low, these findings highlight the importance of considering multimorbidity when interpreting exercise limitation in CRD. PROSPERO, identifier CRD420251125343.

title: Peripheral nerve block injection pressure monitoring: A systematic review.
authorString: De Cassai A, Capdevila X, Coppens S, Dossi R, Dost B, El-Boghdadly K, Hadzic A, Saporito A.
abstractText: To determine whether injection pressure and pressure-time characteristics can discriminate potentially hazardous needle-tip locations during peripheral nerve injection. Systematic review of experimental preclinical studies with narrative synthesis. Animal, ex vivo biological nerve, and human cadaver models of peripheral nerve injection. Needle placement and injection at intraneural, intrafascicular, perineural, or extraneural locations. CENTRAL, PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception to April 28, 2026 and updated on September 19, 2026. Studies reporting opening, peak, or plateau pressure or pressure-time characteristics in relation to anatomically defined needle-tip location were eligible. Human clinical studies and non-biological bench models were excluded. Risk of bias was evaluated using SYRCLE for animal studies and a domain-based framework for cadaveric studies. Because of substantial heterogeneity in experimental models, injection techniques, and pressure definitions, meta-analysis was not considered appropriate. Twenty-eight studies met the inclusion criteria: 12 animal or animal ex vivo studies and 16 human cadaver studies. Intraneural injection was generally associated with higher peak and plateau pressures than perineural injection, but substantial overlap occurred across needle locations. Importantly, low pressure did not reliably rule out intraneural injection, while elevated pressure was also observed during needle-nerve contact and fascial injection. Consequently, the commonly proposed 15-psi threshold showed inconsistent sensitivity across experimental settings. Lower thresholds, including 12 psi, appeared more sensitive in some models but have not been clinically validated. Beyond absolute pressure values, the rate of pressure rise and pressure-time curve morphology showed potential for differentiating needle-tip locations. Injection pressure monitoring may provide a nonspecific warning of needle placement within or against a poorly compliant structure. However, preclinical evidence alone cannot establish whether it should be used routinely or whether it reduces nerve injury. No universal pressure threshold or clinically recommended injection rate can currently be defined.

title: Resting-State Functional MRI and Clinical Outcomes After Acute Disorders of Consciousness: A Systematic Review.
authorString: Kazazian K, Czink D, Iansavitchene A, Owen AM, Norton L.
abstractText: Accurate assessment and prognostication of patients with acute disorders of consciousness (DoC) after severe brain injury remain a substantial clinical challenge. Resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) measures spontaneous, temporally correlated brain activity in the absence of external stimulation and provides objective insight into the integrity of large-scale neural networks that support brain function. Emerging evidence suggests that assessing neural integrity using rs-fMRI may improve outcome prediction in patients with acute DoC. This review summarizes the current evidence of rs-fMRI as an assessment tool during the acute phase of severe brain injury. Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, we conducted a systematic literature search using MEDLINE and Embase databases from January 2006 to March 2026. Eligible studies included peer-reviewed empirical investigations of adult patients with acute DoC (<28 days postinjury) that examined associations between rs-fMRI measures and clinical outcomes. The systematic review protocol was registered in the PROSPERO International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420251085923). Of 396 studies screened, 30 met eligibility criteria. Across these studies, a total of 800 patients (mean age = 48, 69% male) were scanned at a weighted average of 9.31 days after intensive care unit admission. Ten studies included patients exclusively with traumatic brain injury, 8 with cardiac arrest, 2 with encephalopathy, and 10 included mixed etiologies. The most frequently assessed resting-state networks were the default mode (n = 20) and executive control networks (n = 11), followed by visual (n = 6), salience (n = 6), sensorimotor (n = 6), and auditory (n = 5) networks. Across studies, significant associations between rs-fMRI measures and outcome were consistently reported, despite heterogeneity in methodology. The most commonly reported patient outcomes were functional or neurologic status, assessed at hospital discharge or between 3 and 12 months postinjury. Current evidence consistently demonstrates that rs-fMRI acquired during the acute phase of brain injury is associated with neurologic and functional outcomes in patients with DoC. In addition, rs-fMRI may help identify patients more likely to recover consciousness and achieve favorable functional outcomes by characterizing the integrity of large-scale brain networks. However, substantial heterogeneity and small sample sizes limit comparability across studies. Standardized acquisition and analysis frameworks, along with larger prospective studies, are needed to validate the clinical utility of rs-fMRI and support translation into an assessment tool after brain injury.

title: Characteristics of treatment responses to physical exercise and diet in diabetic peripheral artery disease patients: a systematic review.
authorString: Wang Q, Qian N, Liu Y, Zhou M.
abstractText:
Purpose

Peripheral artery disease (PAD) affects walking performance and increases risk of amputation. Diabetes mellitus (DM) not only contributes to disease progression but may also affect treatment effects. Though physical exercise is crucial in PAD management and diet optimization may reduce risk of atherosclerosis, their effects and variations in diabetic PAD patients remain unclear. The present systematic review aims to summarize features of treatment response to physical exercise and diet management in diabetic PAD patients, and provide crucial information on optimization of PAD management of these patients in clinical practice.

Methods

A systematic review was performed on human studies investigating effects of physical exercise and diet on development and improvement of diabetic PAD patients by searching PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and CINAHL. The review was performed according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analysis (PRISMA). The certainty level of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE).

Results

A total of 18 studies were included, 15 of which evaluated effects of exercise on diabetic PAD, and three evaluated correlation between diet and diabetic PAD. Supervised exercise therapy (SET) and home-based exercise were able to improve ankle-brachial index (ABI) and blood flow velocity in diabetic PAD. In contrast, walking performance such as the six minute walk distance (6MWD), maximal walking time and distance, peak walking time (PWT) and claudication onset time (COT) were not significantly improved or presented conflicting results. Administration of multiple exercises or alternative interventions such as shock wave therapy or low-frequency pulsed electromagnetic field therapy (LFPMT) may enhance improvement of ABI. Adherence to Mediterranean diet was associated with blood flow and intermittent claudication, as well as risk of development of PAD. GRADE analysis revealed very low to moderate grade evidence for findings on ABI, flow velocity and functions, mainly due to study types, number of studies available, small sample size, moderate risk of bias and conflicting results. Similarly, low grade evidence was also revealed for effects and association of diet on risk of PAD due to study type and number of studies available.

Conclusion

Diabetic PAD patients may present reduced treatment response to physical exercise in walking performance and other functions, which may be improved by combination of multiple physical exercises or alternative interventions with or without combination of exercise. Mediterranean diet may be associated with beneficial effects, which requires further investigations. These findings were of very low to moderate level of certainty, and therefore, further validation is warranted in the future.

title: Genetic differences between fibroelastic deficiency and Barlow's disease in mitral valve prolapse.
authorString: Feirer N, Weber M, Doppler SA, Knoll K, Li L, Miranda L, Yu M, Lahm H, Vafadarnejad E, Kameric M, Luzius T, Seeler S, Gottmann I, Wirth F, Schwab M, Geirsson A, Lichtner P, Small AM, Berger K, Stoll M, Lange R, Gruber P, Schunkert H, Hagége A, Bouatia-Naji N, Müller-Myhsok B, Trenkwalder T, Krane M, Dreßen M.
abstractText:
Aims

Fibroelastic deficiency (FED) and Barlow's disease represent subtypes of degenerative mitral valve prolapse (MVP). Whether these two conditions represent opposite ends of an anatomic spectrum or rather distinct etiologies remains unclear.

Methods and results

To study this question from a genetic perspective, we conducted the first genome-wide association study (GWAS) on anatomical subtypes of MVP, exploring the MVP-Munich and MVP-France cohorts, including 1,064 FED and 821 Barlow's disease cases, and 11,923 controls. Patients were stratified via echocardiographic and surgical reports. GWAS meta-analysis was performed separately for FED and Barlow's disease. The identified risk loci were analyzed via gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), targeted variant-phenotype association analysis, and mitral valve tissue was analyzed in single-nucleus RNA-sequencing.For FED, one risk locus achieved genome-wide significance (p<5e-8) at 5q23.3 (CHSY3). For Barlow's disease, two independent loci with genome-wide significance were identified at 5q35.2 (CPLX2) and 10q26.12 (WDR11). Further 30 additional independent signals showed a suggestive association (p<5e-5) with FED, and 30 different independent signals with Barlow's disease. Targeted variant-phenotype association analysis revealed an association of FED with atrial arrhythmias, while Barlow's disease was associated with atrial and ventricular arrhythmias. In combination with GSEA, our results linked Barlow's disease to changes in cell cycle, transcription, senescence, and ubiquitination. FED was connected to cardiac, valvular, mesoderm, and endoderm development.

Conclusions

This study suggests genetic heterogeneity between FED and Barlow's disease and identifies risk loci for future investigation.

title: An Infusible Decellularized Extracellular Matrix Material Binds to Vasculature in Infarcted Myocardium and Induces Pro-Reparative Gene Expression Following Acute Myocardial Infarction Through Inherent Avidity and Bioactive Signaling.
authorString: Nguyen MB, Chen A, Lyons Q, Ninh VK, McCabe MC, Luo C, Bridgelal BD, Uhre C, Cheng J, Reimold KE, Cao S, Hansen KC, King KR, Christman KL.
abstractText: To treat acute myocardial infarction (MI), we previously engineered an infusible decellularized extracellular matrix (iECM) biomaterial that reduces vascular permeability and exerts immunomodulatory and pro-reparative effects. To probe the heterogenous contents of iECM and its contribution to infarct localization and downstream biological function, we separated iECM into high and low molecular weight (MW) components. Though mass spectrometry showed similar compositions, biochemical analysis and transmission electron microscopy revealed higher sGAG content within the nanofibrillar high MW, while the globular low MW had more exposed functional groups. These differences translated to a higher binding efficiency of the high MW to ECM proteins and cell surface receptors under flow, while the low MW drove the reduction in vascular permeability. Neither component alone achieved the infarct retention levels of complete iECM, showing that the two components exhibit dependent infarct localization and both are necessary for iECM's overall function. Via single‑nucleus RNA sequencing, both components elicited comparable immunomodulatory and pro‑reparative transcriptional profiles, suggesting that the similarity in composition likely drives the transcriptional response. These findings elucidate the material properties of an intravascularly deliverable ECM biomaterial and how those properties relate to downstream biological behavior, enabling future work investigating nanomaterial mimicry and improvements in material processing and potency.

title: Does thrombocytopenia predict short-term mortality after transcatheter and surgical aortic valve replacement?
authorString: Taban VB, Güner A, Alsancak Y, Dereli Y, Görmüş N.
abstractText:
Objective

Postprocedural thrombocytopenia is frequently observed after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and surgical aortic valve replacement (sAVR), but its independent prognostic value remains unclear. We investigated whether platelet reduction after TAVI and sAVR independently predicts short-term mortality beyond baseline procedural risk.

Methods

This retrospective single-center study included 216 patients who underwent aortic valve replacement between 2015 and 2020. Sixty-seven patients underwent TAVI and 149 underwent sAVR. Mechanical valve recipients were retained in the overall cohort but excluded from the primary TAVI-sAVR comparison. Propensity score overlap weighting was used to reduce baseline differences between groups. Longitudinal changes in platelet count (PLT), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) were evaluated using generalized estimating equation models, and factors associated with 90-day mortality were assessed using Firth penalized logistic regression.

Results

The primary comparative cohort included 67 TAVI and 93 sAVR patients. After overlap weighting, adequate balance was achieved for all measured baseline covariates. Significant treatment × time interactions were observed for PLT (p = 0.001), NLR (p < 0.001), and PLR (p = 0.002). On postprocedural day 3, moderate thrombocytopenia was more frequent after sAVR than TAVI (33.5% vs. 8.3%), whereas normal platelet levels were more frequent after TAVI (45.6% vs. 8.2%; overall p < 0.001). Weighted 90-day mortality did not differ significantly between TAVI and sAVR (12.6% vs. 17.5%, p = 0.487). In Firth regression models, only EuroSCORE II remained independently associated with 90-day mortality.

Conclusion

Postprocedural platelet and inflammatory responses showed different temporal patterns after TAVI and sAVR. However, these biomarker changes were not independently associated with 90-day mortality after adjustment, whereas EuroSCORE II remained independently associated with mortality. Serial hematological changes should therefore be interpreted together with baseline clinical risk rather than as isolated prognostic markers.

title: In Situ Fenestration-Assisted TEVAR in Patients With Complex Pathology Involving the Aortic Arch.
authorString: Petrov IS, Stankov ZI, Vasilev SK, Adam GI, Getzov YS.

journal.title: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists

abstractText:
Purpose

To assess the feasibility, safety, and short-term clinical outcomes of in situ fenestration during thoracic endovascular aortic repair (ISF-TEVAR) employing an electrocautery-connected guidewire combined with a novel, pump-less, extracorporeal femoro-carotid bypass for cerebral perfusion in patients with complex aortic arch pathology.

Materials and methods

This prospective, single-center study included 19 consecutive patients treated between February 2024 and September 2025. A homemade extracorporeal arterio-arterial bypass was constructed using femoral arterial inflow and intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) tubing connected to supra-aortic sheaths to maintain continuous cerebral perfusion during fenestration. Fenestrations were performed with an electrocautery-connected 0.018-inch chronic total occlusion-dedicated guidewire. Patients' demographics, procedural details, perioperative outcomes, and early follow-up data were analyzed, with stratification according to the number of fenestrated supra-aortic branches.

Results

A total of 37 supra-aortic branches were targeted: 3-branch fenestrations in 6 patients (31.6%), 2-branch in 6 patients (31.6%), and single-branch in 7 patients (36.8%). Technical success, defined as successful graft fenestration with patent branches on completion angiography, was achieved in 94.5% (35/37). One failed innominate artery fenestration was managed with chimney-assisted TEVAR, and 1 left subclavian artery fenestration was successfully completed in a subsequent procedure. Operative time increased with procedural complexity (140 ± 12 minutes for 1 branch, 152 ± 10 minutes for 2 branches, and 162 ± 13 minutes for 3 branches; P = .004). No intraprocedural mortality occurred. Two perioperative strokes (10.5%) and 2 in-hospital deaths (10.5%) were recorded, 1 death was due to vertebrobasilar stroke and the other due to retrograde type A aortic dissection with rupture. Median hospital stay was 8 days. During a mean follow-up of 9.2 months, there was no aorta-related mortality, with an overall survival rate of 89.5%. All stented branches remained patent, and 2 endoleaks (10.5%) were successfully treated endovascularly.

Conclusion

In situ fenestration during thoracic endovascular aortic repair using an electrocautery-connected wire combined with a temporary, pressure gradient-driven extracorporeal femoro-carotid bypass is a feasible, reproducible, and safe technique for complex aortic arch repair. This fully percutaneous approach ensures continuous cerebral perfusion, demonstrates efficient procedural metrics, and yields favorable short-term outcomes, representing a practical alternative when custom-made devices or hybrid surgical procedures are not available.Clinical ImpactIn situ fenestration-assisted TEVAR combined with a temporary pumpless extracorporeal femoral-carotid bypass enables continuous cerebral perfusion during complex aortic arch interventions without the need for cardiopulmonary bypass or surgical debranching. This technique expands the feasibility of fully endovascular multibranch arch repair in urgent or anatomically challenging cases where custom-made devices are unavailable. For clinicians, this approach offers a practical and reproducible strategy to mitigate cerebral ischemic risk while maintaining procedural efficiency and percutaneous access. This technique may facilitate broader adoption of in situ fenestration by providing a cerebral protection strategy using readily available endovascular equipment.

title: A semi-supervised diffusion model for automated segmentation of vascular plaques.
authorString: Liu J, Balamuralikrishna PTS, Locke L, Pickhardt PJ, Summers RM.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Int J Comput Assist Radiol Surg
journal.title: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
journal.isoabbreviation: Int J Comput Assist Radiol Surg

abstractText:
Purpose

Segmenting vascular plaques in the carotid arteries, aorta, and iliac arteries on CT is important because plaque burden relates to cardiovascular and stroke risk and can guide treatment. However, manual labeling is often infeasible and time-consuming across large vascular regions. Semi-supervised learning (SSL) can leverage unlabeled CT data to enable accurate plaque segmentation with only limited labels.

Methods

We applied a diffusion-based semi-supervised learning (SSL) method for vascular plaque segmentation in non-contrast CT by formulating the task as multi-class segmentation of plaques and 26 adjacent anatomical structures. The method employs a teacher-student architecture with a shared diffusion encoder to learn domain-invariant feature representations and separate teacher and student decoders to decouple labeled and unlabeled data, reducing overfitting and improving robustness. To address the severe class imbalance caused by the small size of plaques, we developed a plaque-aware oversampling strategy and a labeled-data-guided training for the shared encoder and student decoder. We used 142 NIH non-contrast CT scans, divided into 119 training scans and 23 validation scans. We externally evaluated the method on 95 scans from the University of Wisconsin and 50 scans from Medipol University Mega Hospital and compared its performance with supervised nnU-Net and a strong SSL baseline.

Results

The improved SSL method significantly outperformed the original SSL method and supervised training with the same architecture when using 14 labeled training scans ( p<0.0001 ). With these 14 labeled training scans, it achieved DSC values of 58.8% and 82.3% on CTRATE and Renal Donor, respectively, within 2.7--2.8 percentage points of the same architecture trained with all 119 training scans labeled.

Conclusion

The SSL method segments plaques in the carotid, aortic, and iliac arteries with performance approaching that of fully supervised training while using only 14 labeled training scans, supporting scalable plaque burden assessment.

title: Re: Nadia Bitar, Gabriella Howell, Ming He, et al. Bacterial Vaccines for Recurrent Urinary Tract Infections: A Systematic Review with Emerging Evidence in Kidney Transplant Recipients. Eur Urol Focus. In press. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.euf.2026.06.022.
authorString: Sahni DS, Kingsmore DB, Aitken E.

title: Barriers and facilitators of cardiac rehabilitation focusing on underserved groups: a mixed-methods systematic review.
authorString: Humoud HA, AbuElkhair AA, Mbolo GD, Buckley BJ, Williams NH, Lane DA.

title: Nasal Photodisinfection and Surgical Site Infection Following Coronary Bypass Surgery: An Interrupted Time Series Analysis.
authorString: Rubens FD, Kang N, Charlebois A, Hogan C, Masters R, Neilipovitz K, Al Atassi T, Boodhwani M, Chan V, Clarizia N, Guo M, Issa H, Lam BK, Toeg H, Taljaard M, Voisine P.
abstractText: Surgical site infections (SSI) complicating coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) carry substantial morbidity and mortality. We evaluated compliance with nasal decolonization and SSI rates after institutional implementation of preoperative nasal photodisinfection in isolated CABG. Single-centre interrupted time series (ITS) of 2,172 procedures (June 2023-January 2026, transition month June 2025), comprising 24 pre-intervention months (mupirocin era, n = 1,678) and 8 post-intervention months (photodisinfection era, n = 494). The primary effectiveness outcome was conduit harvest surgical site infection (CHSSI) at 30 days; compliance with nasal decolonization was the primary implementation outcome. Secondary outcomes included total surgical site infection (TSSI). Step changes in log-transformed monthly rates were analyzed using restricted maximum likelihood segmented regression accounting for first-order autocorrelation; compliance was modelled untransformed. Compliance with mupirocin was 35.4% (68.1% in elective patients; 17.5% in non-elective patients), compared with 93.3% compliance with nasal photodisinfection. Compliance rose 37.0 percentage points (95% CI 21.9-52.0). TSSI was 9.1% pre-intervention vs 5.9% post-intervention (change in intercept RR 0.32, 95% CI 0.09-1.15, p = 0.080). CHSSI was 3.6% pre-intervention vs 1.7% post-intervention (change in intercept RR 0.20, 95% CI 0.05-0.72, p = 0.014). CHSSI was decreased after exclusion of the transition month (June, 2025) but this was no longer statistically significant. ITS estimates for sternal outcomes were directionally consistent but did not reach significance. Photodisinfection achieved higher compliance than mupirocin and was associated with significant CHSSI reduction that reached significance in the primary analysis but was dependent on the partial-implementation month of June 2025.

title: Cardioprotective Effects of Xin-Shu-Ning Tablets against Myocardial Ischemia: Involvement of Protein Kinase B-Related Signaling in Apoptosis and Pyroptosis.
authorString: Liu Y, Liu X, Gu Y, Xu F, Chen Y, Su W, Ding S, Qian C, Rong W.
abstractText: Xin-Shu-Ning Tablets (XSNT) are traditionally used to promote blood circulation and resolve blood stasis, including for coronary heart disease-associated angina. Their cardioprotective mechanisms and bioactive constituents remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the cardioprotection of XSNT against myocardial ischemia and to investigate its underlying mechanisms and candidate bioactive constituents. XSNT was evaluated in myocardial infarction (MI) mice using echocardiography, biochemical assays, histopathology, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence. Proteomics and prior network pharmacology guided PI3K/AKT analysis. H9c2 cells underwent 8 h of oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD), with MK-2206 used to assess AKT involvement. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, cellular thermal shift assays, and cellular experiments were used to evaluate the candidates. XSNT improved cardiac function and reduced myocardial injury in MI mice. Reduced TUNEL staining and changes in Bcl-2/Bax and cleaved caspase-3 supported attenuation of apoptosis, while reductions in inflammasome- and GSDMD-related proteins indicated decreased pyroptosis-related signaling. These effects accompanied increased AKT phosphorylation and reduced NF-κB activation. XSNT produced similar responses in OGD-challenged H9c2 cells, and MK-2206 partially attenuated these effects. Puerarin showed a potential interaction with AKT and reproduced some cellular effects of XSNT, which were also attenuated by MK-2206. XSNT attenuated myocardial injury and distinct apoptosis- and pyroptosis-related responses, with pharmacological evidence supporting AKT involvement. Puerarin represents a candidate bioactive constituent. This study has several limitations, including the unclear cellular sources of myocardial pyroptosis-related signals, the lack of genetic validation of AKT involvement, and the need for further confirmation in primary cardiomyocytes.

title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Decrease the Rate of Rupture, Cardiac Events, and Death in Patients with Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
authorString: Go CC, Alcantara ACM, Annie F, Drabish K, Eslami MH.
abstractText:
Objective

Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a degenerative condition involving several processes including inflammation, matrix remodeling, disruptions of vascular smooth muscle cells, and thrombus formation all leading to progressive dilatation of the aorta and eventual rupture. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) are now considered part of the frontline therapeutic options to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus and have also been validated as having compelling anti-inflammatory and cardiovascular protective properties. Data is limited on the impact of GLP-1RA on outcomes of patients with AAA. The aim of this study is to examine the association and possible impact of GLP-1RA on patients with AAA.

Methods

Data was sourced from the TriNetX research network, encompassing 123 health care organizations. Utilizing ICD-10 and CPT codes, we identified patients with AAA who received abdominal imaging every six months. Group 1 was comprised of patients who were treated with GLP-1RA while Group 2 patients were not. Propensity-score-matching (PSM) was used in a 1:1 fashion using age, sex, diabetes, metformin use, hypertension, cardiac disease, tobacco use, chronic kidney disease, and pulmonary disease as covariates. Primary outcomes were aneurysm rupture or repair. Secondary outcomes include mortality and major adverse cardiac events (MACE; myocardial infarction, stroke, and heart failure). Standard statistical methods were used as appropriate.

Results

We identified 412,490 patients with diagnosis of AAA who were undergoing 6-month surveillance between June 1, 2010 and April 16, 2024. After PSM, the GLP-1RA group (N=13,722) underwent fewer elective repairs at each timepoint (1.5% vs 2.3% at 2 years, 2.1% vs 3.0% at 5 years, P<.01) and had significantly fewer ruptures at two years (1.1% vs 1.8%, P<.01) and five years (1.6% vs 2.4%, P<.01) when compared to Group 2 (N=13,722). Group 1 also experienced significantly fewer MACE and all-cause mortality at two and five years. On multivariate analysis, GLP-1RA significantly reduced the risk of undergoing elective repair (HR 0.757, 95% CI [0.636-0.902], P<.01), rupture (HR 0.538, 95% CI [0.418-0.691], P<.01), all-cause mortality (HR 0.474, 95% CI [0.439-0.511], P<.001), and MACE (HR 0.825, 95% CI [0.794-0.857], P<.01) at 5 years.

Conclusions

The use of GLP-1RA in patients with AAA is associated with fewer ruptures, elective repairs, and improved rates of MACE and death. A prospective analysis may further elucidate if GLP-1RA should be prescribed to reduce the rate of aneurysm growth.

title: Global and Segmental Myocardial Strain in Sarcoidosis: Associations With Cardiac Involvement and Clinical Impairment.
authorString: Özer PK, Yavuz ML, Altan G, Gövdeli EA, Dik SA, Işık EG, Dursun M, Umman B, Okumuş G, Bingöl Z.
abstractText: Cardiac involvement is a major determinant of morbidity and mortality in sarcoidosis and may remain clinically silent despite normal conventional cardiac evaluation. Advanced imaging modalities, particularly speckle-tracking echocardiography (STE), may detect subclinical myocardial dysfunction before overt clinical manifestations. This study aimed to evaluate global and segmental myocardial strain patterns in patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis and to investigate their associations with cardiac involvement, NT-proBNP levels, and functional capacity. This observational study included 123 patients with histologically confirmed pulmonary sarcoidosis and 51 controls. According to the 2024 American Heart Association diagnostic probability framework, 25 patients were classified as having highly probable or probable cardiac sarcoidosis (CS+), whereas 98 were classified as possible/low probability (CS-). All participants underwent conventional echocardiography and STE with assessment of left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LV-GLS), right ventricular global longitudinal strain (RV-GLS), right ventricular free-wall strain (RV-FWS), and LV segmental strain. Multivariable linear regression analyses were performed to assess the associations of global strain parameters with log-transformed NT-proBNP and 6-minute walk distance (6MWD), adjusting for age, sex, body mass index, hypertension, and diabetes mellitus. LV-GLS was progressively impaired across controls, CS-, and CS+ patients (-19.02±2.03%, -16.96±3.32%, and -13.17±4.08%, respectively; p<0.001). RV-GLS and RV-FWS were also significantly impaired in CS+ patients (p=0.004 and p=0.035, respectively). Segmental analysis demonstrated predominant impairment of basal and mid-ventricular segments, particularly the inferoseptal and inferior regions. NT-proBNP levels increased across the groups (49 [34-65], 100 [70-153], and 170 [114-713] pg/mL, respectively; p<0.001). After multivariable adjustment, LV-GLS (β=0.287, p=0.001), RV-GLS (β=0.231, p=0.010), and RV-FWS (β=0.210, p=0.020) were independently associated with log-transformed NT-proBNP. LV-GLS was also independently associated with 6MWD (β=-0.262, p=0.003), whereas RV-GLS and RV-FWS were not. Myocardial deformation is impaired in pulmonary sarcoidosis, with the greatest abnormalities observed in patients with cardiac involvement. LV-GLS showed independent associations with both NT-proBNP and functional capacity, while segmental strain analysis revealed a characteristic basal and mid-ventricular pattern of myocardial dysfunction. STE may provide useful complementary information for the assessment of myocardial involvement and clinical severity in patients with sarcoidosis.

title: Inhibition of neutrophil extracellular trap formation ameliorates astrocyte pyroptosis via CUL7-dependent NLRP3 ubiquitination in mice with sepsis-associated encephalopathy.
authorString: Sun Y, Cheng J, Chen X, Wu H, Xiao Z.
abstractText: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) encompasses acute brain dysfunction during sepsis and may be followed by persistent cognitive impairment among survivors. Although neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) have been implicated in sepsis-related organ injury, their role in astrocyte fate determination and neuroinflammation during SAE remains poorly defined. Here, using a cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) model, we demonstrate that NETs accumulate in both the circulation and hippocampus following sepsis. Pharmacological inhibition or degradation of NETs markedly alleviated blood-brain barrier disruption, neuroinflammation, neuronal death, and acute neurobehavioral abnormalities. Mechanistically, NET accumulation was associated with enhanced astrocyte pyroptosis via activation of the NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3)-caspase-1-gasdermin D (GSDMD) pathway. Activation of NLRP3 abolished the neuroprotective effects conferred by NET inhibition. Transcriptomic analysis of human hippocampal tissues identified cullin 7 (CUL7) as a sepsis-associated candidate, and subsequent experiments showed that its expression was restored following NET inhibition. CUL7 physically interacted with NLRP3, enhanced its ubiquitination, and reduced its protein stability, thereby restraining astrocyte pyroptosis. Notably, CUL7 overexpression improved acute neurobehavioral outcomes, preserved blood-brain barrier integrity, and attenuated neuroinflammation in septic mice. Collectively, our findings identify a previously unrecognized NETs-CUL7-NLRP3 axis that governs astrocyte pyroptosis and contributes to the pathogenesis of SAE, highlighting CUL7 as a potential therapeutic target.

title: Early Sudden Cardiac Death Risk in Heart Failure: Time to Rethink Primary Prevention?
authorString: Buter J, DeVore A, Januzzi JL, Khan MS, Lala A, Metra M.
abstractText: Despite advances in drug and device-based therapies, patients with heart failure (HF) face a substantial risk for mortality. Sudden cardiac death (SCD) accounts for up to half of all deaths in patients with HF and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), with a 6- to 9-fold higher risk compared with the general population. Recent data demonstrate that the risk for arrhythmic events cluster disproportionately more frequently within the first ∼6 months following the diagnosis of HFrEF despite the initiation of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT). This period is characterized by electrical instability, neurohormonal activation, and incomplete reverse remodeling; this is exacerbated by suboptimal exposure to GDMT. While temporal analyses suggest an overall decline in SCD rates in patients with chronic HFrEF, a persistent residual SCD risk that is clinically meaningful remains. While pharmacologic therapies reduce the risk for SCD to varying degrees, structural recovery often lags, creating a vulnerable phase during GDMT up-titration. Current guidelines mandate a waiting period of at least 3-6 months prior to implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) implantation to allow for potential ventricular recovery while GDMT is optimized. Moreover, the indication for primary prevention ICD implantation itself is being actively re-evaluated in the contemporary GDMT era. Yet this interval also exposes patients to an early arrhythmic risk, contributing to clinical apprehension. Wearable cardioverter defibrillators (WCD) may provide a noninvasive strategy to mitigate transient early SCD risk during guideline-mandated waiting periods. WCD platforms have demonstrated reliable arrhythmia detection and defibrillation capability, with high first-shock conversion rates and wear-time adherence in large-scale studies performed in clinical practice. WCDs enable continuous rhythm surveillance, which may support individualized decision-making regarding the timing of a permanent ICD implantation. This review synthesizes the contemporary burden and mechanisms of SCD in HFrEF and how approaches to primary prevention have evolved including an appraisal of the impact of GDMT on arrhythmic risk, current guideline recommendations, and examining the potential role of WCD therapy for protection during early phase vulnerability in these patients.

title: Disulfidptosis: Current View of Understanding the Novel Pattern of Regulatory Cell Death.
authorString: Xing K, Li X, Li T, Dong S, Zhu H, Yan M, Yu S, He H.

journal.title: The international journal of biochemistry & cell biology

abstractText: Regulated cell death (RCD) is intimately linked to the onset, progression, and therapeutic outcomes of diseases. Disulfidptosis represents a newly identified form of RCD that is mechanistically distinct from conventional modalities such as apoptosis, pyroptosis, ferroptosis, and cuproptosis. This novel mechanism is driven by solute carrier family 7 member 11 (SLC7A11)-mediated cystine uptake and concomitant reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH) depletion, which together provoke disulfide stress and collapse of the actin cytoskeleton and lamellipodia. Exploiting this vulnerability holds considerable therapeutic promise for cancers characterized by metabolically fragile and for oxidative stress-related disorders. In this review, we summarize the core mechanisms underlying disulfidptosis, with emphasis on SLC7A11-dependent cystine transport, NADPH homeostasis, disulfide stress, and cytoskeletal collapse. We further distinguish experimentally validated regulators from disulfidptosis-related gene (DRG) signatures derived from bioinformatic analyses, and outline three categories of therapeutic strategies. Beyond oncology, we discuss the emerging relevance of disulfidptosis across degenerative, cardiovascular, metabolic, and genetic diseases and conclude with an outlook on future research directions and unresolved challenges in disulfidptosis.

title: Early Cardiac Dysfunction in Pediatric Becker Muscular Dystrophy: A Prospective Cross-sectional Echocardiographic Study.
authorString: Liu J, Shao S, Cai X, Zhang L, Cui Y, Zhou K, Hua Y, Wang C.

journal.title: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography

abstractText:
Background

Becker muscular dystrophy (BMD) is an X-linked disorder characterized by progressive muscle weakness and cardiac involvement, with cardiomyopathy being the leading cause of mortality. While cardiac dysfunction in adult BMD patients is well documented, the early cardiac phenotype in pediatric populations remains poorly understood. This prospective cross-sectional study aimed to characterize age-stratified differences in cardiac function among children with BMD, children with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), and healthy controls.

Methods

This prospective cross-sectional study included male children aged 3-18 years who were enrolled from June 2020 to December 2023 and met strict inclusion criteria: genetically confirmed BMD or DMD diagnosis, no prior cardiac medications, and absence of comorbid conditions affecting cardiac function. Participants were stratified into three age-matched groups: 3 to under 7 years (youngest group), 7 to under 10 years (middle group), and 10 to under 18 years (oldest group), with comparable mean ages across BMD, DMD, and healthy controls within each age stratum. Comprehensive echocardiographic assessments were performed, including conventional parameters, tissue Doppler imaging, and speckle-tracking echocardiography. Statistical comparisons were made between groups within each age range.

Result

The study comprised 86 BMD patients, 86 DMD patients, and 74 controls across three age groups. After normality testing and Bonferroni-corrected post hoc comparisons, BMD patients showed early left ventricular involvement, including lower LVEF (60.54±8.09% vs 65.56±3.04%, p<0.01) and GLS (18.06±2.10 vs 20.66±1.42, p<0.01) than healthy controls from the Younger group onward. Right ventricular enlargement (RV GLS 22.99±3.26 vs 25.58±2.37, p<0.01) and reduced FAC (40.35±6.01% vs 47.8±17.08%, p<0.01) were also evident in BMD, with age-dependent RV strain abnormalities. Compared with DMD, BMD showed larger LVEDV across age groups and relatively preserved GCS, whereas GLS abnormalities (18.06±2.10 vs 20.66±1.42, p<0.01) were still present compared with healthy controls. Left atrial reservoir/conduit indices were better preserved in BMD than DMD in the Older group. In a short-term longitudinal subsample (16 BMD and 19 DMD patients; mean follow-up ∼0.9 years), BMD patients showed a modest decline in LVEF (annualized change 2.01%/year, P = 0.050), while LV-GLS remained stable in both groups.

Conclusion

Pediatric BMD patients exhibit subclinical, age-associated cardiac dysfunction detectable across pediatric age groups. Because abnormalities in LVEF, LV GLS, RV FAC, and RV GLS were already present in the youngest group, the findings support early and regular cardiac surveillance incorporating advanced echocardiographic techniques from preschool age. Longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether these subclinical differences predict clinically overt cardiomyopathy or treatment response.

title: Educational inequalities in mortality after age 65 vary across birth cohorts in Spain.
authorString: Álamo-Junquera D, Subirana I, Marrugat J, Camps-Vilaró A, Vilaplana-Carnerero C, Tor-Roca A, Martínez-Soto A, Grau M.
abstractText: To assess educational inequalities in mortality after age 65 and examine differences across birth cohorts (1920-1939 and 1940-1959) using relative (mortality risk) and absolute (survival beyond age 65) measures. We analysed data from the population-based Girona Heart Registry (REGICOR) cohort (Spain; 1995-2019), including individuals aged ≥65 years or reaching age 65 during follow-up. Educational attainment was classified as primary, secondary, or higher. Relative inequalities in mortality were estimated using Cox regression models. Absolute inequalities were assessed through excess survival at age 65 (ES65), defined as the difference between observed and expected survival at age 65. Models were adjusted for sex, calendar period, birth cohort, and education-by-cohort interaction. Among 6006 participants (52% women; median follow-up: 9 years), significant education-by-cohort interactions were observed. In the 1920-1939 cohort, secondary (Hazard Ratio 0.77; 95% confidence interval 0.65, 0.90) and higher education (0.76; 0.65, 0.91) were associated with lower mortality than primary education. Corresponding gains in ES65 were 0.78 (0.28, 1.29) and 0.97 years (0.35, 1.60), respectively. No associations were observed in the 1940-1959 cohort. Educational inequalities in mortality after age 65 were present only in the older cohort. Relative and absolute measures provide complementary perspectives on inequalities in later life.

title: Atrial fibrillation recurrence pattern and subsequent heart failure hospitalization after ablation in left ventricular systolic dysfunction: A time-dependent analysis.
authorString: Okada M, Tanaka N, Tanaka K, Hirao Y, Iwasa K, Watanabe H, Koyama Y, Iwanaga Y, Okamura A, Iwakura K, Inoue K, Sakata Y.
abstractText: Catheter ablation improves outcomes in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction, but the prognostic significance of postablation recurrence pattern and its evolution remains unclear. We investigated whether evolving postablation recurrence pattern was associated with subsequent heart failure (HF) hospitalization. This retrospective single-center study included 381 of 5535 consecutive patients who underwent first-time AF ablation between 2012 and 2024 and had baseline left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) <50%. Recurrence was defined as any atrial tachyarrhythmia lasting >30 s beyond the 3-month blanking period and classified as paroxysmal or persistent (lasting >7 days). Recurrence pattern was modeled as a time-dependent variable and updated upon documentation of paroxysmal or persistent recurrence during follow-up. During a median follow-up of 49 months, 140 patients experienced recurrence (71 paroxysmal only and 69 persistent, including 21 who progressed from paroxysmal to persistent recurrence) and 61 experienced HF hospitalization. In a multivariable time-dependent Cox model adjusted for age, sex, baseline LVEF, prior myocardial infarction, prior HF hospitalization, and baseline AF type, both paroxysmal recurrence [hazard ratio (HR), 2.38; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.15-4.90; p = 0.019] and persistent recurrence (HR, 5.45; 95% CI, 2.59-11.46; p < 0.001) were associated with HF hospitalization compared with no recurrence. Persistent recurrence was also associated with a higher risk than paroxysmal recurrence (HR, 2.29; 95% CI, 1.00-5.25; p = 0.049). Time-updated assessment of postablation AF recurrence pattern revealed differential risks of subsequent HF hospitalization among patients with LV systolic dysfunction. Both paroxysmal and persistent recurrence were associated with HF hospitalization, with persistent recurrence representing a particularly high-risk state that may warrant closer HF surveillance and reassessment of rhythm-control strategies.

title: Stigmasterol Ameliorates Pulmonary Hypertension by Suppressing the CCL5/CCR5 Signaling Pathway: Taurocholic Acid as a Downstream Mediator.
authorString: Tang Y, Shi Y, Wang M, Cai S, Suo Y, Lu X, Wang J, Lu X, Chen M, Zhang H.
abstractText: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a devastating disease characterized by irreversible pulmonary vascular remodeling (PVR), ultimately culminating in right ventricular failure and death. Although previous studies have demonstrated that stigmasterol (STG) reduces cholesterol levels and prevents cardiovascular diseases, its potential role in PH remains unknown. In this study, we investigated the therapeutic effects of STG on SU5416/hypoxia (Su/Hx)-induced PH in mice and elucidated the underlying molecular mechanisms. Through bioinformatics analysis and network pharmacology, we identified STG as a promising herbal compound for PH treatment. Both in vitro and in vivo experiments validated that STG ameliorates platelet-derived growth factor-BB (PDGF-BB)-induced proliferation and migration of pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs), as well as PVR and right ventricular hypertrophy (RVH). Molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, MM-PBSA calculation, and microscale thermophoresis (MST) were used to validate direct STG-CCL5 binding. Functional rescue experiments with taurocholic acid (TCA) were also performed. Molecular docking, MD simulation, and MST revealed spontaneous direct binding between CCL5 and STG, with an MST-derived KD of 4.72 μM. While CCL5 promoted PDGF-BB-induced PASMC proliferation and migration, CCR5 inhibition counteracted these effects. STG ameliorated PASMC proliferation and migration by modulating CCL5. Furthermore, metabolomics and mass spectrometry analyses showed decreased taurocholic acid levels in lung tissues of CCR5-knockout (CCR5-/-) mice in the Su/Hx model. TCA reversed the protective effects of STG on PASMC proliferation and migration, supporting TCA as a downstream functional mediator. In conclusion, our study demonstrates that STG ameliorates Su/Hx-induced PH by modulating the CCL5/CCR5 signaling pathway, with taurocholic acid acting as a downstream mediator. Further investigations are warranted to explore the clinical applicability of STG-based therapies for PH patients.

title: Semaglutide versus other GLP-1 RAs and cardiovascular risk in obesity-related cancer survivors.
authorString: Abdelgadir O, Hernández-Pérez JG, Hussain MR, Mendoza K, Mian RK, Albayyaa M, Hughes A, Almandoz JP, Cowell LG, Messiah SE, Lopez DS.
abstractText: Obesity-related cancer (ORCa) survivors are a unique population often excluded from landmark GLP-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) trials. Given their cardiovascular risks, we investigated whether semaglutide initiation, compared with other GLP-1 RA, was associated with modified 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) among ORCa survivors with type 2 diabetes (T2D). We emulated a target trial using PCORnet-UTSW electronic health records (2016-2025). Adults with ORCa and T2D initiating semaglutide versus other GLP-1 RA were included. The primary outcome was modified 3-point MACE (myocardial infarction, stroke, or all-cause mortality). Cumulative incidence risk (CIR), risk difference (RD), and hazard ratio (HR) were estimated in 1:1 propensity score-matched cohort. Among 918 matched patients (semaglutide, n = 459; other GLP-1 RA, n = 459), 124 modified 3-point MACE occurred. The 5-year CIR% was 17.6 (95% CI, 12.3-22.9) for semaglutide and 26.6 (95% CI, 20.7-32.6) for other GLP-1 RA. Semaglutide was associated with lower modified 3-point MACE risk (RD%, -7.41 [95% CI, -11.83 to - 2.98];HR, 0.65 [95% CI, 0.44-0.94]) than other GLP-1 RA. Findings were largely consistent across high-risk subgroups. Semaglutide was associated with a lower modified 3-point MACE risk than other GLP-1 RA. These findings suggest potential heterogeneity in cardioprotective effects and warrant confirmation.

title: Long-term evaluation of the effectiveness and safety of autologous haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation for systemic sclerosis (NISSC1-LTE): a cohort study.
authorString: Henes J, Oliveira MC, Labopin M, Badoglio M, Scherer HU, Del Papa N, Daikeler T, Schmalzing M, Schroers R, Martin T, Pugnet G, Marijt EWA, Espinosa G, Rovira M, Greco R, Alexander T, Onida F, Marjanovic Z, Farge D, Autoimmune Disease Working Party of the European Society for Blood and Marrow Transplantation.
abstractText: Systemic sclerosis is a rare and heterogeneous chronic autoimmune disease. It has the highest mortality of the rheumatic diseases and few treatment options exist. Autologous haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation (HSCT) is an effective and established therapeutic option in selected patients with early severe systemic sclerosis. This study aimed to evaluate the long-term safety and effectiveness of autologous HSCT in patients with systemic sclerosis in real-life clinical practice. This cohort study (NISSC1-LTE) followed up patients with systemic sclerosis included in the prospective European Society for Blood and Marrow Transplantation NISSC1 study who had undergone their first autologous HSCT for severe progressive systemic sclerosis. Follow-up data were collected from 13 participating centres in France, Germany, Netherlands, Italy, Spain, Switzerland, and Brazil. Participating centres completed a yearly case report form for each patient alive after 2 years and up to 10 years after autologous HSCT. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival, defined as survival from baseline without evidence of systemic sclerosis progression. Late complications after autologous HSCT, including malignancies, secondary autoimmune diseases, infections, and major adverse cardiovascular events were also analysed. People with lived experience of systemic sclerosis were involved in the design and conduct of this study. The NISSC1 study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02516124) and is complete. All 80 patients with systemic sclerosis who had an autologous HSCT between Dec 4, 2012, and Jan 19, 2016, were included in this long-term extension study. 12 patients were lost to follow-up, including five patients with a follow-up less than 5 years. Median age at autologous HSCT was 43 years (IQR 33-51), 57 (71%) of 80 patients were female, 23 (29%) were male, and median follow-up was 9·2 years (IQR 8·9-9·6) after autologous HSCT. Progression-free survival was 81% (95% CI 71-88) at 2 years, 72% (61-81) at 5 years, and 60% (47-71) at 10 years. 18 patients died during the study; causes of death were autologous HSCT-related in five (6%) of 80 patients, disease progression in nine (11%) patients, post-autologous HSCT malignancy in two (3%) patients, and late serious infection in two (3%) patients. 34 (43%) of 80 patients maintained remission without immunosuppressive treatment over 10 years. This study provides long-term follow-up data after autologous HSCT in patients with systemic sclerosis allowing robust assessment of response rate, late complications, and sustained treatment benefit. The extended timeframe might serve as an important comparator for all upcoming, cellular treatment options. None.

title: Drivers of Increased Resource Utilization After Removal of Donation Service Area in Lung Transplant.
authorString: Kalra A, Fan L, Feng SN, Liu W, Ruck JM, Zhou AL, Akbar AF, Shou BL, Casillan AJ, Agbor-Enoh S, Merlo CA, Bush EL.
abstractText: The removal of donation service area (DSA)-based allocation increased lung transplants (LTs) and transplant hospitalization costs nationally. Regional differences in resource utilization for LT recipients have been identified; however, the specific clinical drivers remain unclear. These findings may inform evaluation of the current Composite Allocation Score system. We studied adult (≥18 y) LT recipients in the National Inpatient Sample in regions with previously increased resource utilization. Cochrane-Armitage was used to evaluate trends in hospital procedures in the DSA (8/2015-10/2017) versus non-DSA (12/2017-2/2020) eras. Multivariable generalized linear regression identified recipient factors associated with hospitalization costs and length of stay. We identified 4870 DSA era and 4045 non-DSA era LT recipients. Over our study period time, we observed increases in the percentage of recipients requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) (14%-36%), mechanical ventilation <24 h (5%-10%), and dialysis (4%-5%; all P ≤ 0.01), while fewer recipients required tracheostomy (38%-26% P = 0.007). After adjustment, length of stay was significantly longer among recipients with prolonged mechanical ventilation (+25 d, 95% CI = 17-33, P < 0.001), tracheostomy (+17 d, 95% CI = 12-21, P < 0.001), ECMO (+8 d, 95% CI = 3-13, P = 0.003), bilateral LT (relative to single LT, +4 d, 95% CI = 1-7, P = 0.048), and higher Charlson Comorbidity Index (+2 d, 95% CI = 1-4, P < 0.001). Hospitalization costs were significantly higher among recipients with prolonged mechanical ventilation (+$152,992, 95% CI = $100,510-$205,473), dialysis (+$119,614, 95% CI = $27,305-$211,923), ECMO (+$113,690, 95% CI = $72,423-$154,957), tracheostomy (+$104,864, 95% CI = $78,887-$130,841), bilateral LT (+$28,829, 95% CI = $6560-$51,098), and higher Charlson Comorbidity Index (+$13,729, 95% CI = $4155-$23,304; all P ≤ 0.01). Factors associated with increased resource utilization post-DSA included mechanical ventilation, dialysis, and tracheostomy during hospitalization, ECMO, bilateral LT, and comorbidities.

title: Difenoconazole-based fungicide formulations interfere with the embryogenesis of the two aquatic vertebrate organisms Xenopus laevis and Danio rerio.
authorString: Flach H, Kaminski F, Dietmann P, Köhler J, Weidinger G, Kühl SJ.
abstractText: Amphibians are among the most threatened vertebrate groups worldwide, with more than 40% of amphibian species currently at risk. Besides habitat loss, pesticide exposure is considered a major driver of this decline. While herbicides such as glyphosate have been widely studied, the effects of fungicides - particularly triazoles - remain underexplored. Difenoconazole (DFZ) is one of the most commonly used triazole fungicides, characterized by environmental persistence. However, its impact on amphibian and fish embryonic development has not been systematically investigated. This study examined lethal and sublethal effects of two DFZ-containing formulations - Difcor® (Difcor; professional use) and COMPO® Duaxo Universal Pilz-frei (Compo; non-professional use) - on Xenopus laevis embryos. Embryos were exposed to environmentally relevant (0.01-1 mg a.i./L) and higher concentrations (10-100 mg a.i./L) for 14 days. Endpoints included mortality, morphology, cardiac and neural development, oxidative stress, gene expression, cell proliferation, and apoptosis. Both formulations caused concentration-dependent mortality with LC50 values of 12.34 mg a.i./L (Difcor) and 16.28 mg a.i./L (Compo). Sublethal effects occurred from 0.01 mg a.i./L, including reduced body length, smaller head and eye areas, pericardial edema, and altered heart rate and mobility. Difcor additionally impaired neural and cardiac development, reduced mhcα expression, and increased proliferation and apoptosis. Complementary analyses with the formulation Difcor in Danio rerio embryos confirmed concentration-dependent mortality and revealed sublethal morphological changes such as peracardial edema. Overall, DFZ-containing formulations exert pronounced lethal and sublethal effects in amphibian and fish embryos, highlighting the need to include amphibians and fish more systematically in the environmental risk assessment of triazole fungicides.

title: Dynamic Early Postreperfusion Physiology Is Associated With Organ Recovery After Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation.
authorString: Gaisendrees C, Jaeger D, Djordjevic I, Walter S, Schlachtenberger G.

journal.title: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)

abstractText: Prognostication after extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) predominantly relies on characteristics available before or at initiation of extracorporeal support. We investigated whether the early metabolic response to extracorporeal reperfusion provides complementary information on subsequent recovery. We retrospectively analyzed 91 patients with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest treated with ECPR. Lactate was assessed before and 12 h after extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) initiation. Outcomes included in-hospital mortality, successful ECMO weaning, cerebral edema/hypoxic brain injury, and favorable neurological survival. Associations were adjusted for low-flow duration. Twelve hour lactate was lower in survivors than nonsurvivors (5.45 vs. 9.04 mmol/L; p = 0.002), whereas prereperfusion lactate did not differ.
