In paired measurements (n = 38), mortality discrimination increased from an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.47 before reperfusion to 0.80 at 12 h. Each 5 mmol/L higher 12 h lactate was associated with mortality (odds ratio [OR] = 2.73), lower odds of ECMO weaning (OR = 0.44), and cerebral edema/hypoxic injury (OR = 2.07) after low-flow adjustment. Early metabolic response after extracorporeal reperfusion was associated with survival and both circulatory and cerebral recovery. Dynamic post-reperfusion physiology may provide complementary information beyond static pre-reperfusion assessment.

title: Whole-Exome Sequencing Identifies a Rare CSRP3 Variant Associated With Familial Brugada Syndrome in a Lebanese Family.
authorString: Bashir Z, Kadhi A, Ballout J, Samara B, Khoury M, Nemer G, Refaat M.
abstractText: Brugada syndrome (BrS) is an inherited arrhythmia associated with an increased risk of sudden cardiac death. Although traditionally regarded as a primary cardiac channelopathy, pathogenic variants in SCN5A account for only 20%-30% of clinically diagnosed cases, leaving most patients genetically unresolved. Emerging evidence suggests that structural cardiac genes may also contribute to BrS susceptibility. We investigated the genetic basis of BrS in a consanguineous Lebanese family with three affected brothers. Whole-exome sequencing was performed in all affected individuals, followed by variant calling, annotation, and phenotype-driven prioritization using Franklin (Genoox). Candidate variants were evaluated according to allele frequency, inheritance model, segregation, and ACMG/AMP classification. Evolutionary conservation, AlphaMissense prediction, protein domain annotation, and structural modeling were performed to assess the potential functional impact of the prioritized variant. Whole-exome sequencing identified a rare homozygous CSRP3 missense variant (NM_003476.5:c.56 A > G; p.His19Arg) shared by all three affected siblings. Following exome-wide filtering under a recessive inheritance model, CSRP3 represented the only rare homozygous coding variant, while no pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were identified in established Brugada syndrome-associated genes. The variant was absent from public population databases and an internal cohort of Lebanese exomes. His19 was highly conserved across vertebrate species, AlphaMissense classified the variant as likely pathogenic (score = 0.942), and structural modeling predicted alterations within the N-terminal LIM domain that may affect protein stability and local residue interactions. Our findings nominate CSRP3 as a candidate susceptibility gene for Brugada syndrome and support the emerging role of structural cardiac genes in inherited arrhythmia syndromes. Although functional validation is required to establish causality, this study highlights the value of whole-exome sequencing in consanguineous and underrepresented populations for identifying rare candidate variants contributing to BrS susceptibility.

title: Validation of a Four-Extrastimulus Ventricular Stimulation Protocol for Arrhythmic Risk Stratification in Tetralogy of Fallot.
authorString: Muñoz LC, Peinado RP, Ferrero TG, Diz J, Argos CM, Colunga PM, García AG, Cantador JR, Gómez RM, Ortega CÁ.
abstractText:
Introduction

Risk stratification for sustained ventricular arrhythmias (SVA) in adults with repaired Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) remains challenging. Although programmed ventricular stimulation (PVS) has shown a high negative predictive value, the prognostic performance of a four-extrastimulus PVS protocol-validated in ischemic heart disease-has not been systematically evaluated in congenital heart disease.

Methods and results

We retrospectively included 41 consecutive adults with repaired TOF who underwent EPS using a standardized four-extrastimulus PVS protocol at two right ventricular sites. Inducibility of SVA was assessed. The primary endpoint was the occurrence of clinical SVA during follow-up. Kaplan-Meier analysis and Firth-penalized Cox regression were used to evaluate prognostic performance, and diagnostic accuracy metrics were calculated. Inducibility was observed in 18 patients (44%). During a median follow-up of 1.68 years, SVA occurred exclusively in inducible patients (5/18; 28%), all corresponding to sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia. No non-inducible patient developed SVA. Inducibility was associated with significantly lower SVA-free survival (log-rank p = 0.015) and an increased risk of events (HR 13.6; 95% CI 1.5-1804; p = 0.017) in univariate analysis. The four-extrastimulus protocol demonstrated a sensitivity of 100% and specificity of 64%.

Conclusions

In adults with repaired TOF and risk factors for sudden cardiac death, the four-extrastimulus PVS protocol identified a subgroup at high arrhythmic risk while reliably excluding events in non-inducible individuals. These findings support the potential value of PVS as part of multimodal risk stratification, particularly for identifying patients in whom ICD implantation may be deferred.

title: Association Between Cumulative Social Determinants of Health and Mortality Among Stroke Survivors.
authorString: Yang M, Yuan Q, Hou Y, Zhang B, Chen Y, Zhang Y, Liu C, Fang S, Liu N, Du H.
abstractText: Social determinants of health (SDoH) are well-established contributors to health disparities. Whether cumulative SDoH burden is associated with long-term mortality among stroke survivors remains poorly understood. We extracted data of 1,404 stroke survivors from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999-2018. Cumulative SDoH burden was calculated incorporating eight individual SDoH indicators across multiple domains: employment status, poverty-income ratio (PIR), food security, education level, healthcare access, health insurance, housing status, and marital status. Survey-weighted Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the associations of individual SDoH indicators and cumulative SDoH burden with all-cause, cardiovascular disease (CVD) and non-CVD mortality outcomes. During a median follow-up of 72 months, 604 deaths were documented, including 237 CVD deaths and 367 non-CVD deaths. Among the eight SDoH indicators, being unemployed, having lower PIR and having government insurance only or being uninsured were significantly associated with all-cause mortality. Looking at cause-specific mortality, having lower PIR was significantly associated with CVD mortality, whereas being unemployed was significantly associated with non-CVD mortality. The risk of mortality from all-cause (p for trend <0.001), CVD (p for trend =0.026) and non-CVD (p for trend <0.001) increased with the increasing SDoH burden. In this nationally representative cohort of stroke survivors, increasing cumulative SDoH burden was significantly associated with higher risks of mortality.

title: Characterizing acute ischemia via ECG: A study of severity, extent, and spatial variability in myocardial infarction and non-infarction groups.
authorString: Rodríguez-Carbó J, Mincholé A, Pueyo E.
abstractText: Ischemic heart disease remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide. Its diagnosis largely relies on detecting dynamic changes in the ST segment of the electrocardiogram (ECG). However, alterations in other ECG waves and intervals have also been reported. One factor that is often overlooked is the presence of a prior myocardial infarction and its influence on the myocardial response to a new ischemic event. This study aimed to quantify the magnitude and temporal dynamics of ECG changes during acute myocardial ischemia and to evaluate how a previous infarction modifies these changes. Twelve-lead ECG recordings obtained before and during acute ischemia induced by percutaneous coronary intervention in one of the three major coronary arteries were analyzed. Dynamic heartbeat averages were computed to extract and track features related to ECG depolarization (QRS width, amplitude, and area) and repolarization (T-wave amplitude and area, ST-segment deviation and area, and T-to-QRS amplitude ratio). The results show that, beyond ST-segment deviation, multiple ECG markers evolve over time during coronary artery occlusion. Repolarization features showed earlier and more pronounced alterations than depolarization features, reaching approximately 37-fold and 23-fold changes at 4 minutes of occlusion compared with baseline, respectively. Males showed faster and more sustained ST increases (up to ~47-fold vs ~30-fold in females); older patients had abrupt early ST peaks (~38-fold at ~2 min after occlusion), whereas younger patients exhibited a more gradual increase. Moreover, patients with a prior infarction showed a stronger association between ECG changes and both the extent and severity of ischemia, reaching maximum correlation coefficients of 0.75 for repolarization markers and 0.57 for depolarization markers. Distinct spatial lead patterns were also identified according to the occluded artery and the presence of a prior infarction. In conclusion, acute ischemia induces dynamic changes across multiple ECG markers beyond the ST segment, where repolarization changes precede and exceed depolarization. These responses are modulated by age and sex; furthermore, prior infarction tightens their correlation with ischemic burden and alters spatial lead patterns.

title: "Food is like all we do all day": a qualitative exploration of nutritional challenges and intervention needs among families of early childhood cancer survivors.
authorString: Fry C, Nava-Coulter B, Roberts J, Revette A, Paul MA, Lokko L, Jones E, Fox K, Umaretiya PJ, Kelly CA, Duhaney L, Kenney LB, Zhang FF, Bona K, Aziz-Bose R.

journal.title: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer

abstractText: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of non-malignant death among childhood cancer survivors (CCS). Food insecurity is a known modifiable cardiovascular risk factor; perspectives on nutrition for CCS parents navigating food insecurity and cardiovascular risk factors are needed. We aimed to describe parent-identified priorities regarding nutrition, explore barriers to and facilitators of healthy eating, and elicit preferences on nutrition intervention design in early survivorship. We conducted a single-center qualitative study embedded within a larger survey study. Twenty semi-structured qualitative interviews were conducted with parents of CCS < 1-year from cancer therapy completion in a purposively sampled cohort based on food insecurity status and the presence of cardiovascular risk factors. We conducted thematic analysis to identify how parents define and prioritize healthy eating, what factors drive their food choices, and preferences for nutrition interventions. Four key themes were identified: (1) healthy eating is highly valued in survivorship; (2) achieving nutritional goals is limited by cost, time, and dietary considerations; (3) early survivorship is a period of ongoing, unmet nutrition and resource needs; and (4) interventions should be modular, empowering, and address access barriers. Although nutrition is highly valued, families with and without food insecurity encounter substantial barriers to healthy eating in early survivorship-a pivotal window for nutrition intervention. Families expressed a strong need for multifaceted and modular nutrition interventions that address access barriers and promote empowerment. Our findings may inform the design of future interventions aimed at improving cardiometabolic health and reducing cardiovascular outcome disparities among CCS.

title: The Recovery Room Is Not Needed Following Hand Surgery With Local Anesthesia in the Outpatient Operating Room: A Prospective Study.
authorString: Nieves-Lopez B, Aziz KT, Ardon AE, Murray PM.
abstractText: The use of an outpatient operating room (OPOR) for hand surgery under local anesthesia only has increased due to efficiency and cost-effectiveness. Although prior research supports the safety of OPOR and outcomes equivalent to traditional operating room settings, the necessity of post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) monitoring for these patients remains uncertain. This study evaluated the safety of discharging patients directly home from the OPOR without PACU recovery. A prospective study enrolled 102 patients who underwent carpal tunnel release and/or trigger finger surgery in the OPOR under local anesthesia only. Patients were discharged directly from the OPOR after a single set of postoperative vital signs. Outcomes included adverse events, emergency department (ED) visits, surgical reinterventions, and intraoperative and postoperative complications within 90 days. The mean patient age was 65.2 years (range, 25-94), and 60.8% were female. No intraoperative or postoperative complications, surgical reinterventions, or deaths occurred. Four patients (3.9%) presented to the ED within 90 days; 1 (0.9%) experienced an adverse event due to community-acquired pneumonia. No ED visits were related to a complication of the hand procedure. All patients were hemodynamically and respiratory stable at discharge. Forty-six patients (45.1%) had elevated blood pressure at discharge, 76.1% of whom had known hypertension. Bypassing PACU after OPOR hand surgery under local anesthesia only is safe. Direct discharge from the OPOR may reduce health care resource utilization, decrease costs associated with PACU recovery, and improve procedural efficiency without compromising patient safety.

title: Serum proteomic correlates of arts and cultural engagement and their associations with health outcomes: cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses in the UK Household Longitudinal Study.
authorString: Qin P, Finn S, Fancourt D.
abstractText: Understanding of the biological mechanisms underpinning associations between arts and cultural engagement (ACEng) and health outcomes remains embryonic. This study aimed to characterize serum proteomic signatures of ACEng, investigate the relationships between ACEng and health conditions, and undertake preliminary analyses to explore whether these proteins may mediate the associations. We analysed prospective cohort data from 6,180 participants in the UK Household Longitudinal Study who had cardiometabolic protein data and/or neurology protein data. Two indices of arts engagement were generated by summing metrics of frequency and diversity of arts participation, cultural attendance, and library, archives, museum, and heritage visits. Geater ACEng was found to be consistently associated across models with differences in 17 proteins after adjusting for sociodemographic confounders and multiple testing. The enriched biological pathways identified involved cell proliferation, receptor-mediated signaling, immune regulation and inflammatory signaling. We then explored longitudinal associations between ACEng and incidence of 15 chronic diseases. ACEng was consistently associated with lower prospective risk of asthma, COPD, CVD, IHD, stroke, arthritis, hyperthyroidism, hypertension, diabetes, clinical depression, and dementia (but not with cancer, heart failure, liver disease or epilepsy). In exploratory analyses, the identified significant proteins mediated 15.95-37.70% of the associations between ACEng and cardiometabolic and respiratory diseases, arthritis, and depression, although as ACEng and proteins were measured near contemporaneously, this does not establish a causal protein pathway. Instead, these findings present, for the first time, proteomic signatures of ACEng and provide preliminary data to help generate hypotheses about potential mediation pathways to health conditions. Future longitudinal research is encouraged to test whether proteins provide causal mechanistic pathways linking ACEng to human health and disease.

title: Trends and disparity of chronic lower respiratory disease and hypertension: A CDC WONDER database analysis 1999-2023.
authorString: Aamir MB, Fatima N, Shahbaz AK, Noor N, Haq FIU, Ahmed T, Chaudry HZ, Ali W, Ali H, Khan F, Mal M.

journal.title: Journal of the National Medical Association

abstractText: In the US, two leading causes of morbidity and mortality are hypertension and chronic lower respiratory disease (CLRD). We aim to analyze the trends of mortality in people with CLRD and hypertension as causes of death in the adult US population. Mortality data from 1999 to 2023 were obtained from the CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death database for U.S. adults aged ≥25 years. ICD-10 codes were used to identify hypertension (I10-I15) and CLRD (J40-J47. In order to determine age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 people. The analyses were stratified according to age groups, sex, race/ethnicity, urbanization status, and geographic region. Between 1999 and 2023, 1433,319 deaths due to chronic lower respiratory disease and hypertension occurred among U.S. adults aged ≥25 years. Overall, the AAMR increased from 9.41 per 100,000 in 1999 to 35.53 in 2023 (AAPC: 5.20; 95% CI: 4.02 - 6.38; p < 0.000001). Mortality increased significantly from 1999 to 2021, followed by a nonsignificant decline through 2023 (APC:4.19; 95% CI:8.95 - 0.82; p = 0.093265). The mean AAMR was higher among males than females (28.72 vs. 21.55). By race/ethnicity, NH Blacks or African American individuals had the highest mean AAMR (29.72), followed by NH White (24.72), NH American Indian or Alaska Native (21.03), Hispanic or Latino (14.02), and NH Asian or Pacific Islander (10.75) individuals. Nonmetropolitan areas had higher AAMR than metropolitan areas (29.02 vs. 22.43). The South had the highest regional mean AAMR (27.67), followed by the Midwest (25.63), West (23.77), and Northeast (18.44). Mean crude mortality rates increased substantially with age, ranging from 1.01 per 100,000 among those aged 35-44 years to 265.35 among those aged ≥85 years. CLRD and hypertension mortality increased substantially, with persistent demographic and geographic disparities, highlighting the need for targeted prevention strategies in high-risk populations.

title: Impact of burst suppression duration on delirium and its diagnostic value in mechanically ventilated ICU patients.
authorString: Tang S, Wang Y, Huang J, Ma Z, Li Q, Wu J, Gao X.

journal.title: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing

abstractText: Intensive care unit (ICU) delirium affects up to 50% of mechanically ventilated patients. This condition is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Although bispectral index (BIS) monitoring is widely used for sedation assessment, its predictive value for delirium remains limited. Burst suppression (BS) is an electroencephalographic pattern reflecting profound cerebral dysfunction. BS has been proposed as a predictor of delirium. However, the quantitative role of burst suppression duration (BSD) in delirium risk stratification has not been established. This prospective observational study enrolled 300 mechanically ventilated adult ICU patients between April 2021 and October 2024 at Harrison International Peace Hospital. Continuous video-electroencephalogram (vEEG) monitoring was performed. BSD was quantified from the vEEG recordings. Delirium was assessed using the Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU (CAM-ICU). Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify independent risk factors. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of BSD. Among 300 patients, 130 (43.3%) developed delirium. The delirium group had significantly longer BSD than the control group (median 81.1 s, IQR 41.5-148.5 vs. 17.2 s, IQR 5.8-32.9; P < 0.001). Multivariate analysis identified BSD (adjusted OR = 1.018, 95% CI 1.012-1.023; P < 0.001), BIS (adjusted OR = 0.964, 95% CI 0.946-0.982; P < 0.001), age (adjusted OR = 1.024, 95% CI 1.002-1.047; P = 0.031), and hypertension (adjusted OR = 1.748, 95% CI 1.002-3.051; P = 0.049) as independent risk factors. ROC analysis demonstrated that BSD achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.871 (95% CI 0.829-0.913). The optimal cutoff of 41.5 s yielded a sensitivity of 80.8% and a specificity of 78.2%. The combination of BSD and BIS improved the AUC to 0.914 (95% CI 0.882-0.946). BSD is an independent risk factor for delirium in mechanically ventilated ICU patients. It demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy as a quantitative biomarker. The combination of BSD and BIS provides superior predictive performance. This combined approach offers a practical quantitative tool for early delirium risk stratification.

title: Highlights of Cardiovascular Disease Prevention Studies Presented at the 2026 European Society of Cardiology Conference.
authorString: Abdul Jabbar AB, Zulfiqar K, Malik SAR, Inam M, Fazal W, Hyder A, Minhas AMK, Slipczuk L, Krittanawong C, Kalra DK, Virani SS.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

This review summarizes key cardiovascular disease prevention studies presented at the 2026 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) Congress, highlighting new evidence in lipid management, cardiovascular risk assessment, blood pressure control, and vaccination.

Recent findings

Several studies addressed persistent gaps in lipid management and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease prevention. STAREE showed that atorvastatin reduced major cardiovascular events in adults aged 70 years and older without established cardiovascular disease, although it did not significantly improve disability-free survival. The SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4 trials showed that plozasiran produced substantial and sustained triglyceride reductions and reduced acute pancreatitis events in patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia. VICTORION-Challenge demonstrated greater LDL-C reduction and target attainment with inclisiran compared with bempedoic acid in high- and very-high-risk patients receiving background statin therapy. In patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, VSA003 substantially lowered LDL-C and several other atherogenic lipoproteins by inhibiting ANGPTL3. Two studies examined imaging-based approaches to preventive therapy: RESPECT2 showed that coronary computed tomography angiography-guided lipid management improved adherence compared with conventional risk-score-based treatment, while CorCal found that coronary artery calcium-guided statin recommendations reduced the number of patients selected for treatment and were associated with greater LDL-C lowering and higher reported adherence, although noninferiority for cardiovascular events was not established. Beyond lipid management, long-term follow-up of the China Rural Hypertension Control Project showed that intensive blood pressure management led by non-physician healthcare providers reduced dementia and cognitive impairment. TIMER demonstrated sustained LDL-C lowering with once-monthly ticalicibart in patients with nonfamilial hypercholesterolemia receiving background statin therapy, while TRANQUILITY demonstrated sustained reductions in high-sensitivity C-reactive protein with the interleukin-6 (IL-6) inhibitor pacibekitug in patients with chronic kidney disease. DAN-RSV demonstrated that RSVpreF vaccination reduced RSV-related respiratory and cardiorespiratory hospitalizations across two seasons. Studies presented at ESC 2026 broadened the evidence base for cardiovascular prevention across pharmacologic therapy, imaging-guided risk assessment, blood pressure management, and vaccination.

title: Pregnancy considerations in women with uncorrected tetralogy of Fallot.
authorString: Bhardwaj A, Balachandran DM, Vasudev I.

journal.title: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics

abstractText: Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) is the most common cyanotic congenital heart disease, accounting for approximately 7-10% of all congenital cardiac malformations. Although early surgical repair has transformed its natural history in high-income settings, with contemporary long-term survival exceeding 90%, uncorrected TOF continues to be encountered in pregnancy, particularly in women from resource-limited regions or those with previously undiagnosed disease. The physiological adaptations of pregnancy, including reduction in systemic vascular resistance, plasma volume expansion, and a 30-50% rise in cardiac output, are poorly tolerated in the presence of a non-restrictive ventricular septal defect and fixed right ventricular outflow tract obstruction, leading to progressive cyanosis, right ventricular strain, and uteroplacental hypoperfusion. Current European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidance classifies unrepaired cyanotic heart disease without Eisenmenger syndrome as mWHO 2.0 class III, while Eisenmenger syndrome is classified as mWHO 2.0 class IV. Contemporary data from the ESC EORP Registry of Pregnancy and Cardiac Disease (ROPAC) report maternal mortality of 0.7% and heart failure in 8.7% of pregnancies with uncorrected congenital heart disease, with markedly worse outcomes in cyanotic subsets. This narrative review synthesizes the pathophysiology, risk stratification, obstetric management, intrapartum anesthetic considerations, comparative outcomes of uncorrected versus corrected disease, and key evidence gaps that continue to constrain care for this population, providing a physiology-driven framework for the pregnancy heart team.

title: Exercise chronotropic inefficiency in patients with heart failure across distinct left ventricular ejection fraction phenotypes.
authorString: Nunes Silva R, Crisci G, Losito M, Serrantoni V, Borghi-Silva A, Arena R, Guazzi M.
abstractText: To characterize the pattern of chronotropic incompetence (CI) response to exercise in patients with heart failure (HF) across distinct phenotypes of the left ventricular ejection fraction and to explore the extent to which heart rate (HR) response should be prioritized as a therapeutic target within personalized HF management strategies. Patients with HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), and healthy controls underwent incremental exercise testing with simultaneous gas exchange and echocardiography assessments. Stroke volume (SV), HR, cardiac output (CO), and arteriovenous oxygen difference [C(a-v)O2] were assessed from rest to peak exercise. Graphical analyses explored relationships amongst determinants of oxygen uptake (V̇O2). Both HF phenotypes exhibited CI and a blunted increase in CO during exercise compared with controls. Peak HR was similarly reduced by 20% in HFpEF and 23% in HFrEF. HFpEF, however, exhibited a steeper HR-VO2 relationship. HFrEF demonstrated a greater compensatory increase in peripheral O2 extraction, with peak C(a-v)O2 73% higher than controls and 21% higher than HFpEF. In contrast, HFpEF showed limited ability to augment C(a-v)O2 and presented the lowest relative peak V̇O2 (-39% vs. controls and -16% vs. HFrEF), despite similar peak V̇O2%pred between HF phenotypes. CI can contribute to exercise intolerance in both HF phenotypes, with distinct compensatory mechanisms. An integrated cardiopulmonary exercise testing-echocardiography approach may support identifying phenotype-specific physiological profiles that might address therapeutic strategies targeting CI, SV reserve, and peripheral O2 utilization to improve functional capacity in HF. Addressing the kinetics of HR slope and ΔHR metrics seems relevant to implement knowledge on the fundamental CI contribution in HF phenotypes.

title: Triglyceride-Glucose Index and Incident Stroke in Elderly Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Prakongyot C, Thohnabutr K, Sopa N, Khumsen N, Chotrattanadachdacho S.
abstractText: The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is a surrogate marker of insulin resistance and has been associated with stroke in general populations. However, evidence regarding its prognostic value for incident stroke in elderly patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remains limited. To evaluate the association between the TyG index and incident stroke in elderly patients with T2DM. A retrospective cohort study conducted at a provincial tertiary care center in Northern Thailand. This study included 1024 patients aged ≥60 years with T2DM. The TyG index was calculated from fasting triglyceride and fasting plasma glucose levels at baseline and categorized into quartiles. The primary outcome was computed tomography-confirmed incident stroke during a 5-year follow-up. Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to estimate hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals, adjusting for age, sex, hypertension, and smoking status. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression. Over a mean follow-up of 4.7 years, 51 patients (5.0%) developed incident stroke. Although higher TyG index quartiles were associated with less favorable metabolic profiles, no significant differences in stroke-free survival were observed across TyG quartiles. In multivariable analyses, the TyG index was not independently associated with incident stroke, whether analyzed as quartiles or as a continuous variable. The TyG index was not associated with incident stroke in elderly patients with T2DM, suggesting limited prognostic utility of the TyG index for stroke risk prediction in this population.

title: Prevalence and prognostic impact of valvular heart disease in transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis.
authorString: Sarrazyn C, Debonnaire P, Claeys M, Graziani F, Meucci MC, Donal E, Regeer M, Pinto FJ, Droogmans S, Van de Veire N, Bertrand P, Sia CH, Ng A, Jurcut R, Adam R, Hirasawa K, Nabeta T, Van De Heyning C, Sturkenboom N, Bax JJ, Ajmone Marsan N.

journal.title: Amyloid : the international journal of experimental and clinical investigation : the official journal of the International Society of Amyloidosis

abstractText:
Background

Significant valvular heart disease (VHD) is associated with adverse prognosis in transthyretin amyloidosis cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM). However, data is limited to isolated VHD. We aimed at evaluating the difference in outcome between isolated and multiple VHD, and particularly with and without aortic stenosis (AS).

Methods

Patients with ATTR-CM were retrospectively included in a multicentric registry. The endpoint was a composite of heart failure hospitalizations and all-cause death.

Results

Of the 694 patients (mean age 75 ± 13 years,74%male), 302(44%) presented with significant VHD. Of these, 98 had VHD including AS (isolated AS in 45%;multiple VHD with AS in 55%), while 204 had VHD without AS (isolated in 64%, multiple VHD in 36%). During a median follow-up of 22(8-38) months, 217(31%) patients reached the endpoint. Significant VHD was associated with worse outcomes than no-VHD (log-rank p < 0.001; HR:3.275; 95%CI (2.472-4.337), remaining significant after adjustment (HR2.006 (1.193-3.047);p = 0.007). Stratification by the presence of AS, and according to isolated or multiple VHD, revealed that isolated significant AS ((HR: 2.462; 95%CI (1.233-4.917); p = 0.011), and multiple VHD including significant AS, had the highest risk for adverse outcomes ((HR: 3.385; 95%CI (1.744-6.573);p < 0.001).

Conclusion

In ATTR-CM, significant VHD is strongly associated with poor prognosis, with the highest risk for adverse events in significant multiple VHD including AS.

title: 17β-Estradiol and Estrogen Receptor α Promote Right Ventricle Angiogenesis in Pulmonary Hypertension via Apelin Signaling.
authorString: Bousseau S, Frump AL, Walts A, Sobrano Fais R, Fisher A, Bharti M, Yakubov B, Provencher S, Breuils Bonnet S, Bonnet S, Lahm T.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Am J Respir Cell Mol Biol
journal.title: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology
journal.isoabbreviation: Am J Respir Cell Mol Biol

abstractText: Right ventricular (RV) failure is the major cause of mortality in pulmonary hypertension (PH). Adaptive angiogenesis and RV endothelial cell (RVEC) function are major modifiers of RV adaptation in PH, but the underlying mechanisms and their regulators remain incompletely understood. RV adaptation in PH is sexually dimorphic, and 17β-estradiol (E2) exerts protective effects on RV cardiomyocytes. Whether E2 modifies angiogenesis and RVEC function in RV failure remains unknown. We hypothesized that E2 and estrogen receptor α (ERα) promote RV angiogenesis and RVEC homeostasis in PH and aimed to identify underlying mechanisms. We assessed E2's angiogenic effects using cultured human cardiac microvascular endothelial cells (hCMVECs), RVECs from PH patients with RV failure, and RVECs from sugen/hypoxia (SuHx) and monocrotaline rat models. In vivo, we evaluated RV capillary density in PH rats treated with E2 or ERα-selective agonist. Apelin signaling was evaluated via apelin receptor (APLNR) blockade and knockdown studies. E2 preserved angiogenesis in male hCMVECs and RV capillary density in male and female SuHx-PH rats. E2 reversed angiogenic alterations in RVECs from SuHx-PH rats via APLNR signaling. In RVECs from RV failure patients, E2 stimulated vascular network formation. In rat and human PH-RVECs, ERα was necessary and sufficient to mediate E2-induced angiogenesis. Activation of ERα with ERα-specific agonist restored RV capillary density in vivo. ERα-mediated angiogenesis required apelin signaling. These data indicate that E2 promotes RV angiogenesis via ERα and apelin signaling and identify a novel ERα-apelin axis in RVECs as a potential therapeutic target to restore RV vascular integrity in PH.

title: Malignant Ventricular Arrhythmias following Pulsed Field Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation: A systematic review of published cases and mechanistic insights.
authorString: Papakonstantinou PE, Charitos D, Fitzpatrick N, O'Brien J, Bolao JIG, Szeplaki G, Boveda S.

journal.title: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology

title: Therapeutic plasma exchange in Amatoxin-associated pediatric acute liver failure-Results from the Amanita-PEX study.
authorString: Stahl K, Pape T, Nalbant B, Laue T, Andreassen BU, Tegtmeyer D, Büscher R, Fritz T, Fichtner A, D'Antiga L, Breteau I, Dahlqvist G, Schenk H, Lanthier N, Levesque E, Lurz E, Lenz D, Giorgio AD, Sturm E, Oh J, Lainka E, Jørgensen MH, Jack T, Baumann U, Borell FV, Taubert R, Amanita‐PEX‐study group.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition

abstractText: Pediatric acute liver failure (PALF) is a rare but life-threatening condition. Amanita poisoning can lead to PALF with rapid clinical deterioration. Therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) has been proposed as a potential supportive intervention and is established in adult acute liver failure. Evidence regarding TPE in Amanita toxin-induced PALF (AT-PALF) remains scarce, and clinical practice varies across liver transplant centers. The Amanita-PEX study is a retrospective, international, multicenter cohort study including pediatric patients with AT-PALF treated between 2013 and 2024. The combined primary endpoint was 28-day transplant-free survival. A total of 30 patients from 10 centers were included; 17 received at least one session of TPE, and 13 were treated with standard-of-care (SOC) alone. Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. The overall 28-day transplant-free survival rate was 53.3% (16/30), with a 28-day mortality of 10% (3/30). All patients received N-acetylcysteine, and 93% were treated with silibinin. Native liver survival did not differ significantly between the TPE and SOC groups (47% vs. 62%, p = 0.63). In contrast, transplant-free survival was primarily associated with established markers of liver failure severity and organ dysfunction, including MELD and LIU scores, the degree of hepatic encephalopathy, acute kidney injury, and the need for vasopressors or mechanical ventilation. After adjusting for these prognostic markers, TPE remained unassociated with improved outcomes. In this real-world cohort of children with AT-PALF, adjunctive TPE showed no clear improvement in transplant-free survival. Outcomes were predominantly determined by the severity of liver injury and multi-organ dysfunction. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06187220, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/.

title: Impact of Inflammatory Burden on Outcomes After Breakthrough Ischemic Stroke: Insights From the ASPERA-R Study.
authorString: D'Anna L, Prandin G, De Santis F, Gabriele F, Ornello R, Cascio Rizzo A, Sessa M, Schwarz G, Tortorella R, Pantoni L, Mele F, Scopelliti G, Cova I, Casolla B, Gulla M, Diallo SM, Baude M, González L, Rigual R, Fuentes B, Caliandro P, Zauli A, Reale G, Abdelalim A, Ahmed S, Ali Ismail S, Zhang L, Latimer T, Elboghday M, Ferrari F, Mazzacane F, Fonseca AC, Antunes B, Piscaglia MG, Balducci G, Miserocchi LM, Zedde M, Elsayed AE, Desai G, Jaffar M, Banerjee S, Polymeris A, Sacco S, Foschi M.
abstractText: Patients with atrial fibrillation who experience ischemic stroke despite oral anticoagulation (breakthrough stroke) remain at high risk of recurrent vascular events and death. Although inflammation has been associated with thromboembolic risk, its prognostic role in breakthrough stroke remains unclear. We investigated whether a composite inflammatory burden index was associated with adverse outcomes after breakthrough ischemic stroke. We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients with breakthrough ischemic stroke from the ASPERA-R registry. Inflammatory burden was assessed using admission neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, and C-reactive protein. Biomarkers were log-transformed, standardized using Z scores, and combined into a composite inflammatory burden index. Patients were classified as having high (upper tertile) or lower inflammatory burden (lower 2 tertiles). Outcomes included new 90-day ischemic events (recurrent ischemic stroke, transient ischemic attack, or systemic embolism), 24-hour hemorrhagic transformation, and 90-day moderate-to-severe bleeding, intracranial hemorrhage, and mortality. Inverse probability of treatment weighting accounted for center, demographics, vascular risk factors and comorbidities, anticoagulation, competing stroke causes, baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale, prestroke modified Rankin Scale, and time to blood collection. Among 1649 patients enrolled in ASPERA-R, 671 patients from 14 centers had complete biomarker data (median age, 80.1 years [interquartile range, 73.5-85.5]; 52.3% female). Of these, 223 (33.2%) had high inflammatory burden, and 448 (66.8%) had lower inflammatory burden. After weighting, high inflammatory burden was associated with increased risks of ischemic events at 90 days (hazard ratio, 1.53 [95% CI, 1.02-2.30]), all-cause mortality (hazard ratio, 1.70 [95% CI, 1.17-2.47]), moderate-to-severe bleeding (hazard ratio, 2.92 [95% CI, 1.04-8.17]), and hemorrhagic transformation at 24 hours (odds ratio, 2.18 [95% CI, 1.43-3.33]). In breakthrough ischemic stroke, high inflammatory burden was associated with increased risks of recurrent ischemic events, mortality, hemorrhagic transformation, and major bleeding. A composite of routinely available inflammatory biomarkers may help identify patients with higher residual vascular risk.

title: Predicting the Absence and Gaps in Recorded Blood Pressure Follow-up Among Patients With Hypertension
authorString: Sandhu R, Hashish MA, Asghar S, Ye J.
abstractText:
Background:

Electronic health record (EHR) data can help identify patients who would benefit from blood pressure reassessment after an elevated reading.

Objective:

To develop and internally validate a model to predict the absence of a recorded blood pressure measurement after an elevated reading among adults with hypertension; evaluate the potential yield of targeted outreach and model performance across subgroups; and determine whether recorded contact patterns provide additional information for predicting subsequent cardiovascular hospitalization.

Methods:

This retrospective cohort study used MIMIC-IV data. Adults with hypertension, a qualifying systolic blood pressure reading >140 mmHg, defined as the first such reading on or after index, and 90 days of subsequent database coverage and survival were included. The primary outcome was the absence of a recorded blood pressure measurement within 90 days of the index reading. Gradient-boosted trees incorporating 62 demographic, clinical, and contact-history features were compared with logistic regression models using a random 6:2:2 training, validation, and test split, with isotonic recalibration. Nested cross-validation was used to assess the tree model. Model discrimination, calibration, simulated outreach yield, and subgroup performance were evaluated.

Results:

Among 30,942 patients, 10,899 (35.2%) had no recorded blood pressure measurement within 90 days. In the test set (n = 6,189), the gradient-boosted tree model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.740 (95% CI, 0.727-0.753), compared with 0.698 for penalized logistic regression and 0.687 for two-variable logistic regression. The calibration slope was 0.91, and the area under the precision-recall curve was 0.568 (95% CI, 0.546- 0.593). Selecting the 20% of patients with the highest predicted risk identified 34.2% (95% CI, 32.7-35.7) of patients without a recorded measurement, with a positive predictive value of 60.4% (95% CI, 57.4-63.2). In out-of-fold subgroup analyses using a common selection threshold corresponding to an overall selection rate of 20%, sensitivity was 21.5% among Black patients, 23.3% among Hispanic patients, and 37.2% among White patients. Among 15,200 participants in the landmark analysis, 664 cardiovascular hospitalizations occurred. Increasing and sustained contact patterns were associated with modestly higher hazards of cardiovascular hospitalization, with the association primarily attributable to heart failure hospitalization. For sustained versus minimal contact, the hazard ratio for the composite outcome was 1.40 (95% CI, 1.06-1.85). However, adding contact gaps and trajectories improved the C-statistic by only 0.0023 (95% CI, -0.0006 to 0.0056).

Conclusions:

The model showed potential for prioritizing blood pressure reassessment outreach, although sensitivity varied across racial and ethnic groups. Recorded contact patterns provided little incremental discrimination for cardiovascular hospitalization.

title: Impact of Iron Deficiency on Short-Term Clinical Outcomes in Patients Admitted With Acute Heart Failure at Benjamin Mkapa Hospital: A Prospective Cohort Study
authorString: Mukky¹ D, Makubi² A, Meda¹˒² J, Masava² K.
abstractText: Introduction: Iron deficiency is a common but under-recognized comorbidity in acute heart failure (AHF) and is associated with poor outcomes. However, data on its impact on short-term outcomes among AHF patients in Tanzania remain limited. This study assessed the association between absolute iron deficiency (AID) and short-term outcomes among patients admitted with AHF at Benjamin Mkapa Hospital (BMH). Methods A prospective cohort study was conducted among adults admitted with AHF at BMH between January 2025 and June 2026. AID was defined as serum ferritin < 100 ng/mL. Participants were followed for 90 days. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality or hospital readmission. Secondary outcomes included quality of life (KCCQ-12 score), NYHA functional status, and length of hospital stay. Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression assessed the primary outcome; secondary outcomes were compared using parametric or non-parametric tests as appropriate. Results A total of 339 participants were enrolled, of whom 330 (97.3%) completed follow-up. The mean age was 61.5 ± 15.5 years, 176 (53.0%) were female and 175 (53.0%) participants had AID. During follow-up, 63 (19.0%) experienced the composite endpoint. Participants with AID had lower event-free survival than those without (72.5% vs. 90.3%, log-rank p < 0.001). After adjustment, AID was independently associated with the composite endpoint (AHR 2.25, 95% CI 1.21–4.17; p = 0.010). At 90 days, AID participants had poorer NYHA functional status, with more remaining in class IV (20.0% vs. 11.6%) and fewer reaching class II (28.0% vs. 37.4%; χ²=21.20, p < 0.001). Participants with AID had a smaller improvement in KCCQ-12 scores (4.1 ± 9.8 vs. 9.2 ± 8.8 points; p < 0.001), and hospital stay was longer (7.9 ± 2.5 vs. 6.8 ± 2.2 days; p < 0.001). Conclusion AID is common among patients admitted with AHF and is independently associated with poorer short-term clinical outcomes. Larger multicentre studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Knowledge, Availability and Utilization of Non-Pneumatic Anti-Shock Garment among Nurses and Midwives Managing Postpartum Hemorrhage in Osun State, Nigeria
authorString: Odesanya L, Oyekale R, Afolabi O, Fasanu A, Onasoga O, Olarewaju S.
abstractText: Background Postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) remains one of the leading causes of maternal morbidity and mortality worldwide, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. The Non-Pneumatic Anti-Shock Garment (NASG) is a low-cost first-aid device used to stabilize women experiencing hypovolemic shock due to obstetric haemorrhage while definitive treatment is being arranged. Adequate knowledge of the NASG among healthcare providers is essential for its appropriate use in maternal healthcare. Objective This study assessed the knowledge of the Non-Pneumatic Anti-Shock Garment (NASG) among nurses and midwives working in primary healthcare facilities in Osun State, Nigeria. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 124 registered nurses and midwives working in primary healthcare facilities in Osun State between October and November 2025. Data were collected using a structured, self-administered questionnaire and analyzed using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) version 20. Descriptive statistics, including frequencies, percentages, means, and standard deviations, were used to summarize the data. Results The mean age of the respondents was 41.71 ± 9.75 years. Most respondents were female (87.1%), married (85.5%), and midwives (67.7%). Overall, respondents demonstrated good knowledge of the NASG. The majority correctly identified the primary purpose of the NASG (95.2%), the appropriate timing of its application (95.2%), the correct sequence of application (95.2%), the correct procedure for removal (93.5%), the physiological mechanism of action (98.4%), and congestive heart failure as a contraindication (95.2%). In addition, 95.2% correctly indicated that the NASG does not replace definitive treatment for postpartum haemorrhage. Conclusion Nurses and midwives working in primary healthcare facilities in Osun State demonstrated good knowledge of the Non-Pneumatic Anti-Shock Garment. Continuous professional education and regular refresher training are recommended to sustain and further improve healthcare providers' knowledge and promote evidence-based management of postpartum haemorrhage.

title: Impaired NK Cell-Mediated Tumor Surveillance in Atherosclerosis Due to Plaque-Induced PPARα Dysfunction.
authorString: Ren T, Yu S, Jiang X, Wen J, Yan C, Du D, Tang J, Peng L, Wu S, Dai C, Yao E, Jin X, Yang L.
abstractText:
Background

Atherosclerosis is frequently associated with both an increased incidence and accelerated development of cancer. However, the impact of atherosclerosis progression on the efficacy of tumor surveillance by cytotoxic immune cells, particularly natural killer (NK) cells, remains poorly understood. This study aims to explore how atherosclerosis affects NK cell-mediated tumor surveillance in both animal models and humans.

Methods

We analyzed peripheral blood NK cells from patients with atherosclerosis with early-stage (<50% stenosis) versus advanced-stage (≥50% stenosis) coronary artery lesions by flow cytometry to assess NK cell frequency, PPARα (peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha) expression, and IFN-γ (interferon gamma) production. In parallel, we used atherosclerotic plaque progression and regression models, including high-fat diet-fed Apo-/- mice and aortic arch transplantation into wild-type, Apoe-/-, Rag1-/-, and NK cell-specific PPARα knockout (Pparaflox/flox Ncr1Cre/+) mice. NK cell phenotype and function were evaluated by flow cytometry for immune checkpoint molecules (PD-1 [programmed cell death protein-1], TIM-3 [T-cell immunoglobulin and mucin-domain containing-3], LAG-3 [lymphocyte activation gene-3], and TIGIT [T-cell immunoglobulin and ITIM domain]) and effector cytokines (IFN-γ, GZMB [granzyme B]). Antitumor capacity was assessed in B16F10 melanoma and ID8 ovarian cancer models in atherosclerosis mice, with or without a PPARα agonist (oleoylethanolamide) or an mTOR (mechanistic target of rapamycin kinase) agonist (MHY1485) treatment. Mechanistic studies included immunoblotting for mTOR pathway components and transcriptomic correlation analyses (GSE94044, GSE24495).

Results

We found that atherosclerotic plaques induced PPARα deficiency in NK cells, which impaired their cytotoxicity and weakened tumor immunosurveillance. Mechanistically, PPARα-deficient NK cells exhibited elevated immune checkpoint expression, an exhaustion phenotype, and markedly diminished mTOR signaling. Administration of the PPARα agonist oleoylethanolamide restored NK cell effector function and enhanced tumor-killing efficacy in vivo, whereas mTOR agonism partially rescued the defect caused by PPARα loss. These findings underscore the suppressive effects of arterial plaques on NK cell-mediated antitumor immunity and suggest PPARα compensation as a potential immunotherapeutic strategy.

Conclusions

Our study unveils a novel association between atherosclerosis and the attenuation of NK cell antitumor immunity. Specifically, plaque-induced downregulation of PPARα in NK cells leads to uncontrolled immune checkpoint expression, causing NK cell exhaustion and diminished antitumor function. Pharmacological enhancement of PPARα signaling rejuvenated NK cell activity and reduced tumor growth in atherosclerosis. Therefore, targeting PPARα offers a promising therapeutic approach for cancer treatment and prevention in individuals with atherosclerosis.

title: Alzheimer's pathology mediates arteriolosclerosis and cerebral amyloid angiopathy associations with cognition.
authorString: Hayes CA, Dharmapuri A, Agwu C, Ramirez V, Newman J, Chambers M, Odden MC, Younes K.
abstractText: Vascular and neurodegenerative pathologies frequently co-occur in aging brains, yet the mechanisms linking vascular neuropathologies to cognitive impairment remain incompletely understood. We examined whether Alzheimer's disease neuropathologic change (ADNC) and Lewy body disease (LBD) mediate or modify associations between vascular neuropathologies and domain-specific cognitive performance. The analytic sample included 1,269 decedents (mean age at death, 84.3 ± 9.1 years; 43.3% female; 94.7% White). At the last evaluation prior to death, 22.5% were cognitively normal, 2.4% were impaired but not mild cognitive impairment (MCI), 14.9% had MCI, and 60.2% had dementia. Vascular neuropathologies included arteriolosclerosis, atherosclerosis of the circle of Willis, cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA), gross infarcts/lacunes, and microinfarcts. Multivariable linear regression models evaluated associations with harmonized memory, executive function, and language z-scores adjusting for age at death, sex, education, and apolipoprotein E ε4 status. Effect modification by ADNC and LBD was tested. Mediation models estimated indirect and direct effects of vascular neuropathologies on cognition through ADNC or LBD using 5,000 bootstrap samples. Greater arteriolosclerosis severity was associated with worse memory (β=-0.16, 95% CI -0.23 to -0.09), executive function (β=-0.18, 95% CI -0.24 to -0.11), and language (β=-0.18, 95% CI -0.24 to -0.12; all p<0.001). CAA was strongly associated with poorer cognition across domains, including memory (β=-0.26, 95% CI -0.33 to -0.19; p<0.001). Atherosclerosis and infarcts showed more limited associations, while microinfarcts were not significantly associated with cognition. Mediation analyses indicated that ADNC statistically accounted for approximately 13-29% of the associations between arteriolosclerosis and cognition across domains and 64-91% of the associations between CAA and cognition. Direct effects of arteriolosclerosis remained significant, whereas CAA effects were largely explained by ADNC. Effect modification by ADNC and LBD was limited, although LBD attenuated associations of arteriolosclerosis and CAA with executive function. Mediation through LBD was not observed. This novel evidence shows that vascular neuropathologies influence cognition through defined pathways with statistically significant patterns of associations. In this autopsy-confirmed cohort, vascular neuropathologies showed different patterns of association with domain-specific cognitive performance and ADNC. A larger proportion of the association involving CAA was statistically accounted for by ADNC, whereas direct associations remained more apparent for arteriolosclerosis. This study clarifies how vascular and neurodegenerative processes interact to shape cognitive impact and inform mechanistic preventions.

title: A Branch-Specific Combined Fenestration Strategy for Chronic Aortic Dissection With Severe Paravisceral True Lumen Compression.
authorString: Wu X, Liu J, Huang Q, Li W, Qin J, Lu X.

journal.title: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR

abstractText:
Purpose

To evaluate a branch-specific combined fenestration strategy to address the technical challenges of severe true lumen (TL) compression during physician-modified fenestration (PMF)-based four-vessel visceral reconstruction in chronic aortic dissection (CAD).

Materials and methods

This retrospective study enrolled twenty-three consecutive patients with aneurysmal CAD and severe paravisceral TL compression (minimum functional TL diameter ≤10 mm) treated between January 2020 and December 2024. All patients underwent visceral reconstruction using anterior-branch PMF and bilateral renal in situ laser fenestration (ISLF) performed following TL expansion. Endpoints included technical success (complete four-vessel reconstruction), 30-day mortality, target-vessel patency, and TL expansion.

Results

Complete four-vessel visceral reconstruction was achieved in all 23 patients (92/92 target vessels). Renal ISLF was successful in all 46 renal arteries, with first-attempt success in 44 (96%). Distal aortic exclusion was required in 20 patients; one interval infrarenal rupture in the staged group was managed with emergency repair. Over a median follow-up of 17.0 months, primary target-vessel patency was 99% (91/92). The median minimum functional TL diameter increased from 8.0 mm preoperatively to 15.9 mm at one-year follow-up. No type I or III endoleak was identified. Thirty-day mortality was 0%. Transient spinal cord ischaemia occurred in one patient (4%), and acute kidney injury (KDIGO Stage 1) in two patients (9%), all resolving before discharge.

Conclusion

In highly selected CAD patients with severe TL compression, this combined fenestration strategy enabled complete four-vessel visceral reconstruction with satisfactory early target-vessel patency and no target-vessel loss, though longer follow-up in larger cohorts is required.

title: Clinical outcomes of total endovascular aortic arch repair by in situ microneedle fenestration using the triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique.
authorString: Ye P, Miao H, Zeng Q, Liu W, Ma M, Chen Y.
abstractText:
Purpose

To investigate the outcomes of total endovascular aortic arch repair (TEAAR) via in situ micro-needle fenestration (ISMNF) with the triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique.

Materials and methods

In this retrospective study, the data of consecutive patients who underwent TEAAR via ISMNF with triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique between August 2022 and April 2025 were analyzed. Three 6-Fr, 90-cm sheaths were placed into ascending aorta without removing the dilator and super-stiff guidewires during main stent-graft deployment. This configuration creates a gutter between the stent-graft and aortic wall to maintain perfusion to supra-aortic branches. Operative details, technical success, 30-day and midterm outcomes, and adverse events were recorded. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to estimate freedom from all-cause death and reintervention.

Results

Overall, 36 patients were included. The technical success rate was 94.4% (34/36). Endovascular reconstruction of cervical branches was successfully performed in all cases. The 30-day mortality was 2.8%. The median follow-up period was 19 months (range, 1-32 months). The all-cause death rate was 11.1% (4/36), with no cases of any aorta-related death. The prevalence of endoleaks during follow-up was 13.9% (5/36). The overall stroke rate was 8.3% (3/36). The 1- and 2-year survival rates were 97.3% ± 2.7% and 85.8% ± 8.1%, respectively. The cumulative rate of freedom from reintervention at 1 and 2 years was 87.5% ± 5.9% and 83.2% ± 7.0%, respectively.

Conclusion

TEAAR via ISMNF with the triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique was performed with a 94% technical success rate and stroke risk similar to open surgery.

title: Association of modified cardiovascular health with long-term all-cause mortality among adults with Ankle-Brachial Index-defined peripheral artery disease: a NHANES 1999-2004 cohort study.
authorString: Wang M, Wang Y.

journal.title: International angiology : a journal of the International Union of Angiology

abstractText:
Background

Whether an integrated cardiovascular health profile is associated with long-term mortality among adults with objectively defined peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains insufficiently characterized in nationally representative cohorts.

Methods

We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999-2004 participants aged ≥40 years with Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) measurements and linked mortality follow-up through December 31, 2019. PAD was defined as a minimum ABI ≤0.90. Modified cardiovascular health (mCVH; range 0-12) was constructed from smoking, Body Mass Index, physical activity, blood pressure, total cholesterol, and glycemic status. Corrected six-year Mobile Examination Center weights and complex survey design variables were used. Weighted Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for all-cause mortality using sequential adjustment for demographic factors, socioeconomic factors, survey cycle, and minimum ABI. Additional analyses evaluated non-PAD participants and cardiovascular mortality.

Results

The primary PAD cohort included 554 adults, among whom 428 deaths occurred during a median follow-up of 123.5 months. PAD participants had a higher absolute all-cause mortality burden than non-PAD participants. Each 1-point higher mCVH score was associated with lower all-cause mortality in Model 1 (HR 0.888, 95% CI 0.842-0.937; P<0.001), Model 2 (HR 0.922, 95% CI 0.870-0.977; P=0.006), and Model 3 (HR 0.926, 95% CI 0.874-0.982; P=0.010). Among non-PAD participants, higher mCVH was also associated with lower all-cause mortality, and the mCVH × PAD status interaction was not statistically significant (P=0.122). In sensitivity analysis, higher mCVH was also associated with lower cardiovascular mortality (HR 0.863, 95% CI 0.786-0.948; P=0.002). Component-level analyses suggested that smoking was the most robust individual component.

Conclusions

Among U.S. adults with ABI-defined PAD, higher baseline mCVH was associated with lower long-term all-cause mortality. These findings support the prognostic relevance of integrated cardiovascular health profiling after objective PAD identification, while highlighting smoking as the most consistent individual component.

title: Caffeic acid mitigates myocardial fibrosis via suppressing MAPKs/CREB-mediated inflammation in myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury mice.
authorString: Xiang M, Ouyang X, Song S, Yang M, Sarapultsev A, Luo S, Dong Y, Hu D.
abstractText: Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI) represents a major form of secondary damage during reperfusion therapy, in which inflammation and myocardial fibrosis are key pathological features. Caffeic acid (CA), a natural phenolic compound abundant in dietary sources, has been implicated in cardiovascular protection; however, the mechanisms by which CA modulates post-MIRI inflammation and fibrosis remain insufficiently defined. To clarify the molecular target(s) and signaling mechanism(s) through which CA attenuates inflammation-associated myocardial fibrosis after MIRI. A LAD ligation-based murine MIRI model was used to evaluate the anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic efficacy of CA. A co-culture system using cardiac fibroblasts and RAW 264.7 macrophages, along with adoptive cell transfer, was applied to interrogate macrophage-fibroblast crosstalk. Transcriptomic profiling (RNA-seq) was performed to identify candidate pathways involved in CA-mediated protection. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assay, CETSA, immunofluorescence, and western blotting were used to assess MAPKs/CREB signaling as a putative intervention axis, and pharmacological activation of MAPKs (anisomycin) or CREB (forskolin), or MAPK14 ablation, was employed to probe pathway involvement. CA improved cardiac function and alleviated inflammatory and fibrotic pathology in MIRI mice, accompanied by suppression of pro-inflammatory cytokines. Conditioned medium from LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 cells promoted fibroblast activation, and adoptively transferred macrophages within the myocardium promoted fibrotic protein expression; both effects were attenuated by CA. RNA-seq implicated MAPK signaling in the protective mechanism of CA, and downstream analyses supported inhibition of the MAPKs/CREB axis. Notably, CA achieved effects comparable to those of MAPK14 ablation, whereas anisomycin or forskolin partially blunted the anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic effects of CA, consistent with functional involvement of MAPKs/CREB signaling in CA-mediated protection during MIRI. CA mitigates MIRI-associated myocardial fibrosis by suppressing MAPKs/CREB-mediated inflammatory signaling, supporting its potential to improve long-term post-MIRI remodeling.

title: Bone morphogenetic protein 12: a novel target for cardiovascular disease.
authorString: Isaza SC, Hernández-García MÁ, Fernández-García CE, Pérez-Utrera C, Álvarez-Rubal M, Muñoz JM, Friera A, García-Monzón C, Gómez-Hernández A, Landete P, Egea J, Alfonso F, González-Rodríguez Á.
abstractText: Bone morphogenetic protein 12 (BMP12) is known to regulate mesenchymal differentiation and extracellular matrix remodeling. Given its structural and signaling similarities to BMP2, which promotes osteogenic phenotypic switching and pro-atherogenic responses in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), BMP12 may also contribute to vascular remodeling and atherosclerosis progression. This translational study aimed to unravel BMP12 involvement in cardiovascular disease (CVD). BMP12 effects on atherogenesis-related processes in VSMCs in absence or presence of BMP type I receptor inhibitors (DMH2 and LDN-193189) were evaluated. Additionally, circulating BMP12 levels were measured in a well-characterized cohort of patients with CV risk factors and correlated with cardiometabolic disorders and vascular damage markers. Results from the experimental study showed increased migration and calcification in BMP12-treated VSMCs. Mechanistically, BMP12 induced expression of osteogenic markers (RUNX2 and ALP) and genes related to cellular migration (Mmp9), while reducing contractile marker Desmin. These pro-atherogenic effects were blocked using BMP type I receptor inhibitors. Furthermore, the clinical study revealed higher serum BMP12 levels in patients with CVD and type 2 diabetes. Moreover, circulating BMP12 concentrations were elevated in patients with carotid and femoral plaques, correlating with plaque volume. Notably, BMP12 emerged as an independent predictor of femoral atherosclerosis. Collectively, these findings identify BMP12 as a previously unrecognized mediator of vascular remodeling, promoting pro-atherogenic effects in VSMCs through canonical BMP signaling. The association between elevated circulating BMP12 levels and subclinical vascular damage further supports its potential value as a contributor to atherosclerosis progression and as a promising novel candidate biomarker for CV risk.

title: Temporal proteomics maps concealed-stage remodeling and reveals early mitochondrial alteration as an intervention target in a model of PKP2-arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Achter JS, Svenningsen M, Mulvey J, Bertoli G, Meyer E, Yepuri G, Zhang M, Ramasamy R, Delmar M, Lundby A.
abstractText: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy is a heritable cardiac disorder commonly linked to alterations in desmosomal proteins. While desmosomal dysfunction is a recognized pathogenic mechanism, the early molecular remodeling that precedes clinical manifestations remains unclear. Here we used a mouse model with inducible cardiomyocyte-specific knockout of Pkp2 (encoding plakophilin-2) and performed time-resolved mass spectrometry-based proteomics to map disease progression from early PKP2 loss to structural remodeling. Molecular changes preceded phenotypic abnormalities, and spatial asymmetry was evident, with earlier and more pronounced proteome remodeling in the right ventricle despite comparable PKP2 depletion in both ventricles. Downregulation of protein networks spanning desmosomes, sarcomeres and mitochondria suggests their functional coupling, with mitochondrial remodeling emerging as an early and progressively worsening feature. Intervention with honokiol attenuated changes across the major protein networks, highlighting mitochondrial pathways as promising therapeutic targets and honokiol as a potential strategy to delay arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy progression. Our findings provide critical insights into the concealed stage of disease progression and identify molecular targets for early intervention.

title: Early BMI-associated increases in central and peripheral blood pressure in primary school children: evidence of a continuous, nonlinear relationship below the overweight threshold.
authorString: von der Born J, Wilmsmeier L, Sugianto RI, Grabitz C, Ubenauf TA, Lehmann E, Memaran N, Braun AC, Homeyer D, Tegtbur U, Schmidt BMW, Melk A.
abstractText: Childhood overweight is associated with elevated blood pressure (BP) and future cardiovascular risk. We aimed to determine the body mass index percentile (BMIp) at which blood pressure (BP) begins to increase in children, particularly below the overweight threshold. Central BP may provide additional insight into early hemodynamic changes. In a cohort of primary school children, peripheral and central BP were measured using standardized protocols. Associations of BMIp with BP were evaluated using spline and linear regression models adjusted for age, sex, and height. BMIp categories were used to identify thresholds at which BP was significantly higher than in children with BMIp < 50. Among 1,183 children (mean age 7.9 years), BP increased progressively with rising BMIp, with the greatest elevations in children with overweight or obesity. Significant increases in peripheral and central systolic BP were observed at BMIp levels below the WHO-defined cutoff for overweight, central BP increased at lower BMIp than peripheral BP. Although peripheral diastolic BP was not associated with BMIp, central diastolic BP increased significantly across higher BMIp ranges. Conclusions: In primary school children, BMI-associated increases in BP are detectable at substantially lower BMIp than commonly considered, reflecting a continuous nonlinear relationship. Both peripheral and central BP increased within the high-normal BMI-range. Central BP identified early, distinct BP alterations, including significant diastolic changes not detected with peripheral BP. These findings suggest that cardiovascular risk related to body weight arises along a continuum and support the potential value of early BP monitoring in children with increasing BMI.Trial registration: Trial Registration Number: NCT04942431. Date of Registration: 08.04.2021. What is Known • Childhood overweight is associated with elevated blood pressure, both are key risk factors for future cardiovascular disease. • However, the body mass index level at which blood pressure begins to rise in children remains unclear. What is New • We identify specific body mass index ranges at which blood pressure increased significantly, highlighting children with high-normal body weight as a group at early cardiovascular risk.

title: The gut-muscle-joint axis in osteoarthritis: Mechanistic insights and therapeutic perspectives.
authorString: Karim A, Ahmad F, Qaisar R.
abstractText: Emerging evidence highlights a complex crosstalk between the gut microbiota, musculoskeletal tissues, and the joint microenvironment, revealing osteoarthritis (OA) as a systemic disorder rather than a localized cartilage disease. The gut-muscle-joint interaction integrates microbial dysbiosis, chronic inflammation, and metabolic dysregulation to influence cartilage homeostasis, muscle strength, and neuromuscular stability. Building upon previously described gut-osteoarthritis and gut-muscle interactions, the Gut-Muscle-Joint (GMJ) axis is presented as an integrative framework linking intestinal permeability, microbial metabolites, systemic inflammatory signaling, neuromuscular health, skeletal muscle function, and joint integrity. Perturbations in this axis amplify oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and extracellular matrix degradation across musculoskeletal tissues. Understanding GMJ axis-driven mechanisms offers novel preventive and therapeutic strategies that target microbiome restoration, metabolic reprogramming, and neuromuscular health through probiotics, postbiotics, AMPK-SIRT1 activators, and structured exercise. This integrative perspective positions the GMJ axis as a unifying framework for intervention, enabling precision approaches to preserve joint function, reduce sarcopenia, and attenuate OA progression.

title: Purpurin Alleviates Chemotherapy-Induced Thrombocytopenia Through Estrogen Receptor α Dependent Phosphoinositide 3-Kinase/Protein Kinase B Signalling.
authorString: Gan X, Wang X, Hao L, Tang X, Liu Z, Wang L, Xie X, Li X, Zhao C, Li Y, Huang X, Liu Y, Wu J.
abstractText: Chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia (CIT) increases bleeding risk and compromises chemotherapy delivery. Purpurin, a hydroxyanthraquinone found in Rubia cordifolia L., has not been examined as a regulator of megakaryopoiesis. We investigated whether purpurin restores platelet production after cyclophosphamide (CTX) exposure and examined the involvement of estrogen receptor α (ESR1)-phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (AKT) signalling. Purpurin was evaluated in K562 and Meg-01 megakaryocytic differentiation models, Tg(itga2b:eGFP) zebrafish, and CTX-induced thrombocytopenic mice. Megakaryocyte (MK) differentiation, DNA ploidy, cytoskeletal remodelling, platelet recovery, and haemostatic function were assessed. Computational target prediction was used for hypothesis generation, followed by drug affinity responsive target stability analysis and pharmacological inhibition of ESR1 and PI3K. At concentrations that did not cause detectable cytotoxicity (2.5-10 μM), purpurin increased CD41+CD42b+ cells, MK ploidy, F-actin remodelling, and expression of NF-E2, GATA1, RUNX1, and FOSB. Purpurin increased thrombocyte abundance in zebrafish and restored platelet counts, MK maturation, and haemostatic function in CTX-treated mice. Purpurin increased the resistance of ESR1 to proteolysis in the drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS) assay. Pharmacological inhibition of ESR1 or PI3K attenuated purpurin-induced differentiation and PI3K/AKT phosphorylation. These findings support the involvement of ESR1-associated PI3K/AKT signalling through which purpurin promotes megakaryopoiesis and platelet recovery. Purpurin warrants further evaluation as a natural-product lead for CIT, including genetic target validation, pharmacokinetic characterization, and assessment in tumour-bearing models.

title: [Early cardiac remodeling in short-duration T2DM: Benchmarking 85 cases against norms in an Algerian population].
authorString: Zemit C, Lounici A, Tabti E, Meftah Y, Ghaib S, Hammadi W, Mesbahi S.
abstractText:
Background

Diabetic cardiomyopathy is traditionally viewed as a late complication of chronic hyperglycemia, but emerging evidence suggests it may manifest early in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), preceding prolonged metabolic exposure.

Objective

To determine whether early cardiac remodeling markers, particularly diastolic dysfunction, are already present in patients with short-duration T2DM (< 5 years).

Methods

We conducted a cross-sectional study of 86 T2DM patients at a university hospital in an Algerian population (2024). Echocardiography was performed using a GE Vivid E95 system. Diastolic dysfunction was defined using ASE/EACVI criteria. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors.

Results

Diastolic dysfunction was present in 20% (17/86) of patients despite recent disease onset. The study population had a mean diabetes duration of 1.8±2.0 years, mean age of 54.7±8.9 years, and mean HbA1c of 8.9±0.27%. Hypertension was present in 35.3% (30/86) of patients, and obesity (BMI≥30kg/m2) in 29.5% (25/86). Impaired myocardial relaxation was widespread: lateral e'<10cm/s in 49.4%, septal e'<7cm/s in 24.4%, and elevated E/e' in 29.1%. Contrary to traditional assumptions, dysfunction was not significantly different between well-controlled (HbA1c<7%) and poorly controlled patients (27.3 vs. 17.2%, P=0.356). Systolic blood pressure was the only independent predictor of diastolic dysfunction (OR 1.07 per mmHg, 95% CI 1.02-1.13, P=0.008). Neither HbA1c (P=0.324) nor diabetes duration (P=0.863) showed significant associations.

Conclusion

Early cardiac remodeling occurs frequently in short-duration T2DM, independent of glycemic control and disease chronicity. This challenges the traditional view that diabetic cardiomyopathy requires prolonged hyperglycemia. Systolic blood pressure is the sole predictor, suggesting mechanisms beyond metabolic control alone. Systematic echocardiographic screening at T2DM diagnosis may be warranted to detect subclinical dysfunction and prevent progression to heart failure.

title: Clinical characterization of LDL-c/ApoB discordance in the metabolic patient: The "false control" as an independent marker of subclinical atherosclerosis.
authorString: Urbaneja Zumaquero V, Coca Prieto I, Rioja Villodres J, Ariza Corbo MJ, Ordoñez Simón RM, Benítez Toledo MJ, Gutiérrez Lara GC, Sánchez Chaparro MÁ, Espildora Hernández J.

journal.title: Clinica e investigacion en arteriosclerosis : publicacion oficial de la Sociedad Espanola de Arteriosclerosis

abstractText:
Introduction and objectives

Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-c) is the cornerstone of lipid-lowering therapy, but it may underestimate the true atherogenic burden in patients with cardiometabolic risk. The discordance between LDL-c (mass) and apolipoprotein B (ApoB, particle number) creates a state of hidden residual risk. The objective of this study was to evaluate the prevalence of this discordance and determine its clinical association with subclinical atherosclerosis.

Material and methods

A cross-sectional observational study was conducted in 103 high-risk patients (mean age 60 years; 62% men) treated in Internal Medicine consultations. Anthropometric parameters, glycemic, and lipid profiles were analyzed. Discordance was determined using the percentile method, and the "false control" status was defined based on the achievement of therapeutic targets according to clinical guidelines. Cardiovascular risk in patients without a previous cardiovascular event was estimated using the SCORE2/SCORE2-OP model. Subclinical atherosclerosis was defined as the presence of carotid plaque assessed by ultrasound. Spearman correlation tests, Kruskal-Wallis comparisons, and a multivariate logistic regression model adjusted for age, sex, and HbA1c were used.

Results

A sample with a high metabolic burden (80% hypertensive, 52% diabetic, BMI 31.9±5.4kg/m2) was included. A total lack of correlation was observed between LDL-c and ApoB (rho=-0.021; p=0.833). Twenty-nine percent presented high-ApoB discordance (subjects whose ApoB percentile exceeded that of LDL-c by>10 units), and 25% were in a state of "false control" (LDL-c on target with elevated ApoB). Patients with high-ApoB discordance showed a more adverse metabolic profile (HbA1c 6.3 vs. 5.8%; p=0.014). Plaque prevalence was significantly higher in the "false control" group (73.1%) than in the "true control" group (36.4%; p=0.035). Concordant lipid control was independently associated with the absence of plaque (OR 6.32; 95% CI: 1.43-27.87; p=0.015).

Conclusions

LDL-c/ApoB discordance is highly prevalent in high-risk patients. In this context, the clinical situation of "false control" is independently associated with a higher burden of subclinical atherosclerosis. The systematic measurement of ApoB is essential to identify this hidden residual risk and optimize cardiovascular prevention in patients with a complex metabolic profile.

title: Ultrasound assessment of fluid tolerance in patients undergoing major gastrointestinal surgery: epidemiology of pulmonary and systemic congestion.
authorString: Klompmaker P, Plantinga C, den Otter CA, van Zwol J, Oomes PPCH, Kho E, Schenk J, Berge-Henegouwen MI, Erdmann JI, Vlaar APJ, Veelo DP, Tuinman PR.
abstractText: Fluid accumulation in surgical patients is associated with worse outcomes. Lung ultrasound (LUS) and venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) grading can assess congestion and thereby fluid tolerance. However, evidence regarding epidemiology, feasibility, and associations of reduced fluid tolerance with outcomes in surgical patients is lacking. This was a prospective single-centre observational cohort study in patients undergoing major gastrointestinal surgery. LUS and VExUS were performed before surgery and daily for up to 5 days after surgery. Reduced fluid tolerance was defined as pulmonary congestion (B profile on LUS), systemic congestion (VExUS ≥2), or both. The primary outcome was the prevalence of reduced fluid tolerance. Secondary outcomes were feasibility of ultrasound assessments, Clavien-Dindo grade ≥3 complications, and length of stay (LOS). Of the 200 participants included, 73 (37%) exhibited signs of reduced fluid tolerance, most commonly on postoperative day 4 (n=28; 14%). Reduced fluid tolerance was primarily driven by pulmonary congestion (n=69; 95%), whereas systemic congestion was rare. In most affected patients (47 of 73; 64%), reduced fluid tolerance was limited to 1 day.
