Of 1200 planned assessments, 146 (12%) were missing: 123 because participants declined, mostly owing to the burden of repeated assessments, and 23 (2%) because of incomplete views. Reduced fluid tolerance was associated with LOS of >7 days (odds ratio 3.29; 95% CI 1.03-10.70), but not with major postoperative complications (hazard ratio 1.18; 95% CI 0.49-2.86). Reduced fluid tolerance detected by ultrasound is common after major gastrointestinal surgery and associated with increased LOS. Ultrasound assessments were technically feasible, but repeated assessments were perceived as a burden by a substantial proportion of patients. NCT06166719 (principal investigator: A.P.J. Vlaar; first registered: 04-12-2023).

title: Associations of Plasma Branched-Chain Amino Acids With Incident Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease by Sex and Type 2 Diabetes Status Among Chinese Adults.
authorString: Su S, Liu F, Ma F, Chen S, Huang K, Cao J, Wang Y, Li H, Yu L, Liu X, Huang J, Gu D, Lu X, Li J.
abstractText: Evidence on associations between branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs) and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) remains limited, particularly in Chinese populations. We investigated associations between BCAAs and ASCVD and whether they differed by sex and Type 2 diabetes (T2D). Using a case-cohort design within a Chinese prospective cohort, we included a random subcohort (n = 2163) and incident ASCVD cases (n = 674). Plasma BCAA concentrations were quantified by ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Associations of BCAAs with incident ASCVD were evaluated using Prentice-weighted Cox proportional hazards models, with stratified analyses and interaction tests by sex and T2D. Mediation analyses assessed the contribution of BCAAs to associations between T2D and ASCVD. During a median follow-up of 10.3 years, plasma BCAAs were positively associated with ASCVD. Associations appeared more pronounced among female participants, although interaction tests by sex were not statistically significant. Among female participants, significant associations were only observed in those with T2D, with hazard ratios (95% CIs) of 2.014 (1.185-3.423), 1.867 (1.142-3.052), 1.814 (1.071-3.078) and 2.030 (1.197-3.442) per standard deviation increment in ln-transformed total BCAA, isoleucine, leucine and valine, respectively. Additive interactions with T2D were detected for total BCAA and leucine. For male participants, no significant associations were observed, regardless of T2D status. Notably, total BCAA, leucine and valine partially mediated the association between T2D and ASCVD among female participants, with mediated proportions of 7.89%, 7.68% and 6.76%, respectively. Higher plasma BCAA concentrations were associated with increased incident ASCVD risk, supporting their potential role as metabolic markers of ASCVD.

title: Ceramides, Particularly Those Containing Very-Long-Chain Saturated Fatty Acids, Are Independently Associated With the Triglyceride-Glucose Index in European Individuals With Type 2 Diabetes.
authorString: Carpentier L, Denimal D, Rouland A, Petit JM, Pais de Barros JP, Duvillard L, Bouillet B, Vergès B.
abstractText: The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is associated with insulin resistance and cardiovascular disease (CVD), but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. As ceramides are implicated in both insulin resistance and CVD, we investigated the association between the TyG index and plasma ceramides in individuals with Type 2 diabetes (T2D). We measured total plasma ceramides and seven ceramide species (C16:0, C18:0, C20:0, C22:0, C24:1, C24:0 and C26:0) in 289 European individuals with T2D using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Associations with the TyG index were assessed using univariate and multivariate analyses, including linear regression as the primary analysis. Total ceramides, long-chain saturated fatty acid (LCSFA) ceramides and very-long-chain saturated fatty acid (VLSFA) ceramides were significantly higher in the upper TyG quartiles. The TyG index correlated significantly (p < 0.0001) with total ceramides, LCSFA ceramides, VLSFA ceramides and all ceramide species except C26:0. Multivariable analyses identified total and VLSFA ceramides as independently associated with the TyG index (p < 0.0001). Our study shows, for the first time, an independent association between the TyG index and plasma ceramides, particularly VLSFA ceramides, in people with T2D. Further research is warranted to elucidate whether this association contributes to the link between the TyG index, insulin resistance and CVD. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT02045563.

title: Clinical factors and the non-linear relationship between age and neurological outcome in comatose patients following cardiac arrest.
authorString: Guevara Tirado A, Guevara Tirado A.

journal.title: Revista espanola de anestesiologia y reanimacion

abstractText: Age is often incorporated as a linear or categorical predictor after cardiac arrest, which may obscure variations in its association with neurological outcome. To evaluate clinical factors associated with good neurological outcome and explore its nonlinear relationship with age in comatose patients after return of spontaneous circulation. Retrospective analysis of 508 patients from the I-CARE cohort. The outcome was Cerebral Performance Category (CPC) 1-2 versus CPC 3-5, based on the best CPC recorded between 3 and 6 months. Age was modeled using restricted cubic splines with four knots. Discrimination, calibration, and optimism were assessed using 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Time to return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), missing in 51.8%, was examined in sensitivity analyses. CPC 1-2 occurred in 38.2%. Age was associated with outcome (χ² = 29.16; p < 0.001) and showed nonlinearity (χ² = 7.79; p = 0.020). A shockable rhythm was associated with a higher probability of good outcome (adjusted OR = 6.68; 95% CI: 4.19-10.66). The AUC was 0.775 for the spline model and 0.767 for the linear model, with no significant difference (p = 0.179); the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.764. In multiple imputation, each additional five minutes to ROSC was associated with a lower probability of good outcome (OR = 0.86; 95% CI: 0.77-0.97). Age showed a nonlinear association with neurological outcome, and flexible modeling improved model fit, although not discrimination. Shockable rhythm was the factor most strongly associated with good outcome.

title: Cardiothoracic Surgery Training Attrition (2014-2023): Predictors, Trends, and Delay-Adjusted Rates Across Traditional and Integrated Pathways.
authorString: Oturoko M, Nair R, Salami A, Hoover E, Reznik S, Heid CA, Sarkaria IS, Erkmen CP, Jessen M, Kernstine K.

journal.title: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery

abstractText: Resident attrition disrupts training pipelines and threatens cardiothoracic (CT) surgical workforce sustainability. This study quantifies national attrition rates and identifies predictors using trainee data from the Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC), while accounting for reporting delays. We analyzed de-identified records of 1,476 CT surgery residents entering ACGME-accredited programs from 2014 to 2023. Attrition was defined as departure before expected completion. Rates were stratified by year, gender, citizenship, and training pathway: integrated (TS-I) versus traditional (TS). Multivariable logistic regression, LASSO, Random Forest, and XGBoost with nested cross-validation were used to identify predictors. A parametric nowcasting model corrected for administrative reporting lag. The overall attrition rate was 3.9% (57/1,476), significantly higher in the TS-I than the TS pathway (7.0% vs. 2.6%, p<0.001). On multivariable logistic regression, the TS-I pathway was the strongest predictor (aOR 7.11, 95% CI 3.16-16.01, p<0.01). Age was also independently associated with attrition, with higher odds in both the 31-36 group (aOR 2.89, 95% CI 1.28-6.54, p=0.04) and the >36 group (aOR 6.05, 95% CI 1.87-19.62) compared with those ≤30 years. Gender and citizenship were not significant after adjustment. Model performance was consistent across methods (AUC 0.67-0.72). Delay-adjusted analyses corrected an apparent decline in recent cohorts, revealing a stable underlying rate with a 3-4-year reporting lag. Training pathways are the strongest predictor of CT resident attrition, with TS-I trainees at markedly higher risk. Correcting reporting delays is critical for accurate workforce planning. These findings support targeted retention interventions for at-risk trainees.

title: The Right Ventricle in Focus: State-of-the-Art CMR Imaging - Challenges, Standards, and Innovations.
authorString: Gunasekaran S, Thornton GD, Kwan AC, Li H, Roujol S, Greil FG, Velthuis B, Bluemke DA.

journal.title: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance

abstractText: The right ventricle (RV) is recognized as a critical contributor to cardiovascular outcomes. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) has emerged as the reference standard for comprehensive RV assessment, enabling precise evaluation of ventricular volumes, function, flow, and tissue characterization. In this review, we provide a state-of-the-art overview of RV imaging using CMR. We first outline the anatomical and physiological features that distinguish the RV from the left ventricle. Next, we highlight the key technical challenges in imaging the RV, notably its complex geometry, prominent trabeculation, and thin myocardial wall. We then summarize current clinical CMR approaches, including cine imaging for volumetric assessment, phase-contrast techniques for flow quantification, and methods for tissue characterization such as late gadolinium enhancement. Additionally, we discuss advanced and emerging CMR techniques aimed at overcoming current RV imaging limitations, including high-resolution three-dimensional cine imaging, four-dimensional flow imaging, parametric mapping, and novel reconstruction strategies. These innovations hold promise for improving accuracy, reproducibility, and mechanistic insight into RV structure and function. Finally, we review the clinical role of CMR in major RV pathologies, including congenital heart disease, pulmonary hypertension, arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy, and tricuspid regurgitation. Across these conditions, CMR provides vital diagnostic and prognostic information, with growing evidence supporting its role in guiding clinical management. As technical advancements continue and standardization improves, CMR is poised to transform RV evaluation from a historically challenging endeavor into a precise and impactful component of cardiovascular care.

title: Developmental exposure to PBDE-47 induces sex- and organ-specific glucose uptake alterations linked to thyroid hormone disruption in rats: phenotypic parallels to early cardiorenal-metabolic crosstalk.
authorString: Wei H, Wen S, Tan B, Qiu X, Li P, Li J, Xia T, Wang A, Gao H, Zhang S.
abstractText: 2, 2', 4, 4'-Tetrabromodiphenyl ether (PBDE-47) is a ubiquitous persistent organic pollutant with developmental toxicity and thyroid-disrupting activity. Increasing evidence links PBDE-47 exposure to metabolic disorders, yet it remains unclear whether developmental PBDE-47 exposure disturbs glucose metabolism in multiple organs of offspring and how thyroid hormone (TH) changes relate to such effects. Using a rat model of perinatal PBDE-47 exposure, organ-specific glucose metabolism were assessed via positron emission tomography with the 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) tracer. Adult male offspring exhibited increased FDG uptake in the heart but decreased uptake in the brain and kidneys, whereas female offspring showed elevated uptake in the brain and kidneys and reduced cardiac FDG uptake. These changes were accompanied by sex-specific TH alterations, with increased T3 in males and decreased T3 and T4 in females. Correlation analyses revealed significant associations between TH levels and organ-specific FDG uptake. Intriguingly, these coordinated metabolic and endocrine disruptions exhibited early phenotypic parallels to features of the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) framework. Network toxicology identified 89 core targets, with PIK3CB, PIK3R1, PIK3R2, PLCG1, and PLCG2 as hub molecules enriched in apoptosis, endocrine signaling, insulin resistance, and central carbon metabolism pathways. Molecular docking suggested high-affinity binding of PBDE-47 to these targets, and gene set analysis further implicated PI3K/AKT, insulin receptor signaling, and the AGE-RAGE pathway. Collectively, this study suggests that perinatal PBDE-47 exposure elicits sex-specific multi-organ alterations in FDG uptake that correlate with TH disruption, providing a hypothesis-generating basis for developmental metabolic toxicity and highlighting phenotypic parallels to early cardiorenal-metabolic crosstalk.

title: A 2026 update on the epidemiology of obesity, related cardio-kidney-liver metabolic complications and beyond; a call to action.
authorString: Boutari C, Mantzoros CS.
abstractText: Obesity has become a major global public health challenge and is associated with an increasing burden of metabolic and non-metabolic comorbidities. We aimed to provide an updated assessment of the global prevalence of overweight and obesity and to examine temporal trends in selected associated with excess adiposity. Data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) Study were analyzed to estimate the prevalence of overweight and obesity among adults aged ≥20 years in 2023, stratified by sex and age group. We additionally examined age-standardized global prevalence trends for obesity and selected diseases associated with excess adiposity, including type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), cardiovascular disease (CVD), along with other chronic diseases associated with excess adiposity, such as dementias and obesity-related cancers, over 2000-2023.In 2023, the prevalence of overweight was generally higher in men, whereas obesity was more prevalent among women, particularly during middle age. Both overweight and obesity increased from early adulthood, peaked during middle age, and subsequently declined at older ages. Globally, obesity prevalence increased by approximately 95% between 2000 and 2023, reaching 19.5% in 2023. During the same period, the age-standardized prevalence of MASLD, T2DM, CKD, dementias, and obesity-related cancers increased. In contrast, age-standardized CVD prevalence decreased slightly and the divergent trends between obesity and age-standardized CVD prevalence highlight the multifactorial nature of cardiovascular risk and the potential impact of improvements in other cardiovascular risk factors. These findings underscore the urgent need for integrated, population-level strategies to prevent and effectively manage obesity and its complications.

title: The BCAA Paradox: From Anabolic Nutrients to Metabolic Signals in Insulin Resistance.
authorString: Magnan C, Alcaire C, Moro C, Andreelli F.
abstractText: Branched-chain amino acids (BCAA), including leucine, isoleucine and valine, play a key role in human metabolism. As regulators of protein synthesis, nutrient signaling and metabolic homeostasis, they are widely used in sports nutrition and clinical practice because of their anabolic properties and ability to enhance muscle protein synthesis. Paradoxically, however, elevated circulating BCAA concentrations are consistently associated with insulin resistance (IR), type 2 diabetes, overfeeding and obesity in humans, while preclinical studies suggest that chronic BCAA excess can contribute to IR, particularly in the context of overfeeding. Conversely, metabolic benefits observed following dietary BCAA restriction or pharmacological enhancement of BCAA catabolism have raised interest in this pathway as a potential therapeutic target. Yet, tissue-specific genetic models demonstrate that lowering circulating BCAA concentrations alone is not sufficient to improve insulin sensitivity, while human studies provide limited evidence for consistent effects of BCAA manipulation on insulin sensitivity or appetite regulation. Collectively, these findings suggest that BCAA and their downstream metabolites should not be considered merely as circulating biomarkers or metabolic substrates, but as components of a tissue-specific metabolic network coordinating nutrient sensing, mitochondrial metabolism and inter-organ communication.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted, Electrocardiogram-Derived, Sequential Rule-Based Decision Tree for Exclusion of Acute Coronary Syndrome as the Etiology of Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Choi A, Yoon H, Won Lee SG, Park C, Han E, Roh YH, Kim JH.
abstractText: After out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) with return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), deciding which patients without ST-segment elevation warrant emergency coronary angiography is difficult, as standard electrocardiogram (ECG), troponin, and echocardiography are limited in the early post-arrest window. We aimed to develop a sequential rule-based decision tree to identify post-ROSC patients in whom acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is unlikely to be the arrest etiology. In this single-center retrospective study, adult patients with OHCA were divided into development (2020-2024; n=329) and temporal validation (2025; n=71) cohorts. Post-ROSC 12-lead ECGs were analyzed by a deep-learning platform generating ten digital biomarkers. Five candidate biomarkers were combined into a rhythm-stratified sequential decision tree under a zero false-negative constraint; its performance was compared with that of individual biomarkers and validated in the temporal cohort. The tree classified 171/329 (52.0%) and 32/71 (45.1%) patients in the development and validation cohorts, respectively, as "ACS not likely," with no adjudicated ACS case misclassified at any node. Yield concentrated in the non-shockable subgroup, in which the model excluded 169/261 (64.8%) non-ACS cases (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC], 0.824), outperforming each individual biomarker. In the shockable subgroup, which carries a high pretest probability of ACS, 38/40 patients (95.0%) were retained as "ACS not excluded." A rhythm-stratified, rule-based decision tree combining AI-assisted ECG-derived biomarkers classified approximately half of post-OHCA patients as "ACS not likely" with no adjudicated ACS case misclassified, principally in the non-shockable subgroup. This transparent, bedside-deployable framework warrants prospective multicenter evaluation.

title: Ventilation Monitoring in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Care.
authorString: Aufderheide TP, Colella MR, Weston BW, Labinski J, Mattrisch L, Jasti J, Pirrallo RG, Szabo A, Chunara F, Sebastian PS, Engel TW, Chinn M, Lenz T, Liu JM, Mausner K, Monti CE, Gottula AL, Kosmopoulos M, Kalra R, Bartos JA, Yannopoulos D, Grawey T.
abstractText: Adherence to American Heart Association (AHA) ventilation guidelines during cardiac arrest is challenging. Prospective, Before/After quality assurance study determining adherence to AHA ventilation guidelines in adults with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest treated by Milwaukee County Emergency Medical Services and Kenosha Fire in Wisconsin using (Before) end tidal carbon dioxide [ETCO2] to monitor ventilations - Real BVM Help® applied but blinded versus (After) Real BVM Help®. mean per-person proportion (%) of ventilations in-target for rate, tidal volume, and both rate and tidal volume. AHA 2020 guidelines were followed. From 9/29/22-12/22/23, 278 patients were entered (148 Before/130 After). Average age: 62.3±16.7 years; 185 (67%) male. Mean per-person proportion (%) of ventilations in Before/After Groups in-target for rate (47.7±25.1% vs 74.4±24.1% respectively, p<0.0001), tidal volume (15.3±15.4% vs 45.4±23.8% respectively, p<0.0001), and rate and tidal volume (7.5±9.6% vs 39.0±23.3% respectively, p<0.0001) were significantly higher in the After Group. In the Before Group, using ETCO2 to monitor all ventilations (N=22,037 ventilations), only 43.8% were in-target for rate, 13.5% in-target for tidal volume, and 6.8% in-target for rate and tidal volume with a lower-than-target tidal volume delivered in 58.2% of all ventilations. Real BVM Help® was associated with statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in adherence to AHA ventilation guidelines. ETCO2 monitoring failed to approach both rate and tidal volume guideline adherence with a lower-than-target tidal volume being the most common parameter delivered out-of-target (58.2%). Ventilation rate and tidal volume monitoring with real-time feedback should be considered during treatment of cardiac arrest.

title: Early Identification of Recurrent Out-of-hospital Cardiac Arrest Using Clinical ECG Features.
authorString: To D, Coult J, Mohamed I, Bhandari S, Sayre M, Kusztos A, Kudenchuk P, Counts C, Rea T, Liang C, Johnson N.
abstractText: Recurrent cardiac arrest (rearrest) after initial return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) is associated with relatively poor outcomes. Early identification of rearrest might allow for intervention to prevent rearrest. In this study, we sought to determine whether clinical ECG features can predict rearrest. We performed a retrospective cohort study of adult out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients who achieved ROSC between 2018-2024. We evaluated the association of ECG features (QRS width, standard deviation of NN intervals, root mean square of successive NN interval differences, and percentage of NN intervals that differ by more than 50 milliseconds) within individual 15-second segments throughout a 5-minute window prior to rearrest as well as their temporal trends over the 5-minute analytic window. Of the 1,489 OHCA patients achieving ROSC, 1,298 were analyzed; 528 (40.7%) experienced rearrest. Rearrest patients were older, less likely to receive bystander CPR (48.7% vs. 61.9%), and had lower survival (20.4% vs. 43.1%) and favorable neurologic outcomes (7.8% vs. 21.2%; all p<0.001). We found lower heart rate, wider QRS, and higher HR variability in those with rearrest. Identification was highest 1 minute prior to rearrest (AUROC 0.74), declining beyond 3 minutes. Models using temporal trends achieved AUROC 0.67; strongest predictors were heart rate variability measures and QRS width. Established ECG features achieved good prediction for rearrest with identification improving closer to time of rearrest. Future work leveraging novel features or more advanced artificial intelligence models may further improve prediction.

title: Aging in cardio-oncology: Pathophysiology, clinical implications and future directions.
authorString: Madaudo C, Cannatà A, Corrado E, Di Lisi D, Rossetto L, Triolo OF, Cacciatore G, Bovo F, Fiore F, Attanasio U, Mercurio V, Galassi AR, Tocchetti CG, Iaccarino G, Novo G, Cuomo A.
abstractText: Population aging is changing the needs of patients seen in cardio-oncology. Older adults with cancer often have cardiovascular disease, multimorbidity, and reduced physiological reserve, which can complicate treatment and recovery. Patients of the same chronological age may differ considerably in cardiovascular health, functional capacity, and treatment tolerance. Frailty and geriatric assessment can help characterize these differences and inform care. This review examines the biological mechanisms linking aging, cancer, and cardiovascular disease and discusses their implications for cardiovascular risk assessment, cancer treatment decisions, and long-term survivorship. Treatment decisions require consideration of the expected oncological benefit, cardiovascular risk, physiological reserve, life expectancy, and patient preferences. Identifying and addressing reversible vulnerabilities may help patients tolerate effective anticancer therapy while preserving function and quality of life. During survivorship, cardiovascular care should account for previous treatment exposure, changing health status, and adherence to preventive therapies. Closer collaboration between cardio-oncology and geriatric medicine may improve the assessment and management of older patients. Evidence specific to frail and very old adults remains limited. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether geriatric and biological aging measures improve cardiovascular risk prediction, treatment decisions, and patient outcomes.

title: Dysnatremia in critically ill burn patients: incidence, timing and association with kidney outcomes.
authorString: Kociolek M, Bellas Z, Walter T, Alexandru C, Maxime C, Emmanuel D, Lucie G, Maïté C, Alexandre P, Chiheb BM, Puech P, Emanuel M, Uhel F, Benoit P, Benjamin D, François D, Louis B.
abstractText: Dysnatremia is common in critically ill patients and has been linked to poor outcomes and renal prognosis. Burn patients are particularly vulnerable, but the prognostic significance of dysnatremia in this population remains unclear. We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of 1,758 burn patients admitted to a French burn center between 2011 and 2023. Dysnatremia was defined as at least one episode of hyponatremia (<135 mmol/L) or hypernatremia (>145 mmol/L) during intensive care unit (ICU) stay. The primary endpoint was the incidence of dysnatremia; secondary endpoints included major adverse kidney events (MAKE) at ICU discharge and acute kidney injury (AKI) occurrence and severity. Dysnatremia occurred in 56.3% of patients (n = 990), with hyponatremia in 50.5% (n = 888) and hypernatremia in 23.8% (n = 418). MAKE at ICU discharge did not differ between hyponatremic and normonatremic patients (12.6% vs. 10.9%, p = 0.304) but was sixfold higher with hypernatremia (32.3% vs. 5.4%, p < 0.001). After adjustment for age and burned total body surface area, hypernatremia was independently associated with MAKE at ICU discharge (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 4.03; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.92-5.56; p < 0.001), whereas hyponatremia was not (aHR 1.15; 95% CI: 0.85-1.55; p = 0.377). Clustering analysis identified three phenotypes: Cluster B (severe burns, worst outcomes), Cluster A (older patients, mostly hyponatremic, intermediate outcomes), and Cluster C (younger patients, mild burns, best outcomes). Dysnatremia affects over half of burn patients. Sodium disturbances should be viewed as markers of systemic severity, warranting close monitoring and preventive strategies.

title: Chronic Neurotoxicity of Di-2-ethylhexyl phthalate (DEHP) at no observed adverse effects level (NOAEL) doses on adult zebrafish links to Neuro-behavioral disorder.
authorString: Dong G, Li W, Yuan Z, Zhou H, Huang Y, Li Y, Hu K, Lv J, Ni T, Ma L, Shi Y.
abstractText: Di-2-ethylhexyl phthalate (DEHP), as the most common member of phthalic acid esters (PAEs), is considered an endocrine-disrupting compound (EDC) and causes prominent developmental, reproductive toxicity, metabolic dysfunctions, and neurotoxicity. However, the potential neurotoxicity associated with chronic DEHP exposure at concentrations below the no-observed-adverse-effect level (NOAEL) in adult zebrafish remains poorly understood, largely due to a lack of experimental evidence from animal studies. Thus, to comprehensively characterize the potential neurological effects of DEHP, adult zebrafish were used as an animal model to evaluate neurotoxicity following 4 weeks of exposure to DEHP at concentrations within the NOAEL range (5, 50, and 200 mg/L). Behavioral assessments included the light-dark preference test, novel tank diving test, novel object exploration test, social interactions test, and conditioned place preference (CPP) test. After 4 weeks of chronic exposure to DEHP, zebrafish exhibited marked neurobehavioral alterations, including increased time spent and distance traveled in the dark zone and reduced exploratory behavior in unfamiliar environments (reduced exploration of the top zone in the novel tank and of the novel object zone); DEHP exposure also disrupted social interactions and impaired learning and memory in zebrafish. The LC-MS/MS results revealed that changes in neuro-behavioral profiles were closely associated with neurotransmitter levels in the brain of zebrafish. The present study provides a valuable reference for drawing attention to the assessment of DEHP neurotoxicity under the NOAEL.

title: Restraining cAMP signaling via EPAC2 allosteric modulation: Conformational transitions and dynamic residue network analysis.
authorString: Qureshi U, Habib A, Uddin R, Nur-E-Alam M, Ul-Haq Z.
abstractText: Exchange Protein Activated by cAMP (EPAC) is a key cAMP-responsive signaling protein that regulates intracellular processes through activation of Rap-family small GTPases and plays important roles in cellular proliferation, metabolism, inflammation, and cardiovascular and neurological functions. Dysregulated EPAC signaling has been implicated in several pathological conditions, including metabolic disorders, cardiovascular diseases, cancer, and neurological dysfunction, making EPAC an increasingly attractive therapeutic target. EPAC2, one of the two major EPAC isoforms, is characterized by its distinct multi-domain architecture and its ability to switch its conformational state upon binding an analogue of cAMP. This conformational plasticity makes EPAC particularly attractive for allosteric inhibition. Drugs targeting EPACs' regulatory mechanisms, including their modulation with RAP-like proteins and associated pathologies, have therefore gained increasing attention. In this context, allosteric inhibitors represent a promising strategy for controlling EPAC activity without directly competing for cAMP binding. Here, we utilize an extensive 1.2 μs atomistic molecular dynamics simulation ensemble to elucidate the structural thermodynamics governing the transitions between the auto-inhibited (closed) and catalytically competent (open) states of EPAC2, specifically focusing on the mechanism of the natural allosteric inhibitor dimethylocta-dienyl methoxy flavone (AAD026). While the exogenous activator, Sp-cAMP, narrows conformational variance (43.5% captured by PC1 alone) to prime the protein for structural opening, the reference inhibitor ESI-05 achieves inhibition purely via localized suppression confined to the cyclic nucleotide-binding domain (cNBD-B) and adjacent hinge regions. In contrast, AAD026 acts as a genuine conformational reverser, broadening structural heterogeneity across a diverse, inactive-like free-energy landscape (Silhouette score 0.69). K- means clustering analysis and dynamic residue network analysis revealed similar regions of intra-protein communications and identified several motifs that specifically mediate the inhibitor-driven reversion of the open conformation. This global change is driven by a prominent topological reachability (ΔLi) spike localized at the cNBD-B lid region, which effectively re-sequesters the catalytic residue Arg886 back into the functional ionic latch (IL). Our findings provide quantitative, network-level evidence that allosteric inhibition can extend beyond simple binding-site obstruction, operating via an active, state-reverting mechanism that overrides active ensembles even in the presence of triggering ligands.

title: Informal caregiving and unmet social needs among U.S. adults at risk of cardiovascular disease.
authorString: Mahmood A.
abstractText: Unmet social needs, such as food insecurity, housing instability, and transportation barriers, are key risk factors for cardiovascular disease (CVD). However, little is known about their prevalence and consequences among informal caregivers at elevated risk of future CVD. This study investigates associations between informal caregiving and unmet social needs among adults at increased risk of future CVD. Pooled, nationally representative, cross-sectional data were analyzed for a sample of 7,215 noninstitutionalized U.S. adults (ages ≥18 years) with ≥one major CVD risk factor (hypertension, diabetes, obesity, or current smoking) and without a known cardiovascular disease. Data were drawn from the 6th (HINTS6, 2022) and 7th (HINTS7, 2024) iterations of the Health Information National Trends Survey (HINTS). Adjusted logistic regressions were fit to estimate marginal predicted probabilities (MPPs) and absolute risk differences (ARDs) for unmet social needs by informal caregiving status. Complex design features of HINTS and jackknife replicate weights were incorporated into analyses to generate robust population-level estimates. Among adults at risk of CVD, 17.6% were informal caregivers. Compared to non-caregivers, caregivers had higher probabilities of food insecurity, including cutting or skipping meals (MPPs: 23.8% vs. 14.1%; ARD: 9.7 percentage points [PPs]) and inability to afford balanced meals (MPPs: 24.9% vs. 15.0%; ARD: 9.9 PPs). Housing instability was also more prevalent among caregivers (MPPs: 18.5% vs. 12.9%; ARD: 5.6 PPs). The findings indicate that informal caregiving was associated with a disproportionate burden of unmet social needs among adults at risk of future CVD. Incorporating caregiver-inclusive screening of social needs and care navigation into preventive care models could support caregiver health and contribute to long-term CVD risk reduction.

title: A sex-specific platelet switch controls anti-tumor immunity in glioblastoma.
authorString: Sloan AR, Bukenya G, Tannish GP, Silver DJ, Aggarwal A, Lee J, Rosoff D, Alban TJ, Juric I, Parsai S, Baruah V, Bodovetz T, Whitfield D, Tack L, Navadgi T, Reitz N, Ho ST, Badani A, Goldberg J, Yuan X, Gaboriau A, Kamatala S, Coker J, Kumar VS, Jain SS, Xu C, Scalise A, Rajasekar B, Vincenti A, Mulkearns-Hubert EE, Horbinski CM, Sloan AE, Hubert CG, Luo J, Rubin JB, Stavrou EX, Lohoff FW, Goodman WA, Miller TE, O'Connor CM, Nieman MT, Sangwan N, Chan TA, Khorana AA, Dhawan A, Cameron SJ, Lathia JD.
abstractText: Sex differences in glioblastoma (GBM) outcomes are shaped by biological, hormonal, and immune factors, but the mechanisms driving these disparities remain unclear. We identify platelet protease-activated receptor 4 (PAR4) signaling as a regulator of sex-specific anti-tumor immunity. GBM patients exhibit increased platelet reactivity driven by PAR4. In murine models, pharmacologic or genetic inhibition of PAR4 prolongs survival in females, but not males, and is estrogen dependent, persisting in hormonal females regardless of chromosomal sex. The survival advantage is mediated within the tumor microenvironment through enhanced CD8+ T cell infiltration and function. PAR4-activated platelets suppress CD8+ T cell activity, whereas CD8+ T cell depletion abolishes both tumor-induced platelet reactivity and the PAR4-dependent survival advantage. Mechanistically, PAR4 inhibition enhances CD8+ T cell signaling through interaction with estrogen receptor β (ERβ). These findings demonstrate that platelets are critical regulators of sex-specific anti-tumor immunity and identify PAR4 as a promising therapeutic target in cancer.

title: The Role of Physical Preparation in Motorsport Athletes Across Different Vehicle Types: A Narrative Review.
authorString: Vieira Barros G, Ramos A, Facchini M, Mulatinho C, Zacca R, Afonso J.

journal.title: International journal of sports physiology and performance

abstractText: Despite motorsport's widespread appeal, early performance models did not consider drivers as athletes, and even drivers often struggled with this classification, which historically contributed to their exclusion from research focused on athletic performance. Slowly but steadily, this paradigm has been changing. To review the evolution of physical conditioning in land-based motorsports and to examine the specific physiological and physical demands imposed on drivers by different vehicle types. A narrative review was conducted to synthesize historical perspectives, physiological demands, and training approaches in motorsport. Peer-reviewed studies, practical reports, opinion articles, and relevant online materials were analyzed to describe the evolution of the physical conditioning required across racing categories. The physical demands in motorsports are characterized by sustained cardiovascular strain, significant neuromuscular loading, large and sustained G-force exposure, and pronounced thermal stress. These demands vary according to vehicle type. Closed-wheel drivers are particularly exposed to prolonged heat stress and require comprehensive muscular endurance and thermoregulatory adaptation. Open-wheel drivers experience large G-forces, demanding exceptional neck and lower-limb strength. Two-wheel riders require enhanced handgrip strength, dynamic neuromuscular control, and high levels of aerobic capacity. Tailored conditioning programs addressing the distinct physiological, neuromuscular, and thermoregulatory demands of each motorsport category are closely linked to performance and safety. Further systematic evaluation of the empirical evidence is necessary to enhance the ecological validity of training recommendations and strengthen their application in competitive motorsport.

title: Subject-independent framework for protocol-defined stress task classification using multimodal physiological signals.
authorString: Kumar A, Ansari IA, Singh SN.
abstractText: Prolonged stress can cause cardiovascular disease, depression, and anxiety. Reliable detection is therefore important. Existing studies using multimodal physiological methods have already reported accuracy, up to 99.7% however, two important aspects remain underexplored. First, most studies separate stress only from a neutral baseline, amusement, and different workload levels. Second, subject-independent performance remains limited because most studies evaluate their models using subject-dependent data splits that are prone to data leakage. This proposed study tries to address these gaps. Protocol-defined stress tasks are detected from everyday activities, not from any workload levels. The proposed model, a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN), is evaluated subject independently using leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) cross-validation. This proposed study was conducted on the GalaxyPPG dataset. The dataset includes ECG, PPG, and BVP signals. This enables multimodal fusion for stress detection during everyday activities. Single modalities achieve mean test accuracies of 62.19% for PPG, 67.74% for BVP, and 47.81% for ECG on LOSO. Fusion (ECG+PPG+BVP) achieves the mean test accuracy on LOSO evaluation, 76.47% }14.60%. To the best of the author's knowledge, this modality's combination (ECG+PPG+BVP) has not been explored in the literature for GalaxyPPG dataset.

title: Open-loop system identification of an AC motor-driven arterial flow generation platform: vessel-specific models and a parsimonious common ARX model.
authorString: Serdar Y, Yildiz H, Akay C, Kaysi F, Sedef H.
abstractText: Accurate reproduction of arterial flow waveforms is important for in vitro cardiovascular experiments and controlled biomedical flow platforms. This study characterizes the open-loop dynamics of an AC motor-inverter-centrifugal-pump platform using five experimentally recorded input-output datasets representing femoral, carotid, iliac, coronary, and aortic waveform conditions. The inverter command was the input, the magnetic flow-meter voltage was the output, and all original recordings were sampled at 100 Hz.Vessel-specific FIR, ARX, and ridge-regularized ARX models were screened separately. A common model was selected using nested chronological validation and assessed on untouched test segments using one-step prediction, recursive free-run simulation, and diagnostic analyses.Vessel-specific one-step validation fits ranged from 80.33% to 92.80%. The common ARX(5,4,80) model achieved mean one-step and free-run fits of 95.82% and 80.04%, respectively. All poles were inside the unit circle, but significant residual autocorrelation showed that the measured response was not fully explained. The common model provides a compact nominal representation of the tested platform. Its comparison with vessel-specific models is descriptive because it uses more training data, and cycle consistency within a recording does not establish between-session experimental reproducibility.

title: Serum Profiles of Pembrolizumab, Cardiac Troponin T, and Interleukin-6 in a Plasma Exchange-Treated Patient With Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Related Myocarditis.
authorString: Narita K, Suzuki S, Kuwahara K, Naito T.
abstractText: A 77-year-old female patient with renal cell carcinoma, treated with intravenous pembrolizumab, developed pembrolizumab-related myocarditis accompanied by myasthenia gravis. For myasthenia gravis-related symptoms, intravenous methylprednisolone was administered on days 24-26 and 29-31 after the administration of 200 mg of pembrolizumab, and plasma exchange (PE) therapy was conducted on days 24, 26, 28, and 30. Serum pembrolizumab levels were monitored in conjunction with serum markers of myocarditis and interleukin-6 (IL-6) in the present patient treated with PE. An elevated serum cardiac troponin T (cTnT) level of 0.542 ng/mL was observed 24 days after the first administration, and the serum pembrolizumab level was 15.7 µg/mL. After the first PE session, the serum levels of cTnT and IL-6 on day 25 were 0.406 ng/mL and 27.9 pg/mL, respectively, in conjunction with a decline of the serum pembrolizumab level to 4.83 µg/mL. Although the patient had a decreased serum pembrolizumab level of 3.86 µg/mL on day 29, the serum cTnT and IL-6 levels had increased to 0.843 ng/mL and 40.6 pg/mL, respectively. After the fourth PE session, serum levels of pembrolizumab, cTnT, and IL-6 on day 31 decreased to 3.62 µg/mL, 0.381 ng/mL, and 10.1 pg/mL, respectively. The overall removal rate after 4 sessions of PE was 76.9%, after which myasthenia gravis-related symptoms gradually disappeared. This patient with a serum pembrolizumab level within the previously reported range developed myocarditis accompanied by myasthenia gravis. PE therapy efficiently extracted circulating pembrolizumab and IL-6 in this patient with immune checkpoint inhibitor-related myocarditis.

title: Omnipolar Technology Near Field Versus Fragmentation Signals Mapping at Anatomically Defined Ganglionated Plexi Sites During Cardioneuroablation.
authorString: Jabbour JP, Bodin A, Raczka F, Pons M, Sportouch C, Clementy N.
abstractText: Cardioneuroablation (CNA) is an established catheter-based therapy for refractory vasovagal syncope (VVS), targeting atrial ganglionated plexi (GPs) by radiofrequency ablation. Omnipolar Technology Near Field (OTNF) is a novel automated spectral mapping algorithm integrated within the EnSite X system; its systematic comparison with fragmentation mapping during CNA has not previously been reported. To evaluate the feasibility, safety, and efficacy of a streamlined, imaging-free anatomically guided CNA approach and to compare real-time OTNF mapping at three spectral thresholds with fractionation analysis in detecting GPs at anatomically consistent locations. Twenty-six consecutive patients (mean age 43.9 ± 16.4 years; 69% female; ≥ 3 VVS episodes/year) were enrolled prospectively at two French centres. All procedures used an HD Grid catheter for bilateral OTNF and fractionation mapping, followed by sequential ablation of five GP sites. Acute success was defined as heart rate increase > 50% from baseline and blunted atropine response (< 25% increment). Directional discordance between fractionation and OTNF map was assessed by McNemar's exact test. Acute procedural success was achieved in 22 out of 26 patients (84.6%), with no complications. Mean procedure time was 95.2 ± 20.5 min. CNA produced significant vagal denervation: heart rate increased from 60.2 ± 12.9 to 88.1 ± 18.2 bpm (p < 0.003), AH interval shortened from 97.6 ± 22.9 to 78.2 ± 21.7 ms (p = 0.007), Wenckebach cycle length decreased from 441.5 ± 118.9 to 330.0 ms (p < 0.003) and SNRT decreased from 1235.0 ± 273.7 to 1028.4 ± 235.1 ms (p = 0.003). At 400 Hz, OTNF showed significantly higher signal positivity than fractionation mapping at the LSGP (concordance 57.7%) and RIGP (concordance 65.4%). At 500 and 600 Hz, no directional asymmetry was detected while concordance remained below 70% at these sites. At a median follow-up of 20.2 ± 7.6 months, 81% of patients were free from syncope. A simplified, anatomical CNA approach is safe, feasible, and effective. OTNF and fragmentation signals mapping shows modest concordance at five anatomically consistent GP locations, confirming that those strategies capture partially non-overlapping electrophysiological information.

title: T-cell states in aortic dissection: from molecular immune profiling toward causal and translational validation.
authorString: Ye X, Wang Y, Li Y, Zhu H, Li X, Song J.
abstractText:
Background/objectives

Single-cell RNA sequencing and T-cell receptor profiling reveal substantial T-cell heterogeneity in aortic dissection (AD), but whether these responses contribute to vascular injury or reflect post-onset immune activation remains uncertain. This review evaluates human and experimental evidence by disease stage, tissue compartment, functional validation, T-cell specificity, and intervention timing, distinguishing descriptive profiling from evidence supporting causal and translational inference.

Discussion

Human studies identify Th1/Th17-associated, CD8+ cytotoxicity-associated, and regulatory T-cell alterations, with stage-related differences in T-cell composition and clonality. Most evidence is cross-sectional and obtained after clinical onset. Antigen specificity, direct aortic-wall cytotoxicity, impaired Treg suppression, and T-cell-mediated aortic-wall injury remain unproven. Single-cell and TCR profiling identify candidate T-cell states and clonotypes for spatial and functional validation, not causal proof. Among candidate pathways, the IL-6-STAT3-IL-17 axis currently has the strongest AD-specific preclinical rationale, but existing interventions are largely non-T-cell-restricted and initiated before or during disease induction. Stronger causal attribution requires convergent human evidence, post-lesion T-cell-restricted perturbation, disease-progression endpoints, and rescue or target-engagement studies. The subacute phase after anatomical and haemodynamic stabilisation may offer a window to study persistent injury-amplifying T-cell responses, whereas early acute and perioperative immunomodulation remains unsupported.

Conclusions

Current evidence supports altered T-cell states after AD onset but does not establish an initiating role. Near-term priorities should be prospective biomarker validation and post-lesion mechanistic studies rather than T-cell-directed immuno-modulation during the early acute and perioperative phases. Clinical translation should await reproducible associations linked to stage-specific causal mechanisms and acceptable safety.

title: Medication background of Japanese men undergoing prostate needle biopsy: A medication profile based on the number of medications and drug classes.
authorString: Sato K, Kawahara T, Hashizume A, Yamazaki M, Ito H, Takeshima T, Kuroda S, Uemura H, Makiyama K, Teranishi JI.
abstractText: Prostate cancer is common in older men, and the treatment decision depends strongly on the patient's general condition and comorbidities. However, the medication background of men who reach prostate biopsy has rarely been described. We used a large Japanese administrative claims database (Medical Data Vision) to profile the medications of men who underwent prostate needle biopsy between April 2008 and June 2019. We examined the number of medications and the drug classes in relation to body mass index (BMI) and age. We identified 67,812 men, all aged 60 years or older. The mean number of medications was lowest at BMI 20-25 and increased toward both low and high BMI, showing a U-shaped pattern (minimum 1.44 drugs at BMI 22.0-22.5); the increase was driven mainly by high BMI. This pattern was consistent across age strata, and in a negative binomial regression adjusted for age the quadratic term of BMI remained significant (p < 0.001), with an adjusted minimum at BMI 20.5. The composition of drug classes differed by body size: metabolic drugs (antihypertensive/cardiovascular, dyslipidemia, diabetes, and hyperuricemia drugs) were more common at high BMI, whereas gastrointestinal and analgesic drugs were relatively more common at low BMI, and all classes increased with age. In conclusion, among men undergoing prostate biopsy, the number of medications was lowest at BMI 20-25 and the qualitative medication profile differed by BMI. These findings describe the medication background of this population and may inform the design of future risk-stratified or prospective studies.

title: Effect of heart rate on hemodynamics in patient-specific intracranial aneurysms: An in vitro study.
authorString: El-Khader BAT, Shirdade N, Korte J, Behme D, Berg P, Church EW, Brindise MC.
abstractText: The rupture of an intracranial aneurysm (IA) has been linked to local hemodynamic environments, but it remains unclear how transient physiological states such as elevated heart rate modulate those environments, and whether different aneurysm geometries respond similarly. Here, we used volumetric particle tracking velocimetry (PTV) to measure 3D velocity fields in two patient-specific IA phantoms, a right middle cerebral artery (MCA) aneurysm and a left vertebral artery (LVA) aneurysm, under three heart rates representative of rest (60 bpm), active movement (100 bpm), and exercise (137 bpm). From these measurements, we quantified coherent structures, turbulent kinetic energy (TKE), wall shear stress (WSS), and oscillatory shear index (OSI). Increasing heart rate did not simply increase peak inflow; it altered the temporal organization of the flow. In the MCA aneurysm, higher heart rates produced a stronger, more anchored intra-saccular vortex and elevated coherent-structure strength and TKE that persisted into mid- and end-diastole, along with broader spatial coverage of elevated WSS that remained high beyond peak systole. The LVA aneurysm exhibited a more muted response, with minimal changes in streamline topology and WSS across heart rates. These results show that heart rate can drive prolonged high-shear, high-energy loading within the cardiac cycle, but that this amplification is morphology-dependent and non-monotonic rather than universal.

title: Prevalence and factors associated with excessive daytime somnolence in adults with HIV - A single-centre UK observational study.
authorString: Read AT, Saigal A, Hossain-Ibrahim SZ, Cheung CM, Xiao S, Smith C, Johnson MA, Lipman MCI, Jaffer A, Mandal S.
abstractText: IntroductionExcessive daytime somnolence is common in people with HIV. The importance of possible contributors such as mental health and obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome is poorly understood. We investigated the prevalence of daytime somnolence and obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome in people with HIV in the UK and assessed what factors were associated with somnolence.MethodsIn this cross-sectional study, adults with HIV attending Royal Free London HIV outpatient service appointments were recruited between May 2018 to October 2019. Participants completed questionnaires as outpatients assessing somnolence, sleep quality, fatigue, mental health symptoms and quality of life. Binary logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with excessive daytime somnolence (defined as Epworth Sleepiness Scale scores >10/24), and prevalence of somnolence and obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome were calculated with 95% confidence intervals.Results313 adults (median age 52 years, body mass index (BMI) 25.9 kg/m2, and 80% male) participated. The excessive daytime somnolence prevalence was 72/313 (23%, 95% CI: 18.5-28.1). Somnolent individuals had more frequent and more severe: anxiety, depression, fatigue and poor sleep quality, with more reported cardiovascular and respiratory disease (p < 0.01). Factors independently associated with excessive somnolence included male gender (OR 3.45; 1.36-8.95; p < 0.01), poor sleep quality (OR 1.12; 1.02-1.22; p = 0.01) and fatigue (OR 1.04; 1.01-1.06; p < 0.01). The minimum detected prevalence of obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome was 8.6% (n = 27/313) in the study population - which represented 54% (n = 27/50) of those participants who had a sleep study.ConclusionsExcessive daytime somnolence is common in people with HIV and frequently identified in individuals reporting poor mental health. Obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome is a potentially treatable contributor to daytime somnolence. Integrated screening for somnolence, sleep disorders and mental health within routine HIV care may improve identification and treatment of common, modifiable and interacting comorbidities.

title: Mesenchymal stem cells inhibit ferroptosis in dopaminergic neurons of Parkinson's disease mice by phosphorylating STAT6.
authorString: Wang X, Zhang M, Ding W, Wang Y, Fang L, Erasmus S, Xu Y, Zhang Y, Zhou L, Li L, Zou Z, Ye J.
abstractText: Ferroptosis is recognized as a critical driver of dopaminergic neuronal injury. Emerging evidence suggests that the neuroprotective effects of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells are partially mediated through signal transducer and activator of transcription 6 (STAT6) signaling. However, few studies have investigated whether bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells can modulate ferroptosis in dopaminergic neurons, and the specific regulatory role of STAT6 in neuronal ferroptosis remains poorly understood. We established an in vitro model of Parkinson's disease using SH-SY5Y cells treated with 1-methyl-4-phenyl-pyridinium and an in vivo model of Parkinson's disease using mice exposed to 1-methyl-4-phenyl- 1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine. Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells were administered via Transwell coculture in vitro and stereotactic brain injection in vivo. Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, transmission electron microscopy, and behavioral tests were used to evaluate neuronal protection and motor function recovery. We assessed phosphorylated STAT6 (p-STAT6), the active form of STAT6, as well as markers related to ferroptosis, iron metabolism, and oxidative stress. Interventions with interleukin-4, AS1517499, and Cas9-mediated STAT6 knockout were performed to verify the regulatory role of the STAT6/p-STAT6 signaling pathway. Laser confocal microscopy was used to analyze the subcellular distribution of p-STAT6 and further elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells-mediated neuroprotection in Parkinson's disease. Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells increased tyrosine hydroxylase expression in dopaminergic neurons and alleviated motor dysfunction in a mouse model of Parkinson's disease. Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells promoted p-STAT6 phosphorylation at Tyr641. Nuclear-cytoplasmic fractionation assays showed that bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells restored nuclear p-STAT6 levels, while confocal microscopy confirmed the nuclear translocation of p-STAT6. Activated p-STAT6 stimulated the SLC7A11-GPX4 antioxidant pathway and restored reduced glutathione levels. Meanwhile, bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells downregulated DMT1 expression, thereby reducing intracellular iron accumulation, reactive oxygen species production, and lipid peroxidation. Interleukin-4 recapitulated the anti-ferroptotic effects of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells, whereas AS1517499 abolished their neuroprotective effects. STAT6 knockout eliminated the ability of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells to inhibit neuronal ferroptosis. This study demonstrates that bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells induce p-STAT6 phosphorylation at Tyr641 and facilitate its nuclear translocation. Activated p-STAT6 alleviates iron overload and lipid peroxidation by regulating SLC7A11-GPX4 and DMT1. Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells activate the STAT6 pathway to inhibit neuronal ferroptosis, increase tyrosine hydroxylase expression, and improve Parkinson's disease-related pathological changes and motor deficits.

title: Cross-Domain Slow Wave Sleep Detection from Single-Lead EEG in Pediatric Congenital Heart Disease Recovery.
authorString: Jiang Y, Zhang J, Xiao Z, Fan P, Wang X, Shi S, Wang H, Han K, Lu J, Li J, Shen B, Liu C.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: IEEE Trans Neural Syst Rehabil Eng
journal.title: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
journal.isoabbreviation: IEEE Trans Neural Syst Rehabil Eng

abstractText: Slow wave sleep (SWS) is vital for neural recovery and cardiovascular stability in children following congenital heart disease (CHD) surgery. However, pediatric CHD sleep patterns are often disrupted by clinical stressors and exhibit substantial domain discrepancies relative to adult data distributions. To address these challenges, this study establishes the Pediatric Cardiac Post-surgical Sleep (PCPS) dataset, a self-collected and expert-annotated pediatric polysomnography (PSG) dataset specifically targeting the early post-CHD surgical period. We further propose PCPS-SleepNet, an end-to-end deep learning framework for cross-domain sleep staging from single-lead EEG, enabling effective knowledge transfer from public sleep data to pediatric post-surgical CHD data. The architecture employs a multi-band input representation across six sub-bands and leverages a Four-Stage Progressive Encoder integrating Multi-Scale Depthwise Convolution (MSDC) for local features, self-attention for global density modeling, and a Conformer block for hybrid refinement. To mitigate limited pediatric data availability and domain shift, this network is pre-trained on public datasets and fine-tuned on the PCPS dataset. Subject-independent validation showed competitive performance, with an overall accuracy of 75.65 ± 0.58%, an AUROC of 89.06 ± 0.18%, an AUPRC of 83.49 ± 0.13%, and a macro F1-score of 76.68 ± 0.70%. For SWS detection, the model achieved an AUPRC of 87.89 ± 0.20% and an F1-score of 81.55 ± 0.74%. Architectural ablations and frequency-band input contribution analysis supported the model design and suggested the complementary discriminative value of slow-wave frequency-band inputs. These results suggest a practical and patient-friendly sleep detection solution for individualized sleep assessment and rehabilitation in vulnerable pediatric populations.

title: Vertical Sleeve Gastrectomy inhibits 11βHSD1 and subsequently reduces IL6 secretion in Mice and Humans: A Shared Anti-Inflammatory Mechanism.
authorString: Liang S, Samarasinghe S, Johnson B, Wang W, Durazzo ID, Tsou P, Riva A, Miras A, Akalestou E.
abstractText: Vertical sleeve gastrectomy (VSG) improves glycaemic control in type 2 diabetes (T2D) through mechanisms that extend beyond weight loss. The interaction between glucocorticoid metabolism and inflammation in this context remains unclear. We investigated the role of 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1 (11βHSD1) in mediating the metabolic effects of VSG in humans and mice. Subcutaneous adipose tissue biopsies were collected before and 6 months after VSG. Parallel studies were conducted in lean and high-fat diet-fed mice undergoing VSG or sham surgery, alongside 11βHSD1 knockout models. Glucose tolerance and expression of 11βHSD1 and interleukin-6 (IL6) were assessed. VSG reduced 11βHSD1 and IL6 expression in human adipose tissue and improved insulin resistance. In lean mice, VSG reduced adipose Hsd11b1 and Il6 expression and altered glucose handling in the absence of detectable changes in total body weight. 11βHSD1 knockout mice exhibited improved glucose tolerance despite increased body weight, partially recapitulating the VSG phenotype. Both interventions reduced circulating and tissue IL6 levels. These findings identify an association between reduced 11βHSD1, inflammatory signalling and metabolic adaptations following VSG, and support further investigation of 11βHSD1 as a potential contributor to the metabolic effects of surgery.

title: The Fibroblast Microenvironment on the Differentiation and Maturation of Stem Cell-Derived Cardiomyocytes.
authorString: Dong Y, Jiang H, Zhou F, Mu J.
abstractText: Cardiac fibroblasts (CFs) are a critical component of the myocardial microenvironment and play essential roles in the differentiation and maturation of stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (CMs). Accumulating evidence indicates that CFs shape a permissive microenvironment for CM lineage commitment, early expansion, and subsequent structural and functional maturation through the secretion of soluble factors, extracellular matrix remodeling, and contact-mediated interactions such as gap junctions. The CF microenvironment exerts stage-specific effects on differentiation efficiency, structural organization, electrophysiological properties, and metabolic maturation of CMs. This review summarizes the recent advances in understanding how the CF microenvironment regulates the differentiation and maturation of stem cell-derived CMs from a continuous developmental perspective and discusses current limitations and future directions in this field.Impact StatementThe core innovation of this review lies in its unique perspective on the influence of fibroblast microenvironment on the differentiation and maturation of stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes. This review has certain academic value.

title: Peripheral intravenous waveform analysis - a novel tool to confirm intravascular catheter placement.
authorString: Barajas MB, Riess ML, Lefevre RJ, Li Z, Baudenbacher FJ, Cooper BD, Eagle SS.

journal.title: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing

abstractText: Peripheral intravenous (IV) catheter infiltration is a common complication which can cause harmful extravasation of fluid and medications. Significant injury can occur before standard infusion pumps detect a threshold pressure. Peripheral IV waveform analysis (PIVA) uses fast Fourier transform (FFT) to measure the amplitude of the venous waveform. This study aims to evaluate if PIVA can differentiate between IV catheter positions, primarily intravenous versus subcutaneous, in a rat model. Surgical cutdown was performed on the right proximal saphenous vein. Pressure and waveforms were recorded from a 22G IV catheter open-to-air, in the vein, and in the adjacent subcutaneous (SC) tissue. Measurements were performed at baseline and after injection of 1 mL Plasmalyte and are reported as median (interquartile range). The peak amplitude corresponding to the heart rate frequency labeled as f1. Pre-flush intravascular f1, 0.0824 mmHg (IQR 0.0256, 0.1480), differed significantly from both SC, 0.0001 mmHg (0.0000, 0.0004), and open-to-air, 0.0001 mmHg (0.0000, 0.0008), conditions, ANOVA p = 0.03, pairwise p = 0.049 and 0.049, respectively. These significant differences remained after flush. Post-flush pressures between IV, 7.9 mmHg (6.6, 8.9) and SC, 20.5 mmHg (11.3, 28.8) were significantly different, p = 0.0001. There was no significant difference in pre-flush and post-flush pressure within IV, SC, and open-air groups, p = 0.687, p = 0.110 and p = 0.219, respectively. PIVA was superior to absolute pressure measurement for detecting intravascular versus extravascular placement of an IV catheter. This study demonstrates utility of PIVA as a novel method for confirming proper IV placement.

title: Neddylation is required for cerebellar development in mice.
authorString: Wang YB, Yong YY, Yu XR, Xie PX, Song NN, Zhao X, Ding YQ, Zhang L.
abstractText: The cerebellum undergoes a prolonged and highly coordinated developmental program that is essential for motor and cognitive function, yet the post-translational mechanisms governing this process are not fully understood. Here, we identify neddylation, a ubiquitin-like post-translational modification that conjugates NEDD8 to substrate proteins, as a critical regulator of cerebellar development. We show that the indispensable neddylation pathway component NAE1 is broadly expressed in the developing mouse cerebellum, including radial glia, granule cell lineage cells, Purkinje cells, and Bergmann glia. Conditional ablation of NAE1 in the developing cerebellum leads to significant cerebellar hypoplasia, defective foliation, and disrupted cortical lamination. Loss of NAE1 reduces granule cell progenitor proliferation, perturbs granule cell organization and migration, and compromises Bergmann glial identity and architecture. These cellular abnormalities result in marked disorganized cerebellar layers and altered distribution of neuronal and glial populations. Mechanistically, NAE1 deficiency increased nuclear accumulation of β-catenin, indicating impaired regulation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway. β-catenin knockdown partially rescued the reduction in granule cell progenitor proliferation and the altered inward migration of granule-lineage cells induced by acute Nae1 deletion. Our findings establish neddylation as a crucial molecular determinant of cerebellar morphogenesis and suggest that disrupting this pathway may contribute to cerebellar malformations and neurodevelopmental disorders.

title: Medicare Part D formulary coverage of SGLT2 inhibitors across cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic indications, 2019-2026.
authorString: Jain V, McCoy RG.
abstractText: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) carry Class I, Level A recommendations for type 2 diabetes (T2D), heart failure (HF), and chronic kidney disease (CKD) but remain underused outside T2D, with formulary restrictions commonly cited as a contributing cause. We assessed whether Medicare Part D formulary restrictions account for this gap and whether the restrictions differ across cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) indications. Cross-sectional analysis of national Medicare Part D formulary files for plan years 2019-2026, using the January/February snapshot (410 formularies in 2019, 330 in 2026; 13,726 SGLT2i monotherapy entries). We measured entry-level prior authorization (PA) and step-therapy prevalence, the proportion of formularies offering at least one and at least two unrestricted SGLT2i drugs, and tier distribution, across three indication groups reflecting cumulative regulatory approvals. PA was uncommon across all indications and years, never exceeding 1.6%, and at least 98% of formularies offered a PA-free SGLT2i in every indication group-year. Step therapy fell to zero by 2025 then rebounded in 2026, concentrated on empagliflozin, whose entry-level step therapy rate rose from 0.00% to 18.18%, coincident with the effective date of its negotiated maximum fair price; co-negotiated dapagliflozin showed no comparable increase (1.21%). Tier 3 was the dominant placement (61.9-78.7%). Canagliflozin coverage fell from 58.3% of formularies in 2019 to 5.8% in 2026, and only 5.8% offered two step-free SGLT2i for CKD by 2026. Formulary restrictions do not appear to be a major barrier to SGLT2i use among Medicare beneficiaries, redirecting attention toward clinician- and system-level factors. Narrowing CKD-indication approved options and an emergent step-therapy rebound warrant monitoring.

title: Combined crocin and treadmill exercise regulate cardiac MicroRNA-23b, nuclear factor Erythroid 2-related factor 2, and tumor necrosis factor-alpha in experimental type 2 diabetes mellitus.
authorString: Habibi M, Nejad DB, Nejaddehbashi F, Dahaz S, Ghorbanzadeh V.
abstractText:
Background

Diabetic cardiomyopathy is a major complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus and is strongly associated with chronic inflammation, oxidative imbalance, and cardiomyocyte apoptosis. MicroRNAs, particularly miR-23b, have emerged as important regulators of inflammatory and metabolic responses; however, its modulation by combined nutritional and exercise interventions in diabetic cardiac tissue remains unclear. The present study evaluated the effects of combined crocin supplementation and treadmill exercise on miR-23b expression and levels of TNF-α, and NRF2 in the heart tissue of rat model of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).

Materials and methods

Thirty-five male Wistar rats were randomly allocated into healthy control and diabetic groups. Type 2 diabetes mellitus was induced in 28 rats using a high-fat diet for four weeks followed by a single intraperitoneal injection of streptozotocin (35 mg/kg). Diabetic rats were divided into four groups (n = 7/group), including diabetic control, crocin-treated (50 mg/kg/day), treadmill exercise, and combined crocin plus exercise groups and treated for eight weeks using combined crocin (50 mg/kg/day) and treadmill exercise. Next, heart tissues were isolated and the gene expression of miR-23b was assessed via SYBR-Green real-time RT-PCR, and the protein levels of TNF-α and NRF2 were measured by ELISA. In addition, apoptosis rate was evaluated by TUNEL method.

Results

Combined crocin and treadmill exercise significantly reduced cardiac TNF-α levels from 8.50 pg/mL in diabetic control rats to 3.78 pg/mL, corresponding to a 55.5% reduction (p < 0.001). In contrast, NRF2 levels increased from 0.2 to 0.82 ng/mg protein, representing a 310% increase following the combined treatment (p = 0.0002). Furthermore, miR-23b expression increased from 0.72-fold in diabetic control rats to 1.82-fold following combined treatment, corresponding to a 151.8% increase (p < 0.001). Combined treatment also significantly reduced cardiac apoptosis compared with the diabetic control group.

Conclusion

Combined crocin supplementation and treadmill exercise improved inflammatory cytokines and antioxidant-related molecular alterations in the cardiac tissue of HFD/STZ-induced diabetic rats by reducing TNF-α levels and increasing NRF2 protein levels and miR-23b expression. Although the combined intervention showed favorable effects compared with individual treatments, further studies are required to determine whether this combination provides synergistic benefits.

title: Atherosclerosis Begins in Childhood: A Life-Course Perspective on Arterial Remodeling from the Bogalusa Heart Study.
authorString: De Anda-Duran I, Flores GG, Bazzano LA, Urbina EM.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

This review summarizes carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) findings from the Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS) and examines how cardiovascular risk factors across the life course contribute to early subclinical atherosclerosis.

Recent findings

BHS studies consistently demonstrate that obesity, dyslipidemia, and SBP are independently associated with increased cIMT in young adulthood. Life-course analyses show that cumulative BMI and LDL-C exposure independently predict adult cIMT, with race-specific sensitive periods identified for obesity. Metabolically abnormal obesity confers greater vascular risk than metabolically healthy obesity. LDL-C and the total cholesterol/HDL-C ratio are the principal lipid determinants of carotid wall thickening, with associations strengthening from childhood through midlife. SBP dominates in cross-sectional models, while BMI shows more consistent independent effects beginning in childhood. Cardiometabolic clustering further amplifies vascular risk, and adolescence represents a key developmental window, with pediatric metabolic syndrome performing no better than BMI alone in predicting adult cIMT. BHS evidence supports the view that atherosclerosis is a progressive disease that begins in childhood and develops through the cumulative burden of risk factors over the life-course. Obesity, dyslipidemia, and elevated blood pressure each independently contribute to cIMT, and their clustering within individuals amplifies this effect, such that the combined sustained burden across the life-course is the strongest determinant of subclinical arterial remodeling. This underscores the importance of early, sustained prevention strategies that target modifiable CV risk factors beginning in childhood.

title: Integrated single-cell transcriptomic and experimental analyses identify macrophage-associated STAT3 signaling contributing to ferroptosis-related injury in septic cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Qiu S, Dai R, Huang X, Zhu W, Zhang W, Feng L, Yang J, Huo M, Shao H.
abstractText:
Background

Septic cardiomyopathy (SCM) is a major complication of sepsis, but how inflammatory immune cells contribute to ferroptosis-related myocardial injury remains unclear. We investigated ferroptosis-associated transcriptional remodeling in SCM and the functional contribution of macrophage STAT3 signaling.

Methods

Single-cell RNA sequencing, cell-cell communication analysis, and independent mouse and human transcriptomic cohorts were integrated to characterize ferroptosis-associated changes. Driver and suppressor signatures were analyzed separately. STAT3 was silenced in LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages, followed by conditioned-medium transfer to H9C2 cardiomyocytes. Ferroptosis-related injury was evaluated using lipid peroxidation, Fe²⁺ accumulation, molecular markers, Ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1) intervention, and an SCM mouse model.

Results

Ferroptosis-associated transcriptional features showed marked cell-type heterogeneity. Inflammatory macrophages exhibited prominent STAT3-related inflammatory signaling and extensive predicted communication with cardiomyocytes. Independent cohorts revealed context-dependent changes in ferroptosis driver and suppressor programs. Conditioned medium from LPS-stimulated macrophages induced cardiomyocyte injury, lipid peroxidation, Fe²⁺ accumulation, decreased GPX4, and increased ACSL4. Macrophage STAT3 knockdown partially attenuated these changes, reduced inflammatory responses, and altered Cp expression. Fer-1 further alleviated conditioned-medium-induced injury. Consistent ferroptosis-related molecular alterations were observed in SCM mice.

Conclusion

Macrophage STAT3 signaling contributes to a paracrine inflammatory environment associated with ferroptosis-related cardiomyocyte injury, linking inflammatory macrophages to myocardial injury in SCM.

title: Comparison of outcomes after transcatheter patent ductus arteriosus closure in infants weighing ≤ 1.5 kg and > 1.5-4 kg.
authorString: Librandi K, Bautista-Rodriguez C, Butera G, Annoni G, Padovani P, Foldvari S, Baruteau AE, Fraisse A.
abstractText: Transcatheter closure of patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) with the Amplatzer Piccolo Occluder is safe and effective in infants ≤ 2 kg. In larger infants, off-label devices are often required, but outcome data are limited. We evaluated outcomes in infants ≤ 4 kg, comparing the ≤ 1.5 and > 1.5-4 kg groups. This retrospective, international, multicenter study included 358 infants who underwent transcatheter PDA closure at 5 tertiary centers between 2016 and 2024: 191 weighed ≤ 1.5 kg (group 1) and 167 > 1.5-4 kg (group 2). Median age was 39 days (interquartile range 25-61) and median weight was 1.48 (1.1-2.2) kg; 93.6% were preterm. Procedural success was higher in group 1 (98.4% vs 94.0%; p = 0.044). Major adverse events were more frequent in group 2 (9.6% vs 3.1%; p = 0.0144; odds ratio = 3.27; 95% confidence interval, 1.25-8.55). Device embolization occurred only in group 2 (5.4% vs 0%; p < 0.001; odds ratio = 22.96; 95% confidence interval, 1.33-397.51). The Amplatzer Piccolo Occluder was used in 97.3% of group 1 vs 69.5% of group 2. Transcatheter PDA closure is safe and effective in infants ≤ 4 kg, but the > 1.5-4 kg group has a higher risk of major adverse events, particularly device embolization. Better patient selection and dedicated devices may improve safety. • Transcatheter PDA closure with the Amplatzer Piccolo Occluder is safe and effective in very small infants. • In larger infants, alternative devices are often used off-label, but evidence on procedural outcomes remains limited. • Infants weighing >1.5-4 kg had lower procedural success and more major adverse events than those weighing ≤1.5 kg. • Device embolization occurred exclusively in the >1.5-4 kg group, supporting careful anatomical assessment and the development of dedicated devices.

title: Detection and Outcome Associations of Low-Grade Intraventricular Hemorrhage in Very Preterm Infants: Influence of Neuroimaging Modality and Grading System.
authorString: Drommelschmidt K, Raudzus J, Mayrhofer T, Foldyna B, Zellner M, Göricke S, Schweiger B, Sirin S.
abstractText: The clinical relevance of low-grade intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) in very preterm infants remains debated. We investigated how cMRI and cranial ultrasound (cUS) influence IVH detection and grading and how differences between the Papile and Volpe classifications affect interpretation and outcome stratification. This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 507 consecutively born infants at < 32 weeks' gestation with serial cUS and cMRI at term-equivalent age (2009-2018). IVH was graded according to the Papile and Volpe classifications. Clinical parameters and neurodevelopmental outcomes at 24 months of corrected age were assessed (Bayley Scales of Infant Development). Univariable and multivariable regression analyses were performed. Among 507 preterm infants, IVH was identified in 85 (16.8%; IVH I° n = 33, IVH II° n = 35, IVH III° n = 13, PVHI n = 4). CMRI and cUS differed significantly in IVH detection (p = 0.025). IVH was not detected on cUS in 32 cases (37.6%, IVH I° n = 21, IVH II° n = 9, PVHI n = 2). Additionally, 48.6% of IVH II° according to Papile were classified as IVH I° on cUS due to non-detection of intraventricular blood. IVH II° was associated with significantly lower cognitive and motor outcomes scores than IVH I° (p = 0.035/p = 0.016). Differences in outcome stratification between grading systems were significant (cognitive p = 0.047/motor p = 0.015) and driven by differences in classification of intraventricular blood. Detection of intraventricular blood was associated with worse cognitive and motor outcomes. Differences between IVH grading systems and the choice of neuroimaging modality may influence risk stratification in infants with low-grade hemorrhage, particularly when small amounts of intraventricular blood are present.

title: Streptococcus oralis induces platelet aggregation through coordinated GPIbα and FcγRIIA signalling.
authorString: Lamerton R, McMahon A, O'Neill A, King S, Kerrigan SW.
abstractText: Streptococcus oralis is the most prevalent viridans group streptococcus associated with infective endocarditis (IE), yet the platelet activation mechanisms that underpin its pathogenicity remain poorly defined. Platelet-bacterium interactions are central to vegetation formation, but the relative contributions of direct adhesion and antibody-dependent signaling in S.oralis-induced platelet aggregation are unclear. To define the molecular mechanisms by which S.oralis induces platelet activation and aggregation, and to determine how bacterial adhesins and host factors cooperate to drive this response. Platelet aggregation and dense granule secretion were assessed using light transmission aggregometry and ATP release assays in platelet-rich plasma and washed platelets.
