title: Diuretics for Management of Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia Associated Pulmonary Hypertension in Preterm Infants-A Systematic Review.
authorString: Kanagaraj UK, Saker A, Cuello-Garcia C, Castaldo M, Shivananda S.
abstractText: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia associated pulmonary hypertension (BPD-PH) in preterm infants results from impaired pulmonary vascular development and contributes significantly to morbidity and mortality. Diuretics are commonly used to reduce pulmonary vascular congestion and improve oxygenation, but their efficacy and safety remain unclear. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of diuretic use in preterm infants with BPD-PH. Primary outcomes were mortality and need for home respiratory support; secondary outcomes were echocardiographic and clinical parameters, and adverse effects such as hyponatremia, nephrocalcinosis. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central, and ClinicalTrials.gov from inception to October 2025. We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and non-randomized studies of interventions (NRSI) evaluating diuretics in preterm infants (< 32 weeks' gestation) with BPD-PH diagnosed by echocardiography at 36 weeks postmenstrual age. Two reviewers independently performed data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment (ROBINS-I). Outcomes were synthesized narratively, and a meta-analysis was performed where sufficient data were available. Of 492 studies identified, 2 NRSI (n = 49) met inclusion criteria, both were at serious risk of bias. No RCTs exist on diuretics for BPD-PH in preterm infants. Mortality, respiratory, discharge outcomes and adverse effects were reported inconsistently. Meta-analysis of limited data demonstrated small improvements in echocardiographic markers, but the certainty of evidence was very low due to heterogeneity between the two included studies. To conclude, evidence supporting the use of diuretics in BPD-PH in preterm infants remains limited and of low certainty. High quality studies are needed to better define their safety and efficacy.

title: Genetic Variants Associated with Ventricular Septal Defect in Malaysia: A Scoping Review of Current Evidence and Research Gaps.
authorString: Kong AS, Ghozi NBMW, Koh GT, Khaw KY, Maran S.
abstractText: Ventricular septal defect (VSD) is the most prevalent congenital heart defect in Malaysia; however, its genetic basis is still not well understood. We conducted a scoping review to evaluate the current evidence on VSD-associated genetic variants in the Malaysian population. A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase from inception to June 2026, following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines. Original studies investigating genetic variants associated with VSD in Malaysian patients were included. Data regarding study characteristics, investigated genes, reported variants, molecular methods, and principal findings were extracted and synthesised. Out of 28 records identified, three studies met the eligibility criteria. The included studies reported variants in three genes: SMAD7, NR0B1, and NIPBL. The identified variants included synonymous substitutions and frameshift alterations that were predicted to cause premature protein truncation. However, the available evidence was limited by small sample sizes, candidate-gene approaches, and the predominance of syndromic cases. We found no nationwide or multicentre studies using high-throughput sequencing technologies. Despite the significant disease burden, the current evidence on the genetics of VSD in Malaysia remains sparse. The lack of comprehensive genomic investigations underscores the need for collaborative studies across the nation that integrate next-generation sequencing and functional validation. This would enhance our understanding of VSD pathogenesis and support future precision medicine initiatives.

title: Echocardiographic markers for left atrial stiffness and left atrial conduction delay in patients with silent paroxysmal atrial fibrillation compared to age-matched controls.
authorString: Bastos L, Al-Khalili F, Bäck M, Manouras A, Engdahl J, Shahgaldi K.
abstractText:
Purpose

To study left atrial stiffness index (LASI) and left atrial activation time (LA-AT) changes in an older population with silent paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (PAF) compared to age-matched control.

Methods

Individuals with newly diagnosed PAF and a randomly selected age-matched control group without AF were enrolled from STROKESTOP2-study. All participants had NT-proBNP levels 125-900 ng/L. TTE examinations were analyzed retrospectively offline using dedicated software. Besides conventional echocardiographic measurements, LA-AT was obtained by measuring the time delay between the onset of the P-wave on ECG and tissue Doppler Á peak wave in lateral LA wall. LASI was calculated as the ratio of left ventricular filling (E/é) to peak atrial longitudinal strain (PALS).

Results

Mean age was 76 ± 0.3 years. The PAF group (n = 67) presented significant increase of LASI (0.41 (0.29-0.60) vs. 0.32 (0.29-0.43), P = 0.001) and prolonged LA-AT (170 (140-180) ms vs. 140 (120-144) ms, P < 0.001) compared to controls (n = 94). Subgroup analysis in participants with normal LA volume index (LAVI) ≤ 34 ml/m2, LASI and LA-AT remained significantly increased/prolonged in PAF (N = 27) compared to controls (N = 72). NT-proBNP-levels did not differ between PAF (228 (181-348) ng/L) and controls (216 (156-317) ng/L) (P = 0.18). ROC curve analysis identified thresholds LASI > 0.54 and LA-AT > 139 msec for discrimination of silent PAF.

Conclusion

Indices reflecting LA stiffness and atrial conduction delay were significantly elevated in recently diagnosed PAF patients. LASI and LA-AT thresholds might non-invasively detect early atrial remodeling without structural enlargement in elderly patients with high risk of PAF and mildly increased NT-proBNP levels.

title: Adjunctive therapeutic plasma exchange as rescue therapy in septic shock due to streptococcal infection: a multicentric retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Ruwisch J, Buhlmann A, Wild L, Wendel-Garcia PD, Pape T, Hofmaenner DA, Putensen C, Kruse P, Holtgrave GH, Schenk H, Bode C, David S, Stahl K, Seeliger B, Bonn-Hannover-Zurich ARDS (BonHanZA) Study Group.
abstractText: Septic shock due to streptococcal infection (SRSS) carries a high mortality and is in part driven by toxin-mediated inflammation. Therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) may modulate the septic host responses by removing injurious mediators while replenishing protective plasma factors, but data specific to SRSS is lacking. We performed a retrospective, multicenter, cohort study of adults with SRSS between 2012-2024. Patients from three tertiary care ECMO centers in Germany and Switzerland were included requiring (i) streptococcal spp. detected in blood or primary focus and (ii) septic shock according to sepsis-3 definition. Adjunctive TPE with fresh frozen plasma at the intensivists` discretion was compared with standard of care (SOC). The primary outcome was 90-day-hospital mortality. Key exploratory outcomes included 24-h kinetics of vasoactive-inotropic score(VIS) and lactate, as well as SRSS-related complications. Results were validated in a 1:1 propensity score-matched (PSM) cohort. Of 149 patients, 31 (20.8%) received TPE and 118 (79.2%) SOC. TPE patients were more severely ill at baseline: SOFA 14 (IQR 13.5-15) vs 11 (IQR 8-14) (p<0.001); lactate 6.4 vs 2.8 mmol/L (p<0.001); Vasoactive-Inotropic-Score (VIS) 70.7 vs 23.3 (p<0.001); more frequent invasive ventilation (87% vs 65%), VV-ECMO (36% vs 19%), and renal replacement therapy (96.8% vs 52.5%). Overall, 90-day hospital mortality was 27.5% (TPE 29.0%, SOC 27.1%). Following SOFA-score adjustment, TPE was associated with lower mortality risk (aHR 0.67 [95% CI 0.5-0.9]; p=0.009). This was validated in the PSM cohort, with an aHR for TPE of 0.44 (95% CI 0.3-0.8); p=0.002. Mixed-effects modeling demonstrated a significant VIS reduction only with TPE (fixed effect 24-h change, p=0.027) and improved lactate decrease versus SOC. In SRSS, adjunctive TPE was associated with rapid hemodynamic stabilization and improved lactate kinetics. Exploratory adjusted survival analyses support prospective evaluation of TPE in SRSS.

title: Early echocardiographic hemodynamic phenotypes and clinical outcomes in congenital diaphragmatic hernia.
authorString: Yoo K, Kim SH, Park J, Kim TG, Kwak JI, Lee JM, Lee HN, Jeong J, Kim CY, Yum SK, Jung E, Lee BS.
abstractText: Early postnatal hemodynamic adaptation may contribute to outcome heterogeneity in congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). We evaluated whether echocardiography-defined hemodynamic phenotypes within 24 h of birth were associated with cardiorespiratory severity and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) or death. This retrospective cohort included infants with CDH admitted to a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit from 2021 to 2025 who underwent echocardiography within 24 h. Phenotypes were classified as no/mild pulmonary hypertension (PH), right ventricular (RV)-predominant PH, or left ventricular (LV)-involved PH based on ventricular function and ductal/atrial shunt direction. Associations with prenatal severity, respiratory indices, and ECMO or death were assessed. Among 66 infants, 21 had no/mild PH, 22 RV-predominant PH, and 23 LV-involved PH. ECMO or death occurred in 0%, 27.3%, and 65.2%, respectively (P < 0.001). Compared with RV-predominant PH, LV-involved PH was associated with greater respiratory severity and more frequent LV dysfunction; observed-to-expected lung-to-head ratio (O/E LHR) did not differ significantly between these two groups. Ordinal phenotype severity remained associated with ECMO or death after adjustment for O/E LHR (odds ratio (OR), 5.98; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.76-20.31; P = 0.004). However, the comparison between LV-involved and RV-predominant PH was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for O/E LHR (OR, 3.42; 95% CI, 0.87-15.10).  Early hemodynamic phenotype was associated with cardiorespiratory severity and ECMO or death in CDH. LV-involved PH identified a high-risk phenotype and may complement prenatal anatomic risk stratification, although its independent prognostic value beyond prenatal lung size requires validation. • Prenatal lung size and liver herniation are established markers of disease severity and outcome in congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). • Pulmonary hypertension and ventricular dysfunction contribute substantially to early cardiorespiratory instability and adverse outcomes in infants with CDH. • Early echocardiographic phenotypes were associated with cardiorespiratory severity and ECMO or death. • LV-involved PH identified a high-risk phenotype, although its prognostic value beyond prenatal severity remains uncertain.

title: The Rising Burden of Atrial Fibrillation and Respiratory Failure Mortality in the United States: A 25-Year Nationwide Retrospective Analysis of Death Certificate Data.
authorString: Hassan ST, Ahmad N, Onaiz SL, Ilyas AF, Kumar S, Yaqubi AJ.
abstractText: Atrial fibrillation (AF) and respiratory failure (RF) frequently co-occur in critically ill patients, but long-term national trends in deaths recording both remain unknown. CDC WONDER multiple-cause-of-death data identified U.S. adults aged ≥ 55 years with both AF (including atrial flutter) and RF listed on death certificates from 1999 to 2024. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) and annual percent changes (APCs) were estimated using joinpoint regression. Sensitivity analyses included adults aged ≥ 25 years, exclusion of COVID-19-related deaths, and stratification by co-listed heart failure (HF). A total of 462 284 deaths listed both AF and RF. The AAMR increased roughly five-fold (7.84 to 41.76 per 100 000), rising steadily through 2018 (APC 7.81), accelerating through 2021 (APC 18.78), and declining thereafter (APC -5.90). Excluding deaths listing COVID-19, the 2018-2021 acceleration was not detected, and AAMRs rose through 2024 (2017-2024 APC 5.25). AAMRs for deaths without HF recorded rose over fourfold. Mean AAMRs were higher in males (26.19) than in females (19.04) and in non-Hispanic (NH) White adults (24.06) than in other groups. The West and nonmetropolitan areas had the highest rates. The 2018-2021 surge was steepest among Hispanic (APC 25.62) and NH Black adults (APC 24.06). Population mortality rates for deaths recording both AF and RF increased substantially over 25 years, beginning before the COVID-19 pandemic, persisting after excluding deaths listing COVID-19, and occurring with and without HF recorded. These data cannot separate changes in disease occurrence from changes in diagnosis or coding.

title: From Blood Clone to Myocardial Lesion: A Tissue-Provenance Framework for Clonal Haematopoiesis in Heart Failure
authorString: Biswas B.
abstractText: Clonal haematopoiesis (CH) is increasingly associated with heart failure, adverse cardiac remodelling and cardiovascular mortality. Yet most human evidence begins and ends in different anatomical compartments: the mutation is detected in blood, whereas the phenotype is measured in the heart. The intervening biological sequence is usually inferred rather than demonstrated. This Mini Focused Review reframes CH-associated heart failure as a tissue-provenance problem. We propose a six-level tissue-provenance framework that distinguishes circulating clone detection, effector-lineage attribution, myocardial entry, spatial localisation, lesion-concordant cellular behaviour and longitudinal phenotype linkage. Experimental studies of TET2, DNMT3A, JAK2V617F, ASXL1, PPM1D and TP53 support driver-specific inflammatory and remodelling phenotypes, while human tissue studies show that mutation-bearing cardiovascular macrophages need not be preferentially enriched to be biologically abnormal. Heart transplantation provides a particularly informative human test system because recipient genotype, cellular provenance, serial endomyocardial tissue and evolving pathology can be interrogated within the same patient. A practical programme combining blood sequencing, targeted tissue genotyping, cellular phenotyping, spatial localisation and longitudinal histopathology could distinguish circulating association from lesion participation. The immediate translational priority is therefore anatomical attribution rather than broader CH screening.

title: Acute pericarditis caused by Kocuria kristinae with successful withdrawal from hemodialysis: a case report.
authorString: Chiba K, Osugi T, Amabe K, Kobayashi T, Kamio A, Kunii A, Fukuda N, Nozaki A, Oshikawa J.
abstractText: Kocuria kristinae is a commensal skin bacterium that occasionally acts as an opportunistic pathogen. However, it is rarely associated with pericardial infection. This report describes the case of a 47-year-old male patient with dialysis-dependent acute kidney injury (AKI) complicated by massive inflammatory pericardial effusion, in whom K. kristinae was isolated. The patient developed a severe heatstroke, which was followed by AKI, subsequently requiring hemodialysis. Approximately 1 month later, the cardiothoracic ratio increased markedly, and echocardiography revealed substantial pericardial effusion. Anti-inflammatory therapy, comprising non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, colchicine, and prednisolone, elicited a poor response, given no improvement in the effusion. Ultrasound guidance was used for pericardiocentesis, resulting in drainage of 1050 mL of pale-yellow, exudative fluid with neutrophil predominance. K. kristinae was subsequently identified using the VITEK 2 system. The vancomycin dosage was determined based on the susceptibility results. Following the implementation of drainage and antimicrobial therapy, pericardial effusion decreased, venous congestion was alleviated, and urine output increased. These interventions may have contributed to renal recovery and the discontinuation of hemodialysis on day 102. Clinicians should regard K. kristinae isolated from pericardial fluid as a possible contaminant notwithstanding a clinically compatible setting. This case suggests that a massive pericardial effusion with venous congestion can delay renal recovery in severe AKI, whereas successful pericardial drainage facilitates recovery of urine output and withdrawal from hemodialysis.

title: Common Femoral Atherectomy yields safe results and low morbidity in the outpatient setting.
authorString: Napier JA, Ayerdi JA, Heidenreich MJ, Kato PJ, Sundararaghavan V, Aziz A.
abstractText:
Objective

Common femoral artery (CFA) endarterectomy is considered the gold standard for the treatment of CFA disease. Some patients with CFA occlusive disease have significant comorbidities that may prevent them from undergoing open surgery. Several endovascular treatment options for the CFA, such as atherectomy, angioplasty, and stenting, are available but have not been widely adopted. This study aimed to describe our experience expanding the use of atherectomy in the outpatient setting for the treatment of CFA disease.

Methods

This is a single-institution, retrospective review of 49 CFA atherectomy procedures performed from January 2017 to November 2022 at Trinity Health Ann Arbor. Primary outcomes included primary patency at 1 year and MALE-free survival. Secondary outcomes involved changes in ankle-brachial index (ABI), toe pressures, and morbidity at 90 days.

Results

49 CFA atherectomies were performed on 45 patients (73 yo ± 7 years), 45% with claudication and 55% with critical limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). TASC classification of the treated lesions was TASC A in 4%, TASC B in 29%, TASC C in 61%, and TASC D in 6%. Three patients also underwent superficial femoral artery (SFA) stenting; one had concomitant CFA stenting, and 24 (49%) underwent treatment distal to the CFA atherectomy site. We encountered three complications: one readmission for dehydration, one postoperative hematoma, and one focal SFA dissection requiring delayed secondary stent placement. There were no deaths within 90 days. Post-procedure, the average ABI increased from 0.59 to 0.80 (P<0.01), and toe pressure rose from 42 to 68 (P<0.01). Thirty-five cases had follow-up of at least one year, showing a primary patency rate of 86% and a 94% MALE-free at one year. Additionally, 71% reported symptom improvement or wound healing at their last follow-up.

Conclusion

When open surgery may be medically prohibited, CFA atherectomy combined with balloon angioplasty can be performed safely, yielding good clinical outcomes as a standalone procedure or with additional infrainguinal interventions. When applied in appropriate clinical and radiologic circumstances, patients experience favorable outcomes with low procedural morbidity. Due to its clinical benefits and low risk, this procedure can be a valuable addition to the modern vascular surgeon's treatment armamentarium.

title: Predicting in-silico ventricular tachycardia induction on fuzzy cardiac digital twins.
authorString: Crabbé O, Bessière F, L'Eplattenier P, Grivot C, Ditac G, Rochette M, Martins R, Haigron P, El Houari K.
abstractText: Ventricular tachycardia (VT) is a leading cause of sudden cardiac death (SCD). To date, clinical VT risk assessment is either inaccurate, invasive or expensive. Patient-specific computer modeling of heart electrophysiology (EP) is a promising non-invasive risk assessment approach. It has three major limitations: computational cost, inaccurate arrhythmogenic substrate geometry and unknown patient-specific tissue EP properties. We present a pacing outcome predictor (POP) that quickly identifies the conditions needed to induce VT in three-dimensional personalized cardiac computer models. The POP is used to test VT induction across multiple model versions of a patient, covering scar geometry and EP property variations, with an added layer of model reduction to further accelerate calculations. The results are combined into a personalized VT risk metric based on in-silico VT inducibility across the patient's models. In a retrospective 10-patient repaired Tetralogy of Fallot cohort, the metric showed complete separation (10/10) between patients with and without clinically inducible VT, suggesting potential for non-invasive VT risk assessment in this population.

title: Orthostatic blood pressure fluctuations and risk of falls in community-dwelling older adults: the role of recovery time.
authorString: Alvarez VA, Hertneck C, Rothenbacher D, Denkinger M, Dallmeier D.
abstractText:
Background

Available literature related to the association between orthostatic blood pressure (BP) variations and falls is controversial. We analyzed how orthostatic hypo- (OH) and hypertension (OHTN) relate to falls considering recovery time (RT) in community-dwelling older adults.

Methods

This analysis uses data from the ActiFE cohort. BP was measured lying, immediately, 1, 2 and 3 min after standing. Systolic OH (sOH) and systolic OHTN (sOHTN) indicate a systolic BP (SBP) drop or increment ≥20 mm Hg, respectively. OH and OHTN further consider a diastolic BP (DBP) drop or increment ≥10 mm Hg. RT was categorized as Early Recovery ( < 1 min), Delayed Recovery (1-3 min), or No Recovery. Falls over 12 months were collected prospectively. Logistic regression examined associations with falls, adjusting for age, sex, diabetes, hemoglobin, instrumental activities of daily living, hand strength, fall risk-increasing drugs, past falls, Falls Efficacy Scale-International and anxiety.

Results

Among 509 subjects (mean age 79 years, 44% female, 168 falls), prevalences were: 16.5% sOH, 26.9% OH, 9.0% sOHTN and 15.5% OHTN. Overall, OH was not associated with falls. However, falls risk increased with Delayed (OR 3.11 [95% CI 1.21-8.01]) and NoRecovery (OR 4.04 [95% CI 1.07-15.26]). sOH showed an adjusted OR of 2.00 [95% CI 1.15-3.47] for at least one fall. Regarding RT the risk of falls was increased in Delayed (OR 4.73 [95% CI 1.71-13.10]) and No Recovery (OR 5.06 [95% CI 1.42-22.27]). OHTN was not associated with falls.

Conclusions

Overall, only sOH was associated with falls. When RT was considered, those with Delayed and No Recovery showed higher risk of falls regardless of the OH definition used.

title: Porto-sinusoidal vascular disorder after trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1) therapy in HER2-positive breast cancer.
authorString: Shigefuku R, Saito K, Iwasa M, Tsukimoto M, Tamai Y, Fujiwara N, Tameda M, Ogura S, Tanaka H, Nakagawa H.
abstractText: Trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1), an antibody-drug conjugate targeting human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2), is used for HER2-positive breast cancer. Although hepatotoxicity and thrombocytopenia are recognized adverse events of T-DM1, long-term hepatic vascular complications associated with this treatment remain poorly characterized. We report a case of porto-sinusoidal vascular disorder (PSVD) with noncirrhotic portal hypertension (NCPH) associated with prolonged T-DM1 therapy. We retrospectively reviewed the clinical course, serial laboratory data, imaging findings, endoscopic findings, and liver histopathology of a woman in her 70s with recurrent HER2-positive breast cancer who received prolonged T-DM1 therapy. After prior maintenance therapy with trastuzumab and pertuzumab, the patient received 60 cycles of T-DM1. During treatment, progressive thrombocytopenia developed. Serial computed tomography demonstrated splenomegaly, portal vein dilatation, and the development of portosystemic collateral vessels. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed newly developed esophageal varices. Laboratory evaluation excluded viral, autoimmune, and metabolic liver diseases. Liver biopsy showed focal sinusoidal dilatation and obliterative portal venopathy without cirrhotic architectural distortion, consistent with PSVD. Retrospective imaging review showed that splenomegaly had developed approximately 12 months after the initiation of T-DM1 therapy. Splenomegaly and platelet counts remained unchanged 2 years after T-DM1 discontinuation, whereas spleen stiffness increased. This case suggests that prolonged exposure to T-DM1 may cause sinusoidal endothelial injury and lead to PSVD with portal hypertension. Progressive thrombocytopenia and splenomegaly during T-DM1 therapy may represent early clinical indicators of this complication. Careful long-term monitoring for signs of portal hypertension should be considered in patients receiving prolonged T-DM1 treatment.

title: Effects of SGLT2 inhibition on cardiac remodeling and heart failure development in aortic stenosis rats.
authorString: Pagan LU, Gomes MJ, Gatto M, Mota GAF, Oliveira JPG, Damatto FC, Souza LM, Rodrigues EA, Santos ACC, Tukiyama GH, Campos DHS, Rodrigues Ferreira M, Correa CR, Murata GM, Polegato BF, Okoshi MP, Okoshi K.
abstractText: Aortic stenosis (AS) is increasingly prevalent in ageing populations, yet no pharmacological therapy has been shown to modify its progression to heart failure (HF). Sodium glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors improve outcomes in HF, but their effects in pressure overload-induced cardiac remodeling remain unclear. Here, we show that rats with long-term AS develop HF features, left ventricular dilation, and systolic and diastolic dysfunction, accompanied by increased oxidative stress, impaired antioxidant defenses, myocardial fibrosis, and transcriptional remodeling. Empagliflozin (10 mg/kg/day for 8 weeks) attenuated cardiac dysfunction and reduced HF features. At molecular level, empagliflozin prevented increase in lipid peroxidation, and decreased interstitial collagen deposition, while increasing glutathione peroxidase and matrix metalloproteinase-2 activity. Transcriptomic analysis identified 1,078 differentially expressed genes and revealed enrichment of pathways associated with extracellular matrix organization and signal transduction in AS. Empagliflozin predominantly regulated genes involved in cardiac contraction, mitochondrial membrane organization, apoptosis, and cell survival. Profibrotic and remodeling-associated genes were upregulated in AS, while empagliflozin induced a distinct transcriptional program associated with improved myocardial homeostasis. AS was associated with reduced activity of energy metabolism enzymes, which was not restored by empagliflozin. Collectively, these findings identify oxidative stress, extracellular matrix remodeling, and transcriptional reprogramming as mechanisms underlying cardiac dysfunction in AS. Empagliflozin mitigates cardiac remodeling and HF progression and modulates fibrosis and gene networks regulating cardiac function. These data highlight SGLT2 inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy in pressure overload-induced heart failure.

title: Clinical features and associated factors for porto-sinusoidal vascular disease in primary Sjögren's disease: a retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Xu YT, Zhang GH, Shen L, Zhang X, Zhou H, Zhang T, Zhao XY, Liu YY.
abstractText: To characterize primary Sjögren's disease (pSjD) patients with porto-sinusoidal vascular disease (PSVD) and identify associated clinical factors. This retrospective study included 7 biopsy-proven pSjD-PSVD patients and 28 age and sex-matched pSjD controls. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and portal hypertension-related data were collected and compared between the two groups. Univariate logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with PSVD. The pSjD-PSVD group had significantly longer disease duration than controls [59 (36, 180) vs. 15 (12, 69) months, p = 0.031]. All PSVD patients presented with splenomegaly, thrombocytopenia [(88 ± 44.01) vs. (176.21 ± 66.37) × 10⁹/L, p = 0.003], leukopenia [(3.05 ± 1.26) vs. (4.51 ± 1.52) × 10⁹/L, p = 0.024], hypoalbuminemia [(35.37 ± 4.06) vs. (38.86 ± 3.00) g/L, p = 0.015], elevated aspartate aminotransferase (AST) [(32.13 ± 11.64) vs. (22.9 ± 7.75) IU/L, p = 0.016], and elevated serum IgG [1970 (1540, 2460) vs. 1435 (1160, 1977.5) mg/dL; p = 0.027]. Univariate logistic regression identified thrombocytopenia (OR = 3.481, p = 0.003), INR > 1.2 (OR = 3.507, p = 0.003), hypoalbuminemia (OR = 8.000, p = 0.007), elevated AST (OR = 1.106, p = 0.04), elevated alkaline phosphatase (ALP) (OR = 1.033, p = 0.023), hypokalemia (OR = 2.408, p = 0.003), and elevated IgG (OR = 2.079, p = 0.039) as factors associated with PSVD. Elevated IgG did not retain significance in Firth's penalized likelihood regression (OR 3.35, p = 0.142). This exploratory study characterizes the clinical features of pSjD patients with PSVD. A constellation of associated features-long disease duration, splenomegaly with hypersplenism, hepatic synthetic impairment (hypoalbuminemia, INR prolongation, elevated AST/ALP), hypokalemia, and hypergammaglobulinemia-may aid in early identification of portal hypertension. These preliminary findings require validation in large prospective cohorts. Key Points • pSjD may represent an autoimmune condition associated with PSVD, featuring long disease duration, splenomegaly, and cytopenias. • pSjD-PSVD shows mild synthetic dysfunction and AST-predominant enzyme elevation without cirrhosis. • Elevated IgG, hypokalemia, and UIP may help identify pSjD patients who warrant closer surveillance for portal hypertension.

title: Interactions between sleep parameters and heart rate variability in temporomandibular disorders.
authorString: Martynowicz H, Trocha M, Marschollek K, Macek P, Trzepietowski W, Przegrałek J, Madziarska K, Więckiewicz M.
abstractText: Temporomandibular disorders (TMD) cause pain and dysfunction in the temporomandibular joints (TMJs) and masticatory muscles and significantly impact quality of life. Temporomandibular disorderrelated pain is associated with sleep disorders and affects heart rate (HR) parameters; however, data from polysomnographic studies remains inconclusive. The aim of the study was to evaluate the impact of TMD on sleep parameters recorded using video-polysomnography (vPSG) and heart rate variability (HRV) monitored with the use of a 24-hour electrocardiogram (ECG). A cross-sectional study included 93 patients with TMD diagnosed according to the Diagnostic Criteria for Temporomandibular Disorders (DC/TMD). Video-polysomnography and 24-hour ECG monitoring were conducted. Pain was assessed using the numeric rating scale (NRS) (0-10) and categorized as mild (≤5) or severe (>5). The study included 93 patients with TMD, divided into groups of low pain intensity (n = 66) and high pain intensity (n = 27). The group with high pain intensity demonstrated lower sleep efficiency (87.7% vs. 90.8%, p = 0.022) and lower oxygen saturation (94.7% vs. 95.2%, p = 0.036). Heart rate variability parameters were similar in both groups. Women reported a higher total pain score (20 vs. 10, p = 0.007) and had a higher percentage of normal-to-normal (NN) intervals differing by more than 50 ms (pNN50) (24 h: 22.5% vs. 14.2%, p = 0.013; daytime: 18.0% vs. 9.8%, p = 0.002), higher daytime root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD) (41.7 vs. 34.8, p = 0.026), and a higher nighttime HR (63.8 vs. 60.5, p = 0.047). Additionally, women demonstrated lower values for very low frequency (VLF) power (1,402.4 vs. 2,214.5, p = 0.010), low frequency (LF) power (1,415.5 vs. 2,494.5, p = 0.028), and the low frequency/high frequency (LF/HF) ratio (1.3 vs. 2.5, p < 0.001). High TMD-related pain intensity is associated with reduced sleep efficiency and lower mean oxygen saturation during sleep. Women experience higher pain intensity but lower sympathetic activation than men.

title: Posterior Pulmonary Vein Isolation Lesion Spacing and Left Atrial Posterior Wall Narrowing During Pulsed Field Ablation.
authorString: Saito Y, Nagashima K, Watanabe R, Otsuka N, Hirata S, Hirata M, Sawada M, Masuda H, Matsushima A, Sakaki M, Okumura Y.
abstractText: Left atrial posterior wall (LAPW) narrowing after excessive extension of bilateral pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) lines during pulsed field ablation (PFA) may create a proarrhythmic substrate. The CARTO 3-integrated variable-loop circular catheter (VLCC) provides real-time tissue proximity indication (TPI) and ablation-tag location, but their relationship with LAPW narrowing remains unclear. Therefore, we evaluated associations of TPI status and inter-tag distance (ITD) with acute LAPW narrowing and whether an ITD-guided workflow was associated with LAPW preservation. Fifty-two retrospective and 27 prospective atrial fibrillation patients underwent PFA using a VLCC. In the retrospective phase, we evaluated the association between ITD, measured using TPI-positive tags and all tags, and LAPW narrowing (< 10 mm) and derived a cutoff. In the prospective phase, the ITD-guided workflow was applied, and we assessed residual LAPW band width. In the retrospective phase, both TPI-positive-tag ITD and all-tag ITD correlated with LAPW band width (r = 0.63 and 0.70, respectively; both p < 0.001). All-tag ITD showed a numerically higher AUC for LAPW narrowing than TPI-positive-tag ITD (0.869 vs. 0.795; p = 0.099), with an optimal all-tag ITD cutoff of 16.5 mm. In the prospective phase incorporating the all-tag ITD cutoff, residual LAPW band widths were wider at the roof (19.4 ± 7.9 vs. 25.1 ± 7.1 mm; p = 0.002) and carina (13.6 ± 7.1 vs. 20.8 ± 8.0 mm; p < 0.001) than in the retrospective phase. An all-tag ITD-guided workflow was associated with greater preservation of the residual LAPW band width.

title: Structural, Enzymatic and Population-Genetic Profiling of CYP17A1 Variants Defines the Molecular Basis of Partial 17α-Hydroxylase/17,20-Lyase Deficiency
authorString: Li K, Yakubu J, Jørgensen FS, Pandey AV.
abstractText:
Context: 17α-hydroxylase/17,20-lyase deficiency (17-OHD) is a rare form of congenital adrenal hyperplasia that presents with hypertension, hypokalemia and absent or incomplete sexual development. The clinical spectrum extends from complete deficiency to partial forms compatible with spontaneous puberty and fertility, and the molecular determinants of this heterogeneity remain incompletely defined.

Objectives:

To define the pathophysiology of 17-OHD by combining clinical phenotyping with functional, structural, computational and population-genetic characterization of seven CYP17A1 missense variants: T131P, L209P, I296T, G303D, R340H, L361P and R449H.

Methods:

Clinical and hormonal data were collated for ten probands. Variants were expressed in HEK293T cells and 17α-hydroxylase and 17,20-lyase activities were measured with [4-14C]-progesterone and [21-3H]-17α-hydroxypregnenolone and normalized to immunoreactive CYP17A1 abundance. Residue environments were measured directly in the experimental structures PDB 3RUK, 4NKX and 4NKZ, and model confidence was taken from AlphaFold. Structural Flexibilities were studied by molecular dynamics simulations and analyzed by principal component analysis and clustering. Variants were annotated with Ensembl VEP, SpliceAI, CADD and dbNSFP predictors, scored with AlphaGenome using adrenal-gland splicing tracks, and placed in population genetic context using gnomAD v4.1, the 1000 Genomes Project and a gene-wide ClinVar survey. Sequence constraint was assessed with a masked protein language model and with 172 to 176 vertebrate orthologues.

Results:

All seven variants retained substantial immunoreactive protein, but below wild type, and the set-level reduction was significant in all assays. Residual 17α-hydroxylase activity ranged from approximately 1% of wild type for L209P to approximately 50% for R340H, and residual 17,20-lyase activity exceeded hydroxylase activity for every variant. None of the seven variants altered splicing by SpliceAI or AlphaGenome, confirming a purely protein-level mechanism. AlphaMissense was the only predictor whose scores agreed with measured residual activity, yet its binary classification called I296T, R340H and R449H benign despite measured deficits and ClinVar pathogenic or likely pathogenic submissions, and CADD ranked the series in the opposite order to severity. Across gnomAD v4.1 the cumulative burden of pathogenic and likely pathogenic CYP17A1 alleles predicted a carrier frequency of 1 in 1,023 globally and 1 in 523 in East Asian individuals. Serum progesterone was raised in all 10 probands but did not distinguish partial from complete deficiency, whereas morning cortisol did.

Conclusion:

The pathogenicity of these CYP17A1 variants reflects specific catalytic and regulatory defects in a largely intact protein rather than loss of steady-state enzyme. Residual activity relates to clinical severity non-linearly, and current missense predictors are not calibrated for the partial-loss alleles that dominate the clinically ambiguous end of the spectrum. Direct measurement of residual activity remains necessary for prognosis and reproductive counselling.

title: Measured, not labelled: un-analyzable input versus misclassification in single-lead wearable ECG.
authorString: Cheng Y, Deng P, Lian Y, Yang R, Sun H.
abstractText:
Objective

Wearable single-lead ECG has expanded arrhythmia screening, but many recordings are inconclusive, and each corpus defines that word differently. We ask how much deployment error is un-analyzable input rather than misclassification when analyzability is measured with one instrument. Approach. We evaluate three diagnostic databases in-domain and leave-dataset-out under a strict loss counting windows carrying each corpus's inconclusive label as errors unless deferred. We score analyzability with an unsupervised morphological criterion calibrated against three experts on free-living ECG. Reference unreadability is sparse and imbalanced: only seven of 15 subjects contain an unreadable window and one supplies 88% of all unreadable windows. Thresholded sensitivity and every prevalence or true-share correction are therefore exploratory. Main results. The criterion flags almost all expert-unreadable windows but only subsets of the windows labelled inconclusive by their corpora: an inconclusive rate measures convention as much as signal. At tau_a = 0.50, criterion-positive windows are 8.1%, 56.7% and 69.6% of the strict proxy loss on Holter, handheld and patch. The true-share point intervals lie below 50% on handheld and above it on patch, but joint calibration-and-sampling envelopes span 50% on both and still do at the Youden threshold 0.60. On handheld, the calibration-only envelope is more than twice as wide as the corpus-sampling-only envelope. Gate-versus-confidence ordering changes with the accounting and corpus; no general selective-risk advantage of the gate is established. Significance. Corpus labels, criterion flags and latent expert unreadability must not be conflated. A gate can win by predicting a labelling convention, and this retrospective study validates neither transfer to smartwatch dry electrodes nor improvement in patient outcomes. Measure the inconclusive rate with a stated criterion on the raw signal; do not inherit it from a corpus label.

title: Numerical simulation of aortic hemodynamic effects modulated by the intra-aortic rotary blood pump with different speed modes.
authorString: Zhou S, Giridharan GA, Chen R, El-Baz A, Gregory SD, Qu P, Song Y, Mu X, Wang Y.
abstractText: Intra-aortic rotary blood pump (IARBP) can improve cardiac and renal function for cardiorenal syndrome (CRS) patients. However, the mechanism of hemodynamic changes in the aorta caused by IARBP is not fully understood. Therefore, this study quantitatively analyzed the aortic hemodynamic effects with IARBP support to evaluate its potential clinical benefits and risks. A three-dimensional aortic model was established from patient-specific image data and coupled with an IARBP. Hemodynamic characteristics and potential blood damage in the aorta under different IARBP speed modes, including flow field, blood flow velocity, pressure, wall shear stress-related indices, scalar shear stress (SSS), and hemolysis index (HI), were systematically evaluated using computational fluid dynamics (CFD). Results showed that constant-speed IARBP support increased downstream aortic flow velocity and pressure by 30.79% and 5.28%, respectively. The pump-outlet jet impinged on the aortic wall, creating localized regions with wall shear stress (WSS) exceeding 40 Pa and potentially increasing the risk of vascular endothelial injury. Compared with the constant speed mode, pulsatile speed modes further reduced low WSS areas to lower atherosclerosis risk, especially that counterpulsation mode increased renal blood flow by 19.33% and reduced HI by 14.4%, but was less favorable for cerebral and upper-limb perfusion. Copulsation mode performed better in this regard. Overall, this study verified the potential clinical benefits and risks of IARBP especially at pulsatile speeds in optimizing downstream and upstream perfusion and reducing vascular adverse events, which could provide support and guidance for optimizing IARBP speed and its clinical treatment strategy.

title: Severe Hypercoagulability With Nonbacterial Thrombotic Endocarditis After KRAS Inhibitor Exposure: A Perfect Storm.
authorString: Villa-Etchegoyen C, Fohtung RB, Lee KS, Ayoub C, Arsanjani R.
abstractText:
Background

Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE) is a rare malignancy-associated condition causing systemic embolization and valvular dysfunction. Its presentation as new severe mitral regurgitation (MR) may be difficult to recognize.

Case summary

A 76-year-old man with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma developed progressive dyspnea after treatment with the KRAS inhibitor daraxonrasib. Echocardiography demonstrated new severe MR with leaflet thickening and broad-based echodensities. His course was complicated by pulmonary embolism, recurrent coronary thrombosis, and persistently negative blood cultures. Transesophageal echocardiography confirmed bilateral leaflet involvement with a central coaptation defect. Anticoagulation was changed to low-molecular-weight heparin.

Discussion

NBTE should be considered in patients with malignancy presenting with new MR and thrombotic events without evidence of infection. The temporal association with KRAS inhibition is noteworthy but does not establish causality.

Take-home message

NBTE may present as subacute MR. Echocardiography and clinical context are essential for timely diagnosis and management.

title: Seven Novel Sonographic Signs
authorString: Ji X.
abstractText: Ultrasound is a widely used imaging modality in clinical practice, and sonographic signs serve as valuable teaching tools that aid in pattern recognition and diagnosis. This review consolidates five novel sonographic signs previously proposed by the author, including the Cracked Earth Sign for subcutaneous edema, the Mushroom Cap Sign for localized gallbladder adenomyomatosis, the LTS Sign for dilated cardiomyopathy, the LTI Sign for endocardial fibroelastosis, and the Three Pipes Sign for the suprasternal long-axis view of the aortic arch. The SFH Sign for advanced cervical insufficiency and the Gentle Upslope Sign for the parvus–tardus waveform are proposed for the first time in this paper. Collectively, these seven signs span the fields of superficial ultrasound, abdominal ultrasound, echocardiography, and obstetric ultrasound. For each sign, its naming logic, definition, clinical implications, and teaching value are described. This review aims to facilitate a better understanding of these signs and to promote their use as teaching aids in ultrasound education.

title: Lipid Mediators and Metabolic Inflammation: From Molecular Mechanisms to a New Therapeutic Paradigm
authorString: Ivchuk V.
abstractText: Chronic low-grade inflammation is a common pathogenetic mechanism of metabolic, cardiovascular, renal, hepatic, and neurodegenerative diseases. This essay critically analyzes the role of lipid mediators in the pathogenesis of chronic inflammation and substantiates the thesis that the key factor in the transition from acute to chronic inflammation is not the excessive production of pro-inflammatory mediators, but the insufficiency of pro-resolution pathways. The molecular mechanisms of metabolic reprogramming of immune cells are reviewed, in particular, the switching of macrophages between glycolytic (M1) and oxidative (M2) phenotypes, the role of CD36 and FATP2 in lipotoxicity, impaired β-oxidation of fatty acids, and the accumulation of toxic lipid intermediates (free cholesterol, ceramides, lactate, succinate). The dual nature of lipid mediators is analyzed – from pro-inflammatory eicosanoids (LTB4, PGE2) to specialized pro-resolution mediators (SPMs), including lipoxins, resolvins, protectins and maresins. Data on the imbalance between pro-inflammatory and pro-resolution mediators in atherosclerosis, metabolic syndrome, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, non-alcoholic steatohepatitis, neurodegenerative and autoimmune diseases are presented. Special attention is paid to the concept of “unalamation”, which radically rethinks the etiology of chronic inflammation. A therapeutic paradigm based on the stimulation of endogenous pro-resolution pathways (SPMs and their synthetic analogues) is substantiated as an alternative to traditional anti-inflammatory therapy that inhibits pro-inflammatory mediators. The limitations of existing research, controversies, and prospects for further scientific exploration in this field are discussed.

title: Reel Syndrome in Subcutaneous Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator Causing Lead Dislodgement and Inappropriate Shock: Successful Rescue with Intermuscular Two-Incision Technique and Serratus Anterior Plane Block
authorString: Uran C, Uccello A.
abstractText:
Background:

Reel syndrome, rotation of the generator on its transverse axis with coiling of the lead, is a rare cause of cardiac implantable electronic device failure. While described for transvenous systems, it is exceptionally rare in subcutaneous ICDs (S-ICD). Case presentation: A 63-year-old woman with dilated cardiomyopathy and S-ICD implanted in 2022 for secondary prevention in a standard subcutaneous pocket presented with a shock during exertion. Remote monitoring (LATITUDE) had not been activated. Device interrogation showed an inappropriate 80J shock due to myopotential oversensing after caudal retraction of the lead. Chest X-ray documented Reel syndrome with proximal coiling around the can and distal tip retracted to the subcostal region, >10 cm from the manubrio-sternal junction, with horizontalization of the shock coil, incompatible with effective defibrillation. Management: The system was explanted and a new S-ICD re-implanted using the intermuscular two-incision technique in the virtual space between serratus anterior and latissimus dorsi. The procedure was performed under ultrasound-guided serratus anterior plane block combined with parasternal block. The generator was anchored to the fascia with non-absorbable sutures. Defibrillation test was effective at 40J. Remote monitoring was activated.

Conclusion:

To our knowledge, this is one of the few documented cases of Reel syndrome in S-ICD with both radiographic and stored electrogram evidence of inappropriate 80J shock, rescued with intermuscular two-incision technique under ultrasound-guided serratus anterior plane block. Intermuscular fixation with non-absorbable sutures, combined with regional anesthesia and systematic remote monitoring, ensures device stability and maintains continuous defibrillation protection.

title: Left anterior laryngeal loop of the common carotid artery in a cluster of bilateral cervicothoracic vascular variants: a case report.
authorString: Dincă V, Jianu AM, Rusu MC.
abstractText:
Purpose

The common carotid artery (CCA) normally ascends in the carotid sheath, posterolateral to the larynx and trachea. Anterior or pretracheal CCA courses are rare and have been described mainly on the right, usually in relation to a high-riding brachiocephalic trunk (BCT) or another arch-level anomaly. We report a CTA case with a common-origin left CCA-BCT trunk, a high-riding BCT and bilateral carotid redundancy, including a left anterior laryngeal CCA loop.

Methods

Computed tomography angiography (CTA) of the aortic arch and bilateral carotid systems was reviewed using multiplanar reformatting and three-dimensional volume-rendered reconstruction. Vessel loops, branching points and relationships to the hyoid-laryngeal framework, thyroid gland and adjacent skeletal landmarks were recorded.

Results

CTA showed a common-origin left CCA-BCT trunk with a high-riding BCT measuring 3.27 cm. The right CCA formed a 1.79 cm lateral loop and bifurcated posterolateral to the hyoid-laryngeal framework; the right external carotid artery (ECA) gave rise to a linguofacial trunk and then formed a retromandibular loop. The left CCA formed a 2.15 cm intramediastinal loop and a 1.75 cm anterior laryngeal loop. The left superior thyroid artery arose directly from the CCA. The left ECA showed independent branching and a retromandibular loop. Tortuosity indices ranged from 33.1% to 92.7%; all segments were tortuous and the right internal carotid artery additionally formed a kink (apex angle 87.3°).

Conclusion

This case documents a rare left anterior laryngeal CCA loop in association with bilateral carotid and external carotid branching variants. The left-sided anterior loop is the main surgical finding because it brings a major cervical artery close to the anterior laryngeal operative field. Recognition of this pattern is relevant before front-of-neck airway access, thyroid surgery, laryngotracheal surgery and central neck procedures.

title: One-Year Sac Regression After Endovascular Aneurysm Repair Is Not Always Associated With Favorable Outcomes.
authorString: Park JK, Park YJ, Ryu HJ, Lee MH, Yang SS, Kim YW.
abstractText:
Objective

It is not clear whether 1-year sac regression after EVAR indicates the completion of treatment. The purpose of our study is to identify the association between 1-year sac behaviors and clinical outcomes and specifically whether it is safe to extend follow-up intervals for patients with 1-year sac regression.

Methods

This is a retrospective, single-center cohort study of 317 consecutive patients who underwent non-ruptured EVAR from January 2011 to December 2020. All patients were stratified into three groups based on their 1-year sac behavior: sac regression (decrease in diameter of ≥ 5mm), stable sac (<5mm change), and sac expansion (increase in diameter of ≥ 5mm). The primary outcome was late re-intervention, including endovascular re-intervention and open conversion.

Results

A total of 317 patients were enrolled based on sac status on 1-year follow-up imaging: 126 with sac regression, 177 with stable sacs, and 14 with sac expansion. Over a median follow-up of 69.5 months, sac expansion was a significant risk factor for late re-intervention compared to sac regression (HR, 2.335; 95% CI, 1.048 - 5.191; P=0.047). However, the rate of late re-intervention was not significantly lower in the sac regression group compared to the stable sac group (HR, 0.694; 95% CI, 0.383 - 1.258; P=0.229). Among patients with sac regression at 1 year, 5.6% (7/126) required embolization due to endoleak, and 3.2% (4/126) needed open conversions.

Conclusion

Late re-intervention rates did not differ significantly between patients with stable versus regressed sacs at 1 year. Patients with sac regression also require regular imaging surveillance to detect late complications.

title: AI-enhanced hemodynamic prediction of patent ductus arteriosus severity in premature infants.
authorString: Kim T, Choi J, Chung MJ, Yang M, Ahn SY, Chang YS, Sung SI.
abstractText:
Background

Hemodynamically significant patent ductus arteriosus (HSPDA) requires timely assessment in premature very low birth weight (VLBW) infants. This study aimed to develop and validate an artificial intelligence (AI)-based surveillance system for predicting HSPDA and supporting real-time NICU decision-making.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed electronic medical record data from VLBW infants with PDA admitted to the Samsung Medical Center NICU between 2013 and 2022. After excluding records with congenital heart disease or missing critical echocardiographic parameters, machine-learning models were trained on 85% of the dataset and tested on the remaining 15%.

Results

The best-performing model, Extra Trees, achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.829, with a sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value of 0.767, 0.766, 0.694, and 0.825, respectively. For transitional records shifting between hemodynamic states, the AUC, sensitivity, and specificity were 0.700, 0.722, and 0.606, respectively, based on the proposed transition-optimized threshold.

Conclusion

The AI-based Extra Trees model demonstrated a robust ability to predict the hemodynamic status of PDA in VLBW infants. Thus, it may help NICU clinicians optimize conservative management and improve clinical decision-making.

Impact

Our AI model achieves 0.829 AUC for predicting hemodynamically significant PDA in premature infants using routine NICU data without requiring echocardiography This study uniquely predicts PDA hemodynamic severity through multimodal clinical data integration, advancing beyond previous binary presence/absence classifications We introduce a transition-optimized threshold that detects dynamic hemodynamic changes, enabling precise monitoring during conservative management The model provides accessible real-time PDA assessment for resource-limited NICUs lacking immediate echocardiographic expertise, optimizing intervention timing and fluid management strategies Our validation across 1033 VLBW infants over 10 years demonstrates robust performance with only 12-h data requirements.

title: A Rare ISL1 Promoter Variant in a Case-Control Cohort of Patent Ductus Arteriosus: In Vitro Functional Characterization
authorString: Zheng S, Wang S, Qi J, Chen H, Yang Q, Chen L, He G.
abstractText: Patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) is a common congenital heart disease. ISL LIM Homeobox 1 (ISL1), a master transcription factor for cardiac progenitor cells, has been linked to CHD, but its promoter variants in PDA have not been explored. We sequenced the ISL1 promoter in 320 PDA patients and 302 healthy controls. Ten variants were found across the ISL1 promoter. Six were identified in patients; five were also present in controls, and one novel heterozygous variant, g.5238 C>T, was found exclusively in a single PDA patient and absent in all controls (two-sided Fisher exact test, p = 1.00). Functional assays using dual‑luciferase reporter in HEK293 and A7r5 cells and electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA) demonstrated that this variant significantly increased reporter activity and altered nuclear protein binding patterns. In addition, bioinformatic analysis predicted disruption of an E2F1 site and creation of novel MYC, MAX, NFE2L2, USF1, and MYCN binding sites. This variant may be associated with PDA susceptibility, although its clinical significance remains uncertain. Our findings highlight the importance of promoter region variants in PDA and provide preliminary information for future studies.
