title: Sepsis: Epidemiology, Pathophysiology, and Management.
authorString: Pan GT, Deng Y, Ma LR, Li YT, Qian Y, Ma YH, Rao HW, Zhu YZ, Yan PY.
abstractText: Sepsis remains a major cause of global morbidity and mortality despite advances in recognition, antimicrobial therapy, and organ support, reflecting its biological heterogeneity and the absence of broadly effective host-directed treatments. Here, we synthesize recent evidence across the three domains that define contemporary sepsis: epidemiology, pathophysiology, and management. Global and regional data indicate a persistently high but uneven burden, shaped by differences in case definitions, population structure, healthcare resources, and ascertainment. Mechanistically, sepsis is best viewed as an interconnected systems disorder in which hyperinflammation and immunoparalysis coexist with oxidative stress, endothelial and coagulation injury, immunometabolic dysfunction, gut dysbiosis, mitochondrial damage, and dysregulated programmed cell death, collectively driving organ dysfunction. Current management remains centered on timely antimicrobials, source control, individualized fluid and vasopressor therapy, corticosteroids, and organ support, while biomarker-guided immunotherapy and other host-directed strategies remain investigational. Recent randomized trials have mainly refined how established treatments are delivered rather than identified a universally effective new therapy. We also evaluate preclinical evidence for natural compounds targeting inflammatory and cell-death networks and highlight persistent methodological, pharmacokinetic, and translational barriers. Integrating rigorous phenotyping, mechanistic biomarkers, and guideline-based care may provide a more realistic path toward precision sepsis therapy.

title: Integration of Aromatherapy and Essential Oils in Asthma Symptom Relief: A Narrative Review.
authorString: Odoom A.
abstractText:
Background and aims

Asthma affects 262 million people globally, causing 455,000 preventable deaths, with higher mortality in low-resource areas due to limited diagnosis and treatment. Aromatherapy, using bioactive essential oils (EOs), has emerged as a promising complementary approach for asthma symptom management.

Methods

This review synthesizes the current evidence on the therapeutic potential of EOs in alleviating asthma-related inflammation, bronchoconstriction, and immune dysregulation through anti-inflammatory, bronchodilatory, and immunomodulatory mechanisms.

Results

Key oils such as lavender, eucalyptus, and peppermint demonstrate efficacy in reducing airway hyperresponsiveness, oxidative stress, and Th2-mediated inflammation, supported by preclinical and clinical studies. Methods of application, including inhalation, topical use, and environmental diffusion, are evaluated for their physiological and psychological benefits, particularly in stress and sleep modulation, which are critical to asthma control. Safety considerations, such as allergenicity, proper dosing, and potential drug interactions, are emphasized to ensure safe integration with conventional therapies.

Conclusion

Despite the promising findings, further large-scale clinical trials are needed to validate the efficacy, optimize protocols, and explore personalized approaches based on genetic and phenotypic variability. This review underscores aromatherapy's role as an adjunctive therapy within a holistic asthma management framework, bridging traditional knowledge with contemporary scientific validation to improve patient outcomes.

title: Does receiving red yeast rice prescriptions (LipoCol Forte®) increase the risk of end-stage renal disease or not? A retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Chang CC, Lam F, Yeh CC, Lin JG, Chen TL, Liao CC.
abstractText:
Background

The potential relationship between the consumption of red yeast rice (RYR) and the development of end-stage renal disease (ESRD) remains poorly understood. We aimed to evaluate the risk of ESRD in patients who used RYR.

Methods

Utilizing insurance claim records from 2010 to 2014, we performed a retrospective cohort analysis comparing 67,876 individuals using RYR against a control group of 90,836 lovastatin users (non-RYR group), with follow-up extending through 2019. The incidence of ESRD was analyzed using adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) within Cox proportional hazard models.

Results

During follow-up, the ESRD incidence was 0.9 per 1,000 person-years in RYR users, compared to 3.7 per 1,000 person-years in lovastatin users (HR 0.36, 95% CI 0.32-0.40). A dose-dependent reduction in ESRD risk was observed with increasing RYR prescriptions. Sensitivity analysis, excluding ESRD cases within the initial six months, confirmed a persistent association between RYR use and reduced ESRD risk (adjusted HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.64-0.81).

Conclusion

RYR intake may be linked to a decreased likelihood of progressing to ESRD. Despite these promising results, factors such as medication adherence necessitate cautious interpretation. Further randomized controlled trials are required to validate these findings and clarify RYR's role in slowing kidney disease progression.

title: Physiological monitoring and physiology-informed strategies in cardiac arrest: current evidence and clinical translation.
authorString: Melo RH, Joelsons D, Guimaraes HP, Passos RDH.
abstractText:
Background

Despite advances in cardiac arrest management, survival with favorable neurological outcomes remains limited. Physiological monitoring may complement standardized resuscitation by providing real-time information about circulatory effectiveness, reversible causes, and treatment responses. However, whether physiology-guided interventions improve patient-centered outcomes remains uncertain. This narrative review examines the current evidence and clinical applicability of physiological monitoring during resuscitation, physiology-informed rescue strategies, and individualized post-cardiac arrest care.

Main body

During cardiopulmonary resuscitation, invasive arterial pressure monitoring, waveform capnography, and echocardiography provide complementary information about the circulation generated by chest compressions and potential mechanisms of resuscitation failure. Although observational and experimental studies support their physiological relevance, no adult diastolic pressure target or pressure-guided vasopressor strategy has been validated to improve survival or neurological recovery. Recent randomized trials of transesophageal echocardiography have demonstrated physiological or procedural effects without establishing clinical benefit. Among rescue strategies, extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation has yielded inconsistent results across randomized trials, with potential benefits dependent on patient selection, intervention timing, and system capabilities. Resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta has not improved clinical outcomes in randomized evaluation, while head-up resuscitation remains investigational. Following the return of spontaneous circulation, randomized trials have challenged the benefits of uniformly higher blood pressure and oxygenation targets, mild hypercapnia, and deeper or prolonged temperature control. Individualized approaches incorporating cerebral autoregulation, venous congestion, and cardiopulmonary physiology are physiologically appealing but lack prospective validation.

Conclusion

Physiological assessment may complement established resuscitation algorithms by refining clinical decisions during and after cardiac arrest. However, improvements in physiological measurements should not be equated with improved patient outcomes. Future trials should determine whether predefined, physiology-guided treatment strategies improve survival and neurological recovery.

title: Strengthening post-market COVID-19 vaccine safety surveillance and research: An interpretive description study from Kenya, South Africa, and Canada.
authorString: Naz AliSher A, Shaik S, Myburgh N, Ndaba N, Hinga A, Okore W, Sang S, Siraj S, Qwabi T, Gutu K, Matano A, Di Castri A, Kochhar S, Kagucia EW, Dangor Z, Cutland CL, Top KA, International Network of Special Immunization Services (INSIS) Investigators.
abstractText: Post-market vaccine safety surveillance and research are essential to detect and evaluate rare adverse events following immunization (AEFIs) not identified in pre-licensure clinical trials, such as myocarditis post-COVID-19 vaccination. AEFI surveillance infrastructure varies between jurisdictions. Factors that enable or hinder vaccine safety evaluation across diverse settings are not well understood. The study objective was to examine clinical, social, and structural/system factors that enable AEFI case identification, reporting, data and biosample collection in high-income countries (HICs) and low-and middle-income countries (LMICs). We conducted a qualitative study informed by Interpretive Description in Kenya, South Africa, and Canada. Three participant groups were recruited using purposive and snowball sampling: (1) key informants with leadership roles in AEFI surveillance and research, (2) healthcare workers, research and laboratory staff involved in vaccine safety evaluation, and (3) past participants in COVID-19 vaccine safety studies. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and focus group discussions. Thematic analysis was conducted. Eighteen key informants, 37 healthcare workers and research staff, and 27 past research participants were enrolled. Facilitators and barriers were identified across two domains: AEFI surveillance and investigation, and vaccine safety research participation. AEFI surveillance and investigation were shaped by trust in system responsiveness, beliefs and awareness around AEFI reporting, digital innovation, and implementation gaps. Research participation was shaped by altruism and social influence, logistics and research infrastructure, and institutional policies and privacy. Facilitators for AEFI surveillance and research included established policies and procedures for surveillance, digital tools, empathic communication about AEFIs, and convenient research processes. Barriers included limitations in workforce capacity, diagnostic testing and funding (especially in LMICs), and cumbersome research approval processes. Findings underscore the need for globally harmonized standards and locally tailored strategies to support AEFI surveillance and research in LMICs and HICs that are patient/participant-centered and include sustainable investments in infrastructure and workforce capacity.

title: Retraction: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Clinical Effectiveness of Intravenous Magnesium Sulphate in the Treatment of Acute Fast Atrial Fibrillation in Non-surgical Adult Patients.
authorString: Mupunga K, Chandavengerwa W, Nyabadza DP, Masungo AB.
abstractText: [This retracts the article DOI: 10.7759/cureus.110978.].

title: Health-Care Burden of Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease in Hong Kong in the Post-COVID Pandemic Era-Impact of Phenotype and Exacerbation History.
authorString: Kwok WC, Choo A, Zhou L, Ma TF, Leung ISH, Wong CK, Ho JCM.
abstractText:
Rationale

Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is known to be associated with substantial health-care utilization and economic costs. Since the COVID-19 pandemic, the epidemiology of various diseases has undergone significant changes, it is important to evaluate the health-care impact and economic burden of acute exacerbations of COPD (AECOPD) in the post-pandemic period, along with factors influencing this burden, to inform effective management strategies and health-care planning.

Objectives

To assess the health-care and economic burden of severe AECOPD from 2022 to 2024, and to identify factors associated with direct health-care costs.

Methods

A territory-wide retrospective cohort study was conducted. Adult patients with AECOPD admitted to acute public hospitals in Hong Kong were included. The primary outcomes were the total number of AECOPD admissions and the associated direct health-care costs.

Measurements and main results

From 2022 to 2024, a total of 11,465 patients were admitted to acute public hospitals for severe AECOPD, resulting in 25,053 hospitalization episodes and 150,717 bed days. The estimated direct health-care costs totaled 1.259 billion Hong Kong dollars (HKD). AECOPD admission numbers increased significantly over the 3 years. Patients with eosinophilic and non-eosinophilic phenotypes had similar annual direct health-care costs related to severe AECOPD. Patients with co-existing bronchiectasis had a significantly higher annual number of severe AECOPD episodes and direct health-care costs from severe AECOPD.

Conclusions

Severe AECOPD imposes a substantial burden on the health-care system. The presence of bronchiectasis and a greater frequency of severe AECOPD episodes were identified as possible factors linked to increased direct health-care costs.

title: Developing an Early Childhood Environmental Health Vulnerability Index to Assess Cumulative Health Impacts Across Contiguous US.
authorString: Liu S, Yang A, Horm D, Zhu M, Cai C.
abstractText: Young children (birth to age five) are uniquely vulnerable to environmental hazards due to their higher exposure relative to body weight, rapid physiological and neurological development, and strong reliance on caregivers for protection and care. Such risks are often amplified in marginalized communities with socioeconomic disadvantage and limited access to resources. However, widely used indices, such as the Social Vulnerability Index (SVI), the Climate Vulnerability Index (CVI), and the Child Opportunity Index (COI), were not specifically developed for young children and may not capture the combined environmental and socioeconomic risks faced by this age group. To address this critical gap, we developed a county-level Early Childhood Environmental Health Vulnerability Index (EC-EHVI) for the contiguous US using multidimensional indicators within an Exposure-Sensitivity-Adaptive Capacity framework and informed by Bronfenbrenner's bioecological model. We identified the underlying drivers and the spatial patterns of the EC-EHVI. Our results showed that the EC-EHVI exhibited the strongest association with county-level mortality among young children and explained a larger proportion of spatial heterogeneity compared with the SVI, CVI, and COI. Elevated vulnerability clustered in the Great Plains and Southeastern US, where over half of high-vulnerability counties were exposure-driven, and 411 high-high hotspots were identified. The EC-EHVI offers a valuable spatial decision-support tool for designing targeted, place-based interventions and advancing environmental health equity for young children.

title: Machine learning-based prediction of clinical outcomes and left ventricular ejection fraction improvement after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with reduced ejection fraction.
authorString: Steinbuch L, Itelman E, Altman Y, Yacobi B, Goren-Peyser O, Bental T, Shostak Y, Codner P, Gurevitz C, Levi A, Witberg G, Talmor Barkan Y, Kornowski R, Perl L.
abstractText:
Aims

The expected clinical and functional trajectory after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with left ventricular dysfunction remains uncertain. Recent trials have highlighted substantial heterogeneity in both clinical outcomes and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) improvement, underscoring the need for improved post-PCI prognostic risk stratification in this high-risk population. This study aimed to develop machine learning models predicting clinical outcomes and LVEF improvement after PCI in patients with reduced LVEF.

Methods and results

This retrospective single-centre study included adults undergoing PCI between 2004 and 2025 with baseline LVEF <45%. Two CatBoost models were developed using 53 routinely available pre- and intra-procedural predictors. The primary endpoint was a 1-year composite of death, myocardial infarction, target vessel revascularization, or coronary artery bypass grafting. The secondary endpoint was an absolute LVEF increase of ≥10 percentage points. Performance was evaluated on a held-out test set using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), area under the precision-recall curve (PR-AUC), and enrichment analysis. The dataset included 3336 procedures from 2793 patients (median LVEF 35%). For the primary endpoint (n = 2152; event rate 37.5%), the model achieved an AUC of 0.78 (95% CI: 0.73-0.83) and a PR-AUC of 0.70 (95% CI: 0.63-0.77), with event rates of 83.7% in the highest-risk decile and 9.3% in the lowest-risk decile. For LVEF improvement (n = 2551; 34.7% improved), performance was moderate (AUC 0.73), with enrichment to 76.9% in the highest-probability decile.

Conclusion

Machine learning models using routinely available patient and procedural data enabled meaningful prognostic stratification in patients with left ventricular dysfunction undergoing PCI, supporting individualized estimation of clinical and functional trajectories after revascularization.

title: Personalized Cardiac Rehabilitation: Integrating Biomarker-Guided, Technology-Enabled, and Population-Specific Strategies in Exercise Medicine.
authorString: Liu T, Xia Y, Wei L.
abstractText: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading global cause of mortality and morbidity, necessitating continuous advancement in secondary prevention strategies. Cardiac rehabilitation (CR), a cornerstone of comprehensive cardiovascular care, has been significantly enhanced by innovations in exercise medicine, evolving towards more personalized and accessible paradigms. This review synthesizes the current frontiers in exercise-based CR, focusing on the synergistic integration of three transformative domains: technological innovation, precision medicine, and population-specific strategies. We first delineate the established physiological benefits and evidence-based efficacy of exercise therapy within CR frameworks. Subsequently, we examine the application of digital and intelligent technologies-including wearable devices, remote monitoring, artificial intelligence (AI), and big data analytics-which enable dynamic, data-driven patient management and remote care delivery. The paper further explores the paradigm of precision exercise prescription, guided by biomarkers, genetic profiling, and other individual biological data, to tailor interventions for optimal safety and therapeutic yield. Special emphasis is placed on addressing the heterogeneous needs of key patient populations, such as the elderly, women, and those with specific comorbidities like heart failure or arrhythmias, by outlining individualized strategies that improve engagement and effectiveness. Finally, we discuss future directions, highlighting multimodal technology platforms and in-depth precision medicine applications as key drivers for the next generation of CR, while critically evaluating the evidence readiness of emerging technologies and addressing implementation barriers. This review aims to inform clinical practice and guide future research towards developing more personalized, technology-enabled, and equitable cardiac rehabilitation models.

title: Analysis of risk factors for glaucoma associated with environmental persistent pollutant exposure based on the NHANES database: Construction of a machine learning prediction model and exploratory pathway decomposition.
authorString: Wang J, Han J, Dong Z.
abstractText: Glaucoma, an irreversible blinding eye disease, may be influenced by environmental pollutant exposure. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the associations between exposure to environmental persistent pollutants and glaucoma risk, and to explore the underlying pathogenic mechanisms. A cross-sectional analysis was performed using data from the U.S. National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), including 2272 participants. Baseline characteristics were summarized, and serum concentrations of 12 PFAS compounds and 4 heavy metals were measured. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, and subgroup interaction tests were used to examine associations between exposure levels and glaucoma risk. Exploratory pathway decomposition was conducted for key exposure factors nominally associated with glaucoma. Additionally, multiple machine learning models were constructed, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was applied for model interpretability. Glaucoma was defined by self-report, which may underestimate true prevalence and cannot distinguish glaucoma subtypes. Participants with glaucoma had a higher prevalence of diabetes and hypertension, as well as higher blood lead and MPAH levels. In the primary analysis, inorganic mercury showed a nominal inverse association with glaucoma, whereas higher quartiles of MPAH and blood lead showed nominal positive associations. However, none of these associations remained statistically significant after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction (minimum *q* = 0.128). Restricted cubic spline models indicated nonlinear dose-response relationships between some exposures and glaucoma risk. Multiple machine learning models achieved satisfactory performance in predicting glaucoma. Exploratory pathway decomposition suggested that the nominal association between MPAH and glaucoma risk might be partly mediated by pathways involving age, race/ethnicity, and blood pressure; however, these results should be interpreted with caution given the cross-sectional design and the lack of FDR-corrected significance. Nominal associations were observed between certain PFAS compounds and heavy metals and glaucoma prevalence, but none survived FDR correction. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger studies. Interpretable machine learning achieved modest discrimination (AUC 0.62-0.74) for glaucoma risk, which may be adequate for population-level signal detection but not for individual diagnostic use. These findings provide epidemiological evidence and methodological support for identifying environmental risk factors, screening susceptible populations, and guiding early prevention of glaucoma.

title: “Every New Day Is a Gift”: Heart Transplantation Beyond 70 Years—From Chronological Age to Biological Reserve and the Patient Perspective
authorString: Ferrara N.
abstractText: Heart transplantation has evolved from an experimental procedure performed mainly in younger patients into an established treatment for selected individuals with advanced heart failure. One important change has been the declining role of chronological age as an isolated criterion for transplant candidacy. Historical experience, together with advances in immunosuppression, surgical techniques, perioperative care, and patient selection, has shown that carefully selected patients in their seventh decade can achieve favorable outcomes after transplantation. Contemporary guidelines recommend a multidimensional assessment that considers comorbidities, functional status, frailty, organ function, nutritional status, cognitive and psychosocial factors, and the potential for postoperative recovery and rehabilitation. Recent registry data indicate that heart transplantation is increasingly being performed in patients aged ≥70 years and can be associated with favorable outcomes, although these recipients remain a highly selected population. This narrative review summarizes the historical evolution of age criteria in heart transplantation, the evidence concerning recipients aged ≥70 years, and the growing importance of biological and functional reserve in transplant evaluation. Particular attention is paid to frailty as a multidimensional geriatric condition rather than simply a consequence of chronological age. The review is complemented by the perspective of Umberto, a 72-year-old man who recently underwent heart transplantation. His experience illustrates the emotional, functional, and social dimensions of transplantation in later life and provides a patient-centered perspective on the geriatric principle that chronological age should be interpreted in the context of biological reserve, resilience, and individual potential for recovery.

title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare in Cambodia: Enhancing Access and Patient Outcomes.
authorString: Lorn S, Chhon Y, San T, Sorn V.
abstractText: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly reshaping healthcare globally and may offer opportunities to strengthen health systems in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), including Cambodia. AI-enabled technologies, including machine learning, deep learning, predictive analytics, computer vision, wearable devices, and generative AI, could help address persistent health-system challenges such as shortages and maldistribution of healthcare professionals, limited specialist services, unequal access to care, and constrained resources, particularly in rural and underserved communities. However, translating these technological opportunities into meaningful health benefits requires more than access to AI tools. Cambodia faces important barriers related to digital infrastructure, health-information systems, data quality and availability, workforce capacity, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, affordability, and regulatory and ethical governance. At the same time, ongoing digital transformation, the expansion of electronic health information systems, emerging AI research capacity, and national efforts toward AI governance provide an evolving foundation for responsible adoption. This perspective examines the current and potential role of AI in Cambodia's healthcare system, focusing on applications in disease diagnosis, clinical decision support, telemedicine, public health surveillance, healthcare administration, and health-system management. Particular attention is given to the gap between technological feasibility and sustainable health-system implementation, including local validation, interoperability, economic evaluation, workforce preparedness, and long-term financing. AI should therefore be introduced through a phased, evidence-based, and patient-centered approach in which technology complements rather than replaces healthcare professionals. Investments in digital infrastructure, human capacity, locally relevant research, ethical governance, and sustainable implementation will be essential to ensure that AI contributes to improved healthcare access, quality, equity, and patient outcomes in Cambodia.

title: Oesophageal perforation secondary to denture ingestion requiring thoracotomy and T-tube placement: a rare case report.
authorString: Baronos K, Lee S, Arshad S, Alogakos M, Ayoub R, Sutton C, Bowrey D.
abstractText: Oesophageal perforation from foreign body ingestion is a life-threatening emergency. Dentures pose particular risk due to irregular shape, size, and radiolucency. We present a 69-year-old female who accidentally ingested a denture. Radiography identified the foreign body at C4/C5. Endoscopic retrieval failed due to mucosal embedding, and a through-and-through oesophageal tear was confirmed. She underwent emergency right thoracotomy with denture retrieval. Given localized inflammation, a 4 cm perforation, and pneumomediastinum, a T-tube was placed across the defect instead of primary repair. Post-operatively, she required intensive care, enteral feeding, and prolonged chest drainage. Recovery was complicated by suspected mediastinitis, candidiasis, and deconditioning, but she ultimately tolerated oral intake and was discharged. In complex thoracic OP with inflammation or a large defect, T-tube placement offers a reliable, oesophagus-preserving alternative to primary repair. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of radiolucent dentures and the importance of multidisciplinary decision-making.

title: Titanium Hypersensitivity as a Potential Contributor to Bronchopleural Fistula and Surgical Staple Extrusion Following Lung Cancer Surgery: A Case Report.
authorString: Lucena M, Regalo S, Manso Preto L, Todo Bom A, Regateiro F.
abstractText:
Introduction

Titanium is widely regarded as a highly biocompatible material and is extensively used in surgical implants. Nevertheless, delayed hypersensitivity reactions are increasingly recognized and may act as potential contributing factors to implant-related complications. Thoracic manifestations remain exceptionally rare, and their impact on clinical decision-making is poorly described.

Case description

A 65-year-old man, with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), a 60 pack-year smoking history (former smoker since 2005) and severe gas transfer impairment, underwent video-assisted thoracoscopic right lower lobectomy for lung adenocarcinoma. The postoperative course was complicated by a prolonged air leak requiring surgical staple reinforcement and talc pleurodesis. Approximately 2 months after surgery, the patient developed invasive pneumococcal disease with Streptococcus pneumoniae bacteremia, which resolved following appropriate antimicrobial therapy. Several months later, the patient developed a bronchopleural fistula (BPF) with endobronchial extrusion of titanium staples, confirmed by computed tomography and bronchoscopy. Given the unusual presentation, allergy evaluation was performed. Patch testing demonstrated epicutaneous sensitization with positive reactions to titanium (IV) oxalate hydrate, cobalt (II) chloride hexahydrate, and manganese chloride. The allergy work-up had a direct therapeutic impact. Endoscopic closure with an Amplatzer device, a procedure documented for central BPFs, was initially considered but deliberately avoided because the considered device contains nitinol (a nickel-titanium alloy), which would expose the sensitized patient to additional titanium. Owing to the high surgical risk, conservative multidisciplinary management with close clinical and radiological surveillance was adopted.

Discussion

BPF is a recognized complication after lung resection and is inherently multifactorial. In this patient, established surgical, anatomical (right lower lobectomy), and patient-related comorbidity risk factors coexisted with documented titanium sensitization, suggesting that hypersensitivity may have acted as a potential contributing or modulating factor to impaired tissue integration and staple extrusion. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of titanium hypersensitivity and the distinction between cutaneous sensitization and operative tissue allergy. Importantly, it illustrates how allergy assessment may directly influence therapeutic decision-making by avoiding further exposure to potentially allergenic metallic devices. Titanium hypersensitivity should therefore be considered as an incremental factor in selected patients with unexplained implant-related complications, even when conventional risk factors are present.

title: Active Fire Detections and Hospital Admissions for Circulatory Diseases in Brazil: An Ecological Panel Study (2013-2024).
authorString: Andreotti GP, Ramos Martines G, Carilo GA, Wladimirski PS, Ottaviani R, Beirith JE.
abstractText:
Background

Wildfire smoke has been associated with cardiovascular outcomes, yet annual counts of fire detections capture a different exposure pattern from the short-term smoke concentrations on which much of that evidence rests. We examined whether fire detection density was associated with hospital admissions for circulatory diseases across Brazil between 2013 and 2024.

Methods

The ecological panel covered 27 federative units over 12 years, giving 324 unit-year observations. Admissions for International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Chapter IX diseases, came from the hospital information system/unified health system; fire detections from the Brazilian National Institute for Space Research; and population and territorial area from the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics. We calculated Spearman correlations and then fitted negative binomial models of admission counts with a population offset and state fixed effects, adding year effects, temperature, poverty, and primary care coverage in successive specifications. Robustness was examined through three temporal subsets and a state-clustered standard-error analysis.

Results

The period comprised 13,801,934 admissions and 2,318,883 fire detections. Ischemic heart disease was the largest individually specified diagnostic group, with 3,301,354 admissions (23.9%). All three correlations lay close to zero: between states ρ = -0.03 (p = 0.87), in the pooled panel ρ = -0.02 (p = 0.70), and after within-state centering ρ = 0.01 (p = 0.89). Across five regression specifications, rate ratios per additional 1,000 detections/100,000 km²/year ranged from 0.979 to 1.020, with the full model at 0.998 (conventional 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.970-1.028; p = 0.913). CIs included unity in every temporal subset and under state-clustered inference as well.

Conclusions

No statistically significant association was detected at the annual state level. These findings do not establish the absence of cardiovascular effects from wildfire smoke; rather, the indirect exposure measure, temporal aggregation, crude outcome rates, and methodological changes in population and healthcare indicators each limit what the data can show.

title: Long-term follow-up revealed hypocalciuric hypercalcemia in a patient initially treated for primary hyperparathyroidism.
authorString: Araya AV, Dupouy J, Gac P.
abstractText: In patients with hypercalcemia and normal or mildly elevated parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels, distinguishing primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) from hypocalciuric hypercalcemia (HH) is crucial. We describe a 70-year-old woman who underwent parathyroidectomy for PHPT at 58 years old. Despite surgery, she remained asymptomatic with persistent hypercalcemia, normal phosphate levels, 25-hydroxyvitamin D, renal function, and mildly elevated PTH levels. Serial imaging suggested recurrent parathyroid disease, and subtotal parathyroidectomy demonstrated parathyroid hyperplasia. Although serum calcium and PTH levels initially normalized, hypercalcemia later recurred with normal PTH levels. Twenty-four-hour urinary calcium excretion was markedly low, and the calcium-to-creatinine clearance ratio (CCCR) was consistent with HH. No pathogenic variant was detected in the calcium-sensing receptor gene (CASR). At 84 years old, the patient remained asymptomatic. Long-term follow-up supported the diagnosis of HH despite negative CASR testing. This case underscores the importance of measuring 24-hour urinary calcium excretion and calculating the CCCR in patients with hypercalcemia, particularly in asymptomatic individuals, before considering parathyroid surgery.

title: Design and Evaluation of Ethylene Glycol Monopiperate as a Novel Antihyperlipidemic Prodrug: Synthesis, Antihyperlipidemic Activity, and Pharmacokinetics.
authorString: Borijihan G, Liu M, Bao M, Sun Z, He M, Li Y.

journal.title: Journal of analytical methods in chemistry

abstractText: Piperine, a major active component isolated from the traditional Mongolian medicine Piper longum L., exhibits antihyperlipidemic activity but also demonstrates inherent toxicity. In this study, ethylene glycol monopiperate (EGM), a piperine derivative, was synthesized via concentrated H2SO4-catalyzed esterification. Its structure was systematically characterized by FTIR, MS, 13C NMR, and 1H NMR, with a yield of 60% and a purity of 99.2%. Subsequently, the in vitro cytotoxicity of EGM on HepG2 cells was evaluated, and the results indicated that over 90% cell viability was observed at concentrations up to 150 μg/mL. It was also investigated in male Wistar rats, and a sensitive, rapid, and accurate solid-phase extraction (SPE)-UPLC method was developed and validated for the quantification of EGM in rat plasma. The novel method showed good linearity over the concentration range of 1-16 µg/mL, a limit of detection (LOD) of 1 μg/mL, and high accuracy and precision (relative error [RE%] < 15%, relative standard deviation [RSD%] < 10%). In terms of antihyperlipidemic efficacy, EGM demonstrated excellent performance in reducing total cholesterol (TC), glucose (GLU), and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), as well as elevating high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C); these effects were notably better than the conventional control drug simvastatin. Pharmacokinetic analysis revealed that the plasma concentration-time profile of EGM followed a first-order open one-compartment model. Calculations using WINNONLIN software (ver. 5.2) showed a half-life (t 1/2) of 1.46 ± 0.67 h and an area under the curve (AUC0-∞) of 7,15,530 ± 522.4 ng h/mL. EGM was stable in plasma over 24 h at room temperature and one month at -20°C, after three freeze-thaw cycles. These results verified that EGM may serve as a promising candidate for an antihyperlipidemic prodrug.

title: Rapid Progression of Acute Acalculous Cholecystitis to Gangrenous Cholecystitis in an Initially Non-Critically Ill Patient: A Case Report.
authorString: Adam RY, Eldein SJ, Mahmoud MM, Elshikhawoda MSM, Musa O, Abdon F.
abstractText: Acute acalculous cholecystitis (AAC) is not confined to the critically ill and may behave like calculous disease. A 65-year-old hypertensive man with localized, stone-free cholecystitis deteriorated on hospital Day 4 with peritonism, acidosis, and acute kidney injury. Emergency open cholecystectomy confirmed gangrene; deterioration warrants urgent source control.

title: The fetal phenotype is a trajectory, not a snapshot.
authorString: Recker F, Walter A, Gembruch U.
abstractText: The fetal phenotype is a trajectory rather than a fixed observation: features emerge, progress, or resolve across gestation, and the anomaly present at 20 weeks is often not the anomaly present at 32. Sequence variants, however, are interpreted against the phenotype supplied when the test is requested, and phenotypic specificity carries evidence weight in variant classification. A scoping review of 59 studies combining serial prenatal phenotyping with sequence-based testing found that a newly emergent phenotype led to a molecular diagnosis in 16 studies and a variant reclassification in 8; yet a gestational age for every phenotypic observation was reported in 2, a serial imaging protocol in 7, and a reclassification with both direction and evidence code in 1. The clinical signal is real, and the literature cannot quantify it. Five reporting practices are proposed, none of which requires new equipment or funding.

title: The AMPK signaling pathway in cell metabolism and human diseases.
authorString: Zhang Z, Gu Y, He H, Qiao S, Shao Y, Long X, Huang J, Zhang L, Zhou F.
abstractText: Adenosine 5'-monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK), a highly conserved energy-sensing kinase, plays a central role in maintaining cellular metabolic homeostasis, such as glucose/lipid metabolism, mitochondrial biogenesis, and autophagy, to counteract energetic stress. Beyond the canonical adenylate-dependent activation of AMPK by sensing the ATP:AMP/ADP ratio, emerging evidence reveals noncanonical activation mechanisms. Proper AMPK signaling is essential for physiological functions, whereas its dysregulation underlies various pathologies, including metabolic diseases, immune disorders, and cancer. This review systematically recapitulates the historical background and landmark discoveries of the AMPK field, including the discovery of AMPK, the structure of AMPK complex, upstream regulators and downstream substrates, and the transcriptional/posttranscriptional and posttranslational regulatory mechanisms. Furthermore, we delineate its roles in maintaining metabolic equilibrium, mitochondrial integrity, and immune competence across organ systems and highlight how dysregulated AMPK activity contributes to pathological diseases, encompassing alterations in its expression levels, intrinsic kinase activity, subcellular localization or upstream regulatory signaling cascades. Specifically, we focus on knock-in or knockout mouse models utilized to study AMPK-associated human diseases and the translational potential of AMPK-targeting agonists or antagonists across diverse pathological conditions. A deep understanding of the multidimensional regulatory network of AMPK and mechanistic insights with therapeutic innovations that we provide with this review will help address the challenges of complex metabolic diseases.

title: Perioperative Management of a Spinal Cord Stimulator During Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: A Case Report.
authorString: Zheng J, Yeoh J, Yudi M, Koshy AN, Weinberg L.
abstractText: Spinal cord stimulation (SCS) is an established treatment for chronic neuropathic pain, and patients with an implanted stimulator are presenting with increasing frequency for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). We describe an 88-year-old man with a high-frequency (10 kHz) spinal cord stimulator for chronic back pain who underwent transfemoral TAVI under sedation for severe symptomatic aortic stenosis. After consultation with the implanting pain service, the stimulator was switched off with the patient's own remote control, which was kept in the procedure room; rapid ventricular pacing was delivered through a bipolar right ventricular lead so that the pacing current was confined to the myocardium and remote from the pulse generator; and external defibrillator pads were positioned away from the generator and the course of the leads. The procedure was uneventful. The patient tolerated the interruption of therapy without clinically significant pain; a new left bundle branch block after valve deployment was identified on an artefact-free trace, stimulation was resumed after the procedure with analgesia equivalent to baseline, and subsequent interrogation confirmed normal device function. The case illustrates the application of a precautionary strategy informed by manufacturer labelling and analogous evidence; because the stimulator was off throughout, it does not establish that any individual measure was necessary. We examine how the hazards of the cardiac catheterisation laboratory differ from those of the operating theatre and propose a structured six-step approach to the management of a spinal cord stimulator during TAVI.

title: Novel Fluorescence-Guided Gastric Calibration Tube in Robotic Paraesophageal Hernia Repair.
authorString: Fontaine-Nicola A, Harman H, Reyes E, Hajjar M, Szoka N.

journal.title: CRSLS : MIS case reports from SLS

abstractText:
Background

Fluorescence-guided (FG) surgery using near-infrared imaging has been adopted to enhance intraoperative visualization in multiple surgical fields. In foregut surgery, calibration tubes are routinely used to calibrate crural closure but due to limited visibility carry a risk of iatrogenic injury, including esophageal or gastric perforation. Techniques that improve visualization of these devices may support safer intraoperative management.

Case presentation

A 75-year-old woman with a symptomatic paraesophageal hiatal hernia and partial gastric volvulus underwent robotic paraesophageal hiatal hernia repair with Toupet fundoplication. A FG gastric calibration tube (size 40 Fr, Endolumik Inc.), was inserted under near-infrared visualization and advanced down the esophagus and into the stomach. The device was used to (1) evacuate gastric contents, (2) guide tube positioning past the gastroesophageal junction, (3) inform mediastinal dissection/esophageal mobilization, (4) enable FG measuring of the length of esophageal mobilization below the diaphragm, and (5) calibrate both crural closure and fundoplication. The procedure was completed without intraoperative complications. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 1 and reported resolution of dysphagia at 8-week follow-up.

Discussion

This case demonstrates the feasibility of FG calibration during robotic paraesophageal hernia repair. Continuous visualization of the calibration device provided an additional intraoperative reference during dissection in the setting of distorted anatomy. This approach may offer improved orientation compared with conventional calibration techniques, although its effect on clinical outcomes remains unknown.

title: En bloc multivisceral resection for a giant retroperitoneal dedifferentiated liposarcoma: technical considerations.
authorString: Al-Hassani S, Akingboye A, Merlini I, Di Saverio S.
abstractText: Retroperitoneal sarcomas are rare, aggressive malignancies that often present late owing to the retroperitoneum's anatomical expansibility. Dedifferentiated liposarcoma is the most common high-grade subtype. We describe the technical management of a 65-year-old man with a giant retroperitoneal dedifferentiated liposarcoma involving multiple adjacent organs, treated by radical en bloc multivisceral resection including the kidney, adrenal gland, spleen, and distal pancreas. Postoperative recovery was complicated by a Grade B pancreatic leak and a left pleural effusion, managed with percutaneous and thoracic drainage, respectively. Histology confirmed a dedifferentiated liposarcoma resected with clear (R0) margins. At 18 months, no radiological recurrence had been observed, although this follow-up interval remains short relative to the recurrence interval reported for high-grade dedifferentiated liposarcoma. This case illustrates the technical conduct of multivisceral resection for a giant retroperitoneal sarcoma and the perioperative surveillance required to manage expected complications such as pancreatic leak.

title: A Novel Insight Into Luspatercept: Therapeutic Implications in Myelodysplastic Syndrome Patients With Elevated Pulmonary Artery Systolic Pressure.
authorString: Jin Q, Tian D, Chen D, Li M, Hou S, Zhang X, Pan W, Zhou D, Guan L, Ge J.
abstractText: Luspatercept enhances late-stage erythroid maturation by sequestering transforming growth factor-β superfamily ligands and attenuating pathological signaling, with a mechanism highly analogous to that of sotatercept, a breakthrough therapeutic agent for pulmonary hypertension (PH). Despite this solid mechanistic basis, the potential vascular and prognostic effects of luspatercept in PH patients remain largely uncharacterized. This retrospective proof-of-concept study aimed to evaluate the impact of luspatercept on pulmonary artery pressure and surrogate prognostic markers, and to explore its novel therapeutic potential in patients with increased pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP). We retrospectively analyzed serial echocardiographic parameters among patients with myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) who received luspatercept treatment, focusing on individuals with elevated baseline PASP. Dynamic changes in cardiopulmonary indicators and laboratory biomarkers were comprehensively compared before and after intervention. A total of five MDS patients with elevated baseline PASP were enrolled in the final analysis. Although formal statistical comparisons failed to reach significance, which was largely attributable to the limited sample size, consistent clinically beneficial improvements were observed after luspatercept treatment. The median PASP decreased from 62.0 (IQR 14) mmHg at baseline to 33.0 (IQR 18.5) mmHg following treatment. Parallel reductions in N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and uric acid levels were identified, accompanied by a mild yet favorable elevation in hemoglobin concentration. In this small cohort of MDS patients with elevated PASP, luspatercept treatment was associated with decreased pulmonary artery pressure, reduced NT-proBNP and uric acid levels, and improved hemoglobin levels. These preliminary findings suggest novel pleiotropic benefits of luspatercept in improving pulmonary arterial pressure, cardiac function, and anemia status, providing a compelling rationale for further prospective clinical studies to verify its therapeutic value in PH populations.

title: Endovascular recanalization of chronic total occlusion of the subclavian artery: fifteen years of technological evolution.
authorString: Babić S, Milačić A, Kovačević V, Pešić S, Mihajlović V, Antonić Ž, Bojić M.
abstractText: Fifteen years ago, endovascular recanalization of chronic total occlusion of the subclavian artery relied largely on coronary guidewires and conventional catheters. An early series achieved technical success in 46 of 56 patients (82.1%). Today, dedicated crossing wires, support catheters, improved imaging, and a wider choice of stents provide additional options for complex lesions. Yet published series report variable technical success and patency, and differences in patient selection and follow-up limit comparisons between treatment eras. This review revisits earlier techniques, examines what has changed in practice, and discusses persistent challenges, particularly heavily calcified and ostial occlusions near the vertebral artery. Technological progress has broadened treatment options, but its independent contribution to long-term outcomes remains uncertain.

title: Anxiety and Coping Strategies in Caregivers of Children With Epidermal Differentiation Disorders: A Case-Control Study.
authorString: Fryze M, Pietrzak A, Mlak R, Wawrzycki B, Wertheim-Tysarowska K, van Veen FCAP, Gostynski AH.
abstractText:
Background

Epidermal differentiation disorders (EDDs) are rare, chronic skin diseases with significant psychosocial impact on patients and families. Their daily management requires complex care, placing caregivers at risk of stress and anxiety. Few studies have systematically examined anxiety and coping strategies in this group.

Objectives

To compare anxiety levels and coping styles between caregivers of children with syndromic or nonsyndromic EDD and caregivers of healthy children.

Methods

In this cross-sectional case-control study, 39 caregivers of children with EDD and 39 matched controls were recruited from a dermatology clinic. Anxiety was assessed with the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI) and coping styles with the Coping Inventory for Stressful Situations (CISS). Sociodemographic and clinical data were collected.

Results

Caregivers of children with EDDs reported significantly higher trait anxiety than controls (79.5% vs. 53.8%; p = 0.017). Task-oriented coping (TOC) was less frequent among EDD caregivers, with more than half showing low TOC compared with less than one-third of controls (56.4% vs. 28.6%; p = 0.019). High avoidance-oriented coping (AOC) was observed more often in controls (21.4% vs. 5.6%; p = 0.044). Anxiety was greater among caregivers of boys than girls (95.7% vs. 56.2%; p = 0.003). Avoidant coping was associated with greater child symptom severity, including pruritus and redness.

Conclusions

Caregivers of children with EDD experience high anxiety and rely less on adaptive coping strategies. These findings emphasize the need for early, family-centered psychosocial interventions to support caregiver well-being and improve outcomes for affected children.

title: Non-invasive ventilation for general paediatricians.
authorString: Sundaram M, Medina A, Pons-Òdena M.
abstractText:
Over the past two decades, non-invasive ventilation (NIV) has transitioned from being primarily used in specialist intensive care units to becoming a standard intervention in high dependency units, general paediatric units, emergency departments, and increasingly, patients' homes. Despite this expansion, many general paediatricians still perceive NIV as outside their primary expertise. With this review, we aim to address that gap and equip general paediatricians with the knowledge and confidence to appropriately initiate NIV, monitor its effectiveness, and recognise when escalation of care is required. We narratively reviewed the physiological rationale for non-invasive respiratory support (NRS), including high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) and the two principal modalities of NIV-continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) and bilevel positive airway pressure (BiPAP)-and summarised disease-specific evidence from recent literature, including randomised trials, systematic reviews, and international consensus statements. This is a narrative rather than a systematic review: we searched PubMed/MEDLINE and Paediatric Respiratory Reviews for English-language publications from January 2018 to June 2026 using the terms "non-invasive ventilation", "high-flow nasal cannula", "CPAP", "BiPAP", and "children", supplemented by references already known to the authors, and selected articles for relevance and recency, prioritising randomised trials, systematic reviews, and consensus statements. HFNC is an oxygenation device rather than a ventilatory device, and its mechanism, clinical applications, and therapeutic goals differ from CPAP and BiPAP. We introduce the Indications, Contraindications, Equipment, Mode and settings, Assessment and monitoring, Next steps (ICEMAN) framework as a practical tool for structured and safe initiation of NIV in routine clinical practice, and apply it across bronchiolitis, acute severe asthma, pneumonia and hypoxaemic respiratory failure, neuromuscular disease, and obstructive sleep apnoea.

Conclusion

 The essential requirements to initiate NIV outside the PICU are well-trained staff, appropriate monitoring, a reliable oxygen supply, and a clear plan for escalation to a higher level of care. Selection of patients for NIV outside the PICU requires careful attention to indication, contraindications, equipment, monitoring, and escalation pathway by using frameworks like ICEMAN.

What is known

• HFNC, CPAP, and BiPAP are established, physiologically distinct respiratory therapies now used well beyond the PICU.

What is new

• The ICEMAN framework, updated with PALICC-2 ARDS criteria, gives non-specialists a structured, teachable approach to safe NIV initiation.

title: Pyelonephritis in cats and dogs - a scoping review.
authorString: Pelander L, Ekstrand C, Scahill K.
abstractText: There is a lack of consensus regarding the diagnosis and treatment of bacterial pyelonephritis (PN) in dogs and cats. The aim of this scoping review was to increase knowledge by describing published scientific literature on the subject, specifically to collate definitions and diagnostic criteria, antimicrobial regimens, reported outcomes, and to identify knowledge gaps. A structured search was performed of the bibliographic databases Biosis, CAB Abstracts, Medline, Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus. We included 176 original studies written in English or German that reported on any aspect of spontaneous PN (risk factors, signalment, history, clinical findings, diagnostic criteria, treatment, prognosis, and outcome) in cats or dogs. Three types of PN were identified in the literature: histologically diagnosed PN, clinically diagnosed PN, and pyonephrosis. Multiple information gaps regarding clinical aspects of PN in dogs and cats were detected. There were no universally accepted clinical criteria for clinical diagnosis of PN and no clinical trials evaluating antimicrobial or other treatment options. Information about short-term outcomes for dogs and cats with PN was scarce, and there were no data regarding long-term outcomes. More information regarding all aspects of clinical PN in dogs and cats is needed.The study protocol was registered prospectively in 2023 ( https://syreaf.org/protocols/ ).

title: Mechanistic insights into polycystic ovary syndrome and periodontal disease: a systematic scoping review of inflammatory, oxidative stress, hormonal-metabolic, and microbial pathways.
authorString: Nassar M, Zatar Y, Sharikadze N, Aladashvili T, Kokhreidze E.
abstractText: To identify critical evidence gaps, this scoping review mapped the extent and nature of published research exploring the biological links between polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and periodontal disease. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines and a pre-registered protocol (OSF: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/WE3XU) a systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, EBSCO, and Google Scholar identified original human studies assessing clinical periodontal parameters and mechanistic biomarkers in PCOS patients. Screening and data extraction were conducted independently by two reviewers. Thirty-three studies met the inclusion criteria. Mapping identified a synergistic pathophysiological network across four domains. The evidence reveals an elevated systemic inflammatory baseline marked by hyper-activated endothelial markers (Endocan) alongside elevated levels of Tumor Necrosis Factor-alpha (TNF-alpha) and Interleukin-6 (IL-6), which appears to lower the threshold for local tissue destruction. This is coupled with a compromised antioxidant defense-notably nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) downregulation-and a "microbial dysbiosis" toward pathogenic microbial complexes. However, current data primarily identify mechanistic intersections rather than definitive causality, with the "PCOS-specific" impact often confounded by shared metabolic risk factors like insulin resistance and adiposity. Mapping this evidence reveals a profound overlap between PCOS and periodontitis through shared pathophysiological networks. Advancing this field requires a Core Outcome Set (COS) and well-designed randomized controlled trials. Clinically, recognizing periodontal disease as a potential contributor to the systemic inflammatory burden suggests that integrating routine.

title: The association between e-cigarette use and dyslipidemia: A systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies.
authorString: Rajha HE, Mohsen S, Alkuwari H, Naeim J, Al-Marri W, Hamdan A, Chivese T, Al Saady RM.
abstractText:
Background

E-cigarette use, also known as vaping, has rapidly increased in recent years, often marketed as a safer alternative to traditional smoking. While the cardiovascular risks of vaping are increasingly being recognized, its relationship with dyslipidemia remains unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association between e-cigarette use and serum lipid levels, specifically total cholesterol (TC), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL), and triglycerides (TG).

Methods

A search of PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, CENTRAL, CINAHL, medRxiv, and Google Scholar was conducted up to May 31,2025. Eligible studies included adult populations and assessed the association between exclusive e-cigarette use and lipids. Study quality was assessed using the Methodological Standards for Epidemiological Research (MASTER) scale. Meta-analysis of adjusted odds ratios (aOR) for dyslipidemia and unadjusted weighted mean differences (uWMD) for each lipid was conducted using a bias-adjusted inverse-variance heterogeneity method. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic, and publication bias using Doi plots and the LFK index, with the LFK index used as the primary quantitative criterion. Planned subgroup analyses by age group and sex could not be performed due to insufficient stratified reporting in included studies. The overall quality of evidence for each lipid outcome was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.

Results

Of 4,160 identified data sources, seven observational studies from the U.S.A., South Korea, Romania, and Iraq with a total of 25,690 participants met the inclusion criteria. Meta-analysis showed that vaping was associated with higher odds of hypertriglyceridemia (aOR 3.10, 95% CI 1.18 to 8.16, I2 = 80.1%, LFK = 1.34), and higher odds of low HDL (aOR 3.26, 95% CI 2.28 to 4.65, I2 = 3.1%, LFK = 1.41). In studies with unadjusted mean lipid levels, the primary quality-effects model showed no statistically significant difference in TC (unadjusted weighted mean difference (uWMD) +3.66 mg/dL, 95% CI -13.89 to 21.20, I2 = 86.9%, LFK = 9.44) but showed higher LDL (uWMD +12.40 mg/dL, 95% CI 7.91 to 16.88, I2 = 29.1%, LFK = 1.05), and VLDL (uWMD +3.23 mg/dL, 95% CI 1.43 to 5.02, I2 = 0.0%, publication bias not assessed). For all outcomes, the GRADE certainty of evidence was very low.

Conclusion

This synthesis suggests that e-cigarette use may be associated with adverse lipid profiles, but the evidence remains observational and of very low certainty, limiting causal inference. Further well-designed longitudinal studies, using validated smoking-status assessment, detailed vaping exposure measures, fasting lipid panels, repeated lipid measurements, and adjustment for key cardiometabolic confounders, are needed to clarify these associations.

title: Novel cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging biomarkers to track response to treatment including Sotatercept in a patient with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension: a case report.
authorString: Castiglione A, Kjellström B, Rådegran G, Ostenfeld E.
abstractText:
Background

Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) causes progressive right ventricular (RV) pressure overload and left ventricular (LV) underfilling. Sotatercept is an activin-signal inhibitor, approved by FDA in 2024 and EMA in 2025, as an add-on treatment in adult patients with PAH. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived atrioventricular plane displacement (AVPD) and left ventricular pressure-volume (PV) loops may represent non-invasive markers of treatment response, particularly important as novel therapies addressing remodelling emerge.

Case summary

A 30-year-old woman was diagnosed with idiopathic PAH, after presenting with dyspnoea and peripheral oedema. Baseline CMR showed severe RV dilation, reduced RV ejection fraction, and low indexed LV stroke volume, with reduced bilateral AVPD and markedly impaired LV PV loop indices, with low stroke work, low mean external power, and high ventriculo-arterial coupling. Initial dual PAH therapy, with an endothelin receptor antagonist and a phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor initially improved symptoms, pulmonary vascular resistance, as well as AVPD and PV loop derived indices, whereas conventional CMR indices showed only minimal change. One year later, despite triple therapy, including prostacyclin analogue, the patient deteriorated clinically and CMR showed worsening of AVPD and PV loop indices. Treatment escalation with Sotatercept immediately improved clinical status, haemodynamic, AVPD, and PV loop indices despite persistent RV remodelling.

Discussion

Serial CMR-derived AVPD and LV PV loops may provide clinically useful additional information during longitudinal follow-up of PAH patients, especially in those approaching maximal available medical therapies. In the present case, both AVPD and LV PV loops reflected treatment response, and showed significant improvement after initiation of Sotatercept.

title: Neutrophil Extracellular Traps (NETs), Immunothrombosis and the Microvascular Siege in Sepsis-ARDS.
authorString: El-Sehrawy AAMA, Mansurov D, Baig MR, Abdelrahim IM, Bainsal N, Bansal P, Abdullah SS, Khaleel ZT, Jabir MS, Smerat A.
abstractText: Sepsis-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains associated with substantial mortality despite decades of research, and the reasons why many disease-modifying treatments have failed remain incompletely understood. This narrative review synthesizes emerging evidence implicating neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in the interaction between innate immunity, immunothrombosis, and microvascular failure in sepsis-ARDS. NETs, extruded lattices of DNA, histones, and granular enzymes, serve as antimicrobial scaffolds but may contribute to tissue injury when excessive or persistent. Within the pulmonary microcirculation, experimental studies indicate that NETs can concentrate tissue factor and proteases, activate platelets, suppress fibrinolysis, and injure endothelium through histone cytotoxicity, supporting a self-amplifying thrombo-inflammatory loop. These processes may contribute to microvascular obstruction and barrier dysfunction, although their relative importance varies across experimental models and patient populations. We critically evaluate emerging NET-directed interventions, including peptidylarginine deiminase 4 (PAD4) inhibition to prevent NET formation, recombinant deoxyribonuclease (DNase) to dismantle existing scaffolds, targeted neutralization of NET components (citrullinated histones), and selective anticoagulation targeting factor XII/XI. Challenges of timing, infection risk, and patient heterogeneity support further evaluation of biomarker-guided "NET-otyping" using plasma myeloperoxidase-DNA, citrullinated histone H3, and experimental molecular imaging. Building on existing work in microvascular protection, we examine whether more effective and selective NET targeting could improve treatment of sepsis-ARDS. Clinical benefit remains to be established.

title: Anemia and high-output cardiac hypertrophy in Tanzania and Haiti: a cross-sectional analysis.
authorString: Rouzier V, Ruselu G, Willkens M, Yan LD, Cichowitz C, Ogyu A, Garbindi A, Kisigo G, Issarow B, Sufra R, Etyang A, Pape JW, Devereux RB, McNairy M, Kapiga S, Peck R, Lee MH.
abstractText:
Background

Low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) face a growing burden of cardiovascular disease (CVD) that is not fully explained by traditional risk factors like hypertension. Anemia is highly prevalent in LMICs and may be an important non-traditional CVD risk factor. We evaluated the association between anemia and preclinical CVD, including left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) and other echocardiographic measures, in two diverse LMIC settings.

Methods

This was a cross-sectional analysis of data from two separate cohorts of adults in Mwanza, Tanzania (n = 999; data collected 2022-2023) and Port-au-Prince, Haiti (n = 3,005; data collected 2019-2021). Participants underwent clinical examinations, laboratory testing, and echocardiography. Models assessing the relationship between anemia and echocardiographic outcomes were adjusted for age, sex, HIV status, blood pressure, and body mass index.

Results

Anemia prevalence was 23% in Tanzania and 32% in Haiti. Despite lower blood pressure and BMI among anemic participants, moderate/severe anemia were strongly associated with higher LVMI and LVH in both cohorts. In combined analyses, moderate/severe anemia were associated with LVMI increases of 8.4 g/m² and 29.7 g/m², respectively. Anemia was also associated with echocardiographic changes characteristic of a high-output cardiac state, including increased cardiac and stroke volume indices. Moderate/severe anemia was associated with18.2% of LVH cases in Tanzania and 9.1% in Haiti, and 34.4% among people with HIV.

Conclusions

Anemia was independently associated with high-output cardiac hypertrophy in two distinct LMIC populations, underscoring anemia as a potentially modifiable CVD risk factor. Enhanced anemia screening and management could serve as a vital strategy to mitigate the rising burden of CVD in these regions.

title: Clinicopathological diagnostic concordance among autopsied adults living with HIV in the Brazilian Amazon: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
authorString: Martins YF, Almeida TVR, Reis MFD, Corrêa VVP, Marinho EPM, Pinto RAA, Bastos MS, de Lima Ferreira LC.
abstractText: With the emergence of antiretroviral therapy (ART), changes have occurred over time in the causes of death and pathological findings among people living with HIV, including an increasing contribution of serious non-AIDS-related diseases. Assessing concordance between ante-mortem clinical and post-mortem diagnoses remains an important approach for evaluating diagnostic performance and monitoring changes in causes of death in this population. This study aimed to evaluate the concordance between ante-mortem clinical diagnoses of the underlying cause of death and autopsy diagnoses among adults living with HIV who underwent autopsy at the Fundação de Medicina Tropical Doutor Heitor Vieira Dourado (FMT-HVD), Manaus, Brazil, between 2014 and 2019. This cross-sectional retrospective study included 101 autopsies. Class I discordances were identified in 48 of 101 cases (47.6%), predominantly involving infectious diseases (37/48; 77.1%), followed by undiagnosed neoplasms (8/48; 16.7%) and other conditions (3/48; 6.2%). Overall concordance for the underlying cause of death was 36.7%, and most deaths were attributable to AIDS-defining diseases. The absence of ART was associated with a higher frequency of class I discordances. The high frequency of major missed diagnoses may also reflect advanced disease at presentation, overlapping clinical manifestations of opportunistic infections, and limitations in the availability of specific diagnostic methods during the study period. Overall clinicopathological discordance was 63.3%, underscoring the continued value of autopsy for identifying missed diagnoses and highlighting the importance of timely clinical assessment and improved access to sensitive and specific diagnostic methods for adults living with HIV.

title: Prevalence and factors associated with sarcopenia in individuals with stroke undergoing rehabilitation: A cross-sectional study.
authorString: Ida FS, Silva EJMCE, Brasil GSM, Peregrino LM, Silva CEPD, Silva PYF.
abstractText:
Objective

To determine the prevalence of sarcopenia and identify clinical and functional factors independently associated with confirmed sarcopenia in individuals with stroke undergoing rehabilitation.

Methods

This cross-sectional study enrolled 209 adults with stroke admitted for neurological rehabilitation. Sarcopenia was defined according to the European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People 2 (EWGSOP2) algorithm, using SARC-CalF, handgrip strength, five-times sit-to-stand test, physical performance measures and appendicular skeletal muscle mass by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Bivariate analyses and multivariable logistic regression were performed to identify factors independently associated with confirmed sarcopenia.

Results

Confirmed sarcopenia was identified in 55 of 209 participants (26.3%; 95% CI: 20.6% to 32.8%). Participants with sarcopenia were older and had lower body mass index (BMI), poorer physical performance, and greater motor impairment than those without sarcopenia. In the multivariable model, lower BMI (OR = 0.70; 95% CI: 0.59 to 0.83), positive SARC-CalF screening (OR = 6.37; 95% CI: 2.03 to 20.05), and lower Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) scores (OR = 0.83; 95% CI: 0.69 to 0.99) remained independently associated with sarcopenia. Motor impairment severity, assessed using Fugl-Meyer motor categories, was also independently associated with sarcopenia.

Conclusion

DXA-confirmed post-stroke sarcopenia affected approximately one in four individuals undergoing rehabilitation and was independently associated with lower BMI, poorer physical performance, and greater motor impairment. These findings indicate that sarcopenia is closely linked to functional impairment after stroke and reinforce the importance of integrating muscle health and functional assessment during rehabilitation. Early identification of individuals at risk may support more individualized rehabilitation strategies and improve clinical decision-making.

title: Circulating IP-10/CXCL10 Correlates With Parasitemia and Disease Severity in Patients With Babesiosis: A Pilot Study.
authorString: Oakley MS, Hayashi CTH, Spichler-Moffarah A, Majam V, Golden M, Meredith S, Zheng H, Leaf DE, Monson A, Roberts SC, Johnston D, Krause PJ, Kumar S.
abstractText:
Background

Human babesiosis is an emerging tick-borne zoonosis that can cause serious complications, including death. Immune mechanisms that confer protection or promote disease severity in human babesiosis are poorly understood.

Methods

We measured the cytokine and antibody profile in a cohort of hospitalized patients who had babesiosis. Cytokine levels were measured in plasma using the Bio-Plex Pro Human Cytokine 27-Plex Assay, and Babesia microti-specific total IgG and its 4 isotypes were measured using an immunofluorescence assay. Cytokine profile was analyzed in relation to immune status, peak parasitemia, lowest hemoglobin levels, and disease severity.

Results

There were enhanced levels of 8 cytokines (eotaxin, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IP-10/CXCL10, MCP-1, MIP-1α, and TNF-α) in the plasma of 16 patients with babesiosis as compared with 7 controls. A positive correlation was found between IP-10 levels and parasitemia (Spearman R = 0.52, P = .04). Patients with severe babesiosis had elevated levels of IP-10 and IL-5 as compared with the other 2 clinical categories (ie, moderate and moderately severe). Immunosuppression was associated with low levels of the VEGF and FGF basic angiogenic factors. There was also an inverse correlation between hemoglobin and IL-1β or IL-9 levels. Last, patients with babesiosis produced abundant levels of immunofluorescence assay total IgG and IgG1 and IgG3 but low levels of IgG2 and no IgG4.

Conclusions

IP-10 and other cytokines that exhibited elevated levels should be further investigated as biomarkers of severe babesiosis.

title: Development of an undifferentiated sarcoma following internal carotid artery aneurysm stenting: causality or coincidence? Illustrative case.
authorString: Scalise M, Cividini A, Peron S, Cannizzaro D, Billo PR, Piano M, Stefini R.
abstractText:
Background

Undifferentiated soft tissue sarcomas are rare tumors lacking identifiable differentiation. Primary sarcomas associated with aneurysm sacs are extremely rare, typically involving large vessels. Intracranial involvement is exceptional and poorly documented.

Observations

The authors report the case of a patient treated in 2009 for a left paraclinoid internal carotid artery aneurysm (18 × 10 mm) by endovascular stenting (Silk 4.5/30). Eleven years later, he developed headache, somnolence, visual blurring, left ptosis, and anisocoria. CT and CTA showed the known thrombosed aneurysm and an adjacent hypervascular midline lesion. Angiography confirmed complete exclusion with a patent stent and no new aneurysms. MRI revealed a suprasellar-retrosellar multilobulated enhancing mass causing marked brainstem compression. Surgery identified a solid lesion seemingly arising along the thrombosed aneurysm sac, and partial resection was performed. The patient initially recovered but subsequently deteriorated with rapid tumor regrowth and died during hospitalization. Histological analysis showed a grade 3 undifferentiated sarcoma (vimentin +, MDM2+, focal smooth muscle actin -, CAM5.2-, GFAP-). Postmortem examination confirmed origin within the aneurysm sac adjacent to the stent.

Lessons

To the authors' knowledge, this is the first reported undifferentiated sarcoma arising from a stent-treated carotid aneurysm. Although causality cannot be established, it parallels rare stent-associated sarcomas in large vessels and highlights the diagnostic challenges of atypical masses in treated vessels. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26659.
