title: Astaxanthin Inhibits ox-LDL-Induced Early Endothelial Progenitor Cells Oxidative Stress and Apoptosis Through Nrf2 Activation.
authorString: Pan K, Xu X, Jiang Q, Gong Z, Li Z, Ding S, Zhang M.
abstractText: Astaxanthin exerts potent protective effects against stem cell apoptosis. This study investigated the protective efficacy of astaxanthin against oxidized low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL)-induced oxidative stress and apoptosis in endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs). Human early EPCs cultured in vitro were challenged with ox-LDL in the presence or absence of astaxanthin. Results showed that ox-LDL exposure significantly reduced nuclear factor-E2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) nuclear translocation in EPCs, while increasing oxidative stress and apoptosis rates. Astaxanthin pretreatment attenuated ox-LDL-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and EPC apoptosis, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP), and concomitantly enhanced nuclear Nrf2 accumulation while upregulating NQO1, HO-1, and glutathione (GSH) levels. Nrf2 small interfering RNA (siRNA)-mediated knockdown completely abolished astaxanthin-induced NQO1 and HO-1 upregulation. Mechanistically, astaxanthin promoted Akt phosphorylation (activation) and inhibited glycogen synthase kinase 3β (GSK-3β) phosphorylation. Pretreatment with LY294002 (a phosphoinositide 3-kinase/PI3K inhibitor) suppressed astaxanthin-induced Nrf2 nuclear translocation, exacerbated ROS production, and reduced NQO1 and GSH levels. Additionally, astaxanthin blocked ox-LDL-induced caspase-3 upregulation and preserved EPC migration and tube formation. Nrf2 siRNA eliminated the protective effects of astaxanthin on EPC ROS production, MMP preservation, apoptosis, and migration; tube formation was not assessed. Overall, these in vitro findings using cells from healthy donors provide mechanistic support for the potential role of astaxanthin in the PI3K/Akt/GSK-3/Nrf2 pathway. However, the application of astaxanthin in the prevention and treatment of atherosclerotic disease requires further validation in disease-relevant models and clinical studies, as the present study was limited to in vitro results.

title: Association Between β1-Selective Beta-Blocker Use and P-Wave Terminal Force in Lead V1 in Hypertensive Patients With Left Ventricular Hypertrophy.
authorString: Alpaslan E, Taş S, Taş Ü, Eyüboğlu M, Duman ÖÖ, Dalgıç O, Candan L, Özdemir AR.
abstractText:
Background

P-wave terminal force in lead V1 (PTFV1) is an electrocardiographic marker of atrial electrical abnormality. We investigated whether β1-selective beta-blocker use was associated with PTFV1 in hypertensive patients with echocardiographically confirmed left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH).

Methods

This retrospective study included 182 eligible patients with essential hypertension and LVH selected from 1372 screened patients. Patients were classified as β1-selective beta-blocker users (n = 82) or nonusers (n = 100). Abnormal PTFV1 was defined as ≥ 0.04 mm s. Multivariable regression and sensitivity analyses were performed.

Results

PTFV1 was lower in beta-blocker users than in nonusers (0.024 [0.015-0.036] vs. 0.030 [0.020-0.048] mm s, p = 0.005). In the primary adjusted model, beta-blocker use was associated with lower PTFV1 (B = -0.008, standardized β = -0.202, 95% CI -0.014 to -0.002, p = 0.009), although model explanatory capacity was limited (R 2 = 0.064; adjusted R 2 = 0.021; overall p = 0.168). In an extended sensitivity analysis additionally adjusting for diabetes, renal function, and concomitant antihypertensive therapies, beta-blocker group status remained associated with lnPTFV1 (standardized β = 0.294, p < 0.001; R 2 = 0.147; adjusted R 2 = 0.081; overall p = 0.011). Beta-blocker use was also associated with lower odds of abnormal PTFV1 (OR = 0.43, 95% CI 0.22-0.84, p = 0.013).

Conclusion

β1-Selective beta-blocker use was associated with lower PTFV1 and a lower likelihood of abnormal PTFV1. These findings suggest a more favorable atrial electrical profile but should be considered hypothesis-generating given the retrospective design and modest model explanatory capacity.

title: Acute Angina in Anomalous Left Main Coronary Artery With Prepulmonic Course: A Case Report.
authorString: Rouzbahani M, Navabifar S, Montazeri N, Rahimi A, Hayati A.
abstractText: Although a prepulmonic left main coronary artery is usually considered a lower-risk AAOCA subtype, it may still be associated with acute ischemic symptoms when significant atherosclerotic coronary artery disease is present. Multimodality imaging is essential for defining the coronary anatomy, and coronary artery bypass grafting may be the preferred strategy when severe multivessel disease coexists.

title: Association of SDF-1β (rs1801157) and TCF7L2 (rs12255372) Gene Polymorphisms With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in the Bangladeshi Population: A Case-Control Study.
authorString: Mobin MAA, Shanto SA, Hasnayan E, Prome SZ, Das O, Afsar A, Rechi JTA, Shaika AH, Nesa F, Mitu MM, Khan F, Shohag MH.
abstractText:
Aims

Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) has a strong genetic component and variations in specific gene alleles can significantly influence individual susceptibility. Stromal cell-derived factor-1 beta (SDF-1β) plays a crucial role in inflammatory responses, glucose regulation, and the maintenance of pancreatic β-cell function, while TCF7L2, a key regulator of the Wnt signaling pathway, governs insulin secretion and overall glucose homeostasis. The present study evaluated the association of the SDF-1β rs1801157 and TCF7L2 rs12255372 polymorphisms with T2DM development in the Bangladeshi population.

Methods

In this case-control study, 140 clinically diagnosed T2DM patients and 95 healthy controls, were enrolled after obtaining approval from the institutional ethics committee. Genomic DNA was genotyped for SDF-1β (rs1801157) and TCF7L2 (rs12255372) SNPs using PCR-RFLP, with MspI used for SDF-1β digestion and MluCI for the TCF7L2 fragment. The resulting genotypes were then identified through agarose gel electrophoresis. Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium was tested in both groups. Genotype and allele frequencies were compared using Fisher's exact test, with crude and adjusted (for age, sex, BMI) odds ratios (ORs).

Results

All genotype distributions were in the Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. Using the homozygous dominant genotype (GG) as the reference, a statistically significant association was observed for SDF-1β (rs1801157) with the AA genotype (p < 0.05), whereas TCF7L2 (rs12255372) showed no significant association. Additionally, the allele frequency distributions for both SDF-1β and TCF7L2 did not differ significantly between cases and controls (p > 0.05).

Conclusions

The SDF-1β (rs1801157) AA genotype was significantly less frequent among T2DM patients, suggesting a possible protective association, whereas TCF7L2 (rs12255372) showed no such association. Given the modest sample size and limited statistical power, these findings indicate a possible association rather than a definitive marker of susceptibility and require replication.

title: Melatonin Mitigates Doxorubicin-Induced Cardiotoxicity by Targeting the USP18/PKM2 Axis Without Compromising Antitumor Efficacy.
authorString: Feng Z, Yang Y, Bai J, Sun P, Sun X, Shang J, Liu Y, Ning Z, Zhang N, Xia YL, Xie Y.
abstractText: Doxorubicin (DOX) remains a widely used chemotherapeutic drug, yet its clinical value is constrained by pronounced cardiotoxicity. Although melatonin is known to protect the heart, how it counters DOX-induced cardiotoxicity (DIC), and whether it interferes with chemotherapy, remains unclear. Here we set out to define how melatonin protects the heart during DOX treatment and to test whether this protection holds in tumor-bearing animals. We used acute and chronic DIC mouse models together with a syngeneic melanoma-bearing model, and combined transcriptomic profiling, pharmacological intervention, cardiomyocyte-specific USP18 overexpression and knockout, co-immunoprecipitation, mass spectrometry, ubiquitination assays, and PKM2 inhibitor treatment. Melatonin markedly improved cardiac function, an effect exerted mainly via the MT1/2 receptors. Mechanistically, DOX activated STAT1, which in turn drove myocardial USP18 upregulation. USP18 bound PKM2 and stabilized it through removing K33-linked ubiquitin chains while favoring K27-linked ubiquitination-thereby aggravating cardiac injury. Overexpressing USP18 specifically in cardiomyocytes worsened DIC and abolished the protection conferred by melatonin, whereas deleting USP18 or inhibiting PKM2 reproduced melatonin's benefits. Notably, in bearing melanoma or lymphoma, melatonin relieved DIC without weakening the antitumor activity of DOX. Together, these findings define a previously unrecognized cardioprotective pathway and provide preclinical support for melatonin as a safe adjunct therapy in cardio-oncology.

title: Human Engineered Heart Tissues Reproduce Trigger- and Substrate-Driven Mechanisms of Ventricular Tachycardia.
authorString: Fiedler M, Vasquez Limeta A, Reyes Sanchez E, Carter L, Altamirano F.
abstractText: Human iPSC‑derived engineered heart tissues (EHTs) are used to model cardiac physiology and drug responses, yet whether they reproduce tissue‑scale ventricular arrhythmia mechanisms remains unclear. We combined modified milliPillar EHT fabrication with high-resolution dual-channel voltage/Ca<sup>2+</sup> optical mapping. Baseline electrophysiology showed action potential durations (APD) within the range reported for human ventricles and conduction velocities approximately half of human longitudinal values, with rate‑dependent restitution of APD and Ca<sup>2+</sup> transient duration, conduction slowing, and physiologic AP-Ca<sup>2+</sup> latency. To interrogate a trigger arm of ventricular tachycardia (VT), we modeled acquired long-QT syndrome (aLQTS; hERG blockade with hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia) in EHTs from two hiPSC lines. aLQTS EHTs developed VT-like episodes with beat‑to‑beat instability. Early afterdepolarizations propagated heterogeneously, generating triggered activity, tissue acceleration, APD dispersion, wavebreak, and rotor formation. These were short and self-terminating (median 0.4 s) and clustered at head/neck region curvatures. To test whether a fixed spatial substrate supports prolonged reentry, we developed a reproducible focal cryoinjury model. After injury, all tissues developed VT-like episodes, and 70% anatomically anchored rotors at the border; three persisted beyond 10 s, a recording-limited lower bound. Dual voltage/Ca<sup>2+</sup> mapping at this resolution establishes EHTs as a non-animal platform for mechanistic study of both trigger- and substrate-driven ventricular arrhythmias.

title: Endothelial p16 expression identifies a subgroup of clear cell renal cell carcinoma with favorable prognosis.
authorString: Stoffel M, Baschun K, Kehl M, Ellinger J, Klümper N, Kadzik S, Winterhagen FI, Ritter M, Hölzel M, Kristiansen G, Toma MI.
abstractText:
Background

Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by extensive angiogenesis and marked architectural heterogeneity. While vascular density has been investigated as a prognostic parameter in ccRCC, little is known about the biological characteristics of intratumoral endothelial cells.

Methods

In this study, we analyzed the p16 expression in a tissue microarray cohort comprising 347 ccRCC cases with clinicopathological and survival data and related the vascular p16 expression to previously described tumor architecture subtypes.

Results

Tumor architecture could be assessed in 315 cases and was classified into nine predominant growth patterns. Tumors with thick trabecular/insular or solid sheet architecture were grouped as high-risk patterns and were associated with higher tumor grade and shorter overall survival (p < 0.001). Tumor cell p16 expression was infrequent and showed no association with clinicopathological parameters or survival. In contrast, endothelial p16 expression was commonly observed in intratumoral blood vessels, with a median of 35% positive vessels per case. Higher endothelial p16 expression, both in extent and intensity, was significantly associated with lower tumor grade, lower pT stage, favorable architectural patterns, and prolonged overall survival. Furthermore, the prognostic impact of architectural growth patterns was most pronounced in tumors with low endothelial p16 expression, whereas tumors with high endothelial p16 expression showed comparable survival independent of architectural subtype.

Conclusion

Endothelial p16 expression is common in ccRCC and is associated with favorable clinicopathological characteristics and prolonged survival. These findings suggest that endothelial p16 expression may complement architectural tumor stratification in ccRCC, identifying cases with good prognosis.

title: Multifaceted role of genetic and epigenetic architecture of glucose homeostasis and diabetes.
authorString: Khokhar M.
abstractText: Glucose homeostasis depends on coordinated genetic and epigenetic regulation of pancreatic beta-cells, insulin-sensitive tissues, and neuroendocrine circuits. This review synthesises evidence from over 600 GWAS loci and the primary literature published between 2008 and 2026, and emerging single-cell functional genomics, CRISPR-based perturbation screens, deep-learning variant-effect predictors (DeepSEA, Enformer, AlphaGenome), and polygenic risk frameworks to explain insulin secretion, insulin signalling, and diabetes susceptibility, converting GWAS associations into mechanistic insight and genotype-guided precision therapies.

title: Transvenous embolization via the pterygoid plexus for a direct carotid-cavernous fistula associated with fibromuscular dysplasia: illustrative case.
authorString: Haruta R, Murai S, Maruno M, Yamada S, Tao Y, Minami-Ogawa Y, Hirai S, Inoue S, Yagi K, Hishikawa T.
abstractText:
Background

Fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) is a nonatherosclerotic arteriopathy that increases the risk of intracranial aneurysm and arterial dissection. Direct carotid-cavernous fistula (CCF) associated with FMD is rare, and the endovascular treatment strategy is not well established.

Observations

A 52-year-old woman developed a high-flow CCF in the setting of bilateral internal carotid artery FMD. Three-dimensional rotational angiography under balloon test occlusion (BTO) enabled precise localization of the fistula proximal to a cavernous-segment aneurysm. Transvenous selective embolization was achieved through the pterygoid plexus, while the transarterial approach through the FMD-affected ICA was performed safely with a flexible distal access catheter.

Lessons

In FMD-associated CCF, accurate localization of the shunt using BTO and meticulous endovascular technique allowed for safe embolization. The pterygoid plexus proved to be a useful and feasible access route. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26625.

title: Repurposing the phospholipase A2 inhibitor, darapladib, to combat multidrug-resistant fungal pathogens, including Candida auris.
authorString: Elgammal Y, Salama EA, Alkashef NM, Lawrence CB, Seleem MN.
abstractText: Candida auris is an emerging multidrug-resistant fungal pathogen and a major global health threat, highlighting the urgent need for new therapeutics. We screened ~2,600 FDA-approved drugs and clinical compounds and identified darapladib (DAL), a phospholipase A2 inhibitor, as a potent antifungal agent against multidrug-resistant C. auris. DAL exhibited antifungal activity against all tested C. auris isolates and showed broad-spectrum activity against other tested clinically important fungal pathogens, including other Candida, Cryptococcus, and mucormycosis-associated species, with minimum inhibitory concentrations of 4-16 μg/mL. DAL also displayed rapid fungicidal activity against C. auris and synergized with amphotericin B against C. auris and filamentous fungal pathogens. More importantly, serial exposure of C. auris to subinhibitory concentrations of DAL for 16 passages did not result in detectable resistance. Mechanistic studies indicated that DAL acts through an ergosterol-dependent membrane targeting mechanism, as exogenous ergosterol attenuated its activity and ergosterol-related haploinsufficient mutants showed reduced susceptibility. Consistent with this mechanism, DAL increased membrane permeability, nucleic acid leakage, and reactive oxygen species. In a Caenorhabditis elegans-C. auris infection model, DAL reduced the C. auris burden to below the limit of detection. Together, these findings support further investigation of DAL as a repurposed antifungal candidate against drug-resistant fungal infections.

title: Intracardiac thrombus and multiple venous thromboses revealing focal segmental glomerulosclerosis.
authorString: Hamzaoui M, Machmachi I, Amar K, Hamdi F, Harmouch T, Haddiya I, Bentata Y.
abstractText: Nephrotic syndrome is associated with a hypercoagulable state, leading to an increased risk of potentially severe thromboembolic events. Although venous thromboses predominantly involve the renal veins and deep veins of the lower extremities, intracardiac thrombosis remains an exceptionally rare manifestation, particularly as the initial presenting feature. We report the case of a 51-year-old woman with a history of schizophrenia and recent cholecystectomy, who was admitted for lower-limb edema and hematuria of two weeks' duration. Computed tomography of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis revealed multiple thrombotic events, including deep vein thrombosis of the lower extremities, partial thrombosis of the left renal vein, and a left ventricular intracardiac thrombus measuring 23 × 20 mm. Laboratory investigations demonstrated nephrotic syndrome with a urine protein-to-creatinine ratio of 10 g/g and hypoalbuminemia of 23 g/L, associated with stage 2 acute kidney injury. Immunological testing was negative, including anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA) and anti-phospholipase A2 receptor (anti-PLA2R) antibodies. Kidney biopsy established the diagnosis of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis. Management consisted of therapeutic anticoagulation, diuretic therapy, and corticosteroid treatment, resulting in progressive clinical and biological improvement. This case highlights the exceptional occurrence of a left ventricular thrombus associated with multiple venous thromboses as the presenting manifestation of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis. It underscores the importance of systematically investigating underlying glomerular disease in patients presenting with multiple or unusual thrombotic events, particularly in the presence of significant proteinuria.

title: Time to Discontinuation and Risk Factors for Outpatient Medical Nutrition Therapy in Primary Care: A Retrospective Cohort Study Using Survival Analysis.
authorString: Ukai M, Abe K, Ohashi K, Ogasawara K.

journal.title: Journal of general and family medicine

abstractText:
Background

Medical nutrition therapy (MNT) provided by registered dietitians is effective for managing non-communicable diseases, but patient discontinuation remains common in clinical practice. Studies examining the timing and predictors of MNT discontinuation are limited. This study aimed to identify the timing and patient factors associated with MNT discontinuation in primary care settings.

Methods

This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients who initiated outpatient MNT at a primary care clinic between April 2018 and March 2023. Patients aged < 18 years and those with cancer- or malnutrition-related conditions were excluded. Discontinuation was defined as no MNT visit or scheduled appointment within 3 months after the last visit. Patients were followed for up to 24 months through March 2025. Kaplan-Meier analysis estimated continuation rates, and multivariable cause-specific Cox proportional hazards models identified factors associated with discontinuation. Multiple sensitivity analyses were performed.

Results

Among 470 patients (median age, 63 years; 59.4% women), 241 (51.3%) discontinued MNT during follow-up. Median time to discontinuation was 15 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 12-21). Continuation rates were 88.3% at 3 months, 70.4% at 6 months, and 43.5% at 24 months. Obesity, dyslipidemia, and medication use were associated with lower discontinuation risk, whereas complications, living with family, and preparation stage of behavior change were associated with higher risk. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the results.

Conclusions

MNT continuation declined rapidly within 6 months. Multiple patient factors were associated with discontinuation risk, suggesting the need for early risk identification and individualized support strategies.

title: High-Resolution Imaging via UHF-US-Based 3D Reconstruction in a 3D In Vivo Tumor Model.
authorString: Ettner-Sitter A, Kuenzel J, Heidenreich M, Mahl L, Pohnert L, Srinivasan D, Pion E, Bauer R, Fuchs D, Wagner BJ, Gröger C, Steger F, Kölbl O, Aung T, Hackl C, Haerteis S.
abstractText: The chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) model resembles a preclinical in vivo platform for the engraftment of different tumors and is especially well-suited for the development and evaluation of novel cancer therapies. Due to the CAM's extensive vascular network, it can sustain engrafted human tumor tissue, which can be used for therapy testing and analysis throughout the experimental process. Although numerous studies have demonstrated successful tumor engraftment and vascular integration into the CAM's blood vessel network, the accurate and sequential measurement of tumor volume remains a significant challenge. Current imaging modalities, such as positron emission tomography/computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging or three-dimensional (3D) digital microscopy are limited by cost, complexity, and potential harm due to injected agents or radiation. This study introduces an innovative imaging approach by utilizing ultrahigh frequency (UHF) ultrasound combined with 3D ultrasound reconstruction of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) on the CAM. By utilizing ultrasound frequencies of up to 71 MHz, two-dimensional (2D) imaging of PDAC tumors was transformed into comprehensive 3D reconstructions. This innovative approach provides a more detailed tissue resolution and enables noninvasive, longitudinal volumetric monitoring of tumor growth in vivo, and in principle provides a platform for future studies assessing angiogenesis and therapy response. In this study the accuracy of 3D UHF ultrasound was tested by comparing it with established imaging techniques such as 3D digital microscopy. In summary, the 3D ultrasound reconstruction resembles a more versatile noninvasive alternative for in vivo tumor volume measurement. This advanced imaging approach adds a valuable methodology for the investigation of tumor biology in the CAM model by providing noninvasive volumetric and morphological characterization of engrafted tumor tissue, thereby linking preclinical research and clinical applications.

title: Delayed incidental dural tears from subfascial drains after spine surgery: illustrative cases.
authorString: Zerebiec KW, Love DL, Callahan KE, Khodadad T, Wicks EE, Methot C, Werheim E, Thakrar R, Ziino C, Tranmer BI, Jewell RP.
abstractText:
Background

Placement of a subfascial drain following open spine surgery is common practice to mitigate postoperative complications, including epidural hematoma, seroma formation, surgical site infection, and wound dehiscence. The authors present 3 cases in which subfascial Hemovac drains were associated with postoperative durotomy following otherwise uncomplicated lumbar surgeries.

Observations

Three patients who underwent single-level lumbar surgery requiring postoperative drain placement subsequently developed CSF leaks, presumed to be secondary to intracorporeal drain movement consistent with the Euler buckling theory.

Lessons

In patients undergoing uncomplicated single-level lumbar spine surgery, consideration should be given to the use of a silicone Jackson-Pratt drain rather than a compression-resistant polyvinyl chloride Hemovac drain. In a small surgical bed, a shorter and more compliant drain may be sufficient, whereas a stiff drain may act as a trocar. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE2640.

title: A rare twist after Ex-vivo RIRS: graft parenchymal urine leak in a living donor kidney.
authorString: Bashir A, Minallah N, Touqeer FA, Asad A, Shan M, Zafar Z, Khan A, Yousaf A.
abstractText: Retrograde intrarenal surgery (RIRS) is performed ex-vivo on donor kidneys prior to transplantation. Upto our knowledge, after the review of existing literature, this is the first reported case of graft parenchymal urine leakage following ex-vivo RIRS in a living donor kidney transplant. Parenchymal urine leaks following ex-vivo retrograde intrarenal surgery (RIRS) in donor kidneys are exceptionally rare. To the best of our knowledge, this represents the first reported case of graft parenchymal urine leakage following ex-vivo RIRS in a living donor kidney transplant. A 29-year-old man was transplanted with a donor kidney following removal of 5 mm upper pole calculus via ex-vivo RIRS. Postoperatively, the patient had bloody drain output, and re-exploration showed a capsular tear. The subsequent clear drain output was confirmed to be a parenchymal urine leak based on drain fluid creatinine concentration and CT urogram. The bleed was managed surgically, and the parenchymal urine leak was treated conservatively using prolonged drainage and double-J stenting. Graft function was stable. Irrigation pressure should be well-controlled during ex-vivo RIRS, and complications should be promptly diagnosed to save the graft function even with rare parenchymal urine leaks.

title: Chronic Rheumatic Heart Disease in Older Brazilians: Hospitalizations and In-Hospital Deaths, 2015-2024.
authorString: Teixeira JR, Ciquini IS, da Costa Rosa AR, Benedet LF, Marques MF, Bernardi TC, Esteves-Pereira TC.
abstractText:
Introduction and objectives

Chronic rheumatic heart disease remains a cause of morbidity in older adults. This study analyzed hospitalizations and in-hospital deaths associated with the disease among Brazilians aged 60 years or older from 2015 to 2024, examining differences by sex and macroregion and temporal trends.

Methods

This ecological time-series study used data from the Brazilian Unified Health System Hospital Information System and official population estimates. Annual crude hospitalization and in-hospital death rates per 100,000 older adults were calculated by sex and macroregion. Joinpoint regression was used to estimate annual and average annual percent changes.

Results

Hospitalizations increased from 2,632 in 2015 to 3,683 in 2024, while crude hospitalization rates changed from 10.56 to 10.78 per 100,000 older adults. In-hospital deaths increased from 362 to 419, whereas corresponding rates declined from 1.45 to 1.23 per 100,000. Nationally, hospitalization rates among women declined by 7.05% annually during 2015-2020 and increased by 10.69% annually during 2020-2024 (both p < 0.001). Among men, rates declined by 6.83% annually during 2015-2021 (p = 0.004) and increased by 16.77% annually during 2021-2024 (p = 0.008). Over the full period, average national trends were not statistically significant for either outcome in either sex. Regional patterns were heterogeneous. In the Northeast, women showed sustained increases in hospitalization rates (5.08% annually; p = 0.021) and in-hospital death rates (11.88% annually; p < 0.001).

Conclusions

Hospitalization rates declined and subsequently rebounded, while population-based in-hospital death rates and their temporal patterns varied by sex and region. These patterns reflect the joint contribution of hospitalization frequency and the proportion of admissions ending in death and should not be interpreted as deaths causally attributable to chronic rheumatic heart disease. Regional variation indicates an uneven distribution of recorded hospital utilization and outcomes but does not, by itself, establish inequalities in access to or quality of care. The recent increase in hospitalizations indicates greater hospital utilization and should not be interpreted as evidence of increased disease incidence. Continued surveillance incorporating both hospitalization rates and the proportion of admissions resulting in death is warranted to better characterize temporal and regional patterns among older adults.

title: When a Contaminant Is Not a Contaminant: A Case Report of Micrococcus luteus Causing Septic Shock in the Absence of Traditional Risk Factors.
authorString: Alajab J, Sooch MK, Yeddi M, Yeddi O, Hussein M, Yeddi A, Frimodig B.
abstractText: Micrococcus luteus is a gram-positive, coagulase-negative coccus commonly regarded as a non-pathogenic commensal organism of human skin and is frequently considered a contaminant when isolated in blood cultures. However, emerging evidence suggests that it may act as an opportunistic pathogen in certain clinical settings. We report a case of septic shock caused by M. luteus in a 47-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus who presented with altered mental status and hemodynamic instability. Despite the absence of indwelling devices, prosthetic material, or structural heart disease, multiple blood cultures were positive for M. luteus, confirming true bacteremia. The patient required aggressive fluid resuscitation, vasopressor support, and intravenous antibiotic therapy, with subsequent clinical improvement and clearance of bacteremia. This case highlights the importance of correlating microbiological findings with clinical presentation and underscores the potential pathogenicity of organisms traditionally considered contaminants.

title: Cloxacillin- and Terbinafine-Associated Mixed Drug-Induced Liver Injury: Contrasting Clinical Outcomes and Causality Assessment Using the Updated RUCAM.
authorString: Casòliva EO, Montero AJA, de Carvalho A, Morer SM, Arvaniti P.
abstractText:
Background

Idiosyncratic drug-induced liver injury (DILI) is an uncommon but potentially severe adverse drug reaction. Although cloxacillin and terbinafine are long-established, widely prescribed agents, both have been associated with mixed/cholestatic DILI, occasionally resulting in prolonged cholestasis or vanishing bile duct syndrome (VBDS). We report two cases with similar clinical and biochemical presentations but markedly different histological findings and long-term outcomes, illustrating that the initial biochemical phenotype may not reflect the extent of bile duct injury or predict subsequent clinical evolution.

Case report

An 83-year-old man presented with jaundice, dark urine, and severe pruritus after receiving cloxacillin for 2 months to treat acute paronychia. A 62-year-old man developed similar symptoms following a 2 month course of terbinafine for a fungal infection. Both patients exhibited a mixed biochemical pattern of liver injury. Comprehensive diagnostic evaluation, including detailed medical history, abdominal imaging, viral and autoimmune serology, excluded alternative causes of liver injury. Causality assessment using the updated RUCAM classified both cases as probable DILI. Liver biopsy demonstrated extensive ductopenia with loss of interlobular bile ducts in more than 50% of portal tracts, consistent with VBDS in the cloxacillin case, whereas the terbinafine case showed intracanalicular cholestasis with preserved bile ducts. HLA genotyping identified the HLA-B∗57:01 and HLA-A∗33:01 susceptibility alleles, respectively. Both patients received supportive treatment with ursodeoxycholic acid, cholestyramine, and rifampicin. The first patient achieved complete biochemical recovery after 8 months, whereas the second fulfilled criteria for chronic DILI with persistent liver test abnormalities beyond 1 year.

Conclusions

These cases illustrate marked clinicopathological heterogeneity despite a similar initial presentation and mixed DILI biochemical pattern. The contrast between biopsy-proven VBDS followed by complete biochemical recovery and preserved bile duct architecture followed by chronic DILI demonstrates that the extent of histological bile duct injury and long-term outcome cannot necessarily be inferred from the initial biochemical phenotype.

title: Cardiac Amyloidosis in Monoclonal Gammopathy of Undetermined Significance.
authorString: Copen S, Copen S.
abstractText: Patients with monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance are followed for years in hematology clinics, and most do not progress to develop defining events of multiple myeloma such as pathologic fractures or a high percentage of plasma cells on a bone marrow biopsy. Newer technologies such as cardiac MRI may lead to the definition of cardiovascular involvement by illness related to monoclonal gammopathy at an earlier time point than previously detected in clinical practice. The link between monoclonal gammopathy and an increased prevalence of transthyretin (ATTR) cardiac amyloidosis also confounds the question of whether changes detected on cardiac MRI indicate AL or ATTR cardiac amyloidosis. Here, a patient with both monoclonal gammopathy, cardiac amyloidosis, and a positive technetium pyrophosphate scan is referred for endomyocardial biopsy to clarify whether he suffers from AL or ATTR cardiac amyloidosis.

title: Late-onset inverse decremental conduction after TAVR: Cause for concern?
authorString: Rajjoub K, Ortega-Torregimeno A, Oristrell G.
abstractText: We report the case of a patient with late-onset inverse decremental conduction following transcatheter aortic valve replacement. We emphasize the importance of recognizing this phenomenon, as it may predict progression to advanced atrioventricular block and the need for permanent pacemaker implantation.

title: Preserved anabolic skeletal muscle capacity in response to exercise and protein intake after critical illness.
authorString: Fischer-Hammerschmied A, Tardif N, Mandić M, Gustafsson T, Apro W, Helleberg J, Amouzandeh M, Grip J, Seldén D, Rooyackers O, Sundström Rehal M.
abstractText:
Background

Low muscle mass and persistent weakness are common after critical illness, but the mechanisms behind impaired recovery are incompletely understood. The aim of this study was to investigate the skeletal muscle anabolic response to combined resistance exercise and protein intake in intensive care unit (ICU) survivors, compared to matched controls without a history of critical illness. We hypothesised that residual anabolic resistance limits muscle regeneration after ICU stay.

Methods

Former patients were enrolled within 3 to 6 months of intensive care unit discharge. Muscle biopsies were obtained before and after resistance exercise using a flywheel leg extension ergometer, combined with ingestion of 24 g hydrolysed protein. Muscle protein fractional synthetic rate was determined from the incorporation of [ring-²H₅]phenylalanine into mixed-muscle protein during a primed continuous intravenous infusion. Anabolic and proteolytic pathways were measured using standard assays. Group-by-time differences were analysed using linear mixed models. The primary comparison was the between-group difference in pre-to-post change in muscle protein synthesis.

Results

Twenty ICU survivors (60 ± 12 years, 30% female, BMI 26.9 (IQR 22.9-28.7), SAPS 3 62.3 ± 15.8) and 20 age- and sex-matched controls were included. ICU survivors had significantly lower quadriceps muscle thickness (p = 0.02) and handgrip strength (p = 0.04) than controls. In ICU survivors, muscle protein synthesis from plasma precursor amino acids was higher at baseline than in controls (0.041%/hour vs. 0.030%/hour, p = 0.009), but increased less (Δ 0.031 vs. Δ 0.040%/hour, p = 0.04). Post-intervention muscle protein synthesis was similar between groups (0.071%/hour vs. 0.070%/hour, p = 0.70). At baseline, ICU survivors showed lower activation of the autophagy-lysosomal pathway. In both groups, the intervention increased anabolic signalling, decreased initiation of autophagy and increased parts of the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway.

Conclusions

In ICU survivors with persistent muscle loss and weakness, the increase in muscle protein synthesis after combined resistance exercise and protein intake was smaller than in controls, in the context of a higher baseline fractional synthetic rate. Post-intervention muscle protein synthesis rates were similar between groups. These findings provide the first mechanistic support for structured exercise-nutrition rehabilitation to promote muscle recovery after critical illness.

Trial registration

This study was prospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05261984), 2022-02-20.

title: Current Status and Treatment Outcomes of Mechanical Thrombectomy for Acute Large Vessel Occlusion during On- and Off-Hours in Our Institution.
authorString: Kanazawa Y, Kuribara T, Nitta Y, Kohyama S, Miyazaki H, Nawashiro H, Kita H.
abstractText:
Objective

Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is the standard of care for acute large vessel occlusion (LVO); however, off-hours treatment may be delayed because of limited staffing. We compared MT outcomes between on-hours and off-hours at a single center and investigated factors associated with 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 0-3.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed 101 consecutive patients with anterior circulation LVO and a pre-stroke mRS 0-2 who underwent MT at Tokorozawa Central Hospital between January 2020 and December 2025. Patients were classified into on-hours (9:00-17:00 on Mondays through Saturdays, excluding national holidays and the period from December 31 to January 3) and off-hours groups based on hospital arrival time. The primary endpoint was 90-day mRS 0-3. Secondary endpoints included Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (TICI) grade 2b-3, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH), and any intracranial hemorrhage. Time metrics, including onset-to-door time (ODT), door-to-image time, door-to-needle time, image-to-puncture time (IPT), door-to-puncture time (DPT), puncture-to-recanalization time (PRT), door-to-recanalization time (DRT), and onset-to-recanalization time (ORT), were compared between the 2 groups, and factors associated with 90-day mRS 0-3 were evaluated using univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses.

Results

The on-hours group comprised 46 patients and the off-hours group 55 patients. Compared with the on-hours group, the off-hours group had significantly longer IPT (median 83 vs. 51 min, p <0.001), DPT (median 103 vs. 71 min, p <0.001), and DRT (median 151 vs. 124 min, p = 0.003). ODT and ORT did not differ significantly between the groups (median 105 vs. 89 min, p = 0.825, and median 285 vs. 234 min, p = 0.154, respectively). PRT did not differ significantly between groups (median 53 vs. 48 min, p = 0.626). The proportion of patients achieving 90-day mRS 0-3 did not differ significantly between groups (45.5% vs. 50.0%, p = 0.692). No significant differences were observed in TICI 2b-3 (80.0% vs. 82.6%, p = 0.802) or sICH (3.6% vs. 4.3%, p = 1.000). In the multivariable logistic regression, younger age (odds ratio [OR] 0.922, p = 0.002) was an independent predictor of 90-day mRS 0-3, whereas off-hours status was not (OR 0.917, p = 0.845).

Conclusion

Despite prolonged time from hospital arrival to treatment initiation in the off-hours group, the proportion of patients achieving 90-day mRS 0-3 did not differ significantly between groups. In multivariable logistic regression, younger age was an independent predictor of 90-day mRS 0-3. Further efforts are needed to identify the causes of off-hours delays and to improve our clinical care system.

title: Machine Learning-Based Diagnosis of Coronary Heart Disease with Clinical and Biomarker Data.
authorString: Zhang Z, Zhao A, Mi Y, Qiao Y, Xue S, Zhang F, Yang J, Song Z.
abstractText:
Purpose

Coronary heart disease (CHD) is a common condition associated with high disability and mortality. Although coronary angiography (CAG) remains the gold standard for diagnosis, its accessibility is limited in medically underserved regions or for patients who are ineligible for the procedure. The aim of this study was to develop a prediction model using machine learning algorithms that integrate clinical data and plasma biomarkers for timely and noninvasive CHD diagnosis.

Patients and methods

A total of 191 patients who underwent CAG at the First Affiliated Hospital of Henan University between March and October 2023, comprising 151 CHD patients and 40 non-CHD controls, were included. Clinical data and plasma samples were collected; the levels of eight biomarkers (LPA, MCP-1, TNF-α, IL-1β, NRG4, S100A8/A9, HMGB1, and cfDNA) were measured by ELISAs and fluorescence spectrophotometry. The dataset was split into training, test, and validation sets (8:1:1) and standardized. After the SMOTE was applied to the training set, key features were selected via recursive feature elimination with cross-validation (RFECV). Six machine learning algorithms were used to construct the models, and their performance was evaluated on the test set and via 10-fold cross-validation. SHAP was used to interpret the optimal model.

Results

Eight important features were identified. Among the six models, the KNN model performed best on the test set, achieving an AUROC of 80.7%, accuracy of 82.7%, F1‑score of 89.5%, precision of 86.4%, and sensitivity of 92.7%.

Conclusion

A machine learning model integrating clinical and plasma biomarker data has potential for predicting CHD in patients who present with chest discomfort, offering a potential diagnostic aid when CAG is not readily accessible, pending validation in larger, multicenter studies. However, these findings are based on a single-center cohort of 191 patients and require external validation in larger, multicenter populations.

title: MiR-532 as a Potential Therapeutic Target and Biomarker: Biological Functions, Molecular Mechanisms, and Clinical Perspectives.
authorString: Mohammadi L, Baluchnejadmojarad T, Roghani M.
abstractText: MicroRNA-532 (miR-532), including miR-532-3p and miR-532-5p, is an important regulator of gene expression involved in numerous physiological and pathological processes. It modulates key signaling pathways, including PI3K/Akt and Wnt/β-catenin, thereby contributing to the regulation of several biological processes, including oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. Dysregulation of miR-532 is associated with various diseases, including neurological disorders, cardiovascular diseases, and musculoskeletal disorders, as well as cancer. miR-532 modulates inflammation, oxidative stress, and cell death. Its role in cancer appears to be context-dependent, functioning as either a tumor suppressor or an oncogenic regulator depending on the tumor type. In addition, miR-532 has been detected in tissues and body fluids, and its altered expression has been reported in several diseases, suggesting its potential as a candidate biomarker for disease-related changes. This narrative review summarizes relevant literature identified through searches of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published up to June 2026. The focus of this review is on the biological functions, molecular mechanisms, and therapeutic and diagnostic significance of miR-532 in human diseases. However, current findings are largely based on preclinical and observational evidence, with relatively few clinical studies available. Overall, miR-532 shows potential as a therapeutic target and biomarker, but further clinical studies are needed to confirm its clinical significance.

title: Association and Discriminative Performance of a Bilirubin-D-Dimer-Albumin Index for LVEF <45% in Patients with Heart Failure: A Single-Centre Retrospective Study.
authorString: Rafiq S, Atajanova J, Pengyi H.
abstractText:
Background

Accurate identification of reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is important for risk stratification and management of patients with heart failure (HF). Because HF involves multiple interrelated pathophysiological processes, a combination of biomarkers may provide information beyond that offered by individual markers. This study evaluated the association and discriminatory performance of the bilirubin-D-dimer-albumin (BDA) Index for identifying LVEF <45% and compared its performance with that of NT-proBNP.

Methods

In this single-centre retrospective study, 338 patients with HF were categorized according to echocardiographic LVEF as <45% (n=149) or ≥45% (n=189). The BDA Index was calculated as ln(total bilirubin [µmol/L]) × ln(D-dimer [ng/mL]) / albumin [g/L]. Discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and DeLong's test. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between the BDA Index and LVEF <45%, with internal validation performed using 1000 bootstrap samples and 10-fold cross-validation. Decision curve analysis (DCA) was used to assess the potential clinical utility of the model.

Results

The BDA Index was significantly higher in patients with LVEF <45% (P<0.001). Its AUC was 0.902 (95% CI, 0.870-0.934), compared with 0.773 (95% CI, 0.723-0.823) for NT-proBNP (DeLong's test, P<0.001). At the Youden-derived cutoff of 0.435, sensitivity and specificity were 87.9% and 78.3%, respectively. After multivariable adjustment, each 0.1-unit increase in the BDA Index was associated with LVEF <45% (OR, 4.65; 95% CI, 2.94-7.36; P<0.001). Adding the BDA Index significantly improved model fit (likelihood-ratio χ2=73.44, df=1, P<0.001) and increased the AUC from 0.873 to 0.934. Internal validation yielded an optimism-adjusted AUC of 0.908, while 10-fold cross-validation yielded a mean AUC of 0.901. DCA showed greater estimated net benefit for the model incorporating the BDA Index across threshold probabilities of 5%-80%.

Conclusion

In this single-centre retrospective cohort, the BDA Index showed good discriminatory performance for identifying LVEF <45% and provided additional information beyond NT-proBNP and other clinical and laboratory variables. Prospective multicentre studies with independent external validation are needed to assess its reproducibility, calibration, and potential clinical utility.

title: Integrated Single-Cell Transcriptomics, Multi-Omics, and Mendelian Randomization Reveal Ferroptosis-Related Molecular Subtypes and a Genetically Supported Causal Candidate in Psoriasis.
authorString: Xu M, Zuo Y, Liu H, Jia H, Liu X.
abstractText:
Background

Ferroptosis contributes to inflammatory skin diseases, but its role in psoriasis remains incompletely understood. We performed an integrated multi‑omics analysis combining single‑cell transcriptomics, bulk transcriptomics, machine learning, consensus clustering, and Mendelian randomization (MR) to characterize ferroptosis‑related molecular features, intercellular communication, immune microenvironment remodeling, molecular subtypes, and causal biomarkers in psoriasis.

Methods

Single‑cell RNA‑seq data (GSE151177) were analyzed to quantify ferroptosis activity across cell populations and infer intercellular communication networks. Bulk transcriptomic datasets (GSE30999, GSE78097) were integrated for differential expression and machine‑learning feature selection with SHAP interpretation. Consensus clustering, immune infiltration, functional enrichment, and drug repurposing analyses were performed. Cis‑eQTLs from eQTLGen (n=31,684) served as instruments for two‑sample MR with psoriasis GWAS from FinnGen (13,667 cases, 395,092 controls).

Results

Macrophages/monocytes and fibroblasts showed the highest ferroptosis scores. MIF signaling (MIF-CD74/CD44, MIF-CD74/CXCR4, MIF-ACKR3) dominated keratinocyte outgoing communication. Transcriptomic integration yielded 72 overlapping ferroptosis-related genes; machine learning identified eight feature genes (CD24, EFNB2, DDX39A, NDRG4, GPRC5A, S100A8, PRSS8, ITPKC). CD24 (AUC=0.979) and S100A8 (AUC=0.974) exhibited top diagnostic performance. Consensus clustering stratified patients into two subtypes (C1, C2); all eight genes were highly expressed in C1, while C2 showed upregulated phagocytic but downregulated innate immune pathways. Drug enrichment suggested MS-275, genistein, and β-adrenoceptor agonists as potential ferroptosis-modulating compounds. MR demonstrated that only PRSS8 eQTL had a nominally significant causal association with psoriasis risk (P < 0.05, β = 0.0073).

Conclusion

Our multi‑omics study delineates the ferroptosis‑related landscape in psoriasis, identifies MIF signaling as a key keratinocyte communication axis, establishes a high‑performance diagnostic model with eight feature genes, defines two distinct immune‑metabolic subtypes, and provides genetic evidence supporting PRSS8 as a putative causal biomarker for psoriasis susceptibility, offering novel insights and potential ferroptosis‑based biomarkers and therapeutic targets for psoriasis.

title: Centrosomal protein 55: Research progress on biological characteristics, disease associations and clinical translational potential (Review).
authorString: Nong S, Huang Q, Huang K, Luo X, Huang Y, Zheng W, Huang W, Liu Z.
abstractText: Centrosomal protein 55 (CEP55), a core member of the CEP centrosomal protein family, is a molecule that regulates cytokinesis during the end of cell division and is also extensively involved in multiple physiological processes, including genomic stability maintenance, immune regulation and embryonic development. It has been shown that CEP55 participates in pathological processes such as tumor cell proliferation, invasion, metastasis and immune escape by modulating multiple signaling pathways including PI3K/AKT, NF‑κB and JAK/STAT. Furthermore, it exhibits a close correlation with poor prognosis among patients with cancer. In addition, dysregulated CEP55 expression is also implicated in the pathological processes of neurological disorders, reproductive‑genetic diseases and chronic metabolic diseases. These findings highlight the potential clinical translational value of CEP55 for disease diagnosis, prognostic evaluation and targeted therapy. Based on recent domestic and international research, the present study systematically reviews the molecular biological properties, expression features and action mechanisms of CEP55 across multi‑system diseases, and summarizes its clinical application potential, to provide a theoretical reference for promoting relevant basic research and implementing precise clinical diagnosis and treatment.

title: Sulbactam/Durlobactam for CRAB Bacteremia and Pneumonia in a Critically Ill Patient in China: A Case Report.
authorString: Deng H, Chen K, Chen K.
abstractText:
Background

Evidence supporting sulbactam/durlobactam (SUL-DUR) for carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) bloodstream infection remains limited, particularly in critically ill patients with multiorgan failure.

Case presentation

A 25-year-old man underwent emergency splenectomy for a ruptured splenic artery aneurysm with 7500 mL estimated blood loss. On transfer to our ICU, PaO2/FiO2 was 68 mm Hg, consistent with severe ARDS. He subsequently developed a grade B postoperative pancreatic fistula. A quality-graded sputum specimen grew carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae and CRAB, and a peripheral blood culture drawn during cefoperazone-sulbactam therapy grew CRAB, indicating breakthrough bacteremia; the blood isolate was susceptible to SUL-DUR but resistant to both carbapenems. Ceftazidime-avibactam was replaced with imipenem-cilastatin plus SUL-DUR for eight days, with nebulized colistimethate sodium. Concurrent care included source control, prone ventilation, and pancreatic collection drainage. Procalcitonin had normalized before SUL-DUR began, whereas IL-6 and hs-CRP rose around the positive blood culture and fell during SUL-DUR; he was extubated on ICU day 27. A post-extubation withdrawal episode with convulsions, bronchospasm, and lactic acidosis resolved with rescue sedation. He was discharged from the ICU on June 17, 2026, with negative follow-up blood cultures, and remained well at outpatient review on July 30.

Conclusion

This case adds real-world experience regarding the potential role of SUL-DUR in CRAB bacteremia with pneumonia. Because recovery occurred alongside source control, ventilatory support, and sequential antimicrobial therapy, the outcome cannot be attributed to SUL-DUR alone. Larger prospective studies are required to define its role in CRAB bloodstream infection.

title: Diagnostic Performance of the FilmArray BCID2 Multiplex PCR Panel Applied to Excised Heart Valve Specimens from Patients with Infective Endocarditis.
authorString: Bilewska A, Skrzeczyńska J, Dorota M, Skowrońska A, Wojtyniak E, Darmofalska K, Woźniak A, Borek K, Sulik-Tyszka B, Skolimowska G, Wróbel K, Michalski W, Magdziak A.
abstractText: Infective endocarditis (IE) is a life-threatening disease in which rapid identification of the causative pathogen is essential for appropriate antimicrobial therapy. Although blood cultures remain the standard microbiological method, complementary molecular techniques have the potential to improve pathogen detection in selected clinical settings. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the FilmArray Blood Culture Identification 2 (BCID2) multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) panel applied off-label to excised heart valve specimens. Excised heart valve specimens obtained from 47 patients undergoing surgery for IE were analysed using the BCID2 panel. The BCID2 results were compared with blood and valve culture results. Forty-two patients were included for blood cultures and 46 for valve cultures. Using blood culture as the clinical reference method, the BCID2 assay demonstrated a sensitivity of 78.4% (95% confidence interval (CI): 61.8-90.2%), a specificity of 60.0% (95% CI: 14.7-94.7%), a positive predictive value (PPV) of 93.5% (95% CI: 78.6-99.2%), and a negative predictive value (NPV) of 27.3% (95% CI: 6.0-61.0%). Agreement between the BCID2 assay and blood culture was low (Cohen's κ = 0.253; 95% CI: -0.068-0.573; p = 0.067). In the secondary comparison using conventional valve culture, sensitivity was 8.8% (95% CI: 1.9-23.7%), whereas specificity was 100% (95% CI: 75.3-100%). These findings suggest that off-label application of the BCID2 panel to excised heart valve specimens may complement conventional microbiological methods in selected patients with infective endocarditis. However, a negative BCID2 result should not be used to exclude infective endocarditis, and larger multicentre studies are warranted to further evaluate the clinical utility of this approach.

title: Impulse Oscillometry Findings in Children and Adolescents with Adrenal Insufficiency: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study.
authorString: Yılmaz E, Topal E, Dündar İ, Yamancan Yılmaz Z, Koker Ozer N, Çamtosun E.
abstractText:
Background

Airway function in children with adrenal insufficiency (AI) has not been well characterized. We evaluated impulse oscillometry (IOS) findings in pediatric AI and compared patients with congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) and AI due to causes other than CAH (non-CAH AI).

Methods

In this cross-sectional study, 52 children with AI underwent IOS. Oscillometric abnormalities were defined using z-score-based upper and lower limits of normal. IOS z-scores and clinical characteristics were compared between the CAH (n = 24) and non-CAH AI (n = 28) groups.

Results

The median age was 16 years (IQR, 6 years; min-max, 4-18 years), and 53.8% of participants were male. CAH was the most common etiology (46.1%). Median (IQR) IOS values were 0.49 (IQR, 0.32) kPa·L-1·s for R5, 0.29 (IQR, 0.13) kPa·L-1·s for R20, 0.20 (IQR, 0.16) kPa·L-1·s for R5-R20, -0.13 (IQR, 0.11) kPa·L-1·s for X5, -0.01 (IQR, 0.08) kPa·L-1·s for X20, 1.74 (IQR, 1.30) kPa·L-1 for AX, and 20.8 (IQR, 5.32) Hz for resonance frequency (Fres). The most frequent abnormality was reduced X5 (21.2%), followed by elevated R5 (19.2%), elevated R5-R20 (19.2%), reduced X20 (15.4%), elevated AX (15.4%), elevated R20 (13.5%), and elevated Fres (7.7%). No significant differences were observed between the CAH and non-CAH AI groups in demographic characteristics, atopic diseases, or any IOS parameter (all p > 0.05).

Conclusions

A subset of children with AI had IOS measurements outside published parameter-specific reference limits. Among individual IOS parameters, measurements outside the applied reference limits were most frequently observed for X5, R5, and R5-R20. Because no healthy control group was included and the reference equations were derived from populations different from the study population, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory.

title: Three-Dimensional Strain for Left Ventricular Function Assessment in Children After Successful Ventricular Septal Defect Repair.
authorString: Kamińska H, Haponiuk-Skwarlińska J, Pietrzak R, Werner B.
abstractText: Background: Ventricular septal defect (VSD) has a good prognosis after surgical treatment. Three-dimensional (3D) strain echocardiography is a novel method adapting AI for assessing ventricular function; however, its utility remains to be tested. The aim of the study was to assess accuracy of 3D strain echocardiography based on a specific population of patients. Methods: The study enrolled children after successful surgical VSD treatment. In all patients, 3D echocardiography was performed to assess left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and global and segmental longitudinal (LS), circumferential (CS), and radial strain (RS) values. The results were compared with those of healthy individuals matched for age and sex. Results: The study group consisted of 20 children (12 males) aged 3-17 years (mean 7.0 ± 4.3 years), with normal ventricular function on routine 2D echocardiography. The global strain values in all patients were within the standard range in the literature for sex and age. Statistically significant differences between study and control groups were observed in terms of LVEF (55.6 ± 6.9% vs. 59.3 ± 4.8%, p = 0.046), global LS (-21.4 ± 4.3 vs. -24.8 ± 3.5, p = 0.010), and RS (38.7 ± 6.1% vs. 43.6 ± 5.0%, p = 0.010). Segmental strain values showed dysfunction limited to the patched septal area. Conclusions: 3D strain echocardiography is able to detect regional subclinical cardiac function impairment in children after successful surgical treatment of VSD.

title: Independent Risk Factors and Combined Predictive Model for Severe <i>Mycoplasma pneumoniae</i> Pneumonia in Children: The Role of Vitamin D Deficiency.
authorString: Zhang M, Fu Y, Ma R, Yu Z, Jin S, Zhang X.
abstractText: Objectives: Vitamin D deficiency had been associated with the pathophysiology of respiratory infections. This research sought to assess the correlation between disease severity, serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] and lung function in children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP). Methods: A cohort of 102 children with MPP aged 6-17 years was recruited. All enrolled participants were 6-14 years old, and they were categorised into a mild group (n = 50) and a severe group (n = 52). Between-group comparisons were performed for demographic characteristics, serum 25(OH)D concentrations, laboratory indicators, imaging results, and pulmonary function. Logistic regression was employed to determine risk variables, and their predictive ability for SMPP was examined by ROC. Results: The severe group had markedly reduced serum 25(OH)D concentrations compared to the mild group (17.23 ± 6.81 vs. 20.49 ± 6.09 ng/mL; p = 0.013). Fever duration was prolonged, and CRP, LDH, D-dimer, NLR, AST and IL-6 were elevated in the severe group (all p < 0.05). Moreover, pleural effusion and pulmonary consolidation were more commonly observed in the severe group (p < 0.05). Pulmonary function showed no disparities between groups. Logistic regression identified 25(OH)D < 12 ng/mL (OR = 11.31), elevated CRP (OR = 1.033), elevated LDH (OR = 1.009), prolonged fever duration (OR = 1.552), and pleural effusion (OR = 41.86) as independent risk variables for SMPP. The integrated model produced an AUC of 0.866 (95% CI: 0.795-0.937), demonstrating 88.5% sensitivity and 74.0% specificity. Conclusions: 25(OH)D < 12 ng/mL, elevated CRP and LDH, prolonged fever duration, and pleural effusion are associated with severe pneumonia in children with MPP aged 6-14 years. Their combined use has exploratory predictive potential for identifying severe disease in children with MPP.

title: SET Domain Genes in Neurodevelopmental Disorders.
authorString: Ohguri A, Nakagawa T, Nakagawa M, Hosoi T.
abstractText: Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) comprise a genetically and clinically heterogeneous group of conditions, with disruption of chromatin regulation and developmental gene-expression programs representing an important molecular mechanism underlying their pathogenesis. SET domain-containing (SETD) proteins constitute a diverse family of chromatin regulators that primarily mediate histone methylation, although some lack demonstrated intrinsic catalytic activity or modify non-histone substrates. Pathogenic variants in multiple SETD genes, including SETD1A, KMT2D, SETD2, NSD1, and EZH2, cause NDDs characterized by developmental delay, intellectual disability, speech and language impairment, autism-related features, epilepsy, growth abnormalities, and congenital anomalies. Representative examples include SETD1A-related neurodevelopmental disorder (OMIM #619056), KMT2D-related Kabuki syndrome type 1 (OMIM #147920), SETD2-related Luscan-Lumish syndrome (OMIM #616831), NSD1-related Sotos syndrome (OMIM #117550), and EZH2-related Weaver syndrome (OMIM #277590). In this review, we summarize the classification, domain architecture, and molecular functions of human SETD proteins and integrate clinical findings with mechanistic insights obtained from genetically modified mouse models. These studies reveal substantial cross-species convergence in cognitive, behavioral, synaptic, and developmental phenotypes while also demonstrating that individual SETD proteins regulate distinct molecular processes. Importantly, phenotypic similarity does not necessarily indicate a common molecular mechanism, and variant-specific effects, including loss-of-function, gain-of-function, dominant-negative, and substrate-selective alterations, must be considered when interpreting experimental models. Several studies further demonstrate partial reversibility of molecular and behavioral abnormalities through restoration of SETD protein function, inhibition of opposing chromatin-modifying enzymes such as LSD1, or correction of downstream signaling pathways. These findings suggest that therapeutic opportunities may extend beyond transcriptional regulation to downstream processes including translation, synaptic function, and cellular signaling. Integrating human genetics with animal and human cellular models will therefore be essential for defining shared and gene-specific mechanisms and identifying therapeutically actionable pathways in SETD-related NDDs.

title: An Evidence-Tiered Developmental Framework for Congenital Vertebral Malformations: Spatiotemporal Thresholds in Genotype-Phenotype Interpretation.
authorString: Wang X, Zhang Q, Ji E, Sui Y, Zhu Q, Li K, Xue X.
abstractText: Congenital vertebral malformations (CVMs) encompass formation, segmentation and mixed defects, with or without scoliosis. This narrative review relates human genetic findings to paraxial mesoderm specification, somitogenesis, sclerotome differentiation and vertebral morphogenesis. An author-defined evidence hierarchy distinguishes established disease relationships, emerging susceptibility mechanisms and hypothesis-generating observations; it is not a formal ClinGen classification. Replicated TBX6 dosage mechanisms and disease-specific segmentation disorders provide stronger etiological evidence than candidate-gene burden signals, regulatory hypotheses or accessible-tissue methylation associations. Evidence is assigned to a defined gene-disease or mechanism-phenotype relationship, not to a gene or pathway universally. Building on previous developmental and gene-environment models, we outline a conceptual spatiotemporal threshold framework in which dosage, developmental stage, tissue distribution and modifiers may influence vertebral anatomy. No numerical human threshold has been established. Explicit appraisal criteria, relationship-specific evidence summaries and proposed experimental tests separate demonstrated findings from extrapolation. Standardized vertebral and rib phenotyping, associated anomalies and inheritance remain essential for genomic interpretation. Molecular diagnosis may inform counseling and syndrome-specific evaluation but does not independently establish prognosis or surgical indications.

title: Preoperative Ballon Aortic Valvuloplasty vs. Conservative Management in Patients Undergoing Hip Fracture Surgery with Underlying Severe Aortic Stenosis.
authorString: De Vita A, Covino M, Mollo F, Vumbaca M, Napolitano C, Tremamunno S, Cambise N, Natali R, Rossi M, Bove T, Vitiello R, Maccauro G, Franceschi F, Trani C, Burzotta F, Lanza GA.
abstractText: Background: Old adults with hip fracture (HFx) and concomitant severe aortic stenosis (AS) represent a high-risk population in whom urgent orthopedic repair is usually required, while definitive valve replacement is rarely feasible preoperatively. The clinical benefit of balloon aortic valvuloplasty (BAV) as a bridging strategy remains uncertain. Methods: In this observational study, we included patients admitted to our Emergency Department for HFx who had concomitant severe AS. Management of severe AS consisted of either conservative therapy or preoperative BAV. The early clinical endpoints included 30-day mortality, time to surgery, length of intensive care unit and hospital stay and need for mechanical ventilation. The late clinical endpoint was 180-day all-cause mortality. Results: Among 3958 patients admitted for HFx fracture, 46 (1.2%) were found to have severe AS and fulfilled the inclusion criteria. Of these, 12 patients (26.1%) underwent preoperative BAV and 34 (73.9%) received conservative management. Thirty-day mortality was 8.3% in the BAV group and 23.5% in the conservative group (HR 0.32; 95%CI 0.04-2.60; p = 0.29). Time to surgery was longer in the BAV group (p < 0.001) with concomitantly longer hospital (p = 0.001) and ICU (p = 0.041) stays. Preoperative BAV was independently associated with lower 180-day mortality (HR 0.13; 95%CI 0.03-0.63; p = 0.011). Conclusions: In patients with severe AS undergoing urgent HFx repair, preoperative BAV was associated with reduced 180-day mortality, suggesting a potential long-term prognostic benefit, which warrants confirmation in larger prospective studies. However, it was not associated with significantly better 30-day survival and was accompanied by surgical delay and greater healthcare resource utilization.

title: Maternal RSV Vaccination and Complementary Infant-Protection Strategies in Singapore: A Modified Nominal Group Technique Consensus Study.
authorString: Chong CY, Goh A, Kale AS, Kang JHL, Lee BW, Mathur M, Tagore S.
abstractText:
Background

Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract disease in infants and a major contributor to infant morbidity and mortality. A previous Singapore consensus addressed RSV disease burden and the role of the monoclonal antibody, nirsevimab, but did not extend to maternal RSV vaccination or its complementary use with long-acting monoclonal antibodies (mAbs). We sought structured expert consensus on positioning maternal RSV vaccination and a complementary prevention strategy in Singapore.

Methods

A modified nominal group technique (mNGT) was used. A multidisciplinary panel of seven Singapore-based experts in obstetrics, including maternal-fetal medicine and paediatrics (respiratory, infectious disease, immunisation, and immunology), reviewed a pre-circulated targeted evidence review and four draft statements across four themes (burden, preventive pathways, maternal RSV vaccination, and complementary strategy), with the opportunity to submit written comments in advance. At a live virtual meeting on 16 June 2026, facilitated by a medical communications agency, the panel first discussed the evidence underpinning each draft statement and then voted openly (non-anonymously) on each statement in sequence. Consensus was predefined as ≥70% agreement. Statements that did not reach consensus were refined collectively, with each expert contributing in turn, and re-voted.

Results

All seven experts attended and voted. Two statements reached consensus in Round 1 (Theme 2, 7/7; Theme 4, 6/7) and two after a single round of modification (Theme 1, 0/7 and then 7/7 after "first months of life" was specified as "first six months of life"; Theme 3, 3/7 and then 6/7 after "eligible pregnancies" was explicitly defined). The final statements cover RSV burden in the first six months of life, informed choice of preventive pathway, maternal RSV vaccination as an antenatal option for eligible pregnancies, and a complementary strategy in which a long-acting mAb (nirsevimab) is considered for infants not adequately protected by maternal vaccination.

Conclusions

This expert consensus supports maternal RSV vaccination as an antenatal prevention option for eligible pregnancies in Singapore and a complementary strategy with nirsevimab for infants not adequately covered by maternal vaccination. The statements represent expert consensus intended to inform, not replace, national guidance.

title: HDL Remodeling in Severe Bacterial Infection in Children: A Potential Biomarker for Diagnosis and Therapeutic Monitoring.
authorString: Finizio A, Sarno M, Botti C, Castaldo A, Catzola A, Cernera G, Crispino G, Di Nardo G, Gelzo M, Lepore L, Mandato C, Mirra V, Moggia S, Nunziata F, Orlando F, Pascarella A, Pierri L, Rosa M, Savoia F, Siani P, Castaldo G.
abstractText: Many pediatric patients with severe bacterial infection (SBI) present with a compromised general clinical picture. Early identification of the infectious and inflammatory state can improve clinical outcomes. Although microbiological culture remains the gold standard for diagnosis, its delayed results highlight the need for early biomarkers to improve clinical decision-making and patient outcomes. During infection, the acute phase response alters lipid metabolism, compromising cholesterol efflux. In this study, we characterized the serum lipid profile and HDL subclasses in 63 children with SBI at hospital admission (T0) and discharge (T1), comparing them with 63 age- and sex-matched healthy subjects. At T0, we found a significant reduction in serum total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, and HDL cholesterol in subjects with SBI compared to controls. Interestingly, at a cut-off value of 41.5 mg/dL, HDL cholesterol discriminated the two groups with a sensitivity of 76% and a specificity of 86% for SBI. At T1, total and LDL cholesterol increased, while HDL cholesterol remained unchanged. Moreover, we observed at T1 a clear remodeling of HDL classes, with a significant decrease in large HDL with pro-inflammatory activity and an increase in the intermediate and small HDL with anti-inflammatory activity, compared to time T0. This study proposes serum HDL cholesterol as a candidate biomarker and highlights the role of HDL cholesterol and its classes in inflammatory and immune regulation in systemic bacterial infection, potentially identifying patients who could benefit from HDL-based therapies.

title: Precision Nutrition and Health Outcomes Across the Lifespan.
authorString: Shi YS, Brown AGM, Dixit S, Shiroma EJ, Farmer N, Lu Q, Sood B, Vitalis D, Ilias M, Lachowicz-Scroggins M, Pratt CA.
abstractText: Precision nutrition is an emerging paradigm that seeks to tailor dietary recommendations and interventions based on individual and population characteristics. Although advances in multi-omics, wearable sensors, and artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) have accelerated discovery, translation into practice remains limited by fragmented evidence across life stages and insufficient integration of knowledge regarding systems biology and other influences on health. Nutritional needs, vulnerabilities, intervention opportunities, and response heterogeneity evolve dynamically from preconception and pregnancy through infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood, and older age. These life stage-specific processes intersect with (epi)genetic, metabolic and microbiome factors, as well as social, psychological, behavioral, and environmental/geographic influences, contributing to heterogeneity in health outcomes. Addressing this complexity requires not only multimodal predictive models but also frameworks that integrate data standards and harmonization, systems biology, implementation science, and community engagement. To provide a structured approach to this complexity, we developed a seven-pillar Precision Nutrition Framework encompassing prevention for all, data sources, quantitative sciences, qualitative sciences, intervention implementation, communities, and education and workforce training. Using this framework and a lifespan perspective, we examine opportunities for promoting cardiovascular, pulmonary, hematologic, and circadian/sleep health, synthesize evidence on key nutrients, dietary patterns, and emerging biomarkers, and adapt and expand the "precision nutrition plate" for implementation research in clinical and community settings. We highlight critical research gaps, including the need for phenotype-guided trials, standardized data integration, and scalable implementation strategies. By integrating biological, behavioral, and broader environmental dimensions across the life course, precision nutrition can advance more effective, accessible, and sustainable approaches for disease prevention and health promotion.

title: Prognostic Value of the Atherogenic Index of Plasma for Severity and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Young Patients (≤35 Years) with Coronary Artery Disease: A Retrospective Study.
authorString: Sun J, Liu J, Wang Y, Zhao F, Han W, Zhou Y, Shi D.
abstractText: Background: Rising coronary artery disease (CAD) in young adults calls for early risk stratification, yet the atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) has been understudied in patients aged ≤35 years. We therefore assessed its association with coronary lesion severity and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in this cohort. Methods: This single-center retrospective study enrolled 948 patients aged 18-35 years with angiographically confirmed CAD. Greater coronary lesion severity was defined as a Gensini score > 40. The association between AIP and MACE was explored. Results: During a median follow-up of 60 months, MACE occurred in 287 patients. After full adjustment, AIP as a continuous variable was independently associated with greater coronary lesion severity (OR = 1.761; 95% CI: 1.052-2.948; p = 0.031). Regarding prognosis, when AIP was dichotomized at 0.4, it was independently associated with MACE (HR = 1.350; 95% CI: 1.060-1.721; p = 0.015) in the fully adjusted model, whereas continuous AIP did not retain significance. Restricted cubic spline analysis suggested a possible U-shaped dose-response relationship between AIP and MACE (overall p < 0.001, nonlinear p = 0.051). Subgroup analyses showed that the association of AIP with MACE was generally consistent across all examined strata, with no significant interactions (all p for interaction >0.05). Conclusions: AIP was independently associated with greater coronary lesion severity and MACE in young CAD patients (≤35 years). These findings support AIP as a practical tool not only for early risk stratification but also for guiding intensive lipid-lowering therapy in this distinct population.

title: Heart Transplantation: A Review of Recent Advancements in Pre-, Peri, and Post-Transplant Screening and Management.
authorString: Ringor M, Nguyen D, Boumelhem F, Joseph Y, Sharma D, Dugal J.
abstractText: Heart transplantation (HT) remains a critical treatment for patients with end-stage heart failure who remain unresponsive to optimized guideline-directed medical therapy. This review examines recent advancements in pre-, peri-, and post-transplant screening and management aimed at improving patient selection, transplant accessibility, and clinical outcomes. Pre-transplant strategies include comprehensive HT candidate evaluation, risk stratification, donor selection, allocation policies that priotize critically ill patients, and mechanical circulatory support (MCS) to stabilize patients awaiting transplantation. Peri-transplant advances focus on strategies to maintain hemodynamic stability, minimize ischemic injury, and maintain graft viability immediately after HT. Post-transplant management emphasizes individualized immunosuppressive regimens, cardiac allograft rejection surveillance, and the prevention and management of complications to improve graft survival and long-term patient outcomes. Despite substantial progress, significant challenges remain, particularly the shortage of suitable donor organs and the risk of immune-mediated graft rejection. Emerging approaches, including artificial intelligence, xenotransplantation, and regenerative medicine, offer promising opportunities to expand the donor pool, enhance clinical decision-making, and improve HT outcomes. This review examines the research that influences the current policies and practices involved in HT, featuring the pivotal findings as well as any shortcomings present among these studies. Ultimately, continued research and multidisciplinary collaboration in each phase of HT are essential to improve the short and long-term health outcomes of transplant candidates. By integrating established evidence-based practices with emerging technologies, clinicians may further improve equitable access, survival, and quality-of-life for patients with end-stage heart failure.

title: Bridging Infant Mental Health Screening and Intervention from NICU to Home: A Single-Center Quality Improvement Project.
authorString: Carson MC, Matic T, Burke RV, Mirzaian CB, Yuen J, Vanderbilt D, Williams ME.
abstractText: Having an infant admitted to a NICU increases parental anxiety, depression and traumatic stress, heightens infants' developmental and mental health risk, and may disrupt infant-parent relationships. Early Connections is a dyadic, trauma-informed universal infant mental health program implemented at Children's Hospital Los Angeles. Child-Parent Psychotherapy-informed dyadic psychological intervention is offered during admission in the NICU. The Parent Navigator model utilizes a parent with lived NICU experience to support linkage to early intervention as families transition home. Finally, a psychologist provides infant mental health screening and tiered intervention in the interdisciplinary outpatient Newborn Follow-up Program (NFP), a high-risk infant follow-up clinic. This manuscript describes preliminary findings from a single-center quality improvement project to explore implementation of the program from December 2025 through March 2026.
