Of the 63 (55.3%) families who met with the NICU psychologist, 88.9% had at least one infant mental health family session and 65.1% had more than one infant mental health session during their child's admission. Of the 66 (57.9%) supported by the parent navigator, 90.9% completed applications for early intervention for their infant; future follow-up will determine the outcome of the application for services. Based on outpatient infant mental health screening conducted with 85 patients (50.5% of those who had appointments), 23.6% of infants and 40.0% of toddlers screened in the NFP were at risk for social-emotional concerns, suggesting there may be a continued need for ongoing screening and intervention following discharge from intensive care. As the needs of families and infants change across inpatient and outpatient medical settings, it is important to offer multiple opportunities to screen needs flexibly and provide tiered intervention.

title: Association of Complete Blood Count Parameters and Systemic Inflammatory Indices with Early Surfactant Administration in Preterm Infants.
authorString: Uygun SS, Comez N, Duysak OS, Kilicli E, Konak M, Soylu H.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: The decision to administer surfactant therapy to preterm newborns is typically based on clinical respiratory findings, oxygen requirements, and the level of respiratory support. The aim of this study was to assess the association of admission complete blood count parameters and derived systemic inflammatory indices with surfactant administration within the first 24 h of life in preterm infants born at ≤32 weeks of gestation, and to evaluate their discriminative performance. Methods: This single-center, retrospective observational cohort study included 100 preterm infants with a gestational age of ≤32 weeks who were admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit between 1 January 2025 and 31 March 2026. The results of the initial complete blood count and blood gas analysis, obtained as part of routine clinical care at admission, were recorded. Systemic inflammatory indices, including the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), red cell distribution width-to-platelet ratio (RPR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and mean platelet volume-to-platelet ratio (MPV/PLT), were calculated from the complete blood count results. The primary outcome was surfactant administration within the first 24 h of life. Associated factors were evaluated using logistic regression analysis, and the discriminative performance of continuous variables was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Results: Surfactant was administered to 45 infants (45%) within the first 24 h of life. Infants who received surfactant had lower gestational ages, birth weights, 1- and 5 min Apgar scores, partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PCO2), hemoglobin levels, and hematocrit values. No significant differences were observed between groups in NLR, PLR, MLR, RPR, SII, or MPV/PLT. In multivariable analysis, lower gestational age (OR = 0.65; 95% CI: 0.50-0.84; p = 0.001), small-for-gestational-age (SGA) status (OR = 4.61; 95% CI: 1.25-16.91; p = 0.021), and lower 1 min Apgar score (OR = 0.67; 95% CI: 0.46-0.96; p = 0.031) were independently associated with early surfactant administration. Hemoglobin was not independently associated with early surfactant administration after adjustment. In the ROC analysis, the AUC values were 0.804 for birth weight, 0.776 for gestational age, 0.694 for hemoglobin, 0.677 for hematocrit, and 0.640 for PCO2. Conclusions: Lower gestational age, SGA status, and lower 1 min Apgar score were independently associated with early surfactant administration. No significant associations were observed between the evaluated complete blood count-derived inflammatory indices and early surfactant administration. Although hemoglobin and hematocrit levels differed between groups, hemoglobin was not independently associated with the outcome after adjustment. ROC analysis provided descriptive estimates of the discriminative performance of gestational age, birth weight, hemoglobin, hematocrit, and PCO2.

title: The Cover of (<i>The Rolling Stone</i>) CASE.
authorString: Sorrell VL.

title: Disruption of Placental Immune Privilege by Complications of Pregnancy: Consequences for Maternal and Child Health.
authorString: Mixtega-Ruiz WK, Contreras Escamilla M, Sevilla-Montoya R, Olmos-Ortiz A, Zaga-Clavellina V, Castro-Rodríguez DC.
abstractText: Maternal chronic conditions, including obesity, diabetes, hypertensive disorders, and autoimmune diseases, promote a systemic proinflammatory environment characterized by oxidative stress and chronic inflammation. These alterations lead to reduced expressions of human leukocyte antigen-G (HLA-G) and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1), decreased regulatory T (Treg)cell activity, and increased T helper (Th)1/Th17 responses, disrupting placental immune privilege and resulting in increased production of proinflammatory cytokines, oxidative stress, trophoblastic dysfunction, and placental senescence. This change in immune privilege contributes to fetal growth restriction, preterm birth, congenital anomalies, and long-term cardiometabolic programming in offspring. Understanding the mechanisms underlying placental immune dysregulation may facilitate the development of targeted therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring immune tolerance and reducing inflammatory and hypoxic signaling pathways to improve maternal and neonatal outcomes. This review summarizes the current state of the field of placental immunological privilege and how maternal chronic conditions like obesity, diabetes, hypertensive disorders, and autoimmune diseases can disrupt it and its possible consequences on the progeny.

title: Left Ventricular Global Longitudinal Strain and Ventricular Repolarization in People with HIV: A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study.
authorString: Özdemir Tutar E, Özbebek YE, Turinay Ertop ZS, Solak Grassie S.
abstractText: Background and Objectives: Subclinical myocardial deformation and ventricular repolarization abnormalities may occur in people with HIV (PWH) despite preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). We evaluated left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LV GLS) and Tpeak-to-end (Tp-e)-based repolarization indices in PWH and examined their within-person relationship. Materials and Methods: This prospective comparative cross-sectional study included 25 PWH and 47 HIV-negative reference participants consecutively recruited from outpatient clinics. All participants were in sinus rhythm and had LVEF ≥50%. Conventional and speckle-tracking echocardiography and 12-lead electrocardiography were performed. Multivariable linear regression assessed associations of HIV status with LV GLS, Tp-e interval, and Tp-e/QTc ratio after adjustment for age, sex, current smoking, and hyperlipidemia. Within-PWH associations were assessed using Spearman correlation with multiplicity adjustment. Results: PWH had less negative LV GLS than reference participants (-17.1% vs. -19.0%; p < 0.001), longer Tp-e intervals (74 vs. 72 ms; p = 0.001), and higher Tp-e/QTc ratios (0.185 vs. 0.173; p < 0.001). HIV status remained associated with LV GLS (B = 2.472 percentage points, 95% CI 1.672-3.272), Tp-e (B = 4.347 ms, 95% CI 2.286-6.408), and Tp-e/QTc (B = 0.013, 95% CI 0.009-0.017; all p < 0.001). Within PWH, LV GLS was not significantly correlated with Tp-e or Tp-e/QTc. Conclusions: PWH with preserved LVEF showed less negative LV GLS and less favorable Tp-e-based repolarization indices than HIV-negative reference participants. These cross-sectional findings do not establish causal, prognostic, or screening implications, and the non-significant within-PWH correlations do not exclude potentially relevant associations. Larger longitudinal studies are warranted.

title: Association Between Local Ascending Aortic Elastic Properties and Left Ventricular Global Longitudinal Strain in Patients with Multiple Sclerosis: A Cross-Sectional Case-Control Echocardiographic Study.
authorString: Özdemir Tutar E, Öztürk P.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Multiple sclerosis (MS) has been associated with subclinical cardiovascular involvement, including impaired myocardial deformation and increased arterial stiffness. However, the local elastic properties of the ascending aorta and their relationship with subclinical left ventricular (LV) longitudinal dysfunction remain insufficiently characterized in MS. Methods: In this prospective cross-sectional study, 67 adults with MS and 67 age-matched controls without cardiovascular disease underwent standardized transthoracic echocardiography. Aortic strain, distensibility and stiffness index (β) were derived from M-mode ascending aortic diameters and simultaneous brachial blood pressure, and LV global longitudinal strain (GLS) was measured by two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography. Multivariable linear regression was utilized to assess associations. Results: LV ejection fraction was similar between groups, while LV GLS was less negative in MS (-17.49 ± 1.81% vs. -19.85 ± 1.80%, p < 0.001). Patients with MS had lower aortic strain (7.54 ± 3.66% vs. 12.91 ± 3.84%) and distensibility (3.81 [2.23-6.06] vs. 5.95 [4.90-9.26] × 10-3 mmHg-1) and a higher stiffness index (4.77 [3.10-7.10] vs. 3.44 [2.31-4.05]) (all p < 0.001). After adjustment for age, sex, and body mass index, MS remained independently associated with aortic strain, distensibility, and stiffness index. Within the MS group, aortic strain was independently associated with LV GLS after adjustment for age, sex, body mass index, Expanded Disability Status Scale score and LDL cholesterol (B = -0.276, standardized β = -0.558, p < 0.001). LV GLS was independently associated with log-transformed distensibility (B = -1.021, p = 0.011) and stiffness index (B = 1.095, p = 0.014). Conclusions: Patients with MS show concurrent, inter-related impairment of local ascending aortic elasticity and LV longitudinal deformation despite preserved ejection fraction. Further studies are needed to establish the temporal sequence and prognostic relevance of these findings.

title: Interatrial Shunt Devices in Heart Failure: A Therapy in Search of the Right Patient.
authorString: Karagianni A, Evangeliou A, Pavlou DO, Schismenos V, Pagourelias E, Giannopoulos G, Papadopoulos C, Karamitsos T, Vassilikos V, Tzikas S.

journal.title: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease

abstractText: Heart failure with preserved or mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFpEF/HFmrEF) accounts for approximately half of the global heart failure burden and remains a syndrome with limited device-based therapeutic options. It is often characterized by a disproportionate rise in left-sided filling pressure during exercise. Interatrial shunt devices (IASDs) aim to reduce left atrial pressure through controlled left-to-right atrial communication. We performed a structured narrative review of mechanistic studies, early feasibility cohorts, randomized trials, meta-analyses, and ongoing studies indexed through to August 2026. Early proof-of-concept studies consistently demonstrated technical feasibility, durable patency, and favorable hemodynamic effects, particularly through reductions in pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP), often accompanied by improved functional status. However, larger sham-controlled randomized trials failed to show consistent overall benefit in unselected populations. Recent mechanistic and observational data indicate that pulmonary vascular reserve, right ventricular-pulmonary arterial coupling, rhythm-device status, and device design may affect benefits and harms. Latent pulmonary vascular disease and impaired right-heart reserve may identify patients poorly suited for shunt implantation, whereas carefully selected, promising phenotypes remain under prospective study. IASDs should therefore remain investigational. Future trials should use exercise hemodynamics and validated noninvasive markers to prospectively define responders, assess device-specific effects, and reconcile physiological unloading with clinical outcomes.

title: Infective endocarditis in children: a 23-year experience at a Southern African tertiary institution.
authorString: Ooka M, Cilliers A.
abstractText:
Background

There is a paucity of data regarding infective endocarditis (IE) in children, particularly in low-to-middle-income settings, with minimal recent data from Sub-Saharan Africa.

Objectives

To determine the demographic and clinical profiles of paediatric patients with IE at the Chris Hani Baragwanath Academic Hospital (CHBAH), Johannesburg, South Africa.

Methods

A retrospective descriptive study of all paediatric patients diagnosed with IE between 1993 and 2015. Demographic data, the presence of congenital or acquired structural heart disease and other risk factors, blood culture results and complications were recorded and analysed using basic statistical methods.

Results

183 patients were included (median age 31.2 months). Ninety-seven patients (53%) had underlying congenital heart disease (CHD), 26 had rheumatic heart disease (14.2%), and 45 (24%) were identified with structurally normal hearts. Underlying sepsis (37.8%), central venous catheters (CVC) (31.2%), prematurity (15.6%) and human immunodeficiency virus (13.3%) were found to be risk factors in the group with normal hearts. Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus viridans were the most common pathogens. Complications were documented in 103 (56.3%) patients. These included cardiac failure (CF), worsening valve lesions, vascular complications (embolisation and mycotic aneurysm formation), other manifestations of sepsis, surgery required to treat complications and death. The overall mortality rate was 23.5%. CF and vascular complications were associated with a high risk of mortality.

Conclusion

CHD is the most common association with IE, followed by structurally normal hearts in premature infants and patients with CVC. The complication rate of 56% and 24% mortality rate highlight the devastating outcomes of IE.

title: Invasive Complications and Infection-Related Reconstruction in Bicuspid Versus Tricuspid Native Aortic Valve Endocarditis: A 12-Year Surgical Cohort Study.
authorString: Zhai Y, Zhang L, Ren S, Liu X, Dong Y, Ma G, Xu S, Zheng J.

journal.title: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease

abstractText:
Background

Detailed operative evidence comparing invasive anatomy and reconstruction between bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) and tricuspid aortic valve (TAV) cases of native-valve infective endocarditis is limited. We examined the association of BAV morphology with non-leaflet invasive complications and infection-related reconstruction.

Methods

We retrospectively studied 317 adults who underwent surgery for native aortic valve infective endocarditis from 2013 through 2025 (113 BAV; 204 TAV). The primary outcome was any non-leaflet invasive complication; infection-related reconstruction was a secondary operative outcome reflecting operative management of invasive anatomy. Modified Poisson regression estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs), corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and marginally standardized absolute differences. Site-specific and invasive-subgroup analyses were exploratory.

Results

Patients with BAV were younger, more frequently male, and had a lower comorbidity burden. Non-leaflet invasive complications occurred in 44.2% of patients with BAV and 18.6% with TAV (aPR, 2.08; 95% CI, 1.41-3.06; adjusted absolute difference, 21.1 percentage points; 95% CI, 9.6-32.6). Abscess involving non-leaflet structures was more frequent in BAV than in TAV (43.4% vs. 16.7%; p < 0.001). In the full cohort, aortic annular and left ventricular outflow tract involvement were more frequent in BAV. Infection-related reconstruction was performed in 31.9% of patients with BAV and 15.2% of those with TAV. Within the invasive subgroup, reconstruction was performed in 72.0% and 81.6% of BAV and TAV cases, respectively (unadjusted PR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.70-1.11). Early mortality was low in both groups, and the adjusted analysis did not identify a clear difference in long-term mortality.

Conclusions

Bicuspid morphology was associated with a higher prevalence of non-leaflet invasive complications, predominantly abscess, and a higher overall frequency of infection-related reconstruction.

title: Mesenchymal Stromal Cells for Heart Diseases: Current Perspective and Future Directions.
authorString: Zajączkowski MA, Deptuła-Knioła M, Zawrzykraj-Motylińska M, Kaczyńska-Miotk A, Pikuła M, Kosiński A.
abstractText: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of mortality worldwide and continue to impose a substantial clinical burden despite major advances in pharmacological and interventional therapies. Because the adult myocardium has limited regenerative capacity, irreversible cardiomyocyte loss frequently leads to adverse remodeling and progressive heart failure (HF). Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) are among the most extensively studied cell therapies for cardiac repair because of their immunomodulatory, pro-angiogenic, anti-inflammatory, and anti-fibrotic effects, mediated predominantly through paracrine signaling. This review summarizes the current evidence for MSC-based therapy in ischemic heart disease (IHD), coronary and microvascular disorders, myocardial infarction, HF, myocarditis, pulmonary arterial hypertension, and valvular heart disease (VHD). We discuss MSC sources, preclinical and clinical evidence, manufacturing and dosing, delivery routes, biomaterial-assisted transplantation, preconditioning, genetic modification, and imaging for cell tracking and treatment monitoring. Although MSC therapy has shown a favorable safety profile and regenerative potential, clinical efficacy remains variable because of limited cell survival, poor myocardial retention, and heterogeneous treatment protocols. Further optimization of manufacturing, delivery, and patient selection, together with well-designed randomized trials, is required to establish standardized protocols and support clinical translation.

title: High-Flow Nasal Oxygenation Is Associated with Improved Respiratory Stability During Moderate Multimodal Analgosedation for Pars Plana Vitrectomy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
authorString: Vuković A, Jukić T, Štanfel M, Mandić K, Mihaljević S, Bartolek-Hamp D.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: High-flow nasal oxygenation (HFNO) may improve respiratory stability during procedural sedation, but treatment-associated differences across patient risk categories remain uncertain. We compared HFNO with low-flow nasal oxygenation (LFNO) during moderate multimodal analgosedation (MMAS) for pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) in patients with ASA physical status I-III. Methods: In this prospective, single-center randomized trial, 164 adults undergoing elective PPV under regional eye anesthesia with MMAS were randomized to HFNO (40 L·min-1, set FiO2 0.40) or LFNO (5 L·min-1, intended to approximate a nominal FiO2 of 0.40). Sedation depth was monitored using the Patient State Index and evaluated using the Ramsay Sedation Scale. The primary outcome was maintenance of target oxygenation (SpO2 94-98%) without hypoxemia (SpO2 < 90%), assessed by peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2) at three predefined time points (T0, T1, and T2). Secondary outcomes included breathing frequency (BF), measured end-tidal CO2 (EtCO2), and clinically significant bradypnea (CSB), defined as ≥1 bradypnea episode (BF < 12 breaths·min-1 persisting ≥1 min) accompanied by SpO2 90-93%, EtCO2 > 45 mmHg, or both. Results: The primary outcome showed no between-group difference. No hypoxemia (SpO2 < 90%) occurred. Oxygenation below the target range (SpO2 90-93%) was less frequent with HFNO peri-procedurally (adjusted RR, 0.14; 95% CI, 0.03-0.56; p = 0.006) and post-procedurally (adjusted RR, 0.15; 95% CI, 0.04-0.64; p = 0.010). Significant treatment × ASA interactions were observed for BF and measured EtCO2 peri-procedurally. In exploratory ASA-stratified analyses, ASA III patients receiving HFNO had higher BF, fewer CSB episodes, and lower measured EtCO2 than those receiving LFNO. Conclusions: HFNO was associated with improved respiratory stability compared with LFNO, with treatment-associated differences varying across ASA strata.

title: Advances in Aerobic Exercise for Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: Mechanisms of Action and Clinical Insights.
authorString: Wang T, Tan Y, Deng L, Li J.
abstractText: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive disease characterized by elevated pulmonary artery pressure and pulmonary vascular resistance, leading to right heart failure and death in severe cases. PAH is classified as Group 1 pulmonary hypertension (PH). Although Groups 2 and 3 PH are more common, this review focuses primarily on PAH. Currently, there are three main classes of targeted drugs in clinical practice, and their main mechanism is to dilate pulmonary artery vessels. These drugs can delay the progression of PAH and improve the quality of life. However, the long-term prognosis is still not optimistic. At present, patients with PAH still need a multi-drug combination and comprehensive treatment. Aerobic exercise, as a non-pharmacological adjunctive therapy, is believed to have a positive impact on PAH treatment when performed regularly in patients with stable conditions. With the widespread application of aerobic exercise in the treatment of cardiovascular diseases, increasing research is exploring its potential in adjunctive therapy for PAH. Studies suggest that exercise-based rehabilitation incorporating aerobic exercise, when added to optimized PAH-targeted therapy, may improve exercise capacity, quality of life, and selected cardiopulmonary or hemodynamic parameters in clinically stable patients with PAH. However, evidence for reversal of pulmonary vascular remodeling or mortality benefit remains limited. This review summarizes the clinical evidence and mechanisms of aerobic exercise specifically in PAH.

title: Clinical Characteristics and Prognostic Analysis of Hospitalized Infants with <i>Chlamydia trachomatis</i> Pneumonia.
authorString: Wei M, Gao L, Xu B, Yin J, Qin Q, Jiao A, Gao Q, Wu X, Guo S.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Chlamydia trachomatis (C. trachomatis) is an important cause of community-acquired pneumonia in early infancy; however, its subtle and nonspecific clinical features often result in underdiagnosis and delayed treatment. Evidence regarding clinical predictors of severe disease and distinctive imaging manifestations remains limited. This study aimed to characterize the clinical and imaging features of hospitalized infantile C. trachomatis pneumonia and to identify potential indicators associated with disease severity. Methods: This retrospective study enrolled infants with confirmed C. trachomatis pneumonia hospitalized at Beijing Children's Hospital from January 2016 to December 2025. Data on demographics, clinical presentations, laboratory findings, chest imaging, treatments, and outcomes were systematically collected. Exploratory subgroup analyses were performed to compare severe and non-severe cases and identify severity-associated factors. Results: A total of 30 infants (16 boys, 14 girls) were included, with a median age of 34.0 days (IQR, 23.5-39.8 days) at symptom onset. Cough was nearly universal (96.7%), while fever, tachypnea, and wheezing were observed in 43.3%, 43.3%, and 40.0%, respectively. Pulmonary crackles were present in 86.7%, and eosinophilia in 40.0%. Cytomegalovirus co-infection occurred in 36.7%. Chest CT revealed patchy opacities (100%), interstitial changes (86.7%), mass-like/nodular opacities (63.3%), and diffuse miliary/granular opacities (13.3%). Among 14 patients undergoing bronchoscopy, 50.0% had thick airway secretions. Tachypnea and retractions emerged as important clinical indicators of severe disease. All patients recovered with macrolide therapy, and no deaths occurred. Conclusions: Infantile C. trachomatis pneumonia typically presents with absent or low-to-moderate fever, paroxysmal cough, and occasional wheezing. Tachypnea and retractions may serve as early indicators of severe disease. Atypical chest imaging patterns, including mass-like and miliary opacities, provide valuable diagnostic clues. Once the diagnosis is established, prompt initiation of macrolide therapy is recommended, and the overall prognosis is favorable.

title: Coronary artery compression in percutaneous pulmonary valve implantation: a case series.
authorString: Buntharikpornpun R, Roymanee S, Promphan W, Duong P.
abstractText: Catastrophic complications of coronary artery compression after percutaneous pulmonary valve implantation (PPVI) are uncommon in patients with a dysfunctional native right ventricular outflow tract after Tetralogy of Fallot repair (rTOF). Nonetheless, we report three rTOFs with a high risk of compromising coronary blood flow for PPVI. This risk has been elucidated by multimodal assessments, including robust pre-procedural cardiac computed tomography and meticulous balloon interrogation with selective coronary angiography.

title: Echocardiographic Assessment of Left and Right Ventricular Systolic Function Beyond Ejection Fraction.
authorString: Hadjigeorgiou N, Stosic T, Melanarkiti D, Ioannou M, Patrianakos A, Mouzarou A.
abstractText: The assessment of left and right ventricular systolic function is vital information for the management of cardiac disease. Everyday clinical practice has traditionally relied on the measurement of the ejection fraction (EF). Nonetheless, EF has known limitations and may not always accurately reflect myocardial systolic performance. Intrinsic myocardial contractility may decline long before reductions in left or right ventricular EF become apparent. Adjunct parameters such as tissue Doppler-derived systolic velocities of the mitral and tricuspid annulus may detect such early abnormalities; however, they do not represent global systolic performance. Consequently, commonly used indices may exhibit suboptimal performance for the detection of systolic dysfunction. Given the limitations of current measurement methods, there is growing concern about the reliability of heart failure (HF) classification based solely on EF. The integration of advanced echocardiographic indices, such as speckle-tracking-derived strain, three-dimensional (3D) volumetric assessment, myocardial work (MW), and cardiac power output (CPO), in combination with classical parameters provides more accurate, reproducible, and clinically meaningful diagnostic and prognostic information in patients with HF. Nevertheless, despite their potential, these techniques remain underutilized in routine practice. Early identification of systolic dysfunction and timely initiation of therapy can substantially improve clinical outcomes. In this setting, this review aims to comprehensively examine both established and emerging echocardiographic techniques used for the assessment of ventricular systolic performance, with the objective of promoting their effective integration into routine clinical practice.

title: Machine Learning to Distinguish Physiologic Causes of Hypoxemia After Bidirectional Glenn Using Bedside Markers.
authorString: Savorgnan F, Pilla P, Visokay S, Ness K, Fiedorek T, Flores S.
abstractText:
Background

Hypoxemia after bidirectional Glenn palliation can result from distinct physiological mechanisms that may produce similar arterial oxygen saturation. We evaluated whether routinely available bedside markers could recover physiological states encoded in a mechanistic virtual-patient model.

Methods

A steady-state zero-dimensional closed-loop model generated five causes of Glenn hypoxemia: elevated pulmonary vascular resistance, veno-venous collateral shunting, pulmonary gas-exchange impairment, increased metabolic demand, and ventricular dysfunction. Hidden physiological variables were withheld from the classifier; inputs were SpO2, heart rate, mean arterial pressure, hemoglobin, Glenn/SVC pressure, and SVC oxygen saturation. Because bedside patterns arise downstream from prespecified equations and phenotype perturbations, classification was interpreted as internal mechanistic recoverability rather than clinical diagnostic performance.

Results

Of 150,000 generated states, 127,162 passed broad physiological criteria and 66,269 met strict hypoxemia/hemodynamic criteria. After balancing, 26,400 virtual patients were analyzed (5280 per mechanism; 19,800 training and 6600 held-out testing). SpO2 alone achieved 26.1% accuracy (macro-AUROC 0.580); the primary bedside model achieved 56.1% accuracy (95% CI 55.0-57.4%) and macro-AUROC 0.845 (95% CI 0.840-0.851). Elevated PVR was the most readily recovered phenotype. Glenn/SVC pressure and SVC saturation provided the largest incremental contributions, while broader measurement-error assumptions substantially reduced performance.

Conclusions

Within this mechanistic simulation, multivariable bedside patterns allowed partial recovery of physiological states encoded by the model. Because phenotypes and their observable consequences were generated from prespecified assumptions, the reported performance quantifies internal recoverability under those assumptions and should not be interpreted as diagnostic accuracy or as independent evidence of bedside information content in patients. The model identifies testable physiologic signatures and areas of overlap for prospective clinical validation.

title: Clinical and Molecular Spectrum of 1q21.1 Copy Number Variations: A Case Series.
authorString: Esen TE, Celik LY, Aydin Gumus A, Ercoskun P, Bozlak S, Gezdirici A, Yavas C, Yilmaz I.
abstractText:
Background

1q21.1 copy number variations (CNVs) are recurrent rearrangements with a clinical spectrum, from neurodevelopmental disorders and congenital anomalies to apparently unaffected carrier status, reflecting incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity.

Methods

Our chromosomal microarray (CytoScan HD) database was retrospectively screened for pathogenic or likely pathogenic 1q21.1 CNVs.

Results

Twenty probands from 19 families (14 postnatal, 6 prenatal) carried 21 CNV events: 11 deletions (52.4%) and 10 duplications (47.6%). Of these, 16 (76.2%) were confined to the distal segment, 3 (14.3%) to the proximal segment, and 2 (9.5%) spanned both. One proband carried coexisting proximal duplication and distal deletion, both inherited from an apparently unaffected father. Of the 17 probands (85%) with parental testing, 7 (41.2%) had de novo and 10 (58.8%) inherited CNVs. Distal CNVs were mostly observed in probands with neurodevelopmental or cardiac phenotypes, whereas bilateral upper extremity anomalies were observed in both prenatally ascertained fetuses with isolated proximal deletions. Corpus callosum atrophy and choanal atresia were infrequently reported co-occurring findings, whereas prenatal intracranial hemorrhage was potentially novel; each occurred in one proband. Given the small proximal subgroup and differing ascertainment, these segment-associated trends are descriptive.

Conclusions

This series highlights the relevance of segment localization and parental segregation data in interpreting 1q21.1 CNVs.

title: Frontiers in the Risk Stratification and Prevention of Sudden Cardiac Arrest and Death in Athletes.
authorString: Cushing J, Hamar L, Fritzlen J.
abstractText: Background: Sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) and sudden cardiac death (SCD) remain the leading causes of exercise-related mortality in athletes. Research in recent years has produced substantial advances in the understanding of athlete-specific risk, the etiologic spectrum of SCA/SCD, and the tools available for screening and risk stratification. Methods: We performed a narrative review of the literature identified through PubMed/MEDLINE searches of related terms, supplemented by targeted searches and reference checking. Summary of the Review: In this narrative review, we synthesize updated evidence on the epidemiology, etiologies, screening, and emerging technologies relevant to SCA/SCD in athletes. Conclusions: Contemporary evaluation of SCA/SCD risk in athletes relies on multimodal, individualized assessment with longitudinal surveillance and shared decision-making. Emerging computational tools may further refine risk prediction, but current evidence remains limited.

title: Liveborn trisomy 22: a case report.
authorString: Jares Baglivo S, Morand MP, Velagaleti GVN, Jain SK, Cooney E.
abstractText:
Introduction

: Trisomy 22 is identified in 2%-5% of spontaneous abortions across various populations, making it the second most common trisomy in spontaneous abortions. Liveborn patients with complete trisomy 22 are rare and present with variable clinical findings.

Methods

A detailed clinical report of a term female neonate with complete trisomy 22 was compiled after obtaining informed consent from her mother.

Results

The neonate was born via spontaneous vaginal delivery, and resuscitation included intubation after multiple attempts. She presented with multiple congenital anomalies, including a single umbilical artery, microcephaly, dysmorphic facial features, absent red reflex, corneal haze, irregular pupil, microcornea, imperforated anus with rectovestibular fistula, bilateral clinodactyly of the fifth digits, and bilateral distal and proximal transverse palmar creases running parallel to each other. An echocardiogram showed Tetralogy of Fallot and hypoplasia of the transverse aortic arch. Abdominal ultrasound revealed small kidneys. The electroencephalogram showed diffuse cerebral dysfunction. Head ultrasound indicated absence of the septum pellucidum. Additional complications included pneumothorax, metabolic disturbances, sepsis, and persistent thrombocytopenia. The neonate's condition deteriorated, leading to demise on the seventh day of life. Chromosome analysis confirmed 47,XX,+22.

Discussion

: This case report contributes to the limited literature on complete trisomy 22, highlighting its prognosis, clinical heterogeneity, and management challenges. The constellation of anomalies observed underscores the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration and adaptability in providing optimal care. By better understanding its clinical presentation, we hope to facilitate early recognition, appropriate management, and counseling.

title: A novel <i>LARP7</i> variant expands the phenotypic spectrum of Alazami syndrome and reveals transcriptomic dysregulation of developmental and extracellular matrix pathways.
authorString: Hassan M, Irshaid M, Batool A, Aldhaheri W, Qehaizel LB, Alzaabi S, Alnuaimi S, Saeed S, Al Jasmi F, Akawi N.

journal.title: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

abstractText:
Background

LARP7 encodes a critical scaffold protein of the 7SK small nuclear ribonucleoprotein (7SK snRNP) complex that regulates RNA polymerase II transcriptional elongation. Biallelic loss-of-function variants in LARP7 cause Alazami syndrome, a rare neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by intellectual disability, growth restriction, and distinctive craniofacial features. However, the transcriptomic consequences of LARP7 deficiency in human cells remain poorly understood, and the phenotypic spectrum of the disorder is incompletely defined.

Methods

We investigated a 6-year-old boy with clinically diagnosed Alazami syndrome who carried a novel homozygous LARP7 frameshift variant. Clinical evaluation and exome sequencing of blood-derived genomic DNA were performed, while quantitative PCR, Western blotting, and transcriptomic analysis were conducted using patient-derived dermal fibroblasts. Transcriptomic consequences of LARP7 deficiency were assessed by RNA sequencing, followed by single-subject differential expression, pathway enrichment, and network analyses.

Results

The patient presented with classical features of Alazami syndrome and tetralogy of Fallot, a cardiac manifestation not previously reported in the disorder. The novel homozygous LARP7 frameshift variant resulted in marked depletion of LARP7 transcripts and complete loss of full-length protein. Transcriptome-wide analysis identified 1,224 dysregulated genes involved in extracellular matrix organization, developmental remodeling, cell-cycle regulation, and immune signaling. Pathway and network analyses highlighted dysregulation of STAT3-associated signaling together with SMAD3-linked extracellular matrix and developmental programs, identifying candidate developmental and tissue-remodeling pathways that warrant further investigation in disease-relevant models.

Conclusion

This study provides the first comprehensive transcriptomic characterization of genetically confirmed LARP7 deficiency in primary human cells and potentially expands the phenotypic spectrum of Alazami syndrome. The findings reveal widespread dysregulation of developmental and extracellular matrix pathways, offering new insight into the molecular basis of the multisystem manifestations of Alazami syndrome and providing a framework for future functional and genotype-phenotype studies.

title: Donor-aware multi-cohort single-cell analysis identifies an LXR-linked tubular cholesterol-handling state in membranous nephropathy with a coordinated five-gene lipid-remodeling signature across renal tumors.
authorString: Mao Y, Li R, Li B, Pan H.
abstractText:
Background

Membranous nephropathy (MN) is an immune-mediated glomerular disease in which sustained proteinuria exposes renal tubular epithelial cells to an abnormal filtered-protein load. The tubular metabolic response to this exposure remains incompletely characterized. We investigated whether MN is associated with a reproducible tubular cholesterol-handling transcriptional state and assessed its relationship to protein overload in vitro. We further evaluated whether an experimentally anchored five-gene subset showed a coordinated tumor-associated transcriptional shift across major renal cancer histologies.

Methods

Three kidney single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets and one glomerular bulk-transcriptomic cohort were analyzed using the donor as the biological replicate. GSE241302 was used for complete-case exploratory discovery, OEP004186 for formal donor-aware support, GSE171458 for directional support, and GSE200828 for tissue-level disease context. A frozen 47-gene LXR-linked cholesterol-handling program and its nested 37-gene cholesterol transport/efflux component were evaluated by donor-level pseudobulk analysis, leave-one-donor-out and leave-one-gene-out sensitivity analyses. HK-2 cells were exposed to protein overload, followed by quantitative reverse-transcription PCR for representative transport and lipid-remodeling genes. The same experimentally anchored five-gene panel was then evaluated in 129 paired tumor-adjacent-normal samples across TCGA-KIRC, TCGA-KIRP, and TCGA-KICH to define a renal tumor-associated lipid-remodeling context.

Results

Across all 3 MN donors in GSE241302, program scores were higher than the internal reference in proximal tubule (PT) and loop-of-Henle/thick ascending limb (loop/TAL) compartments. In OEP004186, the program was increased in PT (effect +0.480, false-discovery rate [FDR] 0.0128), PT-VCAM1 (+0.348, FDR 0.0165), and loop/distal epithelial cells (+0.310, FDR 0.0242), with positive effects in every leave-one-MN-donor-out analysis. GSE171458 provided concordant directional support in PT and loop/TAL. The PT-VCAM1 fraction was not increased in MN, whereas the program remained higher within both PT and PT-VCAM1, favoring a within-state transcriptional change. Sixteen program genes showed positive average effects across the three single-cell resources. In GSE200828, the overall program was higher in MN than in living donors (+0.226, FDR 0.0349) but not higher than in other glomerular diseases. Protein overload increased ABCA1, ABCG1, SREBF1, FASN, and SCD expression in HK-2 cells. Across the three renal cancer histologies, the five-gene panel showed a concordant paired increase (REML-pooled effect +0.967, 95% CI 0.843-1.092), and 85.3% of patients exhibited simultaneous increases in the cholesterol-efflux and lipid-synthesis/remodeling arms.

Conclusion

MN is associated with a donor-supported LXR-linked cholesterol-handling transcriptional state concentrated in PT and loop/TAL-related epithelial compartments. The state is responsive to protein overload in HK-2 cells and may reflect a broader tubular lipid-homeostasis response to proteinuric kidney injury. The data do not establish direct LXR activation, increased cholesterol-efflux flux, or MN specificity. The paired renal cancer analysis further identifies a coordinated tumor-associated five-gene lipid-remodeling signature across KIRC, KIRP, and KICH, while not establishing tumor-cell-intrinsic LXR activation, immune effects, or a causal tumor mechanism.

title: Machine learning, molecular docking, and experimental validation identify shared molecular signatures between idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension and malignant pleural mesothelioma: a retrospective study.
authorString: Zhang N, Wang C, Wang R, Guo X, Yu J, Wang J, Luo Q, Wu Y.
abstractText:
Background

Idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH) exhibits cancer-like features, yet its pathogenesis remains unclear. Given molecular similarities between IPAH and malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM), this study aimed to uncover shared transcriptomic patterns.

Methods

GEO datasets for IPAH and MPM were analyzed. Overlapping DEGs and WGCNA modules were identified. PPI network analysis combined with LASSO, random forest, and SVM-RFE was used to identify candidate biomarker genes. A classification model was constructed and evaluated using leave-one-out cross-validation and bootstrap optimism correction. Immune infiltration was evaluated by ssGSEA. Molecular docking and MD simulations assessed drug binding to candidate target proteins. qRT-PCR validated candidate biomarker gene expression.

Results

Six concordantly upregulated and eleven concordantly downregulated DEGs were shared between IPAH and MPM. Upregulated genes were enriched in cell cycle regulation, while downregulated genes were enriched in neutrophil chemotaxis. WGCNA identified 58 overlapping genes. CXCR2, S100A9, and LCN2 were identified as candidate biomarker genes. A ROTS sensitivity analysis confirmed that all 1710 MPM DEGs were reproducible and directionally concordant at the matching FDR <0.05 threshold despite the imbalanced case-control ratio. The classification model achieved AUCs of 0.909 and 0.875 in training and external validation sets, with a LOOCV AUC of 0.879 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.896. Immune infiltration revealed increased Th17 cells but decreased neutrophils in IPAH. CXCR2 and S100A9 expression correlated with neutrophil infiltration; LCN2 expression correlated with metabolic reprogramming. Navarixin showed the strongest binding affinity to CXCR2 (-10.1 kcal/mol). MD simulations confirmed stable binding of the CXCR2-Navarixin complex. qRT-PCR confirmed significant downregulation of all three genes in IPAH patients.

Conclusion

This hypothesis-generating study identifies shared transcriptomic signatures between IPAH and MPM, highlighting CXCR2, S100A9, and LCN2 as candidate biomarkers linked to immune dysregulation and metabolic reprogramming. The computational and correlative nature of these findings, together with the limited size of the external validation cohort, requires confirmation through functional experiments and validation in larger, independent, and multicentre cohorts before clinical translation can be considered.

title: Endothelial Redox Dysregulation in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: Compartmentalized Mechanisms and Therapeutic Implications.
authorString: Moreno-Caceres S, Marciano DP.
abstractText: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive pulmonary vasculopathy in which endothelial dysfunction drives increased pulmonary vascular resistance and arterial remodeling. Redox signaling is central to endothelial homeostasis, and its disruption in PAH reflects changes in the magnitude, source, and subcellular location of reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, as well as the molecular targets they engage. In healthy endothelium, compartmentalized redox signaling supports adaptive responses while preserving nitric oxide bioavailability. Loss of this spatial control in PAH can convert normally transient redox signals into persistent endothelial dysfunction, although the strength of evidence for this conversion differs substantially between pathways. This review examines how disease-associated stressors reshape endothelial redox signaling through NADPH oxidases, mitochondria, eNOS, iron-dependent chemistry, and nuclear pathways and how these compartments communicate. We also examine emerging circulating markers of redox and endothelial dysfunction and evaluate redox-directed therapies across experimental pulmonary hypertension and PAH. Throughout, we grade each mechanism according to whether it is supported by evidence from human PAH vascular tissue, patient-derived pulmonary arterial endothelial cells, experimental pulmonary hypertension models, and pulmonary endothelial models or by extrapolation from other relevant disease systems, and we identify where compartment-specific evidence is inferred from enzyme localization rather than measured directly. Current evidence supports moving beyond broad antioxidant approaches toward strategies that selectively target pathogenic redox signaling within the relevant endothelial compartment.

title: Clinical Characteristics, Cardiometabolic Risk Burden and Therapeutic Patterns in Patients Attending Cardiology Clinics in Spain: The RIESCAR Study.
authorString: Cosín-Sales J, Campuzano R, Cequier A, Díez-Villanueva P, Aldomà-Balasch A, Arrarte-Esteban VI, López-Sánchez ES, Gómez-Pajuelo C, Fernández-Friera L, Chopo-Alcubilla JM, Muñiz J, Gómez-Doblas JJ, RIESCAR Study Investigators.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Contemporary data on patients attending cardiology outpatient clinics in Spain are scarce. We aimed to characterise cardiovascular conditions, cardiometabolic burden, risk-factor control and treatment patterns. Methods: RIESCAR is a national, multicentre, observational study. This analysis included 2808 adults evaluated in 50 general cardiology outpatient clinics. Results: Hypertension was present in 60.3%, dyslipidaemia in 58.9%, type 2 diabetes mellitus in 24.7%, obesity in 32.4%, and central obesity in 48.7%. Established cardiovascular disease was documented in 59.7%, with coronary artery disease (30.0%), atrial fibrillation (18.2%) and heart failure (11.7%) being the most frequent conditions. Among hypertensive patients, 42.6% had blood pressure ≥ 140/90 mmHg. In patients with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), 37.2% achieved LDL-C < 55 mg/dL. Patients received a high number of cardiovascular drugs (mean 3.9). Among patients with a potential clinical indication for contemporary cardiometabolic therapies, SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 receptor agonists were used in 35.4% and 8.6%, respectively. Conclusions: Patients attending cardiology clinics in Spain have a high cardiometabolic burden, with important gaps in blood-pressure and LDL-C target attainment. Use of contemporary cardiometabolic therapies remains variable, highlighting opportunities to strengthen cardiovascular prevention in routine practice.

title: Successful Nonsurgical Management of Norovirus-Associated Necrotizing Enterocolitis in a Preterm Infant: A Case Report.
authorString: Sessa L, Martini L, Tedesco M, Ferrazza A, Stefanini M, Menzella N, Priolo F, Vento G, Costa S.
abstractText: Norovirus infection has been increasingly reported in association with necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) in preterm neonates, although the clinical spectrum remains poorly defined. We report the case of a 29-week preterm male infant who developed abdominal distension on day 35 of life, with a sepsis-like clinical presentation. Stool reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction confirmed Norovirus infection. Serial abdominal radiographs showed intestinal pneumatosis from day 2 of illness, consistent with Bell stage IIA NEC. The pneumatosis persisted for three days and completely resolved by day 5, without perforation or clinical deterioration. The infant was managed conservatively with bowel rest, parenteral nutrition, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and mechanical ventilation for 7 days. IVIG (500 mg/kg/day for 4 days) was administered for clinically suspected capillary leak syndrome. Enteral feeding was restarted after 8 days, and the infant was discharged at 71 days of life without gastrointestinal complications. This case highlights the heterogeneous clinical spectrum of Norovirus-associated intestinal disease and suggests that conservative management may be successful in selected clinically stable preterm infants with NEC and intestinal pneumatosis.

title: 44th National Congress of the Italian Society of Nephrology Nurses (SIAN).
authorString: Sguanci M, Godino L, Grimaldi A, Ferrara G, Cangelosi G, Morales Palomares S, Mancin S, On Behalf Of The Italian Society Of Nephrology Nurses Sian Board Of Directors.
abstractText: The 44th National Congress of the Italian Society of Nephrology Nurses (SIAN), held in Bologna, Italy, from 4 to 6 May 2026, provided a national forum for discussion on the evolving role of nursing in nephrology. The Congress was preceded by a dedicated pre-congress session focused on education, research, and clinical practice, with particular attention to the involvement of nursing students and early-career professionals in scientific activities. Across plenary sessions, round tables, workshops, oral communications, and digital poster presentations, the scientific programme addressed major areas of contemporary nephrology nursing, including professional development, patient-centred care, vascular access management, dialysis technologies, kidney transplantation, symptom management, home and community care, digital health, artificial intelligence, sustainability, and nutritional care. Particular attention was given to the integration of evidence-based practice, clinical expertise, technological innovation, interprofessional collaboration, and patient education. This Conference Proceedings provides an overview of the scientific and educational activities of the meeting and brings together the accepted contributions presented during both the pre-congress session and the main Congress. Collectively, these contributions illustrate the diversity and continued development of nephrology nursing practice and research in Italy and highlight the importance of scientific societies in promoting professional competence, knowledge exchange, and innovation in kidney care.

title: Invasive group A streptococcal endocarditis on an amplatzer septal occluder.
authorString: Leshin-Carmel D, Bruoha S, Berezovsky V, Bar Nur Y, Ahmet N, J Jakobson D, Yosefy C, Gemer O, Tsyba E.
abstractText: We report the first case of late-onset Streptococcus pyogenes endocarditis on an Amplatzer Septal Occluder, appearing five years post-implantation. Seeding originated from an infected intrauterine device, resulting in multi-organ embolization. This case highlights that interatrial occluding devices can remain vulnerable to hematogenous seeding even years after implantation, requiring multidisciplinary management.

title: A mobile health-assisted cardiovascular follow-up after pregnancy complications (MumCare): protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
authorString: Staff AC, Sugulle M, Noll J, Sollie-Hoel MKC, Oteiza Aguirre B, Fiskå BS, Aasbø G, Klovning A, Estensen ME, Waldum ÅH.
abstractText:
Objective

A history of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and/or gestational diabetes is associated with increased risk of long-term maternal cardiovascular (CV) disease. Despite recommendations for preventive strategies, few women receive CV follow-up postpartum. We have developed a personalized digital mobile Health companion, the MumCare (Mum's cardiovascular health for life) application, aiming at improving control of modifiable risk factors for CV disease and to bridge hospital and community health services. This paper describes the protocol for a MumCare randomized controlled trial in Norway.

Methods

Study participation is offered to women at Oslo University Hospital with a diagnosis of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and/or gestational diabetes. Following informed consent (either during pregnancy or within 4 weeks postpartum), a block randomization process assigns participants to one of two groups (access to the Mum Care app or not). The app provides educational material, allows women to track modifiable risk factors, and prompts feedback to registered blood pressures. It also prompts the women to book the nationally recommended follow-up at their general practitioner's at 3-4 and 12 months postpartum. The primary study objective is to assess the effect of MumCare application access on 1-year follow-up rate with a general practitioner. Secondary objectives are to assess group differences at 14 months postpartum regarding: 1) satisfaction with the postpartum mHealth-assisted technology, 2) self-management evaluation, general self-efficacy; and at 14-18 months: 3) modifiable risk factors for CV disease (including hypertension, dyslipidemia, blood sugar control, smoking, weight and physical activity), CV non-invasive hemodynamics and CV-related biomarkers.

Discussion

This randomized controlled trial tests the effect of a mobile Health-assisted follow-up of modifiable risk factors after pregnancy complications associated with premature CV disease in women. A study limitation is a risk of underrepresentation of recently immigrated women due to the restricted language options offered in the app.

Study protocols registration

NCT05835596.

title: Whole-exome sequencing reveals genetic etiology and pregnancy outcomes in fetuses with ultrasound-detected abnormalities at a tertiary center.
authorString: Cai M, Lin N, Huang H, Fu M, Dai Y, Xu L.
abstractText: Despite advances in prenatal diagnostics, the genetic causes underlying fetal ultrasound abnormalities remain poorly understood, with a significant proportion of cases lacking definitive molecular diagnoses. Invasive prenatal testing was performed in 179 cases, followed by whole-exome sequencing (WES) to identify genetic etiologies. Among 179 abnormal fetuses, 132 had single-system and 47 had multisystem abnormalities. WES identified pathogenic (P) or likely pathogenic (LP) variants in 33 cases (19 single-system, 14 multisystem), with skeletal (7), cardiac (5), and craniofacial defects (2) being most frequent. Thirty-four genes were involved, encompassing 41 variants (15 missense, 10 frameshift, 6 splicing, 6 nonsense, and 4 in-frame deletions). WES yielded a P/LP rate of 17.88% (32/179) for variants that explained the fetal phenotype, with an additional pathogenic finding (overall P/LP rate: 18.44%, 33/179). Inheritance patterns were autosomal dominant (19), recessive (12), X-linked (1), and mosaic (1). Family studies confirmed 27 variants (18 inherited, 9 de novo). Pregnancy outcomes included 60 terminations, 19 intrauterine deaths, and 8 postnatal abnormalities. Most fetal ultrasound phenotypes matched the disease-causing gene profiles. Combining molecular testing with ultrasound helps clinicians identify genetic causes, assess recurrence risk, and inform parents, enabling personalized management for high-risk families.

title: Prospective multicenter study of murmur localization and stage-associated murmur grading in dogs with echocardiographically diagnosed cardiac diseases: the LISTEN study.
authorString: Wess G, Häggström J, Stadler J, König L, Kraszewska K, Bittenecker D, Domenech O, Santamarina G, Van den Noortgate G, Bjerknaes MB, Eberhard J, Kriström K, Vatne L, Gajewski M, Schinner-Peters C, Tater G, Torti M, Schummer C, Ljungvall I.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiac auscultation remains fundamental in dogs with suspected cardiac disease, but large prospective datasets describing clinician-recorded murmur localization and intensity across echocardiographic diagnoses are limited. This study aimed to characterize point of maximal intensity (PMI) patterns in dogs with echocardiographically diagnosed cardiac abnormalities and to evaluate the association between murmur grade and disease stage in dogs with myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) and dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM).

Methods

This prospective international multicenter observational study included 6,996 client-owned dogs examined by 50 cardiology-trained veterinarians. Dogs underwent standardized cardiac auscultation at four predefined thoracic locations and transthoracic echocardiography during the same clinical visit. PMI localization was described across cardiac diagnoses, and murmur grade was evaluated in relation to disease stage in MMVD and DCM.

Results

Dogs with MMVD and DCM predominantly had a left apical PMI, whereas congenital outflow tract diseases and patent ductus arteriosus were predominantly associated with a left basilar PMI. Tricuspid regurgitation and ventricular septal defect were more commonly associated with right apical and right basilar PMIs, respectively. In MMVD, murmur intensity increased with advancing disease stage (p < 0.001), and dogs with a murmur greater than soft had higher odds of being in stage B2 or C/D than B1 (OR 35.9, 95% CI 27.6-46.6). In DCM, 25.8% of dogs had no audible murmur. Although murmur grade distribution differed across DCM stages (p = 0.03), intensity did not show a consistent stage-associated increase.

Conclusion

Clinician-recorded four-point auscultation identified characteristic regional PMI patterns across several canine cardiac diseases. Murmur grade was strongly associated with disease stage in MMVD but provided limited stage-related information in DCM. Auscultation may support initial clinical assessment and prioritization of differential diagnoses, but echocardiography remains essential for definitive diagnosis and staging.

title: Future of cardiac diffusion magnetic resonance imaging: a bibliometric analysis.
authorString: Wu X, Yang Y, Xu Y, Wu Z, Liu H, Chen R.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiac diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (cDMRI) has become a valuable noninvasive tool for assessing cardiac microstructure.

Objective

To perform a systematic and comprehensive bibliometric analysis of cDMRI to explore current status, research hotspots and potential future directions.

Material and methods

A systematic search of Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and PubMed was conducted to identify articles on cDMRI published between 2005 and 2024. All retrieved records were independently screened by two reviewers to exclude the articles unrelated to the topic about cDMRI. Co-citation, collaboration networks, burst keywords, and reference analyses were performed.

Results

There were 359 articles searched in WoSCC and 88 articles in PubMed. Finally, 367 articles met the search criteria in both databases. The cardiac "diffusion tensor imaging" (cDTI) emerged as the most prominent keyword, with the highest occurrence count (191.0) and strongest citation bursts (6.8). The study by Nielles-Vallespin et al. showed the strongest citation burst (26.17), accumulating 163 total citations and an average of 20.38 citations per year, highlighting its substantial influence on the development of cDMRI research. The top-cited articles with the strongest citation bursts concentrated on the clinical application of cDTI, its sequence design, and cardiac electrophysiology based on cDTI. The trend topic analysis further revealed "deep learning" as an emerging research focus in cDMRI since 2022.

Conclusions

To our knowledge, this is the first dedicated bibliometric analysis focusing on cDMRI. By systematically analyzing the current status, research hotspots, and future trends of cDMRI, it provided valuable insights to guide future investigations in this field.

title: Development and multicenter validation of a machine learning model for predicting in-hospital postoperative cardiac arrest in elderly surgical patients: the critical role of intraoperative hemodynamic disturbances and blood transfusion.
authorString: Chen X, Chang Y, Sun T, Liu Y, Liu L, Jiang C, Zhan F, Du W.
abstractText:
Background

In-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) is a rare but life-threatening complication in elderly surgical patients. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning model for predicting IHCA and to identify key perioperative risk factors.

Methods

A multicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted among patients aged ≥65 years who underwent non-cardiac surgery at six tertiary hospitals between January 2020 and January 2025. Clinical, laboratory, and perioperative variables were collected. Five machine learning algorithms, including Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), and K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), were developed and compared. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, calibration, decision curve analysis, cross-validation, and external validation. SHAP analysis was applied to interpret the optimal model.

Results

Among the five models, XGBoost demonstrated the best predictive performance, with AUCs of 0.967 and 0.960 in the training and validation cohorts, respectively. It also achieved the lowest Brier score and the highest clinical net benefit. External validation confirmed excellent discrimination (AUC=0.971) and calibration. SHAP analysis identified advanced age, intraoperative tachycardia, intraoperative hypotension, intraoperative blood transfusion, intraoperative hypoxemia, elevated postoperative neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, B-type natriuretic peptide, lactate, and D-dimer levels as the most important predictors of IHCA.

Conclusion

An interpretable XGBoost-based model demonstrated excellent performance for predicting postoperative cardiac arrest in elderly patients. The identified risk factors reflected perioperative vulnerability, intraoperative hemodynamic instability, and postoperative physiological deterioration.

title: Comparison of cardiopulmonary function in patients with scoliosis at rest and during exercise: a case-control study.
authorString: Zhou B, Song Z, Bi N, Zhang L, Shi Z, Li T, Cao C, Zhao Z, Wang Y.
abstractText:
Background

Preoperative cardiopulmonary assessment in scoliosis is typically dominated by resting spirometry and the Cobb angle, yet resting tests may understate functional impairment and curve magnitude predicts it only weakly. This study integrated resting echocardiography, static pulmonary function testing, CT lung volume, and cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) in the same preoperative patients to characterize cardiopulmonary impairment and to separate the structural determinants of lung volume from those of exercise reserve.

Methods

In this single-center case-control study, 33 consecutive preoperative patients with scoliosis [21 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS), 12 congenital scoliosis (CS); aged 10-20 years] were compared with 20 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Predicted spirometric values were derived from arm span with the GLI Global equations. Analyses used effect sizes with false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction, body-size-adjusted hierarchical regression, and cross-validated ROC analysis.

Results

Resting cardiac function was preserved (left ventricular ejection fraction, cardiac output and cardiac index all non-significant after FDR), whereas restrictive ventilation and exercise reserve were reduced: FVC 72.0% vs. 92.8% predicted (q < 0.001), peak oxygen uptake 21.8 vs. 29.6 mL/min/kg (q < 0.001), O₂ pulse 5.9 vs. 9.7 mL/beat (q < 0.001), and VE/VCO₂ slope 32.4 vs. 27.5 (q < 0.001). Among 13 patients normal at rest, 10 (77%) were abnormal on CPET. Thoracic height independently predicted restrictive impairment beyond the Cobb angle, kyphosis, and body size (FVC %predicted B = 3.65 per cm, 95% CI   1.64-5.65; AUC 0.90, cross-validated 0.84; threshold 19.6 cm), whereas no deformity parameter independently predicted exercise capacity. At matched thoracic height, congenital scoliosis had lower CT lung volume than idiopathic scoliosis (1,881 vs. 2,356 cm3; p = 0.030).

Conclusion

Preoperative scoliosis is characterized by preserved resting indices but a frequently occult reduction in exercise reserve, including an exercise cardiac limitation revealed by O₂ pulse that resting echocardiography does not show. Thoracic height is a body-size-independent predictor of restrictive lung volume with a clinically usable threshold, while exercise reserve is multifactorial and requires direct CPET assessment. The two dimensions of preoperative cardiopulmonary risk should therefore be measured separately.

title: Factors associated with short- and long-term maintenance of sinus rhythm after successful elective electrical cardioversion.
authorString: Radovanović NN, Branković NS, Vujadinović N, Mujović NM, Juričić S, Petrović O, Raspopović S, Milašinović G.
abstractText:
Introduction

Electrical cardioversion (ECV) effectively restores sinus rhythm in patients with persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) and atrial flutter (AFL), although arrhythmia recurrence is common. We aimed to identify factors associated with a higher probability of maintaining sinus rhythm one month after successful ECV, and after one year in those who were arrhythmia-free after the first month.

Methods

This retrospective, single-center study included patients who underwent elective ECV for persistent AF or AFL between January 2011 and June 2023. Clinical, electrocardiographic, and echocardiographic characteristics were analyzed to identify parameters associated with the maintenance of sinus rhythm.

Results

We included 297 ECV procedures. ECV was successful in 91.9% of patients and sinus rhythm was maintained in 89.7% of them at one month and in 40.3% at one year follow-up. Shorter arrhythmia duration (OR = 0.863, 95% CI: 0.76-0.98, p = 0.026) and ventricular pacing on the pre-procedural ECG (OR = 5.212, 95% CI: 1.16-23.48, p = 0.032) were associated with one-month success. Factors associated with one-year sinus rhythm maintenance in patients who were in sinus rhythm during monthly follow-up were smaller left atrial dimensions (OR = 0.817, 95%CI: 0.77-0.98, p = 0.022), the first-ever arrhythmia episode (OR = 3.320, 95%CI: 1.10-10.05, p = 0.034), lower CHA2DS2-VASc score (OR = 0.132, 95%CI: 0.03-0.54, p = 0.005), non-smoking status (OR = 0.120, 95%CI: 0.04-0.37, p < 0.001), no previous ECV (OR = 0.082, 95%CI: 0.01-0.47, p = 0.005), and antiarrhythmic therapy (OR = 2.486, 95%CI: 1.01-8.65, p = 0.05).

Conclusions

ECV is a reasonable rhythm-control strategy in AF/AFL particularly when performed early after arrhythmia onset, in non-smokers and patients with fewer comorbidities, antiarrhythmic treatment, smaller left atrium and no prior ECV.

title: Perinatal and Early Respiratory Factors Associated with Invasive Mechanical Ventilation in Very Preterm Infants: A Retrospective Cohort Study from Kazakhstan.
authorString: Alimukhamedov U, Bozhbanbayeva N, Çetinkaya M, Tolykbayev T, Sadykova A, Suieubekov B, Alseitov U.
abstractText: Background: Evidence on factors associated with the timing of invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) among very preterm infants in Central Asia remains limited. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included infants born at 22-30 weeks gestation in two tertiary perinatal centers in Kazakhstan between 2021 and 2025. Analyses were restricted to 381 infants with complete data. IMV initiated during the first week of life was classified as early IMV, and IMV initiated after the first week as late IMV. Separate multivariable logistic regression models were constructed for any, early, and late IMV. Results: Any IMV was recorded in 191 infants (50.1%), including 132 (34.6%) with early IMV and 59 (15.5%) with late IMV. Early IMV was associated with gestational age ≤ 27 weeks (aOR 3.91, 95% CI 1.66-9.22), absence of spontaneous breathing at birth (aOR 151.93, 95% CI 18.26-1263.88), and initial FiO2 > 0.30 (aOR 4.39, 95% CI 1.97-9.77). Complete antenatal corticosteroid exposure was inversely associated with early IMV (aOR 0.38, 95% CI 0.20-0.72). Late IMV was associated with birth weight < 1000 g (aOR 3.51, 95% CI 1.47-8.35) and initial FiO2 > 0.30 (aOR 2.12, 95% CI 1.02-4.39). An initial set CPAP ≥ 12 cmH2O was recorded in 71.9% of infants and was associated with any IMV but not with early or late IMV separately. Conclusions: Early and late IMV were associated with different clinical patterns. These observational associations may support risk assessment but do not establish causal effects of respiratory-support practices.

title: Outcomes of gastrostomy in children with neurological impairment: a systematic review.
authorString: Ibrahim MK, Jummakhan H, Dawood M, Siam M, Alhusami MA, Khan S, Mokhtar J, Benamer HTS, Babiker MOE.
abstractText:
Introduction

Gastrostomy feeding is widely used for children with neurological impairment and inadequate oral intake, but evidence across family-important outcomes has not been synthesised. Previous systematic reviews were restricted to cerebral palsy and found no controlled studies. The objective of this study is to assess gastrostomy vs. continued oral/nasogastric feeding on nutritional, respiratory, neurodevelopmental, and caregiver-reported outcomes, and to quantify complications.

Methods

A PROSPERO-registered systematic review (CRD420261483110) was conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Five databases were searched to 15 July 2026 for children aged 0-18 with neurological impairment undergoing gastrostomy. Duplicate screening, data extraction, and risk-of-bias appraisal (RoB 2, ROBINS-I, JBI, CASP) were performed. Heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis; narrative synthesis prioritized study design and methodological quality over direction-of-effect vote counting.

Results

From 5,503 records, 120 studies (≈117 cohorts, 30 countries) met the criteria. The evidence was predominantly observational, and most comparative studies carried a serious risk of bias. Nutritional status improved in the majority of 56 studies, though earlier placement's association with more robust catch-up growth does not establish causality. Among 56 respiratory studies, smaller cohorts reported fewer infections, but the largest propensity-matched and population-linked datasets showed no reduction, and in some analyses an increase, in pneumonia hospitalisations. Minor complications were common (20%-95%). Major complications clustered at 0%-3% without concurrent antireflux surgery, but rose several-fold when fundoplication or jejunal extensions were added. Reflux outcomes (59 studies) depended on preoperative status; it is hypothesized from limited physiological data that gastrostomy may increase de novo reflux risk in previously reflux-free children, though <10% required subsequent antireflux surgery. All-cause mortality (67 studies) was high but disease-related; procedure-attributable death was rare, and 30-day mortality was 0%-3% outside the most fragile groups. Quality-of-life data (21 studies) showed favourable caregiver outcomes in 14/17 studies, but the child's quality of life has been measured properly only once and was unchanged. Only 11 studies addressed neurodevelopment; the single study using a standardised instrument found cognitive recovery unrelated to the feeding route.

Discussion

Gastrostomy is consistently associated with improved weight-based nutritional status and carries low serious surgical harm when performed without concurrent antireflux surgery. It does not eliminate aspiration risk and is hypothesized to increase de novo reflux risk in previously reflux-free children. Caregiver quality of life improves on validated measurement; however, the available evidence is insufficient to determine whether gastrostomy has a favourable, unfavourable, or neutral effect on a child's neurodevelopment.

Systematic review registration

PROSPERO: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261483110.

title: Folic Acid Supplementation Adherence During Pregnancy: Evidence from a Cross-Sectional Survey in Italy.
authorString: Licata F, Scicchitano CA, Amodei L, Bianco A.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Periconceptional folic acid (FA) supplementation is a cornerstone of primary prevention of neural tube defects (NTDs). However, adequate preconceptional FA intake remains suboptimal in Italy. This study aimed to assess FA use among pregnant women in the Calabria region, determine whether their intake met United States Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) recommendations, and explore potential predictors that shape these practices. Methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted among pregnant women using face-to-face interviews. The adequacy of FA intake was based on the USPSTF guidelines, which recommend a daily FA intake of 400-800 μg, starting at least one month before conception and continuing through the first two to three months of pregnancy. Results: Among 421 women, 92.3% reported FA intake, predominantly following a medical prescription (86.3%), usually by a gynecologist rather than a general practitioner. General awareness of FA was notably high (79.3%), whereas preconceptional adherence was strikingly low (25.8%). Indeed, among women with planned pregnancies, only 22.6% achieved adequate intake. Furthermore, the strongest predictors of preconception FA use were having received a healthcare worker's recommendation (aOR: 26.84; 95% CI: 11.40-63.17) and having a planned pregnancy (aOR: 6.03; 95% CI: 1.92-18.90). Conclusions: Despite widespread general knowledge, timely preconceptional FA use remains low, reflecting a "knowing-doing" gap and an over-reliance on specialist-driven prescription. These findings support integrating FA counseling into routine primary care and considering mandatory food fortification to ensure equitable, population-level prevention of NTDs, independent of women's education status or pregnancy intention.

title: Alcohol-induced placental vasculopathy reprograms the placental-fetal cardiovascular axis: angiogenic mechanisms linking maternal alcohol exposure to developmental cardiovascular programming.
authorString: Cebral E.
abstractText: Among prenatal insults, maternal alcohol consumption has emerged as an important determinant of fetal cardiovascular development and long-term cardiovascular disease susceptibility. Growing evidence indicates that the placenta is a central biological mediator linking maternal alcohol exposure with abnormal fetal cardiac development. This review integrates current experimental and clinical findings on the developmental relationship between placental vascularization and fetal cardiogenesis, highlighting the placental-embryofetal cardiovascular axis as a conceptual framework for alcohol-induced cardiopathy programming. We examine evidence that prenatal alcohol exposure disrupts placental vascular development through impaired decidual spiral artery angiogenesis and remodeling and altered trophoblast differentiation and invasion, and labyrinthine vascularization. Experimental studies suggest that oxidative stress and hypoxia perturb interconnected angiogenic vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-nitric oxide synthases (NOS)-matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) pathways, and related redox-sensitive mediators, ultimately compromising placental perfusion and fetoplacental hemodynamics. We further discuss that placental dysfunction may alter the molecular, metabolic, endocrine, oxygen-dependent, and hemodynamic signals regulating fetal cardiac development, potentially affecting myocardial morphogenesis, cardiac remodeling, coronary vascularization, septation, valvulogenesis, and cardiovascular maturation during critical developmental windows. Collectively, available evidence supports a model in which disruption of placental angiogenic homeostasis may represent a key intermediary linking maternal alcohol exposure with fetal cardiovascular programming. This perspective integrates direct embryofetal effects with indirect placental-mediated mechanisms and highlights the need to clarify their relative contributions across developmental windows. Improved understanding of the placental-embryofetal cardiovascular axis may facilitate identification of early biomarkers and preventive or therapeutic strategies to reduce the lifelong cardiovascular consequences of prenatal alcohol exposure.

title: The diagnostic value of admission myoglobin for sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy: a prospective cohort study.
authorString: Chen Y, Lin X, Yu G.
abstractText:
Background

Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy (SICM) is a frequent and under-recognized complication of sepsis. Early diagnosis remains challenging. We evaluated the diagnostic value of admission myoglobin (MYO), alone and combined with NT-proBNP and the SOFA score, for SICM in patients with sepsis.

Methods

In this single-center prospective cohort study (April 2022 to May 2024), we enrolled 158 patients with sepsis diagnosed according to Sepsis-3 criteria. Blood samples for MYO and NT-proBNP were collected within 24 h of admission; admission echocardiography was performed as soon as feasible (within 24 h whenever possible, and within 72 h in all enrolled patients); follow-up echocardiography was performed between day 7 and day 14. SICM was defined as left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) below 50% with documented reversibility. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with SICM, adjusting for age, sex, body mass index, and renal function. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, internal validation by 1,000 bootstrap resamples, and decision curve analysis (DCA) were performed. Model calibration was assessed by a calibration plot, the calibration intercept and slope, and the Brier score, with bootstrap optimism-corrected estimates.

Results

Of 158 patients, 63 (39.9%) were diagnosed with SICM. MYO levels were significantly higher in the SICM group than in the non-SICM group (median 395.7 vs. 97.3 ng/mL, P < 0.001). In multivariate analysis adjusting for age, sex, BMI, and renal function, MYO (OR 1.061 per 100 ng/mL, 95% CI 1.008-1.115; P = 0.023) and NT-proBNP (OR 1.087 per 1,000 pg/mL, 95% CI 1.025-1.153; P = 0.005) were independently associated with SICM. The combined model (MYO + NT-proBNP + SOFA) achieved an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.821 (95% CI: 0.750-0.892), outperforming SOFA alone (AUC 0.743; likelihood ratio test P < 0.001); the optimism-corrected AUC after bootstrap validation was 0.812. The model was well calibrated (calibration intercept 0.00, slope 1.00; Brier score 0.173). DCA suggested potential net benefit across threshold probabilities of 0.1-0.7.

Conclusion

Admission MYO, particularly in combination with NT-proBNP and SOFA, may assist in the early identification and diagnosis of SICM.
