abstractText: Background and Objectives: Pituitary adenomas may be associated with metabolic and cardiovascular abnormalities, but comparative evidence across subtypes is limited. We compared cardiometabolic and echocardiographic profiles, left ventricular diastolic dysfunction (LVDD), and carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) among patients with prolactinoma, acromegaly, or nonfunctioning pituitary adenoma (NFPA) and healthy controls and investigated factors associated with LVDD. Materials and Methods: This cross-sectional comparative study included 214 participants evaluated between 2016 and 2018: 91 with prolactinoma, 26 with acromegaly, 45 with NFPA, and 52 healthy controls. Participants underwent clinical, biochemical, echocardiographic, and CIMT assessment. LVDD was diagnosed and graded according to the 2016 American Society of Echocardiography (ASE) and European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging (EACVI) recommendations. Factors associated with LVDD were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Results: The mean age was 41.3 ± 12.4 years, and 64.5% of participants were women. Acromegaly was associated with the highest fasting glucose, HbA1c, insulin, and homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) values (all p < 0.001) and, compared with controls, a higher left atrial volume index (LAVI) and average E/e' ratio and lower left ventricular ejection fraction (despite preserved ejection fraction), E/A ratio, and lateral e' velocity. CIMT was higher in NFPA than in prolactinoma. LVDD was present in 21.5% of the cohort and in 5.8%, 19.8%, 46.2%, and 28.9% of the control, prolactinoma, acromegaly, and NFPA groups, respectively (p < 0.001); 84.8% of cases were grade I. Increasing age was independently associated with LVDD (OR 1.265 per year, 95% CI 1.155-1.385; p < 0.001), and diagnostic group was independently associated with LVDD overall (p = 0.004). Compared with controls, adjusted LVDD odds were higher in prolactinoma (OR 10.9, 95% CI 1.34-89.68), acromegaly (OR 167.5, 95% CI 10.3-2721.4), and NFPA (OR 12.0, 95% CI 1.4-104.8). Conclusions: Pituitary adenoma subtypes were associated with distinct cardiometabolic and echocardiographic profiles and a higher prevalence of LVDD than in healthy controls, particularly in acromegaly. Most LVDD cases were grade I, indicating predominantly impaired relaxation. Although age and diagnostic group were associated with LVDD in the adjusted analysis, the wide confidence intervals warrant cautious interpretation and validation in larger cohorts.

title: Molecular Signaling in Pulmonary Vein Stenosis: Toward Lesion-Specific Phenotyping and Individualized Therapy.
authorString: Moss ME, Klouda T.
abstractText: Pulmonary vein stenosis (PVS) is a rare but life-threatening disease affecting young children, characterized by progressive narrowing of the pulmonary veins. Multimodal treatment, including surgical and catheter-based interventions combined with medical therapy, can improve survival; however, disease recurrence and progression are common. Currently, there is no therapy able to reverse existing disease, leaving lung transplantation the only option for patients with advanced, treatment-resistant disease. Studies using animal models and human tissue have identified several mechanisms that contribute to PVS, including mechanosensitive signaling and endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition. In parallel, advances in cardiac imaging and hemodynamic profiling of individual pulmonary veins have improved risk stratification and provided opportunities to modify treatment strategies. Despite these advances, the development of disease-modifying therapies able to improve patient outcomes will require a more thorough understanding of the underlying pathophysiology. In this review, we examine the histological features of PVS and summarize the cellular contributions and signaling pathways implicated in disease development. We will also explore the potential of integrating patient- and lesion-specific phenotypes and molecular signatures to guide individual treatment strategies, as well as the current limitations and future directions of PVS research.

title: In Memoriam: David S. Cannom, MD, FHRS, 1940-2026.
authorString: Singh JP, Prystowsky EN, Youngblood JH, Lampert R, Ruskin JN.

title: Prospective Associations of Diet Quality During Pregnancy With Cardiovascular Health (Life's Essential 8) Among Women in Midlife.
authorString: Rifas-Shiman SL, Aris IM, Hivert MF, Zhang M, Chavarro JE, Oken E.

journal.title: Journal of human nutrition and dietetics : the official journal of the British Dietetic Association

abstractText:
Introduction

Cardiovascular health (CVH) often declines in midlife. Diet during pregnancy, a similarly sensitive period involving physiological changes, may influence long-term CVH, but few studies have examined this relationship. We examined the associations between diet during pregnancy and CVH in midlife.

Methods

Participants are 776 women enroled in Project Viva during early pregnancy (1999-2002, mean 32.7 years). Participants completed food frequency questionnaires during the first and second trimesters, from which we calculated three diet scores (higher scores = better diet): Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH), Mediterranean Diet (MD) and Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII × -1). We averaged scores across trimesters and generated internal z-scores. At the midlife visit (2017-2021, mean 51.1 y), we assessed CVH using the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (range 0-100; higher scores = better CVH), including behavioural (diet, physical activity, sleep, smoking) and biomedical (BMI, blood pressure, lipids, glucose) subscores. We assessed associations using linear regression adjusted for age, race and ethnicity, nativity, education, parity, marital status and income at enrolment.

Results

Most participants were non-Hispanic White (70%) and college graduates (76%). Mean midlife CVH score was 76.3 points. Higher (per 1-SD) DASH z-scores were associated with better overall (β 3.3; 95% CI 2.2-4.3), behavioural (3.5; 2.5-4.4) and biomedical (3.1; 1.5-4.7) CVH scores. Higher MD z-scores were associated with better overall CVH (2.4; 1.4-3.4), behavioural (2.6; 1.6-3.5) and biomedical (2.6; 1.0-4.2) scores. Higher DII (× -1) z-scores were associated with better overall CVH (2.6; 1.6-3.7), behavioural (2.7; 1.7-3.7) and biomedical (2.5; 0.9-4.1) scores. A better pregnancy diet was associated with higher CVH scores for diet, physical activity and BMI, and both DASH and DII with blood pressure.

Conclusions

Women who consumed healthier diets during pregnancy had better CVH two decades later. Dietary assessment in pregnancy may identify women at risk for both short-term and long-term health problems.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Electrocardiogram Screening for Detection of Low Ejection Fraction in Routine Care: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
authorString: Ahmed AAO, Ahmed OAO, Ahmed RAO, Dishean AS, Gilbert C, Mohamed MMA, Ahmed Y, Abdelmageed MH, Eissa AA.

journal.title: Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc

abstractText:
Background

Left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVSD) is common and treatable but often undiagnosed, especially in early stages with non-specific symptoms. AI applied to standard ECGs offers low-cost screening for low ejection fraction (EF), yet its real-world impact on diagnosis remains unclear.

Methods

A systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs assessed AI-ECG screening for low EF in clinical practice. The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261287652). Databases (PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Central, Google Scholar) were searched from inception to January 18, 2026, for RCTs comparing AI-ECG screening to usual care in adults without known heart failure undergoing routine ECGs. The primary outcome was new low EF (≤ 50%) confirmed by echocardiography. Secondary outcomes included echocardiography referral rates, positive predictive value, and cardiology referral rates. Pooled risk ratios (RR) with 95% CIs were calculated using a random-effects model.

Results

Three RCTs were included (two individual and one cluster) with 37,467 participants. After adjusting for clustering, AI-ECG screening significantly improved detection of new low EF diagnoses compared to usual care (RR 1.36, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.64; p = 0.002; I2 = 0%), with a number needed to screen of 204. No significant difference was found in echocardiography referral rates (RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.96 to 1.09; p = 0.55; I2 = 36%). The PPV of the AI tool ranged from approximately 20% to 34% across studies.

Conclusion

AI-ECG screening added to routine care improves low EF detection without substantially increasing echocardiography referrals. These findings support AI-ECG for earlier LVSD detection in at-risk populations, though further validation across diverse AI platforms is warranted.

title: Incidence of Intensive Care Unit Delirium After Heart Surgery: A Feasibility Study of a Forest Environment Intervention.
authorString: Wagner-Skacel J, Schörghuber M, Kumpitsch C, Skacel P, Stross T, Miksch E, Pilz R, D'Avia C, Wilding M, Jauk E, Lamprecht D, Brandstätter A, Stanschus L, Reininghaus K, Dalkner N, Mörkl S, Reininghaus EZ, Horvath A, Bengesser S.
abstractText:
Background

Postoperative delirium is a serious complication in intensive care units (ICUs), particularly following cardiac surgery. It is associated with circadian rhythm disruption, sleep disturbances and adverse outcomes. ICU environments often lack natural time cues, which may exacerbate circadian misalignment and increase delirium risk.

Aim

The primary aim of the study was the evaluation of the implementation of two chronotherapeutic ICU interventions regarding recruitment, implementability and safety. Its secondary aim was to descriptively assess postoperative delirium across intervention groups.

Study design

This randomized feasibility study was conducted in a tertiary cardiac surgery ICU in Austria. Adult patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery were allocated to one of three groups: (1) forest environment, (2) light exposure or (3) standard ICU care. Interventions were applied for 12 h daily. Delirium was assessed at three postoperative time points using the confusion assessment method for the ICU (CAM-ICU) and intensive care delirium screening checklist (ICDSC).

Results

This study was conducted between March 2020 and 2025. Seventy-seven patients were enrolled, and 64 remained in the final analytical cohort. Interventions were delivered within routine care. Patients and ICU staff did not report intervention-related concerns. Implementation challenges included ICU restructuring, patient transfers due to COVID-19 and deviations from randomized allocation because of operational constraints. No intervention-related adverse events occurred. Delirium assessments were limited at several time points because of sedation, early ICU discharge or transfer. Across all groups, postoperative delirium was detected in 5 of 130 CAM-ICU completed assessments (3.8%) and 8 of 115 ICDSC completed assessments (6.9%), precluding inferential group comparisons.

Conclusions

Chronotherapeutic environmental interventions were feasible and safe in ICU care. Feasibility results highlighted challenges related to ICU logistics, sedation-related assessment limitations and pandemic-related disruptions. The unexpectedly low delirium incidence limited conclusions regarding intervention efficacy. Future trials should include larger high-risk populations and prospectively defined feasibility outcomes.

Relevance to clinical practice

Optimized ICU environments, including noise reduction and light management, may support delirium prevention. Chronotherapeutic environmental interventions are feasible additions to routine ICU care.

title: Synergistic Promotion of Ferroptosis in Cardiomyocytes by Tumor Cell Secretory Factors and PD-1 Blockade.
authorString: Ma X, Li X, Qu F, Cheng H, Liu Y, Liu C.

journal.title: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

abstractText: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) targeting PD-1 frequently cause severe cardiotoxicity, yet the mechanisms involving tumor-host crosstalk remain poorly defined. Emerging evidence implicates ferroptosis, an iron-dependent regulated cell death, in cardiac injury during cancer immunotherapy. Primary neonatal murine ventricular cardiomyocytes (NMVCs) were exposed to lung cancer-derived tumor-conditioned media (TCM; tumor-conditioned media) enriched with exosomes, anti-PD-1 antibody, or both. Ferroptotic markers, mitochondrial bioenergetics, inflammatory signaling, and exosomal microRNA cargo were systematically evaluated using standardized biochemical assays, quantitative PCR, and targeted pharmacological rescue experiments. TCM primed cardiomyocytes for ferroptosis by downregulating the GPX4/SLC7A11/Nrf2 antioxidant axis, depleting glutathione, and elevating labile iron and lipid peroxidation. Anti-PD-1 treatment alone induced minimal oxidative stress but synergized with TCM to amplify ferroptosis > 4.7-fold, triggering profound mitochondrial depolarization and upregulating pro-ferroptotic enzymes ACSL4/LPCAT3. Tumor-derived exosomal miR-214-3p and miR-23a-3p directly suppressed GPX4 and Nrf2, mediating cellular vulnerability. The combined insult hyperactivated NF-κB and STING pathways in a mitochondria-dependent manner, markedly increasing pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion. Co-treatment with ferrostatin-1, deferoxamine, or Nrf2 activators effectively reversed ferroptotic markers and restored mitochondrial function. Tumor-derived exosomal factors and PD-1 blockade synergistically drive ferroptotic cardiomyocyte death by crippling antioxidant defenses and amplifying inflammatory signaling. Targeting ferroptosis or its upstream regulators presents a promising cardioprotective strategy for patients receiving cancer immunotherapy.

title: Renal Function and 4-Year Outcomes in Edoxaban-Treated Patients: A Sub-Analysis From the ETNA-AF Europe Study.
authorString: De Caterina R, Fronk EM, Nunes J, Lamparter M, Kirchhof P, Zoccali C, ETNA‐AF Europe Investigators.
abstractText:
Background

Non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants, like edoxaban, are essential in managing atrial fibrillation (AF). The impact of renal function on edoxaban dosages in real-world settings remains unclear. This 4-year ETNA-AF-Europe study follow-up analysis investigated how chronic kidney disease (CKD) stages affect the safety and effectiveness of usual edoxaban doses.

Methods

ETNA-AF-Europe (NCT02944019) was an observational study conducted from 2016 to 2022 across 776 centres in 10 European countries. Hazard ratios (HR) and annualized event rates were calculated for all-cause death, cardiovascular (CV) death, stroke and bleeding events for the overall population and participants stratified by dose (30/60 mg) and CKD stages at baseline.

Results

Of the 13,164 participants in the full analysis set, 9114 participants with CKD (Stage 1, n = 2064; Stage 2, n = 4855; Stage 3, n = 1985; Stage 4, n = 135; missing, n = 75) received label-recommended edoxaban doses. Compared with CKD Stage 1, higher CKD stages were associated with increased risks for stroke (Stage 3: HR [95% CI]: 1.889 [1.240-2.878], p = 0.003) and CV death (HR [95% CI]; Stage 4: 14.450 [8.270-25.247], Stage 3: 4.672 [3.312-6.969], Stage 2: 2.066 [1.394-3.062], all p < 0.001). All-cause death followed a similar trend. After adjusting for age, sex, body weight, CHA2DS2-VASc and modified HAS-BLED scores, most bleeding and effectiveness outcomes showed no nominally significant differences across CKD stages.

Conclusions

Edoxaban in patients with AF is effective and well tolerated across CKD stages and appropriate label dosing can offset the risk from renal impairment.

title: Evidence for the Existence of Neural Stem-Like Cells in Adult Rodent Intrinsic Cardiac Nervous Ganglia.
authorString: Jean A, Lizot G, Gourmelon M, Antigny F, Cousin L, Crotti M, Arnault P, Bescond J, Bois P, Constantin B, Coronas V, Chatelier A.

journal.title: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology

abstractText: Cardiac function is modulated by the intrinsic cardiac nervous system (ICNS), which integrates autonomic signals and undergoes remodeling in pathological conditions. Here, we demonstrate that adult rodent ICNS ganglia harbor neural stem-like cells that proliferate in vitro, form neurospheres, self-renew, and generate neurons expressing βIII-tubulin and PGP 9.5. In vivo, cells expressing the stem cell marker SOX2 are detected within ICNS ganglia. Moreover, cardiac injury induced by monocrotaline increases the number of SOX2-positive cells expressing the cell cycle marker Ki67 and the number of EdU-incorporating, nestin-expressing cells within the ICNS. Together, our data provide the first evidence of neural stem-like cells in adult ICNS ganglia and suggest their potential role in cardiac neuroplasticity.

title: Rapid Response System Escalation During Recovery of Hospital Bed Occupancy: An Observational Longitudinal Study.
authorString: Noguchi A, Yamada T, Anzai T, Oka K, Ai M, Uchimura Y, Toba M, Takahashi K, Moriwaki M, Wakabayashi K.
abstractText:
Background

Early warning scores (EWS) identify patient deterioration, but their impact depends on how they are integrated into workflows and escalation culture, particularly as hospitals recover from pandemic-related bed pressures.

Aims

To evaluate changes in rapid response system (RRS) escalation processes and rare safety outcomes after embedding an EWS within proactive Critical Care Outreach Team (CCOT) rounds as hospital bed occupancy recovered.

Study design

Observational longitudinal study at a single tertiary hospital in Japan comparing one pre-intervention year (2021) with three post-intervention years (2022-2024). In January 2022, a standardised EWS was embedded into proactive CCOT rounds and used as a prompt for shared clinical reasoning rather than a strict numeric trigger. Monthly aggregated ward-level data were analysed using Poisson regression, adjusting for seasonality, patient characteristics and bed occupancy.

Results

Across 71 985 admissions and 692 942 general-ward patient-days, rates of nurse-initiated escalations, RRS activations and resuscitation-status updates per 1000 patient-days increased in post-intervention analyses, but these differences were attenuated after full adjustment. In fully adjusted models, post-intervention incidence rate ratios (IRRs) were close to 1.0 for all process outcomes. For nurse-initiated escalations, IRRs ranged from 0.94 to 1.14, and all 95% confidence intervals included 1.0. Rates of unexpected in-hospital cardiac arrest and unplanned ICU admission remained low and stable. Bed occupancy increased over the study period, but within-year associations with outcomes were weak.

Conclusions

After adjustment for patient characteristics and hospital bed occupancy, embedding an EWS within proactive CCOT rounds was associated with broadly stable escalation process indicators and no clear evidence of deterioration in rare safety outcomes.

Relevance to clinical practice

These findings suggest that approaches to the RRS afferent limb that embed EWS use within structured dialogue between ward nurses and outreach teams may provide one plausible mechanism for sustaining escalation behaviours under operational pressure.

title: Sequential Associations of Sleep Architecture, Nocturnal Oxygenation, and Respiratory Disturbance With a Composite PSG-Derived Rhythm-Event Index.
authorString: Nikoubakht N, Kashaninasab F, Ghalehbandi MF, Khoozan M, Nazari MA.
abstractText:
Background

Sleep-disordered breathing (SDB), particularly obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), has been associated with cardiovascular complications including cardiac arrhythmias. However, the relative contributions of respiratory, oxygenation, and sleep architecture indices to composite PSG-derived rhythm-event index remain incompletely understood.

Objective

To investigate the sequential associations of sleep architecture, nocturnal oxygenation, and respiratory disturbance indices with the composite PSG-derived rhythm-event index in patients undergoing polysomnography (PSG).

Methods

Demographic, respiratory, oxygenation and sleep-architecture variables were extracted from PSG records. The primary outcome was a composite PSG-derived rhythm-event count, estimated as round(arrhythmia index × TST_hours) from the PSG-exported arrhythmia index, which was calculated during total sleep time only. Negative binomial regression used an offset of log(TST_hours). Because the outcome demonstrated overdispersion, negative binomial regression with an offset of log(TST hours) was used. Because the original 14-predictor model was over-parameterized for the sample size, a six-predictor model (age, sex, BMI, AHI, T90, and sleep efficiency) was chosen post hoc. This reduced model was not prespecified before the original analysis. Sleep efficiency was retained because it showed a strong signal in the exploratory 14-predictor model. The resulting p-values should therefore be interpreted as optimistic and exploratory. A sequential model-building approach (Model 1: age, sex, BMI, AHI; Model 2: plus T90; Model 3: plus sleep efficiency) was used to document the incremental contribution of each domain. A fully adjusted 14-predictor model was fitted only as a supplementary analysis. Wald 95% CIs and bootstrap percentile 95% CIs (2000 resamples) are reported.

Results

Forty-one participants were included (mean age 47.8 ± 13.5 years; median BMI 29.4 kg/m2). Severe OSA (AHI ≥ 30 events/hour) was present in 56.1%. Median arrhythmia index was 3.2 events/hour, with marked overdispersion. In the six-predictor model, only higher sleep efficiency was associated with lower arrhythmia rate (IRR = 0.946 per 1 percentage-point increase, 95% CI 0.921-0.972, p < 0.001; bootstrap 95% CI 0.888-0.984). T90 was associated in the Wald inference (IRR = 1.034, 95% CI 1.006-1.063, p = 0.016) but this association was not robust under bootstrap resampling (95% CI 0.979-1.067). AHI was not associated with arrhythmia rate (IRR = 1.000, 95% CI 0.987-1.014, p = 0.954). Age, sex and BMI were also not significant. A 14-predictor exploratory model had a marginally lower AIC (411.4) but a substantially higher BIC (438.8), consistent with overfitting.

Conclusion

In this exploratory selected sleep-center cohort, AHI and other respiratory-event indices were not independently associated with the composite PSG-derived rhythm-event index. Only higher sleep efficiency showed a robust association with lower arrhythmia rate, but this finding is hypothesis-generating and may reflect unmeasured confounding. These results require confirmation in larger prospective studies and should not guide clinical risk stratification.

title: Immediate drug hypersensitivity severity is associated with cardiovascular risk.
authorString: Okumus Guclu A, Seren OT, Ozaydin Unal SE, Kocabas ME, Aksu B, Ozmen U, Hafizoglu M, Bayrak Degirmenci P.
abstractText: Background: Drug hypersensitivity reactions (DHR) exhibit substantial clinical heterogeneity. Although established cardiovascular disease is a known risk factor for severe anaphylaxis, the impact of subclinical cardiovascular risk on DHR severity remains poorly understood. Objective: This study investigated the association between Systematic Coronary Risk Evaluation 2 (SCORE2) estimated cardiovascular risk and the severity of immediate-type DHRs. Methods: This retrospective study included 161 patients ages 40-69 years (median age, 49 years; 79.5% women) with immediate-type DHRs. To assess the subclinical risk, those with known cardiovascular disease, diabetes, or chronic kidney disease were excluded. Reaction severity was graded by using the Brown system, and SCORE2 was calculated by using clinical data from the 12 months preceding the reaction. Results: Reaction severity was graded as mild (35.4%), moderate (34.8%), or severe (29.8%). The median SCORE2 values were significantly higher in the severe group versus the mild group (4.10% versus 2.50%; p = 0.022). The proportion of patients in high or very high SCORE2 risk categories increased stepwise with reaction severity (35.1% in the mild group versus 64.6% in the severe group; p = 0.011). In an univariable ordinal logistic regression, each 1-point increase in SCORE2 percentage was associated with higher odds of greater reaction severity (odds ratio 1.144 [95% confidence interval, 1.041-1.257]; p = 0.005). This association remained significant after adjusting for the culprit drug class (p = 0.008). Conclusion: Higher subclinical cardiovascular risk, as estimated by SCORE2, is significantly associated with increased DHR severity. Analysis of these findings suggests that vascular reserve may modulate the clinical presentation of drug-induced allergic reactions, potentially aiding in clinical risk stratification.

title: Development and evaluation of X-ray lithophanes as test objects for interventional procedure simulation.
authorString: Saija C, Dietrich M, Facente F, Wei W, Littlefield C, Kryshchuk M, Aparicio-Villar P, Boudjatit N, Pontiki A, Housden RJ, Sejor E, Rhode K, Berthet-Rayne P.
abstractText:
Background

In the growing field of interventional radiology, emerging technologies implement the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to help tackle growing demands for treatment. Due to the anatomical differences in animals, volunteers offer the most realistic training and testing scenario, however safety considerations restrict rapid prototyping of these new technologies. Simulators have been a key facilitator in the testing of new technologies among numerous medical engineering studies, but often lack the realism to reliably test AI.

Purpose

This proof-of-concept study presents methods to create or enhance hyper-realistic radiographic simulators that can effectively function with a medical-grade AI software.

Methods

Iron-filled plastic was used to three-dimensionally (3D) print a series of blocks of heights up to 30 mm. By analyzing the intensities generated by different thicknesses of plastic, anonymous fluoroscopic images were turned into height maps (lithophanes) and 3D-printed. A static scene from transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) was then 3D-printed and imaged with different presets using two different x-ray systems for mathematical analysis. Lithophanes were then used as a radiographic background to experimental and commercial interventional simulators to test Caranx Medical's TAVIPILOT AI. Finally, fluoroscopies from 5 3D-printed lithophanes were mixed with 5 real images and presented to 5 expert volunteers to establish their realism in a structured survey.

Results

The 3D-printed x-ray lithophanes test-plates' radiographic appearance was rated as "Adequate" to "Good" across all fields of the survey, with participants praising their realism. The test-plate was able to reliably recreate the TAVI scene in different x-ray systems, with joint-histogram correlation coefficients above 0.9, and global structural similarity above 0.8. The lithophanes were imaged as a standalone test plate and as a backing to dynamic TAVI interventional simulators; in both cases, TAVIPILOT AI responded to the simulator as if it was operating on a real anatomical image.

Conclusions

Lithophane plates present an easy-to-implement solution to recreate monoplane x-ray scenes, which can be deployed to test software at the point of care with minimal logistical, ethical, or safety concerns. This study opens the door for a new range of interventional simulators able to recreate human-like appearance to test AI, offering a non-exclusive alternative to patient volunteers and anonymous data.

title: Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy With Low Appendicular Muscle Mass Is Associated With Osteoporosis, Falls, and Fractures.
authorString: Zheng B, Zhang Y, Liang D, Shen X, Huang L, Zhao F, Yan S.
abstractText:
Introduction

Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) and low appendicular muscle mass (LAMM) may jointly contribute to adverse skeletal outcomes, but their combined effects remain unclear. We examined their associations with osteoporosis, falls, and fractures in patients with Type 2 diabetes.

Methods

We explored associations of diabetes and grip strength with skeletal outcomes using SHARE v8.0.0 (327 248 participants). The primary analysis used a cohort of patients with Type 2 diabetes from the First Affiliated Hospital of Fujian Medical University. LAMM was defined using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry-derived appendicular skeletal muscle mass index. Associations of clinically diagnosed DPN, LAMM, and their coexistence with osteoporosis, falls, and fractures were evaluated using logistic regression and Cox survival models. Exploratory serum antibody omics was performed.

Results

In SHARE, grip strength was inversely associated with all three outcomes. In the local cohort, coexisting DPN and LAMM were associated with higher odds of osteoporosis (OR 2.151, 95% CI 1.645-2.805), falls (OR 4.667, 95% CI 3.406-6.376), and fractures (OR 2.416, 95% CI 1.367-3.515; all p < 0.001). Cox analyses showed higher hazards of osteoporosis (HR 3.410, 95% CI 1.579-7.362; p = 0.002) and falls (HR 4.385, 95% CI 1.838-10.459; p < 0.001), but not fractures (HR 0.708, 95% CI 0.187-2.675; p = 0.611). Antibody omics suggested a reactivity profile involving endoplasmic reticulum protein processing and neurodegeneration-related pathways.

Conclusion

Coexisting DPN and LAMM were associated with higher odds of all three skeletal outcomes and higher longitudinal hazards of osteoporosis and falls, but not fractures. The exploratory omics findings require functional validation.

title: Machine Learning-Based Classification of Right and Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Premature Ventricular Contractions.
authorString: Botis M, Tsiachris D, Botis GG, Koumpanakis A, Bartsioka LI, Doundoulakis I, Kordalis A, Antoniou CK, Karanikola AE, Matsopoulos GK, Tsioufis K.

journal.title: Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc

abstractText:
Introduction

Idiopathic premature ventricular contractions (PVCs) commonly originate from the right and left ventricular outflow tracts (RVOT and LVOT). The surface 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) is commonly used to differentiate the anatomic site of origin prior to catheter ablation. Machine learning methods can further enhance diagnostic accuracy.

Materials and methods

In this study, 64 ECG-derived features, along with age and gender, were analyzed from 43 patients (65% males, median age 55.6, IQR 30 years), who underwent successful catheter ablation of outflow tract-originating idiopathic PVCs. The site of origin was depicted through 3-D electroanatomical mapping. A logistic regression model was trained to classify the site of origin as either RVOT or LVOT using repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation with five repeats. A model restricted to ECG features and four previously published ECG algorithms was evaluated for comparison.

Results

Across the 25 held-out partitions, the model achieved an accuracy of 0.817 ± 0.143, precision of 0.888 ± 0.122, recall of 0.824 ± 0.206, F1-score of 0.836 ± 0.139 and ROC-AUC of 0.917 ± 0.094. Using the pooled out-of-fold predictions, accuracy was 0.860 (95% CI 0.744-0.953) and ROC-AUC 0.910 (95% CI 0.800-0.987). Age was the most discriminative feature, with increasing values favoring LVOT origin. The ECG-only model achieved an ROC-AUC of 0.853 (95% CI 0.721-0.958; ΔAUC +0.057, p = 0.104).

Conclusions

These findings suggest that machine learning models, based on ECG parameters and demographic characteristics, can classify outflow tract ventricular arrhythmias, supporting their use in automated differentiation and pre-procedural planning.

title: Associations of sFlt-1 and PlGF levels with hematologic and biochemical parameters in normotensive pregnant women.
authorString: Kinugawa M, Kumasawa K, Nemoto K, Nakajima K, Ichinose M, Toshimitsu M, Sayama S, Iriyama T, Harada M, Hirota Y.
abstractText:
Objective

Preeclampsia (PE) is characterized by hypertension accompanied by hematologic and biochemical changes. In PE, these changes are linked to soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFlt-1) and placental growth factor (PlGF), but their relationships during normotensive pregnancy remain unclear. We aimed to investigate the associations of sFlt-1 and PlGF with routine hematologic and biochemical parameters in normotensive pregnancy.

Materials and methods

We analyzed 780 pregnant women who did not develop PE or superimposed PE by measuring sFlt-1 and PlGF at 18 + 0-21 + 6 weeks of gestation with same-day routine hematology/biochemistry results.

Results

Spearman's rank correlations showed weak but statistically significant associations between sFlt-1 and aspartate aminotransferase (AST; ρ = 0.19), alanine aminotransferase (ALT; ρ = 0.16), and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH; ρ = 0.15). In multivariable analyses, these associations remained independent of maternal characteristics.

Conclusion

Even within physiologic ranges, sFlt-1 may reflect subclinical hepatic or hemolysis-related responses, consistent with its pathogenic role in PE.

title: Direct Oral Anticoagulants Versus Vitamin K Antagonists for Atrial Fibrillation After Cardiac Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
authorString: Al-Harrasi A, Almutairi A, Alghazali RA, Alrefaei N, Rusheidi RSA, Zuhair SA, Alfailakawi AKEAEA, Zamzamy DA, Mousa HA, Elkasaby MH, Frishman WH, Aronow WS.
abstractText: Atrial fibrillation after cardiac surgery is common and is associated with stroke, prolonged hospitalization, and mortality; yet, the optimal oral anticoagulant in this setting remains uncertain. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) with vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) in adults requiring oral anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation after cardiac surgery. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception through August 2026 for randomized controlled trials. The primary outcome was any bleeding; secondary outcomes were stroke or transient ischemic attack, systemic embolism, major bleeding, intracranial hemorrhage, reoperation, and length of hospital stay. Odds ratios (ORs) and mean differences (MDs) were pooled with random-effects models, risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, and certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE. Five randomized trials including 302 patients (153 DOACs and 149 warfarin) were included; rivaroxaban was tested in 3 trials, and apixaban and dabigatran in 1 trial each. Any bleeding did not differ significantly between DOACs and VKAs (9.2% vs 8.1%; OR, 1.24; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.39-3.99).

title: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Patients With Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Bacha Z, Shahbaz H, Yasir A, Afridi H, Rashad A, Muneer H, Gohar F, Khan M, Chaudhary MA, Rehman A, Abid M, Afridi MS, Naqvi M, Khan FM, Rahat S, Rafi F, Hassanabad AF.
abstractText: Concomitant coronary artery disease affects 40-75% of patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Three recent randomized trials yielded conflicting findings: NOTION-3 demonstrated reduced composite events with pre-TAVI percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), whereas PRO-TAVI showed non-inferiority of PCI deferral with less bleeding; neither demonstrated mortality benefit. No previous meta-analysis combined all 3 trials with observational evidence, applied design-stratified GRADE certainty, or explored cardiovascular mortality heterogeneity. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 studies (3 randomized trials, 13 observational cohorts; 8,207 patients). Ten prespecified outcomes were pooled using Mantel-Haenszel random-effects risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs); 30-day all-cause mortality was primary. GRADE certainty was assessed separately for randomized and observational evidence. Prespecified design-based subgroup and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed. Pre-TAVI PCI was not associated with significant differences in 30-day all-cause mortality (RR 1.26, 95% CI 0.90-1.77; I2 = 32%) or 1-year mortality (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.87-1.15; I2 = 0%). Major bleeding (RR 1.19, 95% CI 0.98-1.44) and major vascular complications (RR 1.48, 95% CI 0.95-2.30) showed borderline non-significant trends favoring PCI deferral (both I2 = 0%). Excluding Griese et al. 2014, the principal driver of harm and heterogeneity, reduced cardiovascular mortality heterogeneity (RR 0.91; I2 = 24%). No significant differences occurred in stroke, myocardial infarction, acute kidney injury, pacemaker implantation, or rehospitalization. Routine pre-TAVI PCI confers no mortality benefit and may increase bleeding and vascular complications; PCI should be individualized according to coronary complexity, lesion significance, and bleeding risk.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Recaticimab in Patients With Dyslipidemia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials With GRADE Assessment.
authorString: Talkhan A, Abou Elezz AM, Borham NE, Abbas AN, Saeed HT, Taman L, Shehata MM, Elsharkawy MM, Elkasaby MH, Frishman WH, Aronow WS.
abstractText: Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is the principal target for preventing atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, yet many patients do not reach treatment goals with statins, and established proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) antibodies require injections every 2-4 weeks. Recaticimab is a humanized anti-PCSK9 monoclonal antibody designed for dosing intervals of up to 12 weeks. We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library up to March 3, 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing recaticimab with placebo in adults with dyslipidemia. Four double-blind trials (1657 randomized participants) were included. At week 12, recaticimab reduced LDL-C by 47.31 percentage points relative to placebo (95% confidence interval [CI], -49.87 to -44.75; I2 = 0%), with similar reductions for 150 mg every 4 weeks (-49.63), 300 mg every 8 weeks (-49.43), and 450 mg every 12 weeks (-45.50) (P for subgroup difference = 0.29). Recaticimab also reduced non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (-45.17), apolipoprotein B (-42.31), lipoprotein(a) (-31.06), the total cholesterol/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (-36.94), and the apolipoprotein B/apolipoprotein A1 ratio (-45.28), whereas the change in triglycerides was not significant (-10.05; 95% CI, -20.18 to 0.08).

title: Aspirin Use for the Prevention of Preeclampsia, an Evidence-Based Review.
authorString: Patel D, Kallash M, Frishman WH.
abstractText: Preeclampsia is a multisystem hypertensive disorder of pregnancy that is defined by new-onset hypertension after 20 weeks of gestation along with proteinuria or evidence of end-organ dysfunction. Affecting 2-8% of pregnancies worldwide, preeclampsia remains a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality. This disorder originates secondary to defective placentation during the first trimester, causing incomplete remodeling of the uterine spiral arteries, resulting in placental hypoperfusion, oxidative stress, and the release of anti-angiogenic factors into the maternal circulation. This pathophysiology provided researchers a rationale for the use of low-dose aspirin as a preventive strategy for preeclampsia. Early studies investigated low-dose aspirin initiated at variable gestational ages and failed to show significant reductions in the incidence of preeclampsia. However, over the years, multiple meta-analyses studying aspirin use for preeclampsia prevention revealed a consistent decrease in the incidence of preeclampsia with the use of low-dose aspirin initiated at or before 16 weeks of gestation, with the efficacy being largely dependent on the time of initiation. In 2017, a randomized controlled trial demonstrated a statistically and clinically significant reduction in the incidence of preeclampsia leading to preterm delivery with aspirin initiated before 16 weeks gestation in women identified as high risk by first-trimester algorithm-based screening. Based on the strong evidence in support of aspirin use for preeclampsia prevention, current guidelines recommend initiation of aspirin 81 mg after 12 weeks and ideally before 16 weeks for all pregnant women at increased risk for preeclampsia.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence for Detecting ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction on 12-Lead Electrocardiograms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Mohammadi A, Karimian A, Shokri K, Amani-Beni R, Darouei B, Namazi A, Gavili N, Adeel MY, Frishman WH, Aronow WS.
abstractText: Artificial intelligence (AI) may improve electrocardiographic detection of ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), but available studies address distinct diagnostic questions. We systematically reviewed studies evaluating AI-based STEMI detection from 12-lead electrocardiograms and separately synthesized AI performance against a clinical reference standard, AI and clinician performance against a clinical reference, and AI agreement with physician electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from January 2010 through March 10, 2025. Bivariate random-effects models generated pooled sensitivity, specificity, and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (AUC). Twenty-six studies comprising 539,876 ECGs were included. In 20 studies comparing AI with a clinical reference standard, pooled sensitivity was 0.95 (95% confidence interval, 0.91-0.97), specificity 0.95 (0.90-0.98), AUC 0.98 (0.97-0.99), positive likelihood ratio 19.2 (9.3-39.5), and negative likelihood ratio 0.05 (0.03-0.10). In 8 studies reporting both AI and clinician performance against a clinical reference, separate syntheses showed sensitivity of 0.91 (0.86-0.94) for AI versus 0.78 (0.69-0.85) for clinicians, specificity of 0.91 (0.82-0.96) for both, and AUCs of 0.95 and 0.90, respectively. In 7 studies using physician ECG interpretation as the comparator, AI sensitivity was 0.85 (0.70-0.94), specificity 0.99 (0.96-1.00), and AUC 0.98 (0.96-0.99). Sensitivity analyses excluding case-control designs, influential studies, and restricting analyses to deep learning models or raw waveform ECGs produced similar findings.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence for Detecting ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction on 12-Lead Electrocardiograms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Abbas M, Karimian A, Shokri K, Amani-Beni R, Darouei B, Namazi A, Gavili N, Adeel MY, Frishman WH, Aronow WS.
abstractText: Artificial intelligence (AI) may improve electrocardiographic detection of ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), but available studies address distinct diagnostic questions. title: Artificial Intelligence Applied to Echocardiography for Detection of Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction and Elevated Filling Pressures: A Diagnostic Test Accuracy Meta-Analysis.
authorString: A Al-Harbi F, Alawaji HH, Alhabdan HS, Alsultan NS, Alrebdi DA, AlMutairi OH, Alharbi FM, Alosail AF.
abstractText: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) accounts for nearly half of heart failure cases and remains difficult to diagnose non-invasively. Artificial intelligence (AI) applied to echocardiography may improve detection, but its aggregate diagnostic accuracy has not been quantified. We performed a diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis of AI-enabled echocardiography for identifying HFpEF, elevated left ventricular filling pressure, or diastolic dysfunction. MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to June 2026. Studies reporting the accuracy of AI models applied to echocardiography against invasive, guideline-adjudicated, or ASE/EACVI reference standards were included. Sensitivity and specificity were pooled using a bivariate random-effects (Reitsma) model, with a summary receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, diagnostic odds ratio, and likelihood ratios. Risk of bias was assessed with QUADAS-2. Eight studies (2770 participants; 1317 [47.5%] with the target condition) were included. Pooled sensitivity was 84.0% (95% CI: 73.0-91.0%) and specificity 83.0% (95% CI: 73.0-89.0%), with an area under the summary ROC curve of 0.875 (95% CI: 0.791-0.930). The diagnostic odds ratio was 24.73 (95% CI: 18.46-33.12); positive and negative likelihood ratios were 4.84 and 0.20. Heterogeneity was high. Performance did not differ by AI architecture but varied significantly by reference standard. No small-study effects were detected. AI-enabled echocardiography shows good pooled accuracy for detecting HFpEF and elevated filling pressures, supporting its diagnostic potential. High heterogeneity and reference-standard dependence warrant larger, prospectively validated studies before routine clinical adoption.

title: Biointerface-Customized Nanomodulators Induce Mitochondria-Specific Dysfunction to Reprogram Tumor Immunity.
authorString: Zhen X, Chen Y, Li L, Zhang T, Li M, Wang R, Sun Y, Li J, Ma S, Zhou R, Wang S, Xie X.
abstractText: Tumor mitochondria regulate cancer progression and immune evasion. However, current therapeutic strategies lack the subcellular precision required to selectively induce immune-beneficial mitochondrial dysfunction without causing systemic toxicity. Here, we report a biointerface-customized nanomodulator (C/C-HP@M2M-TPP), developed through a biointerface-engineered strategy (BES), that integrates sequential targeting and controlled activation to induce mitochondria-specific dysfunction and reprogram tumor immunity. Through a customized biointerface coating, the nanomodulators achieve preferential tumor accumulation and mitochondria-directed subcellular localization. Co-delivered calcium ion donors and efflux inhibitors cooperatively induce mitochondrial ion interference and dysfunction, which is further amplified by photothermal activation. This localized mitochondrial interference promotes immunogenic cell death and robust antitumor immune activation, resulting in potent tumor regression in mice. Integrated single-cell transcriptomic and proteomic analyses further identify mitochondrial disruption as a key mechanistic driver of tumor immune reprogramming. This work establishes biointerface-customized nanomodulation as a subcellular immunomodulatory therapeutic strategy in vivo.

title: Diagnostic drivers of psychiatric inpatient bed use in Ireland 2013-2023: implications for service planning.
authorString: Healy C, Daly A, Lynn E, O'Connor K, Clifford M, Keating D, Ramsay H, Kelleher I.
abstractText: Psychiatric inpatient care is a high-resource component of mental health systems. Understanding the diagnoses driving inpatient care is essential for evidence-based service planning. This study describes psychiatric inpatient bed use in Ireland from 2013 to 2023 by diagnosis, sex, and age group. National descriptive analyses using aggregated data from the National Psychiatric Inpatient Reporting System, covering acute inpatient admissions in Ireland. The outcome was total number of inpatient bed days, categorised by ICD-10 diagnostic group. Primary analyses focused on public services, with private services reported separately. We additionally report on child and adolescent mental health services (CAMHS), adult services, and sex-stratified results. Between 2013 and 2023, there were k=3,993,628 public and k=1,879,877 private inpatient bed days. In public services, schizophrenia spectrum disorders accounted for 41.9% of bed days (k=1,673,529), more than twice as many as the next most prevalent diagnosis. Men accounted for 51.2% of acute public bed days. In private adult services, depressive disorders accounted for the largest proportion of bed days (28.5%, k=513,166). In public and private CAMHS, eating disorders accounted for the largest proportion of bed days (25.6%, k=46,850 and 24.4%, k=18,775), respectively. This national analysis demonstrates that schizophrenia spectrum disorders represent, by far, the largest diagnostic group, accounting for 42% of public acute psychiatric inpatient beds days, highlighting the sustained, intensive service demands associated with these disorders. These data provide a clear empirical basis for future service planning, highlighting where targeted enhancements to community-based care could most effectively reduce the need for hospitalisation.

title: Cardiac tamponade due to a displaced rib fracture: a case report.
authorString: Saji AP, Dubois AS, Bailey G, Diaz A, Tolani AA, Macys A, Alfa-Wali M.
abstractText: Pericardial effusion causing cardiac tamponade is uncommon following blunt traumatic injury. We report the case of a 78-year-old woman who, following a road traffic collision, developed cardiac tamponade secondary to a displaced rib fracture. This case also demonstrates the value of repeated extended focused assessment with sonography in trauma (eFAST). Close monitoring of patients who are initially hemodynamically stable, in the context of their mechanism of injury, is essential in trauma care to reduce the morbidity and mortality that can occur without prompt management.

title: Intravenous Tenecteplase for Acute Ischemic Stroke in Patients With Recent or Concurrent Non-ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Narrative Review.
authorString: Sharma DN, Shah RK, Agrawal S, Bharagava S, Frishman WH, Aronow WS.
abstractText: Patients presenting with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) alongside a recent or concurrent non-ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) occupy one of the least evidence-supported decision points in acute stroke care, excluded from every pivotal thrombolysis trial. The recent approval and guideline endorsement of tenecteplase-an agent separately licensed for myocardial infarction at twice the cerebral dose-adds a dimension the alteplase-derived literature does not address. This narrative review synthesizes the evidence on intravenous thrombolysis, specifically tenecteplase, in this setting and distinguishes infarct-related from treatment-related barriers to eligibility. Concomitant NSTEMI complicates approximately 1.6% of acute ischemic stroke hospitalizations and carries an adjusted 3.6-fold increase in in-hospital mortality. The historical contraindication derives from mechanisms-myocardial hemorrhage with free-wall rupture, postinfarction pericarditis with hemopericardium, and left ventricular thrombus embolization-that scale with transmurality and are therefore largely ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction phenomena. Registry data from more than 40,000 thrombolyzed patients show no significant excess of thrombolysis-related complications with recent NSTEMI, and fatal ruptures cluster in subacute ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction; the excess mortality is of similar magnitude without thrombolysis, marking a sicker patient rather than a more dangerous drug.

title: Epicardial adipose tissue volumes improve prediction of myocardial infarction in women on top of SCORE2, CACS and plaque burden: Long-term follow-up of 25,000 individuals.
authorString: Molnar D, Wang C, Björnson E, Adiels M, Carlhäll CJ, Shahim B, Kullberg J, Ostenfeld E, Söderberg S, Knuuti J, Bergström G.
abstractText: Increased epicardial adipose tissue volume (EATV) is a risk marker for future myocardial infarction (MI), but its value beyond SCORE2 (Systemic Coronary Risk Evaluation 2), the coronary artery calcium score (CACS) and the coronary artery segment involvement score (SIS) remains poorly studied. To determine the incremental value of EATV normalized to heart volume (EATVh) on top of SCORE2, CACS and SIS in predicting future MI. We studied associations between EATVh, SCORE2, CACS, SIS and the risk of MI in a general population cohort of 25,155 participants (age 50-64, 50.7% women). Sex-stratified multivariable Cox-regression estimated hazard ratios (HR) and ROC-analysis with variables dichotomized at their 75th percentile assessed incremental predictive value. A total of 304 MI (71 in women) occurred during follow-up (median: 7.8 years). In adjusted analysis, EATVh and SCORE2 were independently associated with MI in women, but only SIS and SCORE2 in men. The highest HR per EATVh IQR was found in women <55 years (1.89). ROC-analysis showed that adding EATVh to SCORE2, CACS and SIS improved MI prediction in women but not men (AUC: 0.681 vs. 0.667; p < 0.05 for both). EATVh provides independent, modest incremental information on the risk of future MI in women on top of CACS and SIS, but not in men. Further studies in more diverse population segments including younger and symptomatic individuals are warranted.

title: γ-Glutamyl Transferase as a Practical Predictor of Elevated Liver Stiffness in Heart Failure　- Findings From a Daily Clinical Setting.
authorString: Sugawara H, Tanaka M, Yano T, Yoshida K, Kimura Y, Matsui A, Higashiura Y, Matsumoto T, Nishisato K, Nishimura M, Yamamoto M, Ito H, Ogata H, Furuhashi M.

journal.title: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society

abstractText:
Background

Liver stiffness assessed by liver elastography has been reported as useful for predicting hepatic congestion and outcomes in patients with heart failure (HF). However, liver elastography is not widely available for patients with HF in routine clinical settings. We investigated whether simple biomarkers can predict elevation of liver stiffness.

Methods and results

In all, 52 hospitalized patients with HF were recruited to this study. The primary analysis examined the association between γ-glutamyl transferase (GGT) and liver stiffness in the overall study population. In multivariable linear regression analysis adjusted for age and sex, log-transformed GGT was independently associated with liver stiffness. This association remained significant in separate sensitivity analyses incorporating systolic and diastolic blood pressure, estimated glomerular filtration rate, N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide, ejection fraction, tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient, inferior vena cava diameter, inferior vena cava collapsibility index, and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor use. In exploratory analyses for the prediction of high liver stiffness (>7.1 kPa), the addition of GGT increased integrated discrimination improvement and improved the net reclassification index, whereas the change in the area under the curve was not statistically significant. Direct comparison between models including GGT and the Fibrosis-4 index did not show a significant difference.

Conclusions

GGT levels may provide a simple and clinically accessible signal associated with elevated liver stiffness in patients with HF and possible hepatic congestion.

title: Demystifying Imaging Patterns of Substance Abuse-Related Lung Injury (SARLI).
authorString: Sharma S, Davoudi D, Patsios D, McInnis M.

journal.title: Canadian Association of Radiologists journal = Journal l'Association canadienne des radiologistes

abstractText: Recreational substance abuse causes a broad spectrum of acute and chronic pulmonary injuries through inhalation and intravenous injection. Imaging findings often overlap with infection, pulmonary edema, and other inflammatory lung diseases, particularly when an exposure history is unavailable. This review discusses the mechanisms and characteristic CT imaging patterns of substance abuse-related lung injury (SARLI). Crack lung is an acute pulmonary toxicity syndrome occurring within 48 hours of crack cocaine inhalation and manifests as diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities with patchy consolidations, or a crazy-paving pattern related to pulmonary edema, diffuse alveolar damage, or alveolar hemorrhage. Cannabis smoking is associated with upper-lobe-predominant paraseptal emphysema, apical bullae, and airway inflammation. E-cigarette or vaping product use-associated lung injury is a diagnosis of exclusion and requires vaping exposure within 90 days prior to abnormal pulmonary imaging for establishing the diagnosis. It most commonly demonstrates an organizing pneumonia pattern, although diffuse alveolar damage and alveolar hemorrhage may occur. Intravenous injection of crushed oral medications can cause excipient lung disease, which has three distinct imaging patterns: diffuse centrilobular micronodules, high-attenuation perihilar and upper lobe predominant fibrotic opacities, and lower-lobe-predominant panlobular emphysema (Ritalin lung). It is often accompanied by right ventricular strain and pulmonary hypertension and can lead to sudden death and long-term deterioration of lung function. Additional complications of drug abuse include aspiration, lobar or bronchopneumonia, septic pulmonary emboli, and barotrauma. Recognition of SARLI patterns within the appropriate clinical and temporal context can help radiologists suggest the correct diagnosis and facilitate timely management.

title: Navigating complexity: current evidence and recommendations for management of selected, non-malignant pleural effusions.
authorString: Hagen C, Ingemi M, Feller-Kopman D, Howe J.
abstractText:
Introduction

Pleural effusions are common and carry substantial morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Management can be particularly challenging when effusions arising from systemic diseases such as congestive heart failure (CHF) or cirrhosis are refractory to medical management or when the effusion occurs due to disruption of the thoracic lymphatic system, as in chylothorax.

Areas covered

This review examines current approaches to the diagnosis and management of congestive heart failure-related effusions, hepatic hydrothorax, and chylothorax. In addition, we seek to identify areas for future investigation across all three conditions, particularly the evidence guiding invasive management such as thoracentesis, indwelling pleural catheters, and pleurodesis. To accomplish this, we conducted a literature search in PubMed between 1 August 2026 and 13 August 2026, using a combination of free-text keywords related to the listed effusions.

Expert opinion

If medical/conservative management of complicated pleural effusion fails, there are multiple treatment options for each of the discussed effusions, but no clear-cut superior option as the current literature is limited. Future studies will require multi-center and multi-disciplinary collaboration but will likely reveal that treatment should be based on an individual level, accounting for local expertise and incorporating patients' preferences.

title: Interval-based cycling for wheelchair users with spinal muscular atrophy: feasibility, tolerability, and exercise effects.
authorString: Frølich SV, Receveur N, Vissing J, Poulsen NS.
abstractText: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) often leads to wheelchair use and sedentary lifestyle. Previous exercise studies suggest that prolonged exercise may cause fatigue and limit feasibility. We assessed feasibility and tolerability of interval-based assisted cycling in wheelchair users with SMA and explored potential effects on symptoms, motor performance, and metabolic outcomes. In this exploratory self-controlled crossover study, 15 wheelchair users with SMA completed three test days separated by a control period and an 8-week home-based exercise intervention. Assessments included questionnaires on pain, constipation, fatigue, sleep quality, and quality of life, along with lung function, blood sampling, and cycle testing. Training consisted of 10 min of assisted interval cycling five times weekly. No clinically meaningful changes were observed in primary or secondary outcomes. Nevertheless, attendance was high (95%), no exercise-related dropouts occurred, and no systematic increase in fatigue was observed. During exercise testing, participants increased their heart rate by an average of 42 bpm, indicating cardiovascular engagement. Interval-based assisted cycling was feasible and well tolerated in wheelchair users with SMA without inducing excessive fatigue. Although no clinically meaningful group-level effects were observed, interval training enabled cardiovascular engagement despite severe motor impairments.

title: Comparison of cardiac magnetic resonance findings in idiopathipulmonary arterial hypertension and that associated with CHD.
authorString: Beyazal M, Keceli M, Dogan O, Pamuk U, Cetin II, Ece İ.
abstractText:
Background

To compare cardiac MRI findings between children diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension and those with pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with CHD, and to determine whether there are prognostic differences between these groups.

Methods

This prospective cross-sectional study included 40 paediatric patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension, who underwent standardised cardiac MRI evaluation. Key functional and flow parameters were analysed and compared between the two groups.

Results

There were no significant differences in right ventricular volume, mass, and function parameters, and right atrial volume index, or septal shift findings. However, left ventricular end-diastolic volume index, left ventricular end-systolic volume index, left ventricular ejection fraction, left ventricular mass index, and right-left ventricle volume ratios were significantly different between groups. A ventricular mass index ≥75% was more common in idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension patients.

Conclusion

Cardiac MRI-based assessment reveals meaningful differences in left ventricle volume and mass parameters between idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension and pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with CHD patients. These findings may aid in follow-up strategies for paediatric pulmonary arterial hypertension.

title: Beyond Blood Cultures and Echocardiography: Emerging Diagnostics for Infective Endocarditis.
authorString: Park H, Dhand A.
abstractText: Management of infective endocarditis (IE) is often confounded by the presence of prosthetic valves, transcatheter prostheses, and cardiovascular implantable electronic devices, as well as by changing epidemiologic risks and antimicrobial resistance patterns. For the diagnosis of IE, blood cultures and echocardiography remain foundational, but important gaps persist, particularly in culture-negative and prosthetic/device-associated infections. Contemporary diagnostic criteria and guidelines now support a multimodality approach incorporating molecular microbiology and advanced imaging. This review summarizes emerging technologies including broad-range 16S/18S/28S rRNA polymerase chain reaction and sequencing, fluorescence in situ hybridization coupled with sequencing, targeted and shotgun metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS), plasma microbial cell-free DNA, cardiac computed tomography, and 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron-emission tomography/computed tomography. We also examine the potential role of artificial intelligence in echocardiographic interpretation and of large language models in multimodal data integration. Current evidence suggests that tissue-based molecular testing generally provides greater microbiologic yield than valve culture in culture-negative IE, while blood-based mNGS and microbial cell-free DNA may extend pathogen detection after antibiotic exposure and reduce reliance on tissue-based diagnosis. However, heterogeneity in specimen handling, sequencing pipelines, contamination control, reporting thresholds, and clinical interpretation remains a major barrier to implementation. Future progress should move beyond pathogen detection toward rapid, reproducible, clinically actionable diagnosis that integrates organism identification, anatomic localization, disseminated disease, and personalized treatment. Prospective outcome trials, standardized workflows, cost-effectiveness studies, and multidisciplinary Endocarditis Team integration can help determine whether these technologies translate into better antimicrobial stewardship, procedural decision-making, and patient outcomes.

title: Variation in Pediatric Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Survival After In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: Development and Validation of a Survival Model for Risk-Standardized Survival Rates: An Analysis of the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization Registry.
authorString: Loaec M, Himebauch AS, Balcarcel D, Reilly JP, Feng R, Regan M, Thiagarajan R, Bembea MM, Lasa JJ, Kilbaugh TJ, Sutton RM, Morgan RW, ELSO Member Centers.
abstractText: To develop and internally validate a multivariable prediction model for survival to hospital discharge after pediatric extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) for in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA), and to use this model to derive risk-standardized survival rates (RSSRs) and quantify between-hospital variation in outcomes. Retrospective multicenter cohort study. Hospitals contributing to the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization (ELSO) registry between 2020 and 2023. Children (< 18 yr) treated with ECPR for IHCA. None. Eligible patients were identified from the ELSO Registry and split into derivation (N = 1060) and validation (N = 317) cohorts using a hospital-stratified split to preserve within-hospital clustering. Survival prediction models were derived using penalized logistic regression with the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator. A full-event model incorporating 14 routinely available clinical variables demonstrated fair discrimination (area under the curve, 0.728 in the derivation cohort and 0.678 in the validation cohort) and good calibration (observed-to-expected ratio, 0.995; Brier score, 0.222 in the validation cohort). This model was embedded in a multilevel logistic regression model to generate hospital-level RSSRs for centers reporting five or more ECPR cases. Between-hospital variation was quantified using the median odds ratio, which was 1.30 (95% CI, 1.11-1.93), indicating significant differences in survival likelihood between centers after adjusting for patient-level risk. In a large, international cohort of pediatric ECPR patients, we developed and internally validated a clinically interpretable model for survival to hospital discharge. The model performance as a discriminator likely limits its use as a standalone tool for clinical decision-making. However, strong internal calibration allowed for determination of hospital-level RSSRs, which revealed significant inter-hospital variability. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of developing a risk-adjustment model capable of estimating hospital-level RSSRs. Additional external validation and evaluation of residual case-mix differences are needed before such models can be used for benchmarking across pediatric ECPR centers.

title: Reappraising Bumetanide in Heart Failure: Pharmacology, Comparative Effectiveness, and Opportunities for Contemporary Use.
authorString: Landman S, Masha H, Fishkin T, Makaryus AN, Frishman WH, Aronow WS.
abstractText: Bumetanide is a valuable loop diuretic utilized in the management of heart failure and chronic kidney disease. Although it accounts for less than 5% of all outpatient loop diuretic prescriptions, its oral bioavailability is highly predictable and generally superior to furosemide, which constitutes over 90% of diuretic prescriptions. Bumetanide is longer-acting and more potent than furosemide; however, many physicians utilize bumetanide as a second-line diuretic when furosemide is ineffective or when intestinal edema limits drug absorption. This review summarizes the pharmacology of bumetanide, its clinical application in patients with heart failure with reduced or preserved ejection fraction, and the factors that contribute to its underutilization despite several pharmacokinetic advantages.

title: Cardiovascular Effects of Childhood Radiotherapy.
authorString: Khorasanchi A, Farris J, Choi T, Frishman WH, Aronow WS.
abstractText: Cardiovascular disease is an important, well-studied late effect of childhood cancer therapy that may manifest many years after treatment. Radiotherapy, particularly when the heart is exposed, has been associated with multiple cardiovascular complications, including heart failure, coronary artery disease, valvular disease, and arrhythmias. This review examines the cardiovascular effects of radiotherapy in childhood and adolescent cancer survivors, with a focus on the mechanisms of radiation-induced injury, major cardiovascular outcomes, factors influencing long-term risk, and advances in cardiac-sparing radiotherapy and surveillance. The literature indicates radiotherapy was associated with an increased long-term risk of cardiovascular disease. Cardiovascular risk was influenced by radiation dose and the volume and location of cardiac tissue exposed, as well as age at treatment, anthracycline exposure, and traditional cardiovascular risk factors. Modern radiation techniques, including intensity-modulated and proton therapy, have aimed to reduce cardiac exposure. However, long-term clinical outcome data for these approaches remain limited. These findings support long-term cardiovascular surveillance of childhood cancer survivors and emphasize the importance of minimizing cardiac radiation exposure and addressing modifiable cardiovascular risk factors. Improved assessment of radiation dose to specific cardiac structures may further enable individualized risk stratification and surveillance.

title: Emerging roles of microtubules in directional cardiomyocyte remodeling.
authorString: Scarborough EA, Uchida K, Prosser BL.
abstractText: Past research has long hinted at a connection between microtubules and the growth of the heart. Here, we highlight a new role for microtubules in directing cardiomyocyte hypertrophy by altering protein translation and intercellular adhesion and discuss how these findings illuminate open questions in cardiac remodeling.

title: Staple-line disruption of a short left-middle hepatic venous common trunk causing right atrial injury during extended left hepatectomy: A case report.
authorString: Nakahashi H, Takahashi K, Tatsuzawa M, Furuta T, Miyazaki Y, Shimomura O, Hashimoto S, Oda T.
abstractText: Injury to the inferior vena cava or the major hepatic veins is a life-threatening complication that can occur during hepatectomy. To prevent catastrophic outcomes, careful preoperative assessment of the venous anatomy, the selection of appropriate transection techniques, and advance coordination with cardiovascular surgical teams are essential. A 67-year-old male underwent an extended left hepatectomy with caudate lobectomy for intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma that had invaded the roots of the left and middle hepatic veins. The common trunk of these veins was divided using a vascular stapler, and pulsatile bleeding developed from the staple-line approximately 4 minutes after transection. Despite immediate attempts at hemostasis, the staple-line disruption progressed; the laceration was ultimately found to extend from the hepatic venous confluence into the right atrium, resulting in uncontrollable hemorrhage. Cardiopulmonary bypass was established immediately, and complete hemostasis was achieved with primary repair. The patient recovered without major complications and remains alive 1 year after surgery. An extremely short left-middle hepatic venous common trunk located in close proximity to the right atrium may represent a technically challenging configuration for hepatic vein transection. Recognizing such anatomy preoperatively may encourage surgeons to consider alternative transection techniques and to plan vascular control strategies in advance for unexpected major venous bleeding.

title: Isolated Obtuse Marginal Branch Occlusion Presenting as Recurrent Sinus Arrest without ST-segment Elevation.
authorString: Tanaka R.
abstractText: A 47-year-old man presented with dyspnea and presyncope. Initial electrocardiography showed sinus bradycardia without ST-segment elevation, whereas telemetry revealed recurrent sinus arrest with a maximum pause of 3.3 s. Emergency coronary angiography revealed total occlusion of the obtuse marginal branch. Although the sinoatrial node artery originated near the occlusion, intravascular ultrasound confirmed the preservation of blood flow. Immediate revascularization led to complete resolution of sinus arrest. This case suggests that isolated lateral wall ischemia may represent an unusual manifestation of the Bezold-Jarisch reflex without direct sinoatrial node artery involvement. Therefore, acute coronary syndrome should be considered in unexplained sinus node dysfunction, even in the absence of typical chest pain.

title: Environmental assessment of hemophilia therapies. Comment on: "Carbon footprint of direct oral anticoagulants in atrial fibrillation and venous thromboembolism".
authorString: López MR, Suárez MC.
abstractText: Not available.

title: Organ Donation-Reaching the Next Generation: To and Through High School.
authorString: Herrmann CS, Ters ME.
abstractText:
Introduction

Current transplant rates meet only 10% of the global demand, and the quintessential reason is the lack of donors. The same holds for blood donations, with the number of younger donors increasingly declining.

Objective

This project tested the hypothesis that awareness, knowledge, and comfort levels of blood, organ, and bone marrow (BM) donation are low among high school students but can be raised through education.

Methods

A pre-/post-comparative cohort study was conducted using a 59-item electronic questionnaire administered to students in grades 9, 10, and 11 in a single high school between November 2025 and January 2026 before and after a 10-minute presentation in high school classrooms.

Results

A total of 112 students participated (59% females, age 14-17). Awareness level (5-point scale from 1 (very aware) to 5 (not aware)) was moderate-high for organ and blood donation and moderate for BM (median (IQR) 2 (1-3), 2 (1-2) and 3 (2-4), respectively). Notable increases in knowledge pertained to the number of patients on the transplant list (from 55% pre to 83% post, P < .01), the number of organs that can be donated (from 14% to 22%, P < .01), and the volume of blood per blood donation (from 17% to 24%, P < .01). Comfort level (from 1 (very) to 5 (not at all)) was higher for deceased organ donation than for living organ donation and blood donation (median (IQR) 2 (1-3) vs. 3 (2-4) and 3 (3-4), P < .05) and increased for deceased organ and blood donation after the presentation (median (IQR) 1 (1-3) and 2 (1-3), respectively, P < .001 vs. pre).

Conclusions

Dedicated peer-to-peer initiatives can raise awareness, knowledge, and comfort levels for blood, organ, and BM donation among high schoolers.

title: Projected One-Year Benefit of Heart Failure Pharmacotherapy in Adults With a Fontan Circulation.
authorString: Van den Eynde J, Van Belle H, Troost E, De Meester P, Budts W, Van De Bruaene A.
