title: Acute and Chronic Cardiovascular and Neuromuscular Effects of Blood Flow Restriction Resistance Training in Older Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Norouzi K, Nobari H, Jamali Masoomi S, Saberisani R, Niyazi A, Mohammad Rahimi GR.
abstractText: Low-load blood flow restriction resistance training (BFR-RT) may offer a lower-load alternative to conventional resistance training for older adults, but its cardiovascular responses and neuromuscular benefits remain incompletely characterized. To synthesize the acute cardiovascular responses and chronic cardiovascular and neuromuscular effects of low-load BFR-RT in older adults. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and CINAHL were searched from inception to July 15, 2026. Randomized controlled trials, including parallel-group and crossover designs, comparing low-load BFR-RT with no-exercise/passive control or conventional non-BFR resistance training were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. Meta-analyses were performed using mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Twenty-seven studies were included. Acutely, BFR-RT increased systolic blood pressure versus no exercise (MD, 5.30 mmHg; 95% CI, 0.48 to 10.12) and increased diastolic blood pressure (MD, 5.23 mmHg) and mean arterial pressure (MD, 5.81 mmHg) versus conventional resistance training, while heart rate, stroke volume, and cardiac output were not significantly different. Chronically, resting cardiovascular and endothelial outcomes were largely unchanged. Versus no exercise, BFR-RT significantly improved knee-extension, leg-extension, and leg-press 1RM and quadriceps cross-sectional area. Comparisons with conventional resistance training were mixed and outcome-specific. Low-load BFR-RT improves selected neuromuscular outcomes in older adults, particularly relative to no exercise, while cardiovascular responses are comparator-dependent and chronic vascular effects appear largely neutral. These findings support cautious, individualized application rather than assumptions of cardiovascular superiority or equivalence to conventional resistance training.

title: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion Versus Oral Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation: A Comprehensive Evidence Synthesis.
authorString: Bashir Z, Rehman MA, Hamza M, Yang M, Butt MO, Bukhari S.
abstractText:
Background

Oral anticoagulation (OAC) remains the cornerstone of stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF) but is limited by bleeding risk. Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) devices offer an alternative; however, recent randomized trials have reported inconsistent efficacy compared with OAC.

Methods

We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing LAAO with OAC through April 1, 2026, using MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane CENTRAL. Eligible studies enrolled adults (≥18 years) with AF randomized to LAAO or OAC. Primary and secondary outcomes were pooled as risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Individual patient-level data (IPD) were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves for time-to-event sensitivity analyses.

Results

Six RCTs (n = 7,004; mean age 72 years; CHA2DS2‑VASc 3.9; HAS‑BLED 1.7; mean follow-up 38 months) were included. LAAO showed no significant difference in ischemic stroke (RR 1.20, 95% CI 0.82-1.76), major bleeding (RR 0.77, 95% CI 0.50-1.17), or all-cause mortality (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.82-1.13) compared with OAC. Hemorrhagic stroke risk was significantly lower with LAAO (RR 0.53, 95% CI 0.30-0.93). Reconstructed IPD demonstrated similar stroke and bleeding risks (HR 1.24 and 0.84, respectively) but lower all-cause mortality with LAAO (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.52-0.95).

Conclusion

LAAO provides comparable ischemic stroke prevention and major bleeding outcomes to OAC and reduces hemorrhagic stroke risk. Reconstructed IPD analyses suggest a possible mortality benefit that warrants further investigation. Future studies using contemporary devices and post-ablation populations are needed to refine patient selection and further characterize the comparative clinical outcomes of LAAO and OAC in AF patients.

title: Clinical pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic relationships between drug exposure and the QT/QTc interval: Protocol for a systematic review and quantitative synthesis.
authorString: Molana H, Esmaily H, Mohammadnezhad G.
abstractText: Drug-induced QT/QTc prolongation is a central component of cardiac safety assessment. Concentration-QT/QTc modelling uses measured or model-predicted systemic drug exposure to estimate the magnitude and uncertainty of effects on ventricular repolarisation and can support regulatory decision-making in early clinical development. However, the evidence is dispersed across dedicated thorough QT studies, early-phase studies, population pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic analyses, and secondary pooled analyses, with substantial variation in exposure metrics, electrocardiographic acquisition, heart-rate correction, model structure, assessment of active metabolites and delayed effects, and reporting of uncertainty. This protocol describes a systematic review of quantitative human concentration-QT/QTc evidence. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Google Scholar will be searched from inception without date or language restrictions. Original human studies will be eligible when drug or metabolite concentrations are measured or estimated from a pharmacokinetic model informed by study data and are quantitatively related to QT or QTc outcomes. Two reviewers will independently screen records, extract data, and assess methodological limitations. The primary estimands will be the concentration-QT/QTc drug-effect parameter and the predicted placebo-adjusted change from baseline in QTc at a clinically relevant exposure. Random-effects meta-analysis will be undertaken only within the same active moiety when analyte, endpoint, correction method, model estimand, and exposure scenario are sufficiently comparable; otherwise, structured synthesis without meta-analysis will be performed. Risk of bias will be assessed using design-appropriate tools where applicable, supplemented by a prespecified concentration-QT/QTc methodological framework. Certainty will be evaluated for coherent drug-specific bodies of evidence. This review will provide a transparent map of clinical concentration-QT/QTc methods and estimates and identify priorities for future cardiac safety studies. PROSPERO registration: CRD420261469142.

title: Community-engaged protocol for the modified B-SWELL program randomized control pilot trial.
authorString: Jones HJ, Helsabeck N, Bakas T, Kovacic MB, Christian L, White-Heisel R, Oglesby L, Williams KP.
abstractText: Midlife Black women experience disproportionately high rates of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Evidence supports the use of culturally tailored interventions and community engagement to reduce health disparities in this population. In response, the Midlife Black Women's Stress Reduction and Wellness program (B-SWELL) was co-developed with midlife Black women to address cardiovascular risks and promote healthier lifestyle behaviors. This study aims to: (1) Refine the B-SWELL program to enhance sustainability, update outcome metrics in alignment with American Heart Association guidelines, and integrate findings from a prior feasibility trial; and (2) Conduct a randomized controlled pilot trial of the modified B-SWELL program to assess trends in primary and secondary outcomes and explore the preferences of midlife Black women participating in clinical research. Program refinements were guided by a community-engaged approach. The randomized controlled pilot trial compares the modified B-SWELL intervention with an attention control condition. Midlife Black women from the community will be recruited for participation. The primary outcome is cardiovascular health; secondary outcomes include depressive symptoms, unhealthy days, sleep quality, perceived general health, and symptom burden. Objectives 1 and 2 have been completed. Although the final sample did not reach the target of 64 participants, five cohorts, each comprised of an intervention group and an attention control group, completed the trial with only 9% attrition. The B-SWELL modifications highlight the value of culturally tailored, community-engaged approaches in addressing persistent cardiovascular health disparities among midlife Black women. Clinicaltrials.gov Registration Number: NCT06707636.

title: PROlonged posterior PERicardial chest tube treatment to reduce rates of postoperative atrial fibrillation following cardiac surgery (PROPER trial): Rationale and design of a prospective, multinational, randomized clinical trial.
authorString: Johannesson E, Thelaus L, Larsson M, Teurneau-Hermansson K, Ede J, Forsberg A, Gudbjartsson T, Jeppsson A, Møller CH, Wahba A, Grinnemo KH, Hansson EC, Holmdahl AJ, Krogstad LEM, Riber L, Sjögren J, Nozohoor S, Mörtsell D, Zindovic I.
abstractText: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is the most common complication after cardiac surgery and is associated with increased morbidity and prolonged hospitalization. Accumulation of pericardial blood after surgery triggers a localized inflammatory response that has been identified as a contributing factor in POAF development. The PROPER trial (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06800781) is a prospective, multinational, randomized, controlled clinical trial designed to determine whether evacuation of pericardial blood through prolonged drainage using a posterior pericardial chest tube reduces the incidence of POAF following elective cardiac surgery. In addition to routine surveillance, patients will be monitored using a wearable electrocardiographic patch monitor. Patients undergoing non-emergent, first-time coronary bypass grafting, aortic valve replacement, aortic surgery without circulatory arrest, or a combination of these procedures, are randomized 1:1 to either receive intraoperative placement of a posterior pericardial chest tube or standard care. A total of 624 patients will be enrolled across eight Nordic cardiac surgery centers. The primary endpoint is atrial fibrillation (AF) recorded within seven days after surgery. Secondary endpoints include AF recurrence, hospitalization due to bleeding or ischemic stroke, and all-cause mortality. Patients will be followed for five years. If effective, posterior pericardial drainage represents a readily available, low-risk strategy with the potential for rapid and broad adoption in clinical practice.

title: Rationale for Early Discontinuation of Aspirin After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: Design of the SOLOTAVI Randomized Trial.
authorString: Beygui F, Caussin C, Marlière S, Bonnet G, Durand E, Lhermusier T, Morelle JF, Delépine S, Souteyrand G, Ghostine S, Van Belle E, Barthélémy O, Akodad M, Cayla G, Chamandi C, Chemouni F, Parienti JJ, Bouleti C, Eltchaninoff H, SOLOTAVI Investigators.
abstractText:
Background

Trans-aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become the first line treatment of aortic stenosis, a condition predominantly affecting elderly patients. In absence of a specific indication for antithrombotic therapy, lifetime aspirin is recommended after TAVI while it may be discontinued 3 months after bioprosthetic surgical valve replacement. Primary prevention, using aspirin compared to placebo among elderly patients is associated with an increased risk of major bleeding and no reduction rates of thrombotic events. Hence, there is a gap of knowledge on whether aspirin should be continued >3 months after TAVI.

Study design

SOLOTAVI is a multicenter, open label, blinded endpoint assessment, 1:1 randomized, non-inferiority trial comparing aspirin discontinuation 3 months after TAVI (experimental) to long-term therapy (control). Adult patients with successful transfemoral TAVI for symptomatic aortic stenosis and no indication or contraindication for long-term antithrombotic therapy will be enrolled. Randomization is stratified on center and valve type. The primary endpoint is the 12-month composite of all cause death, myocardial infarction, stroke, and non-procedure-related major or disabling bleeding. A hierarchical analysis is performed for the primary and 3 principal secondary endpoints. The sample size is computed for demonstrating the non-inferiority of the experimental strategy compared with the control strategy, with a conservative non-inferiority margin of 6.5%. A total of 1400 patients will be enrolled.

Conclusions

The SOLOTAVI trial will assess the non-inferiority of a 3-month duration of aspirin compared to the long-term therapy after successful transfemoral TAVI in terms of thrombotic and bleeding events. NCT06518317 clinicaltrials.org.

title: Left Bundle-Branch Area Pacing vs Right Ventricular Pacing for Atrioventricular Block and Preserved Left Ventricular Function: The LEAP-Block Randomized Clinical Trial.
authorString: Li X, Wang H, Zhang W, You L, Qiu C, Jia F, Liu Z, Li X, Wang R, Chen T, Lin W, Ren M, Cheng K, Peng H, Zhou J, Yang H, Wu Y, Zhu H, Wang Z, He C, Sun Z, Chu S, Wang Y, Li W, Zhao Y, Gold MR, Ellenbogen KA, Yao Y, Fan X, LEAP-Block Investigators.
abstractText:
Importance

For patients with atrioventricular block requiring high-burden ventricular pacing, the optimal pacing strategy to reduce heart failure (HF) and all-cause mortality remains uncertain. Robust comparative evidence on the clinical outcomes of left bundle-branch area pacing (LBBAP) vs right ventricular pacing (RVP) in this population is needed.

Objective

To compare 24-month clinical outcomes of LBBAP vs RVP in patients with atrioventricular block and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF; ≥50%).

Design, setting, and participants

The LEAP-Block study was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, controlled, superiority trial conducted across 14 Chinese hospitals from January 2021 to August 2025, with last follow-up on June 3, 2025. Of 551 patients with LVEF 50% or greater requiring ventricular pacing who underwent eligibility assessment, 499 with anticipated ventricular pacing greater than 40% were randomized.

Interventions

Patients were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to LBBAP (n = 249) or RVP (n = 250).

Main outcomes and measures

The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, HF events, or upgrade to biventricular pacing at 24 months. Secondary end points included pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and device-related complications.

Results

The primary analysis included 482 patients (LBBAP, n = 242; RVP, n = 240; mean age, 67 years; 46% female). Acute procedure success was comparable between the 2 groups (LBBAP, 237/242 [97.9%] vs RVP, 239/240 [99.6%]; P = .22), with left bundle-branch capture confirmed in 188 of 236 patients (79.7%). LBBAP significantly reduced the primary end point vs RVP (2.4% vs 12.5%, respectively; absolute risk difference, -10.1% [95% CI, -16.8% to -3.4%]; P = .003). Among secondary outcomes, the LBBAP group had fewer HF events (3.4% vs 11.3%; -7.9% [95% CI, -13.0% to -2.8%]). No significant differences were observed in all-cause death, biventricular pacing upgrade, device-related complications, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. The 24-month Kaplan-Meier estimated cumulative incidence of the primary end point was 5.0% for LBBAP vs 13.2% for RVP (hazard ratio, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.19 to 0.73]; P = .004). LBBAP superiority was consistent across all prespecified subgroups.

Conclusions and relevance

Among patients with atrioventricular block and preserved LVEF requiring high-burden ventricular pacing, LBBAP was superior to RVP in reducing the risk of the composite end point of all-cause death, HF events, or upgrade to biventricular pacing at 24 months.

Trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04730921.

title: Roles of one-carbon metabolism, folate and riboflavin in blood pressure: Can a precision nutrition approach reduce the risk of hypertension?
authorString: McNulty H.
abstractText: Folate, along with the metabolically-related B vitamins (B12, B6 and riboflavin), play essential roles in human health throughout life. Notably, recent UK Biobank evidence implicates folate deficiency in hypertension, the major risk factor contributing to mortality worldwide. An estimated 15% of pregnancies are affected by hypertension, which contributes to serious adverse maternal and offspring outcomes, a greater risk of stroke later in life in the mother and long-term disease risk in the child. Clinical and genome-wide association studies link the C677T polymorphism in the gene encoding the folate-metabolizing enzyme methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) with an increased risk of hypertension. Riboflavin (as flavin adenine dinucleotide; FAD) is required as a cofactor for MTHFR, and randomized trials show that intervention with riboflavin lowers blood pressure, specifically in individuals with the MTHFR 677TT genotype, independently of antihypertensive medications. The health implications of this gene-nutrient interaction are important, especially for populations worldwide with the highest frequencies of the variant TT genotype in MTHFR, including Guatemala (up to 66%), Mexico (32-44%), and Northern China (24%). Further investigation is required to elucidate the mechanisms linking folate-mediated one-carbon metabolism with blood pressure and how riboflavin alleviates the excess genetic risk of hypertension in affected individuals. Riboflavin deficiency is highly prevalent worldwide, particularly in women, but is typically overlooked in health and research settings. This review highlights the roles of folate and riboflavin in blood pressure and the opportunity for a precision nutrition approach to reduce hypertension in at-risk individuals by addressing riboflavin deficiency and thus optimizing folate metabolism.

title: Cardiac Electrophysiological Impact of Sodium Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors: A Comprehensive Review.
authorString: Ashok V, Lim VG, Rahim SMZ, Sandhu H, Dodd MS, Ng GA, Renshaw D, Maddock H, Osman F.
abstractText: SGLT2i (sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors) reduce heart failure hospitalizations, cardiovascular death, and certain arrhythmic events beyond glycemic control. However, their specific effects on cardiac autonomic function and arrhythmogenesis, as well as the potential involvement of microRNAs in mediating these benefits, remain incompletely understood. This review synthesizes clinical and preclinical evidence on the impact of SGLT2i on cardiac autonomic regulation and arrhythmias, emphasizing the interplay between SGLT2i, microRNA expression, and cardiovascular risk. We conducted a comprehensive literature search for clinical trials, meta-analyses, observational studies, and preclinical investigations. Outcomes included heart rate variability, heart rate turbulence, atrial/ventricular arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death. Studies examining microRNA profiles associated with SGLT2i treatment and their links to cardiac fibrosis, inflammation, and arrhythmogenic substrates were analyzed in depth. Clinical evidence indicates that SGLT2i improve cardiac autonomic balance by reducing sympathetic overactivity and enhancing parasympathetic tone in patients with type 2 diabetes and cardiac autonomic neuropathy. Meta-analyses and post hoc data from cardiovascular outcome trials suggest a modest but consistent reduction in atrial fibrillation/flutter and, in some cohorts, sudden cardiac death, potentially reflecting sympathoinhibition, improved hemodynamics, and modulation of myocardial ion homeostasis. Preclinical studies support anti-arrhythmic properties through sodium-hydrogen exchanger inhibition, late sodium current suppression, and metabolic shift towards ketone utilization. SGLT2i modulate several key microRNAs implicated in heart failure and arrhythmic risk, including miR-21, miR-29, miR-30, miR-34a, and miR-92, which may partly underlie the attenuation of arrhythmogenic substrates and improved autonomic regulation. SGLT2i favorably affect cardiac autonomic function and reduce the burden of certain arrhythmias, potentially through modulation of disease-associated microRNAs. Integrating clinical autonomic outcomes with microRNA profiling provides mechanistic insights into their cardioprotective actions. Dedicated trials are warranted to clarify causality, dose-dependency, and the therapeutic potential of microRNA-SGLT2i interactions for arrhythmia prevention and management in high-risk populations.

title: Glutaminolysis Shapes Cardiac Resilience to Stress via Mitochondrial Glutathione.
authorString: Wang X, Zhou J, Bai H, Wei Z, Su L, Xing C, Wu G, Li M, An J, Zhang P, Zhang Y, Ding S, Zhang X, Ren J, Gao F, Li J.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiac reserve is a strong predictor of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, yet the metabolic mechanisms that enable the heart to mount an adaptive response to stress remain poorly understood. In this study, we sought to dissect the specific role of glutaminolysis, a key anaplerotic and redox-supporting pathway, in regulating cardiac reserve.

Methods

Cardiac reserve was assessed by echocardiography under β-adrenergic stimulation in mice with cardiomyocyte-specific deletion of glutaminase and in wild-type controls. Stable isotope tracing with [U-13C] glutamine was performed in Langendorff-perfused hearts. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial of acute glutamine supplementation in healthy volunteers was conducted to evaluate translational relevance (ChiCTR2400082676).

Results

During acute stress, such as exercise or β-adrenergic stimulation, glutaminolysis was rapidly mobilized to supply mitochondrial glutathione, preserving mitochondrial redox homeostasis and sustaining cardiac contractile reserve. Mice with cardiomyocyte-specific deletion of glutaminase exhibited marked impairments in both contractile reserve and exercise capacity, accompanied by a failure to elevate mitochondrial glutathione and consequent mitochondrial oxidative stress. Chronic exercise training upregulated cardiac glutaminase expression and expanded the mitochondrial glutathione pool, linking this adaptive mechanism to training-induced improvements in cardiac reserve. In humans, acute oral glutamine supplementation enhanced cardiac reserve, as assessed by exercise stress echocardiography, in a placebo-controlled crossover design.

Conclusions

These findings reveal a novel metabolic paradigm in which glutaminolysis functions as a dynamic pathway supporting mitochondrial health and cardiac resilience, and highlight glutamine supplementation as a potential therapeutic strategy to enhance cardiac reserve.

title: Perceived Ratings of AI-Generated and Expert-Reviewed vs Clinician-Developed Virtual Cardiology Patient Scenarios Among Medical Students: Randomized Controlled Study.
authorString: Bantidos MG, Dafli E, Karagiannidis E, Fyntanidou B, Gilou S, Nasoufidou A, Bamidis P.
abstractText: Virtual patients (VPs) are widely used in medical education, but creating high-quality cases requires clinical expertise, iterative revision, and alignment with educational objectives. Generative AI may support VP authoring, but direct comparisons between AI-generated and clinician-developed cases delivered within the same educational setting remain limited. This study aimed to compare medical students' learner-perceived ratings of 1 AI-generated, expert-reviewed virtual cardiology patient scenario with those of 1 clinician-developed virtual cardiology patient scenario delivered through the same mobile platform. A randomized, participant-blinded 2-arm controlled study was conducted in October 2025 during scheduled fifth-year emergency medicine course sessions. Eligible participants were fifth-year medical students who had completed the cardiology course. Students were assigned 1:1 to complete either a clinician-developed VP (CD-VP; n=64) or a ChatGPT-generated VP (GPT-VP; n=67). Both scenarios followed a shared acute coronary syndrome blueprint and were delivered through the same mobile-optimized app (mobile VPs app [MobiViP]) with identical interface structure and branching logic. The GPT-VP was generated using GPT-5 and refined through iterative follow-up prompting under expert review; direct manual rewriting was prohibited. After completion, students completed a mandatory 19-item questionnaire covering realism and validity, cognitive load, self-reported learning and reflection, and engagement and satisfaction. Analyses included reliability testing, 1-sample tests against a neutral midpoint, Mann-Whitney U tests, and Spearman correlations. Full scenario content and development details are provided as multimedia appendices. A total of 131 complete questionnaires were analyzed, with no item-level missing data. Mean subscale scores in the CD-VP group were 3.81 (SD 0.64) for realism and validity, 3.67 (SD 0.74) for cognitive load, 3.64 (SD 0.73) for self-reported learning and reflection, and 4.16 (SD 0.64) for engagement and satisfaction; corresponding GPT-VP scores were 4.11 (SD 0.56), 3.03 (SD 0.76), 3.86 (SD 0.77), and 4.28 (SD 0.58), respectively. Compared with the CD-VP, the GPT-VP received higher ratings for realism and validity (Mann-Whitney U=1503.0; P=.003) and lower cognitive load ratings, indicating a lower perceived burden (Mann-Whitney U=1070.5; P<.001). Self-reported learning and reflection showed a marginal difference between groups, with a higher rating for the GPT-VP (Mann-Whitney U=1719.0; P=.05), whereas engagement and satisfaction did not differ significantly (Mann-Whitney U=1922.5; P=.31). Internal consistency was acceptable to good for most subscales, although internal consistency for the realism and validity subscale in the GPT-VP group was moderate (Cronbach α=0.67). In this single-center randomized study, 1 AI-generated, expert-reviewed cardiology VP scenario was rated similarly to or more favorably than 1 clinician-developed scenario in selected learner-perceived domains. Future research should expand to objective learning, retention, development workload, and scalability outcomes.

title: Mind Your Heart-A Web-Based Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension Diet and Mindful Eating Intervention for Working Adults at Elevated Cardiovascular Risk: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
authorString: Reina AM, Padilla HM, Beer JM, Zhang DS, Renzi-Hammond LM.
abstractText:
Background

The Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension Diet (DASH) diet supports heart health; yet, many find it difficult to follow in community settings. Mindful eating can improve adherence, but in-person programs are time-consuming and not always accessible. eHealth offers an accessible, scalable alternative that may increase engagement and compliance.

Objective

This study assessed the feasibility of a DASH eHealth program focused on mindful eating and the preliminary changes in eating behaviors, diet quality, and health outcomes.

Methods

Participants were recruited from a university workplace via email and flyers and randomly assigned to either a web-based DASH diet education program (Diet Only) or the Mind Your Heart (MYH) intervention. The MYH program included the same DASH curriculum plus additional mindful eating instruction, guided practice, and specific, measurable, achievable, realistic, and time frame (SMART) goal setting. Both interventions were fully asynchronous, self-guided, and lasted 6 weeks on the Desire2Learn (D2L) Brightspace platform, with no personalized coaching or counseling. Baseline and postintervention assessments involved in-person measurements of anthropometrics, blood pressure, and blood biomarkers. Participants recorded their diets electronically over 3 days using MyFitnessPal (MyFitnessPal, Inc) and completed validated questionnaires on mindful eating using the Mindful Eating Behaviors Scale (MEBS), eating behaviors using the Three-Factor Eating Questionnaire Revised 21-item (TFEQ-R21), motivation for regulated eating using the Regulated Eating Behaviors Scale (REBS), and perceived stress using the Perceived Stress Scale 10-item (PSS-10). During the intervention, automated ecological momentary assessments (EMAs) were sent electronically 3 times weekly to monitor eating behaviors in real time.

Results

Thirty-seven participants (mean BMI 31.93 SD 7.25, 34/37, 91.9% female, 31/37, 83.8% White) were randomized into groups. Among the 36 who remained enrolled, the mean curriculum completion was 85.9%, SD 21.4; 31 (86.1%) completed≥60% of assigned content, and 32 (88.9%) completed at least half of the scheduled EMA prompts. Thirty-four participants attended the postintervention assessment and completed the questionnaires and the blood pressure assessment, although paired baseline and postintervention data were not available for all anthropometric measures and biomarkers. Participants reported no adverse events, and research staff observed none. Although no significant between-group differences were observed for DASH adherence, anthropometric measures, blood pressure, or cardiometabolic biomarkers, participants in the MYH group showed greater improvements than the Diet Only group in TFEQ-cognitive restraint (mean difference in change 0.39, 95% CI 0.06-0.72; Hedges g=0.81; P=.02) and REBS-controlled regulation (mean difference in change 3.59, 95% CI 0.01-7.16; Hedges g=0.68; P=.05).

Conclusions

A fully asynchronous digital mindful eating plus DASH education intervention and associated research procedures were feasible among working adults at elevated cardiovascular risk. Preliminary changes in eating behaviors suggest that mindful eating warrants further evaluation, but findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample and feasibility design. Larger, adequately powered randomized controlled trials are needed.

title: Tirzepatide Use Resulted in Clinically Meaningful Weight Reduction in Individuals With Obesity or Overweight: 12-Month Real-World Results.
authorString: Chinthammit C, Gibble TH, Dehghan M, Mojdami D, Huang A, Schapiro D, Bays H.
abstractText:
Aims

This study assessed the real-world effectiveness of tirzepatide in commercially insured individuals without diabetes, eligible for obesity medications (OMs), including glucagon like-peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA)-naïve individuals (i.e., no GLP-1 RA prescription during the 12-month pre-index period) and GLP-1 RA-experienced individuals.

Methods

This retrospective, observational cohort study used Optum's de-identified Market Clarity Data (Optum Market Clarity). Adults with ≥ 1 prescription claim for tirzepatide between November 2023 and March 2024, with continuous medical/pharmacy enrollment for ≥ 12 months pre-index and post-index and available pre- and post-index data were included. Baseline demographics, clinical characteristics, and treatment effectiveness (change from baseline in weight, body mass index, and cardiometabolic risk factors) were assessed among OM-eligible individuals who were persistent on tirzepatide for ≥ 12 months.

Results

The GLP-1 RA-naïve and experienced cohorts included 230 individuals (mean age: 49.5 years, 72.2% female) and 123 individuals (mean age: 48.9 years, 81.3% female), respectively, who were persistent on tirzepatide for 12 months with documented pre- and post-index weight measurements. At baseline, more than 85% of individuals in each cohort had ≥ 1 obesity-related complication, most commonly dyslipidemia, hypertension, and prediabetes. At 12 months post-index, the GLP-1 RA-naïve cohort achieved a mean weight reduction of 19.3%, while the GLP-1 RA-experienced cohort achieved a mean weight reduction of 13.1%.

Conclusions

After 12 months of persistent tirzepatide use, individuals experienced clinically meaningful weight reduction, comparable to outcomes reported in clinical trials. These real-world findings were observed both in GLP-1 RA-naïve and experienced individuals.

title: Assessing hemodynamic responses in patients undergoing oral surgery with vasoconstrictor-enhanced local anesthesia: a prospective comparative study between medically compromised and healthy participants.
authorString: Manor Y, Rayyan F, Gal G.
abstractText:
Objectives

The present study deals with hemodynamic responses between different types of patients along different stages of operations.

Methods

In a prospective clinical trial,(approved by the IRB approval number 275-15-ASF) and patient informed consent for the procedure, hemodynamic responses were evaluated before and during minor oral surgical procedures performed under local anesthesia. The study encompassed both medically compromised patients (experimental group) and healthy individuals (control group). Hemodynamic parameters, including blood pressure, heart rate, and oxygenation, were monitored. Statistical analysis was conducted to compare parameter fluctuations within each group and patient. Additionally, clinical indicators were documented using a visual analogue scale. Table 1 presents the characteristics of each group regarding age,gender, medical situation and sort of surgical procedure.

Results

The study findings revealed consistent hemodynamic stability across all stages of the procedures. Patients in both groups maintained stable blood pressure, heart rate, and oxygenation levels prior to and during all stages of surgery. Medically compromised patients showed hemodynamic trends comparable to healthy controls. Local anesthesia with vasoconstrictors demonstrated stable profiles and pain management was effective.

Conclusion

Local anesthesia containing adrenaline (1:100,000) demonstrated safety in hemodynamic parameters of healthy and medically compromised patients undergoing minor oral surgery. Overall, hemodynamic fluctuations were minimal, underscoring both the efficacy and safety of using vasoconstrictor-containing local anesthetics for pain management in a controlled hypertension and other well-managed chronic conditions.

title: Proteinuria, eGFR Decline, and the Pathway to Kidney Failure in Alport Syndrome.
authorString: Gale DP, Miner JH, Rheault MN, Fornoni A, Lennon R.

journal.title: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN

abstractText: Alport syndrome is a genetic disorder caused by pathogenic variants in COL4A3, COL4A4, or COL4A5, which encode the α3, α4, and α5 chains of type IV collagen. These chains form the collagen α3α4α5(IV) network required for basement membrane function in the kidney, inner ear, and eye. In the kidney, impaired production, assembly, or localization of the α3α4α5 network leads to abnormal glomerular basement membrane (GBM) composition, podocyte dysfunction, proteinuria, glomerulosclerosis, progressive loss of filtration capacity, and kidney failure. End point selection for clinical trials in Alport syndrome requires measures that report disease activity and predict meaningful clinical benefit in trials of feasible size and duration. Proteinuria arises from early stages of Alport pathogenesis: abnormal GBM permeability, podocyte foot-process effacement, podocyte detachment, and glomerulosclerosis. eGFR decline is a later readout of cumulative nephron loss and progression toward kidney failure. This review examines the evidence linking proteinuria and eGFR decline to kidney failure in Alport syndrome, focusing on two contributors to proteinuria: 1) podocyte dysfunction with foot-process effacement, which may be partially modifiable, and 2) proteinuria associated with podocyte loss and glomerulosclerosis, which is less likely to be reversible. The relative contribution of these components may vary with genotype, sex, age, and disease duration. Biopsy-based markers, such as collagen α3α4α5(IV) localization, GBM ultrastructure, podocyte foot-process width, glomerulosclerosis, and tubulointerstitial fibrosis, provide staging information along the disease pathway. The current role of these biopsy markers is strongest for target engagement and pathway modification, because quantitative relationships between changes in these markers and kidney failure risk remain incompletely defined. An end point framework for Alport syndrome should account for genotype, sex, age, baseline proteinuria, baseline eGFR, disease duration, and the expected nonlinear trajectories of proteinuria and eGFR decline.

title: Acceptability of three smartphone apps to improve adherence to blood pressure medicines in community pharmacies: a qualitative interview study of patients and pharmacy staff
authorString: Jamison J, Scales J, Bhattacharya D, Mant J, Sutton S.
abstractText:
Background:

Around eight million people in England are treated for high blood pressure; however, many do not take their medications as prescribed, which can lead to serious health complications. Community pharmacists can support patients in taking medication, but they often lack time to do so. Smartphone apps may help patients take medicines in this environment. This study explored the experiences and views of patients and pharmacy staff regarding the use of three apps to manage blood pressure medication as part of a randomized feasibility trial. Methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 30 participants (22 people with hypertension and eight pharmacy staff ) across eight community pharmacies in the East of England . The data were analysed thematically using a constant comparative approach. Key themes were identified, with findings reported as verbatim quotes. Results Five key themes were identified: Two were associated with the general characteristics of reminder apps and three were related to increased app functionality. Participants welcomed the apps’ reminder notification, ability to track multiple medications, direct messaging with pharmacies, and scanning function for uploading medication details. Patients also recommended additional features, including inputting blood pressure readings and the ability to save details on unused medicines and GP appointments. However, implementing this technology may depend on the capacity and resources available at the pharmacy site. Conclusions This study adds to the growing body of research on the use of smartphone apps for the self-management of medications. We found that digital apps were acceptable to patients using blood-pressure-lowering medicines and were supported by staff in community pharmacies. Apps with additional functionality that enables prescription reordering and facilitates direct communication with pharmacists have the potential to simplify medication management. However, further research is needed to assess their effectiveness and explore the best practices for use across a wider pharmacy setting.

title: Ultra-high-resolution Photon-Counting CT for Leaflet-Specific Evaluation of Fibrosis and Calcification in Aortic Stenosis
authorString: Bahaaeldin M, Shamekhi J, Franklin BS, Nowak S, Böhner AM, Kravchenko D, Wrobel J, Phinicarides R, Pennig L, Janssen JP, Gietzen C, Zimmer S, Baldus S, Kelm M, Nickenig G, Zeus T, Mauri V, Luetkens JA.
abstractText:
Objectives

Ultra-high-resolution photon-counting detector (PCD)-CT may enable leaflet-specific analysis of aortic valve fibrosis and calcification, providing insights into early aortic stenosis (AS) disease progression. This study aimed to investigate how PCD-CT leaflet-specific calcific and fibrotic volumes influence cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) leaflet mobility.

Materials and methods

Participants with moderate aortic AS prospectively underwent both PCD-CT (n=80) and CMR (n=58). Using PCD-CT, calcific and fibrotic volumes were segmented for right (RCC), left (LCC), and non-coronary cusps (NCC) and indexed to the aortic annulus area (ICV and IFV). CMR-derived leaflet mobility index (LMI) was assessed. Two raters compared image quality using a Likert-scale (1=poor to 5=excellent) and distinguishability of individual leaflets in PCD-CT with EID-CT (n=82).

Results

PCD-CT analysis showed that calcification was higher in males (e.g., ICV RCC : 15±16 vs. 4±7 µL/cm 2 ;p<0.001) while fibrosis was higher in females (e.g., IFV LCC ; 47±18 vs. 34±15 µL/cm 2 ;p=0.004) across all leaflets. Fibrocalcific ratio was higher in LCC (53±276) compared to RCC (19±48;p<0.001) and NCC (13.5±34;p<0.001). LMI of RCC was higher in females compared to men (0.66±0.21 vs. 0.38±0.33;p=0.008). LMI LCC and LMI NCC showed no sex differences. LMI RCC negatively correlated with ICV RCC (ρ=-0.64[-0.77, −0.46];p<0.001) and LMI NCC with ICV NCC (ρ=-0.69[-0.80, −0.53];p<0.001), whereas LMI LCC negatively correlated with IFV LCC (ρ=-0.35[-0.56,-0.10];p=0.007), particularly in females (ρ=-0.70[-0.89, −0.31];p = 0.003). PCD-CT yielded higher image quality (5[IQR4–5] vs. 3[3–4];p<0.001) and leaflet distinguishability (79/80[99%] vs. 42/82[51%];p<0.001) than EID-CT.

Conclusions

Ultra-high-resolution PCD-CT allows for leaflet-specific quantification of indexed fibrotic and calcific volume. These volumes demonstrate sex- and leaflet-specific differences that may distinctly contribute to AS pathophysiology.

Key Points

Detailed leaflet-level characterization of fibrotic and calcific remodeling in aortic stenosis remains limited with energy integrating CT. Photon-counting CT enabled reliable leaflet-specific quantification of fibrosis and calcification, identified sex-related tissue distribution patterns, and demonstrated associations between calcification and impaired leaflet mobility. Leaflet-specific photon-counting CT assessment may enhance our understanding of aortic stenosis progression and support more individualized imaging evaluation through improved differentiation of fibrotic and calcific valvular remodeling.

Clinical Trials Registration

NCT05851209

title: Medial Arterial Calcification in Diabetes-Related Foot Disease: An Arterial-Wall Dimension Uncharacterized in Current Limb Staging.
authorString: Galassi L, Facchinetti F, Ravini ML, Banfi C.
abstractText:
Objectives

To synthesize the evidence on medial arterial calcification (MAC) in diabetes-related foot disease, addressing its arterial-wall phenotype, effects on haemodynamic assessment, prognostic associations, and its potential role in limb staging.

Methods

Narrative review of clinical, imaging, pathological and mechanistic literature identified through targeted database searches, interpreted with reference to the Wound, Ischaemia and foot Infection (WIfI) classification and the Global Limb Anatomic Staging System (GLASS).

Results

MAC is common in diabetes-related foot disease, particularly with chronic kidney disease, and is an arterial-wall phenotype distinct from intimal atherosclerosis. An elevated ankle-brachial index is uninterpretable, and a reference-range value does not exclude peripheral artery disease. Across cohorts of differing design and definition, MAC has been consistently associated with major amputation, delayed wound healing and mortality, in line with a systematic review of 51 calcification-scoring studies; the five-point pedal score has been externally validated, and associations persisted after adjustment for WIfI stage. Model comparison in one cohort suggests incremental information, but discrimination, calibration and reclassification beyond established staging have not been reported. Neither WIfI nor GLASS characterizes arterial-wall phenotype.

Conclusions

The consistency and reproducibility of the prognostic evidence justify formal consideration of MAC in forthcoming revisions of limb-staging systems and guidelines. Incremental-value analyses should accompany that evaluation and inform the form of any modifier rather than delay it. One concrete route is to use MAC as a qualifier of the reliability of the WIfI ischaemia grade in the individual limb.

title: Multisystem Outcomes of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Versus Active Comparators in Type 2 Diabetes: A Multicenter Target Trial Emulation.
authorString: Vashisht R, Dhruva SS, Patel A, Dahm L, Morris P, Gonzalez D, Follett R, Sirota M, Singh K, Koliwad S, Han C.

journal.title: Journal of diabetes science and technology

abstractText:
Background

Multisystem effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) beyond cardiometabolic outcomes are incompletely characterized against active comparators in type 2 diabetes (T2D). We compared GLP-1RA with sulfonylureas (SUs), sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is), and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP4is) in adults with T2D.

Method

In a multicenter target trial emulation across 5 University of California academic medical centers (2012-2025) using harmonized electronic health record data, adults with T2D newly initiating GLP-1RA, SU, SGLT2i, or DPP4i were propensity score-matched 1-to-1 within site via least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (>11 000 covariates), with up to 5-year follow-up. We screened 181 prespecified incident outcomes across 15 body systems, pooling hazard ratios by random-effects meta-analysis. Robustness required leave-one-medical-center-out stability, E-value ≥1.5, and false discovery rate-adjusted P < .10.

Results

Among 70 982 matched adults, 118 robust associations were identified (65 for reduced risk and 53 for increased risk). Risk reductions were most consistent for cardiovascular outcomes, including myocarditis/cardiomyopathy (summary hazard ratio, 0.38 [95% CI, 0.32-0.44] vs SGLT2i), acute myocardial infarction (0.53 [0.42-0.66]), heart failure (0.71 [0.58-0.88] vs DPP4i), and thromboembolism (0.69-0.72), and for nephritis/nephrosis (0.73 [0.67-0.79]), nutritional anemia (0.70-0.81), coagulation disorders (0.73-0.81), and tobacco-related disorders (0.60 [0.49-0.74]). Risk increases were found for musculoskeletal conditions (22 associations); osteoarthritis 1.48 (1.29-1.68), stress fractures 1.68 (1.15-2.47), diverticular disease (1.18-1.33), sleep-wake disorders (1.27-1.54), and menopausal disorders (1.32-1.52).

Conclusions

Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist initiation was associated with reduced cardiovascular, renal, hematologic, and tobacco-related risk, consistent with outcome trials. Increased risks for musculoskeletal, gastrointestinal, and sleep-wake disorders warrant monitoring as the clinical use of GLP-1RAs continues to expand.

title: Carotid Endarterectomy Versus Trans-Carotid Artery Revascularisation (TCAR) for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Domingos Rosa Schneidwind K, Mofidi R.
abstractText:
Objectives

The treatment for asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis includes a surgical or interventional approach in selected cases. Although endarterectomy should be considered over stenting for selected patients, according to the latest European Society of Vascular Surgery (ESVS) guidelines, the Carotid Revascularization and Medical Management for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis Trials (CREST-2) suggested that carotid stenting would be associated with low rates of perioperative stroke or death. The transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) technique is a relatively new endovascular method, which involves placing a stent at the carotid bifurcation through direct carotid artery access, performed under a flow reversal system. This approach avoids manipulation of the aortic arch, potentially reducing embolic events. The aim of this systematic review is to compare TCAR with carotid endarterectomy (CEA) in asymptomatic patients undergoing carotid intervention. It seeks to evaluate whether TCAR is associated with improved perioperative outcomes, such as lower rates of stroke and death, compared with CEA, given its potentially less invasive approach.

Methods

The review was performed according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) on the platforms PubMed/Medline, OVID/Embase, and Scopus. The following MeSH terms were used: "asymptomatic carotid stenosis" AND "carotid endarterectomy", "transcarotid artery revascularization" OR "TCAR". Full-text screening and data extraction were performed with the support of the COVIDENCE platform. Six studies were selected for this systematic review, comprising a total of 132,684 patients (30,581 undergoing TCAR and 102,103 undergoing CEA). Statistical analysis was performed using R software.

Results

The selected studies for this systematic review showed similar results in terms of perioperative stroke and death for asymptomatic patients who underwent carotid endarterectomy and TCAR.

Conclusion

Our results suggest that there are no significant differences between CEA and TCAR for the treatment of asymptomatic patients who require a surgical or interventional approach. Further studies are necessary to provide more robust data in this field.

title: Acute autonomic and cardiovascular responses to walking in natural versus urban environments: A systematic review and three-level meta-analysis.
authorString: Li C, Zhang Q, Chen L, Xue Z.
abstractText: Acute physiological responses to walking in natural versus urban environments remain uncertain. We reviewed studies of healthy adults completing single walks in actual outdoor settings. Six databases were searched through January 12, 2026, and reporting followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses framework. We included 21 studies; 20 contributed 57 effect estimates to a three-level meta-analysis. Pooled Hedges' g estimates with 95% confidence intervals were -0.01 [-0.26, 0.23] for heart rate (p = 0.90), 0.11 [-0.40, 0.62] for systolic blood pressure (p = 0.63), and -0.14 [-0.36, 0.08] for diastolic blood pressure (p = 0.18). Evidence was inconclusive for high frequency heart rate variability (g = -0.14 [-0.94, 0.66], p = 0.66) and the root mean square of successive differences between normal interbeat intervals (g = -0.01 [-0.89, 0.87], p = 0.98), with few estimates and wide intervals. Exploratory analyses found no clear moderating associations with walking duration or study sample sex composition, although small subgroups limited precision. Overall, current evidence does not show a consistent additional acute physiological response to natural walking. This does not establish equivalence or rule out true differences. Estimates reflect heterogeneous routes and protocols and cannot isolate a uniform causal effect of nature exposure. Psychological restoration, sustained physical activity, disease prevention, and clinical outcomes require separate evidence. Future studies should better characterize environmental exposures and standardize walking and measurement procedures.

title: State-Level Structural Determinants of Multiple Human Trafficking Types and Their Strength of Evidence: A Global Systematic Literature Review.
authorString: Young BR, Chua MM, Watson SN, Golden SD, Kainz K, Moracco KE, Frattaroli S, Polston P.
abstractText: Human trafficking is a global public health problem with negative, wide-ranging effects on individuals, families, and communities. Understanding the structural determinants that influence human trafficking (HT) is imperative to preventing its occurrence. This systematic review identified and summarized existing global literature on State-level structural determinants (SSDs) for HT. We identified peer-reviewed studies from a search conducted in PubMed and gray literature from a United Nations repository. Eligible publications were written in English, included HT victimization as a primary or secondary outcome of interest, and either empirically demonstrated or hypothesized an association between at least one SSD and HT victimization. Hypothesized associations had to be rooted in empirical, practice-based, or theoretical evidence. Forty-eight publications were eligible and presented evidence for the linkage between SSDs and one or more HT types-child marriage, child conscription, organ trafficking, labor trafficking, sex trafficking, and HT generally. Data were derived from six out of the eight UN Sustainable Development Goal regions. The SSDs were thematically grouped into structural determinant families (SDFs) to facilitate comparative analysis. Interestingly, we found that some SDFs were common among various HT types, including the importance of multilateral agreements and coordination for anti-trafficking and the incorporation of regional treaties, conventions, or declarations for human trafficking within local State legislation. These findings highlight the importance of establishing a clear framework for implementing anti-HT laws both within and outside of the State. Future interventions should consider prioritizing shared SDFs to mitigate multiple forms of HT. Additional research, policy, and practice implications are discussed.

title: Long-term proton pump inhibitor use and cardiovascular events, stroke and mortality: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Yahaya HA, Mohd Tahir NA, Makmor Bakry M, Islahudin F.
