title: Dissociation between structural reverse remodeling and clinical outcomes in ischemic cardiomyopathy undergoing cardiac resynchronization therapy: a real-world analysis.
authorString: Massa Pereira J, Andraz S, Hamann L, Baganha D, Carvalho D, Candeias R, Mimoso J, Baptista Gonçalves R, Azevedo P, Costa HA.

journal.title: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace

abstractText: Patients with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) generally exhibit better responses to cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) due to more pronounced reverse remodeling compared to ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) patients. However, the prognostic impact of CRT in ICM patients remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of heart failure (HF) etiology on reverse remodeling, clinical outcomes, and survival following CRT in a real-world population. We conducted a retrospective observational study including patients who underwent CRT-P (pacing)/CRT-D (defibrillator) implantation. Patients were stratified according to HF etiology (ICM vs. NICM). The primary composite endpoint was the occurrence of all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization. Secondary outcomes focused on echocardiographic measures of left ventricular reverse remodeling. Survival analysis was performed using Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox regression models. Of the 95 patients initially screened, 83 were included in the final analysis, of whom 38 (45.8%) had ICM. The mean age was 69.5±10.4 years, and 75.8% were male. Both groups received similar medical therapy. NICM patients demonstrated a significant improvement in reverse remodeling after CRT [left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF): 32.3±11.5% to 44.0±13.2%, p=0.001); end-diastolic volume (LVEDV): 189.6±74.3 mL to 143.9±48.9 mL, p=0.010] with post-CRT LVEF being higher than in ICM patients (44.0±13.2% vs. 35.5±13.5%, p=0.003). NICM patients were more likely to be super-responders (58.1% vs. 25.0%, p=0.014). No significant differences were observed between groups in the primary composite endpoint (27.3% vs. 42.1%, p=0.171) or overall survival over a mean follow-up of 35 months (log-rank p=0.733). Although ICM patients showed less pronounced reverse remodeling following CRT, long-term clinical outcomes and survival were comparable to those observed in NICM. These findings reinforce the role of CRT as a disease-modifying therapy that prevents disease progression irrespective of HF etiology and support its systematic use in all eligible patients.

title: Estimand-based design strategies for cardiovascular recurrent event trials of combination therapies.
authorString: Mukherjee A.
abstractText: Cardiovascular trials increasingly evaluate combination therapies in settings where patients may experience recurrent events such as myocardial infarction, heart failure hospitalization, or stroke. Traditional single-event analyses fail to capture the cumulative disease burden and temporal dynamics, motivating the integration of recurrent event methods within an estimand framework. This manuscript reviews estimand strategies for recurrent event analyses in cardiovascular trials of combination therapies, emphasizing alignment between clinical questions, intercurrent events, and causal interpretation. We compare commonly used models, including the Andersen-Gill, Prentice-Williams-Peterson, and Negative Binomial approaches, highlighting their suitability for different estimands. We distinguish each model's conditional or marginal estimand, its identifiability assumptions, and the difference between sensitivity analyses that vary assumptions under the same estimand and supplementary analyses that target alternative estimands with different intercurrent event strategies. The impact of intercurrent events such as treatment discontinuation, rescue therapy, and mortality on estimand interpretation is explored. Novel methodological considerations specific to combination-therapy trials, including component-specific intercurrent events (ICE), drug-drug interaction estimands, mixed intercurrent event (ICE) strategies, and principal-stratum estimands conditional on dual adherence, are formally defined and discussed with work examples. We further discuss how the choice of estimand influences causal inference and model selection. Finally, we provide a regulatory perspective on estimand-based approaches in cardiovascular trials. This manuscript serves as a methodological guide for designing and analyzing cardiovascular trials with recurrent events for combination therapies to ensure clarity of clinical interpretation, robustness of causal conclusions, and regulatory alignment.

title: Stroke-Heart Syndrome: Mechanisms, Temporal Phenotypes, and Diagnostic Reasoning.
authorString: Lin F, Lyu J, Liu Y, Feng Z, Bao J, Song W, Zhu B, Liu M, Xue J, Weng J, Zhang J, Zhao J, Chen X, Dong B.
abstractText: Stroke-heart syndrome (SHS) encompasses new or worsened cardiac abnormalities that arise after acute stroke, most often within the first 30 days and with an early peak. Its spectrum includes acute myocardial injury, electrocardiographic changes, arrhythmia, ventricular dysfunction, Takotsubo syndrome, and heart failure, but similar findings may reflect antecedent cardiac disease or systemic illness. This Review defines the accepted clinical boundaries of SHS and integrates central autonomic network disruption, neuroendocrine stress, inflammation, endothelial and microvascular dysfunction, oxygen supply-demand imbalance, and premorbid substrate into a time-resolved framework. Eight provisional, non-mutually-exclusive phenotypic domains are proposed to organize current evidence without implying validated endotypes. A diagnostic approach based on symptom chronology, prior cardiac data, serial troponin and electrocardiography, rhythm monitoring, echocardiography, selective coronary assessment, and cardiac magnetic resonance is presented to distinguish stroke-triggered injury from recent myocardial infarction, pre-existing atrial fibrillation, chronic myocardial injury, and established heart failure. No syndrome-specific treatment is validated; care should prioritize recognized cardiac emergencies, correction of reversible stressors, and coordinated stroke-cardiology decision-making. Prospective studies with documented premorbid status, standardized time points, and blinded adjudication are needed to validate the proposed phenotypes and determine whether they improve outcomes.

title: Macrophage GLUD1 is Essential for Redox Balance and Immune Homeostasis in Cardiac Injury.
authorString: Jin T, Lai C, Zhou Q, Wang R, Tong Y, Chen W, Rabrenovic N, Zhang T, Ren X, Huang C, Chen J, Li R, Yu L, Mazzone M, Zhang W, Fu G, Shang M.
abstractText: Excessive free radical production and dysregulated immune responses contribute to myocardial ischemia-reperfusion (IR) injury. However, the mechanisms by which macrophages regulate reactive oxygen species (ROS) homeostasis and orchestrate immune responses during IR injury remain elusive. Here, we show that glutamate dehydrogenase 1 (GLUD1) expression is induced in monocytes from patients with acute myocardial infarction after interventional therapy and in cardiac-recruited macrophages from mice subjected to IR injury. GLUD1-deficient macrophages exacerbate IR injury by increasing mitochondrial ROS accumulation and amplifying pro-inflammatory responses. Mechanistically, GLUD1 deficiency leads to mitochondrial ROS accumulation due to reduced NADPH/NADP<sup>+</sup> and GSH/GSSG ratios during IR injury. Elevated mitochondrial ROS inhibits PHD2 activity, stabilizing HIF-1α and enhancing NF-κB signaling, promoting the release of pro-inflammatory factors and exacerbating myocardial damage. Systemic activation of GLUD1 or adoptive transfer of monocytes pre-treated with a GLUD1 activator preserved cardiac function and mitigated IR injury. These findings highlight macrophage GLUD1 as a critical regulator of redox balance and immune homeostasis, presenting a promising therapeutic target for alleviating IR injury and preserving cardiac function.

title: MCT1-dependent mitochondrial lactate import sustains cardiac metabolism.
authorString: Cluntun AA, Visker JR, Velasco-Silva JN, Carrington J, Cedeño-Rosario L, Napoli GC, Kim JE, Shankar TS, Brothwell MJ, Hamouche R, Narbona-Pérez ÁJ, Ling J, Toshniwal AG, Low HK, Cunningham CN, Eberhardt DR, Li J, Stanley CE, Alcantara QA, Yadav T, Maves RL, Swiatek WI, Offei NA, Blaze B, Shetty SP, Chaudhuri D, Hong T, Rothstein JD, Muoio DM, Paulo JA, Gygi SP, Tseliou E, Navankasattusas S, Cox JE, Funai K, Drakos SG, Rutter J, Ducker GS.
abstractText: The heart possesses a dynamic capacity to oxidize a variety of fuels, including glucose and lactate, to meet its energetic demands under diverse dietary, exertion and injury stressors<sup>1</sup>. Oxidation of carbohydrate substrates is thought to converge on the cytosolic generation of pyruvate, which is transported by the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier (MPC) for entry into the tricarboxylic acid cycle<sup>2</sup>. Here we find that glucose-derived carbon is oxidized in mouse myocardium even when the MPC is genetically ablated. Using genetic and pharmacological tools, we demonstrate that lactate monocarboxylate transporter 1 (MCT1, encoded by Slc16a1) is required for the oxidation of glucose carbon by MPC-deficient myocardium. We further observe that MCT1, traditionally localized to the plasma membrane, also resides in the inner mitochondrial membrane of mouse and human cardiomyocytes. Together with matrix-localized LDHB, MCT1 enables mitochondrial lactate conversion to pyruvate and NADH, directly fueling the electron transport chain. Loss of MCT1 impairs lactate oxidation, disrupts metabolic flexibility and accelerates the development of heart failure with increased mortality after hyperactivation of the neurohormonal axis or ischemia-reperfusion injury. Thus, the existence of a parallel lactate-based pathway for carbohydrate oxidation can sustain cardiac energetics and maintain myocardial structure and function under diverse stress conditions.

title: Multidimensional sleep health and risks of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality: A MAIHDA-based prospective cohort study.
authorString: Zhang Q, Zhou B, Wang Y, Zhang J, Wang Y, Hu K.
abstractText: The combined and interactive effects of multiple sleep dimensions on mortality remain unclear. We applied Multilevel Analysis of Individual Heterogeneity and Discriminatory Accuracy (MAIHDA) to examine how multidimensional sleep health relates to all-cause and cardiovascular mortality. The analytic sample included 4340 adults for all‑cause mortality and 3790 for cardiovascular mortality from the Sleep Heart Health Study. Six sleep dimensions were dichotomized into healthy versus unhealthy categories and combined to form 64 unique strata representing all possible sleep health profiles. Individuals were nested within strata in multilevel Cox MAIHDA models. Three models were estimated: model 1 (null), model 2 (sleep-domain fixed effects), and model 3 (sleep-domain fixed effects plus covariates). In null models, sleep‑health strata explained 8.51% of the variance in all‑cause mortality and 15.01% in cardiovascular mortality, indicating meaningful heterogeneity across sleep profiles. After accounting for sleep-domain main effects and covariates, most between‑strata variance was explained (PCV = 99.95% for all-cause mortality and 78.32% for cardiovascular mortality), indicating that mortality risk was predominantly additive rather than driven by unique non‑additive combinations. Healthier continuity and timing were associated with lower all-cause mortality, while timing was the most consistent sleep feature for cardiovascular mortality; absence of sleep disorders showed a weaker association mainly for all-cause mortality. Strata with multiple unhealthy sleep dimensions consistently had the highest marginal standardized predicted 10-year mortality risks. MAIHDA maps mortality risk across multidimensional sleep profiles and quantifies additive versus non-additive effects. Mortality risk was explained primarily by the additive accumulation of sleep-health attributes.

title: Harnessing Clinical Characteristics to Identify High-Risk of Drug-induced QTc Prolongation in Hospitalized Patients.
authorString: Zhao Y, Weng BB, Lan G, Jin NS, Liao PL, Lai XD, Liu YG, Wang Q.
abstractText:
Background

Drug-induced QTc-prolongation is a major concern for developing ventricular arrhythmias, which may eventually lead to sudden cardiac death. Identifying high-risk patients is essential to support healthcare providers in handling automatically generated alerts in clinical practice. The aim of study was to develop clinical data-driven machine learning methods to predict drug-induced QTc-prolongation.

Methods

Inpatients with paired electrocardiograms were enrolled from Southwest Hospital (2015-2022). Six machine learning (ML) algorithms were developed to predict drug-induced QTc prolongation (ΔQTc > 60 ms). Model performance was evaluated using an internal test set and an independent external validation cohort. Model interpretations were recognized by feature importance and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) methods. Finally, we benchmarked the ML models against the traditional Tisdale risk score.

Results

A total of 2451 participants were recruited, of whom 292 developed QTc-prolongation, while 150 patients from a separate center served as the external validation cohort. The eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model achieved the best performance with recall of 0.884 and AUC of 0.814 in internal test set. During external validation, the AUC remained robust at 0.864, although recall declined to 0.650. SHAP analysis identified baseline QTc and QT intervals, inflammation, high-risk drugs, and hypertension are the primary drivers of model predictions.

Conclusions

The XGBoost algorithm provides a highly sensitive framework for predicting drug-induced QTc prolongation. Integrating this ML tool with identified clinical drivers into hospital decision support systems would facilitate the optimization of treatment strategies and early ECG monitoring strategies.

title: Hemodynamic Indices of Right Ventricular Function are Associated with Adverse Clinical Outcomes Across Heart Failure Subtypes.
authorString: Kosyakovsky LB, Parekh J, Mounsey LA, Zern E, Pomerantsev E, Garan AR, Picard MH, Dudzinski DM, Grandin EW, Sabe MA, Quintero-Pinzon PA, Lau ES, Ho JE.
abstractText:
Background

While right ventricular dysfunction (RVD) is critical to the progression of heart failure (HF), the prevalence and prognostic implications of RVD across HF subtypes remains poorly understood.

Objectives

We aimed to characterize differences in hemodynamic indices of RVD among patients with HF with preserved (HFpEF, EF≥50%) vs reduced (HFrEF, EF<50%) ejection fraction and examine associations of RVD with longitudinal clinical outcomes.

Methods

We identified patients with prevalent HF undergoing clinically indicated right heart catheterization at Massachusetts General Hospital (2005-2016). We examined three RV hemodynamic indices: right atrial to wedge pressure ratio (RA/PCWP), RV stroke work index (RVSWI), and pulmonary artery pulsatility index (PAPi). We used multivariable Cox models to examine the association of each index with HF hospitalizations (HFH) and death.

Results

Of 2,062 patients, 1,242 (60%) had HFrEF and 820 (40%) had HFpEF; 56% of individuals with HFrEF and 53% with HFpEF met at least one hemodynamic criterion for RVD. In HFrEF, lower PAPi was associated with greater risk of HFH (HR 0.84 [0.77, 0.92]), and higher RVSWI was associated with greater risk of death (HR 1.17, [1.07, 1.27], all p<0.001). By contrast, only higher RA/PCWP was associated with greater risk of death in HFpEF (HR 1.11 (1.00, 1.22); p=0.046).

Conclusions

Hemodynamic RVD is common in both HFrEF and HFpEF, and hemodynamic measures of RV function are associated with greater risk of adverse outcomes. Importantly, the prognostic value of RV indices varied by HF subtype, highlighting key differences in the role of RVD in HFrEF vs HFpEF.

title: Functional Vulnerability and Long-Term Mortality in Adults With Ankle-Brachial Index-Defined Peripheral Artery Disease: A NHANES Cohort Study.
authorString: Wang M, Wang Y.
abstractText:
Objectives

Functional limitations are common in peripheral artery disease (PAD), but the association of a brief self-reported functional-burden measure with objectively defined PAD and long-term mortality remains incompletely characterized.

Methods

We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999-2004 participants aged >=40 years with ankle-brachial index (ABI), physical functioning, and linked mortality data. PAD was defined as minimum ABI <=0.90. A NHANES-derived functional vulnerability index (NFVI; range 0-4) was constructed from difficulty walking a quarter mile, walking up ten steps, stooping/crouching/kneeling, and standing for long periods. NFVI was intended as a brief functional-burden measure rather than a diagnostic frailty instrument. Survey-weighted models evaluated PAD status, NFVI, and mortality, with validated modified cardiovascular health (mCVH) used for additional adjustment.

Results

The PAD NFVI cohort included 462 participants and 375 deaths. PAD was associated with high NFVI after adjustment for sociodemographic factors and mCVH (OR 1.748, 95% CI 1.218-2.510; P=0.005). In PAD participants, each 1-point higher NFVI was associated with all-cause mortality after adjustment for sociodemographic factors and minimum ABI (HR 1.095, 95% CI 1.017-1.179; P=0.017). After additional mCVH adjustment, the continuous association was attenuated (HR 1.075, 95% CI 0.993-1.165; P=0.075), whereas high NFVI remained associated with mortality (HR 1.346, 95% CI 1.026-1.767; P=0.032). Complete-case selection was substantial (462/647 PAD participants), with marked differences between included and excluded participants, particularly in age, potentially limiting generalizability.

Conclusions

Functional vulnerability was more common among adults with ABI-defined PAD and was associated with long-term all-cause mortality. These findings demonstrate an epidemiologic association rather than the clinical utility, validation, or incremental prognostic value of NFVI and do not establish a clinically meaningful NFVI mortality threshold. Prospective PAD-specific validation and comparison with established frailty measures are required before clinical use.

title: Effects of Endovascular Repair Timing on the Outcomes of Type B Aortic Dissection in an Asian Multicenter Cohort.
authorString: Cheng TH, Chen SW, Hsieh MJ, Chen DY, Chang FC, Chen CY, Tung YC, Hsiao FC, Chu PH, Cheng YT.
abstractText:
Background

This study assessed thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) timing and its impact on outcomes in type B aortic dissection (TBAD).

Method

This multicenter retrospective study included 247 patients who underwent TEVAR for TBAD between 2011 and 2018, using data from the Chang Gung Research Database. Primary outcomes were in-hospital and postdischarge mortality.

Results

The study included 47, 122, and 78 patients with hyperacute (<1 day), acute/subacute (1-90 days), and chronic (>90 days) TBAD, respectively. Chronic TBAD had more aortic expansion before TEVAR (0% vs 6.6% vs 17.6%; P = 0.001). In-hospital mortality was highest in hyperacute TBAD (17%) and lowest in chronic TBAD (6.4%; adjusted P for trend = 0.036); conversely, long-term mortality was highest in chronic TBAD (12.3%) and lowest in hyperacute TBAD (0%; adjusted P for trend = 0.017). A restricted cubic spline model showed that delayed intervention beyond 90 days is associated with increasing long-term mortality risk. Among secondary outcomes, delayed TEVAR was associated with more aortic, cardiovascular, infection-related deaths, and residual aneurysms (adjusted P for trend= 0.039, 0.012, 0.048, and 0.006, respectively).

Conclusions

TEVAR may lead to unfavorable outcomes in hyperacute and chronic TBAD. Delayed TEVAR in chronic TBAD is associated with adverse aortic remodeling and rising long-term mortality. TEVAR before the chronic phase could be considered to improve short- and long-term outcomes.

title: Comparative Perioperative Outcomes of Rescue FEVAR vs Open Repair for Failed EVAR.
authorString: Gage D, Quinn PL, Corriere M, Go MR, Teng X, Orion K, Tillman B, Peng XK, Oriowo B, Powell C, Stoecker J, Lee KB.
abstractText:
Introduction

Redo aortic repair following previous endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) is often technically challenging and associated with significant morbidity. Technologic advances in custom modified grafts have permitted increased utilization of endovascular versus open repairs. Despite this progress, there is limited data surrounding the comparative perioperative outcomes between these procedural approaches.

Methods

The National Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database was queried for patients undergoing elective open abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) repair or fenestrated endovascular aortic repair (FEVAR) with a physician-modified (PMEG) or custom graft (CMD) following a previous EVAR from 2010 to 2024. A univariate analysis to compare groups was completed with chi square and Fisher's Exact T-test, and outcomes were compared using multivariate logistic and linear regression. Data was analyzed using STATA.

Results

900 patients underwent open repair, and 651 patents underwent FEVAR following previous EVAR. Using multivariate linear regression, patients undergoing open repair had an increased risk of postoperative pneumonia (OR 6.23, p=0.001), postoperative reintubation (OR 2.01, p=0.005), and major adverse cardiac events (OR 2.16, p=0.001) compared to patients undergoing FEVAR. Patients undergoing open repair had a higher risk of mortality (OR 2.02, p=0.018) and were less likely to be discharged home (OR 0.47, p<0.001).

Conclusions

Complex endovascular rescue of previously failed EVAR is associated with decreased the rate of perioperative complications compared to an open approach. FEVAR utilizing PMEG or CMD may be considered as a viable option in patients who are undergoing elective redo AAA repair following a failed EVAR.

title: Long-Term Patency and Clinical Outcomes After Retrograde Mesenteric Bypass for Chronic Mesenteric Ischemia.
authorString: Sezen A, Kapkin AY, Oguz E, Posacioglu H.
abstractText: Chronic mesenteric ischemia (CMI) is an uncommon yet clinically significant condition resulting from insufficient blood flow to the gastrointestinal tract, frequently leading to severe symptoms and increased morbidity. Although endovascular therapy has become the initial treatment strategy in many centres, open surgical reconstruction remains an important option for selected patients. This study evaluated long-term graft patency and clinical outcomes after retrograde mesenteric bypass. We evaluated 34 patients treated with retrograde mesenteric bypass for CMI between 2009 and 2024. Patency rates were measured with Kaplan-Meier analysis. Thrombosis was classified as early (≤30 days), mid-term (31-365 days), or late (>365 days). Superior mesenteric artery bypass was performed in 33 patients (97.1%), celiac bypass in 25 (73.5%), and dual-vessel reconstruction in 24 (70.6%). Median follow-up was 2737 days (IQR, 1760-4353), approximately 7.5 years. No early thrombosis occurred. Two mid-term and three late occlusions were observed. Primary patency rates were 93.3% at 1 and 3 years, 89.4% at 5 years, and 85.0% at 10 years. Clinical symptoms resolved after revascularisation in all patients surviving the perioperative period, and no recurrent symptoms were documented during follow-up. No patient required reintervention. Retrograde mesenteric bypass was associated with stable long-term patency, sustained symptom resolution, and low perioperative mortality. It remains a durable open surgical option for chronic mesenteric ischemia, particularly when endovascular revascularisation is not feasible or is unlikely to provide durable results.

title: Antiplatelet Therapy and Bleeding, Thrombosis, and Aneurysm Growth in Patients with Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
authorString: Crews B, Li J, Kostiuk V, Said S, Bader J, Zwibelman H, Strosberg D, Guzman RJ, Aboian E, Ochoa Chaar CI.
abstractText:
Objectives

Recent guidelines recommend considering antiplatelet therapy (class IIb recommendation) for patients with AAAs, but bleeding risk remains a concern. This study aims to investigate the association of antiplatelet therapy with bleeding, thrombosis, and aneurysm growth among patients with AAAs.

Methods

A single-center retrospective chart review of patients with AAA identified on imaging (2019-2023) was performed. Demographics and outcomes were compared by antiplatelet status, and multivariable regression identified factors associated with mortality, MACE, bleeding, and AAA growth.

Results

Among 886 (73% male) patients studied, 511 (57.7%) were prescribed antiplatelet therapy. Those prescribed antiplatelet therapy had higher rates of atherosclerotic disease than those not on antiplatelets. Patients not prescribed antiplatelet therapy were more likely to be female, have atrial fibrillation, and be prescribed anticoagulation. At a mean follow-up of 1.8 years, there were no differences in bleeding, major adverse cardiovascular events, venous thromboembolism events, or growth rate associated with antiplatelet prescription. Adjusted analyses showed statins (HR=0.73, p=0.02), but not antiplatelets or anticoagulants, were associated with reduced risk of mortality. Diabetes was associated with decreased AAA growth rate, while larger initial diameter was associated with increased growth rate as well as mortality.

Conclusions

Among patients with AAA, antiplatelet therapy was not observed to be associated with an increase in bleeding risk, but was also not associated with decreased mortality, thrombosis, or aneurysm growth. Statins were observed to be associated with reduced mortality. Aneurysmal growth rate was not associated with any medical therapies studied, including statins, and was only influenced by the presence of diabetes.

title: Spanish cardiac catheterization and interventional cardiology registry. 35<sup>th</sup> official report of the Interventional Cardiology Association of the Spanish Society of Cardiology (1990-2025).
authorString: Salinas P, Sánchez-Rubio J, Jurado-Román A, Moreiras JM.
abstractText: Introduction and objectives This report presents the 2025 activity of the Interventional Cardiology Association of the Spanish Society of Cardiology (ACI-SEC). Methods All interventional cardiology laboratories in Spain were invited to complete an online survey. Data were analyzed by an external company and subsequently reviewed and presented by the ACI-SEC board. Results A total of 125 hospitals participated, compared with 118 in the previous year. The number of diagnostic procedures and coronary angiograms increased by 4% and 4.5%, respectively, both reaching record highs. Percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) increased by 3.3%. The trend toward lower relative stent use was confirmed, with a marked increase in the use of drug-coated balloons, both as a standalone strategy and as part of hybrid strategies. The use of intracoronary imaging and coronary physiology techniques increased, reaching record absolute numbers. Interventional treatment of myocardial infarction increased by 3.6%, with primary PCI accounting for 98% of procedures. Structural heart interventions continued to expand: transcatheter aortic valve implantation (+10.1%), percutaneous mitral interventions (+25.2%), tricuspid interventions (+7.9%), and left atrial appendage closure (+8.4%). Renal denervation procedures, interventional treatment of acute pulmonary embolism, and interventions for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension increased significantly. Conclusions The 2025 Spanish cardiac catheterization and interventional cardiology registry shows overall growth in both coronary and structural activity. Full English text available from: www.revespcardiol.org/en.

title: Transient immediate systemic side effects following long-acting cabotegravir and rilpivirine injections in people with HIV: a 5-year cohort study.
authorString: Hocqueloux L, Pires Roteia D, Pallay S, Theillay A, Legros V, Oufella L, Bois J, Beraud G, Prazuck T.

journal.title: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases

abstractText: To characterise transient immediate systemic side effects (TISSE) following long-acting cabotegravir/rilpivirine (CAB-RPV-LA) injections, estimate their incidence, assess treatment continuation, and investigate associated plasma drug concentrations. This prospective single-centre French cohort included adults with HIV receiving CAB-RPV-LA during 2021-2026. Nurses prospectively documented unexpected systemic symptoms. Treatment discontinuation was compared by TISSE status. Plasma concentrations were measured by LC-MS/MS after TISSE events and compared with post-injection concentrations in 24 matched asymptomatic controls and routine trough measurements. Among 308 participants receiving 4,644 monitored on-site injection sessions, 24 experienced 28 TISSE episodes: 0.60% per session (exact Poisson 95% CI, 0.40-0.87%). Symptoms occurred during or shortly after injection, predominantly intense lumbar pain (18 episodes) and dyspnea/chest oppression (16), co-occurring in seven. All symptoms resolved within 15 minutes; none required hospitalisation. No difference in treatment discontinuation was detected (2/24 versus 38/284; Fisher's exact test, p=0.75). In all 17 sampled episodes, RPV and/or CAB concentrations were markedly elevated. RPV elevations occurred in 14 episodes, (up to 767-fold the upper concentration bound at trough), and CAB elevations in four, including one involving both drugs. TISSE episodes were brief and self-limited but clinically striking, potentially mimicking cardiovascular emergencies. Post-event concentration elevations suggest inadvertent systemic passage, predominantly involving RPV, without establishing causality. Possible CAB involvement remains exploratory. Recognising TISSE is important, and healthcare professionals should be familiar with its clinical presentation. NCT02898987.

title: Pulsed field, cryoballoon or radiofrequency catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Johner N, Monaco C, Magnocavallo M, Deville L, Benali K, Carmagnola L, Fortuna M, Boveda S, M'Rabet S, Guenancia C, Van Wabeke J, Verhaeghe L, Ditac G, Bessière F, Vlachos K, Vazirani R, Cruz A, Schiavone M, Tondo C, Rossi P, Bianchi S, Gamer AK, Tétreault-Langlois M, Notaristefano F, Fitzgerald JL, Plant A, Kneizeh K, Benabou L, Charton J, Sacristan B, Arnaud M, Da Costa A, Chierchia GB, Koopman P, Vijgen J, Haïssaguerre M, Duchateau J, Hocini M, Sacher F, Tixier R, Pambrun T, Derval N, Della Rocca DG, Jaïs P.
abstractText:
Background

Patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) exhibit suboptimal outcomes after atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation.

Objective

We sought to compare the efficacy, safety and long-term outcomes of pulsed field ablation (PFA), cryoballoon (CB) and radiofrequency (RF) ablation for AF in HCM.

Methods

Patients with HCM undergoing de novo AF ablation were retrospectively included from 11 centers. Procedure characteristics, safety endpoints and 24-month outcomes were assessed. The primary endpoint was atrial arrhythmia recurrence (AF/atrial tachycardia).

Results

A total of 364 patients with HCM (61.7±11.1 years, 74.5% male, 47.5% paroxysmal AF) underwent AF ablation with PFA (n=84), CB (n=50) or RF (n=230). Procedure-related complications occurred in 1.2%, 4.0% and 5.2% with PFA, CB and RF, respectively (p=0.344). Cumulative 24-month freedom from atrial arrhythmia recurrence was 48.6%. PFA was associated with reduced atrial arrhythmia recurrence compared with RF (adjusted HR, 0.57; 95% CI, 0.36-0.91; p=0.018), while CB showed no significant difference with either group (adjusted HR versus RF, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.42-1.21; p=0.212). In exploratory secondary analyses, PFA was associated with reduced cardiovascular hospitalization (adjusted HR, 0.43; 95% CI, 0.23-0.80; p=0.008), and greater improvement in NYHA class compared with RF (p=0.032), while CB showed no significant difference. Heart failure hospitalization, repeat ablation, ventricular arrhythmias, stroke/transient ischemic attack and mortality did not differ significantly between ablation modalities.

Conclusion

PFA for catheter ablation of AF in HCM was associated with reduced 24-month atrial arrhythmia recurrence, with exploratory signals of fewer cardiovascular hospitalizations and improved NYHA class compared with RF, while CB showed no significant difference.

title: Intraoperative Estimated Blood Loss and Perioperative Transfusion are Independently Associated with Postoperative Morbidity and Mortality After Lower Extremity Bypass.
authorString: Samaan F, Perry L, Soucy JW, Davtyan A, Zil-E-Ali A, Dautruche R, Aziz F.
abstractText: Intraoperative estimated blood loss (EBL) and need for perioperative packed red blood cell (pRBC) transfusion are common during lower extremity bypass (LEB) for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) and have each been associated with adverse postoperative outcomes. However, their joint associations with postoperative outcomes remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion, individually and jointly, with postoperative morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing LEB for CLTI. A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database. Patients undergoing LEB for CLTI between 2014 and 2023 were identified. Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified an optimal EBL threshold of 225 mL (area under the curve 0.72) for predicting transfusion, which was used to stratify patients into low-EBL (<225 mL) and high-EBL (≥225 mL) groups. Primary outcomes included myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, 30-day mortality, and a composite endpoint. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess adjusted associations across four groups defined by EBL and transfusion status. Separate model was used to evaluate the interaction between EBL and pRBC transfusion. Among 36,019 procedures, 58.5% had low EBL and 41.5% had high EBL. Patients who had high EBL and did not require blood transfusion had increased odds of adverse postoperative outcomes, including 30-day mortality (AOR 1.26, 95% CI [1.01, 1.59]), myocardial infarction (AOR 1.88, 95% CI [1.48, 2.39]), stroke (AOR 1.58, 95% CI [1.09, 2.29]), and the composite outcome (AOR 1.51, 95% CI [1.29, 1.78]). Patients who had low EBL and received blood transfusion had increased odds of 30-day mortality (AOR 2.46, 95% CI [1.95, 3.10]), myocardial infarction (AOR 6.57, 95% CI [5.26, 8.21]), stroke (AOR 2.75, 95% CI [1.84, 4.12]), and the composite outcome (AOR 4.08, 95% CI [3.48, 4.78]). Patients who had both high EBL and required perioperative blood transfusion demonstrated the highest odds of adverse outcomes, including 30-day mortality (AOR 2.54, 95% CI [2.09, 3.08]), myocardial infarction (AOR 7.39, 95% CI [6.08, 8.98]), stroke (AOR 3.79, 95% CI [2.76, 5.21]), and the composite outcome (AOR 4.42, 95% CI [3.87, 5.05]). Formal interaction testing demonstrated significant between EBL and transfusion. In patients undergoing LEB for CLTI, intraoperative EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion were both independently and jointly associated with increased postoperative morbidity and mortality. These findings identify EBL and transfusion as markers of perioperative risk and support further investigation of blood-sparing strategies and individualized transfusion practices.

title: Echocardiographic atrial and right heart to pulmonary circulation coupling indices identify high-risk patients in moderate aortic stenosis.
authorString: Santangelo G, Faggiano A, Mallardi GPF, Baroni M, Donisi L, Guareschi A, Pasero G, Sozzi F, Ruscica M, Guazzi M, Carugo S, Bursi F.
abstractText:
Purpose

Emerging evidence points to an increased mortality risk associated to moderate aortic stenosis (AS), yet this population remains insufficiently characterized. We tested the prognostic value of two echocardiographic coupling indices reflecting right and left-sided cardiac function: the ratio of tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion to pulmonary artery systolic pressure (TAPSE/PASP) and the left atrial volumetric/mechanical coupling index (LACI).

Methods

Retrospective, single-center study including 135 patients with moderate AS. TAPSE/PASP was used as a non-invasive surrogate of right ventricular-pulmonary circulation (RV-Pc) coupling, and LACI was defined as the ratio of left atrial volume index to mitral a' velocity. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to assess the prognostic value of both indices.

Results

During a mean follow-up of 1.61 ± 0.79 years, 33 patients (24%) died. Reduced TAPSE/PASP (< 0.67 mm/mmHg) and elevated LACI (> 5.17) were independently associated with an increased mortality (HR: 3.05 and 3.17, respectively, p < 0.01). These associations remained significant even after adjusting for age. Stratification into three groups - preserved, single, or combined uncoupling -showed progressively lower 1-year survival rates, ranging from 95% to 49% (p < 0.0001). None of the coupling-derived variables was associated with hemodynamic progression or need for aortic valve replacement.

Conclusion

TAPSE/PASP and LACI are independently associated with mortality in patients with moderate AS. These parameters may provide incremental prognostic information in this often-overlooked population. These findings may prompt further studies evaluating the potential role of these parameters in helping to refine prognostic phenotyping.

title: Comparing SGLT2 Inhibitors on Incident Major Adverse Kidney Events in Type 2 Diabetes: A Target Trial Emulation.
authorString: Zehra A, Aktay SL, Deng Y, Swarna KS, Neumiller JJ, Polley EC, Herrin J, Galindo RJ, Umpierrez GE, Ross JS, Brito JP, Montori VM, Mickelson MM, McCoy RG.
abstractText: To determine whether canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, and empagliflozin differ in rates of major adverse kidney events (MAKE) in adults with T2D at moderate cardiovascular risk and without stage 3+ chronic kidney disease (CKD) at baseline. Using target trial emulation and U.S. claims data from commercial, Medicare Advantage, and traditional Medicare plans, we compared canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, and empagliflozin among adults ≥ 21years with T2D at moderate cardiovascular risk (1-5% annualized MACE or death risk), without insulin use or stage 3+ chronic kidney disease (CKD) at baseline, initiating treatment from January 1, 2014, and December 31, 2021. Propensity scores estimated via super learner ensemble were incorporated as inverse probability weights into Cox models examining major adverse kidney events (MAKE: stage 3+ CKD, kidney failure, kidney replacement therapy initiation) and all-cause death under intention-to-treat analysis through December 31, 2022. The weighted cohort included 41,248, 17,548, and 72,638 adults initiating canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, and empagliflozin, respectively. One-year post-initiation, rates of MAKE were 3.2% in the dapagliflozin and empagliflozin arms and 3.5% in the canagliflozin arm; by three years, 8.4%, 8.5%, and 9.1%. Compared to canagliflozin, MAKE risk was lower with dapagliflozin (HR 0.91; 95%CI 0.85-0.97) and empagliflozin (HR 0.93; 95%CI 0.88-0.97), with no difference between dapagliflozin and empagliflozin. Empagliflozin and dapagliflozin were associated with modestly lower adverse kidney event rates compared to canagliflozin. These findings provide clinically actionable evidence to support selection of SGLT2i to reduce CKD risk in a highly prevalent subset of people with T2D.

title: Clinical, hematological, biochemical, and biomarker alterations in neonatal canine sepsis.
authorString: da Mata Fuchs K, Pereira KHNP, Xavier GM, Mendonça JC, da Cunha RA, Alferi SV, Ferreira JCP, Tsunemi MH, Lourenço MLG.
abstractText: Sepsis is one of the leading causes of mortality during the first weeks of life in canine neonates, and early diagnosis is essential to reduce these rates. This study aimed to evaluate changes in clinical, hematological, biochemical, and biomarker parameters (procalcitonin, C-reactive protein, and troponin I levels) in neonatal sepsis in dogs. Descriptive statistics, normality testing, group comparisons, and Pearson or Spearman correlations were performed, with significance set at p < 0.05. Biomarker cut-off values were determined using ROC curve analysis based on sensitivity and specificity above 80%. Thirty-one neonates were included, with 17 animals in the sepsis group (SG) and 14 in the control group (CG). In the assessment of clinical parameters, signs of systemic infection, such as diarrhea, erythema of the body, omphalitis, ecchymoses or hematomas, and cyanosis or necrosis of the extremities, were observed. Neonates in the SG showed bradycardia (p<0.05), hypothermia (p<0.05), and reduced neurological reflexes (p<0.05). Leukopenia (p<0.05), hyperlactatemia (p<0.01), hyperkalemia (p<0.05), and increased cardiac troponin I (p<0.01) were observed in the SG. A negative correlation was detected between the leukocyte count and the lactate concentration (r = -0.59; p<0.01) and between the neutrophil count and the troponin I concentration (r = -0.57; p<0.01). A positive correlation was observed between body temperature and leukocytes (r = 0.54, p < 0.01). Additionally, there was a trend toward thrombocytopenia, hypoglycemia, and increased CRP in the SG, although these findings did not reach statistical significance. The origin of the infections was predominantly maternal (intrauterine or via mastitis), with isolation of beta-hemolytic Streptococcus from uterine swabs (41.2%), Staphylococcus sp. from uterine swabs and milk (35.3%), and Streptococcus sp. from milk only (23.5%). Future serial studies are needed to characterize biomarker kinetics during infection. Early diagnosis of neonatal canine sepsis relies on litter monitoring, clinical signs and laboratory tests, including leukopenia, bacterial culture, lactate (≥3mmol/L), and cardiac troponin I (≥0.1ng/dL).

title: Traumatic Emergency Thoracotomy for Resuscitation in Shock (TETRiS): a national service evaluation of resuscitative thoracotomy practice outside the operating theatre.
authorString: Ramage L, Tucker H, Marsden ME, Wohlgemut JM, Naeem S, Christian M, Davenport R, Perkins ZB, TETRiS Collaborative.
abstractText: Resuscitative thoracotomy (RT) is performed in patients with traumatic cardiac arrest or peri-arrest to treat potentially reversible causes of circulatory collapse. Optimal patient selection and timing remain uncertain, and existing evidence is largely retrospective, often excluding prehospital deaths. This prospective service evaluation examined contemporary RT practice and outcomes across a national major trauma system, including prehospital and emergency department settings. Prospective 12-month observational study across 20 UK Helicopter Emergency Medical Services and 26 Major Trauma Centre Emergency Departments, using the PHOTON, TERN, and NaTRIC research networks. A total of 116 patients underwent RT, of which 82 (70.7%) were performed prehospital. Median age was 30 years, 97 patients (83.6%) were male, and 81 (69.8%) sustained penetrating injury. Suspected cardiac tamponade was the most common indication for RT (72/116 [62.1%]), although operative findings demonstrated exsanguinating haemorrhage in 82 patients (70.7%). Overall, 50 patients (43.1%) achieved return of spontaneous circulation and eight (6.9%) survived to hospital discharge. Survival was strongly associated with pathophysiological cause, duration of arrest, and physiological state at the time of intervention, with substantially better outcomes observed in patients with cardiac tamponade than exsanguination. Patients undergoing emergency department RT demonstrated shorter arrest durations, more favourable physiology, and higher survival than those undergoing prehospital RT. There were no survivors beyond 10 minutes of traumatic cardiac arrest. In this prospective national evaluation of RT practice, outcomes were strongly associated with the pathophysiological cause and duration of arrest, and the residual physiology present at the time of intervention. The most favourable outcomes were observed in patients with cardiac tamponade and those undergoing RT before irreversible physiological deterioration.

title: Electroconductive patch promotes heart repair by directing epicardial cells toward endothelial fate.
authorString: Xie Q, Wu D, Li Z, Zou K, Zheng Y, Wang L, Hou H, He Y, Qiu X.
abstractText: Whether epicardium-derived cells (EPDCs) can differentiate into endothelial cells after myocardial infarction (MI) remains unclear. Considering the heart's electrical dependence, we asked if restoring electrical conduction could direct this potential. Using cardiac patches with tunable electroconductivity and genetic fate-mapping approaches in mice, we found that patches matching native myocardial electroconductivity (10-4-10-3 S/cm) specifically promoted proliferation and endothelial differentiation of WT1+ EPDCs, rescuing cardiac function. Single-cell transcriptomic sequencing revealed that electroconductive patches drove WT1+ EPDCs into a distinct WT1+TRPC3+CD93+ transitional state. These cells differentiated into endothelial cells via TRPC3-Ca2+ signaling and integrated into functional vessels. Inhibiting TRPC3 blocked differentiation and reduced infarct vascularization. Thus, improving electrical conduction unlocks and directs the endothelial differentiation of WT1+ EPDCs, offering a strategy for post-MI repair.

title: Sex-specific associations between Mediterranean Diet Score and long-term risk of mortality, dementia and other chronic diseases. 20-year evidence from a Swedish population study of 70-year old individuals.
authorString: Tognon G, Sundh V, Rothenberg E, Samuelsson J, Kern S, Skoog I, Lissner L.

journal.title: The journal of nutrition, health & aging

abstractText: To investigate the association between adherence to the Mediterranean Diet Score (MDS) and the risk of all-cause mortality, cardiovascular disease (CVD), cancer, and dementia morbidity over 10- and 20-year follow-up periods in a population-based cohort of older adults. A prospective population-based cohort study. Gothenburg, Sweden. A total of 1298 participants (56.2% women) aged 70years at baseline from the general population and recruited from the Gothenburg H70 and Population Study of Women in Gothenburg (PSWG) birth cohorts. Dietary intake was assessed via face-to-face, semi-structured diet history interviews. The MDS was calculated based on eight food groups (excluding alcohol). Outcomes were identified through linkage with national health and death registers. Cox proportional hazard models were used, adjusting for BMI, smoking, marital status, physical activity, and education. A higher MDS was associated with a lower risk of 20-year dementia morbidity in men (multivariable-adjusted HR=0.83; 95% CI: 0.71-0.96), but not in women. This association did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple testing, and the sex-by-MDS interaction (p=0.048) was nominally significant, but not robust to multiple testing. No statistically significant associations were found for CVD or cancer morbidity in either sex over the available follow-up (i.e., 10 and 20years, and up to 18years for cancer; 20-year CVD follow-up in men: HR=0.98; 95% CI: 0.88-1.08). For all-cause mortality, an initial association in men at 10years (HR=0.90; 95% CI: 0.82-0.99) was no longer significant after full adjustment (HR=0.92; 95% CI: 0.84-1.01). Higher MDS levels were associated with lower dementia risk in men, but this finding was not robust to multiple testing correction and requires confirmation in larger studies. No association was found with all-cause mortality, CVD and cancer morbidity. A limitation of these findings is that dietary assessment was conducted at a single time point (age 70), and that dementia ascertainment relied on registers which are estimated to miss > 50% of cases, particularly among home-dwellers.

title: Percutaneous Echo-Guided Cervical Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Cannulation by Intensivists in Neonates and Children.
authorString: Moscatelli A, Giardina A, Dato A, Pezzato S, Cheli M, Buratti S, Patroniti NA.

journal.title: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)

abstractText: Cervical cannulation is the standard approach for venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) in neonates and small children but is traditionally performed surgically. We report our initial experience with bedside percutaneous ultrasound- and echocardiography-guided cervical VA-ECMO cannulation performed by intensivists. Three pediatric patients underwent percutaneous right common carotid artery and internal jugular vein cannulation. Vascular access, guidewire advancement, tract dilation, and cannula positioning were guided by ultrasound and transthoracic echocardiography. Median age was 5 months (range, 20 days-6 years) and median weight 7 kg (range, 3-15 kg). Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation was initiated for extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation in two patients and refractory cardiogenic shock in one. Cannulation was successful in all patients without surgical conversion, with a median skin-puncture-to-flow time of 32 minutes (range, 28-35). Target flow (>100 ml/kg/min) was achieved in two patients. No major cannulation-related vascular or cardiac complications occurred. Two patients died on ECMO, while one survived without signs of stroke on follow-up magnetic resonance imaging. Vascular integrity was documented by postmortem examination or Doppler follow-up. Bedside percutaneous echo-guided cervical VA-ECMO cannulation by experienced intensivists appears technically feasible in pediatric patients. Further studies are needed to establish safety, reproducibility, effectiveness, and potential advantages over conventional surgical cannulation.

title: Right Atrial Phasic Function Improves CMR-Based Prognostication in Patients with Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Multicenter Study.
authorString: Wang W, Zhu R, Gao Y, Wang J, Liu W, Liu J, Wu L, Wang W, Bo K, Wang X.
abstractText:
Aims

In multiple cardiovascular diseases, right atrial (RA) function can serve as an independent predictor for the clinical status and prognosis. However, the prognostic value of RA strain in patients with heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF) remains considerably unknown. This study aims to explore the relationships between RA strain derived from cardiac magnetic resonance imaging-feature tracking (CMR-FT) and adverse outcomes in patients with HFmrEF.

Methods and results

This retrospective study enrolled patients with HFmrEF who were referred for echocardiography and CMR at two tertiary medical centers from April 2016 to September 2024. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality, HF-related hospitalization and cardiac transplantation. The findings were validated in a cohort of patients with HFmrEF enrolled from two additional tertiary care centers (January 2019 to January 2025). The development cohort included 1317 patients, and the validation cohort comprised 385 patients. During a median follow-up period of 2.8 years and 2.1 years, respectively, 243 and 72 patients in the development cohort and validation cohort reached the primary endpoint, respectively. Cox regression analysis showed that RA conduit strain was an independent predictor of the primary outcome (HR: 0.86 [0.82, 0.90]; P < .001). The full model integrating clinical variables, traditional imaging, and RA strain achieved the best predictive performance (C-index: 0.80 in development, 0.81 in validation cohorts).

Conclusion

RA conduit strain derived from CMR is an independent predictor of adverse outcomes in patients with HFmrEF, providing incremental prognostic value beyond traditional clinical and imaging-derived risk markers.​.

title: Adjunctive Intracoronary rhTNK-tPA During Primary PCI and Early Regional Left Ventricular Function in STEMI Patients With High Thrombus Burden: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Lai W, Wu L, Liu Q, Li X, Guo Z, Liu N, Wu Y, Wu L, Du S, Guo P.
abstractText: Acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) with high thrombus burden often shows impaired myocardial perfusion despite successful epicardial recanalization. Intracoronary recombinant human TNK tissue-type plasminogen activator (rhTNK-tPA) may reduce microvascular obstruction and preserve ventricular function, but evidence is limited. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 136 STEMI patients with high thrombus burden undergoing primary PCI between May 2022 and February 2025. Patients receiving intracoronary rhTNK-tPA (n=62) were compared with controls receiving standard PCI alone (n=74). The primary endpoint was left ventricular regional wall motion status within 7 days after PCI, assessed by WMSI and normal ventricular wall motion. Secondary endpoints included cTFC, ST-segment resolution, final TIMI flow grade, and clinical and safety outcomes. Baseline characteristics were generally comparable. The rhTNK-tPA group had lower WMSI values (P<0.001) and a higher incidence of normal ventricular wall motion (41.7% vs. 19.6%; P=0.014). rhTNK-tPA was also associated with lower post-PCI cTFC (18.18 ± 6.91 vs. 21.24 ± 9.20; P=0.033) and higher ST-segment resolution (83.9% vs. 68.9%; P=0.043), while final TIMI grade 3 flow was similar. In multivariable analysis, rhTNK-tPA was independently associated with lower odds of ventricular wall motion abnormalities (OR=0.214; 95% CI, 0.106-0.433; P<0.001). MACE were infrequent, and no intracranial hemorrhage occurred. Adjunctive intracoronary rhTNK-tPA during primary PCI was associated with better early preservation of regional wall motion and improved reperfusion indices without an observed increase in major bleeding.

title: Acute kidney injury as a systemic disease.
authorString: Preston HMM, Shemilt R, Chapman FA, Newby DE, Selby NM, Dhaun N.
abstractText: Acute kidney injury (AKI) affects ∼20% of hospitalized patients and is traditionally viewed as a transient complication of acute illness. Evidence suggests that AKI can initiate long-term renal and cardiovascular disease, even when kidney function appears to recover. Survivors of AKI face increased risks of CKD, heart failure, myocardial infarction, and premature mortality, yet post-AKI care remains poorly defined. We synthesize emerging mechanistic and clinical evidence linking AKI to systemic cardiorenal disease and discuss how biomarkers, imaging, and clinical risk prediction may enable identification of high-risk patients and support translational strategies to prevent progression to chronic disease.

title: Climate-sensitive patterns of premature cardiovascular mortality in a subtropical city.
authorString: Carnasciali NMA, Souza FT, Barcellos DDS.
abstractText: This study aimed to investigate climate-sensitive temporal patterns associated with premature mortality due to cardiovascular diseases (CVD), ischemic heart disease (IHD), and acute myocardial infarction (AMI) in a large subtropical city in southern Brazil. Daily premature mortality records (ages 30-69) from 2010 to 2019 were analyzed together with meteorological data, including temperature, humidity, atmospheric pressure, precipitation, wind, and solar radiation, as well as temporally aggregated climatic indicators. An exploratory analytical framework combining multivariate analysis, clustering, and classification rule mining was applied to identify temporal patterns and combinations of climatic conditions associated with mortality outcomes. The approach was designed to support pattern discovery and hypothesis generation rather than causal inference.Linear associations between individual climatic variables and mortality were weak. However, exploratory analyses revealed distinct climate-sensitive temporal patterns. Premature IHD mortality was more frequently associated with colder temperatures, elevated long-term humidity, and specific combinations of atmospheric pressure and temperature. In contrast, AMI mortality showed associations with intermediate maximum temperatures, lower atmospheric pressure, and moderate levels of solar radiation. The classification models demonstrated moderate performance across outcomes, with the highest accuracy observed for AMI, indicating that complex temporal patterns may not be captured by linear analyses alone. The findings demonstrate that climate-sensitive temporal patterns in premature cardiovascular mortality can be identified using exploratory, data-driven approaches. Although causal relationships were not assessed, the results highlight the value of integrating climatic indicators and temporal aggregation into exploratory environmental health research and hypothesis generation. This framework is transparent, reproducible, and applicable to other urban settings, particularly in low- and middle-income countries facing increasing climate variability.

title: Artificial intelligence-based surrogate modeling of hemodynamic indicators in abdominal aortic aneurysms using computational fluid dynamics.
authorString: Suh M, Huh U, Lee C.
abstractText: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a progressive dilatative disease of the abdominal aorta with high rupture-related mortality, emphasizing the need for early risk assessment. Conventional anatomical indicators, such as maximum diameter, are insufficient to characterize rupture risk, motivating the incorporation of hemodynamic parameters. Image-based CFD enables the estimation of these parameters but remains clinically limited by high computational cost and long processing times. To overcome these limitations, deep learning-based surrogate models such as MultiViewUNet have recently been proposed, though previous studies were constrained by relatively low spatial resolution and limited coverage of hemodynamic parameters. In this study, we propose MH-UNet, a multi-view, high-resolution surrogate modeling framework that extends the original MultiViewUNet to a higher input resolution and additional hemodynamic parameters. MH-UNet converts three-dimensional AAA geometries into two-dimensional images from multiple viewing angles and predicts TAWSS, OSI, RRT, and ECAP using data from 101 patients. Both single-inference and dual-inference strategies were implemented and compared. Single-inference consistently outperformed dual-inference across all parameters; the cascaded dual-inference scheme amplified errors through the nonlinear OSI and RRT formulations, resulting in negative R² values for OSI, RRT, and ECAP. Among the single-inference predictions, TAWSS was predicted most reliably (R² = 0.803), whereas OSI was the most challenging to predict. Agreement between single-inference predictions and CFD-derived results demonstrates the potential of MH-UNet as a rapid surrogate tool for estimating WSS-derived hemodynamic indices in AAA under fixed boundary conditions.

title: Stress hyperglycemia impairs FOXK2-dependent macrophage cardiac repair after myocardial infarction.
authorString: Lv H, Liu Z, Feng S, Liu W, Guo Y, Bao K, Shen X, Li Y, Zhou X, Ai D, Yang Q, Zhang Y, Li J.
abstractText: Stress hyperglycemia (SHG) predicts poor outcomes after myocardial infarction (MI), but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we identify FOXK2 as a key regulator of macrophage-mediated cardiac repair. FOXK2 expression was reduced in cardiac macrophages from hyperglycemic mice after MI and in peripheral blood mononuclear cells from patients with MI with SHG, whereas macrophage-specific FOXK2 deficiency aggravated cardiac injury. Under high-glucose conditions, FOXK2 was glycosylated at T552 by O-GlcNAc transferase, promoting its ubiquitin-proteasome-dependent degradation. Mass spectrometry and functional assays showed that the FOXK2T552A variant resisted hyperglycemia-induced degradation. Integrated CUT&Tag and RNA-seq analyses revealed that FOXK2 restrained pro-inflammatory cytokine expression by suppressing H3K27 acetylation. Thus, our findings identify FOXK2 as a critical regulator that supports cardiac repair during hyperglycemia, and targeting excessive FOXK2 O-GlcNAcylation may offer a therapeutic strategy for patients with MI and SHG.
