The present paper describes, to our knowledge, the fifth reported case worldwide of cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum syndrome (CLOCCS) occurring in the context of CP. A review of the previously reported cases was also undertaken to improve understanding of the pathophysiology of this syndrome, its clinical manifestations, imaging features, and prognosis, given the rarity of such presentations in CP.

title: Preclinical Studies of MVT-100, A Novel Ultrasound Enhancing Agent.
authorString: Meuillet EJ, Lusk J, Tadevich H, Lindner JR, Mohammed SA, Ozbay B, Amjad MW, Pacella JJ, Chen X, Sade LE, Villanueva FS, Unger EC.
abstractText: Over the past decades, many investigations have used perfluorocarbon (PFC)-based contrast products to enhance ultrasound (US) imaging. Currently octafluoropropane (OFP), decafluorobutane, and sulfur hexafluoride or a combination of those gases is used for the preparation of ultrasound enhancing agents (UEA). This study reports the development of MVT-100, a novel microbubble ultrasound enhancing agent (UEA) designed for improved stability, safety, and imaging performance. The objective of these studies was to fully characterize and compare the biophysical, chemical and in vivo properties of the new UEA (herein referred to as MVT-100) as compared with the well-known and widely utilized UEA known as perflutren lipid microspheres (Perflutren) (commercialized under the name of Definity®). Analytical methods were used to characterize the MBs. Low mechanical index (MI) contrast-enhanced ultrasound was performed in mice and pigs. Comparison of Perflutren MB with MVT-100 MB showed similarities of the products in their overall particle numbers, gas content, osmolality, pH and phospholipid concentrations. However, MVT-100 exhibited a zeta potential that was essentially neutral (+0.5 ± 0.1 mV), compared with the negative zeta potential of Perflutren (-4.2 ± 2.0 mV), a tighter size distribution and lower polydispersity index (0.114 ± 0.012 vs. 0.159 ± 0.036, p = 0.048). Under accelerated storage conditions (40°C for 4 weeks), MVT-100 demonstrated markedly greater lipid stability, with only 2.05% loss of total phospholipid content compared with 13.10% for Perflutren. Murine renal retention studies showed that MVT-100 MB exhibited significantly lower (∼2.5 fold) renal retention in the kidney as compared with Perflutren. In porcine studies, MVT-100 hemodynamic parameters were identical to those of Perflutren. Echocardiographic porcine studies showed that ventricular opacification and endocardial border delineation following MVT-100 administration were comparable between agents at early time points, with higher and more sustained opacification with MVT-100 at later time points (generalized linear mixed model: main effect of agent p < 0.001, time × agent interaction p < 0.001) and no evidence of a significant difference in acoustic shadowing between agents (p > 0.99). MVT-100 is a novel UEA that exhibits promising properties as a new imaging agent for contrast echocardiography with appealing storage conditions.

title: The Birth of Voice: Acoustic Baselines of Newborn Vocalizations in the First Minutes of Extrauterine Life.
authorString: Holzer M, Bartl-Pokorny KD, Zitta C, Schuller J, Schuller BW, Schwaberger B, Fluhr H, Pichler G, Pokorny FB.

journal.title: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation

abstractText: Newborn crying immediately after birth has traditionally been regarded as a key sign of vitality, reflecting basic cardiovascular and respiratory function. However, initial postnatal vocal behavior not only limited to crying and its underlying mechanisms are not yet fully understood, and systematic acoustic analyses of birth vocalizations (BiVo) are lacking. This study addresses this gap by providing indicative values for established vocalization parameters to comprehensively characterize the very first vocalizations of newborns in a largely homogeneous non-pathological sample. We analyzed publicly available birth videos of 60 vaginally delivered newborns (35 female, 25 male), who exhibited an unremarkable health status. In each video, we manually segmented BiVo during the first 3 minutes after birth, yielding a total of 7681 vocalizations. Each segment was subsequently assigned to one of three predefined vocalization types. On a per-newborn basis, we extracted the number of vocalizations and the time from birth to the respective first vocalization. On a per-vocalization basis, we calculated duration and five standard acoustic parameters, namely mean loudness, harmonics-to-noise ratio, fundamental frequency, jitter, and shimmer. In addition to descriptive analysis, we applied linear mixed-effects models to examine potential sex differences. All analyses were performed both across all vocalizations and separately by vocalization type. We established indicative values, such as a mean number of 128 vocalizations, a mean time of 12 seconds between the time of birth and the first vocalization, a mean vocalization duration of 0.53 seconds, and a mean fundamental frequency of crying vocalizations of 439 Hz. Additionally, we observed sex differences, particularly in the number of vocalizations and the fundamental frequency of crying vocalizations. This work reveals the first comprehensive BiVo characterization and, thereby, represents a fundamental step towards understanding newborn vocal behavior immediately after birth, which is essential for any future attempts to exploit BiVo as a health indicator.

title: Primary cardiac histiocytic sarcoma in a dog.
authorString: Giang NTH, Trang NT, Fuke N, Hirai T, Yamaguchi R.

journal.title: The Journal of veterinary medical science

abstractText: An intact male mixed-breed dog was presented with anorexia and depression. Ultrasonographic examination did not reveal any nodules in the thoracic or abdominal organs. However, several nodules of different sizes were identified in the heart at necropsy, with no gross lesions detected in other organs. Histological examination of the cardiac tissues revealed an accumulation of pleomorphic, round-to-oval phagocytic cells, suggestive of histiocytic origin, which was subsequently confirmed by immunohistochemistry with specific histiocytic antibodies (Iba1 and HLA-DR). Although no gross nodules were observed in the lungs, histologic examination revealed scattered neoplastic cells, indicating metastasis from the primary cardiac lesion. This case represents a rare pathological presentation of primary cardiac histiocytic sarcoma in a dog, expanding the documented anatomical and pathological spectrum of canine histiocytic sarcoma.

title: Temporal Trends, Underuse, and Multilevel Factors Associated With Maximum-Dose Statin Therapy in Acute and Chronic Coronary Syndromes　- A Nationwide JROAD-DPC Study.
authorString: Hayakawa K, Nakao K, Nakao YM, Sumita Y, Kanaoka K, Mitsui K, Murai K, Miura H, Fujino M, Murata M, Takagi K, Yoneda S, Otsuka F, Kataoka Y, Asaumi Y, Miyamoto Y, Yasuda S, Noguchi T.

journal.title: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society

abstractText: High-intensity or maximally tolerated statin therapy has robust evidence for secondary prevention in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and chronic coronary syndrome (CCS), and is strongly recommended in international guidelines. However, comprehensive real-world data on its use and associated factors remain limited. Using data from the JROAD-DPC database (2017-2022), we analyzed ACS and CCS patients who underwent revascularization and were discharged alive. We assessed temporal trends in lipid-lowering therapy and examined associated factors, including patient demographics, comorbidities, treatment strategies, and hospital structural characteristics, using multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression models. Among 358,570 patients with ACS and 392,821 with CCS, the use of maximum-dose statins increased from 8.6% in 2017 to 34.1% in 2022 in ACS and from 7.8% to 19.1% in CCS, but remained suboptimal. After multivariable adjustment, older age, underweight status, and coronary artery bypass grafting were associated with lower use of maximum-dose statins in ACS. In CCS, older age, underweight status, and higher comorbidity burden were associated with lower use of maximum-dose statins. Hospital structural factors, including a higher number of cardiologists, were also associated with a greater use of maximum-dose statins. Maximum-dose statin use among ACS and CCS patients remains suboptimal in Japan. Multilevel factors contribute to this evidence-practice gap, underscoring the need for comprehensive interventions at multiple levels to reduce disparities in care delivery.

title: The Major Iron Transporter DMT1 Promotes Renal Fibrosis by Activating Ferroptosis and Enforcing TGF-β1 Signaling in Renal Tubular Cells.
authorString: Pan Y, Liu M, Qiu J, Jia L, Li M, Gong X, Cao H, Cao H.
abstractText: Renal fibrosis is a common pathological feature of chronic kidney disease (CKD), but effective therapies are still lacking. Ferroptosis has been increasingly associated with CKD; however, the iron-handling proteins that link ferroptotic stress to fibrotic signaling remain poorly defined. Here, we identify the divalent metal transporter 1 (DMT1) as a previously unrecognized regulatory factor that integrates iron metabolism, ferroptotic stress, and transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) signaling in tubular epithelial cells (TECs). DMT1 expression was elevated in TECs from folic acid injection- or unilateral ureteral obstruction-induced mouse CKD models and in isolated primary TECs exposed to TGF-β1 or palmitic acid, accompanied by increased mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) production. Pharmacological inhibition or genetic deletion of DMT1 in TECs significantly attenuated renal fibrosis, with reduced renal fibrosis area, decreased expression of profibrotic genes and markers, lower mtROS production, and restored fatty acid oxidation. DMT1 deficiency also attenuated lipid peroxidation, with reduced 4-HNE levels and lipid droplet deposition in mouse CKD models. Additionally, DMT1 deletion reduced tissue iron content, reversed ferroptosis-associated morphological changes in TECs, and restored tissue glutathione peroxidase-4 expression. Notably, DMT1 deletion reduced both total Smad2 and phosphorylated Smad2 induced by TGF-β1, consistent with suppression of the TGF-β1-Smad axis. These findings support a model in which tubular DMT1 integrates iron overload, ferroptotic stress, and TGF-β1-Smad signaling during fibrotic progression in CKD. DMT1 functions as a signaling hub contributing to TGF-β1-Smad axis activation, although a direct causal chain from iron influx to transforming growth factor beta receptor 1 induction remains to be fully delineated. DMT1 inhibition may offer a tubular-selective therapeutic strategy for CKD. Antioxid. Redox Signal. 00, 000-000.

title: Multifaceted Physiological Roles of Lipoproteins and Understanding Atherosclerosis: Crosstalk Between Lipoproteins and Bioactive Lipids.
authorString: Kurano M.
abstractText: Traditional management of atherosclerosis focuses primarily on cholesterol and triglycerides; however, lipoproteins also transport bioactive lipids that critically regulate systemic inflammation and metabolic health. This review highlights the diverse physiological and clinical roles of apolipoproteins and bioactive lipids beyond classical lipid accumulation. First, we discuss how hepatic transporters NPC1L1 and ABCG5/8 modulate glucose metabolism and handle non-cholesterol lipids, including phytosterols. Second, we emphasize the apolipoprotein M (ApoM) and sphingosine 1-phosphate (S1P) axis. ApoM protects S1P from degradation and directly mediates the pleiotropic benefits of high-density lipoprotein (HDL), including anti-apoptotic, antithrombotic, and renoprotective effects. Third, reverse translational research utilizing genome-wide association studies identifies apolipoprotein D (ApoD) as a key anti-inflammatory modulator. Finally, clinical lipidomics underscores the importance of "minor" lysophospholipids, such as lysophosphatidylinositol and lysophosphatidylserine, alongside lysophosphatidic acid in the pathogenesis of acute coronary syndrome. Understanding the dynamic crosstalk between lipid transporters, apolipoproteins, and bioactive lipids provides novel mechanistic insights into cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, paving the way for innovative biomarkers and precision therapeutic strategies.

title: Neural, vascular, motor and autonomic habituation to high-intensity auditory stimulation: A multimodal characterization of the human defensive responses.
authorString: Muñoz V, Angulo-Ruiz BY, Gómez CM.

journal.title: International journal of psychophysiology : official journal of the International Organization of Psychophysiology

abstractText: The defense reflex has been extensively characterized across sensory modalities; however, the integration of electrical, neurovascular, motor, and peripheral autonomic responses involving the central and autonomic nervous systems remains poorly understood. This study investigated defensive responses to high-intensity auditory stimulation using a multimodal approach combining electroencephalography (EEG), functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), and peripheral physiological measures. Participants were exposed to twenty white-noise bursts (100 dB, 500 ms, instantaneous rise time) separated by silent intervals (50 ± 10 s), grouped into five blocks to assess initial responses and habituation. Hemodynamic responses revealed widespread activation of bilateral auditory and frontal regions following stimulus onset, with a progressive reduction in response amplitude and extension of active channels across blocks. Network analysis suggests progressive reorganization of functional connectivity between sensory and frontal regions across repeated stimulation. At the peripheral level, habituation was observed in phasic electrodermal activity, vascular indices, motor response, EEG-derived ocular activity, and parasympathetic cardiac modulation, primarily after the first block, whereas respiratory measures remained stable. Cardiac defense-like responses show a multi-temporal component structure, with habituation restricted to the late decelerative phase. Multivariate analyses revealed a structured yet partially independent organization of neural and autonomic responses to habituation. Together, these findings provide a comprehensive characterization of multisystem responses to intense auditory stimulation, highlighting selective habituation across central, neurovascular, motor, and autonomic systems, and offering new insights into how neurovascular and peripheral processes adapt to repeated auditory threats.

title: Towards a digital twin for precision diabetes care: a phenotypic mapping and virtual representation of a person living with type 1 diabetes in the SFDT1 study.
authorString: Oliveira M, Aguayo G, Canha D, Benhamou PY, Briet C, Imberti CC, Disse E, Hadjadj S, Hanaire H, Jeandidier N, Joubert M, Page ML, Lucidarme N, Naccache A, Potier L, Renard E, Saade MB, Schaepelynck P, Sola A, Verges B, Riveline JP, Cosson E, Fagherazzi G, SFDT1 study group.
abstractText: T1D is clinically heterogeneous, yet its key parameters are still largely interpreted in isolation. As a first step towards developing a digital twin for T1D, we aimed to build a phenotypic mapping and virtual representation of a person living with T1D (PwT1D) usable at the individual level. We analysed baseline data from 2,187 adults with T1D in the SFDT1 cohort using Discriminative Dimensionality Reduction via learning a Tree (DDRTree). Twenty-five sociodemographic, clinical, biochemical, and continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) variables were used to construct a low-dimensional structure. Structural reproducibility and individual projection were assessed in an unseen set of 235 participants. Cardiovascular disease (CVD) and end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) risks were computed with the Steno T1 Risk Engine. We identified seven interpretable sub-phenotypes, ranging from well-controlled profiles to profiles characterized by poor glycaemic control, metabolic abnormalities, social vulnerability and a high burden of micro- and macrovascular complications. An independently fitted map for the additional participants showed a similar overall branching structure and comparable clinical patterns, and individual projection was accurate (R² 0.85-0.98). A multilingual application enables exploration of the phenotypic map, individual projection, and estimation of Steno risk scores. This phenotypic mapping and virtual representation capture clinically meaningful heterogeneity and let care teams locate and explore individual profiles. It provides the foundation for an AI-enabled digital twin an interpretable virtual representation that integrates a person's clinical, biological, glycaemic, and social profile and supports individualized decisions - and a practical clinical decision-support tool for precision diabetes care.

title: P2X7 receptor-mediated inflammatory and ionic remodeling promotes atrial fibrillation in diabetes.
authorString: Fu Y, Ke Y, Cao Z, Chen Y, Long X, Li Y, Guo K, Luo Y, Hu K, Zhao Q.
abstractText:
Aims

Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a major risk factor for atrial fibrillation (AF), yet the mechanisms by which diabetic metabolic stress promotes atrial arrhythmogenesis remain incompletely understood. Recent evidence suggests that purinergic signaling-driven sterile inflammation plays an important role in cardiac remodeling. This study aimed to investigate the role of the ATP-gated purinergic P2X7 receptor (P2X7R) in DM-associated AF and to explore its underlying mechanisms.

Methods and results

Rats were randomly assigned to four groups: control (Con), diabetes mellitus (DM), P2X7R overexpression in controls (Con+P2X7), and P2X7R knockdown in diabetic rats (DM + P2X7 KD), with gene manipulation achieved using AAV9-cTnT vectors. AF susceptibility, atrial structural and electrical remodeling were systematically evaluated using electrophysiological studies, optical mapping, patch-clamp recordings, and molecular analyses. DM markedly increased AF inducibility and duration, accompanied by enhanced sympathetic nerve activity and activation of P2X7R-related inflammatory signaling. Compared with controls, DM atria exhibited pronounced interstitial fibrosis, connexin remodeling, delayed atrial activation, slowed conduction velocity, and increased conduction heterogeneity. Atrial P2X7R overexpression in control rats recapitulated key arrhythmogenic features, whereas P2X7R KD in diabetic rats significantly attenuated atrial remodeling and reduced AF susceptibility, without altering the diabetes-induced increase in sympathetic activity. At the cellular level, P2X7R selectively modulated INa, ICa,L, and IKur while relatively preserving Ito, and was associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and disturbed Ca2+ homeostasis, characterized by increased mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, loss of mitochondrial membrane potential, increased cytosolic Ca2+ signals, and reduced mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake.

Conclusion

P2X7R-mediated inflammatory and mitochondrial signaling contribute to diabetic atrial remodeling and AF susceptibility. Targeting P2X7R may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for preventing AF in diabetes.

title: Procedure-specific bleeding risk assessment: a multidisciplinary expert consensus companion to the 2026 periprocedural anticoagulant management guidelines.
authorString: Godier A, Roullet S, Lanoiselée J, Aim F, Alantar A, Assouline J, Atallah S, Badet R, Baroncini M, Berdah S, Beyer L, Blanchet MC, Bouchard D, Brenet E, Buffenoir K, Carsuzaa F, Alegria GC, Chauleur C, Cazato L, de Parades V, Delambre J, Destrieux L, Drissi F, Ejeil AL, Fautrel B, Fauchier L, Favier V, Fiard G, Fieux M, Gouin F, Guyot M, Hermann R, Hersant B, Herrero A, Higuero T, Hulet C, Iung B, Juguet F, Karsenti D, Kobeiter H, Lafon A, Lahlou G, Langbour C, Lefevre J, Lescaille G, Lustig S, Mabrut JY, Maggiori L, Mege D, Meneveau N, Merlot I, Moreddu E, Moszkowicz D, Deballon PO, Phulpin B, Pigot F, Poghosyan T, Rabarin F, Radoi L, Rouillon JM, Sapoval M, Soudan D, Teissier N, Vidal V, Vincentelli A, Motte S, Blais N, Bonhomme F, Bourguignon A, Cohen A, de Maistre E, Douillet D, Fontana P, Huet DG, Godon A, Gouin-Thibault I, Gruel Y, Jebara S, Lasne D, Laporte S, Lecompte T, Le Gal G, Martin AC, Mazighi M, Mismetti P, Morange P, Mullier F, Nguyen P, Pernod G, Rosencher N, Roy PM, Schved JF, Sié P, Susen S, Tacquard C, Vardon F, Zufferey P, Mariat C, Mansour A, Albaladejo P.
abstractText: Periprocedural anticoagulant management requires balancing thrombotic risk against procedure-specific bleeding risk. Existing procedure bleeding risk classifications are fragmented across specialties, inconsistent in methodology, and rarely extend beyond a few procedural domains, limiting their clinical applicability. To develop a comprehensive, standardized, procedure-specific bleeding risk classification to accompany the 2026 GIHP-SFAR periprocedural anticoagulant management guidelines. A formal multidisciplinary consensus was conducted under the auspices of GIHP and SFAR, in collaboration with 24 surgical and interventional specialty societies. For each procedural domain, a working group performed a systematic literature review. Procedures were classified into four tiers: no bleeding risk, low bleeding risk, high bleeding risk, and very high bleeding risk. A specific category was created for procedures carrying particular contextual risk (e.g., anatomical site, patient factors, or need for reversible anticoagulation). Consensus was reached by the full expert panel. Twenty-four procedural domains were classified, ranging from regional anaesthesia and digestive endoscopy to cardiac surgery, neurosurgery, and ophthalmology. Each domain provides a procedure-specific bleeding risk table, with narrative supporting evidence. Procedures warranting delayed resumption of anticoagulation (≥72 hours) or use of short-acting/reversible anticoagulants are identified. The classification covers common and complex surgical scenarios, including those with limited published evidence where structured expert opinion was applied. This companion document provides clinicians with a standardized, evidence-based, procedure-specific bleeding risk framework across 24 domains to support individualized periprocedural anticoagulant decisions in daily practice.

title: Mixed-reality-assisted training for vascular anastomosis: An exploratory pilot study.
authorString: Taguchi R, Kowatari R, Minakawa M.
abstractText: This exploratory pilot study aimed to explore the feasibility of mixed reality (MR)-assisted vascular anastomosis training for clinical clerks and to obtain preliminary data on technical performance and learner experience compared with conventional instruction using illustrated handouts. Twelve fifth-year medical students were assigned to either the MR group (n = 6), which used a head-mounted display, or the control group (n = 6), which used printed handouts. After a standardized lecture, participants performed end-to-side vascular anastomosis twice using latex grafts. Technical performance was assessed using a 10-item original scale informed by the Objective Structured Assessment of Technical Skills and the End-Product Rating Score. Subjective feedback was collected after each session using a paper-based, author-developed questionnaire. Total scores did not differ significantly between the two groups in either the first session (28.3 ± 3.1 vs 32.0 ± 2.5, p = 0.106) or the second session (31.8 ± 2.8 vs 30.7 ± 1.7, p = 0.467). The total score increased within the MR group (p = 0.034), although the between-group difference in score change was not statistically significant (p = 0.263). Questionnaire responses indicated greater initial mental fatigue in the MR group, which decreased with repeated use. This exploratory pilot study provides preliminary support for the practical feasibility of incorporating MR-assisted guidance into vascular anastomosis training. Initial mental fatigue and possible device-familiarization effects are practical considerations. Larger, adequately powered studies are needed to determine the comparative educational efficacy of MR.

title: Impact of Angiographic Lesion Distribution on Walking Therapy Outcomes in Lower Extremity Artery Disease.
authorString: El Kaddouri R, Colle A, Cornelis N, Fois L, Shala A, Cornelissen V, Fourneau I.
abstractText:
Aim

To investigate whether angiographic lesion distribution and disease severity influence outcomes of walking therapy in patients with lower extremity artery disease (LEAD) and intermittent claudication (IC).

Methods

In this prospective, single-center cohort study, patients with IC participated in a 12-week hybrid progressive walking program consisting of one supervised treadmill session and two home-based walking sessions per week. Baseline evaluation included assessment of ankle-brachial index (ABI), angiographic imaging (CTA or MRA), and functional exercise testing. Pain-free walking distance (PFWD) and maximal walking distance (MWD) were assessed using standardized treadmill protocols. Angiographic lesion distribution was classified according to lesion location, while disease severity was graded using the ANGIO score.

Results

Thirty-three patients (mean age 69.1 ± 9.4 years, 75.8% male) with available angiographic imaging were included in the present analysis. After three months, PFWD increased from 173 m to 304 m, an increase of 131 m (p < 0.001), and MWD increased from 448 m to 627 m, an increase of 179 m (p < 0.001). Lesion distribution was not significantly associated with changes in PFWD (p = 0.059), and no statistically significant differences were observed for MWD (p = 0.44). Disease severity, expressed by the ANGIO score, was not correlated with walking improvements (ρ = -0.10, p = 0.57 for PFWD; ρ = 0.10, p = 0.56 for MWD).

Conclusion

Walking therapy significantly improved walking capacity in patients with LEAD. In this exploratory cohort, no statistically significant associations were observed between angiographic lesion distribution or disease severity and improvements in walking distance. However, the small overall sample size and limited number of patients within several lesion distribution groups preclude firm conclusions regarding the influence of lesion characteristics on treatment response. These findings should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in larger studies.

title: Early Morphological Changes in Superficial Varicose Veins After Endovenous Radiofrequency Ablation.
authorString: Keles E, Ayvat Ocal Z.
abstractText: To quantify early changes in untreated varicose tributaries and treated saphenous veins after isolated radiofrequency ablation (RFA) and to assess 3-month technical outcomes. This retrospective cohort included 133 patients undergoing RFA of the great saphenous vein (GSV; n=120) or small saphenous vein (SSV; n=13). The primary outcome was within-patient change in the largest untreated varicose tributary diameter from baseline to approximately 3 months. The same radiologist reassessed the anatomically documented site. We used paired analyses, bootstrap confidence intervals, and multivariable analysis of covariance with robust standard errors. Median tributary diameter decreased from 14.2 mm (IQR, 10.5-21.0) to 11.0 mm (IQR, 7.4-14.2). The median within-patient reduction was 3.0 mm (IQR, 0.9-5.8; 95% bootstrap CI, 2.2-3.7; p<0.001). Completion DUS confirmed closure of the proximal treated saphenous segment and patency of the adjacent deep vein in all patients. At approximately 3 months, complete occlusion was present in 99 of 120 GSVs (82.5%) and all 13 SSVs. The remaining 21 GSVs had short-segment partial recanalization with residual reflux near the saphenofemoral junction; none had complete recanalization. In an exploratory adjusted analysis, diabetes mellitus was associated with a 1.15-mm larger 3-month GSV diameter (95% CI, 0.23-2.07; p=0.015). Isolated RFA was associated with an early reduction in untreated varicose tributary diameter. These anatomical findings suggest that reassessment before adjunctive tributary treatment may be reasonable; however, clinical benefit cannot be inferred without patient-reported outcomes. The association between diabetes and 3-month GSV diameter is hypothesis-generating.

title: Dysfunction of three CD36 variants is due to impaired glycosylation and trafficking.
authorString: Tillison EA, Jovanovic V, Luu QQ, Chen Y, Sahoo D.
abstractText: CD36 deficiency is characterized by the loss of CD36 due to genetic mutations. Clinical studies have associated CD36 deficiency with hyperlipidemia, insulin resistance, and cardiomyopathy. However, the structural and functional effects of human CD36 variants remain poorly understood. P90S is a causative mutation of CD36 deficiency while E123K and S127L are of unknown significance and typically found in malarial endemic regions. Despite their variable phenotypes, they are all located in the same structural region of CD36. In this study, we expressed these three naturally occurring human CD36 variants in HEK293 cells and found that all variants exhibited impaired oxLDL binding and uptake that was associated with reduced expression, shortened half-lives, and altered glycan processing, consistent with defects in receptor maturation. Inhibition of proteasomal or lysosomal pathways did not restore variant stability, suggesting that reduced receptor abundance is not mediated by a single canonical degradation pathway. All variants exhibited reduced membrane accumulation without enrichment in specific intracellular compartments, indicating impaired trafficking rather than selective retention. These findings provide mechanistic insight into the regulation of human CD36 expression, maturation, and trafficking, and the functional consequences of genetic variation.

title: Outcomes After Curative-intent Resection of Synchronous Primary Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC): Two is Worse than One.
authorString: Seyoum N, Eaton DB, Brennan L, Rossetti NE, Schoen MW, Thomas TS, Chang SH, Tokaz M, Yan Y, Patel MR, Baumann AA, Kreisel D, Nava R, Meyers BF, Kozower BD, Heiden BT, Puri V, Brandt WS.

journal.title: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery

abstractText: Outcomes following curative-intent resection of synchronous primary lung cancer (SPLC) remain incompletely defined. We compared recurrence and survival in SPLC versus solitary primary tumors among patients with clinical stage I non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Retrospective cohort study of Veterans undergoing curative-intent resection for clinical stage I NSCLC in the Veterans Health Administration (2006-2020). SPLC was defined as two distinct clinical stage I NSCLC tumors diagnosed within six weeks, with curative-intent treatment of both tumors within one year. Propensity score matching (PSM) (1:1) was used to compare patients with SPLC to those with solitary tumors. The primary outcome was cumulative incidence of recurrence (CIR); secondary outcomes were overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS). Additional analyses examined the role of adjuvant treatment and drivers of recurrence in SPLC patients. Of 12,606 Veterans with resected clinical stage I NSCLC, 337 (2.7%) had SPLC. SPLC presented with larger tumors and more advanced pathologic stage. Histology was discordant between the two tumors in 44.2% of SPLC cases. In the propensity-matched cohort (281 pairs), SPLC was associated with higher CIR (HR 1.51, 95% CI 1.10-2.07), worse DFS (HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.03-1.50), and worse OS (HR 1.21, 95% CI 1.01-1.45). Within SPLC, wedge resection of both tumors was independently associated with recurrence. After adjustment, SPLC was associated with higher recurrence and worse survival than solitary tumors, supporting recognition of SPLC as a higher-risk phenotype within clinical stage I NSCLC.

title: Interstage Reinterventions in Hybrid Stage I Palliation - Impact on Survival to Comprehensive Stage II Operation.
authorString: Wride J, Bigelow AM, Wright LK, Texter K, Salavitabar A, Camacho M, Abdelshahid M, Davidson E, Bolling S, Richardson C, Alvarado C, Carrillo SA, McConnell P, Yerebakan C, Galantowicz M.

journal.title: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery

abstractText:
Objective

The need for interstage reinterventions is one of the perceived limitations of Hybrid Stage 1 Palliation (HS1P). We aim to evaluate the impact of unplanned interstage reinterventions on survival to comprehensive stage II (CS2) and characterize their frequency, type, and timing.

Methods

We retrospectively reviewed 199 infants who underwent HS1P at a single institution from 2009 to 2025, tracking all reinterventions between HS1P and CS2. We assessed the likelihood of reaching CS2 using a series of Fine-Gray models at distinct landmarks to assess competing risks, comparing reintervention and non-reintervention groups.

Results

The reintervention rate in our study was 43%, with 132 unique reinterventions received in 86 patients. In the reintervention group, progression to CS2 was 78%, with 4.7% of patients dying after HS1P. Among the 33 patients (17%) who died after HS1P, 88% did not receive reinterventions and 76% died prior to HS1P discharge. Reinterventions before 90 days post-HS1P were associated with no difference in progression to CS2 (sHR 1.20, CI 0.83-1.74), but reinterventions before 150 days post-HS1P were associated with a decreased likelihood of reaching CS2 (sHR 0.61, CI 0.41-0.93). The most common reintervention target was the retrograde aortic arch (45%), with aortic atresia in 72% of these patients.

Conclusions

Interstage reinterventions after HS1P are common, but, if done early, do not appear to worsen survival to comprehensive stage II. Reinterventions play an integral part of HS1P care rather than a marker of failure, especially when performed early.

title: Fecal microbiota transplantation and its role in aging of rats: Behavioral and pathological evidence.
authorString: Ahangari A, Tukmechi A, Hadian M, Mahmoudi S, Babaei-Balderlou F.
abstractText: Aging is associated with progressive oxidative stress, chronic inflammation and functional deterioration across multiple organs. Increasing evidence suggests that the gut microbiota plays a pivotal role in regulating aging through the gut-brain axis and systemic immune interactions. The present study investigated the therapeutic potential of fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) in a D-galactose-induced rat model of accelerated aging. Male rats were allocated into four experimental groups: Healthy control, D-galactose-induced aging, aging treated with FMT and aging treated with antibiotics prior to FMT. Accelerated aging was induced by intraperitoneal administration of D-galactose (150 mg/kg/day). FMT was performed using fecal microbiota obtained from healthy donor rats. Cognitive performance was assessed using the Morris Water Maze (MWM), and histopathological alterations were evaluated in the heart, hippocampus and colon using hematoxylin and eosin staining. D-galactose administration significantly impaired spatial learning and memory and induced marked pathological alterations, including myocardial edema and hemorrhage, neuronal degeneration and vacuolation in the hippocampus, and crypt disruption with inflammatory cell infiltration in the colon. FMT markedly improved behavioral performance and substantially attenuated tissue damage in all examined organs. In contrast, antibiotic pretreatment was associated with less pronounced improvement following FMT, suggesting that the recipient intestinal environment may influence the response to transplantation. These findings provide behavioral and histopathological evidence consistent with beneficial effects of FMT on several features of accelerated aging; however, direct changes in microbial composition, microbial function, and donor engraftment were not assessed.

title: Vascular Surgery is Overrepresented by Multiple Medical Societies Compared to its Peers.
authorString: Tulimieri M, Eagleton MJ, Yassa E, Ascher E, Kashyap VS.
abstractText: Medical societies play an important role in representing physicians and their interests. Our objective was to compare the number, size, and fiscal strength of vascular societies compared to other cardiovascular specialties. All information was found via a systematic Internet search and with publicly available data (i.e. www.aamc.org). Medical societies representing vascular surgery (VS), cardiology (CARD), cardiothoracic surgery (CTS), and interventional radiology (IR) in the United States were compared. Board-certified physicians (www.abms.org) and publicly available financial information were tabulated (www.ProPublica.org). Board-certified vascular surgeons (n=4464) can choose to join 30 VS societies (4 national, 10 regional, 12 city/state, 4 other). In comparison, 12 societies (2 national) represent CTS (n=5869) and 16 (1 national) represent IR (n=4032) physicians. Cardiologists (n=22843) are represented by 14 (5 national) societies and an additional 27 chapters of a parent national society. The available number of vascular surgeons per national society is markedly lower than comparative specialties. Vascular societies generated $23M in revenue compared to $52M for CTS, $6M for IR, and $1.03B for CARD. CARD societies have 93% of total revenue for these four specialties and 52 times the revenues compared to VS societies. Compared to similar specialties, VS has few surgeons, yet a high number of medical societies. This segmentation may dilute the educational, governmental, societal, and patient advocacy impact of VS compared to its peers.

title: Coronary vascular dysfunction is associated with adverse left ventricular filling in patients with angina but no obstructed coronary arteries.
authorString: Oneglia AP, Wei J, Samuels B, Samuel TJ, Sharif B, Azarbal B, Petersen JW, Cui Y, Takahashi T, Handberg E, Pepine CJ, Merz CNB, Nelson MD.
abstractText:
Background

Angina with no obstructive coronary arteries is often due to coronary vascular dysfunction, which is increasingly described as a contributor and predictor of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. We tested the hypothesis that coronary vascular dysfunction contributes to cardiac dysfunction.

Methods

Sixty-eight participants with suspected coronary vascular dysfunction underwent LV pressure-volume assessment at rest and during isometric handgrip stress. Coronary function testing was performed by infusing standard doses of adenosine, acetylcholine, and nitroglycerine through a guiding catheter placed in the left main coronary artery, per established protocols.

Results

Of the participants studied, 12 had normal coronary vascular function while 56 had coronary vascular dysfunction. At rest, there were no differences between groups in any invasive pressure or volumetric measurement. With isometric handgrip, peak filling rate increased significantly in participants with normal coronary vascular function (0.56 ± 0.31 vs. 0.85 ± 0.68 1/s/mmHg) but remained unchanged in participants with coronary vascular dysfunction (0.51 ± 0.22 vs. 0.55 ± 0.43 1/s/mmHg; group x time interaction, p = 0.04). Moreover, left ventricular end-diastolic pressure decreased significantly with isometric handgrip in participants with normal coronary vascular function (12 ± 3 vs. 9 ± 4 mmHg) but increased in participants with coronary vascular dysfunction (14 ± 4 vs. 15 ± 6 mmHg; group x time interaction, p = 0.03).

Conclusions

Coronary vascular dysfunction was associated with an impaired ability of the LV to adapt its filling during stress. Further work is needed to assess potential clinical significance.

title: Association of circumferential dissection on computed tomography angiography with preoperative rupture in type A aortic dissection.
authorString: Xia Y, Mei J, Yao P, Shen X, Wang J, Li R, Yan T, Li C, Zhu J, Ge Y.
abstractText:
Background

To investigate the association between circumferential dissection on computed tomography angiography (CTA) and preoperative rupture in patients with type A aortic dissection (TAAD).

Methods

This retrospective cohort study included 597 consecutive patients diagnosed with TAAD at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. Patients were classified into circumferential dissection (n = 130) and non-circumferential dissection (n = 467) groups based on preoperative CTA. Clinical, laboratory, and imaging characteristics were compared between groups. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to examine factors independently associated with preoperative rupture, and between-group differences in preoperative rupture were compared.

Results

Circumferential dissection was strongly associated with DeBakey type I dissection, supra-aortic branch involvement, and greater false-lumen expansion with true-lumen compression. Preoperative rupture occurred more frequently in patients with circumferential dissection than in those without (33.8% vs 7.1%, P < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression demonstrated that circumferential dissection was independently associated with preoperative rupture ascertained by bedside echocardiography following the admission CTA after adjustment for demographic, laboratory, and imaging factors (OR = 5.24, 95% CI: 1.86-14.76, P = 0.002).

Conclusion

Circumferential dissection on CTA is independently associated with preoperative rupture and may support timely surgical decision-making in TAAD.

title: From receptor architecture to outcome maturity: a clinical framework for multiorgan incretin therapy.
authorString: Sztanek F, Lőrincz H, Nagy AC, Harangi M.

journal.title: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists

abstractText:
Objective

To propose a clinically usable framework that separates receptor architecture and metabolic potency from the maturity of patient-relevant outcome evidence for incretin-based therapies.

Methods

This Commentary draws on recent cardiovascular, kidney, heart failure, peripheral artery disease, liver, and emerging polyagonist evidence to define outcome maturity across five domains: endpoint directness and clinical relevance; study design and evidentiary confidence; comparator and population context; follow-up duration, durability, and safety; and molecule-, dose-, and indication-specific applicability.

Results

Four qualitative states of outcome evidence are proposed: preliminary, emerging, established, and mature. These categories apply to a specific molecule, dose, indication, phenotype, and outcome question and are intentionally nonnumeric. Outcome maturity does not measure treatment-effect magnitude or comparative drug efficacy. A six-step clinical workflow links the dominant organ-risk phenotype, clinically meaningful outcome, evidence maturity, applicability, treatment sustainability, and proportionate clinical positioning.

Conclusion

Receptor architecture defines biological potential, whereas outcome maturity characterizes the directness, robustness, durability, and applicability of clinical evidence. Clinical positioning should remain proportional to phenotype-specific evidence and should not convert differences between nonaligned trials into cross-trial efficacy rankings.

title: A 3D Mitral Valve Interstitial Cell Model Recapitulates Selected Transcriptomic Signatures of Degenerative Mitral Valve Disease.
authorString: Zhao Y, Chen Y, Ding R, Zhang M, Chen S, Tang Q, MacRae VE, Zhu D, Liu M.
abstractText: Degenerative mitral valve disease (DMVD) is a highly prevalent cardiovascular disorder in humans, dogs and pigs. However, the molecular mechanisms driving mitral valve interstitial cell (VIC) activation and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling remain incompletely understood. In this study, we established a three-dimensional (3D) VIC-collagen model (VIC-COL) to investigate the cellular changes of VIC activation and ECM remodeling in response to transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1) stimulation. The results revealed that upregulation of α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA), fibronectin and matrix metalloproteinase 2 (MMP2) was induced by TGF-β1 in the VIC-COL model; subsequent transcriptomic profiling identified a significant phenotypic shift toward pro-inflammatory and matrix remodeling pathways. Crucially, comparative transcriptomic analysis with naturally occurred DMVD public datasets identified 120 shared Gene Ontology (GO) biological process pathways and 111 conserved differentially expressed genes. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway analysis confirmed that TGF-β1 treatment in the porcine in vitro model recapitulates a subset of the transcriptional features of DMVD, including the cell adhesion molecules, ECM-receptor interactions, tumor necrosis factor (TNF) signaling and cytokine-cytokine receptor interactions. Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) further corroborated concordant Hallmark inflammatory signatures, including TNF-α signaling via nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB), and interleukin-6/Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (IL-6/JAK/STAT3) signaling. These shared transcriptomic features indicate that TGF-β1 stimulation captures certain molecular aspects of ECM remodeling, VIC activation, and inflammatory-related signaling seen in naturally occurring DMVD. Collectively, the 3D VIC-COL system provides a reproducible in vitro platform for investigating selected molecular mechanisms of DMVD.

title: Long-term outcomes of cyanoacrylate closure alone versus combined high saphenous ligation and cyanoacrylate closure in large-diameter great saphenous veins.
authorString: Baltacı H, Duman ZM, Taçyıldız SY, Taçyıldız C, Azboy D.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: J Vasc Surg Venous Lymphat Disord
journal.title: Journal of vascular surgery. Venous and lymphatic disorders
journal.isoabbreviation: J Vasc Surg Venous Lymphat Disord

abstractText: Long-term evidence regarding the effectiveness of cyanoacrylate closure (CAC) in large-diameter great saphenous veins (GSVs) is limited. This study aimed to compare the long-term outcomes of CAC alone with those of combined high saphenous ligation and cyanoacrylate closure (HSL + CAC) for large-diameter GSV insufficiency. This single-center retrospective cohort study evaluated 198 extremities in 180 patients treated for symptomatic GSV insufficiency between January 2018 and December 2022 who had a preoperative GSV diameter of ≥8 mm. CAC was performed in 127 extremities and HSL + CAC in 71. Clinical and long-term duplex outcomes were compared using generalized estimating equation (GEE) models that accounted for within-patient clustering and prespecified confounders. Propensity score overlap weighting (PSOW) was used as a sensitivity analysis. Long-term duplex follow-up data were available for 186 extremities (93.9%). HSL + CAC was associated with greater GSV occlusion (84.1% vs 65.8%; P = .007), less saphenofemoral junction (SFJ) reflux (5.8% vs 47.0%; P < .001), a lower postoperative Venous Clinical Severity Score (VCSS; 2.45 ± 2.04 vs 3.15 ± 1.89; P = .019), and greater VCSS improvement (3.45 ± 2.21 vs 1.47 ± 1.93; P < .001). Reoperation was performed in 8.7% of extremities treated with CAC alone but in none treated with HSL + CAC (P = .008). In adjusted GEE analyses, HSL + CAC was associated with a lower postoperative VCSS (β, -1.15; 95% CI, -1.71 to -0.59), greater GSV occlusion (OR, 3.05; 95% CI, 1.31-7.14), and less SFJ reflux (OR, 0.06; 95% CI, 0.015-0.223). PSOW estimates were consistent with the primary analyses. Complication rates were low and similar in both groups. In large-diameter GSVs, HSL + CAC was associated with better long-term anatomic and clinical outcomes than CAC alone, without an appreciable increase in complications. These findings suggest that adding HSL to CAC may improve long-term outcomes in selected patients with large-diameter GSVs.

title: Words under the skin: Physiological responses to interoceptive metaphors.
authorString: Montalti M, Cazzato V, Cuccio V.
abstractText: Embodied accounts of language propose that linguistic meaning is grounded in sensorimotor systems. While previous research has focused on the central nervous system, the involvement of the autonomic nervous system (ANS) in language comprehension remains underexplored. To fill this gap, we investigated whether processing interoceptive metaphors, namely figurative expressions referring to internal bodily sensations (e.g., 'I feel butterflies in my stomach'), modulates the ANS. Forty-five healthy participants read interoceptive metaphors and non-bodily-related literal sentences while cardiac, electrodermal, and respiratory signals were continuously recorded. We further distinguished between two types of interoceptive metaphors, depending on whether the interoceptive element served as the target (INT-target, e.g., 'I feel butterflies in my stomach') or source domain (INT-source, e.g., 'I thirst for success' to convey ambition) of the metaphor. Results revealed subtle but measurable effects: compared to non-bodily-related literal sentences, interoceptive metaphors were associated with higher heart rate variability and longer inspiratory duration. No significant differences emerged between INT-target and INT-source metaphors. These findings provide the first evidence that language grounded in internal bodily experience is associated with subtle differences in selected autonomic indices relative to non-bodily-related literal sentences.

title: Mediating role of frailty in the association between systolic blood pressure trajectories and catastrophic health expenditure among middle-aged and older adults: A longitudinal cohort study.
authorString: Liu W, Yin Z, Li K.

journal.title: The journal of nutrition, health & aging

abstractText:
Background

Routine hypertension management primarily targets acute cardiovascular events, frequently overlooking progressive physiological decline (frailty) and its economic implications. This study aimed to identify systolic blood pressure (SBP) trajectories and evaluate the mediating role of frailty in their association with catastrophic health expenditure (CHE) among middle-aged and older adults.

Methods

We analyzed 3996 participants from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). Group-based trajectory modeling identified SBP evolution patterns (2011-2015). The 2015 Frailty Index (FI), based on a 27-item deficit accumulation model, served as the mediator. The primary outcome was CHE in 2018, defined as annual household healthcare expenditure exceeding 40% of the household's capacity to pay. Mediation analysis quantified total, direct, and indirect effects.

Results

Three SBP trajectories emerged: "Low-stable" (50.0%), "Moderate-increasing" (41.3%), and "High-decreasing" (8.7%). Compared with the Low-stable group, the High-decreasing trajectory was significantly associated with higher 2015 FI scores (β=0.029, P<0.001). A statistically significant indirect effect through frailty was observed for the association between the High-decreasing trajectory and CHE in 2018 (ACME = 0.0084, 95% CI: 0.0031-0.0100, P < 0.001), although the direct and total effects were not statistically significant. Findings were similar in sensitivity analyses using alternative CHE definitions and BMI trajectories.

Conclusions

Frailty may be one pathway linking the High-decreasing SBP trajectory with subsequent household CHE. These observational findings support considering functional health alongside blood pressure in middle-aged and older adults. Further prospective studies are needed to clarify the temporal and causal relationships and to assess whether incorporating frailty assessments into cardiovascular management improves clinical and socioeconomic outcomes.

title: Beyond l-arginine: Uncovering L-tryptophan's cardiovascular therapeutic potential.
authorString: Ozguven K, Karunalia E, Stanley CP.
abstractText: Loss of nitric oxide (•NO) bioavailability is a defining feature of cardiovascular disease (CVD), yet therapies targeting this pathway alone have shown limited success. Here, we argue that l-tryptophan (Trp) catabolism, particularly via indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase-1 (IDO1), represents an underappreciated, mechanistically distinct route to restoring vascular health. Beyond its canonical immunoregulatory role, IDO1-derived metabolites directly modulate plaque stability, blood pressure, and placental vascular function through a variety of signalling mechanisms, positioning Trp catabolism as a genuine complement to l-arginine-nitric oxide biology rather than a peripheral curiosity. Therapeutic strategies range from dietary supplementation to gene delivery and small-molecule catalytic modulators are now emerging, with some already in clinical use for other indications. Although full of potential, the field has key gaps that need addressing, including the potential roles of other enzymes (tryptophan 2,3-dioxygenase [TDO] and indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase-2 [IDO2]), while sex-specific effects remain almost entirely unexplored. In this review, we present the evidence supporting the potential therapeutic benefits of this pathway, highlight therapeutic strategies, and identify key gaps to be addressed to facilitate advancement in the field.

title: Elevated YKL-40 and associations of inflammatory profiles with metabolic parameters in pediatric heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia under pharmacological lipid-lowering therapy.
authorString: Mair KS, Baumgartner-Kaut M, Nigmann C, Neyer M, Andrea S, Greber-Platzer S, Zeyda M.
abstractText:
Introduction

Excess LDL-cholesterol and chronic inflammation accelerate atherosclerosis in familial hypercholesterolemia (FH). In pediatric FH, the inflammatory phenotype, its role in cardiovascular risk stratification and its alterations under lipid-lowering therapy remain poorly understood. Therefore, we comprehensively profiled systemic inflammatory markers in pediatric heterozygous FH (HeFH) under different treatment modalities and investigated associations with liver enzymes and lipid parameters.

Methods

For this exploratory cross-sectional study, we prospectively enrolled 49 children with HeFH grouped as newly diagnosed, treatment-naïve (n = 11), diet-treated (n = 10) and pharmacologically treated with statins ± ezetimibe (n = 28), and 16 unaffected controls (overall median age 11 years; 58.8% female). Fasting blood samples were analyzed for routine laboratory parameters and quantification of 37 inflammatory markers using a multiplex immunoassay.

Results

While traditional inflammatory markers (CRP, IL-6) did not differ between groups, the macrophage activation marker chitinase-3-like protein 1 (YKL-40) was nominally elevated in pharmacologically treated patients vs. controls (p = 0.037). In this subgroup, markers of tissue remodelling and bone metabolism (osteopontin, osteocalcin) as well as immune activation (sCD30, sCD163) showed robust correlations with alkaline phosphatase and liver enzymes. Additionally, soluble TNF receptor 2 correlated inversely with HDL-cholesterol (r = -0.574, p = 0.009) and apolipoprotein A1 (r = -0.607, p = 0.009).

Conclusion

In conclusion, pediatric HeFH patients receiving pharmacological therapy may exhibit persistent, potentially atherogenic macrophage activation reflected by elevated YKL-40 despite effective lipid lowering. The observed associations between immune markers and hepatic and bone metabolic parameters suggest pleiotropic effects of statins ± ezetimibe independent of lipid lowering.

title: Greenspace utilization and obesity burden in urban America: Multi-city analysis with validation in a clinical cohort.
authorString: Chandra Mouli S, Zhang T, Ardakani J, Chen Z, Rajagopalan S, Zhang K, Maddock JE, Nasir K, Dong W, Al-Kindi S.
abstractText: Greenspace engagement is a crucial environmental determinant of obesity, yet evidence remains mixed across urban contexts. Most studies use static measures of greenness, which may mischaracterize pathways through which greenspace influences obesity. This study explores how greenspaces affect obesity across major U.S. metropolitan areas (MSAs) and how these effects vary across cities. Cross-sectional ecological analysis of census tract-level data across nine U.S. metropolitan areas, with validation using a clinical cohort from the Houston Methodist Cardiovascular Disease Learning Health System Registry. Census tract-level data across nine U.S. MSAs were analyzed, integrating greenspace visits, adult obesity prevalence, vegetation (NDVI), demographics, food deserts, and health covariates. Linear models (OLS) estimated adjusted associations, while multiscale geographically weighted regression (MGWR) models assessed neighborhood-level variation. Results were validated using patients' Body Mass Index (BMI) data from the Houston Methodist Registry. The analytic sample included over 15,000 tracts across nine MSAs. In adjusted OLS models, seven MSAs demonstrated inverse associations, with Houston exhibiting the strongest. MGWR analyses revealed substantial within-metro heterogeneity across all MSAs, reflecting neighborhood context, particularly in relation to density, nutrition, and structural constraints. In the Houston Methodist cardiovascular cohort (n = 1,049,782), higher visitation was associated with lower obesity burden. Each additional visit was associated with lower odds of obesity across BMI levels, demonstrating a consistent association across increasing levels of severity. Across U.S. metros, greater greenspace engagement was generally associated with lower obesity prevalence, though associations were not spatially uniform. These findings highlight the importance of actual greenspace use and local context in evaluating the role of urban environments in shaping obesity risk.

title: Quantum Sensing Technologies for Ultrasensitive Biomarker Detection in Biomedical Diagnostics from Fundamental Principles to Clinical Translation.
authorString: Krishnamoorthy U.
abstractText: Quantum sensing technologies offer unprecedented detection sensitivities down to single-molecule, attomolar detection limits and thus are emerging as transformative tools for ultra-sensitive biomarker detection in biomedical diagnostics. This comprehensive review synthesizes insights from over 380 plus studies to provide recent advances in quantum sensor platforms, examining the fundamental quantum mechanical principles that enable enhanced sensitivity, and surveys a diverse range of quantum sensing technologies along with their applications across the biomedical field. Specifically, nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, quantum dots, superconducting quantum interference devices (SQUIDs), and other quantum sensing modalities applied to biomarker detection for cancer diagnostics, cardiovascular disease, neurological disorders, and infectious disease detection are reviewed. Further, the key technical challenges that hurdle their clinical translation are critically evaluated. The review results demonstrate that quantum-enhanced biosensors have achieved detection limits of the order of magnitude below conventional methods. Intrinsic to their capabilities, several quantum sensing platforms have progressed to clinical testing and early commercialization efforts. Specifically, for point-of-care diagnosis, early disease detection, and personalized medicine.

title: Digital System Physiology: Integrating Mechanistic Models, Artificial Intelligence, and Digital Twins.
authorString: Mohsen Y, Trayanova NA.
abstractText: A measurement tells us something about physiology only when a model interprets it, and only when that model keeps the features that matter: organization across scales, feedback, adaptation, and coupling between organs. We use the term digital system physiology for a current version of systems physiology that links many kinds of measurement, mechanistic computation, and artificial intelligence with a clear method for reasoning from data to conclusions and a preset rule for updating. Cardiac electrophysiology is the most developed clinical example. Cardiorenal, metabolic, pulmonary, and neural models are useful but less mature. In all of these areas, the evidence is stronger for mechanistic insight, individualized simulation, and early clinical feasibility than for better patient outcomes. We separate how well a model predicts from how well it explains, and we propose working criteria in which prediction and being built to inform a decision define a twin, with the cadence of updating set by the clinical question rather than by a fixed rule. Progress from here will depend on tracking each patient's state over time, coupling organs together only where it helps, stating uncertainty openly, testing models on data they were not built from, and gathering prospective evidence that matches the intended use.

title: Harnessing AI for Hypothyroidism Monitoring Using Wearable-Derived Heart Rate Data: Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Shin K, Jung Y, Yoo WS, Kim MJ, Oh TJ, Moon JH, Kong SH, Lee WW, Moon JH.
abstractText: Hypothyroidism is a prevalent endocrine disorder characterized by an insidious onset and nonspecific symptoms, often leading to significant diagnostic delays. While biochemical thyroid function tests (TFTs) are the gold standard, their invasive nature and cost make them impractical for continuous, proactive screening of at-risk populations. Thyroid hormones exert direct chronotropic effects on the cardiovascular system, and their levels are closely correlated with heart rate (HR). Wearable devices capable of continuous HR monitoring offer a novel opportunity for noninvasive, digital phenotype-based detection. This study aimed to develop and validate an AI-assisted system that uses wearable-derived sleep HR data as a digital monitoring tool for individuals at risk of hypothyroidism, helping identify those who warrant further confirmatory thyroid testing. This retrospective cohort study used 1677 paired observations consisting of sleep HR data and serum TFT results, including free thyroxine (T4) and thyroid-stimulating hormone levels, from 413 participants (mean age 43.1, SD 9.7 y; women: n=314, 76%). Participants wore consumer-grade wearables (Fitbit) that recorded HR and sleep data. Each TFT result was paired with sleep HR data extracted from the 15 consecutive nights preceding the blood test. An AI system was developed using a gradient boosting algorithm (LightGBM) to classify thyroid status by integrating baseline TFT results with statistical and temporal HR features. The model's performance was evaluated using patient-level leave-one-out cross-validation. To examine the benefit of longitudinal data, performance was compared using 1, 2, or 3 prior paired observations as reference points. To ensure clinical relevance and avoid performance inflation from hyperthyroid cases, we prioritized the analysis of a subset containing only euthyroid and hypothyroid data (n=744 paired observations). In this clinically challenging subset, the system achieved an accuracy of 74.6%, with a sensitivity of 82% and a specificity of 73.5% using a single-reference data pair. Incorporating longitudinal HR patterns further enhanced performance; using 3 reference pairs improved accuracy to 78.1% (sensitivity 81.8% and specificity 77.7%). In the overall dataset (n=1677 paired observations), the system demonstrated an accuracy of 80.8%, with a sensitivity of 82% and a specificity of 80.8% using a single-reference pair. Notably, the system achieved high clinical safety by detecting 96.3% of severe overt hypothyroidism cases (free T4 <0.5 ng/dL). This AI-assisted system demonstrates the feasibility of a sensitive, noninvasive longitudinal monitoring tool for hypothyroidism, robustly identifying a high proportion of hypothyroid cases-particularly severe ones-to prioritize at-risk individuals for confirmatory blood tests. Given the predominantly female iatrogenic-withdrawal cohort, prospective sex-balanced validation in primary hypothyroidism is warranted.

title: Presynaptic filopodia form kinapses and promote convective membrane flow to sustain synchronous neurotransmitter release.
authorString: Jain A, Dong R, Kroll J, Webster JF, Moss J, Bikbaev A, Ultanir SK, Gonzalez-Sulser A, Rosenmund C, Heine M, Liu J, Cousin MA, Ivanova D.
abstractText: Synaptic plasticity is the principal mechanism by which neural circuits compute and adapt. Presynaptic plasticity is traditionally regarded as a transient adaptation of the synaptic vesicle fusion and recycling machinery, whereas the role of structural remodeling of synaptic boutons remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate a mechanical coupling between presynaptic structural remodeling and synaptic efficacy. We find that dynamic presynaptic filopodia emerge during active synaptic transmission and deform synaptic boutons while forming transient contacts with postsynaptic structures, which we term neuronal kinapses. Filopodia formation is activity dependent and occurs in intact circuits and human brain. Mechanistically, filopodial growth induces convective in-plane membrane flow toward the filopodium, accelerating release site clearance, a process associated with sustained release probability during repeated synaptic vesicle fusion. As a result, filopodia formation favors an increase in synchronous over asynchronous neurotransmitter release. These results indicate that presynaptic structural remodeling can alter the spatial organization of neurotransmission and, through the membrane flow it generates, modulate its temporal precision.

title: A systematic pan-cancer analysis of intratumoral microbiota-derived epitopes to inform cancer immunotherapy and prevention.
authorString: Li D, Wang H, Guo J, Leng F, Zhi X, Gong M, Zeng M, Liu K, Sun Y, Li Y, Zhang Y, Xu J.
abstractText: Intratumoral microbial antigens, which mimic tumor antigens, can be presented by human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules, thereby eliciting antitumor immune responses. However, a comprehensive pan-cancer characterization of such molecularly mimicking microbial epitopes is still lacking. Here, we construct a pan-cancer microbial epitope landscape from 1190 samples across 24 cancer types. Pan-cancer analyses reveal that microbial epitopes exhibit higher hydrophobicity, aliphatic indices, and stability than human epitopes. Nine HLA-I alleles tend to bind microbial epitopes, and HLA-C alleles show a stronger tendency to present microbial epitopes than HLA-A and HLA-B alleles. Moreover, we reveal that microbial species capable of generating HLA-I epitopes are more prevalent in tumors, that broadly detected epitopes span more cancer types, and that multiple microbial genera generate numerous immunogenic epitopes. Notably, homologous microbial epitopes and tumor antigens elicit cross-reactive T cell responses, and experimental evidence demonstrates that microbial epitopes exhibit enhanced immunogenicity and antitumor efficacy. Overall, our findings provide a foundation for microbial epitope vaccine development, offering insights for cancer prevention and therapy.

title: Diet quality and blood pressure among adults with hypertension living in a high-altitude region of the Peruvian Andes.
authorString: Tarazona-Meza C, Matsuzaki M, Williams KN, Caulfield LE, Bromage S, Cordova-Ascona L, Underhill LJ, de Las Fuentes L, Cuentas-Canal GM, Vela-Clavo Z, Chiang M, Geng EH, Dávila-Román VG, Hartinger SM, Checkley W.
abstractText: Diet quality plays an important role in the management of non-communicable diseases, including hypertension. A better understanding of dietary profiles in high-altitude populations with hypertension could help improve the effectiveness of interventions. We aimed to characterize diet quality and its association with blood pressure among adults with hypertension living at high-altitude. Cross-sectional study of baseline data from an ongoing trial in Puno, Peru. We enrolled 154 adults with hypertension participating in a community health worker-led intervention aimed at improving hypertension management in a high-altitude region of Peru. Diet was assessed by 24-hour recalls which were analyzed to calculate the Global Diet Quality Score (GDQS, range 0 - 49 with higher scores indicating better diet quality) and categorized into quartiles. We assessed blood pressure using a digital oscillometric tensiometer. We used multivariable linear regression to study the association between diet quality and blood pressure adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics, food security status, hypertension awareness and treatment, BMI, HbA1c and lifestyle habits. We further stratified the analyses by hypertension awareness and treatment. Mean ± standard deviation (SD) age of participants was 66.5 ± 10.9 years and 51.9% were females. Overall mean GDQS was 15.7 ± 3.4 points. While no statistically significant association in the overall sample in multivariable models, we found an inverse association between GDQS quartiles and systolic blood pressure (adjusted mean difference of -4.13 mmHg, 95% CI: -7.72 to -0.53 p-trend = 0.03) among participants who were aware of having hypertension and receiving treatment (n = 102). We found that study participants had generally low diet quality based on GDQS. Among those aware of and receiving treatment for hypertension, higher GDQS scores were associated with lower systolic blood pressure.

title: Peripheral perfusion index combined with end-tidal carbon dioxide in predicting sustained return of spontaneous circulation in adults with in-hospital cardiac arrest: A prospective observational study.
authorString: Zhong H, Gou X, Xu N, Li L, Du X, Gong Y, Kou Z, Zhou M.
abstractText: To evaluate the associations of peripheral perfusion index (PI) and end-tidal carbon dioxide (PETCO2), individually and in combination, with sustained return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) in adults with in-hospital cardiac arrest, and to assess their predictive performance. This prospective observational study included 125 adults with in-hospital cardiac arrest, of whom 62 achieved sustained ROSC and 63 did not. Measurements obtained after ROSC or termination of resuscitation were excluded. Changes in PI and PETCO2 during resuscitation were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Event-average PI and PETCO2 were evaluated for their ability to predict sustained ROSC using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. The combined model was internally validated using 2,000 bootstrap resamples. The median time to ROSC was 11 min (IQR, 5-20). Significant group-by-time interactions were observed for both PI and PETCO2 (both P < 0.001). Event-average PI was higher in the ROSC group than in the non-ROSC group [0.62% (IQR, 0.42-0.90) vs. 0.37% (0.31-0.52)], as was event-average PETCO2 [15.5 mmHg (12.2-17.8) vs. 12.0 mmHg (10.4-13.7)] (both P < 0.001). The areas under the ROC curve (AUCs) were 0.756 (95% CI, 0.670-0.842) for PI, 0.753 (95% CI, 0.666-0.839) for PETCO2, and 0.808 (95% CI, 0.731-0.886) for their combination. The optimism-corrected AUC for the combined model was 0.800. Pairwise comparisons showed no significant differences among the AUCs. In the exploratory fully adjusted model, PETCO2 remained independently associated with sustained ROSC (adjusted OR, 1.626; 95% CI, 1.148-2.302; P = 0.006), whereas PI was not statistically significant (adjusted OR, 1.359 per 0.1% increase; 95% CI, 0.962-1.920; P = 0.082). Higher PI and PETCO2 during resuscitation were associated with sustained ROSC. Combining PI with PETCO2 yielded numerically better discrimination than either measure alone, although the differences in AUC were not statistically significant. External validation is needed before the combined model can be applied in clinical practice.

title: TRPM7 modulates endothelial cell functions and VEGFA-associated signaling in diabetic foot.
authorString: Cheng Y, Jia L, Sheng L, Han X, Zhao Y.
abstractText: Endothelial dysfunction is a central contributor to the development of diabetic foot complications. However, the regulatory mechanisms underlying impaired vascular endothelial cell (VEC) function in diabetic foot remain incompletely understood. Transient Receptor Potential Melastatin 7 (TRPM7) is implicated in cardiovascular pathology, yet its role in diabetic foot-related endothelial impairment is unclear. Primary VECs were isolated from foot vascular tissues obtained from control participants and patients with DFUs and identified by CD31 and factor VIII immunofluorescence. Proliferation, apoptosis, migration, and in vitro tube formation were quantitatively assessed. TRPM7 was overexpressed in control-derived VECs and knocked down using shRNA in DFU-derived VECs. TRPM7 expression and VEGFA-AKT-ERK-related proteins were evaluated using RT-qPCR and Western blotting. Advanced glycation end products (AGEs) and inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) concentrations in conditioned culture supernatants were measured by ELISA. Compared with control-derived VECs, DFU-derived VECs exhibited reduced proliferation, migration, and tube formation, together with increased apoptosis and elevated conditioned-supernatant AGE and iNOS protein concentrations. TRPM7 expression was higher in DFU-derived VECs. TRPM7 overexpression in control-derived VECs induced a dysfunctional cellular phenotype, whereas TRPM7 knockdown in DFU-derived VECs partially restored proliferation, migration, and tube formation and reduced apoptosis. TRPM7 manipulation was also accompanied by changes in VEGFA expression and AKT and ERK phosphorylation, indicating an association between TRPM7 status and dysregulated VEGFA-AKT-ERK-related signaling. In primary human VEC cultures, increased TRPM7 expression was associated with impaired endothelial proliferation, migration, and tube formation and with altered VEGFA-related AKT/ERK signaling. This supporting TRPM7 as a candidate regulator of endothelial dysfunction under diabetic-foot-related conditions.

title: Assessment of the Kidney Size in the African American Population of Children and Adolescents With Sickle Cell Hemoglobinopathy: A Matched Pair Analysis.
authorString: Shaoba ABS, Zhang Y, Gruessner A, Nnaji O, Mongia A, Bamgbola O.
abstractText: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is caused by a variant of the beta-globin gene that produces sickling of the red blood cells. A parallel increase in cardiac output from the ensuing hemolytic anemia leads to glomerular hyperfiltration and progressive nephromegaly. Our goal is to examine the impact of SCD morbidity on the kidney size using kidney ultrasonography. We studied 31 African Americans with SCD with ages between 3 and 20 years, along with 57 age, sex, weight, height and body mass index-matched controls who were seen in an outpatient clinic from January 2018 to December 2022. We examined the impact of genotype variants and the morbidity score of hemoglobinopathy on kidney size. The comparison of the kidney size of matched SCD children with healthy controls showed a larger volume (P<0.0001). A unit increase in SCD morbidity score was associated with a 5.7 cm3 and 5.1 cm3 increase in the volume of the right and left kidneys, respectively. The impact of hyperfiltration on nephromegaly in SCD, compared with healthy controls, was suggested by a higher estimated glomerular filtration rate value among subjects with more severe hemoglobinopathy. The larger volume amongst subset with HBSS compared with those with the HBSC genotype confirmed the is observation.

title: Beliefs about Hereditary Susceptibility to Cancer and Desire to Know about a Genetic Predisposition: An Analysis of the NCI Health Information National Trends Survey.
authorString: Hatch AN, Medina HN, Schlumbrecht MP, Calfa C, Borja NA, Moreno PI.

journal.title: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology

abstractText: This study characterized beliefs about hereditary susceptibility to cancer and desire to know about a genetic predisposition to cancer in a nationally representative survey of US adults. Adjusted regression models using weighted survey analysis of NCI HINTS 2020 data assessed predictors of how much respondents (1) believe genes that are inherited determine whether a person will develop cancer and (2) would want to know if they had a genetic change that increases their chance of getting cancer. On average, respondents endorsed between "somewhat" and "a lot" for how much hereditary susceptibility determines cancer risk. Respondents believed that hereditary susceptibility to cancer, cardiovascular disease, and diabetes were similar (Means= 1.83-1.85, all p>0.6). Individuals who had health insurance (β=-0.42 - -0.37, p=0.017-0.021) and previously sought cancer information (β=-0.19, p<0.001) believed in greater hereditary susceptibility to cancer, whereas those who self-reported good health believed in less hereditary susceptibility to cancer (β=0.16, p=0.022). Individuals who believed in greater hereditary susceptibility to cancer (β=0.14, p=0.001), previously sought cancer information (β=-0.19, p=0.002), had a family history of cancer (β=-0.19, p=0.005), were less fatalistic (β=-0.08, p=0.036), and were Hispanic (β=-0.25, p=.009) or Black (β=-0.47, p<0.001) endorsed a greater desire to know about a genetic predisposition to cancer. Efforts are needed to improve understanding of hereditary susceptibility, address fatalistic beliefs and misinformation, facilitate disclosure of family cancer history indicative of a potential genetic predisposition to cancer. Efforts are needed to improve access to genetic counseling and testing through education and targeted interventions.

title: Massive Mediastinal Hematoma After Reablation for Atrial Fibrillation.
authorString: Huang C, Yang L, Jiang Z, Tian L, Tian Y, Liu Q, Yang Y, Yang Q.
abstractText:
Background

Mediastinal hematoma is a rare but severe complication of atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation. We present a case of a massive mediastinal hematoma following reablation for AF in a patient with a history of cardiac surgery.

Case summary

A 70-year-old woman with rheumatic heart disease, prosthetic aortic and mitral valves, and mild thalassemia underwent catheter ablation for recurrent AF. She developed acute dyspnea and orthopnea 30 hours after the procedure. Computed tomography angiography revealed a 69.2 mm × 51.1 mm hematoma, compressing the left atrium. Conservative management was initiated, including blood transfusion and diuretics. The patient's symptoms improved within 2 days, and subsequent imaging demonstrated complete resolution of the hematoma at 12-month follow-up.

Discussion

The occurrence of the massive hematoma could be attributed to preexisting atrial fibrosis and pericardial adhesions from prior cardiac surgery, potential vascular fragility and platelet dysfunction because of thalassemia, challenges in accessing the scarred atrial septum, thermal injury to the left atrial roof, and the perioperative hemodynamic changes.

Take-home message

For patients with a history of cardiac surgery and thalassemia, vigilance for mediastinal hematoma is essential following catheter ablation procedures.
