title: Homozygous mutation of desmocollin-2 in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy with mild palmoplantar keratoderma and woolly hair.
authorString: Simpson MA, Mansour S, Ahnood D, Kalidas K, Patton MA, McKenna WJ, Behr ER, Crosby AH.
abstractText:
Objectives

The phenotypic triad of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC) associated with palmoplantar keratoderma and woolly hair has been previously associated with homozygous mutations in both plakoglobin and desmoplakin, which are both critical components of the desmosome. We present here a clinical and genetic study of a consanguineous pedigree in which 2 siblings present with ARVC with left ventricular involvement and associated mild palmoplantar keratoderma and woolly hair.

Methods

Clinical evaluation of the 2 patients and their family members was undertaken along with a homozygosity-mapping approach to identify the relevant gene and sequencing analysis to identify the causative mutation.

Results

The homozygosity-mapping approach excluded the involvement of both plakoglobin and desmoplakin in this pedigree. However, an extended region of homozygosity in both affected cases was revealed at the chromosome 18 desmocollin/desmoglein cluster, genes which encode components of the desmosome. Sequence analysis of the democollin-2 gene, located within this cluster, revealed a homozygous single-base deletion in exon 12 (1841delG). This mutation is predicted to lead to a frame shift and a premature termination codon at position 625 (S614fsX625).

Conclusions

This is the first reported case of a mutation in desmocollin-2 associated with autosomal recessive ARVC.

title: Haemodynamic and Respiratory Effects of Dexmedetomidine as an Adjuvant to Oxycodone Patient-Controlled Analgesia After Lumbar Spinal Fusion: A Post Hoc Analysis of the DoseRespDex Randomised Controlled Trial.
authorString: Mäkelä S, Saari TI, Löyttyniemi E, Aantaa R, Liukas A, Uusalo P.
abstractText:
Purpose

Dexmedetomidine has been studied as an adjunct to opioid patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) because of its opioid-sparing properties and limited respiratory depression. However, potential dose-dependent haemodynamic effects should be considered, and data on dexmedetomidine administered via PCA remain limited.

Methods

In this post hoc analysis of a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 98 adults undergoing lumbar spinal fusion were randomised 1:1:1:1 to 24-h PCA with oxycodone 1 mg/mL alone (D0; placebo referring to normal saline replacing dexmedetomidine in the PCA syringe) or combined with dexmedetomidine 2.5 μg/mL (D2), 5 μg/mL (D5) or 10 μg/mL (D10). Outcomes of interest for the present analysis included mean arterial pressure (MAP), heart rate (HR), respiratory parameters and adverse events. Plasma dexmedetomidine concentrations were analysed as a pre-planned pharmacokinetic sub-analysis.

Results

Mean changes over time differed significantly between groups for MAP (p = 0.005) and HR (p < 0.001). Plasma dexmedetomidine concentrations increased across the D2, D5 and D10 groups, with observed median peak concentrations of 0.15, 0.31 and 0.55 ng/mL in D2, D5 and D10. Over 72 h, MAP was lower in D5 versus D0 (-11.2 mmHg, 95% confidence interval [CI] -19.9 to -2.5, p = 0.004) and D10 versus D0 (-9.1 mmHg, 95% CI -17.4 to -0.8, p = 0.032). All dexmedetomidine doses reduced HR versus D0 (D2: -10.2; D5: -9.9; D10: -11.9 bpm; all p < 0.01), without differing from each other. Haemodynamic changes resolved by 48 h. No bradycardia occurred, and no between-group differences were detected in the measured respiratory variables.

Conclusion

Dexmedetomidine as an adjunct to oxycodone PCA produced transient haemodynamic effects without differences in bradycardia or in the measured respiratory variables. Although higher doses resulted in higher plasma concentrations, the magnitude of haemodynamic effects did not follow a clear dose-response pattern in the range studied. Dexmedetomidine 5 μg/mL combined with oxycodone 1 mg/mL may represent a reasonable candidate dose for further investigation.

Editorial comment

In this post hoc analysis of patients undergoing posterolateral spinal fusion, adjunctive dexamethasone (2.5, 5 or 10 mg/mL), administered alongside oxycodone PCA (1 mg/mL), resulted in a transient, minor decrease in mean arterial blood pressure and in heart rate at the highest doses, with no effect on respiratory parameters and with no adverse events. No correlation between plasma concentrations of dexmedetomidine and haemodynamic parameters was demonstrated.

Trial registration

NCT02454881, EudraCT 2014-003252-31.

title: High-Throughput Chromosome Conformation Capture Immunoprecipitation in Skeletal Muscle Stem Cells.
authorString: Massenet J, Caputo L, Nicoletti C, Nicolau M, Barajas JR, Puri PL.
abstractText: Fate determination of muscle stem cells (MuSCs) is associated with the regulation of gene expression across multiple layers of chromatin organization, ranging from local chromatin accessibility to higher-order three-dimensional (3D) genome architecture driven by transcription factors, architectural proteins, and histone marks. Advancements in chromosome conformation capture (3C) technologies have facilitated the mapping of regulatory interactions with increasing precision. HiChIP-based genome-wide detection of chromatin interactions mediated by chromatin-bound proteins or histone modifications provides an optimal genomic reference for high-resolution detection of changes in 3D genome architecture. However, analyzing the regulation of chromatin conformation defined by specific proteins and integrating it robustly with chromatin accessibility and gene expression remains technically challenging in MuSCs. In this chapter, we present a reproducible workflow to generate a HiChIP dataset from a limited number of MuSCs. Finally, we provide integration tools/workflow to integrate HiChIP datasets with ATAC-seq and RNA-seq datasets.

title: Acute Profound Hypotension Following Intraoperative Plasma Transfusion-A Case Series.
authorString: Batz T, Nordström J, Hertzberg D, Brismar V, Kåhlin J, Hedberg M, Von Oelreich E, Jonsson Fagerlund M.
abstractText:
Background

Blood transfusions can be lifesaving but carry risks of serious adverse reactions, including the less recognized hypotensive transfusion reaction, characterized by hypotension that may be difficult to distinguish from other transfusion reactions or haemorrhage-related shock. At the Karolinska University Hospital, an increased incidence of perioperative hypotensive transfusion reactions without typical allergic features has been observed during recent years. The aim of this study was to identify and describe common clinical characteristics among patients who experienced perioperative transfusion reactions.

Methods

This case series utilized data from a local quality registry at the Karolinska University Hospital, Sweden, covering the period from June 2024 to June 2025. Data collected included patient demographics, relevant clinical parameters and summaries of each reaction. Descriptive statistics were applied to identify potential common traits.

Results

Seventeen patients with perioperative transfusion reactions were included. All but one developed hypotension and in 11 cases hypotension was the sole manifestation. None of these 11 showed elevated serum tryptase levels. All patients except one received plasma via a Belmont Rapid Infuser RI-2 and seven patients also received packed red blood cells. In 11 cases, the blood pressure drop occurred immediately after plasma infusion. During this period, the Belmont Rapid Infuser was withdrawn after 7 months. No reactions were reported in the 4 months following withdrawal. However, reactions recurred following subsequent device use.

Conclusion

Most transfusion reactions were characterized by profound and immediate hypotension following plasma transfusion, often presenting as isolated hypotension without biochemical or clinical evidence consistent with IgE-mediated anaphylaxis. A temporal association with the use of the Belmont Rapid Infuser RI-2 was observed. These findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating, warranting further prospective mechanistic and safety studies.

Editorial comment

Hypotensive transfusion reactions are uncommon but clinically important, and may be mistaken for bleeding or anaphylaxis. This case series describes 17 perioperative cases, mainly presenting as abrupt isolated hypotension after plasma administration. The absence of device-use denominators, signs of anaphylaxis in most patients and the incomplete, delayed calcium measurements mean that other mechanisms cannot be separated from a device-related effect. The main message for practice is therefore active vigilance when using a rapid plasma infusion device.

title: Effects of Walnut Consumption on Inflammatory Cytokines and Adipokines in Adults: A Systematic Review and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Mashayekhi G, Ashtary-Larky D, Karimi M, Asbaghi O, Kalajahi AK, Shouhani Z, Moghadam OF, Rezaeyeh AP, Hosseini A, Naderian M.

journal.title: Journal of human nutrition and dietetics : the official journal of the British Dietetic Association

abstractText:
Background

Inflammation and dysregulation of adipokines play key roles in the development of metabolic and cardiovascular disorders. Walnuts (Juglans regia L.), rich in polyunsaturated fatty acids, fiber, and antioxidants, may modulate inflammatory and metabolic pathways; however, evidence from interventional studies remains inconsistent. This systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis aimed to determine the effects of walnut consumption on inflammatory cytokines and adipokines in adults.

Methods

A comprehensive literature search was conducted in databases through July 2026 to identify relevant randomized controlled trials (RCTs) examining the effects of walnut intake on C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), adiponectin, and leptin. Weighted mean differences (WMDs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled. Subgroup, sensitivity, and non-linear dose-response analyses were performed.

Results

The pooled analysis of 24 RCTs (2068 participants) showed that Walnut intake was associated with a small reduction in CRP concentrations (WMD: -1.0 mg/dL; 95% CI: -1.9 to -0.1; p = 0.031) and IL-6 concentrations (WMD: -0.11 pg/mL; 95% CI: -0.20, -0.01; p = 0.028). However, sensitivity analyses indicated that this finding was not robust to the exclusion of several influential studies. No significant effects were observed for TNF-α (WMD: 0.21 pg/mL, p = 0.306), adiponectin (WMD: -0.17 ng/mL, p = 0.678), or leptin (WMD: 1.39 ng/mL, p = 0.314). Subgroup analyses revealed more potent anti-inflammatory effects with interventions lasting more than 12 weeks and doses above 50 g/day.

Conclusions

Walnut consumption may be associated with small reductions in CRP and IL-6 levels, without significant effects on TNF-α or adipokine concentrations. However, these effects are modest, and their clinical relevance remains uncertain.

title: Adjusting for Medication Use in GWAS and Its Impact on Mendelian Randomisation Analyses: An Example of Systolic Blood Pressure in UK Biobank.
authorString: Yap AJY, Hanson AL, Griffith GJ, Sanderson E.
abstractText: Medication use is common in large-scale population cohorts, and can modify phenotypic traits of interest. This can potentially bias effect estimates in genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and impact downstream analyses such as Mendelian randomisation (MR). The best approach to account for medication use in GWAS is unclear. In this study, we compared seven different methods of adjusting for antihypertensive use in a systolic blood pressure (SBP) GWAS of 407,960 White British individuals in the UK Biobank. We found that direct adjustments to measured SBP (adding constants, class-specific constants, censored normal regression) in general yielded a greater number of genome-wide significant variant associations and unmasked stronger GWAS effect estimates than unadjusted measures of SBP. Adjustment for class-specific constants showed the greatest difference relative to unadjusted GWAS. Restriction methods which limit the sample to either untreated individuals or age ranges with low levels of antihypertensive use had less power, due to reduced sample sizes. Effect estimates of treated individuals were deflated relative to untreated individuals, demonstrating the importance of medication adjustment. In MR analyses, we found no substantial differences in inverse-variance weighted (IVW) estimates when using differing exposure GWAS methods in estimation of the effect of SBP on coronary artery disease. Larger variations in IVW estimates were observed for the causal effect of body mass index on SBP across adjustment approaches. This suggests that bias may arise in MR analyses when the exposure included in the estimation affects the probability of treatment. Finally, we demonstrate that medication adjustment can reveal potentially novel genetic loci, offering additional insight into the biology of a trait.

title: Cynomolgus Monkey (Macaca fascicularis) Embryo Models: From Developmental Benchmarks to Functionally Testable Embryoids.
authorString: Jeong Y, Byun J, Moon SH, Kwon T.
abstractText: Stem cell-based embryo models now reconstruct increasingly advanced stages of mammalian development, but developmental fidelity remains a central limitation. This review examines why cynomolgus monkey systems are biologically necessary, how natural embryos and emerging technologies benchmark primate development, and how advanced monkey embryoids can strengthen interpretation of human embryo models.

title: How Nurses Assess Interventions to Promote Patients Sleep on Hospital Wards: Results of a Self-Report Survey.
authorString: Vasse M, Paala E, Kangasniemi M, Koivunen M.
abstractText:
Aim

The aim of this study is to describe how nurses assess interventions to promote patients' sleep on hospital wards.

Desing

The study was a cross-sectional survey, and it was conducted among nurses in Finnish specialist healthcare in 2022.

Methods

Out of 482 eligible participants in the sampling frame, 129 nurses returned a completed questionnaire. The open-ended question was answered by 36 participants. Data were analysed using statistical methods and inductive content analysis.

Results

In general, participants assessed that they perform well in sleep-promoting activities in a hospital ward. Participants gave the highest assessment to supporting patients' mental and emotional well-being. Minimising disturbance related to nursing interventions got the lowest scores. Based on the open-ended questions, respondents described that the realisation of patients' sleep support in the hospital related to the care environment, patient placement within the ward, resources available for nursing interventions, sleep-supporting aids, care culture and training related to supporting patients' sleep.

Conclusion

Nurses assess that they are implementing patient sleep-promotion interventions well. Nurses realise patients' sleep promotion as a part of their daily activities. Nurses can promote patient's sleep with small activities, as long as the organisation takes care of the nurses' skills and ensures practical interventions so that the patient gets enough rest during the treatment period.

title: Pharmacological and Therapeutic Potential of Garlic (Allium sativum): Integrating Phytochemistry, Molecular Mechanisms, and Clinical and Preclinical Evidence.
authorString: Bereda G.
abstractText: Garlic (Allium sativum) is a medicinal plant with diverse pharmacological properties and therapeutic potential in metabolic, cardiovascular, hepatic, immune, inflammatory, infectious, and neoplastic disorders. However, comprehensive integration of clinical and preclinical evidence remains limited. This review synthesized randomized controlled trials, crossover studies, therapeutic clinical investigations, and experimental animal studies evaluating garlic supplementation. Allicin was identified as the principal intermediate precursor generating numerous bioactive organosulfur compounds. Clinical evidence demonstrated reductions in systolic blood pressure of 5.2%-10.5% and diastolic blood pressure of 4.0%, decreases in LDL cholesterol of 11.8%-14.2% and total cholesterol of 7.6%-14.2%, and increases in HDL cholesterol of 11.5%. Fasting glucose decreased by 7.01 mg/dL, and HbA1c by 0.66%. Inflammatory markers, including TNF-α and C-reactive protein, declined by up to 24.7%, whereas antioxidant capacity increased. Preclinical studies demonstrated reduced tumor growth, improved renal function, enhanced epithelial regeneration, and increased survival in experimental infection models. Garlic demonstrates consistent therapeutic benefits across multiple conditions. Nevertheless, additional high-quality, large-scale clinical trials are required to establish optimal dosing, long-term safety, and clinical efficacy.

title: Effects of Whey Protein Supplementation on Muscle Damage, Hepatic Stress, and Inflammatory Markers in Power- and Endurance-Trained Athletes.
authorString: Ben Mhamed M, Landolsi M, M'rad M, Bahlous A, Zarrouk F, Trabelsi H, Weiss K, Rosemann T, Bouhlel E, Knechtle B.
abstractText: This study investigated the effects of 8 weeks of whey protein supplementation (30 g/day) on biomarkers of liver function, inflammation, and muscle damage in trained power-trained (predominantly speed-power/anaerobic-power disciplines) and endurance-trained athletes, in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled design. Fifty-nine male athletes were stratified into power (n = 30) and endurance (n = 29) groups, then randomly assigned to a whey protein group (WG) or a placebo control group (CG). Biomarkers assessed pre- and post-intervention included alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), C-reactive protein (CRP), and creatine kinase (CK). Significant reductions in ALT, AST, and CK were observed in both endurance- and power-trained athletes after supplementation (p = 0.001, p = 0.015, p = 0.001, and p = 0.003 respectively), indicating attenuated hepatic and muscular stress. Among the four biomarkers, only ALT displayed a statistically significant three-way interaction (Time × Supplementation × Training modality; p = 0.003), identifying it as the sole marker showing a genuine modality-specific differential response to supplementation. A significant within-group reduction in CRP was additionally observed in the supplemented power-trained athletes (p = 0.039), whereas endurance athletes showed only minor, non-significant changes; because the omnibus three-way interaction for CRP was not significant, this finding is reported as a within-group trend rather than evidence of a differential effect between modalities. Placebo groups demonstrated stable or increased enzyme and CRP values, particularly in endurance athletes. These findings suggest that whey protein may attenuate exercise-induced hepatic and muscular stress across training modalities, with a modality-specific effect on hepatic stress markers (ALT) observed in power-trained athletes. The results highlight whey protein's potential as a nutritional aid to promote recovery and physiological adaptation, possibly mediated by antioxidant and anti-inflammatory mechanisms. Further studies are warranted to examine long-term outcomes and dose-response effects across different training profiles.

title: Predicting cardiovascular disease in peritoneal dialysis patients using glycated proteomics and machine learning: A prospective multicentre study.
authorString: Ji J, Nie Z, Jiang N, Xie T, Zhang L, Liu X, Lu M, Xiang B, Wu W, Jiang X, Zhang L, Ji J, Zou J, Ding X, Lu H, Yu X.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death among peritoneal dialysis (PD) patients, yet PD-specific biomarkers and prediction models remain limited. This study aimed to identify glycated peptide biomarkers associated with CVD in PD patients and develop a prediction model integrating glycated proteomics and clinical indicators using machine learning.

Methods

In Phase I, a matched discovery cohort (48 PD patients with CVD and 48 without CVD) was used to identify glycated peptides by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), with glmnet used to prioritise candidate biomarkers. In Phase II, candidate biomarkers were quantified in a prospective internal derivation cohort (n = 240) and a multicentre external validation cohort (n = 102). The combined model was developed using F-test feature selection and elastic-net logistic regression. Its predictive performance was compared with three published cardiovascular risk models. Patients were stratified using a training-derived Youden cutoff.

Results

In the discovery cohort, 257 glycated peptides were differentially abundant between groups. Four candidate biomarkers were prioritised, and two peptides, GEAFTLK(g)ATVLNYLPK and K(g)QHLFVK, were retained in the final model together with six clinical indicators: phosphate, diabetes, total Kt/V, albumin, cardiac troponin T, and glycated albumin. The combined model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.784 in the training set, 0.781 in the internal testing set, and 0.822 in the external validation cohort, respectively. Using the training-derived cutoff of 0.373, higher 1-year CVD incidence was observed in the high-risk group in both validation cohorts. The combined model also achieved higher ROC-AUCs than the published cardiovascular risk models.

Conclusion

We developed and externally validated a PD-specific CVD prediction model by integrating glycated peptide biomarkers with clinical indicators, which may facilitate earlier risk stratification and targeted prevention.

title: Definitive Chemoradiotherapy Following Preoperative Induction Chemotherapy in Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Prognostic Impact of Response.
authorString: Hisano O, Yoshitake T, Matsumoto K, Shirakawa Y, Wakiyama H, Takaki M, Imafuku H, Tsuchihashi K, Nakanoko T, Horioka K, Matsumoto S, Ishigami K.
abstractText:
Background/aim

The role of induction chemotherapy (IC) before definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT) in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains controversial, and outcomes among patients who begin chemotherapy with preoperative intent but eventually transition to definitive CRT are not well characterized. This study aimed to describe outcomes of definitive CRT with and without prior IC and to explore the prognostic value of chemotherapy response.

Patients and methods

Patients with clinical stage II-IVa ESCC treated with definitive radiotherapy were retrospectively reviewed at a single center between 2014 and 2022. Of them, 54 patients treated with definitive CRT were analyzed: 31 received preoperative IC before transitioning to definitive CRT, and 23 received upfront definitive CRT (non-IC group). The IC group was clinically heterogeneous, having transitioned to CRT for varied reasons (persistent unresectability in 18, patient preference in 9, comorbidity or perioperative risk in 4). Median follow-up was 22.5 months.

Results

Two-year overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), and locoregional control did not differ significantly between the IC and non-IC groups (OS: 65.4% vs. 59.4%, p=0.559; PFS: 33.7% vs. 52.0%, p=0.465; locoregional control: 53.2% vs. 69.2%, p=0.402). Within the IC group, a response (partial/complete) to chemotherapy was associated with more favorable OS (p=0.008) and PFS (p=0.010); the association with locoregional control was not significant (p=0.059). Grade ≥3 late adverse events were persistent in the IC group, and there were four treatment-related deaths (7%).

Conclusion

Induction chemotherapy before definitive CRT was not associated with improved survival in this selected cohort of ESCC. Response to induction chemotherapy was associated with more favorable OS and PFS and may have prognostic relevance, although it does not justify a response-adapted treatment strategy.

title: Impact of BMI on Perioperative Complications Following CRS and HIPEC for Appendiceal Cancer.
authorString: Mercado M, Vaska AI, Barat S, Wijayawardana R, Ahmadi N, Morris DL.
abstractText:
Background/aim

Obesity is considered a risk factor for poorer postoperative outcomes. Its effect in the context of cytoreductive surgery (CRS) and heated intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) is less well understood. This study examined the effect of body mass index (BMI) on postoperative surgical outcomes in patients with appendiceal cancer who underwent CRS/HIPEC.

Patients and methods

A retrospective analysis performed including adult patients with appendiceal cancer who underwent CRS/HIPEC between 2021 to 2023 and grouped into weight ranges based on body mass index (BMI). Intraoperative and postoperative outcomes were recorded. Continuous variables were compared using Kruskal Wallis tests while categorical variables were compared using Chi squared tests. Multivariate regression analysis was performed and models controlled for age, sex and peritoneal cancer index.

Results

A total of 130 adult patients who underwent CRS/HIPEC for appendiceal cancer were included in the analysis. Intraoperative outcomes were not significantly different between weight range groups. Wound complication rates were higher among patients with BMI >30 (p=0.014). The mortality rate and rate of complications were not statistically different between BMI groups. In the adjusted model, patients with higher BMI were more likely to develop cardiovascular complications [odds ratio (OR)=1.092, p=0.018] but were less likely to develop obstruction or ileus postoperatively (OR=0.911, p=0.045).

Conclusion

Surgery is a key component of the management of peritoneal surface malignancies but patients with higher BMI may be at increased risk of perioperative complications, potentially altering the perioperative management of this patient cohort. However, it is unclear what specific risks obesity confers to morbidity and mortality or oncological outcomes. In our study, when stratified by BMI, there was a significant difference in wound-related complications and increased likelihood of cardiovascular complications in patients with higher BMI who underwent CRS/HIPEC for appendiceal malignancy. There were no other significant differences in intra-operative or morbidity outcomes. These findings would suggest that high BMI should be considered but not prohibit patient selection for operative management. In such patients, BMI and cardiovascular risk profile should be optimised to improve perioperative outcomes.

title: [Advanced heart failure: definition, epidemiology, diagnosis and treatment].
authorString: Di Nora C, Tinti MD, Matassini MV, Capovilla TM, Manca P, Fazzini L, Carigi S, Bianco M, De Gennaro L, Rizzello V, Palmieri V, De Maria R, Aschieri D, Bilato C, Di Fusco SA, Oliva F, Nardi F, Grimaldi M, Gori M.
abstractText: Advanced heart failure represents the most severe and complex stage of a chronic and progressive clinical syndrome that remains one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in industrialized countries. A substantial proportion of patients progress to a condition characterized by persistent symptoms, recurrent episodes of decompensation, and marked functional impairment despite optimized medical therapy and the appropriate use of cardiac devices. This advanced stage is associated with a considerable clinical, healthcare, and economic burden, together with a profound negative impact on the quality of life of both patients and caregivers. Early recognition of advanced heart failure remains a major challenge in everyday clinical practice, partly due to the heterogeneity of clinical presentations. Consequently, increasing clinician awareness, establishing standardized diagnostic criteria, and implementing dedicated care pathways are essential to ensure timely identification and appropriate patient management. In this context, the present review aims to provide an updated overview of advanced heart failure, with a particular focus on diagnostic criteria, currently available therapeutic strategies, and the most effective organizational models for optimizing the care of this complex and high-risk patient population.

title: New Perspectives on Air Pollution and Cardiac Health: from Real-Time Patient and Exposure Monitoring to Precision Cardiac Organoids.
authorString: Ahn N, Kim WS, Kim JB.
abstractText: Recently, ambient particulate matter (PM) levels have significantly escalated, persisting over extended durations. This persistent elevation represents a substantial threat to public health, prompting heightened concerns regarding its health impacts and growing societal interest. Annual increases in concerns about PM-related health issues are directly correlated with rising PM concentrations. Airborne PM is implicated in the pathogenesis of cardiovascular diseases (CVD), contributing to an increased incidence of CVD-related mortality. This review provides comprehensive evidence regarding the relationship between PM exposure and CVD, with an initial focus on the physiological impact of PM on the human body, followed by a detailed explanation of its effects on various CVD. The review also discusses the latest scientific and clinical advancements in this domain, offering insights into the current academic landscape and future research directions, grounded in the authors' research experiences and an extensive review of the literature.

title: Factors Influencing Intention to Quit Tobacco Use Among Patients With Non-Communicable Diseases in Bangladesh: A Multilevel Analysis.
authorString: Kibria MG, Muhammad AA, Sultana P, Alif SM, Karim MN.
abstractText:
Introduction

Tobacco use is a major risk factor for non-communicable diseases (NCD), contributing to disease progression, comorbidities and reduced quality of life. This study aimed to assess the distribution and correlates of intention to quit tobacco use among patients with NCDs attending selected government sub-district hospitals in Bangladesh.

Methods

A cross-sectional study was conducted among 660 patients aged ≥ 18 years attending NCD corners in eight selected government sub-district hospitals in Bangladesh. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire covering sociodemographic, clinical and healthcare, and tobacco use characteristics from 26 May to 14 June 2025. Patients were nested within sub-district hospitals, and multivariable multilevel logistic regression was used to identify the factors associated with quit intentions while accounting for clustering of patients within hospitals.

Results

In the multilevel multivariable logistic regression model, patients with moderate to high levels of knowledge of cessation services (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 2.2; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.19-4.24), heart disease (AOR 2.0; 95% CI 1.18-3.59), stroke (AOR 2.4; 95% CI 1.09-5.12) and ≤ 10 years of tobacco use (AOR 2.1; 95% CI 1.24-3.38) were more likely to express an intention to quit. Among facility-level factors, being asked about tobacco use by healthcare providers (AOR 2.2; 95% CI 1.29-3.69) and receiving advice to quit (AOR 1.8; 95% CI 1.10-2.96) were associated with higher odds of intending to quit.

Discussion and conclusions

Addressing both individual- and facility-level factors through structured cessation support integrated into routine NCD care could strengthen tobacco control efforts in Bangladesh.

title: [Abdominal aortic aneurysms: diagnosis, risk stratification and treatment strategies].
authorString: Squizzato F, Bilato MJ, Antonello M, Piazza M, Colacchio EC, Menegolo M, Grego F.
abstractText: Abdominal aortic aneurysm is defined as a focal aortic dilation ≥3.0 cm in maximum diameter, with rupture-associated mortality approaching 80%. Anatomical classification identifies infrarenal (80%), juxtarenal, pararenal and suprarenal aneurysms. Operative thresholds are 5.5 cm in men and 5.0 cm in women. Endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) provides an early survival benefit, with 30-day mortality of 1.8% vs 4.3% for open repair in the EVAR-1 trial, and substantially comparable long-term outcomes up to 15 years of follow-up, at the cost of a 15-20% reintervention burden and the need for lifelong imaging surveillance. Accordingly, the 2024 European Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines consider EVAR as the preferred treatment in most patients with favorable anatomy, reserving open repair for young patients with long life expectancy, unfavorable anatomy and specific conditions such as connective tissue disease, inflammatory aneurysms, graft infection and failed previous endovascular repair. Treatment selection should be based on the integrated assessment of individual operative risk, aortic anatomy and life expectancy.

title: Low latency and generalizable dynamic MRI via L+S alternating gradient descent and minimization.
authorString: Babu S, Lingala SG, Vaswani N.
abstractText:
Background

Dynamic MRI reconstruction often requires accurate, fast, and low-latency algorithms that generalize across multiple applications, sampling schemes, and rates, without problem-specific parameter tuning. Existing methods either lack generalizability or require extensive parameter adjustment.

Purpose

To develop generalizable, low-latency MRI reconstruction algorithms based on low-rank (LR) and low-rank + sparse (L+S) models that are accurate, fast, and require minimal parameter tuning across diverse dynamic MRI settings.

Methods

We propose a novel Alternating Gradient Descent and Minimization (AltGDmin) approach for L+S matrix recovery from column-wise undersampled measurements, and extend it to a 3-level hierarchical L+S model for dynamic MRI. A few-shot (FS) learning modification (AGM-L+S-FS) is introduced to enable near low-latency reconstruction with per-frame processing time comparable to or faster than scan time. A simpler LR-only variant is also evaluated.

Results

The proposed algorithms were validated on 6 prospective and 12 retrospective dynamic MRI datasets, covering cardiac, speech, and abdominal applications, with Cartesian, pseudo-radial, radial, and spiral sampling schemes. Experiments demonstrate accurate reconstruction, generalizability across datasets and sampling rates, and low-latency performance. Detailed comparisons with state-of-the-art LR, L+S, low-latency, and unsupervised deep learning methods show superior or comparable performance.

Conclusions

Our AGM-L+S-FS approach provide generalizable, fast, and low-latency MRI reconstruction across multiple dynamic MRI applications and sampling schemes, without the need for problem-specific parameter tuning.

title: MEK1/2 Signalling establishes an alloreactive effector T cell program through SMAD4 during cardiac allograft rejection.
authorString: Zhao J, Ran S, Zhou S, Li Y, Zhan W, Lai L, Cui J, Xia J, Wu J.
abstractText:
Background

Acute allograft rejection is largely dependent on T cell-driven immune responses; however, the molecular programs that establish and maintain effector T cell states during rejection remain incompletely defined.

Methods

Single-cell transcriptomic analysis was conducted to characterize the activation of signalling pathways in T cells during acute allograft rejection. The function of MEK1/2 signalling was evaluated both in vitro and in vivo using mice with targeted deletion of Mek1/2 in T cells and pharmacological inhibition. Phosphoproteomic analysis, immunofluorescence staining, and western blotting were conducted to investigate downstream signalling mechanisms, particularly those involving SMAD4.

Results

Effector CD4 and CD8 T cells exhibited enhanced MEK/ERK pathway activation throughout the rejection process. MEK1/2 inhibition, either via genetic deletion or pharmacological blockade, attenuated T cell activation and effector activity, leading to reduced rejection and prolonged graft survival. Phosphoproteomic analysis identified SMAD4 as a key downstream effector of MEK1/2 signalling. Mechanistically, MEK1/2 deficiency reduced SMAD4 nuclear translocation in activated T cells, accompanied by diminished effector T cell responses.

Conclusions

MEK1/2 signalling regulates T cell activation and effector phenotypes via SMAD4 nuclear translocation in heart transplant rejection. Therapeutic intervention targeting this pathway may contribute to alloimmune response regulation and improve transplant outcomes.

title: Association of Tissue Inhibitor of Metalloproteinase 1 rs4898 With Susceptibility to Childhood Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia in Taiwanese Females.
authorString: Pei JS, Chen CC, Tsai HW, Hsu PC, Tsai CL, Tsai CW, Ke YC, Su MY, Bau DT, Chang WS.
abstractText:
Background/aim

Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) is the most common pediatric malignancy, and identification of genetic determinants of disease susceptibility may improve understanding of disease susceptibility and facilitate genetic risk assessment. Tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase 1 (TIMP1) is a multifunctional regulator of extracellular matrix remodeling, proliferation, and apoptosis. However, the contribution of TIMP1 polymorphisms to childhood ALL susceptibility remains poorly investigated. This study aimed to evaluate whether TIMP1 genetic variants are associated with female childhood ALL risk.

Materials and methods

The study included 118 female childhood ALL patients and 118 age-matched healthy controls from Taiwan. TIMP1 polymorphisms, rs4898, rs6609533, and rs2070584, were genotyped. Genotypic distributions and their associations with ALL risk were evaluated using odds ratios (ORs), 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and p-Values.

Results

A significant association was observed between TIMP1 rs4898 and ALL risk (p for trend=0.0024). Compared with the TT reference genotype, the TIMP1 rs4898 CT and CC genotypes exhibited ORs of 1.85 (95%CI=0.97-3.54, p=0.0864) and 2.96 (95%CI=1.46-6.01, p=0.0041), respectively. In the recessive model, TIMP1 rs4898 CC carriers had an OR of 2.04 (95% CI=1.13-3.54, p=0.0232), while the dominant model yielded an OR of 2.24 (95%CI=1.23-4.08, p=0.0119). On the contrary, rs6609533 and rs2070584 showed no significant associations in any model (all p>0.05). Allelic distribution pattern analyses also confirmed the presence of significant differences for TIMP1 rs4898 between the case and control groups (OR=1.82, 95%CI=1.26-2.62, p=0.0017).

Conclusion

These findings indicate that TIMP1 rs4898 was associated with childhood ALL susceptibility among Taiwanese females in this cohort. No statistically significant association was observed for rs6609533 or rs2070584. Larger multicenter studies incorporating functional and transcriptomic analyses are warranted to validate these associations and clarify the biological mechanisms underlying TIMP1-related leukemogenesis.

title: [Role of statin/ezetimibe fixed-dose combination in lipid risk management in the cardiovascular disease continuum].
authorString: Catapano AL, Manzato E, Di Fusco SA, Colivicchi F.
abstractText: Prolonged exposure to high LDL cholesterol (LDL-C) levels represents a time-dependent driver of atherosclerotic risk. Available evidence shows that maintaining low LDL-C levels over time is associated with a reduction in cardiovascular events both in primary and secondary prevention. In this setting, combination therapy with statin and ezetimibe allows for a more effective LDL-C reduction compared with the statin titration alone, thanks to the complementary mechanism of action of the two drugs and improved treatment adherence. Clinical studies have demonstrated that early initiation of combination therapy increases the likelihood of achieving LDL-C goals and of reducing cardiovascular events. In parallel, recent real-world evidence downplays the incidence of complete statin intolerance, suggesting that a significant proportion of reported symptoms is attributable to nocebo effects. Therefore, the fixed-dose statin/ezetimibe combination represents an effective, simple, and generally well-tolerated therapeutic strategy to optimize lipid control. In patients requiring pronounced LDL-C reductions, combination with high-intensity statins contributes to achieving therapeutic goals while limiting the use of more complex and expensive injectable therapies.

title: [From guidelines: cardiovascular risk stratification and therapeutic targets].
authorString: Colivicchi F, Manzato E, Di Fusco SA, Catapano AL.
abstractText: The linear relationship between LDL cholesterol (LDL-C) concentrations and cardiovascular risk, together with evidence of clinical benefit associated with intensive and sustained LDL-C reduction, underlies the "the lower, the better" paradigm. Cardiovascular risk stratification is the prerequisite for defining treatment intensity. In the context of primary prevention, international guidelines recommend the use of validated scores for an objective definition of individual risk. This evaluation must be integrated by considering risk-amplifying factors not included in the algorithms, such as a family history of premature events, elevated lipoprotein(a) and triglyceride levels, and the presence of coronary artery calcium. Statin/ezetimibe combination therapy acts through complementary mechanisms, reducing hepatic synthesis and intestinal absorption of cholesterol, respectively. Evidence indicates greater efficacy in achieving LDL-C targets compared with statin intensification alone, along with favorable treatment adherence. Despite clear recommendations regarding target LDL-C levels, real-world data highlight persistent undertreatment and a low percentage of patients with LDL-C levels consistent with guideline recommendations. In both primary and secondary prevention, the statin/ezetimibe combination represents an effective and safe strategy to achieve recommended therapeutic goals and its early implementation contributes to reducing therapeutic inertia.

title: [Ten questions about cardiogenetics].
authorString: Fortuni F, Matteucci A, Angelini F, Abete R, Palmiero G, Marazia S, Terzi F, Di Gesaro G, Pozzer L, Belfioretti L, De Feo D, Vitulli P, Zambelli G, Vergara A, Marsan NA, Imazio M, Gabrielli D, Oliva F, Nardi F, Grimaldi M.
abstractText: In recent years, cardiogenetics has become a key component in the management of cardiomyopathies and channelopathies, reshaping diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic strategies for conditions characterized by substantial clinical heterogeneity and variable arrhythmic risk. However, the use of genetic testing in clinical practice remains challenging and requires careful assessment of test appropriateness, gene panel selection, and result interpretation. In particular, the frequent identification of variants of uncertain significance highlights the need for an integrated approach combining genetic findings, clinical phenotype, family history, and disease-specific features. This review, organized around ten practical questions, aims to provide clinicians with an updated and pragmatic guide to the use of genetic testing in inherited cardiovascular diseases. The manuscript will address when genetic testing should be requested in cardiomyopathies and channelopathies, which genes should be tested across different conditions, and how genetic results should be interpreted according to the underlying disease. It will also discuss the diagnostic and prognostic value of genetic findings, their role in arrhythmic risk stratification and therapeutic decision-making, and the use of cascade genetic testing in family screening. Finally, disease-specific aspects of genetic counseling, ethical implications, and the importance of a multidisciplinary, patient-centered approach will be emphasized.

title: [Multimodality imaging in heart failure: phenotyping and clinical decision-making].
authorString: Musella F, Carigi S, Tinti D, Fazzari F, Pini D, Mangini F, Turco A, Piroli F, Bilato C, Oliva F, Nardi F, Grimaldi M.
abstractText: Heart failure (HF) is a global health priority traditionally managed based on ejection fraction (EF). However, EF is now recognized as insufficient to represent the pathophysiological complexity and clinical heterogeneity of the syndrome. Modern diagnostics have shifted toward multimodality imaging, acting as an integrated platform for phenotyping. Transthoracic echocardiography remains the first-line tool, evolving into a multiparametric approach that includes global longitudinal strain, right ventricular-arterial coupling assessment, and congestion monitoring via lung ultrasound and venous excess ultrasound. Cardiac magnetic resonance is the gold standard for tissue characterization, which is crucial for etiological definition and arrhythmic risk stratification through fibrosis identification (late gadolinium enhancement). Cardiac computed tomography is essential for coronary anatomy evaluation and procedural planning, while nuclear imaging (single-photon emission computed tomography/positron emission tomography) provides unique insights into metabolism, inflammation, and sympathetic innervation. Integrating these modalities, guided by clinical questions, enables personalized therapeutic management, tracking of disease trajectories (such as improved HF), and optimization of clinical decision-making.

title: Quantification of Aortic Cusp Parameters Using Computed Tomography in Valve-Sparing Aortic Root Replacement Surgery: A Prospective Study.
authorString: Kim HR, Yang DH, Kim JB.
abstractText:
Purpose

Determining the feasibility of valve-sparing aortic root replacement (VSRR) requires accurate preoperative assessment of aortic valve cusp geometry. However, the reliability of computed tomography (CT) for measuring cusp parameters remains unclear. This study evaluated the agreement between CT-derived cusp measurements and intraoperative measurements and explored the potential of CT-based cusp asymmetry to predict intraoperative cusp plication.

Materials and methods

In this prospective study, 32 consecutive patients undergoing VSRR with the reimplantation technique were enrolled. Preoperative CT was used to measure cusp free margin length and geometric height. Agreement between CT-derived and intraoperative measurements was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). An exploratory analysis evaluated whether CT-derived cusp asymmetry predicted the need for intraoperative cusp plication.

Results

CT measurements demonstrated good agreement with intraoperative measurements for cusp free margin length (ICC 0.80-0.87). In contrast, geometric height showed only moderate agreement (ICC 0.44-0.69). Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated moderate discriminative ability of CT-derived cusp asymmetry for predicting intraoperative cusp plication (area under the curve, 0.71; 95% confidence interval, 0.49-0.91), although the association did not reach statistical significance (p=0.06). Postoperative echocardiography demonstrated none-to-mild aortic insufficiency in 96.9% of patients.

Conclusion

Preoperative CT demonstrated good agreement with intraoperative measurements for cusp free margin length in tricuspid valves, although the absolute limits of agreement were wide. CT-based quantification of cusp asymmetry may provide additional information for preoperative surgical planning; however, its association with intraoperative cusp plication remains exploratory and requires validation in larger studies.

Clinical research information service (cris) registration number

KCT0006180.

title: Comparative Physiological and Ecological Characterization of the Photosymbiotic Amoeba Mayorella viridis Across Symbiotic and Aposymbiotic States.
authorString: Yamamoto A, Kaneda Y, Todaka H, Arikawa M.
abstractText: Symbiosis is a fundamental biological strategy that enables metabolic complementation between distinct organisms. The amoeba Mayorella viridis establishes a photosymbiotic relationship with the green alga Chlorella, yet the physiological basis of this association remains poorly understood. Here, we compared symbiotic (green) and aposymbiotic (white) strains to quantify phenotypic effects of the symbiotic state. Cell size did not differ when the cells were fed but was significantly reduced in the white strain under starvation, indicating that Chlorella contributes to host stability under nutrient limitation. Motility was unaffected by symbiosis. In contrast, photoresponses, including positive phototaxis and photophobic responses, were completely abolished in the white strain, demonstrating that symbiotic Chlorella is essential for host photoresponse. Growth and survival were significantly reduced in the white strain under both constant light and constant dark conditions, indicating that the symbiont enhances both proliferation and starvation tolerance. Notably, under dark and nutrient-limited conditions, intracellular Chlorella declined, suggesting digestion and utilization as an internal nutrient source. Photosymbiosis was re-established by reintroducing isolated Chlorella into aposymbiotic cells, restoring green phenotype and photoresponse. These findings establish a reversible system and clarify the physiological roles of photosymbiosis in M. viridis.

title: Phytochemical Profiling and Safety Assessment of Maerua crassifolia Forssk. Aerial Parts Infusion With Pharmacological Validation of Its Analgesic and Anti-Inflammatory Activities.
authorString: Benazzi L, Ouafi S, Semaoui R, Baali F, Eras J, Canela-Garayoa R, Djemouai N.
abstractText: Maerua crassifolia Forssk. is used in Algerian traditional medicine to relieve pain and manage inflammation. This study aimed to explore the composition, safety, in vitro antioxidant activity and in vivo analgesic, and anti-inflammatory effects of the infusion of M. crassifolia aerial parts. The infusion yielded 11.93 ± 1.08% (w/w) and exhibited high total phenolic (620.51 ± 2.54 mg GAE/100 g dry weight (d.w.)) and flavonoid (87.11 ± 0.76 mg QE/100 g d.w.) contents. Ultra-performance liquid chromatography-photodiode array detection-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-PDA-MS/MS) identified 19 phenolic compounds. The infusion showed strong antioxidant activity in the four assays tested. Acute oral toxicity testing showed a favorable safety profile (LD<sub>50</sub> > 5000 mg/kg body weight (b.w.)). The results showed that the infusion exerted dose-dependent analgesic activity, with the highest inhibition of abdominal writhing (74.02 ± 2.17%) and paw-licking time (up to 77.78%) observed at 1000 mg/kg b.w., comparable to paracetamol, the standard analgesic drug. In the anti-inflammatory test, the infusion produced dose-dependent activity, with 44.42% ± 2.30% and 56.22% ± 1.52% inhibition at 500 and 1000 mg/kg b.w., respectively, comparable to the standard anti-inflammatory drug sodium diclofenac. These findings position M. crassifolia as a promising candidate for the management of pain and inflammation.

title: Positive Impact of Hypertension in Patients with Early-stage Lung Cancer Treated With Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy.
authorString: Lim JH, Jang JH, Lee J, Kim HJ, Lee B, Lee CY, Choi Y.
abstractText:
Background/aim

This study aimed to analyze the effect of hypertension on recurrence and progression-free survival (PFS) in patients with early-stage lung cancer who underwent curative stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT).

Patients and methods

This study included 100 patients with T1-T3N0M0 lung cancer who underwent lung SBRT using CyberKnife or volumetric-modulated arc therapy at Inha University Hospital between July 2008 and June 2025. Recurrence rates and PFS were analyzed. Data on hypertension and specific types of antihypertensive medications were retrospectively reviewed from electronic medical records.

Results

The median follow-up period was 31.0 months (range=0.7-136.7 months). Of the 100 patients, 52 had hypertension. Recurrence occurred in 38 patients, including 25 with locoregional failure and 13 with distant metastases. Recurrence rates were significantly lower in patients with hypertension (p=0.015), with reduced locoregional recurrence (p=0.022), whereas distant metastasis showed no significant correlation with hypertension (p=0.315). Hypertensive drug users (n=37) had lower recurrence rates (p=0.003). Recurrence was higher in male patients (p=0.049) and lower in those aged >70 years (p=0.033). Patients with hypertension showed significantly improved PFS (p=0.010) but no difference in overall survival based on hypertension status (p=0.319). Other factors that positively affected PFS included female sex and age >70 years. Patients actively receiving antihypertensive medication showed greater PFS than those who did not (p=0.016). In particular, those using beta-blockers showed a low recurrence rate (0%, p=0.033).

Conclusion

The therapeutic effects of lung SBRT appear more pronounced in patients with hypertension. This favorable outcome may be related to the administration of antihypertensive medications, suggesting the need for further investigation into the underlying mechanisms.

title: [Regional network for advanced heart failure in Tuscany: analysis of referrals and patient pathways for heart transplantation and left ventricular assist device implantation (2020-2025)].
authorString: Selimi A, Righini FM, Sorini Dini C, Pagliaro A, Martini L, Bernazzali S, Lazzeri C, Maielli M, Sponga S, Davoli G, Maccherini M, Valente S.
abstractText:
Background

Advanced heart failure requires regional care pathways capable of identifying patients before clinical deterioration prevents access to heart transplantation (HTx) or left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation. The available data mainly describe patients who have already been selected for, or treated with, advanced therapies, whereas analyses of the entire referral are less frequent. The aim of this study was to describe referral volume, clinical characteristics, and outcomes of patients referred to the Tuscany regional center for evaluation for HTx and/or LVAD implantation in the period 2020-2025, with specific attention to temporal referral trends and distribution of INTERMACS profiles.

Methods

Prospective observational registry including 468 consecutive adult patients referred to the regional reference center between January 2020 and December 2025. INTERMACS profile was assigned during the initial assessment. Candidacy for advanced therapies, pathway status of eligible patients, and temporal trend in INTERMACS groups 1-3, 4-5, and 6-7 were analyzed.

Results

During the observation period, a significant increase in referral volume between 2020-2022 and 2023-2025 was observed (incidence rate ratio 1.46; 95% confidence interval 1.22-1.76; p<0.001). The distribution of aggregated INTERMACS profiles changed over time, with an increase in profiles 6-7 from 3.3% to 20.9% and a reduction in profiles 4-5. Overall, 340 patients (72.6%) were potentially eligible for advanced therapies. Of these, 144 patients, corresponding to 30.8% of the entire cohort, were considered candidates for HTx and/or LVAD. Of these, 123 (36.2%) were listed for HTx, including 5 patients with LVAD support as bridge to transplant. Among listed patients, 75 (61.0%) underwent transplantation, 46 (37.4%) remained on the active waiting list, and 2 (1.6%) died while on the waiting list. Twenty patients underwent LVAD implantation as destination therapy and 1 patient as bridge to candidacy (21 patients in total, corresponding to 6.2% of eligible patients) and 130 eligible patients (38.2%) remained under follow-up.

Conclusions

In this regional experience, the number of referrals to the reference center increased over time. The increasing representation of INTERMACS profiles 6-7, along with the reduction in profiles 4-5, is consistent with earlier patient management. These results demonstrate the consolidation of the regional network for advanced heart failure, but multicenter studies with systematic follow-up are needed to evaluate its impact on clinical outcomes.

title: Correlates of Glycemic Control in Type 2 Diabetes Adults With and Without Comorbid Heart Failure.
authorString: Aga F, Dunbar SB, Kebede T, Guteta S, Higgins MK, Gary R.

journal.title: Journal of nursing scholarship : an official publication of Sigma Theta Tau International Honor Society of Nursing

abstractText:
Introduction

Attaining good glycemic control (GC) in patients with Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is critical, yet the presence of comorbidities like heart failure (HF) presents overwhelming self-care complexities. The aim of this study was to investigate and compare the demographic, psychosocial, and clinical factors associated with glycemic control among T2D adults with and without comorbid HF.

Design

A comparative cross-sectional study.

Methods

A total of 210 adult T2D patients (105 with comorbid HF, 105 without comorbid HF) in Tikur Anbessa Specialized Referral Hospital (TASRH), the largest tertiary healthcare setting in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, were enrolled. Data gathered included demographic traits, clinical parameters including the outcome variable HbA1c (categorized as "good glycemic control" for HbA1c < 7% and "poor glycemic control" for HbA1c ≥ 7%), and standardized psychosocial scales (SDSCA, PDSMS, DKT2, PHQ-9, and ESSI). Bivariate analysis (Chi-square and biserial correlation) and Enter method logistic regression analysis were performed.

Result

Across both groups, good GC (HbA1c < 7%) was alarmingly low, only 10.43% in the non-HF and 9.52% in the HF comorbid group (p = 0.818). In the non-HF group, the multivariate model revealed that only a higher social support (ESSI) score significantly predicted a higher likelihood of good GC (AOR = 1.518, 95% CI: 1.002, 2.302, p = 0.049). Conversely, for those with comorbid HF, a higher diabetes self-efficacy (PDSMS) score (AOR = 1.569, 95% CI: 1.045, 2.355, p = 0.030) and taking a higher number of daily medications (AOR = 2.502, 95% CI: 1.050, 5.962, p = 0.038) significantly predicted good GC.

Conclusion

This study highlights a critical gap in glycemic control regardless of HF status. However, the actionable drivers of glycemic success diverge fundamentally: social support systems are vital for GC success in uncomplicated T2D, whereas promoting self-efficacy and total count of daily medications dictates success in the face of complex HF comorbidity.

title: [The Heart Team as a multidisciplinary approach to the management of patients eligible for surgical and transcatheter treatment of aortic valve disease - Consensus document].
authorString: Baglio G, Bignami EG, De Luca L, Guglielmi E, Indolfi C, Marchese A, Oliva F, Panascia E, Paternoster G, Perrone Filardi P, Pilato M, Ranucci M, Rinaldi M, Saia F.
abstractText: Aortic valve disease, particularly severe symptomatic aortic stenosis, represents a growing public health problem due to the aging population. The increasing complexity of managing this condition - driven by the evolution of surgical and transcatheter techniques and the expansion of treatment indications - requires a multidisciplinary organizational model capable of ensuring quality and safety of care. This consensus document, jointly developed by AGENAS and the leading Italian scientific societies involved in the management of valvular heart disease, defines the principles for the implementation and functioning of the Heart Team as a central element of the decision-making process for patients undergoing evaluation for surgical aortic valve replacement or transcatheter aortic valve implantation. The document describes the composition, responsibilities, and operational procedures of the Heart Team, highlighting the importance of multidisciplinary assessment, patient-tailored treatment, shared decision-making with the patient, and outcome monitoring. The aim is to promote a standardized organizational model across the country, aligned with the scientific evidence and the most recent international guidelines, thereby contributing to improved clinical outcomes and greater efficiency of the Italian National Health Service.

title: Retrospective Study of Pelvic Irradiation in Patients With Advanced Uterine Cervical Cancer.
authorString: Utsumi N, Kawamura H, Yamano T, Hayakawa T, Ueno S, Saito M, Machida F, Matsumoto Y, Mizuno N, Umeda M, Kato Y, Takahashi T.
abstractText:
Background/aim

The clinical role of local therapy for advanced uterine cervical cancer remains unclear. While systemic chemotherapy is the standard treatment, pelvic radiotherapy may contribute to local control and potentially improve outcomes in selected patients. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical significance of pelvic irradiation in patients with advanced cervical cancer with para-aortic lymph node (PAN) and/or distant metastases.

Patients and methods

We retrospectively reviewed 35 patients with cervical cancer with PAN and/or distant metastases who underwent radiotherapy including whole-pelvic irradiation between 2009 and 2019. Patients were classified into a distant metastasis (DM) group and a PAN group. The DM group was further subdivided into patients with lymph node-only metastases (LY group) and those with organ metastases (OR group). Overall survival (OS) was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and compared using the log-rank test and Cox proportional hazards model.

Results

The median OS for all patients was 2.22 years. The median OS was 1.76 years in the DM group and 3.02 years in the PAN group, with no statistically significant difference between the groups (p=0.838). Within the DM group, the median OS was 1.18 years in the OR group and 2.01 years in the LY group, with no significant difference (p=0.590). Treatment was generally well tolerated, with limited severe adverse events. In Cox proportional hazards analysis using the PAN group as the reference, neither the OR nor the LY group showed a statistically significant difference in OS.

Conclusion

Although limited by its retrospective design and small sample size, this study suggests that semi-definitive pelvic radiotherapy may be a reasonable treatment option for selected patients with cervical cancer with distant metastases.
