title: Cortisol in cardio-kidney-metabolic disease.
authorString: Khan MS, Arshad MS, Bhatt DL, Cherney DZI, DeFronzo RA, Green JB, Handelsman Y, Shafi T, Testani J, Butler J.
abstractText: Despite guideline-directed therapy, many patients with cardio-kidney-metabolic (CKM) disease remain uncontrolled due to therapeutic inertia, adherence barriers, and underrecognized secondary causes. Hypercortisolism, ranging from mild autonomous cortisol secretion (MACS) to overt Cushing syndrome, is an increasingly recognized contributor. MACS is associated with a 2.5-fold higher risk of cardiovascular death and increased prevalence of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), and kidney impairment. Cortisol excess promotes muscle insulin resistance, hepatic gluconeogenesis, β-cell dysfunction, sodium retention, and vascular remodelling, worsening glycaemia and blood pressure, leading to poor CKM outcomes. Recent prospective studies suggest that hypercortisolism is more prevalent than previously suspected in selected CKM phenotypes, including 24% in patients with difficult-to-control T2DM in CATALYST and 27% in patients with resistant hypertension in MOMENTUM. The overnight 1 mg dexamethasone suppression test remains the diagnostic test of choice. Therapeutic strategies include adrenal steroidogenesis inhibitors, glucocorticoid receptor antagonists, and pituitary-directed therapies in selected cases, while surgery remains the first-line treatment for surgically remediable disease. This review summarizes the epidemiology and mechanisms linking cortisol excess to CKM dysfunction, and also highlights the need for clinical trials, standardized diagnostic thresholds, and assays to enable integration of cortisol-targeted therapies into management pathways to mitigate residual CKM risk. This review will serve as a practical guide for cardiologists to manage a potentially reversible contributor to poor CKM control.

title: Home-based nurse-led self-management support for heart failure: a randomized controlled trial.
authorString: Çelik H, Özen B.
abstractText:
Aim

To evaluate the effect of a nurse-led, stage-tailored home-based self-management and follow-up programme on self-care behaviour in people with heart failure.

Background

People with heart failure require ongoing education, symptom monitoring, and self-management support after specialist assessment. However, access to structured centre-based cardiac rehabilitation may be limited. A nurse-led home-based model may help bridge the gap between specialist cardiology care and community-based long-term support, particularly where rehabilitation services are unavailable.

Methods

In this parallel-group randomized controlled trial, adults aged 40-75 years with New York Heart Association class I-III heart failure and ejection fraction >30% were allocated to a 12-week home-based programme or usual care. The intervention was delivered through nurse-led home visits and telephone follow-up for clinically stable patients who could not access structured centre-based rehabilitation. The intervention group received home visits and telephone follow-up (n = 32), while the control group received usual care (n = 31). The primary outcome was self-care behaviour. Secondary outcomes were quality of life, self-efficacy, and physical capacity. Exploratory clinical outcomes were body composition, ejection fraction, and HbA1c level.

Findings

At 12 weeks, the intervention group had better self-care scores than the control group (17.78 ± 2.93 vs 40.00 ± 6.49). Secondary outcomes also favoured the intervention group, with better quality of life scores, higher self-efficacy scores, and greater 6-minute walk distance. Exploratory clinical outcomes showed changes in some parameters, including ejection fraction and body-fluid values. Most intervention participants reached the Transtheoretical Model action stage, and New York Heart Association class improved significantly. This primary health care-relevant home-based model was associated with improved self-care behaviour and may support continuity of care for people with heart failure after specialist cardiology assessment when centre-based rehabilitation is unavailable.

Conclusion

The programme improved self-care in people with heart failure and showed potential to support home-based self-management when centre-based cardiac rehabilitation was unavailable.

title: Extended Versus Short Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Duration After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Chronic Total Occlusion: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Emara A, Mansour A, Kasem AW, Hamed BM, Elkasaby MH, Balbaa E, Shubietah A, Frishman WH, Aronow WS.
abstractText: Chronic total occlusion (CTO) percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is associated with substantial ischemic risk, yet the optimal duration of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) after successful CTO-PCI remains uncertain. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing extended DAPT (>12 months) with short-term DAPT (≤12 months) following CTO-PCI. Four electronic biomedical databases were searched from inception to September 2026. Comparative studies evaluating adult patients undergoing successful CTO-PCI with drug-eluting stent implantation were eligible. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random-effects model. Three retrospective cohort studies including 3362 patients were identified, with 1761 receiving extended DAPT and 1601 receiving short-term DAPT. Extended DAPT was associated with a significantly lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events compared with short-term DAPT (RR 0.68; 95% CI 0.55-0.84; P = 0.0004). There was no significant difference in all-cause death (RR 0.25; 95% CI 0.04-1.41; P = 0.116), myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death, major bleeding, or revascularization outcomes. However, extended DAPT was associated with a significantly higher risk of total bleeding (RR 2.34; 95% CI 1.31-4.20; P = 0.0043). Among patients undergoing successful CTO-PCI, extended DAPT was associated with lower major adverse cardiovascular events but increased total bleeding compared with DAPT ≤12 months.

title: Normal-BMI MASLD is Associated with Increased Mortality, Cardiovascular Events, Cancer and Lower GLP-1 Use.
authorString: Casimiro I, Agawa A, Tacata RHN, Lim E, Kuwada SK.

journal.title: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

abstractText: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) can occur in individuals who are not overweight or have obesity (normal-BMI MASLD), yet disease burden and management remain poorly characterized. We compared long-term outcomes and incretin-based therapy use between normal-BMI MASLD (nbMASLD) and overweight/obesity-associated MASLD (obMASLD) across racial and ethnic groups. We conducted a retrospective, observational study using the TriNetX United States Network. Adults diagnosed with MASLD or metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) from 2005-2025 were classified using ethnicity-informed normal-BMI thresholds: <23 kg/m2 for Asian, <27 kg/m2 for Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander, and <25 kg/m2 for White/others. Propensity-score matching balanced demographic and clinical covariates. Outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analyses and Cox proportional hazards models with obMASLD as the reference group. Among 619,171 eligible patients, 51,940 matched pairs were identified. Nb-BMI MASLD was associated with higher all-cause mortality across grouped ethnic groups, with survival of 77.49% versus 83.93% in obMASLD (HR 1.735, CI 1.653-1.822). Ethnicity-specific risks included higher myocardial infarction risk in White and Black patients, higher stroke risk in White patients, higher ESRD risk in Black patients, and increased cancers (colorectal, pancreatic and multiple myeloma) among White patients. Incretin-based therapy (IBT) use was markedly lower in nbMASLD but was associated with improved survival. Patients with nbMASLD demonstrated an increased mortality and ethnicity-specific clinical complications than obMASLD despite a more favorable metabolic profile. These findings demonstrate a potential treatment gap for nbMASLD patients and the shortcomings of BMI-based strategies to risk-stratify MASLD patients.

title: Clinical Trajectories and Cardiac Phenotypes in Danon Disease.
authorString: Tsirelman K, Frishman WH, Aronow WS.
abstractText: Danon disease is a rare X-linked lysosomal cardioskeletal myopathy caused by loss-of-function variants in LAMP2, which impair autophagosome-lysosome fusion and lead to accumulation of autophagic vacuoles in cardiomyocytes. Although cardiac penetrance is high in both sexes, the natural history differs markedly by sex. Males typically present in childhood or adolescence with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, skeletal myopathy, and intellectual disability, and often progress to heart failure or ventricular arrhythmias by early adulthood. Females typically present later in life with a cardiac-predominant phenotype that more often evolves to dilated cardiomyopathy, although a subset develops an early onset, severe phenotype reminiscent of male hemizygotes. Pooled case data suggest that cumulative rates of death, heart transplantation, or ventricular assist device implantation are similar between sexes but occur approximately 2 decades later in females, indicating that women may be delayed rather than spared. Ventricular preexcitation, mediated by fasciculoventricular or extranodal accessory pathways, and a characteristic cardiac magnetic resonance pattern of late gadolinium enhancement with mid-basal septal sparing can support the diagnosis, although septal sparing is less frequent in females. Heart transplantation remains the established treatment, and a phase 1 trial of AAV9-LAMP2B gene therapy has provided early proof-of-concept in males.

title: Deep phenotyping of blood cell data reveals novel clinical biomarkers.
authorString: Chen YL, Zhang C, Lucas F, Hadlock J, Foy BH.
abstractText:
Objectives

The complete blood count with differential (CBD) is one of the most common blood tests worldwide. Although modern CBD analyzers generate flow-cytometry based single-cell measurements, the resultant CBD markers are limited to coarse summary features, such as total cell counts and average cell sizes. This means, they cannot detect subtle cell population shifts that may signal early-stage pathogenesis. To test this, we evaluate whether AI-based analysis of the single-cell CBD data can generate novel and clinically prognostic biomarkers.

Methods

We developed two complementary methods for biomarker discovery using CBD tests from an academic medical center. To create interpretable biomarkers, we clustered cells into known sub-populations and performed statistical summarization. In tandem, self-supervised autoencoders were developed to extract novel non-linear markers. We evaluated the utility of the generated markers for patient prognostication across a range of outcomes (mortality, inpatient admission, and future disease development).

Results

Our study included 242,584 CBD samples from 127,543 patients. Both clustering and autoencoder biomarkers showed strong prognostic associations for all-cause mortality, inpatient admission, and development of anemia, cancer, or cardiovascular disease, with associations remaining significant after adjustment for demographics and clinical CBD markers. A large subset of these markers also showed high novelty, having low correlations to existing CBD markers, while also exhibiting significant correlations with broader physiologic signals, such as inflammatory, infectious, and coagulopathic markers.

Conclusions

Collectively, these results demonstrate how AI techniques can allow for deeper phenotyping of routine clinical blood counts, uncovering clinically informative biomarkers that capture subtle physiological variations.

title: Contraindication-adjusted prescription omission patterns of RASi, beta-blockers, and MRAs in hospitalized heart failure: associations with 30-day and 1-year mortality.
authorString: Ishaqui AA, Tripathi R, Tripathi P, Makeen H, Khardali A, Orayj K.
abstractText: Guideline directed therapy is still underused in heart failure and little is known about how missing specific medications near discharge relates to survival. The aim of this study is to examine whether study-defined omission patterns of RASi (ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or ARNIs), beta-blockers, and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) in the final 48 h before discharge were associated with short-term and 1-year mortality among hospitalized adults with heart failure. Adult admissions with a recorded heart failure diagnosis were identified using ICD-9 and ICD-10 codes. The three classes were RASi, beta-blockers, and MRAs (SGLT2 inhibitors were not included). A contraindication-adjusted operational framework was used to identify admissions without selected laboratory or hemodynamic barriers to these therapies and to classify late-hospital prescription omission patterns. Final-48-h orders were a proxy for treatment near discharge, not a reconciled discharge list. This framework did not establish heart failure phenotype-specific guideline eligibility. Associations with mortality within 30 and 365 days after discharge were evaluated using multivariable regression models. The final analytic cohort included 57,098 admissions from 24,922 patients. The reference group with prescriptions for all three study classes was small whereas omission of 2 or 3 therapies was substantially more common across the cohort. Admissions with prescriptions for all three study classes had the lowest 365-day mortality (13.88%). Crude 365-day mortality was higher in all omission groups, reaching 30.84% when RASi and beta-blocker were omitted and 27.50% when all three classes were omitted. In adjusted analyses, omission of all 3 therapies was associated with higher 30-day mortality (OR = 1.67). For 365-day mortality, the strongest adverse association was observed for omission of renin-angiotensin system inhibitor plus beta-blocker (HR = 1.33). Late-hospital omission patterns involving RASi and omission of all three study therapies were associated with higher post-discharge mortality. As heart failure phenotype and left-ventricular ejection fraction were not incorporated into the eligibility definition, these findings should be interpreted as prognostic associations of prescribing patterns rather than causal effects of withholding guideline-indicated HFrEF therapy.

title: Continuous and Wireless Monitoring of Myocardial Dynamics Using Biocompatible Magneto-Viscoelastic Patches.
authorString: Lee S, Kim S, Yoo J, Kim JH, Kang ES, Lee E, Yu SM, Kim JH, An S, Han DS, Liu P, Avila R, Baek YK, Shin M, Park Y.
abstractText: We report a machine learning (ML)-augmented magnetic sensing system for real-time, wireless monitoring of cardiac kinematics during recovery following surgery. While conventional monitoring focuses on electrical activity, it overlooks mechanical performance and pumping efficiency. To bridge this diagnostic gap, we developed a biocompatible magnetic particle matrix (MPM) patch incorporating biocompatible ferromagnetic α″-Fe16N2 microparticles. By integrating this patch onto the epicardium during surgery, our platform enables passive magnetic readout and analysis of epicardial motion without implanted electronics. The system utilizes an external magnetometer to sense 3D magnetic field vectors generated during cardiac contraction and relaxation. By employing a ML-based regression model, we translate dynamic magnetic field variations into precise 3D spatial coordinates to reconstruct the heart's motion. Beyond positional tracking, this framework enables extraction of clinical-grade myocardial velocity profiles, delivering real-time assessment of cardiac health. In vivo studies in rodent models demonstrate the patch resolves cardiac mechanical motion and quantifies acute diastolic dysfunction, revealing pathological shifts undetected by surface ECG. Furthermore, the absence of adverse tissue responses and negligible systemic toxicity after 12 weeks of implantation underscores the biocompatibility of the magnetic particles. These findings establish a foundation for untethered monitoring of cardiac kinematics and suggest an approach for tracking internal organs.

title: Closed-Loop Bioelectronics: From Functional Materials to Autonomous Therapy.
authorString: Shrikrishna NS, Prakashan D, Gandhi S.
abstractText: Closed-loop bioelectronic systems sense physiological signals, compute adaptive therapeutic decisions, then deliver precisely timed interventions without human oversight, meeting a clinical need that fixed-schedule treatments cannot address. Achieving this capability at clinical scale requires functional materials that form stable, mechanically matched interfaces with living tissue, sensing and actuation components operating across electrical, chemical, or optical modalities, alongside system architectures that integrate real-time feedback control with wireless autonomous operation within implantable form factors. This review traces recent advances along the complete closed-loop pipeline, from functional material families at its foundation, through the transducer technologies and control architectures that enable autonomous operation, to the clinical systems that validate therapeutic outcomes. Spanning neurological, cardiovascular, metabolic, and wound healing applications, closed-loop operation has advanced from preclinical proof-of-concept to human clinical validation, with commercially approved devices now operating across multiple disease domains. Chronic interface stability, the generalization of embedded machine learning beyond controlled experimental settings, and wireless power delivery at clinical tissue depths, alongside the regulatory complexity of next-generation adaptive combination products, constitute the defining challenges at the current frontier of the field.

title: Acute Coronary Occlusion in Patient With Congenitally Corrected Transposition of the Great Arteries-Wiring Towards the Unknown.
authorString: Giangiacomi F, Cuman M, Vermeersch P, Agostoni P, Zivelonghi C.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText: As life expectancy in patients with congenital heart disease continues to increase, coronary artery disease and acute coronary syndromes are encountered more and more in this population, with a higher level of complexity, especially in the acute setting. We present a case of acute thrombotic occlusion of the left circumflex coronary artery in a patient with congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries. This case highlights several challenges from ECG and computed tomography interpretation to coronary angiography and PCI performance. Key pre-procedural and procedural steps are revised to guide toward prompt and successful revascularization.

title: Successful transcatheter treatment of chronic mechanical haemolysis after cardiac surgery: a case report.
authorString: Schupp N, Logeswaran T, Rohde M, Akintürk H, Jux C.
abstractText: Chronic haemolysis is a rare but important postsurgical complication in children with congenital heart defects. A 13-year-old with a previously uncorrected complex heart defect underwent corrective surgery. He developed haemolysis postoperatively. A mechanical cause due to turbulent flow through a narrowed intraventricular Dacron patch tunnel was suspected. Balloon dilatation and stent placement successfully resolved the stenosis and haemolysis.

title: Spontaneous inversion of the left atrial appendage: a first autopsy case report and updated literature review.
authorString: Wathek T, Nouma Y, Atig A, Hamdani M, Harzallah H.
abstractText: A mass in the left atrium commands immediate attention. Echocardiography reflexively points towards thrombus, vegetation, or tumour-the common culprits. Rarer, and easily overlooked, is a fourth possibility that has accumulated a quiet but instructive literature since the earliest days of open-heart surgery: inversion of the left atrial appendage. The spontaneous form, occurring outside any surgical context, is documented in fewer than ten cases worldwide. We present the autopsy findings of a spontaneously inverted left atrial appendage in an 8-month-old male infant who had never undergone cardiac surgery. This case, placed alongside an updated review of the literature from 2020 to 2024, reinforces a simple but easily forgotten message: spontaneous left atrial appendage inversion can occur at any age, even in infants with no surgical history. A pressure gradient across the appendage wall, most often driven by pericardial effusion, appears to be the decisive pathophysiological trigger.

title: Association of haematologic parameters with persistent rheumatic heart disease stage in children: a pilot study.
authorString: Kalay Şentürk NG, Ehlil SA, Karakaş A, Çelik SC, Akay N, Albayrak B, Çulpan HC, Yücel İK, Kasapçopur Ö, Dedeoğlu R.
abstractText:
Purpose

Rheumatic heart disease remains a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity in children. Although echocardiography is central to diagnosis and staging, it does not directly reflect inflammatory processes that may contribute to ongoing valvular damage. This study aimed to evaluate the association between baseline haematologic parameters and persistent rheumatic heart disease stage in children with prior acute rheumatic fever.

Methods

In this single-centre retrospective pilot study, 45 children with persistent rheumatic heart disease were classified as Stage A (n = 23), Stage B (n = 14), or Stage C (n = 8) according to the 2023 World Heart Federation echocardiographic staging framework. Baseline laboratory values obtained during acute presentation were analysed. Clinical and laboratory variables were compared across stages using non-parametric tests. Binary logistic regression identified factors associated with advanced disease (Stage B-C vs Stage A).

Results

Markers reflecting acute inflammatory activity, including leukocyte counts and derived indices, did not differ significantly among stages. In contrast, red cell distribution width, mean platelet volume, and platelet distribution width differed significantly. In multivariable analysis, red cell distribution width, and mean platelet volume were independently associated with advanced persistent rheumatic heart disease stage, with higher values linked to increased odds of Stage B-C disease.

Conclusion

Red cell distribution width and mean platelet volume were associated with advanced stages of persistent paediatric rheumatic heart disease. These widely available haematologic markers may complement echocardiographic assessment. Larger prospective studies are needed to define their clinical utility.Trial registration: Not applicable (retrospective study).

title: Cardiac hemorrhage precedes hypertension-induced fibrosis in plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 deficient mice.
authorString: Pettey AC, Ito S, Franklin MK, Howatt DA, Moorleghen JJ, Levitan BM, Graf DB, Guzmán VZ, Zhang N, Lawrence DA, Sisson TH, Sawada H, Saffitz JE, Lu HS, Daugherty A.
abstractText:
Aims

Plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1) regulates plasmin-mediated proteolysis, thereby influencing vascular stability and tissue remodeling. Angiotensin II (AngII) induces an increase in PAI-1 during the development of ascending thoracic aortic aneurysm (ATAA). The initial purpose of this study was to determine whether deletion of PAI-1 influenced development of ATAA. Subsequently, this study aimed to define the early pathological events preceding cardiac fibrosis in PAI-1 deficiency and the structural domain responsible for its protective effect.

Methods and results

AngII was infused for 4 weeks in whole-body PAI-1 deficient (PAI-1-/-) mice and their wild-type littermates (PAI-1+/+) to examine the role of PAI-1 in ATAA. PAI-1 deficiency did not alter AngII-induced aortopathy but revealed a striking cardiac phenotype characterized by replacement fibrosis predominantly within the epicardium and posterior septum. Ferric iron, indicative of prior hemorrhage, was coincident with fibrosis. Similar phenotypes were observed in PAI-1-/- mice infused with norepinephrine for 4 weeks. To define the pathological events preceding cardiac fibrosis, either AngII or norepinephrine was infused for 1 week in PAI-1+/+ or -/- mice. Both infusions induced extensive epicardial hemorrhage and posterior septal fibrosis in PAI-1-/- mice. To explore the initiation of cardiac pathology, AngII was infused for approximately 1 day. PAI-1-/- mice developed diffuse hemorrhage and cardiomyocyte injury localized to the posterior septum, pathologic changes that preceded overt fibrosis. Finally, to determine the protective domain of PAI-1, saline or AngII was administered to mice harboring loss-of-function point mutations in the protease inhibitory (PAI-1Ala/Ala) or somatomedin B-binding domains (PAI-1AK/AK). Compared to saline infusion, 1 week of AngII induced hemorrhage and heterogeneous fibrosis in PAI-1Ala/Ala, but not PAI-1AK/AK mice.

Conclusions

These findings support that, under hemodynamic stress, PAI-1 deficiency promotes early cardiac hemorrhage and cardiomyocyte injury that lead to fibrosis. Mutational studies implicate dysregulated plasmin generation as an initiator of cardiac injury and fibrosis.

title: Unlike most biomarkers, Lp(a) is far less forgiving on selectivity and metrological shortcomings.
authorString: Cobbaert C.
abstractText: Despite being an established causal risk factor for ASCVD, lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) remains one of the most misunderstood metrics in cardiovascular risk assessment and clinical practice. Standardization of Lp(a) measurement remains challenging due to the marked heterogeneity in apolipoprotein(a) isoform size and co-existence of genetic variants, which affect immunoassay calibration and inter-method comparability, potentially leading to misclassification of cardiovascular risk and impacting clinical decision-making. Stakeholders concerned about accuracy of Lp(a) testing have spent decades trying to solve what was considered a calibration problem for Lp(a). We currently know there is also a measurand heterogeneity problem as revealed by Lp(a) assays with different selectivity's. Consequently, Lp(a) harmonization ultimately requires a clearly defined measurand and supports the transition from mass-based to molar standardization.

title: Survey on lipoprotein(a) testing in Europe. A report by the EFLM Committee on Vascular Risk Biomarkers.
authorString: Cobbaert CM, Di Taranto MD, Fabre-Estremera B, Lackner KJ, Langlois M, Özcan O, Pulkki K.
abstractText:
Objectives

Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a lipoprotein particle similar to low-density lipoprotein with an additional apolipoprotein(a) [apo(a)] covalently linked to apoB-100. Apo(a) is highly polymorphic due to a conserved sequence motif which is repeated 10 to >50-times which is a challenge to immunoassays. Harmonization of diagnostic assays is so far unsatisfactory. This includes the units to report measurement results. This survey should provide information on the current practice of Lp(a) measurement and reporting in EFLM member countries.

Methods

A questionnaire entitled "Lipoprotein (a) - Biomarkers of Cardiovascular Risk" was developed. It consisted of 38 questions for laboratories which measure Lp(a) and 21 questions for laboratories which do not measure Lp(a). A call for the survey was sent out by the EFLM to all members in December 2024. The survey remained open until end of January 2025.

Results

There were 340 laboratories from 40 EFLM countries completing the survey of which 247 measured Lp(a) and 93 did not. There was significant heterogeneity in assay usage, reflected by the fact that the five most common assays made up for only 53 % of all laboratories. Approx. one half each of laboratories reported Lp(a) in mass units or in molar units which was largely dependent on the manufacturer's application.

Conclusions

The survey findings demonstrate that variability in Lp(a) measurement spans all phases of the testing process and involves multiple stakeholders. Laboratories can optimize pre-analytical handling and result reporting. However, the analytical domain is the most critical part which requires coordinated action between standardization bodies and IVD-manufacturers, supported by aligned clinical guidelines.

title: Disproportionality Analysis of Acute Kidney Injury Reports Associated with Sacubitril/Valsartan (ARNI) in the Japanese Adverse Drug Event Report Database.
authorString: Urashima K, Ueda T, Urashima Y, Tamura-Takaori M, Fujimoto A, Tanaka S, Kohda Y, Kitazawa F, Kato R.
abstractText:
Background

Prescriptions of angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI) have increased in recent years; however, few pharmacovigilance studies have investigated acute kidney injury (AKI) reporting associated with ARNI. This study evaluated the disproportionate AKI reporting associated with ARNI in the Japanese Adverse Drug Event Report (JADER) database, compared AKI reporting between reports involving ARNI and valsartan, and explored the factors associated with AKI reporting among reports involving ARNI.

Methods

Reports published in JADER between April 2020 and August 2023 were analyzed. AKI was identified using the narrow and broad scope Preferred Terms of the Standardized MedDRA Query (SMQ) "acute renal failure" (SMQ:20000003). The reporting odds ratios (RORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for ARNI and valsartan. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to estimate adjusted RORs (aRORs) for sex, age, heart failure (HF), diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease (CKD), concomitant diuretics, and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). An additional adjusted analysis directly compared AKI reports between ARNI and valsartan.

Results

A disproportionality signal for AKI was identified in the reports involving ARNI (ROR 7.11, 95% CI 6.27-8.07). Multivariable logistic regression showed that HF (aROR 1.68, 95% CI 1.22-2.31; p = 0.002) and CKD (aROR 2.17, 95% CI 1.60-2.93; p < 0.001) were independently associated with increased AKI reporting among reports involving ARNI. In the adjusted direct comparison, reports involving ARNI had higher odds of AKI reporting than those involving valsartan (aROR 2.03, 95% CI 1.50-2.74).

Conclusions

Disproportionate AKI reporting signals were identified in reports involving ARNI in the JADER database. HF and CKD were independently associated with increased AKI reporting after adjustment. These findings have provided additional pharmacovigilance evidence regarding ARNI-associated AKI in Japan and should be interpreted in light of the inherent limitations of spontaneous reporting data.

title: Question: A silent threat in the left coronary circulation.
authorString: Mantzouranis E, Dardas S, Lavi S.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care
journal.title: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care

title: TNF-induced lethality occurs independently of NLRP3 inflammasome signaling.
authorString: Riebeling T, von Samson-Himmelstjerna FA, Kolbrink B, Schmitt R, Krautwald S.

title: Tumor necrosis factor inhibitors and cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Mesa Rodríguez LF, Zambrano Aristizábal A, Vega Padilla JD.
abstractText: Moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis is associated with persistent systemic inflammation and increased cardiovascular risk. To evaluate the association between anti-TNF therapy and clinical cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. The authors conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and prospectively registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD420251270784). Randomized controlled trials and comparative observational studies evaluating anti-TNF therapy versus placebo, no anti-TNF exposure, topical therapy and/or phototherapy, or non-biologic systemic therapy were eligible. Outcomes of interest were Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE), myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, and all-cause mortality. Fourteen studies were included. In randomized evidence, anti-TNF therapy was not associated with significant differences in the risk of MACE, myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure. In observational analyses stratified by comparator, anti-TNF therapy was associated with a lower pooled risk of reported cardiovascular events versus topical therapy, but not versus oral therapy or phototherapy. The available evidence was limited by short follow-up in randomized trials, low cardiovascular event counts, wide confidence intervals, and indirect assessment of cardiovascular outcomes, as most trials were designed primarily for dermatologic efficacy and general safety rather than cardiovascular endpoints. Anti-TNF agents were not associated with a clear increase in major cardiovascular risk and appear to have an acceptable short-term cardiovascular safety profile. However, current evidence does not establish a conclusive cardioprotective effect, and larger prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed.

title: Effectiveness of Wrist-Worn Wearable-Guided Cardiac Rehabilitation Delivered Through Fully Remote or Hybrid Programs in Patients With Cardiovascular Disease: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
authorString: Choi JH, Lee SY, Seo KC, Lee SY, Lee HK, Heo D, Ryu H, Kim JH, Kwon JE, Kim BR, Lee M.
abstractText: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide, yet participation in cardiac rehabilitation (CR) remains suboptimal. Wrist-worn wearables may support fully remote or hybrid CR through activity monitoring and individualized feedback, but the effectiveness and consistency of benefits remain uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of wrist-worn wearable-guided CR delivered through fully remote or hybrid programs initiated during phase II or III CR in patients with CVD. A total of 8 databases were searched for randomized controlled trials published from January 1, 2015, through August 7, 2026. Eligible trials enrolled adults with CVD and integrated a wrist-worn wearable into fully remote or hybrid CR. Studies focused primarily on heart failure or using wearables only for outcome measurement were excluded. Primary outcomes were peak oxygen consumption (VO2), 6-minute walk distance (6MWD), and daily steps. Random-effects meta-analyses used mean differences (MDs), except for quality of life, which used standardized MDs. Between-study variance was estimated using the DerSimonian-Laird method, pooled-effect CIs used the Knapp-Hartung adjustment, and 95% prediction intervals (PIs) used the Nagashima-Noma-Furukawa parametric bootstrap method. Risk of bias was assessed with Cochrane Risk of Bias 2. Subgroup and univariable meta-regression analyses explored study and intervention characteristics. A total of 18 trials involving 1993 randomized participants, reported in 20 publications, were included; 17 contributed to meta-analysis. Pooled estimates favored wearable-guided CR for peak VO2 (10 studies; 591 participants; MD 1.69, 95% CI 0.46-2.92, 95% PI -2.21 to 5.39 mL/kg/min), 6MWD (9 studies; 1094 participants; MD 31.03, 95% CI 7.66-53.92, 95% PI -62.11 to 123.18 m), and daily steps (8 studies; 474 participants; MD 1062.8, 95% CI 383.5-1825.0, 95% PI -503.0 to 2860.0 steps/day). All 3 PIs included the null, indicating uncertainty about consistency across future comparable settings. No clear pooled effects were observed for anaerobic threshold, BMI, waist circumference, grip strength, or quality of life. Subgroup differences were not statistically significant. In univariable meta-regression, a higher proportion of female participants was associated with greater peak VO2 improvement, although this aggregate-level finding was exploratory. Wrist-worn wearable-guided CR delivered through fully remote or hybrid programs may improve average exercise capacity and physical activity in patients with CVD. However, PIs included the null, indicating uncertainty about consistency across future settings. These programs may extend activity monitoring, individualized feedback, and behavioral support beyond center-based CR, but their multicomponent nature prevents attributing effects to wearables alone. Larger, rigorously designed trials with standardized protocols and outcomes should identify the patients and program components most likely to benefit. Future research should also evaluate long-term adherence, safety, equity, and implementation within routine multidisciplinary CR across diverse health systems.

title: Impact of Elevated Blood Pressure Targets on Splanchnic Ischemia and Mortality in Septic Resuscitation: Systematic Review.
authorString: Cisneros P, Ortiz Caviedes JF, Piñeros Ladino LM, Quintero N, Oñate Cervera VG, Urrea Ospina JD, Cerna Alcantar EP.
abstractText: Sepsis causes deaths worldwide each day, with hemodynamic resuscitation being central to management. Guidelines recommend a 65-mm Hg mean arterial pressure (MAP) target, yet the evidence for elevated targets remains fragmented across mortality, renal, and splanchnic outcomes. This review aims to comprehensively appraise the impact of elevated MAP targets on splanchnic ischemia, mortality, and organ-specific outcomes in septic resuscitation. Following the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 guidelines, we systematically searched PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar for studies comparing MAP targets in septic shock. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2; randomized controlled trials [RCTs]) and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (nonrandomized studies). The findings were synthesized narratively according to the Synthesis Without Meta-Analysis guidelines, with random-effects meta-analysis for mortality outcomes. Evidence certainty was graded using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. From 3254 records, 11 studies (2895 patients; 4 RCTs, 7 nonrandomized) met the inclusion criteria. Pooled 90-day mortality across 3 trials showed a nonsignificant trend toward higher mortality with elevated MAP targets (320/720, 44.4% vs 280/722, 38.8%; OR 1.31, 95% CI 0.97-1.77). Pooled 28- or 30-day mortality showed a similar nonsignificant trend (OR 1.25, 95% CI 0.98-1.61), which was robust to sensitivity analysis. Narratively, mortality findings across nonpooled observational studies were inconsistent; some linked low MAP to higher death risk, and others found no significant association. Renal outcomes were inconsistent, with some studies showing reduced renal replacement therapy or improved acute kidney injury recovery at higher targets, particularly in hypertensive or cirrhotic subgroups. Elevated MAP targets consistently increased vasopressor exposure and were associated with more arrhythmias and fewer organ support-free days. No study reported splanchnic ischemia as a discrete outcome; mesenteric ischemia rates were low and similar between arms. Overall certainty of evidence was very low. Higher MAP targets show no clear mortality or splanchnic perfusion benefit and may increase overall harm, though select subgroups, chronic hypertension, and cirrhosis, may benefit, supporting individualized, risk-stratified MAP targeting over uniformly elevated-target strategies.

title: Pazopanib alternating with bevacizumab in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to treatment: a multicentre, single-arm, phase 1/2 trial.
authorString: George S, Vaishampayan U, Hutson A, Groman A, Pili R, Green K, Herbst L, Kallicharan-Smith R, DiRaddo AM, Farrell E, Gopalakrishnan D, Heath E, Wulff E, Kilari D, Appleman L, Parikh R.
abstractText: VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) are considered the backbone for the treatment of metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. We hypothesise that the administration of bevacizumab during scheduled breaks in pazopanib (TKI) treatment can improve tolerability and prolong progression-free survival compared with historical controls. In this single-arm, phase 1/2 trial in five US academic cancer centres, patients (aged ≥18 years) with histologically confirmed metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 or less, and adequate organ functions were included. The phase 1 portion included patients with up to one previous therapy with high-dose IL-2 or an anti-PD-1 compound alone or in combination with a CTLA-4 inhibitor. The phase 2 portion enrolled only patients with treatment-naive metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. The primary endpoint of phase 1 was to find the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D). We tested a novel regimen using four dose levels: oral pazopanib (600 or 800 mg daily on days 1-28, followed by a 7 day break) alternating with intravenous bevacizumab (5, 7·5, or 10 mg/kg, one on day 36 and one on day 50) on a 10-week cycle in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to TKI treatment. The primary endpoint of phase 2 was median progression-free survival, assessed by a masked central statistician review. Dose selection (in patients who had completed 15 weeks) and activity (in patients who had completed one full 10-week cycle of the novel regimen) were analysed in the per-protocol population. Safety analyses included all patients who received any treatment. This trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01684397) and is ongoing but closed to new participants. Between Nov 21, 2012, and June 11, 2018, phase 1 enrolled 25 patients, with 18 patients evaluable for dose-limiting toxicity during the extended 15-week safety assessment period. The RP2D was established as pazopanib 800 mg daily (days 1-28) and bevacizumab 10 mg/kg on days 36 and 50 of a 10-week cycle. Between Jan 23, 2019, and Oct 19, 2023, phase 2 enrolled 53 patients, of whom 51 (including six from phase 1) were evaluable for activity and 59 were evaluable for safety. 36 (71%) patients were male and 15 (29%) were female, and 48 (94%) patients were White. 33 (65%) patients in phase 2 had favourable risk per the International Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Database Consortium categories. After a median follow-up of 63·7 months (IQR 16·2-73·5), median progression-free survival was 24·8 months (95% CI 17·2-34·3). The most common grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events were hypertension (20 [34%] of 59) and elevated aspartate aminotransferase (seven [12%]) and alanine aminotransferase (ten [17%]). Five (8%) patients discontinued the study for drug-related serious adverse events. No treatment-related deaths occurred. The phase 1 portion identified the safe RP2D. The phase 2 portion showed that this novel regimen has promising antitumour activity in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma in the predominantly favourable risk group who are naive to treatment. Phase 3 randomised controlled trial data are needed to confirm these findings. The Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center (RPCCC), US National Cancer Institute (NCI), Novartis.

title: Advances in HLA desensitization for kidney transplant candidates.
authorString: Chandran S, Huang E, Vo A, Jordan S.

journal.title: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension

abstractText:
Purpose of the review

Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) sensitization is a significant barrier to kidney transplantation. The goal of HLA desensitization is to increase access to transplantation and reduce the risk of antibody-mediated rejection and graft loss. This review outlines currently used therapies and highlights novel strategies for HLA desensitization.

Recent findings

Important advances include promising data on imlifidase, a novel immunoglobulin G (IgG) endopeptidase that cleaves IgG molecules into Fc and F(ab)'2 fragments, negating antibody-dependent cytotoxicity (ADCC) and complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC). A positive phase III study will likely lead to FDA approval in December 2026. Additionally, initial reports of HLA desensitization using ant-CD38 monoclonal antibodies, bispecific T cell engagers targeting B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA), and chimeric antigen receptor T cells targeting CD19 and BCMA, suggest improved efficacy at HLA antibody reduction and lower risk of posttransplant DSA rebound.

Summary

Newer, more potent agents targeting pathogenic IgG molecules, B-cells and plasma cells are likely to improve the efficacy of HLA desensitization regimens. As data emerge from ongoing clinical trials, the clinical applicability of such therapies will depend, in addition to efficacy, on their safety profile, cost and complexity of use.

title: Anticoagulation and All-Cause Mortality in Adults Aged 80 Years and Older with Atrial Fibrillation: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Kaya G, Sanchez Garcia J, Schneider M, Yadav D, Ndukwe M, Chen CH, Joynt Maddox KE.
abstractText: The benefits and risks of anticoagulation therapy in patients aged ≥ 80 years with atrial fibrillation (AF) remain underexplored, as this population is underrepresented in randomized clinical trials. We evaluated mortality and bleeding outcomes associated with anticoagulation use in this population. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using MDClone, a synthetic electronic health record database from a large US health system, including 45,305 patients aged ≥ 80 years with AF after excluding those with mitral stenosis, mechanical heart valves, cirrhosis, or end-stage renal disease. Patients were categorized as continued, initiated, discontinued, or never anticoagulated. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality at 30 days, 6 months, 1 year, and 5 years; secondary outcomes were ischemic stroke, gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB), and intracranial hemorrhage (ICH). To address immortal time bias, the primary analysis used a time-varying Cox model, complemented by a 90-day landmark analysis and propensity score matching. Patients who continued anticoagulation had lower 1-year mortality than those never anticoagulated (8.7% vs 17.7%; p < 0.001). In the time-varying Cox model, anticoagulation was associated with a 25% lower hazard of mortality (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.71-0.79). Compared with continued anticoagulation, mortality was higher among patients who initiated (HR 1.51, 95% CI 1.38-1.66), discontinued (HR 1.64, 95% CI 1.49-1.81), or never received anticoagulation (HR 2.22, 95% CI 2.05-2.41), and persisted after propensity score matching. At 5 years, mortality converged across groups. GIB was more frequent in anticoagulated patients (continued 13.0%, initiated 11.9%), whereas ICH rates were low and comparable across groups (1.3-1.6%, p = 0.129). Among patients aged ≥ 80 years with AF, anticoagulation therapy was associated with lower all-cause mortality despite an increase in gastrointestinal bleeding. These findings support continued anticoagulation in appropriately selected elderly patients, rather than withholding therapy on the basis of age alone.

title: HFSA Scientific Statement on Right Heart Failure.
authorString: Kanwar MK, Carnicelli AP, Belkin MN, Esposito ML, Coons JC, Molina EJ, Airhart S, Cascino TM, Blumer V, Tedford RJ.
abstractText: Right heart failure (RHF), both acute and chronic is increasingly recognized as a distinct and clinically significant syndrome across the spectrum of cardiovascular disease. Estimates suggest RHF complicates >25-30% of hospitalizations for acute decompensated HF and is nearly universal in advanced pulmonary hypertension (PH) (1) Despite recent diagnostic and therapeutic advancements, RHF remains associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and impaired quality of life. Addressing RHF requires dedicated strategies tailored to its pathophysiology, including early identification, risk stratification, and novel therapies. (2) While randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on the topic remain limited, there has been increasing emphasis on early recognition and management of RHF (especially in the setting of left ventricular [LV] failure). In addition, there is an expanding role for temporary mechanical circulatory support (MCS) in acute RHF and percutaneous tricuspid interventions in chronic RHF. Yet, the field remains limited by its under-recognition, lack of standardized definitions, and limited therapeutic options, which underscore the urgent need for consensus and guidance.

title: Home CHF feasibility trial protocol: Impact of at-home Subcutaneous furosemide in patients with Chronic Kidney Disease and Heart Failure.
authorString: Tumelty E, Chung I, Hartshorne-Evans N, Gunc M, Ster IC, Anderson L, Banerjee D.
abstractText: Hospital admissions are common in patients with heart failure (HF), particularly in those with concomitant chronic kidney disease (HF-CKD). Hospitalisation is often driven by fluid overload, requiring intravenous furosemide. Subcutaneous furosemide is emerging as an alternative which may facilitate at-home treatment. This study will assess the feasibility of conducting a randomised controlled trial (RCT) to evaluate whether subcutaneous furosemide can reduce hospital admissions in people with HF-CKD. Stage one - Recruitment and monitoring of at-risk patients: We aim to recruit 200 people with HF-CKD with at least one hospital admission within the preceding year. These participants will be monitored for signs of fluid accumulation. Stage two - Treatment: The second stage will run contemporaneously to the first stage. The first 80 participants to develop fluid accumulation will be randomised to usual care (attend hospital and receive standard treatment) or at-home furosemide. The participants allocated to home treatment will administer SQIN-furosemide via a patch infusor device, 80 mg daily for five days, then be reviewed in a final clinic appointment. These participants will monitor their weight and observations daily, as well as receive a check-in call from the research team. Potassium levels will be checked twice over five days. The primary outcome of this feasibility study will be recruitment and retention of participants, as well as adherence to the intervention. Findings from this feasibility trial will inform the planning of a definitive RCT to evaluate whether subcutaneous furosemide can reduce hospital admissions in people living with HF-CKD.

title: Incidence, factors associated with, and outcomes of acute kidney injury among cancer patients hospitalized in a tertiary hospital in Dodoma, Tanzania
authorString: Kyomo A, Mlwati A, Meremo A.
abstractText: Introduction : Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a significant complication among hospitalized cancer patients, often leading to unfavorable outcomes. However, published data are scarce. This study assessed the incidence, factors associated with, and outcomes of AKI among hospitalized cancer patients at Benjamin Mkapa Hospital (BMH) in Dodoma. Methodology : A prospective longitudinal study was conducted among cancer patients hospitalized at a tertiary hospital in Dodoma between December 2025 and May 2026. Hospitalized adult patients aged ≥ 18 years confirmed with cancer by histopathology were recruited and enrolled via consecutive sampling. At baseline, patients’ demographic and clinical data were collected; laboratory investigations were done, and all were recorded in a questionnaire. AKI was evaluated using the Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria at baseline, 48 hours, and day 7, and estimated glomerular filtration rate was calculated after 3 months using the Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration (CKD-EPI). Data were entered into an Excel spreadsheet and analyzed using SPSS version 27. The modified Poisson regression analysis was used to identify factors associated with AKI among patients hospitalized with cancer. Results : A total of 231 participants were enrolled. The median age was 62.0 (IQR 48–70) years; 55% (127/231) were female. The incidence of AKI among hospitalized cancer patients was 19.5% (45/231). Factors associated with AKI among patients hospitalized with cancer included diabetes mellitus (aRR 2.67; 95% CI, 1.61–4.43; p < 0.001); hematological cancer (aRR 3.88; 95% CI, 2.09–7.19; p < 0.001); advanced cancer stage (aRR 2.50; 95% CI, 1.49–4.20; p < 0.001); cancer related surgery (aRR 2.50; 95% CI, 1.47–4.25; P < 0.001); hypertension (aRR 2.16; 95% CI, 1.30–3.58; p = 0.003) and sepsis (aRR 3.21; 95% CI, 2.07–4.98; p < 0.001). Additionally, 59.5% (25/42) had AKI resolution, 19.1% (8/42) progressed to CKD, and 21.4% (9/42) died. Conclusion : The incidence of AKI is high among hospitalized cancer patients and is associated with advanced stage of cancer, hematological cancer, sepsis, hypertension, and diabetes mellitus. More than one-third of the cancer patients who were found with AKI progressed to CKD or died. Clinical trial number: Not applicable.

title: Localization of Non-Compressible Torso Hemorrhage with Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound: A Swine Model.
authorString: Lee YB, Olson MT, Cuneo M, Goei C, Singh P, Saul-McBeth J, Rall J, Causey MW, Hart TG.
abstractText:
Introduction

Non-compressible torso hemorrhage (NCTH) remains a leading cause of preventable death in civilian and military trauma. In settings without cross-sectional imaging, the Focused Assessment with Sonography in Trauma (FAST) is used to detect hemoperitoneum but is limited in evaluating the retroperitoneum, is highly operator dependent, and cannot reliably localize bleeding. Contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) has demonstrated high sensitivity for solid organ pathology, but its role in detecting and localizing NCTH is not well defined.

Methods

NCTH was induced in 18 swine (70-90 kg) via laparoscopic solid organ injury or endovascular injury to an aortic branch vessel. Standard FAST and CEUS were performed pre- and post-injury in a non-randomized, paired fashion. Outcomes included successful visualization of contrast extravasation with accurate localization of hemorrhage and time to hemorrhage detection.

Results

Both CEUS and FAST detected hemoperitoneum in all cases. CEUS identified active contrast extravasation from solid organ and vascular injuries in 78% of cases and improved detection of low-volume hemoperitoneum. CEUS also detected hemorrhage in the retroperitoneum. Time to detection was similar between modalities.

Conclusion

CEUS is a feasible adjunct to FAST for detecting and localizing NCTH. This swine model provides a reproducible platform for evaluating portable hemorrhage localization technologies in austere environments.

title: Posterior Inter-Antral Linear Ablation Using Pulsed Field Energy: Electrophysiological Validation and Early Clinical Outcomes.
authorString: Liu X, Wang P, Peng X, Wang Z, Guo X, Zuo S, Zhang J, Zhou N, Dong J, Ma C.
abstractText: Durable conduction block across the left atrial roof remains challenging because of complex anatomy and limitations of thermal energy delivery. Pulsed field ablation (PFA) may enable a short posterior inter-antral line as an adjunctive strategy beyond pulmonary vein isolation (PVI), providing linear conduction block at a more inferior posterior LA location than a conventional roofline. However, its electrophysiological characteristics and clinical relevance remain uncertain. In this single-center, nonrandomized comparative cohort study, a prospectively enrolled cohort undergoing PVI plus posterior inter-antral linear ablation was compared with contemporaneous patients undergoing PVI without additional left atrial ablation. The primary clinical endpoint was atrial arrhythmia recurrence beyond a 90-day blanking period. Propensity score matching was the primary comparative analysis; inverse probability of treatment weighting and multivariable Cox regression were sensitivity analyses. Among 306 patients, 65 underwent posterior inter-antral linear ablation and 241 underwent PVI alone. Posterior-line ablation produced characteristic reciprocal pacing responses and a caudal-to-cranial posterior wall activation pattern consistent with conduction block. During a median follow-up of 198 days, atrial arrhythmia recurrence occurred in 4 of 65 (6.2%) versus 38 of 241 (15.8%) patients. In the primary PSM analysis, posterior inter-antral linear ablation was associated with lower recurrence (HR 0.23; 95% CI 0.07-0.78), with consistent results in sensitivity analyses. Posterior inter-antral linear ablation using PFA provides a reproducible electrophysiological pattern of conduction block and was associated with lower short-term atrial arrhythmia recurrence than PVI alone in patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. These findings warrant confirmation in randomized trials.

title: Redefining Cardiometabolic Disease: Expert Consensus on the CardioVascular-Kidney-Liver-Metabolic (CVKLM) Multiorgan Staging.
authorString: Baudry G, Biegus J, López-Azor JC, Bozkurt B, Butler J, Cobo-Marcos M, Dauw J, Francque S, Girerd N, Green JB, Guzik M, Iwanek G, Kobayashi M, Myhre PL, Metra M, Miró Ò, Mullens W, Palazzuoli A, Ponikowski P, Ronco C, Rossignol P, Sanyal A, Zoccali C, Vaduganathan M, Van Spall HGC, Zannad F.
abstractText: Cardiometabolic diseases increasingly manifest as interconnected dysfunction across the heart, vasculature, kidneys, liver, and metabolic system. The global rise in obesity, insulin resistance, and diabetes, together with therapies benefiting multiple organs, has reshaped the epidemiology and understanding of cardiometabolic disease, exposing the limitations of organ-specific or single-stage approaches. The cardioVascular-kidney-liver-metabolic (CVKLM) framework is a multidimensional staging system in which cardiac, vascular, kidney, liver, and metabolic involvement are graded independently from absent to advanced. Analogous to tumour-node-metastasis staging, it provides a standardized language describing disease severity within each organ and its distribution across organs. Rather than replacing existing classifications, CVKLM integrates universal heart failure stages, validated vascular risk assessment, KDIGO chronic kidney disease stratification, contemporary metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and advanced liver disease criteria, and current definitions of diabetes and clinical obesity. Unlike hierarchical frameworks assigning a single overall stage, CVKLM preserves organ-specific information and records coexisting abnormalities across domains. Intended for clinical and research phenotyping and staging rather than as a validated global risk score, it may facilitate systematic recognition of concomitant organ disease, support existing organ-specific diagnostic, referral, and treatment pathways, and provide a standardized taxonomy for observational studies and clinical trials. The prognostic significance of CVKLM profiles, their incremental value beyond established risk tools, and their clinical utility remain to be established. By integrating these domains within a common architecture, CVKLM offers a pragmatic framework spanning the full spectrum of cardiometabolic disease, from preclinical involvement to advanced multiorgan failure.

title: Phenotyping of Arrhythmia-induced Cardiomyopathy: From Bench to Bedside and Back.
authorString: Körtl T, Ruppert J, Sossalla S.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

Arrhythmia-induced cardiomyopathy (AIC) is an increasingly recognized and potentially reversible cause or modifier of heart failure. This review summarizes experimental and clinical evidence with a focus on atrial fibrillation (AFib)-induced left ventricular systolic dysfunction.

Recent findings

Recent studies demonstrate that AIC extends beyond tachycardia alone and involves rhythm irregularity, loss of atrioventricular synchrony, altered calcium handling, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction and substrate vulnerability. Clinical trials demonstrate the superiority of rhythm control therapy by catheter ablation in patients with AFib and heart failure. Emerging data illustrate the importance of phenotyping of AIC according to myocardial substrate and individual ventricular response to AFib. AIC should be considered as a heterogeneous spectrum. Refined phenotyping may improve prediction of recovery and guide specific and individual therapy.

title: Baroreceptor Dysregulation Mediated via Neurohormonal Mechanisms in Heart Failure and its Influence on Renal Function: Potential Role of Baroreflex Activation Therapy.
authorString: Ghoussaini R, Patel A, Simpson B, Gabrah K, Wahba R, Mohanty P, Sriperumbuduri S, Al-Ani M, Patel H, Shah KB, Li P.
abstractText: Baroreflex activation therapy (BAT), which electrically stimulates carotid sinus baroreceptors to modulate autonomic tone, has emerged as a novel adjunct to guideline-directed medical therapy for resistant hypertension and heart failure. Beyond its established cardiovascular benefits, emerging preclinical and early-phase clinical data suggest that BAT may favorably influence renal function and cardiorenal interactions. By suppressing sympathetic nervous system activity and downregulating the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, BAT improves renal hemodynamics and may counteract key mechanisms leading to diuretic resistance. The latter represents a common and clinically significant challenge in patients with advanced heart failure, in whom impaired renal perfusion, neurohormonal activation, and tubular remodeling all contribute to reduced diuretic responsiveness and worsening kidney function. Early evidence indicates that BAT may preserve glomerular filtration rate, reduce proteinuria and improve urinary sodium excretion, suggesting potential renoprotective effects and a therapeutic role in mitigating diuretic resistance. However, these findings remain limited by small sample sizes, short follow-up periods, and heterogenous study populations across diverse clinical settings. This review synthesizes key physiologic mechanisms linking baroreflex signal modulation to renal outcomes and evaluates available clinical data. While BAT offers established cardiovascular benefits in heart failure, its renoprotective and diuretic-sparing potential remains investigational and lacks validation from randomized clinical trials. Dedicated prospective large-scale randomized studies are essential to establish long-term renal efficacy across the cardiorenal disease spectrum.

title: Atrial Fibrillation Burden as an Outcome in Clinical Trials.
authorString: Andrade JG, Kirchhof P.
abstractText: AbstractAtrial fibrillation is the most common cardiac arrhythmia in the world. In clinical trials evaluating interventions for atrial fibrillation, outcomes have been traditionally defined using a thirty second arrhythmia end point. In this Clinical Trials Workshop, we evaluate the role of atrial fibrillation burden as a primary outcome for atrial fibrillation intervention trials. In particular, we evaluate key considerations for ascertainment, definition, and analysis of atrial fibrillation burden while further considering regulatory implications of its use as a primary end point.

title: Development and External Validation of a Machine Learning Model to Predict Post-Implantation Syndrome After Thoracic Endovascular Aortic Repair in Patients With Type B Aortic Dissection
authorString: zhai j, Wang T, Hu A, Zhou L, Yu T, Lei W, Zhu Y, Chen T, Tang C, Yu H, Li Y, Zheng R, Shao J, Shao J, Yuan J.
abstractText: Objective Post-implantation syndrome (PIS) is a common acute inflammatory complication after thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) for type B aortic dissection. However, effective tools for the early identification of high-risk patients are still lacking. This study therefore developed and validated a machine learning–based risk prediction model for PIS after TEVAR. Methods In this two-center retrospective cohort study, 676 patients who underwent TEVAR between 2021 and 2025 formed the development cohort, and an independent external cohort of 198 patients (2023–2025) was used for external validation. Predictors were selected through a four-method voting procedure; eight algorithms were compared under stratified 10-fold cross-validation and evaluated with a composite score on the internal validation set. Model performance was assessed by discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis; the model was interpreted with SHAP and deployed as a nomogram and a web-based calculator to facilitate clinical application. Results Nine predictors were selected. Among the eight machine learning models built with these predictors, ridge logistic regression ranked highest on the composite score and was selected as the optimal model, with a pooled out-of-fold area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.811. The AUC was 0.784 in internal validation and 0.801 in external validation; the Brier score was 0.097 in both cohorts, and the calibration slopes were 0.98 and 1.13, respectively. Conclusions A ridge logistic regression model, integrating disease severity, inflammatory status, and perioperative factors, was developed and externally validated for predicting PIS after TEVAR. The model showed good discrimination and calibration, and was deployed as a nomogram and web-based calculator to facilitate three-tier risk stratification and perioperative decision-making. Clinical trial registration Not applicable, as this study is a retrospective cohort analysis and does not require registration.

title: Management and Outcomes of Bleeding Ectopic Varices in Patients With Liver Cirrhosis: A Systematic Review and Pooled Analysis.
authorString: Zhu A, Rasaratnam K, Majeed A, Kemp W, Clements W, Roberts SK.
abstractText: Bleeding ectopic varices is a rare but life-threatening complication in patients with clinically significant portal hypertension and liver cirrhosis, with limited evidence available to guide treatment decisions. To evaluate the safety and efficacy of current therapies for bleeding ectopic varices. A systematic review with pooled analysis was performed based on searches conducted in Embase, MEDLINE and Cochrane Library databases. Case series, retrospective and prospective studies including adults with a history of liver cirrhosis or portal hypertension presenting with bleeding ectopic varices were included. Individual patient data on interventions, rebleeding, complications and mortality were pooled and summarised using descriptive analysis. No conventional meta-analysis was conducted due to the heterogeneous nature of included studies. 44 studies (15 non-consecutive case series, 25 single-arm retrospective cohort studies, 3 double-arm retrospective cohort studies and 1 single-arm prospective study) involving 458 patients met selection criteria. Alcohol-related liver disease (38.7%), viral hepatitis (18.8%) and primary sclerosing cholangitis (15.7%) were the most common aetiologies. Child-Pugh A, B and C cirrhosis accounted for 29.7%, 46.7% and 23.5% of patients, respectively, and the pooled median Model for End Stage Liver Disease score was 14.0 (IQR 10.0-20.8). The most reported sites of ectopic varices were duodenal (27.7%), rectal (27.3%) and stomal/peri-stomal (23.1%). Endoscopic sclerosant injection appeared to have a lower rebleeding rate than band ligation in the treatment of bleeding rectal varices (3.3% vs. 33.3%). Across variceal subtypes, transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) combined with variceal embolisation, was observed to have a lower rebleeding rate than TIPS alone. The pooled all-cause mortality following small bowel, rectal and stomal variceal bleeding were 25.0%, 42.9%, and 66.6%, respectively, over a median follow-up period of 354 (IQR 120-780) days. Small sample sizes, missing data and significant heterogeneity between studies limited data quality. Bleeding ectopic varices frequently recurs and carries high mortality. An individualised approach in conjunction with early multidisciplinary team discussions is essential in achieving favourable patient outcomes.

title: Long-term outcomes of congenital subaortic stenosis surgery: systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Shieba Y, Olivello J, Asiri A, Zayat R, Moza A, Tewarie L, Mohammed AFA.
abstractText:
Objectives

To estimate recurrence, reoperation, and aortic insufficiency progression after pediatric surgery for subaortic stenosis and explore associated study-level factors.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for eligible studies published from 1 January 2012 to 3 July 2025. We included observational studies of patients <18 years undergoing surgical resection for SAS with a study-level mean or median postoperative follow-up of ≥ 3 years, which was the prespecified operational definition of long-term follow-up. Proportions were pooled using random-effects models; heterogeneity was quantified using I²; meta-regression assessed study-level associations with reoperation and AI progression; and risk of bias was evaluated using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale.

Results

Seventeen retrospective studies included 1,536 patients; 1,493 contributed to the recurrence analysis. Follow-up ranged from 3.0 to 12.7 years. Overall recurrence was 21% (95% confidence interval, 16-28%; I²=88.1%). Reoperation across 16 studies was 17% (95% confidence interval, 14-20%; I²=41.6%); a prespecified definition-harmonized sensitivity analysis yielded the same estimate (17%; 95% confidence interval, 15-20%; I²=19.1%). In isolated discrete subaortic stenosis, reoperation was 8% and 12% after definition harmonization. Progression to moderate or severe aortic insufficiency was 10% (95% confidence interval, 8-13%). Older study-level age at surgery was inversely associated with reoperation (β = -0.2230; P = 0.0138), whereas higher preoperative peak left ventricular outflow tract gradient was associated with aortic insufficiency progression (odds ratio per 10-mmHg increase, 1.25; P = 0.0072).

Conclusions

Reoperation and clinically important aortic insufficiency remain substantial during follow-up after pediatric subaortic stenosis surgery. Meta-regression findings are exploratory, aggregate associations and should not guide individual operative timing or risk prediction.

title: Development and Clinical Validation of a Stroke Risk Decision System for Patients With Carotid Artery Plaque Based on AI-Powered Handheld Ultrasound and Laboratory Markers.
authorString: Jinyi Z, Mingjiao L, Yi P, Rui Y, Wenjun Z.
abstractText: This study aimed to develop and validate a fusion model combining portable artificial intelligence (AI) ultrasound imaging with multidimensional laboratory data to stratify risk and support decision-making in patients with carotid plaque-related anterior circulation stroke, and to assess its predictive performance and clinical utility. This prospective study enrolled 639 patients with carotid plaque via AI-powered ultrasound at community health centers. Anterior circulation stroke (ACS)/transient ischemic attack (TIA) patients were excluded. All participants completed the 180-day follow-up. The primary outcome was new-onset anterior circulation stroke or TIA, defined as focal neurological deficit > 24 h with CT/MRI-confirmed infarction, or transient (< 24 h) deficit without evidence of acute infarction on neuroimaging. Outcomes were adjudicated by two neurologists (attending or above), with a third for disagreements. Participants were classified into ACS group (n = 140) and non-ACS group (n = 499). Ultrasound features of carotid plaques and clinical laboratory data were compared between the two groups. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with ACS, and a nomogram was constructed based on the regression model. Internal validation was conducted using the bootstrap method. Model performance was assessed in terms of discrimination (C-index and area under the curve [AUC]), calibration (calibration curves), and clinical utility (decision curve analysis [DCA] and clinical impact curves [CIC]). (1) Significant differences were observed between the two groups in history of hypertension, smoking, hyperlipidemia, stroke, and myocardial infarction (MI), as well as plasma triglyceride (TG), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), high-density lipoprotein (HDL) levels, carotid plaque thickness, plaque area, plaque echogenicity percentage, degree of carotid stenosis, plaque continuity score, and plaque mutability score (p < 0.05). No significant differences were found in sex, history of diabetes, total cholesterol (TC), plaque location, or plaque fibrous cap continuity analysis score (p > 0.05) (2) Multivariable logistic regression identified history of stroke, history of myocardial infarction, plaque thickness, LDL, and HDL as independent predictors of stroke. A nomogram based on these factors demonstrated good discrimination (C-index/AUC = 0.884), with a sensitivity of 84.29% and specificity of 72.55%, along with excellent calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test p = 0.250). Decision curve analysis showed superior net benefit across a range of risk thresholds compared with the null model, supporting a multi-threshold stratified intervention strategy. Notably, when the predicted risk exceeded 75%, the model's predictions closely aligned with observed outcomes. The stroke risk decision system developed using AI-powered handheld ultrasound and laboratory indicators demonstrates clinical applicability for early prediction of anterior circulation ischemic stroke and is particularly suitable for early screening and risk stratification of high-risk stroke populations in resource-limited settings.

title: Latent Class Analysis Reveals Distinct Profiles Associated with Preeclampsia in Nulliparous Pregnancies.
authorString: Brown RE, Comeaux CR, Hill AV, Patel J, Amabebe E, Singh N, Fitzpatrick V, Noah A, Dumenci L, Taylor BD.

journal.title: Journal of urban health : bulletin of the New York Academy of Medicine

abstractText: Preeclampsia is a major cause of maternal illness and death, with poorly defined risk factors in nulliparous pregnancies. This study used latent class analysis to identify patterns of social, reproductive, health, and behavior factors associated with preeclampsia in 9809 nulliparous individuals who live in a large urban area in the Southeast US. Data were obtained from a perinatal administrative database (2011-2021). Latent indicators included maternal age, sociodemographic factors, foreign-born status, pregnancy intendedness, body mass index, mental and chronic health conditions, drug use, and sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Outcomes were gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, and superimposed preeclampsia. Associations between latent classes and outcomes were examined with structural equation modeling. Of the pregnant patients, 49.1% were < 25 years old, 37.4% were foreign-born, 62.6% were married, 54.4% were on public insurance, 55.3% had unplanned pregnancies, 11.2% had mental health conditions, 5.4% had chronic health conditions, and 8.7% reported drug use. Three latent profiles emerged: Multidomain vulnerability (28%) included those more likely to be < 25 years of age with co-occurring social disadvantage, unplanned pregnancies, STIs, and drug use; social vulnerability (32%) included predominantly foreign-born patients with social disadvantage; health-behavior vulnerability (39%) included those with planned pregnancies and social advantage, but more health and behavior indicators relative to social vulnerability. Multidomain vulnerability (OR 2.0, 95% CI 1.67-2.46) and social vulnerability (OR 2.51, 95% CI 2.09-3.01) had higher odds of preeclampsia compared to the health-behavior vulnerability profile. Our latent class analysis revealed unique clustering of social, behavior, and health risk factors associated with preeclampsia among nulliparous pregnancies.

title: Beyond Traditional Risk: Does Systemic Inflammation Drive Accelerated Atherosclerosis in Rheumatoid Arthritis?
authorString: Chowdhury D, Rao MM, Sahu R, Choubey PK, Namdeo KP, Bodakhe SH.

journal.title: The American journal of the medical sciences

abstractText: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the primary cause of morbidity and mortality in individuals with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and other rheumatic diseases (RDs), contributing to an approximate 50% increased cardiovascular risk relative to the general population. In addition to conventional cardiovascular risk factors, disease-specific processes such as chronic inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and immunological dysregulation substantially accelerate atherosclerosis. This thorough analysis brings together the most recent information on how to measure cardiovascular risk, how to understand the underlying causes of RA and other rheumatic diseases, and how to treat them all together. In RA, long-term inflammation throughout the body causes atherosclerosis through several different mechanisms that are not related to common risk factors. To lower the risk of heart disease, rheumatologists, cardiologists, dietitians, physiotherapists, and immunologists must all work together. Evidence supports the targeting of disease activity, the management of conventional cardiovascular risk factors such as hypertension, dyslipidemia, diabetes, and the use of non-pharmacological therapies.

title: Convergent Cardioprotection through Distinct Nitric Oxide and Carbon Monoxide Signaling Pathways after Myocardial Infarction.
authorString: Cebova M, Kosutova M, Barta A, Bujnova K, Pechanova O.
abstractText: Reduced nitric oxide (NO) bioavailability contributes to endothelial dysfunction and increases myocardial susceptibility to ischemic injury. In addition to NO, carbon monoxide (CO) functions as an important endogenous gasotransmitter that regulates vascular tone, mitochondrial respiration, and cellular defense mechanisms. Although NO- and CO-related interventions activate distinct proximal signaling pathways, it remains unclear whether they converge on a common anti-inflammatory and antioxidant mechanism under conditions of chronic NO deficiency. We therefore investigated cardioprotective signaling induced by the NO donor Nicorandil and the CO-releasing molecule CORM-3 in L-NAME-induced hypertensive rats subjected to myocardial infarction. Male Wistar Kyoto rats received L-NAME (20 mg/kg/day) for four weeks to induce chronic NO-deficient hypertension. Myocardial infarction was induced by left coronary artery occlusion followed by reperfusion. Before reperfusion, Nicorandil or CORM-3 was administered intramyocardially. Seven days later, blood pressure, infarct size, collagen deposition, inflammatory markers, NO synthase (NOS) activity, protein expression of eNOS, iNOS, NF-κB, Nrf2, HO-1, and antioxidant enzymes were assessed. Both Nicorandil and CORM-3 significantly reduced myocardial infarct size and attenuated fibrotic collagen deposition compared with untreated infarcted animals. Furthermore, both treatments reduced circulating TNF-α and IL-6, suppressed myocardial NF-κB activation, decreased iNOS expression, and restored antioxidant enzyme levels. However, the interventions exhibited distinct upstream molecular signatures.
