Nicorandil preferentially enhanced NO-related signaling, increased total NOS activity and eNOS expression, whereas CORM-3 produced stronger activation of the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway. Nicorandil and CORM-3 produce a common structural, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory cardioprotective phenotype associated with distinct molecular signaling profiles under conditions of chronic NO deficiency.

title: Budget Impact Analysis and Alternative Funding Solutions of Sacubitril/Valsartan for the Treatment of Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction in Thailand.
authorString: Luksameesate P, Kulthanachairojana N, Taychakhoonavudh S.
abstractText: This study evaluated the budget impact of sacubitril/valsartan for treating heart failure with reduced ejection fraction compared with enalapril and assessed alternative funding mechanisms under decision uncertainty. The study comprised 3 components. First, a decision tree and a Markov model were used to estimate the budget impact over a 5-year time horizon. The base-case adopted a payer perspective, including direct medical costs, whereas a scenario analysis incorporated direct non-medical and indirect costs. Second, a situation analysis identified key decision uncertainties. Third, an economic impact analysis evaluated alternative funding mechanisms relative to the current reimbursement system. In the base-case, the cumulative net budget impact was United States dollars (USD) 18.40 million. For the scenario analysis, the net economic impact decreased to USD 15.72 million, indicating a partial offset of the additional drug expenditure. The new treatment mix was estimated to avoid 300 heart failure hospitalizations and 146 cardiovascular deaths over 5 years. Key uncertainties included high budget requirements, limited epidemiological data, and variability in clinical outcomes. To address these, 2 funding mechanisms were explored: coverage with evidence development to reduce clinical uncertainty and a price-volume agreement with a capped budget to manage financial risk. Sacubitril/valsartan increased total expenditure compared with the current treatment; however, savings from reduced hospitalizations and broader societal costs partially offset the additional drug cost. Sacubitril/valsartan may be a manageable option when implemented with coverage with evidence development and price-volume agreements, supporting financial sustainability and long-term health outcomes.

title: Stroke knowledge and intended care-seeking behavior among adults with hypertension and type 2 diabetes: A cross-sectional study.
authorString: Alviz LF, Oyola JD, Martinez-Lemus JD, Perez-Lopez JA, Medina-Soler M, Rodriguez JE, Benavides J, Martinez C, Jimenez C.
abstractText: Stroke health literacy refers to the ability of non-medical individuals to recognize stroke symptoms and make timely decisions, which is critical for improving outcomes. However, data on stroke knowledge and intended care-seeking behavior in Bogotá, Colombia, remain limited. To assess stroke symptom knowledge and intended care-seeking behavior among adults with hypertension and type 2 diabetes and to identify sociodemographic predictors of limited knowledge and suboptimal response. A cross-sectional study was conducted between October 2023 and April 2024 in Bogotá, Colombia. A structured questionnaire was administered to 5,402 adults with hypertension and/or type 2 diabetes. Participants were recruited using a non-probabilistic sampling strategy, primarily from individuals under routine follow-up within the Bogotá public health network, and were identified through multiple recruitment strategies, including institutional databases. Surveys were conducted either by telephone or in person. Continuous variables were summarized using descriptive statistics, differences in categorical variables were assessed using chi-square tests, and binomial logistic regression models were applied to evaluate adjusted associations. Of 6,050 respondents, 5,402 met inclusion criteria (median age 67 years; 46.3% male). Although most participants recognized that ischemic stroke can cause disability (89.6%) and death (91.1%), 32.5% reported no knowledge of stroke symptoms. Limited symptom knowledge was independently associated with male sex (OR 1.26, 95% CI 1.12-1.42), low educational attainment (OR 1.59, 95% CI 1.38-1.82), and low socioeconomic status (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.85-2.60). Regarding intended response, 26.6% would not activate emergency medical services, and 52% reported they would schedule an outpatient appointment instead. Lower educational attainment was associated with greater likelihood of reporting non-emergency responses (all p < 0.001). Despite high awareness that stroke can cause disability and death, substantial gaps in symptom recognition and intended response persist, particularly among socioeconomically disadvantaged individuals. These findings highlight the need for targeted strategies to improve stroke literacy in high-risk populations.

title: Causes of stillbirth in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia: Findings from Child Health and Mortality Prevention Surveillance, 2016-2023.
authorString: Rahman A, Lee KH, Arifeen SE, Hossain MZ, Chowdhury AI, Alam M, Afrin A, Ogbuanu IU, Samura S, Kaluma E, Ojulong J, Sow S, Keita AM, Tapia MD, Chawla KK, Kotloff K, Madhi SA, Mahtab S, Adam Y, Wise A, Dangor Z, Mugah C, Oele E, Omore R, Igunza AK, Onyango D, Mandomando I, Bassat Q, Ajanovic S, Varo R, Xerinda E, Assefa N, Scott JAG, Madrid L, Yeshi MM, Temesgen F, Liu L, Mutevedzi P, Blau DM, Akelo V, Breiman RF, Whitney CG, Gurley ES, CHAMPS Consortium.
abstractText: Globally, an estimated 1.9 million stillbirths occur annually, yet significant knowledge gaps exist regarding the causes of stillbirths, particularly in high-burden regions. We investigated fetal and maternal conditions causing stillbirths in seven countries in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia and described missed opportunities for prevention. Child Health and Mortality Prevention Surveillance (CHAMPS) identified stillbirths at sites in Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Kenya, Mali, Mozambique, Sierra Leone, and South Africa. We asked families for consent to conduct minimally invasive tissue sampling (MITS) from December 2016 to December 2023. An expert panel reviewed test results, clinical information, and verbal autopsy data and assigned fetal and maternal conditions leading to stillbirths and identified missed opportunities for prevention. A cause of death (fetal or maternal condition) was determined for 94% (2342/2492) of stillbirths; the most frequent condition in the fetus was intrauterine hypoxia (75%, 1864/2492) across all sites, resulting from either maternal condition (49%, 922/1864) or placental causes (33%, 610/1864). Congenital infections were determined to be the cause of 9% (228/2492) of stillbirths, accounting for the highest proportion in South Africa (31%, 96/306). Group B Streptococcus, Escherichia coli, and Enterococcus faecalis were the most common causative pathogens. Congenital birth defects caused 9% (227/2492) overall and were most common in Ethiopia (24%, 136/568). Primary maternal conditions were identified in 72%, most often placental complications (18%, 446/2492) and maternal hypertension (17%, 414/2492). Complications of placenta, cord and membranes were more common in Mali (43%, 92/212) while maternal medical and surgical conditions were most frequently observed in South Africa (40%, 121/306) and Bangladesh (39%, 158/405). Most (72%, 1808/2492) causes of stillbirth were considered preventable, with heterogeneity observed across sites on the recommended prevention strategies. Complications of pregnancy or delivery accounted for most stillbirths across all sites, with intrauterine hypoxia identified as the predominant fetal condition highlighting widespread and persistent gaps in the timely identification and management of maternal and placental conditions during antenatal and obstetric care across sites in Africa and South Asia. At the same time, substantial geographic variation in causes and prevention opportunities, including for infections and birth defects, underscored the need for locally tailored strategies. Strengthening facility-based care alongside targeted interventions based on site-specific patterns, will be critical to reducing the stillbirth burden in these high-priority regions. The Gates Foundation.

title: Measurement error adjusted prevalence of undiagnosed hypertension in England: A cross-sectional study.
authorString: Castanon A, Hughes A, Grasic K, White M, Sheppard JP, McManus RJ, Pearson-Stuttard J, Stevens R.
abstractText: Hypertension case-finding and management is key to reducing premature morbidity and mortality. In England, 14.8% of people receive treatment for hypertension but the total number of hypertensive individuals remains unclear, as it can only be estimated statistically. This study aimed to estimate how many individuals aged 40 + may unknowingly have hypertension by accounting for differences between clinic and out-of-office blood pressure readings. We analysed individual-level data from the 2017-2019 Health Survey for England (HSE), including individuals aged ≥40 without a hypertension diagnosis. A validated algorithm (Predicting Out-of-Office Blood Pressure- PROOF-BP) was applied to estimate likely out-of-office measurements. Observed BP was defined as the mean of the second and third measurement taken at an HSE visit. Predicted hypertension was calculated using PROOF-BP and observed hypertension using actual clinic measurements. We explored a diagnostic threshold for predicted (out-of-office) hypertension of ≥135/85 mmHg (primary outcome) and of ≥140/90 mmHg (secondary outcome). Weighted hypertension prevalence estimates are presented by age, sex and geographical region. National population statistics were used to extrapolate results to the English population. The observed prevalence of undiagnosed hypertension in the study population was 27.7% (95% Confidence Interval [CI]:26.4%-29.1%). The predicted prevalence after adjustment was 21.8% (95%CI:20.6%-23.0%). Predicted prevalence was nearly double in males (29.8%, 95%CI:27.8%-32.0%) compared to females (14.6%, 95%CI:13.3%-15.9%) and varied by region: West Midlands (26.3%, 95%CI:22.2%-31.0%), London (16.9%, 95%CI:13.5%-20.9%). Extrapolating estimates to the total population aged ≥40 in England we estimate approximately 4.2 million people in England are unaware of their hypertension. Of these we estimate that over 2.9 million could be newly diagnosed by the current diagnostic pathway. Over 4 million people in England are estimated to have undiagnosed hypertension. This study's refined analytical approach provides a more precise estimate of this population, supporting targeted public health initiatives to identify and address undiagnosed cases.

title: Evaluating the cost-effectiveness of enhanced cardiovascular-renal-metabolic (CVRM) screening in UK, France, Germany and Australia: a microsimulation-based enhanced CVRM screening analysis.
authorString: Adshead F, Xydopoulos G, Vasilopoulos V, Babin A, Banerjee A, Detournay B, Espín J, Hassan I, Kearney M, Kielstein JT, Kuwahara K, Lederer N, le Roux CW, Raffoul N, Retat L, Robinson SB, Sindone A, Wasem J, Froguel CE.
abstractText: Cardiovascular-renal-metabolic (CVRM) conditions, including hypertension, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, dyslipidemia, obesity, and heart failure, are major drivers of morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs in the United Kingdom, France, Germany, and Australia. This study evaluated the 20-year clinical, economic, societal, and environmental impact of implementing a comprehensive CVRM screening strategy versus current standard of care (SoC) in these four countries. A discrete-time patient-level microsimulation model projected 20-year health trajectories calibrated to country-specific demographic and epidemiologic profiles. The enhanced screening strategy included broader eligibility, more frequent screening, and assessment of key CVRM indicators relative to SoC. Disease progression across six CVRM conditions was modeled using validated country-specific risk equations capturing multimorbidity and dynamic risk interactions. Analyses were conducted from payer, societal, and environmental perspectives using country-specific costs, wages, and CO2-equivalent emissions factors. Deterministic sensitivity analyses varied key parameters by ±20%. Enhanced CVRM screening produced consistent benefits across all countries that increased over time. Over 20 years, in populations aged ≥35 years, mortality reductions ranged from 109,863 in Australia to 467,297 in Germany, and corresponding life-years gained ranged from 640,870 to 2,803,783. Most survival gains accrued after the first decade. Under the modeled assumptions, the strategy was projected to be cost saving in all countries, with total savings ranging from $368.9 million in Australia to $46.5 billion in Germany, and dominant across payer and societal perspectives. Additional benefits included fewer hospital bed-days, lower productivity losses, and reduced CO2 emissions. Results depended on structural and epidemiologic assumptions, including screening uptake, disease progression, and risk equation recalibration. Uncertainty was assessed using deterministic rather than probabilistic sensitivity analysis. Comprehensive CVRM screening, when embedded in preventive care pathways and linked to appropriate follow-up, may improve population health while generating substantial economic, societal, and environmental benefits.

title: Don't Wait- Ablate! Catheter Ablation in Patients with Advanced Heart Failure and Atrial Fibrillation.
authorString: Moersdorf M, Sommer P, Sohns C.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

Heart failure (HF) and atrial fibrillation (AF) frequently coexist and mutually accelerate disease progression through complex hemodynamic, neurohormonal, and structural interactions. Although earlier rhythm-control strategies failed to demonstrate mortality benefit, largely due to limitations of antiarrhythmic drug therapy, catheter ablation has fundamentally altered the therapeutic landscape.

Recent findings

The CASTLE-AF trial established catheter ablation as a disease-modifying therapy in patients with AF and HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), demonstrating reductions in mortality and HF hospitalization. More recently, the CASTLE-HTx trial extended these findings to patients with end-stage HF eligible for heart transplantation (HTx) or left ventricular assist device (LVAD) therapy. Catheter ablation has demonstrated a marked reduction in mortality and the need of an urgent HTx, or LVAD implantation compared with medical therapy alone. Subsequent subanalyses further refined risk stratification and identified patient subsets deriving the greatest benefit. Therefore, catheter ablation has received a class 1 recommendation for patients with AF and HFrEF. According to recent clinical evidence supporting early rhythm control through catheter ablation in advanced HF, it leads to a paradigm shift in the management of this high-risk population: in selected patients with AF and advanced HF, clinicians should not delay referral-"Don't wait, ablate."

title: Clinical Effects of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors on Children with Single Ventricle Congenital Heart Disease: A Single-Center Experience.
authorString: Canova AO, Newland DM, Albers EL, Bouska ES, Hartje-Dunn CL, Iqbal MS, Kemna MS, Law YM, Kerr SM, Wisotzkey BL, Hong BJ.
abstractText: This study evaluates the impact of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) on pediatric patients with single ventricle (SV) heart disease, using invasive and non-invasive markers of cardiac function. We reviewed patients (< 21 years) with SV physiology who received ≥ 90 days SGLT2i at our center from 2020 to 2025. Baseline laboratory, echocardiographic, and hemodynamic data were recorded and compared to follow up data after ≥ 90 days on SGLT2i. Hospitalizations before and after SGLT2i were also analyzed. Seventy-seven patients with median age 10.5 years (range 47 days-19.9 years) had median treatment duration of 386 days (IQR 218-853). Among 62 patients (81%) with echocardiographic data (Fontan [39], Glenn [18], Stage 1 [5]) there was a significant decrease in median qualitative AVVR score from mild-moderate to mild (p = 0.01). Median BNP decreased from 84 pg/mL (IQR 18-274) to 42 pg/mL (IQR 18-105) (p = 0.02) and mean hemoglobin increased from 14.4 ± 2.5 g/dL to 15.5 ± 2.4 g/dL (p < 0.01). Ten patients had hemodynamic data without significant change in mean pulmonary artery pressure from 17 to 16 mmHg (p = 0.168) or ventricular end-diastolic pressure from 10 to 11 mmHg (p = 0.275). More patients had > 1 hospitalizations for heart failure during the 6-months prior to SGLT2i compared to the 6-months following initiation, with an odds ratio of 4.5 (95% CI: 1.6-13.7, p < 0.01). Overall, we identified significant reductions in AVVR, BNP, and hospitalizations for heart failure after ≥ 90 days of therapy. Further larger scale studies are needed to determine if SGLT2i will affect clinical outcomes in the pediatric SV population.

title: Primary, atrial secondary, and ventricular secondary mitral regurgitation in the general population.
authorString: Keil L, Hapfelmeier A, Wenzel JP, Nikorowitsch J, Kalbacher D, Reichenspurner H, Blankenberg S, Girdauskas E.

journal.title: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society

abstractText: While primary mitral valve regurgitation (PMR) results from structural abnormalities of the mitral valve leaflets, secondary mitral valve regurgitation (SMR) arises from either mitral annular dilatation (atrial type, aSMR) or left ventricle remodelling (ventricular type, vSMR) in the absence of intrinsic leaflet disease. Although SMR is considered the most common cause of clinically relevant mitral regurgitation (MR), population-based data on its prevalence, subtype distribution, and clinical profiles are lacking. We aimed to determine the prevalence of PMR and SMR and to characterize PMR, aSMR, and vSMR in the general population. We analyzed the first 10,000 participants of the population-based Hamburg City Health Study enrolled 2016-2019; 8543 echocardiographic examinations were available. Mitral valve morphology and function were independently assessed by two investigators. PMR was defined by the presence of intrinsic leaflet pathology, whereas SMR was classified as ventricular when left ventricular ejection fraction was less than 50% or less than 55% in the presence of geometric distortion (tenting area ≥ 150 mm2 or coaptation depth ≥ 10 mm) and cases with left ventricular ejection fraction equal to or above 50% were classified as aSMR. A total of 216 participants had moderate or severe MR (2.53% of the total cohort, 95% confidence interval (CI): 2.20%-2.89%, see Fig. 3). Of these, 148 were classified as SMR (68.5%, 95% CI: 61.8%-74.7%), the remaining were mainly of primary etiology (31.5%, 95% CI: 25.3%-38.2%). Among SMR cases, aSMR was predominant (84.5%, 95% CI: 77.5%-89.9%), whereas vSMR accounted for 15.5% (95% CI: 10.1%-22.4%). Compared with aSMR, individuals with vSMR were older, more symptomatic, and more frequently had atrial fibrillation and hypertension. Echocardiographic parameters indicated more advanced cardiac remodelling and dysfunction in vSMR. Compared with SMR, participants with PMR had greater MR severity, while age and the proportion of women were numerically higher without reaching statistical significance. During a median follow-up of 4.56 years, 10 participants had died, with all-cause mortality being significantly higher among participants with PMR than among those with aSMR. In this population-based cohort, SMR accounted for two-thirds of relevant MR, with aSMR being the predominant subtype. MR severity was higher in PMR as compared to SMR. Distinct echocardiographic and clinical profiles suggest more advanced disease in vSMR. Multivariate analysis revealed that atrial fibrillation was significantly more present in the vSMR cohort. These findings highlight the need for refined SMR subclassification and longitudinal studies to define prognostic implications and clinically meaningful definitions. All-cause mortality was highest in participants with PMR than in those with aSMR.

title: A clinical-radiological model for predicting in-hospital mortality in acute exacerbation of COPD.
authorString: Li Y, Wang X, Zhang M, Wang Y, Wang G, Hu Y, Wei Y, Guo Y.
abstractText: Quantitative computed tomography (QCT) has emerged as a promising tool for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) phenotyping. However, its prognostic value in acute exacerbations of COPD (AECOPD) remains insufficiently explored, and existing risk stratification models have limited integration of imaging-derived metrics. This study aimed to develop and validate a prognostic model that integrates multidimensional clinical variables with QCT-derived metrics, and to compare its predictive performance with traditional clinical scores for in-hospital mortality in AECOPD. In this retrospective cohort study, consecutive patients aged ≥40 years hospitalized with severe AECOPD were enrolled from September 2010 to October 2024, with collection of demographic characteristics, clinical features, laboratory indices, and chest CT imaging data. The cohort was randomly split into training and testing sets (7:3). Candidate predictors were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression followed by multivariable logistic regression. Four classification models were developed and evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation. Discriminative performance was assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and compared with conventional clinical scores. A total of 465 patients with AECOPD were included, of whom 47 (10.1%) died during hospitalization. Five independent predictors were identified: confusion, lymphocyte count <0.8 × 109/L, chronic heart failure, white blood cell count ≥10 × 109/L, and reduced pulmonary vascular fractal dimension. The logistic regression model demonstrated the best performance, achieving an AUC of 0.852 (95% CI, 0.738-0.965) in the testing set, significantly outperforming other models and established clinical scores. A predictive model integrating QCT-derived metrics with clinical features improved AECOPD in-hospital mortality prediction over traditional scores, supporting its utility for individualized risk stratification and management.

title: Contrast-Induced Encephalopathy Mimicking Stroke During Vein of Marshall Ethanol Infusion.
authorString: Nie C, Liu X, Zhu S.
abstractText: Contrast-induced encephalopathy (CIE) is a rare, reversible neurologic complication of iodinated contrast exposure that may mimic acute stroke. A 68-year-old man undergoing atrial fibrillation ablation with vein of Marshall ethanol infusion received 40 mL of ioversol. Approximately 4 hours after the procedure, he developed agitation, myoclonic movements, urinary incontinence, and left-sided weakness. Brain computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, magnetic resonance angiography, and diffusion-weighted imaging showed no hemorrhage, acute infarction, or major vascular abnormality. Similar neurologic symptoms recurred approximately 10 hours after the procedure. After neurologic consultation, CIE was considered the most likely diagnosis. Supportive treatment was provided, with complete neurologic recovery within 48 hours. CIE should be considered when acute neurologic manifestations occur after contrast exposure, particularly when initial evaluation does not demonstrate an acute cerebrovascular cause. Recognition of CIE as a stroke mimic may facilitate appropriate evaluation and management while avoiding unnecessary intervention.

title: Apparent Recurrence Differences between Paroxysmal and Persistent Atrial Fibrillation after Catheter Ablation Are Attributable to Blanking-Period Events: A Propensity-Matched Cohort Study
authorString: Li¹ X, Xu² L, Yao¹ N, Liu¹ J, Sun¹ Y, Yin¹ L.
abstractText: Background Whether atrial fibrillation (AF) type independently determines long-term prognosis after catheter ablation remains debated. We compared outcomes between paroxysmal and persistent AF after ablation using propensity score matching (PSM) with inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). Methods This single-center retrospective cohort included 365 patients (239 paroxysmal, 126 persistent) undergoing first-time ablation (2016–2025). Outcomes were all-cause hospitalization, AF recurrence, a composite stroke/bleeding outcome, and heart failure (HF). PSM (1:1, exact on HF history, caliper 0.1) yielded 65 matched pairs; analyses comprised pair-clustered Cox models, restricted mean survival time, IPTW, multivariable adjustment, FDR-corrected subgroups, and LASSO-Cox. Follow-up was protocol-limited to 5 years; no deaths occurred. Results Recurrences within the 3-month blanking period were excluded: 21 of 50 (42%), disproportionately frequent in persistent AF (13/22, 59% vs 8/28, 29%). No outcome differed between groups after matching (hospitalization HR 0.948, 95% CI 0.504–1.784; recurrence 0.411, 0.079–2.140; stroke/bleeding 2.162, 0.186–25.109; HF 0.676, 0.109–4.173). Including blanking-period events produced an apparent two-fold higher recurrence risk in persistent AF (crude HR 1.758, P = 0.049; IPTW HR 2.054–2.223, P < 0.05) that disappeared after exclusion (crude HR 1.020, P = 0.961; IPTW HR 1.147–1.215, P > 0.6). Subgroup findings were exploratory and did not survive FDR correction. Conclusions After applying the consensus blanking-period definition, paroxysmal and persistent AF showed no differences in hospitalization, recurrence, stroke/bleeding, or HF across all analytic approaches; apparent recurrence differences were entirely attributable to blanking-period events, disproportionately frequent in persistent AF. Findings are limited by small event counts and month-level follow-up precision.

title: Prosthesis-patient mismatch after surgical aortic valve replacement with aortic annular enlargement in small aortic annuli.
authorString: Jacquemyn X, Imran M, Serna-Gallegos D, Hasan I, Ogami T, Bonnati J, Kaczorowski DJ, Chu D, West D, Sultan I.
abstractText:
Objectives

Aortic annular enlargement (AAE) during surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) is performed to facilitate implantation of larger prostheses in patients with small aortic annuli and mitigate prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM). However, the clinical impact of residual PPM after AAE remains uncertain.

Methods

All adult patients who underwent SAVR with AAE for small aortic annuli were retrospectively identified from a prospectively maintained institutional database (2011-2024). PPM was defined based on indexed effective orifice area thresholds derived from published reference tables. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality, and secondary outcomes included heart failure (HF) hospitalization, and longitudinal echocardiographic performance.

Results

A total of 169 patients were identified (age 68 years [61-73], 119 female [70.4%]). Median STS risk was 2% [1-4%], and preoperative mean gradient was 45.0 mmHg [36.8-57.2]. Overall median valve size after AAE was 23 mm (21-25), and PPM occurred in 25 patients (14.8%), including 24 (14.2%) with moderate and 1 (0.6%) with severe PPM. Early outcomes were comparable between PPM and no-PPM groups: postoperative stroke 0 (0%) vs. 3 (2.1%, p > 0.999), and 30-day mortality 1 (4.0%) vs. 5 (3.5%, p > 0.999). Over 4 years follow-up, survival (HR 0.94, 95%CI 0.40-2.21, p = 0.896) and freedom from HF hospitalization (HR 1.16, 95%CI 0.45-2.95, p = 0.760) were similar. Echocardiographic trends showed no differences in LVEF (p = 0.123) or mean gradient (p = 0.879) during follow-up.

Conclusions

In patients with small aortic annuli undergoing SAVR with annular enlargement, the incidence of PPM was low, and residual PPM did not adversely impact early postoperative outcomes, mid-term survival, or valve hemodynamics.

title: Conventional Atrioventricular Nodal Reentrant Tachycardia Ablation: 16-Year Acute Outcomes and Pacemaker Requirement.
authorString: Serbest NG, Karakurt H, Eren A, Uysal H, Başarıcı MT, Sadıkoğlu K, Öner E, Sürgit Ö.
abstractText:
Background

This study characterized the acute success, causes of failure, and index-hospitalization permanent pacemaker (PPM) rate of conventional (fluoroscopy-guided, without 3D electroanatomic mapping [3D-EAM]) AVNRT ablation over 16 years at a single center.

Methods

Consecutive adult patients (≥18 years) who underwent conventional ablation for AVNRT between January 2010 and May 2026 were retrospectively evaluated. All procedures were performed by a senior operator or under the direct supervision of a senior operator. Acute success was defined as non-inducibility of AVNRT under isoproterenol. The primary endpoints were index-hospitalization PPM and acute success. Rates are presented with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

Results

Of 1169 SVT cases, 814 (69.6%) underwent AVNRT ablation (age 46.9 ± 13.0 years; 67.0% female). Acute success was 90.3% (735/814; 95% CI 88.07-92.14). Causes of failure (n = 79): anatomic limitation 40 (50.6%), persistent inducibility 29 (36.7%), AV conduction disturbance 8 (10.1%), patient intolerance 1, atrial fibrillation 1. Anatomic limitation denotes ablation deliberately terminated to protect AV conduction rather than technical failure. High-grade AV block developed in 8 patients (0.98%); it resolved spontaneously in 5, and a PPM was implanted during the index hospitalization in 3 (0.37%; 95% CI 0.13-1.08). In the three PPM patients, ventricular pacing remained 100% at follow-up. Acute success showed no significant univariable association with age or sex.

Conclusions

Conventional AVNRT ablation can be performed at an experienced center with high success (90.3%) and a low PPM rate (0.37%). While some AV block events resolved in the laboratory, those that persisted led to a PPM requirement, and AV conduction was not regained in these patients. These findings provide operator-homogeneous real-world reference data from a tertiary referral center in Türkiye.

title: Best clinical practice in kidney transplant and cancer clinics.
authorString: Owoyemi I, Sprangers B, Bregman A, Ramos E, Webber A, Murakami N, Michalski-McNeely B, Gordon E, Blosser CD.

journal.title: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension

abstractText:
Purpose of review

Transplant onconephrology is an evolving subspeciality within nephrology that focuses on the interaction between cancer and the kidney. The goal of this subspecialty is to provide optimal care for people with cancers who are risk or develop cancer-related kidney complications or nephrotoxicity from cancer therapeutics. This goal is accomplished through application of increasing knowledge about transplant nephrology and oncology.

Recent findings

People with a history of malignancy who are evaluated for kidney transplant need careful risk assessment to inform candidacy, immunosuppression management and prevent post-transplant recurrence. Post-transplant malignancies occur frequently and are a leading cause of death in kidney transplant recipients. People with pre- and post-transplant cancers experience significant stressors and healthcare demands, and benefit from multidisciplinary clinical care to address their high-risk conditions.

Summary

This review provides a comprehensive overview of the best practices of outpatient clinical care for the growing population of high-risk patients with cancer before and after kidney transplant based on clinical experience and available data.

title: Barriers and Opportunities in Therapeutic Development for Early-Onset Preeclampsia.
authorString: Massaro A, Karumanchi A, Chang C, de Vries CS, Stepan H, Granger J, Hyett J, Adu-Bonsaffoh K, Vatish M, Soma-Pillay P, Langham Am R, Kumar S, Rana S, Rulisa S, Bhat S.
abstractText: Early-onset preeclampsia (EOPE) remains a major contributor to maternal and fetal/neonatal morbidity and mortality worldwide, with delivery, frequently at early preterm gestations, remaining the only effective way to halt disease progression. Therapeutic development has been limited by disease heterogeneity, unpredictable conditions, a progressive course, ethical and safety concerns in pregnancy, and uncertainty over trial design and regulatory pathways. This document summarizes an international multidisciplinary convening of clinicians, trialists, pharmacologists, regulators, and global health experts who met to explore key challenges and emerging strategies for therapeutic development in EOPE. Discussion centered on EOPE, marked by abnormal placentation, pronounced angiogenic imbalance, and high maternal-fetal risk, viewed as a potentially tractable target for disease-modifying interventions. Key themes included trial eligibility and enrollment, use of angiogenic biomarkers for enrichment and monitoring, defining meaningful maternal and fetal end points, safety oversight in the dual-patient context, and the potential of adaptive trial designs. Participants also considered translational tools such as pharmacokinetic (physiologically based pharmacokinetic) modeling and placental transfer studies. Participants identified both areas of alignment and continued uncertainty. Biologically informed strategies, such as biomarker-supported enrollment and carefully designed early-phase studies were seen as helpful in reducing uncertainty, especially alongside early regulatory engagement. Although many developers are pursuing soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 as a therapeutic target for EOPE, participants stressed the need for further biomarker validation, careful maternal-fetal risk-benefit assessment, and globally feasible approaches. Though focused on EOPE, these discussions may inform future research on late-onset disease, given its distinct underlying biology.

title: Genotype, Phenotypic Severity, and Survival in Pediatric Dilated Cardiomyopathy: A Report From the Pediatric Cardiomyopathy Registry.
authorString: Kantor PF, Ware SM, Chung WK, Martin LJ, Hamza T, Shi L, Colan SD, Rossano JW, Towbin JA, Lee TM, Lal AK, Webber S, Canter CE, Hsu DT, Everitt MD, Pahl E, Bansal N, Ballweg JA, Feingold B, Lytrivi ID, Ryan TD, Bhatnagar S, Aronow BJ, Dexheimer PJ, Schubert JA, Lipshultz SE.
abstractText:
Background

Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) frequently presents with heart failure in children. Whether a genetic cause of DCM is associated with disease severity or eventual outcome in pediatric DCM is unclear.

Methods

A multiinstitutional prospective pediatric cohort study (0-18 years) with nonsyndromic DCM was undertaken from 2013 to 2016. A panel of 37 cardiomyopathy-associated genes was interrogated by exome sequencing with analysis for pathogenic or likely pathogenic (LP) variants. Clinical severity and outcomes of death, cardiac transplant, and continuing left ventricular dysfunction versus echocardiographic normalization were assessed.

Results

A total of 279 DCM probands (47% male) with a median (interquartile range) age at diagnosis of 1.6 (0.4-10.4) years were enrolled. Median follow-up was 1.1 (0.2-4.0) years. Gene variants designated as pathogenic/LP were identified in 18 of the 37 genes evaluated, and of all positive variants, TTN (17%), TNNT2 (15%), MYH7 (15%), RBM20 (9%), and LMNA (8%) were most frequently implicated. Only 19% of the overall cohort yielded an identifiable genetic cause, without any difference between ancestries. Children >12 years old had the highest genetic yield at 34% (P<0.05). Symptoms of heart failure occurred in 62% of patients who carried a pathogenic/LP gene variant, at or within 12 months of presentation, but neither heart failure symptoms, nor echocardiographic severity was associated with having a pathogenic/LP variant. The rate of death or cardiac transplant did not differ with the presence or absence of a pathogenic/LP variant and exceeded 60% by 10 years after diagnosis. On competing risks analysis, a trend (P=0.09) toward greater echo normalization, was noted in those without a pathogenic/LP variant by 10 years after diagnosis.

Conclusions

A genetic cause was detected in a minority of children and was not associated with the phenotypic severity of DCM at diagnosis. Echocardiographic normalization of left ventricular function over time was noted more frequently in patients who did not have an identified pathogenic/LP variant.

title: Long-term patency outcomes after first autogenous arteriovenous fistula creation in patients aged 80 years or older: a competing-risk analysis.
authorString: Doita T, Nakamura T, Yamakura T, Yamasumi T, Miyake K, Miyagawa S.
abstractText:
Objective

Whether chronological age predicts arteriovenous fistula (AVF) durability remains uncertain. We compared primary patency between patients aged ≥80 and <80 years using competing-risk analysis and examined relevant vascular characteristics.

Methods

This single-center retrospective cohort included 416 consecutive patients undergoing first autogenous AVF creation during 2017-2020, with follow-up through March 2025. Intraoperative vessel diameters, macroscopic arterial atherosclerosis and preoperative ankle-brachial and toe-brachial indices were prospectively recorded. Death before primary patency loss was treated as a competing event. Cumulative incidence was estimated using Aalen-Johansen and compared using Gray's test. Associations were assessed using Fine-Gray and cause-specific Cox regression, with age modeled continuously in a sensitivity analysis.

Results

Among 416 patients, 109 (26.2%) were aged ≥80 years. Median follow-up was 48 months. Older patients had more macroscopic arterial atherosclerosis (67.0% vs 47.9%; P<.001), lower ankle-brachial (1.09 vs 1.16; P<.001) and toe-brachial indices (0.69 vs 0.76; P=.002), and more venous diameters <2.5 mm (22.0% vs 13.4%; P=.030). The cumulative incidence of primary patency loss did not differ between groups (Gray P = .710), with 36-month estimates of 43.2% and 38.0%. Age ≥80 years was not independently associated with primary patency loss (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR], 1.12; 95% CI, 0.74-1.70), whereas each 10-year increase was associated with higher risk in a sensitivity analysis (sHR, 1.20; 95% CI, 1.04-1.39). Proximal anastomosis was associated with lower risk (sHR, 0.57; 95% CI, 0.37-0.88), and venous diameter <2.5 mm with higher risk (sHR, 1.70; 95% CI, 1.05-2.75). Assisted primary and secondary patency did not differ. Fewer than 10% of fistulas were permanently abandoned by 60 months in either group, and 60-month survival among older patients was 82.0%.

Conclusions

Among patients selected for autogenous AVF creation, age ≥80 years was not independently associated with primary patency loss, whereas a continuous-age sensitivity analysis suggested a modest increase in risk per decade. These findings suggest that an age threshold alone should not determine AVF candidacy in otherwise suitable patients, although interpretation is tempered by loss to follow-up.

title: Prevalence of vascular dementia in a population-based autopsy study in Brazil.
authorString: Ururahy RDR, Leite REP, Matos C, Padrão I, Paes V, Grinberg L, Pasqualucci CA, Ferriolli E, Suemoto CK.
abstractText:
Introduction

Vascular dementia (VaD) is the second leading cause of dementia. However, estimates of VaD prevalence remain uncertain due to lesion heterogeneity, variable clinical presentations, convenience sampling, and limited clinicopathological data, particularly from diverse populations. We aimed to estimate the prevalence of VaD and describe the frequency of cerebrovascular lesions in a population-based autopsy study in Brazil.

Methods

In this autopsy study (2004-2025), inclusion criteria were age at death ≥18 years, presence of a knowledgeable informant, and either a neuropathological diagnosis of VaD or absence of any neuropathological diagnosis. Clinical data were obtained through informant interviews and complemented by a full-body autopsy with detailed neuropathological assessment. Intracranial atherosclerosis was evaluated across Circle of Willis arteries, while hyaline arteriolosclerosis, infarcts, and microbleeds were assessed in 13 brain regions. VaD diagnosis followed the Newcastle categorization, with additional analyses based on modified versions of the Macroscopic Vascular Lesion Score and the Vascular Staging System.

Results

The sample comprised 1,718 participants (mean age=69.1±14.2 years; 45% women; 59% White). VaD prevalence was 14% according to the Newcastle categorization, but varied substantially across diagnostic criteria. Among individuals with pure VaD or mixed dementia with a vascular component, 69% exhibited cognitive impairment. One-third of participants with VaD had mixed dementia. Hyaline arteriolosclerosis and lacunar infarcts were more frequent than intracranial atherosclerosis and macroscopic infarcts.

Conclusion

VaD prevalence was 14%, but varied substantially according to the neuropathological criteria applied. Mixed dementia was frequent, highlighting the co-occurrence of vascular and neurodegenerative pathologies in this diverse Brazilian sample.

title: Baseline neutrophil-to-HDL cholesterol ratio is associated with subsequent cerebrovascular accident in patients with microscopic polyangiitis or granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
authorString: Chung J, Lee LE, Ha JW, Kwon OC, Park YB, Lee SW.
abstractText:
Objective

A new index, the neutrophil-to-high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol ratio (NHR), has been reported to predict atherosclerosis and acute coronary syndrome (ACS). This study aimed to investigate the clinical utility of baseline NHR in predicting subsequent complications in patients with microscopic polyangiitis or granulomatosis with polyangiitis (MPA/GPA).

Methods

Clinical data of 150 patients with MPA/GPA were analysed retrospectively. Baseline demographic data, the Birmingham vasculitis activity score (BVAS), the five-factor score (FFS), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels were recorded. All-cause mortality, relapse, end-stage kidney disease, cerebrovascular accident (CVA), and ACS were evaluated as subsequent complications. NHR was calculated using the following formula: neutrophil count (× 1000/mm3) / HDL-cholesterol levels (mg/dL). NHR was analysed both as a continuous variable and using exploratory categorical cut-offs. Death before CVA was treated as a competing event in the cumulative incidence analysis.

Results

The median age was 63.5 years (64.0% female). Baseline NHR was significantly correlated with baseline BVAS, ESR, and CRP levels. Of the five subsequent complications, only subsequent CVA demonstrated a significant area under the curve in a receiver operating characteristic curve analysis of baseline NHR. Continuous NHR was not significantly associated with subsequent CVA after adjustment for age and CRP. In complementary exploratory analyses using the cohort-derived cut-off, patients with baseline NHR ≥ 0.17 had a higher frequency of subsequent CVA and a lower CVA-free survival rate than those with baseline NHR < 0.17. The former group also had a higher cumulative incidence of CVA when death before CVA was treated as a competing event. NHR ≥ 0.17 remained significantly associated with subsequent CVA after adjustment for age and CRP.

Conclusion

This study demonstrated the clinical utility of baseline NHR in predicting subsequent CVA in patients with MPA/GPA. Key Points • Baseline neutrophil-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio was significantly correlated with baseline Birmingham vasculitis activity score, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and C-reactive protein levels in patients with microscopic polyangiitis or granulomatosis with polyangiitis. • Patients with baseline neutrophil-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio ≥0.17 had a significantly higher risk of subsequent cerebrovascular accident and a lower cerebrovascular accident-free survival rate than those with baseline neutrophil-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio <0.17. • Baseline neutrophil-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio ≥0.17 remained independently associated with subsequent cerebrovascular accident after adjustment for age and C-reactive protein.

title: Desmoplakin Cardiomyopathy Mimicking Chronic Myocarditis in a Patient With Malignant Ventricular Tachycardia: The Value of Multimodality Diagnosis and Integrated Management
authorString: Huo Z, Wei C, Cai Z, Zhao C, Jin C, Zhang J, Lin X.
abstractText: Background Desmoplakin (DSP) cardiomyopathy is an inherited arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy characterized by myocardial fibrosis, inflammatory-like myocardial injury, and a left ventricular-predominant phenotype. Ventricular arrhythmias may occur despite only mildly reduced left ventricular systolic function, and the disease can mimic chronic myocarditis. Case presentation A 37-year-old woman presented with recurrent sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia and a family history of sudden death. Echocardiography and cardiac magnetic resonance showed mildly reduced left ventricular systolic function (43–44%) and a nonischemic late gadolinium enhancement pattern predominantly involving the subepicardial and mid-myocardial layers of the basal anterior and lateral left ventricular walls. Epicardial mapping demonstrated an extensive posterolateral left ventricular substrate with low-voltage scar, late potentials, and delayed conduction. Epicardial radiofrequency substrate modification was performed, followed by endomyocardial biopsy and extravascular implantable cardioverter-defibrillator implantation. Histopathology initially favored chronic myocarditis. Genetic testing subsequently identified a pathogenic heterozygous truncating variant in DSP (c.4198C > T, p.Arg1400Ter), supporting the diagnosis of DSP cardiomyopathy. At 1-month follow-up, no ventricular tachycardia or device therapy was recorded, and LVEF improved to 50%. Conclusions DSP cardiomyopathy should be considered in patients with malignant ventricular arrhythmias disproportionate to the degree of left ventricular dysfunction, particularly when cardiac magnetic resonance shows a nonischemic left ventricular fibrosis pattern and there is a family history of sudden death. Integrating electrophysiological, imaging, pathological, and genetic findings may help distinguish DSP cardiomyopathy from chronic myocarditis and guide arrhythmic management.

title: Urgent, Emergency, and Salvage Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation for Acute Decompensated Severe Aortic Stenosis: A Prospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Zhao M, Wang J, Gao L, Wu T, Wang Z, Luo S, Li Y, Liu R, Tang Z, Feng M, Hua M, Yuan J, Zhang Y, Bian Y, Chen Y, Li C.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care
journal.title: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care

abstractText:
Background

Acute decompensated severe aortic stenosis may preclude waiting for elective treatment, and evidence for non-elective transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is limited. We assessed 12-month mortality, 30-day safety, and recovery after urgent, emergency, or salvage TAVI.

Methods

We prospectively enrolled patients undergoing urgent, emergency, or salvage TAVI at one centre in 2022-2025. The primary endpoint was 12-month all-cause mortality; secondary endpoints included device success, 30-day safety, and functional and echocardiographic recovery.

Results

Among 53 patients, 36 underwent urgent, 14 emergency, and 3 salvage TAVI. Device success was 52/53 (98.1%). Thirty-day mortality was 1/36, 0/14, and 0/3; 12-month mortality was 2/36, 1/14, and 0/3 (3/53). Kaplan-Meier 12-month survival was 94.3% (95% confidence interval 83.5-98.1%). New atrioventricular block was detected in 2/53 on postoperative day 2; by 30 days, haemofiltration or renal replacement therapy occurred in 1/53 and permanent pacemaker implantation in 0/53. At 12 months, cardiovascular mortality was 2/53, heart-failure readmission 4/53, stroke 1/53, a separate Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 type 2 bleeding event 1/53, and permanent pacemaker implantation 0/53. Paired analyses showed improved New York Heart Association class, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-12, left ventricular ejection fraction, and transvalvular gradients at 30 days and 12 months (all P<0.001).

Conclusions

Selected patients had high device success and low early event rates after non-elective TAVI; paired data showed sustained functional and haemodynamic improvement. These findings support timely Heart Team assessment and consideration of non-elective TAVI, when appropriate, at experienced centres; comparative benefit over alternative strategies warrants prospective study.

title: Minimally Invasive Management of Cardiac Tamponade Complicating Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: A Technical Note.
authorString: Costache VS, Costache A, Oprea SA, Marinescu AD.

journal.title: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists

abstractText:
Purpose

Cardiac tamponade is an uncommon but potentially catastrophic complication of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), particularly when caused by iatrogenic hemopericardium, with high mortality among patients requiring emergency cardiac surgery. We describe a structured minimally invasive subxiphoid protocol modification for immediate intraprocedural tamponade management and place this experience in the context of current evidence.

Materials and methods

Between January 2023 and April 2026, cardiac tamponade developed intra- or peri-procedurally in 4 consecutive patients among approximately 350 TAVI procedures at a single tertiary center. The protocol comprised immediate subxiphoid decompression; insertion of two 16 Fr radiopaque Redon drains, placed anteriorly and posteriorly, each connected to a separate Drainobag bottle sustaining high negative pressure; hermetic layered closure; mechanical ventilation under sedation after decompression for at least 12 hours and progressive drain removal after 72 hours.

Results

All 4 patients achieved immediate hemodynamic recovery without conversion to emergency sternotomy. No hospital deaths or procedure-related complications occurred. No late pericardial reaccumulation, constrictive pericarditis or ventricular pseudoaneurysm occurred.

Conclusion

In this small single-center series, dual-drain subxiphoid drainage with continuous high-vacuum aspiration was feasible and associated with hemodynamic recovery without emergency sternotomy in 4 selected TAVI patients. Larger comparative studies are required before broader use can be recommended. These observations should be considered hypothesis-generating.Clinical ImpactCardiac tamponade during TAVI requires rapid, mechanism-directed treatment. Image-guided pericardiocentesis remains the usual first drainage step, whereas ongoing iatrogenic hemopericardium or failure to stabilize requires immediate surgical escalation. In 4 carefully selected patients, dual-drain subxiphoid decompression with continuous high-vacuum aspiration restored hemodynamic stability without emergency sternotomy. These findings support its feasibility as a rescue option in carefully selected cases, while larger comparative studies are needed to define its hemostatic effectiveness and its role relative to conventional drainage. Persistent bleeding or recurrent hemodynamic instability should prompt surgical conversion.

title: Outcomes of single-branched TEVAR with cervical debranching for zone 0 and zone 1 aortic arch repair: A VQI analysis.
authorString: Baghbani A, Saqib NU, Tanaka A, Martin GH, Estrera AL, Wang SK.
abstractText:
Objective

Single-branched thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) combined with cervical debranching has emerged as a less invasive alternative to open aortic arch reconstruction for patients requiring zone 0 or zone 1 proximal seal. Contemporary multicenter outcomes of this hybrid approach remain poorly defined. We evaluated procedural characteristics and perioperative outcomes of zone 0 and zone 1 single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching using the Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI).

Methods

The VQI TEVAR registry was queried to identify patients undergoing single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching. Patients were included if the proximal landing zone was 0 or 1 and distal disease was confined to zone 5 or more proximal. Chimney, fenestration, stented fenestration, custom-manufactured, and physician-modified repairs were excluded. The zone 0 cohort included patients undergoing innominate side-arm branch repair with left common carotid artery (LCCA) and left subclavian artery (LSA) bypass/transposition, whereas the zone 1 cohort included patients undergoing LCCA side-arm branch repair with LSA bypass/transposition. Outcomes were analyzed descriptively.

Results

Among 38,215 TEVAR procedures screened, 50 patients met study criteria, including 39 zone 0 and 11 zone 1 repairs. Mean age was 73.8±8.5 years for zone 0 and 71.7±12.3 years for zone 1 patients. Prior aortic surgery was common (61.5% vs. 45.5%). Aneurysm was the most frequent indication for repair (66.7% vs. 72.7%). Staged treatment was performed in 74.4% of zone 0 and 45.5% of zone 1 procedures. Median procedure time was 166 and 163 minutes, respectively. Technical success was achieved in all patients. with no conversions to open repair and no completion Type Ia or Ib endoleaks. Cerebrovascular events occurred in 2.6% of zone 0 and 18.2% of zone 1 patients, including stroke in 2.6% and 9.1%, respectively. Spinal cord ischemia occurred in one zone 0 patient (2.6%). Myocardial infarction and postoperative dialysis occurred in 10.3% and 5.1% of zone 0 patients, respectively, and in no zone 1 patients. Thirty-day mortality was 10.3% following zone 0 repair and 0% following zone 1 repair.

Conclusions

Single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching was feasible in selected VQI patients undergoing zone 0 and zone 1 arch repair. Given the small sample size and limited event counts, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive early outcomes rather than evidence of comparative safety or superiority. Cerebrovascular complications remain an important concern after arch endovascular intervention.

title: Incremental Prognostic Value of Ascending Aortic Perivascular Adipose Tissue Radiomics for Short-Term Mortality After Surgical Repair of Acute Type A Aortic Dissection.
authorString: Shuai Y, Li A, Pan H, Chen J, Tang Y, Hou N, Yu Y, Li Y, Xiao X, Zhang T.

journal.title: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

abstractText: The purpose of this study is to investigate whether radiomic features derived from ascending aortic perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) provide incremental prognostic value beyond conventional clinical predictors for predicting short-term mortality after surgical repair of acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD). In this retrospective multicenter study, 241 patients with ATAAD who underwent surgical repair were enrolled and divided into a training cohort (n = 180) and an external validation cohort (n = 61). Radiomic features were extracted from preoperative computed tomography angiography (CTA) images of the ascending aortic PVAT extending from the sinotubular junction to the origin of the brachiocephalic trunk. The best-performing radiomics model was integrated with independent clinical predictors to develop a clinicoradiomics model. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration, decision curve analysis, DeLong testing, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis. Age, neutrophil count, creatinine level, and maximum ascending aortic diameter were identified as independent predictors of 3-month postoperative mortality. The random forest algorithm achieved the best radiomics performance. The clinicoradiomics model achieved superior discrimination, with AUCs of 0.935 and 0.855 in the training and external validation cohorts, respectively, significantly outperforming both the clinical model and the radiomics model (all P < 0.05). SHAP analysis identified multiple PVAT radiomic features among the most influential predictors. Ascending aortic PVAT radiomics provides complementary prognostic information beyond conventional clinical predictors for short-term mortality after surgical repair of ATAAD. A clinicoradiomics model integrating PVAT radiomics with clinical variables improves postoperative risk prediction and may facilitate individualized risk stratification.

title: Fulminant Staphylococcus aureus Pancarditis in an Immunocompetent Adult.
authorString: Koenig B, Kanso M, Roulot K, Faucher L, Marzak H, Jesel L, Ohlmann P.
abstractText:
Background

Infective endocarditis (IE) is rare and deadly. We report the case of IE rapidly progressing to pancarditis.

Case summary

A man in his 60s with no medical history presented with fever, chest pain, and embolic phenomena. Initial evaluation suggested myocardial infarction, but angiography was normal. Echocardiography revealed an aortic valve vegetation. Blood cultures grew methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus. Despite appropriate antibiotics, he developed rapidly progressive purulent pericardial effusion and died. Pericardial fluid cultures confirmed S aureus purulent pericarditis, establishing the diagnosis of pancarditis involving endocardium, myocardium, and pericardium.

Discussion

Bacterial pancarditis is an exceedingly rare and severe complication of IE. Pericardial effusion associated with IE should raise suspicion for purulent pericarditis and prompt rapid referral for surgical drainage or diagnostic puncture.

Take-home messages

Consider bacterial pancarditis when IE is complicated by myocardial and pericardial involvement. Pericardial effusion in IE requires prompt investigation and drainage or at least a diagnostic puncture.

title: Early and Long-term Outcomes of Adjunctive Fibrin Glue Sac Filling during Emergency Endovascular Repair for Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm
authorString: Chen Y, Guo J, Song X, Liu W, Dai X, Song Y.
abstractText: Background : Persistent hemorrhage at the rupture site after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) may be the risk of early mortality in patients with ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA). This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of adjunctive fibrin glue sac filling (FGSF) in emergency ruptured EVAR (rEVAR) for rAAA patients. Methods : A two-center retrospective cohort study was conducted on consecutive patients who underwent emergency rEVAR for rAAA at three tertiary referral centers from January 2010 to December 2024. Patients were classified by whether adjunctive FGSF was performed. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality and long-term survival. Statistical analyses included propensity score matching (PSM), Lasso regression, logistic regression, Cox proportional hazards regression, landmark analysis, and Kaplan–Meier survival analysis. Results : A total of 179 patients were included. After1:1 PSM, 50 patients were matched in each group. Compared with the standard rEVAR group, FGSF exhibited lower requirement of plasma (400 vs. 800 mL, P=0.04) and packed red blood cell transfusion volume (400 vs. 800 mL, P=0.045), and lower rates of early endoleak (2 vs. 18%, P=0.016), early reintervention (2 vs. 18%, P=0.016), and 30-day mortality (12 vs. 20%, P=0.048). Overall survival was also higher for FGSF (median follow-up 36.5 months; P=0.002) than standard rEVAR, but landmark analysis of hospital survivors showed similar long-term survival (median follow-up 48 months; P=0.06). Landmark analysis further demonstrated that FGSF was associated with a lower reintervention rate among hospital survivors (P = 0.041). Multivariable analyses confirmed that FGSF was an independent protective factor against 30-day mortality (OR=0.174, 95%CI: 0.049–0.529, P=0.004), as well as overall mortality (HR=0.248, 95%CI: 0.122–0.505, P<0.001). Conclusions : Adjunctive FGSF was associated with reduced mortality after emergent rEVAR for rAAA. The survival benefit appeared to be confined to the early postoperative period, whereas the reduction in reintervention risk seemed sustained. Further high-quality, prospective multicenter studies are required to validate these findings.

title: Preoperative Predictors of Outcome for Adults Undergoing Congenital Cardiac Surgery: Multicenter Model Validation.
authorString: Ponzoni M, Sugimoto A, Cade J, Khairy P, Buckley D, Barron D, Vanderlaan R, Oechslin E, Alonso-Gonzalez R, Roche L, Honjo O, Mueller B, Heggie J.

journal.title: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery

abstractText:
Objective

Adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) undergoing cardiac surgery represent a growing population in whom conventional surgical risk models perform suboptimally. We externally validated a previously described ACHD-specific preoperative risk model and evaluated whether performance could be improved through recalibration/model updating.

Methods

We conducted a prospective, multicenter observational study of patients ≥16 years undergoing congenital cardiac surgery at four centers (March 2020-April 2023). The primary composite adverse outcome (CAO) comprised in-hospital death, prolonged ventilation >7 days, or new-onset dialysis. We evaluated discrimination and calibration of the original preoperative model (including MELD-XI, cognitive impairment, body-mass index [BMI], prior chest wall incisions, and complex anatomy) and then performed bootstrap-based model updating (200 resamples) to derive refined models with and without the Adult Congenital Heart Surgery (ACHS) procedural mortality score.

Results

Among 538 patients, CAO occurred in 4.3% (n=23). In external validation (n=383 complete cases), the original model preserved discrimination (AUC=0.729, 95% confidence interval: 0.602-0.855) but systematically overestimated risk, indicating need for recalibration. The refined model retained BMI, prior chest incisions, cognitive impairment, age, serum albumin level, and ventricular systolic dysfunction. Discrimination was good without procedural complexity (AUC=0.799; 0.697-0.900) and improved with inclusion of the ACHS score (AUC=0.857; 0.779-0.935).

Conclusions

In this prospective multicenter external validation, an ACHD-specific preoperative risk model maintained discrimination but required recalibration. Incorporating procedural complexity enhanced discrimination, supporting a hybrid patient- and procedure-based approach to guide perioperative planning.

title: Ultrasound-assisted catheter-directed thrombolysis versus anticoagulation alone in intermediate-high risk pulmonary embolism.
authorString: Colombo C, Zuin M, Russo F, Iannaccone M, Solcia M, Musca F, Capsoni N, Fumarola F, Balderi A, Giordana F, Discalzi A, Tua L, Buratti S, Vercelli R, Adamo M, Boccuzzi G, Montorfano M, Chieffo A, Bilato C, Oliva F, Sacco A.
abstractText:
Background

Ultrasound-assisted catheter-directed thrombolysis (USAT) may enhance right ventricular recovery in intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism, but evidence is limited.

Objectives

We compared the safety, efficacy, and net benefit of USAT versus standard anticoagulation.

Methods

We analysed a propensity-matched prospective cohort of 432 intermediate-high-risk patients (216 USAT vs 216 anticoagulation) from the Italian USAT-HI and OPTIRAPE registries. Outcomes included all- cause, cardiovascular (CV) and PE-related death, major bleedings, and a composite net clinical benefit (NCB), with a day-7 landmark analysis distinguishing early (0-7 days) from late (8-30 days) events. Time-to-event analyses used Kaplan-Meier estimates and Cox regression with Hazard ratios (HRs) and relative 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

Results

Baseline demographics (mean age 64 ± 12 years; 48% female) and comorbidities were balanced between cohorts. USAT was associated with lower all-cause (7.4% vs 13.9%; HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.28-0.85; p = 0.01), cardiovascular (3.2% vs 8.3%; HR 0.39; p < 0.001), and PE-related mortality (2.3% vs 6.5%; HR 0.34; p = 0.02) compared with anticoagulation. Major bleeding was similar (2.7% vs 1.9%; p = 0.56). USAT significantly improved net clinical benefit (13.4% vs 25.9%; HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.30-0.75; p = 0.001), mainly driven by reductions in early mortality and clinical deterioration. Landmark analysis indicated that benefits were largely confined to the first 7 days, with favourable but non-significant effects during days 8-30.

Conclusions

In intermediate-high-risk PE, USAT was associated with lower early mortality, improved net clinical outcomes, and a safety profile comparable to standard anticoagulation.

title: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: From pathophysiology to a practical approach to diagnosis and treatment.
authorString: Fernández-Cisnal A, Lorenzo M, Palau P, Núñez J.
abstractText: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous syndrome with increasing prevalence, driven by aging and cardiometabolic comorbidities. It is better understood as a disorder of elevated filling pressures, impaired cardiovascular reserve, recurrent congestion, and systemic multiorgan dysfunction than as heart failure with normal systolic function. Diagnosis remains probabilistic and requires integration of symptoms, natriuretic peptides, echocardiographic structural and functional abnormalities, and, when resting findings are inconclusive, exercise or invasive hemodynamic testing. Treatment has evolved from symptom control toward phenotype-oriented care. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors are foundational therapy, finerenone expands options for selected patients, and obesity is now a modifiable therapeutic target. This review summarizes current mechanisms, diagnostic pathways, and treatment strategies, with emphasis on practical clinical decision-making.

title: Telehealth Utilisation Among Black Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study Using the 2022 Health Information National Trends Survey.
authorString: Owusu B, Bannor R, Turkson-Ocran RN, Chen Y, Spaulding EM, Casseus K, Bivins B, Chepkorir J, Martin SL, Mutaru AM, Romain D, Appiah-Okyere J, Commodore-Mensah Y, Ogungbe O, Baptiste D.
abstractText: Telehealth has expanded access to health care, especially since the COVID-19 pandemic. However, disparities in telehealth use persist among racial and ethnic minorities, including Black adults, who face higher rates of chronic conditions such as diabetes and hypertension. Barriers such as limited digital health literacy, a preference for in-person care, and systemic inequities may hinder telehealth adoption in this population. Nurses play a vital role in assessing, educating, and advocating for patients navigating digital health platforms. This study assessed the prevalence of telehealth use among Black adults in the United States, identified key barriers and facilitators, and examined predictors of telehealth utilisation. Implications for nursing practice were explored to inform strategies for improving digital access and equity. We analysed data from the 2022 Health Information National Trends Survey (HINTS) using descriptive statistics to explore telehealth prevalence, barriers, and facilitators. Multivariate logistic regression identified predictors of telehealth use. Weighted analyses ensured nationally representative results. The analytic sample included 1,044 respondents, representing approximately 32 million Black adults after applying sample weights. Over the past 12 months, 36.5% (standard error [SE], 3.0) of Black adults used telehealth. Among those offered telehealth but opting out, 89.5% (SE, 4.4) preferred in-person care. Key facilitators included convenience (64.6%; SE, 4.6), avoiding hospital-acquired infections (52.0%; SE, 4.0), and provider recommendations (70.0%; SE, 4.0). Adults aged 31-45 years (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.1; p=0.050) and 46-60 years (aOR 2.1; p=0.047) had higher odds of telehealth use than those aged 18-30 years. Black adults with cardiometabolic conditions were three times more likely to use telehealth than those without such conditions (aOR 3.0; p<0.001). Telehealth use among Black adults is motivated by convenience and health concerns but hindered by a strong preference for in-person care. These findings underscore the need for culturally tailored, nurse-led interventions that address digital health literacy and patient engagement, particularly among those without existing chronic conditions. Nurses are uniquely positioned to assess readiness for telehealth, provide personalised education, and advocate for equitable access to digital care. Future nursing research should explore innovative telehealth models that centre patient preferences and reduce digital exclusion in underserved populations.

title: Combined bipolar and unipolar voltage mapping to identify epicardial breakthrough regions after pulsed field ablation.
authorString: Watanabe T, Hachiya H, Yumita Y, Suda N, Okuyama T, Watanabe H, Kamioka M, Makimoto H, Yokota A, Komori T, Kabutoya T, Imai Y, Kario K.
abstractText:
Background

The utility of unipolar voltage (UV) mapping for identifying epicardial breakthrough regions after pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) remains undetermined.

Objective

This study assessed combined bipolar voltage (BV) and UV mapping for identifying epicardial breakthrough regions after pulsed field ablation (PFA).

Methods

Thirty patients with atrial fibrillation underwent initial PFA-PVI with a pentaspline catheter under fluoroscopic guidance. Within the isolated PV antrum (BV <0.1 mV), transmurally ablated regions and epicardial breakthrough regions were defined by UV <1.08 mV and UV ≥1.08 mV, respectively. Unipolar electrogram features were investigated to identify epicardial breakthrough regions.

Results

Seventeen patients had 27 epicardial breakthrough regions, yielding 276 local unipolar electrograms (QR pattern: n=160; RS pattern: n=116). QR electrograms were distributed broadly within the isolated PV, whereas RS electrograms occurred exclusively around the isolation boundary. QR electrograms, indicating possible epicardial breakthrough, had significantly higher UV amplitudes than RS electrograms (median: 1.64 vs. 0.70 mV; P<0.001). The UV amplitude cutoff distinguishing these morphologies was 1.15 mV (sensitivity, 91.9%; specificity, 84.5%; area under the curve [AUC], 0.922; P<0.001). Among 245 local unipolar electrograms around the isolation boundary, excluding QR electrograms, RS electrograms had higher UV amplitudes and steeper negative intrinsic deflection slopes than non-RS electrograms, suggesting possible intramural conduction gaps. Respective cutoffs were 0.48 mV (sensitivity, 83.6%; specificity, 86.8%; AUC, 0.923; P<0.001) and 0.020 mV/ms (sensitivity, 97.4%; specificity, 94.5%; AUC, 0.992; P<0.001).

Conclusion

Combined BV and UV mapping provides additional information for identifying epicardial breakthrough regions at PFA application sites.

title: Left bundle branch pacing vs left ventricular septal pacing in the same patients with heart failure and left bundle branch block.
authorString: Huang X, Huang S, Chen X, Chen S, Li L, Gao Q, Huang K, Song Y, Su M, Cai B, Wang Y.
abstractText:
Background

Left bundle branch pacing (LBBP) and left ventricular septal pacing (LVSP) are considered to be acceptable as left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) strategies. The differences in cardiac mechanical performance between LBBP and LVSP in the same patients with heart failure (HF) and left bundle branch block (LBBB) are yet to be determined.

Objectives

The purpose of this study was to compare mechanical function and resynchronization effect of LBBP and LVSP as CRTP modalities.

Methods

Fourteen patients with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and typical complete LBBB who received cardiac resynchronization therapy pacing (CRTP) implantation were enrolled. All patient implantation with two ventricular pacing leads, enabling both LBBP and LVSP. Acute cardiac function and resynchronization effect were assessed by echocardiography and electrocardiography to compare the differences in LBBB mode, LBBP mode, and LVSP mode within the same patients undergoing CRTP.

Results

Both pacing modes significantly reduced QRS duration (QRSd) and left ventricular activation time (LVAT) versus LBBB (all P<0.001), with LVSP yielding wider QRSd than LBBP (P<0.001). LBBP showed better performance in LV mechanical synchrony parameter (SDI) than LVSP, and both pacing modes were superior to that of LBBB condition (all P < 0.001). LVEF increased significantly with both pacing modes, with a greater increase observed in LBBP compared to LVSP. No significant differences in right ventricular function were observed among the three modes.

Conclusion

In this pilot study of patients with HF and LBBB, both LBBP and LVSP significantly improved left ventricular hemodynamics and mechanical synchrony without compromising RV function. LBBP potentially has superior left ventricular hemodynamic effects to LVSP.

title: Mid-pregnancy plasma environmental chemical exposures and maternal blood pressure in a pilot study of Black women.
authorString: Joseph G, DeBolt CA, Maroli AS, Guan H, Ncube L, Gennings C, Petrick LM.

journal.title: International journal of hygiene and environmental health

abstractText: Epidemiological evidence suggests Black women experience disproportionate exposure to environmental chemicals and diagnoses of hypertension during pregnancy. We characterized environmental chemicals and determined their associations with blood pressure in a cross-sectional analysis of Black women in Philadelphia. We measured 32 plasma chemicals using non-targeted analysis in samples collected between the 16th and 24th weeks of gestation in the MOMENTUM cohort (n = 68). We assessed the association between log2-transformed chemical abundance and blood pressure, as well as preterm hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), using regression analysis. We categorized chemical abundances into tertiles and modelled them as ordinal variables; blood pressure as a continuous variable; and preterm HDP as a binary variable. We assessed the mixture effect with a Weight Quantile Sum regression constraint in the positive direction. Each increase in one tertile of 4-methylbenzophenone (β = 4.48 mmHg; 95% CI: 1.84, 7.12), 4-tert-Butylcatechol (β = 3.83 mmHg; 95% CI: 1.53, 6.14), benzophenone (β = 4.05 mmHg; 95% CI: 1.49, 6.61), carvone (β = 3.50 mmHg; 95% CI: 1.19, 5.81), and tris(2-ethylhexyl) phosphate (β = 3.98 mmHg; 95% CI: 1.23, 6.74) was cross-sectionally associated with a statistically significant increase in diastolic blood pressure. A mixture of flavoring and fragrance agents also showed a positive association with diastolic blood pressure (β = 3.05 mmHg; 95%CI: 0.60, 4.67). Exposures were not significantly associated with systolic blood pressure and preterm HDP. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require replication in large-scale cohort studies.

title: Complexity of patients with hypertension cared for by clinical pharmacist practitioners in the Veterans Health Administration.
authorString: Borzecki AM, Jasuja GK, Qian S, Ndiwane N, McFarland S, Ourth HL, McCullough MM.

journal.title: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists

abstractText: Clinical pharmacist practitioners (CPPs) are well suited to manage complex patients, such as those with hypertension. However, there is limited information about the complexity of patients managed by CPPs with respect to chronic disease. This study compared the clinical complexity of patients with hypertension managed by CPPs to that of patients managed by other providers. In this cross-sectional study, patients with hypertension at 19 Veterans Health Administration (VA) sites during fiscal years 2024 to 2025 were classified by CPP visits into those with more than one visit ("ongoing CPP care"), those with one visit ("consultative CPP care"), and those with no visits ("no CPP care"). Patient complexity was assessed using 7 hypertension-related measures indicating need for more management time and resources. Logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, race, and marital status were generated to analyze differences between the groups. Compared to patients in the group with no CPP care, patients with ongoing CPP care had significantly higher complexity as measured by hypertension medication use (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.36; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.09-1.70), other medications associated with hypertension (aOR, 1.66; 95% CI, 1.26-2.18), hypertension complications (aOR, 1.60; 95% CI, 1.29-1.98), and medication nonadherence (aOR, 1.36; 95% CI, 1.06-1.75). Similar findings were noted for patients with consultative CPP care vs those with no CPP care. A composite complexity score of all 7 measures indicated that patients with ongoing (aOR, 1.89; 95% CI, 1.54-2.32) and consultative (aOR, 1.88; 95% CI, 1.57-2.24) CPP care were significantly more complex than patients with no CPP care. CPPs manage patients with hypertension who are more complex than those managed by other VA providers. These findings underscore the importance of CPPs in improving patient outcomes through comprehensive medication management.

title: Exploring patient perspectives on barriers contributing to lost to follow-up in hypertension care: A qualitative study in a tertiary-care hospital in Coastal Karnataka, India.
authorString: Kamath R, Stanley W, Hazarika PP, Tumkur Shivakumar S, Reshmi B.
abstractText: Hypertension requires lifelong treatment and regular follow-up to prevent complications; however, lost to follow-up (LTFU) remains a major challenge in long-term hypertension care, particularly in resource-constrained settings. This study explored patient perspectives on barriers contributing to LTFU in hypertension management. A qualitative study was conducted among 32 hypertensive patients who were LTFU at a tertiary care hospital in Coastal Karnataka, India. Participants were aged 31-69years, with 21 (65.6%) men and 11 (34.4%) women. Participants were identified through hospital records and interviewed using a semi-structured interview guide. Interviews were conducted from February to April 2026 Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed thematically following COREQ guidelines. Six major themes emerged.: (1) illness perception and self-management practices, (2) care-seeking and follow-up behaviour, (3) structural and socioeconomic barriers, (4) health system and continuity gaps, (5) patient-perceived strategies to improve continuity of care, and (6) health information continuity and interoperability needs. Participants described symptom-driven healthcare seeking, medication non-adherence, occupational responsibilities, and competing family priorities contributing to irregular follow-up. Financial burden, including treatment costs, transportation expenses, and wage loss, substantially affected continuity of care. Long travel distances, dependence on family members, overcrowding, rushed consultations, and inadequate follow-up mechanisms further influenced disengagement from care.
