Participants also reported fragmented healthcare utilisation, repeated investigations, dependence on paper-based records, and poor continuity of medical information across healthcare facilities. Several participants perceived that integrated digital health information systems, decentralised services, appointment reminders, and improved counselling could strengthen long-term hypertension follow-up. LTFU in hypertension care is influenced by interconnected individual, socioeconomic, and health system-related barriers. A notable finding was the fragmented nature of continuity of care and poor health information continuity across healthcare facilities. Strengthening patient-centred follow-up systems, decentralised chronic disease services, financial protection mechanisms, and interoperable health information systems may improve continuity of hypertension care and reduce long-term disengagement from chronic disease management.

title: A GCN1-independent activator of the kinase GCN2.
authorString: Zhu J, Emanuelli G, Masson GR, Vinciauskaite V, Willems H, Cai P, Lim A, Brown CA, Winpenny D, Clarke M, Gilley R, Preston F, Wilson JCJ, Bader A, Rahman T, Chambers JE, Skidmore J, Morrell NW, Marciniak SJ.
abstractText: Mutations of EIF2AK4, which encodes the eIF2α kinase GCN2, cause a severe inherited form of pulmonary hypertension called pulmonary veno-occlusive disease (PVOD). Some pathogenic variants of GCN2 are amenable to pharmacological reactivation by low concentrations of ATP pocket-binding inhibitors. Kinase inhibition at modestly elevated concentrations limits the clinical utility of these drugs against PVOD. We therefore performed an in cellulo chemical screen for GCN2 activators and identified three structurally distinct compounds with low micromolar stimulatory activities. Unlike previously described GCN2 activators, one of these molecules activated GCN2 independently of GCN1. Modelling supported by structure activity screens suggested it binds within the ATP pocket of GCN2, but unlike existing ligands does not protrude inward into the allosteric pocket or outward into the solvent. This overcomes a key requirement of other GCN2 activators.

title: Heart rate and blood pressure variability, and baroreflex sensitivity, during heat exposure in persons with type 2 diabetes and hypertension.
authorString: Rafieian M, Farbu EH, Höper AC, Valtonen R, Kallio M, Hyrkäs-Palmu H, Crandall C, Ikäheimo TM.
abstractText: The autonomic nervous system regulates cardiovascular homeostasis during stressors such as heat, but the effects of type 2 diabetes (T2D) with hypertension on such responses are unclear. Twenty male participants (10 with type 2 diabetes and hypertension and 10 age-matched healthy controls; mean ages 64 ± 4.14 and 63 ± 5.42 years) underwent a 90-minute whole-body heat exposure at 40 °C and 50% relative humidity. Heart rate variability (HRV), baroreflex sensitivity (BRS), and blood pressure variability (BPV) were assessed before, during and after the heat exposure. Heat exposure increased heart rate in both groups but this response was less in T2D (5.43 bpm; ~ 7% increase) versus controls (13.96 bpm; ~ 22% increase; p = 0.014). Similarly, reductions in HRV indices to heat stress were generally smaller in magnitude among participants with T2D. For example, high-frequency power (HF RR) decreased by 31.21 ms² (~54.5% reduction) in T2D because of heat exposure, compared with a reduction of 179.35 ms² (~74% reduction) in controls (p = 0.038). Further, LF BRS decreased by 1.07 ms/mmHg (~25% reduction) vs. 3.96 ms/mmHg (~51% reduction) (p = 0.021), HF BRS by 1.58 ms/mmHg (~35% reduction) vs. 4.15 ms/mmHg (~62% reduction) (p = 0.034), and mean BRS by 1.18 ms/mmHg (~26% reduction) vs. 4.16 ms/mmHg (~58% reduction) (p = 0.010) in those with T2D versus controls, respectively. Low-frequency power (LF RR), LF/HF ratio and BPV parameters also showed smaller (though nonsignificant) changes in T2D. Overall, combined T2D and hypertension produced blunted autonomic responses to short-term heat exposure, potentially increasing vulnerability to temperature extremes.

title: Retinal layer structure on optical coherence tomography in post-traumatic stress disorder.
authorString: Patel SD, Karthik N, Justin GA, Haystead A, Chiu SJ, Stinnett SS, Johnson KG, Grewal DS, Fekrat S.
abstractText: To assess individual retinal layer thickness and volume changes on optical coherence tomography (OCT) in individuals with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) compared to controls. Adults ≥18 years with a PTSD diagnosis were identified. Age- and sex-matched controls (±5 years) without PTSD were recruited. Exclusion criteria included any cognitive disorder, brain injury, glaucoma, diabetes, optic nerve or vitreoretinal disease, uncontrolled hypertension, refractive error >±6 diopters, or best corrected visual acuity <20/40. Non-mydriatic OCT macular cube 512x128 images were obtained using Zeiss Cirrus HD-5000 AngioPlex. The Duke Reading Center DRCVisualizer software was used to segment the ganglion cell/inner plexiform (GC-IPL), inner nuclear (INL), outer plexiform (OPL), outer nuclear (ONL), photoreceptor, and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) layers. Mean retinal thickness and volume were calculated for all layers within the central 1-mm subfield and 3- and 6-mm ETDRS rings, further divided into nasal, superior, temporal, and inferior quadrants. 81 eyes of 42 PTSD patients and 81 eyes of 42 controls were analyzed. Average ages were 48 ± 15 years for PTSD and 51 ± 19 years for controls. Groups were 36% male. PTSD eyes showed significantly decreased photoreceptor thickness and volume and increased RPE thickness/volume across all ETDRS rings and quadrants (all p < 0.05). OPL thicknesses were decreased in PTSD eyes versus controls for temporal 3-mm (25.29 ± 1.36 µm vs. 26.64 ± 3.80µm) and temporal 6-mm (23.47 ± 0.88µm vs. 24.00 ± 1.54µm) rings (p < 0.05). OPL inferior 6-mm thickness was decreased in PTSD eyes (23.98 ± 1.58 µm vs. 24.78 ± 2.34 µm) versus controls (p < 0.05). The ONL nasal 6-mm thickness was decreased in PTSD versus controls (55.96 ± 7.90 µm vs. 56.74 ± 7.47µm) (p < 0.05). After adjusting for multiple testing, RPE differences remained significant across all evaluated regions, while photoreceptor differences remained significant within the central 1-mm and 3-mm ETDRS regions. PTSD eyes demonstrated decreased photoreceptor layer and increased RPE thickness and volume.

title: Atrial fibrillation is independently associated with impaired myocardial perfusion.
authorString: Vartiainen N, Hartikainen S, Rissanen AE, Kariniemi E, Leikas AJ, Strengell E, Halttunen S, Kuikka PI, Hartikainen JEK, Laitinen TP.
abstractText: A characteristic feature of obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) is impaired myocardial blood flow (MBF). Previous studies have shown that atrial fibrillation (AF) is also associated with reduced hyperemic MBF. However, it is unknown whether an independent association exists between AF and MBF in symptomatic patients with suspected obstructive CAD. We studied 874 patients at Kuopio University Hospital (Finland) who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) and [15O]H2O myocardial perfusion positron emission tomography due to suspected obstructive CAD in 2017-2023. The final cohort comprised 31 AF patients and 120 propensity score-matched sinus rhythm (SR) patients. The matching criteria were age, sex, body mass index, number of traditional risk factors for CAD (0-5), calcium score, and total CCTA status (i.e., the overall severity of CCTA findings). Global hyperemic MBF was lower in AF patients than in SR patients (median 1.9 mL/g/min [IQR 1.4-2.6 mL/g/min] vs. 3.0 mL/g/min [IQR 2.4-3.6 mL/g/min], p < 0.001). Impaired hyperemic MBF (< 2.3 mL/g/min in ≥ 1 segment) was more frequent in AF patients (n = 25/31, 81%) than in SR patients (n = 50/120, 42%, p < 0.001). Furthermore, the presence of AF was independently associated with reduced hyperemic MBF in three multivariate general linear models (p < 0.001 in each model). To summarize, AF was independently associated with impaired hyperemic MBF in patients with suspected obstructive CAD. This association should be considered in clinical practice when interpreting the results of myocardial perfusion imaging in patients with AF.

title: Ravulizumab monotherapy for anti-CFH antibody-associated aHUS in an elderly patient: a case report highlighting individualized clinical decision-making.
authorString: Yoshii R, Kajiwara K, Hirose K, Hatanaka T, Shimasaki A, Tomita M, Yokoi H.
abstractText: Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS) is a life-threatening thrombotic microangiopathy caused by complement dysregulation. Although anti-complement factor H (CFH) autoantibodies are a well-recognized cause of aHUS, their occurrence in elderly patients is rare, and optimal management in this population remains unclear. We report the case of an 85-year-old man who presented with acute kidney injury, thrombocytopenia, and microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, alongside severe hypertension. ADAMTS13 activity was preserved, and no secondary causes of thrombotic microangiopathy were identified, leading to a clinical suspicion of complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA). At the time of clinical decision-making, anti-CFH antibody status was not yet available;serum creatinine trends during hemodialysis could not reliably indicate intrinsic renal recovery, and hematological markers, although improving, did not clearly indicate complete resolution of hemolysis. Following an individualized risk assessment regarding plasma exchange (PEX) and immunosuppressive therapy in an octogenarian, ravulizumab was selected as the initial treatment due to its etiology-independent mechanism of action. Following initiation, hematological parameters continued to improve, and renal function gradually recovered, allowing discontinuation of hemodialysis. Subsequent testing revealed elevated anti-CFH antibody levels without pathogenic complement gene variants, confirming the diagnosis of anti-CFH antibody-associated aHUS. This case highlights that, in clinical settings with diagnostic uncertainty, ravulizumab monotherapy may be considered as an individualized initial approach in exceptional cases where PEX and immunosuppression are judged unsuitable based on clearly documented patient-specific risks, and requires careful follow-up including serial anti-CFH antibody monitoring and consideration of immunosuppression if antibody titers persist or relapse risk remains high.

title: Periodontitis Beyond ASCVD: Emerging Cardiovascular Phenotypes in Perio-Medicine.
authorString: Sansavini M, Pieretto G, Samra M, Bacci C.
abstractText:
Background

Periodontitis is increasingly recognized as a chronic inflammatory disease with systemic implications beyond the oral cavity. Within perio-medicine, its association with cardiovascular disease has been extensively investigated, particularly in relation to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). However, the field is now expanding toward a broader and more phenotype-specific cardiovascular framework.

Objective

This narrative review critically examines how the periodontitis-cardiovascular field has evolved from a predominantly ASCVD-centered model toward a broader spectrum of cardiovascular phenotypes, with particular emphasis on differences in evidence maturity, contemporary mechanistic concepts, and unresolved translational questions.

Methods

A structured literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library. Evidence from mechanistic, observational, and interventional studies was qualitatively synthesized according to its contribution to established clinical associations, supportive mechanistic evidence, emerging cardiovascular phenotypes, and unresolved questions regarding causality and clinical translation.

Results

The association between periodontitis and coronary atherosclerotic disease represents the most mature component of the literature, with substantial observational and meta-analytic support, while ischemic cerebrovascular disease is also supported by consistent but more heterogeneous evidence. Beyond ASCVD, atrial fibrillation and heart failure currently represent the most developed emerging cardiovascular phenotypes, whereas evidence concerning abdominal aortic aneurysm and venous thromboembolism remains more preliminary and hypothesis-generating. Contemporary mechanistic models extend beyond bacteremia and systemic inflammation to include endothelial dysfunction, thrombo-inflammatory signaling, trained immunity, immune-cell trafficking, functional dysregulation of the oral microbiome, and shared biological vulnerabilities. However, these pathways differ markedly in cardiovascular-specific evidentiary maturity and should not be interpreted as equivalent evidence of human causality. Periodontal therapy can improve inflammatory biomarkers, endothelial function, selected metabolic parameters, and blood pressure in specific populations, but a persistent translational gap remains between surrogate-marker improvement and demonstrated reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events. Periodontitis may also contribute to chronic systemic inflammatory burden in susceptible individuals, although its role within cardiovascular residual inflammatory risk remains an emerging hypothesis.

Conclusions

The periodontal-cardiovascular field is evolving from a predominantly ASCVD-centered model toward a phenotype-specific continuum of evidence maturity. Periodontitis is best interpreted as a potential modifier of cardiovascular vulnerability rather than as an established causal determinant. Future research should prioritize adequately powered cardiovascular-outcome trials, standardized periodontal phenotyping, and prospective validation of emerging phenotypes and mechanistic frameworks before periodontal information can be considered clinically actionable for cardiovascular prevention.

title: Does raised ICP play a role in cognitive outcome in scaphocephaly?
authorString: B SM, S HT, M J.

journal.title: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery

abstractText: Scaphocephaly, the cranial deformity resulting from premature fusion of the sagittal suture, represents the most common form of nonsyndromic craniosynostosis (Bosnian Journal of Basic Medical Sciences p. 110-6, 2018). Surgical correction is typically performed to normalize cranial morphology and reduce the risk of intracranial hypertension. However, the association between elevated intracranial pressure (ICP) and long-term neurocognitive outcomes remains unclear (Bosnian Journal of Basic Medical Sciences p. 110-6, 2018; Child's Nervous System p. 689-95, 2020). Some studies report an increased prevalence of learning and neuropsychological difficulties in children with sagittal synostosis, yet a direct causal relationship with elevated ICP has not been clearly demonstrated. Evidence suggests that while elevated ICP occurs in a subset of patients, cognitive differences likely arise from a multifactorial interaction between cranial restriction, brain development, and underlying biological mechanisms rather than ICP alone.

title: [Three-dimensional electroanatomic mapping in the electrophysiology lab: when, how and why? : A practical introduction for early-career electrophysiologists].
authorString: Aweimer A, Beck P.
abstractText: Three-dimensional electroanatomic mapping has become an integral part of modern invasive electrophysiology. It combines catheter localization, patient-specific cardiac anatomy, local electrograms, activation timing, voltage information, and ablation lesion documentation within a spatial working model. For early-career electrophysiologists, however, the interpretation of these maps can be challenging. This review provides a practical introduction to three-dimensional (3D) mapping for young electrophysiologists during their first steps in the electrophysiology laboratory. It addresses when 3D mapping is useful or necessary, how a map is created, what information can be derived from different map types, and which pitfalls should be avoided. The article summarizes technical principles and clinical applications of 3D electroanatomic mapping based on current expert consensus documents, review articles, and practical electrophysiological concepts. 3D mapping is particularly valuable in atrial fibrillation ablation, atypical atrial tachycardias, ventricular tachycardias, redo procedures, congenital or postsurgical anatomy, and low-fluoroscopy workflows. Activation maps help visualize the temporal sequence of electrical propagation, whereas voltage maps provide information on scar, low-voltage areas, and potential arrhythmogenic substrate. The quality of a map depends on stable rhythm, reliable temporal and spatial references, catheter contact, signal quality, adequate point density, and correct annotation. 3D mapping is a powerful tool for navigation, mechanism analysis, substrate characterization, and ablation documentation. Nevertheless, it does not replace electrophysiological reasoning. Every map must be interpreted critically and validated using intracardiac electrograms, surface ECG, anatomy, pacing maneuvers, and defined procedural endpoints.

title: Comparative Effectiveness of Individual Angiotensin Receptor Blockers on Osteoporosis and Osteoporotic Fracture Risk: A Nationwide Active-Comparator New-User Cohort Study.
authorString: Wu HM, Wu WT, Tsai CT, Chien WC, Chou YC, Lin MH, Chuang CH.
abstractText: Osteoporosis is a major cause of morbidity and fragility fractures in older adults, and increasing evidence suggests that antihypertensive therapies may influence skeletal health beyond blood pressure control. Although angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) have been associated with favorable skeletal outcomes, whether clinically relevant heterogeneity exists among individual ARBs remains unclear. Telmisartan possesses distinctive pharmacological properties, including partial peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ (PPAR-γ) agonistic activity, which may confer additional effects on bone metabolism. This study evaluated whether skeletal outcomes differ between telmisartan and other ARBs using an active-comparator new-user design. To evaluate whether clinically relevant differences in osteoporosis and osteoporotic fracture risk exist between telmisartan and other ARBs using Taiwan's Health and Welfare Data Science Center (HWDC) Database. Using Longitudinal Generation Tracking Database (LGTD) housed within the Health and Welfare Data Science Center (HWDC), we conducted a nationwide active-comparator new-user cohort study. Hypertensive patients aged 51-80 years who newly initiated telmisartan or another ARB between 2002 and 2021 were identified. Propensity score matching (1:4) was performed to balance baseline characteristics. The primary outcome was a composite of incident osteoporosis or osteoporotic fracture and time to first osteoporotic fracture was additionally evaluated as a secondary outcome. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models. During a mean follow-up of 4.35 ± 4.12 years, telmisartan use was associated with a lower risk of osteoporosis or osteoporotic fracture compared with other ARBs (adjusted HR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.53-0.79). In analyses of individual outcomes, telmisartan use was associated with lower risks of osteoporosis (adjusted HR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.43-0.84) and hip fracture (adjusted HR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.19-0.70). In the secondary fracture-only analysis, telmisartan use was associated with a lower risk of first osteoporotic fracture (adjusted HR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.57-0.90). Compared with other ARBs, telmisartan use was associated with a lower risk of osteoporosis and osteoporotic fractures in this nationwide cohort. These findings suggest that clinically relevant heterogeneity may exist within the ARB class and that antihypertensive drug selection may influence skeletal outcomes beyond blood pressure control. Further prospective studies are warranted to confirm these findings.

title: Floralozone alleviates doxorubicin-induced cardiac senescence and fibrosis by inhibiting the VEGFR1.
authorString: Zhang HD, Wang YT, Yang ZY, Wang HD, Li XY, Zhang CR, Li CZ, Li P.
abstractText: Floralozone(FL) is a medicinal compound with potential cardiovascular protective effects. Vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 1 (VEGFR1) signaling has been implicated in cardiovascular dysfunction. This study investigated whether floralozone ameliorates heart failure (HF) through regulation of VEGFR1. HF was induced in rats by intraperitoneal injection of doxorubicin (DOX) for six weeks. VEGFR1 expression was analyzed by immunofluorescence and Western blotting. Oxidative stress was determined by DHE staining of myocardial ROS and serum MDA and SOD assays. Senescence associated β-galactosidase (SA-β-gal) staining was performed to evaluate the degree of myocardial aging. HE staining was used to observe cardiac morphology. Masson, argyrophilic and orcein staining were applied to detect the degree of myocardial fibrosis, and echocardiography was conducted to assess cardiac function in each group. Floralozone (FL) modulated VEGFR1 expression and alleviated DOX-induced oxidative stress, cardiac aging, myocardial fibrosis, and cardiac dysfunction in HF rats. The protective effects of FL on oxidative stress, cardiac aging, myocardial fibrosis, cardiac function, and VEGFR1 expression were attenuated by pharmacological activation of VEGFR1 with placental growth factor (PLGF), supporting the involvement of VEGFR1 signaling in the cardioprotective effects of FL. These findings suggest that floralozone exerts cardioprotective effects against DOX induced heart failure, at least in part, through modulation of VEGFR1 associated signaling and oxidative stress. Floralozone modulated VEGFR1 expression and was associated with reduced oxidative stress, cardiac aging, and myocardial fibrosis, ultimately improving cardiac dysfunction. However, the precise causal relationship between VEGFR1 signaling and oxidative stress remains to be determined. These findings suggest that floralozone may have therapeutic potential for DOX induced cardiac injury through modulation of VEGFR1 associated pathological processes.

title: Increased Nuclear Susceptibility to Mechanical Stress in Phospholamban R14del Cardiomyopathy: A New Perspective on Disease Heterogeneity
authorString: van der Geest JSA, van der Pol A, Hermans L, Al-khaqani A, van Asten J, van Roessel MA, van Ham WB, te Riele AS, van Mil A, Sampaio-Pinto V, Doevendans PA, Lei Z, Conte V, Sluijter JPG, Bouten CV.
abstractText:
Background

Clinical presentation of phospholamban (PLN) R14del cardiomyopathy is highly variable, from asymptomatic carriers to rapidly progressing heart failure. which cannot be fully explained by its known disturbance of sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium handling. Nuclear calcium signalling, shaped by sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release, plays a key role in regulating gene expression and the cellular response to mechanical stress. However, how the R14del variant affects nuclear signalling under mechanical loading remains unclear.

Objective

To uncover the impact of the PLN R14del variation on mechanosensing, nuclear calcium handling and its link to the variable clinical representation of this cardiomyopathy.

Methods

Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) carrying the PLN R14del variant, an isogenic control, and wildtype control were subjected to mechanical stimulation by cyclic stretch or cultured on substrates with physiological (10-20 kPa) and pathological (65-85 kPa) stiffness. Nuclear morphology, cytoskeletal organisation and nuclear body formation were assessed via immunofluorescence. Traction force microscopy was used to assess mechanical stress and force generation. Cardiac tissues from PLN R14del cardiomyopathy patients, dilated cardiomyopathy patients, and healthy controls were analysed under mechanical loading (at left ventricular assist device implantation) and unloading (at heart transplantation). Living myocardial slices from a PLN R14del patient were maintained under overloading or physiological loading conditions.

Results

PLN R14del hiPSC-CMs showed impaired nuclear calcium handling and, under mechanical stress, exhibited impaired mechanotransduction and elevated nuclear bodies. A strain-avoidance response was triggered but failed to prevent apoptosis. Nuclear abnormalities were confirmed in patient myocardial slices and cardiac biopsies which normalized upon relative mechanical unloading.

Conclusion

PLN R14del increases nuclear susceptibility to mechanical stress, linking nuclear dysfunction to new disease insights and highlighting potential for mechanobiology-based therapeutic interventions.

Condensed abstract

PLN R14del cardiomyopathy presents with highly variable clinical severity, which cannot be fully explained by its known disturbance of sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium handling. We investigated whether the R14del variant impairs nuclear calcium signalling and mechanosensing, thereby contributing to disease heterogeneity. Using PLN R14del, isogenic control, and wildtype hiPSC-CMs subjected to cyclic stretch and substrates of physiological and pathological stiffness, we demonstrate that PLN R14del cardiomyocytes exhibit impaired nuclear calcium handling, elevated nuclear damage, disrupted cytoskeletal organisation, and failed mechanotransduction under mechanical stress. Although a strain-avoidance response was triggered, it was insufficient to prevent apoptosis. These findings were confirmed in living myocardial slices and cardiac biopsies from PLN R14del patients, where nuclear abnormalities were most pronounced under mechanical loading and reversed upon unloading. Together, these data establish increased nuclear susceptibility to mechanical stress as a novel pathological feature of PLN R14del cardiomyopathy, offering new insight into disease heterogeneity and highlighting mechanobiology-based therapeutic opportunities.

title: Incidence and Factors Associated with Acute Kidney Injury Among Adults Admitted to the Medical and Emergency Wards of Two Regional Hospitals in Western Cameroon: A Prospective Cohort Study with a Nested Case–Control Analysis
authorString: DIONE EA, NJONNOU SRS, TCHOKOUAHA FN, LEKPA FK, OUANKOU CN, BALEPNA J, CHOUKEM SP, KOUANFACK C.
abstractText: Background Acute kidney injury (AKI) carries a high burden in sub-Saharan Africa, yet its determinants remain poorly characterised in Cameroon. We estimated the incidence of AKI among adults admitted to medical and emergency wards of two regional hospitals in western Cameroon, classified its pathogenesis and severity, and identified its determinants. Methods We conducted a prospective cohort study with a nested case–control analysis at the Dschang Regional Hospital Annex and the Bafoussam Regional Hospital Centre between February and May 2024. Consecutive adults aged 18 years and over with a creatinine measured within 48 hours of admission and a control creatinine 48–72 hours later were enrolled. AKI was defined by modified KDIGO 2012 criteria and staged accordingly. Cases (AKI) were matched 1:1 with controls on age, sex and history of hypertension. Analyses were performed in SPSS version 23, with logistic regression to obtain adjusted odds ratios; significance was set at p < 0.05. Results Of 345 patients approached, 210 were analysed. AKI occurred in 80 participants, an incidence of 38.1%. Median age was 61 years (IQR 45–75) and 42 cases (52.5%) were men. Pre-renal AKI predominated (75; 93.8%), intrinsic AKI accounted for 5 cases (6.3%) and no post-renal AKI was identified. Most cases were KDIGO stage 1 (57; 71.3%). In bivariable analysis, sepsis (OR 6.33 [95% CI 2.05–19.52]; p  < 0.001), hypovolaemia (OR 2.81 [95% CI 1.26–2.65]; p  = 0.015), shock (OR 4.33 [95% CI 0.89–21.09]; p  = 0.050) and cardiac disease (OR 3.67 [95% CI 1.07–13.87]; p  = 0.043) were associated with AKI. Neither nephrotoxic drug exposure nor comorbidities were associated. After adjustment, sepsis (aOR 5.65 [95% CI 1.75–18.20]; p  = 0.004) and cardiac disease (aOR 4.18 [95% CI 1.08–16.16]; p  = 0.038) remained associated with AKI. Conclusion More than one in three adults admitted to these wards developed AKI, predominantly pre-renal and of mild severity, and sepsis and cardiac disease were the only independent determinants identified. Systematic measurement of renal function in septic patients and those with cardiac diseases at admission is a feasible and low-cost intervention in this setting.

title: Nighttime Toothbrushing and Hypertension Among Korean Adults: Exploring the Role of Systemic Inflammation
authorString: Kim M, Lee N, Ahn C, Cho D.
abstractText: Because salivary clearance and antimicrobial defenses decline during sleep, allowing overnight bacterial accumulation and periodontal inflammatory activity, nighttime oral hygiene may be particularly important; however, its association with hypertension remains largely unexplored. We investigated whether nighttime toothbrushing is associated with hypertension, and whether systemic inflammation mediates this association. We analyzed the cross-sectional 2016 to 2023 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES), including 33,224 adults, using survey-weighted analyses. Participants were classified as Night (brushing teeth after dinner or before bedtime) or None. After adjustment for morning and lunch brushing and risk factors, nighttime toothbrushing was associated with lower odds of hypertension (OR, 0.790; 95% CI, 0.686–0.910; P = 0.001). The association was present at both low (OR, 0.830; 95% CI, 0.702–0.982; P = 0.030) and high daytime brushing frequency (OR, 0.710; 95% CI, 0.555–0.908; P = 0.006), with no significant interaction (P for interaction = 0.299). In mediation analysis, the association was partly mediated by white blood cell count (indirect effect, − 0.539 percentage points; 95% bootstrap CI, − 0.837 to − 0.296; P = 0.004). Nighttime toothbrushing was associated with lower odds of hypertension, supported by a WBC-related inflammatory pathway. These findings suggest that nighttime toothbrushing may represent a simple, modifiable behavior warranting further investigation in hypertension.

title: Determinants of disease in Italian patients at the time of their first diagnosis of liver cirrhosis
authorString: Sarcina T, Masarone M, Errigo E, Angeli P, Incicco S, Ponziani FR, Stella L, Costanzo GGD, Angrisani D, Federico A, Dallio M, Pasta A, Caraceni P, Pompili E, Torre P, Morisco F, Ranieri L, Coppola N, Stanzione M, Aghemo A, De Nicola S, Giannini EG, Marco VD, Persico M.
abstractText: Background : The epidemiology, etiologies and clinical presentation of cirrhosis have changed markedly in recent years; however, national-level data remain limited. Aims: To describe the epidemiological profile and metabolic and non-metabolic determinants of cirrhosis in Italy in 2024. Patients and methods: In this cross-sectional, multicentre observational study, 1195 consecutive patients with cirrhosis were enrolled from 11 tertiary hepatology centres across Italy. Eligible participants had a new diagnosis of previously unknown cirrhosis or a previous diagnosis with first evaluation at a participating centre in 2024. Demographic, socioeconomic, etiological, clinical and laboratory data were collected. Metabolic and non-metabolic determinants of cirrhosis were ranked by prevalence using Pareto chart analysis. Results: Among 1195 patients, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) was the most prevalent etiology (321 patients, 26.9%), followed by alcohol-related liver disease (ALD) (269, 22.5%), viral etiologies (263, 22.0%) and other causes (116, 9.7%). Mixed etiologies were identified in 226 patients (18.9%), including Met-ALD, Met-virus, ALD-virus, Met-ALD-virus and PBC-AIH overlap. In the Pareto analysis, arterial hypertension ranked first, followed by type 2 diabetes mellitus, obesity, HCV infection, alcohol abuse and HBV infection. Despite the growing metabolic burden, viral hepatitis remained a major contributor, accounting for 28% of etiologies (137/490) among patients with a previous diagnosis of cirrhosis. Conclusions: Cirrhosis epidemiology in Italy is shifting toward metabolic predominance, with MASLD emerging as the leading etiology. Nevertheless, viral hepatitis remains a substantial contributor. The frequent overlap of etiologies highlights the increasing complexity of cirrhosis management.

title: Vascular Steatosis as a Proposed Mechanism of Metabolic Hypertension: From Arterial Lipid Accumulation to Increased Vascular Resistance
authorString: Andrade LJdO, de Oliveira GCM, Bittencourt AMV, Salles OJdM, Dinamarco N, de Oliveira LM.
abstractText: Introduction: Hypertension remains the leading modifiable determinant of cardiovascular morbidity worldwide. Metabolic disease frequently coexists with elevated pressure, yet no vessel-level lesion has been clearly defined that converts systemic lipid excess into sustained vascular resistance. Objective: We propose vascular steatosis, defined as lipid accumulation within the arterial wall, as a candidate mechanism of metabolic hypertension and test its molecular and genetic support using human arterial transcriptomes and Mendelian randomization. Methods: This in silico study used two public arterial transcriptomes (GSE100927 for discovery, GSE43292 for paired validation). Summary-level Mendelian randomization used GTEx v8 cis-eQTLs from aorta, coronary, and tibial arteries, with whole blood as negative control, and blood pressure statistics from a European-ancestry genome-wide association study. Sensitivity and colocalization analyses followed. Results: Lesioned arteries showed upregulated CD36, ABCA1, and PLIN2, and downregulation of ACTA2, MYH11, and CNN1. Lipid-handling and contractile module scores were inversely associated (β = -0.42; 95% CI, -0.56 to -0.28), including in control arteries (β = -0.38), and the direction replicated in the validation set (β = -0.35). Genetically higher PLIN2 expression in aorta and CD36 expression in coronary artery were associated with higher blood pressure traits (FDR < 0.05); three associations colocalized (PP.H4 ≥ 0.80). Whole blood showed no association. Conclusion: Arterial lipid-handling programs track with loss of the contractile smooth muscle phenotype, and genetically proxied PLIN2 and CD36 expression is associated with blood pressure, which offers a biologically plausible and testable framework for the mechanistic classification of metabolic hypertension. Lipid quantification and physiological validation in resistance arteries are required to establish causal and clinical relevance.

title: Giant High-Grade Myxofibrosarcoma of the Right Thigh Treated by Hip Disarticulation: A Case Report with Imaging–Pathology Correlation
authorString: Ibrahim M, Saif-aldeen M, Alrifai H, Shams-aldeen E, Mohmmed M, Alzain M, Alsir S.
abstractText: Background Myxofibrosarcoma (MFS) is a soft-tissue sarcoma of fibroblastic origin that typically presents as a slowly enlarging, painless mass. High-grade tumors are locally aggressive, and their diagnosis can be delayed by misleading clinical findings and by under-grading on initial biopsy. Case presentation: A 61-year-old man developed a small fatty-type swelling in the muscular region of the right lower limb in February 2024. It was initially diagnosed as a benign fatty cyst and excised in April 2024. The mass recurred and enlarged, and histology of the excised specimen listed liposarcoma, leiomyosarcoma and rhabdomyosarcoma as differential diagnoses. The patient was referred for chemotherapy, which he received only intermittently (seven cycles of MAID/ifosfamide-based chemotherapy in total). Over the following two years the tumor grew to approximately 31 × 25 × 26 cm. CT showed a cystic-solid necrotic mass eroding the femoral cortex and displacing the femoral vessels, with pelvic and inguinal lymphadenopathy and a small right upper-lobe pulmonary nodule. Pre-operative assessment showed rapid atrial fibrillation with a preserved ejection fraction (58%). Because of neurovascular encasement and bone destruction, limb salvage was not feasible, and a radical right hip disarticulation was performed in July 2026. Histopathology confirmed high-grade MFS with approximately 80% viable tumor after chemotherapy, and R0 margins were achieved. The patient received no adjuvant therapy and was in good condition at the time of writing. Conclusion Deep-seated MFS can remain clinically silent until it reaches massive dimensions. Core biopsy of myxoid-rich tumors may under-grade or misclassify the lesion, radiological stability may mask substantial viable tumor after chemotherapy, and radical amputation remains a valid option when neurovascular encasement and bone destruction preclude limb salvage.

title: The intervention effect and mechanism of nebulized levoperilla alcohol on pulmonary hypertension in rats
authorString: Liang X, Huayu M, Liang Z, Guo Y, Li Z, Nan X.
abstractText: Background and Objective : Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a progressive cardiovascular disorder with limited therapeutic options. Nebulized inhalation provides a direct and efficient route for pulmonary drug delivery, which may enhance local efficacy while minimizing systemic adverse effects. Levoperilla alcohol (L-POH), a natural monoterpenoid with antioxidative and anti-inflammatory properties, was evaluated for its therapeutic potential in PH and its involvement in the JAK2-STAT3 signaling pathway. Methods : Forty-eight male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomly divided into six groups, including control, MCT-induced PH, three nebulized L-POH treatment groups (5, 10, and 25 mg/kg), and sildenafil-treated group. PH was induced by MCT injection, followed by 28 days of nebulized L-POH administration. Cardiac function, pulmonary hemodynamics, right ventricular hypertrophy, and pulmonary vascular remodeling were evaluated. The effects of L-POH on the JAK2-STAT3 signaling pathway and related inflammatory, proliferation, and apoptosis-associated proteins were analyzed by Western blotting. Results : MCT administration induced right ventricular dysfunction, pulmonary hypertension, right ventricular hypertrophy, and vascular remodeling. Nebulized L-POH significantly improved cardiac function, reduced pulmonary arterial pressure, attenuated right ventricular hypertrophy, and alleviated pulmonary vascular remodeling. Mechanistically, L-POH inhibited JAK2-STAT3 pathway activation and regulated the expression of inflammation-, proliferation-, and apoptosis-related proteins. Conclusion : L-POH alleviated PH and right heart dysfunction through regulation of the JAK2-STAT3 pathway, highlighting its potential as a novel therapeutic strategy for pulmonary hypertension.

title: His Bundle Pacing via the Atrial Port of a Dual-Chamber ICD: Programming Solution for Undersensing.
authorString: Vo TD, Tran LUP, Nguyen TVK, Kieu ND.
abstractText:
Background

His-bundle pacing connected to the atrial port of a dual-chamber ICD may lead to sensing failure and unsafe pacing.

Case summary

A 67-year-old man with permanent atrial fibrillation, alternating rapid and slow ventricular rates despite medication, symptomatic pauses longer than 6s, and a dual chamber ICD (His lead in the RA port; DF4 lead in the RV port) presented with palpitations. ECG and 24-hour Holter demonstrated intermittent His-channel undersensing with pacing on the T-wave peak. Interrogation showed small His electrograms followed by a prominent, constant ventricular far-field signal on the atrial channel. We turned off far-field protection after V-sense, intentionally used the ventricular far-field signal for sensing of His lead, and disabled related discrimination algorithms.

Conclusion

A dual-chamber ICD with a His-bundle pacing lead may be associated with complex programming challenges, and targeted reprogramming can avoid lead revision or reimplantation.

title: Marshall Vein Ethanol Infusion and Mitral Isthmus Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation With Durable Pulmonary Vein Isolation.
authorString: Kitami Y, Kamakura T, Ikee T, Shako D, Nakamura T, Oka S, Miyazaki Y, Wakamiya A, Ueda N, Nakajima K, Nakasuka K, Wada M, Ishibashi K, Inoue Y, Miyamoto K, Aiba T, Kusano K.
abstractText:
Background

The clinical significance of adding vein of Marshall ethanol infusion (VoM-EI) and mitral isthmus (MI) ablation to left atrial posterior wall isolation (LAPWI) during repeat ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF) despite durable pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) remains unclear. We assessed whether this combined strategy improves sinus rhythm maintenance.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed 80 consecutive patients with AF who underwent repeat ablation despite durable PVI after prior PVI-only procedures and received either LAPWI plus VoM-EI and MI ablation or LAPWI alone.

Results

Of the 80 patients, 27 underwent LAPWI plus VoM-EI and MI ablation (VoM-EI group) and 53 underwent LAPWI alone (control group). During a median follow-up of 591.5 days, freedom from atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence did not differ significantly in the overall cohort on unadjusted analysis but was higher in the VoM-EI group among patients with persistent AF (log-rank p = 0.041). After multivariable adjustment, the combined strategy was associated with a lower risk of atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence in patients with persistent AF (hazard ratio [HR] 0.38; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.14-0.92; p = 0.03) and in the overall cohort (HR 0.37; 95% CI 0.14-0.86; p = 0.02), mainly driven by persistent AF. Propensity score matching showed a similar association (HR 0.29; 95% CI 0.11-0.75; p = 0.01). Major complication rates did not differ between the groups.

Conclusions

In patients with persistent AF despite durable PVI, adding VoM-EI and MI ablation to LAPWI was associated with lower atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence than LAPWI alone. Because the two components were applied together, this finding is hypothesis-generating.

title: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation After Typical Flutter Ablation: Risk-Stratified Monitoring Using Implantable Loop Recorders.
authorString: Singireddy S, Saravanabavanandan R, Coombes K, Ahsan S, Shoura S, Venugopal D, Patel Y, Bajaj S, Shah S, Mehrotra A, Baman TS.
abstractText:
Background

Atrial flutter and atrial fibrillation (AF) arise from a common arrhythmogenic atrial substrate and frequently coexist in the same patient over the course of their lifetime. We aimed to examine the true incidence and risk factors associated with new-onset AF after successful typical atrial flutter ablation in a real-world population.

Methods

We performed a single-center retrospective cohort study of adults who underwent atrial flutter ablation and received an implantable loop recorder (ILR) between 2019 and 2024 as part of a systematic post-ablation monitoring practice. Demographic and clinical variables were collected from the electronic medical record system. Cox proportional-hazards models and multivariable logistic regression were employed to identify independent predictors of AF, while the cumulative incidence of AF was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, and clinically relevant risk thresholds were subsequently derived.

Results

Among 95 patients (mean age 69.5 ± 7.9 years; 77.9% male; mean CHA2DS2-VASc 3.3) followed for a median of 44.7 months (IQR 34.5-49.0), AF was detected in 61 (64.2%). By Kaplan-Meier estimation the cumulative incidence of AF was 30% at 3 months, 46% at 1 year, and 58% at 2 years; the median time to detection among affected patients was 124 days (IQR 13-385). Patients with detected AF had a larger left atrial volume index (LAVI; 35.2 vs. 28.2 mL/m2, p<0.001) and lower LVEF (53.1% vs. 59.6%, p<0.001) as well as higher incidence of heart failure (p = 0.032). LAVI (adjusted OR 1.10 per mL/m2, 95% CI 1.03-1.17; p = 0.006) and a reduced LVEF (≤50%; adjusted OR 9.2, 95% CI 1.9-44.5; p = 0.006) were independent predictors (AUC 0.79), and both remained independent in a Cox model (LAVI adjusted HR 1.04 per mL/m2; LVEF ≤50% adjusted HR 2.2, 95% CI 1.3-3.9). A LAVI threshold of ≥26 mL/m2 functioned as a rule-out (sensitivity 92%), whereas LVEF ≤50% functioned as a rule-in (specificity 94%, PPV 92%); no single threshold or combination achieved both high sensitivity and high specificity. On stratified analysis the 2-year cumulative incidence of AF was 70% versus 20% above and below the LAVI threshold (log-rank p<0.001) and 73% versus 53% by the LVEF threshold (p = 0.001).

Conclusions

Continuous post-ablation monitoring revealed AF in roughly two-thirds of patients after flutter ablation, often emerging several months following the procedure. More advanced atrial remodeling and impaired ventricular function were independent predictors of higher risk, providing practical and accessible thresholds to guide clinical decisions about which patients warrant prolonged rhythm surveillance and anticoagulation reinitiation after flutter ablation.

title: A plant-based diet attenuates hypertension-induced renal and hepatic stress: an exploratory study.
authorString: Najjar RS, Jarrell ZR, McCarthy C, Lu W, Lim G, Go YM, Ziegler TR, Wang S, Feresin RG, Wainford RD, Gewirtz AT.
abstractText: Hypertension drives progressive renal dysfunction and hepatic injury. In this secondary analysis, we investigated whether a plant-based diet (PBD) could prevent and/or reverse hypertension-induced renal and hepatic insult. Four-week-old female spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHRs) consumed a refined control diet or PBD comprising 28% fruits, vegetables, nuts and legumes, while normotensive Wistar-Kyoto rats consumed the control diet. After 24 weeks, a subset of control-fed SHRs switched to PBD for 12 weeks. Despite sustained hypertension, exploratory analyses indicated that PBD may reduce serum urea during prevention (3.84 ± 1.12 vs. 3.03 ± 0.80 mmol L-1; P = 0.0263) and treatment (4.37 ± 1.80 vs. 3.11 ± 0.93 mmol L-1; P = 0.0248). Estimated glomerular filtration rate may also improve during treatment (1319 ± 277 vs. 1599 ± 432 µL min-1; P = 0.0488). However, this did not reach significance during the prevention phase (P = 0.0518). PBD prevented and reversed elevations in serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT; prevention: 32.61 ± 3.23 vs. 22.50 ± 3.52 U L-1; treatment: 33.34 ± 2.87 vs. 24.48 ± 3.99 U L-1; both P < 0.0001). Further, PBD increased renal antioxidant enzyme expression and reduced hepatic tumor necrosis factor-α during prevention. Qualitatively, PBD may attenuate left kidney glomerular collagen accumulation. These findings warrant additional translational studies testing minimally refined PBDs, with potential pilot clinical studies as an adjunctive therapy in adults with hypertension.

title: Diabetic retinopathy in pregnancy.
authorString: Skaria M, Jacob S.

journal.title: Current opinion in endocrinology, diabetes, and obesity

abstractText:
Purpose of review

Pregnancy is associated with an increased risk of development and progression of diabetic retinopathy. This review examines the mechanisms underlying diabetic retinopathy progression during pregnancy, established and emerging risk factors for diabetic retinopathy progression, current screening strategies, and management options for sight-threatening disease.

Recent findings

The severity of retinopathy at conception, glycaemic control, duration of diabetes and hypertension are established predictors of diabetic retinopathy progression during pregnancy. Recent data suggest that patients with no retinopathy on initial screening have a very low risk of diabetic retinopathy progression, and further screening may not be indicated during pregnancy in this cohort. Pan retinal photocoagulation remains the mainstay of treatment for sight-threatening proliferative disease, while the use of intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy remains challenging because of limited safety data. Evidence regarding the postpartum course of diabetic retinopathy remains limited.

Summary

Pregnancy represents a period of increased retinal risk in women with preexisting diabetes, although this risk is not uniform. Baseline retinopathy status, duration of diabetes, extent of glycaemic control and hypertensive disease may provide a framework for future risk-stratified screening. Further prospective studies are required to determine whether surveillance can safely be individualised, and to clarify the role of anti-VEGF therapy and postpartum monitoring.

title: Employment and life participation in patients with kidney disease: a narrative review.
authorString: Lyons TM, Cavanaugh KL, Pappadis MR, Erickson KF.

journal.title: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension

abstractText:
Purpose of review

People living with kidney disease consistently rank employment and the ability to participate in life activities among their most important outcomes, yet employment among working-aged U.S. patients at dialysis initiation has remained at 20-24% for more than two decades. This review synthesizes recent evidence on why patients with kidney disease stop working and what may help them remain employed.

Recent findings

Job loss begins well before dialysis: only about one-third of working-aged U.S. patients are employed 6 months before starting dialysis, and employment is lowest among patients receiving in-center hemodialysis, recovering only partially after transplantation. Employment is associated with better survival, greater access to transplantation, improved mental health, social connectedness, and protection from illness-related financial insecurity. Patients stop working for multiple reasons, including symptoms, treatment time and travel, employer inflexibility, and benefit structures that penalize work. Flexible dialysis options (home dialysis, evening shifts), psychosocial support, exercise, and vocational rehabilitation may help patients remain employed.

Summary

Employment is a modifiable, patient-prioritized outcome. Restoring patient-level employment reporting in national registries and directly testing employment-focused interventions in kidney disease are priorities for research and quality improvement.

title: Why scale alone is not enough: innovation dynamics in single-centre vs. multicentre kidney paired donation.
authorString: AlMeshari K, Broering D, Ali T.

journal.title: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension

abstractText:
Purpose of review

Kidney paired donation (KPD) has become an established strategy for overcoming immunological barriers to kidney transplantation. Although regional, national, and international registries have expanded donor pools and transplant opportunities, successful KPD depends on more than scale alone. This review examines the evolution of KPD delivery models and the complementary roles of multicentre and mature single-centre programs.

Recent findings

Multicentre KPD programs have facilitated increasingly complex exchanges through larger donor pools, advanced matching algorithms, and international collaboration. However, challenges remain, including logistical complexity, financial barriers, inter-centre variability in immunological assessment, and reduced access for highly sensitized and blood group O recipients. Emerging evidence from experienced single-centre programs demonstrates that standardized human leukocyte antigen (HLA) assessment, integrated multidisciplinary decision-making, and innovative matching strategies - including compatible pair participation, selective HLA- and ABO-incompatible transplantation, and complex exchange chains - can safely expand transplant opportunities while maintaining excellent outcomes.

Summary

Multicentre registries are essential for maximizing donor pool size and equitable access to transplantation. However, mature single-centre programs provide an integrated environment that promotes innovation, standardized immunological assessment, and rapid implementation of novel matching strategies. Future KPD systems should combine the scale of national registries with the expertise, flexibility, and innovation of experienced single-centre programs.

title: Peritoneal dialysis catheter dysfunction: when can the catheter be rescued?
authorString: McMonagle E, Jain AK.

journal.title: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension

abstractText:
Purpose of review

Peritoneal dialysis (PD) catheter dysfunction is frequently treated as a generic access failure, although the appropriate response depends on the underlying mechanism. This review summarizes a practical, mechanism-directed approach to reversible medical causes, image-guided salvage, surgical revision, and catheter replacement.

Recent findings

Recent guidelines and reviews support early exclusion of infection and acute abdominal pathology, deliberate treatment of constipation and fibrin, and early abdominal radiography when flow is impaired. Catheterography and fluoroscopic manipulation can restore selected migrated or partially obstructed catheters. Still, immediate technical success does not ensure durable function when omental wrap, adhesions, fixed kinking, or unfavorable catheter geometry is present. Observational series also support same-session removal and reinsertion for noninfectious mechanical failure and for narrowly selected infection-related indications. Laparoscopic revision remains the definitive treatment for structural abnormalities.

Summary

A successful PD access program requires a written rescue pathway that quickly transitions from reversible causes to mechanism-specific interventions. The meaningful outcome is not radiographic catheter position alone, but rapid return to the prescribed PD regimen while minimizing temporary hemodialysis exposure, repeated emergency visits, and avoidable technique failure.

title: Maternal Microvascular Calcium Sparks Are Reduced in Preeclampsia.
authorString: Parnell LC, Tierney AL, Cottrell EC, Pritchard HAT, Smith MN, Krakowiak K, Unwin RD, Gurney AM, Myers JE, Greenstein A, Worton SA.
abstractText:
Background

Maternal microvascular dysfunction is a hallmark of the hypertensive pregnancy disorder preeclampsia, but the mechanism(s) have not been fully defined. Within vascular smooth muscle cells, the principal pressure-induced vasodilatory pathway depends on localized Ca2+-release events from the sarcoplasmic reticulum ryanodine receptors (Ca2+ sparks), which stimulate BKCa (large-conductance Ca2+-activated potassium channels) to cause spontaneous transient outward currents and vasorelaxation. Here, the Ca2+ sparks-BKCa axis is assessed in preeclampsia for the first time.

Methods

Pressurized omental resistance arteries from normotensive pregnant women and women with preeclampsia were imaged by high-speed spinning-disk laser confocal microscopy to assess Ca2+ sparks (20-110 mm Hg) and caffeine-evoked Ca2+ release (10 mmol/L; 80 mm Hg). Electrophysiology was used to assess spontaneous transient outward currents (-60 to 0 mV) and BKCa currents (-100 to +100 mV) in isolated vascular smooth muscle cells. A liquid chromatography-selected reaction monitoring-tandem mass spectrometry assay measured SERCA2 (sarcoplasmic/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase-2) and unphosphorylated/phosphorylated proteoforms of regulatory PLN (phospholamban). Vasoactive effects of the BKCa-dependent vasorelaxant HBD2 (human β-defensin-2; 0.01-10 nmol/L) were assessed by wire myography.

Results

In microvascular arteries from women with preeclampsia, there was reduced Ca2+ spark frequency (P=1.1×10-10) and spontaneous transient outward current frequency (P=0.023). There was also reduced sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ release in response to caffeine (P=0.0013), reduced sarcoplasmic reticulum refilling (P=2.0×10-4), and decreased ratio of SERCA2 to inhibitory unphosphorylated PLN (P=0.030), implicating increased SERCA2 inhibition. HBD2 (0.01-10 nmol/L) caused BKCa-dependent relaxation (P=4.6×10-10) of omental arteries without affecting Ca2+ spark frequency.

Conclusions

In microvascular arteries from women with preeclampsia, there is a striking reduction in Ca2+ spark frequency and spontaneous transient outward currents, likely secondary to increased inhibition of SERCA2 by unphosphorylated PLN and reduced sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ load. These defects may provide novel therapeutic targets to restore physiological control of the vasculature. BKCa-mediated relaxation by HBD2 was independent of Ca2+ sparks, supporting vasodilatory strategies bypassing disrupted microvascular mechanisms in preeclampsia.

title: Shared Genetics of Hypertension and Preeclampsia Converges on Immune Regulation.
authorString: Farahat MA, Abbas M, Melese M, Gaye A.
abstractText:
Background

Hypertension and preeclampsia are clinically distinct, yet biologically related conditions characterized by vascular dysfunction and elevated cardiovascular risk. Although genome-wide association studies have identified loci associated with blood pressure traits and preeclampsia, the functional mechanisms linking shared variants to gene regulation and clinical phenotypes remain unclear.

Methods

We integrated genome-wide association study summary statistics for hypertension, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, and preeclampsia to identify shared variants (P≤1×10-4). Cis-expression quantitative trait loci analyses were performed in whole blood using RNA sequencing data from 180 Black women. Significant associations (false discovery rate ≤0.05) were evaluated for replication across vascular, metabolic, and endocrine tissues in the Genotype-Tissue Expression project. Associations between gene expression and blood pressure traits were also assessed.

Results

We identified 4792 shared genome-wide association study variants, of which 4663 were tested in expression quantitative trait loci analyses, yielding 1837 significant variant-gene associations across 78 genes. Replication in the Genotype-Tissue Expression project confirmed 645 associations involving 24 genes, many showing cross-tissue regulatory effects. Three genes (C4B, HLA-C, and HLA-DQB1) demonstrated convergent evidence across genome-wide association study, gene regulation, and expression-trait analyses. C4B expression was positively associated with hypertension and systolic blood pressure, while HLA-C showed negative associations with hypertension, systolic blood pressure, and diastolic blood pressure. HLA-DQB1 expression was specifically associated with diastolic blood pressure, suggesting trait-specific effects.

Conclusions

These findings highlight immune-related pathways as key mediators linking hypertension and preeclampsia. Integrating genetic, transcriptomic, and phenotypic data provides a framework for identifying functionally relevant loci and advancing mechanistic insights into cardiometabolic and pregnancy-related disorders.

title: KLHL3-Cab39 Disruption Drives WNK4-Independent Hyperkalemic Hypertension.
authorString: Lin SH, Chen YC, Ding YX, Cheng CJ, Liu PY, Lin YL, Ding JJ, Sung CC, Yang SS, Lee HJ, Lin CM.
abstractText:
Background

Familial hyperkalemic hypertension, also known as pseudohypoaldosteronism type II (PHAII), is characterized by hypertension and hyperkalemic metabolic acidosis and involves dysregulation of the KLHL3 (Kelch-like 3)-cullin3 E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, affecting WNK1/4 (with-no-lysine kinase 1/4)-mediated SPAK (Ste20-related proline/alanine-rich kinase)/OSR1 (oxidative stress response kinase 1)-NCC (Na+-Cl- cotransporter) signaling. How KLHL3 phosphorylation mutations modulate this pathway remains poorly defined.

Methods

We generated knock-in mouse models expressing phosphomimetic (S486D) or phosphodefective (S486G) mutations at Klhl3 S486 (homologous to human S433). Blood pressure, serum and urine biochemistries, immunoblotting, immunofluorescence, coimmunoprecipitation, in vitro ubiquitination assays, and molecular docking were performed. Klhl3 S486G mice were crossed with Wnk4-/- mice to test WNK4 dependence.

Results

Both knock-in strains exhibited typical PHAII features despite unchanged KLHL3 levels, with enhanced SPAK/OSR1-NCC phosphorylation, increased Cab39 levels, and unchanged WNK1/4 expression. Under high-salt loading, Klhl3 S486 knock-in mice maintained severe PHAII phenotypes, with persistently elevated Cab39 and NCC levels despite decreased WNK4 expression. Critically, Wnk4 deletion failed to rescue PHAII phenotypes in Klhl3 S486G mice, demonstrating that Klhl3 S486 mutations drive PHAII independently of WNK4. In vitro, human KLHL3 S433D/S433G mutations reduced KLHL3-Cab39 association and Cab39 ubiquitination, with a corresponding increase in Cab39 abundance. Deletion mapping identified KLHL3 residues 428 to 437 and Cab39 residues 314 to 324 as key determinants of the KLHL3-Cab39 association.

Conclusions

These findings indicate that the integrity of Ser486 itself, rather than its phosphorylation state, is required for KLHL3-mediated Cab39 ubiquitination and define a WNK4-independent PHAII mechanism driven by impaired Cab39 degradation and consequent SPAK/OSR1-Na+-Cl- cotransporter activation.

title: Cost-effectiveness of pulsed field ablation of atrial fibrillation: a primer.
authorString: Qeska D, Cheung CC, Wijeysundera HC.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

Catheter ablation is increasingly used as a primary or first-line rhythm-control strategy in the treatment of atrial fibrillation (AF). Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is an emerging catheter ablation modality that offers comparable clinical effectiveness as thermal ablation whilst avoiding safety events related to thermal injury and improving procedural efficiency. PFA may be associated with increased equipment costs. Cost-effectiveness analyses (CEA) help inform adoption of newer technologies such as PFA within healthcare systems with limited resources.

Recent findings

Accordingly, our review provides a primer for CEA and examines the evidence for PFA. Recent studies have demonstrated that PFA is at least as effective as conventional thermal ablation (radiofrequency or cryoballoon) in treating AF and may be an effective first-line rhythm control therapy. PFA is associated with shorter procedural times which increases throughput and may help to offset higher equipment costs.

Summary

Preliminary work suggests that PFA is likely cost-effective but findings must be interpreted with caution as there are a limited number of CEA and follow-up was generally limited to 1 year post ablation. Additional CEA across healthcare jurisdictions with longer time horizons are required to confirm these findings and may inform uptake of PFA.

title: Association between migraine and angiogenic biomarkers in women with suspected or confirmed hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
authorString: Al-Hassany L, Bruijn NRA, Saleh L, Neümañ RI, van der Arend BWH, Kluivers ACM, Terwindt GM, Visser W, Danser AHJ, MaassenVanDenBrink A.

journal.title: Cephalalgia : an international journal of headache

abstractText: AimMigraine is associated with increased odds of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP). Elevated soluble Fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFlt-1), decreased placental growth factor (PlGF), and upregulated sFlt-1/PlGF ratios are biomarkers of preeclampsia-related complications. Our primary objective was to examine the effect of migraine on sFlt-1, PlGF, and their ratio within subgroups of women with different HDP diagnoses. Our secondary objective was to evaluate the interrelationship between migraine and these biomarkers in the overall cohort with suspected or confirmed HDP.MethodsWe evaluated pregnant women with suspected or confirmed HDP in whom sFlt-1, PlGF and their ratio were measured during index pregnancy. Migraine diagnoses before/during index pregnancy were retrospectively assessed according to ICHD-3 criteria. Both, descriptive and adjusted analyses were performed, comparing women with and without migraine. For the latter analyses, linear regression analyses were conducted for the log-transformed sFlt-1 levels, PlGF levels and their ratio, while adjusting for gestational age, maternal age, and smoking status.ResultsAmong 234 women (mean age 32 years, SD = 5), 91 had (a history of) migraine. No significant association between migraine and the log-transformed biomarkers was observed in women with and without migraine across HDP groups, also when adjusting for confounding factors (adjusted estimates of the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio: β = -0.2 [95% CI: -1.0-0.6] for women with preeclampsia or hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme levels, and low platelet levels syndrome, β = -0.8 [95% CI: -2.0-0.4] for gestational hypertension, and β = -0.1 [95% CI: -0.7-0.4] for those without HDP). Secondary analyses showed that, when pooling the overall study population, women with migraine had lower sFlt-1 levels and sFlt-1/PlGF ratios compared to women without migraine. Adjusted analyses in the overall study population instead showed that migraine was not associated with significant changes in log sFlt-1 levels (β = -0.2 [95% CI: -0.5-0.04]), but rather with higher log PlGFs levels (β = 0.3 [95% CI: 0.03-0.6]) and lower log sFlt-1/PlGF ratios (β = -0.5 [95% CI: -1.0 - -0.08]).ConclusionsResults of this study do not support enhanced angiogenic imbalance by migraine status within HDP groups. As a consequence, interpretation of sFlt-1 and PlGF might not require modification according to migraine status within different HDP diagnoses. The findings observed in the overall cohort require cautious interpretation; whether migraine influences magnitude of angiogenic dysregulation warrants prospective investigation.

title: Are high flow arteriovenous fistulas necessary?
authorString: Alawattegama LH, Patel K, Inston N.
abstractText: Arteriovenous fistulas are the preferred vascular access for haemodialysis but may develop excessive flow. High-flow arteriovenous fistulas (HFAs) are common in practice, although their prevalence is difficult to establish because definitions and management strategies remain inconsistent. HFAs are associated with systemic complications, including high-output cardiac failure, left ventricular hypertrophy and pulmonary hypertension and local complications including ischaemia, dialysis inefficiency, aneurysmal degeneration and venous stenosis or occlusion. Assessment and management remain poorly defined, particularly in patients with mild or subclinical disease. This narrative review provides an updated overview of the definition, pathophysiology, clinical consequences, assessment and management of HFAs, with particular emphasis on continuing areas of uncertainty.

title: Increasing use of SGLT-2 inhibitors among patients with heart failure.
authorString: Hoppe N, Haugh S, Umbreit A, Morlock M, Sathre J, Johnson J, Machacek K, Hinderaker K, Al-Anii A, Bates A.

journal.title: JAAPA : official journal of the American Academy of Physician Assistants

abstractText:
Objective

The objective of this quality improvement project was to identify and address barriers contributing to the underutilization of sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT-2) inhibitors in eligible patients with heart failure across the health system.

Methods

The heart failure registry was used to identify the prescription percentage of SGLT-2 inhibitors pre- and postintervention. Interventions to increase prescribing included pharmacist education to primary care providers and use of a cost information handout.

Results

Following the intervention, SGLT-2 inhibitor prescription for eligible patients improved from 7.1% (n = 630) to 9.0% (n = 814), representing a relative increase of 26.8% from baseline.

Conclusion

A multimodal approach involving pharmacy and primary care effectively increased SGLT-2 inhibitor prescribing in patients with heart failure. Physician associates, a key part of the primary care workforce, play an important role initiating guideline-directed medical therapy.

title: M6A-modified lncRNA RMRP facilitates mitophagy and promotes ox-LDL-induced endothelial cell injury by interacting with PTBP1 and activating the PI3K/AKT pathway.
authorString: Fu Y, Zhang Z, Yu Y, Chai Y, Hao J, Qiao Q.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Biochim Biophys Acta Gene Regul Mech
journal.title: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Gene regulatory mechanisms
journal.isoabbreviation: Biochim Biophys Acta Gene Regul Mech

abstractText:
Background

Endothelial cell dysfunction has been identified as a major risk factor for atherosclerosis. The long non-coding RNA (LncRNA) RNA component of mitochondrial RNA processing endoribonuclease (RMRP) has been detected in mitochondria and is closely associated with inflammation and autophagy. However, the role of the lncRNA RMRP in endothelial cell injury and its potential molecular mechanisms remain unclear.

Methods

Mouse aortic endothelial cells (MAECs) were treated with oxidised low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL). Changes in cell viability, proinflammatory cytokine levels, mitophagy, and mitochondrial membrane potential in MAECs were assessed to investigate the effects of lncRNA RMRP and protein kinase B (AKT3) on endothelial injury. Knockdown and overexpression experiments were performed to determine the effects of lncRNA RMRP, polypyrimidine tract-binding protein 1 (PTBP1), and AKT3 on MAECs stimulated with ox-LDL.

Results

Ox-LDL markedly reduced cell viability, increased proinflammatory factor levels, induced mitophagy, and reduced mitochondrial membrane potential in MAECs. Knockdown of lncRNA RMRP attenuated ox-LDL-induced inflammatory responses and mitophagy in MAECs. Knockdown of Methyltransferase-like 14 (METTL14) suppressed the expression of lncRNA RMRP through m6A modification in ox-LDL-treated MAECs. LncRNA RMRP enhanced AKT3 mRNA stability by interacting with PTBP1. LncRNA RMRP promoted ox-LDL-induced mitophagy by targeting AKT3 and stimulating the Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/AKT pathway in MAECs.

Conclusion

METTL14 regulates the expression of lncRNA RMRP through m6A modification. Overexpressed lncRNA RMRP targets AKT3 by recruiting PTBP1, thus activating the PI3K/AKT pathway to mediate mitophagy and promote the progression of atherosclerosis.

title: LEFT BUNDLE BRANCH AREA PACING IN A POST TRANSPLANT HEART WITH MILD LV DYSFUNCTION- A CASE REPORT.
authorString: Thomas A, Gopi A, Muhammed Musthafa PP, Sundaram S.
abstractText: Left bundle branch pacing (LBBP) is increasingly used as a physiological alternative to right ventricular pacing, with stable thresholds and synchronized left ventricular activation. Its use in a transplanted heart is rarely described, and data on conduction system pacing in this setting is limited. We describe a 38-year-old woman who developed complete atrioventricular dissociation with a wide, LBBB-morphology escape rhythm immediately after orthotopic cardiac transplantation performed for peripartum cardiomyopathy with biventricular dysfunction. Baseline echocardiography showed global LV hypokinesia with an ejection fraction of 45%. Given high-grade AV block with LV dysfunction, we implanted a left bundle branch optimized dual-chamber pacemaker. The paced QRS showed a right bundle branch delay pattern with left axis deviation, in keeping with left posterior fascicular capture, and thresholds remained low and stable at follow-up. The patient has done well since, with a ventricular pacing burden of 100%, no device-related complications, and recovery of LV ejection fraction from 45% to 60% on serial echocardiography. As far as we are aware, this is the first reported instance of left bundle branch pacing in a post-transplant heart. The case suggests that LBBP is feasible in the transplanted heart and may support recovery of LV function even when the heart is denervated, though longer follow-up and further cases will be needed to confirm this. Written informed consent was obtained from the patient for publication of this report and the accompanying images.

title: Reversible cardiomyopathy due to ventricular arrhythmias in a |highly unusual syndrome. A novel phenotypical presentation.
authorString: Pellizzón OA, Nannini S, Vago LI, Blassi F.
abstractText: We present a 16-year-old female with multisystemic disorder characterized by cutaneous hyperpigmentation, hypertrichosis, hepatosplenomegaly, hearing loss, heart anomalies, hypogonadism, low height (short stature), hyperglycemia and hallux valgus and pathogenic variant in SLC29A3 gene (encoding the human equilibrate nucleoside transporter (hENT3), was referred for evaluation due to recurrent non-sustained pleomorphic ventricular tachycardia refractory to amiodarone and catheter ablation. Two-dimensional echocardiography and cardiac magnetic resonance with late-gadolinium enhancement showed reduced biventricular ejection fraction without signs of inflammation or fibrosis. The administration of propranolol and flecainide controlled her ventricular arrhythmias and improved ventricular function. To our knowledge, this the first time that this arrhythmic phenotype has been demonstrated in this unusual syndrome presenting probably as a cardiomyopathy secondary to recurrent non-sustained pleomorphic ventricular tachycardia that was reversed with administration of flecainide and propranolol.

title: Numerical simulation of electroosmotic blood flow through progressive stenotic artery with a catheter under the joule heating and magnetic field effects.
authorString: Keshari A, Yadav S.
abstractText: Atherosclerosis, a condition causing the narrowing of the arteries, is a major contributor to the development of cardiovascular diseases. This emphasizes the importance of examining the rheological behavior of blood flow through such arteries. The mathematical model serves as a framework to gain an understanding of the flow and thermal properties of blood. Thus, we employed a non-Newtonian Bingham-Papanastasiou model to explore the hemodynamics of blood through a catheterized stenotic artery, which is inclined with a progressively irregular stenosis geometry, incorporating the integrated influence of electroosmosis, thermal radiation, a magnetic field, and Joule heating, providing new insights into blood flow dynamics. The equations are solved numerically using an explicit finite difference method and visualized using MATLAB software by plotting velocity, wall shear stress, flow rate, resistance to flow, and temperature profiles. Results show that the axial velocity decreases by 36.66% with increasing catheter radius from 0.1 to 0.3, which can lead to insufficient blood supply. The axial velocity is seen to increase by 42.41% on increasing the electroosmotic parameter from 2 to 3.5, while the reduction in resistance reaches 30.85%. The streamline analysis reveals that increasing the Helmholtz-Smoluchowski velocity stabilizes the flow, while higher stenosis depth enhances the flow disturbance. The temperature is also seen to increase by 34.01% when Joule heating increases from 0 to 4. Thus, our study examines the blood flow behavior and its thermal properties providing useful insight into various medical applications.

title: Chest Radiotherapy Associated Cardiotoxicity: An Update.
authorString: Agarwal R, Gonzales-Uribe AG, Zhang L.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

Chest radiotherapy has improved cancer survival in various thoracic malignancies, including breast cancer, Hodgkin lymphoma, and lung cancer. However, inadvertent radiation exposure to the heart is associated with a broad spectrum of cardiovascular toxicities, collectively termed radiation-induced heart disease (RIHD). We aim to review the pathophysiology of RIHD and the current evidence for their incidence, risk factors, clinical management, and prevention strategies.

Recent findings

RIHD is mediated by oxidative stress, DNA damage, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and progressive fibrosis, leading to accelerated atherosclerosis, myocardial stiffening, valvular degeneration, pericardial disease, and arrhythmias. The risk, timing, and severity of cardiovascular complications are influenced by radiation dose and distribution, age at exposure, baseline cardiovascular risk, and concomitant cardiotoxic therapies. While younger patients may experience prolonged latency before clinical disease onset, older individuals and those with pre-existing cardiovascular disease often develop complications earlier, reflecting radiation-mediated acceleration of underlying pathology. This review summarizes the epidemiology, latency, clinical presentation, surveillance strategies, and management of the different forms of RIHD. It also discusses contemporary approaches to risk mitigation, including advances in radiation delivery techniques, aggressive cardiovascular risk factor modification, lifestyle interventions, and emerging pharmacologic strategies.

title: Tunable Magnetorheological Elastomer Substrates for Studying Mechano-Genetic Interactions in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
authorString: Kargar Gaz Kooh Y, Sun Y, Malayath G, Hayem L, Bahmani B, Devi ND, Jiang H, Long F, Cresci S, Genin GM, Huebsch N.
abstractText: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is the most common inherited cardiac disease. While sarcomeric genomic variants drive HCM, a role for mechanical stress in disease pathogenesis is increasingly appreciated. However, existing  in vitro models of HCM rely on model systems (e.g., hydrogels) with static mechanical properties, precluding investigation of how dynamic mechanical loading interacts with genetic susceptibility during disease initiation. Here, we leveraged a dynamically tunable magnetorheological elastomer (MRE) platform to model progressive mechanical stiffening in order to study mechano-genetic interactions in human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC) derived cardiomyocytes harboring an HCM-associated MYBPC3 frameshift (  MYBPC3 fs) loss-of-function variant. Dynamic stiffening selectively unmasked pathological structural remodeling in  MYBPC3 fs cardiomyocytes while producing only modest changes in isogenic controls, suggesting that  MYBPC3 fs confers heightened mechanosensitivity. In  MYBPC3 fs cardiomyocytes, mechanical stiffening drove hypertrophic remodeling, sarcomere disorganization, nuclear remodeling, dysregulated NFAT3 signaling, and aberrant cell-cycle activity. MRE stiffening also drove fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition in primary cardiac fibroblasts, recapitulating early fibrotic remodeling. Together, these findings position dynamically tunable MRE substrates as a human-relevant platform for dissecting mechano-genetic disease mechanisms and evaluating therapies targeting mechanotransduction pathways in HCM.

title: Genome-Wide Transcriptomics Uncovers a Lung-to-Aorta Inflammatory Program Driving Influenza-Induced Atherosclerosis Exacerbation
authorString: DeVito L, Notaro JC, Constantinesco NJ, Rajasundaram D, Alcorn JF, Gopal R.
abstractText:
SUMMARY

Influenza infection increases cardiovascular risk in individuals with pre-existing atherosclerosis, yet the genome-wide transcriptional basis of this association remains undefined. We performed bulk RNA sequencing of aorta and lung tissues from high-fat diet-fed Apoe −/− mice infected with influenza A/PR/8/34 versus PBS-treated controls at day 15 post-infection, identifying 6,828 differentially expressed genes across both tissues (5,694 in the lung and 1,134 in the aorta; adjusted p < 0.05).
