title: Clinical Outcomes of Contemporary Frozen Elephant Trunk Prostheses and the Ascyrus Medical Dissection Stent in Aortic Arch Surgery: A Systematic Review and Proportional Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Jubouri M, Surkhi AO, Chikhal R, Alaraj RSN, Hammad A, Jubouri YF, Bokobza De la Rosa MD, Halaseh N, Mohammed I, Bailey DM, Williams IM, Bashir M.
abstractText:
Introduction

The frozen elephant trunk (FET) technique is an established strategy for complex aortic arch and descending thoracic aortic pathology. Several covered FET prostheses are available, while the Ascyrus Medical Dissection Stent (AMDS) represents a distinct uncovered hybrid arch adjunct used principally during open repair of acute type A dissection. This systematic review evaluated the reported clinical and aortic outcomes of contemporary FET prostheses and the AMDS.

Methods

MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus and Web of Science were searched from inception to January 2025 in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and the Cochrane Handbook. Random-effects proportional meta-analysis and exploratory study-level meta-regression were undertaken for Thoraflex, E-vita, Frozenix and Cronus, with the AMDS retained as a separate device stratum. Results were reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

Results

A total of 114 studies encompassing 13,051 patients were included. Pooled all-cause mortality over the reported follow-up was 13.2% (95% CI 11.2-15.7%), while combined 30-day/in-hospital mortality was 8.4% (95% CI 7.4-9.5%), ranging from 5.1% to 14.5% across device strata. Five-year survival was 80.0% (95% CI 75.6-83.8%). Permanent neurological deficit ranged from 4.0% to 8.8%, and spinal cord ischaemia or paraplegia ranged from 0% to 7.0%. The pooled reintervention rate was 12.7% (95% CI 10.6-15.2%). Distal stent-induced new entry ranged from 0% to 8.9%, and endoleak ranged from 3.2% to 7.5%. Both clinical and statistical heterogeneity was substantial for several outcomes, and the device strata differed materially in pathology, urgency, age, operative strategy, and follow-up.

Conclusion

Contemporary FET prostheses and the AMDS were associated with broadly acceptable reported outcomes within their respective clinical settings. However, the predominantly observational evidence, heterogeneous case mix and differing device indications preclude definitive conclusions regarding comparative superiority. The pooled values should be used as descriptive benchmarks. Device selection should therefore be individualised according to aortic pathology, anatomy, operative urgency and institutional expertise. Prospective comparative studies using standardised outcome definitions and appropriate risk adjustment are required.

title: Targeting PLN-R14del cardiomyopathy in mice using DWORF gene therapy suggests the necessity of high expression levels.
authorString: Stege NM, Shi C, Dokter MM, de Boer RA, Silljé HHW.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
journal.title: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
journal.isoabbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol

abstractText: There is currently no successful treatment for patients with cardiomyopathy caused by the p.Arg14del mutation in the phospholamban (PLN) gene, other than heart transplantation. Interestingly, transgenic overexpression of the small peptide Dwarf open reading frame (DWORF) could delay disease development and extend life span in a PLN-R14del cardiomyopathy mouse model. Here, we evaluated the potential of DWORF gene therapy using adeno-associated virus cardiotropic serotype 9 (AAV9) in a PLN-R14del mouse model. At postnatal day 7, AAV9-cTnT-DWORF (AAV-DWORF) or control AAV9-cTnT-luciferase (AAV-luciferase) was delivered to homozygous PLN-R14del (R14<sup>Δ/Δ</sup>) mice. The AAV-DWORF construct targeted the majority of cardiomyocytes in the heart, as shown by in situ RNA labeling. Moreover, it significantly increased DWORF protein expression by fivefold, but did not reach the same high 25-fold increased expression level as observed in a DWORF transgenic mice. Previous study showed that high transgenic DWORF expression was able to delay PLN-R14del cardiac impairment and preserved cardiac ejection fraction (EF) in 6-week-old mice. However, the current study reveals that AAV-DWORF did not delay the decline in EF of R14<sup>Δ/Δ</sup> mice. This was corroborated by the observation that the R14<sup>Δ/Δ</sup>-induced increase of heart failure markers and cardiac fibrosis were not inhibited by AAV-DWORF. In conclusion, whereas high transgenic DWORF overexpression can delay cardiac dysfunction in a PLN-R14del mouse model, a fivefold lower AAV-mediated overexpression was not sufficient to delay disease progression. This suggests that only high supraphysiological DWORF levels are able to delay disease development, requiring further optimization of AAV-DWORF therapy.

title: Circulating Lipids, Statins, and Metformin in Thoracic and Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Rodríguez-Palomares JF, Ródenas-Alesina E, Tomasino M, Belahnech Y, Mehmood A, Soriano-Colomé T, Olivella A, Oristrell G, Fresno SD, Videla LS, Soldevilla RO, Galian-Gay L, Orchanian-Cheff A, Foroutan F, Guala A, Dux-Santoy L, Teixidó-Tura G, Ferreira-González I.
abstractText: Thoracic and abdominal aortic aneurysms (TAA and AAA) progress silently, and no drug has been shown to slow their growth. Circulating lipids, statins, and metformin are candidate disease modifiers, but the evidence is heterogeneous and largely observational. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to 24 March 2025, with an update of MEDLINE to 3 October 2026, for randomized and cohort studies of adults with established AAA or TAA. Aneurysm growth was standardized to mm/year and pooled with random-effects models when at least three comparable studies were available. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed with ROBINS-I and GRADE. Thirty-three studies were included, 32 observational and one randomized; fewer than 20% of participants were women. Circulating lipid fractions showed no consistent association with aneurysm growth. Statin use was associated with slower growth (mean difference -0.78 mm/year; 95% CI -1.13 to -0.43; I2 = 92.4%; 95% prediction interval -2.02 to 0.46 mm/year), lower all-cause mortality, and fewer aortic complications. In AAA, metformin use was associated with slower growth in observational studies (-0.34 mm/year; 95% CI -0.48 to -0.20; I2 = 46.3%), while the single randomized trial found no difference. Certainty of evidence was low to very low. In these largely observational data, aneurysm progression was more closely related to statin and metformin use than to circulating lipid levels, a pattern that is hypothesis-generating and from which causality cannot be inferred.

title: Cardiovascular Diseases and Type 2 Diabetes: 2nd Edition.
authorString: Tudoran C.
abstractText: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is associated with multiple comorbidities, the most important being cardiovascular (CV) diseases (CVDs) and especially coronary artery disease (CAD), peripheral artery disease (PAD), stroke, and chronic kidney disease (CKD) [...].

title: Point-of-Care Ultrasound Use in Confirmed Acute Aortic Syndrome: A Five-Year Retrospective Cohort Study at the Ljubljana Emergency Medical Unit.
authorString: Brezigar P, Kukavica J, Jug B, Možina H.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is increasingly used in emergency care, but data on its use in acute aortic syndrome (AAS) remains limited. This single-center retrospective cohort described POCUS use among patients with confirmed AAS and explored factors associated with POCUS use and time to completion of diagnostic workup. Methods: Records coded ICD10 I71.0-I71.8 from the Emergency Medical Unit, University Medical Centre Ljubljana (2019-2023) were reviewed. Clinical, imaging, and outcome data were extracted, and diagnoses were confirmed by two investigators through manual chart review of ED documentation, radiology reports, and specialist consultation notes. Fisher's exact and Wilcoxon rank sum tests were used for comparisons. Associations with POCUS use and time to completion of diagnostic workup (defined from arrival at triage to completion of the emergency department workup) were assessed with univariable logistic regression and linear regression models, respectively. Survival was explored using univariable Cox proportional-hazards models. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results: Among 120,109 emergency department visits, 73 patients had confirmed AAS (type A: 48; type B: 17; intramural hematoma: 8). POCUS was performed in 62% of patients, more often in those who were hemodynamically unstable (87.5% vs. 54.4%; p = 0.020) or had unclear presentations (40% vs. 7%; p = 0.003). Median time to completion of diagnostic workup was shorter with POCUS (110 vs. 213 min), though not statistically significant (p = 0.069). Hemodynamic instability was associated with higher odds of POCUS use (OR 5.87, 95% CI 1.22-28.2; p = 0.028), whereas a clear clinical presentation was associated with lower odds of POCUS use (OR 0.12, 95% CI 0.02-0.55; p = 0.007). Lower triage level was associated with longer time to completion of diagnostic workup (time ratio 5.43, 95% CI 2.21-13.4; p < 0.001 for urgent vs. immediate triage), whereas very high D-dimer levels were associated with shorter time to completion of diagnostic workup (time ratio 0.44, 95% CI 0.21-0.93; p = 0.031 for highest vs. lowest quartile). In-hospital mortality was 14%, with only age associated with mortality (HR 1.06 per year, 95% CI 1.02-1.11; p = 0.007). Conclusions: In this single-center retrospective AAS cohort, POCUS was used more frequently in unstable and diagnostically unclear patients but was not associated with time to completion of diagnostic workup. Findings are descriptive and exploratory; they do not establish that POCUS accelerates diagnosis or improves outcomes.

title: Mitochondrial DNA mediated Kupffer cell activation in the pathogenesis and progression of liver diseases.
authorString: Li Z, Zhu L, Pan L, Ma J, Xie H, Zhang J.
abstractText: The liver serves as a pivotal metabolic and immunological hub, yet its homeostatic equilibrium is highly susceptible to mitochondrial dysfunction. Recent studies have implicated mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) as an important damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) that links mitochondrial injury to sterile hepatic inflammation and KCs (KCs) activation. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of the mtDNA mediated KCs across four major hepatic pathologies: Alcohol-associated Liver Disease (ALD), Metabolic Dysfunction-associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD), Hepatic Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury (IRI), and Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC). We discuss emerging evidence that Z-DNA-binding protein 1 (ZBP1) associated PANoptosis and nerve injury-induced protein 1 (NINJ1) mediated plasma membrane rupture may contribute to inflammatory cell death in severe liver injury, complementing rather than superseding canonical pyroptotic mechanisms. However, the extent to which mtDNA directly activates this axis remains unresolved. Furthermore, we delineate the cell-type-specific dichotomy of cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS) signaling, which fuels pro-inflammatory storms in KCs via the stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway while promoting protective mitophagy in hepatocytes through a STING-independent cGAS-Beclin-1 interaction. In the context of immunometabolism, we also summarize preclinical evidence linking cytidine/uridine monophosphate kinase 2 (CMPK2) dependent mtDNA synthesis to inflammasome activation and mitochondrial calcium uniporter (MCU) acetylation to age-associated mtDNA release during IRI. Finally, we evaluate the clinical translational potential of targeting these molecular hubs and the emergence of cell-free mitochondrial DNA (cf-mtDNA) fragmentomics-including 5' end motif analysis and diversity scoring as a transformative liquid biopsy tool for precision diagnosis. Collectively, available evidence positions mtDNA mediated KCs activation as an important, context-dependent contributor to liver disease and a potential therapeutic target, while underscoring the need for cell-specific and human validation.

title: Design, Synthesis, Evaluation, and Molecular Dynamics Simulation of Tadalafil Derivatives for the Treatment of Erectile Dysfunction.
authorString: Liu W, Zhang B, Jia Y, Kong X, Deng Y, Cui X, Yang L, Ren W, Tang X, Zhang D, Xu L.
abstractText: Erectile dysfunction (ED) remains a global health burden, yet the clinical utility of tadalafil is constrained by its poor aqueous solubility, cross-inhibition of homologous PDE isoforms, and an efficacy ceiling that cannot be overcome by dose adjustment alone. Herein, a series of diketopiperazine-based tadalafil analogues were designed and synthesized by decorating the amide nitrogen with flexible carbon chains and polar fragments (glycine, taurine, cysteine, and succinic/glutaric anhydride spacers), and by replacing the 3,4-methylenedioxybenzyl motif with substituted aromatic aldehydes. All target compounds were characterized by 1H/13C NMR and HR-MS and evaluated for cytotoxicity against rat aortic smooth muscle cells, calculated Log P and aqueous solubility, NO release, and phosphodiesterase type-5A (PDE5A) inhibitory activity, followed by 100 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and MM/PBSA calculations on the leading analogue. Compound 18, bearing a p-methoxyphenyl group and an N-methyl amide, markedly enhanced NO release relative to tadalafil, reduced residual PDE5A activity to 38.69 ± 1.98% at 10 μM, and exhibited negligible cytotoxicity with a predicted logP of 1.53. Docking into PDE5 (PDB: 1XOZ) and MD analysis revealed a stable binding pose anchored by hydrogen bonds to Gln817 and Tyr612, reinforced by π-π stacking with Phe820 and extensive hydrophobic contacts with Leu765, Ile768, Val782, and Met816 (ΔG_bind = -9.13 ± 3.30 kcal/mol), with van der Waals contributions dominating (-41.78 ± 4.60 kcal/mol). Collectively, compound 18 emerges as a promising next-generation tadalafil-derived PDE5 inhibitor lead, and the resulting SAR picture outlines a hydrophobic-anchor-dominated optimization strategy for this scaffold.

title: Genetic Insights into the Comorbidity of Congenital Heart Disease and Neurodevelopmental Disorders: Focus on Copy Number Variations.
authorString: Ye Z, He Y, Guo J, Meng J, Xu Y, Wang Y, Wang B.

journal.title: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease

abstractText: Congenital heart disease (CHD) and neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) frequently co-occur, indicating that cardiac and neural phenotypes can arise from shared developmental disturbances rather than exclusively from the physiological consequences of heart disease. Copy number variations (CNVs) provide a major genomic basis for this overlap, but their effects extend beyond changes in protein-coding gene dosage. This review synthesizes evidence from recurrent CNV syndromes, genomic cohorts, developmental studies, and experimental models to define how CNVs jointly influence heart and brain development. We examine four interconnected mechanisms: dosage alteration of pleiotropic and multiple genes, disruption of non-coding regulatory elements, remodeling of non-coding RNA networks, and reorganization of three-dimensional chromatin architecture. We further describe how developmental timing, cell-type-specific regulatory context, additional genomic variants, cardiac physiology, and clinical exposures shape incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity. Together, these findings support a layered model in which a primary CNV establishes cross-organ susceptibility, whereas genetic and developmental modifiers determine whether CHD, NDD, or both become clinically manifest. Clinically, CNV diagnosis can inform neurodevelopmental surveillance, multisystem management, and genetic counseling. Genotype-first longitudinal cohorts, developmental multi-omics, parallel cardiac and neural models, and prospective clinical studies will advance individualized risk prediction and intervention.

title: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Infection-Associated Epithelial-to-Mesenchymal Transition: Implication in Tumorigenesis and Pathogenesis of HPV-Positive Cancers.
authorString: Kabakov AE, Matchuk ON, Khokhlova AV, Kaprin AD.
abstractText: Epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a programmed and reversible process that allows epithelial cells to temporarily acquire a mesenchymal cell phenotype with increased migratory and invasive capacity. Analogous phenotypic modulation can also occur in carcinoma cells, which, after undergoing EMT, exhibit cancer stem cell-like properties and actively migrate, leading to tumor invasion and metastases. This structured narrative review focuses on the molecular crosstalk between human papillomavirus (HPV) and EMT, which occurs in HPV-infected human epithelium and in HPV-positive cancers of different location (cervical, head and neck, colorectal, lung, and others). The main questions addressed here are: (i) how HPV-driven EMT may contribute to the malignant transformation of HPV-infected epithelial cells, (ii) what mechanistic links may exist between the HPV positivity and EMT in human cancers, and (iii) how EMT in various HPV-positive human tumors may influence their pathogenesis, treatment modalities and outcomes. The relationship between HPV infection and EMT program is delineated as a complex multicomponent mechanism triggered by exogenous and endogenous stimuli and involving specific ligand-receptor interactions, membrane channels, transcription factors, signaling pathways, epigenetic regulators, etc. The review also discusses some of the potential applications of EMT-related biomarkers and molecular targets in the prevention, prediction and treatment of HPV-induced cancers.

title: Perinatal Brain Injuries in Preterm Infants.
authorString: Papazovska Cherepnalkovski A, Brajkovic L, Cogelja K, Milostic LK, Vidovic N, Renic A, Bulat D, Sabljic J, Batinovic E, Bucat M.
abstractText:
Background

Preterm infants are vulnerable to brain injury because of immature white matter, vascular regulation, and neuroprotective mechanisms. White matter injury (WMI), formerly known as periventricular leukomalacia, is a major cause of cerebral palsy and neurocognitive impairment, while perinatal stroke is an important cerebrovascular cause of adverse outcomes. White matter injury: WMI is linked to hypoxia-ischemia, inflammation or infection, oxidative stress, and impaired oligodendrocyte maturation. It may be cystic or diffuse non-cystic, which is now the most common phenotype. Cystic lesions are strongly associated with motor impairment and spastic cerebral palsy, whereas diffuse injury is increasingly related to cognitive, behavioral, and language deficits. Diagnosis relies on cranial ultrasonography and MRI; prevention focuses on optimized perinatal care, infection control, respiratory stabilization, and neuroprotection. Perinatal stroke: Stroke in preterm infants may occur antenatally or neonatally and includes periventricular hemorrhagic infarction, perinatal arterial ischemic stroke, and cerebral sinovenous thrombosis. Periventricular hemorrhagic infarction is the most common subtype and is often associated with germinal matrix hemorrhage-intraventricular hemorrhage. Risk factors are multifactorial, including fetal, neonatal, placental, thrombotic, infectious, and hemodynamic contributors. Clinical signs may be subtle, making neuroimaging central to classification and prognosis.

Conclusion

Despite advances in neonatal care, WMI and perinatal stroke remain major causes of long-term neurological morbidity in preterm infants. Early recognition, systematic neuroimaging, risk stratification, and multidisciplinary follow-up are essential. Future research should identify reliable biomarkers and targeted neuroprotective therapies.

title: Incremental Value of Cardiovascular CT in Neonates and Infants with Congenital Heart Disease: An Integrated Multimodality Imaging Approach.
authorString: Pomiato E, Pozza A, Cattapan I, Cavaliere A, Reffo E, Avesani M, Castaldi B, Motta R, Pergola V, Di Salvo G.
abstractText: Background: Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) is the first-line imaging modality in neonates and infants with congenital heart disease (CHD), whereas cardiovascular computed tomography (CCT) is generally reserved for selected questions that remain unresolved after echocardiography. We evaluated the incremental diagnostic contribution of CCT within this multimodality imaging pathway. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed consecutive patients aged <1 year with CHD who underwent CCT after multidisciplinary review because TTE was inconclusive or additional anatomic definition was required for surgical planning. The primary endpoint was the incremental anatomic information provided by CCT beyond TTE. Secondary analyses included diagnostic performance against operative findings, acquisition characteristics, radiation exposure, contrast administration, and procedural safety. Results: Twenty-six patients were included; 14 (53.8%) were neonates. CCT was requested most frequently to assess coronary anatomy (9/26, 38.5%), followed by the pulmonary veins (4/26, 15.4%), aortic arch (3/26, 11.5%), and pulmonary arteries/MAPCAs (4/26, 15.4%). CCT provided additional anatomic characterization in 14/26 patients (53.8%), predominantly involving extracardiac vascular structures, and was discordant with TTE regarding the unresolved target anatomy in 12/26 (46.2%). Against the operative findings, TTE accuracy was 96.2% for intracardiac abnormalities, 41.2% for extracardiac abnormalities, and 11.1% for coronary abnormalities; corresponding CCT accuracy was 100%, 94.1%, and 100%. CCT directly informed the surgical approach in two patients with total anomalous pulmonary venous drainage. All examinations provided sufficient image quality to address the specific clinical question for which CCT was performed, and no contrast-related adverse events occurred. The median estimated effective dose was 3.62 mSv (IQR, 1.94-6.06). Conclusions: In a highly selected cohort of neonates and infants with CHD in whom expert TTE leaves a clinically relevant question unresolved, CCT may provide incremental information, particularly regarding coronary and extracardiac vascular anatomy. These findings support a targeted multimodality strategy in which CCT complements echocardiography and is tailored to the anatomic question relevant to surgical planning.

title: Comparative Analysis of Foot Temperature Associated with the Use of Sports and School Footwear in Children Aged 9 and 10 Years.
authorString: Fontán-Jiménez M, Sánchez-Rodríguez R, Cáceres-Madrid MV, Martínez-Nova A, Gómez-Martín B, Escamilla-Martínez E.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Children's footwear plays a key role in foot protection and development, influencing both mechanical and thermal comfort. However, there is limited evidence on how different types of footwear affect foot thermoregulation in the pediatric population. Therefore, the aim of the present study was to analyze the thermal pattern of the pediatric foot and to compare temperature differences in plantar and dorsal regions following the use of school and sports footwear. Methods: A total of 108 schoolchildren (61 girls and 47 boys), with a mean age of 9.46 ± 0.52 years, participated in the study. A non-randomized within-participant repeated-measures crossover design was used, in which each participant was assessed wearing both types of footwear on two separate days, with each child therefore serving as their own control. Thermographic measurements were performed using a Flir® E60bx camera (FLIR Systems, Wilsonville, OR, USA) after 3 h of school activity. Footwear conditions were compared within each region of interest (ROI) of the plantar and dorsal surfaces using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Results: Regardless of the footwear used, the highest temperatures were recorded in the medial longitudinal arch on the plantar surface and in the lateral region on the dorsal surface, whereas the lowest temperatures were observed in the fifth toe on both surfaces. Sports footwear was associated with higher mean temperatures than school footwear in all ROIs (0.61 to 0.95 °C). After FDR correction, significant differences remained only in the medial and lateral dorsal regions (+0.95 and +0.94 °C, respectively; q = 0.0139), whereas none of the plantar differences remained significant. A strong period effect was also observed, with foot temperatures 1.28 to 2.24 °C higher at the second visit regardless of footwear; after adjusting for this effect, temperatures remained higher with sports footwear in all ROIs (0.71 to 1.04 °C). Conclusions: The pediatric foot exhibited a consistent thermal pattern across footwear conditions. However, sports footwear was associated with an approximately 1 °C higher temperature in the medial and lateral regions of the dorsal foot, an effect that persisted after accounting for the period effect. These findings underscore the importance of thermoregulatory properties in children's footwear selection.

title: Longitudinal Trajectories of Autonomic Maturation in Preterm Infants Using Serial 24-Hour Heart Rate Variability Monitoring.
authorString: Sugino M, Kuboi T, Tadatomo Y, Kawaguchi N, Sadamura T, Nakano A, Koyano K, Nakamura S, Takahashi K, Kusaka T.
abstractText: Heart rate variability (HRV) is a non-invasive measure reflecting cardiac autonomic regulation and has been used to investigate developmental changes in preterm infants. Short-term HRV recordings have demonstrated developmental changes with advancing postmenstrual age (PMA), but are highly susceptible to transient physiological conditions, limiting reproducibility. We prospectively performed serial 24 h electrocardiographic recordings in 50 preterm infants born at 24-35 weeks' gestation from postnatal life until before 37 weeks' PMA to characterize longitudinal HRV trajectories. A total of 879 recordings were analyzed using a 24 h single-window approach, and developmental trajectories were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models. All HRV indices increased progressively with advancing PMA. Infants born at ≥32 weeks' gestation exhibited significantly higher HRV values after approximately 33 weeks' PMA than those born at <32 weeks, indicating distinct maturational trajectories according to gestational age. PMA remained independently associated with multiple HRV indices after adjustment for major clinical factors, whereas body weight z-score, respiratory support, oxygen supplementation, and caffeine exposure showed little or no independent association after adjustment. These findings characterize longitudinal 24 h HRV trajectories in preterm infants and suggest that serial 24 h HRV monitoring may provide a framework for assessing developmental changes in cardiac autonomic regulation during neonatal intensive care.

title: Vascular Rings as a Cause of Respiratory Difficulties.
authorString: Šulov J, Olekšák F, Vojtková J, Balázsová P, Soršáková A, Petrovičová O, Durdikova A, Durdik P, Jeseňák M.
abstractText: Background: Vascular rings are rare congenital developmental anomalies of the cardiovascular system that present with variable respiratory and gastrointestinal symptoms often refractory to what is considered a standard treatment. The aim of our study was to describe the clinical presentation, diagnostic pathway, and management of children referred to a tertiary pediatric department for unexplained respiratory symptoms in whom a vascular ring was confirmed, with particular attention to the role of echocardiography in raising the initial suspicion, and to compare our findings with published cohorts. Methods: We performed a retrospective descriptive case series of patients (n = 7) diagnosed at the Department of Pediatrics and Adolescent Medicine, Jessenius Faculty of Medicine in Martin, Comenius University in Bratislava, University Hospital Martin, between 2021 and 2025. Results: The median age at onset of clinical symptoms was 30 days (interquartile range [IQR] 1-120 days). The median age at definitive diagnosis was 14.5 months (IQR 4.3-94.0 months). A genetic abnormality was observed in 3 patients (42.9%), and a positive family history of congenital heart defects was present in 4 (57.1%). All patients (n = 7) were symptomatic at the time of definitive diagnosis. We observed double aortic arch (DAA) in 2 patients (28.6%), right aortic arch with aberrant left subclavian artery (RAA + ALSA) in 4 (57.1%), and aberrant right subclavian artery (ARSA) in 1 (14.3%). One patient with RAA + ALSA had a concurrent pulmonary artery sling (PAS). In 6 patients (85.7%), the initial suspicion was raised by transthoracic or prenatal echocardiography. Six patients (85.7%) underwent surgical repair at a median age of 10.5 months (IQR 4.1-20.1 months), while in one case the risk-benefit ratio of surgery is being evaluated. Conclusions: In this series, echocardiography was a useful non-invasive modality for raising the initial suspicion, whereas CT angiography was required to define the vascular anatomy; the majority of patients were definitively diagnosed and treated within the first two years of life. In our cohort, we also identified a rare combination of a vascular ring (RAA + ALSA) and a pulmonary artery sling (PAS) in a single patient.

title: Quantitative CT Geometry of the Patent Ductus Arteriosus in Infants with Congenital Heart Disease: Association with Aortic Arch Obstruction or Hypoplasia.
authorString: Pop M, Bargutin L, Licu RA, Rotariu M, Iurian DR, Negovan T, Suciu H.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Quantitative patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) geometry in congenital heart disease (CHD), particularly in relation to aortic arch abnormalities, is incompletely characterized. We evaluated CT-derived PDA geometry. Methods: This retrospective exploratory single-center study included 168 infants with CHD and a PDA on cardiovascular CT. Aortic-end, pulmonary-end, and mid-duct diameters and ductal length were measured. The Ductal Length-to-Diameter Index (LDI), selected during exploratory analysis, was defined as ductal length divided by the mean end diameter. Seventy-three patients had CT-documented aortic arch obstruction or hypoplasia. Results: LDI was lower in patients with arch obstruction/hypoplasia than in those without these findings (2.04 [1.39-2.84] vs. 3.51 [2.23-4.89]; p < 0.001; rank-biserial r = -0.473) and remained associated after adjustment for age, weight, and sex (OR per +1 LDI, 0.534; 95% CI, 0.412-0.693; p < 0.001). The association remained robust with a conservative definition restricted to coarctation or interrupted aortic arch. LDI had an interobserver ICC of 0.843 (95% CI, 0.685-0.954), with wide limits of agreement (-1.98 to +2.45). Conclusions: CT-documented aortic arch obstruction or hypoplasia is associated with lower LDI. This exploratory geometric association warrants prospective external validation before clinical use.

title: Association of the Vasoactive-Inotropic Score with Postoperative Intensive Care Unit Stay Following Arterial Switch Operation.
authorString: Besnili Acar D, Çevlik B, Oğuz AS, Coban S, Sarı G, Recep E, Ozturk DY, Babayigit A, Hatemi AC, Ozturk E.

journal.title: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease

abstractText:
Introduction

Transposition of the great arteries (TGA) is one of the most common cyanotic congenital heart diseases in the neonatal period, and arterial switch operation (ASO) is the standard surgical treatment. Postoperative low cardiac output syndrome remains an important cause of morbidity. This study evaluated the association between serial vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS) measurements and postoperative intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay in neonates with TGA undergoing ASO.

Methods

This retrospective study included neonates with TGA who underwent ASO and were followed in a tertiary Pediatric Cardiac Intensive Care Unit between 1 August 2020, and 1 August 2022. ICU length of stay was analyzed as a continuous primary outcome. Prolonged ICU stay, defined as the upper quartile of ICU length of stay in the study cohort (≥9 days), was evaluated as a secondary exploratory outcome. VIS values were recorded at ICU admission and at 24, 48, and 72 h after surgery. Associations between VIS parameters and continuous ICU length of stay were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation. ROC analysis and logistic regression were performed for prolonged ICU stay.

Results

A total of 60 neonates were included, and 15 patients (25%) had a prolonged ICU stay. Admission VIS values were similar between groups. However, VIS values at 24 and 48 h were significantly higher in the prolonged ICU stay group (p = 0.005 and p = 0.001, respectively), whereas no significant difference was observed at 72 h. VIS at 48 h showed the strongest correlation with ICU length of stay (Spearman's r = 0.52, p < 0.001), followed by ΔVIS48 (r = 0.48, p = 0.001) and VIS at 24 h (r = 0.44, p = 0.002). In secondary exploratory analyses, VIS at 48 h demonstrated a numerically higher AUC than VIS at 24 h (0.82 vs. 0.74). ΔVIS48 was associated with prolonged ICU stay in multivariable logistic regression (OR, 1.18 per unit increase; 95% CI, 1.05-1.33; p = 0.006). Firth's penalized logistic regression yielded a similar estimate (OR, 1.15; 95% CI, 1.03-1.30; p = 0.012).

Conclusions

In neonates with TGA undergoing ASO, higher VIS during the first 24-48 postoperative hours, particularly an increase from admission to 48 h, was associated with longer ICU stay. These findings support serial VIS assessment as a marker of early postoperative clinical trajectory. Cohort-derived VIS thresholds should be considered exploratory and require external multicenter validation before clinical application.

title: Dexmedetomidine Versus Dexamethasone in Pediatric Cardiac Surgery with Cardiopulmonary Bypass: An Exploratory Randomized Controlled Trial of Inflammatory Biomarkers and Opioid Consumption.
authorString: Salama MA, Al Dammas FK, AlDhuwaihy A, Alanezi K, Alshuwaier F, Almedlej N, AbdelTwab H, ElTantawi N, Sabri RA, Alaidy A, Jamous YF.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) triggers a systemic inflammatory response in children undergoing congenital heart surgery. Although dexmedetomidine has been proposed as an alternative to corticosteroids, the two agents have not previously been directly compared in a pediatric randomized trial. This study aimed to compare the effects of dexmedetomidine and dexamethasone on inflammatory biomarkers and analgesic outcomes in children undergoing congenital heart surgery with CPB. Methods: In this prospective, randomized, controlled exploratory trial, 50 children aged 6 months to 18 years undergoing elective congenital heart surgery with CPB were randomized 1:1 to dexamethasone (n = 25) or dexmedetomidine (n = 25), using institutional regimens that were not equipotent anti-inflammatory doses. Serum interleukin-6 (IL-6) and interleukin-8 (IL-8) were measured at baseline, immediately after separation from CPB (post-CPB), and 12 h postoperatively. The primary endpoint was IL-6 at the two postoperative time points; IL-8 was a secondary biomarker outcome. Secondary outcomes also included Face, Legs, Activity, Cry, Consolability (FLACC) pain scores, fentanyl consumption, and time to first rescue analgesia. Effect estimates included Hodges-Lehmann (HL) median differences with 95% confidence intervals (CIs); a post hoc baseline-adjusted mixed-effects model of log-transformed concentrations served as a sensitivity analysis. Secondary and exploratory analyses were not adjusted for multiple comparisons. Results: All 50 randomized children were analyzed. Median IL-6 was lower in the dexmedetomidine group at 12 h (50 vs. 178 pg/mL; HL difference 86 pg/mL, 95% CI 59 to 144; p < 0.001); the post-CPB difference (46 vs. 77 pg/mL; HL difference 34 pg/mL, 95% CI 0 to 112; p = 0.045) was imprecise and not significant after post hoc Bonferroni correction for the two primary comparisons. In the post hoc baseline-adjusted sensitivity model, the ratio of geometric mean IL-6 concentrations (dexmedetomidine/dexamethasone) was 0.35 (95% CI 0.22 to 0.58; p < 0.001). Among secondary and exploratory outcomes, for which p-values are nominal, IL-8 was also lower post-CPB (159 vs. 381 pg/mL; p = 0.001) and at 12 h (120 vs. 311 pg/mL; p = 0.002). Dexmedetomidine was associated with lower intraoperative (83.0 ± 30.7 vs. 142.6 ± 51.7 µg; p < 0.001) and cumulative 24-h fentanyl consumption (53.8 ± 17.4 vs. 105.4 ± 32.8 µg; p < 0.001), analyzed in absolute units with incompletely documented intraoperative doses, and a longer time to first rescue analgesia (4.68 ± 0.73 vs. 1.84 ± 0.23 h; p < 0.001). Time to extubation did not differ significantly (median 2 vs. 1 h; p = 0.204). Intensive care unit length of stay, an exploratory outcome recorded in days, was distributed toward shorter stays with dexmedetomidine (median 2 [interquartile range 1-2] vs. 2 [2-3] days; p = 0.007). No pre-specified adverse events occurred in either group, although the trial was too small to exclude clinically important safety differences. Conclusions: In this exploratory trial of two non-equipotent institutional regimens, dexmedetomidine was associated with lower early postoperative IL-6 and IL-8 concentrations and lower opioid consumption than dexamethasone. These hypothesis-generating biomarker and analgesic signals do not demonstrate therapeutic superiority or patient-centered clinical benefit and require confirmation in larger, adequately powered multicenter trials.

title: Exploring cardiac kinetic energy in children with atrial septal defects: a case-control study.
authorString: Clausen H, Friberg E, Arvidsson PM, Liuba P, Sjöberg P.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
journal.title: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
journal.isoabbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol

abstractText: Kinetic energy (KE) of intracardiac blood flow constitutes an important part of the heart's energy expenditure and can be quantified using four-dimensional (4-D) flow cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR). Pediatric patients with atrial septal defect (ASD) have volume-loaded right ventricles and underfilled left ventricles due to left-to-right shunting, which could make ASD a useful model to study such altered ventricular loading conditions in congenital heart disease to explore related pathophysiological changes to KE. To characterize ventricular KE in children with ASD before and after treatment, we matched patients to controls. We recruited 22 patients with ASD (8 males, median/[IQR]: 8.5/[5-12] yr) and performed repeat CMR in 16/22 (72.7%) at means ± SD: 7.7 ± 1.7 mo following treatment. Left ventricular (LV) and right ventricular (RV) KE were assessed by 4-D flow CMR. Results were compared with 11 controls. Before treatment, RV peak diastolic KE was higher in patients with ASD compared with controls (P = 0.02) and normalized afterward (P = 0.42) with abolishment of diastolic ASD streaming. Indexed for ventricular volume at the time of peak KE (iKE), RV peak systolic and peak diastolic iKE decreased among repeatedly assessed ASD after treatment (both: P < 0.01), suggesting altered RV energetics not only attributable to RV volume changes. After treatment, RV iKE was comparable between patients and controls (systolic: P = 0.18; diastolic: P = 0.87). Within the ASD group, LV peak systolic KE increased with increased LV volumes after treatment (P < 0.01), whereas LV peak diastolic KE did not change (P = 0.09). How the different RV and LV peak diastolic KE responses reflect different diastolic ventricular remodeling warrants further investigation.NEW & NOTEWORTHY During systole, RV peak KE among patients with ASD decreased after treatment independent of peak RV volumes, whereas LV peak systolic KE increased after ASD treatment due to improved LV filling conditions. During diastole, RV peak KE is higher than normal and reflects both the large ventricular blood volume and the streaming shunt volume from the ASD and normalizes after treatment.

title: Transition readiness in adolescents with congenital heart disease during transfer to adult care: A secondary analysis of the STEPSTONES randomized controlled trial.
authorString: Malmesjö H, Mora MA, Bratt EL, Sparud-Lundin C, Moons P, Saarijärvi M.
abstractText:
Purpose

Adolescents with congenital heart disease (CHD) are at risk of discontinuity of care during transfer from pediatric to adult services. Transition readiness is considered essential for a safe transfer. This study evaluated the effect of the STEPSTONES person-centered transition program on adolescents' self-reported transition readiness compared with usual care.

Design and methods

This secondary analysis was based on a randomized controlled trial conducted at two Swedish CHD centers. A total of 139 adolescents (age 16 years) were randomized to intervention (n = 70) or usual care (n = 69). The intervention group received the STEPSTONES program in addition to usual care over two years. Transition readiness was assessed at ages 16 (T0), 17 (T1), and 18.5 (T2) using the Readiness for Transition Questionnaire. Between-group differences were analyzed with Mann-Whitney U tests, and longitudinal changes were examined using mixed-design ANOVA.

Results

At T2, the intervention group demonstrated significantly higher overall transition readiness compared with controls (p = .011-.015), with a small effect size (r ≈ .23-.24). A significant main effect of time was found (p < .001), indicating increased readiness across adolescence in both groups. No significant group-by-time interaction was detected (p = .177), and no differences were identified at the level of individual questionnaire items.

Conclusions

The STEPSTONES program was associated with higher overall transition readiness at the time of transfer, although effect sizes were small. Structured, person-centered transition programs may enhance preparedness for adult care.

Practice implications

Pediatric nurses are key in supporting transition readiness. Structured transition programs may strengthen adolescents' overall preparedness for adult-oriented healthcare.

Trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02675361.

title: Anomalous Origin of the Right Pulmonary Artery from the Ascending Aorta in an Adult After Prior Patent Ductus Arteriosus Surgery.
authorString: Li D, Liang S, Zhang H.
abstractText: We present an adult patient with a history of surgical treatment of a patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) in whom contrast-enhanced chest computed tomography (CT) demonstrated anomalous origin of the right pulmonary artery (RPA) from the ascending aorta. Axial CT images clearly demonstrate an discontinuity between the main pulmonary artery and the right pulmonary artery (RPA), and delineate an abnormal opening on the ascending aorta; multiplanar reconstruction technology precisely locates the origin of the artery; dynamic volume imaging integrates the three-dimensional anatomical structure into a model nearly equivalent to a surgical perspective. This case illustrates that an anomalous pulmonary artery associated with a ductus may remain unrecognized at the time of ductus surgery and persist into adulthood, and that a single contrast-enhanced CT examination with multiplanar and cinematic reconstruction provides comprehensive, single-session confirmation of the diagnosis, together with the anatomic roadmap required for surgical planning. For any patient undergoing PDA closure-particularly when pulmonary hypertension or right-heart dilation seems disproportionate-deliberate verification of the origin of both pulmonary arteries may prevent a missed lesion and a second, avoidable operation.

title: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion with the Watchman FLX Device: A Single-Centre Retrospective Analysis of Procedural and One-Year Clinical Outcomes.
authorString: Allakkis W, Salem M, Salem M, Elabd M, Balakishiyev A, Aboud M, Fayoud A, Saad M, Hamadneh M.
abstractText: Background: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is an alternative approach to stroke prevention in selected patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation. This single-centre retrospective study describes device implantation, peri-procedural complications and clinical outcomes during the first year after Watchman FLX implantation. Methods: We analysed 100 consecutive patients who underwent LAAO with the Watchman FLX device at Helios Frankenwaldklinik-Hospital, Kronach, Germany, between 2021 and 2024. The primary endpoint was device implantation success, defined as correct device deployment and implantation. The secondary safety endpoint was a composite of major peri-procedural complications within 72 h. Additional clinical outcomes were strokes and mortality at 30 days and one year. Results: The mean age was 70.7 ± 6.5 years, and 47% of patients were female. The mean CHA2DS2-VASc score was 4.9 ± 1.4, and the mean HAS-BLED score was 4.1 ± 1.0. Device implantation was successful in 100% (95% CI 96.4-100%). The reported peri-procedural complication rate was 7% (95% CI 2.9-13.9%), including major bleeding in 6% (95% CI 2.2-12.6%) and pericardial tamponade in 1% (95% CI 0.0-5.4%). Thirty-day mortality was 2% (95% CI 0.2-7.0%), with no reported strokes (0%; 95% CI 0.0-3.6%). One-year mortality was 11% (95% CI 5.6-18.8%), with one reported stroke (1%; 95% CI 0.0-5.4%). Conclusions: Watchman FLX implantation was achieved in all patients in this cohort. Bleeding was the most frequently reported peri-procedural complication. The low observed stroke proportion should be interpreted alongside the 11% one-year mortality and incomplete imaging surveillance. This uncontrolled descriptive study cannot establish comparative efficacy or comprehensive device safety.

title: Preoperative information burden among parents of children with congenital heart disease: a qualitative study of information access, understanding, and decision-making.
authorString: Hu Y, Tian J, Teng M, Li Y, Zheng H.
abstractText:
Background

Parents of children with congenital heart disease must understand complex clinical information, navigate referral and practical barriers, and make treatment decisions on behalf of their child. Information burden may therefore reflect not only information quantity but also whether information is understandable, trustworthy, accessible, and actionable.

Methods

A qualitative descriptive study was conducted at a tertiary paediatric cardiac centre in China. Twelve parents completed individual face-to-face semi-structured interviews. Purposive sampling sought variation in education, residence, and treatment pathway. Sample adequacy was guided by information power, and recruitment ceased when later interviews no longer altered the main analytic categories or theme boundaries. Data were analysed using the Framework Method, combining within-case timelines with cross-case comparison. Reporting followed the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ).

Results

Four interacting themes were developed: threat before understanding; navigating fragmented information pathways; difficulty translating information into child-specific decisions; and information shaping family adaptation and treatment decisions. Parents described technical language, conflicting recommendations, changing findings, non-comparable digital stories, referral barriers, and cost uncertainty. They valued staged plain-language explanations, visual and written materials, explicit monitoring thresholds, a reliable route for clarification, verified digital information, and practical navigation.

Conclusion

Preoperative information burden was driven less by information volume than by difficulty translating fragmented clinical, digital, and practical information into a trusted, child-specific course of action. Public health and paediatric services should treat communication, health-information access, and navigation as connected parts of a family-centred pathway rather than as isolated educational tasks.

title: Atrial Remodeling and Arrhythmia in Scimitar Syndrome: A Literature Review.
authorString: Sahyouni A, Karzoun A, Gomez V, Minetos Y, Pryor S, Nguyen HQN, Jaishankar M, Niha AA, Piskulich N, Sreekanth S, Subbiondo R.

journal.title: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease

abstractText: Scimitar syndrome is a rare congenital form of partial anomalous pulmonary venous return characterized by right pulmonary venous drainage into the inferior vena cava, causing right-sided volume overload and increased risk of supraventricular arrhythmias, particularly in adolescents and adults. However, existing studies do not clearly describe reported arrhythmia patterns or how heart rhythm changes over time. This structured literature review aimed to characterize the reported atrial and supraventricular arrhythmias and conduction disturbances in patients with Scimitar syndrome and examine their relationship with atrial remodeling, hemodynamic burden, associated structural abnormalities, and surgical or catheter-based intervention. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from September 2026. Of 308 abstracts, 42 articles met the inclusion criteria (Scimitar syndrome patients, with broader PAPVR populations included as contextual evidence; literature reviews, abstract only publications, animal studies and non-English articles were excluded). Studies consistently showed that Scimitar syndrome is associated with right-sided volume overload linked to increased atrial and supraventricular arrhythmias, most commonly atrial fibrillation and flutter, with greater risk in patients with associated atrial septal defects or pulmonary hypertension. Because Scimitar syndrome can remain undiagnosed until adulthood, future studies should identify specific predictors of arrhythmia development to improve long-term electrophysiological outcomes.

title: Claims-Based Diagnostic Registration Patterns and Clinical Burden of Selected Common Aneuploidies in Korean Children: A Nationwide HIRA Study (2009-2023).
authorString: Kwon HE, Gwon SH, Son NH, Byun JC.
abstractText:
Background

Selected common aneuploidies, including Down, Edwards, Patau, Turner, and Klinefelter syndromes, are important causes of congenital anomalies and diverse clinical morbidities. However, nationwide evidence regarding the recent diagnostic registration patterns, clinical outcomes, and healthcare burdens in South Korea remains limited.

Methods

We conducted a nationwide descriptive analysis using claims data from the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service (HIRA) of South Korea between 2009 and 2023. Among individuals aged 0-14 years, we evaluated period-based administrative registration frequency and ratios relative to live births, age at diagnosis, comorbidities including congenital heart disease (CHD) and epilepsy, in-hospital mortality, and first-year healthcare expenditures following the first observed claims-code date.

Results

Among the 5,586,770 live births over the 15-year study period, 5900 individuals with one of the five selected common aneuploidies were identified in the HIRA database, corresponding to an overall claims-based diagnostic registration ratio of 105.6 per 100,000 live births. Down syndrome was the most frequently registered disorder, accounting for 59.51% of the cases, followed by Turner syndrome (19.56%), Klinefelter syndrome (14.76%), Edwards syndrome (4.63%), and Patau syndrome (1.54%). The corresponding claims-based diagnostic registration ratios were 62.8, 20.7, 15.6, 4.9, and 1.6 per 100,000 live births, respectively. Edwards and Patau syndromes had the highest clinical burden, with discharge-recorded in-hospital mortality of 34.07% (95% CI, 28.46-40.02) and 32.97% (95% CI, 23.47-43.61), respectively, and the highest median first-year healthcare expenditures of 17,394,435 KRW (Q1-Q3, 1,087,560-61,040,440) and 7,478,665 KRW (Q1-Q3, 510,510-37,524,080), respectively. The prevalence of CHD ranged from 60.7% to 70.3% in Down, Edwards, and Patau syndromes and was approximately 11% in Turner and Klinefelter syndromes.

Conclusions

This nationwide claims-based study demonstrated distinct diagnostic registration patterns and outcome disparities among the selected common aneuploidies in Korean children. These findings support the need for disorder-specific clinical pathways, integrated national surveillance, and targeted supportive care to address the substantial clinical and economic burdens.

title: Role of digital health in the personalized management of heart failure due to Fontan failure: a case report.
authorString: Cavarretta E, Quarta MT, Butera G, Amodeo A, Adorisio R.
abstractText:
Background

Heart failure (HF) represents a major cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with Fontan circulation. Chronic venous congestion, impaired preload, and limited cardiac output reserve make clinical assessment and intermittent invasive evaluations insufficient to capture early haemodynamic deterioration. Pharmacological treatment lack of robust evidence in this subgroup of patients. In this challenging setting, implantable invasive haemodynamic monitoring systems may provide continuous, real-life information capable of guiding personalized HF management.

Case summary

A 26-year-old Fontan male developed protein losing enteropathy and recurrent hospitalizations for decompensated heart failure. Therefore, the patient was candidate to heart transplantation. Over time, episodes of acute HF increased with an escalating requirement of dosage of diuretics. At 22 years of age, another episode of acute decompensated HF prompted a catheter-based intervention with Fontan conduit re-dilatation and re-fenestration with an Atrial Flow Regulator (AFR) implant, and a pulmonary artery pressure monitoring system (CardioMEMS™) was deployed to telemonitor pulmonary artery pressures and adjust the diuretic therapy accordingly. Up to date, 4 years from the intervention, the use of this remote monitoring system was feasible and effective in tailoring medical therapy to prevent further hospitalizations for acute HF. The patient is in clinical follow-up with regular controls.

Discussion

Systems allowing continuous or repeated assessment of haemodynamic status in real-life conditions may support personalized treatment adjustments, improve symptom control, and potentially reduce HF-related hospitalizations in patients with failing Fontan circulation.

title: MultiCaRe-Thorax: A Curated Benchmark Dataset and Reproducible Labeling Framework for Multi-Label Thoracic Disease Classification in Chest X-Ray Imaging.
authorString: Abu Jassar NJ, Almalkawi IT, Al-Hammouri MF, Omari T, Al Bataineh A.
abstractText: Chest X-ray (CXR) imaging remains a widely used diagnostic modality for the detection of thoracic diseases, including pneumonia, tuberculosis, pleural effusion, lung cancer and cardiomegaly. Despite the extensive use of CXR examinations in clinical practice, the development of robust multi-label artificial intelligence (AI) systems remains constrained by limitations in dataset availability, annotation consistency and reproducible labeling methodologies. Existing public datasets frequently rely on heterogeneous labeling protocols, limited pathology coverage or annotations that inadequately account for linguistic negation and uncertainty within radiology reports. In this paper, we introduce MultiCaRe-Thorax, a curated thoracic benchmark dataset derived from the publicly available MultiCaRe repository, with a reproducible negation-aware natural language processing (NLP) framework for automated generation of multi-label thoracic disease annotations. Unlike existing CXR benchmarks that are distributed in their pre-curated form, MultiCaRe-Thorax provides a fully reproducible pipeline from raw case reports to curated dataset, establishing a new resource that is both scalable and transparent. Our pipeline performs thoracic case identification, image-report matching, duplicate removal, data cleaning, disease-specific label extraction and quality-control verification to produce a curated cohort comprising 5252 chest radiographs from 3415 unique patients. Sixteen clinically relevant thoracic pathologies were automatically annotated using a dictionary- and pattern-based NLP framework incorporating explicit negation detection and n-gram mining, achieving 95% accuracy against 500 manually reviewed reports (Cohen's κ=0.89). Sixteen clinically relevant thoracic pathologies were automatically annotated using a dictionary- and pattern-based NLP framework incorporating explicit negation detection and n-gram mining, achieving 95% agreement against 500 manually reviewed reports. Five ImageNet-pretrained convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures (ResNet50, DenseNet121, EfficientNetB0, EfficientNetB7 and InceptionV3) with two hybrid ensemble configurations were evaluated under a patient-level data partitioning protocol. Among individual architectures, DenseNet121 attains the best AUC on tuberculosis (0.757) and pleural effusion (0.767) with roughly one-third the parameters of ResNet50, while ResNet50 attains the higher mean AUC across all sixteen pathologies (0.688 vs. 0.682) and on interstitial lung disease (0.769) and lung mass/cancer (0.777); we report this as an accuracy-efficiency trade-off rather than a single best architecture. The DenseNet121-InceptionV3 ensemble achieves the highest reported AUC of 0.821 for lung mass/cancer detection. We report 95% confidence intervals for the evaluated ensemble and remaining backbones and note substantial estimation uncertainty for the rarest classes (e.g., congenital heart disease, n=8 test cases). Grad-CAM visualizations were also employed to provide clinically interpretable explanations of model predictions.

title: Resting-State Functional Brain Connectivity and Neurodevelopmental Profiles in 3-Year-Olds with Congenital Heart Disease.
authorString: Savard C, Tremblay J, Provost S, Paquette N, Kessouri S, Roger K, Fourdain S, Doussau A, Vannasing P, Simard MN, Gallagher A.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is associated with altered brain development and an increased risk of neurodevelopmental difficulties, particularly in more severe forms of the condition. Although alterations in functional brain connectivity have been reported before and after the first corrective surgery in early infancy, as well as in adulthood, little is known about their presentation in early childhood and their association with neurodevelopmental outcomes. This study aimed to characterize resting-state functional connectivity in 3-year-old children with moderate-to-severe CHD and to examine its associations with neurodevelopmental outcomes, including cognitive, language, and motor abilities. Methods: Twenty-five 3-year-old children with moderate-to-severe CHD and 28 age-matched healthy controls completed resting-state functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) analysis and a standardized neurodevelopmental assessment. Connectivity was compared across networks using a repeated-measures analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), then within each network separately, controlling for maternal socioeconomic status and with sex as a factor. Associations with neurodevelopmental measures were examined using hierarchical linear regressions adjusted for group, sex, and socioeconomic status, with connectivity-by-group interactions tested. Results: Children with moderate-to-severe CHD showed lower resting-state functional connectivity than controls specifically within the right fronto-temporal network, with no group differences in the four remaining networks, as well as poorer language performance. Greater inter-hemispheric functional connectivity was associated with fewer executive function difficulties and better overall motor performance across participants, and greater frontal connectivity with better motor coordination, with no significant differences in these associations between groups. Conclusions: Preschool-aged children with CHD show regionally circumscribed alterations in functional connectivity and language vulnerabilities, while the associations between connectivity and executive and motor functioning appear to extend across both CHD and typically developing children.

title: First-trimester Cardiac Assessment in Fetuses With Increased Nuchal Translucency: A Diagnostic Accuracy Study.
authorString: Yu J, Gu Y.
abstractText:
Objective

To evaluate the independent and incremental value of a standardized first-trimester binary cardiac assessment for screening severe congenital heart disease (CHD) in fetuses with increased nuchal translucency (NT).

Method

This single-center retrospective diagnostic accuracy study included 223 singleton fetuses with NT ≥ 3.0 mm at 11-13+ 6 weeks of gestation who underwent prenatal screening at our hospital between January 2019 and December 2023. First-trimester binary cardiac assessment was performed through blinded review of archived ultrasound images. Clinical and screening variables, including NT thickness and pregnancy-associated plasma protein A (PAPP-A), were collected. Missing serum marker data were addressed using multiple imputation. Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were used to assess the predictive and diagnostic performance of the cardiac assessment alone and in combination with conventional screening indicators. The DeLong test was used to compare the baseline model (NT + PAPP-A) with the incremental model (NT + PAPP-A + cardiac assessment).

Results

A positive first-trimester cardiac assessment was independently associated with severe CHD (adjusted OR = 4.02, 95% CI: 1.09-14.87). In the primary imputed analysis, the baseline model (NT + PAPP-A) had an AUC of 0.840 (95% CI: 0.772-0.912), and the incremental model adding cardiac assessment had an AUC of 0.879 (95% CI: 0.812-0.945); however, the DeLong test did not show a statistically significant difference (p = 0.243). The cardiac assessment showed particularly high sensitivity for left-sided obstructive cardiac malformations (90.0%).

Conclusion

A standardized first-trimester cardiac assessment is independently associated with severe CHD in fetuses with thickened NT. Adding it to NT thickness and maternal PAPP-A did not significantly improve model discrimination in this retrospective cohort, although the AUC increased numerically. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to determine whether this combined strategy provides incremental value.

title: Stroke in Young Adults: A Narrative Review of Clinico-Radiological Approach to Twenty Key Etiologies.
authorString: Vitturi BK, Pacheco FT, Gagliardi RJ.
abstractText: Background: Stroke in young adults is increasing worldwide and is associated with substantial long-term disability. Unlike stroke in older populations, young patients frequently present with uncommon etiologies that require specific diagnostic approaches and targeted secondary prevention strategies. Early recognition of these causes remains a major clinical challenge. Objective: This study aimed to provide a comprehensive review of the principal uncommon causes of stroke in young adults, emphasizing their clinical characteristics and neuroimaging findings relevant to etiological diagnosis. Methods: A narrative review was conducted focusing on cerebrovascular disorders that disproportionately affect young adults, including arterial dissections, patent foramen ovale, moyamoya disease, reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome, cerebral venous thrombosis, thrombophilias, autoimmune diseases, infections, genetic disorders, malignancy, and cardiac conditions. Particular attention was given to neuroradiological patterns and imaging modalities useful for diagnosis. Results: Numerous uncommon etiologies contribute significantly to stroke in young adults and often occur in the absence of traditional vascular risk factors. Neuroimaging plays a pivotal role in diagnosis, helping identify characteristic findings such as double-lumen signs in arterial dissections, collateral vessel networks in moyamoya disease, reversible multifocal vasoconstriction in RCVS, venous filling defects in cerebral venous thrombosis, and distinctive imaging signatures associated with genetic, infectious, inflammatory, and neoplastic disorders. Recognition of these patterns can substantially improve diagnostic accuracy and guide appropriate secondary prevention. Conclusions: Stroke in young adults encompasses a broad spectrum of etiologies that differ considerably from those observed in older populations. Awareness of characteristic clinical and neuroimaging features is essential for accurate etiological investigation and implementation of effective preventive strategies.

title: <b>Unveiling the calcium channel blocking potential of <i>Suaeda fruticosa</i> : From <i>ex vivo</i> studies to molecular docking</b>.
authorString: Saqib F, Javaid S, Khan NY, Kanwal A, Muhammad G, Ahmed Z, Khalid A, Nadeem S, Haq NU, Idrees M, Khurshid F.
abstractText:
Background

Suaeda fruticosa is a widely distributed plant in Pakistan which has been traditionally used as a remedy for constipation, dyspnoea, headache, nausea, neurosis and vertigo.

Objectives

The present study aimed to scientifically validate the traditionally claimed medicinal properties of Suaeda fruticosa.

Methods

The experiment involved the preparation of a 70% ethanolic extract of Suaeda fruticosa (Sf.Cr), which was tested ex-vivo in an isolated rabbit jejunum preparation for spasmolytic activity. Moreover, the crude extract was tested on isolated tracheal and aorta preparations to evaluate the effects.

Results

Sf.Cr dose-dependently relaxed the jejunum and inhibited K+(80 mM)-induced contractions with EC50 value of 0.229 mg/ml and 0.095 mg/ml, respectively. Further, the Sf.Cr caused a rightward shift in Ca2+ concentration response curves (CRCs), similar to verapamil. So, calcium channel-blocking and anticholinergic actions were responsible for the antispasmodic (anti-diarrhoeal) effect. Sf.Cr produced inhibition of carbachol (1 µM)- and K+(80 mM)-induced contractions in isolated rabbit tracheal tissues with EC50 values of 0.8339 mg/ml and 1.022 mg/ml, respectively. Sf. Cr also completely abolished the Phenylephrine (1 µM)- and K+(80 mM)-induced constrictions in isolated rabbit aortic rings, with EC50 values of 0.9448 mg/ml and 0.2026 mg/ml, respectively. Molecular docking against calmodulin (PDB ID: 6M7H) showed that 3-hydroxy-2-quinolinone attained the highest glide score (-6.742 kcal.mol-¹), establishing hydrogen bonding and Pi-Pi stacking interactions with MET124 and PHE92, surpassing the binding affinity of the standard drug verapamil (-5.464 kcal.mol-¹). SwissADME profiling showed that all identified phytoconstituents complied with Lipinski's rule of five, exhibited high gastrointestinal absorption and were predicted to cross the blood-brain barrier, supporting their oral bioavailability as drug candidates.

Conclusion

These findings collectively established Sf.Cr as a source of non-specific calcium channel-blocking phytochemicals with potential for developing antispasmodic, bronchodilator, and vasorelaxant agents.

title: Measurement Properties of Hand-Held Dynamometry for Ankle Strength Assessment: A COSMIN-Based Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Lourenço Ferreira MH, Völker Oliveira JV, Junior NC, Dutra de Oliveira TM, Santos Araujo GA, Filho JE, Sabino GS, Malaguti C, Felício DC.
abstractText:
Objective

This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the measurement properties of handheld dynamometry (HHD) for assessing isometric ankle muscle strength in healthy individuals.

Methods

A comprehensive search was conducted in PubMed, EMBASE, CINAHL, Web of Science, SPORTDiscus, PsycINFO, Scopus, and the Virtual Health Library, with no language or date restrictions. Observational and methodological studies assessing dorsiflexors, plantar flexors, invertors, or evertors using HHD were eligible if they reported reliability, measurement error, or construct validity against isokinetic dynamometry. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed by measurement property and testing configuration, following COSMIN guidance.

Results

Twenty-four studies were included. Inter-rater reliability was good for dorsiflexors (ICC = 0.89, 95% CI 0.80-0.94), plantar flexors (ICC = 0.86, 95% CI 0.72-0.93), invertors (ICC = 0.79, 95% CI 0.66-0.87), and evertors (ICC = 0.75, 95% CI 0.46-0.90). Intra-rater reliability ranged from good to excellent (ICC = 0.88-0.91). External fixation was associated with numerically higher inter-rater ICCs for dorsiflexors and plantar flexors although subgroup differences were not statistically significant. Construct validity was strong for dorsiflexors (r = 0.87, 95% CI 0.42-0.98) but uncertain for plantar flexors (r = 0.72, 95% CI -0.20-0.96). Measurement error remained indeterminate due to the absence of an established minimal important change. Certainty of evidence was high for reliability and low for construct validity; measurement error was not graded.

Conclusion

HHD provides reliable assessment of isometric ankle strength, including without external fixation. Evidence for construct validity, particularly for plantar flexors, and for measurement error remains limited.

title: A Model for Estimating the Risk of Gastrointestinal Bleeding for Patients on Oral Anticoagulants and Interacting Medications.
authorString: Gomez-Lumbreras A, Tawfik AG, Reese T, Witt DM, Del Fiol G, Malone DC.
abstractText:
Introduction

Pharmacodynamic drug-drug interactions (DDI) in patients receiving oral anticoagulants (OAC) may increase the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB). The purpose of this study was to develop and validate a GIB model for patients receiving OACs.

Methods

A risk model, Drug Interactions in Oral AntiCoagulants for Risk of Gastrointestinal Bleeding (DIOAC-GIB), was developed to predict GIB based on interacting medications and other patient-specific risk factors for patients on OAC. Inputs for the model were obtained using random-effect meta-analysis or from the literature for the following attributes: exposure to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs); selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors/serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SSRI/SNRIs); aspirin, antiplatelet medications, and proton pump inhibitors (PPIs); age; and GIB history. The model was correlated to existing OAC models (HAS-BLED and DOAC score).

Results

GIB risk for OACs was based on pivotal trials (1.16% for apixaban; 3.15% for rivaroxaban; 3.00% for dabigatran; 3.31% for edoxaban; and 2.00% for warfarin). The odds ratio (OR) of GIB for NSAIDs ranged from 1.16 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.84-1.61) for celecoxib to 20.67 (95% CI: 14.56-29.34) for ketorolac. ORs for GIB among SSRI/SNRIs ranged from 1.31 (95% CI: 1.07-1.62) for paroxetine to 1.50 (95% CI: 1.32-1.70) for venlafaxine. Risk of GIB also included persons > 65 years of age (relative risk = 2.50, 95% CI: 1.2-5.5); history of GIB (OR = 5.14, 95% CI: 3.92-6.73); exposure to aspirin (OR = 1.31, 95% CI: 0.93-1.85), antiplatelet medications (OR = 1.97, 95% CI: 1.73-2.25), and corticosteroids (OR = 1.69, 95% CI: 1.53-1.87); and PPIs reduced GIB risk (OR = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.62-0.74). Correlations between the DIOAC-GIB and HAS-BLED and DOAC scores were 0.5 for both (p < 0.01).

Conclusion

DIOAC-GIB is a novel GIB-risk model that incorporates pharmacodynamic OAC DDIs to assist clinicians and patients to determine a therapeutic plan while accounting for GIB risk. DIOAC-GIB correlates with other bleeding risk scores and may help identify high-risk patients who may benefit from tailored prescribing.

title: In Vivo Partial Cell Reprogramming With Yamanaka Factors Reduced Ischemic Brain Damage in Aging Mice.
authorString: Mallavibarrena PR, Martín-López G, Rodríguez-Morales J, Ávila J, Hernández F, Pérez-Álvarez MJ.
abstractText: Aging is associated with functional decline and reduced regenerative capacity in the brain, is also the strongest risk factor for ischemic stroke, which remains a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide, and is associated with impaired functional recovery. Here, we investigated whether short-term partial cellular reprogramming through cyclic expression of Yamanaka factors (OSKM) in a Tet-ON mouse model under Rosa-26 promoter has any impact on ischemic damage in aged mice. To assess ischemic resilience, mice underwent permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion (pMCAo). Forty-eight hours after ischemia, OSKM-induced mice displayed significantly smaller damaged area compared with wild-type controls, accompanied by improved neurological scores and enhanced performance in the tightrope test, suggesting preserved sensorimotor abilities. Notably, myelin integrity was preserved in OSKM-treated mice, as shown by Black-Gold staining and stable MAG and MBP expression, whereas wild-type mice exhibited pronounced demyelination. Given the role of oligodendrocytes in myelin maintenance, we quantified the abundance of their different populations. OSKM induction significantly increased total oligodendrocytes (Olig2<sup>+</sup>) and oligodendrocyte precursor cells (PDGFRα<sup>+</sup>) following ischemia, suggesting an enhanced reparative response. Moreover, partial reprogramming preserved neuronal density in the ischemic cortex and prevented the marked astrocytic activation observed in wild-type mice, while microglial responses remained comparable across genotypes. These findings demonstrate that cyclic partial reprogramming in aged mice reduces ischemic damage, highlighting OSKM induction as a promising strategy for enhancing brain resilience during cerebrovascular accidents.

title: Prohibitive Effects of ω-3 on Pancreatic Damage in an Experimental Diabetes Model: Blood Glucose, Insulin, Lipid Profiles, Oxidative Stress, Inflammation, Pancreatic Tissue Morphology, and Apoptotic Pathways.
authorString: Erdemli Z, Gul M, Gokturk N, Ozhilal F, Ozsoy E, Bag HG, Erdemli ME.

journal.title: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

abstractText: This study aimed to investigate the potential protective effects of Omega-3 (ω-3) against damage to pancreatic tissue in rats with experimentally induced diabetes using streptozotocin. Twenty-eight male Wistar Albino rats were divided into four groups: Control, Diabetes Mellitus (DM), ω-3, and DM + ω-3, with seven rats in each group. STZ was injected intraperitoneally (i.p.) into the DM group, and blood glucose levels were measured on the fourth day after injection. Rats with blood glucose levels of ≥ 200 mg/dL were diagnosed with DM. The ω-3 group received 500 mg/kg of ω-3. After the 42-day experiment, pancreatic tissue and blood samples were collected from the rats. The DM group showed increased levels of malondialdehyde (MDA), total oxidant status (TOS), oxidative stress index (OSI), tumor necrosis factor α (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), glucose, LDL, triglycerides, caspase-3 immunoreactivity, and histopathological abnormalities in pancreatic tissue. At the same time, there were decreases in superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), total antioxidant status (TAS), HDL, and insulin levels. Blood, biochemical, histopathological, and immunohistochemical parameters negatively impacted by ω-3 administration have improved. This study demonstrated that in STZ-induced DM rats, DM increased oxidative capacity and led to oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, and tissue damage. It was found that ω-3 has strong antioxidant, pro-apoptotic, anti-inflammatory, and protective effects.

title: Cycloastragenol Attenuates Cisplatin-Induced Ovarian Toxicity in Rats: Associations With TERT Expression, Apoptotic Balance, and FOXO3a-mTOR-Related Signaling.
authorString: Erol GNA, Yar AS, Kaplanoğlu GT.

journal.title: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

abstractText: Cisplatin (CIS)-induced ovarian toxicity is characterized by follicular depletion, apoptosis, and disruption of intracellular survival signaling. This study investigated whether cycloastragenol (CAG), a telomerase-associated bioactive compound, attenuates CIS-induced ovarian injury in rats. Forty female Sprague-Dawley rats were assigned to two vehicle-control groups and CAG, CIS, or CIS + CAG groups for 15 days. Vehicle controls were pooled after confirming no significant differences. Ovarian morphology and follicle counts were evaluated histologically. Immunohistochemical analyses included PCNA, caspase-3, total FOXO3a, phospho-FOXO3a (Ser253), total mTOR, BAX, BCL-2, and TERT. Serum anti-Müllerian hormone and telomerase-related measurements were assessed by ELISA, and relative telomere length was determined by quantitative real-time PCR. CIS reduced primordial follicle numbers, increased follicular atresia, enhanced BAX expression, reduced BCL-2 and TERT immunoreactivity, and increased the BAX/BCL-2 ratio. CAG co-treatment significantly attenuated the changes in BAX, BCL-2, the BAX/BCL-2 ratio, and TERT. Nuclear phospho-FOXO3a was significantly lower in the CIS + CAG group than in the CIS group, whereas cytoplasmic phospho-FOXO3a did not differ significantly. Total mTOR and caspase-3 were numerically reduced by CAG co-treatment but did not remain significant after multiple-comparison correction. PCNA, total FOXO3a, and serum AMH showed partial or nonsignificant recovery. Relative telomere length did not differ among groups. CAG partially attenuated CIS-induced ovarian injury and apoptotic imbalance and was associated with restoration of ovarian TERT immunoreactivity and modulation of phospho-FOXO3a localization. However, these findings do not establish a causal telomerase-FOXO3a-mTOR mechanism.

title: Endurance Training Improves Insulin Sensitivity, Metabolic Flexibility, and Mitochondrial Function in Type 2 Diabetes.
authorString: Hansen M, Møller S, Blom I, Lange KK, Ziegler AK, Farlov JE, Borch J, Hesselager SA, Hansen JK, Liebmann A, Dal MH, Åkerström T, Helge JW, Hellsten Y, Dela F.

journal.title: Scandinavian journal of medicine & science in sports

abstractText: To determine how endurance training influences insulin sensitivity, metabolic flexibility, and mitochondrial function in individuals with and without type 2 diabetes (T2D). Insulin sensitivity (2-step hyperinsulinaemic-isoglycaemic clamp), metabolic flexibility, and mitochondrial respiratory capacity and H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> emission were assessed in participants with T2D (n = 15) and controls (n = 14) before and after 12 weeks of supervised endurance training. Sensitivity analyses were performed using linear mixed-effects models including all available participants. At baseline, glucose clearance was lower in individuals with T2D compared with controls. Training increased glucose clearance (mL/min/kg FFM) in both groups, with larger model-derived improvements in T2D (Step 1: +1.43 [0.88-1.97]; Step 2: +3.18 [2.12-4.23]) than in controls (Step 1: +0.76 [0.21-1.31]; Step 2: +1.49 [0.53-2.45]). The group × time interaction was significant at the higher insulin step. Metabolic flexibility to fat-but not glucose-was reduced in T2D and improved modestly with training.
