abstractText: The transcription factor PAX6 is a crucial regulator of multiple aspects of embryonic forebrain development. It has well-established roles in the regulation of excitatory and inhibitory neuron development in the embryonic cortex in mice but PAX6's roles during human forebrain development are less well understood. Using human cerebral organoids, we investigated PAX6's roles in human neurodevelopment. Homozygous PAX6 mutant (PAX6-/-) organoids were larger than controls and contained increased inhibitory cell types. Excitatory neurons were still generated in PAX6-/- organoids but they were less mature, and a subset showed dysregulated expression of inhibitory identity genes compared to PAX6+/+ controls. The inhibitory cells found in PAX6-/- organoids physically segregated from excitatory neurons and presented a distinct transcriptomic profile when compared to in vivo cortical inhibitory neurons. PAX6-/- organoids showed a dysregulated cellular response to PTN-PTPRZ1 signalling, which contributed to the observed increase in inhibitory neurons and the consequent altered excitatory to inhibitory neuronal ratio.

title: Hemodynamic loading regulates formation and patterning of atrial pectinate muscles in the chick embryo.
authorString: Neradilova C, Neffeova K, Kvasilova A, Sankova B, Vostarek F, Bartos M, Kolesova H, Sedmera D.

journal.title: Developmental dynamics : an official publication of the American Association of Anatomists

abstractText:
Background

The formation and patterning of pectinate muscles (PM) in embryonic atria remain understudied compared to ventricular trabeculae. This study tests the hypothesis that PM are homologous to ventricular trabeculae and depend on hemodynamic loading for their specification.

Results

PM emerged in chick atria at Hamburger-Hamilton stage 23 (embryonic day 4), expanding to comprise over 50% of atrial myocardial cross-sectional area by embryonic day 8. Unlike the compact ventricular myocardium, atrial free wall remained thin (~5-25 μm) throughout development, with proliferation higher in the PM than in the interpectinate regions. Hemodynamic unloading via in vitro culture or in ovo left atrial ligation (LAL) at stages 21-23 inhibited PM formation, reduced myocyte proliferation, and slowed impulse propagation. LAL induced ectopic pacemaking activity in the ligated region, with upregulated HCN4 and downregulated GJA5 and SCN5A expression. Shear stress-responsive gene expression (KLF2, EDN1) was absent in unloaded LAL endocardium, while NOTCH1 expression persisted.

Conclusions

These findings demonstrate that PM formation and atrial myocardial differentiation are highly sensitive to hemodynamic loading. While the early phases of PM formation share mechanosensitivity with ventricular trabeculae, their subsequent growth and myocardial compartment organization differ, suggesting chamber-specific regulatory mechanisms rather than direct developmental equivalence and reflecting their different myocardial architecture.

title: The Effectiveness and Safety of Deep Sedation Protocols for Pulsed Field Ablation of Atrial Fibrillation.
authorString: Zhao Y, Li F, Wang J, Zhou L, Kong X, Wei S, Zhou M, Feng H, Wang Z, Mu Y, Xue J, Wen B, Jiang Y, He L, Jiang C, Xia S, Liu X, Guo X, Zhou N, Li S, Jiang C, Tang R, Sang C, Long D, Du X, Zuo S, Dong J, Ma C.
abstractText:
Background

Deep sedation (DS) is increasingly utilized during pulsed field ablation (PFA) for atrial fibrillation (AF), but the optimal electrophysiologist-led sedation regimen remains unclear.

Objective

To compare sedative effectiveness and safety of three electrophysiologist-led DS protocols.

Methods

In this prospective, single-center study, AF patients undergoing focal-form PFA received (1) midazolam + fentanyl (Midazolam group), (2) flurbiprofen axetil + midazolam + fentanyl (Flurbiprofen group), or (3) dexmedetomidine + fentanyl (Dexmedetomidine group). The primary endpoint was the achievement of the target sedation level at ablation initiation (Ramsay Sedation Score ≥3). Secondary endpoints included intraoperative pain, sedation difficulty, operator satisfaction, and sedation-related adverse events.

Results

166 patients (mean age, 62.2 ± 10.8 years; 62.7% male; 48.2% with paroxysmal AF) were enrolled, with 53, 67, and 46 patients included in the Midazolam, Flurbiprofen, and Dexmedetomidine groups, respectively. The primary outcome occurred more frequently in the Flurbiprofen (73.1%) and Dexmedetomidine (82.6%) groups compared to Midazolam (47.2%) (overall p < 0.001); Flurbiprofen and Dexmedetomidine group did not differ significantly. Intraoperative pain scores were lowest with Dexmedetomidine (overall p < 0.001). Both Flurbiprofen and Dexmedetomidine groups showed lower sedation difficulty and higher operator satisfaction than the Midazolam group (both overall p < 0.001). Dexmedetomidine was associated with more intraoperative hypotension (overall p = 0.047).

Conclusion

Electrophysiologist-led DS protocols with Flurbiprofen and Dexmedetomidine were associated with higher target sedation attainment than the specific low-dose Midazolam regimen during PFA, but Dexmedetomidine is linked to higher hypotension rates, warranting caution.

title: The Promise of Wall Shear Stress Topological Analysis for Cardiovascular Flow Characterization.
authorString: Mazzi V, Calò K, Gallo D, Steinman DA, Morbiducci U.
abstractText: Although interest in cardiovascular flow topology dates back at least to the 1970s, its application to clinically relevant problems gained momentum in the early 2000s, when Ethier et al. used topological analysis?including singular points (also known as critical or fixed points)?to characterize flow and wall shear stress (WSS) patterns in bypass grafts. Since then, topological analysis of WSS and near-wall flow has been broadly applied to coronary and carotid artery disease, cerebral and aortic aneurysms, and cardiothoracic flows. In this paper, we illustrate the theory and recent developments in the practice of topological analysis, including the detection and classification of WSS and surface vorticity fixed points, and the topological constraints underlying them; identification of the manifolds (expansion/contraction regions) connecting fixed points; and the links between these topological features and vascular mechanobiology. Based on an objective literature review focusing on work published since 2020, we identified and tabulated more than 50 peer-reviewed research articles, which highlight the growth of WSS topological analysis in the last five years. A narrative summary of studies is provided to demonstrate the tangible promise of topological analysis for understanding, treating, and even predicting the clinical outcomes of cardiovascular diseases. Current challenges and future perspectives are also highlighted.

title: Consensus Guidance for the Female-Specific Prevention and Management of Cardiovascular Disease: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine.
authorString: Khan SS, Grobman WA, Angell S, Brubaker L, Cameron NA, de Ferranti S, El Khoudary SR, Ferranti EP, Hameed AB, Johnson HM, Kennedy S, Kim ESH, Hannon TS, Maradik ME, Martin KA, Miller EC, Singh RR, Rosen SE, Reed SD, Tabak RG, Darius Tandon S, Thurston RC, Weedn AE, Verma N, Perak AM, American Heart Association; American Academy of Pediatrics; American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists; and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine.
abstractText: There is growing recognition that the optimal prevention and management of cardiovascular disease in girls and women requires attention to sex-specific considerations relevant to the interconnected domains of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health across the life course. Dysregulation in these health domains tends to co-occur and is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease. However, healthcare for girls and women is uniquely fragmented across clinical specialties, including pediatrics, adolescent medicine, primary care, obstetrics, maternal-fetal medicine, gynecology, cardiology, endocrinology, hematology, and neurology. Furthermore, inconsistent alignment across society guidelines contributes to missed opportunities to optimize cardiovascular health. Therefore, the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine convened a multisociety science advisory group and developed the Female Life Stage construct. This construct defines 4 distinct and clinically meaningful stages-perimenarche (S1), ovarian cycling (S2), perimenopause (S3), and postmenopause (S4)-to enable female-specific screening, prevention, and treatment considerations. In addition, this construct incorporates pregnancy as a unique modifying life event when cardiovascular risk may emerge or be unmasked (eg, adverse pregnancy outcomes). This scientific statement crosswalks major society guidelines, synthesizes the evidence, and provides consensus-based clinical guidance for each Female Life Stage and interconnected health domain (ie, hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health). We conclude with a call to action to improve clinical workflows, enhance clinician education, and address scientific and implementation gaps to improve cardiovascular health in girls and women.

title: Phenanthrene disrupts calcium transients and inhibits the Na+/Ca2+ exchanger current, INCX, in zebrafish (Danio rerio) ventricular myocytes.
authorString: Vehniäinen ER, Marris CR, Kompella SN, Hancox JC, Shiels HA.
abstractText: Phenanthrene is a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) that is derived from fossil fuels and is present in most PAH mixtures found in water, air and soil. It has been shown to affect cardiac function of vertebrates, including fish. We investigated the effects of phenanthrene on the intracellular calcium transient and the Na+/Ca2+ exchanger (NCX) current (INCX) in zebrafish (Danio rerio) ventricular cardiomyocytes using Fluo-4 AM imaging and whole-cell patch clamp, respectively. Phenanthrene exposure (25 μmol l-1) reduced the amplitude and slowed the rate of decay of Ca2+ transients. Phenanthrene also inhibited INCX with equal efficacy in forward and reverse mode. We conclude that phenanthrene disrupts Ca2+ handling in zebrafish ventricular myocytes, which could impact cardiac contractility.

title: A Knowledge Database of Physical Activity Interventions for Hypertension using Large Language Models
authorString: Li C, Obioha C, Cui X, Zhou X, Wang M.
abstractText: Physical exercise lowers blood pressure, but guidelines address broad populations and rarely consider age, comorbidities, medications or baseline severity. No structured, queryable database of exercise interventions for hypertension exists, and manual curation is not scalable. We present PAHD (Physical Activity for Hypertension Database), built with large language models (LLMs). An LLM screened 2,548 PubMed records by title and abstract, then full text, selecting 255 studies. LLMs extracted each study's groups, exercise protocols, patient characteristics and results; two LLMs cross-checked the study structure, and every value carries a verbatim quote. Code standardized and joined the extractions into 17,312 records from 254 studies, one per reported comparison. Against adjudicated benchmarks, screening reached 86.3% recall and 80.6% precision, and extraction recovered 90.1% of blood pressure values with 90.5% precision. A web portal matches patients' hypertension stage and comorbidities to studies. PAHD provides a structured evidence base for personalized exercise interventions on hypertension management.

title: Participant and practitioner experiences of the Supervised Pulmonary Hypertension Exercise Rehabilitation (SPHERe) trial: a qualitative process evaluation
authorString: Schultz EB, McGregor G, Bruce J, Ennis S, Sandhu H, Patel S, Heine P, Underwood M, Seers K.
abstractText:
Background:

Pulmonary Hypertension (PH) is a debilitating condition which can lead to avoidance of physical activity and reduced health-related quality of life (HRQoL). The Supervised Pulmonary Hypertension Exercise rehabilitation (SPHERe) multi-centre RCT found that remotely supervised online group exercise-based rehabilitation was safe and well tolerated, but not superior to a single one-to-one advice session for improving walking distance and HRQoL over 12 months. An embedded qualitative study aimed to explore participant and practitioner experiences of the trial and interventions. Design Qualitative process evaluation utilising semi-structured interviews. The framework method was used to analyse findings. Setting England and Scotland, UK. Participants Adults with PH living in the community. Results Twenty intervention participants, 20 usual care participants, and five intervention practitioners were interviewed. Barriers to participation in the SPHERe intervention group included finding time and being ill, whilst the dynamics of being in an online group were seen both as positive and negative. Enablers for participation included the support that came from a shared experience and a sense of belonging. Conclusion Despite a lack of clinical effectiveness, the SPHERe intervention was mostly well received by participants and practitioners. The main barrier was finding time to exercise. The main enabler was being in a group and the support this provided. Online group interventions should be considered important for future research and service models, whilst also appreciating the challenges associated with this mode of delivery.

title: Factors Influencing Proactive Health Behaviors Among Older Adults with Hypertension: A Qualitative Study
authorString: Min Kh, Li² Y, Hu H, Ye⁴ Y, Fang Y, Guan H.
abstractText: Background Older adults with hypertension and overweight or obesity face complex health management demands, including blood pressure control, weight management, and the long-term maintenance of multiple health behaviors. However, how proactive health behaviors are initiated, implemented, and maintained in this population remains insufficiently understood. Objective To explore proactive health behaviors and the factors influencing their initiation, implementation, and maintenance among older adults with hypertension and overweight or obesity, guided by ITHBC, and to inform targeted nursing support strategies. Methods A qualitative descriptive design was adopted. From July to August 2025, 15 older adults with hypertension and overweight or obesity were purposively recruited from the health management center of a tertiary hospital in western China and participated in individual, face-to-face, semi-structured interviews. Recruitment continued until data saturation was achieved. A hybrid deductive–inductive thematic analysis, informed by the ITHBC and guided by Braun and Clarke’s six-phase approach, was conducted. NVivo 15.0 was used to facilitate data management and coding. The study was reported in accordance with the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ). Results Three themes and nine subthemes were generated: (1) health-related cognition and behavioral beliefs influenced the initiation of proactive health behaviors, encompassing health knowledge, disease risk perception, self-efficacy, and health values; (2) self-regulation influenced the implementation and maintenance of proactive health behaviors, encompassing limited goal setting and self-monitoring, personal preferences, behavioral inertia, limited self-control, and established habits; and (3) social support and resource accessibility facilitated or constrained the implementation and maintenance of proactive health behaviors through professional healthcare support, family and peer support, and service and environmental accessibility. Conclusions Proactive health behaviors among older adults with hypertension and overweight or obesity were influenced by interconnected factors related to health-related cognition and behavioral beliefs, self-regulation, and social support and resource accessibility. Nursing practice should move beyond health information provision toward sustained behavioral support through individualized risk communication, support for goal setting and self-monitoring, habit formation, and integration of family, healthcare, and community resources to facilitate the implementation and long-term maintenance of proactive health behaviors.

title: Characterizing hypertension in activated PI3K delta syndrome: Findings from Epic Cosmos.
authorString: Santiago B, Keelin J, Sun X, Chang C.
abstractText: APDS is a rare inborn error of immunity with comorbidity patterns that have yet to be characterized at a large scale. Using Epic Cosmos, a de-identified electronic health record database, we conducted a retrospective, cross-sectional analysis of 866 patients identified by structured diagnosis codes (ICD-10: D84.81; SNOMED: 793412000). Findings revealed that hypertension was coded as affecting 28.5% of the cohort, with age-stratified analyses demonstrating higher prevalence among younger APDS patients compared with age-matched non-APDS peers. Among patients aged ≤50 years, hypertension prevalence was 24.05% in the APDS group compared with 10.89% in the age-matched non-APDS population (prevalence ratio 2.21, 95% CI, 1.90-2.57, P < 0.0001). This association remained prominent in a more specific APDS sensitivity cohort in which the base population required an APDS diagnosis, alongside an allergy and immunology encounter. The findings of this paper provide large-scale characterization of APDS and identify hypertension, particularly among younger APDS patients, as a potentially underrecognized comorbidity that warrants further investigation.

title: From Baveno VII to Baveno VIII: key innovations in risk stratification and personalized care for portal hypertension.
authorString: Téllez L, Donate Ortega J, Fortea JI, Baiges A, Alvarado-Tapias E, Albillos Martínez A.
abstractText: Portal hypertension is a major determinant of disease progression and clinical outcomes in cirrhosis. The Baveno consensus has progressively moved its focus from the treatment of established complications towards earlier risk stratification, prevention of decompensation and modification of the natural history of the disease. Baveno VIII consolidates and extends this approach across the different stages of advanced chronic liver disease. Non-invasive assessment of clinically significant portal hypertension is refined through the incorporation of spleen stiffness measurement and probabilistic models, while longitudinal assessment emphasizes the importance of updating risk according to the most recent evaluation. In compensated disease, prevention of first decompensation remains centred on aetiological treatment and carvedilol in patients with clinically significant portal hypertension, together with management of relevant modifiable factors. In decompensated cirrhosis, greater emphasis is placed on preventing further decompensation and considering transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) earlier in the disease course, with individualized patient selection, stent diameter and strategies to prevent and manage post-TIPS hepatic encephalopathy. Management of acute portal hypertension-related bleeding is further refined, particularly regarding the timing of pre-emptive TIPS and the treatment of gastric varices and vascular gastric lesions. Finally, updated criteria for hepatic recompensation establish durable clinical recovery as a meaningful therapeutic goal. These advances support a more individualized approach to portal hypertension, integrating disease stage, risk of progression and response to treatment throughout the course of cirrhosis.

title: Octyl gallate attenuates atherosclerosis by modulating PPARγ-associated cholesterol homeostasis and enhancing NRF2-NQO1 antioxidant defence.
authorString: Hua J, Yue X, Wu C, Wang J.
abstractText: Atherosclerosis (AS) is a vascular disease driven by dysregulated lipid metabolism, oxidative stress, and chronic inflammation. This study investigated the anti-atherosclerotic potential of octyl gallate (OG), a gallic acid derivative with anti-inflammatory and metabolic regulatory properties. In vitro, OG (20-50 μM) significantly attenuated oxidised low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL)-induced lipid accumulation in THP-1-derived macrophages. This effect was accompanied by increased expression of the cholesterol efflux-related genes ABCA1 and ABCG1, whereas OG had only limited effects on CD36 and SRA expression. In vivo, oral administration of OG (25 or 50 mg kg-1) for 3 months reduced atherosclerotic lesion formation in the aortic arch, whole aorta and aortic root of high-fat diet-fed Apoe-/- mice. OG also improved serum lipid profiles by reducing low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and total cholesterol levels, increasing high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) levels. In addition, OG decreased IL-1β and TNF-α expression in the aortic root. Network pharmacology, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations identified PPARγ as a potential molecular target of OG. Further experiments demonstrated that OG enhanced the expression of PPARγ, LXRα, ABCA1, and ABCG1 in ox-LDL-treated macrophages. Moreover, OG suppressed inflammatory responses and reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation while activating the NRF2-NQO11 antioxidant system and promoting NRF2 nuclear translocation. Collectively, these findings suggest that OG may exert anti-atherosclerotic effects by coordinating macrophage lipid metabolism, redox homeostasis, and inflammatory responses through the PPARγ-LXRα-ABCA1/ABCG1 axis and the NRF2-NQO1 antioxidant pathway, respectively. These results provide experimental evidence supporting the potential of OG as a candidate compound for the prevention and treatment of AS.

title: Genetic Parameters and Genome-Wide Association Analysis of Reproductive Traits in Egyptian Buffalo.
authorString: Amin AMS, El Nagar AG, Khalil MH, Abdel-Shafy H, Hegazy MM, Ashour AF, Salem MMI.

journal.title: Journal of animal breeding and genetics = Zeitschrift fur Tierzuchtung und Zuchtungsbiologie

abstractText: Reproductive efficiency is a crucial factor in the sustainability and profitability of buffalo production systems. However, genetic improvement of reproductive traits is challenging due to low heritability, environmental sensitivity, limited recording, and shrinking reference populations caused by crossbreeding. This study aimed to estimate genetic parameters and detect the genomic architecture of key reproductive traits in Egyptian buffalo using pedigree-based analyses and genome-wide association studies (GWAS). Over a 44-year period (1980-2024), reproductive records from five Egyptian experimental herds were analysed. The dataset comprised 2843 buffalo cows, sired by 140 bulls and out of 1328 dams. In total, 2359 records were available for age at first calving (AFC), 10,478 for gestation length (GL), 7966 for calving interval (CI), 6705 for days open (DO), and 12,909 for calving ease (CE) and stillbirth (SB). For genome-wide association analysis, 275 Egyptian buffaloes were genotyped using the Affymetrix Buffalo 90 K array, and 66,295 high-quality SNPs were retained after quality control. De-regressed proofs derived from pedigree-based genetic evaluations were used as response variables in a mixed linear model implemented in the rMVP package. Genome-wide association analysis identified putative genomic regions associated with GL, CI, CE, and SB, whereas no genome-wide significant associations were detected for AFC and DO. Functional annotation and QTL enrichment analyses were subsequently used to provide exploratory biological context for the identified genomic regions. Heritability estimates were generally low: 0.16 for AFC, 0.06 for GL, 0.02 for CI, 0.02 for DO, 0.18 for CE, and 0.06 for SB. Manhattan plots revealed that 15 genomic regions containing significant SNPs were identified on chromosomes 2, 4, 10, 12, 13, 15, 19, 20, and 25 for the reproductive traits of GL, CI, CE, and SB. These findings provide preliminary evidence of genomic regions potentially contributing to variation in reproductive traits in Egyptian buffalo, although the relatively small number of genotyped animals limits the power to detect and validate small effect loci. Seven significant genomic regions on chromosomes 10, 13, 15, 20, and 25 were associated with the GL trait. Additionally, three suggestive SNPs mapped to chromosomes 2 and 19 were associated with the CE trait, and three suggestive SNPs mapped on chromosome 12 were significantly associated with the SB trait. The results of KEGG enrichment analyses and QTL classification analyses for reproductive traits in Egyptian buffalo suggest that candidate genes within known QTL may be involved in complex biological networks involving immune competence, cellular homeostasis, and systemic physiological resilience. Among the enriched pathways, Fc gamma R-mediated phagocytosis, protein export, viral myocarditis, and arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC) were highlighted. Most annotated genomic regions (QTL) were related to reproductive traits (63.4%), followed by 17.3% for milk production traits, 9.95% for general production traits, 3.47% for meat and carcass traits, 3.71% for body conformation and robustness exterior traits, and 2.08% for health traits.

title: Associations between types of residential greenspace and depressive symptoms in older adults: the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
authorString: van Baar JM, James A, Chivardi M, Lane KJ, Gradus JL, Besser LM, Hirsch JA, Kaufman JD, James P, Jimenez MP.
abstractText: Residential greenspace may prevent older-adult depression, but it is unclear whether this depends on type of greenspace and population subgroup. We examined associations between six greenspace measures and depressive symptoms among 6,799 U.S. older adults in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (1-3 observations per participant in 2000-2012). Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Center for Epidemiological Studies Depression scale. Time-varying residential address-linked exposures included street-view-based vegetation (grass, trees, other, and total), satellite-based Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), and park access. In fully adjusted mixed-effects Poisson models, overall associations were null (symptom count ratios [CRs], 0.98-1.03 per SD increase). Associations varied by site, race/ethnicity, neighborhood socioeconomic status, and population density. In site-stratified analyses, fewer symptoms were associated with NDVI in New York, NY (CR=0.96, 95% CI: 0.92, 0.99), park access in Winston-Salem, NC (CR=0.95, 95% CI: 0.92, 0.99), and grass in Minneapolis, MN (CR=0.87, 95% CI: 0.79, 0.97). The greenspace metric most strongly associated with fewer symptoms differed across racial/ethnic groups. Greater street-level greenspace was associated with more symptoms in high-density areas. Greenspace-depression associations may therefore depend on greenspace type and context, suggesting that mental-health-oriented greenspace interventions should be tailored to local populations and environments.

title: Comparison of Classic Laryngeal Mask Airway and Endotracheal Intubation for Airway Management During Short Urologic Procedures in the Prone Position: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
authorString: Bafghi NN, Motlagh MS, Bafghi NN, Mirzaie V.
abstractText:
Background

Airway management in the prone position remains a major challenge in anesthesia, particularly during short urologic procedures. Although endotracheal intubation (ETT) is considered the standard technique, the Classic laryngeal mask airway (LMA) has emerged as a less invasive alternative in patients without an anticipated difficult airway. This study aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of Classic LMA versus ETT for airway management in prone-position urologic surgeries.

Methods

In this randomized clinical trial, 70 patients undergoing prone-position urologic surgery with an operative duration of ≤ 90 min were assigned to either the Classic LMA group or ETT group (n = 35 each). Primary outcomes included intraoperative ventilatory performance assessed by peak airway pressure (Ppeak), need for conversion of airway technique, and airway-related complications. Secondary outcomes included intraoperative hemodynamic and respiratory parameters, including heart rate (HR), systolic and diastolic blood pressure (SBP/DBP), oxygen saturation (SpO2), end-tidal carbon dioxide (ETCO2), Ppeak, minute ventilation (VE), and postoperative complications.

Results

Baseline demographic and perioperative characteristics were comparable between groups. No significant differences were observed between the Classic LMA and ETT groups regarding intraoperative hemodynamic variables, SpO2, ETCO2, or VE. Ppeak was significantly higher in the ETT group (p < 0.001). During recovery, significant time-related changes were observed in hemodynamic and respiratory parameters in both groups, although no clinically significant intergroup differences were identified. Postoperative complications, including sore throat and laryngospasm, were infrequent and comparable between groups.

Conclusion

Classic LMA provided airway maintenance and ventilation comparable to ETT in short prone-position urologic surgeries and may be considered as a feasible airway device in patients meeting appropriate airway assessment criteria. Trial Registration: Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT): IRCT20250729066688N1.

title: Cardiomyocyte Identity Crisis Without Regenerative Re-entry: A Multi-Scale Atlas of Incomplete Dedifferentiation and Intercellular Communication Rewiring in the Infarcted Human Heart
authorString: qiao s, Li L, He C, Li W.
abstractText:
Background:

Adult mammalian hearts regenerate poorly after myocardial infarction (MI) because cardiomyocytes largely, though not absolutely, exit the cell cycle during postnatal maturation, yet the molecular logic connecting maturation, disease-associated dedifferentiation, and intercellular communication remains unclear.

Methods:

Public single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomes of developing, adult, and infarcted human and mouse hearts (55,342 cardiomyocytes) are integrated with Visium spatial transcriptomics to reconstruct a cross-species maturation trajectory, a directional ligand–receptor communication atlas, and rare-event proliferation counts with donor-aware statistics.

Results:

MI cardiomyocytes show a partial identity erosion — a stress-associated myosin isoform switch, collapse of the ventricular identity factor IRX4, and maturation-score decline — without regenerative proliferative re-entry and without fetal transcription-factor re-activation; cycling nuclei remained exceedingly rare (<0.03%), a state corroborated by chromatin accessibility and human genetics, with only the MYC regulon passing transcriptome-wide correction. Inferred communication reorganization was confined to non-myocyte compartments and did not exceed donor-label permutation nulls; cardiomyocytes remained net receivers without gaining signalling authority. IRX4 knockdown in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes recapitulated this identity loss, including stress-gene induction and elevated NT-proBNP secretion, and IRX4 overexpression attenuated the adrenergic stress response in IRX4-intact cardiomyocytes (orthogonal rescue untested).

Conclusions:

These findings support a model of state–relationship decoupling, in which an intracellular cardiomyocyte identity crisis and an intercellular niche rewiring proceed independently — a decoupling we define operationally and test with donor-level null models and equivalence bounds — and may help explain the limited success of regenerative strategies that target either layer alone.

title: Atypical Spontaneous Cecal Perforation During Redo Kidney Transplant Post Heart-Kidney Transplantation.
authorString: Ripa V, Geffner SR, Hanlon M, Rosenzweig MG, Sun H.
abstractText: Colonic perforation postrenal transplantation is rare (0.5%-2.3% incidence) and often associated with sigmoid diverticulitis, with reported mortality rates of 25%-50%. Right-sided spontaneous colonic perforation is particularly uncommon. We describe a 44-year-old male with a history of combined heart-kidney transplantation who developed rapid-onset cecal perforation following repeat deceased donor kidney transplantation. Despite early return of bowel function, an aggressive bowel regimen, and minimal opioid exposure, he developed acute abdominal distention, nausea, and obstipation on postoperative Day 5. Although he remained afebrile without leukocytosis or peritoneal signs, imaging demonstrated marked colonic dilatation and pneumoperitoneum, prompting emergent surgical exploration. Isolated cecal perforation was identified and successfully managed with right hemicolectomy, primary anastomosis, and diverting ileostomy. The patient recovered with preserved allograft function. This case underscores the potential for atypical and insidious gastrointestinal complications in patients with prolonged and intensified immunosuppression and highlights the importance of early imaging and prompt surgical intervention. Heightened clinical suspicion is essential as retransplantation and multiorgan transplant populations continue to expand.

title: Late sodium current blockade produces genotype-dependent electrophysiological responses across five cardiomyopathy-associated hiPSC-CM lines
authorString: Mercola M, Abdelsayed M.
abstractText: Background and Purpose. Late sodium current inhibitors are expected to shorten the cardiac action potential. Whether that holds across genetically distinct hiPSC-derived cardiomyocyte lines has not been tested with adequate replication. Experimental Approach. Optical action potentials were recorded for 10 s, unpaced, at 100 frames per second: 1,289,329 cells from 4,002 wells across 35 plates. GS-967 was applied at 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 1.0 and 5.0 µM in five cardiomyopathy-associated lines. The continuous endpoint was action potential duration at 90 % repolarisation (APD90). Effects are within-plate differences from controls averaged across plates, with the standard error (SE) across plates; a claim required three plates. Key Results. GS-967 supplied 24 of 83 claim-ready silencing groups and 21 of 60 for APD90, and was the only compound in all five lines. Its APD90 effect was inconsistent in direction. In 15S1, APD90 shortened at all five concentrations (−202.5 ms, SE 101.8, 4 plates, at 0.05 µM). In isogenic 15S1-R943X it lengthened at all five (+170.0 ms, SE 89.6, 3 plates, at 5.0 µM). D4-R14del lengthened at every claim-ready concentration; D4-WT alternated in sign; C9-R14del lengthened in both of its claim-ready groups. The silent fraction rose above matched control in every group, by between +5.3 points (SE 6.0, 2 plates) and +53.7 points (SE 25.6, 3 plates), but concentration profiles were ordered in one line only. Conclusion and Implications. The direction of the APD90 response to late sodium current blockade differed between lines and was not uniformly a shortening.

title: Genomic Cardiomyocyte Maturation Enhancers: Lessons from Cardiac Development and RNA-Based Pharmacology
authorString: Jiang X, Keykhaei M, Barrett M, Yu K, Ekmekchyan M, Kafka G, Wang Y, Abel E, Huang J.
abstractText: Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) remain immature, hindering their utility in disease modeling, drug screening, and regenerative therapies. This review synthesizes recent advances revealing the critical role of genomic enhancers (distal cis-regulatory DNA elements) in orchestrating cardiomyocyte maturation, drawing parallels to developmental pathways. We highlight how specific enhancers, bound by transcription factors (TFs), dynamically regulate tissue structural integrity, ion handling, metabolic shifts, and TF networks through stage-specific epigenetic mechanisms. We organize enhancer-mediated maturation by the functional classes of target genes and propose a framework integrating TF cooperativity, epigenetic regulation, developmental timing, enhancer-derived RNAs, and dual DNA- and RNA-binding proteins. We also discuss computational strategies integrating epigenomic datasets and motif analysis to identify candidate maturation enhancers. We further review pharmacological approaches targeting enhancer regulators, RNA-binding proteins, and enhancer-associated RNAs, distinguishing established uses in cardiac disease from potential strategies for promoting maturation. Validating such enhancers will uncover critical regulatory mechanisms essential for hiPSC-CM maturation. This knowledge could improve hiPSC-derived models with the potential to significantly transform our understanding of cardiac pathobiology and lead to the development of novel therapies.

title: One trigger, two systems: post-infectious severe Guillain-Barre syndrome with concurrent central nervous system demyelination": a case report.
authorString: Numan M, Alhatou M, Hussain Z, Hussain M, Alhatou A, Hamad W.
abstractText: Combined central and peripheral demyelination is a rare but serious neurological condition that is associated with poor outcomes. We report a 31-year-old male presenting with rapidly progressive Acute inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy (AIDP) variant of Guillain-Barré syndrome following an upper respiratory tract infection. The course was complicated by respiratory failure requiring intubation and significant autonomic dysfunction. Despite treatment with intravenous immunoglobulin, there was minimal clinical improvement. Further imaging of the central nervous system revealed multiple acute demyelinating lesions involving the brain and spinal cord. The patient subsequently received plasmapheresis and high-dose intravenous steroids without significant neurological recovery. A severe hospital-acquired infection delayed rituximab initiation until four months after symptom onset; however, neurological recovery remained minimal. This case highlights the rare coexistence of post-infectious central and peripheral demyelination. Early recognition of central involvement in patients with poor response to standard GBS therapy may help guide escalation of immunotherapy and potentially improve outcomes.

title: Comparison of Two Puncture Approaches in Robot-Assisted Percutaneous Kyphoplasty for Upper Thoracic Osteoporotic Vertebral Compression Fractures.
authorString: Yang Y, Chen W, Qin R, Ren C.
abstractText:
Objective

This study aimed to compare the clinical efficacy and safety of the robot-assisted trans-costotransverse joint approach and transpedicular approach in the treatment of upper thoracic single-segment osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures (OVCFs).

Methods

The data of 60 patients who underwent robot-assisted percutaneous kyphoplasty (PKP) from October 2023 to January 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. According to the different surgical approaches, they were divided into two groups: trans-costotransverse joint group (Group A n = 30) and transpedicular group (Group B n = 30). Perioperative indicators and clinical outcomes were compared.

Results

The rate of satisfactory bone cement distribution was significantly higher in Group A than in Group B (90.0% vs. 66.7%, p = 0.028; OR = 4.50, 95% CI: 1.09-18.50), and the bone cement injection volume was greater (2.35 ± 0.34 mL vs. 2.13 ± 0.28 mL, p = 0.008), with mean difference (MD) = 0.22 mL (95% CI: 0.06-0.38 mL). The 1-year follow-up showed that the vertebral recollapse rate in Group A was significantly lower than that in Group B (3.3% vs. 20%, p = 0.044; OR = 0.14, 95% CI: 0.02-1.23). The incidence of bone cement leakage was lower in Group A than in Group B (6.7% vs. 26.7%, p = 0.038; OR = 0.20, 95% CI: 0.04-1.02). Although the VAS score, ODI indices, and local Cobb angle of the two groups were significantly improved compared with those before operation, there was no significant difference between the two groups.

Conclusion

In this retrospective analysis of patients with upper thoracic OVCF, robot-assisted trans-costotransverse joint PKP may result in a more favorable distribution of bone cement and improved short- to medium-term vertebral stability as compared with the transpedicular approach. This procedure shows acceptable safety profile, though further prospective studies are required to validate its clinical benefit.

title: Atypical Presentation of Ramsay Hunt Syndrome in an Immunocompromised Patient: A Case Report.
authorString: Rash DJ, Mangeni O.
abstractText: Ramsay Hunt syndrome (RHS), or herpes zoster oticus, is a rare neurological complication of varicella-zoster virus reactivation within the geniculate ganglion, leading to unilateral facial pain, facial paralysis, otalgia, sensorineural hearing loss, and a painful vesicular rash on the face or ear. Reactivation of the virus most often affects the vestibulocochlear (cranial nerve eight) and facial (cranial nerve seven) nerves in RHS. Early recognition of RHS is important as delays in treatment can lead to permanent facial paralysis, scarring, or irreversible sensorineural hearing loss. In this case, we examine an 84-year-old immunocompromised female patient whose diagnosis of RHS was delayed by multiple medical comorbidities and an atypical initial presentation.

title: HADS-Assessed Anxiety/Depression Status and Ocular Outcomes in Vision-Threatening Diabetic Retinopathy: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Li B, Jiang Y, Li C, Huang Y, Zhao S, Zhou C, Zheng Z, Zhang X.
abstractText:
Purpose

Vision-threatening diabetic retinopathy (VTDR) poses significant blindness risks and the study aimed to identify the impact of psychological factors on its ocular outcomes.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study enrolled 782 VTDR patients from three ophthalmological centers (2018-2021). DR severity was graded using ETDRS criteria. Primary outcomes included tractional retinal detachment (TRD) involving the fovea, neovascular glaucoma (NVG), final best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) <0.3, and recurrent vitreous hemorrhage (VH). Anxiety and depression were assessed via the hospital anxiety and depression scale (HADS). Univariable and multivariable logistic regression evaluated the associations between HADS scores and ocular outcomes.

Results

After a median follow-up of 24.8 months, depressive symptoms (HADS-D ≥8) were associated with higher rates of BCVA <0.3 (67.8% vs. 57.2%, p = 0.033) and NVG (13.6% vs. 6.9%, p = 0.020). Recurrent VH was more frequent in patients with anxiety (21.0% vs. 10.6%, p = 0.031) or depression (20.3% vs. 10.7%, p = 0.045). Multivariable logistic analysis revealed that each 1-point increase in HADS-D score significantly increased adjusted odds of TRD (aOR = 1.06, 95% CI: 1.01-1.11), BCVA <0.3 (aOR = 1.07, 95% CI: 1.02-1.11), recurrent VH (aOR = 1.09, 95% CI: 1.02-1.17), and NVG (aOR = 1.10, 95% CI: 1.03-1.17; all p < 0.05). There was a consistent positive gradient between HADS severity and adverse outcomes.

Conclusion

Depressive symptoms are independently associated with worse ocular prognoses in VTDR patients. Systematic psychological screening and intervention is essential to mitigate vision deterioration risk in this population.

title: Aquaporin water channels: distribution, physiology, pathophysiology, and relevance as therapeutic targets.
authorString: Wang L, Luo Y, Deng X, Chen J, Wang L, Wu T.
abstractText: Aquaporins (AQPs) represent a class of integral membrane proteins that function as selective water channels, facilitating the transit of water molecules across biological membranes. Under specific conditions, these proteins may also mediate the permeation of small solutes, including glycerol, hydrogen peroxide, urea, carbon dioxide, and ammonia. Investigations into AQPs have unveiled distinctive structural attributes and functional properties. Evidence indicates that AQPs are broadly distributed across diverse tissues and organ systems in humans, contributing to essential physiological processes. An expanding body of literature highlights the involvement of AQPs in disease pathogenesis and progression, particularly in cellular behaviors such as proliferation and motility, pulmonary gas exchange, and the modulation of non-canonical signaling pathways. This review comprehensively outlines the tissue-specific and subcellular distribution profiles, physiological roles, and regulatory mechanisms associated with AQPs. It further characterizes the alterations in AQP functionality under pathological states, delineates their involvement and mechanistic contributions to multisystem disorders, and provides an overview of therapeutic strategies targeting AQPs, along with their translational prospects. In addition, key gaps in current knowledge are identified, and pivotal research directions, such as tissue-specific modulation and the design of targeted inhibitors and activators, are proposed to advance the translational application of AQPs as diagnostic and therapeutic targets.

title: Respiratory pathogens across rural populations: general practice patients with community-acquired pneumonia, residents, and goat farmers.
authorString: Roof I, Lotterman A, de Rooij MMT, Meijer A, Yzermans J, van der Giessen JWB, Smit LAM, van Gageldonk-Lafeber AB.
abstractText:
Background

Residents living near goat farms (< 2000 m) in the Netherlands have consistently shown an elevated risk of pneumonia, yet the pathogens underlying this association remain unknown. This study assessed the presence of 33 respiratory pathogens, including bacteria, viruses, and fungi, across rural populations with different goat farm exposures.

Methods

This cross-sectional study included general practitioner (GP)-diagnosed pneumonia patients (PP; n = 108), non-farming rural residents without pneumonia (NFR; n = 200), and goat farm workers (GFW; n = 91). Oropharyngeal and nasopharyngeal swabs were collected and analyzed by a multiplex and two additional PCR test targeting in total 12 bacteria, 20 viruses and 1 fungus. Between-group differences in detection were assessed by Fisher's exact tests. Logistic regression analyses were performed to assess associations between pathogen detection and residential proximity to goat farming and other covariates.

Results

Presence of any of the examined pathogens was highest in the PP group (94.5%), followed by GFW (88.8%), and NFR (70%). The most frequently detected pathogens overall were Haemophilus influenzae, Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Moraxella catarrhalis, and rhinovirus. Of these, M. catarrhalis and S. pneumoniae were significantly more often detected in PP, whereas Salmonella spp. and S. aureus were more frequently detected in GFW. Eight pathogens, including Coxiella burnetii, were not detected. Age, season of sampling, smoking and other covariates were significantly associated with certain bacteria and viruses. However, no associations were identified between residential proximity to goat farming and detection of specific pathogens in NFR and PP.

Conclusions

Respiratory pathogens were detected in nearly all PP, while substantial proportions of positives were also observed in GFW and NFR, likely reflecting (transient) colonization rather than active infection. Detection of the examined pathogens was not associated with residential proximity to goat farms, suggesting that these pathogens do not explain the observed increased pneumonia risk among nearby non-farming residents. As a substantial proportion of the Dutch population (~ 7%) lives within 2,000 m of a commercial goat farm, and goat farming is expanding globally, further research efforts, including microbiologic diagnostics and surveillance, are needed to elucidate the mechanisms underlying the increased pneumonia risk among nearby residents.

title: Brain tissue pulsation responses to a low‐level expiratory resistance manoeuvre: A pilot healthy volunteer study
authorString: Nicholls J, Chung E, Ince J, Pallett E, Minhas J, Lecchini‐Visintini A.

title: Concordance Between Trial Efficacy and Real-World Effectiveness of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Hassanien A, Elhenedy M, Elgohari M.
abstractText: Randomized trials established the efficacy of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). We assessed whether their effectiveness in routine practice is concordant with trial efficacy, appraising and pooling each evidence stream separately. PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from January 1, 2015 to July 2026 for randomized trials and comparative observational studies of SGLT2 inhibitors vs. placebo or nonuse in adults with left ventricular ejection fraction ≤40% reporting mortality or heart failure hospitalization. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Adjusted all-cause mortality was pooled by random-effects meta-analysis with the Hartung-Knapp adjustment; other outcomes were synthesized narratively. Trial and observational estimates were never combined, and certainty was graded with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) criteria. Eleven studies were included (two trials and nine observational). For all-cause mortality, the pooled observational HR (0.75, 95% CI 0.71-0.79; I² = 0%) indicated a larger apparent benefit than the pooled trial estimate (HR 0.87, 0.77-0.98). In one registry, the association attenuated to borderline nonsignificance after adjustment for background therapy. For heart failure hospitalization, a consistent trial benefit (HR 0.69, 0.62-0.78) contrasted with attenuated or null real-world estimates (HR 0.84-1.03). Real-world mortality associations with SGLT2 inhibitors in HFrEF are directionally concordant with trial efficacy, but their larger magnitude most plausibly reflects residual confounding, including co-prescription of other guideline-directed therapy. Real-world hospitalization estimates diverged from trials, likely reflecting outcome ascertainment. With very low-certainty observational evidence, the trial estimate remains the best guide to causal benefit.

title: Identifying the Optimal Respiratory Muscle Training Intervention for Heart Failure Patients: A Network Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
authorString: Tavakoli K, Ansari A, Alaei E, Jahanfard R, Mansouri ES, Ganjalikhani M, Selk-Ghaffari M, Shahi MHP, Memari AH.
abstractText:
Background

Respiratory muscle training interventions have shown promising results in improving functional capacity, quality of life, and prognosis of heart failure patients. However, the optimal respiratory muscle training intervention for rehabilitation remains unclear.

Methods

A systematic review and network meta-analysis was conducted by searching PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane Library until September 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating the effect of respiratory muscle training interventions on maximum inspiratory pressure (MIP), maximum expiratory pressure (MEP), forced vital capacity (FVC), forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV₁), six-minute walk test (6MWT), peak oxygen uptake (VO2max), quality of life, and dyspnea. Random-effect network meta-analysis was used to estimate pooled mean differences. Interventions were ranked using the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA).

Results

A total of 88 RCTs (5,757 participants) were included. Medium-intensity inspiratory muscle training (IMT) ranked highest for improving MIP (SUCRA: 89.8%). Combined aerobic and resistance exercise was optimal for MEP (SUCRA: 79.3%). Aerobic training showed the greatest benefit for FVC (SUCRA: 94.8%) and FEV₁ (SUCRA: 93.8%). Medium-intensity IMT was most effective for enhancing 6MWT performance (SUCRA: 81.6%). A combination of high-intensity IMT with aerobic training yielded the largest gains in improving VO2max (SUCRA: 74.7%), quality of life (SUCRA: 81.4%), and reducing dyspnea (SUCRA: 89.3%).

Conclusion

Respiratory muscle training interventions provide different benefits across key rehabilitation outcomes in heart failure. Accordingly, rehabilitation strategies may be optimized by aligning exercise modalities with patients' rehabilitation needs, preferences, and clinical profiles, rather than adopting a uniform prescription.

title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitor Use and Levels of Hemoglobin, Markers of Iron Metabolism, and Erythropoiesis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
authorString: Yang Y, Yang C, Wang Y, Rawee P, Cases A, Leaf DE, Del Vecchio L, Muka T, Heerspink HJL, Gansevoort RT, Eisenga MF.
abstractText:
Importance

In randomized clinical trials, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor use was associated with increased hemoglobin and hematocrit compared with placebo. However, the magnitude and importance of this association remain unclear.

Objective

To evaluate the associations between SGLT2 inhibitor use and levels of hemoglobin, hematocrit, and markers of iron metabolism and erythropoiesis compared with placebo or active comparator.

Data sources

PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched from inception to July 22, 2026.

Study selection

Randomized, double-masked clinical trials comparing SGLT2 inhibitor use with placebo or active comparators in patients with 1 or more of the following conditions: cardiovascular disease, diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease.

Data extraction and synthesis

Three reviewers independently extracted data and results were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis.

Main outcomes and measures

Primary outcomes were changes in hemoglobin and hematocrit. Secondary outcomes were changes in red blood cell concentration, erythropoietin (EPO), and iron measures (serum iron, ferritin, transferrin saturation, and hepcidin).

Results

A total of 85 randomized clinical trials were analyzed (median [IQR] duration, 24 [12-32] weeks), including 70 543 participants (mean [SD] age, 62.4 [9.4] years; 25 334 female [35.9%]). Mean (SD) baseline hemoglobin was 13.6 (1.5) g/dL; baseline hematocrit was 41.5% (4.9). Seventy-eight clinical trials (67 208 participants) compared SGLT2 inhibitors with placebo, and 7 clinical trials (3335 participants) used active comparators, most commonly sitagliptin (2 trials [1158 participants]). From baseline to follow-up, hemoglobin changed by 0.55 g/dL (95% CI, 0.49 to 0.61 g/dL; P < .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group, and -0.08 g/dL (95% CI, -0.13 to -0.03 g/dL; P = .003) in the control group (difference, 0.60 g/dL; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.66 g/dL; P < .001). From baseline to follow-up, hematocrit changed by 2.17% (95% CI, 1.95% to 2.39%; P < .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group and -0.13% (95% CI, -0.28% to 0.01%; P = .07) in the control group (difference, 2.36%; 95% CI, 2.19% to 2.52%; P < .001). Of the 6 secondary outcomes, 4 showed significant associations with SGLT2 inhibitors, including increased EPO (2.35 mIU/mL in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs 0.04 mIU/mL in control group; difference, 2.11 mIU/mL [95% CI, 0.5-3.71 mIU/mL]; P = .01) and decreased transferrin saturation (-2.2% in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs -0.10% in control group; difference, -0.84% [95% CI, -1.21% to -0.47%]; P < .001).

Conclusions and relevance

In a meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials, compared with control, SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with small statistically significant increases in hemoglobin and hematocrit levels. The clinical significance of these findings is unclear.

title: Management of shift work disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine systematic review, meta-analysis, and GRADE assessment.
authorString: Wright KP, Abbott SM, Ashbrook L, Drake CL, Flynn-Evans E, Framnes-DeBoer S, Kazmi U, Keeler K, McCall C, Morgan R, Shaffer-Hodgeman T, Trotti LM.

journal.title: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine

abstractText:
Introduction

The purpose of this systematic review is to provide supporting evidence for a clinical practice guideline on the treatment of adults with shift work disorder (SWD).

Methods

The American Academy of Sleep Medicine commissioned a task force of six experts in sleep and circadian medicine. A systematic review was conducted to identify randomized controlled trials, observational studies, and treatment trials in which treatments for the symptoms of excessive sleepiness and/or sleep disturbance/insomnia in adults with SWD, and for circadian adaptation to shift work schedules was tested. Evidence from controlled laboratory trials of simulated shift work and of field-based trials of shift workers with and without a diagnosis of SWD was included. Statistical analyses were performed to determine the significance of critical and important outcomes and clinically meaningful thresholds were set to determine the clinical relevance of treatments on the outcomes examined, where possible. Finally, the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) process was used to assess the evidence for making recommendations.

Results

The literature search resulted in 3,045 articles; 118 studies provided data suitable for statistical analyses. The task force provided a detailed summary of the evidence along with the quality of evidence, the balance of benefits and harms, patient values and preferences, and resource use considerations.

title: Blood Pressure Management Before Intravenous Thrombolysis in Acute Ischemic Stroke: Rethinking Treatment Thresholds.
authorString: Aslan T, Bath PM, Kelly PJ, Nederkoorn PJ, Dippel D, Van der Worp HB, Hill MD, Demchuk AM, Wu B, Wang X, Song L, Anderson C, Menon BK, Kruyt N.

journal.title: International journal of stroke : official journal of the International Stroke Society

abstractText: BackgroundElevated blood pressure (BP) is common after acute ischemic stroke (AIS), but it is unclear if it should be lowered. Lowering elevated BP may compromise the ischemic brain, while the time taken to lower BP may delay or even exclude patients from receiving intravenous thrombolysis (IVT).AimTo review the rationale, guideline recommendations, and clinical evidence informing pre-IVT BP management, with a specific focus on patients presenting with a BP above the current guideline thresholds (BP ≥185/110 mmHg).Summary of reviewCerebral autoregulation is impaired in AIS, both in the core and penumbra, creating vulnerability to harm from both excessive hypertension and BP reduction. Major trials of early or intensive BP-lowering in AIS (INTERACT4, MR-ASAP, and RIGHT-2) have either shown neutral or harmful effects with BP reduction. In the TRUTH study, a cluster-based observational comparison, centers that actively treated elevated BP before IVT achieved higher IVT rates but no better 90-day functional outcome, with a non-significant trend toward worse outcomes in the active-treatment arm. No randomized trial has helped define the optimal systolic BP target, speed of reduction, preferred antihypertensive agent, or balance of risks vs. benefits of BP reduction. prior to IVT.ConclusionsCurrent practice on BP treatment prior to IVT is guided by historical thresholds and expert consensus rather than robust evidence. Major gaps persist with respect to causal associations, individualized treatment targets, and safe BP reduction strategies. Higher quality data are needed to establish evidence-based BP management for patients presenting ≥185/110 mmHg otherwise eligible for IVT, to uniform practice towards improved patient outcomes.

title: 2026 THS guidelines for the management of hypertension in older adults: Developed by the task force on the management of hypertension of the Taiwan Hypertension Society (THS) and endorsed by the Taiwan Society of Cardiology (TSOC), Taiwan Association of Gerontology and Geriatrics (TAGG), and Taiwan Society of Family Medicine (TSFM).
authorString: Cheng HM, Yeh CF, Wu CC, Chen MY, Chang YY, Tsai HH, Chen ZW, Lee HC, Pan HY, Hsu RY, Chen FY, Yeh WY, Lin TC, Lee CW, Hung CL, Tsai HY, Li CH, Hsiao CH, Lee YH, Wu YW, Lin TH, Chao TH, Huang YT, Wang TD, Kao HL, Lin HJ, Lai TS, Cheng SY, Chan DC, Lin YH.

journal.title: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi

abstractText: The 2026 Taiwan Hypertension Society Guidelines for the Management of Hypertension in Older Adults provide an evidence-based framework tailored to the needs of an aging population. Recommendations were developed using PICO-formulated clinical questions, systematic evidence appraisal, and the GRADE approach, integrating evidence from randomized trials, observational studies, and expert consensus. A total of 63 actionable recommendations address diagnostic evaluation, blood pressure measurement and monitoring, lifestyle modification, blood pressure targets, and pharmacological therapy, with input from a multidisciplinary guideline panel and an external interdisciplinary expert committee. The guidelines emphasize age-related characteristics of hypertension, including arterial stiffness, salt sensitivity, frailty, orthostatic hypotension, cognitive vulnerability, atrial fibrillation, and multimorbidity. Standardized blood pressure measurement using validated oscillometric devices and regular out-of-office monitoring are strongly recommended. Blood pressure targets are specified according to age groups and common comorbid conditions. Non-pharmacological interventions, particularly dietary sodium reduction, potassium-enriched salt substitutes, healthy dietary patterns, and physical activity, are encouraged. Pharmacological treatment prioritizes individualized therapy and avoidance of overtreatment, especially in frail older adults. Endorsed by relevant national societies, these guidelines offer a practical approach to improving hypertension management and cardiovascular outcomes in older adults.

title: Medicinal plants and functional foods with diuretic effects: A nutraceutical approach to cardiovascular health.
authorString: Mattioli LB, Corazza I, Budriesi R, Camarda L, Aicardi M, Carelli M, Spadotto A, Diemberger I.
abstractText: Fluid and electrolyte balance is essential for cardiovascular homeostasis, and disturbances in renal sodium and water handling contribute to hypertension, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease. Although pharmacological diuretics remain a cornerstone of therapy, their long-term use may be limited by electrolyte disturbances, neurohormonal activation, and reduced tolerability in frail or polymedicated patients. This narrative review examines current experimental and clinical evidence on medicinal plants and functional foods with mild diuretic or renal-vascular effects, highlighting their potential role as adjunctive strategies. Several botanicals, including Hibiscus sabdariffa, Orthosiphon stamineus, Urtica dioica, and Taraxacum officinale, exhibit natriuretic, aquaretic, antioxidant, and vasorelaxant properties through multifactorial mechanisms. However, clinical evidence remains limited, heterogeneous, and frequently derived from multicomponent formulations, hindering the attribution of specific effects. In addition, dietary sources such as potassium-rich foods, herbal infusions, and whole grains may modulate fluid balance and vascular function. Still, their interaction with standard diuretic therapy warrants careful consideration. Potential nutrient-drug interactions may result in either synergistic effects or adverse outcomes, including hyperkalaemia, dehydration, or altered drug absorption. Overall, selected medicinal plants and functional foods may provide supportive benefits in early-stage cardiovascular and metabolic conditions. Still, their clinical use should remain adjunctive and individualized, pending further standardized, well-designed clinical trials.

title: Evaluating the feasibility and impact of a remote, algorithm-based blood pressure titration program in postpartum women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: the postpartum algorithm for text-based hypertension management (PATH) randomized clinical trial.
authorString: Vullikanti M, Del Cueto P, Vivaldi M, Scott N, James K, Goldfarb I, Sarma A.
abstractText:
Objective

Optimal postpartum management of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) remains unknown. This pilot randomized control trial explored feasibility and safety of an algorithmic, text-based intervention targeting a blood pressure (BP) < 130/80 mmHg (in accordance with American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association recommendations - ACC/AHA) on hypertension management at 6 weeks postpartum as compared with routine care.

Study design

200 postpartum patients with HDP (excluding chronic hypertension) were randomized at hospital discharge for delivery or postpartum HDP admission from a tertiary care center in a 1:1 fashion to the intervention (targeting a blood pressure < 130/ 80 mmHg) or routine care. Patients and clinicians were blinded with respect to randomization.

Main outcome measures

The primary outcome was the proportion of patients who achieved normotension as defined by the ACC/AHA (systolic blood pressure < 130 mmHg). Secondary outcomes were frequency of medication titration, outpatient visits, and non-billable healthcare encounters.

Results

The virtual intervention did not differ from routine care with respect to the primary outcome using office- ascertained BPs (72% intervention vs 74% routine care, p = 0.83). At 6 weeks postpartum, clinic systolic BP did not differ by group (121 mmHg vs 119 mmHg, p = 0.3), though home-reported SBPs during the same period were lower among those randomized to the intervention (119 mmHg vs 125 mmHg, p < 0.001). No adverse events occurred in either group.

Conclusions

As compared to routine care delivered at a tertiary care center, no differences were observed with respect to systolic BP at 6 weeks postpartum using a virtual, algorithm-based intervention. A high proportion of patients in both randomized groups achieving normotension by ACC/AHA targets without adverse events.

title: COMPANION-002: A Randomized Phase 2/3 Trial of Tovecimig Plus Paclitaxel versus Paclitaxel Alone as a Second-line Therapy in Patients with Advanced Biliary Tract Cancer.
authorString: Azad NS, Hu I, Pathak P, Sahin I, Aranha O, Iyer R, Heestand G, Liao CY, Hochster HS, Kalyan A, El-Khoueiry A, Paulson AS, Kelley RK, Borad M, Goyal L, Sirard CA, Schuetz TJ, Javle M.

journal.title: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology

abstractText:
Purpose

Patients with previously treated biliary tract cancer (BTC) have a short median overall survival (OS), and few treatment options. Tovecimig, a bispecific antibody to delta-like ligand-4 and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-A, was evaluated in combination with paclitaxel in COMPANION-002, a randomized phase 2/3 study in pretreated patients with advanced BTC.

Methods

Patients with advanced BTC with one prior systemic therapy were randomized to paclitaxel (80 mg/m2; days 1, 8 and 15) with or without tovecimig (10 mg/kg; days 1 and 15). The primary endpoint was RECIST v1.1-defined objective response rate (ORR) as assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR). Secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS) and OS. Crossover from the paclitaxel control arm to tovecimig plus paclitaxel was permitted following BICR-confirmed progression.

Results

168 patients were randomized 2:1 to tovecimig+paclitaxel (n=111) or paclitaxel alone (n=57). Tovecimig+paclitaxel significantly improved BICR-assessed ORR (18.0% vs 5.3%; P=.0228) and PFS (4.7 vs 2.6 months; hazard ratio [HR], 0.44; P<.0001). Among 31 patients (54%) who crossed over, post-progression PFS (time from crossover to subsequent second progression) exceeded initial PFS (PFS from randomization to initial progression on paclitaxel; 3.5 vs 1.9 months; HR, 0.40; P=.0035). Overall, 142 patients (85%) received tovecimig; no difference in OS was observed (HR, 1.05; P=.779). The most common treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) with tovecimig+paclitaxel were hypertension (69.4%) and fatigue (66.7%). Grade ≥3 TEAEs occurred in 93.5% and 64.2% of patients treated with tovecimig+paclitaxel and paclitaxel alone, respectively.

Conclusion

Tovecimig combined with paclitaxel significantly improved ORR and PFS versus paclitaxel alone as second-line therapy for patients with BTC.

title: An α1D-adrenergic receptor vaccine protects against HFpEF in mice.
authorString: Wu J, Shi D, Wang Y, Ma Q, Chen H, Huang J, Ma W, Lama E, Liu C, Gao R, Wang Y, Ni X, Liao Y, Qiu Z, Zhou Z.
abstractText:
Aims

Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) remains a global clinical challenge with high mortality and restricted therapeutic options. Persistent sympathetic nervous system (SNS) overactivation, systemic metabolic dysregulation, and chronic inflammation are hallmarks of HFpEF pathogenesis. We developed ADRQβ-004, a novel therapeutic vaccine targeting α1D-adrenergic receptor (α1D-AR), to evaluate its potential in mitigating HFpEF.

Methods and results

A "two-hit" HFpEF mouse model was established in 6-week-old male ApoE-/- mice via high-fat diet and Nω- nitro-L-arginine methyl ester administration for 17 weeks. Mice were subcutaneously immunized with five doses of ADRQβ-004. We comprehensively assessed blood pressure, glucose/lipid metabolism, diastolic function, and cardiac remodeling. Pericardial adipose tissue (PAT) was specifically analyzed via histology, RNA-seq, and biochemical assays. Furthermore, a monoclonal antibody (ADR-004) was employed in an adipocyte-cardiomyocyte co-culture system to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. ADRQβ-004 elicited high and sustained titer of specific antibody, demonstrating robust immunogenicity. Vaccination significantly improved glucose tolerance, insulin sensitivity, and lipid profiles in HFpEF mice. Morphological and functional analyses revealed that ADRQβ-004 markedly attenuated left ventricular remodeling, diastolic dysfunction, and myocardial mitochondrial impairment. Notably, the vaccine suppressed PAT inflammation and metabolic dysfunction. Mechanistically, blockade of α1D-AR via ADR-004 activated the PPARβ/AMPK/PGC1-α signaling pathway in adipocytes, which subsequently modulated adipocyte-cardiomyocyte crosstalk, leading to enhanced myocardial mitochondrial function and improved HFpEF phenotypes.

Conclusion

The ADRQβ-004 vaccine ameliorates HFpEF by modulating adipocyte-cardiomyocyte crosstalk through the PPARβ/AMPK/PGC1-α pathway. These findings suggest that ADRQβ-004 may serve as a promising immunomodulatory strategy for HFpEF research.

title: Changes in management of FETO-treated infants with severe CDH.
authorString: Jeffreys E, Jenkinson A, Kronfli R, Billington J, Bhat R, Nanjundappa M, Ali K, Muntean A, Harman K, Lawton A, Ashoor G, Nicolaides K, Dassios T, Greenough A, Harris C.
abstractText:
This study aims to evaluate changes in outcomes and management of infants with severe congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) undergoing fetoscopic endoluminal tracheal occlusion (FETO) across two eras, and to compare outcomes by side of defect over the last decade. Retrospective review of liveborn infants with severe CDH (observed to expected lung to head ratio [O/E LHR] < 0.25 left-sided; < 0.45 right-sided) who underwent FETO at King's College Hospital, London, UK, and survived to delivery. Fifty-eight infants were included across two 5-year periods (2002-2007 and 2020-2025). Survival improved from 44.1% to 70.8% (p = 0.044). Right-sided defects were more common in the second epoch (9% versus 54%, p < 0.001). All infants in the second era had echocardiography-guided inotropic and ventilatory management, which was not universally available earlier. In the second epoch surgical repair occurred later (4.0 versus 6.5 days, p = 0.018), repair by two-stage abdominal closure (laparostomy) increased from 0% to 77.8% (p < 0.001) and recurrence fell from 33 to 0% (p = 0.042). Mechanical ventilation, oxygen therapy and admission were longer latterly. In thirty-one infants delivered between 2015 and 2025, preterm prelabour rupture of membranes (PPROM) occurred in 67% of left-versus 92% of right-sided CDH, but at an earlier gestational age in left (p = 0.032). Left CDH infants had longer duration of mechanical ventilation (p = 0.04) and hospital stay (p = 0.006) with no mortality difference (exploratory).

Conclusion

 Survival of FETO-treated severe CDH infants improved from 44 to 71% alongside later repair, staged abdominal closure and echocardiography-guided management. Left-sided defects had greater respiratory morbidity and longer admission than right-sided defects without changing survival.

What is known

• FETO improves survival in severe left-sided CDH, but postnatal management has changed substantially since its introduction.

What is new

• Survival of FETO-treated severe CDH rose from 44 to 71% over two decades despite more right-sided defects. Repair occurred later, following haemodynamic and respiratory stabilisation (as guided by echocardiography) with staged abdominal closure in 77.8% of recent repairs; recurrence decreased from 33 to 0%. • Left-sided CDH infants had greater respiratory morbidity and length of stay than right-sided CDH infants, without a significant difference in mortality.

title: Long-term cost-effectiveness of CKD screening in middle-aged adults.
authorString: Jalkanen K, Aku-Ville L, Piia L, Jari H, Emmi R, Piia K, Satu M, Tarja M, Mikko T, Janne M.

journal.title: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association

abstractText:
Background and hypothesis

Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is common in Finland and frequently remains undiagnosed until advanced stages. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) slow CKD progression and reduce cardio-renal events when used in addition to Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System inhibitor (RAASi) treatment. We hypothesized that a one-time CKD screening program using measurements of estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), followed by SGLT2i and RAASi treatment for identified CKD, would be cost-effective in Finland.

Methods

We developed a cohort-based Markov model to simulate lifetime CKD progression in a Finnish cohort aged 55 years under two strategies: (1) current practice (no screening) and (2) one-time screening with follow-up and SGLT2i and RAASi treatment for screen-positive CKD (eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m² and/or UACR ≥3 mg/mmol; confirmed on a repeat sample after ≥ 3 months to establish chronicity). All CKD stages (G1-G5, dialysis, transplant, and death) were included in the model, and screening could detect CKD at any stage, although the incremental detection was concentrated in earlier, previously undiagnosed stages (G1-G3). Outcomes included discounted costs, quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), life years, and clinical outcomes (acute kidney function decline, heart-failure hospital days, dialysis and transplant patient-years, and deaths). Results are reported as means with 95% confidence intervals (CI).

Results

Screening increased discounted lifetime costs per person by €907 (95% CI €334-2 553) and QALYs by 0.14 (95% CI 0.07-0.31), yielding an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of €6 478/QALY. Screening increased life years by 0.30. Screening reduced acute kidney function decline (0.88 vs 0.90 events/person), heart-failure hospital days (6.47 vs 6.69 days/person), dialysis exposure (0.29 vs 0.32 patient-years/person) and transplant exposure (0.13 vs 0.14 patient-years/person).

Conclusions

In Finns aged 55 years, one-time CKD screening with eGFR/UACR followed by SGLT2i and RAASi treatment improves long-term outcomes and is likely cost-effective.

title: Minimally invasive anaortic quadruple and quintuple coronary artery bypass grafting: Feasibility and early outcomes of automated titanium suture fastener - a case series.
authorString: Grujic D, Gazibara T, Kokotovic T, Radmili O, Lazovic D, Djordjevic A, Aleksic V.
abstractText: ObjectiveTo describe the feasibility and early outcomes of automated terminal suture fastening and conventional hand tying during complex anaortic total-arterial minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS-CABG).MethodsThis retrospective, descriptive, single-center surgical case series included 12 patients who underwent elective anaortic off-pump MICS-CABG between January 2024 and May 2025. The first seven patients underwent conventional hand-tied terminal suture securing, whereas the subsequent five underwent automated terminal suture fastening, reflecting the chronological introduction of the device later in the surgeon's experience. Nine patients underwent quadruple and three underwent quintuple bypass grafting. Clinical follow-up was performed at 30 days and six months after surgery, with CT coronary angiography performed at six months.ResultsAll patients were male, with a mean age of 69.4 ± 7.5 years. Mean operating-room time was 373.0 ± 60.1 minutes overall, 384.3 ± 50.0 minutes in the hand-tied group, and 358.0 ± 75.6 minutes in the automated fastener group. No device-related technical failures, incomplete deployments, or device-related anastomotic revisions occurred. No deaths, perioperative myocardial infarctions, strokes, conversions to sternotomy or cardiopulmonary bypass, or repeat revascularizations occurred. Two patients developed pleural effusion, one developed atrial fibrillation, and one patient with pleural effusion required rehospitalization. At six-month CT angiography, all 30 arterial grafts were evaluable; 28 were classified as FitzGibbon grade A, one as grade B, and one as grade O. Both non-grade-A findings occurred in the hand-tied group, whereas all 13 grafts in the automated fastener group were grade A.ConclusionsIn this selected 12-patient, single-surgeon case series, automated terminal suture fastening using COR-KNOT® MICRO was technically achievable during complex anaortic total-arterial MICS-CABG without observed device-related failure. The small sample, chronological device introduction, operator learning curve, and short follow-up preclude conclusions regarding comparative operating-room time, safety, or graft outcomes. Larger prospective studies with anastomosis-specific timing and graft-level follow-up are required.

title: Low-to-moderate dose ionizing radiation and cerebrovascular disease mortality in U.S. radiologic technologists, 1983-2021
authorString: Little MP, Linet MS, van der Velpen IF, Kwon T, Han HG, Lee C, Cahoon EK, Mai JZ, Miller JS, Alexander BH, Kitahara CM.
abstractText:
Background:

Substantial data confirm the association of cerebrovascular disease (CeVD) with high-dose (>1 Gy) ionizing radiation exposures, but less is known about risks at low- to moderate doses (<1 Gy). A few studies have reported increased CeVD risks at doses <500 mGy, but none of these provided data on CeVD risks by subtype.
