Few studies have investigated the potential modifying effects of age, sex, and other major CeVD risk factors.

Methods:

110,368 radiologic technologists certified for 2 years during 1926-1982 with at least one baseline survey response (1983-1998) were followed-up through December 2021. Linear proportional hazards regression analysis was performed of cumulative occupational radiation exposure and CeVD mortality risks, using estimated thyroid-absorbed dose as a proxy for carotid artery dose, in addition to brain and badge dose.

Results:

During a median 35.1 (maximum 38.9) years of follow-up, 1,199 deaths from CeVD (634 ischemic stroke, 369 hemorrhagic stroke, 196 other types) were identified. Cumulative thyroid dose (mean/maximum=68.4/2784 mGy) was positively associated with deaths from overall CeVD (excess hazard ratio [EHR]/100 mGy=0.07 95% CI 0.01, 0.16, p=0.01) and ischemic stroke (EHR/100 mGy=0.10, 95% CI 0.02, 0.23, p=0.01), while no clear associations were observed for hemorrhagic stroke (EHR/100 mGy=0.04, 95% CI -0.04, 0.23 p=0.43) or other CeVD (EHR/100 mGy=0.02, 95% CI -0.10, 0.29, p=0.81). Trends were similar for total CeVD using badge dose (EHR/100 mSv=0.08, 95% CI 0.02, 0.16, p<0.01), but larger with brain dose (EHR/100 mGy=0.34, 95% CI -0.00, 0.81, p=0.05). Body mass index modified the CeVD dose-response (p=0.04), but year of birth, time since exposure, age at exposure, attained age, sex, smoking, and alcohol consumption did not modify the CeVD dose-response (all p>0.05), nor did adjusting for history of diabetes, hypertension or high cholesterol. Trends remained significant when restricting thyroid doses to <1,000 mGy (EHR/100 mGy=0.06, 95% CI -0.00, 0.16, 1-sided p=0.03).

Conclusions:

In the first cohort study to assess low-to-moderate occupational ionizing radiation dose in medical workers with CeVD mortality risk by subtype, greater occupational ionizing radiation exposure was associated with increased mortality risk from total CeVD and ischemic stroke, independent of demographic and lifestyle-related factors and comorbid conditions.

title: Antithymocyte globulin dose and cytomegalovirus DNAemia in kidney transplant recipients: a retrospective cohort study of the dose–response relationship
authorString: Uçar DF, Koçak K, Güçyetmez E, Usalan Ö, Bulut A, Mete AÖ.
abstractText: Background Cytomegalovirus (CMV) is a leading cause of morbidity and graft loss after kidney transplantation. Although antithymocyte globulin (ATG) induction is known to increase CMV risk, whether this effect is dose-dependent remains unclear in populations with high seroprevalence receiving universal prophylaxis. We evaluated the effect of ATG dose and other factors on CMV DNAemia, and the association of CMV with graft and patient survival. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 494 adult recipients who underwent kidney transplantation at a single centre between 2019 and 2024. Nearly all patients received 100 days of valganciclovir prophylaxis. CMV DNAemia was defined as detection of CMV DNA ≥ 80 copies/mL at least once during follow-up. Independent risk factors were identified by multivariable logistic regression. Results CMV DNAemia developed in 259 patients (52.4%). The DNAemia rate increased stepwise with ATG dose: 41.3% in basiliximab recipients and 44.9%, 61.8% and 65.0% across ATG dose tertiles (p for trend = 0.002). In multivariable analysis, each additional 100 mg of ATG increased the odds of DNAemia by 10% (OR 1.10; 95% CI 1.04–1.16). ATG-containing induction (OR 1.86; 1.20–2.89), donor age (OR 1.39 per 10 years; 1.21–1.61), hyperlipidaemia (OR 1.77; 1.11–2.83) and hypertension (OR 4.32; 1.46–12.73) were other independent risk factors. CMV infection requiring antiviral treatment was twice as frequent in recipients of kidneys from donors older than 43 years (27.1% vs 12.7%). CMV-related hospitalization was an independent risk factor for graft loss (OR 3.88; 2.28–6.59) and mortality (OR 2.41; 1.17–4.96). Mortality was four times higher when DNAemia began within the first four weeks than with later onset (20.9% vs 5.5%). Patients with CMV DNAemia had higher serum creatinine at 1 year (1.30 vs 1.10 mg/dL; p < 0.001). Conclusions ATG increases the risk of CMV DNAemia in kidney transplant recipients in a dose-dependent manner, and older donor age is the most consistent predictor of clinically significant infection. CMV infection requiring hospitalization is a strong, independent risk factor for graft loss and mortality. Individualizing the ATG dose and intensifying post-prophylaxis CMV monitoring are recommended for patients receiving high-dose ATG and those receiving kidneys from older donors.

title: Antenatal diagnosis and classification for placenta accreta (adherence) spectrum: Clinical practice guideline and recommendations by the World Association of Perinatal Medicine and the Perinatal Medicine Foundation.
authorString: Dall'Asta A, Sen C, Aryananda R, Lees C, Pranpanus S, Lombaard H, Fox KA, Shih JC, Adu-Bredu T, Calì G, D'Antonio F, Timor-Tritsch I.
abstractText: This practical guidance was developed by the World Association of Perinatal Medicine in collaboration with the Perinatal Medicine Foundation to support antenatal diagnosis and clinical management in pregnancies at risk for placenta accreta spectrum (PAS). It provides an evidence-informed approach to screening, diagnosis, referral, and peripartum planning across healthcare settings with different resources. PAS is increasingly encountered alongside rising cesarean delivery rates, use of in vitro fertilization, and a history of uterine surgery. It remains associated with severe maternal morbidity, including massive hemorrhage, large-volume transfusion, uterine rupture, peripartum hysterectomy, pelvic organ injury, intensive care admission, and maternal death. Early recognition and multidisciplinary care are therefore central to management. Cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP) is considered a potential precursor of PAS. Women with a low implantation site and a previous cesarean delivery are at increased risk. Early transvaginal ultrasound is advised in women with a previous cesarean delivery to establish the implantation site, identify CSP, and support counseling and timely consideration of uterine-preserving treatment. In the second and third trimesters, combined transabdominal and transvaginal ultrasound assesses placental location, myometrial thickness and contour, and the uterovesical interface. Sonographic markers include placental lacunae, placental bulge, uterovesical hypervascularity, and bridging vessels, which may occur individually or in combination. Two-dimensional grayscale ultrasound is the mainstay of antenatal assessment, supported by color Doppler; three-dimensional imaging may provide additional information in selected specialist settings. Magnetic resonance imaging has a complementary role when ultrasound is inconclusive, placental location is non-anterior or non-previa, or technical factors limit visualization. Suspected CSP or PAS should prompt referral to a perinatal center with multidisciplinary expertise, blood product support, adult and neonatal intensive care, and access to complex pelvic surgery. Delivery timing and surgical preparation should be individualized.

title: Recurrent belly dancer dyskinesia in pregnancy with postpartum resolution.
authorString: Henriques M, Ahmad A, Rodrigues S, Antunes I, Brito M.
abstractText: Belly dancer dyskinesia (BDD) is a rare movement disorder characterized by involuntary, repetitive contractions of the abdominal wall. Pregnancy-associated BDD is exceptionally uncommon, and recurrence in subsequent pregnancies has rarely been reported. We describe the case of a 29-year-old woman in her first pregnancy who developed involuntary abdominal movements at 16 weeks. Her medical history included hypertension and multiple uterine fibroids. Neurological assessment, laboratory investigations, and spinal magnetic resonance imaging were unremarkable, and a clinical diagnosis of BDD was established. Symptoms persisted throughout pregnancy and resolved immediately after delivery. Two years later, during a second pregnancy, similar movements recurred at 15 weeks, again resolving completely after delivery. Recurrence during two consecutive pregnancies suggests a pregnancy-related trigger for BDD, and complete postpartum resolution highlights the self-limiting course of this benign condition.

title: [Eltrombopag-associated bilateral internal jugular vein thrombosis presenting with visual impairment and marked intracranial hypertension: a case report].
authorString: Tsuru A, Takata M, Tsuji A, Oda T, Hamaguchi H.
abstractText: We report an 86-year-old man with immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) who developed bilateral internal jugular vein (IJV) thrombosis during treatment with eltrombopag (EPAG). He had experienced multiple cerebral infarctions over several months, but their cause had remained undetermined and warfarin therapy had been continued. Nine days before admission to our hospital, he developed visual impairment, and ophthalmologic evaluation revealed bilateral papilledema. He was admitted for further evaluation. Lumbar puncture demonstrated markedly elevated cerebrospinal fluid opening pressure (53 ‍cm H<sub>2</sub>O), suggesting intracranial hypertension, and contrast-enhanced MR venography demonstrated bilateral sigmoid sinus thrombosis and bilateral IJV thrombosis. Although early thrombotic changes were retrospectively identifiable on plain MRI obtained at the previous hospital, the diagnosis was delayed because we did not initially recognize the possibility of EPAG-associated thrombosis, and visual impairment persisted despite treatment. In patients receiving EPAG, thrombotic complications should always be considered, and careful assessment of abnormal intraluminal venous signals on plain MRI is important for early diagnosis and therapeutic intervention.

title: Two Eruptive Calcified Nodules in the Same Artery.
authorString: Andreou I, Sabaté M.
abstractText: Simultaneous calcified nodule destabilization may occur in a multifocal manner, analogous to the phenomenon of multiple plaque ruptures, leading to an acute coronary syndrome. Optical coherence tomography can identify multiple eruptive calcified nodules in the same coronary artery and can influence treatment planning.

title: Disparities in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and severe maternal morbidity: Evidence from a statewide birth cohort.
authorString: Solberg A, Hoppe K, Gangnon R, Powell JM.
abstractText:
Objective

Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) complicate 15% of pregnancies nationally and are a major contributor to severe maternal morbidity (SMM). We aimed to characterize temporal trends and demographic disparities in HDP incidence and evaluate the association between HDP and SMM in a statewide cohort.

Methods

This study is a descriptive and regression-based analysis of a retrospective cohort of Wisconsin births from 2017 to 2023. Data were obtained from the Wisconsin Hospital Association (WHA). Subtypes of HDP were identified using ICD-10 codes. Incidence rates of HDP per 10,000 births and average annual percent changes (AAPC) were estimated using Poisson regression and examined across demographic variables. Outcomes measured included SMM incidence, AAPCs, and SMM indicators by HDP.

Results

Among 388,250 pregnancies, the incidence of nearly all HDP subtypes rose from 2017 to 2023. Severe pre-eclampsia had the highest AAPC (11.8%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 10.6%-13.0%). HDP incidence was highest in urban areas, though the AAPC in preeclampsia was greater in rural areas (8.7%; 95% CI, 7.1%-10.3%; p = 0.004). Black patients experienced higher incidences of HDP, with significant differences in AAPC for HDP overall, chronic hypertension, and severe preeclampsia (p < 0.001). Patients with HDP had higher SMM rates compared to those without, though the AAPC in SMM did not differ by HDP status.

Conclusion

These findings highlight a growing burden of HDP in Wisconsin, with an increase in severe preeclampsia incidence and disparities by geography and race. Targeted interventions in rural areas and for Black patients are needed to improve disparities in HDP incidence and reduce SMM across Wisconsin.

title: Daytime Ventilatory and Blood Acid-Base Responses During Ascent to 3500 m Are Larger and More Rapid in Females Than Males.
authorString: Bushfield NV, MacKenzie BWL, Johnson NA, Isakovich R, Keess JL, Strzalkowski NDJ, Zubieta-Calleja G, Wilson RJA, Day TA.
abstractText: With ascent to high altitude (HA), increased ventilation reduces the pressure of PaCO2 (i.e., hypocapnia), resulting in respiratory alkalosis. A subsequent renal compensation is mediated through reductions in [HCO3 -]a, partly-correcting pHa. High inter-individual variability exists in ventilation, blood oxygenation, and acid-base responses with ascent to HA, but potential sex differences have not been well-characterized. We recruited 38 lowland participants (20 M; 18 F) before and after rapid ascent to and residence at 3500 m over 10 days in La Paz, Bolivia. We performed radial arterial blood draws to assess blood oxygenation and acid-base variables before (1100 m), and following ascent to 3500 m both early HA (E-HA; D2/3) and late HA (L-HA; D9/10). With E-HA, all participants had higher calculated V̇ A, and lower PaO2 and SaO2 (p < 0.0001), with subsequent increases in V˙ A, [Hb] and CaO2 L-HA (p = 0.0056; p = 0.0003; p = 0.0013). Although females had higher V˙ A and PaO2 than males E-HA (p < 0.0001; p = 0.0143), males had higher [Hb] and CaO2 at 1100 m, at both E-HA (p = 0.0008; p = 0.0085) and L-HA (p = 0.0007; p = 0.0045). E-HA, all participants had lower PaCO2 and [HCO3 -]a, and higher pHa than 1100 m (p < 0.0001; p = 0.0004, p < 0.0001), suggesting respiratory alkalosis and partial renal compensation. L-HA, PaCO2 and [HCO3 -]a were further reduced (p = 0.0062; p = 0.0202), with pHa only partly-compensated (p = 0.4306). E-HA, PaCO2, [HCO3 -]a and pHa were significantly lower in females (p < 0.0001; p < 0.0001; p = 0.0457), suggesting more complete renal compensation. However, these sex-differences were not apparent at L-HA (p > 0.5341). This is the first clear demonstration of differential ventilatory, oxygenation and acid-base compensation between sexes with rapid ascent to HA.

title: Peer-led examination simulation reshapes psychophysiological and emotional state profiles during problem-based medical learning.
authorString: Gellisch M, Schäfer T.
abstractText: Repeated problem-based learning (PBL) sessions are intended to sustain active, collaborative, and self-directed learning, yet evidence is mixed as to whether familiar PBL routines consistently maintain an appropriate level of learner activation over time. This repeated-measures study examined whether embedding a peer-led examination simulation into regular PBL reshapes psychophysiological and achievement-emotional state profiles. Forty-two medical students were assessed during resting reference, regular PBL, and PBL with peer-led examination simulation. Heart rate variability (HRV) was quantified using RMSSD, SDNN, pNN50, and LF/HF, alongside anxiety, perceived stress, achievement emotions, motivation, self-rated performance, and post-session appraisal. Both PBL formats reduced HRV relative to rest, indicating autonomic activation during regular PBL itself. Compared with regular PBL, examination simulation produced additional HRV withdrawal, higher anxiety and perceived stress, and lower boredom. Baseline-adjusted mixed models supported effects for RMSSD and SDNN; pNN50 did not survive false-discovery-rate correction, and LF/HF showed no robust effect. Enjoyment, motivation, and self-rated performance did not differ significantly. Students reported greater perceived benefit from and stronger preference for the simulation format. Peer-led examination simulation thus shifted PBL toward a more salient, assessment-like psychophysiological and emotional state profile.

title: Association of insulin resistance surrogate indices with multimorbidity among postmenopausal women: cross-sectional and longitudinal evidence from NHANES and CHARLS with machine learning-based evaluation.
authorString: Liang J, Yang M, Tan S, Li R, Xu L, Shi Z, Xie J.
abstractText:
Background

Insulin resistance (IR) is closely linked to multiple chronic diseases, but the comparative associations and discriminatory performance of different IR surrogate indices for multimorbidity in postmenopausal women remain unclear.

Methods

We analyzed postmenopausal women from NHANES and CHARLS. Eleven IR surrogate indices were evaluated using weighted logistic regression in NHANES and Cox proportional hazards models in CHARLS. Dose-response relationships were examined using restricted cubic splines. Discriminatory performance was assessed using ROC analyses, including time-dependent ROC analyses for CHARLS. Machine learning models were additionally developed using NHANES data to classify prevalent multimorbidity.

Results

In NHANES, most IR surrogate indices were positively associated with prevalent multimorbidity, whereas estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) showed a strong inverse association (OR = 0.28, 95% CI 0.21-0.37, p < 0.001). In CHARLS, eGDR was also inversely associated with incident multimorbidity in both baseline (HR = 0.78, 95% CI 0.73-0.84, p < 0.001) and cumulative analyses (HR = 0.67, 95% CI 0.58-0.77, p < 0.001). eGDR showed the highest discrimination among the evaluated indices in NHANES (AUC = 0.809) and in the CHARLS cumulative analysis (AUC = 0.634). Machine learning analysis in NHANES identified eGDR as the most important feature, and the optimal support vector machine model achieved an AUC of 0.835. Sensitivity analyses excluding hypertension, diabetes, and dyslipidemia attenuated the eGDR associations in CHARLS.

Conclusions

Multiple IR surrogate indices were associated with multimorbidity among postmenopausal women, with eGDR showing the most consistent inverse association across analyses. These indices may assist population-level risk stratification, although their clinical utility requires further external validation.

title: Photon FLASH spares radiation-induced lung injury and pulmonary hypertension in a preclinical model.
authorString: Brown KH, Ghita-Pettigrew M, McCabe L, McDowell MP, Kerr BN, Walls GM, McMahon SJ, Butterworth KT.

journal.title: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology

abstractText:
Introduction

Ultra-high dose rate (UHDR) radiotherapy has shown significant promise in reducing normal tissue toxicities with equivalent tumour control compared to conventional (CONV) dose rates termed the FLASH effect. In this study, we compared radiation-induced lung injury and changes in the pulmonary circulation following localised right lung irradiation at UHDR and CONV exposures using photons.

Methods

Acute and late pulmonary radiation responses were assessed in pneumonitis (C3H/NeJ) and fibrosis prone (C57BL/6) mice. 18 Gy was delivered to the right lung at CONV (0.05 Gy/s), FLASH (76.2 Gy/s) and FLASH split dose (FSD, average 2.6 Gy/s) exposures. Early responses (72 h and 4 weeks after irradiation) were investigated by immunohistochemistry (Ly6G, F4/80), fluorescence staining (EdU) and serum profiling (cytokines and lipid peroxidation assays). Fibrosis was assessed at 30 weeks after irradiation by cone-beam CT (CBCT) analysis and quantification of collagen, senescence (p21) and TGF-β levels. Changes in pulmonary vasculature and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) was assessed in C57BL/6 mice at 30 weeks to characterise changes in pulmonary circulation associated with pulmonary hypertension (PH).

Results

At early timepoints, UHDR exposures led to reduced immune cell infiltration (neutrophils and macrophages) and tissue damage in comparison to CONV and FSD groups. Serum analysis supported FLASH sparing with decreased levels of markers associated with chronic inflammation and increased markers of tissue repair in comparison to CONV and FSD groups. At 30 weeks after irradiation at a UHDR, the lung parenchyma was structurally similar to controls (p = 0.33) with minimal collagen deposition supported by CBCT tissue density analysis. In contrast, CONV and FSD animals showed significant collagen deposition (p < 0.01) with thickened alveolar septa and reduced alveolar air spaces. UHDR exposures significantly reduced functional and histological metrics of PH (p < 0.05) compared to CONV.

Conclusions

UHDR photons significantly reduce radiation-induced pneumonitis and fibrosis with secondary effects on the pulmonary circulation sparing PH.

title: Platelet-macrophage crosstalk in cardiac inflammation and remodeling.
authorString: Ahmad F, Qaisar R, Kannan M, Ansari AW.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Biochim Biophys Acta Mol Cell Res
journal.title: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular cell research
journal.isoabbreviation: Biochim Biophys Acta Mol Cell Res

abstractText: Cardiac injury and chronic heart disease are increasingly recognized as multicellular processes driven by dynamic interactions between immune and thrombotic signaling networks. Although platelets and macrophages have been extensively studied individually, the molecular mechanisms through which their reciprocal interactions regulate cardiac inflammation and remodeling remain incompletely defined. A comprehensive understanding of this cellular crosstalk is needed to define the signaling pathways that couple acute injury responses to chronic maladaptive remodeling. Among these interactions, platelet-macrophage crosstalk has emerged as an important regulator of inflammatory responses and tissue remodeling within the injured myocardium. Beyond their traditional roles in hemostasis and innate immunity, platelets communicate with macrophages through adhesion molecules, soluble mediators, and extracellular vesicles, thereby modulating macrophage activation and functional reprogramming. Platelet-derived mediators, including P-selectin, CD40L, PF4 (CXCL4), CCL5, and platelet-derived extracellular vesicles, modulate macrophage inflammatory signaling, cytokine production, redox balance, metabolic reprogramming, and pro-fibrotic responses relevant to cardiac remodeling. During acute myocardial injury, these interactions facilitate immune-cell recruitment, efferocytosis, and tissue repair, whereas persistent platelet-macrophage communication promotes chronic inflammation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and progression to heart failure. This review summarizes current molecular insights into platelet-macrophage interactions, focusing on receptor-mediated signaling, extracellular vesicle cargo transfer, immunometabolic regulation, and redox-dependent pathways. We also discuss emerging evidence linking this axis to trained immunity and inflammatory memory and highlight potential molecular targets for modulating maladaptive immune remodeling in cardiovascular disease.

title: Toward rapid MR-based assessment of osteoporosis in the lumbar spine - Acceleration of IR-UTE imaging for bound water quantification in trabecular bone at 1.5 T.
authorString: Nunn PH, Schad O, Hasenauer N, Grunz JP, Gruschwitz P, Huflage H, Scheidel S, Bley TA, Tran-Gia J, Wech T.
abstractText:
Purpose

This study aimed to explore the feasibility of accelerating inversion recovery-prepared ultra-short echo time (IR-UTE)-based bound water (BW) quantification in trabecular bone of lumbar vertebrae at 1.5 T.

Methods

A 3D radial IR-UTE sequence for selective BW imaging at 1.5 T was implemented using Pulseq to acquire data from the lumbar spine in seven young healthy volunteers and three patients with osteoporosis (OP). Reconstructions from seven reference datasets (30-min acquisition time) and retrospectively undersampled subsets (acceleration factor R = 6) derived therefrom were subsequently paired, yielding 126 input-target pairs for fine-tuning a denoising convolutional neural network (DnCNN) pre-trained on IR-UTE images of the knee. Scalar image quality metrics were calculated, and trabecular BW proton density (BWPD) in L1-L4 was determined using the remaining datasets from two young healthy volunteers and one patient with OP, including an additional prospectively accelerated scan in one healthy volunteer.

Results

Applying the DnCNN enhanced agreement with the reference, as indicated by improved scalar image metrics and reduced bias in BWPD values. Trabecular BWPD, thus derived, was higher in the young healthy volunteers than in the patient with OP (mean across L1-L4 [mol 1H/L]: 2.307 and 2.378, the latter 2.384 prospectively, vs. 0.664).

Conclusion

BW quantification in lumbar spine trabecular bone using IR-UTE at 1.5 T is feasible, and BWPD values differed between the evaluated young healthy volunteers and the patient with OP. Transfer learning via DnCNN fine-tuning demonstrated the potential to accelerate IR-UTE-based BW analysis in trabecular bone while preserving agreement with reference acquisitions.

title: Mapping cardiometabolic risk in Cleveland's urban environment: A participatory systems analysis of place-based drivers and the role of Community Health Workers.
authorString: Ansah JP, Salazar Rua R, Wright J, Zacharia H, Mitcham K, Bikkula S, Chidi I, Abraham Z, Subramanian A, Patki A, Rajagopalan S.
abstractText: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) diseases are shaped by place-based social and environmental conditions, yet the dynamic mechanisms linking structural inequities, neighborhood environments, and healthcare systems remain insufficiently understood. This study employed a participatory system dynamics approach, using Group Model Building (GMB), to examine how spatial, social, and institutional processes interact to shape cardiometabolic risk among low-income African American residents in Cleveland, Ohio, and to explore the role of Community Health Workers (CHWs). A community-engaged Group Model Building process engaged residents, Community Health Workers, healthcare providers, public health practitioners, organizational leaders, and academic partners to co-develop a stakeholder-informed causal loop diagram. Across two Group Model Building workshops conducted on November 18, 2023, and February 17, 2024, participants identified drivers of CKM risk and co-developed a stakeholder-informed system map using structured Group Model Building scripts and qualitative workshop data. The systems map depicts CKM risk as emerging from interactions among economic inequality, neighborhood disinvestment, food access, environmental exposures, healthcare fragmentation, screening access, treatment uptake, and disease management. Stakeholders highlighted upstream forces shaping spatial patterns of disadvantage, chronic stress, and healthcare access, contributing to delayed detection and management of risk factors. Three reinforcing dynamics were identified: (1) a limit-to-success dynamic constraining CHW capacity due to insufficient reimbursement; (2) a shifting-the-burden dynamic emphasizing individual responses over structural reform; and (3) a success-to-the-successful dynamic favoring biomedical care over community-based prevention. These findings suggest how cardiometabolic inequities are sustained through interconnected feedback loops and highlight leverage points-including sustainable CHW financing, cross-sector coordination, and neighborhood investment-to inform place-based strategies to reduce inequities.

title: Polydatin Attenuates Isoproterenol Induced Cardiac Hypertrophy in Association with Reduced Oxidative Stress, NOX2 Subunit Expression, and CaMKII-MEF2C Signaling.
authorString: Yamasan BE, Yıldız M, Ersoy O, Korkmaz S, Topuz RD, Palabıyık O.
abstractText: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy induced by chronic β-adrenergic receptor (β-AR) stimulation contributes to adverse cardiac remodeling and the progression of heart failure, with NADPH oxidase (NOX2)-derived reactive oxygen species (ROS) acting as key mediators of redox-dependent hypertrophic signaling. Sustained ROS generation can promote oxidative activation of Ca²⁺/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII) and downstream myocyte enhancer factor 2 C (MEF2C)-mediated transcriptional reprogramming. Polydatin, a natural glucoside of resveratrol, has been reported to exert antioxidant and cardioprotective effects. However, its influence on the NOX2-ROS-CaMKII-MEF2C axis under chronic β-AR stimulation remains unclear. In the present study, male Wistar rats were assigned to control, isoproterenol (5 mg/kg/day, subcutaneous, 4 weeks), or isoproterenol + polydatin (100 mg/kg/day, oral gavage) groups. Cardiac hypertrophy was evaluated by morphometric indices, ANP and BNP mRNA expression levels, and histological analyses. Oxidative stress was assessed through NADH oxidase activity, protein carbonyl content, and total antioxidant status. Protein expression of NOX2 subunits (gp91phox, p22phox, p47phox, p67phox, p40phox) and components of the CaMKII-MEF2C pathway were determined by Western blot and reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). Isoproterenol administration induced marked cardiac hypertrophy, elevated oxidative stress markers, increased expression of NOX2 regulatory subunits, and activated the CaMKII-MEF2C pathway. Polydatin treatment significantly attenuated hypertrophic indices, reduced NADH oxidase activity and protein carbonyl levels, restored antioxidant capacity, and suppressed p47phox, p67phox, p40phox expression along with p-CaMKII<sup>Thr286</sup>/CaMKII, ox-CaMKII/CaMKII ratios and MEF2C expression. These findings suggest that the attenuation of isoproterenol induced cardiac hypertrophy by polydatin is associated with modulation of oxidative stress, NOX2 subunit expression, and CaMKII-MEF2C signaling, although a causal role of this pathway remains to be established.

title: Type of dialysis may influence the prognostic value of myocardial perfusion imaging in end stage renal disease: an observational [<sup>13</sup>N]NH<sub>3</sub> PET/CT study.
authorString: Wenning C, Gosmann TM, Vrachimis A, Schäfers MA, Reuter S.
abstractText:
Background

Patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) exhibit an elevated risk of cardiovascular events, with imaging-based risk stratification becoming increasingly important. This study compares the prognostic utility of [13N]NH3 PET/CT assessing myocardial blood flow (MBF), coronary flow reserve (CFR) and coronary artery calcium score (CACS) as well as 3D carotid ultrasound (for carotid plaque burden; cPB) in hemodialysis (HD) versus peritoneal dialysis (PD) patients listed for kidney transplantation.

Results

41 ESRD patients (HD n = 31; PD n = 10; median follow-up 4.9 years) without known coronary artery disease underwent myocardial perfusion imaging with [13N]NH3 PET/CT, CACS, and 3D carotid ultrasound. HD patients exhibited lower myocardial stress blood flow (MBFstress) and CFR compared to PD patients (2.67 ± 0.67 vs. 2.97 ± 0.69; p = 0.24 and 2.5 ± 0.74 vs. 3.08 ± 1.12; p = 0.07). In the HD subgroup, only MBFstress correlated inversely with CACS and cPB (r = -0.32; p < 0.05 and r = -0.44; p < 0.05), whereas CFR did not (r=-0.14; p = 0.47 and r= -0.14; p = 0.44). On the other hand, both MBFstress and CFR were predictive of cardiovascular events in HD patients, although the number of events was low (n = 4). In contrast, PD patients exhibited only one single cardiovascular event in the follow-up and no significant imaging correlations were observed.

Conclusions

MBFstress and CFR may emerge as prognostic markers for cardiovascular events in HD patients whereas their prognostic power in PD patients remains uncertain. HD patients show more pronounced impairment in MBFstress and atherosclerotic plaque burden in the carotid artery, highlighting particularly this parameter as a prognostic marker in this group.

title: Effects of uridine on cardiomyocyte mitochondrial function in SHR in the early stage of hypertension.
authorString: Talanov EY, Khmil NV, Venediktova NI.
abstractText: The development of heart failure due to hypertension is known to be accompanied by various mitochondrial dysfunctions. It has previously been established that the pyrimidine nucleoside uridine (U) exerts a protective effect on the structural and functional parameters of mitochondria under various pathological conditions. This study aimed to evaluate the functional state of mitochondria in spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR) in the stage of the early hypertension and to investigate the effect of uridine on mitochondrial dysfunction associated with this pathology. A 30-mg/kg uridine was found not to affect blood pressure (BP) dynamics in SHR and WKY (Wistar Kyoto) animals. In SHR, the levels of thiobarbituric acid-reactive substances (TBARS) in serum increased compared to WKY. SHR cardiac mitochondria showed decrease in respiratory control ratio compared to WKY mitochondria. Injection of uridine was accompanied by a respiratory rate decrease in the SHR + U group relative to the control. Uridine increased the levels of respiratory complexes IV and V subunits in SHR. The rate of H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> generation in SHR cardiac mitochondria to be restored to the control levels after uridine administration. Superoxide dismutase (SOD) and glutathione peroxidase (GPx) activities in SHR decreased; herewith, uridine caused no statistically significant changes in SOD, GPx, and catalase (CAT) activities. This nucleoside was found not to affect the levels of mitochondrial ATP-sensitive potassium channel (MITOK) subunits in both animal strains studied. Thus, uridine exhibited antioxidant effects, contributing to partial normalization of cardiac mitochondrial function in SHR in the early stages of hypertension. This was probably due to modulation of the activity of mitochondrial transport systems, without the risk of hypertensive effects. These data justify further research into uridine as a cardiomyocyte protector. Hypertension, mitochondrial dysfunctions, uridine, oxidative stress, MITOK, SHR rats, OXPHOS.

title: Cardiomyocyte-targeted HSP60 modulates myocardial remodeling pathways and peripheral blood mononuclear cell mitochondrial membrane potential in hypertensive diabetic rats.
authorString: Sklifasovskaya A, Blagonravov M, Azova M, Karpov R, Ovechkina V, Andrianova S, Staroverov D, Belousov V, Mozhaev A.
abstractText: Arterial hypertension and diabetes mellitus frequently coexist and synergistically accelerate adverse left ventricular remodeling through mitochondrial dysfunction, sterile inflammation, and extracellular matrix disorganization. Heat shock protein 60 (HSP60) is a mitochondrial chaperone involved in proteostasis and stress adaptation, but it remains unclear whether cardiomyocyte-restricted augmentation of HSP60 can modulate myocardial remodeling and influence systemic immune-cell bioenergetics. Male spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR) and normotensive Wistar-Kyoto (WKY) rats were studied with or without streptozotocin-induced diabetes. Animals were assigned to WKY, SHR, WKY+HSP60, SHR+HSP60, WKY + DM+HSP60, and SHR + DM+HSP60 groups. HSP60 was delivered using an adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (AAV9) vector under the cardiac troponin T promoter. Myocardial remodeling was assessed by histomorphometry and Masson's trichrome staining, myocardial signaling by immunohistochemistry and RT-qPCR, and peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) mitochondrial membrane potential by JC-1 flow cytometry. Cardiac HSP60 delivery showed a context-dependent pattern. In hypertensive diabetic rats, this pattern included altered NLRP3 subcellular localization, modulation of mitochondrial regulatory and inflammatory-fibrotic transcripts, and increased PBMC mitochondrial membrane potential. PBMC polarization inversely correlated with myocardial fibrosis. Normotensive and single-pathology groups did not show a comparable integrated response profile. These findings indicate that cardiomyocyte-targeted HSP60 overexpression is associated with remodeling-related changes in myocardium and peripheral immune-cell bioenergetics under combined hypertensive and diabetic stress. PBMC mitochondrial membrane potential may represent a candidate peripheral indicator of myocardial state in this preclinical setting.

title: Exposomic Determinants in Heart Failure Among Older Adults - Mechanistic Links, Clinical Evidence, and Future Perspectives.
authorString: Hahad O, Münzel T, Zheng J, Valar A, Hrytseniuk Y, Ramasamy B, Ghosh A, Mishra M, Das T, Lurz P, Daiber A, Kuntic M.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

Heart failure (HF) in older adults emerges from the interplay between biological aging and the totality of environmental and behavioural exposures conceptualized as the exposome. Traditional cardiovascular risk factors and intrinsic cardiac pathology only partially explain HF burden, as chronic exposures to air pollution, traffic noise, temperature extremes, toxic metals and chemicals, artificial light at night, and adverse social environments, along with low greenness and walkability, substantially influence HF incidence, decompensations, and prognosis in older patients with multiple comorbidities.

Recent findings

Recently, epidemiological studies have associated many of the exposomic factors with HF incidence and morbidity. Age‑related impairments of the myocardium and vasculature make them particularly vulnerable to external stressors. Mechanistically, aging, HF, and environmental factors converge on shared pathways including, oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammaging, impaired autophagy and proteostasis, genomic and epigenetic alterations, cellular senescence, dysregulated neurohormonal and circadian signalling, and fibrosis with maladaptive remodelling. Through these mechanisms exposome chronically accelerates cardiovascular aging and lowers the threshold for HF onset and progression. This review considers a shift from an organ‑centred view of HF in older adults to a systems‑level, life‑course perspective that explicitly incorporates exposomic determinants, and argues that reducing harmful exposures while promoting green space, physical activity, walkability, and healthy dietary patterns should be integral to HF prevention and management strategies in aging societies.

title: Diuretic therapy at the heart-kidney interface: from acute decongestion to long-term de-escalation in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
authorString: Tsalouchos A, Dattolo PC.
abstractText: Loop diuretics remain the cornerstone of decongestion in acute heart failure, yet their use in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) is obscured by two competing errors: undertreating congestion because serum creatinine rises, and continuing or escalating diuretics after euvolaemia. This narrative review integrates established evidence and contemporary guidance into a phase-based cardiorenal decision framework. Congestion is framed as a continuum generated by sodium retention, redistribution of stressed blood volume, vascular and ventricular compliance, right-sided pressure, and renal sodium avidity-not as a binary distinction between pressure and volume overload. During acute decompensation, intravenous loop diuretics remain first-line therapy; early urine output and spot urinary sodium can identify inadequate response and support protocolized escalation. Acetazolamide or a thiazide-type diuretic can improve decongestion when loop response is insufficient, although renal and electrolyte surveillance is essential. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors should be initiated for disease modification after stabilization, but their context-dependent natriuretic effect does not replace loop diuretics in marked congestion. A creatinine rise during effective decongestion should be interpreted with residual congestion, haemodynamics, urine output, electrolytes, and evidence of kidney injury rather than through a universal threshold. After stabilization, implementation of foundational HFrEF therapy and reassessment of the minimum effective loop dose become priorities. Studies suggest that dose reduction or withdrawal is feasible in stable, euvolaemic patients, but event-powered evidence and validated outpatient biomarkers are lacking. Diuretics and disease-modifying therapy therefore have complementary, time-dependent roles: remove sodium when congestion is present, protect the kidney while recognizing hypoperfusion and intrinsic kidney injury, and de-escalate only after euvolaemia.

title: Prevalence, predictive factors, and the influential role of physical activity trajectories of cancer-related cognitive impairment among patients newly diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer.
authorString: Ho MH, Vardy JL, Lin YK, Chan WL, Takemura N, Wang L, Cheung DST, Lin CC.

journal.title: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer

abstractText:
Purpose

Evidence on the prevalence, trajectory, and predictors of cancer-related cognitive impairment (CRCI) in newly diagnosed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients remains limited, particularly regarding the role of physical activity patterns. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of CRCI, assess changes in objective and subjective cognitive functions, and identify predictors of CRCI, focusing on physical activity trajectories among patients newly diagnosed with NSCLC in Hong Kong.

Methods

A prospective observational study was conducted with 327 NSCLC patients newly diagnosed within 4 weeks. Cognitive function was objectively assessed using the HK-MoCA 5-Minute Protocol and subjectively measured using the FACT-Cog scale at baseline and monthly for six months. Physical activity patterns were analyzed through group-based trajectory modelling. Multivariate logistic regression identified predictors of CRCI, adjusting for demographic and clinical factors.

Results

The prevalence of objective CRCI ranged from 17.5% to 29.1% over the 6-month period, with 24.1% affected at 6 months. Three distinct physical activity trajectories emerged: consistently low (43.1%), consistently high (11.9%), and declining from high to moderate activity (45%). Both consistently high and declining physical activity trajectories were associated with a significantly reduced CRCI risk (93.8% and 85.9% lower risk, respectively) compared to the consistently low activity group. Consistently high physical activity trajectories were also correlated with better objective and subjective cognitive performance. Additional predictors of CRCI included lower baseline perceived cognitive function and self-efficacy for exercise.

Conclusion

This study provides novel evidence that physical activity trajectories are associated with CRCI in newly diagnosed lung cancer patients.

title: The mediating role of sleep blood pressure in the association between B-type natriuretic peptide and cardiovascular events: The Nagahama Study.
authorString: Tabara Y, Murase K, Matsumoto T, Kawaguchi T, Wakamura T, Hirai T, Chin K, Matsuda F.
abstractText:
Background

B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) is a risk marker for not only heart failure but also cardiovascular diseases (CVD). This study investigated the possible mediating role of sleep blood pressure (BP) in the association between BNP and CVD events.

Methods

Data for 5,751 participants were obtained from the Nagahama Study, a longitudinal cohort study of the general Japanese population. Circulating BNP levels were determined from blood specimens. BP was measured at home in the morning and evening, and three times per night during sleep using a timer-equipped cuff-oscillometric device.

Results

During the mean follow-up period of 9.4 years (54,350 person-years), 169 CVD cases were observed (Incidence rate: 31.1 per 10,000 person-year, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 26.7, 36.2). BNP levels ≥40 pg/mL were independently associated with CVD. The sleep BP-adjusted hazard ratio of high BNP for CVD was 1.80 (95% CI: 1.18, 2.74), while the awake home BP-adjusted hazard ratio was 1.92 (95% CI: 1.26, 2.91). Causal mediation analysis indicated a greater mediation rate of sleep SBP (14.3%, 95% CI: -2.8, 31.3) than awake home SBP (5.8%, 95% CI; -2.6, 14.2) in the association between BNP and CVD incidence. Factors associated with log-normalized BNP levels were age, sex, body mass index, sleep SBP, and nocturnal urination frequency.

Conclusion

Prognostic significance of BNP for CVD events was partially mediated by BP particularly BP during sleep.

title: Parasympathetic dysfunction assessed by deep-breathing CVR-R is associated with early discontinuation of oral semaglutide in type 2 diabetes: A multicenter retrospective study.
authorString: Ogiso K, Deguchi T, Kawade S, Arimura A, Nishio Y, Morino K.
abstractText:
Aims/introduction

Although glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists are widely used for type 2 diabetes, gastrointestinal intolerance frequently leads to early discontinuation. Predictors of oral semaglutide discontinuation remain poorly defined, and its formulation-specific dependence on gastric conditions may influence tolerability. We examined whether the coefficient of variation of R-R intervals (CVR-R) was associated with discontinuation within 6 months.

Materials and methods

In this multicenter retrospective study, 203 consecutive patients initiating oral semaglutide between February 2021 and December 2024 were screened, and 61 were analyzed after exclusions. The Discontinuation Group (n = 21) discontinued because of nausea and/or vomiting within 6 months, whereas the Maintenance Group (n = 40) continued for ≥ 6 months. CVR-R was assessed at rest (CVR-R_rest) and during deep breathing (CVR-R_DB). Associations with discontinuation were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression; exploratory machine learning and time-to-event analyses were performed.

Results

CVR-R_DB was lower in the Discontinuation Group than in the Maintenance Group (median 1.93% vs 3.26%, P < 0.001). CVR-R_DB remained independently associated with discontinuation after adjustment for age and sex (adjusted OR 0.191; 95% CI 0.071-0.512; P = 0.001; AUC 0.832) and further adjustment for neuropathy stage. The AUC was numerically higher for the age- and sex-adjusted model containing CVR-R_DB than for that containing CVR-R_rest (0.832 vs 0.699; DeLong P = 0.085). An internally derived CVR-R_DB cutoff of 2.55% stratified 6-month persistence (43.3% vs 87.1%; log-rank P < 0.001), and machine learning analyses prioritized CVR-R_DB.

Conclusions

Lower CVR-R during deep breathing was associated with early oral semaglutide discontinuation due to nausea and/or vomiting. CVR-R_DB may support risk stratification at initiation.

title: Building Healthy Temples With Less Pressure: A Faith-Based Hypertension Control Pilot Study.
authorString: Wilhite B, Wilmoth SR, Palacios C, Howard J, Zhang J, He M.
abstractText: Hypertension disproportionately affects Hispanic/Latino communities in the United States, yet culturally tailored interventions that support sustained lifestyle modification and self-management remain limited. This study evaluated the feasibility and preliminary effectiveness of Building Healthy Temples with Less Pressure (BHT-LP), a faith-based, lay leader-delivered hypertension self-management intervention implemented in Hispanic church communities. Guided by social cognitive theory, BHT-LP included a Medical Moment and a 12-session hypertension self-management program delivered by trained Church Lay Health Leaders. Forty adults with hypertension or elevated blood pressure were recruited from two Hispanic churches in San Antonio, Texas, during 2021 to 2022. Participants completed baseline and post-intervention assessments, and focus groups were conducted at program completion. Twenty-nine participants completed both assessments. Mean systolic and diastolic blood pressure decreased modestly, although the changes were not statistically significant. Hypertension self-care behaviors, dietary quality, and physical activity improved, with aerobic activity increasing by 72 min/week (p < .01). Participants with excess weight experienced significant reductions in body weight and waist circumference. Qualitative findings indicated program acceptability, high trust in lay leaders, and increased motivation to monitor blood pressure and adopt healthier behaviors. These findings support the feasibility and promise of a spiritually integrated, lay leader-facilitated intervention for hypertension control and related health behaviors in Hispanic faith communities. The program's culturally grounded approach, group support, and integration of self-monitoring tools may offer a practical strategy for advancing community-based hypertension prevention and management.

title: Therapeutic efficacy and systemic pharmacokinetics of a dual-drug hydrogel contact lens for sustained glaucoma therapy.
authorString: Varshitha V, Sankararajan U.
abstractText:
Background

Conventional topical therapy for glaucoma is limited by poor ocular bioavailability, rapid precorneal drug loss, frequent dosing and systemic absorption through the nasolacrimal pathway, which may reduce therapeutic efficacy and increase the risk of adverse effects. Drug-eluting hydrogel contact lenses have emerged as a promising strategy to overcome these limitations by enabling sustained ocular drug delivery.

Objective

This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy, ocular biocompatibility and systemic pharmacokinetic profile of an optimized dual-drug-loaded HEMA-based hydrogel contact lens delivering timolol maleate (TM) and brimonidine tartrate (BT) for sustained glaucoma management.

Methods

Optimized hydrogel contact lenses composed of 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate (HEMA), N, N-dimethylacrylamide (DMA), N-vinylpyrrolidone (NVP) and ethylene glycol dimethacrylate (EGDMA) were fabricated by UV photopolymerization and loaded with TM and BT (4 mg/mL each). Ocular biocompatibility was assessed using the modified Draize irritation test. Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in a steroid-induced ocular hypertension New Zealand White rabbit model by monitoring intraocular pressure (IOP) for 24 h. Systemic drug exposure was determined by validated high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) analysis of plasma samples, while ocular safety was further confirmed through histopathological examination.

Results

The optimized hydrogel lens exhibited excellent ocular biocompatibility, with a maximum Draize score of 0.33 ± 0.12 that resolved completely within 48 h and no histopathological evidence of ocular tissue damage. In hypertensive rabbits, the dual-drug hydrogel lens maintained normotensive IOP (16.1 ± 0.8 mmHg) for 24 h, representing a 43.5% reduction from baseline and significantly outperforming conventional eye drops beyond 4 h (p < 0.01). Plasma concentrations of both TM and BT remained below the limit of quantification (<2.0 ng/mL) throughout the study, whereas conventional eye drops produced measurable systemic exposure (TM: 18.4 ± 2.1 ng/mL; BT: 8.2 ± 1.2 ng/mL), demonstrating effective minimization of systemic drug absorption.

Conclusion

The optimized dual-drug-loaded hydrogel contact lens provided sustained intraocular pressure reduction, excellent ocular biocompatibility and negligible systemic drug exposure compared with conventional topical therapy. These findings highlight its potential as a sustained ocular drug-delivery platform capable of improving therapeutic efficacy, reducing systemic adverse effects and enhancing long-term treatment adherence in glaucoma management. Further long-term preclinical investigations and clinical studies are warranted to support clinical translation.

title: Investigating the TASK1 potassium channel in equine atrial myocardium as a potential treatment target for atrial fibrillation.
authorString: Verhaeghe LM, Jávorszky N, Kraft M, Wiedmann F, Weitkamp FM, Decloedt A, Van Steenkiste G, van Loon G, Schmidt C.
abstractText:
Background and purpose

Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common clinically relevant arrhythmia in horses, with limited pharmacological treatment options in both veterinary and human medicine. TASK1 potassium channels represent a promising atrial-selective antiarrhythmic target, but their relevance in horses has not been established. To characterize equine TASK1 (eqTASK1) channels regarding structural conservation, electrophysiological function, pharmacological sensitivity, cardiac expression pattern and in vivo electrophysiological effects of TASK1 inhibition.

Experimental approach

Sixteen horses killed for non-cardiovascular reasons, of which 10 horses used for tissue harvesting and six horses for in vivo testing. Functional and pharmacological properties of eq TASK1 and human (hTASK1) channels were assessed in Xenopus laevis oocytes using two-electrode voltage clamp recordings. Cardiac expression of eqTASK1 was analysed by qRT-PCR and immunoblotting, while in vivo electrophysiological studies were performed in anaesthetized horses before and after intravenous ketodoxapram administration.

Key results

EqTASK1 and h TASK1 channels demonstrated high structural conservation, comparable potassium-selective background currents and preserved pharmacological sensitivity with species-dependent differences in potency. EqTASK1 expression was strongly enriched in atrial and nodal tissue, whereas ventricular expression was minimal. In vivo administration of ketodoxapram significantly prolonged atrial effective refractory periods from 275 ± 54 to 418 ± 94 ms without significant changes in heart rate or atrioventricular conduction parameters.

Conclusion and implications

EqTASK1 channels are highly conserved with human orthologs and display pronounced atrial-predominant cardiac expression. In vivo TASK1 inhibition prolongs atrial refractoriness in horses, supporting TASK1 as a translational atrial-selective antiarrhythmic target in both human and veterinary medicine.

title: Ambulatory Episodic Hypertension in Parkinson's Disease With Orthostatic Hypotension.
authorString: Deraz HA, Dwivedi AK, Duque KR, Bloemer A, Marsili L, Abanto J, Paredes NC, Gorriti AH, Hill EJ, Duker AP, Mahajan A, Espay AJ.
abstractText:
Objective

The objective of this study was to determine whether ambulatory hypertensive episodes are associated with clinical outcomes in patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) with neurogenic versus non-neurogenic orthostatic hypotension.

Methods

Consecutive patients with PD with suspected orthostatic hypotension (OH) underwent 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring in the home setting. The primary exposure was the number of hypertensive episodes across 24 hours. Neurogenic OH was defined by a heart rate response to orthostatic systolic blood pressure reduction of <0.5 beats/min/mmHg during standardized 3-minute orthostatic testing. The primary outcome was quality of life measured by the Parkinson's Disease Questionnaire-39 Summary Index (PDQ-39 SI). Secondary outcomes included orthostatic symptom burden and motor severity. Multivariable linear regression models with interaction terms were adjusted for age, sex, disease duration, and levodopa equivalent daily dose, with robustness assessed through multiple sensitivity analyses.

Results

Fifty-nine patients with PD were included, 30 with neurogenic OH and 29 with non-neurogenic orthostatic hypotension. Among patients with neurogenic OH, a greater number of hypertensive episodes was associated with better quality of life, lower orthostatic symptom burden, and lower motor impairment scores. In patients with non-neurogenic OH, these associations were absent or occurred in the opposite direction. Associations were stronger during daytime than night-time periods and remained consistent in sensitivity analyses.

Interpretation

In patients with PD and neurogenic OH, ambulatory hypertensive episodes were associated with better clinical outcomes, an association not observed in patients with non-neurogenic OH. ANN NEUROL 2026.

title: Cholesterol Paradox: Multi‑point Heart Failure Prediction from Lipid Panels in Electronic Health Records
authorString: Hou Y, Bhuiyan MK, Samad M.
abstractText: In cardiovascular medicine, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is the main lipid marker used in routine screening to assess cardiovascular risk and guide preventive treatment and dietary changes. An increasing number of studies have recently documented the cholesterol paradox: patients with or at risk of heart failure (HF) often have unexpectedly low levels of LDL-C despite leading to cardiovascular diseases. This paper examines how well retrospective lipid panel measurements, supplemented with apolipoprotein B (ApoB), can predict an initial heart failure (HF) event in several pre-diagnosis time windows, using age-matched patient data from Electronic Health Records (EHRs). This retrospective study uses lipid profiles from multicenter nationwide EHRs from the All of Us Research Program. We apply machine learning and explainable AI (SHAP) to lipid-based prediction and to interpret cholesterol contributions to the diagnosis of first heart failure (HF). One experiment predicts the diagnosis of HF in 36 months; the other distinguishes HF patients from people who have never been diagnosed with cardiovascular disease. A baseline lipid panel that includes ApoB predicts the first HF event up to 36 months in advance, achieving an AUC of 0.624 in men and 0.627 in women. Compared to a group of the same age without previous cardiovascular disease, a lipid profile including ApoB predicts a first HF event with a substantially higher AUC: 0.937 for men and 0.925 for women. Shapley value analyses suggest that higher triglycerides and lower HDL and LDL levels are linked to subsequent HF events, with LDL appearing as the strongest yet counterintuitive predictor. ApoB ranks second in importance; in males, higher ApoB is associated with a greater risk of HF, unlike LDL. In general, the study highlights an unexpected association with LDL and emphasizes the prognostic utility of sex-specific metabolic indicators (TG, HDL) for HF using routinely collected clinical data.

title: Association between autoimmune diseases and risk of developing breast cancer-related lymphedema.
authorString: Wagner BD, Brown S, Barrio AV, Amburn T, Polidorio N, Le T, Boe LA, Kataru RP, Hespe GE, Coriddi MR, Rochlin DH, Yoshimatsu H, Mehrara BJ.
abstractText: Preexisting autoimmune disease may increase susceptibility to breast cancer-related lymphedema (BCRL) through chronic inflammation and immune dysregulation, but its association with BCRL risk is poorly understood. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults undergoing sentinel lymph node biopsy and/or axillary lymph node dissection for breast cancer at a tertiary cancer center between 2010 and 2021. Autoimmune diseases were identified using International Classification of Diseases (ICD)-9/10 codes, and the primary outcome was BCRL diagnosis based on ICD codes. Associations between autoimmune disease and time to BCRL were evaluated using univariate and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. Among 20,027 patients with a median follow-up of 61.7 months (IQR, 38.7-94.2), 1361 (6.8%) had a preexisting autoimmune disease and 1728 (8.6%) developed BCRL at a median of 17.4 months (IQR, 8.0-33.9) after surgery. In multivariable analysis, autoimmune disease was independently associated with increased BCRL risk (hazard ratio [HR], 1.52; 95% CI, 1.30-1.77; P < .001). Elevated risks were observed for rheumatoid arthritis (HR, 1.54), autoimmune thyroiditis (HR, 1.40), Graves' disease (HR, 1.49), multiple sclerosis (HR, 1.87), systemic lupus erythematosus (HR, 2.46), and systemic sclerosis (HR, 2.10). These findings suggest autoimmune disease may be an independent risk factor for BCRL and may improve risk stratification.

title: Villoglandular Adenocarcinoma of the Cervix With Ovarian Metastasis Mimicking a Borderline Ovarian Tumor: A Rare Case Report.
authorString: Ma N, Xu X, Zhu Z, Xin T, Huang Y.
abstractText: This case reports rare cervical villoglandular adenocarcinoma metastasizing to the ovary with a deceptive borderline-like morphology. Diagnosis relied on matching immunohistochemistry and HPV16 DNA detection in both sites. The patient underwent surgery and chemoradiotherapy, remaining recurrence-free. This highlights the critical need for multimodal testing to distinguish such metastases from primary ovarian tumors.

title: Post-embolization dynamic changes in Obsidio Conformable Embolic: volume and radiodensity analysis.
authorString: Harraka M, Amin R, Pourmorteza A, Cohen EI, Afsari B, Sabri SS, Banovac F, Bomberger H, Jones J, Habibollahi P, Nezami N.
abstractText:
Purpose

To characterize the temporal dynamic and clinical remodeling of the Obsidio™ Conformable Embolic (Obsidio) post endovascular delivery using longitudinal quantitative CT volumetry and Hounsfield unit (HU) attenuation.

Materials and methods

This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 21 patients (30 vessels) embolized with Obsidio for acute hemorrhage or hypervascular tumor between 2023 and 2026. Patients had at least two follow-up computed tomography (CT) scans. The primary endpoint was the percent change in embolic cast volume and HU attenuation, measured using standardized Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) segmentation tools. Secondary endpoints included assessment for recanalization.

Results

All embolizations were technically successful (100%). On the first follow-up CT (median 12 days), the mean Obsidio volume was 89.33 ± 13.86% of the original volume (p = 0.0002). On the second follow-up (median 36 days), the volume was 79.51 ± 19.76% of baseline volume (p = 0.0004), representing 20.49% reduction. On third follow-up CT (median 76 days), volume was 85.2 ± 18.92% (p = 0.047). On the fourth follow-up CT, volume was 66.76 ± 16.9% (p = 0.0048). On the fifth follow-up CT, volume was 60.15 ± 3.15% (p = 0.00001) The average volume reduction rate decelerated from 0.99%/day to 0.71%/day to 0.17%/day then stabilized at 0.2%/day. Concurrently, mean Hounsfield unit attenuation increased by 4.85% (p = 0.06) on the second follow-up CT scan. No evidence of recanalization, distal embolization, or cast fragmentation was observed on any of CT scans.

Conclusion

The Obsidio embolic cast undergoes progressive reduction in volume and increase in HU attenuation over time without evidence of vessel recanalization. This temporal dynamic of Obsidio embolic is consistent with bioresorption of its gelatin and water components, supporting the concept of persistent occlusion via in vivo remodeling.
