title: Clinical and Haematologic Correlates of Soluble VCAM-1 in Adults With Steady-State Sickle Cell Disease.
authorString: Ghunney WK, Asare EV, Ayete-Nyampong JB, Doku-Agama W, Kyei-Baafour E, Ofori MF, Obeng Adjei G, Olayemi E.
abstractText:
Background

Endothelial activation contributes to the vasculopathy of sickle cell disease (SCD). We evaluated serum soluble vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (sVCAM-1), a surrogate marker of endothelial activation, and examined its clinical and haematologic correlates in adults with steady-state SCD.

Methods

This was a cross-sectional study of 75 adults with steady-state SCD (HbSS: 86.7%; HbSC: 13.3%) and 75 age-matched comparison participants with normal adult haemoglobin genotype (HbAA). Associations of clinical and haematologic measures with sVCAM-1 were evaluated using correlation and multivariable linear regression analyses.

Results

SCD participants had lower systolic blood pressure (SBP), BMI and haemoglobin and elevated leukocyte, platelet, reticulocyte, total bilirubin and LDH levels, compared with HbAA participants (all p < 0.001). Mean sVCAM-1 was higher in SCD than in HbAA participants (878.8 vs. 507.9 ng/mL; p < 0.001), with no significant difference between HbSS and HbSC. In the combined SCD cohort, sVCAM-1 correlated positively with absolute reticulocyte count (r = 0.24, p = 0.034). In HbSS, sVCAM-1 correlated positively with SBP (r = 0.264, p = 0.033). In multivariable analysis, higher reticulocyte count (B = 73.39 ng/mL per 100x109/L increase, p = 0.014) and lower BMI (B = -15.3, p = 0.038) were independently associated with higher sVCAM-1 in SCD. In HbSS, total bilirubin was inversely associated with sVCAM-1 in the primary model (B = -1.62, p = 0.041), although this association was attenuated in sensitivity analyses.

Conclusion

Higher reticulocyte count was consistently associated with higher sVCAM-1 in adults with steady-state SCD. Associations of sVCAM-1 with BMI, bilirubin and SBP were also observed, but these genotype-specific findings warrant cautious interpretation, particularly given the small size of the HbSC subgroup. These findings support further prospective evaluation of clinical and haematologic correlates of endothelial activation in SCD.

Trial registration

The authors have confirmed clinical trial registration is not needed for this submission.

title: Impact of wildfire smoke waves on the association between long-term exposure to fine particulate matter and cardiovascular hospitalizations among older adults in the United States.
authorString: Zhang S, Wang Y, Wei J, Krumholz HM, Lu Y, Chen K.
abstractText:
Background

Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is a risk factor for cardiovascular disease (CVD), even at concentrations below U.S. air quality standards. The frequency and severity of wildfires are increasing, causing episodic PM2.5 spikes. Our study examined whether associations between long-term exposure to PM2.5 and cardiovascular hospitalizations differed in the presence and absence of wildfire smoke waves.

Methods

We conducted a cohort study of 65.2 million U.S. Medicare beneficiaries aged ≥ 65 years across the contiguous U.S. during 2017-2022. Daily total and wildfire smoke PM2.5 concentrations were estimated at 1 km and 10 km spatial resolutions, respectively, using validated machine learning models that incorporated satellite, meteorological, emission, and land-use data. Exposure estimates were aggregated to beneficiaries' residential ZIP codes by population-weighted averaging. Wildfire smoke waves were defined as ≥ 2 consecutive days with daily smoke PM2.5 > 10 μg/m3. We applied quasi-Poisson regressions to estimate relative risks (RR) of first hospitalizations for overall CVD, ischemic heart disease, cerebrovascular disease, and hypertension in ZIP-years with and without smoke waves.

Results

In the full cohort, an increase in two-year average PM2.5 from 5 μg/m3 (WHO annual air quality guideline) to 9 μg/m3 (current U.S. annual PM2.5 standard) was associated with increased risks of overall CVD, cerebrovascular, and hypertension hospitalizations, with stronger associations in ZIP-years without smoke waves than in those with smoke waves (overall CVD: RR 1.09, 95% CI 1.09-1.10 vs. RR 1.04, 95% CI 1.03-1.04; ratio of RR 1.05, 95% CI 1.04-1.06). Similar patterns were observed among beneficiaries residing in ZIP codes with annual PM2.5 concentrations below 9 μg/m3 throughout the study period. Smoke wave-related differences in PM2.5-CVD associations were greater among males, urban residents, and residents in the western region compared with their counterparts.

Conclusions

The association between long-term PM2.5 exposure and cardiovascular hospitalizations differed by wildfire smoke wave occurrence. These findings suggest that long-term average PM2.5 may not fully capture episodic high-intensity exposures and may underestimate the cardiovascular morbidity burden in smoke-affected areas, highlighting the need for risk assessments accounting for exposure patterns.

title: Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension With Cold Agglutinins Needing Pulmonary Thromboendarterectomy: The Use of Therapeutic Plasma Exchange.
authorString: Naqvi B, Bautista MA, Sanchez AP, Yang JZ, Fernandes TM, Poch DS, Kerr KM, Kim NH, Madani MM, Pretorius VG, Allen ES, Kopko PM, Dilly LD, Ginsberg C, Park SJ, Choi M, Cruz DN, Papamatheakis DG.
abstractText: Cold agglutinins can be detected in patients with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) during pulmonary thromboendarterectomy (PTE) pre-operative testing. Peri-operative management of these patients in anticipation of deep hypothermic circulatory arrest can be challenging and has not been standardized. We describe our relevant experience and suggest a potential protocolized pre-operative approach with this observational, retrospective cohort study. A chart review of all patients undergoing PTE surgery for CTEPH (1107 patients) at UC San Diego between 2019 and 2025 was performed. An Institutional Review Board approved quality improvement database on all patients undergoing PTE surgery was used. Twenty-one patients (1.9%) screened positive for cold agglutinins pre-PTE. A high co-prevalence of antiphospholipid syndrome and cold agglutinins was noted (17/21; 81%). Thermal amplitude testing (when possible) was positive for nine patients between 15°C and 18°C. Fifteen patients underwent therapeutic plasma exchange (median of two sessions) with albumin and plasma replacement fluid followed by PTE surgery with standard cooling protocol. There were no incidents of agglutination or hemolysis peri- or post-operatively. Three patients had post-operative airway hemorrhage, two of which developed heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT). There was one mortality in the setting of HIT with recurrent thrombosis and bleeding. Median intensive care unit and hospital length of stays were 3 and 12.5 days, respectively. We suggest a protocolized approach for the identification and management of high-risk patients with cold agglutinins, which may include therapeutic plasma exchange pre-operatively. This can successfully mitigate the potential risk of hypothermic circulatory arrest causing agglutination during surgery.

title: Association Between Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate and Local Carotid Arterial Stiffness in a Cardiometabolic Risk Population
authorString: Marinova E, Benkova-Petrova M, Shaleva R, Dimova M.
abstractText:
Background:

and Objectives: Kidney dysfunction has been associated with arterial stiffening, but the relationship may depend on shared cardiometabolic and haemody-namic factors. This study examined the association between estimated glomerular fil-tration rate (eGFR) and local carotid arterial stiffness in adults with a high prevalence of diabetes and hypertension.

Materials and Methods:

This single-centre cross-sectional study included 135 adults. Local carotid pulse wave velocity derived from the beta stiffness index (PWVβ) was the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes were the beta stiffness index, pressure–strain elastic modulus, arterial compliance, and augmentation index. Multivariable linear regression evaluated associations with eGFR, age, sex, dia-betes, and hypertension. Separate models replaced hypertension status with peripheral or central aortic systolic blood pressure.

Results:

Mean age was 57.4 ± 7.4 years, and mean eGFR was 83.3 ± 20.0 mL/min/1.73 m². PWVβ differed across the four diabetes–hypertension groups (p < 0.001). In the primary model, based on 117 participants, higher PWVβ was associated with age, diabetes, and hypertension. There was no evidence of an independent association between eGFR and PWVβ (B = −0.003 per mL/min/1.73 m²; 95% confidence interval, −0.014 to 0.009; p = 0.676). eGFR was also not associated with the secondary outcomes. Peripheral and central aortic systolic blood pressure were positively associated with PWVβ in separate adjusted models.

Conclusion:

In this cardiometabolic risk population, eGFR was not independently associated with local carotid arterial stiffness. Age, diabetes, and blood pressure were associated with higher PWVβ. The findings concern contemporaneous associations and should not be extrapolated to ad-vanced chronic kidney disease or interpreted as excluding a longitudinal relationship between kidney function and vascular stiffness.

title: Tumor-to-tumor metastasis of colorectal adenocarcinoma within a gonadotroph pituitary adenoma.
authorString: Murasawa S, Isozaki F, Fukasawa-Maeda M, Takayasu S, Inoshita N, Fujita Y.
abstractText: Pituitary metastases are uncommon, and most cases originate from breast or lung cancer. Tumor-to-tumor metastasis, in which one neoplasm metastasizes into another, is particularly rare in the sellar region. We report a 66-year-old man with metastatic sigmoid colon adenocarcinoma treated with modified FOLFOX6 (5-fluorouracil, L-leucovorin, and oxaliplatin) plus panitumumab; extracranial disease was controlled, whereas a sellar mass initially suspected as a pituitary adenoma slowly enlarged over 2 years. Endocrine testing showed anterior hypopituitarism without arginine vasopressin deficiency. Endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery was performed for continued enlargement and diagnostic uncertainty. Histopathology demonstrated a gonadotroph pituitary adenoma infiltrated by colorectal adenocarcinoma, with extensive intermingling of the 2 components rather than discrete nests, favoring tumor-to-tumor metastasis over a collision tumor. The metastatic component consisted of viable tumor cells without necrosis or convincing treatment effect despite prolonged chemotherapy. This case underscores that metastatic tumor within a pituitary adenoma may enlarge despite favorable systemic therapy outcomes. Metastasis should therefore remain a key differential diagnosis for a sellar mass radiologically suggestive of a pituitary adenoma.

title: Quantification of Neuromotor Control in <i>STXBP1</i>-Related Disorders With Wearable Sensors.
authorString: Orlando JM, Bane B, Chisari T, Magielski JH, Pierce SR, Cunningham KG, Woo C, Tefft S, Nolan J, Ruggiero SM, Boland MJ, McKee JL, Helbig I, Prosser LA.
abstractText:
Background and objectives

STXBP1-related disorders (STXBP1-RD) are a spectrum of neurodevelopmental conditions that present with motor impairments, which include involuntary movements, ataxia, and tremor that have been difficult to measure. The objective of this study was to use wearable sensors to characterize motor control abnormalities in individuals with STXBP1-RD, a spectrum of neurodevelopmental conditions that present with motor impairments affecting motor development.

Methods

In this study, an exploratory analysis to quantify the clinical features of motor control impairment, including tremor, in 23 individuals with STXBP1-RD was conducted and compared these features with those of 18 typically developing control participants using inertial sensors during a reaching task. Clinical relevance of the sensor-derived metrics of motor control was evaluated in the context of traditional developmental clinical assessments collected during a prospective natural history study.

Results

Individuals with STXBP1-RD demonstrated slower reaching time, decreased arm acceleration intensity, less smooth reaching, and tremor frequency characteristics consistent with an unstable or irregular rhythmic movement pattern. More than 65% of individuals with STXBP1-RD presented with tremor in our sample. Combining features from all 4 upper limb sensors predicted tremor with the highest accuracy (area under the curve = 0.87), and multiple motor control metrics were significantly related to developmental assessment scores with reaching duration having the strongest correlation.

Discussion

Our study provides an understanding of motor control in a rare neurodevelopmental disorder and establishes a paradigm to quantify neuromotor control in individuals with developmental differences. Our observations demonstrate significant relations between motor control measures and developmental function, and a tremor prevalence that exceeds twofold what has been reported in historical, retrospective data sets.

title: The A-FABP Nexus in the Neurovascular Unit: Bridging Endothelial Barrier Breakdown and Microglial Lipotoxicity in Ischemic Stroke.
authorString: Ma WY, Yao L, Lan W.
abstractText: Ischemic stroke is a neurological cerebrovascular event characterized by highly complex, spatiotemporally dynamic pathophysiological processes. In recent years, stroke research has shifted from early isolated neuroprotection to the systematic investigation of the multidimensional homeostasis of the entire neurovascular unit (NVU). Within this complex pathological network, neuroinflammation mediated by cerebral lipid metabolic dysregulation has gradually emerged as an important contributor to NVU dysfunction and post-stroke secondary injury. Among various lipid chaperones, adipocyte fatty acid-binding protein (A-FABP) has attracted increasing attention because of its involvement in metabolic dysregulation, vascular injury, and neuroinflammation. This review comprehensively examines the emerging evidence for the multifaceted involvement of A-FABP in ischemic stroke. In the hyperacute phase, A-FABP acts as a potent endothelial disruptor, compromising the integrity of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) by activating MMP-9; Beyond this established vascular mechanism, findings from other experimental contexts suggest that A-FABP may also contribute to microglial lipid dysregulation and associated inflammatory responses, providing a potential mechanistic link between vascular injury and immune-metabolic dysfunction within the NVU. Preclinical studies further indicate that pharmacological inhibition or neutralization of A-FABP can attenuate ischemic brain injury; however, its therapeutic efficacy and safety in patients with ischemic stroke remain to be established. This review provides an in-depth analysis of the dynamic balance of the spatiotemporal effects of A-FABP, further highlighting its core value as a biomarker for poor stroke prognosis and a highly promising therapeutic target. It also examines current translational bottlenecks, including phase-specific intervention windows, applicability across different stroke subtypes, unresolved mechanisms of NVU crosstalk, and pharmacological optimization, aiming to provide directions for future investigation of A-FABP within the stroke immune-metabolic network.

title: Sex-Specific Cross-Sectional Associations and Exploratory Mediation Analysis of Cardiovascular Disease Risk by Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio in Cadmium-Exposed Populations.
authorString: Li X, Wang K, Hui X, Yang R, Kong W, Hou L, Zhang S, Yan P, Lu Y, Niu X.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide, with its burden continuing to rise. Environmental cadmium (Cd) exposure has emerged as a potential risk factor for CVD. This study aimed to investigate the associations between Cd exposure and CVD risk, and to explore cross-sectional associations and a potential inflammatory pathway using exploratory mediation analysis.

Methods

This study utilized data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. Logistic regression models were used to identify factors influencing CVD risk. Dose-response relationships were evaluated using restricted cubic splines (RCS). Exploratory mediation analysis was conducted to assess the potential mediating role of NLR in the association between Cd exposure and CVD risk.

Results

Individuals with CVD had significantly higher levels of blood Cd, urinary Cd, and NLR than controls (p < 0.05) in both sexes. In males, the highest quartile (Q4) of blood Cd (OR = 3.06, 95% CI: 1.45-6.46, p = 0.004) and urinary Cd (OR = 3.02, 95% CI: 1.52-6.02, p = 0.002) were significantly associated with higher CVD prevalence. Conversely, no significant association was observed in females for blood Cd (p = 0.505), and the association for urinary Cd (p = 0.046) was notably weaker and less robust than that in males. Interaction analyses confirmed sex-specific differences (p-interaction < 0.05). NLR showed significant exploratory mediating effects (indirect effects), accounting for 9.4% (95% CI: 3.5%-15.2%) of the blood Cd-CVD link and 5.0% (95% CI: 1.9%-8.1%) of the urinary Cd-CVD link in males. Similar significant mediation was observed in the general population for blood Cd: 7.2% (95% CI: 2.2%-12.2%), and for urinary Cd: 6.4% (95% CI: 2.8%-10.0%).

Conclusions

This cross-sectional study identified significant sex-specific and dose-dependent associations between Cd exposure and CVD risk. Inflammatory responses, particularly those reflected by elevated NLR, were cross-sectionally associated with the observed Cd-CVD link, suggesting a potential pathway that warrants prospective validation, especially in males.

title: 2026 Asia Pacific Heart Rhythm Society (APHRS) Guidelines (Part II) on Stroke Prevention in Atrial Fibrillation.
authorString: Chao TF, Lip GYH, Chan YH, Lee SR, Li M, Kim D, Kuo L, Okumura K, Tse HF, Choi EK, Chen M, Joung B, Krittayaphong R, Middeldorp ME, Soejima K, Pak HN.
abstractText: The 2026 Asia Pacific Heart Rhythm Society (APHRS) Guidelines represent the first comprehensive APHRS guidelines dedicated to the management of atrial fibrillation (AF) and comprise four parts covering epidemiology, detection/screening and integrated care; stroke prevention; rate and rhythm control; and lifestyle risk factor and comorbidity management. Part II focuses on stroke prevention in AF, integrating contemporary global evidence with data and clinical considerations specific to the Asia-Pacific region. It provides evidence-based and practical recommendations for stroke and bleeding risk assessment, oral anticoagulation, selection and appropriate dosing of direct oral anticoagulants, management of patients with special or complex clinical characteristics, and left atrial appendage occlusion. Particular attention is given to issues (and evidence) highly relevant to Asia-Pacific populations, including the evolving risk of ischemic stroke, appropriate anticoagulant dosing, renal function assessment, and balancing thromboembolic and bleeding risks. These recommendations aim to support individualized clinical decision-making, promote appropriate use of stroke-prevention strategies, and improve outcomes for patients with AF across the Asia-Pacific region.

title: 2026 Asia Pacific Heart Rhythm Society (APHRS) Guidelines (Part I) on Epidemiology, Detection/Screening and Integrated Patient Care in Atrial Fibrillation.
authorString: Joung B, Krittayaphong R, Guo Y, Yang PS, Hsieh YC, Ikeda T, Kim D, Kojodjojo P, Chan NY, Yuniadi Y, Dung KN, Apiyasawat S, Almahmeed W, Choi EK, Middeldorp ME, Soejima K, Lip GYH, Pak HN, Chao TF.
abstractText: The 2026 Asia Pacific Heart Rhythm Society (APHRS) Guidelines represent the first comprehensive APHRS guidelines dedicated to the management of atrial fibrillation (AF) and comprise four parts covering epidemiology, detection/screening and integrated care; stroke prevention; rate and rhythm control; and lifestyle risk factor and comorbidity management. Part 1 focuses on epidemiology and integrated care management, integrating contemporary global evidence with data and clinical considerations specific to the Asia-Pacific region. It provides evidence-based and practical recommendations for clinical epidemiology in the region, as well as introduces the need for holistic or integrated care management.

title: Revisiting Parakinesia Brachialis Oscitans: You Yawn, I Move! A Scoping Review.
authorString: Vasireddy RP, Vivanco RA, Koppanatham A, Lenka A.

journal.title: Tremor and other hyperkinetic movements (New York, N.Y.)

abstractText:
Background

Parakinesia brachialis oscitans (PBO) is a rarely reported phenomenon in which a paretic limb moves involuntarily during yawning. The literature consists predominantly of case reports and small series, with limited comparative evidence.

Methods

We conducted a PRISMA-ScR-guided scoping review of PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science from inception to 28 August 2026, with backward citation searching. Eligible reports described one or more patients with an involuntary, stereotyped, yawn-locked movement of a paretic limb after a focal central nervous system lesion, with the lesion site reported on neuroimaging. Data included demographics, movement description, latency, lesion site, etiology, and outcome.

Results

Twenty-two reports describing 31 patients met the inclusion criteria. Most patients were men (67.7%), with a mean age of 56.1 years. PBO involved the upper limb alone in 29 patients (93.5%). Acute ischemic stroke was the most common etiology (83.9%). Lesions were often seen in the internal capsule (44.4%) and the corona radiata or subcortical white matter (40.7%). Onset ranged from immediate to four months after the lesion. Complete resolution was documented in 10 patients (32.3%), PBO persisted for up to three years in five, and outcome was not reported in 15 (48.4%).

Discussion

PBO is associated with focal lesions affecting distributed voluntary motor-control networks, frequently involving subcortical motor pathways. Although no mechanism has been established, the observations suggest a release of preserved brainstem and extrapyramidal circuits. Outcome was unreported in almost half the cases; prospective, standardized reporting is needed to clarify its course and prognostic significance.

Highlights

This scoping review gathered 22 reports describing 31 patients with PBO after a focal brain injury.PBO involved the upper limb alone in 29 patients and lesions were most commonly subcortical, involving the internal capsule.Onset ranged from presentation to four months and PBO persisted for up to three years. However, the outcome was not reported in half of the included cases.

title: Super-Refractory Status Epilepticus (SRSE) Secondary to Neurosyphilis Complicated by a Prolonged Drug-Induced Cardiac Arrest Successfully Bridged With Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (ECMO) and Impella®: A Case Report.
authorString: Gutfreund D, Loretz L, Bloch A, Diem L, Albrecht S, Bossard M.
abstractText: Neurosyphilis is a rare but readily treatable cause of status epilepticus (SE). Nevertheless, SE has a substantial morbidity and mortality if treatment is refractory and/or life-threatening complications occur. Veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) has previously been successfully employed following life- threatening arrhythmias with refractory circulatory failure due to antiseizure medications (ASM) in the context of SE. Here we describe the combined use of VA-ECMO along with an Impella CP® micro-axial pump to provide full circulatory support and left ventricular unloading in a patient with a presumed drug-induced, refractory cardiac arrest amidst treatment for super-refractory status epilepticus (SRSE). This patient presented with a recurrent episode of convulsive SE with subsequent treatment-refractory nonconvulsive seizure activity on incremental ASM therapy. Investigations consistent with neurosyphilis prompted the initiation of antimicrobial therapy. ASM adjustments were made in view of suspected lacoseamide-induced arrhythmias, but subsequently a treatment-refractory cardiac arrest occurred with ensuing pulseless electrical activity and asystole. Mechanical life support followed by VA-ECMO was promptly initiated and an Impella CP® device was then placed given a non-ejecting heart. Subsequently, hemodynamic stabilization and seizure control were readily achieved and full cardiac recovery occurred after seven days. VA-ECMO plus Impella® provided effective circulatory support under which seizure control could be achieved and cardiac function recovered. Increased pro-arrhythmic risks due to possible synergistic inhibition of cardiac ionic channels need to be anticipated when multiple ASM and anesthetic agents are introduced during SE treatment. Neurosyphilis needs to always be considered as a rare cause of SE.

title: Holter-Detected Arrhythmias in Acute Exacerbations of COPD: NT-proBNP Correlates and Hypercapnia Associated with COPD-Related Readmission.
authorString: Ding N, Chen J, Qiu W, Lu Y, Chen Z, Cai R, Chen A.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Int J Chron Obstruct Pulmon Dis
journal.title: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Int J Chron Obstruct Pulmon Dis

abstractText:
Background

Cardiac arrhythmias are increasingly recognized during acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD), but their full spectrum and prognostic significance detected by continuous Holter monitoring remain insufficiently characterized.

Methods

We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of patients hospitalized for AECOPD between April 2022 and January 2025 who underwent continuous Holter monitoring. Arrhythmias were classified as atrial arrhythmias (AA), atrial fibrillation/flutter (AF/AFL), ventricular arrhythmias (VA), or coexistence of ≥2 arrhythmia types. Multivariable regression models were used to identify factors associated with arrhythmias and clinical outcomes. COPD-related readmission was assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses.

Results

Among 548 patients, 60.4% experienced at least one arrhythmia during hospitalization. AA (37.6%) was the most frequent subtype, followed by VA (31.0%) and AF/AFL (12.2%), while 21.5% exhibited multiple arrhythmia types. Older age, male sex, higher heart rate, elevated NT-proBNP, and larger left atrial diameter were independently associated with in-hospital arrhythmias. NT-proBNP was consistently associated with all arrhythmia phenotypes and demonstrated moderate discrimination for arrhythmia identification (AUC=0.730; cutoff, 131.5 pg/mL). AF/AFL was independently associated with prolonged hospitalization (adjusted ratio=1.26, P=0.010). After accounting for the time-dependent effect of age, hypercapnia (PaCO2 ≥45 mmHg) remained associated with a higher risk of COPD-related readmission (adjusted HR=1.85, 95% CI 1.19-2.88; P=0.007).

Conclusion

In-hospital arrhythmias are highly prevalent among patients hospitalized for AECOPD. NT-proBNP is consistently associated with multiple arrhythmia phenotypes and may aid arrhythmic risk stratification. Hypercapnia, but not arrhythmia status, remained independently associated with COPD-related readmission despite the limited sample and observational design.

title: Development and Internal Validation of a Clinical Prediction Model for Coronary Slow Flow Phenomenon in Type 2 Diabetes: A Retrospective Observational Study.
authorString: Hu S, Yan CS, Xu T, Li Y, Tian T, Zhao N, Cao GQ.
abstractText:
Background

Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) may exhibit coronary slow flow phenomenon (CSFP) despite the absence of obstructive epicardial coronary stenosis. Dedicated prediction tools remain limited. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a model for estimating the probability of TIMI frame count (TFC)-defined CSFP in patients with T2DM.

Methods

Among 501 patients with T2DM undergoing coronary angiography at a single center in Xinjiang, China (2021-2025), 429 met eligibility criteria. CSFP was defined as maximum coronary stenosis <40% and TFC >27 frames in at least one major coronary artery. Patients were randomly divided into training (n = 300) and validation (n = 129) cohorts. Predictors selected by penalized regression were entered into multivariable logistic regression. Performance was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC), area under the precision-recall curve (AUC-PR), calibration, bootstrap-corrected concordance index, and decision curve analysis; additional analyses were complementary.

Results

CSFP occurred in 44 patients (14.7%) in the training cohort and 16 (12.4%) in the validation cohort. The final model included smoking history, systolic blood pressure, hemoglobin A1c, lymphocyte count, and uric acid. ROC-AUC was 0.832 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.774-0.889) in the training cohort and 0.840 (95% CI: 0.733-0.946) in the validation cohort; AUC-PR was 0.467 and 0.542, respectively. Calibration was acceptable (Brier scores 0.101 and 0.084); bootstrap-corrected concordance indices were 0.827 and 0.846. Decision curve analysis suggested net benefit across clinically relevant thresholds. Given the limited number of CSFP events in the validation cohort, validation estimates should be interpreted cautiously.

Conclusion

We developed and internally validated a five-variable model for estimating the probability of TFC-defined CSFP in patients with T2DM. The model was translated into a nomogram and web-based calculator as a complementary tool for individualized risk characterization. External validation is required before broader clinical application.

title: Different body components associate differently with diet quality and physical activity in men and in women: a cross-sectional analysis.
authorString: Hosseini-Akhavan N, Bektashi B, Jaeggi AV, Bender N.
abstractText:
Background/objectives

While the association between food quantity and obesity is well studied, the impact of diet components on specific body compartments is less well understood. Furthermore, there seem to be sex differences in the metabolism of different foods and the response towards physical activity (PA).

Methods

We investigated the association between diet components using a food frequency questionnaire, and body composition using bioimpedance analysis. We assessed data from 2021 of a cohort study of the Swiss general population, including 435 persons of both sexes (age range of 19-84 years). We used multivariable linear regression models separated by sex to assess the association between body composition (body mass index (BMI), skeletal muscle mass index (SMI), fat mass index (FMI), and visceral fat (VAT)), and diet quality and PA. Age, education, and place of residence were included as potential confounders.

Results

For both sexes, age showed the strongest positive association with FMI and VAT, while PA was negatively associated, especially in men. In men PA was also associated with BMI (not in women). Diet quality showed associations with body composition measures in women (not in men). In women, meat consumption was positively associated with SMI and FMI (not in men). In men fruits and wholegrain foods were negatively associated with FMI. VAT was negatively associated with fruits in women, and with fruits and wholegrain foods in men.

Conclusion

Our results are in line with evolutionary hypotheses on sex specific energy allocation and might contribute to more precise diet recommendations.

title: 2026 Asia Pacific Heart Rhythm Society (APHRS) Guidelines (Part IV) on Comprehensive Lifestyle Risk Factor and Comorbidity Management in Atrial Fibrillation.
authorString: Choi EK, Middeldorp ME, Ahn HJ, Ariyaratnam JP, Elliott AD, Hung CL, Yu HT, Sharma G, Wang N, Yamaguchi T, Chen M, Joung B, Krittayaphong R, Soejima K, Lip GYH, Pak HN, Chao TF.
abstractText: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is closely associated with comorbidities and lifestyle factors that influence the development, progression, and outcomes. Here the focus is on guidelines for the systematic management of hypertension, heart failure, coronary and structural heart disease, diabetes, dyslipidemia, cerebrovascular disease, obesity, chronic kidney disease, thyroid dysfunction, inflammatory disease, cancer and frailty. In addition, it provides guidelines for lifestyle factors such as nutrition, physical activity, alcohol consumption, tobacco use, sleep and psychological health as key components of AF care. Finally, multimorbidity, polypharmacy and the diverse clinical, cultural, socioeconomic and healthcare contexts of the Asia Pacific region are also addressed. Particular focus is driven by evidence to support the comprehensive management of lifestyle factors as a core component of AF care with equitable access adapted to local resources and patient needs.

title: Semaglutide Remodels the Gut Microbiome Beyond Its Appetite-Suppressing Action: Sex-Specific Gut-Brain Axis Implications.
authorString: Byun S, Sotzen MR, Bento MT, Knappenberger MA, Asker M, Wright JR, Lamendella R, Mu C, Skibicka KP.
abstractText: The gut microbiome communicates bidirectionally with the brain and peripheral metabolic organs to regulate appetite and body weight. Semaglutide (SEMA), a GLP-1 receptor agonist, produces robust weight loss by reducing food intake, largely through brain GLP-1 receptors, yet whether its effects on the gut microbiome are secondary to this centrally driven hypophagia is poorly understood. Given the profound impact of SEMA on food intake and body weight, we propose that SEMA treatment reshapes gut microbial composition and that these shifts are correlated with metabolic outcomes. Diet-induced obese rats received a 4-week SEMA treatment and gut microbial composition was analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. To differentiate the impact of reduced food intake associated with SEMA from other effects of the drug treatment on the gut microbiome, a pair-fed to SEMA group was tested. SEMA significantly reduced body weight gain and food intake in both sexes. Significant SEMA-induced changes in microbial richness and evenness were detected. Linear discriminant analysis Effect Size (LEfSe) identified enrichment of Firmicutes taxa-particularly members of the Clostridiaceae family-in SEMA-treated rats, whereas controls showed greater representation of Bacteroidota taxa. Sex-specific associations between host metabolic parameters and gut microbial composition were also identified. These findings demonstrate profound, not necessarily health positive, partly sex-specific gut microbial community shifts following GLP-1 analogue treatment. Many of the changes in the gut microbiota were not simply driven by the decreased food intake. Thus, GLP-1 analogue treatment engages the gut microbiome through both food intake-dependent (brain-to-gut) and intake-independent pathways.

title: Identification of Patients with Colon Ischemia in the Swedish ESPRESSO Cohort: A Validation Study.
authorString: Klinglöf H, Söderling J, Hedin CRH, Frisell T, Granström AL, Ludvigsson JF, Everhov ÅH.
abstractText:
Background

Colon ischemia is the most common form of intestinal ischemia, yet case identification in epidemiological research remains challenging due to heterogeneous diagnostic criteria and absence of a specific International Classification of Diseases (ICD) code. The use of SNOMED (Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine) for gastrointestinal biopsies and surgical specimens enables a unique possibility to identify colon ischemia cases.

Methods

In this validation study, 231 individuals with SNOMED code M54 (necrosis) and colorectal topography codes (T67-T68) were randomly selected from five Swedish regions. Medical charts were retrieved for 204 cases, where 143 contained sufficient information for evaluation. Cases were classified by clinical overall assessment and assigned an etiological group. Positive predictive values (PPVs) were calculated for overall colon ischemia based on histopathology alone and for etiological subsets where histopathology was combined with ICD codes.

Results

Of 143 patients with sufficient clinical information for validation, histopathological ischemic injury of the colon was confirmed in 141, corresponding to a PPV of 99% (95% CI, 95-99%). Combining SNOMED codes with selected ICD codes yielded a PPV of 84% (95% CI, 73-92%) for clinically confirmed idiopathic colon ischemia, increasing to 92% (95% CI, 79-98%) when more restrictive ICD-based criteria were applied.

Conclusion

SNOMED-based histopathological case identification demonstrated a very high PPV for ischemic injury of the colon but could not distinguish idiopathic disease from ischemia secondary to identifiable clinical conditions. Combining SNOMED and ICD codes provides a feasible and reproducible strategy for identifying underlying causes of colon ischemia in Swedish nationwide health registers.

title: Porta Hepatis Paraganglioma: A Rare Case Report With Diagnostic Pitfalls.
authorString: Vajihinejad M, Najafi S, Amlelshahbaz A, Saeed SA.
abstractText: Paragangliomas are rare neuroendocrine tumors that infrequently localize to the porta hepatis, where they create significant diagnostic challenges by mimicking hepatocellular carcinoma or distinct mesenchymal neoplasms. We report the case of a 64-year-old woman presenting with vague abdominal pain and an enhancing porta hepatis mass compressing the inferior vena cava. An initial core needle biopsy, which suggested a benign mesenchymal tumor, underscores the potential for misdiagnosis in such atypical presentations. During surgery, the patient developed paroxysmal hypertension suggestive of occult catecholamine release. Subsequent histopathological examination revealed a classic zellballen pattern, with immunohistochemical positivity for Chromogranin A, Synaptophysin, and S100 definitively confirming a paraganglioma. The patient remains disease-free at a 2-year follow-up. This case highlights the importance of considering paraganglioma in the differential diagnosis of porta hepatis masses and emphasizes the value of histopathology and immunohistochemistry for accurate diagnosis, particularly in patients who lack preoperative adrenergic symptoms.

title: 2026 Asia Pacific Heart Rhythm Society (APHRS) Guidelines (Part III) on Rate and Rhythm Control in Atrial Fibrillation.
authorString: Chen M, Soejima K, Gunawardene M, Kojodjojo P, Liu H, Liu T, Miyazaki S, Morishima I, Sanders P, Tse HF, Yamaguchi T, Choi EK, Joung B, Krittayaphong R, Middeldorp M, Lip GYH, Pak HN, Chao TF, Kim YH, Chen SA.

title: HbA1c and LDL-C Time in Therapeutic Range: A Study on All-Cause Mortality in Older Adults with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Chronic Kidney Disease.
authorString: Wang X, Yang J, Wang Q, Ye Z, Feng Z, Dong Z.
abstractText:
Introduction

Whether long-term attainment of glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) targets improves prognosis in older adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains unclear. We used time in therapeutic range (TTR) to quantify sustained glycemic and lipid control and examined its association, and interaction, with all-cause mortality.

Research design and methods

This retrospective multicenter cohort study, based on the Tianjin Health Big Data Platform, included 2005 older (≥65 years) and 5973 younger (<65 years) adults with T2DM-CKD. HbA1c-TTR (target <7.0%) and LDL-TTR (target <1.8 mmol/L) were calculated using the Rosendaal method. After Cox-LASSO covariate selection, multivariable Cox models with and without an interaction term were built, supplemented by RCS, subgroup analyses, and landmark and time-varying covariate sensitivity analyses.

Results

Over a median follow-up of 4.56 years, 211 older adults (10.5%) died. Without an interaction term, LDL-TTR (per 10-percentage-point increase) was associated with lower mortality (HR 0.934, P=0.003), while HbA1c-TTR was not (HR 0.983, P=0.459); with the interaction term, the HbA1c-TTR × LDL-TTR interaction was significant (HR 1.016, P=0.006). Adjusted RCS showed a significant nonlinear association for LDL-TTR (P nonlinear=0.020) but not for HbA1c-TTR overall (P=0.231). In the younger cohort, both main effects were significant, but the interaction was not (P=0.124). The interaction remained significant in the time-varying covariate model (HR 1.013, P=0.019) but not in the landmark analysis or under the alternative 6.5-8.0% HbA1c definition, under which LDL-TTR's main effect remained significant.

Conclusions

In older adults with T2DM and CKD, higher LDL-TTR was independently associated with lower mortality, and a significant HbA1c-TTR × LDL-TTR interaction suggested that the inverse association of one TTR measure with mortality was attenuated at higher levels of the other. This interaction was absent in the younger cohort and under an alternative HbA1c target (6.5-8.0%), and was inconsistent across sensitivity analyses (significant with time-varying covariates, HR 1.013, P=0.019; non-significant in a landmark analysis, P=0.968). These exploratory findings do not support changing current management targets and require prospective validation.

title: Opportunistic Cardiovascular Assessment During Lung Cancer Screening with Low-Dose Computed Tomography: A New Window for Prevention.
authorString: Sienkiewicz K, Fijałkowska J, Jelitto M, Byczkowski J, Koliński M, Szurowska E, Rzyman W.
abstractText: Population-based lung cancer screening with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) is expanding across Europe, including a publicly funded Polish programme starting in October 2026. Because screening-eligible individuals share substantial tobacco-related cardiovascular risk, LDCT also offers cardiovascular risk assessment without additional radiation. We conducted a narrative review of the PubMed literature published up to September 2026, prioritising guidelines, lung cancer screening cohorts and systematic reviews. We summarise the cardiovascular findings on non-contrast, non-electrocardiography (ECG)-gated LDCT: coronary artery, aortic valve, mitral annular and thoracic aortic calcification, ascending aortic dilatation, pericardial effusion, and pulmonary artery enlargement, as well as investigational cardiac volumetry, epicardial adipose tissue and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted quantification. We grade each finding by reportability, defined downstream action and supporting evidence, and align reporting thresholds with the European Respiratory Society/European Society of Thoracic Imaging (ERS/ESTI) statement on incidental findings. LDCT cannot replace dedicated cardiac imaging or establish haemodynamic diagnoses. The prognostic value of coronary and aortic valve calcification and of ascending aortic dilatation is established, whereas the evidence for mitral annular calcification and pulmonary artery enlargement is more limited; observational data indicate that reporting these markers changes preventive management, but whether this improves cardiovascular outcomes has not yet been demonstrated. Standardised reporting, proportionate thresholds, and coordinated pathways linking radiology, pulmonology, primary care and cardiology are needed to translate incidental cardiovascular findings into scalable prevention and should be evaluated in implementation studies.

title: Factor H polymorphism elevates granzyme B and impairs complement inhibition in human and mouse models.
authorString: Chakravarthy H, Xi J, Yoo HS, Buss A, Li B, Bell R, Haegert A, Le Bihan S, Granville DJ, Matsubara JA.
abstractText: The complement factor H (CFH) Y402H polymorphism is a leading genetic risk factor for age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Here, we identify extracellular granzyme B (GzmB) as a crucial mediator connecting complement dysregulation to structural pathology. In non-AMD human donor eyes, the high-risk CFH genotype was associated with increased GzmB-positive choroidal mast cells, membrane attack complex deposition, and distinct vitronectin redistribution. Using in vitro human retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) cells, we demonstrate that complement fragment C5a triggers GzmB secretion and zonula occludens-1 disruption. RNA sequencing of GzmB-stimulated RPE cells confirmed transcriptomic signatures of barrier dysfunction and cellular stress. Furthermore, GzmB-deficient mice displayed preserved choroidal vitronectin compared with wild-type controls, supporting a role for GzmB in cleaving this terminal complement inhibitor. These findings delineate a pathogenic C5a-GzmB pathway compromising extracellular matrix integrity, implicating extracellular GzmB as a critical downstream mediator linking genetic risk to early AMD onset.

title: Health-Related Quality of Life in Homozygous Familial Hypercholesterolemia: Results from an Online Survey.
authorString: Evans E, Lichaa C, Jones RD, Wiegman A, Daccord M.
abstractText:
Background and aims

Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH) is a rare inherited disorder characterized by dangerously high low-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels from birth, creating extreme risk of premature cardiovascular events if untreated. Health-related quality of life (HRQoL) associated with HoFH is not well characterized.

Methods

Across multiple countries, patients ≥12 years (y) with HoFH and caregivers ≥18y of patients with HoFH completed an online survey between April-May 2023 and May-August 2024. HRQoL was measured for patients and caregivers using the EuroQol 5 Dimension 5 Level (EQ-5D-5L) and the EuroQol visual analogue scale (EQ-VAS). Utility values were generated based on EQ-5D-5L responses using UK, US, and country-specific tariffs. Median annual cost associated with receiving/accompanying patients to receive lipoprotein apheresis (LA) was estimated.

Results

Most patients (n = 8/15) were aged 25-34y; all caregivers (n = 9) were >35y. Mean age at diagnosis was 6.7y (patients)/4.8y (patients of caregivers). Eleven (73%) patients/six (67%) patients of caregivers were receiving LA. EQ-5D-5L scores were lower in patients (0.74) than reported normal range for age-matched English population (0.79-0.95 [range 18-54y]) and average US adult score (0.85). EQ-VAS scores were lower for patients (mean 64/100) than reported US adult average score (80/100). Caregivers scored in normal range. Patients receiving LA reported lower HRQoL than patients who were not. Patients on weekly LA reported markedly lower HRQoL than those receiving it less frequently. Median annual cost associated with undergoing LA was €4915/y (patients)/€5161/y (caregivers).

Conclusions

HoFH substantially and negatively impacts patient HRQoL. Receiving LA, whilst efficacious, is costly and demanding on patients' and caregivers' time.

title: Robotic resection of cardiac papillary fibroelastoma guided by three-dimensional transesophageal echocardiography: a case report.
authorString: Sakamoto FH, Rodrigues ACT, Fischer CH, Lira-Filho E, Morhy SS, Reche AV, Poffo R, Curcio SAF, Azevedo J, Faustino SAF, Sousa JHD, Vieira MLC.
abstractText: Heart neoplasms are classified as primary or secondary, with primary tumors considered rare. Cardiac papillary fibroelastoma is the second most common benign cardiac tumor. It has distinct morphological features and carries a potential risk of embolization; therefore, surgical excision is generally recommended. The use of three-dimensional transesophageal echocardiography (3D TEE) enables improved characterization of the suspected lesion, provides a detailed anatomical assessment, and assists in intraoperative planning and management. We report the case of a patient diagnosed with a cardiac papillary fibroelastoma of the mitral valve who underwentrobotic-assisted surgery guided by 3D TEE.

title: Endothelial nitric oxide signaling in cellular and systemic metabolism.
authorString: Siragusa M, Dunaway LS, Lammert E, Fleming I, Isakson BE, Cortese-Krott MM.
abstractText: Endothelial cell-derived nitric oxide (NO) is best known for its role in the regulation of vascular tone. However, growing evidence shows that endothelial NO acts as a flux- and compartment-dependent redox regulator of cellular and systemic metabolism. NO directly modulates metabolic networks through reversible or irreversible chemical modification of iron centers, reactive cysteine and tyrosine residues as well as fatty acids. Mechanisms of NO-mediated regulation of cellular metabolism include the S-nitrosation of enzymes involved in glycolysis, oxidative phosphorylation and nucleotide biosynthesis as well as the control of iron and heme availability. NO-derived nitrating species additionally generate electrophilic nitro-fatty acids, which act on metabolic and redox transcriptional programs through reversible cysteine adduction. Moreover, specialized endothelial cells contribute to metabolic regulation across organs, for example lipid trafficking in adipose tissue, iron homeostasis in the liver and erythropoiesis in the bone marrow. Finally, tissue/organ-specific endothelial dysfunction may disrupt organ and systemic metabolic control through multiple mechanisms, raising new questions and therapeutic opportunities. Understanding how cell- and enzymatic source-specific NO signaling defines endothelial heterogeneity and function may provide a mechanistic framework to address organ-specific endothelial dysfunction in cardiometabolic disease.

title: Comment on "Tracing the evolution of cardiology: Pioneering discoveries and paradigm shifts in cardiovascular care".
authorString: Amaravadi D, Dahiya S, Hemalatha PK, Murugesan S.

title: Case Report: Pediatric deep vein thrombosis: when pain in the leg becomes a telltale sign.
authorString: Balyorugulu GG, Barnabas E, Malole N, Almasi H, Makorere J.
abstractText:
Introduction

Deep vein thrombosis is rare in the pediatric population. It carries severe complications such as pulmonary embolism with high mortality. Since it shares presentation with other causes of acute limb pain, diagnosis might be delayed. Early detection of leg pain with immobility, fever, and swelling should raise an alarm for investigating deep vein thrombosis and prompt immediate management. We report a case of a child with chronic thrombocytosis and anemia diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis after sustaining an injury.

Case presentation

Here we report a case of a two-year-old boy presenting with right leg pain for two days with fever after sustaining a fall while playing. x-ray of the leg ruled out fracture, with further investigation showing a raised D-dimer, and a Doppler ultrasound confirming deep vein thrombosis of the right common femoral vein. Standard-of-care anticoagulants were initiated and later discharged on daily oral anticoagulants for six weeks, with scheduled biweekly follow-up clinics and hematologist review.

Conclusion

Deep vein thrombosis, though rare in the pediatric population, requires a high index of suspicion in those presenting with limb pain and risk factors such as trauma. Delay in recognition can lead to catastrophic complications such as pulmonary embolism and death.

title: Clinical characteristics, molecular features and <i>in vitro</i> susceptibility to sulbactam-durlobactam, cefiderocol, and eravacycline in NDM-1-producing versus OXA-23-producing carbapenem-resistant <i>Acinetobacter baumannii</i> isolates from children in Guangxi, China.
authorString: Liu M, Li M, Yan C, Huang L, Zhang H.

journal.title: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

abstractText:
Background

Carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii (CRAB) has been recognized as a critical priority pathogen responsible for a wide range of hospital-acquired infections.

Methods

We included pediatric CRAB infection cases at a Maternal and Child Health Hospital in Guangxi, China, from January 2019 to December 2024. The bacterial isolates had previously undergone whole-genome sequencing (WGS). An NDM-1-producing CRAB strain isolated from a bloodstream infection was subjected to Nanopore sequencing to characterize the NDM-1-encoding plasmid. We then retrospectively analyzed the risk factors for NDM-1-producing CRAB infection in children. In addition, the NDM-1-producing and OXA-23-producing CRAB strains were subjected to antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) against sulbactam-durlobactam, cefiderocol, and eravacycline using the micro-broth dilution method, and their susceptibility profiles were compared. Associated resistance genes were analyzed.

Results

A total of 131 pediatric patients with CRAB infections were included in this study. Based on the WGS data, 33 CRAB strains harboring bla NDM-1 were classified into the NDM-1-producing group, while 98 CRAB strains harboring bla OXA-23 were classified into the OXA-23-producing group. On multivariable analysis, indwelling urethral catheters (OR = 0.293; P = 0.009) and white blood cell (WBC) count (OR = 0.896; P = 0.039) were negatively associated with NDM-1-producing CRAB infection, yet positively associated with OXA-23-producing infections (P < 0.05). WGS analysis revealed that 32 of the 33 (97.0%) NDM-1-producing CRAB isolates co-carried bla PER-1, which has been reported to be associated with cefiderocol resistance in A. baumannii. Plasmid mapping showed that the same plasmid co-harbored bla NDM-1 and bla PER-1, together with a type IV secretion system (T4SS). The resistance rate of NDM-1-producing CRAB isolates to sulbactam-durlobactam was 100%, and to cefiderocol was 66.7%-both rates being significantly higher than those observed in the OXA-23-producing group (1.0% and 0.0%, respectively; P < 0.001). However, all 131 isolates demonstrated susceptibility to eravacycline in vitro.

Conclusion

Clinical characteristics and antibiotic susceptibility differed significantly between NDM-1-producing and OXA-23-producing CRAB infections. Carbapenemase surveillance is critical for the management of CRAB infections among pediatric patients in Guangxi, China, and AST is essential to guide treatment.

title: Case Report: Hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia and arterial aneurysms in KAT6B-related disorder: case observation and literature perspective.
authorString: Improda N, Rosanio FM, Ballarin G, Acquaviva F, di Nardo G, Lepore L, Pascarella A, Mirra V, Licenziati MR.
abstractText:
Introduction

KAT6B-related disorders (KAT6B-RD) are rare autosomal dominant chromatinopathies characterized by variable multisystem involvement and marked phenotypic heterogeneity.

Case presentation

We describe a preterm male infant with intrauterine growth restriction who developed recurrent hypoglycemia toward the end of the first week of life during parenteral nutrition weaning, requiring a glucose infusion rate of up to 12 mg/kg/min. Biochemical findings were consistent with hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia, and glycemic control was rapidly achieved with diazoxide (initiated at 5 mg/kg/day and increased to 6.9 mg/kg/day). After treatment discontinuation at 4 months of age, he exhibited recurrent hypoglycemia again, requiring the resumption of diazoxide. The patient also exhibited complete scrotal agenesis with complex genital anomalies, agenesis of the corpus callosum, generalized hypotonia, severe feeding difficulties requiring gastrostomy, primary hypothyroidism, and aneurysmal dilation of the ascending aorta and proximal right coronary artery. Clinical exome sequencing identified a de novo heterozygous pathogenic KAT6B variant (c.3995del; p.Pro1332Leufs*2) in exon 17. Diazoxide was successfully discontinued at 12 months of age under continuous glucose monitoring.

Conclusion

This case highlights congenital hyperinsulinism and arterial aneurysms as a clinical association observed in a patient with KAT6B-RD. Rather than representing definitive novel features of the syndrome, these manifestations should be interpreted with caution as hypothesis-generating findings potentially linked to KAT6B-mediated epigenetic dysregulation, while accounting for potential perinatal confounding factors. These findings nonetheless support careful endocrine and cardiovascular surveillance and follow-up in patients with KAT6B-RD.

title: Hotspot-targeted life support training reduces code blue alarms in a tertiary children's hospital: a single-center observational before-after study.
authorString: Umlauf VN, Bieri R, Studer D, Riedel T.
abstractText:
Background

Code Blue emergency alarms are activated by hospital staff for life- threatening patient situations. Despite their low frequency in children's hospitals, ward staff must bridge the first critical minutes until arrival of dedicated emergency response teams. Thus, the aim of this study was to identify hotspots and causes of emergencies, and to evaluate whether a hotspot-specific pediatric basic life support training (PBLS) reduces Code Blue alarms.

Methods

This analysis included all Code Blue alarms at the University Children's Hospital Bern before (January 2021-April 2023) and after (January 2024-December 2025) introduction of a hotspot-targeted PBLS program. Following identification of ward-specific hotspots and recurring emergency situations during Period 1, standard PBLS training was reorganized and supplemented by short simulation-based trainings tailored to the most frequent local emergencies. Variables between periods were statistically compared. Incidence rates were calculated per 1000 patient days.

Results

65 Code Blue alarms were analyzed. Respiratory emergencies and seizures were the most common causes, with infants and toddlers being the most affected age group. No weekend but a lunch-time effect was observed. Code Blue incidence decreased from 0.58 to 0.21 alarms per 1000 patient-days after implementation (IRR 0.36, 95% CI 0.19-0.66, p < 0.001). Fragility analysis confirmed result robustness, with no evidence of bias from missing data, case mix index, PICU transfer rates, or non-Code Blue Medical Emergency Team (MET) consultations.

Conclusions

Hotspot-specific PBLS training was associated with a marked reduction in pediatric Code Blue alarms. Identification of local emergency patterns may help hospitals develop targeted ward-based training strategies to improve in-hospital emergency management.

title: Pyogenic brain abscesses in Qatar: A national retrospective observational study.
authorString: Zara S, Al Balushi S, Koleri J, Aziz A, Ansari S, Hussein M, Alzibdeh AH, Saleh A, Munir W, Omrani AS, Al Maslamani M.
abstractText:
Objectives

Pyogenic brain abscess is a life-threatening intracranial infection requiring timely diagnosis and coordinated medical-surgical management. Regional data from the Gulf area remains scarce.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed demographic, clinical, microbiological, management, and outcome data from adults diagnosed with pyogenic brain abscess based on clinical presentation and neuroimaging findings at Hamad Medical Corporation, Qatar, between 2015 and 2023. Outcomes were categorized using the Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS) as favorable (GOS 4-5) or unfavorable (GOS 1-3).

Results

Forty-eight patients were included; 41/48 (85%) were male, with a median age of 34 years. Common comorbidities and predisposing conditions included diabetes mellitus, otitis/mastoiditis, and sinusitis. A microbiological diagnosis was established in 35/48 (73%) patients. The most frequently isolated pathogens were the Streptococcus anginosus group, Staphylococcus aureus, and Klebsiella pneumoniae. Surgical intervention was performed in 38/48 (79%) patients, and 35/48 (73%) achieved a favorable outcome. In unadjusted analyses, recent neurosurgical procedures and Gram-negative infections were more frequent among patients with unfavorable outcomes. These patients had lower baseline Glasgow Coma Scale scores and more frequently presented with altered consciousness.

Conclusion

In unadjusted analyses, favorable outcomes were more frequent among patients who underwent surgical intervention and those presenting with preserved consciousness. However, causality cannot be inferred.

title: The application value of artificial intelligence in medical imaging: foundations, progress, and challenges.
authorString: Sun H, Zhang Y, Shi Y, Ji B, Li C, Yang J, Grzegorzek M, Guo Q.
abstractText: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming medical imaging, reshaping the field as it does everyday life. As imaging data grow in complexity and clinical workloads continue to rise, AI has become increasingly essential for improving diagnostic efficiency and precision. However, despite these technical advances, the clinical adoption of AI in medical imaging remains fragmented, with limited generalizability, insufficient interpretability, and unclear clinical responsibility. In this review, we critically examine the evolution of AI in medical imaging, with a particular focus on its functional roles across the imaging workflow and its actual contributions to contemporary clinical needs. We systematically analyze current application paradigms, identify methodological and translational bottlenecks, and discuss emerging strategies to improve model robustness, interpretability, and clinical integration. In addition, we identify key barriers to the practical implementation of AI in medical imaging, including challenges related to cross-domain generalizability, data privacy issues and regulatory compliance. By examining these opportunities and challenges, this review aims to guide future research directions and foster deeper interdisciplinary collaboration among AI, clinical medicine, and biomedical engineering.

title: Epidemiology, clinical characteristics, and outcomes of infective endocarditis over a decade in a tertiary care hospital in Oman.
authorString: Sakiti NAA, Al-Lawati A, Jose S, Bahrani KA, Khamis F.
abstractText:
Objectives

Infective endocarditis (IE) remains associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, although data from Oman and the Gulf region are limited. We aimed to describe the epidemiology, clinical characteristics, microbiological profile, and in-hospital outcomes of definite IE in a tertiary care hospital in Oman.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients admitted between 2006 and 2016. Cases were identified from electronic medical records using the International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification code I33.0. The modified Duke criteria were applied retrospectively and only definite IE cases were included.

Results

Among 172 screened patients, 130 (75.6%) met the criteria for definite IE. The mean age was 42.3 years, and the median symptom duration before diagnosis was 14 days. Native valve IE occurred in 113 (87.0%) patients and prosthetic valve IE occurred in 17 (13.0%). Staphylococcus species were the most commonly isolated pathogens (43.1%), among which Staphylococcus aureus accounted for 38.5%. In-hospital mortality was 31.5%, and mortality was lower in patients who underwent surgery than in those who did not (18.0% vs 40.0%; P = 0.011).

Conclusion

In this Omani cohort, IE affected a relatively young population and was characterized by predominant S. aureus infection and high in-hospital mortality. These findings support context-specific empiric therapy, early echocardiographic evaluation, and timely surgical assessment.

title: Targeting STAT3 to Modulate the Effectiveness of Cardioprotective Conditioning Strategies Against Myocardial Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury in Subjects With Diabetic Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Wang C, Tian W, Saedi S, Cui H, Liu D, Chu Q, Yang D, Xia Z.

journal.title: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine

abstractText: Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI) is a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Reperfusion, although essential for myocardial restoration, can paradoxically exacerbate injury through oxidative stress, calcium overload, mitochondrial permeability transition pore opening and inflammatory infiltration. The vulnerability to MIRI is substantially amplified in subjects with diabetes mellitus, where chronic hyperglycemia, insulin resistance, and the resulting oxidative stress and low-grade inflammation impair endogenous cardioprotective mechanisms and worsen postinfarction outcomes. Ischemic conditioning strategies, including preconditioning and postconditioning, serve as powerful innate methods to mitigate MIRI by exposing the myocardium to brief, sublethal ischemic episodes that activate crucial prosurvival signalling pathways. Among these pathways, the survivor activating factor enhancement pathway, which is mediated predominantly by signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3), and the reperfusion injury salvage kinase pathway, which involves AKT and ERK, are particularly important. However, in many models of diabetes, diabetes-induced STAT3 dysfunction may disrupt these protective pathways, often making conditioning stimuli less effective. The precise mechanisms underlying this impairment remain incompletely understood. Additionally, paradoxical changes in STAT3 expression have been reported, and key posttranslational modifications of STAT3 have not yet been investigated in the context of diabetic MIRI. This review provides a critical appraisal of the role, regulatory mechanisms and therapeutic potential of STAT3 in ischemic conditioning in patients with diabetes and discusses strategies aimed at restoring cardioprotection in this high-risk population.

title: Persistent Cholelithiasis Following Biochemical Resolution of Parenteral Nutrition-Associated Cholestasis in a Former Preterm Infant: Surgical Management With Open Cholecystectomy.
authorString: Flores-Zepeda BA, Celis-Recio CP, Beltrán-Delgado JO, Sánchez-Flores DA, Soto-Valle JE.
abstractText: Gallstones in early infancy are increasingly detected in survivors of neonatal intensive care, and most contemporary series favor observation because spontaneous resolution is common. Less well described is the divergence that may follow: cholestasis resolves completely while the stones formed during it remain. We present the case of a male infant born at 35 weeks of gestation who required high-frequency oscillatory ventilation, five vasoactive agents for septic shock, and 23 days of parenteral nutrition during a 45-day admission, developing cholestatic liver disease (total bilirubin 11.9 mg/dL, alkaline phosphatase 1,657 U/L). Ultrasonography at 2.8 months showed a cluster of gallstones measuring 9.8 × 5 × 7.4 mm, without cholecystitis or duct dilation. The cholestasis then resolved completely, and growth was restored; at 7.3 months, total bilirubin was 0.15 mg/dL and gamma-glutamyl transferase was 8 U/L. The stones did not resolve, a 6.5 mm calculus persisted at 5.0 months, and the infant remained asymptomatic. After six months of observation, open cholecystectomy was performed at eight months and 26 days of age and 9.1 kg, without complication; a black pigment calculus was recovered, and histopathology showed changes of immaturity without inflammatory infiltrate. He was discharged on the second postoperative day and remained free of biliary symptoms through 102 days. Biochemical recovery of the liver does not predict clearance of established lithiasis, the lithogenic exposures in these infants are multiple and should not be attributed to parenteral nutrition alone, and operating on an asymptomatic infant deserves to be argued explicitly rather than assumed.

title: Strengthening Newborn Screening, Diagnosis and Management of Birth Defects in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Priority for WHO Member States.
authorString: De Costa A, Duran P, Khanna R, Kayita J, Siddeeg K.
abstractText: As infectious causes of child mortality decline, birth defects represent a growing relative proportion of neonatal and under-five deaths (as well as unmeasured morbidity) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), underscoring the need to integrate their prevention, detection and care into child health agendas. In response to World Health Assembly resolution WHA77.5, the World Health Organization (WHO) convened global consultations with LMIC programme leaders, experts, academics, civil society, affected persons and families to develop a framework for integrating newborn screening, diagnosis and management of birth defects into national health systems. This communication summarizes key lessons from country experience and sets out the core principles for implementation captured in the framework: start with one or a few feasible, high-impact conditions; link screening to diagnosis, management and long-term follow-up; assess health-system readiness before scale-up; secure sustainable financing; strengthen data systems; and provide family-centred support. The recent WHO report 'Strengthening Newborn Screening, Diagnosis and Management of Birth Defects' focused on LMICs and offers a pragmatic pathway for countries to expand newborn screening equitably while building the services needed to improve survival, functioning and quality of life for children with congenital conditions.

title: Recurrent Pleural Effusion as the Initial Presentation of T-lineage Lymphoblastic Malignancy in a Child: A Diagnostic Challenge.
authorString: Fakih H, Fakih F.
abstractText: Pleural effusion in children is most frequently associated with infectious diseases, particularly parapneumonic effusion. Recurrent or unexplained pleural effusion, however, should prompt consideration of less common etiologies, including autoimmune disease, tuberculosis, chylothorax, cardiac and renal disease, and malignancy. We report the case of a 10-year-old boy with recurrent large right-sided pleural effusions requiring repeated drainage of more than 1,500 mL. An extensive diagnostic evaluation for rheumatologic and infectious causes was unrevealing. During the current admission, the patient had anorexia, weight loss, axillary lymphadenopathy, leukocytosis, and mild thrombocytopenia, without reported peripheral blood blasts. Chest computed tomography demonstrated a large right pleural collection, bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy, and prominent thymic tissue without a definite bulky anterior mediastinal mass. Pleural-fluid flow cytometry demonstrated an abnormal immature T-lineage lymphoblast population comprising approximately 99% of analyzed cells. Pleural biopsy showed tissue infiltration by atypical lymphoid cells morphologically resembling non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Subsequent bone marrow examination, performed after three days of methylprednisolone therapy, demonstrated diffuse blast infiltration with an immature T-cell immunophenotype and was diagnostic of T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia. Lymph-node biopsy showed lymphoproliferative disease, while lumbar puncture was normal. Pleural-fluid tuberculosis PCR and acid-fast bacilli testing were negative. This case emphasizes that recurrent pleural effusion may be an initial and predominant manifestation of T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, even in the absence of peripheral blood blasts or a typical mediastinal mass. Early pleural-fluid flow cytometry may facilitate diagnosis and prevent diagnostic delay.

title: A Rare Association of Turner Syndrome, Celiac Disease, and Ulcerative Colitis in a Pediatric Patient: A Case Report.
authorString: Rogalidou M, Dimakou K, Stefanaki K, Botsa E, Messaritaki A, Kanaka-Gantenbein C.
abstractText: Background and Clinical Significance: Turner syndrome is associated with an increased prevalence of autoimmune disorders, particularly celiac disease, and is also associated with impaired bone health. The coexistence of Turner syndrome, celiac disease, and ulcerative colitis is rare and represents a challenging clinical scenario requiring multidisciplinary management; Case Presentation: We report the case of a 7-year-old girl referred for short stature who was diagnosed with celiac disease based on positive serology and duodenal histology (Marsh 3a/3c). Cytogenetic analysis revealed 46,X,i(X)(q10) Turner syndrome. Despite strict adherence to a gluten-free diet, persistent growth impairment led to initiation of recombinant human growth hormone therapy. At 14 years of age, she developed bloody diarrhea, weight loss, iron-deficiency anemia, and elevated inflammatory markers. Colonoscopy and histology confirmed extensive ulcerative colitis. During follow-up, dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry demonstrated reduced bone mineral density (lumbar spine Z-score -2.7; whole-body Z-score -2.5). At 16 years of age, treatment with azathioprine and 5-aminosalicylic acid was complicated by pancreatitis, with recurrence of pancreatic enzyme elevation following sequential drug reintroduction, leading to discontinuation of both agents. Infliximab therapy was subsequently initiated, resulting in sustained clinical, endoscopic, and near-complete histological remission. The patient was later transitioned to adult multidisciplinary care; Conclusions: The coexistence of Turner syndrome, celiac disease, ulcerative colitis, and low bone mineral density is an exceptionally rare combination of genetic susceptibility, autoimmunity, and chronic inflammation. This case highlights the importance of lifelong multidisciplinary surveillance in patients with Turner syndrome, including monitoring for additional autoimmune disorders, growth impairment, and skeletal complications.

title: FACE AHEAD 2026 Abstract Report.
authorString: Leung YY, Abdelazeem M, Chaiprakit N, Elbarbary A, Heredero-Jung S, Sánchez-Aniceto G.
abstractText: Welcome to FACE AHEAD 2026.

title: Fetal arrhythmia and heart disease during COVID-19 pandemic in patients who underwent echocardiography.
authorString: Mattos FA, Tavares GMP, Callado GY, Marra AR, Simioni C, Castello RG, Sanchez RC, Santana EFM.

journal.title: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia

abstractText:
Objective

To evaluate the characteristics and the occurrence of fetal heart diseases and arrhythmias in pregnancies that underwent fetal echocardiography examination during COVID-19 pandemic.

Methods

A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data extracted from the Fetal Ultrasound and Fetal Medicine Departments of Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein, a tertiary hospital in São Paulo, Brazil, from January to December 2021. The sample was analyzed using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, and Student's t-test or the Mann-Whitney test. Logistic regression was performed to assess the risk of fetal arrhythmia and/or heart disease.

Results

A total of 148 fetuses were included in the analysis. The prevalence of fetal heart disease/arrhythmia was higher among patients with maternal comorbidities (73.3% vs. 39.1%), fetal defects (14.3% vs. 0.8%), and functional abnormalities (26.7% vs. 4.5%). Maternal COVID-19 showed no significant association with fetal cardiac outcomes. Maternal comorbidity, fetal malformation, and the presence of functional abnormalities were identified as independent risk factors.

Conclusion

Maternal comorbidities were associated with fetal arrhythmia and/or heart disease, but no causal relationship was found between COVID-19 and adverse fetal cardiac outcome.

title: Clinical and Echocardiographic Characterization of Stage B Heart Failure in Asymptomatic Adults With Cardiovascular Risk Factors.
authorString: Amir MA, Hannan A, Shabbir MF, Nathaniel E, Ilgizovich AI, Haleem F, Saeed S, Arshad MU, Idris Abubakr IM, BaniKhalaf S.
abstractText:
Background

Stage B heart failure (pre-HF) is characterized by objective cardiac abnormalities without HF symptoms. This study assessed the prevalence and clinical and echocardiographic characteristics of those who were asymptomatic yet had cardiovascular risk factors and Stage B HF.

Methods

This cross-sectional study included 900 asymptomatic adults with cardiovascular risk factors, consecutively recruited from participating hospitals from October 2025 to July 2026. We performed clinical evaluation and a standardized transthoracic echocardiogram. Stage B/pre-HF was defined as the presence of objective cardiac structural or functional abnormalities in the absence of heart failure symptoms or signs. We evaluated independent factors associated with Stage B/pre-HF using multivariable logistic regression.

Results

In this hospital-based cohort, Stage B/pre-HF was determined in 261 (29.0%) participants. Hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and obesity were more prevalent in the Stage B group, occurring in 154 (59.0%), 118 (45.2%), and 109 (41.8%), respectively. Stage B/pre-HF was characterized descriptively by lower left ventricular ejection fraction and higher left ventricular mass index, left atrial volume index, E/e' ratio, and tricuspid regurgitation velocity, along with impaired diastolic function. Hypertension was the strongest independent association (OR = 5.930, 95% CI: 3.815-9.217), followed by diabetes (OR = 2.945, 95% CI: 1.913-4.532), age, sex, and BMI. The model showed good fit (Nagelkerke R² = 0.565; Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.449).

Conclusion

Stage B/pre-HF was common among asymptomatic adults with cardiovascular risk factors and was characterized by structural and functional cardiac abnormalities. These findings support the potential value of early identification and management of modifiable cardiovascular risk factors in asymptomatic adults at risk for HF.

title: Anomalous Left Brachiocephalic Vein Draining into the Right Internal Thoracic Vein: A Case Report.
authorString: Kang DW, Seo JW, Lee BY.

journal.title: Journal of the Korean Society of Radiology

abstractText: The left brachiocephalic vein (LBCV) rarely exhibits an anomalous course and its major patterns have been described in several studies. Although LBCV anomalies are mostly asymptomatic, their identification and recognition are important in clinical settings such as cardiovascular intervention or surgery. Herein, we report a rare anomalous LBCV that was incidentally detected on chest computed tomography in a 59-year-old female. Instead of directly draining into the superior vena cava (SVC), this anomalous LBCV travelled an extraordinarily long, downward trajectory to drain into the right internal thoracic vein and consequently into the SVC.

title: Severe Pulmonary Hypertension in Critically Ill Children: A 10-Year Single-Center Case Series and Practical Management Considerations.
authorString: Straka K, Polymerou I, Christakou E.
abstractText: Severe pulmonary hypertension (PH) in children may decompensate rapidly during intercurrent illness and is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality in the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU). We describe the clinical presentation, intensive care management, and outcomes of four children with severe PH admitted to a tertiary PICU between January 2014 and December 2024. Three patients were infants, and one was an 11-year-old girl with a history of extreme prematurity and bronchopulmonary dysplasia. All four presented with acute respiratory distress, hypoxemia, and cardiovascular compromise following a recent respiratory tract infection. PH was documented predominantly by echocardiography, with findings including elevated estimated pulmonary pressures, right ventricular (RV) pressure overload, interventricular septal flattening, and/or RV dysfunction.
