title: Update in Liver Transplant Anesthesia.
authorString: Rashid J, Arango D, Lindberg S.
abstractText: Liver transplant anesthesia continues to undergo evolution. This review article explores 6 key domains. Combined heart‒liver transplantation is expanding, driven by Fontan-associated liver disease. Vasoplegia management options have been expanded by hydroxocobalamin and angiotensin II. Machine perfusion has transformed organ preservation, enabling real-time viability assessment and safe utilization of marginal and donation after circulatory death grafts. Viscoelastic hemostatic assays now guide transfusion management, though natural anticoagulant pathways remain undetectable by current platforms. Finally, planned intraoperative renal replacement therapy in carefully selected high-risk patients improves metabolic stability and perioperative outcomes.

title: Preconception Folic Acid Supplementation Associated with Attenuated Effects of Air Pollution on Birthweight Outcomes.
authorString: Ge Y, Zhang Y, Liao J, Lin Y, Yang Z, Berhane K, Bai Z, Han B, Xu J, Gilliland F, Chen Z, Yan W, Huang G, Zhang JJ.
abstractText: Gestational exposure to ambient air pollution has been linked to adverse birth outcomes. Folic acid (FA) supplementation supports fetal development, but the optimal timing for protective effects remains uncertain. This study aims to determine whether maternal FA supplementation prior to conception modifies the association between gestational air pollution exposure and birthweight-related outcomes in a population where most women also took FA during pregnancy. We analyzed data from 10,579 mother-child pairs from a preconception cohort in Shanghai, China. Ambient concentrations of PM2.5, PM10, NO2, and ozone were estimated at a residential level using spatiotemporal models for the preconception period and each trimester. We assessed whether preconception FA supplementation modified the association between air pollution exposure and birth outcomes, including birthweight, birthweight Z-score, small-for-gestational age (SGA), and low birthweight (LBW). Linear and logistic regression models with interaction terms, as well as stratified analyses by FA supplementation status, were applied. Children's sex-specific associations were also explored. Significant interactions between preconception FA supplementation and air pollution exposures were observed for birthweight and SGA. A 10 μg/m3 increase in PM2.5 exposure during pregnancy was associated with a -62.8 g (95% CI: -97.0, -28.6) change in birthweight and a 1.78 (95% CI: 1.16, 2.73) odds ratio for SGA among women without preconception FA supplementation. No such significant associations were found among women receiving preconception FA supplementation, with an estimated change of -1.7 g in birthweight (95% CI: -65.7 to 62.4) and an odds ratio of 0.70 for SGA (95% CI: 0.32-1.44). The protective effect appeared more pronounced for male infants than females. Maternal preconception FA supplementation can attenuate the adverse effects of gestational air pollution exposure on birthweight and SGA risk in women who also received FA supplementation during pregnancy. These findings support the importance of incorporating preconception FA supplementation as a protective measure against gestational exposure to air pollution.

title: Preoperative, operative, and immediate postoperative predictors of the onset of low cardiac output syndrome in CHD.
authorString: Akbasli IT, Tandon A, Cassedy AE, Allan CK, Madugula N, Dickey S, Du S, Nemer G, Bora G, Das A, Norel R, Barra N, Najm H, Marino B, Latifi S, Baloglu O.
abstractText:
Background

Low cardiac output syndrome is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality after CHD surgery. Early, transparent risk estimation at paediatric cardiac ICU admission could guide monitoring and resource allocation.

Objectives

To develop and evaluate a multivariable model that estimates the risk of low cardiac output syndrome using routinely available preoperative, intraoperative, and immediate postoperative variables.

Methods

In this single-centre retrospective observational cohort, children ≤18 years undergoing CHD surgery between February 2023 and November 2024 were included. Low cardiac output syndrome was defined using prespecified criteria from the Paediatric Cardiac Critical Care Consortium. Candidate predictors were screened in univariate analyses; independent associations were estimated with multivariable logistic regression and backward elimination.

Results

Among 191 patients, 46 (24%) developed low cardiac output syndrome. Independent predictors were higher surgical complexity ([RACHS-1] ≥ 4; AOR 3.69, 95% confidence intervals 1.38–9.81), preoperative inotrope use (AOR 2.75, 1.02–7.43), longer cardiopulmonary bypass duration (AOR 1.01 per minute, 1.00–1.02), and a greater number of prior cardiac operations (AOR 2.00 per operation, 1.34–2.97); higher operative weight was protective (AOR 0.92 per kilogram, 0.87–0.97). Model performance metrics were AUROC 0.88 and AUPRC 0.71; at a prespecified decision threshold, accuracy 0.82, positive predictive value 0.66, sensitivity (recall) 0.50, F1 score 0.57, and negative predictive value 0.85.

Conclusions

A parsimonious, interpretable model derived from routinely collected data identifies children at increased risk of low cardiac output syndrome at ICU arrival and can inform early intervention and staffing. Prospective multicentre validation and dynamic updating with continuous postoperative physiology are warranted.

title: Left ventricular dysfunction and massive intracavitary thrombus in unrepaired tetralogy of Fallot with endomyocardial fibroelastosis: a case report.
authorString: Di Cosola R, Rovelli R, Severi E, Raimondi F.
abstractText: Left ventricular dysfunction and thrombosis in unrepaired tetralogy of Fallot are rarely reported. We report the case of a 9-year-old boy with unrepaired tetralogy of Fallot, severe biventricular dysfunction, large left ventricular thrombus, and diffuse subendocardial fibroelastosis. After surgical repair, recovery of ventricular function and thrombus resolution were observed. This case highlights the interplay between cyanosis, myocardial remodelling, and hypercoagulability and emphasises the role of multimodality imaging.

title: Echocardiographic description of pulmonary vein stenosis in a cat with atrioventricular septal defect.
authorString: Seyednejad F, Locquet L, Ardehali P, Astaraki N.
abstractText:
Case summary

A 2.5-year-old, intact female British Shorthair cat was referred for cardiology evaluation owing to intermittent panting and a heart murmur identified on cardiac auscultation before elective surgery. Physical examination revealed a left parasternal grade II/VI systolic murmur without arrhythmia. Thoracic radiographs showed cardiomegaly without pulmonary infiltration. The echocardiography was prompted by auscultation, history and radiological findings. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated marked right atrial enlargement and eccentric hypertrophy of the right ventricle. Echocardiography revealed a partial atrioventricular septal defect characterised by a large ostium primum defect (0.79 cm) and an anterior mitral valve cleft, resulting in a left-to-right shunt (estimated Qp:Qs ≈ 2.2). Doppler interrogation of the left pulmonary vein entering the lateral wall of the left atrium demonstrated focal turbulence and increased peak velocity (1.08 m/s), corresponding to a pressure gradient of approximately 4.7 mmHg, findings consistent with suspected unilateral pulmonary vein stenosis. Tricuspid regurgitation velocity (2.2 m/s) did not reflect increased afterload. Elective surgery was postponed owing to uncertainty regarding peri-anaesthetic haemodynamic risk. Medical treatment with enalapril and clopidogrel was initiated. At the 9-month follow-up, the cat remained clinically stable and echocardiographic findings were unchanged.

Relevance and novel information

Pulmonary vein stenosis is rarely reported in cats. This report describes the concurrent presence of partial atrioventricular septal defect and suspected unilateral pulmonary vein stenosis. These findings highlight the detection of a congenital heart defect in a young cat, despite the low-grade murmur.

title: Long-term outcomes in adults with repaired tetralogy of Fallot: a single-centre retrospective cohort.
authorString: Sanchez-Escobar IC, Ocampo-Aristizabal LA, Davila-Ruales A, Cañas-Arenas E, Zapata-Sanchez MM.
abstractText:
Background

Adults with repaired tetralogy of Fallot represent a growing clinical population at risk for long-term cardiovascular complications. Characterising their postoperative course and late outcomes is essential to guide surveillance and management.

Objectives

To describe the clinical characteristics and long-term outcomes of adult patients (≥18 years) with repaired tetralogy of Fallot who received care at a quaternary-care institution between January 2000 and December 2024.

Methods

We performed a retrospective cohort study. Adult patients with a diagnosis of repaired tetralogy of Fallot who had undergone complete surgical repair either during the study period or before it were included. Clinical and sociodemographic data were obtained.Variables related to prior palliative procedures, type of surgical repair, reinterventions (surgical or catheter-based), and long-term outcomes were analysed.

Results

A total of 56 patients were included; 31 (55.4%) were women. The median duration of follow-up after repair was 23 years; twenty patients (35.7%) had undergone a palliative or prior intervention before complete repair. The most common type of outflow tract reconstruction was a transannular patch (37.5%), followed by homograft implantation (25.0%). Reinterventions occurred in 29 patients (51.8%), most commonly pulmonary valve replacement (23 patients, 41.0%), mainly due to progressive pulmonary regurgitation and right ventricular dilation. Arrhythmic complications included premature ventricular contractions in 35.7% of patients. Long-term mortality was 3.6%.

Conclusions

Adults with repaired tetralogy of Fallot demonstrate high long-term survival; however, late complications are common and frequently require surgical or catheter-based reintervention. These findings underscore the need for lifelong specialised follow-up in adult CHD programmes.

title: Global conversations in adult congenital heart disease webinar series: a global health initiative to enhance education in adult congenital heart disease.
authorString: Bravo-Jaimes K, Sharma G, Guerrero-Chalela CE, Garcia E, Valdez-Ramos M, Hernandez J, Cornejo-Guerra JA, Mouratian M, McLeod CJ.
abstractText:
Background

Specialised knowledge in adult congenital heart disease is crucial but often lacking, particularly in resource-limited settings. The Global Conversations in Adult Congenital Heart Disease webinar series was initiated to provide accessible, global education via virtual platforms.

Objective

This study evaluates the attendance patterns, participant demographics, knowledge outcomes, and audience feedback of the Global Conversations in Adult Congenital Heart Disease webinar series, analysing 19 monthly sessions conducted from October 2023 to April 2025.

Methods

Registration data, session viewership, and total series reach were recorded. Demographics were collected per session. Pre- and post-session quizzes were used to assess changes in knowledge; scores from these independent groups were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test. Post-webinar surveys collected improvement suggestions.

Results

Out of 1,956 registrants from 89 countries, 54.6% attended the sessions, representing 1,068 participants from 64 nations: mainly Colombia (30.9%), Peru (18%), the USA (14.1%), and Mexico (9.9%). Median quiz scores improved from 50% pre-session (n = 120) to 100% post-session (n = 108), a statistically significant gain (p = 0.035). Notably, 29% had no prior adult congenital heart disease education. Most post-webinar survey respondents rated case presentations and discussions as excellent (75.0%) or good (20.1%). Qualitative feedback suggested areas for improvement included audiovisual quality, audience engagement, content delivery, and language accessibility.

Conclusion

The Global Conversations in Adult Congenital Heart Disease webinar series successfully engaged a diverse international audience and showed significant differences in quiz scores between pre- and post-session independent groups, demonstrating the potential benefit and feasibility of virtual education in bridging gaps in adult congenital heart disease training, particularly in resource-limited countries.

title: CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS OF INFLAMMATION IN STEATOTIC LIVER DISEASE: HETEROGENEITY OF NEUTROPHILS IN TISSUE INJURY AND HOST DEFENSE.
authorString: Szabo G, Babuta M, Ribeiro M.

journal.title: Transactions of the American Clinical and Climatological Association

abstractText: Steatotic liver disease is the most common form of liver disease induced by the metabolic syndrome, excessive alcohol use, or their combination. In progression of steatohepatitis to liver fibrosis, sustained inflammation and activation of innate immune cells plays a critical role. Neutrophils play a critical role in sustaining inflammation as well as in host defense. In this study, we identified neutrophil populations with activated or exhausted phenotypes in alcohol-associated steatohepatitis and discovered induction of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) by alcohol in the setting of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). Mechanistically, we describe how the NLRP3 inflammasome and NLRP3-IL-ß axis is a key component in sustained liver inflammation in MASH, alcohol-induced steatohepatitis, and their combined insult. Finally, using preclinical models, we demonstrate that targeting neutrophils, disruption of NETs, or NLRP3 inflammasome activation are promising directions for new therapeutic approaches in steatohepatitis. Abbreviations: MASH, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis; AH, alcohol-associated hepatitis; MASLD, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease; ALD, alcohol-associated liver disease; MetALD, metabolic syndrome and alcohol-associated liver disease; ASC, apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a caspase recruitment domain; NLRP3, nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain-like receptor family, pyrin domain containing 3; DAMPs, damage-associated molecular patterns; PAMPS, pathogen-associated molecular patterns; NETs, neutrophil extracellular traps.

title: [Usefulness of a Split-bolus Injection Protocol for Pediatric Cardiac CT in Congenital Heart Disease].
authorString: Ikeno Y, Morishita M.
abstractText:
Purpose

To propose a split-bolus contrast injection protocol for pediatric cardiac CT and to evaluate its usefulness by comparing it with the early phase protocol and systemic circulation protocol.

Methods

Thirty patients were included in each of the following three protocols: the early phase protocol; the systemic circulation protocol, in which contrast medium was injected slowly over a prolonged period and CT was performed after systemic circulation; and the split-bolus protocol. CT attenuation values were measured in the ascending aorta, descending aorta, pulmonary artery, pulmonary veins, and superior vena cava and compared among the three protocols. In addition, two radiologic technologists independently assessed vascular visualization using a four-point visual scoring system.

Results

CT attenuation values obtained with the split-bolus protocol showed no significant differences from those of the early phase protocol in the ascending aorta, descending aorta, pulmonary artery, or pulmonary veins (p=0.282, 0.174, 0.632, and 0.159, respectively), whereas significant differences were observed compared with the systemic circulation protocol (all p<0.001). In contrast, no significant difference in CT attenuation of the superior vena cava was observed between the split-bolus protocol and the systemic circulation protocol (p=0.923). In the visual evaluation, the split-bolus protocol achieved a median score of 4 for all evaluated vessels across all cases.

Conclusion

The split-bolus protocol may enable visualization of the superior vena cava while maintaining contrast enhancement of the aorta, pulmonary artery, and pulmonary veins, suggesting that it may be a useful contrast injection protocol for pediatric cardiac CT.

title: The miR-511-3p/ATP2A2 Axis Is Required for Propofol-Mediated Cardioprotection Against Hypoxia/Reoxygenation Injury.
authorString: Sun Y, Jiang R, Zhu B, Liu X, Li Q, Huang Y, Liu S.
abstractText:
Background

Propofol (PPF) alleviates myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury (MIRI), yet no existing studies have clarified the function of microRNA-511-3p (miR-511-3p) in cardiac injury or its link to PPF's cardioprotection.

Purpose

This study clarified how the miR-511-3p/ATPase sarcoplasmic/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ transporting 2 (ATP2A2) signaling cascade mediated PPF-induced relief against hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R) cardiac damage.

Methods

H/R damage models were established in H9c2 cells. Cell viability was measured via the CCK-8 assay, and flow cytometry was used to quantify the proportion of apoptotic cells. Cellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels were assessed using the DCFH-DA fluorescent staining method. ELISA and colorimetric tests were combined to measure cardiac injury markers, inflammatory mediators, and oxidative stress-related molecules. RT-qPCR was applied to test the expression levels of miR-511-3p and ATP2A2. Dual-luciferase reporter assays were carried out to confirm the direct binding interaction between the two molecules.

Results

PPF markedly boosted the viability and restrained apoptosis of H9c2 cells subjected to H/R treatment. It also reduced the release of cardiac injury markers and eased excessive oxidative stress and inflammatory responses. H/R exposure raised miR-511-3p abundance, an alteration that PPF treatment could reverse. Forced miR-511-3p expression partially abolished the cardioprotective benefits brought by PPF. ATP2A2 was verified as a direct target of miR-511-3p, whose expression was suppressed by this miRNA. Upregulating ATP2A2 counteracted cell damage triggered by miR-511-3p overexpression.

Conclusions

PPF might mitigate H/R-triggered cardiomyocyte damage, possibly through inhibiting miR-511-3p and increasing its target ATP2A2, and this molecular axis may offer a tentative therapeutic reference for MIRI.

title: Long-Term Changes in Patient-Reported Outcome Measures in People With Multiple Sclerosis 55 Years and Older: Analysis From the New York State Multiple Sclerosis Consortium.
authorString: Jakimovski D, Kavak KS, Coyle PK, Goodman AD, Gottesman MH, Weinstock-Guttman B, Multiple Sclerosis Consortium NYS.
abstractText:
Background

Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) are increasingly utilized in observational and regulated studies of people with multiple sclerosis (MS). However, the impact of aging on PROMs for people with MS remains largely unknown. This study explores the cross-sectional characteristics and longitudinal trajectories of PROMs to determine their ability to predict clinical progression in a large group of people with MS 55 years and older.

Methods

Included in the analysis were people with MS enrolled in the New York State Multiple Sclerosis Consortium (NYSMSC), 55 years or older, with at least 3 clinical visits recorded in the consortium database. All people in the NYSMSC complete PROMs through the LIFEware questionnaire. Additional clinical measures were also collected. The percentage of people with MS who reported severe limitations within each of the LIFEware domains was compared at their baseline visit (≥ 55 years) and at the most recent follow-up visit (average follow-up of 8.3 years). Comparisons between people with MS with stable or increasing disability were also performed.

Results

Of 658 eligible people in the NYSMSC (mean age at most recent follow-up, 66.6 years), a greater percentage reported decreased ability since baseline in all physical PROMs domains (getting up from sofa, 38.4% to 48.8%, P < .001; standing for more than 30 minutes, 59.3% vs 66.9%, P < .001; and functional limitations in all extremities, P < .007). Contrarily, the group reported improvement in multiple psychosocial domains, including pessimism (P < .001), feeling tense (P < .001), feeling annoyed (P = .02), or having morbid thoughts (P = .018). People with increasing disability had significantly worse baseline physical PROMs when compared with people with stable MS.

Conclusions

An increase in physical limitations does not necessarily contribute to a rise in psychosocial limitations. Instead, as people with MS age, they tend to report improvements in their mental health over time. PROMs can be a complementary predictive indicator of future disease progression as individuals with MS age.

title: Three-dimensional regional evaluation of right ventricular myocardial work from cine computed tomography, a pilot study

title: Slowly Conducting Anatomic Isthmuses of Tetralogy of Fallot: An Opportunity for “Prophylactic” VT Ablation

title: Forgotten interventions to promote relational health to prevent child maltreatment.
authorString: Li Q, Palusci VJ, Krugman RD.
abstractText: Harsh parenting and intimate partner violence increased during the pandemic. However, pediatrician-led evidence-based models that link primary care, home visiting, and child maltreatment prevention have been neglected, despite C. Henry Kempe's successful programs from 1971 to 1973. The Kempe randomized trial included comprehensive pediatric follow-up by a single physician and a lay health visitor whenever indicated, and/or weekly visits by a public health nurse in the home 50 years ago. The interventions responded to abnormal parenting practices and early warning signs during pregnancy, labor and delivery, and postnatally and reduced the hospitalization for serious injuries among those 2 years old. The Kempe trial was not cited in many publications but only 402 times in Google Scholar in October 2023. Kempe's call for promoting emotional health and parent bonding 40 years ago was echoed in the American Academy of Pediatrics' Bright Futures and Policy Statements on Promoting Relational Health in 2021. Relational health is a strengths-based approach, which can promote safe, stable, and nurturing relationships, buffer adversity, and build resilience. Screening for relational health should be integrated into Obstetric and Pediatric Care, and home visitation should become linked to primary care as a basic health benefit. Pediatric care must be transformed based on the evidence in the Kempe trial, focus on promoting primary prevention and trusted relationships from pregnancy on, and engage community resources to address unmet social needs, enabling integrated behavioral health, and changing financial incentives that now prioritize procedures and crisis interventions over cognitive services and prevention. The education and training of future pediatricians needs to emphasize the importance of relational health in the family, and the moment is now to collaborate and implement these forgotten interventions.

title: A protective human antibody against respiratory syncytial virus by targeting a prefusion epitope across sites IV and V of the viral fusion glycoprotein.
authorString: Dai L, Song J, Xu L, Gao Z, Xu S, Chai Y, Wang L, Yang M, Ma T, Wang Q, Cao S, Yie J, Zou G, Xie Z, Wu JZ, Gao GF.
abstractText: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is one of the leading pathogens that cause lower respiratory tract infections in infants and the elderly. Passive immunoprophylaxis with monoclonal antibody (mAb) has been approved to prevent morbidity and mortality from RSV infection in infants. Here we report the isolation of two neutralizing mAbs against RSV from convalescent children by prefusion form of fusion (F) glycoprotein as bait. One mAb RV11 exhibited good potency in neutralization of RSV strains from both A and B subtypes in cell-based assay, and protected mice from RSV infection in vivo. An RV11 escape mutant was identified, which contains an S443P mutation in F protein. Crystal structure showed the RV11 bound to a conserved prefusion epitope across the antigenic sites IV and V of the F glycoprotein. RV11 showed a strong synergistic effect when combined with two RSV antivirals, an F-targeting small molecular inhibitor ziresovir and a site Ø neutralizing mAb D25 (the parental mAb for nirsevimab). The study extended our knowledge to the neutralizing and protective epitopes of RSV, and the mAb RV11 deserves further development for clinical translation.

title: Fetal ascites and congenital heart disease
Automated Cerebrospinal Fluid Flow Quantification in Hydrocephalus Using Phase-Contrast Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
authorString: Rodríguez Martínez EA, Liu P, Owashi K, Gayet A, Balédent O.
abstractText: Quantitative cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) flow analysis with phase-contrast magnetic resonance imaging depends on segmentation and is affected by operator variability. This cohort method-comparison study evaluated whether a flow-aware deep learning (DL) model provides reproducible C2-C3 CSF segmentation and flow quantification compared with repeated manual segmentation. Ten hydrocephalus patients underwent 3-T phase-contrast magnetic resonance imaging at C2-C3, with 32 magnitude and phase frames across the cardiac cycle. Three experts and one novice segmented each case twice using semi-automatic software, generating 80 manual annotations. A pretrained flow-aware 2D-UNet generated one fixed automatic segmentation per case. The inference pipeline was deterministic, meaning that repeated processing of the same input with fixed model weights and settings produced identical masks. A multi-expert reference was defined as the arithmetic mean of the expert measurements. Region of interest (ROI) surface area, peak flow amplitude, and stroke volume were compared using mean difference, Bland-Altman 95% limits of agreement, Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (CCC), and intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Expert ICC(1,1) was 0.88-0.97 for surface area, 0.97-1.00 for peak flow amplitude, and 0.97-0.99 for stroke volume; novice values were 0.63, 0.95, and 0.92, respectively. Compared with the multi-expert reference, model mean differences were -0.42 mm<sup>2</sup> for surface area, -0.00 mL/s for peak flow amplitude, and -0.01 mL for stroke volume, with CCC values of 0.50, 0.87, and 0.86. Bland-Altman limits of agreement were -69.12 to 68.27 mm<sup>2</sup>, -1.47 to 1.46 mL/s, and -0.34 to 0.31 mL. The model provided rapid, deterministic CSF segmentation with small cohort-level mean differences in peak flow amplitude and stroke volume; however, individual-level agreement with the flow-derived multi-expert reference was lower than for expert and novice segmentations obtained using the semi-automatic workflow.

title: Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery versus Thoracotomy in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Survival Analysis and Exploratory Predictive Modelling.
authorString: Makarov V, Baimukhametov E, Yessentayeva S, Oljaev S, Arybzhanov D.
abstractText:
Background

This study retrospectively compared outcomes of minimally invasive and open surgical approaches for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in a cohort of 255 patients operated on between 2014 and 2018. A machine-learning analysis was performed as an exploratory, hypothesis-generating component.

Method

Survival was analysed by disease stage using Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank tests. Because the groups were not randomised and were imbalanced at baseline, comparisons are unadjusted and should be interpreted as associations. Exploratory predictive models were developed using five machine-learning algorithms (random forest performing best), with feature contributions interpreted using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP). Missing values were handled by multiple imputation, continuous variables were standardised, and correlated features were excluded.

Results

Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) was used more frequently for adenocarcinoma, in women, and at stage I, with zero postoperative mortality (0% versus 5.8% for thoracotomy). At stage I, there were no differences in median overall survival (65.3 versus 67.7 months; p=0.768); at stage II, VATS was associated with longer survival (75.8 versus 48.8 months; p=0.003); at stage III, a similar direction did not reach significance. Recurrent predictors in the exploratory models were coronary artery disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, intervention volume, tumour histology, and vascular invasion; however, test accuracy remained low (0.39-0.48), precluding clinical use. SHAP analysis highlighted resection completeness, lack of conversion, and tumour morphology.

Conclusions

In this unadjusted retrospective cohort, VATS was associated with lower perioperative mortality, and at stage II with longer overall survival. Given the retrospective design and baseline imbalances, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective, adjusted studies before informing surgical indications.

title: Myocardial remodelling during sacubitril/valsartan therapy in patients with chronic heart failure.
authorString: Tabukashvili D, Kapetivadze V, Lazashvili T, Maglaperidze Z.
abstractText:
Abstract

The aim of the study was to identify differences between aliskiren and sacubitril/valsartan in their ability to influence cardiac remodelling, metabolic balance, neurohumoral activation, and clinical symptom severity. A comparative assessment of the clinical effectiveness and impact on the structural and functional state of the myocardium was conducted for two therapeutic strategies in patients with chronic heart failure in Georgia over a 12-month follow-up. The results demonstrated fundamentally different trajectories of therapeutic response. In the sacubitril/valsartan group, early clinical improvement was observed by 6 months, including significant reductions in systolic blood pressure (-6.2%, p<0.001), respiratory rate (-4.5%, p<0.001), and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels (-10.0%, p<0.05), along with improved oxygen saturation (+3.5%, p<0.001). Left ventricular ejection fraction increased significantly already at 6 months (from 34.2±4.7% to 37.4±4.0%, p<0.001) and further at 12 months (40.5±3.5%, p<0.001), accompanied by rapid improvement in New York Heart Association functional class, with 9.3% of patients achieving New York Heart Association I by study end. In contrast, the aliskiren group exhibited slower but more pronounced structural reverse remodelling. Significant reductions in left ventricular end-systolic volume (-15.8%, p=0.009), end-diastolic volume (-17.6%, p=0.016), and end-systolic diameter (p=0.002) were observed only at 12 months, along with a modest but significant increase in ejection fraction (p=0.030). Regression of functional mitral and tricuspid regurgitation and a significant decrease in pulmonary artery systolic pressure (-19.7%, p<0.05) were more prominent in this group. Both therapies led to significant improvements in carbohydrate and lipid metabolism, including reductions in glycated haemoglobin, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and triglycerides (p<0.05 for all), indicating a favourable systemic metabolic effect. Overall, findings suggest that sacubitril/valsartan may be preferable when rapid clinical stabilization is required, whereas aliskiren may represent an effective therapeutic option for patients with advanced structural cardiac remodelling.

title: Four weeks of isometric handgrip training results in lower awake ambulatory blood pressure compared with control: a randomized clinical trial.
authorString: Oliveira PC, Waclawovsky G, Lehnen AM.
abstractText: We compared the effects of upper-limb (handgrip) and lower-limb (knee extension) isometric training on ambulatory blood pressure in individuals with controlled hypertension. In this randomized controlled trial, 67 adults receiving antihypertensive medication were allocated to a control group (CG, n = 22), small muscle mass isometric training (SMM, handgrip; n = 22), or large muscle mass isometric training (LMM, knee extension; n = 23). Participants completed 12 supervised sessions over 4 weeks, with the exercise protocols performed at 30% of upper-limb MVC or lower-limb maximal isometric load, respectively. Ambulatory blood pressure outcomes were compared using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), adjusting for the corresponding baseline office blood pressure. Hourly 24-h profiles were analyzed using generalized estimating equations with Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc tests. Significant between-group differences were observed only for awake ambulatory blood pressure. Compared with CG, SMM showed lower awake systolic blood pressure (121.8 ± 3.1 vs. 124.2 ± 2.6 mmHg; p = 0.017) and awake diastolic blood pressure (76.3 ± 3.6 vs. 80.8 ± 4.2 mmHg; p = 0.009). No significant differences were observed between LMM and CG, between the two exercise groups, or for 24-h and sleep blood pressure. These findings indicate that, after 4 weeks of supervised isometric training, modest between-group differences in awake ambulatory blood pressure were observed only for handgrip training compared with the control group. Greater muscle mass recruitment did not result in superior antihypertensive effects, suggesting that the chronic blood pressure response to isometric exercise is not determined solely by the amount of muscle mass involved. Trial registration: "ClinicalTrials.gov," "NCT07147595."

title: Albuminuria as a Clinical Marker of Subclinical Myocardial Dysfunction in Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
authorString: Elsheikh E.
abstractText:
Background

Subclinical myocardial dysfunction is common in diabetes and may precede clinically overt heart failure by several years. Albuminuria reflects systemic microvascular injury, but its relationship with the severity of myocardial dysfunction in patients with diabetes remains uncertain.

Objective

To determine whether adults with diabetes and albuminuria have greater echocardiographic evidence of subclinical myocardial dysfunction than those with diabetes and normoalbuminuria.

Methods

Four electronic databases were searched from inception to March 2026 for observational studies comparing adults with diabetes and albuminuria with those with normoalbuminuria. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Random-effects models were used to pool mean differences in global longitudinal strain (GLS), E/e', left ventricular mass index, e', and ejection fraction. Adjusted regression coefficients and odds ratios were also synthesized, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE.

Results

Eighteen reports representing 17 independent cohorts were included, with eight contributing to quantitative synthesis. Absolute GLS was significantly lower in patients with albuminuria (MD, -1.38 percentage points; 95% CI, -2.13 to -0.63; P < 0.001; I² = 82%). A greater strain deficit was observed from microalbuminuria to macroalbuminuria, although formal trend analysis was not possible. E/e' was higher in albuminuric patients (MD, 1.21; 95% CI, 0.18-2.24; P = 0.021), whereas ejection fraction did not differ. Albuminuria remained independently associated with impaired strain (pooled β = 1.06; 95% CI, 0.44-1.68) and higher odds of subclinical dysfunction (OR = 5.55; 95% CI, 3.43-8.98).

Conclusions

Albuminuria identifies patients with diabetes who have greater subclinical systolic and diastolic myocardial impairment despite preserved ejection fraction. Urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio may help identify asymptomatic patients who could benefit from deformation imaging, although prospective validation is required.

title: Acute-phase HOMA2-IR and in-hospital cardiovascular complications in patients with acute coronary syndrome without known diabetes.
authorString: Ngoc Minh Thu N, The Dung B, Vinh Nien L, Vu HV, Hoang Vu V, Chi Thanh N.
abstractText:
Background

Insulin resistance measured during acute coronary syndrome (ACS) may reflect pre-existing metabolic vulnerability as well as the response to acute illness. We examined its association with cardiovascular complications arising during the index hospitalization in patients with ACS and no known diabetes.

Methods

In this single-center prospective cohort, 252 patients with ACS and an admission HbA1c <6.5% had fasting glucose and insulin measured 24-48 hours after admission. Insulin resistance was defined by a HOMA2-IR threshold of ≥1.35 prespecified from independent healthy controls. The composite MACE outcome comprised five prespecified complications occurring between sampling and discharge or death. Logistic and modified Poisson regression were adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, smoking, and hypertension.

Results

Insulin resistance was present in 137 patients (54.4%), and the composite MACE occurred in 57 (22.6%): 28.5% with versus 15.7% without insulin resistance; risk difference 12.8 percentage points (95% CI 2.5-22.6). Insulin resistance was associated with the composite (adjusted OR 3.08, 95% CI 1.55-6.14; adjusted RR 2.29, 95% CI 1.39-3.75); each doubling of HOMA2-IR was associated with higher odds (adjusted OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.09-1.99). The association persisted after GRACE adjustment (adjusted OR 2.83, 95% CI 1.32-6.06) and was attenuated after adding left ventricular ejection fraction, a possible mediator (adjusted OR 2.25, 95% CI 0.97-5.22). Acute heart failure, cardiogenic shock, or pulmonary edema accounted for 53 of the 57 events.

Conclusions

Acute-phase HOMA2-IR-defined insulin resistance was associated with cardiovascular complications during the index hospitalization, mainly heart-failure-related events. These findings are associational and require confirmation in multicenter cohorts.

title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease phenotypes and 1-year cardiovascular outcomes in patients with obstructive coronary artery disease: a prospective cohort study.
authorString: Vu H, Khanh Tuong TT, Dung HT.
abstractText:
Background

The prognostic significance of lean metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) in patients with obstructive coronary artery disease remains uncertain. We evaluated 1-year cardiovascular outcomes in lean versus non-lean MAFLD.

Methods

This prospective observational cohort study included 193 adults with MAFLD and coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-defined obstructive coronary artery disease at Thong Nhat Hospital, Vietnam. Lean MAFLD was defined as a body mass index <23 kg/m² and non-lean MAFLD as a body mass index ≥23 kg/m². The primary outcome was the first expanded major adverse cardiovascular event (eMACE) within 365 days, including ischemia-driven coronary revascularization. Planned first percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) after baseline CCTA was included. Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed.

Results

During follow-up, 115 patients (59.6%) experienced eMACE. The eMACE rate was higher in lean than in non-lean MAFLD (86.2% vs 54.9%, P=0.002). Among these cases, recorded components were revascularization (108), myocardial infarction (13), unstable angina (26), acute heart failure (1), stroke (0), and cardiovascular death (0); components overlapped. These counts do not establish first-event attribution. Lean MAFLD remained associated with eMACE after adjustment for age, sex, and multivessel coronary artery disease (adjusted HR 2.07, 95% CI 1.32-3.26, P=0.002).

Conclusions

Among patients with MAFLD and obstructive coronary artery disease, lean MAFLD was associated with a higher 1-year hazard of eMACE than non-lean MAFLD, after adjustment for age, sex, and multivessel coronary disease. The small lean group and inclusion of planned revascularization limit extrapolation to non-revascularization events, confirmation in larger cohorts is needed.

title: A Systematic Approach to Nontraumatic Falls: Integrating Tilt Table Testing and Amnesia Screening in Clinical Practice.
authorString: Maneesh RK, Haroon H, Raghav A, Rao M, Chakrapani M.
abstractText:
Background

Nontraumatic falls in older adults pose a significant public health issue. Syncope, a temporary loss of consciousness due to global cerebral hypoperfusion, is a frequent and often underrecognized cause of falls. Early identification of syncope is vital for effective management and fall prevention.

Aim of the study

This study aimed to assess the prevalence of syncope as a cause of nontraumatic falls in individuals over fifty years of age, characterize their clinical profiles, and evaluate the effectiveness of the Tilt Table Test (TTT) in diagnosis.

Materials and methods

This observational study was conducted in patients over 50 years of age presenting with nontraumatic falls. Those with recent transient ischaemic attack/stroke, significant carotid stenosis, severe cardiac conditions, or inability to comply with instructions were excluded. Data collection involved a proforma covering demographics, fall characteristics, and diagnostic evaluations, including TTT and carotid sinus massage (CSM), following ESC 2018 guidelines. Statistical analysis was performed via SPSS (version 29).

Results

Sixty-five participants were included, with a mean age of 68.34 ± 10.95 years; 63.1% were male. Intrinsic factors were responsible for falls in 72.3% of cases. TTT results indicated 32.7% positive results for syncope. A significant association was noted between syncope and amnesia (p=0.015).

Conclusion

Syncope is an overlooked cause of nontraumatic falls in elderly individuals. The TTT proved valuable in diagnosing syncope-related falls. The strong association between amnesia and syncope in our study emphasizes the need for detailed evaluation to improve outcomes and reduce the incidence of recurrent falls.

title: Levels of Physical Activity and Ischemic Heart Disease Risk Among Adult Hospital Attendees in Mangalore. A cross-sectional study.
authorString: Mallya A, Dsouza SR, Hrishikesh A, Shetty SS, Divakar A, Veerappa S, Prashanth P, Rv S, Babburi SH.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain a leading cause of mortality globally, with physical inactivity identified as a major modifiable risk factor. There is limited data from Indian settings assessing physical activity using standardized tools and its association with ischemic heart disease (IHD) risk.

Aim

This study aimed to assess physical activity levels and examine their association with 10-year IHD risk among adults in Mangalore.

Materials and methods

A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 101 patient bystanders aged 40-74 years at Government Wenlock Hospital, Mangalore. Physical activity was assessed using the Global Physical Activity Questionnaire (GPAQ), and metabolic equivalents (MET-min/week) were calculated. Participants were categorized based on WHO recommendations (≥600 MET-min/week). The 10-year IHD risk was estimated using WHO/ISH non-laboratory-based risk charts. Data were analyzed using Jamovi, and associations were tested using the Chi-square test with p<0.05 considered significant.

Results

The mean age of participants was 48.9±7.1 years, with 58.4% males. A majority (93.1%) met WHO physical activity recommendations, with a mean activity level of 5803±2964 MET-min/week. Most participants (67.3%) had a low IHD risk (<5%), while 24.8% and 7.9% had moderate (5-<10%) and high (10-<20%) risk, respectively. A statistically significant inverse association was observed between physical activity and IHD risk (χ²=13.22, p=0.001). Among those meeting activity recommendations, 71.3% had low IHD risk, compared to only 14.3% among those not meeting recommendations.

Conclusions

Adequate physical activity is strongly associated with lower IHD risk. Promoting active lifestyles and integrating routine risk assessment using standardized tools can play a crucial role in reducing cardiovascular disease burden in similar populations.

title: Outcomes of a Multidisciplinary Endovascular Aortic Program at the Vietnam National Heart Institute: A Single-Center Observational Study of TEVAR, EVAR, and Registry Data.
authorString: Tuan PM, Hieu TB, Trong DP, Thien LN, Cam TN, Hoa NV, Hoai NTT.
abstractText:
Background

Multidisciplinary aortic programs integrate advanced imaging, standardized clinical pathways, procedural expertise, and longitudinal surveillance. We evaluated the evolution and outcomes of endovascular aortic care at Vietnam National Heart Institute (VNHI), Bach Mai Hospital, using institutional TEVAR and EVAR cohorts and the prospective VNHI Aortic Registry through June 2026.

Methods

Single-center observational report drawing on two historical institutional endovascular cohorts (TEVAR from January 2014 to December 2020, n=102; EVAR from January 2019 to August 2025, n=235) and a prospectively maintained registry (January-June 2026, n=96) in the VNHI Aortic Registry, Bach Mai hospital. Cohorts were summarized separately because enrollment periods, disease profiles, and follow-up differed. Outcomes were analyzed within each source cohort. Prespecified outcomes included technical success, perioperative mortality, major procedure-related complications, aortic remodeling, secondary reintervention, and mid-term survival.

Results

Technical success was 100/102 (98.0%) TEVAR and 235/235 (100%) EVAR cases. In-hospital mortality was 3/102 (2.9%) in the dedicated TEVAR cohort; 30-day mortality was 2/235 (0.9%) in the EVAR cohort. Spinal cord ischemia occurred after TEVAR in 5/102 (4.9%) patients; all affected patients recovered before discharge following a standardized rescue protocol. Thoracic aortic coverage ≥ 270 mm was independently associated with spinal cord ischemia (odds ratio, 10.11; 95% confidence interval, 1.41-72.55; P=0.021). In the historical TEVAR source, complete false-lumen thrombosis in the covered thoracic segment was reported in 87.1% at 12 months; the imaging denominator remains to be confirmed. Estimates of long-term survival and regression-derived associations are withheld from this abstract pending verification of follow-up dates, numbers at risk, and model specifications. The 2026 registry contains 96 recorded entries but is not treated as an additional independent patient cohort until overlap is assessed. Four-year cumulative survival was 87.9% TEVAR and 84.6% EVAR; secondary reintervention occurred in 3.9% and 4.3%, respectively.

Conclusions

A structured multidisciplinary endovascular aortic program at VNHI was associated with high technical success and favorable mid-term outcomes in selected patients undergoing TEVAR or EVAR. These findings support the feasibility of organized aortic care in an emerging healthcare system; however, prospective risk-adjusted evaluation is required to determine the independent effect of the program on clinical outcomes. Complete patient-level reconciliation and standardized longitudinal surveillance are necessary for robust benchmarking.

title: Theranekron Attenuates Inflammation, Oxidative Stress Index, and Apoptosis in Lipopolysaccharide-Induced Cardiovascular Toxicity: Association With Hypoxia-Inducible Factor-1 Alpha-Related Gene Expression.
authorString: Savran M, Asci H, Imeci O, Oguzlar FC, Ozmen O.

journal.title: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

abstractText: This study aimed to evaluate the possible protective effects of Theranekron, an extract derived from Tarantula cubensis venom, on cardiovascular damage induced by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) in an experimental rat model. A total of 32 male Wistar Albino rats were randomly divided into 4 groups: Control, Lipopolysaccharide, Lipopolysaccharide plus Theranekron, and Theranekron alone. Lipopolysaccharide administration caused pronounced histopathological changes in the heart and aorta, including endothelial sloughing, hyperemia, hemorrhage, and infiltration of inflammatory cells. These pathological findings were accompanied by elevated oxidative stress markers, increased tumor necrosis factor-alpha and inducible nitric oxide synthase immunoreactivity, and increased caspase-3 immunoreactivity. Additionally, genes associated with the hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha (HIF-1α) pathway-such as interleukin 6, signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3), and vascular endothelial growth factor-were significantly upregulated in the lipopolysaccharide group. Theranekron pretreatment was associated with partial attenuation of oxidative stress imbalance, of inflammatory and apoptotic immunoreactivity, and of the upregulation of HIF-1α-related transcripts. Overall, these findings suggest that Theranekron may offer partial protection against early LPS-induced cardiovascular injury.

title: Genetic Insights Into Cardiomyopathy With Restrictive Phenotype: Implications for Diagnosis and Personalized Care.
authorString: Zhou N, Sun Y, Wei X, Liang W, Meng F, Ge Z, Sun M, Cui X, Zhang S, Pan C, Ge J, Shu X.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiomyopathy with a restrictive phenotype is uncommon, genetically heterogeneous, and difficult to distinguish from advanced hypertrophic or dilated cardiomyopathy. We aimed primarily to determine the diagnostic yield and spectrum of pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants among patients with an echocardiographically defined restrictive phenotype; genotype-imaging and survival comparisons were prespecified exploratory analyses.

Methods

We screened 568 patients with cardiomyopathy who underwent whole-exome sequencing and comprehensive echocardiography. Thirty-three met the operational definition of restrictive phenotype. Variants were classified. Genotype-imaging associations and survival were analyzed exploratorily.

Results

Among the 568 patients, 33 exhibited a restrictive phenotype: 7 had restrictive cardiomyopathy (RCM), 20 had hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with a restrictive phenotype (HRCM), and 6 had dilated cardiomyopathy with a restrictive phenotype (HDRCM). Variant carriers had a smaller aortic sinus diameter. In addition, MYBPC3 variant carriers had greater ventricular wall thickness and more frequent septal hypertrophy. Both the HRCM and HDRCM groups showed hypertrophic features, with interventricular septal hypertrophy occurring more frequently in the HDRCM group. The estimated 5-year survival was 54.5%, and survival did not differ significantly according to genetic-variant status.

Conclusions

Pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were frequent in this single-center cohort with restrictive physiology and were associated with selected imaging features. These exploratory findings support integrated genetic and echocardiographic evaluation.

title: The impact of periodontitis in cardiac autonomic dysfunction by hrv analysis.
authorString: Vineetha S, Saravanan A, Jeyabanu M, KalyaniPraba P, Rohini P, Thamarai Selvi K.
abstractText:
Introduction

Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease damaging the supportive structure of teeth. It has systemic impacts including cardiac autonomic dysfunction. Heart Rate Variability (HRV) measures an objective analysis of the extent of autonomic regulation and where decreased parasympathetic activity coupled with increased sympathetic predominance was determined to correlate well with risk in cardiovascular events. This research ascertains periodontitis and its correlation to autonomic dysfunction by HRV analysis.

Methodology

In total, 54 periodontitis patients were involved in the study, categorized under four groups, namely Gingivitis (n=14), Mild Periodontitis (n=13), Moderate Periodontitis (n=13), and Severe Periodontitis (n=14). Kubios HRV software version 3.5 was used for the analysis of time-domain and frequency-domain parameters of lead II ECG for HRV analysis. The indices of SNS and PNS were calculated for the assessment of autonomic balance. The correlation between the HRV parameters with the severity of periodontal disease was performed statistically.

Results

The SNS index was higher in the periodontitis groups than in the gingivitis group (Gingivitis: 1.09 ± 0.60; Mild: 4.25 ± 2.4; Moderate: 3.82 ± 2.2; Severe: 4.45 ± 1.5; p < 0.001), although the pattern was not strictly progressive.

Conclusion

Differences in autonomic regulation, including higher SNS index and lower PNS index values, were associated with periodontal disease categories. These findings should be interpreted cautiously because the study lacked a healthy control group and was cross-sectional.

title: Frequency and Risk Factors of Cancer Therapy-Related Cardiac Dysfunction in Patients Receiving Chemotherapy: A Prospective Cohort Study at a Tertiary Centre.
authorString: Ly VC, Tran HC, Nguyen TT, Hoang VS.
abstractText:
Background

Cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) is an increasingly recognised consequence of contemporary oncological treatment. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is insensitive to subclinical myocardial injury, and locally validated thresholds for global longitudinal strain (GLS) are lacking in Vietnamese patients.

Objectives

To determine the frequency and risk factors of CTRCD in patients receiving chemotherapy, and to validate a localised GLS threshold and a biomarker-based surveillance strategy for early detection.

Methods

We conducted a prospective cohort study of 235 patients at Cho Ray Hospital (September 2023-December 2025). Patients were assessed at baseline and every three months with two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography (GLS), high-sensitivity troponin T (hs-TnT) and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP). CTRCD was defined by international consensus criteria. Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis; as the outcome was common, associations were quantified as risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) estimated by modified Poisson regression.

Results

CTRCD occurred in 82 patients (34.9%). Incidence was highest with anthracyclines (41.2%) and HER2-targeted therapy (37.2%). A relative GLS reduction ≥12.1% predicted CTRCD with 73% sensitivity and 83% specificity. hs-TnT achieved a 100% negative predictive value (NPV), and combining GLS with hs-TnT in parallel retained a 100% NPV. Hypertension (RR 2.50, 95% CI 1.78-3.50), coronary artery disease (RR 2.47, 95% CI 1.82-3.35) and dyslipidaemia (RR 2.10, 95% CI 1.49-2.97) were associated with CTRCD. HFA-ICOS stratification was strongly predictive, with a stepwise increase in risk up to the very-high-risk category (RR 18.6, 95% CI 7.94-43.6 versus low risk; 100% event rate).

Conclusions

CTRCD affected one-third of patients. A locally validated GLS threshold combined with hs-TnT enables early, resource-efficient detection, supporting a shift from reactive to proactive cardiac surveillance.

title: Metachronous and Sporadic Bilateral Carotid Body Paraganglioma.
authorString: Facchini V, Iachini I, Belli E.
abstractText:
Purpose

The Authors' goal is to highlight the importance of early diagnosis and management of metachronous carotid body paraganglioma (CBP), analysing and discussing the main features of this rare tumor.

Methods

This study review the literature on a very particular topic, reporting the case of a patient with the rare evidence of a metachronous CBP in the left side of the neck, which onset and was surgically treated 26 years after the first contralateral presentation.

Results

After excision, the diagnosis of CBP was confirmed by histological and immunohistochemical examination of the surgical specimen. Transient dysphonia and dysphagia were observed after surgery, both recovered after 1 years. No cardiac anomalies were detected.

Conclusion

Paragangliomas are rare neuroendocrine neoplasms with an incidence of 2-8 X 1,000,000. Paragangliomas of the head and neck (HNP) originate mainly from the carotid body (60%) and in a few cases from the jugular bulb, the medial promontory of the middle ear (30%), the vagal nerve and the nodose ganglion (5-10 %). Bilateral CBP represents an extremely rare entity, accounting for approximately 5% of patients with CBP. Diagnostic imaging of CBP includes ultrasound, Computed Tomography (CT), Magnetic Resonance Images (MRI) and Angiography. The treatment of choice for CBP is its complete surgical removal. Early detection of symptoms referable to a new CBP is very important, because of the possibility, even after many years, of contralateral presentation of the same tumor. This, if operated at an early stage, decrease the risk of neurovascular complications.

title: Endohepatology in the Management of Portal Hypertension in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
authorString: Praktiknjo M, Wiest R, Cardenas A, Trebicka J, Laleman W.

journal.title: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

abstractText: Portal hypertension is the principal driver of decompensation in advanced chronic liver disease, yet in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) it deviates from the classical sinusoidal paradigm. Growing evidence points to a mixed sinusoidal-presinusoidal phenotype in which the hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) may underestimate true portal pressure, and in which decompensation and varices can occur at lower HVPG values than in viral cirrhosis. This biology is compounded by a diagnostic gap: non-invasive tests such as liver stiffness by vibration-controlled transient elastography, FIB-4, ANTICIPATE-NASH, spleen stiffness and the NICER model, are degraded by obesity through technical limitations and altered diagnostic thresholds, even when test discrimination is preserved. Moreover, no non-invasive rule-in for clinically significant portal hypertension reaches a 90% positive predictive value in obese MASLD, leaving a clinically meaningful grey zone. Endohepatology addresses these diagnostic limitations by providing complementary hemodynamic, elastographic, and histological information. Within a single sedated session, EUS-guided shear-wave elastography and EUS-guided liver biopsy can adjudicate F2-F3 fibrosis when treatment eligibility is uncertain; EUS-guided portal pressure gradient measurement can provide a direct gradient when HVPG or non-invasive tests are discordant with the clinical phenotype; and EUS-based vascular assessment can characterize collateral and variceal anatomy. The same platform extends to therapy, including EUS-guided gastric variceal obliteration and pre-bariatric risk stratification. Current evidence is largely early-phase and requires prospective validation. Rather than replacing established tools, endohepatology offers an integrated pathway tailored to the diagnostic and therapeutic problems most characteristic of MASLD.

title: Blood- and Liver Stiffness-Based Non-Invasive Tests for Clinically Significant Portal Hypertension in Patients With cACLD and HCC.
authorString: Balcar L, Haunold TJ, Jachs M, Semmler G, Simbrunner B, Stättermayer AF, Pereyra D, Schwarz C, Stremitzer S, Kaczirek K, Starlinger P, Quehenberger P, Trauner M, Scheiner B, Reiberger T, Pinter M, Mandorfer M.

journal.title: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

abstractText:
Background and aims

The applicability of non-invasive tests (NITs) for clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH) in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is controversial. We performed a head-to-head comparison of various NITs for CSPH and evaluated rule-in/-out criteria.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective study including 283 patients with HCC undergoing hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) measurement at the Vienna Hepatic Haemodynamic Lab with available, same-day data on NITs (i.e., liver stiffness measurement [LSM], platelet count [PLT], von Willebrand factor antigen [VWF:Ag], and the ratio of VWF:Ag and PLT [VITRO]). For the subsequent analysis, we focused on patients with compensated advanced chronic liver disease (cACLD).

Results

Among 164 patients with cACLD, most were BCLC 0/A (50.6%) and CSPH prevalence was 46.3%, the median LSM was 20.0 kPa (IQR: 13.3-37.9), and mean VWF:Ag/VITRO was 266 ± 119%/2.30 ± 1.81. The VITRO score yielded the highest discriminative ability to detect CSPH (AUROC: 0.834), followed by ANTICIPATE ± NASH (AUROC: 0.822), PLT (AUROC: 0.803), LSM (AUROC: 0.779), and VWF:Ag (AUROC: 0.707). The application of the Baveno VII criterium (LSM ≤ 15 kPa & PLT ≥ 150G/L) and the VITRO score (≤ 1.0) individually showed an excellent performance for ruling-out CSPH (sensitivities: ≥ 95%, NPV: 100%/87.9%). For ruling-in CSPH by individual criteria, the VITRO score provided the highest PPV (≥ 2.5, specificity/PPV: 89.8%/83.0%), followed by the Baveno VII criteria (specificity/PPV: 81.8%/74.6%). When sequentially applying Baveno VII criteria and VITRO, the grey zone could be significantly reduced to 16% (sensitivity/NPV: 94.7%/92.2%; specificity/PPV: 73.9%/84.4%).

Conclusion

The discriminative ability in patients with cACLD and HCC was comparable to patients without HCC. However, PPVs of established criteria were < 90%, which may be explained by the comparatively low prevalence of CSPH in this context.

title: Effects of Lens Status and Prophylactic Transscleral Retinopexy on Vision Outcomes in Boston Terriers Following Phacoemulsification.
authorString: Chin JH, Morton JM, Sanders MT, Mather H, Huang B, Hawes SJ, Stanley RG.
abstractText:
Objectives

To investigate the effects of surgical lens status (pseudophakia or intentional aphakia) and prophylactic transscleral retinopexy (PTR) on postoperative ocular hypertension (POH), glaucoma, retinal detachment, and vision loss following phacoemulsification in Boston Terriers.

Animals studied

Thirty-seven Boston Terriers.

Procedure

A retrospective single-cohort study was conducted on Boston Terriers that underwent phacoemulsification between January 1997 and June 2025, with pseudophakia or intentional aphakia. Time-to-event analyses were performed using parametric interval-censored survival models. Analyses were performed unadjusted and adjusted separately for 4 potential confounders identified using a directed acyclic graph (of which year of surgery was considered the most important).

Results

POH occurred in 22/63 (35%) eyes (46% of pseudophakic and 26% of aphakic eyes), glaucoma in 21/62 (34%) eyes (52% of pseudophakic and 20% of aphakic eyes), and vision loss in 16/61 (26%) eyes (36% of pseudophakic and 18% of aphakic eyes). Only 3 cases of retinal detachment precluded further analysis. Estimated hazard ratios (pseudophakia compared to aphakia, unadjusted and adjusted for year of surgery) were, respectively, 2.0 (95% CI = 0.8 to 5.5; p = 0.157) to 2.8 (95% CI = 1.0 to 7.9; p = 0.052) for POH and 2.9 (95% CI = 0.9 to 9.2; p = 0.075) to 2.7 (95% CI = 1.0 to 7.3; p = 0.050) for glaucoma. Estimated effects of lens status on vision loss and effects of PTR on all three outcomes were imprecise and inconclusive.

Conclusions

In Boston Terrier eyes undergoing phacoemulsification, pseudophakia may result in higher risks of postoperative ocular hypertension and glaucoma compared to intentional aphakia.

title: Risk factors associated with rapid progression of chronic kidney disease. A retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Chogtu B, Prabhu AR, Lakshmi RV, Rao IR.
abstractText:
Objective

To evaluate the association of various risk factors with rapid progression of chronic kidney disease.

Methods

This retrospective study was conducted in CKD patients admitted in a tertiary care hospital between January 2018 to December 2020 with a minimum follow up of one year. Variables including age, sex, hemoglobin, uric acid, serum creatinine, eGFR, proteinuria, presence of AKI and other comorbidities were recorded at baseline. The primary outcome was association of various risk factors with rapid progression of CKD (sustained decline in eGFR of more than 5 ml/min/1.73 m2 /yr.). Each potential risk factor was first evaluated using univariate logistic regression with rapid CKD progression as the dependent variable. Variables with p<0.2 and clinically important variables were taken for multivariate analysis to identify independent predictors.

Results

A total of 993 patients were included in study. Of these 442 (43.5%) were having rapid progression of CKD. Risk factors independently associated with rapid progression of CKD included presence of AKI (OR=1.589, CI= 1.092-2.311, p=0.015), baseline eGFR (OR=1.043, CI= 1.031-1.054, <0.01) and anemia (OR=1.805, CI= 1.178-2.766, p=0.007). Additionally, HbA1c (OR= 1.035, P=0.383), hypertension (OR= 1.258, P= 0.352), proteinuria (OR= 1.242, P= 0.243) and retinopathy (OR= 1.234, P= 0.291) showed a higher odd of rapid CKD progression in multivariable analysis, but the associations did not reach statistical significance.

Conclusion

This study identified presence of AKI, level of baseline eGFR and anemia as risk factors significantly associated with rapid CKD progression.

title: Retroperitoneal Hematoma in Essential Thrombocythaemia: A Diagnostic Challenge.
authorString: Di Gennaro L, Foti F, Benedetti B, Senati M, Chighine A, De-Giorgio F, Carbone L.
abstractText:
Background

Essential thrombocythaemia (ET) is a chronic myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by sustained thrombocytosis and an increased risk of both thrombotic and haemorrhagic events. While thrombotic complications are more frequent, major bleeding remains a rare but potentially fatal occurrence, particularly when anticoagulant therapy is required. Retroperitoneal haematoma represents one of the most severe bleeding manifestations, often linked to anticoagulation or vascular fragility.

Case report

We report the case of an 85-year-old woman with ET, obesity, and hypertension who underwent elective total right hip replacement. Postoperatively, she developed pulmonary micro-embolism and was treated with high-dose enoxaparin. Four days later, she suffered sudden haemodynamic collapse due to a massive retroperitoneal haematoma. Enoxaparin was discontinued and replaced with tranexamic acid infusion. Despite urgent surgical evacuation, multiple transfusions, and intensive care, her condition worsened with the development of femoral vein thrombosis, multidrug-resistant sepsis, worsening pulmonary embolism, and severe thrombocytopenia. She died 34 days after surgery. Autopsy confirmed a large organized haematoma compressing the right renal lodge and inferior vena cava, associated with femoral vein thrombosis.

Discussion

This case highlights the therapeutic and diagnostic challenges of ET, in which thrombotic and haemorrhagic risks may coexist and be further complicated by antithrombotic therapy. Despite individualized enoxaparin dosing based on body weight, the patient developed a major retroperitoneal haemorrhage followed by femoral vein thrombosis. Although disseminated intravascular coagulation and heparin-induced thrombocytopenia were both considered in the differential diagnosis, insufficient clinical and laboratory evidence prevented definitive diagnostic confirmation of either condition.

Conclusions

Early and accurate diagnostic assessment is crucial in ET patients, where thrombotic and haemorrhagic risks coexist. In the absence of clear guidelines, clinical judgment prevails, underscoring the need to reassess physicians' criminal liability.

title: BDH1 Attenuates Macrophage Foam Cell Formation and Inflammation in Atherosclerosis Via Modulating Histone H3K9 Acylation Balance and Activating PPAR Signaling.
authorString: Wang Y, Wang Y, Liu Q, Tian M, Wang B, Lin Q, Huang S.

journal.title: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

abstractText: β-Hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase 1 (BDH1) has been implicated in metabolic disorders. Nevertheless, its function and underlying mechanisms in atherosclerosis (AS) remain ambiguous. A high-fat diet-fed apolipoprotein E-deficient mouse model and oxidized low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL)-induced RAW264.7 macrophages were established. BDH1 expression was evaluated by immunofluorescence and Western blot. RAW264.7 cells with BDH1 overexpression or knockdown were treated with MB-3 (acetylation inhibitor) and Ac-CoA Synthase Inhibitor 1 (ACSS2i, β-hydroxybutyrylation pathway inhibitor). Cell viability, lipid deposition, lipid-related indices, inflammatory cytokines, and histone modifications were evaluated. Bioinformatics analysis was performed to screen downstream pathway of BDH1, and the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) pathway inhibitor GW9662 was applied for functional validation. Herein, BDH1 was markedly downregulated in aortic lesions and plaque macrophages from atherosclerotic mice. In ox-LDL-challenged RAW264.7 cells, BDH1 overexpression increased cell viability and reduced lipid accumulation, triglycerides, total cholesterol, tumor necrosis factor-α, and histone H3 lysine 9 β-hydroxybutyrylation (H3K9bhb) levels, while increasing interleukin-10, and histone H3 lysine 9 acetylation (H3K9ac). Conversely, BDH1 knockdown exacerbated these pathological alterations. MB-3 attenuated the protective effects of BDH1 overexpression and its induction of H3K9ac. ACSS2i partially rescued the deleterious effects of BDH1 knockdown, accompanied by reduced H3K9bhb and restored H3K9ac. PPAR pathway was identified as a downstream pathway of BDH1, and PPAR inhibition reversed the benefits of BDH1 overexpression. Collectively, BDH1 protects against ox-LDL-induced macrophage foam cell formation and inflammatory responses, at least in part by modulating histone acylation including H3K9ac and H3K9bhb, and by activating the PPAR signaling pathway.

title: Cardiovascular outcomes of SGLT2 inhibitors across the spectrum of myocardial infarction: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Elazab A, Elbataa A, Mansour A, Abouzid M, Hammad N, Hassanin MS, Abouzkaly F, Alganadi R, Ali AHG, Alabed A, Mansour A, Shaaban M, Elbahloul MA, Mabrouk MA, Awashra A, Elgendy IY.
abstractText:
Aims

Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) help in heart failure (HF), but their benefit after acute myocardial infarction is unclear. This meta-analysis assesses their impact on mortality and heart failure hospitalization post-acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and identifies which patients benefit most.

Methods

Four databases were searched through August 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and matched studies comparing SGLT2i with control post-AMI.

Primary outcomes

all-cause death and hospitalization for heart failure (HHF); secondary: major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), cardiovascular (CV) death, stroke and recurrent myocardial infarction (MI). Subgroups and meta-regression examined timing, diabetes, follow-up, design, SGLT2i type and baseline HF/diabetes.

Results

Fifteen studies including 117 096 patients (58 613 SGLT2i vs. 58 483 control) were included. A total of 117 096 patients contributed to the all-cause mortality analysis (OR 0.78, 95% CI 0.67-0.90), whereas 116 992 patients across 14 studies contributed to the HHF analysis (OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.63-0.88). All-cause mortality was significantly lower in PSM observational studies (OR 0.64, 95% CI 0.61-0.67), whereas the reduction did not reach statistical significance in RCTs (OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.76-1.01), with a significant interaction by study design. HHF reduction occurred with both early and delayed initiation; dapagliflozin and empagliflozin were similarly effective. MACE was significantly lower with SGLT2i, but CV death, recurrent MI and stroke did not differ. Baseline HF or diabetes showed no association with primary outcomes.

Conclusions

SGLT2i reduced HHF after MI, but this benefit should be interpreted cautiously because of small-study effects and possible publication bias. The all-cause mortality benefit is driven by observational studies; RCTs show a favourable but nonsignificant trend.

title: Effectiveness of Digital Commitment Devices in Improving Lifestyle and Cardiometabolic Outcomes in Adults with Cardiometabolic Risk Factors: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Chen RJ, Goh CSP, Chew NW, Chew HSJ.
abstractText:
Aim

Lifestyle modification is crucial for cardiovascular disease prevention but remains challenging due to complex behavioural factors such as the intention-behaviour gap. Digital commitment devices (DCD) could narrow this gap by leveraging behavioural economics, but its effectiveness remains unclear. Therefore, this review aims to evaluate the effects of DCDs on lifestyle and cardiometabolic outcomes in adults with elevated cardiometabolic risk.

Methods

A systematic search of 12 electronic databases was conducted from database inception to August 2025. Study selection and methodological quality appraisal using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool were performed independently by two reviewers. Where appropriate, effect sizes were pooled using random effects meta-analyses. The certainty of evidence for meta-analysed outcomes was assessed using the GRADE approach.

Results

A total of 7,378 articles were retrieved, of which 29 randomised controlled trials involving 7,534 participants were included. DCDs were found to significantly increase daily step count (WMD=664.87, 95% CI: 463.22 to 866.51, T=6.88, p<0.00001; I2=0%) and weight loss (WMD=-1.90kg, 95% CI: -2.59 to -1.21, p<0.0001; I2=70%), improve self-reported emotional (WMD=-1.34, 95% CI: -2.59 to -0.09, p=0.04; I2=0%) and uncontrolled eating (WMD=-1.74, 95% CI: -3.05 to -0.43, p=0.02; I2=0%) behaviours, body fat percentage, diet and medication adherence.

Conclusion

DCDs could improve lifestyle and cardiometabolic outcomes by improving physical activity and weight management, thus enhancing cardiometabolic disease prevention. Future research should prioritise long-term trials with extended follow-up periods beyond 12 months to observe physiological improvements and assess maintenance of effects.

title: Heart failure with supranormal ejection fraction: is it the new Ariadne's string?
authorString: Katsi V, Maragkoudakis S, Lilikaki G, Marketou M, Farmakis D, Tsioufis K.
abstractText: Heart failure with supranormal ejection fraction (HFsnEF) is an emerging and incompletely characterized phenotype within the heart failure (HF) spectrum. Although no universally accepted LVEF threshold for HFsnEF has been established and different definitions have been used across published studies, for the purposes of this review HFsnEF is operationally defined as HF with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) > 65%. Importantly, a supranormal LVEF should not be interpreted as evidence of enhanced ventricular performance. Patients with HFsnEF may exhibit smaller left ventricular (LV) volumes, concentric remodeling, increased myocardial stiffness, impaired longitudinal deformation, reduced stroke volume and preload reserve, and elevated filling pressures, particularly during exercise. HFsnEF is unlikely to represent a single disease entity; rather, it encompasses heterogeneous pathophysiological substrates and clinical phenotypes, including hypertensive and cardiometabolic remodeling, valvular heart disease, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM), and other conditions associated with hyperdynamic ventricular function. Accordingly, the diagnostic evaluation should extend beyond recognition of an elevated LVEF and systematically identify the underlying phenotype and potentially treatable causes through comprehensive echocardiography, myocardial deformation imaging, cardiac magnetic resonance, disease-specific testing, and exercise or invasive hemodynamic assessment when indicated. Therapeutic evidence specific to HFsnEF remains limited. No randomized clinical trial has specifically evaluated conventional HF pharmacotherapy in a population prospectively defined by LVEF > 65%; therefore, evidence for conventional HF and cardiometabolic therapies is derived predominantly from broader HFpEF populations or subgroup analyses and should be regarded as indirect rather than definitive evidence for HFsnEF. In contrast, recognition of specific underlying diseases, particularly ATTR-CM, HCM, and significant valvular heart disease, may permit evidence-based disease-specific treatment. This review summarizes the epidemiology, pathophysiology, and clinical phenotypes of HFsnEF and proposes a practical phenotype-guided approach to diagnosis and management. Standardized definitions and prospective trials specifically addressing patients with LVEF > 65% are needed to establish evidence-based therapeutic strategies for this population.

title: Herpes Zoster and Cardiovascular Disease: An Unexpected Association.
authorString: Patel D, Kallash M, Frishman WH.
abstractText: Herpes zoster (HZ), the reactivation of latent varicella zoster virus (VZV), is increasingly being recognized as more than a dermatologic and neurologic disease. In recent years, multiple meta-analyses have linked HZ infection to a clinically significant increase in the risk of stroke, myocardial infarction (MI), and other major adverse cardiovascular events, an effect that is most pronounced in the first days to weeks following the acute HZ infection, with a gradual decrease in risk over time. The proposed mechanism centers on a productive viral infection of arterial walls, a phenomenon described as VZV vasculopathy, with transmural inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and thrombosis, all superimposed on the systemic inflammatory and prothrombotic state that accompanies the acute HZ infection. The evidence for an association between HZ infection and cardiovascular events has grown stronger with recent multiple large cohort studies demonstrating that patients who received HZ vaccination had a significantly lower rate of major adverse cardiovascular events, MI, stroke, heart failure, and arrhythmia. However, while these cohort studies have helped researchers identify the potential association of HZ vaccination and reduced cardiovascular risk, there remains a need for a randomized controlled trial to establish causality between these factors. Currently underway, a randomized controlled trial is directly evaluating whether HZ vaccination in a large population lowers the incidence of cardiovascular events, including stroke, MI, and cardiovascular death. Nevertheless, the 2026 American College of Cardiology guidelines now include a strong recommendation for HZ vaccination given the growing body of evidence regarding the association of HZ vaccination with cardiovascular events.

title: Achieving Risk-Specific Absolute LDL-C Threshold with PCSK9 Inhibitors: A Real-World, Single-Center Analysis.
authorString: Ciobanu DM, Berchișan A, Mălan C, Rusu A, Crăciun AE, Inceu G, Tholvay DM, Bala C.

journal.title: Romanian journal of internal medicine = Revue roumaine de medecine interne

abstractText:
Introduction

Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitors emerged as an effective treatment for hypercholesterolemia in clinical trials, however real-world evidence shows considerable heterogeneity. We aimed to assess the effectiveness and safety of injectable PCSK9 inhibitors in real-world patients.

Methods
