Our retrospective analysis included 45 consecutive adults, 18 (40%) men, mean age 57.4 years, inadequately controlled on, or intolerant to, statins and/or ezetimibe, and newly initiated on alirocumab 75 mg or 150 mg, evolocumab 140 mg, or inclisiran 284 mg. Biochemical parameters and adverse events were recorded at baseline and when LDL-C reached the risk-specific absolute threshold or the lowest LDL-C closest to it after starting PCSK9 inhibitors (<55 mg/dL very high, <70 mg/dL high cardiovascular risk, per European Society of Cardiology). LDL-C was also assessed at standardized time points (3, 6, 12, 18, 24 months).

Results

At 3 and 6 months, LDL-C decreased by a median of 54.4% and 59.2% (both p < 0.001), with 52.4% and 50.0% of patients below threshold. The best LDL-C reduction was 66.9% (from 145 mg/dL to 50 mg/dL; p < 0.001) at a median time to first documented threshold attainment of 5 months. In an exploratory analysis, no significant association was detected between LDL-C reduction and sex, diabetes, statin intensity or ezetimibe use. No clinically relevant hepatic or muscular toxicity was attributed to PCSK9 inhibitors.

Conclusion

In real-world patients aiming to achieve the absolute LDL-C threshold on PCSK9 inhibitors, treatment was associated with marked LDL-C reduction after a median of 5 months.

title: Comparative Outcomes of Self-Expanding Versus Balloon-Expandable Valves in Severe Aortic Stenosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Elazab A, Ali AHG, Elbataa A, Mansour A, Hammad N, Galal A, Abdelaziz OA, Sayed MS, Elkasaby MH, Shaaban M, Hassanin MS, Mousa AIA, Elgendy IY, Alharasees M, Aly A, Alali AKA, Frishman WH, Aronow WS.
abstractText: Abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is an established treatment for severe aortic stenosis, with self-expanding valves (SEV) and balloon-expandable valves (BEV) representing the two major platforms. However, their comparative clinical and hemodynamic performance remains uncertain. We systematically searched four electronic databases through August 2026 for studies comparing SEV and BEV in patients undergoing TAVR. The primary outcomes were permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) and change in mean pressure gradient (MPG), while secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), stroke, paravalvular leakage (PVL), heart failure hospitalization, coronary obstruction, and prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM). Twenty-three studies involving 21,609 patients were included. Compared with BEV, SEV was associated with a significantly greater reduction in MPG (MD -4.48, 95% CI -5.29 to -3.67; P < 0.0001) and lower risks of moderate (RR 0.56, 95% CI 0.42-0.75) and severe PPM (RR 0.33, 95% CI 0.25-0.44). Conversely, SEV was associated with higher risks of PPI (RR 1.40, 95% CI 1.14-1.72; P < 0.0001), moderate-to-severe PVL (RR 2.28, 95% CI 1.65-3.14; P < 0.0001), and a small but significant increase in all-cause mortality. No significant differences were observed in MACE, stroke, heart failure hospitalization, or coronary obstruction..

title: Transcatheter versus surgical closure of CHDs in predominantly pediatric populations: a systematic review of comparative and single-arm evidence.
authorString: Majed A, Kmeid P, Safa A, Kahwaji H, Naamani AER, El-Atat M, Ossaily A, Ghanem G.
abstractText:
Background

Transcatheter closure increasingly replaces surgery for congenital heart defects (CHDs), but comparative evidence comes almost entirely from atrial septal defect. We asked whether its trade-offs hold for other lesions in predominantly pediatric cohorts.

Methods

We searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL to June 2026 for cohorts with mean or median age under 18 years (PRISMA 2020). Only direct comparisons informed comparative conclusions. Narrative synthesis was stratified by lesion, with sensitivity analyses for mixed-age cohorts and adverse-event definitions.

Results

Six of eleven studies compared both approaches (1,158 transcatheter, 490 surgical patients), in atrial septal defect, patent ductus arteriosus, and coronary artery fistula; none addressed muscular ventricular septal defect. Procedural success was high with both. Hospital stay was shorter after transcatheter closure in all six (2.4-4.4 days in atrial septal defect), the most consistently observed finding. Major adverse events were less frequent after transcatheter closure in atrial septal defect, but arms differed in age and weight, and the difference was inconsistent in wholly pediatric cohorts; in coronary artery fistula, one study at serious risk of bias found them over twice as frequent after transcatheter closure. Where both arms were followed, reintervention was uncommon in each. GRADE certainty was low for hospital stay and procedural success, otherwise very low.

Conclusions

Shorter hospital stay after transcatheter closure is the most consistently observed finding, at low certainty. Neither approach is shown to be safer: safety findings differed between lesions and, beyond atrial septal defect, rest on single studies. Lesion anatomy determines which approach applies.

title: Whole-transcriptome single-cell spatial landscape of instability in human carotid atherosclerosis.
authorString: Byun JH, Cao Y, Harutyunyan AS, Oikonomopoulos S, Ragoussis J, Veinot JP, Papacostas Quintanilla H, Daskalopoulou SS.
abstractText:
Aims

Carotid atherosclerotic plaque instability is a major cause of ischemic stroke. While current clinical guidelines for carotid endarterectomy rely primarily on stenosis severity and patient symptomatology, unstable plaques can cause strokes even with low to moderate stenosis, suggesting that factors beyond plaque stenosis may drive its instability. This study aimed to characterize the cellular and spatial features of plaque instability at both single-cell and subcellular resolution.

Methods and results

single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed on carotid endarterectomy samples from patients with clinically and histologically classified stable or unstable plaques, consisting of more than 53,000 cells. Vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), macrophages, and T-lymphocytes accounted for ∼85% of plaque-resident cells, with unstable plaques showing increased abundance of inflammatory synthetic VSMCs, GZMK+ cytotoxic T-lymphocytes, and antigen-presenting macrophages. In contrast, stable plaques were enriched in contractile and fibroblast-like VSMCs, alongside MRC1+ resident-like macrophages. To then spatially map these populations, CosMx™ high-plex spatial transcriptomics was integrated utilizing the unprecedented whole-transcriptome (∼18,934 targets) Human Discovery RNA panel. This revealed a distinct spatially disorganized plaque architecture in unstable plaques, characterized by infiltration of inflammatory synthetic VSMCs and effector T-lymphocytes distributed across both the fibrotic cap and lipid core, alongside distinct multicellular microenvironments enriched for adaptive immune engagement. This was in contrast to stable plaques, which exhibited more structured, macrophage-dominant spatial microenvironments and neighborhoods. We lastly profiled ∼90,000 paired peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) to assess the plaque macroenvironment. PBMCs surrounding unstable plaques displayed exclusive enrichment of CD14+CD16+ intermediate monocytes and effector T-lymphocytes, which were depleted surrounding stable plaques. Ligand-receptor interaction analyses within CCL and CXCL-mediated pathways revealed enhanced immune-stromal signaling between PBMC-derived monocytes and plaque-resident VSMCs in the unstable plaque group, with coordinated chemokine-driven interactions indicating a shift toward VSMC- and T-lymphocyte mediated recruitment of circulating immune cells.

Conclusions

These results demonstrate that carotid plaque instability is driven by spatially coordinated expansion of inflammatory VSMCs and effector immune cells within the plaque and from the circulation, with a shift from predominantly innate immune-dominant characteristics in stable plaques toward adaptive immune-enriched responses in unstable conditions. This integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomic approach refines an integrated immune-stromal framework linking local plaque remodeling with systemic immune activation, highlighting key tissue-resident and circulating contributors to instability and establishing a foundation for mechanism-informed diagnostics and targeted therapeutic strategies beyond stenosis severity.

title: Joint Association of Longitudinal Single-Point Insulin Sensitivity Estimator Patterns and Hypertension Status with Incident Stroke Among Adults with Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome Stages 0-3: A Nationwide Prospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Sun J, Ma X, Zhang X, Liu G, Zhou H.
abstractText:
Background

The prognostic value of longitudinal single-point insulin sensitivity estimator (SPISE) patterns for stroke, particularly when considered in combination with hypertension (HTN), remains unclear among adults with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome stages 0-3.

Aims

This study aimed to examine the association of combined longitudinal SPISE patterns and HTN status with incident stroke among adults with CKM syndrome stages 0-3.

Study design

A nationwide prospective cohort study.

Methods

We included adults aged ≥ 45 years with CKM stages 0-3 from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. SPISE was calculated at Waves 1 and 3, and incident stroke was ascertained through Wave 5. K-means clustering was used to identify longitudinal SPISE patterns, which were dichotomized as persistently low or non-persistently low. Participants were then cross-classified according to longitudinal SPISE pattern and baseline HTN status. Cumulative SPISE exposure was calculated from repeated SPISE measurements. Cox models were used to examine associations with incident stroke. Dose-response, subgroup, sensitivity, and model-performance analyses were also performed.

Results

Among 4,443 participants, 348 incident strokes occurred. A persistently low longitudinal SPISE pattern was associated with a higher risk of incident stroke than a persistently high pattern [hazard ratio (HR), 2.29; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.59-3.29]. Compared with the group with no HTN and a non-persistently low SPISE pattern, stroke risk was higher in the group with no HTN and a persistently low SPISE pattern (HR, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.12-1.95), the group with HTN and a non-persistently low SPISE pattern (HR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.10-2.23), and the group with HTN and a persistently low SPISE pattern (HR, 2.45; 95% CI, 1.84-3.26). Higher cumulative SPISE exposure was inversely associated with incident stroke (HR per 1-unit increment, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.93-0.97), with an approximately linear dose-response relationship. Incorporating the combined longitudinal SPISE pattern and HTN status increased the apparent C-index from 0.612 to 0.646. However, optimism-corrected discrimination was comparable between the combined model and the HTN-only model.

Conclusion

The combination of longitudinal SPISE patterns and HTN status identified a subgroup at the highest risk of incident stroke in this CKM population.

title: Early outcomes after complete atrioventricular septal defect repair beyond one year of age: a single-centre comparative study.
authorString: Arslanoglu E, Azizi M, Tatar EN, Gunduz E, Zeybek C, Aliyev B, Bakhshaliyev S.
abstractText:
Background

Complete atrioventricular septal defect is usually repaired during early infancy, but delayed referral remains common where access to specialised congenital cardiac surgery is limited.

Objective

To compare early outcomes after repair in patients aged 12 months or younger and those older than 12 months.

Methods

This single-centre retrospective study included 81 patients who underwent repair between 2020 and 2024. All patients evaluated for repair underwent cardiac catheterisation, and those with elevated pulmonary vascular resistance underwent vasoreactivity testing with 100% oxygen and inhaled nitric oxide. In-hospital mortality, major complications, pulmonary artery pressure, atrioventricular valve regurgitation, and perioperative outcomes were compared.

Results

Thirty-five patients were aged 12 months or younger and 46 were older than 12 months. Median ages were 8 and 14 months, respectively. In-hospital mortality occurred in 3 of 35 and 4 of 46 patients, respectively. Major complications occurred in 6 of 35 and 11 of 46 patients. No statistically significant differences were detected in mortality, major complications, ventilation duration, ICU stay, pulmonary artery pressure, or early atrioventricular valve regurgitation. Confidence intervals around mortality and major-complication estimates were wide.

Conclusion

Repair beyond 12 months was feasible in selected patients considered operable after invasive assessment, but in-hospital mortality remained substantial and estimates were imprecise. These findings do not establish equivalence and should not support intentional delay of repair.

title: Acute myocardial infarction after brief antithrombotic interruption in Kawasaki disease-related coronary aneurysm.
authorString: Kitahori H, Fukamachi D, Fujito H, Matsumoto N, Okumura Y.
abstractText: We report a 20-year-old man with a history of Kawasaki disease-related coronary aneurysm who developed acute myocardial infarction after one week of discontinuing aspirin and warfarin. This case highlights the catastrophic risk of even brief interruption of antithrombotic therapy in patients with Kawasaki disease-related coronary aneurysms. It also suggests that vulnerability during transition to adult care, particularly in terms of self-management and medication adherence, may contribute to such events.

title: Cardiovascular resilience in centenarians.
authorString: Carrera-Bastos P, Plaza-Florido A, Pérez-Prieto I, Radom-Aizik S, Franceschi C, Rodríguez-López C, Serra-Rexach JA, Emanuele E, Lucia A.
abstractText: Centenarians - individuals aged ≥100 years - provide a unique human model for understanding resilience to cardiovascular ageing. Although cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, including hypertension, heart failure, atrial fibrillation and chronic kidney disease, are common in centenarians, their onset is typically delayed relative to that in individuals aged 80-100 years. Centenarians characteristically have structural changes in the heart and vessels, including concentric left ventricular remodelling, increased myocardial stiffness and vascular ageing, but often without the expected burden of myocardial infarction or overt heart failure. Their cardiometabolic profile is generally favourable, marked by preserved insulin sensitivity in cohorts with a low prevalence of diabetes mellitus, mid-range lipid levels and a low prevalence of obesity. Centenarians also have a distinctive inflammatory and gastrointestinal phenotype, characterized by chronic low-grade inflammation with elevated anti-inflammatory signalling, a gut microbiome that more closely resembles that of younger adults, and preserved intestinal barrier integrity. Genetically and epigenetically, exceptional longevity reflects highly polygenic contributions, selective maintenance of genomic stability and markedly younger epigenetic age compared with chronological age. In this Review, we summarize data on the cardiovascular system among centenarians by framing observations of longevity as a composite of delayed pathology, adaptive compensation and survivorship selection. Understanding the biological, behavioural and environmental mechanisms underlying cardiovascular resilience in extreme longevity might inform strategies to extend cardiovascular healthspan across all ages.

title: The Illusion of Recovery From Atrial Fibrillation, a Review of Postcardioversion Anticoagulation Guidelines.
authorString: Patel D, Kallash M, Frishman WH.
abstractText: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia in clinical practice and an independent, well-established risk factor for ischemic stroke. However, restoring sinus rhythm via cardioversion does not eliminate this risk. Cardioversion itself transiently increases thromboembolic risk more than 10-fold, driven by atrial stunning, a state in which the left atrium and left atrial appendage remain mechanically dysfunctional despite normalized electrical activity seen on an electrocardiogram. Retrospective data show that thromboembolic events are clustered heavily within the first 2 weeks postcardioversion, supporting the near-universal recommendation of at least 4 weeks of continued therapeutic anticoagulation postcardioversion for AF duration more than 12 to 48 hours, regardless of baseline stroke risk score. Beyond this initial 4-week recommendation, the decision to continue anticoagulation is based on a comprehensive assessment of the patient's thromboembolic risk profile, rather than rhythm status or cardioversion success. Multiple trials have demonstrated a significant increase in the incidence of ischemic strokes in patients who had a premature discontinuation of anticoagulation postcardioversion. Additionally, having a prior stroke, the heaviest weighted risk-stratification variable, favors indefinite anticoagulation regardless of postcardioversion rhythm outcome. Current guidelines provide a framework for approaching postcardioversion anticoagulation, including a fixed 4-week anticoagulation course encompassing the atrial stunning period, followed by individualized risk-stratification to determine the indication for continued anticoagulation. Nevertheless, future research is still required to better elucidate whether anticoagulation can be safely discontinued after completion of the recommended 4-week postcardioversion anticoagulation course in patients with a prior AF-related stroke.

title: Choosing Cardiovascular Assessment and Risk-Prediction Tools Across the Care Pathway: A Clinician-Oriented Review.
authorString: Perpétuo L, Trindade F, Bastos M, Leite-Moreira A, Vitorino R.
abstractText: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, making accurate and efficient risk stratification essential across the care pathway. Numerous tools support emergency triage, disease assessment, procedural decision-making, long-term prevention, atrial fibrillation management, and evaluation of functional status, but no single model is applicable across all clinical settings or populations. This clinician-oriented review categorizes and critically compares commonly used cardiovascular assessment and risk-prediction tools, including History, Electrocardiogram, Age, Risk factors, Troponin, Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events, and Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction for emergency triage; Agatston, Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis, and Synergy Between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with Taxus and Cardiac Surgery for anatomical and clinical assessment; European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation, Society of Thoracic Surgeons, and Revised Cardiac Risk Index, for procedural risk; and Framingham, the pooled cohort equations implemented in the Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease, Risk Estimator, Systematic Coronary Risk Evaluation 2, QResearch Cardiovascular Risk Algorithm 3, and Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease EVENTs for long-term prediction. Congestive heart failure, hypertension, age ≥75, diabetes, stroke/transient ischemic attack (2 points), congestive heart failure, hypertension, age ≥75 (2 points), diabetes, stroke/TIA (2 points), vascular disease, age 65-74, sex category (female), and hypertension, abnormal renal/liver function, stroke, bleeding history, labile international normalized ratio, elderly, drugs/alcohol, are discussed in the context of atrial fibrillation, alongside New York Heart Association and the Seattle Angina Questionnaire as measures of functional status and quality of life. For each tool, we examine its clinical purpose, principal variables, strengths, limitations, practical applications, and areas of overlap. Differences in implementation across healthcare systems and patient populations are considered to support context-appropriate selection. Persistent limitations include poor standardization, reliance on data that may be unavailable in resource-constrained settings, limited transportability, and incomplete integration into clinical workflows. Greater harmonization, external validation, digital automation, and the careful incorporation of biomarkers and artificial intelligence may support more accessible, dynamic, and personalized cardiovascular risk assessment.

title: Ventilation inhomogeneity in Duchenne muscular dystrophy before the initiation of ventilatory support: Insights from electrical impedance tomography.
authorString: Vianello A, Lionello F, Ciresi M, Pozza M, Bello L, Guarnieri G.
abstractText:
Background

Prior to the onset of overt ventilatory failure, patients with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) can display non-uniform respiratory mechanics, resulting from atelectasis in small lung regions secondary to rapid, shallow breathing and/or peripheral airway obstruction, thereby predisposing to the development of ventilation inhomogeneity.

Objectives

To investigate ventilation distribution in DMD patients before the initiation of long-term assisted ventilation by using electrical impedance tomography (EIT).

Methods

Patients and interventions: Eighteen DMD patients underwent EIT between 1 January and 31 December 2025. Primary study endpoint: Global Inhomogeneity Index (GI). EIT data were compared with those obtained from a group of 11 healthy, similarly aged male medical residents.

Results

GI was significantly higher in the DMD patients with respect to healthy males [0.44 ± 0.13 (0.36-0.77) vs 0.37 ± 0.03 (0.32-0.43); p < 0.001]. A GI of 0.5 maximised the distinction between DMD patients with a ventilation distribution pattern similar to or different from the healthy subjects.

Conclusions

Before initiation of assisted ventilation, a subset of DMD patients may develop lung ventilation inhomogeneity, which can be readily assessed by means of EIT. Whether such inhomogeneity is predictive of major clinical events therefore constitutes a critical question to be addressed.

title: NOR-1 is an upstream regulator of Ca2+ homeostasis and calmodulin kinase II-dependent arrhythmogenesis.
authorString: Vázquez-Sufuentes P, Jiménez-Sábado V, Ballester-Servera C, Casabella-Ramón S, Aceituno C, Alonso J, Cañes L, Manzano-Reche G, García-Aranda J, Herraiz-Martínez A, Rodríguez-Sinovas A, Álvarez-Lacalle E, Ginel A, Chen SRW, Rodríguez C, Echebarria B, Martínez-González J, Hove-Madsen L.
abstractText:
Aims

Dysregulation of NOR-1 has been reported in cardiovascular diseases associated with altered calcium handling. We therefore investigated how NOR-1 affects calcium homeostasis and arrhythmogenesis to identify the underlying mechanisms.

Methods

We assessed the expression of NOR-1 and calcium regulatory proteins in myocardial samples from humans and mice that overexpress human NOR-1 in the heart (TgNOR-1). Gene promoter activity was determined by transient co-transfection assays. Calcium imaging, patch-clamp recordings and immunofluorescent labeling was performed in mouse cardiomyocytes. Experimental data were used for mathematical modeling. Arrhythmias were induced in vivo by an epinephrine/caffeine challenge.

Results

In human cardiac samples, mRNA levels of genes coding for SERCA2a, CASQ2, TN-C1 and PLB correlated with those of NOR-1, while TgNOR-1 mice exhibited higher cardiac levels of these calcium regulatory proteins than wild-type animals (WT). NOR-1 increased luciferase activity driven by the proximal promoter of both human and mouse genes. Calcium transients were smaller in TgNOR-1 cardiomyocytes while L-type calcium current and SR calcium content were unchanged. Mathematical modeling revealed that more calcium binds to CASQ2 and is released from the SR in TgNOR-1 cardiomyocytes, but the resulting calcium transient is smaller because more calcium is buffered by TN-C1. Furthermore, NOR-1 transgenesis increased the level of reactive oxygen species and CAMKII oxidation, as well as RyR2 phosphorylation at Ser-2814, which led to a higher incidence of calcium waves and afterdepolarizations in resting TgNOR-1 cardiomyocytes. In electrically paced myocytes, NOR-1 transgenesis promoted extra-transients at low frequencies and calcium alternans at high frequencies. Importantly, these derangements in intracellular calcium handling concurred with a dramatic increase in epinephrine/caffeine-induced bidirectional ventricular tachycardia in TgNOR-1 mice. Moreover, the antioxidant N-acetylcysteine and the CAMKII inhibitor KN-93 attenuated arrythmia in TgNOR-1 mice and arrhythmogenic calcium release in isolated myocytes.

Conclusions

Our findings highlight NOR-1 as an upstream regulator of CAMKII-oxidation underlying arrhythmia induced by defective calcium homeostasis, pointing to therapies targeting CAMKII as a means to attenuate arrhythmia triggered by pathological upregulation of NOR-1.

title: Sevelamer-Induced Gastrointestinal Bleeding.
authorString: Lerttiendamrong B, Dorman G, Stead C.
abstractText: The authors have reported a case of a male patient in his 70s with end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis and sevelamer use for hyperphosphatemia. The patient's hospital course was complicated by pulseless electrical activity cardiac arrest, infective endocarditis, and bacteremia. During the hospital course, the patient developed 2 episodes of large-volume bloody stools accompanied by hypotension. Colonoscopy was notable for ulcerated and pseudomembrane-covered mucosa in the rectum. Histopathology showed ulcerated colonic mucosa containing "scale- like" foreign crystals, consistent with sevelamer resin. Gastrointestinal bleeding secondary to sevelamer use has rarely been reported, with only 36 cases documented globally as of 2024. The cardiac arrest and hemodynamic instability may have contributed to mucosal vulnerability in the setting of sevelamer exposure. To the knowledge of the authors, this is the first reported case of sevelamer-induced gastrointestinal injury in a patient with recent cardiac arrest. No additional episodes of bleeding were observed after discontinuation of sevelamer.

title: Pharmacist-Led Medication Titration for Cardiometabolic Disease: Evidence, Equity, and Scale.
authorString: Yarlagadda S, Blood AJ.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

To review community-based pharmacist-led medication titration across cardiometabolic conditions and the infrastructure needed to deliver this model at scale.

Recent findings

This review reframes cardiometabolic medication optimization as a continuum from passive gap identification to active longitudinal medication management. Registries, dashboards, audit and feedback, electronic health record alerts, and inpatient initiation can identify undertreatment or prompt prescribing, but they do not provide infrastructure for dose adjustment, monitoring, adherence support, and medication-access navigation. Pharmacist-led, team-based models occupy the active end of this continuum. The strongest evidence is in hypertension, with meaningful blood pressure reductions; in heart failure, interdisciplinary titration programs more directly address target-dose achievement than alerts or decision-support tools. Emerging data extend this framework to diabetes, lipidology, and obesity. Value-based care provides a reimbursement framework to support these services. Pharmacist-led titration can close gaps between therapies and delivery, but scaling requires equity-focused implementation, flexible staffing, population health infrastructure that connects artificial intelligence-enabled patient identification to action, and sustainable reimbursement.

title: Characteristics and Treatment Utilisation Patterns of Individuals Using Tirzepatide for Type 2 Diabetes in Germany.
authorString: Füchtenbusch M, Kraus M, Heitmann E, Wilhelm S, Schwarz L, Bendel J, Hennies N.
abstractText:
Introduction

This study describes real-world characteristics and utilisation patterns of tirzepatide among adults with type 2 diabetes in German office-based practice.

Methods

This retrospective observational study analysed data from the CompuGroup Medical Healthcare Database. Cohort 1 initiated tirzepatide between 1 December 2023 and 31 March 2024 and cohort 2 between 1 July and 30 September 2024. A subgroup of cohort 1 with ≥ 6 months' follow-up data and uninterrupted tirzepatide use (cohort 1a) was also analysed. Descriptive statistics summarised baseline characteristics, prior therapy, and dosing patterns.

Results

Cohort 1 included 1223 individuals and cohort 2 included 2300; mean (± standard deviation) age was 59 ± 12 and 60 ± 12 years, respectively, and approximately 54% were male. Comorbidities, especially hypertension and dyslipidaemia, were frequent. Most individuals had prior insulin and/or glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) treatment (cohort 1, 72.1%; cohort 2, 59.6%). A total of 458 individuals had 6 months' follow-up (cohort 1a). The most common starting dose was 2.5 mg (71.2%). Use of higher doses gradually increased over time, with 5.0 mg becoming the most prevalent; at 6 months, 35.9% of individuals received 5.0 mg and 18.6% received 10.0 mg.

Conclusion

This first comprehensive real-world study of tirzepatide use in Germany showed tirzepatide initiation primarily after GLP-1 RA and/or insulin therapy. Most individuals remained on 5.0 mg, with a notable proportion escalating to 10.0 mg. Cohort characteristics were generally similar to those in the SURPASS trials, supporting the relevance of trial findings to clinical practice.

title: Same Class, Different Risk? Dapagliflozin versus Empagliflozin and Genitourinary Safety in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Retrospective Comparative Cohort Study.
authorString: Danau RA, Munteanu MA, Muraru M, Nicolae C, Predoiu G, Bardan A, Jinga V.

journal.title: Romanian journal of internal medicine = Revue roumaine de medecine interne

abstractText:
Background

Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors are guideline-directed therapy for heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), but comparative genitourinary safety data for dapagliflozin and empagliflozin in HFpEF-treated populations remain limited.

Objective

To compare 6-month symptomatic urinary tract infection (UTI), asymptomatic bacteriuria, and other genitourinary adverse events among patients newly initiated on dapagliflozin or empagliflozin for HFpEF.

Methods

This retrospective, single-centre comparative cohort study included 239 adults with physician-documented HFpEF retained after a requirement for at least 6 months of continuous follow-up: 113 received dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily and 126 received empagliflozin 10 mg once daily. The original outcome of any documented bacteriuria/UTI was separated into symptomatic UTI and asymptomatic bacteriuria. Risk differences and 95% confidence intervals were calculated; a multivariable logistic model of the original documented bacteriuria/UTI composite adjusted for age, sex, and baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR).

Results

Any documented bacteriuria/UTI occurred in 21/113 (18.6%) dapagliflozin-treated participants and 25/126 (19.8%) empagliflozin-treated participants. Symptomatic UTI occurred in 4/113 (3.5%) and 5/126 (4.0%), respectively; 17/113 (15.0%) and 20/126 (15.9%) had documented asymptomatic bacteriuria. The risk difference for the composite, calculated as empagliflozin minus dapagliflozin, was 1.3 percentage points (95% CI -8.9 to 11.2). The adjusted odds ratio was 1.62 (95% CI 0.76-3.45; p = 0.208). Other genitourinary events were uncommon and estimates were imprecise.

Conclusions

No statistically detectable between-group difference was found in symptomatic UTI, asymptomatic bacteriuria, or the original composite outcome. Confidence intervals were wide and compatible with clinically meaningful differences in either direction. These exploratory findings require confirmation in prospective multicentre studies with standardized culture ascertainment and complete follow-up.

title: From mechanism to medicine: lumacaftor for trafficking-deficient long QT syndrome type 2.
authorString: Nimani S, Odening KE.

title: Moving towards integrated and continuous pharmaceutical care in coronary heart diseases.
authorString: Kelleci Cakir B, Bayraktar-Ekincioglu A.

title: Correction to: 2026 ESC Guidelines for the management of cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease, in collaboration with the European Renal Association (ERA): Developed by the task force on the management of cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC).
Cerebral Safety of Two Pulsed Field Ablation Workflows for Pulmonary Vein Isolation: Results From the Randomized TWOSOME MRI Study.
authorString: Hartl S, Reinsch N, Füting A, El-Battrawy I, Tiemessen M, Waldt S, Pongratz J, Neven K.
abstractText:
Background

Data on silent cerebral events/lesions (SCE/SCL) following pulsed field ablation (PFA) for pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) are limited. This study aimed to assess the incidence of SCE/SCL using cerebral magnetic resonance imaging (cMRI) in atrial fibrillation (AF) patients undergoing PVI with two distinct PFA systems and workflows.

Methods

In this prospective, single-center TWOSOME MRI substudy, patients with paroxysmal AF were randomized 1:1 to single-shot or single-tip PFA. Single-shot PVI was performed using a pentaspline PFA catheter (single-transseptal access, PV-angiography, no 3D mapping) and single-tip PVI using a PFA generator with a focal ablation catheter (double-transseptal access, 3D mapping). A predefined consecutive cohort underwent 1.5-T cMRI 24 h after the procedure. SCE were defined as acute cMRI-detected lesions resolving on 6-week follow-up cMRI, and SCL as persistent lesions. Baseline characteristics, neurological symptoms, procedural data, and cMRI findings were assessed.

Results

Fifty patients underwent cMRI (25 per group). Acute SCE were detected in 3/50 patients (6%; 95% CI 1.3-16.5), with 1/25 (4%) in the single-shot group and 2/25 (8%) in the single-tip group (p = 1.00). All SCE resolved on follow-up imaging, with no evidence of persistent SCL. One symptomatic stroke occurred in the single-shot group, unrelated to PFA, and was attributed to air embolization during transseptal puncture. No permanent neurological deficits occurred.

Conclusions

In this exploratory cMRI study, both PFA workflows showed a low incidence of SCE without evidence of SCL or PFA-related neurological complications. Larger studies are required to compare cerebral safety profiles of PFA technologies.

Trial registration

NCT07175727 (clinicaltrials.gov).

title: Evaluation of CardiaZn Pediatric Biodegradable Stent in a Long-Term Animal Model.
authorString: Levi DS, Latson L, Stoffregen WC, Bocks M, Sharawy NK, Moran T.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText:
Background

A survey of interventional pediatric cardiologists identified bioresorbable stents for aortic and pulmonary coarctations as the most needed device.

Aims

PediaStent developed the CardiaZn stent and conducted a 2.5-year GLP preclinical study to evaluate device safety, biocompatibility, and functional performance.

Methods

Twelve Yucatan (17-23 kg) mini swine received two CardiaZn stents in the aorta and one in the pulmonary artery with terminal assessments performed at 3, 28, 360, 540, 730, and 902 days. At 180 days, all remaining animals underwent catheterization, with an additional CardiaZn stent placed over a previous aortic stent in four subjects. All subjects received CT scans at 1 year.

Results

There were no stent migrations, evidence of vessel injury, angiographic obstruction, or stent fragment embolization. From 180 to 360 days, the pulmonary artery, sub-renal, and supra-iliac aortic stents increased in diameter by 18%, 24%, and 28%, on average, respectively. Simultaneously, the pulmonary and sub-renal aortic stents elongated by an average of 40%. All CardiaZn stents explanted from 28 through 902 days were completely endothelialized. Histopathology displayed moderate remodeling of the tunica media without loss of structural integrity or extension into the adventitia. MicroCT analysis showed loss of mass and structural integrity secondary to degradation resulting in stent cell disconnection, allowing for vessel growth by 9-12 months.

Conclusion

The CardiaZn stent provided vascular support for up to 9 months before safely degrading to allow for vascular growth. A clinical trial is planned to confirm safety and efficacy in children.

title: Fully biodegradable ventricular septal defect occluders: from biomaterials to clinical translation.
authorString: Yang L, Pang GY, Wang XJ, Wang RQ, Bai ZX, Zhang S, Liu SF, Song JW, Lu TY, Shan XH, Bai Y, Guo ZF, Qin YW, Zhu N.
abstractText: Ventricular septal defect (VSD) is the most prevalent congenital heart disease (CHD), which is approximately 20% of all congenital cardiac defects. Although transcatheter closure of VSD is a favorable alternative to traditional open-heart surgery, conventional nitinol-based occluders carry permanent risks of atrioventricular conduction disturbances, device erosion, and nickel allergy, which precluded regulatory approval in the United States for perimembranous VSD. Fully biodegradable occluders represent an attractive solution, offering equivalent closure efficacy while eliminating the long-term risks due to a permanent metallic implant. Owing to favorable endothelization-degradation kinetics, biocompatibility, and mechanical performance, polydioxanone (PDO) and poly-L-lactic acid (PLLA) have emerged as the superior framework and membrane materials, respectively. Clinical evidence from case series, retrospective cohort studies, and a multicenter randomized controlled trial suggests high procedural success and favorable short- to mid-term safety, with a low incidence of conduction disturbances following biodegradable VSD occluder implantation. In 2022, the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) of China has granted regulatory approval for the MemoSorb<sup>®</sup> device, which represents the first clinical available fully biodegradable VSD occluder. This review focuses on biomaterials science, structural design principles, preclinical animal studies, and the emerging clinical evidence of fully biodegradable VSD occluder.

title: A randomized study comparing plant sterol- and soluble fiber-enriched soymilk with plain soymilk in adults with elevated LDL cholesterol.
authorString: Buranapin S, Tejavanija S, Wongthanee A, Manosroi W.
abstractText:
Background

Lowering low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is an effective strategy to reduce coronary heart disease risk. Plant sterols/stanols, soluble fiber, and soy protein have each shown LDL-C-lowering effects. This study compared the effects of plant sterol-and soluble fiber-enriched soymilk (SFSM) versus plain soymilk (SM) on LDL-C over 8 weeks.

Methods

A total of 242 adults aged ≥ 18 years with hypercholesterolemia (LDL-C > 130 mg/dL), either untreated or receiving stable lipid-lowering therapy were randomized to receive either plain soymilk (SM; n = 119) or plant sterol- and soluble fiber-enriched soymilk (SFSM; n = 123), with two 180-mL packs consumed daily for 8 weeks. Three participants discontinued the assigned intervention during the study (SM, n = 1; SFSM, n = 2); all three attended the week-2 visit and contributed post-baseline laboratory data, but had no week-8 measurements. Both products provided 5 g soy protein per 180-mL serving; SFSM additionally contained 1 g free plant sterol and 5 g inulin (soluble fiber), with a total dietary fiber content of 5.8 g per serving, corresponding to daily intakes of 2 g free plant sterol and 11.6 g total fiber. Fasting plasma glucose and lipid profiles were measured at baseline and at weeks 2, 4, 6, and 8. Dietary intake and physical activity were monitored throughout the study. The intention-to-treat analysis included all 242 randomized participants.

Results

At week 8, SFSM group had a greater reduction in LDL-C than the SM group, with an adjusted between-group treatment effect of 5.5 mg/dL (95% CI 0.6 to 10.4, p = 0.028), favoring SFSM, after adjustment for baseline lipid values. No significant between-group differences were found in fasting plasma glucose, HDL-C, triglycerides, total cholesterol/HDL-C ratio, total energy intake, total fat intake, cholesterol intake, water consumption, or physical activity; however, fiber intake increased significantly more in the SFSM group.

Conclusions

These findings support the LDL-C-lowering benefit of plant sterol-and soluble fiber-enriched soymilk compared with plain soymilk over 8 weeks; however, secondary and subgroup findings should be interpreted cautiously because they were exploratory in nature. Trial registration Clinical Trials Registry Identifier: (NCT02459314) Retrospectively registered on May 15, 2015; first posted June 2, 2015. The study was conducted from April 2013 to April 2014. The original protocol date 22 October 2012 is provided as supplementary material.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Lucitanib in Advanced Thymic Carcinoma: A Randomized Phase II Trial.
authorString: Fang W, Zhou C, Wang C, Wu K, Fu J, Lin X, Zhang H, Chen J, Zhang P, Zhang Y, Tang P, Zheng Y, Liu Y, Zhi X, Gao Z, Fan Q, Cai H, Li F, Guo X, Zhang B, Mu R, Yu Z.
abstractText: Advanced thymic carcinoma is a rare, aggressive malignancy with limited treatment options after chemotherapy failure. This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (AL3810-202) aimed to evaluate lucitanib, a novel, orally potent tyrosine kinase inhibitor targeting VEGFR1‒3, FGFR1‒3, and PDGFRα/β in patients with advanced thymic carcinoma progressing after chemotherapy. Sixty-eight patients were randomized (2:1) to receive 10 mg lucitanib daily (n = 46) or placebo (n = 22). Although this study did not meet its primary endpoint of independent review committee (IRC)-assessed progression-free survival (PFS) (median 5.8 vs. 3.7 months; hazard ratio [HR]: 0.60; p = 0.1050), the prespecified log-rank test may have underestimated the treatment effect due to an observed non-proportional hazards pattern. Subsequent restricted mean survival time analysis demonstrated a statistically significant PFS benefit (p < 0.05), which was further supported by significantly prolonged investigator-assessed PFS (6.6 vs. 1.9 months; HR: 0.53; p = 0.0306). The most common grade 3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were hypertension (50%), proteinuria (15.2%), and thrombocytopenia (8.7%), with no grade 4/5 events. Considering the totality of the evidence and an acceptable safety profile, lucitanib may confer a meaningful clinical benefit for patients with advanced thymic carcinoma, warranting further investigation.

title: A Practical Treatment Platform Version 3.0 for Using Angiotensin Receptor Blocker-Based Single-Pill Combinations in Patients With Hypertension.
authorString: Tocci G, Burnier M, de la Sierra A, Grassi G, Narkiewicz K, Kreutz R, Tsioufis K, Volpe M.

journal.title: High blood pressure & cardiovascular prevention : the official journal of the Italian Society of Hypertension

abstractText: Elevated blood pressure (BP) is the leading cause of cardiovascular disease and a major contributor to mortality, affecting almost one third of the adult population worldwide. Despite strong scientific evidence, guidelines and multiple therapeutic options, many patients remain undertreated or uncontrolled, largely due to poor medication adherence and medical inertia. Complexity of multi-pill regimens contributes significantly to non-adherence, whereas single-pill combinations (SPCs) improve adherence and persistence, accelerate BP control, and promote better long-term outcomes than multiple combinations. Appropriate selection of SPC in individual hypertensive patients may be a difficult though very important task for physicians. Thus, development of tools that may facilitate use of SPC in clinical practice is desirable. Among renin-angiotensin system blockers, olmesartan (OM) has demonstrated sustained efficacy, favourable tolerability, both as monotherapy and in SPCs with amlodipine and/or hydrochlorothiazide, which are available in multiple dosages. The present OM-based platform builds on earlier frameworks and incorporates guidelines' updates complemented by a systematic review of available literature. This "3.0" proposal expands patient categorization to include comorbidities or complications often overlooked in clinical practice guidelines, providing a practical, evidence-based approach to support individualized hypertension management complementing guideline recommendations.

title: Cardiac perception and self-reported interoception in common mental health disorders: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Lester R, Jones A, Gillespie SM.
abstractText: Atypical interoception may represent a transdiagnostic marker for mental health difficulties. Reviews to date exploring the relationships between interoception and mental health have presented mixed findings, with a narrow focus on cardiac measures of interoception. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies that measured the association of cardiac perception and self-reported interoception with common mental health disorders, including anxiety, depression, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and obsessive-compulsive disorder, in clinical and non-clinical samples of adults. A total of 206 effect sizes from 57 articles (total N = 6,652) were eligible for inclusion in random effects meta-analyses. Overall, pooled associations showed no significant association of mental health difficulties with performance on the Heartbeat Counting Task (r = -.042), but a significant, negative association with Heart Rate Discrimination Task performance (r = -.137). Problems in adaptive interoceptive attention (r = -.183) but not sensing (r =.136), or interpretation (r = -.117), were associated with worse mental health symptomology, as was greater maladaptive interoceptive attention (r =.381). Moderator analyses showed that the size of the effect often varied between different mental health disorders, and there was some evidence of overly influential effect sizes as well as wide 95% prediction intervals. Our findings highlight the importance of methodological choices and potential differences between different performance-based tasks of cardiac interoception and different self-reported interoceptive dimensions. Our results show some support for interoception as a transdiagnostic marker for mental health difficulties that can support the development of evidence-based interventions.

title: The retrieved venous thrombus as a translational platform: a methodologic roadmap for venous immunothrombosis.
authorString: Galassi L, Rossi A, Pellegrino G, Azzahrani L, Meh L, Facchinetti F, Banfi C.
abstractText: Percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy is now widely used for iliofemoral deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) across several device platforms, and every procedure yields intact human thrombus that is routinely discarded. Whether this material can be developed into a translational resource linking thrombus biology to clinical outcome has not been systematically addressed. A narrative, non-systematic review was performed. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library were searched (January 2010 to August 2026) for studies addressing the biology, histopathology and translational analysis of mechanically retrieved venous thrombi, supplemented by reference-list, trial-registry and congress hand-searching. Published venous series remain small and largely confined to descriptive histology, disconnected from longitudinal outcomes. Intra-thrombus biology could address venous-specific questions that peripheral biomarkers and imaging alone cannot: post-thrombotic syndrome, incomplete recanalization, chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension and cancer-associated thrombosis. A device-agnostic framework is proposed, comprising structured intra-procedural sampling at the level of the case rather than the anatomical region, centralized specimen processing under harmonized quality standards, a tiered analytic pipeline anchored on quantitative immunohistochemistry, paired peripheral-biomarker collection, pre-specified hypotheses with feasibility-based sample sizes, and biobank infrastructure embedded in existing trial platforms. The equivalent programme in arterial thrombectomy supplies transferable methodology, subject to explicit boundary conditions. The retrieved venous thrombus is among the more underused translational specimens in vascular medicine. A standardized, registry-embedded characterization framework could accelerate progress toward precision venous thrombosis medicine.

title: The Epidemiology and Associated Factors of Ectopic Pregnancy in Saudi Arabia: A Literature Review.
authorString: Alkathiri M, Almousa A.
abstractText:
Background

Ectopic pregnancy (EP) is a serious maternal complication with a worldwide prevalence of about 2%. It is defined as the implantation of the product of conception outside the uterine cavity. Patients with EP may present with a wide range of clinical symptoms, including abdominal/pelvic pain, vaginal bleeding, missed menstrual cycle, and an empty uterine cavity on ultrasound. After diagnosing EPs, medical and/or surgical treatment options are available based on the patient's hemodynamic status, ectopic location, fetal cardiac activity, size of the gestational sac, level of β-HCG, and patient profile.

Objective

This narrative literature review aims to summarize published primary studies on the epidemiology and reported associated factors of EP in Saudi Arabia between 2000 and 2024.

Results

A total of 1342 EP cases were reported across the included studies. Reported prevalence estimates ranged from 0.23% to 1.20%. The reviewed studies were from different regions of the Kingdom, including Abha, Khamis Mushait, Yanbu, Makkah, Madina, Jeddah, Khobar, and Majmaah. The prevalence of EPs fluctuated between 2000 and 2019 and had three peaks: 1.13% (2012), 1.14% (2013), and 1.2% (2019). Multiple associated factors linked to EP were reported in this review, including a history of pelvic surgery, C-sections, previous EP, abortions, intrauterine contraceptive device (IUCD) use, and pelvic inflammatory diseases (PIDs).

Conclusions

EP is a serious complication that causes significant maternal morbidity and mortality and has a substantial burden on the healthcare system. In this review, eleven studies were reviewed regarding the epidemiology of EPs in the Kingdom. No clear pattern or trend in prevalence was identified, although the majority of studies reported lower EP rates than the worldwide prevalence. Several associated factors were reported across the included studies; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because most studies were retrospective and descriptive in nature.

title: Periodontitis and systemic disease: A clinical perspective.
authorString: Bellanti JA.
abstractText: Periodontitis is a common chronic inflammatory disease that has traditionally been considered primarily within the domain of dentistry. Increasing evidence, however, associates periodontitis with systemic inflammatory conditions, particularly atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Dysbiotic subgingival microbial communities, disruption of the periodontal epithelial barrier, transient bacteremia, microbial products, and locally generated inflammatory mediators provide biologically plausible pathways through which periodontal inflammation may influence systemic vascular biology. Epidemiologic and mechanistic studies support an association between periodontitis and cardiovascular disease, although direct causality has not been established. Importantly, periodontal treatment has been associated with improvement in endothelial function and reductions in selected systemic inflammatory biomarkers, but evidence that treatment prevents myocardial infarction, stroke, or cardiovascular mortality remains insufficient. For the practicing internist, the principal message is therefore both practical and appropriately cautious: Periodontal health should be recognized as one component of overall health, and closer collaboration between physicians and dental professionals may strengthen preventive care. This Perspective reviews the clinical evidence linking periodontitis with systemic disease, using cardiovascular disease as the principal example, and considers its implications for prevention, interdisciplinary care, and future research.

title: Estimated sdLDL-C/LDL-C Discordance Is Associated With Advanced Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome, Incident Cardiovascular Disease and Mortality: Evidence From Two Population-Based Cohorts.
authorString: Sun H, Cui R, Jiang L, Liu J, Wang G.
abstractText:
Background

sdLDL-C is a more atherogenic subfraction of LDL particles. We aimed to investigate the associations of sdLDL-C and its discordance with LDL-C with advanced stages, incident cardiovascular disease (CVD) and mortality among adults across the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome spectrum.

Methods

This study included adults from two cohorts: 16 992 participants from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES, 1999-2018) and 8252 from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS, 2011-2020) across CKM Stages 0-4. sdLDL-C was estimated (E-sdLDL-C) via Sampson's equation. Discordance was defined as an absolute E-sdLDL-C/LDL-C percentile difference of ≥ 10 percentiles. Logistic regression assessed advanced CKM, and Cox models evaluated associations with incident CVD in CHARLS and mortality in both cohorts. Survey-weighted analyses were applied in NHANES, and CHARLS models were fitted with community-level cluster-robust standard errors.

Results

Higher E-sdLDL-C at a given level of E-lbLDL-C and greater E-sdLDL-C/LDL-C discordance were each associated with increased advanced CKM prevalence across both cohorts (discordantly high vs. low in NHANES: OR: 2.89, 95% CI: 2.39-3.50). E-sdLDL-C at a given level of E-lbLDL-C was positively associated with incident CVD risk in CHARLS, whereas the discordance associations were attenuated after adjustment for baseline CKM stage. Each SD increment in discordance was associated with 15% higher all-cause and 20% higher cardiovascular mortality in NHANES, and 23% higher all-cause mortality in CHARLS.

Conclusions

E-sdLDL-C and its discordance with LDL-C are associated with advanced CKM, incident CVD and mortality, suggesting that E-sdLDL-C/LDL-C discordance may reflect LDL-related lipid heterogeneity associated with adverse CKM outcomes.

title: Time-Dependent Mortality Risk in Lean Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease During Long-Term Follow-Up.
authorString: Xie E, Bo Y, Yuan X, He X, Yang Z, Liu X, Shang Q, Zhang X, Yeo YH, Ji F.
abstractText:
Background and aim

The prognosis of lean metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remains controversial. We investigated the long-term prognosis of lean MASLD and its time-dependent associations with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality.

Methods

We analyzed 3568 participants with MASLD from the Third National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. Cox proportional hazards and Fine-Gray competing-risk models assessed all-cause and cardiovascular mortality. Because the proportional hazards assumption was violated for all-cause mortality, 10-year landmark and time-varying coefficient Cox analyses were performed. Restricted cubic splines (RCS) evaluated the association between body mass index (BMI) and early all-cause mortality, and subgroup analyses identified high-risk populations.

Results

During a median 27.7-year follow-up, lean MASLD was associated with higher all-cause mortality within 0-10 years (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 1.68; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.29-2.20), but not thereafter (adjusted HR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.87-1.25). No significant association between lean MASLD and cardiovascular mortality was observed during either pre-landmark (adjusted subdistribution HR [sHR], 1.45; 95% CI, 0.95-2.22) or post-landmark (adjusted sHR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.69-1.36) in the overall population. Time-specific HR demonstrated a gradual attenuation of the excess mortality association over follow-up. RCS demonstrated a nonlinear U-shaped association between BMI and early all-cause mortality. Excess early mortality risks were particularly evident among males aged ≥ 60 years and participants with baseline FIB-4 ≥ 1.30.

Conclusions

Lean MASLD conferred a time-dependent excess risk of all-cause mortality, predominantly within the first decade of follow-up, but was not robustly associated with cardiovascular mortality in the overall population. Older males and patients with elevated FIB-4 scores represented high-risk phenotypes.

title: The PHLPP paradox revisited: from canonical AKT phosphatases to signaling pseudoenzymes in human disease.
authorString: Shaaban EM, Elnaggar MF, Abdelgawad A, Sedeek M, Estfanous S, Eladl O.
abstractText: PHLPP1 and PHLPP2 (pleckstrin homology-domain leucine-rich-repeat protein phosphatases) are multidomain signaling proteins that have been associated with the regulation of AKT phosphorylation in several cellular contexts. PHLPP1 and PHLPP2 have historically been classified as PP2C-family phosphatases that terminate AKT signaling. Recent biochemical evidence challenges this interpretation for PHLPP2, which showed no detectable phosphatase activity in vitro and contained a single Zn<sup>2</sup>⁺ ion in its catalytic center, raising the possibility that it functions as a signaling pseudophosphatase or scaffold. While traditionally characterized as tumor suppressors, emerging evidence reveals that PHLPP isoforms possess distinct, non-redundant roles at the interface of metabolism, cardiovascular integrity, and regulated cell death (RCD). This functional diversity introduces a complex biochemical paradox, in which the tight regulation of these phosphatases dictates divergent pathological and protective outcomes depending on the cellular microenvironment. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of the structural divergence between PHLPP1 and PHLPP2, emphasizing how the PHLPP1-specific N-terminal extension and PDZ-binding motif contribute to spatial signaling specificity and preferential targeting of AKT2/3, while PHLPP2 exhibits preference toward AKT1/3, reflecting isoform-dependent differences in regulatory architecture. The review asks how two decades of cellular and disease evidence should be reinterpreted if PHLPP proteins, particularly PHLPP2, function as signaling pseudoenzymes or scaffolds rather than conventional AKT phosphatases. Finally, we evaluate the therapeutic landscape, focusing on small-molecule inhibitors and cell-penetrating peptides designed to modulate the PHLPP-AKT interface as a programmable node for dual-target therapies.

title: Ultra-early diagnosis recently developments of acute myocardial infarction: Emerging biomarkers and advanced sensing technologies.
authorString: Wang X, Du J, Zhou W, Wang C, Han X, Yang X, Yang H, Liu Y, Liu T, Yu F, Wu Y.

journal.title: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry

abstractText: Currently, myocardial infarction is commonly detected via traditional biomarker analysis, electrocardiography, and echocardiography. In general, conventional clinical approaches are limited by insufficient early-stage sensitivity and time-consuming procedures, thereby delaying therapeutic interventions. To address the above-mentioned drawbacks, this review systematically summarizes recent advances in both ultra-early biomarkers and novel high-sensitivity detection platforms. A panel of ultra-early biomarkers with high sensitivity and specificity (e.g., GPBB, cMyC, cfDNA, MPO, D-dimer, miRNAs, and lncRNAs) is explicitly identified in this review. Recent progress in nano-based, graphene-based, and chemical biosensors for biomarker detection is further elaborated. The application of these biosensors delivers amplified signal outputs, enhanced sensitivity, shortened detection time, multiplex detection capability, and successful miniaturization of detection devices. This review also analyzes the integration of artificial intelligence models with conventional diagnostic modalities (electrocardiography, echocardiography, myocardial perfusion imaging) and gold-standard diagnostic methods (biomarker testing, coronary angiography, cardiac magnetic resonance, coronary computed tomography). Such integrated analytical strategies enable objective, rapid, and early diagnosis. When embedde into wearable monitoring devices, these technologies support non-invasive and continuous real-time monitoring and generate preemptive clinical alerts with ultra-high signal sensitivity. Ultimately, this article establishes a comprehensive framework for the ultra-early diagnosis of myocardial infarction by integrating screened ultra-early biomarkers and innovative high-sensitivity detection techniques.

title: Role of apoptosis and necroptosis in cardiac dysfunction during the development of heart disease.
authorString: Adameova A, Dhalla NS.

journal.title: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology

abstractText: Cell death plays a well established role in the pathogenesis of heart disease, with increasing evidence highlighting the complexity and plasticity of different underlying molecular pathways in both cardiomyocytes and non-cardiomyocytes. The signal transduction mechanisms of cell death do not operate as isolated linear cascades but rather as interconnected regulatory networks governing distinct cell death modalities. Among them, apoptosis and necroptosis represent the principal forms of caspase-dependent and caspase-independent cell death, respectively. Although mechanistically linked, these forms of cell death are morphologically and immunogenically distinct. Importantly, these pathways may be activated simultaneously, shaping both the extent of cardiomyocyte loss and the immunogenic properties of dying cells through the release of damage-associated molecular patterns. The outcome of cell death associated myocardial damage is highly disease-specific, biological sex- and context-dependent, and is determined by factors such as the expression levels, post-translational modifications, and interactions of cell survival and cell death signal transduction proteins. Elucidating these mechanisms in cardiomyocytes, including the contribution of secondary signaling molecules derived from non-apoptotic cells and non-cardiomyocytes, is critical for advancing our understanding of cardiac dysfunction in heart disease as well as for the development of targeted therapeutic strategies. Furthermore, the relative contribution of individual cell death modalities in various types of heart diseases warrants particular attention, as shifts in their balance during disease progression may significantly influence the severity of cardiac dysfunction. Since several pathologic factors are involved in the genesis of heart disease, it is suggested that cell death due to apoptosis and necroptosis may be one of these mechanisms associated with the development of cardiac dysfunction in the failing heart.

title: Outcome-specific associations of remnant cholesterol with myocardial infarction and stroke across traditional risk factor burden.
authorString: Tian R, Chen S, Li J, Xia X, Zhang X, Wu S, Wang A.
abstractText: Remnant cholesterol (RC) is considered a contributor to residual cardiovascular risk, but whether its associations with specific cardiovascular outcomes vary according to the burden of traditional cardiovascular risk factors (CVRFs) remains uncertain. We investigated the associations of RC with myocardial infarction (MI) and stroke in relation to cumulative CVRF burden. We conducted a prospective analysis of 84,806 participants from the Kailuan cohort (baseline 2006) without prior cardiovascular disease. CVRF burden was categorized as 0, 1, 2, or ≥ 3 according to current smoking, overweight (BMI ≥ 24 kg/m²), hypertension, and diabetes. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) for incident MI and stroke through 2021, and interaction terms were used to assess potential effect modification by CVRF burden. During a median follow-up of 15 years, 1,690 MI and 6,416 stroke events occurred. Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest RC quartile was associated with higher risks of MI (HR, 1.59; 95% CI, 1.37-1.83) and stroke (HR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.11-1.28). In supplementary subtype analyses, the stroke association was mainly observed for ischemic rather than hemorrhagic stroke. The RC-MI association appeared stronger across higher CVRF-burden categories (highest vs. lowest quartile HRs: 1.16, 1.52, 1.67, and 1.80 for 0, 1, 2, and ≥ 3 CVRFs, respectively), whereas the corresponding stroke association was attenuated (HRs: 1.44, 1.29, 1.21, and 1.03). After noncardiovascular death was treated as a competing event, the stroke interaction was attenuated and no longer statistically significant (P for interaction=0.21). In this large prospective cohort, RC was associated with higher risks of both MI and stroke, with stronger and more consistent associations observed for MI. The pattern of association differed across levels of CVRF burden, suggesting that the clinical interpretation of RC may benefit from outcome-specific and risk-context-specific assessment.

title: In-Hospital and One-Year Outcomes After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Chronic Coronary Occlusion in Octogenarians.
authorString: Amoey D, Elbasha K, Samy M, Landt M, Kurniadi A, Schiopu O, Allali A, Saad M, Hofmann FJ, Frank D, Toelg R, Richardt G, Fichtlscherer S, Nef H, Mankerious N.
abstractText:
Introduction

Older patients often present with complex coronary artery disease alongside multiple comorbidities. There is limited data on the outcomes of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for chronic total occlusion (CTO) in octogenarians. We aim to investigate the in-hospital and 1-year outcomes following successful CTO-PCI in octogenarians.

Methods

Consecutive patients who had successful CTO-PCI at a single center between 01.2017 and 12.2022 were divided into two groups: octogenarians (age ≥ 80 and < 90 years, n = 123) and a control group (age < 80 years, n = 612). Periprocedural complications, in-hospital major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), and 1-year target lesion failure (TLF) were investigated.

Results

Octogenarians had a higher prevalence of arterial hypertension (96.7% vs. 91.2%, p = 0.036), atrial fibrillation (28.5% vs. 12.1%, p < 0.001), and chronic kidney disease (CKD) (34.1% vs. 16.5%, p < 0.001) compared to younger counterparts. The rate of failed CTO recanalization was higher in octogenarians (18.5% vs. 8.2%, p < 0.001). Incidence of in-hospital MACCE and periprocedural complications was comparable between the study groups, except for a numerically higher in-hospital mortality in octogenarians (2.4% vs. 0.8%, p = 0.114), and a higher incidence of contrast-induced nephropathy (CIN) (11.4% vs. 4.9%, p = 0.006). At 1 year, TLF did not differ significantly between the study arms (16.2% vs. 12.3%, aHR 1.52; CI 0.81-2.84, p = 0.191). Notably, higher cardiac mortality rates were observed in the octogenarian arm (7.6% vs. 2.7%, HR 2.82; CI 1.13-7.08, p = 0.027).

Conclusion

Despite numerically higher in-hospital mortality in octogenarians, CTO-PCI in those patients was performed with comparable periprocedural, and acute adverse outcomes, as well as 1-year TLF, to their younger counterparts. Octogenarians remain inherently at a higher long-term mortality risk. Graphical Abstract available for this article.

title: Analysis of mRNA and microRNA profiles in ischemic cardiomyopathy with LVAD support.
authorString: Dhar K, Basma H, Qiu F, Um JY, Anderson DR, Lowes BD.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiac remodeling after myocardial infarction is common, and recovery from end stage ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) with left ventricular assist device (LVAD) therapy remains rare. Our goal was to identify micro-RNAs (miRNAs) associated with ICM and to evaluate responses to LVAD therapy to better understand epigenetic mechanisms regulating differential gene expression (DGE).

Methods

RNAs were isolated from human myocardial tissues of ICM (n = 11) pre- and post-LVAD placement, along with non-failing (NF) controls (n = 6). Expressions were quantified by utilizing a targeted cardiac panel for mRNA and the nCounter Human v2 miRNA panel for miRNA. Ingenuity pathway analysis (IPA) was performed with DGE. Targeted gene expression profile was validated by performing mRNA-seq.

Results

Compared to NF controls, 33 in pre- and 32 genes in post-LVAD were differentially expressed. IPA of mRNA revealed that signals of inflammatory cytokines and blood pressure disorder were activated in pre-LVAD ICM, and norepinephrine and cells migration were triggered in post-LVAD ICM compared to NF controls. Inflammatory response and apoptosis of cardiomyocytes were inhibited in post compared to pre-LVAD. Relative to NF controls, 195 in pre- and 120 miRNAs in post-LVAD ICM were differentially expressed. IPA of miRNA showed that apoptosis and fibrosis of the heart were stimulated both in pre- and post-LVAD ICM. RNA-seq results validated the targeted gene expression.

Conclusions

In ICM, miRNA expression is linked to apoptosis and fibrosis pathways. These changes persist in post-LVAD therapy and contribute to ongoing changes in mRNA expression associated with Heart failure.

title: External Ventricular Drainage for Refractory Intracranial Hypertension in Traumatic Brain Injury: Efficacy, Safety, and Outcomes.
authorString: Baucher G, Troude L, Lemnos L, Singh A, Marécal L, Duclos G, Zieleskiewicz L, Leone M, Roche PH.
abstractText:
Introduction

External ventricular drainage (EVD) is commonly used to manage refractory intracranial hypertension following traumatic brain injury (TBI), yet its efficacy, timing, and prognostic value remain uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the short-term efficacy of EVD in controlling intracranial hypertension in TBI patients.

Patients and methods

We conducted a retrospective, observational, single-center study including consecutive adult patients with TBI who underwent EVD placement for refractory intracranial hypertension between 2020 and 2024. Demographic, clinical, radiological, surgical, and ICP data were collected. Trauma severity was assessed using the ISS and the SOFA score. EVD efficacy was defined as a sustained reduction in mean ICP below 20 mmHg for at least 24 hours. Functional outcome was assessed at 1 year using the Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS).

Results

Fifty-three patients were included (51±18 years; 75% male). Median ICP significantly decreased after EVD placement (30 [25-35] vs. 15 [10-35] mmHg; p<0.01). Sustained ICP control was achieved within the first 24 hours in 25 patients (47%), whereas 28 (53%) did not reach control, including 8 patients (29%) with transient improvement. Patients with uncontrolled ICP had higher pre-EVD ICP values and greater injury severity scores. Normal basal cisterns were more frequent in the controlled group. One-year mortality was 70%, and 32% of the patients with controlled ICP had a GOS 4 at 12 months. EVD-related complications occurred in four patients (8%).

Conclusion

EVD significantly reduces ICP in selected TBI patients, but sustained control occurs in fewer than half of cases and appears associated with baseline injury severity. Prospective studies are needed.

title: [The role of clinical inertia in the complex care of patients suffering from heart failure].
authorString: Schäffer PP, Forrai Z, Gergely TG, Boldizsár EM, Andréka P, Piróth Z, Bánfi-Bacsárdi F, Muk B.
abstractText: Inertia refers to a lack of energy or helplessness; in the context of heart failure, clinical inertia can be understood primarily as the failure to initiate or optimize therapies known to reduce morbidity and mortality in patients not on optimized therapy. The aim of this review article is to provide an overview of the most recent guidelines and recommendations relevant to the topic, summarize the available international literature, and present the results of practical interventions that may also be feasibly implemented in Hungary. Heart failure remains a condition with an unfavorable prognosis; however, the use of modern, optimal, comprehensive, guideline-directed medical therapies may confer substantial prognostic benefit. In everyday clinical practice, clinical inertia is one of the main barriers to effective treatment, and the need to address it has also been emphasized in recent position statements of the European Society of Cardiology. The integration of multidisciplinary care, structured patient education, and targeted interventions is of fundamental importance in overcoming clinical inertia, optimizing treatment adherence, and improving long-term outcomes. Close follow-up and rapid up-titration of guideline-directed medical therapy in eligible patients are of particular importance and may significantly reduce the relative risk of heart failure hospitalization and all-cause mortality. The use of telemedicine during follow-up, together with the broader exploitation of digital opportunities, provides contemporary clinicians with a range of new possibilities. Based on real-world data, interventions that favorably influence clinical inertia can also be successfully implemented in Hungary, yielding significant clinical benefit for patients with heart failure. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(43): 1719-1729.

title: Sepsis-associated efferocytosis deficiency: Molecular mechanisms and novel therapeutic targets.
authorString: Qin X, Zhong A, Zhou Z, Song X, Song Y, Xu S.
abstractText: Despite advances in critical care, sepsis remains a leading cause of mortality driven by a profoundly dysregulated host immune response. Increasingly, defective efferocytosis-the fundamental physiological process for clearing dead cells-has been identified as a critical catalyst in sepsis pathophysiology. Under normal conditions, efferocytosis resolves inflammation and maintains tissue homeostasis. However, during sepsis, the efferocytotic capacity of phagocytes is severely paralyzed. This clearance failure results in a massive accumulation of apoptotic and necrotic cellular debris within the tissue microenvironment, triggering an unabated release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs). Consequently, this substrate overload sustains a self-amplifying inflammatory storm that accelerates tissue injury and precipitates multiple organ failure. In this review, we dissect the diverse modalities of programmed cell death in sepsis and map the subsequent breakdown of the core, multi-step efferocytotic machinery. We systematically explore the molecular basis of efferocytosis failure across distinct organ-specific complications, including acute lung injury, sepsis-associated encephalopathy, acute kidney injury, and septic cardiomyopathy. Finally, we evaluate emerging targeted therapies aimed at restoring efferocytotic efficiency, highlighting a crucial conceptual shift from primarily suppressing inflammation to actively promoting its resolution and repairing host immunity.

title: Cardiorespiratory Arrest in the Context of Graves' Disease: A Rare Presentation.
authorString: Marques M, Couto J, Martins Vale M, Pinto P, Felgueiras P.
abstractText: Thyroid storm is the most severe and life-threatening expression of thyrotoxicosis, and its diagnosis remains clinical. Although sinus tachycardia and atrial fibrillation dominate its cardiovascular manifestations, malignant ventricular arrhythmias are rare, and cardiorespiratory arrest as the presenting manifestation of Graves' disease has been reported only in a limited number of cases. We report the case of a 44-year-old man with a one-week history of symptoms consistent with hyperthyroidism who suffered a witnessed out-of-hospital cardiorespiratory arrest with ventricular fibrillation as the initial rhythm. Return of spontaneous circulation was achieved after three defibrillations, and urgent coronary angiography showed no obstructive coronary artery disease. Laboratory evaluation revealed severe thyrotoxicosis with positive thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)-receptor antibodies, and thyroid ultrasound findings supported the diagnosis of Graves' disease. Thyroid storm was suspected and treated empirically, but the diagnosis could not be confirmed: the Burch-Wartofsky score reached the diagnostic threshold only when post-arrest coma was included, and the Japan Thyroid Association criteria were not met. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and an ajmaline provocation test did not identify structural heart disease, myocarditis, or a Brugada pattern. Thyroid hormone excess was therefore considered the most likely precipitant of the arrhythmia, although causality cannot be proven. The patient was maintained on antithyroid therapy, and a subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was implanted for secondary prevention following an individualized risk-benefit assessment. This case highlights the importance of considering thyrotoxicosis in the etiological workup of unexplained cardiac arrest. When a clearly established and reversible cause of the arrhythmia cannot be confirmed, management, including the decision on defibrillator implantation, should be based on an individualized risk-benefit assessment.

title: Characterising differential maturation of stem cell-derived islets in mice: Graft function and transcriptomic analysis.
authorString: Sullivan R, Gatward LFD, Hong TW, Lyu Z, Whines WTB, Duff C, Arora R, Lonsane A, Zhao M, Salem V, King AJF, Jones PM, Persaud SJ.

journal.title: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association

abstractText:
Aims

Stem cell-derived islets (SC-islets) offer the potential to revolutionise type 1 diabetes treatment. However, functional maturation in vivo is variable, suggesting that specific, but as-yet undefined, environmental cues are critical. We aimed to identify pathways associated with SC-islet in vivo maturation in mice, assess early functional markers of this, and determine whether a hyperglycaemic graft environment impairs this.

Methods

Mice transplanted with 800 SC-islets but exhibiting differing glycaemic outcomes (cured, semi-cured, uncured) were selected and glucose tolerance and human C-peptide concentrations over time were measured. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of the graft from the cured mouse was compared with in vitro-maintained SC-islets. The impact of hyperglycaemia on in vivo maturation was assessed by comparing mouse recipients of SC-islet grafts which were either hyperglycaemic or normoglycaemic for 1 month post-transplantation.

Results

Superior SC-islet in vivo maturation was broadly associated with progressive improvements in C-peptide and glucose tolerance.
