In vivo maturation was associated with a distinct transcriptomic pattern (including increased MAFA and INS expression) compared with SC-islets maintained in vitro. Finally, a hyperglycaemic post-transplant environment did not affect long-term SC-islet maturation, with no impairment in plasma human C-peptide seen at 6 months, and no changes in gene expression of β-cell maturity markers after SC-islets were transplanted into diabetic mice.

Conclusion

Longitudinal plasma C-peptide and glucose tolerance can be used to characterise in vivo SC-islet maturation, which is associated with transcriptomic changes not observed in vitro. Additionally, elevated blood glucose does not impair long-term functional maturation. These findings support the importance of in vivo cues for SC-islet maturation to inform future preclinical studies.

title: Association Between Traditional Cerebrovascular Risk Factor Burden and Ultrasound-Based Phenotyping of Carotid Atherosclerotic Plaques.
authorString: Li F, Bo F, Jin X.
abstractText:
Objective

To investigate the association between traditional cerebrovascular risk factor burden and ultrasound-based carotid plaque phenotyping.

Method

This single-center cross-sectional study included 486 patients with carotid plaques detected by ultrasound. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with plaque instability, and multiple linear regression was used to examine determinants of plaque maximum thickness and cross-sectional area.

Results

Among 486 patients, 170 (35.0%) had unstable plaques. In the fully adjusted model, male sex (OR = 1.66, 95% CI: 1.06-2.61, p = 0.028), higher BMI (OR = 1.08, 95% CI: 1.01-1.16, p = 0.022), smoking (OR = 1.72, 95% CI: 1.11-2.70, p = 0.015), alcohol consumption (OR = 1.56, 95% CI: 1.01-2.44, p = 0.044), coronary heart disease (OR = 2.63, 95% CI: 1.56-4.48, p < 0.001), and stenosis severity (moderate: OR = 2.69, 95% CI: 1.64-4.42, p < 0.001; severe: OR = 6.89, 95% CI: 3.03-15.81, p < 0.001) were independently associated with plaque vulnerability. Adding clinical and imaging variables significantly improved model discrimination (AUC: 0.749 vs. 0.787; likelihood ratio test: p = 0.003). The diabetes-hyperlipidemia interaction term was significant (OR = 3.30, 95% CI: 1.24-8.79, p = 0.017), suggesting a synergistic effect. Fasting blood glucose (FBG), analyzed as a continuous variable, was independently associated with greater plaque thickness (β = 0.08, 95% CI: 0.01-0.15, p = 0.036) and cross-sectional area (β = 0.70, 95% CI: 0.25-1.16, p = 0.003). Restricted cubic spline analysis further revealed U-shaped dose-response relationships between both FBG and LDL-C with plaque cross-sectional area (P-nonlinear = 0.001 for both), with inflection points at approximately 6.6 and 3.0 mmol/L, respectively.

Conclusion

Male sex, higher BMI, smoking, alcohol consumption, coronary heart disease, and stenosis severity were independently associated with carotid plaque instability. Diabetes and hyperlipidemia exhibited a significant synergistic effect. Diabetes was associated with increased plaque volume. These findings suggest that risk assessment should focus on cumulative risk burden rather than isolated indicators.

title: Longitudinal effects of CGRP-targeting migraine therapies on blood pressure and body mass index: A 12-month retrospective analysis.
authorString: Phan P, Keith S, Li M, Hass R, Hsieh WJ, Marmura M, Yuan H.
abstractText:
Objective

To compare blood pressure (BP) and body mass index (BMI) trajectories associated with individual calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP)-targeting migraine therapies versus matched CGRP-unexposed controls.

Background

CGRP is a potent vasodilator with established roles in vascular homeostasis and metabolic regulation. Postmarketing surveillance identified BP elevations in erenumab-treated patients, prompting a U.S. Food and Drug Administration label update; however, comparative longitudinal data across CGRP monoclonal antibodies and gepants remain limited. Real-world evidence is needed to characterize medication-specific cardiovascular and metabolic effects in clinical practice.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study using structured electronic health record data from the Jefferson Headache Center in Philadelphia, PA, USA (2018 to 2025). Adults initiating erenumab, fremanezumab, galcanezumab, atogepant, or preventive rimegepant were compared with propensity score-matched patients receiving migraine care without CGRP-targeting therapy. Twelve-month systolic BP (SBP), diastolic BP (DBP), and BMI trajectories were evaluated.

Results

A total of 6361 patients were included (1892 controls; 4469 CGRP-treated; 80.4% female; mean age 45.6 ± 15.3 years). Controls demonstrated a positive within-group SBP trajectory (0.16 mmHg/month; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.06 to 0.27) and BMI trajectory (0.022 kg/m2/month; 95% CI 0.004 to 0.040) but not DBP trajectory (0.06 mmHg/month; 95% CI -0.02 to 0.14). Among CGRP-treated groups, only erenumab showed a positive within-group SBP trajectory (0.11 mmHg/month; 95% CI 0.02 to 0.20); however, the difference in slope between erenumab and controls was not significant (-0.05 mmHg/month; 95% CI -0.19 to 0.09). Compared with controls, atogepant (-0.38 mmHg/month; 95% CI -0.61 to -0.15), fremanezumab (-0.27 mmHg/month; 95% CI -0.42 to -0.11), and galcanezumab (-0.31 mmHg/month; 95% CI -0.46 to -0.16) demonstrated more negative SBP trajectories. For DBP, only atogepant showed a more negative trajectory than controls (-0.18 mmHg/month; 95% CI -0.32 to -0.04). For BMI, both atogepant (-0.113 kg/m2/month; 95% CI -0.159 to -0.067) and erenumab (-0.031 kg/m2/month; 95% CI -0.053 to -0.008) had more negative trajectories compared to controls.

Conclusion

In this single-center study, CGRP-targeting therapies were not associated with greater BP increases than matched controls. Cardiometabolic trajectories varied by medication, with generally small BP differences and a robust BMI reduction with atogepant. These findings do not support a uniform adverse cardiometabolic class effect, though prospective studies with systematic monitoring are needed to confirm long-term clinical significance.

title: Mitigation Strategies: A Standardized Multimodal Pathway to Reduce the Severity of Clinically Relevant Pancreatic Fistula After Pancreaticoduodenectomy.
authorString: Casadei C, Zucchini V, Giuliani T, Solaini L, Pacilio CA, La Barba G, Di Gioia P, Cucchetti A, Ercolani G.
abstractText: BackgroundPancreaticoduodenectomy (PD) carries significant morbidity, primarily due to clinically relevant postoperative pancreatic fistula (CR-POPF). This study investigated the clinical impact of a multimodal mitigation strategy in patients undergoing PD, encompassing prehabilitation, standardized surgical techniques, and optimized postoperative management. The secondary aim was to identify factors associated with grade C POPF.MethodsA single-center retrospective analysis was conducted using a prospective database of 520 patients who underwent pancreatic surgery at our hospital between January 2016 and December 2025. One hundred eighty-four patients who underwent PD were selected and divided into two cohorts using 2022 as a cutoff, the year in which our multimodal mitigation strategy was introduced.ResultsIn the after-2022 cohort, a significant reduction in CR-POPF was observed (39% vs 55%, P = .036), with specific decrease in grade C POPF cases (5% vs 23%, P < .001). A statistically significant reduction in PPH was also observed in the after-2022 cohort (3% vs 17%, P < .001). Furthermore, in after-2022 cohort, there were a reduction of reoperation rate (8% vs 25%, P = .001) and LOS (23.0 days vs 14.5 days, P < .001). For the secondary aim, the multivariate analysis identified the after-2022 period and the occurrence of cardiac and pulmonary complications as factors associated with grade C POPF (respectively P < .001, P = .017 and P < .001).ConclusionsThis study highlights the potential of a structured, multi-level mitigation strategy in improving outcomes after pancreatoduodenectomy, in particular, the severity of pancreatic fistula and its consequences.

title: Mesenchymal stromal cell-derived extracellular vesicles improve islet β-cell metabolic function via miRNA-mediated regulation of Ankyrin-B expression.
authorString: Hong TW, Arora R, Sullivan R, Lyu Z, Whines WTB, Gatward LFD, Hubber EL, Huang TC, King AJF, Persaud SJ, Jones PM.

journal.title: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association

abstractText:
Aims

Mesenchymal stromal-cell-derived extracellular vesicles (MSC-EVs) improve islet function, which may be mediated in part through the delivery of microRNAs (miRNAs) to β-cells. To investigate the underlying mechanisms, we identified the most abundant MSC-EV miRNAs, their relative transfer to β-cells and the extent to which Ankyrin-B (Ank2) may represent a downstream target mediating the beneficial effects of EVs on islet function.

Methods

Mouse islets were treated with MSC-EVs, and changes in islet miRNAs were assessed using small RNAseq. miR-21a-5p showed the highest content, and subsequent bioinformatic analysis identified Ank2 as one of its predicted target genes. Expression levels of Ank2 mRNA were assessed by bulkRNA sequencing, while Ank2 protein was quantified by immunoblotting. Knockdown of Ank2 by siRNA was used to evaluate its role in islet function. Cell viability was measured using live/dead staining, oxygen consumption was quantified with a Seahorse analyser, and glucose-stimulated insulin secretion was determined by radioimmunoassay.

Results

MSC-EV treatment of islets was associated with elevated β-cell miR-21a-5p mRNA levels. Bioinformatic and experimental analyses identified Ank2 as a predicted downstream target of miR-21a-5p. Treatment of mouse islets with MSC-EVs was associated with increased Ank2 mRNA and protein expression, which was accompanied by improved β-cell metabolic function and enhanced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. Ank2 knockdown caused a significant reduction in β-cell ATP-coupled respiration.

Conclusions

These findings identify a novel miRNA-mediated mechanism underlying the beneficial effects of MSC-EVs on islet function and support the development of MSC-EV-based cell-free strategies to enhance islet function for diabetes therapies.

title: Restoring Endothelial Mitochondrial Homeostasis With a Bioactive Nanoshield Promotes Vascular Regeneration on Cardiovascular Implants.
authorString: Liu X, Zhang W, Liu L, Gui L, Qin Y, Yang X, Zhang L, Wang C, Hu J, Guo G, Jiang Q, Wang J, Yang L, Zhang B, Wang Y.
abstractText: Defective endothelial regeneration constitutes a fundamental barrier to durable vascular repair. By integrating single cell RNA-sequencing data from rat carotid balloon injury with ultrastructural and histological evidence from rabbit stented arteries, we identified mitochondrial disorganization and dysfunction as common features of injured endothelial cells. Guided by these findings, we developed a poly(citrate-polyglycol-procyanidin) (PCGP) nanoshield to couple mitochondrial protection with anticoagulant and immunoregulatory functions for cardiovascular devices. PCGP preserved mitochondrial integrity, restored endothelial metabolic homeostasis, and rescued the regenerative phenotype of endothelial cells under oxidative stress. In rabbit arterial stent models, this intervention reactivated the PI3K/AKT/eNOS-nitric oxide axis, accelerated functional re-endothelialization, and markedly suppressed neointimal hyperplasia. Collectively, these findings support restoration of endothelial mitochondrial homeostasis as an important mechanistic axis associated with vascular repair.

title: Histone Lactylation Drives WNK1 Expression to Promote Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma Progression Through Histone H3 Ser10 Phosphorylation.
authorString: Yan M, Fang S, Song Y, Zhang L, Zhao K, Wang Z, Shao Y, Liu M, Jia X, Guo Q, Lee MH, Jin G, Dong Z.
abstractText: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) lacks effective targeted therapies, and how metabolic reprogramming drives oncogenic signaling remains poorly defined. Here, we identify histone H3 lysine 23 lactylation (H3K23la) as a key epigenetic mediator linking lactate accumulation to tumor progression. H3K23la is upregulated in ESCC and correlates with poor prognosis. Mechanistically, H3K23la promotes WNK lysine deficient protein kinase 1 (WNK1) transcription, which increases histone H3 Ser10 phosphorylation (p-H3S10) and enhances AKT transcription, thereby driving PI3K-AKT signaling. This defines a lactate-H3K23la-WNK1-p-H3S10-AKT axis connecting metabolism to oncogenic signaling. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of WNK1 by CD03017 disrupts this pathway and suppresses tumor growth in vitro and in patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models. In conclusion, our findings define a metabolic-epigenetic-signaling axis in ESCC and establish WNK1 as a potential therapeutic target downstream of histone lactylation.

title: The Pesticide Pyrethroid Metabolite 3-Phenoxybenzoic Acid (3-PBA) Impairs Human Cardiac Na<sub>v</sub>1.5 and Action Potential Depolarization.
authorString: de Lima Conceição MR, Marques LP, da Silva Alcantara F, de Morais RLT, Fogaça-Santos V, Orts DJB, Pesquero JB, de Souza DS, Roman-Campos D.
abstractText: Pyrethroid insecticides (PYRs) are widely used worldwide, and their primary metabolite, 3-phenoxybenzoic acid (3-PBA), serves as a near-ubiquitous biomarker of human exposure to PYRs. While epidemiological data consistently link urinary 3-PBA to increased cardiometabolic risk and coronary heart disease, the underlying electrophysiological mechanisms of its direct potential cardiotoxicity remain unexplored. Parent PYRs are known to exert cardiotoxic effects by enhancing the late sodium current (I<sub>Na-L</sub>) and inducing arrhythmia, but the direct effect of 3-PBA on heart excitability has not been previously investigated. This study demonstrates that 3-PBA interacts with human cardiac Na<sub>v</sub>1.5 expressed in Human Embryonic Kidney (HEK293) cells, and significantly increases I<sub>Na-L</sub> in a concentration-dependent manner with an EC<sub>50</sub> of 51.3 ± 5.1 µM. The metabolite does not alter the voltage dependence of activation and inactivation, but it significantly delays the recovery from inactivation of the peak sodium current. In human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (CM-hiPSCs) and adult rat ventricular myocytes, 3-PBA reduced maximal depolarization rate (dV/dt), indicating impaired depolarization dynamics and reduced peak sodium current. At the organ level, acute exposure in isolated rat hearts did not significantly alter standard ECG parameters. Collectively, these findings suggest that 3-PBA is not electrophysiologically inert but directly modulates cardiac sodium channel function, although at supraphysiological concentration. This provides new evidence of the biological activity of 3-PBA and suggests that its cardiotoxic potential may become clinically relevant under conditions of high dose and chronic exposure or in susceptible populations.

title: Preventive Effect of Smoking Cessation on Diabetes Onset: A Target Trial Emulation Approach.
authorString: Yamamoto S, Okada H, Shinozaki T, Kasahara K, Kuramoto N, Ichikawa T, Nakajima H, Hashimoto Y, Sano A, Ushigome E, Nakanishi N, Hamaguchi M, Murata H, Kurogi K, Tsuda E, Yoshida N, Ito M, Fukui M.
abstractText:
Aims

Smoking cessation may transiently increase diabetes risk through weight gain, but its temporal trajectory remains unclear. We evaluated the long-term effect of smoking cessation on incident diabetes.

Materials and methods

We conducted a target trial emulation using a sequential-cohort design with repeated annual enrollment. Using annual health checkup data of Japanese employees from 2008 to 2022, we newly enrolled, at each annual assessment, and started follow-up individuals aged 40 years or older who were currently smoking and free of diabetes. Inverse probability weighting was used to adjust for baseline confounding in every sequential cohort. We estimated cumulative risks for quit-smoking and persistent-smoking groups, and their differences and ratios.

Results

From 52 880 unique participants, a total of 331 701 participants were followed-up in the sequential cohorts, with a mean (standard deviation) age of 49.1 (5.7) years, and 25 749 developed diabetes. The risk ratio (95% confidence interval) for diabetes in the quit-smoking group relative to the persistent-smoking group was 1.15 (1.07-1.24) at 3 years and 0.95 (0.85-1.06) at 15 years. Per-protocol analyses showed a similar pattern.

Conclusions

Smoking cessation was associated with a short-term increase in diabetes risk, but this excess risk diminished over time, and no long-term increase in risk was observed. These findings support sustained smoking cessation as metabolically beneficial in the long term.

title: Fatal Neonatal mTORopathy: Expanding the Phenotypic Spectrum of RRAGC-Associated Long-Olsen-Distelmaier Syndrome.
authorString: Lores J, Botia-Arciniegas V, Ramirez-Montaño D, Pachajoa H, Vernaza-Trujillo D, Prada-Casilimas M.
abstractText: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a severe cardiac condition characterized by the enlargement and impaired contraction of the heart's ventricles. Pediatric cases often present unique challenges due to their rarity and the complexity of underlying genetic causes. This study presents the first documented case of a Colombian patient with neonatal DCM, bilateral congenital cataracts, focal epilepsy, and hyperlactatemia. Genetic testing identified a pathogenic variant in the RRAGC gene, establishing the diagnosis of Long-Olsen-Distelmaier syndrome, a rare mTOR-related disorder characterized by syndromic cardiomyopathy and multisystem involvement. Additionally, we review the clinical and molecular characteristics of previously reported cases in the literature.

title: Transitions in metabolically healthy obesity based on a novel definition and their association with incident cardiovascular disease: A cohort study.
authorString: Zeng Y, Xu XW, Hu Z, Zhang GL, Tang R, Li J.

journal.title: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists

abstractText:
Objective

A new metabolic health definition has been developed for cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk stratification. This study aimed to assess the stability of this newly defined metabolic health status and evaluate the association of its transitions with CVD risk.

Methods

This study included 7 395 UK Biobank participants. Metabolic health was defined using the new and the Adult Treatment Panel-III (ATP-III) definition. Participants were cross-classified based on their body mass index (BMI) (normal weight, overweight/obesity) and metabolic health (healthy, unhealthy) at baseline. The transitions of metabolic health status were assessed at the first repeat assessment. Cox proportional hazards models were used to examine the association between metabolic health transitions and CVD risks. Extreme gradient boosting and Shapley additive explanations were used to explore predictors of metabolic transition within the metabolically healthy overweight/obesity (MHOO) population.

Results

Using the new and ATP-III definition respectively, 40.9% and 23.7% of participants with MHOO transitioned to metabolically unhealthy status. Under the new definition, baseline MHOO participants who became metabolically unhealthy exhibited an elevated CVD risk (HR = 1.71, 95% CI: 1.14-2.56), whereas maintaining metabolic health was not significantly associated with increased CVD risk, compared with normal-weight participants maintaining metabolic health. Systolic blood pressure, age, and BMI were the main predictors of metabolic transition.

Conclusions

The newly defined metabolic health yielded a higher reclassification rate over time and maintaining metabolic health was not significantly associated with increased CVD risk. These findings emphasize the importance of periodic health monitoring and preventing metabolic deterioration.

title: Interlocked silk sericin hollow particle aggregates with enhanced adaptability and progressive solubility for sustained drug release.
authorString: Zhou W, Zha T, Qu Z, Li N, Chen J, Li Y, Liu Y, Song Y, Feng Y, Sun X, Li J, Han Q, Du S.
abstractText: The ever-increasing demand for multifunctional delivery carriers has considerably stimulated the need for durable, safe, and superior delivery materials. However, the straightforward and scalable fabrication of adaptable particle aggregates that exhibit biocompatibility, desirable textural characteristics, and high performance remains a big challenge. Herein, we present the creation of bulk silk sericin aggregates (SSAs) via a process involving spray drying followed by vacuum-assisted UV irradiation. These aggregates comprise interlocked hollow particles with an average diameter of 4.94 ± 0.23 μm, reminiscent of pomegranate seeds, which confer enhanced storability. Importantly, these bulk SSAs exhibit enhanced formability and water tolerance, with progressive dissolution due to the transformation of β-sheets (39.72%) from random coils induced by chemical crosslinking and compression. Simultaneously, the SSAs demonstrate favorable vascular compatibility, as evidenced by a hemolysis ratio of only 0.89% and an endpoint scoring value of 0.30. These distinctive characteristics enhance the adaptability of the SSAs for practical applications across various environments. The loaded SSAs exhibit markedly different release profiles for 5-fluorouracil, with a cumulative release of 73.21% at pH 7.4 compared to just 0.25% at pH 4.0 over 180 h. This work offers a sustainable fabrication strategy for the development of bulk drug delivery materials, underscoring their considerable potential for advanced drug delivery and therapeutic applications.

title: The dual role of BDNF in epilepsy: insights from calpain-mediated TrkB-FL cleavage.
authorString: Ribeiro-Rodrigues L, Griškova-Bulanova I, Diógenes MJ, Xapelli S.
abstractText: Despite the efficacy of current antiseizure medications in managing seizures, approximately one-third of patients develop refractory epilepsy, highlighting an urgent need to uncover the molecular mechanisms driving epileptogenesis. This process emerges from a complex interplay of molecular alterations, involving changes in neuronal signaling pathways. Among these, brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and its high-affinity receptor, the full-length tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB-FL), are heavily implicated in epilepsy pathophysiology. While traditionally recognized for promoting synaptic plasticity, BDNF signaling can become maladaptive in pathological states. Consequently, BDNF exhibits a paradoxical dual role in epilepsy, acting as a proepileptogenic factor in the acute phase, while exerting antiepileptic effects during the chronic phase. Recently, a calpain-dependent proteolytic mechanism mediating TrkB-FL cleavage, previously described in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and cerebral ischemia, has been shown to occur during epileptogenesis. Elevated levels of the intracellular cleavage product of TrkB-FL, TrkB-ICD, have been observed in the hippocampus of patients with refractory epilepsy, establishing its clinical relevance. In vitro, TrkB-ICD overexpression depolarizes neuronal membranes, increases miniature excitatory postsynaptic current frequency, and alters the transcription of genes related to synaptic transmission and plasticity. In vivo, its overexpression induces long-term memory impairment, a common comorbidity in epilepsy. Moreover, in experimental epilepsy models, TrkB-ICD protein levels correlate with seizure frequency during the acute phase (status epilepticus) and remain elevated during the chronic phase (established epilepsy). These findings highlight TrkB-FL cleavage and TrkB-ICD formation as molecular determinants in epileptogenesis, providing a biological rationale for the contrasting effects of BDNF. Inhibiting this cleavage, using tools like cell-penetrating peptides, represents a promising therapeutic avenue. As the field moves forward, elucidating the precise functions, regulation, and translational potential of the TrkB-FL proteolysis and TrkB-ICD formation may yield innovative, disease-modifying strategies for epilepsy, moving beyond the symptomatic suppression offered by conventional antiseizure drugs.

title: Targeted exome sequencing Delineates Subtype-Specific genetic Architecture and BMPR2-Associated Prognosis in Chinese paediatric pulmonary arterial hypertension.
authorString: Su TQ, Zhao YX, Liu Q, Zhao WG, Zhang WM, Liu TT, Gu H, Du J, Piao C, Wang Y.
abstractText: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) exhibits greater genetic enrichment in children than in adults; however, genotype-phenotype correlations in Chinese paediatric PAH remain poorly defined. We performed targeted exome sequencing of 16 PAH-associated genes in 154 children with PAH at Beijing Anzhen Hospital (2010-2023) and interpreted variants under a calibrated, point-based ACMG/AMP framework. Pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants were identified in 38 patients (24.7 %): 23 BMPR2 (60.5 %), 7 TBX4 (18.4 %), 5 ACVRL1 (13.2 %), 2 SOX17 (5.3 %), and 1 GDF2 (2.6 %). Thirty variants were upgraded from the baseline automated InterVar classification, including five BMPR2 missense variants reclassified through the PP2 criterion. An additional 42 patients (27.3 %) harboured variants of uncertain significance (VUS) only. P/LP carriers presented with more severe baseline haemodynamics than benign or likely benign (B/LB) carriers, with higher pulmonary vascular resistance indices and lower cardiac indices. Among the 43 patients with available follow-up data, P/LP carriers exhibited significantly worse event-free survival than B/LB carriers and non-carriers (10-year estimate 47.7 % vs. 78.5 %; HR 3.70, 95 % CI 1.04-13.20; log-rank p = 0.0309), an effect largely attributable to BMPR2 variants (HR 4.83, 95 % CI 1.29-18.04). In contrast, VUS carriers resembled B/LB carriers and non-carriers (HR 0.84, p = 0.8436). Thus, the calibrated variant-classification framework substantially increased the diagnostic yield in Chinese paediatric PAH, uncovered an under-recognised contribution of BMPR2 missense variants, and enabled prognostic stratification across the three-tier pathogenicity spectrum.

title: Zfpm1 regulates endothelial-mesenchymal transition and endocardial cell differentiation.
authorString: Lohiya P, Barkas N, Reyes-Corral M, Amante SM, Malim GA, Reumiller C, Ellison-Hughes GM, Holt M, Harmelink C, Tompkins K, Baldwin HS, Montibus B, Oakey RJ.
abstractText: The endocardium is the endothelial component of the heart that forms valves. Endocardial (EC) cells undergo endothelial-mesenchymal transition (EndoMT) which distinguishes them from endothelial (ET) cells, despite sharing markers and a mesodermal origin. Nfatc1, uniquely labels EC cells but is not sufficient for EC cell specification, since knockouts form valves, albeit underdeveloped, therefore the regulators that specify EC fate remain incompletely defined. Using an in vivo Nfatc1 reporter system, we show that EC and ET cells are transcriptionally distinct and identify the transcription factor Zfpm1 (Fog1), as a potential regulator of EC cell specification. In an in vitro embryonic stem cell differentiation model, Zfpm1 knockdown results in an impaired EC cell differentiation, with reduced endothelial-mesenchymal transition and altered contractility and beating phenotype, consistent with reduced differentiation of EC cells affecting the crosstalk with myocardial cells. These findings are consistent with data linking mutations in the human ZFPM1 gene with non-syndromic tetralogy of Fallot. This and the broad expression pattern across all regions of the cardiac outflow tract support a role for Zfpm1 in mammalian EC cell differentiation and endothelial-mesenchymal transition. This study extends the in vivo evidence of its relevance to cardiac development and provides new insights into the transcriptional control of EC lineages.

title: Brain tissue pulsation responses to a low-level expiratory resistance manoeuvre: A pilot healthy volunteer study.
authorString: Nicholls JK, Chung EML, Ince J, Pallett E, Minhas JS, Lecchini-Visintini A.
abstractText: Pulsatility of the brain has been hypothesised to be linked to intracranial pressure (ICP), although the nature of this relationship remains poorly understood. We used a low-level expiratory resistance manoeuvre to characterise brain tissue pulsation (BTP) responses in a pilot healthy volunteer study. BTPs were measured using a transcranial tissue Doppler ultrasound prototype in 10 healthy volunteers at rest and during the manoeuvre. Measurements of mean arterial pressure (MAP), pulse pressure (PP), and heart rate (HR) were also recorded. One-way repeated-measures ANOVA compared changes between baseline, each phase of the manoeuvre, and recovery. Bulk BTP amplitude increased significantly during the initial phase compared with baseline (P = 0.004). A non-significant decrease was observed as the manoeuvre continued, with values decreasing below baseline during the late phase, followed by an increase above baseline during recovery. HR increased significantly during the late phase (P = 0.015). No significant changes were observed in MAP or PP. Bulk BTP amplitude demonstrated a dynamic response during low-level expiratory resistance, characterised by an initial increase followed by a non-significant decrease over the remainder of the manoeuvre. The physiological mechanisms underlying these observations remain uncertain. Future studies incorporating direct ICP measurements and complementary physiological monitoring are needed to clarify the relationship between BTPs and intracranial dynamics.

title: Preprocedural Computed Tomography Guidance Improves Accuracy of Right Ventricular Septal Lead Placement in Pacemaker Implantation.
authorString: Tachibana M, Matsumoto A, Kimura A, Moriya S, Banba K, Teranishi J, Fujio H, Yuasa S.
abstractText:
Introduction

Accurate right ventricular septal lead placement is crucial for optimal pacemaker performance and procedural safety, yet conventional fluoroscopy-guided implantation is limited by inter-individual anatomical variability. We therefore examined whether preprocedural computed tomography (CT) can provide patient-specific anatomical guidance to enable precise lead positioning.

Methods and results

We retrospectively analyzed 501 consecutive patients who underwent initial dual-chamber pacemaker implantation for bradycardia pacing (non-CT-guided, n = 243; CT-guided, n = 258). In the CT-guided group, the midseptal target was determined preoperatively using multiplanar reconstruction of CT images, and reference lines were projected onto the scout image to guide lead placement. We evaluated the total procedure time, fluoroscopy time, right ventricular lead electrical parameters, implantation site, and complications. CT guidance was associated with a higher rate of septal lead placement than non-CT guidance (93.0% vs. 55.6%, p < 0.001), whereas free-wall lead placement was less frequent (7.0% vs. 44.4%, p < 0.001). The procedural radiation dose was lower with CT guidance (CT-guided, 100.2 ± 124.6 mGy vs. non-CT-guided, 169.1 ± 152.4 mGy; p < 0.001). Among patients with complete atrioventricular block and available postoperative paced QRS measurements (n = 303), QRS duration was shorter in the CT-guided group than in the non-CT-guided group (145.3 ± 22.3 ms [n = 165] vs. 155.4 ± 19.0 ms [n = 138], p < 0.001). The association persisted after multivariable adjustment ((adjusted OR, 10.30; 95% CI, 5.91-17.97; p < 0.001). The total procedure time, fluoroscopy time, and pacing parameters were comparable between the groups. Complication rates were low overall, and pocket hematoma was less frequent in the CT-guided group (0.4% vs. 2.9%, p = 0.03).

Conclusion

Preprocedural CT guidance facilitated precise planning of the right ventricular lead target using scout images and was associated with accurate and reproducible placement at the intended septal site without prolonging procedural time or compromising electrical performance. This approach may represent a practical strategy for optimizing lead placement in bradycardia pacing.

title: Artifactual Contact Force Rise During High-Power Radiofrequency Delivery With the QDOT MICRO Catheter: A Comparative Study Using Non-Contact Tests.
authorString: Makita T, Kuwahara T, Takahashi K, Arisuda Y, Shimoshige S, Kanemura J, Futagawa K.
abstractText:
Introduction

Contact force (CF)-sensing technology ensures effective lesion formation and safety during radiofrequency (RF) ablation; however, the potential for an artifactual rise in CF, a false elevation not attributed to physical contact, remains poorly understood. This study aimed to evaluate and compare the occurrence and magnitude of artifactual CF rise between the QDOT MICRO catheter (QMc) and the Thermocool SmartTouch SF catheter (STSFc) using a non-contact RF delivery (NCRD) test.

Methods and results

We retrospectively analyzed 135 patients who underwent NCRD testing in the right atrium (QMc, n = 93; STSFc, n = 42). The NCRD test was performed in a blood pool without tissue contact at power settings of 90, 50, and 40 W for QMc and 50 and 40 W for STSFc. The magnitude and incidence of CF rise (≥ 5 and ≥ 10 g) were compared. In the QMc group, a significant power-dependent increase in CF was observed: 9 g (IQR: 5-12 g) at 90 W, 3 g (IQR: 1-10 g) at 50 W, and 2 g (IQR: 1-3 g) at 40 W (p < 0.001). At 90 W, the incidence of CF rise ≥ 5 g was 76%, and that of CF rise ≥ 10 g was 46%, significantly higher than at lower settings. In contrast, the STSFc group exhibited stable CF measurements with no instances of CF rise ≥ 5 g. QMc also showed significant power-dependent elevation in electrode temperature.

Conclusion

QMc exhibited significant power-dependent artifactual CF rise. These findings suggest that catheter-specific design and thermal effects may influence CF stability during RF delivery. Preprocedural NCRD tests may help identify catheter-specific CF instability before CF-guided ablation.

title: Cavotricuspid Isthmus Ablation Using a Variable Loop Pulsed Field Ablation Catheter: A Single-Center Descriptive Analysis.
authorString: Wiederkehr C, Breitenstein A, Jeger R, Müller A, Brix T, Sepulcri D, Rossotti L, Hofer D.
abstractText:
Introduction

Cavotricuspid isthmus (CTI) ablation is frequently performed concomitant with pulmonary vein isolation (PVI). Pulsed field ablation (PFA) has emerged as the preferred energy source for PVI, but it is unclear whether CTI ablation can be performed with PFA catheters.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed data from patients who underwent PVI and CTI ablation using a variable-loop PFA catheter for feasibility, efficacy, and safety.

Results

Twenty-three patients (mean age 65 years, 57% male) were included in this analysis. Systemic intravenous nitroglycerin was administered to all subjects to prevent vasospasm. Acute CTI block could be documented in all patients at the end of the ablation procedure without complications and with low fluoroscopy exposure. We observed one symptomatic recurrence of possible typical atrial flutter during a mean follow-up of 218 days.

Conclusion

CTI ablation using a variable-loop PFA ablation catheter was feasible, efficient, and safe in the acute setting. Prospective studies with larger patient numbers are needed to evaluate the long-term efficacy and safety of this approach.

title: Coupling Interval Variability of Outflow Tract Premature Ventricular Contractions: A Poincaré Plot-Based Assessment.
authorString: Iszlai MJ, Negrea MO, Simu G, Puiu M, Roșu R, Pop D, Cismaru G.
abstractText:
Purpose

Coupling interval variability (ΔCI) of premature ventricular contractions (PVCs) may provide insight into their site of origin. This study evaluated whether ΔCI, quantified by Poincaré graph analysis, can distinguish PVCs arising from the right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) compared to other locations.

Methods

We screened 117 patients undergoing electroanatomical mapping and catheter ablation for PVCs. Exclusion criteria included: failed ablation, low PVC burden on Holter ECG, non-sinus baseline rhythm, or absence of a qualifying Holter recording. Sixty patients met these criteria: 34 with RVOT PVCs, 11 with left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) PVCs, and 15 with non-RVOT PVCs. ΔCI was assessed using Poincaré plots derived from the Holter ECG recordings.

Results

A ΔCI < 100 ms predicted RVOT origin with a specificity of 100% and a sensitivity of 25%. Poincaré plots effectively visualized CI variability, with narrow PVC clusters (measured along the x-axis) corresponding to RVOT origin. Broader clusters were observed in LVOT and other non-RVOT PVCs, reflecting greater variability.

Conclusions

ΔCI, represented by Poincaré plots, is a reliable and time-efficient marker of RVOT PVC origin. Narrow PVC clusters with low ΔCI strongly suggest RVOT localization, offering a practical adjunct to vectographic mapping in clinical ablation strategies.

title: 19F MRI-Traceable PLGA Nanocarriers: Influence of Particle Architecture on Co-Encapsulation and Release of Immiscible Payloads.
authorString: Larreina Vicente N, Lodrini A, Groeneveld E, Tagit O, Goumans MJ, Srinivas M.
abstractText: Two perfluorocarbon (PFC)-loaded PLGA nanoparticles (NPs) of different architectures were previously established as 19F MRI tracers: sodium cholate (NaCh)-stabilized core-shell particles (CSPs) and PVA-stabilized multicore particles (MCPs). Differing in their stabilizers and internal PFC distribution, they exhibited significant differences in stiffness, permeability, cell uptake, and biological behavior, with MCPs showing dramatically faster in vivo fluorine clearance, addressing an important barrier to the clinical translation of PFCs. Here, we explore the incorporation of rapamycin, a small hydrophobic drug, as a third immiscible phase to develop a theranostic platform for cardiac regeneration. By comparing the drug-loaded particle systems (Rapa-MCPs and Rapa-CSPs) against drug-free and PFC-free (Rapa-PLGA NPs) controls, we study how PFC presence and stabilizer-governed NP architectures affect multipayload incorporation, release, and biological behavior. PFC presence was associated with enhanced drug loading but faster release. A higher drug-to-polymer ratio increased loading but constrained PFC encapsulation above 2 wt %. NP architecture governed multipayload incorporation trade-offs: Rapa-CSPs showed preferential stabilization of the PFC phase over the drug and dye, and unpredictable drug release, reflecting greater sensitivity to multipayload incorporation; Rapa-MCPs could more flexibly accommodate multiple immiscible payloads at the expense of robust PFC stabilization, and showed a fast but gradual release. In vitro, encapsulated rapamycin retained mTOR-inhibitory activity, and Rapa-MCPs reduced TGF-β-driven fibrotic signaling in human living myocardial slices, supporting their therapeutic potential. These findings indicate that the stabilizers and resulting particle architectures govern payload partitioning and release in mutually immiscible multiphasic systems and provide practical design guidelines for structurally tunable polymer nanocarriers for 19F MRI-guided drug delivery.

title: Anomalous papillary muscle insertion beyond hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: insights from reported cases.
authorString: Kudo Y, Takahashi S.
abstractText: Anomalous insertion of the papillary muscle (APM) into the mitral valve leaflet is a rare congenital abnormality of the subvalvular apparatus. Most published reports describe direct papillary muscle insertion in association with obstructive physiology, particularly in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), where it contributes to left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction and systolic anterior motion (SAM)-related mitral regurgitation. However, similar papillary muscle-leaflet continuity may also serve as a primary mechanical determinant of valve dysfunction in patients without a clinical diagnosis of HCM. This review synthesizes published reports of APM insertion across different clinical contexts and interprets them within a mechanism-oriented framework based on LVOT dynamics and functional role of the papillary muscle rather than disease labels. Available reports indicate a heterogeneous clinical spectrum in which hemodynamic manifestations reflect interactions among papillary muscle anatomy, mitral valve mechanics, and ventricular geometry. Although LVOT obstruction remains an important presentation, many cases show predominant mitral regurgitation due to leaflet tethering or, less commonly, functional mitral stenosis from impaired diastolic leaflet opening. These phenotypes arise from subvalvular mechanical restriction rather than primary leaflet pathology. Echocardiography plays a central role in diagnosis, yet APM insertion may be overlooked if assessment focuses primarily on leaflet morphology or Doppler findings. Transesophageal echocardiography, cardiac computed tomography, and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging provide complementary anatomical detail for accurate characterization and surgical planning. Greater awareness of this geometry-based interaction and adoption of a structured imaging approach may reduce diagnostic oversight and improve decision-making in patients with atypical mitral valve dysfunction.

title: Dipicolinic acid has an anti-inflammatory effect and inhibits the expression of NF-κB, miR-101a, miR-140 and miR-195 in diclofenac-induced myocardial injury in rats.
authorString: Kryl'skii ED, Popova TN, Verevkin AN, Scherbakova OA, Sergin VP.
abstractText:
Background

Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, including diclofenac, are commonly used to alleviate inflammation and pain associated with various medical conditions. Prolonged use of these medications may lead to complications related to the cardiovascular system. One of the primary mechanisms of myocardial damage associated with diclofenac is oxidative stress, which is closely linked with the activation of inflammation. The current study aims to evaluate the efficacy of dipicolinic acid (DPA) as a potential treatment for diclofenac-induced cardiac injury. Additionally, the study will investigate the effects of DPA on the expression levels of transcription factor NF-κB and microRNAs (miRNAs), specifically miR-101a, miR-140, and miR-195, which play a role in regulating inflammation.

Methods and results

The results of the study demonstrated that the implementation of DPA led to a substantial reduction in the levels of cardiomyocytes cytolytic markers in the blood serum of the animals, compared to the values observed in the group with myocardial injury. These alterations were associated with decreased concentrations of free radical-induced oxidation products of lipid, protein, and DNA, including diene conjugates, carbonylated proteins, and 8-hydroxy-2-deoxyguanosine. The improvement in the oxidative status of rats was accompanied by a reduction in the levels of pro-inflammatory cytokine mRNA and myeloperoxidase activity. The DPA treatment also reduced the expression of the p65 subunit of the NF-κB factor and miR-101a, miR-140, and miR-195, which were found to be involved in pro-inflammatory signaling.

Conclusions

Therefore, the administration of DPA in diclofenac-induced myocardial injury is associated with an improvement in oxidative status and the inhibition of the inflammatory response, which may involve the modulation of the NF-κB, miR-101, miR-140, and miR-195 expression.

title: Targeting the epigenetic landscape of ECFCs: a new opportunity to enhance vascular repair.
authorString: Liu Y, Lyons CJ, Lagonda CA, Luo Y, Cheng L, Fang Z.
abstractText: Endothelial colony-forming cells (ECFCs) are endothelial progenitor cells characterized by robust proliferative and vasculogenic capacities, making them promising candidates for therapeutic tissue revascularization. However, the clinical application of ECFCs is hindered by their functional impairment under pathological conditions, such as diabetes and cardiovascular disease. Accumulating evidence indicates that aberrant epigenetic modifications, including DNA methylation, histone modifications, and non-coding RNA-mediated regulation, have been implicated in disease-associated ECFC dysfunction. In this review, we summarize current insights into the epigenetic regulation of ECFCs in pathological contexts, discuss epigenetic intervention strategies aimed at restoring ECFC function, and further highlight the therapeutic potential of ECFC-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) as carriers of epigenetic cargo that promotes vascular repair. Collectively, a deeper understanding of the epigenetic landscape of ECFCs and ECFC-derived EVs may facilitate the development of novel therapeutic approaches for vascular regeneration and accelerate the clinical translation of ECFC- and EV-based therapies.

title: Multi-scale 0D-1D, 0D-3D, 1D-3D coupling for cardiovascular simulation and modelling applications: A review.
authorString: Grebenikov DA, Kuchumov AG.

journal.title: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers. Part H, Journal of engineering in medicine

abstractText: Mathematical modelling of systemic haemodynamics plays a crucial role in contemporary biomedical research. Clinical tasks, such as surgical planning, require a personalised and patient-specific approach for a precise mathematical formulation of problems covering all significant physiological phenomena. Application of multi-scale models assumes development of methods to couple low-dimensional and high-dimensional models, which describe interaction between local and systemic processes. Thus, it is necessary to systematise existing approaches to couple 0D, 1D and 3D blood flow models to reveal optimal techniques corresponding to specific clinical and research tasks. The aim of the present work is to classify contemporary methods for coupling multi-scale models for computational haemodynamics applications. To achieve this aim, a systematic analysis of scientific publications was performed. The publications were selected from the electronic databases Google Scholar, PubMed, ScienceDirect, ResearchGate and Scopus using the following keywords: 'coupling', '3d/0d', '1d/0d', '3d/1d', 'computational haemodynamics', 'numerical simulations', 'blood flow', 'mathematical model', 'FSI', 'CFD', 'boundary conditions', 'multiscale model', 'multidimensional model'. As a result of the analysis, the main coupling approaches were systematised and their key features, advantages and limitations were identified. The obtained results allow the most relevant coupling methods for the solution of various cardiovascular problems to be determined. This contributes to the optimisation of computational processes and enhances the reliability of predictive models in personalised medicine.

title: Tricuspid Chordae Tendineae Rupture Detected After Repair of a Delayed Traumatic Left Ventricular Aneurysm: A Case Report.
authorString: Shao H, Liao Y, Li Z.

journal.title: The American journal of case reports

abstractText: BACKGROUND Delayed traumatic cardiac rupture complicated by secondary tricuspid chordae tendineae rupture is an exceedingly rare clinical entity. We report this case to describe the temporal sequence of events from blunt myocardial contusion to left ventricular aneurysm formation and rupture, followed by secondary tricuspid chordae tendineae rupture. While the precise mechanism linking these events remains to be determined, we propose a potential pathophysiological connection. CASE REPORT A patient presented with rupture of a posterior left ventricular aneurysm 54 days after a fall from a height. The patient was emergently placed on venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) for circulatory support and subsequently underwent surgical repair of the aneurysm. Postoperative echocardiography revealed new-onset tricuspid chordae tendineae rupture, prompting elective mechanical tricuspid replacement. Histopathological examination of resected valve tissues revealed chronic degenerative changes. To our knowledge, this is the first report documenting this temporal sequence of delayed left ventricular aneurysm rupture followed by tricuspid chordal rupture after surgical repair. CONCLUSIONS This case highlights the importance of continued clinical and echocardiographic vigilance after severe blunt cardiac injury, particularly for detecting late-emerging structural complications such as aneurysm formation and valvular dysfunction. It also illustrates the potential utility of VA-ECMO as a critical bridging strategy to stabilize patients with traumatic cardiac rupture before surgical repair. The observed temporal association between aneurysm repair and subsequent tricuspid chordal rupture is noted, though the exact causal relationship and underlying mechanism remain uncertain.

title: Endometrial compaction and ongoing pregnancy in modified natural cycle frozen euploid embryo transfer: a prospective multicentre cohort study with standardized transvaginal ultrasound assessment.
authorString: De la Torre Pérez E, Castillo-Farfán JC, Carratalá-Munuera MC, Ortiz JA, Lledó-Bosch B, Olalla García S, Moliner-Renau B, Bernabeu-García A.
abstractText:
Study question

Does endometrial compaction, assessed by transvaginal ultrasound at two measurement time points, predict ongoing pregnancy in patients undergoing single euploid blastocyst transfer in a modified natural cycle frozen embryo transfer (mNC-FET)?

Summary answer

Endometrial compaction of ≥5% between the day of ovulation triggering and the day of embryo transfer was not associated with ongoing pregnancy rate or any secondary reproductive outcome in this prospective multicentre cohort.

What is known already

Endometrial compaction-a reduction in endometrial thickness (EMT) following progesterone-induced secretory transformation-has been proposed as a potential marker of endometrial receptivity in FET cycles. However, existing evidence is conflicting. Retrospective studies have reported positive associations between compaction and ongoing pregnancy in programmed cycles, while prospective data, including the only prior study restricted to euploid single FET, have not confirmed this relationship. Crucially, most studies have used transabdominal ultrasound for the transfer-day measurement, a recognized source of measurement error. No prospective study has examined compaction exclusively in mNC-FET using transvaginal ultrasound at both time points.

Study design, size, duration

Prospective multicentre observational cohort study conducted between March 2023 and March 2025 across six assisted reproduction units of Instituto Bernabeu group (Spain). A total of 207 patients who met all inclusion criteria and completed the full protocol were analysed.

Participants/materials, setting, methods

Women aged 18-50 years undergoing mNC-FET with a single euploid blastocyst (confirmed by preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy via next-generation sequencing) were included. EMT was measured transvaginally at T1 (day of hCG trigger) and T2 (day of embryo transfer). Compaction was defined as a ≥5% reduction in EMT from T1 to T2. Additional thresholds of ≥10% and ≥15% were evaluated as sensitivity analyses. The primary outcome was ongoing pregnancy, defined as foetal cardiac activity at 10 weeks of gestation. Multivariable logistic regression was performed, adjusting for age, previous live births, previous miscarriages, BMI, and oocyte origin.

Main results and the role of chance

Of 207 patients, 58 (28.0%) met the compaction criterion (≥5%). The compaction group had a significantly greater T1 EMT (9.55 ± 1.54 mm vs 8.39 ± 1.14 mm, P < 0.001) and a lower T2 EMT (7.91 ± 1.19 mm vs 9.75 ± 1.55 mm, P < 0.001). Ongoing pregnancy rates were 50.0% in the compaction group versus 53.7% in the non-compaction group (P = 0.633). This difference was not significant on multivariable analysis (adjusted odds ratio 0.80, 95% CI 0.38-1.67, P = 0.546). The null association was consistent across all compaction thresholds (≥10%: P = 0.674; ≥15%: P = 0.928) and across all secondary outcomes, including clinical pregnancy rate (56.9% vs 59.1%, P = 0.777), biochemical pregnancy loss (10.8% vs 8.3%, P = 0.737), and early pregnancy loss rate (12.1% vs 9.1%, P = 0.734). The overall ongoing pregnancy rate was 52.7% (109/207).

Limitations, reasons for caution

The distribution between groups was asymmetric (28% compaction vs 72% non-compaction), deviating from the balanced allocation anticipated at protocol design, which may reduce statistical power. Although both measurements were transvaginal, a subset of T1 measurements from international patients were performed at external centres and validated remotely by Instituto Bernabeu's physicians. Live birth data were only partially available at the time of analysis; however, ongoing pregnancy at 10 weeks is a validated and widely accepted surrogate for live birth in reproductive medicine trials.

Wider implications of the findings

These findings do not support the hypothesis that endometrial compaction is associated with improved reproductive outcomes in mNC-FET with euploid embryos. The consistent null result across multiple thresholds and outcomes, obtained with a fully standardized transvaginal ultrasound methodology, strengthens the current evidence base. Routine assessment of endometrial compaction with the aim of identifying patients with a favourable prognosis does not appear to be clinically justified in this setting; indeed, acting upon compaction status could lead to unnecessary cycle cancellations in patients who would otherwise achieve ongoing pregnancy.

Funding

This study was supported by a Doctoral Research Grant awarded by Miguel Hernandez Public University, Spain (Rectoral Resolution No. 04588/2021). The funding body had no role in the study design, data collection, analysis or interpretation of the data, preparation of the manuscript, or decision to submit the manuscript for publication.

Disclosures

The authors declare no competing interests related to the present study. No personal payments, financial incentives, or commercial benefits were received by any author in relation to this work.

Trial registration number

NCT05960370.

title: Earlier Versus Later Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation in Refractory Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Nationwide Sequential Landmark Target Trial Emulation.
authorString: Sim JH, Park B, Lee H.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care
journal.title: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care

abstractText:
Background

Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) may improve outcomes in refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), but the optimal timing of initiation remains uncertain, partly because prior comparisons did not restrict controls to patients still in refractory arrest at the same decision point.

Methods

We employed target trial emulation with a sequential landmark design in the Korean nationwide OHCA registry (2016-2023). Among patients with presumed cardiac aetiology who were still receiving emergency department (ED) CPR 15 minutes after ED arrival, landmarks were set at 15, 30, and 60 minutes, each comparing ECPR initiation within the subsequent window with no ECPR during that window among patients still in refractory arrest. Treatment effects were adjusted risk differences estimated by propensity score overlap weighting with 22 covariates.

Results

Of 58,668 patients with refractory OHCA, 909 received ECPR. Weighted 30-day survival (ECPR vs. control) was 31.0% vs. 16.0%, 21.6% vs. 7.2%, and 10.9% vs. 3.2% at the 15-, 30-, and 60-minute landmarks; adjusted risk differences were +15.0 percentage points (95% CI 8.0 to 22.0), +14.4 (10.4 to 18.4), and +7.7 (3.7 to 11.7) (all P<.001). Favourable neurological outcomes showed a similar pattern, and in the exploratory timing-gradient analysis, the adjusted risk difference decreased with longer door-to-ECMO times but remained statistically significant through 120 minutes.

Conclusions

ECPR was associated with improved survival and neurological outcomes at every landmark, including initiation beyond 60 minutes, where weighted 30-day survival with continued conventional CPR was 3.2%. Benefit was largest with early initiation but did not disappear at the commonly applied 60-minute benchmark, which may be overly restrictive for selected patients in capable systems.

title: Multimodal functional characterization of the LDLR noncoding landscape
authorString: Vyas HS, Leix K, Burugula BB, Paye SM, Raut C, Speliotes EK, Emmer BT.
abstractText: The expression level of the low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR) gene is a critical determinant of circulating low-density lipoprotein concentrations and the corresponding risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. While the importance of sterol response elements in LDLR transcriptional regulation has been firmly established, the functional contribution of other potential cis-regulatory elements (CREs) remains poorly understood. In this study, we developed and applied a variety of high throughput functional genomic tools to systematically interrogate the noncoding space at the LDLR locus. These included saturation CRISPR nuclease, CRISPR activation, and CRISPR inhibition screening as well as a massively parallel reporter assay. With each approach, we observed robust discrimination of control sequences and significant effects for other regions with a previously unrecognized influence on LDLR expression. The CREs identified by each modality were overlapping but distinct, both in relation to each other and to those regions predicted to harbor CRE activity. Collectively, our findings clarify the functional landscape of the LDLR locus and highlight the complementary nature of different functional genomic approaches to CRE identification.

title: Mechanical history shapes phenotypic plasticity and fibroblast-autonomous 3D remodeling in iPSC-derived cardiac fibroblasts
authorString: Jiang H, Malayath G, Kellogg A, Debeni Devi N, Chen C, Huebsch N.
abstractText: Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiac fibroblasts (iPSC-cFBs) offer a renewable, genetically defined stromal cell source for studying cardiac fibrosis and cardiomyocyte-fibroblast crosstalk during development and disease. Because cardiac fibroblasts are proliferative, expansion of iPSC-cFBs in culture is attractive for applications requiring large cell numbers, including drug screening and tissue engineering. However, phenotypic drift during expansion, particularly premature fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition (FMT), remains a concern. Here, we investigated how differentiation protocol, mechanical culture history, and serial expansion shape iPSC-cFB phenotype, transforming growth factor beta 1 (TGF-beta1) responsiveness, and fibroblast-autonomous remodeling in three-dimensional (3D) tissues. Initial studies of iPSC-cFBs expanded on conventional tissue-culture polystyrene (TCP) revealed passage-associated increases in projected cell area and alpha-smooth muscle actin (alpha-SMA) expression, two markers associated with FMT. These findings prompted us to examine how the stiffness of poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) substrates (15 kPa or 2 MPa) used during iPSC-cFB derivation and expansion influences basal phenotype and response to TGF-beta1. Across two independent differentiation protocols, mechanical culture history shaped passage-dependent basal phenotypes and responses to TGF-beta1. Notably, its effects on collective TGF-beta1 responses in three-dimensional cultures differed from those observed after replating cells onto two-dimensional substrates. Together, these findings demonstrate that mechanical culture history modulates iPSC-cFB responsiveness and tissue-remodeling behavior without irreversibly determining fibroblast state. Subsequent passage and microenvironmental conditions can attenuate or re-express these history-dependent phenotypes. This work supports the use of iPSC-cFBs in basic biological discovery and future tissue engineering applications.

title: Depression and Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: An Inflammatory Perspective.
authorString: Chen H, Zhang N, Feng Y, Tao M, Geng C.
abstractText: Depression is a common comorbidity in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), suggesting potential epidemiological and pathophysiological connections between these two age-related chronic diseases. Extensive clinical evidence demonstrates that depression is closely associated with both the incidence and prognosis of HFpEF. It is currently believed that depression may contribute to the pathogenesis of HFpEF through various interconnected mechanisms, including intestinal dysfunction, endothelial dysfunction, disturbances in fat and energy metabolism, autonomic nervous system dysfunction, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis imbalance, and sex differences. Both conditions often share common comorbidities and genetic predispositions. Notably, inflammation is implicated in all these mechanisms and processes, playing a key role at different stages and facilitating the interaction between the two diseases during their onset and progression. However, the connections between depression and HFpEF have not yet been systematically and thoroughly elucidated. This review aims to comprehensively summarize the associations between depression and HFpEF, focusing particularly on elucidating their interplay in pathogenesis from an inflammation perspective, with special emphasis on the adverse effects of depression on the development of HFpEF. Additionally, we evaluate the management approaches for patients with comorbid depression and HFpEF, which include both pharmacological and nonpharmacological treatments, highlighting that personalized and integrated interventions may offer significant benefits. The review underscores the importance of increased attention and early identification of patients with comorbid depression and HFpEF and is expected to provide valuable insights and guidance for the clinical management of this significant patient population.

title: Expanding Primary Care-Based Echocardiography Access in a Value-Based Care Network: Impact on Heart Failure Detection, Utilization, and Spending.
authorString: Wolf P, Howell S, Avery S, Mackenzie A, Huynh N, Rao K, Rissinger W.
abstractText: This retrospective observational study assessed whether expanding primary care-based echocardiography access within a rural Pennsylvania value-based care network was associated with differences in heart failure (HF) diagnosis patterns, health care utilization, and spending compared with internal controls and a state-level benchmark. Eligibility, medical, and pharmacy claims were analyzed from 2 sources: third-party payers covering the primary care network and Merative's MarketScan Medicare data as a state-level reference. Members with HF-related risk factors were identified using diagnosis codes and followed for 12 months after index risk factor documentation, and the inverse probability of treatment weighting was used, incorporating age, sex, risk score, HF risk-factor category, and eligibility duration to address baseline demographic and clinical differences. Among members with HF risk factors, 21.0% of internal study members received an incident HF diagnosis compared with 13.7% of MarketScan members (P < 0.01). Internal cohort diagnoses were less likely to occur in inpatient (IP) settings than MarketScan diagnoses (0.53% vs. 10.2%; P < 0.01) and occurred after longer intervals from risk factor documentation (202 vs. 142 days; P < 0.01). Among diagnosed members, the internal cohort had lower HF-related IP admissions (21 vs. 28 per 1,000 member-years; P < 0.01), fewer HF-related emergency department visits (34 vs. 49 per 1000 member-years; P < 0.01), and lower average monthly spending ($1,937 vs. $2,826; P < 0.01). These findings suggest that expanding primary care-based echocardiography access in a rural value-based care setting was associated with greater HF detection, more outpatient-based diagnosis, and lower downstream acute care use and spending, broadly applicable to health systems and payers investing in diagnostics.

title: Predictors of in-hospital venous thromboembolism in patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty.
authorString: Mastrokostas LE, Mastrokostas PG, Kucherina A, Tyagi A, Lama G, Magruder M.

journal.title: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie

abstractText:
Purpose

This study evaluated the national inpatient incidence, patient characteristics, and independent predictors of VTE following primary THA.

Methods

A retrospective cohort study was performed using the National Inpatient Sample from 2016 to 2022. Adult patients undergoing primary THA were identified using ICD-10 procedure codes. The primary outcome was in-hospital VTE, defined as deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism during the index admission. Survey-weighted analyses were used to generate national estimates, compare baseline characteristics, and identify independent predictors of VTE using multivariable logistic regression. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05.

Results

Among 855,645 weighted inpatient primary THA admissions, 1660 patients developed in-hospital VTE, corresponding to an incidence of 0.19%. Patients with VTE were older (P < 0.001) and more frequently covered by Medicare (P < 0.001), treated at large hospitals (P = 0.009), and treated at urban teaching hospitals (P = 0.013). They also had a greater prevalence of comorbidities, including autoimmune disease, coagulopathy, congestive heart failure, deficiency anemia, peripheral vascular disease, pulmonary circulation disorders, and moderate renal failure (all P < 0.001), as well as chronic pulmonary disease (P = 0.001) and obesity (P = 0.003). On adjusted analysis, the strongest predictors of VTE were paralysis (OR 9.79, P < 0.001), lymphoma (OR 4.35, P = 0.001), other neurologic disorders (OR 4.30, P < 0.001), and pulmonary circulation disorders (OR 3.50, P < 0.001). Additional independent predictors included peripheral vascular disease (OR 2.19, P < 0.001), autoimmune disease (OR 2.01, P < 0.001), congestive heart failure (OR 1.83, P = 0.022), coagulopathy (OR 1.80, P = 0.035), deficiency anemia (OR 1.65, P = 0.002), hypothyroidism (OR 1.45, P = 0.007), and obesity (OR 1.35, P = 0.018).

Conclusion

In-hospital VTE following primary THA was uncommon but concentrated among medically complex patients. Improved risk stratification may guide perioperative counseling, surveillance, and individualized thromboprophylaxis for higher-risk patients.

title: Variation and temporal trends in Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group billing for carotid endarterectomy across Vascular Quality Initiative centers.
authorString: Facciponte DN, Goodney PP, Mao J, Columbo JA, Bellamkonda KS, Zhou W, Cronenwett JL.
abstractText:
Background

Hospitals use Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group (MS-DRG) coding to bill for each admission, with higher payment provided for those with complications or comorbidities (CCs) or major CCs (MCCs). We analyzed variation in MS-DRG coding for carotid endarterectomy (CEA) across Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) centers to identify opportunities for improvement.

Methods

We matched CEA cases in the VQI registry with Medicare claims data from 2013 through 2023. A multivariable stepwise logistic regression model was created to identify variables associated with CC or MCC billing (with odds ratios [ORs]). We examined variations in CC or MCC billing percentages among centers and applied a multivariable model to compare observed-to-expected (O:E) CC or MCC billing rates to adjust for patient differences. Billing trends over time were analyzed using linear regression.

Results

Among 75,064 primary CEA admissions for Medicare beneficiaries, 39.5% were billed with CCs or MCCs (31.1% CCs, 8.4% MCCs) and 60.5% without. Eleven VQI clinical variables that indicated CCs were significantly associated with CC or MCC billing: dialysis dependence (OR, 22.30), postoperative neurological events (OR, 5.25), length of stay >2 days (OR, 4.98), pre-existing heart failure (OR, 4.08), any postoperative complication (OR, 3.70), reoperation (OR, 3.65), preoperative neurological event (OR, 1.70), higher American Society of Anesthesiologists class (OR, 1.50), urgent/emergent procedure (OR, 1.28), postoperative intravenous blood pressure management (OR, 1.27), and institutional transfer (OR, 1.16). Across 371 VQI centers, CC or MCC billing rates varied 5.6-fold, ranging from 15% to 84% of admissions. After risk adjustment, observed-to-expected ratios still demonstrated 4.2-fold variation, from 0.45 to 1.90 across centers. The observed rate of CC or MCC billing increased over time, from 35.5% in 2015 to 46.1% in 2023 (P < .001). In contrast, the expected adjusted rates predicted by the model remained stable (P = .269). A discrete inflection point was identified between 2016 and 2017, after which higher billing rates persisted (P < .001).

Conclusions

Substantial variation exists for MS-DRG billing for CEA across VQI centers. Billing rates for CCs or MCCs increased from 2013 through 2023. These findings suggest potential underbilling at some centers and overbilling at others. Leveraging Medicare-linked VQI registry data and the proposed model could help to improve coding and billing accuracy, optimize reimbursement, and reduce Medicare audit risk.

title: Euglycemic SGLT2 Inhibitor-Associated Ketoacidosis in a Nondiabetic Patient: A Case Report.
authorString: Zinnato C, Roatta T, Berta G, Penso R, Russotto V.
abstractText: We present the case of a 62-year-old nondiabetic woman receiving dapagliflozin for dilated cardiomyopathy presenting to the emergency department with severe hypoxemic respiratory failure because of suspected cardiogenic pulmonary edema. Despite treatment, she remained symptomatic and required intubation and intensive care admission. After intubation, high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis was unmasked. After exclusion of other common causes, SGLT2 inhibitor-associated ketoacidosis due to dapagliflozin was suspected. Marked ketonuria confirmed the diagnosis despite the absence of hyperglycemia. Dapagliflozin was discontinued, and intravenous insulin, glucose infusion, and early enteral nutrition were initiated. Metabolic acidosis resolved completely within 24 h. The patient was successfully extubated and discharged from the intensive care unit 48 h later. SGLT2 inhibitor-associated ketoacidosis should be considered in patients receiving sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors who develop otherwise unexplained high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, irrespective of diabetic status or blood glucose concentration. Fasting and acute illness are relevant precipitating factors; prompt drug withdrawal, carbohydrate administration, insulin therapy, and nutritional support can lead to rapid resolution.

title: Atom-Efficient Cerium-Based Molecular Cages as Biocompatible Reactive Oxygen Scavengers.
authorString: Li C, Xiang C, Xu Y, Liu Y, Hong K, Zeng F, Xu G, Wang ZX, Sessler JL, Gong P.
abstractText: The development of reactive oxygen species (ROS)-scavenging materials for biomedical applications has been constrained by the difficulty associated with achieving simultaneously broad-spectrum scavenging efficiency and acceptable biosafety. To date, ceria/nanoceria systems have been explored for this purpose; however, they suffer from limited cerium-atom utilization. Inspired by the atom-economy concept of single-atom catalysis, we report a cerium-based molecular-cage strategy for treating oxidative stress-driven atherosclerosis (AS). It involves mixed-valent cerium ions (Ce<sup>3+</sup>/Ce<sup>4+</sup>) that are stably confined within tailored molecular cages and that mimic the cooperation between oxygen vacancies and cerium redox cycling in CeO<sub>2</sub>. This endows the four representative cages of this study with an ability to scavenge superoxide anion (O<sub>2</sub>•<sup>-</sup>), hydrogen peroxide (H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>), and hydroxyl radical (•OH). Their catalytic function can be readily modulated through the ROS-responsive release of the molecular cages at local lesion sites. This capability was found to alleviate oxidative stress and associated inflammation, as inferred from the finding that a lead cerium cage incorporated into a biocompatible nanoparticle reduces the progression of AS in a mouse model. A reduction in plaque lipid deposition, macrophage accumulation, necrotic core formation, and MMP-9-associated matrix was seen.
