title: Empagliflozin Therapy in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: A Feasibility Randomized Controlled Trial.
authorString: Seliger SL, Gitomer B, You Z, Wang W, Ostrow A, Andrews E, Diggs C, George D, West M, Nowak KL, Watnick T, Chonchol M.

journal.title: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN

abstractText:
Key points

Empagliflozin 25 mg once daily for 12 months was safe and well tolerated in adults with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease at high risk of rapid progression. Those randomized to empagliflozin had a greater rate of increase in total kidney volume over 12 months compared with placebo. There was no difference between groups in the chronic rate of change in eGFR, nor in change in vascular stiffness, symptoms, and copeptin.

Background

Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors reduce the risk of diabetic and nondiabetic kidney disease progression; however, their safety and efficacy in patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) are undetermined.

Methods

In this pilot and feasibility randomized controlled trial, we assigned 50 participants, 18-55 years of age, with ADPKD, at high risk of progression, not treated with tolvaptan, to receive empagliflozin (25 mg once daily) or placebo in a 1:1 ratio for 12 months. Primary outcomes were medication safety and tolerability. Secondary outcomes were (1) change in height-adjusted total kidney volume; (2) acute and chronic slope of eGFR; and (3) changes in aortic pulse wave velocity, plasma copeptin levels, urine kidney injury molecule-1, and patient-reported outcomes.

Results

Mean age was 42±7 years, and eGFR was 70±17 ml/min per 1.73 m2. Frequency of adverse events was similar between the 2 groups. Urinary tract infection occurred in 2 empagliflozin-treated patients versus none in placebo and AKI in 1 placebo-treated patient. In total, 96% of the participants in each group tolerated the full dose of the study drug. Among the secondary outcomes, rate of change in height-adjusted total kidney volume was significantly greater in empagliflozin-treated participants (10.5%/yr; 95% confidence interval, 8.2% to 12.7%) compared with placebo (5.1%/yr; 95% confidence interval, 3.0% to 7.3%; P = 0.001). There was a faster acute decline in eGFR at 1 month among the empagliflozin (-6.2 ml/min per 1.73 m2) versus placebo groups (0.1 ml/min per 1.73 m2; P = 0.01), but no differences in eGFR change from 1 to 12 months (empagliflozin group: -0.77±1.44 ml/min per 1.73 m2 per year versus placebo group: -2.87±1.96 ml/min per 1.73 m2 per year; P = 0.4). No between-group differences were observed in changes in aortic pulse wave velocity, copeptin, urine kidney injury molecule-1, and ADPKD Impact Score.

Conclusions

Empagliflozin at 25 mg once daily was well tolerated by patients with ADPKD. Empagliflozin induced an expected acute decline in eGFR by 1 month, followed by stable eGFR. However, those treated with empagliflozin had a greater increase in kidney volume.

Clinical trial registry name and registration number

ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05510115.

title: Practical Prevention of Heart Failure Across Stages A and B: A Scientific Statement From the Japanese Heart Failure Society.
authorString: Suzuki S, Izawa H, Kuwahara K, Sakata Y, Onishi K, Okada Y, Okumura T, Sato Y, Sawamura A, Hanatani A, Kunishima T, Kuwabara M, Inomata T, Kinugawa K.
abstractText: Heart failure (HF) is a growing health problem in Japan, associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, recurrent hospitalization, impaired quality of life, and increasing healthcare costs. Early prevention before the onset of signs and symptoms has therefore become a major priority in cardiovascular medicine. This scientific statement from the Japanese Heart Failure Society provides practical prevention strategies for patients with HF Stage A and Stage B in Japan. Particular emphasis is placed on biomarker-guided screening using brain (B-type) natriuretic peptide (BNP) and N-terminal pro-BNP (NT-proBNP) to facilitate earlier detection of Stage B (pre-HF) and identification of patients at increased risk of progression to symptomatic HF. The statement summarizes evidence-based management of major cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic disorders associated with HF development, including hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, obesity, coronary artery disease, left ventricular dysfunction, valvular heart disease, and atrial fibrillation. It also addresses disease-specific approaches for optimizing blood pressure, glycemic control, renal protection, lipid management, and weight reduction. Preventive strategies include lifestyle modification, pharmacological therapy, serial reassessment of natriuretic peptide levels, and appropriate use of cardiovascular imaging and timely specialist referral. Because many patients at risk for HF are managed outside specialized cardiovascular centers, practical pathways for collaboration between cardiologists and non-cardiologist physicians are essential. The importance of timely referral, shared risk recognition, and multidisciplinary care is therefore emphasized. Implementation of clinically applicable prevention strategies may help reduce progression to symptomatic HF, facilitate earlier therapeutic intervention, and improve long-term cardiovascular outcomes.

title: Precision medicine approaches in diabetic cardiomyopathy: from molecular mechanisms to personalized therapeutic strategies.
authorString: Patel V, Patel K, Patel B, Patel D, Kushwaha A.

journal.title: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology

abstractText: Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a distinct myocardial disease defined by the existence of abnormal myocardial structure and performance in diabetes mellitus patients without hypertension and coronary artery disease. DCM has been identified as a major cause of heart failure, hospitalisation and cardiovascular mortality with increasing global burden of diabetes. However, there is a large interindividual variation in disease susceptibility, disease progression and response to therapy, highlighting the limitations of conventional management strategies that are applied uniformly. Precision medicine provides a transformational approach through the integration of genomic, molecular, imaging, clinical and lifestyle data to allow for personalized risk assessment, early diagnosis, prognostication and treatment. This review presents the recent advances in the field of precision medicine for DCM with a focus on the molecular pathological mechanisms including metabolic disorders, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, fibrosis and microvascular injury. We discuss the relevance of genomics, pharmacogenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, lipidomics and epigenomics in the context of disease heterogeneity and identification of novel therapeutic targets. Emerging biomarkers including circulating microRNAs, non-coding RNAs, inflammatory mediators, fibrosis-related markers and extracellular vesicles are discussed for their potential in personal diagnosis and prognosis. We also consider the increasing role of advanced cardiac imaging, digital phenotyping, wearable technologies, artificial intelligence, and machine learning in enhancing early detection and clinical decision-making. In this review, the therapeutic advances, including sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, anti-fibrotic therapies, mitochondrial-targeted interventions, regenerative medicine, gene therapy, and RNA-based therapeutics, are discussed, with a focus on the precision medicine approach. Finally, we present current challenges in data integration, clinical validation, cost-effectiveness, and ethical issues, and highlight future directions in digital twins, multi-omics integration, and AI-driven personalized cardiology. The combination of these technologies has the potential to revolutionize the prevention and management of diabetic cardiomyopathy and improve cardiovascular outcomes in patients with diabetes.

title: Prognostic value of early post-admission pan-immune-inflammation value in Takotsubo syndrome.
authorString: Sans-Roselló J, Frances BS, Peleg G, Ribas-Closa A, Khakwani MM, Kardenass AE, Sharma V, Torres-Ruiz G, Alkhaldi MM, Cahís-Vela J, Nagar AG, Cabrera-Fernández MA, Medvedofsky D, Cieza-Gómez LA, Martínez-Rubio A, García-García HM.
abstractText:
Background

Inflammation has been associated with adverse outcomes in Takotsubo syndrome (TTS), but the prognostic value of pan-immune-inflammation value (PIV) has not been evaluated in this condition. We assessed whether PIV measured at days 3-5 provides prognostic information beyond clinical characteristics and admission PIV.

Methods

We retrospectively studied 768 patients with TTS from two tertiary centers. PIV was calculated at admission and at days 3-5. A prespecified day-5 landmark analysis evaluated one-year major adverse clinical events (MACE), defined as all-cause death, heart failure events, arrhythmia requiring hospitalization, stroke, or acute myocardial infarction, and the incremental prognostic value of PIV at days 3-5.

Results

The landmark cohort included 722 patients with 218 MACE events. In the primary complete-case analysis (n = 692; 206 events), PIV at days 3-5 was independently associated with MACE after adjustment for clinical variables and admission PIV (HR per doubling, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.16-1.42; p < 0.001), whereas admission PIV was not (HR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.86-1.02; p = 0.142). Adding PIV at days 3-5 to the clinical plus admission-PIV model increased the C-index from 0.659 to 0.682 (ΔC-index, 0.024; 95% CI, 0.005-0.043; bootstrap p = 0.015). The association was approximately linear on the log₂ PIV scale and robust across sensitivity analyses.

Conclusions

PIV measured at days 3-5 was independently associated with one-year MACE and provided incremental prognostic information beyond clinical characteristics and admission PIV. Early post-admission PIV may represent a readily available adjunct to risk assessment, although external validation is required.

title: Estimated Small Dense LDL Cholesterol and Coronary Artery Disease in Familial Hypercholesterolemia.
authorString: Delialis D, Rizos CV, Aivalioti E, Moustou C, Liamis G, Skoumas I, Sfikas G, Kolovou G, Rallidis L, Garoufi A, Tziomalos K, Skalidis E, Kotsis V, Mavrokefalou E, Doumas M, Lambadiari V, Anagnostis P, Filippatos T, Boufidou A, Giannakopoulou V, Anastasiou G, Spantidakis S, Vlachopoulos C, Dima I, Koumaras C, Prodromiadou E, Kolovou V, Fakas G, Papathanasiou KA, Attilakos A, Agapakis D, Zacharis E, Antza C, Antonopoulou A, Boutari C, Kountouri A, Pappa M, Koukou E, Mpellou E, Liberopoulos E, Stamatelopoulos K.
abstractText:
Aim

Recent evidence reports good agreement between measured and estimated small-dense low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (EsdLDL-C) using a readily applicable formula. Its clinical utility in heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) has not yet been evaluated. We aimed to evaluate the sex-specific associations of pre-treatment EsdLDL-C with coronary artery disease (CAD) prevalence in adult patients with HeFH and its discriminative value beyond LDL-C.

Methods

Data from consecutively recruited adults with a clinical diagnosis of HeFH from an ongoing registry (HELLAS-FH, n = 3,276) were analyzed. Patient demographics, lipid parameters, CAD risk factors, and CAD prevalence at registry enrollment were evaluated. EsdLDL-C was calculated at pre-treatment (i.e., before any hypolipidemic therapy initiation) using the Sampson equation.

Results

EsdLDL-C was associated with an increased prevalence of type 2 diabetes and hypertension, a higher body mass index and triglycerides, and lower high-density lipoprotein cholesterol. EsdLDL-C was also the strongest independent lipid-associated factor for CAD (OR: 1.24, p＜0.001). This association was more pronounced in women (OR 1.57, p＜0.001). EsdLDL-C showed higher CAD discrimination than LDL-C (AUC 0.611 vs. 0.522). Incorporating EsdLDL-C into the best discriminative model improved discriminative ability vs the core model (AUC 0.831 vs 0.828, p = 0.038) and overall model fit (ΔAIC) = -10.3). This incremental predictive value was driven predominantly by females (ΔAIC = -14.1; AUC 0.787 vs 0.769, p = 0.015).

Conclusion

In a large sample of patients with clinical HeFH, EsdLDL-C was incrementally associated with CAD beyond LDL-C. This finding was more pronounced in women. The clinical utility of this readily available lipid marker as a risk enhancer should therefore be further investigated.

title: Interleukin-17D deficiency attenuates atherosclerosis by diminishing macrophage inflammation and promoting M2 phenotype.
authorString: Hou J, Gu X, Li X, Zhao J, Weng R, Deng Q, Guo J, Zhong W, Huang Q, Liu S.
abstractText:
Introduction

Macrophages are central to atherosclerosis by driving vascular inflammation, plaque growth, and instability. Although interleukin-17D (IL-17D) has been linked to endothelial inflammation, its role in macrophage-mediated atherosclerosis remains unclear.

Objectives

This study investigated the function and mechanism of macrophage IL-17D in atherosclerosis.

Methods

Using IL-17D knockout, macrophage-specific IL-17D knockdown, and macrophage-specific Spi-B knockdown mouse models on an ApoE-/- background, we assessed aortic lesion burden, necrotic core formation, macrophage accumulation, inflammatory responses, and macrophage polarization. Mechanistic studies were performed using transcriptomic analysis, ChIP-PCR, and luciferase reporter assays.

Results

IL-17D deficiency markedly reduced atherosclerotic plaque formation in the whole aorta and aortic root, decreased necrotic core size, and limited macrophage accumulation and vascular inflammation. Both in vitro and in vivo, IL-17D deficiency promoted M2 macrophage polarization while suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines. Macrophage-specific IL-17D knockdown similarly attenuated atherosclerotic lesion development and inflammation. Mechanistically, IL-17D deficiency activated the Spi-B-STAT6 transcriptional axis. Macrophage-specific Spi-B knockdown reversed the anti-atherosclerotic effects of IL-17D deficiency, confirming its functional importance. Rosuvastatin suppressed IL-17D expression, and IL-17D repression contributed to its anti-inflammatory and anti-atherogenic effects.

Conclusions

These findings identify macrophage-derived IL-17D as a key regulator of atherosclerosis. Targeting IL-17D may promote protective M2 polarization and alleviate vascular inflammation, offering a potential therapeutic strategy for atherosclerotic disease.

title: Bergenin attenuates diabetic cardiomyopathy by inhibiting oxidative stress and ferroptosis through modulation of the YAP signaling axis.
authorString: Kundu S, Yadav M, Mugale MN, Sahu BD.
abstractText:
Aims

Diabetes mellitus-associated cardiac dysfunction arises from metabolic imbalance, oxidative stress, inflammation, maladaptive remodeling, and impaired cardiac performance. Bergenin (BER), a naturally occurring small molecule with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and metabolic regulatory properties, has shown therapeutic potential; however, its role in diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) remains unclear. This study investigated the cardioprotective effects of BER in DCM, with particular emphasis on oxidative stress, the Hippo-Yes-associated protein (YAP), and ferroptosis signaling axis.

Materials and methods

DCM was induced in rats using a high-fat diet combined with low-dose streptozotocin (STZ). Diabetic rats received BER (25 or 50 mg/kg/day) or empagliflozin (10 mg/kg/day). Cardiac function was evaluated by echocardiography, followed by histopathological and molecular analyses. To further investigate the underlying mechanisms, H9c2 cardiomyoblasts exposed to high glucose were used for in vitro assessment of oxidative stress, Hippo-YAP signaling, and ferroptosis-related markers.

Key findings

In vivo, BER treatment significantly improved cardiac function, attenuated histopathological injury, and reduced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and fibrosis in diabetic rats. Consistent with these findings, in vitro, BER reduced reactive oxygen species generation, restored mitochondrial integrity, and prevented high glucose-induced injury in H9c2 cells. Mechanistically, BER modulated YAP signaling and suppressed ferroptosis-related changes. YAP silencing attenuated the protective effects of BER, supporting a critical role for YAP in mediating its anti-ferroptotic effects.

Significance

These findings demonstrate that BER exerts cardioprotective effects against diabetes-associated cardiac dysfunction and provide mechanistic evidence implicating the YAP-ferroptosis axis in this protection. Further studies are warranted to establish its translational potential.

title: The ascending aorta and vascular profile in recreational masters runners: a cross-sectional study.
authorString: Sacharczuk W, Dankowski R, Tritt D, Szałek-Goralewska A, Kuciara M, Baszko A.
abstractText:
Purpose

Endurance exercise remodels the large arteries, but whether a recreational training dose is sufficient to induce such remodelling is unclear. Masters recreational runners over 40 years are under-represented in this research. We compared the ascending aortic diameter and vascular profile of these runners with sedentary controls of similar age.

Methods

This cross-sectional study included 42 masters recreational runners (at least 20 km per week for at least one year) and 27 sedentary controls, all over 40 years, free of cardiovascular disease and without bicuspid aortic valve or connective tissue disorder. We measured the ascending aortic diameter and left ventricular function by transthoracic echocardiography, and brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV) and the ankle-brachial index (ABI) by oscillometry. Circulating collagen-turnover markers (CTX-I, MMP-2) were assayed. The aortic diameter was compared between groups by regression.

Results

The ascending aorta was wider in runners (3.25 vs. 2.90 cm; p = 0.001; Cliff's delta 0.45). The difference persisted after adjustment for age, sex and height (beta 0.31 cm; p = 0.001) and in sensitivity analyses. No aortic diameter reached 4.0 cm; all remained within normal limits. The ABI was higher in runners (1.07 vs. 1.03; p = 0.007), and baPWV did not differ (p = 0.069); both stayed within normal limits. CTX-I and MMP-2 did not differ, and left ventricular function was preserved.

Conclusion

These findings are consistent with modest, exercise-associated aortic remodelling rather than overt aortopathy in recreational masters runners over 40 years.

title: Continuous Stellate Ganglion Block Bridging to Cardiac Sympathetic Denervation in a Long QT Syndrome Neonate.
authorString: Meynet P, Mossetti V, Guerrera F, Ruffini E, Cerrina A, Gennari F, Angelini F, De Ferrari GM, Dusi V, Gabbarini F.
abstractText:
Background

Congenital long QT syndrome (LQTS) with neonatal onset carries a high risk of drug-refractory ventricular arrhythmias. Continuous percutaneous left stellate ganglion block (PLSGB) as a bridge to left cardiac sympathetic denervation (LCSD) is unexplored in neonates.

Case summary

We present a newborn female with in utero onset LQTS, complicated by functional 2:1 atrioventricular block and torsades de pointes (TdP). Despite pacemaker implantation, propranolol, and mexiletine, TdP recurred. At 25 days of life, continuous PLSGB with ropivacaine suppressed TdP. At 4 months, video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS)-LCSD was performed, with no ventricular arrhythmia recurrence in 24 months.

Novelty

First reported case of continuous PLSGB in a neonate with LQTS; among the few VATS-LCSD cases under 1 year.

Take-home messages

Early sympathetic neuromodulation should be considered in high-risk pediatric LQTS when medical therapy fails, as a bridge to LCSD. VATS-LCSD is feasible and safe even under 1 year.

title: A Novel Method for Assessing Left Bundle Branch Capture Using the Bidirectional Conduction Time Difference Between Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing and Coronary Sinus Leads.
authorString: Goto K, Batul SA, Subzposh FA, Shah N, Kazemian P, Demchuk K, Chang GDW, Orlov MV, Vijayaraman P.
abstractText:
Background

Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is an established conduction system pacing strategy; however, confirming left bundle branch (LBB) capture remains challenging.

Objective

We propose a novel method for LBB capture confirmation based on the bidirectional conduction time difference between the LBBAP and coronary sinus (CS) leads.

Methods

This observational study included 60 patients undergoing de novo left bundle branch-optimized cardiac resynchronization therapy. LBB capture was defined by (1) paced QRS transition, (2) LBB potential with current of injury, or (3) ΔV6 R-wave peak time ≥10 ms. LBBAP-to-CS and CS-to-LBBAP conduction times were measured. ΔLBB-CS ([CS-to-LBBAP] - [LBBAP-to-CS]) was compared between nonselective LBB pacing (NS-LBBP) and left ventricular septal pacing (LVSP).

Results

Among 60 patients (74.7±10.4 years; 42 men), 25 had left bundle branch block and 17 had non-specific intraventricular conduction delay. LBB capture was confirmed in 45 patients (75.0%). LBBAP-to-CS was 114.3±28.0 ms during NS-LBBP (n=43) and 134.2±19.0 ms during LVSP (n=29), whereas CS-to-LBBAP was 143.4±28.5 ms (n=60). ΔLBB-CS was greater during NS-LBBP than LVSP (27.5±9.9 vs. 7.9±7.4 ms, P<0.01). Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis identified a 21.5 ms cutoff for LBB capture (74.4% sensitivity; 100% specificity; area under curve [AUC] 0.95). In patients with baseline LBBB (n=25), a 20.5 ms cutoff for LBB capture yielded 92.9% sensitivity, 100% specificity, and an AUC of 0.99.

Conclusion

ΔLBB-CS ≥ 21.5ms may serve as a novel adjunctive marker of LBB capture during LOT-CRT, with greater diagnostic accuracy at a 20.5 ms cutoff in patients with baseline LBBB.

title: Dual Versus Mono Antiplatelet Therapy in Mild Versus Moderate Ischemic Stroke: A Post Hoc Analysis of the ATAMIS Randomized Trial.
authorString: Zhang J, Cui Y, Wang Y, Chen HS.
abstractText:
Background

This prespecified post hoc analysis of the ATAMIS trial (Antiplatelet Therapy in Acute Mild to Moderate Ischemic Stroke) aimed to investigate whether the benefit of dual antiplatelet therapy versus aspirin alone differs in patients with mild versus moderate stroke.

Methods

Using data from the modified intention‑to‑treat population of the ATAMIS trial, eligible patients were divided into mild (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] score 4-5) and moderate (NIHSS score 6-10) groups. The primary outcome was early neurological deterioration at 7 days, defined as an increase in the NIHSS score of ≥2 points from baseline. Safety outcomes included bleeding events and intracranial hemorrhage within 90 days. Binary logistic regression, Cox regression, and generalized linear models were used as appropriate. Adjusted models included age, sex, diabetes, hypertension, onset-to-treatment time, stroke cause, and other imbalanced baseline variables. Treatment-by-baseline stroke severity interaction was assessed.

Results

A total of 2915 patients were included, including 1992 (68.4%) with mild stroke and 923 (31.6%) with moderate stroke. Median age was 66 years (interquartile range, 59-73); 35.0% were women. Clopidogrel plus aspirin was associated with a significantly lower risk of early neurological deterioration compared with aspirin alone in the moderate stroke group (adjusted odds ratio, 0.31 [95% CI, 0.17-0.59]; P<0.001), whereas no significant difference was observed in the mild stroke group (adjusted odds ratio, 0.96 [95% CI, 0.66-1.41]; P=0.841). A significant interaction was identified between treatment effect and NIHSS score subgroup (Pinteraction=0.003). The occurrence of bleeding events and intracranial hemorrhage was similar between treatment groups in both severity subgroups.

Conclusions

In patients with acute mild-to-moderate ischemic stroke, the benefit of clopidogrel plus aspirin versus aspirin alone in preventing early neurological deterioration at 7 days may be greater among patients with moderate stroke (NIHSS score 6-10) than among those with mild stroke (NIHSS score 4-5), without an increased risk of bleeding. These findings suggest that baseline stroke severity may inform antiplatelet therapy selection, and warrant confirmation in future prospective studies.

title: Multidimensional sleep health: risk of cardiovascular disease and mortality, and mediation by plasma proteins.
authorString: Wei Z, Xiao Q, Wang S, Liu L, Meng D, Mao Z, Lu R, Hou R, Zhu X.
abstractText:
Background

Sleep health is a recognised determinant of cardiovascular health, but most previous research has examined individual sleep traits in relation to cardiovascular disease and mortality. The molecular pathways linking multidimensional sleep health to these outcomes remain insufficiently explored. We aimed to examine these associations and identify circulating proteins showing potential mediation signals in these relationships.

Methods

We analysed data on 257,509 individuals from the UK Biobank, including 26,984 with available plasma proteomic data. Using baseline questionnaire data collected by UK Biobank, we calculated a seven-component sleep health score (SHS) and derived data-driven sleep patterns using K-prototypes clustering. We used multivariable Cox proportional hazards models to examine the associations of the SHS and, separately, the sleep patterns with incident coronary heart disease, stroke, atrial fibrillation and heart failure, as well as cardiovascular and overall mortality. Lastly, we identified SHS-related proteins using linear regression, with representative proteins selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, and mediation analyses performed.

Results

Higher SHS was associated with lower risks of coronary heart disease, stroke, atrial fibrillation, heart failure, cardiovascular mortality, and overall mortality, with the strongest associations observed for heart failure and coronary heart disease. Mixed sleep disturbance and non-restorative sleep patterns were associated with higher risks across multiple outcomes. Proteomic analyses identified 188 SHS-related proteins, mainly enriched in inflammatory, immune, and chemotactic pathways. Exploratory mediation analyses identified 34 proteins with potential mediation signals, among which HGF, IGF2R, and FABP4 showed recurrent cross-outcome signals.

Conclusions

Poor multidimensional sleep health was associated with higher cardiovascular disease and mortality risks, with exploratory proteomic analyses suggesting potential involvement of circulating proteins related to inflammation, immunity, chemotaxis, and metabolic dysregulation. These findings support multidimensional sleep assessment as a population-level prevention strategy and provide candidate molecular pathways for future mechanistic and interventional studies.

title: Perioperative Management of Decompensated Peripartum Cardiomyopathy With Severe Left Ventricular Dysfunction: A Case Report.
authorString: Ramkeesoon R, Sang AC, Singh K, Ramdin C.
abstractText: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is a potentially life-threatening cause of heart failure that may be difficult to distinguish from the physiological symptoms of pregnancy. We report the case of a 42-year-old woman at 34 weeks of gestation who presented with progressive dyspnea and was found to have severe global left ventricular systolic dysfunction with an ejection fraction of approximately 20%. Despite initial improvement with diuresis, she developed recurrent acute decompensated heart failure requiring intensive care unit readmission. Point-of-care ultrasonography (POCUS) demonstrated pulmonary congestion and reduced forward flow, with a left ventricular outflow tract velocity-time integral (LVOT VTI) of 10 cm. Following hemodynamic optimization with diuresis and inotropic support, cesarean delivery was performed under general anesthesia with invasive monitoring and titrated vasoactive support. Postoperatively, LVOT VTI increased to 15 cm with corresponding clinical improvement. This case highlights the value of serial hemodynamic assessment, including POCUS, and multidisciplinary perioperative management in severe PPCM with recurrent decompensation.

title: Effect of Microvascular Disease on Re-amputation Risk after Unilateral Amputation due to Diabetes or Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Czerniecki JM, Suckow BD, Henderson AW, Norvell DC.

journal.title: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery

abstractText:
Objective

The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between manifestations of microvascular disease (MVD) and other factors on re-amputation risk within 12 months following incident unilateral lower extremity amputation.

Methods

This was a retrospective cohort study of 8 924 patients with first unilateral transmetatarsal, transtibial, or transfemoral amputation secondary to diabetes and or peripheral arterial disease, identified through a Veterans Affairs database. Re-amputation was defined as any subsequent ipsilateral soft tissue or bony revision or amputation to a higher level. The presence of MVD was determined using a composite variable that required the involvement of each subcomponent (neuropathy, nephropathy, and retinopathy), and also by evaluating each of the subcomponent MVD variables separately. Twenty-nine additional risk factors were evaluated in relation to the primary outcome of re-amputation. A competing risk analysis estimated the cumulative incidence of re-amputation. The effect of risk factors on re-amputation risk was estimated by computing subdistribution hazard ratios (sub-HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

Results

The twelve month re-amputation risk was 38.0% (transmetatarsal), 27.2% (transtibial), and 14.1% (transfemoral). The combined MVD variable was not significantly associated with re-amputation risk. However, re-amputation after transmetatarsal amputation was significantly elevated in patients with retinopathy, leukocytosis, or those who were on kidney dialysis, with the highest risk in those with all three (sub-HR 2.2, 95% CI 1.8 - 2.6). Similarly, for transtibial patients, the risk was higher in the presence of retinopathy, leukocytosis, and kidney dialysis, and in those with a prior ipsilateral revascularisation and those on warfarin. The highest risk was observed in those with all factors present (sub-HR 2.1, 95% CI 1.6 - 2.7).

Conclusion

This study identified an important association between the pre-amputation diagnosis of retinopathy and risk for subsequent failure of primary healing and need for re-amputation. Presence of retinopathy should be considered when evaluating potential failure of healing during amputation level decisions.

title: Polarimetric Imaging: In Search for Clinically Meaningful Vulnerability.
authorString: Minami Y, Ako J.

title: Targeting Metabolic Drivers of Cardiovascular Disease: Insights for Therapeutic Innovation.
authorString: Kansakar U, Hyman M, Volpe E, Mone P, Qin Y, Santulli G.
abstractText: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide, and metabolic dysfunction is increasingly recognized as an important component of its pathophysiology. Clinical evidence supports a role for dysregulated lipid and glucose metabolism in atherosclerosis, heart failure, and cardiometabolic disease, while alterations in amino acid metabolism, mitochondrial energetics, redox signaling, and immunometabolic pathways are supported by growing experimental and observational evidence. Advances in metabolomics, systems biology, and multi-omics approaches have further identified metabolic signatures associated with cardiovascular phenotypes and have provided new insights into pathways regulating endothelial function, vascular inflammation, oxidative stress, and cardiac remodeling. This review synthesizes established clinical evidence and emerging experimental findings on metabolic mechanisms in CVD, with particular emphasis on their potential therapeutic and biomarker implications. We discuss current and investigational strategies targeting lipid and glucose metabolism, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and immunometabolic signaling, while distinguishing clinically validated approaches from those that remain primarily preclinical or hypothesis-generating. Key translational challenges include the complexity and tissue specificity of metabolic networks, limitations of existing experimental models, potential safety liabilities, and the need for longitudinal studies integrating metabolic and clinical phenotypes. Finally, we examine how metabolomics, AI, organ-on-chip models, and systems-level approaches could improve target identification, patient stratification, and therapeutic development. These advances provide a framework for translating mechanistic insights into metabolism-informed cardiovascular therapies and biomarkers, while highlighting the evidence gaps that must be addressed before broader clinical implementation.

title: Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Modeling to Predict Drug-Drug Interactions of Aficamten in the Chinese Population.
authorString: Wang Z, Wu X, Jia R, Wang H.
abstractText:
Background

Aficamten is a next-generation cardiac myosin inhibitor (CMI) developed for the treatment of obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM). Although extensive clinical pharmacology studies have been conducted in Caucasian populations, limited information is available regarding drug-drug interaction (DDI) risks in the Chinese population. Given the contribution of multiple cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes to aficamten metabolism and inter-ethnic differences in CYP-mediated metabolic capacity, it is important to characterize DDI risks and associated changes in aficamten exposure in Chinese subjects.

Methods

A whole-body physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model of aficamten was developed using clinical data from Caucasian subjects and extrapolated to the Chinese population. The PBPK model was subsequently applied to compare aficamten exposure between Chinese and Caucasian populations and to predict DDIs in Chinese subjects.

Results

Ethnic sensitivity analysis indicated that the key PK parameters of aficamten (AUC0-∞, Cmax, and T1/2) were comparable between Caucasian and Chinese populations. Overall, the predicted DDI magnitudes in the Chinese population were generally consistent with the corresponding Caucasian DDI simulations. Specifically, the model predicted that co-administration with the broad-spectrum CYP inhibitors amiodarone and fluconazole increased the AUC0-∞ of aficamten by 1.43- and 2.27-fold, respectively, whereas the strong inducers carbamazepine and rifampicin decreased its exposure by 35% and 71%, respectively. Notably, under the simulated fluconazole or amiodarone co-administration scenarios, the predicted AUC0-∞ of CYP2D6 intermediate metabolizers (IMs) was 2.22-fold and 1.50-fold higher than that in CYP2D6 normal metabolizers (NMs), respectively.

Conclusion

The PBPK model predicted substantial changes in aficamten exposure with broad-spectrum CYP inhibitors (eg, amiodarone, fluconazole) and strong CYP inducers (eg, carbamazepine, rifampicin), and identified CYP2D6 IMs receiving fluconazole or amiodarone as potentially sensitive scenarios. These model-based findings provide quantitative information for DDI risk assessment in Chinese subjects but require clinical confirmation.

title: Knee Flexion and Popliteal Artery Contrast Arrival in Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Pilot Analysis of Bolus Tracking Monitoring Data.
authorString: Tokunaga M, Suhara M, Nagita H, Saigusa H, Sakai K, Okada M, Suzuki Y, Amemiya S, Hayashi T, Hoshina K, Abe O.
abstractText:
Objectives

Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) symptoms can worsen with knee flexion. We examined whether time-enhancement curve (TEC) analysis of discarded bolus tracking data could detect positional differences in popliteal arrival.

Methods

In this secondary analysis of a dedicated research protocol (not routine practice), 22 patients with PAD underwent bilateral lower-extremity CT angiography in extended and flexed positions, at ≈90-degree and at maximum flexion. Arrival time, rise rate, and initial area under the curve (iAUC) were extracted. The flexed and extended limbs were compared with Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.

Results

At maximum flexion, the flexed limb showed a median arrival delay of +1.5 s (p = 0.0002); the within-subject increase from 90-degree flexion to maximum flexion was significant (+0.5 s; p = 0.018). Exploratory subgroup analysis showed significant delays at both angles in unilateral (contralateral ankle-brachial index ≥0.9; n = 15) but not bilateral PAD (n = 7). The rise rate and iAUC did not differ.

Conclusions

The flexed (affected) limb showed delayed popliteal arrival, which was greater at maximum flexion. Because limb position and disease severity were confounded by design, this association is not evidence of causation. These preliminary findings support the feasibility of bolus tracking-derived TEC analysis and motivate within-limb repeated-measures studies.

title: <b>Xinshuaifang improves oxidative stress injury and myocardial remodeling in acute heart failure: Association with the gut-heart axis</b>.
authorString: Wang K, Wang G.
abstractText:
Background

Acute heart failure (AHF) is a leading cause of death from cardiovascular disease and effective treatments are lacking.

Objectives

To investigate whether Xinshuaifang improves oxidative stress injury and myocardial remodeling in AHF mice by regulating the gut-heart axis.

Methods

C57BL/6 mice aged 8-10 weeks and weighing 20-25 g were randomized into 7 groups (n=8/group): control, AHF model, AHF+Xinshuaifang, AHF+control FMT, AHF+intervention FMT, AHF+Xinshuaifang+antibiotics and antibiotics-only control. AHF was induced by isoproterenol injection (5 mg/kg, 7 days). Gut microbiota composition, oxidative stress markers (MDA, GSH, SOD, MPO), cardiac function (LVDd, LVDs, LVEF, NT-proBNP), myocardial fibrosis and tight junction protein expression (ZO-1, Occludin, Claudin-1, Zonulin) were assessed.

Results

Compared with controls, model mice showed significantly reduced Verrucomicrobia and Akkermansia abundance (P<0.01), increased MDA and GSH levels, decreased SOD activity and MPO levels, reduced LVEF, elevated NT-proBNP (P<0.01), decreased ZO-1, Occludin and Claudin-1 expression and increased Zonulin expression. Xinshuaifang intervention significantly reversed all these changes (P<0.01): it increased beneficial bacteria, reduced oxidative stress, improved cardiac function, upregulated ZO-1/Occludin/Claudin-1 and downregulated Zonulin. The FMT intervention group showed similar protective effects, whereas the Xinshuaifang+antibiotics group showed attenuated protection.

Conclusion

Xinshuaifang improves cardiac function and alleviates oxidative stress and fibrosis in AHF mice by regulating gut microbiota, upregulating tight junction proteins and restoring intestinal barrier function.

title: 'I Got Dentures in, So at Least I Can Eat Now': Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples' Perceptions of and Experiences With Removable Dentures.
authorString: Aiyar R, Guzzo GL, Nath S, Reid N, Kapellas K, Groundwater J, Jamieson LM.

journal.title: Health promotion journal of Australia : official journal of Australian Association of Health Promotion Professionals

abstractText:
Introduction

Provision of dentures to people with partial or complete tooth loss aims to restore oral health and improve functions such as chewing and speech, and facial appearance. Lived experience perspectives regarding tooth loss and subsequent oral rehabilitation with dentures are underexplored, particularly among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples in Australia, who experience persistent inequities in oral health and access to dental care. The aim of the current study is to understand Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander adults' perceptions of and experiences with removable dentures.

Methods

The qualitative results are part of a quasi-experimental study exploring culturally safe dental care among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples (retrospectively registered with the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry, trial registration: ACTRN12626000046303). Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 136 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander adults and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis.

Results

Three overarching themes were developed: (1) Decision-making for dentures: Pain, prior treatment and appearance; (2) Unmet needs and expectations of dentures; and (3) Dentures influence social and emotional wellbeing. Together, these themes comprise seven subthemes.

Conclusion

Participants described various impacts including functional challenges related to both tooth loss and denture wearing, limited patient autonomy around denture-related decision-making, high costs and improvements to confidence and social and emotional wellbeing after provision of dentures. SO WHAT?: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander adults highlight the need for equitable approaches to accessible, affordable and patient-centred prosthetic care that ensures a holistic focus on quality of life to promote oral health and wellbeing.

title: <b>The changes of hemodynamics and the effect of RHO kinase regulated by butylphthalein on apoptosis in acute myocardial infarction</b>.
authorString: Feng X, Wang X, Zhang Y, Zhang H.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiomyocyte apoptosis plays a critical role in ventricular remodeling and heart failure following acute myocardial infarction (AMI). The Rho kinase signaling pathway is known to be involved in this pathological process. Butylphthalein, a compound with neuroprotective effects, may exert cardioprotective effects by regulating this pathway.

Objective

This study aims to investigate the effects of butylphthalein on hemodynamic parameters and cardiomyocyte apoptosis in a rat model of AMI and to explore whether these effects are mediated through the Rho kinase signaling pathway.

Methods

Fifty SD rats were randomly divided into five groups: Sham, AMI model, butylphthalein, fasudil (a Rho kinase inhibitor) and combination therapy. AMI was induced by ligation of the left anterior descending coronary artery. Two weeks post-surgery, hemodynamic parameters-including left ventricular systolic pressure (LVSP), left ventricular end-diastolic pressure (LVEDP) and maximal rate of rise and fall of ventricular pressure (±dp/dtmax)-were measured. Cardiomyocyte apoptosis was assessed using TUNEL staining. The expression levels of Bcl-2, Bax, RhoA, ROCK1 and the p-MYPT1/MYPT1 ratio were detected by Western blot.

Results

Rats in the AMI model group exhibited significant hemodynamic impairment and increased cardiomyocyte apoptosis. Compared with the model group, butylphthalein treatment significantly improved LVSP and ±dp/dtmax, reduced LVEDP, decreased the number of TUNEL-positive cells, upregulated Bcl-2 expression, downregulated Bax expression and suppressed the expression of RhoA/ROCK1 and the p-MYPT1/MYPT1 ratio (all P<0.05). The combination of butylphthalein and fasudil resulted in enhanced therapeutic effects, suggesting a synergistic inhibition of Rho kinase activity.

Conclusion

Butylphthalein attenuates cardiomyocyte apoptosis and improves cardiac function in rats with AMI, likely through inhibition of the Rho kinase signaling pathway. These findings support its potential as a therapeutic agent for AMI.All experiments were performed on male Sprague-Dawley rats (n=50).

title: <b><i>Hippophae rhamnoides</i> extract alleviates diabetic cardiomyopathy via the LncRNA NEAT1/miR-147a axis</b>.
authorString: Li W, Kuang C, Xu Q, Zhang D, Jiang Y, Gao C.
abstractText:
Background

The incidence of diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) continues to rise. Although the pathogenesis of DCM has been progressively elucidated, effective treatment options remain insufficient.

Objectives

To investigate the involvement of LncRNA NEAT1 in the protective effect of Hippophae rhamnoides extract on DCM.

Methods

A total of 229 subjects were included, including 127 individuals with DCM. The cardiac condition of the patients was observed using electrocardiography and 5 mL of fasting venous blood was collected. ROC curves assessed the diagnostic value of LncRNA NEAT1 and logistic regression analysis was conducted to identify factors contributing to DCM occurrence. High-glucose (HG) models of H9C2 and HL-1 cells were constructed using 50 mM and 25 mM glucose, respectively. Cells were pretreated with 20 μM SBU to protect them. RT-qPCR detected gene expression and flow cytometry was employed to observe cell apoptosis.

Results

DCM patients exhibited obvious increases in blood glucose and myocardial injury markers. Upregulation of LncRNA NEAT1 was detected in DCM patients and HG-treated cardiomyocytes. LncRNA NEAT1 was identified as a risk factor for the occurrence of DCM. SBU pretreatment was able to downregulate LncRNA NEAT1 expression in damaged cardiomyocytes. oe-LncRNA NEAT1 induced cardiomyocyte apoptosis and increased the expression of myocardial injury markers and oxidative stress levels. Meanwhile, miR-147a was downregulated in DCM patients. miR-147a acted as a negative regulatory factor in SBU-mediated protection of HG cardiomyocytes from damage and could counteract the effects of oe-LncRNA NEAT1 on cardiomyocytes.

Conclusion

LncRNA NEAT1 participates in the protective effect of SBU on damaged cardiomyocytes through miR-147a.

title: <b>Rosmarinic acid attenuates heart failure-related injury through modulation of ferroptosis-related pathways: Network pharmacology and cellular validation</b>.
authorString: Yao Y, Ling J, Wang X.
abstractText:
Background

Ferroptosis-related oxidative injury has been implicated in the progression of heart failure (HF). Rosmarinic acid (RA) has antioxidant and anti-lipid peroxidation properties, but its role in HF-associated ferroptosis-related cardiomyocyte injury remains unclear.

Objectives

This study aimed to investigate whether RA attenuates Ang II-induced cardiomyocyte injury by modulating ferroptosis-related oxidative injury and GPX4/xCT-associated defense responses.

Methods

RA-related targets were retrieved from TCMSP, while HF-related and ferroptosis-related genes were obtained from GeneCards/OMIM and FerrDB. Intersection targets were analyzed using PPI network construction, GO and KEGG enrichment analyses, RA-target-disease-pathway network construction and molecular docking. An Ang II-induced H9c2 cardiomyocyte injury model was established for validation. Cell viability was assessed by CCK-8 assay; ANP and BNP mRNA levels were measured by RT-qPCR; MDA content was measured to evaluate lipid peroxidation; and GPX4 and xCT protein expression was examined by Western blotting.

Results

Twenty-six RA-related targets, 3311 HF-related genes and 1393 ferroptosis-related genes were identified. Intersections yielded 397 HF-associated ferroptosis targets and 9 RA-related candidate targets. Network analysis highlighted PPARG, PTGS2, MAPK1, CDKN1A and CASP3 as important targets. Enrichment analyses indicated associations with oxidative stress, apoptotic regulation, iron ion response, inflammatory signaling, lipid and atherosclerosis, TNF, IL-17 and AGE-RAGE pathways. Molecular docking suggested favorable binding of RA to these targets, especially PPARG and PTGS2. In Ang II-treated H9c2 cells, RA restored cell viability, reduced ANP and BNP expression, decreased MDA accumulation and increased GPX4 and xCT expression; these effects were partially reversed by erastin.

Conclusion

RA may attenuate Ang II-induced cardiomyocyte injury by modulating ferroptosis-related oxidative injury and GPX4/xCT-associated defense responses. These findings provide preliminary computational and cellular evidence supporting RA as a candidate compound for further investigation in HF-related cardiomyocyte injury.

title: <b>Amlodipine besylate and valsartan combined mucoadhesive buccal patch formulations: <i>In-vitro</i> release and <i>ex-vivo</i> permeation studies</b>.
authorString: Anwar N, Gul R, Jan SU, Shahwani GR, Mahmood A, Rabbani T, Abdullah A, Naz S, Jamal F.
abstractText:
Background

Oral fixed-dose combinations of Amlodipine Besylate and Valsartan are widely prescribed for hypertension but are associated with first-pass metabolism and variable bioavailability. Buccal drug delivery provides a favorable substitute to improve systemic availability and provide sustained release.

Objectives

This study aimed to develop and assess mucoadhesive buccal patches containing Amlodipine Besylate and Valsartan to enhance bioavailability and achieve controlled drug release over 24 hours.

Methods

Buccal patches were developed via the solvent-casting method using Hydroxypropyl Methylcellulose, Polyvinylpyrrolidone, Methylcellulose, Sodium Alginate and Metolose as backing membrane polymers. All the prepared films were evaluated for physicochemical parameters by means of X-ray Diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and in vitro and ex vivo drug release. In-vitro drug release was studied with USP Apparatus II (paddle method) in 500 ml 6.8 pH phosphate buffer at 37 ± 0.5°C and 50 rpm for 24 hours. Ex vivo permeation studies were performed using a Franz diffusion cell fitted with rabbit buccal mucosa under similar conditions.

Results

The formulations generally exhibited acceptable physicochemical characteristics within the evaluated parameters. The developed films appeared transparent with a uniform distribution of components. FTIR analysis did not indicate any detectable incompatibility or significant interaction between the drugs and excipients under the study conditions. Among all formulations, F1 contained the highest drug release and permeation. After 24 hours, cumulative release reached 84.45% for amlodipine and 88.03% for valsartan. Ex-vivo permeation was 76.31% and 78.42% for amlodipine and valsartan, respectively. Furthermore, buccal films' histopathological and stability studies were found to be harmless and functioned as an efficient dosage system.

Conclusion

The developed mucoadhesive buccal patches successfully delivered both drugs in a sustained manner. Formulation F1 showed superior release and permeation profiles, suggesting its potential as substitute to conventional oral dosage forms for improved hypertension management.

title: [Diuretic-associated sarcopenia in patients with chronic heart failure: a new clinical and organizational problem].
authorString: Dragunov DO, Sokolova AV, Arutyunov GP.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Probl Sotsialnoi Gig Zdravookhranenniiai Istor Med
journal.title: Problemy sotsial'noi gigieny, zdravookhraneniia i istorii meditsiny
journal.isoabbreviation: Probl Sotsialnoi Gig Zdravookhranenniiai Istor Med

abstractText: Chronic heart failure (CHF) remains one of the leading causes of hospitalization, disability, and mortality among older patients. In this context, sarcopenia is becoming increasingly important, as it is associated with reduced physical functioning, impaired quality of life, and an unfavorable prognosis. The aim of this review was to analyze current evidence on the impact of long-term diuretic therapy, disturbances of sodium and osmotic homeostasis, and the phenomenon of metabolic aestivation on the development of sarcopenia in patients with CHF. The review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA recommendations; the literature search was performed in PubMed, Scopus, eLIBRARY.ru, Google Scholar, WHO IRIS, and other scientific resources. Current evidence suggests that long-term diuretic therapy, osmotic stress, activation of protein catabolism, and increased urea production may be involved in the pathogenesis of sarcopenia. Diuretic-associated sarcopenia has both clinical and organizational significance, as it is associated with increased hospitalization rates, functional dependence, and healthcare costs, supporting the need for sarcopenia screening in patients with CHF receiving long-term diuretic therapy.

title: Association of Risk-Stratified WeChat-Based Tele-Nursing With Self-Care Outcomes and Short-Term Readmission Among Patients With Chronic Heart Failure: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Zhu P, Wang J, Hu Y, Zhou T.
abstractText: Chronic heart failure (CHF) is frequently complicated by post-discharge readmission. This study evaluated structured risk-stratified WeChat-based tele-nursing in routine post-discharge care. This retrospective cohort study included 112 patients with CHF hospitalized during 2023-2024; 58 received tele-nursing and 54 routine follow-up. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed. The primary outcome was 6-month heart failure-related readmission. Six-month readmission occurred in 13.8% versus 31.5% in the unmatched cohort (p = 0.02) and 15.2% versus 32.6% after 1:1 PSM (46 pairs; p = 0.04). The unmatched adjusted Cox estimate was HR 0.43 (95% CI 0.18-0.99), whereas the matched Cox estimate was HR 0.45 (95% CI 0.18-1.08); penalized, complete-case, and Fine-Gray sensitivity analyses were also not statistically significant. The exploratory 12-month HR was 0.55 (95% CI 0.30-1.02; n = 94). All three SCHFI v7.2-C subscales improved more with tele-nursing (all p < 0.001). Tele-nursing was associated with greater improvement in patient-reported self-care and a possible association with lower short-term readmission, which requires prospective confirmation.

title: Factors Associated With the Autonomy of Patients Treated by Haemodialysis in Community Centres. A Cross-Sectional Study.
authorString: Achour A, Béchade C, Lobbedez T, Edet S, Ficheux M, Guillouët S.
abstractText:
Background

In France, haemodialysis is delivered in different settings depending on patients' health status and autonomy. Community centres include self-care and satellite units, which vary in organisation and patient involvement.

Objectives

To describe the characteristics of patients treated in haemodialysis community centres and to identify factors associated with autonomy in self-care units.

Design

Cross-sectional study.

Participants

All patients receiving haemodialysis in community centres in a French region on December 31, 2021.

Measurements

Patient characteristics and multiple dimensions of patient autonomy were recorded. Multivariate analyses assessed associations between patient factors and technical autonomy.

Results

Among 507 patients, 304 were treated in self-care units and 203 in satellite haemodialysis units. Patients in satellite haemodialysis units had a median age of 69 years (IQR 59-78; range 24-90), compared with 66 years (IQR 54-75; range 22-91) in self-care haemodialysis units. They also had more comorbidities. Younger age was associated with greater autonomy in arteriovenous fistula puncture-site dressing (PR 0.97, 95% CI 0.96-0.98), setting the haemodialysis machine (PR 0.97, 95% CI 0.96-0.98), and programming it (PR 0.97, 95% CI 0.95-0.98). Autonomy differed significantly between centres, with centre affiliation significantly associated (p < .001) with autonomy for the arteriovenous fistula puncture-site dressing and machine-related tasks.

Conclusions

Patient characteristics in self-care haemodialysis units did not fully explain autonomy for haemodialysis tasks. Considerable variability between centres was observed, suggesting that centre-related factors may contribute to differences in patient autonomy.

title: Choosing an Appropriate Outlier-Detection Method When Comparing Institutional Performances in Clinical Audits.
authorString: Sui A, Ambler G, Omar RZ, de Belder M, Pavlou M.
abstractText: Clinical audits are essential for monitoring and improving the quality of healthcare with statistical outlier detection used to identify healthcare units whose performance deviates from expected standards. Two commonly used outlier-detection approaches are Common Mean Model (CMM) and Random Effects Logistic Regression (RELR). However, these methods can identify different healthcare units as outliers when applied to the same dataset. Incorrectly flagging a unit as an outlier can have serious consequences, including reputational harm, decreased staff morale, unnecessary regulatory scrutiny, diversion of resources, and loss of public trust. This article investigates the reasons for these discrepancies through a simulation study evaluating the performance of the CMM and RELR under a range of scenarios. The results show that differences in outlier detection are primarily driven by the degree to which a normality assumption holds for each method. When these assumptions are violated, for one or both methods, the two approaches may produce markedly different outlier detection. To choose the most appropriate approach for a given dataset, we recommend assessing each normality assumption, by combining visual diagnostics, such as QQ plots, with quantitative measures, such as Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (CCC).

title: Working Right Ways: Investigating Health Practitioners' Perspectives of Foot Health and Needs for Providing Good Foot Care With and for First Nations Peoples.
authorString: Gerrard J, Godwin Badimaya Yamatji S, Whiteley Wiradjuri K, Charles Kaurna J, Chuter V.

journal.title: Journal of foot and ankle research

abstractText:
Background

History of invasion, ongoing colonisation, and systemic racism excluding First Nations Peoples from healthcare are root causes of health inequalities including disparities in foot health outcomes. Sources of inquiry into current practice, learning, and experience, which may shape reform of providing good foot care with and for First Nations Peoples in the land now known as Australia are health practitioners working in the space. This work seeks to explore foot care service delivery by investigating First Nations and non-Indigenous health practitioners' perspectives regarding providing foot care with and for First Nations Peoples.

Methods

Ways of working are documented in previous work; 'Working right ways in foot health with and for First Nations Peoples: research method guided and governed by First Nations ways of knowing, being, and doing in cross-sectional qualitative study design'. First Nations and non-Indigenous health practitioners provided perspectives with culturally responsive semi-structured interviews guiding talking with consenting participants. Coding utilised constant comparison techniques to explore patterns across the dataset. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis.

Results

Two talking points engaged health practitioners' perspectives of providing foot care with and for First Nations Peoples: (1) What does foot health mean to you as a First Nations or non-Indigenous health practitioner? (2) What are needs for providing good foot care with and for First Nations Peoples? Within responses, themes emerged of mobility and participation, overall health and wellbeing, clinical and biomedical perspective, and advocacy being related to the meaning of foot health. The requirements of cultural safety, workforce, and holistic care were perceived as needed for provision of good foot care with and for First Nations Peoples.

Conclusion

Participants described a meaning of foot health that is relational to physical and spiritual constructs, and central to reclamation of, and continuation of, First Nations cultures; amidst a project of ongoing colonisation. Needs for good foot care provision with and for First Nations Peoples included a workforce continually learning and unlearning to develop cultural capabilities to work with and for, and support, First Nations foot health. This study provides distinct and real first-hand accounts from health practitioners working in the space which the podiatry profession must listen to and receive direction and learning from.

title: Foot Shape in Women With and Without Hallux Valgus Determined Using 3-Dimensional Foot Scanning.
authorString: Limanou GR, Lim PQX, Lithgow MJ, Buldt AK, Munteanu SE, Menz HB.

journal.title: Journal of foot and ankle research

abstractText:
Introduction

Hallux valgus (HV) is a prevalent forefoot deformity that alters foot shape and occurs more frequently in women and older adults. Few studies have investigated the influence of HV on three-dimensional (3D) foot structure in age-matched samples.

Methods

This cross-sectional study utilised data from two separate studies conducted in Melbourne, Australia. Twenty women (mean ± SD age = 63.8 ± 8.7 years) with HV were age-matched to 20 women without HV (63.8 ± 8.6 years). Participants underwent 3D foot scanning, comparing measurements of the most symptomatic HV feet with corresponding control feet. Differences in foot dimensions between groups were calculated using independent sample t-tests.

Results

Women with HV demonstrated larger foot breadth (103.1 ± 6.2 vs. 98.0 ± 5.6, mean difference [MD] = 5.13 mm, p = 0.009), ball girth circumference (245.9 ± 13.9 vs. 234.1 ± 11.5, MD = 11.86 mm, p = 0.006), heel breadth (65.9 ± 3.9 vs. 62.8 ± 3.8, MD = 3.13 mm, p = 0.015), height of top of ball girth (39.9 ± 2.8 vs. 37.4 ± 2.2, MD = 2.56 mm, p = 0.003), and toe 1 angle (24.1 ± 8.0 vs. 9.8 ± 8.0, MD = 14.29°, p < 0.001). There were no differences in rearfoot position (as indicated by heel bone angle) observed between the groups (3.0 ± 2.8 vs. 3.1 ± 3.0°, p = 0.952).

Conclusion

Women with HV exhibited a broader forefoot and heel compared with those without the deformity. Moreover, women with HV displayed a larger ball girth circumference and height of the top of the ball girth, suggesting that vertical dimensional changes occur in this condition. These findings suggest that individuals with HV may benefit from adequate footwear fitting and new lacing techniques and inform the development of targeted footwear modifications or HV-specific footwear manufacturing guidelines.

title: Prenatal ambient ozone exposure and risk of offspring congenital heart disease: A three-level meta-analysis.
authorString: Yao Y, Yuan X, Liao L, All authors have read and approved the final manuscript.

journal.title: Journal of the Air & Waste Management Association (1995)

abstractText: Prenatal exposure to ambient ozone has been hypothesized to increase the risk of congenital heart defects (CHD) in offspring; however, epidemiological evidence remains inconclusive. To quantitatively synthesize the available evidence on the association between prenatal ambient ozone exposure and the risk of congenital heart defects (CHD) in offspring, and to explore potential effect modifiers through subgroup analyses and meta regression. The PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, Embase and CNKI databases were systemically searched from 1970 until April 2026 to find articles related to offspring CHD and periconceptional ozone exposure. Inverse variance weighted random-effects multilevel models were conducted to pool estimates and stratify associations by heart defect type, country income level, study design, investigation time period, and data source. Dose-response relationships were examined via meta-regression and the heterogeneity and publication bias in relevant studies was also examined. A total of 29 studies comprising 302 effect estimates were identified. The overall pooled odds ratio for the association between prenatal ozone exposure and CHD was 1.032 (95% CI: 1.004-1.060). Stronger associations were observed for transposition of the great arteries (OR = 1.172), conotruncal defects (OR = 1.134), and atrioventricular septal defects (OR = 1.204). The embryonic period was the most susceptible exposure window (OR = 1.064, 95% CI: 1.006-1.126). Stronger effects were found in upper-middle-income countries (OR = 1.039), studies conducted after 2020 (OR = 1.145), and hospital-based data (OR = 1.112). Dose-response analysis suggested a 1% odds increase per 10 μg/m3 ozone increment, though not statistically significant. Considerable heterogeneity was observed. This meta-analysis suggests that prenatal ozone exposure may modestly increase CHD risk. The substantial heterogeneity highlights the need for standardized exposure assessment and further prospective studies.

title: Taiwan GEST-TASL-TMASO Joint Position Statement in Managing Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Obesity.
authorString: Cheng PN, Lu CW, Lin CL, Chiang CH, Yang HI, Kao HH, Wang CC, Chou TJ, Chang ML, Hsiao TJ, Peng CY, Huang JF, Chen TP, Dai CY, Yu ML, Huang KC, Kao JH, Lin WY, Liu CJ.

journal.title: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

abstractText: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and obesity share common pathogenesis and are increasingly relevant in clinical care. This joint statement addresses the need for comprehensive guidance in Taiwan for MASLD patients with obesity. The Gastroenterological Society of Taiwan, the Taiwan Association for the Study of the Liver, and the Taiwan Medical Association for the Study of Obesity conducted an evidence-based review, integrating epidemiological data, clinical trial outcomes, and expert consensus to develop position statements covering diagnosis, disease burden, pathogenesis, surveillance, and therapeutic strategies. MASLD prevalence in Taiwanese adults is 30%-45%, reaching 60%-70% in individuals with obesity, with similar high prevalence in children and adolescents. Obesity accelerates hepatic and extrahepatic disease progression, including cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and cardiovascular complications. Lifestyle interventions, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, resmetirom, and bariatric surgery demonstrate efficacy in improving hepatic and metabolic outcomes. Risk stratification using noninvasive tools such as Fibrosis-4 and vibration-controlled transient elastography effectively guides referral and management. A multidisciplinary, precision-based approach, integrating lifestyle modification, pharmacotherapy, surgical options, and risk stratification, is essential for effective MASLD management in patients with obesity, while research into artificial intelligence-driven biomarkers, gut microbiota modulation, and genetic factors represents future directions.

title: Which Small-Sample Correction Should be Used When Analyzing Stepped-Wedge Designs With Time-Varying Treatment Effects?
authorString: Ouyang Y, Taljaard M, Hughes JP, Li F.
abstractText: Stepped-wedge cluster randomized trials (SW-CRTs) evaluate interventions that are sequentially rolled out across clusters. Standard analyses of SW-CRTs typically use immediate-treatment (IT) models, which assume the treatment effects begin at crossover and remain constant thereafter. When treatment effects vary with exposure duration, IT models may misrepresent the target effects. Exposure-time indicator (ETI) models address this by allowing treatment effects to differ by time since exposure and can properly target the time-averaged treatment effect (TATE) and long-term effect (LTE). Like IT models, ETI models require specification of a random-effects structure, which may be misspecified. While robust variance estimators (RVEs) theoretically protect against such misspecification, their empirical performance under ETI models is not well understood. We review RVEs for ETI models and evaluate them in comprehensive simulation studies with continuous and binary outcomes under correctly specified (binary only) and misspecified random-effects structures. We compare the classic sandwich variance, Kauermann-Carroll (KC), Mancl-DeRouen (MD), and Morel-Bokossa-Neerchal (MBN) bias-corrected sandwich variance estimators for inference on the TATE and LTE in primary simulations and additionally evaluate Fay-Graubard (FG) in a sub-study. Our simulations show that under misspecified random-effects structures, model-based standard errors (SE) produced undercoverage, whereas RVEs improved performance under the ETI models. For continuous outcomes, MD with a t-distribution and degrees of freedom equal to the number of clusters minus two gave the closest to nominal coverage probabilities. Surprisingly, however, MBN was the only consistently reliable option for binary outcomes. MD, however, could be unstable in one-cluster-per-sequence designs because of data sparsity. Across scenarios, both model-based SE and RVE for LTE were unstable, indicating that greater caution is needed when targeting LTE under ETI models.

title: The Effect of Acute Beetroot Juice and Caffeine Supplementation on Specific Judo Performance During a Simulated Competition Day in Judo Athletes.
authorString: Karabağ S, Sajedi H, Güler O, Alaeddinoğlu V, Çakır E, Khodadadi D, Akpınar S.
abstractText: Beetroot juice (BJ) and caffeine (CAF) are well-established ergogenic aids for exercise performance. However, little is known about their efficacy and interaction within the specific context of a judo competition day. This study investigated the acute effects of BJ, CAF, and their combination (BJCAF) on judo-specific performance across a simulated competition day. Using a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover design, 35 competitive judo athletes (age 23 ± 5 years; body mass 74 ± 13 kg) completed 4 sessions (BJ, CAF, BJCAF, and placebo), each consisting of 5 trials of judo randori and a Special Judo Fitness Test (SJFT), followed by neuromuscular and cognitive assessments. Compared with placebo, CAF enhanced SJFT performance, neuromuscular function, and cognition in trials 1-3 but not in trial 5 (p < 0.05). Conversely, BJ improved these same metrics in trial 5 (p < 0.05). BJCAF enhanced SJFT performance across trials 1-3 and 5, cognitive functions in trials 1, 2, and 4, and neuromuscular performance in all trials (p < 0.05). Importantly, in trial 5, both BJ and BJCAF conditions yielded improved SJFT performance, neuromuscular function, and cognitive outcomes compared to CAF alone (p < 0.05). The results demonstrate that the ergogenic effect of CAF was not maintained throughout the simulated competition day, whereas BJ provided late-stage benefits. Co-ingestion effectively counteracted the later-session decline observed with CAF alone while maintaining its early advantages. This highlights the importance of considering temporal dynamics and metabolic costs when designing nutritional strategies for multi-bout, high-intensity sports tournaments such as judo.

title: Impact of YAQ001 on the Gut Microbiome, Permeability and Markers of Systemic Inflammation in Patients With Cirrhosis.
authorString: Liu J, Garcia-Guevara F, Macnaughtan J, Jin Y, Ferret-Miñana A, Clasen F, Yuen N, Maset RG, Ramón-Azcón J, Kerbert AJC, Portlock T, Martinez J, Habtesion A, Phillips A, De Chiara F, Ingavle G, Baldwin T, Jimenez C, Zaccherini G, Husi K, Rodriguez-Gandia M, Cordero-Sanchez P, Soeda J, Oben JA, Church K, Li JV, Jalan A, Juanola A, Sola E, Eaton S, Morgan C, Avery T, Kowalski M, Green D, Gander A, Edwards LA, Cox IJ, Cortez-Pinto H, Wiest R, Durand F, Caraceni P, Elosua R, Vila J, Pavesi M, Arroyo V, Davies N, Mookerjee RP, Sandeman S, Mehta G, Marchesi JR, Albillos A, Rohn JL, Andreola F, Shoaie S, Jalan R.

journal.title: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

abstractText:
Background & aims

YAQ001 is a novel, non-absorbable, gut-restricted, multiporous, carbon bead adsorbent. Pre-clinical studies and a clinical trial suggested its therapeutic potential and safety in patients with cirrhosis. This substudy aimed to explore the effects of YAQ001 on the gut microbiome and their exploratory association with biomarkers of gut permeability and systemic inflammation.

Methods

Twenty-eight-patients with cirrhosis were randomized (double-blind) to receive YAQ001 (4 g once daily) or placebo. Gut microbiome and biomarkers of inflammation and gut permeability were assessed at baseline, after 4 and 12 weeks. Changes in biomarkers and relationship with microbiome composition and gene profiling were assessed. The effect of YAQ001 on Klebsiella pneumoniae biofilms was assessed in vitro.

Results

Overall alpha and beta diversity remained unaltered. YAQ001 increased the abundance of bacteria associated with improved gut health such as Adlercreutzia equolifaciens, a bacterium commonly depleted in liver disease, and decreased the abundance of bacteria associated with infections and poor outcomes such as Klebsiella pneumonia, and Streptococcus mutans. YAQ001 impacted positively on virulence factors such as siderophores, fimbriae structures, and lipopolysaccharides that are associated with inflammation and invasion. Antibiotic resistance genes decreased significantly in the YAQ001 group. These changes were associated with a reduction in markers of gut permeability and systemic inflammation. YAQ001 prevented K. pneumoniae biofilms in vitro.

Conclusion

YAQ001 was associated with favourable compositional shifts and trends towards reduced virulence-related gene signatures in the gut microbiome, alongside trends towards improved inflammatory biomarkers. The in vitro anti-biofilm effect of YAQ001 warrants further mechanistic investigation. The findings position YAQ001 as a potential microbiome therapeutic.

title: Factors Associated With Overweight and Obesity Among Adolescents in South Asia: A Narrative Review of Recent Evidence.
authorString: Siddiquee T, Bhowmik B, Moreira NCDV, Munir SB, Nasrin H, Islam T, Mahmud F, Nesa LQ, Akhtar S, Khan S, Khan FR, Amin MR, Khan AKA.
abstractText:
Introduction

Adolescent overweight and obesity are increasing across South Asia, contributing to diabetes and other noncommunicable diseases. Previous reviews have examined prevalence and selected associated factors, but evidence remains heterogeneous across countries, populations and adiposity definitions. This narrative review synthesised recent evidence on prevalence and factors associated with overweight and obesity among South Asian adolescents.

Methods

We conducted a structured narrative review reported in accordance with the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles. PubMed, Scopus and Google Scholar were searched for peer-reviewed studies published from January 2015 to March 2025, supplemented by targeted searches through August 2026. Studies of adolescents aged 10-19 years and predominantly adolescent populations with overlapping age ranges were considered. Primary studies and evidence syntheses were analysed separately. Methodological quality was evaluated using design-appropriate Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal checklists, and findings were synthesised narratively.

Results

Thirteen publications were included: eight primary studies and five systematic reviews or meta-analyses. Prevalence varied by population, setting, adiposity measure and classification system. Regional meta-analytic estimates were 12.4% for overweight, 6.6% for obesity and 19.3% for combined overweight/obesity, although these were not directly comparable with adolescent-specific primary studies. More consistent evidence concerned physical inactivity, sedentary behaviour and unhealthy dietary practices. Associations with socioeconomic position, urban residence, sex and gender, familial factors and media exposure were more limited and context dependent. Sleep, mental health, food insecurity and neighbourhood environments were insufficiently examined. Most primary evidence was cross-sectional and school based.

Conclusions

Adolescent overweight and obesity in South Asia are associated with behavioural, dietary and socio-environmental factors within changing food and urban environments. Interpretation is limited by heterogeneous definitions, uneven country coverage and predominantly cross-sectional designs. Standardised population-based and longitudinal studies, including out-of-school adolescents, are needed to guide context-specific prevention.

title: Correction to "Skin Closure Techniques After Cardiac Implantable Electronic Device Implantation and Their Impact on Pocket Complications: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis".
