title: National Trends and Predictors of Adverse Outcomes in Hypoglycemia Hospitalizations in the United States, 2017-2022.
authorString: Bin Gulzar AH, Hakeem S, Sohail MU, Tahir A, Tariq T, Shehroz R, Khan MS, Rahim I, Aiman U, Ashraf MA, Rai S, Mavora M, Cheema AAA, Nadeem H.
abstractText:
Objective

To assess national trends and inpatient outcomes among adults hospitalized with a primary diagnosis of hypoglycemia in the United States from 2017 to 2022.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of the National Inpatient Sample. Adult hospitalizations aged 18 years or older with a principal ICD-10-CM diagnosis of hypoglycemia were included. The annual share of primary hypoglycemia hospitalizations was calculated per 100,000 adult NIS discharges. Outcomes included in-hospital mortality, length of stay(LOS), and inflation-adjusted hospital cost standardized to 2022 US dollars. Multivariable survey-weighted logistic regression was used for mortality, a survey-weighted generalized linear model (GLM) with a quasi-Poisson distribution and log link was used for LOS, and a survey-weighted GLM with a gamma distribution and log link was used for inflation-adjusted hospital cost.

Results

The analysis included 330,910 weighted hypoglycemia hospitalizations. Mean age was 67 years; 52% were women; and 70% were Medicare-insured. Diabetes mellitus (91%) was the most common comorbidity, while obesity (17%) was least common. Primary-hypoglycemia discharges peaked in 2019 (195 per 100,000 adult NIS discharges), declined in 2021 (180), and increased again in 2022 (190). Mortality occurred in 1.6%, and median LOS was 3 days. Compared with 2017, adjusted mortality odds were higher in 2020 (OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.04-1.61), 2021 (OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.16-1.79), and 2022 (OR 1.33, 95% CI 1.07-1.65). Similarly, LOS and hospital costs were also higher in 2020, 2021, and 2022 compared to 2017. Congestive heart failure (CHF) and AF were associated with higher mortality odds, LOS, and cost.

Conclusion

Primary hypoglycemia hospitalizations declined during the pandemic years but became more severe and resource-intensive over time. Patients with CHF or AF had higher mortality, higher LOS, and higher hospital costs, highlighting the need for integrated hypoglycemia surveillance and cardiometabolic care.

title: A retrospective analysis of health care utilization and costs by body mass index category among adults with, or at risk of, cardiovascular disease.
authorString: Zhang Y, Huang A, Mojdami D, Gronroos NN, Gremel GW, Quicksell K, Chinthammit C.

journal.title: Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy

abstractText:
Background

There is a need for more real-world evidence to better understand the long-term effect of excess weight on health care resource utilization (HCRU) and costs over time among people at risk for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) (primary prevention population) and those with established ASCVD (secondary prevention population).

Objective

To describe all-cause HCRU and costs during a 5-year follow-up period, stratified by body mass index (BMI) category among commercially insured US adults at risk of or with known ASCVD in both primary and secondary prevention populations.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study used Optum administrative claims and electronic health record (EHR) data from January 1, 2007, to December 31, 2023 (study period). Included adult patients had at least 1 BMI measure in the identification period (January 1, 2008, through December 31, 2018), with the date of the first BMI measure being the index date. Patients had to have continuous health plan enrollment on a commercial insurance plan and EHR clinical activity for 12 months before index (baseline period) and 5 years after index (follow-up period). Patients were assigned to the primary prevention cohort if there was evidence of ASCVD risk factors, and patients with evidence of ASCVD conditions were assigned to the secondary prevention cohort. Cohort-specific results were reported by BMI category. The outcomes of interest were all-cause HCRU and costs. Descriptive results were reported, and adjusted cost ratios were calculated using multivariable modeling with repeated measures.

Results

A total of 26,430 patients were included in the primary prevention cohort (37.9% female, 73.5% non-Hispanic White, and mean [SD] age = 53.9 [9.0] years), and 9,020 patients were included in the secondary prevention cohort (28.9% female, 73.9% non-Hispanic White, and mean [SD] age = 56.1 [9.8] years). Numerically, unadjusted total all-cause HCRU and costs increased with higher BMI classes; this was consistent across years of follow-up. In both the primary and secondary prevention cohorts, total costs among people with obesity ranged from 1.1-fold (class 1, ≥30 to <35 kg/m2) to 1.3-fold (class 3, ≥40 kg/m2) higher than those of people with normal weight after adjustment.

Conclusions

This real-world study highlights the increasing economic impact of obesity in commercially insured people with or at risk of ASCVD. Future research is warranted to examine weight management strategies as an integral part of the primary and secondary prevention of ASCVD.

title: Unequal spending, unequal care: Race and ethnicity and their interactions with clinical and socioeconomic factors in health care expenditures among older adults with cardiovascular disease.
authorString: Zakeri M, Arefin P, Sansgiry SS.

journal.title: Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy

abstractText:
Background

Cardiovascular disease (CVD) accounts for the highest health care expenditures in the United States, with persistent disparities among racial and ethnic minorities.

Objective

To evaluate factors contributing to differences in total health care expenditure among Hispanic, non-Hispanic Black (hereafter Black), and non-Hispanic White (hereafter White) adults aged 65 years and older with CVD.

Methods

This study had a repeated cross-sectional design and used data from the Medical Expenditure Panel Survey (2014-2021). The primary outcome was the total health care direct expenditure (inpatient, outpatient, and medical and pharmacy cost). Inclusion criteria were being aged at least 65 years and having at least 1 lifetime diagnosis of CVD. Survey-weighted descriptive analyses were conducted, followed by 3 hierarchical log-linear regression models. Model 1 included race and ethnicity only. Model 2 adjusted for clinical factors (sex, age at first CVD diagnosis, CVD severity, and Elixhauser comorbidity score). Model 3 additionally incorporated socioeconomic, functional, and contextual factors, including education, income, insurance status, physical and cognitive limitations, geographic region, and survey year.

Results

The final sample included 8,585 participants (weighted N = 11,412,569). In the unadjusted model, Hispanic and Black participants had 9% (P = 0.03) and 11% (P = 0.005) lower health care expenditures, respectively, compared with White participants. After adjustment for clinical factors, Hispanic participants had 26% lower expenditures (P < 0.001), and the Black-White difference was no longer statistically significant. In the fully adjusted model, race and ethnicity were not independently associated with expenditure; however, significant interactions were identified between race and ethnicity and sex (Hispanic women: +32%, P = 0.002), physical limitations (Hispanic: +131%, P = 0.005; Black: +118%, P = 0.04), cognitive limitations (Black: +129%, P = 0.008), and geographic region, alongside independent associations with education, income, insurance status, and physical and cognitive limitations.

Conclusions

Differences in health care expenditure among older adults with CVD appear to be shaped by a combination of clinical, socioeconomic, and contextual factors rather than race and ethnicity alone. These findings highlight the importance of equity-focused, value-based strategies that address underlying social determinants of health to improve access, reduce disparities in health care utilization, and potentially lower overall health care costs. Importantly, lower expenditures may reflect underutilization of necessary care rather than improved efficiency.

title: Joint segmentation and landmark detection for cardiac MRI with multi-scale inter-task feature fusion and gradient-bridged anatomical constraints.
authorString: Chen H, Liu Z, Hu C.
abstractText:
Background

Segmentation and landmark detection are essential yet complex tasks in Cardiac MRI (CMR) for quantitative assessment of the heart. Existing automatic CMR analysis methods typically handle the two tasks independently, overlooking their synergies that could improve the performance of both tasks.

Purpose

To develop an accurate and efficient multi-task learning (MTL) framework that jointly performs segmentation and landmark detection for CMR.

Methods

The proposed SLaDNet-GaB framework integrates a Segmentation and Landmark Detection Network (SLaDNet) with a Gradient-as-Bridge (GaB) loss. SLaDNet adopts a shared feature encoder and two separate decoders to generate segmentation and landmark predictions, respectively. Inter-Task Feature Fusion (ITFF) modules are inserted between the decoders at multiple resolution scales to facilitate bidirectional information exchange via channel-wise attention. Along with two intra-task losses, the dedicated GaB loss is further introduced during training to enforce inter-task anatomical consistency. Specifically, the loss guides the predicted landmarks toward the segmentation objective boundaries using gradient maps. We comprehensively evaluated the proposed method against both single- and MTL baselines on two public CMR datasets: a cine dataset (ACDC; 105/15/30 subjects for training/validation/testing) and a T1 mapping dataset (STONE; 150/20/40 subjects for training/validation/testing).

Results

SLaDNet-Gab outperformed the baselines in both segmentation (dice scores: 92.37/94.27% on ACDC/STONE, p < 0.05) and landmark detection (point-to-point distances: 2.22/1.51 voxels on ACDC/STONE, p < 0.05). For downstream tasks, the proposed method consistently achieved lower strain and T1 quantification errors than the other methods in most myocardial segments, with per-segment measurements closely agreeing with the manually derived values. Moreover, SLaDNet-GaB demonstrated relatively low training times (11.4/3.2 hours on ACDC/STONE) and an inference time of 6.12 msec./sample suitable for clinical adoption.

Conclusions

The proposed multi-tasking method achieves improved accuracy in CMR segmentation, landmark detection, and downstream quantification, while maintaining high computational efficiency.

title: Association of Traditional and Emerging Anthropometric Indices With Subclinical Carotid Atherosclerosis in Young Healthy Adults: Insights From the Tehran Lipid and Glucose Study.
authorString: Abiri B, Ahmadi AR, Hosseinpanah F, Dehghan P, Ramezankhani A, Mataji-Amirroud M, Farsinajad N, Azizi F, Valizadeh M.
abstractText:
Background

Obesity is a major risk factor for cardiovascular disease, but traditional measures like BMI and waist circumference have limitations. New indices, BRI and ABSI, may better reflect fat distribution and cardiovascular risk. This study examined their association with carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) in young healthy adults.

Methods

In this cross-sectional study within the Tehran Lipid and Glucose Study (TLGS) framework, 572 adults aged 20-40 years underwent anthropometric assessments, biochemical tests and carotid ultrasound for cIMT measurement. Anthropometric indices including BMI, WC, waist-to-height ratio (WHtR), ABSI and BRI were calculated. Associations between these indices and cIMT were analysed using correlation and multivariable linear regression models adjusting for demographic, metabolic and lifestyle factors. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses assessed the predictive ability of the indices for elevated cIMT.

Result

BRI and WHtR were nearly collinear (r = 0.997) and showed modest positive correlations with cIMT in unadjusted analyses (r = 0.103 for both), but these associations weakened after adjustment for cardiometabolic risk factors. WC was the only independent predictor of cIMT in partially adjusted models, though this significance disappeared in fully adjusted analyses. ABSI exhibited a significant but mechanistically unexpected inverse association with cIMT. ROC analyses indicated limited discriminative power for all anthropometric measures in predicting high cIMT, with BRI and WHtR having the highest but still modest area under the curve (AUC).

Conclusion

In young healthy adults, BRI and WHtR showed modest associations with subclinical carotid atherosclerosis, which weakened after adjustment. Waist circumference was an inconsistent predictor, and ABSI demonstrated an inverse relationship with cIMT. Further longitudinal studies are needed to confirm their clinical utility.

title: Mitochondrial DNA Copy Number and Mitochondrial Homeostasis Genes in Acute and Stable Coronary Artery Disease.
authorString: Canale P, Campolo J, Parolini M, Dellanoce C, Piccaluga E, Bossi I, Maurina M, Oreglia JA, Sicari R, Andreassi MG.
abstractText:
Background

Mitochondrial dysfunction is increasingly implicated in coronary artery disease (CAD), but the relationship between mitochondrial DNA copy number (mtDNA-CN) and mitochondrial homeostasis across CAD presentations remains unclear. We investigated mtDNA-CN together with the expression of key regulators of mitochondrial biogenesis (PGC-1α and TFAM) and mitophagy (PINK1) in patients with stable angina (SA) and acute coronary syndrome (ACS).

Methods

This observational study included 334 patients: 170 ACS, 117 SA and 47 individuals with non-obstructive coronary arteries (NCA). Peripheral blood mtDNA-CN and the expression of PGC-1α, TFAM and PINK1 were quantified by real-time PCR. Associations with clinical characteristics, inflammatory markers and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) were evaluated.

Results

ACS patients exhibited significantly lower mtDNA-CN than SA and NCA groups (p = 0.01 and p = 0.004, respectively). PINK1 expression was reduced in both ACS (p = 0.005) and SA (p = 0.01) compared with NCA. TFAM expression was increased in SA (p = 0.009), while PGC-1α expression was higher in ACS (p = 0.02). MtDNA-CN and mitochondrial biomarkers were inversely associated with inflammatory markers, whereas mtDNA-CN and TFAM correlated positively with LVEF. Lower mtDNA-CN was independently associated with ACS (OR = 0.98, p = 0.0004) and SA (OR = 0.99, p = 0.04), while higher PINK1 expression was associated with reduced odds of SA (p = 0.03) and ACS (p = 0.02).

Conclusions

Mitochondrial markers are altered across CAD phenotypes. ACS is characterized by lower mtDNA-CN and altered expression of mitochondrial homeostasis-related genes, whereas SA shows a pattern consistent with a possible compensatory response. Combined assessment of mtDNA-CN and mitochondrial homeostasis-related gene expression may provide a novel biomarker strategy for CAD risk stratification and targeted therapies.

Trial registration

VICTORIA study, (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06313645).

title: Device-Measured 24-h Movement Behaviors and Arterial Intima-Media Thickness in Young Adults.
authorString: Suorsa K, Laitinen T, Heiskanen J, Leskinen T, Meng Y, Pasanen J, Rovio S, Koskinen JS, Mykkänen J, Heinonen OJ, Viikari J, Rönnemaa T, Niinikoski H, Raitakari O, Stenholm S, Pahkala K.

journal.title: Scandinavian journal of medicine & science in sports

abstractText: Physical activity, including light physical activity (LPA) and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), sedentary behavior (SED), and sleep, often referred to as "24-h movement behaviors", are modifiable behaviors that may be associated with arterial intima-media thickness (IMT). However, their combined associations with arterial IMT, especially aortic IMT, where cardiometabolic risk burden may be reflected at an earlier age, have not been studied before. This study examined how 24-h movement behaviors associate with aortic and carotid IMT among young adults. Participants (n = 327) were healthy young adults (mean age 26.1 years, SD 0.2) from the Special Turku Coronary Risk Factor Intervention Project (STRIP). 24-h movement behaviors were measured using a wrist-worn accelerometer for 1 week. Aortic and carotid IMT were measured with ultrasonography. Associations between 24-h movement behaviors and aortic and carotid IMT were analyzed using compositional data analysis and compositional isotemporal substitution analysis, adjusting for sex, education, smoking, and distribution of dietary fats. Descriptive model-based estimations indicated lower aortic IMT values for compositions with a higher proportion of LPA. However, theoretical time reallocations between LPA and other behaviors did not indicate significant differences in aortic IMT (e.g., 30 min from sleep to LPA, -0.005 mm [95% CI -0.020-0.010 mm], from SED to LPA, -0.006 mm [95% CI -0.018-0.006], and from MVPA to LPA, -0.008 mm [95% CI -0.038-0.021]). No associations were found for carotid IMT either. No apparent associations were observed between 24-h movement behaviors and arterial IMT among young adults.

title: Body mass index at diagnosis, postdiagnosis change, and role of metabolic comorbidities in relation to survival in nonmetastatic renal cell carcinoma patients.
authorString: Sarker M, Deng Z, Kauffman EC, Tang L, Kwan ML, Langston ME, Gupta S, Grass GD, Singer EA, Zakharia Y, Viscuse PV, Graham L, Ghodoussipour S, Salhia B, Kern SQ, Ayanambakkam A, Myint Z, King J, Oderinde S, Churchman ML, Rounbehler RJ, Batai K.
abstractText:
Background

Obesity is a recognized risk factor for renal cell carcinoma (RCC) incidence, but higher body mass index (BMI) measured at diagnosis has been paradoxically associated with improved survival. This study investigated whether postdiagnosis changes in BMI and metabolic comorbidities combined with BMI at diagnosis are associated with survival.

Methods

This study examined 1289 patients with nonmetastatic RCC (stage I-III) from the Oncology Research Information Exchange Network. BMI was assessed at diagnosis and at 2 and 3 years postdiagnosis. Multivariable Cox regression and restricted cubic spline models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS).

Results

Modest weight gain (<10%) and stability were most favorable trajectories. Compared with modest weight gain, postdiagnosis weight loss was associated with worse OS and DFS (>10% loss at 2 years: OS HR, 7.77; 95% CI, 3.00-20.16; DFS HR, 3.13; 95% CI, 1.68-5.82), independent of BMI at diagnosis, whereas substantial weight gain was associated with worse OS (>10% gain at 3 years: OS HR, 3.26; 95% CI, 1.14-9.32). Nonobese patients with diabetes had significantly worse DFS (HR, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.22-2.76), whereas the association between obesity and improved survival was mainly limited to patients without diabetes (HR, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.58-0.97).

Conclusions

Postdiagnosis weight trajectory and metabolic health are important prognostic factors for nonmetastatic RCC. Weight stability and absence of diabetes were associated with more favorable outcomes. Incorporating repeated BMI measurements and diabetes status may improve risk stratification during RCC survivorship.

title: Association Between Genetically Predicted 25-Hydroxyvitamin D and Type 2 Diabetes Risk in South Asians: An Exploratory Two-Sample Mendelian Randomization Study.
authorString: Zaka A, Khan S, Shah A, Khalid AA, Khalil I, Kamrul-Hasan ABM.
abstractText:
Background

Vitamin D deficiency and Type 2 diabetes (T2D) are highly prevalent in South Asian populations. Observational studies report inverse associations between serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] and T2D risk, but these findings may reflect confounding or reverse causation. We used Mendelian randomization (MR) to assess the association between genetically predicted 25(OH)D and T2D risk in South Asians.

Methods

We conducted a two-sample MR analysis using publicly available OpenGWAS summary statistics. One variant (rs3755967) met the conventional genome-wide significance threshold (p < 5 × 10-8), while two additional variants (rs2459139 and rs72744878) met an exploratory threshold (p < 1 × 10-6). The three variants served as instruments for serum 25(OH)D in a South Asian GWAS (ukb-e-30890_CSA; n = 7380; mean F-statistic = 29.6; total R2 = 1.06%). The primary outcome was BMI-unadjusted T2D (ebi-a-GCST90093109; n = 50,533; 16,677 cases), with a BMI-adjusted GWAS used for sensitivity analysis. The primary estimator was inverse-variance weighted (IVW), supported by weighted-median, MR-Egger, simple-mode, and weighted-mode analyses. Heterogeneity and directional pleiotropy were assessed using Cochran's Q and the MR-Egger intercept, respectively. Partial participant overlap could not be excluded because UK Biobank contributed to both datasets.

Results

The primary IVW analysis showed no statistically significant association between genetically predicted 25(OH)D and T2D risk (β = 0.058, SE = 0.120, p = 0.630; OR = 1.06, 95% CI: 0.83-1.36). Weighted-median and mode-based estimates were also non-significant. The MR-Egger estimate was highly imprecise (OR = 32.0, 95% CI: 0.11-9103) because only three instruments were available. No significant heterogeneity or directional pleiotropy was detected, although these tests had limited power. The BMI-adjusted sensitivity analysis produced similar findings.

Conclusions

We found no statistically significant evidence of a linear association between genetically predicted serum 25(OH)D and T2D risk. However, the small exposure GWAS, limited instrument set, exploratory instrument threshold, and possible sample overlap mean that small-to-moderate causal effects cannot be excluded. Larger South Asian GWAS are needed for more definitive inference.

title: Real-Time Continuous Glucose Monitoring Use and Kidney Function Among People With Diabetes and CKD or At-Risk for CKD.
authorString: Hannah KL, Chen C, Castle JR, Norman GJ, Galindo RJ.
abstractText:
Introduction

Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) use may benefit people with diabetes and chronic kidney disease (CKD). In this propensity-matched, retrospective analysis using Truveta-provided de-identified EMR data, changes in kidney function and glycemia were compared between cohorts starting real-time CGM (RT-CGM) use and CGM non-users (No CGM).

Methods

Adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes, treated with any insulin, with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 15-89 mL/min/1.73 m2 were included. Changes in eGFR, albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR), and HbA1c between baseline and 3-year follow-up were assessed.

Results

RT-CGM initiation (N = 518 per cohort) was associated with a significantly slower decline in eGFR compared to No CGM. There was no significant difference in change in ACR between the groups (N = 138 per cohort). RT-CGM use (N = 461 per cohort) was associated with a significantly greater decrease in HbA1c compared to No CGM.

Conclusions

These findings support RT-CGM initiation among people with diabetes and CKD or at risk for CKD.

title: Systems Pharmacology Investigation of Phytochemicals From Scilla peruviana L.: Integrated Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry Profiling, Network Pharmacology, and Molecular Docking Reveal Potential Anti-Inflammatory Mechanisms.
authorString: Zatout R, Benslama O, Garzoli S.
abstractText: This study aimed to characterize the volatile and fatty acid constituents of S. peruviana and investigate their potential anti-inflammatory mechanisms. Volatile compounds were identified by headspace solid-phase microextraction coupled with gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (HS-SPME-GC-MS), whereas fatty acids were analyzed by GC-MS following derivatization. The identified phytochemicals were subjected to target prediction, followed by protein-protein interaction (PPI), Gene Ontology (GO), Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway enrichment analyses, and molecular docking. HS-SPME-GC-MS analysis identified 11 volatile compounds, predominantly hexahydrofarnesyl acetone (48.4%) and dihydroactinidiolide (23.5%), followed by dehydro-β-ionone (5.6%), 2-methylbutanal (5.5%), and 3-methylbutanal (5.1%). Fatty acid profiling revealed palmitic acid as the predominant fatty acid (47.7%), followed by α-linolenic acid (29.9%), linoleic acid (11.6%), and stearic acid (10.8%). Network pharmacology identified 253 overlapping targets between phytochemical-associated proteins and inflammation-related genes, with TNF, IL1B, PTGS2, EGFR, STAT3, and PPARG emerging as the principal hub proteins. KEGG enrichment analysis revealed significant enrichment in inflammation-associated pathways, including NF-κB, IL-17, NOD-like receptor, and advanced glycation end-products (AGE)-receptor for advanced glycation end-products (RAGE) signaling pathways. Molecular docking predicted interactions between the major phytochemicals and the selected targets, with palmitic acid showing the lowest predicted binding energy for COX-2 (-7.0 kcal/mol), while hexahydrofarnesyl acetone and stearic acid showed the lowest predicted binding energies for PPARγ (-8.3 kcal/mol).

title: Genome Aging in Women: Hematopoietic Loss of X Chromosome as An Exemplar.
authorString: Guo X, Dai X.
abstractText: Genome aging refers to age-related acquisition and expansion of de novo mutations in somatic cells, and is now increasingly viewed as a central driver of organismal aging. Loss of X chromosome (LOX), the state in which one X chromosome (ChrX) is missing, represents the most common genetically inferred type of acquired mutation in women. Recent technological advancements, along with the growing availability of large-scale cohorts for association studies, have provided powerful new insights into this phenomenon. The frequency and clone size of LOX increase significantly with age: with over 10% of women aged 55 years or older showing detectable LOX in blood. LOX preferentially affects the inactivated ChrX derived from either parent, or in some cases, affects the ChrX from one specific parent. Besides aging, the acquisition and expansion of LOX are shaped by factors related to ChrX itself, genome-wide inherited and acquired variants, and lifestyle and environmental stressors. Due to the critical biological roles of ChrX, even in its inactive state, LOX impairs cellular functions and is strongly linked to hematological malignancies and a range of benign diseases. Understanding the mechanisms driving the causes and consequences of LOX may expand the sex-biased genomic architecture of aging and uncover strategies for disease prevention in women. In this review, by integrating the most recent progress in LOX studies with unique biology of ChrX and perspectives from aneuploidy, we provide a synthesized and updated understanding of the rise, expansion and consequences of blood LOX, while also posing key questions for future research.

title: A Cilia-Centered Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide (NAD<sup>+</sup>) Signaling Network Regulates Hypothalamic Lysosomal Homeostasis and Metabolic Aging.
authorString: Park SE, Roh E, Park JW, Kim SJ, Jeong SY, Park CB, Lim HS, Kim JS, Kim MG, Kim MJ, Cho YI, Jeong W, Kang GM, Kim SY, Min SH, Kim MS.
abstractText: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD<sup>+</sup>) is an essential metabolite that regulates diverse cellular metabolic processes. Primary cilia, hair-like organelles on the cell surface, function as critical signaling hubs. Here, we demonstrate that cellular NAD<sup>+</sup> levels are key regulators of both primary cilia growth and lysosomal function in hypothalamic neurons. NAD<sup>+</sup> depletion induces ciliary shortening and diminishes lysosomal activity in a cilia-dependent manner. Mechanistically, the lysosomal repair complex protein CHMP4B translocates from periciliary satellites to lysosomes during lysosomal stress, a process impaired by ciliary dysgenesis. Disrupted lysosomal recruitment of CHMP4B leads to abnormal lysosomal Ca<sup>2+</sup> signaling and lysosomal dysfunction. Aged mice with hypothalamic NAD<sup>+</sup> deficiency exhibit shortened cilia and lysosomal stress phenotypes, both of which are restored by calorie restriction (CR). Moreover, CR improves aging-associated metabolic dysfunction, at least in part, through hypothalamic cilia-dependent mechanisms. These findings identify a primary cilium-mediated-NAD<sup>+</sup> signaling axis that maintains lysosomal homeostasis in hypothalamic neurons, the disruption of which drives metabolic aging.

title: Caregiver Contributions to Self-Care in Parkinson's Disease: A Qualitative Descriptive Study.
authorString: Monica P, Rosario C, Chiara T, Anna C, Giovanni M, Isaias IU, Salvatore B, Arturo C, Angela C, Ercole V, Gianluca P.

journal.title: Journal of nursing scholarship : an official publication of Sigma Theta Tau International Honor Society of Nursing

abstractText:
Introduction

Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disorder after Alzheimer's disease, and is characterized by motor symptoms such as bradykinesia, rigidity, and reduced movement automaticity. Caregiver contributions (CC) to self-care in PD represent an important resource for supporting people with PD. However, this topic has not yet been fully explored.

Aim

To explore CC to self-care in PD across the domains of CC to self-care maintenance, monitoring, and management.

Method

A qualitative study design was conducted using a combined deductive and inductive approach. An initial deductive framework guided the analysis, while an inductive process allowed the identification of additional codes emerging from the interview data.

Results

Twenty semi-structured interviews were conducted. Caregivers of people with PD were 75% women, with a mean age of 63.7 years, and were 90% spouses and 95% living with the patient. The analysis showed that the CC to self-care emerges across all domains: in self-care maintenance, through support for medication adherence, physical activity, safety, and diet; in self-care monitoring, through support in daily activities, routine symptom monitoring, and alert system monitoring; and in self-care management, through symptom management strategies and caregiver attitudes. More broadly, this contribution also emerged in relation to caregiving difficulties, interactions with healthcare professionals, and the information that guides self-care.

Discussion-conclusion

The findings from this study showed that caregivers of persons with PD play a significant role in CC to self-care maintenance, monitoring, and management, particularly through non-pharmacological strategies.

Clinical relevance

These data are fundamental for guiding educational interventions aimed at the caregivers of patients with PD.

title: Lipoprotein(a) analytical variation and cardiovascular thresholds.
authorString: Bargnoux AS, Aamoum A, Grillet PE, Plawecki M, Dupuy AM, Roubille F, Cristol JP.
abstractText:
Objectives

The study was designed to evaluate the analytical performances of six automated immunoturbidimetric lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) assays, each corresponding to a combination of a reagent and an analyzer (Binding Site Optilite Lp(a) kit, Diagam Lp(a) reagent on Mindray BS480, Diagam Lp(a) reagent on Roche c502, Randox Lp(a) reagent on IDS-ISYS, Roche Tinaquant LPA2 on Roche c702 and Siemens Atellica CH Lp(a)/Atellica® CH 930) using results expressed in mg/dL or nmol/L.

Methods

Imprecision was assessed on manufacturer controls according to the CLSI EP15-A3 protocol. One hundred and 45 patient serum samples from the cardiology department were assessed to compare each method using Spearman's correlation, Passing-Bablok regression and Bland-Altman analyses. Percent agreement was calculated according to the European Atherosclerosis Society and American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Lp(a) cut-offs for cardiovascular risk.

Results

All immunoturbidimetric methods achieved the desirable imprecision of 5.1 % based on biological variation. Highly significant correlations were found across multiple comparisons (p<0.001). The absolute mean of the difference according to Bland-Altman ranged between 0.4 and 2.6 for Lp(a) assays in mg/dL and between 0.6 and 6.5 for Lp(a) assays in nmol/L. The percent agreement between two assays varied from 87.6 to 96.6 % and from 82.8 to 93.8 % using the EAS or the ACC/AHA thresholds.

Conclusions

Despite acceptable correlation among the six Lp(a) turbidimetric assays, a risk of "misclassifications" between two assays up to 12.4 % with the EAS recommendations and 17.2 % with the ACC/AHA guideline remains a major concern. Standardization of methods, including expression of results in nmol/L is needed.

title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated cardiotoxicity: incidence, diagnosis, and management.
authorString: Haddad SF, Philip L, Padrón L, Zoghbi M, Jacobson K, Burk K, Chaftari P, Markides DM, Dendy S, Krishnamani P, Mendoza Hernández A, Cruz Carreras MT.

journal.title: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer

abstractText:
Purpose

Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized cancer therapy but are associated with immune-related adverse events (irAEs), including cardiotoxicity. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the incidence, mechanisms, diagnosis, and management of ICI-associated cardiotoxicity, highlighting emerging biomarkers, diagnostic algorithms, and risk stratification strategies.

Methods

We conducted a narrative review of the literature, synthesizing findings from recent clinical studies, guidelines, and case reports concerning ICI-associated cardiovascular complications such as myocarditis, pericarditis, and arrhythmias. As a narrative rather than systematic review, studies were selected to illustrate current concepts and were not appraised against predefined eligibility criteria.

Key findings

ICIs are associated with a low overall incidence of cardiovascular toxicities; however, myocarditis remains the most severe and potentially life-threatening manifestation. Reported case-fatality estimates vary widely, and the highest figures derive largely from early case series and pharmacovigilance data. Emerging biomarkers, evolving risk stratification tools, and updated diagnostic and management frameworks may improve early recognition, guide timely intervention, and support multidisciplinary care for patients with suspected ICI-associated cardiotoxicity, although most supporting evidence remains retrospective.

Conclusions

Early recognition and prompt management of ICI-associated cardiotoxicities are essential for improving patient outcomes. This review provides oncologists and cardiologists with updated diagnostic approaches, treatment frameworks, and practical considerations for monitoring at-risk patients, while acknowledging that current recommendations rest largely on low-certainty evidence.

title: Sex differences in the association of late-life blood pressure decline with postmortem brain vessel pathology.
authorString: Baumgartner NW, Du L, Mehta RI, Casaletto KB, Wood Alexander M, Rabin JS, van Sloten T, Bennett DA, Capuano AW, Arvanitakis Z.
abstractText: Although hypertension is the leading modifiable risk factor for cerebrovascular disease, less is known about the relation of late-life change in blood pressure (BP) and cerebrovascular pathology beyond brain infarcts. Our previous work found sex-specific associations between declining systolic BP (SBP) and cognitive decline in late-life, suggesting that cerebrovascular pathology may be an upstream contributor to these sex differences. However, postmortem studies have not examined whether BP change differentially relates to vascular brain pathology in men and women, despite well-established sex differences in BP trajectories and cerebrovascular pathology. We examined associations between change in late-life BP and postmortem cerebrovascular (arteriolosclerosis, atherosclerosis, and cerebral amyloid angiopathy) pathology from 2033 community-dwelling older adults (mean baseline age = 79.7 [SD = 7.1] years; 69% women) from four longitudinal cohort studies with brain autopsy (mean age-at-death = 89.8 [6.6] years). Person-specific late-life BP slopes estimated from annual clinical evaluations over an average of 9.1 [5.7] years were entered in ordinal regressions adjusted for age-at-death, sex, antihypertensive medication use, and BP slope × sex, age-at-death × sex, and BP slope × age-at-death interactions. Faster SBP decline was associated with greater severity of arteriolosclerosis (OR = 1.24, 95%CI 1.08-1.42) and atherosclerosis (OR = 1.41, 95%CI 1.22-1.63). A sex × SBP slope interaction (p = 0.01) revealed a stronger association of SBP decline with arteriolosclerosis severity in women than men. This longitudinal, clinical-pathologic study of older decedents showed sex differences in the association of declining SBP in late-life with severity of arteriolosclerosis, extending prior associations with cognitive decline to cerebrovascular pathology, and suggests potential for longitudinal BP monitoring for precision medicine approaches in cerebrovascular disease risk stratification.

title: Ferroptosis in health and disease.
authorString: Oyedokun PA, Ashonibare VJ, Akhigbe TM, Ashonibare PJ, Adeogun AE, Adegbola CA, Omole AI, Akhigbe RE.
abstractText: Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent, non-apoptotic form of regulated cell death that is driven by lipid peroxidation. In the past decade, it has emerged as a core pathogenic mechanism in a wide range of human diseases, such as neurodegenerative disorders, cardiovascular disease, cancer, and notably, reproductive dysfunction. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the molecular mechanisms underlying ferroptosis with a specific focus on the System Xc⁻-GSH-GPX4 axis, iron metabolism, lipid peroxidation, and the regulatory roles of key modulators such as Nrf2, ACSL4, and CISD2. This review also explores the physiological roles of ferroptosis in development, tissue homeostasis, and immune regulation, as well as its pathological contributions to obesity, diabetes mellitus, atherosclerosis, neurodegeneration, stroke, cancer, infectious diseases, and reproductive disorders. A substantial part of this review discusses the role of ferroptosis in the pathogenesis of reproductive disorders, such as male reproductive pathologies, including varicocele, testicular ischemia-reperfusion, cryptorchidism, oligospermia, erectile dysfunction, and testicular cancer, and female pathologies like primary ovarian insufficiency, polycystic ovary syndrome, endometriosis, ovarian cancer, and pre-eclampsia. Moreover, the interplay between ferroptosis and immune dysfunction in reproductive tract infections was highlighted. Furthermore, we evaluated current biomarkers, emerging therapeutic strategies, and key translational challenges, highlighting the promise of ferroptosis-modulating agents for novel diagnostic and therapeutic interventions in reproductive medicine and beyond.

title: Community-Level Wastewater Surveillance of Nicotine Biomarkers Tracks Cardiovascular Disease Burden and Myocardial Infarction
authorString: Joseph KM, Qin X, Clark KM, Li F, Hartmann E, Nanez J, Humble L, Turlington C, Balliew J, Cassidy C, Narula J, Mena KD, Wu F.
abstractText:
BACKGROUND

Tobacco smoking is the largest modifiable contributor to cardiovascular disease (CVD), yet population-level surveillance still relies on self-reported and retail data, which are subject to measuring bias and lag. Urinary and salivary cotinine quantify individual tobacco exposure, but no analogous, objective metric exists at the community level. Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) has transformed surveillance of infectious diseases and illicit drug use; whether the same approach can yield a community-level signal of CVD risk is unknown.

OBJECTIVE

The primary objective of this study is to track community-level wastewater nicotine biomarkers and evaluate potential correlations with relative CVD burden in El Paso, Texas.

METHODS

We integrated wastewater nicotine biomarker surveillance with electronic health record (EHR) data across four sewersheds in El Paso, Texas. Twenty-four-hour composite influent samples were collected monthly (June 2024–May 2025; n=48) and quantified by liquid-chromatography tandem mass spectrometry for five nicotine metabolites. Cotinine, nornicotine, and trans-3’-hydroxycotinine (3HC) were detected in 91.6–100% of samples, whereas tobacco-specific nitrosamines were below limit of detection. CVD cases (January 2021–December 2024) were obtained from the Paso del Norte Health Information Exchange and mapped to sewersheds by residential ZIP code using ArcGIS. At the sewershed level, population-normalized nicotine mass loads tracked the proportional burden of atherosclerosis/ischemia/infarction and heart failure. Across the sewersheds, monthly 3HC mass load and the nicotine metabolite ratio (NMR) were strongly and specifically associated with incident ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) (3HC vs. STEMI: ρ = 0.893, p = 0.012), without parallel associations for non-ST-elevation or old myocardial infarction.

CONCLUSIONS

To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration that integrating wastewater nicotine surveillance with EHR data can reveal community-level 3HC and NMR as specific indicators of incident STEMI. Our findings indicate wastewater surveillance as a novel, objective tool to inform cessation policy and CVD prevention.

Lay Words

This study investigated using wastewater to measure population-level nicotine consumption and to see if it was related to local cardiovascular disease. The study took place in El Paso, Texas, USA across 4 different wastewater treatment collection points over the course of one year. Three metabolites of human nicotine consumption were detected in wastewater samples. The increased nicotine mass loads were proportional with community-level heart failure and atherosclerosis. Wastewater can be a helpful tool to inform cardiovascular disease prevention efforts and smoking cessation practices.

title: TRIM65 deficiency exacerbates HFD-induced obesity in mice associated with elevated adipose tissue inflammation and lipid accumulation.
authorString: Wei W, Wang D, Han X, Cui Y, Sun X, Li L, Ni Y, Jiang M.
abstractText: Obesity is linked to metabolic and cardiovascular complications, such as atherosclerosis, type 2 diabetes (T2DM), and hypertension. Despite current therapies alleviate certain clinical manifestations, effective disease-modifying targets remain scarce. TRIM65 (tripartite motif-containing 65) has been linked to carcinogenesis, immune modulation, and inflammatory responses, yet its role in obesity remains unknown. Here, we aimed to elucidate the pathophysiological function of TRIM65 in obesity and to reveal the molecular networks regulating this process. Our results demonstrated a significant decrease in TRIM65 expression under obese conditions. Notably, TRIM65 knockout mice exhibited exacerbated high fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity, as evidenced by marked increases in body and white adipose tissue (WAT) weight, enlarged adipocyte sizes, elevated systemic and tissue inflammation, and impaired glucose and insulin tolerance. Furthermore, knockout of TRIM65 aggravated HFD-induced dyslipidemia, hepatic steatosis, and liver injury. Mechanistically, TRIM65 deficiency triggered the ERK1/2-NF-κB signaling cascade, leading to a pro-inflammatory environment and aggravating insulin resistance. Simultaneously, TRIM65 deficiency enhanced the expression of adipogenic and lipogenic genes while diminishing that of lipolytic genes, culminating in increased lipid accumulation. Collectively, TRIM65 is established by our findings as a pivotal negative regulator that coordinately curbs lipid synthesis and inflammatory responses, thereby positioning it as an attractive therapeutic target for obesity and its metabolic complications.

title: Prospective evaluation of stereotactic arrhythmia radioablation for refractory ventricular tachycardia: initial clinical experience in Japan.
authorString: Kawamura M, Shimojo M, Inden Y, Kamomae T, Komada T, Kuwatsuka Y, Kinoshita F, Tanaka H, Mukohara T, Murohara T, Naganawa S.
abstractText:
Purpose

This prospective study evaluated the 1 year safety and efficacy of stereotactic arrhythmia radioablation (STAR) delivered using the CyberKnife system for refractory ventricular tachycardia (VT) in Japanese patients, in accordance with a prespecified clinical protocol.

Materials and methods

Three male patients with radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA)-refractory VT and structural heart disease, namely hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), and ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM), were enrolled. A single fraction of 25 Gy was delivered to the target volume defined by multimodal image fusion. The primary endpoint was the absence of Grade ≥ 3 treatment-related adverse events within 12 months.

Results

The primary endpoint was achieved, with no acute or subacute Grade ≥ 3 toxicities observed in any patient during the first year. Although all patients experienced a reduction in VT burden, the clinical course differed by etiology. Cases 2 (DCM) and 3 (ICM) showed typical responses, including delayed efficacy and late recurrence requiring repeat RFCA. In contrast, Case 1 (HCM), with a substantially larger target volume (133 mL), showed a rapid response but a progressive decline in left ventricular ejection fraction by myocardial scintigraphy, from 59.7% to 40.0%, during the 24 month extended follow-up.

Conclusion

STAR demonstrated preliminary feasibility as a noninvasive salvage therapy for refractory VT in this initial Japanese pilot experience. However, the late functional decline observed in Case 1 highlights the need for long-term follow-up and myocardium-sparing techniques for large target volumes. (jRCTs042230030).

title: Using Implementation Science to Improve Guidelines-Based Care to Lower Atherosclerosis Risk Due to Familial Hypercholesterolemia.
authorString: Hallquist MLG, Brangan A, Cawley D, Gabriel JL, Kunnmann M, Ly K, Morales A, Romagnoli K, Savatt JM, Walters NL, Gidding SS.
abstractText:
Purpose of the review

Implementation science, a multi-method research area that integrates input from constituents and content experts, has emerged as an important tool in improving implementation of evidence-based practices. This review summarizes three ongoing implementation studies focused on identification of patients with significantly increased risk for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) due to genomic risk such as familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) within a single health system.

Recent findings

Despite the existence of evidence-based guidelines for identifying individuals with increased risk for ASCVD from FH and managing their care to reduce risk, substantial care gaps exist in guideline implementation. These include patient understanding of the importance of heart disease prevention, clinician implementation of screening for risk factors, and adherence to recommended treatments. While guidelines often focus on the encounter between a patient and clinician, implementation science enlarges the field of study to encompass factors external to the encounter. These factors include multi-level barriers and facilitators to implementation. By developing strategies to overcome barriers and leverage facilitators, management can be improved for those with FH. Implementation science methods described herein are transferable to other health care settings, with a goal of improving preventive medicine practice and increasing adherence to evidence-based practices for FH.

title: Silent Cardiac Progression in a Woman With Fabry Disease Despite Normal Baseline CMR.
authorString: Szczepara S, Pacia K, Szachowicz-Jaworska J, Podolec P, Kopeć G, Komar M.
abstractText:
Background

Fabry disease in women may progress silently, and normal baseline cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) does not exclude subsequent cardiac involvement.

Case summary

A 39-year-old woman with genetically confirmed Fabry disease and no prior disease-specific therapy had normal biomarkers, renal function, echocardiography, and CMR in 2022. In 2025, she developed acroparesthesias, reduced sweating, tinnitus, and constipation. Echocardiography showed increased left ventricular wall thickness. Follow-up CMR demonstrated preserved left ventricular ejection fraction, basal septal thickening to 14 mm, low native T1 (874 ms), extracellular volume of 26.9%, and new midwall late gadolinium enhancement. Enzyme replacement therapy was initiated.

Discussion

Women with Fabry disease may develop structural cardiac involvement despite preserved systolic function and normal cardiac biomarkers, supporting individualized serial multimodality surveillance.

Take-home message

Preserved left ventricular ejection fraction and normal cardiac biomarkers do not exclude Fabry cardiomyopathy; interval echocardiographic changes or symptoms should prompt repeat CMR and reassessment for disease-specific therapy.

title: A 78-Year-Old Man With a Previously Stable Atherosclerotic Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Presenting With Impending Rupture Following COVID-19.
authorString: Hori T, Hirohama D, Kaseda K, Kawagoe M, Tomomitsu Y, Yasukawa M, Morimoto C, Asakawa S, Yamazaki O, Tamura Y, Fujigaki Y, Shibata S.

journal.title: The American journal of case reports

abstractText: BACKGROUND Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) rupture is a life-threatening condition. Although elective repair is generally guided by aneurysm size, impending rupture can occur when rapid aneurysmal expansion or periaortic inflammatory changes develop before overt hemodynamic deterioration. This report describes the case of a 78-year-old man with a previously stable 43-mm atherosclerotic AAA who presented with impending rupture after coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). CASE REPORT A 78-year-old Japanese man with a known AAA under imaging surveillance developed fever and was diagnosed with COVID-19 by nasopharyngeal polymerase chain reaction testing. Seven days later, he was admitted for recurrent fever, cough, poor appetite, and elevated inflammatory markers. His medical history included hypertension, heavy smoking, advanced chronic kidney disease, and diffuse atherosclerotic disease. The aneurysm had shown minimal growth over 2 years, with a stable maximum short-axis diameter of approximately 43 mm on serial computed tomography. After admission, C-reactive protein levels initially decreased but rose again on hospital day 11, accompanied by new-onset mild low back pain and no marked blood pressure elevation or hemodynamic instability. Repeat non-contrast abdominal computed tomography performed 18 days after COVID-19 diagnosis demonstrated rapid AAA expansion from 43 mm to 51 mm within 2 months, with periaortic fat stranding, consistent with impending rupture. Urgent endovascular aneurysm repair was performed before hemodynamic deterioration. The postoperative course was stable, and the patient was discharged without ischemic or procedural complications. CONCLUSIONS This case shows that a previously stable AAA can abruptly destabilize after recent COVID-19. Repeat imaging should be considered when inflammatory markers rise or new symptoms occur, even when symptoms are mild.

title: Jiedu Quyu Ziyin Decoction attenuates high-phosphate-induced calcification-associated phenotypes in cultured human aortic smooth muscle cells.
authorString: Xiang X, Ran T, Guo J, Yang J, Song L, Qiu S, Xu L.
abstractText: Vascular calcification is one of the complications related to chronic kidney disease, and there are correlations between vascular calcification and oxidative stress, inflammation, and ferroptosis. This study examined whether Jiedu Quyu Ziyin Decoction (JQZYD) attenuates high-phosphate-induced calcification in cultured human aortic smooth muscle cells and evaluated the contribution of NRF2-associated antioxidant signalling. Human aortic vascular smooth muscle cells were exposed to high-phosphate conditions and treated with JQZYD. Calcification was assessed by Alizarin Red S staining, calcium content, alkaline phosphatase activity, and osteogenic markers. Ferroptosis-associated changes were evaluated by BODIPY 581/591 C11 oxidation, intracellular Fe2⁺, glutathione, glutathione peroxidase activity, and GPX4/SLC7A11 expression. NRF2 activation was assessed by immunofluorescence and protein analysis. Ferrostatin-1, RSL3, and NFE2L2 silencing were used for mechanistic evaluation. Inflammatory mediators and conditioned-medium effects were also examined. JQZYD reduced high-phosphate-induced mineral deposition, osteogenic marker expression, lipid peroxidation, Fe2⁺ accumulation, and inflammatory responses. These changes were accompanied by increased glutathione peroxidase activity, greater NRF2 nuclear accumulation, higher GPX4 and SLC7A11 transcript abundance, and increased NRF2 and GPX4 protein abundance. Ferrostatin-1 reproduced several protective effects of JQZYD. RSL3 and NFE2L2 silencing partially attenuated JQZYD-associated protection, supporting contributions of GPX4-related lipid peroxide regulation and NRF2-associated signalling without establishing direct NRF2 regulation of SLC7A11/GPX4 or pathway order. Conditioned medium from JQZYD-treated donor cells induced weaker inflammatory and calcific responses in recipient HASMCs, although the responsible mediators and potential contribution of residual treatment components remained unresolved. JQZYD attenuated high-phosphate-induced calcification-associated phenotypes and accompanying oxidative and inflammatory responses in cultured HASMCs. NFE2L2 silencing supports NRF2 involvement without establishing direct regulation of SLC7A11/GPX4 or pathway order. These findings are restricted to a cellular model and do not establish prevention of vascular calcification or therapeutic efficacy in CKD. Validation in CKD-relevant animal models and more physiologically complex vascular systems is required.

title: Human T cells from resistant hypertension patients promote hypertension via tnf in humanized mice.
authorString: Rahman M, Bartolomaeus H, Hering L, Yakoub M, Yang G, Holle J, Streese L, Arifaj D, Hahn M, Kantauskaite M, Grüner TF, Meister J, Wilck N, Kleinewietfeld M, Rump LC, Müller DN, Temme S, Stegbauer J.
abstractText:
Aims

Preclinical studies suggest a pivotal role of adaptive immunity, particularly T cells, in hypertension. However, due to the multifactorial pathogenesis, there is still no definitive evidence for a causal role of T cells in the development of hypertension in humans. We sought to determine whether T cells from patients with treatment-resistant hypertension (TRH) directly modulate blood pressure and vascular function in vivo.

Methods and results

Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from TRH patients and healthy controls (HC) were adoptively transferred into immunodeficient NSG-(KbDb)^null mice. Hypertension was induced by angiotensin II infusion for 14 days and monitored continuously by radiotelemetry. Following T cell engraftment, blood pressure was assessed at baseline and during AngII infusion in both groups of recipient mice. At baseline, systolic blood pressure did not differ between both groups. However, mice receiving TRH-PBMCs developed a significantly higher systolic blood pressure following AngII compared with HC-PBMC recipients. Endothelial dysfunction in isolated perfused kidneys was more pronounced in AngII-challenged TRH-PBMC recipients compared to HC-PBMC recipients. TRH-PBMC recipients displayed elevated effector memory CD4+ T cells and Th17 frequencies in spleen and kidney, along with markedly increased renal expression of human T cell-derived TNF. Overnight incubation of mouse aortic rings with human TNF induced endothelial dysfunction, indicating a causal role of T cell-derived TNF. As a proof of concept, TNF inhibition attenuated AngII-induced hypertension in TRH-PBMC-engrafted mice.

Conclusions

T cells from patients with treatment-resistant hypertension promote an exaggerated hypertensive response and endothelial dysfunction in PBMC-engrafted humanized mice, promoted by TNF-mediated mechanisms. These findings provide evidence that T cell-derived TNF may contribute to the pathogenesis of human hypertension.

title: Pharmacological interactions of carvedilol and curcumin nanomicelles in spontaneously hypertensive rats: a bliss and HSA analysis.
authorString: Plantamura YAS, Allo M, Riedel J, Fuentes P, Riesco AS, Carranza A, Donato M, Garces M, Evelson P, Bernabeu E, Chiappetta D, Gorzalczany S, Höcht C.
abstractText: Hypertensive target organ damage (TOD), including cardiac fibrosis, vascular remodeling, and low-grade inflammation, is driven by oxidative stress and proinflammatory cytokines. We previously demonstrated that acute carvedilol-curcumin co-administration in a Soluplus® nanomicellar formulation synergistically reduces mean arterial pressure in spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR). However, the chronic protective effects of this combination on TOD remain unknown. The aim of this study to evaluate whether 8-week co-administration of carvedilol and curcumin in a Soluplus® nanomicellar system exerts synergistic effects on carotid SBP, aortic remodeling, cardiac inflammation, and oxidative stress in SHR and to quantify the drug interaction using the Bliss independence model. SHR received carvedilol (9 mg/kg/day), curcumin (6 mg/kg/day), their combination, or vehicle for 8 weeks. We measured (i) hemodynamics (tail-cuff and carotid SBP, beat-to-beat and short-/medium-term blood pressure variability); (ii) aortic and ventricular fibrosis (histomorphometry); (iii) oxidative stress (protein carbonyls, TBARS); and (iv) cardiac TNF-α, IL-6, and TGF-β (Western blot). We assessed synergy using Bliss independence analysis and the Highest Single Agent (HSA) model. The Bliss analysis revealed antagonistic interactions for cardiac fibrosis and cardiac TBARS, and additive interactions for TGF-β, aortic carbonyls, and aortic TBARS. The HSA analysis revealed that IL-6, TNF-α, and cardiomyocyte size showed additive/independent effects, while aortic fibrosis showed a synergistic interaction (ΔE_HSA =  + 22.22%, p < 0.0001). No synergistic interactions were observed for other parameters. However, the combination still significantly reduced all these parameters compared to vehicle-treated SHR. Chronic co-administration of carvedilol and curcumin in Soluplus® nanomicelles produced a synergistic antifibrotic effect on the aorta, while other parameters showed additive, independent, or antagonistic interactions. The combination preserved the beneficial effects of the monotherapies on oxidative stress and fibrosis, suggesting that the co-administration still provides target organ protection, although not through broad synergistic mechanisms.

title: Maternal E-cigarette Exposure Augments Murine Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm
authorString: Spin JM, Mulorz J, Shen W, Amirahmadi M, Rhee YH, Deng A, Chavan S, Butterfield J, Mulorz P, Wagenhauser MU, Headley CA, Qiu T, Tsao PS.
abstractText:
ABSTRACT

Background

Smoking and family history are major risk factors for abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). Smoking and nicotine are modulators of DNA methylation, capable of causing heritable epigenetic alterations. Nicotine infusion and e-cigarette (e-cig) vaping augment murine AAA. We investigated the effects of murine maternal e-cig vaping on offspring experimental AAA, and impacts on transgenerational DNA methylation and accessibility.

Methods

We performed perinatal e-cig nicotine vaping in two strains of adult female mice (ApoE-/- and C57BL/6J). Mice were mated to control males, and treated through gestation. A parallel group were instead sacrificed after treatment, for DNA analysis. Offspring were aged to adulthood, and AAAs were then induced by elastase (C57BL/6J) or angiotensin-II infusion (ApoE-/-), and ultrasound-tracked for 4 weeks. In a second cohort, parental and offspring aortic tissue and blood DNA underwent RRBS and ATAC-seq analysis respectively. Offspring abdominal aortic anatomy was examined, and stiffness was assessed with ex vivo arterial myography.

Results

Maternal e-cig exposure increased offspring AAA growth in both models and genders. AAA incidence was increased in ApoE-/- males, and observed effects were overall more pronounced in males. Maternal vape exposure altered aortic DNA methylation and blood DNA accessibility in mothers and offspring, with differential sites in numerous genes identified, including AAA-related genes and pathways. Pathways were enriched for transcription factors, inflammation/immune-related genes, and angiogenesis genes, with similar changes identified in exposed mothers. Male offspring displayed more differential genes. Significant changes were located in genes known to harbor AAA risk loci in humans, and overlapped with published epigenetic alterations in human smokers. Differences also occurred in offspring aortic structure and stiffness.

Conclusions

Maternal e-cig nicotine exposure augments AAA growth in multiple models across generations. These effects are accompanied by broad epigenetic DNA reprogramming of key AAA modulator genes and pathways.

title: Patient-specific finite element modeling of image-derived shell morphoelastic growth: A general framework and application to stented aortic dissection
authorString: Gaffney AD, Dhara S, Davis C, Singh S, Donik Ž, Pocivavsek L, Nguyen N.
abstractText: Vascular pathology often manifests in complex shape evolution visualized by longitudinal computed tomography (CT) imaging. Growth and remodeling (G&R) frameworks have been integrated into finite element (FE) modeling to probe the mechanics underlying this progression, extending into patient-specific approaches. Their scalability and translatability, however, are limited by the computational burden associated with heterogeneous, anisotropic growth fields and through-thickness meshing. While existing shell growth formulations can mitigate this burden, they require nontrivial FE implementation especially in commercial softwares (e.g., Abaqus) and their efficacy in patient-specific geometries under complex loading is unclear. In this work, we present a general computational framework to implement shell morphoelastic growth computed directly from registered patient-specific CT images. This shell implementation is validated against solid 3D formulations, allows thickness tunability, and increases compatibility with CT surfaces. We demonstrate the robustness of this formulation through modeling post-operative growth in a patient-specific aortic dissection under stent-based loading. Results first show that complex stent-based loading can deform the shell dissection flap to reproduce post-operative geometry. The outer aortic wall is then given a growth field calculated from registration of 1-month and 5-year post-operative CT images, which is implemented along with stent-based loading and pressurization. Results from this model capture the trends in total and lumen morphological evolution observed at intermediate timepoints. These findings establish a general framework, validated with a patient-specific case study of aortic dissection, with the potential to expand to other complex systems, scale to larger patient populations, and apply G&R to clinical translation.

title: Dedicated versus off-label transcatheter devices for pure native aortic regurgitation via transfemoral access: a meta-analysis of contemporary outcomes.
authorString: Hon JJ, Egrilmezer A, Hon JKF.
abstractText:
Background

Pure native aortic regurgitation (PNAR) poses unique technical challenges for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), including annular dilatation and absent calcification for anchoring. Whilst dedicated aortic regurgitation (AR) devices have been developed, their comparative performance against off-label devices specifically via transfemoral access - the contemporary standard approach - remains incompletely defined.

Aims

We aimed to compare the outcomes of dedicated versus off-label transcatheter devices for PNAR via transfemoral access in contemporary practice.

Methods

We systematically searched PubMed (MEDLINE) and Cochrane CENTRAL (January 2020-November 2025) for studies reporting transfemoral TAVI outcomes in PNAR. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. Random-effects meta-analysis with meta-regression was performed.

Results

Twenty-four studies (2,956 patients) were included comprising 25 cohorts: 4 cohorts (537 patients) evaluated dedicated devices, and 21 cohorts (2,419 patients) assessed off-label devices. Overall, 30-day mortality was 3.3% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.3-4.8%). Dedicated devices showed a trend towards lower mortality (1.9% vs 4.1%, odds ratio [OR] 0.45, 95% CI: 0.20-1.00; p=0.051; risk ratio 0.40, 95% CI: 0.19-0.83). Dedicated devices achieved higher device success (95.8% vs 85.7%, OR 3.64; p=0.012), lower rates of residual AR >=moderate (0.6% vs 6.2%, OR 0.11; p=0.048), reduced valve embolisation (2.0% vs 7.3%, OR 0.26; p=0.048), and fewer reinterventions (2.0% vs 7.9%, OR 0.22; p=0.010). Permanent pacemaker implantation (20.8%), stroke (2.6%), and major bleeding (3.0%) were similar between groups.

Conclusions

In contemporary transfemoral TAVI for PNAR, dedicated devices demonstrated superior procedural outcomes compared with off-label devices. These findings support the preferential use of dedicated devices in this population, though randomised trials are needed to establish definite treatment recommendations.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Pharmacologic Therapies in Nonobstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Systematic Review.
authorString: Patel S, Gandhi A, Pabani A, Shah R, Shah P, Martinez MW, Bavishi A.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) affects approximately one-third of all patients with HCM and carries substantial morbidity, yet no approved disease-modifying therapies exist. We conducted a systematic review of prospective interventional studies evaluating pharmacologic therapies in adults with nonobstructive HCM.

Methods

A systematic search of PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Clinicaltrials.gov was performed through September 2025. Eligible studies included randomized and nonrandomized prospective interventional trials. A narrative synthesis was performed by pharmacologic class and outcome domain.

Results

Twenty-nine clinical trials evaluating 9 pharmacologic classes were identified: cardiac myosin inhibitors, cardiac sarcomere modulators, metabolic modulators, angiotensin II receptor blockers, angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, SGLT2 (sodium-glucose cotransporter 2) inhibitors, beta blockers, and calcium channel blockers. Cardiac myosin inhibitors demonstrated reductions in left ventricular hypertrophy, improvements in diastolic function, and marked reductions in cardiac biomarkers, although improvements in exercise capacity and symptoms were variable. SGLT2 inhibition showed concordant improvements in diastolic function, atrial remodeling, biomarkers, and functional status in patients with symptomatic nonobstructive HCM and comorbid type 2 diabetes. Angiotensin receptor blockade showed signals of structural remodeling with valsartan and candesartan without consistent functional benefit. Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism and angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibition demonstrated largely neutral effects. Among metabolic modulators, ninerafaxstat improved ventilatory efficiency and quality of life in patients with greater baseline symptom burden.

Conclusions

Pharmacologic responsiveness in nonobstructive HCM is variable and appears to be mechanism- and disease stage-dependent. Ongoing trials evaluating cardiac myosin inhibitors, SGLT inhibitors, and novel therapeutic agents including ninerafaxstat and EDG-7500 will be critical in further defining the therapeutic landscape.

title: Cardioprotective mechanisms and efficacy of colchicine, methotrexate, hydroxychloroquine, sulfasalazine and leflunomide in inflammatory rheumatic and musculoskeletal diseases.
authorString: Agca R, Mohamed SS, Popa CD, van Durme C, Vonkeman HE, Simsek S, Heslinga S, van Leuven SI, Nurmohamed MT.
abstractText: Chronic systemic inflammation contributes to the excess risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) in inflammatory rheumatic and musculoskeletal diseases (RMDs), raising the possibility that anti-inflammatory treatment may modify vascular risk. This review sought to critically review the mechanistic and clinical evidence for atheroprotection with colchicine and the commonly used conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (csDMARDs) methotrexate, hydroxychloroquine, sulfasalazine and leflunomide. We performed a targeted narrative review of key experimental studies, randomized cardiovascular outcome trials, observational RMD cohorts and systematic reviews, prioritizing evidence directly relevant to ASCVD outcomes and cardiometabolic mechanisms. Colchicine has the strongest randomized evidence for reducing recurrent ASCVD events in patients with established coronary disease, with supportive observational data in gout. Methotrexate is associated with fewer cardiovascular events in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), whereas the CIRT trial was neutral in patients without inflammatory arthritis. Hydroxychloroquine has favorable lipid, glycaemic and antithrombotic effects and observational associations with lower cardiovascular risk in RA and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), but no definitive cardiovascular outcome trial. Evidence for sulfasalazine is limited and observational, and human data for leflunomide are conflicting. Cardiovascular benefit differs substantially between agents and is most convincing for colchicine in secondary prevention and for inflammation control with methotrexate in RA. Dedicated prospective trials in inflammatory RMD populations are needed before any csDMARD can be prescribed primarily for ASCVD prevention.

title: Procedural Success, Predictors of Failure, and Clinical Outcomes of Conduction System Pacing in Korea: The Korean Conduction System Pacing (K-CSP) Registry.
authorString: Lee SR, Hwang J, Kim TH, Park SJ, Kim SS, Kwon S, Lim WH, Choi JH, Kwon CH, Hwang JK, Lee JH, Ahn JH, Choi Y, Gwag HB, Kim SH, Choi SH, Park YM, Jung LY, Roh SY, Lee DI, Kwon HJ, Kim M, Lee SH, Yang SY, Jin ES, Chun KJ, Jeong JH, Choi JI, Kim YR, Park JS, Park JK, Kim HJ, Kim DH, Park YJ, Lee E, Choi WS, Jin MN, Park J, Im SI, Hwang YM, Yu GI, Ahn HJ, Choi EK, Oh S, Park YJ, Cho MS.
abstractText:
Background

Conduction system pacing (CSP), particularly left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP), is a promising physiologic pacing strategy, but large-scale Asian data are lacking.

Objective

To evaluate the feasibility, predictors of failure, and clinical outcomes of CSP in a nationwide Korean multicenter registry.

Methods

This observational registry included 2,215 consecutive patients undergoing attempted CSP at 35 Korean centers between January 2021 and June 2025. Capture types were classified using EHRA criteria.

Results

Stylet-driven leads were used in 87.0%. CSP succeeded in 87.4% (1,932/2,211). Among 1,922 LBBAP patients, left bundle branch pacing (LBBP) was achieved in 35.1%, left fascicular pacing (LFP) in 31.3%, and left ventricular septal pacing (LVSP) in 17.2%. Independent predictors of CSP failure included prior open-heart surgery involving septal manipulation, right-sided approach, and male sex. Pacing parameters were stable over 17.0±10.8 months. CSP failure was associated with worse composite outcomes on unadjusted analysis, but these associations were attenuated and no longer significant after adjustment. Among LBBAP patients, LVSP was associated with a higher adjusted risk of heart-failure hospitalization (adjusted HR 3.04, 95% CI 1.05-8.73, p=0.039) than LBBP+LFP; however, this association was based on few events with wide confidence intervals and was not significant on unadjusted analysis.

Conclusion

In this large-scale Asian CSP registry, LBBAP was feasible and safe, performed predominantly with stylet-driven leads. Direct conduction system capture (LBBP+LFP) was associated with a lower adjusted risk of heart-failure hospitalization than LVSP, although this was based on few events; these findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in randomized trials.

title: Distal Reinterventions after Branched Stented Anastomosis Frozen Elephant Trunk Repair (B-SAFER): A Report from a Prospective Trial.
authorString: Vargo PR, Leib P, Pasricha A, Gould J, Lowry AM, Lou X, Koprivanac M, Caputo F, Kalahasti V, Kuramochi Y, Roselli EE, B-SAFER Investigators.

journal.title: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery

abstractText:
Objective

Optimal timing for distal reintervention after frozen elephant trunk repair remains debated. We evaluated patient characteristics, clinical outcomes, and predictors of distal aortic reintervention following Branched Stented Anastomosis Frozen Elephant Trunk Repair (B-SAFER).

Methods

From May 2021 to January 2025, 405 patients underwent B-SAFER in a prospective, single-arm, nonrandomized PS-IDE cohort. Among them, 117 patients required 148 distal reinterventions. Indications for initial repair were acute type A dissection (36/189, 31%), chronic dissection (62/138, 53%), and degenerative aneurysm (19/78, 16%). Most reinterventions (n=132, 92%) were planned. Primary endpoints were operative mortality, stroke, and paralysis. Kaplan-Meier analysis assessed survival and freedom from reintervention. Median follow-up was 1.3 years, and median time to reintervention was 8.7 months.

Results

Mortality after first reintervention was 6.5% (n=8). Permanent stroke occurred in one patient (0.8%), with no cases of paralysis. Causes of death included sepsis (n=4), hemorrhagic shock (n=2), pulmonary embolism (n=1), and intracranial hemorrhage (n=1). Freedom from reintervention at 2 years was 64%, lowest in chronic dissections (48%), intermediate in degenerative aneurysms (71%), and highest in acute dissections (74%). Larger descending and abdominal aortic diameters were the strongest predictors of reintervention. Survival at 2.5 years was similar across groups (81% acute, 81% chronic, 77% degenerative).

Conclusions

Distal reinterventions after B-SAFER are common, safe, and are associated with acceptable early outcomes. Disease chronicity and aortic diameter predict reintervention risk. Frozen elephant trunk is an effective platform for staged aortic repair, and earlier reintervention in high-risk patients warrants further study. (245).

title: The evolution and future of conduction system pacing.
authorString: Lee SR, Vijayaraman P, Huang W, Jastrzębski M, Joza J, Burri H, Ponnusamy SS, Tung R, Lustgarten D, Choi EK.
abstractText: Cardiac pacing has undergone a fundamental paradigm shift from conventional right ventricular apical pacing towards physiological activation of the native conduction system of the heart. Decades of evidence have established that chronic right ventricular pacing induces ventricular dyssynchrony, contributing to pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and adverse clinical outcomes. Conduction system pacing, which engages the intrinsic His-Purkinje network of the heart, has emerged as a transformative approach that preserves or restores the natural ventricular activation sequence. His bundle pacing, the earliest form of conduction system pacing, provided proof of concept but is limited by technical challenges and high capture thresholds. Left bundle branch area pacing has since become the dominant modality, offering greater procedural success, lead stability and broader applicability: from management of bradycardia and prevention of pacing-induced cardiomyopathy to cardiac resynchronization therapy in heart failure. Bachmann bundle area pacing is an emerging atrial counterpart: by capturing a preferential interatrial conduction pathway, this approach reduces interatrial conduction delay and produces a more physiological atrial activation sequence than conventional right atrial appendage pacing. Bachmann bundle area pacing might, therefore, help to prevent atrial fibrillation. In this Review, we bring these ventricular and atrial strategies together under the unifying principle of physiological pacing, describe their mechanistic basis and technical evolution, appraise the latest evidence from randomized trials and address the practical questions that arise in clinical application, indicating where more evidence is required.

title: Role of Plasma Proteins in the Association Between Socioeconomic Status and Cardiovascular Disease Events: Results From Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine Cohorts.
authorString: Glover LM, Gillman MG, Green MD, O'Brien SN, Casanova R, Floyd JS, Kooperberg C, Odden MC, Rich SS, Rotter JI, Shah A, Tindle HA, Wood AC, Gerszten R, Reiner A, Garcia L, Cai Y, Akinyemiju T, O'Brien EC, Sims M, Raffield LM.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Socioeconomic status (SES) is strongly associated with cardiovascular disease burden and risk. Plasma proteins may elucidate a biological mechanism through which low SES increases the risk of cardiovascular disease.

Methods

Participants from the following 3 cohorts were included: the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (n=2139), Jackson Heart Study (n=967), and Women's Health Initiative (n=1104). SES was approximated using a cumulative score (range 0-3) across education, income, and employment status. A meta-analysis of Cox proportional hazards ratios was used to assess the association between SES and incident events for coronary heart disease (CHD) and stroke. Linear regression was used within each cohort to determine associations between SES and Olink proteins (n=1270 proteins) and the results were meta-analyzed across cohorts. Regression-based mediation analysis was used to determine whether the identified proteins were statistical mediators of the association of SES and incident events.

Results

Higher SES scores were associated with a lower risk of CHD (hazard ratio [HR], 0.74 [95% CI, 0.63-0.87]) and stroke (HR, 0.81 [95% CI, 0.66-1.00]). After correcting for multiple testing (P<3.937×10-5), 233 proteins were associated with SES in the meta-analysis. Of these 233 proteins, 21 had a significant indirect effect on SES and CHD. Because the SES-stroke association was not statistically significant, proteins were not tested as mediators.

Conclusions

Our analysis of multiple cohorts identified evidence of different proteomic pathways associated with SES and cardiovascular disease. This work suggests that exogenous social factors (eg, SES) may influence cardiovascular disease via proteomic profiles.

title: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Endovascular and Open Surgical Repair for Infective Native Aortic Aneurysms.
authorString: Coutinho ML, Bregalda Neves CR, Torres IO, Delgado LM, D'Oria M, Zerati AE, Leão PP.
abstractText:
Background
