Infective native aortic aneurysms (mycotic) are rare but highly lethal, and the optimal treatment strategy between endovascular repair and open surgical repair (OSR) remains debated because of a persistent trade-off between early survival and durable infection control. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing early and long-term outcomes of endovascular repair and OSR, complemented by a single-arm meta-analysis characterizing outcomes after endovascular repair.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to June 16, 2026. Comparative studies were pooled using inverse-variance random-effects models with REML estimation of between-study variance (ORs); single-arm proportions were pooled using logit-transformed, inverse-variance-weighted random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I. Outcomes included 30-day and 1-year all-cause mortality, reinfection (a new or persistent infection requiring antimicrobial therapy or source control), sepsis recurrence (a new episode meeting sepsis criteria after initial clinical resolution), reintervention, and acute kidney injury (AKI).

Results

Thirty-five retrospective studies were included: 18 comparative studies (2,853 enrolled patients; 1,305 endovascular repair and 1,548 OSR; 17 of which, comprising 2,836 patients, reported 30-day mortality) and 17 single-arm studies (444 endovascular repair patients; 16 of which reported 30-day mortality). Endovascular repair was associated with significantly lower 30-day mortality than OSR (OR 0.72, 95% CI 0.55-0.93) but not with 1-year mortality (8 studies, 1,630 patients; OR 1.23, 95% CI 0.66-2.29), and with a higher risk of reinfection (14 studies, 1,448 patients; OR 2.56, 95% CI 1.71-3.82). No significant differences were found for sepsis recurrence, reintervention, or AKI, though these comparisons were imprecise and compatible with both clinically meaningful benefit and harm, and should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence between strategies. In the single-arm analysis, pooled 30-day mortality after endovascular repair was 6.5%, 1-year mortality was 22.4%, and reinfection was 14.7%.

Conclusions

In pooled analysis, endovascular repair was associated with lower early mortality compared with open surgical repair, although this finding was sensitive to the inclusion of a single large registry-based study and should be interpreted with caution. No significant difference in 1-year mortality was observed, but this comparison was imprecise and based on few studies and should not be interpreted as evidence that a survival advantage is absent. Endovascular repair carries a higher risk of reinfection. Careful patient selection, prolonged antimicrobial therapy, and structured postoperative surveillance remain essential regardless of the repair strategy chosen. Certainty of evidence for all comparative outcomes was very low (GRADE), reflecting the observational design, serious risk of confounding by indication, and imprecision of the pooled estimates.

title: Mapping human genetic associations to drug targets in valvular heart disease: an integrative evidence synthesis.
authorString: Moura-Ferreira S, Ustunkaya T, Siddiqui M, Kukendrarajah K, Schmidt F, Ahmed R, Khanji M, Chahal A, Verwerft J, Providencia R.
abstractText:
Background

Valvular heart disease (VHD) lacks disease-modifying pharmacological therapies. Drug repurposing guided by human genetics may help identify therapeutic opportunities. We aimed to integrate human genetic associations, drug-target information, and clinical evidence to identify repurposing opportunities and prioritise potentially druggable targets across the VHD spectrum.

Methods

We retrieved VHD-associated genetic variants from the NHGRI-EBI Genome-Wide Association Studies Catalogue and Ensembl, interrogated annotated genes in the Open Targets Platform, and evaluated linked drugs through structured searches of MEDLINE and ClinicalTrials.gov. The study protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251071741).

Findings

We identified 1464 genetic associations corresponding to 844 unique variants and 582 candidate genes. Of these genes, 431 had tractability information and 51 had linked compounds, comprising 388 distinct pharmacological agents, 273 in phase 3 or 4 of clinical development. Drug-linked targets were concentrated in aortic stenosis. Clinical evidence supported therapeutic potential for 14 drugs, with preclinical or mechanistic cardiovascular support for eight additional drugs and adverse cardiovascular signals for four. An exploratory evidence-weighted framework prioritised targets according to genetic-functional evidence, tissue and mechanistic context, and translational tractability.

Interpretation

This genetics-informed evidence synthesis identifies drug-repurposing opportunities and a substantial gap between genetically supported targets and available therapies. The findings provide a hypothesis-generating framework for mechanistic validation and future valve-focused studies.

Funding

Limburg Clinical Research Centre of UHasselt, Jessa and ZOL; British Heart Foundation; National Institute for Health and Care Research; UK Research and Innovation; European Research Council; Horizon Europe.

title: Greater Neighborhood Resources Predict Reduced In-Hospital Death for Children With Heart Failure and Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Markiewitz ND, O'Connor MJ, Liu H, Penney C, Ludomirsky A, Dewitt A, Kozyak BW, Eichner J, Ahmed H, Edwards J, Lin KY, Chaudhary A, Khan S, Wittlieb-Weber C, Maeda K, Rossano J, Edelson JB.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Patients with pediatric heart failure (HF) face significant morbidity and death. However, there are limited data describing neighborhood characteristics in pediatric patients with HF or exploring the relationship of these factors to resource use and clinical outcomes. We used the Child Opportunity Index 3.0 (COI), a composite index of community resources pertinent to child health, to describe neighborhood characteristics for children with HF and identify its associations with in-hospital death.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study used the Pediatric Health Information System, a national administrative database of tertiary care pediatric hospitals. Inpatient encounters between January 2014 and December 2024 for pediatric patients (aged <18 years) with HF and cardiomyopathy were identified using International Classification of Diseases (ICD) codes. The primary exposure of interest was the COI, and the primary outcome of interest was in-hospital death. Mixed logistic regression models were estimated, unadjusted and adjusted for administrative sex, age, race, and primary payor.

Results

Our cohort consisted of index HF admissions in 7060 patients. Half of the cohort was in either the very low (n=2034 [29%]) or low (n=1521 [22%]) COI quintile. After adjustment, patients with a very high COI were less likely to experience in-hospital death than those living in very low COI neighborhoods (odds ratio, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.54-0.99]; P=0.048).

Conclusions

A substantial proportion of children admitted with HF have limited neighborhood resources. Those with higher neighborhood resources are more likely to survive to discharge, emphasizing the relationship between environmental factors and clinical outcomes in pediatric HF.

title: PASCAL Precision System Outcomes by Implant Location and Lesion Location in Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation Patients From the STS/ACC TVT Registry.
authorString: Ramanathan PK, Makkar R, Waggoner T, Latib A, Kipperman RM, Hanson I, Sinha AK, Chakravarty T, Sharma RP, Depta JP, Castellanos JA, Kodali S, Krishnaswamy A, Whisenant B, Menees D, Lim DS, Gilani F, Sanchez CE, Gheewala N, Garcia S, Gada H, Kapadia S, Shah PB, Renard B, Theodos G, Yaryura R, Gardner B, Steinberg DH, Gnall E, Kaddissi G, Chhatriwalla AK, Frangieh AH, Eleid MF, Géneréux P, Saxon JT, Villablanca P, Matar F, Agarwal H, Chetcuti S, Frisoli T, Zahr F.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair can be more challenging in noncentral regions of the valve and in anterior or bileaflet lesions. We assess effect of implant location and leaflet lesion location on safety and effectiveness of PASCAL Precision system in degenerative mitral regurgitation (MR).

Methods

Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair outcomes in patients with degenerative MR treated with PASCAL Precision system (September 2022-October 2024), from the US STS/ACC TVT (Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy) Registry, were analyzed by implant location (A2P2/non-A2P2) and leaflet lesion location (anterior/posterior/bileaflet). Procedural, clinical, and echocardiographic outcomes to 30 days were assessed.

Results

At 30 days, both A2P2 (n=1526) and non-A2P2 (n=299) groups had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 1.1% versus 1.0%, mitral valve reintervention: 0.4% versus 0.0% and single leaflet device attachment: 0.5% versus 0.3%; all P>0.05) and demonstrated significant MR reduction (P<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference between groups (P=0.750) (MR ≤2+: 93.4% versus 95.4%; MR ≤1+: 72.0% versus 73.3%). Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores improved significantly in both groups (∆19.3, ∆17.7 points; P=0.741). The anterior (n=250), posterior (n=902), and bileaflet (n=192) disease groups also had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 0.4%, 1.1%, 0.0%; mitral valve reintervention: 0.8%, 0.1%, 0.5%; and single leaflet device attachment: 0.8%, 0.2%, 0.5%; all P>0.05), and demonstrated significant MR reduction (P<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference across groups (P=0.459) (MR ≤2+: 94.1%, 93.1%, and 94.5%; MR ≤1+: 79.0%, 69.2%, and 72.4%). All groups experienced significant improvement in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores (∆21.4, ∆18.8, ∆12.0 points; P=0.087).

Conclusion

In real-world patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation, treatment with the PASCAL Precision system was associated with favorable safety and effectiveness at 30 days, regardless of implant location or leaflet lesion location.

title: Arrhythmic events and genetic variants as drivers for Takotsubo Syndrome: a patient-specific atrial stem-cell model.
authorString: Brand C, Zinke C, Syed Ali G, Hübscher D, Ajmail K, Seedorf A, Steinker P, Treu F, Jung P, Eberl H, Li Y, Dybkova N, Feld L, Ghadri JR, Templin C, Sossalla S, Maack C, Voigt N, Nikolaev VO, Wollnik B, Streckfuss-Bömeke K.
abstractText: Takotsubo Syndrome (TTS) is an acute, potentially life-threatening condition often complicated by ventricular dysfunction and arrhythmias. Atrial fibrillation (AF) is common in TTS patients and associated with increased mortality. However, the arrhythmic mechanisms, genetic variability underlying TTS, and personalised therapy remain unclear. We generated induced pluripotent stem cell-derived atrial and ventricular cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs) from TTS patients and provoked TTS-like events by isoprenaline (Iso) stimulation. Compared with controls, atrial TTS iPSC-CMs exhibited enhanced diastolic sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) Ca²⁺ leak and increased arrhythmogenic potential following Iso exposure. Iso-induced stress further increased systolic Ca²⁺ transient amplitude and reduced phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE4) activity in TTS iPSC-CMs. Under baseline conditions, atrial TTS iPSC-CMs demonstrated unchanged Ca<sup>2+</sup> transient amplitude, reduced diastolic Ca<sup>2+</sup>, elevated SERCA2 activity with faster Ca²⁺ decay compared to controls, which could be explained by increased phosphorylation of PKA-specific phospholamban S16. In contrast, ventricular TTS-iPSC-CM showed increased L-Type Ca<sup>2+</sup> current density, but reduced Ca<sup>2+</sup> transient amplitude with increased resting Ca<sup>2+</sup> leak and reduced PDE4 activity post-Iso-exposure. In atrial TTS iPSC-CMs, the PDE4 activator MR-L2 restored PDE4 activity, normalised several defects in Ca²⁺ handling and prevented arrhythmias more efficiently than the β-blocker metoprolol. Genetic analyses identified variants in the Ca²⁺ handling genes AHNAK and CASQ2 in TTS. Using CRISPR/Cas9, we generated isogenic rescue and mutation-insertion lines, confirming a causal role of p.P5390T in catecholamine-induced arrhythmogenic phenotypes in atrial TTS iPSC-CMs. Our findings support a mechanistic link between genetic predisposition to an excessive catecholaminergic stress response, dysregulated PDE/cAMP signalling, and atrial arrhythmogenesis in TTS-CMs, identifying PDE4 as a potential therapeutic target in this critical condition.

title: MAF transcription factors: Emerging key players in cardiovascular health and disease.
authorString: Tang Z, Zhou B.

journal.title: The international journal of biochemistry & cell biology

abstractText: Cardiovascular diseases are a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, and their complex pathophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. The regulatory role of transcription factors provides a crucial avenue for investigating the mechanisms underlying these diseases. The MAF transcription factor family is a key member of the AP-1 superfamily, comprising two subfamilies: large MAFs (including MAFA, MAFB, MAF [c-MAF], and NRL) and small MAFs (including MAFK, MAFG, and MAFF). Different members exhibit distinct cellular expression patterns and functions within tissues: small MAFs members show high expression in cardiac tissue, participating in core pathological processes such as myocardial antioxidant stress, inflammatory response, and lipid metabolism disorders. They are closely associated with common cardiovascular diseases, including heart failure, myocardial fibrosis, atherosclerosis, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Large MAFs are more widely distributed across other tissues and cell types. For instance, MAFB is primarily expressed in macrophages, pancreatic α-cells, neurons, and microglia. MAF regulates cell differentiation and immune responses in diverse tissues, including the lens, pancreas, and kidney. MAFA and NRL are specifically expressed in pancreatic β-cells and retinal photoreceptor cells, respectively. However, preliminary evidence suggests that large MAFs may play a significant role in maintaining physiological homeostasis and driving pathological progression within the cardiovascular system. Therefore, this review will first summarize research progress on small MAFs in the cardiovascular system, and then discuss the potential biological roles of large MAFs, particularly MAFB and MAF, in maintaining physiological homeostasis and driving pathological progression within the cardiovascular system. Finally, we lay out future paths for elucidating the roles of MAFs, particularly large MAFs, in the cardiovascular system.

title: Rifampicin-soaked versus bovine prostheses in the management of aortic graft infections: a retrospective single-center cohort study.
authorString: Strzoda VW, Yordanov MD, Oberhuber A, Ibrahim A.
abstractText:
Background

Aortic vascular graft and endograft infections (aortic VGEI) remain a rare but life-threatening complication following aortic reconstruction. This retrospective study compares outcomes between bovine pericardial graft prostheses and rifampicin-soaked Dacron grafts.

Methods

In this retrospective single-center cohort study, we analyzed 62 patients between January 2018 and December 2025 for aortic vascular graft or endograft infection requiring graft explantation and in-situ reconstruction. Patients received either a bovine pericardial graft (n=21) or a rifampicin-soaked Dacron prosthesis (n=41). Survival, treatment failure, perioperative variables, and microbiology were analyzed.

Results

Patients in the bovine and rifampicin groups were comparable in terms of age (72.57 vs. 73.58 years, p = 0.685) and sex distribution (85.71% vs. 73.17% male, p = 0.346). BMI, preoperative dialysis, and aortic clamping time were higher in the bovine group. Four treatment failures, defined as persistent or recurrent infection of the reconstructed aortic segment, occurred during follow-up; all were observed after reconstruction with rifampicin-soaked Dacron (4/41, 9.8%), whereas no treatment failure occurred in the bovine pericardial group (0/21). In-hospital mortality was comparable between groups (n=3:14.3% vs. n=8: 19.5%, p = 0.735). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated no significant difference in survival (p = 0.256) or treatment failure rate (p = 0.833). Candida spp. were the most frequent pathogens (27.8%) and significantly associated with secondary aorto-enteric fistula (p=0.003).

Conclusion

Survival and treatment failure rates were comparable, with a trend toward fewer infection-related complications after bovine pericardial grafting. Despite use in more complex cases, bovine grafts may represent a promising biological alternative.

title: Residual Risk From Remnant Cholesterol and Inflammation Despite Lipid-Lowering Therapy and Association With Incident Peripheral Artery Disease in Type 2 Diabetes.
authorString: Liao R, Xiao Z, Huang C, Chen L, Liu Y, Wei X, Li M, Shen M, Hu Z, Bin J.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Despite guideline-recommended lipid-lowering therapy, patients with type 2 diabetes retain a significant residual risk for peripheral artery disease (PAD). The contributions of remnant cholesterol (RC) and systemic inflammation in this treated population, particularly beyond achieved low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, remain incompletely understood.

Methods

This prospective cohort study included 18 741 participants with type 2 diabetes from the UK Biobank who were free of PAD and were on lipid-lowering therapy at baseline. Plasma RC and hsCRP (high-sensitivity C-reactive protein) levels were measured at baseline. Incident PAD was ascertained over a median follow-up of 13.6 years. Multivariable Cox models were used to estimate hazard ratios after adjustment for demographic, clinical, metabolic, and treatment-related covariates, including low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and baseline coronary artery disease.

Results

During follow-up, incident PAD occurred in 1223 participants (6.5%). Elevated RC and hsCRP levels were each independently linked to an increased risk of PAD. Participants with concurrent elevations in both RC and hsCRP exhibited the highest risk of incident PAD. These associations remained robust across multiple sensitivity analyses, including exclusion of participants with baseline coronary artery disease, removal of events within the initial 2-year follow-up, elimination of individuals with hsCRP >10 mg/L, competing-risk analyses accounting for death, and further adjustment for detailed lipid-lowering therapy categories.

Conclusions

Among patients with type 2 diabetes receiving lipid-lowering therapy for primary prevention of PAD, elevated RC and systemic inflammation are independently and jointly associated with future PAD risk. These findings highlight substantial residual risk beyond managed low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and support the need for further strategies targeting both remnant lipoproteins and inflammation in this high-risk population.

title: Differences between Japan and France in transcatheter aortic valve implantation: insights from the TOTO-TAVI study.
authorString: Iwata J, Hayashida K, Arow Z, Masumoto A, Tsuruta H, Yamada T, Shimizu H, Ieda M, De Biase C, Dumonteil N, Tchétché D.
abstractText:
Background

The number of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) procedures is increasing worldwide. However, studies comparing regional differences remain scarce.

Aims

This study aimed to compare clinical outcomes after TAVI between Japan and France using a database compiled from two large hospitals.

Methods

The TOTO-TAVI study included patients who underwent TAVI in Japan and France. The primary endpoint was in-hospital death. Periprocedural safety outcomes and 3-year all-cause mortality were also evaluated. A subgroup analysis was performed to assess the independent TAVI risk for each country.

Results

Among 6,967 patients who underwent TAVI between 2016 and 2024, 1,422 in Japan and 4,771 in France were included. Although patients in Japan showed a significantly smaller body size, a smaller aortic valve, and a higher operative risk than those in France, the in-hospital death rate was comparable between the two groups (0.6% vs 1.3%; p=0.068). The new pacemaker implantation rate was lower in Japan than in France. There was no significant difference in 3-year all-cause mortality between Japan and France (22.5% vs 23.5%, hazard ratio 0.678, 95% confidence interval: 0.114-4.033; p=0.583). For the subgroup analysis, there were no statistically significant independent risk factors for composite outcomes, including in-hospital death, stroke, and bleeding, in Japan; however, in France, female sex, higher body mass index, lower haemoglobin levels, previous coronary artery bypass grafting and cerebrovascular disease, bicuspid annulus, and general anaesthesia were independent risk factors.

Conclusions

Despite differences in patient backgrounds, in-hospital and 3-year mortality were comparable between Japan and France, suggesting that procedural safety and medium-term prognosis after TAVI were established regardless of procedural risks.

title: Secondary Intervention Burden After Fenestrated Endovascular Aortic Repair: A Patient-Level and Procedure-Level Analysis of a 14-Year Single-Center Experience.
authorString: Rossillon A, Massad N, Sagnet R, Gonzalez Urquijo M, Magnan PE, Bartoli MA.

journal.title: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists

abstractText:
Purpose

To quantify the patient-level and procedure-level burden, concentration, timing, and characteristics of secondary interventions after fenestrated endovascular aortic repair (FEVAR), and their association with subsequent mortality.

Materials and methods

This retrospective single-center study included 189 consecutive patients treated with FEVAR between 2007 and 2021. Secondary interventions were classified by clinical magnitude, approach, timing, and primary indication. The cumulative incidence of a first secondary intervention was estimated using the Aalen-Johansen method with death as a competing event. The association with subsequent mortality was assessed using a time-dependent Cox model.

Results

Technical success was achieved in 185 of 189 patients (97.9%). Median observed follow-up was 40.9 months (interquartile range, 25.1-61.2), and median potential follow-up was 57.4 months. Forty-eight patients (25.4%) underwent 67 secondary procedures. Nine patients, representing 4.8% of the cohort, underwent repeated interventions and accounted for 28 procedures (41.8%). Of the 67 procedures, 25 (37.3%) were major, 42 (62.7%) were minor, and 52 (77.6%) were endovascular. Thirty-seven procedures (55.2%) occurred more than 1 year after FEVAR. The 48-month cumulative incidence of a first secondary intervention was 24.7%, compared with 27.0% using 1 minus Kaplan-Meier. At the last available imaging examination, 610 of 615 assessable fenestrated target vessels were patent (99.2%). Secondary intervention was not statistically associated with subsequent mortality (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.11; 95% confidence interval, 0.68-1.80; P = .687).

Conclusion

Secondary interventions affected approximately one quarter of patients after FEVAR, but a small subgroup accounted for a disproportionate share of the procedural burden. Most procedures were minor and endovascular, and more than half occurred beyond 1 year. No statistically significant average association with subsequent mortality was identified. Reporting both patient- and procedure-level burden may better characterize FEVAR durability and follow-up requirements.Clinical ImpactSecondary interventions after fenestrated endovascular aortic repair (FEVAR) are commonly reported as the proportion of patients undergoing at least 1 procedure, which does not capture cumulative procedural burden. In this cohort of 189 patients, 48 underwent 67 secondary interventions, whereas only 9 patients, representing 4.8% of the cohort, accounted for 41.8% of all procedures. Most interventions were minor and endovascular, but more than half occurred beyond 1 year. These findings indicate that first reintervention rates alone incompletely describe FEVAR durability. Reporting both patient- and procedure-level burden may better inform patient counseling, surveillance planning, and comparisons across devices and centers by highlighting the concentration of procedures in a small subgroup.

title: Transient ST-T Changes During Submaximal Exercise Revealing Anomalous Right Coronary Artery Origin in an Asymptomatic Athlete.
authorString: Illinger V, Kovanda J, Slabý K, Procházka M, Radvanský J, Materna O, Marek J.
abstractText:
Background

Anomalous aortic origin of a coronary artery is a recognised structural cause of sudden cardiac death in athletes younger than 35 years. Most affected individuals are asymptomatic prior to cardiac events, and resting and exercise electrocardiography (ECG) findings are frequently normal or non-specific, limiting the effectiveness of preparticipation screening.

Case summary

We report a case of a 22-year-old asymptomatic athlete in whom preparticipation screening revealed transient ST-segment depression and T-wave inversions during submaximal exercise and recovery, whereas findings at peak exercise remained normal. Point-of-care echocardiography performed by a sports medicine specialist raised suspicion of an anomalous origin of the right coronary artery from the left aortic sinus of Valsalva, which was subsequently confirmed by computed tomography coronary angiography. High-risk anatomical features included an acute ostial angle and an interarterial course of the right coronary artery. Functional testing with exercise myocardial stress scintigraphy showed no inducible perfusion defect. Following multidisciplinary consultation, a conservative management strategy with activity modification and close follow-up was adopted.

Discussion

This case highlights the potential clinical significance of transient ST-T abnormalities occurring during submaximal exercise and recovery, even in the absence of symptoms or abnormalities at peak workload. In this patient, recognition of this reproducible but non-specific ECG pattern prompted further structural evaluation leading to the diagnosis of AAOCA. It also underscores the limitations of current guidelines in managing asymptomatic athletes with high-risk coronary anatomy but without evidence of inducible ischaemia, supporting the need for individualised decision-making.

title: Outcomes of Total Endovascular Repair of Aortic Arch and Thoraco-abdominal Aortic Aneurysms in the International Multicenter Aortic Research Group in a Selected Group of Patients with Extensive Aortic Aneurysm Disease.
authorString: Gallitto E, Oderich GS, Kölbel T, Haulon S, Tsilimparis N, Dias N, Schanzer A, Sobocinski J, Mani K, Gargiulo M, TEAR study group.

journal.title: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery

abstractText:
Objective

The aim of this study was to report outcomes of total endovascular aortic repair (TEAR) using arch branched endovascular aortic repair (aBEVAR) and thoraco-abdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA) fenestrated branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR).

Methods

Clinical data from 16 participating centres in the International Multicenter Aortic Research Group from 2014 to 2024 were retrospectively analysed. All patients who underwent TEAR were included. The primary outcome was aortic related mortality (ARM). Secondary outcomes included stroke and or transient ischaemic attack (TIA), spinal cord ischaemia (SCI), and freedom from target artery (TA) instability, re-interventions, and new cardiovascular events (CVEs) within 1 year.

Results

Of 98 patients scheduled for TEAR, 95 (97%) completed both stages, including 46 (48%) with chronic post-dissection aneurysms and 49 (52%) with degenerative aneurysms. A multistage approach with aBEVAR followed by TAAA FBEVAR was used in all patients, with a median interval between stages of 11 months (interquartile range [IQR] 5, 14). One (1%) rupture occurred between the staged procedures (successfully managed with off the shelf TAAA multibranch stent graft). Custom made and off the shelf TAAA FBEVAR devices were used in 79 (83%) and 16 (17%) patients, respectively. There were 12 (13%) stroke and or TIAs (aBEVAR, ten; TAAA FBEVAR, two); five (5%) had a modified Rankin Scale score > 3. Sixteen patients (17%) experienced SCI (aBEVAR, two; TAAA FBEVAR, 14) with three cases (3%) of paraplegia. Four patients (4%) died within thirty days; these were the only cases of ARM. Median follow up was 32 months (IQR 3, 61). Of 67 patients (71%) with available one year follow up, there were six (9%) with TA instability and five (7%) CVEs. Estimated three year survival was 79 ± 5% with a cumulative incidence of re-intervention of 31 ± 6%.

Conclusion

Multistage TEAR with aBEVAR followed by TAAA FBEVAR was associated with low ARM, re-intervention, and TA instability. Stroke and SCI remain significant and must be carefully weighed during patient selection and treatment.

title: A Geometrically Tunable Cardiovascular Shunt for the Individualized Care of Neonates with Congenital Heart Defects.
authorString: Seiner AJ, Posthill E, Hager L, Gontarski R, Zamora ME, Espy CL, Sarkar B, Brenner JS, Spiller KL, Throckmorton AL, Rodell CB.
abstractText: Congenital heart defects (CHDs), particularly single-ventricle anomalies such as hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS), require early surgical intervention using fixed-diameter vascular shunts. However, current shunts are incapable of adapting to the physiological changes of infant growth, often leading to hemodynamic imbalance and elevated mortality risk. Here, we report a geometrically tunable cardiovascular shunt lined with a photoresponsive hydrogel based on methacrylated dextran (DexMA) and dithiothreitol (DTT). This dual-stage crosslinked hydrogel system enables minimally invasive modulation of the inner lumen diameter in response to external blue light. We optimized the hydrogel composition to achieve both mechanical robustness (Young's modulus ≈ 8.5 kPa) and light-induced deswelling, allowing for lumen expansion up to 39% with high stability over one month. In vitro studies confirmed excellent cytocompatibility, hemocompatibility, and minimal immune activation. Prototype annular shunts demonstrated precise, programmable diameter increases (15-18%) corresponding to computational models of infant growth. This dynamic, photoresponsive platform is a critical advance toward implantable materials for personalized cardiovascular interventions and a significant step toward growth-accommodating pediatric medical devices.

title: Shared Genetic Architecture Between Mental Disorders and Heart Failure Subtypes: A Comprehensive Multitrait Genome-Wide Analysis.
authorString: Yan S, Chai K, Yang J, Cui J, Wang H.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Mental disorders and heart failure frequently co-occur, but their shared genetic architecture remains incompletely understood.

Methods

Prospective Cox regression analysis in the UK Biobank (UKB) quantified the risk of incident heart failure associated with mental disorders. Linkage disequilibrium score regression estimated genetic correlations, while multitrait genome-wide association and cross-phenotype association analyses identified candidate pleiotropic loci. Statistical fine mapping and gene-level association analyses prioritized candidate variants and genes. Bayesian colocalization assessed evidence for shared candidate variants, and exploratory Gene Ontology biological-process overrepresentation analysis provided descriptive biological context. Single-cell RNA sequencing and genetically informed spatial mapping (gsMap) provided cellular and spatial context for prioritized genes. Geneformer-based in silico perturbation analysis was performed using a cardiac cell atlas of dilated cardiomyopathy to prioritize candidate pleiotropic genes and identify cardiac cell states showing predicted embedding shifts.

Results

Prospective UKB analyses demonstrated that mental disorders, such as posttraumatic stress disorder, depression, and bipolar disorder, were associated with a higher risk of incident heart failure. Multitrait analysis identified 607 pleiotropic variants, with fine-mapping and colocalization converging on prioritized candidate loci, including TMEM18, NKX2-2, and XRN2. Single-cell expression profiling and spatial mapping provided context at the cellular and tissue levels for the prioritized genes. Geneformer-based in silico perturbation prioritized FOXP1 and TMEM106B as leading pleiotropic candidate genes on the basis of their predicted changes in downstream gene embeddings in cardiac cellular contexts.

Conclusions

This study identifies shared genetic architecture between mental disorders and heart failure and prioritizes candidate pleiotropic genes associated with both. Transcriptomic and in silico perturbation analyses provide exploratory cellular, spatial, and cardiac functional context. Functional validation is required before mechanistic or therapeutic interpretation.

title: Association between atherogenic index of plasma and microvascular complications in patients with type 2 diabetes achieving low-density lipoprotein cholesterol targets: a real-world cohort study.
authorString: Zhang S, Shao Y, Li M, Wang Y, Yu H, Cong R, Chen Z, Yin X, Zhou Y, Ren H.
abstractText:
Background

Despite achieving low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) targets, patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remain at significant risk for microvascular complications. We aimed to investigate whether the atherogenic index of plasma (AIP), a marker of atherogenic dyslipidaemia, is associated with these complications in a real-world cohort of patients with controlled LDL-C.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study using electronic health records from community health centres in Shenzhen, China (2018-2024). We included 16,469 participants with T2DM and LDL-C<2.6 mmol/L at baseline, categorising them into tertiles (T1-3) based on baseline AIP. The primary outcome was a composite of incident diabetic retinopathy, diabetic nephropathy, and diabetic peripheral neuropathy, identified via ICD-10 codes. We used multivariable Cox proportional hazards models to assess associations.

Results

During a median follow-up of 4.6 years, 1,056 participants developed microvascular complications. We observed a graded association between AIP tertiles and the risk of microvascular complications. Participants in T3 had a significantly higher risk of total microvascular complications than those in T1 (hazard ratio (HR) = 1.34; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.15-1.56), while T2 showed no statistically significant increase in risk (HR = 1.10; 95% CI = 0.94-1.28). Specifically, compared to T1, T3 participants had significantly higher risks of diabetic nephropathy (HR = 1.62; 95% CI = 1.30-2.01) and diabetic peripheral neuropathy (HR = 1.39; 95% CI = 1.13-1.70), while no statistically significant association was found for diabetic retinopathy risk (HR = 1.23; 95% CI = 0.93-1.63). In contrast, compared with T1 participants, those in T2 had higher risks of nephropathy (HR = 1.28; 95% CI = 1.02-1.59), but no statistically significant associations were found for diabetic peripheral neuropathy or diabetic retinopathy.

Conclusions

We found that AIP is independently associated with increased risk of microvascular complications, particularly diabetic nephropathy and diabetic peripheral neuropathy, even in T2DM patients achieving LDL-C targets. These results suggest that AIP may serve as a simple, lipid-based marker to help identify patients with residual microvascular risk beyond conventional LDL-C control.

title: Inflammatory regulatory mechanisms and targeted therapy of antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies in atherosclerosis (Review).
authorString: Cui J, Cui Q, Dou J, Li X, Chang W, Shi L, An L.
abstractText: Atherosclerosis is the core pathological basis of cardiocerebrovascular diseases, and inflammatory response runs through the course of its occurrence, progression, and adverse events. Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCAs) are autoantibodies targeting the lysosomal components in the cytoplasm of neutrophils and monocytes, and their association with atherosclerosis and pathogenic effects have become a research hotspot in cardiovascular medicine. The present review systematically examined the core molecular mechanisms of ANCA‑mediated atherosclerosis, focusing on analyzing the pro‑atherogenic effects of ANCAs through the regulation of monocyte dysfunction, induction of the formation of neutrophil extracellular traps, and activation of the synergistic complement‑platelet pathway, and clarified the subtype‑specific pathogenic pathways mediated by myeloperoxidase‑ANCAs and proteinase 3‑ANCAs. The present review also summarized the clinical evidence linking ANCA positivity to the risk of atherosclerosis, plaque characteristics, and clinical outcomes and explores the precise intervention strategies for targeting ANCA‑related pathways in atherosclerosis. Finally, it highlighted the limitations of current research and future directions to provide a theoretical reference and novel insights for the risk stratification of populations at high risk of atherosclerosis and the precise management of residual inflammatory risk.

title: Genetic and functional analysis of CDH2 reveals new insights into CDH2-related disorders.
authorString: Reis LM, Chisholm SAM, Frank K, Poplawski AB, Replogle MR, Capasso JE, Banke I, Thompson S, Ceroni F, Becmeur-Lefebvre M, Argilli E, Roberts AE, Livesey H, Murch O, Lenberg J, Sweeney NM, Wigby K, Ismail V, Rasmussen M, Rokkjær M, Auber B, Moutton S, Martin-Berenguer S, Acosta AX, Fernandes BS, Squire A, Glass I, Gowda VK, Naara VR, Srinivasan VM, Sorlin A, Marchese A, Gazdagh G, Wedderburn S, Beneteau C, Denis-Musquer M, Remmelzwaal PC, Bohnsack BL, Sherr EH, Chassaing N, Ragge N, Levin AV, Arno G, Sergeev YV, Semina EV.

journal.title: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics

abstractText:
Purpose

Pathogenic variants in CDH2 cause agenesis of the corpus callosum, cardiac, ocular, and genital syndrome (ACOGS). We aimed to define the clinical and molecular landscape of CDH2-related developmental disorders.

Methods

Newly identified and previously reported families were analyzed for genotype-phenotype correlations; variants were assessed using protein modeling and splicing assays.

Results

Screening identified 20 new families carrying (likely) pathogenic ((L)P) alleles (n=16) or high-priority variants of uncertain significance (VUS) (n=4), including 12 novel CDH2 alleles. The combined (L)P cohort (37 individuals) showed variable ACOGS core features (mean 3; range 1-5), along with abdominal wall and/or diaphragmatic hernias and nipple, spine or gastrointestinal anomalies, each seen in ∼20% of individuals. Novel ACOGS findings included ambiguous genitalia, female genital malformations and dilated cardiomyopathy. Missense variants, principally within extracellular cadherin domains, accounted for 86% of unique (L)P alleles with clusters in EC1 and EC4-EC5; the remainder produce late protein truncations or in-frame deletions. Disruption of calcium binding was predicted by modeling. Conversely, VUS were primarily nonsense-mediated decay-sensitive or deletions (71%), linked to neurodevelopmental, kidney or other anomalies.

Conclusion

We expand the ACOGS spectrum and highlight its striking clinical variability. Additionally, we identify a possible milder phenotype associated with CDH2 haploinsufficiency.

title: Structure bioinformatics of eight human ATP synthase F0 subunits and their AlphaFold3-predicted reduced-hydrophobicity QTY analogues.
authorString: Wang Z, Chen E, Zhang S.
abstractText: Human mitochondrial ATP synthase is an essential rotary motor enzyme that produces most of the cellular ATP through oxidative phosphorylation. Its membrane-embedded F0 sector contains highly hydrophobic transmembrane subunits that are challenging to study in aqueous environments without detergents. We applied the QTY code to eight human ATP synthase F0 subunits: ATP6, ATP8, ATPK, ATP68, ATPMK, AT5G1, AT5G2, and AT5G3. Hydrophobic amino acids leucine (L), isoleucine (I), valine (V), and phenylalanine (F) in transmembrane regions were systematically replaced with hydrophilic glutamine (Q), threonine (T), and tyrosine (Y). Four native subunits with available CryoEM structures from human ATP synthase (PDB: 8H9S) were superposed with their AlphaFold3-predicted QTY analogues. For subunits without complete CryoEM structures, AlphaFold3-predicted native structures were superposed with their AlphaFold3-predicted QTY analogues. Additional structural analyses were included, and key structural and functional regions, including ATP68 and the ATP6-c-ring interface, were modeled. The native ATP synthase F0 subunits superposed well with their respective QTY analogues. For the CryoEM-native comparisons, RMSD values ranged from 0.565 Å to 6.952 Å. For the AlphaFold3-native comparisons of subunits without CryoEM structures, RMSD values ranged from 0.204Å to 0.297Å. Considering all eight subunits, despite substantial QTY substitutions in the transmembrane regions, ranging from 38.89% to 50.79%, the QTY analogues retained similar overall folds, molecular weights, and isoelectric points. Hydrophobic surface analysis showed that the QTY analogues had reduced hydrophobic surfaces compared with their native counterparts. These structural bioinformatics studies suggest that the QTY code is applicable to ATP synthase F0 subunits to generate more hydrophilic, water-soluble analogues while preserving overall structural similarity. These results extend the application of the QTY code to the membrane-embedded F0 sector of ATP synthase and provide a foundation for future experimental studies for these QTY analogues expressed, purified, and evaluated for self-assembly.

title: Macrophage-Derived Glycoprotein Nonmetastatic Melanoma Protein B Attenuates Cardiac Dysfunction by Promoting Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor-Independent Angiogenesis.
authorString: Lin H, Yang Z, Zhang C, Ruan L, Huang Z, Hong C, Lu H, Lin J.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Pressure overload-induced heart failure involves maladaptive cardiac remodeling and inadequate angiogenesis. The limitations of VEGF (vascular endothelial growth factor)-based therapies underscore the need to identify alternative angiogenic pathways. GPNMB (glycoprotein nonmetastatic melanoma protein B) is a macrophage-secreted protein implicated in tissue repair, but its role in pressure overload-induced cardiac remodeling and its potential to modulate angiogenesis remain unknown.

Methods

Myeloid-specific Gpnmb knockout and control mice were subjected to transverse aortic constriction. Cardiac function, remodeling, and capillary density were assessed. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed to identify transcriptomic changes. In vitro, human endothelial cells were treated with recombinant GPNMB to assess proliferation, migration, and tube formation, and to dissect the underlying signaling pathways. The therapeutic potential of Gpnmb overexpression was evaluated using AAV9 vectors.

Results

Myeloid Gpnmb deletion exacerbated transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac dysfunction, hypertrophy, fibrosis, and capillary rarefaction. Single-cell sequencing revealed a reduced capillary endothelial cell population and pathway enrichment indicative of endothelial dysfunction and metabolic reprogramming in myeloid-specific Gpnmb knockout hearts. Mechanistically, GPNMB directly promoted endothelial cell proliferation, migration, and tube formation by activating the mTOR (mechanistic target of rapamycin) pathway in a CD44-dependent manner, independently of VEGF signaling. Cardiac-specific Gpnmb overexpression rescued angiogenesis, improved cardiac function, and attenuated pathological remodeling after transverse aortic constriction.

Conclusions

Macrophage-derived GPNMB is a critical regulator of cardiac adaptation to pressure overload. It promotes a VEGF-independent angiogenic program probably via the CD44/mTOR axis, as supported by in vitro mechanistic studies. GPNMB represents a promising therapeutic target for heart failure characterized by microvascular rarefaction.

title: Plasminogen Activator Inhibitor-1 Deficiency Exacerbates Pressure Overload-Induced Cardiac Hypertrophy in Mice.
authorString: Huang C, Shu S, Yue X, Piao J, Narisawa M, Zhong C, Zhao L, Wang N, Zhang H, Chen Y, Zhang M, Cheng XW, Li S.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Pathological cardiac hypertrophy is a key precursor to heart failure. PAI-1 (plasminogen activator inhibitor-1) is a recognized profibrotic mediator, yet its role in the heart remains paradoxical and incompletely understood.

Methods

Six-week-old male wild-type (PAI-1+/+) and PAI-1 knockout (PAI-1-/-) mice underwent sham or transverse aortic constriction surgery, followed by assessment of cardiac morphology, molecular markers, and function. In H9C2 cardiomyocytes, PAI-1 was silenced or overexpressed before angiotensin II stimulation, with or without targeted signaling inhibitors, followed by coimmunoprecipitation, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence.

Results

Pressure overload increased plasma and myocardial PAI-1 levels. PAI-1 deficiency exacerbated transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac dysfunction, hypertrophy, and fibrosis, accompanied by JAK2/STAT3 (Janus kinase 2/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3) activation and collagen overexpression, whereas cardiac-specific overexpression attenuated these maladaptive changes. Moreover, STAT3 inhibition reversed the adverse cardiac remodeling associated with PAI-1 deletion. In vitro, PAI-1 knockdown potentiated angiotensin II-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, an effect that was rescued by PAI-1 overexpression. Mechanistically, PAI-1 associated with JAK2 and STAT3, with reduced phosphorylation of both proteins and impaired STAT3 nuclear translocation. Critically, pharmacological inhibition of STAT3 abolished the harmful effects of PAI-1 silencing.

Conclusions

PAI-1 acts as an endogenous cardioprotective checkpoint by negatively regulating JAK2/STAT3 signaling. These findings suggest a noncanonical cardiomyocyte-associated function of PAI-1 beyond its classical fibrinolytic role and identify the PAI-1-JAK2/STAT3 axis as a potential therapeutic target for heart failure with hypertrophy.

title: Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Inducing Kinase- and Inhibitor of Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Kinase Subunit Beta-Binding Protein Promotes Pathological Cardiac Hypertrophy by Regulating Inhibitor of Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Kinase Subunit Beta-Mediated Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Activation.
authorString: Xie Z, Zuo Y, Wang M, Zhang X, Zhang L, Liu Z, Zhang B, Su Z, Yang S, Yang H, Zhang J, Ni Z, Liu H, Pei F.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Pathological cardiac hypertrophy is a major risk factor for heart failure. NIBP (NF-κB [nuclear factor kappa-B] inducing kinase- and inhibitor of NF-κB kinase subunit beta-binding protein) is a key regulator of cytokine-induced NF-κB signaling, but its role in cardiac hypertrophy remains unknown.

Methods

We established transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac hypertrophy in mice and phenylephrine-induced hypertrophy in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes. Genetic interventions included generation of whole-body Nibp knockout mice via CRISPR-Cas9; creation of cardiomyocyte-specific Nibp knockout mice using adeno-associated virus serotype 9-delivered Cre and single-guide RNAs in Rosa26-LSL-Cas9 mice; and cardiac-specific Nibp overexpression via adeno-associated virus serotype 9delivery. In neonatal rat ventricular myocytes, NIBP was knocked down or overexpressed using adenoviruses. Phenotypes were assessed by echocardiography, histology (wheat germ agglutinin, picrosirius redstaining), and molecular analyses. Mechanisms were investigated via RNA-sequencing, coimmunoprecipitation, and Western blotting for key signaling molecules.

Results

NIBP protein was upregulated in hypertrophic hearts and cardiomyocytes. Both Nibp-knockout and cardiomyocyte-specific Nibp knockout attenuated transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac dysfunction, hypertrophy, and fibrosis, whereas Nibp overexpression exacerbated these pathologies. Consistently, in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes, NIBP knockdown mitigated, while its overexpression aggravated, phenylephrine-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and inflammatory responses. Mechanistically, NIBP directly interacted with IKKβ (inhibitor of NF-κB kinase subunit beta), enhanced its phosphorylation, and drove hyperactivation of the downstream NF-κB pathway. Overexpression of a kinase-dead IKKβ mutant reversed the hypertrophic effects of NIBP.

Conclusions

NIBP promotes pathological cardiac hypertrophy by activating the IKKβ/NF-κB axis, identifying it as a potential therapeutic target for cardiac remodeling and heart failure.

title: Current Applications of Robotic Surgery in Aortic Procedures: A Scoping Review.
authorString: Filippini D, Farres H, Polania-Sandoval C, Erben Y.
abstractText: ObjectiveTo map the applications and outcomes of robotic technologies in aortic and aortoiliac procedures, including robot-assisted laparoscopic surgery, endovascular procedures, and micro-robotics.MethodsPubMed was searched up to October 4, 2026, for primary studies including at least 3 patients treated with robotic or robot-assisted interventions for aortic or aortoiliac disease, following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Case reports and two-patient series were summarized separately.ResultsFifteen observational studies (552 patients) were included. Robot-assisted laparoscopic surgery (9 studies; 494 patients) was mainly applied to aortoiliac occlusive disease (385 procedures), with robotic proximal aortic anastomosis and open distal anastomoses, and less frequently to aneurysm repair. Conversion rates ranged from 0% to 20%, graft patency from 89% to 100% at up to 48 months, and hospital stay from 4 to 8 days. Robot-assisted endovascular procedures (5 studies; 49 patients) were mostly applied to single procedural steps. Robotic target vessel cannulation succeeded in 81% of vessels, and robotic gate cannulation achieved a shorter catheter path length than manual cannulation (35.7 vs 74.1 cm; P = 0.019), but longer cannulation time. Robotic arch navigation was associated with fewer cerebral high-intensity transient signals (median 0 vs 2; P = 0.018), and operator radiation dose at the shielded console was 96.5% lower than at the procedure table. No robot-related complications were reported. Micro-robotic sac puncture for type II endoleak embolization (1 study; 9 patients) succeeded in all cases.ConclusionRobotic technologies are a promising and feasible option for selected patients undergoing aortic procedures at experienced centers. Robot-assisted laparoscopic surgery showed acceptable conversion rates and favorable mid-term patency, while endovascular robotics improved technical and surrogate endpoints. As current evidence is limited to small observational series, prospective comparative studies are needed to define the clinical benefit of robotics compared with open and endovascular repair.

title: A semi-rapid deployment workflow to reduce device time in Evolut FX self-expanding transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
authorString: Doi S, Iwata H, Sato E, Takahashi N, Kaneko T, Nozaki YO, Uchiyama D, Okazaki S, Tabata M, Tang GHL, Minamino T.
abstractText:
Background

As transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) expands, improving deployment efficiency is increasingly important. We developed and implemented a semi-rapid pacing-assisted deployment workflow for the Evolut platform.

Aims

We sought to evaluate the procedural efficiency and early safety of this workflow for transfemoral (TF) Evolut FX TAVI.

Methods

In a single-centre registry, we performed a retrospective before-and-after analysis of consecutive TF Evolut FX procedures: semi-rapid deployment (n=48) versus conventional deployment (n=53). Device time was defined as the interval from initial advancement of the delivery system to final release of the Evolut FX valve. Prolonged device time was defined as >14 minutes (>75th percentile), and determinants were assessed using Firth's penalised logistic regression.

Results

The device time was shorter with semi-rapid deployment (9.0 [interquartile range [IQR] 6.0-13.0] minutes vs 14.0 [IQR 11.0-16.0] minutes; p<0.001), while operation and procedure times were similar (p=0.13 and p=0.16, respectively). The mean recapture count was higher in the semi-rapid group (0.85±1.09 vs 0.53±0.70; p=0.08), and contrast volume was higher (32.0 [IQR 25.0-42.0] mL vs 25.0 [IQR 15.0-33.0] mL; p=0.008). Paravalvular leak >=mild (31.2% vs 32.1%; p=1.0) and in-hospital pacemaker implantation (2.1% vs 7.5%; p=0.37) did not differ significantly between the groups. In multivariable analysis, recapture predicted a prolonged device time (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 4.74, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.75-14.19; p=0.002), whereas the semi-rapid workflow predicted a reduced device time (adjusted OR 0.10, 95% CI: 0.01-0.66; p=0.015).

Conclusions

Semi-rapid pacing-assisted Evolut FX deployment selectively reduced device time without compromising early in-hospital safety outcomes. Deployment efficiency represents a practical procedural target for workflow refinement in self-expanding TAVI.

title: A Vascular Surgery and Primary Care Partnership for Improving Resident Training in Peripheral Artery Disease Management.
authorString: Hmeluk NV, Nsa W, Homco J, Lesselroth B, Nelson PR, Zamor K, Kempe K.
abstractText:
Background

Early diagnosis, establishment of best medical management, and timely specialty referral for patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD) remain ongoing challenges. In this study, we sought to identify gaps in internal medicine (IM) and family medicine (FM) residents' self-rated competency of PAD management and investigated whether an educational session led by vascular surgeons could promote recognition and confidence in patient care.

Study design

A single educational session, featuring a PowerPoint presentation, hands-on training (pulse and Doppler examination), and open discussion, was offered to IM and FM residents on two separate occasions. A pre-session survey assessed self-rated knowledge, practices, attitudes, and medical training regarding PAD, followed by a truncated post-session survey. The responses were grouped as high vs. moderate/low. Descriptive statistics and the McNemar Exact test were used for paired sample comparison.

Results

Thirty-one residents completed both surveys (65% IM, 35% FM, 58% male, and 77% first- or second-year trainees). Pre-session data revealed gaps in knowledge with few residents rating their understanding as "high." Post-session, there was a significant increase across all measured areas (p<0.001). Notably, improvements were seen in the number of residents who felt highly confident in diagnosing PAD (from 16.1% to 90.3%), using a vascular Doppler (6.5% to 83.9%), ordering non-invasive testing (from 6.5% to 83.9%), performing a lower extremity pulse exam (from 12.9% to 87.1%), managing PAD for amputation prevention (from 12.9% to 71.0%), and referring to a vascular specialist (from 25.8% to 83.9%).

Conclusion

Resident knowledge and confidence improved significantly as a result of a singular educational session. This collaborative model between vascular surgery educators and primary care residency programs demonstrates an adaptable framework that successfully addresses a gap in PAD management training.

title: Emergency Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Mixed Bicuspid Aortic Valve Disease With a Horizontal Aorta: Return of Spontaneous Circulation Only After Left Ventricular Unloading.
authorString: Simone T, Cattaneo G, Testa L, Bedogni F, Cannone G.
abstractText: A 74-year-old man with mixed bicuspid aortic valve disease, combining severe calcific stenosis with severe regurgitation, and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 26% presented in normotensive cardiogenic shock with anuria and an arterial lactate of 12 mmol/L. Computed tomography showed a fibrocalcific left-right raphe and an aortic angulation of 66 degrees. Emergency transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve implantation was undertaken. The delivery system could not be advanced across the aortic arch despite escalation of guidewire support, and ventricular fibrillation degenerated into pulseless electrical activity refractory to resuscitation. Peripheral venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation was established, after which a 29 mm self-expanding prosthesis was implanted with an acceptable haemodynamic result and patent coronary ostia. Pulseless electrical activity nonetheless persisted. Return of spontaneous circulation followed only after a microaxial pump was advanced retrogradely across the freshly deployed prosthesis under fluoroscopic guidance alone, establishing an ECMELLA configuration. The patient died of multiorgan failure two days later. This sequence identifies continued left ventricular loading, rather than any residual valve lesion, as the reason resuscitation failed, and argues for anticipating unloading when extracorporeal support is instituted across a valve just rendered competent in a severely dysfunctional ventricle. The outcome appeared determined by end-organ injury already established before intervention.

title: Chronic thoracic aortitis versus primary medial degeneration in ascending aorta: a digital morphometric analysis of aortic layers remodelling.
authorString: Vasova B, Sokolova T, Hrnciarova L, Karalko M, Stejskal V.

journal.title: Cardiovascular pathology : the official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology

abstractText:
Introduction

Chronic aortitis (CA) represents a diverse group of inflammatory conditions often diagnosed incidentally in ascending aorta biopsies. While the 2015 and 2016 Consensus Statements on the surgical pathology of the aorta provide standardised histological classifications, data quantifying structural remodelling within individual aortic layers remain limited. Furthermore, distinguishing CA from primary non-inflammatory medial degeneration (MD) can be challenging, particularly when inflammation is sparse or burnt out, and secondary degenerative changes predominate. We aimed to compare morphological changes in CA and MD aneurysms and apply digital image analysis to quantify aortic wall layers.

Methods

Retrospective histological analysis was performed on 63 ascending aortic specimens: CA (n=21), MD (n=21), and autopsy controls (n=21). Digitised elastic-stained sections were analysed using QuPath software to measure the thickness and cross-sectional area of the intima (I), media (M), and adventitia (A). Overall MD scores (i.e., summaries of each MD grade component) were evaluated. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis based on binary logistic regression models.

Results

CA demonstrated a profound architectural shift, characterised by medial thinning alongside marked intimal and adventitial expansion, resulting in significantly lower M/(I+A) thickness and area ratios compared with MD and controls (p <0.001). CA specimens also exhibited the most severe secondary degenerative changes, with significantly higher overall MD scores (median: 15 vs. 8; p < 0.001). ROC curve analysis revealed diagnostic utility of both the M/(I+A) thickness ratio (AUC = 0.964) and the M/(I+A) area ratio (AUC = 0.955) for identifying CA. A multivariable model combining the overall MD score with the M/(I+A) thickness ratio achieved an AUC of 0.971 (accuracy 88.1%), whereas combining it with the M/(I+A) area ratio yielded an AUC of 0.968 (accuracy 90.5%).

Conclusion

Digital morphometric analysis provides a reproducible and feasible method for quantifying structural remodelling in chronic aortitis. Changes in the proportions of the aortic layers, specifically intimal and adventitial expansion combined with medial thinning and severe secondary medial degeneration, can facilitate accurate differentiation of aortic wall pathologies, particularly in cases with sparse inflammation.

title: Computational Modeling Reduces Leaflet Modification Rates in Valve-In-Valve and Redo Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
authorString: Valle NJ, Saleh OA, Jafar O, Munoz-Moreno J, Harper AM, Martin CM, Dolsen JD, Benza RL, Kemp CD, Parikh PK, Mahoney PD, Talreja DR, Peterson BD, Cohen JA, Summers MR.
abstractText:
Background

Coronary obstruction (CO) complicates valve-in-valve (ViV) and redo transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) at higher rates than native TAVR. Leaflet modification mitigates this risk but increases procedural burden. Traditional computed tomography angiography (CTA)-based risk stratification relies on static parameters that may overestimate risk; computational predictive modeling (CPM) uses patient-specific data to refine risk assessment.

Objectives

The study aims to characterize leaflet modification rates in conventional ViV TAVR and redo-TAVR and evaluate the impact of CPM preprocedural planning augmentation on leaflet modification rates.

Methods

A total of 157 consecutive ViV TAVR or redo-TAVR patients treated from 2022 to 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. CO risk status was derived from traditional CTA parameters. Leaflet modification rates among CTA high-risk subgroups (non-CPM, n = 62; and CPM, n = 29) were compared using Boschloo's one-sided exact test. CPM risk-reclassification patterns were studied using counterfactual binomial analysis.

Results

Leaflet modification occurred in 26.3% of ViV TAVR and 24.1% of redo-TAVR procedures that used only conventional CTA-based planning methods. Among patients deemed high risk for CO by conventional methods, leaflet modification was significantly lower in the CPM-augmented subgroup vs that in the non-CPM subgroup (24.1% vs 46.8%; OR: 2.76; 95% CI: 1.03-7.40; P = 0.021). CPM-augmented planning reclassified 82.8% of patients to low-risk status, and 79.2% of reclassified patients were managed without leaflet modification. No COs occurred during the study period.

Conclusions

Among ViV TAVR and redo-TAVR patients at high risk of CO based on conventional CTA-based planning, the use of CPM to augment standard risk assessment was associated with a significant reduction in leaflet modification procedures.

title: Lens dislocation, OCTA, and archived FBN1 reports: An exploratory study.
authorString: Çevik MÖ, Simsek M, Cevik SG, Perente I.
abstractText:
Purpose

Lens dislocation (ectopia lentis) is a recognized anterior-segment manifestation of fibrillinopathy. This exploratory phenotype-first study compared macular optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) parameters between participants with and without documented lens dislocation and descriptively reviewed available archived clinical FBN1 reports.

Methods

This retrospective, availability-based study included 16 participants classified by verified current or historical lens-dislocation status. Participant-level superficial capillary plexus (SCP) vessel density was calculated by averaging valid bilateral measurements or using the single valid eye. Five OCTA endpoints were compared using two-sided Mann-Whitney U tests; Benjamini-Hochberg q values were used as a multiplicity sensitivity analysis. Seven archived clinical FBN1 reports from lens-dislocation-positive (LD+) participants were summarized without variant reclassification. No genotype-OCTA association was assessed.

Results

The cohort comprised 7 LD+ and 9 lens-dislocation-negative (LD-) participants; 15 participants (6 LD+ and 9 LD-) contributed quantitative OCTA data. Foveal SCP vessel density was lower in LD+ participants (median [IQR], 19.38% [18.68-20.04] vs 30.20% [29.20-31.85]; p = 0.036), but the finding was not retained after multiplicity sensitivity analysis (q = 0.180). Whole-image, parafoveal, and perifoveal vessel-density comparisons were not significant (p = 0.328, 0.272, and 0.238; q = 0.410 each), and OD-only foveal avascular zone area did not differ (n = 14; p = 0.606; q = 0.606). Six of seven archived reports documented an FBN1 variant; one was negative within its assay scope.

Conclusions

The unadjusted foveal signal was not robust to multiplicity analysis, and other OCTA endpoints did not differ significantly. Marked between-group differences in spherical equivalent and axial length, the small sample, and heterogeneous routine-care genetic reports limit interpretation. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish OCTA as a diagnostic or prognostic test or demonstrate an individual-level genotype-OCTA association.

title: Exercise Capacity, Muscle Mass, and Quality of Life in Pediatric Patients with Fontan Circulation.
authorString: Jose JT, Bernstein D, Palaniappan L, Leonard MB, Long J, Lui M, Dehoney J, Olson I, Myers J, Schnieder L, Tierney S.
abstractText:
Objective

To examine how measures of cardiac, vascular, and muscle health relate to Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory TM (PedsQL) score in a cohort of children and adolescents with Fontan circulation.

Study design

We performed a cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from children and adolescents (8-19 years) with Fontan circulation enrolled in a prospective study. Participants underwent a series of tests, including a cardiopulmonary exercise test, dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry measures of appendicular lean mass index (ALMI, kg/m2), leg dynamometry, and the 23-item PedsQL. The survey quantifies Physical, Emotional, Social, and School functioning into 1 total score and 2 summary scores for physical and psychosocial health.

Results

135 patients (median age 12.7 [IQR 10.2, 15.6] years) completed the baseline visit. Median time from Fontan operation was 8.7 years [IQR 5.9, 12.0]. Peak VO2 was 1309 [IQR 1070, 1670] mL/min, and indexed peak VO2 was 31.1 [IQR 25.2, 36.1] mL/kg/min. Physical and Psychosocial PedsQL summary scores were 78.1 [IQR 67.2,90.6] and 76.7 [IQR 63.3, 90], respectively, and the total score was 76.1 [IQR 65.2, 88.0]. Absolute peak VO2 was weakly correlated with PedsQL Physical Summary Score (ρ=0.21, P=0.015), but indexed peak VO2, % predicted peak VO2, and Fontan-specific peak VO2 z-score were not ALMI z-score was -0.84 [IQR -1.56, -0.14] and positively correlated with total PedsQL score (ρ=0.28, P=0.001) and the Physical Functioning domain (ρ=0.30, P<0.001).

Conclusions

Skeletal muscle mass was associated with quality of life in children with Fontan circulation. The association between VO2 and physical function was attenuated with body-size normalization.

title: Life's Essential 8 Cardiovascular Health Characteristics in Children and Adolescents with Congenital Heart Disease.
authorString: Zielonka B, Chiert H, DrPh YH, Gauvreau K, de Ferranti SD.
abstractText:
Objective

To describe the cardiovascular health (CVH) characteristics in children and adolescents with congenital heart disease (CHD) using a modified version of the American Heart Association (AHA) Life's Essential 8 criteria and examine differences in CVH by CHD complexity.

Study design

This single-center, cross-sectional study included youth 8-19 years old with CHD and an available total cholesterol within 3 years of a clinic visit. Patients were categorized into simple, moderate, or complex anatomic groups according to AHA anatomic classification guidelines for CHD. Modified CVH scores were calculated using 3 to 5 CVH metrics: nicotine exposure, body mass index (BMI), blood lipids, blood glucose, and blood pressure. The association between anatomic complexity and CVH was assessed using multivariable linear regression.

Results

The study cohort included 629 patients. Modified CVH scores were low or moderate in 46.1% of patients, with prevalent low or moderate scores in blood lipids (49.4%), blood pressure (42.4%), and BMI (31.9%). Median CVH scores differed across anatomic groups (simple 83 vs moderate 78 vs complex 84, P=0.01). Complex CHD was associated with a higher (more favorable) modified CVH score and blood pressure score than moderate CHD and a higher blood lipids score than simple and moderate CHD.

Conclusions

Despite vulnerable cardiac anatomy, almost half of youth with CHD had suboptimal CVH, with prevalent deficits in blood lipids, blood pressure, and BMI. Complex CHD anatomy was associated with a more favorable CVH profile. These findings highlight the need to incorporate health screening and promotion into the routine care of the pediatric CHD population.

title: Distal-to-Proximal Conduction System Ablation as a Bailout Strategy in Refractory Multi-Exit Purkinje-Related Premature Ventricular Contractions and Ventricular Fibrillation.
authorString: Khalaph M, Didenko M, Darma A, El-Shirbiny H, Trajkovska N, El Hamriti M, Fink T, Sciacca V, Guckel D, Lucas P, Braun M, Akkaya E, Jurisic S, Moersdorf M, Sohns C, Sommer P, Imnadze G.
abstractText:
Background

Ablation of premature ventricular contractions (PVCs) originating from the Purkinje network-particularly those with multiple exit sites and morphologies-poses a significant clinical challenge. In refractory cases where conventional ablation fails, proximal conduction system ablation may represent a viable alternative strategy.

Objective

to evaluate the safety and efficacy of proximal conduction system ablation in patients with refractory multi-exit Purkinje PVCs with diverse morphologies.

Methods

This retrospective cohort included consecutive patients with drug-refractory, symptomatic Purkinje PVCs who underwent proximal conduction system ablation. Multiple exit sites and morphologies were observed during mapping and ablation, indicating complex activation within the Purkinje network.

Results

Among the 22 patients included, 14 (63.6%) had PVC-triggered ventricular fibrillation. Acute elimination of the PVC by distal-to-proximal conduction system ablation achieved in 21 patients (95.5%), while one procedure (4.5%) was discontinued at the patient's request due to the anticipated risk of conduction system injury. The initial site of earliest activation arose from the posterior fascicle in 63.6% (n=14), the septal fascicle in 22.7% (n=5) and the anterior fascicle in 13.6% (n=3). During ablation, all patients demonstrated a shift in the site of earliest activation. Conduction disturbances occurred in 5 patients (22.7%). During a median follow-up of 32.3 months (IQR 17.5-54.5), one patient (4.5%) experienced PVC recurrence requiring repeat ablation; however, no patient experienced recurrent ventricular fibrillation.

Conclusion

Distal-to-proximal conduction system ablation can be an effective bailout strategy for patients with refractory multi-exit fascicular/Purkinje-related PVCs and recurrent VF. Larger prospective studies are needed to confirm its long-term safety and efficacy.

title: Leadless Atrial Pacing Targeting Bachmann Bundle for Atrial Resynchronization: A Single Center Registry.
authorString: Hollis Z, Mehta A, Yang E, Alkalbani M, Atwater B.
abstractText:
Background

Interatrial conduction delay (IACD) resulting from fibrosis or functional block in Bachmann bundle (BB) occurs often in patients with sinus node dysfunction (SND) and increases the risk of atrial fibrillation (AF). Pacing the BB in patients with SND may reduce AF burden. Little is known of the feasibility and effectiveness of BB leadless atrial pacemaker (BBLAP) implantation.

Objective

To determine if BBLAP is safe, feasible and improves IACD.

Methods

This registry prospectively enrolled 21 consecutive adults with baseline P wave duration (PWD) >120ms undergoing BBLAP for SND. Fluoroscopy, intracardiac echocardiography and left atrial conduction time (LACT) measurements from a decapolar coronary sinus (CS) catheter were used to facilitate implantation. BBLAP implant success was defined as improved PWD, P wave morphology, and LACT. Baseline and BBLAP LACT and PWD, axis, and morphology were compared.

Results

Of the 21 patients enrolled, 17 had successful BBLAP (81%). Among those with successful BBLAP, baseline PWD was 150 (±21) ms, BBLAP PWD was 113 (±23) ms, a reduction of 37 (±13) ms, p < 0.001. BBLAP P wave axis was inferiorly directed in all cases. 8/8 patients with a negative terminal P wave in the inferior leads at baseline had correction with BBLAP. LACT decreased from 113 (±35) ms to 78 (±33) ms, mean difference 35 (±15) ms, p <0.001, with BBLAP. 13/17 patients demonstrated a shift in CS activation from proximal-distal activation to mid- or distal-proximal activation during BBLAP. In all cases there were no complications.

Conclusion

The BBLAP implant technique presented in this registry is feasible and reduced IACD. Further study on the effect of BBLAP on AF burden is needed.
