title: Efficacy and Safety of Argatroban as an Adjunct to Antiplatelet Therapy in Ischemic Stroke: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
authorString: Fatima ST, Raza A, Javed A, Ijaz S, Noor M, Uzair SD, Malik AR, Mustafa RA, Daim SUR.
abstractText:
Introduction

Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is a life-threatening condition. Argatroban can limit thrombus progression and improve AIS's functional outcomes. This study assessed the efficacy and safety of argatroban in combination with antiplatelet therapy compared to control.

Methods

PubMed and Scopus were searched. Primary outcomes were Modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 0-2 and composite hemorrhage; secondary outcomes included mRS (0-1), early neurological deterioration (END), change in National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score, mortality, intracranial and organ hemorrhage. A random-effects model was used, with risk ratios (RRs) reported for binary outcomes, while mean differences (MDs) for continuous outcomes at 95% confidence intervals (CI) and a p-value of 0.05.

Results

17 studies were included with a total of 51,703 and 18,759 patients in the argatroban and control group, respectively. The primary outcomes, mRS (0-2), and composite hemorrhage showed no significant difference between argatroban and control (RR: 1.03, CI: 0.97-1.10, p = 0.26 and RR: 1.10, CI: 0.98-1.23, p = 0.11, respectively). However, argatroban significantly reduced END (RR: 0.48, CI: 0.30-0.75, p < 0.05) and favored mRS (0-1) with RR:1.22 (CI: 1.01-1.48, p = 0.03). The change in NIHSS score and incidence of mortality, stroke recurrence, intracranial and organ hemorrhage was comparable between the two groups. Subgroup analyses by antiplatelet drug in the intervention and comparison groups confirmed that argatroban showed the most pronounced results when combined with DAPT. While the overall pooled analysis did not demonstrate increased hemorrhagic risk, subgroup analysis restricted to randomized controlled trials revealed a significant increase in composite and intracranial hemorrhage with argatroban. GRADE assessment of RCT-derived evidence indicated very low to high certainty across all outcomes.

Conclusion

Argatroban as an adjunct to antiplatelet therapy did not significantly improve overall functional outcome (mRS 0-2) or reduce composite hemorrhage compared with antiplatelet therapy alone. However it appears safe and may reduce END significantly.

title: Association Between Intramuscular Injection Site and Ulcer Healing in Patients with Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia Treated with Recombinant Human Hepatocyte Growth Factor Naked Plasmid: A <i>Post Hoc</i> Analysis of the HOPE CLTI-2 Trial.
authorString: Wang P, Lian W, Rong Z, Li F, Liu J, Zhou J, Liu C, Di X, Ni L.
abstractText: This study was based on the multicenter, double-blind, randomized phase III HOPE CLTI-2 trial. An exploratory post hoc analysis was performed to investigate the association between intramuscular injection site and ulcer healing outcomes in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) treated with recombinant human hepatocyte growth factor (rh-HGF), and to explore factors associated with ulcer healing. The analysis included 108 patients with CLTI treated with rh-HGF, comprising 184 ischemic lower-limb ulcers. Patients were classified according to injection site into a single-segment group, with injections limited to the calf muscles, and a multi-segment group, with injections administered to both the thigh and calf muscles. Outcomes included ulcer healing rate, time to ulcer healing, ankle-brachial index (ABI), Rutherford category, Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection (WIfI) classification, and adverse clinical events. At the study endpoint, the unadjusted ulcer healing rate was significantly higher in the single-segment group than in the multi-segment group (75.0% vs. 57.1%, p = 0.014), and the observed time to ulcer healing was shorter (153.00 [91.00-184.00] days vs. 181.00 [94.00-191.00] days, p = 0.022). No significant between-group differences were observed in changes in ABI (p = 0.290) or in WIfI classification (p = 0.407). However, the distribution of Rutherford categories at study endpoint favored the single-segment group (p = 0.016). In the multivariable logistic regression analysis, baseline ulcer area (odds ratio [OR]: 0.684, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.519-0.901, p = 0.007) and male sex (OR: 3.924, 95% CI: 1.164-13.232, p = 0.028) were independently associated with ulcer healing. Although the unadjusted comparisons favored the single-segment group, injection site was not independently associated with ulcer healing after multivariable adjustment (OR: 1.560, 95% CI: 0.703-3.460, p = 0.269). Therefore, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating. Whether a more anatomically targeted rh-HGF injection strategy under a fixed-dose regimen can improve ulcer healing requires evaluation in prospectively designed studies.

title: Computed-Tomography Angiography-Based Carotid Plaque-RADS, Recurrent Vascular Events, and the Effect of Colchicine: An Imaging Substudy of the CONVINCE Randomized Trial.
authorString: Maes L, Wouters A, Peluso JP, Demeestere J, Desfontaines P, De Pauw A, Collins R, McCabe DJH, Cronin S, Williams DJ, De Raedt S, Purroy F, Vanhooren G, Pope G, Vanacker P, Cassidy T, Nerney D, Walsh C, Bos D, Kelly P, Lemmens R.
abstractText:
Background

The carotid Plaque Reporting and Data System (Plaque-RADS) provides a standardized framework for evaluating plaque morphology, but prospective validation remains limited. We investigated the association between computed tomography angiography-based Plaque-RADS categories and subsequent ischemic events in patients with noncardioembolic stroke/transient ischemic attack, from a completed clinical trial of colchicine. Second, we assessed whether the effect of colchicine differed by Plaque-RADS risk classification.

Methods

We conducted a posthoc observational cohort analysis of 517 participants in the CONVINCE trial (Colchicine for Prevention of Vascular Inflammation in Non-CardioEmbolic Stroke) from 13 European sites. Associations between Plaque-RADS and recurrent ipsilateral stroke, any stroke/transient ischemic attack, and major adverse cardiovascular events were assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. Plaque-RADS was analyzed as both dichotomized (<3 versus ≥3) and ordinal (per 1-point increase) variables. Treatment effects were assessed by Plaque-RADS classification using interaction and stratified analyses.

Results

A total of 510 patients (median age, 67.0 years; 72.2% male) with 966 internal carotid arteries were included. Among 321 internal carotid arteries ipsilateral to the index ischemic stroke, 12 recurrent ipsilateral strokes, 32 any strokes/transient ischemic attacks, and 37 major adverse cardiovascular events occurred over a median 35.7-month follow-up. Plaque-RADS ≥3 (n=140) was independently associated with recurrent ipsilateral stroke (adjusted hazard ratio, 7.80 [95% CI, 1.55-39.30]; P=0.01), any stroke/transient ischemic attack (adjusted hazard ratio, 3.94 [95% CI, 1.68-9.24]; P<0.01), and major adverse cardiovascular events (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.52 [95% CI, 1.19-5.34]; P=0.02) after adjustment for age, sex and cardiovascular risk factors. A significant interaction with colchicine treatment was observed for major adverse cardiovascular events (P=0.047), with greater benefit among patients with Plaque-RADS scores ≥3 (hazard ratio, 0.35 [95% CI, 0.15-0.82]).

Conclusions

In internal carotid arteries ipsilateral to the index ischemic stroke, computed tomography angiography-based carotid Plaque-RADS was associated with recurrent ischemic stroke and cardiovascular events. Importantly, treatment effects of colchicine varied across Plaque-RADS classification (<3 versus ≥3), suggesting that plaque vulnerability assessment may help refine patient selection for anti-inflammatory therapy beyond stenosis-based classification.

title: Heart-reactive antibody levels differentially associate with ventricular function in hereditary cardiomyopathies.
authorString: Schiffer D, Afshar B, Grosser D, Pet J, Schmidbauer L, Bauser M, Ramos G, Boivin-Jahns V, Jahns R, Frantz S, Heuschmann P, Störk S, Gerull B, Beyersdorf N, Morbach C.
abstractText:
Background

gCMP are a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. While agonistic anti-β1-adrenergic receptor antibodies (anti-β1AR-ECII) have a recognized pathogenic role in idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), the relevance of HRA in gCMP remains unclear.

Methods

One hundred gCMP patients with confirmed genetic variants in cardiomyopathy genes were compared with 100 age- and sex-matched healthy individuals. Antibody reactivities were quantified using bead-based flow cytometric assays against cardiac antigens: The second extracellular loop of the β1 adrenergic receptor (β1AR-ECII), Troponin I3 (TPI3), Tropomyosin 1 (TPM1), Myosin heavy chain 6 and 7 (MYH6, MYH7) and Myosin light chain 7 (MYL7).

Results

gCMP patients showed higher anti-TPI3 and lower anti-TPM1 antibody levels compared to controls indicating increased induction of the former and loss of the latter in gCMP patients. Age and sex influenced HRA patterns in both groups. Anti-MYH6 and anti-TPM1 antibody levels were negatively associated with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), both overall and within specific gCMP subtypes, including hypertrophic and arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy. Additionally, anti-MYH6 antibody levels were negatively associated with right ventricular function, measured by tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE).

Conclusion

Our findings stress the diagnostic potential of HRA profiling and indicate that gCMP patients might profit from therapeutic targeting of HRA.

title: Mining tailings dam failures and human health: a scoping review of environmental exposure, potentially toxic elements, and epidemiological evidence, 2015-2025.
authorString: Souza TP, Ferreira AD, Viana DG, de Sousa JES, Ferreira TO.
abstractText: Mining is essential for economic development; however, the increasing number of tailings dam failures has become a major environmental and public health concern. This review aimed to characterize mining tailings dam disasters reported worldwide between 2015 and 2025 and summarize the available evidence on their human health impacts. A scoping review was conducted using Web of Science, Scopus, MEDLINE, Google Scholar, and institutional sources institutional reports from World Information Service on Energy (WISE), United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), GRID-Arendal, and World Health Organization (WHO). Each identified disaster was individually investigated to compile information on disaster characteristics, released tailings, mineral commodities, potentially toxic elements (PTEs), and available epidemiological evidence. A total of 670 deaths and 112 injuries were reported, while approximately 75 people were reported missing. At least 728 displaced people and 55 displaced families were also reported. Gold, copper, and jade were the mineral commodities most frequently involved, while arsenic, lead, mercury, manganese, and zinc were the most frequently reported PTEs in the tailings associated with these disasters. Despite the large number of disasters, only two incidents (Mariana and Brumadinho) have been investigated in population-based studies evaluating human health following the events, revealing a major global knowledge gap.

title: Predictive and operational artificial intelligence in emergency radiology for early risk stratification in acute care settings: a scoping review.
authorString: Tovar Acosta N, Salcedo Garrido G, Urueña Ramírez JA, Hernández Rincón EH.
abstractText:
Introduction

Emergency departments face increasing overcrowding, resulting in diagnostic delays, higher mortality, and rising healthcare costs. Early risk stratification is essential to optimise clinical decision-making. Although medical imaging plays a central role in initial assessment, workload pressures and operational constraints have driven the development of artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support triage and prioritisation in emergency radiology.

Objective

To map and synthesise evidence on the applications, performance, and limitations of AI in emergency radiology for early risk stratification in acute care.

Materials and methods

A scoping review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines and Joanna Briggs Institute recommendations. The protocol was developed a priori and registered in the Open Science Framework. A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science identified studies published between 2015 and 2025 that evaluated AI applications in medical imaging in acute care settings. Evidence was synthesised using conceptual mapping and thematic analysis.

Results

Seventy-one studies were included. Computed tomography was the most frequently evaluated modality, followed by radiography and ultrasound. Major domains included neurovascular disease, acute cardiopulmonary conditions, trauma, COVID-19, and acute aortic syndromes. Studies reported high diagnostic performance and potential workflow benefits; however, evidence was predominantly retrospective and internally validated, with limited prospective evaluation, external validation, or evidence of improved patient-level outcomes.

Conclusions

AI applications in emergency radiology show promising diagnostic and workflow-support capabilities. However, current evidence largely reflects early-stage development, with limited prospective validation, scarce real-world impact assessment, and insufficient evaluation of clinically meaningful outcomes.

Key points

Question How clinically mature are AI applications designed to support early risk stratification and prioritisation in time-sensitive emergency radiology workflows? Findings Most studies report high diagnostic performance in time-sensitive conditions, yet evidence remains predominantly retrospective with limited external validation or prospective real-world implementation. Clinical relevance AI may support earlier identification and prioritisation of critical imaging findings, but routine adoption requires prospective external validation and evidence of meaningful effects on clinical decisions and patient outcomes.

title: Salvage Use of Sotatercept for Potts Shunt in Refractory Pulmonary Hypertension.
authorString: Xu Z, Zhang M, Chen Y, Yu X, Sun Y, Bai J, Xu Z, Fu L, Zhang H.
abstractText: The reverse Potts shunt (RPS) is a promising palliative intervention for pediatric patients with drug-refractory severe pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), yet it carries substantial risks of perioperative mortality and hemodynamic instability. We report two high-risk pediatric female patients who developed acute hemodynamic instability and recurrent pulmonary hypertensive crises following successful percutaneous RPS creation. Despite maximal targeted triple therapy and vasoactive support, no sustained improvement was observed. Following multidisciplinary consensus, a single salvage dose of sotatercept (0.3 mg/kg) was administered. Both patients demonstrated rapid, hemodynamic stabilization within 48 h, enabling the swift withdrawal of vasoactive support and inhaled nitric oxide within 1 week. Follow-up echocardiography revealed significant recovery of right ventricular function, and both patients were successfully weaned off treprostinil. These findings suggest that short-term perioperative sotatercept can serve as an effective acute rescue therapy to safeguard high-risk surgical interventions in critical pediatric PAH.

title: Extending the Lower Limits of Body Weight for Bi-directional Glenn Shunt in Developing Countries: Is it Feasible?
authorString: Talwar S, Das D, Bhende VV, Gohil AA, Krishnakumar M, Sharma AS.
abstractText: The bi-directional Glenn (BDG) shunt is an established stage of palliation for functionally single-ventricle congenital heart disease, but optimal timing and the influence of severe underweight remain uncertain. We report a 102-day-old male infant, born at 38 weeks' gestation and weighing 2.7 kg at surgery, with double-outlet right ventricle, difficult/non-routable intracardiac anatomy, D-malposed great arteries, and severe pulmonary stenosis who underwent a right-sided BDG with atrial septectomy and partial main pulmonary artery (PA) ligation. The infant was discharged on postoperative day 11 with an oxygen saturation of 92%. Available follow-up documentation over 18 months described a patent BDG on two-dimensional echocardiography. This single case demonstrates technical feasibility in a selected severely underweight infant; it does not establish a safe lower age or weight threshold, comparative mortality, or long-term Fontan outcome. Larger studies with complete nutritional, hemodynamic, and longitudinal follow-up data are required.

title: A complementary proteomics and cardiac magnetic resonance approach to characterize right ventricular remodeling after tetralogy of Fallot repair.
authorString: Jones AL, Edwards JJ, Fazelinia H, Frank D, Clouthier KL, Patel C, Spruce L, Ding H, Sabella J, Avitabile CM, Friedberg MK, Fogel MA, Ischiropoulos H, Reddy S, Mercer-Rosa L.
abstractText:
Background

Patients with repaired tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) can develop right ventricular (RV) dilation and failure. We sought to utilize an untargeted serum proteomics approach to characterize the proteome signature associated with RV dilation in repaired TOF to improve the understanding of mechanistic drivers of RV remodeling.

Methods

Patients with repaired TOF undergoing cardiac magnetic resonance imaging were recruited. Groups were based on indexed RV end-diastolic volume (RVEDVi). Serum proteomics identified differentially abundant proteins (p value < 0.05), and pathway enrichment identified functional pathways.

Results

Fourteen TOF adolescents (median age 16 years; IQR 15, 18) were divided into Group 1 (n = 9; median RVEDVi 146 ml/m2; IQR 139, 164) and Group 2 (n = 5; median RVEDVi 114 ml/m2; IQR 104, 130). Group 1 had a higher indexed RV stroke volume (85 ml/m2 vs. 59 ml/m2, p = 0.023) with a similar RV ejection fraction. Group 1 had altered regulation of genes in multiple pathways, including glucose and fatty acid metabolism and antioxidant response.

Conclusion

Patients with repaired TOF and moderate-severe RV dilation have a distinct serum proteomic profile despite preserved ejection fraction, which may reflect alterations in fuel sources and oxidative stress. These hypothesis-generating findings are a first step in the integration of proteomics into clinical management.

Impact

An untargeted serum proteomics approach to identifying altered protein profiles associated with CMR-defined RV dilation is a novel approach to characterizing right ventricular remodeling after tetralogy of Fallot repair. RV dilation after repair of tetralogy of Fallot is associated with a specific proteomic profile suggesting adaptive and maladaptive remodeling. Identification of dysregulated proteins associated with RV remodeling provides insight into the mechanisms leading to ventricular failure after tetralogy of Fallot repair. With additional data from future larger studies, serum proteomics evaluation may assist in prognostication and clinical decision making in patients after tetralogy of Fallot repair.

title: Congenital heart disease confers gestational age-dependent risks of mortality and morbidity in preterm infants.
authorString: Chaudhry PM, Sweeney N, Zaniletti I, Martin LJ, Edwards EM, Gowda SH, Padula M, Murthy K, Grover TR, Morton SU, DiGeronimo R, Shepherd JL, Levy PT, Ball MK, Children’s Hospital Neonatal Consortium Cardiac Focus Group.

journal.title: Journal of perinatology : official journal of the California Perinatal Association

abstractText:
Objective

To determine the incremental risks of mortality and major neonatal morbidities associated with congenital heart disease (CHD) beyond prematurity alone.

Study design

Secondary analysis of two North American neonatal registries (2010-2022) including infants <35 weeks' gestation: 11,221 with CHD from the Children's Hospitals Neonatal Consortium and 720,846 without CHD from the Vermont Oxford Network. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes were major neonatal morbidities.

Results

Preterm infants with CHD had fourfold higher odds of in-hospital mortality (OR 4.0, 95% CI 3.76-4.21). Mortality was similar at ≤26 weeks' gestation, but the relative impact of CHD increased with advancing gestational age. CHD was associated with significantly increased risks of severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia, intraventricular hemorrhage, and necrotizing enterocolitis.

Conclusion

The impact of CHD on mortality is gestational age dependent, with prematurity predominating at the lowest gestational ages and CHD increasingly driving mortality as gestational maturity improves.

title: CCR5, CD163, CSF1R, and FCGR3A as Candidate Biomarkers Associated With Mitophagy in Atherosclerosis.
authorString: Fu J, Dong Y.
abstractText: Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammatory disease, and the role of mitophagy in its pathogenesis remains unclear. To address this, this study integrated atherosclerosis-related transcriptome data and single-cell sequencing data from the GEO database, obtained mitophagy-related genes from MSigDB, and assessed mitophagy activity via GSEA and ssGSEA; WGCNA was used to screen disease- and mitophagy-associated module genes, and their intersection with differentially expressed genes yielded 286 candidate genes. A protein-protein interaction (PPI) network and cytoHubba algorithms were subsequently used to prioritize key genes, and dual machine learning algorithms (LASSO regression and SVM-RFE) to screen potential biomarkers, which were designated as CCR5, CD163, CSF1R, and FCGR3A. The expression patterns of all four candidates were further assessed in the independent GSE43292 dataset and were concordant with those observed in the discovery dataset. GSEA of samples stratified by candidate-gene expression identified enrichment of gene sets related to myogenesis, allograft rejection, and inflammatory responses; candidate drug-target associations were predicted using DSigDB, and exploratory AutoDock analysis suggested a feasible interaction between sunitinib and CSF1R. Additionally, exploratory single-cell analysis of three atherosclerosis patients identified seven major cell populations, with CD163, CSF1R, and FCGR3A showing macrophage-enriched expression within this dataset. Collectively, this study provides hypothesis-generating evidence for an association between mitophagy-related transcriptional patterns and atherosclerosis. Four candidate biomarkers (CCR5, CD163, CSF1R, and FCGR3A) were prioritized, and a potential CSF1R-sunitinib interaction was proposed for future experimental validation.

title: Beyond Pigmentation: Interplay of Metabolic Profile, Carotid Intima-Media Thickness, and Fatty Liver in Vitiligo: An Age- and Sex-Matched Case-Control Study.
authorString: Mozafar M, Bigdeli Y, Looha MA, Samiee R, Shakoei S, Etesami I, Aryanian Z, Khorasanizadeh F, Hatami P.
abstractText:
Background and aims

Vitiligo shares inflammatory and metabolic pathways with cardiovascular and hepatic steatosis. Carotid intima-media thickness (IMT) is an established marker of early subclinical atherosclerosis, whereas non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) reflects hepatic involvement in chronic inflammatory and metabolic dysregulation. This study aimed to evaluate subclinical vascular and hepatic changes in patients with vitiligo and to explore their associations with disease characteristics and metabolic parameters.

Methods

In this age- and sex-matched case-control study, adults with mild vitiligo (Vitiligo Area Severity Index [VASI] < 5%) and no metabolic syndrome were compared with healthy controls. Participants underwent carotid duplex ultrasonography to assess common carotid IMT and atherosclerotic plaques, liver ultrasonography for steatosis grading, and laboratory testing, including lipid profile (total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein [LDL], high-density lipoprotein [HDL], and triglycerides [TG]), fasting blood glucose (FBS), and body mass index (BMI). Disease duration and VASI score were also assessed.

Results

A total of 46 participants (23 patients with vitiligo and 23 healthy controls) completed all assessments. Common carotid IMT measurements and liver ultrasound findings were comparable between groups. However, abnormal HDL levels were more frequent among patients with vitiligo (69.6% vs. 39.1%, p = 0.03). Greater disease severity, measured by VASI score, and higher BMI were independently associated with increased right carotid IMT (p = 0.01, 0.02, respectively). Exploratory interaction analyses demonstrated significant sex-dependent associations of HDL, triglycerides, and fatty liver status with carotid IMT. Post hoc analyses identified higher carotid IMT among male patients with abnormal HDL.

Conclusion

Selected subgroups of patients with vitiligo, particularly men with HDL metabolic abnormalities, may exhibit differences in subclinical carotid atherosclerosis. Disease severity and BMI may also contribute to the vascular risk. Although exploratory, these findings warrant further investigation of cardiovascular and hepatic risk profiles in selected patients with vitiligo.

title: Associations of the Baseline Level and Change in Triglyceride Glucose-Body Roundness Index With Cardiovascular Diseases: Two Large Prospective Cohorts in Europe and Asia.
authorString: Han WY, Li YQ, Yang PN, Jia YM, Sun LL, Wang RR, Shi MY, Zheng XW, Zhang YH, Zhu ZB.

journal.title: The Kaohsiung journal of medical sciences

abstractText: The aim of this study was to investigate the association of baseline and changes of TyG-BRI with incident CVD based on the UK Biobank and China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). A total of 418,510 and 7923 individuals from the UK Biobank and CHARLS were included in Analysis 1 (baseline TyG-BRI with CVD risk). In Analysis 2 (change in TyG-BRI with CVD risk), a total of 11,682 and 4637 participants were included in Cox proportional hazard models. We found participants with the highest baseline TyG-BRI level were associated with increased risk of incident CVD in UK Biobank (HR = 1.45, 95% CI: 1.39-1.52) and CHARLS (HR = 1.35, 95% CI: 1.13-1.61). Multivariable-adjusted restricted cubic spline analyses presented positive linear associations between TyG-BRI and CVD risk. Compared to persistently low levels of TyG-BRI (Class 1), those with persistently high levels (Class 3: 1.23 (1.02-1.49) and 1.42 (1.11-1.55); Class 4: 1.48 (1.17-1.87) and 1.45 (1.16-2.28); Class 5: 2.58 (1.86-3.58) and 1.63 (1.16-2.28) for UK Biobank and CHARLS) in follow-up were associated with increased risks of incident CVD. In conclusion, a high baseline TyG-BRI level and different changes in TyG-BRI level are associated with increased risks of incident CVD.

title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Followed by Lung Cancer Resection in an Older Patient: A Case Report.
authorString: Khan L, Qadri SS.
abstractText: The individual incidences of lung cancer and cardiovascular disease in the elderly population mean that there is a strong likelihood of both occurring simultaneously. Common practice for severe aortic stenosis (AS) would be surgical aortic valve replacement (AVR), unless deemed high-risk for this surgical procedure. Age and lung cancer both increase a patient's surgical risk; hence, the less invasive transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) to manage valve disease ahead of lung resection for lung cancer is an acceptable alternative after assessing other factors such as procedural risk, comorbidities, and prognosis. We present the case of an 82-year-old female patient who underwent a TAVI seven months before lung resection for an incidental diagnosis of lung cancer with staging T1b N0 M0. Postoperatively, she was treated for atrial fibrillation and lung collapse, then discharged after resolution of these complications on the eighth day after surgery, and remained well at follow-up three months later. This case report explores a situation when this sequence of interventions was appropriate due to increased surgical risk in the elderly population.

title: Colchicine usage and recurrent pericarditis in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus.
authorString: Xiao T, Powell N, Trotter K, Ko K.
abstractText: ObjectivePericarditis is a common and recurring manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). While guidelines for the management of SLE include the use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), colchicine, and glucocorticoids, the evidence for various treatments in SLE is limited. Evidence for the usage of colchicine for pericarditis in patients with SLE exists primarily in case reports and case series. The purpose of this study was to investigate colchicine usage and rates of recurrent pericarditis among patients with SLE.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included patients with SLE treated at a tertiary care center between 2015 and 2025. Patients were included if they presented to the hospital with pericarditis based on the 2025 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) Guidelines and had follow-up for at least 1 year. Based on the ESC guidelines, recurrent pericarditis was defined as new symptoms or disease activity after clinical remission and was captured within 1 year of the initial presentation.ResultsOf the 55 patients included in the study, 47.3% received colchicine, 52.7% received NSAIDs and 56.4% received glucocorticoids. Recurrent pericarditis occurred in 45.5% of patients. In univariate analyses, age less than 40 years at first presentation of pericarditis was significantly associated with recurrent pericarditis as was treatment with an initiation or increase of glucocorticoids. Treatment with colchicine trended toward reduced recurrence, but the result was not statistically significant. In multivariate logistic regression including age, treatment with colchicine, and treatment with glucocorticoids, only treatment with glucocorticoids was significantly associated with recurrent pericarditis (odds ratio 4.31; 95% confidence interval 1.12-16.55).ConclusionsIn this study, recurrent pericarditis was common among patients with SLE and was associated with treatment with glucocorticoids. Colchicine was associated with a trend toward decreased recurrence rates, but this was not statistically significant. Given high recurrence rates among patients treated with steroids, additional studies are needed on non-steroidal therapies for pericarditis in SLE, including further research on colchicine.

title: Aortic morphology and fenestration-related leak in fenestrated frozen elephant trunk: A cohort study.
authorString: Ikebata K, Koizumi K, Hashimoto T, Kaneyama H, Hashizume K, Shimizu H.
abstractText:
Objectives

Objective anatomical criteria for selective fixation of the fenestration after fenestrated frozen elephant trunk (FET) are lacking. We examined the association between preoperative aortic morphology and fenestration-related leak.

Methods

We retrospectively analysed 44 consecutive patients with aortic dissection who underwent fenestrated FET during total arch replacement between 2021 and 2025. True aneurysms were excluded. Preoperative computed tomography (CT) was used to assess aortic short-axis diameter and true lumen (TL) morphology at three levels spanning the left subclavian artery origin. The outcome was fenestration-related leak, defined as persistent perigraft flow on the first postoperative contrast-enhanced CT scan before discharge. Comparisons used exact tests with Firth penalized logistic regression for adjusted associations.

Results

Leak occurred in 12 patients (27.3%): 3 of 26 (11.5%) with fixation and 9 of 18 (50.0%) without (P = 0.007). Aortic diameter was larger in patients with leak (34.5 vs 29.9 mm; P = 0.002; area under the curve 0.80, 95% CI 0.63-0.97), and leak incidence rose across diameter strata (12.5%, 57.1%, 80.0%; exact trend P = 0.001). Flat TL morphology was more frequent with leak (P = 0.025); TL position was not associated. Diameter remained associated after penalized adjustment (odds ratio 1.29 per mm; P = 0.001); fixation was independently protective (odds ratio, 0.07; P = 0.002).

Conclusions

Fenestration-related leak was associated with larger preoperative aortic diameter and flat TL morphology, most evidently above 36 mm. Because fixation was chosen intraoperatively and few events occurred, these findings are exploratory and require prospective validation before they can be used to guide selective fixation.

title: Neonatal brain network integration trajectories predict neurodevelopment in congenital heart disease.
authorString: Harasymiw L, Kuang A, Xu D, Scheffler A, George E, Peyvandi S, McQuillen P.
abstractText:
Background

Infants with critical congenital heart disease (CHD) are at high risk for abnormal brain development and later neurodevelopmental impairment. We hypothesized that the trajectory of perioperative whole-brain network development would predict neurodevelopmental outcomes in early childhood.

Methods

This prospective longitudinal cohort of neonates with critical CHD (n = 97) underwent preoperative and/or postoperative brain MRI with diffusion imaging. Whole-brain network measures were derived from structural connectomes from 80 infants, and 50 had neurodevelopment assessed at 1-4 years using the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development.

Results

White matter injury was associated with a slower perioperative increase in global efficiency (p = 0.013), a measure of network integration, whereas cardiac physiology was not associated with network development. Infants with greater perioperative increases in global efficiency had higher cognitive (p = 0.001), language (p < 0.001), and motor (p = 0.008) scores. For each 1-standard deviation increase in the trajectory of global efficiency, cognitive scores increased by 8.2 points (95% CI: 3.64-12.78), independent of brain injury and socioeconomic factors.

Conclusion

In infants with critical CHD, longitudinal whole-brain network development was associated with neurodevelopment across multiple domains. Early network development may serve as a biomarker of neurodevelopmental risk and resilience in this population.

Impact

In infants with critical congenital heart disease, perioperative increase in whole-brain network integration was associated with cognitive, language, and motor outcomes in early childhood. White matter injury was associated with a slower increase in network integration, whereas cardiac physiology subtype was not associated with network development. This study extends prior work by showing that a longitudinal measure of neonatal whole-brain network development, rather than a single imaging timepoint, predicts neurodevelopment across multiple domains. These findings identify early network development as a potential biomarker of neurodevelopmental risk and resilience, and support future risk-stratification and intervention studies in this population.

title: Fetal brain volumes in complete vascular ring: A cross-sectional MRI study.
authorString: Ren JY, Chen CA, Zhu M, Zhang X, Li Y, Dong SZ.
abstractText:
Background

The association between complete vascular ring (CVR) and prenatal brain development remains poorly characterized.

Objective

To compare global and regional fetal brain volumes between fetuses with CVR and controls, accounting for gestational age (GA), fetal sex, and estimated fetal weight.

Methods

In this retrospective single-center study, 70 prenatally diagnosed CVR fetuses and 200 GA-matched controls with normal brain anatomy (22-37 weeks) underwent 1.5-T fetal MRI. Motion-corrected three-dimensional brain reconstructions were generated by slice-to-volume registration, and 19 regions were automatically segmented using a deep-learning pipeline. Linear regression included continuous GA, group, their interaction, fetal sex, and estimated fetal weight. Regional-to-intracranial volume ratios and sensitivity analyses incorporating maternal body mass index were evaluated. Multiple comparisons were controlled using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure.

Results

At the 28-week reference age, adjusted supratentorial brain, cortical gray matter, white matter, thalamic, lentiform nucleus, brainstem, and lateral ventricular volumes were smaller in the CVR group (all false-discovery-rate-adjusted P < 0.05). Intracranial volume did not differ significantly. Thalamic, lentiform nucleus, brainstem, and lateral ventricular proportions were also smaller. No group-by-GA interaction survived correction in the primary model.

Conclusions

CVR was associated with differences in selected fetal brain volumes, including regional differences relative to intracranial volume. Larger longitudinal studies with postnatal follow-up are needed.

title: ACR lung-RADS: updates and future directions.
authorString: Petranović M, Prosper AE, Hunsaker AR, Lam S, Christensen JD.

journal.title: Cancer imaging : the official publication of the International Cancer Imaging Society

abstractText: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and low-dose CT (LDCT) screening has been shown to significantly reduce lung cancer deaths in high-risk populations. The American College of Radiology (ACR) introduced the Lung CT Screening Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) in 2014 to standardize the reporting and management of screen-detected pulmonary nodules. Since its inception, Lung-RADS has undergone iterative updates reflecting advances in evidence, clinical practice, and the expanding scope of lung cancer screening. This review summarizes the major updates to Lung-RADS, highlights areas of active discussion within the Lung-RADS Committee, and outlines future research directions. Key topics include the ongoing evaluation of volumetric versus diameter-based nodule measurement, the management of subsolid nodules and the balance between surveillance and intervention, the implementation of Category 0 for infectious or inflammatory findings, clarification of juxtapleural nodule classification, the approach to incidental findings, and the development of a Lung-RADS Atlas. Future directions address the integration of risk-based and category-based assessment approaches, the role of artificial intelligence and deep learning in nodule stratification, the potential incorporation of incidental nodules into Lung-RADS, and the prospect of international harmonization for lung cancer screening reporting and management. Lung-RADS has become an essential reporting and quality tool for lung cancer screening in the United States and increasingly worldwide. Continued refinement, guided by emerging evidence, multidisciplinary collaboration, and technological innovation, will be critical to advancing precision screening strategies and reducing the global burden of lung cancer.Clinical trial numberNot applicable.

title: High-intensity interval training and moderate-intensity continuous training versus usual care in adults with familial hypercholesterolaemia: protocol for the UPPA-FH three-arm randomised trial.
authorString: Vargas-Hitos JA, González-Bustos P, Martín-Jáimez MJ, Orellana-Jaén J, Diaz-Chamorro A, Sánchez-Checa B, Ortiz-Parra A, Quesada-Jiménez L, García-Mateo P, Martínez-Rosales E, Garcia-Sanchez C, Baena-Raya A, Hernandez-Martinez A, Sánchez-Sánchez R, Bellón-Guardia ME, García-Rivero Y, Román-Muñoz A, Contreras-Rodríguez Á, Lainez Ramos-Bossini AJ, López-Milena G, Rivera-López R, Peñafiel Burkhardt R, López-Espinosa V, Del Señor López Vélez M, Rodríguez-Alemán F, Blanco-Ramos J, Aomar-Millán IF, Montes-Romero JA, Fernández-Almira ML, Sánchez-López P, Romacho T, Abreu AC, Fernández I, Jaén-Águila F, Mediavilla-García JD, Navarrete-Navarrete N, Christensen R, Gavilán-Carrera B, Soriano-Maldonado A.

title: Dietary context and ethanol-related injury in preclinical models: A contemporary systematic review of predominantly obesogenic diets and liver outcomes.
authorString: Agbonifo WO, Chimezie J, Amoo ZA, Chukwukaeme C, Francis HO, Awoleye MO, Adedeji TG.
abstractText: Diet composition is an important food-derived exposure that may influence alcohol-related tissue injury. However, evidence on how specific dietary contexts modify ethanol-induced injury and its underlying biological mechanisms in controlled preclinical models remains fragmented. This systematic review examined whether defined dietary patterns modify ethanol-related injury in controlled mammalian studies. Following PRISMA 2020, PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched for studies published from January 2021 to January 15, 2026. Eligible studies were controlled in vivo mammalian experiments comparing ethanol exposure under defined dietary patterns. Evidence was narratively synthesized by diet type, organ system, and mechanism; random-effects meta-analyses and prespecified interaction analyses were conducted when sufficiently comparable data were available. Twenty-seven studies met the inclusion criteria (24 mouse and three rat studies); 18 used male-only animals, most examined high-fat or Western-type diets, and liver outcomes predominated. Evidence for non-obesogenic diets was limited to one ketogenic-diet study. In acute high-fat-diet models, adding ethanol increased serum ALT (SMD 2.31, 95% CI 1.46-3.16), AST (SMD 1.18, 95% CI 0.54-1.81), and hepatic triglycerides (SMD 2.06, 95% CI 0.96-3.17). Acute interaction analysis identified dietary effect modification only for ALT (MD 74.56, 95% CI 59.03-90.10), while chronic analyses showed a negative interaction for hepatic triglycerides (MD -0.048, 95% CI -0.092 to -0.004; P = 0.03). Extrahepatic, microbiome, and multi-omics findings were sparse and heterogeneous. High-fat and Western-type diets generally exacerbated ethanol-induced hepatic injury, whereas evidence for other dietary patterns remains limited.

title: Co-occurrence of aortic dissection and polycystic kidney disease: a case report.
authorString: Raj G, Westaby J, Sheppard MN.
abstractText:
Background

Aortic dissection is a rare and often fatal condition which arises when there is aortic wall weakening. Multiple risk factors could lead to this condition, including hypertension, atherosclerosis, connective tissue diseases such as Marfan's, Ehlers-Danlos and Loeys Dietz syndromes, as well as smoking, cocaine usage, bicuspid aortic valve, pregnancy and trauma. Polycystic kidney disease (PKD) is a rare condition characterized by the development of multiple renal cysts, which is caused by genetic abnormalities leading to autosomal dominant or autosomal recessive inheritance. However, the presentation of both pathologies simultaneously is rare and has been infrequently reported.

Case presentation

We report a death attributed to the co-occurrence of both conditions, involving a 19-year-old Caucasian male with no known past medical history, who collapsed during sexual intercourse. Post-mortem examination revealed hemopericardium with an aortic dissection, which was associated with PKD. The heart and the great vessels were sent to the author's place of practice for a detailed cardiovascular pathology examination.

Conclusion

This case is a reminder to all forensic and clinical pathologists that an extremely uncommon manifestation can occur; therefore, a meticulous approach should always be adopted before corroborating a cause of death, especially in young individuals. The relationship between both conditions in this case remains uncertain; however, PKD may represent an associated finding and possibly a predisposing factor rather than a direct causal mechanism. The co-occurrence of both pathologies raises the likelihood of an underlying predisposition to vascular pathology and may have implications for the screening and clinical evaluation of surviving blood relatives.

title: Nationwide Q Fever Hospitalizations in Italy, 2014-2023: Evidence of Underrecognition and a Sardinian Hotspot.
authorString: Cifo D, González-Barrio D, Mateo-Urdiales A, Pezzotti P, Ciervo A, Fanelli A, Natale A, Gómez-Barroso D, Estévez-Reboredo RM.
abstractText:
Background

Q fever is a zoonotic disease caused by Coxiella burnetii. In Italy, serologic evidence shows exposure in humans and livestock, but surveillance data are sparse, and underreporting is likely. We aimed to characterize Q fever-related hospitalizations in Italy during 2014-2023 and examine environmental risk correlates.

Method

We conducted a nationwide retrospective study using the Italian National Hospital Discharge Database. Hospitalizations with ICD-9-CM code 083.0 as primary or secondary diagnosis were included. We calculated hospitalization rates by age, sex, and region and described clinical characteristics. We linked hospitalizations with climatic, livestock, and land-use data; for Sardinia, we fitted Bayesian spatial regression models including bovine, ovine, and caprine density, temperature, precipitation, and land use.

Results

We identified 428 hospitalizations (67% male), corresponding to a rate of 0.07 per 100 000 person-years. Rates were highest in children and older adults. The overall case fatality ratio was 2.4%. The most frequent Q fever-related concomitant diagnosis was pneumonia. Sardinia had the highest case count and adjusted hospitalization rate, 7-fold the national rate (0.55 vs 0.07). Spatial models for Sardinia showed hotspots in the north of the island and a 12% increase in spatial hospitalization risk per 10 bovine heads/km2 (adjusted relative risk 1.12, 95% credible interval 1.03-1.24).

Conclusions

Q fever causes an underrecognized burden of hospitalizations in Italy, with marked regional heterogeneity and a Sardinian hotspot associated with high cattle density areas. Clinical awareness, surveillance, and One Health interventions are warranted in high-risk areas.

title: Astrocyte-enriched and cilia-related genetic signatures in dementia: A whole-exome sequencing study.
authorString: Deng M, Chen Y, Zhao L, Song W, Qiu Q, Sun L, Lin X, Wang W, Lin GN, Li X.
abstractText:
Background

Alzheimer's disease (AD), the most prevalent form of dementia, is highly heritable, yet much of its genetic basis remains unexplained. Most genetic studies have focused on European populations, with limited data from under-represented groups. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) in the Han Chinese population may help identify novel rare variants and population-specific genetic risk factors.

Aims

This study aims to use WES to identify potential candidate genes associated with dementia and AD in the Han Chinese population.

Methods

In this exploratory pilot study, we performed WES in 63 Han Chinese patients with dementia, including 43 with AD and 20 with non-AD dementia (including one with dementia with Lewy bodies, one with Parkinson's dementia, four with frontotemporal dementia and 14 with mixed dementia), to identify rare coding variants. Gene-based case-control burden analyses using public gnomAD controls were conducted in the overall dementia cohort and the AD subgroup. Protein-protein interaction, functional enrichment, weighted gene coexpression network analysis (WGCNA) and gene set variation analysis (GSVA) using single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) datasets were performed to evaluate biological relevance and cell-type-specific activity. Cell-type marker enrichment analysis was used to identify relevant neuronal subtypes. Multilevel evidence was integrated to prioritise candidate risk genes.

Results

We identified suggestive rare variant signals in genes involved in cilia-related pathways, with stronger signals in the AD subgroup. These candidate genes were enriched in WGCNA modules associated with ageing, microtubule organisation and dementia pathology. GSVA showed increased activity of candidate genes in astrocytes using the snRNA-seq dataset. Cell-type marker analysis revealed strong enrichment in Ex6 excitatory neurons. Finally, integration of multilevel evidence prioritised 10 candidate genes.

Conclusions

This pilot study provides preliminary evidence that cilia-related pathways may be involved in dementia, especially AD susceptibility in the Han Chinese population. Further validation in larger independent cohorts with ancestry-matched controls and in functional experiments is required. Larger sample sizes for each dementia subtype will improve the detection of both dementia-shared and subtype-specific signals.

title: Multimodal imaging of papillary fibroelastoma.
authorString: Quintana Reusche LD, Velarde-Acosta K, Falcón-Quispe L, Cachicatari-Beltran A, Cupe-Chacalcaje K, Urdanivia-Ruiz D, Rafael-Horna E, Lozano Purizaca R, Baltodano-Arellano R.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur Heart J Imaging Methods Pract
journal.title: European heart journal. Imaging methods and practice
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur Heart J Imaging Methods Pract

abstractText: Papillary fibroelastoma is a rare primary cardiac tumor with a benign histology. However, it can cause serious complications, primarily thromboembolism to the brain. Multimodal imaging is important for tumor detection, tissue characterization, assessing complications, planning surgery, and postoperative follow-up. In summary, multimodal imaging plays an essential role in managing papillary fibroelastoma and is crucial in determining interventional decisions.

title: Increased IL-23 is Associated to Heliotrope Sign in Multivariate Model on Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathies.
authorString: Juarez-Gomez C, Pizano-Martinez O, Ramírez-Dueñas MG, Gomez-Rios CA, Cabrera-López M, Llamas-García A, Aguilar-Vazquez A, Vazquez-Del-Mercado M.
abstractText: Heliotrope rash is a pathognomonic feature of dermatomyositis (DM); however, the molecular pathways implicated in cutaneous involvement have not been fully explored. Although the IL-23/Th17 axis has been implicated in inflammatory and autoimmune diseases, the clinical significance of circulating IL-23 across the idiopathic inflammatory myopathy (IIM) spectrum, particularly in cutaneous disease expression, remains insufficiently defined. In this cross-sectional study, we aimed to quantify serum IL-23 levels in patients with IIM and evaluate their association with cutaneous involvement, including overall skin disease activity assessed by the Cutaneous Dermatomyositis Disease Area and Severity Index (CDASI) and the presence of specific skin manifestations, particularly pathognomonic lesions, using a univariate analysis. Serum IL-23 levels were measured by Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA) in patients with IIM and healthy controls (HCs), and their relationships with clinical and cutaneous variables were analyzed using univariable and multivariable approaches. Higher IL-23 levels were associated with cutaneous involvement, especially with pathognomonic skin manifestations and, most notably, heliotrope sign. IL-23 also showed a positive correlation with CDASI activity; the relationship with heliotrope sign remained consistent. Applying a multivariate model, heliotrope rash remained the only independent factor associated with IL-23 levels: in other words, IL-23 increases by 437.3 pg/mL when heliotrope is present. These findings suggest that IL-23 may be preferentially associated with a cutaneous phenotype characterized by heliotrope rash, rather than with global skin burden alone.

title: LC-MS/MS-based metabolomics and PK/PD correlation analysis reveal the mechanism of hyperlipidemia treatment with <i>Gastrodia elata</i> fine powder.
authorString: Xie W, Liu M, Li J, Zhang Y, Xu J, Wang C, Yuan Y, Jin Y, Du Y, Li D.
abstractText: Gastrodia elata Blume is used as both a food and a traditional medicine in East Asia. This study evaluated the lipid-lowering effects of G. elata fine powder (GFP) and the associated metabolic responses in Sprague-Dawley rats with high-fat diet (HFD)-induced hyperlipidemia. Thirty-five rats were assigned to seven groups: a normal-diet control, an untreated HFD model, three GFP groups (150, 300, or 500 mg kg-1 per administration, three times daily), and two positive-control groups receiving simvastatin or fenofibrate. Following a 6 week modeling period and a 2 week intervention, serum biochemical parameters, liver histology, and serum, urinary, and fecal metabolic profiles were assessed using biochemical assays, histological examination, and untargeted liquid chromatography-high-resolution mass spectrometry. A separate cohort of six hyperlipidemic rats received gastrodin (25 mg kg-1) for pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) analysis. Compared with the untreated HFD group, medium- and high-dose GFP improved serum lipid profiles, reduced serum aminotransferase activities, and ameliorated hepatic histopathological changes. Metabolomic profiling revealed 14 urinary, 8 fecal, and 16 serum metabolites whose HFD-associated alterations shifted toward normal-control levels following high-dose GFP treatment. The associated pathways included phenylalanine metabolism, taurine and hypotaurine metabolism, and the tricarboxylic acid cycle. Gastrodin exhibited a biphasic plasma concentration-time profile, whereas responses of five endogenous metabolic markers lagged behind systemic drug exposure. These findings support the short-term lipid-lowering activity of GFP in HFD-fed rats and its association with changes in amino acid, bile-acid-related, and energy metabolism.

title: Activation of TLR4 promotes oxidative inflammation via NADPH oxidase signaling in platelets of subjects with autism spectrum disorder.
authorString: Algahtani MM, Ahmad SF, Al-Harbi NO, Al-Ayadhi LY, Alhazzani K, Attia SM, Alanazi AZ, Bakheet SA, Nadeem A.

journal.title: Saudi pharmaceutical journal : SPJ : the official publication of the Saudi Pharmaceutical Society

abstractText: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a complex neurobehavioral disorder where both immune system and neurological dysregulations are known to play crucial roles. Platelets are known to play key roles in systemic oxidative inflammation through production of oxidants. However, there is still scarcity of data regarding the role of blood platelets in ASD subjects. Platelets are known to express innate receptors such as toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), transcription factors such as NFkB, and oxidative enzymes such as NADPH oxidase (NOX2), however the molecular mechanisms in generation of oxidative inflammation in platelets of ASD subjects have not been investigated until now. Therefore, this study was aimed at investigating expression of TLR4, NFkB, NOX2, reactive oxygen species (ROS) and lipid peroxides (a marker of oxidative damage on lipid membranes) in platelets of ASD children (n = 27) and typically developing children (TDC; n = 22) through molecular and biochemical analyses. Further, correlation analysis was carried out with severity of the disease. Our data showed an upregulated expression of TLR4 and p-NFkB in ASD platelets as compared to TDC platelets. Further, elevated TLR4/ NFkB signaling was linked with elevated NOX2-derived ROS and oxidative stress. It was confirmed by the utilization of NFkB and NOX2 inhibitors which caused reduction in LPS-induced ROS and oxidative stress in ASD platelets. Further, there was positive correlation between platelet oxidative stress and severity of the disease. Our data suggests that elevated TLR4/ NFkB signaling in platelets of ASD subjects might predispose them to increased systemic oxidative inflammation through NOX-2 derived ROS generation and oxidative stress.

title: Systemic OPA1 overexpression reshapes cardiovascular metabolism and cardiac physiology during high-fat diet feeding.
authorString: Da Dalt L, Giancane G, Fantini F, Castiglioni L, Uboldi P, Pedretti S, Mitro N, Moregola A, Terenghi O, Sironi L, Baragetti A, Norata GD.
abstractText:
Introduction

Optic atrophy 1 (OPA1) is a mitochondrial inner-membrane GTPase that coordinates mitochondrial fusion, cristae organization, and respiratory efficiency. Beyond mitochondrial bioenergetics, OPA1 contributes to cardiovascular homeostasis, including the maintenance of vascular cell function and phenotype. Although increasing OPA1 expression has been proposed to improve mitochondrial performance, the consequences of sustained OPA1-driven oxidative activation in the lipid-exposed cardiovascular system remain incompletely defined. Here, we investigated cardiac structure, tissue metabolism, and cardiomyocyte bioenergetics in mice with systemic OPA1 overexpression maintained on a high-fat diet (HFD).

Methods

OPA1-overexpressing mice were fed high-fat diet for 20 weeks, followed by indirect calorimetry and echocardiographic analysis. Tissues were used for OMICs investigation and metabolic analysis.

Results

OPA1-overexpressing mice displayed preserved global left-ventricular systolic function and ventricular volumes but presented reduced anterior and lateral wall thickness. Histological analysis further revealed a decrease in cardiomyocyte cross-sectional area accompanied by increased myocardial collagen deposition. Cardiac triglyceride content was elevated, whereas cholesterol content was unchanged. In neonatal cardiomyocytes, OPA1 overexpression resulted in increased oxygen consumption, with the strongest response observed in cells co-incubated with very-low-density lipoprotein. Under this lipid-rich condition, ATP-linked respiration, maximal respiration, and spare respiratory capacity were increased.

Discussion

Collectively, these findings indicate that systemic OPA1 overexpression was associated with myocardial lipid accumulation and early fibrotic remodeling during HFD feeding, despite preserved systolic function. In vitro, OPA1 overexpression increased cardiomyocyte respiratory capacity under lipid-rich conditions. These data identify a context-dependent effect of OPA1 in which enhanced respiratory capacity may become maladaptive when lipid supply exceeds coordinated oxidative and storage capacity.

title: Furan fatty acids reprogram hepatic lipid metabolism via acyl-CoA conjugates in obesity.
authorString: Vazquez MM, Salvatore SR, Rowart P, Anand SK, Colussi N, Fazzari M, Cole AR, Espinosa-Diez C, Jobbagy S, Liu JJ, Luo J, Gomez D, Liu S, Skarke C, Bello FM, Jurczak MJ, Prentice KJ, Wheeler MB, Trebak M, Khoo NKH, Rom O, Chang F, Schopfer FJ.
abstractText: Dietary fish oil (FO) and omega-3 fatty acids are associated with cardiometabolic benefits, yet their molecular mediators remain incompletely defined. Furan fatty acids (FuFAs), a distinct lipid class enriched in FO, have emerged as potential regulators of metabolic health. Here, we identify and quantify FuFA species in prescription omega-3 formulations and natural fish oils, and synthesize structurally engineered analogs designed to isolate antioxidant activity and β-oxidation susceptibility from FuFA bioactivity. In a diet-induced obesity mouse model, both natural and synthetic FuFAs reduced fat accumulation and inflammatory markers, while 11U3-2M additionally produced significant improvement in glucose tolerance, dyslipidemia, and hepatic steatosis. The superior activity of 11U3-2M reflects the stable accumulation of its acyl-CoA conjugate that activates peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα) signaling and allosterically inhibits acetyl-CoA carboxylases (ACCs) to reprogram hepatic lipid metabolism. These findings position FuFAs as functional dietary lipids contributing to fish oil's metabolic effects and define fatty acid structural determinants that govern hepatic metabolic activity.

title: The association of cardiovascular comorbidities with malignant and benign colorectal neoplasms.
authorString: Wani F, Marrufo IM, Bhavsar V, Whitmer R, Singh J, Kichloo A.
abstractText:
Background

Each year, thousands of patients are diagnosed with gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding. Many of these patients undergo colonoscopy and are subsequently diagnosed with benign or malignant colorectal neoplasms. The aim of this study is to evaluate whether patients with cardiovascular comorbidities, many of whom are on anti-platelet or anticoagulation therapy, are more likely to be diagnosed with new benign or malignant colorectal neoplasms than patients without cardiovascular comorbidities.

Methods

From the 2007-2011 NIS, 802,080 primary lower GI bleed admissions (ICD-9) were identified; 283,925 had cardiovascular comorbidities. We compared patients with vs without these comorbidities for the primary outcome of new benign or malignant colorectal neoplasms. Weighted analyses accounting for the complex survey design were performed in SAS 9.4, with trends assessed using Cochran-Armitage tests and linear regression and associations with colorectal cancer stage evaluated by multinomial logistic regression (p ≤ 0.05).

Results

Between 2007-2011, the odds of malignant colorectal neoplasms increased between 49.9% and 65.3% for patients without cardiovascular comorbidities when presenting with a lower GI bleed, compared to those with cardiovascular comorbidities. Between 2007 and 2011, the most notable and statistically significant difference was observed in 2010, when patients with cardiovascular comorbidities had 10.5% higher odds of being diagnosed with benign colorectal neoplasms than those without cardiovascular comorbidities.

Conclusion

Patients presenting with a lower gastrointestinal bleed without cardiovascular comorbidities were significantly more likely to be diagnosed with malignant colorectal neoplasms than those with cardiovascular comorbidities.

title: p66Shc mediates SUMO2-induced endothelial dysfunction.
authorString: Kumar J, Uppulapu SK, Kumari S, Sharma K, Paradee WJ, Yadav RP, Kumar V, Kumar S.
abstractText: Sumoylation is a post-translational modification that can regulate different physiological functions. Increased sumoylation, specifically conjugation of SUMO2/3 (small ubiquitin-like modifier 2/3), is detrimental to vascular health. However, the molecular mechanism mediating this effect is poorly understood. We used cell-based assays and mass spectrometry to show that p66Shc is a direct target of SUMO2 and that SUMO2 regulates p66Shc function via lysine-81 modification. To determine the effects of SUMO2-p66ShcK81 on vascular function, we generated Shc1K81R mice and crossbred them toLdlr-/- mice to induce hyperlipidemia. Next, to determine p66ShcK81-SUMO2ylation-induced changes in endothelial cell signaling, we performed mass spectrometry followed by Ingenuity Pathway Analysis. Our data reveal that p66Shc mediates the effects of SUMO2 on endothelial cells. Mass spectrometry identified that SUMO2 modified lysine-81 in the unique collagen homology-2 domain of p66Shc. SUMO2ylation of p66Shc increased phosphorylation at serine-36, causing it to translocate to the mitochondria, a step critical for the oxidative function of p66Shc. Notably, sumoylation-deficient p66Shc (p66ShcK81R) was resistant to SUMO2-induced p66ShcS36 phosphorylation and mitochondrial translocation. Shc1K81R mice were resistant to endothelial dysfunction induced by SUMO2ylation and hyperlipidemia. Ingenuity Pathway Analysis revealed multiple signaling pathways regulated by p66ShcK81-SUMO2ylation in endothelial cells, highlighting JAK-STAT as a major pathway affected by SUMO2-p66ShcK81. Collectively, our work reveals SUMO2-p66Shc signaling as a fundamental regulator of vascular endothelial function. We discovered that p66ShcK81 is an upstream modification regulating p66Shc signaling and mediates hyperlipidemia-induced endothelial dysfunction and oxidative stress.

title: Immune-related Plasma Proteins Associated with Recurrent Aphthous Stomatitis Identified by Mendelian Randomization and Clinical Validation.
authorString: Wang Y, Che J, Guan C, Guo H.
abstractText:
Purpose

To identify immune-related plasma proteins causally associated with susceptibility to recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS) through two-sample Mendelian randomization, and to validate their biological and clinical relevance using integrative multi-omics analyses and clinical samples.

Materials and methods

Two-sample Mendelian randomization was performed using protein quantitative trait locus (pQTL) data for immune-related plasma proteins from the deCODE genetics database and genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics for RAS to identify proteins with potential causal associations. Candidate proteins were further evaluated by Gene Ontology (GO)/Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment, protein-protein interaction (PPI) network, summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR), and colocalization analyses. Single-cell transcriptomic data from oral mucosa were integrated to characterize the cellular expression patterns of the corresponding genes. Finally, plasma levels of the candidate proteins were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) in 35 patients with RAS (sampled during both the ulcerative and healing phases) and 35 healthy controls to validate their clinical relevance.

Results

A total of 28 immune-related plasma proteins were identified as having potential causal associations with RAS through two-sample Mendelian randomization. Functional enrichment analysis indicated that these proteins were mainly involved in immune and inflammatory pathways, including natural killer (NK) cell-mediated cytotoxicity, Th1/Th2 cell differentiation, and the IL-17 signaling pathway. SMR and colocalization analyses highlighted IL17A, MMP1, and IL2RA as key candidate genes, with IL17A showing the strongest genetic evidence. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis further revealed distinct cell-type-specific expression patterns of these genes in the oral mucosa. Clinical validation confirmed statistically significant alterations in the plasma levels of IL17A, MMP1, and IL2RA across different stages of RAS.

Conclusions

This integrative study combining genetic analysis, single-cell transcriptomics, and clinical validation identified IL17A, MMP1, and IL2RA as key immune-related molecules associated with RAS. Among them, IL17A showed the strongest genetic evidence and may serve as a promising biomarker and potential therapeutic target for RAS.

title: Hydrogel platforms for 3D cardiac tissue engineering and fibrotic disease modelling.
authorString: Porritt H, Winbo A, Malmström J.
abstractText: Tissue engineering offers significant potential to advance the understanding and treatment of cardiac disease by generating in vitro models that recapitulate myocardial physiology in both healthy and diseased states. Specifically, hydrogel-based systems have been widely employed to engineer 3D cardiac tissues due to their ability to support cell viability and mimic aspects of the extracellular matrix. However, conventional hydrogels are inherently isotropic and electrically insulating, limiting their capacity to reproduce the anisotropic structure and conductive properties of native myocardium. To address these limitations, increasingly sophisticated hydrogel platforms have been developed that incorporate conductive, piezoelectric and/or aligned architectures to enhance electrical coupling, guide tissue organisation and promote cardiomyocyte maturation. These hydrogel-based systems can also be tuned to recapitulate pathological states. Cardiac fibrosis is characterised by increased tissue stiffness, and researchers have sought to model this process by modulating the mechanical microenvironment to induce fibrotic phenotypes. With recently developed hydrogel platforms, mechanical properties can be controlled with both spatial and temporal precision, enabling systematic investigation of how dynamic and heterogeneous stiffness influences tissue formation, remodelling and disease progression. Although these platforms are not yet fully translational, they provide powerful tools to modulate multiple physiological parameters, thereby advancing our understanding of cardiac development and informing strategies to treat prevalent pathological conditions.

title: Automated phase recognition in the cardiac catheterization laboratory with deep learning.
authorString: Vijfvinkel TS, Frassini E, Weijenberg Y, Nikookar B, Butler RM, Constandse J, van der Elst M, Hendriks BHW, van den Dobbelsteen JJ.
abstractText:
Background

An efficient workflow in the cardiac catheterization laboratory is important to guarantee quality of care and keep healthcare affordable. Automated surgical process monitoring of diagnostic coronary angiograms (CAGs) has the potential to increase workflow efficiency, reduce non-clinical workload, and optimize scheduling. The aim of this study is to automatically classify workflow phases of CAGs using deep learning models trained on a real-world dataset.

Methods

With an observational study we collected a dataset, composed of an integration of video recorded CAGs, clinical data, and system logging data. Every procedural phase was annotated by a medical doctor based on clinically relevant key points in time. A Scaled-YOLOv4 object detection algorithm was employed to extract features from the video images. We implemented Long short-term memory (LSTM) and LSTM-Fully convolutional network (LSTM-FCN) on the integrated time series data to classify the workflow phases. The accuracy in the classification was weighted on the duration of the phase.

Results

A dataset including video, clinical and logging data of 222 CAG procedures was obtained. A weighted accuracy for phase classification of 91.3% was reached for the LSTM model, compared to 90.8% for the LSTM-FCN model. No significant difference was found after statistical comparison between both models. However, the LSTM network was 2.2 times faster in training while requiring around 40% less parameters.

Conclusions

This study demonstrates the potential of deploying deep learning models on a real-world integrated dataset to automatically detect CAG phases with more than 90% accuracy. No statistically significant difference was found between the performance of the two models, although the LSTM model required less training time compared to the LSTM-FCN. Thus, we suggest the employment of these models for phase recognition challenges based on composite datasets. Given the promising accuracy of these deep learning techniques, automated phase recognition could become a cornerstone of dynamic schedule optimization and increase future hospital efficiency.

title: Necrotizing Enterocolitis Secondary to Congenital Syphilis in an 18-Day-Old Neonate: Successful Treatment With Intravenous Penicillin.
authorString: Chap C, Bin V, Bin S.
abstractText: Congenital syphilis remains a preventable yet persistent global health challenge, particularly in resource-limited countries. Gastrointestinal involvement is uncommon, and necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) has rarely been reported as a manifestation of early congenital syphilis. We present the case of an 18-day-old neonate who was initially admitted with a diagnosis of NEC, with abdominal distension, feeding intolerance, and characteristic radiologic signs, corresponding to Grade IIb NEC according to the Modified Bell criteria. However, the presence of desquamation on the soles, along with a markedly enlarged liver, warranted a test for congenital syphilis, which was subsequently confirmed. The infant was successfully treated with intravenous penicillin alongside standard medical therapy for NEC, resulting in clinical recovery without surgical intervention. This case underscores the role of Treponema pallidum as a potential, yet often unrecognized, causative agent of NEC in neonates. Early recognition and timely, targeted antibiotic therapy are critical to preventing severe complications.

title: Haemoptysis in chronic pulmonary vascular disease: a narrative review.
authorString: Kamp JC, Budhram B, Jevnikar M, Olsson KM, Peperhove MJ, Neubert L, Hoeper MM, Humbert M.

journal.title: European respiratory review : an official journal of the European Respiratory Society

abstractText: Haemoptysis, the expectoration of blood from the lower airways, is a complication of several pulmonary vascular diseases (PVDs). The pathophysiology of haemoptysis in chronic PVDs is complex and varies depending on the underlying condition. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography remains the gold standard for localising the bleeding source and guiding interventional therapies. Management of haemoptysis in patients with chronic PVDs can range from oxygen supplementation to angiography-guided bronchial artery embolisation, depending on bleeding severity, anatomical features and specific features of the associated disease. Regardless of the management strategy, long-term follow-up is essential in these patients owing to the risk of recurrent bleeding. The aim of this review is to comprehensively explore the characteristics of haemoptysis in selected chronic PVDs, summarise current knowledge of the pathophysiology, and provide guidance on contemporary diagnostic and treatment strategies.

authorString: Takafuji M, Naderi H, Sia CH, Chambers B, Farooq M, Anderton T, Plein S, Greenwood JP, Swoboda PP.

title: Pregnancy outcome after first-trimester exposure to JAK inhibitors - an evaluation of the German Embryotox cohort.
authorString: Habbel AS, Beck E, Mueller A, Dathe K.
abstractText:
Background

Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi) are increasingly being used in the management of autoimmune diseases across rheumatology, gastroenterology, and dermatology, including in women of childbearing age. Consequently, pregnancies occurring during JAKi treatment are becoming more common. However, uncertainties regarding their safety during pregnancy remain, and current human data are insufficient to allow a comprehensive assessment of fetal risk.

Methods

Observational data of pregnancies with first trimester JAKi exposure, recorded in the German Embryotox database, was analyzed. Pregnancies were prospectively enrolled between January 1, 2017, and November 15, 2025. Study endpoints included major congenital anomalies, pregnancy loss, and neonatal parameters.

Results

The cohort comprised a total of 44 pregnancies exposed to baricitinib (n = 17), filgotinib (n = 3), tofacitinib (n = 8), or upadacitinib (n = 16). A total of 32 live births were recorded. Among these, two major congenital anomalies were observed, one ventricular septal defect and one hypospadias. Five spontaneous abortions occurred, including one case of fetal anencephaly, and seven elective terminations of pregnancy were reported. Additional neonatal assessments revealed two preterm births at 36 weeks' gestation, three infants born small for gestational age, and two newborns large for gestational age.

Conclusions

The current evidence is insufficient to establish or exclude an association between JAK inhibitor exposure and adverse fetal outcomes. To date, the potential for harmful effects cannot be ruled out due to the limited available data. Therefore, routine use of JAKi during pregnancy is not recommended and treatment should be approached with caution, and requires a critical risk-benefit assessment until further data is obtained.

Trial registration

The study was retrospectively registered in the German Clinical Trials Register on March 16, 2026 (DRKS00039622).
