title: Nationwide outcomes of biliary atresia after Kasai portoenterostomy in Taiwan: the impact of postoperative cholangitis and corticosteroid use.
authorString: Yang HH, Huang WT, Wang JH, Chen MC, Wen SH.
abstractText:
Purpose

To provide updated nationwide outcomes of biliary atresia (BA) among patients in Taiwan, focusing on postoperative cholangitis, liver transplantation (LT), corticosteroid use, and renal outcomes.

Methods

Infants with BA who underwent Kasai portoenterostomy were identified from the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database (2008-2019). Postoperative outcomes were evaluated, and the association between cholangitis episodes and LT was analyzed using exploratory logistic regression analysis. Corticosteroid exposure was categorized by duration, and acute kidney injury was assessed as a secondary outcome.

Results

This study included 334 infants. Acute cholangitis occurred in 76.3% of cases, with 24.9% experiencing ≥ 5 hospitalizations. A greater number of cholangitis episodes was associated with a higher likelihood of LT (odds ratio: 1.08, 95% confidence interval: 1.00-1.16, p = 0.044). Approximately 30.8% of patients developed biliary cirrhosis, and 33.8% received LT. Corticosteroids were prescribed to 96% of patients, and a longer treatment duration was associated with higher complication rates. About 1.8% of patients developed acute kidney injury, with no progression to end-stage renal disease.

Conclusion

Postoperative cholangitis remains an important clinical factor associated with LT in infants with BA. Corticosteroid treatment duration may reflect underlying disease severity rather than therapeutic benefit. Renal complications are uncommon. Optimizing postoperative care-particularly timely cholangitis management-is essential to improve outcomes.

title: Effectiveness of prenatal predictors for congenital diaphragmatic hernia on survival to discharge and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation requirement: a retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Rogers E, Le Vance J, Naidu S, Singh A, Jester I, Gurney L, Pachl M.
abstractText:
Introduction

Congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) is associated with high mortality and morbidity. Antenatal counselling enables parents to prepare for the postnatal outcomes and relies on effective prognostic tools. Ultrasound (USS) predictors including observed/expected lung head ratio (o/e LHR) and liver position, are used independently, or combined into severity classifications. The aim was to evaluate the association between USS predictors, and severity classifications with survival to discharge and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) requirement in prenatally diagnosed CDH at Birmingham Women's and Children's Hospital (BWC).

Methods

CDH patients from BWC with dates of birth between 1st December 2013-1st December 2023 were retrospectively collected. Study inclusion required o/e LHR measurement between 22- and 32-weeks gestational age (GA.) Comparisons between groups was assessed by Fisher exact test and Mann-Whitney U test. Logistic regression was performed to determine prognostic ability, with area under curve (AUC) calculated.

Results

91 eligible patients were identified, which included 82 left-sided, and 9 right-sided CDH. Overall, 55% survived to discharge and 13% required ECMO. In the left CDH cohort, 57% of infants survived to discharge, and 15% required ECMO. O/e LHR, liver position and the combined predictive model including o/e LHR and liver position were predictive of survival to discharge with good prognostic ability (AUC 0.769, AUC 0.703, and AUC 0.823, respectively). O/e LHR, liver position, and the combined predictive model were not predictive of ECMO requirement. In the right CDH patients, 33% survived to discharge, O/e LHR and liver position were not predictive of survival to discharge.

Conclusion

O/e LHR, liver position and the combination of these predictors, predicted survival to discharge in prenatally diagnosed left CDH with the combined model, the most predictive particularly in the isolated left CDH sub-group. Further analysis into effective predictors for ECMO requirement, and for right and complex left CDH is required.

title: Secreted factors mediate the crosstalk between liver fibrosis, atherosclerosis, and bone metabolism.
authorString: Hu L, Li H, Zhang W, Chen S, Cai Z, Chen M, Liang W, Bai X, Liu X.
abstractText: This study investigates the potential bidirectional communication between non-skeletal organs and bone in disease states such as liver fibrosis and atherosclerosis. Transcriptomic analysis of mouse models of liver fibrosis and atherosclerosis identified 782 and 878 differentially expressed potential secreted factors, respectively. Mendelian randomization analysis revealed causal associations between multiple secreted factors (e.g., Sfrp1, Il18bp, Adam11) and bone mineral density, with shared bone-influencing factors across both disease models. Integration with population-based proteome-phenome databases further indicated that these factors predominantly correlate with osteoporosis risk, primarily as risk factors. Concurrently, proteomic analysis of bone tissue from disease model mice revealed that liver fibrosis significantly impacts pathways related to bone development and cartilage formation, while atherosclerosis primarily disrupts bone remodeling and resorption processes. Furthermore, simultaneous detection of proteins in bone tissue and bone marrow supernatant revealed significant alterations in osteokines (e.g., CD5L, SERPING1) in disease conditions, which suggested genetic or epidemiological associations with multiple systemic diseases. Collectively, by integrating multi-omics data from murine models and human populations, this study screens candidate proteins for liver-bone and artery-bone crosstalk, suggesting that the liver and arteries may remotely regulate bone metabolism via secreted factors in pathological states, and that bone may influence systemic processes through endocrine feedback, thereby laying a theoretical foundation for future functional validation of these bidirectional regulatory mechanisms.

title: Changes of serum fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) and Klotho in diabetic kidney disease and their correlation with coronary artery calcification: a retrospective study.
authorString: Hong Y, Wang J, Lu Q, Sun W, Sun J.
abstractText:
Objective

This study investigated the association among fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23), Klotho, and coronary artery calcification (CAC) in patients with diabetic kidney disease (DKD).

Subjects and methods

A total of 176 DKD patients and 160 age-and diabetes-matched controls were retrospectively analyzed. We measured serum FGF23 and Klotho levels by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and assessed CAC by CAC scoring. Correlation and receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed to evaluate the associations of these biomarkers with CAC and their ability to discriminate CAC.

Results

FGF23 levels were significantly higher and Klotho levels were lower in patients with DKD than in controls. FGF23 correlated negatively with estimated glomerular filtration rate and positively with the albumin-to-creatinine ratio and blood urea nitrogen, whereas Klotho correlated positively with estimated glomerular filtration rate and negatively with albumin-to-creatinine ratio and blood urea nitrogen. In patients with CAC, FGF23 levels were higher and Klotho levels were lower. Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed that both FGF23 and Klotho discriminated CAC, and FGF23 showed a higher area under curve than Klotho. Correlation analysis further confirmed the association of FGF23 and Klotho with CAC severity.

Conclusion

FGF23 and Klotho were associated with renal impairment and CAC in patients with DKD and may serve as potential biomarkers of renal and cardiovascular risk.

title: Xanthine oxidase inhibitory evaluation of prenylated flavonoids from peanut (<i>Arachis hypogaea</i> L.) shells: <i>in vitro</i> and <i>in silico</i> molecular docking studies.
authorString: Hoang PTN, Do TNV, Than TBT, Mai TV, Truong DM, Nguyen PT, Le KM, Nguyen HX, Le TH, Nguyen MTT.
abstractText: Sustainable agriculture has become a crucial priority because the improper management of agricultural waste currently contributes to greenhouse gas emissions, as well as soil and air pollution. The shells of Arachis hypogaea L., which is commonly discarded as an agricultural by-product, have been reported to contain various secondary metabolites, including flavonoids, stilbenes, triterpenoids, etc. This work led to the isolation of two new prenylated flavonoids, arachisflavones A (1) and B (2), together with five prenylated flavones (3-7), two prenylated chalcones (8-9), and three prenylated flavanones (10-12) from the EtOAc extract of peanut shells. Notably, this is the first report isolating prenylated flavonoids from the Arachis genus and evaluating their xanthine oxidase (XO) inhibitory activity. The XO inhibitory assays revealed that 6/12 isolated compounds showed inhibitory activity, with IC50 values ranging from 0.256 to 59.1 µM. Among them, yinyanghuo E (6) showed the strongest XO inhibitory effect with an IC50 value of 0.256 ± 0.008 µM (95% CI: 0.238 to 0.275), comparable with the positive controls, allopurinol (IC50 = 2.34 ± 0.08 µM) (95% CI: 2.17 to 2.52) and febuxostat (IC50 = 0.018 ± 0.002 µM) (95% CI: 0.014 to 0.022). Molecular docking suggested that the active compounds exhibited favorable docking scores through interactions with key catalytic residues, including Arg880, Thr1010, Phe914, and Phe1009. Furthermore, ADMET prediction analysis revealed that arachis flavones A (1) possessed the most favorable predicted drug-likeness properties among the isolated compounds.

title: Rational design and synthesis of furan-based Schiff base quinazolin-4-amine hybrids: spectral elucidation, molecular docking, DFT studies, and <i>in silico</i> ADMET-antioxidant study.
authorString: Narode SD, Vora M, Maheta JB, Bhola YO, Lakhnotra DK, Patel NJ.
abstractText: In this work, a new series of furan-based quinazoline-4-amine hydrazone (Schiff base) derivatives (4a-h) was rationally designed and synthesized in good yields (84-90%) through a multistep route involving nucleophilic aromatic substitution, Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling, and hydrazone/Schiff base condensation reactions. The synthesized compounds were characterized by FT-IR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and ESI-mass spectrometry, which confirmed the proposed structures. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed to optimize the molecular geometries and to derive frontier molecular orbital energies, global reactivity descriptors, Mulliken atomic charges, and molecular electrostatic potential (MEP) surfaces, providing insight into the stability, reactivity, and radical-scavenging propensity of the compounds. Molecular docking studies against the Kelch domain of Keap1 (PDB 4L7B), the principal negative regulator of the Nrf2-mediated antioxidant response, were carried out using the Schrödinger Suite (Glide, Maestro interface) to explore, in silico, a possible interaction of the derivatives with this target; the docked compounds gave Glide docking scores of -7.325 to -8.603 kcal mol; these results constitute an in silico hypothesis of Keap1 binding that remains to be tested experimentally. Computational ADMET profiling indicated drug-like physicochemical properties overall, with the dimethoxy- and phenolic-substituted analogues 4e and 4h showing the most favourable predicted oral bioavailability (score = 0.55) among the series. The in vitro antioxidant potential of compounds 4a-h was evaluated using the DPPH radical-scavenging assay, giving IC50 values of 85.5 ± 3.7 to 148.1 ± 3.2 µM, compared with 235.2 ± 4.6 µM for the standard antioxidant ascorbic acid; on a molar basis, all eight derivatives were therefore more potent than ascorbic acid in this cell-free assay. Among the series, compounds 4d and 4f displayed the most promising radical-scavenging activity (IC50 = 85.5 and 90.8 µM, respectively), although the global DFT reactivity descriptors did not correlate with the measured activity across the series.

title: CYP1B1 is a potential target of kaempferol in renal fibrosis: a multi‑omics and single‑cell transcriptomics study.
authorString: Huang C, Shi X, Yan Z.
abstractText:
Background

Renal fibrosis (RF) is a progressive and irreversible pathological process for which effective treatments are limited. This study explores the molecular targets and mechanisms through which kaempferol (Kae) ameliorates RF, with particular emphasis on cytochrome P450 1B1 (CYP1B1).

Methods

Using a combination of transcriptomic profiling, weighted gene co‑expression network analysis (WGCNA), multi‑algorithm machine learning [least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), support vector machine‑recursive feature elimination (SVM‑RFE), and Random Forest], and single‑cell transcriptomics, we identified the core targets of Kae intervention in RF. shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis evaluated gene contributions to the predictive model, while cell‑type identification by estimating relative subsets of RNA transcripts (CIBERSORT) estimated the immune microenvironment. The cell type-specific distribution of core targets was further characterized through single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and the scTenifoldKnk (a machine learning-based virtual gene knockout tool) algorithm simulated the effects of CYP1B1 loss-of-function on fibroblast activation and extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition. Finally, molecular docking was performed to predict the binding conformations of kaempferol with the proteins encoded by the six prioritized genes.

Results

Six core genes (VCAM1, NFKBIA, SFN, CCL5, CYP1B1, and AXL) were identified from 25 Kae-RF-related genes, with CYP1B1 as an upstream regulatory hub. Immune infiltration analysis revealed increased plasma cells and eosinophils, alongside decreased M0/M1 macrophages and activated NK cells. Single-cell analysis localized CYP1B1 to smooth muscle cells and fibroblasts, with significant upregulation during late-stage fibroblast-to-myofibroblast differentiation. Virtual knockdown of CYP1B1 upregulated 46 genes associated with fibrosis-related biological processes, including cell adhesion, G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) signaling, ion transport, and cytoskeletal remodeling. The six-gene diagnostic model achieved area under the curves (AUCs) of 0.889 (training) and 0.759 (external validation). Molecular docking showed favorable Kae-CYP1B1 binding (- 6.5 kcal/mol).

Conclusion

CYP1B1 may serve as a potential functional target of Kae in RF, likely through modulation of fibroblast activation and ECM remodeling. These findings are hypothesis‑generating and provide a computational basis for future experimental validation of CYP1B1‑targeted strategies in RF.

title: MicroRNAs and polymorphisms influencing MICA immune modulation.
authorString: Nicoletti MB, Ferraz IM, Moço AC, da Cruz Castelli E, Castro CFB.
abstractText: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are small non-coding RNAs that play a central role in post-transcriptional gene regulation. They act mainly by interacting with sequences located in the 3' untranslated regions (3'UTRs) of messenger RNAs (mRNAs), thereby influencing mRNA stability and translation. Through these mechanisms, miRNAs contribute to the fine-tuning of multiple biological pathways, including immune activation, inflammatory signaling, and cellular stress responses. Among the genes involved in immune surveillance, the major histocompatibility complex class I polypeptide-related sequence A (MICA) has emerged as an important target for post-transcriptional regulation due to its role as a ligand for the activating receptor NKG2D (natural killer cell group 2-D), which is expressed in natural killer (NK) cells and cytotoxic T lymphocytes. MICA is highly polymorphic, and several allelic variants differ in sequence composition, structural organization, and expression patterns, potentially influencing miRNA-mRNA interactions. Growing evidence suggests that miRNA-mediated regulation of MICA contributes to immune modulation in cancer, viral infections, and autoimmune disorders, particularly through mechanisms associated with immune evasion and altered NKG2D signaling. In addition, genetic polymorphisms and structural variations within regulatory regions, especially within the 3'UTR, can alter miRNA binding affinity by creating, disrupting, or modifying target sites. This mini review discusses the current understanding of miRNA-mediated regulation of MICA, emphasizing the impact of allelic diversity and regulatory polymorphisms on post-transcriptional control. Furthermore, it highlights current knowledge gaps and future perspectives regarding allele-specific regulation.

title: Survival benefit in patients with native aortic regurgitation using a dedicated transcatherter valve vs non-dedicated transcatheter valves.
authorString: Messori A, Brunoro R, Rivano M.

journal.title: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions

abstractText:
Background

Until recently, no standard of care has been established for patients with symptomatic native aortic regurgitation (AR) who are unsuitable for surgery. Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has been explored in this setting using off-label, non-dedicated valves originally designed for aortic stenosis. The recent ALIGN-AR trial evaluated the Trilogy valve, a dedicated transcatheter device specifically designed for native AR.

Methods

We performed an indirect comparison between the overall survival (OS) reported for the Trilogy valve in ALIGN-AR and OS from seven single-arm studies using non-dedicated valves. Individual patient data were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves using the IPDfromKM method. To ensure homogeneity, the follow-up period for the survival analysis was truncated at 24 months. Survival was analyzed using both hazard ratios (HR) and restricted mean survival time (RMST).

Results

The analysis included 492 patients treated with the Trilogy valve and 867 treated with non-dedicated valves. OS was significantly improved with the Trilogy valve (HR 0.399; 95% CI 0.275-0.578; p = 0.0000011). RMST at 12 months was 11.4 months for the Trilogy valve versus 10.4 months for non-dedicated valves, corresponding to an OS gain of 1.0 months (95% CI 0.72-1.32) over the first year.

Conclusions

In patients with native AR undergoing TAVI, use of the dedicated Trilogy valve was associated with a highly significant survival advantage compared with non-dedicated devices, corresponding to an approximate 1-month gain in OS during the first 12 months after implantation.

title: A Case of Platypnea-Orthodeoxia Syndrome Caused by Patent Foramen Ovale, Accompanied by Dilated Ascending Aorta, Thoracic Kyphosis and Persistent Eustachian Valve.
authorString: Kishimoto A, Namiki T, Ogata Y, Sunabe H, Inui T, Ishikawa H, Watanabe H, Ohta C, Numata R, Kawamatsu N, Machino-Ohtsuka T, Hoshi T, Sakamoto T.
abstractText: We present a case of platypnea-orthodeoxia syndrome (POS) associated with patent foramen ovale (PFO). In the upright position, right atrial compression resulting from a dilated ascending aorta and thoracic kyphosis modifies the spatial alignment of the PFO, orienting it toward inferior vena cava (IVC) inflow and increasing its tendency to remain patent. Further, a prominent Eustachian valve redirected blood returning from the IVC toward the PFO and thereby promoting right-to-left shunting. The patient subsequently underwent percutaneous transcatheter PFO closure. Even 10 months after the procedure, oxygen saturation measured on room air remained stable at 99% in both supine and upright positions.

title: 20-year analysis of protocol-driven quality improvement in cardiac homograft banking.
authorString: Baruji MA, Syed Nong SN, Abdul Aziz KA, Nordin MN, Md Taib ME, Gaaffar IF, Kepli AS, Sallehuddin A.
abstractText: Cardiac homografts are indispensable in complex cardiac surgery, particularly in the paediatric population. Optimising procurement and minimising discard rates are important for maintaining graft availability, especially in resource-limited settings. This study evaluated 20 years of cardiac homograft procurement at a tertiary cardiovascular centre, focusing on discard rates, causes of discard, microbiological profiles, and the impact of protocol refinements. A retrospective analysis was conducted using procurement records from the Cardiac Homograft Tissue Bank at the Institut Jantung Negara, Malaysia, between January 2004 and December 2024. The data collected included annual procurement volume, reasons for discarding, and microbiological culture results. In 2015, a revised procurement protocol was introduced, which incorporated instrument and operative field segregation, aseptic redraping, and enhanced donor screening. A total of 190 hearts were procured (mean 9.05 ± 4.18 hearts/year), with an overall discard rate of 13.7% (of 26/190). Prior to 2015, the discard rate was 17.2% (20/116), with environmental contamination accounting for the majority of the discards (75%; n=15). Fifteen microbial isolates were identified in the pre-revision period: Candida (n=6), Klebsiella (n=4), Acinetobacter (n=2), Streptococcus spp. (n=1), Streptococcus viridans (n=1), and Pseudomonas spp. (n=1). Following the 2015 protocol revision, the overall discard rate decreased to 8.1% (6/74), representing a 53% reduction, although this difference was not statistically significant (p=0.074). Environmental contamination-related discards decreased significantly from 12.9% (15/116) to 1.4% (1/74) (89% reduction; p=0.005), with only one Candida isolate identified post-revision. Protocol refinement has therefore produced a statistically significant reduction in contamination-related discards and a shift in the microbiological spectrum.

title: Apixaban for thromboprophylaxis in paediatric cardiology patients: Real-world data from a single institution.
authorString: Bosch A, Berger F, Dave H, Albisetti M.
abstractText:
Background

Thrombosis is a major complication in children with congenital or acquired heart disease, contributing to significant morbidity and mortality. Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), including apixaban, are increasingly used for thromboprophylaxis in this population yet real-world paediatric data remain limited.

Objectives

To evaluate the safety and effectiveness of apixaban as thromboprophylaxis in paediatric cardiac patients receiving commercially available adult tablet formulations outside a clinical trial setting.

Patients/methods

This retrospective cohort study included patients aged ≤18 years with congenital or acquired heart disease who received apixaban at the University Children's Hospital Zurich from October 2022 to June 2025. Dosing was approximated to the SAXOPHONE trial using commercially available tablets that were split or crushed, without therapeutic laboratory monitoring. Outcomes included incident thrombosis (primary), major bleeding, clinically relevant non-major bleeding (CRNMB), and all-cause mortality.

Results

Sixty-seven patients were included with a median age of 4.6 years (IQR 3.3-9.8) and median apixaban exposure of 210 days (IQR 83-461), totalling 18,799 patient-days (51.5 patient-years). Single ventricle physiology was the most common underlying diagnosis (40/67, 60%) and Fontan circulation the most frequent indication (34/67, 51%). Two thrombotic events occurred (incidence rate 3.9 per 100 patient-years), both in the context of additional thrombotic risk factors. No major bleeding or CRNMB events were recorded.

Conclusions

Apixaban appeared safe and effective as thromboprophylaxis in this paediatric cardiology cohort, with no major or CRNMB and a low rate of thrombotic events. These findings add to the growing body of real-world evidence supporting DOAC use in children with cardiac disease.

title: Newly diagnosed and relapsed follicular lymphoma: EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up.
authorString: Ladetto M, Bolaños N, Bouguet G, Herfarth K, Klapper W, Leppa S, Linton K, Lopez-Guillermo A, Luminari S, Morschhauser F, Okosun J, Paszkiewicz-Kozik E, Thieblemont C, Tonino SH, Trneny M, Trotman J, Yilmaz U, Dreyling M.
abstractText: Follicular lymphoma (FL) is the second most common lymphoma subtype in Europe, with a median age at diagnosis of 60-65 years. It is generally considered an indolent disease, and the median overall survival at diagnosis now likely exceeds 20 years. However, considerable heterogeneity exists. Diagnosis requires adequate biopsy material and a specialized hematopathologist. Staging and prognosis rely on positron emission tomography (PET)-computed tomography (CT). Prognostication at diagnosis is based on several validated clinical prognostic scores. Localized disease is usually treated with radiotherapy ± Rituximab. The treatment of disseminated disease includes active surveillance (or in selected cases Rituximab monotherapy) for low-tumor burden patients, and most often immunochemotherapy (or in selected cases chemo-free therapeutic options), ±antibody maintenance in high-tumor burden patients. For relapsed or refractory disease, treatment with Rituximab-Lenalidomide combination ± Tafasitamab or Epcoritamab from the first relapse and single-agent bispecific antibodies, chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy (CAR-T) cells, and Zanubrutinib-Obinutuzumab after second relapse should be prioritized over immunochemotherapy. Given the long natural history and risk of relapse, careful follow-up is an important part of patient management. Patients should be actively involved in decision-making. In this guideline, we present current evidence-based recommendations for diagnosis, staging, treatment, and follow-up.

title: Umbilical cord blood miR-125b-5p: a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for neonatal respiratory distress syndrome.
authorString: Zhang Y, Liu Z, Zhang Y, Hou Y, Sun L.

journal.title: Revista paulista de pediatria : orgao oficial da Sociedade de Pediatria de Sao Paulo

abstractText:
Objective

Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (NRDS) is a common respiratory disease. This study aimed to detect the expression of miR-125b-5p in the umbilical cord blood of NRDS patients and to evaluate its diagnostic and prognostic value.

Methods

Fluorescence-based real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction was used to detect miR-125b-5p expression in the umbilical cord blood of NRDS patients and controls. The correlation between miR-125b-5p expression and NRDS clinical data was analyzed. Survival was analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method. Cox regression identified risk factors for adverse outcomes, and the ROC curve evaluated diagnostic and prognostic accuracy.

Results

The level of miR-125b-5p in NRDS patients was higher than that in controls. High miR-125b-5p expression was correlated with C-reactive protein levels, umbilical artery blood gas parameters, and the lung ultrasound score. Patients with high miR-125b-5p expression had significantly shorter event-free survival (HR 2.358, 95%CI 1.345-4.133, p<0.05) and long-term survival (HR 2.489, 95%CI 1.201-5.161, p<0.05). Cox regression identified high miR-125b-5p expression, high lung ultrasound score, high PaCO₂, and high PaO₂ as prognostic factors.

Conclusions

Umbilical cord blood miR-125b-5p is highly expressed in NRDS. It may serve as a biomarker for the diagnosis and prognosis of NRDS.

title: Left main coronary artery-Pulmonary trunk fistula incidentally detected during acute coronary infarction: Complementary roles of coronary angiography and CCTA.
authorString: Ejjebli HE, Boulouiz S, Bazid Z, Ismaili N, El Ouafi N.
abstractText: Coronary artery fistulas (CAFs) are rare vascular anomalies, and fistulas originating from the left main coronary artery (LMCA) are particularly uncommon. A 63-year-old woman with hypertension and obesity presented with acute anterior myocardial infarction and left ventricular systolic dysfunction. Coronary angiography incidentally identified a tortuous vascular tract arising from the proximal LMCA, but couldn't define its drainage site. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) demonstrated a 3.9 cm fistulous tract with an origin and maximal diameter of 6 mm, coursing anteriorly and to the right of the pulmonary trunk before draining into it. No focal aneurysmal dilatation, mural thrombus, calcification, or secondary branches were identified. The pulmonary trunk measured 29 mm, the right-sided cardiac chambers were not dilated, and transthoracic echocardiography showed no noninvasive evidence of a large hemodynamically significant left-to-right shunt or right-sided volume overload. Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) was performed for the culprit left anterior descending lesion, after which the symptoms resolved. The clinical course favored the LAD lesion as the dominant cause of ischemia, although a contributory fistula-related steal phenomenon was not formally assessed. Following discussion among several cardiovascular experts, conservative clinical and echocardiographic surveillance was selected. This case highlights the complementary roles of coronary angiography and CCTA in defining fistula anatomy and supporting individualized management and follow-up planning.

title: Clinical profile, risk factors and in-hospital outcomes of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction in young versus older adults: a 5-year retrospective cohort study at a tertiary care centre in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

title: Vancomycin Population Pharmacokinetics and Exposure Variability in Children with Multiple Organ Dysfunction Syndrome.
authorString: Scheetz MH, Shiau J, Amajor V, Bwint A, Sharova A, Hensley J, Shein SL, Hume JR, Rowan CM, Grijalba CQ, Malone MP, Stenson EK, Weiss SL, Zinter MS, Kannan S, Dahmer MK, Nofziger R, Rhodes NJ, Zuppa AF, Pai MP, Hall MW, Downes KJ, PALISI Network Investigators.
abstractText: In children with multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS), vancomycin dosing is frequently guided by population-based approaches followed by therapeutic drug monitoring that requires considerable blood volumes. We sought to develop a population pharmacokinetic (PK) model and describe vancomycin exposures using blood-sparing, whole-blood volumetric absorptive microsampling (VAMS). In this multicentre prospective observational study, up to 15 PK samples were collected per subject over 3 days. Individual whole-blood areas under the concentration-time curve during 0-24 hours (AUC<sub>0-24h</sub>) and 24-48 hours (AUC<sub>24-48h</sub>) after treatment initiation were estimated. Simulations explored exposures across weight and renal function strata. Sixty-five subjects were included in the final model cohort (median age, 10 years [range, 1 month-17 years]; median weight, 30 kg [3-214 kg]). A two-compartment, allometrically scaled model incorporating renal function best described vancomycin PK. The median dose preceding the first PK sample was 380 mg (15 mg/kg), with most subjects receiving vancomycin every 6 hours. In the fully paired analysis set (n=46), median whole-blood AUC<sub>0-24h</sub> and AUC<sub>24-48h</sub> were 475 mg·h/L (range, 232-1,749) and 594 mg·h/L (range, 188-2,157), respectively. Simulations demonstrated substantial exposure variability across weight and renal function strata. These findings demonstrate substantial interindividual exposure variability despite population-based dosing. The model provides a foundation for prospective evaluation of individualized exposure estimation using sparse VAMS sampling. Whole-blood VAMS AUC therapeutic targets remain unvalidated, and direct interpretation against established plasma-based targets is an important future effort.

title: The relationship between surgical fear, spiritual well-being, and religious coping in patients scheduled for open heart surgery: a cross-sectional study.
authorString: Kılınç T, Yayla A, Ergün A.
abstractText:
Background

Open-heart surgery involves surgical fear as a frequently experienced condition in patients because of uncertainty, perception of death, pain, and intense stress. In this process, spiritual well-being and religious coping mechanisms stand out as important psychosocial resources that can influence how patients cope with fear and anxiety. The study aimed to determine the relationship between surgical fear, spiritual well-being, and religious coping in patients scheduled for open-heart surgery.

Method

This was a cross-sectional descriptive correlational study. The study was conducted with patients scheduled for open-heart surgery in the cardiovascular surgery department of a university hospital in eastern Turkiye. Data were collected during the preoperative period between March and October 2025. Participants who met the inclusion criteria and agreed to participate were recruited using a convenience sampling method. The study was completed with 179 patients. The data were collected using the "Personal Information Form", "Surgical Fear Questionnaire (SFQ)", "3-Factor Spiritual Well-being Scale (3F-SWBS)", and "Religious Coping Scale (RCS)". Descriptive statistics (percentages, mean values, frequencies, and standard deviation values), t-test, and Pearson correlation analysis were used for analyses. Also, stepwise linear regression analysis was performed to identify factors influencing surgical fear.

Results

The average age of the patients was 64.99 ± 9.27 years. The mean SFQ score was 22.69 ± 19.79, the mean 3F-SWBS score was 124.78 ± 12.04, the positive religious coping score was 26.21 ± 2.87, and the negative religious coping score was 10.05 ± 3.59. 3F-Spiritual well-being (Beta = -0.282 ; p < 0.001) was significantly associated with surgical fear, followed by negative religious coping (Beta = 0.208; p=0.005 p) and having previous non-cardiac surgery (Beta = 0.166; p=0.019 p).

Conclusion

The study found that patients reported low levels of surgical fear, high levels of spiritual well-being, and positive religious coping, alongside low levels of negative religious coping. Higher spiritual well-being was associated with lower surgical fear, whereas higher negative religious coping and a history of previous non-cardiac surgery were associated with higher surgical fear.

title: Factors Associated with Predischarge Morbidity and Mortality in Small for Gestational Age Infants: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study
Case Report: Multidisciplinary and individualized management of periprocedural arterial thrombosis and ischemic stroke in children: a three-case series.
authorString: Zhou G, Ge W, Wan H, Chen R, Hou K, Ji Z.
abstractText: Pediatric arterial thromboembolism is rare but may cause limb loss, extensive cerebral infarction, permanent disability, or death. Evidence guiding reperfusion therapy in children remains limited. We describe three periprocedural events treated according to their vascular territory, threatened tissue, and bleeding risk. A male neonate born at 37 weeks' gestation developed catheter-associated left external iliac-femoral arterial thrombosis after umbilical arterial catheterization during treatment for shock and respiratory illness. Intravenous urokinase and low-molecular-weight heparin achieved complete thrombus resolution on ultrasonography six days after diagnosis. A 5-year-and-5-month-old boy developed acute left internal carotid-middle cerebral artery occlusion with extensive left hemispheric infarction three days after thoracoscopic resection of pulmonary sequestration. Emergency stent-retriever thrombectomy with aspiration achieved immediate recanalization, which persisted at one week; independent ambulation was restored after rehabilitation, although mild right upper-limb symptoms remained at discharge. A 4-month-old boy developed right frontotemporal-insular ischemic infarction after balloon angioplasty for recurrent aortic coarctation. Because no retrievable intracranial large-vessel occlusion was identified and the recent cardiac intervention increased the bleeding risk, aspirin, low-molecular-weight heparin, and supportive treatment were administered. Follow-up MRI one week after diagnosis showed regression of the initial lesion but revealed a new right thalamic lesion suspicious for acute infarction. These heterogeneous cases highlight the need for prompt vascular imaging and individualized multidisciplinary management based on the vascular territory, threatened tissue, patient size, recent procedures, bleeding risk, and procedural feasibility. As a descriptive case series, this report does not establish the comparative efficacy of the treatment strategies.

title: Functional assessment of CELSR1 variants associated with human developmental defects.
authorString: Stenson JM, Giang W, Latario SG, Williams CL, Trujillo Adorno V, Sha CM, Stahley SN.

journal.title: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

abstractText: During development, collective and oriented cell behaviors that drive organ formation and tissue patterning require coordination among neighboring cells governed by the highly conserved planar cell polarity (PCP) pathway. Deficiencies in PCP gene function result in severe developmental defects in model systems from flies to mice, while PCP gene mutations are associated with human birth defects impacting the neural tube and heart. Atypical cadherin Celsr1 engages in cell-cell adhesion to coordinate the asymmetric localization of Fz6 and Vangl2 to opposing sides of the PCP junction between neighboring cells. However, whether CELSR1 genetic variations disrupt function or contribute to disease pathogenesis remains poorly understood. Using cell-based assays for Celsr1 function, along with in silico modeling, we test a cohort of 17 Celsr1 mutations previously identified in patients with neural tube and congenital heart defects. In junctional enrichment assays, we find 13 variants displayed altered enrichment at cell borders relative to WT, including both loss- and gain-of-function behaviors. Further analysis of select Celsr1 mutations revealed defects in membrane mobility and perturbed co-recruitment of PCP protein Fz6. Our findings link Celsr1 mutations associated with human birth defects to functional defects in adhesion and PCP. In addition, our approach supports a framework for evaluating PCP function alongside genomics and in silico predictions toward understanding the pathophysiology impacts of genetic variations associated with human developmental disorders and gaining insight into Celsr1 function during development.

title: <i>DYRK1A</i> - a gene dose paradox.
authorString: Plećaš A, Gough G, Kunštek S, Babić M, Murray A, Nižetić D, Alić I.

journal.title: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

abstractText: The DYRK1A (Dual-Specificity Tyrosine Phosphorylation-Regulated Kinase 1A) gene is located on human chromosome 21 (HSA21) within the Down Syndrome Critical Region (DSCR). As a protein kinase, DYRK1A is involved in the regulation of the cell cycle, cell growth, transcription, and cellular communication. It also plays essential roles in embryonic and neuronal development, and in disease pathogenesis. Dysregulation of DYRK1A has been associated with several human disorders, including DYRK1A syndrome, caused by DYRK1A haploinsufficiency (i.e., one functional copy of the gene) and Down syndrome (DS), caused by trisomy 21 (i.e., three functional copies of the gene). DYRK1A is an extremely dosage-sensitive gene and is considered one of the "Goldilocks" genes, for which both increased and decreased gene dosage can lead to pathological phenotypes. Interestingly, these two syndromes share several overlapping clinical features. This apparent paradox represents/highlights a major gap in our current understanding of DYRK1A function and raises important biological questions. In this review, we summarise the most important findings related to both DYRK1A syndrome and Down syndrome, as well as the available human cellular and animal models that provide valuable platforms for future research. To obtain a comprehensive understanding of DYRK1A role, it is necessary to integrate data from multiple experimental systems and sources. Such an integrated approach will facilitate the identification of novel therapeutic targets and support the development of treatments that may ultimately advance to clinical trials.

title: Use of intraoperative right ventricular strain as a predictor of outcomes in adult heart transplant patients.
authorString: Bryant J, Settlemire B, Ahmad A, Deegan R, Neumann DA, Sileshi B, Williams A, Bommareddi S, Trahanas J, Schlendorf K, Petrovic M, Wang CC, Kraitem A, Duggal N, Ziegler T, Jhaveri A, Baker M, Pretorius M, Shah A, Jelly CA, Lima B.
abstractText:
Background

Right ventricle (RV) evaluation in the perioperative period is challenging for anesthesiologists, given the limited objective assessment methods available for transesophageal echocardiography (TEE). Speckle-tracking strain imaging may offer a more objective evaluation of RV function. This study evaluated the predictive value of intraoperative RV free wall strain (RVFWS) for early outcomes following orthotopic heart transplantation (OHT).

Methods

This was a single-center retrospective cohort study of 147 adults who underwent isolated OHT between January 2025 and December 2025. Patients with multiorgan transplant, congenital cases, and those without measurable intraoperative RVFWS were excluded. Post-bypass RVFWS was measured using TEE at a single time point with speckle-tracking analysis. The primary outcome was 90-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included severe primary graft dysfunction, 30-day mortality, need for postoperative venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), vasoactive-inotropic score, and cardiac index at 24 and 72 h, and intensive care unit length of stay. Multivariable Firth-penalized logistic and median quantile regressions were used, adjusted for a priori pre-transplant weighted risk score.

Results

The median post-bypass RVFWS was -13.9% IQR (interquartile range) -19.3 to -9.6. Fourteen recipients (9.5%) died within 90 days of transplantation. After adjusting for the pre-transplant risk score, RVFWS was independently associated with higher 90-day mortality [odds ratio (OR) 2.84 per 5% decrease in magnitude, 95% confidence interval 1.65-5.58; p < 0.001]. Among the secondary outcomes, the associations with severe primary graft dysfunction (OR 2.70; raw p = 0.001), CRRT (OR 1.58; raw p = 0.001), and 30-day mortality (OR 2.94; raw p = 0.002) remained statistically significant after Bonferroni adjustment for eleven secondary comparisons (adjusted p = 0.011, 0.011, and 0.022, respectively). RVFWS demonstrated higher discrimination for 90-day mortality [area under the curve (AUC) 0.83] than qualitative intraoperative RV grading (AUC 0.68), although this difference in AUC did not reach statistical significance. RVFWS retained independent prognostic value in a combined model.

Conclusions

Intraoperative post-bypass RVFWS is a feasible and objective intraoperative measure that is independently associated with early adverse outcomes after adult OHT. RVFWS shows promise as a signal of early allograft dysfunction that is not fully explained by pre-transplant risk factors.

title: Case Report: Concurrent ventricular septal defect, pulmonic stenosis, and intrapulmonary arteriovenous anastomoses in a Korean raccoon dog (<i>Nyctereutes procyonoides koreensis</i>).
authorString: Kim S, Kim M, Han JI, Lee K, Yoon H.
abstractText: A 3-month-old intact male Korean raccoon dog (Nyctereutes procyonoides koreensis) was rescued and admitted to the Jeonbuk Wildlife Rescue Center with lethargy, dehydration, and dermatologic lesions consistent with Sarcoptes scabiei infestation. Physical examination detected a grade IV/VI systolic murmur, and thoracic radiography revealed generalized cardiomegaly. Transthoracic echocardiography identified a perimembranous ventricular septal defect (VSD) with left-to-right shunting. Although no distinct structural abnormalities of the pulmonic valve were observed, increased pulmonic flow velocity (3.87 m/s), mild pulmonic regurgitation (1.68 m/s), and post-stenotic dilation of the main pulmonary artery supported a diagnosis of pulmonic stenosis (PS). Agitated saline contrast echocardiography demonstrated intrapulmonary arteriovenous anastomoses (IPAVAs), with microbubbles appearing in the left heart after the fourth cardiac cycle; this shunting decreased following oxygen supplementation. Five weeks later, thoracic radiography demonstrated a reduction in cardiac silhouette size, although cardiomegaly persisted. Echocardiography demonstrated progression of the VSD to bidirectional shunting. Systolic doming of the pulmonic valve, together with increased pulmonic flow velocity (4.39 m/s) and pulmonic regurgitation velocity (2.07 m/s), indicated worsening PS. Repeat agitated saline contrast echocardiography revealed microbubbles in the left heart within four cardiac cycles and in the abdominal aorta, indicating a right-to-left shunt component consistent with bidirectional shunting. These findings were attenuated after oxygen supplementation. The Korean raccoon dog subsequently died during anesthetic induction for further diagnostic imaging. Postmortem examination confirmed a perimembranous VSD and type A valvular PS characterized by fused commissures, with concurrent right ventricular hypertrophy, dilation, and interventricular septal thickening. To our knowledge, this case report is the first to describe the concurrence of VSD, PS, and IPAVAs in a Korean raccoon dog. It suggests that progressive PS may contribute to reversal of shunting across a VSD.

title: The role of vascular pathology in SMA: implications for pathogenesis and treatment.
authorString: Parson SH, Allardyce H.
abstractText: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) has become a paradigm for precision medicine following the development of transformative therapies targeting the disease-causing deficiency of survival motor neuron (SMN) protein. As more than 98% of SMA cases arise from mutations in the SMN1 gene, restoration of SMN expression through nusinersen (Spinraza; Biogen, Cambridge, MA), risdiplam (Evrysdi; Roche, Basel, Switzerland) and onasemnogene abeparvovec (Zolgensma and Itvisma; AveXis, Novartis, Chicago, IL) has produced unprecedented clinical benefits and established SMA as the first treatable motor neuron disease. To date, therapeutic success has focused on rescuing motor neurons, the principal site of clinical pathology. However, growing evidence indicates that SMA is a multisystem disorder in which pathological changes extend beyond the motor unit. In particular, vascular pathology has emerged as a recurring feature across numerous affected tissues. Vascular abnormalities have been identified throughout the neuromuscular system, including the spinal cord and skeletal muscle, as well as in systemic organs such as the heart, kidney, gastrointestinal tract and spleen. Experimental studies suggest that endothelial dysfunction is a direct consequence of SMN deficiency, impairing angiogenesis, vascular maturation and vessel stability, while patient-derived biomarkers, including retinal vascular imaging and elevated circulating endothelial cells (CEC), provide evidence of ongoing endothelial dysfunction in patients. These vascular abnormalities have the potential to compromise tissue perfusion, promote local hypoxia, disrupt barrier integrity and enhance inflammatory signaling, thereby exacerbating disease progression. Collectively, the evidence suggests that SMN-dependent vascular pathology may represent an under-recognized feature of SMA pathogenesis and a potential therapeutic target. Here, we review the current evidence for vascular pathology in SMA, discuss its implications for disease progression, long-term patient outcomes and therapeutic response, and consider whether vascular abnormalities are adequately addressed by existing SMN-restorative therapies.

title: Pregnant women's perceived understanding and antenatal information needs regarding newborn screening for inherited metabolic diseases in southwestern China: a cross-sectional study.
authorString: Yang H, He F, Xia D, Wang X, Liu H.
abstractText:
Background

Newborn screening (NBS) can reduce morbidity from some inherited metabolic diseases (IMDs) through early detection and timely treatment. Clear antenatal communication can support informed participation and timely follow-up by helping parents understand the purpose and pathway of screening. Evidence on pregnant women's perceived understanding, attitudes, antenatal information engagement, and screening- and follow-up-related intentions regarding newborn IMD screening in China remains limited. This study described these four domains and examined their associations with sociodemographic and reproductive-history characteristics in southwestern China.

Methods

This hospital-based cross-sectional survey used a purposive sample recruited at a tertiary women's and children's hospital (National Regional Medical Center in China) from January 2024 to December 2024. After data-quality review, 1,320 eligible records were analyzed. All 21 questionnaire items were retained and analyzed as four domains: perceived understanding, attitudes, antenatal information engagement, and screening/follow-up intentions. Internal consistency, post hoc exploratory factor analysis, Pearson correlations, and four fully adjusted linear models with HC3 robust standard errors were evaluated. Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction was applied across 92 non-intercept coefficients.

Results

Parallel analysis supported four factors (Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin = 0.912; Bartlett χ2 = 21,719.21, p < 0.001), explaining 67.5% of variance. Mean (SD) scores were 15.15 (4.54)/35 for perceived understanding, 25.43 (3.77)/30 for attitudes, 9.34 (2.31)/15 for antenatal information engagement, and 20.09 (3.16)/25 for intentions; Cronbach's α values were 0.918, 0.950, 0.745, and 0.914. Fifteen coefficients had nominal p < 0.05, but none remained significant after FDR correction (all q ≥ 0.051); adjusted R2 values were 0.010-0.039.

Conclusion

Participants reported limited self-perceived understanding alongside favorable attitudes, moderate antenatal information engagement, and strong stated intentions. Adjusted R2 values of 0.010-0.039 and the absence of FDR-significant predictors indicate that the measured sociodemographic and reproductive-history variables had negligible explanatory value and should not be used for subgroup prediction or targeting. The domain pattern supports universal, nursing-led antenatal communication focused on screening procedures, abnormal-result interpretation, recall, confirmation, and follow-up, while future work should refine the questionnaire and test whether education improves observed participation and follow-up.

title: A predictive model based on maternal immune-inflammatory markers for ARDS identification in mechanically ventilated late-preterm and term neonates.
authorString: Zhang C, Jing H, Xu D, Gao Z, Diao K, Yang X, Ji Y, Yin H, Han T, Wu S.
abstractText:
Objective

To develop and internally evaluate a model that uses maternal blood markers obtained before delivery to differentiate neonatal acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) from other causes of respiratory distress in late-preterm and term neonates requiring mechanical ventilation.

Methods

This retrospective study enrolled 227 mother-infant pairs from two tertiary hospitals between June 2024 and January 2026. Neonates born at 34-40 weeks' gestation with ventilation-dependent respiratory distress were divided into a training cohort and an internal test cohort. Predictors were screened using elastic-net regression with 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Four feature sets and six algorithms were then compared by 20 repeats of stratified five-fold cross-validation, and a six-predictor random forest (RF) was ultimately selected. Discrimination, calibration and net benefit were assessed, with 500-resample bootstrap optimism correction and Shapley additive explanation (SHAP) interpretation.

Results

Maternal systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) and related inflammatory ratios were higher, and antenatal infection was more frequent, in the ARDS group, whereas recorded antenatal corticosteroid (ACS) use was less frequent (P < 0.001). Six predictors were retained in the final model: SII, antenatal infection, maternal age, gestational hypothyroidism, gestational diabetes mellitus and ACS use. The principal internal performance estimate, the mean training-set cross-validated area under the curve (AUC) was 0.729 ± 0.080, the fixed-pipeline optimism-corrected AUC was 0.793 and the internal test-set AUC was 0.827 (95% CI, 0.712-0.923), with an average precision of 0.828 and a Brier score of 0.175. These three values are not interchangeable and are reported as one principal and two secondary estimates, and none represents fully independent performance. At the training-derived threshold of 0.424, sensitivity was 78.8% and specificity 77.8%. SHAP identified SII as the largest contributor, without implying a causal effect for any predictor. Logistic regression using the same six predictors reached a numerically higher internal test-set AUC (0.838 versus 0.827, ΔAUC = -0.011, P = 0.744) and a cross-validated AUC of 0.706 ± 0.082 versus 0.729 ± 0.080, the RF therefore conferred no discriminative advantage.

Conclusions

In mechanical ventilation needed neonates born at 34-40 weeks' gestation with respiratory distress, the six-predictor RF showed moderate discrimination, whereas evidence of adequate calibration was limited. The model remains preliminary and requires external validation, recalibration and prospective clinical-impact evaluation before clinical use.

title: Case Report A Rare Cause of Cardiofaciocutaneous Syndrome-KRAS p.Pro34arg: Clinical Delineation, Diagnostic Challenges, and Implications for RASopathy Classification.
authorString: Mérida De Ia Torre FJ, Coll Vidal M, Rubio Martínez I, Quintana Tello L, Brugada Terradellas R.
abstractText: Background and Clinical Significance: Cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome (CFC) is a rare autosomal dominant RASopathy characterized by craniofacial dysmorphism, congenital heart defects, cutaneous abnormalities, growth impairment, and neurodevelopmental delay. Pathogenic variants in KRAS account for a minority of cases and define cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome type 2 (CFC2). Establishing a molecular diagnosis is often challenging because of the substantial clinical overlap among RASopathies, including Noonan and Costello syndromes. Case Presentation: We describe a one-year-old boy presenting with macrocephaly, ventriculomegaly, hypotonia, developmental delay, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, gastroesophageal reflux, and mild dermatological abnormalities. To clarify the diagnosis, a custom next-generation sequencing panel targeting RASopathy-associated genes was performed. Genetic analysis identified a heterozygous KRAS variant, NM_033360.4:c.101C>G, p.(Pro34Arg), which was confirmed by Sanger sequencing and shown to have arisen de novo through parental testing. Additional variants of uncertain significance were detected in ABCC9, CACNA1G, and DES; however, these were considered unlikely to account for the phenotype because of limited clinical concordance and current ACMG/AMP classification. The KRAS variant was classified as pathogenic based on its de novo occurrence, absence from population databases, localization within a critical functional domain, supportive computational evidence, and previously reported pathogenic substitutions affecting the same residue. Conclusions: This case provides additional evidence supporting the pathogenicity of KRAS p.(Pro34Arg), a variant reported only rarely in association with CFC. The observed phenotype further expands the clinical spectrum of KRAS-associated CFC and highlights the value of comprehensive molecular testing for the differential diagnosis of RASopathies and the refinement of genotype-phenotype correlations.

title: Autologous Platelet-Rich Plasma Decreases Intraoperative Allogeneic Transfusion in Cyanotic Patients Undergoing Cardiac Surgery.
authorString: Li H, Li H.

journal.title: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia

abstractText:
Objectives

To evaluate the effect of autologous platelet-rich plasma (aPRP) on perioperative allogeneic blood product transfusion requirement in patients undergoing cyanotic congenital heart disease (CCHD) surgery and patients' prognosis.

Design

A retrospective cohort study.

Setting

A tertiary university hospital.

Participants

A total of 95 patients with CCHD who underwent cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) between January 2020 and August 2025 were included, of whom 81 (85.3%) underwent redo operation.

Interventions

Patients were divided into the aPRP group and the control group according to whether aPRP apheresis was employed. In the aPRP group, aPRP was harvested after anesthesia and transfused back to the patient after protamine neutralization, whereas the concurrently collected concentrated red blood cells (cRBCs) were reinfused during CPB or chest closure (from weaning from CPB to skin closure).

Measurements and main results

In the original cohort, the aPRP group had significantly lower packed red blood cell (PRBC) transfusion rates, as well as PRBC and fresh-frozen plasma (FFP) transfusion volume, than the control group. After propensity score matching, the intraoperative PRBC transfusion rate no longer differed significantly between groups (aPRP v control: 17.4% v 43.5%, p = 0.180). However, the PRBC transfusion volume remained significantly lower in the aPRP group, both as total volume (0 [0, 0] v 0 [0, 400] mL; p = 0.037) and as weight-adjusted volume (0 [0, 0] v 0 [0, 15.7] mL/kg; p = 0.045). The matched intraoperative FFP transfusion requirements were also significantly reduced in the aPRP group (200 [0, 600] v 600 [400, 1,000] mL, p < 0.05). Viscoelastic testing indicated significantly improved coagulation and platelet function following aPRP administration in the treatment group. No difference in intraoperative blood loss, postoperative allogeneic blood products, 24-hour chest tube drainage, use of coagulation agents, postoperative ventilation time, or intensive care unit stay was observed.

Conclusions

In a predominantly redo cohort of patients with CCHD undergoing cardiac surgery, the use of aPRP was associated with reduced intraoperative allogeneic blood and plasma transfusion requirements, and it also effectively preserved hemostatic function in these patients. However, the reduction in allogeneic product use may not be primarily due to the preserved hemostatic function conferred by aPRP but rather to autologous substitution of allogeneic products.

title: Association of Enteral Chloral Hydrate with Benzodiazepine Exposure and Delirium After Pediatric Cardiac Surgery: A Retrospective Before-and-After Cohort Study.
authorString: Ozden O, Yakici AE, Isik E, Kabadayi B, Balkan B, Kizilkaya MH, Bicer M, Odemis E, Tanyildiz M.

journal.title: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia

abstractText:
Objectives

To evaluate the association between the addition of enteral chloral hydrate to a postoperative sedation protocol and benzodiazepine exposure, sedation quality, withdrawal, delirium, and short-term clinical outcomes in children undergoing congenital heart surgery.

Design

Single-center retrospective before-and-after cohort study.

Setting

Pediatric cardiac intensive care unit of a tertiary referral center.

Participants

Eighty-six children who underwent congenital heart surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass, required postoperative mechanical ventilation for more than 24 hours, and received sedation for at least 24 hours.

Interventions

Patients were treated according to the institutional postoperative sedation protocol before (July 2021-June 2023) and after (August 2023-July 2025) implementation of enteral chloral hydrate as an adjunctive sedative.

Measurements and main results

The primary endpoint was cumulative midazolam exposure during the pediatric cardiac intensive care unit stay. Secondary endpoints included sedative and analgesic requirements, sedation and pain scores, withdrawal, delirium, and clinical outcomes. Compared with the preprotocol group, the chloral hydrate group had significantly lower cumulative midazolam exposure (10.2 v 13.2 mg/kg, p = 0.010) and peak midazolam infusion rates (0.15 v 0.20 mg/kg/h, p < 0.001), and a lower observed frequency of delirium (14.6% v 37.8%, p = 0.015). No significant between-group differences were observed in sedation quality, pain scores, withdrawal, duration of mechanical ventilation, length of stay in the pediatric cardiac intensive care unit or hospital, or mortality.

Conclusion

Addition of enteral chloral hydrate to a postoperative sedation protocol was associated with reduced benzodiazepine exposure and a lower observed frequency of delirium without statistically significant differences in sedation quality or short-term clinical outcomes. Prospective multicenter studies are warranted to confirm these findings.

title: Early Prediction of Cardiomyopathy in Pediatric Cancer Survivors Using Echocardiographic Video-Based Deep Learning.
authorString: Sharma S, Martinez Di Pietro B, Nandula A, Goplani T, Chen H, Armenian S, Bhat A, Blythe N, Border W, Leger KJ, Leisenring WM, Meacham LR, Narasimhan S, Nathan PC, Sachdeva R, Sadak K, Stratton K, Chow EJ, Edwards LA, Boyle PM.
abstractText:
Purpose

Cardiomyopathy (CM) is a leading cause of late mortality in childhood cancer survivors, but it is often identified only after irreversible cardiac remodeling has already occurred. In this proof-of-concept study, we assessed whether deep learning applied to routine echocardiographic videos can identify features predictive of future CM.

Methods

We analyzed parasternal short-axis clips from cancer survivors ≤21 years old at cancer diagnosis. 3D deep convolutional neural networks were trained to classify CM-positive versus CM-negative studies from echocardiograms conducted up to five years prior to CM diagnosis. The performance was assessed on internal hold-out validation (Center 1) and external validation cohorts (Centers 2, 3). The model's prognostic value was evaluated by stratifying patients into high- and low-risk groups for developing CM, and probability of future CM was assessed using cumulative incidence and proportional hazards regression analysis.

Results

The model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.87±0.05 and an area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.74±0.07 on the internal hold-out set. External validation showed near-chance single-study discrimination (AUROC 0.55±0.02 and 0.60±0.03; AUPRC 0.22±0.02 and 0.21±0.03 for Centers 2 and 3, respectively). Nevertheless, analysis of the external cohort showed significantly higher probability of CM in high- versus low-risk groups (hazard ratio 2.78, 95% CI = 1.52-5.10, p = 0.00056).

Conclusion

Deep learning models have the potential to identify subtle echocardiographic markers years before CM diagnosis in pediatric cancer survivors and could serve as a preliminary step toward risk-guided CM surveillance. Further refinement and validation are needed to determine the utility of deep learning for early identification of pathologic cardiac remodeling in this population.

title: Recanalisation quality, not first-pass effect, drives outcomes in paediatric mechanical thrombectomy: a multicentre prospective study.
authorString: Dmytriw AA, Kiani I, Bhatia K, Abruzzo T, Pabst L, Fraser S, Chung MG, Lo W, Othmann A, Steinmetz S, Jensen-Kondering U, Schob S, Kaiser DPO, Marik W, Wendl C, Kleffner I, Henkes H, Kraehling H, Nguyen-Kim TDL, Chapot R, Yilmaz U, Wang F, Ubaid Hafeez M, Requejo F, Limbucci N, Kauffmann B, Möhlenbruch M, Nikoubashman O, Schellinger PD, Dugar F, Musolino P, Alawieh A, Wilson J, Grieb D, Gersing AS, Liebig T, Olivieri M, Paulasova Schwabova J, Tomek A, Papanagiotou P, Boulouis G, Naggara O, Fox CK, Orlov K, Kuznetsova A, Parra-Farinas C, Muthusami P, Regenhardt RW, Martinez ML, Brechbühl D, Steinlin M, Sun LR, Hassan AE, Guenego A, Molyneux A, Kemmling A, Lee S, Fullerton HJ, Fiehler J, Psychogios MN, Wildgruber M, Sporns PB, Save Child S Pro Investigators.
abstractText:
Introduction

In adult endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), first-pass success is associated with better outcomes, but whether this "first-pass effect" also holds true in childhood stroke remains unknown. We investigated the association of thrombectomy pass counts with 90-day outcomes after paediatric EVT.

Patients and methods

We analysed prospectively collected data from the international Save ChildS Pro registry (ages 0-17 years). All EVT-treated patients were included irrespective of the reperfusion grade achieved. Successful reperfusion was defined as expanded thrombolysis in cerebral infarction (eTICI) ≥ 2b and complete/near-complete reperfusion as eTICI 2c-3. The primary outcome was ordinal 90-day mRS in a proportional odds model. Single-pass and multiple-pass patients were then compared with each other within the subgroup achieving eTICI 2c-3. Logistic regression for mRS > 2 was fitted with pass count and eTICI grade as covariates.

Results

Of 103 patients (median age 11 years [IQR 6-15]; 55/102 [53.9%] male), median passes were 2 (IQR 1-3); 39 (37.9%) had 1 pass, 61 (59.2%) more than 1 and 3 (2.9%) recanalised without a thrombectomy pass. Multiple passes were associated with lower eTICI 2c-3 rates (30.0% vs 82.1%; P < .001), and worse 90-day mRS (common odds ratio 3.47; 95% CI, 1.63-7.38; P = .001). However, among patients achieving eTICI 2c-3 (n = 50), we detected no difference by pass count (mRS 0-2: 93.8% vs 94.4%; risk difference - 0.6%, 95% CI, -15% to +20%; P = 1.000). After accounting for eTICI, pass count was not independently associated with mRS > 2, while eTICI remained significant.

Conclusions

In this analysis of the first-pass effect in paediatric thrombectomy, multiple passes were associated with worse functional outcomes, but this effect appeared to be largely mediated through recanalisation quality. Subgroup analyses were underpowered to exclude a clinically relevant residual effect of pass count, and these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating.

title: Fetal Echocardiography After a Normal Anatomy Assessment: A Retrospective Cohort of In Vitro Fertilization Pregnancies.
authorString: Dickson B, Maher H, Maynard S, Scalf R, Sundlof M, Tessier KM, Peck D, Ambrose M, Jones CW.
abstractText:
Purpose

To investigate the detection rate of congenital heart disease (CHD) on fetal echocardiogram after a normal and complete detailed fetal ultrasound among pregnancies conceived by in vitro fertilization (IVF).

Methods

This retrospective cohort study examined singleton IVF pregnancies that underwent a detailed fetal anatomic survey without any identified abnormalities, followed by fetal echocardiogram. The primary outcome was the rate of CHD diagnosis after normal and complete anatomic ultrasound. Patients with multifetal gestation, pre-gestational diabetes, a known family history of CHD, fetal abnormalities on anatomy ultrasound, or patients who had an incomplete initial anatomy ultrasound were excluded. Prenatal CHD was confirmed with neonatal imaging and infants were followed after birth.

Results

300 pregnancies were included, and of these 266 had a normal and complete anatomy ultrasound. 1.5% (n = 4) of pregnancies had minor CHD identified on fetal echocardiography which was not identified on the anatomy ultrasound. None of the infants required cardiac-related interventions in the first year of life.

Conclusion

No major CHD was identified at fetal echocardiography after a normal and complete anatomic survey. Our results support the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine guidelines that state a dedicated fetal echocardiogram may be considered, but is not recommended, for singleton IVF pregnancies.

title: DNA methylation analysis of aortic wall tissue in ascending aortic dilatation/aneurysm and dissection.
authorString: Goncharova IA, Zarubin AA, Markov AV, Shipulina SA, Babushkina NP, Koroleva IA, Sleptcov AA, Nazarenko MS.
abstractText: Ascending aortic dilatation/aneurysm and dissection are life-threatening cardiovascular conditions. However, the epigenetic regulatory mechanisms within aortic cells underlying these pathologies remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify differentially methylated genes (DMGs) in aortic tissues from patients with ascending aortic dilatation/aneurysm and dissection by performing a re-analysis of publicly available DNA methylation datasets. A re-analysis was conducted on three DNA methylation datasets (GSE50192, GSE202047, GSE84274) from the Illumina Infinium HumanMethylation450 BeadChip. To account for tissue heterogeneity, cellular deconvolution was performed using the HEpiDISH algorithm and a custom reference panel of cell-type-specific CpG sites for key vascular cell types (endothelial cells, fibroblasts, smooth muscle cells, immune cells). Our re-analysis revealed that aortic dissection and bicuspid aortic valve patients with aortic dilatation/aneurysm exhibit distinct DNA methylation profiles compared to intact aorta. These pathologies differ from each other in the number and the spectrum of DMGs. The adjustment for cellular heterogeneity eliminated the majority of the initially identified DMGs. However, this correction helped to make an assessment of vascular inflammation, characterize its impact on aortic wall stability, and identify genes with differential DNA methylation associated with the disease phenotypes, rather than with inter-group heterogeneity. The genes NFIX, PCDH7, MED13L, LMO4, DIP2C, PLEKHF1, NKD1, C10orf41 (ZNF503-AS2), ARAP2, TBX3, and TBX5, which remained in the DMG status after adjustment for cellular composition and are expressed in individual cells/whole aortic tissue, can be considered as new candidate genes for the development of aortic dilatation/aneurysm in patients with bicuspid aortic valve. NFIX, LMO4, DIP2C, C10orf41 (ZNF503- AS2), MED13L, TBX3, TBX5 are transcriptional regulators or modulators; NKD1 is a recognized inhibitor of the Wnt pathway. Our findings highlight the necessity of a rigorous approach to cohort design, which includes comprehensive phenotyping (encompassing aortic valve morphology) and underscore the importance of future single-cell investigations.

title: The Current Perspective, Ethical Considerations, and a Position Statement on Expanded Newborn Screening from the College of Paediatrics, Academy of Medicine of Malaysia.
authorString: Khoo EJ, Thong MK, Yong SC, Chee SC, Lee JKF, Teh SH, Taib F, Ali A, Cheah FC.
abstractText: Newborn screening (NBS) is an essential public health intervention for early detection and secondary prevention of inherited disorders in asymptomatic infants at birth. Advances in this field and the accessibility of new screening methods and therapies in the last decade have insurmountably surpassed Malaysia's national NBS programme, which has stagnated. Currently, our mandatory nationwide routine screening is limited to only two conditions: glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency and congenital hypothyroidism. While services such as universal newborn hearing and critical congenital heart disease screening are available in many settings, most treatable genetic and metabolic disorders remain unscreened. Consequently, preventable morbidity and mortality, from inborn errors of immunity and metabolism, and genetic diseases persist. This position statement reviews the evidence for expanding the national NBS programme in Malaysia, arguing that a modernised, contemporary and pragmatic method is both clinically tenable and morally imperative. By embracing advancements for expanded NBS, Malaysia can safeguard children's right to an open future, fulfil intergenerational justice, and ensure that no infant is left without the opportunity for life-saving care.

title: Multi-Trait GWAS Analyses of Blood Pressure Traits Provide Limited Gains in Locus Discovery or Polygenic Risk Score Performance Compared to Single-Trait GWAS.
authorString: Ma Y, Argoty-Pantoja AD, Xie T, Barnes MR, Munroe PB, Cabrera CP, Snieder H, Warren HR, UMCG Genetics Lifelines Initiative (UGLI) group author: LifeLines Cohort Study.
abstractText: High blood pressure (BP) represents a major cause of life-threatening cardiovascular conditions. GWAS have identified >2000 BP-associated signals. BP-GWAS usually analyze each BP trait individually. However, multi-trait GWAS may yield novel loci and improve polygenic risk scores (PRS) prediction. We explored whether multi-trait BP-GWAS can: (i) find novel loci undetected by single-trait GWAS; (ii) increase heritability estimates; (iii) improve PRS prediction of hypertension within the Lifelines Cohort Study. We investigate the utility of multi-trait GWAS approaches of correlated BP traits (systolic BP, diastolic BP, pulse pressure). We tested two multi-trait methods inputting results from the latest N > 1 million single-trait BP-GWAS: (a) Multi-Trait Analysis of GWAS (MTAG); (b) genomic structural equation modeling (GenomicSEM); and compared results with single-trait results. We only identified one novel locus from multi-trait GWAS: ZNF268. Neither heritability estimates nor PRS performance improved using multi-trait GWAS. In this scenario of complete sample overlap across BP-GWAS, we observed little gain in results from multi-trait BP-GWAS over single-trait BP-GWAS. Our findings quantify the limited benefit of multi-trait methods under this specific setting. Future BP genetic discoveries are more likely to come from larger GWAS adding new cohort data. However, conclusions may differ for other traits, depending on trait-specific genetic architecture.

title: Predictors and Patterns of Metastatic Candidozyma auris Infection, Spain, 2016-2024.
authorString: Suarez-Urquiza P, Ruiz-Gaitán A, Calabuig E, Tasias M, Bustos VG, Moreno I, Ferre MÁ, Moret AM, Frasquet J, Favier P, Pemán J, Castaño-Aroca MJ, Brell PM, Gordon M, Gomez-Ruiz MD, Salavert-Lleti M.
abstractText: Metastatic infection after Candidozyma auris candidemia remains poorly characterized. We retrospectively studied patients with C. auris candidemia at a tertiary hospital in Spain during 2016-2024. Of 108 patients, 24 (22.2%) experienced metastatic infections; endocarditis was most frequent (7.4%), followed by osteoarticular infection, meningitis, and hepatosplenic infection (3.7% each). In multivariable Fine-Gray regression, a cardiac device or prosthetic valve was independently associated with metastatic infection (subdistribution hazard ratio [HR] 2.89 [95% CI 1.21-6.91]), although that association was attenuated in a sensitivity analysis restricted to echocardiographed patients. Persistent candidemia showed a higher, nonsignificant risk for metastatic infection in the day-5 landmark analysis (subdistribution HR 2.67 [95% CI 0.86-8.32]). Metastatic infection was associated with increased deaths in time-dependent analyses at 60 days (adjusted HR 2.21 [95% CI 1.04-4.67]) and 90 days (adjusted HR 2.26 [95% CI 1.09-4.67]). Our findings support echocardiography in patients with intracardiac devices.

title: Invasive Enterovirus and Parechovirus Infections in Adults, Alberta, Canada, 2023-2025.
authorString: Kanji JN, Zhou HY, Zelyas N, Pabbaraju K, Wong A, Gill K, Lynch T, Tipples G, Nathoo N, Kabbani D, Adatia A.
abstractText: We conducted a retrospective, population-based laboratory surveillance study during May 2023-December 2025 in Alberta, Canada, to characterize adult invasive enterovirus and parechovirus infections and to identify groups at high risk for those infections. Of 15,621 samples tested, 162 (1.0%) were virus positive, of which 51 (31.5%) samples from 39 patients indicated invasive infections. Cerebrospinal fluid, blood, and cardiac tissue were the most frequent virus-positive specimens. The invasive enterovirus and parechovirus incidence rate was 0.37 cases/100,000 person-years; rates were higher in patients <50 versus >50 years of age (incidence rate ratio 8.2; p<0.001). The annual incidence rates were 0.20-0.56 cases/100,000 person-years; rates appeared higher in 2025 than in 2024 (incidence rate ratio 2.1; p = 0.11). Severe disseminated enterovirus infection occurred in 2 patients who received ocrelizumab. Continuous surveillance and ongoing optimization of enterovirus and parechovirus detection assays is essential for comprehensive public health tracking.

title: Sex-Specific Prevalence and Distribution of Electrocardiographic Variants in Healthy Vietnamese Freshmen.
authorString: Ngoc TN, Minh QN, Thu ABT, Tien TV, Thu SH, Cao CD, Hoai VN, Thanh CN, Van BT, The AD.

journal.title: Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc

abstractText:
Background

Data on ECG characteristics and qualitative ECG variants in healthy young Vietnamese adults remain limited. We evaluated sex-specific ECG differences and factors independently associated with common ECG variants in first-year Vietnamese university students.

Methods

This cross-sectional study included 6099 healthy students (3440 female [56.4%], 2659 male [43.6%]; mean age, 17.85 ± 0.65 years) undergoing standardized cardiovascular screening. Resting 12-lead ECGs were analyzed for quantitative parameters and qualitative variants.

Results

All four core ECG parameters differed by sex (all p < 0.001). Females had higher heart rates (84.64 vs. 81.55 bpm) and longer QTc intervals (423.54 vs. 406.46 ms), whereas males had longer PR intervals (141.99 vs. 138.99 ms) and wider QRS complexes (91.44 vs. 80.81 ms). Males had higher prevalences of sinus arrhythmia (22.7% vs. 19.2%), early repolarization pattern (6.1% vs. 0.1%), right bundle branch block (4.4% vs. 0.3%), and sinus bradycardia (4.5% vs. 1.3%; all p < 0.001). Male sex was independently associated with early repolarization pattern (aOR, 37.7; 95% CI, 17.2-107) and right bundle branch block (aOR, 13.1; 95% CI, 7.55-25.2; both p < 0.001), but not sinus arrhythmia (aOR, 1.01; 95% CI, 0.84-1.21; p = 0.896).

Conclusions

ECG parameters and several qualitative variants differed by sex. These findings provide descriptive, population-specific data on ECG characteristics and common qualitative variants in healthy young Vietnamese university students.

title: Apparent mineralocorticoid excess mimicking Bartter syndrome in infancy.
authorString: Hatipoğlu S, Yıldırım E, Şalbaş ÖY, Şahin KC, Kaygusuz G, Yildiz G, Bayram MT, Demir K, Soylu A.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

abstractText:
Objectives

Apparent mineralocorticoid excess (AME) syndrome is a rare monogenic disorder caused by loss-of-function variants in the HSD11B2 gene encoding 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 (11β-HSD2). Deficient enzyme activity results in cortisol-mediated activation of the mineralocorticoid receptor, leading to low-renin hypertension.
