Because affected infants frequently present with polyuria and hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, AME syndrome is often misdiagnosed as Bartter syndrome, resulting in significant diagnostic delay.

Case presentation

A 13-month-old girl presented with polyuria, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, hypercalciuria, and failure to thrive and was initially managed as Bartter syndrome. During follow-up, persistent hypertension accompanied by markedly suppressed plasma renin activity and aldosterone levels prompted evaluation for monogenic hypertension. Urinary steroid analysis demonstrated a markedly reduced cortisone-to-cortisol ratio (0.02), consistent with 11β-HSD2 deficiency. Next-generation sequencing of the HSD11B2 gene identified a homozygous likely pathogenic splice-site variant, c.665-1G>A, confirming the diagnosis of AME syndrome. Treatment with spironolactone, amlodipine, potassium supplementation, and dietary salt restriction achieved blood pressure control and improved electrolyte abnormalities.

Conclusions

AME syndrome should be included in the differential diagnosis of infants presenting with hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis and polyuria, particularly when hypertension is detected. Systematic blood pressure assessment is essential in this clinical context, as early recognition of this monogenic disorder may prevent long-term cardiovascular and renal complications.

title: Impact of colchicine on cardiovascular outcomes in acute coronary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis
authorString: Lanari VC, Jha A, Paudel N, Saddique MN, Bashir MA, Bakry NS, Javaid H, Gill OA, Ali MF, Malik MA, Khan AA, Krasuski RA, Sarwar AH.
abstractText: Background: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains a major contributor to global mortality and long-term cardiovascular risk despite optimal treatment. Colchicine, an anti-inflammatory agent, has gained attention for its potential benefits in ACS. This meta-analysis evaluates its safety and impact on major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) levels, and cardiac function in ACS patients. Methods: We performed a systematic literature search of randomized controlled trials on PubMed (MEDLINE), Embase, and Scopus databases from inception to January 1st, 2025. We pooled dichotomous outcomes as risk ratios (RR) and continuous outcomes as mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals, using random-effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 and X2 statistics. Statistical significance was defined by a p-value <0.05. Analyses were performed with RevMan 5.4. Results: The meta-analysis included 18 RCTs involving 14,688 patients (7,336 receiving colchicine and 7,352 controls). 11,742 (79.94%) were men and mean age was 59.8±8.8 years. Compared to placebo, colchicine reduced the rate of MACE (RR=0.74, 95%CI:0.60 to 0.92), even when examined after 1 or more years of therapy (RR 0.83, 95%CI:0.70 to 0.98), reduced hsCRP levels (MD -0.80, 95%CI:-1.34 to -0.27), and improved left ventricular ejection fraction (MD 1.13, 95%CI:0.25 to 2.02]). While no increase in overall adverse events was seen with colchicine (RR 1.00, 95% CI: 0.95 to 1.06), diarrhea occurred more frequently (RR=1.52, 95%CI: 1.03 to 2.24). Conclusion: Colchicine appears safe and may improve long-term outcomes in ACS patients. However, larger studies with more extended follow-up are needed for definitive evidence.

title: Intravenous Iron Supplementation in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Systematic Review.
authorString: Sheriff A, Qin AR, Sheriff A.
abstractText: Iron deficiency affects approximately half of patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and impairs functional capacity, yet evidence for intravenous (IV) iron in this population is limited. We evaluated the effect of IV iron on functional, biochemical, biomarker, and clinical outcomes in HFpEF. This systematic review followed PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 and was prospectively registered [International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) CRD420261360828]. Four databases were searched on April 11, 2026. Eligible studies enrolled adults with HFpEF and iron deficiency receiving IV iron, with at least 4 weeks of follow-up. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias. Because few studies were eligible and heterogeneity was substantial, findings were synthesized narratively without meta-analysis in accordance with the synthesis without meta-analysis guideline, and certainty was rated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation framework. Seven reports of 6 studies were included: 1 randomized trial, 2 controlled observational studies, and 3 single-arm before-after studies. Across studies, IV iron consistently increased ferritin, transferrin saturation, and hemoglobin. The randomized trial improved 6-minute walking distance but not functional class or quality of life, and was stopped early. Effects on natriuretic peptide concentrations were inconsistent. The 2 controlled studies disagreed on clinical events: a propensity-matched analysis reported fewer hospitalizations, whereas a registry found no benefit. Certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate. In HFpEF, IV iron reliably corrects iron indices, but a clinical benefit remains unproven, and the evidence base is sparse and largely uncontrolled. Adequately powered randomized trials are required.

title: Dose-Response Associations of Exercise Modalities With Cardiorespiratory Fitness in Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Zhang W, Du M, Zhan Y, Zhang Z, Chen L, Dong J.
abstractText: Exercise training improves cardiorespiratory fitness in patients with heart failure, yet the dose-response relationship across different exercise modalities remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of different exercise modalities and their standardized doses on peak oxygen uptake (VO2peak) in patients with heart failure. We systematically searched multiple databases from inception through March 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing exercise interventions with controls. Exercise modalities were categorized as interval aerobic training (IAT), continuous aerobic training (CAT), resistance training (RT), mind-body training (MBT), and their combinations. Exercise dose was uniformly quantified as weekly metabolic equivalents (MET-min/week). A Bayesian model-based network dose-response meta-analysis was performed. A total of 100 trials involving 5,353 patients were included. The dose-response relationship followed an Emax curve, with ED50 values clustering around 80-90 MET-min/week. A weekly dose of 500 MET-min yielded considerable benefit, and 750-1000 MET-min approached maximal benefit for nearly all modalities. The top three ranked interventions were IAT (Emax = 3.50, 95% CrI: 2.49-4.60), RT (Emax = 3.66, 95% CrI: 1.96-5.85), and IAT+RT (Emax = 3.49, 95% CrI: 1.26-5.79). The exercise dose-response relationship in heart failure follows an Emax curve, with distinct dose-benefit profiles across different exercise modalities. Based on the current evidence, the following preliminary considerations may be offered: for patients with limited exercise tolerance, MBT may be considered as one of the preferred options; for those with moderate exercise tolerance, IAT+RT or CAT+RT may be suitable choices; for patients with good exercise tolerance, IAT or RT may be considered; and for patients with comorbid obesity, CAT may be incorporated into a comprehensive management program.

title: Interim Analysis of a Phase 3 Trial of Povetacicept in IgA Nephropathy.
authorString: Barratt J, Zhang H, Han SH, Suzuki Y, Tumlin J, Chacko B, Noronha IL, Madan A, Duivenvoorden R, Azzi JR, Nester C, Dong C, Ahluwalia N, Li J, Bozic C, Egbuna O, Wong MG, Lafayette R, RAINIER AIS-D08 Trial Group.

journal.title: The New England journal of medicine

abstractText: B-cell activating factor (BAFF) and a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL) have distinct roles in IgA-producing B-cell populations and appear to be central to the pathogenesis of IgA nephropathy. Povetacicept, an enhanced, variant transmembrane activator and calcium-modulator and cyclophilin-ligand interactor (TACI)-Fc fragment fusion therapeutic, is engineered for dual inhibition of BAFF and APRIL. In this ongoing, phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, participants with biopsy-proven IgA nephropathy receiving stable background therapy were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive povetacicept at a dose of 80 mg or placebo subcutaneously every 4 weeks. The primary end point of this prespecified interim analysis was the change in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at week 36. Secondary end points were the change at week 36 in galactose-deficient IgA1 levels and hematuria resolution at week 36 among participants with baseline hematuria. A total of 557 participants received povetacicept (372 participants) or placebo (185 participants). Efficacy analyses included the first 199 participants who had undergone randomization (131 in the povetacicept group and 68 in the placebo group). The 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio decreased by 52.0% with povetacicept and by 4.3% with placebo by week 36 (adjusted difference, -49.8 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -58.6 to -39.2; P<0.001). Galactose-deficient IgA1 levels decreased by 77.4% with povetacicept and increased by 9.1% with placebo (adjusted difference, -79.3 percentage points; 95% CI, -82.2 to -75.9; P<0.001). Among the participants with baseline hematuria, resolution occurred in 85% with povetacicept and in 23% with placebo (adjusted difference, 62 percentage points; 95% CI, 45 to 78; P<0.001). The incidence of adverse events (75% with povetacicept and 78% with placebo) and serious adverse events (3% and 4%, respectively) were similar in the trial groups. Povetacicept led to a significantly greater reduction in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo by week 36 in participants with IgA nephropathy. (Funded by Vertex Pharmaceuticals; RAINIER AIS-D08 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06564142.).

title: Search for the glycated hemoglobin target minimizing mortality among people with type 2 diabetes with rare incidence of treatment-related severe hypoglycemia - Epidemiologic analysis of J-DOIT3 randomized controlled trial.
authorString: Noda M, Ueki K, Sasako T, Ishizuka N, Miyake K, Miyoshi K, Aoyama T, Okazaki Y, Ohashi Y, Yamauchi T, Kadowaki T, J-DOIT3 Study Group.
abstractText: In recent years, with the considerable changes in the therapeutic armamentarium for diabetes, the incidence of hypoglycemia events, especially severe hypoglycemia events, associated with drug treatment in people with diabetes has markedly decreased. We were prompted to evaluate the threshold for each intervention target, especially glycemic control, associated with a minimized risk of the macrovascular complications of diabetes in this setting. In the Japan Diabetes Optimal Integrated Treatment study for 3 major risk factors of cardiovascular diseases (J-DOIT3) conducted by us previously, we recruited 2542 participants and assigned them to a conventional therapy group (n = 1271) and an intensive therapy group (n = 1271; two ineligible participants were removed from all analyses afterwards), and the incidence of severe hypoglycemia events was low in both groups (7 in the intensive therapy group and 4 in the conventional therapy group during a median 8.5 years' follow-up). Towards the objective of this study, we undertook a landmark analysis with a landmark time-point of 1 year after the baseline of the J-DOIT3 study. Then, using the updated mean values of the glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), systolic blood pressure, and LDL-cholesterol and HDL-cholesterol levels, we determined the optimal levels of each of these variables associated with the lowest hazard ratios for outcomes, including the primary and cardiovascular outcomes. For glycemic control, our results revealed no clear lower threshold of the glycated hemoglobin associated with the lowest risk of myocardial infarction or all-cause mortality; for other risk factors, it might be an important treatment target to maintain the LDL-cholesterol levels at below 80 mg/dL to minimize the risk of stroke. The present analysis suggested that the treatment target for HbA1c to minimize the risk of all-cause mortality in participants with diabetes with a low incidence of severe hypoglycemia episodes could be < 6.5% (ClinicalTrials.gov, number NCT00300976).

title: Current aspects in surgical treatment of advanced heart failure with future durable mechanical circulatory support.
authorString: Zaradzka JP, Kremer J, Meyer AL.

journal.title: European surgical research. Europaische chirurgische Forschung. Recherches chirurgicales europeennes

abstractText: Background Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death worldwide, resulting in an increasing demand for long-term treatment options for patients with end-stage heart failure. While heart transplantation is the gold standard, donor organ shortage continues to be a major limitation, particularly in countries with opt-in consent systems. Summary Durable mechanical circulatory support (dMCS) devices have emerged as a critical therapy for patients with advanced heart failure, either as a bridge to transplantation or as destination therapy. Technological innovations over recent decades have transitioned from pulsatile to continuous-flow systems, with the HeartMate 3 currently representing the only long-term left ventricular support, due to its superior hemocompatibility, clinical outcomes, and full magnetic levitation. However, limitations persist, especially regarding right-sided and biventricular support, driveline infections, and patient quality of life. This review provides a comprehensive overview of both currently approved and investigational dMCS devices, highlighting key engineering features, hemocompatibility advancements, and the status of ongoing clinical trials. Emerging devices such as the Corheart 6, BrioVAD, EvaHeart 2, CorWave, FlowMaker, and TorVAD aim to enhance physiologic support, minimize shear stress, and enable full implantability. Additionally, novel concepts for biventricular and total heart replacement, including BerlinHeart Excor, reBEAT, DuoCor BiVAS, SynCardia, Emperor and BiVACOR are discussed. Key Messages •HeartMate 3 remains the only approved LVAD in Europe following HVAD withdrawal. •Next-generation devices aim to improve hemocompatibility, reduce complications, and support full implantability. •Options for biventricular or right heart failure remain limited, but novel concepts are emerging.

title: [Evidence-based treatment of valvular heart disease].
authorString: Nettersheim FS, Baldus S.
abstractText: Valvular heart disease is a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide. As the prevalence of most valvular heart diseases increases with age, population ageing has led to a substantial increase in disease burden. Due to advanced age or significant comorbidities, many patients are considered unsuitable for conventional surgery. Whereas medical therapy was therefore often the only treatment option in the past, the rapid evolution of transcatheter interventions has fundamentally transformed the management of valvular heart disease over the past two decades. Today, effective catheter-based treatment options are available for virtually all valvular pathologies. For patients with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis, the prognostic benefit of transcatheter aortic valve replacement is firmly established. Large randomized trials have demonstrated non-inferiority of transcatheter aortic valve replacement compared with surgical aortic valve replacement across most patient populations, leading to an expanding use of this approach in younger and lower-risk patients. Similarly, transcatheter edge-to-edge repair for mitral and tricuspid regurgitation has been shown to improve symptoms, quality of life, and heart failure-related hospitalizations. In carefully selected patients with secondary mitral regurgitation, this strategy also confers a survival benefit. In addition, dedicated transcatheter devices have recently emerged as promising treatment options for native aortic regurgitation. Given the rapid evolution of transcatheter therapies, current efforts are increasingly focused on selecting the optimal treatment strategy for the individual patient and determining the optimal timing of intervention.

title: Structured Vs Conventional Endoscopic Vein Harvesting Training: Vein Integrity and Learning Curve Performance
authorString: Krishnamoorthy B, Raaj S, Air R, Ruiz Segria C, Enriquez R, Olufemi S, Sarma J, Barnard J, Rajai A, Akowuah E, Venkateswaran R.
abstractText: Background Endoscopic Vein Harvesting (EVH) reduces wound complications compared with open vein harvesting. However, concerns remain that conduit injury may occur during the learning curve . The impact of EVH training on vein integrity and progression to independent practice remains unclear . We evaluated whether a structured EVH training programme improved vein quality, technical skill and trainee confidence. Methods This study was originally designed as a multicentre cluster-randomised trial but was prematurely halted and completed as a two-centre study with cluster allocation. Four EVH trainees were included: Two received Structured Training (ST) incorporating simulation, psychomotor reinforcement, video review and competency-based progression. Two underwent Conventional Training (CT), consisting of standard company-led training. Endothelial integrity was assessed using CD34 immunohistochemistry across proximal, random and distal sections. Endothelial stretching and muscle hypertrophy were graded. Trainee performance, anxiety and consultant-rated vein quality were recorded. Patients were followed to 12 months for Major Adverse Cardiac Events and 24 months for survival. Analyses were descriptive. Results Forty-six patients underwent EVH (ST n = 40; CT n = 6). Technical performance improved in all trainees but CT trainees discontinued independent EVH practice during the study period. ST trainees demonstrated better endothelial integrity with less stretching and muscle hypertrophy. CT vein samples showed greater endothelial variability. Clinical event rates were low. At 6–24 months, MACE was infrequent with repeat angina (4.3%), myocardial infarction (2.2%), re-intervention (6.5%) and non-cardiac death (2.2%). Among the 38 vein grafts assessed by computed tomography angiography in asymptomatic patients, 23 (60.5%) were patent, five (13.2%) demonstrated flow-limiting stenosis, and 10 (26.3%) were occluded. These findings were predominantly observed in small-calibre target vessels in patients with diabetes. Conclusion Structured EVH training was associated with better endothelial preservation during the learning curve. Given the small sample size and incomplete imaging follow-up, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger multicentre studies.  Clinical registration: ISRCTN27493194; February 2022; amended 2024. This work has been presented at International Society of Minimally Invasive Surgery (ISMICS) annual conference meeting as a e-poster online on 10-13  th June 2026. e-poster online; Available at ismics2026.109014b.NORMAL.pdf

title: Effectiveness of Remotely Monitored Home-Based Baduanjin using Wearable Devices for Elder Patients after coronary revascularization: A Study Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial
authorString: Li T, Jiang H, Lin Z, Li X, Xiao X, Liu M, Zhao L, Gao T, Yang P.
abstractText: Introduction: Coronary artery disease(CAD) is a prevalent cardiovascular disorder, and coronary revascularization, including percutaneous coronary intervention(PCI) and coronary artery bypass grafting(CABG), is a common treatment. However, many patients still suffer from cardiopulmonary dysfunction after the surgery. Baduanjin, a traditional Chinese exercise, may have potential benefits for these patients, but evidence is limited. This trial aims to determine the effectiveness and safety of remotely monitored home-based Baduanjin for post-coronary revascularization patients with cardiopulmonary dysfunction. Methods and analysis: This is a multicenter, assessor-blinded, two-armed randomized controlled trial. Three hundred and ninety-eight patients will be recruited from China-Japan Friendship Hospital, Fuwai Hospital, Xuanwu Hospital, and Guang'anmen Hospital, and randomly assigned to two groups (group A or group B) in a 1:1 ratio. Patients in group A will receive remotely monitored home-based Baduanjin training combined with conventional secondary prevention education of CHD, while patients in group B will receive conventional secondary prevention education alone for 12 weeks. The primary outcome will be the peak oxygen uptake (VO 2 peak) obtained from cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) at week 12 compared with baseline. Secondary outcomes will include 6-minute walk distance (6MWD), Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ), health-related quality of life measured by EQ-5D-VAS and EQ-5D-5L, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), anxiety and depression scales (GAD-7 and PHQ-9), Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), composite cardiovascular events (including re-revascularization, AMI, death, stroke, heart failure rehospitalization), and other relevant indicators at weeks 0, 4, 8, and 12. Safety indicators will be monitored throughout the trial. Ethics and dissemination: This study has been approved by the clinical research ethics committee of China-Japan Friendship Hospital (No.2024-KY-031), the results of this study will be disseminated via peer-reviewed publications or conference presentations. Trial registration number: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (No. ChiCTR2400088668, https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=232409) registered on 23 August 2024.

title: Three ablation strategies using very high-power short-duration catheter in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: The Q-INDEX randomized trial.
authorString: Lee SR, Cho Y, Han S, Lee KY, Ahn HJ, Kwon S, Kang KM, Park SW, Oh S, Park HS, Choi EK.
abstractText:
Background

Very high-power short-duration (vHPSD; 90 W/4 sec) ablation shortens pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) but produces shallower lesions that may be inadequate in the thick anterior left atrium.

Objective

To compare vHPSD, ablation index (AI)-guided, and hybrid strategies for PVI in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.

Methods

In this multicenter, randomized, open-label trial, 150 patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation were assigned 1:1:1 with the QDOT MICRO catheter to (1) AI-guided (AI 500 anterior, 400 elsewhere), (2) hybrid (AI-guided anterior [AI 500], vHPSD elsewhere), or (3) vHPSD (90 W/4 sec, all segments). The primary endpoint was total ablation time; secondary endpoints included acute PV reconnection, safety, and 1-year freedom from atrial arrhythmia.

Results

Acute PVI was achieved in all patients. Total ablation time was longest with AI-guided and shortest with vHPSD ablation (median 2220 vs 1450 vs 794 sec; P < .001). Acute reconnection across the 14 PV segments was lowest with AI-guided and highest with vHPSD (7.7% vs 9.4% vs 10.6%; P = .40). One-year freedom from atrial arrhythmia was 92.0%, 85.4%, and 77.6%, respectively (log-rank P = .13; for AI-guided vs vHPSD; P = .049). No tamponade occurred; steam pops occurred only in the 90 W groups. Two minor periprocedural strokes occurred (both vHPSD; full recovery), and silent cerebral lesions on magnetic resonance imaging did not differ among the groups (5%, 10%, 0%; P = .35).

Conclusion

Uniform vHPSD more than halved PVI ablation time but was associated with the lowest 1-year efficacy, whereas the hybrid strategy preserved efficiency without significant loss of durability. These exploratory findings-from a trial powered for ablation time-support region-tailored lesion depth in point-by-point ablation and warrant confirmation.

title: The applications of artificial intelligence in liver transplantation: A comprehensive scoping review.
authorString: Borakati A, Agilinko J, Wu J, Hunter S, Alhaq A, Froghi F, Teo J, Bernal W, Callaghan C, Cortes-Cerisuelo M, Wallace D.
abstractText: Liver transplantation (LT) is a complex surgical intervention, with intricate decision-making and risks at all stages before, during and after the procedure itself. Artificial intelligence (AI) may assist the process but has seen limited use. This scoping review assessed primary articles reporting on clinical AI in LT in MEDLINE and Embase from 2000 to September 2026. 196 articles were identified: focusing on the pre-operative period before transplant (21.9%), organ retrieval (9.7%), intra-operative issues (3.6%), short-term post-operative complications (16.8%), long-term post-operative complications (45.9%) and natural language processing (2.0%). 95.9% had retrospective designs and only 12.8% had direct multi-centre data, with the rest from national registries or single centres. 13.8% of studies externally validated their AI tools. Only one study performed a prospective evaluation of their tool with a randomized controlled trial. Progress towards clinically deployable tools will require harmonised, higher-granularity datasets, consistent reporting, and prospective evaluation within real-world transplant workflows.

title: Dietary Behaviors and Urinary Biomarkers in a Self-Management Support Program Among Low-Income Adults with CKD.
authorString: Banerjee T, Velasquez A, Simoni J, Powe NR, Tuot DS.
abstractText: CKD disproportionately affects socioeconomically disadvantaged populations, among whom adoption of kidney-friendly diets is often constrained by structural barriers. Self-management support (SMS) programs can improve CKD awareness and cardiovascular risk factors; however, their ability to influence dietary behaviors and diet-related physiologic markers when nutrition content is limited remains uncertain. We evaluated whether participation in a culturally tailored SMS program with modest dietary education was associated with changes in self-reported dietary behaviors and urinary biomarkers among low-income adults with CKD. We conducted a secondary exploratory analysis of a randomized controlled trial (NCT01530958) among low-income adults with early-to-moderate CKD. Participants were randomized to an SMS program that included limited dietary education focused on reducing sodium, refined sugar, and fast-food consumption. Outcomes included self-reported intake of soda, fruit-flavored drinks, and fast food, as well as urinary biomarkers reflecting sodium-potassium balance and inflammation, including sodium-to-potassium ratio (Na/K), interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1). Multivariable linear regression models adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics and body mass index were used to assess associations at intervention completion and 6-month follow-up. Among 266 participants (mean age 57.5 years; 51% men; 34% African American, 36% Hispanic, 19% Asian/Pacific Islander, and 9% non-Hispanic White), 97% reported annual household income below $50,000. The intervention was not associated with significant changes in self-reported dietary behaviors, urinary Na/K ratio (β [95% CI]: 0.24 [ -0.61, 1.09]), urinary IL-6 (-1.86 [-4.96, 1.25]), or urinary TGF-β1 (5.41 [-1.08, 11.54]). A modest reduction in urinary TNF-α was observed (-0.24 [-0.43, -0.02]). In this low-income CKD population, an SMS program with limited dietary content was not sufficient to produce measurable changes in dietary behaviors or most diet-related urinary biomarkers. These findings underscore the need for more intensive, nutrition-focused, and structurally supported interventions to achieve meaningful dietary and physiologic change in CKD.

title: Thermal convective and flow dynamics of blood trihybrid nanofluid inside a stenosis artery for cardiovascular disease treatment using artificial intelligence approach.
authorString: Mrabet B, Ponnore JJ, Jawo R, Yildirim Y.
abstractText: This article briefly discusses the influence of heat radiation and heat source on the convective flow of a blood-based trihybrid nanofluid inside a stenotic artery with chemical reaction. It can assist in investigating and predicting blood flow dynamics and heat transmission in constricted arteries for thermal therapy, targeted drug delivery, and cardiovascular disease treatment. By replicating the intricate interactions of many nanoparticles with blood, the model also aids in the design and optimization of biomedical devices like stents and artificial organs. The AI technique also makes it possible to make quick, precise, and patient-specific predictions, which helps doctors plan treatments and enhances the efficacy of cardiovascular procedures. The artificial intelligent neural network (AINN) is one sophisticated machine learning approach. The difficulty led to the system of PDEs (partial differential equations), which are transformed into ODEs (ordinary differential equations) via dimensionless similarity. The dataset was filtered using the Bvp4c method before being incorporated into the Bayesian-regularization algorithm (BRA). Regression-based statistical analysis, error histograms, absolute error, and MSE (mean squared error) are used to measure the determination, verification, convergence, and stability of Bayesian-regularized neural network mappings for this hybrid model. The thermal field increases as upsurge the values of thermal Biot number.Clinical trial: This study is not a clinical trial.

title: Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients and spectral features directly drive micro-level autonomic reflexes during brief respiration practices
authorString: Chang J, Yao Z.
abstractText: While digital health platforms increasingly deliver guided mindful breathing interventions via audio, the specific acoustic properties of the guidance are fundamentally ignored as potential active ingredients. This within-subject study implemented an unprecedented high-density experimental design to investigate how distinct, computationally engineered acoustic features (e.g., pitch, zero-crossing rate, natural background sounds) modulate acute cardiovascular, respiratory, and autonomic responses. To rigorously eliminate sex-related physiological variance, 21 meditation-naïve female university students completed 13 randomized audio sessions of a standardized 4-minute-and-5-second guided breathing practice (yielding 273 high-density recording epochs). Multiparametric biosignals, including pulse rate variability (PRV), respiratory dynamics, and electrodermal activity (EDA), were continuously recorded. Results demonstrated a robust reduction in blood pressure independent of audio conditions, confirming the fundamental efficacy of a single bout of spontaneous breath awareness. However, high-resolution analyses revealed a highly modular architecture where peripheralautonomic indices (EDA and PRV) were acutely sensitive to fine-grained acoustic features, specifically Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs). Furthermore, physiological coupling patterns reorganized dynamically depending strictly on the acoustic context. These indings fundamentally challenge the assumption that meditation audio is a neutral delivery medium, establishing acoustic parameters as potent, independent modulators of human autonomic reflexes for future digital therapeutics.

title: Effects of Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation (tDCS) in Paracanoe Athletes: A Randomized Sham-Controlled Crossover Trial
authorString: Vieira VM, Lima SLM, Braz MECS, de Abreu LdS, Bastos KRG, Marques LERM, Paraizo VHR, Silva IRP, Oliveira ALMB, Pedreiro RCdM, Miarka B.
abstractText: Background Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) over the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex has been investigated as a non-invasive strategy to modulate cognitive performance and autonomic regulation in sport, but evidence in Paralympic athletes remains scarce. This study evaluated the acute effects of anodal tDCS over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex on cognitive performance and cardiovascular autonomic modulation in para-canoeing athletes. Methods This pilot, randomized, sham-controlled, single-blind, within-subject crossover trial included eight male para-canoeing athletes (35.4 ± 5.4 years). In randomized order, separated by a seven-day washout, each participant received one session of anodal tDCS (anode at F3, cathode at Fp2; 2 mA; 20 minutes) and one sham session. Cognitive performance was assessed with the Stroop Test (eight athletes) and cardiac autonomic modulation with heart rate variability indices (five athletes with adequate signal quality). Differences between conditions and time points were estimated with the percentile bootstrap (10,000 resamples; 95% confidence intervals), with simulation-based power projection for larger samples. Results In the anodal condition, correct responses on the color Stroop increased from pre- to post-intervention (mean pre-minus-post difference − 7.63; 95% confidence interval − 15.50 to − 1.75). After the intervention, markers of relative sympathetic modulation of heart rate variability (absolute low-frequency power, its natural logarithm, and the ratio of low- to high-frequency power) were higher in the anodal than in the sham condition. In the sham condition, heart rate increased and the R–R interval decreased from pre- to post-intervention. Conclusions In this pilot sample, anodal tDCS over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex was associated with improved Stroop accuracy and a sympathetic shift in cardiac autonomic modulation, a promising signal that requires confirmation in a larger, independent sample before any applied recommendation. Trial registration: Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry (ReBEC), RBR-47g8ts7, registered on 18 May 2026 (retrospectively registered).

title: Shunt-Dependent Hydrocephalus and Cognitive Outcomes After Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
authorString: Rossong H, Veilleux C, Macdonald RL, Eagles ME.
abstractText: Hydrocephalus is a common complication after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH), frequently requiring permanent cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) diversion. The relationship between chronic, shunt-dependent hydrocephalus and cognitive outcomes after aSAH remains poorly defined. This study evaluated whether patients requiring permanent CSF diversion demonstrate worse cognitive outcomes at 90 days after aSAH. A post hoc analysis of the multicenter NEWTON-2 clinical trial data set was conducted. Patients with ruptured saccular aneurysms (World Federation Neurosurgical Societies 2-4) who had Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scores available at 90 days were included. Patients undergoing ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement were classified as having chronic hydrocephalus. The primary outcome was MoCA score at 90 days. Negative binomial regression was used to model MoCA scores, and logistic regression was performed using a clinically validated cutoff for cognitive impairment (MoCA ≤25). Multivariable models adjusted for age, sex, hypertension, World Federation Neurosurgical Societies grade, and delayed cerebral ischemia. Among 215 patients with available 90-day MoCA scores, 77 (36%) required permanent CSF diversion. Median MoCA scores were lower in shunted patients compared with nonshunted patients (24 [IQR 16-26] vs 26 [IQR 22-28], P = .0007). Shunt placement was independently associated with increased odds of cognitive impairment at 90 days (odds ratio 2.13, 95% CI, 1.11-4.14) and an approximately 2.7-point reduction in MoCA scores after adjustment for covariates. Permanent CSF diversion after aSAH is independently associated with worse cognitive performance at 90 days. Shunt-dependent hydrocephalus may identify patients at increased risk for persistent cognitive impairment who may benefit from enhanced monitoring and targeted rehabilitation.

title: Interleukin-6 as an Inflammatory Biomarker of Thyroid Dysfunction in Patients Undergoing Maintenance Hemodialysis: A Cross-Sectional Study
authorString: Mudjanarko SW, Retnaningtyas FD, Oktavian P, Thaha M, Tjempakasari A, Kusumawindani D.
abstractText: Background Thyroid dysfunction is common in chronic kidney disease (CKD) and is increasingly linked to systemic inflammation. Interleukin-6 (IL-6), a pro-inflammatory cytokine, can alter the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis and peripheral thyroid hormone metabolism. Aims To evaluate serum IL-6 as an inflammatory biomarker of thyroid dysfunction in CKD patients on maintenance hemodialysis, and to determine its independent predictive and discriminatory performance. Methods This cross-sectional study included 65 consecutive patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis at Airlangga University Hospital, Surabaya. Associations between IL-6 and five thyroid parameters were examined using Spearman correlation with Bonferroni correction. Multivariable linear regression assessed the independent association of IL-6 with thyroid hormones after adjustment for age, sex, body mass index, hemodialysis duration, albumin, diabetes mellitus, and hypertension. ROC curve analysis with bootstrap-derived 95% confidence intervals evaluated discrimination for thyroid dysfunction. Results Median IL-6 was 10.10 pg/mL (IQR 6.13–17.16). Thyroid dysfunction occurred in 48 patients (73.8%), most commonly low T3 syndrome (49.2%). IL-6 correlated positively with TSH (r = 0.344; raw p = 0.005; Bonferroni-adjusted p = 0.025). In multivariable analysis, higher IL-6 was independently associated with lower total T3 (β=−0.0025; 95% CI − 0.005 to − 0.0001; p = 0.040; R² = 0.270, adjusted R² = 0.164). IL-6 showed moderate discrimination (AUC = 0.665; 95% CI 0.528–0.799). A cutoff of ≥ 10.10 pg/mL with sensitivity 60.4%, specificity 76.5%, PPV 87.9%, NPV 40.6%. Conclusions IL-6 is independently associated with reduced total T3 and shows moderate discriminatory ability for thyroid dysfunction. An IL-6 cutoff of 10.10 pg/mL have a potential role as a practical biomarker for thyroid dysfunction threshold, but this finding needs further research. Clinical Trial Registry: ClinicalTrials.gov, TRN: NCT07328113, Registration date: 2 January 2026.

title: Association between nighttime heat exposure and emergency hospitalization for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: A time-stratified case-crossover study in Japan.
authorString: Nishimura H, Nawa N, Fushimi K, Fujiwara T.
abstractText: Few studies have explored the adverse health effects of nighttime heat exposure. This study examined the association between nighttime heat exposure and emergency hospitalization for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) in Japan. Hospitalizations were identified from a nationwide administrative database covering the period from May to September between 2011 and 2021. Days with minimum temperatures higher than region-specific 92.5th percentile temperatures were considered as exposed to nighttime heat. Daily maximum temperature was adjusted for as a proxy for daytime heat exposure. First, a time-stratified case-crossover study using conditional quasi-Poisson regression analysis was conducted to estimate location-specific heat-related relative risks (RRs) of emergency hospitalization for OHCA over lag 0-6 days. Second, a random-effects meta-analysis was conducted to estimate pooled RRs. The analysis was further stratified by age, sex, and region. Third, in an attempt to account for the geographical heterogeneity in RRs, the location-specific penetration rate of air conditioners (ACs) was included as a meta-regressor. A total of 135,898 hospitalizations for OHCA were identified. Nighttime heat exposure was associated with increased emergency hospitalizations for OHCA (RR: 1.090 (95% confidence interval (CI): 1.047-1.135). Higher RRs were observed among people aged ≥ 75 years and females living in northern areas (1.295 (95%CI: 1.117-1.500) and 1.352 (95%CI: 1.145-1.596), respectively). In locations with a lower penetration rate of ACs, females and those aged ≥ 75 years were at higher RRs.

title: Immediate vs delayed extubation after pediatric liver transplantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Daverio M, Laucaityte G, Goldstein MA, Berti G, Bulut Y, Deep A, PALISI Liver Failure Special Interest Group.
abstractText: Immediate extubation (IE) in the operating room following orthotopic liver transplantation (OLT) is increasingly adopted in adults but pediatric evidence remains limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to identify factors associated with IE and compare outcomes between IE and delayed extubation (DE) after pediatric OLT. MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, CINAHL, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to October 30, 2025. Studies comparing IE and DE in pediatric OLT recipients were included. Outcomes included reintubation, mortality, thrombosis, reoperation, tracheostomy, PICU, and hospital length of stay (LOS). Random-effects meta-analysis was pre-specified for all outcomes; sensitivity, meta-regression, and subgroup analyses were performed. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I. Twelve retrospective single-center studies comprising 1323 patients (1158 unique children after accounting for two center-level cohort overlaps) were included. IE was associated with lower odds of reintubation (OR 0.32, 95% CI 0.17-0.59) and mortality (OR 0.35, 95% CI 0.18-0.68); both estimates were confirmed by a correction-free Peto odds ratio (0.29 and 0.31, respectively). No significant differences were observed for thrombosis or reoperation. IE was associated with shorter PICU LOS (SMD - 0.88, 95% CI - 1.39 to - 0.37), hospital LOS (SMD - 1.16, 95% CI - 2.00 to - 0.31). Donor-type subgroup analyses showed effect sizes in the same direction as the overall analysis for PICU and hospital LOS, but none of the within-subgroup estimates reached statistical significance. Meta-regression identified intraoperative transfusion differences as predictor of hospital LOS (β =  - 0.045, p = 0.006, R2 = 57.1%), a pattern more consistent with confounding by indication than with a beneficial mechanism of transfusion itself. IE was associated with lower reintubation, mortality, and shorter LOS in pediatric OLT, but these findings derive exclusively from retrospective studies at high risk of selection bias, and causality cannot be established. Children undergoing IE were likely older and in better preoperative condition; hospital LOS findings are particularly susceptible to confounding. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to confirm these outcomes benefit. • Delayed extubation with prolonged mechanical ventilation has been standard after pediatric orthotopic liver transplantation. • Immediate extubation in the operating room is increasingly used after adult liver transplantation experiences. • Pediatric evidence on immediate extubation comes from single-center retrospective studies. • This meta-analysis of 12 studies found immediate extubation associated with lower reintubation, mortality, and shorter length of stay. • These associations likely reflect selection bias rather than a proven causal benefit. • Immediate extubation appears feasible and safe in selected children, but prospective multicenter studies are needed to determine patients benefiting from this approach.

title: Amyloid-targeted PET after negative or low-grade bone scintigraphy for cardiac amyloidosis: a systematic review.
authorString: Chiaravalloti A, Di Biagio D.

journal.title: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging

abstractText: To assess myocardial positron emission tomography (PET) positivity after negative or low-grade bone scintigraphy, while distinguishing test discordance from independently confirmed cardiac amyloidosis. PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science were searched through 5 August 2026, with targeted source assessment through 2 October 2026. Negative and low-grade imaging denoted Perugini grades 0 and 1, respectively; study-defined negative results were described separately. Eligibility required linked PET and bone-scan results with an extractable denominator. Acquisition modality, PET thresholds and cardiac reference standards were examined. A restricted synthesis required documented tomographic acquisition; a broader three-report synthesis was exploratory. Nine reports provided extractable paired results. In the hereditary transthyretin subgroup examined with carbon-11 Pittsburgh compound B, 20/23 participants were PET-positive after excluding one acquired, domino-transplant case. The exploratory pooled proportion was 87.0% (95% profile-likelihood confidence interval, 68.5-97.8%). Restriction to clearly documented cohort-wide tomography retained only two reports, precluding the planned pooled analysis. Uptake definitions and cardiac verification differed substantially. General diagnostic studies without complete bone-grade denominators, including REVEAL, were excluded from the eligible synthesis and retained as context. PET positivity is common in selected hereditary transthyretin cohorts with negative or low-grade bone scans, but does not establish cardiac amyloidosis or earlier diagnosis. Conditional diagnostic accuracy remains unresolved. Prospective paired studies require tomographic localization, tracer-specific thresholds and independent cardiac verification.

title: IL-6 Blockade for Antibody-Mediated Transplant Rejection: What Does the Evidence Say?
authorString: Kanbay M, Copur S, Altunbulakli C, Eren ZB, Gulmaliyev I, Genc NI, Süsal C, Covic A, Altindal M.

journal.title: BioDrugs : clinical immunotherapeutics, biopharmaceuticals and gene therapy

abstractText: Two of the most significant challenges in transplantation medicine are human leukocyte antigen sensitization, which limits access to kidney transplantation for patients with end-stage kidney disease owing to the lack of effective desensitization strategies, and chronic active antibody-mediated rejection (cAMR), a major cause of allograft dysfunction and graft loss following transplantation. Despite its substantial clinical significance, there remains a lack of high-quality evidence and well-established therapeutic algorithms for the management of cAMR, while many patients continue to be excluded from kidney transplantation because of immunological barriers. Interleukin-6 (IL-6) is a pleiotropic cytokine that plays a central role in both innate and adaptive immune responses. Beyond its immunological functions, IL-6 has been implicated in the pathogenesis of a wide range of conditions, including atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, diabetes mellitus, and various neurological disorders. Consequently, targeting the IL-6/IL-6 receptor signaling pathway has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy in transplantation medicine, particularly for desensitization protocols and the treatment of cAMR. However, the current evidence base is restricted to studies evaluating tocilizumab and clazakizumab, with clinical benefits remaining inconsistent across studies. Limited evidence is available regarding the desensitization effectiveness of tocilizumab monotherapy. In cAMR, the phase III IMAGINE trial found no improvement in kidney function with clazakizumab despite reduced C-reactive protein. Current evidence does not support a routine IL-6 pathway blockade in cAMR, while further studies are required to prove the potential benefits in desensitization. In this narrative review, we comprehensively examine the role of IL-6 in the pathophysiology of kidney transplantation and critically appraise the available clinical evidence regarding IL-6/IL-6R-targeted therapies for the management of human leukocyte antigen sensitization and cAMR.

title: Temporal Patterns of Multimorbidity Progression Among Inpatients With a Recorded Hypertension Diagnosis Across Three Counties in Rural Henan, China: Retrospective Cohort Study Using Temporal Network Analysis.
authorString: Wang Y, Mao Y, Wang X, Liu R, Cui M, Feng R.
abstractText:
Background

Hypertension is a key driver of multimorbidity; however, its role in shaping dynamic disease progression, especially in rural populations, remains underexplored.

Objective

This study aimed to characterize temporal patterns of multimorbidity progression among inpatients with a recorded hypertension diagnosis and to examine whether these patterns differed by sex, age, insurance type, and county.

Methods

We analyzed electronic health record data from 34,099 inpatients with a recorded hypertension diagnosis across 3 rural counties in Henan, China (2019-2023), constructing a temporal comorbidity network of 250 disease nodes and 1512 disease transitions. Statistical validation was performed using bootstrap resampling, case-dropping, and permutation tests. Subgroup analyses were conducted by sex, age, insurance type, and county.

Results

The temporal comorbidity network revealed a densely interconnected core involving hypertension, atherosclerotic heart disease, and cerebral infarction, with type 2 diabetes occupying a bridging position between cardiovascular and multisystem disease clusters. The ordering of dominant recorded pathways differed by sex (earlier coronary involvement among female inpatients vs more direct progression to stroke among male inpatients), was more complex in inpatients older than 70 years of age, and was more diffuse among those covered by urban-rural resident insurance compared with urban employee insurance.

Conclusions

Multimorbidity among inpatients with recorded hypertension followed structured and heterogeneous temporal patterns that differed by sex, age, insurance type, and county. Cardiovascular and cerebrovascular conditions formed the principal recorded progression pathways, while type 2 diabetes connected cardiovascular pathways with broader multisystem complications. These findings support further evaluation of risk-stratified and locally adapted approaches to chronic disease prevention and longitudinal care.

title: Polycystin dysfunction and cardiac electrical abnormalities in ADPKD.
authorString: Devapatla P, Hsu CY, Hsieh-Li HM, Huang LY.
abstractText: Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD) is one of the most common inherited kidney disorders characterized by the progressive formation of renal cysts. It is a systemic disease with significant extra-renal manifestations. Among these, cardiac electrical abnormalities are increasingly recognized as clinically important yet underappreciated contributors to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Beyond cyst formation, pathogenic variants in PKD1 or PKD2, which encode polycystin-1 (PC1) and polycystin-2 (PC2), respectively, interfere with calcium homeostasis, mechanotransduction, and mitochondrial function in both kidney and heart tissues. These molecular changes trigger a cascade of pathological events, including RAAS activation, TGF-driven fibrosis, and oxidative stress, leading to structural and electrical remodeling of the heart. These alterations contribute to cardiac electrical remodeling, manifesting clinically as QT interval and corrected QT (QT/QTc) prolongation, left ventricular hypertrophy, atrial fibrillation, ventricular arrhythmias, and other electrocardiographic abnormalities. Despite growing evidence, cardiac electrical abnormalities in ADPKD remain understudied in clinical practice. Early detection of subclinical cardiovascular abnormalities may be facilitated by electrocardiographic monitoring, cardiac imaging, and complementary biomarker assessment. Additionally, findings from iPSC-derived cardiomyocyte models support the translational potential of personalized drug-screening platforms. This review summarizes current evidence linking polycystin dysfunction to cardiac electrical abnormalities in ADPKD by integrating molecular mechanisms with experimental and clinical findings. It also highlights the need for integrated cardio-renal approaches to improve cardiovascular surveillance, risk stratification, and future therapeutic development in ADPKD.

title: Sex differences in cardiovascular disease burden, risk factors, and disease spectrum in Europe: a global burden of disease 2023 analysis within the ESC Atlas framework.
authorString: Conrad N, Torbica A, Wood AM, Townsend N, Van Belle E, Kaplon-Cieslicka A, Kazakiewicz D, Scherr D, Lüscher TF, Vardas PE, Petersen SE, Timmis A.
abstractText: Despite growing recognition of sex disparities in cardiovascular disease (CVD), contemporary, harmonized analyses of sex-specific burden in the European region that could inform targeted prevention strategies, remain limited. Sex-specific patterns in CVD burden and risk factor exposure across 55 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) member countries were examined using data from the 2023 Global Burden of Disease study. Risk factor exposure was quantified using age-sex-standardized summary exposure values for 10 established cardiovascular risk factors. Disease incidence and mortality for major CVD categories, including maternal hypertensive disorders, were estimated by calculating age-sex-standardized rates per 100 000 person-years using the 2013 European Standard Population. Analyses were performed by sex at country, regional, and ESC-wide levels and over time (1990-2023). In 2023, in the ESC region, the overall CVD burden was broadly similar in men and women, with women accounting for 55% (6.0 million) of cases and 50% of deaths (1.5 million). This apparent parity, however, concealed marked sex differences in disease composition, risk exposure, and geographic disparities. Compared with men, women had a lower proportion of CVD due to ischaemic heart disease (21% vs 38%) and a higher contribution from peripheral arterial disease (23% vs 19%). Major differences were also apparent in risk profiles, particularly for behavioural risk factors-with summary exposure values of tobacco and alcohol being 10%-20% points higher in men than women; contrasting with cardiometabolic factors, such as high body mass index and low physical activity, that were often 5%-15% points higher in women than men, and more modest differences in environmental and biological risks, including air pollution, fasting glucose, or cholesterol. Cardiovascular disease burden further varied widely across countries and disparities affected women more strongly than men, with an approximately three-fold difference between the lowest- and highest-incidence countries in women, compared with a two-fold difference in men, and even larger disparities in mortality and premature mortality (up to 25-fold in women). Maternal hypertensive disorders substantially shaped both the scale and composition of CVD burden in women, accounting for 25% of incident CVD in women and exhibiting substantial geographic variation, with up to 18-fold differences in incidence across countries. These findings challenge conventional approaches that treat CVD as a homogeneous condition. In particular, the substantial contribution of non-ischaemic conditions and maternal hypertensive disorders to the burden in women, alongside distinct patterns of risk exposure and wider geographic disparities, underscore the importance of adopting a life-course and sex- and gender-informed approach to cardiovascular prevention and policy.

title: Advanced Subclinical Atherosclerosis in Young Individuals and Risk of Mortality Over 30 Years: The Coronary Artery Calcium Consortium.
authorString: Choi S, Dzaye O, Dardari Z, Yao Z, Cao T, Burka S, Erhabor J, Jelwan Y, Diener-West M, Budoff M, Berman DS, Nasir K, Shaw LJ, Miedema MD, Rumberger J, Al Rifai M, Bittencourt MS, Whelton SP, Blumenthal RS, Blaha MJ.
abstractText:
Importance

Coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring is a well-established tool for predicting cardiovascular risk, but its long-term prognostic value in young adults remains unclear. As early preventive intervention may yield substantial lifetime benefit, understanding long-term implications of elevated CAC in young adults is important for informing prevention strategies.

Objective

To investigate the long-term risk of all-cause, cardiovascular disease (CVD), and coronary heart disease (CHD) mortality associated with premature advanced subclinical atherosclerosis.

Design, setting, and participants

This cohort study used the CAC Consortium dataset, a retrospectively assembled cohort of referred individuals with clinically indicated CAC scans. Using multivariable regression models for time-to-event analysis, the association of CAC with all-cause, CVD, and CHD mortality was assessed, adjusting for age, sex, and traditional atherosclerotic CVD risk factors. Cumulative incidence was derived for these outcomes in 5-year increments up to 30 years using a mixed approach involving the Kaplan-Meier method and Weibull modeling. The proportion of deaths attributable to CVD and CHD across CAC groups was evaluated. Four institutions across the US provided patient-level data to assemble the CAC Consortium. Included in the analysis were adults aged 30 to 45 years from the CAC Consortium. They were followed up for a median of 22.6 years. Study data were analyzed from October 2025 to September 2026.

Exposure

Elevated CAC in adults aged 30 to 45 years, specifically CAC score greater than 90%.

Main outcomes and measures

Participants were followed up for underlying cause of mortality.

Results

Among 12 847 participants, the mean (SD) age was 40.5 (3.6) years, and 9922 (77.2%) were male; 9262 (72.1%) had CAC score of 0, 1626 (12.7%) had a CAC score between 75% to 90%, and 1703 (13.3%) had a CAC score greater than 90%. In total, there were 624 deaths (149 CVD and 81 CHD). Multivariable adjusted hazard ratios for CAC score greater than 90% vs CAC score of 0 were 1.87 (95% CI, 1.54-2.27), 2.60 (95% CI, 1.77-3.82), and 3.71 (95% CI, 2.24-6.16), for all-cause, CVD, and CHD mortality, respectively. Over 30 years, the group with a CAC score greater than 90% had significantly higher modeled risk of all-cause (12.9% vs 7.5%), CVD (4.5% vs 1.5%), and CHD (3.0% vs 0.6%) mortality, compared with the group with a CAC score of 0.

Conclusions and relevance

Results of this cohort study suggest that young adults with a CAC score greater than 90% face significantly higher long-term risk of all-cause, CVD, and CHD mortality, suggesting potential implications for guiding the intensification of preventive intervention in this high-risk phenotype.

title: Arrhythmic Risk Stratification in Non-Ischaemic Cardiomyopathy: The Role of Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
authorString: Sia RI, Hammersley DJ.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

This review aims to evaluate the contemporary and evolving role of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging in arrhythmic risk stratification for patients with non-ischaemic cardiomyopathy, specifically focussing on dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and non-dilated left ventricular cardiomyopathy (NDLVC). This review synthesises current data on late gadolinium enhancement (LGE), parametric mapping, strain imaging and artificial intelligence (AI), and contextualises these among emerging genetic risk stratification approaches.

Recent findings

Left ventricular ejection fraction has been the cornerstone for guideline-based arrhythmic risk stratification in patients with DCM, despite limited precision. Observational data and meta-analyses have established the presence of replacement fibrosis through LGE-CMR as a powerful independent predictor of ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) and sudden cardiac death. Crucially, the absence of LGE identifies a low-risk cohort. Much recent focus has been on understanding whether more precise characterisation of scar can further enhance arrhythmic risk stratification, for example through scar quantification. Although data exists supporting a potential role for T1 mapping for arrhythmic risk prediction in this cohort, further research is required to support its widespread adoption. Emerging multimodal approaches using artificial intelligence and personalised computational "digital twins" are areas of important interest, offering scope for integration of imaging, electrocardiographic and genomic data layers. Arrhythmic risk stratification in non-ischaemic cardiomyopathies remains challenging despite significant advances. Progressive refinement in precision has accompanied a shift from a restrictive, functional assessment towards an integrated, substrate-driven precision model. CMR represents the cornerstone of this evolution.

title: A Whole-Heart Fluid-Structure Interaction Model for Transcatheter Mitral Valve Repair in Primary Mitral Regurgitation.
authorString: Sadipour M, Davey M, Wells DR, Kheradvar A, Vavalle JP, Griffith BE.
abstractText: Primary mitral regurgitation (MR) resulting from chordal rupture leads to acute volume overload and elevated left atrial pressure. Transcatheter edge-to-edge mitral valve repair (TMVr) devices can effectively reduce MR, but their impact on global cardiac mechanics and diastolic filling remains difficult to predict. This study develops a whole-heart FSI framework for TMVr by extending a previously developed whole-heart model to represent chordal rupture and edge-to-edge repair and to quantify their structural and hemodynamic consequences. A three-dimensional FSI model of the heart derived from cardiac CT imaging was used to simulate three conditions: healthy baseline, chordal rupture-induced MR, and post-TMVr. The immersed finite element-difference method enables fully coupled simulation of blood flow, valve dynamics, and myocardial contraction. Hemodynamic metrics, including regurgitant fraction (RF), left atrial pressure (LAP), stroke volume (SV), stroke work (SW), and pressure-volume relationships, were compared with clinical reference data. Chordal rupture produced moderate-to-severe MR (RF = 38%) and doubled left atrial V-wave amplitude, consistent with clinical observations. After TMVr, the central regurgitant jet produced by chordal rupture was eliminated, RF decreased to 21%, and LAP returned to near-baseline levels. However, the double-orifice valve configuration generated dual high-velocity inflow jets and reduced diastolic filling. The repair effectively reduces regurgitation and atrial pressure while also influencing diastolic filling and ventricular output. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating both regurgitation reduction and inflow characteristics when assessing TMVr outcomes and demonstrate the potential of patient-specific computational modeling for procedural planning and optimization.

title: The predictive value of <sup>99m</sup>Tc-MIBI SPECT/<sup>18</sup>F-FDG PET myocardial perfusion/metabolic imaging in patients with unrevascularized coronary chronic total occlusion and left ventricular dysfunction.
authorString: Ma X, Wang L, Fang W, Han X, Song S, Li B, Meng L, Guan M, Zhang J, Bi Y.

journal.title: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging

abstractText: To explore the predictive value of hibernating myocardium detected by single photon emission computed tomography (SEPCT)/positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion/metabolic imaging for the adverse cardiovascular events in unrevascularized chronic coronary total occlusion (CTO) patients with left ventricular (LV) dysfunction. Additionally, we explore whether hibernating myocardium in the CTO territory can independently predictive outcomes. Patients with at least one unrevascularized CTO on coronary angiography and LV dysfunction and who underwent rest 99mTc-MIBI SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging as well as 18F-FDG PET myocardial metabolic imaging were enrolled. All patients were followed up through telephone interviews and review of medical records. The extent of total hibernating myocardium, the extents of hibernating myocardium in the CTO and non-CTO territories, the extent of total scarred myocardium, and the extents of scarred myocardium in the CTO and non-CTO territories were calculated according to the segmental perfusion/metabolism score and the segmental assignment of coronary dominance and the results of coronary angiography. The Cox proportional hazards regression models were employed to analyze the relationship between the extent of hibernating or scarred myocardium and adverse cardiovascular events. Seventy eight patients were included in the final analysis. The median follow-up duration was 70.2 (27.7, 80.3) months. The extent of total hibernating myocardium and the extent of hibernating myocardium in the CTO territory were both independent predictors for cardiac death [hazards ratio (HR) = 1.289, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.083-1.533, P = 0.004; HR = 1.262, 95% CI 1.022-1.557, P = 0.030] and the composite endpoint events (HR = 1.190, 95% CI 1.032-1.372, P = 0.016; HR = 1.273, 95% CI 1.025-1.581, P = 0.029). The extent of hibernating myocardium in the non-CTO territory, the extent of total scarred myocardium, the extents of scarred myocardium in the CTO and non-CTO territories were all not associated with the outcome. 99mTc-MIBI /18F-FDG SPECT/PET myocardial perfusion/metabolic imaging has an important predictive value for prognosis in unrevascularized CTO patients with LV dysfunction. The extent of total hibernating myocardium, especially hibernating myocardium in the CTO territory, was an independent predictor for adverse cardiovascular events.

title: Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance in MINOCA and Acute Myocarditis: A Comparative Multiparametric Evaluation.
authorString: Tognola C, Daus F, Pedroli S, Bernasconi D, Sormani P, Bassi I, Milazzo A, Quattrocchi G, Giannattasio C, Pedrotti P.

journal.title: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging

abstractText: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) and acute myocarditis (AM) often present with overlapping clinical features and biomarker profiles, making early differential diagnosis challenging. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) is the reference modality for etiological assessment through functional evaluation and multiparametric tissue characterization. The aim of this study was to compare clinical and CMR characteristics of patients with MINOCA and suspected AM, and to identify imaging features enabling accurate differentiation. We retrospectively analyzed 127 consecutive patients undergoing CMR (February 2021-October 2024): 62 with suspected MINOCA and 65 with suspected AM. Clinical data, laboratory findings, ECG, and CMR parameters (cine imaging, T1/T2 mapping, extracellular volume [ECV], and late gadolinium enhancement [LGE]) were assessed. MINOCA patients were older (median 59 years) and predominantly female (64.5%), whereas AM patients were younger (median 29 years) and mainly male (81.5%). AM was associated with higher troponin and inflammatory markers. Among patients initially referred with suspected MINOCA, LGE was present in 50.0%, compared with 93.8% of those referred with suspected acute myocarditis (p < 0.001). MINOCA showed predominantly ischemic LGE patterns, while AM exhibited non-ischemic subepicardial or mid-wall LGE with myocardial edema. CMR confirmed myocardial infarction in 48.4% of patients and identified alternative diagnoses in 41.9%, while 9.7% had normal CMR findings. Multiparametric CMR reliably distinguishes ischemic from inflammatory myocardial injury in patients with chest pain, elevated troponin, and non-obstructive coronaries. Early CMR integration improves diagnostic accuracy and supports tailored management.

title: Disulfide-oxidized HMGB1 mutant construction and its mechanism in AMI-induced myocardial injury.
authorString: Sun G, Xu X, Jiang S, Tang J, Zhao L, Yan H, Li N, Zhao H, Jin Z, Yang Y, Liu J.

journal.title: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death

abstractText: Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of mortality and disability worldwide. Disulfide-bond oxidized HMGB1 (ds-HMGB1) functions as a core damage-associated molecular pattern that mediates acute myocardial injury. Nevertheless, commercially available HMGB1 reagents exhibit mixed proteoforms, unstable biological activity and low receptor affinity, which greatly hinder mechanistic investigations in this field. This study generated a novel mutant full-length murine ds-HMGB1, systematically dissected its molecular mechanisms underlying aggravated ischemic myocardial injury, and sought to provide a standardized protein reagent and theoretical framework for HMGB1-targeted therapies against myocardial damage. A K184S/K185S mutant HMGB1 plasmid was constructed, and protein purified by three-step chromatography. Structural modeling, mass spectrometry, SPR and PLA were used to analyze conformation, modification and receptor binding kinetics. Hypoxic cardiomyocyte co-culture and mouse myocardial infarction models were established. Flow cytometry, echocardiography, histological staining, qPCR, Western blot and RNA-seq were applied to detect molecular phenotypes and signaling pathways. The K184S/K185S mutation preserved the native overall conformation and functional disulfide bond of HMGB1, while markedly enhancing HMGB1 binding to RAGE and promoting TLR4-MD2 complex assembly. In vitro experiments revealed that mutant ds-HMGB1 either acted directly on cardiomyocytes or synergized hypoxia through endothelial-cardiomyocyte paracrine signaling to induce robust intracellular ROS accumulation, mitochondrial dysfunction and cardiomyocyte apoptosis. In vivo administration expanded myocardial infarct size, impaired cardiac systolic performance and exacerbated inflammatory infiltration in cardiac tissue. Transcriptomic profiling identified 53 core injury genes specifically upregulated by ds-HMGB1 under ischemic stress. The mutant ds-HMGB1 developed in this study addresses the intrinsic drawbacks of commercial HMGB1 preparations. We further identified 53 key myocardial injury genes modulated by ds-HMGB1. This work delivers a standardized experimental reagent and multi-layered mechanistic evidence supporting HMGB1 as a therapeutic target for acute myocardial infarction.

title: Functional and Structural Neuroanatomic Correlates of Intraoperative Anesthetic Dose-Adjusted EEG Alpha Power Among Older Surgical Patients
authorString: Reekes T, Browndyke JN, Reese Smith M, Weiss Y, Yu J, Cooter Wright M, Kang HJ, Timko NJ, Boykin P, Hsia B, Devinney MJ, Berger M.
abstractText:
Background:

Alterations in intraoperative electroencephalography (EEG) alpha power and anesthetic dose-adjusted EEG alpha power (ADA-FP alpha power) have been associated with both preoperative cognitive impairment and postoperative delirium (POD) among older surgical patients, yet the neurologic underpinnings of alterations in these anesthetic brain response patterns are unknown.

Methods:

We conducted a single center prospective observational cohort study (ALADDIN), of older adults undergoing non-cardiac/non-cranial surgery, which included preoperative structural and resting state functional MRI, lumbar punctures to obtain CSF, 32 channel intraoperative EEG recordings, and repeated POD assessments. To account for anesthetic dose, frontoparietal EEG alpha power (ADA-FP alpha power) was adjusted using our established formula: [intraoperative alpha power]/(2.5 - end-tidal MAC fraction). Multivoxel pattern analysis (MVPA) with follow-up seed-to-voxel analyses identified functional connectivity patterns associated with intraoperative ADA-FP alpha power. Voxel-wise regression analysis with threshold free cluster estimation (TFCE) correction was used to evaluate associations between cortical thickness and ADA-FP alpha power. CSF biomarker values were obtained from NULISA proximity extension assays. Delirium incidence and severity was assessed with the 3-Minute Diagnostic Confusion Assessment Method (3D-CAM). Delirium severity area under the curve (AUC) during hospitalization was defined as the sum of all 3D-CAM delirium severity scores within the postoperative hospitalization period (for up to 7 days after surgery). The Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) was used in cases of non-verbal/intubated patients.

Results:

ALADDIN enrolled 215 patients, of whom 168 underwent surgery and had high-quality intraoperative EEG data (44.6% female; mean age 70.9 years). MVPA showed that ADA-FP alpha power was associated with altered functional connectivity within the bilateral frontal poles, left superior frontal gyrus and the right superior parietal lobule (p-FWE < 0.05). Seed-to-voxel analyses revealed that higher ADA-FP alpha power was associated with increased connectivity between DMN MVPA regions and DMN, DAN and salience/ventral attention and decreased connectivity with visual regions. Conversely, right superior parietal lobule connectivity shifted towards greater DMN segregation and increased somatosensory/motor coupling (p-FWE < 0.05). Lower ADA-FP alpha power was also associated with lower cortical thickness in left occipitotemporal and superior parietal cortices (TFCE-corrected p < 0.05). ADA-FP alpha power was also lower among participants with (vs those without) postoperative ward/floor delirium (mean difference, 1.33; 95% CI, 0.22 to 2.44; p=0.019), and ADA-FP alpha power was inversely associated with peak delirium severity (spearman's rho = -0.26; 95% CI, -0.40 to -0.11; p <0.001) and delirium severity AUC (spearman's rho = -0.28; 95% CI, -0.42 to -0.13; p < 0.001).

Discussion:

These findings suggest a functional and structural neuroanatomic basis for the decreased EEG ADA-FP alpha power values seen among some older surgical patients, which may explain the association between decreased EEG ADA-FP alpha power and increased rates of both preoperative cognitive impairment and postoperative delirium. More specifically, these findings suggest that altered default mode and dorsal attention network connectivity is linked to decreased EEG ADA-FP alpha power and raise the possibility that preoperative/baseline functional connectivity alterations within these networks may play a role in delirium risk.

title: Impact of Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Burden on Echocardiographic Remodeling and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Hypertension
authorString: Kim HM, Bak M, Park J, Choi H, Yoon YE, Cho G, Hwang I.
abstractText:
Aims:

: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome highlights the interrelationship between metabolic, renal, and cardiovascular disorders. However, whether CKM burden influences longitudinal cardiac structural and functional recovery and subsequent cardiovascular outcomes remains unclear.

Methods:

We studied 1,600 patients from the STRATS-HHD registry who underwent echocardiography at baseline and 6-18 months after treatment initiation. CKM burden was defined by obesity, diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and severe hypertension (0-1, 2, or ≥3 components). The primary outcome was cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization (HHF).

Results:

CKM burden was 0-1 in 973 patients (60.8%), 2 in 440 (27.5%), and ≥3 in 187 (11.7%). Higher burden was associated with worse baseline cardiac abnormalities and increased primary outcome risk (adjusted HR, 3.09; 95% CI, 1.92-4.98 for ≥3 vs 0-1; adjusted HR, 1.53; 95% CI, 1.27-1.84 per +1 CKM component). The prognostic association persisted after additional adjustment for hepatic steatosis index-defined metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. Despite overall improvement in most echocardiographic parameters after treatment, patients with CKM burden ≥3 showed less favorable E/e′, LV global longitudinal strain (GLS), and LA stiffness index at follow-up. Normalization of these parameters at follow-up was associated with substantially lower subsequent cardiovascular risk. Mediation analyses suggested that echocardiographic abnormalities partially mediated the association between high CKM burden and the primary outcome.

Conclusion:

CKM burden identifies hypertensive patients with less favorable cardiac function after treatment and increased cardiovascular risk. These findings highlight the association of CKM burden with cardiac functional recovery and prognosis in patients with hypertension.

title: Ruxolitinib adverse events beyond the disease: an indication-restricted and class-comparative disproportionality analysis in myelofibrosis
authorString: Gaddam DP, Devi S.
abstractText: Aim: To characterise the post-marketing safety signals of ruxolitinib in myelofibrosis and to separate drug effects from those of the disease, the Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor class and reporting. Methods: Primary-suspect ruxolitinib reports carrying a myelofibrosis or myeloproliferative neoplasm indication in the US Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS; 2004Q1–2025Q4) were compared with 19,485,990 background reports using four disproportionality measures. Signals were re-estimated against a background restricted to these indications and head-to-head against fedratinib, pacritinib and momelotinib, then classified against the prescribing information. Results: Of 2,041 preferred terms in 26,892 reports, 625 were signals (264 high-confidence); 133 were disease-related and 154 undocumented. Indication restriction retained 38 and the head-to-head comparison 10; 366 could not be estimated head-to-head. Of the seven terms passing both, three were clinical: anaemia (reporting odds ratio 9.92, 95% CI 9.50–10.36), weight increased (3.05, 95% CI 2.85–3.27) and contusion (6.40, 95% CI 5.96–6.88); weight increased exceeded the comparators 6.10-fold. Squamous cell carcinoma of skin (12.29, 95% CI 10.01–15.09), herpes zoster and tuberculosis (8.20, 95% CI 6.91–9.72) persisted within myelofibrosis. Portal vein thrombosis (7.52, 95% CI 5.28–10.71) did not, and myocardial infarction, stroke, deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism were not signals. Conclusion: Most crude ruxolitinib signals in myelofibrosis reflect the disease. Erythroid suppression and weight gain distinguish ruxolitinib from the other myelofibrosis JAK inhibitors, and its labelled skin cancer and opportunistic infection risks persist within the indication, whereas the class warnings on cardiovascular and venous thromboembolic events find no counterpart in its reports.

title: Effects of Plaque Morphology and Vascular Curvature on Rupture Risk in Coronary Atherosclerosis: A Parametric Computational Fluid Dynamics Study
authorString: Huang J, Huang C.
abstractText: Plaque rupture is a leading mechanism underlying acute myocardial infarction and has been associated with elevated wall shear stress (WSS) and wall shear stress gradient (WSSG). This study uses a parametric computational fluid dynamics (CFD) approach to investigate the effects of plaque morphology and vascular curvature on coronary hemodynamics. Idealized coronary artery geometries containing atherosclerotic plaques were modeled using OpenFOAM. The parameters included percent area stenosis, plaque longitudinal skewness, eccentricity, and vascular curvature. The incompressible Navier–Stokes equations were solved using a non-Newtonian blood viscosity model and pulsatile flow boundary conditions. WSS and WSSG were then evaluated from the resulting flow fields. For concentric plaques, increasing vascular curvature produced approximately linear increases in both WSS and WSSG, with symmetric responses at positive and negative curvature angles.
