In contrast, eccentric plaques exhibited asymmetric and nonmonotonic responses to vascular curvature. At an eccentricity of 0.2, the lowest peak WSS and WSSG occurred at a curvature angle of -15 degrees. Proximally skewed eccentric plaques combined with large positive curvature angles produced the highest WSS and WSSG. These findings demonstrate that plaque morphology and vascular geometry interact to strongly influence local coronary hemodynamics, highlighting the importance of accounting for both factors when assessing hemodynamic conditions associated with plaque vulnerability.

title: An Unexpected Cause of STEMI in Partially Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot.
authorString: Iavarone M, Formigli D, Vetrano DS, Rossi LU, Esposito GM, Covino S, Orlando A, Murredda A, Mollo N, Scherillo M.
abstractText:
Background

Coronary embolism (CE) is an uncommon but clinically relevant nonatherosclerotic cause of ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Adult patients with congenital heart disease may be particularly vulnerable when residual intracardiac shunts, atrial enlargement, and atrial arrhythmias coexist.

Case summary

A 77-year-old man with partially repaired tetralogy of Fallot, residual ventricular septal defect with bidirectional shunting, and new-onset atrial fibrillation presented with inferior STEMI. Coronary angiography revealed distal right coronary artery occlusion with a large thrombus burden, in the absence of significant atherosclerotic disease. Sustained mechanical aspiration thrombectomy was successfully performed, with clinical and electrocardiographic improvement.

Discussion

To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of sustained mechanical aspiration thrombectomy for STEMI due to CE in an adult patient with congenital heart disease with residual intracardiac shunt.

Take-home message

In adult patients with congenital heart disease with STEMI, CE should be suspected when intracardiac shunts and embolic risk factors coexist.

title: High-Grade Atrioventricular Block and Recurrent Cardiac Arrest in Suspected Isolated Cardiac Sarcoidosis.
authorString: Talib AM, Alalawi S, Abozinadah YM, Boudal AM, Saklou RM, Mandoorah BM, Alfakih A, Elsheikh AH, Ibrahim OM, Bezerra MA, Ouriques BF, Alyousef HA, Gharbi MA, Azhari A.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiac sarcoidosis may cause advanced atrioventricular block, ventricular dysfunction, and sudden cardiac death. Isolated cardiac presentations are diagnostically challenging when histologic confirmation and fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography are unavailable.

Case summary

An 18-year-old woman with recurrent syncope developed high-grade atrioventricular block and recurrent brady-asystolic cardiac arrest requiring temporary transvenous pacing. Echocardiography showed severe left ventricular dysfunction. Cardiac magnetic resonance demonstrated regional septal thickening, basal to midseptal midmyocardial late gadolinium enhancement and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 38.9%. No extracardiac sarcoid pattern or biopsy target was identified. Giant cell myocarditis and inherited cardiomyopathy remained important alternative diagnoses. She received corticosteroid therapy and subsequently underwent cardiac resynchronization therapy-defibrillator implantation.

Conclusion

Cardiac sarcoidosis should remain a diagnostic consideration in young patients with malignant conduction disease and inflammatory cardiomyopathy, while important mimics must be actively considered.

title: Longitudinal blood pressure trajectories and time to stroke among hypertensive patients: A Bayesian multivariate joint modeling study in Benishangul-Gumuz, Ethiopia.
authorString: Assefa SK, Tadesse K, Yenus S, Tegene T, Bekeko SD, Abegaz HM, Endalemew SG, Feleke DB, Bemgako AB, Gobena AE, Redi BA, Asgedom DK.
abstractText: Stroke is a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with hypertension being its most important modifiable risk factor. Although the association between elevated blood pressure and stroke is well established, the extent to which longitudinal blood pressure patterns influence the timing of stroke remains poorly understood, particularly in low-resource settings. We investigated the association between longitudinal systolic and diastolic blood pressure trajectories and time to stroke among hypertensive patients in Ethiopia. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 494 newly diagnosed hypertensive patients receiving follow-up care at two general hospitals in Benishangul-Gumuz, Ethiopia, between January 1, 2015, and September 1, 2024. Time to stroke was analyzed using a Cox proportional hazards model, while repeated systolic and diastolic blood pressure measurements were modelled using linear mixed-effects models. The longitudinal and survival processes were jointly estimated using a Bayesian multivariate joint modelling framework. Posterior adjusted hazard ratios (AHRs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs) were estimated. The incidence of stroke was 2.19 per 100 person-years (95% CI: 1.60-2.64). Higher current underlying systolic and diastolic blood pressure levels were associated with increased stroke risk, with posterior AHRs of 3.25 (95% CrI: 1.85-5.83) and 2.32 (95% CrI: 1.35-4.27), respectively. Older age (≥65 years; AHR: 6.18; 95% CrI: 2.32-18.05), comorbidity (AHR: 4.00; 95% CrI: 1.72-10.25), and stage II hypertension (AHR: 4.06; 95% CrI: 1.49-16.36) were associated with earlier stroke occurrence. Rural residence was associated with a lower hazard of stroke (AHR: 0.16; 95% CrI: 0.05-0.40). Higher longitudinal systolic and diastolic blood pressure trajectories were associated with earlier stroke occurrence. These findings support regular blood pressure monitoring and targeted prevention strategies among older adults and patients with comorbidities in similar resource-limited settings.

title: Impact of cerebral venous outflow on futile recanalization despite complete reperfusion following mechanical thrombectomy.
authorString: Adiyaman HB, Uysal Kocabas Z, Aykac O, Ozdemir AO.
abstractText: A substantial proportion of patients with acute ischemic stroke remain functionally dependent despite complete angiographic reperfusion (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction [mTICI] 3) after mechanical thrombectomy (MT). This mismatch, commonly termed futile recanalization, may reflect tissue-level hypoperfusion not captured by arterial reperfusion grading. We investigated whether cerebral venous outflow, assessed using the Cortical Vein Opacification Score (COVES), provides prognostic information beyond conventional clinical and arterial imaging variables. We retrospectively analyzed 420 adults with anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion who underwent MT between 2015-2025 and achieved mTICI 3 reperfusion. Venous outflow was graded on baseline computed tomography angiography using COVES. Futile recanalization was defined as a 90-day modified Rankin Scale score of 3-6. Independent associations with futile recanalization were evaluated using multivariable binary logistic regression. Futile recanalization occurred in 191 patients (45.5%). After adjustment for age, admission NIHSS, ASPECTS, total passes, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, previous stroke, and arterial collateral status, higher COVES remained independently associated with lower odds of futile recanalization (OR per 1-point increase, 0.649; 95% CI, 0.537-0.784; p < 0.001). Age (OR, 1.031; p = 0.005), admission NIHSS (OR, 1.091; p = 0.001), and total passes (OR, 1.538; p < 0.001) were independently associated with higher odds of futile recanalization. Arterial collateral status was not independently associated with outcome. COVES showed greater discrimination than admission NIHSS (AUC, 0.742 vs 0.624). Baseline COVES was independently associated with 90-day functional outcome among patients achieving complete reperfusion after MT. COVES may serve as a complementary prognostic imaging marker rather than a treatment-selection tool. Prospective external validation is required.

title: An update on post-marketing safety signals of sugammadex: A retrospective pharmacovigilance analysis of the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS).
authorString: Sun L, Jiang Y, Liang C, Li J, Zhong H, Qu L, An H, Feng Y.
abstractText: ObjectiveWith the expanding use of sugammadex, continued post-marketing surveillance remains warranted. This study aimed to characterize reporting patterns and update potential sugammadex-associated safety signals in the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS).MethodsWe conducted a retrospective pharmacovigilance study of FAERS reports from January 2012 through September 2025 in which sugammadex was the primary suspect drug. Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) preferred terms (PTs) were compared with all other drugs in the OpenVigil 2.1 FAERS reference set using the proportional reporting ratio (PRR), reporting odds ratio (ROR), and chi-square statistic. Signals were hypothesis-generating and did not establish incidence, comparative risk, or causality.ResultsA total of 1,077 unique cases were included. Among 887 cases with known sex, 443 (49.9%) were male and 444 (50.1%) were female; the median age among 710 age-known cases was 51 years (interquartile range, 29-66 years). Of 501 PTs evaluated, 92 met the prespecified statistical criteria. After separating 15 medication-error/product-use terms, 2 exposure terms, and 4 procedure/management descriptors, 71 clinical adverse-reaction PTs remained. In sensitivity analyses, 59 of 92 signals and 43 of 71 clinical PTs persisted at a ≥ 5; IC025 was >0 for 80 signals and conservative BH q-value upper bounds were <0.05 for 87 signals. Prominent clinical clusters involved hypersensitivity, cardiovascular, respiratory, and neuromuscular events. Kounis syndrome, complete atrioventricular block, and hypercapnia were absent from the approved adverse-reaction list, whereas post-procedural hemorrhage was interpreted in the context of labeled coagulation warnings.ConclusionsFAERS identified patterns of disproportionate reporting for sugammadex that warrant further evaluation, particularly for hypersensitivity and selected cardiovascular, respiratory, and neuromuscular events. These findings are signals rather than estimates of incidence, comparative risk, or causality. The three PTs absent from the approved adverse-reaction list require independent confirmation, and the post-procedural hemorrhage signal should be interpreted alongside labeled coagulation warnings.

title: A Wearable Ultrasound Sensor for the Simultaneous Assessment of Hemodynamics and Blood Pressure.
authorString: Li X, Zhu S, Wang H, Zhou Z, Wu B, Li Y, Zheng C, Fu Y, Tian Y, Liu T, Ma J, Zhang R, Zhang J.
abstractText: Cardiovascular disease remains a major global health burden, and monitoring vascular information is crucial for the management of cardiovascular disease in daily life. However, existing wearable technologies suffer from limitations such as poor signal quality, limited sensing modalities, and low accuracy. Here, we propose a wearable ultrasonic array patch system comprising 64 elements to overcome the above difficulties and be used for tracking blood dynamics and blood pressure fluctuations. Guided by finite-element piezoelectric simulations, the size of the ultrasonic array was designed. Additionally, the patch utilizes a hydrogel material to ensure proper coupling with the skin. Testing revealed that the patch achieves a -6 dB bandwidth of 71% and a peak-to-peak received voltage of 0.22 V. The patch achieves a high spatial resolution of 0.96 mm × 0.60 mm at a detection depth of 15 mm. The system employs two key approaches to acquire physiological information. The first is a multimodal acquisition scheme capable of simultaneously capturing relative blood pressure trends and hemodynamic characteristics. The second is an angle-dependent reduced vector Doppler framework that utilizes multi-angle beams to calculate blood flow vectors. This work builds on existing wearable ultrasound devices and establishes a platform for the continuous assessment and monitoring of vascular hemodynamics.

title: Multiplexed and implantable fiber sensor for real-time blood monitoring.
authorString: Wu Z, Chen F, Liang J, Zhang Y, Huang Q, Zhang C, Li P, Li S, Shu H, Cheng X, Tam HY, Chai Y, Zheng Z.
abstractText: Accurate and real-time monitoring of blood electrolyte composition, particularly sodium (Na<sup>+</sup>) and potassium (K<sup>+</sup>), is crucial for guiding intraoperative and postoperative decisions, as these ions regulate critical bodily functions such as cardiac rhythm and fluid balance. Current blood analysis relies on ex vivo blood sampling, which introduces substantial time delays and can be susceptible to inaccuracies caused by temperature fluctuations. To address these challenges, we report here a multiplexed and implantable fiber sensor (MIFS) capable of monitoring Na<sup>+</sup> and K<sup>+</sup> ions in real time directly in the bloodstream. MIFS integrates three parallel liquid metal channels with a multilayer surface-electrode architecture, which synergistically enhances sensitivity, minimizes sensing drift, ensures mechanical flexibility, and offers outstanding biocompatibility for vascular implantation. In vivo testing in rabbit models and validation in human blood samples demonstrate MIFS's superior sensing accuracy, real-time, and stable sensing in agreement with conventional ex vivo measurements. This work paves the way for real-time blood monitoring in clinical practice.

title: An innovative colon inflammation-targeting platform for ulcerative colitis treatment.
authorString: Islam W, Chen H, Li L, Salimian KJ, Selaru FM.
abstractText: The therapeutic options for patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) have recently expanded substantially. Tofacitinib, an oral small-molecule inhibitor of Janus kinase (JAK), recently FDA approved for ulcerative colitis, represented a paradigm shift in a field previously dominated by biologics. Tofacitinib, however, carries a black box warning for major adverse cardiovascular events, an elevated risk of malignancies, risk of blood clots, and pulmonary embolism. In addition, tofacitinib is avoided in pregnancy and used with caution in women of child bearing age due to potential risks to the developing fetus. Notably, these potential complications are all due to the systemic distribution of tofacitinib. To address these issues, we developed Lipo-tm-HA, a liposomal platform incorporating mannitol (m) and hyaluronic acid (HA) for targeting tofacitinib (t) to the inflamed colon. We characterized Lipo-tm-HA and have shown that it (i) remains stable in gastric conditions due to HA coating, (ii) adheres to transferrin in inflamed mucosa due to its negative charge, and (iii) enhances macrophage uptake through mannose receptor-mediated endocytosis. Due to targeting, we show that a single oral administration of Lipo-tm-HA at a dose of 10 milligrams per kilogram is superior in efficacy compared with daily treatment with free tofacitinib in a dextran sodium sulfate-induced colitis model. Collectively, our innovative formulation will enable colonic inflammation targeting, reduce systemic exposure, and allow administration of decreased doses.

title: Balancing protection and progress: is New Zealand's ethical review framework appropriate for low-risk research?
authorString: Benatar J, Wang T, Lesiawan E, Gonzales J, Van Pelt N, Nielsen L, Ershad S, O'Connor M, Sebastian J, Lever N, Altman N, Chan D, Somaratne J, Kueh A, Chaggar P, Scott T, Gladding P, Armstrong G, de Zoysa J, Webster M, Edwards NC, Pemberton J, Stewart R.
abstractText: Clinical audits, observational studies and patient registries are essential for evaluating healthcare quality, identifying inequities and improving patient outcomes. New Zealand's ethics system plays an essential role in protecting participants and maintaining public trust and includes pathways for expedited review of low-risk research. However, New Zealand already has proportionate review mechanisms. The difficulty is that, in practice, studies requiring temporary access to identifiable information often receive the same level of scrutiny regardless of their actual participant risk, creating barriers that can prevent valuable studies from proceeding. The cost of these barriers is overlooked. When low-risk research is delayed or abandoned, opportunities to improve care are lost. Important questions affecting Māori and Pacific communities may remain unanswered, inequities may persist and New Zealand risks contributing less to international research efforts. The burden also falls on clinicians, particularly early-career doctors, who may become discouraged from undertaking research altogether. We argue that more consistent application of existing principles of proportionate review would maintain appropriate ethical oversight while supporting a health system that learns from everyday practice and continually improves care for all New Zealanders.

title: Multienzyme cascade biotransformation of L-Tyrosine to Danshensu by engineered Escherichia coli.
authorString: Xiong T, Li S, Li X, Li X, Wu M, Liu J, Guo J, Li X.
abstractText: Danshensu (DSS), a water-soluble bioactive compound with significant antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, cardioprotective and neuroprotective properties, is widely utilized in cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease. In this study, we established a multi-enzyme cascade system in engineered Escherichia coli to synthesize DSS from L-Tyrosine. The initial co-expression of 4-hydroxyphenylacetate 3-monooxygenase (HpaBC), L-amino acid deaminase (aadL), glucose dehydrogenase (gdh) and D-lactate dehydrogenase (ldhD) yielded 5.1 mM DSS. The production of DSS increased to 6.53 mM through optimizing plasmid copy number. After optimizing the conditions, the yield of DSS reached 8.66 mM from strain 6. Finally, whole cell biotransformation using strain 6 in bioreactor yielded 19.47 mM DSS within 32h. These findings provide valuable insights for the scalable biosynthesis of pharmaceutically important compound of DSS from naturally available substrates of L-Tyrosine.

title: Intratracheal microspray delivery of iohexol for sustained lung-parenchymal enhancement in preclinical micro-computed tomography: A feasibility and acute-safety study in mice.
authorString: Lin SC, Lin KK, Aristyo K, Lin HM, Liu WH, Hsieh EH, Tseng CL.
abstractText: Preclinical thoracic micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) is constrained by the brief pulmonary enhancement window of intravenously (IV) administered iodinated contrast, which the kidneys clear rapidly. We performed a feasibility study in mice comparing IV tail-vein injection with intratracheal microspray instillation of the clinical agent iohexol. Mice received iohexol (100 µL, 500 mg/mL) by either route. Whole-body projections were acquired to 120 min and thoracic sections to 30 min, each animal scanned before contrast in the same session. Contrast distribution was recorded by compartment and quantified from regions of interest. IV delivery produced vascular and cardiac opacification with progressive bladder accumulation, which was the largest signal in every IV animal by 120 min. Intratracheal delivery produced widespread, comparatively uniform lung-parenchymal opacification at 5, 15 and 30 min with no discrete bladder opacity at any time; coronal thoracic signal was 0.77 at 5 min and 0.72 at 30 min, against 0.09 to 0.19 after IV injection. Acute safety was assessed at 5 and 29 h by serum biochemistry and histopathology against untreated controls. ALT, AST and blood urea nitrogen did not differ among groups. Creatinine was modestly higher than in controls after both routes, with no difference between routes, consistent with renal excretion of absorbed iohexol. Lung, heart, liver, spleen and kidney showed preserved architecture without acute injury. These data identify intratracheal microspray delivery as a practical way to hold iodine in the lung parenchyma across a thoracic micro-CT acquisition and provide the basis for a confirmatory quantitative study.

title: Q-AortaECG: A Quantum-Inspired Multi-Agent 12-Lead ECG System for Early Triage of Acute Aortic Syndrome.
authorString: Yu L, Qiao G, Jiang X, Liu Y, Wang P, Xi W, Fu W, Fang G, Dong Z.

journal.title: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics

abstractText: Acute aortic syndrome (AAS) is a time-critical vascular emergency in which delayed recognition may occur because the presenting symptoms and electrocardiographic phenotypes often overlap with acute coronary syndrome, pulmonary embolism, pericarditis, and other emergency diagnoses. Computed tomographic angiography (CTA) remains the confirmatory standard, but the 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) is usually obtained earlier, is universally available at triage, and may carry distributed signatures of malperfusion, ischemia mimicry, autonomic stress, conduction delay, and hemodynamic compromise. We developed Q-AortaECG, a classically implemented quantum-inspired multi-agent ECG system that integrates multiscale waveform representations, specialist ECG agents, density-state uncertainty fusion, a variational-circuit style consensus layer, and a safety-gated multidisciplinary team-style report for early AAS triage. The system was evaluated in three suspected-AAS/CTA-evaluable cohorts comprising 1,251 patients, including 467 with CTA-, surgery-, or autopsy-confirmed AAS. Across 700 locked-test patients, Q-AortaECG achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.881 (95% confidence interval (CI), 0.852-0.908), area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.743 (95% CI, 0.695-0.790), sensitivity of 0.955 (231/242; 95% CI, 0.920-0.977), specificity of 0.721 (330/458; 95% CI, 0.677-0.761), positive predictive value (PPV) of 0.643, and negative predictive value (NPV) of 0.968 at the prespecified high-sensitivity threshold. Performance remained consistent in external retrospective validation and prospective silent-run evaluation, although AUPRC decreased in the lower-prevalence prospective cohort. Ablation experiments supported the contributions of self-supervised ECG pretraining, agent specialization, density-matrix uncertainty fusion, and differential diagnosis modeling. In a counterbalanced paired reader study, Q-AortaECG assistance improved overall clinician sensitivity from 0.696 to 0.870 while preserving specificity (0.851 ver sus 0.846). In prospective silent-run analysis, counterfactual alerts would have advanced the median time to the correct diagnostic pathway from 187 to 61 minutes among initially unsuspected AAS presentations. These findings support ECG first, calibrated, safety-gated decision support as an early warning scaffold for AAS triage, while preserving CTA and expert imaging interpretation as the diagnostic standard.

title: High cardiometabolic burden among people with HIV and obesity in Peru.
authorString: Hidalgo JA, Pinedo Y, Agurto EC, Cárdenas L, Gómez de la Torre JC, Ayarza R, Valenzuela-Rodríguez G, Rocca TJ, La Rosa A.
abstractText:
Introduction

Cardiometabolic disease has been studied in people with HIV, but evidence focused on people with HIV and obesity remains limited. This study assessed atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, metabolic abnormalities, markers of inflammation, and cardiovascular risk scores among people with HIV and obesity.

Methods

We conducted an observational, cross-sectional study in clinically stable people with HIV aged ≥35 years and BMI >30 kg/m² in Lima-Callao, Peru, in 2024.

Results

Participants enroled were 126; 77.7% were male, mean age was 50.6 years, mean time on antiretroviral therapy (ART) was 12.4 years, mean CD4 count was 759.8 cells/µL, and 97.6% had HIV-RNA <200 copies/µL. Mean BMI was 34.0. Clinical cardiovascular disease history was uncommon (2.4%); however, carotid Doppler ultrasound showed atherosclerotic changes in 34.4% (increased CIMT or carotid plaque), which associated with older age and longer time of ART. Abnormal glucose metabolism was identified in 89.7%, dyslipidemia in 82.5%, metabolic syndrome in 50.8%, elevated inflammatory markers in 28.2%, and low apolipoprotein A1 in 22.6%. Only 8.1% had normal findings across all evaluations. High cardiovascular risk was observed in 19.4% by Framingham, 9.4% by ACC/AHA, and 75.4% by HIV-CARDIO-PREDICT score.

Conclusions

This population of middle-aged, clinically stable people with HIV and obesity presented substantial burden of subclinical atherosclerosis and metabolic abnormalities despite low reported cardiovascular disease history. Cardiovascular risk estimates varied substantially across scores, with an HIV-specific score identifying a much higher proportion of patients as high risk than general-population scores. Targeted evaluation and timely preventive management may help reduce cardiometabolic complications.

title: The cardiovascular risk of metabolically healthy obesity: an inflammatory perspective.
authorString: Lozano-Núñez J, Lakshmi A, Benny BA, Sharma P, Jayakumar A, Swathi NL.

journal.title: Journal of basic and clinical physiology and pharmacology

abstractText: Metabolically healthy obesity (MHO) is a heterogeneous phenotype characterized by preserved traditional metabolic markers despite excess adiposity. However, accumulating evidence suggests that MHO may not be uniformly benign and may confer increased long-term cardiovascular risk through inflammatory and adipose tissue-mediated mechanisms. This narrative review synthesizes contemporary evidence on cardiovascular risk in MHO, focusing on visceral adiposity, ectopic fat, and immune metabolic pathways. Literature published between January 2010 and December 2025 was identified through PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library. Across the reviewed evidence, MHO is frequently associated with the progression to metabolically unhealthy obesity, although transition rates and cardiovascular risk estimates vary according to MHO definitions. Visceral and ectopic fat are associated with subclinical atherosclerosis, coronary calcification, and cardiovascular events, including in individuals without overt metabolic abnormalities. Evidence regarding heart failure and ventricular dysfunction remains limited and inconsistent. Low-grade inflammation and adipose immune remodeling, including NLRP3 inflammasome activation, provide plausible mechanisms, although human evidence remains predominantly observational. Key gaps include inconsistent MHO definitions, limited longitudinal imaging and biomarker integration, population diversity, and lack of validated MHO-specific risk models. Standardized phenotyping and prospective validation of inflammation-based risk stratification are required.

title: Circadian rhythms in health and disease.
authorString: Liu X, Du X, Qi S, Yuan L, Liu L, Zhang K, Wang L, Zhang W, Liu Q, Wu M, Huang Y.
abstractText: Circadian rhythms, serving as a crucial temporal bridge linking neural activity and pathological biology, are regulated by central pacemaker neurons to maintain cellular homeostasis and coordinate diverse biological processes. Circadian rhythm disruption is closely associated with various diseases, including neurodegenerative disorders, metabolic disorders, and cancer. Circadian rhythms are controlled by core clock genes, such as BMAL1 and CLOCK, modulating numerous physiological processes, encompassing metabolism, immune responses, neural activity, and hormone regulation. Circadian rhythms disruptions arising from shift work, jet lag, or inconsistent sleep schedules are implicated in both the onset and progression of numerous diseases, notably Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease. The article highlights how circadian dysregulation alters cellular processes to potentially accelerate disease progression. Circadian disruption results in impaired immune function, further promoting disease development and resistance to treatment. Potential therapeutic applications based on circadian biology, such as chronotherapy and personalized medicine, are also discussed. Recent technological advances, embodied in wearable devices and omics approaches, are increasingly providing deeper insights into circadian biology. Further unveiling the role of circadian in health and disease opens new avenues for tailoring treatment timing to patients' biological rhythms, thereby enhancing therapeutic outcomes across various diseases. By bridging fundamental circadian mechanisms with clinical pathology, this review provides a roadmap for future chronotherapeutic interventions in precision medicine.

title: Evaluation of Myocardial Blood Flow Using <sup>18</sup>F-flurpiridaz PET: Established Applications with Pharmacologic Stress and Roadmap for Exercise Stress Implementation.
authorString: Ali FZ, Slomka PJ, Packard RRS.
abstractText: Recently approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration, 18F-flurpiridaz for positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) enables high-quality assessment of myocardial blood flow (MBF). Its half-life of approximately 110 min supports regional distribution and allows unit-dose delivery. These features make this probe well suited for MBF quantitation and expand access to quantitative cardiac PET at smaller centers. During pharmacologic stress, absolute MBF and myocardial flow reserve provide incremental diagnostic information beyond relative perfusion imaging. These measures have been validated across multiple methods and software platforms. Further study of this tracer under peak exercise may provide clinically relevant assessment of myocardial demand-induced changes in flow. Potential investigational approaches include artificial intelligence (AI)-derived virtual MBF, exercise-adjusted standardized uptake value (SUV) ratio-derived myocardial flow reserve (MFR) surrogate, and direct kinetic modeling during in-scanner ergometry. While conceptually promising, limitations inherent to exercise-based approaches in stress MBF and/or MFR estimation highlight the need for pragmatic research strategies before potential clinical applicability.

title: The AGT M235T variant and renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system parameters in a predominantly hypertensive elderly black South African cohort: a hypothesis-generating descriptive case series.
authorString: Grobler CJ, Oldewage-Theron W, Chalwe JM.
abstractText: Hypertension (HTN) is a key cardiovascular risk factor, with its pathogenesis remaining incompletely understood. Blood pressure (BP) regulation involves the Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS), including the Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE), Angiotensin I (Ang I) and Angiotensin II (Ang II). The rs699 variant (M235T) may influence BP via the RAAS. This study aimed to evaluate the relationships between the rs699 genotypes, RAAS parameters, BP, Body mass index (BMI) and gender in a black elderly population. Data were collected from 48 participants aged ≥60 years, using World Health Organization (WHO) obesity guidelines and South African Hypertension Society (SAHS) 2019 standards for HTN categories. Statistical analysis was performed using IBM SPSS version 27 and Python 3.14. Most participants possessed the rs699 variant (GG: 93.8%, AG: 4.2%). ACE levels were low in 64.6%, while Ang II was elevated in the same percentage. The majority were classified as hypertensive and obese. No significant associations were found between the rs699 variant and ACE, Ang I, Ang II, HTN, BMI or gender, though BMI showed sex-related differences in females. Our findings suggest no significant association of the rs699 variant on RAAS or cardiometabolic parameters within the study population, warranting cautious interpretation. These findings require validation in larger and more diverse populations, as meaningful statistical inferences cannot be drawn from the current data.

title: The sirtuin family: from mechanisms to therapy.
authorString: Xiao J, Li Y, Xie Y, Chen Y, Liu Q, Li H, Sun R.
abstractText: Sirtuins (SIRT1-SIRT7) are evolutionarily conserved NAD<sup>+</sup>-dependent deacylases that function as metabolic sensors, coupling cellular metabolic state to epigenetic, transcriptional and post-translational regulatory programs across distinct subcellular compartments. Despite two decades of research, isoform- and disease-specific aspects remain poorly integrated, limiting both conceptual clarity and therapeutic translation. This review synthesizes recent advances in sirtuin biology into a family-wide framework. Rather than functioning as isolated longevity factors, sirtuins operate as a distributed compartmentalized regulatory network in which nuclear SIRT1, SIRT6 and SIRT7, cytosolic SIRT2 and mitochondrial SIRT3, SIRT4 and SIRT5 collectively govern glucose and lipid metabolism, mitochondrial quality control, autophagy, inflammation and immune tolerance. This network operates across metabolic disorders, cardiovascular and neurodegenerative diseases, inflammatory conditions and cancer, where dysregulated sirtuin signalling influences disease development in a disease- and tissue-specific manner. Therapeutic strategies are evaluated, ranging from isoform-selective small-molecule modulators and NAD<sup>+</sup>-targeted interventions to emerging protein-degradation approaches, with isoform selectivity, off-target effects and the systemic consequences of NAD<sup>+</sup> modulation identified as key translational barriers that have contributed to heterogeneous clinical outcomes. Viewing sirtuins as a context-sensitive compartmentalized network, not isolated targets, offers a coherent framework to guide mechanistic interrogation and the design of more precise sirtuin-based therapies, with priority areas including tissue-selective degradation and network-level biomarkers.

title: Traversing the labyrinth: multimodality imaging of Kawasaki disease with saccular coronary artery aneurysms.
authorString: Sanders E, Arthur L.

journal.title: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging

abstractText: Kawasaki disease (KD), an acute vasculitis of childhood, is the leading cause of acquired heart disease in developed countries with approximately 25% of untreated cases resulting in coronary artery aneurysms (1). Treatment during the acute phase with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) and aspirin reduces the prevalence of coronary artery abnormalities; long-term management with thromboprophylaxis, beta blockers, statins, or surgical coronary artery bypass is determined based on coronary Z score, response to treatment, and evidence of myocardial ischemia throughout surveillance (2). The presented case highlights the severe complications of KD, necessity of multimodality imaging, and long-term management in high-risk patients.

title: Sequential multimodality imaging-guided transseptal strategy for cryoballoon ablation in cor triatriatum sinister.
authorString: Romano G, Bonomo V, Sabatino F, Giusti M, Polizzi V.

journal.title: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging

abstractText: To describe a sequential multimodality imaging strategy for transseptal access during cryoballoon ablation in a patient with cor triatriatum sinister (CTS). A 55-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and CTS underwent preprocedural cardiac computed tomography (CCT), followed by real-time transesophageal echocardiography (TEE), contrast confirmation, and fluoroscopic guidance during the procedure. CCT demonstrated pulmonary vein drainage into a Proximal Chamber (Posterior-Superior), separated from the Distal Chamber (Anterior-Inferior) by a membrane. Real-time TEE identified and confirmed an anterosuperior transseptal site, with septal tenting before needle passage. After a single BRK needle puncture, contrast confirmed access to the pulmonary-vein-containing chamber, allowing advancement of the FlexCath Advance catheter (Medtronic) and cryoballoon isolation of all 4 pulmonary veins without procedural complications. In CTS, transseptal access should be tailored to the individual atrial anatomy. Sequential use of CCT, real-time TEE, contrast, and fluoroscopy can provide complementary information at the successive stages of the procedure.

title: Aorto-Pulmonary Shunt Creation in Congenital Heart Disease: Different Indications, Various Modifications, but Common Technical Challenges.
authorString: Bakoš M, Georgiev S, Wustman K, Heinisch PP, Borgmann K, Renner D, Eicken A, Lemmer J, Ewert P, Gendera K.
abstractText: Percutaneous creation of an aorto-pulmonary (AP) shunt has been explored in preclinical models for over 15 years, yet its clinical application remains limited. Surgical AP shunts are widely used to augment pulmonary blood flow in cyanotic congenital heart disease, but repeated thoracic operations and general anesthesia carry substantial risks in critically ill or surgically complex patients. A less invasive transcatheter alternative could therefore represent a transformative option. We report a case series of two pediatric patients in whom a percutaneous connection between the aorta and pulmonary artery was successfully established. Indications were severe cyanosis due to compromised pulmonary blood flow in one child and suprasystemic pulmonary arterial hypertension requiring decompression in the other. The procedures were technically feasible and resulted in the intended immediate hemodynamic effects, either by enhancing pulmonary perfusion or by enabling right-to-left shunting for right heart decompression. Conceptually, percutaneous AP shunt creation parallels the transcatheter Potts shunt, which is increasingly recognized as a therapeutic option in pulmonary arterial hypertension. Both approaches establish controlled communication between the aorta and pulmonary artery, adapted to distinct physiological settings. Our report represents, to our knowledge, the first description of percutaneous AP shunt creation to improve pulmonary blood flow and oxygenation in congenital heart disease, as well as the first percutaneous connection between the ascending aorta and the pulmonary artery. These cases illustrate the technical feasibility of catheter-based AP shunt creation in selected pediatric patients and support further evaluation of this approach.

title: Maternal Anxiety Surrounding Fetal Cardiac Evaluation: A Prospective Single-Center Cohort Study.
authorString: Bogarapu S, Legro T, Jantzen DW, Shah JJ, Albaro CA.
abstractText: Fetal echocardiography has transformed prenatal cardiac diagnosis, yet the emotional burden of referral and evaluation remains poorly characterized. We aimed to quantify maternal anxiety before and after fetal cardiac evaluation (FCE), identify clinical predictors of anxiety, and assess whether anxiety changes following evaluation and consultation regardless of outcome. In this prospective cohort study, 117 pregnant women undergoing initial or follow-up FCE completed pre- and post-consultation assessments using a seven-item symptom inventory adapted from the Stanford Acute Stress Reaction Questionnaire (SASRQ; score range 7-42). Participants were classified as anxious or non-anxious by direct self-report. Scores were compared with paired t-tests; exploratory multivariable models adjusted for clinical, demographic, and referral covariates, including prior pregnancy loss, psychiatric history, and diagnostic outcome. 80% of participants (94/117) reported anxiety about the FCE before evaluation; prior pregnancy loss was associated with anxious state (p = 0.049). Following FCE and consultation, mean symptom scores in the anxious group fell from 15.07 to 9.03, a 6.04-point (40.1%) reduction (p < 0.001), with reductions across symptom domains regardless of diagnostic outcome. Scores in the non-anxious group did not change significantly (8.48 to 7.87; p = 0.27). Most women referred for FCE report anxiety before evaluation. FCE with consultation was associated with a substantial reduction in anxiety symptoms in these women, irrespective of whether a cardiac abnormality was found. Although the uncontrolled pre-post design cannot establish causation, these findings suggest that diagnostic clarity and expert consultation may themselves be anxiety-reducing and support evaluation of integrated psychosocial care models in fetal cardiology.

title: The role of extracardiac radiotracer biodistribution in the evaluation of cardiac amyloidosis: a retrospective multicenter study on [99mTc]Tc-DPD and [99mTc]Tc-HMDP.
authorString: Di Giorgio A, Battisti G, Bonazzi N, Prisco SE, Starace M, Longhi S, Fanti S, Berti V, Cappelli F, Bonfiglioli R.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging
journal.title: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
journal.isoabbreviation: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

abstractText: Bone scintigraphy using [99mTc]Tc-DPD or [99mTc]Tc-HMDP is a non-invasive cornerstone for diagnosing transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CA). However, their interchangeability and the clinical relevance of systemic extracardiac uptake (ExtCU) remain poorly defined. To systematically compare the diagnostic performance and whole-body biodistribution profiles of [99mTc]Tc-DPD and [99mTc]Tc-HMDP in patients with suspected cardiac amyloidosis (CA). We retrospectively evaluated a multicenter cohort of patients investigated for suspected CA who underwent late planar whole-body scintigraphy and targeted SPECT/CT with either radiotracer as part of their diagnostic workup. Inclusion required a final, confirmed diagnosis of ATTRwt, ATTRv, or AL amyloidosis. Myocardial visual Perugini score (VISUAL_PS) and systemic ExtCU (pulmonary, appendicular muscular, visceral, and miscellaneous) were recorded. The study included 224 patients (DPD: n = 109, comprising 70 ATTRwt, 20 ATTRv, 19 AL; HMDP: n = 115, comprising 90 ATTRwt, 13 ATTRv, 12 AL). In ATTRwt, the DPD cohort presented predominantly with Perugini Grade 2 (76%), whereas the HMDP cohort skewed toward Grade 3 (72%, p < 0.001). DPD was significantly associated with appendicular muscular uptake (ATTRwt: 84% vs. 38%, p < 0.001), creating a competitive "soft-tissue sink effect". Conversely, HMDP demonstrated a unique predilection for pulmonary retention (ATTRwt: 68% vs. 46%, p = 0.008; ATTRv: 61% vs. 10%, p = 0.006). Visceral uptake was rare in ATTR but was a robust negative predictor strongly favoring AL amyloidosis (OR 0.016, p < 0.001). [99mTc]Tc-DPD and [99mTc]Tc-HMDP possess distinct biodistribution profiles precluding direct interchangeability. HMDP maximizes myocardial contrast, whereas DPD provides a superior representation of the systemic musculoskeletal amyloid burden. Nuclear medicine physicians must adopt tracer-specific interpretive approaches to optimize non-invasive phenotyping. not applicable.

title: Thyroid-stimulating hormone exacerbates mitochondrial energy dysregulation and cardiac remodeling with involvement of the AMPK/PGC-1α pathway.
authorString: Lu X, Han Z, Zhao C, Wang J, Tian L.
abstractText: Subclinical hypothyroidism (SCH) is linked to the progression of heart failure (HF); however, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the role of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) in the regulation of HF and myocardial energy metabolism. In vitro, cardiomyocytes were treated with TSH to assess pathological stress markers and mitochondrial energy metabolism. In vivo, a SCH model was established in thyrocyte-specific TSHR knockout mice, with concurrent isoproterenol (ISO)-induced HF. Serum FT4 and TSH levels, cardiac function, and myocardial energy metabolism (ATP levels, mitochondrial ultrastructure, key metabolic enzymes) were evaluated. Cardiomyocyte-specific TSHR knockout mice were used to confirm findings, and the involvement of the AMPK/PGC-1α pathway was investigated in vitro. In vitro, TSH treatment increased the expression of pathological stress markers in cardiomyocytes. It also induced alterations in energy substrates, decreased ATP levels, and reduced mitochondrial membrane potential. In vivo, compared to the ISO group, mice in the SCH + ISO group exhibited more severe cardiac structural damage and functional impairment, accompanied by aggravated energy metabolism remodeling and mitochondrial dysfunction-characterized by lower ATP content, exacerbated mitochondrial ultrastructural damage, increased glycolysis, and decreased aerobic glucose oxidation. Notably, cardiomyocyte-specific TSHR knockout mitigated cardiac damage and metabolic remodeling in HF mice induced by ISO. Further mechanistic studies suggest that the AMPK/PGC-1α signaling pathway is involved in the regulation of TSH-mediated mitochondrial energy metabolism and cardiac remodeling. Our findings indicate that SCH exacerbates HF progression and further implicate TSH/TSHR signaling in the regulation of myocardial energy metabolism.

title: Combined multimodal monitoring during neonatal transition in preterm infants: feasibility, safety and post-implementation evaluation.
authorString: Oikonomopoulou N, Rodriguez MJ, Corredera A, Cortés-Ledesma C, Vierge E, Martinez-Orgado J, Arruza L.
abstractText: The transitional period involves major cardiovascular adaptations that could affect cerebral perfusion. Combined multimodal monitoring (CMM) may provide a more comprehensive physiological assessment than individual monitoring modalities. We aimed to evaluate the feasibility and safety of CMM integrating near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS), amplitude-integrated electroencephalography (aEEG), targeted neonatal echocardiography (TNE), and head ultrasound (HUS) during the transitional period in preterm infants ≤ 32 weeks' gestation and to explore healthcare professionals' perceptions following its implementation. Prospective observational cohort study. Participants underwent continuous NIRS and aEEG monitoring, two TNE assessment and one HUS during the first 72 h of life. Feasibility was defined as acquisition of ≥ 75% of intended NIRS and aEEG recording time, and completion of all imaging studies. Safety outcomes included TNE-related procedural intolerance and NIRS-related skin reactions. Healthcare professionals completed a post-implementation survey assessing acceptability and perceived clinical usefulness. Forty-seven infants were included. Overall CMM feasibility was 78.7%. Individual monitoring completion was 93.6% for NIRS, 95.7% for aEEG, 89.3% for TNE and 100% for HUS. Transient desaturations occurred in 7.9% of 89 TNE assessments, while mild NIRS-related erythema occurred in 11.3% of monitored infants. Healthcare professionals reported favorable perceptions of CMM, particularly regarding clinical relevance and complementarity with standard monitoring. CMM was feasible and well tolerated during the first 72 h of life in preterm infants ≤ 32 weeks' gestation and was perceived favorably by healthcare professionals. Future studies are needed to explore its impact on clinically relevant outcomes. • The transitional period in preterm infants involves complex cardiovascular and cerebral adaptations associated with an increased risk of brain injury. • Individual monitoring modalities (NIRS, aEEG, TNE and HUS) provide complementary information on cardiovascular and cerebral physiology but are commonly assessed separately. • Structured CMM integrating NIRS, aEEG, TNE and HUS is feasible and well tolerated during the transitional period in preterm infants ≤ 32 weeks' gestation. • Healthcare professionals perceive CMM as clinically relevant and complementary to standard monitoring, supporting further evaluation of integrated multimodal assessment in neonatal care.

title: Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia in Italian children: a road map through a single center's experience.
authorString: Perrino D, Monopoli D, Verrigni D, Lorefice E, Macchiaiolo M, Gonfiantini MV, Vecchio D, Taurisano R, Novelli A, Bartuli A, Gnazzo M, Buonuomo PS.
abstractText: This study aims to evaluate the clinical, biochemical, and molecular characteristics of pediatric patients with suspected familial hypercholesterolemia (FH, OMIM #143890) and to investigate whether the presence of pathogenic low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR) variants is associated with differences in lipid profile severity and treatment initiation compared with inconclusive genetic findings. We report the clinical, biochemical and molecular data of 382 patients diagnosed in a single pediatric center. Patients carrying pathogenic low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR) variants exhibited significantly more severe dyslipidemia compared with those with inconclusive genetic findings, particularly in terms of elevated LDL-C, the hallmark of FH. No significant differences were observed in age, weight, height, or body mass index, confirming that lipid abnormalities are primarily attributable to genetic factors. Treatment uptake was higher in the pathogenic group, with 87% initiating statin-based therapy compared with 50% in the inconclusive group, suggesting that a confirmed genetic diagnosis may improve treatment adherence. Pathogenic variants in the LDLR gene are associated with a more severe lipid profile and a higher likelihood of initiating lipid-lowering therapy. These findings support the clinical value of genetic testing in familial hypercholesterolemia, both for improving diagnostic accuracy and for promoting earlier therapeutic intervention and adherence. • Familial hypercholesterolemia is a common, treatable genetic disorder, and early diagnosis with lipid-lowering therapy from childhood reduces lifelong cardiovascular risk. • Most cases of heterozygous FH are caused by pathogenic LDLR variants, but data on treatment uptake in children are limited. • In 382 Italian children, those with pathogenic LDLR variants had higher LDL-C than those with inconclusive genetic results. Their lipid profiles also differed depending on the exon and protein domain affected. • Treatment was started in 87% of children with a confirmed genetic diagnosis and in 50% of those with inconclusive results. This suggests that genetic confirmation may help families accept treatment.

title: Interpretable computational SHG microscopy enables quantitative tissue phenotyping of cardiac remodeling in nonischemic heart failure
authorString: Master R, Poon W, Uzma R, Bannikov S, Krishnamoorthi MK, Veeraraghavan A, ZHAO H, Bhimaraj A, Raghunathan R, Wong ST.
abstractText: Heart failure is characterized by extracellular matrix remodeling and collagen deposition that impair myocardial function. Second harmonic generation (SHG) microscopy provides label-free visualization of fibrillar collagen and myosin but lacks standardized, interpretable, and quantitative frameworks with clinical-level performance. We present a feature extraction pipeline integrating 87 biologically interpretable SHG-derived metrics for automated classification of nonischemic heart failure in murine specimen. The framework distinguished normal, heart failure, and natural recovery states with area-under-the-curve values of 0.84-0.99, outperforming established open-source SHG feature extraction tools. These findings support interpretable, SHG-based quantification of cardiac remodeling and establish a methodology for future multimodal biophotonics applications.

title: Advanced Maternal Age Impairs Decidual Angiogenesis and Spiral Artery Remodelling
authorString: Duan WK, Nakatsui N, Spyracopoulos A, Castillo E, Garcia Rivas J, Bellissimo C, Riddell M.
abstractText: Pregnancy presents an extreme physiological challenge that relies on rapid angiogenic vascular expansion and remodelling to establish the maternal-fetal vascular unit at the uteroplacental interface. These adaptations to the pregnancy-specific decidual vasculature are necessary for pregnancy progression. Advanced age pregnancies (AAP; pregnant person >35 years old) are associated with increased risk of poor pregnancy outcomes. Despite increasing evidence of the centrality of vascular aging in mediating organotypic dysfunction, whether vascular aging in the decidua occurs in the context of AAP is unknown. Using a murine model of AAP, we find that alongside embryonic developmental delay and deficient placental vascularization, AAP dams had impaired decidual angiogenesis and spiral artery remodeling with imbalances in both systemic and local uterine angiogenic factor expression in the VEGF and angiopoietin signalling families. These findings reveal that pregnancy may expose vascular aging mechanisms that contribute to declining reproductive success and increased cardiovascular risk later in life.

title: BeatRatePy - Automated Hight-Throughput Python-Based Beat Rate Quantification and Generation of Speed and Contraction Traces
authorString: Held M, Partington W, Waring T, Dev A, Isherwood L, Boulton B, Sharma P, Herbert R, Kudoh T, Corbett AD, Burton RA.
abstractText: Analysing cardiac motion from label free imaging can be difficult, especially when recordings vary in quality or show complex movement. We developed a Python-based pipeline that automatically measures beat rate, contraction, speed from transmitted light timelapse data. The workflow runs in a Jupyter notebook and uses straightforward steps that can be followed easily, making the analysis accessible including to users with limited coding experience. Using human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes imaged on a Zeiss Cell Discoverer 7, the pipeline produced beat rates, contraction and contraction speed measurements that matched expected behaviour. To test wider use, we applied the same workflow to killifish larvae heart recordings and public datasets, changing only basic input parameters. The pipeline performed consistently across these different systems and did not require changes to the underlying code. By supporting clear parameter control and use across laboratories, microscopy platforms and repositories, this approach strengthens reproducible analysis of cardiac motion from label free imaging.

title: The anger-insula-body link in heart arrhythmias
authorString: Mazzola V, Martins-Dominati E, Bondolfi G, Arciero G.
abstractText: Anger is a well-known risk factor in cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) since it triggers a sympathetic hyperactivity of peripheral autonomic nervous system (ANS). As our previous findings showed, facing an angry situation instead of a joyful one elicits in healthy participants an affective engagement that involved mainly the insular reactivity and its connectivity. On the other hand, stimulating the insula, the key neural hub of the cardiovascular brain, can induce cardiac arrhythmias. Unfortunately, still little is known about the interplay between the anger and the insula as the underlying emotional-brain-body link that can trigger or precipitate a series of neurogenic cardiac events in CVDs patients. To address this question, we employed a multimodal method combining neuroimaging, behavioral and blood data to gain a more complete picture of the insula activity and its connectivity in patients with different types of heart arrhythmias. The present findings show a greater generalized involvement of the bilateral posterior insulae in the patients group both when facing angry context and squeezing the handgrip device, suggesting an automatic engagement of the sympathetic nervous system/SNS. Moreover, the bilateral insulae were functionally coupled with the bilateral lateral ventricles selectively under angry conditions, suggesting an insular role in glymphatic dysfunction and CSF dynamics due to the neurovascular coupling. Clearly, understanding this anger-insula-heart link may factually contribute to lower the probability of adverse cardiac outcomes in orienting the necessary treatment of the person, taking into account the emotion-related cardiovascular pathologies and the psychological health.

title: BMI Deviations from Genetic Prediction Are Associated with Distinct Molecular Signatures in Finnish Population Cohorts
authorString: Zhu T, Drouard G, Heikkinen A, Hukkanen M, Palviainen T, Berntzen BJ, Lyytikainen L, Raitoharju E, Pietilainen KH, Lehtimaki T, Raitakari O, Ala-Korpela M, Kaprio J, Cristofari R, Ollikainen M.
abstractText:
Objective:

Polygenic risk scores (PRS) estimate genetically predicted BMI, but lifestyle and environmental factors may cause deviations between observed and predicted BMI. We investigated whether such deviations are associated with distinct molecular profiles and whether these differ by direction of deviation.

Methods:

We analyzed 2,508 adults from the Finnish Twin Cohort and 1,715 from the Young Finns Study with clinical, metabolomic, DNA methylation, and proteomic data. PRS-informed residual BMI (rBMI) quantified deviations between observed and genetically predicted BMI. Associations between rBMI and multi-omic profiles were assessed using linear mixed-effects models with a hinge term to compare effects above vs. below genetic prediction. Twin analyses further accounted for shared genetic and environmental factors.

Results:

rBMI is associated with distinct cardiometabolic and molecular profiles depending on whether BMI is above or below genetic prediction. When BMI exceeds genetic prediction, rBMI shows stronger associations with inflammatory and cardiovascular markers. In contrast, several metabolites and plasma proteins show stronger associations when BMI is below genetic prediction. Epigenetic aging increases with higher rBMI regardless of direction. Similar patterns are observed in BMI-discordant twin pairs.

Conclusion:

Deviations from genetically predicted BMI are associated with distinct clinical and molecular signatures beyond absolute BMI alone.

title: Cardamonin and Alpinetin Mitigate Fructose-Induced Endothelial Damage: An In Vitro Evaluation Using HUVEC Model
authorString: Arya V, Rajendran K.
abstractText: Background Endothelial dysfunction is a pivotal mechanism in hypertension and cardiovascular disease. Excessive dietary fructose accelerates vascular injury by reducing nitric oxide (NO) bioavailability, activating inflammatory cascades, and upregulating adhesion molecules. Natural phytochemicals such as cardamonin and alpinetin possess antioxidant and vasoprotective properties, yet their efficacy against fructose-induced endothelial stress remains insufficiently characterized. Objective To evaluate and compare the prophylactic and therapeutic effects of cardamonin and alpinetin against fructose-induced endothelial dysfunction in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs), using losartan as a clinical benchmark. Methods HUVECs were exposed to fructose-induced metabolic injury and treated under pre-conditioning (prophylactic) and post-conditioning (therapeutic) regimens. Cytotoxicity was assessed by microscopy and MTT assays to define safe concentration ranges. Cytoprotective efficacy was quantified via viability assays, while mechanistic insights were obtained through RT-qPCR and agarose gel electrophoresis of eNOS, RAGE, Endothelin-1, and ICAM-1 transcripts. Results Alpinetin and losartan exhibited broad cytocompatibility, whereas cardamonin showed a narrower safety margin. In prophylactic assays, alpinetin and losartan preserved endothelial monolayers, while cardamonin provided limited cluster protection. In therapeutic assays, cardamonin demonstrated potent low-dose rescue, whereas alpinetin and losartan achieved recovery at higher concentrations. Molecular analyses confirmed that post-conditioning more effectively restored eNOS and suppressed RAGE and Endothelin-1, while pre-conditioning strongly reduced ICAM-1. Conclusion Cardamonin, alpinetin, and losartan confer distinct cytoprotective benefits against fructose-induced endothelial injury. Cardamonin excels in post-injury rescue, whereas alpinetin and losartan act as robust prophylactic stabilizers. These findings highlight the translational potential of phytochemicals as complementary strategies for mitigating metabolic endothelial dysfunction.

title: COVID-19 Vaccine Injury Compensation Claims in Israel: Characteristics, Approval Rates, and Factors Associated with Compensation
authorString: Brosh-Nissimov T, Rahav G, Stienlauf S, Moses AE.
abstractText: Background Vaccine-injury compensation programs (VICPs) are an essential component of national immunization programs, yet little data has been published regarding the characteristics of submitted claims or factors associated with compensation decisions. We analyzed all COVID-19 vaccine injury compensation claims (VICC) submitted and assessed in Israel. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study of all COVID-19 VICC submitted between February 2021 and March 2026. Data from all adjudicated claims were retrospectively analyzed under MoH Helsinki Committee approval (#008-2026). Standardized demographic, clinical, and causality assessment data were collected by all adjudicating specialists. Factors associated with claim approval were evaluated using univariate and multivariable analyses. Results Overall, 313 claims submitted by 268 individuals were adjudicated by five specialists; 69 (22%) claims involving 67 (25%) individuals were approved for compensation. Approval was independently associated with the absence of a relevant prior comorbidity (aOR 0.3, p  = 0.022), claims following the first two vaccine doses (aOR 0.3 for ≥ 3 vs. 1–2 doses, p  = 0.013), and a shorter interval from vaccination to symptom onset (aOR 0.97/day, p  = 0.001). Approval rates did not differ according to adjudicating specialist, legal representation, sex, ethnicity, psychiatric comorbidity, vaccine type, or injury severity. The most frequently compensated conditions included myocarditis/pericarditis (n = 52 claims, 42% approved), facial palsy (n = 18, 44%), and inflammatory skin diseases (n = 14, 57%), whereas no cardiovascular, thrombotic, or neoplastic conditions were approved. Compensation decisions were strongly associated with established causality assessment criteria, including temporal association, absence of alternative explanations, and supportive epidemiological evidence. Conclusions Approximately 40 COVID-19 VICC were submitted per million vaccinated individuals in Israel, of which one-quarter were approved. Compensation decisions were consistently associated with established causality assessment principles rather than demographic or procedural factors. These findings provide the first comprehensive description of the Israeli COVID-19 VICP and contribute to greater transparency regarding vaccine injury compensation.

title: High Sensitivity Hemoglobin Biosensing Using a Plus Shaped Gold Metasurface Refractive Index Sensor
authorString: Musthafa S, Hussain FM, Asif AH, Khan AM.
abstractText: Hemoglobin concentration is one of the most important clinical parameters for diagnosis of anemias or cardiovascular diseases but label-free accurate quantification of this is still reliant on bulky laboratory infrastructure. A gold with Germanium Antimony Tellurium (Ge 2 Sb 2 Te 5 ) metasurface is called GST with a Plus shape is proposed here as a reconfigurable intelligent surface for hemoglobin detection. Localized surface plasmon resonance oscillations of the gold resonators are analyzed to establish the unit cell geometry and optical properties of hemoglobin within its physiological refractive index range to specify the sensing window. Gold is chosen for its chemical stability and plasmonic strong confinement of the plasmonic field, in the RIS configuration a reconfigurable layer is added to retune the resonant behavior after fabrication. Using numerical simulation, the absorption, electric-field, and magnetic-field response is evaluated, and the response to the geometric changes is analyzed. The spectral response is obtained and key geometrical parameters are optimized systematically to maximize the sensitivity. The design is then compared to reported hemoglobin sensors using metasurfaces. The maximum sensitivity of the crystalline GST is 766.67 nm/RIU which exceeds the maximum sensitivity of amorphous GST, 700 nm/RIU. The thickness of the substrate is 0.6 micrometers and metasurface is 0.3 micrometers. The crystalline GST is more sensitive than the amorphous GST. Then the suggested sensor is compared in contrast to the previous designed ones that are already published. The comparison shows that the designed design is able to identify the smaller change compared to the alternatives, thus it could be proposed as the basis to be developed further for medical sensors.

title: Trajectories of Cardiopulmonary-Depressive Symptom Comorbidity Burden and Subsequent Activities of Daily Living Disability and Cognitive Function among Middle-Aged and Older Chinese Adults: A Nationally Representative Longitudinal Cohort Study
authorString: Cao# F, Jiang# Y, Chen C.
abstractText: Background With population aging, the coexistence of cardiopulmonary diseases and psychological distress has evolved into a severe symptom cluster. Traditional static disease count fails to capture the dynamic accumulation of chronic conditions. This study aimed to identify the long-term trajectories of comorbidity burden characterized by cardiopulmonary diseases and depressive symptoms, and to explore their predictive effects on activities of daily living (ADL) disability and cognitive function among middle-aged and older adults in China. Methods Data were derived from four waves of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) conducted between 2011 and 2018, and a total of 13,008 participants were included. A comorbidity score (range: 0–3) was constructed based on depressive symptoms, chronic respiratory diseases and cardiovascular diseases. Growth mixture modeling (GMM) was used to identify comorbidity trajectories. Multivariate logistic regression and linear regression analyses were applied to examine the associations between trajectories and incident ADL disability as well as memory scores in 2018. Results Three distinct trajectories were identified: stable low burden group (81.2%), persistent high burden group (12.6%), and rapidly increasing burden group (6.2%). In the fully adjusted model, compared with the stable low burden group, the persistent high burden group (OR = 1.75, 95% CI: 1.38–2.22) and rapidly increasing burden group (OR = 1.88, 95% CI: 1.37–2.54) were strong predictors of incident ADL disability. Regarding cognitive function, only the rapidly increasing burden group was significantly associated with lower memory scores in 2018 (β = −0.368, 95% CI: −0.661 to − 0.075, P  = 0.014), while no significant independent association was observed in the persistent high burden group ( P  = 0.084). Conclusions Both persistently high burden and rapid growth of cardiopulmonary-depressive comorbidity significantly elevate the risk of functional disability. Rapid accumulation of comorbidity is a key risk factor for impaired memory function in later life. Clinical assessment should shift from static disease evaluation to dynamic trajectory monitoring, with targeted attention to older adults experiencing accelerated comorbidity progression.

title: Impact of serial changes of D-dimer in patients with Kawasaki disease: Correlation between the peak D-dimer level and coronary arterial lesions
authorString: Okumura K, Izumi K, Sugawara T, Itoi K, Sekine K, Wada T, Nishikado M, Amimoto Y, Awaguni H, Arai I, Nagasawa M, Shinozuka J, Hamaoka K.
abstractText: Purpose D-dimer levels are thought to reflect coronary artery lesion activity in patients with Kawasaki disease (KD). This study aimed to clarify the relationship between peak D-dimer levels and coronary artery abnormalities by analyzing serial changes in D-dimer levels in patients with KD. Methods D-dimer levels were measured in pediatric 62 patients with KD and in 36 febrile subjects serving as controls. All patients with KD received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). In the KD group, D-dimer and other laboratory parameters were assessed serially at the following time points: pre-IVIG (on admission) and post-IVIG (after the first IVIG, at discharge, 1 month, and 4 months). The peak D-dimer level during the clinical course was determined, and maximum Z scores of the right and left main coronary arteries were evaluated by echocardiography. Results Pre-IVIG D-dimer levels were significantly higher in patients with KD than in the control group (p < 0.001). In patients with KD, D-dimer levels did not normalize rapidly after IVIG treatment. The Z score of the right coronary artery (RCA), the highly involved site, was significantly correlated with the peak D-dimer level. A peak D-dimer cutoff value of > 2.6 mg/dL predicted coronary artery lesions, with a sensitivity of 70.0% and a specificity of 69.2%. Conclusions Failure of D-dimer levels to decrease after IVIG treatment may indicate ongoing coronary artery involvement. In such cases, repeat echocardiography and consideration of additional treatment are warranted.

title: HFA-ICOS Risk Stratification for Trastuzumab-Related Cardiac Dysfunction in HER2- Positive Breast Cancer: A Cohort Study from Saudi Arabia
authorString: Alqaseer¹ M, Elalfy SEMB, Alabdullatif³ MA, Alibrahim⁴ IA, Alturani⁵ M, Muslem⁶ S, Maqsood⁷ MB.
abstractText: Background Cancer survival rates have improved substantially with advances in cancer therapy; however, treatment-related cardiotoxicity has become a growing concern. Cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) is a recognized adverse effect of anti-HER2 therapies, including trastuzumab. The Heart Failure Association-International Cardio-Oncology Society (HFA-ICOS) risk stratification tool was developed to predict CTRCD risk and guide clinical management. This study assessed the correlation between HFA-ICOS risk stratification and CTRCD incidence in patients receiving trastuzumab therapy at a tertiary care hospital in Saudi Arabia, and the overall incidence of CTRCD in this population. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 369 adult patients who received trastuzumab therapy at King Fahad Specialist Hospital, Dammam, from January to December 2023. HFA-ICOS risk scores were calculated at baseline, and CTRCD was assessed via serial echocardiography over 3–12 months. Associations between risk category and CTRCD were analyzed using Chi-square and Fisher’s exact tests. Results Among 369 patients (mean age 53 ± 11 years; 96.7% female), baseline HFA-ICOS risk stratification classified 57.7% as low risk, 21.1% as medium, 14.6% as high, and 6.5% as very high risk. Overall CTRCD incidence was 10.6% (39/369). CTRCD prevalence increased sharply with risk category: 5.2% in low-risk, 5.1% in medium-risk, 18.5% in high-risk, and 58.3% in very high-risk patients (OR 25.71, 95% CI 9.33–70.82 for very high vs. low risk; p < 0.001). Diabetes mellitus (35.9% vs. 18.2%, p = 0.04) and hypertension (43.6% vs. 24.8%, p = 0.018) were significantly more common among patients who developed CTRCD. Seven patients (1.9%) developed clinically overt heart failure, of whom only one also met CTRCD criteria. Conclusion The HFA-ICOS risk stratification tool effectively predicts CTRCD risk in patients receiving trastuzumab therapy, with incidence rising sharply from low to very high-risk categories. These findings support risk-based cardiac surveillance strategies and highlight diabetes and hypertension as modifiable comorbidities warranting closer monitoring in high-risk patients.

title: Comprehensive Investigation of Esmolol-Related Organic Impurities: Synthesis, Purification, Characterization, and In Silico ADME-Toxicity Evaluation
authorString: Wakade S, Tapkir A, Pathak A, Rashinkar S, Kore S, Pomaji A.
abstractText: Background Esmolol hydrochloride is a short-acting, β₁-selective adrenergic blocker commonly used in acute cardiovascular care. However, information on the preparation and characterization of several Esmolol-related impurities is still limited. Objective The study was undertaken to prepare, purify, characterize, and assess selected Esmolol-related impurities using experimental and in silico approaches. Materials and Methods Esmolol Impurities 7, 9, 10, 11, and 12, N-Ethyl Esmolol, Esmolol Isopropyl Amide (USP), and Esmolol Dimer (USP) were prepared through appropriate organic transformations. The products were purified by recrystallisation and column chromatography using suitable solvent systems. Structural confirmation was performed using FTIR, 1 H NMR, and mass spectrometry. SwissADME was used to examine physicochemical and ADME characteristics, while ProTox-3.0 was used for toxicity prediction. Results The investigated impurities were obtained, and their structures were confirmed by spectroscopic and mass-spectrometric techniques. Most compounds showed acceptable physicochemical characteristics and satisfied Lipinski’s rule of five, while Esmolol Dimer did not fully meet these criteria. Predicted oral LD₅₀ values ranged from 500 to 8140 mg/kg, corresponding to toxicity classes IV-VI. No predicted hepatotoxic, neurotoxic, or cardiotoxic effects were observed. Esmolol Isopropyl Amide and Esmolol Dimer were isolated in yields of 15% and 20%, respectively. Conclusion The study establishes practical methods for obtaining selected Esmolol-related impurities and provides their preliminary physicochemical and toxicity profiles, which may be useful for impurity profiling, analytical method development, stability studies, and regulatory assessment.

title: Incidental Discovery of Double Inversion Physiology with a Novel Right Atrial to Left Ventricular Shunt During Workup for Acute Abdominal Pain and Uterine Leiomyomas: A Case Report
authorString: Astaraki P, Heydarian M, Rajabzadeh O.
abstractText:
Background: Complete situs inversus with levocardia and congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries (CCTGA) is an exceptionally rare and complex congenital heart defect. We report a unique case featuring a previously unreported direct right atrium to left ventricle (RA-LV) shunt, discovered incidentally during an abdominal workup, which highlights the extraordinary compensatory capacity of double inversion physiology. Case presentation: A 35-year-old woman presented with acute abdominal pain. Pelvic and abdominal ultrasonography revealed multiple large uterine leiomyomas and incidentally identified complete situs inversus. Contrast-enhanced multidetector computed tomography (MDCT) confirmed complex cardiac anomalies, including CCTGA, a large perimembranous ventricular septal defect, patent ductus arteriosus, right aortic arch with mirror-image branching, and severe pulmonary hypertension. Crucially, a novel direct RA-LV shunt was identified, creating a paradoxical pathway that likely maintained balanced circulation for three decades. Laboratory tests showed an acute inflammatory response correlating with a 53-mm abdominal wall muscular lesion and suspected localized bowel ischemia. Due to advanced pulmonary vascular disease, cardiac surgery was deemed high-risk and deferred; the patient was managed conservatively for her abdominal complaints and discharged with informed consent.

Conclusions:

This case underscores the critical role of high-resolution MDCT in mapping complex, atypical intracardiac shunts that echocardiography might miss in inverted hearts. Clinicians must maintain a high index of suspicion for profound congenital anomalies whenever visceral heterotaxy is incidentally detected, ensuring comprehensive cardiovascular evaluation and lifelong multidisciplinary surveillance.

title: Dynamic responses of metabolic rate and heart rate under occupational heat stress
authorString: Huang M, Wang J, Fu M, Li Y, Shen L, Shen S, Aerts J.
abstractText: Characterizing the dynamic metabolic rate (MET) and heart rate (HR) is essential for understanding workers’ heat strain under occupational heat stress. This study examined the dynamic responses of MET and HR under different thermal and clothing conditions. Ten participants performed light-to-heavy treadmill exercise across three bidirectional thermal sequences (25-30-25°C, 25-35-25°C, and 25-40-25°C), wearing either a normal ensemble or a firefighting protective ensemble. Results showed that MET and HR responded similarly during activity but diverged during recovery. Activity intensity was the primary determinant of quasi-steady-state MET and HR, followed by clothing condition, whereas ambient temperature had a comparatively limited effect under the conditions investigated. Based on these findings, polynomial relationships between movement speed and quasi-steady-state MET/HR were established for the two clothing conditions (R 2  ≥ 0.80), together with linear quasi-steady-state HR-MET relationships during activity (R 2  ≥ 0.83). These relationships differed from those specified in ISO 8996:2021, suggesting that standardized relationships may not fully capture condition-specific MET and HR responses under the thermal burden investigated. In addition, first-order dynamic models were further established to characterize the transient responses of MET (R 2  ≥ 0.88) and HR (R 2  ≥ 0.70). Together, these empirical relationships provide a quantitative characterization of dynamic metabolic and cardiovascular responses under the investigated occupational heat-stress conditions and may serve as a basis for future heat-strain modeling and assessment.

title: Effects of Early Alirocumab Plus Statin Therapy on Lipid Control and Vascular Endothelial Function After PCI in Patients With Coronary Artery Disease
authorString: Qiao Y, Lei J, Cao Y, Wei J, Bai W, Zhou J, Wu J, Li Y.
abstractText: Objective To compare the effects of early treatment with alirocumab injection (brand name: Praluent) plus statin therapy versus statin monotherapy on lipid control, vascular function, and short-term laboratory safety at 8 weeks after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with coronary artery disease. Methods This single-center observational cohort study included 62 patients with coronary artery disease who underwent PCI. Based on the post-PCI lipid-lowering regimen, 22 patients received alirocumab plus statin therapy and 40 received a regimen without a PCSK9 inhibitor; follow-up was scheduled at 8 weeks. Lipid profiles and inflammatory and laboratory safety measures were compared between baseline and follow-up. Paired vascular ultrasonography was available in 22 patients (9 in the combination group and 13 in the comparison group), in whom brachial artery flow-mediated dilation (FMD), quantitative intima-media thickness (QIMT), and local carotid stiffness indices were evaluated. Results At 8 weeks, total cholesterol and LDL-C had decreased from baseline in both groups (all P < 0.001). The reductions in total cholesterol, LDL-C, and ApoB were greater in the combination group than in the comparison group, with between-group P values for change of < 0.001, 0.001, and 0.017, respectively. In the vascular subgroup, between-group differences were observed for changes in FMD, compliance coefficient, right QIMT, stiffness coefficient beta, and local PWV (P = 0.013, P = 0.008, P = 0.018, P = 0.012, and P = 0.038, respectively). ALT and AST decreased from baseline in the combination group (P = 0.030 and P = 0.002, respectively), while between-group differences in changes in creatinine and CK were not statistically significant (P = 0.373 and P = 0.335, respectively). Conclusion Compared with statin monotherapy, early alirocumab plus statin therapy after PCI achieved greater reductions in LDL-C, total cholesterol, and ApoB and was associated with favorable changes in FMD and selected measures of arterial elasticity.
