No consistent adverse changes in hepatic or renal function or muscle enzyme levels associated with alirocumab plus statin therapy were observed within 8 weeks.

title: Intractable Pulmonary Edema After PCI: An Extremely Rare Iatrogenic Mechanical Cause.
authorString: Vijayachandra Y, Sreeram J, Wilson A, Kumar AM, Chandrasekaran K.
abstractText:
Background

Permanent aortic valve injury following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is a rare but catastrophic complication that can cause acute severe aortic regurgitation (AR) and heart failure.

Case summary

A 49-year-old man developed recurrent acute pulmonary edema after a failed staged PCI for chronic total occlusion of the left anterior descending artery. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed severe eccentric AR caused by a 7-mm injury to the noncoronary cusp and left cusp confirming iatrogenic cusp laceration. He underwent successful surgical repair with pericardial patch reconstruction and coronary artery bypass grafting, with excellent recovery.

Discussion

Literature on catheter-induced aortic valve injury is sparse. This case highlights a rare cause of post-PCI shock where prompt echocardiography guided lifesaving surgical intervention.

Take-home messages

Not all post-PCI cardiac decompensation is ischemic. Severe AR from iatrogenic aortic cusp injury, though rare, should be promptly excluded.

title: Real-Time Hemodynamic Guidance During Valve-in-Valve TAVI.
authorString: Konami Y, Sakamoto T, Suzuyama H, Horio E, Sato T, Maeda M, Yamada M, Ideta I, Koyama J.
abstractText:
Objectives

To describe hemodynamic guidance during valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve implantation using simultaneous aortic and left ventricular pressure monitoring.

Key steps

A 90-year-old woman with a failed 19-mm surgical bioprosthesis and severe transvalvular regurgitation underwent valve-in-valve implantation with a self-expanding valve guided by a SavvyWire. During the first deployment, the aortic waveform remained completely flat after pacing was discontinued, whereas left ventricular pulsatility persisted; the valve was recaptured. During the second deployment, aortic pulsatility recovered after pacing cessation; final release was performed. Postdilatation reduced the invasive mean transvalvular gradient from 23 to 11 mm Hg.

Potential pitfalls

A flat aortic waveform with preserved left ventricular pulsatility is a warning sign warranting system confirmation and multimodality reassessment, not a specific diagnosis of leaflet dysfunction.

Take-home message

Simultaneous pressure monitoring can complement fluoroscopy when valve function is uncertain during deployment and may support timely recapture when abnormal hemodynamics persist.

title: Femoral-to-Carotid Shunting During Carotid-Access TAVR in Moyamoya-Pattern Vasculopathy.
authorString: Mourad N, Chan AW, Tauh K.
abstractText:
Background

Carotid access is an alternative for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) in patients with prohibitive transfemoral anatomy, but it may cause cerebral hypoperfusion with impaired intracranial collateral circulation.

Case summary

A 67-year-old woman with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis, extensive comorbidities, and unsuitable transfemoral access underwent TAVR. Neuroimaging demonstrated moyamoya-pattern intracranial vasculopathy with limited collateral reserve. During left carotid exposure, test occlusion caused a >50% decline in cerebral near-infrared spectroscopy despite blood pressure augmentation. A femoral-to-carotid arterial shunt was established to maintain cerebral perfusion. A 26-mm self-expanding Evolut FX+ valve was successfully implanted via left carotid access, with excellent hemodynamics and no neurologic complications.

Discussion

This approach demonstrates a novel cerebral protection strategy for selected patients with compromised cerebrovascular reserve.

Take-home messages

Carotid-access TAVR in moyamoya-pattern vasculopathy carries hypoperfusion risk. Real-time near-infrared spectroscopy may detect intolerance to carotid clamping, while femoral-to-carotid shunting may offer cerebral protection.

title: Pacing Rate Acceleration in Right-Sided Heart Failure: Insight From an On-Off-On Clinical Course.
authorString: Mai J, Fang Y, Bai Y, Pan W.
abstractText:
Background

Treatment options remain limited for patients with right-sided heart failure (RHF) and severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR). Whether higher heart rate is beneficial in patients with RHF remains unclear.

Case summary

A 74-year-old woman with RHF and severe TR experienced marked hemodynamic and symptomatic improvement after increasing her permanent pacing rate from 60 to 90 beats/min. At 3 months, rate reduction to 60 beats/min provoked symptom recurrence within 3 days; restoring the rate to 90 beats/min promptly relieved symptoms. At 6 months, left ventricular ejection fraction remained preserved and right ventricular size remained reduced, although TR remained severe.

Discussion

This case suggests that increasing the pacing rate may optimize right-sided heart hemodynamics and improve symptoms in selected patients with RHF, although further validation is needed.

Take-home message

An on-off-on response to pacing-rate adjustment-symptoms improving with higher rates and worsening at lower rates-supports a potential beneficial effect of heart rate elevation in selected patients with refractory RHF.

title: Two-Port Endoscopic Left Atrial Myxoma Resection Under Ventricular Fibrillation Without Aortic Cross-Clamping.
authorString: Kim JY, Yoo JS.
abstractText:
Objective

To describe a reproducible 2-port, 3-dimensional totally endoscopic technique for left atrial myxoma resection under ventricular fibrillation without aortic cross-clamping.

Key steps

Peripheral cardiopulmonary bypass is established through femoral cannulation. After 2 right thoracic ports are positioned, ventricular fibrillation is induced, the left atrium is opened, and a left atrial vent is inserted. The tumor is removed en bloc with an adequate septal margin. Continuous carbon dioxide insufflation, titrated venting, a gently blood-filled left atrium, and transesophageal echocardiography-guided de-airing provide embolic protection.

Potential pitfalls

Aortic regurgitation, interatrial shunting, inappropriate venting, tumor fragmentation, and prolonged fibrillatory arrest can compromise safety.

Take-home messages

In carefully selected patients, a short fibrillatory interval can simplify 2-port myxoma resection by avoiding aortic clamping, root cannulation, and cardioplegia. Meticulous left-heart decompression and de-airing are essential.

title: SEMAGLUTIDE TREATMENT IN TWO VERY YOUNG CHILDREN WITH SEVERE EARLY-ONSET OBESITY.
authorString: Canbaz AT, Kahveci A, Kurt I, Demir S, Geçkinli BB, Bereket A, Haliloglu B.
abstractText: Monogenic obesity comprises a group of rare genetic disorders characterized by severe early-onset obesity and hyperphagia. Pharmacological treatment options for severe early-onset obesity remain limited, particularly in young children. We report two children younger than 6 years of age with severe early-onset obesity, including one with genetically confirmed monogenic obesity, who showed reductions in BMI-SDS during semaglutide treatment. Case-1: A 4.5-year-old girl with a homozygous ADCY3 (c.1102G>A) variant presented with severe obesity, hyperphagia, hypertension, hepatosteatosis and Blount's disease. Baseline BMI was 48.0 kg/m2 (+5.5 SDS). Semaglutide was initiated at 0.125 mg/week and titrated to 1.5 mg/week. After 18 months, BMI-SDS decreased from +5.5 to +4.1 (-25.5%), accompanied by improved in hyperphagia and resolution of left ventricular hypertrophy. No significant adverse effects were observed, and linear growth remained age appropriate. Case-2: A 3.3-year-old boy with hyperphagia, severe obesity and dyslipidaemia was diagnosed with Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY). Clinical Exome Sequencing identified no causative variant for obesity. Baseline BMI was 32.6 kg/m2 (+5.7 SDS). Semaglutide was initiated at 0.0625 mg/week and gradually titrated to 2.0 mg/week. After 21 months, BMI-SDS decreased from +5.7 to +4.4 (-22%). Treatment was generally well tolerated, with normal linear growth. This two cases describe reductions BMI-SDS during semaglutide treatment in very young children with severe early-onset obesity, including one child with genetically confirmed ADCY3-related monogenic obesity. These findings suggest a potential clinical benefit of semaglutide in this young population, warranting evaluation in larger studies.

title: Factors influencing elderly people's intentions to use smartphone mHealth apps: Quantitative research.
authorString: Huang T, Cai W.
abstractText: Smartphone mHealth apps (mHealth apps) have played a highly positive role in medical services, which provides a new direction for users' medical services and health management. Although smartphone mHealth apps provide many benefits for users, people know little about the factors that drive elderly users to adopt this new service platform in the context of an aging population. This study aims to learn the factors that affect elderly people's intentions to adopt smartphone mHealth apps, and use the technology acceptance model as a theoretical basis to integrate perceived convenience, perceived quality, perceived risk and perceived trust, in an attempt to construct a research model on the intentions to use smartphone mHealth apps. The elderly users' data were collected by questionnaire survey and analyzed quantitatively by structural equation model. By analyzing the 263 valid data collected, the results showed that users' perceived trust (β = 0.427, p < .001), attitude (β = 0.285, p < .001), and perceived quality (β = 0.278, p < .001) of mobile medical applications positively influenced users' intention to use the applications, while perceived risk (β = -0.173, p < .001) had a negative impact on the intention to use. Perceived trust was also directly positively influenced by perceived quality (β = 0.434, p < .001) and perceived ease of use, and perceived convenience positively influenced perceived usefulness (β = 0.358, p < .001) and attitude (β = 0.299, p < .001). These findings can help us better understand the factors that influence the adoption of smartphone mHealth apps. This study further extends the technology acceptance model and its application domains to help mHealth researchers, designers, marketers, and service providers improve mHealth services and help increase users' intentions to adopt mHealth apps.

title: Internal Jugular Compression Syndrome Because of Compression Between the Styloid Process and C1 Transverse Process: Clinical Presentation, Diagnosis, and Management.
authorString: Shenoy VS, Lazaro T, Kelly-Hedrick M, Basner L, Seward C, Ghodke B, Sekhar LN.
abstractText:
Background and objectives

Internal jugular vein (IJV) compression at the skull base represents a rare cause of cerebral venous outflow obstruction and may mimic Eagle's syndrome. Unlike classic Eagle's syndrome, this condition results from venous compression between the hypertrophic C1 transverse process and the styloid process, producing symptoms such as pulsatile tinnitus, headache, and cognitive disturbances. We describe our experience highlighting the diagnostic protocol and management strategies.

Methods

We retrospectively reviewed 5 patients with symptomatic IJV compression syndrome. Demographics, clinical presentation, and treatment outcomes were analyzed. Diagnostic evaluation included computed tomography venography, duplex ultrasonography with head rotation, and cerebral angiography. Four (80%) patients underwent microsurgical decompression of the IJV through a posterolateral suboccipital approach with resection of the hypertrophic C1 transverse process and decompression of the V2-V3 vertebral artery. One patient was managed conservatively.

Results

The mean age was 57 years (3 females, 2 males). The mean symptom duration was 7.2 years. Presenting symptoms included pulsatile tinnitus, headache, dizziness, syncope, ear pain, and cognitive complaints. Two patients (40%) had undergone previous treatment without symptom relief. Postoperatively, 3 patients (75%) experienced complete resolution of symptoms and one demonstrated partial symptom improvement with persistent tinnitus attributable to neurovascular compression of cranial nerve VIII. Imaging confirmed restoration of IJV patency in all cases. One patient had spontaneous symptom resolution because of extensive venous collaterals. One patient developed intraoperative vertebral artery dissection because of atherosclerosis which was managed by endarterectomy and reconstruction with Hemashield patch.

Conclusion

IJV compression syndrome caused by the hypertrophic C1 transverse process is a distinct clinical condition that should be considered in patients with refractory pulsatile tinnitus or suspected venous intracranial hypertension. Computed tomography venography of head and neck along with head rotation is critical for diagnosis. Microsurgical decompression through a posterolateral far-lateral approach provides effective symptom relief and durable restoration of venous outflow.

title: Safety and Efficacy of Microhook Ab Interno Trabeculotomy Combined with Cataract Surgery in Older Patients with Glaucoma.
authorString: Ebisutani S, Noro T, Yamada Y, Kitaoka Y.
abstractText: Evidence regarding minimally invasive glaucoma surgery in very old patients remains limited, making surgical decision-making challenging in this population. We investigated age-related differences in the safety and efficacy of microhook ab interno trabeculotomy combined with cataract surgery (combined µLOT). This single-center retrospective study in Japan included 67 consecutive glaucomatous eyes of 67 patients who underwent combined µLOT and were followed for at least 6 months. The cohort comprised 27 male and 40 female patients. Patients were divided by median age into younger (< 76 years, n = 32) and older (≥ 76 years, n = 35) groups. Qualified success was defined irrespective of postoperative glaucoma medication use and without the need for additional glaucoma surgery, and was evaluated using three intraocular pressure (IOP) criteria: criterion A, 6 ≤ IOP ≤ 18 mmHg; criterion B, 6 ≤ IOP ≤ 15 mmHg; and criterion C, 6 ≤ IOP ≤ 13 mmHg. The mean age of the older group was 82.5 years. At 6 months, qualified success probabilities were 94.0%, 82.1%, and 60.0% for criteria A, B, and C, respectively. Although the older group had higher qualified success under criterion C (71.4% vs. 46.9%; nominal P = 0.04) and lower IOP from week 2 to month 6, age was not independently associated with surgical failure in multivariable Cox analyses. Higher preoperative IOP, hypertension, and antithrombotic therapy showed exploratory associations with failure. Postoperative hyphema, transient IOP elevation, corneal endothelial cell loss, and systemic complications were not increased in the older group. Combined µLOT provided favorable short-term IOP control without an increased complication burden in older patients, although baseline medication burden may have confounded the age-group comparison. These real-world findings provide clinically relevant evidence for surgical decision-making in very old patients and may be informative for other aging societies.

title: Acute Changes in Left Atrial Appendage Flow Velocity During Pulsed Field Ablation: An Intraprocedural Intracardiac Echocardiography Study
authorString: Pan Y, Osmancik P, Knize T, Hornof J, Herman D, Hassouna S, Slusnakova E, Soukup S, Hozman M.
abstractText: **Background:** Despite the close anatomical relationship between the left pulmonary veins (PVs) and the left atrial appendage (LAA), acute changes in LAA flow during pulsed field ablation (PFA) remain poorly characterized.  **Objectives:** To characterize acute intraprocedural changes in LAA flow and transmitral filling during PFA for atrial fibrillation (AF) using paired intracardiac echocardiography (ICE).  **Methods:** Patients with paroxysmal or persistent AF undergoing PFA were prospectively enrolled if they were in sinus rhythm at the beginning of the procedure. ICE was performed immediately before and after PFA to assess LAA emptying velocity (LAAEv), LAA filling velocity (LAAFv), transmitral E- and A-wave velocities, and E-wave deceleration time (EDT). Paired pre-to-post PFA changes were assessed, followed by a sensitivity analysis using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) and exploratory subgroup analyses.  **Results:** Among 98 patients, LAAEv increased from 35.45 to 40.00 cm/s immediately after PFA (estimated paired increase, 4.95 cm/s; 95% CI, 2.35-7.80; P less than 0.001), while LAAFv increased by 4.36 cm/s (95% CI, 1.81-6.91; P=0.001). E-wave velocity increased by 8.69 cm/s and EDT decreased by 31.73 ms (both P less than 0.001), whereas A-wave velocity did not change significantly (P=0.08). In the ANCOVA model, changes in heart rate, systolic blood pressure, and vasopressor use were not significantly associated with changes in LAAEv. A marked acute reduction in LAAEv (20% or greater) occurred in 12 patients (12.2%). No significant subgroup interactions were observed.  **Conclusions:** LAA flow velocities increased acutely after PFA, accompanied by changes in transmitral filling, although a minority of patients showed a marked acute reduction in LAA emptying.

title: Adherence to a modified DASH diet, intake of key food groups, and infertility in women and men: the Norwegian Mother, Father and Child Cohort Study
authorString: Hernaez A, Caspersen IH, Grindstad T, Paulsen MM, Castro-Barquero S, Hernandez MH, Magnus MC.
abstractText:
Background:

& Aims: Diet is a modifiable exposure that may contribute to reproductive health. While most previous studies focused on selected nutrients in relation to fertility treatment outcomes or semen parameters, large cohort data addressing overall diet quality and clinical infertility in both women and men remain limited. We aimed to assess how adherence to a modified Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) dietary pattern and intake of key food groups relate to infertility in women and men.

Methods:

We included 59,218 women and 26,866 men participating in the Norwegian Mother, Father and Child Cohort Study (MoBa). Diet was assessed using dietary questionnaires and summarized using a modified DASH score comprising fruits, vegetables, nuts/legumes, whole grains, low-fat dairy, sweet beverages, red and processed meat, and a snack/fast food proxy. Fish was also assessed. Infertility was defined as having tried to conceive for at least 12 months or using assisted reproductive technologies. Logistic regression models were fitted separately in women and men, adjusting for age, education, body mass index, smoking, and number of offspring. Food-group analyses were evaluated using a multiple-comparison threshold of p-value <0.0167, derived from Horn's parallel analysis.

Results:

A higher modified DASH score was associated with lower odds of infertility in women (adjusted OR per 1-SD increment: 0.97, 95% CI 0.95 to 0.995) and men (OR: 0.91, 95% CI 0.87 to 0.94). In women, higher red and processed meat intake was associated with higher odds of infertility (adjusted OR per 1-SD increment: 1.04, 95% CI 1.02 to 1.07), and a nominal association was observed for the snack/fast food proxy (OR 1.03, 95% CI 1.01 to 1.05). Whole grains and fish showed evidence of non-linear associations: the lowest estimated odds of infertility were observed at approximately 5 servings/day for whole grains, and at approximately 0.4 serving/day for fish. In men, higher intakes of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and fish were associated with lower odds of infertility (5-6% lower odds per 1-SD higher intake). Higher values of the snack/fast food proxy were associated with higher odds of infertility (7% higher odds per 1-SD higher intake). Associations were attenuated in women after adjustment for their partner's modified DASH score, but not vice versa.

Conclusion:

Greater adherence to a modified DASH dietary pattern was associated with lower odds of infertility in both women and men, with stronger and more consistent associations in men and partly sex-specific food-group patterns, although maternal diet was assessed during pregnancy and may not reflect preconception intake. These findings support considering overall diet quality and both partners' diets when studying infertility and highlight the need for preconception studies and dietary interventions using clinically relevant couple-level fertility outcomes.

title: Explainable Multimodal AI for In-Hospital Detection of Lung Cancer and Heart Failure Using Routine Data: Development, Internal Validation, and Simulated Federated Evaluation
authorString: Ahmed M, Rahman MM, Wahid ST, Rabbi G, Rafy A, Khondoker GS, Dutta S, Saadat MA, Haque MM.
abstractText:
Objective:

To determine whether combining four routine data sources improves in-hospital detection of lung cancer and heart failure, which sources drive each prediction, whether explanations are faithful, whether models are fair, and how much benefit federated training retains.

Methods:

In this retrospective single-centre study, we linked MIMIC-IV admissions (73,637 patients) to chest radiographs, radiology reports, 12-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs) and laboratory tests from the first 48 hours. For each disease, excluding prior cases, we compared single-source models, gradient boosting and early, late and attention-based fusion on patient-level splits. We tested explanations for faithfulness and weight dependence, audited performance by sex, age, race and ethnicity, and insurance, and simulated five unequal hospitals to compare federated, centralised and local training.

Results:

Lung cancer was coded in 1.7% and heart failure in 15.6% of patients. For lung cancer, attention fusion reached an area under the ROC curve (AUROC) of 0.833 (95% CI 0.809-0.859) against 0.753 for gradient boosting on laboratory data; for heart failure, 0.885 (0.878-0.892) against 0.794 (both p < 0.001). Early and late fusion performed similarly. Laboratory data and radiology reports contributed most to lung cancer, and the ECG to heart failure. Explanations passed a deletion test; a weight-randomisation check on absolute attributions passed for ECG but not for laboratory explanations. For heart failure, discrimination fell with age. Federated training recovered 95% of the centralised gain over local training for heart failure; for lung cancer, federated averaging (FedAvg) recovered 51% and FedProx 82%.

Conclusion:

Fusing routine data improved in-hospital detection of both diseases over laboratory data alone, and which data matter depends on the disease. Explanation checks should be run per source and per similarity measure, and performance in older patients monitored. For the rare outcome, FedProx, which limits drift between sites, retained more of the pooled benefit than FedAvg. External validation is needed.

title: Six-hour landmark prediction of poor subsequent urine output in critically ill adults with heart failure: model development and external validation
authorString: Zhuang X, Zhang X, Fang T.
abstractText: Background Early response to loop diuretics may help identify critically ill patients with heart failure who will have low subsequent urine output. We assessed whether information recorded during the first six hours improved prediction across intensive care databases. Methods We developed models in MIMIC-IV and externally evaluated them in eICU-CRD. The prediction landmark was six hours after the first qualifying intravenous loop-diuretic record. Poor subsequent response was defined as mean urine output during hours 6–24 at or below the development-cohort lower quartile (approximately 0.718 mL/kg/h). Four candidate algorithms underwent subject-grouped, candidate-specific nested cross-validation. A development-selected XGBoost model was applied unchanged externally. Evaluation included area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), calibration, threshold performance, decision curves and inverse-probability-of-inclusion weighting. Results The development cohort included 1,450 stays and 363 events. The external cohort included 545 stays and 147 events across 69 hospitals. Development out-of-fold AUROC was 0.760 (95% confidence interval 0.732–0.787), conditional on algorithm-family selection and potentially optimistic. External AUROC was 0.729 (0.690–0.789). Compared with baseline elastic-net regression, external AUROC increased by 0.080 (0.028–0.126). However, early-response elastic-net regression achieved a higher external AUROC of 0.756; the paired XGBoost-minus-elastic-net difference was − 0.027 (− 0.057 to − 0.004). External calibration slope was 0.682. At the locked threshold, sensitivity was 75.5%, specificity 56.0% and positive predictive value 38.8%; incremental net benefit over reviewing all patients was uncertain. Inclusion-weighted external AUROC was 0.690 (0.632–0.750). Conclusions Six-hour early-response information improved prediction of subsequent low urine output, but the more complex algorithm showed no advantage. Calibration limitations, selection for observable outcomes and measurement differences between databases limit immediate clinical use. Prospective evaluation should compare parsimonious models and establish whether risk-guided review improves care.

title: Acute Mitral Regurgitation With Unilateral Pulmonary Edema: Preferential Pulmonary Venous Loading From an Eccentric Jet.
authorString: Zhang K, Ishak M, Doyle M, Baraket M, Juergens C.
abstractText:
Background

Acute severe mitral regurgitation (MR) can cause rapidly progressive asymmetric pulmonary edema that mimics pneumonia.

Case summary

A 22-year-old man presented with fever, dyspnea, and a new pansystolic murmur. Within hours, he developed hypoxemic respiratory failure. Serial chest imaging captured rapid progression from subtle right hilar vascular prominence to extensive right-predominant airspace opacification. Echocardiography showed posterior leaflet chordal rupture with a flail P2 segment and a severe eccentric MR jet directed toward the right pulmonary venous inflow, with systolic flow reversal in a sampled right pulmonary vein. Mitral valve repair produced marked clinical and radiographic improvement.

Discussion

Concordance among the MR jet trajectory, pulmonary venous abnormalities, and edema distribution supported preferential right pulmonary venous loading. Recognition of this pattern helped distinguish asymmetric cardiogenic pulmonary edema from pneumonia.

Take-home message

Rapidly evolving focal pulmonary opacification with a new systolic murmur should prompt urgent echocardiography.

title: Making vascular outcomes visible: an implementation framework for an Irish national vascular registry.
authorString: McLoughlin MT, Neachtain SN, Joyce DP, Walsh SR.
abstractText:
Background

Ireland lacks a coordinated national vascular registry, despite a 2023 National Model of Care recommendation to establish one for quality improvement and implant surveillance.

Aims

To identify transferable features of established national vascular registry and audit systems and translate them into a proportionate implementation framework for Ireland.

Methods

A structured narrative review and comparative implementation analysis. Five mature comparator systems, purposively selected for relevance to predefined implementation domains, were characterised using contemporary programme documentation and targeted peer-reviewed literature. Features were mapped to Irish policy objectives.

Results

Transferable functions included explicit measurement of case ascertainment, clinically granular procedure-specific modules, recurrent provider feedback, linkage to routinely collected data, and progressive development of risk-adjusted benchmarking and research capability. We propose an Irish registry beginning with infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, carotid intervention, lower-limb arterial revascularisation, and major amputation. The initial architecture should combine a limited universal clinical core with procedure-specific modules, reconciliation against Hospital In-Patient Enquiry activity, structured implant capture, and rapid feedback to participating centres. Procedure-specific risk adjustment, longitudinal linkage, complex aortic modules, and participation in VASCUNET should follow only after completeness and data quality are established. Prospective pilot evaluation should measure denominator validity, case ascertainment, mandatory-field completion, data-entry burden, provider acceptability, staffing requirements, and cost per completed case.

Conclusions

Ireland does not require further proof that national vascular audit is feasible; it requires a deliberately limited, testable, and sustainably commissioned implementation model.

title: Z-Score Calculators for Cross Sectional Area to Height Ratio of the Aortic Root and Ascending Aorta in Healthy Children.
authorString: Chaudhary AA, Tomlinson AZ, Drant S, Jones AL.
abstractText: In pediatrics, echocardiographic measurements of the aorta are normalized using body surface area (BSA), which do not account for differences in body composition amongst children or as they grow. Height has been shown to have a linear relationship with measures of aortic size in pediatrics. Data from the Pediatric Heart Network (PHN) Echo Z-Score database was used to develop z-scores for cross sectional area to height ratio (CSA/ht) on 3215 healthy pediatric patients ≤ 18 years old. Aortic root and ascending aorta CSA/ht (cm<sup>2</sup>/m) were calculated. Linear regression was performed to assess the relationship between patient sex, age at echocardiogram, and CSA/ht of the aortic root. An interaction term was included to allow the effect of age to vary by sex. Estimates from the final regression model were utilized in the z-score calculator. An identical analysis was repeated for ascending aorta CSA/ht. Older children had larger aortic root CSA/ht (β = 0.10, p < 0.001) and ascending aorta CSA/ht (β = 0.08, p < 0.001). Male children had larger aortic root CSA/ht (β = 0.13, p < 0.001) and ascending aorta CSA/ht (β = 0.08, p < 0.001). There was a significant interaction of sex and age in the aortic root model (β = 0.015, p < 0.001), but not in the ascending aorta model (β = 0.003, p = 0.16). We created two z-score calculators for CSA/ht of the aortic root and the ascending aorta in normal children, ideally allowing for more accurate assessment of aortic size in children.

title: CD160 is an inducible endothelial checkpoint that suppresses sprouting angiogenesis through LRP1-dependent autophagy
authorString: Aziz A, Mocquery-Corre M, Berquand A, Thevenard-Devy J, Martins A, Hachet C, Potteaux S, Merrouche Y, El Fatimy R, Duca L, Bensussan A, Ben Mkaddem S, Devy J.
abstractText: Pathological angiogenesis is a hallmark of cancer and other chronic diseases, yet therapeutic strategies remain largely focused on blocking pro-angiogenic signals rather than restoring endogenous mechanisms that restrain endothelial sprouting. The identification of endothelial checkpoints capable of limiting pathological vessel growth therefore remains an important unmet need. CD160 is a glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchored immunoglobulin-superfamily receptor of cytotoxic lymphocytes and an inhibitory checkpoint receptor on CD4 T cells. It is also present on endothelium and has been targeted therapeutically. Here, we identify CD160 as an inducible endothelial checkpoint that emerges in response to pro-angiogenic cues and limits pathological angiogenesis. CD160 is absent in resting endothelium. It is induced by basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF) and most strongly by combining VEGF-A and bFGF, and it is detected in the sprouting region of  ex vivo mouse aortic rings. Targeting of CD160 using monoclonal antibody reduces tubulogenesis, scratch closure and aortic-ring sprouting, and softens the cell cortex, while viability and membrane integrity remain intact. Mechanistically, CD160 associates with the endocytic receptor LRP1 as demonstrated by proximity ligation assay, lipid-raft co-immunoprecipitation and super-resolution fluorescence microscopy. Both receptors appear in a common complex, and two independent computational methods converge on the first ligand-binding cluster of LRP1 as the interface. Silencing CD160 or LRP1 abolishes the anti-angiogenic response mediated by the antibody. Under a chloroquine clamp, engagement raises autophagic flux in a CD160- and LRP1-dependent manner, and lysosomal or LDL-receptor-family blockade removes the anti-sprouting effect. CD160 therefore acts as an inducible endothelial checkpoint that suppresses sprouting through autophagic flux. Thus, CD160 represents an inducible endothelial checkpoint that is activated in a pro-angiogenic environment, and targeting CD160 restrains pathological angiogensis.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Sotatercept in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: A GRADE-Assessed Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials with Trial Sequential Analysis.
authorString: Emara A, Emara M, Gadelmawla AF, Mansour A, Aboeldahab H, Hamed BM, AbuBaha M, Elbsiony M, Mohamed MR, El Masry M.
abstractText: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive disease characterized by pulmonary vascular remodeling and increased pulmonary vascular resistance. Sotatercept, an activin-signaling inhibitor, is a novel therapy targeting this pathology. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess its efficacy and safety in PAH. A systematic search of PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted, to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating Sotatercept in adults with PAH. Data were pooled using random-effects models to estimate mean differences (MDs) and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Four RCTs enrolling 921 patients were included. Compared with placebo, Sotatercept significantly improved 6-minute walk distance (MD 30.54 m, 95% CI 4.05-57.04, P=0.02), WHO functional class (RR 1.71, 95% CI 1.37-2.15, P<0.00001), multicomponent improvement (RR 2.77, 95% CI 1.45-5.29, P=0.002), pulmonary vascular resistance (MD -197.01 dyn⋅s⋅cm-5, 95% CI -213.16 - -180.86, P<0.00001), and reduced clinical worsening events (RR 0.28, 95% CI 0.21-0.38, P<0.00001). There were no significant differences in NT-proBNP levels or all-cause mortality. Safety analysis showed lower risks of serious adverse events (AEs), peripheral edema, and right ventricular failure, but higher rates of bleeding, epistaxis, and drug-related AEs. Sotatercept demonstrated meaningful clinical benefits in exercise capacity, hemodynamics, and disease progression among patients with PAH, with a generally acceptable safety profile. These findings support Sotatercept as a promising adjunct to standard therapy, though longer-term trials are needed to confirm durability and survival impact.

title: CATHETER ABLATION VERSUS SHAM FOR SYMPTOMATIC ATRIAL FIBRILLATION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND BAYESIAN META-ANALYSIS OF RANDOMIZED TRIALS.
authorString: Kakarla S, Iwakawa H, Andrade JG, Ariyaratnam JP, Gunawardene MA, Marrouche N, Middeldorp ME, Elliott AD, Kistler PM, Kalman JM, Sanders P.
abstractText:
Background

Catheter ablation reduces atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence and improves symptoms and quality of life (QoL), but sham-controlled trials have reported discordant results.

Objective

To synthesise sham-controlled trials of AF ablation and identify why QoL results differ.

Methods

We searched databases and registries for randomized trials of catheter ablation versus sham in symptomatic AF. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in Atrial Fibrillation Effect on Quality-of-Life (AFEQT) score, pooled using a Bayesian random-effects model. Certainty was rated with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation.

Results

Four trials (468 patients) were eligible; three (448 patients) were pooled. Ablation improved AFEQT relative to sham by 13.5 points (95% credible interval [CrI] 1.6 to 26.9), with a posterior probability of benefit 0.98, of exceeding the 5-point minimal clinically important difference 0.94, and by 12.9 points (-0.4 to 27.1; probability 0.97 and 0.91) with PVI-SHAM-AF's primary estimator. Heterogeneity (τ 8.2 points, I2 85.3%) was largely attributed to PVI-SHAM-AF, which differed from the other trials in symptom severity, rhythm monitoring and assessment of blinding; without it, the difference was 18.9 points (6.7 to 31.4). Ablation reduced AF recurrence in every trial (pooled risk ratio 0.49, CrI 0.17-0.89). Certainty was moderate for AF burden and recurrence and low for QoL.

Conclusion

Compared with sham embedded in active rhythm control, catheter ablation reduces AF recurrence and burden and has a high probability of clinically important QoL benefit, although its magnitude remains uncertain. Trials differ in population, monitoring, and estimator, not direction of effect.

title: NaV1.8 Inhibition and the Future of Nonopioid Analgesia in Otolaryngology: A Narrative Review.
authorString: Tham T, Lee JB, Megwalu UC.
abstractText: Postoperative pain management in otolaryngology requires balancing effective analgesia while minimizing adverse effects, such as opioid-related complications. Suzetrigine is a first-in-class selective voltage-gated sodium channel (NaV1.8) inhibitor that has been recently approved by the US Food and Drug Administration. Suzetrigine selectively inhibits NaV1.8 channels expressed in peripheral nociceptive neurons, thereby reducing pain signaling without the respiratory depression, sedation, or misuse potential associated with opioids. This review summarizes the pharmacology, efficacy, safety profile, limitations, and potential applications of suzetrigine in otolaryngology. Prospective clinical trials consist of 2 phase 2 randomized clinical trials, 2 phase 3 randomized placebo-controlled trials, and 1 phase 3 open-label study involving more than 3000 patients. Across abdominoplasty and bunionectomy pain models, suzetrigine demonstrated superior analgesia compared with placebo and mixed efficacy comparable to hydrocodone/acetaminophen. The drug was generally well tolerated, with adverse event rates similar to placebo and no significant respiratory, cardiac, or sedating adverse effects reported. Additionally, 1 retrospective cohort study has reported results in patients undergoing free flap reconstruction and transoral robotic surgery. Suzetrigine is a promising nonopioid analgesic with demonstrated efficacy compared to placebo in acute postoperative pain and a favorable safety profile. In otolaryngology, suzetrigine may serve as an adjunct to multimodal analgesia and an opioid-sparing option for patients with contraindications to traditional analgesics, opioid use disorder, or procedures that are expected to have high opioid utilization such as tonsillectomy, sleep surgery, and major head and neck surgery. Future studies in otolaryngology are warranted to evaluate whether suzetrigine can meaningfully reduce postoperative opioid exposure without compromising analgesic effectiveness.

title: Effect of telemedicine-based integrated management of atrial fibrillation in village clinics on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events: a secondary analysis of the MIRACLE-AF trial.
authorString: Liu W, Li M, Di X, Chu M, Zhang S, Yang G, Peng Z, Lip GYH, Chen M, MIRACLE-AF Investigators.
abstractText:
Background

Atrial fibrillation (AF) is an increasing public health challenge, particularly among rural older adults, where awareness and treatment remain inadequate. While the MIRACLE-AF trial demonstrated that telemedicine-based, village doctor-led integrated care reduced cardiovascular mortality or first major cardiovascular events, its impact on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events remains unknown.

Objective

To evaluate the effect of the MIRACLE-AF care model on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events.

Methods

We conducted a secondary analysis of the MIRACLE-AF trial (NCT04622514), a cluster-randomized controlled trial enrolling 1,039 rural patients aged ≥65 years with confirmed AF across 30 village clinics over 36 months. Village clinics were randomized 1:1 to village doctor-led telemedicine integrated care or enhanced usual care. The primary outcome was recurrent nonfatal events over 36 months, including strokes, hospitalizations for worsening heart failure or acute coronary syndrome, and emergency visits for AF, analyzed using a conditional frailty model.

Results

Among 1039 patients (mean age 75.8 ± 5.7 years; 44.3% female), the intervention experienced fewer cardiovascular events than the control (118 events in 82 patients [15.65%] vs. 173 events in 122 patients [23.69%]). The observed recurrent event rates were 6.75 and 9.11 per 100 patient-years, respectively. The estimated hazard ratio was 0.76 (95% CI, 0.583-1.004; p = 0.053), indicating that the difference did not reach statistical significance.

Conclusion

Although the overall difference did not reach statistical significance, directional trends consistently favored telemedicine-based integrated care, suggesting a potential reduction in recurrent cardiovascular event burden. Larger studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings.

title: LungCheck: Pilot Testing a Theory-Informed Multicomponent Strategy to Increase Lung Cancer Screening in Primary Care Settings.
authorString: Groner LK, Reuter K, Moise N, Thomas C, Wisherop C, Tamimi RM, Phillips E.

journal.title: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR

abstractText: Lung cancer screening (LCS) with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) reduces lung cancer-specific and all-cause mortality, yet uptake remains low. This study evaluates LungCheck, a theory-informed multicomponent behavior change and implementation strategy designed to increase LDCT ordering in two diverse primary care settings. This pilot study compared 16-month pilot and pre-pilot periods at a federally qualified health center (FQHC) and an academic faculty practice in New York City. LungCheck comprised educational meetings, materials and clinician reminders, an implementation blueprint, patient navigation, and EHR modifications. LDCT ordering rates (primary outcome) were compared using generalized estimating equations (GEE). Post-implementation surveys assessed acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility. A total of 5,918 patient-period observations were included (1,569 academic; 4,349 FQHC). Among patients with documented LCS eligibility, the odds of LDCT ordering were significantly higher during the pilot at both the academic practice (OR, 2.67; 95% CI, 1.47-4.85; p=0.001) and FQHC (OR, 4.53; 95% CI, 2.29-8.94; p<0.001). A combined-site multivariable model adjusting for site, age, sex, and race confirmed higher odds of LDCT ordering during the pilot (OR, 1.95; 95% CI, 1.44-2.63; p<0.001). Among patients with an LDCT order, completion was 71.4% (10/14) pre-pilot versus 35.7% (15/42) during the pilot at the academic practice and 42.9% (18/42; 95% CI, 28%-59%) versus 39.3% (24/61; 95% CI, 27%-53%) at the FQHC. The strategy was rated as highly acceptable (AIM, 4.47/5), appropriate (IAM, 4.44/5), and feasible (FIM, 4.41/5). LungCheck was associated with significantly increased LDCT ordering at both sites, high acceptability, feasibility, and appropriateness ratings and high provider knowledge, confidence, and perceived skills related to LCS. Although a corresponding improvement in LDCT completion was not observed, the small number of LDCT orders limited the precision of completion estimates. Persistent environmental and patient-level barriers underscore the need to adapt LungCheck into a multilevel intervention addressing patient-, provider, and system-level barriers across the LCS continuum, to be evaluated in a future cluster randomized trial.

title: Short-term safety, feasibility, and performance of a novel soft robotic biventricular mechanical circulatory support device avoiding blood contact - The MISSION reBEAT trial.
authorString: Ruhparwar A, Schueler S, Stock U, Hanke J, Schmitto J, Pauli H, Karsten J, Møller CH, Møller-Sørensen PH, Schmid MR, McDiarmid AK, Bauersachs J, Wildhirt S, Schmack B.
abstractText: Mechanical Circulatory Support (MCS) remains limited in advanced heart failure due to blood-contact complications and the absence of biventricular support. We report the first prospective clinical trial of a novel soft-robotic, biventricular, pulsatile technology placed externally around the heart without blood contact, designed to deliver individualized cardiac assistance (reBEAT®, AdjuCor GmbH, Munich, Germany). The system was temporarily applied in 10 end-stage heart failure patients immediately before elective LVAD implantation. Devices were custom-manufactured using preoperative CT scans to match individual cardiac anatomy. Safety, feasibility, and effects on haemodynamics were evaluated. Implantation was rapid (3±2 min), demonstrating procedural feasibility. We observed two procedure-related adverse events while no device- or procedure-related severe adverse events occurred. Absence of new ECG abnormalities, and no tissue injury confirmed safety. An iterative assessment on haemodynamics provided key insights into individualized cardio-circulatory support. While device presence reduced preload dependent haemodynamics in some patients, low average support pressures of 65-66 mmHg produced variable improvements towards baseline, predominantly on the pressure signal: mean arterial pressure (MAP; 67.5 ± 10.6 vs. 76.2 ± 11.7 mmHg, p<0.01), stroke work (SW; 347.8 ± 118.2 vs. 434.1 ± 131.0 mJ, p<0.01), and cardiac power output (CPO; 407.9 ± 108.2 vs. 503.7 ± 116.2 mW, p<0.01). Additionally, effects were observed on atrioventricular valve function and interventricular balance, which were not significant. This soft-robotic biventricular MCS platform provides short term evidence of a safe and feasible approach to pulsatile biventricular support without blood contact. Significant increases in MAP, CPO, and SW towards baseline indicate functional effects. Continuous device-driven workflow improvement is mandatory and further data are required to refine individualized optimization strategies. This technology may offer a novel biventricular assist modality. Its reduced complexity may enable broader adaption for both temporary and durable support. Avoiding blood contact and enabling balanced biventricular assistance will be central drivers of its continued clinical development.

title: Wireless Home Blood Pressure Monitoring With Health Coaching for Hypertension Management at a Federally Qualified Health Center: Pilot Randomized Controlled Feasibility and Acceptability Study.
authorString: Magalit N, Moran R, Narezkina A, Patrick K, DeMaria A.
abstractText: Only approximately half of adults with hypertension, a leading cardiovascular risk factor, achieve blood pressure (BP) control, with persistent disparities among low-income and minority populations. Wireless home BP monitoring (HBPM) with remote patient monitoring can improve BP control, but evidence is limited in medically underserved, predominantly Hispanic populations served by federally qualified health centers (FQHCs). The primary objective was to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of wireless HBPM among predominantly Hispanic adults with hypertension receiving FQHC care. Comparing BP outcomes between wireless and conventional HBPM was a secondary exploratory objective. We conducted a 6-month, 2-arm randomized controlled pilot feasibility and acceptability trial nested within the San Diego: Heart Attack and Stroke Free Zone program. Adults aged ≥18 years with uncontrolled or newly diagnosed hypertension (BP ≥140/90 mm Hg) were enrolled across 3 FQHC networks and randomized 1:1 by unrestricted simple randomization to wireless HBPM (Bluetooth cuff and cellular hub; weekly transmitted summaries reviewed by health coaches) or standard HBPM (home monitor with paper log). Both arms received standardized health coaching. The primary outcomes were feasibility (proportion of 210 expected BP readings transmitted) and acceptability (postintervention satisfaction survey in the wireless arm). Exploratory analyses compared BP outcomes between arms among participants with >2 BP measurements. Of 316 recruited participants, 290 (92%) were eligible, and 200 (63%) were analyzed (wireless: n=73, 23%; and standard: n=127, 40%); arm-level allocation counts were not retained. The mean age was 61 years (SD 9.1), 57% (115/200) were women, and 51% (n=102) self-identified as Hispanic, with no significant baseline differences between arms. Among analyzed wireless-arm participants, 86% (63/73) transmitted multiple readings (mean 160.6, SD 129.1) over 6 months, corresponding to 76.2% (160/210) of expected readings among transmitting participants and 66% across all 73; only 5% (7/127) of standard-arm participants returned paper logs. Of 60 respondents (82.2% response rate), 95% (n=57) agreed or strongly agreed that the device was easy to set up and use. Both arms showed significant within-arm BP reductions at 6 months (P<.001). At 6 months, 63% (46/73) of the wireless arm and 74% (94/127) of the standard arm achieved systolic BP <140 mm Hg (P=.08; adjusted odds ratio, standard vs wireless, 1.6, 95% CI 0.78-3.4; P=.19). These exploratory comparisons were not powered and do not constitute evidence of equivalence. Among analyzed participants, wireless HBPM was feasible, and survey respondents reported high acceptability in a medically underserved, predominantly Hispanic FQHC population. Feasibility among all randomized participants could not be estimated because arm-level allocation counts were not retained. The absence of a between-arm difference in BP control is not evidence of equivalence because this pilot was not powered to compare clinical effectiveness; the BP findings are hypothesis generating.

title: Cause-Specific Endovascular Thrombectomy Time Windows in Basilar Artery Occlusion: ATTENTION Trial Post Hoc Analysis.
authorString: Guo Z, Nguyen TN, Liu X, Tao C, Xu P, Zhang C, Liu X, Nogueira RG, Hu W, Xiao G, ATTENTION Investigators.
abstractText:
Background

Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) outperforms best medical treatment (BMT) for basilar artery occlusion (BAO), but the influence of stroke cause on the time sensitivity of EVT remains unclear. We hypothesized nonatherosclerotic BAO would require earlier EVT, whereas atherosclerotic BAO-with chronic stenosis and more robust collaterals-would retain EVT benefit in extended windows. We conducted a post hoc 3-way interaction analysis of the ATTENTION trial (Trial of Endovascular Treatment of Acute Basilar Artery Occlusion) to explore cause-specific EVT time patterns.

Methods

Using randomized ATTENTION trial data (36 Chinese centers, 2021-2022), patients were stratified by onset-to-puncture time (<6 versus ≥6 hours) and TOAST (Trial of ORG 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment) cause (atherosclerotic: large-artery atherosclerosis; nonatherosclerotic: cardioembolism/undetermined/other causes). The primary outcome was 90-day favorable functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score 0-3), with relative risk as the primary estimand; the 3-way interaction was tested via joint Wald test. A weighted 1-hour interval odds ratio trend analysis served as an exploratory tool, with multivariable regression adjusting for confounders.

Results

Among 340 patients (226 EVT+BMT, 114 BMT), for onset-to-puncture time <6 hours, patients without atherosclerosis with EVT achieved a significantly higher favorable outcome rate (46.7% versus 20.4%; relative risk, 2.29 [95% CI, 1.25-4.18]; P=0.007); patients with atherosclerosis showed numerical outcome benefit (40.4% versus 26.1%, P=0.259). For onset-to-puncture time ≥6 hours, numerical benefit of patients with atherosclerosis increased from 14.3% to 30.6% (56.9% versus 26.3%; P=0.199), accompanied by ordinal modified Rankin Scale score improvement (common odds ratio, 3.30 [95% CI, 1.13-9.62]; P=0.029) and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score reduction; patients without atherosclerosis' benefit decreased from 26.3% to 17.8% with loss of significance (39.5% versus 21.7%, P=0.341). The treatment time×cause interaction was not significant (P=0.662). The weighted 1-hour interval odds ratio trend analysis identified a provisional 5.3-hour reference point in patients without atherosclerosis.

Conclusions

Compared with nonatherosclerotic BAO, atherosclerotic BAO appears less time-sensitive, potentially retaining EVT responsiveness over longer windows. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

Registration

URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04751708.

title: Pulmonary vein isolation with a contact force-sensing, large-tip focal pulsed field ablation catheter with 3D mapping for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: Omny-IRE 12-month results.
authorString: Duytschaever M, Vijgen J, Neuzil P, Grimaldi M, Verma A, De Potter T, Macle L, Kautzner J, Linz D, Anic A, Chun J, Van Herendael H, Almorad A, Berte B, Bhardwaj R, Reichlin T, Mansour M, Schmidt B, Knecht S, Reddy VY, Rackauskas G.
abstractText:
Background

Omny-IRE (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT05971693) evaluated the safety and effectiveness of a large-tip focal, multielectrode, contact force-sensing, pulsed field ablation basket catheter with electroanatomic mapping integration.

Objective

The purpose of this study was to report 12-month (12M) study outcomes.

Methods

Pulmonary vein isolation was performed using the OMNYPULSE catheter. Patients underwent follow-up through the 12M postablation visit with electrocardiography (preprocedure, predischarge, and at 1, 3, 6, and 12M), 24-hour Holter monitoring (3, 6, and 12M), and remote rhythm monitoring (weekly: 1-5M; monthly: 6-12M; and symptom-triggered recordings). The secondary effectiveness end point was 12M freedom from documented symptomatic or asymptomatic atrial arrhythmia (≥30 seconds) and acute procedural failure. Device- and/or procedure-related serious adverse events, quality of life assessed using Atrial Fibrillation Effect on Quality-of-Life scores, and health care utilization (cardiovascular-related hospitalizations and antiarrhythmic drug use) were also evaluated.

Results

Of the 188 enrolled patients, 136 comprised the main phase cohort for safety and effectiveness evaluations. In this cohort, 12M freedom from symptomatic or asymptomatic atrial arrhythmia was 82.5% (90.1% using standard-of-care monitoring only). Clinical success, defined as freedom from documented symptomatic arrhythmia and acute procedural failure, was 89.9%, while single procedural success was 89.2%. Device- and/or procedure-related serious adverse events occurred in 2.9% of main phase patients. The mean overall Atrial Fibrillation Effect on Quality-of-Life score improved by 25.5 points from baseline to 12M. Cardiovascular-related hospitalizations decreased by 40.9% compared with the 12M preprocedure period, and class I or III antiarrhythmic drug use decreased by 49.3% from baseline to 6-12M postablation.

Conclusion

Omny-IRE results demonstrated the effectiveness, safety, and health care benefits of pulsed field ablation with the OMNYPULSE catheter.

Clinical trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05971693.

title: Triple-helical ligands selectively targeting the closed αI domain of integrin α2β1.
authorString: Shibata SS, Oki H, Kawahara K, Kokame K, Masuda R, Fujii KK, Koide T.
abstractText: Integrins α1β1, α2β1, α10β1, and α11β1 are known to recognize the GxxGEx motif of the collagen triple helix through their αI domains, with the Glu residue engaging the domain via a divalent metal cation. The binding amino acid sequences containing these motifs, identified from native collagen, exhibit low subtype selectivity. Here we identify novel triple-helical peptides that selectively bind the α2I domain independently of Glu and metal ions. Yeast two-hybrid screening of randomized triple-helical peptide libraries yielded non-natural sequences in which the canonical Glu was replaced by aliphatic residues such as Met. X-ray crystal structural analysis of the representative variant GFOGMR in complex with the α2I domain revealed a new binding mode. In this mode, peptides are recognized by the closed, inactive conformation of the α2I domain without metal coordination. This cryptic interaction, likely unused by native ligands, provides a new basis for the design of subtype-specific ligands targeting collagen-binding integrins.

title: Design and rationale of a multicenter randomized trial assessing strategies for catheter ablation of persistent atrial fibrillation- The STAR AF 3 trial.
authorString: Macle L, Sebag F, Yamane T, Champagne J, Romero J, Scherr D, Roux JF, Deyell MW, Hayashi H, Amit G, Sadek M, Novak P, Kistler PM, Grimaldi M, Essebag V, Raymond-Paquin A, Roca-Luque I, Sanders P, Zei P, Nery P, Dyrda K, Joza J, Steinberg C, Ha A, Quadros K, Harada M, Andrade J, Verma A.
abstractText:
Rationale

Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) is the cornerstone of catheter ablation procedures for the treatment of atrial fibrillation (AF). However, the success rates of PVI are limited for patients with persistent AF. Yet, the optimal ablation strategy beyond PVI alone in patients with persistent AF remains to be established.

Study design and objectives

The STAR AF 3 trial is an international multicenter prospective, single-blind, blinded endpoint, clinical trial that includes patients with persistent AF of more than 3 months duration referred for a first catheter ablation procedure. Enrollment will occur at 33 centers in Europe, Canada, Australia, USA and Japan. The aim of this study is to compare the strategy of PVI alone with two strategies that add ablation to PVI: PVI+drivers ablation and PVI+posterior wall isolation. Patients will be equally randomized into one of these three ablation strategies. Patients will be followed up for 18 months. The primary endpoint will be the time to first recurrence of documented atrial tachyarrhythmia (atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter, or atrial tachycardia) between 91 days and 18 months after a single ablation procedure. An atrial tachyarrhythmia will qualify as a recurrence if it lasts 30 s or longer and is documented by 12-lead electrocardiogram, electrocardiographic rhythm strips, or transtelephonic monitor recordings. Although a post-ablation blanking period of 3 months will be observed, a repeat left atrial ablation procedure done at any time will also qualify as a primary endpoint event. Enrollment is completed and a total of 617 patients have been recruited into the trial. The trial is registered at the Clinicaltrials.gov (NCT04428944) CONCLUSIONS: The STAR AF 3 trial is a large multicenter randomized trial assessing the optimal ablation strategy for patients with persistent AF.

title: Rapid Transport to Extracorporeal CPR: Urging Caution Prior to Implementation.
authorString: Kimbrell JM, Kreinbrook JA, Robinson AE, Bunting AJ, Ambur S, Prekker ME, Simpson NS, Cheskes S.
abstractText: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) has survival that remains near 10% despite years of research and advancements in care. Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) has been explored as an option for patients who suffer OHCA and are refractory to traditional therapies. In nearly every system that implements ECPR for OHCA, there is a requirement to incorporate intra-arrest transport (IAT). There are three major randomized controlled trials which have evaluated the role of ECPR in OHCA. These include ARREST, INCEPTION, and Prague OHCA. While ARREST has the strongest data to support ECPR, it includes only 30 patients. The larger trials such as INCEPTION and Prague OHCA did not show statistically significant results in favor of ECPR. Each trial has a unique study design and statistical analysis.The current evidence is not strong enough to support widespread adoption of ECPR into the prehospital systems of care. Examining the statistical pitfalls, potential biases, and methodological confounders of the existing ECPR literature against the background of previously reported data surrounding IAT─the full impact of effect of ECPR cannot exclude consideration of the impact of the effect of IAT. As more data is needed to better understand the full impact of implementing ECPR into a system of care, we encourage caution and thoughtful analysis to leaders who may be considering the addition of ECPR into an existing system of care. ECPR shows early promise for select patients. The development of an ECPR system is complex and has numerous facets, typically including the incorporation of early IAT for OHCA. At this time, more studies are needed on the full impacts of implementing ECPR into a system of care for OHCA.

title: Patiromer Efficacy across Kidney Function and Hyperkalemia Subgroups in Heart Failure and Reduced Ejection Fraction: A DIAMOND Post Hoc Analysis.
authorString: Kalogeropoulos AP, Rashid AM, Anker SD, Bayes-Genis A, Böhm M, Budden J, Cleland JGF, Coats AJS, Ezekowitz JA, Filippatos G, Goudev A, Khan MS, Lindenfeld J, Lund LH, Merkely B, Mentz RJ, Metra M, Moutchia J, Ponikowski P, Priest EL, Rossignol P, Senni M, Waechter S, Weir MR, Pitt B, Butler J.
abstractText: In the DIAMOND (Patiromer for the Management of Hyperkalemia in Subjects Receiving RAASi Medications for the Treatment of Heart Failure) trial, patiromer enabled optimization of renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system inhibitors (RAASi) for patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and current or recent hyperkalemia. Impaired kidney function substantially increases hyperkalemia risk due to impaired potassium excretion. Therefore, in this post hoc analysis, we examined the efficacy of patiromer across baseline kidney function and hyperkalemia subgroups. We classified all patients randomized to patiromer (N=439) or placebo (N=439), after successful run-in optimization, into 4 subgroups according to estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <45 vs ≥45 mL/min/1.73m2 (trial eligibility criterion: ≥30 mL/min/1.73m2) and baseline hyperkalemia (≤5.0 vs >5.0 mEq/L; trial required K >5.0 or prior RAASi discontinuation for hyperkalemia). Patiromer reduced adjusted mean change in serum potassium (primary outcome) across all subgroups, with the largest effect in patients with eGFR <45 mL/min/1.73m2 and hyperkalemia (-0.28 mEq/L, 95% CI -0.38 to -0.18, P<0.001) and the smallest in those with eGFR ≥45 mL/min/1.73m2 and normokalemia (-0.08 mEq/L, 95% CI -0.12 to -0.04, P<0.001; Pinteraction <0.001). Patiromer reduced time-to-first hyperkalemia consistently across subgroups. Patients with eGFR <45 mL/min/1.73m2 and baseline hyperkalemia derived the numerically greatest effect in prevention of mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist down-titration (hazard ratio 0.39, 95% CI 0.18-0.84, P=0.02) and had the highest win ratio for hyperkalemia-related morbidity-adjusted outcomes (3.03, 95% CI 1.96-4.70, P<0.001). However, Pinteraction values for these secondary endpoints were not statistically significant. Patiromer reduced serum potassium across baseline kidney function and hyperkalemia subgroups, with greater effect in patients with reduced kidney function and baseline hyperkalemia. These findings suggest potential heterogeneity in potassium-lowering effects of patiromer across subgroups, although the analysis is exploratory and should be considered hypothesis-generating.

title: Evidence Suggests Linoleic Acid Exerts Health Benefits Beyond Cardiovascular Disease: A Brief Review of Clinical and Observational Studies.
authorString: Messina M, Nagra M, Goldman D, Nechuta S.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

Questions challenging the healthfulness of diets high in linoleic acid (LA) and seed oils, which are major sources of this essential fatty acid, have recently arisen. These questions are especially relevant to adherents of plant-based diets as their LA intake is higher than the general population. Some maintain that LA increases inflammation and oxidative stress and for these reasons, despite its ability to lower circulating LDL-cholesterol levels when replacing saturated fat, does not lower cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. Because most of the discussion about LA has focused on CVD, the primary focus of this manuscript is to examine the effects of LA on health outcomes aside from CVD.

Recent findings

Interventional and observational studies indicate increasing LA intake lowers risk of CVD. Beyond CVD, possible benefits include preventing hepatic fat accumulation, increasing muscle mass, decreasing risk of skin cancer, decreasing epigenetic aging, increasing the healthspan, and improving cognitive function and decreasing risk of developing neurocognitive disorders. Support for these proposed benefits comes from observational studies and randomized controlled trials (RCTs), although more from the former. The observational evidence is especially robust in the case of cognitive function and neurological disorders, as the results of all but one of the eight recently published cohort studies show LA exposure, as assessed by dietary intake or circulating levels, is supportive of benefit, although much of the data come from analyses of one cohort. While it is premature to conclude that LA intake exerts benefits beyond CVD, evidence is sufficient to warrant that this possibility should be included in discussions about the role of LA and seed oils in the diet. Given the large contribution LA makes to energy intake, particularly among consumers of plant-based diets, research aimed at more definitively determining the range of possible benefits, especially related to cognitive function, is warranted.

title: Pneumothorax rates following cardiac surgery with versus without continuous serratus anterior plane catheters: a secondary analysis of trial data with propensity score matching to a historic cohort.
authorString: Saeed H, Kang S, Uppal V, Ho L, Herman C, Bailey JG.

journal.title: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie

abstractText: Moderate to severe pain is common after cardiac surgery, especially in the first two postoperative days. Inadequate pain control may prolong intensive care unit (ICU) stay, may increase cost, and contributes to chronic pain. Enhanced Recovery After Cardiac Surgery (ERACS) protocols prioritize multimodal analgesia, including regional anesthesia techniques. In a recent randomized trial with continuous serratus anterior plane (SAP) catheters, we found unexpectedly high pneumothorax rates. To address this, we aimed to design a propensity-score-matched comparison using patients from the same institution to control for institutional practice patterns, surgical techniques, and patient demographics that could confound comparisons with published literature rates from other centres. We conducted a secondary analysis of RCT data with propensity score matching to a historic cohort. We compared the pneumothorax rates in patients receiving continuous SAP catheters in our previous Cardiac-Serratus Anterior Plane (Cardiac-SAP) trial with those in a retrospective institutional database cohort of patients receiving standard care undergoing cardiac surgery via sternotomy. The two groups were propensity score matched in a 1:20 ratio based on age, sex, smoking status, surgery type, and pre-existing respiratory disease. We analyzed univariate comparisons using Fisher's exact test or the percentile bootstrapping method. We matched 50 patients from the Cardiac-SAP trial to 989 retrospective cohort patients. After matching, the SAP catheter group was associated with a significantly higher risk of pneumothorax (12% vs 3%; odds ratio, 5.3; 95% confidence interval, 2.1 to 13.6; P < 0.001). There were no significant differences for other outcomes, including ICU readmissions, length of ventilation, and length of ICU or hospital stay. Patients who developed a pneumothorax had longer ventilation time and longer hospital stays. Our data suggest that SAP catheter use as a part of a randomized trial for cardiac surgery was associated with a higher rate of pneumothorax in trial participants than in a historic cohort of a similar population, though causality is unclear. Differences in monitoring within the trial and the inherent risks in this population may have contributed.

title: Non-Invasive Stimulation of the Median Nerve: Neuromodulation to Reduce Atrial Arrhythmias in Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation (The Randomized BEAT-AF Pilot Study).
authorString: Chorin E, Iakobishvili Z, Schwartz LA, Banai A, Rosso R, Viskin S, Holand Y, Benari A, Ziv A, Reddy VY.
abstractText:
Background

Non-invasive low-level electrical stimulation of the median nerve favorably affects atrial electrophysiology and reduces inflammation.

Objective

To determine whether a novel wearable home-care neuromodulation device that performs median nerve stimulation (MNS) reduces atrial arrhythmias (AA) and related symptoms.

Methods

BEAT-AF was a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled, 12-week pilot study. Patients with a paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF) burden of 0.5-25% on ambulatory 14-day ECG (aECG) monitoring were randomized 1:1 to either MNS or Sham, using a wristband-like neuromodulation and ECG monitoring device.

Results

Among 31 patients (n=15 MNS / n=16 Sham; age 67.3±9.7; 23 M / 8 F; CHA2DS2-VASc 2.6±1.7; median AF burden 4.9% [IQR 5.2%]),immediate pre-/post-treatment ECG recordings demonstrated a 35% reduction in premature atrial contraction (PAC) burden with MNS versus a 7% increase with Sham (p=0.039).Comparing baseline to 12-week 14-day ECGs, PAC burden was reduced by 26.5% (p=0.046) vs a numerical change of +3.94% (p=0.94; Sham, between group p=0.46), and the adjusted median AF burden numerically was reduced by 63% (MNS) vs 4.1% (Sham; p=0.42). By EHRA classification, symptomatology improved with MNS (0.45 vs 0.02 reduction in score; p=0.017), with a 26.3% shift from EHRA Class III to I with MNS) (vs Sham; p=0.048).

Conclusions

In patients with paroxysmal AF, non-invasive median nerve stimulation reduced PAC burden and improved symptomatology; there was a numerical but non-significant reduction in AF burden. This pilot study sets the stage for future pivotal trials of MNS in AF patients.

title: Zero-fluoroscopy approach to left atrial appendage closure using intracardiac echo guidance.
authorString: Hoskins MH, Bestawros M, Nair S, Adjei-Poku Y, Remo B, Mazer S.
abstractText:
Background

Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) with the Watchman™ device is typically performed with the use of transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) and fluoroscopy. LAAC guided by intracardiac echo (ICE) without the use of fluoroscopy has not been previously described.

Objective

In this series, we describe the safety and feasibility of Watchman™ implantation using only ICE imaging and without the use of fluoroscopy.

Methods

214 patients undergoing LAAC with the Watchman FLX™ or Watchman FLX™ Pro device and using a planned fluoroscopy-free approach were studied. ICE was used for echocardiographic imaging in all cases. TEE was not used in any cases. Fluoroscopy was used as a bail-out approach when it was felt to be clinically necessary by the operator. Peri-procedural, 45-day, and 1-year efficacy and safety outcomes were assessed.

Results

In 203/214 patients (94.8%), LAAC was completed without the use of fluoroscopy. Bail-out fluoroscopy was required in 11/214 patients (5.1%). Successful device implantation was completed in 212/214 patients (99.1%). The rate of any peri-device leak at 45 days post-procedure was 11.6%. Procedural complications were limited to one pericardial effusion and one case of ventricular tachycardia.

Conclusion

LAAC with the Watchman™ device using ICE imaging and without the use of fluoroscopy appears to be safe and effective. The rates of procedural success, complications, and peri-device leaks on 45 day follow up were consistent with that seen in pivotal clinical trials. Further studies are needed to assess the broader applicability of this technique.

title: Prognostic Impact of Ventricular Arrhythmia Timing in Acute Coronary Syndromes Treated with Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Pizzi D, Fazzini L, Pugliesi GM, Faizan MA, Rehman T, Meshkati H, Perego GB, Curti E, Mapelli M, Montisci R, Agostoni P, Senni M, Gori M, Jentzer JC.
abstractText:
Background

Ventricular arrhythmias (VA) often complicate acute coronary syndromes (ACS). The prognostic impact of VA timing relative to percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains unclear.

Objective

To assess the prognostic significance of VA based on their timing of occurrence in relation to PCI.

Methods

Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies reporting all-cause mortality with and without VA (sustained or hemodynamically unstable VT/VF) in ACS patients undergoing PCI. The endpoints analyzed were short-term (30 days/in-hospital) and long-term (1 year) mortality. A network meta-analysis comparing VA-before PCI, VA-during PCI, and VA-after PCI with the group not experiencing VA as a reference was conducted.

Results

Twelve studies comprising 49,963 patients were included, of whom 3,475 (7.0%) experienced VA. VA was associated with increased short- (OR 5.04, 95%CI 3.78-6.72) and long-term mortality (OR 2.92, 95%CI 2.20-3.86). In patients alive at discharge/30 days, subsequent long-term mortality risk did not differ between those with and without VA (OR 0.97, 95%CI 0.62-1.52). The network meta-analysis showed that all VA timings are associated with a significantly higher risk compared with the group not experiencing VA. Sensitivity analysis found that VA-after is associated with higher short-term mortality than earlier VA (OR 3.37, 95%CI 1.46-7.82).

Conclusions

VA substantially increase the risk of death in patients with ACS undergoing PCI. Mortality risk emerges to be associated with the timing of VA occurrence, with VA-after PCI associated with the highest risk. These findings highlight the prognostic relevance of arrhythmic events across the entire peri-procedural window, underscoring the need for refined risk stratification.

title: Recurrence analysis of cardiac arrhythmias: A systematic review of methods, substrate characterisation and clinical translation.
authorString: Moualla M, Gomes J, Salinet J.
abstractText: Cardiac arrhythmias are a major cause of morbidity and mortality, and catheter ablation depends on accurate identification of the underlying substrate. Cardiac signals are nonlinear and non-stationary, which limits Fourier-based analysis. Recurrence quantification analysis (RQA) and related recurrence methods make fewer assumptions, but their use in arrhythmia research has not been systematically synthesised. This review examines what recurrence analysis has demonstrated, how consistently its methods have been applied, and what remains before it can support clinical substrate characterisation. Of 309 records retrieved from four databases (207 after deduplication), 48 studies met the eligibility criteria and citation searching added one, giving 49. Each study was examined in full text for its signals, cohorts, embedding parameters, threshold selection, metrics and results, and assigned to one of six methodological categories. The three studies that tested recurrence against surrogate or shuffled data each found structure in fibrillatory signals that matched stochastic surrogates did not reproduce. Recurrence metrics and dominant frequency were weakly correlated and diverged in substrate characterisation, so they are not interchangeable. Threshold selection was the most consequential uncontrolled variable: five strategies were in use, ten of the 35 studies that apply a threshold reported no selection rule, and only three examined how their results depended on it. Determinism and laminarity, although the most frequently reported metrics, were not consistently the strongest discriminators. Clinical readiness is not established: only one study used recurrence mapping prospectively to guide ablation, in ten patients without randomisation. A shared threshold-selection standard and prospective multicentre validation are needed.

title: Atacicept in IgA Nephropathy - Phase 3 Trial Final Efficacy Analysis.
authorString: Barratt J, Brenner RM, Barbour SJ, Campbell KN, Doan T, Eren N, Floege J, Fordyce MW, Jha V, Khawaja Z, Kim BS, Liew A, Maes B, Pal A, Pecoits-Filho R, Phoon RKS, Rizk DV, Suzuki H, Tesař V, Trimarchi H, Wei X, Yu L, Zhang H, Lafayette R, ORIGIN Phase 3 Trial Investigators.

journal.title: The New England journal of medicine

abstractText: Atacicept resulted in a significantly greater reduction in the urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo in a previously published analysis of this trial, ORIGIN 3. Final prespecified efficacy results are reported here. We randomly assigned adults with biopsy-confirmed IgA nephropathy to receive weekly subcutaneous atacicept at a dose of 150 mg or placebo. We carried out final analyses of two secondary end points: the change in the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) at week 52 and the annualized eGFR slope through week 104; additional hierarchically tested end points and safety were assessed. Of 431 patients who underwent randomization, 428 received atacicept or placebo (214 per group). At week 52, the mean change in the eGFR was -0.11 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area (95% confidence interval [CI], -1.44 to 1.22) with atacicept and -5.69 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, -7.04 to -4.35) with placebo (mean difference, 5.58 ml per minute per 1.73 m2; 95% CI, 3.68 to 7.48; P<0.001). Through week 104, the mean annualized eGFR slope was -0.60 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, -1.62 to 0.41) with atacicept and -5.60 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, -6.64 to -4.57) with placebo (difference, 5.00 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 per year; 95% CI, 3.55 to 6.45; P<0.001). Composite kidney-disease progression occurred in 11 patients (5.1%) in the atacicept group and in 38 patients (17.8%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.12 to 0.48; P<0.001); no patients in the atacicept group had progression to dialysis, transplantation, or death, as compared with 7 patients in the placebo group. Adverse events occurred in 160 of 214 patients (74.8%) in the atacicept group and in 167 of 214 patients (78.0%) in the placebo group; serious adverse events occurred in 7.0% and 15.4%, respectively. One patient (in the placebo group) died. Atacicept slowed and stabilized the decline in the eGFR as compared with placebo. (Funded by Vera Therapeutics; ORIGIN 3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04716231.).

title: Economic evaluations in emergency medicine: a 25-year systematic review of patient-level cost-effectiveness analyses (2000-2025).
authorString: Wilmé V, Chenou A, Sauleau EA, Kepka S.

journal.title: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine

abstractText: Emergency departments (EDs) face rising demand and resource constraints. Cost-effectiveness analyses (CEAs) can inform resource allocation, but patient-level CEAs in emergency care remain methodologically heterogeneous.
