This review aimed to identify and describe patient-level CEAs in emergency care between 2000 and 2025, appraise their methodological quality, and explore temporal trends and evidence gaps. This systematic review was reported according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020. PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and gray literature were searched for patient-level CEAs of clinical or organizational interventions across prehospital, ED, and postemergency settings. Data were synthesized narratively across key methodological domains. Methodological quality of the economic evaluations was assessed using the quality of health economic studies (QHES) instrument. Descriptive and exploratory analyses were performed. Forty-seven studies were identified, of which 96% were conducted in EDs. Infectious diseases and ED crowding were the most addressed topics, followed by cardiovascular conditions and trauma, although a broad range of issues was covered. Studies were mainly conducted in high-income countries and evaluated organizational or diagnostic interventions. Healthcare system or hospital perspectives and short time horizons predominated. QHES scores were moderate-to-high (mean: 80.0, SD: 9.2, range: 56-96), with substantial variability and only a weak exploratory temporal trend toward higher scores. Prehospital and postemergency settings were underrepresented. Patient-level CEAs in emergency medicine are increasing, with many studies achieving high QHES scores, but remain heterogeneous in scope and methods. This review highlights the range of interventions evaluated and the methodological features relevant to interpreting economic evidence in emergency care.

title: Fatigue Interventions in Patients With Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease and Heart Diseases: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Holmgaard FG, Raunkiaer M, Hansen RS, Shabnam J.
abstractText: Fatigue is a significant yet under-addressed symptom in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and heart diseases, impairing quality of life. This systematic review aims to investigate the effectiveness of rehabilitation interventions, including exercise and psychosocial support, in managing fatigue in COPD, ischemic heart disease, and heart failure, providing evidence to guide clinical practice. This systematic review is registered in PROSPERO and follows the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, EMBASE, MEDLINE, CINAHL, and PsycINFO. The pooled meta-analysis with all studies had an overall mean difference of -11.93 [-15.63; -8.24]. Physical activity had the largest effect (-17.01 [-24.40; -9.61]), while combined psychosocial and physical activity interventions were insignificant. Results remained unchanged after sensitivity analysis. Meta-analyses highlight the effectiveness of non-pharmacological rehabilitation interventions, particularly physical activity, in managing fatigue. Psychosocial interventions show potential but may be less effective. Future research should optimize strategies, explore fatigue mechanisms, and address patient needs to improve intervention efficacy.

title: Cardiac Structure and Function in Women After Preeclampsia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Yao JV, Wang B, Wong C, Browne A, Peters S, Taylor A, Brennecke S, Winship I, Zentner D.
abstractText:
Background

Preeclampsia increases the risk of long-term heart failure (HF) by 4-fold. Unfortunately, however, universal guidelines for postpartum HF surveillance are lacking. Stage B/subclinical HF has been shown to predict risk of major adverse cardiac outcomes. Some suggest that initiating cardioprotective therapy at this early stage can reduce progression to symptomatic HF.

Objectives

The aim of this review was to explore cardiac structure and function in women with a history of preeclampsia and to identify when subclinical HF develops in this group.

Methods

A systematic search of MEDLINE, EMBASE and CINAHL was conducted according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines to identify all studies assessing left ventricular function on transthoracic echocardiography in women with a history of preeclampsia.

Results

A total of 45 case-control studies comprising 8,991 women, including 2,288 women with a history of preeclampsia, were included in the final analysis. During pregnancy, women with preeclampsia had a higher left ventricular mass index (LVMI) (standard mean difference: 10.85 [95% CI: 6.30-15.39]), relative wall thickness (0.05 [95% CI: 0.03-0.08]), E/e' (1.58 [95% CI: 1.02-2.13]), isovolumetric relaxation time (8.74 [95% CI: 3.14-14.34]), lower E/A ratio (-0.27 [95% CI: -0.51 to -0.04]) and reduced absolute global longitudinal strain (GLS) values (2.27 [95% CI: 0.43-4.11]), indicating reduced myocardial function compared with normotensive controls. Postpartum, GLS remained reduced, and LVMI remained elevated in women with a history of preeclampsia. This difference persisted out to 10 years postpartum. There was no significant difference in all other variables >6 months postpartum. Evidence for persistent LVMI elevation >6 months postpartum was not robust in sensitivity analyses excluding overlapping cohorts. Left ventricular ejection fraction and right ventricular function remained similar in the preeclampsia and control groups throughout.

Conclusions

Preeclampsia is associated with subclinical myocardial dysfunction, characterized by impaired GLS and increased LVMI. Persistent impairment in GLS was observed up to 10 years postpartum, whereas the association with elevated LVMI beyond 6 months postpartum should be interpreted with caution. Further studies are required to assess when subclinical myocardial dysfunction progresses to symptomatic clinical HF.

title: Long-term efficacy and safety for the complement factor B inhibitor iptacopan in IgA nephropathy.
authorString: Rovin BH, Trimarchi H, Maes B, Perkovic V, Kashihara N, Zhang H, Barratt J, Cheng H, Lee H, Lee SH, Lim SK, Raju SB, Satirapoj B, Seyahi N, Tian YC, Wu CH, Xiong ZY, Xue H, Yee SY, Petrovic-Bulatovic K, Attari Z, Butylin D, Jacinto-Sanders S, Pletscher M, Magirr A, Renfurm R, Hach T, Rizk DV.
abstractText:
Introduction

Iptacopan, a factor B inhibitor, targets alternative complement pathway overactivation, a key driver of glomerular inflammation in IgA nephropathy. In the phase 3 APPLAUSE-IgAN trial (NCT04578834), iptacopan significantly slowed kidney function decline versus placebo over 24 months (difference in total estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] slope: 3.02 ml/min per 1.73 m2 per year [95% confidence interval (CI) 2.02, 4.01; P < 0.001]).

Methods

Patients who completed APPLAUSE-IgAN or the phase 2 iptacopan trial (NCT03373461) could enter an open-label rollover extension program (REP) (NCT04557462). Patients in this REP receive oral iptacopan 200 mg twice daily alongside supportive care. Patients from the phase 2 trial were not included in efficacy analyses.

Results

Overall, 194 and 174 patients from the APPLAUSE-IgAN iptacopan and placebo arms, respectively, entered the REP. In patients who received iptacopan for up to 48 months, the total annualized eGFR slope was -3.49 ml/min per 1.73 m2 per year (95% CI -4.17, -2.80). Urine protein-to-creatinine ratio from first morning void (UPCR-FMV) reduction was sustained through 48 months with iptacopan (geometric mean ratio to baseline: 0.61 [95% CI 0.50, 0.75]). Before receiving iptacopan, the total eGFR slope over 24 months in APPLAUSE-IgAN placebo arm patients who entered the REP was -5.29 ml/min per 1.73 m2 per year (95% CI -6.09, -4.49). After switching to iptacopan, the total eGFR slope improved to -2.11 ml/min per 1.73 m2 per year (95% CI -3.08, -1.13) over the next 24 months. UPCR-FMV decreased after switching (geometric mean ratio to baseline at month 48: 0.74 [95% CI 0.59, 0.91]). Long-term safety up to 5 years (median treatment duration: 29.9 months) was consistent with the known profile of iptacopan.

Conclusions

Long-term treatment with iptacopan led to sustained slowing in eGFR decline and proteinuria reduction that were also observed after switching from placebo. No new safety signals were observed.

Trial registration

Registered at ClinicalTrials.gov with study numbers NCT04578834 (APPLAUSE-IgAN), NCT03373461 (phase 2 trial of iptacopan in IgAN), and NCT04557462 (rollover extension program).

title: Clinical Factors Associated with Intraoperative Increase in Cardiac Troponin and Its Prognostic Value During Liver Transplantation.
authorString: Kim YJ, Kim KS, Kim SH, Kwon HM, Jun IG, Song JG, Hwang GS.
abstractText: Perioperative elevations of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) are common during liver transplantation (LT); however, the clinical significance of new-onset intraoperative elevations remains unclear. We evaluated the frequency, magnitude, associated factors, and prognostic implications of intraoperative hs-cTnI elevations, distinguishing new-onset from pre-existing elevations. We retrospectively analyzed 4151 consecutive LT recipients (2008-2021). The primary endpoint was 90-day mortality. Elevated hs-cTnI was defined as > 40 pg/mL (1× upper reference limit [URL]). The relative importance of 19 variables for new-onset intraoperative hs-cTnI > 400 pg/mL (10× URL) was ranked using an exploratory shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis. Intraoperative hs-cTnI > 1× URL occurred in 66.1% (2745/4151) of patients, including new-onset elevation in 62.5% (2304/3685) of patients with normal baselines (~90% had an increase of > 20%). In pre-existing elevation, an exploratory threshold > 22× URL was associated with mortality (adjusted HR 5.91, 95% CI 3.11-11.22; P < 0.001), whereas new-onset elevation was not (P = 0.74). Per doubling of intraoperative hs-cTnI, 90-day mortality increased overall (adjusted HR 1.21, 95% CI 1.11-1.32) and in pre-existing elevation (adjusted HR 1.29, 95% CI 1.13-1.46; both P < 0.001). Low intraoperative hematocrit, anemia, factor VIII, von Willebrand factor, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio showed the highest SHAP importance for new-onset >10× URL. New-onset intraoperative hs-cTnI elevations were common during LT and linked to anemia, hypercoagulability, and inflammation. However, they did not predict 90-day mortality in patients with normal baselines; risk increased only in pre-existing elevations. Intraoperative hs-cTnI elevations should be interpreted in the context of preoperative levels.

title: Electrophysiological remodeling in the hypertrophic cardiomyopathy MYBPC3 R943X mutant in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes and modulation by I<sub>Kto</sub>-targeting drugs.
authorString: Abdelsayed M, Gianitsos ET, Yu A, Mercola M.

journal.title: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology

abstractText: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is a leading cause of sudden cardiac death, often driven by pathogenic variants in sarcomeric genes such as MYBPC3. The precise electrophysiological mechanisms underlying arrhythmogenesis in HCM, particularly in the context of MYBPC3 truncating mutations, remain incompletely defined, hindering the development of targeted therapies. Here, we leveraged human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) carrying the MYBPC3 p.R943X mutation to systematically characterize action potential remodeling and evaluate the efficacy of ion-channel-modulating drugs.High-throughput optical AP assays revealed that R943X mutant hiPSC-CMs exhibit profound baseline electrophysiological disruption, with a marked reduction in normal AP profiles and increased incidence of pro-arrhythmic morphologies, including AP prolongation, early afterdepolarizations, and delayed afterdepolarizations, compared to isogenic non-diseased controls. Pharmacological profiling demonstrated that NS-5806, a Kv4 channel modulator, exerts a biphasic, dose-dependent effect in non-diseased isogenic control cells and partially restores normal AP morphology in R943X mutants by enhancing repolarizing current and suppressing AP prolongation. In contrast, Acacetin, an I<sub>To</sub> and late Na<sup>+</sup> current inhibitor, preserved electrical stability in non-diseased isogenic control cells but conferred limited and dose-sensitive rescue in mutants, with higher concentrations exacerbating arrhythmic features. These findings provide direct evidence that targeted augmentation of transient outward K<sup>+</sup> current can selectively mitigate mutation-induced arrhythmogenic remodeling in hiPSC-CMs modeling HCM. Our study highlights the therapeutic promise, and challenges, of precision ion-channel modulation in genetic cardiomyopathy and establishes a scalable platform for genotype-guided drug discovery.

title: Clinical Implementation of Angiography-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve for Revascularization Guidance: Initial Multicenter United States Experience.
authorString: Sara JDS, Carvalho PEP, Mutlu D, Belzer W, Goel M, Fath AR, Murad B, Whitbeck M, Strepkos D, Alexandrou M, Williford NN, Kladou E, Poulose A, Traverse J, Voudris K, Rangan BV, Brilakis ES, Sandoval Y.
abstractText: Real-world data on the adoption and clinical performance of angiography-derived physiology in the United States (U.S.) remain limited. We evaluated the implementation of FFRangio (CathWorks, Tel Aviv, Israel) and associated clinical outcomes across a multicenter U.S. healthcare system. We performed a multicenter observational cohort study across 4 centers involving consecutive adult patients undergoing invasive coronary angiography in whom FFRangio was performed in at least 1 coronary vessel based on clinical indication. The primary endpoint was target-vessel failure (TVF), defined as a composite of cardiovascular death, target vessel myocardial infarction and target vessel revascularization during follow-up, stratified by FFRangio values >0.80 versus ≤0.80. A total of 675 vessels in 469 patients were assessed by FFRangio; 240 (36%) had values ≤0.80 and 435 (64%) >0.80. Among lesions with FFRangio ≤0.80, 182 (76%) underwent PCI, 27 (11%) CABG, and 32 (13%) were managed medically. Among lesions with FFRangio >0.80, revascularization was deferred in 406 (92%), with 22 (5%) undergoing PCI and 12 (3%) CABG. The LAD was the most frequently treated vessel (51%). At a median follow-up of 10.2 months, the incidence rate of TVF was 1.55% per 100 lesion-years (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.57-3.36) in the FFRangio >0.80 group versus 6.30 per 100 lesion-years (95% CI, 3.25-11.0) in the FFRangio ≤0.80 group (hazard ratio [HR] 4.61, 95% CI: 1.61-13.2; p=0.002). Among deferred lesions with FFRangio >0.80, TVF rate was 1.73 per 100 lesion-years (95% CI: 0.64-3.77). In conclusion, FFRangio supported safe deferral of revascularization and risk-stratification, with low event rates among lesions with values >0.80.

title: Management of Antiplatelet Regimen During Surgical Procedures: a Report from the MARS Registry.
authorString: Vazquez DF, Akram T, Bruneman B, Weideman S, Monhollen A, Jeong M, Pelton J, Minniefield N, Angiolillo DJ, Banerjee S.
abstractText: Optimal perioperative management of patients on dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains controversial, with substantial variability in current clinical practice. The MARS registry is a prospective multicenter observational study evaluating perioperative outcomes in post-PCI patients on DAPT undergoing surgery within 2 years of PCI. We assessed the incidence of Net Adverse Cardiovascular Events (NACE), defined as a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), ischemic stroke, urgent coronary revascularization, or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) type ≥3 bleeding. A total of 132 consecutive patients undergoing moderate- to high-risk surgery were followed from 14 days preoperatively to 30 days postoperatively. Of the 132 patients, 79 underwent non-cardiac surgery (NCS) and 53 underwent cardiac surgery (CS). The mean age was 66 years, and 68% were male. Diabetes mellitus was present in 48%, chronic kidney disease in 29%, and 42% had undergone PCI for an acute coronary syndrome. Mean time from PCI to surgery was 269 ± 217 days. Prior bleeding and stent thrombosis were reported in 11% and 5% of patients, respectively. Aspirin was continued in 60% and P2Y12 inhibitors in 36%, with mean discontinuation 4 and 6 days preoperatively, respectively. Intravenous antiplatelet bridging with cangrelor was used in 12 patients (9.1%) and unfractionated heparin as anticoagulant therapy in 15 patients (11.0%). NACE occurred more frequently after CS compared with NCS (18.9% vs. 10.1%, p=0.17). Major bleeding (BARC ≥3) occurred in 5.3% with no difference between CS and NCS. There were no cardiovascular deaths and no difference in all-cause mortality. Compared with no bridging, cangrelor bridging was associated with numerically higher NACE (25.0% vs. 12.5%, p=0.22), without differences in bleeding. On multivariable logistic regression, cangrelor bridging was not independently associated with NACE (adjusted OR 2.18, 95% CI 0.43-8.71, p=0.34). In conclusion, among post-PCI patients on DAPT undergoing moderate- to high-risk surgery, aspirin was continued in 60%, cangrelor bridging was used in 9.1%, and although NACE rates were numerically higher after cardiac surgery and with bridging, these differences were not significant after multivariable adjustment, consistent with confounding by indication.

title: Depressive Symptoms and Incident Peripheral Arterial Disease Among Adults With CKD: Findings From the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) Study.
authorString: Nizamuddin M, Missikpode C, Chen HY, Lash JP, Wang G, Fischer MJ, CRIC Study Investigators.

journal.title: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation

abstractText: Depression is associated with cardiovascular disease among adults with CKD, but its relationship with peripheral arterial disease (PAD) has not been thoroughly examined despite both conditions being common in this population. We evaluated the risk for incident PAD and death associated with elevated depressive symptoms among adults with CKD. Observational prospective cohort study. Adults with mild to moderate CKD in the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort Study (CRIC) Study. Elevated depressive symptoms as defined by a Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) score ≥ 11. Incident PAD, defined as an Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) < 0.9 or confirmed clinical PAD event (amputation or angioplasty). Composite outcome of incident PAD or death. The association between baseline elevated depressive symptoms and incident PAD, as well as a composite of incident PAD or death, was examined with Cox proportional hazard models. Mediation analysis explored the pathways between elevated depressive symptoms and these outcomes. Among 2,757 individuals, 25% had elevated depressive symptoms (BDI ≥11) at baseline. During a median follow-up of 10 years, 24% of participants developed incident PAD. The rate of incident PAD was higher in those with elevated depressive symptoms (3.6 events per 100 person-years) compared with those without (2.2 events per 100 person-years). After accounting for other factors, baseline elevated depressive symptoms were associated with a higher risk of incident PAD (HR 1.23; 95% CI: 1.02-1.47). Smoking and physical inactivity mediated 20% and 10%, respectively, of this association. Similar associations were found between baseline elevated depressive symptoms and a composite of incident PAD or death. Findings were not different when elevated depressive symptoms were defined by BDI >14 and BDI ≥16. Residual bias and confounding. Absence of depression diagnosis. Elevated depressive symptoms were associated with a significantly increased risk of incident PAD in adults with CKD, which is partly mediated by smoking and physical inactivity. Renal failure, depression, peripheral vascular disease, mortality, health behaviors.

title: Outcomes Following Kidney Failure From IgA Nephropathy Compared to Diabetic Kidney Disease and Other Glomerular Diseases.
authorString: Bagchi S, Wang J, Teixeira-Pinto A, Scholes-Robertson N, Lim WH, Wong G.

journal.title: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation

abstractText: IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is a major cause of kidney disease worldwide, yet contemporary comparative outcome data following kidney failure are limited. We compared trends in access to kidney transplantation and mortality among patients with kidney failure due to IgAN, to those with diabetic kidney disease (DKD) or other glomerular diseases (GD). Longitudinal cohort study. Patients with kidney failure initiating maintenance dialysis (1965-2023) due to IgAN, DKD, or other GD in Australia. Kidney failure etiology. All-cause death, death from cardiovascular disease and cancer, and entry onto the deceased donor kidney transplant waitlist. Age-standardized incidence, prevalence, and mortality rates and temporal trends assessed using log-linear regression-derived estimated annual percentage change (EAPC). Associations between kidney failure etiology and outcomes estimated using inverse probability treatment-weight (IPTW)- adjusted Cox proportional hazards models. 44,659 patients (4,925 with IgAN; 15,079 with other GD; 24,655 with DKD) were studied with a median follow-up of 53 months (IQR 23.3-109.8). The age-standardized incidence of IgAN remained stable over the past two decades (EAPC -0.01%, 95% CI - 0.80 to 0.78). Compared with other GD, patients with IgAN experienced lower all-cause (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.65-0.73; p < 0.001) and cardiovascular (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.60-0.74; p < 0.001) mortality, and increased rates of being placed on the transplant waitlist (HR 1.55, 95% CI 1.39-1.73; p < 0.001). Compared with IgAN, patients with DKD had higher all-cause (HR 1.58, 95% CI 1.53-1.64, p<0.001) and cardiovascular mortality (HR 1.81, 95% CI 1.71-1.91, p<0.001), lower cancer-related mortality (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.70-0.95, p=0.009), and lower rates of being placed on the transplant waitlist (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.60-0.69, p<0.001). Residual confounding, diagnostic misclassification due to variation in biopsy practices. Differences in survival and placement onto the kidney transplant waitlist exist across patients with different etiologies of kidney failure. Individuals with IgAN have longer survival and enter the transplant waitlist more often than those with DKD or other GD.

title: Transvenous Lead Extraction Without Dedicated Surgical Back up in Low-Risk Patients.
authorString: Mekary W, Bhatia N, Merchant FM, El-Chami MF.
abstractText:
Background

Transvenous lead extraction (TLE) is associated with major complications that could require immediate surgical rescue. These procedures are performed in an EP lab or hybrid OR with the presence of a surgical team on standby. We have designed an institutional protocol that permits performance of TLE in low-risk situations, in an EP lab without dedicated surgical back-up.

Objectives

To investigate outcomes of TLE in low-risk patients METHODS: We retrospectively identified patients who underwent low-risk TLE at Emory Healthcare between 2010-23. Low-risk TLE were defined as an extraction of a pacing or ICD lead with a dwell time >= 1 and <= 5 years or a lead < 1 year that required extraction tools.

Results

Among 482 patients who met the criteria, the average lead age was 2.8 ± 1.2 years. The mean number of targeted leads per patient was 1.6±0.7. Extraction tools were required in 33.1% of cases. Major complications occurred in 0.83% of patients (n=4): 2 pericardial effusions requiring pericardiocentesis, 1 pneumothorax and 1 death from cardiogenic shock in an end stage heart failure patient. The patients with pericardial effusions and pneumothorax were part of a procedure that required lead revisions and the insertion of 1 or more new leads. No patients required surgical rescue.

Conclusion

This study suggests that, in selected "low-risk" patients, TLE can be performed safely in an experienced EP lab at centers with on-site cardiac surgery but without a dedicated surgical standby team, potentially reducing resource utilization in resource-limited healthcare environments.

title: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors and mortality and liver-related outcomes in patients with alcoholic cirrhosis, type 2 diabetes, and obesity.
authorString: Osman MM, Sims OT, Chiang DJ.
abstractText: Sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2-i1) improve cardiovascular and renal outcomes in type 2 diabetes mellitus, but their safety and clinical impact in advanced liver disease remain uncertain because patients with cirrhosis were underrepresented in major trials. Using the TriNetX research network, we identified adults with alcoholic cirrhosis, type 2 diabetes, and obesity and compared outcomes according to SGLT2-i exposure. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 5,128 matched pairs were analyzed. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes included all-cause hospitalization, ascites, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, hepatic encephalopathy, and variceal bleeding. In the matched cohort, SGLT2-i use was associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.66 to 0.78), hospitalization (HR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.80 to 0.89), ascites (HR, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.77), spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (HR, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.62 to 0.87), and variceal bleeding (HR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.99), with no difference in hepatic encephalopathy. Among patients with alcoholic cirrhosis, type 2 diabetes, and obesity, SGLT2-i use was associated with improved survival and fewer liver-related complications.

title: Impact of surgical timing in left-sided infective endocarditis with persistently positive blood cultures.
authorString: Gómez-Ramírez D, Olmos C, López J, Sáez C, Landín P, Zulet P, de Miguel M, Oña A, Gómez-Lus VG, Lozano A, Vilacosta I, Alberto San Román J.
abstractText: Guidelines define persistent infection in infective endocarditis (IE) as positive blood cultures after 7 days of adequate antibiotic therapy. However, persistently positive blood cultures (PPBC) at 48 to 72 hours are already associated with a worse prognosis. We aimed to assess the clinical profile, temporal trends, and impact of surgical timing on outcomes in patients with left-sided IE and PPBC at 48 to 72 hours. We performed a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data from 3 Spanish tertiary centers (1998-2024). We compared patients with PPBC with those with blood culture clearance and assessed the effect of surgical timing using a time-dependent Cox model, inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting, and a day-7 landmark analysis to minimize immortal time bias and confounding by indication. Among 1265 patients with positive baseline cultures, 283 (22.4%) had PPBC at 48 to 72 hours. These patients exhibited a more severe clinical and microbiological profile and higher in-hospital mortality (36.0% vs 22.3%; P < .001). In the day-7 landmark analysis, surgery within the first 7 days was associated with lower in-hospital mortality (HR, 0.53; 95%CI, 0.30-0.95), with consistent trends across the time-dependent Cox and inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting models. PPBC at 48 to 72 hours identifies a high-risk subgroup of patients with left-sided IE. In these patients, early surgery within the first 7 days was associated with a potential survival benefit in adjusted models, supporting earlier reassessment of infection control to optimize surgical timing.

title: Early Outcomes of Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis in Aortic Arch Pathologies: A Nordic Multicentre Study.
authorString: Karelis A, Asciutto G, Jonsson M, Svarre S, Lind R, Dorenberg EJ, McGeevy D, Mani K, Dias NV, Resch T, NordAARC Consortium.

journal.title: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery

abstractText:
Objective

This study evaluated the feasibility and early clinical outcomes of the Gore thoracic branch endoprosthesis (TBE) in the treatment of aortic arch pathologies.

Methods

This multicentre retrospective study, conducted and reported in accordance with the STROBE statement, included consecutive patients undergoing thoracic endovascular aortic repair with TBE between February 2024 and July 2025. No restrictions were applied regarding the type or extent of aortic disease, use of staged procedures, or concomitant adjunctive endovascular interventions. Primary endpoints were technical success, thirty day mortality, and overall survival, while endoleak occurrence, primary target vessel patency, stroke, and spinal cord ischaemia (SCI) were secondary.

Results

Sixty-four patients (median age 73 years [interquartile range 59, 77]; 69% men) were included. Indications for treatment included degenerative aneurysm (n = 26; 41%), chronic dissection (n = 18; 28%), subacute dissection (n = 11; 17%), and acute dissection (n = 9; 14%). The left subclavian artery was the target vessel in 59 cases (92%), followed by the brachiocephalic trunk in three (5%) and the left common carotid artery in two (3%). Technical success was achieved in 95% of cases (n = 61), with failures attributed to two type Ia endoleaks and one type IIIa endoleak. Thirty day mortality was 3% (n = 2). Early unplanned re-interventions occurred in four patients (6%). No strokes or SCI were observed. Median follow up was 6 months (2, 10). No late mortality was observed, and primary patency of all branches was 100%. One late unplanned re-intervention, unrelated to the TBE device, was required. During follow up, 12 patients (19%) had endoleaks, including type II (n = 4), type Ia (n = 4), type Ib (n = 2), type III (n = 1), and type V (n = 1). Estimated freedom from type Ia endoleak at 12 months was 93 ± 3%, while estimated overall survival at 12 months was 97 ± 2%.

Conclusion

TBE demonstrated high technical success and acceptable early outcomes across a range of aortic arch pathologies. However, the relatively high rate of endoleaks and need for early re-interventions highlight the importance of careful patient selection and close continuous post-operative surveillance.

title: Impact of donor care unit opening and use on lung donation from deceased organ donors after brain death.
authorString: Ho FY, Wang X, Schaubel DE, Biscotti M, Kerlin MP, Reese PP, Christie JD, Vail EA.

journal.title: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation

abstractText: Deceased donors after brain death (DBD) transferred to donor care units (DCUs) have higher rates of lung donation than donors remaining in hospitals, but contributions of regional DCU availability and donor transfer to lung donation remain unknown. Cohort study using Organ Procurement & Transplantation Network (OPTN) deceased donor registry files, including adult DBDs managed in donation regions with operating DCUs, 2017-2024. Multivariable logistic regression and G-computation were used to test the hypothesis that individual donor transfer to DCU, rather than regional DCU availability, is associated with a higher likelihood of lung donation (primary outcome). Among 27,795 DBDs managed by 28 OPOs, lung donation rate was 28.6% (7,958 donations). After adjustment for donor characteristics, predicted lung donation rates were similar before (29.1%, 95% CI 27.9-30.2) and after (28.9%, 95% CI 28.3-29.6) regional DCU adoption. Despite wide variation in regional transfer rates (5.2-96.7%), greater regional transfer was not associated with lung donation. After adjustment for donor factors, organ recovery year, and organ procurement organization, donor transfer to DCUs (vs. hospitals) remained associated with higher odds of lung donation overall (aOR 1.32, 95% CI 1.20-1.46) and for each DCU type (independent (aOR 1.41, 95% CI 1.21-1.65) and hospital-based (aOR 1.27, 95% CI 1.12-1.44)). Superior lung donation rates were seen only for donors transferred from regional hospitals to DCUs. There was no observable association between the proportion of donors transferred and lung donation, suggesting that superior donation outcomes may reflect the selection of donors for transfer rather than system-wide effects of DCU availability.

title: Decoding Atrial Fibrillation Heterogeneity: A Nationwide Phenome-Wide Association Study in England.
authorString: Yoshimura H, Chung SC, Lip GYH, Schmidt AF, Providencia R.
abstractText:
Background

Age and sex influence atrial fibrillation (AF) prevalence and outcomes, yet comprehensive data on sex- and age-specific health care utilization in patients newly diagnosed with AF remain limited.

Objectives

We aimed to address this gap using a phenome-wide association study (Phe-WAS) approach.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study using nationwide Clinical Practice Research Datalink data linked to Hospital Episodes Statistics. Adults diagnosed with AF between 1998 and 2016 (n = 199,433) were matched 1:1 by age and sex to non-AF control subjects. Primary and secondary care interactions 5 years post diagnosis were analyzed using Phe-WAS with Bonferroni-adjusted significance thresholds. Logistic regression estimated odds ratios for conditions in AF vs control groups, stratified by sex and age. Associations were assessed for novelty through literature review and causality using published Mendelian randomization studies.

Results

Patients with AF had higher rates of cardiovascular and noncardiovascular conditions than control subjects, with marked sex- and age-specific patterns. Women had more bleeding complications, pneumonia, Clostridium difficile enterocolitis, cholangitis, and electrolyte disturbances, whereas men had higher rates of alcohol-related disorders, ventricular arrhythmias, cardiac arrest, and cardiomyopathy. Younger patients with AF (<50 years) more often had alcohol-related mental and behavioral disorders, gout, and dilated cardiomyopathy, while older patients (>60 years) more often had heart failure, ischemic stroke, renal failure, and respiratory infections. Of 51 phenotypes more common in AF, 28 were previously reported, and 23 were potentially novel. Mendelian randomization analyses suggested AF was causal for 19 associations.

Conclusions

This Phe-WAS demonstrates the broad spectrum of health care interactions in AF beyond traditional cardiovascular complications.

title: Cardiac screening in the young for the detection of cardiovascular disease and prevention of sudden cardiac death.
authorString: Tardo DT, Sharma S.
abstractText: Sudden cardiac death in the young is often due to silent inherited cardiac conditions. Although evidence increasingly supports cardiac screening as a preventative strategy, policies and frameworks differ globally. Structured screening frameworks that utilise AI-enabled technologies show great potential for enhancing disease detection and risk prediction.

title: Transitioning towards life-cycle management and burden monitoring of atrial fibrillation.
authorString: Poggio A, Moretti A, Cavallone E, Juvenal F, Carbonaro A, Saglietto A, De Ferrari GM, Anselmino M, Ballatore A.
abstractText:
Introduction

Atrial fibrillation (AF) poses a significant burden on public health, being associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. In most cases, disease progression follows a continuum, ranging from a predominantly electrical disorder to late stages characterized by profound disruption of atrial architecture and advanced atrial cardiomyopathy.

Areas covered

Common cardiovascular risk factors play a pivotal role in the progression and self-perpetuation of AF by promoting left atrial remodeling, creating the substrate necessary for the maintenance of the arrhythmia. Correction of these risk factors, together with rhythm-control strategies, can delay and, in some cases, interrupt disease progression while improving patients' quality of life. Catheter ablation, when combined with life-style modifications and risk factors management, has the potential to positively modify the arrhythmogenic substrate that favors AF and could promote reverse atrial remodeling.

Expert opinion

Comprehensive management of risk factors and comorbidities, together with novel ablation techniques (e.g. pulsed field ablation) and the development of atrial-selective antiarrhythmic drugs, may further improve AF care. In addition, redefining long-term rhythm control success from freedom from AF recurrence to AF burden may allow better patient stratification, inform therapeutic decisions, and ultimately improve patient outcomes.

title: Lung Transplantation for Interstitial Lung Disease: A Northern Ireland Cohort Study.
authorString: Martin N, Mathews A, Connor R, Aboaly M, Albelushi M, Box A, Ball P, Clarke A, Convery R, Cullen K, Donnelly S, Gardiner E, Green A, Hagan C, Henry K, John A, Jackson E, Kara J, Kelly C, Kelly M, Linden D, Lindsay J, Macpherson L, McCloskey M, McCord A, McIntyre P, McKenna P, Major E, McManus T, McNicholl D, Minnis P, Mohammad N, Mohammed S, Muse H, Murtagh E, Okpoko F, Polley L, Rutherford C, Sarup L, Shamboul A, Sharkey R, Taylor-Straford S, Fisher A, Chaudhuri N.
abstractText: Lung transplantation (LTx) is the definitive treatment for advanced fibrotic interstitial lung disease (ILD), but referral timing remains challenging. Data on outcomes of Northern Ireland (NI) patients referred for LTx are limited. In this multicentre retrospective cohort study, all ILD referrals for LTx from the five NI healthcare trusts between January 2014 and March 2024 were analysed. Demographic, clinical, lung function and transplant outcome data were extracted from electronic health records. Patients were classified according to transplant assessment and listing outcomes. One hundred thirty-eight patients were referred (median age 60.5 years; 64.5% male; 35.5% female); idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis was the most common diagnosis (44.2%). Of 138 referred patients, 64 (46.4%) were considered suitable for advanced LTx assessment, while 68 (49.3%) were unsuitable and 6 (4.3%) declined further assessment. Of those suitable for advanced assessment, 28 (43.8%) were listed for transplantation and 11 (17.2%) died before completion of assessment. Age was the only independent predictor of mortality before assessment completion, increasing risk by 13.9% per year (p = 0.011). The median interval between initial referral to LTx satellite clinic review was 131.5 days for the eligible cohort. The median interval from initial transplant clinic review to advanced assessment was 80 days excluding those patients with intentional pathway prolongation due to a watch-and-wait approach. Forty-five per cent of pre-transplant investigations, particularly coronary angiography, occurred > 6 months after satellite clinic review and may have contributed to some delays from referral to advanced assessment. Of patients listed for transplantation, 14 (50.0%) died while waiting, 11 (39.3%) underwent LTx, and 3 remained active on the waiting list. Nearly half of ILD referrals were unsuitable for advanced LTx assessment, largely because of age and comorbidity. Delays in assessment pathways, for example watchful waiting and access to coronary angiography, may contribute to high pre-transplant mortality. Earlier referral and streamlined investigation pathways may improve transplantation outcomes.

title: Retinal Microvascular Morphometry in Recreational Athletes Using Anabolic-Androgenic Steroids: A Cross-Sectional Study.
authorString: El-Cheikh Mahmoud AA, Thinggaard BS, Hjortebjerg R, Buhl LF, Grauslund J, Christensen LL, Glintborg D, Andersen MS, Lindholt JS, Diederichsen A, Thevis M, Kistorp C, Frystyk J, Pedersen FN.
abstractText: Illicit use of anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS) is common among recreational athletes and is associated with cardiovascular complications and premature death. However, effects on the microvasculature have not been quantified. The retina provides non-invasive access to the systemic microvasculature, and retinal vessel morphometry has been associated with incident cardiovascular events. We conducted a cross-sectional study of 151 recreational athletes from the Fitness Doping in Denmark study: 74 active AAS users, 26 former users who had ceased AAS use at least 3 months before enrollment, and 51 age- and sex-matched controls with no lifetime AAS exposure. Disc-centered fundus photographs were analyzed using semiautomated software to obtain the arteriovenous ratio (AVR), central retinal arteriolar and venular equivalents (CRAE/CRVE), arteriolar and venular fractal dimensions, and arteriolar and venular tortuosity. Associations of active AAS use and cumulative lifetime AAS exposure with retinal vessel morphometry were assessed through multivariable linear regression models adjusted for age, sex, and body fat percentage. Active users had a lower arteriolar fractal dimension than both controls (1.12 vs. 1.16, P < 0.05) and former users (1.12 vs. 1.18, P < 0.05), and a lower AVR than controls (0.67 vs. 0.70, P < 0.05) in multivariable models. Former users did not differ from controls on any retinal variable. Cumulative lifetime AAS exposure was not independently associated with any outcome. Active AAS use was associated with lower arteriolar fractal dimension and lower AVR after adjustment. These differences were absent in former users and unrelated to cumulative exposure duration. The cross-sectional design precludes determining the prognostic significance of these differences. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT05178537.

title: The FIBR-CMR score: a novel risk model integrating fibrinogen and cardiac magnetic resonance for major adverse events after STEMI.
authorString: Jiang YJ, Wei L, Hou XC, Zhao Q, Zhao CX, Dong JX, Ge H, Yang YN, Pu J.
abstractText: Survivors of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) face a substantial residual risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCEs). Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) excellently delineates structural injury but does not assess the concomitant systemic prothrombotic state. We investigated whether fibrinogen, a key mediator of thrombosis, provides incremental prognostic value beyond CMR for risk stratification. In a prospective multicenter cohort of 532 STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), plasma fibrinogen was measured post-procedure. CMR was performed within 7 days to assess left ventricular thrombus (LVT) and aneurysm (LVA). The primary endpoint was MACCEs over a median follow-up of 55.5 months. A novel risk score (the Fibrinogen and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Score, or FIBR-CMR score) was derived from a multivariable Cox model, and its performance was assessed through internal validation using bootstrap resampling (optimism-corrected C-index = 0.73). Elevated fibrinogen independently predicted LVT (adjusted OR 1.46, 95% CI 1.09-1.96) and LVA (adjusted OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.20-1.79) after adjusting for clinical and CMR confounders. Fibrinogen (≥ 3.36 g/L) independently predicted MACCEs (HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.10-1.53), an effect partially mediated by LVT (48.5%) and LVA (38.0%). The FIBR-CMR score (1 point for elevated fibrinogen, 2 for LVT, 2 for LVA) stratified patients into low (0 points), intermediate (1-2 points), and high (≥ 3 points) risk groups. The high-risk group had a strikingly elevated 5-year MACCE incidence of 48.3%, compared to 15.2% and 6.0% in the intermediate- and low-risk groups, respectively (optimism-corrected C-index = 0.73). The integration of fibrinogen with CMR-defined structural injury provides powerful synergism for risk assessment. The FIBR-CMR score, derived from a prospective multicenter cohort, effectively identifies a high-risk phenotype of STEMI patients. This score now requires external validation but represents a promising step toward personalized risk assessment. Clinicaltrials.gov; NCT03768453.

title: Machine-learning-integrated NLRC3 and cardiac troponin T dual-analyte lateral-flow biosensor for point-of-care acute coronary syndrome screening and acute myocardial infarction-unstable angina discrimination.
authorString: Gu X, Teng P, Li X, Zhang Q, Hou J, Liu S.
abstractText: The implementation of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin assays has significantly improved the prompt diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Nevertheless, early risk stratification and the swift diagnosis of acute coronary syndromes (ACS) remain challenging. We report a machine-learning-integrated NLRC3/cTnT dual-analyte time-resolved fluorescent lateral-flow immunoassay biosensor for quantitative ACS screening and discrimination of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) from unstable angina (UA). The biosensor uses europium nanoparticle time-resolved fluorescence in a dual-channel lateral-flow setup to simultaneously detect NLRC3 and cTnT within 20 min. The original serum sample is diluted separately for each channel, with 100 µL of the diluted sample applied to each. The optimized NLRC3 and cTnT assays demonstrated strong quantitative performance, precision, minimal cross-reactivity, and acceptable interference resistance. In clinical evaluation, NLRC3 alone identified ACS with 80.5% accuracy but was less effective in distinguishing AMI-UA. By combining NLRC3 and cTnT using a Naïve Bayes classifier, the dual-analyte biosensor improved to 84.6% sensitivity, 89.6% specificity, and 87.8% accuracy for AMI-UA discrimination. This study introduces a dual-pathophysiology lateral-flow biosensor that merges inflammatory-risk and myocardial-injury detection, providing a practical POCT method for decentralized ACS triage.

title: Immunohistochemical markers for dating cardiac conduction system injury: current knowledge and forensic implications.
authorString: Aktar N, De Simone S, Fabrello C, Orsini F, Bibbò R, Cipolloni L.
abstractText: The postmortem timing of myocardial injury remains a major challenge in forensic pathology, particularly when conventional histological methods are insufficient during the early hours after an ischemic insult. We conducted a critical narrative review of immunohistochemical markers for myocardial injury dating, focusing on their biological applicability to the cardiac conduction system (CCS). The search was performed using PubMed and Scopus; no date restriction was applied. Over the past three decades, markers including complement components (C5b-9), cardiac troponins, fibronectin, and connexin 43 have been investigated, with varying degrees of validation, for injury dating in working ventricular myocardium. However, the CCS - comprising the sinoatrial node, atrioventricular node, bundle of His, and Purkinje fibers - is a histologically and molecularly distinct tissue that has received remarkably little attention in this context. We highlight fundamental differences in cellular composition, connexin expression profiles, extracellular matrix content, and baseline protein abundance between conduction and ventricular tissue that are likely to significantly alter marker behavior and temporal kinetics. The direct application of ventricular-based immunohistochemical timelines to the CCS lacks empirical support and may lead to forensic misinterpretation. The medico-legal implications are potentially significant, as accurate timing of conduction system injury is relevant to cases of sudden unexplained death, drug-induced arrhythmias, blunt cardiac trauma, and medical negligence litigation. Systematic, tissue-specific validation studies are urgently needed.

title: Pregnancy Outcomes After Living Kidney Donation.
authorString: Wang C, Naylor KL, McArthur E, King JA, Sontrop JM, Beyene J, Connaughton D, Hendren E, Hladunewich M, Lam NN, Lentine KL, Lyons R, McDonald SD, Roshanov PS, Youngson E, Garg AX.
abstractText: People who become pregnant after living kidney donation may be at increased risk of pregnancy-related adverse outcomes, although the evidence is unclear. To determine whether pregnancies after living kidney donation are associated with a higher risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes than matched pregnancies among nondonors. This matched cohort study used provincial administrative health care databases from Ontario, British Columbia, and Alberta, Canada, and included living female kidney donors aged 18 to 42 years who donated a kidney between July 1992 and August 2021 and subsequently had singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation. These pregnancies were matched 1:4 with singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation among female nondonors. Pregnancies in donors and nondonors were matched on delivery date, age at delivery, years between cohort entry and delivery, number of prior pregnancies, and income. Final follow-up occurred until March 2023. Outcome analysis occurred from August 2024 to September 2026. The primary outcome was a composite of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia. Secondary outcomes included 12 maternal, fetal and neonatal adverse outcomes, including the individual components of the primary outcome, the composite of low birth weight or preterm birth, and small for gestational age at birth. The sample included 385 pregnancies in 252 living kidney donors (mean [SD] age, 27.8 [5.0] years) matched to 1540 pregnancies in 1535 nondonors (mean [SD] age, 27.0 [4.8] years). The primary composite outcome of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia occurred in 46 donor pregnancies (11.9%) and 128 nondonor pregnancies (8.3%; risk ratio, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.10-2.08). Among the 12 secondary outcomes, the 95% CI for the risk ratio excluded 1.00 for the outcome of small for gestational age, which occurred in 53 donor pregnancies (13.8%) and 121 nondonor pregnancies (7.9%) (risk ratio, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.37-2.52). In this study, pregnancy after living kidney donation was associated with a higher risk of the composite outcome of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia, when compared with matched pregnancies in nondonors. Most postdonation pregnancies were uncomplicated. These findings support counseling donor candidates who may become pregnant about this risk and informing the prenatal care of donors who become pregnant.

title: Atrial Fibrillation Pattern and Outcomes After Contemporary Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion.
authorString: Singh A, Bandaru RR, Singh V, Bolaji O, Nerella N, Arias R, Katinic J, Pasupuleti S, Sanon S.
abstractText:
Background

Atrial fibrillation (AF) pattern predicts thromboembolic risk during anticoagulation, but its prognostic importance after left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is uncertain.

Objectives

To determine whether AF pattern independently predicts residual clinical risk after contemporary LAAO and whether peri-device leak (PDL) or device-related thrombus (DRT) identify a persistently high-risk subgroup.

Methods

We studied 3,459 patients with documented AF pattern undergoing LAAO in a contemporary multicenter registry. AF was classified as paroxysmal, persistent or long-standing persistent, or permanent. The primary endpoint was a 2-year hierarchical composite of death, stroke or systemic embolism (stroke/SE), and major bleeding analyzed by win ratio. Inverse probability weighting and propensity score methods adjusted for baseline differences. Follow-up imaging assessed PDL and DRT.

Results

After inverse probability weighting, persistent and permanent AF were associated with progressively worse hierarchical outcomes compared with paroxysmal AF (win ratios 1.39 and 1.59, respectively). Non-paroxysmal AF was associated with higher stroke risk (HR 1.64; 95% CI 1.07-2.50), without increased mortality or major bleeding. PDL and DRT were more frequent in non-paroxysmal AF. In the PDL/DRT subgroup, non-paroxysmal AF was associated with higher first stroke/SE risk (HR 1.83; 95% CI 1.00-3.34), concentrated 180-540 days after LAAO.

Conclusions

AF pattern independently stratified residual clinical risk after LAAO, with progressively worse severity-weighted outcomes from paroxysmal to persistent and permanent AF. Excess risk was driven primarily by thromboembolism. In the PDL/DRT subgroup, the association was concentrated 180-540 days after LAAO, suggesting these patients may benefit from prolonged thromboembolic surveillance.

title: Clinician adherence to peri-procedural warfarin bridging guidelines for patients with atrial fibrillation enrolled in an anticoagulation management service.
authorString: Sinan HH, Li M, Kang EM, Chow RH, Sylvester KW, Connors JM.
abstractText: The 2023 AHA/ACC/HRS guidelines recommend against peri-procedural bridging of warfarin in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) based solely on CHA₂DS₂-VASc score without additional thromboembolic (TE) risk factors. At our institution, decisions regarding bridging in moderate-to-high TE risk AF patients who require anticoagulation interruption incorporate patient-specific factors. To evaluate adherence to institutional peri-procedural guidelines and associated TE and bleeding events. This retrospective, single-center, observational study included AF patients receiving warfarin for stroke prevention enrolled in the anticoagulation management service. Patients had moderate-to-high TE risk (CHA₂DS₂-VASc ≥5 or other TE risk factors) and underwent moderate-to-high bleeding risk procedures between August 2023 and August 2024. Major outcomes included a composite of TE events (deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, cerebrovascular accidents, or transient ischemic attack) and a composite of International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis (ISTH) major and clinically relevant non-major bleeding (CRNMB) events within 30 days post-procedure. Minor outcomes included individual components of the composite outcomes and adherence to the institutional guideline. Of the 145 procedures, bridging therapy was used in 87 (60%) and omitted in 58 (40%), with 92.4% compliance to institutional guidance. No TE events were observed. Of 21 bleeding events, one ISTH major bleed occurred in the bridging group and was attributed to the procedure, while 20 were CRNMB events. There were 15 (17.4%) CRNMB events in the bridging group and 5 (8.6%) in the non-bridging group. High adherence to institutional bridging guidelines was observed. A trend towards fewer bleeding events with no increased TE events was found in the non-bridging group in patients with moderate-to-high TE risk.

title: Placental mitochondrial impairment in preeclampsia patients.
authorString: Vaka R, Hinton E, Edwards K, LaMarca B.
abstractText: Preeclampsia is a pregnancy-specific hypertensive disorder characterized by new-onset hypertension after 20 weeks of gestation, accompanied by end-organ dysfunction with or without proteinuria. Affecting approximately 5-7% of pregnancies worldwide, it remains a leading cause of maternal and fetal morbidity and mortality. Despite decades of research, the underlying pathophysiology of preeclampsia remains incompletely understood. However, increasing evidence implicates placental mitochondrial oxidative stress in its pathogenesis. In this review, we summarize the current literature pertaining to ultrastructural evidence of mitochondrial damage, defects in oxidative phosphorylation and electron transport chain activity, and alterations in reactive oxygen species production, antioxidant defense, and mitochondrial biogenesis. Finally, we discuss translational considerations and highlight how therapeutic strategies targeted at restoring mitochondrial function may represent a promising approach for managing preeclampsia.

title: When to Start Oral Anticoagulant Therapy Post-Stroke: From Common to Rare Conundrums.
authorString: Budinčević H, Črnac P, Meštrović A, Ernoić M, Vogrinc D, Poje JM, Penić SZ, Vujović S.
abstractText: This review summarizes recent evidence on when to start oral anticoagulant therapy following stroke, including both common and rare clinical conundrums. While previous recommendations based on Diener's rule suggested waiting up to 12 days based on stroke severity and neuroradiological findings, newer data support earlier initiation or resumption of anticoagulation, particularly for mild and moderate ischemic strokes, generally within 4 days. In patients with a history of intracerebral hemorrhage, anticoagulation resumption involves weighing thromboembolic risk against recurrent hemorrhage risk, requiring individualized decisions regarding whether and when anticoagulation should be resumed. Clinical recommendations for post-stroke anticoagulation emphasize early, individualized initiation of direct oral anticoagulants for mild-to-moderate ischemic strokes based on neuroimaging. After intracerebral hemorrhage, anticoagulation is generally restarted within 4 to 8 weeks for atrial fibrillation, with earlier resumption potentially warranted in selected high-thromboembolic-risk patients, particularly those with mechanical heart valves.

title: Age-stratified mortality following operative management of complete versus incomplete traumatic subaxial cervical spinal cord injury.
authorString: Singh A, Sbaih O, Botros M, Furst T, Molinari R, Rubery P, Puvanesarajah V.

journal.title: The journal of spinal cord medicine

abstractText: Postoperative mortality following traumatic subaxial cervical spinal cord injury (cSCI) remains substantial, yet the combined influence of neurologic completeness and age on survival is poorly characterized in operatively treated patients. This study evaluated age-stratified mortality after surgical management of complete versus incomplete traumatic subaxial cSCI. Retrospective cohort study using risk ratio analysis, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards. Global federated electronic health record database (TriNetX). Adults who underwent surgery for traumatic subaxial cSCI, identified using ICD-10 and CPT codes, with injury classified as complete or incomplete (n = 5,477). Operative management of traumatic subaxial cSCI. All-cause mortality at 3, 6 months, and 1 year postoperatively. Independent predictors of mortality were identified via Cox regression. Complete cSCI was associated with significantly higher mortality at 3 months (10.73% vs. 7.7%; RR 1.39), 6 months (12.5% vs. 9.2%; RR 1.36), and 1 year (14.7% vs. 11.2%; RR 1.31) (all P < 0.001). Mortality differences were most pronounced in patients aged 61-80 years, with approximately twofold higher risk in complete injuries. Increasing age, male sex, diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease independently predicted mortality. Complete traumatic cSCI carries significantly higher postoperative mortality than incomplete injury, particularly among patients aged 61-80 years. These findings underscore the combined prognostic impact of neurologic severity and age, and may guide perioperative counseling and risk stratification, but should not be interpreted as demonstrating formal age-dependent effect modification.

title: Prolonged QT Interval in Hospitalized Internal Medicine Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study of Determinants and Reversibility.
authorString: Chebbi D, Bougarn W, Mtar F, Dahmen FB, Abdallah M.

journal.title: Romanian journal of internal medicine = Revue roumaine de medecine interne

abstractText: QT interval prolongation is a common electrocardiographic abnormality in hospitalized patients, associated with malignant ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death. Its determinants in internal medicine, and the reliability of correction formulas used to identify it, remain insufficiently characterized. We conducted a retrospective, single-center study including 277 patients hospitalized with QTc prolongation - defined by Bazett correction (QTcB >450 ms in men; ≥460 ms in women) - between January 2016 and December 2023. QTc was independently calculated using Bazett (QTcB) and Framingham (QTcF) formulas, and agreement between the two was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis. Multivariable logistic regression (complete-case analysis) explored predictors of QTcF-confirmed prolongation, and reversibility was assessed by repeat ECG performed after correction of the underlying reversible cause, or within 72 hours when no such cause was identified. Mean age was 59.2 ±17.2 years, with a slight female predominance (54.2%). Only 78 patients (28.1%) had QTcF-confirmed prolongation despite all meeting QTcB inclusion criteria. Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of +31.7 ms between QTcB and QTcF (SD 18.9; 95% limits of agreement: -5.3 to +68.7 ms), strongly correlated with heart rate (r=0.92, p<0.001): the overcorrection increased from +3.6 ms at heart rate <70 bpm to +64.4 ms at >110 bpm. QTcB normalized on the follow-up ECG in 68.2% of patients. In a complete-case multivariable model (n=96 with available serum bicarbonate), no variable reached conventional statistical significance; serum bicarbonate (OR=1.121 per mmol/L; 95% CI: 0.991-1.268; p=0.069) and hypertension (OR=2.522; 95% CI: 0.875-7.275; p=0.087) showed borderline associations with QTcF-confirmed prolongation. In an exploratory analysis of the diabetic subgroup (n=148), peripheral neuropathy (DN4 ≥4) was associated with a 15.8 ms higher mean QTcB (age-adjusted 95% CI: 4.7-27.0 ms; p=0.006). Bazett's formula substantially and heart-rate-dependently overestimates QT prolongation compared with the Framingham formula, a discrepancy now precisely quantified. QT prolongation in hospitalized internal medicine patients is predominantly acquired and reversible. Diabetic peripheral neuropathy was associated with higher QTcB values in an exploratory analysis. Serum bicarbonate showed only a non-significant trend toward association with QTcF-confirmed prolongation after complete-case multivariable adjustment; this hypothesis warrants confirmation in prospective studies with complete acid-base characterization before any clinical application.

title: Contemporary US Practice Patterns Regarding Anticoagulation and LAA Closure in ICH Survivors With Atrial Fibrillation.
authorString: Kamel H, Viscoli C, Francois C, Khatri P, Elm J, Feske S, Bachmann A, Gama-Chonlon L, Brigger H, Bianco G, Murthy S, Tirschwell DL, Shaban A, Buletko BA, Venkatasubramanian C, Sheth KN.
abstractText: Optimal secondary stroke prevention remains uncertain for patients with intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and atrial fibrillation (AF). Anticoagulation reduces ischemic stroke in AF but increases hemorrhage. Left atrial appendage (LAA) occlusion is emerging as an alternative to anticoagulation, but few data exist on its safety in patients with ICH. Amid this uncertainty, little is known about US practice patterns in this scenario. We performed a study using linked electronic health record, pharmacy, and insurance claims data on >11 million patients at 29 US healthcare organizations, each with multiple hospital sites, in the TriNetX Linked platform. Validated International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision codes were used to identify adults with AF hospitalized for ICH during 2016 to 2024. To identify antiplatelet and anticoagulant prescriptions, we used RxNorm codes, a standardized drug naming system from the National Library of Medicine. LAA occlusion was defined using validated Current Procedural Terminology codes. Kaplan-Meier statistics were used to calculate cumulative rates of therapy utilization from discharge through 5 years. We created 3 mutually exclusive treatment groups with censoring at LAA occlusion for analyses of antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy and at anticoagulation for analyses of antiplatelet therapy. We identified 2276 patients with AF hospitalized with ICH. Their mean age was 65.4 (±12.8) years, 40.6% were female, median CHA2DS2-VASc score was 5 (interquartile range, 5-6), 19.6% had Medicare, 26.9% received an anticoagulant prescription within 90 days before ICH, and half were discharged home or to an acute rehabilitation facility. Cumulative 5-year rates were 59.8% (95% CI, 55.5%-64.2%) for anticoagulation, 39.9% (95% CI, 34.1%-46.3%) for antiplatelet therapy, and 4.5% (95% CI, 2.6%-7.6%) for LAA occlusion. LAA occlusion rates did not differ by index ICH date (P=0.88). In a contemporary, multicenter US cohort of patients with ICH and AF, 60% were prescribed anticoagulation after discharge, and the remainder were mostly treated with antiplatelet therapy only. These findings suggest widespread use of different secondary stroke prevention strategies in patients with AF and ICH.

title: Proteome-Wide Mendelian Randomization Identifies Therapeutic Targets for Ischemic Stroke.
authorString: Song K, Li C, Shi M, Qi S.
abstractText:
Background

Ischemic stroke carries substantial residual risk despite acute revascularization and secondary prevention, and small-vessel disease (SVD) lacks specific preventive therapy. Mendelian randomization (MR) using cis-acting protein quantitative trait loci (pQTLs) identifies circulating proteins whose lifelong modulation alters stroke risk.

Methods

We screened 589 conditionally independent cis-pQTLs from the INTERVAL study against four GIGASTROKE outcomes: any ischemic stroke (AIS), large-artery atherosclerosis (LAA), cardioembolic stroke (CES), and SVD. Wald ratio estimates were corrected by Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) within each outcome, with a pooled cross-outcome correction as a sensitivity analysis. FDR-significant associations underwent colocalization (approximate Bayes factor; H4 > 0.80), replication in the independent deCODE pQTL cohort, cell-type expression validation in a human brain vascular single-nucleus atlas (65,479 nuclei), and phenome-wide safety screening.

Results

Ten protein-outcome associations reached FDR < 0.05; nine replicated in deCODE and eight colocalized at H4 > 0.80, with two further pairs (ABO-LAA, cyclin H-CES) in the suggestive range (H4 0.70-0.80). For SVD, higher SPATA20 raised risk (OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.24-1.73, p = 5.3 × 10⁻⁶), and higher KDELC2 lowered risk (OR 0.82, 95% CI 0.74-0.91, p = 2.2 × 10⁻⁴). A protective cyclin H signal for CES passed outcome-wise FDR (q = 0.046) but not the pooled correction (q = 0.059) and is reported as preliminary. ABO, MMP-12, and SWAP70 confirmed earlier reports; SCARA5 failed colocalization and replication and was excluded. Colocalization confirmed the lead liabilities for MMP-12 (atopic dermatitis, two cohorts) and SWAP70 (rheumatoid arthritis) as on-target effects; two further liability associations (allergic asthma, ER-negative breast cancer) did not meet the colocalization threshold and remain hypothesis-generating.

Conclusions

Proteome-wide MR prioritizes two SVD-associated proteins: SPATA20 (risk-raising; now independently confirmed across screens) and KDELC2 (protective; newly reported). Both require replication on orthogonal proteomic platforms and functional validation before therapeutic development.

title: Impact of hypothermia level on neurological and renal outcomes in emergency aortic surgery: a single-centre experience.
authorString: Chan JTN, Fazmin IT, Vokshi I, de Silva R, Farid S.
abstractText: BackgroundTemperature management during emergency surgery for acute aortic syndrome is critical for neurological, renal, and systemic protection. Recent European Association for Cardio-Thoracic Surgery (EACTS) guidelines recommend moderate hypothermia with antegrade cerebral perfusion for hemiarch procedures. Nevertheless, deep hypothermic circulatory arrest (DHCA) remains common. This study evaluates neurological and other postoperative outcomes across different intraoperative temperature ranges.MethodsA single-centre retrospective study of consecutive patients undergoing surgery for acute aortic syndrome between 2018-2023. Demographic, intraoperative, and postoperative data on mortality, hospitalization, neurological, renal outcomes, and blood product usage were collected. Patients were stratified by intraoperative temperature: deep (≤20°C), low-moderate (20.1-24°C), high-moderate (24.1-28°C), and mild (>28°C) hypothermia. Logistic regression identified predictors of binary adverse outcomes. A sensitivity analysis was conducted using 24.0°C as the threshold in hemiarch surgery patients.ResultsA total of 175 patients (median age 64 years; 37% female) were included; of whom 89% underwent hemiarch replacement. Cardiopulmonary bypass duration decreased progressively with warmer intraoperative temperatures, ranging from 270.5 minutes in deep hypothermia to 164 minutes in mild hypothermia. The 30-day mortality was 18.9% (n = 33/175), and the overall stroke rate was 19.4% (n = 34/175). Among patients undergoing hemiarch repair, warmer temperatures were associated with lower stroke incidence (mild hypothermia 11%) compared with high-moderate (8.8%), low-moderate (26%), and deep hypothermia (27%) (p = 0.049), and with shorter intensive care admission (p = 0.036). However, multivariate regression showed that the four-category comparison did not reach significance for the assessed outcomes once adjusted for confounding variables. A sensitivity analysis at 24.0°C showed an independent association with reduced stroke risk (OR 0.23, 95% CI 0.08-0.64, p = 0.005).DiscussionOur findings support current EACTS recommendations favouring moderate-to-mild hypothermia for hemiarch replacement, with potential protective effects. Further studies should determine the optimal temperature strategy for patients undergoing total arch replacement.

title: A Descriptive Case Series of Pericarditis Treatment After Trauma With Colchicine Monotherapy Versus Other Treatment.
authorString: Bollinger CJ, Shuder CJ, Philpott CD, Frasier L, Droege CA, Droege ME.
abstractText: Limited data exist describing the optimal treatment of pericarditis after acute blunt or penetrating trauma. Treatment with high-dose nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAID), colchicine, or corticosteroids may not be feasible due to concomitant injuries. This was a retrospective, single-center, descriptive case series at a large, academic, Level 1 Trauma Center over a 10-year period. Patients admitted to the trauma service with a diagnosis of pericarditis at any point during index admission were eligible for inclusion. Groups were defined as colchicine-based treatment (monotherapy or combination) and any therapy besides colchicine, including no medications (surgical). The primary endpoint was therapy escalation defined as treatment modification, chart note documenting therapy failure, rehospitalization, repeat pericardial surgical intervention, or documentation of recurrent pericarditis. Secondary outcomes were treatment intolerance documented in a chart note including gastrointestinal bleed (GIB) and acute kidney injury (AKI). Eleven patients with traumatic pericarditis were included. Four (36%) patients received colchicine-based therapy: monotherapy (2, [50%]) or combination with NSAID (2, [50%]). Seven (63%) patients received non-colchicine treatment: 2 (29%) NSAID alone; 5 (71%) surgical management without medication. There were no occurrences of therapy escalation in either group. Treatment intolerances occurred in 1 (25%; AKI) patient in the colchicine group and 3 (43%; AKI, 2 [29%], GIB, 1 [14%]) patients in the non-colchicine group. Pericarditis is a rare complication after trauma, and no patients in this case series demonstrated treatment escalation. Additional, larger sample studies are necessary to guide optimal treatment in this uncommon but important population.

title: Individual-ecological triangulation of risk factors for peripheral artery disease: concordant evidence for smoking and diabetes, discordant evidence for kidney disease
authorString: Zhang Y, Shi J, Wu R, Zhao F.
abstractText:
Background

Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is studied either through individual-level cohorts or national mortality statistics; the two evidence streams carry different biases and have not been formally compared within one design.

Methods

We triangulated two pre-specified streams. Individually, we analyzed 3,268 NHANES 1999-2004 participants aged 40 years and older with ankle-brachial index measurements (235 with PAD) linked to mortality through 2019, using survey-weighted logistic and Cox models, a Fine-Gray model, and attributable fractions. Ecologically, we used national Multiple Cause of Death records for 1999-2024 (390,174 PAD deaths) to estimate five-year-band trends in the share of PAD deaths mentioning tobacco (F17.0-F17.9), diabetes (E00-E89), or renal failure (N17-N19). Per a pre-specified protocol, we compared directions of association, each bridge quantified by a bootstrap direction-agreement probability.

Results

Weighted PAD prevalence was 5.05% (95% CI, 4.18 to 5.92). PAD was associated with cardiovascular death (hazard ratio, 2.65; 95% CI, 1.87 to 3.76). Smoking showed the strongest PAD association (odds ratio, 3.37) and the steepest rise in its mortality share (2.20% to 18.50%; direction-agreement probability, 1.000). Diabetes was associated with PAD (1.68) and rose after a 2014 trough (7.35% to 10.92%; probability, 1.000). Renal failure was associated with PAD (1.78) but its mortality share was flat for 26 years (14.55% to 14.49%; probability, 0.445).

Conclusions

The two streams agreed in direction for smoking and diabetes and diverged for kidney disease, reflecting different estimands. Smoking and diabetes are the factors supported by both streams for population-level PAD prevention.

title: Butein Attenuates Cardiac Hypertrophy by Restoring Redox-Mitochondrial Homeostasis Through Nrf2-Sirt3 Signaling.
authorString: Tungalag T, Yang DK.
abstractText: Butein (3,4,2',4'-tetrahydroxychalcone) is a bioactive chalcone with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and cytoprotective properties. However, its effects on pathological cardiac hypertrophy and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, neonatal rat ventricular cardiomyocytes stimulated with phenylephrine and mouse models of transverse aortic constriction (TAC) at 2 and 8 weeks were used to investigate the protective effects of butein in vitro and in vivo. Butein markedly reduced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, decreased intracellular and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential, and restored mitochondrial bioenergetic status. Mechanistically, butein enhanced nuclear accumulation of Nrf2, restored antioxidant gene expression, and reactivated AMPK-Sirt3-FoxO3a signaling while reversing SOD2 hyperacetylation. In vivo, butein suppressed cardiac hypertrophy during the early compensated stage (2week TAC) and alleviated cardiac remodeling, fibrosis, and functional deterioration during the advanced pathological stage (8-week TAC). Notably, genetic silencing of Nrf2 or Sirt3 and pharmacological inhibition of Nrf2 attenuated the protective effects of butein, supporting the involvement of Nrf2-Sirt3 signaling both in vitro and in vivo. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that butein mitigates pathological cardiac hypertrophy by restoring redox and mitochondrial homeostasis through coordinated Nrf2-Sirt3 signaling.

title: Co-Designing a Digital Platform for the Management of Modifiable Risk Factors and Comorbidities in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation: Mixed Methods Usability Study.
authorString: Klavebäck S, Braunschweig F, Lidin M, Svennberg E.
abstractText: Clinical guidelines recommend integrated, person-centered care with control of modifiable risk factors and coexisting conditions in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF), but many receive insufficient risk factor management. Digital health technologies may provide valuable support in addressing this gap. Our aim was to evaluate the usability of a co-designed digital platform for supporting person-centered management of modifiable risk factors in individuals with AF. This mixed methods usability study was conducted at a tertiary university hospital in Sweden between March and April 2025. Eligible participants with AF were recruited to evaluate the co-designed digital platform using the System Usability Scale (SUS) and semistructured interviews analyzed with inductive manifest content analysis. A total of 22 patients were included (mean age 67.7, SD 7.6 y); 32% (7/22) were female, the mean BMI was 27.7 (SD 3.6) kg/m2, 65% (14/22) had paroxysmal AF, 36% (8/22) had persistent AF, and the median AF duration was 26 (IQR 13.3-72.8) months. Relevant comorbidities were hypertension (17/22, 77%), heart failure (8/22, 36%), diabetes mellitus type 2 (3/22, 14%), and ischemic heart disease (4/22, 18%). Usability was rated high, with a median SUS score of 78.8 (IQR 63.8-86.9), indicating above-average user acceptance. Participants' requirements were summarized into 4 main categories and 10 subcategories. First, they valued a clear layout, simple design, and easy navigation. Second, they appreciated positive content, which is informative, inclusive, and motivating. Third, they requested personalized information on different aspects and provided on different levels. Fourth, they desired individualized medical recommendations that are personalized and flexible but open to individual choice. Participants found the usability acceptable and valued specifically a clear layout, positive content, personalized information, and individualized medical recommendations.

title: Beyond LDL-C: A Case-Based Review of Complex Dyslipidemia.
authorString: Fanaropoulou NM, Varghese RT.

journal.title: The American journal of the medical sciences

abstractText: Dyslipidemia is clinically heterogeneous, and LDL-C alone may not fully capture atherogenic particle burden, metabolic risk, treatment response, or inherited disease. This case-based review presents three dyslipidemia phenotypes that illustrate common diagnostic and management challenges. The first case describes diet-sensitive LDL particle and lipoprotein insulin resistance changes despite LDL-C values near conventional targets in a patient with subclinical coronary atherosclerosis. The second highlights persistent low HDL-C and HDL particle number despite substantial LDL-C reduction with non-statin and incretin-era therapies in the setting of obesity and strong family history. The third demonstrates genetically confirmed familial hypercholesterolemia due to a pathogenic LDLR variant despite absent classic physical stigmata. Together, these cases support a phenotype-driven approach that integrates LDL-C, ApoB or LDL particle number, diet response, metabolic context, imaging, medication tolerance, and selective genetic testing to individualize dyslipidemia risk assessment and treatment.

title: When Swallowing Triggers VT.
authorString: Breslin L, Zipse M, Garg L, Grubb A, Padalia K, Adewumi J, Tumolo A, Rosenberg M, Tzou W, Sandhu A.
abstractText: We describe a case of swallowing-induced ventricular tachycardia in a young, otherwise healthy male with a structurally normal heart which was refractory to multiple anti-arrhythmic medication and was successfully treated with ablation of a cardiac ganglion in the crux of the heart. We use this case to describe an unusual disease presentation and highlight current evidence related to evaluation and management of ventricular arrhythmias and add to the limited body of evidence related to swallowing induced tachycardia.

title: Mapping cellular senescence in heart failure: knowledge evolution, mechanistic modules, and senotherapeutic opportunities.
authorString: Meng L, Liao X, Wu Z, Hu Z.
