abstractText: Cellular senescence is increasingly recognized as a mechanistic link between cardiovascular ageing, inflammatory-fibrotic remodelling, and heart failure (HF) progression. However, the knowledge structure, thematic evolution, and translational frontiers of senescence research in HF remain incompletely mapped. This study mapped the global research landscape of cellular senescence in HF from 2005 to 2025 by integrating dual-database bibliometric analysis with BERTopic-based semantic topic modelling. English-language articles and reviews were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus. After field verification, standardization, and deduplication, 479 publications were included. VOSviewer, CiteSpace, SCImago Graphica, Pajek, Python, and Microsoft Excel were used for bibliometric and visualization analyses. PubMedBERT-based embeddings and BERTopic were applied to identify latent semantic themes from titles, abstracts, and keywords. Publications increased rapidly after 2020, with 336 papers published between 2020 and 2025, accounting for 70.1% of the corpus. China and the United States were the leading contributors, with the United States showing higher collaboration strength and accumulated citation counts within the analysed dataset. Co-citation analysis identified foundational studies in senescence biology, senolytics, cardiovascular ageing, and HF remodelling. Keyword evolution showed a shift from oxidative stress, cardiac stem/progenitor cell senescence, and vascular cell senescence toward inflammation, metabolic remodelling, biomarkers, HF phenotypes, and senotherapeutics. BERTopic identified 17 substantive topics, with Cardiac and Cardiovascular Aging as the largest theme, followed by Cardiac Fibrosis and Fibroblast Activation, SASP-related Cardiovascular Senescence, Cardiac Regeneration, and Doxorubicin Cardiotoxicity. Bibliometric and semantic analyses indicate growing research interest in cell-type-specific senescence, inflammatory-fibrotic remodelling, HF phenotype heterogeneity, biomarkers, and senotherapeutics. These findings highlight opportunities for integrating mechanistic research with clinical investigation. Future studies should prioritize cell-specific senescence atlases, multidimensional biomarkers, comorbidity-aware HF stratification, and cautious evaluation of senotherapeutics in HF subgroups with evidence of senescence-associated pathology.

title: MRPL40 Regulates Cardiac Outflow Tract Septation by Modulating Neural Crest Cell Migration via CREB-MSX1 Signaling.
authorString: Ji C, Zhao W, Zhan X, Yang Z.
abstractText: 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22q11.2DS) causes multi-system disorders, among which congenital heart defects are predominant, typically manifesting as conotruncal anomalies. Within the deleted 22q11.2 region, several genes have been identified as critical regulators of heart development; however, the functions of most genes in this interval remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated Mrpl40, which encodes the mitochondrial ribosomal protein L40 (MRPL40), to determine its function in cardiac morphogenesis. Deletion of Mrpl40 in neural crest cells (NCCs) resulted in conotruncal defects. Specifically, Mrpl40 deficiency impaired NCC migration, leading to delayed outflow tract (OFT) septation and aberrant rotation. Mechanistically, we found that Mrpl40 loss disrupted CREB phosphorylation, resulting in reduced expression of Msx1, a crucial regulator of NCC migration and differentiation. Collectively, this study demonstrates the pivotal function of mitochondria in NCC behavior and defines the essential role of Mrpl40 in OFT development, and provides new insights to understand the etiology of 22q11.2DS.

title: Interventricular septal LGE predicts response trajectories and clinical prognosis in heart failure patients undergoing left bundle branch area pacing.
authorString: Zhu K, Zhou D, Zeng J, Li X, Zhu H, Chen J, Lai Z, Zou J, Lu M, Fan X.
abstractText:
Background

Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is an alternative strategy for heart failure (HF) patients with left bundle branch block (LBBB). Interventricular septal (IVS) fibrosis is linked to LBBAP efficacy.

Objective

To investigate the association between IVS late gadolinium enhancement percentage (IVS LGE%) and LBBAP response in non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) patients with LBBB.

Methods

This was a two-center prospective observational study. Patients with NICM and complete LBBB were consecutively enrolled and received LBBAP from January 2021 to December 2024. Patients were divided into early, delayed, and non-response groups based on absolute left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) improvement ≥5% at 6 and 12 months.

Results

A total of 113 patients were included, with 86 (76.1%) early responders, 13 (11.5%) delayed responders, and 14 (12.4%) non-responders. IVS LGE% linearly increased the risk of non-early response, with each 1% increase conferring a 14% higher risk of adverse response progression (early to delayed or non-response) (adjusted OR=1.14, 95%CI 1.05-1.23; P=0.002). 75.3% of IVS fibrosis-related 6-month impairment was mediated by failed LBB captured (direct effect P=0.204), while the direct inhibitory effect of IVS fibrosis emerged at 12 months (mediation proportion 60.8%, β=-0.33, P=0.005). Optimal IVS LGE% cut-off values were 7.62% for early response and 12.33% for delayed response, with 12-month response rates of 95.06%, 93.75% and 43.75% across low, intermediate and high IVS LGE% groups, respectively.

Conclusion

IVS fibrosis independently predicts LBBAP response and prognosis in NICM patients with complete LBBB, and modulates LBBAP efficacy through a time-dependent biphasic mechanism.

title: Association of Left Atrial Intramyocardial Fat Infiltration With Atrial Arrhythmia Recurrence After Pulsed-Field Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
authorString: Fukushima T, Yanagisawa S, Miyazawa H, Tanaka Y, Kitahara T, Hiramatsu S, Hiramatsu T, Adachi K, Teraoka T, Ota R, Shimojo M, Tsuji Y, Inden Y, Murohara T.
abstractText:
Background

Computed tomography (CT)-derived left atrial intramyocardial fat infiltration (inFAT) is an emerging imaging phenotype of the atrial substrate in atrial fibrillation (AF).

Objective

This study aimed to evaluate inFAT and peri-left atrial epicardial adipose tissue (LA-EAT) using artificial intelligence-based CT analysis software (ADAS 3D) and to assess their association with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after persistent AF ablation.

Methods

This retrospective single-center study included 59 patients who underwent pulsed-field ablation for persistent AF. inFAT and LA-EAT were quantified using a semi-automated algorithm. Cox regression analysis was performed to evaluate the association of inFAT and LA-EAT with recurrence. Kaplan-Meier analysis was performed after stratification according to the tertile of each parameter.

Results

During a median follow-up period of 11.2 [6.4-11.9] months, atrial arrhythmia recurrence occurred in 21 (36%) patients. The inFAT volume was significantly greater in patients with recurrence than those without (1.25 [0.78-1.53] vs. 0.72 [0.45-1.09] cm3, p=0.021). In contrast, LA-EAT volume was comparable between the groups (21.8 [13.7-30.4] vs. 17.5 [14.1-26.8] cm3, p=0.419). In Cox regression analysis, higher inFAT was significantly associated with recurrence, whereas LA-EAT was not significantly associated (inFAT: hazard ratio [HR], 1.93; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.13-3.27; p=0.015; LA-EAT: HR, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.99-1.06; p=0.227). The significant association between inFAT and recurrence remained consistent after adjustment for body mass index.

Conclusions

Greater inFAT volume was associated with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after pulsed-field ablation for persistent AF, suggesting that inFAT may represent a candidate imaging marker of recurrence risk.

title: Sex-based differences in bi-atrial voltage in atrial fibrillation: a multimodal and digital twin approach to distinguish physiological variation from pathological remodelling.
authorString: Bodagh N, Vigneswaran V, Gharaviri A, Kotadia I, Klis M, Mannakkara NN, Maciunas K, Von Kietzell A, Bell M, Cuthbert H, Wright M, Whitaker J, Rinaldi CA, Shetty A, Adhya S, Dhillon G, Jogiya R, Buckley U, Jones D, Chen Z, Chiribiri A, Grubb NR, Lang C, Pancinha C, Williams MC, Niederer S, Haldar S, O'Neill M, Williams SE.
abstractText:
Background

Sex-based differences in atrial voltage have been reported in atrial fibrillation (AF), but it is unclear whether these differences reflect pathological remodelling or physiological variation.

Objective

To assess sex-based differences in voltage, contextualised by complementary measures of substrate remodelling and AF mechanisms.

Methods

A multicentre, prospective study was conducted in patients scheduled for AF ablation. Bi-atrial voltage mapping was combined with electrophysiological assessment, structural and functional assessment using cardiac MRI, and mechanistic interrogation using patient-specific digital twins. Propensity score matching was used to account for baseline differences between sexes. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analysis was conducted to estimate sex-specific mean left atrial voltage cutoffs based on 12-month arrhythmia recurrence status.

Results

Seventy patients (62±12 years; 31% female) were included. Women demonstrated lower mean bipolar voltages than men, with this difference persisting after 1:1 propensity score matching (n=44) in both left (1.66±0.71mV versus 2.12±0.55mV, p=0.028) and right atria (1.79±0.49mV versus 2.20±0.59mV, p=0.025). Propensity score-matched analyses revealed no significant differences in other structural, functional, or electrophysiological parameters, with digital twin analyses demonstrating no significant differences in AF termination, phase singularity count, wave dynamics, or response to virtual ablation. Women had lower mean left atrial voltage cutoffs calibrated to 12-month arrhythmia recurrence status than men (1.74mV versus 2.26mV).

Conclusions

Women with AF exhibit lower bi-atrial voltages despite comparable substrate characteristics and AF mechanisms, suggesting that observed voltage differences may reflect physiological variation rather than pathological remodelling. Sex-specific voltage thresholds may improve the accuracy of substrate assessment and facilitate personalised treatment.

title: Pulmonary vein narrowing after voltage-guided adjunctive pulmonary vein sleeve pulsed field ablation.
authorString: Sasaki T, Masuyama T, Minami K, Yoshimura S, Nishiuchi S, Kodama A, Hattori K, Kaseno K, Funabashi N, Naito S, Nakamura K.
abstractText:
Background

Pulsed field ablation (PFA) for pulmonary vein (PV) isolation (PVI) has been associated with a low risk of PV stenosis when performed using the standard ostial workflow. However, the risk of PV narrowing after adjunctive PV sleeve PFA remains insufficiently evaluated.

Objective

To assess PV narrowing after voltage-guided adjunctive PV sleeve PFA.

Methods

We retrospectively studied 147 patients who underwent an initial pentaspline PFA-based PVI for atrial fibrillation. In addition to standard ostial PVI, voltage-guided PFA applications were delivered to target PV sleeve potentials identified on pre-ablation voltage mapping. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography was performed before and approximately six months after ablation. PV cross-sectional areas (PVAs) were measured at predefined levels, and the maximum PVA reduction rate was defined as ΔPVA. Significant PV narrowing was defined as ΔPVA ≥25%.

Results

Post-ablation PVA was significantly smaller than pre-ablation PVA at all PV sites. The median ΔPVA was 5.4%, 6.4%, 4.6%, and 4.0% in the left superior, left inferior, right superior, and right inferior PVs, respectively, and differed significantly among the four PV sites (P = 0.012). No significant PV narrowing was observed in this cohort.

Conclusions

In patients undergoing an initial PFA-based PVI, no significant PV narrowing was observed approximately six months after voltage-guided adjunctive PV sleeve PFA using a pentaspline catheter. Further controlled studies with larger populations and longer follow-up are needed to better characterize the safety and clinical utility of this strategy.

title: Ten-year Performance of the Multi-Layer Insulated Defibrillation Lead in the Medicare Population.
authorString: Schaller RD, Haqqani H, Birgersdotter-Green U, Callahan T, Jan A, Li W, Nabutovsky Y, Charan V, Desmond M, Leclercq C.
abstractText:
Background

Long-term surveillance of implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) leads is essential because clinically important mechanical failures may emerge years after implantation.

Objective

To evaluate 10-year mechanical complication-free survival of the Optisure ICD lead (Abbott, Sylmar, CA) in a large real-world Medicare population.

Methods

Manufacturer device-tracking records were linked to Medicare Fee-for-Service claims and device complaint data using the EP PASSION framework. Patients receiving an Optisure lead from February 2014 through December 2024 were included. Mechanical lead-related complications were defined by claims containing both a diagnosis of mechanical lead malfunction and a lead-related surgical intervention more than 30 days after implantation. Kaplan-Meier survival was estimated under a best-case scenario including confirmed Optisure-related events and a worst-case scenario also including potentially related events.

Results

The cohort included 26,830 patients with 27,033 Optisure leads. Mean age was 73.8 ± 8.6 years, 28.4% were women, and 49.8% had cardiac resynchronization therapy ICDs. Overall, 379 complications were classified as confirmed lead-related and 606 as confirmed or potentially lead-related. At 10 years, complication-free lead survival was 97.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], 96.7%-97.7%) in the best-case scenario and 95.6% (95% CI, 94.9%-96.2%) in the worst-case scenario. Survival did not differ significantly by age, lead length, coil configuration, or device type.

Conclusion

The Optisure ICD lead demonstrated favorable mechanical performance through 10 years in routine clinical practice. These findings support both the long-term durability of Optisure and the use of integrated real-world data for post-market device surveillance.

title: Epicardial Closure for Peridevice Leaks from Endocardial Left Atrial Appendage Closure - Early LARIAT-4-PDL Registry Results.
authorString: Katapadi A, Evonich R, Garg J, Mi J, Kabra R, Park P, Koerber S, Horton R, Dukkipati S, Turagam M, Gopinathannair R, Sievert H, Nair D, Lee RJ, DiBiase L, Kar S, Natale A, Reddy V, Lakkireddy D.
abstractText:
Background

Closure of clinically significant peri-device leaks (PDLs) after left atrial appendage (LAA) occlusion remains crucial to prevent thromboembolism. A variety of techniques exist to close PDLs, each with its own advantages and disadvantages. The LARIAT (Atricure, Mason, OH) suture device may provide an alternative for closing PDLs.

Objective

We report the initial feasibility of LARIAT for endocardial LAA closure PDLs.

Methods

In a multicenter, retrospective study, we reviewed consecutive patients who underwent LARIAT for closure of device-related LAA leaks. All patients had PDLs ≥3 mm after either a Watchman FLX Pro (Boston Scientific, Marlborough, MA) or an Amplatzer Amulet (Abbott, Chicago, IL) endocardial LAA occluder, as seen on postoperative imaging. Acute PDL closure - pericardial access with device deployment and elimination of the PDL on intraprocedural imaging - was evaluated with either transesophageal or intracardiac echocardiogram, along with 45-day safety.

Results

We report 10 cases in patients aged 67.2±10.7years, 30.0% female, and with a body mass index 32.4±6.4 kg/m2. Baseline comorbidities included a CHADSVASC of 4.4±0.7 and HASBLED of 3.7±0.7. Initially, patients underwent Watchman (80.0%) or Amulet (20.0%) with an average PDL of 5.4±0.8 mm. Few cases had attempted PDL closure with radiofrequency ablation (10.0%), coiling (20.0%), or a previous device (10.0%). After procedural and fluoroscopy times of 48.7±10.8 min and 7.0±3.7 min, respectively, LARIAT PDL closure was successful in all cases, and no difference when stratified by initial endocardial LAA closure type.

Conclusion

These initial results suggest that a LARIAT may be an alternative strategy in patients with clinically significant PDLs after endocardial LAA closure. Future studies are needed to corroborate our initial findings and long-term closure results.

title: Deciphering traditional Mongolian medicine Sugemule-3 decoction: Chemical profiling and therapeutic effect evaluation against myocardial fibrosis.
authorString: Huang D, Wan H, Lu Y, Yang J, Li C, Wan H.
abstractText: Sugemule-3 Decoction (SD3) is developed from 'Four Continuations of Medicine', one of the traditional Mongolian medical classics compiled in the late 8th century. SD3 consists of Baidoukou (Amomum kravanh Pierre ex Gagnep.), Xianghanqin (Cuminum cyminum L.) and Biba (Piper longum L.). It has been demonstrated with significant therapeutic efficacy against cardiovascular diseases in clinic, while its underlying chemical profiles and pharmacological mechanisms remain unclear. The purpose of this study is to investigate how SD3 counteracts Isoproterenol (ISO)-induced myocardial fibrosis via gut microbiota and metabolites. SD3 components were analyzed by LC-MS and GC-MS. In ISO-induced MF mice, SD3 (14-day oral gavage) improved cardiac function and fibrosis, remodeled gut microbiota and metabolites, and regulated GPR43/NF-κB signaling, as confirmed by exogenous SCFAs. In this study, 79 hydrophilic and 85 hydrophobic compounds were identified in SD3 using HPLC-Q-Exactive MS and GC/Q-TOF MS. SD3 improved cardiac function, reduced cardiac fibrosis and intestinal injury in mice with MF, and downregulated α-SMA and collagen I expression. It also decreased the Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio and pathogenic bacteria abundance, restored SCFAs and BAs, and reduced 3-hydroxybutyrate (3-HB). Mechanistically, SD3 activated GPR43 and suppressed the NF-κB/IL-6 axis. Exogenous acetate, propionate, and valerate alleviated MF, whereas 3-HB exacerbated it. This study presents deciphered traditional Mongolian medicine SD3 from both chemical profile and pharmacological effect against MF. Additionally, it highlights the potential significance of restoring gut homeostasis in managing long-term cardiac diseases as MF.

title: Mitral Annular Calcification: Operative Decision Making and Technical Considerations.
authorString: Kreso A, Bihun R, Melnitchouk S.
abstractText: Mitral annular calcification (MAC) presents a formidable challenge in mitral valve surgery owing to risks of atrioventricular groove disruption, circumflex artery injury, and paravalvular leaks. The optimal operative strategy varies according to the severity of annular calcification, extent of ventricular extension, and the patient-specific risk profile. A narrative expert review was performed synthesizing contemporary surgical series, imaging-guided approaches, and transcatheter strategies for mitral valve intervention in the setting of MAC. Technical considerations, complication avoidance strategies, and decision-making frameworks were integrated into a new severity-based operative algorithm. We developed a decision matrix to stratify patients into four categories to guide preoperative planning and operative decisions. MAC management lies on a spectrum between working around the MAC with no resection ("respect" the MAC) to complete MAC resection with atrioventricular groove reconstruction ("resect" the MAC). Severe or circumferential MAC demands tailored strategies, including transcatheter or hybrid approaches. In patients with mild MAC, mitral valve repair remains feasible and preferred. Moderate MAC requires individualized decision-making; repair is achievable when leaflet mobility is preserved, and decalcification permits secure annuloplasty. Replacement is favored when leaflet restriction or annular rigidity precludes durable reconstruction. The extent of decalcification should be tailored to the patient's risk profile and surgical expertise to ensure durable results. Mitral valve intervention in the setting of MAC requires an individualized approach. We propose a practical management algorithm, stratified by patient risk and anatomic feasibility.

title: Infant Feeding Practices Are Associated with Cardiovascular Profiles in Early Childhood: Findings from a Prospective Australian Cohort Study.
authorString: Ghobadi S, Hesketh KD, Abbott G, Heitmann B, Vuillermin P, Burgner D, Mansell T, O'Hely M, Saffery R, Tang MLK, Zheng M.

journal.title: Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics

abstractText: Breastfeeding is associated with reduced risk of childhood obesity, but associations with cardiovascular risks in childhood are less well understood. This study investigated associations between infant feeding practices and cardiovascular profiles in early childhood and the potential mediating role of infant rapid weight gain (RWG). This secondary data analysis was conducted using data from the Barwon Infant Study, an ongoing prospective pre-birth cohort in Australia commenced between 2010 and 2017, recruited through an unselected antenatal sampling frame. Children aged 4 years (n=606) who participated in the 4-year cardiovascular risk assessment follow-up. Infant feeding variables, including breastfeeding duration, exclusive breastfeeding at 3 months, and predominant breastfeeding at 6 months, were collected via caregiver questionnaires at 1, 3, 6, 9, and 12 months, and 2 years post-birth. Latent profile analysis, including 4-7 cardiovascular risk markers measured at age 4 years, was used to derive cardiovascular profiles. Multivariable logistic regression with adjustment for gestational age, maternal education, and pre-pregnancy maternal body mass index (BMI), examined the association between infant feeding practices and cardiovascular profiles, and whether these associations were mediated by RWG in infancy. Three cardiovascular profiles of 'Low' (44.1% of children), 'Medium' (46.4%), and 'High' (9.5%) were identified at age 4 years. Infants who were exclusively breastfed at age 3 months and predominantly breastfed at age 6 months were less likely to belong to the 'Medium' versus 'Low' cardiovascular profile (RRR 0.51, 95% CI 0.27 to 0.95, p= 0.034; and RRR 0.43, 95% CI 0.18 to 0.99, p= 0.048, respectively) than those who were not. No significant association was observed for the 'High' versus 'Low' cardiovascular profile or between breastfeeding duration and cardiovascular profiles. Mediation analyses suggested indirect associations between infant feeding practices and cardiovascular profiles involving infant RWG. Exclusive breastfeeding to age 3 months and predominant breastfeeding to age 6 months were linked with a more favorable cardiovascular profile at age 4 years. Mediation analyses suggested that infant RWG may partly account for these associations. Further studies are needed to investigate the mechanisms that may underlie the observed associations between breastfeeding practices and cardiovascular profiles.

title: Arrhythmias detected by implanted cardiac rhythm recorders in transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis.
authorString: Aguilera-Agudo C, Peiró-Aventín B, de Castro D, Castro-Urda V, Toquero-Ramos J, Jaén EG, Jiménez-Sánchez D, Veloza-Urrea D, Lozano-Jiménez S, Domínguez F, Fernández-Lozano I, García-Pavía P, Gonzalez-Lopez E.
abstractText: Arrhythmias are a common complication of transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM). We sought to characterize the prevalence, risk factors, and prognosis of arrhythmias in ATTR-CM using implantable loop recorders (ILRs). ILRs were implanted in 49 patients with ATTR-CM (84% male; median age, 73.2 [66.2-78.8] years; 71% wild-type, 51% with known atrial fibrillation [AF]). Factors associated with the development of AF or pacemaker implantation were analyzed, and clinical outcomes were compared with those of a contemporary cohort of patients with 125 ATTR-CM without an ILR. During a median follow-up of 37.2 [26.6-41.1] months, an advanced conduction disorder (ACD) prompting pacemaker implantation was detected in 16 individuals (33%) and new-onset AF was detected in 17 patients (71% of those without previous AF). Patients with new-onset AF more frequently had wild-type ATTR-CM. Those who needed pacemaker implantation were older and had a higher prevalence of hypertension and right bundle branch block, and a longer PR interval. Compared with patients without an ILR, early detection of arrhythmias by ILR was not associated with a prognostic benefit in terms of survival (P = .57), reduction of syncope (P = 1), heart failure admissions (P = .34), or embolic events (P = .999). Although a higher incidence of arrhythmias was identified through ILR monitoring in patients with ATTR-CM, no significant benefits were observed in terms of survival or other hard clinical endpoints. Significant differences were identified in patients who developed new-onset AF and ACD. These differences should be considered during the clinical follow-up of this population.

title: Engineered mitochondria-derived vesicles suppress colorectal cancer through metabolic reprogramming and mtDNA-cGAS-STING signaling.
authorString: Zhang Z, Yan Z, Huang S, Yang X, Wang Q, Huang J, Wang H, Du Y, Qi T, Hu L, Ouyang X, Wang X, Dai Z.
abstractText: Metabolic reprogramming and innate immune signaling are closely involved in colorectal cancer (CRC) progression, but the effects of extracellular mitochondria-derived vesicles (MDVs) on these processes remain unclear, partly because of their low natural yield. In this study, we overexpressed MDV formation-related genes in mesenchymal stem cells and identified OPA1 and PINK1 as regulators that increased the recovery of extracellular MDVs. The resulting OPA1- and PINK1-MDV preparations were characterized and then incubated with LOVO and SW480 CRC cells to assess their uptake, metabolic effects, inflammatory signaling, and antitumor activities. OPA1-MDVs contained a TOMM20-positive/PDHE1α-positive vesicle population and shifted CRC cell metabolism away from glycolysis toward oxidative phosphorylation, as shown by reduced glycolytic enzyme activity and lactate production, together with increased oxygen consumption, respiratory-chain activity, and mitochondrial membrane potential. These changes were accompanied by reduced reactive oxygen species levels and impaired CRC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. In contrast, PINK1-MDVs impaired mitochondrial function, increased reactive oxygen species production, and were associated with activation of cGAS-STING-related inflammatory signaling, possibly through the delivery of mitochondrial DNA. Both MDV preparations suppressed tumor growth in an immunocompetent syngeneic MC38 tumor model. These findings suggest that MDVs derived from OPA1- or PINK1-overexpressing cells suppress CRC growth through distinct metabolic and innate immune mechanisms and provide a potential strategy for engineering extracellular mitochondrial vesicles for cancer research.

title: Differential Peri-Strut Vascular Healing After Stent Deployment in Swine Subclavian and Carotid Arteries.
authorString: Isobe A, Nishio K, Mohseni N, Shimabukuro J, Lam C, Leet C, Appleberry M, Relat RMB, Callahan R.

journal.title: Cardiovascular pathology : the official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology

abstractText: Vascular healing after stent implantation is influenced by local biomechanical and anatomical environments. Swine carotid and subclavian arteries are commonly used in preclinical vascular device studies; however, regional differences in peri-strut healing responses between these vascular territories remain incompletely defined. This study compared histopathological vascular healing after stent implantation in swine carotid and subclavian arteries. Self-expanding stents were implanted in both carotid and subclavian arteries in the same domestic swine according to the instructions for use. Animals survived for either 3 or 28 days before necropsy (n=6/time point). Stented vessels were perfusion-fixed, embedded in plastic, and stained with hematoxylin and eosin and Movat's pentachrome stain. Histopathological evaluation included injury, inflammation, fibrin, thrombus, endothelialization, neointimal maturity, fibrosis, and hemorrhage. Histomorphometry included percent stenosis, neointimal thickness, and area. Stent-to-artery ratios were comparable between carotid and subclavian arteries. At 28 days, subclavian arteries demonstrated significantly greater persistent peri-strut fibrin deposition and intramural hemorrhage than carotid arteries (fibrin: 1.67 ± 0.72 vs. 0.03 ± 0.18, p<0.05; hemorrhage: 1.53 ± 1.06 vs. 0.03 ± 0.18, p<0.05). Percent area stenosis was also greater in subclavian arteries (28.77 ± 18.35% vs. 14.94 ± 5.25%, p<0.05). No significant regional differences were observed at 3 days. Subclavian arteries demonstrated peri-strut delayed vascular healing characterized by persistent fibrin deposition, hemorrhage, and increased neointimal formation compared with carotid arteries despite similar stent deployment conditions. Mechanical stress associated with forelimb movement may contribute to delayed healing and subsequent neointimal formation in the subclavian artery.

title: Escalation of Resting Heart Rate and Tachycardia as a Response to Thoracic Radiotherapy: Implications for Cardiovascular Outcomes after Radiotherapy.
authorString: Ajdari A, Bobic M, Ciausu C, Cooper AJ, Guthier C, Bortfeld T, Owoseeni O, Khandekar MJ, Neilan TG, Gainor J, Willers H, Jimenez RB, Keane FK.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys
journal.title: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
journal.isoabbreviation: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys

abstractText: Cardiac toxicity is a well-recognized, but poorly understood complication of radiotherapy (RT). In non-oncological settings, there is an established relationship between resting heart rate and cardiovascular health. To study the incidence and pattern of resting heart rate (rHR) as an early sign of cardiotoxicity among patients with non-metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) treated with RT. We retrospectively analyzed serial rHR measurements of consecutive patients with locally advanced NSCLC treated with definitive chemoradiation (CRT) over 6-7 weeks of daily radiation treatments followed by immunotherapy (durvalumab) between 2017-2022. Radiation dose to the heart and 17 cardiac substructures were extracted. Associations between heart rate elevation, tachycardia, cardiac substructure dose and outcomes were evaluated using generalized additive mixed models (GAMMs) and regression analysis. We identified 110 patients, 56.4% with pre-existing heart disease. Median follow-up was 33.6 months. Median age was 70.4 years. Median rHR increased significantly during RT, rising from 81.5 bpm to 93 bpm at end of RT (p < 0.0001), remaining elevated in 30.6% of patients 12 months post-RT. Tachycardia incidence rose from 11.2% at baseline to 36.5% at 1-month post-RT (p < 0.0001). After adjusting for comorbidities, higher mean sinoatrial node (SAN) dose was associated with higher rHR elevation, delayed HR recovery and persistent tachycardia (all p < 0.05). Higher rHR during and after RT (β = 0.23, p = 0.005, and β = 13.49, p = 0.049, respectively), as well as the incidence of tachycardia episodes during RT were associated with increased odds of developing an arrhythmia (OR, 2.97, 95% CI, 1.17-7.52, p = 0.022). Elevated rHR and tachycardia are observed during and after RT for NSCLC and are associated with higher mean SAN dose. HR elevation was associated with increased risk of de novo arrhythmias, suggesting that heart rate may represent a non-invasive biomarker of subclinical cardiac injury. Prospective studies might be warranted to test the potential of routine HR monitoring and proactive dose reductions to the SAN to enable early detection and help mitigate the risk of post-treatment arrhythmia.

title: Microvasculopathy in spinal muscular atrophy: The endothelium as a target of SMN deficiency and an amplifier of disease.
authorString: Corti S, Ottoboni L, Beatrice F, D'Angelo A, Marcotti F, D'Agostino M, Rizzo F, Magni G, Comi GP.
abstractText: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is caused by deficiency of the ubiquitous survival motor neuron (SMN) protein. Degeneration of anterior horn motor neurons defines the disease, but many organs are affected, including heart, liver, kidney, and bone. The vascular compartment is among them: digital necrosis in infants with the fewest SMN2 copies, capillary rarefaction in SMA mice, and decreased von Willebrand factor with fibrinogen extravasation in human post-mortem spinal cord. Whether these reflect endothelial injury by SMN deficiency itself or capillary adaptation to atrophic, denervated tissue has not been examined systematically. SMN-depleted endothelial cells form defective networks and migrate poorly in neuron-free systems, but this is based on a single unreplicated study in macrovascular and progenitor cells, which do not recapitulate human spinal cord microvascular endothelium. Ventral horn hypoxia precedes or accompanies weakness, retinal vessels fail before ganglion cells are lost, but retinal networks and patient-derived endothelial progenitors recover when SMN is restored. Demand-matched regression, reduced cardiac output, post-mortem artefact, critical illness, autonomic dysfunction and measurement confounding account for part of the phenotype, not all. Throughout, we keep vascular abnormality distinct from impaired perfusion, demonstrated only in mice. SMN has never been deleted from, or restored in, the endothelium alone in vivo. We therefore hypothesise, as a falsifiable model, not a proven mechanism, that the endothelium is injured cell-autonomously alongside other SMN-dependent lineages and amplifies rather than initiates disease, and we outline the genetic experiments required to falsify it. Retinal angiography and capillaroscopy are accessible readouts, neither visualising the cord.

title: CircNFIB attenuates hypoxia/reoxygenation-induced ferroptosis in AC16 cardiomyocytes with involvement of the miR-338-3p/GPX4 pathway.
authorString: Huang R, Wang J, He J, Zhong M.
abstractText: Cardiomyocyte ferroptosis contributes to myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury, but the upstream noncoding RNA mechanisms remain incompletely defined. This study examined whether nuclear factor I B-derived circular RNA (circNFIB) regulates hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R)-induced ferroptosis in human ventricular cardiomyocyte-derived AC16 cells and whether the miR-338-3p/GPX4 pathway contributes to this effect. The circNFIB back-splice junction was verified by Sanger sequencing. Cell viability, malondialdehyde, intracellular Fe2+, boron-dipyrromethene (BODIPY) 581/591 C11 oxidation, and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4), and transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1) protein abundance were evaluated. H/R decreased circNFIB expression, cell viability, and GPX4 abundance, while increasing lipid peroxidation, intracellular Fe2+ accumulation, and ACSL4 abundance; the reference ferroptosis inhibitor ferrostatin-1 partially reversed these changes. circNFIB overexpression improved cell viability, reduced intracellular Fe2+ accumulation and lipid peroxidation, partially restored GPX4 protein abundance, and lowered ACSL4 and TfR1 abundance. circNFIB was predominantly cytoplasmic. In reporter assays, miR-338-3p decreased the activity of reporters containing the wild-type circNFIB sequence or GPX4 3' untranslated region (3'UTR), whereas no significant reductions were observed with the corresponding mutant reporters. H/R increased miR-338-3p expression, whereas circNFIB overexpression reduced it. miR-338-3p overexpression aggravated the ferroptosis-associated phenotype and partially counteracted the protection associated with circNFIB overexpression. These findings indicate that circNFIB attenuates H/R-induced ferroptosis in AC16 cells, with the miR-338-3p/GPX4 pathway contributing to this effect.

title: BMI-anchored transcriptomics uncovers oxidative and inflammatory poles of obesity heterogeneity.
authorString: Yin-Yuan S, Linnaeus B, Yin-Cheng C, Erind G, Benedikt G, Sandy R, Mariami J, Sergio Eliseo PV, Anne H, Adhideb G, Christian W, Matthias B, Shahaf P, Antje G, Diana LD, Chen-Ching L.
abstractText: BMI remains the dominant clinical index of obesity, but does not resolve adipose molecular programs that distinguish metabolic resilience from vulnerability. Among 1,479 available human visceral adipose RNA-seq profiles, 1,298 samples from individuals with BMI 30-60 were included in the primary modeling cohort. Using BMI as a phenotypic anchor, we fit a LASSO regression model to derive transcriptome-predicted BMI and applied the resulting BMI-anchored transcriptomic model to mouse selection lines with divergent obesity phenotypes. In humans, directional discordance between measured and predicted BMI was used to define transcriptome-derived metabolically healthy obesity-like (MHO-like) and metabolically unhealthy obesity-like (MUO-like) states and to characterize pathophysiologic variation beyond measured BMI. Model-selected genes converged on immune, metabolic, mitochondrial, growth, structural-remodeling, and proteostasis programs. Cross-species application showed that BMI-anchored transcriptomic scores more closely tracked adipose-tissue content than body-size condition factor, distinguishing lipid-anabolic and inflammatory features of obesity-prone DU6 mice from the oxidative-catabolic phenotype of DU6P mice characterized by increased muscle mass. Gene-level associations with the transcriptomic score mirrored DU6-associated expression changes, linking the cross-species axis to an obesity-vulnerable adipose state. In humans, MHO-like individuals showed enhanced mitochondrial energy-production programs and more favorable glycemic and lipid profiles, whereas MUO-like individuals showed stress-adaptive metabolic remodeling and greater cardiometabolic medication use. In a separate, non-overlapping validation cohort, projection onto the primary-cohort PCA space retained a signal associated with insulin resistance that remained essentially unchanged after adjustment for sex. These findings support a conserved adipose transcriptomic axis linking oxidative metabolic resilience to healthier obesity and lipid-inflammatory remodeling to metabolic vulnerability.

title: Environmental toxicants associated with cardiovascular disease and a novel LE8 indicator approach for screening potential cardiovascular toxicants.
authorString: Lu Y, Li J, Chen X, Li Z, Gong Y, Ru S, Wang W.
abstractText: Environmental chemicals are emerging as inducers of cardiovascular disease (CVD), but identifying CVD-relevant toxicants across the exposome remains challenging. In this study, we analyzed 149 environmental chemicals from the 2013-2016 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey using analyte-specific survey-weighted single-pollutant models, mixture analyses, mediation and interaction analyses, and network toxicology to identify CVD-relevant toxicants. Adjusted data found no direct CVD correlations for many chemicals. Yet, using Life's Essential 8 (LE8) score (which covers diabetes, hyperlipidemia, and hypertension) as a quantitative cardiovascular health index revealed inverse associations with 41 chemicals after multiple-testing correction. These chemicals mainly included several volatile organic compound (VOC) metabolites, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH), and aromatic amines. BKMR analysis further suggested potential CVD associations for selected exposure mixtures, particularly serum metals and urinary PAHs. Exploratory mediation analysis identified significant positive indirect associations through LE8 for 37 chemicals, most of which showed directionally consistent patterns. Interaction analyses also indicated that several exposure-CVD associations may vary by LE8 health behaviors, with smoking-related interactions particularly evident for PAH- and VOC-related chemicals. Network toxicology linked LE8-associated toxicants to CVD-relevant pathways and protein modules involving vascular, cardiometabolic, inflammatory, and hemostatic processes, with PTGS2, ESR1, and MAPK1 among the most frequently connected genes. These findings support LE8 as a effective cardiovascular health indicator, and provide a framework for identifying CVD-relevant chemicals from the exposome via LE8.

title: Left Ventricular Volume Indexing in Athletic Brazilian Sport Horses Using Body Weight.
authorString: Wolff LB, Rosa LP, Padilha FGF, Ferreira AMR.
abstractText: Left ventricular (LV) volume assessment evaluates cardiac size and remodelling in horses. Single-plane Simpson method of discs (SMOD) provides volumetric measurements requiring body size normalization. We described LV volumes using SMOD in healthy Brazilian Sport Horses (BH) and evaluated thoracic-girth-estimated body weight (BWe) versus scale-measured weight (BWs) for indexing. Thirty BH horses (15 males, 15 females; 4-16 years) underwent echocardiography. LV end-diastolic (LVEDV), end-systolic volumes (LVESV), and ejection fraction (EF%) were obtained using SMOD. Body weight was scale-measured and estimated via thoracic girth formula. Volumes were indexed to BWs, BWe, and a 500-kg reference. Mean LVEDV was 1060 ± 154 mL (95% CI: 1003-1118), LVESV 318 ± 77 mL (95% CI: 290-347), and EF 70.0 ± 5.4%. Overall, BWe was associated with BWs (R² = 0.61; P < 0.0001) with mean bias of +33.25 kg (limits of agreement: -37.59 to +104.09 kg), mean absolute error of 39 ± 28.83 kg, and percentage error of 8.92 ± 7.27%. LVEDV/BWs averaged 2.30 ± 0.29 mL/kg and LVEDV/BWe 2.15 ± 0.26 mL/kg. Normalization to 500 kg yielded LVEDV[500] of 1151 ± 146 and 1069 ± 131 mL, and LVESV[500] of 346 ± 83 and 321 ± 70 mL (BWs; BWe). Indexed variables showed moderate to strong linear association between methods. In this sample, no sex or age differences were detected. Body weight normalization improved interindividual comparability. While BWe offers a practical field alternative, estimation errors warrant caution in individual evaluations, making BWs preferred.

title: Silent Ears, Failing Heart: Dilated Cardiomyopathy in an Infant With LARS2-Related Perrault Syndrome Type 4 (PRLTS4).
authorString: Alkateb FA, Aljohani R, Alkahmous MS, Mushiba A.
abstractText: We report a 19-month-old girl with molecularly confirmed Perrault syndrome type 4 (PRLTS4), due to a homozygous LARS2 variant (c.457A>C, p.Asn153His), who developed dilated cardiomyopathy (ejection fraction 21%) at 2 months of age despite a normal neonatal echocardiogram, alongside bilateral profound sensorineural hearing loss and global developmental delay. No second causative cardiac variant was identified. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of dilated cardiomyopathy in molecularly confirmed LARS2-related PRLTS4, expanding the recognised phenotypic spectrum of this disorder and supporting cardiac surveillance in affected infants.

title: HearTec: An Embedded Dual-Site Oscillometric Platform for Blood Pressure and Arterial Stiffness Monitoring - Design and Preliminary Feasibility Study.
authorString: Omari T, Baji I, Caulier F, Rochd M, Carlier S.
abstractText: Arterial stiffness is an independent predictor of cardiovascular risk, yet traditional bloodpressure monitors are inherently unable to assess it, since they perform only single-site,single-cuff measurements and do not capture the pulse wave propagation dynamics requiredfor its estimation. Existing systems capable of arterial stiffness assessment remain expensive,bulky, and confined to specialised clinical settings, limiting their accessibility for routine orpersonal use. This work presents HearTec, a compact and low-cost biomedical instrumentationplatform for dual-site oscillometric acquisition at the brachial and ankle locations, designed tobe affordable enough for personal use outside the clinical environment. The system integratessynchronized pneumatic modules, piezoresistive pressure sensors, and dedicated analog front end circuits designed to separate DC cuff pressure from AC oscillometric pulsations. A keyhardware contribution is the implementation of a dual-solenoid-valve pneumatic architectureenabling active stabilization of cuff pressure at the mean arterial pressure (MAP), whichprovides a stable window for reliable waveform acquisition and pulse transit time analysis.The embedded platform, based on an Arduino microcontroller, performs pneumatic control,conditioning circuits, and wireless data transmission via Bluetooth with simultaneous localstorage. These preliminary results demonstrate the technical feasibility of signal acquisitiononly; they do not establish the clinical or physiological validity of the estimated parametersand do not constitute a clinical validation.&#xD.

title: Chronic exposure to the tire-wear contaminant 6-PPDQ induces senescence-associated biomarkers and neurobehavioral deficits: Involvement of ABL1-p53-autophagy signaling.
authorString: Ma Z, Bai M, Xia C, Li J, Lu J.
abstractText: While 6-PPD quinone (6-PPDQ) is known for its acute lethality to salmonids, its chronic impacts on non-target species remain elusive. Here, we evaluated the chronic toxicity of 6-PPDQ across multiple biological models. Our results demonstrate that 6-PPDQ exposure significantly curtailed the survival and physiological motility of the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans, while inducing cellular senescence-associated biomarkers and a secretory phenotype (SASP) in human MRC-5 cells. In adult zebrafish, chronic exposure over a 28-month follow-up window precipitated cognitive and neurobehavioral deficits, characterized by impaired spatial learning, elevated agonistic reactivity, and glutamatergic excitotoxicity. Through computational screening, molecular docking, and pharmacological rescue, we identified ABL1 as a prioritized candidate target and functional mediator of 6-PPDQ toxicity. Total ABL1 protein abundance was elevated in exposed zebrafish brains alongside p53 accumulation and autophagic substrate (p62 and LC3-II) retention. Importantly, concurrent treatment with the ABL1 kinase inhibitor nilotinib attenuated p53 induction, restored autophagic flux, and rescued locomotor deficits, implicating the ABL1-associated pathway in these phenotypes. Because overt organismal morbidity was manifest predominantly at upper-bound exposure concentrations (10 µg/L), these phenotypes reflect chronic toxic stress rather than an acceleration of natural aging. These findings identify an ABL1-associated mechanism of chronic neurotoxicity and emphasize the need to assess long-term neurological risks associated with tire-wear pollution.

title: Antimitochondrial antibodies in rheumatic diseases: beyond primary biliary cholangitis.
authorString: De Carvalho JF, Rodrigues CEM, Gomes KWP, de Messias KLM, Timilsina S, Gershwin ME.
abstractText: Antimitochondrial antibodies (AMAs) targeting the E2 subunit of the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex are the serological hallmark of primary biliary cholangitis (PBC), but may also occur across systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases. This narrative review integrates clinical and experimental evidence on AMAs in rheumatic diseases, delineating disease-specific patterns and clinical implications beyond the hepatobiliary context. AMAs and other mitochondrial autoantibodies have been reported in systemic sclerosis, systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis, Sjögren disease, and inflammatory myopathies. In systemic sclerosis and Sjögren disease, AMAs frequently indicate autoimmune overlap with PBC. In lupus and rheumatoid arthritis, mitochondrial autoantibodies have been associated with systemic inflammation, apoptosis, and innate immune activation. In inflammatory myopathies, AMAs identify a distinct phenotype characterized by chronic muscle involvement and increased cardiac risk. Thus, mitochondrial autoimmunity extends beyond hepatobiliary disease, and its interpretation should consider disease context, potentially indicating polyautoimmunity, systemic immune activation, or distinct clinical phenotypes.

title: Aptamer-Functionalized Pro-Photosensitizers for Targeted Elimination of Drug-Resistant Bacterial Biofilm Infection by Sequentially Activated Photodynamic-Antibiotic Therapy.
authorString: Wu Y, Zhang Y, Xie S, Li X, Han X, Wang H, Li W, Yang D, Liu X, Wang P, Zeng Q, Liao Y, Zheng J.
abstractText: Drug-resistant bacterial infections seriously threaten public health, and the formation of a biofilm barrier plays an important role. Drug-resistant biofilms are difficult to remove because the penetration and specificity of traditional antimicrobial drugs are poor, and the microenvironment in the inner layer of biofilms is hypoxic. Herein, we developed activatable aptamer-functionalized pro-photosensitizers (APMB) by modifying the clinical photosensitizer methylene blue (MB) with an aptamer that can specifically bind to drug-resistant bacteria. The APMB can simultaneously achieve imaging-guided efficient anti-infection and biofilm destruction, thereby increasing the therapeutic efficiency of the treatment of bacterial biofilm infections. Additionally, we co-loaded APMB and the antibiotic metronidazole (MNZ) into hydrogels to prepare a degradable microneedle patch, which can utilize photodynamic effects to eliminate biofilms under normoxic conditions and potentiate the hypoxic microenvironment to activate the antibacterial activity of MNZ, ultimately resulting in the synergistic killing of deep-seated bacteria. To summarize, this simple and intelligent phototheranostic molecular platform improves deep anti-infection efficacy through the synergistic effect of sequential activation while decreasing systemic toxicity, thereby providing a promising avenue for clinical translation to combat antimicrobial resistance.

title: UNOS Registry Analysis: How Does Heart Transplant Recipient Weight Affect Waitlist Days?
authorString: Kawabori M, Chung JW, Malik MJ, Dahal M, Ogburn EA, London-Bounds T, Reda H, Loebe M, Birks EJ.

journal.title: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)

abstractText: Body weight of heart transplant (HTx) recipients affects waitlist days. However, no prior report exists to articulate this in detail. The aim of this study is to analyze the effect of recipients' weight to HTx. The United Network of Organ Sharing (UNOS) registry was analyzed under the current allocation from 2018 to 2023. The cohort was divided into three even weight groups: low (<77.1 kg), middle (77.1-92.1 kg), and high (>92.1 kg). Candidate/donor demographics, weight distributions, waitlist days in UNOS Status, cumulative incidence of HTx and delisting, post-HTx survival, and cutoff weight for earlier HTx were analyzed. A total of 16,664 HTx recipients were included (5,535: low, 5,537: middle, and 5,592: high). Donors and recipients had a weight distribution mismatch (p = 0.003). For waitlist days, status 1 was comparable; however, the high group with status ≥2 had approximately twice longer waitlist days than the low group. The high group had a lower incidence of HTx (p < 0.001) and higher delisting (p = 0.02) than the low group. One year survival was comparable (p = 0.28). The weight cutoff for earlier HTx was 80 kg with a 21.6% increased rate of HTx (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.216; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.171-1.263, p < 0.001). Recipients weighing <80 kg had earlier HTx and a higher incidence of HTx. The effect of pre-HTx weight management requires further study.

title: Ex Vivo Heart Perfusion Versus Cold Storage in Prolonged Preservation Period: A Juvenile Porcine Experimental Model.
authorString: Kobayashi Y, Li J, Ingarao J, Zahiri Y, Parker M, Deng MX, Kadowaki S, Signorile M, Runeckles K, Fan CS, Nagy A, Honjo O.

journal.title: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)

abstractText: Cross-clamp times greater than or equal to 4 hours are critical for donor heart viability. We compared cold storage (CS) and normothermic ex vivo heart perfusion (EVHP) during prolonged preservation using a juvenile porcine model. Twenty-two piglet hearts (~10 kg) were assigned to CS or EVHP for 6 or 8 hours, followed by 2 hours of working-mode (WM) perfusion. Metabolism, cardiac function, and cell damage were compared using two-sample t-tests or Fisher's exact tests, and temporal changes during perfusion were assessed using linear mixed-effects models and generalized estimating equations. During EVHP, the minimal rate of pressure change decreased, and arterial lactate levels increased after 5-6 hours. Compared to CS, EVHP hearts showed higher left atrial pressure (6 vs. 0 mm Hg, p = 0.011), arterial lactate levels during WM (p < 0.001), and NFκB-p65 levels (p = 0.002) at 6 hours, and lower cardiac output (90 vs. 120% of normal, p = 0.026), higher left atrial pressure (7 vs. 3 mm Hg, p = 0.009), higher arterial lactate levels during WM (p < 0.001), and increased neutrophil infiltration (p = 0.033) at 8 hours. Ex vivo heart perfusion hearts deteriorated beyond 5-6 hours and showed greater hemodynamic, metabolic, and inflammatory changes at both 6 and 8 hours. Ex vivo heart perfusion enhancements reducing immune response and inflammation are crucial for expanding the donor pool.

title: Frequent Premature Ventricular Complexes and Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation.
authorString: Alshakhs A, Andrade JG, Hawkins NM, Laksman ZW, Bennett RG, Yeung-Lai-Wah JA, Chakrabarti S, Bennett MT, Krahn AD, Deyell MW.
abstractText: Frequent premature ventricular complexes (PVCs) are often observed in patients undergoing ablation of atrial fibrillation (AF). However, the relationship between AF ablation and PVCs is uncertain. The purpose of this study was to examine the prevalence of frequent PVCs before and after catheter ablation of AF. This was a retrospective cohort study of patients undergoing ablation of AF at two tertiary centers. All patients undergoing initial or repeat ablation of AF were eligible. Patients were followed in AF clinics before and after ablation with routine ambulatory ECG monitoring. The cohort consisted of 421 patients (mean 63 years, 33% female, 57% paroxysmal). At baseline, 18.4% and 4.7% had ≥ 1% and ≥ 5% PVCs respectively. In the 179 days post-ablation, 9.0% developed new onset ≥ 1% PVCs, whereas 10.9% of patients had regression from ≥ 1% to < 1% PVCs. In the total follow up period of 2 years, there was a significant increase in the proportion of patients with ≥ 1% PVCs. Multivariable modeling revealed baseline PVC burden and hypertension as the only predictors of an increasing PVC burden in the post-ablation period. Frequent PVCs are highly prevalent among patients undergoing AF ablation. However, there was no signal of an increase in frequent PVCs in the immediate post-ablation period.

title: Association among Dietary Inflammatory Index, sleep quality and nutritional status in fixed daytime and rotating shift workers.
authorString: Sünbül Ş, Türker PF.
abstractText: Shift work is associated with irregular eating behaviors, increased energy intake, and impaired sleep quality. Poor dietary patterns may elevate systemic inflammation, contributing to long-term metabolic and cardiovascular risks. The aim of this study was to investigate differences in the Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII), sleep quality, dietary intake, and anthropometric and body composition measures between fixed daytime workers and rotating shift workers and to examine the associations among these parameters. This cross-sectional study included 52 male workers employed at a defense industry factory in Ankara, Türkiye, who worked either fixed daytime or rotating shifts. Dietary intake was assessed using 24-h dietary recalls for three non-consecutive days, from which macronutrient and micronutrient intakes were calculated. DII scores were computed to assess the inflammatory potential of the diet. Sleep quality was evaluated using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Anthropometric measurements, body composition, blood pressure, and biochemical parameters, including fasting plasma glucose, lipid profile (total cholesterol, HDL-C, LDL-C, and triglycerides), C-reactive protein, and homocysteine, were measured using standardised protocols. Rotating shift workers had significantly higher total energy intake and higher daily intakes of fructose, total fat, saturated and monounsaturated fatty acids, cholesterol, and several micronutrients, including vitamin A, folate, iron, calcium, and phosphorus compared with fixed daytime workers (p < 0.05). Mean DII scores did not differ significantly between the groups (Fixed daytime: 0.2 ± 1.86; rotating shift: -0.2 ± 2.25). DII scores were positively correlated with global PSQI score (r = 0.278, p = 0.046), the PSQI sleep duration component score (r = 0.319, p = 0.021), and daytime dysfunction component score (r = 0.287, p = 0.039); however, the association between DII and overall sleep quality was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for potential confounding factors (age, BMI, smoking status, physical activity, and work schedule). These findings suggest that dietary habits, pro-inflammatory dietary patterns, and poor sleep quality may represent co-existing factors associated with metabolic risk, and addressing these factors may contribute to better overall metabolic health.

title: First-trimester plasma asprosin and its association with gestational diabetes mellitus: A prospective cohort study.
authorString: Inthavong S, Jatavan P, Kumfu S, Chattipakorn N, Tongsong T.
abstractText: Asprosin a glucogenic adipokine associated with insulin resistance, has been found to be elevated in the plasma of women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). Emerging evidence indicates that it can serve as a promising biomarker for the diagnosis of GDM during the second trimester. However, its utility in the first trimester has not yet been investigated. Therefore, the present study aimed to establish first-trimester reference ranges for plasma asprosin and to evaluate its predictive performance for the subsequent development of GDM. In this prospective cohort study, low-risk women with singleton pregnancies at 10-14 weeks of gestation were consecutively enrolled. Participants with pregestational diabetes were excluded. Baseline clinical characteristics were documented, and blood samples were obtained for the measurement of plasma asprosin concentrations. The diagnosis of GDM at 24-28 weeks of gestation was established using the two-step screening approach. Among the 302 participants, 98 (32.5%) developed GDM. Asprosin concentrations did not differ significantly across gestational ages between 10 and 14 weeks. However, asprosin levels increased significantly with maternal BMI (p < 0.001), demonstrating a quadratic relationship. A first-trimester reference range for plasma asprosin was established. Nevertheless, first-trimester asprosin showed poor predictive performance for subsequent GDM (AUC = 0.516), whereas maternal BMI and age showed modest predictive ability. First, a reference range for first-trimester asprosin was established, which may serve as a valuable benchmark for future investigations examining various aspects of diabetes in pregnancy. Second, first-trimester asprosin concentrations did not discriminate between women who subsequently developed GDM and those who did not.

title: Relationship Between Objective Measures of Sleep and Nocturnal Cardiovascular Physiology and Swimming Performance in Collegiate Female Athletes: A Bayesian Analysis.
authorString: Vatne EA, Cencer D, Vatne M, Pulvermacher K, Saenz C, Kraemer WJ, Robinson B, Jones P, Quebedeaux N, Sprague R, Dial M, Carpenter T, Hagen J.

journal.title: Journal of strength and conditioning research

abstractText: Vatne, EA, Cencer, D, Vatne, M, Pulvermacher, K, Saenz, C, Kraemer, WJ, Robinson, B, Jones, P, Quebedeaux, N, Sprague, R, Dial, M, Carpenter, T, and Hagen, J. Relationship between objective measures of sleep and nocturnal cardiovascular physiology and swimming performance in collegiate female athletes: A Bayesian analysis. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-There is substantial evidence that sleep influences athletic performance; however, relationships with real-world competition outcomes remain unclear. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to explore the associations between objectively measured sleep, nocturnal cardiovascular physiology on the night before competition, and swim performance in female collegiate athletes. Female swimmers (n = 11) who wore a sleep monitoring device the night before competition, competed in the 200-yard freestyle (short course yard), and had ≥21 of 28 prior nights of valid data were included. Sleep metrics included total sleep time (TST), time in bed (TiB), and sleep efficiency (SE), whereas nocturnal cardiovascular metrics included heart rate variability (HRV) and resting heart rate (RHR) standardized as individualized z-scores. Race times were obtained from a publicly available database. Bayesian linear mixed-effects models estimated posterior probabilities of performance improvement. Results indicated a high probability that greater TST and TiB were associated with faster race times, with substantial support for improvements of at least 1 second per additional hour of sleep. In contrast, SE, HRV, and RHR showed low posterior evidence of meaningful associations with performance. These findings extend prior sleep and performance literature that has been confined to proxy assessments of athletic performance in controlled settings to real-world competition that should inform athlete education, emphasizing the importance of sufficient sleep opportunity and duration before competition.

title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Predicting Early Onset Hypertension in the US.
authorString: Wu LW, Kim K, Washington P, Park C.
abstractText: Early onset hypertension is often overlooked despite its association with lifelong cardiovascular disease risk. We developed an interpretable machine learning model to predict early onset hypertension in US adults using the 2022 Medical Expenditure Panel Survey, incorporating demographic, socioeconomic, health care utilization, and comorbidity features. We analyzed data on adults aged 55 years or younger. Hypertension was defined by International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Clinical Modification code number I10 or self-reported physician diagnosis at or before age 55 years. Eighty-four variables were screened; Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator reduced the set to 45 variables. Extreme gradient boosting was trained with stratified 5-fold cross-validation. Performance metrics included accuracy, precision, recall, F2 score, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC AUC), and area under the precision-recall curve (PR AUC). We assessed fairness across subgroups and used Shapley Additive Explanations to quantify feature influence. Among 9,850 adults, 1,647 (weighted prevalence, 15.2%) had hypertension. Discrimination was strong, with a ROC AUC of 0.807 (95% CI, 0.787-0.827), PR AUC of 0.486 (95% CI, 0.439-0.530), recall of 0.848 (95% CI, 0.816-0.878), and F2 score of 0.606 (95% CI, 0.578-0.634). Key predictors included older age, high body mass index, and a diagnosis of high cholesterol. Fairness analyses showed slightly higher true positive rates for Hispanic (+0.11) and Asian (+0.08) people, with performance for African American people modestly lower than that for White people. Both medical and nonmedical predictors contributed meaningfully, with high cholesterol particularly influential among adults older than 40 years and race and ethnicity especially important among African American adults. Prospective validation and routine fairness audits are warranted to ensure equitable benefit across populations. This interpretable model supports recall-oriented screening to identify younger adults at risk of hypertension for further evaluation and early intervention.

title: Modern antidiabetic therapy in older adults with type 2 diabetes: evidence, best practice and a clinical pharmacist's framework.
authorString: Martinc B, Šabovič M, Janić M, Lunder M.
abstractText: Older adults with type 2 diabetes require treatment that balances cardiovascular and kidney protection against hypoglycemia, treatment burden, undernutrition, and functional vulnerability. This narrative review considers PubMed-indexed literature and ClinicalTrials.gov records covering January 2010-October 2026, with targeted updating on 12 October 2026. It examines sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, tirzepatide, and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors. Age-stratified outcome evidence is distinguished from whole-trial results and the limited evidence in adults aged 80 years or older. Body-composition findings, neurodegenerative outcomes, kidney-protective treatment, and pharmacist-supported regimen modification are critically appraised. Organ protection and glycemic simplification should be considered separately. Frailty is not synonymous with kidney impairment, and reductions in lean mass do not establish treatment-induced sarcopenia. Weight-neutral therapy remains useful when weight loss is undesirable. A structured medication review should integrate patient priorities, nutrition, physical performance, renal function, and hypoglycemia risk, followed by explicit monitoring and communication across care transitions. Prospective validation of this integrated framework in the oldest and most vulnerable populations is needed.

title: Chair-Rise Difficulty as a Functional Correlate in the Longitudinal Association Between Loneliness and Incident Osteoarthritis in Older Adults.
authorString: Karim A, Azhar Hussain M, Qaisar R.

journal.title: Journal of applied gerontology : the official journal of the Southern Gerontological Society

abstractText: ObjectiveTo examine whether chair-rise difficulty functions as a functional mediator in the association between loneliness/social isolation and incident osteoarthritis (OA).MethodsData from 6,232 adults ≥50 in 12 European countries (SHARE waves 7-9, 2017-2022). Social isolation and loneliness were exposures; depression, physical inactivity, and chair-rise difficulty were mediators; OA onset was the outcome. Structural equation modeling tested mediation, adjusting for covariates.ResultsNo direct associations were found; both exposures had significant indirect effects via depression and functional decline. Chair-rise difficulty was the strongest mediator (β = 0.74, p < 0.001), followed by depression (β = 0.04, p = 0.033). Physical inactivity acted indirectly through chair-rise difficulty (β = 0.26, p < 0.001). Female sex and older-age independently increased OA incidence.ConclusionLoneliness and social isolation were indirectly linked to incident OA via psychological, behavioral, and functional mechanisms. Chair-rise difficulty is a functional intermediary linking psychosocial distress to physical vulnerability and increased OA incidence, not a direct cause of joint-degeneration.

title: Cellular Senescence as a Core Mechanistic Link between CKD, Cardiac Fibrosis, and Aging.
authorString: Di Carmine S, Baird DP, Mylonas KJ.
abstractText: CKD and cardiovascular disease frequently coexist and represent a major global health burden. Cellular senescence may connect these disorders through persistent inflammation, fibrosis, and metabolic stress. Senescent cells undergo sustained proliferative arrest and release a pro-inflammatory, pro-fibrotic secretome called the senescence-associated secretory phenotype. In kidney and heart tissue, persistent senescent cells may promote immune-cell infiltration, fibroblast activation, extracellular matrix deposition, and tissue stiffening. Human biopsy, cardiac-tissue, urinary-biomarker, circulating-proteomic, and early senolytic data support associations between senescence markers, kidney dysfunction, and cardiovascular remodelling. However, most causal and interventional evidence still comes from cell-culture and animal models. This review critically evaluates cellular senescence as a plausible cardiorenal-fibrosis mechanism while emphasizing that causality, biomarker specificity, and therapeutic benefit in humans remain to be fully elucidated.

title: Metal-supported versus conventional ultra-fine chest drains after pulmonary resection: a historical cohort study of drainage outcomes and placement learning curves.
authorString: Liu Y, Ma K, Lin R, Wei N, Bai S, Yang L, Su J, Rivas DG, Ma M, Han B.
abstractText: Ultra-fine chest drains are susceptible to kinking and obstruction. We compared drainage outcomes and device-placement learning curves for a 10-F metal-supported, multi-side-port drain and a conventional 12-F drain after pulmonary resection. This single-centre historical cohort comprised 5,235 patients treated between 2006 and 2023. A conventional drain was used in 2,614 patients during 2006-2017, whereas 2,621 patients received the metal-supported drain during 2018-2023. The co-primary outcomes were additional catheter drainage and encapsulated pleural effusion. Firth logistic regression adjusted for age, gender, BMI, and ASA score. For the learning-curve analysis, a designated observer timed the first 261 consecutive procedures after adoption of each device, from the initial skin puncture to fixation of the final drain. Additional catheter drainage was required in 7/2,621 (0.3%) patients in the metal-supported group and 30/2,614 (1.1%) in the conventional group (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.24, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.10-0.51; P < 0.001). Encapsulated pleural effusion occurred in 15/2,621 (0.6%) versus 34/2,614 (1.3%) patients, respectively (aOR 0.44, 95% CI 0.24-0.79; P = 0.006). Mean total placement time was 24.1±7.8 min with the metal-supported drain and 44.3±7.7 min with the conventional drain. The CUSUM curves reached their peaks at cases 90 and 71, respectively, and then declined. Although drainage duration, length of stay, and pain differed statistically, the absolute differences were small. The metal-supported drain was associated with fewer drainage-related reinterventions, fewer encapsulated pleural effusions, and shorter placement times. Because device use was determined by treatment era, residual temporal confounding precludes firm causal inference.

title: Real-World Effectiveness of Mavacamten in Canada: Insights from the MAVEN Study.
authorString: Ward MR, Crean AM, Desplantie O, Tyrrell BD, Corriveau S, Brellier F, Ong KC.
abstractText:
Introduction

Previous studies have demonstrated the efficacy and safety of mavacamten in patients with symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM), primarily outside of Canada, with limited Canadian real-world data evidence. The MAVEN study aimed to describe the real-world effectiveness of mavacamten in Canadian patients with oHCM.

Methods

This multi-center, retrospective physician survey of patient charts included 115 patients with oHCM who initiated mavacamten between January 2023 and November 2024 across five Canadian sites. Effectiveness was assessed by changes in clinical characteristics and outcomes, including New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class, resting and Valsalva left ventricular outflow tract (rLVOT and vLVOT, respectively) gradients, and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), from treatment initiation to the most recent available assessment.

Results

Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics were consistent with previously published data (median age 63.0 years; 66.1% aged ≥ 60 years; 51.3% male, 48.7% female patients; 57.4% NYHA class II, 42.6% NYHA class III). Median baseline rLVOT and vLVOT gradients were 44.0 and 78.0 mmHg, respectively, and median LVEF was 65.0%. Overall, 72.7% of patients improved by ≥ 1 NYHA functional class. Median reductions in rLVOT and vLVOT gradients were - 25.5 (interquartile range [IQR]: - 61, - 8) mmHg and - 51.0 (IQR: - 83, - 24) mmHg, respectively, while median LVEF changed by - 3.0% (IQR: - 8, 0). Mavacamten was discontinued in 8.7% of patients, including 2.6% due to treatment-emergent adverse events. Reductions in LVEF < 50% were observed in 6.1% of patients, and no patient experienced an LVEF < 30%.

Conclusions

In this first Canadian real-world study of mavacamten effectiveness, treatment was associated with improvements in symptoms and LVOT obstruction. Reductions in LVEF < 50% were observed in a minority of patients, with no cases of LVEF < 30%. Given the retrospective design and heterogeneous follow-up of this study, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Graphical abstract available for this article.

title: Serum Proteoglycan Alterations Associated with Cardiovascular Risk in Pb-Battery Recycling Workers Using Exploratory Proteomics and Independent ELISA Validation.
authorString: Matte K, Pingle S, Tumane R, Ramaiah MK, Ravibabu K.
abstractText: Lead (Pb) is a prevalent environmental and occupational toxin that disrupts several biological systems. Its toxicological effects are well known but serum proteomic alterations associated with Pb remain insufficiently characterized. This study investigated serum proteomic changes in Pb-battery recycling workers (Pb-BRW) to identify the candidate proteins associated with Pb exposure using high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS). Blood samples (5 mL) were collected from Pb-BRW (n = 78) and age-matched unexposed controls (n = 65) from three industries in Karnataka, India. Blood Pb levels were assessed using inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectroscopy. Serum samples (n = 10) pooled from each group were analyzed using quantitative discovery HRMS. Data are available via ProteomeXchange with identifier PXD082567. Raw files were processed using Proteome Discoverer, and proteins were identified using the UniProt Homo sapiens reviewed database. Further data were analysed in Perseus with log<sub>2</sub> transformation and imputation. Gene ontology was used for functional enrichment analysis. Candidate proteins were selected (nominal p < 0.05 and |log<sub>2</sub>FC| ≥ 1.2) as exploratory filtering criteria and visualized using a volcano plot and heatmap. Selected proteins were further validated using ELISA in an independent set of serum samples obtained from Pb-BRW (n = 68) and control subjects (n = 55). A total of 257 serum proteins were identified. Exploratory HRMS-based proteomic profiling identified 26 candidate proteins with nominal p < 0.05. Functional enrichment analysis suggested associations with cardiovascular-related processes. Of these, eight candidate proteins met both exploratory filtering criteria, including five showing higher and three showing lower abundance in Pb-BRW. Lumican (LUM) and Proteoglycan-4 (PRG4) were selected for ELISA-based validation based on their abundance patterns and biological relevance to extracellular matrix organisation and vascular homeostasis. Exploratory serum proteomic profiling revealed alterations in proteins involved in lipid transport and extracellular matrix organization in Pb-BRW. The identification and independent validation of LUM and PRG4 suggest their potential as candidate biomarkers associated with Pb-related cardiovascular alterations.

title: The impact of nationwide folic acid fortification on genetic variants associated with conotruncal heart defects.
authorString: Morton SU, Mondragon-Estrada E, Qian R, Oluwafemi OO, Au KS, Northrup H, Chung WK, Agopian AJ, Findley TO.
abstractText: Folate deficiency is associated with increased risk of conotruncal heart defects (CTHD), but its interaction with genetic factors remains unclear. Our objective was to investigate genome-wide associations between common genetic variants and birth before versus after universal folic acid fortification among children with CTHD and other heart defects. Sequencing data were available through the Pediatric Cardiac Genomics Consortium, aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38/hg38), and jointly processed to ensure uniform variant detection and minimize batch effects. Analyses were restricted to individuals with European-inferred genetic ancestry, limiting generalizability to other ancestral groups. Genome-wide association study (GWAS) models compared allele frequencies across fortification eras among all participants (n = 1285), the subset with CTHD (n = 534), and the remaining individuals with other heart defects (n = 751). Functional enrichment was assessed using the Database for Annotation, Visualization and Integrated Discovery (DAVID). Among the full analytic group, eight loci had at least two suggestive variants before compared to after fortification. Among the subset with CTHD, two variants located in DHRS3 (rs7551703, odds ratio [OR] 2.10, and rs6541043, OR 2.21) and four variants located in PPARGC1B showed suggestive association after fortification (OR 4.47-4.51). Enriched biological pathway terms were consistent with cardiac developmental processes. In summary, this study examined the association between folic acid fortification and genetic risk for CTHD and other heart defects and identified associations with fortification era that suggest some shift in risk following fortification. Identified pathways suggest gene-nutrient interactions may modulate cardiac developmental pathways, underscoring the relationship between maternal folate status and cardiovascular development.

title: [Psychotherapeutic interventions for reducing stress in patients with cardiac arrhythmias].
authorString: Meesmann M.
abstractText: Cardiac arrhythmias may remain asymptomatic, but they can also be experienced as palpitations or implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) shocks that feel existentially threatening. Even harmless arrhythmias can trigger intense anxiety reactions, including traumatic processing. Therefore, in addition to cardiological diagnostics and treatment, an integrative psychocardiological perspective is needed. From a cardiological point of view, the symptom burden should be reduced, for example, by avoiding substances that promote arrhythmias, treating underlying diseases, and-particularly in ICD patients-optimizing potassium levels. Psychoeducation is central: patients should understand why extrasystoles may be experienced as missed beats, strong palpitations, or a sensation of the "heart beating up into the throat." Equally important is discussing the vicious circle of anxiety: tension, worry, and self-monitoring lower the threshold for perception; perceived cardiac symptoms then intensify anxiety and autonomic arousal. Since these signals are interoceptive, avoidance is not possible, and patients should be taught routines that help them break out of the anxiety cycle. Special attention should be given to patients after an ICD shock or cardiac arrest. They may develop posttraumatic stress disorder induced by the cardiac event (CDI-PTSD). Supportive communication, realistic hope, and basic psychosomatic or psychocardiological interventions can reduce nocebo effects and anxiety spirals.
