title: Conduction System Pacing Versus Biventricular Pacing for Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
authorString: Singireddy S, Shoura S, Venugopal D, Saravanabavanandan R, Coombes K, Baman T, Shah S.
abstractText:
Background

Conduction system pacing (CSP) is an emerging alternative to biventricular pacing (BVP) for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). Recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have yielded divergent results, creating uncertainty about the comparative effectiveness.

Methods

We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs comparing CSP with BVP for CRT, searching PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL through May 2026 (updating a prior review). The primary outcome was change in left ventricular ejection fraction (ΔLVEF), analyzed with random-effects models and prediction intervals.

Results

Eight parallel-group RCTs including 799 patients (396 CSP, 403 BVP) were included. Pooled ΔLVEF did not differ significantly (MD +2.40%, 95% CI -0.49 to 5.29, p = 0.091; I 2 = 75%). CSP showed a non-significant trend toward shorter paced QRS (MD -7.6 ms, p = 0.14) and improved NYHA class (SMD -0.33, p = 0.12). Heart failure hospitalization (RR 0.69), mortality (RR 1.17), complications (RR 0.84), and procedure time did not differ. The four trials enrolling exclusively LBBB patients favored CSP (MD +5.00%, 95% CI 3.01 to 6.98, p = 0.004; I 2 = 0%), consistent in the three using confirmed LBBAP/LBBP (MD +5.37%, 95% CI 3.23 to 7.52, p = 0.008; I 2 = 0%).

Conclusions

In this analysis of randomized trials of CRT, no statistically significant difference was observed between CSP and BVP for any outcome. Because no non-inferiority margin was prespecified and the clinical-event analyses were underpowered, these findings should not be interpreted as establishing equivalence or comparable safety. Exploratory analyses suggest that patients with LBBB undergoing LBBAP/LBBP may derive incremental benefit, warranting confirmation in adequately powered trials.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Benmelstobart Plus Anlotinib in Advanced Endometrial Cancer: Results of a Multi-Cohort, Phase II Study (ETER200).
authorString: Liang S, Chen X, Wang K, Wang D, An R, Hou J, Yang Y, Wang D, Qu P, Zhang B, Duan W, Li X, Zang A, Yu G, Lou H, Yao D, Wang S, Yan D, Li L, Liu X, Zhao W, Chen Z, Fei J, Li J, Wang J, Wang Z, Yao S, Ning F, Zhou H, Sun L, Pan L, Liu Q, Yang H, Wang L, Zhang M, Chen X, Yuan J, Zhang X, Zhang Y, Liao Q, Wu X.
abstractText: Patients with advanced endometrial cancer (EC) have a poor prognosis and limited therapeutic options after failure of prior systemic therapy. In this multi-cohort Phase II study (ETER200), patients with metastatic or recurrent EC who had received at least one chemotherapy regimen were enrolled. Based on MSI/MMR status, patients received benmelstobart plus anlotinib (Cohort 1), benmelstobart (Cohort 2), or anlotinib (Cohort 3) every 3 weeks. Primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) assessed by independent review committee (IRC) per RECIST v1.1. Here, the results of Cohort 1 expansion stage were reported. As of May 9, 2024, 85 of the 107 non-MSI-H/pMMR EC patients enrolled in Cohort 1 constituted the expansion stage population for primary efficacy analysis. The IRC-assessed ORR was 34.1% (95% CI, 24.2-45.2), with a median duration of response of 15.2 months (95% CI, 6.9-not evaluable). Median progression-free and overall survival were 8.8 months (95% CI, 5.8-15.2) and 21.8 months (95% CI, 19.5-29.1), respectively. Grade ≥ 3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 69.2% of patients, most commonly hypertension (21.2%) and palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia syndrome (9.4%). Overall, benmelstobart plus anlotinib showed promising anti-tumor activity and an acceptable safety profile in advanced non-MSI-H/pMMR EC, supporting further evaluation of this combination in randomized Phase III studies. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04574284.

title: Bromocriptine for Myocardial Recovery in Peripartum Cardiomyopathy: Design and Rationale of the REBIRTH Trial.
authorString: Wang T, Ibarra AJ, Simpson D, Kirsch J, Koczo A, Briller JE, Abebe KZ, McNamara D, Givertz MM.
abstractText:
Background

There is evidence suggesting that bromocriptine potentially improves outcomes among women with peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM); however, there is currently no randomized controlled trial comparing bromocriptine vs placebo on top of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in a diverse, multiethnic cohort in North America.

Objectives

The REBIRTH trial will enroll 200 women with PPCM to evaluate whether the addition of oral bromocriptine to GDMT is superior to placebo for improving myocardial function and event-free survival. In addition to the randomized trial, REBIRTH will enroll 50 women with PPCM excluded from randomization because of breastfeeding into an observational cohort.

Methods

The principal inclusion criteria are ≥18 years of age, within 5-months postpartum, and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤40%. The primary endpoint is LVEF at 6 months postrandomization. Secondary endpoints include LVEF at 12 months, survival free from major events (ie, death, heart transplantation, or implantation of a durable left ventricular assist device), and survival free from heart failure hospitalization for up to 3 years.

Results

The study is currently enrolling women in both the randomized trial and observational breastfeeding cohort. Primary results are expected to be reported in 2027.

Conclusions

REBIRTH will determine whether the addition of bromocriptine to GDMT for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction improves postpartum myocardial recovery and clinical outcomes in a diverse cohort of women with PPCM. (Randomized Evaluation of Bromocriptine in Myocardial Recovery Therapy for PPCM [REBIRTH]; NCT05180773).

title: Right Ventricular-Pulmonary Arterial Coupling by Serial TAPSE/sPAP: A Noninvasive Predictor for Clinical Outcomes in Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension.
authorString: Wen J, Yiminniyaze R, Li Y, Gong S, Zhu L, Yang Y, Hong C, Yang Z, Wan J, Cui X, Chen H, Ji Y, Li C, Cheng Z, Zhang Y, Xiong C, Wang L, Ji Q, Li F, Zhang Z, Zhang Y, Huang Q, Zhen Y, Liu M, Li L, Zhai Y, Li A, Fu L, Zhang S, Xie W, Zhai Z, Wang C.
abstractText: The ratio of tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion to systolic pulmonary artery pressure (TAPSE/sPAP) is a noninvasive surrogate of right ventricular-pulmonary arterial coupling, but its value for dynamic risk stratification in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) remains uncertain. This multicenter prospective cohort enrolled adults with CTEPH between 2016 and 2023. Patients were stratified by quartile-based baseline TAPSE/sPAP cutoffs into < 0.15, 0.15 to 0.30, and > 0.30. The primary outcome was clinical worsening (CW) within 12 months, comprising all-cause death, hospitalization for worsening pulmonary hypertension, escalation of pulmonary hypertension-targeted therapy, or a > 30% increase in pulmonary vascular resistance. Associations were examined using Kaplan-Meier, Cox regression, and time-dependent Cox analyses. Among 949 patients, 868 had follow-up and 212 (24.4%) experienced CW during a median follow-up of 10.3 months (interquartile range, 5.4-12.2 months). Lower baseline TAPSE/sPAP was associated with worse functional and hemodynamic profiles, and CW-free survival differed across strata (log-rank p = 0.004). Each 0.1-unit increase in baseline TAPSE/sPAP was associated with lower CW risk (adjusted HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.79-0.99; p = 0.039). Among 593 patients with serial measurements, higher time-updated TAPSE/sPAP (adjusted HR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.52-0.83; p < 0.001) and greater improvement from baseline (adjusted HR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.71-0.92; p = 0.002) were associated with lower subsequent CW risk. Lower TAPSE/sPAP identifies greater disease severity and CW risk in CTEPH. Serial TAPSE/sPAP may support noninvasive dynamic risk stratification and residual risk assessment during follow-up.

title: Reduction in Right Ventricular Stroke Work Index After Balloon Pulmonary Angioplasty is Associated With Long-Term Prognosis in Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension.
authorString: Ushijima R, Imamura T, Hida Y, Ueno H, Kinugawa K.
abstractText: The prognostic relevance of the relative change in right ventricular stroke work index (RVSWI) after balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) remains uncertain. This retrospective single-center study included 38 patients with CTEPH. Follow-up began at post-BPA catheterization. Relative change in RVSWI (%RVSWI; negative values indicate reduction) and conventional measures were compared using Cox models and direction-fixed C-indices. Bootstrap resampling assessed selection optimism across 14 candidates. RVSWI decreased from 16.96 to 9.83 g·m/m2/beat. During a median 4.1 years, 7 patients reached the composite endpoint of all-cause death or heart failure hospitalization. A smaller reduction was associated with higher risk (hazard ratio 1.24 per 1 percentage-point increase in %RVSWI, 95% confidence interval 1.06-1.44; p = 0.007). %RVSWI had the highest apparent C-index (0.942, 95% confidence interval 0.86-0.99), but its difference from achieved mean pulmonary artery pressure (C-index 0.855) was not statistically distinguishable. %RVSWI ranked first in 62% of bootstrap resamples; the optimism-corrected C-index was 0.922. Component log-ratios were essentially uncorrelated (r = 0.01, 95% confidence interval -0.31 to 0.33). Greater RVSWI reduction after BPA was associated with better prognosis. With seven events, these findings are hypothesis-generating; superiority over conventional measures and the physiological interpretation of the SVI component remain unestablished.

title: Home non-invasive ventilation in chronic respiratory failure: Evidence-based guidelines.
authorString: Khilnani GC, Tiwari P, Mittal S, Dhar R, Christopher DJ, Suri JC, Singh V, Chaudhry D, Nene A, Swarnkar R, Munje R, Koul PA, Ahuja K, Singh PK, Nath M, Mohan A, Hadda V, Parmez AR, Abhiyankar N, Halder I, Suri TM, Gupta M, Bhattacharya A, Kumar R, Ahuja A, Jain N, Chawla R, Samaria JK.

journal.title: Lung India : official organ of Indian Chest Society

abstractText: Home non-invasive ventilation (NIV) is used across a range of causes of chronic respiratory failure, but patient selection and management are disease-specific. These guidelines provide evidence-based recommendations on initiating, titrating, and monitoring long-term home NIV across different disease spectrums. The panel reviewed studies from international databases, relevant guidelines, and reference lists. The panel refined recommendations through two rounds of consensus and graded them using the Indian Chest Society framework. In chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), home NIV is recommended for eligible patients with persistent daytime hypercapnia, including those who remain hypercapnic 2 to 4 weeks after an exacerbation. High-intensity bilevel ventilation should be titrated to achieve a meaningful reduction in arterial carbon dioxide. In neuromuscular disorders, respiratory muscle weakness or hypoventilation warrants timely assessment for NIV, alongside evaluation of interface tolerance and secretion clearance. For stable obesity hypoventilation syndrome with severe obstructive sleep apnoea, continuous positive airway pressure is generally the preferred initial treatment; NIV is appropriate when severe obstructive sleep apnoea is absent or continuous positive airway pressure fails or is not tolerated. The guidelines also address heart failure with sleep-disordered breathing, chest-wall deformity, interstitial lung disease, bronchiectasis, post-tuberculosis lung disease, central hypoventilation syndromes, and palliative care. Across indications, management should include individualised ventilator settings, objective assessment of ventilation, patient and caregiver education, and structured follow-up. Where evidence is limited, recommendations reflect expert consensus and should be applied in the context of patient goals, clinical feasibility, and available resources.

title: Multisource Coronary Artery Fistula Draining Into the Coronary Sinus: Multimodality Imaging and Surgical Repair.
authorString: Trung NQ, Dung LV, Minh Ly NT, Tai MT, Dat BT, Van Diep P, Cuong NN, Linh LT.
abstractText: Coronary artery fistula (CAF) is a rare congenital coronary anomaly. Multisource CAF draining into the coronary sinus is exceptionally uncommon and anatomically complex. A woman presented with progressive exertional dyspnea and right-sided heart failure. Multimodality imaging, including transthoracic echocardiography, coronary computed tomography angiography, and invasive coronary angiography, demonstrated multisource CAFs arising from the right coronary artery and left circumflex artery draining into the coronary sinus with diffuse aneurysmal coronary dilatation. The patient underwent surgical ligation of the dominant right CAF with concomitant tricuspid annuloplasty. Postoperative imaging demonstrated successful closure of the dominant right CAF with thrombus formation within the ligated fistulous tract, whereas the smaller left circumflex artery fistula persisted, and serial follow-up demonstrated clinical improvement. Multimodality imaging is essential for diagnosis, treatment planning, and postoperative surveillance of complex CAF. Surgical repair remains an effective treatment strategy for anatomically complex fistulas associated with significant hemodynamic consequences.

title: Heart Failure Progression in the Setting of Persistent Atrial Fibrillation, Frequent Premature Ventricular Complexes, and Malignancy-Related Limitations to Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy: A Case Report.
authorString: Roger D, Shaker W, Yavari M, Thakur R, Castellani M, Siddiqi Z, Tiotsop M.
abstractText: Persistent atrial fibrillation and frequent premature ventricular complexes may contribute to worsening heart failure, particularly when malignancy limits guideline-directed medical therapy. In patients with progressive ventricular dysfunction and limited pharmacologic options, atrioventricular nodal ablation with cardiac resynchronization therapy-defibrillator implantation may provide durable rate control and support subsequent ventricular functional recovery.

title: Automated carotid artery atherosclerotic inflammation segmentation in PET using MSR-Net.
authorString: Li R, Jha AK, Zheng J, Laforest R, Liu Y, Zayed M, Fraum TJ, Siegel BA, Itani M, Mhlanga JC, Woodard PK.
abstractText: AbstractObjective. To develop an automated method for segmentation and uptake quantification ofcarotid atherosclerotic inflammation on 64Cu-CANF-comb PET while accounting forpartial-volume and tissue-fraction effects.Approach. Synthetic carotid PET images with known fractional-volume ground truth weregenerated by combining MR-derived high-resolution activity maps with GATE MonteCarlo simulation incorporating major PET physical processes and matched to theBiograph mMR acquisition and reconstruction. A two-stage network first localized thecarotid vessel wall from T1-weighted MR and then estimated voxel-wise inflammationfraction from masked PET. Both stages used a multiscale residual (MSR) convolutionalbackbone. Performance was compared with U-Net, Transformer U-Net, DUCK-Net, anditerative Yang partial-volume correction.Main results. In a two-alternative forced-choice study, five nuclear-medicine physiciansidentified real images with 54% accuracy (54/100; Wilson 95% CI 0.44-0.63; exactbinomial p = 0.48). On 184 simulated test slices from five held-out patients, the proposedmethod achieved a weighted DSC of 0.79, compared with 0.73 for U-Net, 0.69 forTransformer U-Net, and 0.75 for DUCK-Net, with corresponding HD values of 1.85, 2.29,2.32, and 2.23 voxels. Patient-cluster bootstrap comparisons favored the proposed methodfor DSC and HD against all three baselines (Holm-corrected p ≤ 0.031). Overall ENRMSEwas 0.24 versus 0.59, 0.68, and 0.59 for the three DL baselines and 0.57 for iterative Yang.In seven patients, corrected SUV showed a positive association with MR-derivedlipid-rich/necrotic core with hemorrhage.Significance. The proposed framework improved carotid PET segmentation and uptakequantification under simulated conditions. The patient analysis is preliminary and requiresexternal validation with biological reference standards before clinical deployment.

title: Effect of randomness and delay in extracellular glucose transportation into cardiac contractility under diabetic conditions.
authorString: Das PN, Ghosh V.

journal.title: Mathematical medicine and biology : a journal of the IMA

abstractText: The present in-silico study incorporates a stochastic framework for GLUT4 recruitment to examine the coupled dynamics of glucose transport and myocardial contractile function. In their previous study, Das et al. (2020) developed a glucose-insulin interaction model incorporating a transportation delay associated with GLUT4-mediated glucose uptake. However, prior evidence suggests that GLUT4 recruitment exhibits stochastic behavior. Accordingly, the present study extends the model by introducing stochastic perturbations into GLUT4-mediated glucose transport. The results indicate that stochasticity constrains parameter recalibration under diabetic conditions. Moreover, in the absence of delay, although the deterministic system attains a steady state, the stochastic counterpart exhibits persistent temporal fluctuations, inducing transient dynamics at the molecular level.

title: Assessment and Reversibility of Hepatic Abnormalities in Heart Failure: Liver in Heart Failure.
authorString: Sack JS, Khan MS, Te HS.
abstractText: Hepatic abnormalities in non-Fontan heart failure result from congestive hepatopathy and hypoperfusion-related ischemic injury, compounded by neurohormonal activation and systemic inflammation. Assessment of liver disease severity is challenging because standard liver biochemistries, serum fibrosis markers, severity score models, elastography, and imaging modalities have limited diagnostic accuracy in congestive hepatopathy, and hepatic fibrosis is often heterogeneous on histology in this population. Management focuses on optimization of cardiac function through medical therapy or mechanical circulatory support. Although liver biochemical abnormalities frequently improve with restoration of cardiac function, histologic reversibility is variable and not consistently observed. In patients with advanced heart failure needing heart transplantation, histologic cirrhosis and/or fibrosis accompanied by portal hypertension may merit consideration of combined heart-liver transplantation, but correlation between fibrosis and clinical outcomes varies. There remains an unmet need for tests that can reliably assess liver disease severity and predict liver outcomes in non-Fontan congestive hepatopathy.

title: Anatomical Variations of Renal Arteries: Clinical, Radiological, and Surgical Considerations.
authorString: Rodinos E, Chrysikos D, Troupis T.
abstractText:
Objective

To synthesize the current knowledge regarding the embryological basis, anatomical classification, imaging characterization, and clinical implications of accessory renal arteries.

Background

Anatomical variations in the renal arteries are common, affecting approximately 20-35% of the population, and have significant implications for clinical outcomes and surgical planning. Accessory renal arteries are usually terminal vessels that serve discrete renal islands with minimal collateral circulation in the body; therefore, their preoperative identification is important. However, there has been no modern synthesis of embryology, imaging, and multidisciplinary clinical treatment for these variations.

Methods

A narrative review of the literature was conducted by searching PubMed and Google Scholar for publications from December 2015 to December 2025. MeSH terms and free-text keywords related to "accessory renal artery," "multiple renal arteries," "renal artery variations," "renal vascular anatomy," "kidney transplantation," "renovascular hypertension," "computed tomography angiography," "magnetic resonance angiography," and "endovascular aortic repair" were used in Boolean combinations. Peer-reviewed original studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and case series were included. Conference abstracts, unpublished data, and non-English publications were excluded.

Discussion

This review addresses the embryological basis and anatomical classification of accessory renal arteries; the diagnostic roles of Doppler ultrasound, computed tomography angiography, and magnetic resonance angiography; and their clinical implications in kidney transplantation, partial nephrectomy, and endovascular aortic repair, including the contested association with renovascular hypertension. Available data suggest that most accessory vessels do not independently cause hypertension, whereas stenosis of larger vessels may be a correctable etiology in selected cases.

Conclusion

Accessory renal arteries have a significant clinical impact, primarily determined by the size of the vessels and the area of the kidney they supply. Preoperative characterization based on modern imaging can be reliable and can help plan and manage surgery for each patient. More prospective research is required to establish evidence-based principles for vessel maintenance and evaluate new technologies in this context.

title: Occult Abdominal Para-Aortic Ectopic Insulinoma Localized by 18F-NOTA-Exendin-4 PET/CT.
authorString: Wan Y, Wang H, Feng L, Zhang W.
abstractText: Solitary ectopic insulinomas without concurrent pancreatic or gastrointestinal lesions are exceedingly rare. We report the 18F-NOTA-exendin-4 PET/CT findings of a solitary ectopic insulinoma in a 68-year-old woman with a 10-year history of recurrent hypoglycemic syncope. Endogenous hyperinsulinemia was confirmed, but conventional imaging and laparoscopic pancreatic exploration were negative. PET/CT revealed a solitary intense focus in the para-abdominal aortic region. Surgical resection confirmed a solitary ectopic insulinoma, and postoperative hypoglycemia resolved. This case highlights the value of 18F-NOTA-exendin-4 PET/CT in identifying occult solitary ectopic insulinomas when conventional imaging and surgical exploration are unrevealing, enabling curative resection.

title: Aortic Dissection Incidentally Detected on PET/CT During Evaluation for Suspected Multiple Myeloma.
authorString: Han J, Zhang L, Yang F.
abstractText: The identification and diagnosis of aortic dissection on PET/CT remain challenging without the use of contrast agents. Such cases are prone to misdiagnosis or being overlooked, particularly when the examination is focused on an unrelated primary clinical objective. We present a case of thoracic aortic dissection that was incidentally detected on initial PET/CT during the further evaluation of suspected multiple myeloma. The FDG-avid lesion was initially mistaken for an esophageal mass, with differential diagnoses including extramedullary plasmacytoma associated with multiple myeloma and primary esophageal neoplasm.

title: Coronary artery disease management in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
authorString: Bujak K, Giacoppo D, Laudani C, Spagnolo M, Mazzone PM, Mauro MS, Cutore L, Di Leo G, Finocchiaro S, Greco A, Capodanno D.

journal.title: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background

The optimal management of coronary artery disease in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains uncertain.

Aims

We aimed to compare clinical outcomes between routine coronary revascularisation and conservative management in patients undergoing TAVI and to assess the relative effectiveness of individual revascularisation strategies by performing a meta-analysis of randomised trials.

Methods

We conducted a pairwise meta-analysis comparing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with conservative treatment and a network meta-analysis comparing the relative effectiveness of individual strategies, including angiography-guided and physiology-guided PCI. The primary outcome was a study-defined composite endpoint of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Secondary endpoints included the individual outcomes of all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, unplanned revascularisation, and major bleeding.

Results

Five trials (N=1,644 patients) were included in the systematic review, and four were included in the primary quantitative synthesis (N=1,476). Compared with conservative treatment, routine PCI was associated with lower risks of MACE (risk ratio [RR] 0.80, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.65-0.98) and unplanned revascularisation (RR 0.30, 95% CI: 0.11-0.83) and an increased risk of major bleeding (RR 1.57, 95% CI: 1.07-2.32). In the network meta-analysis, physiology-guided PCI significantly reduced MACE, stroke, and unplanned revascularisation compared with conservative treatment and ranked highest for all ischaemic outcomes among revascularisation strategies.

Conclusions

Among patients referred for TAVI, routine revascularisation reduces the risk of ischaemic outcomes compared with conservative treatment. In this setting, physiology-guided PCI may be associated with the most favourable efficacy profile across available strategies. (PROSPERO: CRD420261330194).

title: Safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System in acute intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism: the SPIRARE II pivotal trial.
authorString: Sayfo S, Stępniewski J, Gallo V, Rossi JS, Lang IM, Ingrassia J, Rosenberg RD, Amin R, Aggarwal V, Jaber W, Mahfoud F, Kopec G, Toma C, Ii Trial Investigators OBOTS.

journal.title: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background

Percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy can rapidly reduce afterload in acute pulmonary embolism (PE), but catheter stiffness and instability may limit access and prevent effective right ventricle (RV) unloading. The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System with Transforming Fixation (TFX) technology is designed to address current limitations of existing catheter-based systems by separating the flexibility necessary for safe navigation from the support that is essential for procedural control.

Aims

We aimed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System for mechanical aspiration thrombectomy in acute intermediate-risk PE.

Methods

SPIRARE II was a prospective, single-arm, multicentre pivotal investigation conducted at 19 sites in the United States and Europe. Eligible patients had acute PE (≤14 days), a computed tomography angiography-assessed RV to left ventricle (RV/LV) ratio>0.9, and haemodynamic stability (systolic blood pressure ≥90 mmHg). Co-primary endpoints were composite major adverse events (MAE) within 48 hours and core laboratory-assessed RV/LV change from baseline to 48 hours. Prespecified secondary endpoints were collected immediately pre- and post-procedure in all patients including mean pulmonary artery pressure, total pulmonary vascular resistance, and cardiac index.

Results

In 123 patients, the 48-hour composite MAE rate was 2.4% (3/123), meeting the prespecified performance goal (one-sided p<0.0001). The mean RV/LV diameter ratio decreased from 1.44±0.33 at baseline to 1.05±0.21 at 48 hours, a mean reduction of 0.39±0.33, exceeding the prespecified performance goal (p<0.0001).

Conclusions

The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System met its prespecified safety and effectiveness endpoints in acute intermediate-risk PE. TFX delivered precise, stable control with reliable vessel access, enabling consistent right ventricular unloading. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06576427).

title: Early outcomes of transcatheter vacuum-assisted mass extraction in the left heart and the aortic arch.
authorString: Fang JX, O'Neill BP, Frisoli TM, Eng MH, Gonzalez PE, Shimamura J, Ahmad HA, Haidry SA, Giustino G, Jabri A, Ibrahim R, von Bardeleben RS, Gregerson S, Giacaman A, Chiang M, So KC, Lok Lai LK, Lee JC, Zweig B, Fram GK, Wang DD, O'Neill WW, Villablanca PA.

journal.title: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background

Transcatheter vacuum-assisted mass extraction (TVME) in the systemic circulation is increasingly being reported. However, its feasibility, effectiveness, and safety remain poorly defined.

Aims

We sought to investigate the feasibility, effectiveness and safety of TVME in the left heart and aortic arch.

Methods

Consecutive patients from 6 centres in the United States and Canada were included. Feasibility was defined as technically successful mass extraction without unplanned cardiac surgery or intraprocedural mortality. The effectiveness endpoint was feasibility with successful debulking of ≥70% mass volume. The primary safety endpoint was the 30-day composite of procedure-attributable mortality, major cardiac structural complications, major vascular complications, Type 3-4 bleeding, acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and stroke, all according to Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC)-3 definitions. Intraprocedural events were also reported.

Results

A total of 62 consecutive patients were evaluated. Feasibility was reached in 85.5% of patients and effectiveness in 77.4% of patients - except for 11.3% with suboptimal debulking, 3.2% with access-related case abortion, and 8.1% with case cancellation where no mass was found intraprocedurally. The primary safety endpoint occurred in 14.5% of patients, with a procedure-attributable mortality rate of 3.2%. VARC-3 major cardiac structural complications, major vascular complications, Type 3-4 bleeding, ACS, and stroke occurred in 3.2%, 8.1%, 3.2%, 3.2%, and 6.5% of patients, respectively. Intraprocedural events included hypoxia (6.5%), hypotension (9.7%), embolism (3.2%), air embolism (1.6%), and increased mitral regurgitation (6.5%).

Conclusions

TVME in left-sided and aortic arch masses is feasible and demonstrates reasonable effectiveness. However, the considerable rate of safety-related events highlights the need for better case selection and procedural refinement, such as optimal embolic protection.

title: Postdischarge Class-Complete Secondary Prevention Medication Nonadherence After Ischemic Stroke: Overall and Comorbidity-Specific Patterns.
authorString: Li Y, Jiang Y, Zhao Q, Lee WL, Wu L, Chen C.
abstractText:
Objective

This study aimed to evaluate postdischarge class-complete secondary prevention medication nonadherence after ischemic stroke and identify overall and comorbidity-specific factors associated with 180-day nonadherence.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study using prospectively collected follow-up data from a stroke registry, including consecutive patients hospitalized with acute ischemic stroke. Medication use was assessed at discharge, 90 days, and 180 days after discharge. Class-complete discontinuation-that is, discontinuation of at least one of the secondary prevention medication classes prescribed at discharge, including antiplatelet agents, anticoagulants, lipid-lowering medications, antihypertensive medications, and glucose-lowering medications-was the primary outcome. Any-use adherence, defined as continued use of at least one secondary prevention medication class, was used for comparison. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with 180-day class-complete nonadherence, with subgroup analyses among patients with hypertension and diabetes mellitus.

Results

A total of 2549 patients with ischemic stroke were included. At 180 days, 1408 patients (55.2%) had discontinued at least one prescribed secondary prevention medication class, whereas only 738 (29.0%) had discontinued all prescribed classes; 1141 (44.8%) continued every class prescribed at discharge. Class-complete adherence declined from 59.4% at 90 days to 44.8% at 180 days, whereas any-use adherence was 85.9% and 71.0%, respectively. Each additional discharge medication class was associated with higher odds of 180-day class-complete nonadherence in a prespecified multivariable model (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 1.50; 95% CI, 1.27-1.79). Cardioembolism (OR, 2.11; 95% CI, 1.37-3.26), dyslipidemia (OR, 1.50; 95% CI, 1.09-2.07), and large-artery atherosclerosis (OR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.03-1.49) were also associated with nonadherence; hypertension was of borderline significance (OR, 1.23; 95% CI, 0.99-1.54; P = 0.067). In subgroup analyses, the association with number of discharge medication classes was similar across the hypertension and diabetes mellitus subgroups, with no evidence of effect modification (P for interaction = 0.32 and 0.67), whereas the association with large-artery atherosclerosis was stronger among patients with hypertension (OR, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.08-1.73) or diabetes mellitus (OR, 1.43; 95% CI, 1.10-1.87) than among those without (P for interaction = 0.036 and 0.009, respectively).

Conclusion

Class-complete medication nonadherence was common within 180 days after ischemic stroke discharge and often reflected partial discontinuation rather than complete cessation of secondary prevention therapy. Medication-class-specific follow-up may help identify incomplete regimen continuation and guide targeted support for patients with greater treatment complexity, atherosclerotic stroke mechanisms, or chronic vascular comorbidities.

title: Patient-Level Perivascular Adipose Tissue Density Aggregation and Plaque Progression: Plaque-Free vs Plaque-Adjacent Segments.
authorString: Lee SE, Sung JM, Andreini D, Al-Mallah MH, Budoff MJ, Cademartiri F, Chinnaiyan K, Choi JH, Chun EJ, Conte E, Gottlieb I, Hadamitzky M, Kim YJ, Lee BK, Leipsic JA, Maffei E, Marques H, de Araújo Gonçalves P, Pontone G, Stone PH, Virmani R, Narula J, Shaw LJ, Bax JJ, Lin FY, Min JK, Chang HJ.
abstractText:
Background

Perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) density on coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA) reflects pericoronary inflammation, but measurements adjacent to existing plaques may be confounded by local inflammatory signaling from the plaque itself-a form of reverse causation. Whether systematically comparing patient-level PVAT aggregation approaches (including measurements restricted to plaque-free segments) can identify a more robust inflammatory biomarker has not been evaluated.

Objectives

The authors aimed to compare the predictive performance of 4 patient-level PVAT aggregation approaches for coronary plaque progression.

Methods

From the PARADIGM serial coronary CTA registry, 412 patients with baseline coronary plaque who underwent serial coronary CTA at identical tube voltages were included (mean age: 61.1 ± 9.3 years; 61.7% male; mean interval: 3.2 ± 1.2 years). Four patient-level PVAT measures were compared: proximal right coronary artery (pRCA), whole-coronary, plaque-free, and plaque PVAT. Multivariable regression models were constructed for annualized plaque volume (PV) progression with adjustment for clinical risk factors and imaging covariates.

Results

Annualized increases in pRCA PVAT (β = 0.804; P = 0.033), whole-coronary PVAT (β = 1.142; P = 0.022), and plaque-free PVAT (β = 1.419; P = 0.007) were each independently associated with total PV progression, whereas plaque PVAT did not reach significance (β = 0.755; P = 0.083). For noncalcified PV progression, plaque-free PVAT was the only significant measure (β = 1.086; P = 0.026). None of the 4 baseline PVAT measures were significantly associated with plaque progression (all P > 0.50). Pairwise comparisons revealed no significant differences among the 4 measures.

Conclusions

Changes in pRCA, whole-coronary, and plaque-free PVAT were each independently associated with total PV progression. For noncalcified PV progression, plaque-free PVAT change was the only significant measure. (Progression of AtheRosclerotic PlAque DetermIned by Computed TomoGraphic Angiography Imaging [PARADIGM]; NCT02803411).

title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals renal ER stress in alcohol-associated kidney injury.
authorString: Harris PS, McGinnis CD, Trujillo MN, Galligan JJ, Orlicky DJ, Saba LM, Fritz KS.
abstractText: Alcohol misuse damages numerous organs, including the liver, heart, brain, and pancreas. The kidney remains a severely understudied target of alcohol-induced injury despite renal injury being commonly observed in end-stage alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) patients. A 6-week murine ethanol (1-6% v/v) model for early-stage ALD combined with carbon tetrachloride (CCl<sub>4</sub>) treatment was utilized to reveal mechanisms of renal injury. This paradigm yields elevated kidney damage markers when compared to ethanol consumption alone, including elevated urinary KIM-1 in 3 weeks. Hypothesis-generating tissue spatial analysis was used to explore ethanol-related transcriptomic alterations across kidney morphology. Using a publicly available scRNA-seq dataset, the predominant cell-type specific differences were identified and allowed for the generation of spatially resolved gene clusters. Ethanol + CCl<sub>4</sub> increased kidney injury marker gene expression in proximal tubule cells, signifying extensive damage. Overall, a decrease in expression of ethanol metabolizing genes was localized to the renal cortex. Genes associated with the unfolded protein response (UPR) were induced across the kidney and were morphologically associated throughout the nephron. Key mRNAs (Hspa5, Hsp90b1, Ndrg1) and ribosomal transcripts were altered due to ethanol metabolism across proximal tubules. Furthermore, epigenetic alterations in regulatory marks of lysine acetylation or trimethylation are associated with the combination treatment. Collectively, the application of tissue spatial transcriptomics to a well-defined model of alcohol toxicity reveals dynamic morphologic changes in gene expression across renal cell types due to ethanol. Our results indicate ER stress and the UPR are significantly impacted by ethanol metabolism throughout proximal tubules, associating with ethanol-induced renal dysfunction.

title: The pathogenic role of high-titer anti-Ro52 antibodies in neonatal lupus erythematosus: insights from a 9 case series.
authorString: Cheng S, Jiang Y, Zhang S, Huang J, Wang X, Xie H, Wang M.
abstractText:
Background

Neonatal Lupus Erythematosus (NLE) is a rare acquired autoimmune disease caused by the transplacental transfer of maternal anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB antibodies. Despite the high prevalence of these antibodies in mothers with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) and Sjögren's Syndrome (SS), the clinical manifestations in neonates are highly heterogeneous, ranging from transient cutaneous lesions to life-threatening congenital heart block (CHB).

Methods

This study analyzed a case series of nine mother-infant pairs diagnosed with NLE. We integrated clinical outcomes, maternal serological profiles (including quantitative anti-Ro52, Ro60, and La titers), and pharmacological interventions to explore the determinants of disease severity and organ-specific manifestations.

Results

Among the nine mothers, six (66.7%) had Sjögren's syndrome and three (33.3%) had systemic lupus erythematosus, including two with secondary antiphospholipid syndrome. Notably, 88.9% of mothers were diagnosed with autoimmune disease during or after the affected pregnancy. All mothers demonstrated antinuclear antibody positivity and were uniformly positive for anti-SSA/Ro, anti-SSB/La, and anti-Ro52 antibodies. Cardiac involvement occurred in three pregnancies, including recurrent complete CHB leading to pregnancy termination in one mother. One fetus with second-degree atrioventricular block received prompt dexamethasone therapy and achieved successful reversal of conduction abnormalities. Cutaneous manifestations were observed in five neonates, while hematologic involvement, primarily thrombocytopenia and anemia, occurred in four cases. Maternal hypocomplementemia and elevated inflammatory markers appeared to be associated with more severe fetal outcomes.

Conclusion

All nine mothers (100%) tested positive for high-titer anti-Ro52 antibodies, a finding consistent with the proposed role of anti-Ro52 as a risk biomarker for NLE. Intensive fetal echocardiographic surveillance between 16 and 26 weeks of gestation is vital to capture the critical window of low-degree conduction block, where synergistic immunomodulation with dexamethasone can reverse fetal heart block prior to irreversible nodal fibrosis. NLE serves as an early warning sign of occult maternal autoimmune disease, requiring long-term maternal follow-up.

title: Microcirculatory Alterations and Endothelial Glycocalyx in Fontan Circulation: Association With Central Venous Pressure.
authorString: Shiraishi M, Izumi G, Saito H.
abstractText:
Objective

Fontan circulation is characterized by chronically elevated central venous pressure (CVP) and reduced cardiac output, which may adversely affect the systemic microcirculation. We investigated whether Fontan circulation is associated with alterations of the endothelial glycocalyx.

Methods

Forty-four patients with congenital heart disease undergoing postoperative endothelial glycocalyx evaluation were included. The perfused boundary region (PBR), an inverse indicator of glycocalyx dimensions, was measured noninvasively using GlycoCheck. PBR was compared between patients with Fontan and biventricular circulation, and its relationship with CVP was evaluated.

Results

Fourteen patients had Fontan circulation, including three with bidirectional Glenn circulation, and 30 had biventricular circulation. PBR was significantly higher in patients with Fontan circulation than in those with biventricular circulation (2.07 ± 0.15 vs. 1.72 ± 0.17 μm, p < 0.0001). CVP was also significantly higher in the Fontan group (13.0 ± 2.2 vs. 7.1 ± 2.8 mmHg, p < 0.0001). PBR was positively correlated with CVP (r = 0.58, p < 0.0001).

Conclusions

Fontan circulation is associated with an increased PBR, suggesting alterations of the endothelial glycocalyx. The association between PBR and CVP suggests that chronic venous hypertension may be associated with systemic microcirculatory alterations in Fontan circulation.

title: Human induced pluripotent stem cells and organoid models in space for investigating severe pediatric metabolic and congenital disorders.
authorString: Benedetti S, Štupica H, Zuccotti GV, Weissig V, Marotta D, Pappone C, Tull A, Rubins KH, Beheshti A, Mason CE, Ferraro S.
abstractText: As biomedical research in space expands, microgravity and spaceflight-associated stressors are revealing cellular responses that may provide new insights into rare and severe metabolic and congenital disorders. Human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and organoids are particularly promising as they enable patient-specific modelling in the space environment. In this review, we examine the current literature on space-based hiPSC experimental models, highlighting their relevance to pediatric disorders with well-defined genetic backgrounds, namely mitochondrial diseases and congenital heart disorders. We summarize the evidence that spaceflight conditions alter mitochondrial function, cytoskeletal organization, oxidative stress, calcium handling, cellular maturation, and gene expression, and discuss how these responses may converge with metabolic disease-associated phenotypes. We highlight both adaptive and pathological responses reported in space-based hiPSC studies and identify key experimental and mechanistic gaps. Finally, we consider how advances in stem cell technologies and space-based biomedical research may enable the development of personalized, patient-specific disease models and therapeutics for rare pediatric diseases, ultimately accelerating translational discovery and clinical innovation.

title: The Diverse Clinical Spectrum of Noonan Syndrome in Pediatric Endocrinology: From Classical to Atypical Phenotypes.
authorString: Aszkiełowicz S, Łupińska A, Zygmunt A, Stawerska R.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Noonan syndrome (NS) is characterized by marked phenotypic variability. Although the classical phenotype includes short stature, craniofacial dysmorphism, skeletal abnormalities, and congenital heart defects, some patients present with subtle or atypical manifestations, making clinical recognition challenging. Methods: This retrospective case series included six pediatric patients with molecularly confirmed NS managed at the Department of Endocrinology and Metabolic Diseases, Polish Mother's Memorial Hospital-Research Institute, Lodz, Poland. Medical records were reviewed for auxological data, phenotypic features, endocrine and skeletal assessment, cardiovascular findings, associated conditions, and multidisciplinary management. The aim of this study was to characterize the phenotypic diversity of NS in pediatric endocrine practice, with particular emphasis on growth patterns, endocrine and skeletal manifestations, and atypical clinical presentations. Results: The six patients demonstrated markedly heterogeneous clinical presentations. One boy exhibited the classical phenotype with severe short stature and pulmonary valve stenosis, whereas a girl with typical NS features maintained relatively preserved growth around the 3rd percentile. Another patient presented with progressive resorption of permanent incisor roots and a coexisting pathogenic NBN variant. A boy with LZTR1-associated NS and Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY) demonstrated a blended phenotype and height between the 25th and 50th percentiles. Two girls lacked characteristic NS dysmorphism and presented predominantly with growth impairment, accompanied by markedly low bone mass in one case and a prolonged diagnostic pathway in the other. GH deficiency was not identified in the evaluated patients, and rhGH therapy was initiated in three patients. Conclusions: NS encompasses a broad clinical spectrum, ranging from classical phenotypes to atypical presentations dominated by growth, skeletal, or dental abnormalities. Neither the absence of characteristic dysmorphism nor relatively preserved growth excludes the diagnosis, while coexisting genetic conditions may further modify the phenotype. Awareness of this heterogeneity is essential for appropriate recognition and individualized multidisciplinary care. In selected children with otherwise unexplained growth or atypical clinical findings, consideration of NS and genetic evaluation may help establish a unifying diagnosis and potentially shorten the diagnostic pathway.
