title: Heart-Liver Interactions: Pathophysiology and Diagnosis of Hypoxic Hepatitis, Congestive Hepatopathy, and Cirrhotic Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Popovic D, Blagojevic N, Dragasevic Vucicevic S, Dragovic M, Blagojevic D, Glisic T, Mijac D, Stojkovic-Lalosevic M, Filipovic B, Bogdanovic J, Bogdanovic L, Nikolic N, Stojanovic M.
abstractText: The heart and liver are closely interconnected through complex hemodynamic, neurohumoral, inflammatory, and metabolic mechanisms. Dysfunction of either organ may adversely affect the other, giving rise to a broad spectrum of cardiohepatic disorders with important diagnostic and prognostic implications. This narrative review is based on a literature search strategy of PubMed and the Web of Science Core Collection covering publications from January 2000 through June 2026, with a focus on hypoxic hepatitis, congestive hepatopathy, and cirrhotic cardiomyopathy. Cardiac diseases may induce liver injury through acute hypoperfusion or chronic venous congestion, resulting in distinct clinical entities characterized by different pathophysiological mechanisms, laboratory findings, imaging features, and therapeutic approaches. Conversely, advanced liver disease may be associated with impaired cardiovascular function, including cirrhotic cardiomyopathy, a condition that frequently remains clinically silent until physiological or therapeutic stress unmasks impaired cardiac reserve. Recent advances in multimodal imaging, including echocardiography with myocardial deformation analysis, abdominal ultrasonography with Doppler evaluation, elastography, computed tomography, and cardiac magnetic resonance, together with emerging biomarkers, have provided additional tools for the recognition and characterization of these disorders, although the clinical value of some newer techniques and biomarkers remains under investigation. Nevertheless, differentiating congestion-related liver injury from progressive fibrosis and identifying subclinical cardiac dysfunction remain important clinical challenges. A comprehensive understanding of the bidirectional interactions between the heart and liver is important for timely diagnosis, accurate risk stratification, and appropriate management. Future studies should focus on standardized diagnostic pathways, validation of novel imaging techniques and biomarkers, and multidisciplinary strategies that may improve outcomes in patients with complex cardiohepatic disease.

title: Transition from paediatric to adult congenital heart disease care in Central and South-Eastern Europe: current practices and opportunities for improvement.
authorString: Arvanitaki A, Prokšelj K, Šimkova I, Vranešić II, Strenge A, Komar M, Lipczynska M, Kaneva A, Gumbiene L, Antonova P, Balint HO, Coman IM, Sinan UY, Caruana M, Nikolic A, Maser M, Panfile E, Bartsota M, Kostovska ES, Giannakoulas G, Kovačević-Preradović T, Bajraktari G, Kratunkov P, Tomkiewicz-Pajak L, Klymyshyn Y, Lebid I, Gatzoulis MA, Brida M.
abstractText:
Aims

Transition from paediatric to adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) care is a critical determinant of lifelong disease management for individuals with congenital heart disease (CHD). However, structured transition programmes remain inconsistently implemented, and data are lacking on current practices in Central and South-Eastern European (CESEE) countries. This study aimed to evaluate existing transition practices across CESEE and to identify opportunities to improve the development and implementation of structured programmes.

Methods and results

An online questionnaire was distributed to centres involved in CHD care across CESEE countries. The survey assessed centre characteristics, transition services, transfer processes, and development priorities. Responses from 60 healthcare CHD professionals representing 43 centres in 21 countries were analysed. A formal ACHD service was reported in 29 (67%) of 43 centres, mostly established after the year 2000 (72%), caring for a median of 1500 (interquartile range 782-4000) patients with ACHD. Overall, only 10 (23%) centres reported having a formal transition programme. Transition counselling was typically delivered in a single outpatient visit, commonly involving paediatric and adult CHD physicians, but rarely nurses and psychosocial professionals (20% each). Structured transfer processes were inconsistently implemented, and only half of the centres monitored non-attendance at initial adult visits. In centres without formal programmes, informal counselling largely occurred at the final paediatric or first adult visit, relying on patient self-referral, and lacking follow-up.

Conclusion

Formal transition programmes remain limited across CESEE ACHD centres. Standardized clear pathways, investment in dedicated transition clinics, and trained workforce are needed to improve continuity of care for adolescents with CHD.

title: Competing Hemodynamic Goals During Hepatectomy in Patients with Fontan Circulation: A Systematic Review of Case Reports.
authorString: Minote T, Yonezawa H, Kinoshita M, Tanaka K.

journal.title: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia

abstractText:
Objectives

To synthesize available evidence on perioperative management and clinical outcomes of hepatectomy in patients with Fontan circulation, focusing on hemodynamic strategies and surgical safety.

Design

A systematic review of case reports and case series.

Settings

Published studies were identified through databases (PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, ICHUSHI, and CiNii Research).

Participants

Thirty-one patients from 28 studies underwent hepatectomy after the Fontan procedure.

Interventions

Open or laparoscopic hepatectomy, primarily for hepatocellular carcinoma in the setting of Fontan-associated liver disease.

Measurements and main results

All patients had stable Fontan physiology, and no perioperative mortality was reported. Preoperative baseline central venous pressure (CVP) ranged from 10 to 15 mmHg. Intraoperative management consistently favored a baseline-CVP strategy over conventional low-CVP targets. Laparoscopic approaches uniformly used low-pressure pneumoperitoneum below baseline-CVP levels. The Pringle maneuver was well tolerated; however, inferior vena cava clamping was associated with significant hypotension. The median blood loss was 1,106 mL (range 10-4,130 mL). Congestion-related complications, including ascites, pleural effusion, heart failure, and unspecified fluid retention, were most commonly reported postoperatively.

Conclusion

Hepatectomy appears feasible in carefully selected patients with stable Fontan circulation. Practical perioperative considerations summarized from reported patterns include maintaining CVP near baseline, minimizing increases in pulmonary vascular resistance, and keeping pneumoperitoneum pressure below baseline CVP during laparoscopic surgery. However, hepatectomy-specific risk stratification has yet to be established, and optimal perioperative management of patients with impaired Fontan physiology remains uncertain. A critical knowledge gap remains regarding hemostatic approaches that optimize bleeding control while preserving the Fontan circulation.

title: Epilepsy Mechanisms in Down Syndrome: Genetic and Pathophysiological Perspectives Across the Lifespan.
authorString: Stafstrom CE, Shao LR.
abstractText: Down syndrome (trisomy 21) is the most common genetic cause of intellectual disability. Seizures are a frequent comorbidity in individuals with Down syndrome and can exert significant negative consequences on cognitive capacity and quality of life. In Down syndrome, seizures cluster at two extremes of the lifespan. In the first year of life, infantile epileptic spasms syndrome affects 5-10% of children with Down syndrome. The second peak occurs after age 30 years, when myoclonic seizures appear at the time of onset of Down syndrome-related dementia of the Alzheimer type (late-onset myoclonic epilepsy in Down syndrome or LOMEDS). While epilepsy at these two disparate time points has been long recognized in the Down syndrome population, the mechanisms underlying seizure pathogenesis have not been studied in detail. For example, it is not known whether the brain developmental abnormalities that characterize Down syndrome are primarily responsible for the epilepsies or whether distinct mechanisms underlie seizures at the two ages. This narrative review addresses possible mechanisms of seizure propensity across the lifespan, with special reference to potential age-specific treatments.

title: Perioperative Management for Placement of Patent Ductus Arteriosus Stents in Infants With Ductal-Dependent Pulmonary Circulation.
authorString: Hamilton ARL, Yuki K, Staffa SJ, Odegard KC.

journal.title: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia

abstractText:
Objectives

Stenting of the patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) offers a minimally invasive alternative to the modified Blalock-Thomas-Taussig shunt in infants with ductal-dependent pulmonary blood flow. This study reviews the periprocedural management of infants undergoing ductal stenting in the cardiac catheterization laboratory.

Design

A retrospective single-center review.

Setting

Quaternary children's hospital.

Participants

Infants receiving PDA stents in the cardiac catheterization laboratory from 2018 to 2021 were included.

Interventions

None.

Measurements and main results

Sixty-eight patients were included; median age was 5 days [1-62]; 95.6% (65/68) were neonates and 23.5% (16/68) premature. Pulmonary atresia with intact ventricular septum was the most common cardiac diagnosis (n = 23, 33.8%); 22.1% (15/68) presented with a syndrome and 35.3% (24/68) with noncardiac comorbidities. In total, 39.7% (27/68) developed intraoperative events. Median time to extubation was 19.4 hours [3.2-372.5].

Conclusions

Infants with ductal-dependent pulmonary blood flow undergoing ductal stenting may present with a wide range of challenges in the perioperative period. Meticulous care and interdisciplinary coordination are required to optimize the outcomes for this particularly vulnerable patient group.

title: Incremental Anatomical Value of CT Angiography Beyond Echocardiography in the Preoperative Assessment of Pediatric Conotruncal Anomalies: A Surgical Correlation Study.
authorString: Kangel D, Çevlik B, Karimov E, Oğuz AS, Sağlam S, Tüzün B, Hatemi AC, Baş S, Öztürk E.
abstractText: Background: Conotruncal anomalies frequently involve extracardiac vascular structures that are critical for surgical planning yet incompletely assessed by transthoracic echocardiography (TTE). We evaluated the incremental diagnostic value of CT angiography (CTA) beyond TTE using intraoperative findings as the reference standard. Methods: In this single-center retrospective study, 239 children who underwent surgical repair of a conotruncal anomaly and had both preoperative TTE and CTA were analyzed. The incremental contribution of CTA was graded as none, minor, or major by two independent reviewers. Diagnostic performance of each modality was compared with operative findings for coronary artery anomalies, right aortic arch, aortic arch hypoplasia, interrupted aortic arch, and pulmonary artery atresia, non-confluence, and hypoplasia. Results: CTA provided incremental information beyond TTE in 232 patients (97.1%), classified as major in 51.9% and minor in 45.2%; interobserver agreement was almost perfect (quadratic-weighted κ = 0.825). CTA was superior for coronary artery anomalies (sensitivity 91.7% vs. 50.0%), branch pulmonary artery hypoplasia (97.3% vs. 89.3%), and aortic arch hypoplasia (100% vs. 87.5%; all p < 0.05), and identified aortopulmonary collaterals and a persistent left superior vena cava more frequently than TTE. The two modalities performed comparably for aortic arch sidedness and interrupted aortic arch, and pulmonary atresia. Conclusions: CTA provides additional, operatively confirmed anatomical information beyond TTE in the majority of children with conotruncal anomalies, with the greatest value for extracardiac vascular anatomy. Rather than replacing echocardiography, CTA should be regarded as a complementary modality that refines preoperative anatomical assessment.

title: Collaborative Multidisciplinary Assessment of Performance: A Development Guide for Pediatric Heart Centers.
authorString: L'Heureux TE, McGlinchey AM, Torres SM, Hancock Friesen CL.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Jt Comm J Qual Patient Saf
journal.title: Joint Commission journal on quality and patient safety
journal.isoabbreviation: Jt Comm J Qual Patient Saf

abstractText: In July 2023 the Criss Heart Center at Children's Nebraska launched weekly Collaborative Multidisciplinary Assessment of Performance Rounds (CMAP) as part of a structured, prospective Safety Management System framework. CMAP are designed to facilitate transparent, timely, and multidisciplinary evaluation of patient outcomes following pediatric heart surgery. This initiative uses real-time data from the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Congenital Heart Surgery Database to create plots of each surgical patient's journey of risk-versus-time, from surgery through discharge, which are presented at weekly one-hour rounds. The ultimate goal of CMAP is to improve team performance and enhance patient outcomes.

title: Lung Ultrasound in Children: Principles, Techniques, and Clinical Applications.
authorString: Di Sarno L, Caroselli A, Pansini V, Capossela L, Ferretti S, Clemente A, Musolino AM, Villani A, Chiaretti A, Gatto A.
abstractText: Lung ultrasound (LUS) has become established as a pivotal, non-ionizing imaging modality within pediatric medicine, facilitating expedited, point-of-care evaluation of diverse respiratory pathologies while eliminating patient exposure to harmful radiation. This narrative review summarizes contemporary clinical evidence regarding LUS and discusses its current utilization within pediatric medicine, focusing on fundamental physics, acoustic artifacts, standardized scanning protocols, and primary clinical indications. LUS effectively detects and characterizes pleural effusion, pulmonary consolidation, interstitial syndromes, and pneumothorax, demonstrating diagnostic performance comparable to chest radiography across numerous clinical settings while offering highly advantageous utility within diverse point-of-care clinical environments. Educational research indicates that proficiency in LUS is attainable relatively rapidly, though mastery necessitates a defined learning curve and standardized training. Consequently, LUS serves as a powerful adjunct to physical examinations in pediatrics, enhancing diagnostic precision, guiding interventions, and facilitating sequential monitoring whilst minimizing cumulative radiation. Future pediatric-focused research remains essential to refine standardized protocols, validate quantitative assessment instruments, and integrate novel technologies into clinical practice.

title: Anterior Spinal Artery Aneurysms Associated with Coarctation of the Aorta: A Focused Narrative Review with an Illustrative Case.
authorString: Park DS, Chun YI, Roh HG, Park JJ, Jeon YS.
abstractText: Anterior spinal artery (ASA) aneurysms are rare causes of subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), and coarctation of the aorta (CoA) may recruit the spinal arterial circulation into a high-flow collateral network. We report the case of a 58-year-old woman who was resuscitated after pulseless electrical activity arrest. Noncontrast CT demonstrated SAH concentrated in the cervical spinal canal with limited intracranial extension. Cervically extended CT angiography identified a C5-6 ventral spinal aneurysm, severe thoracic CoA with extensive collateralization, and diffuse left subclavian artery hypoplasia. Digital subtraction angiography confirmed the presence of a multilobulated sidewall ASA aneurysm supplied by an artery of the cervical enlargement arising directly from the subclavian artery. Selective coil embolization achieved complete aneurysm occlusion with preservation of the parent artery; this was followed by C5-6 laminectomy and posterior arthrodesis the next day. At approximately 1 year, the patient had regained left-sided motor function, whereas severe right-sided weakness and wheelchair dependence persisted. A focused PubMed/MEDLINE review identified eight well-characterized previously published cases that included sufficient data for detailed tabulation of both a spinal arterial aneurysm and CoA. CoA-associated lesions clustered in the cervical and upper thoracic regions and were managed microsurgically, endovascularly, or conservatively, with no comparative evidence favoring one approach. Spinal-predominant SAH should raise suspicion for a spinal vascular source and prompt consideration of cervical vascular imaging. When enlarged spinal or systemic collateral vessels are identified, assessment of the thoracic aorta may also be considered.

title: Predictors and Factors Associated With Delayed Primary Cleft Surgery in Bangladesh.
authorString: Ghosh TP, Dhar LK, Bithi DD, Hossain SA, Ahmed TT, Jahan I, Khan MRK.
abstractText: Background Delayed primary cleft surgery remains a major challenge in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where barriers to timely access coexist with medically necessary postponements. Understanding factors associated with delayed surgery and the relative contribution of presentation-related and medical reasons may help improve comprehensive cleft care. This study aimed to identify predictors of delayed primary cleft surgery, characterize the distribution of reasons for surgical delay, and evaluate factors associated with delayed presentation among patients treated in a comprehensive cleft care program in Bangladesh. Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery (NIBPS), Dhaka, Bangladesh. Medical records of patients undergoing primary cleft surgery between January 2016 and December 2020 were reviewed. Of 792 records screened, 424 met the eligibility criteria after exclusion of secondary or revision procedures, syndromic clefts, and incomplete records. Delayed primary surgery was operationally defined as primary cleft lip repair performed after 9 months of age or primary cleft palate repair performed after 18 months of age, according to predefined study criteria. Demographic and clinical variables were analyzed using univariate and multivariable binary logistic regression to identify factors associated with delayed primary surgery. A secondary multivariable analysis evaluated factors associated with operationally defined delayed presentation. Six prespecified predictor variables were included in the multivariable models. Results Among 424 patients, 132 (31.1%) underwent delayed primary cleft surgery. Operationally defined delayed presentation was the most frequently identified reason for delayed surgery, accounting for 70 (53.0%) delayed cases, followed by congenital heart disease (16.7%), anaemia (12.1%), and other causes (18.2%). In multivariable analysis, urban residence was independently associated with lower odds of delayed primary surgery compared with rural residence (adjusted OR 0.642, 95% CI 0.418-0.988; p=0.044), whereas congenital heart disease was associated with higher odds of delayed primary surgery (adjusted OR 2.720, 95% CI 1.424-5.197; p=0.002). For delayed presentation, congenital heart disease was independently associated with lower odds of delayed presentation (adjusted OR 0.205, 95% CI 0.048-0.876; p=0.032). Residence, gender, cleft phenotype, other congenital anomalies, and anaemia were not significantly associated with delayed presentation. Conclusion Nearly one-third of patients experienced delayed primary cleft surgery, with delayed presentation being the most frequent documented contributor. Rural residence and congenital heart disease were independently associated with delayed primary surgery, whereas residence was not independently associated with delayed presentation. Congenital heart disease was independently associated with lower odds of delayed presentation, a finding that should be interpreted cautiously. These findings highlight the need to distinguish potentially preventable access-related delays from medically indicated postponements when planning strategies to improve timely cleft care.

title: Minimally Invasive Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting for Predominantly Multivessel Coronary Artery Disease: Early Perioperative Outcomes of 149 Patients.
authorString: Khan D, Zehri AA, Altaf R.
abstractText: Background Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS-CABG) has evolved from single-vessel revascularization to multivessel surgery without median sternotomy. Although favorable outcomes have been reported, experience remains concentrated in specialized centers. This study evaluated the demographic, operative, and early postoperative characteristics of patients undergoing MICS-CABG, off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OP-CABG) at a single institution. Methods This retrospective observational study included 149 CABG/OPCAB procedures identified from an institutional database of 186 cardiac surgical records. Demographics, cardiovascular risk factors, operative details, number of grafts, cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) and cross-clamp times, postoperative ventilation, chest drainage, transfusion requirements, and documented complications were analyzed. Continuous variables were summarized as mean ± standard deviation and median with interquartile range (IQR), and categorical variables as frequencies and percentages. Missing data were not imputed. Results The mean age was 57.8 ± 9.5 years; 139 (93.3%) patients were men. Diabetes mellitus was present in 86 patients (57.7%), hypertension in 100 (67.1%), and tobacco exposure in 65 (43.6%). Procedures included eight one-graft, 41 two-graft, 86 three-graft, and 13 four-graft operations; one procedure lacked standardized graft documentation. Overall, 140/149 (94.0%) procedures had two or more explicitly coded grafts. CPB data were available for 137 patients, with a mean duration of 170.2 ± 37.4 minutes and a median of 168 minutes (IQR: 148-190). Mean cross-clamp time was 94.6 ± 30.5 minutes. Ventilation data were available for 146 patients, with a mean duration of 7.6 ± 4.4 hours and a median of six hours (IQR: 4-11). Chest drainage was documented in 134 patients, with a mean of 899 ± 510 mL. Early postoperative outcomes included conversion to sternotomy in nine patients (6.0%), return to the operating room for bleeding in nine (6.0%), stroke in 3 (2.0%), respiratory insufficiency in two (1.3%), new-onset atrial fibrillation in 36 (24.2%), and 30-day or in-hospital mortality in three (2.0%). Outcome-specific denominators were based on the number of patients for whom the corresponding variable was available. Conclusion This institutional experience demonstrates the feasibility of minimally invasive coronary surgery for predominantly multivessel revascularization. Most procedures involved two or more grafts, with three-graft surgery being the most common. Postoperative ventilation was generally short; however, incomplete complication and transfusion documentation limits interpretation of other perioperative outcomes. Prospective standardized data collection and comparative studies with conventional CABG are warranted.

title: Microbiological aetiology of paediatric ventilator-associated pneumonia and risk factors for carbapenem-resistant acinetobacter and <i>Pseudomonas</i> in a tertiary-care hospital in Thailand.
authorString: Chruakanchana N, Chantasrisawad N, Horapong W, Anugulruengkitt S.
abstractText:
Background

Paediatric ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) worsens outcomes and mortality. Characterizing local microbiology and resistance patterns is crucial for empirical therapy and guiding targeted infection prevention and control.

Objective

This study aimed to determine the aetiology of VAP, identify risk factors associated with VAP caused by carbapenem-resistant (CR) Acinetobacter and Pseudomonas, and assess the clinical burden and outcomes of VAP in paediatric patients.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective study of patients under 18 years of age diagnosed with VAP between January 2022 and December 2024, using Centres for Disease Control and Prevention/National Healthcare Safety Network (CDC/NHSN) surveillance criteria. Data including demographics, microbiology, and outcomes were retrieved from electronic medical records. Risk factors for CR-VAP were assessed using logistic regression.

Results

A total of 71 VAP patients with 95 episodes, were analysed (median age: 7.1 months [interquartile range {IQR}, 2-63]; 49% male). The VAP incidence rate showed a decreasing trend (9.1 to 4.7 per 1000 ventilator-days, 2022-2024). The median time to VAP onset was 25 days (IQR, 13-51) postintubation. The predominant isolated pathogens were Gram-negative bacteria, specifically Acinetobacter baumannii (22%; 64% CR), Pseudomonas aeruginosa (19%; 56% CR), and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia (19%). Staphylococcus aureus (8%; 21% Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus [MRSA]) was the most common Gram-positive isolate. Thirteen patients (18%) experienced multiple VAP episodes. The overall 90-day mortality rate was 24%. Prolonged hospitalization was linked to carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii (CRAB) (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 4.3; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.36-13.61; P = 0.013), while prolonged intubation was associated with carbapenem-resistant P. aeruginosa (CRPA) (aOR, 6.61; 95% CI, 1.42-30.85; P = 0.016).

Conclusion

VAP remains a challenge in the paediatric setting, characterized by a high prevalence of multi-drug-resistant pathogens, particularly CR Acinetobacter and Pseudomonas. Continued surveillance, antimicrobial stewardship, and intensified prevention are essential to reduce VAP burden and improve outcomes.

title: Adult Presentation of a Large Congenital Pulmonary Airway Malformation Discovered After Traumatic Rib Fractures.
authorString: Hranec B, Hudson L, Khouzam M, Hensley JW, Layish D, Khouzam N.
abstractText: Congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM) is a rare developmental lung lesion that is usually identified prenatally or in early childhood, and adult presentations are uncommon. A 44-year-old woman presented after a fall with right-sided chest pain and dyspnea. CT chest revealed nondisplaced fractures of the right seventh through ninth ribs and incidentally identified a large multilocular cystic lesion in the right lower lobe consistent with CPAM, unchanged from imaging performed 15 years earlier. Pulmonary function testing demonstrated mild small-airway dysfunction, air trapping, and reduced diffusing capacity without restrictive physiology. Given the lesion's size and potential risk for infection or malignant transformation, the patient underwent flexible bronchoscopy followed by right muscle-sparing thoracotomy with right lower lobectomy and thoracic lymphadenectomy. Intraoperative findings included dense vascular adhesions and distorted tissue planes. The postoperative course was uncomplicated. Pathology confirmed a benign cystic congenital pulmonary lesion without malignancy. This case highlights an uncommon adult presentation of long-standing CPAM incidental discovery and underscores that radiographic stability does not exclude clinically significant disease requiring surgical management.

title: Multimodal imaging in discriminating atrial septal defect combined with mobile echoic strands in fossa ovalis: a case report
Late-Detected Sinus Venosus Atrial Septal Defect and Subsequent Enteroviral Central Nervous System Infection: A Case Report.
authorString: Chamma AG, Saliba W, Chamma L.
abstractText: Sinus venosus atrial septal defect (SVASD) is frequently associated with partial anomalous pulmonary venous return and may be missed on routine transthoracic echocardiography because of its superior and posterior location. We report a 68-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation who presented with dyspnea and marked right-sided chamber enlargement. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging identified a 33 × 21-mm superior SVASD, anomalous drainage of the right upper and middle pulmonary veins, and a persistent left superior vena cava. The Qp/Qs was 3.7 by cardiac magnetic resonance and 3.2 by right heart catheterization, with a low indexed pulmonary vascular resistance of 1.7 Wood units·m², supporting surgical repair. Three and a half months after successful repair, the patient presented with transient loss of consciousness. Cardiac evaluation showed no residual interatrial shunt, no intracardiac thrombus, and no significant arrhythmia, although right ventricular dysfunction persisted. Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated asymmetric cortical and deep gray matter abnormalities. Cerebrospinal fluid showed lymphocytic pleocytosis, mildly elevated protein, preserved glucose, and positive enterovirus polymerase chain reaction. These findings supported enteroviral central nervous system infection. Because atrial fibrillation and postoperative cardiac abnormalities provided competing explanations for the neurologic presentation, the exact mechanism of the transient loss of consciousness remained uncertain. This case illustrates the importance of avoiding diagnostic anchoring when new neurologic symptoms develop after congenital cardiac surgery.

title: The ncRNA-Epigenetic-Cuproptosis Axis in Liver Diseases: From Copper Homeostasis to Precision Hepatology.
authorString: Wang G, Jiang G, Tao J, Feng W.

journal.title: Journal of clinical and experimental hepatology

abstractText: Cuproptosis, a recently defined copper-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by excess intracellular copper, is characterized by copper binding to lipoylated tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle proteins, causing aberrant protein oligomerization, iron-sulfur cluster loss, and proteotoxic stress. Given the liver's central role in copper homeostasis, hepatocytes are particularly vulnerable to this death modality. This review examines the emerging non-coding RNA (ncRNA)-epigenetic-cuproptosis axis in liver diseases, critically evaluating the evidence across a spectrum from well-established biochemical principles to largely hypothetical connections. Epigenetic mechanisms, including DNA methylation, histone modifications, and N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modifications, can modulate cuproptosis sensitivity. The methyltransferase-like 3 (METTL3)-m6A- fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein 1 (FMR1)-ferredoxin 1 (FDX1) axis, which confers cuproptosis resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) through translational repression of FDX1, represents the strongest mechanistic evidence in hepatic contexts. ncRNAs, including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), and circular RNAs (circRNAs), add additional regulatory layers; miR-133a-5p has been shown to facilitate cuproptosis in hepatocellular carcinoma by targeting ATP7B. We additionally highlight high-copper HCC phenotypes, the MYC-CTR1 and COMMD3 pro-tumor axes, and ferroptosis-cuproptosis combination strategies as priority translational directions. We systematically evaluate the ncRNA-epigenetic-cuproptosis axis across major liver diseases, including metabolic-associated steatotic liver disease, alcohol-associated liver disease, viral hepatitis, cholestatic liver disease, hepatic fibrosis, ischemia-reperfusion injury, Wilson disease, and HCC. Evidence tiers range from direct functional validation, such as copper ionophore-induced cuproptosis in HCC cells and cholestatic liver injury models, through promising but incomplete data, to largely bioinformatic associations lacking functional validation. Translational opportunities include biomarker development, copper ionophore-based therapeutics, and ncRNA-targeted interventions; we further distinguish mechanistic evidence from available human clinical data and outline how tumor copper phenotype, ncRNA signatures, viral etiology, immune context, and individual copper metabolism status could inform precision hepatology. We identify six priority questions and propose a research roadmap to advance this field from correlative associations toward rigorous mechanistic understanding, quantification of cuproptosis relative to established liver-cell death pathways, and eventual clinical implementation in precision hepatology.

title: Dating, disclosure, and romantic relationships pose challenges for adults with congenital heart disease: A mixed-methods study.
authorString: van der Meijs FC, Kiès P, van Winden LAM, Duijkers M, Janssen VR, Elzevier HW.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Int J Cardiol Congenit Heart Dis
journal.title: International journal of cardiology. Congenital heart disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Int J Cardiol Congenit Heart Dis

abstractText:
Background

As survival into adulthood has improved, adults with congenital heart disease (CHD) increasingly face psychosocial challenges related to long-term living with their condition. Romantic relationships are a key source of social support, yet the impact of the condition on dating and romantic experiences remains poorly understood.

Objectives

To explore dating and romantic relationship experiences in adults with congenital heart disease (CHD), focusing on disclosure and communication, while describing patterns by sex and disease complexity and incorporating partner perspectives.

Methods

This national cross-sectional online survey included individuals aged ≥16 years with CHD. Dating- and relationship-related questionnaire items were analyzed using descriptive quantitative and inductive thematic qualitative analyses, including descriptive subgroup analyses by sex and disease complexity. Partner perspectives were included to provide relational context.

Results

Among 109 CHD patients (69% women, 54% aged 26-40 years, 87% with moderate to severe disease), 21% reported dating difficulties, 40% difficulties disclosing their condition to dates, and 14% relationship dissolution attributed to CHD. Relationship challenges mainly concerned family planning (27%) and limitations in shared activities (25%). Qualitative findings, supplemented by five partner perspectives (n = 5), suggested fear of rejection during early disclosure and the importance of open communication. Descriptively, women and patients with moderate to severe disease reported more difficulties.

Conclusions

This mixed-methods study provides novel exploratory insight into the relational impact of CHD. Disclosure and communication appear particularly challenging during relationship establishment, whereas physical limitations contribute to challenges within established relationships. These findings support integrating relational support into routine CHD care.

title: Reducing surgical site infections among paediatric patients undergoing cardiac surgery: a multi-disciplinary quality improvement initiative

Development and internal validation of a nomogram for predicting flexible bronchoscopy utilization in children with lobar pneumonia caused by <i>Mycoplasma pneumoniae</i>: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Huang L, Li J, Liu C, Yang X, Xu H.
abstractText:
Background

The recent resurgence of Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) pneumonia has increased the number of children with lobar pneumonia who may receive flexible bronchoscopy (FB), yet the decision to perform FB remains subjective, and no quantitative tool exists for this specific high-risk subgroup. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a nomogram to predict FB utilization in children with MP-related lobar pneumonia using routine admission indicators to support real-time bedside decision-making.

Methods

This single-center retrospective study included 345 children (aged 1 month-18 years) with serology-confirmed MP-related lobar pneumonia (January 2022-March 2025); those with congenital heart disease, immunodeficiency, or plastic bronchitis were excluded. Patients were divided into FB (n=171) and non-FB (n=174) groups based on whether FB was performed. Laboratory predictors were restricted to values obtained within 72 hours of admission and before the FB decision. FB was recommended if symptoms or signs persisted after ≥72 hours of standard therapy. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify predictors, and a nomogram was constructed and internally validated by 10-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed by area under the curve (AUC), calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA).

Results

Viral coinfection [odds ratio (OR) =23.271, 95% confidence interval (CI): 9.299-64.900, P<0.001] was the strongest independent risk factor for FB utilization, while bacterial coinfection (OR =0.215, 95% CI: 0.088-0.507, P<0.001) and male sex (OR =0.146, 95% CI: 0.061-0.313, P<0.001) were independent protective factors. The nomogram incorporating these six variables demonstrated moderate discrimination (apparent AUC =0.741, 95% CI: 0.689-0.792; cross-validated AUC =0.705) and good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow P=0.56). At the optimal cutoff value of 0.56, the model had a sensitivity of 51.5% and a specificity of 85.1%. DCA demonstrated net clinical benefit over a "treat-all" strategy within a threshold probability range of 0.1-0.3.

Conclusions

The nomogram showed modest ability to predict FB use in this single-center cohort, but its clinical utility for identifying children with lobar pneumonia caused by MP who truly require FB remains uncertain.

title: Neonatal and 18-24-Month Growth and Neurodevelopmental Outcomes in Very Low Birth Weight Infants With Severe Congenital Heart Disease: A Korean Neonatal Network Study.
authorString: Kwak JI, Kim SH, Yoo K, Kim TG, Park J, Kwak A, Roh JH, Lee JM, Lee HN, Jeong J, Kim CY, Jung E, Lee BS.
abstractText:
Background and objectives

Severe congenital heart disease (CHD) in very low birth weight (VLBW) infants poses substantial risks, yet contemporary national data remain limited. This study evaluated the prevalence, lesion spectrum, and neonatal and 18-24-month outcomes of VLBW infants with severe CHD in South Korea.

Methods

We conducted a nationwide cohort study using the Korean Neonatal Network registry (2013-2021). Severe CHD was defined as a structural defect requiring surgical or catheter-based intervention within the first year of life and was categorized by physiological lesion type. Neonatal mortality, mortality before neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) discharge, major neonatal morbidities, and growth and neurodevelopmental outcomes at 18-24 months' corrected age were compared between infants with and without severe CHD.

Results

Among 15,145 VLBW infants, 147 (1.0%) had severe CHD. Infants with severe CHD had higher neonatal mortality within 28 days (27.2% vs. 9.3%; adjusted odds ratio [OR], 3.37; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.26-5.04) and mortality before NICU discharge (35.4% vs. 10.6%; adjusted OR, 5.95; 95% CI, 3.94-9.00) than those without severe CHD. Pulmonary hypertension, moderate-to-severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia, and necrotizing enterocolitis (stage ≥2) were more frequent in the severe CHD group. At 18-24 months, severe CHD was associated with higher rates of growth failure and neurodevelopmental impairment (34.1% vs. 20.0%; OR, 2.07, 95% CI, 1.32-3.24).

Conclusions

Severe CHD occurred in ~1% of VLBW infants and was associated with markedly higher mortality, greater neonatal morbidity, and increased risks of impaired growth and neurodevelopment at 18-24 months' corrected age.

title: Risk factors for acute gastrointestinal injury after cardiac surgery in underweight children with congenital heart disease: a single-center retrospective study.
authorString: Gao T, Jin Y, Liu Q, Liu J, Liu Y, Liu J.
abstractText:
Background

Acute gastrointestinal injury (AGI) is an underrecognized complication after cardiac surgery in children with congenital heart disease (CHD), particularly in those with low body weight. This study aimed to identify independent risk factors for postoperative AGI in underweight children (≤10 kg) undergoing CHD surgery.

Methods

This single‑center retrospective study enrolled 386 underweight children who underwent CHD surgery between October 2021 and July 2022. Patients were divided into AGI and non‑AGI groups based on postoperative occurrence. Multivariate binary logistic regression was performed to identify independent risk factors.

Results

Of the 386 enrolled patients, 91 cases (23.6%) developed clinically significant postoperative AGI. Multivariate analysis demonstrated that the minimum intraoperative rectal temperature (P=0.002) was an independent risk factor. In addition, patients with AGI had significantly longer duration of mechanical ventilation, longer intensive care unit (ICU) stay and longer overall hospital stay (all P<0.001). They also presented with higher transfusion requirements and a higher rate of extubation failure (P<0.001).

Conclusions

The minimum intraoperative rectal temperature is an independent risk factor for AGI in underweight children with CHD. Early identification of this factor facilitates risk stratification and guides targeted perioperative gastrointestinal protection strategies, thereby improving therapeutic outcomes in this high‑risk population.

title: Awareness and Perceived Need for Transitional Care in Childhood-Onset Cardiomyopathy Among Adult Cardiologists: A Nationwide Survey in Japan.
authorString: Soma K, Ochiai R, Minatoya R, Sakka M, Tsutsui H, Takeda N, Yao A.
abstractText:
Background

Transitional care is essential for patients with childhood-onset chronic diseases to ensure age-appropriate lifelong care. In contrast to congenital heart disease (CHD), for which transition/transfer systems have been relatively well established, childhood-onset cardiomyopathy (ChO-CM) lacks an established transitional care system in Japan. Our previous nationwide survey clarified the pediatric cardiologists' perspective, but awareness of and perceived need for transitional care among adult cardiologists have remained unclear. Therefore, this study investigated adult cardiologists' awareness of and perceived need for transitional care for ChO-CM.

Methods and results

A nationwide questionnaire survey was conducted in 1,347 cardiovascular departments in Japan to examine adult cardiologists' awareness of and perceived need for transitional care for ChO-CM. Valid responses were obtained from 332 departments. Among the respondents, 157 (47.3%) were aware of transitional care, whereas 200 (60.2%) answered that transitional care was necessary for all CM cases. Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that experience in treating hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) was independently associated with both awareness of transitional care and perceived need for it.

Conclusions

Awareness of transitional care for ChO-CM among adult cardiologists in Japan remains limited. However, most respondents recognized the need for transitional care. Clinical experience with HCM may promote recognition of the importance of transitional care. These findings highlight the need to develop structured transition systems for patients with ChO-CM in Japan.

title: Dynamic profiles and subpopulation characteristics of extracellular vesicles in patients undergoing transcatheter pulmonary valve replacement.
authorString: Liang R, Wu J, Abudurexiti N, Ling J, Peng Z, Wang C, Li J, Zhang Y, Yuan H, Wen S.

journal.title: Extracellular vesicles and circulating nucleic acids

abstractText: Aim: Transcatheter pulmonary valve replacement (TPVR) is a crucial intervention for severe pulmonary regurgitation (PR). Extracellular vesicle (EV) surface proteins reflect cardiovascular pathology. This study employed a proximity barcoding assay (PBA) to dynamically monitor EV protein profiles during TPVR. Methods: In this study, 40 biological plasma samples were analyzed in triplicate, including 10 from healthy controls (N group) and 30 from TPVR patients across three time points: preoperative (T1 group), 1 day postoperative (T2 group), and 1 week postoperative (T3 group). We performed combinatorial and functional analyses of membrane proteins across different groups and evaluated their predictive performance. EV subpopulations were clustered and characterized. Results: Compared with the N group, patients in the T1 group exhibited significantly downregulated expression of DSCAML1, ALCAM, and LAG3 proteins, while CD8A, NECTIN1, and LGR5 were significantly upregulated (P < 0.001; AUC: 0.94-1.00). Postoperatively, the expression of ALCAM and LAG3 rapidly rebounded. The ALCAM&CD36&DSCAML1&PECAM1 combination was significantly elevated in the control group, whereas CD36&CD8A&DSCAML1&TACSTD2 was reduced. Gene Ontology (GO) analysis indicated associations with response to stress, side of membrane, and protein binding pathways. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analysis revealed enrichment in the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (PKB/AKT) signaling pathway. Subpopulation analysis revealed that Cluster 1 was significantly elevated, whereas Cluster 2 was markedly decreased in the disease group. Additionally, Cluster 4 dominated in the T3 group. Furthermore, CD8A is most abundant in Cluster 1, while DSCAML1 dominates in Clusters 2 and 4. Conclusion: This study provides the first dynamic profiles and subpopulation characteristics of plasma EVs in patients undergoing TPVR, establishing a molecular atlas of perioperative right ventricular remodeling.

title: Heterotaxy Syndrome Combining Univentricular Heart, Polysplenia and Truncated Pancreas: A Case Report.
authorString: Akanmu CT, Wonang CN, Nyam DD, Ifeacho OH, Kenis SF, Shut GZ, Amusa GA, Okeahialam BN.
abstractText:
Background and objectives

Univentricular heart is a complex congenital heart disease with rare survival into adulthood. It could be part of a heterotaxy syndrome when, apart from the cardiac malformations, there are associated abnormal arrangements of extra-cardiac organs like the lungs, spleen and pancreas. The syndrome is said to be rarer than the univentricular heart and to have a worse clinical outcome.

Methods

After clinical assessment, the patient was investigated with Chest X-ray, Electrocardiography, Echocardiography, and contrast-enhanced CT scan of the chest and abdomen to make the diagnosis.

Results

We hereby report the case of a 19-year-old female who survived into adulthood with a functional single ventricle, double outlet right ventricle, atrial septal defect and dextrocardia without surgical intervention. She also had other extra-cardiac congenital anomalies like a truncated pancreas and polysplenia.

Conclusion

Though survival to adulthood is rare without surgical intervention, the left isomerism subtype recorded here is milder and has better survival prospects.

title: A giant left ventricular aneurysm in an apparently asymptomatic child. the value of multimodality assessment for risk stratification.
authorString: Sadeghpoor Tabaei S, Rashidi Ghader F, Mortezaeian H, Abedipoor F, Sadeghpour Tabaei A, Ansari Z, Naghmehsanj Z.
abstractText:
Background

Congenital left ventricular aneurysm (LVA) is a rare abnormality most commonly located at the LV apex. It must be differentiated from left ventricular diverticulum (LVD). Congenital LVA is typically isolated, whereas the latter is often associated with other congenital heart disease and midline thoraco-abdominal wall defects.

Case presentation

A large apical LVA was diagnosed in a 3-year-old girl referred after incidental cardiomegaly was detected on chest radiography. At this center, LVA was confirmed by echocardiography, magnetic resonance imaging, and angiography. The patient subsequently underwent surgical aneurysmorrhaphy. Notably, during surgical resection, the aneurysm was found to be filled with massive thrombotic material, composed primarily of extensive thin fibrous tissue and appeared highly prone to rupture. This case highlights the potential discrepancy between clinical presentation and disease severity, especially in a 3 year who is unaware of important clinical symptoms in this regard. The pathological report confirmed the diagnosis.

Conclusions

Left ventricular aneurysm appears as an akinetic or dyskinetic protrusion composed primarily of fibrous tissue and lacking organized myocardium. Although some patients can be managed medically, others require surgical intervention to prevent lethal complications.

title: Risk factors and outcomes of early postoperative complications following congenital heart surgery: a retrospective study at a tertiary care hospital in Nairobi, Kenya.
authorString: Adan NI, Orwa J, Ahmed I, Awori M, Rossi SD.
abstractText:
Introduction

Congenital Heart Disease (CHD) remains a major health challenge globally, with surgical interventions being the primary treatment modality for many defects. While advancements in cardiac surgery have improved survival rates, early postoperative complications continue to pose risks, particularly in settings with limited resources like Kenya. The study aimed to assess the rate of any early postoperative complications and identify factors associated with it in children after cardiac surgery at a tertiary care hospital in Nairobi, Kenya from 2019 to 2024.

Methods

This was an single-center retrospective study including children (< 18 years) who underwent cardiac surgery due to congenital heart disease at a tertiary care hospital in Nairobi, Kenya, over a 5-year period. Categorical variables were described as frequencies and percentages, while continuous variables were described as medians with interquartile ranges (IQR). Categorical variables were compared using chi-square or Fisher exact test and continuous variables compared using Mann-Whitney U test. Variables with p-value < 0.1 in the univariable analysis were included in the multivariable logistic regression, with p-value < 0.05 set as the level of significance. All analyses were performed using Rstudio version 4.5.1.

Results

A total of 97 children were included in the study. The median age in months was 25.0 (IQR: 8.5-67.5) and 50 (51.5%) were male. Patent ductus arteriosus, ventricular septal defect, and atrial septal defect were the predominant preoperative diagnoses. At least one early postoperative complication occurred in 52.6% (95%CI: 42.6% to 62.5%) of the children. Preoperative oxygen saturation (AOR: 0.92; 95%CI: 0.85-0.98, p = 0.021) and closed heart surgery (AOR:0.32; 95%CI:0.11-0.86, p = 0.027) were significantly associated with early postoperative complications.

Conclusion

The study findings highlight gaps and opportunities in perioperative care of children undergoing congenital heart surgery at a tertiary care center in Kenya. Preoperative oxygen saturation and closed heart surgery were independently associated with reduced odds of early postoperative complications. These findings suggest that optimizing preoperative physiological status and further investigating the factors driving the association between surgical approach and outcomes may inform strategies to improve perioperative care in this setting.

title: Fetal cardiac interventions versus expectant management in congenital heart disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Ning P, Liu J, Lin S, Zhao C, Ji Z, Pan S.
abstractText:
Objectives

To evaluate biventricular circulation (BVC), live birth, and postnatal mortality after fetal cardiac intervention (FCI) compared with expectant management, and to examine outcomes according to technical success of FAV.

Methods

This systematic review and meta-analysis followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from database inception through 31 December 2025 for observational FCI studiehis systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISs. The primary analysis was limited to studies with an internal expectant-management comparator; eligible non-comparative FAV studies were considered only for the secondary technical-success analysis. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed in Stata, and heterogeneity was assessed using I².

Results

Eleven comparative reports representing 11 independent study populations were included in the primary FCI-versus-expectant-management synthesis, comprising 775 fetuses (418 interventions and 357 controls). Overall FCI estimates included both technically successful and unsuccessful procedures. Among cohorts with available live-birth data, live birth occurred in 271/315 (86.0%) FCI cases and 287/319 (90.0%) controls, with no significant difference between groups (OR 0.680, 95% CI 0.350-1.320; p = 0.256). Postnatal death among live-born infants with available postnatal outcome data occurred in 53/271 (19.6%) in the FCI group and 94/287 (32.8%) in the expectant-management group and was lower after FCI (OR 0.457, 95% CI 0.280-0.746; p = 0.002). For FAV, postnatal death among live-born infants was lower (OR 0.419, 95% CI 0.216-0.813; p = 0.010), whereas BVC showed a non-significant trend (OR 2.260, 95% CI 0.970-5.290; p = 0.060). Fetal pulmonary valvuloplasty (FPV) showed no significant association with BVC (OR 2.430, 95% CI 0.880-6.760; p = 0.088) or postnatal death among live-born infants (OR 0.432, 95% CI 0.098-1.909; p = 0.268). Technically successful FAV was associated with higher odds of BVC and live birth compared with unsuccessful FAV. Fetal atrial septal intervention (FASI) analyses included live birth and postnatal death among live-born infants only. No statistically significant difference was found for live birth (OR 0.480, 95% CI 0.110-2.060; p = 0.325) or postnatal death among live-born infants (OR 0.433, 95% CI 0.127-1.482; p = 0.183).

Conclusions

FAV was associated with lower odds of postnatal death among live-born infants and showed a non-significant trend toward improved BVC, while technically successful FAV was associated with higher odds of BVC and live birth than unsuccessful FAV. In contrast, comparative evidence for FPV and FASI remains sparse, and these findings should be interpreted as exploratory.

abstractText: The article presents an analysis of international experience in providing medical care to pediatric patients with chronic non-communicable diseases (CNDs). The main models of providing medical care to pediatric patients with chronic diseases such as heart failure, cardiomyopathies, Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, and familial hypercholesterolemia are considered. One of the models is specialized centers established for the treatment of pediatric patients with cardiovascular diseases and inflammatory bowel diseases. The article reflects the results of the implementation of pediatric care models in medical organizations in a number of countries: the United States, Italy, Canada, etc. The results of foreign studies highlight the importance of the implemented models of medical care for children with CVD. abstractText:
Objective

to study the dose-dependent hypolipidemic effect of ϖ-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) in patients with cardiovascular diseases.

Material and methods

An open, single-center, prospective study was conducted at the clinic of the Federal Research Center for Nutrition and Biotechnology. The tolerability, safety, and effectiveness of dietary therapy enriched with various sources of ϖ-3 PUFAs at dosages ranging from 300 to 3000 mg per day were evaluated in patients with cardiovascular diseases.

Results

The study of different sources and dosages of ω-3 PUFAs demonstrated their good tolerability and safety, and revealed a dose-dependent effect on lipid profile parameters. The study demonstrated the dominant effect of different sources of ω-3 PUFAs on serum TG levels in patients with CVD.

Conclusion

The results of this study suggest that the inclusion of ω-3 PUFAs in the basic diet of patients with CVD and hyperlipidemia has an additional anti-atherogenic effect.

title: Electrosurgical Septotomy Across the Full Spectrum of Aortic Dissection.
authorString: Weiss G, Trnka H, Tauber S, Manville E, Arnold Z, Winkler B, Folkmann S, Grabenwöger M.

journal.title: European journal of cardio-thoracic surgery : official journal of the European Association for Cardio-thoracic Surgery

abstractText:
Objectives

Transcatheter electrosurgical septotomy divides the dissection membrane to reconstitute a single aortic lumen. Reported experience is largely confined to chronic post-dissection aneurysms. We assessed the technique across the full spectrum of descending aortic dissection, including stand-alone treatment of malperfusion.

Methods

A retrospective intention-to-treat analysis of 21 consecutive patients scheduled for septotomy between June 2022 and May 2026. The membrane was crossed by needle re-entry and divided with an electrified through-and-through guidewire at 40-60 W under fluoroscopy, without routine intravascular ultrasound or image fusion. A perfused-lumen index (perfused lumen divided by total aortic diameter) was measured before and after the procedure.

Results

Septotomy was performed in 20 of 21 patients (technical success 95% on an intention-to-treat basis). Indications were landing-zone preparation (57%), malperfusion (33%), preparation for open repair, and true-lumen collapse. Malperfusion resolved in all 7 patients treated for that indication, and the perfused-lumen index rose from a median of 0.16 to 0.98 (18 patients, P < .001). There was no stroke, spinal cord ischaemia, or retrograde type A dissection. Thirty-day, in-hospital, and overall mortality were 10%, 14%, and 19%, respectively, with 1 fatal delayed aortic rupture and no intraprocedural death. Three unplanned reinterventions occurred; median follow-up was 5.1 months.

Conclusions

Electrosurgical septotomy was feasible across the full spectrum of aortic dissection and, in selected patients, as stand-alone treatment for malperfusion, using standard electrosurgical equipment. Given the small, heterogeneous cohort and short follow-up, these findings demonstrate feasibility rather than durability.

title: An Ascorbic-Acid Containing Poly(Carbonate) Urethane With Antioxidant Bioactivity for Application in Heart Valve Scaffold Development.
authorString: Pedersen DD, Kohyama K, Fujii T, Barbuto M, Ye S, Park S, Falci F, Park J, Seo KS, Long W, D'Amore A, Kim S, Wagner WR.

journal.title: Journal of biomedical materials research. Part A

abstractText: Prosthetic heart valve development consists of several branching, innovative strategies to mediate the complex native environment that wears down valve durability. Anti-calcification treatments are being applied to pericardial tissue, durable polymers are being developed that mitigate oxidative degradation and stress cracking, and heart valve tissue engineering has introduced resorbable scaffolds that can develop into stable, functional tissue. In each case, an increasing breadth of strategies is being developed to curb the persistent issue of valve deterioration. This study aimed to synthesize and characterize an ascorbic acid-containing polyurethane to impart antioxidant properties to degradable scaffolds for tissue engineered heart valve (TEHV) replacement. Blends of poly(carbonate-ascorbic acid) urethane (PCAU) and poly(carbonate urethane) urea (PCUU) were fabricated into microporous scaffolds to evaluate the impact of PCAU in vitro on mechanics, degradation, cell viability, calcification, bacterial adhesion, and in vivo on native tissue response in a juvenile rat subcutaneous model. PCAU blended with PCUU in a 25:75 ratio (PCAU-25) had mechanical properties similar to PCUU, while higher concentrations of PCAU were not mechanically robust. PCAU-25 showed greater reactive oxygen species (ROS) inhibition and degradation, and reduced calcification and bacterial adhesion in vitro. In a juvenile rat subcutaneous model, both PCUU and PCAU-25 groups showed negligible calcification after 4 weeks. PCAU-25, however, showed much greater cell infiltration and immune response, possibly due to an accelerated rate of degradation. PCAU-25 was then fabricated into a polymeric valve scaffold and underwent basic mechanical and hydrodynamic performance assessment that demonstrated function similar to PCUU valves previously reported. These findings demonstrate proof-of-concept for a new polyurethane formulation incorporating ascorbic acid for antioxidant bioactivity and translatability into a functional TEHV scaffold.

title: KDOQI Commentary on the 2025 AHA/ACC Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults.
authorString: Chang TI, Cluett JL, Cohen DL, Drawz P, Hudson JQ, Kramer H, Rahman M, Awdishu L.

journal.title: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation

abstractText: Hypertension prevention, diagnosis, and management are central to modifying the progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD). Although the nephrology community has long recognized CKD as an independent risk factor for cardiovascular disease, CKD has not historically been incorporated in cardiovascular risk prediction models. The new 2025 American Heart Association and American College of Cardiology (AHA/ACC) Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults addresses this gap by formally adopting the PREVENT calculator, which combines cardiovascular, kidney, and metabolic health parameters to guide risk assessment and clinical decision making. The AHA/ACC guideline reinforces the broad blood pressure target of <130/80 mm Hg as well as makes recommendations for complex and resistant hypertension. Given the impact of these recommendations on persons living with kidney disease, the Kidney Disease Outcomes Quality Initiative (KDOQI) convened an expert work group to review and comment on the guideline. This KDOQI commentary focuses on recommendations from the AHA/ACC guideline that are pertinent to individuals at risk of CKD or with non-dialysis-dependent CKD (stages 1-5), hence excluding commentary on hypertension management in patients receiving maintenance dialysis. In areas where the AHA/ACC guideline does not offer formal recommendations (eg, medication interactions, electrolyte imbalances, and kidney injury), the work group provides expert commentary about implications for people with CKD. Overall, the work group supports the majority of the AHA/ACC recommendations and identifies areas where evidence remains limited or management in CKD warrants additional consideration.

title: End-to-end film-based characterization of gated delivery latencies in a spot-scanned synchrotron-based proton therapy system.
authorString: Stottler ZS, Kruse JJ, Deisher AJ.

journal.title: Journal of applied clinical medical physics

abstractText:
Background

Temporal mismatches between gating signals and beam activation-beam-on and beam-off latencies-in gated particle beam therapy can compromise dose integrity. Yet standardized measurement techniques are lacking, and system-specific characterization, particularly for synchrotron-based proton systems, remains limited.

Purpose

To implement a novel strategy for precise end-to-end gating latency measurements of a spot-scanned proton beam using Gafchromic film.

Methods

Gating latencies have been measured for a Hitachi ProBeat accelerator equipped with a Varian RPM gating system. EBT4 films were positioned within a stack of acrylic blocks on a QUASAR respiratory motion platform operated with a 1.5 cm amplitude and 12 bpm sinusoidal pattern. A stainless-steel ball bearing (BB), positioned atop the film, facilitated localization. During irradiation, the BB produced a dose shadow on the film that indicated the phantom position. A proton plan consisting of a single 85.3 MeV spot was delivered to isocenter during a single gate-on/off interval initiated near the 25% phase, to maximize phantom velocity. Fifty-one measurements were made with a variety of gating intervals. Beam-on latency and delivery time produced a separation between the BB-shadow and the centroid of the Gaussian proton spot. Spot duration information was extracted from accelerator log files. BB-shadow/spot separation is modeled analytically based on phantom motion enabling the direct calculation of the total beam-on and beam-off latencies. Accelerator latency was measured directly with an oscilloscope, enabling isolation of the relative contributions of the RPM gating system.

Results

An average beam-on latency of 142±27 ms is observed for the RPM+ProBeat system for the first gate of a delivery, which includes a known 69 ms beam extraction judgment time for the first proton spot in a spill from the Hitachi synchrotron. The corresponding average beam-off latency is 87±30ms . The average gate-on and gate-off latencies of the RPM system are calculated as 72±27ms and 81±30ms , respectively. The associated average contributions of the accelerator to the beam-on latencies are measured as 69.3±0.2ms (first gate in new spill) and 0.53±0.07ms (subsequent gates in existing spill) and similarly 6±4ms for beam-off latency.

Conclusion

A novel, high-precision method for gating-latency measurements has been implemented using film to characterize gating latencies in a spot-scanned particle beam. Commissioning and regular quality assurance methods to precisely characterize the temporal accuracy of a gating system ensure treatment accuracy and will become increasingly vital to consider for higher-frequency applications, such as cardiac gating or FLASH-capable systems.

title: The Senokine Gas6 Promotes Aortic Valve Calcification Through CaMKII-DRP1-Mediated Terminal Scission of Mitochondrial-Derived Vesicles.
authorString: Zhang Y, Zhang J, Xu Y, Lei W, Xu F, Li J, Wei Z, Su B, Liu S, Zhou J, Li H, Ran J, Li W, Tuerdi T, Wang X, Fang Z, Huang F, Chen M.
abstractText: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is an age-associated valvular disorder in which calcification expands from discrete foci into adjacent tissue. We investigated whether mitochondrial-derived vesicles (MDVs) released by human valvular interstitial cells (hVICs) exert pro-calcific effects on recipient cells and how MDV release is regulated. Using ex vivo hemodynamic perfusion of human CAVD tissue, multi-omics profiling, live-cell single-organelle tracking, MDV transfer assays, and in vivo Gas6 deletion, we found that calcifying hVICs hypersecreted MDVs that exerted pro-calcific effects in recipient hVICs. High-resolution imaging showed that mitochondria remodeled into donut-shaped structures under pro-osteogenic conditions; these structures served as physical platforms for MDV budding. Human CAVD valve tissues and hVICs treated with pro-osteogenic medium also exhibited senescence-associated features. Multi-omics profiling identified growth arrest-specific 6 (Gas6), a senokine, among 36 concordantly upregulated candidates. Functional analyzes showed that Gas6 promoted terminal MDV scission while leaving donut-shaped mitochondrial precursor formation intact. Mechanistically, Gas6 promoted intracellular Ca<sup>2+</sup> accumulation, calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII) activation, and dynamin-related protein 1 (DRP1) phosphorylation at Ser616, supporting a Ca<sup>2+</sup>-CaMKII-DRP1 axis that facilitates terminal MDV scission. Pharmacological inhibition of CaMKII or DRP1 reduced MDV hypersecretion and subsequent recipient-cell calcification, and Gas6 deletion in vivo attenuated valvular stenosis, calcification, and fibrotic remodeling. These findings identify Gas6-dependent terminal MDV scission as a mechanism contributing to the intercellular propagation of valvular calcification in a CAVD context characterized by senescence-associated features.

title: Cardiovascular Adverse Events with Anti-CD38 Antibodies Added to Identical Myeloma Regimens: A Systematic Review and Meta- analysis
authorString: Aly AS, Elmestiri M, Yacoub J, Yacoub Z, Abulbida S, Idris AE.
abstractText: Anti-CD38 antibodies improve multiple-myeloma outcomes, but uncommon cardiovascular harms are incompletely characterized. We reviewed randomized trials comparing an anti-CD38 antibody plus a regimen with the identical regimen alone. Six bibliographic databases, ClinicalTrials.gov and regulatory reports were searched to October 2026. Twenty-five myeloma trials were eligible; 15 contributed to meta-analysis, with 6,785 participants in their safety populations. Of these, 14 trials with 6,478 participants contributed registry data. Serious adverse-event preferred-term counts were reconstructed from registry tables and analyzed using Mantel-Haenszel count-based ratios with nominal 95% confidence intervals. Four secondary outcomes were more frequent with anti-CD38 therapy: ischemic heart disease, 1.56 (1.11–2.18); any serious cardiac adverse event, 1.33 (1.12–1.58); arterial thromboembolism, 1.37 (1.01–1.86); and nonserious hypertension, 1.64 (1.43–1.88). The primary atrial fibrillation (AF)/flutter estimate was 1.44 (0.97–2.13), and cardiac failure was 0.88 (0.61–1.27). Unequal treatment duration and incomplete outcome reporting limited interpretation. The ischemic and cardiac findings warrant attention and confirmation in future studies. Clinical vigilance should be balanced against established oncologic benefit; these results do not establish a screening strategy or a preferred antibody.

title: Predictors of recurrent stroke among patients with lacunar stroke receiving intensive blood pressure control: a secondary analysis of the secondary prevention of small subcortical strokes trial.
authorString: Shakir M, Huang Y, Gomez CR, Qureshi AI.
abstractText:
Background

Intensive systolic blood pressure (SBP) lowering to <130 mm Hg is recommended in contemporary secondary stroke prevention guidelines; however, it did not significantly reduce overall recurrent ischemic stroke in the Secondary Prevention of Small Subcortical Strokes (SPS3) trial. In this post hoc secondary analysis of participant-level SPS3 trial data, we sought to identify baseline predictors of recurrent ischemic stroke among patients with lacunar stroke assigned to the lower SBP target in SPS3.

Methods

This post hoc secondary analysis included SPS3 participants randomized to the lower SBP target (<130 mm Hg). The primary outcome was centrally adjudicated recurrent ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke. Candidate predictors were evaluated with multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and reported as hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

Results

Among 1501 participants (41.1% aged ≥ 65 years; 60.8% were men), 120 (8.0%) experienced recurrent ischemic stroke over a median follow-up of 3.49 years (interquartile range, 1.80-5.08), corresponding to an incidence rate of 2.43 events per 100 person-years. In unadjusted comparisons, recurrent ischemic stroke was associated with diabetes mellitus (44.2% vs 34.2%; p = .036), coronary artery bypass grafting/coronary stent (9.2% vs 4.1%; p = .018), Black race (24.2% vs 14.4%; p = .007), elevated serum creatinine (14.2% vs 7.7%; p = .022), aspirin or clopidogrel use at the qualifying lacunar stroke (44.2% vs 28.5%; p < .001), large-vessel atherosclerosis (29.3% vs 17.9%; p = .004), and lower prevalence of a subcortical qualifying stroke (21.7% vs 46.1%; p < .001). In multivariable analysis, aspirin or clopidogrel use at the qualifying lacunar stroke (HR, 1.69; 95% CI, 1.14-2.50; p = .009) and large-vessel atherosclerosis (HR, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.08-2.413; p = .020) were independently associated with recurrence. Randomization to aspirin plus clopidogrel was not associated with recurrent ischemic stroke (HR, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.75-1.57; p = .661).

Conclusions

In SPS3 participants assigned to intensive SBP control, 8.0% experienced recurrent ischemic stroke. Aspirin or clopidogrel use at the qualifying lacunar stroke and large-vessel atherosclerosis remained independent predictors of recurrence. These findings may help identify patients who require preventive strategies beyond intensive SBP lowering.

title: One-Year Clinical Outcomes of Paclitaxel-Coated Balloon Angioplasty in Patients With and Without Acute Coronary Syndrome: The ALLIANCE Registry.
authorString: Muramatsu T, Tanabe K, Kadota K, Tadano Y, Ando K, Nakamura S, Ashikaga T, Kinoshita Y, Kuriyama N, Ohnishi Y, Kataoka T, Nishida K, Iijima R, Nozoe M, Morishige K, Takahashi T, Murakami Y, Kozuma K, Nakamura M.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText: Real-world data after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) using drug-coated balloons (DCBs) in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) are limited. We compared 1-year clinical outcomes after PCI with paclitaxel DCBs between the ACS and non-ACS patients. The ALLIANCE is a prospective, multicenter registry of PCI using paclitaxel DCBs. Primary endpoint was target lesion failure (TLF), defined as a composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction (MI), or clinically driven target lesion revascularization. Secondary endpoints included all-cause mortality at 1 year. Adverse events were adjudicated by an independent committee. Propensity score matching was performed to adjust for baseline differences between the ACS and non-ACS patients. From July 2023 to February 2024, 1794 patients with de novo lesions (ACS 513 [28.6%] and non-ACS 1281 [71.4%]) were enrolled at 57 medical institutions in Japan. Mean age was 71 years, and 76% were male. Among ACS patients, 34.7% had ST-segment elevation MI, 33.9% non-ST-segment elevation MI, and 31.4% unstable angina. Intracoronary imaging was used in 88.5% of lesions. Bailout stenting after DCB angioplasty was required in only 1.1% of 1984 lesions. Technical success, defined as post-procedural residual stenosis < 40% and absence of flow-limiting coronary dissection, was significantly lower in patients with ACS than those with non-ACS. At 1 year, TLF occurred in 7.0% of ACS and 3.8% of non-ACS patients (adjusted HR 1.83; 95% CI 1.06-3.17, p = 0.03). All-cause mortality was 6.4% and 3.3%, respectively (adjusted HR 2.06; 95% CI 1.13-3.75, p = 0.02). One-year TLF and all-cause mortality were significantly higher in ACS than non-ACS patients treated with paclitaxel DCBs in real-world clinical settings. Japan Registry of Clinical Trials (https://jrct.mhlw.go.jp); unique identifier: jRCT1032230218.

title: Point-of-care ultrasound–guided early decongestion and 6-month outcomes in patients hospitalized with acute decompensated heart failure on an internal medicine ward: a comparative cohort study
authorString: Genc¹ A, Erman¹ H, Boyuk¹ B.
abstractText: Background Residual congestion is a major driver of early events after hospitalization for acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF), and physical examination detects it poorly. We examined whether a point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS)–guided early decongestion strategy was associated with 6-month outcomes in patients with ADHF managed on an internal medicine ward. Methods In this single-center comparative cohort study, patients with ADHF managed with a POCUS-guided strategy were enrolled prospectively. In this strategy, an inferior vena cava (IVC) diameter > 2.1 cm with collapsibility < 50% triggered 200 mg of intravenous furosemide in the first 24 hours. Patients with ADHF who did not undergo POCUS in the clinic were retrospectively selected as controls. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death or heart failure (HF) readmission within 6 months after discharge, ascertained from hospital records and analyzed with Cox regression. Results Of 100 patients, 94 had verifiable follow-up (46 POCUS-guided, 48 controls; mean age 75.4 years; 55% women). The primary outcome occurred in 25 (54%) POCUS-guided patients and 19 (40%) controls (hazard ratio [HR] 1.49, 95% CI 0.82–2.71; adjusted HR 1.36, 95% CI 0.73–2.53). HF readmission (24% vs. 19%), death (37% vs. 31%), 30-day outcomes and length of stay did not differ significantly. Conclusions In this real-world cohort, POCUS-guided early intensified decongestion was not associated with improved 6-month outcomes. Adequately powered randomized trials that separate ultrasound assessment from diuretic intensity are needed before this strategy is adopted.

title: Whether to hold and what to measure: perioperative euglycemic ketoacidosis in patients taking SGLT2 inhibitors.
authorString: Park EJ, Hong JM.
abstractText: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are widely used for type 2 diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease, including in patients without diabetes. Their ketogenic effects may be amplified perioperatively by fasting, surgical stress, and volume loss, resulting in ketoacidosis without marked hyperglycemia. Reported frequencies depend on ascertainment. Where ketones were measured against a diagnostic threshold, cohorts reported 0-1.8% in non-cardiac and mixed populations and 0-15.1% in cardiac surgery; one prospective study using a lower threshold (≥ 0.6 mmol/L) reported a far higher figure, and studies without ketone measurement reported surrogate metabolic-acidosis endpoints of 30-41%. None of these are comparable incidence estimates. Severe and fatal cases have been reported. Because plasma glucose may be normal, diagnosis requires attention to acid-base status and ketones. Quantitative blood β-hydroxybutyrate is preferred when SGLT2 inhibitor (SGLT2i)-associated ketoacidosis is suspected; urine ketone tests may screen when blood testing is unavailable, but a negative result does not exclude it. Perioperative guidance remains inconsistent: some bodies recommend withholding SGLT2i for 3 days (4 days for ertugliflozin), whereas others support risk-stratified continuation in selected patients under specified fasting and dietary conditions. No randomized trial has compared continuation with discontinuation using perioperative ketoacidosis as an endpoint; observational evidence remains limited and conflicting, and ketone thresholds and monitoring intervals lack prospective validation. This review summarizes evidence on recognition, diagnosis, withholding, monitoring, and postoperative restart.

title: Effectiveness of digital health interventions for care integration in coronary artery disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Chan A, Lim HM, Lim WX, Leong JT, Abdullah A, Dunn AG.
abstractText: To assess the effectiveness of digital health interventions (DHIs) supporting care integration for coronary artery disease (CAD) in improving health outcomes compared to usual care. For this systematic review, we searched MEDLINE, CINAHL, EBSCO Psychology and Behavioural Sciences Collection, Scopus, and Web of Science from 1 January 1995 to 5 November 2025. We included studies reporting primary data on DHIs supporting care integration for patients with CAD. Primary endpoints were all-cause mortality and readmissions, and CVD events. Secondary endpoints were the control of cardiovascular risk factors. We conducted random-effects meta-analyses in RevMan and assessed risk of bias with Cochrane's RoB tools. We included 72 studies (23,111 participants), assessing 45 in the meta-analysis. All DHIs supported person-centred care integration (n=72) while few DHIs addressed clinical care integration (n=22), professional integration (n=12) and functional integration (n=22).
