B3 derived HR and HRV closely matched reference measures across tasks, with high quality ECG recordings and minimal data loss, except during vigorous arm swinging. Respiratory rate and pattern metrics, including exhalation peak timing, also showed strong agreement. The B3 thermistor accurately tracked respiration rate even at higher breathing frequencies, although minor timing offsets occurred during some guided respiration segments. Overall, B3 performed comparably to the reference system for cardiac and respiratory measures, offering an affordable, open-source solution for physiological monitoring in real-world interactive settings.

title: Impact of Right Ventricular Pacing Burden on Left Ventricular Deformation and Rotational Mechanics: A Cohort Study
authorString: K.S R, Samanth J, Pai U, R P, Prabhu MA, Devasia T, Nayak R, Srinivas S, Nayak KA.
abstractText: Background Permanent right ventricular pacing may impair left ventricular function through abnormal electrical activation and mechanical dyssynchrony. Early effects on myocardial mechanics in structurally normal hearts remain unclear, as ejection fraction may not detect subtle dysfunction. Speckle-tracking echocardiography allows sensitive assessment of myocardial deformation. This study evaluated the short-term impact of right ventricular pacing burden on left ventricular function and mechanics Methods This prospective study included 117 patients undergoing permanent pacemaker implantation for conduction abnormalities (single-chamber or dual-chamber). A pacing burden threshold of 40% was selected a priori, based on prior evidence of this level as a clinically meaningful inflection point for pacing-induced left ventricular dysfunction. Patients were stratified into ≤ 40% (n = 50) and > 40% (n = 67) pacing-burden groups. Clinical and echocardiographic evaluation, including conventional and speckle-tracking imaging, was performed at baseline and 6 months. Results Among 117 patients (mean age 61.8 ± 13.3 years; 51.3% female) stratified by pacing burden into ≤ 40% (n = 50) and > 40% (n = 67) groups, global longitudinal strain (GLS) declined significantly in the > 40% group (18.7 ± 4.8% vs 16.3 ± 3.7%, p < 0.001; group× time interaction p = 0.05) but was unchanged in the ≤ 40% group. LVEF and circumferential strain declined numerically more in the > 40% group, without a significant group× time interaction. Radial strain and rotational mechanics (twist, torsion) did not change significantly in either group. Pacing burden > 40% (OR 2.32, 95% CI 1.01–5.37) and RV apical pacing site (OR 2.62, 95% CI 1.07–6.39) were independently associated with reduced GLS at 6 months (both p < 0.05). Conclusion Increased right ventricular pacing burden is associated with early impairment of left ventricular GLS, with a less certain effect on circumferential strain and no significant effect detected on radial or rotational mechanics at 6 months. Speckle-tracking echocardiography, particularly GLS, may enable earlier detection of subclinical dysfunction than ejection fraction.

title: Associations of average sleep duration and cumulative AIP with cardiometabolic multimorbidity risk in middle-aged and older Chinese adults: a CHARLS longitudinal study
authorString: Feng Z, Zhang S, Han L, Li J, Gao Y, Jiang P, Zheng Y, Wang H, Duan L.
abstractText: Objective To investigate the relationship between the Atherogenic Index of Plasma (AIP) and sleep duration on the risk of developing cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) in middle-aged and older Chinese adults, we utilized data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). Methods Middle-aged and older participants without chronic metabolic diseases (CMM) at baseline were selected from the CHARLS database. Both the atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) and sleep duration were categorized into four distinct groups, resulting in 16 combined subgroups. Utilizing the group with the lowest AIP and average sleep duration as the reference, multivariable Cox regression models were employed to investigate the associations between average sleep duration, cumulative average AIP, and the incidence of CMM. Results A total of 3,422 participants was included in the study, of whom 520 (15.20%) developed new-onset CMM. Multivariable Cox regression analysis indicated that, after full adjustment for age, sex, residence, marital status, education, smoking, drinking, hypertension, and dyslipidemia, each 1-unit increase in cumulative average sleep duration was associated with a 9.1% reduction in the risk of CMM (HR = 0.909, 95% CI: 0.857–0.964, P  = 0.001). In contrast, each 1-unit increase in cumulative average AIP corresponded to a 68.1% increase in risk (HR = 1.681, 95% CI: 1.236–2.286, P  < 0.001). Interaction subgroup analyses revealed that longer sleep duration significantly decreased CMM risk only among individuals with low AIP levels, with the most pronounced protective effect observed in the sleep-Q3 combined with AIP-Q1 subgroup (HR = 0.538, 95% CI: 0.336–0.862). Conclusion Cumulative average sleep duration and AIP serve as independent determinants of new-onset CMM in middle-aged and older populations, operating through distinct pathogenic pathways. A joint assessment of these factors may improve risk prediction. In individuals with a lower atherosclerotic burden, adequate sleep provides additional cardiovascular benefits, indicating that clinical prevention strategies should encompass both lipid metabolism and sleep health management.

title: Ramus Intermedius Anatomy and Left Main Coronary Geometry on Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography: A Retrospective Single-Center Study
authorString: Lv H, Luo X, Dong Y, Zhang L, Yu S, Xu Y.
abstractText: Background Ramus intermedius (RI) changes the left main (LM) coronary division from bifurcation to trifurcation, but its associations with LM geometry, CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR), and adjacent-vessel atherosclerotic features remain incompletely characterized. Methods In this retrospective single-center study, consecutive adults who underwent clinically indicated coronary computed tomography angiography between December 2024 and April 2025 were screened. The final age-matched cohort included 300 patients (150 with RI and 150 without RI). LAD-LCX angle, vessel diameter and cross-sectional area (CSA), plaque features, stenosis severity, and CT-FFR were evaluated. RI-specific analyses by ostial location, diameter, and functional status were exploratory. Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction was applied within prespecified outcome families. Because sex distribution differed between groups, the primary LAD-LCX angle comparison was supplemented by an aggregate tipping-point sensitivity analysis. Results Patients with RI had a wider LAD-LCX angle than patients without RI (99.35° ± 25.61° vs. 69.22° ± 17.83°; P < 0.001), with a mean difference of 30.13° (95% CI, 25.11°-35.15°), and had larger LM diameter and CSA. Diseased-segment analyses showed no significant between-group differences in plaque composition or stenosis severity. Within the RI group, proximal-LAD RI origin remained associated after multiplicity correction with smaller LAD CSA (q < 0.008) and more frequent LAD CT-FFR positivity (q = 0.009), whereas nominal anatomic stenosis signals were attenuated (q = 0.051). Only 10 patients had RI CT-FFR ≤ 0.80; findings stratified by RI CT-FFR status were therefore presented descriptively. In the aggregate sensitivity analysis, a male-female LAD-LCX angle difference of approximately 105.1° would be required for the observed sex imbalance alone to reduce the primary group contrast to zero, but this calculation does not replace patient-level adjustment. Conclusions RI presence was associated with a wider LM bifurcation angle and larger LM dimensions on CCTA. Selected RI ostial-location associations persisted after multiplicity correction. These observational findings do not establish causality, and residual confounding and the sparse RI CT-FFR-positive subgroup warrant cautious interpretation and external validation.

title: Non-independence in network-structured Mendelian randomization: a permutation framework and six failure modes
authorString: Prabhakar P.
abstractText: Background. Protein Mendelian randomization (MR) is now routine, and a common inference treats an estimate built from a ligand's own cis protein quantitative trait locus (pQTL) and one built from its receptor's as evidence about the same pathway. That assumption has not been tested since it means comparing MR estimates across a network of interacting proteins, and network comparisons violate the independence that standard multiple-testing corrections assume. Methods. Using cis-pQTLs as instruments, we analyzed 660 of the 661 UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project proteins spanning 1,129 curated ligand–receptor pairs, and estimated effects on coronary artery disease in two genome-wide association studies (GWAS): Nikpay 2015 (60,801 cases, no UK Biobank overlap) and Aragam 2022 (181,522 cases, which include the Nikpay data). Discordance between ligand-level and receptor-level estimates was tested against a permutation null holding every protein's estimate and degree fixed and randomizing only the pairing. Estimates were followed up with Bayesian colocalization and with replication on a second proteomic platform. Results. Ligand and receptor estimates agreed no more than randomly paired proteins: 48.5% same-direction against a rewired null of 49.8% (p = 0.64) in Nikpay, and 47.0% against 50.0% (p = 0.20) in Aragam. Counts of significantly discordant pairs rose threefold with outcome power, from 10 to 31, and the null rose with them, from 9 to 30 (p = 0.85). Bonferroni correction across 476 deduplicated pairs built from 361 proteins reported ten discoveries that three proteins account for. A node-shuffling null gave p = 0.014 because protein degree correlates with effect size in Aragam (rho = + 0.133, p = 0.008). Flagging protein-altering instruments, a routine sensitivity analysis, flagged PCSK9 and showed no enrichment among causal proteins (Fisher p ≥ 0.44). Colocalization verdicts survived a change of outcome GWAS at only 11 of 14 loci (PP.H4 ≥ 0.8), mostly through outcome power; one locus reversed outright. Conclusions. Ligand-level and receptor-level MR are not interchangeable evidence about a pathway. More important, the naive analysis that appears to identify specific discordant pairs is reproducible. It returns ten pairs after correction, headed by one at p = 8.5 × 10 − 7 , and we show what removes them.

title: Clinical diagnoses associated with FIV seropositivity: reexamining expected clinical patterns in a large matched primary care cohort
authorString: Morrow BL, Taylor-Rakocevic M, Beck OL, Twomey B, Lin D, Topdjian K.
abstractText: Background Feline immunodeficiency virus (FIV) has historically been associated with progressive disease across multiple organ systems, but the clinical effects of naturally acquired infection remain uncertain. This retrospective matched cohort study evaluated whether FIV seropositivity was associated with diagnoses across 12 systems-based categories in a large North American primary care population. Results De-identified electronic medical records from more than 1,000 Banfield Pet Hospital clinics collected from January 2013 through December 2023 included 30,034 FIV+ cats aged at least 6 months and 60,184 FIV- controls selected at approximately two controls per FIV + cat and matched by sex and birth year. Per-cat prevalence and unadjusted and adjusted ORs with 95% CIs were calculated using logistic regression. After adjustment for sex and sterilization status, cardiovascular, neurologic, and overall weight/nutrition diagnoses were not associated with FIV seropositivity. Renal/urinary diagnoses showed a small inverse association (adjusted OR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.89-1.00). Six categories showed weak positive associations (adjusted ORs, 1.12–1.45). Dermatological diagnoses showed a moderate positive association (adjusted OR, 1.68; 95% CI, 1.63–1.73), with abscesses (9.5% vs 4.0%) and dermatitis (14.7% vs 10.0%) contributing prominently. Hematological diagnoses showed a strong positive association (adjusted OR, 6.54; 95% CI, 6.07–7.04), driven mainly by anemia and potentially influenced by surveillance bias and FIV-specific diagnostic coding. Conclusions FIV seropositivity was not broadly associated with disease across multiple organ systems in this large primary care population. These findings indicate that historical descriptions substantially overstate the usual clinical impact of naturally acquired FIV. A positive test should prompt hematological evaluation for anemia but, by itself, does not justify euthanasia or exclusion from adoption or return-to-field pathways.

title: FLNA-related periventricular nodular heterotopia with multisystem involvement: a case report
authorString: Wen L, Yang Y, Shang P, Yuan C.
abstractText: Background FLNA-related periventricular nodular heterotopia (PVNH) is an X-linked neuronal migration disorder classically associated with epilepsy. Accumulating evidence indicates that it is a multisystem disorder involving cardiac valvular, pulmonary, and ophthalmologic manifestations. We report a patient with an unusually comprehensive multisystem phenotype to emphasize the need for systematic extracranial evaluation in FLNA-related PVNH. Case presentation: A 33-year-old woman presented with two decades of headache and palpitations. Physical examination revealed digital clubbing and prominently dilated cardiac valves. Brain MRI demonstrated bilateral periventricular heterotopia. Enhanced whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous pathogenic nonsense variant in FLNA (NM_001110556.2:c.2193C > G, p.Tyr731Ter). Multisystem involvement comprised focal epilepsy, polyvalvular regurgitation, interstitial lung disease, and ophthalmologic abnormalities. Seizures were controlled with oxcarbazepine and lamotrigine, and the patient was referred for coordinated cardiologic, pulmonary, and ophthalmologic follow-up. Conclusions FLNA-related PVNH should be managed as a multisystem disorder rather than isolated epilepsy. Routine cardiovascular, pulmonary, and ophthalmologic screening, combined with genetic counseling for X-linked dominant transmission, should be integrated into standard care.

title: Individual Cardiometabolic Risk Factors and Long-Term Cardiovascular Outcomes in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease
authorString: Shibata N, Morita Y, Ito T, Kanzaki Y, Watanabe N, Yoshioka N, Arao Y, Miyazawa H, Yasuda S, Toyoda H, Morishima I.
abstractText: Background: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is defined by hepatic steatosis and at least one of five cardiometabolic risk factors (CMRFs); however, whether individual CMRFs carry equivalent prognostic information for cardiovascular outcomes remains unclear. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 2,962 patients with MASLD who underwent abdominal ultrasonography between 2006 and 2015. Patients were randomly assigned to derivation (n = 2,073) and validation (n = 889) cohorts. Associations of five MASLD-qualifying CMRFs with major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) were evaluated using multivariable Cox regression. Patients were subsequently classified according to CMRFs independently associated with MACCE. Results: During follow-up of up to 10 years, 183 MACCE occurred in the derivation cohort. After adjustment for age, sex, and all five CMRFs, diabetes mellitus (DM) (hazard ratio [HR], 1.42; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.06–1.90) and low high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) (HR, 1.43; 95% CI, 1.05–1.95) were independently associated with MACCE, whereas body mass index ≥ 23 kg/m², hypertension, and hypertriglyceridemia were not. Patients were classified as having neither factor, DM alone, low HDL-C alone, or both factors. MACCE risk differed significantly among the four groups in both the derivation and validation cohorts (log-rank P < 0.001 and P = 0.019, respectively). In the validation cohort, the 5-year time-dependent area under the curve was 0.757 for age and sex, 0.763 after incorporating CMRF count, and 0.777 after incorporating the DM/low HDL-C classification. Conclusions: Among patients with MASLD, individual CMRFs were not equally associated with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular outcomes. The type and combination of CMRFs, particularly DM and low HDL-C, may provide useful prognostic information beyond CMRF count alone. Retrospectively registered: The study was approved by the ethics committee of Ogaki Municipal Hospital (approval number: 20230928-11).

title: A novel RYR2 variant associated with catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia requiring extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation and complicated by cervical vascular injury: a case report
authorString: Kim TT, Dong NV, Hieu PT, Giang HK, Duyen DT, Dat TM, Luan VT, Vy ND, Cuong DM, Thanh NT.
abstractText: Background Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT) is an inherited arrhythmia syndrome that can cause sudden cardiac arrest. Its recognition after resuscitation may be obscured by troponin elevation and transient ventricular dysfunction, resembling fulminant myocarditis. Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) can provide temporary circulatory support during refractory cardiac arrest; however, cervical cannulation carries a risk of vascular thrombosis and bleeding. We report a case of a child with ryanodine receptor 2 ( RYR2 )-associated CPVT, complicated by a compressive cervical haematoma after decannulation. Case presentation A 9-year-old boy with two previous syncopal episodes sustained a startle-triggered out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and developed recurrent polymorphic ventricular tachycardia after admission to the paediatric intensive care unit. Right cervical veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation was established after continuous cardiopulmonary resuscitation without sustained return of spontaneous circulation, with an estimated resuscitation-to-flow interval of approximately 60 minutes. Serum troponin I was measured at 5.11 µg/L and left ventricular ejection fraction was 42–44%, prompting treatment for suspected diagnosis of fulminant myocarditis; the ejection fraction subsequently fell to 33%. Whole-exome sequencing identified a novel heterozygous RYR2 variant, c.11836G > A (p.Gly3946Ser), classified as pathogenic by the reporting laboratory according to ACMG/AMP criteria. The variant is absent from ClinVar, relevant population reference databases, and the published literature, and its identification, together with the patient’s characteristic clinical phenotype, supported the diagnosis of RYR2 -associated CPVT. During anticoagulation for cervical vascular thrombosis after decannulation, an enlarging haematoma with active extravasation and tracheal compression required surgical evacuation, carotid repair, jugular thrombectomy, and venorrhaphy. The child was discharged after 41 days with a signficant improvement ejection fraction of 67%, persistent internal jugular occlusion, and propranolol and aspirin therapy. Conclusions CPVT should be reconsidered after an adrenergic cardiac arrest, even when post-arrest findings suggest myocarditis. ECPR can provide temporary rescue support. A rare RYR2 variant detection may support the clinical diagnosis and intervention.

title: Cleveland Heart Disease Dataset: From Primary Data to an AI-Ready Resource.
authorString: Chuiko G, Yaremchuk O.
abstractText: Background. The Cleveland Heart Disease Dataset is one of the most widely used benchmark resources for cardiovascular risk prediction. Despite its extensive use in clinical artificial intelligence research, relatively little attention has been paid to dataset quality, feature redundancy, and label noise, which may affect the reliability and reproducibility of predictive models. Objective. This study aims to transform the Cleveland Heart Disease Dataset from primary clinical data into an AI-ready resource through systematic data engineering. Methods. An integrated data-engineering workflow was developed using WEKA. Ensemble feature selection based on eight independent attribute evaluators was applied to identify informative clinical variables and reduce dataset dimensionality. Label noise was detected using the CAIRAD algorithm. Potentially mislabeled records were removed, resulting in a reduced and cleansed dataset. The utility of the resulting resource was evaluated using three neural-network-based classifiers and repeated cross-validation. Results. Feature selection reduced the number of predictive attributes from 13 to 7, while label-noise detection identified 49 potentially mislabeled records. The resulting AI-ready resource contained 254 instances. Across all evaluated classifiers, the engineered dataset demonstrated statistically significant improvements in Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, Matthews Correlation Coefficient, and Precision-Recall AUC compared with the original dataset. Differences among classifiers were substantially smaller than those associated with dataset engineering. Conclusions. Systematic feature reduction and label-noise removal transformed the Cleveland Heart Disease Dataset into an AI-ready resource with improved predictivity and reduced data complexity. The proposed workflow highlights the importance of health data quality and reproducible data-engineering practices for clinical AI and decision-support applications.

title: Post-transcriptional Rac1 activation driven by lipid modification enzymes in atrial fibrillation: a multi-dataset bioinformatics study with experimental validation
authorString: Du H, Yang X, Zhang J, Tuerhong Z, Guo Y, Gu X, Li S, Zhang Y, Tang B.
abstractText: Background Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia, but the post-translational mechanisms linking mitochondrial dysfunction to arrhythmogenic signaling remain poorly understood. Whether the small GTPase Rac1—central to cardiomyocyte redox signaling—is activated through transcriptional upregulation or post-translational modification (PTM) has not been dissected. Methods We constructed a 77-gene Mitoxyperilysis Gene Set (MGS) and performed differential expression analysis in the discovery cohort GSE115574 (AF = 26, SR = 31; Affymetrix GPL570). ssGSEA scored four mechanistic arms: glutathione (GSH) metabolism, mitochondrial damage, RhoA axis, and mTORC2 axis. A 44-gene PTM enzyme panel was assessed across three datasets (GSE115574, GSE41177, GSE79768; AF = 29, SR = 5 and AF = 11, SR = 9 in the validation cohorts). Rac1 protein activation was examined via immunofluorescence (IF) in human right atrial tissue (AF = 3, SR = 3; TOM20/RAC1 dual staining, eight fields per sample). Results Among 170 differentially expressed genes, 3 MGS genes were significantly altered. The GSH metabolism arm was markedly downregulated in the discovery cohort (P = 1.57 × 10⁻⁴, FDR = 0.0012). The PTM enzyme panel revealed 30/44 genes significantly altered in ≥ 1 dataset, with 5 showing cross-dataset concordant upregulation (GGPS1, ZDHHC4, ZDHHC5, ZDHHC20, AKT1). RAC1 mRNA was not significantly different (log₂FC = 0.12, P = 0.34), and the transcriptional RAC1/RHOA ratio was consistently lower in AF across all three datasets (a negative finding). In human atrial tissue, Rac1 immunofluorescence showed a trend toward higher intensity (8.51 ± 2.95 vs 7.08 ± 2.00, P = 0.53) and membrane-to-cytoplasm ratio (0.93 ± 0.07 vs 0.84 ± 0.13, P = 0.40) in AF (pilot validation, n = 3/group); trimmed-mean and median analyses confirmed that these trends were not driven by bright spots. Conclusions AF atrial tissue exhibits concurrent "transcriptional RhoA relative dominance" and "post-translational Rac1 activation trend," which are not contradictory. Rac1 activation in AF appears to be modification-driven (geranylgeranylation/palmitoylation) rather than transcription-driven, warranting further validation by site-specific PTM assays.

title: Evaluating the use of blood pressure and oral microbiome screening in primary care dental clinics
authorString: DOBLE AS, BESCOS R, WITTON R, MUDDIMAN KJ, STEPHEN AS, NICOLAS T, ZAHRA D, CANA-BISHOP M, BROOKES ZL.
abstractText: Blood pressure and oral microbiome screening are gaining popularity in non-medical settings, the hypotheses communicated to hypertensive patients being that: altering the abundance of certain bacterial species via oral hygiene could be beneficial for cardiovascular health, especially nitrate reducing species that lower blood pressure. Two-hundred participants (58.410.8 y/o) therefore underwent Systolic (SBP) and diastolic (DBP) blood pressure screening in a primary care clinic at some other time than dental treatment. 43.5% were normotensive (NT; SBP<120mmHg; DBP<80mmHg) and 31.5% were hypertensive (HT; SBP>140mmHg; DBP>90mmHg). After confounding factors were removed (NT-OM and NT-OM), the relative abundance of total oral nitrate-reducing bacteria (ONRB; determined using 16S rRNA, sequencing) and oral nitrate reducing activity (ONRA; determined using high-performance liquid chromatography; HPLC) increased in HT-OM (N=15) compared to NT-OM (N=24) (P=0.031). In agreement, some nitrate reducing bacterial species were higher, such as Neisseria flavescens however, Neisseria subflava were lower in HT-OM (P<0.05). Using strict protocols, primary care dental clinics can therefore reliably identify undiagnosed hypertension alongside changes to the oral microbiome. However, given that functional species-level differences may not align with expected systemic changes, further research is needed before dental clinics use oral microbiome screening to identify specific bacteria for guiding oral hygiene to manage hypertension.

title: Atypical MPO-ANCA–Associated Vasculitis Presenting as Acute Tubulointerstitial Nephritis and Cardiac Involvement: A Case Report
authorString: Ying H, Zhu R, Wu H, Chen S, Gao X.
abstractText: Background Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV) usually presents with pauci-immune necrotizing and crescentic glomerulonephritis, hematuria, and rapidly progressive kidney dysfunction. However, AAV may rarely manifest as tubulointerstitial-dominant renal injury without hematuria, creating diagnostic uncertainty. Cardiac involvement in AAV can also mimic acute coronary syndrome, particularly when dynamic electrocardiographic changes and elevated cardiac biomarkers are present. Case presentation: A 64-year-old man with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with severe oliguric acute kidney injury and acute left heart failure. Urinalysis showed predominantly tubular proteinuria without hematuria. After continuous renal replacement therapy, his heart failure improved substantially, but dynamic electrocardiographic changes and marked Troponin I elevation to 1.6 ng/mL developed on hospital day 3. Coronary angiography revealed moderate left anterior descending artery stenosis of 60–70%, which was insufficient to explain the extent of myocardial injury. MPO-ANCA was strongly positive at 215.6 AU/mL. Kidney biopsy demonstrated predominant acute tubulointerstitial nephritis with relative glomerular sparing and pauci-immune immunofluorescence, supporting a diagnosis of microscopic polyangiitis with atypical renal involvement. Although heart failure had improved, cardiac biomarkers continued to rise before subsequently normalizing in parallel with ANCA decline, suggesting vasculitis-driven myocardial injury. The patient received double filtration plasmapheresis combined with immunosuppressive therapy. ANCA titers rapidly normalized, cardiac biomarkers improved, and the patient was gradually weaned off renal replacement therapy. Conclusion This case illustrates an unusual presentation of MPO-ANCA-associated microscopic polyangiitis with tubulointerstitial-dominant nephritis without hematuria and concurrent cardiac involvement mimicking acute coronary syndrome. Improvement in volume overload or heart failure does not exclude ongoing vasculitis-related myocardial injury. In patients with unexplained acute kidney injury and concurrent myocardial injury, AAV should be considered even when hematuria is absent, and early ANCA testing, kidney biopsy, and timely immunosuppressive therapy may be crucial for organ recovery.

title: Role of ivabradine in postoperative tachyarrhythmias after congenital cardiac surgery
authorString: Mohsin M, khokar RA, Adil F, Waseem M, Batool A, Sheikh AS.
abstractText: BACKGROUND Postoperative tachyarrhythmias are a common complication following congenital cardiac surgery. Junctional ectopic tachycardia (JET) is the most frequent arrhythmia, often linked to heightened automaticity. Ivabradine, a selective inhibitor of the funny current (HCN4), has recently gained attention for its potential role in managing automatic tachyarrhythmias. Standard antiarrhythmic therapies, such as amiodarone, are limited by significant side effects. METHODS This retrospective study was conducted at a high-volume cardiac center between January 2024 and June 2025. 55 patients developed postoperative tachyarrhythmias who were treated with ivabradine at 0.2 mg/kg/dose, either as monotherapy or in combination with other antiarrhythmic agents. Patients with postoperative ventricular tachycardia were excluded. RESULTS Among 55 patients, the most common arrhythmia was JET (n = 42), followed by ectopic atrial tachycardia (n = 5), premature atrial contractions (n = 5), and inappropriate sinus tachycardia (n = 3). Overall, 69% of patients were successfully managed with ivabradine monotherapy, while 31% required adjunctive therapy, most commonly amiodarone. Patients requiring adjunctive therapy were more difficult to achieve rhythm control and had longer ICU and hospital durations (72 hours vs 24 hours, p < 0.001). No significant hemodynamic compromise or adverse effects associated with ivabradine were observed. CONCLUSION Ivabradine monotherapy is effective for the majority of postoperative automaticity-driven tachyarrhythmias in patients undergoing congenital cardiac surgery who are hemodynamically stable. However, adjuvant therapy to ivabradine might be needed, especially in patients at risk for deteriorated condition.

title: Interleukin 6 and high sensitive C reactive protein in predicting in-stent restenosis in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention
authorString: Bouzidi N, Majed H, Abdennebi HB.
abstractText: Background and Aims: In-stent restenosis (ISR) remains a major limitation of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Inflammatory biomarkers such as interleukin-6 (IL-6) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) may contribute to ISR pathogenesis. This study aimed to evaluate the predictive value of IL-6, hsCRP, and the Gensini score (GS) for ISR in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) undergoing drug-eluting stent implantation. Methods and Results : A total of 262 CAD patients treated with PCI were enrolled. Patients were classified into ISR (n=107) and non-ISR (n=155) groups. ISR was assessed by protocol-driven coronary angiography performed between 6 and 12 months in all patients. Clinical, angiographic, and biochemical parameters were assessed. IL-6 and hsCRP levels were measured pre-procedurally, and CAD severity was evaluated by the Gensini score. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to determine predictive values. Serum IL-6, hsCRP levels, and GS values were significantly higher in the ISR group when compared with No ISR group (p=0.012, p=0.017, and p=0.032, respectively). ROC analysis showed moderate predictive value for IL-6 (AUC=0.717, p=0.012) and GS (AUC=0.674, p=0.040), whereas hsCRP did not reach statistical significance (AUC=0.602, p=0.171). Conclusions: Elevated IL-6 and increased GS were significantly associated with ISR, highlighting the importance of both systemic inflammation and angiographic CAD severity in restenosis risk. ClinicalTrials.gov Number: NCT03075566 (09/03/2017).

title: Expedient protocol for myocardial viability assessment with 18 F-FDG positron emission tomography
authorString: Ma J, Ozkan E, Alavi MH, Jain S, Parihar AS, Schindler TH.
abstractText: Background We assessed image quality by applying an expedient metabolic preparation period (eMPP) combining simultaneous intravenous insulin and 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose ( 18 F-FDG) administration without requiring a specific plasma glucose target for PET myocardial viability imaging in patients with ischemic cardiomyopathy. Methods Expedient MPP for cardiac 18 F-FDG uptake was assessed from the time of intravenous infusion of 12.5 or 25 gram of 50% dextrose to the time of 18 F-FDG injection. Cardiac 18 F-FDG image quality was analyzed according to a 5-point scoring system (5 = excellent to 1 = non-diagnostic) by two independent observers where consensus was achieved in joint reading for cases of disagreement. Further, 58 patients, who underwent the prior standard and MPP (sMPP) for i.v. glucose loading and insulin administration for 18 F -FDG PET, served for comparison. Results Eighty-nine consecutive patients (age: 62.5 ± 12.1 yrs, men n = 74 and women n = 15) underwent rest 99m Tc-tetrofosmin SPECT/CT and 18 F-FDG PET/CT for the evaluation of myocardial viability. Comparing eMPP and sMPP, the quality scores were excellent in 48% vs. 48%, very good in 26% vs. 24%, good in 16% vs. 10%, fair in 6% vs. 5%, and non-diagnostic in 3% vs. 5%. The mean quality score was not significantly different between eMPP and sMPP (4.10 ± 1.10 vs 4.13 ± 1.17; p = 0.810). As regards the eMPP in diabetic and non-diabetic patients, the quality scores were excellent in 50% vs. 46%, very good in 25% vs. 27%, good in 10% vs. 27%, fair in 10%% vs. 0%, and non-diagnostic in 5% vs. 0%, while the quality score was widely comparable among groups (4.05 ± 1.23 vs 4.18 ± 0.87; p = 0.731). The average MPP was significantly less in the eMPP than in the sMPP group (35 ± 12 vs. 68 ± 19 min; p < 0.0001). Conclusions Using an eMPP after intravenous infusion of dextrose by combining “simultaneous” intravenous insulin and 18 F-FDG administration without requiring a specific plasma glucose target, reduces the MPP by 52% compared to prior standard protocol, while maintaining image quality.

title: Effect of radical (chemo)radiotherapy on cardiovascular autonomic function in patients with head and neck cancer: a prospective observational study
authorString: Khan AA, Kumar S, Gupta S, Joseph D, Kulshrestha P, Saini PK, Kashyap A, Singh A, Gupta M.
abstractText: Purpose Radiotherapy for head and neck cancer irradiates the carotid sinus, yet early effects on cardiovascular autonomic function are poorly described. We prospectively evaluated autonomic function before, at the end of, and six months after definitive radiotherapy with or without concurrent chemotherapy. Methods Thirty-one adults aged 18–74 years with squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity, oropharynx, larynx or hypopharynx underwent autonomic function testing at baseline, at the end of treatment and at six months. Each session included a ten-minute supine recording for heart rate and blood pressure variability, followed by deep breathing, Valsalva manoeuvre, lying-to-standing, isometric handgrip and cold pressor tests. Repeated-measures analysis of variance and paired t-tests were used; analyses were exploratory and unadjusted for multiple comparisons. Results Twenty-nine patients completed the end-of-treatment assessment and seventeen the six-month assessment. High-frequency power of heart rate variability was higher than baseline at the end of treatment (P = 0.040) and at six months (P = 0.012). Systolic and diastolic blood pressure and their low-frequency variability increased at the end of treatment but not at six months. Deep breathing, Valsalva, lying-to-standing and handgrip responses did not change. The cold pressor diastolic response showed no overall change (P = 0.093); an isolated baseline-to-six-month difference (P = 0.049) indicated a smaller pressor rise. Conclusion Within six months, conventional autonomic reflex tests showed no significant deterioration, and changes in resting variability were mostly transient. These exploratory findings do not establish baroreflex dysfunction; longer follow-up with direct measurement of baroreflex sensitivity is needed.

title: Subjective, Behavioral, and Physiological Responses to Cognitive Workload in Individuals with Chronic Non-Specific Low Back Pain and Healthy Controls
authorString: Rastgordani Z, Mokhtarinia HR, Vahedi M, Melloh M.
abstractText: Background Cognitive workload can influence performance and physiological responses during computer-based work, but these responses remain insufficiently understood in individuals with chronic non-specific low back pain (CNSLBP). This study investigated subjective, behavioral, electromyographic, and cardiac responses to increasing cognitive workload in individuals with CNSLBP and healthy controls during a dual-task computer-based paradigm. Methods Thirty participants, including 15 individuals with CNSLBP and 15 healthy controls, completed four experimental conditions combining two typing-speed levels and two cognitive workload levels. Subjective workload was assessed using the NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX). Behavioral performance and typing errors were recorded, while physiological responses were assessed using facial electromyography (EMG) and heart rate. Outcomes were analyzed using mixed repeated-measures analysis of variance to examine the effects of experimental condition, group, and their interaction. Results Increasing task demands significantly increased perceived workload (F = 34.63, p < 0.001) and reduced behavioral performance (F = 31.12, p < 0.001), whereas typing errors did not change significantly. No significant between-group differences were observed in perceived workload or behavioral performance. In contrast, participants with CNSLBP exhibited significantly greater RMS activity in the corrugator supercilii and frontalis muscles (both p < 0.001), and a significant condition × group interaction was observed for corrugator RMS (p = 0.018). Heart rate did not differ significantly across experimental conditions or between groups. Conclusions Individuals with CNSLBP maintained subjective workload ratings and behavioral performance comparable to healthy controls but exhibited greater facial muscle activation during task performance. These findings suggest that maintaining performance under cognitive demands may require greater physiological effort in individuals with CNSLBP. Multimodal assessment combining subjective, behavioral, and physiological measures may provide a more comprehensive understanding of cognitive workload responses in people with chronic low back pain.

title: Integrated Computational Prioritization and Characterization of Structurally Distinct Putative AT1R Ligands from a Cardiovascular-Focused Chemical Library
authorString: Rahman M, Hossain M, Hasan R, Qurishi ZA, Biswas MMA, Zubair TH, Keya LA, Hossen MS.
abstractText: Hypertension remains a major contributor to the global burden of cardiovascular disease, motivating the exploration of chemically diverse angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) ligands. This study applied an integrated computer-aided drug design (CADD) workflow to prioritize candidate ligands from a cardiovascular-focused ChemDiv library containing 23,000 compounds. Molecular docking was performed against AT1R (PDB ID: 4ZUD), using olmesartan (PubChem CID: 158781) as the reference ligand. Redocking reproduced the crystallographic pose with an RMSD of 1.01 Å. The 15 highest-ranked compounds based on docking scores were subjected to post-docking MM-GBSA analysis, and nine with more favorable predicted MM-GBSA energy estimates were advanced to physicochemical, pharmacokinetic, drug-likeness, and toxicity assessments. Three compounds (CIDs: 3825369, 53151618, and 71841126) were selected for further characterization using ligand-based structural analysis, density functional theory, exploratory AT2R docking, and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations. Their docking scores ranged from −9.054 to −9.096 kcal/mol, compared with −8.556 kcal/mol for olmesartan. Fingerprint-based analysis indicated low structural similarity to olmesartan (Tanimoto coefficients: 0.132–0.181). The molecular dynamics analyses revealed compound-dependent differences in conformational behavior and protein–ligand interaction profiles. CID 3825369 and CID 53151618 showed comparatively consistent profiles across the evaluated computational analyses, whereas the results for CID 71841126 showed greater variation in selected dynamic and energetic descriptors. These findings identify structurally distinct computational candidates for further experimental investigation of AT1R ligand activity. However, experimental validation is required to determine receptor binding, functional activity, selectivity, and therapeutic relevance.

title: Changes in the apoptotic index, along with gene and protein expression levels, in splenomegaly due to portal vein stenosis in rats.
authorString: Zhang H, Lu J, Li J, Zhao B, Zhong Y, Chu H, Xu Y, Liu T.
abstractText:
Background

The spleen is an important peripheral immune organ, and splenomegaly (SM) is a common complication of portal hypertension. However, the regulatory mechanisms underlying splenic apoptosis remain poorly understood.

Materials and methods

A portal vein stenosis-induced SM model was established in Sprague-Dawley rats, using a sham-operated (SO) group as the control. Apoptotic changes in splenic tissue cells were evaluated using the terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick end labeling (TUNEL) assay, immunohistochemistry staining, quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) analysis, and western blot analysis.

Results

Compared with the SO group, the SM group had a significantly higher proportion of apoptotic cells and higher mRNA expression levels of the pro-apoptotic Bax, caspase-3, and caspase-9 genes, whereas the proportion of apoptotic cells and mRNA expression levels of anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 were significantly lower in the SM group. The protein expression levels of pro-apoptotic Bax, caspase-3, and caspase-9 were significantly increased in the SM group compared with the SO group. Transmission electron microscopy imaging revealed that macrophages of rats with SM had swollen mitochondria, marginated chromatin, and pyknotic nuclei.

Conclusion

In rat SM, the concurrent activation of pro-apoptotic pathways and anti-apoptotic pathways leads to increased cell apoptosis. This suggests that an imbalance in the Bax/Bcl-2 ratio promotes apoptosis through the mitochondrial pathway.

title: Online high-dose hemodiafiltration: a path towards improved clinical outcomes and green dialysis.
authorString: Kotanko P, Ficociello LH, van der Sande F.

journal.title: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension

abstractText:
Purpose of review

There are concerns that online high-dose hemodiafiltration (HDF) is particularly resource-intensive and environmentally challenging. It has recently been suggested that HDF consumes more water and generates more plastic waste than expanded hemodialysis (HDx) using medium cut-off membranes. To further address this matter, we examined the available evidence on water use and plastic waste generation across high-flux hemodialysis, HDx, and HDF.

Recent findings

Our analysis reveals that plastic waste generation is lowest with HDF and highest with HDx: modern HDF dialyzers weigh on average 36% less than MCO dialyzers, and online HDF requires no saline bags, together saving approximately 68-123  kg of plastic per 1000 sessions compared to HDx. Regarding water, online high-dose HDF may use less water than HD or HDx if dialysate flow is minimized/optimized (-8% vs. hemodialysis at standard European dialysate flow; -12.6% in a US setting). Individualization of dialysate flow reduces water consumption by a further 27.8% without compromising dialysis adequacy.

Summary

Despite the suggestive 'high-dose' attribute in its name, online high-dose HDF with optimized dialysate flow may use less water and generates substantially less plastic waste than HDx. These findings challenge the view that HDF adoption is environmentally costly and indicate that HDF is a meaningful step towards green dialysis.

title: Hyponatremic-Hypertensive Syndrome as a Rare Manifestation of Renovascular Hypertension: A Case Series.
authorString: Bujanowicz A, Michalczewska A, Pytlos J, Skrzypczyk P.

journal.title: The American journal of case reports

abstractText: BACKGROUND Hyponatremic-hypertensive syndrome is a rare but distinctive manifestation of renal ischemia caused by unilateral renal artery stenosis. It is characterized by severe arterial hypertension accompanied by hyponatremia, hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, and polyuria, resulting from complex interactions between the ischemic kidney and the contralateral functioning kidney. Owing to its rarity and potentially life-threatening course, early recognition and appropriate management are crucial. The purpose of this report is to highlight the clinical presentation, diagnostic challenges, and therapeutic outcomes in pediatric patients. CASE REPORT We describe the cases of 2 girls, aged 4 and 9 years, who presented with severe hypertension and electrolyte disturbances secondary to unilateral right renal artery stenosis. Both patients exhibited typical biochemical features, including hyponatremia, hypokalemia, and elevated renin-aldosterone activity. Imaging studies confirmed significant unilateral renal artery stenosis due to fibromuscular dysplasia, with renal asymmetry. In the younger patient, progressive clinical deterioration and complete renal artery occlusion necessitated nephrectomy, resulting in resolution of hypertension and electrolyte abnormalities. In the older patient, percutaneous transluminal renal angioplasty was successful, leading to normalization of blood pressure, restoration of renal size symmetry, and sustained clinical remission at 1-year follow-up. CONCLUSIONS Hyponatremic-hypertensive syndrome should be considered in any child with severe hypertension accompanied by electrolyte disturbances, polyuria, and polydipsia. These 2 cases of girls with fibromuscular dysplasia underscore the importance of early recognition and individualized management strategies in pediatric renovascular hypertension. Prompt diagnosis and definitive treatment of renal artery stenosis, either by revascularization or nephrectomy when appropriate, can be curative and prevent severe morbidity. It is important to note that the course of HHS can vary among patients depending on their age, the severity, and the location of the stenosis.

title: Associations with SARS-CoV-2 Positivity Among People in Refugee Settlements
authorString: Muwonge TR, Klabbers RE, Ajidiru S, Pham P, Vinck P, Mujugira A, Nsubuga R, Sharma M, Borthakur S, Mohammed N, Ratanshi PR, Celum C, O’Laughlin KN.
abstractText:
Introduction:

Limited SARS-CoV-2 testing capacity during the early COVID-19 pandemic required approaches to identify individuals at highest risk of infection for prioritized testing. We assessed the association between symptoms and exposures reported at the time of SARS-CoV-2 testing and test positivity among individuals referred for testing through an interactive voice response (IVR) platform in refugee settlements in Uganda. Methods. We used Dial-COVID, a multilingual, toll-free interactive voice response (IVR) platform to survey residents of refugee settlements in Uganda regarding COVID-19 symptoms, exposures, and comorbidities. Respondents reporting symptoms or exposures were invited for SARS-CoV-2 testing using nasal or oropharyngeal swab specimens. At the time of testing, an interviewer-administered questionnaire assessed symptoms and exposures occurring within the preceding two weeks. Log-binomial regression was used to identify factors associated with SARS-CoV-2 positivity. Results. Between February 2021 and March 2022, 6,913 of 15,467 Dial-COVID callers (44.7%) completed the IVR survey. Among survey respondents, 5,184 (75.0%) reported at least one symptom or exposure. Of these, 1,361 (26.3%) were invited for testing, and samples were collected from 751 (55.2%) within seven days of survey completion. SARS-CoV-2 test results were available for 741 individuals, of whom 48 tested positive (6.5%). Among symptoms reported at the testing visit, severe muscle pain (risk ratio [RR] 2.08; 95% CI 1.20–3.57) and unusual fatigue (RR 2.34; 95% CI 1.36–4.03) were associated with SARS-CoV-2 positivity in unadjusted analyses. After adjustment for sex, refugee status, hypertension, and diabetes, only unusual fatigue remained independently associated with a positive test result (aRR 2.10, 95% CI 1.20–3.67). Conclusion. Few self-reported symptoms were associated with SARS-CoV-2 positivity, highlighting the challenges of prioritizing testing based on symptoms alone. IVR-based platforms may provide a feasible approach for screening, surveillance, and linkage to testing in resource-constrained humanitarian settings.

title: Retinal biomarkers and dementia risk: A review of evidence across the 14 Lancet modifiable risk factors for dementia
authorString: Barrett-Young A.
abstractText: As the only central nervous system tissue that can be directly imaged non-invasively using widely available technology, the retina offers a uniquely accessible window into the brain. Quantitative retinal measures can be derived at scale and have been associated with mechanistic processes in the brain and throughout the body, positioning retinal biomarkers as promising tools for dementia prevention and intervention research. Evidence indicates that several retinal biomarkers can distinguish individuals with Alzheimer’s disease (AD) from cognitively healthy controls; however, it remains unclear whether these markers reflect preclinical AD-specific pathology or broader profiles of dementia risk, particularly in the earliest stages of disease. This review synthesises current evidence on retinal microvascular and neuronal morphological biomarkers and their associations with 14 modifiable dementia risk factors identified by the Lancet Commission on dementia. Robust evidence indicates that retinal biomarkers are influenced by vascular and metabolic risks, specifically hypertension and diabetes. However, associations with other modifiable risk factors, including social isolation, lower educational attainment, hearing loss, smoking, air pollution, and traumatic brain injury, are sparse or absent. Critical research gaps persist regarding how, when, and for whom the retina reflects vascular and metabolic risk factors, and whether non-biological risk factors, such as social isolation and educational attainment, are better understood as independent or confounding variables than as direct biological determinants of retinal biomarkers. Clarifying these associations is essential to establish retinal biomarkers as scalable, non-invasive indicators of dementia risk and to support their integration into targeted risk stratification, early detection, and preventive intervention studies.

title: Safety of Early Mobilisation and Rehabilitation in Critically Ill Patients: A Prospective Multicentre Cohort Study
authorString: Parada-Gereda HM, Bustos J, Duarte MP, Ruiz C, Avendaño JM, Rojas N, Mogollón P, V DS, Ortíz M, Melo JE, Alfonso FA, Ayala A, Castañeda M, Chaverra RM, Medina-Parra J, Benavides-Cruz J, Gaitán-Duarte H.
abstractText: Background Early mobilisation and rehabilitation have become increasingly integrated into the care of critically ill patients. However, uncertainty remains regarding their safety in patients at increased haemodynamic risk, particularly those requiring vasopressor support. Evaluating safety events during these interventions and their associated factors in routine clinical practice may provide evidence to guide their implementation in this population. Methods This prospective multicentre cohort study was conducted in tertiary intensive care units (ICUs). Adult patients undergoing a structured early mobilisation and rehabilitation protocol were included. Patients could contribute multiple mobilisation sessions, resulting in repeated observations within individuals. Clinical characteristics, session-related variables, safety events and mobility levels, assessed using the ICU Mobility Scale (IMS), were recorded. Descriptive statistics were used to summarise the data. Exploratory analyses examined the association between vasopressor use and the occurrence of safety events using generalised estimating equation (GEE) models, with patients specified as the clustering unit to account for within-patient correlation across repeated sessions. Results A total of 262 patients (mean age 60 ± 19 years; 52% female) underwent 1,136 mobilisation and rehabilitation sessions. Passive and active in-bed mobilisation accounted for 32.8% and 26.4% of sessions, respectively. Overall, 26 safety events occurred (2.3% of sessions), predominantly oxygen desaturation (n = 7), hypotension (n = 6), hypertension (n = 6) and simple arrhythmias (n = 5). No safety event required session termination, and only one necessitated a transient increase in vasopressor support. Vasopressors were administered during 20.4% of sessions. In the overall GEE analysis, vasopressor use was not significantly associated with safety events (odds ratio 1.71; 95% confidence interval 0.81–3.59). Conclusions Safety events were infrequent during early mobilisation and rehabilitation in critically ill patients. Most events were transient, and none required session termination. No statistically significant association was observed between vasopressor use and safety events. These findings provide pragmatic data on the occurrence of safety events during mobilisation under the clinical conditions studied, while the observational design limits causal inference.

title: Demographics, Therapeutic Efficacy, and Comorbid Burden in Pityriasis Rubra Pilaris: Insights from a Retrospective Cohort
authorString: Silva ACe, Keum H, Veshagh A, Greiling TM.
abstractText: Pityriasis rubra pilaris (PRP) is a rare, severe inflammatory skin disorder characterized by follicular papules, papulosquamous red-orange plaques, and palmoplantar keratoderma. Despite its clinical significance, epidemiological data on PRP remains scarce, there is no FDA-approved therapy, and comorbid conditions are unclear. This study analyzed a cohort of 74 patients with PRP at Oregon Health & Science University using a retrospective chart review from January 2013 to December 2023. Juvenile onset PRP (n = 12) represented 1 in 2,863 unique patients to dermatology, with a mean (SD) age at diagnosis of 9.0 (4.6) years. Adult onset PRP (n = 62) represented 1 in 1,798 unique patients seen by dermatology, with a mean (SD) age at diagnosis of 56.8 (15.2) years. Of the total cohort, 45/74 (60.8%) were male, and 29/74 (39.2%) were female sex (Fig. 1). Within the juvenile-onset group, 6/12 (50%) were male and 6/12 (50%) were female sex. Within the adult-onset group, 39/62 (62.9%) were male and 23/62 (37.1%) were female sex. The majority of patients self-identified as White. Half of juvenile-onset patients and over 90% of adult onset patients were treated with systemic therapy. Biologic therapies, particularly IL-17 inhibitors and IL-23 inhibitors demonstrated the highest treatment efficacy with good responses in adult patients of 57.1% and 64.7% respectively. The oral agents methotrexate and acitretin were commonly prescribed to adult patients but had lower efficacy, with good response rates of 26.3% and 29.2% respectively. Comorbidities included common conditions such as hypertension, hyperlipidemia, type 2 diabetes, obesity, anxiety, depression, and sleep disorders. It remains unclear whether these are more common in PRP or simply reflect the demographics of the cohort. This study provides insight into the prevalence, epidemiology, treatment outcomes, and comorbidities of PRP.

title: Prevalence, Socioeconomic Determinants, and Health-System Factors Associated with Laboratory-Confirmed Renal Impairment Among Adults Attending Tertiary Referral Hospitals in Mogadishu, Somalia: A Cross-Sectional Study
authorString: RN MBAMA, almis H.
abstractText: Background Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is an important and growing public health challenge that disproportionately affects populations in low- and middle-income countries. Limited diagnostic capacity, constrained access to care, and socioeconomic disadvantage contribute to delayed diagnosis and poor clinical outcomes. In Somalia, evidence describing the burden and determinants of CKD remains limited despite the increasing prevalence of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and other non-communicable diseases (NCDs). This study estimated the prevalence of renal impairment among adults attending tertiary referral hospitals in Mogadishu, identified associated socioeconomic and clinical factors, and examined health system barriers to kidney care. Methods A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted between April and July 2026 in two tertiary referral hospitals in Mogadishu, Somalia. Systematic sampling was used to screen 312 adult outpatients, resulting in 200 participants with complete clinical, laboratory, and questionnaire data for analysis. Renal function was assessed using serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), urine protein dipstick testing, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) calculated using the 2021 CKD-EPI race-free equation. Multivariable binary logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with renal impairment, with results reported as adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Among the 200 participants, 145 (72.5%) had reduced eGFR (<60 mL/min/1.73 m²), 168 (84.0%) had elevated serum creatinine, 158 (79.0%) had proteinuria on dipstick testing, and 117 (58.5%) had elevated BUN concentrations. Overall, 128 participants (64.0%) reported a previous clinical diagnosis of CKD. Socioeconomic disadvantage was common, with 130 (65.0%) reporting a monthly household income below USD 100 and 110 (55.0%) having no formal education. Independent factors associated with renal impairment included age ≥48 years (aOR = 2.85; 95% CI: 1.42–5.72; p = 0.003), hypertension (aOR = 3.15; 95% CI: 1.58–6.28; p = 0.001), diabetes mellitus (aOR = 2.48; 95% CI: 1.25–4.92; p = 0.009), frequent use of non-prescribed non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) (aOR = 2.21; 95% CI: 1.12–4.36; p = 0.022), and treatment non-adherence (aOR = 1.95; 95% CI: 1.02–3.73; p = 0.043). Conclusions Renal impairment was common among adults attending two tertiary referral hospitals in Mogadishu and was strongly associated with established cardiometabolic risk factors, frequent non-prescribed NSAID use, and indicators of socioeconomic disadvantage. These findings suggest opportunities to strengthen early detection and management of kidney disease through integration of routine renal assessment within primary care and NCD services, expansion of diagnostic capacity under Somalia's Essential Package of Health Services (EPHS 2020), improved regulation of nephrotoxic medications, and enhanced community-based screening and referral within the national Universal Health Coverage (UHC) agenda. Trial registration: Not applicable

title: Educational inequalities in multimorbidity among older adults in China: an underreporting-corrected analysis using CHARLS
authorString: Fu X, Feng L, Shen Z, Tarimo CS, Zhang J, Qin J, Song X, Zhang H, Lv T, Ma Y, Zhao Y, Ye B.
abstractText: Background Educational attainment is a key social determinant of health inequalities in later life. However, most previous studies of the relationship between education and multimorbidity have relied on self-reported physician diagnoses. Such reliance may underestimate the true burden of chronic conditions and bias the assessment of education-related inequalities. Methods We analyzed five waves (2011–2020) of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, comprising an analytic sample of 6,906 adults aged 60 years or older at baseline. Self-reported multimorbidity was defined from participants’ reports of physician-diagnosed chronic conditions. To address potential underreporting, we drew on objectively measured blood pressure, fasting glucose, glycated hemoglobin, and lipid biomarkers to identify underreported cases of hypertension, diabetes, and dyslipidemia, and constructed an underreporting-corrected multimorbidity outcome. Generalized estimating equations were used to assess the association between education attainment and multimorbidity and to compare the education-by-age interaction across outcome definitions. Logistic regression was applied to identify factors associated with chronic disease underreporting. Results At baseline, the prevalence of self-reported multimorbidity was 45.40%, rising to 62.93% after correction for underreporting. Underreporting rates for hypertension, diabetes, and dyslipidemia were 16.25%, 7.01%, and 31.29%, respectively. When multimorbidity was based on self-reported diagnoses, the education-by-age interaction was not statistically significant ( P  = 0.762). By contrast, this interaction became statistically significant when using the underreporting-corrected multimorbidity measure ( P  = 0.019). Further analyses showed that older age was associated with higher odds of underreported hypertension and any chronic disease underreporting. Female sex was associated with higher odds of underreported dyslipidemia and any underreporting, whereas having a high school education or above was associated with lower odds of underreported dyslipidemia. Conclusions Reliance on self-reported information alone may substantially underestimate the burden of multimorbidity among older adults in China and obscure education-related health inequalities. Future research on healthy ageing and health equity should explicitly account for chronic disease underreporting and its social patterning so as not to understate the impact of educational disadvantage on later-life health.

title: Protein lactylation in atherosclerosis - Mechanisms and therapeutic potential: A narrative review.
authorString: Zou L, Zhu Y, Lan Y, Cheng Y, Han B, Chen J, Qin C, Cheng D.
abstractText: Protein lactylation, which links cellular metabolism to gene regulation and protein function, may influence atherosclerosis. This narrative review explores its cellular mechanisms and therapeutic potential. We searched PubMed from inception to September 30, 2026, for English-language studies and reviews. The synthesis differentiated lactylation from lactate signaling and distinguished direct evidence in atherosclerosis from findings in other disease models. Predominantly preclinical evidence suggests that both histone and non-histone lactylation are involved in endothelial inflammation, endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition, macrophage polarization and ferroptosis, and vascular smooth muscle cell senescence, phenotypic remodeling, and calcification. Depending on the cellular context, modification site, and downstream targets, lactylation can either promote vascular injury or support anti-inflammatory responses and plaque stabilization. Candidate interventions target lactate production, transport, and lactylation-related enzymes, but their effects often lack specificity for lactylation. Much of the therapeutic evidence originates from non-atherosclerotic models, and clinical validation is currently absent. Therefore, therapeutic development should consider cell type, disease stage, and modification site, with validation of causal mechanisms, selectivity, and safety in atherosclerosis models prior to clinical translation.

title: Circulating Immune and Cancer Driver Gene Biomarkers Precede Prostate Cancer Diagnosis by over 10 yr.
authorString: Huang Z, Parsaeian M, Viallon V, Wang Z, Papier K, Desai T, Chan WC, Collister JA, Breeur M, Tong TYN, Cabrera-Castro N, Guevara M, Jimenez-Zabala A, Johansson M, Kolijn PM, Lill CM, Mills IG, Sacerdote C, Tumino R, Zamora-Ros R, Chatterjee N, Platz EA, Ferrari P, Gunter MJ, Riboli E, Atkins JR, Smith-Byrne K, Travis RC.
abstractText:
Background and objective

Prospective proteomic and proteogenomic studies may enhance the understanding of proteins associated with prostate cancer (PCa) development.

Methods

In a case-cohort study within the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC), baseline plasma samples from 982 incident PCa cases and 1573 subcohort participants were profiled using the SomaScan 7k platform (over 6000 proteins). Associations were estimated using Prentice-weighted Cox models. The coprimary end points were incident overall PCa and aggressive PCa (n = 290). Findings were evaluated in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) study and supported by Mendelian randomization (MR) and exome gene-burden analyses.

Key findings and limitations

ACP3, FLT4, and KLK3 were associated with overall PCa risk (hazard ratio [HR] per 1 standard deviation [SD] increase were 1.20 [1.10-1.31], 1.26 [1.13-1.40], and 2.28 [1.96-2.65], respectively). Seven proteins were associated with aggressive PCa risk, with ANKRD1 consistently associated across multiple clinically relevant disease subtypes. Twelve proteins were associated with PCa diagnosed >15 yr after blood draw, including ANXA2, GZMK, and OSCAR. ACP3, ANXA2, APOC2, and KLK3 showed consistent associations in both EPIC and ARIC. Additionally, four proteins had support from MR analyses and eight from rare-variant burden tests. Circulating products of established PCa driver genes, including ERBB3, KRAS, and NRAS, were associated with future aggressive disease. Limitations include incomplete external replication and differences in end point availability across cohorts.

Conclusions and clinical implications

Prospective plasma proteomic analyses identified circulating proteins associated with future PCa risk, including proteins related to immune, adhesion, angiogenesis, and PCa driver-gene pathways. These findings identify candidate protein risk factors for overall and clinically significant PCa, and warrant further validation and mechanistic evaluation.

title: Deletion of LRP1 in Smooth Muscle Cells Induces Infrarenal Aortic Aneurysms in Mice
authorString: Franklin MK, Fan G, Li B, Wang P, Howatt DA, Moorleghen JJ, Mullick AE, Daugherty A, Lu HS.
abstractText:
ABSTRACT

Background

Low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 1 (LRP1) in smooth muscle cells (SMCs) is essential for maintaining aortic wall integrity. This study investigated whether deletion of LRP1 in SMCs induces region-specific aortic pathology and evaluated a potential therapeutic strategy.

Methods

Lrp1 -floxed mice were bred with Sm22-Cre +/0 mice to generate mice with SMC-LRP1 deletion (SMC-LRP1-/-) and wild-type littermates (SMC-LRP1+/+). Micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) was used to visualize the aorta, and aortic tissue sections were characterized histologically. To evaluate a potential therapeutic strategy, antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) targeting hepatocyte-derived angiotensinogen (AGT) were administered to inhibit AGT synthesis.

Results

Immunostaining and Western blotting confirmed LRP1 deletion in aortic SMCs. At 40 weeks of age, micro-CT revealed marked increases in aortic width and volume. Although dilatation occurred throughout the aorta, the infrarenal region exhibited the greatest expansion in both male and female SMC-LRP1-/-mice compared with SMC-LRP1+/+ littermates; subsequent analyses therefore focused on this region. LRP1 deletion in SMCs caused pronounced SMC loss and increased collagen deposition in the infrarenal aorta. Inhibition of hepatocyte-derived AGT with ASO attenuated infrarenal aortic dilatation and preserved aortic wall integrity in both male and female mice.

Conclusions

Deletion of LRP1 in SMCs causes progressive aortic dilatation that includes the infrarenal aorta. Pharmacologic inhibition of hepatocyte-derived AGT attenuates infrarenal aortic dilatation.

What Are the Clinical Implications?

Deletion of low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 1 (LRP1) in smooth muscle cells (SMCs) causes diffuse aortic dilatation, with spontaneous aneurysm formation most prominent in the infrarenal abdominal aorta—the most common site of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs) in humans. Given the strong association between LRP1 variants and human AAAs, these findings identify SMC-derived LRP1 as a critical contributor to aortic wall integrity and provide a valuable tool for investigating disease mechanisms. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of hepatocyte-derived angiotensinogen with an antisense oligonucleotide significantly attenuated infrarenal aortic dilatation, highlighting a promising therapeutic strategy for AAAs.

GRAPHIC ABSTRACT

title: Toxic metals, lung function, blood pressure and arterial function in young adults: a multi- ethnic cross-sectional study
authorString: Talaei M, Griffiths A, Golda P, Karamanos A, Cruickshank JK, Harding S, Shaheen SO.
abstractText: Background Contemporary population-based studies of toxic metal exposure and health outcomes are lacking in the UK. We aimed to investigate associations between blood lead, cadmium and arsenic concentrations and lung function, blood pressure (BP), and arterial function in young adults. Methods In the Determinants of Adolescent Social Well-being and Health study, a multiethnic London cohort, blood lead, cadmium and arsenic concentrations were measured by Inductively Coupled Plasma Quadrupole Mass Spectrometry at 21-24.5 years of age. We analysed cross-sectional associations with lung function [Forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV 1 ), forced vital capacity (FVC), and forced expiratory flow at 25–75% of FVC (FEF 25−75 )], BP (systolic /diastolic), and arterial function [pulse wave velocity (PWV) and central augmentation index (AIx)] (N = 442–473). Results The median (range) of blood lead concentrations was 10.8 (3.39–65.4) µg/L. In multivariable adjusted models, there was a non-linear negative association between blood lead concentrations and FEV 1 /FVC and FEF 25−75 , with the steepest reduction seen at the lowest concentrations; the reduction was − 4.78% (95% CI: -7.97, -1.59) and − 0.45 L/Sec (-0.82, -0.07), respectively, comparing the top with the bottom quintiles of lead. We did not find convincing evidence for associations between cadmium or arsenic and lung function, or between lead or cadmium and BP. However, there was evidence of non-linear positive associations between lead concentration and AIx and PWV, as well as between arsenic concentrations and BP. Conclusions Even at low levels of lead exposure, higher blood lead concentrations were associated with obstructive lung function impairment and increased aortic augmentation in young adults.

title: Left atrial appendage occlusion for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation: recent evidence, catheter ablation, and future trials.
authorString: Samaras A, Nair DG, Nielsen-Kudsk JE, Tzikas A.
abstractText: Oral anticoagulation (OAC) remains the standard for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF), but bleeding, non-persistence and thromboembolism despite treatment create important unmet needs. Catheter ablation and left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) address distinct mechanisms and do not reproduce systemic anticoagulation. This narrative review covers randomized anticoagulation-withdrawal studies after ablation, trials and pooled evidence on LAAO, patients unable to sustain anticoagulation, procedural imaging and healing, post-implant antithrombotic therapy, and future trial design. Targeted searches of PubMed/MEDLINE and ClinicalTrials.gov were supplemented by citation screening and review of contemporary congress reports, for evidence spanning 2005-10 October 2026. The completed randomized LAAO programme mainly tests substitution where OAC remains feasible. Precision source control should be investigated as rescue when OAC cannot be sustained and as a potential dose-sparing complement in selected patients, while addressing residual ischemic risk and verifying durable closure.

title: Initiation of Apixaban Versus Warfarin in Patients With Kidney Failure on Hemodialysis With Newly Diagnosed Atrial Fibrillation: A Target Trial Emulation.
authorString: Winkelmayer WC, Montez-Rath ME, He M, Erickson KF, Gregg LP, Khairallah P, Chertow GM, Chang TI, Niu J.

journal.title: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation

abstractText: Patients with kidney failure on hemodialysis (KFHD) and atrial fibrillation (AF) are at high risk of ischemic stroke. Oral anticoagulation (OAC) may reduce this risk but at the expense of excess bleeding. We emulated a randomized comparative effectiveness trial of apixaban versus warfarin initiation in patients with KFHD and newly diagnosed AF. Trial emulation embedded in the US Renal Data System. Medicare-insured patients with KFHD and newly diagnosed AF without recent OAC use (2014-2019). Initiation of apixaban versus warfarin within 30 days from AF diagnosis. Ischemic stroke, clinically important bleeding (co-primary outcomes). Other thromboembolic and bleeding events, death (secondary). We compared propensity-matched new users of apixaban and warfarin using Cox proportional hazards models. Among previously OAC-naïve patients with KFHD and newly diagnosed with AF, 3985 initiated apixaban and 6426 initiated warfarin. Propensity matching 3978 apixaban users with 3978 warfarin users balanced all measured characteristics. Median CHA2DS2-VASc score was 4 (IQR: 3-5). Apixaban was initiated a median 6 (IQR: 3-12) days after AF and used for a median 58 (IQR:37-135) days; warfarin was initiated a median 5 (IQR: 2-12) days after AF and used for a median 93 (IQR:38-238) days. In intention-to-treat analyses, rates of ischemic stroke were 34% lower (HRITT=0.66; 95%CI, 0.47-0.94; p=0.02) and rates of clinically important bleeding were 28% lower (HRITT=0.72; 95%CI, 0.63-0.83; p<0.001) in patients who initiated apixaban. All-cause mortality did not differ between groups; neither did negative control outcomes of hip fracture and pneumonia. Results were robust when restricting analyses to patients with CHA2DS2-VASc score of ≥2. Potential for residual confounding. Initiating apixaban soon after newly diagnosed AF was associated with lower risks of ischemic stroke and clinically important bleeding compared with initiating warfarin.

title: Early Rhythm Control vs Usual Care After Acute Ischemic Stroke in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation.
authorString: Egashira S, Inoue K, Koga M, Toyoda K, Jensen M, Thomalla G, Toda T, Imanaka Y.
abstractText: Early rhythm control reduces cardiovascular events in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF); however, its effectiveness in the setting of acute ischemic stroke remains uncertain. We aimed to examine whether early rhythm control after acute ischemic stroke is associated with a lower risk of recurrent stroke or systemic embolism (SE) in patients with AF. This nationwide cohort study used the DeSC-IQVIA integrated database, an administrative claims database covering approximately 16 million individuals in Japan. Adults hospitalized for acute ischemic stroke with AF present at admission between 2014 and 2025 were included. The exposure was initiation of rhythm control (antiarrhythmic drugs, catheter ablation, or electrical cardioversion) within 8 weeks of admission (early rhythm control) vs no initiation (usual care), assessed at a landmark. The primary outcome was hospitalization for recurrent ischemic stroke or SE. Secondary outcomes included major bleeding, heart failure (HF) hospitalization, and all-cause mortality. Baseline differences were adjusted using propensity score overlap weighting. Cause-specific hazard ratios (HRs), cumulative incidence with death as a competing risk, and risk differences at 5 years were estimated. Among 14,355 patients who survived event-free through the 8-week landmark (median age, 83 years [IQR, 78-88]; 6,935 [48.3%] women), 268 (1.9%) received early rhythm control. During 23,583 person-years, early rhythm control was associated with a lower risk of stroke/SE (HR, 0.56; 95% CI 0.32-0.97; weighted 5-year cumulative incidence, 8.0% vs 13.8%; risk difference, -5.9 percentage points [95% CI -11.0 to 0.8]). Among secondary outcomes, no association was observed with major bleeding (HR, 1.44; 95% CI 0.74-2.82) or HF hospitalization (HR, 0.73; 95% CI 0.39-1.38); early rhythm control was associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR, 0.72; 95% CI 0.53-0.97). Results were consistent across landmark periods of 4-24 weeks. In this nationwide cohort study, early rhythm control after acute ischemic stroke in patients with AF was associated with a reduced risk of recurrent stroke or SE. These findings suggest that early rhythm control may serve as an additional secondary prevention strategy for ischemic stroke, with flexible timing of initiation. These observational findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in randomized controlled trials.

title: Obesity in Children Aged 2 to 12 Years: A Review.
authorString: Fox CK, Armstrong SC, Kelly AS.
abstractText: Obesity affects 15% of children aged 2 to 5 years and 22% of children aged 6 to 11 years in the US. Obesity in children is associated with dyslipidemia, hypertension, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, and obstructive sleep apnea. Compared with normal-weight peers, children with obesity have lower quality of life and are 5 times more likely to have obesity in adulthood. Body mass index (BMI; calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared) is used to identify children at risk for excess adiposity, and guidelines recommend that clinicians screen for obesity using BMI starting at age 2 years. Among children, obesity is defined using standardized age- and sex-specific growth charts, with obesity defined as BMI in the 95th or higher percentile and severe obesity as BMI of 120% or greater of the 95th percentile. Obesity treatment in children includes intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment, consisting of at least 26 contact hours of face-to-face group or family-based activities that incorporate nutrition, physical activity, and behavior change education delivered to the child and caregivers over a 3- to 12-month period. Intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment reduces BMI by 0.7 compared with children who do not participate in intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment. The only obesity pharmacotherapy currently approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for children younger than 12 years is setmelanotide, a melanocortin-4 receptor agonist, which is indicated for 3 forms of rare monogenic obesity (LEPR, POMC, and PCSK1 genetic variants), Bardet-Biedl syndrome, and acquired hypothalamic obesity. Liraglutide is currently only FDA approved for youth aged 12 years or older; however, a randomized clinical trial among children aged 6 to younger than 12 years demonstrated that, compared with placebo, liraglutide reduced BMI by 7.4%.
