Metabolic and bariatric surgery is rarely used in children younger than age 12 years and evidence supporting its use in children is limited. Early identification and treatment of obesity during childhood may reduce risk of type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and mortality in adulthood. Obesity in children is associated with chronic disease, such as hypertension, and with poor quality of life. Evidence-based treatment for obesity in children includes intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment, and pharmacotherapy may provide additional benefit, although short- and long-term safety and efficacy data are limited. Early identification and treatment of obesity during childhood may reduce risk of type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and mortality in adulthood.

title: Systemic Arterial Blood Pressure Targets and Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation or Death in Persistent Pulmonary Hypertension of Newborns: A Cohort Analysis.
authorString: Oren MS, Lakshminrusimha S, Bautista L, Babata K, Brown LS, Kapadia V, Makkar A.
abstractText: Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN) is a life-threatening condition requiring intensive cardiopulmonary support. The optimal systemic blood pressure target in this population remains unknown. We evaluated the association between clinician-selected mean arterial pressure (MAP) targets and in-hospital outcomes in infants with PPHN. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of infants ≥35 weeks' gestation with PPHN treated with inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) who had a clinician-documented MAP target within the first 48 hours of age. Infants were classified as having a MAP target <50 mmHg or ≥50 mmHg. The primary outcome was the composite of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) and/or death. Among 109 infants, 82 (75%) were in the MAP target group < 50 mmHg and 27 (25%) were in the ≥ 50 mmHg MAP target group. Compared with a < 50 mmHg MAP target, a ≥ 50 mmHg MAP target was associated with higher rates of ECMO cannulation (33% vs 11%, p=0.01) and ECMO/death (48% vs 20%, p<0.01). Use of epinephrine and hydrocortisone, use of more than two vasoactive agents, and the vasoactive-inotropic score were also higher in the ≥ 50 mmHg MAP target group. After adjustment for HIE, pneumothorax, and initial oxygenation index, the ≥ 50 mmHg MAP target remained associated with ECMO cannulation (aOR 4.8; 95% CI 1.6, 15.0) and ECMO/death (aOR 5.9; 95% CI 2.0, 17.3). Among neonates treated with iNO for PPHN, clinician-selected MAP targets ≥ 50 mmHg were independently associated with ECMO cannulation and ECMO/death. Randomized trials are needed to define safe MAP targets in PPHN.

title: Beyond Conventional Antihypertensives: RNA Interference, Endothelin Antagonism, and Aldosterone-Synthase Inhibition in the Current Therapeutic Landscape.
authorString: Gaudio GV, Derosa G, De Angelis G, Tremamondo J, Lupi A.

journal.title: American journal of cardiovascular drugs : drugs, devices, and other interventions

abstractText: Hypertension is the leading modifiable cardiovascular risk factor, yet long-term adherence to antihypertensive therapy remains suboptimal. RNA-based approaches targeting hepatic angiotensinogen (AGT) have emerged as an attractive strategy for upstream renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system suppression and warrant a timely, focused review of the field. PubMed/MEDLINE, ClinicalTrials.gov and the most relevant scientific and academic databases were searched up to February 2026 to draft a narrative review of peer-reviewed clinical trials, pivotal translational studies, contemporary hypertension guidelines, and official regulatory documents relevant to innovative antihypertensive treatments, such as antisense AGT suppression (zilebesiran), endothelin antagonism (aprocitentan), and aldosterone-synthase inhibition (baxdrostat). Zilebesiran demonstrated durable blood-pressure lowering in monotherapy (KARDIA-1: placebo-adjusted ambulatory systolic blood pressure (BP) - 16.7 mmHg at month 3) and as add-on therapy (KARDIA-2: greatest effect with indapamide background). KARDIA-3 extended evaluation to a higher-risk, heavily medicated population, in which the primary endpoint was not met. The ongoing ZENITH outcomes trial will determine whether AGT silencing reduces hard cardiovascular end-points. Aprocitentan reduced office and ambulatory systolic BP in resistant hypertension (PRECISION trial) and has received regulatory approval in the USA, EU, and UK, with specific monitoring requirements for fluid retention and hematological effects. Baxdrostat demonstrated selective aldosterone-synthase inhibition with meaningful BP reductions across two phase II trials. RNA interference targeting AGT represents one of the most advanced disease-modifying platforms in hypertension, alongside the already-approved endothelin antagonism and the emerging aldosterone synthase inhibition strategy. The available evidence supports cautious optimism and continued translational investment, but not premature adoption into routine practice.

title: Effect of a Multilevel Intervention on Racial Disparities in Medication Adherence: An Analysis of the Rich Life Project.
authorString: Meche A, Cooper LA, Mehta HB, Alexander GC, Jackson JW.
abstractText: Despite advances in hypertension treatment and control, racial disparities in medication adherence persist. We evaluated whether a multilevel collaborative care team intervention reduced racial disparities in medication adherence among adults with uncontrolled hypertension. The RICH LIFE Project was a pragmatic, cluster-randomized trial in 30 primary care practices in Maryland and Pennsylvania, comparing Collaborative Care/Stepped Care (CC/SC) and Standard of Care Plus (SCP) arms. Its primary outcomes were blood pressure control (systolic BP ≤ 140 mm Hg, diastolic BP ≤ 90 mm Hg) and patient activation at 12-months. Participants were non-Hispanic Black and non-Hispanic White adults with uncontrolled hypertension. This analysis examined medication adherence, a prespecified secondary outcome, assessed at 12-months using the 4-item scale adapted from Morisky, Green, and Levine and dichotomized into adherent or nonadherent. A weighting-based approach estimated average potential outcomes within each racial group under the assigned intervention arm and the average intervention effect on the racial disparity in adherence. Sensitivity analyses categorized adherence into high, medium, and low levels and restricted follow-up to the pre-pandemic period. Among 1,555 participants with treated but uncontrolled hypertension (64.2% Black, 35.8% White), Black participants were younger (mean age: 58.0 vs. 65.2 years) and more often female compared to White participants. At 12-months, adherence was similar across arms for Black participants (CC/SC: 45.4%, SCP: 46.1%) and adherence was 66.9% for White participants in the CC/SC arm versus 63.7% in the SCP arm; neither difference was statistically significant. The average intervention effect on disparity was -3.9% (95% CI: -15.8%, 9.4%), indicating no significant disparity reduction. Sensitivity analyses yielded similar findings. The RICH LIFE multilevel intervention did not reduce racial disparities in medication adherence. Evidence-based strategies are needed to reduce disparities in medication adherence.

title: Mitochondrial pharmacology of cardiovascular and antidiabetic drugs: Mechanistic basis of cardioprotection and cardiotoxicity in the diseased heart.
authorString: Kurian GA.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Biochim Biophys Acta Mol Basis Dis
journal.title: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
journal.isoabbreviation: Biochim Biophys Acta Mol Basis Dis

abstractText: Mitochondrial function is a central determinant of cardiomyocyte survival, yet mitochondrial pharmacology remains under-integrated into cardiovascular and antidiabetic drug classification, safety assessment, and therapeutic decision-making. Many cardiometabolic drugs exert direct or indirect effects on mitochondrial bioenergetics, redox balance, calcium handling, quality control, and genome stability effects that can confer protection in some contexts while precipitating toxicity in others. In diseased myocardium, where mitochondrial reserve is constrained by ischemia, metabolic stress, ageing, or heart failure, these drug-mitochondria interactions frequently dictate clinical benefit or harm beyond the nominal drug class. This review synthesises the mitochondrial actions of widely used cardiovascular and antidiabetic therapies, including statins, renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system inhibitors, β-blockers, metformin, sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, and incretin-based agents, across acute and chronic exposure windows. We integrate key mechanistic domains encompassing electron transport chain modulation, redox and cofactor reprogramming, calcium permeability transition coupling, mitochondrial dynamics, mitophagy, and stress signalling, and relate these signatures to clinically relevant cardiometabolic disease contexts. We propose a unifying framework in which mitochondrial reserve capacity and quality control competence function as the central decision node determining whether pharmacologic mitochondrial engagement is adaptive or injurious. Finally, we outline principles for mitochondria-conscious prescribing, risk stratification, and drug development, and propose that systematic incorporation of mitochondrial endpoints into clinical trials and safety pipelines is essential for advancing precision cardiometabolic therapy.

title: Impact of Stent Age on Antithrombotic Strategy for Atrial Fibrillation in Patients with Drug-eluting Stents.
authorString: Jin IT, Kim DH, Yun KH, Ahn JH, Lee BK, Cho DK, Kim SY, Kim U, Kang TS, Lee SH, Lee YJ, Lee SJ, Ahn CM, Kim BK, Ko YG, Choi D, Hong MK, Kim JS, Shin S, Hong SJ.
abstractText: Although non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulant (NOAC) monotherapy is generally recommended beyond 1 year after drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF), the temporal evolution of ischemic and bleeding risks remains inadequately characterized. This study assessed whether the effects of NOAC monotherapy versus combination therapy differ by stent age in patients with AF who underwent DES implantation ≥ 1 year earlier. This prespecified analysis of the Appropriate Duration of Anti-Platelet and Thrombotic Strategy After 12 Months in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation Treated with Drug-Eluting Stents (ADAPT AF-DES) trial compared NOAC monotherapy with combination therapy (NOAC plus clopidogrel) by stent age. Patients were classified into the remote percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) group (stent age > 2 years; n = 577) and the intermediate PCI group (stent age 1-2 years; n = 383). The primary endpoint was 1-year net adverse clinical events (NACE). No significant interaction between antithrombotic strategy and stent age was found for NACE. NOAC monotherapy was associated with less major bleeding or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding than combination therapy in both subgroups without interaction. Although a significant interaction was observed for composite ischemic outcomes in the prespecified analysis, it was no longer observed when stent age was modeled as a continuous variable or after adjustment in sensitivity analyses. Among patients with AF ≥ 1 year post-DES, no consistent interactions by stent age were observed for clinical outcomes, supporting the safety and effectiveness of NOAC monotherapy across the spectrum of stent age.

title: Dual antithrombic therapy with DOAC plus ticagrelor versus DOAC plus clopidogrel after PCI: results from the ReDUAL PCI real life registry-based randomized controlled trial.
authorString: Janssen S, Winkler PJC, Luijkx JJP, Woelders ECI, Peeters DAM, Merry AHH, Damman P, van Geuns RJM, Rasoul S, Hof AWJV', ZON-HR investigators.
abstractText:
Background

Balancing thrombotic and bleeding risk in patients requiring direct oral anticoagulation (DOAC) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains challenging. This study evaluated the safety of dual antithrombotic therapy with DOAC plus ticagrelor compared with DOAC plus clopidogrel in patients undergoing PCI for acute coronary syndrome or with high thrombotic risk.

Methods

The ReDUAL PCI Real Life study was a Dutch, open-label, multicentre, registry-based randomized controlled trial within the Southeast Netherlands Heart Registry (ZON-HR), aiming to enrol 850 patients. Patients requiring DOAC were randomized 1:1 to DOAC plus ticagrelor or DOAC plus clopidogrel after PCI. The primary endpoint was any bleeding (BARC ≥2) at 1 year. Secondary endpoints included major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), and net adverse clinical events (NACE: MACCE plus major bleeding). Outcomes were compared with a non-randomized ZON-HR cohort eligible for inclusion.

Results

The study was terminated prematurely due to slow recruitment, with 109 patients randomized (53 ticagrelor, 56 clopidogrel). Overall bleeding rates were similar between ticagrelor and clopidogrel (13.2% vs 14.3%). Major bleeding (9.4% vs 1.8%), MACCE (13.2% vs 5.4%), and NACE (20.8% vs 7.1%) occurred more frequently with ticagrelor, without statistical significance. In 397 eligible non-randomized clopidogrel-treated patients, major bleeding rate was 3.4%, MACCE occurred in 12.5% and NACE in 14.5%.

Conclusions

In patients undergoing PCI requiring oral anticoagulation, DOAC plus ticagrelor showed similar overall bleeding but numerical increase in major bleeding without apparent ischemic benefit compared with DOAC plus clopidogrel. This prematurely terminated study was underpowered, limiting abilities to draw definitive conclusions.

title: Multimodality imaging for predicting regional wall motion recovery after percutaneous coronary intervention for chronic total occlusion.
authorString: Kawai H, Yamada A, Ishikawa M, Hoshino M, Hoshino N, Nakashima C, Toriya T, Uwatoko T, Matsuwaki Y, Matsuyama T, Takahashi H, Yoshinaga M, Ohta M, Ota H, Yanase M, Ozaki Y, Inoue M, Muramatsu T, Sarai M, Izawa H.
abstractText:
Background

Predicting regional left ventricular (LV) functional recovery is essential for optimizing patient selection for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in chronic total occlusion (CTO), yet direct comparisons of imaging modalities remain limited. We aimed to compare the predictive performance of dobutamine stress echocardiography (DSE), cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging, and single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), alone and in combination, for regional LV wall motion recovery after PCI for CTO.

Methods and results

We prospectively examined 66 patients with CTO undergoing successful PCI. Multimodality imaging was performed within 3 months prior to PCI. Wall motion recovery was defined as an improvement of ≥1 grade in segmental wall motion score assessed by resting echocardiography at 6 to 8 months post-PCI. Among 153 dysfunctional segments within the CTO territory, recovery was observed in 115 (75%). DSE at 20 μg/kg/min demonstrated high sensitivity (96.5%), CMR demonstrated high specificity (68.4%), and SPECT showed moderate sensitivity (76.5%) and specificity (52.6%). The area under the curve (AUC) for the combination of CMR and DSE (0.819) was comparable to that of all three modalities combined (0.825) and significantly exceeded that of any single modality (CMR: 0.738, DSE: 0.733; both P < 0.05).

Conclusions

In patients with CTO undergoing PCI, multimodality imaging provides complementary information for predicting regional LV wall motion recovery. An imaging strategy in which modalities are selected and combined according to the clinical context may help optimize decision-making for revascularization.

Trial registration

UMIN Clinical Trials Registry (UMIN000046847). Short tweet: Can multimodality imaging predict LV wall motion recovery after PCI for chronic total occlusion? Combining dobutamine stress echo and cardiac MRI matched 3-modality performance, aiding CTO revascularization decisions. #CTO #CardioTwitter.

title: Effectiveness of cardiac resynchronization therapy in cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Magalhães A, Araújo I, Brabec M, Menezes MN, Fiúza M, Caldeira D.

journal.title: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer

abstractText:
Introduction

Advances in cancer treatment have increased the number of survivors, making cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) an important concern. While cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) is established for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and conduction disorders, its role in CTRCD remains unclear. We conducted a meta-analysis to assess the benefit of CRT in patients with CTRCD.

Methods

We performed a literature search of studies showing CRT outcomes in the specific group of CTRCD patients. The outcomes of interest were left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and LV volume improvement. A random effects meta-analysis was done to estimate 95% confidence intervals (CI).

Results

This analysis included four studies (one prospective and three retrospective) comprising 110 patients with CTRCD, the majority (91%, n = 100) being survivors of breast cancer or lymphoma/leukemia. Baseline LVEF ranged from 18.6% ± 7.6% to 28.5% ± 3.8% (mean 24% ± 7%). After a mean follow-up of 9 ± 5 months, LVEF increased by 9.95% (95% CI 7.79-12.11) and end-systolic volume decreased by 39.17 mL (95% CI 24.99-53.35). Three studies included a control group of patients with other forms of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy who underwent CRT implantation, showing no significant difference in LVEF improvement between the two groups.

Conclusion

This meta-analysis suggests that CRT improves LVEF and LV volumes in selected patients with CTRCD, with a magnitude of reverse remodeling that appears similar to that observed in other etiologies of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy. However, the evidence is limited to small observational studies, so conclusions about clinical outcomes remain uncertain. Thus, CRT may be considered in cancer patients who meet standard criteria for CRT implantation, but the decision should be individualized and guided by multidisciplinary assessment, cancer prognosis, and competing clinical risks.

title: Exploratory topological modeling of reported frequencies of aortic arch branching variations.
authorString: Muro S, Nimura A, Akita K.
abstractText: Anatomical variations in the branching patterns of the aortic arch affect endovascular access, surgical planning, and cerebral perfusion strategies. However, the quantitative relationship between branching topology and the frequency distribution of these variations remains unclear. The study aimed to explore whether topological differences among final aortic arch branching configurations are associated with their reported frequencies. Seven pooled type-level frequency estimates from a published meta-analysis were analyzed. Node-Shift and Edge-Loss-Change Scores were defined from the final branching topology relative to Type 1 (separate brachiocephalic, left common carotid, and left subclavian origins from a left-sided arch). A three-parameter log-linear model was fitted by ordinary least squares to natural-log-transformed frequencies. Leave-one-out cross-validation and sensitivity analyses by study modality, study size, and exclusion of Type 1 or Type 4 (common brachiocephalic-left common carotid origin with a left vertebral artery arising directly from the arch) were performed. The fitted log-linear model had an intercept of 4.491 and coefficients of -2.751 for the Node-Shift Score and - 5.474 for the Edge-Loss-Change Score. The coefficient of determination was 0.932 on the log-frequency scale and 0.974 after back-transformation to the original frequency scale. Leave-one-out Q² values were 0.821 and 0.778 on the log and original scales, respectively. Coefficients remained negative in imaging-only, cadaveric-only, studies with at least 100 specimens, Type 1-excluded, and Type 4-excluded analyses. Within this seven-type aggregated dataset, configurations with larger topological scores had lower reported frequencies. The proposed scores provide a compact exploratory description of branching variation, but the model does not establish a developmental mechanism, predict individual anatomy, or support direct clinical decision-making without external validation.

title: Prehospital point-of-care ultrasound as a decision-support tool: A structured narrative review.
authorString: Ferreira AM.
abstractText:
Background

Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) may support focused bedside decisions, but prehospital implementation remains limited by operational constraints, heterogeneous protocols, variable training, and limited outcome-focused evidence. This narrative review examines prehospital POCUS as a clinical decision-support tool across cardiac, thoracic, trauma, pediatric, and obstetric applications.

Methods

A structured narrative review was conducted in MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central from April 2017 to February 2026. Search terms combined the prehospital setting, ultrasound, and clinical applications. Of 464 records identified, 38 full-text articles were included, including nine systematic reviews on cardiac evaluation (n = 2), thoracic evaluation (n = 3), and trauma assessment (n = 4). Screening and full-text assessment were performed by a single reviewer. No formal risk-of-bias assessment, certainty grading, quantitative synthesis, or meta-analysis was performed.

Results

In cardiac arrest, prehospital POCUS may identify cardiac activity and selected reversible causes, guide interventions, confirm return of spontaneous circulation, and support prognostic assessment, provided that image acquisition does not interrupt resuscitation or delay defibrillation. In nontraumatic shock and cardiac dysfunction, focused cardiac, lung, and vascular ultrasound may help characterize shock mechanisms, guide fluid therapy, and identify actionable findings such as pulmonary congestion, pericardial effusion, right ventricular strain, or major aortic pathology. In acute dyspnea, lung ultrasound may improve diagnostic confidence, particularly for cardiogenic pulmonary edema. In trauma, E-FAST has high specificity and may support triage, destination choice, trauma pathway activation, and preparation for definitive care; however, limited sensitivity prevents its use as a rule-out test. Pediatric and obstetric applications are feasible but remain emerging.

Conclusions

Prehospital POCUS is an adjunctive decision-support tool rather than a standalone diagnostic test. Its value lies in answering actionable questions that may influence treatment, triage, transport destination, hospital prealert, or pathway activation. Implementation requires protocols, training, quality assurance, and governance, and must not delay time-critical care or transport.

title: A Photocurable Hydrogel Cardiac Patch Incorporating Formononetin-Loaded Lipid Nanoparticles for Myocardial Repair After Acute Ischemia.
authorString: Yang J, Cheng Z, Zhang H, Kong L, Dai T, Ding X, Zhao X, Jin X, Li T, Qi Z, He C, Liu Z.
abstractText: Myocardial infarction (MI) induces ventricular dysfunction through ischemic necrosis and fibrotic remodeling, progressing to heart failure and constituting a major global cardiovascular burden. To address this, we developed a photocurable, hydrogel-based cardiac patch (Gel-CS/FMN@LNP hydrogel) with favorable mechanical robustness. The patch is composed of methacryloylated carboxymethyl chitosan (CACSMA) and methacryloylated gelatin (GelMA), incorporating Formononetin-loaded lipid nanoparticles (FMN@LNPs) for myocardial restoration. In vitro studies demonstrated that the Gel-CS/FMN@LNP hydrogel not only inhibited cardiomyocyte apoptosis by scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS) but also promoted migration and tube formation of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs). Moreover, when a co-culture system of the Gel-CS/FMN@LNP hydrogel and heart-forming organoids (HFOs) was subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) conditions, the system effectively inhibited HFO apoptosis and suppressed HFO fibrosis. In vivo experiments in MI model rats revealed that the Gel-CS/FMN@LNP hydrogel group preserved a higher left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF: 67.2 ± 1.9%) compared to the MI group (LVEF: 41.7 ± 4.7%) at 28 days post-MI, thereby improving cardiac function. Histological analysis showed that the Gel-CS/FMN@LNP hydrogel reduced myocardial fibrosis in the infarct border zone, promoted angiogenesis, and facilitated macrophage polarization toward the M2 phenotype. RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) identified pathways associated with metabolic regulation (PPAR signaling pathway), myocardial protection (PI3K-Akt signaling pathway), anti-fibrosis (inhibition of extracellular matrix remodeling), and anti-inflammatory immune regulation (TNF signaling pathway). Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) revealed that the Gel-CS/FMN@LNP hydrogel promoted post-MI cardiac repair through a multi-target network involving circadian rhythm remodeling, matrix regulation, immune balance, and vascular protection. Our hydrogel system, which combines facile injectability, sustained release of active factors, and synergistic therapeutic effects, represents a promising therapeutic approach for post-MI repair.

title: Racial and Geographic Disparities in Co-Documented Prostate Cancer and Hypertension Mortality Among U.S. Men, 1999-2024: A Multiple Cause of Death Analysis.
authorString: Atif K, Atif E, Das V, Qazi S, Mazhar MA, Abdullah A.

journal.title: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities

abstractText: Androgen deprivation therapy for prostate cancer is associated with incident hypertension, but this burden is largely invisible to conventional surveillance because hypertension is recorded as a contributing rather than an underlying cause of death. We characterized 25-year trends and disparities in co-documented prostate cancer and hypertension mortality among U.S. males. Deaths in which ICD-10 code C61 and codes I10-I15 co-appeared on the same certificate were extracted from CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death data (U.S. males aged ≥ 45 years, 1999-2024). Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) were stratified by age, race and ethnicity, Census region and urbanization, and Joinpoint regression estimated annual and average annual percent change (APC, AAPC). Four alternative cause definitions and place of death were also examined. Co-documentation followed four phases: a sharp rise (APC + 31.4%, 1999-2001), a plateau, renewed acceleration (APC + 13.4%, 2018-2021), and a further plateau; the full-period AAPC was + 3.5% (95% CI 1.9 to 5.1). The AAMR rose from 6.76 to 17.78 per 100,000, and rates rose in every age, race and ethnicity, and regional stratum. Non-Hispanic (NH) Black men carried the highest burden in every year (39.79 vs. 16.91 per 100,000 in NH White men in 2024), although the Black-to-White ratio narrowed from 3.9 to 2.4. The South rose fastest (AAPC + 4.5%) and had the highest 2024 rate, having had the lowest in 1999. Mortality with prostate cancer as the underlying cause fell 42% over the same period. Co-documented mortality rose across 25 years while prostate cancer mortality itself fell, so the rise cannot be attributed to a growing number of prostate cancer deaths. The burden remained concentrated in NH Black men, the South and non-metropolitan communities. The post-2021 plateau is consistent with documentation change and with reduced access to care, which these data cannot separate. The findings point to implementation of existing monitoring recommendations as the more likely constraint on reducing this disparity.

title: Periprocedural Cardiac Hemodynamic Changes and Clinical Outcomes After Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt.
authorString: Feng Z, Wu B, Su H, Zhou H, Shi H, Liu S, Yang W, Zhou W.
abstractText: To characterize serial changes in cardiac structure and function before and after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) using comprehensive echocardiographic assessment and to explore their clinical relevance. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 149 patients with decompensated cirrhosis who underwent TIPS between January 2018 and October 2024. Transthoracic echocardiography was performed preoperatively, within 5 days after TIPS, and at 3-6 months of follow-up. Additional echocardiographic parameters were assessed preoperatively and early after TIPS during hospitalization to further characterize periprocedural cardiac functional changes. Echocardiographic parameters were compared across time points using repeated-measures analysis or paired tests. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis was used to examine associations with clinical outcomes. After TIPS, right atrial diameter and right ventricular end-diastolic diameter increased significantly (both P < 0.001), accompanied by a modest increase in pulmonary artery systolic pressure (P = 0.029), while left ventricular structure and systolic function showed no significant changes. The tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion/pulmonary artery systolic pressure ratio showed a numerical decrease early after TIPS, followed by partial recovery during follow-up, although the changes were not statistically significant. Among the additional echocardiographic parameters, color M-mode flow propagation velocity (Vp) increased significantly from 62.8 to 75.1 cm/s (P = 0.04), whereas E/A, E/e', and other diastolic parameters remained largely unchanged. During a median follow-up of 1057 days, one patient developed early postoperative heart failure. Survival and overt hepatic encephalopathy did not differ significantly among groups stratified by baseline E/A ratio. In patients with relatively preserved baseline cardiac function following appropriate pre-TIPS cardiovascular assessment, TIPS was associated predominantly with mild and transient right-sided cardiac changes, without significant deterioration in conventional left ventricular systolic function. The low incidence of clinically overt cardiac decompensation observed during follow-up suggests an acceptable cardiac risk profile in appropriately evaluated patients.

title: Clinical phenotypes, outcomes, and myocardial transcriptomic signatures in inflammatory myocardial disease: A prospective cohort study.
authorString: Björkenstam M, Ljungman C, Falk LH, Jamialahmadi O, Romeo S, Backelin CN, Bobbio E, Dahlberg P, Valeljung I, Bartfay SE, Mellberg T, Wideqvist M, Andersson B, Bergh N, Hjalmarsson C, Bollano E.
abstractText:
Background

Inflammatory myocardial disease encompasses diverse clinical phenotypes, from subtle symptoms to fulminant heart failure. Differentiating myocarditis, cardiac sarcoidosis (CS), and non-confirmed cardiomyopathy (NC) remains diagnostically and prognostically challenging. We compared clinical presentation, outcomes, and myocardial transcriptomic profiles across these groups.

Methods

In this prospective cohort study, 218 adults undergoing evaluation for cardiomyopathy were classified as myocarditis (n = 81), CS (n = 84), or NC (n = 53). The primary composite outcome was all-cause mortality, mechanical circulatory support, or heart transplantation. RNA sequencing of endomyocardial biopsies was performed in 53 patients with differential expression analysis adjusted for age, RNA integrity number, and systolic blood pressure.

Results

Patients with myocarditis were younger than those with CS or NC (34.7 ± 15.8 vs 57.4 ± 8.7 vs 57.6 ± 14.0 years); 70-75% were male. Myocarditis was characterized by chest pain and elevated inflammatory biomarkers, whereas CS was associated with arrhythmias and right ventricular dysfunction. Although unadjusted Kaplan-Meier analysis suggested differences in event-free survival, adjusted Cox regression showed no significant between-group differences (myocarditis vs NC: HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.22-4.43, p = 0.985; CS vs NC: HR 1.67, 95% CI 0.63-4.43, p = 0.307). Transcriptomic profiling revealed a more pronounced inflammatory gene expression profile in myocarditis, whereas CS showed limited differential expression and substantial overlap with NC.

Conclusions

Inflammatory myocardial disease shows distinct clinical presentations, while adjusted analyses did not demonstrate significant differences in long-term outcomes. Myocarditis showed a stronger inflammatory transcriptional signature, whereas CS exhibited limited transcriptomic differences. These findings support further investigation of RNA-based profiling as a complementary tool.

title: COVID-19 severity among individuals with chronic diseases.
authorString: Reichenberg Y, Hasson L, Leibovich M, Oberman B, Strahl T, Shlomi D.
abstractText: Previous studies reported that individuals with underlying chronic diseases who are infected with COVID-19 are at greater risk for more severe outcomes. In this study, we measured these risks among a wide range of comorbidities in a large cohort. In this retrospective study, we analyzed the risk for hospitalization and the severity and mortality risk of COVID-19 among adults with obstructive lung diseases, hypertension, cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, kidney diseases, malignancies and immunosuppression states before the emergence of the Omicron variant. We used univariant analyses and adjusted for age, sex, Body Mass Index (BMI), smoking habits, Socioeconomic Status (SES) and the Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI). Of the 44,866 individuals who were positive for COVID-19, 2358 were hospitalized. The adjusted Odds Ratio (aOR) for hospitalization was significantly greater for most chronic diseases, with the highest risk for individuals who underwent a kidney transplant (15.06; 95% Confidence Interval [95% CI 7.86-28.73]). A significantly greater risk for severe COVID-19 than for mild to moderate disease (602 and 1657 patients, respectively) was found for patients with cerebrovascular diseases (aOR = 1.46; 95% CI 1.07-1.99). A greater mortality risk was demonstrated for individuals who had undergone kidney transplantation (aOR = 4.23; 95% CI 1.36-11.82) and those with Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) (aOR = 1.43; 95% CI 1.02-1.99). Individuals with cerebrovascular disease were at increased risk for severe COVID-19, whereas individuals with CKD and past kidney transplantation were at increased mortality risk. These individuals should receive early medical intervention when they are diagnosed.

title: Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation With Previous Intracranial Bleeding: Competing Adverse Events in a Nationwide Cohort.
authorString: Tiili P, Lehto M, Halminen O, Lehtonen O, Haukka J, Linna M, Satopää J, Korja M, Niemelä M, Kinnunen J, Aro A, Mustonen P, Hartikainen JEK, Airaksinen JKE, Putaala J.
abstractText: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and previous intracranial bleeding are at high risk of ischemic and bleeding events, and the benefits and risks of oral anticoagulation (OAC) remain uncertain. We investigated competing risks of recurrent intracranial bleeding, ischemic stroke (IS), and death from other causes according to anticoagulation strategy. This nationwide Finnish cohort study using linked administrative registries included patients with first-ever AF diagnosed in 2010-2018 and intracranial bleeding at least 120 days earlier. Follow-up began 90 days after AF diagnosis. Patients were categorized as receiving direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), warfarin, or no OAC based on drug purchases. Warfarin users were further stratified by time in therapeutic range (TTR). Inverse probability of treatment weighting balanced baseline characteristics. Competing risks were analyzed using adjusted cumulative incidence functions and cause-specific Cox regression. Among 1,502 patients (median age 78 years [IQR 71-85], 44% female, 41% with only traumatic intracranial bleeding), 15% received DOACs, 29% warfarin, and 56% no OAC. At 1 year, adjusted absolute risks of IS were 0.7%, 2.1%, and 4.1%; intracranial bleeding, 1.2%, 2.7%, and 1.9%; and death from other causes, 4.7%, 8.6%, and 14.7%, respectively. Compared with no OAC, DOAC use was associated with lower risks of IS (HR 0.17, 95% CI 0.04-0.71) and death (HR 0.20, 95% CI 0.09-0.46) without increased intracranial bleeding risk (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.19-2.50). Warfarin use was associated with lower risks of IS (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.26-0.93) and death (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.44-0.80), but increased intracranial bleeding risk (HR 1.85, 95% CI 1.01-3.41). Among warfarin users, TTR ≥70% was associated with lower risks of IS (HR 0.24, 95% CI 0.08-0.79) and death (HR 0.19, 95% CI 0.10-0.36); associations were attenuated with poorer or missing TTR. In patients with AF and previous intracranial bleeding, OAC was associated with lower risks of IS and death. DOAC use was not associated with increased intracranial bleeding risk, whereas warfarin use was. Limited information on previous intracranial bleeding and potential residual confounding warrant cautious interpretation. These findings support individualized anticoagulation decisions in this high-risk population.

title: Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias is Associated with Worse Clinical and Patient-centered Outcomes in Patient Admitted for Heart Failure.
authorString: Hendricks E, Pei Q, Li A, Guo Y, Shah S, Price CEC, Rashidi P, Scali S, Berceli S, Shah K.
abstractText: The aims of this study are to assess clinical and patient-centered outcomes following admission for HF as stratified by ADRD status. We identified patients 65 years or older in the OneFlorida+ data trust with first admission for HF between October 1, 2015 and December 31, 2022. ICD-10 diagnoses codes were used to identify HF, ADRD, and relevant comorbidities. Exclusion criteria were admission with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) or shock. The primary clinical outcome was all-cause 1-year mortality, and the secondary clinical outcome was 90-day readmissions. Patient-centered outcomes were length of stay and discharge home. 22,342 patients with first HF hospitalization during the study period were identified. Of these, 5,261 (23.5%) patients carried a diagnosis of ADRD. Patients with ADRD were more likely to be women (57.7% vs. 53.1%, p<0.05) and Black (21.1% vs. 14.6%, p<0.05). 1-year mortality was higher in patients with ADRD (HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.10-1.36, p < 0.005) as was 90-day readmissions (HR 1.23, 95% CI 1.18-1.28, p <0.005). Patients with ADRD demonstrated longer lengths of stays (5.7 vs. 5.4 days, p <0.005) and were less likely to be discharged home (OR .81, 95% CI 0.77-0.84, p<0.001). Patients with ADRD hospitalized for HF demonstrate higher 1-year mortality and 90-day readmissions. Patient-centered outcomes are also worse in patients with ADRD, with longer lengths of stay and are less discharge home. These findings should be used to identify research priorities and to facilitate advanced care planning in patients with ADRD and HF.

title: Multimodal Atrial Cardiomyopathy Phenotypes for Risk Stratification in Severe Aortic Stenosis Undergoing TAVI.
authorString: Mistrulli R, Fiori E, Storozhenko T, Corradetti S, Kechichian A, Stalikas N, Buytaert D, Ausiello D, Viscusi MM, Paolisso P, Belmonte M, Gallinoro E, Weerts J, Barbato E, Van Camp G, Penicka M, Wyffels E, Vanderheyden M.
abstractText:
Background

Atrial cardiomyopathy (AtCM) is highly prevalent in patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS), even in the presence of preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Structural, functional, and electrical atrial remodeling may differentially influence outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), although their integrated prognostic role remains unclear.

Objectives

To assess whether multimodal markers of AtCM identify distinct risk phenotypes associated with adverse outcomes after TAVI in patients without prior atrial fibrillation (AF).

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed 122 consecutive patients with severe AS, preserved LVEF, and sinus rhythm undergoing TAVI. Structural/functional AtCM (Echo-AtCM Risk) was assessed using indexed left atrial volume (LAVI) and left atrial reservoir strain (LASr), whereas electrical AtCM (ECG-AtCM Risk) was defined according to P-wave duration and morphology. Patients were followed for all-cause mortality, heart failure (HF) hospitalization, and new-onset AF. Prognostic associations were evaluated using multivariable Cox regression analyses.

Results

Mean age was 82.3±5.6 years. High Echo-Risk was present in 54.1% of patients and High ECG-Risk in 19.7%. During a median follow-up of 13.6 months, the composite endpoint of all-cause mortality or HF hospitalization occurred in 39 patients (32.0%), while new-onset AF developed in 17 (13.9%). High Echo-Risk independently predicted death/HF hospitalization (HR 4.17, p=0.008), whereas High ECG-Risk independently predicted incident AF (HR 3.07, p=0.034). Combined profiling identified distinct phenotypes: High Echo/Low ECG predicted HF/death (HR 4.86, p=0.008), Low Echo/High ECG predicted AF (HR 8.99, p=0.004), and combined High Echo/High ECG conferred the worst prognosis (HR 6.23, p=0.015).

Conclusions

Structural, functional, and electrical AtCM represent complementary domains with distinct prognostic implications in AS patients undergoing TAVI. Their integration may refine post-TAVI risk stratification; these exploratory findings require external validation before clinical management can be guided by AtCM phenotype.Keywords: Atrial cardiomyopathy; Aortic stenosis; TAVI; Left atrial strain; Heart failure; Atrial fibrillation.

title: Lunar phases, meteorological conditions, astrological signs, and postoperative outcomes of acute type A aortic dissection: Results of a retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Mathieu L, Beurton A, Sorbier C, Hautcoeur W, Detchepare J, Germain C, Dib N, Roubertie F, Ouattara A.
abstractText: BackgroundAcute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) is a surgical emergency associated with high mortality. While patient-related risk factors are well-established, beliefs persist regarding the influence of lunar phases, meteorological conditions, and astrological signs on disease occurrence and outcomes.MethodsWe retrospectively analysed all patients who underwent emergency surgery for ATAAD at Bordeaux University Hospital between 1996 and 2020. The primary objective was to assess the association between environmental factors (lunar phases, atmospheric pressure, temperature, and astrological signs) and ATAAD incidence. Secondary objectives included assessing their association with 30-day mortality and postoperative morbidity (intensive care unit length of stay, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation use, and mesenteric infarction). Meteorological data were available for 603 patients from 2010 onward.ResultsAmong 920 patients (70% male; mean age 63 ± 13 years), the 30-day mortality rate was 9.7%. Lunar phases were not associated with ATAAD incidence (first quarter 26%, last quarter 25%, new moon 25%, full moon 24%; p = 0.91), mortality, or complications. Atmospheric pressure showed no association with ATAAD occurrence or outcomes. Temperature showed a weak correlation with ATAAD incidence (r = 0.11, p = 0.01), but not with mortality. Astrological signs were not associated with ATAAD incidence, mortality, or morbidity. Longer cardiopulmonary bypass duration (odds ratio [OR] = 0.994 per minute; p = 0.01) and diabetes (OR = 4.63; p = 0.01) were associated with 30-day mortality.ConclusionsEnvironmental factors were not associated with ATAAD incidence or outcomes. Established clinical factors remain the primary determinants of mortality.

title: Echocardiographic predictors of left ventricular ejection fraction improvement after transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
authorString: Sato S, Kumagai A, Ninomiya K, Murofushi A, Shimada K, Yoshizawa M, Ninomiya R, Fusazaki T, Morino Y.
abstractText:
Background

Improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has been associated with better clinical outcomes, but predictors of recovery remain poorly defined. This study aimed to identify echocardiographic parameters associated with post-TAVR LVEF improvement in patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) and reduced LVEF.

Methods

Among 1,133 consecutive patients who underwent TAVR between December 2013 and June 2024, 128 with baseline LVEF < 50% and follow-up echocardiography within 3 months were analyzed. LVEF improvement was defined as an absolute increase ≥ 10%. Independent predictors were identified using multivariable logistic regression. Post-procedural outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis.

Results

LVEF improvement occurred in 64 patients (50%). Multivariable analysis identified higher left ventricular mass index (LVMI) (OR 1.02, 95% CI 1.00-1.03, P = 0.01) and higher E/e' (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.03-1.18, P < 0.01) as independent predictors of improvement, whereas larger left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) (OR 0.98, P = 0.01) and larger AVA (OR 0.67 per 0.1 cm², P < 0.01) were inversely associated. Patients with LVEF improvement had significantly lower 1-year all-cause mortality (98.2% vs. 87.0%, P = 0.01).

Conclusions

Echocardiographic parameters reflecting pressure overload and diastolic dysfunction predict LVEF recovery after TAVR. Postoperative LVEF improvement was associated with better 1-year survival, underscoring its prognostic value.

title: Feasibility and outcomes of long-segment tracheal replacement with biological and engineered scaffolds.
authorString: Su Q, Liu D, Han Y.
abstractText:
Objectives

To synthesize adult long-segment tracheal replacement using a combined anatomical and graft-based framework and to compare clinically established and investigational strategies with emphasis on mortality, morbidity, airway function, and reintervention.

Methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure were searched from January 1, 2000, to June 30, 2026. Adult replacements were classified as Type I (upper/cervical), Type II (cervico-mediastinal), Type III (intrathoracic), or Type IV (distal trachea/carina) and by graft class. Forty-three reports comprising 147 extractable patients were synthesized descriptively. The overlapping 50-patient TRITON-01 registry was analyzed separately as the principal cryopreserved aortic-allograft benchmark.

Results

Among 147 patients, 72 were Type I, 33 Type II, 25 Type III, and 17 Type IV; 113 (76.9%) had malignant disease. Autologous vascularized tissue composites were used in 74 patients (50.3%) and cryopreserved aortic allografts in 52 (35.4%). Overall 30-day and 90-day mortality were 4.8% and 9.5%, respectively. Decannulation was achieved in 103/139 (74.1%); 25.2% required repeat endoscopic intervention and 19.0% developed recurrent stenosis. In the updated 50-patient TRITON-01 registry, 30-day mortality was 4%, major complications 30%, stent-related granuloma 52%, and stent removal 30%. Reliable Type I-IV-specific mortality rates could not be pooled because primary reports did not consistently cross-tabulate outcomes by anatomical level.

Conclusions

Anatomy should precede material choice when interpreting tracheal replacement. Autologous vascularized composites have the most mature experience for selected Type I-II reconstruction, whereas Type III-IV intrathoracic and distal/carinal replacement remains more technically hazardous. Cryopreserved aortic allografts provide the current clinical benchmark for biologic full-circumference replacement but require structured stent and bronchoscopic management. Tracheal allotransplantation and engineered or xenogenic constructs remain limited or investigational.

title: Early and Mid-Term Mortality After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: Five-Year Experience from the KOSUTAVI Study.
authorString: Zehir R, Alizade E, Usalp S, Emiroğlu MY, Kargın R, Özdemir N, Kırma C, Kaymaz C, Türkmen MM, Pala S, Külahçıoğlu Ş, Kırali MK.
abstractText:
Background

Although transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) outcomes are well-documented, predictors of mortality beyond conventional surgical risk scores and valve-related factors in real-world, high-risk cohorts require further elucidation. This study aimed to identify the key determinants of 30-day and 1-year mortality following TAVI, with a focus on both patient-specific and procedure-specific complications.

Methods

The KOSUTAVI study is a single-center, retrospective cohort analysis of 859 consecutive high-risk individuals with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI between 2020 and 2025. Primary endpoints were 30-day and 1-year all-cause mortality. Multivariate Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to identify independent risk factors.

Results

Mean age was 78.7 ± 6.5 years, and mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons score was 7.4 ± 2.2. The 30-day and 1-year mortality rates were 6.5% (n = 56) and 12.4% (n = 107), respectively. The 5-year all-cause mortality rate was 26.3%. In multiple Cox's analysis, chronic renal failure (hazard ratio [HR] = 7.75, P = .008, 95% CI = 1.29-16.54), presentation with cardiogenic shock (HR = 5.83, P = .028, 95% CI = 1.19-15.41), major vascular injury (HR = 22.7, P = .019, 95% CI = 1.89-45.91), and cardiac tamponade (HR = 17.9, P = .012, 95% CI = 8.13-52.62) were independently associated with 30-day mortality. While these factors were all significant in univariate analysis for 1-year mortality, they did not retain independence in the multiple model. Valve type, access route, and sex were not associated with increased mortality.

Conclusion

In a high-risk TAVI population, early mortality is predominantly driven by pre-existing renal dysfunction and acute procedural complications (shock, vascular injury, and tamponade), rather than valve-specific factors. These findings underscore the critical importance of optimizing renal function before the procedure and implementing advanced vascular protection strategies to improve early survival after TAVI.

title: Computed tomography angiography with three-dimensional reconstruction for planning aortic valve replacement via right anterior mini-thoracotomy.
authorString: Li W, Hu J, Gong W, Chen T, Zhang C, Zhang R.

journal.title: Hong Kong medical journal = Xianggang yi xue za zhi

abstractText:
Introduction

This study explored the value of computed tomography angiography (CTA) with three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction in aortic valve replacement (AVR) via right anterior mini-thoracotomy.

Methods

Clinical data were retrospectively collected from 168 patients who underwent AVR at our institution in China between 1 July 2018 and 1 September 2022. After 1:1 propensity score matching, the experimental group (right anterior mini-thoracotomy) and control group (median sternotomy) each comprised 43 patients. Patients in the experimental group underwent preoperative aortic CTA with 3D reconstruction to guide individualised selection of the intercostal incision site. Perioperative and clinical outcomes were compared between groups.

Results

The experimental group had significantly lower 24-hour postoperative drainage volume and shorter mechanical ventilation time, intensive care unit stay, and total hospital stay than the control group (all P<0.001). No intraoperative conversion to median sternotomy or postoperative reoperation for bleeding or pericardial tamponade occurred in the experimental group. Postoperatively, five patients (11.6%) developed atelectasis or pulmonary infection, five (11.6%) developed pleural effusion, and five (11.6%) developed subcutaneous emphysema or pneumothorax; none required thoracentesis. Aortic cross-clamping and cardiopulmonary bypass times were approximately 8 minutes longer, respectively, in the experimental group. At 24 months, the incidence of the composite endpoint-including all-cause mortality, cardiocerebrovascular complications, and readmission for massive pleural effusion or coagulation dysfunction-did not differ significantly between groups.

Conclusion

Preoperative CTA with 3D reconstruction enables accurate localisation of the right intercostal incision for AVR via right anterior mini-thoracotomy. This technique preserves minimally invasive surgery benefits and does not increase risks of mid/long-term adverse events.

title: Burden of congenital birth defects in the ten countries with the highest numbers of births from 1990 to 2023, with projections to 2040: A retrospective population-level ecological study.
authorString: Kuang Q, Yang C, Tao C, Deng Q, Chu H, Mao C.
abstractText: ObjectiveCongenital birth defects (CBDs) are major causes of neonatal mortality and lifelong disability worldwide. The ten countries with the highest numbers of births account for over half of global neonates, yet their CBD burden trends remain insufficiently studied. This study aimed to assess the CBD burden and temporal trends in these countries from 1990 to 2023 and project trends to 2040.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective population-level ecological study using publicly available data from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 on CBD burden. We analysed incidence, mortality, disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), and age-standardized rates (ASRs) for CBDs in India, China, Nigeria, Pakistan, Indonesia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ethiopia, the United States, Bangladesh, and Brazil from 1990 to 2023. Temporal trends were assessed using estimated annual percentage change (EAPC), future trends (2024-2040) were projected using ARIMA models, and associations with the Socio-demographic Index (SDI) were evaluated by Spearman correlation.ResultsIn 2023, India had the highest number of CBD cases (1,160,697), followed by Nigeria and China. Ethiopia showed the highest age-standardized incidence rate, while the United States had the lowest. From 1990 to 2023, age-standardized incidence, mortality, and DALYs generally declined, with China showing the largest reductions in mortality and DALYs. Nigeria was the only country with increasing mortality. Congenital heart anomalies were the leading cause of deaths and DALYs across all countries. Neural tube defects showed the greatest decline in incidence, whereas urogenital congenital anomalies demonstrated increasing mortality trends. SDI was negatively correlated with incidence, mortality, and DALYs (all P < 0.05). ARIMA projections suggested increasing ASIR in several countries, particularly China and Indonesia, while China and Nigeria were projected to experience increases in ASMR and ASDR through 2040, particularly among females, while Bangladesh, Ethiopia, and the United States are expected to remain stable or decline.ConclusionThe CBD burden showed marked heterogeneity across the ten countries with the highest numbers of births. Strengthening healthcare systems, prenatal care, and screening in low-SDI countries, together with targeted prevention strategies in countries with projected increases, may help reduce the global CBD burden and improve health equity.

title: Coronary microvascular dysfunction in takotsubo syndrome: An interventional perspective on pathophysiology, diagnostic workflow and prognosis.
authorString: Damera RR, Rivero H, Riaz MS, Sridhar A, Oprysko C, Khan RN, Betancourt A, Kundal S, Balasubramanian S, Merino E, Kaur J, Pillai N, Gilchrist IC, Khanna N, Chikvashvili D, Selim S, Burke FW, Rao G.
abstractText: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) is an acute, usually reversible left ventricular dysfunction mimicking acute coronary syndrome without a culprit epicardial lesion. Once considered benign, it carries in-hospital mortality comparable to ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is frequently observed during the acute phase, but its relationship to TTS remains uncertain: it may be a predisposing substrate, a mediator of catecholamine-induced injury, or a consequence of edema, extravascular compression, altered loading conditions, and ventricular dysfunction, and human evidence shows association rather than mechanism. The index of microcirculatory resistance (IMR) is an established invasive measure of hyperemic microvascular resistance. In TTS, IMR is frequently elevated during the acute phase, and microvascular function appears to improve as left ventricular function recovers, although often incompletely. In a pooled analysis of individual patient data from 166 patients, acute-phase IMR was the only invasive index that remained associated with mortality after adjustment. The cutoff of 54 used in that analysis is an exploratory, hypothesis-generating prognostic threshold: derived within the same dataset, it requires external validation and should be distinguished from the diagnostic threshold of ≥25 used in CMD algorithms that have not been validated in acute conditions such as TTS. Wire-based IMR remains the gold standard; angiography-derived IMR is promising, but available software platforms remain investigational. This review examines proposed mechanisms, measurement methods and their validation, prognostic evidence, and management, and outlines a workflow for future research. We conclude that the clinical utility and optimal timing of invasive coronary function testing in TTS remain uncertain.

title: Carcinomatous meningitis: Current insights into diagnosis, prognosis and management.
authorString: Gambaretti M, Lavalley A, Ollivier M, Tourdias T, Engelhardt J.
abstractText: Carcinomatous meningitis, or leptomeningeal metastasis, is a severe neurological complication of solid and haematological malignancies caused by dissemination of tumour cells within the leptomeninges and cerebrospinal fluid pathways. Clinical presentation is heterogeneous, including headache, intracranial hypertension, cranial nerve palsies or radiculopathy, which frequently leads to diagnostic delay. Diagnosis relies on converging clinical, radiological, and cerebrospinal fluid findings, with gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging of the brain and spine and cerebrospinal fluid cytology remaining central despite imperfect sensitivity. Emerging tools, particularly cerebrospinal fluid circulating tumour cells and circulating tumour DNA, may improve early detection and molecular characterisation. Prognosis remains poor, with survival usually measured in months. Management should be individualised according to performance status, tumour subtype, and systemic disease control, and may combine symptomatic measures, radiotherapy, targeted systemic therapies, and, in selected patients, intrathecal chemotherapy. Early integration of palliative care remains a key component of management.

title: Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance Imaging in Cardio-Oncology: An Expert Consensus Statement from the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance. Endorsed by the International Cardio-Oncology Society (ICOS).
authorString: Baldassarre LA, Reinhardt SW, Jordan JH, Bandettini WP, Barac A, Bucciarelli-Ducci C, de Lara Fernandes J, Dent S, Ferreira V, Fontana M, Frank L, Hundley WG, Khattab MH, Leiner T, Lopez-Mattei J, Ojha V, Rochitte CE, Schulz-Menger J, Srichai-Parsia MB, Thavendiranathan P, Toro-Salazar O, Weinsaft J, Manisty C.

journal.title: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance

abstractText: This document represents a position statement from the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance (SCMR) on recommendations for clinical utilization of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) in patients with cancer. The document was prepared by the SCMR Consensus Group on CMR Imaging for Cardio-Oncology and endorsed by the SCMR Publications Committee and SCMR Executive Committee. This document aims to: (1) guide the informed selection and timing of CMR; (2) inform clinical decision-making based on CMR findings; (3) educate stakeholders on the advantages and limitations of CMR in specific clinical scenarios; and (4) provide suggested protocols to tailor the CMR exam to the particular clinical question. The statements of clinical utility presented in the current document focus on the following clinical scenarios: evaluating left ventricular dysfunction with ejection fraction and volumes; identifying pre-clinical left ventricular (LV) dysfunction with myocardial strain; and myocardial injury or edema with parametric mapping and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE); myocarditis; vascular toxicity, with a focus on coronary artery disease (CAD); iron overload; cardiac amyloidosis; pericardial disease; valvular disease; pulmonary hypertension; and cardiac masses. Sections devoted to the special situations of radiation therapy (RT), hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), and survivorship and pediatrics are also included. As an expert consensus statement, some recommendations are based on expert opinion and accepted best practices. This position statement emphasizes the optimal utilization of CMR in oncology patients with known or suspected cardiovascular disease; however, the authors acknowledge that CMR is not always locally available or accessible. Finally, the principal aim of this position statement is to provide specific recommendations on the use of CMR to help improve the health of cancer patients with cardiovascular disease.

title: Matching Electrode Configuration to Signal Sensing for Cardiac Electroanatomic Mapping: A Critical Appraisal.
authorString: Castells F, Ruipérez-Campillo S, Rodrigo M, Ramirez Candela E, Merino JL, Roig JM, Narayan SM.
abstractText: The management of cardiac arrhythmias has been transformed by electroanatomical mapping, yet it is often underappreciated how dependent mapping is to electrode configuration, sensing modality, catheter geometry, and signal-processing characteristics. This review systematically evaluates how these features influence mapping, in the context of catheters in contemporary linear, circular, grid, star-shaped and basket configurations. We compare direct sensing strategies in unipolar and bipolar configurations, monophasic action potentials, and discuss post-processing approaches including omnipolar, multipolar, and Laplacian techniques. We gather evidence from computational, experimental and clinical studies to critically discuss how these considerations may influence signal acquisition and mapping resolution in the context of clinical mapping needs and, in particular, which may be most relevant for the complex arrhythmias of atrial fibrillation (AF) and ventricular tachycardia (VT). We conclude by pointing out future directions such as ultra-high-resolution mapping, adaptive catheter geometries, computational reconstruction, and AI-guided signal interpretation.

title: From Polycystic Ovary Syndrome to Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome: A Practical Clinical Review.
authorString: Cardozo LLY, Eissa MA, Basnet J, Thompson K, Romero DG.

journal.title: The American journal of the medical sciences

abstractText: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS), recently renamed Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS), is the most common endocrine disorder affecting women of reproductive age. The new nomenclature reflects growing recognition that this condition extends far beyond ovarian dysfunction, encompassing complex endocrine, metabolic, cardiovascular, and psychological abnormalities. Although the diagnostic criteria remain unchanged, the name change emphasizes the multisystem nature of the disorder and may improve disease recognition and patient care. This review provides a practical, evidence-based overview of the diagnosis and management of PMOS/PCOS, highlighting recent updates from the 2023 International Evidence-Based Guideline. We discuss the evaluation of hyperandrogenism and ovulatory dysfunction in reproductive-aged women, as well as the assessment and treatment of obesity, insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyslipidemia, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, obstructive sleep apnea, and mental health disorders. Finally, we summarize current pharmacological therapies and emerging treatment strategies, highlighting key knowledge gaps that must be bridged to optimize long-term cardiometabolic and reproductive outcomes.

title: Gut Dubosiella newyorkensis alleviates noise-related atherosclerosis by reducing N1-methyl-4-pyridone-3-carboxamide.
authorString: Chen M, Fang N, Wang R, Wang Z, Gao Y, Min R, Hong Y, Wang J, Zhang Y, Li Y, Gong Y.
abstractText: Environmental noise is ubiquitous in daily life and has emerged as a major risk factor for cardiovascular diseases. Nevertheless, the association between noise exposure and coronary heart disease, as well as the underlying molecular mechanisms, remains poorly understood. Here, analyses of UK Biobank (UKB) data revealed that noise exposure was associated with an increased risk of coronary heart disease. We further demonstrated that noise exposure elevated circulating levels of N1-methyl-4-pyridone-3-carboxamide (4PY) in both humans and rodents. Accumulation of 4PY suppressed endothelial NR4A1 expression, activated NF-κB signaling, facilitated monocyte adhesion and inflammatory cytokine release, and ultimately accelerated atherosclerotic progression. Mechanistically, we found that noise exposure reduced the abundance of Dubosiella newyorkensis (D. newyorkensis) in the gut microbiota of humans. Supplementation with D. newyorkensis upregulated hepatic ACMSD expression, lowered circulating 4PY levels, and alleviated noise-related atherosclerotic progression in mice. Our findings provide mechanistic insights into the therapeutic potential of D. newyorkensis in mitigating noise-related atherosclerosis by reducing circulating 4PY levels. Targeted modulation of the gut microbiota may represent a promising strategy for preventing and managing cardiovascular complications triggered by environmental noise.

title: Standardizing cardiopulmonary bypass management for left ventricular assist device implantation: A clinical framework and checklist.
authorString: Deng L, Zhou C.
abstractText: BackgroundPatients undergoing left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation often present with end-stage heart failure, severe pulmonary hypertension, and systemic inflammation. During this procedure, cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) acts as a double-edged sword: it provides essential life support but can exacerbate right ventricular (RV) dysfunction and trigger severe vasoplegia. Despite the critical nature of the transition from CPB to mechanical support, there is a lack of standardized, phase-specific CPB management protocols.MethodsBased on current guidelines, frontline perfusion experience, and an interdisciplinary approach integrating mechanical engineering principles with surgical practice, a comprehensive clinical framework for CPB management was developed. The protocol deconstructs the procedure into four distinct phases: pre-bypass assessment, on-bypass management, weaning, and post-bypass care.ResultsA four-stage standardized checklist and an intraoperative emergency quick reference card were created to facilitate clinical translation. Key interventions include identifying anatomical "minefields," maintaining a golden balance of hemodilution, executing a dynamic flow-speed handover to prevent suction events, and managing hemodynamics cautiously during protamine administration to mitigate RV dysfunction.ConclusionsStandardizing CPB management during LVAD implantation provides a practical tool to optimize hemodynamic stability and improve perioperative safety.

title: Targeting ZIP12-mediated Zn<sup>2+</sup> signaling as a treatment for pulmonary hypertension.
authorString: Zhao L, Hopley S, Chen CN, Kibreab I, Xie C, Baxan N, Ashek A, Zhao L, Fellows A, Kostyunina DS, Oliver E, Wang L, Ning S, Rutter G, Gorelik J, Gurrell R, Butt R, Hamblin P, Wilkins MR.
abstractText: ZIP12, a membrane-bound zinc importer, is up-regulated in the remodeled pulmonary arterioles of patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Genetic deletion of its encoding gene, Slc39a12, ameliorates the disease in rodent models. Here, we show that ZIP12 overexpression in human pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs) increased intracellular labile Zn2+ and promoted proliferation. ZIP12 siRNA knockdown attenuated pulmonary hypertension in rodent models. We developed a humanized anti-ZIP12 monoclonal antibody, APL-9796, that normalized intracellular Zn2+ concentration, suppressed proliferation in fibroblasts derived from patients with PAH and PDGF-stimulated PASMCs, and reduced PDGF-induced cytoskeletal remodeling in PASMCs and contractility in PASMCs and engineered pulmonary artery tissues. APL-9796 showed dose-dependent efficacy in humanized Slc39a12 rats, improving cardiopulmonary parameters after induction of pulmonary hypertension and was well tolerated in phase 1 clinical studies. Transcriptomic profiling revealed modulation of several molecular pathways, including those involving AMPK, PPAR, and PI3K-Akt. ZIP12-driven labile Zn2+ signaling underpins the pathogenesis of PAH. Targeting ZIP12 with APL-9796 offers a promising therapeutic strategy.

title: Seeing the invisible: Reorienting cardiovascular risk prediction across the disease trajectory.
authorString: Tang X, Gao P.
abstractText: Current risk equations miss many cardiovascular events in people classified as low risk. Prediction is simultaneously advancing on two axes: broadening predictors toward molecular omics, and expanding outcomes toward earlier subclinical atherosclerosis and later heart failure.

title: Anti-annexin A5 Autoantibodies in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Related to Human Immunodeficiency Virus Infection (HIV-PAH): A Case-Control Study.
authorString: Thoreau B, Renaud A, Chafey P, Clary G, Le Gall M, Broussard C, Launay O, Launay D, Hachulla E, Deligny C, Baruteau AE, Vallet-Pichard A, Chaigne B, Yaici A, Sitbon O, Montani D, Humbert M, Mouthon L.
abstractText: Autoantibody profiles in HIV-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension (HIV-PAH) remain poorly characterized. Using a validated proteomic pipeline (two-dimensional immunoblot, mass spectrometry, ELISA), we compared 20 HIV-PAH patients with 20 HIV controls without PAH. Anti-annexin A5 (AnxA5) autoantibodies were present in 55% of HIV-PAH patients versus 0% of controls (P < .001) and anti-14-3-3ε in 35% versus 5% (P = .04), despite comparable HIV duration, CD4 counts, and virological control. Both remained associated with PAH after adjustment for coinfections. These autoantibodies mirror those described in connective-tissue-disease-PAH, suggesting a possible overlap in autoimmune features and a research biomarker warranting prospective validation.

title: Association between SGLT2 inhibitor use and functional outcomes in elderly patients receiving ferric carboxymaltose: a retrospective observational cohort study.
authorString: Armentaro G, Pastura CA, Marino DM, Severini G, Maruca F, Condoleo V, Miceli S, Maio R, Andreozzi F, Vitale C, Volterrani M, Rosano GMC, Sciacqua A.
abstractText: Anemia and iron deficiency (ID) are extremely common comorbidities in elderly patients with chronic heart failure (CHF), and are associated with reduced functional capacity and worse prognosis. The objective of this study was to evaluate the association of one-year therapy with SGLT2i as add-on to intravenous infusion of ferric carboxymaltose (FCM) with improvement in functional abilities, in a cohort of elderly patients with HFrEF/HFmrEF with ID anemia. This study enrolled outpatients with CHF with ID anemia receiving intravenous administration of FCM and stratified into two groups according to SGLT2i use. The study endpoint was an achievement of Short physical performance battery (SPPB)>8pt at one year of follow-up. 222 patients, with a mean age of 75.5±6.0 years were enrolled and 53 received SGLT2i while 169 not. After 1 year of follow-up, a significant improvement in the main clinical, laboratory, echocardiographic and CGA parameters were observed in both groups; however, these improvements were statistically greater in those patients receiving also SGLT2i. The mean dose of FCM administered to the entire population at baseline was 734.2 ± 331.7 mg, with no significant differences between the two groups (p=0.475). Add on therapy with SGLT2i was associated with a greater improvement in functional abilities (OR 7.66; CI 95% 3.70-15.9, p<0.0001), while the presence of obesity was associated with a reduced probability of functional abilities improvement of 68% (OR 0.32; CI 95% 0.14-0.71, p=0.005). In patients with CHF and ID anemia, improvements in clinical symptoms and physical function were observed at one-year follow-up, as reflected by changes in SPPB scores. These improvements were greater among patients receiving concomitant SGLT2i therapy.

title: Does Ethnicity Influence the Long-Term Outcomes of Sleeve Gastrectomy? Results from a Prospectively Maintained Israeli Database.
authorString: Tibi N, Kirshtein B, Peleg N, Shmilovich H, Tatarov A, Issa N, Bekhor EY.
abstractText: Ethnic disparities often influence patient's outcomes. This study aimed to compare the weight loss and metabolic outcomes of laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG) in Israeli-Arab and Israeli-Jewish patients. A prospectively maintained cohort of 892 patients (262 Arabs and 630 Jews) who underwent LSG between 2009 and 2022 at a single tertiary academic center was retrospectively analyzed. Demographic, peri-operative, and long-term outcome data were compared between the two groups. Arabs were younger (35 vs. 44 years) and had a higher baseline BMI (45.1 vs. 42.9). Jews had more postoperative follow-ups (6.8 vs. 6.0). Despite these differences, long-term weight loss outcomes were broadly comparable between groups. %EWL outcomes did not differ significantly at 1- and 5-year follow-up. Although Arab patients demonstrated numerically higher %TWL at 1 year, this difference did not reach statistical significance and was not sustained at longer-term follow-up. Rates of comorbidity remission, including diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidemia, were similarly high. Despite baseline ethnic disparities, LSG was associated with comparable long-term weight loss and comorbidity resolution among Israeli-Arab and Israeli-Jewish patients.

title: Long non-coding RNA LINC00657 aggravates atrial fibrosis in atrial fibrillation via the miR-144-3p/ROCK1 competing endogenous RNA axis.
authorString: Liang X, Ou Z, Wang Y, Yan L.
abstractText: The clinical significance and fibrogenic mechanisms of long non-coding RNA LINC00657 in atrial fibrillation (AF) remain unclear. This study aimed to elucidate whether LINC00657 served as a mechanistic driver of atrial fibrogenesis in AF via modulation of the microRNA-144-3p (miR-144-3p)/Rho-associated coiled-coil containing protein kinase 1 (ROCK1) axis. LINC00657 expression was quantified in peripheral blood from 150 AF patients and 150 matched controls. Angiotensin II (Ang II)-stimulated primary rat cardiac fibroblasts and continuously infused C57BL/6 mice served as in vitro and in vivo fibrosis models, respectively. Functional assays (cell counting kit-8 (CCK-8), flow cytometry, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), western blot) and mechanistic experiments (subcellular fractionation, RNA pull-down, RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP), dual-luciferase reporter) were conducted to dissect the LINC00657/miR-144-3p/ROCK1 competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) axis. Clinically, elevated circulating LINC00657 discriminated AF patients from controls and independently predicted AF risk, correlating positively with high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP). In vitro, Ang II induced LINC00657 upregulation; silencing LINC00657 suppressed cardiac fibroblast proliferation, attenuated the release of inflammatory cytokines interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), reduced the expression of fibrotic markers including type I/III collagen and transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β), and promoted apoptosis. In vivo, knockdown of LINC00657 significantly attenuated Ang II-mediated atrial fibrosis in mice. Electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring and transesophageal atrial pacing further revealed that silencing LINC00657 significantly restored the atrial effective refractory period (AERP) and markedly decreased both the inducibility and duration of AF. Mechanistically, LINC00657 was predominantly localized to the cytoplasm and functioned as a ceRNA to sponge miR-144-3p, with ROCK1 identified as a direct downstream target of miR-144-3p. Both AF patients and model mice exhibited decreased miR-144-3p and increased ROCK1 expression, which negatively and positively correlated with LINC00657 levels, respectively. Rescue experiments demonstrated that miR-144-3p inhibitors partially reversed the anti-fibrotic effects of LINC00657 silencing, whereas further ROCK1 knockdown abrogated this reversal. Mechanistically, dissection of ROCK1 downstream signaling revealed that the LINC00657/miR-144-3p/ROCK1 axis specifically activated the ROCK1/myosin light chain 2 phosphorylation pathway, enhancing actomyosin contractility and stress fiber formation to drive the fibrotic cascade. The LINC00657/miR-144-3p/ROCK1 regulatory axis contributed to atrial fibrosis in AF.

title: Safety and Effectiveness of Dolutegravir/Rilpivirine in Japanese People Living with HIV: Final Report of 6-Year Post-marketing Surveillance Study.
authorString: Sebata A, Nagao T, Matsukawa T, Yoshikawa Y, Fukuda A, Wang D.
abstractText: Previous phase 3 studies demonstrated that a two-drug combination of dolutegravir (DTG) and rilpivirine (RPV) was non-inferior to three-drug antiretroviral therapy (ART) regimens in people living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) with stable plasma HIV-1 RNA. In Japan, DTG/RPV was approved in 2018 for maintenance of HIV-1 suppression, but evidence on its long-term safety and effectiveness is limited. In this post-marketing surveillance, data on the real-world clinical use of DTG/RPV were obtained through the HIV-Related Drug Cooperative Survey, a national joint post-marketing program overseen by manufacturers of HIV medications in Japan. The data collection period was from November 26, 2018 to November 26, 2024. Adverse drug reactions (ADRs) and potential risk factors associated with their incidence were examined. Effectiveness was evaluated by longitudinal changes in plasma HIV RNA levels and peripheral CD4+ T cell counts. Forty-four participants were registered, of whom 43 were assessed for safety and 41 for effectiveness. Safety analyses included 39 men and 4 women, with a mean age of 53.3 years. All participants switched from other ART regimens. DTG/RPV treatment exceeded 2 years in 76.74% of participants. Four ADRs, all non-serious, occurred in three participants (6.98%): weight increased (n = 1), hypertension (n = 1), hyperuricemia (n = 1), and condition aggravated (n = 1, aggravated hyperuricemia in the participant with hyperuricemia). The incidence of ADRs differed by the following participant characteristics: treatment duration, hepatic disorder, and renal disorder. Plasma HIV RNA levels remained < 50 copies/mL for 3 years after switching to DTG/RPV in most participants. The mean (standard deviation) peripheral CD4+ T cell count was 563.3 (207.2) cells/mm3, which remained stable throughout 3 years.
