This 6-year post-marketing surveillance confirms the long-term safety and effectiveness of DTG/RPV in people living with HIV in Japan who were virologically suppressed and switched to this two-drug regimen.

title: Giant macular hole in a female patient with X-linked Alport syndrome harboring a novel de novo COL4A5 variant.
authorString: Higa N, Hayashi T, Mizobuchi K, Maki H, Matsumoto T, Yokoo T, Nakano T.
abstractText: To report a female patient with genetically confirmed X-linked Alport syndrome (AS) presenting with progressive retinal thinning and giant macular hole formation. A 28-year-old woman with a history of bilateral LASIK surgery was referred for evaluation of bilateral progressive maculopathy. Comprehensive ophthalmic examinations, including optical coherence tomography (OCT) and full-field and multifocal electroretinography (ERG), were performed. Targeted next-generation sequencing of COL4A3, COL4A4, and COL4A5 genes was performed. At presentation, decimal best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was 0.7 in the right eye (OD) and 1.2 in the left eye (OS). The patient had no hearing loss or family history of renal or ocular disease. OCT revealed bilateral retinal thinning. During follow-up, progressive thinning of all retinal layers was observed, and a macular hole developed in OS, gradually enlarging from 546 µm at age 34 to a giant macular hole measuring 1684 µm in minimum diameter at age 39. At 37 years of age, full-field ERG demonstrated preserved rod system function with mild cone system dysfunction, and multifocal ERG showed significantly reduced macular responses bilaterally. Genetic testing identified a novel de novo heterozygous COL4A5 variant (p.Gly775Val), classified as pathogenic, confirming X-linked AS. X-linked AS may present with progressive diffuse macular thinning and giant macular hole formation even in female patients without hearing loss or a family history. AS should be considered in the differential diagnosis of unexplained bilateral macular thinning and giant macular hole in women.

title: Comparative cost analysis of Eluvia™ versus Zilver<sup>®</sup> PTX<sup>®</sup> in treating femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease utilizing real-world data.
authorString: Genovese EA, Williams AO, Sato R, McGovern AM, Jaff MR.
abstractText: Aim: To compare the hospital-based costs among patients with femoropopliteal artery (FPA) disease treated with Eluvia™ versus Zilver® PTX® drug-eluting stents using a large real-world USA hospital database. Materials & methods: This retrospective study included adults in the Premier Healthcare Database who underwent lower extremity FPA endovascular revascularization with Eluvia or Zilver PTX between 1 April 2019 and 31 March 2022. Total hospital-based costs during the index procedure and cumulative 1- and 2-year post-discharge follow-up were compared using multivariable generalized linear models adjusted for age, sex, race and baseline chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) status. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted by care setting (hospital inpatient and hospital outpatient) and among patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and CLTI. Results: A total of 7208 patients were included, comprising 4218 treated with Eluvia and 2990 treated with Zilver PTX. Patients treated with Eluvia had a higher prevalence of several comorbidities, including congestive heart failure and CKD. Unadjusted mean hospital-based index procedure costs were similar between groups (Eluvia, $28,631 vs Zilver PTX, $28,359; difference, -$272; p = 0.7233). After adjustment, mean index procedure hospital-based costs did not differ significantly between treatment groups ($30,031, p = 0.8491). However, Eluvia was associated with lower adjusted cumulative hospital-based costs at the 1-year (difference, $4,017; p = 0.0066) and 2-year (difference, $6250; p = 0.0021) follow-up. Similar associations were observed in the hospital inpatient and CKD subgroups, whereas no statistically significant differences were observed in the CLTI subgroup. Conclusion: Across patients undergoing femoropopliteal endovascular revascularization, Eluvia was associated with significantly lower post-discharge cumulative hospital-based follow-up costs than Zilver PTX while index procedure costs were comparable. These findings reflect hospital-based costs captured within participating hospitals and do not include medication costs or costs of care received outside the Premier Healthcare Database; therefore, they should not be interpreted as total healthcare costs.

title: Association Between Age, Systemic Diseases and Oral Health Habits in Stomatological Teaching Hospital Patients: A Cross-Sectional Study.
authorString: Shi Y, Du S, Huang C, Li Y, Liu F.
abstractText: This study examined age-related disease patterns and health behaviours in dental outpatients to enhance risk assessment and guide clinical decision-making, providing strategies for managing medical risks in dental clinics. This cross-sectional study enrolled 2,241 consecutive patients from a tertiary stomatological teaching hospital between November 2024 and April 2025. Based on the Pre-Treatment Risk Assessment Questionnaire for Dental Outpatients, a validated questionnaire was used to assess general demographic characteristics (10 items), systemic disease and medication use history (36 items) and oral hygiene habits (9 items). Data were analysed using SPSS 23.0 and Python 3.9. It showed that 12.5% of patients were aged ≥ 60 years. Elderly dental patients had a significantly higher prevalence of both single-system and multi-system diseases compared to other age groups (p 0.001). Specifically, the population showed significantly greater proportions of sensory disorders, cardiovascular diseases, respiratory system diseases, urogenital disorders, gastrointestinal disorders, neurological disorders, and endocrine system diseases, medication use, and history of organ transplantation than younger patients, especially coronary heart disease, hypertension, cardiac arrhythmia, diabetes mellitus, thyroid dysfunction and osteoporosis than younger age groups (all p 0.01). Furthermore, compared to younger patients, elderly patients had lower frequencies of toothbrushing, dental floss use, water flosser use, professional cleaning, and dental check-ups but exhibited reduced gingival bleeding and oral malodor(all p 0.001). Elderly patients exhibit higher systemic comorbidities but poorer oral hygiene than younger individuals, necessitating integrated care with risk assessment and oral health education. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating geriatric medicine training to improve interdisciplinary collaboration.

title: Multimodal Left Ventricular Rehabilitation Enabling Double-Switch Repair in Congenitally Corrected Transposition of the Great Arteries.
authorString: Martens AM, Thatte N, Breitbart RE, Kuriakose EM, O'Leary E, Emani SM, Kobayashi RL.
abstractText: In congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries, pulmonary artery banding (PAB) may prepare the morphologic left ventricle (LV) for systemic work before double-switch repair; however, development of ventricular dysfunction threatens candidacy. 2-year-old boy with corrected transposition of the great arteries and Ebstein-like tricuspid valve malformation developed biventricular dysfunction after PAB tightening, atrial septal stenting, and single-site epicardial pacing for heart block. Biventricular resynchronization therapy, heart failure therapy, and PAB loosening restored ventricular function. Pressure-volume analysis demonstrated comparable ventricular contractility, preserved LV diastolic function, and loading tolerance before uncomplicated double-switch repair. Multimodal rehabilitation and serial reassessment may preserve anatomic repair candidacy when reversible dysfunction complicates LV training. Ventricular dysfunction during LV preparation warrants evaluation for reversible contributors, including pacing-associated dyssynchrony and excessive pressure loading, before abandonment of anatomic repair. Following multimodal rehabilitation, serial imaging and pressure-volume analysis can assess LV systolic recovery, diastolic reserve, and loading tolerance for systemic work.

title: Clinical Characteristics, Lesion Distribution, and Systemic Comorbidities in Patients With Oral Lichen Planus.
authorString: Eninanç İ, Yalçın D.

journal.title: Journal of oral pathology & medicine : official publication of the International Association of Oral Pathologists and the American Academy of Oral Pathology

abstractText: This cross-sectional study aimed to comprehensively evaluate clinical forms, anatomical location, symptoms, systemic comorbidities, and potentially relevant factors in patients with oral lichen planus (OLP). Seventy-two patients with histopathologically confirmed OLP were included. Awareness of the disease, clinical forms, lesion location, and symptoms and their relationships were investigated. Smoking and alcohol consumption, and the presence of adjacent prosthetic or restorative materials were evaluated as potentially relevant factors. The prevalence of systemic diseases was assessed. The reticular form was the most frequent clinical presentation, followed by plaque-like and erosive forms. Lesions were most commonly localized on the buccal mucosa, followed by the tongue and the gingiva. The reticular form was most frequently observed on the buccal mucosa and tongue (p = 0.001). The combination of the reticular and erosive forms was most frequently observed on the buccal mucosa (p = 0.001), whereas the combination of the reticular and plaque-like forms was more commonly observed on the buccal mucosa and tongue. The erosive form was associated with more prominent symptoms (p = 0.003, p = 0.001). The most frequent systemic comorbidities were hypertension, diabetes, and hypothyroidism. No significant differences were observed in systemic diseases, symptoms, or relevant factors between sexes. Clinical forms of OLP may coexist within the same patient and, in some cases, within the same lesion. The most common combination was the coexistence of the reticular form with plaque-like or erosive forms. The erosive form is symptomatic. Systemic comorbidities were also commonly observed among patients with OLP, warranting attention during clinical evaluation.

title: Superior cervical sympathetic ganglion enlargement in idiopathic intracranial hypertension: An exploratory case-control study.
authorString: Muneer MS, Hasabo EA, Massoud TF.

journal.title: Cephalalgia : an international journal of headache

abstractText: AimIdiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) may involve bidirectional interactions between elevated intracranial pressure (ICP) and sympathetic nervous system activity along an ICP-sympathetic axis. We hypothesized that superior cervical sympathetic ganglion (SCG) volume is increased in IIH and investigated whether SCG enlargement on MRI may serve as a potential imaging covariate of disease severity associated with cerebrospinal fluid opening pressure (OP).MethodsIn this retrospective case control study, we selected IIH patients with a brain MRI within six weeks prior to lumbar puncture, and control participants with normal MRIs. We measured bilateral SCG volumes on MRI, and performed group comparisons and linear regression analyses.ResultsThirty-six IIH patients and 36 controls were included. Median OP in IIH was 24.5 cmH2O. Right, but not left, SCG volume was greater in IIH than controls (281 vs. 208 mm3, P = 0.038; BMI-adjusted P = 0.032). Combined bilateral SCG volume was also increased (631 vs. 381 mm3, P = 0.030; BMI-adjusted P = 0.026). A right SCG cutoff of ≥442 mm3 discriminated elevated OP (AUC = 0.713, optimal point for OP = 37.5 cmH2O) and was associated with increased odds of elevated OP (12.11, P = 0.016).ConclusionSCG enlargement may provide a potential imaging covariate for disease severity. However, given the exploratory nature of this investigation, future validation studies will determine its value in clinical decision-making and longitudinal assessment.

title: Structural Racism and Chronic Kidney Disease Among African Americans: A Research Process Guided by Public Health Critical Race Praxis.
authorString: Airhihenbuwa CO, Ameen K, Smith AJ, Franks NM, Urbanski M, Harris R, Howard B, Lea J, Arriola KJ.
abstractText: Structural racism has a profound impact on the ability of Black patients to access needed chronic kidney disease (CKD) treatment and care. Studies that have documented various forms of inequities in CKD diagnosis and treatment of CKD among Black patients are mostly focused on kidney disease outcomes with little attention to the processes of intervention implementation. Focusing on outcomes alone tends to assume the process of research, including study design and implementation, is neutral to the outcome. In actuality, the process, including methods employed by the researcher, all influence and shape the outcomes of research. Thus, closing gaps in differences in health outcomes requires a different approach; one that attends to the critical role of 'the process' of investigating these outcomes in research. In this paper, we focus on the processes employed to develop an intervention to address the role of structural racism in CKD treatment and care while acknowledging the importance of documenting disparities in outcomes. We emphasize the need to prioritize engagement with community leaders in the process of research interventions to be implemented in the community.

title: Dysregulation of Growth Hormone Axis after Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass.
authorString: Pei L, Cummings C, Saeed H, Amore A, Farahmandsadr M, Sheehan A, Ferraz-Bannitz R, Simonson DC, Patti ME.

journal.title: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

abstractText: Bariatric metabolic surgery has potent effects on glucose metabolism, with increases in insulin sensitivity and insulin secretion contributing to both improved glycemia and/or remission of type 2 diabetes (T2D) and development of hypoglycemia (post-bariatric hypoglycemia, PBH). Previous studies suggest GH secretion and/or action are altered after bariatric surgery and may mediate early post-surgical improvements in glycemic control. Given the importance of GH signaling in glucose metabolism, we hypothesized that reductions in GH signaling and/or action could also contribute to PBH. Assessment of GH responses to two distinct stimuli: (1) experimental hypoglycemia induced by hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemic clamp and (2) glucagon stimulation. Academic medical center. Individuals with history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) with PBH (n=20), without hypoglycemia (n=20), and weight-matched non-surgical controls (n=10). GH responses were assessed (1) during experimental hypoglycemia and (2) after glucagon stimulation. Plasma GH receptor (GHR) and insulin-like growth factors and binding proteins were also measured. Glucagon-stimulated GH levels were 5-6 times higher in both post-RYGB groups vs. controls at 120 minutes: control: 481±137 pg/ml; RYGB non-hypo 2521 ± 678 pg/ml; PBH: 3018 ±137pg/ml (control vs RYGB non-hypo p=0.02; control vs PBH; p=0.005). In contrast, PBH participants showed lower GH responses to experimental hypoglycemia. Additionally, plasma GHR and IGF-1 levels were reduced in PBH vs. controls. We find that plasma GH response to 2 distinct experimental stimuli differed in participants with a history of bariatric surgery. However, these patterns did not differ in those with and without PBH. Further studies will be required to determine if tissue-level alterations in GH action contribute to improved glycemic control after bariatric surgery.

title: Diabetes, stone composition, and renal function in a large cohort of patients with nephrolithiasis.
authorString: Besor O, Cohen M, Nasser S, Malachi A, Fremder A, Liran O, Shilo Y.
abstractText: Nephrolithiasis is linked to chronic kidney disease (CKD), and diabetic patients may be at higher risk for renal decline. However, the interaction of diabetes, stone composition, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) trajectory in patients with nephrolithiasis remains underexplored, particularly in community-based populations. In this retrospective cohort study of adult stone formers with a urinary stone composition analysis on file, diabetes status and stone composition were extracted from electronic records of a large health maintenance organization. Longitudinal eGFR measurements assessed renal function decline, and the effects of stone type, diabetes, and recurrent stone events on eGFR trajectory were evaluated. This study included 6,771 stone formers; 1,543 (23%) had diabetes. Diabetic patients had a significantly higher prevalence of uric-acid stones (18.3% vs. 6.5%, p<0.0001). Baseline eGFR differed robustly by stone type and diabetes status. After adjustment for age, sex, BMI, and hypertension, the rate of eGFR decline did not differ significantly by diabetes status within either the calcium-oxalate nor uric-acid subtype. Recurrent stone formers had greater renal function loss, while socioeconomic status had limited impact on eGFR change. Diabetic and non-diabetic stone formers show distinct baseline eGFR profiles that differ by stone composition, and diabetes was strongly associated with uric-acid stone formation; however, diabetes was not associated with an accelerated rate of eGFR decline once adjusted for age, sex, BMI, and hypertension. These findings support baseline risk stratification, rather than an accelerated-decline phenotype, as the key actionable insight for diabetic stone formers.

title: Potential roles for transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
authorString: Gao Z, Bao J, He C, Pan H, Zhang H, Zhai C.
abstractText: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous syndrome in which diastolic dysfunction develops against a background of interacting mechanisms: inflammation, oxidative stress, impaired calcium homeostasis, myocardial fibrosis, coronary microvascular dysfunction, mitochondrial impairment, and neurohumoral activation. Effective mechanism-targeted therapies remain limited. Transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) is a nonselective cation channel expressed in cardiac sensory nerves, vascular endothelial cells, immune cells, and possibly other cardiovascular cell populations. It responds to diverse physical and chemical stimuli and may influence calcium handling, inflammatory signaling, oxidative stress, myocardial fibrosis, mitophagy, and ferroptosis. Preclinical studies have linked altered TRPV1 expression or activity to myocardial remodeling, impaired relaxation, microvascular dysfunction, and heart failure progression, but direct evidence in HFpEF is still sparse. This review summarizes the biological properties of TRPV1, considers how its signaling might intersect with HFpEF pathophysiology, reviews experimental TRPV1-targeted interventions, and identifies the evidence needed before TRPV1 can be evaluated as a potential therapeutic target.

title: Association of Antihypertensive Medications with Orthostatic Hypotension among OIder Adults.
authorString: Khan MM, Col H, Larbi Kwapong F, Patil D, Zhang M, Turkson-Ocran RN, Ngo LH, Cluett JL, Mukamal KJ, Selvin E, Lutsey PL, Windham BG, Mosley TH, Hughes TM, Lipsitz LA, Coresh J, Valint A, Juraschek SP.
abstractText:
Background

Orthostatic hypotension (OH) is common among older adults actively prescribed hypertension pharmacotherapy. Associations between antihypertensives and OH are inconsistent, due to differences in drug classes and OH assessment protocols.

Methods

Three supine and six standing blood pressures (BPs) were measured over 6 minutes, timed to initiate immediately (0 minutes) and 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 minutes after standing. OH was defined as a drop of systolic/diastolic BP ≥ 20/10 mmHg upon standing from the supine position. OH phenotypes were initial (immediately after standing), early (within 3 minutes), late (after 3 minutes), and sustained (during 6 minutes of standing). Participants were asked about orthostatic symptoms experienced during OH assessment. We investigated associations of antihypertensive classes with OH phenotypes and orthostatic symptoms via multivariable logistic regression.

Results

Of 863 participants (mean age 84 years), 41% had initial, 24% early, 18% late, and 17% sustained OH; 81% used antihypertensive medications. First-line antihypertensives (renin angiotensin aldosterone system blockers, dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers, and thiazide diuretics) were not associated with OH or orthostatic symptoms. Among non-first-line, alpha blockers were significantly associated with initial OH (OR 1.80, 95%CI 1.07, 3.01) and orthostatic symptoms during postural change (OR 2.64, 95%CI 1.34, 5.23), whereas combined alpha-beta blockers were significantly associated with early, late, or sustained OH (2.24 [1.15, 4.37], 2.50 [1.21, 5.17], 2.99 [1.41, 6.30], respectively) and experienced symptoms while standing (3.08 [1.10, 8.65]).

Conclusions

First-line antihypertensives are not associated with OH among older adults, which does not support their discontinuation in the setting of non-neurogenic OH.

title: Renal artery imaging through long-term follow-up after radiofrequency renal denervation: Results from the SPYRAL Clinical Program.
authorString: Mahfoud F, Kandzari DE, Townsend RR, Kario K, Weber MA, Schmieder RE, Tsioufis K, Parmar G, Uretsky S, Gibson CM, McKenna P, Böhm M.
abstractText: Background: Renal denervation (RDN) safely reduces blood pressure (BP) in patients with uncontrolled hypertension. A potential long-term concern is the development of de novo renal artery stenosis (RAS) secondary to vascular injury. This study assesses the long-term vascular safety and incidence of RAS in patients treated with radiofrequency RDN from the SPYRAL HTN-OFF MED and -ON MED trials. Patients and methods: All patients underwent renal angiograms for assessment of the renal anatomy prior to randomization. Patients with RAS >50% were excluded from enrollment. At long-term follow-up (439+/-288 days), patients underwent duplex ultrasound imaging (DUS), computerized tomography angiography (CTA), and/or magnetic resonance angiography (MRA). Independent core labs evaluated all images. Clinically significant RAS was predefined as a stenosis ≥70%, confirmed by angiography. Results: A total of 610 patients were treated with RDN in the SPYRAL trials. At least one imaging modality was performed in 557 of the 610 patients (91%): 329 patients underwent DUS imaging, 230 underwent CTA, 148 underwent MRA, and 15 underwent renal angiography. With one possible exception, no clinically significant RAS was detected. No patients had renal artery reintervention. The proportion of images fulfilling pre-specified criteria for technical adequacy by the core lab was 100% (angiography), 87.5% (DUS), 80.6% (CTA), and 32.4% MRA. Conclusions: RF RDN appears to be safe, without confirmed vascular injury or RAS among 557 patients who had long-term imaging. Diagnostic utility of imaging modalities determined by specific criteria for technical adequacy for core lab evaluation was lowest with MRA and highest with DUS.

title: Remnant Clearance Capacity as a Determinant of Lipoprotein Oxidation: A Flux-capacity Framework.
authorString: Nakajima K, Murakami M, Tanaka A.
abstractText: The oxidative modification of apoB-containing lipoproteins has traditionally been considered to occur mainly after their retention within the arterial intima. However, oxidatively modified remnant-like lipoprotein particles are reproducibly detectable in the circulation under both fasting and postprandial conditions. This observation suggests that remnant oxidation may begin before arterial entry; however, the metabolic processes that permit such modifications still remain poorly understood. In this Review, we propose that delayed processing and the prolonged residence of triglyceride-rich lipoprotein (TRL) remnants provide temporal and spatial opportunities for oxidative modification in the circulation. TRLs are processed within an organized vascular-hepatic pathway involving GPIHBP1-bound lipoprotein lipase (LPL), progressive particle remodeling, apoE-dependent receptor recognition, and the hepatic uptake. We defined the integrated efficiency of this pathway as the remnant clearance capacity (RCC). Within the proposed Flux-Capacity framework, an imbalance between TRL production and RCC prolongs the remnant residence time and increases repeated exposure to endothelial surfaces, reactive oxygen species, inflammatory cells, and lipolysis-derived products. We further propose a two-stage model of remnant oxidation: limited oxidative modification may begin during prolonged circulation or endothelial processing, thus generating minimally modified remnants, whereas subsequent subendothelial retention permits more extensive oxidation and inflammatory amplification. This framework does not imply that the residence time directly demonstrates oxidation; rather,it identifies the residence time as a determinant of oxidative opportunity. Stable isotope kinetic studies, standardized meal testing, and molecular characterization of remnant-associated oxidative products are required to test this model. By linking impaired remnant clearance to pre-arterial oxidative modification, RCC provides a testable mechanistic framework for remnant-related residual cardiovascular risk.

title: Incidence, Modifiable Risk Factors, and Management of Cardiomyopathy After Ventricular Leadless Pacemaker Implantation.
authorString: Van Weyenbergh T, Willems R, Vörös G, Vandenberk B, Poels P, Dorrestijn A, Garweg C.
abstractText:
Background

Leadless ventricular pacemakers (LPM) provide only RV pacing, which may lead to pacing-induced cardiomyopathy (PICM). It is unclear whether LPM implant site or atrioventricular synchronous pacing using the Micra AV device influence PICM occurrence.

Objective

To evaluate the incidence of cardiomyopathy after LPM implantation and explore the association of implant site and AV-synchronous pacing with cardiomyopathy risk and LVEF evolution.

Methods

This single-center retrospective study included 401 patients implanted with an LPM (Micra AV n=145) between July 2015 and March 2025. PICM was defined as cardiomyopathy (≥10% LVEF decline to <50%) in the presence of >20% ventricular pacing, where pacing was considered the primary cause. Risk factors for cardiomyopathy and LVEF evolution were assessed using Cox regression and mixed-effects modelling.

Results

Over a median follow-up of 33.0 months, all-cause cardiomyopathy occurred in 13.6% (4.8%/year), while PICM was identified in 5.5% (1.9%/year). RVOT implantation was independently associated with a lower incidence of all-cause cardiomyopathy (HR 0.48, P=0.019), and a slower LVEF decline (-0.56%/year vs -1.43%/year, P=0.013) compared with mid-septal implantation. Device type (Micra AV vs VR) was not associated with clinical outcomes or LVEF evolution. Among patients developing cardiomyopathy, 92.7% were medically treated, with 57.9% achieving ≥10% LVEF improvement, and 36.8% complete recovery. CRT upgrade was uncommon (7.3%).

Conclusion

Cardiomyopathy occurred in a substantial proportion of LPM recipients. RVOT implantation was associated with lower cardiomyopathy incidence and slower LVEF decline, whereas Micra AV implantation did not improve clinical outcomes. However, higher AV synchrony was linked to slower LVEF deterioration.

title: Immunosuppressive termination of pro-inflammatory miRNA degradation via circular RNA nanosponge for sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy treatment.
authorString: Wang Y, Li W, Zhou Y, Liu S, Gu X, Tao L, Zhou J, Ding Y.

journal.title: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society

abstractText: Managing inflammatory cytokine storms is prevalent in treatment of sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy (SICM), yet it remains a challenge to immunosuppression weaning. We herein propose an immunosuppressive termination of pro-inflammatory microRNA-33 (miR-33) degradation strategy for on-demand anti-inflammatory management. Inspired by circular RNA (cRNA) sponging capacity, we designed a miR-33-targeted sequence of cRNA (cRNA-33), including 11 of miR-33 binding sites and a single microRNA-223 (miR-223)-specific immunosuppression binding site. To improve drugability, cRNA-33 is compressed into reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive polymeric assembly, and covered by tannic acid-modified hyaluronic acid to enhance cardiac inflammatory macrophage accumulation. Triggered by intracellular ROS, cRNA-33 rapidly dissociates from assembly and binds sufficient miR-33 to alleviate inflammatory actions of NLRP3 and IL-1β induction. Macrophages are subsequently shifted from pro-inflammatory to anti-inflammatory phenotype, resulting in high expression of miR-223 that destabilizes cRNA-33 through the miR-223-responsive site to discontinue immune responses. The cRNA-33 treatment yields 80% decrease of inflammation efficacy, 90% cardiac function recovery and 87.5% survival rate in study mice. Collectively, this study has provided an advanced anti-inflammatory therapy for SICM, at a safe level.

title: Multiscale modeling reveals non-linear dynamics of AKT-mediated NO-ROS crosstalk in shear stress-induced endothelial phenotype.
authorString: Zhang YY, Wang YT, Qiu Y, Li YJ, Chen D, Qin KR.
abstractText: Endothelial dysfunction is a critical initiating event in atherosclerosis. The regulatory role of the AKT signaling pathway in the transition between injury and repair remains unclear. This study developed a multiscale model to elucidate how AKT signaling modulates endothelial repair under shear stress. The framework integrates hemodynamic stimuli, cellular behaviors, and nonlinear AKT/NO/ROS biochemical kinetics coupled with endothelial phenotypic transitions. Results demonstrate that endothelial dysfunction is driven by a spatial mismatch between NO production and ROS consumption rather than global deficiency. Phenotypic restoration is governed by the nonlinear interactions within the NO-ROS network. Systematic simulations identified a golden window, where Day 1 intervention and moderate AKT activation effectively restored endothelial cells and normalized redox status. Conversely, excessive activation caused supra-physiological over-suppression. These findings suggest that repair is determined by the tight coupling of redox homeostasis and immune dynamics, highlighting intervention timing and dosage as critical factors for precision vascular therapy.

title: Lipidomics Analysis Reveals That Lipid Profile Is Associated With the Liver and Plasma in ApoE<sup>-/-</sup> Atherosclerotic Mice.
authorString: Zhang L, Xie Y, Liu Y, Tang M, Xing S.
abstractText: The key pathogenesis of atherosclerosis is lipid disorders resulting from aberrant liver metabolism and release of lipids into the bloodstream, leading to endothelial damage and deposition of lipids beneath the endothelial layer. Currently, there exists a limited amount of information pertaining to alterations in liver and blood lipid metabolism. This study aimed to examine the lipid profile associated with the liver and plasma of ApoE<sup>-/-</sup> mice. ApoE<sup>-/-</sup> mice were selected because one high-fat dietary challenge produces aortic lesions and hepatic steatosis in the same animal, allowing plaque and hepatic lipid disturbance to be sampled together. Mice were randomly divided into a normal diet (ND) group and a high-fat diet (HFD) group. To validate the atherosclerosis model, histopathologic analysis techniques such as HE stain, Oil Red O stain, and Masson stain were employed. The lipid profile in both liver and plasma was evaluated using UHPLC-Q Exactive plus MS, utilizing positive and negative ionization modes. In comparison to the ND group, the HFD group exhibited elevated levels of lipid deposition, plaque area, and collagen fiber. Specifically, the liver contained 40 distinct lipids, while the plasma contained 177 distinct lipids. Further examination demonstrated that 11 distinct lipids exhibited differential content in both the liver and plasma. This study demonstrated the existence of a comprehensive lipid profile in the liver and plasma of atherosclerotic mice, with a particular emphasis on PC and TG, which may provide a new biomarker and a better understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying atherosclerosis.

title: Modelling the human IL6RA Asp358Ala variant in mice: effects on atherosclerosis and abdominal aortic aneurysm
authorString: Takaoka M, Sharma R, Lareyre F, Clement M, Harrison J, Masters L, Lu Y, Paul D, Mallat Z.
abstractText: The association of IL6RA Asp358Ala variant with reduced risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) prompted interest in targeting IL6 signalling in these conditions. A recent report that ziltivekimab, a neutralising anti-IL6 antibody, did not reduce major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with ASCVD and chronic kidney disease, has cast doubt on the causal role of IL6 signalling in ASCVD. Here, we show that introducing the orthologous IL6RA Glu357Ala substitution in male mice leads to the same alteration in soluble IL6RA levels seen in humans, and significantly prevents atherosclerosis and AAA. Thus, therapies that more closely reproduce the biological effects of the IL6RA Asp358Ala variant on IL6 signalling are needed to reduce cardiovascular risk in humans.

title: Quality standards for the diagnosis and management of ATTR and AL amyloidosis: a nominal group technique study.
authorString: Obici L, Damy T, Galan L, Moody W, Agostinho J, Barton C, Campos C, D'Alessio G, Dares K, Dohrn MF, Fine N, Gregory D, Jammes E, McIntosh K, Ripoll-Vera T, Yilmaz A, Ritchie I, Palladini G.

journal.title: Amyloid : the international journal of experimental and clinical investigation : the official journal of the International Society of Amyloidosis

abstractText:
Background

Transthyretin (ATTR) and immunoglobulin light-chain (AL) amyloidosis are progressive conditions that can have debilitating effects on people. Delayed diagnosis and variable access to high-quality care continue to affect quality of life and prognosis. Clear and ambitious quality standards could drive consistent care and improve outcomes.

Methods

A modified nominal group technique was used to develop consensus-based quality standards for the diagnosis and management of ATTR and AL amyloidosis. Eighteen experts participated, including patient representatives and clinicians from high-income, publicly funded health systems in Europe and Canada. Each quality standard was paired with at least one measurable indicator to support implementation and monitoring.

Results

A total of 29 provisional statements were generated, with consensus achieved on eight quality standards. These span the full care pathway and emphasise the need for timely, person-centred and interdisciplinary care. Twenty accompanying indicators were developed.

Conclusion

This is the first comprehensive set of consensus-based quality standards for ATTR and AL amyloidosis care. They provide a practical and aspirational framework to guide quality improvement across health systems. Adoption of these standards could improve early diagnosis, equitable access to treatment, and quality of life. Future research may explore their feasibility and adaptation for other health system settings.

title: Development of an artificial intelligence algorithm for automated detection of cardiovascular intervention-related complications.
authorString: Okken A, Wanders R, Klappe A, Beukema KF, Oirbans T, Noordzij PG, van Lent A, Haanemaaier SH, Balt JC.

journal.title: Netherlands heart journal : monthly journal of the Netherlands Society of Cardiology and the Netherlands Heart Foundation

abstractText:
Background

Intervention-related complications negatively affect healthcare quality and costs. Complication registration and reporting play an important role in the improvement of healthcare outcomes but are time-consuming and hampered by under-reporting.

Methods

We developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-aided tool that extracts specific complications, including bleeding, tamponade, CVA and phrenic paralysis, from electronic healthcare records of patients undergoing pulmonary vein isolation (PVI), percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA) and transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Both structured and unstructured data were used, along with additional signals identified through machine learning. The model was optimized to achieve high sensitivity.

Results

Electronic records of 6,564 patients undergoing PVI, PTCA, and TAVI, performed at our hospital from 2017-2022, were used. The final model detected the various complications with a sensitivity between 94.4 and 100%, while specificity ranged from 99.4-100%. This resulted in positive predictive values ranging from 47.5-81%, with F‑scores varying between 0.64-0.87.

Conclusion

We developed an AI-driven tool capable of automatically detecting complications following cardiac interventions from patient healthcare records, achieving a very high sensitivity. Our tool enables registration of complications while significantly reducing administrative burden on the healthcare providers and data managers. It provides valuable and high-quality input for improvement cycles, thereby enhancing patient safety and healthcare quality.

title: Prostatic Artery Embolization in a Patient With Bilateral Internal Iliac Artery Occlusions.
authorString: Wang SZ, Song A, Arett C, Rostambeigi N.
abstractText: Background: Prostatic artery embolization (PAE) is an established treatment for lower urinary tract symptoms due to benign prostatic hyperplasia but can be challenging in complex anatomy. Study Sample: An 86-year-old male with history of abdominal aortic aneurysm repair and aortobifemoral bypass presented with gross hematuria and urinary retention. Imaging and clinical evaluation confirmed BPH-related clot retention as the etiology. Careful review of preprocedural CT angiography revealed occluded bilateral internal iliac arteries, a right aberrant obturator artery (AOA) (corona mortis variant), arising from the inferior epigastric artery, which itself originated from the native right external iliac artery. The AOA supplied the entire prostate, perfusing both lobes and contributing to the contralateral pelvic circulation as well. Cone-beam CT and angiography confirmed the perfusion to both prostatic lobes. PAE was performed by accessing the native common femoral artery and selectively catheterizing the AOA. Embolization of the prostatic parenchyma was completed successfully while preserving flow to adjacent pelvic structures, avoiding non-target embolization. Results: The patient had complete resolution of hematuria and urinary retention and remained catheter-free at 1-year follow-up. Conclusions: This case highlights the importance of pre-procedural evaluation and planning, demonstrating that PAE can be safely and effectively performed even in variant vascular anatomy.

title: Perioperative Challenges of Unrepaired Tetralogy of Fallot in a Child With Severe Secondary Erythrocytosis: Lessons for the Modern Era.
authorString: Kamojjala R, Hoenig SM, Faniyi LA, Bhavana S, Zhu Y, Stumh L, Clark J, Stewart RD, Karamlou T.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
journal.title: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
journal.isoabbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg

abstractText: In the United States, secondary erythrocytosis in children with unrepaired Tetralogy of Fallot (ToF) is rare yet may present in children from underresourced environments. title: The triglyceride-glucose index and intramyocardial hemorrhage identify a high-risk phenotype in STEMI.
authorString: Li Z, Zhang M, Wang Y, Chen L, Sha W, Yang Y, Lu Y.
abstractText:
Aims

The prognostic value of combining the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and intramyocardial hemorrhage (IMH) in STEMI is unclear. We assessed their individual and combined association with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).

Methods

This retrospective study included 456 STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI. TyG index was calculated from admission blood samples; IMH was assessed by cardiac magnetic resonance. The primary outcome was MACE (median follow-up 4 years). Multivariable Cox regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, incremental prognostic assessment (C-index, NRI, IDI), and interaction testing were performed.

Results

MACE increased across TyG tertiles (15.79% → 27.63% → 43.42%). The highest tertile remained independently associated with MACE (adjusted HR 1.86; 95% CI 1.09-3.20). Patients with high TyG (≥8.66) plus IMH had the worst prognosis (HR 4.00; 95% CI 2.49-6.39; P < 0.001), far exceeding either factor alone. Adding the combined variable to a base model improved discrimination and reclassification (C-index 0.640 → 0.658; NRI = 0.216, P = 0.020; IDI = 0.025, P = 0.008). Neither additive nor multiplicative interaction was significant, and results were consistent in diabetic and non-diabetic patients. A significant interaction was observed between TyG index and infarct location (P for interaction = 0.037), with a stronger effect in anterior (HR 1.59) than non-anterior infarction (HR 0.75).

Conclusions

The TyG index independently predicts long-term MACE in STEMI. Combining high TyG with IMH identifies a high-risk phenotype with a 4.0-fold higher MACE risk and incremental prognostic value. The TyG effect is stronger in anterior infarction, suggesting infarct location should be considered in metabolic risk stratification.

title: Conduction System Pacing for Resynchronization Therapy in Heart Failure: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
authorString: Pajareya P, Chuanchai W, Laohasurayotin K, Chumpangern Y, Suphalak P, Phutinart S, Siranart N, Chokesuwattanaskul R, Prasitlumkum N.
abstractText: Conduction system pacing (CSP) has emerged as a promising modality for cardiac resynchronization therapy, but evidence of CSP in heart failure (HF) remains controversial. The authors aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of CSP, including left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) and His bundle pacing, to biventricular pacing (BiVP) in HF. The MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CENTRAL databases were searched from inception until May 2026. The primary endpoint was a composite of hospitalization for heart failure (HHF) and all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints included clinical endpoints (HHF, all-cause mortality), cardiac resynchronization therapy responses (predefined and super-response), echocardiographic parameters (left ventricular ejection fraction and left ventricular end-systolic volume), electrophysiologic parameters (paced QRS duration and capture threshold), functional status (NYHA functional class and 6-minute walk test distance), procedural performance (procedural time, fluoroscopy time, lead implantation time), and device-related complications. (PROSPERO registration: CRD420261388077). Twelve randomized controlled trials involving 1,054 patients (566 CSP and 488 BiVP) were included. CSP showed a significant reduction in primary composite endpoint (OR: 0.30; 95% CI: 0.18-0.52; I2 = 0%), improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction (mean difference: 3.06%; 95% CI: 0.82%-5.30%; I2 = 55%), and shorter paced QRS duration (mean difference:-11.49 ms; 95% CI: -20.70 to -2.28; I2 = 85%), compared with BiVP. In the LBBAP group, there were greater reductions in primary composite endpoint with higher rates of super-response (OR: 2.18; 95% CI: 1.44-3.30; I2 = 54%) compared with BiVP. No differences were observed in functional status or device-related complications. CSP, and potentially LBBAP, was associated with a significantly lower composite endpoint of HHF and all-cause mortality compared with BiVP, supporting CSP as an alternative to BiVP in HF.

title: A Cross-sectional Study for Estimation of Prevalence of Cognitive Impairment in Epileptic Patients.
authorString: Akhilesh B, Dasgupta SS, Kannadka C, Gupta R, Nagar SJ, Boppana L.
abstractText: Cognitive impairment is a frequent, but frequently overlooked, complication of epilepsy that has a negative impact on patients' quality of life and functioning. Recurrent seizures and neurological factors can have a deleterious effect on multiple cognitive domains such as memory, attention, and executive function. The Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scale was used to assess cognitive impairment in patients with epilepsy in this study. The objectives of this study were to estimate the prevalence of cognitive impairment in patients with diagnosed epilepsy for more than 2 years using the MoCA scale, assess cognitive function using the MoCA score in epilepsy patients, and determine the prevalence of cognitive impairment. A hospital-based prospective observational study was conducted among 97 patients with epilepsy for 18 months. A MoCA scale (0-30) was used to evaluate cognitive function. Means and standard deviations were given for numerical variables, and frequencies and percentages were reported for categorical variables. The Fisher's exact test or Chi-square test was used for the analysis of categorical variables as appropriate. The prevalence of cognitive impairment was significantly higher in the group with hypertension (45, 95.7%) than in the group without hypertension (40, 80.0%) (χ2 = 5.54, P = 0.02). The association between cognitive impairment and diabetes mellitus was not statistically significant. The associations with hypothyroidism, cerebrovascular accident, and ischemic heart disease were not statistically significant, as per Fisher's exact test (P = 0.99, 0.07, and 0.99, respectively). Based on these findings, it is concluded that there is a need to consider cognitive impairment as an important and often unrecognized comorbidity with the overall disease burden of patients with epilepsy. The authors emphasize that it is crucial to include routine cognitive assessments in daily clinical practice.

title: The Impact of Immunoglobulins on Cardiovascular Diseases and Lipid Profiles in Elderly and Middle-Aged Chinese Individuals: A 15-Year Retrospective Study.
authorString: Li Y, Jiao L, Gao Y, Ni XF.
abstractText:
Background

Humoral immunity defends via immunoglobulins. This study aimed to evaluate the association between immunoglobulins and CVDs and lipid profiles in a cohort of individuals aged 45 years and older.

Methods

Data from 982 subjects were analyzed. The cohort had a median age of 61 years (IQR 56-72), was predominantly male (84.8%), and had a high prevalence of CVDs at baseline, including hypertension (30.3%), dyslipidemia (20.7%), arrhythmia (22.3%), coronary heart disease (12.1%), and atrial fibrillation (4.5%). Logistic regression analysis was used to examine the association between baseline and time-varying serum levels of IgG, IgA, and IgM and the presence of five CVDs: coronary heart disease, atrial fibrillation, arrhythmia, hypertension, and dyslipidemia. We additionally explored the relationship between these immunoglobulin levels and lipid profiles.

Results

No significant differences in immunoglobulin levels were found between CVD and non-CVD groups at baseline, and baseline immunoglobulin levels were not associated with any CVD. However, longitudinal changes in IgG and IgA levels were positively associated with changes in free fatty acids (FFAs). Intriguingly, longitudinal increases in IgM levels were positively associated with total cholesterol, LDL-C, non-HDL-C, and HDL-C.

Conclusions

This study provides longitudinal evidence that increases in IgG and IgA levels are associated with elevated FFA levels, while increases in IgM are associated with an adverse lipid profile characterized by higher total cholesterol, LDL-C, and non-HDL-C, and lower HDL-C. These findings suggest a link between humoral immunity and lipid metabolism that warrants further investigation, with potential implications for cardiovascular risk assessment.

title: Genetic Characterization of Familial and Multifactorial Chylomicronemia in Taiwanese Patients with Severe Hypertriglyceridemia.
authorString: Lin CF, Chen YH, Charng MJ.
abstractText:
Aims

Familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS) and multifactorial chylomicronemia syndrome (MCS) are clinically overlapping causes of severe hypertriglyceridemia (HTG). This study aimed to delineate the genetic characterization of FCS and MCS in Taiwanese patients with severe HTG.

Methods

After exclusion of identifiable secondary causes, patients with severe HTG, defined as fasting plasma triglyceride (TG) concentrations ≥ 500 mg/dL, were enrolled. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) was performed with focused analysis of canonical FCS-related genes, including LPL, APOC2, APOA5, LMF1, and GPIHBP1. Cascade screening was performed when appropriate.

Results

Among the 20 patients with severe HTG (mean age, 47.2±10.8 years; 60% male), five patients were classified as having FCS and 15 as having MCS. The mean highest untreated plasma TG concentration was 2163.0±1382.9 mg/dL in the FCS group and 3196.8±2095.5 mg/dL in the MCS group; the corresponding mean TG/TC ratios were 7.9±3.5 and 7.1±3.4, respectively. Among patients with FCS, four carried homozygous APOA5 G185C and one carried compound heterozygous LPL variants consisting of R270H and linked L279R/S474X. MCS showed genetic heterogeneity, including heterozygous disease-causing variants in FCS-related genes, the APOE ε2/ε2 genotype, and candidate TG-raising variants. Several variants in APOA5, LMF1, APOC3, CREB3L3, GCKR, MLXIPL, and NCAN were considered as candidate TG-raising variants. Cascade screening supported the autosomal recessive inheritance in LPL- or APOA5-associated FCS.

Conclusion

WES-based genetic testing helps define the genetic architecture of FCS and MCS. This study highlights the heterogeneous genetic background of severe HTG in Taiwan and provides a foundation for future population-specific studies of disease-causing and candidate TG-raising variants.

title: Stenosis of a novel frozen elephant trunk in a patient with chronic dissection.
authorString: Tokunaga S, Okamura H, Yamaguchi A.
abstractText: A partial elephant trunk (PET), a new type of frozen elephant trunk, was designed to prevent distal stent graft-induced new entry using a thinner nitinol wire with less radial force. We report a case of PET stenosis in chronic dissection. Total arch replacement was performed using a PET. After weaning from cardiopulmonary bypass, the lower-limb blood pressure decreased to 90% of the upper-limb blood pressure. Intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography revealed incomplete PET expansion, and on postoperative day 1, the lower-to-upper body blood pressure ratio further decreased to 70% due to PET stenosis at the steeply angulated arch. Emergency thoracic endovascular aortic repair was successfully performed, completely resolving the pressure gradient.

title: Intravascular Lithotripsy of Aortic and Renal Lesions as a Therapeutic Tool for Pickering Syndrome: A Case Report.
authorString: Martínez-Cachero García M, Ariza Molina C, Sanmartino González SA, Zanabili Al-Sibbai A.
abstractText: We report the case of a 73-year-old woman admitted with Pickering syndrome, a life-threatening condition characterized by recurrent flash pulmonary edema secondary to severe renovascular disease. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated an atrophic left kidney, a heavily calcified visceral aorta with a coral-reef morphology, and a near-occlusive stenosis of the right renal artery. Urgent endovascular treatment was performed with intravascular lithotripsy for plaque modification of the suprarenal aorta and the right renal artery, followed by renal artery stenting. The patient showed prompt clinical recovery, with resolution of pulmonary edema, stabilization of blood pressure, and improvement of renal function. This case illustrates the potential role of intravascular lithotripsy as a minimally invasive adjunct for managing severely calcified aorto-renal disease in high-risk patients, enabling endovascular treatment in otherwise challenging anatomy.

title: Advances in Smart Hydrogels for Myocardial Infarction Therapy: A Scoping Review of Applications, Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
authorString: Ahadzi E, Manu OD, Antwi-Baah R, Agbe H, Adjei PE.
abstractText: Smart hydrogels are stimuli-responsive biomaterials that enable targeted, sustained, and controlled therapeutic delivery. Their unique ability to respond to physiological cues such as pH, temperature, reactive oxygen species (ROS), and enzymatic activity makes them highly attractive for myocardial infarction (MI) therapy. This scoping review explores advances, applications, challenges, and future perspectives related to the use of smart hydrogels in MI. An initial comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, and ScienceDirect yielded 1802 records, from which 32 studies published between 2011 and 2025 met the inclusion criteria under the PRISMA-ScR framework. An updated search identified seven additional eligible studies, bringing the total to 39 included studies. These studies primarily focused on smart hydrogels for delivering bioactive agents, including growth factors, stem cells, exosomes, and nanoparticles, to enhance myocardial regeneration and repair. Evidence from preclinical models consistently demonstrated improvements in myocardial remodeling, angiogenesis, cell survival, and functional cardiac recovery. Despite these encouraging findings, several important limitations were identified. Studies relied on short evaluation periods, lacked long-term follow-up, and were restricted to small-animal models, thereby limiting the robustness of translational insights. Large-animal studies and early clinical investigations remain scarce, highlighting the gap between experimental progress and clinical application. Nonetheless, smart hydrogels stand out as a promising therapeutic platform because of their capacity for localized, adaptive, and sustained responses within the complex postinfarct microenvironment. Future work should prioritize long-term efficacy studies, development of minimally invasive delivery methods, and the use of clinically relevant preclinical models to better facilitate translation to human MI therapy.

title: The 'Upstairs-Downstairs' heart with complete main pulmonary artery agenesis and PDA-dependent pulmonary circulation: A rare structural intersection characterized by multi detector computed tomography.
authorString: Kanji AM, Aziz T, Fundikira L, Akberali U, Salingwa L, Lyimo F, Jacob M.
abstractText: Superior-inferior ventricular arrangement is an exceedingly rare form of congenital cardiac malposition, representing fewer than 0.1% of all congenital heart diseases, and is almost invariably associated with complex intracardiac anomalies. We report a 3-year-old male who presented with persistent cyanosis, exertional dyspnea, and failure to thrive. Prospective ECG-gated CT angiography demonstrated situs solitus with levocardia. A superior-inferior ventricular arrangement was present, with the morphologic left ventricle positioned superior to the morphologic right ventricle. The great arteries were normally related, with a left-sided aortic arch. A large ventricular septal defect was identified. Pulmonary atresia was present, characterized by the absence of the right ventricular outflow tract, pulmonary valve, and main pulmonary artery. Native confluent branch pulmonary arteries were present and received pulmonary blood flow through a large patent ductus arteriosus supplying the left pulmonary artery, with additional small systemic-to-pulmonary collateral vessels. The morphologic right ventricle was dilated and hypertrophied, with associated enlargement of the right atrium. Pulmonary venous drainage was normal, and no abnormalities of the systemic venous drainage were identified. This case underscores the critical role of cardiac CT angiography in comprehensive anatomical delineation of rare and complex congenital cardiac malformations, with direct implications for surgical planning and prognostication.

title: Clinical Outcomes After Recovered, Positive, and Negative Pulse Oximetry Screening Results Among Newborns.
authorString: Karppi L, Kiviranta P, Sankilampi U.
abstractText:
Importance

Pulse oximetry screening (POS) detects critical congenital heart defects (CCHDs) and other neonatal morbidities, but the clinical significance of initially abnormal results that normalize on repeat testing remains unclear.

Objective

To assess the prevalence and clinical implications of positive, recovered, and negative early POS results in asymptomatic newborns.

Design, setting, and participants

This population-based cohort study included asymptomatic neonates born at 35 weeks' gestation or later who underwent early POS at 2 to 6 hours of age at a tertiary-level university hospital in Eastern Finland between January 1, 2012, and December 31, 2019. Data were analyzed from August 2025 to August 2026.

Exposure

Positive POS result or indeterminate POS result that normalized to a negative POS result (recovered) with repeat testing.

Main outcomes and measures

Primary outcomes were neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission and continued hospitalization at 7 days; secondary outcomes included diagnostic investigations and neonatal morbidities. Associations between POS screening results and outcomes were examined using modified Poisson regression adjusted for maternal age, parity, body mass index, and cigarette smoking during pregnancy and newborn sex, gestational age, and birth weight Z score.

Results

The cohort included 16 599 newborns born at 35 weeks' gestation or later who underwent early POS at 2 to 6 hours of age (8349 [50.3%] female; mean [SD] gestational age, 39.8 [1.3] weeks). POS results were negative in 16 160 newborns (97.4%), recovered in 208 (1.3%), and positive in 231 (1.4%). Compared with a negative POS result, a recovered or positive POS result was associated with higher risk of NICU admission (adjusted risk ratio [ARR], 5.62 [95% CI, 4.58-6.91] and 13.04 [95% CI, 11.77-14.44], respectively) and continued hospitalization at 7 days (ARR, 4.70 [95% CI, 3.07-7.19] and 11.97 [95% CI, 9.26-15.47], respectively). Recovered POS was also associated with greater risk of antibiotic exposure before 72 hours of life (ARR, 5.45 [95% CI, 3.94-7.52]) and need for respiratory support (ARR, 10.16 [3.53-29.21]) compared with a negative result. Respiratory disease was more common in newborns with recovered than negative POS results (27 [13.0%] vs 214 [1.3%]), as were sepsis (10 [4.8%] vs 127 [0.8%]) and hypoglycemia (17 [8.2%] vs 565 [3.5%]). No CCHD occurred among newborns with recovered POS.

Conclusions and relevance

In this cohort study of neonates born at 35 weeks' gestation or later, those with initially indeterminate POS results that normalized on repeat testing had increased risks of treatable neonatal conditions and hospital care but not of CCHD. Further prospective studies should investigate whether targeted assessment of these newborns could reduce morbidity and prolonged hospitalization.

title: Early Morbidity and Survival After Left Lateral Segment Versus Whole Liver Graft Transplantation in Children.
authorString: Linge H, Pfister ED, Muth V, Arbabzadah S, Forner J, Linge T, Richter N, Quante M, Tsui TY, Baumann U, Schmelzle M, Felgendreff P, Van Beekum CJ.
abstractText:
Background

Left lateral segment (LLS) grafts expand graft availability for infants and small children requiring liver transplantation (LT). However, their cumulative early postoperative burden compared with whole liver grafts (WLGs) remains incompletely characterized.

Methods

This retrospective single-center cohort study included 95 consecutive primary pediatric LT recipients treated between 2019 and 2024, comprising 56 LLS and 39 WLG recipients. Cumulative postoperative morbidity within 90 days was quantified using the Comprehensive Complication Index (CCI). Additional outcomes included biliary and vascular complications, unplanned surgical reinterventions, length of stay, graft loss, retransplantation, and graft and patient survival.

Results

LLS recipients were younger and smaller than WLG recipients. Cumulative 90-day morbidity was greater after LLS transplantation (median CCI 53 vs. 45, p = 0.002). LLS recipients had higher rates of bile leakage (18% vs. 3%, p = 0.024), intra-abdominal bleeding (15% vs. 0%, p = 0.019), and unplanned surgical reintervention (43% vs. 8%, p < 0.001). Although the overall incidence of biliary complications was similar between groups, anastomotic biliary strictures during follow-up were more frequent after WLG transplantation (28% vs. 9%, p = 0.014). Hospital stay was longer after LLS transplantation (median 43 vs. 27 days, p < 0.001). No statistically significant differences in graft loss, retransplantation, or graft and patient survival were detected between groups.

Conclusions

LLS transplantation was associated with greater cumulative morbidity within 90 days, characterized by higher rates of bile leakage, intra-abdominal bleeding, unplanned surgical reintervention, and prolonged hospitalization. Despite this greater early postoperative burden, no statistically significant differences in graft loss, retransplantation, or graft and patient survival were detected during the available follow-up. These findings support continued use of LLS grafts to expand transplant access. Given the associated early morbidity, it highlights the importance of an experienced surgical and medical team.

title: Comparison analysis of the triglyceride-glucose index, triglyceride-glucose and frailty index in cardiovascular disease and mortality association among patients with rheumatoid arthritis: A population-based cohort study.
authorString: Xu Y, Zhao H, Gao Y, Han J, Wu Z, Zhang L, Zhao J.
abstractText: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a major cause of excess mortality among patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Conventional risk assessment may not fully capture the metabolic abnormalities and physiological vulnerability associated with RA. We investigated whether the triglyceride-glucose-frailty index (TyG-FI), which combines a surrogate marker of insulin resistance with accumulated health deficits, was associated with prevalent CVD and cardiovascular mortality among adults with RA. We analyzed 1090 adults with self-reported RA from 10 cycles of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey conducted between 1999 and 2018. TyG-FI was calculated as the product of the triglyceride-glucose index and a 49-item deficit-accumulation frailty index. Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine the association with prevalent CVD, whereas Cox proportional hazards regression was used to examine cardiovascular mortality. Restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses, sensitivity analyses, and discrimination analyses were conducted as secondary analyses. In the fully adjusted models, each 1-unit higher TyG-FI was associated with higher odds of prevalent CVD (odds ratio, 4.50; 95% confidence interval, 3.20-6.33) and a higher hazard of cardiovascular mortality (hazard ratio, 1.77; 95% confidence interval, 1.16-2.70). The reported areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0.80 for prevalent CVD and 0.81 for cardiovascular mortality in models incorporating TyG-FI, compared with 0.73 and 0.80, respectively, in models incorporating TyG. An exploratory subgroup analysis suggested a stronger association between TyG-FI and prevalent CVD among participants aged ≤65 years (P for interaction = .044). Higher TyG-FI was associated with prevalent CVD and cardiovascular mortality among US adults with self-reported RA. TyG-FI may capture complementary metabolic and frailty-related information; however, its incremental predictive value, calibration, clinical utility, and external validity require further evaluation before clinical implementation.

title: [Association of maternal dietary intake, folic acid supplementation and offspring betaine-homocysteine methyltransferase (<i>BHMT</i>) and <i>BHMT2</i> gene polymorphisms with congenital heart disease].
authorString: Luo MJ, Tang JP, Sun MT, Ruan XR, Chen KB, Bao XX, Wang TT, Song Y, Qin JB.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Zhonghua Liu Xing Bing Xue Za Zhi
journal.title: Zhonghua liu xing bing xue za zhi = Zhonghua liuxingbingxue zazhi
journal.isoabbreviation: Zhonghua Liu Xing Bing Xue Za Zhi

abstractText: Objective: To evaluate the associations of maternal dietary intake, folic acid supplementation, offspring BHMT and BHMT2 gene polymorphisms and their interactions with the risk for congenital heart disease (CHD) and its main subtypes. Methods: A hospital-based case control study was conducted. From January 2018 to May 2019, a total of 620 children with simple CHD and their mothers were consecutively recruited as the case group from Hunan Children's Hospital. During the same period, 620 children without any congenital anomalies and their mothers, who were diagnosed at the same hospital, were enrolled as the control group. The information about their demographic characteristics and periconceptional exposure information were collected by using structured questionnaire. In addition, peripheral venous blood samples were obtained from the children for genotyping of BHMT and BHMT2 polymorphisms. Multivariable logistic regression analysis and crossover analyses were conducted to evaluate the associations of maternal dietary intake, folic acid supplementation, offspring BHMT and BHMT2 gene polymorphisms and their interactions with the risk for CHD and its subtypes. Results: After correction for multiple testing, multivariable logistic regression analyses showed that maternal excessive intakes of smoked food, barbecued food, fried food, pickled vegetable during early pregnancy was associated with increased risk for overall CHD in offspring [aOR>1.00, false discovery rate (FDR)-adjusted P<0.05], while maternal regular intakes of fish and shrimp, fresh egg, bean, milk product as well as periconceptional folic acid supplementation were associated with reduced risk for offspring overall CHD (aOR<1.00, FDR-adjusted P<0.05). Significant associations were observed between BHMT polymorphisms and overall CHD risk, including rs3733890 (AA vs. GG, aOR=2.61, 95%CI: 1.52-4.50), rs1316753 (recessive model, aOR= 1.63, 95%CI: 1.17-2.29), and rs1915706 (CC vs. TT, aOR=2.72, 95%CI: 1.42-5.21), similar results were also found in atrial septal defect and ventricular septal defect population. Moreover, BHMT gene polymorphisms showed antagonistic interactions with the intake of fish and shrimp, as well as bean (aOR<1.00, relative excess risk of interaction <0). Conclusions: Maternal dietary patterns, folic acid supplementation, and BHMT gene polymorphisms (rs3733890, rs1316753, and rs1915706) are associated with the risk for CHD and its subtypes. In addition, interactions between BHMT polymorphisms and maternal dietary intake might contribute to the development of CHD in offspring.

title: c-Jun N-Terminal Kinase-2 Mediates Alcohol and Corticosterone-Induced Tissue Injury at the Gut-Liver Axis.
authorString: Basa L, Shashikanth N, Shukla PK, Shekhar C, Meena AS, Jones N, Raju P, Nguyen C, Swarna S, Willis NB, B Gowda SG, Lee SC, Pierre JF, Rao R.

journal.title: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology

abstractText: Chronic stress and the stress hormone corticosterone are exacerbating factors in alcohol-induced gut and liver injury; however, the underlying mechanisms are poorly defined. This study investigates the potential role of c-Jun N-terminal kinase 2 (JNK2) in alcohol- and corticosterone-mediated gut and liver injury. The effects of chronic ethanol feeding and corticosterone administration on gut and liver injury were evaluated in JNK2 knockout (JNK2-KO) and wild-type mice. We measured gut permeability to FITC-inulin in vivo; epithelial tight junction (TJ) integrity by immunofluorescence confocal microscopy; microbiota dysbiosis by 16S rRNA sequencing; mucosal inflammatory responses by cytokine mRNA assay; endotoxemia by plasma lipopolysaccharide (LPS) levels; systemic inflammation by cytokine ELISA; and liver damage by multiple assays. Data show that chronic ethanol feeding-induced gut barrier dysfunction, epithelial TJ disruption, and colonic mucosal inflammatory responses were potentiated by corticosterone in the wild-type mice, but not in JNK2-KO mice. Microbiota analyses indicated that the gut microbiota composition in pair-fed and ethanol-fed JNK2-KO mice is distinctly different from that of wild-type mice. The effects of ethanol and its potentiation by corticosterone on Paneth cell-specific genes were absent in JNK2-KO mice. Ethanol-induced intestinal mucosal inflammatory responses, endotoxemia, and systemic inflammation, and their potentiation by corticosterone, were absent in JNK2-KO mice. Ethanol-induced liver injury and its potentiation by corticosterone, as assessed by plasma AST/ALT, liver triglyceride, histopathology, and cytokine expression, were also absent in JNK2-KO mice. These data demonstrate that JNK2 plays a pivotal role in ethanol-induced tissue injury at the Gut-Liver axis and that this effect is potentiated by corticosterone.

title: Extracellular Vesicles in Neonatology: Have We Found the Magic Bullet?
authorString: Papadogeorgou P, Tsantes AG, Valsami S, Fortis SP, Kriebardis AG, Mougiou V, Iliodromiti Z, Boutsikou T, Iacovidou N, Sokou R.
abstractText: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) represent nanoparticles released by numerous cell types and exerting distinct biological roles. Extracellular vesicles are enclosed in a lipid layer and contain proteins, lipids, nucleic acids, carbohydrates or even mitochondria. The fundamental utility of EVs is intercellular communication, while their implication in various biological processes, such as inflammation and hemostasis, is well-documented. Growing evidence indicates the significant usefulness of EVs as biomarkers in certain prematurity-related diseases, like bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) and necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC). Moreover, many in vitro and in vivo studies have been undertaken in order to explore the potential therapeutic impact of EVs in BPD, NEC and retinopathy of prematurity (ROP), some of them yielding promising results. The present narrative review aims towards the summarization of the existing data on the application of EVs in diverse neonatal disorders, such as BPD, NEC, ROP, sepsis, multi-organ failure, coagulopathy and brain injury. The widespread investigation of EVs in neonatology and their potential implementation in clinical practice may lead towards a revolutionary approach and management of neonatal diseases, as well as an innovative perception of prematurity.

title: Genetic Insights Into Cryptogenic Stroke: From Etiologic Heterogeneity to Clinical Translation.
authorString: Li L, Sun Z, Wang H, Zhang J, Cheng S.
abstractText: Cryptogenic stroke remains challenging because its complex etiology and limited diagnostic tools hinder precise secondary prevention. Growing genetic evidence suggests that cryptogenic stroke may have identifiable genetic architectures that provide additional insights into etiologic classification. In recent years, large-scale genome-wide association studies, multi-omics integration, and other genetic investigations have begun to reveal signals linked to several potential causes, including occult atrial fibrillation and atrial cardiopathy, nonstenotic carotid artery plaque, patent foramen ovale-related paradoxical embolism, monogenic disorders, clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential, and cancer-related thrombosis. These findings suggest a possible shift from exclusion-based diagnosis toward a more mechanism-driven approach. Recent genetic discoveries have enabled preliminary work on predictive models for risk stratification. Emerging genetic tools may also offer promising approaches for etiologic stratification and mechanistic investigation. However, current research in this area remains limited by heterogeneous definitions, modest sample sizes, limited ancestral diversity, and gaps in mechanistic and prognostic evidence. Consequently, clinical translation remains at an early stage. Future research should establish larger and more diverse genomic cohorts with longitudinal phenotyping and advance multidimensional data integration. These efforts may refine etiologic classification and support precision treatment in cryptogenic stroke.

title: Reduced Plasma Cardiac Myosin-Binding Protein-C Concentrations in Cats with Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Evidence from Chronic, Treated Disease.
authorString: Tanakwang N, Sakunasing N, Kumphune S, Mektrirat R, Na Lampang K, Boonyapakorn C, Pongkan W.

journal.title: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

abstractText: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), the most common cardiac disease in cats, is associated with genetic variants, including MYBPC3, which encodes cardiac myosin-binding protein C (cMyBP-C), a key sarcomeric protein involved in myocardial contractility. Although circulating cMyBP-C has emerged as a biomarker of myocardial injury in humans, its clinical relevance in feline HCM remains unclear. This study characterized plasma cMyBP-C and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) concentrations across different stages of feline HCM, evaluated their diagnostic performance, and assessed their associations with echocardiographic parameters. A cross-sectional study included 65 cats: 25 healthy cats, 25 with subclinical HCM, and 15 with clinical HCM (chronic and treated). Plasma NT-proBNP was significantly higher in clinical HCM than in healthy cats (p = 0.0117), whereas plasma cMyBP-C was lower in clinical HCM than in subclinical HCM (p = 0.0462) and healthy cats (p = 0.001). At a cut-off of <1.270 ng/mL, plasma cMyBP-C showed 76.19% sensitivity and 65.38% specificity for distinguishing HCM. NT-proBNP alone showed higher overall diagnostic accuracy (76.67%) than the combined use of cMyBP-C and NT-proBNP. Neither plasma NT-proBNP nor cMyBP-C correlated significantly with echocardiographic parameters. Reduced circulating cMyBP-C concentrations in cats with chronic, treated HCM suggest a biomarker pattern distinct from that reported in acute myocardial injury and warrant further investigation.
