title: A Systematic Review of Complications Following Elective Foot and Ankle Surgery.
authorString: Spencer L, Phillips C, Alam S, Ferguson K, Feinn R, McHugh D, Kannegieter E.

journal.title: Journal of foot and ankle research

abstractText:
Introduction

Complications following elective foot and ankle surgery are a significant source of morbidity and may impair recovery. Evidence is often procedure specific, limiting a broader understanding. This review aimed to synthesize complication profiles, risk factors, and mitigation strategies across elective procedures.

Methods

PubMed, Scopus, and CINAHL were searched for studies published between 1 January 2020 and 30 June 2025. Eligible studies included adults undergoing elective foot and ankle surgery and reporting postoperative complications. Data were extracted on complication type, incidence, and risk factors, and synthesized narratively due to heterogeneity.

Results

Nine studies (n = 20,455) were included. Complication rates varied: infection (0.3%-12.5%), wound healing problems (0.5%-10.0%), nonunion (0.8%-18.7%), hardware removal (3.8%-15.5%), nerve injury (0.2%-10.0%), pain or stiffness (0.8%-18.7%), and systemic complications (3.6%-7.4%). Consistent risk factors included diabetes, obesity, smoking, and peripheral vascular disease. Higher complication rates were associated with revision surgery, prolonged operative time, and multisegment reconstruction.

Conclusion

Complications after elective foot and ankle surgery are common and multifactorial, with consistent risk patterns across procedures. These findings support improved risk stratification, targeted preoperative optimization, and structured postoperative care.

title: Evidence-based management of kawasaki disease in the emergency department.
authorString: Lee A, Seaton KK.
abstractText: Kawasaki disease is currently the leading cause of acquired heart disease in children in developed countries. Signs and symptoms of Kawasaki disease may mimic other childhood illnesses, making it difficult to diagnose, especially in children who present with an incomplete form of the disease. Untreated Kawasaki disease may lead to the formation of coronary artery aneurysms and sudden cardiac death. Emergency clinicians should consider Kawasaki disease in pediatric patients presenting with prolonged fever, as prompt evaluation and management can significantly decrease the risk for serious cardiac sequelae. This review discusses the presentation, diagnostic criteria, and management of Kawasaki disease in the emergency department.

title: Dynamic control of carbon-ion radiation dose distribution amid respiratory motion challenges: A review of prediction research using geant4 and deep learning physics-constrained models.
authorString: Ding J, Li P, Yeong CH.

journal.title: Journal of applied clinical medical physics

abstractText:
Background

Carbon ion radiotherapy (CIRT) offers superior dose conformity and biological effectiveness; however, its precision is highly sensitive to respiratory motion, leading to dose uncertainty and interplay effects that compromise treatment accuracy.

Methods

A comprehensive literature synthesis was conducted on studies employing motion-resolved imaging techniques (e.g. SMEIR), dynamic dose prediction, 4D robust planning, and hybrid adaptive methods for CIRT. The study emphasised the use of Geant4 Monte Carlo simulations combined with deep learning models, including physics-informed neural networks, to simulate and predict dose perturbations caused by respiratory motion. This review also examined clinical treatment planning systems, radiobiological modelling, and adaptive strategies to mitigate the effects of motion.

Results

The integration of Geant4 with deep learning enabled high-fidelity, computationally efficient dose prediction under respiratory motion, improving accuracy in dose localization and adaptation. Motion management techniques such as respiratory gating, rescanning, and 4D robust optimization demonstrated enhanced tumor control and normal tissue sparing. Hybrid models combining Monte Carlo data and AI inference show promise for near-real-time adaptive therapy. Despite these advances, challenges remain, including limited motion-rich datasets, computational demands for real-time recalculations, and the complexity of incorporating variable relative biological effectiveness (RBE) into adaptive planning.

Conclusions

Combining Geant4-based Monte Carlo simulations with deep learning frameworks shows emerging promise for controlling carbon ion dose distributions amid respiratory motion, though direct clinical validation for this combination remains limited. These hybrid models may enhance the precision and adaptability of CIRT, offering improved outcomes. Future efforts should focus on clinical validation, standardization, and overcoming computational and data limitations to facilitate clinical translation of motion-adaptive CIRT. These approaches remain at Technology Readiness Levels (TRL 3-5) and require prospective clinical validation before routine implementation.

title: Women With Bipolar Disorder are at Increased Risk of Sarcopenia.
authorString: Williams LJ, Stuart AL, Berk M, Quirk SE, West EC, Koivumaa-Honkanen H, Honkanen R, Heikkinen J, Davis JA, Weerasinghe DK, Pasco JA.
abstractText:
Introduction

While bipolar disorder is associated with significant comorbidity, little is known about the musculoskeletal health of individuals with bipolar disorder. Thus, we aimed to investigate the association between bipolar disorder and muscle strength, mass, quality and sarcopenia.

Methods

Women with bipolar disorder (n = 106) were recruited from healthcare settings and age-matched to controls (n = 300), without bipolar disorder, from the Geelong Osteoporosis Study. Both groups, aged ≥ 20 years. were drawn from South-Eastern Australia. Bipolar disorder was identified using a clinical interview (SCID-I/NP). Maximum handgrip strength (HGS) was measured using a Jamar dynamometer, appendicular lean mass (ALM) using a Lunar densitometer and body mass index (BMI, kg/m2) was calculated. Foundation for the National Institute of Health (FNIH) and European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People (EWGSOP2) algorithms were used to determine low HGS, ALM, probable and confirmed sarcopenia. Socioeconomic status (SES) was determined and information on lifestyle obtained via questionnaire.

Results

Higher proportion of women with bipolar disorder met criteria for low HGS and ALM compared to those without bipolar disorder. Using FNIH and EWGSOP2 criteria, 36 (8.9%; 34 probable and 2 confirmed) and 46 (11.4%; 43 probable and 3 confirmed) women met criteria for sarcopenia, respectively. Women with bipolar disorder were twice as likely to have sarcopenia (FNIH; OR 2.24, 95% CI: 1.11-4.55 and EWGSOP2; OR 2.78, 95% CI: 1.47-5.20), independent of age, smoking, activity, alcohol, diet and SES.

Conclusion

These data suggest women with bipolar disorder have an increased likelihood of sarcopenia. Replication and research into underlying mechanisms are next necessary steps.

title: Body Composition Phenotypes and Their Metabolic Associations in Treatment-Naïve Patients With Newly Diagnosed Type 2 Diabetes: A DXA-Based Cluster Analysis.
authorString: Zhang X, Zhang R, Jiang T.
abstractText:
Background and aims

We characterized body-composition heterogeneity in treatment-naive type 2 diabetes (T2DM) using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), and assessed whether cluster-metabolic associations persisted after accounting for sex-related body-composition differences.

Methods

K-means clustering of 50 DXA-derived body-composition variables classified 185 treatment-naive T2DM patients. Variance decomposition, sex-stratified analyses, sex-stratified clustering, sex-specific standardization clustering and multiple imputation (20 datasets) addressed sex confounding and missing data.

Results

Four exploratory body-composition clusters were identified: Low Fat-Low Muscle, Male-Predominant Central Obesity (98.6% male), Female-Predominant Low-Muscle High-Adiposity (98.0% female) and High Fat-High Muscle. Two clusters showed strong sex predominance; sex-specific normalization reduced sex-cluster dependence while preserving metabolic associations. In multiple-imputation-adjusted models, Clusters 2 and 4 had markedly higher MASLD odds (OR = 9.69 and 8.55, respectively), while Cluster 4 had lower osteoporosis (OR = 0.16) and higher hyperuricemia (OR = 6.36) odds versus Cluster 1. Bone turnover markers, diabetic retinopathy and diabetic kidney disease showed no significant associations.

Conclusions

DXA-based body-composition clusters are associated with distinct metabolic and comorbidity profiles-particularly MASLD, osteoporosis and hyperuricemia-that persisted after sex-specific standardization and multiple imputation. Given the sex-cluster overlap and modest silhouette width, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

title: Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasonography of Orbital and Intraocular Pathologies in 24 Dogs and 6 Cats.
authorString: Ortner JI, Hittmair KM, Nell B, Blohm KO.
abstractText:
Objective

Contrast-enhanced ultrasonography (CEUS) is a noninvasive and relatively safe imaging technique to assess ocular perfusion, showing high sensitivity and specificity for tumor characterization in human oncology, while reports on its application in canine and feline diseased eyes are limited. This study aimed to describe the CEUS features of orbital and intraocular pathologies in dogs and cats in order to evaluate its diagnostic value in detecting and characterizing various lesions.

Animal studied

CEUS examinations of 30 animals (24 dogs, 6 cats) were evaluated retrospectively.

Procedures

Following B-mode ultrasonography, CEUS examinations utilizing sulfur hexafluoride were performed. Pathologies were categorized in one of the following groups: orbital neoplastic lesions, orbital inflammatory lesions, intraocular neoplastic lesions, intraocular inflammatory lesions and retinal detachment. Qualitative perfusion parameters, contrast intensity, enhancement pattern, perfusion type and time to wash-in and wash-out were evaluated.

Results

CEUS detected vascularization in orbital and intraocular pathologies, with variable enhancement characteristics. Persistent vascularization was observed in all cases of retinal detachment. In orbital and intraocular neoplastic lesions, CEUS improved lesion localization, assessment of interactions with surrounding tissues and tissue perfusion. For inflammatory pathologies such as abscesses, myositis, and steatitis, the additional diagnostic value of CEUS compared to B-mode ultrasonography was limited.

Conclusion

Findings indicated that CEUS could identify a variety of orbital and intraocular pathologies and provided additional diagnostic information to B-mode ultrasonography, particularly for assessing neoplastic lesions and retinal detachments. CEUS has the potential to enhance ophthalmic ultrasonography in differentiating specific pathologies. Prospective studies are warranted to further evaluate its clinical use.

title: What Counts as 'Real' in Healthcare Interaction? Examining Human/Technology Hybrid Simulation Interactions in Communication Skills Training.
authorString: Pilnick A, Bridgstock L, Albert S, O'Brien R, Borneuf AM.
abstractText: Simulated interaction is a common healthcare training tool and is increasingly technologically mediated. Although the need for clinical realism or authenticity of simulated interactions is commonly understood, less attention has been paid to their interactional realism. However, research beyond healthcare suggests that participants interact differently in simulated scenarios. This paper examines simulations conducted through the MetaHuman Live platform, where a human tutor is live-linked to an avatar using the tutor's voice and mapping their gaze and facial expressions. We use conversation analysis (CA) to analyse student nurses' interactions with this platform, identifying key areas where they differ from 'real' interactions. These are openings, closings, establishing shared knowledge, interactional progressivity and orientation to simulation platforms as an assessment tool. We suggest that features of a hybrid platform which aim to increase realism can also make interaction more complicated for learners trying to navigate between 'the person' and 'the system'. We conclude that, although our analysis suggests ways forward for the more effective integration of simulation technologies in training communication skills in healthcare, it also points to our continued need for a better sociological understanding of how interaction itself works in practice, to provide an evidential basis for design and evaluation of such simulations.

title: Diabetic Polyneuropathy Patients Exhibit an Altered Skeletal Muscle Proteome Phenotype.
authorString: Thybo FF, Khan KS, Jakobsgaard JE, Andersen H, Vissing K, Palmfeldt J.
abstractText:
Purpose

Diabetic polyneuropathy (DPN) is a debilitating complication of diabetes that affects motor nerves and may impair skeletal muscle health. This study investigated skeletal muscle proteomic alterations associated with DPN compared with type 2 diabetes without DPN (T2D) and healthy controls (CON).

Experimental design

An exploratory proteomic profiling was performed in 15 participants divided into three groups based on clinical and neurophysiological diagnosis (DPN, n = 5; T2D, n = 5; CON, n = 5). Biopsies from the gastrocnemius lateralis muscle were analyzed using LC-MS/MS-based proteomics and pathway enrichment analyses.

Results

A total of 265 and 444 proteins were differentially expressed in DPN compared with T2D and CON, respectively (q < 0.05). Enrichment analyses revealed marked alterations in mitochondrial-related pathways, including cellular respiration, distinguishing DPN from both comparison groups. Differences between T2D and CON were present but less pronounced. DPN was characterized by downregulation of glycogen-regulating proteins (phosphorylase kinase G1 and A1) and upregulation of ferritin light chain (FTL), alpha actin 2, and myosin-binding protein H.

Conclusions and clinical relevance

DPN is associated with a distinct and progressive skeletal muscle proteomic phenotype, supporting mitochondrial dysfunction as a key feature and providing a basis for future mechanistic and therapeutic studies.

title: Efficient Propranolol Delivery Enabled by Manganese-Based Bioactive Metal-Organic Frameworks With High Loading Capacity.
authorString: Borhanipasvisheh H, Dehghani Siyahaki S, Gholamhosseinzadeh E.
abstractText: A green and efficient method was developed for propranolol delivery utilizing manganese-based bioactive metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) as biocompatible drug carriers. Mn-based bioactive MOFs with a high aspect ratio were synthesized and characterized for size (average, 17 µm), morphology, stability, elemental composition, crystallinity, functionality, charge character, and biocompatibility (a protein adsorption capacity of 0.03 µg µg<sup>-1</sup> (5 h) and a hemolysis ratio of < 0.5%). Afterward, the MOFs were utilized for drug loading via an encapsulation method, and the drug release studies were also performed. The drug loading was confirmed using the zeta potential, CHN analysis, and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) measurements. An encapsulation efficiency of 96% (0.5 W/W (drug/MOFs)) and a maximal capacity (Q<sub>max</sub>) of 0.526 mg mg<sup>-1</sup> were obtained. The drug release showed that 93.72% of the loaded drug was released after 10 h for a composite of 0.25 W/W (drug/MOFs), while for 0.5 W/W (drug/MOFs), the drug release reached a plateau after 3 h. The kinetic studies showed longer release times and higher release rates for higher drug loading efficiency. Overall, herein, a bioactive platform for efficient delivery of propranolol was developed to improve the therapeutic efficacy by enhancing the drug loading and achieving controlled drug release.

title: Identification of Risk-Related Prenatal Medication Exposure Profiles for Childhood Asthma Using the Bayesian Profile Regression: A Cohort Study Using the POMME Cohort.
authorString: Russo S, Bénévent J, Beau AB.
abstractText:
Purpose

To identify prenatal medication exposure profiles associated with childhood asthma.

Methods

This population-based cohort study used data from the POMME (PrescriptiOn Médicaments Mères Enfants) cohort, including 18 851 children born in the Haute-Garonne area (France) in 2010 and 2015, and followed until 2023. Prenatal exposure was defined as medications dispensed to mothers during pregnancy, classified by Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical subclasses, assessed separately for each trimester as none, one dispensing, or at least two dispensings. Childhood asthma from Age 4 years onward was identified using an algorithm based on dispensing of asthma medications. Bayesian profile regression was applied to simultaneously cluster children according to prenatal medication exposure profiles and asthma occurrence. High-risk profiles were characterised by predominant medication classes, timing of exposure and maternal and infant characteristics.

Results

Seventeen prenatal medication exposure profiles were identified. Six profiles were associated with a higher average risk of childhood asthma compared with the overall population risk (15.2%). High-risk profiles were characterised by repeated exposure throughout pregnancy to medications for acid-related disorders, thyroid hormones, antibiotics, asthma medications and antihistamines, as well as by combinations involving antibiotics, nasal medications and cold medicines in late pregnancy. Mothers in high-risk profiles more frequently presented chronic conditions and pregnancy-related complications.

Conclusion

This exploratory study identified prenatal medication exposure profiles associated with childhood asthma using a semi-supervised Bayesian approach. This method highlights combinations and critical windows that may warrant further investigation and supports Bayesian profile regression as a useful tool for signal detection in perinatal pharmacoepidemiology.

title: Excessive Weight Loss with Zepbound Is Associated with Higher Rates of Adverse Events, Electrolyte Imbalances, and Hospitalization than Moderate Weight Loss
authorString: Murugadoss K, Gregg CJ, Varma G, Shiv S, Venkatakrishnan A, Montorzi M, Smith JM, Rosen CJ, Gibson CM, Soundararajan V.
abstractText: Zepbound (tirzepatide) is among the most effective obesity medicines for weight reduction, in both clinical trial and real-world settings. Product marketing largely centers on weight-loss magnitude, which may reinforce the expectation that larger reductions are always better. Using de-identified EHRs, we compared 1,039 Zepbound initiators (1.7%) whose first-year weight loss reached ≥30% (“excessive weight loss”) with 20,668 Zepbound initiators (34.7%) who lost 5%-15% (“moderate weight loss”). After 1:4 propensity score matching (837 versus 3,348 patients), large language model (LLM)-curation extracted 24 adverse events that physician notes explicitly attributed to weight loss. The rate of any weight loss-attributable adverse event was significantly higher with excessive weight loss, at 39.4 versus 14.4 per 100 patient-years, representing 294 (35.1%) versus 479 (14.3%) patients (rate ratio [RR]: 2.78, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.40-3.21; P<0.001). Falls, weakness, syncope, alopecia, low blood pressure, gastro-intestinal symptoms, and muscle loss were significantly enriched in the excessive weight loss cohort after false-discovery-rate correction (all q<0.001). Hospitalization was documented in 215 patients (25.7%) with excessive weight loss versus 527 patients (15.7%) with moderate weight loss (RR: 1.63, 1.42-1.87), Intensive care admission in 44 patients (5.3%) versus 77 patients (2.3%) (RR: 2.29, 1.59-3.28) (both q<0.001), and newly recorded heart-failure diagnosis in 11 patients (1.3%) versus 16 patients (0.5%) (RR: 2.75, 1.28-5.91; q=0.028). Laboratory tests and vital measurements recorded within 30 days of the lowest achieved body weight corroborated these findings, including significant enrichments in systolic (<90 mmHg) or diastolic (<60 mmHg) hypotension (RR: 3.19, 95% CI 2.51-4.05), anemia (RR: 1.86, 1.45-2.40), hyponatremia (RR: 2.74, 1.63-4.60), hypokalemia (RR: 2.34, 1.58-3.46), hypocalcemia (RR: 3.25, 1.87-5.68), hypoalbuminemia (RR: 2.93, 1.83-4.70), and hypoproteinemia (RR: 3.89, 2.32-6.52) in excessive weight loss patients (all q<0.001). While residual confounding and documentation differences may contribute to some real-world associations, the significantly greater burden of adverse events, hospitalization rates, laboratory test anomalies, and vital-sign abnormalities among Zepbound patients with excessive weight loss warrants further investigation. These findings support moving towards individualized weight-loss goals, motivate the need for prospective studies into the risk-benefit profile of Zepbound, and call for closer scrutiny of pharmaceutical marketing to clarify that the greatest weight reduction may not translate into better health outcomes.

title: Biological age measured by DNA methylation clocks and mortality: A systematic review and meta-analysis
authorString: Tay JH, Barros D, Dong J, Choudhury S, Bakulaite A, Wang W, Maier AB.
abstractText: This systematic review aimed to synthesize evidence on the association between DNA methylation (DNAm) age and all-cause and disease-specific mortality risks in adults. A systematic search of six databases from Jan 1 2011 to April 15 2026 identified articles assessing the association of DNAm age measures and all-cause or disease-specific mortality in adults from general or disease-specific populations. Effect sizes were pooled as hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using inverse-variance random-effects models. Of 42 023 records screened, 125 articles (380 705 participants) met the inclusion criteria, with 53 included in meta-analyses. Overall, 48 distinct DNAm clocks were evaluated. Higher DNAm ages were associated with higher risks of all-cause, cardiovascular, and cancer mortality risks. In general populations, GrimAge epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) showed consistent associations across mortality outcomes, with each 1 year higher GrimAge EAA associated with ~6-10% higher all-cause (31 cohorts, n=53 642, HR per SD: 1.46 [95% CI 1.38, 1.55], HR per 1-year: 1.09 [95% CI 1.08, 1.11], I^2=84.1%, p-value=1.21 x 10^(-14)), cardiovascular (6 cohorts, n=30 751, HR per SD: 1.55 [95% CI 1.38, 1.73], HR per 1-year: 1.10 [95% CI 1.07, 1.13], I^2=28.0%, p-value=1.71 x 10^(-4)), and cancer (5 cohorts, n=27 187, HR per SD: 1.31 [95% CI 1.15, 1.50], HR per 1-year: 1.06 [95% CI 1.03, 1.10], I^2=33.6%, p-value=4.76 x 10^(-3)) mortality. Clocks incorporating additional surrogates and technical refinements showed numerically larger pooled associations than their original counterparts. GrimAge2 (HR per SD: 1.65 [95% CI 1.53, 1.77] vs 1.46 [1.38, 1.55]) and PCGrimAge (1.56 [1.36, 1.78] vs 1.51 [1.32, 1.74]) showed higher pooled HR association with all-cause mortality than GrimAge. Further work is warranted to evaluate the responsiveness of DNAm clocks to interventions and potential clinical utility.

title: Buffalo Hump, Neck Circumference, and Stroke Risk: A Narrative Review from a Surface Landmark to an Untested Intervention Target
authorString: Huang X.
abstractText:
Background:

Buffalo hump is often oversimplified as localized fat accumulation, but its tissue composition is heterogeneous, and its clinical significance extends beyond cosmetic concerns. Neck circumference has accumulated relatively consistent evidence in cardiometabolic epidemiology, but most integrated analyses have used metabolic risk factors or metabolic syndrome as endpoints rather than hard endpoints such as stroke. Whether enlargement of the buffalo hump leads to an increase in neck circumference, and whether interventions that reduce the buffalo hump or neck circumference can translate into stroke prevention, remain unresolved. This narrative review examines the evidence linking buffalo hump and neck circumference to stroke risk and identifies structural gaps that currently preclude translation into prevention strategies.

Methods:

PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure were searched through March 2026 using terms for buffalo hump or dorsocervical fat, neck circumference, stroke or carotid atherosclerosis, and physical therapy or exercise. Population studies, intervention studies, mechanistic studies, and systematic reviews/meta-analyses reporting neck circumference, buffalo hump, carotid imaging, or stroke/cardiovascular endpoints were included. Case reports alone, narrative reviews without quantitative outcomes, and duplicate publications were excluded. After deduplication, title/abstract screening, and full-text assessment, 42 articles were included. As a narrative review, screening was performed by a single author without independent dual screening; selection bias cannot be excluded, and exhaustive retrieval according to systematic review standards is not claimed.

Results:

Buffalo hump is morphologically heterogeneous and frequently co-occurs with obesity and metabolic disorders. Increased neck circumference is associated with ischemic stroke and its subclinical precursor, independently of overall obesity. In a cohort of 3,009 patients with type 2 diabetes, high neck circumference was associated with an approximately 2.3-fold higher risk of a composite cardiovascular endpoint that included stroke; this estimate was not stroke-specific. The association was relatively robust in women in some East Asian cohorts; however, a cohort using the same cutoffs reported stronger predictive performance in men, and negative results from the Jackson Heart Study and the Framingham Offspring Cohort indicate that the direction and presence of the association are not uniform across populations. Pericarotid fat density and perivascular adipose tissue attenuation show incremental predictive signals beyond plaque burden in some studies, but this incremental value has not been consistently quantified, and their quantitative relationship with neck circumference has not been established. Surgical debulking, diet, physical therapy, and exercise have preliminary evidence, but none has reported postintervention neck circumference change in relation to stroke endpoints. Forward head posture remains an untested candidate pathway.

Conclusions:

The existing evidence supports treating buffalo hump and neck circumference as surface markers of stroke risk and potential intermediate targets, but it is still insufficient to support the clinical conclusion that treating or reducing buffalo hump, or lowering neck circumference, can prevent stroke. Concurrent collection of neck circumference, buffalo hump subtype, carotid imaging parameters, obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) severity, atrial fibrillation, forward head posture parameters, and stroke endpoints, together with systematic tracking of postintervention neck circumference trajectories, may translate the current descriptive associations into testable prevention hypotheses.

title: Beyond Kidney Volume: 3D Mapping of Parenchymal, Cortical and Medullary Thickness with Disease, Anthropometry and Kidney Adiposity
authorString: Thanaj M, Basty N, Whitcher B, Niglas M, Bradford-Bell C, Srinivasan R, Li AS, Lennon R, Cule M, Tomaszewski M, Bell JD, Thomas EL.
abstractText:
Introduction:

Kidney volume is associated with renal function, but conventional whole-organ measurements may miss regional changes in kidney substructures. We used magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to test whether kidney substructure volumes and three-dimensional (3D) thickness phenotypes are associated with disease, adiposity, and incident outcomes.

Methods:

Automated abdominal MRI segmentations from 70,270 UK Biobank participants were used to quantify left and right kidney cortex, medulla, and parenchyma volumes and mesh-based thickness maps. Mass univariate regression generated statistical parametric maps linking regional thickness to anthropometric traits and disease (CKD, type-2 diabetes [T2D], hypertension). Bidirectional causal mediation analyses were performed using kidney substructure volumetric, thickness PCs and kidney adiposity. Longitudinal changes were assessed in 2,610 participants with repeat imaging. Cox proportional hazards models tested the associations between kidney volumes and principal component (PC) scores of thickness and incident CKD, T2D, hypertension, cardiovascular disease (CVD), and mortality.

Results:

CKD was associated with thinning of the parenchyma and most pronounced in the medulla (87.7% left, 72.8% right), whereas associations in the cortex were mixed. In contrast, T2D and hypertension were predominantly associated with increased thickness, most extensively in the cortex (T2D: 84.39% left, 96.35% right; hypertension: 94.8% left, 99.9% right). Age-disease interactions were associated with reduced thickness across all conditions. Smaller medulla volume and lower cortical thickness mediated the association between CKD and renal sinus fat. Kidney substructure volume was inversely associated with incident CKD across all substructures and both kidney sides (p<0.05), but positively associated with incident hypertension and mortality (p<0.05). Thickness PC scores also predicted outcomes independently of volume, with PC3 in the left cortex (HR 0.91 [0.84-0.98]), reflecting inferior pole/hilar thickness, associated with incident CKD.

Conclusions:

MRI-derived kidney substructure volumes and 3D thickness maps provide complementary, spatially-resolved markers of kidney morphology, that are mechanistically linked to renal adiposity and future disease risk.

title: Fully Automated Multi-Chamber Strain Profiling in Consecutive Patients Undergoing Transthoracic Echocardiography: Feasibility, Functional Clustering, and Prognostic Implications
authorString: Noh SA, Park J, Yoon YE, Jeon J, Jang Y, Lee S, Bak M, Choi H, Hwang I, Cho G.
abstractText:
Aims:

: Myocardial strain enables sensitive assessment of cardiac function, but its clinical application has largely focused on individual chambers or selected patient populations. We evaluated the feasibility and clinical relevance of fully automated multi-chamber strain assessment in consecutive patients undergoing routine transthoracic echocardiography (TTE). Methods and results: This retrospective study included 8,350 consecutive adults undergoing TTE. A hospital-wide artificial intelligence (AI)-based system automatically measured left ventricular (LV) global longitudinal strain (LVGLS), left atrial (LA) reservoir strain (LASr), and right ventricular (RV) free-wall strain (RVFWS). AI-derived LVGLS was available from at least one apical view in 97.1% of patients and from all three views in 94.8%; LASr and RVFWS were available in 94.1% and 94.5%, respectively, resulting in complete multi-chamber strain assessment in 90.3%. Strain measures showed modest correlations with conventional chamber-specific echocardiographic parameters and differential associations with clinical outcomes. Gaussian mixture modeling identified three distinct clusters characterized by preserved multi-chamber function, RV-dominant dysfunction, and pan-chamber dysfunction. Compared with the preserved cluster, pan-chamber dysfunction was associated with the highest risk of all-cause death or heart failure hospitalization (adjusted hazard ratio, 3.44; 95% CI, 2.43-4.88; P<0.001). Prognostic associations remained evident in patients with LV ejection fraction (LVEF) ≥50%, and cluster assignment provided incremental prognostic information beyond clinical factors, LVEF, and RV fractional area change.

Conclusions:

Fully automated multi-chamber strain assessment was feasible in a large consecutive TTE cohort. Integrating strain across cardiac chambers may provide complementary functional characterization and identify clinically relevant clusters with prognostic information beyond conventional assessment.

title: Plantar Thermography for Longitudinal Remote Monitoring of Chronic Heart Failure
authorString: Esposito ML, Xuan L, Zemp E, Zile MR, Tedford RJ, Linders D, Prins KW.
abstractText: Rural patients with heart failure (HF) have poor access to care, worse outcomes, and may benefit from at-home monitoring. We evaluated whether foot temperature measured using a thermographic floor mat was associated with invasively measured cardiac output and whether longitudinal temperature changes preceded HF events. We conducted a two-part prospective, observational single-center study using the SmartMat (Podimetrics, Somerville, MA), which acquires plantar thermograms and ambient temperature. In the acute study, patients undergoing clinically indicated right heart catheterization completed 4 scans on the same day. In the chronic study, patients with a HF hospitalization in the past year and New York Heart Association Class II-III symptoms were instructed to use the device and a scale daily for 6 months. A HF event was defined as receiving at least one dose of intravenous or subcutaneous diuretic. Thirty patients were enrolled in the acute study. Mean right hallux temperature positively correlated with thermodilution cardiac output (r=0.63, p<0.001). 42 patients were enrolled in the chronic study. Among patients experiencing an HF event, ambient-adjusted hallux temperature declined in the 15 days immediately preceding the event compared with days 15-30 before the event. Plantar thermograms are associated with invasively measured cardiac output and may detect subclinical worsening before HF events. Foot temperature may provide complementary information regarding HF decompensation, supporting further evaluation of plantar thermography for remote HF monitoring.

title: FloTrac®-guided haemodynamic resuscitation for profound cefuroxime-induced anaphylactic shock after induction of anaesthesia for cervical spine surgery: a case report
authorString: Salleh K, Hassan WMNW.
abstractText: Background Perioperative anaphylaxis is a life-threatening emergency requiring rapid haemodynamic intervention. Diagnosing anaphylactic shock following anaesthesia induction is challenging, as it mimics more common intraoperative complications and occurs amidst simultaneous exposure to multiple potential triggers. This report details the presentation of this critical condition and highlights how advanced functional haemodynamic monitoring via the FloTrac® system can reveal the exact real-time physiological severity of distributive shock, thereby guiding highly individualised, goal-directed resuscitation. Case: A 44-year-old female with well-controlled hypertension underwent elective cervical spine surgery. Minutes after anaesthesia induction and cefuroxime administration, she hyperacutely developed severe bronchospasm, elevated peak airway pressures (40 cmH2O), cutaneous flushing, and unmeasurable non-invasive blood pressure. Despite discontinuing anaesthetics and administering salbutamol and phenylephrine, profound distributive shock persisted, with an arterial line registering a nadir of 38/23 mmHg. Following emergency stabilisation and abortion of the surgery, she was transferred to the surgical intensive care unit requiring high-dose epinephrine and norepinephrine infusions. Advanced functional haemodynamic monitoring via the FloTrac® system revealed severe capillary leak (initial stroke volume variation [SVV] of 30%). FloTrac-guided SVV successfully titrated aggressive volume expansion, while real-time systemic vascular resistance index (SVRI) and cardiac index (CI) parameters precisely guided vasopressor and inotrope titration to resolve the distributive shock and normalise systemic vascular resistance. By post-admission day 3, metabolic acidosis and lactatemia cleared, vasopressors were discontinued, and the patient was successfully extubated. Subsequent intradermal allergy testing confirmed a definitive, selective hypersensitivity to cefuroxime. Conclusion The diagnostic complexity of post-induction anaphylaxis often delays targeted treatment amidst multiple drug exposures. However, utilising real-time functional haemodynamic monitoring using the FloTrac® system provides the immediate physiological precision required during severe distributive shock. Continuous tracking of SVV, SVRI, and CI directly guides successful, goal-directed fluid and vasopressor titration to optimise patient outcomes in life-threatening perioperative emergencies.

title: Real-World Cardiovascular Disease Awareness and Educational Interventions: Their Impact on Medical Student Confidence in Recognizing Cardiac Conditions
authorString: Patel R, Wallizada N, Warren S.
abstractText:
Background:

Cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide, yet medical students may have limited confidence in recognizing cardiac conditions. This study evaluated whether prior real-world cardiovascular exposure, a brief educational intervention, and completion of a cardiology block were associated with medical students’ confidence and cardiovascular knowledge. Methods A longitudinal survey-based study was conducted among second-year osteopathic medical students at a college of osteopathic medicine in the southeastern United States. Sixty-five students completed a pre-survey before the cardiology block. Thirty-four participants received a brief cardiovascular educational module, while 31 completed a control survey without the module. Fifty-one participants completed a common post-survey following the cardiology block. Confidence was measured using 5-point Likert-scale items, and cardiovascular knowledge was assessed using multiple-choice and case-based questions. Relationships between prior cardiovascular exposure, confidence, and knowledge were also evaluated. Results Before the cardiology block, students receiving the educational module reported higher confidence across measured domains than controls, with differences of approximately 0.6–0.7 points and large effect sizes. Students with prior clinical cardiovascular exposure also demonstrated higher baseline confidence than students with family or media exposure alone. Following completion of the cardiology block, both groups demonstrated high confidence across domains, and most between-group differences were no longer statistically significant. Confidence was not consistently associated with knowledge accuracy. Conclusions Brief educational interventions and prior clinical exposure may improve early cardiovascular confidence; however, comprehensive longitudinal cardiology instruction appears to have a greater influence on sustained confidence. These findings also demonstrate the importance of evaluating objective knowledge alongside self-reported confidence.

title: hvantk: an agentic multi-omics framework for variant annotation and analysis
authorString: Audain E, Perez-Riverol Y, Hitz M.
abstractText: Large-scale genetic variant analysis involves multiple computational steps, data formats, gene and variant annotation sources and compute requirements. Some of the steps like joint calling for large cohorts are run on large compute clusters, while gene/variant classification algorithms can be run in a desktop computer. At the same time, variant annotations such as gene expression and gene constraints metrics from gnomAD are provided in different formats, by resources that frequently change their versions. Here, we present  hvantk , a framework that provides a common data model for large-scale annotation and analysis of genetic variants, by extending popular data formats such as Hail MatrixTable and AnnData. hvantk agentically integrates 21 public multi-omic data providers as plugins that a developer, bioinformatician or an AI agent can author without modifying the framework’s core, drives analysis workflows using agent skills, and scales from single desktop computers to high-performance computing clusters. We used hvantk for reanalysing three case-control cohorts, comprising congenital heart disease (CHD), developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (Epi25) and schizophrenia (SCHEMA). Re-ranking of gene-based burden testing results using multi-omic annotations improved the recovery of curated disease genes from 26% to 49% in CHD, 40% to 48% in Epi25 and 51% to 54% in SCHEMA, among the top decile re-ranked genes. Expression at bulk and single-cell levels were the features contributing the most over a baseline of burden, gene constraint and publication count.

title: MiR-208b-3p is an upstream regulator of redox-associated cardiomyocyte survival
authorString: Hossain MB, Siga H, ElBeck Z.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiac stress induces MYH6 -to- MYH7 remodeling and activates redox-defense programs, but the regulatory mechanisms that distinguish adaptive from maladaptive stress responses remain incompletely defined. We investigated the role of miR-208b-3p, an intronic MYH7 microRNA, in cardiac stress adaptation.

Methods and Results

We integrated myocardial transcriptomic and small RNA sequencing from stress-adapted Mlp −/− mice and human cardiomyopathy to identify stress-adaptive programs associated with preserved myocardial viability and complemented these analyses with in vivo miR-208b-3p inhibition and cellular gain-of-function experiments. Mlp −/− hearts exhibited marked Myh7 induction accompanied by an ≈20-fold increase in miR-208b-3p, whereas this coordinated response was blunted in human end-stage dilated and ischemic cardiomyopathies. In vivo inhibition of miR-208b-3p selectively reduced Myh7 , without altering Myh6 or baseline cardiac function. This reduction in Myh7 occurred without induction of established Myh7 transcriptional repressors, and miR-208b-3p gain-of-function similarly reduced MYH7 while suppressing several canonical repressors, indicating that its relationship with MYH7 extends beyond the established repressor pathway. miR-208b-3p inhibition activated oxidative stress, NRF2, autophagy, and cell-survival pathways. Oxidative stress transiently suppressed miR-208b-3p, with rebound induction after stress removal, whereas antioxidant treatment increased its expression. Pharmacological NRF2 activation did not alter miR-208b-3p, whereas miR-208b-3p gain-of-function reduced oxidative stress-associated apoptotic signaling and suppressed ATM, a predicted target and regulator of cellular stress responses, supporting an upstream role for miR-208b-3p in stress adaptation.

Conclusions

MiR-208b-3p is a dynamic component of cardiac stress adaptation that links myosin remodeling with redox and survival responses. Its regulation of ATM and association with NRF2-related stress responses support an upstream role in coordinating cellular adaptation to cardiac stress.

title: Cardiac MRI at 3.0T in the presence of implantable cardioverter defibrillators (ICDs)
authorString: Reiter T, Weber OM, Weiss i, Kraus N, Kress S, Bauer WR.
abstractText: Patients with implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) often are excluded from receiving CMR scans at 3.0T due to ICD-induced image artifacts. This work aims to transfer sequence protocols established for CMR imaging in the presence of ICDs at 1.5T to a first human application at 3.0T. All measurements were performed on a clinical 3T MRI scanner. Phantom measurements were used to establish and optimize wideband PSIR LGE imaging at 3.0T. Volunteer measurements with externally placed ICDs were used for optimization of CINE imaging and wideband PSIR imaging. Thirdly, patients with implanted ICD were examined with the optimized protocols. Human measurements showed that SA stacks obtained with spoiled GRE after contrast agent showed a markedly lower artifact burden than the conventional approach. For scar imaging, a wideband PSIR with a bandwidth of 3kHz and a frequency offset of +750Hz allowed a sufficient suppression of relevant artifacts in the majority of scans. No strong correlation between the image quality and the distance between the cardiac silhouette and the device was detected. The presented work shows the feasibility of clinical cardiac MRI at 3.0T including GRE-CINE and wideband PSIR-LGE for patients with ICDs.

title: Association Between Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio and Cardiac Sympathetic Denervation in Parkinson's Disease
authorString: Takahashi M, Yoshino K, Nozaki R, Yamaguchi T, Taguchi K, Suzuki Y, Takahashi K, Takahashi K, Iwaoka K, Maeda T.
abstractText:
Background:

Peripheral inflammation has been implicated in the pathophysiology of Parkinson's disease (PD), but its relationship with autonomic dysfunction remains unclear.

Objectives:

To explore the association between peripheral inflammation, assessed by the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and autonomic function in patients with PD.

Methods:

We retrospectively analyzed 97 patients with PD who underwent 123I-metaiodobenzylguanidine (MIBG) cardiac scintigraphy and differential blood cell counts. Associations of NLR with early and delayed heart-to-mediastinum (H/M) ratios, washout ratio, and the coefficient of variation of R-R intervals (CVRR) were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation and multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, sex, and disease duration.

Results:

No significant univariable correlations were observed between NLR and the autonomic measures. In multivariable analysis, higher NLR was associated with a lower early H/M ratio (B = −0.802, 95% CI −1.598 to −0.005, P = 0.049), whereas no significant associations were observed with the delayed H/M ratio, washout ratio, or CVRR. Sensitivity analyses showed a generally consistent direction of association, although the effect estimate was attenuated after exclusion of two influential observations and statistical significance was not consistently retained.

Conclusions:

Higher NLR was associated with lower early cardiac MIBG uptake after adjustment for age, sex, and disease duration in patients with PD. This exploratory finding raises the possibility of an association between systemic inflammation and sympathetic dysfunction in PD and requires confirmation in larger prospective studies.

title: Reporting of Pericardial Adverse Events with Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: A Disproportionality Analysis of the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System
authorString: Balakrishna K, Bhatt V, Hammond A, Bawoke MM, Fradley MG, Zlotoff DA, Neilan TG.
abstractText:
Background

Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) can cause immune-related adverse events in almost any organ. While myocarditis has received the most attention, data on pericardial disease with ICI use are limited. We examined pericardial adverse event reporting with nine ICIs using the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS).

Methods

We combined legacy AERS and current FAERS quarterly files from January 2011 to June 2026 into 18,629,240 unique cases, deduplicated by case number, and removed cases the FDA had listed as deleted. ICI exposure was identified from generic names, brand names, development code names and the active-ingredient field. Pericardial events were defined by seven MedDRA preferred terms. We estimated reporting odds ratios (ROR), proportional reporting ratios (PRR), Bayesian information components (IC) and empirical Bayes geometric means (EBGM). We also examined myocarditis co-reporting, time trends, a comparison with other antineoplastic agents, a MedDRA query-based outcome, and 14 alternative definitions.

Results

The analysis included 18,514,045 cases: 277,434 involved an ICI, 34,792 carried a pericardial term, and 1,680 had both. Pericardial events were reported disproportionately with ICIs (ROR 3.35 (95% CI 3.19 to 3.52); PRR 3.34; IC025 1.62). Eight of nine agents had a ROR above 1 (3.32 to 5.63). Among the most frequently reported terms, estimates were highest for cardiac tamponade (5.59 (95% CI 4.98 to 6.28)), followed by pericardial effusion (3.83 (95% CI 3.60 to 4.07)) and pericarditis (2.09 (95% CI 1.89 to 2.31)). After removing cases that also reported myocarditis, the ROR was 3.13 (95% CI 2.98 to 3.30). Most sensitivity analyses gave similar estimates (ROR 3.13 to 3.47); defining exposure by generic drug names alone, which identified only 44% of exposed cases, gave 3.99. Compared with cases naming other L01 antineoplastic agents, the ROR was 1.13 (95% CI 1.08 to 1.19): 1.28 (95% CI 1.20 to 1.36) for ICI-only cases and 0.96 (95% CI 0.89 to 1.04) when another antineoplastic was also named. The ICI-specific reporting odds ratio fell each quarter (odds ratio 0.977 per quarter, 95% CI 0.973 to 0.980).

Conclusions

In FAERS, pericardial events were reported more often with ICIs than with other drugs across most agents and terms; however, incidence and causation cannot be determined. The excess over other antineoplastic agents was small, and reporting disproportionality declined over time. These findings support clinical awareness of pericardial disease in patients receiving ICIs and warrant study in data that can measure incidence.

title: Exploratory molecular-dynamics comparison of wild-type, N97S, and I52V calmodulin–CaV1.2 IQ-domain complexes
authorString: Khandekar S.
abstractText: Background: Calmodulin (CaM) binds the IQ motif in the C-terminal region of the cardiac L-type calcium channel CaV1.2 and contributes to calcium-dependent channel regulation. The structural consequences of CALM1 missense variants can be explored by molecular dynamics (MD), although trajectory descriptors alone cannot establish clinical pathogenicity or binding affinity. Methods: The CaM–CaV1.2 IQ-domain crystal structure (PDB 2F3Y) was used to prepare wild-type, N97S (current reference nomenclature p.Asn98Ser), and I52V (p.Ile53Val) models. One 100-ns GROMACS trajectory was analysed for each model using the AMBER99SB-ILDN force field, a TIP3P water model, a nominal 0.15 M NaCl concentration, and a stated 310 K simulation temperature. Analyses included backbone root-mean-square deviation (RMSD), Cα root-mean-square fluctuation (RMSF), solvent-accessible surface area (SASA), an SASA-derived buried-area term (ΔSASA), radius of gyration (Rg), and inter-chain polar heavy-atom proximity counts. Results: Mean overall-complex RMSD values were 0.250, 0.211, and 0.238 nm for wild type, N97S, and I52V, respectively. Mean Rg values were closely grouped (1.593, 1.603, and 1.603 nm). Mean ΔSASA was 29.60, 28.69, and 28.99 nm², while mean Cα RMSF across residues was 0.146, 0.110, and 0.127 nm. The mean distance-based polar-pair count was lower in N97S (13.98) than wild type (17.09), but the method does not validate hydrogen-bond geometry and depends on fixed atom-index selections. Conclusions: The sampled trajectories show modest differences in global deviation, residue fluctuation, interface-associated SASA, and distance-based contacts, while average complex compactness is similar. Because each condition is represented by a single trajectory, the statistics are descriptive rather than inferential. Metal-ion handling and atom-selection provenance also require verification. The findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish changes in calcium affinity, channel function, binding free energy, or clinical classification.

title: Cardiovascular Risk Burden Assessed by China-PAR Score and Its Link to Cognitive Performance in Older Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study
authorString: Qi Y, Zhang W, Gao S, Chen H, Huo X, Zhou S, Yuan J, Ma F.
abstractText: Background Cardiovascular risk burden has been linked to cognitive impairment, yet evidence on the association between cardiovascular risk estimated using models developed specifically for the Chinese population and multidomain cognitive performance remains limited. This study examined the association between the China-PAR score and cognitive function in community-dwelling older adults. Methods Using cluster random sampling, 733 adults aged below 85 years from Tianjin, China, were included in this cross-sectional study. Ten-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk was estimated using the China-PAR model. Cognitive function was assessed using the Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale–Revised in China (WAIS-RC), including FIQ, VIQ, PIQ, and 11 subtests. Multiple linear regression models evaluated associations between the China-PAR score and cognitive performance, adjusting for years of education, body mass index, and APOE ε 4 carrier status. Results Higher China-PAR scores were consistently associated with lower FIQ, VIQ, and PIQ. In the fully adjusted model, the higher China-PAR score was associated with lower FIQ, VIQ, and PIQ: FIQ, − 0.153 (− 0.226 to − 0.081), p  < 0.001; VIQ, − 0.110 (− 0.174 to − 0.047), p  = 0.001; PIQ, − 0.185 (− 0.270 to − 0.099), p  < 0.001. Significant negative associations were also observed for Information, Comprehension, Arithmetic, Vocabulary, Digit Symbol, Picture Completion, Block Design, Picture Arrangement, and Object Assembly, but not for Similarities or Digit Span. Conclusions Higher China-PAR scores were associated with lower global and domain-specific cognitive performance in community-dwelling older adults. Prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings, establish causality, and clarify the underlying biological mechanisms and pathways.

title: Alagille Syndrome: A Comprehensive Review of Clinical Heterogeneity, Genetic Mechanisms, and Evolving Therapeutic Strategies
authorString: Khamar F, Shah D, Kanani M, Patel K, Khandai B.
abstractText: Alagille Syndrome is a rare, autosomal dominant, multisystem disorder, mainly associated with mutations in the JAG1 gene and, to a lesser extent, NOTCH2. It is associated with bile duct paucity and a spectrum of cholestasis, congenital heart defects (especially peripheral pulmonary stenosis), skeletal defects, ocular defects (posterior embryotoxon), renal defects, and characteristic facial features. Clinical presentation is highly variable, even within the same family carrying identical genetic mutations, which complicates diagnosis and treatment. Progress in molecular genetics, particularly regarding the Notch signalling pathway, has enhanced diagnostic accuracy and clarified disease pathogenesis. Hepatic manifestations, usually presenting in infancy, may progress to end-stage liver disease requiring transplantation. Cardiac and vascular anomalies are significant contributors to poor survival and represent a special management concern. A common and complex presentation includes neuropsychological delay, growth failure, and nutritional deficiencies, all of which require management by a multidisciplinary team. In atypical or mild cases, genetic testing has emerged as an important diagnostic tool. Management focuses on symptom control, nutritional support, and organ-specific interventions, and new drugs targeting bile acid metabolism and the Notch pathway show promise. This review provides a thorough overview of Alagille Syndrome, highlighting its clinical heterogeneity, underlying genetic mechanisms, diagnostic dilemmas, and evolving therapeutic approaches.

title: Human Plasma Causal Immunome-Phenome Mapping Reveals Cardiovascular Enrichment and Therapeutic Target Opportunities
authorString: Taslima S, Zhang J, Tan H, Liu Y, Ahmad D, Young M, Verma S, Xie M, Zhao J, Wang Y.
abstractText: Background Circulating immune proteins represent an important class of therapeutic targets, but existing proteome-wide genetic studies have not systematically resolved immune-related target–disease relationships across a broad disease phenome within a unified framework that integrates causal inference, locus colocalization, orthogonal protein-level support, independent replication, and standardized evidence grading. Methods We developed the Human Plasma Immune Atlas (HPIA), a tiered proteogenomic framework built from public datasets. We curated 1,007 plasma immune proteins from 2,923 Olink Explore analytes, instrumented each encoding gene with its strongest blood cis-expression quantitative trait locus (eQTLGen), and tested effects on 2,469 FinnGen R12 disease endpoints by Mendelian randomization (MR), followed by colocalization, protein-level validation with INTERVAL cis-protein quantitative trait loci, 2-population replication in UK Biobank, and prespecified 5-tier evidence grading. A companion Plasma Immune Risk Score (PIRS; elastic-net Cox) is released for predicting targets. Results Across 1,656,872 evaluable gene–disease tests, 1,016 associations involving 220 immune genes and 381 diseases met FDR < 0.05, of which 417 showed strong evidence of colocalization (PP.H4 ≥ 0.80). Positive-control analyses recapitulated five established immune drug-target relationships and the ACE–hypertension relationship with directionally concordant genetic effects. Among 189 discovery associations evaluable in UK Biobank, 162 (86%) showed concordant effect directions and 89 met the prespecified replication criterion. Cardiovascular phenotypes contained the largest number of high-confidence associations, accounting for 67 of 176 core target–disease pairs, while hypertension was associated with 28 immune proteins. Integration of MR, colocalization, protein-level evidence, and replication promoted five target–disease pairs to the highest evidence tier, including ANXA2-hypertension and PPP3R1-venous/lymphatic disease. Systematic prioritization further identified 45 colocalized candidate therapeutic target–indication pairs with genetically inferred directions of intervention. In validation evaluation, the PIRS achieved a cross-validated concordance index of 0.777. Conclusions HPIA provides an open, genetics-anchored map connecting the circulating immune system to the human disease phenome and distinguishes initial genetic associations from target–disease relationships supported by orthogonal evidence. The framework identifies cardiovascular phenotypes as a major concentration of genetically supported immune associations and provides experimentally testable hypotheses for therapeutic target discovery, drug repurposing, and immune-informed disease stratification.

title: Accelerating Machine Learning in Health Care by Addressing the Labeling Bottleneck: Development and Evaluation Study
authorString: Vecile S, Dixon W, Assadi A, Kim M, Greer R, Siddiqui A, Ehrmann D, Goodwin A, Eytan D, Mazwi M, Bulic A, Goodfellow SD.
abstractText: Background: Timely detection of postoperative arrhythmias after pediatric cardiac surgery is essential for preventing hemodynamic compromise, yet machine learning models are constrained by the scarcity of labelled datasets reflecting real-world monitoring. Existing approaches rely on adult 12-lead electrocardiograms, which are rarely used continuously in pediatric intensive care units (ICUs) and fail to capture age-dependent waveform variability. Rare arrhythmias such as junctional ectopic tachycardia are especially difficult to find and label within large continuous monitoring streams. Objective: We evaluated how efficiently a staged, self-bootstrapping labeling pipeline surfaces a rare arrhythmia class relative to naive random review of an unlabelled dataset, and how that efficiency evolves across the pipeline's dependent stages. Methods: Leveraging a repository of over 1.6 million hours of unlabelled continuous lead II electrocardiogram (ECG) from more than 9,000 pediatric patients, we implemented four sequential sourcing stages, each enabling the next: retrospective MUSE (GE Healthcare Inc.) studies and real-time ICU observations produced an expert-labelled seed set, which trained a preliminary classifier that then guided two active-learning stages, uncertainty sampling and embedding-based retrieval. All labels were assigned by clinical experts; the classifier was used only to prioritize which segments they reviewed. To benchmark the pipeline, we labelled 200 randomly drawn segments and compared junctional yield using the Fisher exact test. Results: Random sampling yielded junctional arrhythmia in only 2 of 200 segments (1.0%). The full pipeline produced a dataset that was 15.3% junctional by labelled hours and 24.7% by patient, a roughly 15-fold and 25-fold enrichment over random sampling, respectively (Fisher exact test, P<.001). Yield rose at each successive stage, from 7.6% of labelled hours (MUSE) to 35.7% (embedding retrieval), reflecting efficiency compounding as the pipeline matured. Of segments retrieved from the junctional embedding region, 60.2% were confirmed junctional once labelled. The final dataset comprised 181.2 hours of expert-labelled ECG from 1,447 unique patients. Conclusions: A staged pipeline that bootstraps model-guided sampling from a small expert-labelled seed set enriches a rare arrhythmia class roughly 15-fold over random review, directing scarce clinician effort toward informative segments. We make no claim about the guiding model's diagnostic performance, which will be reported separately. This methodology is broadly applicable to clinical domains where expert annotation is limited and rare events dominate.

title: Characterization of pharmacological inhibition of the hERG potassium channel by nitazene opioids
authorString: Chowdhury MR, Baque M, Osborne T, Cheng H, Hannington O, Zhang Y, Harchi AE, Copeland C, Corey RA, Harmer SC, Hancox J.
abstractText: Nitazene opioids are ‘street’ drugs, many of which are substantially more potent than heroin. They are linked to respiratory depression, but other adverse effects have not been widely investigated. Machine learning models have predicted that several nitazenes may interact with a major drug anti-target, the hERG cardiac potassium channel. This study was conducted to evaluate effects on hERG of isotonitazene, protonitazene, etonitazene, metonitazene and the related piperadine benzimidazoline brorphine. hERG-expressing HEK293 cells were studied using automated patch clamp. Using a standard + 20 mV command (WT) hERG tail current (I hERG ) was acutely inhibited by all 5 compounds with IC 50 values between 0.5 µM (protonitazene) and 1.32 µM (isotonitazene). Inhibition showed voltage- and time-dependence consistent with gating-dependent block. The IC 50 values for I hERG inhibition for inactivation-attenuated (N588K) hERG were 3.3–5.1 fold those for WT for protonitazene and isotonitazene. Mutations at S5 and S6 aromatic residues (F557, Y652, F656) affected both compounds, with a particularly marked influence of F656A (13-fold WT IC 50 for isotonitazene and 73-fold for protonitazene). Neither isotonitazene nor protonitazene impaired hERG channel trafficking to the surface membrane. In silico docking and molecular dynamics simulations reproduced binding to canonical binding residues. Combining fentanyl with isotonitazene or protonitazene exacerbated block compared to each compound alone. Hypokalemia (1 mM [K + ] o ) increased the potency of isotonitazene but not protonitazene. In conclusion, hERG is a direct target for nitazene opioids.

title: Connected but Unequal: Cardiovascular Risk Burden and Digital Health Engagement Among US Adults
authorString: Hinneh T, Ogungbe O, Adegboyega A, Falls CD, White BM.
abstractText: Adults with multiple cardiovascular risk factors may have greater need for digital tools that support prevention of chronic diseases; however, the use and patterns of engagement remain unclear. Using data from the nationally representative Health Information National Trends Survey cycles (2019, 2020, 2022, and 2024) we examined associations between cardiovascular risk-factor burden and digital health engagement among US adults. Five cardiovascular risk factors (hypertension, diabetes, smoking, physical inactivity, and overweight or obesity) were summed and classified as low (0–1), moderate (2–3), or high (4–5) burden. Digital health engagement included online health information seeking, provider messaging, test-result access, appointment scheduling, and wearable-device use (score, 0–5). Multivariable regression models were used to examine associations between cardiovascular risk-factor burden and digital health engagement. Among 16,861 adults, weighted mean (SE) age was 47.2 (0.18) years; 49.5% were male and 63.6% were non-Hispanic White. Risk-factor burden was low in 38.8%, moderate in 51.4%, and high in 9.9%. Adjusted mean engagement scores differed by burden (low, 2.81; moderate, 2.92; high, 2.96; P = .03). Compared with low burden, moderate burden was associated with higher odds of provider messaging (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 1.20; 95% CI, 1.07–1.35) and online test-result access (AOR, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.11–1.53). High burden was associated with test-result access (AOR, 1.50; 95% CI, 1.21–1.85) and wearable use (AOR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.16–1.78). Greater cardiovascular risk-factor burden was associated with modestly higher digital health engagement, particularly for test-result access, provider messaging, and wearable use.

title: Genetic Analysis of Polar Metabolites Identifies Genetic Control of Betaine in White Flour of Wheat
authorString: Richard RR, Lovegrove A, Wingen LU, Ward J, Tosi P, Griffiths S, Shewry PR.
abstractText: White wheat flour contains a range of polar metabolites, including amino acids, organic acids, sugars (mono-, di- and tri-saccharides) and methyl donors (choline and betaine), which may contribute to a healthy diet. We have used 1H NMR to quantify the concentrations of 28 polar metabolites in the white flour of a double haploid population of the cross Malacca x Hereward comprised of 106 lines grown in field trials in 2020 and 2021 and a sub-set of 76 lines grown in 2005. This identified a total of 106 QTL for individual or groups of metabolites of which three were present in two of the three datasets. These “stable” QTLs include two for betaine, QBet-4D.1 and QBet-5B.1, explaining 14-31% and 21-24% of the variation, respectively, and one for succinate, QScc-7B.1, explaining 16-18% of the variation, with average additive effects of + 0.09(M), +0.03(M), and +0.06 (H) mg. g-1 of flour. Betaine has established health benefits in humans by remethylating homocysteine, which is a risk factor for cardiovascular disease. The availability of markers from our study will therefore allow the selection of new types of wheat with higher betaine in white flour.

title: Various Subtypes of Endometriosis and Cardiovascular Disease: Emerging Molecular Links and Clinical Implications: A Narrative Review
authorString: Kong L, Zhang S, Ding Y, Sun X, Wang R, Liu L, Zhang W, Xia H.
abstractText: Endometriosis is associated with increased cardiovascular risk, but how its subtype heterogeneity informs this association remains unclear. This narrative review examines the biological characteristics of superficial peritoneal endometriosis (SUP), ovarian endometrioma (OMA), and deep infiltrating endometriosis (DIE) and their potential cardiovascular relevance. English-language literature identified through PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, and reference screening was synthesized across susceptibility factors, molecular and vascular alterations, and treatment exposures. Subtype-related findings highlight differences in anatomical location and tissue microenvironment, including peritoneal immune interactions in superficial lesions, intracystic iron accumulation and oxidative injury in OMA, and inflammatory and fibromuscular remodeling in deep lesions. These features provide a basis for investigating how lesion heterogeneity may relate to systemic lipid dysregulation, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and coagulation abnormalities. Ovarian function, surgical history, and hormonal regimens further inform interpretation of these relationships. By integrating phenotype and treatment exposure while distinguishing local findings from circulating biomarkers, vascular measurements, and clinical events, this review identifies evidence gaps linking biological heterogeneity to cardiovascular outcomes. Emerging subtype-related evidence supports further investigation but does not establish differences in cardiovascular event risk among SUP, OMA, and DIE. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether incorporating endometriosis subtype improves cardiovascular risk assessment beyond conventional factors. (Figure 1)

title: Mechanism-Based Discovery of New TRIDs Targeting Ribosome Pockets
authorString: Asuma J, Wang H, Bhat SY, Zhu H, Li H, Jabak AA, Chenoweth DM, Cooperman BS.
abstractText: Approximately 10% of all human pathogenic mutations are nonsense mutations which give rise to premature termination codon (PTC) diseases, leading to an estimated 35 million people worldwide who harbor such mutations. To date, no approaches leading to medical treatments which increase PTC readthrough have received FDA approval. However, one well-tolerated translation readthrough inducing drug (TRID), ataluren, was conditionally approved for 11 years by the European Medicines Agency for treatment of nonsense mutation Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy. In recent work we have shown that ataluren increases readthrough indirectly, by exclusively inhibiting termination without directly affecting readthrough by suppressor aminoacyl-tRNAs (sup-aa-tRNAs). Based on the idea that this mode of action (MoA) might be the reason for the low toxicity of ataluren, we have discovered potential new TRIDs, which target pockets within the ribosome to which the termination factor eRF1 binds but sup-aa-tRNAs do not. These new TRIDs, dipeptide derivatives of eRF1 and some Sartans, mimic the MoA of ataluren. Three Sartans, which are angiotensin II receptor blockers and FDA-approved for treatment of hypertension, are significantly more potent than ataluren in our reconstituted in vitro readthrough assay. These compounds might be more effective than ataluren in treating some PTC diseases. We anticipate that further development of these lead compounds will lead to more general effectiveness, used both alone and in combination with other classes of readthrough inducers.

title: Blocking NEDD4L-Mediated ACE2 Ubiquitination at Lysine 788 Alleviates Hypoxia- Induced Pulmonary Hypertension: A Mechanistic Study
authorString: Wang R, Wang R, Liu T, Chen Q, Wang Z.
abstractText: Background We previously showed that neural precursor cell-expressed developmentally down-regulated gene 4-like (NEDD4L), an E3 ubiquitin ligase, drives pulmonary hypertension by promoting the ubiquitination and subsequent degradation of angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2). Whether this regulation occurs at a specific residue, and whether targeting that residue is therapeutically useful, had not been determined. Methods Based on bioinformatic prediction combined with previously validated ubiquitin-acceptor lysines in the intracellular C-terminal tail of ACE2, we substituted lysine 788 with arginine to generate the K788R ACE2 mutant. Co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) in pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs) was used to examine the interaction of NEDD4L with wild-type or K788R ACE2. For in vivo experiments, ACE2-knockout rats were given adeno-associated virus (AAV) carrying either wild-type or K788R ACE2, followed by 4 weeks of chronic hypoxia (10% O₂). Echocardiography, blood-gas analysis, histology, TUNEL staining, quantitative PCR, and Western blotting were performed to evaluate pulmonary artery pressure, oxygenation, pulmonary vascular remodeling, apoptosis, and gene and protein expression. Results Under both normoxic and hypoxic conditions, the K788R mutation greatly weakened the NEDD4L–ACE2 association in PASMCs and in rat lung tissue, although wild-type and mutant ACE2 were expressed at comparable levels. Relative to ACE2-knockout rats reconstituted with wild-type ACE2, those reconstituted with K788R ACE2 showed markedly lower pulmonary artery pressure, less pulmonary arteriolar muscularization and medial wall thickening, a higher oxygenation index, and reduced hypoxia-induced apoptosis in lung tissue. Conclusion These findings establish K788, a validated ubiquitin-acceptor lysine in the intracellular tail of ACE2, as an essential residue for the NEDD4L–ACE2 interaction, and they show that selectively blocking ACE2 ubiquitination at this single site alleviates hypoxia-induced pulmonary hypertension in rats. Intervention at the NEDD4L–ACE2 axis through K788 may thus offer a precision therapeutic approach that stabilizes ACE2 while sparing global NEDD4L function.

title: Left Ventricular Diastolic Intraventricular Pressure Differences and Propagation Velocity with 4D-Flow MRI in Patients with Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
authorString: Stipechi LV, Craiem D, Gencer U, Casciaro ME, Hulot J, Hagege A, Soulat G, Mousseaux E.
abstractText:
Background

Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) remains the gold standard for assessing left ventricular (LV) diastolic dysfunction (DD), but noninvasive alternatives are needed to overcome geometric and acoustic limitations. 4D-Flow MRI enables comprehensive assessment of intraventricular pressure differences (IVPDs) and flow propagation velocity (VP). We aimed to evaluate 4D-Flow-derived IVPDs and VP in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM).

Methods

Thirty-eight HCM patients and 38 age- and sex-matched healthy controls underwent TTE and 4D-Flow MRI. Spatiotemporal maps of velocity and IVPDs, decomposed into inertial and convective components, were derived along the main inflow streamline from the mitral valve to the apex. Peak early filling rate (PEFR) was used to normalize IVPDs and VP.

Results

While absolute peak flow rates were comparable, HCM patients exhibited significantly faster VP (100.4 vs. 60.2 cm/s, p < 0.01) and higher positive early E IVPD (1.40 vs. 0.92 mmHg, p < 0.01) compared to controls. Normalizing IVPDs by PEFR amplified group differences, revealing a markedly increased flow-normalized E-IVPD (5.13 vs. 2.94 × 10⁻³ mmHg·ml⁻¹·s, p < 0.001) and deeper reverse ER IVPD (-6.06 vs. -4.61 × 10⁻³ mmHg·ml⁻¹·s, p < 0.01) in HCM. These differences were primarily driven by the inertial components. Multivariable analysis demonstrated that ER IVPD is independently determined by PEFR and the TTE E/E’ ratio (r = 0.65, p < 0.001).

Conclusions

4D-Flow MRI-derived, flow-normalized IVPDs and propagation velocity provide robust, noninvasive markers of altered LV chamber stiffness and impaired diastolic filling in HCM, offering deeper 3D hemodynamic insights into diastolic dysfunction.

title: Computational Identification of Secreted Molecular Candidates for Perivascular Hydrogel Delivery in Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm
authorString: Cheng H.
abstractText:
Background:

Perivascular hydrogel wrapping combines circumferential mechanical reinforcement with sustained local release of therapeutic payloads and is an emerging preclinical strategy for abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). Because no hydrogel-intervention transcriptome is publicly available, the molecular payloads best suited to extra-adventitial delivery remain undefined. This study used human AAA transcriptomes to prioritize secreted molecules that could be loaded into a perivascular hydrogel. Methods. Differential expression was performed with limma on human AAA datasets (GSE57691, with small and large AAA; GSE7084, AAA wall; GSE47472, AAA neck), and the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were intersected with the Human Protein Atlas predicted secreted-protein set (1,902 genes). Candidates were examined by Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment, STRING protein-protein interaction, single-sample gene-set enrichment analysis with immune correlations, single-cell localization (GSE166676), and cross-species comparison with mouse AAA (GSE12591). Results. The AAA molecular program was already established in small AAA, with no significant additional transcriptomic change between small and large lesions. Intersecting the DEGs with the secretome yielded 82 candidate secreted proteins (16 up-regulated and 66 down-regulated in small AAA). Up-regulated drivers (IL1B, IL6, TNF, CCL3L1, CXCL1, CXCL5) correlated with M1 macrophages, NLRP3, and MMP9, whereas down-regulated protective factors (FRZB, TIMP4, SPARCL1, SMOC2, IGFBP5, GPX3) localized to vascular smooth muscle cells and fibroblasts. NELL2 was the only novel secreted protein robustly up-regulated across datasets. Cross-species agreement with the angiotensin II mouse model was poor. Conclusions. This computational study identifies a tiered list of secreted molecules potentially suitable for perivascular hydrogel-cell delivery against AAA: inflammatory drivers to antagonize, lost protective factors to replenish, and novel targets such as NELL2 to validate. The mechanical supportive effect of hydrogels cannot be assessed by transcriptomics, and the candidates require biomaterial, animal, and safety experiments.
