title: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction: From Mechanisms to Winning Team of Management
authorString: Sisakian H.
abstractText: Heart failure is a global public health and clinical problem affecting 1-2% of the adult population and course with high mortality despite of significant advances in disease modifying in past few decades. Heart failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) is a progressive clinical state with presence of typical symptoms of heart failure and characterized by high mortality with recurrent hospitalizations. In HFrEF evidence-based management strategies are available based on positive results of large clinical trials outcomes. Recent clinical investigations and consensus statements have generated increased clinical interest to the evidence based treatment strategies. These strategies include renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system inhibitors, beta-adrenergic blockers, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors. In addition, nonpharmacological approaches such as implantable cardiac defibrillators, cardiac resynchronization therapy, moderate physical activity and several other new treatment approaches have been shown to decrease mortality in selected subpopulation of patients with HFrEF. Despite of proven guideline directed medical treatment in HFrEF, significant proportion of patients remain undertreated due to not proven medication and not appropriate combination management, suboptimal dose adjustment, high comorbidity burden. In this review we discuss the proven evidence based efficacy of each pharmacologic and device therapy option in HFrEF as well as novel therapeutic strategies. On the basis of existed evidence the outcome directed effective treatment, improve of outpatient monitoring, escape of vulnerable phases of disease and target of comorbidities should be the aim of management and care on HF patients in everyday practice.

title: Effect of Sleep Hygiene on Metabolic Syndrome in an Adult Rural Population in India: Protocol for a Cross-Sectional Study.
authorString: Kothari R, Choudhari S.
abstractText:
Background

Metabolic syndrome (MetS) refers to a group of conditions including high blood pressure, excess weight, high blood glucose, and abnormal cholesterol and triglyceride levels that together substantially increase the risk of heart disease and diabetes. Poor sleep hygiene is associated with a higher likelihood of type 2 diabetes, while sleep duration can affect the development of various MetS components. Approximately 25% of adults worldwide currently have MetS, and this prevalence is projected to increase to 50% by 2035. However, there is a distinct lack of evidence about the specific impact of sleep hygiene on cardiometabolic health within the rural Indian population. This study will focus on addressing this literature gap by evaluating these risk factor associations by using validated tools to help develop targeted community interventions.

Objective

This study aims to estimate the prevalence of poor sleep quality and cardiometabolic risk factors in a rural Indian population and to determine the association between sleep hygiene and cardiometabolic risk factors.

Methods

This study will be a community-based, cross-sectional, analytical study, and data collection will be carried out by trained personnel using validated tools during house-to-house visits. In this cross-sectional study of 281 rural Indian adults aged ≥40 years, sleep quality will be assessed via the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (a score >5 indicates poor sleep), alongside direct measurements of blood pressure, fasting plasma glucose, BMI (≥25 kg/m² for obesity), waist circumference, and the Madras Diabetes Research Foundation-Indian Diabetes Risk Score for diabetes risk. Data will be collected through a door-to-door approach, with informed consent entered into Google Forms, and quality checked via training and regular reviews. Using R software, analyses will include prevalence estimates with 95% CIs; chi-square or t tests for associations between poor sleep and cardiometabolic risks; and logistic regression (P<.05) adjusted for confounders such as diet, stress, and physical activity.

Results

This study began in January 2025 with conceptualization and ethics approval obtained in June 2025. Data collection commenced in August 2025 following Clinical Trial Registry-India registration, with 53 participants enrolled as of May 5, 2026. Standardized tools (GAD-7, PHQ-9, and GPAQ) were incorporated to assess key confounding variables. Data collection is projected to finish by January 2027, with final analysis and study conclusion expected by March 2027.

Conclusions

The relationship between MetS and sleep hygiene warrants greater attention, particularly as poor sleep habits become increasingly prevalent alongside MetS. This study will deepen the understanding of their connection, paving the way for targeted interventions and prevention strategies.

Trial registration

Clinical Trial Registry-India CTRI/2025/08/092892; https://tinyurl.com/3sak2h9x.

International registered report identifier (irrid)

DERR1-10.2196/90117.

title: Real-world renoprotective effects of polyethylene glycol-loxenatide in type 2 diabetes: a multicenter, ambispective cohort study.
authorString: Ye J, Li J, Chen Y, Chen F, Zhu D, Zhang C, Chen Q, Tian Y, Yang S, Xu W, Xie B, Chen ZS, Hou K.
abstractText: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease face persistent risks despite standard care. Polyethylene glycol-loxenatide lacks real-world renoprotective evidence in high-risk Chinese populations relative to non-incretin-based standard care. This multicenter, ambispective cohort study enrolled 3305 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, renal impairment, and elevated cardiovascular risk at six Chinese tertiary institutions (median follow-up 36.4 months; trial registration: ChiCTR2300073001). Data were extracted via an artificial intelligence-enhanced pipeline. Co-primary analyzes comprised multivariable-adjusted Cox regression and 1:1 propensity score matching (332 per group); pre-specified landmark analyzes at 6 and 12 months addressed immortal time bias. Polyethylene glycol-loxenatide was associated with a reduced risk of the primary kidney composite outcome in the original cohort (hazard ratio [HR], 0.49; 95% CI, 0.25-0.95; P = 0.035), which was corroborated in the propensity score matched cohort (HR, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.20-0.97; P = 0.043) and progressive across 6-month (HR, 0.40; 95% CI, 0.19-0.84) and 12-month (HR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.14-0.75) landmarks. While a reduction in 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events was observed in the unmatched cohort (HR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.43-0.85; P = 0.004), this association was not sustained in the matched analysis (HR, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.57-1.48; P = 0.735). In conclusion, long-term therapy was associated with an attenuated risk of major renal events. Given the null findings in the matched cohort, the cardiovascular observations are exploratory and require randomized confirmation.

title: Review of the Association Between Neck Circumference and Multisystem Diseases: From an Anthropometric Indicator to a Clinical Risk Marker
authorString: Huang X.
abstractText:
Background:

Obesity is a core risk factor for multiple chronic diseases. Adipose tissue distribution has greater predictive value for metabolic and cardiovascular risk than total fat mass. Neck circumference, a simple anthropometric indicator of upper-body subcutaneous fat accumulation, has gained increasing attention in recent years for its value in metabolic and cardiovascular risk stratification.

Objective:

To systematically search for and synthesize evidence on the association between neck circumference and multisystem diseases and to evaluate the evidence base and key challenges for translating neck circumference from an anthropometric indicator into a clinical risk marker.

Methods:

This review is a systematically searched narrative review. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and CNKI were searched from database inception to June 30, 2026. A supplementary search was performed for 2026 articles published online after the search cutoff date. Systematic reviews and meta-analyses of the association between neck circumference and disease or risk factors served as the primary evidence source and were supplemented by large prospective cohort studies and key cross-sectional studies. Case reports, small-sample uncontrolled studies, purely hypothetical articles, conference abstracts, preprints, and registered trial protocols were excluded. Evidence was synthesized narratively, and effect sizes were not pooled. The review was not prospectively registered, and no formal evidence grading was performed with tools such as GRADE. Related limitations are discussed in Section 9.1.

Results:

A total of 130 articles were included. Current evidence indicates that increased neck circumference is epidemiologically associated with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), components of metabolic syndrome (MetS), dyslipidemia, obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), atrial fibrillation, heart failure, ischemic stroke, chronic kidney disease (CKD), hyperuricemia, gout, and the risk of cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality. Associations with left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH), cardiac electrical remodeling, subclinical atherosclerosis, arterial stiffness, retinal microvascular changes, decline in lung function, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), coronary heart disease, cognitive impairment, and reduced brain gray matter volume have also been reported, but the evidence is weaker, inconsistent in direction, or confined to subgroups. The prognosis of hemorrhagic stroke also requires further validation. The direction of associations for geriatric and nutritional outcomes such as sarcopenia, malnutrition, and decline in activities of daily living (ADL) is inconsistent, with some studies showing risk associated with lower neck circumference; presarcopenic obesity, in contrast, is positively associated with increased neck circumference. Evidence for associations with metabolic syndrome in children with type 1 diabetes mellitus, bone mineral density, depression, and sleep quality is weak, inconsistent in direction, or confined to specific subgroups. Some associations, such as those for T2DM and hypertension, remain significant after adjustment for body mass index (BMI), and the CKD evidence is partially supportive. Evidence strength was judged comprehensively based on study design, cross-population consistency, whether associations remained significant after adjustment for BMI or waist circumference, and the availability of Mendelian randomization (MR) evidence; overall, the evidence was heterogeneous. However, neck circumference is strongly collinear with waist circumference and BMI. Some meta-analyses have shown no significant association between neck circumference and the composite MetS endpoint. The Jackson Heart Study found no independent association between neck circumference and cardiovascular outcomes after full adjustment. MR studies have shown a protective causal association between neck circumference and metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD), contradicting observational studies; other MR studies have not found a causal association between neck circumference and bone mineral density. Wrist circumference outperforms neck circumference in predicting insulin resistance in children, and in children with type 1 diabetes mellitus, waist circumference has a higher area under the curve (AUC) than neck circumference for predicting MetS. Causality has not yet been fully established. Genetic evidence indicates that neck circumference has a genetic basis independent of overall obesity. Intervention studies suggest that neck circumference can be changed by lifestyle interventions, but its changes are not fully synchronized with improvements in neck adipose tissue or core OSA endpoints. Evidence from nontraditional cardiovascular risk markers, mechanistic studies, studies in special populations, measurement standardization studies, and evidence on local effects in head and neck cancer has further expanded the boundaries of clinical application of neck circumference. Prospective evidence in the field of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) shows that in postmenopausal women with normal BMI, baseline neck circumference still independently predicts NAFLD incidence. Studies in young Chinese adults suggest that there are significant sex differences in the performance of neck circumference for diagnosing obesity.

Conclusions:

As a systematically searched narrative review, this review suggests that neck circumference is epidemiologically associated with multisystem diseases, but the strength of evidence is heterogeneous. Current evidence supports its use as an adjunctive indicator for risk screening; however, it cannot yet serve as an independent causal risk marker. Cross-disease comparisons of effect sizes are influenced by differences in indicator type, baseline risk, and follow-up duration and should not be used as a direct basis for clinical decision-making.

title: The Clinical Efficacy of Cardiac Rehabilitation in Takotsubo Syndrome.
authorString: Tayon KG, Carlisle AE, Schneider A, Shapiro BP, Dineen EH, Cooper LT, Taylor BJ.

journal.title: Journal of cardiopulmonary rehabilitation and prevention

abstractText:
Purpose

Despite normalization of left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), symptoms and impaired exercise capacity can persist ~1 year after Takotsubo syndrome (TTS). We evaluated the impact of cardiac rehabilitation (CR) on cardiac structure and function, functional exercise capacity, and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in patients with TTS.

Methods

Patients with TTS who completed (TTS-CR, n = 33) and did not complete (TTS-CTL, n = 24) CR were retrospectively analyzed. Cardiac structure and function (via echocardiogram) were assessed at index hospitalization and follow-up (post-CR in TTS-CR; >1 month later in TTS). The 6-minute walk test distance and Dartmouth Cooperative Functional Assessment Charts quality-of-life score were assessed pre- and post-CR (TTS-CR). Major adverse cardiovascular events within 1-year post index hospitalization were recorded (all groups).

Results

The LVEF improved similarly in TTS-CR (39 ± 9% vs 60 ± 6%) and TTS (39 ± 10% vs 60 ± 7%, P = .58). The left ventricular end-diastolic volume decreased similarly in TTS-CR (125 ± 40 vs 105 ± 37 mL) and TTS-CTL (126 ± 26 vs 109 ± 27 mL, P = .81). In TTS-CR, 6-minute walk test distance (330 ± 126 vs 364 ± 97 m, P = .007) and Dartmouth Cooperative Functional Assessment Charts quality-of-life score (22 ± 6 vs 19 ± 7 m, P = .04) improved significantly from pre- to post-CR. Rates of major adverse cardiovascular events were similar between groups (P > .05).

Conclusions

Cardiac rehabilitation did not enhance cardiac structural or functional recovery but did improve functional exercise capacity and HRQoL in patients with TTS.

title: Public brain health: a framework for action to promote and safeguard brain health.
authorString: Daly T, Horstkötter D, Eyre HA, Murphy E, Gale SA, Cosgrove L, Bruno D, Cotter E, Slachevsky A, Fletcher JR, Wallace L, Wajnerman-Paz A, Manly JJ, Fuller J, Paddick SM, Manet R, Shaaban CE, Ienca M, Winkler AS, Arenaza-Urquijo E, Brayne C, Ibáñez A, Riedel-Heller S, Richard E, Walsh S, Dufouil C.
abstractText: The promotion of brain health has generally been undertaken at the level of individuals, for instance, in the quest for precision treatments for persons with, or at high risk of, neurological disorders. But the growing global burden of neurological conditions and the increasing understanding of the brain's central role in all facets of human life have spurred interest in public health approaches to the brain that emphasise population-level strategies benefitting everyone as part of a "brain health for all" vision of society. This article defines the emerging concept of public brain health as intersectoral action to establish brain health priorities, empower communities, and reduce health inequities, with the ultimate goal of improving brain health at the population level across the lifetime. We propose a framework to promote and safeguard population brain health with the following key elements: co-defining priorities with communities, balancing prevention strategies, and reducing global gaps in brain health through ambitious policy-making. Public brain health calls for collective responsibility to maximise brain health equity across the life course.

title: Mitophagy coordinates organelle crosstalk in health and diseases.
authorString: Wu M, He P, Lian Y, Zhang T, Wu Y, Wang L, Tang D, Yao Y, Yao R.
abstractText: Eukaryotic cells contain various membrane- and non-membrane-bound organelles, whose spatial and functional organization underpins intracellular homeostasis. Organelle coordination is governed by complex signaling and metabolic networks, often facilitated by direct physical contacts and molecular exchange. Mitochondria, as central hubs of bioenergetic and metabolic activity, are essential to functional coordination among cellular organelles. They engage in diverse cellular processes, encompassing ATP production, biosynthesis of key metabolites, calcium ion buffering, redox balance, and cellular turnover. To preserve their integrity and functionality, dysfunctional mitochondria undergo selective elimination via mitophagy, a specialized form of macroautophagy. Mitophagy plays dual roles in maintaining mitochondrial fidelity and actively shapes interorganelle communication. Through bidirectional signaling, mitophagy influences the activity of multiple organelles, including the endoplasmic reticulum, nucleus, lysosomes, peroxisomes, and lipid droplets. This interorganelle crosstalk is essential for adapting to metabolic stress, maintaining redox balance, and coordinating cell fate decisions. In this review, we explore the intricate signaling networks connecting mitophagy with various organelles and discuss how these interactions influence organ function and overall cellular health. We also highlight emerging small-molecule modulators of mitophagy, providing insight into potential therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring or enhancing organelle communication in pathological conditions.
