authorString: Chen H, Li Z, Hu X, Zhu C, Yang H, Wang Z, Wang Y.

title: Vascular dementia and vascular cognitive impairment-current treatments and future prospects.
authorString: Markus HS.

journal.title: International journal of stroke : official journal of the International Stroke Society

abstractText: Vascular cognitive impairment (VCI) and vascular dementia (VaD) represent a substantial and growing global health burden, yet remain under-recognized and comparatively under-researched. Two broad categories are post-stroke cognitive impairment, and VCI secondary to chronic cerebrovascular disease of which the most common cause is cerebral small vessel disease (SVD). In addition, cerebrovascular pathology frequently coexists with Alzheimer's disease (AD), increasing the probability that AD pathology will manifest as clinical dementia. Current management focuses primarily on prevention through modification of cardiovascular risk factors and lifestyle interventions. Intensive blood-pressure control has shown the strongest evidence, reducing future all-cause dementia while slowing progression of white-matter abnormalities. Multidomain lifestyle interventions incorporating exercise, diet, cognitive training, and vascular risk monitoring may also preserve cognition, although results across trials remain variable. In established VCI and VaD, treatment options are limited; cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine lack convincing evidence of benefit, and no pharmacological therapy has definitively demonstrated symptomatic improvement or delayed disease progression. Advances in understanding SVD and VCI pathophysiology are, however, identifying promising therapeutic targets. Emerging evidence highlights endothelial dysfunction, impaired cerebral autoregulation, increased blood-brain barrier permeability, inflammation, and glymphatic dysfunction as possible mechanisms underlying SVD. Current trials are evaluating treatment approaches based on this framework including cerebral vasodilators such as cilostazol, isosorbide mononitrate and phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors, anti-inflammatory therapies, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, remote ischemic conditioning, and strategies targeting glymphatic function. Improved mechanistic understanding, appropriately targeted interventions, and adequately powered long-term clinical trials are required to translate these emerging approaches into effective treatments for VCI and VaD.

title: Imaging-Enhanced Prediction of Upper Limb Motor Function After Stroke Using Automated Segmentation and Cluster Analysis.
authorString: Cha S, Ryu WS, Hwang B, Kim DY, Lee SH.
abstractText:
Background

Stroke is a leading cause of long-term disability, and early prediction of motor outcomes is critical for guiding individualized rehabilitation strategies. Although neuroimaging offers prognostic insights, its clinical integration remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate whether explainable imaging-derived features can improve the prediction of upper limb motor impairment and to identify distinct recovery profiles through cluster analysis.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed 242 patients with acute ischemic stroke who underwent brain magnetic resonance imaging and motor function assessment. Clinical and imaging variables-including infarct volume, motor tract involvement, and subtype classification-were extracted using automated software. Predictive models for Fugl-Meyer Assessment upper extremity (FMA-UE) scores were developed using hierarchical regression, and K-means clustering was applied to standardized baseline data. Cluster characteristics were compared, and recovery profiles were visualized.

Results

Incorporating imaging variables improved prediction of FMA-UE scores (adjusted R²: 0.595), with motor tract lesion volume emerging as a key predictor. Cluster analysis revealed three distinct patient subgroups: Cluster 1 (mild impairments, younger age), Cluster 2 (older patients with multiple comorbidities), and Cluster 3 (severe neurological deficits, large infarcts). Functional outcomes differed significantly across clusters, with Cluster 3 showing the greatest disability (76% with follow-up modified Rankin Scale 4-6, P < 0.001).

Conclusion

Imaging-derived features from early magnetic resonance imaging improve the prediction of upper limb motor outcomes after stroke. Cluster-based stratification identifies clinically meaningful subgroups, supporting precision rehabilitation through personalized care planning and targeted secondary prevention.

title: Neutrophil Extracellular Traps-Mediated Intraplaque Angiogenesis and Microvascular Permeability Promote Rapid Plaque Progression following Myocardial Infarction.
authorString: Lei Z, Yin Y, Zeng L, Yang N, Zhai M, Zeng Y, Shi Y, Yu Q, Gong S, Jian W, Zhuang J, Zhang L, Peng W.
abstractText: Despite adherence to guideline-recommended therapies, survivors of myocardial infarction (MI) remain at high risk for recurrent ischemic events. This study aimed to elucidate the underlying mechanisms responsible for this residual risk. Using Mendelian randomization analysis and retrospective cohort study, we established a causal relationship between MI and plaque progression, potentially mediated by neutrophils. In a murine atherosclerotic model, MI precipitated a marked expansion in plaque volume accompanied by reduced stability; these pathological changes are consistent with the hallmark features of rapid plaque progression, which may trigger recurrent ischemic events. Pharmacological inhibition and adoptive transfer experiments using Padi4flox/floxLyz2Cre mice confirmed the pivotal role of neutrophils in MI-driven rapid plaque progression via neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) formation. Further investigations revealed that NETs promote intraplaque hemorrhage by facilitating intraplaque angiogenesis and enhancing microvascular permeability, thereby exacerbating post-MI atherosclerotic inflammation. Mechanistically, bioinformatics analyses and in vitro experiments identified the transcription factor ETS proto-oncogene 1 as a critical regulator of NETs-mediated angiogenesis and endothelial permeability through the activation of the vascular endothelial growth factor A/vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2 signaling pathway. In vivo pharmacological inhibition of ETS proto-oncogene 1 with TK216 markedly attenuated the rapid plaque progression after MI. In summary, this study provides the first comprehensive evidence that neutrophils and NETs drive rapid plaque progression following MI by modulating intraplaque angiogenesis and hemorrhage. These findings offer novel insights into the mechanisms underlying post-MI ischemic event recurrence and highlight promising therapeutic targets for clinical prevention.

title: Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction Is Associated With Greater Cardiovascular Risk Following Lumbar Interbody Fusion.
authorString: Thiru SS, Goheer HE, Harris CJ, Nazif A, Botros M, Carmouche JJ.
abstractText: Study DesignRetrospective cohort study.ObjectiveTo compare perioperative cardiovascular outcomes between patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) following transforaminal or posterior lumbar interbody fusion (TLIF/PLIF).MethodsThe TriNetX Research Network was used to identify patients undergoing elective TLIF or PLIF between 2011 and 2025. Cohorts were defined by heart failure phenotype and propensity score-matched (PSM) 1:1 for baseline demographics and comorbidities. Outcomes included postoperative atrial fibrillation or flutter (AF/AFL), myocardial infarction (MI), and secondary complications within 90 days. Odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals were calculated. Significance was defined as p < 0.05.ResultsOf 46,431 patients, 1,253 (2.7%) had HFrEF, 1,920 (4.1%) had HFpEF, and 43,258 (93.2%) had no heart failure. After PSM, both phenotypes carried elevated risk relative to non-HF controls across measured complications, including acute respiratory failure, pneumonia, AF/AFL, acute kidney injury, venous thromboembolism, and 90-day emergency department visits (all p<0.05). In the direct phenotype comparison (1,217 matched pairs), acute MI occurred more frequently in HFrEF than HFpEF patients (14.4% vs. 8.7%, p<0.001). HFrEF was associated with greater odds of acute MI (OR 1.760 [95% CI: 1.363, 2.273], p<0.001) and AF/AFL (OR 1.278 [95% CI: 1.079, 1.513], p=0.005) compared with HFpEF.ConclusionAmong patients with heart failure undergoing TLIF or PLIF, those with HFrEF are at increased risk of postoperative AF/AFL and MI compared with HFpEF patients. These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing heart failure phenotype during preoperative risk stratification and may support enhanced perioperative precautions.

title: Sorting nexin 10 promotes triple-negative breast cancer progression through modulating cholesterol biosynthesis via stabilizing SREBP2.
authorString: Guo Y, Li J, Zhang W, Xia M, Liu G, Zhong X, Yi Y, Chen Y, Zhong J.
abstractText:
Objective

Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) lacks effective therapeutics in clinical practice. Sorting nexin 10 (SNX10) plays essential roles in various cancers, and the role of SNX10 in TNBC remains unknown. This study investigated the role and action mechanism of SNX10 in TNBC.

Methods

Using the Kaplan-Meier Plotter database and bc-GenExMiner database to analyze the SNX10 expression and clinical significance. Functional assays, including MTT, colony formation, transwell assays, and xenograft experiments, were used to evaluate the role of SNX10 in TNBC. The GeneChip PrimeView Human Gene Expression Array was used to determine the downstream targets and pathways. Cholesterol levels and the expression of enriched cholesterol synthesis genes were detected by Filipin assay, RT-PCR, and Western Blot. The relationship of SNX10 and cholesterol biosynthesis was confirmed using CO-IP and immunofluorescence staining assays.

Results

SNX10 is positively related to poor prognosis of breast cancer and markedly up-regulated in TNBC. Knockdown of SNX10 suppressed cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, and slowed the tumor growth in vivo. Mechanistically, SNX10 positively regulates the content and distribution of cellular cholesterol, as does the expression of enriched cholesterol synthesis genes, and SNX10 interacts with SREBP2 and prolongs its half-life. Blocking with lovastatin, cholesterol, or siSREBP2 reversed these effects caused by altering SNX10 in TNBC cells in vitro.

Conclusion

SNX10 promoted TNBC progression through the regulation of cholesterol biosynthesis, which was mediated by interaction with SREBP2 and maintenance of its stability. SNX10 may be an effective therapeutic target for TNBC, and our study provides new insights into therapeutic strategies.

title: Bioactive components from Sinomenium acutum exhibit anti-inflammatory activity and sensitize cervical cancer cells to paclitaxel.
authorString: Wang X, Zhu C, Du X, Wang Q, Yu J.
abstractText: Six previously undescribed compounds, together with twelve known compounds, were isolated from Sinomenium acutum. The structures of the unreported compounds were determined by comprehensive spectroscopic data analysis, <sup>13</sup>C NMR calculations followed by DP4 + analysis, ECD calculations, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis. Nine compounds exhibited more potent anti-inflammatory activities than the positive control indomethacin. The structure-activity relationship of the isolates with anti-inflammatory effects was elucidated, providing some useful clues for designing and developing structurally novel anti-inflammatory drugs. Furthermore, five compounds reversed the paclitaxel resistance in paclitaxel-resistant cervical cancer cells HeLa/PTX. The combination of compound 4 and paclitaxel promoted cancer cell apoptosis.

title: Expanding role of nuclear medicine in cardiac amyloidosis: insights from the EJNMMI collection.
authorString: Zirakchian Zadeh M, M Osman M.
abstractText: Recent advances in nuclear medicine are reshaping the evaluation of cardiac amyloidosis, as highlighted by the recent collection published in EJNMMI (collection link: https://link.springer.com/collections/igfdhcddjg). This commentary summarizes key insights from these studies, emphasizing the evolving shift from conventional diagnostic imaging toward a more integrated and comprehensive approach. Emerging developments include novel amyloid PET tracers, improved diagnostic accuracy with SPECT/CT, multimodality imaging strategies, and enhanced assessment of systemic disease burden extending beyond the left ventricle. There is also growing interest in longitudinal monitoring, pre-symptomatic detection, and the role of artificial intelligence. Together, these advances position nuclear medicine as an essential tool for disease characterization, risk stratification, and treatment assessment.

title: Percutaneous Retrieval of a Fractured Catheter Migrated via a Patent Foramen Ovale With High-Risk Morphology.
authorString: Fujimura Y, Morikawa T, Shigeno R, Hasegawa F, Hirohata A.
abstractText:
Background

A fractured central venous port catheter can rarely migrate into the left heart via a patent foramen ovale (PFO).

Case summary

A man in his 70s presented with a fractured central venous port catheter. Electrocardiogram-gated contrast-enhanced computed tomography confirmed that the fragment straddled from the right ventricular apex, through a PFO, into the right upper pulmonary vein. Because direct snaring of the ends was considered difficult, percutaneous retrieval was performed under transesophageal echocardiography guidance using the wire-loop technique. The catheter was dragged into the inferior vena cava and successfully retrieved into a 16-F sheath.

Discussion

In a situation where direct snaring was anatomically difficult, we successfully retrieved the fractured catheter with the wire-loop technique. Detailed preprocedural multimodality imaging of the PFO crossing significantly contributed to successful retrieval.

Take-home messages

In patients with a PFO, a fractured catheter can migrate into the left heart. Preprocedural evaluation using multimodality imaging is crucial for safe retrieval.

title: Occupational Specific Heavy Metal Exposure: Association With Age and Anthropometric Characteristics Relative to Hypertension.
authorString: Uzomba GC, Nwafor C, Ugah C, Ogbodo H, Amaku C, Onwe K, Cookey-Gam TI, Obaje GS, Mbajiorgu E.
abstractText: The present study aimed at investigating the association between serum heavy metals, anthropometric characteristics, and hypertension among different occupations and analyzing the prediction between heavy metals, anthropometrics, and hypertension among male and female miners, artisans, laborers, and farmers. Body weight, height, and circumferences were measured via the direct standard anthropometric approach. Blood pressure (BP) was measured using a standardized mercury sphygmomanometer with an appropriate cuff size. Blood samples were analyzed using an atomic absorption spectrophotometer. Chi-square and binary logistic regression analysis were conducted at a significance level of p < 0.05 (∗). For miners, there was no significant association between serum heavy metals, anthropometric characteristics, and hypertension (p > 0.05). Among artisans, age and anthropometric circumferences showed significant association with hypertension (χ 2 = 5.266 - 21.206, p < 0.05∗). Among laborers, age was significantly associated with hypertension (χ 2 = 62.548, p < 0.05∗). For farmers, age showed significant association with hypertension (χ 2 = 3.925, p < 0.05∗). The derived regression model, which included age as a predictor, showed that increasing age was significantly associated with higher odds of hypertension among miners (aOR: 1.076, 95% CI: 1.029-1.125) and artisans (aOR: 11.938, 95% CI: 3.349-38.621). Furthermore, anthropometric circumferences were significant predictors of hypertension among artisans (aOR: 3,427, 95% CI: 1.205-9.747) and laborers (aOR: 2.50, 95% CI: 1.130-3.207). The study contributes to the understanding of relevant of heavy metals and specific anthropometrics to BP. Understanding the effects of heavy metals and age have implications in occupational health and contribute to the development of public health interventions.

title: The macroeconomic burden of four alcohol-attributable diseases in China, 1990-2023, and projections to 2030: results from GBD 2023.
authorString: Yang X, Xin L, Yu J, Yang Q, Gong Y, Guo Z, Yang K.
abstractText:
Background

Alcohol consumption contributes markedly to the global burden of disease, but macroeconomic assessments of alcohol-attributable diseases in China remain limited. Using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) data, this study quantified the macroeconomic burden of four alcohol-attributable diseases in China: alcohol use disorders (AUD), alcoholic cardiomyopathy (ACM), cirrhosis and other chronic liver diseases due to alcohol use (ALD), and liver cancer due to alcohol use (LCA).

Materials and methods

Disability-adjusted life year (DALY) data for the four diseases from 1990 to 2023 were extracted from GBD 2023. The macroeconomic burden was estimated using the value of lost welfare (VLW) approach, which combined DALYs with age-adjusted value of a statistical life year (VSLY) estimates derived from willingness-to-pay methodology. Results are expressed in 2021 international dollars and as a percentage of GDP. Temporal trends were evaluated using Joinpoint regression analysis, and exploratory forecasts to 2030 were generated using ARIMA, XGBoost, and LightGBM models.

Results

From 1990 to 2023, VLW increased substantially for all four diseases: AUD from $1.84 billion to $32.40 billion; ACM, $0.04 to $0.53 billion; ALD, $0.22 to $3.26 billion; and LCA, $0.09 to $2.48 billion. Joinpoint regression confirmed continuously increasing trends (all AAPC > 0, all p < 0.001). Males predominated across all conditions, with male-to-female VLW ratios of 7:1 (AUD), 10:1 (ALD), 3:1 (LCA), and 14:1 (ACM) in 2023. Age at peak VLW varied: 35-39 years for AUD, 50-59 years for ALD, 65-69 years for LCA, and 50-54 years for ACM (shifted from 35-39 years in 1990). Conditional on the continuation of their respective historical trends, the three models produced divergent exploratory projections to 2030.

Conclusion

The macroeconomic burden of four alcohol-attributable diseases in China increased markedly from 1990 to 2023, with AUD consistently dominating and the burden overwhelmingly concentrated among males aged 35-64 years.

title: A Milestone in the Globalization of Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance and a Legacy for Brazil and Latin America.
authorString: Rochitte CE, Azevedo C, Fernandes JL.
abstractText: Central Illustration : A Milestone in the Globalization of Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance and a Legacy for Brazil and Latin America SCMR Rio 2026 represented the transition from geographic internationalization to the development of regional scientific capacity. The meeting brought together global participation, Latin American leadership, education, certification, and multidisciplinary collaboration as pillars to expand access to high-quality CMR.

title: Lipid metabolism remodeling in human cardiomyocyte differentiation and maturation.
authorString: Tang H, Liu R, Xiong Z, He Q, Lu G, Chan WY, Wang W.
abstractText: Cardiac development involves extensive metabolic remodeling, yet dynamic changes of endogenous lipid species during human cardiomyocyte (CM) differentiation remain poorly characterized. In this study, we systematically performed high-coverage lipidomic profiling across five consecutive CM differentiation stages, using high-performance liquid chromatography. MYL2 expression confirmed ventricular lineage specification in late-stage CMs. Ceramide levels peaked at the cardiac progenitor cell (CPC) stage, suggesting a stage-specific association with the mesendoderm (MES)-to-CPC transition. Meanwhile, lipid categories such as monosialodihexosylganglioside, phosphatidylcholine (PC), lysophosphatidylcholine, and lysophosphatidic acid were markedly elevated in mature CMs. Integrated transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility analyses further delineated the temporal regulatory landscape underlying stage-dependent lipid remodeling during cardiogenic differentiation. Functional assays revealed that PC promotes the expression of mature CM marker genes and improves CM viability. Collectively, these findings establish a comprehensive, high-resolution dynamic lipidomic atlas of in vitro hESC-derived CM differentiation, providing a valuable resource for understanding lipid-associated mechanisms in heart development.

title: Coronary Flow Velocity Reserve by Stress Echocardiography: The Prognostic Key of Multiple Heart Diseases.
authorString: Lowenstein J.
abstractText: Although evaluating coronary flow velocity reserve (CFVR) via stress echocardiography (SE) has been available for over three decades, its integration into routine clinical practice remains underutilized globally despite substantial technical and conceptual advances. A diminished CFVR serves as a potent predictor of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and all-cause mortality across a broad spectrum of cardiovascular diseases. Its prognostic value is particularly robust in epicardial coronary artery disease, heart failure, coronary microvascular dysfunction, nonischemic cardiomyopathies, metabolic disorders (e.g., diabetes mellitus and obesity), hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, systemic autoimmune diseases, and cardiac allograft vasculopathy. This comprehensive narrative review details the technical methodology for interrogating resting and stress-induced coronary flow velocity (CFV) under physical and pharmacological protocols. Furthermore, it highlights the clinical applicability of CFVR by synthesizing single-center observational insights with evidence from large-scale multicenter registries, advocating for its broader adoption into diagnostic workflows to refine risk stratification and guide therapeutic management.

title: Molecular Biomarkers Linking Psoriasis and Cardiovascular Disease: Current Evidence and Clinical Perspectives.
authorString: Matwiejuk M, Myśliwiec H, Mikłosz A, Jarocewicz O, Chabowski A, Flisiak I.
abstractText: Psoriasis is a chronic, immune-mediated inflammatory disease affecting the skin, nails, and joints. Its complex pathogenesis results from interactions between genetic susceptibility and environmental factors and is accompanied by an increased risk of multiple systemic comorbidities, particularly cardiovascular disease. Growing evidence indicates that both conditions share common molecular pathways driven by chronic inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, metabolic disturbances, and immune dysregulation. Among the emerging molecular biomarkers, chemerin, endocan, and growth differentiation factor-15 (GDF-15) have attracted considerable attention due to their role in vascular homeostasis, adipose tissue biology, glucose metabolism, and inflammatory signaling. This review summarizes current evidence on the involvement of these biomarkers in psoriasis and cardiovascular disease, highlighting their contribution to the molecular mechanisms underlying the psoriasis-cardiovascular disease axis. Furthermore, we discussed their potential usefulness as candidate biomarkers for cardiovascular risk. However, prospective validation is strictly required to confirm their clinical utility and establish their incremental predictive value beyond conventional risk factors.

title: Nosocomial Respiratory Syncytial Virus in the Post-Pandemic Era: Evolving Epidemiology and Integrated Prevention Strategies.
authorString: Huang PH, Huang PH, Liu PY, Yeh TK.
abstractText:
Background/objectives

Pandemic non-pharmaceutical interventions virtually eliminated respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) circulation in 2020-2021, and their relaxation was followed by unprecedented off-season resurgences. This narrative review, informed by a structured literature search, synthesizes current evidence on healthcare-associated RSV (HA-RSV), including transmission dynamics, vulnerable inpatient populations, and integrated prevention strategies, in the post-pandemic era.

Methods

We searched PubMed/MEDLINE and Europe PMC (January 2000-October 2025) using two complementary strategies, supplemented by WHO and CDC guidance. Primary hospital-based studies reporting laboratory-confirmed HA-RSV cases formed the core evidence set; surveillance reports, systematic reviews, and guidance were used as labeled contextual evidence and synthesized narratively.

Results

Twenty-nine primary studies from neonatal, pediatric, adult, geriatric, and immunocompromised settings provided direct evidence on HA-RSV, which accounted for 3-15% of RSV hospitalizations depending on setting and case definition and was associated with prolonged stay, escalation of respiratory support, higher costs, and, in children, higher mortality than community-onset infection. Universal masking and pre-admission screening were followed by reductions in HA-RSV in most before-after studies. Post-pandemic surveillance shows earlier, less predictable RSV activity and periods of concurrent circulation with influenza and SARS-CoV-2. RSV spreads mainly through short-range respiratory particles and contaminated hands and surfaces; asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic healthcare workers are one potential source of introduction.

Conclusions

Prevention of HA-RSV rests on hand hygiene, transmission-based precautions, environmental disinfection, rapid molecular diagnostics, and supportive healthcare-worker and visitor policies, escalated according to local surveillance rather than the calendar. Immunoprophylaxis and vaccination reduce severe RSV disease in eligible groups, but direct evidence that they prevent healthcare-associated transmission is lacking.

title: Integration of hereditary thrombophilia data and polygenic risk scores into prognostic models improves differential diagnosis of CTEPH.
authorString: Kubkin Y, Nikulin D, Okhrimenko G, Minushkina L, Dyachkova E, Lyzhenkova A, Danilova A, Dankovtseva E, Borovikova I, Zamyatin V, Averyanov A, Poptsova M, Zateyshchikov D.
abstractText:
Background

Differential diagnosis between pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) is crucial for treatment selection, particularly regarding surgical intervention. The prevalence of hereditary thrombophilias in Russian CTEPH patients and the utility of genetic data in differential diagnosis remain understudied.

Objectives

To evaluate the prevalence of inherited thrombophilia among patients with CTEPH and PAH, to benchmark the results against published data from other cohorts, and to assess the potential utility of integrating genetic findings and polygenic risk score (PRS) parameters with clinical data for differentiating CTEPH from PAH.

Methods

The study included 390 patients (252 PAH, 138 CTEPH). Whole-genome sequencing was performed to analyze classical thrombophilia genes (PROC, PROS1, SERPINC1, F2, F5, ADAMTS13, HRG, JAK2, PIGA, THBD, F9, FGA, FGB, FGG, CALR) and calculate VTE polygenic risk scores. A meta-analysis of 15 studies on hereditary thrombophilia prevalence in CTEPH was conducted. AutoML algorithm was used to construct diagnostic models.

Results

Rare variants in thrombosis-associated genes were significantly more prevalent in patients with CTEPH than in those with PAH (12.3% vs. 1.2%, p < 0.001). Similarly, carriers of the common F5 and F2 thrombophilia variants were more frequent in the CTEPH group (15.9% vs. 6.3%, p = 0.002). Meta-analysis yielded pooled prevalence estimates in CTEPH of 3.0% for antithrombin deficiency, 3.6% for protein S deficiency, 4.7% for protein C deficiency, 7.9% for F5 Leiden, and 5.6% for F2 G20210A; these estimates were consistent with those reported in other populations. The clinical model yielded an ROC AUC of 0.883. The addition of PGS004854 and rare variants in thrombosis-associated genes increased the AUC to 0.951, representing an absolute increase of 0.068 (7.7%; p = 0.026). In the multivariable model, PGS004854 was the strongest positive genetic predictor of CTEPH (β = 1.869, p < 0.001).

Conclusions

The genetic profile of CTEPH patients differs significantly from PAH, with a higher frequency of hereditary thrombotic risk factors. Integrating clinical data with polygenic risk scores and thrombophilia variants improves differential diagnosis accuracy and may optimize the clinical workup.

title: Combined assessment of fibrinogen-to-platelet ratio and ApoB/ApoA1 ratio for pre-angiographic risk stratification of severe multivessel coronary disease in NSTEMI.
authorString: Zhou Z, Wang W, Zhou H, Chen Z, Jiang M, Li Z, Li L.
abstractText:
Background

Residual inflammation and dysregulated lipid metabolism are closely associated with the extent of severe multivessel coronary disease (MVD) in patients with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI). The fibrinogen-to-platelet ratio (FPR) and the apolipoprotein B/apolipoprotein A1 (ApoB/ApoA1) ratio reflect these two residual risk pathways, respectively, whereas the clinical value of their combined assessment for pre-angiographic identification of severe MVD remains to be evaluated.

Objective

To evaluate the incremental value of combining FPR with the ApoB/ApoA1 ratio for pre-angiographic identification of severe MVD in patients with NSTEMI and to develop an adjunctive risk-stratification model.

Methods

This single-center retrospective study included 580 patients with NSTEMI who underwent coronary angiography. Correlation analyses, logistic regression, and restricted cubic spline models were used to assess the associations between the two biomarkers and MVD. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) were used to evaluate the incremental value of the biomarkers. A nomogram was developed and internally validated using bootstrap resampling. Decision curve analysis (DCA) was performed to assess net clinical benefit, and subgroup analyses were conducted.

Results

FPR remained independently and positively associated with severe MVD, with an approximately linear dose-response relationship; the association of the ApoB/ApoA1 ratio was attenuated after full adjustment, although it showed complementary value in patients with a very high coronary lesion burden. With the combined model, the AUC increased from 0.683 to 0.719, while the continuous NRI and IDI were 0.488 and 0.037, respectively; adding the ApoB/ApoA1 ratio to the model containing FPR did not significantly improve the AUC (P = 0.266) but yielded further improvements in NRI and IDI. Potential effect modification by diabetes status was observed (P for interaction = 0.025).

Conclusion

FPR is an important adjunctive biomarker for the pre-angiographic identification of severe MVD in patients with NSTEMI, whereas the ApoB/ApoA1 ratio provides complementary reclassification information. The nomogram incorporating both biomarkers may facilitate pre-angiographic risk stratification.

title: Case Report: When cardiomyopathy is the clue: late-presenting propionic acidemia manifesting as acute heart failure.
authorString: Nti BK, Trapp N, Ali A, Lanpher B, Weatherhead J.
abstractText:
Background

Propionic acidemia (PA) is a rare inborn error of metabolism that typically presents in infancy; however, late-onset variants may manifest with atypical features, including cardiac involvement. Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is an uncommon but serious complication.

Case summary

A 15-year-old with no prior medical history but a significant maternal family history of cardiomyopathy of unknown etiology from an Amish background presented with altered mental status, increased work of breathing, and progressive edema in the context of preceding viral illness. Evaluation revealed severe biventricular dysfunction, chamber dilation, and findings consistent with chronic DCM. Despite supportive management, her course was complicated by ventricular arrhythmias and clinical deterioration. Metabolic workup demonstrated elevated propionylcarnitine and increased urinary 2-methylcitric acid, confirming late-onset variant PA. She was treated with intravenous carnitine and a specialized metabolic formula; however, cardiac function remained severely impaired. In accordance with family wishes, she was discharged home on hospice care.

Conclusion

Late-onset PA can present as isolated cardiomyopathy in adolescence. Early consideration of metabolic etiologies is essential in unexplained DCM, particularly in high-risk populations.

title: Functional Capacity as a Correlate of Health-Related Quality of Life in Patients With Heart Failure: A Cross-Sectional Study.
authorString: Dos Santos JAG, de Oliveira Mangueira S, Santos VB, Juárez-Vela R, Cabral JVB, de Sousa MM.
abstractText: This study aimed to analyze the associations among functional capacity, self-care, and health-related quality of life in patients with heart failure (HF). A cross-sectional correlational study was conducted. Functional capacity was measured with the Duke Activity Status Index, self-care with the European Heart Failure Self-Care Behaviour Scale, and health-related quality of life with the Minnesota Living with Heart Failure Questionnaire. Data were analyzed using Spearman's correlation and simple linear regression analyses. Ninety-six patients with HF participated. The median functional capacity was 18.90 (IQR: 9.95-32.30), the mean self-care score was 29.60 (SD = 5.68), and the median quality of life was 51.50 (IQR: 40.00-66.00). Functional capacity was strongly and inversely correlated with health-related quality of life (ρ = -0.700, p < 0.001) and accounted for 40.0% of the variance in health-related quality of life scores. In this sample of outpatients with HF, better functional capacity was associated with better health-related quality of life.

title: Successful systemic fibrinolysis in pulmonary embolism with a thrombus-in-transit.
authorString: Ivanova S, Irfan I, Radkova M, Stoyanova K, Karamfiloff K.

journal.title: Blood coagulation & fibrinolysis : an international journal in haemostasis and thrombosis

abstractText: Right heart thrombus-in-transit with acute pulmonary embolism (PE) is a rare but potentially lethal clinical finding. Optimal management remains controversial, particularly when major contraindications or risk factors coexist. We present a 72-year-old male admitted to the emergency room with leading diagnosis acute coronary syndrome who was later diagnosed with acute PE and a massive, mobile right heart thrombus along with a concomitant ascending aortic aneurysm. Due to high surgical risk, systemic fibrinolysis was performed under close monitoring. Follow-up echocardiography demonstrated complete resolution of the intracardiac thrombus, rapid right ventricular recovery, and an intact thoracic aorta. This case highlights the importance of echocardiography in initial evaluation of patients with acute cardiovascular symptoms and also systemic thrombolysis as a viable, life-saving strategy for right heart thrombosis even in complex clinical scenarios.

title: Effects of Aerobic Exercise on Autonomic and Endothelial Function and Splanchnic Hemodynamics in Compensated Cirrhosis: RCT Study.
authorString: Kittiprachakul S, Rangkla S, Kulaputana O, Kositanurit W, Tabtieang T, Sukprakun C, Seehaboot K, Woramuksik P, Sanguanrungsirikul S, Chaiteerakij R.

journal.title: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

abstractText:
Background

Patients with cirrhosis often develop autonomic dysfunction (AD) and endothelial dysfunction (ED), which correlate with higher mortality. Aerobic exercise (AE) is a potential intervention, yet its effects on the autonomic nervous system (ANS) and hemodynamics remain underinvestigated in cirrhosis.

Methods

We conducted a parallel-group randomized controlled trial including 50 sedentary patients with compensated cirrhosis. Participants were randomized to a 16-week moderate-intensity AE plus nutritional consultation (AE group; n = 25) or nutritional consultation alone (control group, CG; n = 25). Outcomes included heart rate variability (HRV), flow-mediated dilation (FMD) for peripheral circulation, mesenteric Doppler ultrasound for splanchnic hemodynamics, and sarcopenia-related outcomes (body composition, handgrip strength dynamometry, and the 6-min walk test [6MWT]). Data were analysed using intention-to-treat (ITT), modified ITT (mITT), and per-protocol approaches, as well as general linear mixed models (LMM).

Results

Of the 50 participants (mean age, 62.6 ± 7.0 years; 60% female), 44 participants completed the study. Although most outcomes showed no statistically significant between-group differences, LMM analysis confirmed a significant reduction in the low-frequency to high-frequency (LF/HF) (β = -0.87, p = 0.04), indicating worsening ANS while AE remained stable. Based on mITT analysis, the AE group showed a significant with-in group increase in portal vein volume flow (median Δ = 350.66 mL/min, p = 0.003). Additionally, AE demonstrated significant improvement in 6MWT compared with CG (mean Δ = 32 m, IQR: 12.00-51.60 m, p < 0.01). No major adverse events occurred.

Conclusions

AE is safe and effectively improves functional capacity in compensated cirrhosis. However, positive signals in autonomic and hepatic parameters were not between-group significant, necessitating a cautious interpretation.

title: A multifaceted intervention to increase bystander CPR rates after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in France: a stepped-wedge, cluster-randomised, controlled trial.
authorString: Debaty G, Ribes S, Ray P, Chouihed T, Desseigne N, Usseglio P, Serre P, Pradeau C, Bounes V, Roupioz T, Lucas AS, Giolito D, Zamour C, Boyer C, Hubert H, Savary D, Tazarourte K, Freund Y, Watson SI, Hemming K, Lamhaut L, Labarère J.
abstractText:
Background

Bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is a key determinant of survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), but rates remain suboptimal worldwide. We evaluated whether a multifaceted intervention targeting emergency dispatch systems and community response could increase bystander-initiated CPR before emergency medical service (EMS) arrival.

Methods

We conducted a stepped-wedge, cluster-randomised trial in 15 French EMS agencies. The intervention combined dispatcher training for early recognition of cardiac arrest and telephone-assisted CPR, activation of trained volunteers through a geolocation smartphone application, and structured audit and feedback provided to EMS agencies. Consecutive adults (≥18 years) with non-traumatic OHCA were included. Randomisation was stratified by tercile of OHCA volume managed by each EMS in 2015. The intervention was implemented during a 1-month transition period before the intervention period at each EMS centre. A dedicated protocol guided dispatchers to identify cardiac arrest from unresponsiveness and abnormal breathing, then gave scripted compression-only instructions and activated volunteers, targeting recognition within 60 s of call pick-up and first compression within a further 60 s. The primary outcome was bystander-initiated CPR before EMS arrival. The trial was prospectively registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03633370) and is completed.

Findings

Of the 15 EMS agencies initially randomised, two withdrew before recruitment began and were replaced, and one enrolled no patients. Therefore, between Aug 27, 2018, and Feb 20, 2022, 14 EMS agencies recruited a total of 2160 patients. The intention-to-treat analysis included 1684 patients (686 control, 998 intervention) enrolled across the 12 originally randomised EMS agencies. The mean age for all patients included in the intention-to-treat analysis was 67 years (SD 15), and 1205 (71·6%) were male. Bystander-initiated CPR before EMS arrival occurred in 421 (61·4%) patients in the control group and 708 (70·9%) patients in the intervention group (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 1·54 [95% CI 1·09-2·19]; p=0·017). Estimates were consistent across six prespecified sensitivity analyses (OR range, 1·38-1·55), remaining significant in four, but not after adjustment for cluster-specific secular trends (1·38 [0·98-1·94]) or baseline characteristics (1·39 [0·97-1·98]). No intervention-related adverse events were reported.

Interpretation

A multifaceted intervention was associated with increased bystander-initiated CPR after OHCA, although the estimate was sensitive to the modelling of secular trends, and it did not translate into improved clinical outcomes. These findings support further investigation of coordinated community-based strategies to strengthen the early links in the chain of survival at a population level.

Funding

Direction Générale de l'Offre de Soins.

title: Estimating GFR: what it is, what it is not, and why prediction cannot settle the question.
authorString: Delanaye P, Agarwal R.
abstractText: Schultheiss et al. show that replacing Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration with European Kidney Function Consortium cystatin C-based equations reclassifies women, but not men, into milder chronic kidney disease stages, while outcome prediction is unchanged. We argue that prediction of kidney failure cannot validate a glomerular filtration rate equation: dialysis initiation is a clinical decision, not a filtration measurement. The analysis is cross-sectional, leaving longitudinal performance untested. Equations are population tools; at the bedside, non-glomerular filtration rate determinants of both creatinine and cystatin C can mislead.

title: The effect of food taxes in the UK on health and economic outcomes, and equity: a modelling study.
authorString: Pidd K, Wilson LB, Pryce R, Brennan A, Morris D, Reynolds C, Lake AA, Moore HJ, Burrows A, Wells R, Vogel C, Connor N, Breeze P.
abstractText:
Background

WHO recommends using fiscal policies (such as taxes on unhealthy foods) that discourage consuming foods that contribute to unhealthy diets. Food tax evaluations require consideration for sociodemographic differences, consumer and industry behaviour, reformulation, and long-term health-related outcomes and health inequalities. We aimed to model the potential benefits and harms of three food tax policy designs, to health, costs, and inequalities, in the UK.

Methods

Using a microsimulation model, we performed an economic evaluation of three UK food tax policy designs: (1) a Sugar Snacks tax targeting snacks, cakes, and milk drinks; (2) an Unhealthy Food tax high in fat, sugar, or salt; and (3) a Sugar and Salt tax. Consumption and nutritional changes for a UK representative synthetic population (aged ≥5 years) were estimated by applying a hierarchical Almost Ideal Demand System, accommodating key socio-demographic differences. Our primary analysis simulated outcomes for consumer response only. Secondary analyses incorporated industry responses in the model. The microsimulation estimated changes to weight, cardiometabolic risk factors, lifetime health, discounted National Health Service (NHS) costs, social care costs, unemployment or inactivity, and social benefit receipts.

Findings

The estimated average reduction in daily calorie intake was -25 kcal (95% credible interval [95% CrI]; -31 to -19), -42 kcal (-51 to -33), and -58 kcal (-66 to -50) for the Sugar Snacks, Unhealthy Food, and Sugar and Salt taxes respectively, with reductions in sugar, salt, and saturated fat. Long-term modelling showed improved health, including reduced cardiovascular disease, and type 2 diabetes for all three tax policies. The taxes reduced NHS costs (Sugar Snacks -£168 [95% CrI -461 to -73], Unhealthy Food -£268 [-722 to -105], and Sugar and Salt -£374 [-1033 to -159]) and social care costs. The impact on health inequalities varied by policy design. Only the Sugar and Salt tax had a positive impact on health inequalities.

Interpretation

The overall health impact of each of the three tax policy designs modelled was positive, but it can be associated with important nutritional trade-off-cross-price elasticities led to a reduction in fibre intake. Of the three policies modelled, the Sugar and Salt tax generated the greatest gains and reduced health inequalities. Policy design should consider potential impacts on health inequalities and should be part of a multi-component strategy.

Funding

National Institute for Health and Care Research.

title: Proton arc therapy reduces the dose delivered to circulating blood compared to intensity-modulated proton therapy for head-and-neck cancer.
authorString: Tattenberg S, Liu P, Cong X, Hoehr C, Ding X.

journal.title: Journal of applied clinical medical physics

abstractText:
Background

Compared to intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT), proton arc therapy (PAT) has various dosimetric advantages. However, questions have been raised over whether the larger low-dose bath during PAT may increase radiation-induced lymphocyte killing, which is correlated with adverse clinical outcomes.

Purpose

The purpose of this study is to quantitatively compare radiation dose delivery to circulating blood during IMPT and PAT.

Methods

For each of 10 head-and-neck cancer patients, one IMPT and one PAT treatment plan were created, and the hematological dose (HEDOS) blood dose model was used to simulate radiation dose delivery to circulating blood. HEDOS simulations utilized gantry angle-wise dose distributions (including for PAT) and considered gantry rotation and energy layer switching as well as irradiation times. Blood dose histograms as well as the mean dose to all simulation blood particles (Dmean) and the dose delivered to the 90% and 10% of blood particles receiving the highest dose (D90% and D10%) were then compared between IMPT and PAT.

Results

For IMPT, blood dose metrics (in the form of mean over all patients ± one standard deviation) were (0.522 ± 0.204)Gy(RBE) for D90%, (0.563 ± 0.212)Gy(RBE) for Dmean, and (0.605 ± 0.219)Gy(RBE) for D10%. For PAT, D90% was (0.430 ± 0.184)Gy(RBE), Dmean was (0.483 ± 0.195)Gy(RBE), and D10% was (0.538 ± 0.207)Gy(RBE). The Wilcoxon signed-rank test indicated statistically significant (p < 0.05) differences between blood dose metrics of IMPT and PAT for all patients, and IMPT did not increase the percentage of blood particles which received no radiation dose during the delivery of a single treatment fraction.

Conclusions

Compared to IMPT, proton arc therapy was associated with significantly lower radiation dose delivery to circulating blood across a variety of different metrics. Proton arc therapy for head-and-neck cancer is therefore not expected to result in higher radiation-induced killing of circulating lymphocytes compared to IMPT.

title: Uncertainty-suppressed long-tailed learning with lightweight feature adaptation for multi-label chest X-ray classification.
authorString: Li L.

journal.title: Journal of applied clinical medical physics

abstractText:
Background

Report-mined chest radiograph datasets commonly contain both long-tailed label distributions and uncertain annotations. Conventional frequency-based re-weighting can strengthen rare-label learning, but it may also amplify unreliable supervision when uncertain labels occur in minority classes.

Purpose

To develop and evaluate an uncertainty-suppressed long-tailed learning method with lightweight feature adaptation for multi-label chest X-ray (CXR) classification under imbalanced and uncertain report-derived supervision.

Methods

The proposed uncertainty-suppressed long-tailed feature adaptation (USLFA) method combines a lightweight label-adaptive feature head with an uncertainty-suppressed long-tailed loss. The primary analysis used a patient-level 70%/10%/20% split of CheXpert for 14 observation labels. Robustness was further examined across two additional patient-level partitions, on the recommended MIMIC-CXR-JPG test split without retraining, and on the official radiologist-annotated CheXpert test set. Performance was assessed using macro-AUROC, macro-AUPRC, macro F1, frequency-group analysis, ablation studies, and uncertainty-handling comparisons. Ninety-five percent confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated by patient-level bootstrap resampling, and formal pairwise tests in the primary CheXpert analysis used paired permutation testing with Holm correction.

Results

On the primary CheXpert split, USLFA achieved a macro-AUROC of 0.864 (95% CI, 0.856-0.871), macro-AUPRC of 0.547 (95% CI, 0.532-0.560), and macro F1 of 0.501 (95% CI, 0.487-0.514). Compared with ConvNeXt-Tiny using binary cross-entropy (BCE), the gains in macro-AUPRC and macro F1 were both 0.051 and remained significant after Holm correction (both p < 0.001). Compared with label-distribution-aware margin (LDAM), USLFA improved macro-AUPRC by 0.018 (Holm-adjusted p = 0.024) and macro F1 by 0.017 (Holm-adjusted p = 0.041). The ordering was preserved across three patient-level partitions, with USLFA macro-AUPRC ranging from 0.540 to 0.555. On MIMIC-CXR-JPG, USLFA achieved a macro-AUPRC of 0.485 (95% CI, 0.467-0.502), and on the official CheXpert test set it achieved a mean AUROC of 0.920 (95% CI, 0.908-0.931) across the five competition observations.

Conclusions

USLFA improved macro-AUPRC and rare-label recognition without introducing an additional inference-time branch. Macro F1 was significantly higher than the principal BCE and LDAM baselines in the main comparison, whereas the additional macro F1 gain attributable to uncertainty suppression over U Soft was not significant after Holm correction. The repeated-split, external-dataset, and official-test analyses provide complementary evidence that the observed advantage is not confined to a single custom partition.

title: Diagnostic image quality of shoulder magnetic resonance imaging at 0.55T in healthy subjects and patients with rotator cuff injury: Prospective comparison with 1.5T.
authorString: Liu J, Gao Y, Gao G, Li W, Wang X, Zhu J, Liu X, Wang X, Zhou K, Liu H, Qiu J.

journal.title: Journal of applied clinical medical physics

abstractText:
Background

Lower‑field 0.55 T MRI scanners with large‑bore design could offer patients more comfortable feeling and flexible position. With the advances in deep‑learning reconstruction and hardware optimization, 0.55T have greatly improved their image quality and cost‑effectiveness for musculoskeletal applications. However, its feasibility for shoulder evaluation remains unstudied.

Purpose

To evaluate the image quality of shoulder using 0.55T MRI in volunteers and patients with rotator cuff injury with comparison of conventional 1.5T.

Methods

Fifty participants (25 volunteers, 25 patients) were prospectively enrolled. All participants underwent shoulder MRI both at open 0.55T with contour coils and deep learning (DL) and 1.5T MR without DL. The nonparametric method was utilized to compare image quality scores and quantitative metrics (signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (|CNR|)). Arthroscopy have been conducted in 16 patients. Kappa statistics was used to assess interobserver and interstudy agreement for lesion evaluation. Comfort feeling was also compared.

Results

The scan time was 11'25″ for 0.55T MRI and 11'42″ for 1.5T MRI. The interobserver analyses showed high consistency (κ = 0.771-1.000, P: 0.008 ∼ < 0.001) among 3 readers. The scores for coronal fat suppressed T2 weighted imaging (fsT2WI) and coronal T1 weighted imaging (T1WI) were significantly higher for 0.55T MRI. Most sequences at 0.55T demonstrated significantly higher SNRs (P:0.04 ∼ < 0.001). Additionally, |CNR| values for lesions were significantly higher in fs proton weighted imaging (PDWI) and fsT2WI at 0.55T. Perfect interstudy agreement between 0.55T and 1.5T was observed between 2 readers (Kappa = 1, P < 0.001) for lesion assessment. Agreement between MRI findings and arthroscopic results was perfect or good. The 0.55T system received higher scores in comfort ratings.

Conclusion

The 0.55T MRI with DL, showed comparable or better image quality in healthy subjects and patients with rotator cuff injury to 1.5T MRI without DL.

title: Circular RNAs in Drug-Induced Cardiotoxicity: Roles, Mechanisms, and Therapeutic Potential.
authorString: Leng K, Yang Z, Shi L, Sun Z, Gu M, Tang N.

journal.title: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

abstractText: Drug-induced cardiotoxicity (DIC) remains a major challenge in drug development and clinical practice, often resulting in treatment interruption, drug attrition, and adverse cardiovascular outcomes. DIC has been associated with a wide range of therapeutic agents, including anthracyclines, HER2-targeted therapies, tyrosine kinase inhibitors, immune checkpoint inhibitors, and other cardiotoxic drugs. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have attracted increasing attention as stable and versatile regulatory RNAs involved in cardiovascular injury. This review summarizes the biogenesis and functional mechanisms of circRNAs, their pathological roles in DIC, biomarker potential, therapeutic implications, and translational challenges. CircRNAs regulate gene expression through diverse mechanisms, including miRNA sequestration, interactions with RNA-binding proteins, transcriptional regulation, modulation of alternative splicing, and, in some cases, peptide translation. These regulatory functions have been implicated in apoptosis, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammatory signaling, pyroptosis, and cardiac remodeling during DIC. Emerging evidence suggests that circRNAs may serve as candidate molecular markers and potential therapeutic targets for DIC. However, the current evidence is derived predominantly from cellular and animal models, with doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity accounting for a substantial proportion of available studies. Clinical validation, particularly in well-characterized patient cohorts and across different drug classes, remains limited. Overall, further efforts are needed to establish standardized circRNA detection and quantification methods, validate their functional roles, conduct prospective clinical studies, and determine their incremental value in combination with established cardiac biomarkers before circRNA-based approaches can be translated into clinical management of DIC.

title: Tumor-Associated Mast Cells Drive Immunosuppression and Resistance to Anti-PD-1 Therapy in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Through CCL17/CCR4-mediated Regulatory T-Cell Recruitment.
authorString: Yang S, Yang C.

journal.title: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

abstractText: This study investigated how tumor-associated mast cells (TAMCs) contribute to immunosuppression and anti-PD-1 resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). TAMC infiltration as well as the levels of stem cell factor (SCF) and various chemokines were measured in clinical specimens obtained from 59 HCC patients. The recruitment and maintenance of TAMCs by HCC-conditioned medium were examined, with a focus on the role of SCF in these processes. In addition, the chemotactic effect of CCL17 (secreted by activated TAMCs) on CCR4-expressing regulatory T cells (Tregs) was evaluated. The functional impact of the recruited Tregs was further assessed by examining their capacity to inhibit the proliferation of CD8<sup>+</sup> T cells and to suppress the secretion of cytotoxic effector molecules. In vivo experiments were also conducted to evaluate the antitumor efficacy of combining anti-PD-1 antibodies with either cromolyn sodium or CCR4 antagonists. Analysis of HCC specimens revealed a marked accumulation of TAMCs, and the extent of TAMC infiltration was found to be positively correlated with both SCF and CCL17 levels. HCC cells were shown to actively recruit TAMCs and promote their proliferation through the secretion of SCF. Upon activation, TAMCs released CCL17, which potently chemotaxed Tregs in a CCR4-dependent manner and subsequently suppressed the antitumor activity of CD8<sup>+</sup> T cells. In vivo, the combination of anti-PD-1 antibodies with cromolyn sodium or CCR4 antagonists yielded a synergistic antitumor effect, outperforming each agent used as monotherapy. Overall, these findings suggest that TAMCs drive immune suppression and confer resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy in HCC through CCL17/CCR4-mediated Treg recruitment.

title: Spiked Helmet Sign in the Early Post-Heart Transplantation Period: A Dramatic STEMI Mimic in a Structurally Normal Donor Heart.
authorString: Lima DRM, Segundo GSD, Targueta GP, Teixeira RTB, Meira AT, Athayde GAT.

journal.title: Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc

abstractText: A 36-year-old woman with severe dilated cardiomyopathy (LVEF 14%, NYHA IV) underwent heart transplantation. Postoperatively, she developed subarachnoid hemorrhage and septic shock. The ECG revealed a spiked helmet sign (SHS) pattern, with repolarization abnormalities and QT prolongation. Despite transient clinical improvement and resolution of the ECG changes after intensive support, the patient died due to infectious complications. This case highlights the occurrence of SHS in the early posttransplant period in a structurally normal donor heart, a previously unreported presentation, reinforcing its extracardiac origin and association with critical illness and poor prognosis.

title: Renin-Angiotensin System Activation Drives Early Cardiorenal Dysfunction in Normotensive Prediabetes.
authorString: Bakkar NZ, Ghazi R, Mougharbil N, Hammoud SH, Sabra R, Eid AH, El-Yazbi AF.
abstractText:
Introduction

Prediabetes is increasingly recognised as a stage at which cardiovascular and renal dysfunction begin to develop despite the absence of overt metabolic disease. The mechanisms underlying these early alterations remain poorly understood. Because adipose tissues surrounding blood vessels and kidneys can locally generate components of the renin-angiotensin system (RAS), we hypothesised that subclinical RAS activation contributes to early cardiorenal dysfunction in prediabetes.

Methods

Using a pre-established normotensive, non-obese rat model of prediabetes induced by 12 weeks of mild hypercaloric feeding, we examined the impact of systemic angiotensin II (AngII) elevation and angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibition on cardio-, cerebro- and renovascular function by invasive hemodynamics, ex vivo pressure myography, and ex vivo renal perfusion experiments, respectively.

Results

Prediabetic rats exhibited impaired parasympathetic baroreceptor sensitivity and altered renovascular endothelium-dependent vasodilation despite preserved blood pressure and cardiac function. Systemic AngII infusion further exacerbated autonomic and renovascular dysfunction. In contrast, treatment with a non-hypotensive dose of the ACE inhibitor captopril restored baroreceptor sensitivity, improved renovascular endothelial function, reduced brainstem inflammation, and attenuated renal tubular fibrosis. Examination of perivascular and perirenal adipose tissues revealed significantly higher protein concentration of ACE1 in prediabetic rats compared to controls.

Conclusion

These findings are consistent with an early activation of RAS contributing to subclinical cardiovascular and renal dysfunction during prediabetes independently of hypertension. Targeting RAS signalling at this early stage may therefore represent a strategy to limit progression of cardiorenal complications along the continuum from prediabetes to diabetes.

title: Teclistamab Induced a Profound Hematologic Response in Light Chain Deposition Disease With Probable Cardiac Involvement.
authorString: Xiong X, Zhao D, Li J, Shen K.
abstractText: We report the first case of using teclistamab, a BCMA × CD3 bispecific antibody, in a 63-year-old male with κ-light chain deposition disease (LCDD) involving the kidneys and probably the heart. The patient initially responded to daratumumab-pomalidomide-dexamethasone but experienced hematologic relapse. Salvage therapy with teclistamab induced a rapid and sustained hematologic complete response without cytokine release syndrome or neurotoxicity. Renal and cardiac functions remained stable. This case provides critical early evidence that BCMA-directed immunotherapy may serve as an effective salvage strategy for this rare plasma cell disorder, addressing a significant unmet therapeutic need.

title: No lysine? No problem: the surprising roles of WNK kinases in physiology and disease.
authorString: Jung JU, Jaykumar AB, Taylor CA, Cobb MH.
abstractText: WNK (With No lysine K) protein kinases gained early attention because gain-of-function mutations in genes encoding two of them cause hypertension. They differ from other kinases due to the unusual location of the catalytic lysine, hence the name WNK. These kinases control many aspects of ion transport in the kidney and are essential for development and maintenance of the cardiovascular system. In the present review, we describe WNK proteins and selected substrates, in particular, the kinases oxidative stress-responsive kinase 1 and SPS1-related proline/alanine-rich kinase, and their regulation. We spotlight findings that emphasize the broad relevance of WNKs in normal physiology and disease. Our overview focuses on basic aspects of ion transport that occur in many cell types and tissues, functions in the endothelial system, interactions with insulin-dependent and metabolic pathways, the importance in the brain in part through controlling chloride ion balance, and the whirlwind of findings in cancer that reveal how WNK signaling can be repurposed. Other actions that may be of equal importance, e.g., influences on the immune system, are touched on only briefly. We also note a few genome-wide association studies that have uncovered multiple SNPs in genes encoding WNKs and downstream effectors in an array of diseases, in anticipation of more to come in the future.

title: Fingerprinting the polycystic kidney: radiomics of the noncystic parenchyma for earlier ADPKD detection.
authorString: Kline TL.
abstractText: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease risk stratification relies on total kidney volume, a validated marker of cyst burden and progression. Kremer et al.'s pilot study used rapid breath-hold magnetic resonance fingerprinting with radiomics to evaluate noncystic renal parenchyma in children and young adults. Quantitative T1/T2 texture features distinguished autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease from controls independently of total kidney volume, cyst fraction, age, or body size, suggesting early tissue changes. Small, cross-sectional, unmatched data require longitudinal validation of reproducibility, prognostic value, and clinical utility.

title: Are we ready for the widespread application of transcutaneous measurement of the glomerular filtration rate?
authorString: Pieters TT, Besseling PJ, Joles JA.
abstractText: Accurate assessment of glomerular filtration rate is central to renal evaluation in clinical and preclinical settings. Transcutaneous glomerular filtration rate offers practical advantages over conventionally measured glomerular filtration rate, including minimally invasive and continuous monitoring, but requires robust validation. The observations by Shimada et al. highlight both the promise and limitations of transcutaneous glomerular filtration rate, particularly in conditions that affect distribution volume, underscoring the need for rigorous evaluation across diverse physiological and disease states.

title: Adiposity and the risk of aortic dissection incidence and mortality: results from the UK Biobank, the J-SHC study and a meta-analysis of cohort studies.
authorString: Dillman A, Otaki Y, Sanchez-Perez M, Irfan Khan MY, Hibino M, Konta T, Yamagata K, Fujimoto S, Tsuruya K, Narita I, Kasahara M, Shibagaki Y, Iseki K, Moriyama T, Kondo M, Asahi K, Watanabe T, Watanabe T, Watanabe M, Aune D.
abstractText: Few studies have investigated the association between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection and data is lacking on adiposity measures other than body mass index (BMI). We analyzed the association between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection in the UK Biobank, and the Japan Specific Health Checkups (J-SHC) Study, and conducted a meta-analysis of cohort studies to clarify the associations between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection. The analytical cohorts included 496,255 participants in the UK Biobank and 630,841 participants in the J-SHC Study. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to analyze associations between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection. PubMed and Embase were searched for relevant studies up to February 27, 2026. Random effects models were used to calculate summary relative risks (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the association between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection. In the UK Biobank and J-SHC, there were 371 and 105 aortic dissections during 12.3 and 4 years follow-up, respectively. In the UK Biobank, positive associations (HRs, 95% CIs) were observed between high BMI (1.54, 1.01-2.37, p<sub>trend</sub>=0.01), waist circumference (1.82, 1.27-2.60, p<sub>trend</sub>=0.001), hip circumference (1.77, 1.25-2.50, p<sub>trend</sub><0.001), waist-to-height ratio (1.88, 1.30-2.70, p<sub>trend</sub>=0.10), and fat mass (1.36, 0.97-1.91, p<sub>trend</sub>=0.02) and aortic dissection risk, but no clear association was observed for waist-to-hip ratio (1.28, 0.90-1.81, p<sub>trend</sub>=0.08) and body fat percentage (1.09, 0.77-1.54, p<sub>trend</sub>=0.53). In the J-SHC Study, higher BMI (2.36, 0.98-4.84, p<sub>trend</sub>=0.018), waist circumference (2.26, 1.18-4.60, p<sub>trend</sub>=0.003), and waist-to-height ratio (2.61, 1.27-5.92, p<sub>trend</sub>=0.009) were positively associated with aortic dissection mortality. Five cohort studies were included in the meta-analysis on BMI and aortic dissection (2007 cases and 4,962,288 participants). The summary RR per 5 kg/m<sup>2</sup> increment in BMI was 1.09 (1.00-1.20, I<sup>2</sup> = 43%), per 10 cm increment in waist circumference was 1.21 (1.05-1.40, I<sup>2</sup> = 50%, n = 2), and per 0.1 unit increment in waist-to-height ratio was 1.32 (1.08-1.61, I<sup>2</sup> = 39%, n = 2). These findings provide evidence for a positive association between both general and abdominal adiposity and the risk of aortic dissection, with the strongest associations observed for high waist-to-height ratio. Although further large-scale studies are warranted for confirmation, these findings suggest avoiding excess weight may be an important strategy for the prevention of aortic dissection.
