title: Cardioplegia.
authorString: Ghanem FK.
abstractText: "Cardioplegia" is a poem situated at the intersection of medicine, mortality, and human attachment. Drawing on the clinical language of cardiac surgery, the poem considers the paradox of deliberately arresting the heart in order to preserve life. Cardioplegia becomes both a physiological intervention and a metaphor for the ways human beings confront vulnerability, loss, and emotional suspension. By placing the technical vocabulary of medicine alongside the symbolic and intimate meanings attributed to the heart, the poem explores the tension between the heart as an organ and the heart as a site of memory, love, and grief. "Cardioplegia" seeks to illuminate how medical language can carry meanings beyond its clinical function and how poetic attention may create space for reflection on the lived and emotional dimensions of medicine.

title: Aspiration Thrombectomy for High-Risk Pulmonary Embolism With Life-Threatening Anemia and Active Uterine Bleeding: A Case Report.
authorString: Saoudi O, Wang B.

journal.title: The American journal of case reports

abstractText: BACKGROUND High-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) carries significant mortality, and management becomes complex when it coexists with severe anemia and active bleeding, as thrombolysis is then contraindicated. We report the case of a patient with high-risk PE complicated by severe anemia (hemoglobin 41 g/L) and active uterine bleeding from adenomyosis. CASE REPORT A 48-year-old woman presented with haemodynamic instability (blood pressure 74/47 mm Hg), critical anemia (hemoglobin 41 g/L), and a 3-year history of irregular vaginal bleeding from adenomyosis. Computed tomography (CT) pulmonary angiography confirmed bilateral PE with right pulmonary artery main-trunk occlusion; echocardiography showed severe pulmonary hypertension, and duplex ultrasound showed extensive left lower-limb deep vein thrombosis. Thrombolysis was contraindicated. Emergency percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy was performed using large-bore catheters (22F, 20F, 16F) with concurrent inferior vena cava filter placement, reducing pulmonary artery pressure from 51/23 to 34/12 mm Hg; the estimated blood loss, quantified from filtered aspirate, was approximately 100 mL. Adjuncts included transfusion of 13 units of packed red cells, dilatation and curettage, gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist therapy, and titrated anticoagulation. At discharge after a 24-day hospitalization she was hemodynamically stable, and free of dyspnea, with resolved edema and hemoglobin 72 g/L, on oral rivaroxaban. CONCLUSIONS In this thrombolysis-contraindicated patient, aspiration thrombectomy with inferior vena cava filter placement was a feasible rescue strategy that achieved rapid hemodynamic and angiographic improvement without thrombolysis, with palliative rather than curative intent. As a single case, it cannot establish comparative safety or efficacy, and broader conclusions regarding efficacy cannot be drawn. It illustrates a potentially useful approach in similarly complex scenarios where coordinated multidisciplinary care is essential.

title: Atorvastatin protects cardiomyocytes from doxorubicin toxicity by modulating YAP/TAZ signaling.
authorString: Lim H, Jin S, Lee CJ, Lim G, Park S, Lee SH, Oh J, Kang SM.
abstractText: Doxorubicin (DOX) is a widely used anthracycline chemotherapeutic agent; however, its clinical efficacy is hampered by dose-dependent cardiotoxicity, which can lead to irreversible heart failure. Despite extensive research, effective strategies for preventing or mitigating DOX-induced cardiac injury remain lacking. The Hippo signaling effectors, Yes-associated protein (YAP) and transcriptional co-activator with PDZ-binding motif (TAZ), are known to regulate cardiomyocyte survival, apoptosis, and mitochondrial quality control; however, their role in protecting the heart from DOX toxicity remains unclear. In this study, we investigated whether atorvastatin, a widely prescribed HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor with pleiotropic effects, attenuated DOX-induced cardiomyopathy by modulating the YAP/TAZ signaling axis. In H9c2 cardiomyocytes, DOX suppressed the expression of YAP and TAZ, leading to the downregulation of their downstream targets, Survivin and Park2, and activation of apoptotic cascades. Atorvastatin pretreatment restored YAP/TAZ expression at both mRNA and protein levels and reversed DOX-induced apoptosis. RNA interference-mediated knockdown of YAP or TAZ abolished the protective effects of atorvastatin, confirming the importance of this pathway. In a murine model of DOX cardiotoxicity, atorvastatin preserved left ventricular systolic function, reduced myocardial apoptosis and fibrosis, and restored YAP/TAZ, Survivin, and Park2 expression in the cardiac tissue. These findings suggest that atorvastatin exerts cardioprotective effects by restoring YAP/TAZ-mediated anti-apoptotic and mitochondrial quality control signaling. Our study highlights a novel mechanism via which atorvastatin mitigates DOX-induced cardiotoxicity and supports the therapeutic potential of YAP/TAZ modulation for cardioprotection.

title: Exercise for Older People with Heart Failure and Frailty: Should We Even Try?
authorString: Krishnan S, Goddard ACN, Annals M, Squire IB, Sze S.
abstractText: The benefits of exercise in older patients with heart failure (HF) and frailty are twofold: (i) improvement in cardiopulmonary capacity, thus reducing HF-related sequelae; (ii) attenuation of decline in physical function, thus improving frailty status. Despite the clear benefits, exercise training (ET) remains underutilised as a treatment modality in this patient population. Guidelines on the specific type of exercise intervention best suited for this population are still lacking. In this review, we discuss (i) pathophysiology underlying exercise intolerance in patients with HF; (ii) impact of frailty on HF and exercise capacity; (iii) benefits and safety of ET; (iv) recommended ET programme for this population; (v) mode of delivery and (vi) potential barriers in the uptake of ET and strategies to overcome them. An effective ET intervention in this population warrants individualisation to patient's physical capacity, while addressing possible barriers to uptake so as to ensure sustained participation in the programme.

title: Multidomain Autonomic Dysfunction assessed with COMPASS-31 among patients with type 2 diabetes in Zanzibar: prevalence and associated factors.
authorString: Haji HT, Ali RM, Khamis AG, Ramaiya K, Munseri P, Mashili FL.
abstractText:
Background

Autonomic dysfunction is an important but frequently under-recognized complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), particularly in settings where objective autonomic testing is not routinely available. The Composite Autonomic Symptom Score-31 (COMPASS-31) provides a practical symptom-based approach for assessing autonomic dysfunction across multiple domains. This study compared socioeconomic, lifestyle, and clinical characteristics among adults with T2DM in Zanzibar according to COMPASS-31-defined autonomic dysfunction and examined factors associated with its presence.

Methods

This hospital-based cross-sectional study included 665 adults with T2DM attending the diabetes clinic at Mnazi Mmoja Hospital, Zanzibar. Autonomic symptoms were assessed using COMPASS-31, including the orthostatic intolerance, gastrointestinal, and bladder domains. Participants were classified as having autonomic dysfunction when they met the prespecified threshold for dysfunction in at least one assessed domain. Cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy (CAN) was assessed separately using standardized cardiovascular autonomic reflex tests performed with an automated CAN Analyzer and was not included in the COMPASS-31 composite outcome. Modified Poisson regression with robust variance estimation was used to calculate adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

Results

Overall, 309 participants (46.5%) had COMPASS-31-defined autonomic dysfunction. Orthostatic intolerance was the most common domain, affecting 271 participants (40.8%), followed by gastrointestinal dysfunction in 177 (26.6%) and urinary dysfunction in 123 (18.5%). Separately, 305 participants (45.9%) met the analyzer-based criteria for CAN. In the multivariable analysis, autonomic dysfunction was more prevalent among participants without a family history of diabetes (aPR = 1.37, 95% CI: 1.16-1.61; p < 0.001), those with diabetes duration of ≥ 10 years (aPR = 1.45, 95% CI: 1.14-1.75; p < 0.001), those not using oral hypoglycemic agents (aPR = 1.66, 95% CI: 1.39-1.97; p < 0.001), and those who rarely consumed vegetables or consumed one portion per day (aPR = 1.79, 95% CI: 1.37-2.34; p < 0.001).

Conclusion

Approximately half of the adults with T2DM in this tertiary-care population had COMPASS-31-defined autonomic dysfunction. Higher prevalence was associated with no family history of diabetes, longer diabetes duration, non-use of oral hypoglycemic agents, and lower vegetable intake. These findings highlight the potential value of symptom-based autonomic assessment and support further prospective research to better understand the clinical and lifestyle factors associated with autonomic dysfunction among adults with T2DM in Zanzibar.

title: Association between urinary heavy metal(loid)s exposure and dyslipidemia in children from e-waste dismantling areas.
authorString: Sun R, Qu S, Chen J, Kang R, Zhang J, Xu X, Tan L, Huo X.

journal.title: Biometals : an international journal on the role of metal ions in biology, biochemistry, and medicine

abstractText: To assess temporal trends of urinary heavy metal(loid)s burden and lipid levels, and explore the single and joint associations of heavy metal(loid)s exposure with lipid profiles among children in Guiyu, a typical e-waste dismantling area in China. Based on 2016 and 2024 surveys in Guiyu, 197 children (aged 3-7) were enrolled. Urinary concentrations of 13 heavy metal(loid)s were determined using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). Serum lipid parameters including total cholesterol (TC), triglycerides (TG), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) were measured, and non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (non-HDL-C) was calculated. To investigate the independent and combined associations between metals and blood lipid profiles, multiple linear regression and Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR) models were employed. Urinary concentrations of Chromium (Cr), Nickel (Ni), Copper (Cu), Cadmium (Cd), and Lead (Pb) in 2024 were significantly lower than those in 2016 (all P < 0.05). In adjusted models, Manganese (Mn), Cobalt (Co), Cd, and Pb were positively associated with TC and non-HDL-C, while Cd and Pb were negatively associated with HDL-C (all P < 0.05). BKMR confirmed a significant joint positive effect of a 12-metal mixture on TC and non-HDL-C, and a negative effect on HDL-C. Despite decreased individual metal levels over the eight-year interval, the biological risk from co‑exposure to these metals remains a critical concern These findings highlight the need for vigilance regarding the synergistic cardiovascular toxicity of heavy metals on pediatric lipid homeostasis.

title: A Web-Based Registry Framework Linking Transfusion Practice to Long-Term Patient Outcomes: Design and Single-Center Feasibility Study.
authorString: Nürenberg-Goloub E, Friedrichson B, Nordine M, Storf H, Zacharowski K, Kloka JA.
abstractText: Blood transfusions are among the most common medical interventions performed worldwide. Several comprehensive databases link transfusions to routinely collected health data but do not include the indication and the decision-making basis for a particular administration, nor patient-reported long-term outcomes. We developed a web-based registry for the standardized assessment of transfusion practice and patient outcomes, designed for an observation period of up to 30 years. The framework combines clinical data captured at the point of care with patient-reported outcome measures collected through automated digital follow-up, ensures privacy by design through physical separation of identifying and medical data, and codes diagnoses and procedures in SNOMED CT. We evaluated feasibility in a single-center pilot at Goethe University Hospital Frankfurt (11 September 2024-15 January 2026), with patient-reported follow-up collected through 13 August 2026. A total of 408 patients were enrolled, yielding 1,298 administrations across nine treatment categories in a predominantly cardiac surgical cohort. The pilot demonstrated that the registry integrates into routine clinical workflows, captures the parameters required for guideline-adherence monitoring, and supports sex-disaggregated, descriptive analyses of transfusion practice. Follow-up was completed by 12.5% of patients at 3 months and 15.2% of patients at 1 year; paired baseline-follow-up assessments of physical capacity and frailty demonstrate the data structure for capturing functional recovery. Risk-adjusted benchmarking, network-wide analyses, and donor outcomes are designed capabilities of the framework that were not evaluated in this pilot. The platform is available in 16 languages and participation is open to further institutions.

title: Context-dependent vascular effects of platycodin D: inhibition of neointima formation but aggravation of atherosclerosis with involvement of mTORC1 signaling.
authorString: Yan BJ, Belke D, Chen YX, Zheng XL.
abstractText: Platycodin D (PD), a triterpenoid saponin from Platycodon grandiflorus, has been reported to have cardiovascular activity, but its actions in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) and atherosclerosis remain unclear. We integrated network pharmacology, molecular docking, 100-ns molecular dynamics simulation, VSMC assays, and two mouse carotid models. In VSMCs cultured under basal conditions, PD reduced viability and BrdU incorporation, downregulated cyclin D1/E1, and induced TUNEL positivity and cleaved caspase-3. At the cellular level, PD activated mTORC1-associated signaling, increased p70S6K and eIF2α phosphorylation, increased ATF4 protein and activated ATF6, impaired autophagic flux, and induced CHOP-associated endoplasmic reticulum stress. Rapamycin and 4-phenylbutyric acid attenuated PD-induced apoptosis, whereas MHY1485 and thapsigargin exacerbated it. Perivascular PD reduced neointimal hyperplasia after complete carotid ligation in C57BL/6J mice. In contrast, PD accelerated early carotid atherosclerosis after partial ligation in ApoE<sup>-/-</sup> mice fed a high-fat diet. Under ox-LDL challenge, PD increased VSMC lipid accumulation, Olr1/Cd36 expression, mTORC1-p70S6K signaling, and BrdU incorporation; rapamycin limited these effects. These findings suggest that PD activates an mTORC1-associated stress program whose vascular outcome depends on lipid and flow context. PD may have local anti-neointimal potential but warrants caution in hyperlipidemic atherosclerosis.

title: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus and lupus nephritis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Suruagy-Motta RFO, Canuto AMG, Ferreira BMV, Carvalho BCP, Nogueira CFSC, Firmino MMR, Souza-Carvalho JA, Martinez D, Costa AFP, Figueroa MLCO.
abstractText: IntroductionSystemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) and lupus nephritis (LN) carry substantial cardiorenal risks. Conventional immunosuppressive therapies primarily target inflammation but leave a burden of residual renal and metabolic damage. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) provide clear cardiorenal protection in general populations, but data specific to SLE remains limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of SGLT2i in patients with SLE and LN.MethodsComprehensive searches across five electronic databases (PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, Embase, and Scopus) were conducted up to April 2026 to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies assessing SGLT2i in adult SLE/LN patients. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to synthesize cardiorenal and safety outcomes using R Software.ResultsSix studies published between 2024 and 2025 were included. Pooled data demonstrated that SGLT2i use was associated with a significant improvement in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) compared to controls (MD: 4.02; 95% CI: 1.39-6.65; I<sup>2</sup> = 60.1%). SGLT2i significantly reduced the risks of progression to end-stage kidney disease (RR: 0.37; 95% CI: 0.25-0.56; I<sup>2</sup> = 11.0%), heart failure development (RR: 0.65; 95% CI: 0.56-0.75; I<sup>2</sup> = 0.0%), incident lupus nephritis (RR: 0.58; 95% CI: 0.44-0.76; I<sup>2</sup> = 0.0%), and re-hospitalizations (RR: 0.67; 95% CI: 0.57-0.79; I<sup>2</sup> = 0.0%). Furthermore, a significant reduction in all-cause mortality was observed (RR: 0.55; 95% CI: 0.36-0.86; I<sup>2</sup> = 76.2%). SGLT2i treatment demonstrated an acceptable safety profile across the included cohorts. The certainty of evidence for these findings was rated as low to very low, and results remain vulnerable to residual confounding from variables such as disease activity, corticosteroid burden, and immunosuppressive regimen.ConclusionPreliminary exploratory evidence suggests potential associations between SGLT2 inhibitors and cardiorenal outcomes in lupus nephritis. Given the low certainty of evidence and vulnerability to residual confounding from disease-specific variables, these hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in well-designed randomized controlled trials.

title: Finerenone: A Non-Steroidal Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonist and Its Emerging Role in Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome.
authorString: Fischer KG, Beavers CJ.
abstractText: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome represents the interconnected pathophysiology of metabolic risk factors, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and cardiovascular disease, leading to multiorgan dysfunction and elevated adverse outcomes. Overactivation of the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR), via aldosterone-dependent and ligand-independent pathways, drives inflammation, fibrosis, and oxidative stress and facilitates CKM progression. Finerenone is a selective non-steroidal MR antagonist (nsMRA) that exhibits high MR affinity, has balanced cardiac and renal distribution, and minimal off-target steroidal effects, which make it mechanistically different from steroidal MRAs. Large phase 3 trials such as FIDELIO-DKD and FIGARO-DKD in type 2 diabetes with CKD, and FINEARTS-HF in heart failure (HF) with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) > 40%, demonstrated consistent cardiorenal benefits. The prespecified FINE-HEART pooled analysis showed finerenone reduced all-cause mortality (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.84-0.99), HF hospitalizations (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.75-0.92), and the kidney composite outcome (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.72-0.90), with benefits consistent across CKM components and background therapies including sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors. Recent data from FIND-CKD extend utility to non-diabetic CKD. Various guidelines incorporate finerenone as an additive therapy for patients with persistent albuminuria on maximal renin-angiotensin system inhibition (RASi) + SGLT2i. This review summarizes the MR pathophysiology in CKM syndrome, compares the mechanisms of non-steroidal versus steroidal MRAs, synthesizes clinical trial evidence, safety, and guideline-directed place in therapy, addresses implementation barriers, including cost, and outlines future research directions. Finerenone may fill a critical gap in multimodal CKM management, enabling comprehensive pillar-based therapy to mitigate residual cardiorenal risk.

title: Tirzepatide for Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Trial Evidence, Cardiometabolic Effects, and Implications for Cardiovascular Practice.
authorString: Arslan FS, Ahmad R, Frishman WH, Aronow WS.
abstractText: Obstructive sleep apnea affects approximately one billion adults worldwide and is associated with hypertension, atrial fibrillation, heart failure, and stroke. Obesity is its dominant reversible cause, yet positive airway pressure therapy splints the pharyngeal airway without addressing the adiposity that narrows it, and randomized trials have not shown that it reduces cardiovascular events. In December 2024, the United States Food and Drug Administration approved tirzepatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, as the first drug for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity. We summarize the pharmacology of tirzepatide and the anatomic basis by which weight reduction improves upper airway patency, notably reduction of tongue and parapharyngeal fat. We then review the SURMOUNT-OSA program: two parallel 52-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials enrolling 469 adults with obesity and an apnea-hypopnea index of at least 15 events per hour, one conducted without positive airway pressure and one during established positive airway pressure use. Tirzepatide reduced the apnea-hypopnea index by an estimated 20.0 and 23.8 events per hour relative to placebo, with concurrent reductions in sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden, body weight, systolic blood pressure, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein.

title: Sacubitril/Valsartan for Breast Cancer Therapy-Related Cardiac Dysfunction: An Integrated Meta-Analysis and Bioinformatics Study
authorString: Zhong R, Lin Q, Huang H, Cheng X.
abstractText: Background Sacubitril/valsartan has proven efficacy in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, but its role in breast cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) remains unclear. We evaluated its efficacy and therapeutic targets via integrated meta-analysis and bioinformatics. Methods We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, Web of Science, and CNKI for sacubitril/valsartan studies in breast cancer CTRCD and performed meta-analysis. Candidate targets from network pharmacology were intersected with GEO differentially expressed genes; LASSO and SVM-RFE identified core targets. Two-sample Mendelian randomization assessed causality, and molecular docking verified binding. Results The meta-analysis included 7 studies (n = 409). In patients with established CTRCD, sacubitril/valsartan treatment significantly improved LVEF from baseline (MD = 5.27, 95% CI: 1.35–9.20, P = 0.008) and reduced NT-proBNP (MD=-2323.96, 95% CI: -4370.12 to -277.79, P = 0.03); in those with normal baseline cardiac function, LVEF also improved (MD = 1.30, 95% CI: 0.04–2.56, P = 0.04), and the incidence of CTRCD decreased (RR = 0.11, 95% CI: 0.01–0.93, P = 0.04). Mechanistically, machine learning identified 9 core therapeutic targets from 141 candidate targets. Mendelian randomization suggested causal associations of PIK3CG (OR = 0.88, 95% CI: 0.81–0.97, P = 0.006) and KEAP1 (OR = 1.12, 95% CI: 1.01–1.24, P = 0.028) with heart failure as a clinical endpoint of CTRCD. Molecular docking showed binding energies between sacubitril/valsartan and the above targets ranging from − 5.7 to -10.0 kcal/mol. Conclusions Sacubitril/valsartan improves cardiac function in both therapeutic and preventive settings of breast cancer CTRCD, with PIK3CG and KEAP1 as potential cardioprotective targets. Functional experiments and larger randomized trials are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Oral Versus Injectable Incretin-Based Anti-Obesity Therapies: An Integrated Computational and Evidence-Based Comparison of Orforglipron, Semaglutide, and Tirzepatide.
authorString: Sahu L, Nayak L, Tripathy A, Ramachandiran S, Gunasekaran B, Lokaiah T.

journal.title: Omics : a journal of integrative biology

abstractText: Incretin-based agents are transforming obesity pharmacotherapy, and orforglipron, the first oral non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist to complete phase 3 testing, invites direct comparison with the injectable agents semaglutide and tirzepatide. We integrated clinical trial evidence, including the direct head-to-head SURMOUNT-5 trial, independently verified molecular descriptors, a fully specified drug-target-disease network with permutation-tested hub significance, hypergeometric pathway enrichment, and multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) across four weighting schemes with formal sensitivity analysis. Tirzepatide produced significantly greater weight loss than semaglutide under randomized, head-to-head conditions (20.2% vs. 13.7% at week 72) and ranked highest under balanced, efficacy-, and safety-dominant MCDA models once a composite ADMET score misapplied to two large peptides was removed. Orforglipron's lipophilicity exceeds the Lipinski ceiling, showing that its oral absorption reflects deliberate chemistry rather than default small-molecule developability; it nonetheless ranked highest under an accessibility-dominant model driven by oral feasibility and manufacturing scalability. These rankings were stable under Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis for three of four weighting schemes, with the balanced model comparatively fragile. Tirzepatide's cardiovascular evidence has also advanced, with SURPASS-CVOT reporting non-inferiority to dulaglutide. No single agent dominates every criterion; treatment selection should match the clinical priority the individual patient weights most heavily.

title: Later-line Treatment Selection in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer: Trifluridine/Tipiracil Plus Bevacizumab, Regorafenib, and Fruquintinib.
authorString: Sagawa T, Hirakawa M, Nagashima H, Fujikawa K.
abstractText: Later-line therapy for metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) increasingly requires selection among treatments with different mechanisms, toxicity profiles, and sequencing evidence. Trifluridine/tipiracil plus bevacizumab has robust randomized evidence from SUNLIGHT, but objective response remains uncommon and hematologic toxicity can limit treatment delivery in heavily pretreated patients. Regorafenib and fruquintinib are minimally myelosuppressive oral alternatives, yet they differ in dose strategy, hepatotoxicity, hand-foot skin reaction, hypertension, and proteinuria. This narrative review updates pivotal and recent evidence and proposes an evidence-informed framework that treats hematologic reserve as a clinical fitness construct rather than a fixed laboratory threshold. We additionally examine the clinical implications of low response rates, prior anti-angiogenic exposure, emerging molecular predictors including KRAS G12, evidence in older or vulnerable patients, and recent phase III developments. Current data do not support a validated molecular biomarker for choosing among these three options, and no randomized head-to-head comparison of regorafenib and fruquintinib exists. Accordingly, treatment selection should be individualized according to prior therapies, toxicity vulnerability, organ function, tumor tempo, and patient goals. Hypertension and proteinuria are important selection factors but may also be modifiable treatment-delivery factors. The proposed algorithms and adverse-event radar chart are intended as practical visual syntheses rather than validated guidelines or formal cross-trial comparisons.

title: Dietary strategies to combat arterial stiffness in cardiometabolic disease: a network <i>meta</i>-analysis.
authorString: Norouzzadeh M, HasanRashedi M, Afrashteh S, Emamat H.
abstractText: Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) and hypertension (HTN) are leading causes of global morbidity and mortality. Arterial stiffness, assessed via augmentation index (AIx) and pulse wave velocity (PWV), serves as an independent prognostic marker of vascular damage; however, the comparative efficacy of dietary interventions on these parameters remains poorly characterized. This network meta-analysis (NMA) aimed to compare and rank the efficacy of dietary interventions, including supplements, nutraceuticals, and dietary patterns, on AIx and PWV in individuals with CVD or HTN. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched for eligible randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published up to January 2025. Two independent reviewers screened and extracted data following PRISMA-NMA guidelines. A total of 48 RCTs comprising 2719 participants and 31 dietary interventions were included. Study quality and certainty of evidence (CoE) were assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool and GRADE approach, respectively. A random-effects NMA within a frequentist framework estimated mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). For PWV, grape seed extract (MD: -1.70; 95%CI: -3.36 to -0.04; CoE: Moderate) and vitamin B9 (MD: -1.46; 95%CI: -2.61 to -0.31; CoE: Moderate) reduced arterial stiffness versus placebo. No intervention reached significance for AIx, though alpha-linolenic acid, dietary nitrate, and wine extract showed the greatest numerical improvements. Sensitivity analyses yielded results consistent with the primary analyses, with no publication bias detected. The grape seed extract and folic acid show potential to reduce arterial stiffness. Future population-specific, dose-optimized RCTs are warranted to establish definitive therapeutic recommendations.

title: VERINA: A Phase IV Prospective Multicenter Study of Vericiguat in Indian Patients with Worsening Heart Failure and Reduced Ejection Fraction.
authorString: Seth S, Abhyankar A, Abdullakutty J, Banerjee S, Sharma K, Vijan V, Bhalani NC, Chopra VK, Aggarwal RK, Oomman A, Bansal S, Jain RK, Kahale P, Sodhi P, Gupta D, Gawde A.
abstractText:
Introduction

Patients with heart failure (HF) with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) remain at high risk of cardiovascular (CV) death and hospitalization following a worsening heart-failure event. Data on vericiguat, a prescription oral medication used to treat symptomatic chronic HF, in adult Indian patients are limited.

Methods

Adults with chronic HFrEF and a worsening heart-failure event were enrolled in a prospective, multicenter, open-label, single-arm phase IV study design. Participants received vericiguat in addition to foundational medical therapy (FMT) and were followed for approximately 48 weeks. The primary endpoint was CV death or first hospitalization for HF. Secondary endpoints included CV death, first hospitalization for HF, all-cause death or first hospitalization for HF, all-cause death and safety outcomes.

Results

Of 231 patients who underwent screening, 205 received vericiguat and comprised the safety analysis set; of these, 203 patients constituted the full analysis set. The mean age of participants was 58 years. Baseline use of angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors was 52.7% and 75.6%, respectively. At week 48, Kaplan-Meier (KM) estimates were 10.1% for the primary endpoint, 3.3% for CV death, 9.1% for first hospitalization for HF, 11.5% for all-cause death or first hospitalization for HF, and 5.9% for all-cause death. Attainment of the target dose was 91.6%, with 69.5% of participants reaching and maintaining 10 mg by week 4. Study drug-related adverse events (AEs) were reported in 3.4% of participants, and treatment-emergent AEs requiring discontinuation in 2.0% of participants.

Conclusion

In Indian patients with worsening HFrEF, high target-dose attainment and no new safety signals were observed during 48 weeks of vericiguat treatment.

Trial registration

Clinical Trials Registry-India: CTRI/2022/11/047636.

title: Safety outcomes of semaglutide by chronic kidney disease severity in the FLOW trial.
authorString: Tuttle KR, Andersen MR, Arici M, Arslan EG, Bellary S, Idorn T, Ji L, Kamenov Z, Kashihara N, Mahaffey KW, Mann JFE, Perkovic V, Rasmussen S, Rossing P, Schytz PA, Sreenivasamurthy L, Pratley RE.
abstractText: People with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) often experience medication intolerance and side effects that worsen with lower estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). This prespecified secondary analysis assessed the safety of semaglutide by baseline eGFR. FLOW (NCT03819153) was a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial testing the efficacy of subcutaneous semaglutide 1.0 mg once-weekly on a primary kidney outcome (50% or more eGFR reduction, kidney failure, or death due to kidney or cardiovascular causes) in participants with T2D and CKD. Safety data were collected selectively and included serious adverse events (SAEs), AEs leading to treatment discontinuation, and prespecified AEs of special interest (AESIs). In this descriptive assessment, systematically collected safety data were reported numerically by baseline eGFR. Of 3533 participants, 1767 received semaglutide and 1766 received placebo. Fewer SAEs were reported with semaglutide than placebo across baseline eGFR subgroups (45.1% versus 50.4% in the 60 or more ml/min per 1.73 m2 subgroup, and 56.4% versus 60.4% in the under 30 ml/min per 1.73 m2 subgroup). SAEs related to infections and infestations; cardiac disorders; respiratory, thoracic and mediastinal disorders; and metabolism and nutrition disorders were generally less frequent with semaglutide than placebo, regardless of baseline eGFR. Treatment discontinuations due to AEs were higher with lower baseline eGFR across treatment groups (60 or more ml/min per 1.73 m2: semaglutide 11.2%, placebo 11.3%; under30 ml/min per 66 1.73 m2: semaglutide 18.8%, placebo 18.7%). Discontinuations specifically due to gastrointestinal AEs were reported more frequently with semaglutide (4.5%) than placebo (1.1%), regardless of baseline eGFR. Frequencies of AESI were similar between treatment groups across baseline eGFR subgroups. In this safety assessment, SAEs were reported less frequently with semaglutide than placebo, with corresponding patterns observed for treatment discontinuations and AESIs. No unexpected safety concerns were identified across the spectrum of eGFR represented in the FLOW trial.

title: A study using the REIN registry suggests a statin therapy benefits for secondary prevention in patients receiving dialysis.
authorString: Letourneau P, Koppe L, Couchoud C, Laville SM, Gavoille A, Nourredine M, REIN Collaborators.
abstractText: While statins are effective for cardiovascular prevention in the general population, their benefit in patients with CKD G5D (kidney failure treated by dialysis) remains uncertain. Previous randomized controlled trials included mixed populations for primary and secondary prevention while excluding patients with recent cardiovascular events, leaving a knowledge gap regarding statin effectiveness for secondary prevention immediately following an atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) event. Here, we address this gap by providing real-world evidence. We conducted a landmark-based observational study, informed by the target trial framework using the French Renal Epidemiology and Information Network (REIN) registry and merged with data from the French national healthcare system database from 2010 to 2023. We included adults with CKD G5D who experienced an ASCVD event. We used inverse probability of treatment weighting to balance baseline characteristics between statin initiators and non-initiators, thereby estimating the average causal effect on all-cause mortality. Results focus on the relative and absolute risk difference and the life expectancy gain using delta restricted mean survival time (dRMST). The study cohort included 5534 patients (median age: 75 years; 67% male). During the ten years of follow-up, statin use was associated with a reduced risk of mortality. The survival curves reached a maximum absolute difference at year four (risk difference -6.2% (95% CI: -10.2; -2.2); relative risk 0.88 [95% CI: 0.81; 0.96]). Life expectancy extended significantly over time with a mean survival gain of 69 days at five years (95% CI: 14-125) and reaching 135 days at ten years (95% CI: 31-239). No difference was identified between groups regarding hospitalizations for rhabdomyolysis or toxic hepatitis. In patients receiving dialysis, statin initiation following an ASCVD event is safe and associated with a modest-to-moderate ten-year cumulative survival benefit. While interpreted within observational limitations, this real-world evidence supports their use in this secondary prevention setting.

title: Study protocol of a prospective, non-interventional cohort study evaluating the benefits of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma receiving first-line atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (NISTIPS TRITICC-4, IKF092).
authorString: Angendohr C, Weigel C, Kunstein A, Joerdens M, Goetze T, Al-Batran SE, Zäpf B, Gonzalez-Carmona M, Sahin C, Berres ML, Foerster F, Ben Khaled N, Koch C, Kandulski A, Wege H, Trebicka J, Jochheim LS, Dill MT, Springfeld C, Daum S, Treese C, Ehmer U, Luedde T, Bode J, Roderburg C.
abstractText:
Background

Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with most patients diagnosed at an advanced stage. Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab is a current standard first-line therapy; however, outcomes are strongly influenced by underlying cirrhosis and clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH). Complications such as ascites and variceal bleeding may limit treatment continuation, particularly as bevacizumab increases bleeding risk. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) reduces portal pressure and may improve outcomes, but its role in patients receiving immunoncology-based systemic therapy remains unclear.

Methods

NISTIPS TRITICC-4 is a prospective, multicentre, non-interventional cohort study conducted at up to 25 centers in Germany. A total of 350 adult patients with cirrhosis and unresectable or metastatic HCC receiving first-line atezolizumab plus bevacizumab will be enrolled. Patients are allocated to two cohorts: TIPS in situ plus atezolizumab and bevacizumab or atezolizumab plus bevacizumab alone, according to routine clinical practice.The primary endpoint is time to deterioration of liver function (TTDL), defined as persistent worsening of liver parameters for >4 weeks. Secondary endpoints include overall survival, time on treatment, overall response rate, time to new extrahepatic lesions or death, and safety with focus on bleeding and TIPS-related complications.Time-to-event endpoints will be analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox models. Propensity score matching will be applied to adjust for confounding. Analyses are exploratory.

Discussion

This study will provide real-world evidence on the impact of TIPS in HCC patients receiving atezolizumab plus bevacizumab and may support more individualized management strategies in this high-risk population.

Clinical trial registration

www.clinicaltrials.gov identifier is NCT07365930.

title: Outcome measures and monitoring framework in juvenile systemic sclerosis: bridging routine care and clinical trials.
authorString: Foeldvari I, Marrani E.
abstractText:
Introduction

Juvenile systemic sclerosis (jSSc) is an orphan multisystem autoimmune disease that can cause significant morbidity during childhood and can lead to significant worsening of quality of life. The pathophysiological features are identical with adult-onset systemic sclerosis (SSc), jSSc exhibits a distinct clinical phenotype characterized by a significantly higher prevalence of diffuse cutaneous involvement, frequent overlap syndromes, distinct autoantibody profiles, and different long-term survival trajectories. Historically, the evaluation of jSSc has relied heavily on the extrapolation of adult outcome measures, which fail to account for developmental physiology, somatic growth, and pediatric-specific feasibility constraints.

Areas covered

This review provides a comprehensive overview of indicators of disease activity and severity which might be used in daily clinical practice and adapted as outcome measures in future clinical trials. It includes global outcome measures, organ-specific outcomes (including skin, pulmonary, cardiac, gastrointestinal, musculoskeletal, renal, and vascular involvement), patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), and clinician-reported outcomes (ClinROs). The performance of adult indices within pediatric cohorts are evaluated, if applicable. Additionally, we analyze severity scores like the Juvenile Systemic Sclerosis Severity Score (J4S) alongside modern consensus metrics derived from the international Hamburg symposia. We emphasize the integration of pediatric-adapted clinical assessments, quantitative imaging, and patient and physician related outcomes.

Expert opinion

The development of outcome measure in jSSc requires a paradigm shift from static severity scores to dynamic, multi-dimensional indicators capable of differentiating reversible inflammatory activity from potential permanent damage accrual. Validating pediatric-specific thresholds for physiological and cutaneous change remains an urgent priority. Over the next decade, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven quantitative imaging, decentralized home-based digital health tools, and molecular biomarkers probably will gain an essential role to optimize clinical trial readiness and personalize therapeutic strategies for children with systemic sclerosis.

Clinical trial number

Not applicable.

title: Association Between Capnographic Changes During Pulse Checks of Varying Durations and Clinical Outcomes During Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation: A Multicenter Study From Türkiye (CaPTuRe).
authorString: Yılmaz G, Özer MR, Köylü R, Bora ES, Aksu ŞH, Arıkan C, Çekmen B, Ataş İ, İnan G, Arslan M, Bol O, Demir O, Şahin N, Şahin H, Erdoğan A, Demir HA, Küçükceran K, Ayrancı MK, Akıllı NB, Güler EE, Sönmez BM, Tarhan A, Ersunan G, Bilir Ö, Baykan N, Toker İ, Çelik A, Hür İ, Gönüllü H, Bekfelavi A, Kadıoğlu E, Can O, Aktaş İ.
abstractText: To investigate the association between capnographic changes during pulse checks of different durations and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) outcomes. This multicenter, prospective, controlled, quasi-randomized study categorized patients according to pulse check duration: Group A (≤5 seconds) and Group B (>5 to ≤10 seconds). Five measurements were obtained during the first six CPR cycles. Four capnographic parameters were evaluated for each measurement: Post-CPR end-tidal carbon dioxide (ETCO2), Pre-CPR ETCO2, loss rate (percentage decrease between Post- and Pre-CPR ETCO2), and recovery time (time required to regain the previous cycle's Post-CPR ETCO2). The study included 252 cardiac arrest patients (Group A, n=124; Group B, n=128). In Group A, patients with return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) had markedly lower loss rates and shorter recovery times than non-survivors, together with higher pre- and post-CPR ETCO2 values (all p<0.001). Group A also had a higher ROSC rate than Group B (36.3% vs. 19.5%; p=0.005). Logistic regression identified pulse check duration as an independent predictor of ROSC, with Group A having 2.39-fold higher odds of ROSC than Group B (odds ratio [OR]=2.39, 95% confidence interval [CI]=1.347-4.242; p=0.003). Pre-CPR ETCO2 was strongly negatively correlated with loss rate (ρ=-0.770), whereas Pre- and Post-CPR ETCO2 values (ρ=0.96) and loss rate and recovery time (ρ=0.89) were strongly positively correlated. Pulse checks completed within 5 seconds were associated with more favorable capnographic dynamics and higher ROSC rates than those lasting 6-10 seconds. These findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant prospective validation.

title: A Recipe for Better Diabetes Management: The DASH4D Dietary Pattern.
authorString: Selvin E, Sullivan V, Yeh HC, Fang M, Pilla S, Mitchell C, Appel L, Rebholz C.
abstractText: The 2026 American Diabetes Association "Standards of Care in Diabetes" includes extensive nutrition recommendations for people with diabetes but stops short of recommending a specific dietary pattern. Instead, the guidelines recommend that all patients be referred for individualized nutrition therapy. This approach appropriately acknowledges diverse patient needs; however, it is difficult for providers to deliver any form of individualized dietary guidance without a clear starting point to guide them. In this article we examine the tension between the needs for individualization and evidence-based nutritional standards in diabetes care. We argue that the DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) dietary pattern stands out as being supported by decades of evidence from rigorous randomized clinical trials, meta-analyses, and large observational studies that have established its benefit for cardiovascular health. We summarize the recently completed DASH for Diabetes (DASH4D) trial, which demonstrated that a modified version of the original DASH eating plan, adapted for adults with diabetes, significantly reduced blood pressure and improved glycemic control in participants with type 2 diabetes and hypertension. We conclude that while individualized dietary counseling remains the standard of care, the DASH4D diet should be a recommended diet for patients with diabetes.

title: Cardiac unloading via a transvalvular pump prevents arrhythmias following myocardial ischemia / reperfusion by preserving coronary microcirculation and cardiomyocyte nanostructure
authorString: Ammon M, Melo PH, Nowak K, Nuovo G, Granada JF, Burkhoff D, Kaluza GL, Kyrollos AA, Curran J, Unudurthi SD, Veeraraghavan R.
abstractText: Cardiac damage in the aftermath of myocardial ischemia / reperfusion (MI/R) compromises both electrical and mechanical function, predisposing patients to arrhythmia and heart failure. Microvascular obstruction (MVO) is increasingly recognized as a sequela of MI/R and a contributor to proarrhythmic cardiac remodeling. While transvalvular unloading (TVU) using a percutaneously delivered pump is garnering appreciation as a means of limiting infarct size and preserving mechanical function following percutaneous coronary intervention, its benefits for arrhythmia prevention remain unclear. We used a porcine model to test the hypothesis that cardiac unloading prior to and through reperfusion mitigates MVO, preserves cardiomyocyte nanostructure, and alleviates arrhythmias following MI/R. Anesthetized domestic swine undergoing acute ischemia (LAD occlusion, 90 mins) and reperfusion (120 mins) were randomized to TVU (n=5) and no treatment (control; n=6) treatments. Thioflavin-S was infused into the mid-LAD to assess coronary microcirculation and quantify MVO. Arrhythmia burden was assessed by in vivo electrocardiography using 3 lead EKG. Cardiac tissues were preserved for histology and optical microscopy studies. Compared to no treatment controls, TVU hearts evidenced significantly reduced infarct area (48 +/- 5 % vs. 59 +/- 11 % p = 0.03) and MVO (19 +/- 4 % vs. 27 +/- 5% , p = 0.03) normalized to area at risk and a higher myocardial salvage index (52 +/- 5 % vs. 41 +/- 11% p = 0.03). Extensive perivascular edema, and neutrophil infiltration observed in controls was markedly reduced in TVU hearts. Confocal microscopy and spatial pattern analysis revealed significantly mitigated disruption of gap junctions and NaV1.5 dissociation from N-cadherin in TVU hearts compared to controls. Importantly, severity-adjusted arrhythmia burden during reperfusion was significantly lower in TV-P hearts (8+/-8 vs. 12+/-5 episodes lasting greater than 5seconds in controls). Our results demonstrate that TVU effectively prevents arrhythmias during reperfusion by preserving coronary microvasculature and cardiomyocyte nanostructure.

title: Key considerations in the design, conduct, analysis, and interpretation of observational studies in dialysis.
authorString: Quinn RR, Lam NN.

journal.title: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension

abstractText:
Purpose of review

In this review, key considerations in the design, conduct, and analysis of observational studies in dialysis research are explored in a unique patient population for which interventional trials are challenging and limited.

Recent findings

The use of target trial emulation is increasing and provides a conceptual framework for the design of observational studies. A target trial is a hypothetical trial that would be conducted to answer a research question. It requires investigators to ask a clinically relevant question and then specify eligibility criteria, the treatment strategies that will be compared, the follow-up period, outcomes of interest, and the causal contrast (intention-to-treat vs. per-protocol analysis). The protocol for an observational study is then created to mirror the target trial. In doing so, the question is clear, bias is reduced, and underlying assumptions are made transparent. Illustrative examples are used to highlight common pitfalls in dialysis research.

Summary

In conclusion, randomized controlled trials are not always feasible or even the ideal approach for answering certain questions. However, observational studies are challenging and require careful planning and execution to ensure robust, unbiased results. Target trial emulation provides a blueprint to improve the quality of observational study design.

title: Nanomaterial Design for Macrophage Reprogramming: Emerging Strategies and Mechanistic Insights for Inflammation and Tumor Therapy.
authorString: Giri N, Chakraborty A.
abstractText: Macrophages play a paradoxical role in inflammation and tumor. They can protect the host during acute inflammation but act as the main driver for the chronic inflammation which is a common characteristic of several diseases including rheumatoid arthritis, atherosclerosis, type 2 diabetes, inflammatory bowel disease, and neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease. In the tumor microenvironment, macrophages switch their phenotype to the immunosuppressive M2 state that promotes tumor growth, angiogenesis, and metastasis. Emerging nanomaterial platforms are trying to offer transformative solutions by enabling the precise delivery of immunomodulatory drugs directly to disease-site macrophages. This review will provide comprehensive comparative analysis of these emerging nanomaterial designs strategies across two disease paradigms: inflammatory diseases and tumor. The discussion will focus on various strategies which include inhibiting chemokine axis (CCL2-CCR2 axis), selective elimination of macrophages through apoptosis, metabolic reprogramming, biomimetic and apoptotic cell-inspired nanoparticles leveraging natural macrophage clearance pathways to promote M2 polarization in inflammation, and the activation of tumor-associated macrophages via TLR and STING agonist. We highlight the role of nanoparticle surface chemistry, composition, and targeting ligands in achieving the two opposite therapeutic outcomes of these two diseases while maintaining some common design principles including EPR-mediated accumulation at the disease sites and biomimetic modifications. We also mentioned novel next-generation nanoparticle-based platforms that are currently in clinical trials for the treatment of tumor and inflammatory diseases. Finally, we discuss the barriers that limit the clinical translational potential of broad nanoparticles, with particular emphasis on nanoparticle-related immunotoxicity, macrophage heterogeneity, and manufacturing reproducibility of the nanoparticles.

title: Bipolar Disorder and the Risk of Cardiovascular Diseases: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Observational Studies.
authorString: Motta FDS, Ruffini ML, Ritter AC, Ferrão SM, Silva RS, Mastella NDS, Montezano BB, Ajub E, Kapczinski F, Pinto JV, Passos IC.
abstractText:
Introduction

Bipolar disorder (BD) is a chronic psychiatric illness characterized by recurrent manic and depressive episodes, affecting 2% of the global population. It is associated with premature mortality, including cardiovascular disease (CVD)-related mortality. Although clinically important, the absolute burden and incidence of cardiovascular outcomes in BD remain incompletely characterized. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized observational evidence on CVD prevalence and incidence in adults with BD.

Methods

Following PRISMA guidelines and prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD42023484712), we searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Scopus, and PsycInfo, screening 11,909 records. Thirty-two observational studies in adults with BD were included after Newcastle-Ottawa Scale assessment. Data were extracted on overall CVD, coronary artery disease, cerebrovascular disease, peripheral arterial disease, comorbidities, and psychotropic exposure. Pooled prevalence and incidence rate ratios were calculated using random-effects models when data were comparable.

Results

The pooled CVD prevalence in BD was 7.70% (95% CI: 5.07-11.52), with coronary artery disease at 6.89% (95% CI: 4.05-11.47), cerebrovascular disease at 4.45% (95% CI: 2.13-9.05), and peripheral arterial disease at 3.30% (95% CI: 1.66-6.45). However, prevalence estimates showed extreme heterogeneity and should be interpreted as broad indicators of absolute burden rather than precise estimates for a single BD population. In controlled incidence studies, BD was associated with increased CVD incidence (IRR 1.66, 95% CI: 1.32-2.08), with elevated coronary and cerebrovascular estimates. Clinical variable analyses involving medication use, lifestyle factors, and cardiometabolic comorbidities were not feasible because reporting was insufficient and noncomparable.

Conclusion

Adults with BD show substantial cardiovascular burden and increased incidence. However, extreme heterogeneity, limited incidence data, observational designs, and insufficient moderator reporting limit the precision and generalizability of pooled estimates. These findings support integrated cardiovascular screening in BD populations and future prospective studies.

Trail registration

PROSPERO CRD42023484712.

title: Pre-reperfusion paracetamol and peak troponin in ST-elevation myocardial infarction: a single-centre open-label non-randomised study with matched historical controls.
authorString: Owen A, Majeed K, Pillay R, Jeyakumar J, Wu Z, Stiles M.

title: Deep learning algorithms for predicting intraoperative hypotension: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Duan J, Chen Z, Wang J.
abstractText: Intraoperative hypotension (IOH) is associated with myocardial injury, acute kidney injury, perioperative stroke, and 30-day mortality. Deep learning (DL) refers to a family of machine-learning methods that learn multiple levels of data representation through nonlinear transformations. In perioperative monitoring, DL models can learn patterns from time-varying physiological signals and combine them with clinical variables to estimate impending IOH risk. DL algorithms applied to continuous physiological waveforms therefore represent a rapidly expanding paradigm for early IOH prediction, but their pooled diagnostic accuracy has not been synthesised within a unified diagnostic-accuracy framework. To quantify the pooled diagnostic accuracy of DL-based IOH prediction models and to identify factors that modify their performance. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched through March 2026. Methodological quality was appraised with PROBAST+AI and certainty of evidence with GRADE. A bivariate random-effects model generated pooled sensitivity, specificity, and SROC-AUC; heterogeneity was quantified by τ2(Se), τ2(Sp), and ρ. Subgroup analyses (prediction window, DL architecture, modality, IOH reference, analysis unit) and random-effects meta-regression were performed. Twelve studies were included; nine contributed 22 validation datasets. Pooled sensitivity was 0.78 (95% CI 0.73-0.81), specificity 0.88 (0.82-0.92), and SROC-AUC 0.87 (0.83-0.90); diagnostic odds ratio 24.7 (16.1-37.9), positive likelihood ratio 6.31, negative likelihood ratio 0.26. Heterogeneity was τ2(Se) = 0.25, τ2(Sp) = 1.04, ρ = -0.28. The 5-min window achieved the highest performance (sensitivity 0.81; specificity 0.91). Meta-regression identified DL architecture as the only significant moderator of specificity (P = 0.02), with hybrid CNN-RNN exceeding pure CNN (β = 1.77, 95% CI 0.45-3.09). Deeks' test was non-significant (P = 0.06). GRADE certainty was Low. DL models for IOH prediction achieve moderate diagnostic accuracy, with hybrid CNN-RNN architectures and 5-min prediction windows showing the most favourable performance. Universal absence of formal calibration assessment, scarce external validation, and geographic concentration constrain immediate clinical translation. PROSPERO CRD420261377604 Reporting guideline: PRISMA-DTA.

title: Risk Factors and Clinical Outcomes of Reocclusion after Endovascular Treatment for Acute Ischemic Stroke: An Updated Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis and Meta-Regression.
authorString: Gonçalves OR, Nogueira BV, Monteiro GA, Leite M, Cardoso LJC, Gonzalez JVP, da Silva AMP, Lacerda LL, Filho RSL, Silva EPO, Alexandre A, Chausson N, Nguyen TN, Dmytriw AA, Boulouis G, Kalsoum E, Clarençon F, Scarcia L.

journal.title: Journal of neuroradiology = Journal de neuroradiologie

abstractText:
Background

Early reocclusion after endovascular treatment (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is underrecognized; its determinants and impact remain poorly defined.

Methods

Random-effects meta-analysis of early reocclusion after successful EVT (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library through January 2026). Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE. Post hoc sensitivity analyses included only same-site reocclusion definitions.

Results

Ten studies (3,381 patients) were included; 244 (7.2%) reoccluded. Reocclusion was associated with lower 90-day functional independence (OR 0.25, 95% CI 0.17-0.38) and higher mortality (OR 1.86, 1.29-2.68), both moderate certainty. Reocclusion was more frequent with large-artery atherosclerosis (OR 2.24, 1.41-3.55; same-site 3.04, 1.73-5.33) and less frequent with cardioembolism (OR 0.40, 0.28-0.57) and atrial fibrillation (OR 0.39, 0.26-0.59), mutually confounded associations reflecting one embolic-versus-atherothrombotic axis. Prestroke antiplatelet therapy (OR 0.43, 0.28-0.67) lost significance under the same-site definition (0.60, 0.31-1.16). Exploratory data (two cohorts) linked eTICI 2c-3 reperfusion with less reocclusion (OR 0.44, 0.28-0.69). No study reported when etiology was adjudicated; the atherosclerosis association may be partly outcome-induced.

Conclusions

Early reocclusion is uncommon but carries a substantial prognostic penalty. Its determinants appear to lie in the vascular substrate rather than thrombectomy technique; prospective studies with uniform same-site definitions and systematic follow-up imaging are needed.

title: Preoperative Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index and Clinical Outcomes After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
authorString: Nourian S, Rad KJ, Ghasemi M, Mirkalaie MM, Tayebi N, Ashrafi MM, Nourallahzadeh MH, Norouzi AR.
abstractText:
Background

The systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) is a routinely available blood-derived marker with potential prognostic relevance after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). We evaluated associations between preoperative SII and postoperative outcomes.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, Scopus and Web of Science were searched to 1 October 2026, with supplementary searches through 14 October 2026. Peer-reviewed observational studies evaluating preoperative SII in adults undergoing CABG were eligible. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale. Compatible categorical associations and exploratory adjusted continuous mortality effects were pooled separately using restricted maximum-likelihood random-effects models; other findings were summarized descriptively.

Results

Thirty-one reports were included, with an aggregate sample of 30,976 and possible cohort overlap; five contributed to meta-analysis. Two off-pump cohorts comprising 1,378 patients and 180 atrial-fibrillation events yielded an imprecise crude association with postoperative atrial fibrillation (OR 1.60, 95%CI 0.53–4.82; I 2 =68%). An exploratory crude synthesis indicated greater intra-aortic balloon pump use with higher SII (OR 2.45, 95%CI 1.16–5.18; I 2 =51%). Two cohorts with differing follow-up yielded an exploratory adjusted mortality HR of 1.11 (95% Wald CI 1.05–1.18) per study-specific SD increase in log-SII. In one 624-patient cohort, high SII was associated with postoperative acute kidney injury after adjustment (OR 3.35, 95% CI 2.25–4.97).Apparent atrial-fibrillation discrimination varied (AUC 0.587–0.946).

Conclusions

Preoperative SII showed associations with selected adverse outcomes after CABG, supporting further evaluation as an accessible prognostic marker. Its incremental value beyond established clinical risk models requires validation.

title: Admission Inflammatory Biomarkers and New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation After Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authorString: Salameh H, Alqaraleh A, alkasem A, Abdelrahman A, Mohamad A, Jawabrah A, Jarrad L, Salman S, Altarawneh A, AbuDawwas M, Khalili H.
abstractText:
Background:

New-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF) complicates acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and worsens prognosis. Systemic inflammation may contribute, but the value of admission inflammatory biomarkers is uncertain.

Methods:

Following PRISMA 2020 (PROSPERO CRD420261470060), we searched six databases from inception to 26 September 2026 for observational studies comparing admission neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), C-reactive protein (CRP), or high-sensitivity CRP (hs-CRP) between AMI patients with and without NOAF. Risk of bias was assessed with QUIPS and certainty of evidence with GRADE. We used random-effects models, prediction intervals, leave-one-out sensitivity analyses, and Doi plots with the LFK index.

Results:

Sixteen studies (12,509 patients; 1,103 with NOAF) were included. NOAF was associated with higher NLR (MD 1.78, 95% CI 0.44 to 3.11; I² 70.6%), CRP (MD 4.17, 1.42 to 6.91; I² 53.8%), and hs-CRP (SMD 0.84, 0.47 to 1.20; I² 88.6%). PLR did not differ significantly (three studies; MD 57.19, 95% CI −13.38 to 127.77). CRP and hs-CRP remained significant in every leave-one-out analysis, whereas NLR lost significance after omitting one study (p = 0.055). All prediction intervals crossed no effect. Funnel plots, Doi plots, and LFK indices (2.46 to 7.25) indicated asymmetry. Certainty of evidence was very low for all biomarkers.

Conclusion:

Higher admission NLR, CRP, and hs-CRP are associated with NOAF after AMI, but the evidence is very low certainty and PLR findings are inconclusive. These markers cannot yet identify individual high-risk patients; prospective studies with standardized sampling, continuous rhythm monitoring, and adjusted analyses are needed.

title: Words That Heal: A Systematic Review of Healthcare Providers-Patient Communication to Enhance Chronic Care Management and Practice Recommendations.
authorString: Pietrabissa G, Rapelli G, Marchesi G, Castelnuovo G.
abstractText: Chronic diseases represent a major global health burden, and suboptimal treatment adherence remains a key obstacle to long-term management. Healthcare provider (HCP)-patient communication is a modifiable determinant of adherence and psychological functioning, yet evidence remains fragmented across conditions and communication domains. This review builds on patient-centered communication scholarship and established models of communication functions and pathways linking clinician-patient communication to health outcomes. This systematic review synthesizes empirical evidence on HCP-patient communication strategies associated with treatment adherence and psychological outcomes among adults with chronic diseases, including diabetes, cancer, cardiovascular, and respiratory conditions. Following PRISMA guidelines and PROSPERO registration (CRD42020171690), five databases (Scopus, PubMed, PsycINFO, Cochrane Library, Google Scholar) were searched. Results: Twenty-seven studies met the inclusion criteria. Communication strategies clustered into four macro-domains: (1) trust and interpersonal relationship; (2) information exchange and decision processes; (3) active involvement, empowerment, and autonomy; and (4) change processes, emotional regulation, and management of difficulties. Domains were defined a priori from patient-centered communication, self-management, and behavior-change literature and refined during data extraction. Across conditions, integrated communication patterns addressing multiple domains were generally associated with favorable adherence, self-management, clinical, quality-of-life, and healthcare-utilization outcomes, although evidence strength varied by study design, disease context, and methodological quality. Findings support a provisional, evidence-informed framework in which HCP-patient communication strategies, organized within relational, informational, participatory, and change-regulatory macro-domains, may engage proximal regulatory processes that, in turn, may be associated with adherence and other chronic-care outcomes. Prospective studies are needed to test these pathways.

title: Evaluating selected gene therapies for cardiovascular diseases: an updated scoping review and evidence map of randomised controlled trials.

title: EXPRESS: Letter to the Editor Regarding "Much ado about eating: Intermittent fasting and post-stroke neuroprotection".
authorString: Carneiro GB, Pace CM, Figueiredo EG.

journal.title: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism

abstractText: Vemuganti and colleagues highlight intermittent fasting (IF)'s neuroprotective potential post-stroke via autophagy and mitochondrial biogenesis. However, clinical translation faces hurdles in metabolically vulnerable patients. This letter critiques IF's bedside applicability, emphasizing post-stroke catabolic stress, dysphagia (~50% cases), sarcopenia risk, and cardiovascular concerns. Recent evidence links short eating windows to higher mortality, countering IF benefits. The obesity paradox suggests nutritional reserves aid survival. Strategies: protein-prioritized planning, dysphagia screening, dietitian monitoring, and supplements. Until RCTs confirm safety/efficacy, prioritize nutritional adequacy. Preclinical insights warrant study.Keywords: dysphagia, intermittent fasting, neuroprotection, obesity paradox, sarcopenia.

title: Spanish catheter ablation registry. 25th official report of the Heart Rhythm Association of the Spanish Society of Cardiology (2025).
authorString: Manuel Rubio-Campal J, García BC, Amador PB, Rodríguez-Entem F, Cuervo DC, collaborators of the Spanish catheter ablation registry.
abstractText:
Introduction and objectives

We report the results of the 2025 Spanish catheter ablation registry.

Methods

This retrospective registry included catheter ablation procedures performed at participating hospitals in Spain and recorded in the REDCap database using a dedicated data collection form.

Results

A total of 109 centers participated, reporting 33 435 ablations. Atrial fibrillation was the most commonly treated arrhythmia (14 452 cases), with single-shot techniques being the most frequently used approach (63%) and a marked increase in pulsed field ablation (37% vs 21% in 2024). The remaining arrhythmia substrates remained at similar levels. The overall acute success rate was 95%, the complication rate was 1.6%, and the mortality rate was 0.04%. There was a marked increase in outpatient procedures (33% vs 18% in 2024), particularly atrioventricular nodal re-entrant tachycardia ablation (50%) and cavotricuspid isthmus ablation (45%). A total of 467 pediatric ablations were performed in 38 centers. Accessory pathway ablation was the most common procedure (65.3%), with a 97% success rate.

Conclusions

A similar number of centers participated, with a slight increase in the number of procedures compared with 2024. Atrial fibrillation remained the most frequently treated arrhythmia. Acute success, complication, and mortality rates remained stable. The accreditation process for centers and professionals is well-established, with a stable number of annual accreditations. Full English text available from: www.revespcardiol.org/en.

title: Reversible wall motion abnormalities do not predict long-term mortality if coronary flow reserve is accounted for: A 15-year contrast stress-echo study.
authorString: Gaibazzi N, Niccoli G, Sartorio D, Tuttolomondo D.
abstractText:
Background

Stress echocardiography (SE) is widely used to detect myocardial ischaemia in the scenario of chronic coronary syndromes (CCS). Despite that, the prognostic value of SE has been rarely assessed. We aim to establish whether the presence of reversible wall motion abnormalities (RWMA), remains independently associated with long-term mortality when considering myocardial perfusion (MP) and Doppler coronary flow velocity reserve in the left anterior descending artery (CFVR-LAD).

Method

1002 subjects who underwent Dipyridamole contrast SE, for suspected CCS, between 2007 and 2012 at the Parma University Hospital were enrolled. The endpoint is all-cause mortality. The probability of survival was calculated using the Kaplan-Meier method and event-rate curves were compared using the log-rank test.

Results

There were 376 deaths (37.5%) during a median follow-up of 13.8 years. Mean age was 66 ± 11 years, females represented 38%, 32% had known CCS. SE results showed RWMA in 17.5%, reversible MP abnormalities in 26.2%, and reduced CFVR-LAD in 42% of the study population. Revascularization within 3 months of the SE was performed in 185 subjects (18.5%). In multivariate Cox proportional hazard analysis, among the SE variables, only CFVR-LAD<2 remained associated with mortality (HR 2.44, 95% CI 1.94-3.5, p < 0.0001).

Conclusion

In the setting of CCS patients, CFVR-LAD is the only SE variable maintaining independent association with long-term mortality.

title: Advanced right heart failure stage at first documentation of severe tricuspid regurgitation: beyond the late-referral paradigm.
authorString: Fiore G, Ingallina G, Ancona F, Stella S, Biondi F, Gaspardone C, Margonato D, Denti P, Maisano F, Agricola E.
abstractText:
Background

Patients with severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) frequently present with advanced right heart failure (RHF), commonly attributed to delayed referral for intervention. Whether this reflects delayed referral or the stage at which severe TR is first documented remains uncertain.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed 625 consecutive patients with a first echocardiographic diagnosis of severe TR. RHF severity was classified using a validated hierarchical staging system (Stages 1-4). In a subgroup of 310 patients with a previous echocardiogram documenting non-severe TR, RHF stage was retrospectively assessed before severe TR was first documented. Two-year all-cause mortality was evaluated.

Results

At first documentation of severe TR, 66.4% of patients were classified as Stage 3 and 17.3% as Stage 4, whereas only 16.3% were in Stages 1-2. Functional TR accounted for 85% of cases. RHF stage was associated with progressively higher TRI-SCORE and two-year mortality. Among patients with prior non-severe TR, 78% were already in Stage 3-4 before severe TR was first documented, whereas only 7% had reached Stage 4.

Conclusions

Severe TR was predominantly diagnosed in patients with stage 3-4 RHF. Higher RHF stages were already present in most patients before severe TR was first documented. These findings suggest that delayed referral alone may not fully explain the advanced clinical profile of severe TR and that eligibility for guideline-directed intervention frequently coincides with an already advanced stage of disease.

title: Late gadolinium enhancement dispersion mapping predicts major arrhythmic events in patients with prior myocardial infarction.
authorString: Licordari R, Todiere G, De Gori C, Barison A, Grigoratos C, Marcucci A, Alberti M, Fulceri L, Emdin M, De Caterina R, Di Bella G, Aquaro GD.
abstractText:
Background

Myocardial scar heterogeneity is a key determinant of ventricular arrhythmias after myocardial infarction (MI). Late gadolinium enhancement dispersion mapping (LGE-DM) quantifies structural complexity, but its prognostic role in ischemic cardiomyopathy remains unevaluated.

Methods

We retrospectively included 364 consecutive patients with prior MI (>90 days). For each LGE image, a parametric map was generated and each enhanced pixel scored (0-8) based on surrounding signal distribution; the global dispersion score (GDS) was calculated as the mean pixel score, quantifying pixel-to-pixel heterogeneity. The endpoint was a composite of sudden cardiac death (SCD), resuscitated cardiac arrest, sustained ventricular tachycardia, or appropriate ICD therapies.

Results

During a median follow-up of 4 years, 42 arrhythmic events occurred. Patients with events showed significantly higher GDS than event-free patients (0.53 vs 0.32, P < 0.0001). Multivariable Cox regression confirmed GDS as an independent predictor (HR 1.16 per 0.1-unit increase, 95% CI 1.03-1.29), while LVEF and LGE extent were not, and GDS remained independently associated with events when LGE extent was forced into the model (HR 1.12 per 0.1-unit increase, P = 0.005). In patients with LVEF >35%, GDS was the only independent predictor across all multivariable models. Harrell's C-index was 0.682, with an optimism of 0.012 on bootstrap resampling. ROC analysis identified GDS >0.5 as a provisional cut-off derived within the same cohort (apparent AUC 0.74 overall; 0.81 in the LVEF >35% subgroup). Kaplan-Meier analysis confirmed worse prognosis in patients with GDS >0.5 (overall: p = 0.0002; LVEF >35%: p < 0.0001).

Conclusions

LGE dispersion independently predicts malignant ventricular arrhythmias post-MI, outperforming LGE extent and LVEF. GDS may improve SCD risk stratification particularly in patients with LVEF >35%, a population not adequately targeted by current LVEF-based criteria. External validation is required before the proposed threshold can be used clinically.

title: Pressure-volume loop reconstruction of Impella support in severe aortic regurgitation: explaining a hemodynamic paradox.
authorString: Takagi H.
abstractText:
Background

Severe aortic regurgitation (AR) causes left ventricular (LV) volume overload, while transvalvular Impella support may permit regurgitant recirculation. We constructed schematic pressure-volume (PV) loops to illustrate the interaction between ventricular unloading and systemic perfusion in severe AR.

Methods

Conceptual LV PV loops were constructed from established principles of ventricular mechanics to depict progressive AR, cardiogenic shock (CS), and alternative hypothetical responses to Impella support. No patient-specific measurements or numerical simulation were used.

Results

Increasing AR was depicted by rightward PV-loop displacement and greater LV volume excursion without quantifying effective forward stroke volume. The hypothetical transition to CS showed lower LV pressure and greater end-systolic volume. During Impella support, a leftward loop shift and smaller enclosed area were compatible with unloading; regurgitant recirculation could offset its benefit and permit recurrent LV distension. Pump flow, regurgitant flow, and effective systemic output could not be derived from the loops.

Conclusions

This qualitative framework illustrates a plausible hemodynamic paradox: LV unloading during Impella support may coexist with limited improvement in net systemic perfusion in severe AR. It does not establish the magnitude or temporal sequence of these responses.

title: American Association for Thoracic Surgery Quality Gateway Procedural Outcomes Models for General Thoracic Surgery Quality Assurance.
authorString: Ishwaran H, Blackstone EH.

journal.title: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery

abstractText: To develop quality assurance models for adverse procedural events after lung resection and esophagectomy for cancer. Using procedural outcomes after 16,430 lung resections and 3,068 esophagectomies for cancer at 9 hospitals in 7 hospital systems, we developed 5 individual and 2 composite outcome models from preoperative information. Random forest quantile classification for imbalanced data with model-free variable priority screening identified predictors. Out-of-bag prediction provided regularized estimates and internal validation. Hospital-holdout analysis assessed institutional benchmark stability. Of 71 lung resection and 63 esophagectomy preoperative variables, 35 and 29, respectively, were identified as important predictors across the 7 outcome models. These included demographics, advanced cancer, organ dysfunction, higher acuity, and planned surgical approach and resection extent. Out-of-bag calibration covered a modest range of probabilities. Out-of-bag geometric mean ranged from 0.588 to 0.713 for lung resection and 0.517 to 0.649 for esophagectomy. Continuous risk factors, particularly pulmonary function, provided high-importance information content, with complex dependency and interaction structure among predictors. Risk-factor magnitude differed among hospitals, as did their risk-adjusted outcomes according to patient risk as determined by counterfactual inference within a framework of virtual twins. For lung resection operative mortality, hospital-specific contrasts were stable when each focal hospital was excluded from the aggregate benchmark. Using contemporary machine learning, initial models for adverse procedural events after lung resection and esophagectomy for cancer have been developed. They provide surgeons, their patients, and hospital and hospital systems tools for patient risk assessment and for informing quality improvement initiatives in general thoracic surgery.

title: Prospects for adiponectin-based therapeutics in myocardial ischemia reperfusion injury.
authorString: Bahit MC, Gibson CM, Lei Y, Hsu HH, Scherer PE, Sweeney G.
abstractText: Adiponectin is an adipocyte-derived hormone with broad cardiometabolic benefits, circulating at high levels in healthy individuals but reduced in obesity, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease. Low adiponectin concentrations are strongly associated with coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction, myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI), and heart failure. MIRI remains a major unmet need in contemporary ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) care. Although reperfusion is essential in limiting ischemic myocardial necrosis, it causes deleterious effects such as impaired carbohydrate oxidation, excessive fatty-acid oxidation, intracellular acidosis, calcium (Ca<sup>2+</sup>) overload, oxidative/nitrative stress, and mitochondrial fragmentation, that expand infarct size, worsen microvascular obstruction, and fuel adverse ventricular remodeling.
