Activation of the adiponectin-adiponectin receptor (AdipoR) axis directly counteracts these processes by stimulating adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK)-dependent metabolic rebalancing, restoring mitochondrial fusion-fission homeostasis, enhancing oxidative capacity, reducing inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS-) and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH) oxidase-mediated injury, improving endothelial nitric oxide (NO) bioavailability, and enhancing microvascular perfusion. In animal models, adiponectin or its mimetics consistently reduced infarct size, improved myocardial function, and attenuated apoptosis, inflammation, and no-reflow. A growing array of therapeutic strategies has emerged, each bringing its own pharmacologic nuances and implications for translation to the clinic. This review summarizes current strategies to enhance adiponectin action, highlights the progress in peptide and small-molecule mimetics, and discusses future directions for clinical translation in cardiometabolic diseases.

title: Prognostic Value of Late Gadolinium Enhancement Findings in Isolated Left Ventricular Dilatation and Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Gonçalves T, Duhamel S, Toupin S, Sanguineti F, Garot P, Unterseeh T, Hovasse T, Akodad M, Champagne S, Chevalier B, Neylon A, Gall E, Martial PJ, Ballout E, Mirailles R, Sibilia B, Unger A, Bondue A, Florence J, Dillinger JG, Henry P, Bousson V, Garot J, Pezel T.

journal.title: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance

abstractText:
Background

Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and isolated left ventricular dilatation (ILVD) are defined as left ventricular (LV) dilatation, with reduced or preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), respectively. We aimed to assess the prognostic value of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) findings, including LGE extent, location, and number of areas to predict all-cause death in ILVD and DCM, separately.

Methods

Between 2008 and 2021, we conducted a bicentric retrospective study including all consecutive ILVD and DCM patients referred for cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR). The primary outcome was all-cause death. A propensity-score matching was performed to balance characteristics between ILVD and DCM populations. Cox regressions were performed to determine the prognostic value of each LGE feature.

Results

Of 2,752 patients (age 52±8 years, 56% males), 408 (15%) patients died after a median (interquartile range) follow-up of 9 (7-12) years, including 268 (16%) of 1,668 DCM patients and 140 (13%) of 1,084 ILVD patients. Overall, 737 (27%) patients had LGE, including 472 (28%) of 1,668 DCM patients and 265 (24%) of 1,084 ILVD patients. After propensity-score matching, in ILVD patients with LGE (N=265), the LGE extent (hazard ratio [HR] 1.38, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.06-1.78, p=0.015), multiple LGE areas (HR=3.39, 95% CI: 1.66-6.92, p<0.001), and its septal location (HR=2.68, 95% CI: 1.59-4.52, p<0.001) were strong prognosticators of death after adjustment. Similarly, after propensity-score matching, in DCM patients with LGE (N=277), the LGE extent (HR=1.39, 95% CI: 1.06-1.83, p=0.018), multiple LGE areas (HR=2.70, 95% CI: 1.20-6.08, p=0.017), and its septal location (HR=2.82, 95% CI: 1.47-5.41, p=0.002) were strongly associated with death. The CMR LGE score performed well in participants with LGE (area under the curve [AUC] at 10 years, 0.79 [95% CI: 0.69-0.89]).

Conclusions

LGE findings were strongly and independently associated with death in both ILVD and DCM patients, with each successive LGE characteristic providing significant incremental prognostic value beyond traditional prognosticators, including LVEF.

title: The Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) study measured hepcidin, cardiovascular, kidney and metabolic outcomes in chronic kidney disease.
authorString: Cho ME, Mehta RC, Greene T, Hansen JL, Sweeney C, Cheung AK, Wolf M, Rincon-Choles H, Hsu J, Raj D, Rosas SE, Lash J, Hsu CY, Dobre M, Unruh ML, Rao P, Fino N, CRIC Study Investigators.
abstractText:
Introduction

Abnormal iron homeostasis plays a critical role in extra-hematopoietic disorders. The relationship of hepcidin, the master iron regulator, to clinical outcomes, has not been characterized in a large cohort of chronic kidney disease (CKD).

Methods

To determine if plasma hepcidin level predicts cardiovascular (CV), kidney, and metabolic outcomes in patients with CKD, we studied 3826 patients enrolled in the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) study. Hazard ratios for hepcidin tertiles were estimated from Cox Proportional Hazards regression for primary outcomes of incident heart failure (HF), end stage kidney disease (kidney failure) or halving of the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and new onset diabetes or prediabetes. Secondary outcomes included atherosclerotic events and all-cause and CV mortality.

Results

The median and interquartile range of plasma hepcidin level was 43 (22, 77) ng/mL. Higher plasma hepcidin levels were associated with older age, male sex, non-Hispanic Black race, diabetes, lower eGFR, higher albuminuria, increased plasma levels of iron indices, C-terminal fibroblast growth factor 23, and markers of inflammation (high-sensitivity C-reactive protein and interleukin-6). We found no association between plasma hepcidin level and the risk for incident HF or prediabetes/diabetes. However, compared to the middle tertile, the highest hepcidin tertile was independently associated with increased risk for kidney outcomes (hazard ratio 1.19; 95% confidence interval 1.09, 1.30) and atherosclerotic events (hazard ratio 1.34; 95% confidence interval 1.09, 1.64), while the lowest hepcidin tertile was associated with increased risk for all-cause and CV mortality in fully adjusted multivariable models including iron indices and inflammation.

Conclusion

Both low and high plasma levels of hepcidin are associated with adverse clinical outcomes.

title: Convergent Ferroptosis and Pyroptosis in MASLD-Associated Cardiac Remodeling.
authorString: Gui H, Yuan X, Zhang Y.

journal.title: Translational research : the journal of laboratory and clinical medicine

abstractText: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects ∼30% of the global population and is associated with increased risks of heart failure (particularly heart failure with preserved ejection fraction), atrial fibrillation, and cardiovascular mortality. Despite well-established epidemiological links between MASLD and cardiovascular disease, the molecular pathways driving MASLD-related cardiac remodeling remain incompletely understood. This state-of-the-art mini review examines ferroptosis and pyroptosis as potentially convergent regulated cell-death pathways relevant to both the steatotic liver and the remodeling heart. Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent, lipid peroxidation-driven cell death that mediates hepatocyte injury in experimental MASLD and contributes to cardiomyocyte injury under cardiac stress. Pyroptosis is an inflammasome-mediated pro-inflammatory cell death executed by gasdermin D, which amplifies tissue inflammation in hepatic and cardiac disease. Direct preclinical evidence from a pressure-overload heart-failure model demonstrates ferroptosis-to-pyroptosis signaling through the ACSL4/ALOX12/12-HETE/NLRP3 axis; however, this cascade has not yet been directly validated in MASLD models or in patients with MASLD-associated cardiac remodeling. We therefore distinguish experimentally established within-organ mechanisms from hypothesized interorgan liver-heart links, highlight shared regulators including reactive oxygen species, the cGAS/STING pathway, and the NRF2 hub, and discuss translational strategies and evidence gaps that should guide future validation.

title: Shock Index-Creatinine as a Predictor of In-Hospital Clinical Outcomes in Patients with Anterior Wall ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Undergoing Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
authorString: Venkadesan K, Nath RK, Aggarwal P, Sinha SK, Kuber D, Rao S, Pandit BN.
abstractText:
Background

Early risk stratification in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) is essential but established scores such as TIMI and GRACE require multivariable computation. The Shock Index-Creatinine (SIC) is a simpler bedside alternative, yet Indian data are sparse.

Objective

To assess whether admission SIC predicts in-hospital adverse events in anterior wall STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).

Methods

Two hundred consecutive patients with anterior wall STEMI undergoing primary PCI at a tertiary care centre in northern India were prospectively enrolled over 12 months. SIC was computed at admission as (Shock Index × 100) - Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance. The primary outcome was in-hospital death; secondary outcomes were heart failure, cardiogenic shock, contrast-induced acute kidney injury (CI-AKI), and life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia. Discrimination was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).

Results

The cohort was 73.0% male with a mean age of 54.5 years; in-hospital mortality was 10.0% (n = 20). Admission SIC was markedly higher in non-survivors than survivors (82.0 ± 42.4 versus -20.1 ± 19.4; p < 0.001). AUCs were 0.992 for mortality and cardiogenic shock, 0.971 for CI-AKI, 0.909 for ventricular arrhythmia, and 0.907 for heart failure (all p < 0.001). A SIC ≥ 20 predicted death with 95.0% sensitivity and 98.9% specificity.

Conclusions

In this Indian cohort, admission SIC was a powerful bedside predictor of adverse in-hospital events after primary PCI for anterior wall STEMI. The unusually high discriminative performance requires external validation in larger multicentre populations before routine clinical adoption.

title: Early morphological and physiological parameters of survival and mortality in cultured southern flounder (Paralichthys lethostigma) larvae.
authorString: Thibault O, Butler J, Cason P, Hala D, Petersen LH.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Comp Biochem Physiol A Mol Integr Physiol
journal.title: Comparative biochemistry and physiology. Part A, Molecular & integrative physiology
journal.isoabbreviation: Comp Biochem Physiol A Mol Integr Physiol

abstractText: This study focused on the relation between larval southern flounder (Paralichthys lethostigma) growth, cardiac performance, and metabolic physiology (metabolic rate, hormones). Two-way ANOVAs were performed among larvae groups that successfully survived through metamorphosis (n = 1) vs. those that succumbed to mass mortality early in development (n = 2). Larvae were monitored from 5 to 50 days post hatch (dph). The comparison of morphological and physiological parameters for the three batches for equivalent life-stages from 5 to 12 dph (n = 8-10/dph), showed specific growth rate (SGR) in the surviving larvae to be ~3-fold higher than the two failed batches. Similarly, the absolute oxygen consumption rate (AMO2) was ~5-fold higher in the surviving batch vs. the two failed batches. In contrast, mass specific oxygen consumption rate (MO2) and heart rate (HR) were significantly lower in the surviving batch (~3-fold) versus the two failed batches. This mismatch for the surviving batch (a high SGR contrasted with low MO2 and HR), suggested a reduced cost of growth and likely bioenergetic conservation prior to metamorphosis-an energetically demanding process. The subsequent monitoring of the surviving batch through metamorphosis (~30-40 dph), showed a ~ 10-fold increase in AMO2 and ~ 2-fold increase in thyroid and corticoid hormones. Lastly, a strong negative correlation of HR vs. MO2 during early development putatively suggested future batch failure.

title: Mcu upregulation triggers mitochondrial oxidative stress and cardiomyocyte injury after myocardial infarction yet is suppressed by Fto and Ythdf2 in an m6A-dependent manner.
authorString: Chen R, Wang X, Qin L, Liu Z, Yu C, Li X, Zhang Z, Yang F, Zhang H, Lan H, Luan X, Xu X, Qu C, Li B, Li G, Chu XM.
abstractText: Mitochondrial calcium uniporter (Mcu) is essential for mitochondrial calcium homeostasis, yet its function and upstream regulatory mechanism in myocardial infarction (MI) remain unclear. This study was designed to define the pivotal regulatory pathway controlling Mcu expression post-MI and verify whether Mcu can act as a therapeutic target for MI. Mendelian randomization was used to verify the genetic link between Mcu and MI. In vitro gain- and loss-of-function assays together with m6A-seq, MeRIP-qPCR, RIP-qPCR and dual-luciferase assays were applied to explore the m6A-dependent regulatory mechanism of Fto/Ythdf2 on Mcu, and the biological effects of this axis on mitochondrial homeostasis and cardiomyocyte injury were validated via cell-based gene interventions. In vivo MI mouse models with cardiomyocyte-specific Fto/Mcu overexpression or DS16570511-mediated pharmacological Mcu inhibition were constructed to detect cardiac function, infarct size, myocardial fibrosis and mitochondrial injury. Our results demonstrated that elevated Mcu is positively associated with MI risk; excess Mcu triggers mitochondrial calcium overload, ROS buildup, mitochondrial membrane potential loss and respiratory chain damage to facilitate cardiomyocyte damage, whereas Mcu knockdown alleviates these pathological alterations. Mechanistically, ischemic injury downregulates Fto to increase m6A modification of Mcu mRNA. Meanwhile, ischemia-suppressed Ythdf2 expression impairs its binding to Mcu mRNA, which enhances Mcu mRNA stability and translation efficiency and leads to Mcu upregulation. Both Fto and Ythdf2 overexpression counteract Mcu-induced mitochondrial dysfunction and cardiomyocyte damage. In vivo experiments further confirmed that specific Mcu overexpression partially offsets Fto-mediated cardioprotection, and the Mcu inhibitor DS16570511 significantly ameliorates post-infarction cardiac dysfunction. In conclusion, Mcu aggravates ischemic myocardial damage by disturbing mitochondrial calcium balance, and we newly identify an Fto-Ythdf2-Mcu regulatory axis, providing a promising therapeutic target for MI.

title: Deubiquitination of WBP11 governs OPLAH-mediated glutathione biosynthesis to suppress triple programmed cell death in prostate cancer.
authorString: Zhuang X, He W, Zhang J, Wang Z, Zheng K, Zhuang Y, Song Z, Sun W, Shao Z, Fu X, Liao Y.
abstractText: Prostate cancer (PC) is one of the most common male cancers. Cancer cells are well known for their capacity to avoid programed cell death (PCD) via a variety of molecular pathways, allowing them to survive oncogenic stress and therapeutic challenges. Although oncogenic splicing factors are frequently dysregulated in tumors, their functional interplay with PCD regulatory networks in PC remains largely uncharacterized. Here, we demonstrate that WBP11 exerts a pro-tumorigenic effect by promoting PC cell proliferation, while its genetic silencing triggers concurrent induction of apoptosis, pyroptosis, and ferroptosis. Mechanistically, WBP11 directly binds to and stabilizes OPLAH mRNA, leading to elevated intracellular glutathione levels that facilitate efficient clearance of reactive oxygen species (ROS). Additionally, we demonstrate that USP13 deubiquitinates WBP11 by specifically eliminating K48-linked ubiquitin chains at lysine 626, which increases the stability of the WBP11 protein and prevents proteasomal destruction. Using a combination of in vitro functional assays, in vivo tumor models, and systematic rescue experiments, we define a previously unrecognized signaling axis, USP13-WBP11-OPLAH, that orchestrates glutathione metabolism and confers resistance to PCD, ultimately driving malignant progression of PC. Consistent with these functional findings, clinical validation reveals that USP13, WBP11, and OPLAH are significantly upregulated at the protein level in human PC tissues, and that USP13 expression positively correlates with both WBP11 and OPLAH protein abundance. Collectively, our study identifies the USP13-WBP11-OPLAH axis as a critical regulatory module linking glutathione metabolism to PCD resistance, offering promising therapeutic targets for the treatment of advanced PC.

title: Homocysteine and related B-vitamins throughout our International Conferences: a historical perspective.
authorString: Rosenberg I.
abstractText: In this invited keynote review, I reflect on biochemical, clinical, and epidemiological evidence on the role of folate and vitamin B12 in one-carbon metabolism and their relationship with homocysteine, integrating over five decades of research. One-carbon metabolism represents a central biochemical network linking folate-dependent one-carbon transfer reactions with vitamin B12-dependent remethylation of homocysteine to methionine. Disruptions in this pathway result in elevated homocysteine concentrations and impaired methylation capacity, providing a mechanistic link between micronutrient status and chronic disease. Early work demonstrated that folate is a major determinant of plasma homocysteine levels, supporting folic acid fortification policies that significantly reduced neural tube defects worldwide. Research in my laboratory in older adults shifted the paradigm of deficiency from inadequate intake to impaired bioavailability. Elevated homocysteine has been associated with cardiovascular disease, stroke, and cognitive decline, although intervention trials have yielded mixed results, suggesting that homocysteine is best interpreted as a marker of metabolic dysfunction, but when elevated, a potential target for mitigating cognitive decline. Recent advances in epigenetics and gene-nutrient interactions have expanded the relevance of one-carbon metabolism, highlighting its role in DNA methylation and gene regulation. Future research in precision nutrition may refine strategies for preventing chronic disease and promoting healthy aging.

title: Myocardial Infarction Within 6 Months before Total Shoulder Arthroplasty is Strongly Associated with Postoperative Complications.
authorString: Parmar RP, Sahni VS, Holle AM, Amini MH, McKee M, Lederman E, Patel M.

journal.title: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery

abstractText: As total shoulder arthroplasty (TSA) is increasing in volume, limited data exist regarding how recent myocardial infarction (MI) influences postoperative outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of MI timing, type, treatment, and anatomical location on rates of postoperative cardiac, medical, and surgical complications following TSA. A national insurance database, PearlDiver, was queried to identify patients with a history of MI within two years prior to TSA. These patients were propensity-matched 1:4 to controls without prior MI based on demographics and comorbidities. The MI cohort was stratified by timing (0-6 months, 6-12 months, 12-18 months, 18-24 months), and subgroup analyses were performed by MI type (Type 1 vs. Type 2), ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI) vs Non-ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (NSTEMI) classification, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT), and infarct location. A history of MI within 2 years preceding TSA had a strong association with higher odds of postoperative MI (OR 5.67; 95% CI, 3.86-8.32). The strongest association was observed when MI occurred within 6 months of TSA (OR 9.95; 95% CI, 6.50-15.24). Type 1 MI was strongly associated with postoperative MI, particularly within 6 months (OR 10.86; 95% CI, 6.96-16.95). Type 2 MI within 6 months was strongly associated with postoperative MI (OR 10.69; 95% CI, 2.50-45.63), DVT (OR 9.81; 95% CI, 2.30-41.79), and PJI (OR 5.24; 95% CI, 1.60-17.18). Both STEMI (OR = 6.17) and NSTEMI (OR = 5.77) were strongly associated with postoperative MI. Anterior MI was strongly associated with postoperative MI (OR 7.22; 95% CI, 3.36-15.49), whereas inferior MI was strongly associated with 90-day mortality (OR 6.46; 95% CI, 1.85-22.60). MI within 2 years and specifically 6 months of TSA was associated with higher odds of postoperative complications. MI timing, subtype, treatment, and location should be carefully weighed when considering TSA in this high-risk population.

title: Refractory Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Supported by Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation due to Leptospirosis at Réunion Island and a Literature Review.
authorString: Bordier E, Vidal C, Delmas B, Jabot J, Traversier N, Miltgen G, Belmonte O, Allyn J, Allou N.

journal.title: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene

abstractText: Leptospirosis is a zoonosis prevalent on Réunion Island. Severe forms with acute respiratory failure can lead to refractory hypoxemia, requiring the use of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). The aim for the present study was to describe all cases of leptospirosis complicated by refractory acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) requiring veno-venous ECMO on Réunion Island and to conduct a literature review. This retrospective observational study was conducted in a multidisciplinary intensive care unit of the University Hospital of Réunion Island. The aim was to describe the clinical, biological, and prognostic characteristics of patients who developed leptospirosis complicated by refractory ARDS requiring ECMO between January 2011 and December 2024. A total of 14 patients with a median age of 38 years and few comorbidities were included. The organ failure most commonly associated with respiratory involvement was acute kidney injury (93%). The median delay between mechanical ventilation and ECMO support was 0 (0-1) days. The median duration of ECMO support was short (7 [4-12] days). The mortality rate in this population was 29%. A systematic literature review revealed 50 cases of patients with leptospirosis requiring ECMO, with a median age of 34 years and a mortality rate of 20%. The favorable prognosis of patients with refractory ARDS due to leptospirosis justifies the use of ECMO. Early referral to a center equipped with ECMO is essential, given the rapid decline in respiratory function.

title: Time-Varying Spatial Ventricular Gradient Orientation Is Associated With Anthracycline Heart Failure.
authorString: Rosas Diaz AN, Stabenau HF, Tung P, Nelson J, Hurtado GP, Warack S, Alilou S, Sau A, Peters NS, Ng FS, Upshaw JN, Kramer DB, Asnani A, Waks JW.
abstractText:
Background

Anthracycline use is limited by cardiotoxicity resulting in heart failure (HF). The spatial ventricular gradient (SVG) is a vectorcardiographic measurement of myocardial electrical heterogeneity associated with sudden death and incident HF. It is unclear if serial measurement of SVG after anthracycline initiation can help predict subsequent HF.

Objectives

The objective of the study was to determine if time-varying SVG measurements are associated with anthracycline HF.

Methods

Retrospective, single-center study of adult patients with cancer treated with anthracyclines between 1992 to 2019. Standard 12-lead electrocardiograms obtained within 6 months before and up to 5 years after anthracycline initiation were analyzed. Patients with prior HF or ≤1 electrocardiogram within 5 years were excluded. Median vectorcardiograms were constructed, and the SVG vector was obtained by integrating under the X, Y, and Z QRST complexes. Multivariable competing-risks regression was performed with SVG parameters included as time-varying covariates, incident HF as the main outcome, and death as a competing outcome.

Results

Among 594 patients (median age 61 years, 48% male), 83 (14%) developed HF within 5 years. In multivariable competing-risks regression, time-varying SVG azimuth (circular angle in the transverse plane) was independently associated with HF (P = 0.0024), demonstrating a 9.4-fold gradient in risk across values. Leftward/anterior azimuth values were the lowest risk areas, whereas posterior/rightward orientations were the highest risk.

Conclusions

Time-varying SVG azimuth was independently associated with HF risk in patients treated with anthracyclines. Assessing dynamic changes in SVG azimuth during anthracycline treatment may enhance early identification of patients at risk for HF and inform the use of cardioprotective strategies during cancer therapy.

title: Epidemiological comparison of cirrhosis to other long-term health conditions in the United Kingdom.
authorString: Innes H, Morling J, Buch S, Kendall TJ, Fallowfield JA, Guha IN.
abstractText:
Background

Although cirrhosis is a serious long-term health condition (LTC), it tends to receive little attention from healthcare policymakers. Here, we sought to describe how cirrhosis compares to other LTCs to inform priority-setting discussions.

Methods

We analysed data from the Our Future Health (OFH) study, a cohort of ∼1.7 million individuals from England, United Kingdom. Self-reported diagnosis status for cirrhosis and 15 benchmark LTCs (including type 1 diabetes, type 2 diabetes, Parkinson's disease, chronic kidney disease, schizophrenia, and stage 4 cancer) were ascertained from the enrolment questionnaire. Each LTC was profiled with respect to: sociodemographic characteristics; mortality; comorbidity burden; and late diagnosis. Furthermore, information on each LTC's trajectory (i.e., increasing, stable, or decreasing over time) was determined from background mortality data over the last decade.

Results

The study cohort included 1,613,777 participants, of whom 2,606 (0.2%) reported a diagnosis of cirrhosis. Mortality elevation for participants with cirrhosis versus without was substantial (HR: 7.46; P<0.001, with adjustment for age/sex) and comparable to dementia (HR:7.60), stage 4 cancer (HR:7.06), whilst higher than schizophrenia (HR:4.46) and heart failure (HR:4.01). People with cirrhosis had more co-existing health conditions/diseases than other LTCs (i.e., elevated prevalence for 58/145 distinct health conditions; second only to stage 4 cancer). Area-based deprivation score was third highest for cirrhosis, behind COPD and schizophrenia. Late diagnosis of cirrhosis was commonplace, with <15% of new-onset liver failure reporting cirrhosis at enrolment. Cirrhosis also exhibited an upward trajectory, with mortality increasing by ∼20% in the last decade.

Conclusion

Cirrhosis is an anomaly LTC with respect to its deprivation, comorbidity, mortality, upward trajectory, and late diagnosis profile. Our data provide comparative evidence to inform priority-setting discussions with policymakers.

Impact and implications

Various levers are available to policy makers for reducing incidence of liver cirrhosis. However, other health conditions are often prioritised by policy makers ahead of cirrhosis; the decision-making process around this is not always transparent nor grounded in evidence. This study explores the characteristics of cirrhosis relative to other long-term conditions through a public-health lens. Our findings may guide priority-setting discussions between policy makers, advocates and other stakeholders and may shift current discourse onto a more empirical footing.

title: Apnea-hypopnea index-oxygen desaturation index (AHI-ODI) discordance in obstructive sleep apnea: association with symptom burden and cardiometabolic comorbidity: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
authorString: Ehab A, Abdelwahab HW, Hamoda M, Elhosiny MM.
abstractText:
Background

The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) counts respiratory events but not the depth or duration of accompanying desaturation. We examined AHI-ODI discordance (AHI minus oxygen desaturation index, ODI) and its associations with daytime symptom burden and prevalent cardiometabolic comorbidity.

Methods

Single-center retrospective cross-sectional study of 200 adults with OSA (January 2023-January 2025). Five indices (AHI, ODI, mean SpO2, T90 and AHI-ODI discordance) were examined; excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS; Epworth Sleepiness Scale ≥ 11) was the primary outcome. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, BMI and an AHI-ODI × sex interaction.

Results

The cohort was 77.5% male, median age 57 years (48.8-64.2). For EDS, AHI-ODI discordance showed the numerically highest AUC (0.639, p < 0.001), followed by T90 (0.627), and mean SpO2 and ODI (0.609 each); AHI was not significant (0.546, p = 0.264). No pairwise difference was significant. AHI-ODI discordance remained independently associated with EDS after adjustment (OR 1.04 per event/h, 95% CI 1.01-1.07, p = 0.008), with no significant sex interaction. Among secondary outcomes, T90 showed the highest AUCs for diabetes mellitus (0.644) and hypertension (0.615), and mean SpO2 for heart failure (0.608). No index discriminated against previous stroke or atrial fibrillation.

Conclusions

AHI-ODI discordance was independently, but only modestly, associated with EDS, whereas oxygenation indices were related to prevalent cardiometabolic comorbidity. The discrimination was insufficient, and all reported cut-offs are exploratory. AHI-ODI discordance is not a measure of sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden.

title: Integrative analysis of systemic biomarkers and carotid plaque instability in patients with atherosclerosis: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
authorString: Xie C, Hong J, Zhang M, Peng Y, Huang Y.
abstractText: ObjectiveCarotid plaque instability is associated with ischemic stroke; however, its relationship with systemic pathways remains incompletely understood. We explored associations between inflammatory, coagulation, metabolic, and renal biomarkers and ultrasound-defined carotid plaque instability.MethodsThis exploratory, single-center, retrospective cross-sectional association study included patients who underwent carotid ultrasonography between March 2021 and March 2025. Laboratory and imaging variables were compared between stable and unstable plaques. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed in four system-specific models adjusted for age, sex, hypertension, and diabetes mellitus, followed by an integrated analysis. The incremental contribution of CRP and eGFR beyond clinical covariates was explored by comparing discrimination and calibration, with bootstrap resampling used to assess optimism.Results361 patients were included (311 stable; 50 unstable). A history of stroke was more common in the unstable-plaque group (p < 0.05). CRP levels were higher in the unstable-plaque group, whereas eGFR did not differ between groups. In multivariable analyses, no biomarker was independently associated with plaque instability. In the integrated model (n = 326; 43 events), history of stroke was associated with plaque instability (OR = 2.46, 95% CI 1.15-5.25, p = 0.020), whereas CRP (OR = 1.002 per 1 mg/L, 95% CI 0.997-1.007, p = 0.450) and eGFR (OR = 0.999 per 1 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>, 95% CI 0.988-1.011, p = 0.913) were not associated. AUCs were 0.704 for the clinical model and 0.709 for the integrated model (ΔAUC = +0.005), indicating minimal incremental discrimination.ConclusionsHistory of stroke was associated with carotid plaque instability, whereas CRP and eGFR were not independently associated after multivariable adjustment. Adding CRP and eGFR to clinical variables provided minimal incremental discrimination, suggesting limited additional value for distinguishing ultrasound-defined plaque instability. Given the cross-sectional design, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than temporal or causal relationships.

title: Astrocytic glutamate transporter loss drives chemoreflex hyperactivity and cardiorespiratory dysfunction in a heart failure model.
authorString: Diaz-Jara E, Vicencio SC, Pereyra KV, Schwarz KG, Ortiz FC, Toledo C, Bernal-Santander I, Kaur S, El Dakkak B, Del Rio R.
abstractText: Heart failure (HF) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Breathing instability and exaggerated chemoreflex activation contribute to adverse HF outcomes, yet the central mechanisms linking respiratory control to cardiac dysfunction remain poorly defined. The retrotrapezoid nucleus (RTN) is a key brainstem chemosensory region regulating ventilatory and autonomic output, but whether glial dysfunction within this circuit contributes to HF pathophysiology is unknown. We hypothesized that loss of astrocytic glutamate transporter 1 (GLT-1) in the RTN disrupts glutamate homeostasis, producing chemoreflex hyperactivity and cardiorespiratory dysfunction in HF. In a rat model of nonischemic HF, reduced astrocytic GLT-1 expression in the RTN was accompanied by extracellular glutamate accumulation and heightened excitability of chemosensitive neurons. These changes were associated with exaggerated central chemoreflex responses, breathing instability, autonomic imbalance, and impaired cardiac function. Astrocyte-specific GLT-1 restoration normalized RTN glutamate levels, reduced central chemoreceptor neuron hyperexcitability, stabilized breathing, and improved cardiac performance. Systemic riluzole, an FDA-approved glutamate-modulating drug, similarly reduced RTN glutamate accumulation and attenuated chemoreflex-driven respiratory instability. These findings identify loss of astrocytic GLT-1-mediated glutamate homeostasis in the RTN as a mechanism contributing to cardiorespiratory dysfunction in HF and support pharmacological targeting of brainstem glutamate homeostasis as a therapeutic strategy requiring further investigation.

title: Impact of Fixed-Dose Combination Therapies on Cardiovascular Mortality and Major Cardiovascular Events.
authorString: Chia JE, Lee E, Iglesias J, Ang SP.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

Fixed-dose combination therapy (the polypill) was developed to reduce treatment complexity and improve adherence to evidence-based cardiovascular therapies. This review evaluates contemporary evidence for its effects on major cardiovascular events and cardiovascular mortality across primary prevention, secondary prevention, and emerging heart failure applications, while addressing implementation barriers and remaining evidence gaps.

Recent findings

Early pharmacodynamic and adherence trials established that co-formulation preserves the effects of individual components and improves medication adherence. Event-powered trials subsequently demonstrated clinical benefit: PolyIran and TIPS-3 reduced major cardiovascular events in predominantly primary prevention population, whereas SECURE reduced recurrent events after myocardial infarction. Individual-participant and aggregate-data meta-analyses showed relative reductions of approximately 20% to 40% in composite cardiovascular outcomes and a reduction in cardiovascular mortality, with larger benefits among patients with greater adherence and in aspirin-containing strategies. POLY-HF extended the approach to heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, improving left ventricular ejection fraction and uptake of guideline-directed therapy; reductions in heart failure events were secondary findings that require confirmation in larger outcome trials. These findings supports fixed-dose combination therapy as an effective strategy for improving adherence and reducing cardiovascular events, with a cardiovascular mortality benefit supported by pooled analyses. Its greatest potential may be in high-risk populations and resource-limited settings, where treatment complexity impedes implementation. Broader adoption will require formulation standardization, sufficient dosing flexibility, longer-term safety data, and effective integration into clinical guidelines and health systems.

title: Incident Comorbid Diabetes and Outcomes in Multiple Sclerosis: An English Population-Based Cohort Study.
authorString: Lau Y, Zabihi S, Hartmann M, Mathlin G, Banerjee S, Marouf E, Hadley C, Cooper C, Dobson R.

journal.title: Annals of clinical and translational neurology

abstractText:
Objective

To compare the incidence of diabetes mellitus and its associations with hospitalisation and mortality in adults with multiple sclerosis (MS) and matched controls.

Methods

Using English primary care data from the Clinical Practice Research Datalink, linked to hospital and mortality records, we matched adults with MS with up to 10 controls without MS by age, sex and practice. We excluded individuals with pre-existing diabetes mellitus. Outcomes included all-cause hospitalisation (number and duration) and mortality. We used Poisson, negative binomial, linear and Cox proportional hazards models, adjusting for demographic and socioeconomic factors, with interaction terms for ethnicity, deprivation and urbanity.

Results

We included 47,247 individuals with MS and 458,951 matched controls. Over a mean follow-up of 15.2 years, people with MS had a higher incidence of diabetes mellitus (adjusted incidence rate ratio = 1.16, 95% confidence interval 1.11-1.21). Among people with MS, incident diabetes mellitus was associated with higher hospitalisation rates (adjusted incidence rate ratio = 1.52, 1.42-1.64), longer hospitalisation duration (median 12 vs. 2 days) and increased mortality (adjusted hazard ratio = 1.41, 1.31-1.49). Similar patterns were observed among controls. The association between diabetes mellitus and increased hospitalisation was stronger in rural areas among those with MS and in White groups among controls.

Interpretation

MS was associated with a higher incidence of diabetes mellitus, which was in turn associated with greater hospitalisation and mortality. These findings may support consideration of equitable screening, prevention and management of diabetes mellitus in people living with MS.

title: Dynamic Changes in Serum Glial Fibrillary Acidic Protein Levels Predicts Early Neurological Deterioration After Intravenous Thrombolysis in Minor Stroke.
authorString: Zhou J, Qu Y, Abuduxukuer R, Zhang P, Wang T, Gao JH, Pan DW, Yuan ZM, Li CY, Chen LP, Chen JH, Gu JL, Wang AY, Jiang LG, Liu L, Jiang YF, Wang CF, Jia Y, Xin H, Jiang CL, Qi YB, Hu XF, Li S, Jin H, Guo ZN, Yang Y, Biomarkers of Brain Injury Investigator Study Group.

journal.title: Annals of clinical and translational neurology

abstractText:
Objective

Minor strokes may be associated with early neurological deterioration (END) and disabilities. The objective was to investigate the role of serum glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) levels in predicting END.

Methods

Data originated from a multicenter cohort study conducted prospectively. ΔGFAP was calculated as the ratio of post-thrombolysis GFAP at 24 h to baseline GFAP. Univariable and multivariable binary logistic regression analyses were performed to assess the association between ∆GFAP and END, and a nomogram was established to illustrate its predictive value.

Results

END occurred in 20 (7.35%) of the 272 patients with minor stroke who underwent intravenous thrombolysis (IVT). Elevated ∆GFAP was independently associated with END (OR, 3.50; 95% CI, 1.67 to 7.31; p < 0.001), even after adjusting for confounders (adjusted OR, 4.64; 95% CI, 1.86 to 11.54; p < 0.001). Furthermore, a model combining ∆GFAP, age, and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score at admission demonstrated a good predictive value for END (AUC = 0.77; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.89).

Interpretation

∆GFAP is a strong, independent predictor of END in patients with minor strokes. Integrating ∆GFAP, age, and NIHSS score into a prognostic model results in a good discriminative ability for predicting END.

title: Association between thyroid feedback quantile-based index and the risk of in-hospital amputation in patients with diabetic foot ulcer.
authorString: Wang J, Huang Y, Wang F, Lao M, Lan L, Liang P.
abstractText:
Aims

To investigate the relationship between the thyroid feedback quantile-based index (TFQI) and the risk of amputation during hospitalization in patients with diabetic foot ulcers (DFU).

Methods

This single-center retrospective study included 381 hospitalized patients with DFU and normal thyroid function. Logistic regression assessed continuous TFQI and quartiles. Model 1 was unadjusted; Model 2 adjusted for age, sex, BMI, and smoking; Model 3 additionally adjusted for diabetes duration, HbA1c, diabetic peripheral neuropathy, peripheral arterial disease, hypertension, CRP, and dyslipidemia. RCS assessed dose-response patterns; Firth regression was used for sensitivity analysis.

Results

Fifty-six patients underwent amputation. In Model 3, each 1-SD increase in TFQI (equivalent to a 1-unit increase in pre-scaled TFQI) was associated with higher odds of amputation (OR 2.27, 95% CI 1.63-3.15; P < 0.001). Compared with Q1, ORs were 2.94 (0.98-8.83; P = 0.055), 5.60 (1.88-16.67; P = 0.002), and 14.79 (5.22-41.89; P < 0.001) for Q2, Q3, and Q4, respectively. RCS showed an overall association (P = 0.002) and nonlinearity (P = 0.046) in Model 3. Firth estimates were broadly consistent with conventional regression.

Conclusion

Among hospitalized DFU patients with normal thyroid function, higher TFQI levels are associated with an increased risk of amputation during hospitalization. Nevertheless, the clinical utility of TFQI requires further validation in prospective studies.

title: Long-term ozone exposure and adverse outcomes in atrial fibrillation: the population-based ARS-PARTICLES cohort.
authorString: Wang C, Lip GYH, Jemielita P, Święczkowski M, Kurasz A, Zhao D, Han B, Kuźma Ł.
abstractText:
Introduction

Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) remain at high risk of cerebrovascular and cardiovascular events, but evidence on long-term ozone (O3) exposure in this population is limited.

Objectives

We examined whether long-term O3 exposure was associated with adverse cerebrovascular and cardiovascular outcomes.

Patients and methods

We analyzed the population-based ARS-PARTICLES cohort of 20757 adults with prevalent AF residing in Podlaskie Voivodeship, northeastern Poland, in 2014, with follow-up through December 31, 2019. O3, nitrogen dioxide and fine particulate matter concentrations were estimated using the GEM-AQ model and assigned by residential municipality. The primary endpoint was a composite of ischemic stroke, transient ischemic attack or ischemic stroke-related death; cardiovascular mortality was the key secondary endpoint. Associations were estimated using Fine-Gray competing-risk models with annually updated previous-year O3 exposure, adjusted for clinical characteristics, meteorology, area-level socioeconomic status, co-pollutants and outdoor artificial light at night.

Results

The mean (SD) age was 72.6 (11.5) years, and 52.9% were women. The median follow-up was 5.6 years (interquartile range [IQR], 2.8-6), during which 3,139 primary composite events and 5,400 cardiovascular deaths occurred. The median annual O₃ concentration was 43.48 μg/m³ (IQR, 42.6-46.63). Each IQR increase in annually updated O₃ exposure (4.03 μg/m³) was associated with higher risks of the primary composite endpoint (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR], 1.27; 95% CI, 1.02-1.59), cardiovascular mortality (sHR, 1.14; 95% CI, 1.01-1.29), and ischemic stroke (sHR, 1.38; 95% CI, 1.08-1.77). Associations were directionally consistent across adjustment strategies and sensitivity analyses.

Conclusions

Long-term O3 exposure was associated with higher cerebrovascular and cardiovascular risks in patients with AF. O3 may contribute to residual risk in this clinically vulnerable population and warrants evaluation in other high-risk cardiovascular cohorts.

title: Deep Learning-Based 3D CT Body Composition Is Associated With Mortality in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
authorString: Hadzic I, Brendel JM, Mayrhofer T, Jung M, Cooke LH, Kolossvary M, Yucel E, Ersözlü S, Juhasz V, Langenbach IL, Langenbach MC, Patel NK, Abohashem S, Raghu VK, Ghoshhajra B, Hedgire S, Nikolaou K, Tawakol A, Lu MT, Douglas PS, Aerts HJWL, Foldyna B.
abstractText:
Background

Recent advances in artificial intelligence enable fully automated 3-dimensional computed tomography (CT)-based body composition quantification. We investigated whether automated CT-derived thoraco-abdominopelvic body composition measures are associated with mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement.

Methods

In this retrospective multicenter study, consecutive patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement with preprocedural CT imaging were included between 2014 and 2023. A deep learning-based pipeline performed automated 3-dimensional segmentation of thoraco-abdominopelvic noncontrast CT scans to quantify volumes (L/m2) and attenuations (Hounsfield units) of subcutaneous adipose tissue, visceral adipose tissue, muscular adipose tissue, and lean skeletal muscle, indexed to body surface area. Associations with mortality were evaluated using Cox models and Harrell C statistics, adjusting for demographics (age, sex, body mass index) and cardiometabolic risk factors (hypertension, diabetes, chronic renal failure).

Results

Among 915 patients (median age, 84 years [interquartile range, 77-90]; 58% men), 160 (17.5%) died over a median follow-up of 22 months (interquartile range, 14-36). Restricted cubic spline analyses demonstrated that lower subcutaneous adipose tissue volume and higher adipose tissue attenuation were associated with increased mortality, whereas higher skeletal muscle volume and attenuation were associated with improved survival. Addition of body composition measures provided incremental discriminatory value beyond demographics and cardiometabolic risk factors (Harrell C, 0.66 versus 0.71; P<0.001).

Conclusions

Automated 3-dimensional CT-derived body composition measures provide independent prognostic information and improve risk stratification for mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Low subcutaneous adipose tissue volume and higher adipose tissue attenuation identify patients at increased risk, whereas higher skeletal muscle volume and attenuation are associated with lower mortality.

title: Short- and long-term effects of dronedarone on Cav3.1- and Cav3.2-T-type calcium channel current.
authorString: Jiang X, Xu J, He H, Cao Z, Liu D, Chen Z, Ding L, Zheng M.
abstractText: T-type calcium channels (TTCCs), including the Cav3.1 and Cav3.2 subtypes, play a critical role in regulating cardiac electrical activity. Their abnormal expression is closely associated with arrhythmias and cardiac dysfunction caused by myocardial infarction (MI). Dronedarone, a multi-target antiarrhythmic drug, is widely used to treat atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter but has shown adverse effects under pathological conditions such as MI. This study aims to investigate the direct effects and underlying mechanisms of dronedarone on TTCCs. Using neonatal rat cardiomyocytes, HEK293T cells transfected with Cav3.1 and Cav3.2, and MI rat model, we systematically analyzed the effects of dronedarone on TTCC activity. Dronedarone significantly inhibited Cav3.2 channel activity with an IC50 of 9.20 µM, while its effect on Cav3.1 was weaker (IC50 = 46.41 µM). Chronic treatment with dronedarone also slowed the activation and inactivation kinetics of TTCCs. In vivo experiments demonstrated that dronedarone exacerbated myocardial damage and fibrosis in the MI model. These findings suggest that dronedarone inhibits TTCC activity, particularly the Cav3.2 subtype, and alters its kinetic properties. This study reported the electrophysiological effects of dronedarone on T-type calcium channels, providing new insights into its electrophysiological properties and potential role in adverse cardiac events.

title: Social Isolation and Loneliness Across the Cardiovascular Disease Spectrum: A Narrative Review of Evidence, Mechanisms, and Clinical Implications.
authorString: Kaushik S, Naeem IA, Nandyal S, Gajjar R, Nubla A, Tasamma AT, Imran A, Salama B, Frishman WH, Aronow WS.
abstractText: Social isolation is the objective paucity of social ties; loneliness is the subjective distress of relationships falling short of what one desires. Both are common, affecting roughly a quarter to a third of older adults, and both have cardiovascular consequences through several mechanisms, with some estimates suggesting an increase of 29% in coronary heart disease risk and 21-23% in heart failure hospitalization. We review the evidence for social isolation and loneliness' impact on cardiovascular disease separately for ischemic heart disease, heart failure, arrhythmia and sudden cardiac death, and stress- and substance-related cardiomyopathies. We also highlight plausible mechanisms by which social isolation and loneliness are linked to downstream adverse cardiovascular events, limitations with existing evidence, societal guidance, and policy frameworks currently aimed at addressing them. The evidence is densest for ischemic heart disease, though the largest cohort shows a 43% excess risk of myocardial infarction attenuating by approximately 84% to nonsignificance after full adjustment, and Mendelian randomization estimates a far smaller effect. The prognostic signal is more consistent than the etiologic one, with low functional social support carrying a pooled hazard ratio of 1.59 in established coronary disease. In heart failure, objective isolation rather than loneliness predicts post-diagnosis mortality, mainly in women, consistent with a self-care-dependent behavioral pathway.

title: Hidden in Plain Sight: Clinical Profile, Diagnosis, and Outcomes of Cardiac Amyloidosis in Cali, Colombia
authorString: Barbosa-Balaguera S, Castaño O, Echeverry EJ, Llano CDM, Muriel Ruiz ÁJ, Díaz JB, Córdoba ÁMT, Ayala-Zapata S, Velásquez-Trujillo LA, Escandón ÁH.
abstractText:
Background:

Cardiac amyloidosis is an increasingly recognized cause of heart failure in older adults, yet Colombian data, and data from the southwest of the country in particular, remain scarce. We describe the clinical, diagnostic, imaging and outcome profile of patients with cardiac amyloidosis at two high-complexity institutions in Cali. Methods Observational, descriptive, retrospective, two-center study. Patients were identified in the institutional registries of both centers using ICD-10 codes for amyloidosis, and clinical data were abstracted manually from medical records. Continuous variables are reported as median (interquartile range) and categorical variables as counts and percentages over the number of patients with available data. Results Thirty-two patients were analyzed (median age 77 years; 68.8% men). Heart failure (90.6%), atrial fibrillation (46.9%) and carpal tunnel syndrome (31.2%) were frequent. The etiological classification depended on the test considered: bone scintigraphy was positive (Perugini 2–3) in 23 of 26 patients studied (88.5%), but a monoclonal protein was screened for in only 22, and the full non-invasive criteria for ATTR were met in 16 of 32 (50.0%). Genetic testing was positive in 9 of 18 tested, and the variant was Val142Ile in all 8 patients in whom it was characterized. The working diagnosis was ATTR in 26 patients (81.2%) and AL in 6 (18.8%). Tafamidis was used in 37.5%. Eleven of the 31 patients with known vital status died (35.5%), and NT-proBNP was markedly higher among those who died (6640 vs 1186 pg/mL; p=0.003). Conclusions In this southwestern Colombian cohort, cardiac amyloidosis presented as the classic transthyretin phenotype, with the Val142Ile variant in all 8 patients in whom it was characterized. Bone scintigraphy was frequently positive, but screening for a monoclonal protein was often omitted, so only half the cohort met the full non-invasive criteria for ATTR. Mortality was high and closely associated with NT-proBNP.

title: Multimorbidity and cardiometabolic clustering among university employees: findings from a comprehensive health assessment program in India
authorString: Jagtap AH, Ingole Patil AS, Kudale AM.
abstractText:
Abstract Objective To estimate the burden and patterns of multimorbidity and cardiometabolic multimorbidity among university employees undergoing a comprehensive health assessment programme, and to examine demographic and behavioural factors associated with multimorbidity. Design Cross-sectional study. Setting A public university in Maharashtra, India. Participants A total of 266 university employees who underwent a comprehensive health assessment were included. Main outcome measures Multimorbidity was defined as the presence of two or more of nine chronic conditions: hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidaemia, ischaemic heart disease, chronic kidney disease, thyroid disease, stroke, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and cancer. Cardiometabolic multimorbidity was defined as the presence of two or more of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidaemia, ischaemic heart disease and chronic kidney disease. Results Hypertension was identified in 119 participants (44.7%), comprising 50 participants with pre-existing hypertension and 69 newly identified during the assessment. Dyslipidaemia was present in 189 (71.1%) and diabetes mellitus in 45 (16.9%). Overall, 108 participants (40.6%) had multimorbidity and 103 (38.7%) had cardiometabolic multimorbidity. The prevalence of multimorbidity increased progressively with age, from 17.5% among participants aged <30 years to 83.3% among those aged ≥60 years. The predominant exact multimorbidity patterns were hypertension with dyslipidaemia alone (49 participants) and hypertension, diabetes mellitus and dyslipidaemia (27 participants). Overall, 173 participants (65.0%) had at least one newly identified hypertension, diabetes mellitus or dyslipidaemia diagnosis. In multivariable logistic regression, age (adjusted OR [aOR] 1.058 per year, 95% CI 1.027 to 1.091), BMI (aOR 1.163 per kg/m2, 95% CI 1.076 to 1.257) and tobacco use (aOR 3.296, 95% CI 1.377 to 7.888) were independently associated with multimorbidity. The model had an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.731. Conclusion Multimorbidity affected approximately two in five university employees, with cardiometabolic conditions accounting for most of the observed disease clustering. Comprehensive health assessment identified a substantial burden of previously unrecognised chronic disease. Integrating institutional or occupational health assessment with longitudinal primary care follow-up may provide an opportunity for earlier detection, risk-factor modification and coordinated management of multimorbidity.

Keywords:

Multimorbidity; cardiovascular diseases; hypertension; diabetes mellitus; dyslipidaemia; occupational health; university employees; India

title: Towards Non-Invasive Multiparameter Monitoring from a Single Fingertip Photoplethysmogram: Prototype Design and Preliminary Evaluation of Heart Rate, SpO2, Blood Pressure, and Glucose Estimation
authorString: Noman M, Rehman HU, Ahsen M, Afzal R, Zulfiqar MH, Iqbal N.
abstractText: Diabetes mellitus and hypertension are leading causes of morbidity and premature mortality, yet routine monitoring depends on fingerstick glucometry and pneumatic cuffs, which limit adherence. This paper presents the design and a preliminary, small-cohort evaluation of a low-cost prototype that derives heart rate (HR), peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2), systolic/diastolic blood pressure (SBP/DBP), and blood glucose (BG) estimates from a single fingertip photoplethysmogram (PPG). The hardware combines a MAX30102 dual-wavelength sensor (660 nm red, 940 nm infrared), an ATmega328P-based Arduino Nano, and a 3D-printed light-shielding enclosure. The signal pipeline uses lower-envelope detrending and zero-phase Butterworth filtering. HR is obtained by peak detection, SpO2 by the red/infrared ratio of ratios, and cuffless BP by first-derivative timing and amplitude features. For glucose, autoregressive, Teager–Kaiser energy, spectral-entropy, log-energy, and single-pulse morphological features were supplied to Linear Regression (LR), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Random Forest (RF) regressors. Data came from 30 fasting volunteers (32 recordings of 30 s each) with fingerstick glucometer, oscillometric cuff, and commercial pulse-oximeter references. On this dataset RF gave the lowest error (RMSE 11.11 mg/dL, MAE 7.85 mg/dL, R² = 0.8655) and 74.19% three-band classification accuracy, versus RMSE 24.31 and 26.45 mg/dL for LR and KNN. HR and SpO2 agreed closely with the references, and a single resting BP trial differed from the cuff by about 1.4 mmHg. Because the cohort is small, validation was limited, and glucose may be confounded by correlated physiological variables, these results demonstrate feasibility only. Subject-independent validation, Clarke/Parkes error-grid analysis, and a larger multi-day study are required before any clinical claim can be made.

title: Heart-rate-based clock alignment in intensive-care ECGs, serial-ECG matching and administrative follow-up in MIMIC-IV
authorString: Probst L.
abstractText: Objective: To audit the timing, matching and observation requirements of serial electrocardiogram (ECG) studies that use routine clinical records in an intensive-care subset (9% of recordings). Approach: We used two person-disjoint, previously inspected development partitions of MIMIC-IV-ECG linked to MIMIC-IV. Intensive care unit (ICU) heart-rate alignment was assessed against identifiability criteria, simulated offsets and two null constructions. Pairs: development, internal assessment. Main results: Offsets were identifiable for 392 of 17,067 (2.3%) and 145 of 5,846 (2.5%) ICU-linked people; 91% were lost before estimation. Among people with at least three complete ECGs, the criteria were met in 27.1% as observed and in 19% to 22% under null constructions that weaken the alignment. Only 0.5% of ICU-linked people (117 of 1,979, 5.9%) had an offset with additional algorithmic support, not a calibrated uncertainty. Of the identifiable, 67.1% and 70.3% lay within ± 60 min (86% in simulation at zero offset), so the missed 90% criterion tested the procedure, not the clocks. Potassium matching limits rose from 352 and 69 to 562 and 136 sets when the baseline tolerance widened from 0.3 to 1.0 mmol/L. With exact timestamps, 34.6% and about 36% of index discharges had no later ECG or hospital discharge (36.7% and about 38% including deaths dated on or before discharge; emergency visits not counted as contact), and the follow-up span ended before 365 days in 26.4% and 25.6% of people with later contact and no documented atrial fibrillation or flutter (AF). A control in MC-MED (emergency department), locked before analysis and not a validation, missed its prespecified threshold (28.3% of 11,913 eligible visits), neither confirming nor refuting the MIMIC results. Significance: Individual clock offsets were rarely identifiable by heart-rate matching against intermittently charted rates. Matching counts depend on tolerances, and absent later contact is not absent events.

title: <span data-teams="true">Availability and Access to Cardiovascular Medicines in Mozambique: A Scoping Review
authorString: Manguele M, Sitoe U, Muchanga M, Dique E, Cumbe A, Michal S, Manjate E, Cuinica G, Monjane D, Cumbe G, Andarusse T, Ngovene A, Muchanga I.
abstractText: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are a leading cause of mortality worldwide, with more than 80% of deaths occurring in low- and middle-income countries. In Mozambique, non-communicable diseases account for approximately 28% of deaths, with CVDs contributing substantially to this burden. Despite the country’s hierarchical health system and the World Health Organization target of 80% availability of essential medicines, access to cardiovascular medicines remains poorly documented. This scoping review mapped the availability, prices, affordability, physical access, and health-system barriers affecting access to essential cardiovascular medicines in Mozambique. The review followed the PRISMA-ScR guidelines and the Arksey and O’Malley framework. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were systematically searched without publication-year restrictions. Eligible studies assessed the availability, stock-outs, prices, affordability, or health-system barriers related to cardiovascular medicines and diagnostics in Mozambique. Study selection and data extraction were independently performed by multiple reviewers. Consistent with the scoping review design, formal risk-of-bias assessment was not undertaken. Fifteen studies met the inclusion criteria. Essential cardiovascular medicines showed persistently low availability, with mean availability of approximately 21% across public hospital pharmacies, private retail outlets, and private hospitals, substantially below the WHO 80% target. Public facilities consistently provided only a limited range of older first-line medicines, while second- and third-line medicines, statins, digoxin, direct oral anticoagulants, and diagnostic reagents were frequently unavailable. When public stocks were depleted, patients relied on private-sector purchases, where generic medicines cost an average of 4.51 times international reference prices. Long-term secondary prevention could require 14.0–17.8 days of wages per month for low-income workers. These barriers were associated with low hypertension awareness, treatment, and control, substantial target-organ damage, high stroke case-fatality, and poor anticoagulation control. Access to cardiovascular medicines in Mozambique is severely constrained by low availability, frequent stock-outs, and unaffordable private-sector prices. Strengthening medicine selection, supply-chain management, financial protection, and decentralized protocol-based care is essential to improve equitable access to cardiovascular treatment.

title: Hydatid Pulmonary Embolism: A 25-Year Single-Center Case Series with Review of Current Management
authorString: Amina A, Bouassida I, Ben Amara K, HADJDAHMEN M, HABBOURIA C, AZABOU N, SOUILHI J, Hazem Z, Mahdi A, MARGLI A.
abstractText:
Introduction:

Hydatid pulmonary embolism is a rare but serious complication of cystic echinococcosis. It most often results from the rupture of a cardiac hydatid cyst into the right chambers or, more rarely, from the extension of a hepatic cyst into the inferior vena cava with embolic migration to the pulmonary arteries. Diagnosis is difficult due to non-specific clinical presentation. Methods We conducted a retrospective study including patients treated for hydatid pulmonary embolism in the thoracic and cardiovascular surgery department between 2000 and 2024. Clinical, radiological, therapeutic and evolutionary data were analysed. Results Nine patients were identified (5 women, 4 men), with a mean age of 39 years (19–64 years). All were symptomatic. The diagnosis was based on chest computed tomography and/or pulmonary angiography. The involvement was right-sided in six cases, left-sided in one case and bilateral in two cases. Six patients had an associated hepatic cyst and two had cardiac involvement. Eight patients underwent surgery (lobectomy, segmentectomy, pneumonectomy or embolectomy with cystectomy). One patient died before surgery due to compressive pericardial effusion. The average length of postoperative hospitalisation was four days, with no immediate complications. At follow-up (6 months to 7 years), the majority of patients were stable. One late death due to acute heart failure occurred at 12 months and one recurrence was observed at 7 years. Conclusion Hydatid pulmonary embolism is a rare condition with a potentially severe prognosis. Surgical treatment remains central. The role of adjuvant medical treatment with albendazole remains to be clarified.

title: Beyond stroke: atrial fibrillation and the broader burden of thromboembolic events in the population-based EpiHealth study.
authorString: Höiby P, Zarrouk M, Lind L, Basna R, Overton MC, Elmståhl S.
abstractText:
Objectives

To investigate the distribution and risk of thromboembolic events (TEs) among adults with and without atrial fibrillation (AF), and to assess oral anticoagulant (OAC) use over time.

Design

This population-based longitudinal cohort study included EpiHealth participants recruited between April 2011 and December 2016 and followed through linkage to Swedish health data registers from baseline until the first TE, death, or December 31, 2016.

Results

At baseline, 873 of 22,616 participants (3.9%) had AF and 297 developed incident AF during follow-up. 484 participants experienced at least one TE during 70,587 person-years. Participants with AF had higher TE incidence (68 events, 5.9%; p < 0.001), predominantly arterial (73.5%), with 94% of arterial events involving the cerebral circulation. Approximately one quarter of TEs among participants with AF occurred outside the cerebral circulation and comprised both venous and non-cerebral arterial events. Although participants with incident AF represented less than one quarter of participants with AF, they accounted for 40% of TEs in the AF group. OAC use increased from 39.0% to 50.4%, with a shift from predominantly warfarin to direct oral anticoagulants. In time-dependent Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, and prior arterial thromboembolism, untreated AF was associated with increased thromboembolic risk compared with no AF (HR 2.53), whereas OAC use was associated with lower risk.

Conclusions

AF was associated with substantially increased thromboembolic risk, predominantly arterial in nature. One in five TEs among participants with AF coincided with newly diagnosed AF, suggesting potential opportunities for earlier AF detection and timely initiation of anticoagulant treatment.

title: Restoration of full length filamin C is sufficient to prevent FLNC deficient cardiomyopathy in mice.
authorString: Jiang Z, Feng W, Chen Z, Bogomolovas J, Li M, Ye M, Gu Y, Zhou X, Chen J.
abstractText: Filamin C (FLNC) is an essential cytoskeletal protein required for cardiomyocyte structural integrity and mechanotransduction. Truncating FLNC variants cause haploinsufficiency associated with dilated and arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathies, yet no therapies currently address the underlying defect of FLNC deficiency. Gene replacement is challenging because the approximately 8.2-kb FLNC coding sequence exceeds the packaging capacity of conventional adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors. Here, we engineered a triple-AAV strategy optimized for full-length FLNC reconstitution in the heart. Screening in HEK293 cells identified GP41-1 and IMPDH as a compatible orthogonal pair for efficient full-length FLNC reconstitution. In tamoxifen-inducible, cardiomyocyte-specific Flnc knockout mice, systemic delivery of optimized MyoAAV2A vectors restored full-length FLNC expression and re-established sarcomeric localization following cardiomyocyte FLNC depletion. A total vector dose of 1 × 10¹³ genome copies/kg restored FLNC to approximately endogenous abundance, preserved systolic function and ventricular dimensions, limited cardiac enlargement, attenuated fibrotic remodeling and prevented premature death. FLNC replacement also attenuated pathological transcriptional remodeling and compensatory changes in cytoskeletal and junction-associated proteins. These findings demonstrate that systemic split-intein-mediated reconstitution of full-length FLNC can preserve cardiac structure and function in vivo, providing preclinical support for a mutation-independent therapeutic strategy for FLNC-associated cardiomyopathy.

title: Rev-erbα inhibits vascular calcification by repressing osteogenic reprogramming in atherosclerosis
authorString: Ferri L, Bellengier C, Diedisheim M, Bongiovanni A, Julla J, Delhaye S, Kara-Ali G, Duhem C, Farge S, Thorel Q, Hebras A, Leduc M, Quemener S, Eberlé D, Dombrowicz D, Dupont A, Susen S, Rosa M, Germain S, Sebti Y, Tardivel M, Venteclef N, Haas J, Staels B, Gauthier J, Duez H, Pourcet B.
abstractText:
Background

Atherosclerotic plaque rupture is the most deleterious atherogenic event, responsible for the majority of fatal acute atherothrombotic and myocardial infarctions. Intimal microcalcification is a major cause of atherosclerotic plaque instability. Yet, a thorough characterization of the mechanisms controlling intimal calcification is needed to develop innovative therapeutic strategies to treat high risk patients. The nuclear receptor Rev-erbα regulates lipoprotein metabolism and exerts anti-inflammatory activities. Here, we hypothesized that Rev-erbα modulates atherogenesis by regulating arterial calcification processes.

Methods

We used a multi-omics approach in the ANGIOSAFE and the ATHEROPORTAL human cohort to identify pathways and factors associated with vascular calcification in diabetic patients. We then compared REV-ERBα expression between calcified and non-calcified areas of human endarterectomies using laser capture microdissection assays (n=11-22/group). We further assessed the functional role of Rev-erbα on calcium deposition and expression of osteoblast markers in aortic roots of 18-month-old Ldlr –/– Rev-erbα –/– and Ldlr –/– Rev-erbα +/+ mice (n=10/group). Rev-erbα -dependent molecular pathways that drive calcification were identified using gene expression profiling in aortic plaques from Ldlr –/– Rev-erbα –/– and Ldlr –/– Rev-erbα +/+ mice (n=8–10/group). We then confirmed omics data in vitro using primary aortic smooth muscle cells (SMCs) (n=3-6) and assessing inflammation-driven calcification process as well as Rev-erbα-dependent transcriptional mechanisms.

Results

In the ANGIOSAFE cohort (n=668), REV-ERBα expression is significantly lower in circulating classical CD14 + CD16 - monocytes from diabetic patients with low coronary artery calcium (CAC) compared to those exhibiting high CAC scores. In human atheromatous lesions from the AtheroPortal cohort (N=968), REV-ERBα expression is lower in highly calcified plaques from patients with diabetes mellitus compared to those with no diabetes or no calcification. Consistently, in laser capture microdissection experiments, REV-ERBα expression is markedly lower in calcified areas of human endarterectomy samples, compared to non-calcified regions. Rev-erbα deficient 18-months-old Ldlr −/− mice exhibit accelerated atherogenesis and vascular calcification, and aortic smooth muscle cells (SMCs) exhibit an extensive reprogramming toward an osteochondroblastic phenotype. Functional in vitro studies show that Rev-erbα maintains SMC identity by preventing their IL-1β-driven transdifferentiation into osteochondroblast-like cells, notably through the repression of key osteogenic regulators, including Runx2, Spp1, Osterix and Sox9 . Finally, we demonstrate that Rev-erbα represses the hyaluronidase Cemip expression during SMC transdifferentiation. Because hyaluronic acid degradation promotes intimal calcification, we provide here a mechanistic link between Rev-erbα activity, extracellular matrix remodelling, and vascular calcification.

Conclusions

Rev-erbα is identified as an important brake on SMC-driven vascular calcification, suppressing both osteogenic reprogramming and matrix-remodeling pathways. Thus, this study opens new avenues for developing novel therapeutic tools targeting Rev-erbα to reduce vascular calcification and associated cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients.

title: Early and follow-up results of reinterventions for type 2 endoleak following endovascular repair of abdominal aortic aneurysm (EVAR): the multicenter REinterventions for Type 2 Endoleak (RETE) study.
authorString: Falso R, Speziali S, Perini P, Leone N, Esposito D, Campolmi M, Kahlberg AL, Troisi N, Dorigo W, Pulli R, RETE study collaborators.
abstractText:
Background

Type II endoleak (T2EL) is frequent after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR) and may require reintervention in selected patients. However, the optimal treatment strategy for durable resolution remains uncertain. The aim of this study is to retrospectively analyze perioperative and long-term results of T2Els' reinterventions, both endovascular and open surgical, in a large patient cohort from twenty high-volume academic centers.

Methods

A retrospective analysis of consecutive patients undergoing first reintervention for T2ELs was conducted across 20 centers over a 10-year period. Patients requiring concomitant treatment for other endoleak types were excluded. A total of 403 patients were included. Primary outcomes included technical success, 30-day AAA-related mortality and reintervention-free survival during follow-up. Secondary outcomes were perioperative complications, early reintervention, overall survival, freedom from aneurysm-related death and rupture, freedom from recurrent endoleaks, freedom from open conversion or semi-conversion in patients previously treated endovascularly and sac behavior during follow-up. Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox regression analyses were performed to analyze follow-up results.

Results

Patients were predominantly male (90%) with a mean age of 77 years. Reintervention was indicated for sac enlargement in 94.5% of cases; 4% presented with rupture. Median time from EVAR to reintervention was 4.3 years. Lumbar arteries (55%) and the inferior mesenteric artery (35%) were the main sources. Endovascular treatment was performed in 86% and open conversion/semi-conversion in 14%. Technical success was 96%, with 1% mortality and 4% major complications. Overall survival was 80.5% and rupture-free survival 79.2% at 5 years. Recurrent T2EL occurred in 64.2%, and reintervention-free survival was 48.3%. Endovascular group showed significantly lower freedom from reintervention rates when compared to open conversion/semi conversion group (42.4% vs 86.8%, SE 0.04 vs SE 0.05, p<0.001, log-rank 15.9). Conversion/semi-conversion after endovascular treatment occurred in 14%. No differences were recorded comparing different fabric materials of the endograft in terms of freedom for reintervention and freedom from open surgery. A sac diameter ≥7 cm at the time of reintervention predicted further reinterventions, while primary open treatment improved durability.

Conclusions

Reinterventions for T2ELs are safe, with satisfactory immediate technical success and low perioperative mortality. During follow-up, risks of rupture and AAA-related death remain low. However, the endoleak recurrence rate exceeds 60% at five years, necessitating reintervention in over 40% of patients. Early intervention for patients with a sac diameter approaching 7 cm can be suggested, while a primary open approach may be considered in low-risk patients.

title: Computer tomography imaging for suspected acute aortic syndrome.
authorString: Leslie JA, Pisanie LD, Bailey K, Gaine VW, Turner H, Meighan V, Halpenny D, McCabe A.
abstractText:
Background

Acute Aortic Syndrome (AAS) is a life-threatening condition that presents diagnostic challenges due to variable clinical presentations. Limited data exists regarding Computed Tomography Angiography (CTA) utilisation patterns and outcomes for patients with suspected AAS in Irish emergency departments (ED). This study evaluates trends in CTA utilisation and positivity rate for patients with suspected AAS presenting to a level 4 hospital ED.

Methods

A retrospective single-centre chart review was conducted of all adult patients (≥ 16 years) who underwent CTA aorta imaging requested by emergency medicine physicians in Tallaght University Hospital between January 2018 and December 2025. Patient demographics, imaging findings, time metrics, disposition and mortality were analysed.

Results

Among 457,735 ED attendances, 797 eligible CTA aorta studies were performed. There was a 2.86 fold increase in CTA scans done across the study period from 37 studies in 2018 to 106 in 2025. Overall positivity rate for AAS was 2.76% (n = 22). Acute aortic dissection accounted for 77% of positive cases (n = 17), followed by penetrating atherosclerotic ulcers (n = 3) and intramural hematomas (n = 2). Overall mortality among patients with confirmed AAS was 27.27%.

Conclusion

This study highlights the low positivity rate of CTA aorta scans in an Irish ED but high mortality of patients diagnosed with acute aortic syndrome. Increasing CTA utilisation, alongside the overall low incidence of AAS, suggests opportunities to improve diagnostic efficiency.

title: Development of the Readiness to Change Diet Questionnaire (RCdQ) for Assessing Willingness to Adopt Anti-Inflammatory Diet Among Coronary Artery Disease Patients.
authorString: Chauhan S, Singh A, Kaur S, Bhushan S, Ghosh-Jerath S, Roy A.

journal.title: Health education & behavior : the official publication of the Society for Public Health Education

abstractText: This study aimed to develop and validate a questionnaire to assess readiness to change for adopting an anti-inflammatory diet among patients with coronary artery disease. The Readiness to Change Questionnaire-Treatment Version (RCQ-TV) was adapted for dietary behavior, translated into Hindi, and evaluated using an e-Delphi approach for face validation. The study was conducted in the National Capital Region, India. Domain experts (n = 6) assessed the clarity, content, and structure of the adapted questionnaire across iterative rounds, and consensus-driven revisions were made. The validated tool was subsequently pilot tested among 25 participants. Scores for each stage of change were calculated using an established scoring template, with the highest scale score indicating stage of readiness. Open-ended expert feedback from each iteration was summarized to inform revisions, and internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach's alpha. Modifications included simplification of terminology, revision of instructions and specific items, addition of definitions, and simplification of the Hindi version. Pilot testing classified two participants in the pre-contemplation stage, 10 in contemplation, and 13 in the action stage. The questionnaire demonstrated acceptable internal consistency (Cronbach's α = .73). Participants reported the tool to be concise, with instructions, definitions, items, and response options understandable, relevant, and appropriate, although 10 participants required assistance to complete it. Overall, the adapted questionnaire demonstrated satisfactory face validity, internal consistency, and usability in both English and Hindi, suggesting wide applicability for assessing readiness to change dietary behavior in populations.

title: Sonographic Diagnosis and Anatomic Mapping of a Radial Artery Pseudoaneurysm Following Transradial Cardiac Catheterization.
authorString: Franco MF, Rizzo M, Meiling JB.
abstractText: Radial artery pseudoaneurysm is a rare complication of transradial catheterization. We report a 74-year-old woman on rivaroxaban who developed a pulsatile distal forearm mass 1 day after transradial cardiac catheterization. High-frequency ultrasound showed a rounded extra-arterial lesion (7.6 × 8.9 × 7.0 mm) not involving all wall layers, with thrombus, a discrete communicating neck, turbulent bidirectional "yin-yang" color Doppler, and preserved distal flow. Anatomic mapping showed the lesion abutting adjacent tendons and the palmar cutaneous branch of the median nerve. Surgical excision and microscopic repair succeeded. Sonographic characterization provided anatomic detail that, with clinical and surgical assessment, informed individualized management.

title: Saponin extract from Astragalus membranaceus (Fisch.) Bunge regulates gut-brain axis through intestinal Escherichia coli to reduce cerebral oxidative stress to treat vascular dementia in rodents.
