authorString: Yin W, He C, Gu S, Li L, Bian Y, Lu W, Xie M, Li Z, Yang Z, Wang Q.
abstractText:
Background and purpose

Vascular dementia (VD) is a cognitive dysfunction syndrome caused by cerebrovascular diseases. Astragalus membranaceus (Fisch.) Bunge (AS) has antioxidative, gut microbiota-regulating, and cognitive-improving effects. Escherichia coli (E. coli) abundance is associated with cognitive dysfunction. This study explored the mechanism by which AS improves VD by regulating E. coli along the gut-brain axis, providing a basis for VD drug research and development.

Experimental approach

VD models were established by permanent ligation of the common carotid artery. Morris water maze, Doppler cerebral blood flow measurement, blood lipid assays, pathological staining, Western blot, and ELISA were used to evaluate AS's protective effects on the brain. 16S rRNA sequencing analyzed gut microbiota to screen differential strains. Metabolomics screened endogenous differential metabolites. Oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) was established to evaluate 5-aminovaleric acid effects on neuronal mitochondrial function and oxidative stress.

Key results

AS significantly improved cognitive dysfunction, restored cerebral blood flow, and attenuated abnormal protein accumulation and oxidative stress in VD rat brains. Microbiota analysis revealed that AS inhibited E. coli proliferation and mitigated associated pathological damage. Furthermore, endogenous metabolite 5-aminovaleric acid alleviated OGD-induced neuronal damage and oxidative stress.

Conclusion and implications

AS can treat cognitive dysfunction and brain injury in rodents, regulate gut microbiota balance, and reduce the contribution of E. coli. Meanwhile, AS-regulated endogenous metabolite 5-aminovaleric acid can also treat OGD-induced nerve cell injury. These findings suggest that AS may be a promising candidate for VD treatment and provide mechanistic insight into gut-brain axis regulation.

title: EXPRESS: Cardio‑Glymphatic Association: Left‑Heart Dysfunction in CSVD and Its Association With Glymphatic‑Related Cognitive Impairment.
authorString: Zhan C, Wang W, Lu X, Xie X, Li Y, Huang CC.

journal.title: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism

abstractText: Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) is a leading cause of vascular cognitive impairment. The glymphatic system, a brain-wide waste clearance pathway, may be impaired in CSVD, but its upstream drivers and role linking systemic factors to cognitive impairment remain unclear. This study explored whether glymphatic dysfunction statistically mediates the association between left-heart dysfunction and cognitive impairment in CSVD. We enrolled 80 CSVD-VCI, 80 CSVD-NCI, and 80 normal controls aged 50-80 years. All participants underwent neuropsychological assessment, cardiac ultrasound (measuring left ventricular ejection fraction [LVEF], left ventricular end-diastolic diameter [LVEDD], and left atrial diameter [LAD]), and brain MRI to measure the DTI-ALPS index of glymphatic activity. The DTI-ALPS index was progressively reduced: NC > CSVD-NCI > CSVD-VCI. It correlated positively with LVEF and negatively with LAD, and was associated with multiple cognitive domains. Mediation analysis suggests that DTI-ALPS statistically significantly mediated the effects of LVEF and LAD on cognitive performance. These cross-sectional findings suggest that glymphatic dysfunction is a key feature of CSVD and may represent a potential correlative link connecting left-heart dysfunction to cognitive impairment, consistent with a potential cardio-glymphatic pathway in CSVD pathophysiology.

title: Perioperative management of acute type A aortic dissection using extended half-life factor IX (Alprolix) in a patient with severe hemophilia B: a case report.
authorString: Kitamura T, Ryu Y, Nakaji S, Taniguchi S.

journal.title: General thoracic and cardiovascular surgery cases

abstractText:
Background

Emergency surgery for acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) in patients with severe hemophilia B is extremely rare, and perioperative coagulation management is a major challenge.

Case presentation

A 63-year-old man with severe hemophilia B (factor IX activity < 1%) was diagnosed with ATAAD and underwent emergency surgery. Replacement therapy with an extended half-life factor IX product (eftrenonacog alfa; Alprolix) was administered targeting a factor IX activity of 80-100%, and total arch replacement was performed. Cardiopulmonary bypass was performed under standard heparinization conditions. Since rapid measurement of factor IX activity was not possible, postoperative replacement therapy was based primarily on the clinical assessment of hemostasis, with serial activated partial thromboplastin time measurements providing supportive information, whereas intraoperative anticoagulation was managed using standard activated clotting time monitoring. Intra- and postoperative bleeding volumes were within ranges comparable to those observed in standard complex aortic surgery, and the postoperative course was uneventful.

Conclusions

The use of an extended half-life factor IX product may be a practical option for perioperative coagulation management during emergency aortic surgery in patients with severe hemophilia B.

title: Massive enlargement of a previously unrecognized bronchogenic cyst over 8 years with intracystic hemorrhage and complex surgical resection: a case report.
authorString: Kobayashi S, Fukui E, Nagata H, Kimura K, Kimura T, Kanou T, Ose N, Shintani Y.

journal.title: General thoracic and cardiovascular surgery cases

abstractText: Bronchogenic cysts are usually asymptomatic and are often detected incidentally; however, they may become symptomatic due to infection, hemorrhage, or enlargement. We report a case of a previously unrecognized bronchogenic cyst that showed substantial enlargement from 4.8 to 13 cm over an 8-year interval, with intracystic hemorrhage, ultimately requiring partial resection of the esophageal muscularis. A man in his 20s presented with upper abdominal pain and nausea. Computed tomography revealed a 13-cm mass extending from below the tracheal bifurcation to the level of the gastric cardia. A CT scan obtained eight years earlier during the evaluation of abdominal pain had shown a 4.8-cm cystic lesion below the tracheal bifurcation, demonstrating substantial enlargement over the intervening period. Although conservative treatment was attempted, compressive symptoms persisted; therefore, surgical resection was performed for definitive diagnosis and symptom relief. Severe inflammatory adhesions necessitated right open thoracotomy with partial resection of the esophageal muscularis. The cyst contained a large hematoma, and histopathological examination confirmed the diagnosis of a bronchogenic cyst with intracystic hemorrhage. This case demonstrates substantial enlargement of a previously unrecognized bronchogenic cyst from 4.8 to 13 cm over an 8-year interval, with intracystic hemorrhage, symptomatic progression, and technically demanding surgical resection. The potential for substantial enlargement and increasing surgical complexity should be considered when determining the timing of resection for bronchogenic cysts.

title: Cardio-renal dysfunction in prediabetes and early type 2 diabetes: insights from myocardial strain and renal Doppler assessment.
authorString: Atef A, Fayed A, El-Haddad H, Fathy M, El Deeb H.
abstractText:
Background

Prediabetes and early type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) may be accompanied by subclinical cardiac and renal injury before overt disease appears. This study evaluated early cardio-renal dysfunction in prediabetes and early T2DM using myocardial strain imaging and renal Doppler assessment.

Methods

This cross-sectional study included 180 participants: 60 with prediabetes, 60 with newly diagnosed T2DM (≤ 2 years), and 60 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Conventional echocardiography and two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography were used to assess left ventricular (LV) function and left atrial (LA) mechanics. Renal vascular resistance was assessed using the Doppler-derived renal resistive index (RRI) and pulsatility index (PI). Glycemic status and albuminuria were evaluated using fasting glucose, oral glucose tolerance testing, HbA1c, and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio.

Results

Compared with controls, participants with prediabetes and T2DM showed early alterations in LV relaxation/filling indices and reduced LA strain. LV ejection fraction was modestly lower, while GLS became progressively less negative across the dysglycemic groups (p < 0.001), consistent with reduced longitudinal myocardial deformation. Renal resistive index (RRI) and pulsatility index (PI) were significantly increased in the dysglycemic groups. RRI correlated positively with E/e', linking higher renal vascular resistance with higher estimated LV filling pressure (r = 0.440, p < 0.001).

Conclusions

Prediabetes and early T2DM were associated with subclinical abnormalities in myocardial mechanics and renal vascular indices despite preserved conventional cardiac and renal function. Myocardial strain and renal Doppler measures may provide complementary phenotypic information, but prospective validation is required before routine clinical application.

title: Comparison of Labeled Dosages Between Japan and the United States for Drugs Approved in Japan from 2020 to 2025.
authorString: Funatogawa T, Yoshida A.
abstractText: Although approved doses in Japan have generally been lower than in Western countries, these differences have been diminished with global drug development. Studies evaluating dose differences between Japan and the United States (US) using post-2010 data are limited, and none have focused on the 2020s. This study characterized labeled dosage differences between Japan and the US for new molecular entities approved during 2020-2025. Major differences were defined as a ≥2-fold difference in the maintenance or maximum dose; all others were classified as minor differences. Of 187 comparable drugs, 38 (20.3%) had dosage differences between Japan and the US: seven drugs (3.7%) showed major differences (three with higher doses in Japan and four with higher doses in the US), and 31 drugs (16.6%) showed minor differences. Common minor differences included initial-dose differences and body weight-based subgroup differences. Nervous system drugs showed the highest proportion of dosage differences (50.0%), followed by alimentary tract and metabolism (31.3%) and cardiovascular system drugs (22.2%). In contrast, dermatological (11.1%), antineoplastic (10.7%), and systemic anti-infective drugs (8.3%) showed lower proportions. No large differences were observed across assessed factors such as dosing types (fixed dose, per body weight) and administration routes. Approximately 20% of drugs approved in Japan during 2020-2025 had dosage differences from those in the US. The proportion of drugs with dosage differences varied across therapeutic areas. Only 3.7% had major differences. These findings may reflect progress in the international harmonization of labeled drug dosages between Japan and the US.

title: Increased Endometrial CD38 and CD138 Positivity in Women with Ectopic Pregnancy History: A Retrospective Study.
authorString: Li Y, Li Y, Chen D, Xie X, Zhang C, Zhong X, Xie M.
abstractText: Ectopic pregnancy (EP) represents the most common gynecological emergency. However, its specific etiology and pathogenesis remain incompletely understood. This retrospective study investigated the correlation between chronic endometritis (CE) markers (CD38 and CD138) in the endometrium and EP. Patients were categorized as follows: women with a history of EP but no prior intrauterine operations (EP Group A; n = 98), women with a history of EP and at least one intrauterine operation (EP Group B; n = 244), and a control group of women with recurrent spontaneous abortion (RSA; n = 267). The prevalence of CD38 and/or CD138 positive cells was 54.1% (53/98) in Group A, 72.5% (177/244) in Group B, and 28.1% (75/267) in the RSA group. Our findings demonstrate a significantly higher rate of CD38 and/or CD138 positivity in the endometrium of women with a history of EP compared to the RSA controls. This result suggests that chronic endometritis may be an underlying pathogenic factor contributing to ectopic pregnancy.

title: Shared variance across FrACT visual tasks: Robust positive associations but inconclusive latent structure.
authorString: Carabba F, Altieri E, Ghiani A, Musa M, Rosengart E, Maniglia M, Battaglini L.
abstractText: A long-standing question in vision science is whether individual differences in visual performance reflect a general visual ability or a set of largely task-specific processes. Previous studies have often reported weak associations across heterogeneous perceptual tasks, challenging the idea of a common visual factor. Here, we asked whether shared variance becomes more evident when visual tasks are conceptually and procedurally similar. One hundred fifty-eight adults completed eight low-level acuity and hyperacuity paradigms implemented in FrACT10: single letter, Landolt C, tumbling E, row of optotypes, flanking rings, frame ring, Vernier two-line, and Vernier three-line tasks. After outlier exclusion, analyses were conducted on 132 participants. Within-session test-retest reliability was moderate for most tasks. Pairwise correlations revealed a broad positive manifold: all correlations were positive, 27 of 28 survived false-discovery-rate correction, and Bayesian analyses provided strong evidence for nonzero associations in most task pairs. However, association strength depended strongly on task similarity, with robust correlations among optotype-based tasks and weaker links between optotype and Vernier paradigms. Exploratory factor analyses indicated substantial shared covariance but failed to support a stable latent structure: A one-factor model fit poorly, whereas two-factor and three-factor solutions produced improper estimates. These findings support an intermediate account of visual individual differences. Visual performance is neither fully independent across tasks nor reducible to a strong general visual factor; instead, commonality appears partial, task-dependent, and shaped by the composition of the task battery. OPEN PRACTICES STATEMENT: The data, data dictionary, analysis code, and rendered analysis reports that support the findings of this study are available on OSF ( https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/AKSN3 ). The study materials are described in the Method section and are based on FrACT10. This study was not preregistered.

title: Association of serum element levels with cardiovascular diseases and type 2 diabetes mellitus risk in a Kurdish population of western Iran.
authorString: Nakhaee S, Tinkov AA, Mansouri B, Ramazani Z, Fooladi K, Elahinia A.

journal.title: Biometals : an international journal on the role of metal ions in biology, biochemistry, and medicine

abstractText: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are a significant public health concern globally. Among the most prevalent NCDs the study aims to explore the association of some elements with the the likelihood of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D) development. In this cross-sectional case control study, 300 individuals with CVDs (n = 110), T2D (n = 70), and a control group (n = 120) from the Ravansar Non-Communicable Disease (RaNCD) cohort in western Iran were examined. The RaNCD cohort is part of the PERSIAN cohort study, consisting of 10,000 adults. Participants aged 35-65 were stratified into three clusters based on their health status. Various elements, including aluminum (Al), calcium (Ca), magnesium (Mg), phosphorus (P), manganese (Mn), potassium (K), cobalt (Co), lithium (Li), boron (B), molybdenum (Mo), and vanadium (V) in the blood serum was performed using the ICP-MS method, and data were analyzed using multivariable techniques, including logistic regression and clustering analysis. Our analysis revealed a notable association between most elements and the risks of CVD and T2D in the logistic regression model after adjusting for age and gender. Specifically, increased odds ratios of CVD and T2D were identified for higher Ca, Mn, Mg, Li, V, Al, P, and Mo levels. In the T2D group, four clusters were identified: Al-B, Mn-Co-Mo, K-P, and V-Li-Ca-Mg. In the CVD group, five clusters were observed: K, B-Co-Mo, Li-Mg, Ca-P, and Mn-Al-V. The study provides valuable insights into the role of some essential elements in the development of CVDs and T2D. The key elements that are most linked to the elevated risk of CVDs and T2D include calcium, manganese, molybdenum, vanadium, lithium, aluminum, phosphorus, and magnesium. Further exploration of the intricate relationships between elements and disease risk could enhance our understanding of preventive strategies and personalized interventions for individuals at risk of CVDs and T2D.

title: Spatial multi-omic atlas profiles early organogenesis of a Carnegie stage 12 human embryo.
authorString: Wang LJ, Yang H, Song J, Zhao R, Liu S, Hou H, Zhang C, Tian H, Gao J, Chen J, Chen ZJ, Zhao H, Liu B, Wu K.
abstractText: Organogenesis marks one of the most dynamic periods of early human embryonic development. Although the morphological features of this period have been described, the underlying transcriptional and metabolic landscapes remain poorly understood owing to the lack of an integrated spatial strategy. We present spatial transcriptomic and metabolomic maps of a Carnegie stage 12 (CS12) human embryo, co-registered with embryonic anatomy to generate a unified spatial multi-omic framework. Unsupervised clustering of the spatial transcriptomic data identified 17 cell populations covering the major organ primordia. Notably, we observed spatially separable hepatocyte- and cholangiocyte-lineage primed transcriptional programmes within the liver primordium, and detected cardiac outflow tract and sinoatrial node progenitors at CS12. Furthermore, integration of gene and metabolite abundance highlighted regional associations between transcription factors and metabolic pathways underpinning lineage specification. Our work presents a spatially resolved multi-omic atlas of a human embryo at the onset of organogenesis.

title: Food insecurity in the development of metabolic diseases.
authorString: Pérez-Escamilla R, Hernández-Cordero S, Franco-Lares B, Lara-Mejía V.
abstractText: This Review discusses the current evidence on the relationship between food insecurity, obesity, metabolic syndrome and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), and identifies potential interventions to mitigate the effect of food insecurity on these conditions. Studies in adults (mainly cross-sectional) have consistently found associations between food insecurity and several cardiometabolic diseases, including obesity (mainly among women), hyperlipidaemia, metabolic syndrome, hypertension, cardiovascular disease and T2DM. These associations represent plausible causal relationships given that food insecurity can be a powerful psycho-emotional stressor that can cause distress, anxiety and depressive symptoms across the life course; poor dietary quality can increase the risk of metabolic syndrome and T2DM through increased visceral adiposity and insulin resistance, inflammation and an unhealthy microbiome; and food insecurity can cause healthcare behavioural trade-offs such as prioritizing purchasing food over medications for T2DM prevention or management. Community-based, healthy lifestyle promotion, early-life nutrition and Food as Medicine programmes could mitigate the negative effect of food insecurity on T2DM risk and metabolic health. There is a need to rigorously evaluate the results of promising large-scale interventions on food insecurity and cardiometabolic health outcomes.

title: PEAK: a phenotype-based classification of genetic variants.
authorString: Maass JG, Schubert T, Sprehe LK, Schaaf CP.
abstractText: Current variant classifications do not capture clinical severity relative to other pathogenic variants in the same gene. We propose phenotype-exceeding-(mono)allelic-knockout (PEAK) as a term for variants associated with a more severe clinical phenotype than that of heterozygous null alleles. This mechanism-independent designation may facilitate genotype-phenotype interpretation and identify candidates for allele-selective therapeutic development.

title: Late-pregnancy maternal serum alkaline phosphatase levels and risk of early postpartum cardiometabolic disease: A municipality-wide electronic health record-based cohort study in Tianjin, China.
authorString: Xu X, Fang Y, Zhang R, Li J, Zuo L, Lv L, Yang Q, Zhou X.
abstractText:
Objective

To investigate the association between gestational age-standardized maternal alkaline phosphatase (ALP) levels and early postpartum cardiometabolic disease.

Methods

The study included 166,986 singleton pregnancies from the Tianjin Health and Medical Data Platform in Tianjin, China (2009-2023). Maternal serum ALP levels measured within two weeks before delivery were gestational age-standardized and categorized into quartiles. Primary outcomes were early postpartum cardiometabolic diseases including hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, cardiovascular disease (CVD), and a composite outcome comprising these conditions. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

Results

During a median follow-up of 4.7 years, compared with the highest gestational age-standardized ALP quartile, the lowest quartile was associated with higher risks of postpartum hypertension (HR: 1.18, 95% CI: 1.09, 1.28), diabetes mellitus (HR: 1.23, 95% CI: 1.10, 1.37), CVD (HR: 1.17, 95% CI: 1.07, 1.28), and composite outcome (HR: 1.13, 95% CI: 1.08, 1.20). Exploratory analyses showed limited incremental discrimination after adding gestational age-standardized ALP to models containing adverse pregnancy outcomes.

Conclusions

Lower gestational age-standardized maternal ALP levels before delivery were associated with a higher risk of early postpartum cardiometabolic disease. Further studies across ethnically and geographically diverse populations are warranted to validate these findings.

title: Temporal trends and outcomes of intravascular imaging in chronic total occlusion interventions: insights from the PROGRESS-CTO registry.
authorString: Akyel A, Carvalho PEP, Vichos T, Tsourous M, Desai PV, Gavlasova D, Gorgulu S, Alaswad K, Basir MB, Nakhle A, Young L, Poommipanit P, Jaffer FA, Azzalini L, Krestyaninov O, Khelimskii D, Frizzell J, Ozdemir R, Uluganyan M, Jefferson BK, Goktekin O, Chandwaney R, Choi JW, Davies RE, ElGuindy AM, Rangan BV, Mastrodemos OC, Voudris K, Sandoval Y, Brilakis ES.
abstractText:
Background

In this study we investigated temporal trends, indications, practice variation, and outcomes associated with intravascular imaging (IVI) use in a large, multicenter chronic total occlusion (CTO) percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) registry.

Methods

We analyzed CTO PCIs performed at 76 US and international centers in 2012-2026 in the PROGRESS-CTO registry. Patients were categorized according to IVI use. P value <0.05 was considered statistically significant.

Results

Among 18,024 CTO PCIs, IVI was used in 10,569 procedures (58.6%). IVI use increased over time. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) was the predominant modality, accounting for 98.1% of IVI-guided procedures. Following 1:1 propensity score matching, technical (85.8% vs 78.8%; p < 0.001) and procedural success (83.6% vs 78.1%, p = 0.003) remained higher in the IVUS-to-cross group. Difference was also pronounced when IVUS was used to cross ambiguous proximal cap: technical success was 85.1% versus 75.9% (OR, 1.81; 95% CI, 1.49-2.21), and procedural success was 83.0% versus 75.1% (OR, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.34-1.99). Centers contributing <100 cases had lower IVI use than centers contributing ≥100 cases (47.7% vs 58.7%; p < 0.001).

Conclusion

IVI use during CTO PCI continues to increase. Procedures in which IVUS was used to facilitate lesion crossing were associated with higher technical and procedural success rates and similar in-hospital MACE rates. The association with success was also pronounced when IVUS was used to resolve proximal cap ambiguity. IVI use varied significantly among participating centers, highlighting differences in practice patterns and adoption of IVI during CTO PCI.

title: Relationship between coronary microvascular and epicardial spasm at intracoronary acetylcholine testing in patients with ANOCA.
authorString: Fischer A, Saccardi L, Hubert A, Martinez-Pereyra V, Bekeredjian R, Seitz A, Ong P.
abstractText:
Background

Patients with Angina and unobstructed coronary arteries (ANOCA) frequently suffer from coronary spasm. Intracoronary provocative testing may reveal microvascular and/or epicardial spasm. However, the relationship of these two spasm types has not been investigated systematically.

Methods

We enrolled 142 ANOCA patients (mean age 63 years, 44% female) in whom intracoronary acetylcholine testing demonstrated epicardial spasm at the highest acetylcholine dose (i. e. 200 μg) in the left coronary artery according to the COVADIS criteria. In all patients, demographic data, cardiovascular risk factors and procedural data were recorded. The latter included symptoms and/or ischemic ECG shifts during lower acetylcholine doses. This enabled diagnosis of microvascular spasm before documentation of epicardial spasm.

Results

49 out of 142 patients (35%) had microvascular spasm before documentation of epicardial spasm. Thirty-one patients (22%) had an uneventful test and in 62 (43%) the acetylcholine test was inconclusive. Statistical analysis revealed no significant differences between patients with and without microvascular spasm regarding cardiovascular risk factors. However, patients with microvascular spasm were significantly more often female (55% vs. 29%, p = 0.037). Multivariable analysis revealed female sex as significant predictor for the occurrence of microvascular spasm (OR 3.0, 95% CI 1.15-7.80, p = 0.021).

Conclusion

In patients with epicardial spasm microvascular spasm at lower acetylcholine doses can be diagnosed in 35% of ANOCA patients. Independent of cardiovascular risk factors women are affected by this scenario three times more often than men. Our results underline the importance of the coronary microcirculation and sex-specific differences in the pathophysiology of coronary spasm.

title: The Society of Thoracic Surgeons (2026) Expert Consensus Document on Management of Borderline Left Heart Excluding Unbalanced Atrioventricular Septal Defect and Strategies for Biventricular Conversion.
authorString: Karamlou T, Woo JL, Lam CZ, Emani S, Barron DJ, Honjo O, Jacobs JP, Oh N, Morales DL, Patel CR, Anderson BR, Najm HK, Pizarro C, Bleiweiss M, Feins E.
abstractText:
Background

Strategies to recruit the left ventricle in borderline left heart (BLH), whether utilizing primary or staged recruitment strategy, are challenged by lack of consensus regarding optimal substrate, timing, and technique.

Methods

A panel of experienced congenital cardiac surgeons, cardiologists and imaging experts were convened to develop key questions related to BLH management, excluding unbalanced atrioventricular septal defect, from neonatal period through 1 year, using the PICO (Patients/Population, Intervention, Comparison/Control, Outcome) framework. Literature searches were performed for each question. Using a modified Delphi method, consensus statements were developed.

Results

For neonates with BLH, primary biventricular repair should be adopted cautiously, and only with favorable anatomic and physiologic criteria determined by echocardiography and/or magnetic resonance imaging. Neonates in the 'grey-zone', with smaller mitral and aortic valve sizes, endocardial fibroelastosis, indexed left ventricular diastolic volume < 25 ml/m2 and ascending aortic flow < 2.0 L/min/m2, should undergo staged recruitment to potentially facilitate growth of left-sided structures and more durable surgical rehabilitation of left ventricular inflow and outflow. Timing and type of subsequent procedures should be guided by interval cardiac catheterization and magnetic resonance imaging data. Initial palliation of grey-zone neonates can be accomplished with either surgical Norwood or hybrid stage 1 with possible atrial level restriction, and subsequent endocardial fibroelastosis resection along with aortic and mitral valve repair as components of successful complete biventricular conversion.

Conclusions

Biventricular approaches in BLH should be guided by integration of anatomic and physiologic criteria, with most neonates recommended for staged recruitment rather than primary repair.

title: Prognostic Stratification of Adjuvant Immunotherapy After Neoadjuvant Chemoimmunotherapy and Quality Surgery in LA-ESCC.
authorString: Sun J, Bao P, Bai Y, Chen C, Lv H, Lin J, Wang C, Shen J, Mei X, Han Y, Liu Z, Zhang Z, Zhong Q, Jiang Y, Xu L, Li X, Qian D, Ma D, Ye M, Wang C, Wang Z, Tian Z, Leng X, Li Z, Guo X, Yan X, Zhao J.

journal.title: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery

abstractText: In locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (LA-ESCC), neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NCIT) plus high-quality surgery (R0 resection with systematic lymphadenectomy >19 nodes) is a promising strategy. However, the value of adjuvant immunotherapy remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between postoperative adjuvant immunotherapy and survival outcomes in a multicenter cohort. This multicenter retrospective study enrolled LA-ESCC patients receiving NCIT from eight high-volume Chinese centers between 2019 and 2023. After screening for high-quality surgery, propensity score matching (PSM) balanced characteristics between the two groups: NCIT plus surgery (NCIT+S) and NCIT plus surgery followed by adjuvant immunotherapy (NCIT+S+ICI). The primary endpoints were overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS). A prognostic framework based on major pathological response (MPR) and postoperative pathological N stage (ypN) was constructed to refine patient selection. Among 724 patients with a median follow-up of 40.3 months, 3-year OS and DFS rates were 73.0% and 67.7%, respectively. After PSM, adjuvant immunotherapy significantly improved DFS (77.1% vs 65.8%, log-rank P=0.037), but not OS (83.4% vs 69.4%, log-rank P=0.058). Multivariate analysis identified ypN, MPR, and postoperative adjuvant immunotherapy as independent prognostic factors for DFS. Stratification by MPR and ypN status showed that DFS benefit from adjuvant immunotherapy was restricted to the non-MPR/ypN+ subgroup (HR=0.339; 95% CI: 0.173-0.662; log-rank P<0.001), with a significant treatment-by-subgroup interaction (P for interaction=0.025). Among LA-ESCC patients receiving NCIT and high-quality surgery, adjuvant immunotherapy significantly improves 3-year DFS in the non-MPR/ypN+ subgroup, with no significant benefit in other subgroups.

title: PLCB3 as a causal regulator linking ferroptosis and immune remodeling in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
authorString: Zhu H, Qin C, Yang J, Luo S, Guo Y.
abstractText:
Background

Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a complex syndrome lacking effective targeted therapies, but its causal genes and mechanisms remain poorly defined.

Objective

To investigate the role of PLCB3 and its association with ferroptosis in HFpEF.

Methods

We integrated transcriptomic data and genome-wide association studies (GWAS) data and employed differential expression analysis, mendelian randomization (MR), summary data-based mendelian randomization (SMR), and colocalization analysis to identify key genes associated with HFpEF. Furthermore, functional validation was performed using a HFpEF mouse model and siRNA mediated PLCB3 knockdown in AC16 cardiomyocytes. Cell viability, reactive oxygen species (ROS), lipid peroxidation, and ferroptosis related protein expression were subsequently assessed to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying PLCB3-mediated ferroptosis.

Results

Phospholipase C beta 3 (PLCB3) was identified as a candidate causal gene for HFpEF. PLCB3 expression was significantly reduced in HFpEF cardiac tissue and a mouse model induced by high-fat diet and L-NAME. Knockdown of PLCB3 decreased cell viability and induced ferroptosis, as indicated by reduced GPX4 and FTH1 expression, increased ACSL4 levels, and elevated lipid peroxidation and reactive oxygen species. These effects were significantly reversed by the ferroptosis inhibitor Ferrostatin-1. In vivo, ferroptosis-related markers were similarly altered in HFpEF mice. In addition, immune infiltration analysis revealed significant differences in multiple immune cell populations between HFpEF and controls. Single-cell eQTL-based MR analysis further suggested that PLCB3 expression is associated with specific immune cell subsets, including B cells, CD4+ naïve T cells, and natural killer cells.

Conclusion

PLCB3 is a potential regulator of HFpEF and may contribute to disease progression by promoting ferroptosis and immune alterations. These findings provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms of HFpEF and suggest that targeting PLCB3 may represent a novel therapeutic strategy.

title: Fatigue, Anxiety and Depression 12 Months After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Population Based Cohort Study.
authorString: Okyere DO, Nehme E, Bray J, Dainty KN, Dantanarayana A, Nehme Z.
abstractText: To determine the prevalence and factors associated with fatigue, anxiety, and depression 12 months after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA); examine their associations with health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and functional recovery; and compare symptom burden with population norms. This prospective, population-based cohort study included adults (≥18 years) who received EMS-attempted resuscitation and survived to hospital discharge following non-traumatic OHCA in Victoria, Australia, between July 2019 and June 2022. Survivors were identified from a statewide OHCA registry and completed a 12-month telephone interview. Primary outcomes were fatigue (Modified Fatigue Impact Scale), anxiety and depression (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale). Secondary outcomes included HRQoL (EQ-5D, SF-12), functional recovery (GOSE), living arrangement, and return to work. Of 1068 eligible 12-month survivors, 728 (68.2%) completed follow-up (median age 61 years; 555 [76.2%] male). Fatigue was reported by 35.8% (250/699), anxiety by 22.6% (162/716), and depression by 18.0% (129/716). Higher symptom burden was associated with lower EQ-5D and SF-12 scores, worse GOSE outcomes (all p<0.001) and reduced return-to-work rates. Compared with population norms, survivors reported greater fatigue (SMD 0.64; 95%CI, 0.50-0.78;p<0.001), and depression (SMD, 0.12; 95%CI, 0.02,0.21;p=0.02) but lower anxiety (SMD, -0.27; 95%CI, -0.35 to -0.18;p<0.001). In adjusted models, younger age, preexisting anxiety or depression, diabetes and initial non-shockable arrest were associated with higher symptom burden, whereas EMS-witnessed arrests were associated with lower symptom burden. Fatigue, anxiety, and depression were common at 12 months after OHCA and are associated with poorer recovery. Fatigue exceeded population norms and may be an under-recognised component of cardiac arrest survivorship.

title: Regional implementation of a prehospital advanced life support program with video-assisted physician direction and outcomes after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
authorString: Choi Y.
abstractText: The smart advanced life support (SALS) program was introduced to provide prehospital advanced life support under real-time video-assisted physician direction for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). This study evaluated the association between regional SALS implementation and OHCA outcomes. This retrospective cohort study used difference-in-differences and event-study analyses with data from the OHCA surveillance system in South Korea and included adult OHCA cases (aged ≥19 years) from 2 years before through 4 years after SALS implementation in August 2015. The exposure was region-level implementation of SALS. Outcomes were the prehospital time interval, prehospital return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), survival to discharge, and favorable neurological outcome. Pre- to post-implementation changes were compared between regions with and without SALS. A total of 129,207 cases were included. SALS regions had greater increases in the prehospital time interval (4.12 minutes; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.91 to 5.33) and prehospital ROSC (1.35 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.56 to 2.15) than regions without SALS. No significant additional improvements were observed in survival to discharge (-0.35 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.31 to 0.62) or favorable neurological outcome (-0.35 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.08 to 0.37). Event-study analyses suggested differential pre-intervention trends for prehospital time, but not for the other outcomes. SALS regions showed greater increases in prehospital time and prehospital ROSC without significant improvements in survival to discharge or favorable neurological outcome, but the finding for prehospital time should be interpreted cautiously because differential pre-intervention trends were observed.

title: Identifying the Operational Bottleneck to Shock Delivery After Automated External Defibrillator Activation.
authorString: Nojima T, Yumoto T, Obara T, Tokioka K, Hongo T, Kosaki Y, Tsukahara K, Nakao A, Naito H.
abstractText: Cardiac arrest registries record automated external defibrillator (AED) use and shock delivery but not post-activation operational timing. We aimed to identify the largest measurable bottleneck and an exploratory pad-application target for shock delivery within 60 seconds of AED power-on. We retrospectively analyzed timestamps from remotely monitored Nihon Kohden AEDs between January 2018 and February 2026. After excluding inspection records, we grouped records into activation events and quantified intervals. Shock-timing and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were restricted to initially shock-advised events with recorded shock delivery. We analyzed 8,115 activation events. Median times were 42 seconds (interquartile range [IQR], 30-56) from power-on to completion of pad application, nine seconds (IQR, 9-11) from pad application to the first analysis, and 52 seconds (IQR, 40-66) from power-on to the first analysis endpoint. The power-on-to-pad-application interval accounted for a median of 81% (IQR, 75-85) of the total power-on-to-first-analysis interval, increasing to 87% (IQR, 85-90) when first analysis occurred more than 60 seconds after power-on. Among 900 initially shock-advised events with recorded shock delivery, the median pad-application-to-shock interval was 15 seconds (IQR 13-17). Exploratory ROC analysis yielded a power-on to pad-application threshold of ≥ 51 seconds in relation to first recorded shock delivery occurring more than 60 seconds after AED power-on. The interval from AED power-on to electronically detected completion of pad application, encompassing all intervening actions, was the largest measurable post-activation bottleneck. Completion within 50 seconds may serve as an exploratory process target for first recorded shock delivery within 60 seconds among initially shock-advised events.

title: Association between burst-suppression with identical bursts and multimodal measures of cerebral oxygenation after cardiac arrest.
authorString: Faiver L, Tam J, Ratay CR, Elmer J, Coppler PJ, Pittsburgh Post Cardiac Arrest Service Investigators.
abstractText: Burst-suppression with identical bursts (BSIB) is an electroencephalographic (EEG) pattern associated with severe post-cardiac arrest brain injury (PCABI). Whether modifiable mechanisms of brain injury underlie BSIB is unknown. We hypothesized BSIB is associated with impaired cerebral oxygen metabolism, reflected as pathologically elevated jugular bulb venous oxygen saturation (SjvO2), higher brain tissue oxygen tension (PbtO2), normal jugular bulb venous-to-arterial carbon dioxide gradient (PbCO2 gap, and lower intracranial pressure (ICP) compared to other EEG patterns. This single-center retrospective study included patients resuscitated from cardiac arrest who underwent EEG and SjvO2 or PbtO2 monitoring. We categorized EEG patterns as BSIB, malignant without BSIB, and non-malignant. Using mixed effects linear regression, we examined associations between EEG and SjvO2, PbCO2 gap, PbtO2, and ICP. The SjvO2 and PbtO2 cohorts included 109 and 33 patients, respectively. SjvO2 did not differ between BSIB and malignant EEGs (β=3; 95% CI, -0.6 to 7.0), butwas higher with BSIB compared to non-malignant patterns (β=12; 95% CI, 7.0 to 16.0). BSIB was associated with lower PbCO2 gap compared to malignant (β=-1.4; 95% CI, -2.6 to -0.3) and non-malignant (β=-2.6; 95% CI, -4.1 to -1.0) patterns. PbtO2 was highest with BSIB, but not significantly higher compared to malignant patterns in our adjusted model (β=4.0; 95% CI, -4.7 to 13.0). ICP was lower in those with BSIB compared to malignant patterns (β=-19.0; 95% CI, -32.5 to -5.6). Interpretation BSIB may represent a distinct subtype of PCABI characterized by impaired oxygen metabolism with preserved oxygen delivery and diffusion.

title: Real-time feedback during bag-valve-mask ventilation for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a before-and-after study (VEntilation during Cardiac Arrest Resuscitation Study, VECARS-2).
authorString: Jost D, Petermann A, Tassart B, Salome M, Lemoine F, Liscia J, Frattini B, Derkenne C, Lemaire M, Travers S, Paris Fire Brigade Cardiac Arrest Task Force (collaborators).
abstractText: This study compared bag-valve-mask ventilation quality and adherence to the guideline-recommended ventilation volume range during 30:2 cardiopulmonary resuscitation for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest before and after the implementation of real-time feedback. We conducted a before-and-after observational study of two sequential adult cohorts with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest managed by basic life support teams from the Paris Fire Brigade. A bidirectional sensor measured insufflated volume (Vi) and expiratory tidal volume (Vt). The display was masked during Period-1 and provided real-time feedback during Period-2. We assessed adherence to the guideline-recommended range using mixed-effects regression; we analyzed Vt and leak volume using gamma log-link generalized linear mixed models. We analyzed 4,300 ventilations in 163 patients, 96 without feedback and 67 with feedback. Median Vi was lower with feedback (471 mL) than without (513 mL, p=0.03 for the first ventilation of each cycle) but median Vt was unchanged (235 vs. 243 mL, p=0.84). Vi dispersion was reduced by 35% (mean within-patient IQR ratio 0.65 [95%-CI, 0.53-0.77]). Vi was 400-600 mL in 68% of ventilations with feedback vs. 42% without feedback. In contrast, Vt was 400-600 mL in only 14% of ventilations with feedback vs. 15% without feedback. In multivariable analysis, leak volume was 12% lower with feedback (mean ratio, 0.88 [95%-CI, 0.77-0.99]). Real-time feedback was associated with improved adherence to the guideline-recommended range for Vi, less dispersed Vi,and lower leak volume. Causal inference, clinical significance, and generalizability warrant further evaluation.

title: Integrative genetic analyses for drug repurposing identify emodin as a candidate modulator of STAT3 signaling in abdominal aortic aneurysm.
authorString: Liu Y, Xu Z, Deng L, Zhang C, Ruan X, Zhao L, Yang Y, Wang Z, Lu H.
abstractText: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a life-threatening vascular disease lacking effective pharmacological therapies. To identify potential therapeutic targets and candidate compounds, we performed integrative genetic analyses for drug repurposing by combining Mendelian randomization (MR), summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR), and Bayesian colocalization. This framework prioritized multiple druggable candidates, among which STAT3 emerged as a key regulatory node. Subsequent functional studies demonstrated that emodin suppressed vascular smooth muscle cell proliferation, migration, phenotypic switching, and inflammatory responses. These effects were accompanied by reduced STAT3 phosphorylation and nuclear localization. Molecular docking suggested a potential binding mode of emodin within the STAT3 SH2 domain, while cellular thermal shift assays demonstrated thermal stabilization of STAT3 by emodin in intact cells, consistent with target engagement. Notably, emodin and the selective STAT3 inhibitor STAT3-IN-13 produced comparable effects, and co-treatment did not yield additive efficacy, suggesting overlapping mechanisms. In vivo, emodin attenuated aneurysm development and reduced vascular inflammation in experimental models. Collectively, these findings identify emodin as a candidate modulator of AAA progression acting through suppression of STAT3-associated signaling pathways, and demonstrate the potential of genetic evidence-guided drug repurposing strategies in complex vascular diseases.

title: Longitudinal Proteomics Integrated with Multi‑Omics Reveal Molecular Drivers of Responses to Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy in Rectal Cancer.
authorString: Mai L, Shao C, Cao Y, Du F, Liu J, Zhang Q, Sun L, Dong Y, Lou J, Hou Y, Ni Y, Yang M, Liu Y, Zhang Q.
abstractText: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) is the standard treatment for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC), yet its molecular determinants of response remain unclear. We conducted longitudinal 4D-DIA proteomic profiling of pre- and post-treatment specimens from 156 patients, including 31 patients with matched pre- and post-treatment specimens, and integrated with bulk RNA sequencing, single-cell transcriptomics, and functional validation. At baseline, responders were enriched in innate and adaptive immune pathways, whereas non-responders showed proliferative and metabolic programs. Pre-treatment RAC2, elevated in responders, was positively associated with immune activation, oxaliplatin sensitivity, and survival, and was validated in GSE139255 and GSE35640 (all P < 0.05). Moreover, RAC2 demonstrated strong predictive performance (training AUC = 0.867; testing AUC = 0.857). During treatment, NAC induced fibrosis-related remodeling across all groups (all P < 0.05), while responders uniquely preserved CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration (P = 0.031). Responders and RAC2-high tumors exhibited concordant pathway dynamics during NAC. Single-cell analysis further revealed that pre-treatment tumor RAC2, higher in responders, transmitted signals to CD8⁺ T cells while receiving inputs from fibroblasts (P < 0.05). In vitro and in vivo, RAC2 knockdown reduced baseline tumor growth but promoted under oxaliplatin (all P < 0.05). Overall, this study offers proteomic insights into NAC in LARC, supports therapeutic decision-making, and identifies potential targets.

title: Veno-arterial ECMO for the management of propofol infusion syndrome following cardiac surgery.
authorString: Sanchis-Haba I, Rubio B, Morales-Rey I, Luna R, Pereda D, Sandoval E.

journal.title: Revista espanola de anestesiologia y reanimacion

abstractText: Propofol infusion syndrome (PRIS) has been described in patients requiring prolonged sedation with this drug, as may occur in some cases after cardiac surgery. Its treatment is based on discontinuation of the drug and supportive management of organ dysfunction until resolution. In the postoperative period of cardiac surgery, diagnosing PRIS poses a challenge, since it must be differentiated from other, more common complications such as postcardiotomy shock. In these patients, PRIS may fatally worsen the prognosis. Veno-arterial ECMO therapy may help maintain cardiac output. Both the diagnosis of PRIS after cardiac surgery and its treatment with ECMO have been scarcely reported. We present a case of PRIS after cardiac surgery successfully managed with ECMO.

title: Global insulin supply insecurity and the role of manufacturing innovation.
authorString: Hirsch IB, Parkin CG, Amiel SA, Mohan V, Aleppo G, Mathieu C, O'Neal DN.
abstractText: Insulin availability and affordability have long limited access in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), and recent shortages and product withdrawals in higher-income settings underscore the need for reliable supply worldwide. While documented disruptions do not establish an aggregate global manufacturing deficit, commercial decisions, regulatory barriers, procurement, financing, and distribution can restrict access even where production capacity exists. Nevertheless, product prioritization and investment decisions can constrain the capacity allocated to insulin and reduce the ability to respond to changing demand. This narrative review examines global insulin demand, supply insecurity, market structure, affordability, and health-system barriers, distinguishing the circumstances of the United States, other high-income countries, and LMICs. We consider the potential effects of incretin therapies on insulin requirements and industrial investment and assess manufacturing modernization, including continuous production, as one component of a broader response. Proposed technological benefits require insulin-specific validation of quality, productivity, cost, and commercial feasibility. Priorities include stronger shortage surveillance, diversified qualified suppliers, regulatory cooperation, sustainable procurement, reduced waste, and dependable distribution. Supply security must extend through safe storage, administration, education, and glucose monitoring. Coordinated action across manufacturing and health systems is needed to maintain uninterrupted, affordable access to appropriate insulin treatment.

title: When Clinical Prediction Models Meet Clinical Judgment: A Framework for Classifying Prediction Approaches.
authorString: Kerscher F, Peringa IP, Cox EGM, Neumann M, van der Horst ICC, Meijer RR, Koeze J.
abstractText: There is an ever increasing interest in using clinical prediction models to improve diagnostic and prognostic accuracy. However, the literature often conflates distinct prediction approaches, resulting in ambiguous findings and slowing scientific progress. This commentary aims to clarify the various ways in which physicians use clinical prediction models and highlight the implications of these approaches for prediction accuracy by drawing on an existing framework from the judgment and decision-making literature. We promote a framework distinguishing between four distinct prediction approaches: clinical judgment, mechanical judgment, clinical synthesis, and mechanical synthesis. We apply this framework to recent studies and illustrate how it distinguishes between previously conflated approaches. Our analysis demonstrates that current research often obscures meaningful differences between the prediction approaches, thereby impeding improvement in patient care. The framework provides conceptual clarity and highlights clinical synthesis, in which the physician incorporates the model output into their own judgment, as a practical yet under-researched approach. The prediction accuracy achieved in practice depends on how physicians use clinical prediction models. Greater recognition and use of the proposed framework can improve future research by properly classifying prediction approaches, fostering more accurate research syntheses, and supporting the more effective and fair application of clinical prediction models in practice.

title: Diaphragm Ultrasound-Guided PEEP Titration in COPD with Dynamic Hyperinflation.
authorString: Quiñones P, Sepúlveda P, Arriagada R, Cappuccio E, Rocco PRM, Battaglini D.
abstractText: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by airflow limitation, dynamic hyperinflation, and intrinsic positive end-expiratory pressure (iPEEP), which increase inspiratory threshold load and complicate ventilatory support. Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) is the preferred initial ventilatory support for COPD exacerbations complicated by acute or acute-on-chronic respiratory acidosis, while invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) may be required when NIV fails. External PEEP may reduce the inspiratory threshold load in patients with expiratory flow limitation, although excessive levels can increase lung volume and compromise hemodynamics. During IMV, PEEP adjustment requires assessment of respiratory mechanics, expiratory flow, hyperinflation, and cardiovascular tolerance. During NIV, where iPEEP cannot usually be measured directly, expiratory positive airway pressure (EPAP) should be adjusted according to clinical response, patient-ventilator interaction, and signs of excessive lung inflation. Inappropriate ventilatory assistance may also contribute to diaphragm dysfunction. Diaphragm ultrasound allows bedside assessment of muscle thickness and inspiratory thickening fraction (DTF), although these measurements are influenced by ventilatory assistance, respiratory drive, and lung volume. This review examines the physiological basis, available evidence, and limitations of using diaphragm ultrasound to complement PEEP adjustment in patients with COPD and dynamic hyperinflation. No DTF target or clinical benefit of ultrasound-guided PEEP titration has been established in this population.

title: Ovariectomy abolishes cardioprotection against diastolic dysfunction and impairs cardiac glucose oxidation in female mice with type 2 diabetes.
authorString: Chan JSF, Saed CT, Kirschenman R, Wagg CS, King AN, Dimaano MTE, Benyaminov F, Greenwell AA, Dong L, Yang K, Al-Imarah S, Eaton F, Ferrari SR, Tabatabaei Dakhili SA, Davidge ST, Ussher JR, Gopal K.
abstractText: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) increases the risk for diabetic cardiomyopathy (DbCM), which is often characterized by diastolic dysfunction. Pre-menopausal women have a reduced incidence of both T2D and DbCM, but this disappears following menopause. Our goal was to evaluate the potential role for ovarian hormones in mediating these differences. The effect of ovariectomy (OVX) was investigated in female mice with experimental T2D following high-fat diet feeding for 12-weeks in combination with a low-dose treatment of streptozotocin at week 4. Body weight and body composition, glucose homeostasis, cardiac structure/function via ultrasound echocardiography, and myocardial substrate metabolism via isolated working heart perfusions were assessed. Sham and OVX female mice with T2D exhibited increases in body weight and fat mass, as well as impaired glucose homeostasis, though these parameters were more prominent in OVX than sham females when compared to their lean counterparts. However, only OVX female mice with T2D developed diastolic dysfunction as reflected by a significant decrease in the mitral E/A and tissue Doppler e'/a' ratios, as well as an increase in the E/e' ratio. Isolated working hearts from both sham and OVX female mice with T2D exhibited a reduction in glucose oxidation, though this was more pronounced in the latter. Lastly, only OVX female mice with T2D demonstrated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy. Our data illustrate key roles for ovarian hormones in impacting how T2D impacts the progression of DbCM in females, which may have relevance to women living with T2D as they transition to menopause.

title: Dose-Response Profiles in Incretin and Multi-Agonist Obesity Pharmacotherapy.
authorString: Yousefian M, Baharmast M.

journal.title: Clinics and research in hepatology and gastroenterology

abstractText: Incretin and multi-agonist therapies have transformed obesity pharmacotherapy, but dose selection remains less mature than efficacy assessment. This critical narrative review examines nonlinear relationships among administered dose, systemic exposure, weight and cardiometabolic benefit, gastrointestinal tolerability, treatment persistence, and maintenance. Across established and newer programs, average efficacy generally increases with dose, yet incremental gains may narrow at higher exposure while adverse-event burden and discontinuation can increase. The maturity of evidence is heterogeneous, and later-stage programs should not be interpreted as clinically equivalent to agents supported mainly by earlier-phase dose-ranging data. Moreover, an "optimal dose" is not an endpoint-independent quantity: the exposure most appropriate for weight loss may differ from that relevant to glycemic control, cardiovascular benefit, body composition, tolerability, or maintenance. We therefore distinguish nominal dose from exposure and present response-guided titration as a hypothesis-generating framework for prospective testing, not as an evidence-based dosing algorithm. Existing continuation and withdrawal studies support the importance of ongoing pharmacological treatment after successful weight loss but do not establish a minimum or optimal de-intensified maintenance dose. Future trials should jointly model efficacy, safety, body composition, patient-reported outcomes, pharmacokinetics, and discontinuation to test objective-specific, patient-level dosing strategies.

title: Effectiveness of respiratory syncytial virus immunisation in practice.
authorString: Groenendijk RW, Franck Z, Baral R, Basso LJ, Batista FD, Bonten M, Caballero MT, Clark A, Cohen C, de Cellès MD, Esteban I, Falsey AR, Fourati S, Graham BS, Halasa N, Hartert T, Kops AL, Kragten-Tabatabaie L, Kriek L, Manzoni P, Marchant DJ, Martinon-Torres F, Mejias A, Midulla F, Nakimuli A, Nisar MI, Nyiro JU, Piedra PA, Richmond PC, Shaaban FL, Srikantiah P, Stein RT, Tahibo AB, Terstappen J, Viegas M, Vizzotti C, Watson CH, Wee LE, Weinberger DM, Bont LJ, Mazur NI.
abstractText: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) affects all ages, with infants and older adults most affected by severe disease. The RSV prevention landscape includes 39 candidates in clinical development, alongside setbacks such as the discontinuation of a promising paediatric live-attenuated vaccine candidate. Several products have been approved, including a maternal vaccine, infant monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines for older adults and adults at high risk. Due to high cost, implementation of these products remains limited to higher-income settings. Real-world evidence confirms high effectiveness, with emerging benefits beyond respiratory disease, including reduced cardiovascular events in older adults. Despite comparable effectiveness of maternal vaccination and monoclonal antibodies, differences in uptake highlight that product availability alone will not ensure population impact. Achieving uptake requires integration into accessible routine care, recommendation by trusted providers, and context-sensitive delivery strategies. This Review summarises RSV preventive products, real-world effectiveness and uptake, and the opportunity of using communication in translating RSV prevention into impact.

title: Atrial Fibrillation in Valvular Heart Disease: Assessing the Impact of Genetics in the UK Biobank.
authorString: Cristin L, Tang JJ, Tastet L, Jhawar R, Glidden DV, Marcus GM, Delling FN.
abstractText:
Background

Atrial fibrillation (AF) in valvular heart disease (VHD) is generally attributed to pressure or volume overload with atrial remodeling, but the independent contribution of genetic predisposition remains unclear.

Objectives

The authors evaluated the predictive value of a previously developed AF polygenic risk score (PRS) across VHD subtypes in the UK Biobank.

Methods

In this prospective cohort study (UK Biobank, 2000-2022), incident AF and VHD status were defined using ICD codes. VHD subtypes included mitral valve (MV) disease (MV prolapse [MVP], mitral regurgitation, mitral stenosis) and aortic valve (AV) disease (aortic stenosis, aortic regurgitation). PRS was categorized into quintiles and grouped as low, intermediate, and high.

Results

Among 452,841 participants with available PRS, 385 had MVP, 1,058 mitral regurgitation, 81 mitral stenosis, 421 aortic regurgitation, and 509 aortic stenosis. In Cox models, PRS was independently associated with incident AF in MV disease (HR: 1.7, P = 0.03 for intermediate PRS; HR: 2.3, P = 0.002 for high PRS), with the strongest effect in MVP (HR: 3.1, P = 0.03 for high PRS). In AV disease, PRS was not significantly associated with AF risk (P = 0.93 and P = 0.07 for intermediate and high PRS, respectively). Interaction analyses confirmed attenuation or absence of the PRS effect in AV disease (P = 0.04 and P = 0.004 for intermediate and high PRS, respectively), whereas no significant interaction was observed in MV disease (P = 0.80 and P = 0.11, respectively).

Conclusions

In VHD, AF PRS predicts AF risk, but the genetic impact differs by subtype. AV disease shows minimal genetic contribution, suggesting predominantly hemodynamic risk, while MV disease-particularly MVP-shows substantial genetic influence.

title: Physiologic Stress During Walking and Cycling Early After Cardiac Surgery.
authorString: Dzikowicz DJ, Mummidi SK, Yu Y, Xia X, Couderc JP, Lachant DJ.

journal.title: Journal of cardiopulmonary rehabilitation and prevention

abstractText:
Purpose

To characterize cardiac effort and heart rate (HR) responses during the 6-minute walk test (6MWT) early after cardiac surgery, compare HR patterns between walking and cycle ergometry, and evaluate differences by sex, frailty, and atrial fibrillation status.

Methods

We analyzed a publicly available PhysioNet dataset of adults ≥65 years with pre-frailty/frailty undergoing cardiac surgery who completed a 6MWT and symptom-limited cycle ergometry with continuous single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring (Polar H10). Cardiac effort was defined as total 6MWT heartbeats divided by distance walked (beats/m). Associations with cycle-ergometry performance were assessed using Spearman correlations with bootstrap CI; paired t tests compared HR responses between modalities; subgroup differences were evaluated using Welch t tests and multivariable linear regression.

Results

Of 80 enrolled participants, 66 (83%) had analyzable 6MWT ECG recordings (mean age 73 ± 5 years; 67% male; 18 ± 8 days post-surgery). Mean 6-minute walking distance (6MWD) was 300 ± 79 m, and mean cardiac effort was 1.62 ± 0.52 beats/m. In 38 participants with paired cycle-ergometry data, HR responses were similar between walking and cycling. Greater 6MWD was associated with better cycle-ergometry performance, while higher cardiac effort was associated with lower cycle-ergometry performance. In multivariable analysis, female sex was independently associated with higher cardiac effort (β = .34 beats/m; P = .042), atrial fibrillation with lower average and end-of-test HR (P ≤ .035), and greater frailty with shorter 6MWD (P = .036).

Conclusions

Cardiac effort is a feasible ECG-derived metric that complements 6MWD by integrating heart rate response with functional performance early after cardiac surgery. In this frail, predominantly beta-blocked cohort, HR responses during walking closely mirrored cycle ergometry.

title: Validity and agreement of bioelectrical impedance equations against dual energy X-ray absorptiometry for muscle mass assessment in patients on hemodialysis: A cross-sectional study.
authorString: Borges S, Martins TF, Machado FVC, Júnior GC, Cipriano GFB.

journal.title: Nutrition in clinical practice : official publication of the American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition

abstractText:
Background

Low muscle mass is common in patients on hemodialysis (HD), and bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) predictive equations have been proposed as an alternative for estimating muscle mass. This study aimed to analyze the validity and agreement of different BIA-based prediction equations against dual energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) for estimating skeletal muscle mass (SMM) and appendicular skeletal muscle mass (ASMM) in patients on HD.

Methods

A cross-sectional study enrolled patients on HD. Clinical and laboratory data and body composition by BIA and DXA were collected. The accuracy of six prediction equations (Janssen, Barbosa-Silva, Kyle, Lin, Macdonald, and Sergi) for estimating SMM and ASMM was tested against DXA as the reference standard. Agreement was assessed using Lin's Concordance Correlation Coefficient (CCC), Bland-Altman analysis, Kappa statistics, Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curves, and Passing-Bablok regression.

Results

The sample consisted of 57 participants, age 52 ± 13 years, 32 (56%) male, median dialysis vintage 14 (4-40) months, 17 (30%) with diabetes, and 48 (84%) with hypertension. The best agreement with DXA was observed for the Lin (CCC = 0.911), Sergi (CCC = 0.902) and Kyle (CCC = 0.902) equations. For low muscle mass diagnosis, Kappa values ranged from moderate to substantial, with the Lin equation showing the highest agreement (κ = 0.734). Additionally, the Lin equation demonstrated good accuracy (AUC = 0.794, 95% CI 0.68-0.91), with 68,4% sensitivity and 89.5% specificity.

Conclusion

The Lin equation provided the most accurate and reproducible estimates of muscle mass compared with DXA and showed good diagnostic performance for low muscle mass in patients on HD.

title: MEDA-PKD: a dynamic, real-time analytics platform for precision care in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
authorString: Grundmann F, Arjune S, Alkarkoukly S, Bartram MP, Beck BB, Benzing T, Boehm V, Bohl K, Burst V, Busch M, Cakiroglu F, Cukoski S, Gerke P, Große-Hokamp N, Halbritter J, Matrisch L, Persigehl T, Petzold F, Schmidt J, Schmitt R, Todorova P, Wanner C, Antczak P, Müller RU, AD(H)PKD Study Group.
abstractText: The use of medical real-world data is constrained by fragmented data infrastructures and the absence of tools integrating longitudinal clinical with molecular data at scale. Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), the most common monogenic cause of kidney failure, exemplifies this gap given its phenotypic complexity and the need for individualized treatment decisions. We present MEDA-PKD (MEdical DAta translation service of Polycystic Kidney Disease), an interactive, near-real-time analytics platform that integrates clinical routine with research data from the German AD(H)PKD Tolvaptan Registry (NCT02497521, DRKS00008910) into a harmonized database ( https://doi.org/10.18716/adpkd_registry ). MEDA-PKD provides automated near-real-time analysis and dynamic visualization, replacing traditional static approaches to clinical cohorts. As of March 2026, MEDA-PKD visualized data from 1735 patients (mean follow-up 796 days). eGFR slope analysis of data from patients initiating tolvaptan therapy (332 patients) demonstrates the platform's capacity to evaluate real-world therapeutic impact in real-time. Other tabs include family history, medication, lifestyle, quality of life and a wide array of lab values (20,894 entries). Besides, MEDA-PKD integrates proteomics data and allows for secure individual patient-level data access. MEDA-PKD represents a paradigm shift by transforming static cohort data into a living, actionable knowledge resource in ADPKD and will serve as a template for other diseases.

title: Experiences and Challenges of Home Blood Pressure Monitoring Among Patients with Uncontrolled Hypertension: A Qualitative Study.
authorString: Moosa AS, Peh RWC, Oka P, Ng CJ.

journal.title: Journal of primary care & community health

abstractText: IntroductionHome blood pressure monitoring (HBPM) is recommended for hypertension management. However, patients' experiences and challenges with HBPM, particularly among those with uncontrolled hypertension, remain poorly understood. This study aimed to explore how patients with uncontrolled hypertension experience and perform HBPM, and the challenges they encounter.MethodSeventeen adults aged ≥21 years with uncontrolled hypertension were purposively recruited from three public primary care clinics in Singapore. A qualitative descriptive-interpretive study used in-depth, semi-structured, audio-recorded face-to-face interviews until data saturation. Interview transcripts were analysed thematically. The qualitative data were managed using NVivo version 14.ResultsMost participants owned an HBPM device, yet their practices varied widely. Patients engaged in selective monitoring, measuring blood pressure mainly when symptomatic or close to clinic visits. Many adapted HBPM routines to fit competing life demands, resulting in irregular timing and frequency. Selective recording of readings, including omission of higher values, was frequently reported. Documentation preferences differed by digital literacy, with older patients preferring paper records. HBPM was often perceived as a healthcare provider (HCP) assigned task rather than a self-care behaviour. Limited and inconsistent guidance from HCP contributed to confusion and reduced motivation.ConclusionAmong patients with uncontrolled hypertension, guideline-concordant HBPM was shaped by practical barriers, uncertainty about correct monitoring and documentation, and the extent of HCP engagement. Participants' selective monitoring and recording practices highlight the need for clearer patient education, consistent provider feedback, and tailored documentation approaches to support more reliable use of HBPM in primary care.

title: Association of Spinal Epidural Lipomatosis With Systemic Lipid Metabolism in Patients With Lumbar Spinal Stenosis: A Propensity Score-Matched Study.
authorString: Zhang B, Zhou Q, Zhong C, Wang S, Zhao Q, Hu Z, Wang B, Qiu Y, Zhu Z, Sun X.

journal.title: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society

abstractText:
Background context

Spinal epidural lipomatosis (SEL) is often regarded as a local consequence of obesity, yet its relationship with systemic lipid metabolism and symptom severity in lumbar spinal stenosis remains unclear. Apolipoprotein B (ApoB) is central to atherogenic lipid transport and ectopic fat deposition. Examining the association between systemic lipid metabolic abnormalities, including elevated ApoB levels, and epidural fat accumulation may provide insights into the metabolic pathogenesis and clinical relevance of SEL.

Purpose

To determine whether SEL is associated with systemic lipid metabolic abnormalities and greater preoperative symptom burden in patients undergoing surgery for lumbar spinal stenosis (LSS).

Study design

Retrospective, propensity score-matched cohort study.

Patient sample

A consecutive series of 1,145 patients who underwent posterior decompression for symptomatic LSS between December 2023 and December 2025. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 90 patients with SEL were compared with 90 patients without SEL.

Outcome measures

Serum lipid and other biochemical markers, epidural fat/spinal canal (EF/SpC) index on lumbar magnetic resonance imaging, Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and visual analog scale (VAS) scores for leg and back pain.

Methods

SEL was diagnosed and graded on preoperative lumbar MRI according to the Borré classification, using the epidural fat/spinal canal index. Propensity score matching was performed for age, sex, body mass index (BMI), smoking history, drinking history, hypertension, and diabetes. Biochemical variables and preoperative clinical scores were compared between matched SEL and non-SEL patients. Conditional logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with SEL. BMI-adjusted partial Spearman correlation analyses were performed to evaluate associations between the EF/SpC index and biochemical markers. Regression-based trend analyses were conducted to assess changes in lipid-related markers across increasing SEL severity grades.

Results

Among 1,145 patients with LSS, 105 (9.2%) met the diagnostic criteria for SEL. After matching, 90 patients with SEL were compared with 90 non-SEL controls. The SEL group had higher apolipoprotein B (ApoB) levels than controls, as well as higher low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, triglycerides, and total cholesterol. ApoB remained independently associated with SEL in conditional logistic regression (odds ratio per 0.1 g/L, 1.141; 95% confidence interval, 1.019-1.277; P=0.022). Within the SEL group, the EF/SpC index correlated positively with triglycerides (ρ=0.43, q<0.001) and ApoB (ρ=0.40, q=0.002), while atherogenic lipid markers increased progressively with SEL severity. Patients with SEL also showed higher Oswestry Disability Index and leg-pain visual analog scale scores, whereas back-pain scores were similar between groups.

Conclusion

In patients undergoing surgery for LSS, SEL was associated with a more atherogenic lipid profile after matching for BMI and other major baseline characteristics, as well as greater preoperative disability and leg pain. The association of ApoB with SEL, together with the graded relationships of ApoB and triglycerides with epidural fat burden, suggests that SEL may reflect systemic lipid metabolic dysfunction rather than local epidural fat deposition alone.

title: White Matter Hyperintensities of Presumed Vascular Origin: Current Understanding of Development and Progression.
authorString: Shang T.

journal.title: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association

abstractText:
Background and purpose

White matter hyperintensities (WMH) of presumed vascular origin are among the most common MRI manifestations of cerebral small vessel disease and are a major contributor to vascular contributions to cognitive impairment and dementia. Although WMH have traditionally been attributed to chronic ischemia resulting from small vessel pathology, the biological mechanisms underlying their development and, more importantly, their progression remain incompletely understood. Recent advances in longitudinal neuroimaging, quantitative MRI, pathology, genetics, and physiological imaging have substantially expanded our understanding of WMH progression, making this an appropriate time to evaluate current concepts and synthesize emerging evidence.

Observations

We review contemporary evidence regarding the biological processes implicated in WMH development and progression, including hypertension and vascular risk factors, acute ischemic injury, chronic hypoperfusion, blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction, endothelial activation and vascular inflammation, arterial stiffness, intracranial artery dolichoectasia (IADE), altered cerebral fluid dynamics and genetic susceptibility. Longitudinal studies demonstrate that WMH exhibit dynamic trajectories characterized by progression, stability, and partial regression, indicating that lesion evolution is not uniformly irreversible. Pathological and advanced neuroimaging studies show that WMH represent heterogeneous tissue injury involving demyelination, axonal loss, gliosis, interstitial fluid accumulation, and microvascular abnormalities. Hypertension and blood pressure variability are consistently associated with greater WMH burden and progression, whereas baseline WMH burden is the strongest predictor of future lesion expansion. Acute ischemic lesions detected by diffusion-weighted imaging contribute to, but account for only a minority of WMH progression. Longitudinal studies evaluating cerebral perfusion, BBB permeability, inflammation, arterial stiffness, IADE and cerebral fluid dynamics have yielded variable findings but, together with genetic evidence, support roles of BBB leakage, vascular inflammation, chronic hypoperfusion, arterial and extracellular-matrix remodeling, and impaired interstitial fluid clearance in WMH progression.

Conclusions

Emerging evidence supports a paradigm in which WMH are viewed as a dynamic manifestation of progressive neurovascular dysfunction rather than the consequence of chronic ischemia alone. Current data suggest that early neurovascular injury evolves into a potentially self-reinforcing process characterized by persistent BBB disruption, vascular inflammation, chronic hypoperfusion, altered fluid dynamics, and recurrent ischemic injury, collectively contributes to WMH progression. Future multimodal longitudinal studies integrating cerebral hemodynamics, neurovascular function and intracranial arterial remodeling will be essential to understand WMH progression.

title: Predicting cholesterol screening behavior using machine learning: Social-ecological approach.
authorString: Kuo WC, Chen J, McDonald AD, Li T, Chang JH, Johnson HM.
abstractText: IntroductionCurrent preventive screening reminders use generic due-date notifications that lack personalization. Targeted reminders allow personalized messages and resource allocation, yet the accuracy of behavioral forecasting with cholesterol screening behaviors remains unconfirmed. Therefore, this study aims to examine the accuracy of machine learning in predicting adults' future cholesterol screening behavior.MethodsThis study included 8,288 participants from the Health and Retirement Study. Never receiving cholesterol screening over 12 years of follow-up (2007-2018) was identified as the target outcome. Predictors were constructed based on the Social-Ecological Model. Four machine learning (ML) algorithms were compared: logistic regression, random forests, gradient boosting machine (GBM), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). Model performance was evaluated by Recall, Precision, and false-negative rate (FNR).ResultsAmong the four ML algorithms, XGBoost performed best, with higher Recall (average: 0.8850) and the lowest FNR (0.1311), but suboptimal precision (average: 0.6228). The top five predictors were past cholesterol screening behavior, diagnosis of hypertension, osteoarthritis or rheumatoid arthritis, number of private insurance plans, and gender.ConclusionML might be used to predict individuals' cholesterol screening behavior. Future research is needed to examine whether leveraging ML in targeted reminders might enhance cholesterol screening behaviors.

title: Sucrose induces Cardiac Hypertrophy and Renal Perivascular Fibrosis in a Novel Mouse Model of Hypertension.
authorString: Terada Y, Nakayama Y, Zhang Y, Cetinkaya-Un B, Elliott KJ, Hashimoto T, Adebiyi A, Osei-Owusu P, Eguchi S.
abstractText:
Background

Excess sugar consumption increases the risk for hypertension. We previously reported pilot data demonstrating that male mice drinking 2% sucrose water develop hypertension. However, the sucrose effects on left ventricular hypertrophy, kidney fibrosis, or sex difference in hypertension remain unclear. In the present study, we characterized the cardiac and renal pathology in a larger cohort including female mice to establish a novel sucrose-induced mouse model of hypertension associated with cardiovascular remodeling.

Methods

Eight- to nine- week-old C57BL6 mice were given drinking water containing 2% sucrose or regular water for 4 weeks. Blood pressure was monitored using a tail-cuff system. Echocardiography was performed to evaluate cardiac remodeling. Sirius red staining was performed to evaluate heart and kidney fibrosis.

Results

Male mice drinking the sucrose water developed hypertension (systolic blood pressure 122.0±1.3mmHGvs 162.2±4.3 mmHG at day 28).
