Sucrose treatment increased left ventricular wall thickness and induced perivascular fibrosis of the heart and kidney compared to control mice. Cardiac functions were preserved. In female mice, sucrose treatment induced milder hypertension than male mice (126.9±2.4 mmHg vs 143.7±3.2 mmHg at day 28). However, sucrose treatment caused similar degree of left ventricular hypertrophy in female mice.

Conclusion

Sucrose water induced hypertension, cardiac hypertrophy, and fibrosis of the heart and kidney in male mice. Female mice were partially protected from hypertension but not from cardiac hypertrophy. This mouse model represents a useful tool to investigate molecular mechanisms by which hypertension and end organ damage develop with excess sugar consumption.

title: Arterial Hypertension and Kidney Function Decline in Systemic Sclerosis and Sjögren's Disease: A Longitudinal Comparative Study.
authorString: Gigante A, Pellicano C, Grilli E, Di Virgilio EM, Gattamelata A, Iannazzo F, Cianci R, Rosato E, Priori R.

journal.title: High blood pressure & cardiovascular prevention : the official journal of the Italian Society of Hypertension

abstractText:
Introduction

Renal involvement is increasingly recognized in Systemic Sclerosis (SSc) and Sjögren's Disease (SjD). However, the association between hypertension and renal function decline in these conditions remains poorly understood.

Aim

to compare renal function changes over time in patients with SSc and SjD; identify factors associated with clinically relevant renal function decline; and to evaluate whether the association between hypertension and renal function differs between the two diseases.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed patients with SSc and SjD, followed for up to 3 years. Renal function was assessed using estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Clinically relevant renal decline was defined as a reduction in eGFR ≥10 ml/min Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with renal function decline, including the interaction between diagnosis and hypertension.

Results

A total of 238 patients were included (114 with SSc and 124 with SjD), with a median age of 55 years (IQR 45-65) in SSc and 57 years (IQR 48-66) in SjD. At baseline, SSc patients showed higher eGFR compared to SjD, but experienced a greater decline over time (median -6 vs -2.1 ml/min, p < 0.05). Overall, 33.8% of patients developed clinically significant renal decline. In multivariable analysis, hypertension was independently associated with renal function decline (OR 10.01, 95% CI 3.51-28.56, p < 0.001), whereas diagnosis was not. A significant interaction between diagnosis and hypertension was observed (OR 6.56, 95% CI 1.03-41.69, p = 0.046), indicating a stronger association between hypertension and renal function decline in SSc than in SjD. In subgroup analyses, hypertension was significantly associated with renal decline in SSc but not in SjD.

Conclusions

Hypertension was independently associated with renal function decline, with a stronger association in SSc than in SjD. These findings warrant confirmation in prospective studies. Systemic Sclerosis, Sjögren's disease, Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate; arterial hypertension.

title: The ups and downs of human UNC93B1: Autoimmune and viral conditions.
authorString: Idiiatullina E, Casanova JL, Zhang SY.
abstractText: Mouse Unc93b1 was identified in 2006 by forward genetics as an ER membrane protein essential for the activity of the endosomal nucleic acid-sensing receptors TLR3, TLR7, and TLR9. In vitro studies in mouse and human cells have revealed its cellular functions, including ER-based stabilization and trafficking of endosomal TLR proteins (TLR3, TLR7, TLR8, and TLR9) and regulation of signaling thresholds through competitive trafficking control (TLR7 and TLR9). Human genetic studies have clarified the physiological role of UNC93B1 in natural conditions. Biallelic loss-of-function UNC93B1 mutations impair TLR3 signaling in central nervous system-resident cells, thereby conferring a predisposition to HSV-1 encephalitis. UNC93B1 deficiency may also predispose to other viral infections, as suggested by patients with inherited TLR3 or TLR7 deficiency. Conversely, monoallelic or biallelic UNC93B1 gain-of-function variants enhancing TLR7 and/or TLR8 signaling predispose patients to autoimmunity and inflammation, including early-onset systemic lupus erythematosus and chilblain lupus. Thus, in humans, UNC93B1 maintains a delicate balance between host defense and tolerance to self.

title: Clinical Risk Factors for Advanced Fibrosis in Pathology-Proven Steatotic Liver Disease: Emphasis on Nonelder Subjects.
authorString: Huang CT, Huang SC, Kang CL, Tang SW, Su HJ, Su TH, Tseng TC, Hsu SJ, Hong CM, Liu CH, Yang HC, Chen PJ, Kao JH, Liu CJ.
abstractText:
Background and aim

Steatotic liver disease (SLD) may lead to advanced liver diseases. We aimed to identify clinical risk factors for advanced fibrosis in pathology-proven SLD patients in a hepatitis B virus (HBV) endemic population, with emphasis on nonelder subjects.

Methods

Adult SLD patients diagnosed via pathology at National Taiwan University Hospital between June 2009 and December 2023 were recruited. Advanced fibrosis was defined as F2 to F4 fibrosis. Patients were stratified by age (< 50 years defined as nonelder), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and HBV infection. Clinical risk factors for advanced fibrosis and at-risk steatohepatitis were investigated, and the predictive performance of noninvasive scores was examined.

Results

Among 223 pathology-proven SLD patients, older age (odds ratio [OR]: 1.04), alcohol consumption (OR: 5.77), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) (OR: 2.13), chronic HBV infection (OR: 2.52), and obesity (OR: 2.64) were independent risk factors for advanced fibrosis. In the nonelder subgroup, older age (OR: 1.10) and obesity (OR: 3.75) were significant. In the MASLD subgroup, older age (OR: 1.04), hypertension (OR: 2.31), T2DM (OR: 3.07), and chronic HBV infection (OR: 3.59) remained significant. Obesity (OR: 4.14) was a significant risk factor for at-risk steatohepatitis in the nonelder subgroup. NAFLD fibrosis score had the highest AUROC (0.724) for advanced fibrosis in the entire cohort, while FIB-4 performed best in nonelder subjects.

Conclusions

Older age, alcohol, T2DM, chronic HBV infection, and obesity were associated with advanced fibrosis. Risk factors and noninvasive score performance varied in nonelder subjects.

title: Interrelationships Between Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Domains, Age, and Sex for Patients With Heart Failure: Findings From the CHAMP-HF and CORC Registries.
authorString: Girard AA, Jones PG, Fu Z, Sherrod CF, Cantu Martinez O, Greene SJ, Bachmann JM, Fonarow GC, Butler J, Spertus JA, Arnold SV.
abstractText:
Background

Although Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) domains independently quantify patients' symptoms, physical and social functioning, and quality of life, the interrelationships between domains (eg, symptoms impacting physical limitations) have not been described, nor whether these vary by age or sex.

Methods

Cross-sectional data from adult outpatients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction from 2 multicenter US registries, the Change the Management of Patients With Heart Failure Registry (2015-2017) and Cardiovascular Outcomes Research Consortium (2001-2002), were used to fit recursive path analysis models relating age, sex, and KCCQ domain scores. The interrelationships of these factors were quantified using unstandardized and standardized effect estimates. Unstandardized effects denote the linear effect of the independent variable on the dependent variable in units specific to both variables. Standardized effects are unitless and are obtained by multiplying the unstandardized effect by the ratio of the standard deviations of the dependent and independent variables.

Results

The analytic cohorts included 4839 patients from the Change the Management of Patients With Heart Failure Registry (mean age, 66.1±12.5 years, 29.3% women) and 547 patients from the Cardiovascular Outcomes Research Consortium (mean age, 66±12 years, 23.8% women). Standardized effect estimates revealed moderate to strong interrelationships among the KCCQ domains (effect size range, 0.34-0.70). Symptoms were strongly associated with all other domains (range, 0.61-0.70). Quality of life was most associated with symptoms and social limitations (range: 0.48-0.60), and less so with physical limitations (effect size=0.34). By comparison, the associations of age and sex with KCCQ domains were much smaller (effect sizes <0.2), and no interactions by age and sex were found.

Conclusions

KCCQ domains were strongly interrelated, and these relationships did not differ appreciably by age or sex. These data enhance the interpretation of KCCQ domain scores in research and clinical practice; in particular, symptoms and social limitations may be key drivers of impaired quality of life in heart failure. Targeted interventions prioritizing these domains may most effectively improve patients' overall health status.

title: High-Altitude Pulmonary Edema in Children in Mexico City: A Case Series.
authorString: Ferreiro Marín A, Ferreiro Soria MP, Sánchez Olivera K, Suárez Ortega A, Garrido García LM.
abstractText: Marín, Alejandro Ferreiro, María Paula Ferreiro Soria, Karla Sánchez Olivera, Aranza Suárez Ortega, and Luis Martín Garrido García. High-altitude pulmonary edema in children in Mexico City: A case series. High Alt Med Biol. 00:00-00, 2026.-High-altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE) is a potentially life-threatening form of noncardiogenic pulmonary edema caused by hypobaric hypoxia. Although well characterized in adults, pediatric cases remain underrecognized and are frequently mistaken for pneumonia.We describe four pediatric patients aged 7-12 years diagnosed with HAPE at a Private Tertiary Referral Medical Center in Mexico City. One patient developed classic HAPE after ascent from low altitude, and three patients developed reentry HAPE after returning to high altitude following temporary stays near sea level.All patients presented with hypoxemia (SpO2 77%-93%), respiratory symptoms, bilateral pulmonary infiltrates, absence of fever, and low inflammatory markers. Echocardiography demonstrated elevated or borderline elevated pulmonary artery pressures without structural heart disease. Supplemental oxygen resulted in rapid clinical improvement in all cases. Hospital stay ranged from 2 to 4 days, and none required mechanical ventilation. One patient experienced recurrence shortly after discharge.HAPE should be considered in children presenting with acute hypoxemic respiratory illness after recent ascent to high altitude. The combination of hypoxemia, bilateral infiltrates, low inflammatory markers, and rapid response to oxygen therapy may help distinguish HAPE from infectious pneumonia and facilitate timely treatment.

title: From Physiological to Potential Cardiovascular Maladaptation in Endurance Exercise: Current Evidence, Pathophysiology, and Clinical Implications.
authorString: Luvianto J, Suastika LOS.
abstractText: Emerging evidence suggests that the cardiovascular benefits of exercise may not increase indefinitely with training volume and intensity. As participation in ultraendurance sports continues to rise, concerns have been raised regarding the potential adverse cardiovascular effects of exposure to extreme or ultraendurance exercise. In this Review, we synthesize the current evidence and the pathophysiology regarding the structural, functional, and electrical cardiovascular maladaptations to endurance exercise and highlight the clinical implications of these changes. Several evidences demonstrate that extreme exertion can induce transient cardiac dysfunction; when sustained over years, it may contribute to myocardial fibrosis and associated arrhythmic events. Endurance athletes frequently exhibit a higher prevalence of coronary artery calcification, atherosclerotic plaque burden, and increased arterial stiffness. The alteration driven by long-term endurance training is also strongly implicated in the higher incidence of atrial fibrillation. Although definitive long-term outcomes remain debated, the assumption that limitless exercise yields exclusively protective cardiovascular effects might no longer seem prudent. While regular exercise is unequivocally cardioprotective, extreme endurance training may cross a threshold from physiological adaptation to potential maladaptation. Understanding the pathophysiological mechanisms of exercise-induced cardiac remodeling is critical to optimize the benefit of exercise and the potential risk associated with exercise.

title: Construction and validation of a predictive model for sleep disorders among rural older adults with mild cognitive impairment.
authorString: Yang T, Chi J, Song J, Yan L, Li W, Xu Z, Li H, Dai C, Leng M.

journal.title: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology

abstractText:
Objective

to construct and validate a risk assessment model for sleep disturbance among rural older adults with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), to support early screening and targeted intervention.

Design

a cross-sectional study using data from the 2024 baseline survey of the Active Aging Cohort in Rural Areas, Shandong Province, China.

Subjects

1,049 rural older adults aged ≥ 60 years with MCI.

Methods

demographic, lifestyle, disease history, and psychological factors were collected through face-to-face survey questionnaires and health examinations. Sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Logistic regression identified independent predictors, which were used to build a nomogram. Model performance was evaluated with ROC curve, calibration curve, decision curve analysis, and bootstrap validation.

Results

the prevalence of sleep disturbance was 54.2%. Sex, hypertension, self-rated health, and depression were identified as independent predictors. The nomogram demonstrated good discrimination (AUC = 0.759, 95%CI: 0.731-0.778) and calibration, with internal validation confirming robustness.

title: Factors associated with serum GDF-15, iron deficiency and lower hemoglobin levels in patients with chronic heart failure and healthy elderly people.
authorString: Fukuda T, Tokoi S, Nishikawa R, Hasegawa T, Kondo K, Kayashima R, Kono K, Inami S, Amano H, Arikawa T, Yagi H, Yamaguchi S, Sakuma M, Toyoda S, Nakajima T.
abstractText:
Background

Coexistent chronic heart failure and iron deficiency is frequently encountered in clinical practice and affects prognosis. We investigated factors associated with serum growth differentiation factor (GDF)-15, iron deficiency and lower hemoglobin levels in patients with heart failure and healthy elderly individuals.

Methods and results

Blood tests were performed on 90 patients with heart failure (aged 75.0 ± 10.7 years) and 73 healthy elderly individuals (aged 76.3 ± 6.4 years). Serum GDF-15, tumor necrosis factor (TNF) α, N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and hepcidin concentrations were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Left atrial volume index (LAVI) was measured by echocardiography. Hemoglobin (Hb) in healthy elderly individuals correlated with serum iron and hepcidin. In contrast, Hb in patients with heart failure correlated with serum iron and GDF-15. Serum GDF-15 concentration in healthy elderly subjects correlated with estimated glomerular filtration rate, serum iron, and hepcidin. In contrast, in patients with heart failure, it correlated with NT-proBNP and TNFα. In patients with heart failure, serum iron correlated with LAVI.

Conclusions

Lower hemoglobin levels in patients with heart failure might be associated with elevated serum GDF-15 due to higher serum NT-proBNP and inflammation, as well as iron deficiency. In contrast, lower hemoglobin levels in healthy elderly individuals might involve lower serum iron and hepcidin levels. Lower serum iron concentration was suggested to be involved in left atrial remodeling in patients with heart failure.

title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Cardiovascular Conditions in Medicare Advantage In-Home Health Risk Assessments.
authorString: Oseran AS, Liu-Hass M, Shanab BM, Zheng Z, Lalani C, Yeh RW, Wadhera RK.
abstractText:
Background

Medicare Advantage insurers conduct in-home health risk assessments (HRAs) to identify high-risk patients and facilitate appropriate care. Critics argue this practice increases risk-adjusted payments without improving quality. Comprehensive data on use of in-home HRAs and downstream treatment are lacking.

Objective

To examine trends in cardiovascular conditions diagnosed during in-home HRAs, characteristics associated with HRA-based diagnoses, and treatment rates after diagnoses.

Design

Cohort study.

Setting

Population-based.

Participants

Medicare Advantage beneficiaries.

Measurements

Using 100% Medicare claims, trends in the proportion of cardiovascular conditions diagnosed during in-home HRAs (vs. facility-based visits) were examined. Multivariable logistic regression models were fit to estimate the association between beneficiary- and plan-level characteristics and HRA-based diagnoses and compare treatment rates across settings.

Results

Among 21 496 506 Medicare Advantage beneficiaries diagnosed with a cardiovascular risk factor or disease, the proportion diagnosed during in-home HRAs increased between 2018 and 2022 for hypertension (45.9% to 47.7%), hyperlipidemia (57.8% to 66.7%), diabetes (47.8% to 51.6%), atrial fibrillation (30.0% to 36.0%), ischemic heart disease (37.2% to 41.6%), peripheral vascular disease (64.5% to 73.9%), and heart failure (34.7% to 42.6%). Racial and ethnic minority beneficiaries and those enrolled in lower-rated plans were more likely to receive HRA-based diagnoses. Treatment rates were substantially lower after HRA-based diagnoses across all conditions.

Limitations

Differences in the severity of conditions between groups could not be assessed. Prescription fills were used as a proxy for management. Observed differences in the diagnosis and treatment of conditions across encounter settings may be susceptible to unmeasured confounding.

Conclusion

Among Medicare Advantage beneficiaries, an increasingly large share of cardiovascular conditions are being diagnosed through in-home HRAs, but treatment rates after these diagnoses are consistently lower than after facility-based encounters.

Primary funding source

National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute.

title: Renovascular hypertension drives ischemic white matter injury via brain endothelial AT1R signaling
authorString: Jin X, Kim H, Jung H, Cui Y, Singh SS, Seo HG, Kim SE, Lee HW, Farr TD, Wardlaw JM, Cox SR, Choi SH, Valdés Hernández MdC, Choi JY, Kim BG.
abstractText: BACKGROUND: White matter hyperintensities (WMHs), the principal imaging manifestation of cerebral small vessel disease, lack an animal model that produces pathology of sufficient magnitude to validate potential therapeutics. We characterized white matter (WM) degeneration in a renovascular hypertension (RVH) rat model, interrogated its mechanism, and tested its relevance in patients.  METHODS: RVH was induced by two-kidney, two-clip surgery and assessed by T2-weighted and diffusion MRI, myelin and axonal histology, and blood-brain barrier (BBB) leakage markers. The influence of angiotensin II (Ang II) on barrier function in brain endothelial cells was examined using transendothelial electrical resistance and reactive oxygen species (ROS) assays. Losartan was infused intracerebroventricularly to block brain AT1R (Ang II type 1 receptor) without systemic blood pressure reduction. WMH burden was compared between patients with and without renal artery stenosis, and WMH progression across antihypertensive classes was assessed in the CHALLENGE (Korea), MSS2 (UK), LBC1936 (UK), and SPRINT-MIND-MRI (US) cohorts. RESULTS: Approximately two-thirds of RVH rats developed WMHs that expanded between 7 and 9 weeks, accompanied by reduced fractional anisotropy, demyelination, axonal and mature oligodendrocyte loss, and glial activation. IgG, albumin, and fibrinogen leakage was confined to affected WM. Ang II impaired endothelial barrier function and generated ROS through AT1R. Intracerebroventricular losartan attenuated WM pathology and improved behavior while blood pressure remained comparably elevated. Patients with renal artery stenosis had higher WMH volumes (10.52 versus 6.52 mL; P = 0.035). Angiotensin receptor blocker use was associated with the slowest tertile of annual WMH progression in the Korean cohort (OR, 2.57 [95% CI, 1.20-5.61]) and among White participants in SPRINT-MIND-MRI (OR, 3.52 [95% CI, 1.05-12.29]).  CONCLUSIONS: RVH produces prominent ischemic WM degeneration driven by AT1R signaling, identifying a blood pressure-independent therapeutic target with corroborating clinical evidence.

title: Electronic Health Record Coding of Self-Reported Diagnoses in the All of Us Research Program
authorString: Asiaee A, Aryan K.
abstractText:
Importance: Conditions that are hard to diagnose, several more common in women, may be missing from electronic health records (EHRs), hiding patients from research cohorts and case finding.

Objective:

To measure how often the EHR contains a diagnosis code for chronic conditions that participants report, and to compare this with national survey benchmarks. Design, Setting, and Participants: This cross-sectional study used the All of Us Research Program Registered Tier Dataset v9. Participants were adults with EHR visits in both 12-month periods from July 2021 to June 2023 who completed a health history survey. We analyzed the data in October 2026. Exposures: Self-reported clinician diagnosis of 10 conditions with ongoing visits or treatment, as well as sex at birth, race and ethnicity, age, and years of EHR records. Main Outcomes and Measures: Share of participants reporting current care who had a qualifying diagnosis code, alone and relative to hypertension and type 2 diabetes, and the ratio of age-standardized coded shares to national survey prevalence.

Results:

Of 161,480 respondents, 114,610 (73,870 female [64.5%], median [IQR] age 63 [50-72] years) had at least 5 years of EHR records before the survey. Among those reporting current care, 84.6% (95% CI, 84.2%-85.0%) with hypertension and 87.0% (95% CI, 86.5%-87.6%) with type 2 diabetes had a code, compared with 41.3% (95% CI, 38.9%-43.8%) for endometriosis, 39.4% (95% CI, 34.3%-44.8%) for Lyme disease, and 24.4% (95% CI, 23.2%-25.6%) for chronic fatigue. Counting ICD-9-CM and other mapped codes, 55.3%, 51.5%, and 28.3%, respectively, had any qualifying record. Women had lower coded shares than men for hypertension, type 2 diabetes, obesity, depression, and anxiety (crude ratios 0.93-0.96, within-health-system ratios 0.98-1.02) and higher shares for migraine and fibromyalgia (within health systems, 1.11 [95% CI, 1.07-1.15] and 1.41 [95% CI, 1.29-1.57]). Age-standardized coded shares among active patients were 1.1 to 2.4 times national prevalence of the same self-reported diagnoses. Conclusions and Relevance: In this cross-sectional study, fewer than half of participants reporting ongoing care for chronic fatigue, Lyme disease, or endometriosis had a qualifying ICD-10-CM code. Linking each participant's report to their own record measured this gap directly.

title: Prior hormonal contraceptive use and preeclampsia in Angola: a hospital- based, individually matched case–control study
authorString: Tchitali RF, Pedro H, Lueto T, Kapitão A.
abstractText: Background: Evidence on whether prior hormonal contraceptive use is associated with preeclampsia is sparse and inconsistent, particularly for progestogen-only injectables, and no data exist from Angola. We aimed to estimate this association overall and by method, duration and time since discontinuation. Methods: In this hospital-based case–control study with incidence-density sampling at Hospital Geral de Benguela, Angola, incident cases of preeclampsia (2021 International Society for the Study of Hypertension in Pregnancy criteria with confirmed proteinuria, adjudicated blind to exposure) were each matched to two randomly sampled controls on age, parity group, gestational age and calendar time. The primary exposure was any hormonal contraceptive use before the index pregnancy, obtained by structured calendar interview and verified against records; secondary exposures were method, cumulative duration and time since discontinuation. The primary outcome was preeclampsia; secondary outcomes were early-onset, late-onset and severe preeclampsia. Conditional logistic regression was adjusted for confounders prespecified with a causal diagram. Results: Between January and June 2026, we enrolled 165 cases and 330 controls. Prior hormonal contraceptive use was reported by 54 (32.7%) cases and 62 (18.8%) controls (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.19, 95% CI 1.35–3.57; p = 0.0016). Compared with never use, the aOR was 3.03 (95% CI 1.59–5.78) for depot medroxyprogesterone acetate, which did not differ clearly from other hormonal methods (aOR 1.85, 95% CI 0.83–4.13), and 3.12 (95% CI 1.50–6.50) for discontinuation less than three months before conception; among users, cumulative duration was not associated with preeclampsia. The association was attenuated with documented exposure only (aOR 1.84, 95% CI 0.99–3.44), in a post hoc analysis excluding referred cases (aOR 1.58, 95% CI 0.87–2.86) and against users of non-hormonal methods only (aOR 1.68, 95% CI 0.73–4.11). Conclusions: Prior hormonal contraceptive use was associated with higher odds of preeclampsia, but referral, selection, information or indication bias may explain part of this association, and there was no clear evidence that depot medroxyprogesterone acetate differed from other hormonal methods. These findings do not justify changes to contraceptive counseling and require prospective confirmation.

title: Rutaecarpine mediates phenotypic transition of vascular smooth muscle cells via ADAM17-TNF-NLRP3 signaling pathway
authorString: Tian H, Liu Y, Shi P, Yang Y, Chen Y, Zhou C, Zeng S.
abstractText: The Chinese herbal monomer rutaecarpine is extracted from Evodia rutaecarpa, which has been widely used for hundreds of years to treat hypertension. Rutaecarpine can inhibit pressure overload-induced vascular remodeling and oxidized low-density lipoprotein-induced phenotype transition in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). However, further studies are needed to elucidate the role of rutaecarpine in preventing VSMC phenotypic transition and its underlying mechanisms. This study aimed to explore the inhibitory effect of rutaecarpine on angiotensin (Ang) II-induced VSMC phenotypic transition and its mechanisms. In vitro experiments revealed that rutaecarpine inhibited Ang II- induced VSMC phenotypic transition. Further studies revealed that a disintegrin and metalloproteinase 17 (ADAM17) mediated Ang II- induced VSMC phenotypic transition through tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-NLRP3 signaling pathway. Moreover, treatment with rutaecarpine could inhibit the ADAM17 -TNF-NLRP3 signaling pathway in VSMCs stimulated with Ang II. In conclusion, rutaecarpine prevents Ang II- induced VSMC phenotypic transition via the ADAM17- TNF-NLRP3 signaling pathway.

title: Association between insulin resistance surrogate indices and incident chronic kidney disease among the population with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome stage 0-3: a cohort study
authorString: Wu J, Lin M, Tan X, Chen Y.
abstractText: Background Insulin resistance (IR) is central to the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome. Routine-biochemistry surrogate indices of IR are widely used, but prospective evidence that they identify high-renal-risk individuals within the CKM staging framework is lacking. We compared six such indices for association with new-onset chronic kidney disease (CKD) in middle-aged and older adults at CKM stage 0–3. Methods From the 2011 and 2015 waves of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study we included 4,068 adults aged ≥ 45 years at CKM stage 0–3 with blood data in both waves, excluding baseline eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m², CKM stage 4, and missing or implausible key values. Incident CKD was defined as an eGFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m² in 2011 and an eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m² in 2015 (2021 CKD-EPI creatinine equation). Six indices (TyG, cumulative TyG, TyG-WC, TyG-WHtR, TyG-BMI, METS-IR) entered logistic regression per 1-SD increase and in tertiles, with stepwise adjustment (M1 demographic and behavioural factors; M2 plus blood pressure, LDL-C, uric acid and BUN; M3 plus baseline creatinine, hypertension and diabetes). Restricted cubic splines, ROC analysis (DeLong), eight-subgroup interaction tests and three sensitivity analyses were performed. Results Over four years, 120 participants developed CKD (2.9%). All six indices were higher at baseline in incident cases (P = 0.048 to < 0.001); incidence was highest in the top tertile for all, with significant trends for five (TyG-WHtR 2.14% to 4.20%, P = 0.001). Per-SD odds ratios (ORs) were 1.19–1.42 in crude and M1 models. TyG and cumulative TyG lost significance in M2, whereas the four composite indices remained significant after full adjustment: TyG-WC 1.27 (95% CI 1.03–1.56), TyG-WHtR 1.28 (1.03–1.59), TyG-BMI 1.28 (1.04–1.58) and METS-IR 1.26 (1.03–1.54). No non-linearity was detected (P = 0.087–0.948) and AUCs were 0.563–0.592. Cumulative TyG and METS-IR associations were stronger at BMI < 24 kg/m² (interaction P = 0.035, 0.043); composite-index associations were confined to non-drinkers (interaction P = 0.016–0.041). Excluding BMI ≥ 28 kg/m² or removing uric acid did not change composite-index significance. Conclusions In CKM stage 0–3, composite indices (especially TyG-BMI and TyG-WHtR) were more robustly associated with incident CKD than TyG alone, while all indices showed limited discrimination. These low-cost indices may complement CKM staging in identifying subgroups needing eGFR monitoring.

title: Avoiding Data Leakage in Machine Learning Models for Diabetes and Hypertension Classification Using Routine Occupational Health Screening Data
authorString: Alizadeh-dizaj G, Amiri-Ara M, Teymourzadeh E, Mehdizadeh P, Mesri M, Yaghoubi M.
abstractText: Background and Aim: Reliable clinical prediction using machine learning requires leakage-free model development, yet this critical methodological concern is often overlooked. Type 2 diabetes and hypertension represent major public health challenges in Iran, and early identification of at-risk individuals using routine workplace health screening data could enable cost-effective prevention. This study had a dual objective: first, to develop and validate machine learning models for identifying diabetes and hypertension using routine occupational health screening data; and second and more critically to demonstrate how the inclusion of outcome-defining predictors (fasting blood glucose and blood pressure) artificially inflates model performance through data leakage, a methodological pitfall often overlooked in clinical prediction studies. By comparing 'full' models (with all predictors) against 'clinically meaningful' models (excluding outcome-defining variables), we provide empirical evidence of the magnitude of this bias and offer a transparent framework for avoiding it in similar studies. Methods A retrospective cross-sectional analysis was conducted on 370 health screening records. Five algorithms Decision Tree, Ridge Classifier, Logistic Regression, XGBoost, and Random Forest were developed and compared. Two modeling strategies were implemented: (1) a full model including all predictors, and (2) a clinically meaningful model excluding outcome-defining predictors (fasting blood glucose and blood pressure). The dataset was split into 80% training and 20% testing sets. Five-fold cross-validation was used for hyperparameter optimization, and SMOTE was applied solely to the training set to address class imbalance. Performance was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, AUC-ROC with 95% CI, calibration plots, and Brier scores. Feature importance was assessed using SHAP values. Results The prevalence of diabetes and hypertension was 18.4% (68 cases) and 20.5% (76 cases), respectively. In the clinically meaningful models that excluded outcome-defining predictors (fasting blood glucose and blood pressure), discrimination performance was moderate, with Random Forest achieving an AUC-ROC of 78.34% (95% CI: 72.15–84.92) for diabetes and 76.81% (95% CI: 70.23–83.45) for hypertension. In contrast, when these predictors were included in the full models, performance was artificially inflated (Random Forest AUC-ROC: 96.22% for diabetes and 94.59% for hypertension), confirming substantial data leakage. XGBoost performed comparably in both approaches. SHAP analysis identified age, BMI, waist circumference, and psychological distress (GSI) as the most important non-outcome predictors. Conclusion After excluding outcome-defining predictors to prevent data leakage, machine learning models particularly Random Forest and XGBoost showed moderate but clinically realistic discriminative ability for identifying diabetes and hypertension using routine screening data. Psychological variables contributed meaningfully to prediction, supporting integrated physical and mental health screening in occupational settings. External validation in independent cohorts is required before clinical implementation.

title: Anti-Factor H Antibody–Associated and Complement–Mediated Atypical Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome With Homozygous Cfhr1-Cfhr3 Deletion: A Case Report
authorString: P AP, R S, SAGAYARAJ B.
abstractText: Background Atypical uremic syndrome is rare, life-threatening complement mediated thrombotic microangiopathy characterized by microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia and acute kidney injury. Anti complement factor H (CFH) antibody associated atypical HUS is strongly associated with homozygous deletion of the CFHR1 and CFHR3 genes. Early diagnosis and prompt treatment are essential to prevent irreversible renal injury. We Report a case of previously healthy 10-year-old girl presented with fever, upper respiratory tract symptoms, vomiting, severe anemia, thrombocytopenia, hypertension, acute kidney injury without preceding diarrheal illness. Laboratory investigations demonstrated microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, with schistocytes, elevated lactate dehydrogenase, thrombocytopenia, proteinuria and renal dysfunction. Complement levels C3, C4 within normal limits. Antifactor H antibody titre was markedly elevated (18224 U/ml). Whole -exome sequencing with copy number variation analysis revealed a homozygous deletion involving the CFHR1 and CFHR3 genes. The patient under went five sessions of therapeutic plasma exchange along with corticosteroids and supportive care, resulting in normalization of platelet count, improvement in renal function and clinical recovery. Conclusion This case highlights the importance of combining the clinical findings with complement studies and genetic analysis in diagnosing complement mediated thrombotic microangiopathy. Early plasma exchange resulted in favorable renal recovery in this child with anti-factor H antibody associated aHUS. Categories : General medicine, Pediatrics, Hematology.

title: Governing Digital Health for Noncommunicable Diseases Equity Gender and Sustainable Health Systems in Developing Economies
authorString: Agarwal N, Kumar G, Saxena S.
abstractText: The challenge of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) is greater now than ever before for many healthcare systems in the developing world; at the same time, digital transformation is becoming a crucial aspect of NCD prevention and control, surveillance and health system governance. This paper examines how governance arrangements shape the introduction of digital health into NCD policies and how digital health relates to health equity, gender, and the sustainability of healthcare systems’ development. To achieve this purpose, we conducted a qualitative document analysis of 40 NCD documents published between 2010–2026. An 18-variable coding framework examined NCD governance, digital health and data governance, health equity, capabilities and access, gender, sustainability, and alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Overall, the results show the growing importance of digital technologies in NCD governance; however, they also highlight barriers to implementing these technologies in practice. Diabetes, CVD/hypertension and cancer are the most frequently encountered NCDs. Although the materials examined addressed equity extensively, gendered governance was far less common: gender appeared in only 8 documents (20%), while SDG 5 appeared in only 2 documents (5%). In contrast, SDG 3 appeared in the majority of documents 40, while SDG 10 and SDG 17 appeared in 38 documents each. Therefore, although digitalisation produces some NCD-related outcomes, it does not necessarily guarantee equitable or sustainable results. The value of digital processes depends on governance, accessibility, integration into institutional practices, workforce and funding capacity, and considerations of gender and related inequalities. Thus, digital health should be considered within the framework of sustainable health systems development rather than as a series of open technological innovations.

title: Cardiovascular Risk Factors in Adults with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Retrospective Study
authorString: Goicochea-Ríos EdS, Yupari-Azabache IL, Otiniano NM, Gómez-Goicochea NI.
abstractText:
Introduction:

Diabetes mellitus is a metabolic disease with high prevalence worldwide and is considered a major cardiovascular risk factor. Objective To determine cardiovascular risk factors in adults with controlled and uncontrolled type 2 diabetes mellitus. Material and methods Retrospective descriptive study. Data regarding age, gender, disease duration, cardiovascular risk factors, and laboratory findings were gathered from a final sample of 518 patients (from an initial sample of 560). The study included patients of both sexes treated between 2024 and 2025. Chi-square and Mann-Whitney U tests were applied. Bivariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors specifically associated with poor metabolic control (HbA1c > 7%). A p< 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results 58.2% of patients > 65 years of age had hypertension as a risk factor. In the 51-65 age group, 60% had three risk factors (hypertension, obesity, and dyslipidemia). 57.9% of patients were female. The average duration of the disease is >10 years, and more than 50% of patients have poor metabolic control (HbA1c >7%). 85% of patients receive nephroprotection with ARA II. Albuminuria <30 mg/g was predominant in 83.2% of cases, and stage G1 chronic kidney disease in 70.8%. This pathology is associated with diabetes mellitus regardless of HbA1c values. Among patients with chronic kidney disease, 23% are stage G1 and have albuminuria < 30 mg/g, and 39.9% are stage G2. Bivariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses showed that age (p= 0.03), disease duration (p= 0.00), and hypertension (p=0.01) are associated with poor metabolic control. Also, multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that albuminuria is a factor associated with poor glycemic control (p<0.05). Conclusions Cardiovascular risk factors associated with uncontrolled T2D are age >65 years old, disease duration >10 years, and hypertension. Albuminuria and chronic kidney disease are associated with T2D regardless of metabolic control.

title: Updated practical guide for validation studies of automated cuff blood pressure monitors according to the Universal Standard by the Association for the Advancement of Medical Instrumentation/European Society of Hypertension/International Organization for Standardization (ISO 81060-2:2018) and Amendments 1:2020 and 2:2024.
authorString: Stergiou GS, Menti A, Asmar R, Bilo G, Ntineri A, Palatini P, Parati G, Shennan A, Wang JG, Sierra A, Kollias A, Schutte AE, STRIDE BP and European Society of Hypertension Working Group on Blood Pressure Monitoring..
abstractText: Validated blood pressure (BP) monitors are essential for the accurate diagnosis and management of hypertension. In 2018, the Association for the Advancement of Medical Instrumentation (AAMI), the European Society of Hypertension (ESH), and the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) introduced the AAMI/ESH/ISO Universal Standard (ISO 81060-2:2018) to establish globally accepted requirements for validation studies. This standard is developed specifically for cuff BP devices and is inadequate for cuffless ones, which require different validation procedures. In 2018, the ESH Working Group on Blood Pressure Monitoring published a practical guide and checklist for performing and reporting validation studies of cuff BP devices. Thereafter, two recent amendments (1:2020 and 2:2024) introduced additional requirements for limb and cuff size distribution to ensure that the entire limb range per cuff is adequately assessed. Despite these major initiatives, regular reviews of published validation studies performed by STRIDE BP have identified persistent violations of the validation requirements and incomplete reporting of important data. This statement, prepared by STRIDE BP and the ESH Working Group on Blood Pressure Monitoring, provides an updated guide and checklists, which are complementary to our 2019 guide and aim at assisting investigators and reviewers in performing and reporting high-quality validation studies of cuff BP devices that comply with the latest requirements by the AAMI/ESH/ISO Universal Standard.

title: Plasma proteomic signatures of subclinical atherosclerosis progression for cardiovascular risk stratification: A cohort study.
authorString: Huang Y, Gao R, Li J, Yang B, Huang K, Chen S, Cao J, Liu X, Shen C, Yu L, Zhao L, Li Y, Hu D, Huang J, Lu B, Gu D, Liu F, Lu X.
abstractText:
Background

Existing risk stratification tools inadequately identify individuals with subclinical atherosclerosis (SA) who could benefit from early intervention. This study aimed to develop protein risk scores (ProtRSs) for SA progression and assess their incremental value for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk prediction.

Methods and findings

In a community cohort consisting of 903 individuals undergoing repeated SA assessments (coronary artery calcium [CAC] or carotid plaque) over 6 years (2008-2009 to 2013-2014), protein biomarkers were selected from a panel of 117 proteins using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression to construct SA ProtRSs for CAC and plaque progression, respectively, and their predictive abilities for incident ASCVD risk were evaluated based on a guideline-recommended traditional risk score in a case-cohort of 1,835 individuals (2007-2008 to 2018-2021, median follow-up of 10.4 years). The ProtRSs each included 14 proteins for CAC and plaque progression, explaining 17.1% and 18.4% of respective variances. Effect sizes of these proteins on SA progression showed strong concordance with those on incident ASCVD (r  > 0.75). Each standard deviation increase in CAC and plaque ProtRSs was associated with hazard ratios of 1.36 (95% confidence interval [CI] [1.20,1.54]) and 1.38 (95% CI [1.23,1.54]) for ASCVD risk, respectively. Addition of the SA ProtRSs to the traditional risk score yielded a net reclassification improvement of 0.127 (p < 0.001). Importantly, 18.6% of traditional intermediate-risk individuals were reclassified into the high-risk category (10-year ASCVD event rate: 10.9%), indicating the need for preventive interventions, whereas 32.8% of traditional high-risk individuals were identified as having an even higher rate (13.7%), suggesting the requirement for intensified management. The main limitation is that the predictive value of ProtRSs warrants further large-scale external validation.

Conclusions

SA ProtRSs of coronary calcification and carotid plaque progression may provide additional value over traditional risk assessment, highlighting their potential in refining risk stratification and guiding targeted intervention strategies.

title: Yin-Yang: The Dual Role of Lactate as a Context-Dependent Immunometabolic Regulator in the Inflammatory Microenvironment.
authorString: Wang S, Gan P, Chen Y, Yang B, Ding T, Wu H.
abstractText: Lactate, once regarded merely as the terminal product of glycolysis, is now recognised as a pivotal immunometabolic regulator that actively shapes inflammatory responses. However, accumulating evidence reveals an apparent paradox that lactate can either amplify immune activation or promote inflammation resolution depending on the biological context. The mechanisms underlying this functional duality remain incompletely understood, limiting the development of effective lactate-targeted therapies. In this review, we propose that lactate functions as a context-dependent immunometabolic rheostat whose Yin-Yang properties are determined by the integration of four key factors: lactate concentration, cellular identity, disease stage and inflammatory microenvironment. We summarise how lactate regulates immune responses through coordinated control of metabolic reprogramming, intercellular lactate shuttling, receptor-mediated signalling, intracellular sensing, and protein lactylation, thereby orchestrating the activation and resolution of inflammation. We further discuss the cell-specific actions of lactate across endothelial cells, macrophages, fibroblast-like synoviocytes, neutrophils, and lymphocytes, highlighting how these mechanisms collectively remodel the inflammatory microenvironment. Beyond mechanistic insights, we examine evidence from representative inflammatory disease models, including rheumatoid arthritis, sepsis, and atherosclerosis, and evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies targeting lactate production, transport, sensing and metabolism. Rather than advocating indiscriminate lactate inhibition, current evidence supports context-specific modulation of lactate signalling according to disease stage and immune landscape.

title: Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy Associated With Severe Medetomidine Withdrawal: A Case Report.
authorString: Krishna D, Bennett B, Lin A, Spadaro A.
abstractText:
Background

Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (TCM) is a transient syndrome of cardiac dysfunction with no occlusive coronary arterial disease, which may mimic an ischemic cardiac event. The pathogenesis of TCM is thought to be primarily driven by the effects of a temporary catecholamine surge on cardiac and vascular tissue. Medetomidine (an a2 agonist commonly found in the Philadelphia fentanyl supply) withdrawal is characterized by agitation and sympathetic hyperactivity that can precipitate a catecholamine surge. Though withdrawal from other Central Nervous System (CNS)-depressing substances such as opioids and clonidine have been found to be associated with TCM, there is little documentation of this phenomenon occurring from medetomidine withdrawal.

Case

A 51-year-old woman with no reported medical history other than opioid use disorder presented to the emergency department due to concern for withdrawal from fentanyl and medetomidine. Her opioid withdrawal was well controlled with methadone and oxycodone. Shortly after coming off her dexmedetomidine infusion (started for medetomidine withdrawal), she developed acute ST-segment changes on electrocardiogram, elevated troponin levels on bloodwork, and regional wall-motion abnormalities on transthoracic echocardiogram. Her coronary angiography showed no occlusion and repeat cardiac laboratory workup days later had normalized with improvement in ejection fraction on cardiac echocardiography and magnetic resonance imaging. This signifies a temporary stress cardiomyopathy, likely from a2 agonist withdrawal.

Discussion

This case describes TCM in a patient experiencing medetomidine withdrawal. This patient's cardiac dysfunction was transient, temporally correlating with the cessation of her dexmedetomidine infusion. This suggests an a2 agonist mediated withdrawal leading to sympathetic hyperactivity which can precipitate TCM.

title: Spatial Patterns of White Matter Hyperintensities and Cognitive Function in Older Adults: A Community-Based Study
authorString: Chen X, Nishimaki K, Tomoshige S, Chotiyanonta JS, Uchida Y, Wasserman BA, Gottesman RF, Guallar E, Windham BG, Oishi K.
abstractText:
Objectives

White matter hyperintensities (WMH) are associated with cognitive decline in older adults. We examined whether anatomically defined spatial WMH patterns are associated with cognitive performance and subsequent decline in a large community-based cohort with approximately six years of follow-up.

Methods

We analyzed 1,667 participants (mean age 76 years) from the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Neurocognitive Study. WMH were segmented from FLAIR images and mapped to 112 white matter regions using deep-learning-based parcellation. Principal component analysis identified dominant WMH distribution patterns; candidate components were selected by Horn’s parallel analysis and retained if stable across resampled split samples. Linear mixed-effects models examined associations between WMH patterns and cognitive performance at baseline and follow-up, adjusting for demographic, genomic, and vascular risk factors. Robustness was assessed using analyses accounting for total WMH burden, study center, and selective attrition.

Results

Of 14 candidate principal components (PCs) identified by parallel analysis, eight met the resampling stability criterion and were retained, together explaining 42% of the variance. Three components were associated with cross-sectional or future cognition. PC3, characterized by deep white matter burden in the corpus callosum and anterior corona radiata with relative preservation of superficial white matter, showed no cross-sectional association at baseline but was associated with accelerated decline across multiple domains.

Interpretation

A deep spatial pattern of WMH loading on the corpus callosum and anterior corona radiata was associated with subsequent cognitive decline in the absence of a cross-sectional association at baseline, independent of total lesion burden.

title: MitoFLUX-EM reveals damaged mitochondria are captured by pre-existing mitolysosomes during PINK1-dependent mitophagy in the heart
authorString: Narendra D, Petersen J, Huang X, Guillermier C, Wilson M, Florio DD, Lin H, D'Silva T, Li Y, Springer W.
abstractText: Damaged mitochondria are cleared by PINK1-Parkin mitophagy, but the pathway is incompletely understood in vivo. Here, we developed MitoFLUX-EM, combining electron microscopy with nanoscale ¹⁵N isotope tracing to resolve the temporal sequence of mitophagy intermediates in vivo, and applied it to a cardiomyopathy mouse model (CHCHD10 S59L) with high PINK1-dependent mitophagy. Unexpectedly, we found that damaged mitochondria are directly captured by pre-existing mitolysosomes, resulting in multisegmented mitolysosomes that sequestered as many as 33 mitochondria at distinct stages of ultrastructural degradation. Autophagosomal-like membranes arising from the mitolysosomes preferentially engaged the intact outer membrane of damaged mitochondria and neither protein removal nor rupture of the outer membrane was required for mitophagy, contrary to prior models. Pink1 loss disrupted this pathway, causing accumulation of aggregates within mitochondria and reduced survival. These findings reveal that PINK1-dependent mitophagy proceeds through a novel form of microautophagy to safeguard cardiac mitochondrial quality in vivo and establish MitoFLUX-EM as a platform for resolving organelle turnover.

title: Transarterial Computed Tomographic Angiography in Patients With Impaired Renal Function Undergoing Endovascular Aortic Repair.
authorString: Beropoulis E, Pitoulias AG, Bisdas T, Torsello GB, Torsello GF.
abstractText: PurposeComputed tomography angiography (CTA) is crucial for preoperative planning and postoperative surveillance of endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). Renal function impairment however limits pre- and postoperative assessment. The aim of our study was to evaluate the safety and diagnostic value of a novel technique in the setting of patients undergoing EVAR.Methods216 patients with chronic kidney disease undergoing transbrachial placement of an angiography catheter in the aorta for contrast medium administration were analyzed retrospectively. 45 patients with normal kidney function and aortic aneurysms were included as control group. 27 were female, 84 cases were for thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm, while 106 cases were for abdominal aortic aneurysm. Primary endpoint was the freedom from contrast-induced acute kidney injury. Secondary safety endpoints were freedom from access site complications and cerebrovascular incidents. Imaging quality endpoints were attenuation values and contrast-to-noise-ratios in predefined vessels, validated by intraclass correlation coefficients.ResultsMean creatinine change was -.11 mg/dL, mean GFR change was 2.13% in the intervention group. There were 10 (4.6%) false aneurysms and two access site hematoma (0.93%). Two cerebrovascular incidents (0.9%) were transient. Transarterial CTA attenuation values varied between 210.4 (±89) and 241.4 (±98) Hounsfield units (HU), and 306.35 (±63.27) to 321.39 (±70.12) HU in the control group. The mean amount of contrast medium used in the catheter group was significantly reduced (31.70 ± 5.82 mL) compared to the control group (P = .001). Contrast-to-noise ratios varied between 9.1 (±4.6) and 11.1 (±4.4. Intraclass correlation coefficients between the readings were very good (0.987-0.992).ConclusionCatheter-based transarterial computed tomographic angiography is a safe and efficacious way to evaluate patients with aortic aneurysms, both prior and after EVAR.

title: Percutaneous Multivalvular Endocarditis Debulking With a Whole-Body Embolic Protection Device.
authorString: Younes A, Oostra C, Roether R, Crescenzo D, Dabaja M, Georgescu C, Younes S.
abstractText:
Background

Percutaneous debulking of left-sided endocarditis and thrombus has previously relied on cerebral-only embolic protection devices. The Emboliner is an investigational nitinol-mesh filter that provides whole-body embolic protection and has been studied in transcatheter aortic valve replacement.

Summary

We describe its first reported use as an adjunct to AngioVac-based debulking in 2 patients: 1 with aortic valve endocarditis and 1 with combined tricuspid and mitral endocarditis.

Discussion

The Emboliner was successfully deployed in both cases, with over 90% of vegetation removed and no periprocedural or in-hospital embolic events. Deployment technique differed by vegetation location: in the aortic valve case, the AngioVac cannula was advanced through the filter's access port; in the tricuspid/mitral case, no further interaction with the filter was required once deployed.

Novelty

This represents, to our knowledge, the first reported use of whole-body embolic protection during aortic and combined tricuspid/mitral percutaneous endocarditis debulking.

Take-home message

Whole-body embolic protection may offer an important adjunct to percutaneous debulking in patients at high surgical risk.

title: Correlation of Neuron-Specific Enolase and S100ß Protein Levels, Inflammatory Cytokines, and Neurological Injury in Children Undergoing Cardiopulmonary Bypass.
authorString: Twite M, Sophocles A, Pan Z, Friesen R.
abstractText:
Background

The systemic inflammatory response syndrome to cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) affects all organ systems including the brain. Perioperative brain injury in children with congenital heart disease is often clinically silent in the acute perioperative period and may not be detected until patients are older. The plasma biomarkers neuron-specific enolase (NSE) and S100ß protein show potential for detecting neurological injury in the perioperative period.

Objectives

The three objectives of this study were to examine the correlation of NSE and S100ß protein levels with inflammatory cytokines, parameters of CPB, and the development of neurological injury in the intensive care unit following cardiac surgery in children.

Methods

50 children undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB had blood samples drawn at three time points: after induction of anesthesia, 30 min post-CPB, and 24 h post-CPB. Blood samples were analyzed for NSE, S100ß, and the inflammatory cytokines IL-6, IL-8, and IL-10. Data were collected on CPB durations and neurological injury diagnosed in the postoperative period.

Results

NSE and S100ß increased significantly following bypass and correlated with increases of IL-6, IL-8, and IL-10. There was a significant positive correlation of NSE and S100ß with duration of CPB, and of S100ß with duration of aortic cross clamp. Three patients suffered neurological insult. These patients had greater levels of NSE during the post-CPB period (p = 0.02) and S100ß at 24 h post-CPB (p = 0.02) than patients without neurological deficits.

Conclusion

The positive correlation between NSE, S100ß, inflammatory cytokines, and neurological deficits suggests that the systemic inflammatory response to CPB may contribute to neurological injury and that NSE and S100ß may be useful tools to detect neurological injury following CPB.

title: Percutaneous and Endovascular Embolization-Based Treatments of Type 1A and Type 1B Endoleaks after Endovascular Aneurysm Repair.
authorString: Incesu MM, Akkan MK, Barutcu Asfuroglu B, Asfuroglu U, Erdogan Kaydu N, Ozer A, Demirtas H, Oktar GL, Ilgit ET.
abstractText: ObjectiveThis retrospective, observational study was conducted to evaluate the efficacy of embolization-based treatments for Types 1A and 1B endoleaks following endovascular aneurysm repair.DesignA total of 26 patients who underwent endovascular aneurysm repair between January 2005 and September 2023 and subsequently received embolization therapy for Types 1A or 1B endoleak, either at the end of the procedure or during follow-up, were retrospectively reviewed.MethodsEmbolization was performed in 16 patients with Type 1A endoleaks and 10 with Type 1B. Eight of the 16 patients who underwent embolization for Type 1A endoleaks required additional treatments such as aortic cuff placement or a chimney graft. Similarly, six out of the 10 patients treated with embolization for Type 1B endoleaks underwent adjunctive procedures such as iliac stent-graft extension. The primary endpoint was the absence of aneurysm sac enlargement. Secondary endpoints included technical success and the avoidance of endoleak-related reintervention.ResultsAneurysm sac regression or stabilization was observed in 68.7% of Type 1A and 70% of Type 1B endoleak cases over mean follow-up periods of 43.1 and 22.3 months, respectively.ConclusionEmbolization-based endovascular treatment, alone or combined with adjunctive endograft procedures, may achieve aneurysm sac stabilization or regression in a substantial proportion of patients with Types 1A and 1B endoleaks. However, the possibility of recurrence and reintervention, particularly in Type 1A endoleaks, remains an important limitation of this approach and warrants continued imaging surveillance.

title: EXPRESS: Cerebral Microbleed Burden After Aortic and Cardiac Surgery Is Associated With Extracorporeal Circulation Exposure: Evidence From Young Patients With Heritable Connective Tissue Disorders.
authorString: Vornetti G, Regazzo R, Barone V, Belacchi V, La Rosa G, Mariucci E, Donti A, Tonon C, Lodi R, Spinardi L.

journal.title: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism

abstractText:
Background and purpose

Cerebral microbleeds (CMBs) occur after surgery involving extracorporeal circulation (ECC), though confounding risk factors may obscure this association. Patients with heritable connective tissue diseases (HCTDs) requiring early surgery provide an ideal model to investigate ECC-related CMBs. We aimed to assess CMB prevalence, distribution, and surgical correlates in a genetically confirmed HCTD population.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed 111 HCTD patients with brain magnetic resonance. CMBs number and location were correlated with clinical and surgical data, including procedure frequency, type, and, when available, ECC duration.

Results

All 58 patients exposed to surgery under ECC exhibited CMBs, compared to only four surgery-naïve individuals. CMBs showed a predominantly lobar pattern. CMB burden was significantly higher in patients with multiple surgeries and longer ECC duration (P<0.001), whereas valve type and surgical technique showed no associationDiscussion:In our cohort, CMBs were identified in all individuals with ECC exposure. The absence of significant differences in CMB burden across surgical techniques weakens the hypothesis that CMBs originate solely from metallic microemboli. In young, normotensive patients with HCTDs, ECC exposure was uniformly associated with CMBs, with burden increasing with repeated procedures and ECC duration.

title: Computational Repurposing of Small-Molecule Drugs for Local Perivascular Hydrogel Delivery in Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm
authorString: Cheng H.
abstractText:
Background:

Perivascular hydrogel wrapping of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) can sustain high local drug concentrations while avoiding systemic exposure, but no study has systematically prioritized which approved small molecules are best suited to such an extra-adventitial depot. This study combined drug-target evidence with physicochemical filtering to rank small-molecule candidates for local hydrogel formulation. Methods. Differentially expressed AAA genes were integrated from public human datasets (GSE57691, GSE7084, GSE47472) and mapped to approved small molecules using the Open Targets platform and ChEMBL. Links were filtered for coherent direction (inhibitors targeting up-regulated genes), and retained drugs were profiled with RDKit for molecular weight, lipophilicity (logP), and topological polar surface area (TPSA). A local-fit rule (molecular weight 200-500, logP 1-4, TPSA below 150) was applied, and candidates were organized into three tiers. Results. The integrated AAA target set contained 2,437 genes. Matching to approved small molecules yielded 1,061 drug-target links, and coherent filtering retained 152 links (121 drugs, 32 targets). The leading Tier 1 candidates were sulfasalazine, dasatinib, and celecoxib, targeting ALOX5/PTGS2 and the Src-family kinases. A second tier included diclofenac, etoricoxib, zileuton, balsalazide, idelalisib, ibuprofen, and ketorolac. The literature anchors colchicine (suitable physicochemistry) and doxycycline (borderline, overly hydrophilic) were retained separately, and the central AAA targets matrix metalloproteinase (MMP)-9, MMP-12, NLRP3, and CASP1 had no approved small-molecule ligand. Conclusions. This computational analysis prioritizes a small set of approved, physicochemically suitable small molecules for local perivascular hydrogel delivery against AAA. The ranking is a formulation hypothesis rather than evidence of efficacy; local release, toxicity, and in vivo effects require biomaterial and animal validation.

title: Optimal Resources for Children's Surgery 2: Tiered Recommendations for Minimum Essential Children's Surgical Procedures Across Health System Levels.
authorString: Biswangree A, Ameh EA, Lakhoo K, Shalaby M, Cairo SB, GICS Membership.
abstractText:
Background

In 2015 the World Health Assembly (WHO), based on recommendations by the Lancet Commission on Global Surgery, passed resolution (68:15) on strengthening emergency and essential surgical care and anesthesia as a component of universal health coverage. However, children's surgery was not adequately represented and in response, the Global Initiative for Children's Surgery (GICS) published the Optimal Resources for Children's Surgical Care (OReCS) in 2019 providing insight into procedures which should be performed at different facility types. OReCS 2 addresses a gap in both policy and published literature to further define surgical conditions and procedural capabilities by hospital level.

Methods

We performed a review of the literature to identify procedures routinely performed in a variety of settings. We then used an iterative Delphi like approach to identify specialty-specific procedures and nursing skills by hospital level. Participation was open to all members of GICS with representation from 21 working groups and more than 50 low-middle income countries (LMICs) and high-income countries (HICs). Data on essential procedures were collected for twelve specialty groups. Modifications of the recommendations provided by the working groups were made by the executive board based on firsthand knowledge of capabilities at lower-level facilities where subspecialists have less experience. Final recommendations were made based on greater than 75% agreement by respondents and review of the executive board of GICS.

Results

Procedures performed at health centers were limited to those not requiring anesthesia or sedation and were largely identified to help triage and stabilize patients for transfer to higher level care. Similarly, first level hospital procedures focused on stabilization and transfer to referral level hospitals for most specialties. Alternatively, specialties such as ophthalmology and dental surgery have identified definitive procedures for lower-level facilities. Procedures performed at the National Children's Hospital level include those requiring specialty providers and equipment such as transplantation, repair of congenital heart disease, and reconstructive surgery for complex trauma, congenital anomalies, and burns.

Conclusions

This updated version of OReCS provides specific examples of procedural capabilities for twelve subspecialties at the health center, first, second, third, and referral level hospitals in LMICs. Whereas the list is not meant to be all inclusive, it provides a framework within which to define the minimum essential material resources, equipment, and personnel by hospital level.

title: Ultrasound-Guided versus Fluoroscopy-Guided Femoral Access for Structural Heart Procedures: Outcomes From Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation and Left Atrial Appendage Closure.
authorString: Kıvrak A, Sezer C, Canpolat U, Ateş AH, Çöp S, Çöteli C, Yorgun H, Şahiner ML, Kaya EB, Özer N, Aytemir K.
abstractText:
Background

Transfemoral access is the default approach for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and left atrial appendage closure (LAAC). Although ultrasound (US)-guided femoral puncture improves first-pass success and reduces vascular complications in randomized trials, real-world data in contemporary structural heart interventions, including both arterial and venous large-sheath access, remain limited. The authors aimed to compare US-guided vs. conventional transfemoral access in patients undergoing TAVI and LAAC.

Methods

This single-center, retrospective cohort study included 165 consecutive patients undergoing transfemoral structural procedures between January 2022 and December 2024 (93: TAVI; 72: LAAC). Ultrasound guidance was used in 57 procedures (34.5%). Arterial and venous cohorts were analyzed separately. Primary outcomes were absolute hemoglobin decrease (ΔHb) and access-site vascular complications (hematoma, pseudoaneurysm, and arteriovenous fistula). In the arterial cohort, 1 : 1 propensity score matching was performed to adjust for baseline differences.

Results

Hemoglobin decline was significantly smaller with US guidance in both venous (0.80 ± 0.95 vs. 1.50 ± 1.11 g/dL; P = .009) and arterial procedures (0.58 ± 0.97 vs. 1.29 ± 1.00 g/dL; P = .002). In the venous cohort, complication rates were numerically lower but not statistically different (3.8% vs. 17.4%; P = .143). In contrast, arterial complications were significantly reduced with US guidance. After propensity matching (31 patients per group), complications occurred in 3.2% vs. 29.0% [Absolute Risk Reduction(ARR) = 25.8%, Number Need to Treat (NNT) = 4, P = .013].

Conclusions

Ultrasound-guided transfemoral access was associated with reduced hemoglobin decline and fewer vascular complications, particularly in large-bore arterial procedures, supporting routine integration of real-time US guidance in structural interventions.

title: Percutaneous approach to aortic disease: EVAR, TEVAR and newer techniques for more proximal disease.
authorString: Borghese O, Lodico T, Felice G, Tshomba Y.
abstractText: Advances in device design, imaging and vascular-closure technology have driven a progressive shift from surgical femoral exposure to totally percutaneous strategies for endovascular aortic repair. This narrative review summarises contemporary evidence and practical considerations for percutaneous access across the spectrum of aortic disease, from infrarenal endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) to thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR), fenestrated/branched repair and endovascular treatment of the aortic arch. Percutaneous femoral access is now supported by randomized evidence, large registries and administrative cohorts showing high technical success, fewer wound complications, shorter operative times and shorter hospital stay compared with routine surgical cutdown, and real-time ultrasound-guided puncture has become a guideline-endorsed standard of care. Major contemporary developments include computed tomography-based access planning centred on calcification burden and sheath-to-artery ratio; an individualised, anatomy-driven choice between suture- and plug-based closure devices; endovascular preparation of hostile iliofemoral anatomy with pave-and-crack, endoconduits and intravascular lithotripsy; low-profile endografts that have widened transfemoral eligibility; and percutaneous axillary and carotid routes that enable complex TEVAR, fenestrated/branched and selected arch repairs in experienced centres, although evidence for these latter applications remains largely observational. Looking ahead, further reductions in delivery-system profile, dedicated large-bore closure technologies, image-fusion guidance and off-the-shelf branched devices are expected to extend fully percutaneous repair to increasingly complex anatomy, while prospective, aortic-specific and device-level comparisons with standardized anatomical metrics and long-term follow-up are needed to refine patient selection and confirm durable limb and target-vessel patency.

title: Deep learning-based echocardiography for cardiac assessment: a systematic literature review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Romano-Martinez A, Zeid S, Krolevets M, Kontohow-Beckers K, Ten Cate V, Lurz P, Engelhardt S, Kramer S, Troebs SO, Wild PS.
abstractText:
Aims

Artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning (DL), has shown significant potential for enhancing the assessment of echocardiograms in clinical practice. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the performance of DL models and to identify factors affecting their performance.

Methods and results

A systematic review of the PubMed, CENTRAL, and Web of Science databases was conducted, yielding 16 248 potential publications. Of these, 160 studies met the inclusion criteria. Only studies applying fully automated DL networks to echocardiographic loops were considered. Performance estimates were pooled using a random-effects meta-analysis. The studies were categorized into five distinct groups: prediction of disease or mortality, replication of established measures, segmentation of cardiac chambers, classification of chamber views, and assessment of image quality. High heterogeneity that could not be resolved was observed in studies focusing on cardiac chamber segmentation and classification. Model performance was influenced by a variety of different factors, including medical target and input characteristics such as video resolution, number of frames used, and total participants included during training.

Conclusion

DL models achieve high performance across various applications in echocardiography. In selected tasks, they may reduce reliance on expert input and support greater automation of echocardiographic workflows. However, further validation, assessment of clinical utility, and evaluation in real-world settings are required before widespread clinical adoption.

title: Systematic Review of Devices, Designs, and Trials for the Treatment of Deep Venous Reflux.
authorString: Ofori KA, Li S, Grimshaw AA, Chaer R, Ochoa Chaar CI.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: J Vasc Surg Venous Lymphat Disord
journal.title: Journal of vascular surgery. Venous and lymphatic disorders
journal.isoabbreviation: J Vasc Surg Venous Lymphat Disord

abstractText:
Objective

Chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) is driven primarily by venous reflux and affects nearly one-third of adults. While superficial reflux is effectively treated with ablation, therapeutic options for deep venous reflux (DVR) remain limited. Despite decades of innovation, no prosthetic or bioprosthetic venous valve has achieved U.S. regulatory approval. We systematically reviewed device strategies, clinical and hemodynamic outcomes, complications, and barriers to translation for devices designed to treat DVR.

Methods

We conducted a PROSPERO-registered systematic review (CRD420251101761) of six databases from inception through February 2026, including in vivo animal and human studies evaluating prosthetic or bioprosthetic devices for DVR. Studies of native valve repair or autotransplantation were excluded. The primary outcome for human studies was clinical improvement, and secondary outcomes included patency, procedural complications, valvular function, and thrombosis.

Results

Of 516 records identified, 15 met inclusion criteria: 8 human and 7 animal studies. Two principal strategies were identified: intraluminal valve restoration (VR) and external compression (EC), with approximately 40% of devices delivered percutaneously or endovenously. In human studies, technical success ranged from 87.7%-100%, patency from 67%-100%, and perioperative complication rates from 0%-44%, consisting primarily of bleeding, wound infection, and valve thrombosis. Valve occlusion occurred in up to 28% of animal implants and 18%-22% of select human cohorts. Two perioperative deaths occurred in animal studies; none were reported in human studies. Among human studies, valve competency assessment methods varied substantially. Reported competency ranged from 0%-92%, reflecting heterogeneity in imaging modalities and definitions. Discordance between anatomic patency, duplex-derived reflux reduction, and clinical improvement was frequently observed. In contemporary multicenter trial data, fewer than half of patients met predefined reflux-reduction endpoints despite high device patency and substantial clinical improvement, highlighting discordance between anatomic, hemodynamic, and patient-centered outcomes. By one year, pain had improved in 75%-97% of patients; rVCSS decreased by 37%-81%, with clinically meaningful (≥3-point) improvement in up to 84.6%; and ulcer healing ranged from 67%-100%. Longer follow-up extended to 2 years in animal studies and up to 11 years in human series with various outcomes reported.

Conclusion

Several devices developed for DVR have demonstrated technical feasibility and symptom improvement. However, the risk of thrombosis, the marginal impact on valvular function, and the lack of standardization and selection of adequate endpoints in the measurement of results remain major barriers to regulatory approval. Standardized composite endpoints integrating objective hemodynamic measures with patient-centered outcomes are essential to advance durable DVR device development and clinical translation.

title: Vascular Risk Factors and Late-Onset Epilepsy.
authorString: Choi H, Gutierrez J, Wang T, Liu M, Leu CS, Misiewicz S, Han J, Bello NA, Biggs ML, Briceño EM, Brickman AM, Burke JF, Chen L, Colantonio LD, Diaz Andino SP, Elkind MSV, Fitzpatrick AL, Gonzalez Corona C, Gottesman RF, Gross AL, Huang L, Johnson EL, Johnson WC, Levine DA, Longstreth WT, Pelagalli Maia S, Mayeux RP, Petersen BC, Obalana O, Reyes-Dumeyer D, Rundek T, Sanchez D, Shea SJ, Strobino K, Tom SE, Zhu CW, Thacker EL.
abstractText:
Importance

Late-onset epilepsy (LOE; onset at age ≥65 years) is increasingly recognized in older adults and may be associated with vascular risk.

Objective

To identify vascular risk factors (VRFs) associated with incident LOE in older adults.

Design, setting, and participants

This study is an individual participant data meta-analysis of 6 US population-based prospective cohort studies (the Epilepsy-Cog Study). In 5 cohorts linked to Medicare for epilepsy case ascertainment, follow-up for LOE began when a participant had accrued 2 years of continuous fee-for-service enrollment and was 65 years of age or older and extended to the end of continuous enrollment. Claims linkage covered 1991-2018 in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study (ARIC), 1992-2019 in the Cardiovascular Health Study (CHS), 2000-2019 in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA), 2000-2020 in the Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke Study (REGARDS), and 1999-2019 in the Washington Heights/Inwood Columbia Aging Project (WHICAP). In the Northern Manhattan Study (NOMAS), which was not Medicare linked and used cohort-based epilepsy case ascertainment, follow-up for LOE began at cohort entry in 1993-2008 and extended to 2024. Data analysis was completed in January 2026.

Exposures

Sociodemographic characteristics and VRFs assessed by self-report, examinations, laboratory measures, and medication use.

Main outcome and measures

The primary outcome was incident LOE. Associations between risk factors and incident LOE were evaluated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios.

Results

From 43 753 participants in Epilepsy-Cog, 551 participants with prevalent epilepsy and 945 with no follow-up after Epilepsy-Cog baseline were excluded. Among 42 257 participants (mean [SD] age, 71.4 [6.9] years; 23 383 [56.0%] female) followed up for a mean (SD) of 9.3 (6.2) years, 1500 participants (3.5%) developed LOE (3.8 per 1000 person-years). In fully adjusted models, LOE risk was higher with current smoking (HR = 1.39; 95% CI, 1.18-1.64), hypertension (HR = 1.17; 95% CI, 1.04-1.31), diabetes (HR = 1.42; 95% CI, 1.25-1.62), chronic kidney disease (HR = 1.29; 95% CI, 1.13-1.48), history of stroke (HR = 1.99; 95% CI, 1.63-2.43), and apolipoprotein E ε4 allele (1 ε4 allele: HR = 1.22; 95% CI, 1.07-1.39; 2 ε4 alleles: HR = 1.84; 95% CI, 1.36-2.50). Associations of VRFs with LOE were similar across age, sex, and race and ethnicity subgroups.

Conclusions and relevance
