In this pooled analysis of 6 US cohorts, multiple VRFs and a history of stroke were associated with incident LOE. These findings suggest that LOE may reflect the underlying burden of brain vascular disease.

title: Neointimal Hyperplasia and Restenosis: Epidemiology, Pathophysiology, Animal Models, Clinical Features, Diagnosis, and Management.
authorString: Wang K, Zhang D, Hu Y, Zhao Y, Wang X, Jiang L, Jiang M.
abstractText: In-stent restenosis (ISR) remains a major complication following vascular interventions, with neointimal hyperplasia representing a central pathological process that can adversely affect postoperative outcomes. Accumulating evidence indicates that neointimal hyperplasia is driven by vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) phenotypic transition, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and multiple forms of programmed cell death. Despite substantial advances, the underlying pathogenic mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This review comprehensively examines neointimal hyperplasia from the perspectives of epidemiology, pathophysiology, preclinical animal models, clinical manifestations, diagnostic approaches, and therapeutic strategies. Particular attention is given to the emerging associations between recently characterized forms of programmed cell death, including ferroptosis and cuproptosis, and neointimal hyperplasia. In addition, commonly used preclinical animal models are reviewed, together with potential therapeutic approaches such as colchicine and vasostatin-2 and their underlying mechanisms. The diagnostic roles of invasive imaging and noninvasive modalities in evaluating neointimal hyperplasia are discussed, with emphasis on their respective advantages and limitations. Furthermore, current stent-based strategies, pharmacological therapies, and alternative interventions for ISR are summarized, along with critical consideration of their limitations and potential avenues for improvement. By integrating mechanistic evidence with available therapeutic options, this review aims to provide a comprehensive theoretical framework for the clinical management of ISR.

title: The Efferocytosis-Driven Macrophage Polarization: A Concerto in the Tumor Immunosuppressive Microenvironment.
authorString: Chen Q, Wu C, Huang C, Zhou H.
abstractText: Efferocytosis plays a critical role in maintaining tissue homeostasis and controlling inflammation. However, in the tumor microenvironment, this process is hijacked to promote immune suppression. Treatments like radiotherapy and chemotherapy lead to widespread tumor cell death, which triggers efferocytosis and drives macrophages into an immunosuppressive state, allowing the tumor to evade the immune system and resist treatment. Nonetheless, the way efferocytic signals alter macrophage function and promote protumor effects during the recognition, engulfment, and digestion of apoptotic cells remains largely unclear. Therefore, this review thoroughly examines the influence of signaling molecules during the three stages of efferocytosis on macrophage phenotype and function. Subsequently, we explore the impact of polarized M2-type macrophages on shaping the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and regulating the development of drug resistance. Additionally, we critically evaluate the current status of clinical translation of efferocytosis receptor-related drugs and analyze the potential reasons for their synergistic or antagonistic interactions with chemotherapy and immunotherapy. This study provides a comprehensive understanding of the regulatory mechanisms of efferocytosis in macrophage polarization, enhancing knowledge of the fundamental mechanisms underlying tumor immune evasion and offering important guidance for the development of anticancer therapies targeting the efferocytosis process.

title: Heterogeneity in Time-Outcome Associations After Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Binational Registry Study.
authorString: Lin CJ, Kim YS, Yang CH, Hsieh YC, Park JM, Chen CH, Kang K, Shan Sung P, Lee SJ, Chen YW, Cha JK, Lin KH, Park TH, Tang CW, Lee K, Chu HJ, Lee J, Fu CH, Hong KS, Chou CL, Yu KH, Lin CH, Kim DE, Yen SY, Kim JT, Chen PL, Choi JC, Kwon JH, Shin DI, Sohn SI, Chiou HY, Kim C, Park KY, Kim CK, Lien LM, Heo SH, Lee JT, Chan L, Tang SC, Kim BJ, Chung CP, Jeng JS, Bae HJ, TREAT-AIS and CRCS-K investigators.

journal.title: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association

abstractText:
Background

Although "time is brain" remains a core principle in acute stroke care, the association between treatment timing and functional outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) varies across patients. Some individuals treated in extended time windows still achieve favorable outcomes, a phenomenon termed the "late window paradox." Differences in stroke pathophysiology across etiologies may contribute to heterogeneity in the time-outcome relationship after EVT. We investigated factors associated with heterogeneity in time-dependent EVT responsiveness, with particular attention to stroke etiology.

Methods

We analyzed data from two multicenter registries in Korea (CRCS-K) and Taiwan (TREAT-AIS) from January 2019 to April 2023. Patients with anterior circulation acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism (CE) or large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) were included. Multivariable regression and interaction analyses were performed to evaluate the association between onset-to-puncture (OTP) time and 90-day functional outcomes and to identify effect modifiers.

Results

Among 4,719 patients (mean age 72.0 years; 42.9% women; median NIHSS 15), longer OTP time was associated with lower odds of 90-day functional independence (adjusted OR per hour, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.96-0.98; p=0.001). The impact of OTP time varied by stroke characteristics. CE etiology, MCA occlusion, higher NIHSS, and male sex were associated with greater time sensitivity. In CE strokes, each hour of delay reduced the odds of functional independence by 4% (aOR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.94-0.97; p<0.001), whereas no significant association was observed in LAA strokes (P_interaction=0.028).

Conclusion

The association between EVT timing and functional outcome varies according to stroke etiology and clinical characteristics, highlighting heterogeneity in time-outcome relationships among EVT-treated patients and providing observational insight into outcome variability in extended treatment windows.

title: Family screening for genetic cardiomyopathies in ECG-positive phenotype-negative adolescents: a joint clinical and genetic approach.
authorString: Abela M, Debattista J, Scerri J, Felice T, Grech V, Scerri C.
abstractText: Adolescents may present with abnormal ECG findings despite having no structural or electrical evidence of cardiomyopathy. The value of extending family screening to this subgroup remains uncertain. To evaluate the impact of family screening in ECG-positive phenotype-negative adolescents, and determine whether a joint clinical-genetic approach improves the diagnostic yield. In this prospective cohort study, adolescents with an abnormal ECG identified through a nationwide screening program underwent comprehensive clinical/genetic evaluation. Phenotype-negative individuals were included. Relatives underwent clinical screening, with cascade genetic testing offered when probands carried a likely/definite pathogenic (LP/P) cardiomyopathy variant. Abnormal screening outcomes included relatives with (i) de novo cardiomyopathy diagnosis, (ii) early cardiomyopathic traits, or (iii) gene-positive/phenotype-negative (G + P -) status. Sixteen adolescents (0.6%) met inclusion criteria, and 3 (18.8%) were G + (MYBPC3, MYH7, ACTC1). One in five relatives (n = 13/71, 18.3%; 95% CI 11.0-28.9%) were referred, most having an abnormal ECG (12.7%). Nine relatives (12.7%; 95% CI 4.9-20.4%) exhibited early cardiomyopathy traits at baseline. One (1.4%) relative was G + /P - . Cardiomyopathy was diagnosed in 3 (4.2%, 95% CI 0.9-11.8%) relatives at baseline (n = 2 HCM, n = 1 DCM). One relative with early cardiomyopathy traits underwent phenoconversion (NDLVC) during follow-up at 77 months, yielding an overall diagnostic rate of 5.6% (95% CI 2.0-13.8%) in 4 unrelated families. A joint clinical-genetic approach enabled personalized surveillance in 6 relatives (8.5%), including 2 (2.8%) diagnoses that would otherwise have been missed with conventional clinical screening.Conclusion: One in five relatives of ECG‑positive phenotype‑negative adolescents received a cardiomyopathy diagnosis or had early cardiomyopathy traits. A joint clinical-genetic approach in this subgroup may aid early cardiomyopathy detection in selected families, though findings remain exploratory and require validation in larger cohorts. What is Known - What is New: •Resting ECG can identify individuals harboring conditions linked to sudden cardiac death •The penetrance of cardiomyopathy is age dependent, which explains why screened adolescents may exhibit abnormal ECG patterns in the absence of a cardiomyopathy diagnosis •Our data indicate that extending screening to relatives of ECG-positive, phenotype-negative adolescents is justified, with one in five relatives receiving a new cardiomyopathy diagnosis (5.6%) or exhibiting early cardiomyopathy traits (11.3%) •A joint clinical/genetic evaluation in this context may help personalize screening strategies.

title: Integrating volumes into myocardial work: the prognostic role of non-invasive pressure-strain-volume analysis in transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
authorString: Turschl TK, Ladányi Z, Ferencz A, Fábián A, Tokodi M, Szijártó Á, Ruppert M, Nagy A, Molnár AÁ, Molnár L, Zima E, Kovács A, Lakatos BK, Merkely B.
abstractText: The accurate echocardiographic assessment of the left ventricular (LV) contractile state remains challenging in aortic stenosis, as ejection fraction and even global longitudinal strain are markedly load-dependent. The novel pressure-strain loop-derived myocardial work were developed to overcome this limitation; however, incorporation of instantaneous LV volume may further improve this method. We aimed to quantify myocardial work using pressure-strain-volume (PSV) loops and to evaluate its prognostic value in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). We enrolled 300 patients scheduled for TAVI (age 78.7 ± 6.3 years, 41% female). The endpoint was all-cause mortality, reached by 62 patients over a median follow-up of 25 months. Echocardiography and non-invasive blood pressure measurements were performed one day before TAVI. LV pressure was estimated noninvasively, while strain curves were derived from speckle-tracking analysis. Pressure-strain relations were adjusted to instantaneous LV volumes to construct PSV loops, yielding volume-adjusted indices (GWIVi and GCWVi). GWIVi showed similar extent of LV dysfunction in classical and paradoxical low-flow low-gradient AS phenotypes compared to the normal flow-high gradient patients (46.98 ± 20.71 vs. 51.99 ± 18.43 vs. 63.74 ± 22.26 mmHg%L/m<sup>2</sup>, p < 0.001), while other LV function parameters did not. In multivariable Cox-regression, GWIVi was an independent predictor of mortality (Hazard ratio: 0.955 [confidence interval: 0.773-0.993], p < 0.05) alongside clinically relevant other markers such as hemoglobin and atrial fibrillation. PSV loop-derived myocardial work detected LV mechanical differences between AS phenotypes and provided independent prognostic value in TAVI candidates, potentially offering a more physiologically accurate assessment of LV function in this population.

title: Determinants of outcome in atrial functional tricuspid regurgitation.
authorString: Aldakhil J, Patel K, Badiani S, Petersen SE, Lloyd G, Bhattacharyya S.
abstractText:
Background

Atrial functional tricuspid regurgitation (AFTR) is increasingly recognized as a result of atrial remodelling in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). However, prognostic predictors in this population remain incompletely defined.

Objectives

To evaluate echocardiographic characteristics and identify predictors of all-cause mortality in patients with AFTR.

Methods

We retrospectively studied consecutive patients with AF who underwent transthoracic echocardiography between 2017 and 2025. Inclusion required significant right atrial remodelling, defined as a right atrial area > 25 cm2. Patients with at least moderate functional tricuspid regurgitation comprised the AFTR cohort, while patients with mild/trivial/no tricuspid regurgitation served as controls. Patients with primary valvular disease, cardiomyopathy, congenital heart disease, device-related valve disease, RV dilatation, or more than mild RV systolic dysfunction were excluded. Cox proportional hazards regression was performed to identify predictors of mortality.

Results

A total of 152 patients were included, comprising 120 patients with AFTR and 32 controls. Compared with controls, patients with AFTR demonstrated larger atrial dimensions, higher right-sided hemodynamic-burden, impaired RV longitudinal strain, and reduced reservoir RA strain. During a median follow-up of 6.3 years, 53 deaths (45%) occurred among patients with AFTR. In univariable Cox analysis, age (HR 1.02, 95% CI 1.00-1.04; p = 0.016), TR Vmax (HR 1.59, 95% CI 1.07-2.35; p = 0.020), and lower reservoir RA strain (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.84-0.96; p = 0.003) were associated with mortality. In multivariable analysis, reservoir RA strain remained independently associated with mortality (adjusted HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.81-0.95; p < 0.001).

Conclusion

AFTR is characterized by marked biatrial remodelling and impaired right atrial function. Reduced RA reservoir strain was independently associated with mortality, supporting a potential role for RA deformation imaging in risk stratification in AFTR.

title: Early and Late Outcomes Following Cardiac Surgery in Patients With Immune-Mediated Inflammatory Diseases.
authorString: Amano K, Takami Y, Akita K, Matsuhashi K, Niwa W, Okamoto K, Kawamoto N, Abe T.
abstractText:
Background

Immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs) are associated with increased cardiovascular risk, but surgical outcomes in the modern era of immunosuppressive therapy remain unclear. We evaluated early and late outcomes after cardiac and thoracic aortic surgery in patients with IMIDs, focusing on the impact of glucocorticoids and disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs).

Methods

A total of 140 patients with IMIDs who underwent cardiac or thoracic aortic surgery between 2008 and 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. The primary endpoints were in-hospital mortality and long-term overall survival.

Results

Median age was 70 [61-76] years, and 62% were women. Rheumatoid arthritis was the most common IMID (36%). Prednisolone and DMARDs were used in 68% and 33% of patients, respectively. Procedures included valve (43%), ischemic (26%), and thoracic aortic surgery (23%). In-hospital mortality was 4.3%. During a median follow-up of 5.9 years (93% completeness), overall survival was 91% at 1 year, 87% at 3 years, 78% at 5 years, and 62% at 10 years, respectively. Outcomes did not differ by a surgical category or IMID subtype. Glucocorticoid use was independently associated with worse late survival (HR, 2.91; 95% CI, 1.01-8.41; p = 0.048), whereas DMARD use showed a trend toward improved survival (HR 0.46; 95% CI, 0.19-1.09; p = 0.08). Notably, a dose-dependent relationship was observed, with high-dose prednisolone (≥ 5 mg/day) showing significantly worse survival compared with low-dose (< 5 mg/day) or no glucocorticoid use (p = 0.004). Diabetes mellitus and preoperative anemia were also independent predictors of late mortality.

Conclusions

Cardiac surgery in patients with IMIDs provides acceptable early outcomes but suboptimal long-term survival. Glucocorticoid use was associated with worse late survival, with a dose-dependent relationship, whereas DMARD use showed a nonsignificant trend toward better survival, underscoring the importance of optimized immunosuppressive management.

title: Diagnostic performance of aortic valve calcium and CT-derived aortic valve area in low-gradient aortic stenosis.
authorString: De Cecco D, Scoma C, Powell C, Joseph M, Truesdell W, Chetcuti S, Harris AW.
abstractText:
Background

Practice guidelines recommend the use of computed tomography (CT) aortic valve calcium (AVC) scores for patients with low-gradient aortic stenosis (LG-AS). AVC has not been studied in comparison to invasive aortic valve study (IAVS).

Objectives

To determine the diagnostic performance of AVC and CT-derived aortic valve area (CT-AVA) compared to IAVS as a reference standard.

Methods

We included consecutive patients with LG-AS with echocardiography, CT and IAVS performed within 1 year at a single tertiary center. Severe AS was defined by aortic valve area (AVA) ≤1.0 cm2 measured by IAVS. CT-AVA was retrospectively measured by a blinded reader. CT-AVA and sex-based AVC were compared to AS defined by IAVS. Diagnostic performance was compared using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. AVC and CT-AVA were compared to cardiac events consisting of death, aortic valve replacement and cardiovascular hospitalization.

Results

Out of 294 patients in the overall cohort, 206 patients with definite AS severity by IAVS were included as the primary diagnostic cohort. Severe AS according to invasive AVA (≤1.0 cm2) was present in 72 patients (35.0%). Sex-based AVC scores had relatively poor diagnostic performance compared to the reference IAVS with AUCs of 0.59 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.48-0.70) and 0.58 (95% CI 0.45-0.71) for men and women, respectively. CT-AVA had better diagnostic performance with an AUC of 0.82 (95% CI 0.77-0.87).

Conclusions

In our study population, CT-AVA had significantly better diagnostic performance than AVC compared to the reference standard, IAVS.

title: In-Hospital Mortality After Aortic Valve Replacement Surgical Versus Transcatheter: A Nationwide Study with Machine Learning-Based Risk Prediction.
authorString: Sharma A, Ubaid MJ, Shalini F, Yousaf H.
abstractText:
Introduction

Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) are two preferred methods for treating aortic stenosis. This study compared the in-hospital mortality rates associated with SAVR and TAVR.

Methods

In accordance with the STROBE guidelines, we conducted an analytical cross-sectional study utilizing data from the National Readmission Database (NRD) spanning from 2016 to 2020. Patients who underwent TAVR or SAVR were identified using specific ICD-10 procedure codes. We employed adjusted multivariate logistic regression analysis to determine the odds ratio (OR) of death associated with SAVR compared to TAVR. Patients were followed for a year and OR with 95% CI were calculated. AI based XGBoost model were used to find the predictors of mortality.

Results

Our study included a total of 361,875 patients. Among these, 182,443 underwent TAVR, while 179,432 underwent SAVR. In the TAVR group, 2,563 patients (1.4%) died during hospitalization, whereas 6,671 patients (3.7%) died in the SAVR group. The multivariate logistic regression analysis indicated that SAVR is associated with higher in-hospital mortality (OR = 2.66, 95% CI 2.51-2.81, p < 0.001) compared to TAVR. Follow up data at 30 days, three months, six months, did not find any difference in mortality between TAVR and SAVR. Notably, liver failure, HLD, renal failure, SAVR, female, CHF, and atrial fibrillation are amongst the top predictor of mortality in patients undergoing (TAVR or SAVR). While in cardiac rehospitalization, risk factors like female gender, CHF, Afib, HLD, DM have higher predictability than procedure.

Conclusion

Our study demonstrates that SAVR is associated with a higher likelihood of in-hospital mortality compared to TAVR, with organ dysfunction (liver failure, kidney dysfunction) as a predictor of mortality.

title: Treatment selection and long-term survival in patients aged 50 to < 75 years undergoing valve reintervention for failed surgical aortic bioprostheses: insights from the Netherlands Heart Registration.
authorString: Kostea A, van Niekerk J, Uchoa de Assis L, Adrichem R, Timmermans MJC, Tonino PAL, Voskuil M, de Weger A, Porta F, Kardys I, Van Mieghem NM, Nuis RJ, THI and Cardiothoracic Surgery Registration Committees of the Netherlands Heart Registration.

journal.title: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society

abstractText:
Objectives

To describe real-world treatment allocation and observed long-term survival in patients aged 50 to < 75 years with failed surgical aortic bioprostheses who underwent reintervention through valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve implantation (ViV-TAVI) or redo surgical aortic valve replacement (redo-SAVR) in the Netherlands.

Methods

Patients aged 50 to < 75 years who underwent ViV-TAVI or redo-SAVR for a failing surgical bioprosthesis between 2015 and 2020 were identified from the Netherlands Heart Registration. Baseline characteristics and Dutch surgical-risk categories were compared by treatment strategy. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with ViV-TAVI selection. Kaplan-Meier analysis described survival, and treatment-specific Cox models explored factors associated with all-cause mortality.

Results

Of 345 patients, 41% underwent ViV-TAVI and 59% redo-SAVR. Patients selected for ViV-TAVI were older (median 71 vs. 67 years, p < 0.001), had higher surgical risk (EuroSCORE II: 6.2% vs. 4.6%, p = 0.014), and had a greater comorbidity burden than redo-SAVR patients. Despite these baseline risk differences, estimated survival within the ViV-TAVI cohort was 94.2% at 30 days, 89.6% at 2 years, and 74.4% at 4 years; corresponding redo-SAVR estimates were 96.1%, 89.8%, and 88.4%. Left ventricular ejection fraction ≤ 30% and chronic lung disease were associated both with ViV-TAVI selection (OR: 8.04, 95% CI: 2.16-29.92 and OR: 3.25, 95% CI: 1.53-6.92, respectively) and with all-cause mortality after redo-SAVR (HR: 15.70, 95% CI: 2.49-67.14 and HR: 4.23, 95% CI: 1.53-13.14, respectively).

Conclusion

In this Dutch observational registry, ViV-TAVI was predominantly selected for patients with a higher-risk clinical phenotype, while redo-SAVR was more often used in lower-risk reintervention candidates and showed higher observed long-term survival. These data describe contemporary treatment selection and prognosis but do not establish comparative superiority of either strategy.

title: The Evolution of Anesthesia for Congenital Heart Disease.
authorString: Odegard KC, Zaleski KL, Nasr VG.
abstractText: This educational review describes the historical development of pediatric congenital cardiac anesthesia and its expanding role in the care of patients with congenital heart disease (CHD). Over the past eight decades, the specialty has evolved from an era in which few congenital heart defects were surgically treatable and perioperative mortality was high to one in which survival into adulthood is expected for most children with CHD. This transformation has been driven by parallel advances in surgical techniques, cardiopulmonary bypass technology, myocardial protection, monitoring, intensive care, and anesthetic management. From the first successful patent ductus arteriosus ligation in 1938 to the development of fetal cardiac interventions and the many major technological and scientific advances of the late twentieth and early twenty-first centuries, anesthesiologists have played a pivotal role in improving the care of patients with CHD. As survival has improved, the population of adults and elderly patients living with repaired or palliated CHD has grown, and the specialty's focus has expanded beyond reducing perioperative mortality to improving lifelong outcomes. Today, congenital cardiac anesthesiologists are integral members of multidisciplinary teams responsible for perioperative risk assessment, hemodynamic optimization, neuroprotection, coagulation management, mechanical circulatory support, and enhanced recovery. The history of the specialty highlights the importance of multidisciplinary collaboration and continued scientific progress in improving patient safety, recovery, and long-term outcomes.

title: Heart Transplantation in Adult Fontan Patients: New Insights from Fontan-Associated Liver Disease Beyond Traditional Predictors.
authorString: Rybicka J, Coats L, Crossland D, Patel P, Scott J, Anderson K, Hermuzi A, Adhvaryu K, Kakarla J, Erturk E, Seller N, White S, Gonzalez-Fernandez O, MacGowan G, Nassar MS, Kenny L, Jansen K.

journal.title: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation

abstractText:
Background

Fontan patients are considered high risk for heart transplantation (HT) owing to their complex anatomy, multiple prior chest entries, and universal Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD). The impact of FALD and other preoperative factors remains, however, uncertain.

Objectives

We sought to identify factors associated with 90-day mortality after isolated HT in adults with Fontan circulation, with particular focus on the relationship between liver-related parameters and post-transplant outcomes.

Methods

A retrospective cohort study of all adult Fontan patients undergoing isolated HT was conducted. Factors associated with 90-day mortality were assessed using appropriate univariate analyses and penalized multivariable logistic regression. ROC analysis was used to derive liver size cut-offs and compare the discriminative performance of selected variables. A descriptive analysis of adult Fontan patients undergoing combined heart-liver transplantation (CHLT) was also performed for contextual comparison.

Results

Thirty-seven patients (mean age 30 years) underwent isolated HT; 19% (n=8) died within 90 days. Factors associated with increased 90-day mortality were >4 previous chest entries, major perioperative bleeding, and small liver size [total liver volume (TLV) ≤1366 mL, total liver volume indexed to body surface area (TLVi) <786 mL/m2 and liver transverse dimension (LTD) <21 cm]. Multiple chest veno-venous collaterals, >4 previous chest entries, and small liver were strongly associated with bleeding and subsequent fatal complications including sepsis, graft dysfunction, and bowel ischaemia. Within the study period, five other patients had undergone CHLT. All had biopsy confirmed advanced liver disease with features of clinically significant portal hypertension or hepatocellular carcinoma. One patient died within 90 days following prolonged cardiopulmonary bypass, major bleeding, graft dysfunction and sepsis, culminating in multiorgan failure.

Conclusions

In Fontan patients undergoing isolated HT, >4 previous chest entries, major bleeding, and small liver volume were associated with increased 90-day mortality. Objective liver metrics (TLV ≤1366 mL, TLVi <786 mL/m2, TLD <21 cm) may provide adjunctive risk stratification for Fontan patients considered for isolated HT; however, these measures and proposed thresholds remain exploratory and require external validation. CHLT is a viable option, although non-liver related transplant risk factors may similarly influence outcomes. Detailed liver assessment and management at experienced, high-volume congenital transplant centres are important to optimizing outcomes in this complex population.

title: A multifunctional bishydroxycoumarin conjugate exhibiting AIE characteristics and tandem Co<sup>2+</sup>/ATP detection with logic gate operations, on-site sensing and bioimaging applications.
authorString: Kishore Kumar R, Manoharan S, Perumal E, Murugesapandian B.
abstractText: An efficient coumarin-based fluorescent probe, HCPD, was synthesized via condensation of 7-diethylamino-4-hydroxycoumarin aldehyde with o-phenylenediamine. The structure of the probe was confirmed by FT-IR, NMR and HRMS studies. The probe, HCPD exhibited aggregation-induced emission (AIE) characteristics in a THF-water mixture, showing enhanced emission at 80% water fraction. The probe functions as a molecular switch for the sensitive detection of the environmentally and biologically significant metal ion Co2+ at the nanomolar level. HCPD emits green emission at 500 nm which selectively detects Co2+ ions in a DMF/Tris-HCl buffer system (9 : 1, v/v) through an emission "turn-off" response, attributed to paramagnetic quenching. In addition, Job's plot and HRMS analysis established a 1 : 1 binding stoichiometry between HCPD and Co2+ ions. The probe demonstrated remarkable sensitivity with a low detection limit of 11.7 nM and a binding constant of 3.6798 × 104 M-1. Notably, the emission of the HCPD-Co2+ ensemble was restored upon the addition of ATP over various competing anions, enabling reversible sensing behavior not previously reported in the reversibility of Co2+ ions. The regeneration capability of the probe facilitated practical on-site applications, including paper strips, cotton swabs and the construction of an IMPLICATION logic gate circuit. Furthermore, HCPD was also successfully applied in bio-imaging studies of MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cell lines, highlighting its biological relevance. Overall, HCPD represents a highly sensitive and reversible dual-responsive fluorescent probe for Co2+ and ATP detection with significant environmental and biological applications.

title: Ipsilateral Versus Contralateral Femoral Access for Inferior Epigastric Artery Embolization: Impact of Patient Age on Procedural Efficiency.
authorString: Carrubba C, Punzi E, D Antuono F, Giurazza F, Corvino F, Pane F, Brignola N, Lombardi G, Niola R.
abstractText:
Purpose

Abdominal wall hematomas (AWHs) are relatively uncommon causes of acute abdominal pain but may represent potentially life-threatening vascular emergencies, particularly in elderly patients receiving anticoagulant therapy or in the setting of significant hemorrhage. Transcatheter arterial embolization of the inferior epigastric artery is the recommended first-line therapy. The contralateral femoral approach may be technically demanding in elderly patients with iliac tortuosity, calcifications, or diffuse atherosclerosis. This bicentric retrospective study compared ipsilateral versus contralateral femoral access for inferior epigastric artery embolization, evaluating procedural efficiency, radiation exposure, and clinical outcomes.

Material and methods

A bicentric retrospective study included 48 patients treated in emergency settings for epigastric artery bleeding between June 2022 and June 2025. Patients were divided into ipsilateral (n = 23) or contralateral (n = 25) femoral access groups, with further stratification by age (< 60 vs. ≥ 60 years). Technical and clinical success, total angiographic procedure duration, fluoroscopic dose (Air Kerma, mGy), access-site complications, transfusion requirements, rebleeding, and 30-day/3-month survival were analyzed. A subgroup analysis in patients ≥ 60 years (n = 33) assessed the impact of vascular anatomy on procedural metrics.

Results

Technical success was 100% in both groups, whereas clinical success was comparable between the contralateral and ipsilateral groups (96.00% vs. 95.65%, respectively). In patients ≥ 60 years, ipsilateral access significantly reduced procedure time (27.90 ± 6.40 vs. 33.30 ± 8.30 min, p = 0.046) and radiation dose (254.00 [IQR 219.00-272.00] vs. 283.50 [IQR 248.80-310.80] mGy, p = 0.023). No major complications or significant between-group differences in rebleeding or survival were observed. In exploratory multivariable analysis, ipsilateral access was associated with lower Air Kerma (β = -56.43 mGy; 95% CI, -91.91 to -20.95; p = 0.002), whereas the adjusted estimate for procedure duration was less precise and did not reach statistical significance.

Conclusions

Both femoral access routes are safe and effective. In patients aged ≥ 60 years, ipsilateral access was associated with shorter procedure duration and lower radiation exposure in unadjusted analyses. Exploratory adjusted analyses suggested an association between ipsilateral access and lower radiation exposure, whereas the adjusted association with procedure duration was not statistically significant. These findings require confirmation in larger prospective cohorts.

title: Hemodynamic and Geometrical Parameters Associated with Carotid Artery Stenosis: A Cross-Sectional Study Using 4D Flow MRI and CFD.
authorString: Mokhtari A, Bergmann A, Strecker C, Andrae J, Harloff A, Obrist D.
abstractText:
Purpose

Carotid geometry and local hemodynamics are closely associated with atherosclerosis, yet how anatomy and disturbed flow jointly mark disease presence and relate to pro-atherogenic flow in still-non-stenosed bifurcations remains unresolved. This study quantifies the cross-sectional association between three-dimensional carotid bifurcation geometry and pro-atherogenic flow and identifies anatomical biomarkers for non-invasive risk stratification.

Methods

Geometric analyses included 346 carotid bifurcations, comprising 240 stenosed and 106 non-stenosed bifurcations. Patient-specific CFD was performed in 176 bifurcations: 101 stenosed and 75 non-stenosed. Eight geometric descriptors, including a new offset flow divider capturing bifurcation apex asymmetry, and four ICA bulb hemodynamic indices (TAWSS, OSI, RRT, BFI) were extracted; logistic and linear regression assessed the association of geometry with (i) stenosis presence and (ii) pro-atherogenic flow.

Results

Bifurcation angle, ICA angle, tortuosity, and offset flow divider were significantly elevated in stenosed bifurcations (all p<0.001 ); a four-feature geometric model showed moderate discrimination between stenosed and non-stenosed bifurcations (cross-validated AUROC=0.767 ). The post-stenotic expansion ratio was more strongly associated with local flow disturbance than the degree of luminal narrowing. In non-stenosed bifurcations, multivariable geometric models explained 49 to 60% of the variance in the flow-normalized low-TAWSS, elevated-OSI, and elevated-RRT outcomes, with bulb area and area ratio providing the largest independent contributions, indicating that geometric variation is strongly associated with candidate pro-atherogenic flow patterns even in the absence of detectable luminal narrowing.

Conclusions

Carotid geometry carries two complementary signals: markers of disease presence (bifurcation angle, ICA angle) and candidate anatomical substrates of pro-atherogenic flow in still-non-stenosed bifurcations (bulb area, area ratio). Together with the post-stenotic expansion ratio, these geometric features define a compact, image-derivable set of candidate biomarkers for future early carotid risk stratification.

title: The evolving role of cardiac CT: Emerging technologies and clinical impact.
authorString: Oda S, Iima M, Yanagawa M, Saida T, Ide S, Takumi K, Ito R, Kurokawa R, Honda M, Nishioka K, Sakata A, Sofue K, Ueda D, Sugawara S, Watabe T, Kawamura M, Hirata K, Naganawa S.
abstractText: Cardiac computed tomography (CT) has progressed from a non-invasive test primarily used to exclude obstructive coronary artery disease into a comprehensive cardiovascular imaging platform for coronary artery disease, myocardial disease, valvular heart disease, and structural heart disease. Coronary CT angiography (CCTA) is now endorsed as a first-line test in appropriately selected patients with stable chest pain or suspected chronic coronary syndromes because it can exclude obstructive disease, depict coronary atherosclerotic burden, support preventive treatment, and inform referral for invasive coronary angiography. At the same time, contemporary cardiac CT is moving beyond luminal stenosis. CT-derived fractional flow reserve and myocardial CT perfusion add a functional assessment of ischemia, whereas late iodine enhancement, CT-derived extracellular volume fraction, myocardial strain, and pericoronary fat attenuation index provide information on fibrosis, ventricular mechanics, vascular inflammation, and prognosis. Cardiac CT also has an established role in transcatheter valve therapy, left atrial appendage occlusion, and prosthetic valve assessment by providing a three-dimensional roadmap for device selection, access planning, and complication prediction. Photon-counting detector CT and artificial intelligence are further expanding the capabilities of cardiac CT through higher spatial resolution, spectral quantification, automated segmentation, quantitative plaque analysis, image reconstruction, and structured reporting. This review summarizes the evidence, technical foundations, clinical applications, and implementation challenges of contemporary cardiac CT, with an emphasis on its transition toward a decision-making platform for personalized cardiovascular care.

title: Paradoxical attenuation of dyslipidemia and atherosclerosis in Apoe<sup>-/-</sup>Mpst<sup>-/-</sup> mice.
authorString: Zampas P, Markou M, Bertos N, Ravani S, Papapetropoulos A.
abstractText: Hydrogen sulfide (H<sub>2</sub>S) is a signaling molecule that affects multiple (patho)physiological pathways. Deficiency of H<sub>2</sub>S due to cystathionine γ-lyase (CSE) deletion has been proven to accelerate atherosclerotic plaque formation. However, the role of 3-mercaptopyruvate sulfurtransferase (MPST), a related H<sub>2</sub>S-producing enzyme that impacts metabolism, has not been studied in atherogenic dyslipidemia. We generated a double Apoe/Mpst knockout mouse (Apoe<sup>-/-</sup>Mpst<sup>-/-</sup>) in the C57BL/6 background. C57Bl/6, Mpst<sup>-/-</sup>, Apoe<sup>-/-</sup> and Apoe<sup>-/-</sup>Mpst<sup>-/-</sup>mice were fed a western diet for 14 weeks, after which blood and tissues (aorta and liver) were collected; the circulating lipid profile, atherosclerotic plaque formation and expression of enzymes involved in lipid biosynthetic pathways in the liver were evaluated in the four mouse lines. H<sub>2</sub>S production was reduced in the liver of double knockout mice, while the expression of CBS and CSE was not altered. In the serum of Apoe<sup>-/-</sup>Mpst<sup>-/-</sup>, we observed decreased levels of total cholesterol, low-density lipoproteins (LDL) and triglycerides (TGs) compared to Apoe<sup>-/-</sup>; hepatic apolipoprotein B (ApoB) levels were also downregulated. However, the expression of other key enzymes that participate in cholesterol and fatty acid synthesis remained unchanged. In addition, hepatic lipid deposition was not significantly altered among genotypes. In line with the reduced circulating LDL and TGs levels, atherosclerotic lesions were found to be reduced in the aorta of Apoe<sup>-/-</sup>Mpst<sup>-/-</sup>. Our results indicate that MPST deletion in the Apoe<sup>-/-</sup> dyslipidemia model leads to decreased circulating lipid levels and atherosclerosis, that correlate with a downregulation of hepatic ApoB expression.

title: Radiation Vasculopathy of the Coronary Arteries: State-of-the Art Review.
authorString: Xia J, Kim J, Sharma A, Yang B, Alluri PG, Atkins K, Miller ED, Williams TM, Addison D, Arbune A, Chandra A, Koutroumpakis E, Zhang KW, Zaha VG.
abstractText: Radiation-associated coronary artery disease (RACAD) is a distinct form of coronary artery disease with several specific biological and clinical aspects as well as key knowledge gaps. RACAD is prevalent in patients with cardiac exposure to radiotherapy. As radiotherapy is integral to the effective treatment of many thoracic malignancies, improved long-term survivorship is coupled with increased risk for RACAD. Ionizing radiation induces free radical generation and activation of proinflammatory cascades, leading to endothelial dysfunction and accelerated atherosclerosis. Risks for RACAD are determined both by radiotherapy, including the radiation dose and the proximity of coronary arteries to the radiotherapy field, and by patient-specific factors, such as younger age, higher baseline cardiovascular risk, and concurrent cardiotoxic systemic therapies. Importantly, radiotherapy delivery is highly individualized on the basis of tumor location and treatment strategy, resulting in heterogeneous coronary exposure to radiation and patient-to-patient variability. Clinical presentation may occur early, within 1 to 2 years, especially in patients with higher cardiac radiation doses (eg, lung or esophageal cancer), or after a latency period of 5 to 20 years with lower cardiac dose radiation exposure (eg, left-sided breast cancer). Patients generally present with symptoms similar to conventional coronary artery disease. However, RACAD symptoms may be underrecognized in cancer survivors due to overlapping treatment-related fatigue, pulmonary disease, or competing oncologic symptoms. Diagnosis and management generally follow standard coronary artery disease guidelines while incorporating cancer-specific considerations, such as planned oncologic surgeries, bleeding risk, postradiotherapy complications such as atretic internal mammary arteries, and cardiotoxic effects of systemic cancer therapies. Primary prevention of RACAD is critical, emphasizing advances in precision radiotherapy, including delivery techniques with improved coronary dosimetry, and cardiac shielding. Key knowledge gaps include understanding long-term outcomes with contemporary 3-dimensional conformal radiotherapy techniques, validated cancer-specific risk prediction models on the basis of coronary dosimetry, optimal surveillance protocols, targeted molecular pharmacotherapies, and risk analysis of percutaneous versus surgical management of RACAD. Prospective studies are needed to develop cancer- and dosimetry-specific risk calculators, validating cardioprotective interventions, and improving multidisciplinary cardio-oncology collaboration to optimize early detection of RACAD and timely intervention in the growing population of cancer survivors.

title: Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation in Dextrocardia: Lessons From a Complex Redo Case.
authorString: Fu J, Gu Z, Li J, Shuang D, Sun B, Yimingjiang Y, Chen L.

journal.title: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)

abstractText: Dextrocardia with situs solitus poses significant surgical challenges for left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation, particularly in patients with prior sternotomy and complex valvular disease. We report on a 60 year old man with dextrocardia, advanced heart failure, prior mechanical mitral valve replacement, and bicuspid aortic valve disease who underwent successful Corheart 6 LVAD implantation during redo sternotomy with concomitant bioprosthetic aortic and mitral valve replacement. Intraoperative findings included extensive pannus/thrombus on the mechanical mitral prosthesis (causing relative stenosis) and an unsuspected 10 g left atrial thrombus, both of which were removed. Total cardiopulmonary bypass time was 330 minutes, and aortic cross‑clamp time was 233 minutes. Postoperative acute kidney injury requiring dialysis resolved, and the patient was discharged after 137 days. At 1 year follow-up, the left ventricular end-diastolic diameter decreased from 69 to 66 mm, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) remained stable (28-25%), New York Heart Association (NYHA) class improved from IIIb‑IV to II, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) recovered from 32 ml/min at 9 months to 51 ml/min at 1 year.

title: A Common CD36 Variant and the Genetic Landscape of Dilated Cardiomyopathy in Individuals of African Ancestry.
authorString: Challa SP, Biddinger KJ, Abramowitz SA, Zheng A, Mead JO, Judy RL, Jurgens SJ, Gaziano L, Wang X, Choi SH, Halford J, Jordan E, Liu J, Chang KM, Vest A, Tang WHW, Tsao PS, Kinnamon DD, Damrauer SM, Ellinor PT, Levin M, Hershberger RE, Huffman JE, Aragam KG.
abstractText:
Importance

Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a major cause of heart failure that disproportionately affects individuals of predominantly African ancestry, among whom familial clustering of disease is more pronounced relative to those of predominantly European ancestry. Truncating variants in TTN, which encodes the sarcomeric protein titin, are the most common established monogenic cause of DCM. A common CD36 nonsense variant enriched among individuals of African ancestry has also been shown to account for a substantial burden of DCM.

Objective

To compare the contribution of a CD36 nonsense variant to DCM risk with that of truncating variants in TTN and pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in other established genes for DCM.

Design, setting, and participants

Multicohort genetic association study including participants of African and European ancestry with exome or genome sequence data and DCM case status from the following 4 US datasets: All of Us Research Program (recruitment: 2017-present; last follow-up: August 27, 2024), Million Veteran Program (recruitment: 2011-present; last follow-up: September 30, 2024), Penn Medicine Biobank (recruitment: 2013-present; last follow-up: November 14, 2022), and the DCM Precision Medicine Study (recruitment: 2016-2020; last follow-up: March 15, 2020).

Exposure

Carrier status for TTN truncating variants, pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in 11 high-confidence genes for DCM, and the nonsense variant CD36 Y325* (0, 1, or 2 copies).

Main outcomes and measures

Risk of DCM, prevalence of variant carriers among DCM cases, and population attributable fraction of DCM.

Results

Among 82 623 individuals of predominantly African ancestry across 4 cohorts, the mean age was 53.4 years (SD, 13.9 years), 47 124 were male, and 1316 had DCM. Individuals who were homozygous for the CD36 Y325* risk allele had a higher risk of DCM (odds ratio [OR], 4.8; 95% CI, 3.1-7.3) as did those who were heterozygous (OR, 1.4; 95% CI, 1.2-1.7). TTN truncating variants also conferred an elevated risk of DCM in participants of African ancestry (OR, 8.5; 95% CI, 5.5-13.0). Among 1316 individuals of African ancestry classified as DCM cases, 33 (2.5%) were homozygous for CD36, 56 (4.3%) had TTN truncating variants, and 16 (1.2%) had pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in other high-confidence genes for DCM. In population-level analyses incorporating both heterozygous and homozygous CD36 Y325* carriers, the population attributable fraction for CD36 (9.0% [6.2% for heterozygous carriers and 2.8% for homozygous carriers]) surpassed the population attributable fraction for TTN truncating variants (3.7%).

Conclusions and relevance

In 4 US cohorts, an ancestry-specific CD36 variant contributed more to DCM burden among individuals of African ancestry than established genes for DCM, including TTN truncating variants that are typically considered the most common genetic cause. These findings reshape the known genetic architecture of DCM in individuals of African ancestry and highlight the importance of representation in genomic research.

title: Associations of cumulative exposure and dynamic trajectories of the combined atherogenic-frailty index with incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity: a prospective cohort study.
authorString: Wu H, Song Z, Ye T, Yang C.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) poses a growing global health burden, yet effective tools for early risk stratification remain limited. The combined impact of atherogenic dyslipidaemia and physiological frailty, captured by the atherogenic index of plasma-frailty index (AIP-FI), on CMM development is poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the associations of cumulative exposure and longitudinal trajectories of AIP-FI with incident CMM.

Methods

This prospective cohort study included 4,157 participants aged ≥45 years without baseline CMM from CHARLS. The AIP-FI was constructed as the product of AIP and a 37-deficit frailty index. Cumulative AIP-FI was calculated from repeated measurements. Longitudinal trajectories were identified using K-means clustering. Associations with incident CMM were evaluated by multivariable Cox models, RCS, K-M curves, ROC/NRI/IDI, mediation, interaction, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses.

Results

Over a mean 8.5-year follow-up, 612 incident CMM cases occurred. Both higher baseline and cumulative AIP-FI were significantly associated with increased CMM risk, with cumulative exposure showing a stronger effect (fully-adjusted HR per SD increment: 1.46; 95% CI = 1.38-1.54). Participants in the highest quartile of cumulative AIP-FI had a near 4-fold higher CMM risk compared to the lowest (HR = 3.95; 95% CI = 2.95-5.29). Clustering analyses revealed that groups with high-stable AIP-FI exhibited the highest CMM risks. Cumulative AIP-FI demonstrated superior predictive performance for CMM (AUC = 71.17%) and significantly improved risk reclassification over traditional markers (NRI = 0.157). Mediation analyses suggested bidirectional synergistic effects between AIP and FI.

Conclusions

In this national cohort, both the cumulative burden and adverse longitudinal trajectories of AIP-FI were independently associated with an elevated risk of CMM. Dynamic monitoring of this composite biomarker could facilitate the early identification of high-risk individuals, thereby informing targeted prevention strategies for middle-aged and older adults in China.

title: Partial heart transplantation in resource-limited settings: challenges and feasibility.
authorString: Lee DS, Rajab TK.
abstractText:
Introduction

Partial heart transplantation provides living, growth-capable valve implants for paediatric recipients. The feasibility and challenges of implementing partial heart transplantation in resource-limited settings are evaluated, where the burden of valvular heart disease is greatest and paediatric valve replacement options remain severely limited.

Methods

A comprehensive search was conducted examining partial heart transplantation clinical outcomes, organ procurement logistics, immunosuppression requirements, and the infrastructure landscape for cardiac surgery in low-and middle-income countries. A feasibility framework was developed by mapping partial heart transplantation-specific requirements against existing low-and middle-income country cardiac surgical capacity.

Results

Compared to orthotopic heart transplantation, several features of partial heart transplantation are inherently favourable for low-and middle-income country adaptation: it allows for longer graft ischaemia times, requires only tacrolimus monotherapy, and can source valves from hearts unsuitable for orthotopic heart transplantation. However, significant barriers persist, including limited organ procurement infrastructure, absence of regulatory frameworks for equitable donor-recipient matching, restricted access to therapeutic drug monitoring, and high rates of loss to follow-up.

Conclusions

Implementation of partial heart transplantation in resource-limited settings is feasible at established middle-income country cardiac surgery centres with transplant capability. A phased strategy leveraging international partnerships, existing infrastructure, and generic immunosuppression offers a realistic pathway to bringing this innovation to the children who need it most.

title: Swallowed dental prosthesis causing late oesophageal obstruction and tracheo-oesophageal fistula in a young patient.
authorString: Prasanna H, Boyle D, Bowrey D.
abstractText: A 25-year-old man presented to the emergency department after a rugby accident having swallowed a dental plate. Initial assessment at the time of ingestion, including a chest radiograph, was unremarkable and the plate was presumed to have been expectorated. Five years later he presented with progressive dysphagia, recurrent food bolus obstruction, and haemoptysis. Computed tomography of the thorax performed 5 years later revealed circumferential oesophageal thickening and a large inflammatory mass around a retained radio-opaque foreign body at the level of the carina, with an associated tracheo-oesophageal fistula. Endoscopy confirmed near-complete obstruction of the oesophagus. He underwent a right thoracotomy with oesophagectomy, removal of the retained dental prosthesis and repair of the fistula. He made a slow but steady recovery and has required anastomotic dilatation for a stricture. This case highlights the risk of complications from retained oesophageal foreign bodies and the limitations of plain radiography in detecting non-radio-opaque dental plates.

title: Non-traumatic acute mediastinitis secondary to acute phlegmonous esophagitis: a rare case report.
authorString: Biza MH, Degife EK, Tadesse SZ, Mengistie CT, Atsbha EM, Mengistie BT.
abstractText: Acute mediastinitis secondary to acute phlegmonous esophagitis (APE) is an exceptionally rare, life-threatening condition with high morbidity. We report a 75-year-old diabetic female with recent severe pneumonia who presented with pleuritic chest pain, dyspnea, and elevated inflammatory markers. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography excluded embolism but revealed diffuse long-segment esophageal wall thickening with mediastinal fat stranding, aortic encasement, and pleural effusion, features consistent with APE and secondary non-traumatic mediastinitis without overt perforation. Given clinical stability, endoscopy was deferred to avoid disrupting a possible contained micro-perforation. The patient was successfully managed with 14 days of empiric broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics (vancomycin, cefepime, metronidazole), achieving complete clinical and radiographic resolution. This case underscores that in hemodynamically stable patients without free perforation or large abscess, conservative antimicrobial therapy can be definitive. It also highlights the importance of considering APE in non-surgical patients presenting with acute chest pain.

title: Activated B cells steer fibroblasts towards a proinflammatory phenotype in giant cell arteritis.
authorString: Xu S, Jiemy WF, Inrueangsri N, Ko Y, Abdulahad WH, Verschoor E, van Sleen Y, Graver JC, van der Geest KSM, Verstappen GM, Brouwer E, Heeringa P, Boots AMH, Sandovici M.
abstractText:
Objectives

Giant cell arteritis (GCA) is characterized by chronic large-vessel inflammation and remodelling. Within affected arteries, especially in aorta, organized B cell clusters are mainly localized in adventitia, where fibroblasts represent the dominant stromal population. This study aims to investigate fibroblast heterogeneity within these clusters and B cell-fibroblast interactions in vitro as possible contributors to disease chronicity in GCA.

Methods

Fibroblast phenotypes in CD20+B cell clusters in GCA and atherosclerotic aortic tissues were characterized using immunohistochemistry for fibroblast markers (CD90, PDPN, FAP, CD248, α-SMA) and cytokine expression (IL-6, GM-CSF, BAFF). In vitro, peripheral blood B cells from treatment-naïve GCA patients and healthy donors were stimulated and cocultured with human aortic adventitial fibroblasts (HAoAFs) using either direct cell coculture or transwell systems. To identify relevant molecular pathways for B cell-fibroblast interaction, HAoAFs were pre-treated with infliximab, tocilizumab, baricitinib or upadacitinib, followed by exposure to activated B cell conditioned medium (aBCCM). Protein secretion was assessed by ELISA, Luminex and Olink, mRNA expression was determined by qPCR.

Results

CD90+PDPN+immunofibroblasts mainly localized centrally, whereas CD90+FAP+ and CD90+CD248+fibroblasts mostly located at the border of the clusters. Fibroblasts in/around clusters co-expressed IL-6, GM-CSF, and BAFF. In vitro, HAoAFs cocultured with activated B cells or supernatants thereof upregulated IL-6, GM-CSF, PDPN, and FAP mRNA, and actively secreted IL-6, GM-CSF and BAFF, while type I collagen expression was suppressed. JAK-STAT inhibition abrogated these pro-inflammatory effects, whereas TNF-α and IL-6 receptor blockade did not.

Conclusion

Activated B cells drive fibroblasts toward a pro-inflammatory phenotype, potentially sustaining chronic inflammation and disease progression in GCA. JAK-STAT signalling appears central to this effect, highlighting its therapeutic potency at the vascular level in GCA.

title: Absent Septum Pellucidum Without Polymicrogyria or Seizures in TCP1-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder.
authorString: Biton D, Dutta D, Garg R.

journal.title: American journal of medical genetics. Part A

abstractText: T-complex protein 1 (TCP1) encodes the TCP1α subunit, one of eight subunits of the chaperonin containing TCP1 ring complex (TRiC). Heterozygous TCP1 variants cause autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by developmental delay or intellectual disability, seizures, pyramidal or cerebellar signs, and brain malformations, particularly polymicrogyria. However, the reported clinical spectrum remains limited. We report a 4-year-old girl with global developmental delay, speech and motor delay, behavioral dysregulation, microcephaly, hypotonia with core weakness, and a previously unreported heterozygous likely pathogenic TCP1 variant, c.1392delT (p.A465Qfs*3). This frameshift variant is located in exon 11, truncates the final 16.5% of the protein, is predicted to undergo nonsense-mediated decay, and is absent from gnomAD. Biological parental testing was unavailable, precluding determination of variant inheritance. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated an absent septum pellucidum with mild bilateral frontal sulcation/gyration asymmetry without polymicrogyria; the optic nerves and pituitary were normal. No seizures were documented through age 4 years. Additional findings included bicuspid aortic valve with mild aortic insufficiency, asthma, severe eczema/atopy, and multiple food allergies. This case suggests that the molecular and neuroimaging spectrum of TCP1-related neurodevelopmental disorder may be broader than previously recognized; however, a causal association between TCP1 and absent septum pellucidum cannot be established from a single case. The relationship of the cardiac and atopic findings to TCP1 remains uncertain. Additional cases and functional studies are needed to clarify genotype-phenotype relationships.

title: Computed Tomography-Derived Abdominal Aortic Calcification Independently Predicts Survival in Rectal Cancer Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Rouse M, Hadi A, Kaleem Y, Besson A, Reid F, Yeung JM.
abstractText:
Background

Contemporary rectal cancer treatment pathways remain predominantly guided by tumour-related characteristics, including stage and histopathology, with comparatively limited objective assessment of physiological reserve for treatment planning. Aortic calcification represents a potential imaging biomarker reflecting systemic vascular disease, chronic inflammation and physiological reserve. We evaluated computed tomography (CT)-derived abdominal aortic calcification as a prognostic imaging biomarker for postoperative outcomes and long-term survival.

Methods

A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the prospectively maintained Australian Comprehensive Cancer Outcomes and Research Database (ACCORD) of rectal cancer patients treated between 2013 and 2022. Pre-treatment staging CT was subjected to semi-automated volumetric quantification of calcium using 3D Slicer software. Calcification volume was assessed segmentally at vertebral levels L1-L4 and at the iliac vessels. Primary outcomes were major postoperative complications (Clavien-Dindo ≥ III) and overall survival. Cox proportional hazards modelling was performed using a prespecified parsimonious multivariable model.

Results

A total of 174 patients were included in the analysis. Increasing calcification burden demonstrated no statistically significant association with major postoperative complications (OR 1.09 per 1000-unit increase; 95% CI 0.99-1.19; p = 0.07). Increasing calcification independently predicted worse 5-year survival after multivariable adjustment (HR 1.17 per 1000-unit increase ([CI 1.08-1.28, p = 0.001]). Kaplan-Meier analyses showed separation between calcification groups, although dichotomised analyses did not reach statistical significance.

Conclusion

Aortic calcification independently predicts long-term survival following rectal cancer surgery but not short-term postoperative complications. Quantitative CT-derived calcification assessment may provide a rapid, objective imaging biomarker that reflects physiological reserve and represents a potential adjunct to future risk stratification pathways.

title: Kommerell diverticulum in right aortic arch with aberrant left subclavian artery: Routine resection or selective management?
authorString: Alsoufi B.
abstractText: Right aortic arch with aberrant left subclavian artery (RAA-ALSA) is one of the most common complete vascular rings encountered in pediatric cardiovascular practice. The associated Kommerell diverticulum (KD), a remnant of the primitive fourth dorsal aortic arch from which the aberrant subclavian artery arises, forms part of the posterior ring and may contribute importantly to persistent airway and esophageal compression. Historically, repair consisted of division of the ligamentum arteriosum. Recognition that posterior compression can persist after ligamentum division has led many surgeons to add diverticulum resection and transfer or reimplantation of the aberrant subclavian artery. The optimal strategy remains controversial. Advocates of routine KD resection cite persistent compression after simple ring division, the low morbidity of resection in experienced centers, and abnormal diverticular histopathology that may imply future aneurysmal risk. Opponents emphasize that most children do well after less extensive repair that persistent symptoms frequently reflect associated airway disease rather than residual vascular compression, and that evidence proving superiority of universal resection is lacking. This review summarizes the embryology, anatomy, pathophysiology, and surgical management of KD in RAA-ALSA; critically examines evidence for routine and selective resection; and proposes a practical anatomy-driven approach.

title: Spatial multi-omics implicates vascular adipocytes proximal to tertiary lymphoid structures in human aortic aneurysm and B-cell autoreactivity.
authorString: Meher AK, Huang W, Yamaguchi DJ, Yin C, Swyers MM, Dubis G, Yang LV, Mannie MD, McNamara CA.
abstractText:
Objective:

Perivascular Adipose Tissue (PVAT), tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS), and the B lymphocytes they harbor have been implicated in regulating vascular diseases, including abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). Yet, the relationship of adipose tissue to TLS and B-cell responses is poorly understood. Approach and Results: Here, using multi-omics approaches, we characterized the potential interplay of vascular adipocytes and TLSs in shaping microenvironments conducive to pathogenic B-cell immunity in human AAA pathology. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing identified white adipocytes expressing transcripts for lipogenesis, lipolysis, and extracellular remodeling. Unexpectedly, these adipocytes expressed haptotactic and chemotactic factors such as thrombospondin 1 and autotaxin, and extracellular matrix proteins with potential to recruit CD44+ leukocytes within AAAs. Immunohistology revealed two anatomical compartments for the adipocytes within AAAs: PVAT and the medial-adventitial region. Medial-adventitial adipocytes were frequently associated with CD44+ TLSs and were largely absent from control non-aneurysmal abdominal aortas. Visium HD spatial transcriptomics revealed mature TLSs recapitulated the organization of functional secondary lymphoid structures, with multiple B-cell follicles clustered to form a nodular structure partly covered by a layer of smooth muscle cells. The TLSs harbored isotype-switched B cells expressing IgG1, IgG3, or IgA, with dominant kappa chain usage and IgG antibodies to the aortic wall. Myeloid cells in AAA were implicated in promoting B-cell effects, as they were the primary producers of B-cell activating factor (BAFF), a cytokine that promotes B-cell infiltration, survival, and function.

Conclusion:

Altogether, our results support a model in which new adipocytes in the medial-adventitial layer elicit inflammatory pathways that promote early TLS formation, and BAFF produced by myeloid cells promotes the survival and maturation of vascular wall-antigen-exposed B cells, leading to mature TLS formation, production of antibodies to AAA antigens, fueling inflammation and AAA growth.

title: Volumetric Analysis versus Diameter Measurement for Early Detection of Post-EVAR Sac Progression.
authorString: Özçelik S, Külahcıoğlu E, Türkcü MA, Gül EB, Gevrek M, Şenel E, Erkal E, Işcan HZ.
abstractText: ObjectiveTo compare diameter- and volume-based surveillance after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) and determine whether volumetric sac assessment identifies postoperative remodeling not captured by conventional maximum diameter measurement.MethodsThis retrospective single-center study included 383 patients who underwent elective EVAR for infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm between January 2016 and April 2024. All patients had preoperative and postoperative computed tomography angiography and at least 1 year of follow-up. Maximum sac diameter, total aneurysm sac volume, thrombus volume, thrombus density, neck morphology, and other anatomical variables were assessed using standardized morphometric and three-dimensional morphovolumetric measurements. Sac dynamics were classified by diameter criteria (≥5 mm decrease, stable, or ≥5 mm increase) and volumetric criteria (>10% decrease, stable, or >10% increase).ResultsEndoleaks occurred in 26.1% of patients (n = 100), and secondary interventions were required in 14.1% (n = 54), with a mean time to reintervention of 21.7 ± 10 months. At final follow-up, 74.7% demonstrated sac diameter reduction, 18.5% were stable, and 6.8% had enlargement, whereas volumetric analysis showed shrinkage in 81.7%, stability in 6.0%, and enlargement in 12.3%. At 1, 6, and 12 months, cohort mean diameter changed by -0.6%, -3.1%, and -6.5% from baseline, respectively, while cohort mean volume changed by -0.5%, -5.7%, and -12.5%. Among diameter-stable sacs, 32.4% enlarged volumetrically and 38.0% regressed volumetrically. In enlarging sacs, a 10% volume increase corresponded to an approximately 4 mm diameter increase (R2 = 0.72; P < 0.001); this 4 mm value was a regression estimate, not the diameter threshold used for sac classification. Preoperative morphometric and morphovolumetric variables were associated with endoleak and secondary intervention in exploratory analyses.ConclusionVolumetric sac analysis identified additional postoperative remodeling beyond maximum diameter measurement, particularly in apparently stable sacs. A practical surveillance strategy combining rapid diameter-based screening with selective volumetric analysis in stable, borderline, or clinically suspicious cases may improve recognition of adverse sac behavior without requiring routine volumetry in every follow-up study.

title: Comprehensive cardiac, vascular, and pulmonary characterization of a cardiometabolic HFpEF model.
authorString: Aykac I, Baumgartner CA, Hamza O, Kiss A, Podesser BK.
abstractText:
Background

Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous syndrome in which translational progress is limited by experimental models that insufficiently reflect the cardiometabolic phenotype while affecting endogenous endothelial function. We aimed to characterize a cardiometabolic "two-hit" HFpEF model combining metabolic stress (db/db) with chronic mineralocorticoid excess (d-aldosterone), focusing on integrated cardiac, vascular, and pulmonary phenotyping.

Methods

Female db/db mice received 4-week d-aldosterone (0.3 µg/h) or vehicle via osmotic minipumps. Metabolic profiling, high-resolution echocardiography including strain and left atrial mechanics, invasive right-heart catheterization, and thoracic aortic wire myography were performed.

Results

Aldosterone-treated db/db mice developed cardiac hypertrophy and pulmonary congestion with preserved LVEF but marked diastolic dysfunction, left atrial remodeling with increased stiffness, and impaired global longitudinal LV strain. Pulmonary hypertension with right ventricular dysfunction was evidenced by elevated RVSP/estimated mPAP, reduced PAT/PET, and reduced TAPSE. Thoracic aortae from untreated db/db mice already showed impaired endothelium-dependent relaxation, which was further aggravated by aldosterone, whereas maximal endothelium-independent relaxation remained largely preserved.

Conclusions

The db/db+d-aldosterone model recapitulates key features of cardiometabolic HFpEF across the cardiac-vascular-pulmonary axis and provides a translational platform for mechanistic and therapeutic studies targeting endothelial and ventricular-vascular dysfunction in HFpEF. New & Noteworthy: Current HFpEF animal models often limit the investigation of vascular dysfunction, a central component of cardiometabolic HFpEF. We provide a comprehensive functional characterization of a db/db+d-aldosterone two-hit model demonstrating obesity, diabetes, diastolic dysfunction, atrial remodeling, endothelial dysfunction, pulmonary hypertension, and right ventricular impairment. By preserving endogenous endothelial nitric oxide signaling, this model offers a translational platform for studying vascular and cardiopulmonary mechanisms in cardiometabolic HFpEF.

title: Evaluation of the Caval-Aortic Index During Early Fluid Resuscitation in Patients With Acute Pancreatitis.
authorString: Şafak T, Erdem AB, Vural NV, Çakar E.

journal.title: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research

abstractText: BACKGROUND Early fluid resuscitation is a cornerstone of acute pancreatitis management; however, bedside assessment of the early hemodynamic response remains challenging. We prospectively evaluated serial ultrasonographic parameters and peripheral venous pressure (PVP) during initial fluid resuscitation in patients with acute pancreatitis. MATERIAL AND METHODS Patients with confirmed acute pancreatitis underwent serial measurements of inferior vena cava (IVC) diameter, aortic diameter, caval-aortic (IVC/Ao) index, PVP, and mean arterial pressure (MAP) before and 2 hours after fluid resuscitation. Early hemodynamic response was defined as an increase of at least 10% in MAP from baseline. Correlation and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses with DeLong's test were performed. RESULTS Sixty patients were included. After fluid resuscitation, IVC diameter, IVC/Ao index, PVP, and MAP significantly increased, whereas aortic diameter remained unchanged. Changes in IVC diameter (ΔIVC) were positively correlated with changes in MAP (ΔMAP); changes in aortic diameter (ΔAorta) showed a significant inverse correlation. The ΔIVC/Ao index showed a similar positive trend, but this correlation was not statistically significant. ΔAorta demonstrated the highest discriminatory performance for identifying MAP-defined early hemodynamic response (area under the curve, 0.680; 95% confidence interval, 0.535-0.824), although pairwise ROC analysis revealed no significant superiority over the other ultrasonographic parameters. CONCLUSIONS Serial ultrasonographic assessment may provide clinically relevant information during early fluid resuscitation in acute pancreatitis. No ultrasonographic parameter demonstrated clear superiority. ΔAorta showed the numerically highest, although modest, discriminatory performance in this cohort. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and warrant further investigation before any comparative advantage of arterial ultrasonographic assessment can be inferred.

title: Time-aligned segmental strain as a diagnostic marker for obstructive coronary artery disease in patients with chronic chest pain.
authorString: Rösner A, Caglayan HA, Jazbani M, Sari SØ, Castellote PM, Kjønås D, Queirós S.
abstractText:
Background

Myocardial strain curves provide valuable insights into coronary artery disease (CAD) beyond conventional peak strain measurements. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic utility of time-aligned segmental strain and strain rate (S/SR) curves to identify obstructive CAD in consecutive chest pain patients.

Methods

A total of 510 chest-pain patients referred to coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) were included. Segmental strain curves were time-aligned using aortic valve closure (AVC) and cardiac cycle length as reference points. Average S/SR curves were generated for 18 myocardial segments, establishing reference curves from a group of 314 chronic chest-pain patients without CAD (No-CAD). Deviations were defined based on thresholds of peak S/SR or average S/SR curve deviation over systole and the first half of diastole.

Results

Significant differences were observed between groups, particularly between the revascularized MI, CABG, or 3-vessel CAD groups compared to the No-CAD group (p<0.05). ROC curve analysis demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance for CABG patients (AUC up to 0.933), while the detection rate for PCI was limited (AUC < 0.7). Global longitudinal strain rate in early diastole (GLSR E) and segmental peak SR E showed the highest diagnostic accuracy. These findings confirm that time-aligned strain analysis improves the detection of significant CAD but remains limited for identifying patients with mild disease.

Conclusion

Time-aligned segmental strain analysis improved detection of high-grade disease requiring CABG but could not distinguish single-vessel from non-obstructive CAD. Pathological strain patterns became significant only in advanced CAD, indicating that segmental resting strain analysis has clinical utility primarily for identifying advanced CAD.

title: Narrow Is Slow: CT-Derived Anatomic Isthmus 3 Width and Arrhythmogenic Substrate in Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot
authorString: Kosmopoulos M, Liskov S, Amir R, Berger RD, Cedars A, Chehab O, Chrispin J, Fisher S, Fuller S, Fraint H, Armstrong AK, Ziakas I, Aronis KN.
abstractText:
Background

Anatomic isthmus 3 (AI 3) is defined as the myocardium between the pulmonary valve annulus and the ventricular septal defect patch that persists after tetralogy of Fallot (ToF) repair. Ventricular tachycardia (VT) propagated through slow conducting AI 3 (SCAI 3) represents a significant cause of morbidity in ToF. There is an unmet need for non-invasive identification of SCAI 3 in patients with ToF.

Objectives

To assess whether the anatomic features of AI 3 as derived from cardiac computed tomography (CT) can predict slow conduction velocity during EP study.

Methods

This retrospective single-center study included patients with ToF who underwent an electrophysiologic study and had AI 3 width measured from the pre-procedure cardiac CT. All patients underwent programmed ventricular stimulation, and electroanatomic. Logistic regression was performed to assess the relationship between AI 3 width and the presence of SCAI 3.

Results

Of 27 consecutive patients with ToF, twelve patients were found to have SCAI 3, and ten patients were found to have SCAI 3 mediated VT. The AI 3 was significantly narrower in patients with SCAI 3 compared to those with normal AI 3 conduction (18.4 ± 6.6 mm vs. 29.2 ± 9.0 mm; p = 0.001). An AI 3 width above 21.5 mm carried a negative predictive value of 80.0%.

Conclusion

In adults with repaired ToF referred for electrophysiology study, a narrower CT-derived AI 3 width was associated with SCAI 3 identification. AI 3 width measured on a CT obtained before PV replacement could help guide invasive risk stratification.

title: Design of Screening Cardiometabolic Opportunities Using Transformative Echocardiography Artificial Intelligence (SCOUT-Echo-AI).
authorString: Eusuff S, Kim J, Fatima Z, Yalcinkaya D, Sahashi Y, Sandhu A, Nguyen LH, Ambrosy AP, Cheng PP, Chang ST, Go AS, Ahmad FS, Cheung A, Cheng S, Kwan AC, Ouyang D.
abstractText:
Background

Steatotic liver disease (SLD) is highly prevalent among individuals with cardiovascular disease, but often remains undiagnosed until advanced sequelae such as fibrotic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma develop. ​​Transthoracic echocardiography routinely captures incidental subcostal views of the liver that are not used clinically. The EchoNet-Liver algorithm uses artificial intelligence (AI) to predict the presence of liver disease based on routine clinical echocardiograms. Prospective evaluation in real-world practice is needed to understand the clinical utility and impact of AI-enabled opportunistic liver disease screening.

Methods

The SCOUT-Echo-AI study is a single-arm, prospective, multicenter, open-label pragmatic interventional trial that will be conducted across six diverse U.S. healthcare systems (Kaiser Permanente Northern California, Stanford Healthcare, Cedars-Sinai Medical Center, University of California Los Angeles, Northwestern Medicine, and Massachusetts General Brigham). Routine echocardiograms will be analyzed by the EchoNet-Liver AI algorithm with an estimated enrollment of ∼3,000 patients. Treating clinicians or participants themselves will be notified of potential undiagnosed liver disease with site-specific workflows in place to ensure routine clinical care for definitive case confirmation. Primary outcomes will be SLD and fibrotic liver disease detection rates and positive predictive values within 12 months of AI identification. Pre-specified secondary outcomes will assess diagnostic accuracy against other gold-standard modalities, treatment initiation, time to diagnosis, and impact on other clinical events. Outcomes will be compared against historical usual-care and contemporary below-threshold cohorts.

Conclusion

SCOUT-Echo-AI is a prospective multicenter study evaluating the real-world impact of AI-enabled opportunistic liver disease screening using routine echocardiography.

title: High-Frequency Electrograms Abolition as a Valuable Target for Remap During Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation. The HF REMAP Study.
authorString: Cauti FM, Valente D, Magnocavallo M, Martini N, Ricciardi D, Fioravanti F, Tanese N, Rossi P, Della Rocca DG, Radinovic A, Rampa L, Calore F, Peretto G, Barengo A, Della Bella P.
abstractText:
Background

peak frequency (PF) analysis has recently emerged as a novel tool to assess electrogram properties through their frequency spectrum. PF is an indirect marker of local myocardial activity, and its reduction after radiofrequency ablation reflects effective tissue modification.

Objective

our study aims to evaluate PF analysis as an objective method to validate lesion efficacy during ventricular tachycardia (VT) ablation.

Methods

we retrospectively analyzed 43 (out of 247) consecutive patients who underwent VT ablation between January 2023 and December 2024, using the EnSite X mapping system with Advisor HD Grid catheter (Abbott, Minneapolis, USA). Complete pre- and post-ablation high-density sinus rhythm maps were obtained. PF analysis was applied offline to quantify the residual high-frequency (HF) electrogram burden, expressed as a percentage of the ablated area. Patients were stratified according to residual HF burden, and outcomes were assessed with Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox regression analysis.

Results
