During a median follow-up of 372 days, 11 patients reached the primary endpoint (VT recurrence or arrhythmic storm). Patients with <70% residual HF post-ablation had significantly higher VT-free survival (≈90% at 12 months) compared to those with ≥70% residual HF (≈25%; log-rank p<0.001). Cox regression confirmed residual HF ≥70% as an independent predictor of recurrence (HR 13.36; 95% CI 3.52-50.7; p<0.001).

Conclusion

PF analysis during re-mapping provides an operator-independent, reproducible tool to validate lesion efficacy. A low post-ablation residual HF burden is associated to a significantly increased VAs-free survival rate.

title: Temporal Changes in LGE-CMR Enhancement After Monopolar Biphasic Focal Pulsed Field Ablation for Pulmonary Vein Isolation.
authorString: Moersdorf M, Forkmann M, Abou-Khalil M, Busch S, Linz D, Marrouche N, Sommer P, Sohns C, Mahnkopf C.
abstractText:
Background

Pulsed field ablation (PFA) has emerged as a novel non-thermal ablation modality for pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) in atrial fibrillation (AF). While chronic lesion formation after PFA has been described, data regarding acute lesion characteristics and lesion maturation remain limited.

Objective

To characterize acute and chronic lesion formation following focal point-by-point PFA for PVI using serial late-gadolinium-enhancement cardiovascular-magnetic-resonance-imaging (LGE-CMR).

Methods

Six consecutive patients with symptomatic paroxysmal or persistent AF underwent index PFA-guided PVI using the CENTAURI system and a focal point-by-point lesion delivery strategy. LGE-CMR was performed 1 day and 90±10 days after ablation. Quantitative assessment of regional and global left atrial (LA) enhancement was performed using a standardized segmentation protocol. Changes in enhancement burden and LA dimensions were analyzed between imaging timepoints.

Results

Among six patients at mean age 65±7 years, five patients (83%) had paroxysmal AF. Acute PVI was achieved in all patients without procedural complications. Serial LGE-CMR demonstrated substantial temporal changes between acute and chronic imaging. Enhancement within the right pulmonary vein (PV) region decreased from 3.3±2.2% to 0.8±0.8%(p=0.030), while the proportion of enhanced tissue decreased from 24.1±13.5% to 5.7±5.8%(p=0.017). Similar reductions were observed around the left PVs (4.4±3.1%vs.1.4±1.2%, p=0.064). Posterior wall enhancement decreased from 2.4±1.1% to 0.3±0.3%(p=0.007) and global LA enhancement from 12.8±6.2% to 3.3±1.6%(p=0.013), while LA volume remained unchanged.

Conclusion

Serial LGE-CMR demonstrated substantial enhancement reduction of acute lesions following focal point-by-point PFA for PVI, which remained largely confined to the PV antra and adjacent posterior wall, providing novel in-human insights into lesion maturation following focal PFA delivery.

title: Predictors of Surveillance Imaging Non-compliance Among Patients with TEVAR for Blunt Thoracic Aortic Injury.
authorString: Pekar B, Anderson MP, Gadsden L, Tanious A, Mukherjee R, Ruddy JM.
abstractText: ObjectivesBlunt Thoracic Aortic Injury (BTAI) is the second leading cause of death for patients with blunt trauma. Thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) has become the standard of care for high-grade BTAI, reducing morbidity and mortality while requiring long-term surveillance imaging to ensure graft integrity and prevent future complications. However, adherence to this protocol is poor. Previous studies evaluating the factors associated with post-operative imaging non-compliance have yielded conflicting results. This study aimed to evaluate predictors of post-TEVAR non-compliance inpatients presenting with BTAI.MethodsA retrospective study on 23 patients was conducted using a single institution Aortic Center Database (2015-2025). Inclusion criteria included patients who were age >18 years and underwent TEVAR for BTAI. Demographic, comorbidity, hospital course, and follow-up data were collected. The Distressed Communities Index (DCI) score was derived from patient's home address ZIP code. Time-to-event analysis defined loss to follow up (LTFU) for vascular imaging as the failure event. Patients were censored at death or if compliant through 1 year following the index TEVAR. Statistical analysis included chi-square, t-tests, and Kaplan-Meier survival.ResultsBased on this single-center review on TEVAR follow-up for BTAI, sex, race, and hospital length of stay did not impact compliance. Medical comorbidities were also non-significant. Patients who presented with a lower injury severity score (P = 0.02) and lived more than 20 miles from their follow-up appointment (P = 0.02) were more likely to be LTFU. While the type of facility was not impactful, all patients who were discharged to a non-home location were LTFU. Interestingly, DCI and insurance status had no impact on follow-up non-compliance.ConclusionsThis study supports the development of targeted, patient-centered surveillance strategies, especially amongst rural populations and those discharged to a non-home location. To fully understand this complex problem, further investigation using a larger database may be indicated.

title: Coil Embolization and Open Splenectomy for a Massive Splenic Vein Aneurysm: A Case Report.
authorString: Vu K, Brown L, Durrence B, Patel T, Larsen R, Gordy S.
abstractText:
Background

Splenic vein aneurysms (SVAs) are a rare vascular anomaly of the portal system that are often asymptomatic and found incidentally on imaging. Intervention is reserved for aneurysms that are enlarging, thrombosed, symptomatic, or ruptured to avoid catastrophic complications. This can range from endovascular to open, complex procedures. Here, we present the case of a massive, symptomatic, partially thrombosed SVA that required a hybrid approach involving both minimally invasive and open surgery.

Case presentation

A 56-year-old woman presented to the emergency department for an infected right foot wound and was admitted for intravenous antibiotics and surgical debridement. While hospitalized, she had a worsening transaminitis with associated abdominal pain, prompting investigation with a computed tomography (CT) scan, which identified a massively dilated, partially thrombosed SVA measuring 18 cm. Given the enormous size of the aneurysm and substantial risk of impending rupture, urgent surgical intervention was planned. Preoperative coil embolization of the splenic artery was performed first to reduce the arterial inflow to the SVA and to minimize the risk of intraoperative hemorrhage during open resection. Three days after embolization, the patient underwent open splenectomy with aneurysmectomy for definitive management. The patient's postoperative course was complicated by a bleeding gastric ulcer that was successfully cauterized, and she was discharged home on postoperative Day 10 after receiving the recommended postsplenectomy vaccines.

Conclusion

No standard treatment algorithm exists for SVAs, as management is individualized, and treatment evidence is limited to case reports and series. This patient had one of the largest SVAs ever recorded, and management was based on the acuity of symptoms, size, and rupture risk of the aneurysm sac. This case also demonstrated the success of a novel management approach to massive SVAs, using preoperative embolization of the splenic artery followed by open resection without portal reconstruction.

title: Clinical utility and impact of myocardial viability imaging with F-18 FDG positron emission tomography to predict left ventricular function improvement following revascularization in ischemic heart disease : a single center retrospective study.
authorString: Qureshi MA, Saleem M, Ananthasubramaniam K.

journal.title: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging

abstractText: Recent studies have questioned the benefit of myocardial viability identification and its clinical impact on revascularization decisions. We aimed to evaluate whether F-18 fluorodeoxyglucose (F-18 FDG)-positron emission tomography (PET) influences real-world revascularization decisions and whether PET-defined viability helps predict improvement in ejection fraction (LVEF). We conducted a retrospective chart review of Rubidium-82 (Rb-82)/F-18 FDG PET ischemia and viability studies performed from 2020 to 2024 at our institution. Baseline characteristics including comorbidities, ejection fraction (EF) at 3 months and 1 year and PET study results were evaluated. Among patients with viability, a linear mixed-effects model adjusted for baseline EF was performed to assess temporal changes and treatment strategy interaction. One hundred and eleven patients underwent rest-stress Rb-82 PET with F-18 FDG PET imaging, of whom 99 received FDG for myocardial viability assessment. Among these patients, 65 (65.6%) demonstrated ischemic viable myocardium, while 31 (31.3%) had non-viable myocardium. Viability-positive patients were more likely to undergo revascularization (57% (n = 37) vs. 36% (n = 28) received medical therapy only). At 3-month follow-up, both revascularization and medical therapy were associated with significant improvement in LVEF among viability-positive patients. In contrast, viability-negative patients did not demonstrate significant EF improvement. Among viability-positive patients with both 3-month and 1- year EF measurements (N = 28), linear mixed-effects model adjusted for baseline EF revealed that baseline EF was a strong independent predictor of follow-up EF (p < 0.0001). From 3 months to 1 year, the revascularization group demonstrated a significant increase in EF (+ 4.28%, p = 0.014), whereas the medical therapy group showed a non-significant change (+ 1.40%, p = 0.53). However, the overall EF improvement did not differ significantly between groups after adjustment (p = 0.30). EF changes in viability-negative patients remained non-significant over time. Symptomatic improvement was documented in 55.3% of viability-positive patients. Our single-center experience shows that FDG-PET viability test continues to guide management and decision making regarding revascularization and can predict functional recovery and symptomatic improvement.

title: MicroRNA Regulatory Networks in Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease: Mechanisms from Steatosis and Inflammation to Fibrosis.
authorString: Shihao D, Dongqin Y, Qianqian L, Jianing G, Zhijun L.
abstractText: Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) is a leading cause of liver-related morbidity and mortality worldwide and progresses through steatosis, alcohol-associated hepatitis, fibrosis, and cirrhosis. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are established post-transcriptional regulators whose roles in ALD-associated signaling networks have been increasingly characterized. Recent high-throughput sequencing and functional studies have revealed dual regulatory roles of miRNA families, such as miR-122, miR-155, and miR-21, at different disease stages. However, most studies have focused on individual miRNAs, and network-level cooperative regulation and clinical translation remain underexplored. This narrative review examines the molecular mechanisms of miRNAs in alcohol-induced steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis, with a particular focus on network-level cooperative regulation. Key findings indicate that miRNAs function as stage-specific and cell-type-specific regulators, with miR-122, miR-155, miR-21, miR-29, and miR-34a acting as central network nodes. These insights provide a framework for the identification of early diagnostic biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets in ALD.

title: Electromechanical Window Negativity and Arrhythmic Risk in Arrhythmogenic Mitral Valve Prolapse.
authorString: Deissler PM, Berkovitch A, Bergh J, Harutyunyan K, Pype LL, Langenberg B, Van De Heyning CM, Beinart R, Sohns C, Sommer P, Volders PGA, Haugaa KH, Sabbag A, Ter Bekke RMA.
abstractText:
Background

Mitral valve prolapse (MVP) is generally a benign valvular heart disease, but a subset of patients is at particular risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias (AMVP).

Objectives

The authors evaluated the electromechanical window (EMW) as an arrhythmia-risk marker in (A)MVP (the sum of all MVP and AMVP patients).

Methods

Healthy controls, patients with MVP without ventricular arrhythmia (MVP/-VA), and patients with AMVP with nonsustained (AMVP/nsVA) or sustained ventricular arrhythmia (AMVP/VA) (ventricular arrhythmia >30 seconds) were retrospectively included from 3 centers (derivation cohort). An independent validation (A)MVP cohort was recruited from 2 centers. EMW was calculated blinded from apical Doppler echocardiography by subtracting the QT time from the simultaneous Q-to-aortic-valve closure time (QAoC).

Results

In the derivation cohort (31 controls, 31 MVP/-VA, 29 AMVP/nsVA, 14 AMVP/VA), patients with (A)MVP displayed a borderline shorter QAoCc (P = 0.06) and significantly longer QTc than controls (P < 0.0001), resulting in a more negative EMW (-18 ms [-47 to -8 ms]; P < 0.0001). EMW was most negative in patients with AMVP/VA (-71 ms [-177 to -30 ms]). These findings were reproduced in the validation cohort (n = 76 with [A]MVP), albeit at different absolute values. In a pooled receiver-operating characteristic analysis, EMW identified patients with AMVP/VA with an area under the curve of 0.82 (95% CI: 0.73-0.91), significantly outperforming QTc and QAoCc. An EMW threshold of -30 ms was the optimal cutoff (sensitivity: 0.71; specificity: 0.83). EMW was independently associated with AMVP/VA status and improved model performance in addition to established risk parameters.

Conclusions

EMW is markedly negative in patients with AMVP/VA, reflecting electromechanical discordance. Thus, EMW emerges as a promising risk-associated marker in (A)MVP.

title: Optimization of Anticoagulation Strategy During Cardiopulmonary Bypass in Neonates with Congenital Heart Disease: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
authorString: Wang H, Liu Q, Gao P, Liu J, Jin Y, Gao T, Wang W, Bayartaikishigtai D, Zhang Y, Liu J.
abstractText:
Purpose

Neonatal hemostatic immaturity complicates anticoagulation during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). Current practice largely follows the strategy of 400 U/kg from adult protocols, as neonatal-specific guidelines and high-quality evidence remain lacking, which frequently fails to achieve adequate anticoagulation. This single-center randomized controlled trial evaluated the initial heparin dose of 600 U/kg to refine neonatal CPB anticoagulation.

Patients and methods

In this prospective, randomized, controlled, single-blind trial, 76 neonates undergoing CPB were assigned to receive an initial heparin dose of either 600 U/kg (n = 38) or 400 U/kg (n = 38). The primary endpoint was the pre- to post-CPB change in prothrombin fragment 1+2 (ΔF1+2). Secondary endpoints included the proportion of neonates achieving the ACT threshold after the initial heparin bolus, perioperative coagulation measures, postoperative blood loss, transfusion requirements, and adverse clinical outcomes.

Results

Mean ΔF1+2 was 0.70 vs 4.08 nmol/L in the 600 and 400 U/kg groups, respectively (treatment-minus-control mean difference, -3.38 nmol/L; 95% confidence interval, -4.58 to -2.18; P <0.001). ACT target achievement rate after the initial dose was higher in the 600 U/kg group (84.2% vs 44.7%, P < 0.001). Surgical preparation time was shorter (median 31.50 vs 36.50 mins, P = 0.028), and supplemental heparin use was lower, while total heparin dose did not differ significantly. Secondary endpoints showed lower 72-hour chest drainage and albumin use and shorter mechanical ventilation duration (P = 0.036, 0.028, and 0.031, respectively). Red-cell, plasma, and platelet transfusion requirements and most other clinical outcomes did not differ significantly. One in-hospital death occurred with 600 U/kg and none with 400 U/kg. Complete-case sensitivity analysis supported the primary finding.

Conclusion

An initial heparin dose of 600 U/kg in neonatal CPB was associated with a smaller F1+2 increase and greater initial ACT response. Larger studies are needed to establish clinical benefit and safety.

Clinical trial registry number

ChiCTR2300069157.

title: Unraveling the Genotype-Phenotype Landscape of Kleefstra Syndrome Through <i>EHMT1</i> Variant Analysis.
authorString: Kim JM, Cha JH, Kim W, Kim SY, Ko JM, Lim B, Lee S, Chae JH.
abstractText:
Background and objectives

Kleefstra syndrome type 1 (KLEFS1) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder caused by pathogenic variants in EHMT1, which play a key role in epigenetic regulation. Core features include global developmental delay (GDD), intellectual disability (ID), facial dysmorphism, congenital heart defects (CHDs), and neuropsychiatric manifestations.

Methods

This retrospective study included patients with KLEFS1 evaluated at Seoul National University Hospital between January 2022 and April 2025. Genetic diagnoses were made using chromosomal microarray or whole-exome or whole-genome sequencing, and clinical data were extracted from medical records. To enhance statistical power, we conducted a joint analysis with established cohorts of at least 30 clinically characterized patients.

Results

Among the 15 patients with KLEFS1, 14 (93.3%) exhibited GDD or ID, with frequent comorbidities such as CHDs (8/12, 66.7%), orthopaedic manifestations (6/12, 50.0%), epilepsy (6/15, 40.0%), and sleep problems (4/11, 36.4%). Brain MRI revealed abnormalities in 10 of the 12 patients (83.3%), including pituitary anomalies in 2 (16.7%). By combining our data with recently published multicenter international cohorts, we assessed genotype-phenotype correlations by comparing the clinical features of 202 patients with different variant subtypes. Patients with multigene deletions had a significantly higher prevalence of CHDs (53.5% vs 25.8%, p value = 2 × 10-4), cortical visual impairment (12.5% vs 1.7%, p value = 0.004), microcephaly (37.1% vs 17.8%, p value = 0.009), corpus callosum abnormalities (17.9% vs 5.9%, p value = 0.02), and hearing impairment (39.7% vs 25.6%, p value = 0.04) than those with single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) or short insertions/deletions (indels), in addition to the previously identified features including epilepsy, constipation, and short stature. We also observed that a recurrent EHMT1 variant (p.Arg948Trp), identified in multiple unrelated patients, was linked to significant phenotypic heterogeneity, including late-onset neurocognitive regression.

Discussion

Our study showed that patients with multigene deletions are significantly more likely to exhibit multiorgan involvement, including CHDs, cortical visual impairments, microcephaly, corpus callosum abnormalities, and hearing impairments, compared with those with SNVs or indels, emphasizing the importance of genotype-informed management. We report pituitary gland abnormalities in KLEFS1, expanding the phenotypic and neuroimaging spectrum of KLEFS1. The patient showing regression in their 30s necessitates long-term, comprehensive studies to support care.

title: The ‘Upstairs-Downstairs’ heart with complete main pulmonary artery agenesis and PDA-dependent pulmonary circulation: A rare structural intersection characterized by multi detector computed tomography
authorString: Kanji A, Aziz T, Fundikira L, Akberali U, Salingwa L, Lyimo F, Jacob M.

title: Pathogenic Variants in NKX2-5 Associated With Familial Atrial Septal Defect and Conduction System Disease.
authorString: Srivatsav V, Guerin A, Abdollah H, Archer SL.
abstractText:
Background

Most atrial septal defects (ASDs) occur sporadically, but familial cases can occur and carry a 10% risk of transmission to offspring.

Case summary

We describe a 3-generation family with autosomal dominant secundum ASD and conduction system disease related to a novel NKX2-5 variant (c.300del; p.Asp101Thrfs∗75). The index patient, a 58-year-old woman with prior ASD repair and mitral valve replacement, presented with chronotropic incompetence, atrial fibrillation, left bundle branch block, and prolonged pauses, leading to pacemaker implantation. Her mother had an ASD, atrial fibrillation, left bundle branch block, and pulmonary arterial hypertension. The proband's daughter also had an ASD. Genetic testing revealed a novel NKX2-5 pathogenic variant in all 3 patients.

Review summary

The combination of an ASD and conduction system disease represents the most common phenotype in patients with pathogenic NKX2-5 variants.

Take-home message

A thorough family history and genetic testing are needed when evaluating patients with ASD and concurrent conduction system abnormalities.

title: Burden, healthcare utilization, and costs of chronic liver disease-related hospitalizations in California: a population-based study of trends and projections, 2005-2035.
authorString: Fan H, Mao X, Su X, Wang J, Yan T, Cheung R, Nguyen MH.
abstractText:
Background

Long-term trends in hospitalization burden, healthcare utilization, and costs of chronic liver disease (CLD) in the United States remain poorly characterized. Using statewide hospital discharge data, we quantified trends from 2005 to 2018 and projected future burden through 2035 across demographic subgroups.

Methods

We used average annual percent change (AAPC) to quantify trends in hospitalized patients, hospitalizations, deaths, along with age-standardized rates (ASHPR, ASHR, and ASMR); hospitalizations per patient-year, average length of stay, 30-day readmission, in-hospital mortality; and inflation-adjusted hospital charges (2019 US dollars). Analyses were conducted overall and for hepatitis B virus(HBV), hepatitis C virus(HCV), alcohol-associated liver disease(ALD), and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).

Findings

From 2005 to 2018, hospitalized CLD patients increased from 71,214 to 122,810 (AAPC, 4.37%; 95% CI, 3.87%-4.88%), and deaths from 11,455 to 24,560 (6.02%; 4.20%-7.86%). ASHPR increased from 275.12 to 377.88 per 100,000, and ASMR from 45.53 to 74.77. Hospitalizations and charges increased from 116,482 to 185,268 and $9.63 billion to $18.63 billion, while in-hospital mortality declined (AAPC, -7.02%; 95% CI, -8.72%-5.30%). MASLD- and ALD-related hospitalizations increased, whereas HBV- and HCV-related hospitalizations declined. Men had higher hospitalization and mortality rates, particularly for ALD. Hispanic populations had the fastest-rising burden, driven by MASLD; HBV burden was concentrated among non-Hispanic Asian populations, whereas overall CLD and ALD-related mortality were highest among non-Hispanic White populations.

Interpretation

Findings highlight the need for targeted prevention and screening, early management of metabolic and alcohol-related risk factors, and equitable access to liver care.

Funding

No funding.

title: Exploring the Expanding Role of Nuclear Receptor LRH-1/NR5A2 in Cell Biology and Immunity.
authorString: Tsapalou E, Michael P, Georgoula M, Michail K, Papoutsopoulou S, Campbell BJ.
abstractText: LRH-1/NR5A2 is a member of the NR5A subfamily of nuclear receptors, acting as a crucial transcription factor involved in diverse biological processes. Although LRH-1 has been extensively studied in vitro and in vivo, in relation to its role in embryonic development and differentiation and in adult tissue processes, such as cholesterol, glucose, and ethanol metabolism, current knowledge about its function in immunity is very limited. This review, therefore, presents the most recent knowledge regarding NR5A2 regulation and LRH-1 function, including the wide spectrum of its target genes. In addition to LRH-1 regulating steroidogenesis in tissues such as the ovaries, testes, pancreas, and breast adipocytes, it is also key in driving glucocorticoid production in intestine, where its immunomodulatory activity is undoubtedly important in maintaining gut homeostasis and countering inflammation. Likewise, LRH-1 also appears to be crucial to the enterohepatic circulation, regulating hepatic bile acid synthesis and secretion, and intestinal transport/reabsorption. Our review also highlights fundamental roles for LRH-1 in macrophage polarization and in T cell homeostasis, revealing a major role in Th2 immune responses. Although no studies to date have explored the association of LRH-1 with respect to B-lymphocyte biology, we highlight the need for understanding its wider role in the immune system and its interplay with tissues and organs in health and disease.

title: Intravascular Ultrasound Guidance for Transcatheter Pulmonary Valve Replacement: A Feasibility Study.
authorString: Sadowski KA, Kania M, Stark W, Woźniak O, Kobari Y, Kądziela J, Mintz GS, De Backer O, Demkow M, Kalińczuk Ł.

title: Advancing cardiac xenotransplantation: overcoming challenges and ethical considerations for clinical integration.
authorString: Abdelrehim AA, Hurst DJ, Gray WH, Sorabella R, Padilla LA.
abstractText: Advanced heart failure affects over 6 million adults in the United States alone. Orthotopic heart transplantation remains the definitive treatment, with over 90% one-year survival and meaningful gains in functional status and quality of life. The therapy is, however, constrained by an intractable supply problem. For decades, xenotransplantation (XTx), the transplantation of organs across species, has been proposed as a means of closing this gap, though for most of that time it remained a theoretical aspiration. With the discovery of CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, improved immunosuppressive strategies, and refined preclinical models, the field has accelerated at an unprecedented pace. Multi-gene-edited porcine donors have survived for more than 200 days in orthotopic non-human primate models, and two compassionate-use pig-to-human cardiac transplants at the University of Maryland (2022 and 2023) demonstrated some feasibility for clinical cardiac XTx for the first time. In May 2026, the FDA granted clearance under an investigational new drug application to allow the EXPRESS study, the first prospective clinical trial of a gene-edited porcine heart, to proceed. In this perspective, we discuss the ethical, regulatory, and equity considerations that remain as decisive barriers to clinical integration and may shape how this therapy is introduced along the remaining immunologic and virologic challenges. We outline what we regard as the near-term priorities: defining the antibody targets that drive xenograft rejection, standardizing virologic surveillance, candidate selection and outcome benchmarking, and building access patterns with embedded distributive justice from the outset of its implementation.

title: <i>Parvimonas micra</i> and central nervous system infections: mechanisms of transformation from oral commensal to intracranial pathogen and clinical evidence.
authorString: Gong C, Jing X, Jiang S, Yu C.

journal.title: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

abstractText: Parvimonas micra (P. micra), an anaerobic oral coccus long dismissed as a culture contaminant, is increasingly recognized as a causative agent of pyogenic central nervous system (CNS) infections, yet its neuropathogenesis remains poorly defined. This narrative review synthesizes 41 peer-reviewed studies identified via a structured comprehensive literature search of PubMed, Embase and Web of Science through June 2026. Epidemiologically, pooling available case reports and small series (n=64 confirmed CNS cases), P. micra is among the most frequently isolated Gram-positive anaerobic cocci in reported brain abscess series, with proportions ranging from approximately 4% to over 10% in individual cohorts; species-level data are inconsistently reported and a precise pooled estimate cannot be derived. A male predominance (approximately 2.7:1) is observed among reported cases, though this should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample size and potential reporting bias. Approximately two-thirds of patients have no documented immunosuppressive condition. Brain abscess represents ~80% of CNS manifestations, with 60-70% presenting as polymicrobial infection. We propose a five-step pathogenic cascade-periodontal dysbiosis, epithelial barrier breach, intravascular survival, blood-brain barrier (BBB) translocation, and intracranial suppuration-as a conceptual framework. Virulence factors including the TmpC-AppA axis and extracellular vesicle DnaK have been characterized in non-CNS models (oral carcinoma, periodontitis, oral lichen planus); their relevance to CNS infection is inferred, and BBB translocation mechanisms remain entirely hypothetical. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) outperforms conventional culture in selected brain abscess cohorts (~85% vs ~50% in pus; ~84% vs ~8% in CSF across CNS infections), though performance varies by specimen type, prior antibiotic exposure, and sequencing platform. All-cause mortality is 5-10% and 20-25% of survivors sustain neurological sequelae, though these estimates may overestimate true population rates due to publication bias. P. micra shows consistently low in vitro minimum inhibitory concentrations to metronidazole and β-lactams. Early empirical anaerobic coverage and consideration of mNGS as a complementary diagnostic tool are recommended for suspected odontogenic brain abscess.

title: Disseminated BCG disease and recurrent pulmonary infections in a child with trisomy 21 carrying a novel <i>BACH2</i> variant of uncertain significance: a 5-year case report.
authorString: Marangu-Boore D, Maugo B, Boateng RA.
abstractText:
Background

Trisomy 21 is associated with combined immune dysregulation, including lymphopenia, impaired responses to vaccines, and heightened susceptibility to respiratory infections, driven in part by triplication of chromosome 21-encoded interferon receptor genes. BACH2 haploinsufficiency is a rare monogenic immunodeficiency characterized by lymphopenia, hypogammaglobulinemia, and susceptibility to infections and autoimmune diseases. Co-occurrence of these two conditions has not been previously described.

Case presentation

We report a 5-year longitudinal course in a Kenyan girl with trisomy 21, congenital heart disease, aspiration, and severe gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) found via whole exome sequencing to carry a heterozygous BACH2 missense variant (c.1420C > G;p.Leu474Val) of uncertain significance; parental segregation remains incomplete. In silico protein structural modeling (FoldX and Missense3D) yielded discordant predictions of the variant's effect on the protein's stability and structure. Additional in silico pathogenicity predictions were also inconsistent: Sorting Intolerant from Tolerant (SIFT), Evolutionary Model of Variant Effect (EVE), PolyPhen-2, and CADD Phred scores predicted pathogenicity, while REVEL and AlphaMissense suggested a lack of deleteriousness. Persistent panlymphopenia and profoundly low IgM levels were documented throughout the follow-up period. Over these 5 years, the girl sustained six hospitalized lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs), with four requiring intensive care, which were disseminated Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) disease, respiratory syncytial virus and SARS-CoV-2 infections, and influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 pneumonia. Chest computed tomography at 4 years showed bilateral consolidations without bronchiectasis. Annual autoimmune screening remained negative.

Conclusion

This case illustrates the burden caused by severe and diverse respiratory pathogenic infections in a child with trisomy 21 and a candidate BACH2 variant. Trisomy 21 alone plausibly explains much of the phenotype; an independent contribution from the BACH2 variant remains unproven pending functional and segregation studies. Clinical considerations supported by this case include the potential value of prevaccination immunological screening to prevent BCG disease, equitable access to viral prophylaxis, and early specialist engagement in refractory cases.

title: Incidence and epidemiological characteristics of congenital adrenal hyperplasia in Hangzhou newborns, China (2014-2024): a population-based cross-sectional study.
authorString: Dai Y, Zhu L, Zeng Y, Chen Y, Qian X, Li X, Wu T.
abstractText:
Background

Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) is a rare but potentially life-threatening autosomal recessive disorder. Its incidence varies by region and ethnicity. This study aimed to evaluate the birth incidence, trends, and clinical characteristics of neonatal classic CAH in Hangzhou (2014-2024) to support regional clinical prevention and management.

Methods

This retrospective population-based study collected data from Hangzhou's information systems. Classic CAH cases were identified through newborn screening and clinical follow-up to age 3, with diagnosis confirmed by pediatric endocrinologists. Incidence was calculated per 100,000 live births. Categorical variables were compared using chi-square or Fisher's exact test. Temporal trend was assessed by Poisson regression.

Results

Among 1,235,815 live births, 40 CAH cases were identified, giving an incidence of 3.24/100,000. The annual incidence ranged from 0/100,000 (2020) to 6.56/100,000 (2017), with no significant temporal trend (P = 0.297). The incidence was highest in urban (4.28/100,000), followed by suburban (2.37/100,000) and rural areas (1.93/100,000) (P = 0.16). Males accounted for 65% (26/40) of cases and females 35% (14/40), with a male-to-female ratio of 1.86:1. The incidence was 4.03/100,000 in males and 2.37/100,000 in females (P = 0.104). Among the 40 cases, salt-wasting (SW) was the predominant phenotype (33/40, 82.5%), and 21-hydroxylase deficiency accounted for 95% (38/40) of cases. Two neonates (5%) presented with salt-wasting crises, and two female infants with the simple virilizing (SV) form were initially misclassified as male. Prenatal ultrasound showed increased nuchal translucency in 6 cases (15%), adrenal enlargement in 3 cases (7.5%), and ambiguous genitalia in 1 case (2.5%). CAH was strongly associated with congenital heart defects (OR: 13.93, P < 0.001), and congenital hypothyroidism (OR: 42.26, P < 0.001).

Conclusion

The incidence of classic CAH in Hangzhou (3.24/100,000) was lower than many global estimates. Although temporal and regional differences were not statistically significant, the predominance of SW cases, the occurrence of adrenal crises, and the presence of comorbidities (congenital heart defects, hypothyroidism, and cognitive developmental delay), highlight the need for improved early recognition, strengthened diagnostic capacity in suburban and rural areas, and long-term multidisciplinary management.

title: Shenze shugan capsules alleviate alcoholic liver injury in association with modulation of the TGF-β/smad4 signaling pathway.
authorString: Wang L, Gu Q, Tinghe J, Sun Z, Wang D, Li L, Zang H, Lin L, Chen J, Wang C.
abstractText:
Background

Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) represents a major contributor to liver fibrosis globally, and current therapeutic options remain inadequate. The TGF-β/Smad4 cascade is critically involved in alcohol-evoked activation of hepatic stellate cells and subsequent extracellular matrix accumulation. Although Shenze Shugan capsule (SZSG) has been clinically used for non-alcoholic steatohepatitis, its efficacy and mechanisms in ALD are unclear. This study aimed to explore how SZSG exerts protective effects against alcohol-triggered liver injury and the underlying mechanisms.

Methods

Both acute and chronic ALD mouse models were established to assess liver injury, fibrosis, inflammation, gut microbiota composition, and serum metabolomic profiles.

Results

SZSG treatment markedly attenuated hepatic steatosis, fibrosis, and inflammation, as evidenced by reductions in lipid accumulation, collagen deposition, and pro-inflammatory cytokine levels. Concurrently, it reshaped the gut microbiota and restored metabolites dysregulated by alcohol exposure. These beneficial effects appear to involve modulation of the TGF-β/Smad4 signaling pathway and its downstream effectors, α-SMA and Collagen I.

Conclusion

Collectively, our findings suggest that SZSG combats ALD by simultaneously modulating the TGF-β/Smad4 signaling axis and preserving gut-liver homeostasis, thereby representing a promising multi-target therapeutic candidate.

title: Parenteral Nutrition Exposure, Nutritional Trajectory, and Clinical Outcomes in Neonates with Surgical Gastrointestinal Conditions: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Zekovic L, Nikolic D, Sindjic-Antunovic S, Medjo B, Vujovic D, Grubac Z, Ristic N, Jeremic RS, Raus M.
abstractText: Background/Objectives: Neonates with surgical gastrointestinal conditions frequently require parenteral nutrition and are exposed to multiple overlapping risks for hepatobiliary, infectious, and nutritional complications. This study aimed to determine whether the timing and initial composition of parenteral nutrition (PN) were independently associated with hepatobiliary dysfunction, treatment-related complications, and nutritional outcomes. Methods: This retrospective cohort included 91 neonates hospitalized at the University Children's Hospital between January 2024 and July 2026 who received parenteral nutrition (PN) for >5 consecutive days. Associations between PN timing, modality, duration, enteral progression, clinical severity, feeding type, and hepatobiliary, infectious, and growth outcomes were assessed using univariable and multivariable analyses. Results: Cholestasis occurred in 18 patients (19.8%) and intestinal failure-associated liver disease (IFALD) in 14 (15.4%). The interval from enteral feeding cessation to PN initiation and initial PN modality were not significantly associated with cholestasis or IFALD. Patients with IFALD had longer PN exposure than those without IFALD (21 vs. 12 days; p = 0.010). Each additional PN day increased the adjusted odds of catheter-related bloodstream infection by 9.7% (OR 1.097, 95% CI 1.032-1.167; p = 0.003). Simultaneous amino-acid and lipid initiation was associated with the highest unadjusted weight-gain velocity and numerically lowest cholestasis and IFALD rates, but no independent protective effect was established. Conclusions: Longer PN duration was associated with IFALD and CRBSI, although the IFALD association should be interpreted cautiously because PN duration contributes to its operational definition. Short delays in PN initiation and initial lipid timing were not independently associated with these outcomes. Management should remain individualized, with advancement of enteral nutrition when clinically feasible and minimization of unnecessary PN and central-line exposure.

title: Comparison of Drug-Coated Versus Conventional Balloons for the Side Branches of Bifurcation Lesions: OCVC-BIF Study.
authorString: Ishihara T, Dohi T, Sakamoto D, Kida H, Okamoto N, Kikuchi A, Kawai T, Mori N, Shutta R, Ichikawa M, Ueda Y, Nakamura D, Mano T, Nishino M, Watanabe T, Higuchi Y, Hida E, Sato T, Hikoso S, Nakatani D, Sotomi Y, Sakata Y, OCVC-BIF Investigators.
abstractText:
Background

Coronary bifurcation lesions remain one of the most challenging lesions. In particular, satisfactory clinical outcomes have not yet been achieved for side branches. The use of drug-coated balloons (DCBs) has demonstrated acceptable clinical outcomes in native coronary arteries. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of additional DCB inflation in the side branches of bifurcation lesions.

Methods

The OCVC-BIF study (Comparison of Drug-Coated Versus Conventional Balloons for the Side Branch of Bifurcation Lesions) was conducted as a multicenter, randomized, open-label trial. Patients with bifurcation lesions scheduled for drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation in the main vessel followed by kissing balloon inflation were enrolled in the study. The patients were randomized to receive either additional dilatation of the side branch using a DCB after DES implantation with kissing balloon inflation (DCB group) or only DES implantation with kissing balloon inflation using conventional balloons (non-DCB group). The primary end point was restenosis of the side branch, assessed using scheduled coronary angiography at 9 months or symptom-driven coronary angiography during the 1-year follow-up. Restenosis was defined as ≥50% stenosis of the side branch, determined using 3-dimensional bifurcation quantitative coronary angiography. The key secondary end points included major adverse cardiac events at 12 months, which were defined as a composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, clinically driven target lesion revascularization, and stent thrombosis.

Results

In total, 299 patients were randomized into the DCB (151 patients) and non-DCB (148 patients) groups between October 2019 and September 2024. Serial 3-dimensional bifurcation quantitative coronary angiography evaluation was performed in 262 (87.6%) patients. The restenosis rate was lower in the DCB group than that in the non-DCB group (8.1% versus 18.3%, P=0.012). However, the incidence of major adverse cardiac events at 12 months was similar between them (10.1% versus 12.4%, P=0.58).

Conclusions

Additional DCB inflation in the side branch after main-vessel DES implantation with kissing balloon inflation decreases restenosis in the side branch in the treatment of bifurcation lesions.

Registration

URL: https://jrct.mhlw.go.jp/en-latest-detail/jRCTs052200077; Unique identifier: jRCTs052200077.

title: Chios Mastic in Well-Controlled Hypertension: Findings From the HYPER-MASTIC Randomized Controlled Trial.
authorString: Kalafati IP, Kyriazopoulou-Korovesi AA, Mentsiou-Nikolaou E, Papaioannou M, Konstantaki C, Angelidakis L, Gianniou DD, Mikropoulou EV, Giardoglou P, Valakos D, Vatsellas G, HYPER‐MASTIC Consortium, Andreadou I, Manios E, Halabalaki M, Trougakos IP, Dedoussis GV, Stamatelopoulos K.
abstractText: Residual cardiovascular risk persists in patients with adequately controlled hypertension, driven partly by inflammation, oxidative stress and endothelial dysfunction. Chios mastic (Pistacia lentiscus var. Chia) has shown antihypertensive, antioxidant and vascular effects in experimental and clinical settings. This trial evaluated whether Chios mastic supplementation confers additional cardiovascular benefits in well-controlled hypertensive individuals. In this double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, 106 adults with stable, well-controlled hypertension and variable cardiovascular risk, based on SCORE2, received low-dose Chios mastic (1500 mg/day), high-dose Chios mastic (2800 mg/day) or placebo for 3 months. Primary endpoints were changes in 24-h ambulatory systolic and diastolic blood pressure. Secondary endpoints included vascular function, oxidative stress and proteasome activity in peripheral blood mononuclear cells and red blood cells. Transcriptomic profiling was performed in a predefined high-risk subgroup. Chios mastic supplementation was well tolerated, with high adherence confirmed by dose-dependent increases in plasma masticadienonic and isomasticadienonic acids. No significant between-group differences were observed in 24-h systolic or diastolic blood pressure after the intervention. Oxidative stress markers and proteasome activity remained unchanged across groups. In high-risk participants, mastic supplementation induced distinct transcriptomic changes, particularly in pathways related to endothelial junction organization and vascular integrity. Overall, in adults with well-controlled hypertension and low baseline cardiovascular risk, Chios mastic supplementation did not lower blood pressure over 3 months, likely reflecting a ceiling effect. Transcriptomic findings suggest biologically meaningful vascular effects in individuals with higher residual cardiovascular risk, supporting future investigation in higher-risk populations.

title: Astragaloside IV and Ferroptosis Modulation in Pathological Cardiac Hypertrophy: Current Evidence, an Integrative Hypothesis, and Future Directions.
authorString: Liu P, Deng Y.
abstractText: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy is initially an adaptive response to sustained mechanical, neurohormonal, or metabolic stress; however, it can progress to fibrosis, contractile dysfunction, arrhythmia, and heart failure. Ferroptosis is a type of regulated cell death caused by iron-dependent phospholipid peroxidation. Evidence consistent with ferroptosis, such as disrupted iron homeostasis, lipid peroxidation, mitochondrial dysfunction and impaired antioxidant defense, has been reported in experimental models of pathological cardiac hypertrophy; however, these findings do not by themselves establish ferroptosis as a cause of hypertrophic remodeling. Astragaloside IV (AS-IV) is a cycloartane-type triterpene saponin from Astragalus species that has shown anti-hypertrophic, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, metabolic-regulatory and mitochondrial-protective effects in experimental cardiovascular models. AS-IV has also shown anti-ferroptotic effects in several cardiac and extra-cardiac disease models by means of Nrf2-centred antioxidant defense, regulation of SLC7A11/GPX4, p53 signaling, CD36-dependent lipid handling, and 14-3-3η-linked regulation of GPX4 stability. Nevertheless, whether ferroptosis inhibition directly contributes to the anti-hypertrophic effect of AS-IV in pathological cardiac hypertrophy remains unproven because direct causal validation in dedicated hypertrophy models is lacking. This review collects evidence on the biology of ferroptosis in pathological cardiac hypertrophy, the established anti-hypertrophic pharmacology of AS-IV, its reported anti-ferroptotic effects, and relevant pharmacokinetic considerations. Based on this, we propose that AS-IV may reduce the susceptibility of cardiomyocytes to ferroptosis and thus partially inhibit pathological cardiac remodeling; however, this is not yet a proven mechanism. Direct verification requires etiologically distinct hypertrophy models, multi-modal ferroptosis measurements, targeted genetic or pharmacological disruption, dose-response and pharmacokinetic experiments, and cell-type-resolved analysis.

title: The Impact of Anaesthesia Method on the Use of Anaesthesia Department Resources in Total Knee Arthroplasty.
authorString: Lahtinen K, Reponen E, Skants N.
abstractText:
Background

Spinal and general anaesthesia seem to lead to similar health-related outcomes in total knee arthroplasty. However, to produce economically and environmentally sustainable health care, we should also consider other factors. Current guidelines recommend preferring regional anaesthesia and total intravenous anaesthesia to reduce environmental impact. In this study, we analysed time, costs, and disposable materials associated with spinal anaesthesia and total intravenous anaesthesia during total knee arthroplasty.

Methods

A total of 395 patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty were randomised to spinal or general anaesthesia. Outcomes were total operating room time, non-operative operating room time, post-anaesthesia care unit time, use of drugs affecting haemodynamics, and the need for arterial cannulation and urinary catheterisation. In addition, we evaluated the financial costs and waste produced by single-use equipment and medicines in both anaesthesia methods.

Results

Anaesthesia method did not affect operating room time (median 152 min [interquartile range 136-168 min] vs. 150 min [137-165 min], Hodges-Lehmann estimate 2 min [95% CI -3 to 6 min], p = 0.49). However, after spinal anaesthesia, patients appeared to spend more time in the postanaesthesia care unit than after general anaesthesia (median 104 min [71-148 min] vs. 73 min [49-98 min], Hodges-Lehmann estimate 32 min [95% CI 23-42 min], p < 0.001). Medication for hypotension was more common in the general anaesthesia group, whereas medication for hypertension was more common in the spinal anaesthesia group. General anaesthesia generated more disposable material (1252 vs. 611 g), and both medicine and equipment expenses were higher (total costs €83 vs. €36).

Conclusion

With this anaesthesia regimen, knee arthroplasty patients occupied the operating room for a similar duration regardless of anaesthesia method, but patients required longer recovery in the postanaesthesia care unit after spinal anaesthesia. Regarding disposable material and medicine use, spinal anaesthesia appeared to be more economical and material-sparing than total intravenous anaesthesia. Furthermore, spinal anaesthesia appeared to cause less hypotension requiring haemodynamic interventions than general anaesthesia.

Editorial comment

This health-economic analysis estimates for how different aspects of general or spinal anaesthesia care contribute to process flow and item costs. Findings suggest that there may be measurably more costs associated with one of the anaesthesia type choices compared with the other, though this will depend on choices for materials and more.

Trial registration

EudraCT (2016-002035-15).

title: Evaluating Darbepoetin Treatment Strategies for Managing Anaemia in Haemodialysis Patients: Effects on All-Cause Mortality From a Target Trial Emulation Using Electronic Health Record Data.
authorString: Birnie K, Caskey FJ, Ben-Shlomo Y, Nitsch D, Casula A, Murray EJ, Sterne JAC.
abstractText:
Purpose

Anaemia is a common complication of chronic kidney disease, often treated with erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs), but the optimal haemoglobin (Hb) target remains uncertain. Using electronic health records, we emulated a target trial comparing different Hb targets in haemodialysis patients to estimate their effects on mortality.

Methods

We used electronic health records from UK kidney centres reporting to the UK Renal Registry. Adults aged ≥ 18 years, receiving haemodialysis for ≥ 3 months, and without marked ESA resistance were eligible. Using the clone-censor-weight method, we emulated trials comparing Hb targets: (1) 105-125 versus 95-115 g/L and (2) 125-145 versus 95-115 g/L. Darbepoetin dosing followed a standardised protocol with predefined dose adjustments and a maximum dose of 150 μg/week. The outcome was all-cause mortality over 8 months.

Results

The study included 8628 patients from 10 centres between 2004 and 2016; 62% male, median age 66 years (IQR 52-76). At baseline, mean Hb was 97.7 g/L (SD 15.1), and 79% of patients were receiving darbepoetin. The hazard ratio for mortality was 0.92 (95% CI 0.75-1.12) for the 105-125 versus 95-115 g/L comparison, and 1.20 (95% CI 0.94-1.54) for the 125-145 versus 95-115 g/L comparison. Adherence to the highest Hb target was lower, limiting precision.

Conclusions

Targeting an Hb range of 105-125 g/L under controlled ESA dosing was not associated with increased mortality compared with 95-115 g/L. Targeting Hb levels above 125 g/L may increase mortality risk, consistent with previous trial findings.

title: Active Helicobacter pylori Infection and Atrial Fibrillation in Patients Hospitalized With Acute Myocardial Infarction.
authorString: Hashem M, Sundqvist MO, Wärme J, Bäck M, Hofmann R.

journal.title: Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc

abstractText:
Objective

Chronic Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection may promote systemic inflammation and has been proposed as a contributor to atrial fibrillation (AF), but clinical evidence is inconsistent. The aim of the study was to explore whether active H. pylori infection was associated with AF in patients hospitalized with acute myocardial infarction (AMI).

Methods

This cross-sectional analysis included adults from a two-center observational AMI cohort. Active H. pylori infection was assessed during hospitalization using a urea breath test (UBT). AF was defined as AF documented before admission or identified during the index hospitalization. Associations were estimated using logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, center, and smoking. Exploratory multivariable interaction analyses were also performed.

Results

Of 310 enrolled patients, 300 had conclusive H. pylori screening results; 60 (20.0%) were positive. AF was recorded in 4 of 60 H. pylori-positive patients (6.7%) and 30 of 240 H. pylori-negative patients (12.5%). H. pylori positivity was not significantly associated with recorded AF (unadjusted OR, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.17-1.41; p = 0.228; adjusted OR, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.16-1.46; p = 0.235). These estimates refer to pooled AF; only four AF cases occurred among patients testing positive.

Conclusions

No statistically significant association was detected between H. pylori breath-test positivity and pooled documented AF among patients hospitalized with AMI, but a clinically meaningful association cannot be excluded. Larger prospective studies with longitudinal follow-up are needed to clarify whether active H. pylori infection is associated with incident AF after AMI.

title: Longitudinal Modeling of Cardiometabolic Dysfunction in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Using Item Response Theory.
authorString: Yu C, Kunina H, Wellhagen GJ, Kjellsson MC.
abstractText: Cardiometabolic dysfunction in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) is reflected by multiple risk factors and cannot be fully characterized by any single biomarker. Item response theory (IRT) provides a framework for integrating observed risk factors into latent measures of underlying cardiometabolic dysfunction. Routinely collected measurements of systolic and diastolic blood pressure (sBP and dBP), high- and low-density lipoproteins (HDL and LDL), triglycerides (TG), HbA1c, and BMI from 33,396 adults newly diagnosed with T2D were analyzed, with biomarkers categorized into four ordered levels. A two-dimensional model described the data better than a unidimensional, identifying a blood pressure-related latent variable ( ψ <sub>1</sub>) primarily informed by sBP and dBP, and a metabolic latent variable ( ψ <sub>2</sub>) primarily informed by HDL, HbA1c, TG, and BMI, while LDL showed low discrimination on both dimensions. At baseline, age at T2D diagnosis was associated with both latent variables, with opposing effects of 0.02 for ψ <sub>1</sub> and -0.07 for ψ <sub>2</sub>. Sex was associated with ψ <sub>2</sub>, with women scoring 0.43 units lower than men on the latent variable scale. Longitudinally, ψ <sub>1</sub> and ψ <sub>2</sub> showed post-baseline offsets of -0.10 and -0.22, respectively, followed by separately estimated annual slopes of approximately -0.03 year<sup>-1</sup>. HbA1c exhibited a distinct trajectory with an initial post-baseline improvement followed by deterioration, requiring an item-specific slope of 0.45 year<sup>-1</sup>. The ψ <sub>2</sub> contributed modest additional information for all-cause mortality beyond age and sex. This framework integrated routinely collected biomarkers into continuous latent measures of multidimensional cardiometabolic dysfunction while accounting for differences in their contributions to the latent dimensions.

title: Metabolic gatekeepers shape immune cell function in rheumatoid arthritis.
authorString: Jia L, Kothagundla MN, Goronzy JJ, Weyand CM.
abstractText: Immune cell function is tightly coupled to cellular metabolism, with glycolysis, oxidative phosphorylation, and amino acid and lipid metabolism governing activation, differentiation, survival, and effector responses. In rheumatoid arthritis (RA), an autoimmune disease characterized by destructive joint inflammation, metabolic checkpoints have emerged as critical regulators of immune-cell behavior and drivers of tissue pathology. RA CD4+ T cells undergo profound metabolic reprogramming: glycolysis is suppressed, and glucose is redirected into the pentose phosphate pathway, resulting in NADPH accumulation, reduced ROS levels, and a highly reductive intracellular environment. Concurrent defects in mitochondrial DNA repair and electron transport chain function compromise mitochondrial fitness, leading to NAD+ depletion, altered tricarboxylic acid cycle activity, and metabolic exhaustion. The resulting accumulation of citrate and acetyl-CoA promotes lipogenesis and protein acetylation, driving membrane remodeling, tissue invasiveness, and proinflammatory effector functions. Depletion of oxaloacetate and aspartate limits NAD+ regeneration, inducing endoplasmic reticulum expansion and enhanced tumor necrosis factor production. Defective lysosomal coordination of AMPK and mTORC1 signaling uncouples energy sensing from anabolic programs, enabling cellular activation and proliferation despite metabolic insufficiency. Macrophage fate and function are similarly shaped by metabolic state. In synovial macrophages, GLUD1-dependent glutamine oxidation sustains mitochondrial respiration and ATP production, enabling survival under nutrient-deprived conditions while promoting antigen presentation. Conversely, metabolic stress in MerTK+ macrophages activates the NAD+ hydrolase SARM1, triggering NAD+ depletion, mitochondrial collapse, and PANoptotic cell death. Together, these findings identify NAD+ availability, mitochondrial fitness, and organelle-based signaling as central metabolic gatekeepers linking bioenergetic stress to immune-cell dysfunction and chronic inflammation in RA.

title: Pharmacological Modulation of Catecholaminergic Brain Injury by Dapagliflozin and Its Nanovesicular Formulation in an Isoproterenol Model.
authorString: Bhat FA, Haque SE, Aqil M, Akhtar M, Najmi AK.

journal.title: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

abstractText: Sustained β-adrenergic stimulation represents a pharmacologically relevant stressor capable of inducing systemic oxidative and inflammatory injury that extends to the central nervous system. Isoproterenol (ISO), a synthetic catecholamine, is widely used to model catecholaminergic injury in experimental settings. Dapagliflozin, a sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor, exhibits pleiotropic antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties; however, its effects on catecholamine-induced brain injury remain poorly defined. In the present study, we investigated the pharmacological effects of dapagliflozin and a bile salt-stabilized dapagliflozin-loaded nanovesicular formulation in an ISO-induced model of catecholaminergic brain injury in rats. ISO administration resulted in marked oxidative imbalance, neuroinflammatory activation, behavioral dysfunction, and structural alterations in hippocampal and cortical regions. These changes were accompanied by reduced expression of stress-responsive and neurotrophic proteins, including SIRT6, TRAP1, and BDNF, along with enhanced astroglial activation as indicated by increased GFAP immunoreactivity. Treatment with dapagliflozin attenuated these molecular, cellular, and functional alterations, while the nanovesicular formulation produced a more pronounced improvement of redox balance, suppression of inflammatory responses, normalization of protein expression, and preservation of neuronal architecture and behavior. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that dapagliflozin mitigates catecholaminergic brain injury through attenuation of oxidative and inflammatory stress, with enhanced efficacy achieved via formulation-assisted drug delivery, without implying a distinct pharmacodynamic mechanism.

title: Chamber-Specific Morphometry and Quantitative Cardiac Histology in the Broad-Snouted Caiman (Caiman latirostris).
authorString: Nascimento MEN, Maggio GN, Almeida MB, Vasconcelos CRS, Brito VJDSC, Oriá AP, Dias FGG, Rodrigues MA.
abstractText: Quantitative cardiac morphology remains poorly documented in crocodilians. Hearts from four commercially reared male Caiman latirostris were examined by gross morphometry, histology, stereology, reticulin staining and Masson's trichrome. Relative heart mass averaged 0.125% of body mass. The left ventricular wall was numerically thicker than the right. Cardiomyocyte volume density and cross-sectional area varied among chambers, whereas collagen-positive area was greater in the right ventricle. Pulmonary arterial walls were markedly thinner than the systemic aortae, and the left pulmonary arterial wall was thicker than the right. These findings extend quantitative cardiac reference data for this species.

title: Female Representation and Quality Indicators in Anesthesiology and Critical Care Podcasts.
authorString: Steinsdóttir P, Asif S, Kristinsdóttir RN, Rosenström A, Niklasson A, Dietz N, Fåhraeus SÅ, Hylander J, Bjurström MF.
abstractText:
Background

Podcasts have emerged as prominent tools for asynchronous medical education, widely adopted across training levels and specialties. Diverse representation strengthens medical discourse, making an evaluation of speaker demographics essential for understanding equity and quality in digital knowledge dissemination. This study systematically evaluates female representation and quality assurance indicators in anesthesiology and critical care podcasts, including longitudinal publication trends.

Methods

We systematically searched Apple Podcasts and Spotify using specialty-specific terms and manually reviewed the top twenty journals in the field for affiliated podcasts. Included were active, English-language, physician-hosted podcasts.

Results

Eighty-five podcasts (53.0% US-based) comprising 10,190 episodes were analyzed. Of 12,522 hosts, 31.5% (n = 3945) were female; of 10,822 guests, 35.9% (n = 3882) were female. Notably, among US-based podcasts, female guest representation exceeded the 26.5% female workforce proportion among US anesthesiologists. Episodes with exclusively male hosts had 2.13 times the odds of featuring only male guests (95% CI 1.88-2.41). A positive trend of increasing female participation was observed from 2010 to 2024. Content support was variable: using broad, inclusive definitions, 42.0% of episodes had show notes and 48.4% provided supplemental material. Analysis of quality-related structures showed that 40.0% (n = 34) of podcasts produced episodes linked to a publication, 50.6% featured some episodes with three or more speakers, 21.2% of podcasts were journal-affiliated, and 20.0% were university-affiliated.

Conclusion

While a sex imbalance persists in anesthesiology and critical care podcasting, female participation among US-based podcasts exceeds local workforce demographic benchmarks, with a clear positive trend from 2010 to 2024. However, persistent sex similarity in speaker selection suggests ongoing biases. Quality assurance mechanisms remain highly variable, highlighting opportunities for incremental improvement. Future efforts could focus on structured guest selection and transparent quality indicators to accelerate progress toward equitable representation and educational quality in this influential medium.

Editorial comment

In modern times, many clinicians look for, and listen to, podcasts aimed at education in clinical specialties. This sampling of podcasts related to our specialty looked at how females and males contributed to podcast content generation and dissemination, as a marker for male versus female representation in speakership for continuing specialty education.

title: Drug-Specific Associations of Angiotensin Receptor Blockers With Parkinson's Disease Risk in a Multicenter Electronic Health Record Cohort.
authorString: Tran K, Yang J, Pham S, Luong D, Martin BA, Sasaki S, Hahn J, Luu R, Kim GJ.
abstractText:
Background

Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) have demonstrated neuroprotective effects in preclinical models of Parkinson's disease (PD), but individual ARBs differ in pharmacological properties that may influence their neuroprotective potential.

Objectives

Using large-scale hospital electronic health records of the University of California health system, we tested whether specific ARBs are associated with lower PD risk.

Methods

We conducted a new-user, active-comparator cohort study in the University of California Health Data Warehouse, encompassing 890 712 hypertensive patients across six academic medical centers from 2012 to 2025. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios for individual ARB associations with incident PD, adjusting for demographics, nine preindex comorbidities, and index date. Robustness was assessed through propensity score matching and negative-control analysis.

Results

Drug-specific Cox analysis identified irbesartan (HR = 0.588, 95% CI 0.434 to 0.796, p = 0.0006) and olmesartan (HR = 0.797, 95% CI 0.665 to 0.956, p = 0.015) as associated with lower PD risk. Irbesartan survived Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons, and propensity score matching supported both associations.

Conclusion

In this large multicenter EHR cohort, irbesartan and olmesartan were associated with lower incident Parkinson's disease risk. These findings support further investigation of the renin-angiotensin system as a therapeutic target in Parkinson's disease and may inform the development or repurposing of agents with favorable central nervous system penetration and neuroprotective potential.

title: Hemodynamic effects of ventilating or not, during cardiopulmonary bypass in a porcine model.
authorString: Kvalheim VL, Mongstad A, Husby P, Stangeland L, Nginamau ES, Osman TA, Yamada S, Grong K, Svendsen ØS.
abstractText: Background. Optimal ventilator setting during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) is unknown. Improved gas exchange and lung compliance have been suggested as favourable outcomes when lungs are ventilated. However, long-time effects have been hard to demonstrate. There has been less focus on the immediate circulatory effects of ventilator settings during cardioplegia and CPB, and potentially hemodynamic effects of different ventilator strategies are unknown. Methods. Sixteen anesthetized pigs on normothermic CPB with 80 min of aortic cross-clamp and cardioplegic arrest were randomized to a ventilated and a not ventilated group. After weaning, both cardiac-, hemodynamic-, and pulmonary functions were evaluated for up to 120 min. Results. Left ventricular variables and cardiac output did not differ between the two study groups, neither before nor after weaning. After weaning, mean pulmonary artery pressure was increased in ventilated compared to not ventilated animals. Neither pulmonary compliance nor oxygen uptake differed between groups in surviving animals. Conclusions. Disconnection of the ventilator during CPB and cardiac arrest did not affect lung compliance and oxygen uptake, neither positively nor negatively. In the ventilated group, a temporary increase in the pulmonary pressure after weaning was observed.

title: Use of vaginal estrogens in urogynecology: current evidence, controversies and clinical applications.
authorString: Singh P, Pancholy J, Pancholy A.
abstractText: Genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) is a prevalent yet underrecognized condition in postmenopausal women, characterized by progressive vulvovaginal and lower urinary tract symptoms from estrogen deficiency. Vaginal estrogen therapy is the first-line pharmacologic treatment for GSM. However, as new evidence emerges, understanding of its efficacy, safety, and use in special populations continues to evolve. This review summarizes current evidence on vaginal estrogen formulations, clinical effectiveness, safety, and therapeutic applications. Recent randomized controlled trials confirm that low-dose vaginal estrogen significantly improves GSM symptoms - including vaginal dryness, dyspareunia, and irritation - while restoring epithelial integrity and normalizing pH. Evidence also supports its role in reducing recurrent urinary tract infections by restoring lactobacilli-dominant flora, reinforced by a 2025 multisociety clinical guideline recommending topical, but not systemic, estrogen for this indication. Comparative studies show similar efficacy across creams, tablets, inserts, and rings, differing primarily in convenience and absorption rather than effectiveness. Large cohort studies indicate no increased risk of cardiovascular disease, venous thromboembolism, or malignancy. Use in breast cancer survivors remains controversial, but emerging data suggest minimal systemic absorption and no clear increase in recurrence risk, supporting shared decision-making. In addition, long-term outcomes show that adjunctive vaginal estrogen does not improve anatomic surgical success after native tissue apical prolapse repair. Nonhormonal therapies and agents like ospemifene or prasterone offer alternative options, though they demonstrate lower or more variable efficacy than vaginal estrogen. Vaginal estrogen therapy is the most effective, evidence-based treatment for GSM and helps prevent recurrent urinary tract infections in postmenopausal women. Its favorable safety profile and multiple formulations enable individualized care. Recent evidence clarifies that while overall safety is reassuring, caution is necessary for breast cancer survivors using aromatase inhibitors. Additionally, longer-term perioperative trial data temper expectations regarding surgical-recurrence benefits, while confirming its value for local tissue optimization. Ongoing research should focus on long-term safety in high-risk groups and the effectiveness of emerging non-estrogen alternatives.

title: CCTP-Atlas: Compartment-Resolved Ciliary Transcriptional Dysregulation in Tetralogy of Fallot — A Six-Dataset Integrative Meta-Analysis
authorString: Tahir R, Javed T, Bin Rasheed MM, Aslam Q, Afsheen N.
abstractText:
Background

Primary cilia coordinate Hedgehog-dependent outflow tract morphogenesis. Concurrent human genetics implicates ciliary loss-of-function in nonsyndromic tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) risk, yet compartment-resolved ciliary transcriptional programmes in public TOF snRNA-seq remain unmapped at module resolution.

Methods

We curated a Cardiac Ciliary Transcriptomic Panel (CCTP; 1,611 genes; four modules) and executed a ten-phase integrative pipeline on six public sc/snRNA-seq resources. Differentially expressed gene tables were harmonised (adjusted p < 0.05; |log2FC| ≥ 0.5 where available), mapped to CCTP modules, and tiered by evidence strength. Patient-level pseudobulk (three TOF versus five donors), permutation-validated Compartment Dysregulation Index (CMDI), Cross-Species Concordance Score (CSCS), STRING protein–protein interaction analysis, and diffusion pseudotime on 17,290 Ho organoid cells were performed.

Results

Among 1,263 unique CCTP-associated hits, 396 genes recurred in at least two dataset tables (exploratory tier; Tier A endothelial anchor n = 24 from Zulibiya et al.). Only Zulibiya endothelial M1 structural-assembly CMDI exceeded a module-size-matched permutation null (p = 0.015). Patient-level pseudobulk returned zero false-discovery-rate-significant CCTP genes. CCTP-conditioned overlap with recent ciliary genetics was non-significant (Fisher p ≈ 0.13). Ho organoid pseudotime showed highest M1/M2 activity at day 8, declining toward day 21. Genome-wide CSCS classified 11 genes as fully conserved and 136 as partially conserved among scoreable orthologs.

Conclusions

Ciliary transcriptional correlates in TOF are compartment-specific and module-structured, with the strongest inferential signal in TOF endothelium (M1). CCTP-Atlas provides a reproducible, tiered prioritisation resource linking public TOF snRNA-seq, organoid maturation proxies, and partial cross-species patterns. Findings are hypothesis-generating and complement—but do not replicate—recent ciliary genetics evidence until expanded cohorts and functional validation are performed.

Data availability

Processed gene lists, manifests, and scripts: Zenodo deposit [DOI to be inserted after upload; see submission checklist]. Source datasets: GSE203274, GSE168464, GSE166462, GSE126128; Li et al. (2025) supplementary tables. This is a preprint and has not been peer-reviewed.
