title: Umbilical Cord Hernia is Not an Isolated Pathology: High Rate of Associated Anomalies in a Tertiary Center Cohort
authorString: YILDIZ M, YILMAZ Y, ERTEN EE, AZILI MN, SENEL E.
abstractText: Purpose This study aimed to evaluate the clinical profile of umbilical cord hernia (UCH), a defect often considered a minor variant of omphalocele, with a specific focus on the prevalence and spectrum of associated congenital anomalies. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 45 neonates with anterior abdominal wall defects treated between August 2019 and July 2024. Patients were categorized into three groups: omphalocele (n = 15), gastroschisis (n = 19), and UCH (n = 11). Demographic data, prenatal diagnosis, associated anomalies, surgical management, and outcomes were analyzed. Results In the UCH group, six patients (54.5%) had at least one major associated anomaly. Major cardiac anomalies were present in 45.5% (5/11), chromosomal anomalies in 27.3% (3/11), and genitourinary anomalies in 36.4% (4/11) of patients. The spectrum included Tetralogy of Fallot, Trisomy 13, 18, 21, and genetic syndromes (e.g., 3MC syndrome). Four patients (36.4%) had isolated UCH. Mortality in the UCH group was 18.2%, exclusively occurring in patients with major associated anomalies. Conclusion Contrary to traditional belief, umbilical cord hernia is frequently associated with serious cardiac, chromosomal, and multisystemic anomalies. These findings necessitate a paradigm shift in management, advocating for comprehensive screening including echocardiography, renal ultrasound, and genetic evaluation in all neonates with UCH, similar to the standard for omphalocele.

title: When tiny lungs Struggle to breathe; a rare cause of Refractory Primary Pulmonary Hypertension
authorString: Sivakumar M, Philip DC, Bukelo MF.
abstractText: Alveolar capillary dysplasia with malpositioned pulmonary veins (ACD/MPV) is a lethal congenital lung disorder with a mortality rate of almost 100%. Infants deteriorate within the first 24 hours of life. Here, we present a 2-day old female child born of full term normal vaginal delivery and cried immediately after birth. The baby presented with Respiratory distress within 6 hours of life and was put on extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. 2-D echo revealed no congenital heart disease. The child continued to have pulmonary hypertension non-responsive to pharmacotherapy and eventually passed away. A post mortem histopathology examination revealed immature lung parenchyma with arrest in the saccular phase, thickened alveolar septae with abnormally positioned pulmonary capillaries. Focally, there were thin-walled vessels invested in the same adventitial sheath as the pulmonary arteries. The pulmonary arterioles exhibited features of pulmonary artery hypertension. Based on this constellation of features, the baby was diagnosed with ACD/MPV. The rarity and the focal nature of this condition make it a diagnostic challenge in terms of awareness of this entity and subsequent interpretation. Conclusion : This case reiterates the importance of knowing and understanding normal histology. A high degree of clinical suspicion as well as expertise in the field of thoracic pathology is required for appropriate diagnosis.

title: Impact of prolonged balloon inflation on valve expansion and early clinical outcomes following contemporary balloon-expandable transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
authorString: Cardaioli F, Fovino LN, Fabris T, Masiero G, Panza A, Napodano M, Fraccaro C, Putortì F, Tarantini G.

journal.title: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstractText:
Background

Incomplete expansion of balloon-expandable (BE) transcatheter heart valves (THVs) after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) may affect valve performance and durability. Routine THV post-dilatation (the "double-tap" technique) has been proposed to optimise device expansion; however, it may increase procedural complexity.

Aims

We sought to evaluate the impact of a prolonged balloon inflation implantation strategy on BE THV expansion, haemodynamic performance, and early clinical outcomes.

Methods

This single-centre study analysed consecutive TAVI patients treated for native tricuspid aortic stenosis with the SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA THV using a prolonged balloon inflation strategy (8 seconds). Valve expansion was assessed by fluoroscopy at multiple frame levels and compared with three validated reference standards. Results were also descriptively compared with previously published data on the double-tap technique. Clinical and haemodynamic outcomes at 30 days were adjudicated according to Valve Academic Research Consortium 3 criteria.

Results

A total of 84 patients (mean age 78.8 years, 58% male, median Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score 3.9%) were included. Prolonged inflation resulted in complete THV expansion at the inflow and outflow levels, with only mild underexpansion (98.5±1.3%) detected at the midframe level when manufacturer-defined nominal values were used as the reference. When compared with previously published data on the double-tap technique, expansion values for the 23, 26, and 29 mm valves were consistently similar or higher, whereas lower expansion was observed for the 20 mm size. Device success was achieved in all cases, with no stroke at 30 days. Permanent pacemaker implantation occurred in 6% of patients. Haemodynamic performance was favourable (mean gradient 9.2 [interquartile range 7.0-10.3] mmHg at 30 days), with no patients having moderate or severe paravalvular leak.

Conclusions

Prolonged balloon inflation during BE THV deployment is associated with favourable valve expansion, haemodynamic results, and a favourable safety profile, consistent with values reported in double-tap series. If confirmed in larger studies, this strategy may represent a simple alternative to routine double-tap in selected patients.

title: Role of the lipolysis stimulated lipoprotein receptor LSR in the regulation of macrophage lipid homeostasis and metabolic activity
authorString: Vanotti G, Kleinberg N, Louis H, Maskali F, Bäck M, Mercier N, Yen FT.
abstractText: In atherosclerosis, monocyte-derived macrophages in the subendothelial space of the arterial wall, become lipid-laden and pro-inflammatory. Macrophages depend on lipoprotein receptors to regulate lipid influx, thereby shaping macrophage metabolic state and potentially dictating their phenotype. The lipolysis stimulated lipoprotein receptor, LSR, contributes to lipid homeostasis and was detected by immunofluorescence in aortic atherosclerotic plaques from ApoE-/- mice and by immunoblot in macrophages. The aim was to determine LSR’s role in macrophage lipid handling by studying LSR expression and activity before (M0) or after polarization of Raw 264.7 cells using LPS/IFNγ (M1) or IL-4/IL-13 (M2), respectively. LSR mRNA (0.48-fold, p < 0.001), protein levels (0.28-fold, p < 0.001) were significantly lower in M1 (iNOS+/MCP1+) as compared to M2 (CD206+/Arg1+) macrophages. LSR activity, measured as oleate-induced uptake of DiI-labelled LDL, was significantly lower in M1 as compared to M2 macrophages. siRNA-mediated LSR knockdown (87±4%, p < 0.01) in M0 cells led to significantly decreased expression of genes involved in lipid influx (LDL-R, LRP1) and transport (ABCA1), increased basal glycolysis and decreased glycolytic reserve, but without changes in inflammatory markers. Raw 264.7 macrophages transformation into foam cells by 24h incubation with oxidized LDL also led to reduced LSR activity and expression. We propose that the lower LSR expression and activity observed in M1 and foam cell macrophages contribute to reduced lipid influx and increased glycolytic state that is associated with pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype. This provides new insight towards understanding how these immune cells depend on lipoprotein receptors regulating their metabolic uptake.

title: The NT-proBNP/hs-cTnT Ratio Identifies Distinct Hemodynamic Phenotypes in Wild-type Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis: a multicenter Italian study
authorString: Bellini F, Lisi DD, Nardi E, Gagliardo CM, Gesaro GD, Giammanco A, Teresi L, Macaione F, Colarusso L, Licordari R, Cefalù AB, Bella GD, Novo G, Noto D.
abstractText: Background Wild-type transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTRwt-CA) is a progressive pseudo-hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and an increasingly recognized cause of heart failure in elderly patients. Methods Seventy patients with confirmed ATTRwt-CA from three Italian tertiary centers were included in this hypothesis-generating analysis. Per-patient median values across available visits were used to define phenotypic profiles. Patients were stratified into tertiles of the NT-proBNP/hs-cTnT ratio, and group differences were assessed using age-, sex-, NT-proBNP-, and hs-cTnT-adjusted models. Results Median age was 80.5 years (IQR 76.5–85.0), and 88% were male. Ratio tertiles were < 29.9 (T1), 29.9–51.0 (T2), and > 51.0 (T3). hs-cTnT was similar across tertiles (p = 0.639), whereas NT-proBNP progressively increased (1258, 4301, 7118 pg/mL; p < 0.001). T1 showed preserved ejection fraction, better renal function, and lower atrial fibrillation prevalence. T2 displayed reduced renal function and markedly higher atrial fibrillation and device implantation prevalence. T3 showed reduced ejection fraction, impaired longitudinal strain, right ventricular dysfunction, and the lowest eGFR. Conclusions The NT-proBNP/hs-cTnT ratio identifies three distinct ATTRwt-CA phenotypes. Prospective validation in larger cohorts is warranted.

title: Seven Novel Sonographic Signs
authorString: Ji X.
abstractText: Ultrasound is a widely used imaging modality in clinical practice, and sonographic signs serve as valuable teaching tools that aid in pattern recognition and diagnosis. This review consolidates five novel sonographic signs previously proposed by the author, including the Cracked Earth Sign for subcutaneous edema, the Mushroom Cap Sign for localized gallbladder adenomyomatosis, the LTS Sign for dilated cardiomyopathy, the LTI Sign for endocardial fibroelastosis, and the Three Pipes Sign for the suprasternal long-axis view of the aortic arch. The SFH Sign for advanced cervical insufficiency and the Gentle Wave Sign for the tardus-parvus waveform are proposed for the first time in this paper. Collectively, these seven signs span the fields of superficial ultrasound, abdominal ultrasound, echocardiography, and obstetric ultrasound. For each sign, its naming logic, definition, clinical implications, and teaching value are described. This review aims to facilitate a better understanding of these signs and to promote their use as teaching aids in ultrasound education.

title: Functional fine-mapping of the 9p21.3 cardiovascular disease locus implicates the lncRNA MIR31HG as an effector transcript in endothelial cells
authorString: Zhigulev A, Poujade F, Gryzunov N, Buyan A, Li H, Bergman O, Liu M, Pradhananga S, Franco-Cereceda A, Swoboda P, Kulakovskiy IV, Eriksson P, Sahlén P, Björck HM.
abstractText:
BACKGROUND

The chromosome 9p21.3 locus is among the strongest genetic risk loci for cardiovascular disease (CVD), yet the regulatory mechanisms underlying this association remain poorly understood. Previous vascular disease studies focused predominantly on the role of this locus in smooth muscle cell (SMC) dysfunction, whereas its potential role in endothelial cells (ECs) remains less well characterized. Here, we sought to identify candidate regulatory variants at 9p21.3, their distal target genes, and effector transcripts that contribute to CVD-related phenotypes in ECs.

METHODS

Promoter capture Hi-C was used to map chromatin interactions at 9p21.3 in primary human ascending aortic SMCs (n=6), supplementing the previously obtained ECs (n=16) dataset. To support the regulatory relevance of these interactions, expression quantitative trait locus analysis was performed in 136 vascular biopsies. Variant effects were prioritized in silico using AlphaGenome. The regulatory activity of the prioritized region was validated using CRISPR activation.

RESULTS

Chromatin interaction mapping identified a complex regulatory architecture at the 9p21.3 locus involving 19 putative regulatory elements and 15 genes across ECs and SMCs. MIR31HG showed the most recurrent distal promoter connectivity with the 9p21.3 region. Consistent with the chromatin interaction map, expression of MIR31HG transcripts was associated with genetic variation at the 9p21.3 locus. In ECs, the lncRNA MIR31HG, but not miR-31, was responsive to hemodynamic flow. Depletion of MIR31HG in ECs was associated with endothelial activation. Epigenetic tracks and deep learning predictions highlighted an active enhancer element at 9p21.3, which was subsequently validated by CRISPR activation and increased MIR31HG expression, confirming its capacity to regulate MIR31HG over a large genomic distance of approximately 538 kb.

CONCLUSIONS

Altogether, these data implicate lncRNA MIR31HG as a likely effector of the 9p21.3 CVD locus, linking the cis-regulatory element and heritable genetic variation in the respective region to endothelial activation through long-range enhancer regulation.

Clinical Perspective

What Is New? Promoter capture Hi-C in primary human vascular cells identified recurrent long-range interactions between the 9p21.3 cardiovascular disease locus and the MIR31HG promoter, extending the regulatory landscape beyond the nearest genes. Expression of MIR31HG transcripts was associated with 9p21.3 genetic variation in vascular tissue; the lncRNA MIR31HG was responsive to hemodynamic flow in endothelial cells and influenced the endothelial activation transcriptional programs upon depletion. Integrated sequence-based, epigenomic, genetic, and CRISPR activation analyses nominated the 9p21.3 enhancer as a regulator of MIR31HG in endothelial cells. What Are the Clinical Implications? The findings suggest that the cardiovascular disease associations of 9p21.3 may involve stronger than previously anticipated endothelial regulatory mechanisms in addition to characterized effects in other vascular cell types. lncRNA MIR31HG provides a molecular link between noncoding genetic variation at 9p21.3 and endothelial cell-state regulation relevant to vascular disease.

title: Activation of perivascular thermogenic fat improves aortic stenosis
authorString: Hildebrand S, Wunderling K, Siwik-Róg Z, Schmidt A, Barrero JA, Gómez-Banoy N, Reverte-Salisa L, Freyter B, Zimmer S, Nickenig G, Cohen P, Pfeifer A.
abstractText:
Aim

Aortic stenosis (AS) is a common condition with exponential increases in incidence in aging populations. Perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) forms the outer layer of the aortic wall and has – especially in the thoracic area – characteristics of thermogenic adipose tissue, which dissipates energy and releases endocrine factors. Here, we set out to investigate the role of thermogenic PVAT in AS.

Methods and results

We studied the role of (PVAT) in the development of AS in a murine model of AS. To specifically delineate the role of PVAT activity in AS, we used a pharmacological β3-adrenergic agonist as well as cold exposure in combination with a genetic mouse model with deficient PVAT development. To investigate the role of thermogenic adipose tissue in human AS, we used 18 F-FDG PET-CT imaging. We found that pharmacological activation of thermogenic adipose tissue resulted in an improvement of AS, but not in mice genetically deficient in PVAT. Similarly, PVAT was found to be protective against AS during physiological stimulation of PVAT using cold exposure. Mechanistically, PVAT activation resulted in enhanced aortic distensibility and cellular remodeling of the aortic wall, possibly via release of polyunsaturated fatty acids and oxylipins from perivascular adipocytes. Finally, analysis of thermogenic fat activity in humans revealed that mediastinal thermogenic fat activity correlated negatively with diagnostic criteria of AS severity, suggesting an important role for PVAT activity in human AS.

Conclusion

Our data indicate that PVAT activation reduces aortic stenosis and supports aortic remodeling to improve ascending aorta hemodynamics. PVAT activation might be a novel therapeutic target to ameliorate AS progression.

Translational perspective

Currently, there are no effective strategies for treating AS other than valve replacement. Since the molecular mechanisms underlying the disease progression remain unclear, there are no pharmacological agents approved for either treatment or prevention of this disease. Furthermore, AS development cannot currently be predicted and is often only diagnosed when patients develop symptoms, which may be 10-20 years after disease onset. Therefore, identifying novel mechanisms that improve aortic valve function and prevent AS is of high medical need. This study identifies activation of PVAT-dependent aortic remodeling as a potential new therapeutic approach to improve or prevent AS.

title: A 4D Ultrasound Strain Imaging Framework for In Vivo Identification of Anisotropic Properties in Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms: Preliminary Validation against Mechanical Testing of Porcine and Human Tissue
authorString: Hegner A, Wittek A, Derwich W, Schönborn M, Oikonomou K, Huß A, Gámez AJ, Blase C.
abstractText: Abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs) carry a substantial risk of rupture, underscoring the need for accurate biomechanical assessment of the individual patient. We present a computationally efficient method to identify the hyperelastic, anisotropic properties of AAA walls in vivo from non-invasive 4D ultrasound strain imaging, using only two load cases. The identification is posed as an inverse finite element problem, in which patient-specific models of the wall and the intraluminal thrombus (ILT) are iteratively optimized until the simulated deformations under blood pressure loading match the measured ones. Because the ILT geometry is resolved as well, the framework is applicable to the majority of clinical cases. As a proof of concept, the method is subjected to a preliminary validation against mechanical testing of both porcine aortic and human AAA wall tissue. The in vitro case comprised a porcine aorta in a controlled inflation–extension experiment; in vivo, the identification was performed in two AAA patients and compared against tensile tests of their excised wall tissue (n=6 specimens). In vitro, the stress–stretch responses derived from ultrasound and from mechanical testing agreed closely (R²=0.96-0.99). In vivo, agreement was good in one patient and moderate in the other. A complementary sensitivity analysis identified wall thickness and the degree of nonlinear stiffening as the parameters with the strongest influence on the identification. These results demonstrate the feasibility of non-invasive, patient-specific identification of AAA wall properties and represent a major step toward personalized biomechanical modeling and improved clinical risk stratification.

title: Effect of Left Ventricular Assist Device Pulsatility Mode and Cannula Angle on Aortic Blood Flow Characteristics, Blood Renewal Efficiency, Hemolysis, and Platelet Activation
authorString: Sun K, Han Y, Li G, Chen Z.
abstractText: Purpose: This study aimed to investigate the effects of left ventricular assist device (LVAD) pulsatility mode, outflow graft angle, and partial recovery of native cardiac function on aortic hemodynamics, blood renewal, and thrombosis risk. Methods: A patient-specific normal aortic model implanted with an LVAD was established for computational fluid dynamics simulations. Different outflow-graft angles, support modes (continuous and pulsatile flow), and cardiac recovery conditions were investigated. Hemodynamic characteristics were evaluated using wall shear stress-related indices, blood washout behavior, hemolysis, and platelet activation metrics. Results: Outflow-graft angle primarily determined the organization and impingement behavior of the LVAD-induced jet within the ascending aorta. Pulsatile support periodically reconstructed the flow field and alleviated persistent low-velocity regions observed under continuous-flow support, thereby improving blood washout characteristics. Progressive cardiac recovery enhanced large-scale flow mixing between native ventricular ejection and LVAD outflow and improved overall blood transport within the proximal aorta. However, recovery conditions also generated increasingly complex oscillatory flow structures near the aortic root because of intensified dual-source flow interaction. In addition, pulsatile support reduced sustained high-shear exposure and demonstrated lower hemolysis and platelet activation levels compared with continuous-flow conditions. Conclusions: Aortic hemodynamics under LVAD support are governed by the coupled interaction between graft orientation, pulsatile support, and native cardiac recovery. Different support conditions exhibit competing effects on blood transport, wall shear distribution, and hemocompatibility. These findings may provide theoretical guidance for individualized LVAD implantation and support optimization.

title: Biomechanical properties of the porcine thoracic aorta: An in- depth analysis of elastic modulus, stress-strain behavior and tissue toughness with regard to anatomical location and loading orientation
authorString: Haunstetter F, Gruetzner F, Berken J, Zerwes S, Gasser TC, Hyhlik-Duerr A, Pyanova A, Westerhausen C.
abstractText: The mechanical integrity of the aortic wall is crucial for its physiological function and susceptibility to vascular pathologies. This study provides a systematic biomechanical characterization of the porcine aorta, focusing on regional and orientation-dependent variations in stiffness, strength, and tissue toughness. A total of 480 specimens from ten porcine aortas were obtained from defined anatomical regions and subjected to uniaxial tensile testing in circumferential and longitudinal orientations. No significant differences were found regarding specimen position (anterior, posterior, left, right), whereas biomechanical properties varied along the cranial–caudal axis in a parameter- and orientation-dependent manner. The high-strain modulus, and rupture stress in longitudinal specimens, increased towards the distal aorta, with the most pronounced differences occurring between proximal and distal segments. Toughness decreased distally in circumferential specimens but increased in longitudinal specimens. Circumferential specimens exhibited higher stiffness, strength, and toughness at high strains, whereas at low strains longitudinal specimens tended to be stiffer. In longitudinal specimens, the intima consistently ruptured first, followed by the media and adventitia at higher strains; in circumferential specimens, all three layers ruptured simultaneously. These findings demonstrate distinct regional, orientation-, and strain-dependent biomechanical behavior of the porcine aorta and emphasize the importance of anatomical location and loading direction in experimental aortic biomechanics, biomechanical modeling, and the development of vascular devices.

title: A Case of Misidentity: Rare Case of Hidradenocarcinoma of Ear
authorString: Gopalakrishnan D, Zahedi FD.
abstractText: Hidradenocarcinoma is an exceedingly rare and aggressive malignant tumour arising from sweat gland tissue, accounting for less than 0.001% of all tumours. It most commonly affects the head and neck region and typically presents in the fifth to seventh decades of life. We report a 75-year-old Chinese male with underlying diabetes mellitus, hypertension, infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm, and degenerative spine disease, who presented with a five-month history of a progressively enlarging, painless right ear lobule swelling associated with itching and minimal contact bleeding. Examination revealed a 3 × 3 cm broad-based, smooth, exophytic mass over the right ear lobule with surface crusting and bleeding on touch. Excision biopsy was performed under local anaesthesia. Histopathological examination demonstrated an intradermal malignant epithelial tumour composed of pleomorphic polygonal and clear cells with prominent nucleoli, frequent mitoses, tumour necrosis, and a Ki-67 proliferation index of 50–60%. Immunohistochemistry showed positivity for CK5/6 and epithelial membrane antigen (EMA), with negativity for CEA and BerEP4, consistent with hidradenocarcinoma. The patient declined further staging imaging and adjuvant treatment, opting instead for close clinical surveillance. He remains disease-free without evidence of local recurrence or distant metastasis at more than one year following excision. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of hidradenocarcinoma, which may clinically mimic a benign cutaneous lesion, and underscores the importance of histopathological and immunohistochemical evaluation of unusual ear lesions. Given the lack of consensus guidelines, individualised management with complete surgical excision and long-term surveillance remains essential.

title: Successful Renal Artery Stenting in an Infant With Middle Aortic Syndrome: Resolution of Malignant Hypertension and Normalization of Renal Growth   ​
authorString: Wong N, Bratincsak A.
abstractText: Renal artery stenosis (RAS) in infants is rare but often results in severe hypertension and renal failure. Middle aortic syndrome (MAS) is a common etiology of RAS in children. Management remains controversial due to limited evidence defining optimal therapy in infants. Vascular stenting in infants is limited by anatomical and technical challenges. We present a case of renal artery stenting in an infant with MAS. The patient presented neonatally with malignant hypertension and renal hypoperfusion. Progressive right RAS and persistent hypertension required multiple antihypertensive agents. Surgery was initially not feasible because of the patient’s size. At 22 months, the patient underwent successful renal artery stenting followed by balloon dilation. Following intervention, blood pressure normalized, and right kidney growth recovered. This case illustrates that renal artery stenting can result in sustained resolution of hypertension and normalization of renal growth in infants with severe MAS when surgery is not feasible.

title: A randomized controlled trial of a novel AI-based prognostic decision support tool integrated into the electronic health record for ischemic heart disease: Rationale and design of the PM Heart trial.
authorString: Ringgaard AK, Rand SA, Zheng C, Møller MEE, Christensen AH, Riis-Jensen AC, Wimmer B, Høfsten DE, Bundgaard JS, Valder F, Gjødsbøl IM, Gørtz M, Hartlev M, Svendsen MN, Ostrowski SR, Sørensen E, Pedersen OB, Ghouse J, Gustafsson I, Lindholm MG, Salomon SA, Ryde H, Duan H, Therkelsen SK, Soja AMB, Bertelsen MLN, Tønder N, Walichiewicz PM, Lyngbæk S, Sibilitz KL, Pedersen F, Køber L, Iversen KK, Gudbjartsson DF, Holm H, Brunak S, Holm PC, Haue AD, Bundgaard H, (others from Iceland?).
abstractText:
Background

Ischemic heart disease (IHD) is the leading global cause of years of life lost. Although the clinical presentation and progression of IHD differ widely, clinical management is relatively uniform. To improve risk stratification and clinical management, we developed a decision support tool - the PMHeartIHD Algorithm (also named PMHNet) - based on extensive clinical, registry and biochemical data. This algorithm automatically calculates one-year survival following an IHD event. We hypothesize that presenting the prognoses calculated by the PMHeartIHD Algorithm to the treating physicians will improve both the clinical management and outcome of the individual patient.

Objective

The objectives of the PM Heart trial include clinical and technical aspects. First, the primary aim is to investigate if the clinical use of the prognosis calculated by the algorithm improves patient prognosis and minimizes the risk of re-hospitalization, compared to standard of care. A secondary objective is to generate knowledge on how decision support tools in cardiology may be implemented, received, and used directly in clinical practice.

Methods

The PMHeartIHD Aalgorithm has been integrated into the electronic health record (EHR) system (Sundhedsplatformen (SP), EPIC) for clinical use. The PM Heart trial is designed as a multicenter, prospective, randomized, open-label, clinical trial, automatically enrolling and randomizing hospitalized patients with coronary artery disease at the cardiology departments in The Capital Region and Region Zealand in Denmark. Patients are randomized (1:1 ratio) immediately after coronary angiography, to either show or hide the calculated PMHeartIHD-prognosis or not in the electronic health record.

Results

The primary outcome is a composite outcome consisting of re-admissions within 30 days and one-year survival rates after randomization. Inclusion began September 2023, and follow-up is expected to finish in 2026.

Conclusions

We present the design of and rationale for the PM Heart trial. Our aim is to assess the clinical value of implementing an artificial intelligence-based decision support tool in clinical practice.

title: Sustained improvement in sickle cell cardiomyopathy after haematopoietic stem cell transplantation is superior to that with disease-modifying therapy.
authorString: Rai P, Selukar S, Bi Y, Chen S, Merlocco A, Morin CE, Goode C, Towbin JA, Rushing M, Rebolledo MA, Joshi V, Leonard A, Hankins JS, Manwani D, Takemoto CM, Gottschalk S, Triplett B, Johnson JN, Sharma A.
abstractText: Allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is curative for sickle cell disease (SCD) - a group of inherited haemoglobin disorders encompassing homozygous haemoglobin S (HbSS) and compound heterozygous sickling disorders, including haemoglobin SC disease (HbSC), haemoglobin S/β<sup>0</sup>-thalassaemia (HbSβ<sup>0</sup>), haemoglobin S/β<sup>+</sup>-thalassaemia (HbSβ<sup>+</sup>), etc., but its long-term impact on SCD myocardial remodelling is incompletely characterized. We performed serial cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) and echocardiography in children and young adults with SCD undergoing matched-sibling or haploidentical HSCT in a prospective clinical trial with up to 36 months of post-HSCT follow-up. CMR assessments were conducted before HSCT and through the post-HSCT period. Echocardiographic parameters at 12 months post HSCT were compared with those of age-matched participants receiving disease-modifying therapies (DMTs). Among 20 HSCT recipients (mean age 14.8 years), CMR demonstrated progressive reductions in biventricular volumes and left atrial volume over 36 months, with preservation of ejection fraction. Extra-cellular volume, a surrogate marker of myocardial fibrosis, showed significant improvement from baseline, having normalized in nearly all participants assessed at 36 months. Compared with age-matched DMT recipients, HSCT recipients had lower tricuspid regurgitant jet velocity and improved diastolic parameters at 12 months post-HSCT, with normalization of cardiac output on echocardiography. These findings demonstrate sustained reversal of myocardial fibrosis and structural cardiac remodelling after HSCT for SCD. HSCT may, therefore, modify the trajectory of SCD cardiomyopathy beyond the improvements achieved with current DMTs.

title: Doxorubicin-induced Cardiotoxicity in Dogs: A Narrative Review.
authorString: Sunpongsri S, Roos T, Gerhing R, Zandvliet M, Santarelli G.
abstractText: Doxorubicin, an anthracycline widely used in both human and veterinary oncology, is highly effective against a variety of malignancies in dogs, including lymphomas, sarcomas and carcinomas. Despite its efficacy, doxorubicin exposure can be associated with cardiotoxicity, which may present acutely or chronically, potentially leading to severe cardiac arrhythmia and congestive heart failure. Mechanisms underlying cardiotoxicity are multifactorial, including oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, DNA damage via topoisomerase IIβ, inflammation and dysregulated cell death pathways such as apoptosis, pyroptosis and ferroptosis. In dogs, known risk factors include higher cumulative dose, breed predisposition to idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy, and higher body weight. Cardiac biomarkers, electrocardiography, echocardiography and other advanced imaging techniques have been employed to detect cardiac changes that can be seen also in the absence of clinical signs. However, current evidence is predominantly derived from experimental and retrospective research, highlighting the need for large prospective clinical studies to strengthen recommendations for monitoring and prevention. A deeper understanding of doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity in dogs is needed to identify factors influencing individual susceptibility, clarify the progression from subclinical damage to clinical cardiac dysfunction, and guide future research. Emerging approaches, including advanced echocardiography, microRNAs, proteomic biomarkers and pharmacokinetic modelling, may help improve early detection and guide more individualised dosing to minimise toxicity.

title: Patterns of cardiovascular disease subtypes and associated factors among young adults in Peshawar, Pakistan: a multicenter hospital-based cross-sectional study.
authorString: Arif N, Khan I, Khan TA, Afaq S, Ahmad B, Ahmad G, Ijaz M, Haq ZU.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are a major cause of morbidity and mortality. Evidence on CVD subtypes in young Pakistani adults is limited. This study characterized CVD subtypes and associated factors among young adults in Peshawar Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.

Methods

A multicentre, cross-sectional study was conducted at four hospitals among patients aged 18-45 years. Data were extracted from three-year hospital records. Associations were assessed using chi-square/Fisher's exact tests and logistic regression.

Results

8,650 CVD cases, 2,090 (24.2%) were young adults, predominantly male (64.6%), with a median age of 40 years (IQR: 36-44). ACS was the most common subtype (61.0%), followed by cardiomyopathy (39.0%). Overweight/obesity (77.0%), hypertension (56.5%), smoking (39.7%), dyslipidaemia (21.8%), and diabetes (14.4%) were the most prevalent factors. Compared with ACS, cardiomyopathy was independently associated with high heart rate, hypertension, dyslipidaemia, diabetes, and family history. Smoking was associated with lower odds of cardiomyopathy than ACS (aOR: 0.50, 95% CI: 0.41-0.61, p < 0.001).

Conclusions

Young adults accounted for 24.2% of CVD cases, with ACS and cardiomyopathy the most common subtypes, highlighting the need for targeted strategies. The cross-sectional design, findings indicate subtype differences rather than causal effects, while supporting smoking cessation and early hypertension detection in young adults.

title: MYLK c.4079G>A, p.(Gly1360Asp) Variant Associated With Hereditary Thoracic Aortic Diseases and Early Onset Aortic Dissection.
authorString: Virtanen M, Keskinen S, Björn R, Paavola M, Pohjola P, Hietala M, Haanpää MK, Malmberg M, Rahikkala E.
abstractText:
Aims

Thoracic aortic aneurysms and dissections are major causes of sudden cardiovascular death. We aimed to evaluate the clinical significance of the MYLK c.4079G>A, p.(Gly1360Asp) variant in Finnish families with heritable thoracic aortic disease (HTAD) and to assess evidence for a potential founder effect.

Methods

We evaluated the clinical significance and potential founder effect of the missense variant MYLK c.4079G>A, p.(Gly1360Asp) in Finnish families. Eight individuals from four unrelated Finnish families carrying the MYLK c.4079G>A heterozygous variant were recruited. Clinical histories, imaging data, and pedigrees were reviewed. Genetic testing included exome‑based gene panel sequencing or targeted familial variant testing. Variant classification followed the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics 2015 guidelines.

Results

Thoracic aortic dilatation or aneurysm occurred in 6/8 carriers (75%), with a mean age at diagnosis of 45 years (range 34-67). Ascending aortic diameters ranged from 26-59 mm, most often measured at the aortic root. Aortic dissection occurred in 4/8 (50%) at a mean age of 46 years (range 34-68), including three early‑adult events. Extrathoracic arterial involvement (carotid) was observed in one variant‑positive individual.

Conclusion

The MYLK c.4079G>A, p.(Gly1360Asp) variant was present in six affected individuals from four unrelated families and is enriched in the Finnish population, supporting a founder effect. The MYLK c.4079G>A, p.(Gly1360Asp) variant is associated with early‑adult‑onset, high‑penetrance thoracic aortic disease and substantial dissection risk, underscoring the need for vigilant surveillance and early intervention in affected individuals and at‑risk relatives.

title: LUR1 (SPRING1) promotes sortilin-induced macrophage lipid accumulation and aortic atherosclerosis via furin maturation.
authorString: Lv Y, Fan X, Lin C, Li H, Wang Y, Jiang X, Tang X, Liu F.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Biochim Biophys Acta Mol Cell Biol Lipids
journal.title: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular and cell biology of lipids
journal.isoabbreviation: Biochim Biophys Acta Mol Cell Biol Lipids

abstractText:
Background

This study was undertaken to investigate the contributions of largely Golgi-localized proteins-lipid uptake regulator 1 (LUR1, SPRING1), the protease furin, and sortilin-in oxidized low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL)-treated macrophages and atherosclerotic mouse models.

Methods

Bioinformatics analysis was employed to predict the interaction between LUR1 and furin and their potential involvement in AS. The binding of LUR1 to furin was detected using a co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) assay. Gene and protein expression was determined by real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) and western blot in THP-1 macrophages transfected with recombinant lentiviruses. Cellular lipid content was measured by colorimetry, and lipid droplets were evaluated by Oil Red O staining. Plasma lipid profiles were measured using an enzymatic oxidation method. Histological staining was performed to investigate aortic atherosclerotic lesions in male LDLR-/- mice fed a high-fat diet (HFD).

Results

LUR1 increased the expression and maturation of macrophage sortilin. Co-IP confirmed LUR1-furin binding. The mRNA and protein levels of furin and sortilin were increased upon LUR1 OE, while the ratios of pro-furin/mature-furin and pro-sortilin/total-sortilin decreased, thereby enhancing lipid uptake in macrophages. Infection with adeno-associated virus 9 (AAV9)-LUR1 elevated plasma levels of total cholesterol (TC), triglycerides (TG), and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), and increased lipid deposition and AS plaque area in the vessel walls of male HFD-fed LDLR-/- mice.

Conclusion

LUR1 was implicated in furin/sortilin maturation, accelerating macrophage lipid accumulation and the progression of aortic AS.

title: Thioredoxin-2 Alleviates Osteoporosis by Restraining FOXO3a Nuclear Translocation.
authorString: Zhan C, Zhou Z, Ding Y, Lian R, Li X, Zhang X, Cao J, Tang Z, Lin Z, Song Z, He F.
abstractText: Osteoporosis is a prevalent age- and disease-associated skeletal disorder characterized by bone loss, remodeling imbalance, and vascular niche deterioration, yet how endothelial redox dysfunction drives this process remains unclear. Here, we identify mitochondrial thioredoxin-2 (TRX2) as an endothelial safeguard against osteoporotic bone loss. TRX2 was markedly reduced in aging bone vascular endothelial cells, and endothelial Trx2 deficiency accelerated skeletal degeneration by suppressing osteogenic activity and enhancing osteoclastogenesis. Mechanistically, TRX2 directly bound FOXO3a through a redox-sensitive Cys90-Cys31 disulfide interaction, retaining FOXO3a at the mitochondrial outer membrane and limiting its nuclear translocation. TRX2 loss or oxidative stress disrupted this complex, enabling FOXO3a-dependent transcriptional activation of tumor necrosis factor-related apoptosis-inducing ligand (TRAIL) and generating a pro-osteoclastogenic vascular niche. TRAIL neutralization or endothelial TRX2 restoration attenuated ovariectomy-induced osteoporosis by preserving angiogenic-osteogenic coupling. These findings establish the endothelial TRX2-FOXO3a-TRAIL axis as a vascular redox checkpoint and potential therapeutic target for osteoporosis.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy and incident atrial fibrillation in non-diabetic adults with obesity and chronic kidney disease: a propensity matched cohort study.
authorString: Hassan A, Okorigba E, Grace C, Otabor E, Osineye B, Olayiwola O, Oyeleye T, Amin P.
abstractText:
Background

Obesity and chronic kidney disease (CKD) are potent risk factors for atrial fibrillation (AF), yet whether GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) prevent incident AF in non-diabetic adults with obesity and CKD is unexamined. We assessed whether GLP-1RA therapy reduces 1-year AF incidence in this cardiorenal phenotype.

Methods

Using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network (66 healthcare organizations), we conducted a retrospective target trial emulation of non-diabetic adults aged 18 or older with obesity and CKD stages 3-5 diagnosed 2021-2024. Patients receiving semaglutide, liraglutide, or tirzepatide (n = 10,985) were compared with unexposed patients (n = 94,527). After propensity score matching, 7326 patients remained per cohort. The primary outcome was incident AF at 1 year; secondary outcomes included AF subtypes, ventricular tachyarrhythmias, and all-cause hospitalization. Cox models generated hazard ratios (HRs); sensitivity analyses extended follow-up to 2-3 years with landmark analyses.

Results

At 1 year, GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly lower incident AF (1.63% vs. 2.62%; HR 0.655, 95% CI 0.508-0.844; p = 0.001), a 34.5% relative risk reduction. Reductions were consistent for paroxysmal (HR 0.586), persistent (HR 0.482), and longstanding persistent AF (HR 0.527; all p < 0.05); permanent AF was non-significant at 1 year. Ventricular tachyarrhythmias (HR 0.556; p = 0.002) and hospitalization (HR 0.668; p < 0.001) were also significantly reduced. Benefits persisted across 2- and 3-year follow-up and remained consistent in landmark analyses.

Conclusions

In non-diabetic adults with obesity and CKD, GLP-1RA therapy was associated with significant, durable reductions in incident AF, ventricular arrhythmias, and hospitalization. These findings are consistent with a possible cardiorenal benefit and support prioritizing this phenotype for dedicated randomized trials.

title: Periodontal Disease and Heart Failure: Current Evidence and Perspectives.
authorString: da Silva AE, de Almeida VD, Cavalcante GA, da Silva Júnior RR, de Almeida DRQ, Fernandes JV, do Nascimento EGC, de Mesquita Andrade C, de Medeiros Fernandes TAA.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

Periodontal disease has been increasingly recognized as a chronic inflammatory condition with potential systemic implications, particularly in the cardiovascular system. Heart failure (HF), a pro-inflammatory syndrome with multisystem involvement, remains a major public health burden. This state-of-the-art narrative review aims to analyze the current scientific evidence on the association between periodontal disease and heart failure, emphasizing epidemiological data, cardiac biomarkers, inflammatory mediators, and future perspectives.

Recent findings

Current evidence indicates a high prevalence of periodontal disease among patients with HF and suggests associations between periodontal disease and elevated cardiac biomarkers, including NT-proBNP and troponin T, as well as systemic inflammatory mediators such as C-reactive protein, IL-6, and TNF-α. Interventional studies have reported reductions in some of these biomarkers following periodontal treatment, suggesting a potential biological link between periodontal inflammation and HF. However, findings remain heterogeneous, and some studies have failed to demonstrate significant associations. Current evidence supports an association between periodontal disease and heart failure, with systemic inflammation representing a potential biological link. Nevertheless, the heterogeneity of study designs, small sample sizes, and predominance of observational and cross-sectional evidence limit causal inference. Longitudinal studies and randomized clinical trials are needed to clarify causal mechanisms and determine whether periodontal prevention and treatment can contribute to integrated strategies for patients with HF.

title: Periconceptional and early-pregnancy exposure to SGLT2 inhibitors and congenital malformations: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Dutta D, Mahajan K, Gupta G, Sharma M, Sugandha S, Kamrul-Hasan ABM.
abstractText:
Purpose

Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are increasingly prescribed to women of reproductive age for type 2 diabetes and cardiorenal protection, and are commonly continued through the periconceptional period until pregnancy is recognized. Human safety data on inadvertent first-trimester exposure remain scarce, creating substantial clinical uncertainty.

Methods

We systematically searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL from inception to 15 May 2026 for observational cohort studies comparing early-pregnancy or preconception exposure to SGLT2 inhibitors with active antidiabetic comparators among women with type 2 diabetes. Adjusted risk ratios (RRs) were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis.

Results

Three cohorts, including 669 SGLT2 inhibitor-exposed pregnancies, were eligible. In the prespecified insulin-comparator analysis, SGLT2 inhibitor exposure was not associated with major congenital malformations (RR 0.94, 95% CI 0.68-1.29) or cardiac malformations (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.64-1.48). The inclusion of a preconception sulfonylurea comparator cohort yielded a similar estimate for major congenital malformations (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.74-1.29). In a Korean cohort, exposure during gestational weeks 4-10 was associated with congenital heart defects (RR 2.79, 95% CI 1.16-7.06).

Conclusions

Based on the limited observational evidence available, early SGLT2 inhibitor exposure was not associated with an increased risk of overall major congenital or cardiac malformations; however, the estimates were imprecise and could not rule out clinically important increases in risk. Certainty of the evidence was low to very low because of residual confounding, live-birth selection, heterogeneous exposure definitions, and few exposed events. A possible timing-specific cardiac signal requires replication.

title: Rapid Progression of Cardiac Allograft Vasculopathy With Sudden Cardiac Death Within the First Year of Heart Transplantation: A Case Report.
authorString: Dix M, Iskandar JP, He L, Serdah MS, Joshi AA, Godishala A, Chaturvedi A, Kaproth-Joslin K, Dombroski DA, Chen Y, Cheruiyot WA, Chong-Yik R, Schwartz RG, Alexis J, Gosev I, Wood KL, Thomas S.
abstractText: Cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV) is a major cause of mortality and morbidity within the first 3 years of heart transplantation (HT). CAV results in progressive coronary artery stenosis and may lead to arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death. In some cases, sudden cardiac death represents the initial presentation of CAV, as cardiac denervation blunts anginal symptoms that otherwise could have preceded sudden cardiac death (SCD). Here, we describe the case of a 56-year-old man with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy. He underwent left ventricular assist device implantation followed by orthotopic HT. Five months after transplantation, he presented with atypical mid-sternal chest discomfort initially thought to be musculoskeletal in origin. Routine coronary angiography at 12 months revealed severe, diffuse 3-vessel disease consistent with International Society of Heart and Lung Transplantation (ISHLT) CAV-3, and cardiac MRI revealed full thickness delayed enhancement in the inferior wall consistent with infarction. Despite overall preserved left ventricular ejection fraction, he developed polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (VT) with an appropriate shock from a wearable cardioverter-defibrillator (WCD) and was transferred with an intra-aortic balloon pump to a larger transplant center and underwent another heart transplantation. This case highlights rapid CAV progression leading to infarction and arrhythmia despite preserved LVEF, emphasizing the need for enhanced screening with biomarkers and imaging as well as earlier consideration for device-based strategies to prevent sudden cardiac death in high-risk transplant recipients.

title: Complement C3a plays a role in diabetic cardiomyopathy mainly via C3aR-ERK-PANoptosis pathway.
authorString: Zhang Y, Xie Y, Wang L, Zhong X, Wang M, Luo L, Lei P, Lai P, Li L, Vaczy A, Atlasz T, Dai L, Zeng H, Wang H.
abstractText:
Background

Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is one of the leading causes of death in diabetic patients. However, the pathogenesis of DCM remains incompletely understood, and effective targeted therapies are lacking. This study aims to investigate the role of complement C3a in the development of DCM, providing a novel theoretical foundation for its precise prevention and treatment.

Methods

Eight-week-old male C57BL/6 J mice were injected with streptozotocin (STZ) to induce a diabetes model for 26 weeks. The two intervention groups were injected with C3a receptor antagonist (SB290157, 30 mg/kg/d) and novel C3 cleavage inhibitor (CP40-KK, 2 mg/kg/d) by intraperitoneal injection for 8 weeks. Cardiac function/histopathological changes were determined by echocardiogram examination, and Millar catheter system. Human cardiomyocytes (AC16) were employed in vitro.

Results

C3a was significantly upregulated in the plasma of the STZ-induced DCM model, and PANoptosis plays a critical role in cardiac tissue and cardiomyocytes. The C3a receptor antagonist (SB290157) could significantly improve the cardiac function of diabetic mice, reduce myocardial hypertrophy, and inhibit the activation level of PANoptosis pathway in cardiac tissue. Furthermore, inhibiting the C3aR/ERK pathway could regulate cardiomyocyte PANoptosis by pyroptosis (NLRP3-dependent), apoptosis (caspase-3-dependent), and necroptosis (RIP-dependent) in the DCM model and C3a-treated cardiomyocytes. The novel complement C3 inhibitor CP40-KK exerts comparable therapeutic efficacy to SB290157 in treating DCM at a lower drug dosage.

Conclusion

We demonstrate the crucial role of the C3a/C3aR signaling axis, and CP40-KK treatment was protective in the STZ-induced DCM model. These findings provide valuable evidence supporting potential complement-based therapies targeting the C3a/C3aR/ERK/PANoptosis pathway in DCM treatment.

title: Structured postmortem genetic counselling and testing in sudden unexplained death among young adults in the Netherlands: results and implications regarding hereditary risk.
authorString: Wemeijer TM, Verbaan LA, Duijst WLJM, Hoedemaekers YM, Christiaans I.
abstractText:
Introduction

Sudden unexplained death (SUD) in young adults may result from hereditary cardiovascular disorders that remain undetected even after conventional autopsy. Routine postmortem genetic testing may identify these disorders, improving determination of the cause of death while providing diagnostic and preventive opportunities for surviving blood relatives.

Methods

Between September 2022 and October 2025, 100 cases of SUD in young adults in the Netherlands were investigated using the NODOV (Nader Onderzoek naar de DoodsOorzaak bij (jong)Volwassenen) procedure. Genetic counselling was offered to surviving blood relatives in 50 cases where conventional autopsy findings suggested an inherited cardiovascular disorder. Conventional autopsy findings, medical history and family history guided phenotype-directed genetic testing using targeted gene panel analysis following whole-exome/genome sequencing.

Results

Genetic testing was successfully performed in 46 out of 50 cases and identified pathogenic variants in six cases involving the CACNA1C, BAG3, MYBPC3, LDL-R, KCNJ2, and PKD1 genes. Pretest genetic counselling proved important in guiding genetic testing in 10% of all cases and 50% of genetically confirmed cases. Pathogenic variants were identified in both structurally abnormal and autopsy-negative cases. Families received tailored genetic counselling and recommendations for clinical follow-up based on predictive genetic testing. Among the 44 families without a genetic diagnosis, 43 were advised to undergo clinical cardiovascular screening.

Conclusion

This study highlights the importance of a structured multidisciplinary postmortem investigation, such as the NODOV procedure, integrating pretest genetic counselling and tailored postmortem genetic testing. This approach may improve determination of cause of death (particularly in autopsy-negative cases), aid in the identification of hereditary cardiovascular disorders and facilitate preventive strategies for at-risk blood relatives.

title: A Transcritical Bifurcation at Infinity Governs Plaque Stability in a Lipid-Structured Macrophage Model of Atherosclerosis.
authorString: Endes EA, Pelen NN.
abstractText: Atherosclerotic plaques are fatty deposits in arterial walls and a major cause of heart attacks and strokes. Macrophage proliferation triggers plaque growth and instability, but the specific conditions that convert stable plaques into unstable ones remain unclear. To provide insight into the conditions for this transition, we apply bifurcation analysis to the lipid-structured atherosclerosis model proposed by Chambers et al. (Bull Math Biol 86(8):104, 2024). We demonstrate that, in the asymptotic regime where macrophage levels become large ( M→∞ ), the model exhibits an asymptotic fast-slow structure that does not hold outside this limit. Within this asymptotic regime, we reduce the full system onto a slow invariant manifold, providing a simplified yet accurate description of the dynamics near the critical proliferation-emigration threshold. We prove, via centre manifold theory, that the positive steady state loses stability through a transcritical bifurcation at infinity at the critical proliferation-emigration threshold ρc=1+γ . The analysis reveals that the positive equilibrium branch approaches and exchanges stability with a boundary equilibrium at infinity, providing a rigorous dynamical explanation for the transition that was identified but left unexplored in the original study. Complementing this analytical contribution, we conduct a global sensitivity analysis using Partial Rank Correlation Coefficients (PRCC), identifying macrophage proliferation, emigration, and efferocytosis as the dominant regulators of plaque dynamics. Targeted parameter investigations near ρc reveal a regulatory decoupling between macrophage accumulation and necrotic core growth, providing new biological insight into the behaviour of the model near the critical proliferation-emigration threshold.

title: Quantitative assessment of foot microcirculation by CT perfusion differentiates chronic limb-threatening ischemia from claudication in peripheral artery disease.
authorString: Du S, Gao P, Zhou K, Zhang J, Zhu T, Zhang W.
abstractText:
Introduction

Computed tomography perfusion (CTP) is validated to assess foot microcirculatory perfusion in peripheral artery disease (PAD). This study aimed to investigate differences in foot microcirculation on CTP between patients with claudication (Cla) and chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) and to develop diagnostic models for CLTI.

Methods

This single-center prospective study enrolled hospitalized patients with PAD at Huadong Hospital, China (October 2022 to January 2024). Participants underwent preoperative foot CTP and were stratified into Cla (Rutherford category 3) and CLTI (Rutherford categories 4-6) groups. Baseline characteristics and perfusion parameters were recorded. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic curve analysis were performed.

Results

A total of 57 patients with PAD were included (34 Cla, 23 CLTI). Resting ankle-brachial index and Global Limb Anatomic Staging System scores did not differ significantly between groups. Diabetes mellitus (DM) prevalence was higher in the CLTI group (95.7% vs 52.9%; p = 0.002). Multivariable logistic regression identified hemoglobin (Hb) level (OR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.822-0.986; p = 0.024), time to peak (TTP) (OR, 1.135; 95% CI, 1.045-1.250; p = 0.003), and blood flow (BF) (OR, 0.668; 95% CI, 0.499-0.894; p = 0.007) as independent predictors for CLTI. Four diagnostic models were constructed: model A (BF + DM, area under the curve [AUC] 0.864), model B (BF + Hb, AUC 0.890), model C (TTP + DM, AUC 0.895), and model D (TTP + Hb, AUC 0.874).

Conclusion

Foot microcirculation differed significantly between patients with Cla and CLTI on CTP. Hb, TTP, and BF were independent predictors for CLTI. All models demonstrated good diagnostic performance, with model C yielding the highest AUC.

title: C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte index and coronary microvascular dysfunction after primary percutaneous coronary intervention: The mediating role of insulin resistance.
authorString: Wang W, Qiu H, Wang J, Jiang H.
abstractText:
Background

The C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte (CALLY) index integrates systemic inflammation, nutritional status, and immune function. We investigated its association with angiography-derived microvascular resistance (AMR)-defined coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and performed an exploratory statistical mediation analysis involving estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR).

Methods

This retrospective, single-center observational study included 456 consecutive patients with STEMI undergoing primary PCI. AMR-defined CMD was prespecified as AMR ≥250 mmHg·s/m. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS), and prespecified subgroup analyses were performed. Sensitivity and exploratory mediation analyses were also performed.

Results

AMR-defined CMD was present in 228 patients (50.0%). In Model 3, each doubling of CALLY was associated with lower odds of AMR-defined CMD (OR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.80-0.94; P < 0.001). Compared with Q1, Q3 and Q4 were associated with 44% (OR, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.32-0.97; P = 0.037) and 52% (OR, 0.48; 95% CI, 0.28-0.84; P = 0.010) lower odds, respectively (P for trend = 0.018). RCS analysis showed an overall association (P = 0.001) without evidence of nonlinearity (P = 0.310). No significant subgroup interactions were observed. Exploratory mediation analysis estimated that eGDR statistically accounted for 15.47% of the observed association.

Conclusions

Higher CALLY values were inversely associated with AMR-defined CMD after primary PCI for STEMI. eGDR may account for part of this association. CALLY may serve as an auxiliary marker for AMR-defined CMD risk stratification, pending prospective multicenter validation.

title: Associations of PM<sub>2.5</sub> components with dynamic and accelerated progression of different kidney function states and subsequent cardiovascular events: The GOLD-Health cohort.
authorString: Rao M, Chen J, Hu P, Ai Z, Wang M, Liu X, Zhang Z, Lin H.
abstractText:
Background

Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) has been associated with an increased risk of chronic kidney disease (CKD) and cardiovascular disease (CVD). However, the relationships between specific PM2.5 components and the dynamic cardiorenal trajectory remain uncertain.

Methods

Employing multistate and accelerated failure time (AFT) modeling in a prospective cohort of 307,639 participants, we examined the associations of 2-year exposure to PM2.5 and its components (sulfate [SO42-], nitrate [NO3-], ammonium [NH4+], organic matter [OM], and black carbon [BC]) with dynamic and accelerated progression from different kidney function categories (1-4, according to estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] and self-reported CKD) to CVD, and ultimately to cardiovascular death.

Results

Over 1,058,210 person-years of follow-up, we documented 23,948 CVD cases and 7763 cardiovascular death cases. We observed that PM2.5 and its components were significantly associated with the dynamic cardiorenal trajectory, with SO42-, NO3-, and NH4+ exhibiting larger hazard ratios (HRs). Per-interquartile range (IQR) increments in SO42-, NO3-, and NH4+ were positively correlated with the transition from kidney function category 2 to 3, and the HRs were 1.273 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.257-1.289), 1.304 (95% CI: 1.290-1.317), and 1.280 (95% CI: 1.267-1.294), respectively. The AFT model indicated that higher levels of PM2.5 and its constituents significantly accelerated the dynamic cardiorenal trajectory. The predictive transition times from kidney function category 2 to 3 for 2-year NO3- exposure were 1727.43 days at 4.2 μg/m3 and 868.56 days at 7.0 μg/m3.

Conclusions

Our findings revealed that PM2.5 components (2-year exposure) may be important risk factors for adverse cardiorenal outcomes.

title: Dose-dependent cardiac autonomic dysregulation under classroom crowding: heart rate variability analysis and machine learning classification.
authorString: Naeem M.
abstractText: Classroom overcrowding affects hundreds of millions of students globally, yet its physiological impact on cardiac autonomic function remains uncharacterized. This controlled within-subjects experiment enrolled 30 healthy university students who attended standardized 30-min lectures under three calibrated density conditions: low (30 students/150 m<sup>2</sup>), medium (60/150 m<sup>2</sup>), and high (100/150 m<sup>2</sup>), with all environmental parameters held constant. Twenty-five heart rate variability (HRV) parameters spanning time-domain, frequency-domain, and nonlinear domains were extracted from continuous electrocardiogram (ECG) recordings. Subjective workload was assessed via the NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX), and RoBoSS-SVM (a Support Vector Machine using the Robust, Bounded, Sparse, and Smooth loss function) with Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) classified density conditions from HRV features. Repeated-measures ANOVA revealed significant density effects on all 25 HRV parameters (all p < 0.001), with 64% demonstrating exceptionally large effect sizes (η<sup>2</sup>p ≥ 0.50). Parasympathetic markers showed the largest responses: pNN50 declined 52% (η<sup>2</sup>p = 0.702), HF power declined 51% (η<sup>2</sup>p = 0.654), and RMSSD declined 32% (η<sup>2</sup>p = 0.420) from low to high density-while sympathetically influenced indices showed substantially smaller effects, confirming parasympathetic withdrawal as the predominant autonomic mechanism. These suppression magnitudes approach levels associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes. NASA-TLX scores increased 74% across conditions (p < 0.001) and correlated with HRV vagal indices (r = -0.69 to -0.76), providing corroborating, though not definitive, evidence that crowding engages both subjective and autonomic stress pathways (see Discussion for caveats regarding this association). Temporal analysis confirmed progressive autonomic suppression without habituation across 10-min windows. RoBoSS-SVM achieved 92.2% accuracy for three-class discrimination and 97.2% accuracy (AUC = 0.993) for binary classification, with parasympathetic time-domain features comprising 64% of the optimal feature set. Classroom spatial density produces dose-dependent, mechanism-specific cardiac autonomic dysregulation dominated by vagal withdrawal-consistent with polyvagal theory's prediction for social-environmental stressors. The excellent classification performance supports feasibility of real-time wearable monitoring for evidence-based classroom capacity management.

title: Differences in Office and Ambulatory Pulse Wave Analysis in Patients with White Coat Hypertension and Other Hypertension Phenotypes.
authorString: Schäfer AC, Nuhn EM, Lüders S, Grupp C, Wallbach M, Koziolek MJ.

journal.title: High blood pressure & cardiovascular prevention : the official journal of the Italian Society of Hypertension

abstractText:
Introduction

Increased arterial stiffness is a sign of vascular damage; therefore, assessing it is crucial for evaluating cardiovascular risk. Arterial stiffness parameters such as pulse wave velocity (PWV) and augmentation index (at heart rate 75 bpm, AIX@75) were shown to correlate directly with blood pressure (BP).

Aim

Since these parameters may consequently be altered in patients with white coat effect (WCE), this study examined differences in office and 24h measurements of these parameters across various BP phenotypes.

Methods

In this multicenter cross-sectional study, conducted between 2018 and 2023 at three nephrology clinics, office and 24h BP measurements and pulse wave analysis (PWA) of 208 patients were examined.

Results

189 patients were included; 48 were diagnosed with controlled hypertension (HTN), 63 with uncontrolled HTN, 22 with a masked HTN phenotype, 30 with WCE, of whom 11 had white coat HTN (WCH) and 19 had white coat uncontrolled HTN (WCUH), and 26 had normal BP. By definition, patients with WCE had significantly higher office peripheral and aortic BP than the respective 24h values (p<0.0001 each). Their AIX@75 was significantly higher on office (32.7±11.4%) than on 24h measurement (27.4±7.2%, p=0.0354), and they showed a significantly greater reduction in PWV between office and 24h measurement than normotensives and all other BP phenotypes (padj <0.0001 each).

Conclusions

In patients with WCE, there are significant differences in arterial stiffness parameters between office and 24h measurements, suggesting that both measurement methods provide complementary hemodynamic information. Prospective studies are needed to determine the prognostic significance of these differences.

title: Hyperdense Renal Lesion Characterization on Three DECT Technologies: Can Iodine Quantification Differentiate Hyperattenuating Renal Cysts From Papillary Renal Cell Cancers?
authorString: Majeed NF, Cao J, Mroueh N, Kambadakone AR.
abstractText:
Rationale and objectives

To evaluate the performance of dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) in differentiation of hyperattenuating renal cysts (HCs) from papillary renal cell cancers (pRCCs) on three different DECT technologies (dual-source [dsDECT], rapid kVp-switching [rsDECT], and dual-layer detector-based [dlDECT]).

Materials and methods

In this institutional review board-approved retrospective study, we included 85 patients with a total of 108 incidental hyperdense renal lesions detected on contrast-enhanced DECT scans (dsDECT, n = 41; rsDECT, n = 42; and dlDECT, n = 25). The study cohort included HCs (n = 73) and pRCCs (n = 35). Final confirmation was obtained with histopathology for pRCCs and with magnetic resonance imaging within 6 months of the DECT for HCs. Quantitative iodine evaluation was performed with iodine concentration (IC) measured within the lesion and the abdominal aorta. Normalized IC (NIC) was generated for each lesion by normalizing the lesion IC to the aortic IC.

Results

Both IC and NIC measurements yielded significant differences between HCs and pRCCs for the dsDECT and rsDECT techniques (P < 0.001) but not for the dlDECT (P > 0.05). Cutoff values with 100% sensitivity for pRCC detection were 0.30 and 0.60 mg/mL for dsDECT and rsDECT, respectively. Normalization to the abdominal aorta allowed creation of a uniform cutoff on both technologies, with an NIC value of 0.09 allowing 100% sensitivity for each.

Conclusion

Significant intertechnique differences exist for the differentiation of HCs from pRCCs. Normalization of IC to the aorta provides a uniform cutoff for differentiation of these lesions on dsDECT and rsDECT.

title: Amifostine attenuates pressure overload-induced cardiac hypertrophy and metabolic remodeling via the SIRT1/PPAR-α axis in rats.
authorString: Shahbazian M, Imani A, Faghihi M, Ebrahimi SSS, Rahimi M, Rakhshan K.
abstractText: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy induced by chronic pressure overload is accompanied by significant metabolic disturbances, including impaired myocardial lipid metabolism. This study ascertained whether the cytoprotective agent amifostine (WR-2721) exerts cardioprotective effects along pressure overload-induced remodeling and whether these effects are linked to modulation of the SIRT1/PPAR-α axis. Male Wistar rats (n = 24) were assigned to Sham, abdominal aortic constriction (AAC), and AAC + amifostine (200 mg/kg, i.p., weekly for 8 weeks) groups, with amifostine administered concurrently with hypertrophic stress. The cardiac structure and function were appraised using echocardiography and histological analyses, with the expression of SIRT1, PPAR-α, and key regulators of lipid metabolism examined by Western blotting. Amifostine treatment was associated with attenuation of pressure overload-induced cardiac hypertrophy, reflected by lower heart and lung weight ratios, preservation of functional indices, and diminished myocardial fibrosis. At the molecular level, amifostine administration was accompanied by relative normalization of SIRT1 and PPAR-α expression, elevated levels of fatty acid oxidation-related proteins, and suppression of lipogenic markers. These findings suggest that amifostine mitigates pressure overload-induced cardiac remodeling and is associated with improved myocardial metabolic homeostasis, accompanied by favorable changes in the expression of SIRT1, PPAR-α, and lipid metabolism-related proteins. While these observations support the potential involvement of the SIRT1/PPAR-α signaling pathway, further mechanistic studies are required to establish its causal role in mediating the cardioprotective effects of amifostine.

title: Unintended Shifts in High-Priority Adult Heart Transplant Listings after the OPTN's September 2025 Policy Change.
authorString: Ramos C, Horwitz A, Singer R, White M, Narang N, Khush KK, Parker WF, Ahn DJ.

journal.title: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation

abstractText: The Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network amended Status 2 heart allocation criteria in September 2025, requiring documented failure of high-dose inotropes before candidates could qualify via intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) or percutaneous endovascular ventricular assist device (PEVAD) support. Using OPTN data, we compared seasonally matched pre-policy (September 2024-June 2025, n=4,206) and post-policy (September 2025-June 2026, n=4,231) adult candidates. While standard Status 3 high-dose inotrope listings increased 2.0% to 4.1% and standard Status 2 IABP/PEVAD listings decreased 18.2% to 11.0%, Status 1 listings and Status 2 exceptions increased 7.7% to 10.6% and 17.5% to 21.5%, respectively (all p<0.001). Consequently, combined initial Status 1/2 listings were unchanged (44.5% vs 44.0%, p=0.71). Furthermore, overall transplant volume remained similar, but status at transplant shifted from standard Status 2 toward Status 2 exceptions and Status 1. Tightening standard Status 2 eligibility was associated with redistribution across high-priority pathways rather than reduced high-priority listings.
