title: Multistage Preclinical Evaluation of MRI-Guided Stenting for Coarctation of the Aorta using in vitro and Porcine Models.
authorString: Gholami Bajestani D, Reich CM, Birkigt J, Mulik C, Kauffold J, Sigmarsson HL, Jochimsen T, Sattler B, Sabri O, Steinmetz M, Melzer A.
abstractText:
Purpose

This study evaluated the technical and procedural feasibility of MRI-guided stent implantation for CoA using a structured multistage preclinical evaluation protocol.

Materials and methods

A commercially available MR Conditional guidewire and dedicated research prototypes comprising nitinol stents, delivery systems, and balloon catheters were assessed in a three-stage protocol. Device visibility was evaluated in a standardized water phantom at 1.5 T and 3.0 T. In a polymer-based CoA vessel phantom, 10 stent implantations were performed by novices (n = 6) and experts (n = 4), with four separate expert-led balloon dilatations. MRI-guided stent implantation was subsequently performed in five porcine models.

Results

All devices were visible at both field strengths, with lateral artifact widths of 5.3-7.8 mm for the guidewire, 20.9-38.5 mm for the stent delivery system, 13.1-19.9 mm for the expanded stents, and 17.4-30.5 mm for the balloon catheter. Phantom stenting duration was 10.2 ± 7.2 mins for novices and 6.2 ± 2.7 mins for experts. MRI-guided stent implantation was successfully performed in all five animals, with a mean duration of 13.6 ± 7.5 mins. In one animal, balloon post-dilatation was additionally performed as a procedural proof of concept.

Conclusion

MRI-guided stent implantation for CoA is feasible within a structured multistage preclinical evaluation protocol and supports further clinical translation of radiation-free endovascular treatment.

title: Persistent hypertension and left ventricular remodeling after stenting for coarctation of the aorta: a single-center cohort study.
authorString: Zhao K, Wu Z, Mao Y, Zhang W, Luo M, Shu C.
abstractText: Persistent hypertension (HTN) remains common after covered stent implantation for coarctation of the aorta (CoA). However, existing evidence is derived predominantly from surgical repair cohorts and cross-sectional echocardiography, leaving the individual trajectory of left ventricular (LV) remodeling after stenting poorly defined. We retrospectively studied 84 patients with complete persistent HTN status, and 75 patients with paired follow-up echocardiography for LV remodeling analyses. Multivariable logistic and linear regression were performed to identify factors associated with persistent HTN and follow-up LV mass index (LVMI) separately. Paired changes in LV hypertrophy (LVH) and LV geometry were assessed using McNemar and Stuart-Maxwell tests. Persistent HTN occurred in 46 of 84 patients (54.8%) at a median clinical follow-up of 9 years, and was associated with older age at repair and higher preoperative systolic blood pressure. Higher follow-up LVMI was associated with higher baseline LVMI, male sex and longer follow-up duration. At a median echocardiographic follow-up of 2 years, LVH prevalence decreased from 41.3-24.0%. This net decline masked bidirectional individual trajectories: 19 of 31 patients with baseline LVH (61.3%) no longer met LVH criteria, whereas 6 of 44 patients without baseline LVH (13.6%) developed new-onset LVH. Anatomical relief after CoA stenting therefore does not preclude ongoing myocardial burden, and patients developing new-onset LVH would not be identified by preoperative risk stratification alone. Serial echocardiographic assessment should complement long-term blood pressure surveillance, though these findings require validation in larger cohorts with standardized follow-up.

title: QTc reference ranges in eastern European children aged 6 to 18 years: a large-scale population study and comparison with international normative datasets.
authorString: Cismaru G, Lazea C, Mureşan L, Gusetu G, Rosu R, Pop D, Negru A, Căinap SS.
abstractText:
Background

QT interval corrected for heart rate (QTc) is important. Appropriate reference ranges support ECG interpretation, but data for Eastern European children remain limited. We aimed to derive age- and sex-stratified QTc reference ranges, estimate proportions exceeding cut-offs, and compare results with normative datasets.

Methods

12‑lead ECGs from 22,335 children aged 6-18 years were obtained through the CARDIOPED screening programme in northwestern Transylvania, Romania. QTc was calculated using Bazett's formula. Age- and sex-stratified percentile curves (P2.5-P97.5) were derived using spline regression. Correlations with anthropometric variables and proportions exceeding QTc cut-offs of 440, 460, and 480 ms were assessed. Results were compared with the Davignon, Rijnbeek, Saarel, Bratincsák, and Mason datasets.

Results

Overall median QTc was 408.2 ms in males and 409.9 ms in females. Upper reference limits (P97.5) were 451.4 ms and 457.0 ms, respectively. The sex difference increased from 2.6 ms in the 6-12-year group to 5.7 ms in the 12-18-year group. Obesity and anthropometric variables showed weak, non-significant correlations with QTc. Values were closely aligned with Rijnbeek et al. QTc exceeded 440 ms in 6.0% of males and 460 ms in 1.2% of females; 14 children (0.06%) had a single screening QTc measurement ≥480 ms.

Conclusions

QTc reference ranges in this Eastern European cohort were consistent with European paediatric normative data. Upper reference limits were approximately 450 ms in males and 460 ms in females. Proportions exceeding cut-offs describe cohort distributions, not diagnostic false-positive rates. Percentiles are statistical reference limits rather than validated clinical decision or diagnostic thresholds.

title: Low-dose juglone attenuates pressure overload-induced cardiac hypertrophy through Lys207-dependent FoxO1 activation and mitochondrial protection.
authorString: Chen H, Yang Z, Zhang C, Ge C, Zhao Y, Cheng S, Wang Y, Chen H, Xu C, Wang D, Yang J.
abstractText: Pressure overload-induced cardiac hypertrophy is characterized by mitochondrial dysfunction and redox imbalance. Here, we investigated the efficacy, safety window, and redox-regulatory mechanism of juglone, a naturally occurring 5-hydroxy-1,4-naphthoquinone. In mice subjected to transverse aortic constriction (TAC), high-dose juglone induced cardiac, hepatic, and renal toxicity, whereas 1 mg/kg/day was well tolerated and attenuated cardiac hypertrophy. Juglone also suppressed Ang II-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy in vitro and preserved mitochondrial ultrastructure and mitochondrial membrane potential, respiration, ATP production, and redox homeostasis. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) revealed that juglone reduced stress-associated cardiomyocyte states and enriched calcium-handling cardiomyocytes. Integrated transcriptomic analyses, Biotin-Juglone pull-down assay, surface plasmon resonance, cellular thermal shift assays, molecular docking, and mutational analyses identified FoxO1 as a functional target of juglone. Juglone engaged the FoxO1 DNA-binding domain in a Lys207-dependent manner, and was associated with FoxO1 deacetylation, nuclear accumulation, and transcriptional activation. Activated FoxO1 induced Sesn3 transcription and restored AMPK phosphorylation at Thr172. Sesn3 silencing markedly attenuated juglone-induced AMPK activation and impaired its protective effects against cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and mitochondrial dysfunction. FoxO1 silencing, FoxO1-K207Q mutation, blockade of FoxO1 deacetylation, or inhibition of FoxO1 transcriptional activity impaired these benefits. Importantly, myocardium from patients with aortic valve stenosis-associated hypertrophy exhibited increased FoxO1 acetylation, reduced cardiomyocyte nuclear FoxO1 localization, decreased Sesn3 expression and AMPK phosphorylation, and increased 4-HNE. Collectively, low-dose juglone attenuates pathological hypertrophy and preserves mitochondrial homeostasis through the FoxO1-Sesn3-AMPK axis, while highlighting the importance of dose-dependent redox effects in determining its therapeutic efficacy and systemic toxicity.

title: Effectiveness of Discrete Strategies and Implementation Bundles for Improving Clinician Prescription of Clinical Practice Guideline-Recommended Medications for Atherosclerotic Occlusive Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Kirkham AM, Candeliere J, Presseau J, McIsaac DI, Shorr R, Fergusson DA, Roberts DJ.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

We sought to determine the effectiveness of discrete strategies and implementation bundles for improving clinical practice guideline (CPG) strongly recommended medication prescription to adults with atherosclerotic occlusive disease.

Methods

We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, PsycINFO, and Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (inception to December 9, 2025) for randomized controlled trials evaluating discrete strategies or implementation bundles for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription to adults with atherosclerotic occlusive disease. Two investigators screened titles/abstracts and full texts, extracted data, assessed risk of bias, and classified discrete strategies and implementation bundles. Random-effects models were used for meta-analysis. Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation was used to assess certainty.

Results

We included 31 randomized controlled trials studying 29 unique discrete strategies and implementation bundles. The implementation bundle with the largest effect size for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription combined case management, team changes, continuous quality improvement, audit/feedback, and clinician and patient education (relative risk, 2.62 [95% CI, 2.08-3.29]; moderate certainty). Meta-regression analyses suggested that discrete strategies and implementation bundles using patient education were more effective at improving statin (P=0.037) and all CPG strongly recommended medication (P=0.006) prescription. Combining case management, team changes, facilitated relay of information, and audit/feedback reduced all-cause death and new vascular event risk. Team changes improved prescription of all CPG strongly recommended medications (relative risk, 1.23 [95% CI, 1.11-1.36]; moderate certainty) and reduced major adverse cardiac event risk.

Conclusions

Combining case management, team changes, continuous quality improvement, audit/feedback, and clinician and patient education had the largest effect size for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription and improved patient outcomes. Team changes improved CPG strongly recommended medication prescription and reduced major adverse cardiac event risk.

title: Cardiovascular Toxicities Associated With Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: Clinical Phenotypes, Mechanisms, Diagnosis, and Management-A Narrative Review.
authorString: Wu S, Yang J, Wang X, Lang J, Wang WJ, Sun X.
abstractText:
Objective

Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have improved cancer outcomes, yet cardiovascular toxicities remain difficult to recognize and manage. We review their clinical spectrum, mechanistic evidence, diagnostic work-up, surveillance, and treatment, with particular attention to where evidence is established and where it remains preliminary.

Methods

We conducted a narrative review of PubMed through September 2026 and hand-searched reference lists of relevant guidelines, reviews, and primary studies. We prioritized international guidance, systematic reviews, multicenter registries, prospective cohorts, and clinically informative mechanistic studies. Case reports and experimental studies were retained when they addressed questions not covered by higher-level evidence. The review was not protocol driven and did not include duplicate screening, formal risk-of-bias assessment, or a PRISMA flow diagram.

Results

ICI-related cardiovascular toxicity extends beyond myocarditis to temporally associated atherosclerotic events, pericardial disease, and heart failure without demonstrable myocardial inflammation, although causal attribution is less secure for these non-myocarditis phenotypes. Current guidance supports baseline cardiovascular assessment and risk-adapted surveillance, but neither a universal troponin threshold nor an outcome-proven monitoring schedule has been established. Corticosteroids remain first-line treatment for clinically significant ICI myocarditis. Abatacept, ruxolitinib, alemtuzumab, and other intensified regimens are off-label and rest largely on nonrandomized or case-level evidence.

Conclusion

Management should combine early recognition, careful exclusion of competing diagnoses, and coordinated oncology-cardiology decision-making. Current evidence does not justify uniform screening thresholds or a standard rescue regimen, and investigational biomarkers, imaging probes, and targeted immunomodulators require prospective validation.

title: Cilostazol and Risk of Major Adverse Limb and Cardiovascular Events after Revascularisation for Peripheral Artery Disease.
authorString: Shu-Han Lin D, Wu HP, Chung WJ, Hsueh SK, Hsu PC, Lee JK, Chen CC, Huang HL.

journal.title: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery

abstractText:
Objective

Patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD) remain at high risk of major adverse limb events (MALE) and cardiovascular events (MACE) after revascularisation. Cilostazol, a phosphodiesterase-3 inhibitor with antiplatelet and antiproliferative effects, reduces re-stenosis but its real world impact on clinical outcomes is uncertain. This retrospective, nationwide, propensity score matched cohort study evaluated the effectiveness and safety of cilostazol on MALE, MACE, and all cause mortality after lower limb revascularisation for PAD.

Methods

Using the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database, patients who underwent lower limb revascularisation for PAD from 2010 - 2023, with follow up through 2024 were identified. Patients with prior cilostazol use were excluded. 1:1 propensity score matching (n = 5 464 per group) adjusted for baseline differences. Cox regression and Fine-Gray competing risk models were used to evaluate outcomes. The comparison reflects cilostazol used with or without background antithrombotic therapy.

Results

Cilostazol use was associated with significantly lower risks of MALE (78.7 vs. 154.0 events/1 000 person-years; subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR] 0.50; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.46 - 0.53) and MACE (97.9 vs. 117.1 events/1 000 person-years; hazard ratio [HR] 0.84; 95% CI 0.79 - 0.89). All cause mortality was also reduced (116.0 vs. 127.6 events/1 000 person-years; HR 0.91; 95% CI 0.86 - 0.96). Major bleeding did not differ significantly between groups (SHR 0.90; 95% CI 0.81 - 1.00), although the absolute rate was high in both groups (12.1% vs. 13.1%). Subgroup analysis showed greater limb benefit in patients not on other antiplatelet agents.

Conclusion

Cilostazol after PAD revascularisation was associated with lower risks of limb and cardiovascular events and mortality. These effects were observed without any increase in the rate of major bleeding, although this rate was high in both groups. Randomised trials focused on cardiovascular events are needed.

title: EARLY STROKE AFTER AORTIC ARCH REPAIR: COMPARATIVE AND PROPORTIONAL META-ANALYSES OF OPEN, HYBRID, AND TOTAL ENDOVASCULAR STRATEGIES.
authorString: Lourdes Del Río Solá M, Caja MJ, de la Torre Casaseca C, García EÁ, Padrón CG, Fernández SP.
abstractText:
Objective

Early stroke remains one of the most devastating complications after aortic arch repair. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated early stroke after open, hybrid, and total endovascular aortic arch repair using separate comparative and proportional frameworks.

Methods

PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception through July 27, 2026. Observational studies reporting neurological outcomes after adult open, hybrid, or total endovascular aortic arch repair were included. The primary comparative meta-analysis pooled propensity score-matched or weighted studies comparing hybrid with open repair using random-effects restricted maximum likelihood models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Separate proportional random-effects meta-analyses estimated pooled stroke incidences for each strategy. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and the Joanna. Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261461659).

Results

Thirty-four studies were included. Seven propensity score-matched or weighted cohorts comprising 948 patients (474 open and 474 hybrid repairs) contributed to the primary comparative meta-analysis. No significant difference in early stroke was identified between hybrid and open repair (OR 1.99, 95% CI 0.46-8.58; P=.292; I2=52.9%). Post hoc comparative analyses restricted to dissection cohorts (3 cohorts; 572 patients) and Zone 0 hybrid repair (3 cohorts; 448 patients) were also inconclusive and highly imprecise. In descriptive proportional analyses, pooled early-stroke incidences were 5.3% after open, 7.5% after hybrid, and 6.4% after total endovascular repair. Technique-stratified incidences were 6.1% for conventional open repair, 4.4% for open repair with frozen elephant trunk, and 5.3% for branched total endovascular repair.

Conclusion

Adjusted comparative evidence showed no significant difference in early stroke between hybrid and open aortic arch repair. Evidence for total endovascular repair remains predominantly non-comparative. Treatment should be individualised according to aortic pathology, urgency, anatomy, operative risk, and institutional expertise.

title: Short and Long-Term Results of Kidney Transplantation From Extended Criteria Donors.
authorString: Mán E, Hódi Z, Rokszin R, Rárosi F, Szederkényi E.
abstractText:
Introduction

The prevalence of chronic kidney disease (CKD) is around 9%, and with the aging of the population, it is increasing. The growing gap between the number of patients on waiting lists and the number of donors made it necessary to transplant organs from extended criteria donors (ECD).

Material and methods

Results of 211 kidney transplantations between 2013 and 2018 were analyzed retrospectively. Short- and long-term results were investigated, such as delayed graft function (DGF), post-transplantation e-GFR levels, rejection, graft and patient survival. The initial vasculopathy in "0" biopsy samples and the effect of the level of vasculopathy on the survival of the graft were also analyzed. The statistical analysis was made by SPSS 2.0 program. The level of significance was P < .05.

Results

Between 2013 and 2018, 30 transplantations (16.57%) were carried out from ECD and 181 (83.43%) from standard donors (SD). A significant difference was found in DGF (ECD n = 10 vs SD n = 27, P = .016), and in the e-GFR levels at the control in the 1, 3, and 6. Furthermore, there was no significant difference in the incidence of rejection (ECD group n = 6, SD group n = 38, P = .572) or in the 10-year death-censored graft survival (ECD 93% vs SD 85%, P = .267). According to the vasculopathy in "0" biopsy sample results, atherosclerosis was significantly higher in the ECD group (P = .02), but it did not affect graft survival significantly.

Conclusion

Transplantation from ECDs can be used safely, and it increases transplantation activity in clinical practice without serious long-term harmful effects.

title: Transcarotid Access for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement With the Evolut Self-Expanding Valve: Outcomes from a Real-World Registry.
authorString: Allen KB, Huded C, Cohen DJ, Reardon M, Saxon J, Modine T, Leroux L, Paone G, Kemp C, Eisenberg R, Grier E, Chhatriwalla AK.
abstractText:
Background

Transcarotid access for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is the most commonly used alternate access in the United States. Real-world evidence on transcarotid access using the Evolut self-expanding valve based on larger numbers of patients may help inform treatment optimization towards better outcomes.

Methods

The Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapies Registry™ was queried for patients undergoing native TAVR using transcarotid access with an Evolut (January 2015-December 2024). In-hospital, 30-day, and 1-year outcomes are reported.

Results

We identified 2,105 patients (mean age 78.3±7.9 years) with mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons predicted risk of mortality 6.4±5.3. Most were high/extreme surgical risk (60.0%) with New York Heart Association class III/IV heart failure symptoms (66.8%) and mean baseline Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) Score 45.3±25.4. Implant success was 99.6% primarily using general anesthesia (95.8%) with median procedure time of 88.0 (Q1=68.0, Q3=115.0) minutes. Median length of stay was 2.0 (Q1=1.0, Q3=3.0) days; 89.0% were discharged to home. In-hospital, 30-day and 1-year all-cause mortality was 2.1%, 3.8% and 16.5%; stroke occurred in 3.1%, 3.8% and 5.1% of patients, respectively. At 30 days, major vascular complications (1.9%), valve related (0.4%) and non-valve related (10.9%) readmissions were low. The mean change in KCCQ score from baseline to 1-year was +30.5±27.1 points.

Conclusions

Transcarotid TAVR with the Evolut TAV is an effective, safe approach for patients with unfavorable iliofemoral anatomy. Heart teams should become facile with this technique to provide optimal care across the anatomy spectrum.

title: The triad of vascular ageing: Cellular senescence, inflammaging, and epigenetic remodelling in atherosclerosis.
authorString: Dabravolski SA, Borodko DD, Antonov SA, Lukina SS, Poletaev AA, Sukhorukov VN.
abstractText: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease remains a leading global cause of the cardiovascular mortality burden, yet traditional lipid-centric models fail to explain the residual cardiovascular risk observed in older populations. This review, synthesising contemporary literature from 2020 onwards alongside foundational studies, explores the paradigm shift towards the 'geroscience hypothesis', positing that intrinsic biological ageing of the vascular wall is a potent amplifier and primary driver of atherogenesis acting in synergy with circulating lipids. We delineate a pathogenic triad: cellular senescence, systemic inflammaging, and epigenetic dysregulation. At the cellular level, mechanical and metabolic stressors force endothelial and vascular smooth muscle cells into a usually stable senescent state, triggering the Senescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype. Immunologically, ASCVD in the elderly is driven by metabolically exhausted macrophages, the emergence of clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential, and cytotoxic memory T cells. Crucially, metabolic stressors such as hyperglycaemia induce long-lasting alterations to the chromatin landscape of haematopoietic stem cells, establishing 'trained immunity' and a persistent pro-inflammatory metabolic memory. These processes are deeply governed by an altered epigenetic landscape, including the loss of protective sirtuins and aberrant RNA methylation, which dynamically accelerate biological clocks like GrimAge. Clinically, vascular ageing trajectories are highly sexually dimorphic and heavily influenced by midlife metabolic clustering and endocrine shifts and murine models suggest highly sexually dimorphic plaque immunophenotypes. Finally, we evaluate the translational frontier of precision senotherapeutics. We contrast senomorphics, such as repurposed metformin and natural polyphenols that suppress the SASP, with targeted senolytics. Emerging nanotechnology-including in vivo CAR-T lipid nanoparticles and responsive peptide nanoassemblies-offers preclinical proof-of-concept strategies to selectively clear senescent cells without systemic toxicity. Ultimately, mitigating ASCVD requires moving beyond lipid management to integratively target the biological clock of the artery.

title: Inflammation-Responsive baicalin-delivering glycocalyx-mimetic hydrogel-functionalized bioprosthetic valve for antithrombosis and immunomodulation.
authorString: Chen L, Feng Y, Huang X, Jiang D, Zheng C, Wang Y.
abstractText: Valvular heart disease (VHD), a prevalent age-associated condition associated with high mortality, is primarily treated by prosthetic valve replacement. Bioprosthetic heart valves (BHVs) are increasingly preferred in clinical practice owing to their favorable hemodynamic performance and compatibility with transcatheter delivery. However, current glutaraldehyde crosslinking fails to confer antithrombotic, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory properties, leaving BHVs prone to thrombosis, oxidative stress, inflammation, and calcification, all of which accelerate structural valve deterioration (SVD) and shorten their lifespan. Herein, an inflammation-responsive, glycocalyx-mimetic hydrogel-functionalized BHV (BA@ALG-PP) was constructed using mussel-inspired catechol chemistry, which integrated a vascular glycocalyx-like layer with baicalin-loaded, reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive nanoparticles. With the introduction of a biocompatible glycocalyx-mimetic layer on the xenogeneic collagenous matrix, BA@ALG-PP exhibited improved antithrombotic and endothelialization performance, which was further confirmed in vivo by the rabbit intravascular implantation experiment. Moreover, the ROS-responsive nanoparticles effectively scavenged oxidative species and enabled stimulus-responsive on-demand release of anti-inflammatory molecule baicalin, thereby modulating local inflammatory responses. Transcriptional analysis of macrophages indicated that BA@ALG-PP regulated the expression of key inflammatory-related genes (Tnfaip3, Hmox1, Stat1, and Saa3) as well as suppressed pro-inflammatory signaling pathways, including NF-κB, MAPK, and JAK-STAT. Furthermore, BA@ALG-PP demonstrated improved anti-calcification property in the subcutaneous implantation experiments in rats. Collectively, this multifunctional strategy endows BHVs with synergistic antithrombotic, antioxidant, immunomodulatory, and anti-calcification capabilities, thereby offering a potential strategy for improving BHV performance that warrants further investigation in large animal models and potentially mitigating factors contributing to SVD. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Glutaraldehyde-crosslinked bioprosthetic heart valves (BHVs) suffer from structural valve deterioration driven by thrombosis, oxidative stress, and chronic inflammation, yet current surface engineering strategies remain functionally limited. This study reports an inflammatory-responsive glycocalyx-mimetic hydrogel functionalized BHV (BA@ALG-PP) engineered via mussel-inspired catechol chemistry. The system integrates non-glutaraldehyde crosslinking, ROS-responsive baicalin release, and endothelial glycocalyx mimicry into a multifunctional platform. BA@ALG-PP demonstrates enhanced antithrombotic performance, accelerated endothelialization, effective ROS scavenging, and macrophage polarization from M1 to M2 phenotype through NF-κB, MAPK, and JAK-STAT pathway modulation. Furthermore, it significantly reduces calcification in vivo. This work establishes a comprehensive strategy for BHV crosslinking and surface engineering, offering a clinically translatable strategy to prolong BHV durability and improve patient outcomes.

title: Staphylococcus aureus Purulent Myopericarditis and Cardiac Tamponade in a Patient With Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
authorString: Roslund C, Checchio L, Schneider S, Daudelin I, DeCaro M, Farzad D, Marhefka GD.
abstractText:
Background

Purulent bacterial pericarditis (or myopericarditis) is a rare condition that can lead to the development of pericardial effusion and cardiac tamponade.

Case summary

We report a complicated case of methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus myopericarditis complicated by cardiac tamponade in a young, immunocompromised patient undergoing treatment for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).

Discussion

This case highlights how SLE and immunosuppression can predispose patients to rare, life-threatening infections such as purulent myopericarditis. We review potential mechanisms of how bacterial pathogens may seed the pericardial space, as well as different treatment options that should be considered, including intravenous and, in some cases, intrapericardial antibiotic delivery.

Take-home messages

Purulent pericardial effusions can rapidly develop and progress to cardiac tamponade, hemodynamic instability, and death if not recognized promptly. SLE and immunosuppression are risk factors for the development of this rare condition.

title: Purulent MRSA Pericarditis Secondary to Chronic Diabetic Foot Osteomyelitis: A Case Report.
authorString: Itani M, Rivera-Alvarez G.
abstractText: Purulent pericardial effusion is a rare but life-threatening manifestation of bacterial infection, most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia. We report the case of an 86-year-old female with chronic diabetic foot osteomyelitis complicated by persistent methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) bacteremia. The patient subsequently developed purulent pericarditis, bilateral exudative pleural effusions, septic shock, and acute renal failure requiring continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) after intolerance to intermittent hemodialysis due to refractory hypotension. Despite broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy and drainage of infected compartments, the patient developed refractory multiorgan failure and expired on hospital Day 26. This case highlights the high mortality associated with purulent pericarditis in the setting of persistent bacteremia and delayed source control.

title: Pre-Operative Ankle Brachial Index in Assessing Major Amputation Level and Outcomes in Patients With Peripheral Artery Disease.
authorString: Wetoska N, Shiva A, Hardy J, Park A, Jreij G, Nagarsheth K.
abstractText: BackgroundThe ankle brachial index (ABI) is a non-invasive tool used to assess vessel stenosis hindering limb perfusion. It is commonly used in diagnosis of peripheral artery disease (PAD). We propose that this diagnostic tool may have predictive applications in amputation level of patients with PAD and may contribute to the diagnostic evaluation of CLTI.Materials and MethodsThis study is a retrospective chart review of 97 patients with PAD admitted from 2014 to 2022 who underwent major lower extremity amputation (MLEA) at a major tertiary referral center. Patients were stratified into two groups by ABI severity (ABI ≤0.4: severe PAD, 0.4P = 0.013; OR = 2.833) as a primary MLEA surgery. Receiver operator curve (ROC) shows that at an ABI threshold of 0.42, the model achieves a sensitivity of 0.58 and a specificity of 0.65, yielding a Youden's J of 0.23. There was no difference in readmission, ipsilateral revision, or 5-year mortality between cohorts.DiscussionBased on our cohort of 97 patients, pre-operative ABI measurements contributed modestly to amputation level assessment within the broader clinical framework; however, ABI was not independently predictive of post-operative outcomes.

title: SGLT2 inhibitors and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis receiving biologic therapy: A propensity score-matched cohort study.
authorString: Gotor-Rivera A, Hernández Sánchez J, Chamorro Jiménez E, García Rivera E, Ortiz Romero PL, Rivera-Diaz R.
abstractText:
Background

Patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis have an increased risk of cardiovascular disease. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors provide cardiovascular benefits, but their association with cardiovascular outcomes in patients with psoriasis remains insufficiently studied.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the global TriNetX research network. Patients older than 40 years with plaque psoriasis receiving biologic therapy were categorized according to SGLT2 inhibitor use. Propensity score matching was performed to balance demographic characteristics, cardiovascular risk factors, kidney disease, and concomitant antidiabetic medications.

Results

After matching, 2,016 patients were included in each cohort. SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with a significantly lower incidence of acute myocardial infarction (HR, 0.601; 95%CI, 0.426-0.849), stroke (HR, 0.553; 95%CI, 0.381-0.804), heart failure (HR, 0.751; 95%CI, 0.581-0.970), peripheral artery disease (HR, 0.648; 95%CI, 0.470-0.894), and angina pectoris (HR, 0.601; 95%CI, 0.404-0.894). No significant association was observed for transient ischemic attack.

Conclusions

SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with favorable cardiovascular outcomes in patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis receiving biologic therapy. These findings support further prospective investigation of SGLT2 inhibitors as a potential strategy for cardiovascular risk reduction in this population.

title: Body Height and Stentgraft Diameter Drive Thrombus Formation After Frozen Elephant Trunk Repair: A Risk-Focused Analysis.
authorString: Kletzer J, Kondov S, Lescan M, Dimov A, Berger T, Czerny M, Kreibich M.
abstractText:
Background

Intraluminal thrombus formation is an increasingly recognized complication after frozen elephant trunk (FET) repair. This study aims to identify the key factors driving thrombus risk, and to characterize the prognostic impact of thrombus on long-term survival.

Methods

Retrospective single-center analysis of 458 patients undergoing FET repair between 2013 and 2024. Parameters were evaluated for association with new intraluminal thrombus formation using Fine-Gray competing risk regression. Thrombus risk was visualized using a height-stentgraft diameter risk heatmap. Estimated intraprosthetic blood velocity was analyzed by receiver-operating-characteristic analysis and restricted cubic splines.

Results

Sixty patients (13.1%) developed new intraluminal thrombus during a median follow-up of 3.2 years (IQR 1.1-5.5). In multivariable analysis, the standardized stentgraft-to-patient-height-ratio was independently associated with new thrombus formation (HR 1.55 [95% confidence interval 1.11-2.16]; p=0.009), alongside fresh frozen plasma transfusion (HR 1.46 [95% CI 1.00-2.13]; p=0.049). The risk-heatmap demonstrated highest adjusted thrombus risk in short-statured patients receiving large-diameter stentgrafts. Estimated intraprosthetic blood velocity was significantly lower in patients who developed thrombus; an optimal velocity threshold of 14.4 cm/s (area under the curve 0.644; sensitivity 82.8%, specificity 43.2%) was associated with a 3-fold higher thrombus rate below vs. above this threshold (16.1% vs. 5.0%). Maximum thrombus diameter was an independent predictor of death within the thrombus subgroup (HR 1.130 [1.041-1.227] per mm; p=0.004).

Conclusions

Post-FET thrombus risk is highest when a disproportionately large stentgraft is implanted in a short-statured patient; reduced intraprosthetic blood velocity may represent a contributing hemodynamic mechanism, a hypothesis-generating finding that requires prospective validation.

title: Midterm Outcomes of the Minos Ultralow Profile Endograft: Results from the Multicentre MINER Registry.
authorString: Antonello M, Bilato MJ, Cognolato D, Talarico F, Silingardi R, Chiappa R, Bonvini S, Marone EM, Ronchey S, Grego F, Piazza M, Squizzato F, MINER Investigators.

journal.title: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery

abstractText:
Objective

The aim of this study was to assess midterm outcomes of the ultralow profile Minos endograft in a physician initiated registry.

Methods

A non-sponsored registry collected consecutive patients treated with the Minos device in 20 Italian centres (2021 - 2025). Elective patients (the primary analysis population) were stratified by access quality (hostile vs. standard access); hostile iliac-femoral access was defined by a narrowest iliac diameter < 7 mm, iliac artery tortuosity index > 1.6, aortic bifurcation diameter < 16 mm, or severe circumferential calcification. Proximal neck features were covariates only; urgent and emergent procedures were analysed separately. Outcomes were thirty day technical success, mortality, and major adverse events (MAEs), and midterm freedom from rupture, limb occlusion, type I or III endoleak, and re-intervention.

Results

Of 310 patients (mean aneurysm diameter 54.8 ± 10.0 mm), 288 (92.9%) were elective. Among these, 154 (53.5%) had a standard access and 134 (46.5%) a hostile access. The latter were more frequently women (16.4% vs. 6.0%; p = .009) and more frequently had peripheral arterial disease (31.6% vs. 16.8%; p = .006). Elective technical success was 100%, with no thirty day deaths. The thirty day MAE rate was higher with hostile access (8.2% vs. 1.3%; p = .032), mainly from access related events and blood loss > 1 000 mL (3.7% vs. 0.0%; p = .021), as was early re-intervention (3.7% vs. 0.0%; p = .021). At 3 years there were no aneurysm related deaths; freedom from limb occlusion was 97% vs. 100% (p = .025) and from type I OR III endoleak was 98% vs. 100% (p = .18) in the standard and hostile access groups, respectively.

Conclusion

The Minos ultralow profile endograft was safe and effective for the treatment of elective abdominal aortic aneurysms. Peri-operative morbidity was higher when the iliac-femoral access was hostile, and limb occlusion, type I - III endoleak, and re-intervention were more evident compared with standard access anatomy. An ultralow profile platform can extend endovascular repair to unfavourable access vessels without affecting midterm device performance.

title: A New HOPE for Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome: Technique for Primary En-Bloc Heart and Aorta Transplant with Hypothermic Oxygenated Recovery of a DCD Heart.
authorString: Thomassen MB, Moeslund N, McCheyne A, Bivona C, Henriksson H, Warburton J, Lenbroch KV, Helming L, Walker M, Runge M, Henderson P, Kenny LA.

journal.title: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation

abstractText:
Background

Primary heart transplantation for hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) has been limited by the scarcity of neonatal donors. Although hypothermic oxygenated machine perfusion (HOPE) enables donation after circulatory death (DCD) heart transplantation, previous cannulation techniques sacrificed the donor aortic arch, precluding the reconstruction required for HLHS.

Methods

A neonatal-sized porcine DCD heart was recovered with the entire thoracic aorta preserved en-bloc using a novel split-cannulation strategy compatible with HOPE. Following 304 minutes of ex situ preservation, the heart-aorta graft was transplanted into a recipient after reconstruction designed to replicate HLHS anatomy. Graft function, haemodynamics, myocardial oedema, and systemic outflow were assessed.

Results

The split-cannulation strategy enabled stable HOPE preservation of the intact heart-thoracic aorta graft throughout ex situ perfusion. Myocardial oedema was minimal (8% weight increase during preservation, 2% above baseline after transplantation). Successful implantation was demonstrated by spontaneous recovery of electrical activity, restoration of sinus rhythm, progressive improvement in cardiac output, and satisfactory ventricular contraction on epicardial echocardiography. No significant pressure gradient was detected across the reconstructed aortic arch.

Conclusions

This study demonstrates the technical feasibility of recovering, preserving, and transplanting an intact neonatal-sized DCD heart-thoracic aorta graft using a novel split-cannulation HOPE strategy. By preserving the donor thoracic aorta for arch reconstruction, this technique overcomes a key anatomical barrier to primary DCD heart transplantation for HLHS and provides the technical foundation for clinical translation.

title: Atrial Septostomy and Left Ventricular Venting During Peripheral VA-ECMO.
authorString: Kapoor AB, Stouffer J, Sarma D, Nayak N, Visrodia P, Petree B, Adjei E, Dereshgi AT, Hollis EN, O'Leary J, Alvis B, Williams A, Bacchetta M, Rali AS.
abstractText:
Background

Peripheral venoarterial (VA)-extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) increases left ventricular (LV) afterload, and therefore the risk of LV distension, pulmonary edema, and cardiac stasis. Balloon atrial septostomy (BAS) provides atrial-level unloading, but the durability of LV venting remains uncertain.

Objectives

This study aimed to evaluate the clinical effectiveness of BAS for LV venting in patients requiring peripheral VA-ECMO for cardiogenic shock (CS).

Methods

The authors conducted a retrospective study of consecutive adults with CS supported with peripheral VA-ECMO who underwent BAS for LV unloading at an academic center (2019-2024). The primary endpoint was LV venting failure, a composite of pulmonary edema, LV distension, spontaneous echocardiographic contrast, LV or aortic root thrombus, stroke due to ECMO, or escalation to additional mechanical support.

Results

A total of 28 patients were included in the study. BAS resulted in a significant reduction in mean left atrial pressure (20.5-13.5 mm Hg; P < 0.001). Durable LV venting was achieved in a subset of patients; however, LV venting failure occurred in 53.6%, driven primarily by pulmonary edema. Pulse-pressure trajectories differed according to eventual LV venting-failure status (interaction P = 0.018). Model-estimated pulse pressure was higher at 48 hours (P = 0.010) and 72 hours (P = 0.031) among patients who ultimately did not experience venting failure.

Conclusions

Among patients receiving peripheral VA-ECMO for CS, BAS achieves atrial-level decompression and may provide durable LV venting in select patients, although venting failure remains common. Observed arterial pulse-pressure trajectories differed according to eventual LV venting failure status.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes following aortic valve replacement: a nationwide observational study.
authorString: Krasniqi L, Hamandi M, Mortensen PE, Nissen H, Pellikka PA, Borlaug BA, Gerke O, Haujir A, Krasniqi LO, Terkelsen CJ, Riber LP, Dahl JS.
abstractText:
Background

GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce major adverse cardiovascular events among patients with diabetes, overweight, and obesity. Whether these benefits extend to patients undergoing aortic valve replacement (AVR) for severe aortic stenosis (AS) remains unknown. Thus, we investigated the association between GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes after AVR.

Methods

Nationwide population-based cohort study including consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI or SAVR in Western Denmark between January, 2016 and April, 2022. Patients were followed until death, emigration, crossover, or end of follow up on May 12, 2026. Propensity score-matching was performed to balance confounding. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, or aortic valve reoperation. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, aortic valve reoperation, with analyses accounting for the competing risk of death.

Results

Among 5259 eligible patients undergoing AVR, 292 propensity score-matched patients were included in the final analyses. During a mean follow up of 4.8±2.4 years, GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite outcome compared with controls (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.50-0.96, p=0.029). GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was also associated with lower risk of all-cause mortality (HR 0.66, 95%CI 0.46-0.95, p=0.025). In competing risk analyses accounting for death, lower risks were observed for heart failure hospitalization (HR 0.67, 95%CI 0.48-0.93, p=0.018), and aortic valve reoperation (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.49-0.98, p=0.037).

Conclusion

Treatment with GLP-1 receptor agonists was associated with lower risk of cardiovascular outcomes including mortality following AVR among patients with severe AS.

title: The emerging molecular landscape of abdominal aortic aneurysms: non-coding RNAs as diagnostic and therapeutic targets.
authorString: Skórka P, Brelik J, Kiełbowski K, Dorsz D, Szulc J, Bakinowska E, Rynio P, Pawlik A.
abstractText: An abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a progressive, often asymptomatic condition whose rupture is associated with a high mortality rate. Ultrasonography and computed tomography are established diagnostic methods, while molecular biomarkers may provide additional information about disease activity. This review discusses the potential role of non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) as diagnostic and therapeutic tools in AAAs. These molecules, including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) and circular RNAs (circRNAs), are strongly involved in the regulation of gene expression. Through binding to their target mRNAs, miRNAs primarily suppress translation or promote mRNA degradation. Some lncRNAs and circRNAs act as miRNA sponges, affecting their availability. Here, these mechanisms are discussed by pathological function, distinguishing human tissue and circulating studies from animal, cellular and computational findings. Particular attention is given to miR-21, H19, GAS5, circCdyl and miR-26b-3p, which have functional experimental evidence or human biomarker data beyond expression profiling. Abnormal expression can be detected in peripheral blood or aortic tissue, but these findings do not necessarily predict aneurysm growth or rupture. Integration of ncRNA profiling with imaging and clinical parameters may improve the assessment of AAAs. However, prospective validation and further studies of delivery and safety are needed before these molecules can be used in clinical practice.

title: Occult Penetrating Trauma: A STEMI Mimic Hiding in Plain Sight.
authorString: He X, Li Y, Luo W, Dang H.
abstractText:
Background

We report a case of acute pericarditis caused by an occult penetrating foreign body manifesting as an ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction mimic.

Case summary

The patient initially presented with chest pain, increased cardiac troponin I, and ST-segment elevation. Following emergency intravenous thrombolysis and urgent coronary angiography, an alternative etiology was suspected. Subsequent verification of the medical history and imaging examinations ultimately identified the culprit: a nail. The patient received prompt treatment, and the pericardial foreign body was successfully extracted.

Discussion

Acute pericarditis and acute myocardial infarction are common causes of acute chest pain. Diagnostic confusion and treatment delays may arise due to overlapping symptoms, elevation of cardiac biomarkers, ST-segment elevation, cognitive bias, and incomplete history taking.

Take-home messages

This case highlights the value of bedside echocardiography combined with chest radiography. In patients with suspected ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, it is crucial to differentiate acute coronary occlusion from other causes, especially foreign body-induced pericarditis.

title: Intraoperative ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Complicating Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair.
authorString: Lu X, Luo Y, Wang F, Cao W, Cheng J, Lu P, Xu S, Luo J.
abstractText:
Background

Acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction concurrent with endovascular aneurysm repair for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm is an extremely rare and life-threatening emergency, currently lacking unified clinical guidelines for reference.

Case summary

A 61-year-old male patient underwent endovascular aneurysm repair for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm and experienced persistent hypotension during the procedure. Postprocedural electrocardiogram and cardiac enzyme tests confirmed acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. The patient underwent emergency coronary angiography, which revealed severe stenosis, followed by successful balloon angioplasty. The patient recovered and was discharged following multidisciplinary postoperative care.

Discussion

This case demonstrates the management principles for multiple life-threatening complications, where the clinical challenge formed by the huge retroperitoneal hematoma (bleeding risk) and the requirement for antiplatelet therapy after urgent revascularization (ischemic risk) was properly addressed. Through accurate identification, precise intervention, and multidisciplinary team collaboration, the patient was successfully rescued. This case provides a referable practical path for clinical decision-making in similar rare scenarios, highlighting the critical value of individualized treatment strategies.

title: Association between low-carbohydrate diet scores and macrovascular events or all-cause mortality in adults with type 1 diabetes in Japan.
authorString: Sato J, Mita T, Negami T, Fujikawa S, Nagashima H, Takagi E, Aoyama S, Otani E, Nishida Y, Ikeda F, Aso K, Watada H.
abstractText:
Aims/introduction

The effects of lifestyle factors on macrovascular events or all-cause mortality remain unclear in type 1 diabetes. We examined the associations of diet, physical activity, and sleep with these outcomes among adults with type 1 diabetes living in Japan.

Materials and methods

This multicenter prospective cohort included 352 adults with type 1 diabetes from the Juntendo-Aso Type 1 Diabetes cohort. Lifestyle factors were assessed by questionnaire. Dietary intake was evaluated using a brief-type self-administered diet history questionnaire, from which Total, Plant, and Animal low-carbohydrate diet scores were calculated. The primary composite outcome was the first occurrence of ischemic heart disease, cerebrovascular disease, peripheral artery disease, or all-cause mortality. Associations were analyzed using Cox proportional hazards models.

Results

Mean age was 51.4 ± 15.1 years, mean HbA1c was 7.9 ± 1.1%, and carbohydrate accounted for 49.3% of energy intake. During follow-up, 35 participants experienced the primary composite outcome. In multivariable Cox models, the Total LCDS (HR, 0.90; 95% CI: 0.82-0.98; P = 0.012), Plant LCDS (HR, 0.85; 95% CI: 0.76-0.94; P = 0.003), and Animal LCDS (HR, 0.93; 95% CI: 0.87-0.996; P = 0.037) were inversely associated with the outcome.

Conclusions

Among adults with type 1 diabetes living in Japan, low-carbohydrate dietary patterns, particularly the Plant low-carbohydrate diet score, were inversely associated with macrovascular events or all-cause mortality.

title: Multivariate Genomic Analysis Reveals Shared Genetic Architecture and Potential Therapeutic Targets for Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease.
authorString: Xu Y, Wang J, Zhang R, Hou C, Sun X, Li Q, Liu C.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) is a leading cause of mortality worldwide and comprises multiple clinical phenotypes, but their shared genetic architecture remains incompletely defined.

Methods

We integrated genome-wide association study summary statistics for coronary artery disease, peripheral artery disease, large-artery atherosclerotic stroke, and carotid plaque using genomic structural equation modeling to derive a multivariable ASCVD common factor. We applied fine-mapping, multi-marker analysis of genomic annotation, transcriptome-wide association studies, Mendelian randomization, colocalization, mediation analysis, and virtual screening.

Results

We identified 289 linkage disequilibrium-independent lead single-nucleotide polymorphisms mapping to 177 genomic risk loci; 13 lacked corresponding genome-wide significant signals in the input genome-wide association studies. Eleven had prior genome-wide association study catalog association records, whereas no relevant records were identified for the loci represented by rs2294777 near SASH1 and rs4843053 near AKAP13. Fine-mapping prioritized 26 putative causal variants. Integrated functional summary-based imputation, multi-tissue transcriptome-wide association study, and multi-marker analysis of genomic annotation analyses implicated 123 genes. Enrichment analyses highlighted endothelial cells and H3K27ac-marked regulatory regions. Lipidomic analyses linked higher triacylglycerols and sterol esters to increased multivariable ASCVD common factor risk. Protein Mendelian randomization analyses in deCODE and Fenland prioritized aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (ALDH2), phosphodiesterase 5A (PDE5A), HtrAserinepeptidase 1 (HTRA1), and transcription elongation factor A2 (TCEA2) as candidate targets. Colocalization supported a shared causal variant between TCEA2 and multivariable ASCVD common factor. Mediation analyses suggested partial mediation by diastolic blood pressure for ALDH2, PDE5A, and TCEA2 and by triglycerides for TCEA2. Virtual screening identified candidate compounds with favorable predicted binding to PDE5A and ALDH2.

Conclusions

Integrating multivariate genome-wide association study with multi-omics and causal inference analyses identified shared genetic signals associated with ASCVD susceptibility and prioritized candidate protein targets, informing future functional studies and target validation.

title: Dapagliflozin After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation According to Frailty in DapaTAVI Trial.
authorString: Gonzalez-Manzanares R, Ojeda S, Amat-Santos I, Ariza-Solé A, Romaguera R, López Otero D, Nombela-Franco L, Gheorge L, Sanz-Sánchez J, Baladrón Zorita C, Gallo I, Cobas Paz R, Muñoz García AJ, Vilalta V, Veiga Fernández G, Córdoba Soriano JG, Cepas-Gillén P, Sandín Rollán M, Flores Ríos X, Palma-Carbajal R, Martín Reyes R, Avanzas P, García Blas S, Franco-Peláez JA, Martín Moreiras J, Gonzalez Juanatey JR, Gonzalo N, Calle G, Díez JL, Santos-Martínez S, González Ferreiro R, Muñoz García E, Fernandez-Nofrerias E, Sanmartín X, Tirado G, Gutierrez Barri A, González Bermúdez I, Rosselló X, Fuster V, Ibáñez B, Raposeiras Roubín S.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

Frailty is common in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation and portends worse outcomes. Whether the benefit of posttranscatheter aortic valve implantation dapagliflozin differs by frailty is uncertain.

Methods

In this post hoc analysis, we investigated the efficacy of dapagliflozin according to frailty status in the DapaTAVI (Dapagliflozin in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial. Frailty was assessed through the Fatigue, Resistance, Ambulation, Illnesses, and Loss of Weight scale (robust=0, prefrail=1-2, frail=3-5). The primary outcome was the composite of all-cause death or worsening heart failure at 1 year.

Results

Among 1222 patients with baseline frailty assessment, 47.2% were frail, 40.3% prefrail, and 12.4% robust. Over 12 months, 215 patients (17.6%) experienced the primary end point. Patients who were prefrail and frail had higher risk than robust patients (adjusted hazard ratios [HRs], 1.88 [95% CI, 1.05-3.38] and 2.29 [1.29-4.07], respectively; P=0.004). Dapagliflozin was associated with a lower risk of the primary end point in patients who were frail (HR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.36-0.77]) but not in those who were prefrail (HR, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.66-1.55]) or robust patients (HR, 1.26 [95% CI, 0.42-3.75]); P for interaction=0.021. There was no evidence that frailty modified the safety profile of dapagliflozin.

Conclusions

Frailty was common and independently associated with worse outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation. Dapagliflozin appeared to confer greater relative benefit in patients with frailty.

title: Echocardiographic Assessment and Clinical Applications of the Left Atrial Stiffness Index in Cardiovascular Disease.
authorString: Liu X, Xu H, Tong Y, Ding Y, Wang S.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText: The left atrial stiffness index is an emerging echocardiographic marker that integrates pressure-related burden and atrial reservoir deformation to provide a composite measure of left atrial pressure-deformation coupling. This review summarizes the pathophysiological basis of left atrial stiffness, the methodological principles underlying echocardiographic left atrial stiffness index assessment, and the current evidence supporting its clinical applications across cardiovascular diseases. The strongest evidence is available in heart failure and atrial fibrillation, in which increased left atrial stiffness index has been associated with adverse hemodynamics, exercise intolerance, rhythm recurrence, and adverse clinical outcomes. In hypertension, cardiomyopathies, valvular heart disease, and congenital or aortic disorders, available data suggest potential clinical relevance, although the evidence remains more heterogeneous and less mature; by contrast, evidence in ischemic, inflammatory, and stroke-related settings is still preliminary. Despite its physiological appeal, broader clinical adoption remains limited by methodological heterogeneity, variable thresholds, limited invasive validation, and uncertain incremental value beyond its component measures. At present, left atrial stiffness index is best positioned as an adjunctive marker for phenotyping, hemodynamic assessment, and risk stratification, particularly in heart failure and atrial fibrillation, pending further methodological harmonization and prospective disease-specific validation.

title: Exercise and Thoracic Aortic Aneurysms: A Paradigm Shift Toward Informed, Personalized Activity Guidelines.
authorString: Jabagi H, Imperatore G, Nantsios A, Sun LY, Lewis A, Boodhwani M, Mir H, Takayama H, Patel H, Burns P, Grau JB.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText: Exercise is widely recognized for its cardiovascular benefits; however, its safety and role in patients with thoracic aortic aneurysms (TAAs) remains complex due to its distinctive biomechanical vulnerabilities. Fundamentally different from abdominal aortic aneurysms, TAAs develop from distinct pathophysiological processes that affect their hemodynamic responses to stressors and influence their risk of adverse aortic events. Exercise induces acute hemodynamic changes, including increased stroke volume, systolic and pulse pressures, and transient aortic stiffening. These changes impose mechanical stress on the aortic wall, potentially accelerating aneurysm progression or triggering adverse aortic events. Although moderate aerobic exercise generally appears safe with potential cardiovascular benefits, evidence supporting safe practices in TAAs is limited. Current guidelines frequently extrapolate from abdominal aortic aneurysm data, which overlook the specificities of the thoracic aorta. This review underscores the urgent need for comprehensive research, using advanced imaging, biomarker profiling, and real-time hemodynamic monitoring to understand how different exercise modalities and intensities affect TAAs. Well-designed prospective studies are crucial to improve risk stratification, optimize antihypertensive strategies, develop personalized exercise prescriptions, and provide evidence-informed guidance to patients. Perioperative strategies like prehabilitation and structured postoperative rehabilitation show promise but lack rigorous evaluation. Ultimately, this work advocates a paradigm shift from conservative inactivity toward informed, individualized physical activity regimens tailored to each patient's risk profile. This approach aims to maximize cardiovascular benefits while minimizing adverse aortic events, thereby improving overall health and quality of life in patients with TAAs.

title: Preoperative Anxiety Among Hospitalized Pediatric Patients with CHD: A Qualitative Study From the Perspectives of Health Care Professionals and Parents.
authorString: Li Q, Yanglan R, Yang J, Wang Y, Peng S, Yao W, Zhang J, Ma F.

journal.title: Journal of perianesthesia nursing : official journal of the American Society of PeriAnesthesia Nurses

abstractText:
Purpose

Preoperative anxiety commonly occurs in children with congenital heart disease(CHD), undermining their psychological function and postoperative recovery. Targeted anxiety interventions require a systematic understanding of children's preoperative stress. As key caregivers, parents and health care professionals(HCPs) undrepin intervention development; therefore, this study aimed to explore how parents and HCPs perceive preoperative anxiety in pediatric patients with CHD within the Chinese cutural and social context.

Design

This studyadopted a descripitive phenomenological qualitative approach.

Methods

. Between January and April 2026, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 23 parents of pediatric patients with CHD and nine HCPs in a tertiary hospital in Kunming. Interview data were managed via NVivo 12.0 and analyzed through thematic analysis.

Findings

(1) Existence versus non-existence of preoperative anxiety, (2) Preoperative anxiety due to children and parental factors, (3) Diverse manifestations of preoperative anxiety, and (4) Ways of coping with Preoperative Anxiety.

Conclusions

Anxiety in pediatric patients with CHD is sometimes suppressed or overlooked. It is crucial to improve the ability of parents and HCPs to identify pediatric anxiety and encourage children to express their emotions. Surgery-related information should be delivered to children in age-appropriate and comprehensible language. Given the communal nature of family emotions, parental negative emotions also require attention, and unnecessary parent-child separation should be minimized. Among the management strategies for preoperative anxiety, pharmacological interventions exert rapid effects, while non-pharmacological interventions are more favored due to the absence of adverse reactions. Influenced by the Confucian culture of "forbearance", some parents tend to ignore their children's anxious emotions, highlighting the importance of educating parents about the value of appropriate support.

title: Prenatal echocardiographic predictors that increase the risk of urgent Ballon Atrial Septostomy (BAS) after birth in patients with Dextro-Transposition of the Great Arteries- Retrospective Study from Tertiary Center Lodz- Poland ICZMP (2014-2024).
authorString: Moszura A, Strzelecka I, Respondek-Liberska M.
abstractText:
Objective

Dextro-transposition of the great arteries (d-TGA) is a critical congenital heart disease (CHD) requiring prompt postnatal intervention, primarily: a line for Prostin infusion, hospitalization in an Intensive Care Unit, and in some cases, Balloon Atrial Septostomy (BAS) as a rescue procedure before planned Arterial Switch Operation (ASO). In this part, we focus on prenatal prediction of postnatal BAS.

Materials and methods

This retrospective study was conducted at the Department of Prenatal Cardiology, Polish Mother's Memorial Hospital in Lodz, covering the years 2014-2024. From a total of 112 prenatally diagnosed d-TGA cases, 70 fetuses (46 with isolated d-TGA and 24 with d-TGA and VSD) met the inclusion criteria; follow-up of four pregnancies ended up in other hospitals, so the final series was 66 cases. Statistical analyses were performed using Statistica software.

Results

Out of 66 analyzed cases, 32 newborns (48%) required postnatal BAS, with 87.5% of these procedures performed within the first 24-48 hours of life. Prenatal echocardiography correctly predicted the postnatal management pathway in 90.9% of cases (60/66), identifying all 26 neonates requiring urgent balloon atrial septostomy (100% positive predictive value), while 6 neonates in the planned group required unexpected postnatal septostomy. We noted that the 18% (n=6) of cases not identified prenatally occurred when the last scan was performed > 14 days before birth, suggesting that the time interval significantly impacts the reliability of late-gestation FO assessment. The study identified 10 prenatal "red flags," including FO size < 3 mm, bi-directional FO flow, and pulmonary vein velocity ≥ 45 cm/s and other features, as high-reliability indicators for urgent postnatal intervention.

Conclusion

Prenatal functional assessment of the foramen ovale in the late third trimester was highly effective in predicting the need for postnatal urgent BAS in d-TGA cases. The accuracy of these "red flags" was significantly higher when the last fetal echocardiogram was performed within 14 days to delivery.

title: Congenital Cardiac Surgical Workforce Inequities Across 194 Countries: A Global Cross-Sectional Analysis.
authorString: Francis J, Corno AF, Peng E.
abstractText: Congenital heart disease is the most common birth defect globally, yet access to surgery remains inequitable. The availability of congenital heart surgeons (CHS) relative to paediatric population needs is poorly defined. A cross-sectional study of the Cardiothoracic Surgery Network was conducted across 194 United Nations-recognised countries and 54 territories and dependencies (T&Ds). Of 248 countries and T&Ds analysed, 123 (49.6%) had ≥ 1 CHS. A total of 4,296 CHS were identified; 71 (37% of recognised) countries with 189.5 million children had none. Low-income countries had a median of 0.15 CHS per million children compared with 9.29 in high-income countries. CHS density was strongly correlated with gross domestic product per capita. Average CHS ratios per million children were: high-income country 9.3, upper-middle-income country 2.0, lower-middle-income country 1.1, and low-income country 0.2 (p < 0.0001), representing a 46-fold disparity between high-income countries and low-income countries. Regional analysis showed North America and Europe had the highest CHS ratios (≥ 9 per million), and Sub-Saharan Africa and East Asia and Pacific had medians of zero (p < 0.0001). Only 3 T&Ds reported at least one CHS. Our findings confirm that human resource levels are even more disproportionate than previously estimated. A significant proportion of children globally remain without access to cardiac surgery, representing a major and largely unquantified burden of preventable morbidity and mortality. Accurately quantifying this unmet need should be an urgent priority for future population-level and health systems research.

title: Comparison of Feeding, Nutritional, and Procedural Outcomes in Infants with Ductal-Dependent Pulmonary Blood Flow Undergoing Surgical Systemic-to-Pulmonary Artery Shunt Versus Ductal Stenting.
authorString: Tran P, MacBeth M, Wolfe K, Vichayavilas P, Olson KE, Leahy R, Stone M, SooHoo M.
abstractText: Ductal stenting and surgical systemic-to-pulmonary artery shunting (surgical shunt) are alternative strategies to establish pulmonary blood flow in infants with ductal-dependent circulation. The impact of palliation strategy on feeding, nutrition, and neurodevelopment remains unclear. We conducted a single-center retrospective study of 100 infants with ductal-dependent pulmonary blood flow (2017-2024) undergoing surgical shunt (n = 57) or ductal stenting (n = 43). Outcomes included feeding, nutrition, hospital course, and neurodevelopment. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated factors associated with gastrostomy tube (GT) placement. Baseline demographics were similar except for cardiac anatomy. Ductal stent patients reached target enteral feeds post-procedurally sooner (3 vs. 6 days, p < 0.001), had higher discharge weight-for-age z-scores (- 1.30 vs. -1.98, p = 0.02), and smaller declines in growth during hospitalization (p = 0.007). GT placement was less frequent following ductal stenting (26% vs. 51%, p = 0.011), but palliation strategy was not independently associated with GT placement after adjustment (OR 0.43, 95% CI 0.14-1.24, p = 0.12). Oral feeding or breastfeeding within 5 days following palliation was independently associated with lower odds of GT placement (OR 0.24, 95% CI 0.06-0.81, p = 0.03). Ductal stent patients also had shorter mechanical ventilation and ICU stays and required less vasoactive-inotropic support. Total hospital length of stay, need for reintervention, suspected or diagnosed necrotizing enterocolitis, and mortality did not differ significantly between groups. Ductal stenting was associated with improved early post-procedural recovery, faster feeding progression, and better preservation of growth compared with surgical shunt palliation. Although GT placement was less frequent following ductal stenting in unadjusted analysis, palliation strategy was not independently associated with GT placement after adjustment. Early post-procedural oral feeding was independently associated with lower odds of GT placement but may also reflect feeding readiness and clinical recovery.

title: Transplantation for Congenital Heart Disease in Children-A Quest to Do Better.
authorString: Rosenthal LM, Koehl D, Cantor R, Laks J, Shugh S, Dyal J, Kirklin J, Haller C, Power A, Dipchand AI.
abstractText: Children with congenital heart disease (CHD) represent the largest group of pediatric heart transplant recipients but experience lower graft survival than those transplanted for cardiomyopathy. We evaluated post-transplant outcomes among CHD recipients at the Hospital for Sick Children (HSC) and identified predictors of graft loss. Pediatric patients (< 17 years) undergoing heart transplantation for CHD between 1993 and 2023 were analyzed using the Pediatric Heart Transplant Society registry. Outcomes of CHD recipients at HSC (CHD HSC) were compared with cardiomyopathy HSC recipients, CHD recipients at other centers (CHD Non-HSC), and a propensity score-matched (PSM) cohort adjusting for pre- and peri-transplant risk factors. Kaplan-Meier survival and multivariable Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed. Among 4,362 pediatric CHD transplant recipients, 152 underwent transplantation at HSC. Freedom from graft loss for CHD HSC at 5, 10, and 15 years was 71.8%, 63.0%, and 58.4%, lower than in Cardiomyopathy HSC recipients (p < 0.0001), but similar to CHD Non-HSC (p = 0.6043). Survival remained comparable in the PSM cohort (n = 140, p = 0.4599). Conditional survival beyond 1 year was similar between groups, suggesting early mortality drives differences. CHD HSC recipients demonstrated longer freedom from CAV (p = 0.0041) and infection (p = 0.0335). Predictors of graft loss included pre-transplant ECMO (HR 3.11), ICU admission (HR 2.39), PRA > 10% (HR 2.49), African American/Black race/ethnicity (HR 2.71), and longer waitlist duration (HR 1.06). Graft survival in CHD recipients at HSC remains lower than in cardiomyopathy recipients but comparable internationally. Optimizing pre-transplant care, sensitization management, and equity-focused interventions may enhance outcomes.

title: Stroke Risk-Based Anticoagulation After Atrial Fibrillation Ablation: ALONE-AF Post-Hoc Analysis.
authorString: Lee YS, Uhm JS, Park J, Kim D, Yang PS, Yu HT, Kim TH, Shim J, Choi EK, Oh IY, Kim J, Ko JS, Park KM, Sung JH, Park HW, Park HS, Kim JY, Kang KW, Kim D, Park JK, Kim DH, Kim JB, Pak HN, Lee YS, Joung B, ALONE-AF Investigators.
abstractText:
Background

Discontinuation of oral anticoagulant (OAC) in patients without recurrent atrial arrhythmia after ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF) has been demonstrated to reduce composite outcomes of stroke, systemic embolism, and major bleeding compared with continued OAC.

Objective

This study aimed to evaluate the optimal OAC strategy according to baseline stroke risk and AF recurrence.

Methods

In this post-hoc analysis of the Long-Term Anticoagulation Discontinuation after Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation (ALONE-AF) trial, patients were stratified according to CHA2DS2-VASc score ≤2 and ≥3. Within each stratum, outcomes were compared between the OAC discontinuation and continuation subgroups. The cumulative incidence of stroke, systemic embolism, and major bleeding at 2 years was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, with competing risk analysis accounting for AF recurrence.

Results

Among 840 patients, 584 and 256 had a CHA2DS2-VASc score ≤2 (mean age 62.0±7.5 years, 15.9% female) and ≥3 (mean age 68.9±7.3 years, 45.3% female), respectively. In the CHA2DS2-VASc ≤2 stratum, the primary outcome occurred in one patient (0.4%) in discontinuation subgroup vs. six (2.4%) in continuation subgroup (absolute difference -1.9 percentage points, P=0.066). In the CHA2DS2-VASc ≥3 stratum, two events (1.8%) occurred in the continuation subgroup only (absolute difference -1.8 percentage points, P=0.172). All major bleeding events (n=5) occurred in the continuation subgroups. Competing risk analysis yielded consistent results.

Conclusions

In this exploratory post-hoc analysis, no statistically significant differences in outcomes were observed between OAC strategies when stratified by CHA2DS2-VASc score, though event numbers were limited. Larger prospective trials are needed to confirm these observations.

Trial registrations

ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04432220.

title: Steatotic liver disease phenotypes and stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation: A nationwide population-based cohort study.
authorString: Go YH, Lee SR, Kim JH, Han S, Choi J, Lee KY, Ahn HJ, Kwon S, Kim B, Han KD, Oh S, Lip GYH, Choi EK.
abstractText:
Background

The updated nomenclature of steatotic liver disease (SLD) recognizes distinct phenotypes, including Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), MASLD with increased alcohol intake (MetALD), and alcohol-related liver disease (ALD). Although cardiovascular risk may differ across SLD phenotypes, their association with stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) remains unclear.

Objective

This study aimed to investigate the association between SLD phenotypes and ischemic stroke risk in AF patients.

Methods

AF patients diagnosed between 2010 and 2018 were identified from the Korean health insurance database. According to SLD phenotype, patients were categorized into No-SLD, MASLD, MetALD, and ALD. The primary outcome was ischemic stroke. Subgroup analyses were conducted by CHA2DS2-VA score.

Results

Among 196,242 patients (No-SLD: 101,308; MASLD: 77,715; MetALD: 8,678; ALD: 8,541), median follow-up was 5.9 years. Compared with No-SLD, MASLD was not associated with stroke risk (adjusted hazard ratio and 95% confidence interval; 1.00, 0.97-1.04), whereas MetALD and ALD were associated with higher risk (1.09, 1.00-1.18 and 1.16, 1.08-1.26, respectively). In exploratory subgroup analyses, the higher risk associated with alcohol-related phenotypes appeared more apparent at lower CHA2DS2-VA scores; however, the 6-year absolute risk differences were approximately 1% or less, and these findings are regarded as hypothesis-generating.

Conclusion

In patients with AF, stroke risk was significantly higher in the alcohol-related SLD phenotypes, MetALD and ALD, whereas MASLD was not associated with stroke risk. These findings are consistent with the current recommendations for comprehensive risk-factor management in AF, with particular attention to alcohol intake in patients with alcohol-related SLD phenotypes.

title: Latent class analysis-derived patterns of comorbidities in patients with atrial fibrillation, adherence to integrated care and impact on long-term outcomes: an analysis from a prospective cohort.
authorString: Mantovani M, Vitolo M, Mei DA, Bonini N, Trapanese P, Tartaglia E, Paolini M, Orlandi M, Imberti JF, Boriani G.
abstractText:
Background

Atrial fibrillation (AF) commonly coexists with multiple cardiovascular (CV) and non-CV comorbidities, which may cluster in distinct clinical phenotypes with different outcome implications.

Objective

We aim to identify comorbidity-based phenotypes in AF using latent class analysis (LCA), characterize their clinical course and assess the association of integrated care adherence with outcomes across phenotypes.

Methods

A LCA based on 11 conditions (CV and non-CV) was performed. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, thromboembolic (TE) events, and acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Secondary outcomes were all-cause death and ACS/TE events.

Results

We included 1233 AF patients (median age 75 [66-82] years, females 37.5%). Four clinical LCA-derived phenotypes were identified: "Low comorbidity" (31.5%); "Cardio-metabolic" (33.9%); "Elderly comorbid" (22.9%); and "Atherosclerotic-HF" (11.8%). During a median follow-up of 542 days, 234 patients (22.7%) experienced the primary outcome. Compared to "Low comorbidity", "Cardio-metabolic" (aHR 1.64, 95% CI 1.13-2.39), "Elderly comorbid" (aHR 1.62, 95% CI 1.09-2.42) and "Atherosclerotic-HF" (aHR 2.81, 95%CI 1.83-4.34) phenotypes were independently associated with a higher risk of the primary outcome. Adherence to integrated care varied across phenotypes and was associated with a lower risk of adverse events, with no evidence of significant heterogeneity across phenotypes (p int=0.157).

Conclusions

Latent class analysis identified distinct AF clinical phenotypes characterized by specific patterns of comorbidities and associated with different risk of adverse outcomes. The absence of significant heterogeneity in the association between integrated care and outcomes across phenotypes supports its potential value across different levels of clinical complexity in AF patients.

title: Perioperative Management of a Toddler With Tuberous Sclerosis and Dilated Cardiomyopathy Undergoing Open Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair: A Case Report.
authorString: Ho M, Brown J, Duca J.
abstractText: Toddler abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA) are rare and lack defined perioperative guidelines. Aneurysms may be associated with tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) but rarely occur with concurrent dilated cardiomyopathy. This case report describes the anesthetic and surgical considerations for a two-year-old male with TSC and dilated cardiomyopathy with low ejection fraction undergoing open infrarenal AAA repair. Our most important perioperative considerations included advanced hemodynamic monitoring, management of intraoperative blood loss, and the physiological changes associated with aortic clamping. Transesophageal echocardiography was used throughout the operation to guide inotropic support and assess ventricular filling using renal-protective strategies and balanced transfusion.

title: Schinifoline attenuates atherosclerosis and modulates gut microbiota and bile acid metabolism in ApoE<sup>-/-</sup> mice.
authorString: Liu Q, Xi T, Wen Y, Ma L, Zou G, Yu W, Yuan Z, Yu C.
abstractText: Atherosclerosis (AS) remains a major global health burden despite advances in lipid-lowering therapies. Zanthoxylum bungeanum Maxim (ZBM) has demonstrated anti-atherosclerotic potential; however, the role of its active component, schinifoline (SF), in atherosclerosis remains unclear. In this study, we evaluated the anti-atherosclerotic effects of SF in high-fat diet (HFD)-fed ApoE<sup>-/-</sup> mice. SF treatment attenuated aortic plaque formation, improved serum lipid parameters, and decreased inflammatory responses.
