title: Efficacy, Effectiveness, and Immunogenicity of the Respiratory Syncytial Virus Prefusion F Vaccine Administered During Pregnancy: Protocol for a Living Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Mazzoni A, Bardach A, Berrueta M, Ciapponi A, Klein K, Brizuela M, Nigri C, Castellana N, Ballivian J, Sambade JM, Stegelmann K, Patel D, Atwell JE, Deese J, Cox SN, Wang L, Xiong X, Stergachis A, Munoz FM, Buekens P.
abstractText:
Background

Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract disease in infants, with the highest burden in the first 6 months of life. Maternal immunization with the bivalent (RSV-A and RSV-B) prefusion F (RSVPreF) protein subunit vaccine (ABRYSVO) is a recently recommended strategy for preventing RSV-related outcomes in infants. First licensed for use in pregnancy in 2023, the RSVPreF vaccine demonstrated efficacy in a single pivotal randomized trial (Maternal Immunization Study for Safety and Efficacy; MATISSE); postlicensure real-world evidence on vaccine effectiveness across settings, seasons, and subgroups and on antibody durability and transplacental transfer remains limited and has not been synthesized in a continuously updated framework, motivating this review.

Objective

This living systematic review and meta-analysis will synthesize emerging postlicensure data on the efficacy, effectiveness, and immunogenicity of the RSVPreF vaccine in real-world settings.

Methods

We will conduct, in real time, a living systematic review and meta-analysis following Cochrane methods and PRISMA-P (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Protocols) guidance, including randomized clinical trials and postlicensure real-world studies (eg, cohort, case-control, test-negative, and quasi-experimental studies). Primary objectives are evaluation of vaccine efficacy and effectiveness in preventing RSV-specific and all-cause respiratory disease and immunogenicity in infants and pregnant individuals. Vaccine effectiveness outcomes include RSV laboratory-confirmed infection, RSV acute respiratory illness, RSV lower respiratory tract disease, RSV hospitalization, RSV complications, all-cause lower respiratory tract disease and hospitalization, and antibiotic use in infants with RSV infection. Immunogenicity outcomes include maternal neutralizing antibody titers, maternal-infant transfer ratios, infant titers over time, and RSV viral load. We will search MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, LILACS, Science Citation Index Expanded, Chinese biomedical and citation databases, clinical trial registries from January 2023 onward with no language restrictions, updating at least monthly. Two investigators will independently select studies, extract data, and assess risk of bias. Adjusted estimates will be standardized to vaccine efficacy and effectiveness. Certainty will be graded using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) system.

Results

This living systematic review was funded in June 2025. Searches began in January 2023 and will continue with surveillance updates at least monthly until April 2028. As of January 2026, 837 records were screened, 105 (12.5%) were assessed in full text, and 12 (1.4%) met the inclusion criteria, of which 10 (1.2%) contributed extractable data. Data collection and analysis are ongoing and displayed on an interactive dashboard. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, conferences, and a real-time dashboard, with the first effectiveness estimates available in July 2026.

Conclusions

This living systematic review and meta-analysis will provide a continuously updated synthesis of real-world evidence on maternal RSVPreF vaccination to inform clinical and policy decisions.

title: Contemporary Management of Subclavian and Axillary Artery Aneurysms in Connective Tissue Disease: Navigating Therapeutic Uncertainty in a Rare Vascular Disease Without Dedicated Guidelines.
authorString: Borghese O, Lodico T, Ibrahimi A, Felice G, Sposato F, Pisani A, Tshomba Y.
abstractText:
Background

Subclavian artery aneurysms (SAAs) represent one of the rarest forms of peripheral arterial aneurysmal disease. Despite their low incidence, management in patients with underlying connective tissue disorders poses specific challenges related to intrinsic vessel fragility. Because of their rarity, the available literature is largely confined to case reports and small, heterogeneous retrospective series, and management remains largely experience-based rather than evidence-based. Explicit guidance from the Society for Vascular Surgery and the European Society for Vascular Surgery is lacking.

Methods

We performed a systematic review of the English-language literature to identify all reported cases of subclavian and axillary artery aneurysms in patients with heritable connective-tissue disorders. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to June 30, 2025. Data were extracted on treatment modality (open surgical, endovascular, or hybrid) and clinical outcomes (limb loss, revascularization patency, complications, and need for reintervention). The review protocol was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420261332695) RESULTS: Of 142 records identified, 24 studies met the inclusion criteria after duplicate removal and screening. These studies described 43 subclavian and axillary artery aneurysms in 25 patients (15 men [60%] and 10 women [40%]; median age, 46 years; range, 11-68). Aneurysm diameter was reported for 36 of 43 aneurysms (84%; median, 40 mm; range, 22-100 mm) and was not reported for the remaining 7 (16%). Marfan syndrome was the most frequent underlying disorder (20/25, 80%), followed by vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome type IV (3/25, 12%) and Loeys-Dietz syndrome/TGFBR2-related arteriopathy (2/25, 8%). Eight aneurysms (8/43, 19%) required urgent or emergent treatment. Treatment modalities comprised open surgical repair in 22 of 43 aneurysms (51%) - including interposition grafting in 12/22 (55%), bypass in 5/22 (23%), arterial ligation in 3/22 (14%), and aneurysmectomy with end-to-end anastomosis in 2/22 (9%) - hybrid procedures in 15 (35%), and endovascular therapy in 6 (14%) - including covered stent-grafting in 5/6 (83%) and coil/liquid embolization in 1/6 (17%). Immediate technical success - complete aneurysm exclusion without endoleak at the index procedure- was 95% (41 of 43 aneurysms). Two aneurysms (4.7%), both in the hybrid group, represented an index-procedure failure due to endoleak (one type I, one type III); freedom from reintervention was therefore 95% (41/43). Both were subsequently excluded after a secondary reintervention, yielding a delayed technical success rate of 100% (43/43). No 30-day mortality or limb loss was reported. Primary patency of the treated segment was 100% (43/43), as no graft/segment thrombosis, occlusion, or flow-limiting stenosis occurred; secondary patency was 100% (43/43). Where a numeric follow-up duration could be extracted, mean follow-up was 8 months (range, 6-11 months) in the endovascular group (4/5 patients), 15 months (range, 2 weeks-4 years) in the open group (5/13 patients), and 15 months (range, 1-60 months) in the hybrid group (6/7 patients); a precise duration was not reported for the remaining patients.

Conclusion

The available evidence demonstrates that both open and endovascular repair can achieve satisfactory short- and mid-term outcomes. However, patient selection, procedural planning, and surveillance protocols remain poorly standardized. The observed recurrences and the limited duration of follow-up reported in the literature underscore the need for rigorous, lifelong surveillance. Prospective multicenter registries are warranted to refine best practice and to guide the development of devices and techniques tailored to fragile connective-tissue vessels.

title: Pelacarsen and Lp(a)HORIZON: Interpreting the Disconnect Between Lipoprotein(a) Lowering and Cardiovascular Outcomes.
authorString: Sabouret P, Giamundo DM, Asher E, De Rosa S, Andò G, Gragnano F, Blumenthal RS, Atar D, Mamas MA.
abstractText: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and calcific aortic valve stenosis. Pelacarsen, a hepatocyte-directed antisense oligonucleotide targeting apolipoprotein(a), was evaluated in Lp(a)HORIZON, the first large phase 3 cardiovascular outcomes trial specifically designed to test whether pharmacological Lp(a) lowering reduces cardiovascular events. Topline results announced in September 2026 indicated that pelacarsen lowered Lp(a) but did not reduce the primary composite cardiovascular endpoint in patients with established cardiovascular disease. Full trial data are awaited, and the mechanisms underlying this neutral result remain uncertain. We discuss potential explanations, including treatment after prolonged cumulative Lp(a) exposure, advanced vascular disease, intensive background prevention, the magnitude and duration of Lp(a) suppression, patient selection, baseline cardiovascular risk, and biological heterogeneity. We also examine implications for emerging therapies, including olpasiran, zerlasiran, lepodisiran, and muvalaplin, and for the design of ongoing cardiovascular outcome trials.

title: Optimizing Echocardiographic Evaluation of Chronic Mitral Regurgitation: Comparison With Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Implications for Guideline Recommendations.
authorString: El-Tallawi KC, Angulo C, Chamsi-Pasha M, Qamar F, Graviss EA, Shah DJ, Zoghbi WA.
abstractText:
Background

The ASE (American Society of Echocardiography) guidelines recommend the presence of at least 4 specific criteria to confirm a diagnosis of definite severe mitral regurgitation (MR). However, the performance of these criteria, particularly when <4 are present, remains unclear.

Objectives

This study aims to evaluate and optimize the ASE native MR guidelines by comparing them with quantitative cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), considered the reference standard for MR assessment.

Methods

In this prospective study, 177 patients underwent near-simultaneous CMR and transthoracic echocardiography for the assessment of MR. MR severity was classified using a 4-grade scale based on CMR-derived regurgitant volume, which was calculated as the difference between total left ventricular (LV) stroke volume and aortic forward flow. MR severity was similarly graded using the ASE algorithm, with quantification performed when necessary, by averaging the regurgitant volume from 3 methods: 1) the proximal isovelocity surface area method; 2) the biplane LV volumetric method; and 3) the mitral valve volumetric method.

Results

The study cohort had a median age of 61.7 years, with 55% being men. Primary MR was the predominant pathology (73% of patients), with 42% having mitral valve prolapse and 25% presenting with flail leaflets. There was exact agreement between transthoracic echocardiography and CMR MR grading in 51% of cases, whereas agreement within 1 grade was observed in 89%. Patients who met any of the ASE severe MR criteria were predominantly classified as having grades 3 to 4 MR by CMR. The following ASE parameters demonstrated high specificity for identifying grade 4 MR by CMR: pulmonary vein systolic flow reversal (specificity 88%), enlarged LV with normal systolic function (specificity 85%), proximal isovelocity surface area radius ≥1.0 cm (specificity 83%), and vena contracta width ≥0.7 cm (specificity 80%). Combining color Doppler with either pulmonary vein systolic reversal or enlarged LV with normal function resulted in 91%-95% specificity for severe MR. Importantly, reliance on fewer ASE criteria reduced the need for quantification from 86% (4 criteria) to 73% (3 criteria) and 59% (2 criteria), thereby enhancing diagnostic efficiency.

Conclusions

Certain ASE criteria, especially when used in combination, are highly specific for diagnosing severe MR, even when <4 criteria are present. This study suggests that in many cases, the reliance on extensive quantification may be reduced, streamlining the diagnostic process and improving clinical workflow.

title: Long-Term Durability of Bare-Metal Stenting in Complex Iliac Disease: External Iliac Artery Involvement as the Principal Determinant of Late Patency Loss.
authorString: Mastrorilli D, De Massari C, Forcella E, Nicolis M, Garriboli L.
abstractText:
Objective

Long-term durability after endovascular treatment of complex aortoiliac disease remains incompletely defined. The present study evaluated late primary patency after bare-metal stenting (BMS) in TASC C-D lesions and examined whether anatomical extension beyond the common iliac artery influences long-term outcomes independently of traditional TASC classification.

Methods

A single-center retrospective cohort study was conducted including 153 consecutive iliac limbs with TASC C-D occlusive disease treated with BMS between 2014 and 2024. Covered stents, kissing configurations, and acute occlusions were excluded to ensure a homogeneous technical cohort. The primary endpoint was primary patency. Kaplan-Meier estimates were reported through 72 months. Restricted mean survival time (RMST) regression at τ = 72 months and Firth penalized logistic regression were applied to identify independent predictors while minimizing small-event bias.

Results

Technical success exceeded 97%, with no perioperative mortality. Primary patency remained high and comparable between TASC C and D lesions at 72 months (86% vs 84%; log-rank p = 0.8). In contrast, extension into the external iliac artery (EIA) was associated with progressive late attrition. Adjusted RMST analysis demonstrated a 7.6-month reduction in mean primary patency at 72 months for EIA-involved lesions (95% CI -11.6 to -3.6; p < 0.001). Firth regression confirmed increased late risk of patency loss at 60 months (OR 10.5; p = 0.034) and 72 months (OR 25.8; p = 0.003). Technical optimization (best-practice stenting) showed limited and model-dependent mitigation, without consistent protection across time points.

Conclusions

In complex iliac BMS reconstruction, long-term durability appears primarily determined by distal anatomical extension rather than TASC class. External iliac artery involvement identifies a subgroup at risk for late failure and may represent a more clinically meaningful stratification parameter for endovascular planning.

title: Current Generation Self-Expanding and Balloon-Expandable Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Retrospective Multicenter Analysis.
authorString: Scheffel EC, Putman K, Ridley LA, Wisniewski AM, Guiry J, Ramos GA, Da Cruz Alves B, Chattha A, Biswas A, Ragosta M, Akujuo AC.
abstractText:
Background

Evolving transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) technology warrants updated comparisons of the most commonly used current generation self-expanding (SE) versus balloon-expandable (BE) transcatheter heart valves (THV).

Methods

This 9-center retrospective analysis stratified patients undergoing TAVR from 2021-2024 into SE-THV and BE-THV cohorts balanced via propensity score matching. Primary outcomes were all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, stroke, and permanent pacemaker (PPM) need. Secondary outcomes were paravalvular leak (PVL) and acute kidney injury. All outcomes were assessed perioperatively and at 30 and 400 days. Analyses were repeated within LVEF , aortic valve area, and center-level strata.

Results

The total cohort included 2,594 BE-THV and 1,058 SE-THV patients. Matching yielded 680 patients per cohort. After matching , SE-THV patients had higher risk for ischemic stroke (p<0.05) and PPM (p<0.05) during index hospitalization, with no difference in mortality. At follow-up, the SE-THV cohort had higher risk of mild (p<0.05) and moderate (p<0.05) paravalvular leak, stroke (p<0.05) and PPM (p<0.05). PPM after SE-THV was significantly lower in high-volume compared to low-volume centers. Kaplan-Meier survival did not differ. Among patients with LVEF ≥45%, SE-THV was associated with higher stroke risk (p<0.05); BE-THV patients with LVEF < 45% were associated with increased all-cause mortality.

Conclusions

In this cohort, SE-THV correlated with higher rates of ischemic stroke, PPM need, and PVL during index hospitalization and increased mild and moderate PVL upon follow-up. Mortality did not differ during index hospitalization or at follow-up. The normal LVEF SE-THV cohort was associated with higher stroke risk compared to all other groups.

title: In-hospital vascular surgery consultation is associated with improved follow-up and earlier identification of aneurysmal degeneration after acute Type A aortic dissection.
authorString: Murphy BE, Lee AE, Stone KW, DeRoo SC, Burke CR, Smith MC, Sweet MP, Zettervall SL.
abstractText:
Objective

Acute Type A aortic dissections (TAAD) are historically managed by cardiac surgery. However, subsequent treatment of residual dissection within the thoracoabdominal aorta often requires vascular surgical intervention and lifelong surveillance. This study assesses long-term outcomes by completeness of follow-up after operative intervention for acute TAAD.

Methods

Patients who underwent surgical intervention for acute TAAD from 2014 to 2025 were identified. Patients who experienced death within 30-days or those with dissection limited to Zone 0/Zone 1 were excluded. Vascular surgery evaluation and time to consultation (index-hospitalization, outpatient, none) was documented. Follow-up was classified as complete, incomplete, or lost (LTF) according to the frequency of contrasted thoracoabdominal imaging, consistent with clinical practice guidelines. Trends in completeness of follow-up were described. Demographics, anatomic/operative characteristics, and perioperative outcomes were compared between complete follow-up and incomplete follow-up/LTF groups. Long-term outcomes (aortic degeneration, planned secondary intervention, survival) were assessed with Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox regression analysis.

Results

241 patients were included; 80% had vascular surgery consultation (70% inpatient, 30% outpatient) and 86% of consultations occurred within 1-year of index procedure. In total, 46% of patients had complete follow-up, 41% had incomplete follow-up, and 13% were LTF. In-hospital consultation increased by 58% over the study period. Demographics, comorbidities, and anatomic characteristics were similar between groups. Patients with complete follow-up had higher rates of complex arch repair (Zone 1-3) (complete 56% vs. incomplete/LTF 27%, p<0.001), were more likely to undergo genetic testing (complete 52% vs. incomplete/LTF 18%, p<0.001), in-hospital TEVAR extension (7% vs. 2%, p=0.028), and TEVAR extension within 3 months (complete 17% vs. incomplete/LTF 5%, p=0.002). In time-to-event analysis, complete follow-up was associated with more planned secondary interventions (complete: 12% vs. incomplete: 5%, p=0.007) and identified aneurysmal degeneration (32% vs. 15%, p=0.002) within 1-year of acute dissection. Long-term survival differed by completeness of follow-up; 1-year (complete: 97% vs. incomplete: 97% vs. LTF: 91%), 3-years (complete: 92% vs. incomplete: 95% vs. LTF: 81%, p=0.021). There were no aortic-related deaths for patients with complete follow-up and five aortic-related deaths (5%) in patients with incomplete follow-up (p=0.13). In-hospital vascular surgery consultation was associated with complete follow-up (HR 2.87, 95% CI 1.6-5.1) and planned secondary interventions (HR 2.07, 95% CI 1.1-3.9).

Conclusion

Vascular surgery consultation is associated with increased identification of aneurysmal degeneration, planned secondary interventions, and mid-term survival. These data suggest that longitudinal vascular surgical care, starting with in-hospital consultation, is a critical component of care following acute TAAD and should be strongly considered to ensure appropriate postoperative surveillance and improve long-term patient outcomes.

title: Clinical Outcome of Late Survivors Following the Classic Fontan Procedure.
authorString: Matsubara M, Reyhaniye J, Kienmoser D, Schaeffer T, Palm J, Ruda C, Piber N, Hager A, Ewert P, Hörer J, Ono M.
abstractText: Heart failure and multi-organ dysfunction develop insidiously in adults with a classic Fontan circulation. We evaluated late outcomes and risk factors for failing Fontan beyond 20 years after the classic Fontan procedure. Among 170 patients operated between 1978 and 1995, those surviving beyond 20 years without Fontan conversion were included. Clinical outcomes and risk factors were assessed. Sixty patients were included: tricuspid atresia in 37, double-inlet left ventricle in 14. Over 35.2 years' median follow-up, 13 (21.7%) died and 31 (51.7%) developed failing Fontan at a median of 30.8 years. Survival was lower with failing Fontan (70.2% vs. 95.2% at 35 years; P = .013) than those without. In multivariable analysis, double-inlet left ventricle (hazard ratio 2.42; P = .027) and ascites (hazard ratio 2.70; P = .007) were independent risk factors. At the last follow-up, the failing group had lower serum albumin (4.2 vs. 4.6 g/dL; P = .017) and higher N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (774 vs. 404 pg/mL; P = .004); hepatic markers, total protein, and platelet count did not differ. After adjustment for the interval since diagnosis and exclusion of protein-losing enteropathy, only the natriuretic peptide association persisted. Peak oxygen uptake was also lower (P < .01). Late mortality and failing Fontan remained substantial beyond two decades. Double-inlet left ventricle and ascites were independent risk factors. Higher natriuretic peptide and reduced exercise capacity characterized the failing group, whereas lower albumin did not independently identify it. Regular assessment of these markers may aid surveillance.

title: Age-associated clinical patterns in paediatric myocarditis: left ventricular function as the key early risk stratifier.
authorString: Seidel F, Huber C, Opgen-Rhein B, Boehne M, Weickmann J, Hecht T, Anderheiden F, Reineker K, Rentzsch A, Wiegand G, Böcker D, Kiski D, Fischer M, Frede W, Ruf B, Papakostas K, Tarusinov G, Voges I, Kaestner M, Gummel K, Schiebel A, Kramp J, Herberg U, Kerst G, Wannenmacher B, Gatzweiler E, Knirsch W, Rolfs N, Schwanzkopf E, Garfias-Veitl T, Pickardt T, Rudolph A, Böhmer J, Friede T, Schubert S, Messroghli D, MYKKE consortium.
abstractText:
Background and aims

In myocarditis, early identification of high-risk patients is essential, robust prognostic markers are lacking. We aimed to identify early clinical risk stratifier at index hospitalization for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).

Methods

We analysed 725 paediatric patients with possible/definite myocarditis enrolled in the prospective multicentre MYKKE registry (2013-2024). MACE included mechanical circulatory support (MCS), heart transplantation, or death during initial admission. Model-based recursive partitioning (MOB) and bootstrap-based logistic regression with multiple imputation were applied for risk stratifier selection out of 20 baseline variables. The model was externally validated in the Swedish SWEDCON- cohort (n = 243). Discrimination was assessed by the area under the curve (AUC).

Results

Among 725 patients (median age 14.3 years [IQR 4.0-16.4]; 33% female), 88 (12.2%) experienced MACE (MCS 10.9%, transplantation 4.3%, death 2.2%). MOB identified left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤ 39% as the only stable risk stratifier, delineating a "heart failure type" in younger children (1.9 years; LVEF 24%), and a "chest pain type" in adolescents with preserved LVEF (15.6 years; LVEF 59%). LVEF was confirmed as the sole robust risk stratifier (OR per 1% increase: 0.90 ; 95% CI 0.881-0.917; p < 0.01; AUC 0.90, 95% CI 0.896-0.903). In SWEDCON (7.4% MACE), discrimination was maintained (AUC 0.894, 95% CI 0.80-0.991).

Conclusion

Reduced LVEF at presentation was the only reproducible and externally validated risk stratifier of MACE during index hospitalization. Two age-associated clinical patterns were observed: a high-risk "heart failure type" in younger children and low-risk "chest pain type" in adolescents.

title: Classification and Outcomes of Coronary Microvascular Disease in Myocardial Infarction and Angina With Nonobstructive Coronary Arteries.
authorString: Carrington JG, Nogami K, Kanaji Y, Lewis BR, Moustafa AO, Gulati R, Tweet MS, Vassiliou V, Prasad A, Lerman A, Raphael CE.
abstractText:
Background

Myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries (MINOCAs) and angina with nonobstructive coronary arteries (ANOCAs) present diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. We assessed the frequency of coronary microvascular disease (CMD) and its subtypes in MINOCA compared with ANOCA and evaluated long-term cardiovascular outcomes.

Methods

Patients with nonobstructive coronary arteries undergoing invasive coronary function testing from 2012 to 2022 were prospectively enrolled and retrospectively classified as MINOCA or ANOCA (reference group). Myocardial infarction due to atherothrombosis, myocarditis, and Takotsubo syndrome were excluded. Invasive provocation testing was performed. CMD was classified as endothelium-independent (coronary flow reserve <2.5 with adenosine) and endothelium-dependent (<50% increase in coronary blood flow with acetylcholine). Major adverse cardiovascular events (cardiac death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, heart failure hospitalization, urgent revascularization, stroke) were recorded over 8 years.

Results

Of 622 patients, 73 (12%) had MINOCA (69% female, median age 56 years) and 549 (88%) ANOCA (72% female, median age 53 years). CMD was common in both groups (71% versus 64%; P=0.271), while endothelium-independent CMD was more frequent in MINOCA (41% versus 21%; P<0.001). Over a median follow-up of 4.5 years, major adverse cardiovascular events occurred more often in MINOCA (40% versus 11%; adjusted hazard ratio, 2.4; P=0.001). CMD predicted higher major adverse cardiovascular events in both MINOCA (hazard ratio, 3.6 [95% CI, 1.1-12.0]; P=0.038) and ANOCA (hazard ratio, 7.9 [95% CI, 2.9-21.8]; P<0.001).

Conclusions

CMD is common in both MINOCA and ANOCA. The higher prevalence of endothelium-independent CMD in MINOCA suggests a potential mechanistic role in infarction. Patients with MINOCA have a worse prognosis than ANOCA, particularly when CMD is present.

title: Clinical Impact of Physiology-Guided PCI: 1-year Results of the Post-Revascularization Optimization and Physiological Evaluation of Intermediate Lesions using Fractional Flow Reserve (PROPHET-FFR) Study.
authorString: Galante D, Vicerè A, Todisco S, Migliaro S, Zimbardo G, Cialdella P, Giuliana C, Viccaro V, Pollio Benvenuto C, Calò L, Lunardi M, Paraggio L, Buffon A, Fracassi F, Aurigemma C, Romagnoli E, Campo G, Biscaglia S, Trani C, Burzotta F, Leone AM.
abstractText: Background: The clinical value of physiological assessment after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains uncertain. We evaluated clinical outcomes associated with post-PCI physiology and temporal trends in its adoption. Methods: PROPHET-FFR (NCT05056662) is an ambispective observational study of patients undergoing invasive physiological assessment of intermediate coronary stenoses. Patients were categorized into three strategies: deferred revascularization based on non-ischemic physiology (deferred PCI), PCI for ischemic lesions without post-PCI physiological assessment (conventional PCI), and physiology-guided PCI with post-PCI assessment and optimization when indicated (post-PCI physiology). Temporal trends in the use of post-PCI physiology and physiology-guided optimization were evaluated, together with the incidence of 12-month major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), comprising cardiovascular death, spontaneous myocardial infarction, and target-vessel revascularization (TVR). Propensity score matching between conventional PCI and post-PCI physiology was performed to confirm the primary findings. Results: Among 1,986 patients, 1,307 underwent deferred PCI, 331 conventional PCI, and 348 post-PCI physiology. At 12 months, MACE occurred in 4.1%, 7.6%, and 3.4%, respectively (p=0.011). Compared with conventional-PCI, post-PCI physiology had lower MACE (3.4% vs 7.6%; p=0.019), primarily driven by reduced TVR (2.6% vs 5.4%; p=0.057), with consistent findings after propensity score matching (226 patients/group; 2.7% vs 8.0%; p=0.0114). Post-PCI physiology increased from 11.8% to 22.8% across registry phases (p<0.001), with a numerical increase in physiology-guided optimization (11.6% vs 18.1%; p=0.08). Conclusions: In this observational study, post-PCI physiology appears to be associated with lower 12-month MACE compared with conventional PCI, with consistent findings after propensity score matching.

title: Donor-aware integration of public single-cell and spatial transcriptomes identifies a VIC remodeling program and FN1-NT5E spatial association in calcific aortic valve disease.
authorString: Song C, Sha T, Zhang X, Tang S, Liu C, Li J.
abstractText: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) involves interacting endothelial, interstitial, immune and extracellular-matrix programs, but public single-cell studies contain many cells and few donors. A staged, donor-aware computational workflow was applied to five public human transcriptomic datasets. GSE220774 was used for single-cell discovery; GSE51472, GSE194180 and GSE235995 for fixed-signature replication; and GSE306288 for donor-level spatial assessment. Donors or patients, rather than cells or spots, were treated as biological replicates. VIC9 ranked highest for a prespecified fibrocalcific composite, although reliable coverage was limited to two donors. Its CTHRC1/FAP/IBSP/CDKN2A core program increased across disease-stage, osteogenic-culture and independent patient datasets. FN1-NT5E was the only prespecified candidate pair detected above the 0.5% spot floor in all six spatial donors. Immediate-neighbor associations were positive in 6/6 donors (median Spearman rho = 0.0717; exact one-sided sign-test P = 0.015625) and remained directionally stable in sensitivity analyses. These results define a reproducible VIC9-like remodeling program and an FN1-rich, NT5E-associated spatial context. They are hypothesis-generating and do not establish direct binding, causal signaling, an irreversible VIC transition or a histologically defined calcification front.

title: Targeting Nupr1-Mediated p53 Mitochondrial Sequestration Alleviates Aortic Dissection by Restoring the Gadd45b-Dependent Survival Program.
authorString: Yang X, Chen KY, Tian Y, Jiang ZS, Lei J, Zhuang XH, Wu JB, Tang LL, Li HY, Chen XH, Wang Y, Li YM, Qiu ZH, Cai ZW, Chen LW.
abstractText: Aortic dissection (AD) is a catastrophic cardiovascular emergency triggered by severe pathological stress. While continuous stress drives vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) apoptosis via mitochondrial dysfunction, the precise upstream orchestrators linking these stress signals to the mitochondrial apoptotic cascade remain elusive. By integrating clinical observations and single-cell RNA sequencing, we found that Nuclear Protein 1 (Nupr1), a critical stress-responsive factor, is significantly upregulated in aortas from AD patients and murine models, with enrichment in VSMCs. Remarkably, VSMC-specific Nupr1 deficiency significantly ameliorated AD progression in vivo. Mechanistically, Nupr1 undergoes massive mitochondrial accumulation in Ang II-induced apoptotic VSMCs. Rather than operating as a conventional transcriptional regulator, mitochondrially enriched Nupr1 functions as a pathological spatial switch. It sequesters p53 within mitochondria, driving transcription-independent apoptosis while simultaneously blunting the protective Gadd45b-mediated survival program. Furthermore, in vivo Gadd45b overexpression was sufficient to rescue mitochondrial dysfunction and ameliorate vascular collapse. Taken together, our findings conceptualize the Nupr1-p53-Gadd45b axis as an important determinant of VSMC fate and provide a novel and promising therapeutic strategy for preventing AD progression.

title: Spatial transcriptomics unveils the in situ cellular and molecular hallmarks of the lung in fatal COVID-19.
authorString: Garcia-Prieto CA, Musulen E, Grases D, Davalos V, Ferrer G, Pérez-Miés B, Caniego-Casas T, Palacios J, Saenz-Sardà X, Englund E, Porta E, Esteller M.
abstractText: Severe Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can induce progressive diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) leading to fatal outcomes. Here, we leveraged data from Visium spatial transcriptomics for COVID-19 and control lung samples to unravel insights into cellular and molecular events driving lethal COVID-19. We report a progressive loss of endothelial cell types, pneumocytes type I and natural killer cells coupled with a continuous increase of myeloid and stromal cells, mostly peribronchial fibroblasts, across acute and proliferative DAD. Spatial organization analysis also identified specific compartmentalization including immune-specific clusters across DAD patterns. Importantly, spatially informed ligand-receptor interaction analysis revealed intercellular communication signatures defining COVID-19 induced DAD. Transcription factor activity enrichment analysis identified the TGF-β pathway as DAD driver, highlighting the antagonizing roles of SMAD3 and SMAD7 activity during fibrosis. Integration of these data yielded a signaling kinase pathway in peribronchial fibroblasts with amenable novel targets. Finally, spatio-temporal trajectory analysis characterized an alveolar epithelium regeneration program.

title: Aspirin for primary prevention in patients with high lipoprotein(a): A promising therapeutic option while awaiting future therapies?
authorString: Vittone F, Autiero G, Malerba SA, Grolla E, Dalla Vestra M.
abstractText: Elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined cardiovascular risk factor, linked to both atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and aortic valve stenosis. Plasma Lp(a) levels between 30-50mg/dL suggest a moderate risk, while levels of 51-180mg/dL indicate high risk, and concentrations exceeding 180mg/dL are linked to a very high cardiovascular risk. Currently, there are no approved therapies specifically indicated to lower Lp(a). Recent evidences indicate a role of aspirin in reducing cardiovascular events in primary prevention in patients with high Lp(a). In this review, we discuss the results of the studies that explored the impact of aspirin in reducing cardiovascular events in primary prevention in patients with increased Lp(a) while waiting for the results from large-scale research initiative exploring the impact of RNA-targeting Lp(a)-lowering therapies in reducing cardiovascular risk. In conclusion, waiting for the ongoing trials on emerging RNA-based therapies, the use of aspirin in a subgroup of patients with high atherosclerotic cardiovascular risk, with very high Lp(a) levels and without important bleeding risk could be an interesting strategy. Emerging RNA-targeted therapies might offer in future increased protection against the occurrence of major atherosclerotic cardiovascular events compared to standard lipid management agents in these patients.

title: Differential impacts of fine particulate matter constituents on congenital heart disease across critical periconceptional windows.
authorString: Qu Y, Lin X, Wei J, Liu X, Lin S, Bloom MS, Wang X, Gao X, Wu Y, Zhou X, Zhuang J, Zhang W, Chen J.
abstractText: The effect of specific chemical constituents of fine particulate matter (PM<sub>2.5</sub>) on congenital heart disease (CHD) remains unknown and urgently needed. This study aimed to quantify the associations between PM<sub>2.5</sub> constituents and CHD risk, identify critical exposure windows, and explore potential effect modifiers. We included 12,680 CHD cases and 10,266 controls from the Guangdong Registry of CHD (2004-2022). Multilevel logistic regression found that PM<sub>2.5</sub> total mass and its constituents were significantly associated with CHD, particularly during the preconception period, with each interquartile range (IQR) increase corresponding to a 9-16% elevated risk. The associations were generally attenuated in later exposure windows, whereas BC and nitrate showed significant associations during pregnancy. Conotruncal defects showed the strongest association with PM<sub>2.5</sub> constituents (ORs ranged from 1.14 to 1.36 per IQR increase). Mixture analyses indicated that sulfate and BC dominated the effects during preconception, while BC and nitrate prevailed subsequently. Subgroup and interaction analyses showed that higher socioeconomic status significantly amplified PM<sub>2.5</sub> constituent-related CHD risk during the preconception period, whereas multiparity and lack of folic acid supplementation significantly modified risk during later windows (P for interaction <0.05). These findings underscore that periconceptional exposure to PM<sub>2.5</sub> is associated with increased CHD risk, with effects varying by constituent and exposure window. Targeting emissions of BC, sulfate, and nitrate may help mitigate PM<sub>2.5</sub>-related CHD burden.

title: 2025 European Society of Cardiology guidelines for the management of cardiovascular disease and pregnancy : Statement of endorsement by the NVVC.
authorString: van der Zwaan HB, Kalkman DN, Broekman MJ, Evers ACC, Stegeman BH, Kiès P, van der Marel CM, van der Vloed J, Westendorp ICD, Cornette JMJ.

journal.title: Netherlands heart journal : monthly journal of the Netherlands Society of Cardiology and the Netherlands Heart Foundation

abstractText: This article contextualises the 2025 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines for managing cardiovascular disease (CVD) and pregnancy in the Netherlands. The guideline addendum provides additional recommendations for situations where the ESC guidelines may not fully align with Dutch clinical practice. By endorsing the ESC guidelines through this addendum, the Netherlands Society of Cardiology (Nederlandse Vereniging Voor Cardiologie) supports its members in adhering to evidence-based management strategies for CVD and pregnancy.

title: Developmental Systems Cardiology III: Measuring Adaptation Across the Lifespan.
authorString: McMahon CJ, Rossano J, Kim J, Lewin M.
abstractText: Developmental Systems Cardiology (DSC) conceptualizes congenital heart disease as a lifelong adaptive process shaped by interactions among biological, developmental, psychosocial, environmental, and healthcare systems. As survival has improved, contemporary challenges increasingly include neurodevelopment, psychosocial wellbeing, educational participation, healthcare engagement, and long-term adaptation, requiring multidimensional assessment beyond traditional physiological outcomes. This third article in the DSC series proposes a measurement framework for operationalizing adaptation across the lifespan. Rather than introducing new measurement domains or replacing established assessment recommendations, DSC provides an integrative architecture for linking existing measures across genomics and epigenomics, prenatal exposures, developmental physiology, neurocardiac interactions, family and social determinants, environmental influences, digital phenotyping, and healthcare-system context. Longitudinal measurement serves as a cross-cutting principle for characterizing adaptive trajectories and identifying periods of vulnerability and opportunity. Within this framework, adaptation is a dynamic, measurable process emerging through interactions among individuals, families, healthcare systems, and broader environments. Measurement therefore encompasses developmental functioning, resilience, participation, quality of life, healthcare transitions, and implementation outcomes alongside biological and clinical indicators. Established domain-specific standards, including neurodevelopmental assessment recommendations, can populate this broader architecture. This approach emphasizes integration rather than instrument development, while preserving the specificity and utility of established measures within individual domains. By integrating validated measures across domains, developmental stages, and time, DSC may provide a common language for research, registries, quality improvement, implementation science, and lifespan care. Its proposed contribution lies in organizing multidimensional measurement to better understand how adaptive and maladaptive trajectories emerge and evolve across development.

title: Perinatal management and delivery-room stabilization in congenital complete heart block: an 11-year experience at a tertiary center.
authorString: Sarrato SEZ, Martín TÁ, Chamorro IP, Sarrato GZ, Bravo DB, Luna MS.
abstractText: Congenital complete heart block (CCHB) is a rare condition associated with significant perinatal hemodynamic instability. Although advances in prenatal diagnosis and pacing have improved survival, evidence guiding delivery-room stabilization remains limited. To describe our institutional experience in the perinatal management of CCHB, focusing on delivery-room stabilization and neonatal outcomes. We conducted a retrospective study at a tertiary center including newborns with CCHB over an 11-year period (2009-2020). Fetal characteristics, delivery-room interventions, and neonatal outcomes were analyzed. In 2014, a structured delivery-room stabilization protocol was introduced, incorporating ECG monitoring, anticipatory preparation for respiratory support and intravenous isoproterenol, and immediate availability of transcutaneous pacing (TCP) when indicated. Fourteen newborns were diagnosed with CCHB, with prenatal diagnosis in 13/14. Major congenital heart defects (CHD) were present in 3/14 newborns, and nine cases were immune-mediated. Prematurity occurred in 9/14. Respiratory support in the delivery room was required in 10/14 infants. Two infants with severe cardiorespiratory instability required intubation, TCP, and isoproterenol in the delivery room. Following NICU admission, invasive mechanical ventilation was required in 5/14 infants and inotropic support in 6/14. Invasive pacing was required in 9/14 infants, including 3/14 within the first 24 h of life. One patient required ECMO support. Survival to neonatal discharge was 13/14.Conclusion: Newborns with CCHB may require advanced stabilization at birth. A structured delivery-room strategy may incorporate anticipatory respiratory and hemodynamic support, including TCP in selected unstable newborns. Multidisciplinary coordination and CCHB-specific delivery-room planning provide a framework for anticipating potential stabilization needs. What is Known • Congenital complete heart block is associated with significant perinatal morbidity and may require early pacing. • Standard neonatal resuscitation algorithms may be insufficient in these patients. What is New • This study describes an 11-year experience with perinatal management and delivery-room stabilization of newborns with CCHB. • A CCHB-specific strategy integrating anticipatory cardiorespiratory support and transcutaneous pacing in selected unstable newborns is proposed as a pragmatic framework for delivery-room stabilization.

title: Exercise Prescriptions for Cardiovascular Health in Adults: 2026 ACC Scientific Statement: A Report of the American College of Cardiology.
authorString: Myers J, Beckie TM, Chastin S, Fleg JL, Kitzman DW, Thompson PD, Wasfy MM.

journal.title: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

abstractText: Regular physical activity and structured exercise are foundational for cardiovascular prevention and treatment, yet exercise prescription remains inconsistently integrated into routine cardiovascular care. This American College of Cardiology scientific statement provides contemporary, practical guidance for clinicians on prescribing exercise across the spectrum of cardiovascular health and disease. The statement reviews evidence supporting physical activity, exercise training, and cardiorespiratory fitness as powerful determinants of cardiovascular outcomes, emphasizing that the greatest absolute benefits occur when inactive individuals begin moving and that additional benefits accrue with higher volumes and intensity, within appropriate clinical limits. It summarizes approaches to aerobic, resistance, balance, and flexibility training; highlights the role of cardiac rehabilitation and supervised, home-based, hybrid, and virtual models; and addresses individualized exercise prescription for patients with coronary artery disease, peripheral artery disease, heart failure, cardiomyopathies, hypertension, overweight and obesity, adult congenital heart disease, and older age. The statement also discusses when exercise testing is useful to assess safety, guide intensity, establish baseline fitness, and monitor responses, while recognizing that routine preparticipation testing is not required for most asymptomatic individuals. Wearable devices and digital tools are reviewed as adjuncts to self-monitoring, goal setting, and cardiac rehabilitation extension, with attention to equity, access, and digital literacy. Key implementation priorities include improving clinician training, embedding physical activity counseling into cardiovascular care, tailoring prescriptions to patient goals and functional capacity, and expanding research on long-term adherence, clinical outcomes, diverse populations, and scalable delivery models. Exercise should be prescribed as a core component of cardiovascular prevention and disease management.

title: Direct SVC Access for Valve Replacement With Percutaneous Venotomy Suture System Hemostasis: A Way In.
authorString: Ghandakly E, Sinha S, Linnane N, Aboulhosn J.
abstractText:
Background

Adult patients with congenital heart disease often have limited vascular access due to previous procedures and anatomic variations.

Case summary

This case describes how a percutaneously placed venotomy suture system allowed for direct percutaneous superior vena cava access for delivery sheath insertion for transcatheter pulmonary valve replacement. This system allowed for a novel access approach and the achievement of hemostasis in an otherwise noncompressible site.

Discussion

The availability of percutaneously placed venotomy suture placement systems allows for a more daring approach to noncompressible sites within the mediastinum and has the potential to be applied to allow large-bore closed chest access to other mediastinal structures.

title: Assessment of Severity of Chronic Aortic Regurgitation: Importance of a Hierarchical Approach to Echocardiogram Doppler Parameters.

authorString: Chorin E, Merin R, Giladi M, Henriques L, Banai A, Rosso R, Viskin S.

title: Can a Wrist-Worn Stimulator Improve the Results of an AF Ablation?
authorString: Olshansky B, Mhanna M.

title: Polymeric and metallic occluders for interventional therapy of cardiovascular diseases.
authorString: Liu R, Wang Q, Ding J.
abstractText: Interventional therapy has, as a minimally invasive approach, been widely adopted for treating cardiovascular diseases, particularly structural heart disease, where occluders play a pivotal role in transcatheter closure. This paper comprehensively reviews the evolutionary trajectory and emerging frontiers of cardiovascular occluders, beginning with their interventional applications in congenital heart defects (atrial septal defect, ventricular septal defect, patent foramen ovale, and patent ductus arteriosus) and left atrial appendage closure. The focus then shifts to occluder materials and design principles, tracing the progression from early non-degradable metals like stainless steel to the current gold standard, nitinol, whose hyperelasticity enables self-expanding devices. To promote rapid endothelialization on nitinol implants, surface nanocoatings of bioceramics such as titanium nitride have been developed to modulate cell-material interactions. To eliminate risks from permanent metallic implants, biodegradable occluders have emerged as an alternative. The design of biodegradable occluders utilizing medical polymers such as polylactic acid and polydioxanone is illustrated, highlighting structural innovations such as locking strategies to overcome the lack of hyperelasticity. Key considerations including matching degradation rate with tissue regeneration and achieving X-ray visibility are also described. Finally, future perspectives are presented: expanding applications to infants and the elderly, incorporating tissue engineering for in situ regeneration, and leveraging nanotechnology and artificial intelligence to optimize device performance. The ongoing advancement of occluder technologies will propel interventional therapy for structural heart disease toward a safer and more effective treatment.

title: Cardiovascular Complications of Chronic Liver Disease.
authorString: Park S, Gupta DK, Izzy M, VanWagner LB.
abstractText: Chronic liver disease is an increasingly prevalent and heterogeneous syndrome with important consequences for cardiovascular function. As the global burdens of chronic liver disease and cirrhosis continue to rise, cardiovascular disease has emerged as a major driver of overall morbidity and mortality in affected patients. Despite the growing recognition of the intersectionality between hepatology and cardiology care clinically, cardiovascular disease risk among patients with liver disease is underrecognized. This state-of-the-art review summarizes the current understanding of the bidirectional interactions between the liver and the cardiovascular system. Shared mechanisms-including inflammation, endothelial injury, and neurohormonal overactivation-that contribute to the development of adverse myocardial remodeling, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure, arrhythmias, pulmonary vascular syndromes, and cirrhosis-associated cardiovascular syndromes are reviewed. A specific focus is placed on metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, the most common form of chronic liver disease, while highlighting the distinct cardiovascular manifestations associated with other types of chronic liver disease. These include alcohol-associated liver disease and infiltrative diseases that affect the liver and heart with cardiovascular implications across the spectrum from early stages of liver disease through cirrhosis. We discuss practical approaches to detecting liver disease, including the assessment of liver fibrosis noninvasively in individuals at risk. We discuss the approach to assessing cardiovascular risk through cardiac imaging, biomarkers, and cardiac functional testing once chronic liver disease is detected. Management considerations for commonly encountered cardiovascular conditions and a critical appraisal of the evolving evidence supporting cardiometabolic therapies in patients with chronic liver disease are discussed to underscore potential cardiovascular and liver benefits. Critical evidence gaps and future research priorities are identified, including the development and evaluation of liver-informed cardiovascular risk models, incorporation of cardiovascular end points into liver disease trials, and implementation of integrated cardiohepatometabolic care pathways. Improved recognition of chronic liver disease and related cardiovascular disease risk represents a major opportunity to facilitate earlier disease detection, enhance risk stratification, and improve outcomes across the spectrum of chronic liver disease.

title: Microbial cues and T cell immunity: deciphering their interactions in chronic liver disease.
authorString: Liu Y, Yu B, Liu Q, Ma X, Tang R.
abstractText: Chronic liver disease (CLD) poses a major global health challenge, as its progression to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma significantly contributes to worldwide morbidity and mortality. Mounting evidence has identified the gut microbiota as a critical modulator of CLD progression, primarily via the gut-liver axis. The liver is continuously exposed to gut-derived signals through the portal circulation, while reciprocally secreting bioactive mediators that shape intestinal microbial composition and function. This bidirectional network enables intricate crosstalk between the gut microbiota and the host immune system. In particular, T lymphocytes, the central effectors of adaptive immunity, are tightly regulated by gut microbiota and their metabolites. Conversely, T cells also modulate the gut microbial ecosystem. Herein, we summarize current knowledge on this bidirectional crosstalk, focusing on how gut microbiota shape T cell differentiation, function and plasticity, as well as the reciprocal impact of T cells on the gut microbiota. Furthermore, we evaluate how these interactions influence the development and progression of various CLDs, including autoimmune liver diseases, alcohol-associated liver disease, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and viral hepatitis. Finally, we discuss the therapeutic potential of targeting gut microbiota-T cell interactions through immunomodulatory and microbiota-directed strategies to offer novel therapeutic approaches.

title: Sonographic findings in fontan-associated liver disease across pediatric and adult patients: A cross-sectional imaging study.
authorString: González García RA, Parhofer R, Schröder C, Hermann Y, Dittrich S, Zapke M, Siebenlist G, Knieling F, Wällisch W, Schöffl I, Jüngert J.
abstractText:
Background

This study aimed to characterize sonographic hepatic findings across pediatric, adolescent, and adult Fontan patients and to examine their cross-sectional relationships with time since Fontan completion and chronological age. As a secondary objective, we explored a composite score integrating complementary sonographic findings.

Materials and methods

In this retrospective cross-sectional analysis of a prospectively established single-center Fontan cohort, hepatic ultrasound findings from 153 patients were evaluated, including gray-scale imaging, Doppler assessment, and shear-wave elastography performed according to institutional acquisition protocols. Individual sonographic findings were analyzed as the primary imaging outcomes. Cross-sectional associations with time since Fontan completion were assessed using sex-adjusted regression models; additional models simultaneously included chronological age, time since Fontan completion, and sex to examine their closely related contributions. A secondary exploratory 5-point composite score integrating five complementary sonographic domains was evaluated descriptively.

Results

Longer time since Fontan completion was associated cross-sectionally with greater IVC diameter, liver size, shear-wave velocity, structural abnormality, and hepatic nodularity in sex-adjusted analyses. Chronological age and time since Fontan completion were nearly collinear (r = 0.970). When both variables and sex were included simultaneously, associations with IVC diameter, liver size, shear-wave velocity, and structural classification were attenuated and no longer statistically significant, whereas hepatic nodularity remained associated with time since Fontan completion (OR = 1.22/year; 95% CI 1.03-1.45; p = 0.024). Complete composite-score data were available in 101 patients; mean scores were 0.81 ± 0.88, 2.15 ± 1.26, 3.18 ± 0.80, and 4.27 ± 0.80 across < 5-, 5-<10-, 10-<20-, and ≥ 20-year post-Fontan categories, respectively. In 15 patients with serial examinations, scores were higher at the later examination in 10 and unchanged in five (p = 0.004). In a stratified subset of 40 independently reread examinations, interobserver agreement was high for liver size (ICC = 0.922) and IVC diameter (ICC = 0.947), whereas agreement for qualitative sonographic findings was lower (κ = 0.202-0.369).

Conclusion

Sonographic vascular, morphologic, structural, elastographic, and nodular abnormalities differed across patients examined at increasing intervals after Fontan completion. However, because chronological age and Fontan duration were nearly collinear, this cross-sectional study cannot determine whether these imaging gradients reflect duration of Fontan physiology, chronological maturation, or both. Hepatic nodularity showed the most robust association with time since Fontan completion in simultaneous models. The composite score provides a secondary exploratory framework for integrating complementary sonographic findings but requires prospective longitudinal and external validation. The limited interobserver agreement for qualitative findings further emphasizes the need for standardized image interpretation and supports the exploratory status of the composite score.

title: A leakage-controlled multiscale contextual involution-inception framework for spectral-spatial classification of neonatal hyperspectral images.
authorString: Cihan M, Ceylan M.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Spectrochim Acta A Mol Biomol Spectrosc
journal.title: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
journal.isoabbreviation: Spectrochim Acta A Mol Biomol Spectrosc

abstractText: Early and reliable assessment of neonatal conditions is important in neonatal intensive care units, where non-invasive imaging approaches may provide complementary information for clinical evaluation. Hyperspectral imaging provides a non-invasive means of capturing spatially resolved spectral information from neonatal tissue; however, its high dimensionality and the limited availability of clinical samples make robust model development challenging. This study proposes the Multiscale Contextual Involution-Inception Network (MC-I<sup>2</sup>Net), a leakage-controlled framework for neonatal HSI classification. The model combines spatially adaptive involution operators, Inception-based multiscale feature extraction, and contextual feature fusion to learn compact and discriminative spectral-spatial representations. A balanced six-class neonatal hyperspectral imaging dataset containing 240 samples was evaluated, including coarctation of the aorta, intracranial hemorrhage, necrotizing enterocolitis, pneumothorax, respiratory distress syndrome, and healthy control groups. Fixed signal-conditioning operations were applied using predefined processing rules, whereas PCA was treated as a data-adaptive transformation. PCA was fitted exclusively on each training fold, and the learned transformation was subsequently applied to the corresponding held-out test fold. All models were assessed using the same 5-fold cross-validation protocol repeated 10 times. MC-I<sup>2</sup>Net achieved an overall accuracy of 94.38 ± 4.60% and a Macro-F1 score of 94.35 ± 4.57%, with only small numerical differences in OA relative to MC-3DCNN, ViT-HSI, and Swin-HSI. The model used fewer trainable parameters than MC-3DCNN, ViT-HSI, and Swin-HSI and substantially fewer FLOPs than MC-3DCNN, supporting a favorable performance-complexity profile rather than a large predictive-performance margin. An additional anatomically controlled analysis restricted to PTX and RDS samples acquired from the same thoracic region retained an OA of 95.75 ± 6.49% and a Macro-F1 score of 95.66 ± 6.68%. Sequential nested cross-validation, with PCA dimensionality and involution hyperparameters selected using training data only, yielded a pooled outer out-of-fold OA of 95.00% and a Macro-F1 score of 94.98%. Ablation, sensitivity, calibration, nested-validation, runtime, and saliency analyses provided complementary evidence regarding architectural behavior, robustness, computational characteristics, and preliminary explainability. Overall, these findings support MC-I<sup>2</sup>Net as a proof-of-concept framework for neonatal HSI classification and provide a methodological basis for future prospective, multicenter, and cross-device evaluation.

Beyond Taxonomy: Fungal Nutraceutical Supplementation Modifies the Functional Potential of the Gut Microbiome in Colorectal Cancer.
authorString: Rodríguez-Costas N, Rodríguez-Blanco A, Expósito CR, Cubiella J, Stompel ES, Fernández-de-Ana Portela C, Martín AID, Taboada-Rodríguez P, Silva BF, Fernández MDR, Zarraquiños S, Remedios D, Gómez CAS, Lorenzo SA, Poceiro RF, Parga MLC, Ramírez VH, Pérez-Castro S.
abstractText: The gut microbiome is increasingly recognized as an important determinant of host immune regulation, intestinal homeostasis, and recovery after colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery. Although our previous randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial demonstrated that fungal nutraceutical supplementation with Micodigest<sup>®</sup> was associated with favorable taxonomic and systemic inflammatory changes in patients undergoing CRC surgery with curative intent, the functional consequences of this intervention remain poorly understood. Here, we performed a functional metagenomic analysis of fecal samples collected from patients enrolled in the original clinical trial to investigate whether Micodigest<sup>®</sup> supplementation was associated with changes in the functional potential of the gut microbiome. A total of 37 patients were analyzed, including 24 receiving Micodigest<sup>®</sup> and 13 receiving placebo, with paired samples collected before supplementation and after 4-6 weeks of intervention. Shallow shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed, and microbial functional potential was characterized using KEGG Orthologues (KOs). Differential abundance analysis identified 14 significantly different KOs between groups at baseline and 23 after intervention, with no overlap between the two sets of orthologues. Following supplementation, Micodigest<sup>®</sup>-treated patients exhibited increased representation of functions related to CRISPR-associated systems, bacteriophage biology, and chitin-derived carbohydrate utilization, together with reduced representation of nutrient acquisition systems, conjugative transfer, sulfur metabolism, and components of the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway. These functional signatures suggest coordinated changes in microbial ecological adaptation, nutrient utilization, genetic exchange, and metabolic activity following fungal nutraceutical supplementation. Integration with previously reported taxonomic and inflammatory findings supports the hypothesis that Micodigest<sup>®</sup> may promote coordinated remodeling of the gut microbiome and host-microbiota interactions during the perioperative period. Although the present study cannot establish causality or directly infer microbial activity from metagenomic potential, these findings provide novel functional insights into the microbiome response to fungal nutraceutical supplementation in patients with CRC and highlight functional metagenomics as a valuable complement to taxonomic profiling.

title: Neonatal abstinence syndrome in Norway - a registry study.
authorString: Kaarby T, Fredriksen H, Lang AM, Guthe HJ, Støen R, Klingenberg C.

journal.title: Tidsskrift for den Norske laegeforening : tidsskrift for praktisk medicin, ny raekke

abstractText:
Background and aim

Medications and illicit substances taken during pregnancy are transferred to the foetus via the placenta. When the supply ceases after birth, the infant can develop withdrawal symptoms. The aim of the study was to investigate the incidence, neonatal morbidity and regional differences in hospital admissions of infants with neonatal abstinence syndrome (NAS) in Norway.

Material and method

Using the Norwegian Neonatal Network quality registry, we identified all neonates in Norway with a gestational age of ≥ 36 weeks who were discharged from a neonatal unit and diagnosed with NAS during the study period from 1 January 2012 to 31 December 2023. We extracted key register data, including additional diagnoses and length of stay in the neonatal unit.

Results

We identified 621 neonates with NAS over the 12-year period, corresponding to a national incidence of 0.95 per 1,000 liveborn infants with a gestational age of ≥ 36 weeks. The median length of stay in a neonatal unit for all infants included in the study was 6-8 days throughout the study period. However, the hospital stay was ≥ 14 days for 134 infants (22%). A total of 119 infants (19%) had a birth weight below the 10th percentile, defined as small for gestational age. Seven infants (1%) were diagnosed with neonatal seizures. Congenital heart defects were identified in 14 infants (2%).

Interpretation

The incidence of NAS in Norway was lower than reported figures in other Western countries. Consistent with findings in the literature, one in five infants with NAS were small for gestational age.

title: Latent profiles and network analysis of emotional behaviors in preschool children after congenital heart disease surgery.
authorString: Xu Q, Zhang X, Li Y, Liu J, Li M.
abstractText:
Background

Emotional and behavioral problems are prominent and highly heterogeneous among preschool children after congenital heart disease surgery, but their latent subgroup characteristics and core symptoms remain unclear. The associations between the family psychological environment (e.g., parenting stress, family hardiness) and children's emotional and behavioral outcomes also need further clarification.

Objective

To identify heterogeneous subgroups and central symptoms of emotional and behavioral problems in preschool children after congenital heart disease surgery, and to examine the associations between parenting stress, family hardiness, and children's emotional and behavioral outcomes.

Methods

A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 273 mothers of children aged 3-6 years after congenital heart disease surgery. Latent profile analysis was used to identify subgroups, and network analysis was applied to construct association networks of symptoms and related factors.

Results

Two subgroups were identified: the well-adjusted subgroup (82.1%) and the maladjusted subgroup (17.9%). Hyperactivity/inattention was the node with the highest strength centrality in both subgroups. Parenting stress was independently associated with emotional and behavioral problems (OR = 1.086), while family hardiness was independently associated with a lower risk (OR = 0.907). The "challenge" dimension of family hardiness showed the highest centrality in the well-adjusted subgroup, whereas the "control" dimension showed the highest centrality in the maladjusted subgroup.

Conclusion

Emotional and behavioral problems in preschool children after congenital heart disease surgery show significant heterogeneity. Different dimensions of family hardiness may serve as candidate targets for future intervention research, and early identification and management of hyperactivity/inattention should be prioritized.

title: Systemic immune activation coexists with compartment-specific regulatory enrichment in matched blood, peritumor, and tumor tissue from advanced oral squamous cell carcinoma.
authorString: Galdino NAL, Pignataro-Oshiro F, Scarini JF, Sales de Sá R, Evangelista GFB, Figueiredo AB, Cavalcanti CM, Morais KLP, Gasparini VA, Kohler HF, Bueno de Oliveira T, Kowalski LP, Gollob KJ.
abstractText:
Background

Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is the most prevalent form of oral cancer and is characterized by a poor prognosis and frequent immune evasion. While the tumor microenvironment (TME) plays a central role in modulating responses to therapy, its relationship with systemic immune signatures remains poorly understood.

Methods

We performed high-dimensional immune profiling in matched peripheral blood, adjacent non-neoplastic peritumor mucosa, and tumor tissue from Human Papillomavirus (HPV)-negative, treatment-naïve patients with advanced OSCC. Soluble mediators were quantified by multiplex immunoassay, and immune cell phenotypes were assessed by multiparametric flow cytometry. Compartment-specific patterns were evaluated using paired and unpaired comparisons, dimensionality reduction, ordinal trend analysis, unsupervised clustering, and correlation networks.

Results

Seventeen plasma mediators were significantly elevated in OSCC patients compared with healthy donors. Paired cellular profiling identified compartment-specific differences across blood, peritumor and tumor, and selected PD-1+CD95+, CD25+FoxP3+, and PD-L1+ populations showed significant progressive trends along the blood-peritumor-tumor axis. CD4+ mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT)-like cells (TCR Vα7.2+CD161+) were relatively enriched in peritumor tissue, but the peritumor compartment was not uniformly intermediate across all populations. Correlation networks showed limited overlaps, with greater overlap between peritumor and tumor networks than between either tissue compartment and blood. Plasma profiling showed elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, and growth factors, consistent with systemic immune activation. Peripheral blood exhibited an activated phenotype with increased frequencies of activated T and NK cells, alongside CD4-CD8- TCR Vα7.2+CD161+ cells. In contrast, the tumor microenvironment was enriched for CD95+PD-1+ CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, NK cells and PD-L1+ monocytes and CD4+ MAIT-like cells. The peritumor compartment showed a distinct immune profile marked by regulatory T cell accumulation and other immunosuppressive mediators, rather than a uniform intermediate state between blood and tumor. Correlation networks revealed pronounced shifts in immune coordination across compartments.

Conclusions

Advanced OSCC is associated with distinct systemic and tissue immune profiles. These exploratory findings identify compartment-specific immune features and selected monotonic trends that warrant future spatial, functional, and clinical validation.

title: Post-Operative Acute Kidney Injury After Pediatric Heart Transplantation and Longitudinal Invasive Assessment of Cardiac Filling Pressures.
authorString: Zafar F, Gist KM, Floh AA, Ollberding NJ, Fuhrman D, Soranno DE.
abstractText:
Background

Acute kidney injury (AKI) has been associated with diastolic dysfunction in pre-clinical studies, but with limited evaluation in clinical settings. We sought to examine the association between post-operative AKI and diastolic function after pediatric heart transplantation.

Methods

We conducted a single-center retrospective review of patients ≤ 21years undergoing first-time heart transplantation between May 2010-July 2023. AKI was defined and staged per the KDIGO creatinine criteria, with Stage 2 or 3 classified as severe. Right ventricular end-diastolic pressure (RVEDP) and pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) obtained from surveillance cardiac catheterizations in the first two years post-transplant were used to assess diastolic function. Linear mixed-effects models were used to compare hemodynamics between groups.

Results

We included 101 patients, aged 0-20 years, median 4 years (IQR 0-13). Pre-transplant diagnosis was congenital heart disease (CHD) in 51 (50%) and cardiomyopathy in 50 (50%) patients. Post-operative AKI occurred in 29 (29%) patients; 16/29 had severe AKI. AKI was more common in patients with CHD than cardiomyopathy [20/29 (69%) vs. 9/29 (31%), p = 0.02]. On mixed-effects model analysis adjusting for pre-transplant diagnosis, ischemia time > 4 h, and time since transplantation, severe AKI was associated with higher filling pressures over the first 2 years post-transplant, including a 2.2 mmHg increase in RVEDP (95% CI 1.3-3.1; p < 0.0001) and a 1.8 mmHg increase in PCWP (95% CI 0.8-2.8; p = 0.0005).

Conclusions

Severe post-transplant AKI was independently associated with higher biventricular filling pressures, suggesting a clinically relevant kidney-heart interaction. Larger studies are needed to further define its mechanistic and clinical implications.
