title: Hearing loss, hearing-aid use, and mortality risk: individual participant data meta-analysis of population-based studies from Australia, Iceland, and the USA and a replication study from Norway.
authorString: Li CM, Hoffman HJ, Engdahl B, Gopinath B, McMahon CM, Themann CL, Gudnason V, Davis AC.
abstractText:
Background

Hearing loss is associated with poorer health, depression, cognitive decline, and perhaps, with increased mortality risk. Whether hearing aids ameliorate this association is not well understood. We conducted a meta-analysis with a replication study to examine associations between hearing loss, current use of hearing aids, and mortality.

Methods

Hearing threshold data, all-cause mortality, and cardiovascular disease (CVD)-related mortality (available across datasets) were analysed using individual participant data (IPD) meta-analysis of three combined population-based studies: Blue Mountains Hearing Study (BMHS, Australia, 1997-2007), Age, Gene/Environment Susceptibility-Reykjavik Study (AGES-RS, Iceland, 2002-06), and National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES, USA, 1999-2006). The Nord-Trøndelag Hearing Loss Study (NTHLS, Norway, 1996-98) was chosen for replication. An IPD meta-analysis of the combined consortium datasets for BMHS (n=2689), AGES-RS (n=5171), and NHANES (n=5992) was performed using Cox regression to estimate hazard ratios and 95% CIs, after adjusting for age, sex, education, BMI, smoking, angina or heart attack, diabetes, hypertension, stroke, and noise-exposure history; NTHLS data were analysed similarly. Hearing loss was defined by better ear pure-tone average categories endorsed by the Global Burden of Disease Hearing Loss Expert Group and WHO.

Findings

The IPD meta-analysis included 13 851 participants, with a mean age of 61·8 (SD 18·5; men 6228 [45·0%], women 7622 [55·0%]). Mild (1·19 [95% CI 1·10-1·29]), moderate (1·55 [1·42-1·70]), and moderately severe or worse (1·56 [1·38-1·76]) hearing loss were associated with increasing all-cause mortality risk. Mild (1·18 [95% CI 1·02-1·37]), moderate (1·43 [1·22-1·67]), and moderately severe or worse (1·30 [1·05-1·60]) hearing loss were also associated with increased CVD-related mortality risk. Current use of hearing aids was associated with reduced all-cause mortality risk [0·91 (95% CI 0·83-0·99)] and reduced CVD-related mortality [0·85 (0·73-0·99)]. The NTHLS replication study of 50 277 adults (men 23 532 [46·8%], women 26 745 [53·2%]) corroborated these findings.

Interpretation

The IPD meta-analysis and Norwegian NTHLS confirmed that increasing severity of hearing loss is significantly associated with higher mortality risk. Use of hearing aids was associated with reduced mortality risk. The potential link between hearing-aid use, other forms of hearing rehabilitation, and increased life expectancy in adults is an important area for future research investigation.

Funding

Macquarie University; National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders, National Institutes of Health; Icelandic Heart Association (Hjartavernd); National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; and Norwegian Institute of Public Health.

title: Biomechanical Characterization of Human Pluripotent Stem Cell-Derived Cardiomyocytes by Use of Atomic Force Microscopy.
authorString: Pribyl J, Pesl M, Kabanov D, Beckerová D, Svěrák F, Vrana Š, Rotrekl V.
abstractText: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) is not only a high-resolution imaging technique but also a sensitive tool able to study biomechanical properties of biosamples (biomolecules, cells) in native conditions-i.e., in buffered solutions (culturing media) and stable temperature (mostly 37°C). Micromechanical transducers (cantilevers) are often used to map surface stiffness geometry, elastic, and contact parameters of living cells; however, they can also be used to monitor time course of dynamic forces (beating), their rate, and other biomechanical properties of cardiomyocyte contractility. Here we describe the construction of an AFM-based biosensor setup designed to study the biomechanical properties of cardiomyocyte clusters, using standard uncoated silicon nitride cantilevers. Force-time curves (mechanocardiograms, MCG) are recorded natively and in the presence of cardiomyocyte-contraction-affecting drugs (e.g., isoproterenol, metoprolol) in the medium, under physiological conditions. The average value of contraction force and the beat rate as basic biomechanical parameters represent pharmacological indicators of different phenotype features. Robustness, low computational requirements, and optimal spatial sensitivity (detection limit 200 pN or 20 nm) are the main advantages of the presented method.

title: Refractory Angina Pectoris: Medical and Interventional Treatment Options.
authorString: Ullrich-Daub H, Daub S, Lurz P, Gori T.
abstractText:
Background

Coronary heart disease (CHD) is among the more common cardiovascular diseases, affecting 4.7 million people in Germany alone. As many as 20% of patients with CHD still suffer from angina pectoris despite appropriate antianginal therapy and revascularization. Refractory angina pectoris reduces quality of life and increases mortality. In this review, we describe therapeutic strategies and the clinical evidence underlying them.

Methods

This review is based on publications up to December 2025 retrieved through a selective search in Medline/PubMed for RCTs, before-and-after studies, and guidelines on the treatment of refractory angina pectoris.

Results

The treatment of refractory angina pectoris begins with reducing risk factors, optimizing pharmacotherapy, and considering revascularization for functionally significant coronary stenosis. If these treatment options have been exhausted, the implantation of a sinus reducer may be considered, as recommended in the European guidelines (recommendation grade IIb). The evidence for this is derived from randomized trials and from multiple registry and observational studies. In the sham-controlled COSIRA trial, which involved 104 patients, an improvement in angina symptoms by at least two classes on the Canadian Cardiovascular Society (CCS) grading scale was observed in 35% of patients six months after implantation, compared with 15% in the control group. The multicenter ORBITA-COSMIC trial, which involved 51 patients, also yielded a reduction in daily angina pectoris compared with the control group (OR 1.40; 95% CI: [1.08; 1.83]). Potential complications include migration, embolization of the reducer, and coronary sinus perforation or dissection in 1-2% of patients. These events are only rarely clinically significant.

Conclusion

The sinus reducer may improve symptoms in selected patients, but the reported periprocedural complications and limited evidence to date on long-term outcomes should enter into the decision whether to provide this treatment to the individual patient.

title: Enhanced respiratory syncytial virus surveillance of young children admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network, 2019-2023.
authorString: Saravanos GL, Meredith K, Wong S, Burrell R, Bartlett A, Homaira N, Britton PN, Kandasamy R.
abstractText:
Objectives

In this study, we aimed to comprehensively describe the clinical characteristics, management and outcomes of children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network (SCHN), determine the full burden of severe disease and identify population-specific risk factors for intensive care unit (ICU) admission.

Study type

Multi-centre, retrospective cohort study conducted over 5 years.

Methods

The study was conducted at two tertiary paediatric hospitals in metropolitan New South Wales, Australia, before implementation of government-funded immunisation programs against RSV in children. Participants were children aged <2 years hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV from 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2023, comprising all ICU admitted, and a random sample of non-ICU admitted patients. The main outcome measures were characteristics and incidence rate of RSV hospitalisations and ICU admissions among children aged <2 years.

Results

Over a 5-year period, 4414 children were hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV, of whom 11.3% (499/4414) were admitted to ICU. The median age was younger in the ICU cohort (n = 499) compared with the non-ICU sample (n = 1000; 3.3 vs 7.1 months, P < 0.0001). Factors associated with higher odds of ICU admission in multivariate logistic regression were decreasing month of age (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.06-1.11), prematurity (OR 2.17, 95% CI 1.61-2.91), Indigenous identity (OR 4.10, 95% CI 2.30-7.56) and cardiac disease (OR 3.39, 95% CI 2.06-5.70). The average hospitalisation incidence rate was 1615 per 100,000 (95% CI 1565-1666), with higher rates among children aged <1 year, 2141 per 100,000 (95% CI 2061-2224) compared with those aged 1-2 years, 1088 per 100,000 (95% CI 1030-1148).

Conclusions

RSV immunisation programs are expected to substantially reduce the burden of hospitalisation among Australian children in their first year of life. Children who are Indigenous, were born prematurely or have heart disease are at greatest risk of severe disease and may benefit from extended preventative programs.

title: The missing link: prevention guidelines fail to include clear guidance for their implementation.
authorString: Barnes C, Bialek C, Mantach S, Turon H, Lane C, Shoesmith A, Jones J, Wolfenden L.
abstractText: This paper aims to characterise implementation recommendations within current international prevention guidelines. An audit of prevention guidelines hosted on the Guidelines International Network library was conducted. Recommendations from implementation process models were used as a guide for data extraction of eligible guidelines. This included the presence or absence of strategies, such as assessing and addressing barriers to implementation, engaging end-users in the development and execution of implementation guidelines, and the inclusion of empirical research to support implementation recommendations. Approximately two-thirds of eligible prevention guidelines included implementation recommendations. Of these guidelines, 37.5% provided guidance on assessing barriers to implementation, 14.9% made suggestions on selecting strategies to overcome barriers, and 36.6% included advice on engaging end-users in the implementation process. Only 44.6% referred to empirical evidence to support their implementation recommendations. A greater emphasis on the principles of implementation science is required during the development of prevention guidelines. This should include the utilisation of existing resources developed in consultation with implementation specialists.

title: Impact of Trimetazidine on Echocardiographic Indices and Clinical Outcomes in Ischemic Cardiomyopathy: An Updated Meta-Analysis of Clinical Trials.
authorString: Davis E, Alexander L, Fernando BC, Tandexci G, Chang TW, Hsu JC, Wu YW, Ridjab DA, Hananta L.
abstractText: Ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) is a major cause of chronic heart failure with impaired left ventricular (LV) function. This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate trimetazidine's effect in patients with ICM compared to standard therapy alone. A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, ProQuest, SAGE, EBSCO Host, Wiley, Science Direct, Springer link, Clinicaltrials.gov , EMBASE, WHO ICTRP databases until November 2024. Clinical trials assessing trimetazidine versus standard therapy in ICM were included. Data were analyzed using a random-effects model to calculate mean differences (MD) and relative risk (RR), with heterogeneity evaluated using the I 2 statistic. Twelve studies met the inclusion criteria. Trimetazidine significantly improved left ventricular ejection fraction (MD 6.35, 95% CI: 4.63- 8.07, p < 0.05, I2 = 69%), reduced LV end-systolic diameter (MD -4.51, 95% CI: -6.21- -2.81, p < 0.05, I2 = 56%), LV end-diastolic diameter (MD -3.13, 95% CI: -6.07- -0.18, p < 0.05, I2 = 86%), and LV end-systolic volume (MD -14.20, 95% CI: -21.19- -7.21, p < 0.05, I2 = 72%). There was no significant difference in left ventricular end-diastolic volume. Exercise capacity improved with a mean increase of 83.64 meters in the 6-minute walking test (MD 83.64, 95% CI: 22.88- 144.41, p < 0.05, I2 = 96%). NYHA class also improved (MD -0.80, 95% CI: -1.48- -0.12, p <0.05, I2 = 97%). Trimetazidine significantly reduced nitrate consumption (MD -2.76, 95% CI -3.84 to -1.68; I 2 = 95%), while its effect on anginal episodes was not significant (MD -1.52, 95% CI -4.49 to 1.46; I 2 = 99%) but became significant after excluding a study with an imputed standard deviation. Trimetazidine as an adjunct to standard therapy may improve cardiac function and exercise capacity in ischemic cardiomyopathy patients. The findings of this meta-analysis must be interpreted with caution due to high heterogeneity in some outcomes. Further large-scale trials are warranted to assess long-term outcomes such as mortality and hospitalization.

title: Plasma proteome of the EAT-Lancet diet and long-term risks of cardiovascular disease and mortality.
authorString: Guan W, Yang J, Chen J, Sullivan VK, Rebholz CM.
abstractText: Background: The EAT-Lancet diet, designed for planetary and human health, has been associated with lower risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and mortality. Identifying plasma proteins associated with the EAT-Lancet diet may help elucidate biological pathways underlying dietary associations with health outcomes. Methods: In 9623 Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities study participants with proteomic data at visit 3 (1993-1995, baseline) measured using the SomaScan™ v4.0 platform, multivariable linear regression was used to identify proteins associated with Planetary Health Diet Index (PHDI) score in a randomly selected subset of 2/3 of the study population (discovery, n = 6415) and the remaining 1/3 subset (internal replication, n = 3208). Cox models were used to evaluate associations of PHDI score-related proteins with incident CVD and all-cause mortality from baseline through December 31, 2022. Results: Among 4955 proteins examined, 154 were significantly associated with PHDI score at a false discovery rate <0.05 and 74 replicated. During a median follow-up of 21 years, 3401 incident CVD events occurred; during a median follow-up of 24 years, 5899 deaths occurred. Of the 74 PHDI score-related proteins, 9 were significantly associated with both incident CVD and all-cause mortality and an additional 8 were associated with all-cause mortality only in discovery and replication. For example, higher ASGR1 levels were associated with higher risk of incident CVD and all-cause mortality. Conclusions: PHDI-related proteins were prospectively associated with long-term CVD and mortality risk and may support future risk stratification and dietary prevention strategies.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Enlicitide in Hypercholesterolemia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
authorString: Farhan M, Murtaza M, Rasool MM, Khan F, Amjad H, Rai KD, Ali SME, Raza AA, Sohail MA, Samadi A, Hassan F.
abstractText:
Background

Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of global mortality, with low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) reduction being the cornerstone of prevention. Despite effective therapies, many high-risk patients do not achieve recommended LDL-C targets. Enlicitide (MK-0616), an oral proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitor, offers a potential alternative to injectable PCSK9-directed therapies.

Objective

To evaluate the efficacy and safety of enlicitide in adults with hypercholesterolemia and assess its dose-dependent effects on lipid parameters.

Methods

We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Google Scholar were searched from inception through March 2026. Random-effects meta-analysis using restricted maximum likelihood estimation was performed. The primary outcome was the percentage change in LDL-C from baseline. Secondary outcomes included non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (non-HDL-C), apolipoprotein B (ApoB), lipoprotein(a), triglycerides, and safety outcomes. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using RoB 2.0 and GRADE.

Results

Three placebo-controlled RCTs involving 3593 participants were included. Enlicitide significantly reduced LDL-C compared with placebo (mean difference [MD], -56.19%; 95% CI, -64.14 to -48.25; p < 0.0001), with moderate heterogeneity (I2 = 56.9%). Significant reductions were also observed in non-HDL-C (MD, -51.36%), ApoB (MD, -47.09%), lipoprotein(a) (MD, -20.10%), and triglycerides (MD, -13.12%). A numerical dose-response gradient was observed, although subgroup differences were not statistically significant. Sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the findings. Rates of adverse events, serious adverse events, and treatment discontinuation were comparable between groups.

Conclusion

Enlicitide produced substantial reductions in LDL-C and other atherogenic lipid parameters without an apparent increase in adverse events. However, findings should be interpreted cautiously given the limited number of trials, moderate heterogeneity, and reliance on surrogate endpoints. Dose-response, duration-related lipoprotein(a), and triglyceride findings were exploratory and substantially driven by single trials. Long-term cardiovascular outcomes trials are needed to establish clinical benefit.

title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Systemic Immunomodulatory Therapies for Non-Infectious Uveitis: A Systematic Review With Pairwise and Network Meta-Analyses.
authorString: Chen KY, Chan HC, Chan CM.
abstractText:
Introduction

Non-infectious uveitis (NIU) is a chronic immune-mediated ocular inflammatory disease that may cause irreversible visual impairment. The comparative efficacy and safety of systemic immunomodulatory therapies, including conventional agents and biologics, remain incompletely defined. This systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluated systemic immunosuppressive therapies for NIU.

Methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception to May 2, 2026. Randomized controlled trials and prospective comparative cohort studies evaluating systemic immunomodulatory or biologic therapies for NIU were included. The primary efficacy outcome was treatment failure. Safety outcomes included mortality, urinary tract infection, upper respiratory tract infection, injection-site reactions, ocular hypertension, macular edema, and headache. Random-effects pairwise meta-analysis and frequentist network meta-analysis were performed using risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

Results

Seven studies including 992 participants were included; six were randomized controlled trials and one was a prospective cohort. In the pairwise meta-analysis, adalimumab significantly reduced treatment failure compared with placebo (RR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.58-0.78; p < 0.0001; I² = 28.1%). The mortality estimate was inconclusive (RR, 3.80; 95% CI, 0.42-34.15), with three deaths in the adalimumab groups and none in the placebo groups. Adalimumab was associated with a higher risk of injection-site reactions than placebo (RR, 2.67; 95% CI, 1.73-4.12). Network meta-analysis showed no significant differences for most safety outcomes, including upper respiratory tract infection, ocular hypertension, macular edema, and headache. Infliximab showed an imprecise urinary tract infection signal versus placebo (RR, 40.98; 95% CI, 1.82-922.17), based on sparse events and one nonrandomized comparison.

Conclusion

Adalimumab provides the most consistent evidence for reducing treatment failure in NIU. Comparative safety estimates, particularly for infliximab, remain uncertain and hypothesis-generating. Larger, long-term, head-to-head trials are required.

title: Reframing traumatic brain injury and spinal cord injury as chronic multisystem disorders: toward integrated, long-term care.
authorString: Marini S, Schneider ALC, Alshaya A, Bragge P, Corrigan JD, Dams-O'Connor K, Giacino JT, Halabi C, Hendrick K, Hutchinson PJA, Khan T, Khattak AF, Kirshblum S, Lala T, Løvstad M, Manley GT, Mediratta S, Nagayama M, Newcombe VFJ, Pugh MJ, Rosseau G, Tenovuo O, Venturini S, Wilson F, Wilson L, Menon DK, Hammond FM, Zafonte R, Izzy S, Global Coalition for TBI as a Notifiable and Chronic Condition.
abstractText: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) and spinal cord injury (SCI) affect more than 220 million people worldwide and are associated with cardiometabolic, endocrine, neurological, and psychiatric sequelae for years to decades after an acute injury. However, most health systems still treat neurotrauma (TBI and SCI, collectively) as a time-limited event, leaving long-term surveillance of these patients fragmented or absent, which leads to preventable mortality and avoidable readmissions. TBI and SCI in adults should be reclassified as acute-onset multisystem chronic-risk conditions. Existing cardiovascular, endocrine, and psychiatric services do not capture neurotrauma-specific risks, including trauma-induced hypopituitarism, autonomic dysregulation, accelerated ageing, and cognitive-behavioural impairment, so neurotrauma care is best framed as a missing node in chronic neurological care. We propose a risk-stratified pathway of care navigation, multisystem screening, and telehealth; convergence with adjacent stroke, cardiometabolic, memory, psychiatric, pain, and epilepsy services; and the financing, workforce, and registry reforms needed to deliver measurable reductions in 5-year mortality, avoidable rehospitalisation, and long-term disability.

title: Improving access to cardiac rehabilitation in Australia: a policy reflection on equitable secondary prevention.
authorString: Silva SA, Silva S, Duwadi B, Tang EK.

journal.title: Australian health review : a publication of the Australian Hospital Association

abstractText: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) is an evidence-based secondary prevention intervention associated with reduced cardiovascular mortality and hospital readmissions and improved quality of life. Despite strong guideline recommendations, participation remains low in Australia and internationally, particularly among rural and remote populations, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and other underserved populations. This reflects a service delivery challenge rather than an evidence gap. Current CR models remain largely centred on metropolitan hospital-based programs that may not adequately meet the needs of geographically dispersed populations. This policy reflection argues that improving CR participation requires a shift towards more accessible and integrated models of care, including automatic referral pathways, telehealth and hybrid delivery models, stronger primary care involvement and partnerships with Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Organisations. Improving access to CR should be viewed as a broader health system priority with important implications for healthcare equity, chronic disease management and cardiovascular outcomes.

title: Understanding the Mortality Trends in Patients With Ventricular Arrhythmias and Cardiomyopathy: A 25-Year Retrospective Analysis From 1999-2024.
authorString: Pervaiz N, Naveed H, Razzak MJ, Shafiq SB, Hasan M, Gul S, Abbasi M, Kamil KA, Farhan SA.

journal.title: Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc

abstractText:
Background

Ventricular Arrhythmias (VA) associated with Cardiomyopathy (CM) continues to be the major cause of death. However, a national longitudinal study examining mortality trends from these conditions is still lacking. This study assessed mortality trends due to these conditions among U.S. adults aged ≥ 25 years from 1999 to 2024.

Methods

An observational analysis of U.S. mortalities due to VA in patients with CM (ICD-10 I47.2, I49.0 and I25.5, I42 respectively), was conducted using CDC WONDER. Adjusted Mortality Rates (AAMR) per 100,000 calculated and trends were assessed by calculating Average and Annual Percent Change (AAPC, APC), using joinpoint regression stratified by year, sex, race, and region.

Results

From 1999 to 2024, 81,204 VA with CM-related deaths occurred with the overall AAMR declined from 2.54 in 1999 to 1.01 in 2024 (AAPC: -3.55%; p < 0.000001). AAMRs decreased from 1999 to 2007 (APC: -7.93), remained stable till 2022 (APC: -0.66), and dropped by 2024 (APC: -6.87). Men exhibited greater AAMRs (2.42) than women (0.68). Racially, the AAMRs were most pronounced in Non-Hispanic (NH) Blacks (1.97), followed by NH Whites (1.42), whereas Hispanics and NH Others experienced similar AAMRs of 0.97. Geographically, Delaware and the Western regions experienced the highest rates of mortality (2.2 and 1.53, respectively). Urban areas had higher AAMRs than rural settings (1.45 vs. 1.4) CONCLUSION: Although VA-CM mortality has declined over the past two decades, differences by race, sex, and geography remain, underscoring the need for targeted healthcare strategies.

title: Postoperative Vasoactive Exposure Patterns and Outcomes After Non-Cardiac Surgery: A Prespecified Analysis of the SQUEEZE Cohort.
authorString: Ripollés-Melchor J, Jammer I, Creagh-Brown B, Monge-García MI, Espinosa ÁV, Abad-Motos A, Navarro-Pérez R, Budithi R, Abad-Gurumeta A, Aldecoa C, Squeeze Investigators.
abstractText:
Background

Postoperative vasoactive therapy is usually summarised by its presence or duration, although haemodynamic support evolves over time. We investigated whether reproducible postoperative vasoactive exposure patterns provide prognostic information beyond the duration of postoperative vasoactive therapy.

Methods

We performed a prespecified substudy of the international SQUEEZE cohort. Adults receiving postoperative vasoactive infusion within seven postoperative days after non-cardiac surgery were included. Unsupervised k-means clustering identified exposure patterns using duration of postoperative vasoactive infusion, cumulative vasoactive agent-days, and peak number of concurrent agents. Associations with 30-day mortality, acute kidney injury (AKI), and hospital length of stay were assessed using multivariable regression. A prespecified landmark analysis evaluated early postoperative vasoactive exposure burden during postoperative days 0-1.

Results

Among 25,672 patients, 6676 (26.0%) received postoperative vasoactive infusion. Four reproducible exposure patterns were identified. Adjusted 30-day mortality ranged from 9.7% in the low-burden pattern to 35.3% in the high-burden pattern but was not strictly monotonic, whereas adjusted AKI risk increased from 28.0% to 56.0% across patterns. In covariate-adjusted models fitted to the same complete-case cohort, discrimination was higher when exposure pattern rather than duration was included (AUC 0.818 vs. 0.795), while adding duration to pattern classification resulted in little additional discrimination (AUC 0.819). Findings were consistent in the early postoperative landmark analysis.

Conclusions

Postoperative vasoactive exposure follows reproducible patterns characterised by persistence and overall treatment burden rather than binary classification alone. These patterns were associated with mortality, AKI, and hospital length of stay, and provided prognostic information beyond duration alone.

Editorial comment

This substudy and analysis of the SQUEEZE cohort, which represents a large sample of cases with focus on post-operative vasopressor treatments, shows that more intensive vasopressor therapy was associated with worse postoperative outcomes, including for mortality and 30 days and postoperative acute kidney injury occurrence.

Trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03805230.

title: Does COVID-19 Vaccination Protect Against Post-COVID Cardiovascular Conditions?
authorString: Maria LFBS, Naves MCX, Duarte EC, Carvalho IPSF, Peixoto HM.
abstractText: Cardiovascular diseases, such as acute myocardial infarction, heart failure, and arrhythmias, have been associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection, representing an important cause of long-term morbidity and mortality. In addition to preventing primary infection, COVID-19 vaccination has emerged as a protective factor against post-COVID cardiovascular outcomes. This study aims to analyse the evidence supporting a causal relationship between COVID-19 vaccination and the prevention of post-COVID cardiovascular conditions, based on classical and contemporary epidemiological criteria, including the Bradford Hill criteria (BHC) and the sufficient component cause (SCC) model. A qualitative synthesis of the evidence was performed according to the nine BHC and the SCC model. Scientific evidence indicates that COVID-19 vaccination meets four of the nine BHC as a protective factor against post-COVID cardiovascular conditions, namely strength of association, consistency, temporality, and biological gradient. Three criteria, biological plausibility, coherence, and analogy, were partially met. Specificity and experimental evidence were not supported by the available literature. The SCC model highlights the fundamental role of vaccination as a preventive causal component. It also contributes to two criteria, strength of association and temporality, while emphasising the limitation of specificity in causal inference. COVID-19 vaccination has proven effective beyond the acute phase of the disease, with protection extending to a reduced risk of post-COVID cardiovascular conditions. Comprehensive immunisation strategies and reinfection prevention are essential to mitigate the burden of post-COVID conditions. Additional studies are needed to explore the underlying biological mechanisms, interactions, and the role of COVID-19 vaccination in preventing post-COVID complications.

title: The Process to Caregiver Expertise: A Constructivist Grounded Theory Study of Parents of Infants With Critical Congenital Heart Disease.
authorString: Casey S, Pickens N, Poskey G.
abstractText:
Background

Caregivers of hospitalized infants with critical congenital heart disease (CCHD) experience stress, emotions and contextual challenges with staff and unit culture during their infant's stay in critical care units, especially if the stay is lengthy. These compounding adverse conditions impact a caregiver's ability to learn to care for their infant. The purpose of this constructivist grounded theory study was to construct an explanatory theory, based on the analysis of the caregivers' perspectives, uncovering the process caregivers of hospitalized infants go through to become experts in their infant's care in the critical care setting.

Methods

Fifteen mothers and one father participated in semistructured and intensive interviews. Data collection, data analysis and theory formation transpired through an iterative process of constant comparison within and among data cases, theoretical sampling, memos, member-checking and participant feedback.

Results

The result was a co-constructed overarching framework, the Process Model to Caregiver Expertise, progressing through four sequential phases-disorienting, orienting, adapting and knowing-showing how caregiver confidence develops over time and through active participation in caregiving tasks. Findings also indicate that caregivers need prompt peer and mentorship connections and early active participation in caregiving tasks to hasten their transformation into independent, expert caregivers.

Conclusion

Knowing this process may empower caregivers to understand their journey and guide education, support and tool development for healthcare providers. Additional research is needed to explore the paternal caregiver role, healthcare professionals' perceptions of this process and how the model develops as the child ages.

title: Radial Tiny Golden Angle UTE (tyGA-UTE) for Cardiac MRI in the Small Animal Model.
authorString: Li H, Metze P, Han P, Wei B, Rasche V.
abstractText: Robust cardiorespiratory motion correction is critical for high-quality ultra-high-field (UHF) preclinical cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Whereas radial tiny golden angle (tyGA) sampling, data-driven self-gating (sg), compressed sensing (CS), and ultrashort echo time (UTE) are individually well-established techniques, their integration into a unified acquisition and reconstruction pipeline, together with systematic validation at 11.7 T remains insufficiently explored. This study presents and validates a UHF-optimized tyGA-based UTE workflow that enables high-temporal-resolution sliding-window dynamic imaging (SW-tyGA-UTE) and high-spatial-resolution cardiorespiratory self-gated cine imaging (Gated-tyGA-UTE) from a single continuous acquired tyGA acquisition. All experiments were performed on an 11.7-T small-animal MRI system in 16 healthy wild-type mice. Cardiac functional parameters, image quality metrics (signal-to-noise ratio [SNR] and contrast-to-noise ratio [CNR]), and inter-/intra-observer reproducibility were systematically compared between the proposed tyGA-UTE pipeline and two navigator-gated reference techniques: retrospectively gated FLASH and UTE methodologies. SW-tyGA-UTE and Gated-tyGA-UTE reconstructions yielded global left ventricular functional parameters comparable to those obtained with the reference methods (all p > 0.05). All functional metrics showed excellent intra-observer (ICC = 0.94-0.99) and inter-observer (ICC = 0.90-0.98) reproducibility, with ejection fraction showing the highest measurement consistency. Image quality was evaluated using an image-based within-ROI noise quantification approach that captures both thermal noise and reconstruction-related artifacts. In this analysis, the Gated-tyGA-UTE protocol showed no statistically significant differences in left ventricular blood-pool SNR, myocardial SNR, or CNR relative to the reference sequences. In contrast, the high-temporal-resolution sliding-window reconstruction showed significantly reduced image quality across all three metrics, consistent with the expected spatiotemporal trade-off of undersampled dynamic imaging. This study validates a robust, UHF-optimized tyGA-UTE imaging workflow that generates both high-fidelity quantitative cine data and ultra-fast dynamic cardiac images from a single acquisition. The unified pipeline eliminates the need for sequential repeated scans, minimizes anesthesia-related physiological variability, and improves experimental efficiency, providing a practical tool for preclinical cardiac phenotyping, longitudinal studies, and drug screening.

title: Radiographic Comparison of Pulmonary Lobar Vasculature Dimensions in Medically Managed and Drug-Naive Dogs With Left Heart Failure Secondary to Myxomatous Mitral Valve Disease.
authorString: Huguet E, Sleeper M, Robertson J, Berry C.

journal.title: Veterinary radiology & ultrasound : the official journal of the American College of Veterinary Radiology and the International Veterinary Radiology Association

abstractText: Myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) is the most common acquired cause of left heart failure (LHF) in dogs, and radiographic identification of pulmonary venous enlargement is traditionally used to support the diagnosis of LHF. However, the absence of venous enlargement has been anecdotally observed after initiation of therapy. Therefore, we aimed to compare radiographic pulmonary vessel size in LHF patients with ongoing medical management ± receiving acute rescue therapy. Dogs with echocardiographically confirmed MMVD and radiographic cardiogenic pulmonary edema were retrospectively selected. Pulmonary lobar artery and vein widths were measured using standardized rib-to-vessel ratios: cranial vessels at the intersection with the fourth rib on lateral projections and caudal vessels at the ninth rib on ventrodorsal/dorsoventral projections. Pulmonary vein-to-artery (PV/PA) and vessel-to-rib ratios were calculated, with enlargement defined as >1.2 and small vessel size as <0.8, and treatment groups were compared using Welch-corrected t-tests. 200 radiographic studies from 163 dogs were reviewed. In all dogs, the veins measured larger than the arteries in all lung lobes. Chronically untreated dogs who received furosemide immediately before radiographs had no venous enlargement. All other groups had vascular asymmetry or venous enlargement in at least two lung lobes. All control dogs with reoccurrence of LHF had absence of venous enlargement after initiation of therapy. Pulmonary venous enlargement was most pronounced in the right caudal lung lobe. These findings indicate that dogs chronically managed for MMVD may decompensate into LHF without radiographic pulmonary venous enlargement and that furosemide administration prior to imaging can normalize vessel size.

title: Comparative Chemical and Pharmacodynamic Evaluation of Different Purification Procedures for Yangxin Dingji Capsules.
authorString: Lu X, Li D, Hou Z, An Q, Hou F, Xue Z, Xie Z, Liu Y, Zheng Q, Li Y, Guo L, Zhang D.
abstractText: Yangxin Dingji Capsules (YXDJ), derived from Zhigancao Decoction, are used clinically for arrhythmia. Four D101 macroporous-resin purification procedures involving different Asini Corii Colla incorporation modes and elution solvents were compared; the co-decoction procedures additionally included centrifugation and filtration before resin purification. The unpurified preparation and four purified preparations were characterized by UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS and evaluated in a barium chloride-induced rat arrhythmia model using electrocardiographic, biochemical, and histopathological indicators. Fifty-five constituents were tentatively identified. The 60% ethanol-eluted preparations CF1 and CF3 retained 52 and 51 constituents, respectively, whereas the water-eluted preparations CF2 and CF4 retained 21 and 14. CF1 showed the highest Pearson correlation with YXDJ among the purified preparations (r = 0.520), while CF3 had the highest five-indicator comprehensive pharmacodynamic score among the purified preparations (CPS5 = 3.540); unpurified YXDJ scored 3.827. Compared with the model group, CF3 significantly increased heart rate, shortened QRS duration, reduced serum lactate dehydrogenase, and increased Na<sup>+</sup>/K<sup>+</sup>-ATPase activity. Exploratory one-component partial least-squares variable-importance and gray relational analyses generated a provisional list of 12 constituents for subsequent targeted quantification and pharmacological verification.

title: Working With AI and Robotic Systems While Preserving Clinical Judgement, Professional Accountability and Person-Centred Care: Critical Care Nurses' Perspectives.
authorString: Sengul T, Yilmaz Akyaz D, Macit Kaplan B, Akyol YE, Cevizci T, Demiral M, Mahasneh D, Shoqirat N, Kirkland-Kyhn H.
abstractText:
Background

The integration of AI and robotic systems into critical care necessitates examining how ICU nurses preserve clinical judgement, professional accountability and person-centred care while using these technologies.

Aims

To explore ICU nurses' perceptions of AI and robotic systems in critical care, focusing on clinical judgement, trust, responsibility, professional roles and person-centred care.

Study design

A qualitative descriptive study using scenario-based elicitation was conducted. Data were collected through seven semi-structured focus group discussions (FGDs) with 38 ICU nurses working in general, paediatric and cardiovascular surgery ICUs in two hospitals in Istanbul City. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis, supported by MAXQDA 2024.

Findings

Four themes were developed: negotiating trust in AI-supported critical care; preserving human authority, accountability and boundaries; protecting the human core of intensive care nursing; and reimagining AI and robotic systems as supportive partners. ICU nurses evaluated these systems through bedside verification, patient safety, professional responsibility and person-centred care. AI recommendations were useful only when nurses could question, verify, delay or override them according to the patient's current condition. Robotic systems were valuable when they reduced documentation or physical workload, but not when they replaced clinical judgement, emotional presence, reassurance or accountability.

Conclusions

ICU nurses conceptualised AI and robotic systems as acceptable only when clinically verifiable, professionally bounded and subordinate to human judgement. The findings support a model of AI- and robot-supported ICU care that is responsible, human-led and person-centred.

Relevance to clinical practice

AI and robotic systems should be implemented in ways that strengthen, rather than replace, nurses' clinical judgement, accountability and bedside presence. Clear protocols are needed to verify AI outputs, define robotic task boundaries, support nurses' authority to question or override recommendations and preserve person-centred care in technologically intensive ICU environments.

title: Tailored Amino Acid Treatment for Pediatric Patients With Mitochondrial Aminoacyl-tRNA Synthetase Deficiencies.
authorString: Muffels IJJ, Kok G, Tang Z, Medeiros LS, Poswar FO, Vermeij WP, Rodenburg R, Smit K, Sukumaran SK, Wortmann SB, Averdunk L, Munch J, Ho JP, Kwok AMK, Nieuwenhuis EES, van Hasselt PM, Schwartz IVD, Lubout CMA, Bosch AM, Koop K, van Konijnenburg EMMH, Fuchs SA.
abstractText: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases (ARSs) facilitate the loading of transfer RNAs with their cognate amino acids in the cytosol (ARS1), mitochondria (ARS2), or both (dual ARS). ARS deficiencies are clinically heterogeneous and can cause severe, occasionally fatal disease. Supplementation with cognate amino acids to prevent local amino acid depletion has shown promise in ARS1 deficiencies, but its potential in ARS2 deficiencies remains largely unexplored. We investigated the effects of cognate amino acid depletion on mitochondrial function in fibroblasts from seven patients with ARS2 deficiencies using Seahorse respirometry and imaging flow cytometry. During amino acid depletion, patient fibroblasts showed decreased mitochondrial membrane potential and reduced basal and maximal respiratory capacity. We additionally evaluated oral cognate amino acid supplementation in nine patients with SARS2, EARS2, LARS2, WARS2, FARS2, or VARS2 deficiencies. Supplementation was well tolerated, with no adverse effects observed. Several patients showed clinical improvements during treatment, including improved development, increased growth, and/or improved cardiac function. In two patients, treatment discontinuation coincided with severe neurological regression. Together, these findings demonstrate that assessing mitochondrial function during cognate amino acid depletion provides a novel functional assay for ARS2 deficiencies that may aid variant interpretation and supports a biological rationale for cognate amino acid supplementation. Clinical supplementation was well tolerated and showed preliminary beneficial effects. These findings support further investigation of cognate amino acid supplementation as a potential supportive treatment strategy for patients with ARS2 deficiencies.

title: Correlative X-ray imaging and fluorescence microscopy in hydrated environments.
authorString: Sinha M, Yu B, Mendes Da Silva R, Rölleke U, Luley P, Tiburcy M, Zimmermann WH, Burghammer M, Köster S.
abstractText: Imaging cellular organization in its native state is essential for understanding how the molecular architecture governs biological function. Fluorescence microscopy is one of the pivotal techniques that provides molecular specificity for imaging in real space, but is limited to labeled components. In contrast, X-rays are sensitive to electron density variations, enabling label-free structural characterization in reciprocal space. In particular, scanning small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) combines information from real and reciprocal space and enables access to intact cells owing to the high penetration power of X-rays. To harness the complementary strengths of these approaches, we developed a correlative imaging platform integrating a modular, compact, and beamline-compatible fluorescence microscope with scanning SAXS. The system enables fast sequential imaging of the same cellular regions under hydrated, near-native conditions using a dedicated microfluidic chamber. Applying this approach to keratin bundles in epithelial cells and force-generating actomyosin in cardiomyocytes, we demonstrate good agreement between fluorescence and SAXS-derived orientation maps. This result shows that label-free SAXS captures cytoskeletal organization throughout the cell, and can be directly linked to specific molecular information under physiologically relevant conditions. Our work establishes a general strategy for multimodal imaging of cellular architecture and enables studies of living cells under drugs and chemical manipulation.

title: Evaluating Perfusion Quantification for Phase-Resolved Functional Lung MRI Using Gaussian Filtering.
authorString: Schmidt KJ, Voskrebenzev A, Glandorf JMW, Klein MM, Behrendt L, Wacker F, Vogel-Claussen J, Klimeš F.
abstractText: Phase-resolved functional lung (PREFUL) MRI enables contrast-free lung perfusion quantification (Q<sub>Quant</sub>). Current quantification uses a single median value per slice of maximal blood exchange fraction (ΔS), which limits regional assessment, whereas regional ΔS causes artifacts. This retrospective study aims to optimize Q<sub>Quant</sub> by applying Gaussian filtering to ΔS to improve intrascan/interscan repeatability in healthy volunteers, while evaluating whether the optimized Q<sub>Quant</sub> retains agreement with dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) MRI in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) patients and exhibits a physiologically plausible gravity-dependent perfusion gradient. Analysis was performed on 29 healthy subjects (11 female, age: 19-33 years), 20 COPD patients (three female, age: 46-76 years) and 15 CTEPH patients (six female, age: 44-82 years), scanned at 1.5 T. Healthy subjects underwent four PREFUL scans in two sessions. Patients just underwent one PREFUL and DCE scan. Q<sub>Quant</sub> maps were calculated while applying different Gaussian filter options to ΔS. In patients, PREFUL-derived Q<sub>Quant</sub> maps were coregistered to DCE-derived pulmonary blood flow (PBF) maps for global and voxel-wise correlations. In healthy subjects, the gravity-dependent perfusion gradient was quantified by linear regression of slice-wise Q<sub>Quant</sub> across five coronal slices. Gaussian filtering ΔS with σ = 1.5 improved intrascan and interscan repeatability in healthy subjects (mean bias: ≤ 2.94 mL/100 mL; Cohen's d: 0.2) compared with the current slice median setting (mean bias: ≥ 3.75 mL/100 mL; Cohen's d: 0.68). Correlations with PBF remained stable after filtering (σ = 1.5) in COPD (filtered vs. default ΔS: global r = 0.57 vs. r = 0.59, voxel-wise r = 0.32 vs. r = 0.32) and CTEPH (global r = 0.32 vs. r = 0.28, voxel-wise r = 0.40 vs. r = 0.41), all significant except global CTEPH. The filtered Q<sub>Quant</sub> maps showed a significant gravity-dependent perfusion gradient (ΔS filtered σ = 1.5) of 1.47 mL/min/100 mL/cm. Gaussian filtering ΔS with σ = 1.5 improved Q<sub>Quant</sub> repeatability while preserving DCE-MRI agreement and is therefore recommended. The observed gravity-dependent perfusion gradient confirms physiological plausibility, supporting potential in clinical use.

title: CT protocol optimization for oncologic surveillance imaging: phantom-based comparison of multi-scan and single-scan acquisition strategies.
authorString: Kostova-Lefterova D, Simeonov F, Hitova-Topkarova D, Yordanov A, Payakova V.
abstractText: Computed tomography (CT) plays an important role in oncologic surveillance after treatment of gynecological malignancies, including patients treated with vaginal electronic brachytherapy. This phantom study evaluated CT acquisition strategies for oncologic surveillance, focusing on radiation dose reduction and objective image quality in the cranial, thoracic, and upper abdominal regions assessed quantitatively. CT acquisition protocols were investigated using an anthropomorphic Kyoto Kagaku phantom. Two acquisition strategies were analyzed: a multi-scan approach with separate acquisitions for the head, neck, thorax, and abdomen-pelvis, and a single-scan head-torso acquisition with region-specific reconstructions. Different exposure parameter settings and reconstruction kernels were evaluated. Objective image quality was assessed using semi-automated region-of-interest measurements with a custom FIJI/ImageJ macro. Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and Artifact Index (AI) were calculated for cranial, thoracic, and abdominal regions. For the single-scan protocols, CTDIvol decreased from 4.21 mGy in the standard protocol to 2.97-3.99 mGy in the optimized protocols, while DLP decreased from 410 mGy.cm to 287-388 mGy.cm. Across all anatomical regions, SNR and CNR remained comparable with the standard protocol. Thoracic CNR ranged from 2.68 to 3.01, abdominal CNR remained stable in both liver and aortic regions, and AI demonstrated only moderate variability across the optimized protocols. Optimized CT acquisition protocols reduced radiation dose while preserving the evaluated objective image quality metrics in the cranial, thoracic, and upper abdominal regions. Among the evaluated configurations, a reduced dose single scan head-torso acquisition using reduced tube voltage and tube current modulation showed a favorable balance between radiation dose reduction and objective image quality under the investigated phantom conditions and was identified as a candidate protocol for subsequent clinical and reader performance validation.

title: Perioperative Hemodynamic Management in Elderly Hypertensive Patients: A Systematic Review of Monitoring-Guided Strategies and Postoperative Outcomes
authorString: Ashiq M, Zhang W, Li L.
abstractText: Background Older adults receiving long-term antihypertensive therapy represent a rapidly growing surgical population in whom intraoperative blood pressure management remains contentious. Observational evidence consistently links intraoperative hypotension with adverse postoperative outcomes, but whether specific blood pressure targets or hemodynamic management strategies improve clinical outcomes remains uncertain Methods We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov from 1 January 2013 to 15 January 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and prospective or retrospective cohort studies of haemodynamic monitoring-guided management in patients with a mean or median age of at least 65 years receiving chronic antihypertensive therapy or with documented chronic hypertension undergoing non-cardiac surgery. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data using a piloted form capturing design, setting, population, hypertension status, intervention, comparator, and raw outcome events, and assessed risk of bias (RoB 2 for RCTs; ROBINS-I for cohort studies). Quantitative pooling was prespecified only for comparisons with three or more studies sharing design, intervention class, and outcome definition; otherwise, a structured narrative synthesis with fully tabulated study-level effect data was performed. Certainty was rated with GRADE. Reporting follows PRISMA 2020. Results Nineteen studies (7 randomized controlled trials reported in 9 publications; 12 cohort studies) comprising 1,074,313 patients were included. In RCTs, higher or individualized intraoperative blood pressure targets did not reduce major vascular or organ-injury composites compared with routine targets (POISE-3: risk ratio [RR] 0.99, 95% CI 0.89–1.11; IMPROVE-multi: RR 1.10, 95% CI 0.93–1.30), although one small trial favoured individualized systolic targets (INPRESS: RR 0.74, 95% CI 0.57–0.95); certainty was low because of inconsistency and indirectness. Observational cohorts consistently reported duration-dependent associations between intraoperative hypotension and acute kidney injury or myocardial injury (moderate certainty for the association, not for a causal effect of any specific target). Goal-directed haemodynamic therapy was neutral in the largest contemporary trial (OPTIMISE II: postoperative infection RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.88–1.18) but beneficial in smaller earlier trials (low certainty). Continuing renin–angiotensin-system inhibitors increased intraoperative hypotension (RR 1.31, 95% CI 1.19–1.44) without increasing major complications (RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.87–1.19; moderate certainty). A hypotension-avoidance strategy did not reduce postoperative delirium in randomized data (cogPOISE-3: RR 1.04, 95% CI 0.79–1.38), and observational findings were inconsistent (low certainty). Conclusions Intraoperative hypotension is consistently and duration-dependently associated with organ injury in observational surgical cohorts, although much of this evidence is derived from broader non-cardiac surgical populations rather than exclusively elderly hypertensive patients. Randomized evidence specific to elderly hypertensive populations remains limited and does not demonstrate consistent benefit from higher blood pressure targets, goal-directed haemodynamic therapy, or specific antihypertensive withholding strategies.Recommendations for this population should rest on guidelines and individualized judgment rather than on claims of moderate-certainty trial evidence that the current literature does not provide. Renal denervation and other device-based therapies are outside the scope of this review and are identified as future research priorities only.

title: Right Vertical Infra-Axillary Minithoracotomy Versus Median Sternotomy for Doubly Committed Subarterial Ventricular Septal Defect: A Retrospective Cohort Study of 689 Patients
authorString: Li X, Bao W, Jin D, Wang Y, Zhu J, Shi J, Li T, Pan Y, Yin M.
abstractText:
Background: Minimally invasive approaches are increasingly used for surgical repair of congenital heart defects. However, evidence for right vertical infra-axillary minithoracotomy (RVIAT) in doubly committed subarterial ventricular septal defect (dcVSD) remains limited. This study compared the perioperative outcomes of median sternotomy and RVIAT in patients with dcVSD and evaluated the safety, feasibility, and overall incision-related satisfaction of RVIAT.

Methods:

This single-center retrospective study included 689 consecutive patients with dcVSD who underwent primary surgical repair between January 2021 and October 2025. Patients were classified into two groups according to the incision type: the median sternotomy group (Mid group, n = 222) and the right thoracic incision group (Right group, n = 467). Perioperative outcomes, postoperative complications, follow-up findings, and a five-level overall incision-related satisfaction rating were compared between groups. Age-stratified analyses and propensity score matching (PSM) were performed to reduce the impact of baseline differences.

Results:

Compared with the Mid group, patients in the Right group had significantly shorter hospital stay and mechanical ventilation duration (both P < 0.001). Cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) time and cardiac intensive care unit (CICU) stay were comparable between groups. Age-stratified analyses showed subgroup-specific differences, whereas PSM confirmed shorter hospital stay and mechanical ventilation duration in the Right group. The incidence of residual shunt remained low and comparable both postoperatively and at 6-month follow-up (all P  > 0.05). Similarly, no significant differences were observed in the progression of aortic regurgitation or reoperation rates. No in-hospital mortality occurred. Overall incision-related satisfaction was significantly higher in the Right group than in the Mid group (84.3% vs. 36.0%, P < 0.001).

Conclusions:

In patients with dcVSD, the RVIAT approach provides perioperative safety and clinical outcomes comparable to those of median sternotomy, and higher reported overall incision-related satisfaction at six months. It provides a feasible alternative to median sternotomy. Trial registration Clinical trial number: Not applicable.

title: Association of daily and on-demand tadalafil use with all-cause mortality and cardiovascular outcomes in men with erectile dysfunction and lower urinary tract symptoms: a propensity score-matched real-world cohort study
authorString: Lee YS, Chen C, Lai G, Li J.
abstractText: Background Erectile dysfunction (ED) and lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) secondary to benign prostatic hyperplasia are common conditions in middle-aged and older men and are associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease and mortality. Emerging evidence suggests that phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5) inhibitors may provide cardiovascular benefits beyond symptomatic improvement. Tadalafil is unique among PDE5 inhibitors because it is prescribed as either a once-daily low-dose regimen (5 mg) or an on-demand high-dose regimen (20 mg). However, whether these dosing strategies differ in their association with long-term mortality and cardiovascular outcomes remains uncertain. This study evaluated the association of daily tadalafil 5 mg and on-demand tadalafil 20 mg use with all-cause mortality and cardiovascular outcomes in men with ED and/or LUTS. Methods This retrospective cohort study used de-identified electronic health record data from the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Men aged ≥ 40 years diagnosed with ED and/or LUTS between January 2012 and December 2022 who received tadalafil 5 mg or tadalafil 20 mg were identified and compared with patients who did not receive PDE5 inhibitors. Patients with pre-existing major cardiovascular disease, exposure to other PDE5 inhibitors, or receipt of both tadalafil regimens were excluded. A two-phase analysis was performed, comparing each tadalafil regimen with non-users, followed by a direct comparison between tadalafil 5 mg and tadalafil 20 mg. Propensity score matching was performed for demographic characteristics and major comorbidities. The primary outcomes were all-cause mortality, cerebrovascular accident, heart failure, and ischaemic heart disease in the period of 14 years of follow-up. Results The final study population included 28,376 patients receiving tadalafil 5 mg, 31,321 receiving tadalafil 20 mg, and 1,066,587 patients who did not receive PDE5 inhibitors. After propensity score matching, both tadalafil 5 mg and tadalafil 20 mg were associated with significantly lower risks of all-cause mortality (risk ratio [RR] 0.574 and 0.617, respectively), cerebrovascular accident (RR 0.727 and 0.818), heart failure (RR 0.668 and 0.704), and ischaemic heart disease (RR 0.819 and 0.856) compared with non-users. In the propensity score-matched head-to-head comparison, Kaplan–Meier analyses demonstrated improved overall survival (HR 1.116, 95% CI 1.033–1.205; P  = 0.005) and cardiovascular disease-free survival (HR 1.050, 95% CI 1.010–1.091; P  = 0.013) among patients receiving tadalafil 20 mg compared with tadalafil 5 mg. Conclusions Among men aged ≥ 40 years with ED and/or LUTS, treatment with either tadalafil 5 mg or tadalafil 20 mg was associated with lower risks of all-cause mortality and individual cardiovascular outcomes compared with non-use of PDE5 inhibitors. In this observational study, on-demand tadalafil 20 mg was associated with more favourable long-term survival outcomes than daily tadalafil 5 mg in time-to-event analyses. Prospective randomized studies are warranted to confirm these findings and determine whether the observed associations reflect a causal treatment effect. (Clinical trial number: not applicable)

title: Mycoplasma hominis bloodstream infection following transfemoral cannulation for extracorporeal life support: a case report
authorString: Yin Z, Lv L, Yu Z, Song D, Hu W.
abstractText: Background Mycoplasma hominis(M. hominis) is a common commensal of the urogenital tract frequently associated with localized infections; however, hematogenous dissemination is uncommon, and cases secondary to indwelling central venous catheters are exceedingly rare. Here, we report a case of M. hominis bloodstream infection following transfemoral cannulation for extracorporeal life support, including an intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). Case Presentation: A 68-year-old male patient underwent coronary stent implantation for acute myocardial infarction at Haining People's Hospital on July 25, 2025. Postoperatively, he developed heart failure and cardiogenic shock, necessitating IABP support. Although, his cardiac function and hemodynamics improved, and the patient’s IABP was weaned on Day 8. However, the patient subsequently developed recurrent dyspnea, along with increasing body temperature and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels. CRRT was therefore initiated to maintain fluid balance and metabolic homeostasis and to remove inflammatory mediators. Despite this, the patient continued to experience fever with persistently elevated inflammatory markers. On Day 13, blood cultures, urine cultures, and catheter tip cultures were obtained. Hemodynamic deterioration occurred on Day 15, prompting veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) support. Dynamic monitoring revealed a rising trend in troponin I levels, and repeated coronary angiography demonstrated occlusion of the coronary stent, which was managed with balloon dilatation. The patient was then transferred to the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University for further management. On Day 16, the microbiology laboratory at Haining People's Hospital reported that the blood cultures yielded M. hominis ; this finding was communicated to the receiving hospital. Subsequent anti-infective therapy with omadacycline was administered. After undergoing left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation, the patient ultimately improved and was discharged in stable condition. Conclusions In terms of femoral catheter-related infections adjacent to the urogenital tract, uncommon atypical pathogens such as M. hominis warrant consideration in addition to routine bacterial etiologies.

title: Predictive Value of EuroSCORE II in Contemporary Cardiac Surgery : Insights from the EPICARD Registry
authorString: PICCOLI J, Youinou M, Roussel J, Leprince P, Verhoye J, Baufreton C, Kindo M, Bouchot O, Vincentelli A, Maureira J, Bourguignon T, Pernot M, Roques F, De Boissieu P, De Brux J, Guihaire J.
abstractText: Objective The predictive performance of EuroSCORE II may have evolved over the last decade owing to major changes in cardiac surgery practice, including an ageing population, increasing comorbidity burden, and advances in perioperative management. We aimed to evaluate the contemporary performance of EuroSCORE II in a large nationwide French cohort. Methods We conducted a retrospective analysis of consecutive adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery between 2020 and 2024 in centers participating in the French EPICARD registry (French Society of Cardiothoracic and Vascular Surgery, Federation des Specialites Medicales, France). Patients undergoing heart transplantation, durable mechanical circulatory support implantation, cardiac tumor surgery, or with missing EuroSCORE II data were excluded. The primary endpoint was operative mortality, defined as in-hospital or 30-day mortality, identified through linkage with the French national mortality database (INSEE). Discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), while calibration was evaluated using the Hosmer–Lemeshow test and calibration plots. Results A total of 108,412 patients were included. Median EuroSCORE II was 1.7% [IQR 1.0–3.4], and overall operative mortality was 3.3% (n = 3,572). EuroSCORE II demonstrated acceptable discriminative performance (AUC 0.83, 95% CI 0.82–0.84). Calibration varied across surgical subgroups, with slight overestimation in low-risk patients and isolated CABG, and underestimation in high-risk settings, particularly acute aortic dissection and combined CABG-aortic procedures. Conclusions EuroSCORE II remains a valuable risk stratification tool in contemporary cardiac surgery but shows calibration limitations in specific high-risk populations, supporting the need for periodic recalibration and updated risk models.

title: Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection Presenting with Monomorphic Ventricular Tachycardia in a Young Man Hospitalized for Pneumonia and Severe Coughing Episodes: A Case Report
authorString: Ersin A, Açar M, Berk ME, Uçar M, Özyurtlu F, Çetin N.
abstractText: Background: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) accounts for approximately 5% of myocardial infarction (MI) cases and predominantly affects young women without traditional cardiovascular risk factors; it is markedly less common in men. Recognized triggers include severe physical exertion, emotional stress, and conditions that acutely raise intrathoracic pressure, such as severe coughing. Case Presentation: A 21-year-old male was hospitalized with a preliminary diagnosis of pneumonia after severe coughing episodes. He had recently started tirzepatide for obesity. During hospitalization he developed chest pain and tachycardia; an electrocardiogram (ECG) captured monomorphic ventricular tachycardia (VT), and a repeat ECG after rate control showed inferior ST-segment elevation. Echocardiography revealed a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 35%. Coronary angiography demonstrated spontaneous dissection of the circumflex artery (CX) without atherosclerotic disease elsewhere. The patient was managed conservatively with dual antiplatelet therapy and enoxaparin, remained free of recurrent symptoms, and was discharged with an improved LVEF of 40%. Conclusion: SCAD should be considered in young men presenting with chest pain or arrhythmia after severe coughing, even without classic cardiovascular risk factors. The co-occurrence of CX-related SCAD, inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), and monomorphic VT is rarely reported and raises the possibility of Purkinje-related arrhythmogenesis in this territory, a mechanism warranting further study.

title: Time to Death and its Predictors among Stroke Patients with Hypertension at Comprehensive Specialized Public Hospitals
authorString: Bizu YS, Ayenew KD.
abstractText: Background Stroke is a leading cause of death, with hypertension significantly increasing mortality risk. However, studies on time to death and its predictors among hypertensive stroke patients are scarce in Ethiopia. This study aimed to assess the time to death and its predictors among h stroke patients with hypertension admitted at public hospitals in the Amhara region, 2023. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted among stroke patients with hypertension admitted to selected public hospitals in the Amhara region, Ethiopia. Data were collected using a structured checklist, entered into EPI Data 4.2, and analyzed with STATA 16. The proportional hazards assumption was checked, and model fitness was assessed using Cox–Snell residuals (p > 0.05). Variables with p < 0.25 in bi-variable analysis were included in the multivariable Cox regression to control for confounders, and predictors of time to death were identified in the final model using adjusted hazard ratios (AHR) with p < 0.05. Result: The study included 737 participants, 307 (45.7%) of them died, with an overall median time to death of 40 days (IQR: 39, 57), and 400 (54.3%) were censored. Most of 309 (91.7%) death were greater than aged 65 years old and 246 (73%) were males with proportion of 333(98.8%) death in hemorrhagic stroke. Age group > 65 years [AHR=3.2(95%CI,1.28-8.06)], elevated blood pressure [ARH=5.75(95%CI,2.23,14.79)],Cardiovascular disease [AHR= 0.08 (95%CI:0.01- 0.43)],consumed alcohol [AHR=12.9 (95% CI: 2.57- 65.51)] , complication at admission [AHR= 8.2 (95% CI: 4.19-16.37)], unconscious (GCS<8) [AHR:=3.30 (95% CI: 1.46-7.47)] and drowsy (GCS 9-12) at the time of admission [AHR:2.30 (95% CI:1.06-4.99)] were statistically significant predictors of death patients stroke with hypertension. Conclusion and recommendation: A study reported a median recovery time of 40 days for stroke patient with hypertensive, with a recovery rate of 10 per 1,000 person-days. Age, blood pressure, presence of cardiovascular disease, alcohol use, Glasgow Coma Scale score, and associated complications were significant associated predictors of death.

title: Acute Extensive Anterior Myocardial Infarction Complicated by Intramyocardial Dissecting Hematoma of the Interventricular Septum with Perforation: A Case Report
authorString: Chen J, Deng S.
abstractText: Background Intramural dissecting hematoma (IDH) is a rare but life-threatening subacute cardiac rupture type that occurs after acute myocardial infarction or during its remodeling process. IDH may resolve spontaneously, or it may extend and destroy adjacent structures, leading to serious mechanical complications. Owing to its low incidence and limited literature, there is currently no standardized diagnostic, therapeutic, or management consensus. Case presentation: A 67‑year‑old male with acute extensive anterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction underwent emergency coronary angiography and percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty. After the procedure, the patient still had precordial discomfort and was transferred to our hospital. One week later, repeat angiography with intra‑aortic balloon pump (IABP) support revealed suspected left anterior descending branch (LAD) dissection, prompting two-stent implantation. The next day, echocardiography showed an apical septal myocardial dissecting hematoma with complex perforation. Surgical ventricular septal repair was planned electively. On day 25 after infarction, cardiogenic shock and multiple organ failure developed; after IABP and biventricular assist device support, acute cerebral infarction occurred, and the family ultimately withdrew treatment. Conclusion Ventricular septal IDH with perforation after acute myocardial infarction is a rare and catastrophic mechanical complication. Early recognition, appropriate timing of intervention, and adequate use of mechanical circulatory support are key to improving prognosis.

title: Development and Validation of a Nomogram for Predicting Cardiogenic Shock in Elderly Patients with ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Retrospective Cohort Study
authorString: Liu Z, Yang S, Mao Y, Ma L, Song W, Huang H.
abstractText: Background Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains the most lethal complication of ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), particularly in elderly patients who lack dedicated prediction tools. This study developed and internally validated a nomogram for admission-time CS risk stratification in elderly (≥ 60 years) STEMI patients, and evaluated the incremental value of combining Killip classification with laboratory parameters. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study consecutively enrolled 527 patients aged ≥ 60 years with STEMI between January 2019 and December 2022; after excluding 4 patients with missing CS status, 523 were analyzed (CS, n = 39; non-CS, n = 484). Admission demographics, Killip classification, comorbidities, vital signs, laboratory tests, echocardiography, and coronary angiography data were collected. Candidate variables were screened by univariate logistic regression (P < 0.1), followed by multivariate logistic regression. Discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration by the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and internal validation by 1000 bootstrap resamples; the likelihood ratio test and DeLong test compared models, and decision curve analysis evaluated clinical utility. Results Killip class III-IV (OR = 13.531, 95% CI: 5.541–33.039, P < 0.001) and age (OR = 1.076, 95% CI: 1.016–1.139, P = 0.013) were independent predictors of CS. The combined model (Killip class, D-dimer, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, left ventricular ejection fraction, glucose, and age) achieved an AUC of 0.874 (95% CI: 0.819–0.927), significantly outperforming Killip classification alone (AUC = 0.815, DeLong P = 0.001) and the laboratory-only model (AUC = 0.775, DeLong P = 0.014). A parsimonious Killip + age model achieved a comparable AUC of 0.864 (likelihood ratio test P = 0.168; DeLong P = 0.140). The bootstrap-corrected AUC was 0.858 with good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.412). Decision curve analysis demonstrated positive net benefit across the 5%-25% threshold range, and a simplified 25-point bedside scoring rule achieved an AUC of 0.846. Conclusions The nomogram effectively predicts admission-time CS risk in elderly STEMI patients. When Killip classification is available, adding age alone yields a powerful and parsimonious bedside tool, while the full nomogram remains preferable when maximal predictive performance is pursued. External validation is required.

title: Development and temporal validation of a prediction model for emergence agitation in older patients undergoing orthopedic surgery with general anesthesia: a single-center retrospective cohort study
authorString: WU L, Chen L, Huang X, Zhang D, Chen M, Wang Z, Fu C, Wu Y.
abstractText: Background To develop and validate a risk prediction model for emergence agitation (EA) in older patients undergoing orthopedic surgery under general anesthesia, thereby providing an adjunctive tool for early risk stratification in the post-anesthesia care unit (PACU). Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study included 1,339 patients treated between January and December 2025 in the model development cohort and 670 patients treated between January and June 2026 in a same-center temporal validation cohort. Predictors were selected using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO). Five candidate models were developed using logistic regression (LR), classification and regression tree (CART), random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and support vector machine (SVM). Model performance was evaluated using nested stratified fivefold cross-validation. The final model was selected by jointly considering discrimination, calibration, the Brier score, and decision curve analysis, and was interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Results The incidence of EA was 29.6% in the development cohort and 22.2% in the temporal validation cohort. LASSO selected seven predictors: drinking history, history of hypertension, history of stroke, sevoflurane use, patient-controlled analgesia pump setup, indwelling urinary catheter, and PaCO₂. Considering overall performance and parsimony, LR was selected as the final model. Its area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.929 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.913–0.945) in internal validation and 0.904 (95% CI 0.876–0.932) in temporal validation. The calibration intercept was − 0.797 and the calibration slope was 0.729, indicating some overestimation of risk. Conclusions The LR model showed good discrimination and may support risk stratification in the PACU. Multicenter external validation and evaluation of calibration in new target populations are required before broader implementation.

title: Familial Tracheobronchopathia Osteochondroplastica in Two Mongolian Siblings: A Case Report
authorString: Jiang X, Wang Q, Ma S, Li J, He Z.
abstractText: Background Tracheobronchopathia osteochondroplastica (TO) is a rare disorder characterized by submucosal cartilaginous or ossified nodules in the tracheobronchial tree. Although chronic inflammation and trauma have been implicated, genetic factors remain unexplored. Case presentation This study enrolled two Mongolian siblings diagnosed with TO. The 38-year-old female patient presented with a 5-year chronic cough and acute onset of high fever and purulent sputum. Imaging examinations revealed bronchiectasis and diffuse tracheal wall calcification. Bronchoscopy showed tracheal mucosal granular hyperplasia, and pathological biopsy confirmed airway chronic inflammation and multifocal interstitial ossification. Her 38-year-old elder brother had a 6-year history of hypertension and one month of intermittent exertional chest tightness and wheezing. Chest CT demonstrated irregular tracheal wall thickening and luminal stenosis. Bronchoscopy detected diffusely distributed fragile airway nodules, and pathological examination verified bronchial mucosal metaplasia and interstitial ossification lesions. Both patients received standardized comprehensive symptomatic treatment including oral moxifloxacin and aerosolized budesonide and terbutaline during hospitalization. Clinical symptoms were significantly relieved after treatment. In follow-up lasting 4–6 months, only intermittent mild respiratory symptoms were observed without severe disease recurrence or adverse events. Conclusion This sibling case report of tracheobronchopathia osteochondroplastica (TO) suggests potential genetic factors underlying the pathogenesis of this disease.

title: Preoperative Glucose-to-Albumin Ratio and Postoperative Acute Kidney Injury in Patients Admitted to the Cardiac Surgery Recovery Unit: Association Analyses and Interpretable Machine Learning Based on the MIMIC-IV Database
authorString: wang p, Ren H, zhang q.
abstractText: Background Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a frequent and serious complication after cardiac surgery. The glucose-to-albumin ratio (GAR) is an emerging composite biomarker, but its association with postoperative AKI in the cardiac surgery recovery unit (CSRU) remains unclear. Methods Adult CSRU patients were extracted from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV, version 3.1). AKI was defined and staged according to the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria using both serum creatinine and urine output. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, propensity score matching, subgroup interaction tests and causal mediation analyses were used to characterize the GAR–AKI association. Ten machine learning algorithms were trained on 15 candidate predictors including GAR, and model performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, decision curve analysis and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Results Of 4,418 patients, 3,524 (79.8%) developed AKI. Median GAR increased stepwise with AKI severity (non-AKI 26.92; stage 1, 27.78; stage 2, 29.36; stage 3, 31.94; P for trend < 0.001). In the fully adjusted model, the third and fourth GAR quartiles were associated with higher odds of AKI (OR 1.608, 95% CI 1.292–2.004; OR 1.465, 95% CI 1.181–1.821, respectively). Restricted cubic spline analysis indicated an approximately linear dose-response relationship (P for nonlinear = 0.444).
