The association remained robust after propensity score adjustment and matching. Significant interactions were observed for body mass index, hypertension and diabetes. Mediation analysis suggested that hypoalbuminemia, comorbidity burden and illness severity partially mediated the association. The logistic regression model achieved the best discrimination in the validation set (AUC = 0.942), with good calibration and clinical net benefit. SHAP analysis confirmed GAR as an independent contributor. Conclusions Elevated preoperative GAR is independently associated with postoperative AKI and its severity in CSRU patients. As an inexpensive, routinely available composite biomarker, GAR may facilitate early AKI risk stratification, and interpretable machine learning models incorporating GAR show excellent predictive performance pending external validation.

title: Multimodal Circulating Myeloid Cell Analysis in Peripheral Artery Disease Reveals Neutrophil Priming and Monocyte Dysfunction
authorString: Kurt S, Pirronello F, Reitsema RD, Farkas SA, Carlsson J, Petri MH, Hjelmqvist H, Dreifaldt M, Zegeye MM, Maffia P, Demirel I, Rangel I, Sirsjö A, Kumawat AK.
abstractText: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is a common age-associated cardiovascular disease, but how circulating innate immune cells are remodelled in PAD remains incompletely understood. Here, we performed an integrated analysis of circulating myeloid cells in PAD patients with intermittent claudication and healthy controls, combining high dimensional flow-cytometric immunophenotyping, ex vivo functional assays, plasma inflammatory markers, transcriptomic profiling of neutrophils and monocytes, and exploratory epigenetic analysis of neutrophils. PAD was associated with expansion of circulating neutrophils, conventional dendritic cells, and monocyte subsets, together with altered CD162⁺ myeloid cell profiles. Several of these differences persisted after adjustment for age, body mass index, and smoking status. Functionally, PAD neutrophils showed enhanced IL-6 and IL-8 production after LPS stimulation but reduced phagocytic capacity and lower intracellular reactive oxygen species. PAD was also associated with elevated circulating myeloperoxidase, without increased circulating NET-associated markers. In contrast, monocytes displayed attenuated cytokine production and impaired phagocytosis despite increased absolute counts. Transcriptomic analysis revealed an enrichment of inflammatory pathways, including TLR/NLR/NF-κB and JAK–STAT signalling, and reduced enrichment of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and autophagy programs in PAD neutrophils, whereas classical monocytes showed no significant resting-state differential gene expression. These findings identify systemic myeloid immune remodelling as a feature of PAD and suggest cell type-specific innate immune dysfunction in the context of aging.

title: A 20-year indwelling dual-coil passive-fixation ICD lead complicated by CIED pocket infection in an 85-year-old patient: a rare case report
authorString: Bao Y, Zhang Q, Li L, Han H.
abstractText: Background Complete removal of the cardiovascular implantable electronic device (CIED) system is the only curative treatment for CIED pocket infection. Advanced age and prolonged lead dwell time significantly increase the risks of transvenous lead extraction (TLE). However, reports of TLE in patients over 85 years with leads indwelling for two decades are exceedingly rare. Case presentation We report an 85-year-old man with a dual-coil passive-fixation implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) lead implanted 20 years prior, who presented with CIED pocket infection. Intraoperatively, occlusion of the mid-to-distal lead lumen was encountered during locking stylet advancement, precluding laser sheath extraction. An 11-F TightRail™ rotational mechanical dilator sheath was therefore used to dissect dense fibrotic tissue surrounding the lead in a layer-by-layer fashion, enabling complete lead extraction. After one week of antimicrobial therapy, a subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (S-ICD) was implanted due to persistent high risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias and the risk of recurrent pocket infection associated with transvenous lead reimplantation. Conclusions This case represents a rare clinical scenario of TLE in an octogenarian with a 20-year indwelling dual-coil passive lead and multiple comorbidities. The successful outcome underscores the importance of meticulous preoperative risk stratification, multidisciplinary collaboration, and individualized procedural strategies for such high-risk patients.

title: Preoperative central nervous system stimulant exposure and atrial fibrillation after coronary artery bypass grafting: a propensity-matched federated cohort study
authorString: Lum J, Jordan A, Hisamoto K.
abstractText: Background Postoperative atrial fibrillation is a common complication of coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), and prescription stimulant use is increasing among adults. We evaluated the association between recorded preoperative stimulant exposure and atrial fibrillation or flutter after CABG. Methods Using the TriNetX Research Network, we compared patients with an order for 1 of 6 stimulants within 3 months before or on the date of CABG with patients without a recorded order. Patients with atrial fibrillation or flutter documented at least 1 day before CABG were excluded before matching. Cohorts were matched 1:1 on 43 characteristics. The primary outcome occurred during postoperative days 1 through 30. Results Among 1082 matched patients per group, atrial fibrillation or flutter occurred in 147 exposed patients (13.6%) and 115 controls (10.6%; risk ratio [RR] 1.28, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.02–1.61; P  = 0.035). The risk difference was 3.0 percentage points (95% CI 0.2–5.7) and the hazard ratio was 1.29 (95% CI 1.01–1.65). Sensitivity analyses remained above the null but varied in magnitude (RR range 1.28–2.47). Conclusions Recorded preoperative stimulant exposure was associated with a modestly higher rate of atrial fibrillation or flutter after CABG. The direction of association was consistent across sensitivity analyses, although the magnitude varied with cohort and outcome definitions. These observational data do not establish causality or support a specific perioperative medication strategy.

title: Transthoracic echocardiography for initial screening of single coronary artery anomaly: a case with multimodal imaging evaluation
authorString: Liang C, Wang Z, Shi X, Su Q, Xu H.
abstractText: Single coronary artery anomaly (SCA) is a rare congenital coronary malformation with only one aortic coronary ostium supplying the whole myocardium. Clinical outcomes mainly depend on the anatomical course of the aberrant vessel. We report a 73-year-old female presenting with intermittent precordial chest pain. Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) revealed a dilated right coronary artery (RCA) with normal ostial location, non-visualization of the left coronary artery ostium, and diastolic low-resistance arterial flow signal within the interventricular septum along the expected left anterior descending artery (LAD) territory. Coronary computed-tomography angiography (CCTA) demonstrated right-dominant coronary circulation, absence of the native left coronary artery, and an abnormally extended posterior descending artery travelling into the anterior interventricular groove. Multimodal imaging highly suggested Lipton-Yamanaka type R-I SCA. The patient received conservative medical therapy for co-existing mild coronary atherosclerosis. This case underlines TTE as a valuable first-line screening tool for congenital coronary anomalies. Nevertheless, definitive subtyping requires CCTA or invasive coronary angiography.

title: [18F]NaF PET Radiomics and Coronary Calcium Score Progression: Associations Beyond Baseline Calcium Score and TBR
authorString: Li S, Kendrick J, Ebert MA, Hassan GM, Barry N, Lee SC, Francis RJ, Bellinge JW, Schultz C.
abstractText: Background: [ 18 F]NaF positron emission tomography (PET) can quantify coronary calcification activity before coronary calcium score (CCS) progression, which is a surrogate measure of cardiovascular disease risk. It remains uncertain whether advanced PET quantification, including radiomics, improves prediction of CCS progression. Participants with type 2 diabetes underwent baseline [ 18 F]NaF PET/CT, baseline CCS and a follow-up CCS after 2 years. CCS progression was evaluated on a per-patient and a per-artery level. [ 18 F]NaF activity was evaluated using the TBR max , and radiomics features. Logistic regression models were used to determine the features most associated with CCS progression. Results: In total, 91 participants (median age [interquartile range]: 66 [60 – 70], 71.4% male) were examined. In total, 68 patients (74.7%) demonstrated CCS progression. Clinical variables and baseline CCS discriminated CCS progressors and non-progressors modestly (AUC 0.72, 95% CI 0.55–0.86). The TBR max demonstrated good discrimination (AUC 0.83, 95% CI 0.73–0.92), while multi-feature radiomics models achieved the highest discrimination performance (AUC 0.90, 95% CI 0.80–0.97). A total of 211 coronary arteries (58.0%) demonstrated CCS progression. The combined CCS and TBR max model discriminated CCS progressors and non-progressors modestly (AUC of 0.67, 95% CI 0.60–0.73), while the multi-feature radiomics demonstrated good discrimination (AUC 0.77, 95% CI: 0.70–0.84). Conclusions: [ 18 F]NaF PET radiomics improves prediction of CCS progression compared with baseline CCS, clinical features, and the TBR max .

title: Pericardial Effusion Presenting as Isolated Right Upper Quadrant Pain with Deranged Liver Enzymes a Diagnostic Pitfall in the Emergency Department a Case Report
authorString: Jha A, Jassim G, Dvorkin LS, Verasingam P.
abstractText: Background Pericardial effusion typically presents with chest pain, dyspnoea, and positional discomfort. Presentation with isolated abdominal pain in the absence of cardiopulmonary symptoms is rare and closely mimics acute hepatobiliary pathology. Recognition is critical, since unrecognised pericardial effusion may progress to life-threatening cardiac tamponade. Case Presentation A 43-year-old black African woman with virologically suppressed human immunodeficiency virus infection (HIV), ulcerative colitis, and a history of previously treated latent tuberculosis (TB) infection presented to the emergency department with a one-day history of abdominal pain radiating to the flanks and epigastrium. Right upper quadrant tenderness on examination and elevated liver enzymes upon further investigation prompted a provisional diagnosis of cholecystitis. A subsequent chest radiograph showed a globular cardiac silhouette and bedside echocardiography confirmed a large pericardial effusion. Computed tomography (CT) demonstrated an effusion with features of right cardiac impairment, hepatic congestion and pericholecystic fluid, with no evidence of acute cholecystitis. Pericardiocentesis yielded haemoserous fluid, with resolution of symptoms and improvement in liver enzymes. The effusion re-accumulated within 5 days, with right ventricular diastolic collapse and this was surgically managed. The rapid recurrence raised suspicion of a potential inflammatory aetiology; however, the definitive aetiology remains unclear. Conclusions Pericardial effusion should be considered in patients with undifferentiated abdominal pain and liver enzyme derangement, even in the absence of typical cardiac symptoms or Beck’s triad. This case highlights the potential for cardiac pathology to mimic acute hepatobiliary disease and emphasises the importance of maintaining a broad differential diagnosis in atypical abdominal presentations.

title: Characteristics of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest calls unrecognised by machine learning versus medical dispatchers: a nationwide observational study
authorString: Nord A, Wärneryd A, Byrsell F, Claesson A, Jonsson M, Hollenberg J, Robertsson S, Forsberg S.
abstractText: Background Early recognition of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) during emergency medical calls is critical, yet nearly one-quarter of cases are missed by dispatchers. Machine learning (ML) models offer promise but require evaluation regarding their specific failure patterns. The aim of this study was to describe and compare the characteristics of OHCA calls with discordant recognition by medical dispatchers and an ML model. Methods This observational study analysed a predefined sub-cohort of unrecognised emergency 112 calls from a representative nationwide sample of Swedish OHCA cases in 2018. Audio logs were systematically audited using standardised Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival (CARES) criteria. Calls missed by either the ML model or medical dispatchers were analysed using univariate logistic regression to identify characteristics associated with recognition by either ML or by dispatchers. Results Ninety calls met the inclusion criteria. OHCA was recognised by the ML model but missed by medical dispatchers in 58% (52/90) of calls, while medical dispatchers recognised OHCA missed by the ML model in 42% (38/90). ML recognition was positively associated with the caller knowing the patient (OR 1.69, 95% CI 1.08 to 2.70), being a layperson (OR 2.98, 95% CI 1.20 to 7.64), being alone (OR 8.33, 95% CI 2.93 to 35.01), OHCA occurring at home (OR 1.78, 95% CI 1.08 to 3.02), and calls occurring in the evening (OR 4.29, 95% CI 1.09 to 21.82). Conversely, medical dispatchers were more likely to recognise OHCA when CPR was already in progress (OR for ML recognition 0.07, 95% CI 0.004 to 0.33) or when the caller was not alone (OR for ML recognition 0.09, 95% CI 0.02 to 0.28). Conclusions Among discordant OHCA calls, medical dispatchers and ML models showed different recognition patterns. These findings support further evaluation of whether ML-based decision support may complement dispatcher recognition of OHCA.

title: Association between remote dielectric sensing and transpulmonary thermodilution–derived lung water after cardiac surgery: a repeated- measures exploratory study
authorString: Duan W, Ren Y, Hu S, Zheng Y, Chen X, Yu H, Fan J.
abstractText: Background Remote dielectric sensing (ReDS) is a non-invasive technology that estimates pulmonary fluid content and may provide a convenient approach for monitoring thoracic fluid status. However, its relationship with invasive transpulmonary thermodilution-derived measures of pulmonary fluid in patients after cardiac surgery remains uncertain. This exploratory study investigated the association between ReDS measurements and PiCCO-derived extravascular lung water (EVLW) and extravascular lung water indexed to predicted body weight (ELWI). Methods We conducted a single-centre observational study of patients after cardiac surgery who underwent paired ReDS and PiCCO measurements during intensive care unit stay. A total of 88 paired measurements from 29 patients were analysed, with repeated measurements clustered within patients. Linear mixed-effects models with a patient-specific random intercept were used to evaluate associations between ReDS and PiCCO-derived parameters. The primary analysis assessed the association between ReDS and ELWI, while the key secondary analysis evaluated the association between ReDS and absolute EVLW. Patient-level mean values and first-measurement analyses were performed as sensitivity analyses. Exploratory analyses examined whether central venous pressure (CVP) modified the association between ReDS and pulmonary fluid parameters. Results Across 29 patients, 88 paired ReDS–PiCCO measurements were available, with a median of 3 measurements per patient (IQR, 1–4). In the primary mixed-effects analysis, ReDS was not significantly associated with weight-indexed ELWI (β = 0.129 per 1% increase in ReDS; 95% CI, − 0.066 to 0.324; P = 0.195). In contrast, ReDS was positively associated with absolute EVLW (β = 16.41 mL per 1% increase in ReDS; 95% CI, 6.45–26.36; P = 0.001). Patient-level sensitivity analyses showed similar patterns, with no significant association between mean ReDS and mean ELWI (r = 0.073, P = 0.706), whereas mean ReDS was positively correlated with mean EVLW (r = 0.518, P = 0.004). Unadjusted CVP-stratified analyses showed a stronger ReDS–ELWI correlation among measurements with CVP > 12 mmHg; however, the formal interaction analysis did not demonstrate statistically significant effect modification by CVP. Conclusions In this exploratory cohort of patients after cardiac surgery, ReDS was not significantly associated with weight-indexed ELWI but showed a significant positive association with absolute EVLW. These findings suggest that ReDS may reflect aspects of overall thoracic fluid burden without being interchangeable with thermodilution-derived ELWI. Larger longitudinal studies focusing on within-patient changes and incorporating independent reference measures are warranted to determine the clinical utility of ReDS for postoperative pulmonary fluid monitoring.

title: Coronary Coronary CT Angiography phase acquisition strategies in sinus arrhythmia: prospective evaluation of image quality and diagnostic accuracy
authorString: Wang N, Ge L, Liu J, Zhu J, Zhu Y, Cai W, Fang Y, Ma h.
abstractText: Objective This study aimed to evaluate the impacts of absolute-phase and relative-phase acquisition protocols on image quality, interpretability and stenosis diagnostic accuracy in sinus arrhythmia patients undergoing prospectively ECG-triggered axial coronary CTA. Materials and Methods Consecutive patients with sinus arrhythmia between January 2022 and December 2024 were enrolled and randomly assigned into absolute-phase (Group B) and relative-phase (Group C) groups at a 1:1 ratio. With age, gender and baseline HRas covariates, propensity score matching was adopted to select matched patients with regular sinus rhythm as the control group (Group A). Objective and subjective image quality, the proportion of interpretable coronary segments, and diagnostic accuracy (using invasive coronary angiography as the gold standard, stenosis ≥ 50% as the positive cutoff) were compared across three groups. Results No significant differences in objective image parameters were found. Subjective scores in Group A, B and C were 3.84 ± 0.61, 3.76 ± 0.74 and 3.62 ± 0.92 ( all P  < 0.001). The rates of interpretable segments were 96.4%, 94.9% and 90.7%, with segment-based diagnostic accuracy of 93.1%, 95.8% and 88.9%, respectively ( P  < 0.05). Conclusion Increased heart rate variability aggravates coronary motion artifacts at moderate heart rates. Compared with relative-phase strategy, absolute-phase acquisition effectively reduces artifacts, and improves image interpretability and diagnostic performance in arrhythmic patients.

title: Clinical and Biochemical Outcomes of Ketogenic Diet Therapy over a Decade: Experience from a Single Center
authorString: Güneş H, Gülbahçe A, İpekten F, Canpolat M, Per H, Gümüş H, Öztekin D, Kardaş F.
abstractText: Purpose The ketogenic diet, high in fat and low in carbohydrates, is used to treat metabolic diseases and drug-resistant epilepsy. This study evaluates the clinical outcomes, metabolic changes, and treatment adherence among patients receiving the ketogenic diet. Methods We retrospectively analyzed the hospital records of 18 pediatric patients who received ketogenic diet therapy at a single center between 2014 and 2024. Results Patient age ranged from 4 to 240 months, with a median treatment duration of 21 months. Follow-up revealed significant increases in total cholesterol, AST, and free carnitine; LDL and triglycerides rose in six months but decreased by twelve months, while HDL gradually declined. There were no significant changes in glucose, complete blood count, or vitamin levels. Seizure frequency decreased in 88.9% of patients; two discontinued due to lack of efficacy. Two patients developed kidney stones, but no cardiac complications were observed. Conclusion Over the ten years, the ketogenic diet proved to be a safe and sustainable treatment for children, with side effects manageable through careful monitoring.

title: Low-kV ECG-Gated Dual-Phase CT Angiography in Aortic Dissection: Dose Reduction with Improved Aortic Root Image Quality
authorString: Chen Y, Sun J, Hua M, Li B, Zhang H.
abstractText: Background and Objectives: Acute aortic dissection is a life-threatening condition. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) is the first-line modality; however, conventional non-ECG-gated protocols generate cardiac motion artefacts at the aortic root that compromise accuracy while exposing patients to substantial radiation. This retrospective study evaluated a dual-phase 100 kV aortic CTA protocol with prospective ECG-gating for dose reduction and improved image quality versus conventional 120 kV non-ECG-gated CTA. Materials and Methods: We retrospectively screened 80 consecutive patients with suspected aortic dissection undergoing CTA at Tianjin Chest Hospital (January 2024–December 2025) via the institutional Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) and electronic medical records. Patients were grouped by scanning protocol according to a historical control design: conventional 120 kV non-ECG-gated CTA (n = 40, January–June 2024) and dual-phase 100 kV CTA with prospective ECG-gating of the aortic root (n = 40, July 2024–December 2025). Image quality was assessed by subjective scoring and objective signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR). Effective dose, scan time, and diagnostic accuracy were compared between groups. Propensity score matching was applied to balance baseline characteristics. The ethics committee approved this study (no. 2024-LW-036; 15 December 2024) and waived informed consent. Results: The 100 kV protocol reduced effective dose by 48% (10.59 +/- 3.89 versus 20.25 +/- 3.28 mSv, p < 0.05) and scan time by 55% (11.36 +/- 1.41 versus 25.23 +/- 2.36 s, p < 0.05). The aortic root motion artefact rate fell from 90.0% to 7.5% (p < 0.05). SNR (24.35 +/- 2.25 versus 20.25 +/- 3.28) and CNR (44.10 +/- 2.47 versus 34.20 +/- 3.25) were significantly superior (both p < 0.05). Diagnostic accuracy for Stanford Type A dissection was 100% versus 80% (p < 0.05), with entry tear visualisation improving from 60.0% to 95.83%. Conclusions: The dual-phase 100 kV prospective ECG-gated protocol significantly reduces radiation exposure and scan duration whilst virtually eliminating aortic root motion artefacts and improving diagnostic accuracy for Stanford Type A dissection. These findings support adoption of this protocol as the preferred CTA technique for aortic dissection on 256-slice CT platforms.

title: Psychological Distress, Heart-Related Quality of Life, and Follow-up Participation in Outpatient Cardiac Rehabilitation: A Retrospective Longitudinal Cohort Study
authorString: Brokatzky S, Sila R, Jellestad L, Buser M, Germann N, Rickli H, Schmid DA.
abstractText: Background To examine associations of baseline depression and anxiety with HeartQoL levels and change, questionnaire follow-up participation, and documented early programme dropout during outpatient cardiac rehabilitation (CR). Sex differences were evaluated as a secondary question. Methods HeartQoL data from 453 adults entering a nine-week outpatient CR programme at a Swiss centre (1 July 2022-31 December 2024) were analysed using random-intercept linear mixed-effects models with patient-level CR2 inference. Follow-up participation and documented early dropout were examined in a linked cohort of 453 participants using age- and sex-adjusted logistic regression, bootstrap analysis, and multiple imputation. Results Mean age was 62.6 years, 104 (23.0%) were female, and 249 (55.0%) had valid Global HeartQoL follow-up. HeartQoL increased in Global (B = 0.308), Physical (B = 0.344), and Emotional domains (B = 0.208; all p < .001). Higher PHQ-9 scores were associated with lower HeartQoL across domains, while higher GAD-7 scores were associated with lower Global and Emotional HeartQoL. No distress-by-time interaction reached statistical significance; the Emotional HeartQoL Time × GAD-7 estimate was borderline (B = 0.032, 95% CI [-0.001, 0.066], p = .060) and remained so in the expanded sensitivity analysis (p = .053). In the linked cohort, 204/453 (45.0%) had no nine-week HeartQoL item. Higher baseline distress was associated with missing follow-up (OR = 1.44 per SD, 95% CI [1.15, 1.80], p = .001), but not clearly with documented early programme dropout (OR = 1.26, 95% CI [0.98, 1.61], p = .068). Of 76 documented dropouts, 60 lacked follow-up and 16 provided it. Conclusions Baseline psychological distress was associated with poorer HeartQoL and lower questionnaire follow-up participation, but did not clearly predict documented early programme dropout. The borderline anxiety-related estimate for Emotional HeartQoL change was exploratory and requires confirmation. Programme dropout and questionnaire nonresponse should be recorded and analysed as distinct outcomes.

title: A High-Risk Substrate in a Small Heart: Ablation of a Concealed Para-Hisian Accessory Pathway in a 3-Year-Old：A Case Report
authorString: Li Y, xiaokereti J.
abstractText: Background: Catheter ablation of para-Hisian accessory pathways (PHAP) in children is technically demanding and carries a substantial risk of atrioventricular (AV) block. This risk is magnified in very young patients, in whom small cardiac dimensions place the AV node and His bundle in close anatomical proximity to the ablation target. Concealed PHAP cannot be localized by pre-excitation mapping, further increasing procedural difficulty. We report a 3-year-old girl with a concealed para-Hisian accessory pathway, representing two high-risk features: very young age and an ablation target immediately adjacent to the His bundle. Case summary: A 3-year-old girl presented with recurrent paroxysmal tachycardia. Electrophysiological study confirmed orthodromic atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia mediated by a concealed para-Hisian accessory pathway. Activation mapping during tachycardia identified the earliest retrograde atrial activation adjacent to the His bundle at the 12 o’clock position of the tricuspid annulus. Radiofrequency energy was delivered in temperature-controlled mode at 25 W with a maximal target temperature of 45°C; tachycardia terminated within 3 seconds, followed by 60 seconds of consolidation ablation at identical parameters. No accelerated junctional rhythm or AV conduction deterioration was observed during energy delivery. Post-ablation, ventriculoatrial dissociation was documented, and no permanent AV conduction disturbance occurred. The patient remained free of arrhythmia-related symptoms at 2-week and 1-month follow-up. Conclusions: : This case demonstrates that radiofrequency catheter ablation can be performed safely and effectively in selected very young children with concealed septal accessory pathways. Success depends on meticulous activation mapping, stable catheter-tissue contact, and individualized low-power, temperature-titrated energy delivery. Additional multicenter experience is required to validate long-term safety and efficacy in this population.

title: Sealing the Leak: Percutaneous Deep Dorsal Penile Vein Embolization Using Glubran for Veno-Occlusive Erectile Dysfunction - A Case Report
authorString: Raheb-Khelo R, Irani E, Jaber R, Karam K, Khoury JE.
abstractText: Erectile dysfunction (ED) is highly prevalent, and vascular disease is the leading cause of organic ED, including veno-occlusive dysfunction (VOD), in which impaired restriction of venous outflow from the corpora cavernosa prevents the blood retention needed to maintain an erection. We report a 67-year-old man with controlled hypertension and a 35-pack-year smoking history who presented with a 1.5-year history of ED refractory to sildenafil (IIEF-5 score 10; Erection Hardness Score 2). Penile duplex Doppler ultrasonography following intracavernosal papaverine demonstrated preserved arterial inflow (peak systolic velocity 71.4 cm/s) together with a markedly elevated, persistent end-diastolic velocity (23 cm/s) suggestive of VOD, although inadequate penile rigidity limited definitive assessment. Pelvic arteriography excluded a significant arterial abnormality, and cavernosography confirmed VOD, showing rapid and persistent opacification of the retropubic venous plexus and pelvic veins with failure to sustain an erection despite high-flow injection. Using ultrasound-guided anterograde access through the deep dorsal penile vein, the retropubic venous plexus was embolized with a cyanoacrylate (Glubran) and lipiodol mixture, with a tourniquet applied at the penile base to prevent reflux, and final control angiography showed a satisfactory result. This case demonstrates that endovascular pelvic venous plexus embolization is a feasible, minimally invasive treatment for medically refractory ED due to VOD and underscores the importance of a structured diagnostic pathway combining duplex ultrasonography, arteriography, and cavernosography. To our knowledge, this is the first such procedure reported in Lebanon and the Arab region. Further experience with standardized outcome reporting and longer follow-up is needed to define its durability and role.

title: Machine Learning and Large Language Models for Maternal Cardiometabolic Risk Prediction Across Harmonised Public Pregnancy Datasets
authorString: Wen S, Tang Y, Ma B, Cao B, Deng Z.
abstractText: Background Pregnancy-related cardiometabolic complications remain important contributors to adverse maternal and fetal outcomes. However, risk-prediction models developed from a single dataset often have limited transportability, and the role of large language models in maternal risk stratification remains unclear. Methods We used two publicly available datasets: the Maternal Health Risk dataset and the Preeclampsia in Pregnant Women dataset. Low-risk, mid-risk, and high-risk labels were harmonised, and a binary high-risk versus non-high-risk endpoint was constructed. We compared several machine-learning models and undertook internal cross-validation, external validation, calibration, decision-curve analysis, and sensitivity analyses. Structured records were subsequently converted into label-free case narratives; DeepSeek and Qwen were evaluated under different prompting strategies, and the concordance between keywords in large language model explanations and machine-learning feature importance was examined. Results In internal validation, HistGradientBoosting showed the strongest overall performance, with a macro-averaged F1 score of approximately 0.876. Performance declined in external validation, in which multiclass accuracy was approximately 0.389. Across sensitivity analyses, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve ranged from 0.437 to 0.528. Among the large language model configurations, Qwen with few-shot chain-of-thought prompting performed best, with an accuracy of approximately 0.583 and a macro-averaged F1 score of approximately 0.467. Explanatory keywords generated by the large language models most often concerned blood glucose or diabetes, blood pressure or hypertension, haemoglobin or anaemia, previous complications or medical history, and proteinuria. Conclusion We developed an integrated framework for maternal cardiometabolic risk prediction that combines feature harmonisation, conventional machine learning, external validation, and large language model explanations. Machine-learning models performed well internally but generalised poorly across datasets. Large language models showed some ability to assess risk from case text and generate readable clinical explanations, but require validation in larger, multicentre, prospective studies.

title: Prevalence of High-Risk Human Papillomavirus Infection in Pregnant Women and Its Association with Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes: A Cross-Sectional Study
authorString: Pokchainun T, Phoolcharoen N, Pohthipornthawat N, Panyavaranant P.
abstractText: Background High-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is common among women of reproductive age, but data on HPV infection during pregnancy in South-East Asia remain limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of high-risk HPV infection and abnormal cervical cytology among pregnant women in Thailand, identify factors associated with high-risk HPV infection, and explore its association with adverse pregnancy outcomes. Methods This cross-sectional study included pregnant women aged ≥ 18 years attending antenatal care at a tertiary referral hospital in Bangkok, Thailand, between June 2024 and May 2025. Cervical samples were tested for 14 high-risk HPV genotypes using real-time polymerase chain reaction and assessed by liquid-based cytology. Demographic, reproductive, and epidemiological characteristics were collected using questionnaires and electronic medical records. Pregnancy outcomes were recorded after delivery. Logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with high-risk HPV infection. Results Among 255 participants, 40 tested positive for high-risk HPV, giving a prevalence of 15.7% (95% CI 11.5–20.7). Other high-risk HPV genotypes were most common (12.2%), followed by HPV 16 (3.9%) and HPV 18 (1.6%). Abnormal cervical cytology was detected in 2.0% of participants (four ASC-US and one HSIL). Younger age and having three or more lifetime sexual partners were independently associated with high-risk HPV infection. Pregnancy outcome data were available for 216 participants. No statistically significant associations were observed between high-risk HPV infection and abortion, preterm delivery, preterm premature rupture of membranes, fetal growth restriction, low birth weight, gestational hypertension, or pre-eclampsia. Conclusions High-risk HPV infection was identified in 15.7% of pregnant women, while abnormal cervical cytology was uncommon and most high-risk HPV infections occurred in women with normal cytology. Antenatal care may provide an opportunity to improve cervical cancer screening coverage. No significant association between high-risk HPV infection and adverse pregnancy outcomes was observed, although the study was not powered primarily to assess these outcomes.

title: Shared Transcriptomic Signatures of the Hypothyroid State and Hypertension Identified by Integrative Network Analysis
authorString: Andrade LJdO, de Oliveira GCM, Salles OJdM, Dinamarco N, Bittencourt AMV, de Oliveira LM.
abstractText: Introduction: Thyroid dysfunction contributes to arterial hypertension, but the evidence is inconsistent and their transcriptomic overlap remains unmapped. Objective: To identify transcriptomic signatures shared by the hypothyroid state and arterial hypertension in peripheral blood and to define candidate molecular hubs. Methods: This in silico analysis used public Gene Expression Omnibus data: GSE103305 (whole blood; eight athyroid patients, hypothyroid versus levothyroxine-replete) and GSE75360 (mononuclear cells; 10 hypertensive, 11 normotensive), with GSE24752 and GSE74144 for sensitivity analyses. Differentially expressed genes (FDR < 0.05; |log2 fold change| ≥ 0.585) were identified with DESeq2 and limma and intersected. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis, STRING networks (score ≥ 0.700), cytoHubba ranking, enrichment, and receiver operating characteristic analysis followed. Results: The thyroid and hypertension signatures comprised 486 and 173 genes and shared 19 (P = 0.0032); 14 (74%) were concordant in direction. Eleven shared genes were also candidate co-expression hubs, forming a nine-node STRING network in which STAT3, IL6R, and VEGFA ranked highest. The shared signature was enriched for JAK-STAT signaling (FDR = 0.008). STAT3 and IL6R, but not VEGFA, were dysregulated in additional hypertension datasets (P < 0.05). A three-gene panel yielded an area under the curve of 0.74 (95% CI, 0.61-0.86) in the discovery cohort and 0.69 (95% CI, 0.55-0.82) in GSE74144. Conclusion: The hypothyroid state and hypertension share a modest inflammatory and angiogenic transcriptomic signature in peripheral blood involving STAT3, IL6R, and VEGFA. These hubs are hypothesis-generating and need validation in larger cohorts.

title: Follicular Dendritic Cell Sarcoma Arising in the Aortopulmonary Window: A Case Report of Complete Resection Using Proximal Pulmonary Artery Control
authorString: Yokota N, Horikiri A, Niwa Y, Taki T, Takase Y, Kanai Y, Atsushi K, Niki T, Tsubochi H.
abstractText:
Background: Follicular dendritic cell sarcoma is a rare malignant neoplasm, and its occurrence in the aortopulmonary window is exceptionally uncommon. Tumors in this location are technically challenging because of the limited operative space and their close relationship to the aortic arch, left pulmonary artery, left main bronchus, and left recurrent laryngeal nerve. We report a case of follicular dendritic cell sarcoma arising in the aortopulmonary window that was completely resected using a strategy for proximal pulmonary artery control. Case presentation: A 46-year-old man was referred to our institution after an abnormal mediastinal shadow was incidentally detected on chest radiography. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography showed a 48 × 29 mm well-circumscribed mass in the aortopulmonary window, broadly contacting the aorta, left pulmonary artery, and left main bronchus. Positron emission tomography showed moderate fluorodeoxyglucose uptake without distant metastasis. Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration suggested a neuroendocrine tumor but did not establish a definitive diagnosis. Surgical resection was performed through median sternotomy combined with a left anterior second intercostal thoracotomy. Because direct exposure and encirclement of the tumor-adjacent left pulmonary artery were considered hazardous, proximal vascular control was established through the transverse pericardial sinus before tumor manipulation. Division of the ligamentum arteriosum increased pulmonary artery mobility and improved exposure of the operative field. The tumor was completely separated from the left pulmonary artery, aorta, left main bronchus, and recurrent laryngeal nerve without combined organ resection. Histopathological examination showed spindle-shaped tumor cells arranged in whorled and rosette-like patterns. Immunohistochemical staining was positive for CD21, CD23, D2-40, and somatostatin receptor 2, confirming follicular dendritic cell sarcoma. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient remained free of recurrence 3 years after surgery.

Conclusions:

Complete resection of a tumor arising in the aortopulmonary window can be facilitated by secure proximal pulmonary artery control and mobilization of surrounding structures. These technical principles may also be useful for other tumors in this anatomically complex region when direct manipulation of the tumor-adjacent pulmonary artery is considered hazardous.

title: A Four-Quadrant Phenotyping Model Based on Partitioned Exercise Pressure–Flow Slopes in Adolescent
authorString: Higashi K, Ishii T, Nakajima H, Aotsuka H.
abstractText: Background In Fontan circulation, an elevated exercise mean pulmonary arterial pressure–to–flow slope (ΔmPAP/ΔQp slope > 3.0 mmHg/L per min) indicates impaired pulmonary vascular reserve. However, because mPAP represents the sum of transpulmonary gradient (TPG) and pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP), an elevated slope can stem from pre-capillary, post-capillary, or combined components. This exploratory study aimed to dissect ΔmPAP/ΔQp slope into pre-capillary (ΔTPG/ΔQp) and post-capillary (ΔPAWP/ΔQs) slope components using a four-quadrant model to characterize Fontan phenotypes and their association with exercise capacity. Methods Invasive exercise stress catheterization was performed in 14 stable adolescent Fontan patients (median age 14.0 years). Patients were categorized into four dynamic quadrants using pre-capillary (ΔTPG/ΔQp > 1.2 mmHg/L per min) and post-capillary (ΔPAWP/ΔQs > 2.0 mmHg/L per min) thresholds. Results The quadrant model dissected ΔmPAP/ΔQp slope into post-capillary (50%, n = 7), pre-capillary (14%, n = 2), combined (14%, n = 2), and non-limited (21%, n = 3) phenotypes. Peak %predicted VO 2 varied across phenotypes: patients with post-capillary or combined phenotypes showed reduced exercise capacity (peak %predicted VO 2 : 63%–84%), whereas those with pre-capillary or non-limited phenotypes maintained preserved capacity (90%–136%). Conventional resting hemodynamics showed no correlation with exercise capacity. Conclusions Dissecting the overall ΔmPAP/ΔQp slope into pre- and post-capillary components refines the pathophysiological evaluation of Fontan exercise hemodynamics. Dynamic post-capillary restriction was frequently observed in adolescent Fontan patients with reduced exercise capacity. Furthermore, identifying specific pre- or post-capillary dynamic restrictions may help guide phenotype-targeted therapeutic strategies.

title: Shotgun metagenomic and untargeted metabolomic analysis of gut microbiome associated with peripheral artery disease
authorString: Niraula S, Jang JW, Jung J, Stirewalt SL, Alagna M, Du J, Staley C, Seed P, Green SJ, Ho KJ.
abstractText:
Background

While the human gut microbiome is a potentially important and modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular diseases, the links between the gut microbiome and peripheral artery disease (PAD) and its clinical subgroups (claudication and chronic limb-threatening ischemia; CLTI) are not well understood.

Methods

We used shotgun metagenomics and untargeted metabolomics to analyze the fecal samples of people with PAD and age- and sex-matched non-PAD controls collected in a cross-sectional manner. We used functional prediction pathways, a network analysis, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis of metagenomic, metabolomics, and clinical data to better understand PAD-associated dysbiosis.

Results

Alpha and beta diversity were similar between the PAD (n=78) and non-PAD (n=20) groups. Differentially abundant species were dominated by those belonging to the Lachnospiraceae, Ruminococcaceae and Enterobacteriaceae families. Fecal butyrate levels were reduced between the non-PAD and PAD groups, but differences were not statistically significant. There was significantly reduced alpha diversity in the samples of the CLTI compared to claudication subgroup. Abundance of multiple butyrate producers were greater in the claudication group compared to CLTI. Network analysis revealed 5 meta-modules, each with specific associations to PAD presentation and metabolomic profiles, and species that are both top module hubs and differentially abundant between groups. Community interconnectedness appears to increase in claudication, followed by community disintegration in CLTI.

Conclusions

This metagenomic-metabolomic analysis of the gut microbiome of individuals with PAD, highlights the importance of studying functional capacity, diversity, and connectivity between species. Microbial modules may allow an integrative view of the microbial ecology relevant to presence and progression of PAD.

title: Reduced physiological reserve and a blunted response to acute exercise in adults with cerebral palsy
authorString: Corell L, Horwath O, Edman S, Reitzner SM, Hangasjärvi W, Meza G, Castaings J, Kruse A, Starck J, Valtonen N, Hjalmarsson E, Kvist O, Cardinale DA, Pontén E, Sörensson P, Fernandez-Gonzalo R, Dayanidhi S, Peterson MD, Norrbom J, von Walden F.
abstractText: Cerebral palsy (CP) is an early-onset neurodevelopmental condition associated with metabolic impairment and an increased risk of non-communicable diseases across the lifespan. However, the basis of these changes remains largely unknown. This study provides a comprehensive cardiometabolic and physical function profile of 23 adults with CP relative to 33 typically developing (TD) adolescents and 61 TD adults. Compared to TD individuals, adults with CP exhibited reduced cardiorespiratory fitness, smaller cardiac dimensions, and lower muscle mass. Circulating metabolomic and proteomic profiling identified a distinct molecular signature in CP, including altered tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle metabolites, and elevated myostatin, matrix-related proteins and pro-inflammatory cytokines. We further tested the capacity for physiological and molecular adaptation using an acute bout of endurance exercise. In response to exercise, individuals with CP exhibited an attenuated response compared to TD groups, characterized by a blunted lactate response and lower venous oxygen levels. TD participants also increased canonical exercise-responsive factors, including NADK, IL-8, ANGPTL1 and GDF15, whereas these responses were attenuated in CP. These novel findings define a distinct cardiometabolic profile in adults with CP at rest and reveal an attenuated molecular response to exercise. These data carry implications for targeted interventions and prevention strategies across the lifespan.

title: Human iPSC-Derived Cardiomyocytes Maladaptively Remodel to Cyclic Stretch in Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome
authorString: Verma RS, Zhang I, Chen X, Pierce MS, Subramanyan RK, McCain ML.
abstractText:
Background

Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome (HLHS) is a severe congenital heart defect characterized by underdevelopment of left-sided cardiac structures, requiring staged surgical palliation that establishes the right ventricle as the single ventricle maintaining systemic circulation. After surgery, patients remain highly susceptible to heart failure, possibly due to the increased hemodynamic load imposed on the single surviving ventricle. Because the etiology of HLHS remains poorly understood, elucidating the mechanisms that drive ventricular dysfunction requires model systems that capture both patient-specific genetics and the dynamic mechanical environment of the ventricle. Thus, our objective was to compare how induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs) from patients with HLHS differ from control in static culture and in response to cyclic stretch.

Methods

Control iPSCs from two unaffected donors and iPSCs from four HLHS patients were differentiated into iPSC-CMs, engineered into aligned tissues, and cultured statically or exposed to cyclic 20% uniaxial stretch at 1 Hz for 48h. Sarcomere organization was quantified in static tissues using images of immunostained α-actinin. Calcium transients at 1 Hz pacing frequency in static and stretched tissues were evaluated using Fluo-4 calcium indicator dye. Bulk RNA sequencing was performed to evaluate stretch-induced transcriptomic changes in control and HLHS iPSC-CMs.

Results

In static culture, HLHS iPSC-CMs had modest defects in sarcomere organization and calcium transient morphology compared to control. In response to cyclic stretch, control iPSC-CMs exhibited calcium transients with quicker rise time, a response observed in only one of four lines of HLHS iPSC-CMs. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that all four lines of HLHS iPSC-CMs failed to upregulate calcium handling and sarcomere-associated genes in response to stretch, unlike control iPSC-CMs. Stretch also induced HLHS iPSC-CMs to exhibit pronounced activation of inflammatory signaling pathways, a response not observed in control iPSC-CMs.

Conclusions

iPSC-CMs from HLHS patients demonstrate aberrant responses to cyclic stretch, including blunted adaptation of calcium transients and heightened inflammatory signaling. These findings implicate defective mechanoadaptation as a potential contributor to single ventricle failure and identify potential candidate biomarkers and new opportunities for therapeutic interventions for HLHS patients.

title: Upadacitinib for refractory prurigo nodularis: a two-centre real-world cohort using step-up dosing
authorString: Yıldırım G, Yıldız B, Engin B.
abstractText: Upadacitinib, an oral selective Janus kinase 1 inhibitor, has growing off-label evidence in prurigo nodularis (PN), but real-world data are limited. We evaluated its effectiveness and safety in adults with refractory, biologic-naïve PN without atopic dermatitis and describe a response-guided step-up dosing strategy. We retrospectively reviewed 20 adults with moderate-to-severe PN (≥ 20 nodules) treated at two dermatology centres in Istanbul between January 2024 and December 2025. All patients started upadacitinib 15 mg daily, escalating to 30 mg if the Worst Itch Numeric Rating Scale (WI-NRS) score had not decreased by ≥ 4 points after ≥ 12 weeks. WI-NRS and Peak Pruritus Numerical Rating Scale (PP-NRS) scores were compared between baseline and the last visit. Seventeen patients (85%) were women; mean age was 54.1 years. Eleven (55%) remained on 15 mg and nine (45%) required 30 mg. After a median of 6.6 months (range, 6–18), mean WI-NRS decreased from 9.25 to 0.65 (p < 0.001); all patients achieved a ≥ 4-point reduction and 14 (70%) were itch-free. Mean PP-NRS decreased from 9.05 to 0.95 (p < 0.001). Four patients (20%) had non-serious adverse events; none discontinued treatment. In exploratory analyses, patients requiring escalation were older, all had diabetes or cardiovascular disease, and more often had > 100 nodules, whereas baseline itch was similar. Upadacitinib was associated with marked itch improvement in refractory PN, and step-up dosing allowed 55% of patients to remain on 15 mg. It may be a useful oral option when approved biologics are inaccessible; controlled studies with longer follow-up are needed.

title: Preoperative Predictors and Scoring System for Incisional Hernia: A Case–Control Study
authorString: Kanoksin S, Muangnoijaroen K, Techapongsatorn S.
abstractText: Objective Incisional hernia (IH) is a common complication of abdominal surgery; preoperative identification of high-risk patients enables targeted prevention. We aimed to identify independent preoperative predictors of IH and to derive a simple risk-stratification score in a Thai population. Methods We conducted a retrospective, matched 1:1 case–control study at Vajira Hospital, comparing 100 patients who developed an IH after abdominal surgery with 100 patients who did not, individually matched on type of operation. Preoperative variables ascertained before the index operation were analysed by conditional logistic regression. Discrimination was assessed by the area under the ROC curve (AUC) and calibration by the Hosmer–Lemeshow test; internal validity was examined by 1000-iteration bootstrap resampling. Results Six independent preoperative predictors were identified: hypertension (odds ratio [OR] 4.36, 95% CI 1.53–12.46), diabetes (OR 4.20, 1.11–15.89), female sex (OR 3.66, 1.20–11.15), previous abdominal operation (OR 3.25, 1.37–7.72), body mass index (OR 1.24 per kg/m  2 , 1.10–1.41), and age (OR 1.05 per year, 1.01–1.09). The model showed good discrimination (apparent AUC 0.82; optimism-corrected AUC 0.80) and good calibration (Hosmer–Lemeshow p = 0.72). A 6-factor points score stratified patients into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups. Conclusion Six routinely available preoperative factors independently predict IH and can be combined into a practical risk-stratification score to support individualized counselling and preventive strategies. Because of the case–control design, the score stratifies relative risk and is not intended to estimate absolute probability; external, prospective validation is warranted.

title: Post-treatment risks of transcatheter aortic valve implantation: should we be increasing preventative measures?
authorString: Theofilis P, Vlachakis PK, Koutsopoulos G, Kachrimanidis I, Iliakis P, Ktenopoulos N, Patsalis PC, Toutouzas K, Tsioufis K.
abstractText:
Introduction

Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become an established treatment for severe aortic stenosis across an expanding risk spectrum. As indications extend to younger and lower-risk patients, post-treatment complications with implications for survival, quality of life, and valve durability require attention.

Areas covered

This narrative review discusses major post-TAVI complications with direct implications for procedural planning and lifetime management, including cerebrovascular events, conduction abnormalities, coronary obstruction and aortic root injury, bioprosthetic valve dysfunction, valve thrombosis, residual regurgitation, and TAVI-associated infective endocarditis. Evidence was reviewed from pivotal randomized trials, contemporary registries, consensus documents, systematic reviews, and mechanistic studies addressing incidence, pathophysiology, predictors, prognosis, prevention, diagnosis, and management of these complications.

Expert opinion

Post-TAVI risk reduction should move beyond reactive complication management toward individualized prevention. Meticulous computed tomography-based planning, optimized valve selection and implantation technique, rational antithrombotic therapy, structured rhythm and valve surveillance, selective use of cerebral embolic protection, timely correction of clinically or hemodynamically significant residual regurgitation, and infection-prevention pathways are central components of contemporary care. Future progress will depend on better risk stratification, longer-term durability data, and targeted preventive strategies adapted to lower-risk patients with longer life expectancy.

title: Management of Abnormal Uterine Bleeding in a Patient “Bridged” with LVAD
authorString: Simonenko M, Komlichenko E, Kohreidze N, Lanskaya E, Ismail M, Pervunina T, Fedotov P.
abstractText:
Background:

Mechanical circulatory support significantly improved survival in end-stage heart failure patients. However, this treatment associated with a wide range of complications, including infections, stroke and bleeding. Abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB) is often underreported gynecological disorder in female patients following left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation. Case Presentation: A 15-year-old female patient with dilated cardiomyopathy and chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction underwent implantation of “Heart Mate 3” as a “bridge” to transplant. After LVAD implantation she had recurrent nosebleeds and AUB complicated with moderate anemia. She frequently admitted to the hospital and then managed with antifibrinolytic medication (Tranexamic acid: 500 mg was administered once a day for 3 days) and blood transfusions. By heart team it was decided to reduce antithrombotic therapy: antiplatelets were discontinued and her INR level was maintained 1.4-1.8. For 2 years prior to HTx LVAD function kept fine on minimized antithrombotic therapy without thromboembolic complications. It was made a multidisciplinary team decision to avoid combined oral contraceptives due to the high risk of thromboembolic complications outweighing the benefits. Twice she underwent urgent laparoscopic surgeries but after all her fertile function remained preserved.

Conclusions:

LVAD patients should be managed with a multidisciplinary heart team. In case of recurrent bleeding and low-risk of thromboembolic complications reduction of antithrombotic therapy should be considered. A personalized approach is essential to determine whether conservative or surgical management is superior, as it balances evidence-based medicine with individual patient needs, reducing the risks of futile or overly aggressive care. Taking into account the reproductive function, an organ-preserving operation was performed for the subsequent preservation of fertile function. Surgical interventions for gynecological disorders can be safely performed in patients “bridged” with LVAD.

title: Combined statin probiotic treatment mitigates atherogenic dyslipidemia fueling NAFLD in high-cholesterol-diet fed rats
authorString: Rajkumar A, Elangovan P, Panchalingam G, Perumal D, Rangaswamy VS, PERIANDAVAN K.
abstractText:
Background:

Chronic hypercholesterolemia accelerates metabolic dysregulation, systemic oxidative stress, and endothelial dysfunction, driving the initiation and progression of atherogenesis. Although statins like Atorvastatin (AS) represent the clinical cornerstone of lipid lowering therapy, long term high dose use is often constrained by adverse side effects. Probiotic interventions targeting the gut heart axis, such as Bifidobacterium longum (B), offer a promising therapeutic strategy to enhance lipid homeostasis and reduce vascular inflammation.

Methods:

Male rats were fed a High Cholesterol Diet (HCD) for 120 days to establish hypercholesterolemia, dyslipidemia, and systemic vascular pathology. Experimental groups were administered AS monotherapy, B. longum monotherapy, or their dual combination (AS + B) daily from day 90 to 120. Redox dynamics (GSH, MDA, GSH/MDA ratio), functional HDL associated proteins (PON1, APOA1), circulating oxidized LDL (oxLDL), inflammatory cytokines (CRP, TNF alpha;, IL 6, IL 8), and all adhesion molecules (ICAM 1, VCAM 1) were quantified, alongside histopathological evaluation of hepatic and aortic tissue microarchitecture.

Results:

High cholesterol diet feeding induced severe dyslipidemia, vascular remodeling, lipid peroxidation, and endothelial inflammation in rats. Monotherapy with Atorvastatin (AS) or Bifidobacterium longum (B) significantly reversed metabolic impairment (p<0.001), while dual AS + B therapy achieved maximum efficacy (p<0.01 vs. AS alone) in restoring hepatic and aortic microarchitecture. Mechanistically, combination treatment blunted oxidative stress by minimizing malondialdehyde and upregulating Paraoxonase 1 and Apolipoprotein A1 (p<0.01), which markedly suppressed low density lipoprotein oxidation (p<0.001). Furthermore, dual therapy yielded the maximum downregulation of pro inflammatory cytokines (C reactive protein, tumor necrosis factor alpha;, interleukin 6, interleukin 8) and adhesion molecules (ICAM1,VCAM1); p<0.001), demonstrating potent anti inflammatory effect against diet induced atherogenesis.

Conclusion:

Co administration of Atorvastatin and Bifidobacterium longum demonstrates multi targeted therapeutic synergy by effectively restoring HDL functional capacity, attenuating vascular endothelial inflammation, and mitigating hypercholesterolemia simultaneously, this dual pharmacological probiotic strategy provides a robust, novel intervention against diet induced atherogenesis.

Keywords:

Hypercholesterolemia, Atorvastatin, Bifidobacterium longum, Lipid Peroxidation, Endothelial Dysfunction, Vascular Inflammation

title: Network-enabled drug repurposing identifies lithium to promote cardiomyocyte proliferation
authorString: Wintruba KL, Verma S, Kathiriya IS, Kostina A, Aguirre A, Kuyumcu-Martinez M, Saucerman JJ.
abstractText: The adult mammalian heart has minimal regenerative capacity, limited in part by endogenous cardiomyocyte (CM) renewal. Although CM proliferation is a promising target in both congenital and adult heart disease, no current therapies specifically target this process. Progress has been hindered by the complexity of CM proliferation signaling networks, which may require systems-level approaches. The overall goal of this study was to leverage systems modeling to identify FDA approved drugs that have the potential to be repurposed towards CM proliferation. To achieve this goal, we developed a computational drug repurposing framework that integrates drug-target interaction data with a previously developed logic-based network model of CM proliferation signaling. Using this framework, we identified 81 drugs that directly target nodes within the CM proliferation network, corresponding to 32 unique drug-target interactions. Virtual screening predicted 5 unique drug-target interactions that increase CM proliferation and 14 that decrease CM proliferation outputs. Lithium, a GSK3β inhibitor widely prescribed for bipolar disorder, was predicted and experimentally validated to promote CM proliferation through a Cyclin D/CDK4 pathway.  In vivo , treatment of pregnant mice with lithium increased DNA synthesis in the CMs of their embryos. A retrospective analysis of the FDA Adverse Events Reporting System confirmed that relative to other mood stabilizers,  in utero exposure to lithium was associated with an increased incidence of congenital heart defects, in males but not females. Together, this work provides a computational-experimental framework for repurposing FDA-approved drugs to modulate CM proliferation, which highlights therapeutic potential of lithium for adult CM regeneration but congenital risks to developing embryos.

title: The Evolving Landscape of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Treatment: Are Guidelines Keeping Pace?
authorString: Shusterman V, Salamatbad G, Weintraub S, Wharton R.
abstractText:
Background

Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a common inherited cardiovascular disorder associated with morbidity. Rapid advances in therapeutics-particularly the emergence of cardiac myosin inhibitors (CMIs)-suggest that current management guidelines are lagging best practices.

Areas of uncertainty

Cardiac myosin inhibitors have revolutionized the management of patients with obstructive HCM. Patients with nonobstructive HCM have had limited therapeutic options historically; however, the recently published ACACIA-HCM trial demonstrated significant benefit in these patients and may represent a new treatment option in these patients, although more long-term data and research are needed in this population.

Data sources

A literature review was performed using PubMed/MEDLINE, Google Scholar, society guidelines, and recently published clinical trials evaluating HCM, cardiac myosin inhibitors, beta blockers, calcium channel blockers, septal reduction therapy, and emerging therapies for obstructive and nonobstructive HCM.

Therapeutic advances

Historically, HCM management has centered on negative inotropic/chronotropic agents to alleviate left ventricular outflow tract obstruction by decreasing the force of contraction and increasing diastolic filling time. The introduction of CMIs represents a paradigm shift by directly targeting the underlying hypercontractility, representing the first therapy specifically designed to treat obstructive HCM, obviating the need for earlier agents, which had limited data and at best modest therapeutic benefit. There may finally be an available treatment for diastolic heart failure in patients with nonobstructive HCM with myosin inhibition, as results from a recent trial ACACIA-HCM were favorable. Furthermore, ongoing investigations are exploring novel approaches such as metabolic modulators.

Conclusions

The management of HCM is undergoing substantial transformation, yet guideline recommendations continue to prioritize beta blockers as first-line therapy despite mounting evidence supporting CMIs. Although treatment strategies for obstructive HCM have evolved significantly, optimal approaches for nonobstructive disease remain unclear. Addressing this gap represents a critical priority for future research.

title: Von Willebrand Factor Biomarkers in Prosthetic Valve Dysfunction: An Adjunct to Imaging and Hemodynamic Assessment.
authorString: Arshad S, Khan S, Zahid M.
abstractText: Imaging remains the foundation of prosthetic valve surveillance because it identifies valve morphology, lesion mechanism, and hemodynamic severity. However, acoustic shadowing, eccentric or multiple regurgitant jets, loading conditions, and reader variability can complicate assessment, particularly for paravalvular regurgitation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. High shear stress unfolds von Willebrand factor (VWF), promotes proteolysis of its high-molecular-weight multimers, and produces a measurable defect in primary hemostasis. Multimer analysis, closure time with adenosine diphosphate (CT-ADP), and the VWF activity-to-antigen ratio therefore provide a biologic signal of abnormal flow rather than an anatomic image. Prospective studies show that VWF abnormalities track residual paravalvular regurgitation during transcatheter aortic valve replacement, occur with dysfunctional prostheses, change after mitral paravalvular-leak repair, and are associated with bleeding. The evidence nevertheless remains observational; most diagnostic cohorts are small and single-center, thresholds lack independent validation, assays are vulnerable to hematologic and preanalytic confounding, and no completed randomized trial has shown that VWF-guided management improves outcomes. VWF testing is best viewed as an investigational adjunct when imaging and the clinical picture are discordant or when prosthetic dysfunction coexists with otherwise unexplained bleeding. It should not replace guideline-directed echocardiography or be used for routine surveillance outside research protocols.

title: Impaired Flow and Physiology in Coronaries With Anomalous Origin From the Opposite Sinus of Valsalva.
authorString: Lo Rito M, Squillace M, Agnifili ML, Rosato A, Anglese S, Chiavetta A, Muritti C, Deamici M, Negri J, Attanasio A, Guida G, Disabato G, Secchi F, Conti M, Frigiola A, Chessa M, Giamberti A, Bedogni F.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText:
Background

Anomalous Aortic Origin of a Coronary Artery (AAOCA) high-risk anatomical features (intramural segment, acute take-off angle, slit-like ostium) cause coronary stenosis leading to myocardial infarction. How these features alter coronary physiology remains unclear.

Aims

We aimed to evaluate their impact on coronary blood supply using continuous thermodilution.

Methods

We prospectively enrolled 51 AAOCA patients undergoing continuous thermodilution. Subjects were classified into an ischemic risk (IR) group (intramural segment, acute angle, oval or slit ostium) or non-ischemic risk (no-IR) group. Non-anomalous coronary arteries served as controls. We measured absolute coronary blood flow (CBF) and microvascular resistance.

Results

Subjects (median age 48.4 years) presented mostly with angina, syncope, and arrhythmia. Final analysis included 48 AAOCA cases (31 IR, 17 no-IR) and 45 controls. The IR group had a median IM length of 9 mm, take-off angle of 31.9°, and a slit-like or oval ostium. The no-IR group had a median angle of 51.5° and an oval or round ostium. At rest, absolute CBF and microvascular resistance showed no significant differences among groups. However, during hyperemia, the IR group had significantly reduced CBF compared to controls (179 vs. 290 mL/min, p = 0.015). The IR group demonstrated higher microvascular resistance at rest (1473 vs. 1150, p = 0.024) and during hyperemia (433 vs. 305, p = 0.012), indicating persistently increased coronary vascular tone.

Conclusions

High-risk anatomical features of AAOCA are associated with altered coronary physiology. An intramural segment, acute take-off angle, and slit-like or oval ostium are linked to reduced hyperemic coronary blood flow due to increased microvascular resistance.

title: Differential Effects of Direct Plasmin Inhibition and Tranexamic Acid on Atherosclerosis Progression and Vascular Remodeling in Apoe/Ldlr Double-Knockout Mice.
authorString: Yoshihama N, Kurisu N, Shimatani K, Hyodo K, Ohta N, Ishii H, Yamashita T.
abstractText:
Aim

The fibrinolytic system may protect against or promote atherosclerosis; however, the effects of distinct antifibrinolytic interventions on plaque development and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling remain unclear.

Methods

We compared YO-2, a direct plasmin inhibitor, and tranexamic acid (TXA), a lysine analog that interferes with plasminogen/plasmin binding to fibrin, in Apoe/Ldlr double-knockout mice fed a Western diet. The atherosclerotic burden, plaque structure, vascular marker expression, leukocyte-endothelial interactions, and nitric oxide (NO)-related indices were assessed.

Results

YO-2 significantly increased the atherosclerotic lesion area compared to the control, whereas TXA had minimal effects. The thrombolytic activity in the He-Ne laser-induced thrombosis model and NO-related indices did not differ significantly among the groups. Vascular t-PA expression increased in both treatment groups. YO-2 was associated with reduced uPAR and MMP-9 expression and preservation of the internal elastic lamina and medial elastin fibers, suggesting reduced pericellular ECM degradation. TXA increased PAI-1 and TAFI expression without altering uPAR. Both treatments significantly reduced leukocyte rolling, and the E-selectin expression was significantly decreased with YO-2, with a similar trend with TXA. eNOS mRNA expression was significantly higher in both groups, although the corresponding increase in the eNOS protein expression was only a non-significant trend.

Conclusions

Direct plasmin inhibition with YO-2 aggravated atherosclerosis and it was associated with a reduced uPAR/MMP-9 expression and altered vascular ECM remodeling. TXA had limited effects on lesion burden while increasing PAI-1 and TAFI expression. These findings suggest that direct plasmin inhibition and TXA-mediated antifibrinolysis may differentially affect atherosclerosis and vascular remodeling.

title: Accelerated Systemic Atherosclerosis Following Immune-Related Adverse Events in a Patient with Primary Thoracic Melanoma: A Case of Sequential Coronary and Peripheral Revascularization.
authorString: Nishikawa T, Higaki A, Mori S, Miyoshi T, Yamamoto S, Yamaguchi O.
abstractText: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) improve survival in advanced melanoma, but they may accelerate atherosclerosis, particularly in patients with immune-related adverse events (irAEs). A 64-year-old man with stage IV BRAF-wild-type primary thoracic melanoma achieved complete remission after nivolumab plus ipilimumab, but he later developed grade 3 immune-related hepatitis, requiring treatment discontinuation. Three and a half years later, symptomatic peripheral artery disease required revascularization, followed by severe coronary artery disease requiring percutaneous coronary intervention one year later. This case suggests that severe irAEs may be associated with accelerated systemic atherosclerosis, highlighting the importance of long-term cardiovascular surveillance following ICI therapy.

title: Fatty liver and adipokines: converging pathways linking insulin resistance to early atherosclerosis in obese children and adolescents.
authorString: Soliman AT, AlHumaidi N, Elawwa A, Alyafei F, Hamed N, Ahmed S, Alaaraj N.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

abstractText:
Introduction

Childhood obesity drives nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and adipokine dysregulation, converging on insulin resistance (IR) to promote subclinical vascular injury measurable as increased carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT). Pediatric-specific mechanistic integration of these pathways with early atherosclerosis remains incompletely characterized. This review synthesizes evidence on NAFLD severity and cIMT in obese youth, examines the roles of resistin, high-molecular-weight (HMW) adiponectin, chemerin, and inflammatory mediators in IR-driven vascular remodeling, and evaluates their diagnostic and therapeutic implications.

Content

A structured narrative review following SANRA guidance was conducted. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched from January 2000 to March 2025 for studies enrolling children aged 2-18 years with obesity and reporting cIMT measured by B-mode ultrasonography alongside NAFLD or adipokine measures. Quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) and AMSTAR-2. Across ten included studies (NOS scores: 5-8/9), obese children with NAFLD demonstrated consistently higher cIMT than controls (pooled weighted mean difference: +0.06 mm; 95% CI: 0.04-0.08 mm). Biopsy-proven nonalcoholic steatohepatitis independently predicted greater cIMT than simple steatosis (r=0.41; p<0.01). Resistin showed the strongest adipokine-cIMT association (r=0.47; p<0.001), with direct (β=0.31) and indirect effects via HOMA-IR (β=0.18) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (β=0.12). HMW-adiponectin deficiency, rather than total adiponectin, defined the preatherosclerotic phenotype. Chemerin correlated with cIMT (r=0.44; p<0.01) and metabolic syndrome score (β=0.39; p<0.001). Weight-loss intervention reduced cIMT by 0.03 mm (p<0.05), accompanied by adipokine normalization.

Summary and outlook

NAFLD and adipokine dysregulation constitute interdigitated, IR-centered pathways associated with early atherosclerosis in obese youth, detectable from age 7 and partially reversible with timely intervention. A tiered algorithm incorporating BMI, liver enzymes, HOMA-IR, cIMT, and adipokine profiling is proposed for clinical risk stratification.

title: Identification of perioperative risk factors for retrograde type A dissection after thoracic endovascular aortic repair for type B dissection.
authorString: Li J, Zhang Y, Chen X, Tan X, Xie A, Ma M, Wang J, Wei X, Hu M.
abstractText:
Objective

To identify risk factors and develop a predictive model for retrograde type A dissection (RTAD) following thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) for type B aortic dissection (TBAD).

Methods

We analyzed TBAD patients who underwent TEVAR from 2014 to 2024 (IRB:No. TJ-IRB20230805). Patients developing RTAD within 1 year were matched with controls by age, sex, operation date, and location. Logistic regression identified risk factors, and a nomogram was constructed. Model performance was assessed using ROC curves.

Results

Of 2383 patients, 76 (3.19%) developed RTAD within one year. 65 RTAD cases and 195 matched controls were analyzed. RTAD patients had a greater horizontal distance of the ascending aorta (HDAA) than controls (53.34 mm vs. 43.05 mm, p < .001). Multivariate analysis identified younger age (OR = 0.95, p = .008), larger HDAA (OR = 1.14, p < .001), aortic root dilatation (OR = 2.85, p = .006), shorter stent length (OR = 0.99, p = .029), and absence of postoperative bradycardic drug use (OR = 0.31, p = .005) as independent RTAD risk factors. The model showed good discrimination (AUC = 0.85).

Conclusion

Younger age, larger HDAA, aortic root dilatation, shorter stent length, and no bradycardic drugs postoperatively are independent predictors of RTAD after TEVAR. For TBAD patients with a high risk of RTAD, clinicians should consider the possibility of having connective tissue diseases, select stents appropriately, and optimize postoperative treatment with strict follow-up.

title: The Congenital Heart Surgeons' Society Center for Research and Quality 2025 Annual Report.
authorString: Jacobs JP, DeCampli WM, Najm HK, Honjo O, Alsoufi B, Karamlou T, Jegatheeswaran A, St Louis JD, Lambert LM, Manlhiot C, Kumar SR, Howell A, Kirklin JK, Tchervenkov CI, Austin EH, Overman DM, Dearani JA, Romano JC, Svensson LG, Williams WG, Jacobs ML, Blackstone EH, Jaquiss RDB.

abstractText: The Congenital Heart Surgeons' Society (CHSS) is viewed by many as one of the most prestigious professional societies dedicated to pediatric and congenital cardiac surgery. The CHSS Center for Research and Quality (CRQ) Fall 2025 Work Weekend was held in Chicago on Saturday, October 25, 2025. The purpose of this article is to summarize the proceedings of the CHSS CRQ Fall 2025 Work Weekend and to provide a 2025 Annual Report of the CHSS CRQ. At the CHSS CRQ Fall 2025 Work Weekend, multiple topics were discussed related to ongoing CHSS research and quality initiatives. The CHSS CRQ is evolving to keep pace with the rapid evolution of medical informatics and the ever-evolving regulatory issues of clinical research. This 2025 Annual Report of the CHSS CRQ summarizes some of the ongoing initiatives at CHSS CRQ designed to assure that the CHSS CRQ continues to lead innovative and collaborative clinical research to improve pediatric and congenital cardiac care.

title: Leadless Pacemakers After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Meta-analysis With Time-to-Event Analysis.
authorString: Wijayanto FPS, Tristan CD, Aditya MR, Simanjuntak AMT, Pranata R.
abstractText:
Background

Permanent pacemaker implantation is a common complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Leadless pacemakers (LPs) may reduce lead- and pocket-related complications, but their clinical outcomes after TAVR remain uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the safety and effectiveness of LPs compared with transvenous pacemakers (TVPs).

Methods

PubMed, Scopus, and ScienceDirect were searched from inception to June 10, 2026. Randomized and observational studies were included. Random-effects meta-analyses pooled proportions, risk ratios (RRs), and mean differences (MDs). Reconstructed Kaplan-Meier data were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs).

Results

Ten studies involving 10,809 patients (1030 LP and 9779 TVP recipients) were included. The pooled procedural success rate of LP implantation was 98% (95% CI 95%-99%). Implantation success was comparable between LP and TVP (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.98-1.02). Sensitivity analysis demonstrated a shorter hospital stay with LP (MD -1.37 days, 95% CI -2.33 to -0.41) and a lower risk of heart failure hospitalization (RR 0.37, 95% CI 0.14-0.96). Overall survival did not differ between groups (HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.44-1.23), although reconstructed survival curves showed late separation favoring LP. Device-related and vascular complications were comparable between LP and TVP.

Conclusions

LP implantation after TAVR demonstrates excellent procedural success and clinical outcomes comparable to TVPs. LPs may reduce hospital stay and heart failure hospitalization, supporting their use as an alternative pacing strategy in appropriately selected patients.

title: Outcomes of Open vs Endovascular Repair of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Involving the Iliac Bifurcation.
authorString: Veranyan N, Kang Sim DE, Ilyas S, Wang S, Oderich GS, Malas MB.
abstractText:
Background

Aneurysmal involvement of the iliac bifurcation increases the complexity of both open and endovascular repair of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA), potentially raising the risk of postoperative complications. Randomized trials comparing endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) and open aortic repair (OAR) for AAA showed that EVAR is associated with a lower postoperative mortality rate. However, it remains unclear whether these results apply to AAA involving the iliac bifurcation (AAAIB). Several small single-institutional studies have shown conflicting results. This study aims to compare the outcomes of EVAR and OAR for AAAIB in a real-world, multi-institutional setting.

Methods

The Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database was queried for patients who underwent repair for AAAIB. The cohort was divided into two groups based on the intervention: EVAR vs OAR. Baseline demographic, clinical, and perioperative characteristics, as well as outcomes such as overall 30-day mortality, in-hospital mortality, Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE: death, myocardial infarction, stroke), intestinal ischemia, overall reinterventions, and 1-year survival, were compared between the groups. Univariable analysis, multivariable inverse probability-weighted regression (IPWR), survival analysis with the Kaplan-Meier method, log-rank test, and Cox proportional hazards regression were performed.

Results
