Of all reviewed patients, 7,535 were included in the final analysis, of whom 5,742 (76.2%) underwent EVAR, whereas 1,793 (23.8%) underwent OAR. In IPWR models, patients who underwent EVAR had significantly lower odds of overall in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.25, 95%CI: 0.18-0.34, p<0.001), 30-day mortality (OR: 0.31, 95%CI: 0.23-0.42, p<0.001), MACE (OR: 0.24, 95%CI: 0.19-0.31, p<0.001), and other postoperative adverse events compared to OAR. The Cox proportional hazards model demonstrated a significantly higher 1-year survival rate for EVAR compared to OAR (HR: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.50-0.76, p<0.001).

Conclusions

In this real-world, multi-institutional study, EVAR for AAAIB was associated with lower odds of overall in-hospital mortality, 30-day mortality, MACE, as well as a higher 1-year survival rate, compared to the OAR. EVAR should be considered the primary method for repairing aortoiliac aneurysm involving the iliac bifurcation in anatomically suitable patients. Longer follow-up studies are needed to confirm these findings and compare the long-term reintervention and aorta-related mortality rates between the two treatment modalities.

title: Gut microbiome and metabolite signatures in critical limb threatening ischemia.
authorString: Messiha D, Lange E, Tratnik A, Westendorf AM, Rinke M, Lenz S, Hendgen-Cotta UB, Buer J, Rassaf T, Rammos C.
abstractText: Background: Atherosclerotic disease entails with distinct clinical phenotypes, of which chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) and critical limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) are key manifestations. While plaque morphology and clinical course differ in vascular territory, the underlying pathophysiology leading to distinct diseases remain unexplored. The gut-microbiome axis with derived mediators trimethylamine-N-oxide (TMAO) and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) has emerged as proatherogenic or protective in vascular diseases, however the differential abundance, composition and metabolites have not been investigated in CCS or CLTI. Patients and methods: In this cross-sectional clinical trial, we included patients with CCS and CLTI within 24 h of clinical presentation. Analyses of the gut microbiome and downstream metabolites were assessed. Microbiome-derived metabolites were analyzed from peripheral blood samples. Gut microbiome samples were characterized by 16S rRNA gene analysis. Results: We enrolled 40 patients with 20 patients each presenting with CCS and CLTI, respectively. While alpha and beta diversity were similar, CCS patients exhibited distinct microbial signatures, including higher abundance of Dialister, Monoglobus, Lachnospira, Barnesiella, Fusicatenibacter, Collinsella, and Roseburia. Subsequent analysis of microbiome-derived metabolites revealed significantly lower serum concentrations of isovaleric acid and a non-significant trend toward TMAO elevation in the CLTI group compared to the CCS group. Conclusions: In this pilot trial we demonstrate that distinct differences in gut bacteria and microbiome-derived metabolites exist between patients with CCS and CLTI. These findings may highlight microbiome-metabolite interactions in chronic atherosclerotic disease and support larger studies to elucidate causal mechanisms.

title: Short-Term Complications of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (PROLONG-TAVR).
authorString: Castillo-Perez M, León-Gutiérrez H, Jerjes-Sánchez C, Royzman-Rivera L, Paredes-Vazquez JG, Jimenez-Franco V, Gutiérrez-Gallegos P, Cabada-Garcia MJ, Rodriguez-Rivera J, Paredes-Gutierrez E, Quevedo-Salazar R, Sanchez-Avila JF.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText: To estimate the cumulative incidence of short-term complications across different transcatheter heart valve (THV) prostheses used for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA and a prospectively registered PROSPERO protocol. Observational studies published from 2002 through May 2024 that included patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing predominantly transfemoral TAVR and reported prosthesis-specific complications were eligible. Although the original protocol intended to evaluate both short- and long-term complications, long-term outcomes were too sparse and inconsistently reported for robust pooled analyses; therefore, the present analysis focuses on short-term complications. Pooled cumulative incidences were calculated using random-effects models. We included 242 studies comprising 181,187 patients. SAPIEN 3 had the lowest incidence of moderate-to-severe paravalvular leak (PVL) (1.04%, 95% CI 0.69-1.55) and stroke (1.87%, 95% CI 1.64-2.14), whereas ACURATE neo2 had the lowest incidence of permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) (7.7%, 95% CI 5.82-10.11). Evolut PRO and SAPIEN 3 showed among the lowest rates of major vascular complications (3.56%, 95% CI 2.77-4.57 and 3.87%, 95% CI 3.22-4.66, respectively) and major or life-threatening bleeding (2.96%, 95% CI 2.09-4.17 and 4.8%, 95% CI 4.04-5.69, respectively). Short-term complications have decreased with newer-generation THV prostheses. PVL remains more frequent with self-expanding valves, whereas PPI is the most frequent complication and is generally less frequent with balloon-expandable valves and ACURATE neo2. Stroke rates have changed little across newer generations, and annular rupture, coronary artery obstruction, and valve embolization remain rare (< 1%).

title: Artificial Intelligence for Predicting Amputation and Related Outcomes in Peripheral Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Hsu H, Wang MJ, Chu YY, Huang YJ, Lee CH.
abstractText:
Background

Peripheral artery disease (PAD) affects over 236 million individuals globally and carries substantial risks of amputation, major adverse limb events (MALE), and mortality. Existing clinical scoring systems focus on short-term surgical outcomes and lack generalizability. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising tool for PAD outcome prediction.

Objective

To conduct the first quantitative meta-analysis evaluating the discriminative performance, methodological rigor, and certainty of evidence of ML-based prognostic models for adverse limb outcomes in PAD.

Methods

Following PRISMA/PRISMA-S guidelines, PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception through March 15, 2026. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and PROBAST risk-of-bias assessment. Random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian-Laird with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman correction) and hierarchical summary ROC (HSROC) analysis were performed; certainty was rated with GRADE.

Results

Ten studies were included. The pooled AUC for amputation-related outcomes was 0.88 (95% CI, 0.83-0.94; prediction interval, 0.79-0.98) with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 95.4%). HSROC yielded pooled sensitivity 0.855 and specificity 0.836. Registry-based studies showed higher pooled AUC than non-registry studies (0.92 vs 0.80; p = 0.004). All models had high or unclear risk of bias in the analysis domain; none underwent independent external validation. GRADE certainty was very low.

Conclusions

ML models demonstrate high discriminative performance for predicting amputation-related outcomes in PAD, but very low certainty of evidence, absence of external validation, and high risk of bias currently limit clinical implementation. Prospective multicenter validation and adherence to AI reporting guidelines are essential before clinical translation.

title: Non-General Anesthesia for Endovascular Aneurysm Repair: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Clinical Outcomes and Robustness of Evidence.
authorString: Nisi F, Piscopo R, Aurelli F, Calgaro G, Meco M, Giustiniano E, Piccioni F, Lepidi S, D'Oria M.
abstractText:
Background

The optimal anesthetic strategy for endovascular aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR) remains debated. While recent meta-analyses suggested potential benefits for non-general anesthesia (Non-GA), available evidence is observational, and the robustness of pooled estimates remains uncertain.

Methods

A systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative observational studies (2015-2025) was conducted across PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus. Primary outcomes were 30-day and in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included length of stay (LOS) and postoperative complications. Random-effects models utilized the Paule-Mandel estimator with Hartung-Knapp adjustment, prediction intervals, and prespecified influence diagnostics.

Results

Twenty-two studies comprising >150,000 EVAR procedures were analyzed. Non-GA was not associated with reduced 30-day mortality compared with general anesthesia (RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.54-1.52; I2≈86%; wide prediction interval). Influence diagnostics identified one influential study; its exclusion yielded a lower mortality for Non-GA (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.59-0.87; I2≈1%). Non-GA was associated with a modest reduction in hospital LOS (mean difference -0.53 days, 95% CI -1.02 to -0.03), but no consistent differences were observed in ICU stay or major complications. The overall certainty of evidence was judged very low (GRADE).

Conclusions

Non-GA for EVAR does not increase 30-day mortality risk compared to general anesthesia. However, survival estimates are sensitive to study-level characteristics and procedural complexity. Current observational evidence supports individualized anesthetic selection rather than proving superiority or equivalence of either technique.

title: Endoscopic versus open great saphenous vein harvesting for lower extremity arterial bypass: A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression.
authorString: Maris MI, Eissa-Garces A, Pérez GC, Tsapara A, Madera D, Avram MF, Ho K, Vavra A, Navarro T, Lopes L.
abstractText:
Objective

To compare postoperative outcomes of patients undergoing lower extremity arterial bypass (LEAB) for peripheral artery disease (PAD) with endoscopic great saphenous vein harvest (EVH) versus open vein harvest (OVH), and to investigate the impact of publication year on bypass patency.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched from inception through January 2025 for comparative studies of EVH versus OVH in LEAB. Individual patient data were reconstructed from Kaplan-Meier curves and analysed using Cox proportional hazards models. Binary and continuous outcomes were pooled using random-effects models. Meta-regression and subgroup analyses by publication year (≤2015 vs >2015) were performed to explore temporal trends in patency.

Results

Thirteen retrospective cohort studies comprising 12 401 patients were included. EVH was associated with higher risk of primary patency loss compared with OVH (HR 1.32; 95% CI 1.04-1.68; p=.030) and a borderline longer operative time (MD 58.98 minutes; 95% CI 0.63-117.32; p=.050; I2=96%), but significantly lower wound complications (RR 0.68; 95% CI 0.57-0.80; p<.001). No differences were observed in primary-assisted patency, secondary patency, length of stay, major amputation, limb salvage, or mortality. Subgroup analysis showed that the primary patency disadvantage was driven by studies published up to 2015 (HR 1.49; p=.010), with no significant difference in studies published after 2015 (HR 0.97; p=.900), although the interaction test was not significant (p=.100). Meta-regression did not demonstrate an association between publication year and primary patency effect size (p=.890).

Conclusion

EVH significantly reduces wound complications but is associated with lower primary patency and potentially longer operative times compared with OVH, disadvantages that do not translate into differences in secondary patency, limb salvage, major amputation, or mortality. Further prospective studies are needed to define the role of EVH to better inform LEAB operative planning.

title: Aortoduodenal syndrome: evolving management of a rare cause of duodenal obstruction in the endovascular era.
authorString: Koliakos N, Bakopoulos A, Tzortzis AS, Papakonstantinou D, Georgiadou C, Lazaris A, Schizas D.
abstractText:
Objective

Aortoduodenal syndrome (ADS) is a very rare complication of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA), characterized by extrinsic compression of the duodenum leading to proximal bowel obstruction. This systematic review sought to aggregate all published ADS cases, with emphasis on patient demographics, diagnostic workup, treatment modalities, and outcomes.

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted across MedLine/PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science from database inception through 2 February 2026, following PRISMA guidelines. Reports containing original patient data describing duodenal obstruction attributable to abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA), irrespective of rupture status, were eligible for inclusion, provided that the obstruction was attributed to aneurysmal mass effect. Extracted variables included demographic characteristics, clinical presentation, aneurysm morphology, diagnostic imaging, therapeutic interventions, and follow-up results. This study has been registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251456530).

Results

Forty studies encompassing 44 patients were analyzed. The cohort was predominantly male (86.6%), with a mean age of 74.5 years. The most common presenting symptoms were vomiting, abdominal pain, and a palpable pulsatile abdominal mass. Computed tomography served as the primary diagnostic tool, whereas upper gastrointestinal contrast series and endoscopy were employed mainly to exclude alternative obstructive etiologies. The third duodenal portion was the most frequently compressed segment, with a median aneurysm diameter of 72.5 mm. Surgical intervention was performed in most patients, comprising open aortic repair (n = 18) or endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR, n = 13). Gastrointestinal bypass procedures were reserved for selected or salvage situations. Outcome data were available for 42 patients. Mortality was reported in 6 patients (14.3%), including two patients who did not undergo operative treatment. Among the 39 patients who underwent operative treatment, postoperative complications were reported in 9 patients (23.1%).

Conclusion

EVAR represents an increasingly reported treatment option in anatomically suitable patients, particularly those at high operative risk; however, the available evidence remains insufficient to establish EVAR as the preferred first-line treatment. Treatment should be individualized according to aneurysm anatomy, clinical condition, operative risk, and severity of duodenal obstruction.

title: RNA-Based Therapies for Lipoprotein(a) Reduction: Antisense Oligonucleotides, Small Interfering RNAs, and Emerging Platforms.
authorString: Parcha V, Bittner VA.
abstractText:
Purpose of review

Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an independent, genetically determined, and causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and calcific aortic valve stenosis. Elevated Lp(a) affects approximately 20% of the global population and is not meaningfully modified by lifestyle intervention or existing lipid-lowering pharmacotherapy. This review summarizes the biology of Lp(a) as a therapeutic target, evaluates the efficacy of currently available lipid-lowering agents against this target, and describes the mechanistic principles, clinical evidence, and unresolved questions associated with RNA-based and emerging small-molecule and gene-editing approaches to Lp(a) reduction.

Recent findings

Four RNA-directed agents targeting hepatic apolipoprotein(a) [apo(a)] synthesis have entered phase 2/3 development. This includes pelacarsen, an antisense oligonucleotide (ASO), and olpasiran, zerlasiran, and lepodisiran, which are N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc)-conjugated small interfering RNAs (siRNAs). Phase 2 data demonstrate Lp(a) reductions ranging from 79% to approximately 97% on a placebo-adjusted basis, approaching the practical limit of apo(a) suppression, with favorable short-term safety profiles. A fifth, structurally distinct siRNA conjugated with GalNAc at both strand termini has recently completed first-in-human testing, sustaining reductions up to 97% through 48 weeks after a single dose without injection-site reactions. Recently, the topline results of phase 3 Lp(a) HORIZON (pelacarsen) were released and demonstrate a substantial Lp(a) reduction without meeting the trial's primary composite cardiovascular endpoint. Two further outcomes trials, OCEAN(a)-Outcomes (olpasiran) and ACCLAIM-Lp(a) (lepodisiran), remain ongoing. An oral small molecule, muvalaplin, achieved comparable reductions in phase 2 testing. Lastly, early non-human primate data, together with a completed phase 1 trial of an analogous CRISPR-Cas9 construct targeting a related hepatic lipid gene, support the feasibility of a CRISPR-Cas9-based gene-editing approach capable of durable apo(a) suppression from a single administration. The pharmacology of Lp(a) suppression is now well characterized across three distinct therapeutic modalities. Whether the magnitude of biochemical reduction observed translates into a meaningful and safe reduction in cardiovascular events across different populations remains undetermined and will be addressed by the ongoing outcomes trials.

title: Comparative Outcomes of Left Anterior Thoracotomy Versus Resternotomy for Pulmonic Valve Replacement After Tetralogy of Fallot Repair.
authorString: Taksaudom N, Phothikun A, Horsatidkul J, Thepsuwan T, Woragidpoonpol S.
abstractText:
Objective

Redo pulmonary valve replacement (PVR) in patients with prior tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) repair is surgically challenging. This study aimed to compare the clinical outcomes of the left anterior minithoracotomy (LAT) approach with the traditional resternotomy approach for PVR.

Methods

A retrospective analysis was conducted on 38 TOF patients who underwent redo PVR, categorized into LAT (n = 20) and resternotomy (n = 18) groups. Patients requiring concomitant valvular surgeries or repair of residual intracardiac shunts were excluded. We compared demographics, operative details, and postoperative outcomes.

Results

Baseline demographics were comparable between groups, except for a higher proportion of males in the LAT group (75% vs 38.9%, P = 0.047). The LAT approach demonstrated nonsignificant favorable trends, including shorter operative times (157.05 ± 49.42 vs 178.06 ± 58.69 min, P = 0.239) and shorter postoperative hospital stays (4.75 ± 1.21 vs 6.17 ± 4.38 days, P = 0.173). Vasoactive-inotropic scores were significantly lower in the LAT group both immediately postoperatively (0.05 ± 0.22 vs 4.36 ± 6.95, P = 0.009) and on postoperative day 1 (0 vs 2.17 ± 4.52, P = 0.039). Postoperative complications, such as atrial fibrillation and pleural effusion, were similar between groups. There was no mortality in either group.

Conclusions

The LAT approach for PVR after TOF repair is a safe alternative to resternotomy. Comprehensive preoperative imaging evaluation is crucial for determining the optimal incision site. Further studies with larger cohorts are needed to confirm the potential benefits of this approach.

title: Role of 12/15-lipoxygenase and its metabolites in cardiovascular diseases.
authorString: Yu J, Ni W, Lin Y, Gao Y, Zhou J, Li Y.
abstractText: 12/15-Lipoxygenase (12/15-LOX), a key oxidoreductase enzyme, catalyzes the peroxidation of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) including omega-6 and omega-3 fatty acids. This enzyme is expressed in multiple cell types such as macrophages, endothelial cells, and epithelial cells, where it participates in arachidonic acid (AA) metabolism through the hydroperoxidation pathway. The catalytic activity of 12/15-LOX generates bioactive lipid mediators, notably 12-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid (12-HETE) and 15-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid (15-HETE), which serve as signaling molecules in physiological and pathological processes. Emerging evidence establishes 12/15-LOX as a critical mediator in oxidative stress and inflammatory cascades. Its pathophysiological involvement has been mechanistically linked to the pathogenesis of cardiovascular disorders, particularly through promoting atherosclerotic plaque formation, vascular endothelial dysfunction, and myocardial ischemic injury. Clinical epidemiological studies further demonstrate significant associations between 12/15-LOX activity and disease progression in atherosclerosis, essential hypertension, and acute myocardial infarction. In this review, we systematically examine the biosynthetic origin of 12/15-LOX, delineate its metabolic pathways and its pleiotropic functions in modulating inflammatory responses, redox homeostasis, and programmed cell death cascades. Furthermore, we critically evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies targeting 12/15-LOX enzymatic activity or its downstream effectors, with particular emphasis on translational opportunities for cardiovascular disease management. This synthesis aims to advance the development of precision therapies targeting the 12/15-LOX pathway in cardiometabolic disorders.

title: Embolic and atherosclerosis-associated acute mesenteric ischemia: distinct clinical entities with different outcomes.
authorString: Peter D, Thurner A, Kroth A, Kollmann L, Kelm M, Kickuth R, Germer CT, Flemming S.
abstractText:
Background

Acute arterial occlusive mesenteric ischemia is associated with high mortality. Embolic and atherosclerosis-associated forms differ in vascular pathology, collateral circulation, and ischemic tolerance, which may contribute to differences in clinical presentation and outcomes. This study compared clinical presentation, treatment strategies, and outcomes between embolic acute mesenteric ischemia (EAMI) and atherosclerosis-associated acute mesenteric ischemia (AAMI).

Methods

This retrospective single-center study included all consecutive patients diagnosed with acute arterial occlusive mesenteric ischemia between January 2004 and March 2026. Patients were stratified into EAMI and AAMI groups. The primary endpoint was in-hospital mortality. Secondary analyses evaluated clinical presentation, imaging findings, and treatment strategies. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to assess the association between etiology and in-hospital mortality.

Results

Of 216 patients identified, 190 were included in the final analysis (EAMI, 56.8%; AAMI, 43.2%). Patients with EAMI more frequently presented with sudden-onset abdominal pain, whereas AAMI was characterized by acute-on-chronic symptoms and longer symptom-to-treatment intervals. Imaging findings indicative of advanced bowel ischemia, including pneumatosis intestinalis and portomesenteric venous gas, as well as bowel resection at initial surgical exploration, were more common in AAMI (40.2% vs. 21.3%, p = 0.005). In-hospital mortality was higher in AAMI than in EAMI (75.6% vs. 60.2%, p = 0.025). In multivariable analyses, EAMI was independently associated with lower in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratios 0.41-0.47; both p < 0.05).

Conclusion

EAMI and AAMI represent distinct clinical entities with different presentations and outcomes. AAMI is associated with delayed presentation, more advanced ischemic injury at diagnosis, and higher in-hospital mortality. Etiology is independently associated with in-hospital mortality and should be considered in risk stratification and the design of future studies.

title: Lentinan-induced FUBP1 O-GlcNAcylation suppresses macrophage ferroptosis and atherosclerosis via the Tp53/SLC7A11 axis.
authorString: Liu X, Xu Z, Cheng F, Hu S, He M, Zheng W, Wei H, Li J, Yang H, Fang L, Wang Y, Zheng L, Rao X, Fang Q.
abstractText: Atherosclerosis remains a leading cause of cardiovascular mortality, driven by macrophage dysfunction and necrotic core expansion. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent cell death, is a critical driver of plaque instability; however, pharmacological interventions targeting ferroptosis remain scarce. Lentinan (LNT), a bioactive β-(1,3)-glucan extracted from shiitake mushrooms, exhibits potent antioxidant properties but its potential role in the modulation of macrophage ferroptosis remains unexplored. We investigated the therapeutic potential and molecular mechanisms of action of LNT in atherosclerosis. LNT administration significantly attenuated atherosclerotic progression in mice. Specifically, LNT mitigated macrophage ferroptosis by enhancing glutathione homeostasis and reducing lipid peroxidation. Notably, these protective effects were significantly abrogated in mice deficient in solute carrier family 7 member 11 (SLC7A11), indicating that the effect of LNT is dependent on this molecule. We found that LNT directly binds to far upstream binding protein 1 (FUBP1) and that T559 is required for FUBP1 O-GlcNAcylation and subsequent nuclear translocation. In the nucleus, FUBP1 binds to tumor protein p53 (Tp53), thereby relieving the transcriptional repression of SLC7A11. The resulting activation of the SLC7A11 signaling axis not only inhibits ferroptosis but also promotes scavenger receptor B type 1 (SR-B1)-mediated cholesterol efflux. These findings highlight LNT as a novel modulator of the FUBP1/Tp53/SLC7A11 axis, offering a promising natural therapeutic strategy to stabilize atherosclerotic plaques.

title: The epigenetic-metabolic axis of trained immunity: dual roles in disease pathogenesis and intervention.
authorString: Liao L, Zhai Z, Zhong L, Shi C, Yao S, Tao L, Cheng YX, Liu X.
abstractText: As early as 1931, bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccination was hypothesized to reduce neonatal mortality through nonspecific immune stimulation. The concept of trained immunity was formally proposed in the 21st century, and clinical observations during the COVID-19 pandemic further stimulated interest in the possibility that BCG vaccination might confer broad, non-specific protection against heterologous infections. Trained immunity represents a paradigm-shifting concept in immunology, defining the innate immune system's ability to develop a memory-like state through persistent epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming following initial stimulus exposure. This process enables enhanced, nonspecific responses upon re-exposure, extending immune memory beyond adaptive immunity. The dual role of trained immunity is context-dependent: it is protective in acute infections by improving pathogen clearance, but pathogenic in chronic conditions such as atherosclerosis and certain tumor microenvironments, where sustained proinflammatory memory promotes disease progression. Central mechanisms involve mTOR-HIF-1α signaling, metabolic rewiring of mevalonate/cholesterol pathways, and histone modifications including H3K4me3 and H3K27ac. This review systematically synthesizes the cellular basis, inducing factors, and disease spectrum of trained immunity, providing a conceptual framework for advancing host-directed therapies and precision immunology in infectious, inflammatory, and oncological contexts.

title: Prognostic value of liver scoring systems in predicting early outcomes after pericardiectomy: a single-center retrospective study.
authorString: AlShiekh M, Muppiri V, Helal A, Bazerbashi S, Sethi A, Kathuria U, Bashir A, Allam M, Dalrymple-Hay M.

journal.title: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace

abstractText: Pericardiectomy for constrictive pericarditis remains a high-risk operation, and early outcomes are inadequately predicted by conventional cardiac risk models despite the high prevalence of chronic hepatic congestion in this population. We performed a retrospective observational analysis of 104 consecutive patients undergoing isolated pericardiectomy between 2010 and 2024 to determine whether established hepatic scoring systems [Child-Pugh, Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) and Model for End-Stage Liver Disease-Sodium (MELD-Na)] predict early mortality and major postoperative morbidity. Preoperative clinical and biochemical variables were used to derive the hepatic scores. The primary endpoint was 30-day mortality; the secondary endpoint was new postoperative renal-replacement therapy. Thirty-day mortality was 4.8% (5/104). Patients were classified as Child-Pugh A in 66 (63.5%), B in 35 (33.7%), and C in 3 (2.9%), with corresponding mortalities of 1.5%, 2.9%, and 100% (p<0.01 for trend). Discrimination for 30-day mortality was strong for Child-Pugh [area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) 0.89, 95% confidence interval 0.73-1.00], MELD (0.85, 0.60-0.98), and MELD-Na (0.83, 0.55-0.97), whereas EuroSCORE II showed no meaningful predictive ability (AUC≈0.51). Hepatic dysfunction quantified by Child-Pugh and MELD-based scores is a strong predictor of early mortality after pericardiectomy and outperforms conventional cardiac risk models in this cohort. Incorporation of structured hepatic assessment into preoperative risk stratification may improve perioperative planning and patient counseling; however, the small number of Child-Pugh C patients and the retrospective single-center design necessitate validation in larger prospective cohorts.

title: Clinical Outcomes and Exploratory Haemodynamic Numerical Simulation of Patients with Multichannelled Aortic Dissection: A Multicentre, Retrospective Cohort Study.
authorString: Yang J, Luan J, Shao S, Yang Y, Mao L, He F, Luo Y, Zhu T.

journal.title: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery

abstractText:
Objective

Multichannelled aortic dissection (MCAD) is a rare type of aortic dissection with limited data on its clinical features and outcomes. This multicentre, retrospective cohort study compared clinical outcomes between MCAD and double channelled aortic dissection (DCAD) and explored haemodynamic differences.

Methods

Patients with aortic dissection were enrolled from three tertiary hospitals. Patients with one true lumen and one false lumen were classified as having DCAD, whereas those with one true lumen and multiple false lumina were classified as having MCAD. Propensity score matching balanced baseline characteristics. Primary outcomes were 30 day and five year all cause mortality after diagnosis. Secondary outcomes included preprocedural mortality, aortic dissection related mortality, post-operative complications, and re-intervention. Overall survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Haemodynamic differences were evaluated by exploratory computational fluid dynamics (CFD) analysis.

Results

After matching, 50 patients were included in each group (n = 100). The difference in 30 day mortality was significant (p = .046) and largely reflected preprocedural deaths, which occurred in six patients with MCAD (12%) and none with DCAD (p = .027). Overall survival differed between groups (log rank p = .037; hazard ratio 2.72, 95% confidence interval 1.03 - 7.18; p = .044). Kaplan-Meier estimated mortality at 30 days, one year, and five years was 16%, 23%, and 29% in MCAD compared with 4%, 8%, and 12% in DCAD, respectively. Among treated patients, re-intervention was more frequent in MCAD than in DCAD (21% vs. 6%; p = .036), whereas post-operative complication rates did not differ. Exploratory CFD analysis suggested greater false lumen haemodynamic burden in MCAD.

Conclusion

MCAD was associated with greater preprocedural mortality and more frequent re-intervention than DCAD. These findings may identify MCAD as a higher risk phenotype warranting closer surveillance and timely evaluation. Haemodynamic observations remain exploratory and require validation in larger prospective cohorts.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Transperitoneal vs Retroperitoneal Approaches of Open Aortic Repair for Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Stratified by the Iliac Bifurcation Involvement.
authorString: Veranyan N, Kang Sim DE, Ilyas S, Wang S, Abou-Zamzam A, Malas MB.
abstractText:
Background

Aortic aneurysm involving the iliac bifurcation (AAAIB) is associated with higher rates of systemic comorbidities and increased complexity of open aortic repair (OAR), resulting in worse outcomes compared to OAR for isolated abdominal aortic aneurysm (IAAA). The Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) practice guidelines recommend the retroperitoneal approach (RPA) for OAR in certain patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). However, there is limited evidence to determine whether the relative advantages and disadvantages of RPA and the transperitoneal approach (TPA) change depending on whether the aneurysm distally involves the iliac bifurcation. This study aims to compare the outcomes of TPA and RPA for AAA, stratified by the iliac bifurcation involvement, in a multi-institutional, real-world setting.

Methods

The SVS Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database was queried for patients who underwent OAR for AAA from January 2003 to September 2024. Patients were stratified as AAAIB or IAAA based on whether the aneurysm involved the iliac bifurcation and required a distal anastomosis beyond the common iliac artery (CIA) bifurcation, or not. Baseline characteristics, as well as outcomes such as overall 30-day mortality, Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE: death, myocardial infarction, stroke), and 1-year survival, were compared between the TPA and RPA groups in patients with IAAA and AAAIB. Univariable and multivariable analyses, as well as a confirmatory analysis with inverse probability-weighted regression (IPWR), were performed.

Results

Of all reviewed patients, 17,009 were included in the final analysis, of whom 15,218 (89.5%) had IAAA, and 1,791 (10.5%) had AAAIB. Among patients with IAAA, compared to RPA, TPA was associated with higher odds of overall 30-day mortality (OR: 1.26, 95%CI: 1.05-1.49, p=0.011), MACE (OR: 1.26, 95%CI: 1.11-1.44, p=0.001), and a lower 1-year survival rate (HR: 1.23, 95%CI: 1.09-1.39, p=0.001). Among patients with AAAIB, TPA was associated with lower odds of lower extremity (LE) ischemia (OR: 0.47, 95%CI: 0.25-0.91, p=0.024) without significant differences in 30-day mortality (OR: 0.80, 95%CI: 0.42-1.51, p=0.485), MACE (OR: 0.86, 95%CI: 0.52-1.42, p=0.563), and 1-year survival (HR: 0.93, 95%CI: 0.59-1.47, p=0.768).

Conclusions

In this real-world study, involvement of the iliac bifurcation in AAA was an effect modifier for the outcomes of different OAR approaches. For patients with IAAA, compared with RPA, TPA was associated with worse 30-day mortality, MACE, and 1-year survival. Whereas for patients with AAAIB, TPA was associated with lower odds of LE ischemia, without significant differences in 30-day mortality, MACE, or 1-year survival. This study suggests that RPA may be the procedure of choice for IAAA if it is otherwise feasible. However, TPA may be the procedure of choice for patients with AAAIB who are otherwise anatomically suitable. Larger prospective studies are warranted to validate these findings.

title: Neurodevelopmental risk in a referred sample of hospitalized children with congenital heart disease: interrelation between communication and feeding vulnerabilities.
authorString: Pimentel-Piemonte C, Sassi FC, Ritto AP, Medeiros GC, Andrade CRF.
abstractText:
Objective

To determine the prevalence of communication developmental risk in hospitalized children with Congenital Heart Disease (CHD) and to identify clinical, surgical, and hospitalization-related factors independently associated with increased risk.

Methods

This cross-sectional observational study was conducted at a tertiary pediatric cardiac center between September 2024 and April 2025. Sixty-five children referred for speech-language pathology assessment underwent communication development screening using a structured developmental observation protocol. Functional feeding status was assessed using the Pediatric Functional Oral Intake Scale. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with communication developmental risk, with Firth's penalized logistic regression performed as a sensitivity analysis given the low events-per-variable ratio.

Results

Twenty-five children (38%) were classified as being at risk for delayed communication development. Hospitalization in a ward setting, compared with intensive care, was independently associated with lower odds of risk classification (adjusted OR = 0.13, 95% CI 0.02‒0.77, p = 0.025), an association confirmed by the Firth sensitivity analysis (adjusted OR = 0.18, 95% CI 0.03‒0.80, p = 0.024). Length of hospital stay, cyanotic physiology, cardiopulmonary bypass duration, and aortic cross-clamp time were not independently associated with risk. Children classified as at risk also showed significantly greater feeding restrictions.

Conclusion

Communication developmental risk was common among hospitalized children with CHD. Hospitalization setting and feeding performance, rather than traditional markers of clinical severity, were associated with communication risk, suggesting a multifactorial model that integrates biological, functional, and environmental factors. These findings suggest that feeding function, alongside hospitalization setting, may help flag children at higher developmental risk before formal communication assessment is available. These exploratory findings support incorporating structured developmental surveillance into routine pediatric cardiac care.

title: Deletion of Nephrocystin-4 Exacerbates Kidney and Cardiac Function in Mice Cardiorenal Syndrome Model via the Interaction with Itch E3 ligase.
authorString: Otaki Y, Sato J, Watanabe T, Takehara T, Kuramasu Y, Yamaguchi R, Ono H, Tachibana S, Goto J, Takahashi H, Arimoto T, Ichikawa K, Ochi H, Konta T, Watanabe M.
abstractText: Cardiorenal syndrome (CRS), characterized by cardiac and renal dysfunction, is an increasingly common health issue with a high mortality rate. Nephrocystin 4 (NPHP4) is the major reason for end-stage renal disease in children. We have reported that a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) in NPHP4 is a genetic risk factor for CRS in the general population. However, the functional role of Nphp4 in CRS development remains unexamined. Systemic Nphp4 knockout (KO) mice were developed by deleting exons 3-8. RNA sequencing of the heart and kidney tissues revealed that the gene sets associated with mitochondrial function were significantly downregulated in Nphp4 KO mice compared with their wild-type (WT) littermates. Furthermore, Nphp4 KO mice exhibited less cardiac hypertrophy but exacerbated kidney and cardiac function compared with the WT mice in the CRS models induced via thoracic transverse aortic constriction and 0.2% adenine-diet. Immunoprecipitation confirmed the interaction between Nphp4 and the HECT-type E3 ligase Itch. Furthermore, we observed that Itch targets Lats2 and insulin-like growth factor-1 receptors in cardiomyocytes. Nphp4 knockdown activated Hippo signaling and worsened mitochondrial function in H9C2 cardiomyocytes by inhibiting Itch-dependent Lats2 degradation. Furthermore, it inhibited insulin-like growth factor-1 signaling by disturbing itch-mediated endosome function. Nphp4 deletion exacerbates kidney and cardiac function in the mouse CRS models via mitochondrial dysfunction. Nphp4 mediates Hippo and insulin-like growth factor-1 signaling by interacting with Itch. Nphp4/Itch axis plays the pathophysiological role in CRS development.

title: Protocol-based medical management for inflammatory abdominal aortic aneurysms: a five-year single-center experience.
authorString: Hamzah M, Hayek F, Sfeir J.
abstractText:
Background

Inflammatory abdominal aortic aneurysm (IAAA), a distinct clinical entity characterized by dense periaortic fibrosis and elevated inflammatory markers, lacks a consensus-driven optimal management strategy. While medical therapy is often utilized, comparative data against surgical or endovascular interventions remain limited. We report our experience with a standardized medical protocol for the management of IAAAs.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 27 consecutive patients diagnosed with IAAA between 2012 and 2019. Predefined diagnostic criteria for IAAA included an ESR>100 mm/h, aortic wall thickness >10 mm, and inflammatory symptoms. Risk of rupture was assessed using a PET-CT scan for patients with a maximal aortic diameter exceeding 5.5 cm. A standardized medical protocol was used for low rupture risk patients including IV methylprednisolone followed by oral prednisone taper. Methotrexate was introduced for steroid-refractory cases. Endovascular or open aortic repair was used for patients with high risk of rupture.

Results

Patients had a mean age of 62.3 years, and 70.4% were male. The mean baseline aortic diameter was 48±5 mm (95% CI 46.0-50.0). Twenty-three patients (85.2%) were treated initially with corticosteroids. At the 3-month mark, 69.6% of medically treated patients achieved an acceptable response with steroids alone. Five steroid-refractory patients received methotrexate and demonstrated clinical improvement. ESR normalized in 95.7% of medically treated patients. During five-year follow-up, no medically managed patient required emergency surgical intervention. Eleven patients required temporary steroid reintroduction at 3 years, with sustained stability at 5 years. Three patients underwent EVAR with favorable outcomes. One patient underwent open repair, which was associated with significant perioperative morbidity and late mortality.

Conclusions

In selected patients with low risk of aortic rupture, protocol-based medical therapy for IAAA is safe and effective with minimal risk upon mid-term follow-up. PET-CT scan assessment for risk of immediate rupture is appropriate for patients with aortic diameter between 5.5 to 6.5 cm. Methotrexate introduction may be effective for steroid-refractory cases. Endovascular repair remains a suitable option when intervention is required. Larger prospective studies are needed to establish definitive management guidelines for IAAAs.

title: Impact of the Extent, Pattern, and Location of Replacement Myocardial Fibrosis on Clinical Outcomes in Aortic Regurgitation.
authorString: Li B, Dai L, Liu Y, Han Z, Tang Y, Chen X, Zhang A, Ma X, Zhou P, Jia X, Xu W, Aisikaier K, Han S, Sa F, Yang K, Zhao K, Yan C, Zhao S, Chen X.
abstractText:
Aims

The prognostic significance of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE)-detected replacement myocardial fibrosis in aortic regurgitation (AR) remains incompletely understood. This study aims to explore the association between the extent, pattern, and location of LGE and clinical outcomes in patients with chronic AR.

Methods and results

Between 2010 and 2024, consecutive patients with moderate-to-severe AR and no significant coronary artery stenosis who underwent contrast-enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) were included. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as cardiovascular mortality, heart transplantation, or rehospitalization for heart failure. The association between LGE characteristics and MACE was evaluated. Overall, 363 patients (mean age 52.6 ± 14.2 years; 54 female) were included. Over a median follow-up of 56.6 months, 73 patients experienced MACE. LGE was present in 200 patients (55.1%). An LGE extent threshold of 2.6% provided robust risk stratification, yielding the highest C-index of 0.797, a likelihood ratio chi-square of 97.30, and the lowest Akaike information criterion of 681.06. Furthermore, predominant subendocardial-involved LGE was present in 13.5% of LGE-positive patients and was independently associated with MACE after adjusting for LGE extent (HR 3.028; 95% CI 1.216-7.539; P = 0.017). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated that patients with both LGE extent >2.6% and predominant subendocardial-involved LGE pattern were at the highest risk of MACE.

Conclusions

In AR, an LGE extent > 2.6% predicts MACE better than LGE presence alone. Furthermore, non-ischemic predominant subendocardial-involved LGE is independently associated with MACE. The coexistence of both features further amplifies the risk of MACE.

title: Single-Ventricle Physiology as a Dominant Determinant of Mortality, Resource Utilization, and Pulmonary Vein Reintervention in Total Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Connection: A Large Multicenter Study.
authorString: Turner D, Mehdizadeh-Shrifi A, Lee B, Ahmed HF, Chappell G, Batlivala S, Lehenbauer D, Ashfaq A, Morales DLS, Ricci M.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
journal.title: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
journal.isoabbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg

abstractText: BackgroundChildren with single ventricle (SV) physiology and total anomalous pulmonary venous connection (TAPVC) face high surgical risk. Despite advances in single ventricle care, survival in SV/TAPVC patients has plateaued. We investigated multicenter outcomes, reintervention rates, and healthcare burden in this complex population.MethodsThe Pediatric Health Information System was queried for TAPVC repairs (2015-2024). Infants were stratified by single-ventricle versus biventricular (BiV) anatomy.ResultsAmong 1258 infants undergoing TAPVC repair, 10% (N = 120) had SV and 90% (N = 1138) had BiV anatomy. SV/TAPVC patients showed higher prematurity (11% [13/120] vs 8% [91/1138], P < .001), low birthweight (14% [17/120] vs 9% [102/1138], P < .001), and neurologic abnormalities (13% [16/120] vs 5% [60/1138], P < .001). Postoperatively, SV/TAPVC had increased delayed sternal closure (11% [13/120] vs 4% [45/1138], P < .001) and ECMO use (7% [8/120] vs 3% [34/1138], P < .001). Healthcare burden was substantially higher in SV/TAPVC children: 5-fold longer hospitalizations (102 vs 29 days, P < .001), 6-fold more hospital visits (6 vs 1, P < .001), and 5-fold higher costs ($1,019,390 vs $259,303, P < .001). Survival at 1 year after repair was severely reduced (SV: 52% vs BiV: 88%, P < .001). Pulmonary vein reinterventions were substantially higher (12-month cumulative incidence: 32% vs 5%, P < .001). Single ventricle physiology was a strong mortality predictor (HR: 3.69, P < .001), particularly pulmonary atresia with intact septum (HR: 6.62, P < .001) and hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HR: 4.42, P < .001).ConclusionsSingle ventricle physiology remains a powerful predictor of adverse outcome in children with TAPVC, with 1-year survival rates approaching 50%. Children with SV/TAPVC face substantially longer hospitalizations, higher reintervention rates, higher hospital visits, and overall 5-fold greater healthcare costs.

title: Infracardiac and mixed total anomalous pulmonary venous connection: Surgical challenges and practical solutions.
authorString: Alsoufi B, Alsoufi M.
abstractText: BackgroundTotal anomalous pulmonary venous connection (TAPVC) remains a complex congenital cardiac malformation. Despite improved survival, infracardiac and mixed variants continue to carry disproportionate risks of early mortality, postoperative pulmonary venous obstruction (PVO), and reintervention.MethodsThis narrative review examines the anatomic and technical challenges of infracardiac and mixed TAPVC, mechanisms and consequences of postoperative PVO, and contemporary strategies to reduce residual or recurrent obstruction, with particular emphasis on primary sutureless repair and anatomy-specific surgical approaches.ResultsContemporary operative mortality for TAPVC is approximately 3-10% but remains higher in patients with preoperative obstruction. Postoperative PVO occurs in approximately 5-15% and is an important determinant of reintervention and late mortality. In infracardiac TAPVC, obstruction may occur along with the descending vertical vein, producing severe pulmonary venous hypertension and physiologic instability. Mixed TAPVC presents additional challenges from heterogeneous drainage, multiple or small confluences, isolated veins, and complex geometry. Primary sutureless repair has evolved from treatment of recurrent PVO to a preventive strategy in high-risk primary TAPVC by avoiding pulmonary venous suture lines and facilitating wide, unobstructed drainage.ConclusionsManagement of infracardiac and mixed TAPVC requires an anatomy-specific approach focused on preventing postoperative PVO. Important strategies include selective preoperative stabilization, primary sutureless reconstruction in high-risk anatomy, a no-touch approach to selected isolated veins in 3 + 1 mixed TAPVC, and complete reconstruction of the cardiac component when appropriate.

title: Beyond conventional anthropometry: Muscle-related indicators and muscle strength in adults with congenital heart disease: A retrospective study with a comparison group.
authorString: de Sousa HRP, Pinho CPS.

journal.title: Nutrition in clinical practice : official publication of the American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition

abstractText: Anthropometric characteristics and muscle strength remain insufficiently characterized in adults with congenital heart disease (CHD). The aim of the study was to characterize anthropometric indicators and muscle strength in hospitalized adults with CHD and examine differences according to cardiac lesion complexity. Exploratory comparisons with adults without CHD were performed as secondary analyses. This cross-sectional study included 109 hospitalized adults with CHD and an external convenience group of 115 adults without CHD. Body mass index (BMI), mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC), triceps skinfold thickness (TSF), mid-arm muscle circumference (MAMC), arm muscle area (AMA), corrected arm muscle area (cAMA), and handgrip strength (HGS) were assessed. Cardiac defects were classified as mild, moderate, or complex. Associations of lesion complexity and previous cardiac surgery with anthropometric indicators and HGS were examined using multivariable linear regression. Comparisons with adults without CHD were conducted as exploratory analyses using the same approach. Among adults with CHD, 57.8% had mild, 24.8% moderate, and 17.4% complex defects. Lesion complexity was associated with MAMC (P = 0.032); participants with complex defects had lower MAMC than those with mild defects (B = -2.44 cm; 95% CI: -4.26 to -0.63). Previous cardiac surgery was associated with higher BMI, MUAC, MAMC, and AMA. In adjusted exploratory comparisons, adults with CHD had lower weight, height, BMI, MUAC, MAMC, AMA, and HGS than adults without CHD, whereas TSF was similar. Values below reference ranges for BMI, MUAC, MAMC, cAMA, and HGS were more frequent in CHD. Greater lesion complexity was associated with lower MAMC, whereas previous cardiac surgery was associated with higher BMI, MUAC, MAMC, and AMA. Muscle-related anthropometric measures and HGS may provide complementary information beyond body size and adiposity in adults with CHD.

title: Impact of Socioeconomic Status and Rurality on the Rate of Prenatal Detection of Major and Critical Congenital Heart Disease in Western Australia.
authorString: Hurwitz SB, O'Connell E, MacDonald B, Kothari D, Dickinson JE, Yim D.

journal.title: Journal of paediatrics and child health

abstractText:
Aim

Prenatal diagnosis of congenital heart disease (CHD) is associated with reduced infant morbidity and mortality. Location and subsequent socioeconomic status influence rates and timing of prenatal diagnoses of CHD. We investigated the impact of socioeconomic status and rurality on the rate of prenatal diagnosis of critical and major CHD in Western Australia (WA).

Methods

This retrospective cross-sectional study reviewed all critical (surgical intervention ≤ 30 days of life) and major (surgical intervention ≤ 1 year of life) CHD in WA between 2017 and 2021. Patients were identified from the WA Fetal Cardiology and Perth Children's Hospital Cardiology Databases. Clinical records were used to identify diagnoses, outcomes, postcode, rurality (via the Modified Monash Model [MMM]) and socioeconomic status (Socio-Economic Indexes for Areas [SEIFA] Index of Relative Socio-economic Disadvantage). Postcode was used to estimate SEIFA index and MMM rurality.

Results

There were 478 cases with major CHD; 282 (59%) were prenatally diagnosed, of which 268 cases were critical CHD, with a 77% detection rate. Seventy-four percent of patients were from metropolitan areas. The distribution of SEIFA decile (p = 0.15) and MMM (p = 0.09) were not significantly different between pre- and postnatal groups. The diagnosis rate of univentricular CHD was 94% (n = 102) and 49% (n = 180) for CHD undergoing biventricular repair.

Conclusion

Critical CHD increases the likelihood of prenatal diagnosis in WA; however, rurality and socioeconomic status were not found to influence diagnosis rates. Further studies are needed to review the availability of obstetric services in rural communities to ensure equitable healthcare.

title: Abdominal Pain as the First Presentation of Severe Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction and Left Ventricular Thrombus in a Young Asymptomatic Patient: A Diagnostic Interception.
authorString: Alarfaj MO, Alsuwailem BS, Aljeezan MK, Alhlibi BS, Haya MMB, Alnaaim AA, AlTaweel MO.
abstractText: A young, physically active patient with no cardiac symptoms presented with abdominal pain and was found, through incidental findings of elevated BNP, cardiomegaly, and new ECG changes, to have severe HFrEF with a left ventricular apical thrombus. Early cardiac evaluation changed management and led to complete thrombus resolution.

title: Physiological within-day Variation in Lipoprotein(a): Is a Once-in-a-lifetime Measurement Sufficient for Cardiovascular Risk Evaluation?
authorString: Song S, Hirayama S, Inaba H, Hori A, Horiuchi Y, Ichikawa Y, Kimura Y, Fukushima Y, Ueno T, Uehara Y, Miida T.
abstractText:
Aims

Lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) is a strong risk factor for cardiovascular events, independent of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C). Because the Lp(a) concentration is largely determined by genetic factors, some dyslipidemia guidelines recommend a once-in-a-lifetime measurement of Lp(a). Furthermore, a non-fasting lipid profile assessment is allowed for initial screening of dyslipidemia. Although the LDL-C concentration decreases slightly throughout the day, the within-day variation of Lp(a) remains unknown. We aimed to investigate whether the Lp(a) concentration remains stable throughout the day.

Methods

Lp(a) concentrations were measured at seven time points throughout the day in 34 patients using a latex turbidimetric immunoassay. The Lp(a) values are expressed in molar units, which are equivalent to those determined by a mass spectrometry-based reference measurement procedure.

Results

We found that the Lp(a) concentrations decreased by 2.9±5.2 nmol/L at 14:00 (p＜0.05), 3.6±4.8 nmol/L at 20:00 (p＜0.001), and 2.9±5.1 nmol/L at 24:00 (p＜0.05). The mean percent Lp(a) decreased significantly at 17:30 (-6.2±0.1%) and 24:00 (-7.0±0.1%) from the fasting level.

Conclusion

The Lp(a) concentration decreases slightly, but significantly, throughout the day. Considering physiological variations, it is preferable to re-evaluate the Lp(a) concentration in those with a borderline elevation.

title: Associations of Albuminuria and eGFR with Stiffness Parameter β in Type 2 Diabetes.
authorString: Nakatani S, Morioka T, Kakutani Y, Miyamoto S, Natsuki Y, Miki Y, Kurajoh M, Nakatani S, Emoto M.
abstractText:
Aims

The stiffness parameter β is a clinical index of arterial stiffness that reflects systemic atherosclerosis. Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major cardiovascular risk factor in type 2 diabetes; however, it remains unclear whether a reduced kidney function or albuminuria is more strongly associated with arterial stiffness. This study examined the relative associations of estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) with stiffness parameter β in patients with type 2 diabetes.

Methods

This cross-sectional study enrolled 1,924 patients with type 2 diabetes. The stiffness parameter β was assessed at the common carotid artery using ultrasonography.

Results

The participants were 58.8% male, with a median age of 63 years and a median HbA1c level of 8.3%. According to univariate analyses, stiffness parameter β was significantly correlated with both eGFR and UACR. However, after adjusting for conventional cardiovascular risk factors, stiffness parameter β remained independently associated with UACR, whereas no independent association was observed with eGFR. Similar findings were observed when eGFR and albuminuria were analyzed according to the CKD categories. No significant interactions were observed between UACR and either age or body mass index in relation to stiffness parameter β.

Conclusions

In patients with type 2 diabetes, albuminuria, but not eGFR, was independently associated with stiffness parameter β after multivariable adjustment. These findings suggest that albuminuria may serve as a marker of local carotid arterial stiffening and vascular injury.

title: Mitophagy and ER-phagy in doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity: mechanisms, crosstalk, and therapeutic implications.
authorString: Tian Y, Chang A, Guo Z, Zhou H, Chang X, Wu J.
abstractText:
Background

Doxorubicin (DOX) is a key chemotherapeutic agent for hematologic malignancies and many solid tumors, but its clinical use is limited by doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity (DIC). DIC may present as subclinical myocardial injury, arrhythmias, left ventricular dysfunction, cardiomyopathy, or heart failure. DOX can disrupt organelle function through topoisomerase IIβ (Top2β)-mediated DNA damage and transcriptional stress, oxidative stress, disrupted iron homeostasis, and calcium imbalance. Mitochondrial and endoplasmic/sarcoplasmic reticulum (ER/SR) injury are therefore central pathological features of DIC.

Aim of review

This review summarizes current evidence on mitophagy and ER-phagy in DIC, with emphasis on discrepancies in reported findings across different experimental settings, potential crosstalk mechanisms, and the translational limitations of targeting these pathways for cardioprotection.

Key scientific concepts

Current studies suggest that mitophagy in DIC follows a checkpoint-dependent pattern. Depending on DOX dose, exposure duration, and lysosomal degradative capacity, mitophagy may remove damaged mitochondria, but it may also worsen mitochondrial injury when initiation is insufficient, activation is excessive, or flux is stalled. In contrast, direct evidence for ER-phagy in DIC remains limited. This evidence is mainly derived from CCPG1-mediated protective ER-phagy in chronic fractionated DOX models and FAM134B-associated ER-phagy-related injury signals in acute high-dose injury models. Thus, the functional divergence of ER-phagy in DIC requires confirmation in additional experimental models with rigorous autophagic flux assessment. Mitochondria-associated ER membranes (MAMs) may coordinate mitophagy and ER-phagy by regulating calcium transfer, autophagosome formation, and receptor localization. Overall, current evidence does not support indiscriminate activation or inhibition of mitophagy and ER-phagy. Instead, future interventions may need to preserve flux-complete organelle clearance while avoiding excessive or stalled autophagic signaling. In addition, this framework may help generate research hypotheses that integrate cardioprotection with preservation of antitumor efficacy. However, most evidence comes from cell and animal studies, and further validation in human myocardial tissue and confirmation of cardiac target engagement are still needed.

title: Postoperative complications following carotid endarterectomy are differentially impacted by sex and plaque instability.
authorString: Kuate Defo A, Gasbarrino K, Daskalopoulou SS.
abstractText:
Background

This study aimed to provide novel evidence on the role of sex and plaque instability in post-carotid endarterectomy outcomes. Current clinical guidelines regarding recommendation for carotid endarterectomy rely solely on grade of stenosis and cerebrovascular symptomatology, despite emerging evidence emphasizing the role of sex and plaque instability in determining postoperative outcomes.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective analysis of an ongoing cohort study of males and females undergoing carotid endarterectomy for clinical indications. We performed multivariable binary logistic regression to examine the relationship of biological sex and plaque instability with postoperative outcomes.

Results

Data of 394 participants (31% female) were analyzed. Plaque instability was independently associated with decreased odds of hemorrhagic complications at 1 month and 1 year post-surgery, as well as with decreased respiratory complications at 1 year post-surgery. Plaque features accounting for these associations were lipid core, cap infiltration, and plaque inflammation. Female sex was independently associated with increased odds of restenosis at 1 month and 1 year post-surgery. Additionally, females with unstable plaques had more cerebrovascular complications at 1 month than males with unstable plaques, and females with stable plaques had double the odds of any complication at 1 month compared with males with unstable plaques.

Conclusions

Our findings show that sex and plaque instability differentially impact post-endarterectomy outcomes, with males with unstable plaques experiencing the least postoperative complications. Sex and plaque instability may therefore be important factors that play a role in postoperative complications, highlighting their importance in the context of surgical decision-making.

title: Association between increased superficial calcification clusters in carotid atherosclerosis and cardiovascular events after carotid artery stenting: A retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Zhu J, Tang H, Ding Y, Han T, Yan D, Shen T, Tang X, Guo D.
abstractText:
Background

The role of calcification in carotid atherosclerosis before and after carotid artery stenting (CAS) remains controversial. This study assessed the association between the extent of calcification in target carotid plaques and outcomes after CAS.

Methods

A total of 292 subjects with carotid stenosis who underwent CAS were retrospectively enrolled. Follow-up for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) was conducted via outpatient visits and telephone. Ultimately, 211 subjects completed 2-year follow-up. Superficial calcification clusters were counted on CTA. Subjects with ≥4 superficial calcification clusters (n=24) were matched in a 1:4 ratio to those with <4 superficial calcification clusters (n=96). Sensitivity analysis was performed based on the matched cohort.

Results

Over a median follow-up of 1.92 years, 14 MACEs occurring more than 30 days after discharge were recorded. In univariate Cox analysis, symptom status (P= 0.0116), alcohol abuse (P= 0.0091), total number of calcification clusters (P= 0.0428), and number of superficial calcification clusters (P= 0.0022) were significantly associated with MACEs. In bivariate analyses, the number of superficial calcification clusters maintained a reasonably good association with MACEs. In sensitivity analysis, superficial calcification clusters remained significantly associated with MACE when loss to follow-up was classified as MACE (P= 0.0256, HR= 1.2548, 95% CI 1.0281-1.5315) or as no MACE (P= 0.0265, HR= 1.4948, 95% CI 1.0479-2.1323).

Conclusion

The number of superficial calcification clusters may independently serve as a prognostic risk factor in patients with carotid atherosclerosis undergoing CAS.

title: MicroRNA-145 hinders carotid plaque growth via suppression of tumor growth factor-β receptor type II and autophagy.
authorString: Jiao Y, Ma G, Ma J, Yuan F, Wu Z, Di W, Huang X, Huang Y, Duan Y, Liu J, Lei H.

journal.title: Biochimica et biophysica acta. General subjects

abstractText: Plaque erosion is increasingly recognized as a critical pathological mechanism in acute coronary syndrome. In this study, we found that microRNA-145 (miR-145) levels were significantly reduced in plaques with grade III-IV stenosis compared with controls. Using an apoE<sup>-</sup>/<sup>-</sup> mouse model fed a high-cholesterol diet, we demonstrated that inhibition of miR-145 with antagomiR-145 increased plaque volume and elevated LC3-II expression, a marker of autophagy. Transmission electron microscopy further confirmed a greater abundance of autophagosomes in carotid atherosclerotic plaques from antagomiR-145-treated mice. Mechanistically, miR-145 suppressed both transforming growth factor-β receptor type II (TGFβR-II) expression and autophagy in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). Silencing TGFβR-II with specific siRNA recapitulated the effects of antagomiR-145 in cultured VSMCs and in vivo. Collectively, these findings suggest that miR-145 may protect against carotid plaque progression by downregulating TGFβR-II and limiting autophagy.

title: What every intensivist should know about dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction.
authorString: Rola P, Augustin K.
abstractText: Dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO) is an underrecognized, load dependent cause of hemodynamic instability in critically ill patients. Although classically associated with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, it frequently occurs in the ICU in settings such as septic shock, hypovolemia, postoperative states, and right ventricular failure. Standard shock therapies, including inotropes and afterload reduction, may paradoxically worsen obstruction and lead to escalating hemodynamic instability. Bedside echocardiography is central to diagnosis, typically revealing a small hyperdynamic left ventricle and a late-peaking Doppler profile. Management focuses on restoring preload, increasing afterload, and reducing excessive contractility. In some patients, LVOTO is secondary to right ventricular failure, requiring targeted right ventricular support. Dynamic LVOTO is a reversible and often iatrogenic cause of shock. Early recognition and physiology-guided management can rapidly improve hemodynamics and prevent harmful therapeutic escalation.

title: Exploratory Analysis of the Innate Immune System in Aortic Stenosis Patients With and Without ASCVD.
authorString: van Broekhoven A, van Doorn EPM, Broeders W, Cetinyurek-Yavuz A, Zegers ES, Netea MG, Vonk ABA, van Royen N, Niessen HWM, Cornel JH, Riksen NP, El Messaoudi S.
abstractText: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) leads to aortic stenosis (AS) through inflammation and fibro-calcific remodeling. Although CAVD and atherosclerosis share features, not all patients with AS develop atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), suggesting mechanistic heterogeneity. This case-control study evaluated inflammatory profiles and valvular remodeling in 128 patients with AS (59.4% with ASCVD) and 105 controls. Immune cell composition and monocyte markers were analyzed by flow cytometry, whereas cytokine production was assessed after peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) stimulation. Both AS groups had higher interleukin (IL)-6, leukocyte, monocyte, and neutrophil counts than controls, with lower monocyte human leukocyte antigen-DR isotype and higher C-C chemokine receptor (CCR)2 expression. Cytokine responses were also elevated, particularly in AS patients with ASCVD. They also showed higher IL-6 concentrations, higher proportions of classical monocytes, and lower intermediate and non-classical monocytes compared with patients without ASCVD. Overall, AS was associated with a pro-inflammatory monocyte phenotype and function, most prominently in patients with ASCVD. ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT04717219.

title: Lipoprotein(a) and long-term revascularization burden: a recurrent-event analysis of the UK Biobank.
authorString: Cesaro A, Calabrò P, Jamialahmadi O, Pugliese N, Flagiello V, Barreby E, Mancina RM, Romeo S.
abstractText:
Aims

To investigate whether elevated Lp(a) is independently associated with cumulative coronary, peripheral, and carotid revascularization burden in a primary prevention cohort.

Methods and results

We analysed 237 729 UK Biobank participants of European ancestry free of ASCVD at baseline, followed for a median of 14.1 years. Lp(a) was analysed using the ESC/EAS 2025 threshold of 105 nmol/L and continuously (per 50 nmol/L increment). The primary outcome was the total number of coronary, peripheral, and carotid revascularization procedures per person. Given the genetically determined, lifelong nature of Lp(a) exposure, to capture the full sequence of procedures over time, rather than time-to-first-event alone, we applied recurrent-event statistical models, including the Andersen-Gill model, negative binomial regression, and the Prentice-Williams-Peterson gap-time model. Overall, 10 731 revascularization procedures occurred in 237 729 participants. The proportion undergoing ≥1 procedure was higher with Lp(a) ≥ 105 vs. <105 nmol/L (4.36% vs. 2.96%), with larger differences for ≥2 (1.53% vs. 0.95%) and ≥3 procedures (0.36% vs. 0.18%). In Andersen-Gill analysis, Lp(a) ≥ 105 nmol/L was associated with a higher revascularization rate (HR 1.50, 1.42-1.60), with a 55% higher rate of revascularization procedures during follow-up by negative binomial regression (IRR 1.55, 1.45-1.65). The association was strongest for the first procedure (HR 1.48, 1.40-1.56), attenuated for the second (HR 1.28, 1.09-1.50), and non-significant for the third (HR 1.23, 0.94-1.62). Findings were consistent across coronary and peripheral territories.

Conclusion

In this large primary prevention cohort, elevated Lp(a) was independently associated with a higher long-term revascularization burden across multiple vascular territories. The association was robust for coronary, supportive for peripheral, and inconclusive for carotid revascularization owing to limited statistical power. These findings, derived from recurrent-event methodology, provide a more complete quantification of Lp(a)-associated cardiovascular procedural risk than time-to-first-event analyses alone.

title: MD-1 Deficiency Mitigates Atherosclerosis by Inhibiting NLRP3 Inflammasome Activation via cGAS-STING Dependent Pathway in Macrophages.
authorString: Zhao F, Jin Z, Cai Z, Zhang Q, He T, Kong X, Chen M, Lu Z, Hu X, Cheng WL.
abstractText: MD-1 plays significant roles in various pathological processes closely associated with cardiovascular diseases through its functions in different cell types. However, the critical effects and molecular mechanisms mediated by MD-1 in macrophages involved in the development of atherosclerosis remain elusive. In this study, we observed that the expression of MD-1 was upregulated in atherosclerotic plaques derived from human carotid arteries, as analysed through the Gene Expression Omnibus database. Additionally, MD-1 expression was elevated in the aortas of hyperlipidemic ApoE-deficient mice and in oxidised low-density lipoprotein-stimulated bone marrow-derived macrophages, as demonstrated by RT-PCR and western blot analyses. Furthermore, MD-1 expression exhibited strong co-localisation with macrophages, as confirmed by double immunofluorescence staining. Notably, MD-1<sup>-/-</sup>ApoE<sup>-/-</sup> mice subjected to a high-fat diet displayed a significant reduction in atherosclerotic plaques throughout the entire aorta, aortic root, and brachiocephalic arteries. Moreover, the plaques in MD-1<sup>-/-</sup>ApoE<sup>-/-</sup> mice were more stable, characterised by a decreased necrotic core size, reduced macrophage infiltration, and lower lipid deposition, alongside an increased accumulation of collagen and smooth muscle cells. Bone marrow transplantation from MD-1<sup>-/-</sup>ApoE<sup>-/-</sup> mice to ApoE<sup>-/-</sup> mice markedly attenuated the development of atherosclerosis. This attenuation was associated with an enhanced anti-inflammatory macrophage phenotype and a reduction in pro-inflammatory macrophage polarisation. Similar effects of MD-1 ablation on macrophage behaviour were also observed in vitro. Mechanistically, MD-1 deficiency inhibited the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes-TANK-binding kinase 1-IRF3 pathway, thereby attenuating NLRP3 inflammasome activation in macrophages. However, the use of the STING agonist DMXAA counteracted the effects of MD-1 deficiency on macrophage polarisation. Our findings reveal MD-1 promotes pro-inflammatory (M1-like) macrophage polarisation in atherosclerosis by inhibiting NLRP3 inflammasome activation via a cGAS-STING dependent pathway. These results suggest that MD-1 neutralisation could be a potential therapeutic strategy for atherosclerosis management.

title: Pre-Procedural Prediction of Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction Normalization After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
authorString: Hida Y, Imamura T, Ueno H, Kinugawa K, Yamamoto M, Tokuda T, Shimura T, Shirai S, Ishizu K, Ohno Y, Yashima F, Naganuma T, Watanabe Y, Yamanaka F, Nakazawa G, Noguchi M, Izumo M, Asami M, Nishina H, Suzuyama H, Yamasaki K, Nishioka K, Hachinohe D, Fuku Y, Otsuka T, Hayashida K, OCEAN‐TAVI Investigators.

journal.title: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstractText:
Background

Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is an established therapy for severe aortic stenosis. Among patients with left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction, recovery of LV function after TAVI is heterogeneous, and reliable tools for pre-procedural risk stratification and patient counseling remain limited.

Aims

We sought to identify simple pre-procedural predictors of complete LV functional recovery after TAVI and to develop a clinically applicable risk score to support patient counseling and post-procedural management.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed patients with severe aortic stenosis and baseline LV ejection fraction (LVEF) < 40% enrolled in a large multicenter registry in Japan. The primary outcome was complete LVEF normalization (LVEF > 50%) at 1 year after TAVI. Independent predictors were identified using multivariable logistic regression in a derivation cohort, and an exploratory weighted score was constructed. The score was preliminarily assessed in a separate single-center cohort.

Results

The derivation cohort comprised 177 patients (median age 84 years; 44% women), of whom 94 (53%) achieved LVEF normalization. Lower body mass index (odds ratio [OR] 0.86, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.77-0.95; p = 0.004), higher aortic valve peak velocity (OR 2.45, 95% CI 1.40-4.29; p = 0.002), and smaller LV end-diastolic diameter (OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.88-0.98; p = 0.020) were independently associated with LVEF normalization. The derived score stratified patients into low-, intermediate-, and high-probability groups (15%, 45%, and 71%, respectively; p < 0.001), with consistent discrimination in the validation cohort.

Conclusions

A simple exploratory score incorporating body mass index, transvalvular peak velocity, and LV size was associated with the probability of complete LV functional recovery after TAVI. This pre-procedural tool may facilitate patient counseling, expectation-setting, and identification of patients who may require closer heart failure follow-up after TAVI. It should not be used to determine eligibility for TAVI.

title: It Is Possible to Save the Kidney With Renal Artery Occlusion Without Autotransplantation: A Case Report.
authorString: Şafak A, Karakaya E, Demir İ, Baskın E, Yıldırım S, Sezgin A, Haberal M.
abstractText: Renal artery stenosis is a rare but important cause of renovascular hypertension in children that may lead to malignant hypertension and renal failure. A 13-year-old girl presented with malignant hypertension and acute kidney injury, and imaging demonstrated occlusion of both renal arteries. Endovascular recanalization was unsuccessful because of complete, heavily fibrotic occlusions involving a long segment of the right renal artery extending to the hilum, leaving no suitable distal artery for reconstruction, and a 7.3-mm segment of the left renal artery at its aortic origin. To preserve renal function, surgical revascularization was performed by in situ reimplantation of the left renal artery into the aorta, without autotransplantation. Postoperatively, renal function recovered, the proteinuria present at admission regressed, and the patient became normotensive without antihypertensive medication.

title: THE CLINICAL PROFILE OF RUPTURE: A 19-YEAR CASE-CONTROL STUDY OF ABDOMINAL AORTIC ANEURYSMS.
authorString: Río Solá MLD, Casaseca CT, Jiménez de la Caja M, Fernández SP, Rodríguez SA.
abstractText:
Objective

To identify factors associated with ruptured infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) presentation and quantify ruptures below current sex-specific elective repair thresholds.

Methods

This retrospective case-control study compared patients presenting with ruptured infrarenal AAA with a contemporaneous comparison group undergoing elective infrarenal AAA repair. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associations with ruptured presentation. The primary model included maximum aneurysm diameter, age, female sex, and calendar year; the extended model additionally included hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and dyslipidemia. Discrimination was evaluated using optimism-corrected area under the curve (AUC).

Results

Among 394 patients with infrarenal AAA, 194 presented with rupture and 200 underwent elective repair. Median diameter was 80.0 versus 53.0 mm (P < .001), and women comprised 10.9% versus 3.0% (P = .002), respectively. Diameter per 10-mm increase (odds ratio [OR], 2.19; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.84-2.61) and female sex (OR, 4.72; 95% CI, 1.49-14.94) were independently associated with ruptured presentation. Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.836 for diameter alone, 0.832 for the primary model (diameter, age, female sex, and calendar year), and 0.840 for the extended model (primary model plus hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and dyslipidemia). Sixteen of 160 ruptures (10.0%) occurred below sex-specific thresholds.

Conclusions

Diameter was the dominant factor associated with ruptured presentation, but female sex remained independently associated. These findings support diameter-based practice while highlighting the need for prospective, sex-aware, multiparametric risk assessment.

title: Prevalence of Guideline-Recommended Genetic Testing in Patients at Risk for Heritable Thoracic Aortic Disease.
authorString: Robledo A, O'Leary S, Pedrosa DDT, Penalver J, Sancassani R.
abstractText: Heritable thoracic aortic diseases (HTAD) include genetic conditions that increase risk of thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection. The 2022 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) guidelines recommend genetic testing for at-risk individuals, but real-world uptake remains unclear. We evaluated adherence to testing recommendations and demographic differences across major HTAD risk cohorts. We conducted a retrospective study using the TriNetX Research Network (2005-2025). Three guideline-based cohorts were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes: (1) thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, (2) family history of thoracic aortic disease, and (3) non-thoracic arterial aneurysms.
