Genetic testing was defined by ICD-10-CM codes for genetic screening or susceptibility. Testing prevalence was stratified by age, sex, race, and ethnicity, and annual testing incidence (2005-2024) was evaluated. Among 57,935 patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, 1,205 (2.09%) underwent genetic testing. Among 2,811,862 patients with a family history of thoracic aortic disease, 66,699 (2.38%) received testing. Among 347,000 patients with non-thoracic arterial aneurysms, 4,913 (1.42%) underwent testing. Testing was consistently higher in females than males and varied across age groups. Annual testing incidence increased over time but remained <0.6% by 2024. In conclusion, genetic testing for HTAD remains markedly underutilized, with < 2.5% of at-risk patients tested despite guideline recommendations, highlighting persistent implementation gaps and the need to improve equitable access to genetic evaluation.

title: Strain-Based Assessment of Post-TAVR Left Bundle Branch Block in Bicuspid Aortic Valve Using Patient-Specific Computational Modeling.
authorString: Anam S, Kovarovic B, Parikh P, Hamdan A, Haj-Ali R, Bluestein D.
abstractText:
Purpose

Post-transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) left bundle branch block (LBBB) is the most common post-TAVR cardiac conduction abnormality (CCA), particularly in bicuspid aortic valve (BAV). Prior computational studies evaluated generalized CCA risk but did not quantify LBBB-specific mechanical injury or compare self-expanding (SE) and balloon-expandable (BE) devices in BAV. This proof-of-concept study established a patient-specific computational framework to (1) quantify mechanical stretch in the left bundle branch (LBB)-adjacent region, (2) identify a preliminary, cohort-specific strain-based separation value associated with post-TAVR LBBB, and (3) compare device-related LBBB risk trends between SE and BE devices.

Methods

Cardiac CT scans from six type I BAV TAVR patients were analyzed (two with LBBB and four without CCA). Patient-specific finite element models incorporated anatomy and leaflet calcification. The LBB region was defined using membranous septum length and anatomical landmarks. Simulations reproduced implantation of deployed SE devices and virtual BE devices at standardized depth. Area-weighted logarithmic strain (LE), contact pressure, oversizing index, eccentricity index, and expansion metrics were computed.

Results

LBB-adjacent LE showed clear separation (0.15-0.24 in LBBB vs. 0.03-0.11 without CCA), with 0.11 as a preliminary cohort-specific separation value. Mean LE was higher with SE than BE devices (0.11 vs. 0.08). Contact pressure showed no consistent association with outcome, suggesting that LE differences reflect multiple contributing factors.

Conclusion

In this six-patient cohort, LBB-adjacent strain clearly separated LBBB from No-LBBB cases, whereas contact pressure showed no consistent relationship with outcome. Larger cohorts and sensitivity analyses are needed to establish its clinical utility for BAV TAVR risk stratification or device selection.

title: A Real-World Clinical Study on Computed Tomography Pulmonary Angiography-Based Artificial Intelligence-Driven Risk Stratification in Pulmonary Embolism.
authorString: Li Z, Zheng J, Yang S, Zhang B, Hou W, Tian Q, Zhu S, Xiao Y, Zhao W, Huang X, Jin C, Jian Z, Wei Y, Shi F, Yang J, Liu Z.
abstractText:
Purpose

To evaluate the efficacy of a computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA)-based artificial intelligence system for use in the clinical setting to stratify the risk of pulmonary embolism (PE).

Materials and methods

This study enrolled 115 patients diagnosed with PE based on positive CTPA reports at our institution between January 1 and October 10, 2023. Cases were classified as relatively high-risk or low-risk according to the 2019 ESC Guidelines. Two radiologists independently and blindly measured risk-related imaging parameters, including main pulmonary artery diameter (MPAD), ascending aortic diameter (AAD), right and left ventricular diameters (RVD, LVD), the right-to-left ventricular diameter ratio (RVD/LVD ratio), pulmonary artery obstruction index (PAOI), and pulmonary embolism volume (PEV). These results were compared with those from the automated artificial intelligence (AI) system to assess consistency.

Results

The agreement (intraclass correlation coefficients, ICCs) of MPAD, AAD, RVD, PAOI, LVD, and RVD/LVD ratio between AI system and manual measurements were 0.94, 0.79, 0.78, 0.80, 0.54, and 0.48, respectively. Among the AI-extracted covariates, an RVD/LVD ratio >1.2 showed good performance in identifying relatively high-risk PE cases, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.771. The AI model incorporating all covariates achieved an AUC of 0.848 for classifying high-risk PE.

Conclusions

The CTPA-based AI system can rapidly extract the key imaging parameters relevant to PE risk stratification in real-world clinical settings, significantly reducing the CTPA interpretation time and improving evaluation efficiency.

title: Ebselen attenuates selected cardiac and vascular alterations in rats exposed to a cholesterol/cholic acid diet.
authorString: Ozhan O, Demez S, Tasdemir S, Ermis N, Yildiz A, Turkoz Y, Vardi N, Soysal K, Parlakpinar H.
abstractText: Hypercholesterolemia (HCT) is a major risk factor for cardiovascular diseases and promotes myocardial and vascular injury primarily through oxidative stress (OS)-mediated mechanisms. Ebselen (EBS), a glutathione peroxidase-mimetic antioxidant, has been associated with attenuation of tissue injury in several experimental OS-related models; however, its short-term effects on selected outcomes in HCT-associated cardiovascular damage remain unclear. Twenty-four male Wistar albino rats were randomly assigned to three groups: Control, cholesterol/cholic-acid diet (HCT), and the same diet treated with EBS (HCT+EBS). Rats in the HCT-designated groups received a diet containing 2% cholesterol and 0.5% cholic acid for six weeks; serum lipids were not measured. EBS (10 mg/kg/day, intraperitoneal) was administered during the final week. Hemodynamic and electrocardiographic parameters, serum injury biomarkers, myocardial oxidative-stress parameters, and cardiac and descending-aortic histopathology were assessed. Relative to Control, the cholesterol/cholic-acid diet group designated HCT showed higher myocardial lipid peroxidation, lower superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity, higher serum myoglobin and lactate dehydrogenase, and more severe cardiac and aortic histopathological alterations. Compared directly with HCT, HCT+EBS showed lower myocardial malondialdehyde, higher SOD activity, lower injury biomarkers, and less severe histopathological alterations. Because serum lipids were not measured, these differences cannot be separated from a possible EBS-associated difference in lipid profile. EBS administration also induced a marked hypotensive response: systolic blood pressure was significantly lower in HCT+EBS than in both HCT and Control. Short-term EBS administration was associated with selected biochemical and histopathological differences in rats exposed to a cholesterol/cholic-acid diet. However, the lipid phenotype was not confirmed, and a possible EBS-associated difference in serum lipids cannot be excluded. Together with the absence of an EBS-only control group, this prevents attribution of the findings specifically to direct antioxidant actions of EBS or interpretation as therapeutic efficacy.

title: Circadian melatonin suppression and vitamin D deficiency disrupt aortic reactivity via MT1/MT2 and VDR-dependent mechanisms in rats.
authorString: Shekh RS, Maulood IM.

journal.title: Pflugers Archiv : European journal of physiology

abstractText: Circadian disruption and vitamin D deficiency (VDD) are increasingly prevalent and independently associated with cardiovascular dysfunction. However, their combined impact on vascular reactivity and receptor signaling remains insufficiently defined. This study investigated the independent and interactive effects of melatonin (MEL) suppression induced by continuous light (CL) or pinealectomy (Px) and VDD on vascular contractility, endothelial function, and MT1/vitamin D receptor (VDR) gene expression in rat thoracic aorta. Isolated aortic rings were subjected to cumulative concentration response curves for phenylephrine (PE) and acetylcholine (ACh). Pharmacodynamic parameters, potency (pD₂), maximal efficacy (Emax), and area under the curve (AUC) were calculated. MEL and calcitriol modulation with receptor antagonism was performed to determine receptor dependence. Relative MT1 and VDR mRNA expression was quantified using quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR). CL, Px, and VDD significantly enhanced PE-induced maximal contraction, with the combined deficiency groups exhibiting the greatest augmentation of α₁-adrenergic responsiveness. In contrast, ACh-induced relaxation was selectively impaired under dual-deficiency conditions, characterized by reduced Emax without major changes in pD2, indicating compromised endothelial efficacy rather than altered receptor sensitivity. MEL attenuated vasoconstriction and enhanced relaxation in a receptor-dependent manner, whereas calcitriol potentiated contractility through VDR signaling. Notably, combined CL + VDD produced marked upregulation of MT1 (~ 10-fold) and VDR (~ 108-fold), suggesting compensatory transcriptional remodeling. Circadian disruption and VDD synergistically promote vascular hyperreactivity and endothelial dysfunction. Their convergence amplifies α₁-adrenergic signaling while impairing nitric oxide (NO) mediated relaxation, identifying a mechanistic axis linking modern light exposure and hypovitaminosis D to heightened cardiovascular risk.

title: 4D Flow Acquisition Parameters as Technical Correlates of Hemodynamic Measurements: An Analysis of the multicenter Tetralogy of Fallot Registry of 4D flow Energetics and Kinetics (TREK).
authorString: Loke YH, Lee M, O'Hara R, Muegge W, Drews K, Gonzalez B, Axt-Fliedner R, Klein J, Friesen R, Dove M, Ta H, Kochav J, Goyal A, Schoeneberg L, Christopher A, Olivieri L, Krishnamurthy R, Balaras E, d'Udekem Y, Sotelo J, Taylor M, Fricke S, Bilionis I, Meyers BA, Capuano F.

journal.title: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance

abstractText:
Background

Advanced 4D flow cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) biomarkers such as kinetic energy (KE), vorticity (ω), and viscous energy loss (VEL) are increasingly used to characterize abnormal flow in repaired tetralogy of Fallot (rTOF), but their sensitivity to acquisition parameters including magnet vendor, sequence and signal quality has not been defined. We sought to evaluate the real-world variability in 4D flow sequences and technical correlates to 4D flow measurements of the aorta (Ao) and right ventricle, leveraging the multicenter Tetralogy of Fallot 4D flow Registry of Energetics and Kinetics (TREK).

Methods

This was a multicenter observational analysis of clinically acquired 4D flow CMR processed at a core laboratory. The technical analysis focused on systolic Ao and diastolic RV hemodynamic measurements of KE, ω and VEL. Time-resolved hemodynamic curves were summarized and compared across sequence/reconstruction type, contrast agents and sequence parameters. Interobserver variability was assessed with Bland-Altman analysis and intraclass correlation coefficients. Apparent signal-to-noise ratio (aSNR), apparent velocity-to-noise ratio (aVNR) and presence of velocity aliasing were also measured. Multivariable linear/logistic regression was used to identify acquisition parameters associated with aSNR, aVNR and aliasing. Multivariable linear regression models were constructed to evaluate associations of aSNR, aVNR, and aliasing with KE, ω, and VEL after adjustment for clinical covariates.

Results

The cohort included 345 datasets (295 rTOF studies and 50 controls). Sequence/reconstruction type, field strength, voxel volume, temporal resolution, and VENC were associated with aSNR and aVNR in multivariable models. Aliasing was associated with lower VENC. ω and VEL varied substantially across sequence/reconstruction type and contrast groups, whereas KE was comparatively more stable. In multivariable models, lower aSNR was associated with higher measured hemodynamic values after adjustment for clinical covariates, with stronger associations for ω and VEL rather than KE.

Conclusions

In a real-world multicenter 4D flow CMR registry, measured advanced hemodynamic biomarkers were associated with acquisition/reconstruction characteristics, apparent image quality, and residual aliasing. 4D Flow harmonization efforts should therefore extend beyond vendor types alone and explicitly account for aSNR, aVNR, and aliasing when interpreting derivative-based 4D flow measurements.

title: Weight-stratified analysis of the heterogeneous effects of miniaturized cardiopulmonary bypass on perioperative outcomes in children with congenital heart disease: A retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Ti Y, Wang Y, Zhang S, Zhou X, Liu H, Wang P, Yang H, Wu W, Zheng F, Zhang R, Du J, Chen B, Meng B, Hua Z.
abstractText: IntroductionMiniaturized cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) circuits may reduce intraoperative transfusion in pediatric cardiac surgery, but their effects across body weight categories remain unclear. This study compared transfusion and outcomes between conventional and miniaturized CPB circuits, emphasizing weight-stratified analyses.MethodsThis retrospective study included 3,196 pediatric cardiac surgery patients (2015-2024) receiving conventional (n = 548) or miniaturized (n = 2,648) circuits. Primary outcomes were transfusion avoidance during CPB, in the ICU, and combined. Secondary outcomes included ICU length of stay, mechanical ventilation, ultrafast-track extubation, 24-h chest tube drainage (normalized to mL/kg), and hematocrit dynamics. Multivariable logistic regression and subgroup analyses were performed.ResultsMiniaturized circuits improved CPB transfusion avoidance overall (47.9% vs. 29.0%; P < 0.001), especially in children weighing 3-9 kg (all P < 0.01). ICU transfusion avoidance was lower with miniaturized circuits overall (82.1% vs. 94.5%; P < 0.001), except in the 1-2 kg subgroup. Combined avoidance was higher with miniaturized circuits across 3-9 and 12-13 kg (all P < 0.05). ICU length of stay was shorter with miniaturized circuits in most weight subgroups, whereas it was prolonged in the 2-3 kg subgroup (150 vs. 75 h; P < 0.001). Overall mean 24-h chest tube drainage was significantly lower in the miniaturized group (9.05 ± 9.10 vs. 10.82 ± 7.76 mL/kg; P < 0.001); however, stratified analysis showed a significant increase only in the 4-5 kg subgroup (14.52 ± 7.88 vs. 11.96 ± 6.69 mL/kg; P = 0.046), with no differences in other weight strata. Multivariable analysis indicated that miniaturized circuits were an independent predictor of increased ICU transfusion risk (OR 2.59; P < 0.001), whereas higher body weight was associated with reduced risk (OR 0.76 per kg; P < 0.001).ConclusionsMiniaturized CPB circuits reduce intraoperative transfusion, particularly in children weighing 3-9 kg, but are associated with higher postoperative ICU transfusion and variable effects on chest tube drainage that are weight-dependent. The net benefit appears weight-dependent. These findings underscore the need for weight-stratified circuit selection, although further prospective studies are warranted.

title: The Fontan Procedure in Patients with Single-Lung Physiology: Insights from a Case Report and Scoping Review.
authorString: Guerrero-Becerra AF, Rubio-Duarte AF, Fontecha-Vargas EA, Márquez-Bohorquez D.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
journal.title: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
journal.isoabbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg

abstractText: The Fontan operation represents the third stage of single-ventricle palliation and requires optimal cardiovascular and pulmonary conditions to achieve success. We report a 6-year-old boy with tricuspid atresia, pulmonary atresia, and functional single-lung circulation secondary to severe left pulmonary artery (LPA) hypoplasia and disconnection after previous palliation. Following comprehensive clinical, hemodynamic, and anatomic evaluation, including unsuccessful attempts at LPA recruitment, the patient underwent an extracardiac fenestrated single-lung Fontan procedure. At 2 years of follow-up, he remained in good functional status without Fontan-related complications or the need for reintervention. Additionally, we present a scoping review of published case reports and case series of children with single-lung physiology undergoing the Fontan procedure, focusing on early and follow-up survival. This case, together with the available literature, suggests that single-lung Fontan completion may be feasible in carefully selected patients following meticulous multidisciplinary evaluation, although long-term outcomes remain uncertain.

title: Postnatal evolution of electrocardiographic parameters in preterm infants: a prospective longitudinal cohort study.
authorString: Satpathy SK, Choudhary S, Paswal CM, Singh AK, Gupta N, Soni JP, Kumar RK, Choudhary R.
abstractText:
Electrocardiography (ECG), an indispensable bedside tool in neonatal intensive care, complements echocardiography by providing assessment of cardiac rhythm and conduction, and when advanced imaging is unavailable, serves as a screening tool. Preterm birth alters cardiac and autonomic maturation. Applying term-based ECG norms may misclassify physiological findings in preterm. We aimed to characterise serial ECG maturation in preterms from birth to term-equivalent age and define gestational- and postnatal-age-specific patterns relevant to clinical interpretation. In this prospective cohort, infants between 28⁰/₇ and 36⁶/₇ weeks' gestation without congenital heart disease underwent serial 11-lead ECG recording within 24 h of birth, on day 7, day 28 and at term-equivalent age. Postnatal and gestation-based differences in ECG parameters were analysed and centile charts were generated. Among 249 infants (mean gestation-334/₇ weeks), 213 completed follow-up until term-equivalent age. ECG parameters demonstrated consistent maturation across time points. The mean QRS axis shifted leftward from 117° at birth to 82° at term-equivalent age (p < 0.001). PR-interval, QRS and P-wave duration remained stable across all time points. Mean QTc showed minimal overall change. Transient QTc prolongation occurred in 8.1% of infants and resolved by term-equivalent age. Right precordial R-wave amplitudes declined over time, whereas left precordial amplitudes increased. At term-equivalent age, very preterm infants exhibited a more leftward QRS axis compared with late preterm infants. Infants with bronchopulmonary dysplasia showed trends toward right ventricular dominance.

Conclusion

Preterm ECG findings are dynamic, gestation-dependent markers of cardiovascular transition. This study characterises longitudinal ECG maturation in preterms and provides reference values, supporting improved decision-making in preterm care.

What is known

• Electrocardiographic reference nomograms used in neonatal practice are primarily based on paediatric cohorts or cross-sectional studies of term infants. These references provide limited information on longitudinal electrophysiologic maturation in preterm neonates.

What is new

• In a cohort of 249 preterm infants, serial ECG measurements demonstrated changes in axes, QTc, and precordial voltages from birth to term-equivalent age. • These gestation and age-specific trajectories support cautious interpretation of preterm ECGs using term-derived standards.

title: 2026 update on the COVADIS diagnostic criteria of international standardization for microvascular angina.
authorString: Ong P, Camici PG, Beltrame J, Berry C, Crea F, Escaned J, van de Hoef T, Kaski JC, Pepine C, Sechtem U, Shimokawa H, Zeitz C, Merz NB.
abstractText: Microvascular angina, in the context of ischemia with non-obstructed coronary arteries (INOCA), is a highly prevalent clinical condition in cardiovascular medicine. Although it remains frequently underdiagnosed, clinical research and practice have made substantial progress in the last 10 years. This includes better characterisation of affected patient cohorts, new data on the prevalence of coronary vasomotor disorders and improved diagnostic assessments (non-invasive and invasive). The aim of this paper is to update our previous 2018 recommendations for the standardization of diagnostic criteria for microvascular angina. The updated COVADIS (Coronary Vasomotor Disorders Study Group) criteria focus on the following 4 criteria: (1) symptoms of myocardial ischemia; (2) non-obstructive coronary disease (stenosis <50%); (3) objective evidence of myocardial ischemia and (4) evidence of impaired coronary microvascular function. The updated criteria incorporate new suggestions for endotype definitions based on the invasive assessment of coronary physiology including coronary flow reserve and the index of microvascular resistance during pharmacological stress as well as acetylcholine testing for epicardial and/or microvascular spasm. The updated criteria should contribute to improved recognition and better management of this condition.

title: Effects of tirzepatide (GIP/GLP-1 dual receptor agonist) on cardiorenal biomarkers and functional capacity in heart failure: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Eisa N, Khoury M.

journal.title: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

abstractText:
Background

Tirzepatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist, has demonstrated clinical benefits in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and obesity. However, its effects on cardiorenal biomarkers and functional capacity have not been comprehensively synthesized. We hypothesized that tirzepatide produces significant reductions in cardiorenal biomarkers and improvements in functional capacity compared to placebo or standard of care.

Methods

This systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO: CRD42026137255) searched PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, Web of Science, and Scopus from inception to April 17, 2026, without restrictions. Randomized controlled trials and prospective observational studies reporting NT-proBNP, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score (KCCQ-CSS), 6-minute walk test (6 MWT), or renal outcomes with tirzepatide vs placebo or standard of care were included. Data were pooled using random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment.

Results

Seven studies (5 RCTs, 2 observational; 5406 participants) were included. Tirzepatide significantly reduced hsCRP by 34.3% (95% CI: -38.4% to -30.1%; P < .0001; I2 = 0.0%; 6 studies) and NT-proBNP by 17.6% (95% CI: -26.7% to -8.5%; P = .0001; I2 = 58.1%; 3 studies). In the SUMMIT trial, KCCQ-CSS improved by 5.1 points (P < .001) and 6 MWT by 15.8 m (P = .004). Single-trial data demonstrated estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) preservation (+2.90 mL/min/1.73 m2/year; 95% CI: 0.94 to 4.86) and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio reduction (-25.0%; 95% CI: -36.0% to -13.0%).

Conclusion

Tirzepatide produces consistent anti-inflammatory effects and significant natriuretic peptide reductions, supported by moderate Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation certainty. Evidence for functional and renal outcomes remains limited to single-trial analyses and should be considered hypothesis-generating pending larger dedicated heart failure trials.

Prospero registration

CRD42026137255.

title: Nurse Practitioner-Led Integration of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Patients With Obesity-Related Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Prospective Clinical Effectiveness Study.
authorString: Cline L.
abstractText:
Background

Obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is characterized by systemic inflammation and reduced functional capacity. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) improve symptoms and weight in randomized trials, but uptake in routine cardiovascular practice is inconsistent.

Objective

The purpose of this study was to evaluate a structured nurse practitioner-led program for GLP-1 RA initiation in obesity-related HFpEF.

Methods

Prospective 12-month, single-center pre-post effectiveness study at a U.S. urban academic outpatient cardiology clinic. Adults with left ventricular ejection fraction ≥45%, body mass index ≥30 kg/m2, New York Heart Association class II-III symptoms, and at least 1 cardiometabolic comorbidity were enrolled. The intervention included registry-based identification, baseline assessment, patient education, protocolized titration, and longitudinal follow-up. Each participant's 12-month preenrollment period served as a comparator. The primary outcome was GLP-1 RA initiation and 12-month persistence.

Results

Of 156 enrolled, 128 (82.1%) completed follow-up. Mean age 67.4 ± 11.2 years; 61.7% female; 43.8% Black. GLP-1 RA use rose from 7.8% to 92.2% (87.5% at target dose). Mean weight decreased 6.2 ± 3.8 kg, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score improved 16.6 ± 11.3 points, and 6-minute walk distance rose 48.3 ± 36.2 m (all P < .001). Systolic blood pressure, hemoglobin A1c (diabetic subgroup), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide all decreased significantly. Heart failure hospitalization fell from 18.2% to 4.7% (P = .002). Gastrointestinal symptoms were most common; 4.7% discontinued for intolerance.

Conclusions

A structured nurse practitioner-led cardiometabolic program was associated with high GLP-1 RA initiation and persistence and with clinically meaningful improvements in symptoms, function, and hospitalization in obesity-related HFpEF.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Anomalous Aortic Origin of Right Coronary Artery from the Left Coronary Sinus.
authorString: Yang T, Lee J, Pack KY, Ha KE, Jang Y, Kang WC, Moon J.
abstractText:
Introduction

Anomalous Aortic Origin of Right Coronary Artery (AAORCA) is a rare congenital anomaly that may be associated with adverse cardiac events, including sudden cardiac death. Surgical correction is commonly recommended in patients with AAORCA. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is a prevalent diagnostic modality, which increases AAORCA detection. However, the clinical significance of incidentally detected AAORCA remains unclear.

Methods

This non-randomized retrospective analysis included 10,134 patients who underwent CCTA between January 2014 and December 2022, either for suspected coronary artery disease (CAD) or a medical check-up. Three groups were created: patients with normal coronary anatomy (normal), with AAORCA (anomaly), and CAD without AAORCA (CAD). CAD was defined as a percentage diameter stenosis of ≥50% in one or more segments. Cardiac mortality was this study's primary endpoint.

Results

Normal, anomaly, and CAD group comprised 7592 (74.9%), 66 (0.7%), and 2476 (24.4%) patients, respectively. During a median follow-up of 33.7 months (IQR: 13.2-53.4), Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed no significant difference in the cardiac death occurrence between the normal (15 events, 0.2%) and anomaly groups (0 events, 0%) (log-rank p=0.685). Cox proportional hazards model revealed no difference in mortality in the anomaly group compared with normal group.

Conclusions

In our cohort, incidentally detected AAORCA in adults did not demonstrate a clearly elevated cardiac death risk relative to CAD during mid-term follow-up. However, given the small number of events, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive rather than confirmatory evidence of a benign natural course, particularly in populations at higher risk of exertional sudden cardiac death.

title: Physical activity and quality of life in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in Japan: a quantitative study.
authorString: Kitaoka H, Kubo T, Torigoe M, Ikeda Y, Shimoura K, Suo S, Takeda R, Maekawa Y.
abstractText:
Aim

To describe the burden of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) using patient-reported outcome tools and a study-specific questionnaire.

Patients and methods

This two-phase, cross-sectional, non-interventional, observational study (qualitative [previous] and quantitative [current]) included adults with HCM and New York Heart Association functional classification 2/3 recruited from healthcare facilities across Japan. The International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ), Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ), Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Symptom Questionnaire (HCMSQ), and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) were used alongside a questionnaire developed using the qualitative findings.

Results

The analysis included 120 patients (mean age, 59.1 ± 16.3 years; 55.5% [66/120] male), 60 each with non-obstructive and obstructive HCM. Patients with (vs. without) lifestyle changes had lower median IPAQ score (495.0 [363.0-1803.5] vs. 990.0 [369.4-2295.0], p = 0.159) and KCCQ - Clinical Summary Score (81.3 [65.6-90.7] vs. 92.0 [81.4-97.9], p < 0.001), and higher HADS-Depression (5.0 [3.0-8.0] vs. 2.0 [1.0-6.0], p = 0.001) and HCMSQ-shortness of breath (5.0 [2.0-6.0] vs. 3.0 [0.0-4.5], p < 0.001) scores. Most patients (83.9%) noticed HCM symptoms, and some patients attributed symptoms to causes other than HCM. Most patients (89.0%) told others about their HCM. Primary care physicians were the main information source (99.2%).

Conclusions

In this quantitative analysis, HCM affected patients' lifestyles and physical activity.

Clinical trial registration

NCT06181617 (ClinicalTrials.gov).

title: Central and peripheral vascular recovery following resistance exercise with and without blood flow restriction across age groups: a parallel group crossover randomized trial.
authorString: Melo X, HOLD TIGHT 1.0 Team, Laranjo S, Fernhall B, Marôco JL.
abstractText:
Background

High-intensity resistance training (HIRT) benefits musculoskeletal and vascular health but may be poorly tolerated by older adults. Low-intensity resistance training (LIRT) is an alternative, yet evidence on arterial stiffness is mixed, and it often fails to improve vascular health due to insufficient stimulus. Blood flow restriction (BFR) enhances hemodynamic stimulus, but its acute cardiovascular effects in older adults remain unclear.

Purpose

To compare central and peripheral vascular responses following acute LIRT with BFR versus HIRT across age groups.

Methods

In a randomized crossover design, 19 young (22±3 years) and 19 older (70±9 years) adults completed three sessions: HIRT (3 × 10 reps at 75%1RM), LIRT+BFR (4 × 20 reps at 30%1RM with continuous cuff occlusion), and no exercise. Central and peripheral vascular function were assessed via oscillometric pulse wave analysis at rest, 5-min (RECOV1), and 30-min (RECOV2) post-exercise.

Results

In older adults, neither HIRT nor LIRT+BFR altered total peripheral resistance (TPR), aortic reservoir function, or subendocardial viability ratio (SEVR) throughout post-exercise, with no differences observed between conditions. Conversely, young adults exhibited reductions at RECOV1 following HIRT in TPR (Δ = -  0.176 PRU), reservoir function (Δ = -  11.9%), and SEVR (Δ = -  47.1%), persisting at RECOV2 (all p < 0.05). LIRT+BFR elicited minor changes. Most variables normalized within 30 min for both groups.

Conclusion

In older adults, LIRT+BFR elicits post acute central vascular responses comparable to HIRT, with stable coronary perfusion and rapid recovery supporting the short-term tolerability of both modalities. LIRT+BFR thus represents a viable alternative to HIRT for older population.

Trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov (ID: NCT06596304).

title: Evidence on Valve Selection for Small Aortic Annuli in Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
authorString: Maia ADS, Neves G, Aliyu U, Kilic A, Sá MP.
abstractText: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement in patients with small aortic annuli presents unique challenges related to prosthesis-patient mismatch, residual gradients, conduction disturbances, and lifetime valve management. Recent observational data have suggested potential differences in mid-term survival between self-expanding valve and balloon-expandable valve platforms; however, these findings have not been consistently supported by other observational studies or long-term randomized evidence. Importantly, both severe prosthesis-patient mismatch and permanent pacemaker implantation may carry prognostic implications, underscoring the competing risks involved in valve selection. In conclusion, current evidence does not establish the clinical superiority of one transcatheter valve platform over another, supporting an individualized approach to valve selection.

title: Fibro-Inflammatory Signaling, Fibrosis, and Microvascular Ischemia as Convergent Translational Substrates of Sudden Cardiac Death in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Systematic Review.
authorString: da Silva Menezes Junior A, Wastowski IJ, Carneiro LC.
abstractText: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) remains an important cause of sudden cardiac death (SCD), but the biological determinants of ventricular arrhythmic vulnerability remain incompletely defined. This systematic translational review examined whether fibro-inflammatory signaling, fibrotic remodeling, and microvascular ischemia represent convergent components of the arrhythmogenic substrate in HCM. MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to January 2026. Of 167 records, 37 full-text reports were assessed and 11 studies included. Fibrosis emerged as the most clinically mature substrate marker, while microvascular ischemia appeared to amplify electrical instability, particularly in remodeled myocardium. Molecular and tissue studies suggested upstream fibro-inflammatory programs involving activated fibroblasts, extracellular matrix dysregulation, SMAD/TGF-beta signaling, CRLF1/LIFR-JAK-STAT signaling, and altered multicellular communication. Overall, the evidence supports an integrated mechanism-to-substrate model, but prospective outcome-validated studies are needed before these biological layers can refine SCD risk stratification beyond established clinical and imaging markers in contemporary HCM practice.

title: Temporal Trends and Demographic Disparities in Percutaneous Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion Utilization in the United States, 2016–2022
authorString: Shaun B, Movahed MR, Hashemzadeh M, Hashemzadeh M.
abstractText:
Background

Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) provides non-pharmacological stroke prevention for non-valvular atrial fibrillation patients with contraindications to long-term oral anticoagulation. National long-term data on age-adjusted utilization trends and demographic adoption disparities remain limited.

Objectives

To evaluate national temporal trends, hospital characteristics, clinical acuity shifts, and demographic adoption patterns of percutaneous LAAO procedures.

Methods

Using the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) from 2016 through 2022, percutaneous LAAO procedures were identified using ICD-10-PCS code 02L73DK. Weighted national estimates were used to evaluate patient demographics, hospital factors, clinical acuity, and overall in-hospital mortality. Age-adjusted rates per 100,000 population were calculated using direct standardization to the 2000 U.S. standard population.

Results

A total of 190,020 weighted LAAO procedures were identified increasing from 4,875 in 2016 to 60,445 in 2022. The mean patient age was 76.3 ± 7.6 years, and 58.5% were male. Most patients were White (90.4%), while Hispanic (4.3%), Black (3.9%), and Asian/Pacific Islander (1.3%) patients accounted for smaller proportions of procedures. Most procedures were performed at urban teaching hospitals (87.0%). Overall in-hospital mortality was 0.1% (n = 225, p = 0.582). Minor APR-DRG risk of mortality increased from 43.5% to 55.5%, while all others decreased ( p < 0.001). Age-adjusted LAAO rates rose from 34.19 to 379.87 per 100,000 population ( p -trend < 0.01). Significant differences in utilization across racial groups persisted throughout the study period.

Conclusions

Percutaneous LAAO utilization expanded rapidly with exceptionally low inpatient mortality. Persistent gaps in age-adjusted rates highlight key racial, sex, and geographic disparities in structural heart care.

Condensed Abstract

Using the 2016–2022 National Inpatient Sample, this study evaluated temporal trends and demographic adoption patterns of percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO). Among 190,020 weighted procedures, annual volume increased from 4,875 to 60,445. In-hospital mortality was exceptionally low (0.1%). Age-adjusted procedural rates rose from 34.19 to 379.87 per 100,000 population. However, significant disparities persisted, characterized by heavy centralization in urban teaching hospitals (87.0%) and disproportionately lower absolute age-adjusted utilization among female, Black, Hispanic, and Asian/Pacific Islander patients compared to male and White cohorts. Targeted initiatives are needed to ensure equitable access to structural heart interventions.

title: Prognostic associations of left atrial strain with major adverse cardiovascular events and atrial fibrillation: Data from the Akershus Cardiac Examination (ACE) 1950 Study.
authorString: Solberg MG, Rønningen PS, Berge T, Enger S, Pervez MO, Orstad EB, Kvisvik B, Aagaard EN, Lyngbakken MN, Omland T, Røsjø H, Steine K, Tveit A.
abstractText:
Background

Left atrial (LA) reservoir (LASr), conduit (LAScd) and contractile (LASct) strain are known to reflect atrial remodeling and is prognostic in atrial fibrillation (AF) and heart failure. Evidence is scarce on prediction of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in general populations. LA mechanical dispersion (LA MD) and stiffness index (LASI) are less studied strain-derived indices of AF and cardiovascular risk.

Methods

The Akershus Cardiac Examination 1950 Study included 3706 participants from the general population who underwent baseline echocardiography in 2012-2015. MACE (cardiovascular death, non-fatal stroke, non-fatal myocardial infarction or coronary intervention) and incident AF were recorded through 2022. Prognostic value of LA strain was assessed by Cox regression.

Results

In 3229 participants with baseline LA strain analysis, MACE was recorded in 242 (7.5%) and incident AF in 157 (5.0%) over a median 8.3 years (IQR 7.9-8.9) of follow-up. LASr, LAScd and LASI were associated with MACE in univariable analyses, and LASI remained independently associated with MACE after multivariable adjustment (HR per 1SD increment 1.12, 95% CI 1.04-1.21). LASr (HR per 1SD decrement 1.21, 95% CI 1.01-1.45), LASct (HR per 1SD decrement 1.26, 95% CI 1.04-1.52) and LA MD (HR per 1SD increment 1.23, 95% CI 1.03-1.48) were independently associated with incident AF after multivariable adjustment. Accounting for competing risk of all-cause death, LA MD remained independently associated with incident AF, whereas LASr and LASct did not.

Conclusion

In a general population, LASI was independently associated with MACE, whereas LASr, LASct and LA MD were associated with incident AF.

title: Salvianolic acid B increases the stability of atherosclerotic vulnerable plaques by inhibiting macrophage apoptosis via the Piezo1/JNK pathway.
authorString: Zou L, Meng P, Li Z, Ou X, Guo X, Zhang Q, Xu Y, Wang J, Sun X, Liu Q, Fang Y, Xu X, Pei K.
abstractText:
Background

Atherosclerosis is the leading cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, and plaque vulnerability is a critical determinant of acute cardiovascular events. Previous studies have reported that Salvianolic acid B (Sal-B), a main active constituent of Salvia miltiorrhiza, inhibits AS by targeting Piezo1 and have clarified its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects in endothelial cells. However, the specific signaling pathway downstream of Piezo1 that regulates apoptosis in macrophages remains unclear, and the molecular mechanism by which Sal-B affects macrophage apoptosis through directly regulating Piezo1 still needs to be further explored.

Objective

This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of Sal-B on atherosclerosis and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms, with particular emphasis on macrophage apoptosis and the Piezo1-JNK signaling pathway.

Methods

An atherosclerosis model was established in ApoE-/- mice fed a high-fat diet, followed by oral administration of Sal-B at different doses. Plaque morphology, fibrous cap thickness, and lipid profiles were assessed using Oil Red O, hematoxylin and eosin (H&E), and Masson's staining. Macrophage apoptosis and related protein expression were evaluated by TUNEL staining, flow cytometry, Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry in both in vivo and in vitro experiments.

Results

Sal-B significantly reduced plaque area, increased fibrous cap thickness, and improved serum lipid profiles. It markedly downregulated the expression of pro-apoptotic Bax and cleaved caspase-3 while upregulating the anti-apoptotic protein Bcl-2, thereby inhibiting macrophage apoptosis. Consistently, Sal-B suppressed the expression of Piezo1, JNK, and phosphorylated JNK (p-JNK) in vivo and in vitro. Overexpression of Piezo1 enhanced JNK/p-JNK activation, increased Bax and cleaved caspase-3 levels, decreased Bcl-2 expression, and aggravated macrophage apoptosis, indicating that excessive Piezo1 activity may counteract the anti-apoptotic effects of Sal-B.

Conclusion

Sal-B stabilizes atherosclerotic plaques by suppressing Piezo1 activation and downstream JNK/p-JNK signaling, thereby reducing macrophage apoptosis, limiting necrotic core expansion, and ultimately attenuating the progression of atherosclerosis. This finding offers novel mechanistic insights into the anti-atherosclerotic effects of Sal-B and identifies the macrophage apoptosis-related Piezo1 channel as a potential therapeutic target for atherosclerotic lesions.

title: Cardiac Manifestations of EGPA: An Overlap Phenotype of Inflammatory Myocardial Injury and Takotsubo-Like Syndrome.
authorString: Shalit B, Buonomo G, Shaw DG, Grisé AP.
abstractText:
Background

Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) often presents with eosinophilic myocarditis, but the spectrum of cardiac findings is scarcely reported. We describe a case of EGPA with an unusual presentation of acute left ventricular (LV) dysfunction associated with lymphocyte-predominant myocardial inflammation and Takotsubo-like syndrome with LV thrombus.

Case summary

A 42-year-old woman with history of asthma presented with chronic cough, dyspnea, and rash. Findings of peripheral eosinophilia, cutaneous vasculitis, mononeuritis multiplex, and myocardial inflammation confirmed antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies-negative EGPA. Her course was complicated by transient severe LV systolic dysfunction with Takotsubo-like regional wall-motion abnormalities, lymphocyte-predominant myocardial inflammation on biopsy, and LV thrombus. Management included pulse-dosed steroids, rituximab, and mepolizumab.

Discussion

Although EGPA frequently causes cardiac manifestations, typically eosinophilic myocarditis, an overlap phenotype of inflammatory myocardial injury, Takotsubo-like cardiomyopathy, and LV thrombus is exceedingly rare.

Take-home messages

Cardiac involvement remains the leading cause of mortality in EGPA. This case highlights the heterogeneity of its cardiac phenotypes, illustrating the importance of early cardiology evaluation and diagnostics.

title: Impact of <sup>18</sup>FDG-Avidity and Immunosuppression on Idiopathic and Genetic Cardiomyopathies.
authorString: Tabaghi S, Bevan GH, Hankinson S, Gumuser ED, Lal M, Pico M, Chatterjee N, Vasbinder A, Cheng RK, Stempien-Otero A, Lakdawala NK, Blankstein R, Di Carli MF, Levin B, Divakaran S, Nazer B.
abstractText:
Background

Myocardial 18fluorodeoxyglucose (18FDG)-avidity is frequently seen in patients with genetic cardiomyopathy, as well as a growing "idiopathic 18FDG-avidity" group of genotype-negative patients who do not clearly have cardiac sarcoidosis. The prognostic implications of 18FDG-avidity in patients with and without genetic cardiomyopathy, and the effects of immunosuppression in the latter, remain uncertain.

Methods

This multicenter, retrospective study included all patients who were referred for both 18FDG-PET and cardiomyopathy genetic testing. Patients with acute myocarditis, biopsy-proven sarcoidosis, or extracardiac 18FDG-avidity were excluded. We investigated heart failure (HF) composite (left ventricular assist device, heart transplant, HF hospitalization, or death) and arrhythmia composite (sustained ventricular arrhythmias [ventricular tachycardia/VF], atrioventricular block, or death) outcomes using survival analysis, including Cox proportional hazards modeling and inverse probability of treatment weighting.

Results

Among 372 patients, 142 (38%) were 18FDG-avid. The prevalence of genetic cardiomyopathy among 18FDG-avid patients (12%) was similar to that of 18FDG-negative patients (18%; P=0.11). Unadjusted, 18FDG-avidity was associated with an increased risk of HF composite (hazard ratio, 1.69 [95% CI, 1.04-2.75]; P=0.034) and arrhythmia composite (hazard ratio, 1.63 [95% CI, 1.1-2.4]; P=0.014) outcomes compared with 18FDG-negative patients. However, these associations were not statistically significant after multivariable adjustment, nor were there significant differences in 18FDG-associated risks in patients with genetic cardiomyopathy versus genotype-negative patients. After inverse probability of treatment weighting, immunosuppression of 18FDG-avid patients (n=49) was not associated with a reduction in HF or arrhythmia composite outcomes compared with those who were not immunosuppressed (n=93).

Conclusions

Myocardial-only 18FDG-avidity is not significantly associated with HF or arrhythmia risk in patients who do not clearly have cardiac sarcoidosis (including those with genetic cardiomyopathy). Immunosuppression therapy does not seem to modify the disease course, suggesting that not all myocardial 18FDG uptake reflects clinically significant inflammation.

title: Definition and Prognosis of Mitral Regurgitation in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: A Multicenter International Cohort Study.
authorString: Hauptmann L, Kronberger C, Schwarting SK, Tomasoni D, Schlender LS, Koschatko S, Autherith M, Jantsch C, Demirel C, Duca F, Kammerlander A, Bordignon L, Guidi Colombi G, Schwegel N, Serenelli M, Porcari A, Muller SA, Verheyen N, Oerlemans MIFJ, Papathanasiou M, Hengstenberg C, Merlo M, Hausleiter J, Adamo M, Bartko PE, Nitsche C.
abstractText:
Background

In transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy, mitral regurgitation (MR) severity may be underestimated by conventional (semi-)quantitative echocardiographic criteria due to restrictive low-flow hemodynamics. We sought to define and validate disease-specific MR risk thresholds and compare their prognostic performance with guideline definitions.

Methods

In a multicenter cohort study (8 centers, 4 countries), 1101 patients with newly diagnosed transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (derivation, n=722; validation, n=379) underwent standardized echocardiography with blinded core laboratory analysis, including MR measures (vena contracta width, effective regurgitant orifice area, regurgitant volume, and regurgitant fraction). All-cause mortality and time to first heart failure hospitalization (HFH) served as end points. Prognostic thresholds were derived from spline analysis, validated externally, and compared with American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology, European Society of Cardiology/European Association for Cardiothoracic Surgery, and American Society of Echocardiography definitions.

Results

During a median follow-up of 24.9 months (interquartile range, 12.0-42.0), 314 patients (28.5%) died and 244 (22.2%) experienced HFH. All MR metrics independently predicted mortality and HFH (all P<0.05). Spline-derived thresholds identified intermediate risk at vena contracta width ≥3.0 mm, effective regurgitant orifice area ≥0.10 cm2, regurgitant volume ≥15 mL, and regurgitant fraction ≥20% and high risk at effective regurgitant orifice area >0.25 cm2, regurgitant volume >38 mL, and regurgitant fraction >35%. Compared with guideline grading (≈12%-13%), the composite MR grading scheme classified a significantly higher proportion (21%) as severe MR and provided superior discrimination for clinical outcomes at 12 and 24 months in both the derivation and validation cohort. After multivariable adjustment, only the composite MR grading scheme remained strongly predictive for both mortality (hazard ratio, 1.20 [1.07-1.36]) and HFH (hazard ratio, 1.21 [1.05-1.38]).

Conclusions

Quantitative MR thresholds in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy are substantially lower than current guideline cutoffs. A validated, risk-based composite MR grading scheme improves prediction of both mortality and HFH, better reflecting the restrictive low-flow pathophysiology of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy and supporting disease-specific MR grading.

Registration

URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT06836011.

title: Genetic landscape of paediatric channelopathies and cardiomyopathies in Hong Kong.
authorString: Kwok SY, Leung HT, Shi JZ, Shih FY, Chen RHS, Lun KS, Mak CM, Chung BHY, Yung TC, Tsao SSL.

journal.title: Hong Kong medical journal = Xianggang yi xue za zhi

abstractText:
Introduction

Cardiac channelopathies and cardiomyopathies are important causes of sudden cardiac death. The genetic background of these conditions in Asian paediatric populations has rarely been reported. This study aimed to report the genetic underpinnings of these conditions in patients treated at a single tertiary paediatric cardiac centre in Hong Kong.

Methods

All patients diagnosed with cardiac channelopathy or cardiomyopathy who underwent genetic testing in our cardiology centre between 2007 and 2022 were included in this cohort study. Phenotype classification, genetic testing methodologies, and results were reviewed. Genetic yields were assessed.

Results

In total, 165 probands were identified. Ninety-four probands carried at least one pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) variant (57.0%), whereas 27 probands (16.4%) had only variants of uncertain significance (VUS). Pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were identified in 58 patients with channelopathy (63.7%) and 36 patients with cardiomyopathy (48.6%), including 22 novel variants (16 P/LP variants and 6 VUS). The yield of P/LP variants was highest in catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (81.8%). The clinical features of selected probands with significant mortality or morbidity were described in relation to variant details. The yield of subsequent cascade genetic screening among first-degree relatives was 27.3%.

Conclusion

This study describes the genetic landscape of paediatric cardiac channelopathies and cardiomyopathies at a single tertiary paediatric cardiology centre in Hong Kong. The findings facilitated genotype-guided management and enabled identification of at-risk family members for the prevention of sudden cardiac death.

title: Genotype and arrhythmic risk in dilated cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Padalia K, Fornaro A, Claggett B, Jason M, Moritz S, Medo K, Graw S, Hespe S, Ingles J, Ho CY, Helms AS, Shore S, Sinagra G, Merlo M, Khan SS, Lin K, Olivotto I, Owens A, Wheeler M, Stevenson L, Reza N, Rossano J, Paldino A, Verdonschot JAJ, Taylor MRG, Tayal U, Heymans SRB, Prasad S, Lakdawala NK, Parikh VN, Mestroni L, Wilsbacher LD, DCM-SHaRe Investigators.
abstractText:
Background and aims

Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) presents with variable risk of life-threatening arrhythmias. Genetic diagnosis guides sudden death prevention strategies, but risk magnitude for arrhythmogenic genes remains unknown. This study leveraged the international Sarcomeric Human Cardiomyopathy Registry (SHaRe) to address this gap and improve risk stratification.

Methods

Effects of pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants in genes associated with DCM and ventricular arrhythmia on clinical events were analysed in DCM-SHaRe patients. Patients were stratified by presence of a P/LP variant in a high-arrhythmogenic risk gene (LMNA, DSP, FLNC, RBM20, PLN, SCN5A, DES, TMEM43), a low-arrhythmogenic risk gene (TTN, TNNT2, MYH7, others), or gene-elusive. Outcomes included age-, sex-, and baseline left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF)-adjusted risk of major ventricular arrhythmia (MVA), atrial fibrillation (AF), heart failure (HF), death, and their composite.

Results

Among 2660 genotyped adults with DCM (mean diagnosis age 47 ± 15 years, 39.8% female), 434 (16%) had P/LP variants in high-arrhythmogenic genes, 451 (17%) in low-arrhythmogenic genes, and 1775 (67%) were gene-elusive. Compared with gene-elusive patients, patients with high-arrhythmogenic P/LP variants showed increased MVA [hazard ratio (HR) 3.25, 95% confidence interval (CI) 2.63-4.01], AF (HR 2.42, 95% CI 1.96-2.98), HF (HR 2.46, 95% CI 1.89-3.19), and composite (HR 1.97, 95% CI 1.69-2.29) risk, which remained significant after adjusting for age, sex, and LVEF. Patients with high-arrhythmogenic P/LP variants and LVEF ≥ 50% maintained increased MVA (HR 2.36, 95% CI 1.59-3.51) and composite (HR 1.63, 95% CI 1.25-2.12) risk.

Conclusions

Genetic testing enables powerful risk stratification for arrhythmias and HF in DCM independent of age, sex, or LVEF.

title: Disproportionality Analysis of Reporting Signals for Pericardial Disorders in the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System, 2000 to 2025.
authorString: McCall KL, Bush KT, George CE, Goudy HN, Mento DT, Schwier NC.
abstractText:
Background/objectives

Pericardial syndromes cause significant morbidity, decreased quality of life, and rarely mortality. Drug-associated pericardial syndromes are underreported. This study characterized reports of pericardial disorders, described demographic and reporting features, and identified disproportionality signals across suspect drugs and therapeutic classes.

Methods

This study analyzed FDA Adverse Event Reporting System reports from January 2000 to March 2025, using predefined preferred terms for pericardial syndromes. Duplicate and pediatric reports (<18 years) were excluded, resulting in 12,106 unique reports. A lower 90% confidence limit of the Empirical Bayes Geometric Mean (EB05)>2 and a lower limit of the 95% credibility interval of the Information Component (IC025)>0 were indicators of signals.

Results

Raw counts of reports increased from 133 in 2000 to 939 in 2024. The cohort had a balanced sex distribution and a mean age of 55.5 years. Among females, antineoplastic (e.g., rituximab, EB05 = 13.3, IC025 = 3.7) and immunomodulating agents (e.g., adalimumab, EB05 = 3.1, IC025 = 1.6) were most frequently suspected. Among males, antithrombotic agents (e.g., aspirin, EB05 = 7.1, IC025 = 2.8) predominated. A higher age-adjusted reporting odds of death was observed in females versus males (OR=1.14, 95% CI 1.03-1.25; deaths: females n=1,030, males n=925).

Discussion

Raw report counts of pericardial syndromes increased over 25 years, supporting heightened vigilance for drug-induced etiologies. Sex-stratified drug rankings were exploratory and do not demonstrate drug-by-sex interactions. The results extend the existing literature by providing a broad descriptive overview of the reporting landscape for pericardial disorders within a national spontaneous reporting system.

Conclusions

Immunomodulating, antineoplastic, and antithrombotic agents generated reporting signals involving pericardial disorders, with sex-based differences and reported drug classes and outcomes. These findings do not establish causality and warrant confirmatory studies.

title: Characterizing One-Year Mortality in Early Survivors of Open Thoracoabdominal Aortic Repair.
authorString: Karla A, Rebello KR, Orozco-Sevilla V, Nguyen L, Green SY, LeMaire SA, Chatterjee S, Moon MR, Coselli JS.
abstractText:
Background

Although operative mortality after open thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA) repair is well characterized, only limited data describe 1-year survival among patients who survive the index hospitalization. This study sought to further characterize 1-year mortality among operative survivors of open TAAA repair.

Methods

From January 1986 through July 2025, 3838 open TAAA repairs were performed within our single practice. After operative deaths and patients lacking 1-year follow-up were excluded, 3378 early survivors comprised the study cohort. Demographic, operative, and postoperative data were compared between patients who survived ≥1 year after repair and those who did not. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of 1-year mortality.

Results

Among early survivors, 328 (9.7%) died within 1 year. One-year mortality was associated with older age, prior percutaneous coronary intervention, prior stroke, and chronic kidney disease. Postoperative complications-namely paraplegia (odds ratio [OR] 1.96, P=.03), dialysis dependence (OR 2.00, P=.001), arrhythmia (OR 1.48, P=.01), tracheostomy (OR 2.17, P<.001), and 1-year repair failure (OR 5.13, P<.001)-independently predicted death, whereas elective repair (OR 0.57, P<.001) and discharge home (OR 0.38, P<.001) predicted 1-year survival. Model discrimination was good (C-statistic=0.77 [0.74-0.81]). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed markedly greater 1-year survival in patients initially discharged home (94%) versus elsewhere (73%; P<.001).

Conclusions

Among operative survivors of open TAAA repair, 1-year mortality remains considerable and is primarily determined by persistent postoperative complications and repair durability rather than intraoperative variables. Vigilant surveillance, structured rehabilitation, and multidisciplinary follow-up may be needed to ensure success beyond the perioperative period.

title: Preoperative Risk-assessment Score for Elective Total Aortic Arch Repair: AAORTA Risk Tool.
authorString: Guinn MT, Miles TJ, Glover VA, Green SY, Nguyen LH, Etheridge GM, Barron LK, Xue AH, Orozco-Sevilla V, Chatterjee S, Moon MR, Coselli JS.
abstractText:
Objective

Total transverse aortic arch replacement is a complex operation performed to address aortic aneurysm with and without chronic aortic dissection. To predict 90-day survival after this procedure, we created a holistic tool for predicting postoperative mortality in patients who undergo total arch repair (TAR): the Aortic Arch Operation Risk Tool for Assessment (AAORTA) score.

Methods

Univariate and multivariate analyses were performed on data from patients (N=470; 243 with nondissecting aneurysm, 227 with chronic Type A dissection) who underwent TAR at a high-volume practice between April 2006 and November 2024. Regression analysis identified variables to be used in the AAORTA score. The predictive performance of the score was assessed with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCC), Brier score, and linear fitting.

Results

Of 470 patients who underwent TAR, 65 (13.8%) died within 90 days of repair. The AAORTA score relied on five preoperative variables: heritable thoracic aortic disease, prior coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), kidney disease, pulmonary disease (restrictive or obstructive), and no history of smoking. Previous CABG was the strongest predictor of 90-day mortality. The AAORTA score had an AUROCC of 0.784, a Brier score of 0.105, and a goodness-of-fit R 2 of 0.954.

Conclusion

The AAORTA score can accurately stratify 90-day mortality risk in patients who undergo elective TAR, using only five variables easily acquired during standard preoperative evaluation. This score could be used to aid preoperative counseling with patients and families. Prospective multicenter validation will help establish its generalizability.

title: Endovascular versus open repair for aortoiliac occlusive disease - nationwide in-hospital outcomes by sex.
authorString: Salm J, Böhme T, Noory E, Bacmeister L, von Zur Mühlen C, Westermann D, Zeller T, Kaier K.
abstractText: Background: Evidence comparing endovascular therapy and open surgery for aorto-iliac occlusive disease remains limited, particularly for early complications, resource use, and sex-specific outcomes. Patients and methods: We conducted a retrospective nationwide cohort study using the 2023 German inpatient dataset. Adult hospitalisations with major endovascular or open aorto-iliac reconstructive procedures and arterial occlusive disease were included. Hospitalisations with aneurysm, dissection, or combined procedure codes were excluded. Outcomes included in-hospital mortality, myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), complications, length of stay, and reimbursement. Adjusted estimates were obtained employing a doubly robust estimator using machine learning algorithms and were stratified by sex. Results: Among 2,710 hospitalisations, 1,923 (71.0%) underwent open surgery and 787 (29.0%) endovascular therapy; 41.3% involved women. Endovascular therapy was associated with lower adjusted risks of in-hospital mortality (RR .44, 95% CI .31-.64), MACCE (RR .47, 95% CI .34-.64), acute kidney injury (RR .38, 95% CI .29-.50), major bleeding (RR .36, 95% CI .25-.51), prolonged ventilation (RR .28, 95% CI .18-.43), and SAEs (RR .46, 95% CI .33-.65). Length of stay was shorter after endovascular therapy (-8.57 days, 95% CI -9.63 to -7.52), while reimbursement did not differ significantly. Sex-stratified estimates were more pronounced in men but exploratory without interaction testing. Conclusions: Endovascular therapy was associated with lower in-hospital morbidity and mortality and shorter hospital stay than open surgery, with similar reimbursement. Case-based data lacked longitudinal follow-up and detailed clinical, anatomical and treatment-selection information, limiting causal and patient-level interpretation.

title: Long-Term Outcomes After Heart-Lung Transplantation: A Contemporary 20-Year Single-Center Experience.
authorString: Székely M, Yousefzai R, Lopez-Trevino M, Chihara R, Del Val FR, Gecse II, Ghobrial RM, Duarte V, Martin C, Huang HJ, Guha A, Akay MH, Bhimaraj A, Reardon MJ, Quarti AG.

journal.title: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery

abstractText:
Objective

(s): We aimed to evaluate long-term outcomes after heart-lung transplantation (HLTx) including comparisons between adult congenital (CHD) and non-congenital (non-CHD) recipients and outcomes before and after implementation of the 2018 United Network for Organ Sharing heart allocation system change.

Methods

Consecutive patients undergoing HLTx between February 2006 and February 2026 were retrospectively reviewed. The primary endpoint was overall survival. Secondary endpoints included chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD)-free survival and perioperative outcomes. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used for time-to-event outcomes.

Results

Sixty-two patients underwent HLTx, including 20 (32.3%) with CHD and 42 (67.7%) with non-CHD etiologies. Despite greater operative complexity, perioperative outcomes were comparable between groups, with an overall 30-day mortality of 11.3%. Median overall survival was 7.8 years with estimated 1-, 5-, and 10-year survival of 80.1%, 58.8%, and 37.9%, respectively. Median CLAD-free survival was 5.9 years with estimated 1-, 5-, and 10-year rates of 76.6%, 53.5%, and 24.0%, respectively. Overall and CLAD-free survival were similar between CHD and non-CHD recipients (p=0.151 and p=0.354, respectively). Most late deaths were lung-related (20/27, 74%), whereas cardiac causes were uncommon (1/27, 3.7%), and CAV developed in two patients (3.2%). Recipients transplanted after the allocation change demonstrated improved survival (p=0.022), mainly due to a decline in perioperative mortality from 17.5% to 0% (p=0.044).

Conclusions

Long-term outcomes after HLTx remain primarily limited by CLAD and lung-related complications. Adults with CHD achieved survival comparable to non-CHD recipients. Improved contemporary outcomes appear to be driven predominantly by reduced perioperative mortality.

title: Establishing the reliability of non-contrast 4D flow in congenital heart disease at 1.5T.
authorString: Brown NK, Romberg EK, Schmitt C, Pinto NM, Howard W, Robinson JD, Soriano B, Buddhe S.
abstractText:
Background

4D flow has been shown to correlate well with 2D phase-contrast (2D PC) flow measurements, although most of the current literature is based on post-contrast imaging.

Objective

Given recent interest in non-contrast techniques, we hypothesized that non-contrast 4D flow (NC 4D Flow) would correlate well with 2D PC and ventricular stroke volumes.

Methods and materials

A prospective cohort of pediatric and young adult patients with suspected/confirmed congenital heart disease (CHD) underwent cardiac MRI at 1.5T with acquisition of NC 4D Flow and 2D PC. Pearson correlation, linear mixed-effect correlations, and Bland-Altman comparisons were performed to compare these methods with secondary analyses of internal consistency and image quality/noise.

Results

In our cohort of 30 patients (age, 8-20 years), NC 4D Flow correlated strongly with 2D PC for net flow (r=0.76), peak velocity (r=0.9, P<0.001), and regurgitant fraction (r=0.75, P<0.001). By Bland-Altman comparison, NC 4D Flow was 10.1% lower for net flows and 18.9% higher for peak velocity compared to 2D PC. NC 4D Flow also slightly underestimated ventricular stroke volumes (18.1% lower for ascending aorta vs. left ventricular stroke volume and 13.9% lower for main pulmonary artery vs. right ventricular stroke volume). Both datasets were internally consistent; 2D PC had a higher relative signal intensity, but no difference in signal-to-noise or contrast-to-noise ratios (SNR/CNR).

Conclusion

Non-contrast 4D flow correlates well with 2D PC in CHD with a slight underestimation in flows and overestimation in peak velocities, but good internal consistency and comparable SNR/CNR.

title: Association between the inferior vena cava collapsibility index and Fontan pressure in patients with Fontan physiology: a two-centre prospective pilot study.
authorString: Campbell MD, Mir A, Behere S, Huang JH, Burch G, Alnoor M, Madriago E.
abstractText:
Introduction

Patients with functional single ventricle anatomy undergo staged surgical palliation in early childhood culminating in the Fontan procedure whereby the inferior vena cava is connected to the pulmonary artery. Fontan circulation inherently requires elevated central venous pressure to maintain adequate pulmonary blood flow; however, excessive elevation is associated with morbidity and mortality. In adults, a key component of echocardiographic evaluation is the use of a "sniff test" as a surrogate of downstream right atrial pressure. This technique has not yet been validated as a measure of pressure assessment in patients with Fontan circulation.

Methods

This was a two-center prospective study of patients with functional single ventricle physiology who had undergone the Fontan procedure and were undergoing previously scheduled transthoracic echocardiogram and cardiac catheterization as part of their standard clinical care. We correlated collapsibility index on echocardiogram with directly obtained Fontan pressure measurements from cardiac catheterization performed the same day.

Results

15 patients were enrolled and analyzed for the study. Collapsibility index demonstrated an inverse correlation with Fontan pressure, (Pearson r = -0.72, R2 = 0.51, p = 0.003). Collapsibility index was significantly higher for patients with non-elevated Fontan pressure (45% vs 30%, p = 0.0005). Using a collapsibility index threshold of 35.0% demonstrated a 100% positive predictive value for detecting elevated Fontan pressure (greater than 14 mmHg).

Conclusions

There was a significant inverse relationship between the collapsibility index and Fontan pressure. These findings may suggest a possible association between collapsibility index and Fontan pressure, warranting further investigation in larger studies.

title: National Survival Estimates After Surgical Repair of Congenital Heart Disease.
authorString: Fundora MP, Gauvreau K, Yang Y, Jacobs JP, Oster ME, Jenkins KJ, Kochilas L.
abstractText:
Background

Survival estimates after congenital heart surgery (CHS) in the United States are essential for planning healthcare services for this growing, resource-intensive patient population. However, the absolute number of individuals living after interventions for congenital heart disease is unknown because nationally representative survival estimates are unavailable. Understanding postoperative survival from a representative national sample is a critical first step toward estimating the size and future healthcare needs of this population. This study aimed to develop nationally representative long-term survival estimates after CHS in the United States, focusing on benchmark procedures defined by the Society of Thoracic Surgeons.

Methods

We used 3 US data sets of children aged 0 to 20 years at the time of their benchmark CHS from 1998 to 2002 and surviving to hospital discharge. The Pediatric Cardiac Care Consortium (PCCC), a multi-institutional clinical registry, was matched to the National Death Index to determine mortality through December 2019. The Kids' Inpatient Database 2000, a nationally representative administrative claims data set, was used to derive age- and sex-specific weights. Kaplan-Meier curves were estimated from the PCCC-National Death Index cohort for benchmark operations, and Kids' Inpatient Database 2000 weights were applied. Unweighted PCCC survival estimates were also compared with those of Boston Children's Hospital, a large tertiary care center.

Results

Nationally representative survival curves were generated for 7 benchmark CHS from 7973 cases; 3802 (48%) were female, and 4505 (57%) were infants at the time of CHS. These weighted national survival curves closely mirrored the unweighted curves derived from PCCC-National Death Index. Unweighted survival estimates from PCCC also closely approximated those from BCH, with only modest differences observed for selected lesions.

Conclusions

The weighted PCCC-National Death Index methodology provides the first nationally representative estimates of long-term survival after benchmark congenital heart disease in the United States. These estimates provide an important resource for healthcare planning and research for the growing population of individuals with congenital heart disease.

title: Mechanism of Mortality in Individuals with Elevated Risk Pulmonary Emboli: A Multicenter Analysis of a Contemporary Cohort.
authorString: Rozenbaum Z, Gnall E, Gholam A, Chang MF, Divya A, Sanina C, Wiley J.
abstractText: The underlying causes of mortality in patients with pulmonary embolism have been investigated in the past, yet management of pulmonary emboli has evolved and newer therapeutic options are available. Data from four hospitals during 2022-2025 were analyzed and all patients with intermediate-high risk and high risk pulmonary emboli who died during follow up were included. The results depicted in the research letter provide insight into the mechanism of morality in patients with pulmonary emboli by risk category and thereby help improve care and patient selection for interventions.

title: A 0/2-Hour Algorithm Using a Novel Point-of-Care High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin I Assay for Suspected Myocardial Infarction.
authorString: Koechlin L, Lopez-Ayala P, Boeddinghaus J, Sigg N, Durak K, Nestelberger T, Wildi K, Strebel I, Bima P, Crisanti L, Recuenco LH, Yueksel A, Miró Ò, Martin-Sanchez FJ, Kawecki D, Keller DI, Christ M, Buser A, Biefer HRC, Dzemali O, Broughton MN, Mahfoud F, Mueller C, APACE investigators.
abstractText: This letter describes the derivation and internal validation of an assay-specific hs-cTnI-SPINCHIP 0/2h-algorithm for rapid triage of patients with suspected myocardial infarction (MI) in the emergency department (ED). The algorithm provided very high safety for rule-out, high accuracy for rule-in, and enabled definitive triage within 2 hours in approximately 80% of patients. These findings support the clinical potential of the novel point-of-care hs-cTnI-SPINCHIP assay for accelerated ED decision-making.

title: Lifetime management of valvular heart disease in younger and low risk patients.
authorString: Novelli L, Ortiz NF, Varona GM, Gil JLD, Sanchez JS.
abstractText: Valvular heart disease in younger and low-risk patients presents unique therapeutic challenges because treatment decisions must account not only for immediate procedural success but also for the durability of the index intervention, the feasibility of future reinterventions, and the preservation of subsequent treatment options. Consequently, lifetime management has emerged as a longitudinal treatment paradigm in which every intervention influences the sequence, complexity, and outcomes of future procedures. Over the past decade, transcatheter valve therapies have expanded rapidly from a treatment reserved for elderly and high-surgical-risk patients to an increasingly adopted option in younger and lower-risk populations. Although contemporary evidence has demonstrated excellent procedural safety and mid-term outcomes, important uncertainties remain regarding long-term durability and the optimal management of structural valve deterioration and repeat interventions. These considerations highlight the importance of approaching each intervention not as an isolated procedure, but as a step within a predefined lifetime therapeutic strategy. In this context, structured Heart Team discussion and shared decision-making are fundamental to develop an individualized treatment plan that optimizes outcomes while preserving future surgical and transcatheter options across decades of patient care. This review aims to provide a practical framework for the lifetime management of aortic, mitral, and tricuspid valve disease in younger and low-risk patients.

title: Orai3 deficiency drives atrial remodeling and fibrillation susceptibility via Orai channel remodeling and SOCE hyperactivation.
authorString: Wu X, Xue Y, Lu H, Cao Y, Li D, Liang A, Zheng P, Zhang R, Jia Z, Zhao R.
abstractText:
Aims

Atrial remodeling is the pathological substrate for atrial fibrillation (AF), yet no targeted therapies exist. The Orai3 calcium channel regulates cardiac homeostasis, but its role in atrial remodeling remains unexplored.

Methods

Wild type and Orai3 knockout rats were subjected to Angiotensin II infusion or acetylcholine‑calcium chloride injection to model atrial fibrosis and AF. Cardiac function, Orai channel related protein expression and co-localization, SOCE activity, and downstream signaling were evaluated by echocardiography, histology, immunofluorescence, calcium imaging, and western blotting.

Results

Orai3 deficiency exacerbated Ang II induced atrial dilation, fibrosis, and ultrastructural damage, with transcriptomic analysis revealing enrichment of extracellular matrix pathways. Mechanistically, Orai3 loss was associated with reduced Orai1/Orai3 co-localization and enhanced Orai1/STIM1 co-localization, driving SOCE hyperactivation. This aberrant Ca2+ signal bidirectionally upregulated TGF-β and suppressed Cx43 effects reversible by SOCE inhibition or Orai3 overexpression. Orai3 has been proposed to function as a molecular rheostat that down tunes STIM1 mediated gating when in complex with Orai1, its loss removes this brake, unleashing pathological SOCE. Consequently, Orai3 deficient rats exhibited increased AF susceptibility, with disrupted Cx43 distribution, shortened gap junctions, and impaired STAT3 mediated Cx43 transcription.

Conclusions

Orai3 acts as an endogenous protective brake against atrial cardiomyopathy. The Orai3-SOCE-TGF-β/Cx43 axis links calcium dyshomeostasis to both fibrotic and electrical remodeling, positioning Orai3 as a potential prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target for AF.

title: Lipoprotein(a) in Disaggregated South Asian Groups: An Analysis of MASALA and the UK Biobank.
authorString: Bal KS, Reyes MP, Kanaya AM, Taub P, Tsai MY, Kandula NR, Islam N, Wilkinson MJ, Ramsis M, Mahmud E, Shah NS, Kulkarni A, Kalra D, Bhatia HS.
abstractText:
Background

South Asian individuals have a high prevalence of elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)], but little is known about the variation between disaggregated South Asian subgroups.

Objectives

The authors aimed to evaluate Lp(a) levels, nongenetic influences, and the association with incident atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) in South Asian populations using data from the Meditators of Atherosclerosis in South Asians Living in America (MASALA) and the UK Biobank (UKB) studies.

Methods

Lp(a) levels were assessed by South Asian country of origin and by state among Indian-origin participants. The association between nongenetic factors and Lp(a) levels was evaluated in multivariable linear regression models. Cox proportional hazards models evaluated the association between Lp(a) and ASCVD events in UKB participants.

Results

Among 2,074 MASALA participants born in the South Asian subcontinent (mean age: 56.7 ± 9.6 years), median [Q1-Q3] Lp(a) was 20.7 [10.5-43.0] mg/dL with significant variation by country of origin (P = 0.035). Median Lp(a) was 23 [11-48], 19 [10-37], 22 [11-47], and 17 [10-34] mg/dL in participants from Bangladesh, India, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka, respectively. Vegetarian diet, statin use, postmenopausal status, and fewer years in the United States were associated with higher Lp(a) levels while alcohol consumption was associated with lower Lp(a) levels. However, these associations were all very modest. Among 6,845 UKB participants (mean age: 55.1 ± 8.7 years; median Lp(a): 31 [13-65] nmol/L), the associations between Lp(a) and ASCVD did not vary by country of origin or South Asian ethnicity (P interaction > 0.05).

Conclusions

There is modest variation in Lp(a) levels, but no difference in the association between Lp(a) and ASCVD outcomes, across South Asian subgroups.

title: Machine Learning of Echocardiographic Left Ventricular Myocardial Radiomics for Identification of Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Elzieny AA, Alreshq R, Ullah I, Fine D, Teruya S, Helmke S, Gallegos C, Miller EJ, Slivnick JA, Maurer MS, Li B, Ruberg FL.
abstractText:
Background

Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is an important cause of heart failure (HF) with increased left ventricular (LV) wall thickness that can be challenging to distinguish from other LV hypertrophic processes. Echocardiographic myocardial radiomic texture analysis may identify imperceptible amyloid-induced structural changes.

Objectives
