The study aims to develop and validate an echocardiography-based machine learning model using myocardial radiomics to identify ATTR-CM.

Methods

In this retrospective and prospective multicenter study, 854 echocardiographic scans were analyzed. Conventional and novel radiomic features were extracted from parasternal short-axis views at basal, mid, and apical LV levels, with incorporated age and sex from echocardiogram metadata. A machine learning pipeline was developed using a balanced training set (150 ATTR-CM, 150 nonamyloid HF). Performance was evaluated on an independent internal validation set (50 ATTR-CM, 399 nonamyloid HF) and an external validation set (10 ATTR-CM, 10 immunoglobulin light-chain-amyloid, 10 hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, 75 nonamyloid HF).

Results

In internal validation, the model achieved 86% sensitivity (95% CI: 73.8%-93%), 92% specificity (95% CI: 88.9%-94.3%), 57.3% positive predictive value (95% CI: 46.1%-67.9%), 98.1% negative predictive value (NPV) (95% CI: 96.2%-99.1%), and receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve 0.938 (95% CI: 0.891-0.985). Performance was consistent in the external validation (100% sensitivity, 78.9% specificity, 33.3% positive predictive value, 100% NPV, and receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve of 0.917). The model correctly classified 77.3% of nonamyloid HF, 70% of AL-amyloid cases, and 100% of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy cases as non-ATTR in subgroup analysis.

Conclusions

We developed an echocardiographic radiomics-based tool to identify ATTR-CM with excellent discrimination and very high NPV in a cohort that approximates clinical experience. These preliminary findings require validation in larger, more diverse cohorts.

title: Acid-responsive nanoparticles with microneedles for anti‑inflammatory sonodynamic therapy of gouty arthritis.
authorString: Weng J, Feng L, Xie B, Liu L, Shen S, Chen X, Wang L, Xie Y, Yao J, David L, Yan Q.
abstractText: The pathological microenvironment of acute gouty arthritis (AGA) features local tissue acidification and the release of a storm of pro-inflammatory cytokines. To address this dual challenge, we engineered an acid-responsive curcumin-loaded nanoparticles microneedle system (Cur-PNPs@MN) that delivers curcumin with pH-triggered release and anti-inflammatory activity. This integrated platform combines a hyaluronic acid (HA)-based dissolving microneedle for localized transdermal delivery of acid-degradable PCADK (poly (cyclohexane-1,4-diyl acetone dimethylene ketal)) curcumin nanoparticles (Cur-PNPs), which are designed for pH-triggered curcumin release at the pathological site. Together, they deliver curcumin, a dual-function agent acting both as an anti-inflammatory compound and a nanoenhanced sonosensitizer. In vitro, the system exhibited acid-responsive drug release and also promoted macrophage uptake, achieving significant curcumin accumulation within 1 hour and saturation by 4 hours. Moreover, it could generate potent ultrasound-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS). The ROS generation capability of Cur-PNPs was 1.47-fold higher than that of Cur‑aggregates, resulting in anapoptosis rate of 29.9% in M1 macrophages. In vivo, the chemo-sonodynamic therapy (Cur-PNPs@MN+Ultrasound (US)) in a rat AGA model significantly alleviated joint swelling and inflammatory infiltration, while drastically suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokines, with IL-1β decreasing from 170.3 to 67.3 pg/mL, TNF-α from 20.8 to 5.9 pg/mL, and IL-6 from 140.9 to 48.2 pg/mL, and achieved therapeutic efficacy comparable to conventional drugs. This work demonstrates a synergistic chemo‑sonodynamic strategy by coupling pH-triggered curcumin release with ultrasound-enhanced ROS generation. This acid-responsive therapeutic strategy enhances anti-inflammatory efficacy and reduction of M1-associated inflammatory responses, offering an effective approach for AGA therapy.

title: CYP2U1: a cardiac metabolic switch alleviating obesity cardiomyopathy via lipid metabolic reprogramming.
authorString: Chen J, Chen ZX, Lan YB, Fang R, Xie JJ, Yang JS, Zhang XD, Jia SL, Huang GY.
abstractText: Cytochrome P450 2U1 (CYP2U1) modulates lipid metabolism, yet its role in obesity-induced cardiomyopathy remains unknown. Here, we demonstrate that cardiac-specific overexpression of CYP2U1 safeguards against high-fat diet (HFD)-induced myocardial dysfunction. Mice received tail-vein injection of adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (AAV9) carrying CYP2U1 under the cardiac troponin T promoter (AAV9-cTnT-CYP2U1) and were maintained on a 16-week HFD. Cardiac-specific CYP2U1 overexpression was associated with better preservation of systolic function and with reduced myocardial hypertrophy, interstitial fibrosis, and cardiac inflammation. By combining transcriptomics, untargeted metabolomics, and oxylipidomics, we identified two protective mechanisms. Transcriptomic analysis indicated that CYP2U1 attenuated multiple inflammatory cascades, including nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) p65 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation, with a corresponding reduction in interleukin-6 (IL-6) transcription; CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein β (C/EBPβ) may contribute to this regulation. Metabolomic analysis suggested that CYP2U1 remodels polyunsaturated fatty acid metabolism, consistent with a "metabolic switch" that shifts the balance away from pro-inflammatory arachidonic acid-derived hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acids (HETEs) toward the docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) pathway, with increased levels of the protective lipid mediators 19,20-epoxydocosapentaenoic acid (19,20-EDP) and protectin DX (PDX). In vitro, CYP2U1 overexpression in palmitic acid-challenged H9C2 cells reproduced these anti-inflammatory and metabolic features. CYP2U1 therefore limits obesity-driven cardiac inflammation by coupling suppression of the NF-κB/C/EBPβ-IL-6 axis with a shift in lipid mediators toward DHA-derived specialized pro-resolving mediators. Whether targeted activation of CYP2U1 can be translated into a therapeutic strategy for obesity-associated cardiomyopathy warrants further investigation.

title: Refractory Ventricular Tachycardia-Induced Severe Cardiomyopathy in a Child: Successful Radiofrequency Ablation With ECMO Support.
authorString: Lubarsky D, Nandi D, Hayes E, Kertesz N, Kumthekar R.
abstractText:
Background

Ventricular tachycardia (VT)-induced cardiac dysfunction is a recognized but uncommon cause of cardiomyopathy in children.

Case summary

A 7-year-old girl presented with severely depressed left ventricular function and incessant VT that was refractory to multiple antiarrhythmics and attempted cardioversions. Because of hemodynamic instability, the patient required extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) support and ultimately radiofrequency ablation of a focal VT that was localized to the right midventricular septum near the moderator band. The patient had a subsequent return of normal biventricular function.

Discussion

Focal VT causing severe dysfunction, unresponsive to both medical therapy and cardioversion, originating from the moderator band of the right ventricle, requiring ECMO support and radiofrequency ablation is extremely rare in the pediatric population, with few reports in the literature.

Take-home message

High-risk radiofrequency ablation of unusual focal VT originating from the right ventricular midventricular septum during ECMO may be accomplished with excellent clinical outcomes.

title: When Imaging is Negative: Endoscopic Diagnosis of a Secondary Aortoduodenal Fistula.
authorString: Kaur A, Shah A, Gupta A, Jhandier MN.
abstractText: Aortoenteric fistula is a life-threatening aortic graft complication with a narrow opportunity for treatment. We present a patient with aortobifemoral bypass who developed recurrent anemia and melena. Despite previous upper endoscopy and colonoscopy, computed tomography angiogram, and tagged red blood cell scan, his symptoms were persistent. Capsule endoscopy showed blood in the duodenum. Push enteroscopy revealed graft erosion in the duodenum, confirming aortoduodenal fistula. He underwent aortobifemoral graft excision, and resection of the third portion of the duodenum with end-to-side duodenojejunostomy, highlighting the importance of endoscopy in timely diagnosis of aortoenteric fistulae.

title: Primary adrenal small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma in a patient with sarcoidosis and synchronous colon adenocarcinoma.
authorString: Sano A, Takeichi T, Miyamaoto A, Nishii Y, Yamamoto T, Kusama Y.
abstractText: Primary adrenal neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC), particularly the small cell subtype, is exceptionally rare. In patients with sarcoidosis, inflammatory lymphadenopathy may mimic a metastatic disease, making disease detection difficult. A 76-year-old man with sarcoidosis was referred for an enlarging left adrenal incidentaloma that had increased in size from 7 mm to 19 × 14 mm over 3 years. Hormonal evaluation revealed unremarkable findings; laparoscopic adrenalectomy was performed because malignancy could not be excluded. Histopathological examination revealed small cell NEC with positive synaptophysin and chromogranin A staining, and a Ki-67 labeling index of 80%. One month after surgery, para-aortic lymphadenopathy was detected. Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (CT) showed uptake in the para-aortic lymph nodes and ascending colon, where colonoscopy identified synchronous adenocarcinoma. The cause of the lymphadenopathy was uncertain because of coexisting sarcoidosis and colon cancer. Cisplatin plus irinotecan induced a partial response; however, disease progression was observed. CT-guided lymph node biopsy confirmed metastatic NEC. Second-line amrubicin therapy reduced tumor size; comprehensive genomic profiling revealed a tumor mutation-burden-high phenotype. This case highlights diagnostic challenges in the evaluation of lymphadenopathy in patients with sarcoidosis and synchronous malignancy, emphasizing the importance of pathological confirmation for guiding appropriate management.

title: Aortic coarctation and McArdle disease in histiocytosis-lymphadenopathy plus syndrome: expanding the <i>SLC29A3</i> spectrum.
authorString: Rehman B, Hassan SMD, Sagri MN, Kirmani S, Arif M.
abstractText: Histiocytosis-lymphadenopathy plus syndrome (HLPS) is a rare inherited disorder caused by SLC29A3 variants. We report 2 Pakistani brothers with HLPS and markedly different clinical features despite identical genotypes. The 15-year-old had severe growth failure, facial dysmorphism, insulin-dependent diabetes, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, and coarctation of the aorta (CoA) requiring balloon dilatation. Genetic testing identified SLC29A3 and PYGM variants, indicating concurrent HLPS and McArdle disease. His 20-year-old brother had insulin-dependent diabetes and celiac disease from age 3, later developing hypertension, proteinuria, and characteristic skin changes. This case highlights marked intrafamilial variability in HLPS and identifies CoA as a rare cardiovascular feature. It also supports comprehensive genetic testing in patients with early-onset diabetes and multisystem disease.

title: Radiographic phenotyping of healthy and diseased aortas.
authorString: Boudreaux JC, Chaudhry S, Yasmine N, Dhakal S, Zhang H, Sonka M, Wahle A, Vigmostad S, Ramachandra AB, Thiel WH, Smith LE, Streeter J, Bello RM, Singhal AK.
abstractText:
Background

Ascending aortic diameter guides intervention for thoracic aneurysms. Many patients with acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) present with ascending aortic diameters below 5.5 cm, rendering diameter an insufficient risk discriminator. This study evaluated computed tomography angiography (CTA) morphology to identify predissection radiographic features associated with ATAAD.

Methods

Control (n = 50, CTA for non-aortic indications), aneurysm (n = 61, thoracic ascending aorta [TAA] ≥ 4.5 cm), and predissection (n = 13, CTA within 3 years before dissection) groups were studied. Scans were interpreted by thoracic radiologists using predefined measurements.

Results

Age and sex distribution differed overall among groups (P < 0.001 and P = 0.010, respectively). The aneurysm group was older than controls, but the age difference from the predissection group was not significant (P = 0.084). Maximum TAA diameter (MaxD) was 3.11 ± 0.30, 4.96 ± 0.52, and 3.89 ± 0.60 cm in control, aneurysm, and predissection groups respectively; all predissection MaxD values were below 5.5 cm (maximum, 4.9 cm). Ascending aortic length (AAL) was elevated in both disease groups (aneurysm group, 9.03 ± 1.08 cm; predissection group, 10.73 ± 1.41 cm; P < 0.001 vs. control group, 6.38 ± 0.75 cm). The AAL/MaxD ratio differed significantly between every pair of groups (control group, 2.06 ± 0.22; aneurysm group, 1.83 ± 0.21; predissection group, 2.80 ± 0.50; all pairwise P < 0.001), reflecting disproportionate elongation in predissection aortas. Aneurysm patients demonstrated diffuse thoracic dilation, whereas predissection group patients showed predominantly ascending aortic involvement.

Conclusions

In a small exploratory study, predissection aortas displayed a distinct morphological phenotype characterized by disproportionate elongation, moderate dilation, and a relatively nondilated descending aorta-distinct from the diffuse dilation of aneurysm. Ascending aortic length and the AAL/MaxD ratio may provide complementary morphological information beyond maximal diameter alone.

title: Predicting acute kidney injury in type B aortic dissection: development and validation of a clinical nomogram.
authorString: Chen W, Li Z, Shu X.
abstractText:
Objectives

Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) is a frequent and serious complication in patients with Type B Aortic Dissection (TBAD). Existing prediction models are mainly derived from type A or mixed cohorts and do not account for the distinct pathophysiology of TBAD. This study aimed to develop and validate a nomogram for individualized AKI risk prediction in TBAD patients.

Methods

Data were obtained from the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD) and the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV). The eICU-CRD cohort was used for model development and internal validation, while MIMIC-IV served for external validation. A three-step variable selection strategy combining Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO), univariate, and multivariate logistic regression analyses was applied. Model performance was evaluated using the Area Under the receiver operating characteristic Curve (AUC), calibration curves, and Decision Curve Analysis (DCA).

Results

Six independent predictors were identified: ICU length of stay, minimum glucose, minimum sodium, maximum bicarbonate, minimum creatinine, and minimum diastolic blood pressure. The nomogram showed excellent discrimination, with AUCs of 0.926 (95% CI: 0.893-0.956), 0.922 (95% CI: 0.869-0.967), and 0.921 (95% CI: 0.895-0.944) in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. Calibration analysis demonstrated good agreement, and DCA indicated clinical utility within a threshold probability range of 0-70%.

Conclusions

This study developed a practical nomogram based on six readily available variables for dynamic in-hospital prediction of AKI in TBAD patients. The model may assist early risk stratification, although further prospective validation is warranted.

title: Exercise improves heart failure by regulating cardiomyocyte autophagy via the ILF3/lncRNA NEAT1 axis.
authorString: Zhang Y, Song R, Zhao Y.
abstractText: Heart failure (HF) is a common cardiovascular disease. It has been reported that the lncRNA NEAT1 is involved in the progression of HF and that exercise can regulate the expression of NEAT1 in muscle tissue. This study aimed to investigate whether exercise can influence HF progression by regulating NEAT1 expression and to elucidate its molecular mechanisms. Two independent rat HF models were established separately by intraperitoneal injection of isoproterenol hydrochloride (ISO) or by abdominal aortic constriction (AAC), whereas an in vitro HF model was induced by angiotensin II (Ang-II) in rat H9c2 cardiomyocytes. After 4 weeks of exercise training, serum NT-pro BNP levels were measured in the rats, and cardiac injury was assessed via HE staining and Masson staining. The expression of key genes and proteins was detected using RT‒qPCR, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence, and apoptosis was evaluated via TUNEL staining. RNA immunoprecipitation experiments were performed to validate the interaction between NEAT1 and ILF3. NEAT1 expression is upregulated in HF, and its knockdown can inhibit cellular damage in in vitro and in vivo HF models and improve cardiac function in rats. Additionally, exercise training reduces the expression of NEAT1 in the cardiac tissues of HF rats, and overexpression of NEAT1 weakens the inhibitory effect of exercise training on the progression of HF in rats, indicating that exercise training improves HF progression by suppressing NEAT1 expression. Mechanistic studies revealed that upregulated ILF3 in HF binds to NEAT1 to stabilize its expression, thereby activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway, which subsequently inhibits autophagy, ultimately leading to HF. Exercise training can downregulate NEAT1 expression, thereby suppressing abnormal activation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway and further relieving HF progression through the activation of autophagy. Additionally, NEAT1 expression is regulated by ILF3.

title: From maturation to degeneration: Distinct biological trajectories in bicuspid and tricuspid aortopathy.
authorString: Akhtar R, Riley DO, Madine J, Field M.
abstractText: Ascending thoracic aortic aneurysm formation differs fundamentally between patients with bicuspid (BAV) and tricuspid (TAV) aortic valve phenotypes, yet current clinical management largely relies on shared diameter thresholds, although clinical and scientific data fail to correlate with diameter and risk of rupture. Over the past two decades, histological, biochemical and biomechanical studies have revealed unique differences between dilated tissue properties from patients with BAV- and TAV-associated idiopathic degenerative ascending aortic aneurysms even at similar aortic diameters. This review focuses on histological, biochemical and biomechanical differences between BAV and TAV aortopathy with a focus on ageing. Idiopathic degenerative TAV aortopathy is characterised by medial degeneration with elastic lamellar fragmentation and loss, smooth muscle cell depletion, medial fibrosis, mucoid extracellular matrix accumulation and inflammatory features. These degenerative changes correlate with ageing and, in region-specific mechanical testing, with reduced delamination resistance and age-dependent biomechanical weakening. In contrast, BAV aortopathy frequently demonstrates relative preservation of medial architecture despite similar dilatation, alongside altered collagen maturation, and distinct osteogenic/microcalcification signatures. Lifespan analyses indicate that TAV follows a maturation-stabilisation-degeneration trajectory, whereas BAV exhibits aberrant vascular maturation without a true stabilisation phase. Importantly, aortic diameter correlates poorly with histological severity or biomechanical vulnerability, particularly in BAV. Collectively, these data support the concept that ascending thoracic aortic aneurysms in BAV and idiopathic degenerative TAV patients represent biologically divergent aortopathies requiring phenotype-informed risk stratification beyond diameter alone.

title: Associations Between Early Vascular Aging and Quality of Life in the Adult Population: Pooled Data From 2 Epidemiological Studies.
authorString: Fenoll-Morante M, Cavero-Redondo I, Fenoll-Morante N, Martinez-Rodrigo A, Saz-Lara A.
abstractText:
Background

Early vascular aging (EVA) is associated with increased cardiovascular risk and poor health-related quality of life. The extent to which EVA affects the physical and mental components of quality of life across different age groups remains insufficiently described.

Objective

We aimed to analyze the associations between EVA and the physical and mental components of quality of life and examine global associations and age-stratified differences.

Methods

A total of 583 participants from the EVasCu and VascuNet cohorts were analyzed. EVA was defined as a construct integrating 4 parameters (aortic pulse wave velocity, a-PWV; pulse pressure; glycosylated hemoglobin A1c, HbA1c; and advanced glycation end products, AGEs). Distance to healthy vascular aging (HVA) and the EVA/HVA ratio were computed. Health-related quality of life was assessed using the 12-item short form health survey.

Results

Physical quality of life was negatively correlated with EVA risk (r = -0.209; P = .001) and the distance to HVA (r = -0.240; P < .001) and positively correlated with the EVA/HVA ratio (r = 0.168; P < .001). Mental quality of life was negatively correlated with the EVA/HVA ratio (r = -0.095; P = .022). Significant differences in physical quality of life were found by EVA/HVA ratio in people aged 25-60 (P = .008) and >60 (P = .036).

Conclusions

Vascular deterioration is related to physical health and perceived emotional well-being, reinforcing the usefulness of the EVA model as a comprehensive marker of vascular aging. These findings suggest that individuals' perceptions of their physical and mental health are closely associated with EVA risk.

title: Elevated lithium levels in drinking water are associated with higher prevalence of Wolff-Parkinson-White diagnoses.
authorString: Teraoka JT, Agarwal A, Tang JJ, Dewland TA, Marcus GM.
abstractText:
Background

Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) and Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) are potentially highly symptomatic and, rarely, lethal arrhythmias associated with atrioventricular accessory pathways. While the etiology of accessory pathways remains largely unknown, they are frequently observed with Ebstein's Anomaly, a congenital heart disease associated with maternal medicinal lithium use. Therefore, we evaluated whether in utero exposure to lithium from environmental sources is associated with the prevalence of accessory pathways.

Methods

We conducted a county-level ecological comparison of lithium levels in drinking water versus prevalence of WPW diagnoses among patients < 18-years-old in California using multivariable logistic regression. Children were analyzed given their high likelihood to reside in the same county during fetal development. WPW cases were identified using diagnostic codes. Positive and negative controls, including falsification endpoints, were analyzed.

Results

Among 2,329,090 patients (mean age 8.2 ± 5.9 years, 47.8% female), 686 (0.03%) were diagnosed with WPW. Areas where lithium levels ≥ 75th percentile were associated with 71% greater odds of WPW (OR 1.71, 95% CI 1.44 to 2.03). Areas above the lithium health-based screening limit had 29% greater odds of WPW (OR 1.29, 95% CI 1.05 to 1.58). Similar results existed in a New York statewide cohort. In validation analyses, areas where lithium levels ≥ 75th percentile were associated with a higher prevalence of SVT, syncope, palpitations, and catheter ablation procedures.

Conclusions

Higher lithium levels in drinking water were associated with a greater prevalence of childhood-diagnosed WPW, implicating a potentially modifiable risk factor for the development of accessory pathways.

title: Right Ventricular Function Assessed by Speckle Tracking Echocardiography in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Pulmonary Valve Replacement.
authorString: Kucuk M, de Alba CG, Zablah J, Leahy R, Taylor A, Iskander C, Rajic B, Morgan GJ.
abstractText: The effect of pulmonary valve replacement (PVR) on right ventricular (RV) function remains unclear. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) is the gold standard for RV assessment but has practical limitations. Speckle tracking echocardiography (STE) may offer an alternative for evaluating RV systolic function. This study used STE to assess changes in RV systolic strain and right atrial (RA) strain following PVR. STE parameters including RV free-wall longitudinal strain (RVFWSL), RV four-chamber strain (RV4CSL), regional basal, mid-ventricular, apical RV strain, RA reservoir and contraction strain were assessed in 50 patients who underwent TPVR at pre-, post-operative day 1 and at six-month follow-up. RV systolic strain significantly improved after TPVR. RVFWSL increased from - 20.3 ± 5.1% at baseline to - 23.3 ± 5.2% (P < 0.001), and RV4CSL improved from - 18.5 ± 4.1% to - 21.3 ± 4.1% (P < 0.001). Regional RV strain also significantly improved at the basal, mid-cavity and apical levels (- 18.1 ± 4.3% to - 21.4 ± 5.5%, P < 0.001). RA reservoir and contraction strain, did not change significantly. Patients with RV end-systolic volume index < 80 mL/m<sup>2</sup> demonstrated greater improvement in RV4CSL than those with larger RV systolic volumes. Transcatheter PVR is associated with significant improvement in RV systolic strain at six months, with no significant change observed on postoperative day 1. This delayed recovery highlights the importance of longitudinal assessment, for which STE may serve as a feasible complementary tool to CMR in guiding follow-up imaging.

title: VSD Device Removal Due to Intermittent Complete Heart Block.
authorString: Farhati A, Ben Othman R, Msaad H, Hakim K, Arab R, Lehmayer E, Ouarda F.
abstractText:
Background

Percutaneous closure of perimembranous ventricular septal defects (pmVSDs) has markedly increased with the development of newer, softer occlusion devices.

Case summary

We report a 12-year-old girl who underwent percutaneous pmVSD closure. One week later, she was admitted for paroxysmal complete heart block (CHB). She was started on intravenous corticosteroids. A percutaneous retrieval of the device was performed successfully. Sinus rhythm was maintained throughout the 8-month follow-up period.

Discussion

Paroxysmal CHB is a rare but serious complication following percutaneous pmVSD closure. Its management remains challenging because of the potential for recurrence despite medical therapy. To our knowledge, percutaneous retrieval of a well-positioned ventricular septal defect occluder in this context represents the first case reported in the literature.

Take-home messages

Selecting the optimal device for pmVSD closure is crucial to ensure procedural success and reduce the risk of complications. CHB may occur immediately, early, or late after defect closure.

title: Updated systematic review and meta-analysis comparing Myval versus Sapien 3 transcatheter heart valves in severe aortic stenosis: focus on early and one-year mortality.
authorString: Yang L, Yu G, Pan M, Liu Y, Zhu Y, Zhang M, Yu H, Pei Z.
abstractText:
Background

Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a guideline-recommended treatment for severe aortic stenosis (AS). While the balloon-expandable Edwards Sapien 3 valve has long been the benchmark, the newer Myval valve has emerged as a potential alternative. Comparative data on mid-term survival, specifically one-year all-cause mortality, are lacking but crucial for clinical evaluation.

Methods

This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesised direct comparative evidence on the Myval versus Sapien 3 valves in patients undergoing TAVI, searching PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central up to November 2025. The primary outcomes included all-cause mortality within 30 days and 1 year. Secondary outcomes were 30-day safety events and hemodynamic parameters.

Results

Five studies (n = 2771) were included. The pooled analysis indicated no statistical difference in 30-day mortality (RR: 1.05, 95% CI: 0.53-2.07; p = 0.89; I2=0%) or in one-year all-cause mortality (RR: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.64-1.35; p = 0.70; I2=0%). Rates of stroke, major bleeding, pacemaker implantation, and other 30-day complications were also comparable (all p > 0.05). Hemodynamically, the Myval valve was superior at 30 days, with a lower mean gradient (MD: -2.37, 95% CI: -3.45 to -1.30; p < 0.0001) and larger effective orifice area (MD: 0.26, 95% CI: 0.17-0.35; p < 0.00001). Available one-year data from two randomised trials indicated this hemodynamic benefit was sustained.

Conclusion

This updated meta-analysis demonstrates that the newer Myval valve offers comparable early safety and one-year survival to the established Sapien 3 valve, with superior and sustained hemodynamic performance. These findings support its role as a safe and effective alternative in the TAVI landscape.

title: 1-Year Outcomes of Endovascular Repair of Zone 0/1 Aortic Arch Lesions with a Thoracic Branched Endoprosthesis.
authorString: Brinkman WT, Shutze WP, Gable DR, Sweet MP, Burke CR, Dake MD, Matsumura JS, Lee JT, Ohki T, Atkins MD, Leshnower BG, Patel HJ.
abstractText:
Background

The GORE® TAG® Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis (TBE) pivotal non-randomized, multicenter, prospective trial evaluated 1-year outcomes in patients at high risk for open surgical repair undergoing aortic arch and descending thoracic aorta endovascular repair (Zone 0/1).

Methods

Endpoints evaluated from endovascular procedure through 12 months included aortic-related death, disabling stroke, permanent paraplegia or paraparesis, new onset renal failure, and unanticipated reintervention. Core-lab identified endpoints included aortic rupture or enlargement (≥5 mm), Type I/III endoleak, device integrity, device migration, fistula, patency, and new dissection.

Results

The 77 enrolled patients had aneurysm (n=50), dissection (n=24), or other isolated lesion types (n=3); 90.9% had a Zone 0 proximal stent landing zone. Patients were a mean age of 70.8±10.8 years, 66.2% male, and 57.1% white and all had the aortic and side branch component implanted. Technical success was 94.8%. Early outcomes to 12 months included 8 (10.4%) aortic-related deaths, 6 (7.8%) disabling strokes (all aneurysm cohort), 4 (5.2%) unanticipated reintervention, 2 (2.6%) aortic ruptures, and 1 (1.3%) renal failure. Type IA/IB or Type III endoleaks occurred in 6 (7.8%) patients. Loss of side branch patency occurred in 1 (1.3%) patient. There was no permanent paraplegia or paraparesis or loss of device integrity or migration. A total of five patients had aortic enlargement; none required reintervention.

Conclusions

Early data from this prospective investigation of the TBE device in Zone 0/1 applications signals that the device is a reasonable therapeutic alternative in patients with appropriate anatomy deemed high risk for open arch surgery.

title: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair in hyperacute type B aortic dissection: a mini review.
authorString: Baek J.
abstractText: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) is established as the preferred treatment for many patients with complicated acute type B aortic dissection (TBAD). However, its role during the hyperacute phase (within 24 hours of symptom onset) remains controversial, as the acutely dissected aortic wall may be vulnerable to device-related injury. Nevertheless, hyperacute timing should not be regarded as an absolute contraindication to TEVAR. In patients with rupture, malperfusion, impending aortic rupture, persistent pain, refractory hypertension, or progressive true-lumen collapse, prompt entry-tear coverage can restore perfusion and prevent irreversible organ injury. Similarly, in patients without initial complications, high-risk anatomical features may help identify those who could benefit from early intervention. However, evidence supporting routine TEVAR within the first 24 hours remains limited and is predominantly observational. To ensure safe hyperacute TEVAR, careful assessment of the landing zones, conservative device sizing, avoidance of aggressive balloon molding, preservation of branch-vessel and spinal cord perfusion, and prompt recognition of retrograde type A dissection, stroke, spinal cord ischemia, and stent-graft-induced new entry are required. Ultimately, hyperacute TEVAR may be a reasonable option for selected patients with complicated TBAD, with a potential role in high-risk uncomplicated TBAD. Future prospective randomized trials integrating multimodal imaging and dynamic biomarkers are warranted to establish definitive criteria for timing and candidate selection.

title: Anticoagulation after transcatheter and surgical bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement: A narrative review.
authorString: Arab S, Chhatwal K, Mizori R, Rustogi A, Fuad M, Sokhal BS, Motairek I, Al-Shakarchi N, Ahmed R, Showkat M, Punjabi P.
abstractText: BackgroundBioprosthetic aortic valve replacement, specifically surgical (SAVR) and transcatheter (TAVR), is among the most frequently performed cardiac interventions globally, yet anticoagulation strategies after implantation remain incompletely defined. Atrial fibrillation, notably prevalent pre- and post-operatively in these patients, substantially amplifies thromboembolic risk and complicates decision-making in an already elderly, frail, and comorbid population.ObjectivesTo critically evaluate current anticoagulation strategies after bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement across sinus rhythm and atrial fibrillation in both SAVR and TAVR, and to identify evidence gaps and guideline inconsistencies.MethodsWe conducted a narrative review of major international guidelines (ESC/EACTS 2025, ACC/AHA 2020, and NICE 2021) and key clinical trials on antithrombotic therapy in valve replacement populations. Focus was placed on bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement, with mechanical and non-aortic valves excluded.ResultsAspirin monotherapy is the most consistently supported strategy after bioprosthetic TAVR in sinus rhythm, though guidelines diverge on duration and recommendation strength. In atrial fibrillation, all three guidelines apply uniform CHA<sub>2</sub>DS<sub>2</sub>-VASc-based frameworks irrespective of AF phenotype, procedural context, or detection modality, reflecting lacking evidence rather than deliberate clinical judgement. No trial has enrolled patients specifically with new-onset post-procedural AF or stratified by AF subtype, and subclinical AF after bioprosthetic AVR remains entirely uncharacterised.ConclusionsGuideline divergence reflects a structurally inadequate evidence base rather than genuine clinical equipoise. Individualised decisions informed by procedure type, AF phenotype, frailty, and bleeding risk are required to guide clinical practice, alongside an adequately powered stratified randomised trial incorporating mandatory continuous rhythm monitoring.

title: Comparison of Effectiveness of Caudal Dexmedetomidine vs. Caudal Fentanyl with Bupivacaine during Pediatric Cardiac Surgery with regards to Hemodynamic Fluctuations and Postoperative Pain.
authorString: Manwani RN, Wadaskar D, Panbude P, Mankhair S, Kanakam S.
abstractText:
Background

Optimum analgesia, reflecting into attenuation of stress response, is pertinent in pediatric cardiac surgery. Narcotics are still the mainstay in providing analgesia, and they are a common adjunct in caudal epidural analgesia. Unwanted effects of narcotics warrant a constant search for nonopioid analgesics.

Objective

To compare dexmedetomidine vs. fentanyl as an adjuvant in caudal anesthesia in pediatric cardiac surgery.

Materials and methods

Sixty patients, 1 to 8 years of age, with acyanotic congenital heart disease were divided into two groups randomly: group A received caudal dexmedetomidine 0.5 µg/kg with 2 mg/kg bupivacaine diluted to 1.6 ml/kg with normal saline. Group B received caudal fentanyl 1 µg/kg with 2 mg/kg bupivacaine diluted to 1.6 ml/kg with normal saline.

Results

Stress response assessed by surge in heart rate and blood pressure after induction was significantly lower in group A (Dexmedetomidine group). The mean time to successful discontinuation of mechanical ventilation was significantly lower in the dexmedetomidine group (1.2 ± 0.4 vs. 1.73 ± 0.58 h). Children in the dexmedetomidine group had lower FLACC pain scores at 4 hours postextubation (2.93 ± 1.04 vs. 3.83 ± 0.83), implying better pain control. The time to need for rescue analgesia was longer in the dexmedetomidine group (6.1 ± 1.21 vs. 3.96 ± 0.96 h).

Conclusion

Caudal dexmedetomidine gave better control of hemodynamic parameters when compared with fentanyl and was associated with earlier extubation postoperatively. It also has superior and prolonged analgesia compared to caudal fentanyl as an adjunct.

title: Platelet P2Y12 inhibitor use and risk of colorectal cancer incidence and colorectal cancer-related mortality: a Swedish registry-based cohort study.
authorString: Fuchs M, Ha J, Yan J, Bottai M, Song M, Simon TG, Ye W, Chan AT, Ludvigsson JF.
abstractText:
Background

Low-dose aspirin use is associated with reduced CRC incidence and CRC-related mortality. A similar association with P2Y12 inhibitor use remains uncertain. We investigated whether the use of P2Y12 inhibitors was associated with CRC incidence and CRC-related mortality among individuals diagnosed with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD).

Methods

From the ESPRESSO cohort, we identified 334,882 patients diagnosed with ASCVD between 2006 and 2021. We identified patients who initiated P2Y12 inhibitors ≥ 84 consecutive Defined Daily Doses (cDDDs). We estimated the risk of incident CRC and CRC mortality according to P2Y12 inhibitor use using Cox proportional-hazards regression models adjusting for potential confounders including comorbidities and regular aspirin use.

Results

We documented 4,015 incident CRC cases and 2,610 CRC-related deaths during a median follow-up of 5.1 years (IRQ, 2.1-9.0 years). We did not observe an association between P2Y12 inhibitor use and CRC incidence. In contrast, a longer duration of P2Y12 inhibitor use was associated with lower CRC-related mortality. Compared to non-users, multivariable-adjusted hazard ratio (HR) for CRC mortality were 0.73 (95% CI, 0.60-0.89) in patients with 336-671 cDDDs of P2Y12 inhibitor and 0.81 (95% CI, 0.68-0.97) in those with ≥672 cDDDs. Among patients with incident CRC diagnosis, subsequent initiation of P2Y12 inhibitor after CRC diagnosis was associated with significantly lower CRC mortality (HR 0.42; 95% CI, 0.29-0.60).

Conclusions

P2Y12 inhibitor use was not associated with risk of incident CRC but was significantly inversely associated with CRC mortality, which appeared to be due to improved survival among individuals who initiate P2Y12 inhibitors after CRC diagnosis. These findings merit further study given the observational nature of the analysis and potential for residual confounding.

title: Abnormal left ventricular mass as a prognostic marker for outcomes in infants and children with cirrhosis.
authorString: Bashir DA, Thadani S, Nack T, Gebara N, Gorgis N, Virk M, Banc Husu AM, Doan TT, Nguyen Galvan NT, Umair M Mian M, Hosek K, Fuller K, Patel KR, Sabapathy D, James ST, Fogarty T, Penny DJ, Dinh D, Kennedy CE, Desai MS.
abstractText:
Background/aims

Cirrhotic cardiomyopathy (CCM), a clinically consequential comorbidity of cirrhosis, remains undefined and underappreciated in children. This study aimed to characterize myocardial structural, functional, morphometric, and histopathologic features in pediatric cirrhosis and objectively derive a reliable echocardiographic (2DE) metric to predict perioperative adverse events, including mortality.

Methods

2DE, morphometry, histopathology, and vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS) were compared between children with (n=226) and without (n=160) cirrhosis listed for liver transplantation (LT) over 2011-2021. Discriminatory performance of left ventricular mass index (height)2.7(LVMI g/m2.7) for predicting waitlist decompensation, composite serious adverse events post liver transplant and mortality was assessed using ROC analysis, with AUCs and optimal thresholds compared against PELD-Cr/MELD scores.

Results

LV mass was significantly higher in children with cirrhosis on 2DE and necropsy specimens compared to non-cirrhotic controls, with ∼25% demonstrating LV hypertrophy, with OR of 6.9 [CI 3,16], p< 0.0001. In the cirrhotic cohort, LVMI correlated with vasoactive needs under stress of LT (p <0.001) and was significantly higher in patients with WLD, CSAE, and non-survivors. In cirrhosis, LVMI values ≥ 88 g/m2.7, ≥ 91 g/m2.7, and ≥ 95 g/m2.7 were independently associated with WLD, CSAE, and mortality, when adjusting for PELD-Cr/MELD, bilirubin, and INR (p <0.01). Combining LVMI + PELD-Cr/MELD significantly outperformed PELD-Cr/MELD in discriminating both WLD and CSAE, whereas LVMI alone significantly outperformed PELD-Cr/MELD for CSAE and was comparable for WLD. All three models performed comparably in discriminating death.

Conclusion

LVMI is a strong predictor of morbidity and mortality, serving as a prognostic marker in children with cirrhosis. Incorporating LVMI into PELD-Cr/MELD may enhance risk stratification and organ allocation.

title: A nonexercise equation to predict VO<sub>2</sub> peak in chronic heart failure: Integrating clinical variables for prognostic assessment.
authorString: Borghi-Silva A, Santos-de-Araújo AD, Montalvo S, Christle JW, Myers J.
abstractText:
Background

Peak oxygen consumption (pVO2) has been widely recognized to identify potential pathophysiological mechanisms of exercise intolerance and to stratify risk in patients with heart failure (HF).

Aims

To develop a non-exercise equation to estimate pVO2 (esVO2) and to determine its association with all-cause mortality.

Methods

A total of 5176 HF patients (age 48 ± 17 years) who underwent a CPET for clinical reasons, and were followed between May 2011, and December 1, 2023. Clinical and historical variables and forced expiratory volume in 1-s (FEV1) were used in a stepwise multivariate regression analysis to predict pVO2 measured from CPET. Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox proportional hazards analyses were used to determine the association between esVO2 and all-cause mortality.

Results

The first esVO2 model was significantly associated with pVO2 (multiple R = 0.73, P < 0.001). Two other models considered gender separately (male: multiple R = 0.72, P < 0.001 and female (multiple R = 0.70, P < 0.001). A fourth model was proposed when spirometry is not available (age, BMI, resting SBP, HR and gender (multiple R = 0.69, P < 0.001)). The fifth proposed model included history of atrial fibrillation and previous stroke (multiple R = 0.70, P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier survival curves differentiated patients according to esVO2 and pVO2 ≤ and > 14 mL/kg-1 per min-1. Univariate Cox proportional hazard analyses indicated significant prognostic value when esVO2 and pVO2 were ≤ 14 mL/kg-1 per min-1 (P = 0.001).

Conclusions

Multivariable nonexercise models combining spirometry and/or clinical variables commonly obtained during a clinical assessment predict pVO2 reasonably accurately in HF.

title: Preoperative levels of biomarkers of coagulation to predict massive bleeding after surgical repair for acute type A aortic dissection: a retrospective cohort study.
authorString: Norén E, Ede J, Larsson M, Nozohoor S, Sjögren J, Teurneau-Hermansson K.
abstractText:
Background

Acute type A aortic dissection is a highly emergent condition with a high mortality rate. The condition poses an imminent risk of serious complications such as coagulopathy with massive bleeding. This increases the risk of mortality even after surgical repair. Procoagulant drugs are routinely administered but some patients still suffer postoperative massive bleeding that can be fatal. The study aimed to investigate whether massive bleeding after surgical treatment for type A aortic dissection can be predicted preoperatively through routine coagulation tests such as APTT, PT (INR), fibrinogen, D-dimer, and platelets.

Methods

The study was a retrospective, single-center, cohort study performed at a tertiary cardiac surgery unit. A total of 474 patients who underwent surgery for type A aortic dissection at our department between January 2005 and May 2023 were included in the study. Of these, 87 patients had massive postoperative bleeding after surgery for type A aortic dissection and were compared to 387 patients who did not have massive postoperative bleeding. Uni- and multivariable analyses were performed using logistic regression. The multivariable model included predictors of massive bleeding. Bleeding-related routine lab variables were then forced into the model.

Results

Patients with massive bleeding (18%) had higher preoperative activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) (33 s vs 29 s, p<0.01), and creatinine (97 µmol/L vs 87 µmol/L, p<0.01), as well as lower preoperative platelet counts (172 × 109/L vs 187 × 109/L, p=0.03) compared to patients without massive bleeding. Patients with massive bleeding also had longer duration of cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) (221 min vs 170 min, p<0.01) and suffered more postoperative complications. Multivariable logistic regression identified preoperative APTT per mmol increment (OR 1.04 (95% CI 1.01-1.07, p=0.01), preoperative APTT > 34.5 s (OR 2.95 (95% CI 1.60-5.47), p<0.01), preoperative creatinine > 82.5 µmol/L (OR 2.16 (95% CI 1.15-4.06), p=0.02), hypertension (OR 1.83 (95% CI 1.01-3.32), p<0.05) and CPB time per 10 min increment (OR 1.09 (95% CI 1.05-1.13, p<0.01)) as independent predictors of massive bleeding.

Conclusion

Preoperative APTT exceeding 34.5 s was independently associated with massive bleeding after type A aortic dissection repair and may, pending prospective validation, help identify patients who could potentially benefit from earlier hemostatic intervention.

title: Development and Validation of an Adult Medical Urgency Score for US Donor Heart Allocation.
authorString: Lyden GR, White M, Ahn DJ, Menteer J, Daly RC, Narang N, Khush KK, Jasseron C, Dorent R, Masotti M, Wood NL, Colvin MM, Gentry SE, Parker WF.
abstractText:
Importance

One in 5 heart transplant candidates in the US die or are delisted without transplant. Donor hearts are currently allocated by a 6-status therapy-based system criticized for limited risk stratification and susceptibility to gaming.

Objective

To develop a new heart allocation policy based on an objective medical urgency score that ranks candidates based on the interaction between physiology and mechanical circulatory support.

Design, setting, and participants

Registry-based observational study using data from the US organ transplant system. All adult (aged ≥18 years) heart transplant candidates from January 2019 to August 2025 were included, split into training (2019-2023), validation (2023-2024), and test (2024-2025) datasets.

Main outcomes and measures

A marginal structural model of 6-week mortality without transplant was estimated (the US Candidate Risk Score [US-CRS]). Eight models were compared in held-out data by weighted time-dependent area under the curve (AUC) and calibration by status. Finally, US-CRS was converted into an allocation policy and a match-run simulation of waitlist reordering was performed compared with the current 6-status system.

Results

Adult heart transplant candidates were partitioned into consecutive training (n = 21 859), validation (n = 7897), and test (n = 8256) datasets (mean [SD] age, 53 [13] years; 74% male). The chosen US-CRS model included 5 laboratory values and 4 therapeutic devices (durable left ventricular assist device, intra-aortic balloon pump, microaxial flow pump, and advanced mechanical circulatory support). In test-set cross-sections of candidates actively waiting on the same calendar date, US-CRS had similar or significantly higher time-dependent AUC than the current 6-status system (mean AUC, 0.807 vs 0.693, respectively) and acceptable calibration by status, especially for candidates who received their status by exception. In match-run analysis (n = 45 530 donor hearts), a US-CRS-based system led to 67% of transplant recipients moving down in rank order and increased observed 6-week transplant-censored mortality for the first candidate on the match run from 11.2% (95% CI, 10.1%-12.5%) under the current system to 15.7% (95% CI, 13.9%-17.6%) under the US-CRS-based system.

Conclusions and relevance

In this registry-based study of US heart transplant candidates, a US-CRS-based allocation system prioritized sicker candidates with higher mortality without transplant compared with the current medical urgency statuses.

title: The Importance of Family Centered Care and Cascade Screening in Patients with Heritable Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm Disease.
authorString: Schwartz BJ, Starr LJ, Cratsenberg D, Gonzalez V, Yetman AT.
abstractText: Heritable thoracic aortic aneurysm diseases (HTAAD) may be either syndromic or non-syndromic. While family screening for all forms of HTAAD has been recommended, providing care to an entire family is often fragmented in our siloed healthcare delivery model. We sought to determine the frequency of cascade family screening in the current era with either cardiovascular imaging (cascade cardiac screening) and/or genetic testing (cascade genetic screening), and to assess the impact of such testing on adverse outcomes in first degree family members. Of the 184 HTAAD patients who presented to our academic center without a known family history of aneurysmal disease, 84 were followed in a cardiology clinic, 40 in a genetics clinic and 60 in a combined cardiovascular genetics clinic for both children and adults. Cascade cardiac or genetic screening of ≥ 1 family member occurred during the course of care in 138 of 184 (75%) families. Complete cascade screening (genetic and/or cardiac) of all at-risk first-degree family members occurred in only 61 (33%) families and varied by clinic type (12%, 10% and 78%, p = 0.001) for those initially evaluated in a cardiology, genetics, or combined cardiovascular genetics clinic. As a result of cascade screening or an aortic event, 461 additional family members were identified as at risk for an aortic event. Of these, 53 family members from 42 families experienced an unexpected HTAAD-related event. Cascade screening was associated with a lower incidence of an event (1/53 vs. 52/53, p < 0.0001) during follow-up. Clinics that offer family-based care and on-site cascade screening facilitate timely diagnosis and intervention thereby reducing mortality from aortic disease.

title: Association of chronic kidney disease with major cardiovascular outcomes following lower extremity endovascular revascularization.
authorString: Khan N, Shah H, Rodriguez de la Vega P, Seetharamaiah R, Vaidean G.
abstractText:
Objective

Chronic kidney disease (CKD) amplifies cardiovascular risk, yet its stage-specific influence on perioperative outcomes following endovascular lower extremity revascularization (LER) for peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains poorly characterized.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the ACS NSQIP registry (2013-2022). Adults undergoing endovascular LER for PAD were stratified by preoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) via the CKD-EPI 2021 equation: G1 (≥90), G2 (60-89), G3 (30-59), G4 (15-29), and G5 (<15 mL/min/1.73 m2 or dialysis dependent). The primary outcome was 30-day major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: myocardial infarction, stroke, or death). Multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI).

Results

Among 22,424 patients (64.6% aged ≥65 years; 36.1% women), comorbidity burden increased progressively with CKD stage. Within 30 days, 556 patients (2.5%) experienced MACE. Event rates rose stepwise: 1.5% (G1), 1.6% (G2), 2.7% (G3), 4.9% (G4), and 6.0% (G5). After adjustment for age, sex, race/ethnicity, ASA class, admission status, presenting symptoms, and preoperative hematocrit, advanced CKD remained independently associated with MACE: OR 2.30 (95% CI 1.50-3.52) for G4 and OR 3.15 (95% CI 2.28-4.35) for G5 versus G1.

Conclusion

CKD stage provides independent prognostic information in patients undergoing endovascular LER. Advanced CKD independently predicts 30-day MACE with a dose-response relationship across stages. Preoperative eGFR should be incorporated into perioperative risk stratification protocols to guide cardiovascular optimization and surveillance planning.

title: Calprotectin Accelerates Pathogenic Calciprotein Particle Maturation to Promote Vascular Calcification in Chronic Kidney Disease.
authorString: Zhang J, Kanki T, Tsushida M, Komaba H, Date R, Fujimoto D, Kakizoe Y, Izumi Y, Adachi M, Mukoyama M, Yokoi H, Kuwabara T.
abstractText:
Background

Vascular calcification is a hallmark of chronic kidney disease (CKD)-mineral and bone disorder and a major determinant of cardiovascular mortality. Secondary calciprotein particles (CPP2) are key mediators of vascular calcification; however, the mechanisms regulating their maturation and pathogenic properties remain incompletely understood. CPT (Calprotectin, S100A8/A9), a myeloid-derived inflammatory mediator, is elevated in CKD and predicts cardiovascular events and mortality, particularly under high-phosphate conditions, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.

Methods

We investigated the role of CPT in vascular calcification using CKD-mineral and bone disorder mice with myeloid-specific CPT deletion. Aortic calcification was assessed by ex vivo imaging, histology, and calcium quantification. Serum calciprotein particle (CPP) fractions were determined by flow cytometry. Mechanistic studies were performed in vascular smooth muscle cells exposed to CPP2 in the presence or absence of macrophage-derived CPT. Calcification propensity was evaluated using the T50 assay, and CPP2 elemental composition was analyzed by high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy-energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy.

Results

Myeloid-specific CPT deletion significantly attenuated aortic calcification and osteogenic gene expression in CKD-mineral and bone disorder mice without altering renal function or systemic mineral parameters. These changes were accompanied by an increased circulating immature CPP fraction. Macrophage-derived CPT markedly enhanced CPP2-induced vascular smooth muscle cell calcification by accelerating CPP maturation, reflected by a shortened T50, and by altering CPP2 composition to be enriched in calcium and phosphate. Although no direct interaction between CPT and CPPs was detected, CPT modified the physicochemical milieu, including ionized calcium and pH. Consistently, CPP2 from CPT-deficient serum exhibited substantially reduced calcification potency, indicating that CPT shapes CPP pathogenicity by modulating particle quality rather than quantity. Importantly, CPT-mediated CPP maturation occurred in a cell-free milieu, indicating a TLR4-independent mechanism distinct from its known receptor-mediated actions.

Conclusions

CPT is a previously unrecognized regulator of pathogenic CPP maturation and composition, thereby promoting vascular calcification in CKD-mineral and bone disorder. Targeting CPT may represent a novel therapeutic strategy to attenuate vascular calcification in CKD.

title: The Prognostic Value of Entropy from T1 Mapping in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
authorString: Zhao J, Guo J, He J, Chen C, Liu X, Yin L, Pu S, Li Y, Xu Y, Wang J, Wan K, Han Y, Chen Y.

journal.title: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance

abstractText:
Background

The prognostic value of left ventricular (LV) entropy from T1 mapping in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains unexplored.

Study design and methods

This prospective study enrolled patients with PAH who underwent cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) within 72h of right heart catheterization (RHC). Myocardial native T1, extracellular volume fraction (ECV) and entropy were calculated in mid-ventricular short-axis slice. The primary endpoint was defined as all-cause mortality or lung transplantation. Outcomes were further analyzed across groups stratified by survival status using Cox proportional hazards regression and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis.

Results

A total of 312 patients were analyzed over a median follow-up of 36.10 months, with 59 deaths. Elevated LV entropy was positively correlated with log-transformed NT-proBNP, right ventricular (RV) end-systolic, end-diastolic volume indices, LV native T1 and ECV, and inversely correlated with RV ejection fraction (all P < 0.01). LV entropy did not differ significantly across etiological subgroups, whereas LV entropy without IPs was higher in congenital heart disease-associated PAH. Both LV entropy ≥8.60 and LV entropy without IPs ≥8.30 independently predicted all-cause mortality (HR, 2.207; 95% CI, 1.324-3.678; P = 0.002; and HR, 2.357; 95% CI, 1.405-3.955; P = 0.001, respectively) and were associated with reduced survival (both log-rank P < 0.005). Adding LV entropy improved ESC models (χ²: 55.79 to 60.61, C-statistic: 0.782 to 0.801) and ESC-CMR models (χ²: 35.31 to 41.77, C-statistic: 0.805 to 0.813).

Conclusions

Elevated LV entropy was related to disease severity, RV dysfunction, and adverse clinical outcomes, and served as an independent predictor of all-cause mortality in patients with PAH.
