gov; Unique identifier: ChiCTR1800019314 and ChiCTR1900025518.

title: High-Potency P2Y12 Inhibitors Among Patients With Chronic Coronary Syndrome Undergoing PCI: An Analysis From the NCDR CathPCI Registry.
authorString: Fath AR, Rymer J, Marks A, Wojdyla D, Gilchrist IC, Sandoval Y, Shah B, Brilakis E, Rao SV, Elgendy IY.
abstractText:
Background

Clinical practice guidelines recommend the use of clopidogrel among patients with chronic coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention. The frequency of high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors, such as ticagrelor or prasugrel, in this setting is not well known.

Methods

Using the National Cardiovascular Data Registry CathPCI registry, we analyzed patients with chronic coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention from April 2018 to June 2024, excluding those discharged on oral anticoagulants. Temporal trends in high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor prescription were examined. A mixed-effects multivariable logistic regression model with a random intercept for hospital was used to identify patient-, procedural-, and institutional-level factors associated with high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor prescription while accounting for within-hospital clustering. Between-hospital variation was quantified using the median odds ratio.

Results

Among 783 977 patients across 1815 hospitals, 35% were prescribed a high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor at discharge. The use of high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors declined from 35% in 2018 to 31% in 2024 (P-trend=0.019), driven by a reduction in ticagrelor (from 29% to 23%, P-trend <0.001) despite a modest increase in prasugrel use (from 6.2% to 8%, P-trend=0.10). Male sex, prior myocardial infarction, and markers of procedural complexity (high-complexity/type C lesions, left main coronary artery, proximal left anterior descending artery, or use of mechanical circulatory support) were associated with higher odds of high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor prescription. In contrast, older age (≥75 years), prior stroke/transient ischemic attack, prior coronary artery bypass graft, severe renal dysfunction, and chronic total occlusion were associated with lower odds. University hospitals had lower odds of prescribing high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors, with considerable variability in prescription patterns among institutions (median odds ratio, 2.59).

Conclusions

Nearly one-third of chronic coronary syndrome patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention were discharged on high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors, with decreasing trends over time. Practice patterns reflected perceived ischemic versus bleeding risk and significant institutional variation, underscoring opportunities for quality improvement and guideline alignment.

title: A Combined Network Toxicology and Docking Study to Identify Putative Molecular Targets Linking Styrene Exposure to Atherosclerosis.
authorString: Yan S, Shen G, Huang YQ, He GD.
abstractText:
Background

Styrene is a ubiquitous volatile organic compound linked to hematologic and vascular alterations; however, the molecular mechanisms connecting exposure to atherosclerosis remain poorly characterized.

Methods

We integrated peripheral blood mononuclear cell transcriptomic profiles (GSE23746) with toxicogenomic data from the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database, applying support vector machine recursive feature elimination and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator machine learning algorithms to identify core targets at the styrene-atherosclerosis intersection. Immune infiltration was assessed using CIBERSORT and single-sample gene set enrichment analysis, and molecular docking evaluated binding potential.

Results

Four model genes-CCND3, CCR1, MYC, and MYD88-were identified and constituted a diagnostic signature with high accuracy (area under the curve > 0.9). These genes were enriched in IL-17 and NF-κB inflammatory pathways and correlated with distinct immune cell alterations, particularly neutrophils and T cell subsets. Molecular docking predicted direct, moderate-affinity binding of styrene to CCND3 (Vina score = -6.4 kcal/mol), involving multiple contacts within the cyclin domain.

Discussion

The convergence of transcriptomic screening and molecular docking identifies CCND3 as a putative target for styrene-protein interaction and suggests a mechanistic hypothesis linking styrene to atherosclerosis via inflammatory and immune dysregulation. The computational framework provides a basis for future experimental validation.

Conclusion

This computational framework generates the hypothesis that styrene may contribute to atherosclerosis through coordinated perturbations of immune signaling and cell cycle regulation, with CCND3 representing a candidate molecular target for future experimental validation in styrene-exposed populations.

title: ATF4 alleviates doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy by promoting H<sub>2</sub>S production and antioxidant defense.
authorString: Xu S, Shi Y, Zhao X, Chen X, Liu Y, Zhang F, Yu F, Jiang X, Zhang G.
abstractText: Doxorubicin (DOX) remains a cornerstone in cancer treatment. However, its clinical utilization is significantly hampered by dose-dependent cardiotoxicity. The generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) constitutes the central component of the pathogenesis of DOX-induced cardiotoxicity. Activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4) has been demonstrated to exert a cardioprotective effect and augment cardiac antioxidative capacity in settings of heart failure. To explore the role of ATF4 in DOX-induced cardiomyopathy, cardiac-specific ATF4 conditional heterozygous mice and AAV9 mediated ATF4 overexpression mouse models were utilized. Cardiac function was assessed by echocardiography. The upstream regulator and downstream mediator of ATF4 were evaluated using RNA-seq analysis and further verified using ChIP assay and luciferase reporter assay. ATF4<sup>+/-</sup> mice exhibited a higher degree of susceptibility to DOX-induced cardiotoxicity in comparison with ATF4<sup>flox/flox</sup> mice. In contrast, cardiac-specific overexpression of ATF4 by AAV9 confers robust cardioprotection against DOX-induced cardiomyopathy. Mechanistically, we identified the upstream regulator of ATF4 as KLF16. Further, the decrease of ATF4 led to a reduction in cystathionine γ-lyase (CSE) transcription and hydrogen sulfide (H<sub>2</sub>S) production in the context of DOX-induced cardiotoxicity. ChIP and luciferase reporter assays revealed that ATF4 functioned as the transcription factor of the CSE gene. In contrast, the ectopic expression of ATF4 mitigated oxidative stress and apoptosis in DOX-induced cardiotoxicity, both in vivo and in vitro. The study identified a novel function of ATF4 in opposing oxidative stress in DOX cardiotoxicity through the promotion of CSE transcription. Targeting ATF4 may offer therapeutic benefits for DOX-induced cardiomyopathy.

title: Linking obesity and type 2 diabetes: Mechanistic insights and personalized nutritional strategies.
authorString: Banu M, Ambaru PSB.
abstractText: BackgroundGlobally, the incidence of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and obesity is increasing at an alarming rate, with the World Health Organization reporting a sharp rise in both conditions over the past two decades. The emerging concept of "diabesity" underscores the close interconnection between excessive weight gain and the development of T2DM, together posing a major global public health challenge. Obesity directly and indirectly contributes to chronic diseases such as diabetes, atherosclerosis, hypertension, and certain cancers. Obese individuals show altered levels of inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor-α, and C-reactive protein, and this inflammation from visceral adiposity promotes insulin resistance, a key mechanism in T2DM development.AimThis narrative review aims to: (1) explore the pathophysiological mechanisms linking obesity to T2DM, with an emphasis on adipose tissue dysfunction, chronic low-grade inflammation, and insulin resistance; and (2) critically evaluate the potential of personalized nutrition-tailored dietary and lifestyle interventions based on an individual's metabolic, genetic, and lifestyle profile as a preventive strategy against diabesity.MethodsTo provide a comprehensive grasp of the subject, pertinent research on obesity, T2DM mechanisms, and personalized dietary approaches was found, examined, and summarized.SummaryVisceral adiposity and other obesity-related metabolic abnormalities play an important role in insulin resistance, a significant underlying mechanism in the aetiology of type 2 diabetes. By transcending the "one-size-fits-all" paradigm, personalized nutrition facilitates more precise and sustainable prevention and management of diabesity. "Personalized nutrition may transform diabetes management and prevention when incorporated into public health frameworks.

title: Novel Compound Heterozygous ATAD3A Variants in Harel-Yoon Syndrome With Congenital Cataracts and Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Wen T, Chen H, Yu L, Zhang X.

journal.title: American journal of medical genetics. Part A

abstractText: Harel-Yoon syndrome is a rare mitochondrial disorder caused by pathogenic variants in ATAD3A, typically characterized by neonatal respiratory insufficiency, cataracts, developmental delay, hypotonia, and cerebellar atrophy. We report a pediatric patient with compound heterozygous missense variants in ATAD3A (c.655C>T, p.R219C and c.980G>C, p.R327P) who presented with an atypical phenotype manifested as early-onset congenital cataracts and progressive dilated cardiomyopathy. Notably the patient did not show typical neurological manifestations nor the cardiac presentations of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. The maternally inherited c.655C>T variant was absent from population databases, while paternally inherited c.980G>C was previously associated with Harel-Yoon syndrome. In silico protein structure modeling demonstrated that the mutant ATAD3A hexamer showed a looser and more disorganized conformation compared to that of the wild-type, suggesting functional impairment. This case expands the phenotypic spectrum of ATAD3A-related disorders and highlights the importance of long-term surveillance in patients with ATAD3A variants, even in the absence of classical neurological features. In addition, our findings support the inclusion of ATAD3A in the genetic differential diagnosis for patients with congenital cataracts and cardiomyopathy.

title: Genetic susceptibility in Takotsubo syndrome: a candidate gene association analysis in the French TAKOGENE cohort.
authorString: Nicolas L, Garnier S, Gerbaud E, Paganelli F, Doyen D, Motreff P, Meimoun P, Donal E, Probst V, Ducrocq G, Aupetit JF, Cohen A, Tribouilloy C, Nallet O, Lamblin N, Logeart D, Moulin F, Durand E, Varenne O, Lim P, Lieng T, Olaso R, Lechner D, Deleuze JF, Charron P, Mansencal N, TAKOGENE Consortium.
abstractText: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) is a stress-induced left ventricular (LV) cardiomyopathy with an unclear genetic predisposition. We investigated whether single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) previously associated with other cardiomyopathies or LV physiological traits contribute to TTS susceptibility. We conducted a case-control study based on the French multicentre TAKOGENE study (NCT01520610), including 261 unrelated TTS patients and 259 sex- and age-matched controls presenting with acute coronary syndrome. All participants were of European ancestry. A total of 325 SNPs were selected from large-scale genome-wide association studies of cardiomyopathies (n=202) and LV structural/functional traits (n=123), derived from polygenic risk scores. Genotyping was performed using the Infinium OmniExpressExome-8 array. Associations were assessed by logistic regression under an additive model, adjusted for age and sex, with group-specific Bonferroni correction. A sensitivity analysis compared the 261 TTS cases with 973 French population controls from the EPP3 cohort. After quality control and statistical analysis, seventeen SNPs (nine related to cardiomyopathies and eight to LV traits) showed nominal associations (P < 0.05), but none remained significant after group-specific Bonferroni correction. The strongest signal was observed for rs6885658 in the CPEB4 gene (OR 1.62, 95% CI 1.23-2.15; P = 5.8 × 10<sup>-4</sup>) related to cardiomyopathy traits. The EPP3 population-control sensitivity analysis was consistent with the primary analysis, with no association remaining significant after correction. In conclusion, common genetic variants previously associated with cardiomyopathies or LV traits do not appear to have a major effect on TTS risk. These findings support a disease-specific polygenic architecture of TTS, distinct from that underlying chronic cardiomyopathies and baseline LV traits. Future studies should explore alternative approaches, such as pathway-based analyses focusing on stress-response mechanisms.

title: C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index and diabetic vascular complications risk among patients with diabetes: a national cohort study.
authorString: Xiong S, Wang H, Wang B, Mu M, Zhang L, Lai X.
abstractText:
Introduction

The C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI) has emerged as an innovative biomarker for insulin resistance and inflammatory processes. Nevertheless, the association between CTI and diabetic vascular complications (DVCs) and its subtypes in individuals with diabetes remains unclear.

Methods

This cohort study included 23 068 participants with diabetes from the UK Biobank at baseline (2006-2010). Cox proportional hazards models and restricted cubic splines (RCS) were employed to evaluate the associations of CTI and triglyceride-glucose-related indices with the risk of DVCs and its subtypes. Separate analyses were conducted for individuals with type 2 diabetes (T2D). The predictive performance of these indices was assessed using the net reclassification index (NRI) and Harrell's concordance index.

Results

During a mean follow-up period of 13.3 years, 4089 (26.8%) individuals developed DVCs. A significant positive linear relationship was observed between CTI and the risk of incident DVCs. For 1 SD increase in CTI, the corresponding HRs (95% CIs) were 1.05 (1.02 to 1.11) for overall DVCs, 1.21 (1.16 to 1.27) for diabetic kidney disease, 1.19 (1.13 to 1.26) for diabetic retinopathy (DR), 1.34 (1.26 to 1.43) for diabetic neuropathy (DN), 1.22 (1.14 to 1.31) for peripheral artery disease (PAD) and 1.05 (1.00 to 1.10) for cardiovascular disease. RCS revealed approximately an inverse L-shaped relationship for DR, DN and PAD. The addition of CTI to the model significantly improved NRI and Harrell's concordance index for DVCs incidence.

Conclusions

Our findings demonstrated a significant positive association between CTI and the incidence of DVCs in individuals with T1D and T2D. Furthermore, our study revealed dose-response relationships between CTI and all subtypes of DVCs, providing more comprehensive risk stratification information for individuals with diabetes.

title: Cytoprotective effect of microencapsulated Vaccinium floribundum Kunth on porcine vascular wall mesenchymal stem cells under serum deprivation conditions.
authorString: Biondolillo G, Tubon I, Antognoni F, Melotti L, Salaroli R, Zannoni A, Bernardini C.
abstractText: Vascular Wall Mesenchymal Stem Cells (VW-MSC) are vascular-resident stem cells with multipotent differentiation ability, contributing to vascular homeostasis and repair. Their secretome, including growth factors, cytokines, and extracellular vesicles, mediates paracrine effects on angiogenesis, immunity, and tissue regeneration. Given the pivotal role of VW-MSC in vascular repair and their sensitivity to environmental stressors, bioactive plant-derived compounds have emerged as promising modulators of their survival and regenerative potential. In the present study, we investigated the protective potential of microencapsulated extract of Vaccinium floribundum Kunth (VFM) berries on porcine VW-MSC exposed to serum deprivation induced cytotoxicity. Our results demonstrated that VFM extract did not alter pVW-MSC morphology but enhanced cell viability. Serum deprivation induced loss of cell adhesion, cell rounding, membrane blebbing, and reduced pVW-MSC viability by ~50%, whereas VFM treatment restored normal morphology and viability. Gene expression analysis revealed a significant decrease in caspase-3 expression, suggesting a possible attenuation of apoptosis. No significant changes in BAX, BCL2l1 or TP53 were detected. These effects are consistent with VFM bioactive compounds previously associated with cytoprotective and antioxidant activities in a model of porcine Aortic Endothelial Cells. Collectively, our results suggest that VFM supports pVW-MSC survival under stress conditions by modulating apoptosis and highlight its potential as a protective agent for stem cell-based regenerative and cardiovascular applications.

title: Aggregatibacter aphrophilus bacteraemia with suspected infective endocarditis in a patient with bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement and atrial septal defect repair.
authorString: Co DG, Misra T, Lin L, Mok M, Mina N, Kadhim T, Losie JA.
abstractText: Introduction. Despite the established pathogenicity of Aggregatibacter aphrophilus, few clinical cases have been described in published literature. A. aphrophilus is a rare cause of prosthetic valve endocarditis and diagnosis is challenging based on nonspecific symptoms on presentation. High clinical suspicion for infective endocarditis is warranted in patients with cardiac prosthetic material and positive blood cultures. Poor dentition and dental procedures, along with other risk factors, are associated with A. aphrophilus bacteraemia. We describe a case of A. aphrophilus bacteraemia in which the diagnosis of infective endocarditis was complicated by equivocal echocardiographic findings and an initially challenging Gram stain interpretation. Case Presentation. A 59-year-old male patient with a history of bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement, atrial septal defect repair and remote dental cleaning presented to the emergency department with persistent high fevers, headaches and lethargy. Initial blood cultures were drawn and were positive for 'Gram-positive organisms', but specific morphology was challenging to determine. Subsequent testing, including MALDI-TOF, confirmed the growth of A. aphrophilus. Conclusion. Rapid identification of A. aphrophilus and recognition of the potential for infective endocarditis are paramount to ensuring adequate treatment initiation and success. This case highlights the diagnostic difficulty associated with initial Gram stain interpretation of this fastidious organism.

title: Fatal thoracic aortic transection following a motor vehicle collision: Medico-legal significance of the seat belt sign.
authorString: Wijenayaka PRC, Perera UCP, Warushahennadi J.
abstractText: Traumatic thoracic aortic transection is one of the most lethal consequences of blunt chest trauma; it is commonly associated with high-speed deceleration injuries in road traffic collisions. Despite advances in trauma management, survival rates remain poor due to rapid internal haemorrhage and the presence of multiple associated injuries. We report a fatal case of thoracic aortic transection in a 50-year-old restrained male driver involved in a high-velocity head-on collision with a truck. Following admission, he presented with hypotension, left-sided flail chest, multiple long bone fractures and reduced consciousness. Although emergency resuscitation was initiated, he developed sudden cardiovascular collapse during radiological evaluation and could not be revived. Medico-legal autopsy revealed a patterned seat belt contusion across the anterior chest wall, multiple rib fractures, extensive mediastinal haemorrhage, left-sided haemothorax and a circumferential full-thickness transection of the proximal descending thoracic aorta distal to the left subclavian artery. Toxicological analysis detected alcohol and morphine. This case highlights the characteristic pathological features of traumatic thoracic aortic injury and emphasises the medico-legal significance of the seat belt sign in identifying severe underlying thoracic trauma and reconstructing fatal motor vehicle collisions.

title: A Pilot Study of Photon Counting CT Spectral Analysis Following Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma Resection to Differentiate Local Recurrence From Postsurgical Fibrosis.
authorString: Platt S, Bansal B, Bagga B, O'Donnell T, Dane B.
abstractText:
Objective

To assess photon counting CT (PCCT) spectral parameters in the differentiation of locally recurrent pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC) from benign postsurgical fibrosis after PDAC surgical resection.

Methods

Twenty-two patients [12 male, mean±SD: age 71 (8) y] who underwent pancreas protocol PCCT following surgery for PDAC were retrospectively identified. Local recurrence required tissue histopathology or enlarging FDG-avid soft tissue. Nonrecurrence required soft-tissue reduction with stable or decreased CA 19-9. Two blinded radiologists independently drew regions of interest within the surgical bed soft tissue to determine iodine density (I), I normalized to aortic enhancement (I%), fat fraction, and extracellular volume (ECV), which were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test. A P<0.05 indicated statistical significance. The intraclass correlation coefficient was used to assess inter-reader reliability. ROC analysis was performed using mean measurements.

Results

On pancreatic parenchymal phase imaging, median [IQR] postcontrast attenuation for patients with nonrecurrence (n=10) and recurrence (n=11) was 32.3 (16.4 to 42.9 HU) and 57.0 (50.2 to 65.5 HU)(P=0.001); enhancement was 23.7 (10.2 to 26.0 HU) and 40.0 (34.4 to 44.5 HU) (P=0.001); I was 0.6 (0.5 to 0.90 mg/mL) and 1.8 (1.5 to 2.0 mg/mL) (P<0.001); I% was 8.3 (6.3% to 11.1%) and 34.3 (29.8% to 40.9%) (P<0.001); and ECV was 5.8 (4.4 to 6.9 mL) and 23.0 (18.0 to 25.8 mL) (P<0.001), respectively. To differentiate nonrecurrent from recurrent soft tissue, a postcontrast 45.7 HU threshold had 100% sensitivity and 80% specificity [AUC=0.92 (0.80-1.00)]; enhancement of 31.9 HU had 81.8% sensitivity and 100% specificity [AUC=0.98 (0.93-1.00)]; 14.0 mL ECV had 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity [AUC=1.00 (1.00-1.00)]; 1.27 mg/mL I had 90.9% sensitivity and 100% specificity [AUC=0.99 (0.98-1.00)]; and 20.3% I% had 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity (AUC=1.00). Inter-reader agreement was near-perfect (ICCs 0.86 to 0.96).

Conclusions

PCCT spectral parameters demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance in differentiating locally recurrent PDAC from postsurgical fibrosis on pancreatic parenchymal phase imaging.

title: Hodgkin Lymphoma With Sarcoid-Like Reaction: Importance of Clinicopathological Correlation in Granulomatous Lymphadenopathy.
authorString: Fujita R, Ono S, Sakamoto S, Taguchi H, Senzaki S, Kakiwaki A, Nishimura N, Yoneima R, Matsubara M, Morita T, Yada N, Yoshimoto K.

journal.title: The American journal of case reports

abstractText: BACKGROUND Sarcoid-like reaction, characterized by noncaseating epithelioid granulomas, occurs in 13.8% of Hodgkin lymphoma cases. When the granulomatous component is prominent and neoplastic cells are scarce, the initial biopsy may lead to a misdiagnosis of sarcoidosis. Reliance on pathological findings alone, without integration of the clinical context, can result in considerable diagnostic delay. CASE REPORT A 63-year-old man with systemic lymphadenopathy underwent cervical lymph node biopsy, which showed epithelioid granulomas without identifiable neoplastic cells. Sarcoidosis was initially suspected based on the pathological findings. However, comprehensive evaluation revealed no typical manifestations of sarcoidosis, including bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, uveitis, or elevated serum angiotensin-converting enzyme levels. The discordance between the pathological diagnosis and clinical findings led us to retain malignant lymphoma in the differential diagnosis. During follow-up, the patient developed B symptoms with substantially elevated soluble interleukin-2 receptor levels. Repeat biopsy of the left supraclavicular lymph node, performed 7 months after the initial presentation, revealed Reed-Sternberg-like multinucleated cells surrounded by a sarcoid-like reaction, confirming classical Hodgkin lymphoma. CONCLUSIONS This case illustrates that pathological findings alone may be insufficient for a definitive diagnosis of granulomatous lymphadenopathy. Malignant lymphoma should remain in the differential diagnosis, even when the initial biopsy suggests sarcoidosis. When clinical features are inconsistent with the pathological diagnosis, clinicians should reconsider the differential diagnosis, and repeat biopsy may be warranted. Integration of clinical findings, imaging, and histopathology is important to avoid diagnostic delay.

title: Prospective assessment of myocardial deformation in fetuses with suspected aortic coarctation.
authorString: Zwanenburg F, Trigler-Rinner J, Smit RM, Oberhoffer R, Wacker-Gussmann A, Ten Harkel ADJ, Haak MC.
abstractText:
Introduction

Prenatal identification of true aortic coarctation (CoA) remains challenging as evidenced by high false-positive rates. Myocardial deformation has been proposed to improve prediction of postnatal outcome. This prospective study aimed to determine whether fetal myocardial deformation analysis can differentiate true CoA from false-positive cases throughout gestation.

Methods

All fetuses with a prenatal suspicion of isolated CoA were prospectively recruited at our fetal cardiology services. Cases were classified as true CoA or false-positives based on their postnatal diagnosis. Speckle-tracking echocardiography was performed longitudinally to assess left and right ventricular global longitudinal strain (GLS), strain rate, and segmental strain throughout gestation. Measurements were compared between true CoA and false-positive cases.

Results

Thirty-eight fetuses were included (19 true CoA, 19 false-positives). True CoA cases exhibited smaller left-sided cardiac dimensions, including the aortic valve (mean Z-score -3.2 vs. -1.6, p<0.001), aortic isthmus (-3.5 vs. -1.7, p=0.001), and mitral valve (-4.9 vs. -3.1, p<0.001), whereas right-sided cardiac dimensions were comparable (pulmonary valve Z-score 3.0 vs. 2.6, p=0.64; arterial duct Z-score 1.9 vs. 3.2, p=0.61). No clinically relevant differences in myocardial deformation parameters were observed between groups, with similar left ventricular GLS (-20.1% vs. -20.5%, p=0.57), right ventricular GLS (-20.0% vs. -19.1%, p=0.13), strain rates and segmental strain.

Conclusion

Fetal myocardial deformation analysis does not provide additional predictive value for postnatal outcome in prenatally suspected isolated CoA. Conventional assessment of cardiac dimensions and flow patterns remains the cornerstone of prenatal CoA diagnosis, yet current imaging modalities cannot provide sufficient diagnostic certainty to safely triage perinatal management.

title: Emergency Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation for Decompensated Aortic Stenosis accompanied by Cardiogenic Shock.
authorString: Singh A, Kaliyadan CP, Chandra P.
abstractText:
Abstract

Patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) often present acutely with decompensated heart failure, cardiogenic shock or cardiac arrest requiring immediate intervention. Treatment options for these patients include palliative care, balloon aortic valvuloplasty (BAV), emergency transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), or surgical aortic valve replacement. TAVI procedure is performed electively in majority of the patients. However, it can be considered a rescue therapy in patients with cardiogenic shock secondary to acutely decompensated valvular AS. Here, we report the successful use of emergent TAVI for a patient presenting with cardiogenic shock secondary to decompensated AS.

title: Bentall Procedure in a Patient with Loeys-Dietz Syndrome: A Case Report.
authorString: Arora D, Chaudhary S, Gopalakrishnan RM, Bhate S.
abstractText:
Abstract

Loeys-Dietz syndrome (LDS) is a rare autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder characterized by aggressive aortopathy, craniofacial anomalies and systemic involvement. Rapid aortic root dilatation and valvular dysfunction mandate an early surgical intervention. We report a case of 15-year-old boy with LDS, rapidly progressive aortic root dilatation and severe aortic regurgitation (AR) who underwent successful Bentall procedure. The case highlights the need of early detection, multidisciplinary involvement and meticulous anesthetic care.

title: Linking preclinical models with functional imaging and artificial intelligence to decode tumor angiogenesis.
authorString: Varinská L, Koolwijk P.
abstractText: Tumor angiogenesis is a hallmark of cancer, influencing oxygen delivery, immune cell trafficking, and therapeutic response. Although anti-angiogenic therapies have achieved clinical relevance, their efficacy remains limited by tumor heterogeneity, adaptive resistance, and insufficient functional assessment of tumor vasculature. In this review, we evaluate preclinical models of tumor angiogenesis with a focus on their ability to generate quantitative and physiologically relevant readouts. We discuss established assays such as tube formation, fibrin bead assay, aortic ring, and chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) models, alongside emerging systems including vascularized organoids and organ-on-a-chip platforms, as well as zebrafish and murine tumor models. Particular emphasis is placed on advanced imaging modalities enabling longitudinal assessment of perfusion, permeability, and vascular remodeling, as well as on the growing role of artificial intelligence (AI) in automated and quantitative data interpretation. We further highlight the integration of single-cell and multi-omics approaches for resolving endothelial heterogeneity and tumor-stroma interactions. By linking biologically relevant models with functional imaging and computational analysis, this review outlines strategies to improve the predictive power and translational relevance of angiogenesis research.

title: Adaptive Sealing in Protruding LVOT Calcification During TAVR: A 4-Patient Case Series.
authorString: Salem AM, Rao K, Norman S, Ali N, Cunnington MS, Blackman D, Malkin CJ.
abstractText:
Background

Protruding left ventricular outflow tract calcification represents a high-risk anatomical feature for transcatheter aortic valve replacement, predisposing to paravalvular regurgitation (PVR), annular injury, and conduction disturbance.

Case summary

We present 4 patients with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis and protruding left ventricular outflow tract calcific nodules treated with the Navitor self-expanding valve system. Despite uniformly hostile landing-zone anatomy, procedural success was achieved in all cases. Residual PVR ranged from trivial to mild-to-moderate, with no patient developing moderate-or-greater PVR. All patients demonstrated hemodynamic improvement and early symptomatic benefit.

Conclusions

Calcific morphology and nodule orientation, rather than calcium burden alone, may be key determinants of PVR following Navitor implantation in hostile landing-zone anatomy. These findings are hypothesis-generating; the observed pattern of adaptive cuff sealing requires verification in larger, preferably comparative studies before conclusions regarding device-specific sealing mechanisms can be drawn.

title: Labetalol-induced hyperkalemia in acute aortic dissection: A rare but clinically relevant adverse effect.
authorString: Butt F, Khan Z, Badua PM.

journal.title: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists

abstractText:
Background

Hyperkalemia is a potentially life-threatening electrolyte abnormality often associated with renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) inhibitors, renal dysfunction, or potassium-sparing agents. Non-selective beta-blockers, including labetalol, may also precipitate hyperkalemia through beta-2 (β-2)-adrenergic blockade, although this adverse effect is underrecognized, particularly in patients without underlying renal disease.

Case presentation

A 59-year-old man with hypertension, diabetes, asthma, and polysubstance use disorder presented with severe chest pain and hypertensive emergency (243/132 mmHg). Imaging revealed aortic dilatation and confirmed acute type B aortic dissection. After initial medical management with intravenous (IV) esmolol and nicardipine, oral labetalol was initiated and escalated to 600 mg for anti-impulse therapy. The patient developed persistent, non-hemolyzed hyperkalemia (5.2 to 5.8 mmol/L) temporally correlating with labetalol dose escalation, despite preserved renal function (serum creatinine 1.4 to 1.8 mg/dL) and absence of RAAS inhibitors or heparin exposure. Conservative management failed, and the patient underwent thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) with thoracic branch endoprosthesis (TBE). Post-operatively, labetalol was discontinued and replaced with carvedilol. Serum potassium (K+) normalized within 48 hours and remained without further K+ lowering agents. Naranjo Adverse Drug Reaction Probability Scale assessment yielded a score of 7, indicating a probable adverse drug reaction.

Conclusions

Labetalol may induce clinically significant hyperkalemia independent of renal impairment or typical precipitating medications. This case highlights the importance of monitoring K+ in patients receiving labetalol for acute aortic syndromes and supports carvedilol as a potentially safer non-selective beta-blocker alternative with respect to K+ homeostasis.

title: Establishing reference values for aortic pulse wave velocity in healthy Chinese adults: a national multicenter prospective study.
authorString: Wang Z, Yang Y, Wang K, Sun X, Lai Y, Liu X, Gao J, Xu X, Liu A, Li H, Liu S, Dong F, Chen L, Zhang C, Jin Q, Liu Y, Liu L, Jia Y, Liu X, Hao Y, Jin L, Gao M, Tian X, Yue J, Wu S, Zhao J, Yang Y, Yuan L, Study Investigators.
abstractText:
Objective

The use of carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cfPWV), a reliable indicator of aortic stiffness and a powerful predictor of cardiovascular disease, has remained limited in routine clinical practice in China, due to the lack of standardized reference values. This national multicenter study aimed to establish the reference values for cfPWV in healthy Chinese adult population.

Methods

Participants were prospectively recruited across 29 participating centers in China and were categorized by age decade and blood pressure (BP) categories. A consistent ultrasound semi-automatic technique along with standardized measuring protocols was applied across all centers and participants to measure cfPWV. The carotid-femoral transit distance was determined using 0.8× direct carotid-femoral tape measure distance, and the cfPWV was calculated as transit distance/transit time.

Results

The study included 3328 adult participants (1431 men, 43%), age 45.7 ± 14.4 years. The distribution of cfPWV values with age and BP categories were described, and reference values were established. The 5th and 95th percentile values for cfPWV were: 18-29 years: 4.27, 7.57 m/s; 30-39 years: 4.65, 8.45 m/s; 40-49 years: 5.14, 9.49 m/s; 50-59 years: 5.34, 10.82 m/s; 60-69 years: 5.52, 12.04 m/s; and at least 70 years: 6.05, 14.69 m/s, respectively. Age, mean arterial pressure, heart rate, sex, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol level and family history of cardiovascular disease were independently correlated with cfPWV (P < 0.05).

Conclusion

Based on a large cohort of Chinese population, this study has established the reference values for cfPWV. Given the profound cardiovascular implications and powerful predictive value of cfPWV, the findings of this study represent a critical step forward in facilitating the wider integration of aortic stiffness assessment into routine clinical practice in China.

title: Improved Visualization of Heart Valves With 4D-CT Using a Novel Motion Correction Algorithm.
authorString: Zedler D, Demmert TT, Ritter A, Allmendinger T, Schmidt B, Kasel AM, Dzemali O, Manka R, Mergen V, Flohr T, Eberhard M, Alkadhi H.
abstractText:
Objective

Motion artifacts remain a limitation of cardiac CT when assessing both native and prosthetic heart valves, particularly during phases of rapid motion. This may lead to reduced image quality, potentially impairing the evaluation of valvular movement and pathology. The purpose of this study was to evaluate whether a novel reconstruction-based motion correction algorithm improves image quality and reduces motion artifacts of native and prosthetic heart valves compared with standard reconstructions in photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT).

Materials and methods

In this retrospective single-center study, 57 patients [21 women; median age, 71 (interquartile range, 57 to 78 y)] who underwent clinically indicated 4D cardiac CT for suspected native and prosthetic valvular disease were included. Images were acquired using retrospectively electrocardiography (ECG)-gated spiral dual-source PCD-CT without ECG-pulsing. Images were reconstructed in 10% steps throughout the RR-interval using both standard (TrueStack) and an otherwise identical reconstruction using the novel motion correction algorithm (ZeeFreePlus). Subjective image quality and motion artifacts were independently assessed by 2 blinded, experienced readers using a 4-point visual analog scale for 3 categories: valve frame/annulus, valve leaflets, and valvular pathology. Objective analysis included quantification of the volume of artifacts throughout the cardiac cycle.

Results

A total of 68 valves were evaluated, including 57 prosthetic valves (22 transcatheter aortic valve replacements and 19 surgical valves, 11 mitral valves, and 5 tricuspid valve interventions) and 11 native valves. Valvular pathology was present in 29 cases, with the most prevalent being hypoattenuated leaflet thickening in 14/29 (48%). Motion-corrected reconstructions significantly improved image quality and reduced motion artifacts across all cardiac phases and all categories (all, P<0.001). The largest improvements were observed during systole, particularly at 10% of the RR-interval, with significantly greater gains than during diastole (P<0.05). Improvements were consistent across aortic and atrioventricular prosthetic valves and translated into improved visualization of valvular pathology (P<0.001). Objective quantitative analysis corroborated the subjective image quality findings by demonstrating reductions in the volumes of motion-induced artifacts when using the algorithm (P<0.001).

Conclusions

A novel motion correction algorithm substantially reduced motion artifacts and improved image quality in both native and prosthetic heart valve imaging with PCD-CT, with the largest improvements in systole. These benefits resulted in enhanced visualization of valvular pathology, potentially reinforcing the growing clinical role of cardiac CT for the assessment of valve disease.

title: Complications associated with thoracic endovascular aortic repair: highlighting the role of peri- and post-operative cardiac monitoring.
authorString: Xanthopoulos A, Androutsopoulou V, Zotos PA, Giamouzis G, Skoularigis J, Magouliotis DE.
abstractText:
Introduction

Thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) is first-line therapy for most descending thoracic aortic pathologies, yet it is performed in patients with a heavy burden of coronary disease, hypertension and limited cardiac reserve, and its cardiac complications remain underemphasized relative to neurological and device-related events.

Areas covered

We summarize the complication profile of TEVAR briefly and then concentrate on its cardiac dimension: myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery, arrhythmia, acute heart failure, and the chronic ventricular consequences of stent-graft-induced aortic stiffening. We review the mechanisms linking endograft deployment to ventricular-arterial uncoupling, the echocardiographic markers of interest, blood pressure management, and a phase-based framework for peri- and post-operative cardiac monitoring, distinguishing guideline-supported recommendations from expert opinion and from evidence extrapolated from general vascular surgery. PubMed/MEDLINE were searched from database inception to August 2026.

Expert opinion

Cardiac surveillance around TEVAR is inconsistent and largely informal. We argue for baseline echocardiography in all elective patients, protocolized high-sensitivity troponin and natriuretic peptide measurement, defined-duration rhythm monitoring, structured blood pressure control, and longitudinal assessment of ventricular-arterial coupling within a heart-team pathway. TEVAR-specific outcome data and Windkessel-preserving graft design are the priorities for the next phase of endovascular aortic care.

title: An Extremely Rare Association of the Giant Right Atrium with Uncorrected Tetralogy of Fallot in an Adolescent Male Patient.
authorString: Maiti A, Guha A.
abstractText:
Abstract

Uncorrected tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) can be associated with widespread abnormalities, but the giant right atrium (RA) is an extremely rare one. The giant RA can cause additional problems causing atrial arrythmias, thromboembolism, and compression of adjacent structures. Tricuspid regurgitation is common with annular dilatation. In symptomatic cases, reduction atrioplasty is recommended. Sternotomy should be careful to avoid damage to the giant RA. In asymptomatic cases, anticoagulation should be carried out. We report a rare case of uncorrected TOF associated with the giant RA and got successfully treated with surgery.

title: Management of Non-cardiac Surgery in an Elderly Patient with Uncorrected Double Inlet Left Ventricle: Utility of the Pulse Contour Analysis-Based Cardiac Output Monitor.
authorString: Honda J, Yamazaki Y, Hasegawa T, Noji Y, Inoue S.
abstractText:
Abstract

Double inlet left ventricle (DILV) is a rare congenital heart disease that usually requires surgical treatment in childhood but can survive to old age untreated under certain conditions. In such patients, general anesthesia management requires an understanding of their unique hemodynamics and pathophysiology, along with the ability to maintain these conditions. In this case, long-term survival was possible due to the maintenance of an appropriate pulmonary-systemic blood flow balance achieved by pulmonary artery stenosis (PS), necessitating anesthesia management that preserved this balance. We report a case of non-cardiac anesthesia in an untreated adult patient with DILV, where systemic vascular resistance (SVR) monitoring and anesthesia management using remimazolam were employed to maintain stable circulatory control.

title: Early-Onset Gastric Varices After Fontan Completion Associated with a Pre-Existing Gastro-Renal Shunt.
authorString: Takenaka S, Shinohara T, Yasuda M, Kimura H, Koyama S, Saitoh S.
abstractText: Gastroesophageal varices are recognized complications of Fontan-associated liver disease, but clinically significant varices have generally been reported more than 10 years after Fontan completion. The mechanisms of early variceal formation remain unclear. We report a child with tricuspid atresia who developed isolated gastric varices approximately 7 years after extracardiac Fontan completion in the presence of a pre-existing gastro-renal shunt (GRS). The patient underwent bidirectional Glenn palliation at 9 months of age. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) performed before Fontan completion incidentally demonstrated a GRS, which progressively dilated after Fontan completion. At 8 years of age, contrast-enhanced CT obtained during evaluation for hypoxemia incidentally revealed isolated gastric varices. The patient had no ascites, marked splenomegaly, thrombocytopenia, or evidence of advanced hepatic dysfunction. Cardiac catheterization showed an inferior vena cava (IVC) pressure of 14 mmHg. Given the potential risk of massive hemorrhage, the gastric varices were successfully treated with transvenous coil embolization and balloon-occluded retrograde transvenous obliteration through the GRS. No recurrence was observed during follow-up. This case suggests that a pre-existing GRS may contribute to the relatively early development of gastric varices after Fontan completion, even in the absence of markedly elevated systemic venous pressure or other clinical features of advanced portal hypertension. Because a pre-existing GRS could predispose patients to gastric variceal formation after Fontan completion, preoperative assessment of the abdominal venous anatomy using contrast-enhanced CT could be important.

title: Effect of Postoperative Arrhythmia in Children Less Than 18 Years of Age Following Congenital Cardiac Surgery: A Prospective Study.
authorString: D R, Mk S, Ms K, Sp S, S T, V D.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
journal.title: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
journal.isoabbreviation: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg

abstractText: BackgroundPostoperative arrhythmias are common among children after congenital cardiac surgery, potentially compromising hemodynamic stability and postoperative recovery. This study aimed to assess the impact of arrhythmias on hemodynamics and clinical outcomes.Material and MethodsThree hundred and twenty-nine children under 18 years of age undergoing congenital cardiac surgery were studied prospectively. In addition to standard postoperative hemodynamic monitoring, electrical cardiometry (ICON®) was used to assess hemodynamic parameters across time points (prearrhythmia, during arrhythmia, and postarrhythmia). Repeated measures were analyzed using Friedman test followed by Wilcoxon signed-rank test with Bonferroni correction for pairwise comparisons. Poisson regression with robust variance estimation was used to identify independent predictors and calculate incidence rate ratios (IRR).ResultsPostoperative arrhythmias occurred in 53/329 patients (16.1%). Junctional ectopic tachycardia (34%, [18/53]) and supraventricular tachycardia (30.2%, [16/53]) were the most common. Arrhythmias were associated with low cardiac output (IRR 3.43; 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.27-5.17; P < .001), ventricular dysfunction (IRR 2.55; P < .001), acute kidney injury (IRR 2.01; P = .006), and liver dysfunction (IRR 4.56; P = .002) on unadjusted analysis. However, these associations were attenuated after adjustment for prearrhythmia hemodynamic variables like central venous pressure (CVP) and vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS) on multivariable analysis. Elevated CVP, VIS, and hypokalemia were predictors of arrhythmia.ConclusionsArrhythmias occurred in approximately one-sixth of children following congenital cardiac surgery and were associated with adverse hemodynamic changes, organ function, and recovery. However, these associations were attenuated after adjustment for prearrhythmia hemodynamic variables (CVP and VIS), suggesting that arrhythmia may reflect underlying instability rather than a primary causal factor.

title: Coronary artery imaging in Kawasaki disease: recent updates in imaging techniques and clinical indications.
authorString: Patharateeranart K, Goo HW, Kotoku A, Haifa AL, Wen L.

journal.title: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging

abstractText: Coronary artery involvement in Kawasaki disease should be evaluated throughout all disease stages. Generally, multimodality imaging is necessary for both the acute and chronic phases of coronary artery abnormalities. This review summarizes current clinical indications and recent technical advances in coronary artery imaging in Kawasaki disease with an emphasis on the roles of computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging. Echocardiography remains the first-line modality in all disease stages for evaluating coronary artery lesions and ventricular function. Recent technical developments in coronary computed tomography angiography can provide the accurate diagnosis of coronary artery lesions including stenosis and thrombus at substantially reduced radiation dose, supporting its selective use in serial follow-up. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging offers the comprehensive evaluation of inducible myocardial ischemia, ventricular function, inflammation, and fibrosis. Invasive catheter angiography is reserved for complex or interventional cases. This review also addresses technical considerations and potential pitfalls for each imaging modality. Continued technical developments and their optimization with standardized imaging protocols and reports are expected to enhance diagnostic precision and eventually improve clinical outcomes in children with Kawasaki disease.

title: Cardiovascular effects of continued vs. discontinued anabolic-androgenic steroid use: a longitudinal follow-up study.
authorString: Abdullah R, Bjørnebekk A, Hullstein IR, Thorsby PM, Helle-Valle T, Edvardsen T, Haugaa KH, Almaas VM.
abstractText:
Aims

Anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) use is prevalent among men engaged in strength training and is associated with adverse structural and functional cardiac changes, but longitudinal data are lacking. This follow-up study examined myocardial effects of AAS with continued use and reversibility following discontinuation.

Methods and results

Participants of a previously published cohort (2017-19) of 101 AAS users and 71 non-using weightlifting controls (WLCs) were invited for a follow-up study and underwent interviews, hormonal profiling, and transthoracic echocardiography. Current AAS users at baseline were continued or discontinued users at follow-up, while former users at baseline were those with continued abstinence and those who relapsed.Among those re-enrolled, 70 were AAS users, of whom 35 continued, 15 discontinued, 14 maintained abstinence, and 6 relapsed, and 35 were WLCs. Continued AAS users had persistent indexed left ventricular mass (LVMI 119 ± 30 g/m2), reduced LV ejection fraction (LVEF 48 ± 10%), and worsened diastolic function. Continued AAS users receiving antihypertensive therapy showed improved LVEF compared with untreated users (Δ = 5 ± 8 vs. -4 ± 8%, P = 0.005). Discontinued AAS users showed reduction in LVMI (Δ = -21 g/m2, P = 0.01) and improved LVEF (Δ = 6%, P < 0.001). At follow-up, these changes were comparable with WLCs, which showed statistically but clinically insignificant differences.

Conclusion

Continued AAS use was associated with sustained LV hypertrophy, LV systolic dysfunction, and worsening diastolic function. Antihypertensive therapy among ongoing AAS users was associated with improved LV systolic function. Discontinuation of AAS use was associated with improvement in cardiac structure and function towards values observed in WLCs.

title: Multichannel Dysfunction Associated With a Dominant-Negative <i>KCNH2</i> Missense Variant, p.G604S, Results in Action Potential Duration Prolongation and Early Afterdepolarizations in a Patient-Specific, Reengineered Cardiomyocyte Model of Type 2 Long-QT Syndrome.
authorString: Huynh T, Ye D, Zhou W, Tester DJ, Garmany R, Giudicessi JR, Ackerman MJ.
abstractText:
Background

Type 2 long-QT syndrome results from KCNH2-encoded Kv11.1 loss-of-function, but whether secondary inward-current dysfunction amplifies dysfunction remains unclear.

Methods

We characterized sodium (SCN5A, INa) and L-type calcium channel (CACNA1C, ICa) function in KCNH2-G604S and variant-corrected isogenic control induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs). Whole-cell patch-clamp measured action potential duration at 90% repolarization (APD90), and potassium (IKr), sodium (INa), and calcium (ICa, L) currents. Fluo-4 imaging quantified calcium transients. A modified Kernik-Clancy iPSC-CM model incorporated experimentally measured persistent INa,L and ICa,L fractions and simulated isolated and combined current defects.

Results

KCNH2-G604S caused severe IKr loss-of-function (72.5% reduction). APD90 was prolonged in G604S-iPSC-CMs (765±58 ms) compared with isogenic controls (368±37 ms; P<0.005), with early afterdepolarizations in 50% of G604S cells. Nifedipine, verapamil, and mexiletine successfully shortened APD90 and abolished early afterdepolarizations. Compared with isogenic control, INa,L (0.60±0.1% versus 0.26±0.06%; P<0.01), persistent ICa,L (2.88±0.55% versus 1.26±0.35%; P<0.05), and calcium transient decay times (P<0.0001) were greater in G604S iPSC-CMs. Increased persistent ICa,L was phenocopied by E-4031 in isogenic controls and reduced by nifedipine in G604S iPSC-CMs. In silico modeling revealed that the IKr defect alone prolonged APD90 to only 620 ms. The addition of the observed INa,L defect had a small additive effect (+20 ms); however, incorporating persistent ICa,L synergistically extended APD90 to 758 ms, replicating the experimental phenotype. Flux dynamics analysis indicated that this persistent Ca2+ entry suppresses the forward-mode sodium-calcium exchanger, forcing a compensatory reliance on sarcoplasmic-endoplasmic reticulum Ca-ATPase that primes for calcium instability.

Conclusions

The KCNH2-G604S variant drives a severe multihit phenotype via primary IKr loss-of-function and secondary state-dependent gain-of-function in persistent ICa,L. These comprehensive validations demonstrate that the remodeled persistent ICa,L acts as the essential amplifier driving extreme action potential duration prolongation and Ca2+ mishandling.

title: Pulsed field ablation with Renal denervation for persistent Atrial fibrIllation: Rationale and design of the PRAISE-AF randomized trial.
authorString: Guo J, Qin M, Jiang W, Ji Q, Miao Y, Sang Z, Li R, Hou X, Han W.
abstractText:
Background

Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia worldwide and is associated with increased risks of stroke, heart failure, hospitalization, disability, and mortality. Catheter ablation has become an established rhythm-control strategy for symptomatic AF; however, the recurrence rate after ablation remains substantial, especially in patients with persistent AF. Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is an emerging nonthermal ablation technology with myocardial tissue selectivity and a potentially improved safety profile compared with conventional thermal ablation. Renal denervation (RDN) reduces sympathetic nervous system activity and has shown promising effects in reducing AF recurrence when combined with catheter ablation, mainly in patients with paroxysmal AF and hypertension. Whether RDN combined with PFA improves rhythm outcomes in patients with persistent AF remains unknown.

Trial design

This is a single center, prospective, randomized, patient-blinded, sham-controlled pilot exploratory trial. A total of 86 patients with symptomatic persistent AF undergoing first-time catheter ablation will be enrolled and randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either PFA combined with RDN or PFA combined with a sham RDN procedure. Antiarrhythmic drugs (AADs) will be discontinued after the index procedure in both groups. The primary endpoint is freedom from documented atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence, including AF, atrial flutter, or atrial tachycardia lasting more than 30 seconds, within 12 months after a single ablation procedure without AADs. Secondary endpoints include freedom from atrial tachycardia recurrence within 3 months, AF burden, blood pressure changes, and major adverse cardiovascular events. Safety endpoints include cardiac, vascular, renal, and other procedure-related adverse events.

Conclusions

This trial will assess the safety and efficacy of PFA with RDN in a postablation contemporary persistent AF patient population.

Trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov:NCT07320768.

title: Jiawei Dingzhi Wan ameliorates chronic cerebral hypoperfusion-induced vascular cognitive impairment by modulating ACER2 and S1P-mediated microvascular angiogenesis and aortic vasoconstriction.
authorString: Fang C, Jia Z, Pu X, Dai Y, Yan X, Wei Z, Liu J, Li Y, Gao J, Xiao H.
abstractText:
Ethnopharmacological relevance

Jiawei Dingzhi Wan (DZW), a formula from Gujin Yijian (1576), was traditionally used for forgetfulness. However, it remains unclear whether DZW alleviates chronic cerebral hypoperfusion (CCH)-induced vascular cognitive impairment (VCI) and what the underlying mechanisms are.

Aim of the study

To investigate the main active components and mechanisms by which DZW ameliorates CCH-induced VCI.

Materials and methods

A 2-vessel occlusion (2VO) rat model was used to assess the effect of DZW (4 and 2 g/kg) on CCH-induced VCI. Cerebral blood flow (CBF), cognitive function (Morris Water Maze), and histopathology were evaluated. Immunofluorescence (IF) was used to evaluate the number of cerebral microvessels. In vitro, a thoracic aorta ring was used to test vasoconstriction. Network pharmacology, untargeted metabolomics, and targeted sphingolipomics were used to explore the mechanisms. Related protein levels were determined by Western blot. High-performance liquid chromatography coupled with triple quadrupole mass spectrometry (HPLC-QQQ-MS) was used to quantitatively analyze the main components of DZW and the components absorbed into the plasma after intragastric administration of DZW in rats. Drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS) analysis identified plasma-absorbed components and their direct binding targets. Wound healing and aortic ring assays assessed effects on angiogenesis and vasoconstriction.

Results

DZW (4 g/kg and 2 g/kg) significantly increased cortical CBF by approximately 63% and 44%, respectively, compared to the model group. DZW also significantly shortened escape latency in the Morris Water Maze test and increased the number of platform crossings in the probe trial. DZW significantly increased the expression of CD31 in CCH rats, suggesting that DZW can promote angiogenesis. Additionally, the intestinal absorption solution of DZW (20-640 μL) had a contractile effect on thoracic aorta vessels, both with and without endothelialization. Network pharmacology and untargeted metabolomics revealed that sphingolipid signaling is a strongly correlated pathway. Further targeted sphingolipomics found that the levels of sphingosine (Sph) and sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) increased, while the levels of ceramide (Cer 18:0, Cer 18:1, Cer 20:0, Cer 22:0, and Cer 24:0) decreased after DZW (4 g/kg) treatment, which was associated with the S1P synthesis enzyme ACER2. Our study found that DZW promotes angiogenesis through the S1PR3/VEGF/VEGFR2 signaling pathway and regulates vasoconstriction through the S1PR3/ROCK1 signaling pathway. Subsequently, 25 components in DZW and 13 components absorbed into the plasma were identified as the main components by high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with triple quadrupole mass spectrometry (HPLC-QQQ-MS) analysis. DARTS-based immunoblot analysis confirmed that among the 13 plasma-absorbed components, in addition to 3-butylphthalide and ginsenoside Re, 11 other compounds directly bound to ACER2 and affected its expression. All 13 components absorbed into the plasma directly bound to S1PR3 and affected its expression. Further research has shown that paeoniflorin, ferulic acid, ginsenoside Rg1, ginsenoside Re, ligustilide, and 3-butylphthalide (20 μM) can promote vascular endothelial cell migration in the wound healing assay, while paeoniflorin, polygalaxanthone III, tenuifolin, and senkyunolide I (100 μM) were found to induce vasoconstriction in thoracic aortic ring assays.

Conclusion

This study demonstrates for the first time that DZW ameliorates CCH-induced VCI through ACER2 and S1P-mediated dual vascular regulation, including both microvascular angiogenesis and aortic vasoconstriction. We identified six angiogenesis and four vasoconstrictive components of DZW. These findings provide novel mechanistic insights into the multi-component therapeutic strategy of TCM for CCH-induced VCI.

title: Subclinical Leaflet Thrombosis, Transcatheter Heart Valve Characteristics and Structural Valve Deterioration: Rationale and Design of the POPular PET TAVI Study.
authorString: van Ginkel DJ, Overduin DC, Craig NJ, De Backer O, Keijsers R, Hasbak P, Fuchs A, Kofoed KF, Aarts HM, Bække PS, Clark L, van Nuland PJA, Rensing BJWM, Timmers L, Schurgers LJ, Delewi R, Swaans MJ, Dweck MR, Ten Berg JM.

journal.title: Journal of nuclear cardiology : official publication of the American Society of Nuclear Cardiology

abstractText:
Background

Subclinical leaflet thrombosis is common after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and may contribute to structural valve deterioration over time, this may be influenced by transcatheter heart valve (THV) design and other valve-related factors.

Methods

The 'Effect of Subclinical Leaflet Thrombosis and Prosthesis Type on Transcatheter Aortic Valve Degeneration (POPular PET TAVI)' study is an international, multicenter, cross-sectional cohort study. Patients (n=180) are enrolled at five years after TAVI for a detailed assessment of THV structure and function using a multi-modality imaging approach. High-resolution four-dimensional cardiac computed tomography (4D-CT) is used to assess subclinical leaflet thrombosis and THV characteristics (e.g. neosinus volume, prosthesis deformation index, valve expansion and commissural alignment). 18F-sodium fluoride (18F-NaF) positron emission tomography (PET) is used to measure micro-calcification activity in the THV leaflets as a marker of structural valve deterioration. Transthoracic echocardiography is performed to evaluate THV and cardiac function. Obtained images are analyzed by dedicated Core Laboratories for PET and 4D-CT. To facilitate comparisons between balloon-expandable, intra-annular and self-expanding, supra-annular prostheses, enrollment is stratified for valve size and type. As of September 2026, 159 patients have been enrolled successfully, completion is anticipated in December 2026.

Conclusion

The POPular PET TAVI study evaluates the interplay between subclinical leaflet thrombosis, THV characteristics and structural valve deterioration at five years after TAVI. Improved understanding of these mechanisms may inform individualized antithrombotic strategies and optimized valve design aiming to enhance long-term valve durability.

title: Long-term outcomes following modified Blalock-Taussig-Thomas shunt placement in 13 dogs with cyanotic congenital heart disease.
authorString: Rossanese M, Hannabuss J, Brockman D.

journal.title: The Journal of small animal practice

abstractText:
Objectives

To describe long-term outcome and owner-perceived quality of life in dogs with cyanotic congenital cardiac disease undergoing modified Blalock-Taussig-Thomas shunt procedure.

Materials and methods

Medical records of dogs that underwent Blalock-Taussig-Thomas shunt between 2009 and 2025 at a small animal referral hospital were retrospectively reviewed. Complications, long-term outcomes and quality of life were assessed via clinical examination and/or contact with owners or referring veterinarians.

Results

Thirteen dogs were included. The predominant clinical signs were exercise intolerance, cyanosis and a heart murmur. Diagnosis included tetralogy of Fallot (n = 8), double outlet right ventricle (n = 3); tetralogy of Fallot-double outlet right ventricle spectrum (n = 1) and tetralogy of Fallot with pulmonary atresia spectrum (n = 1). All dogs survived surgery. Follow-up was available for 12 dogs, ranging from 58 to 2094 days. Eight dogs died or were euthanased for cardiac-related reasons, three were alive at follow-up and one dog was alive 278 days after surgery at last point of contact. All dogs showed a marked postoperative clinical improvement. Shunt obstruction or partial obstruction was documented in three of 12 dogs at 265, 587 and 693 days. Postoperative balloon valvuloplasty was performed in three of the 12 dogs, one died during the procedure and two dogs showed clinical improvement and extended good quality survival. Owners' perception of the procedure outcome and quality of life was described as good, with only mild adjustments needed for exercise.

Clinical significance

Blalock-Taussig-Thomas shunt is an effective palliative option for dogs with cyanotic congenital cardiac diseases associated with reduced pulmonary blood flow, providing sustained clinical improvement and quality of life. Recurrence of clinical signs could indicate shunt obstruction and warrants prompt assessment.

title: Optimizing management strategies for T4b esophageal cancer: the role of TEVAR in multimodal treatment approaches.
authorString: Koliakos N, Tzortzis AS, Papakonstantinou D, Mela E, Hasemaki N, Peroulis M, Bakopoulos A, Schizas D.
abstractText:
Background

T4b esophageal cancer with aortic invasion remains a major therapeutic challenge because treatment-related tumor regression may precipitate aortoesophageal fistula formation and catastrophic hemorrhage. While chemoradiotherapy is the backbone of disease control, the role of thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) as prophylaxis or bridge therapy within a multimodal treatment strategy is increasingly recognized.

Methods

This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the use of TEVAR in T4b esophageal cancer. Relevant clinical studies, reviews and guideline documents were evaluated qualitatively, with emphasis on treatment sequencing, bleeding prevention, resectability and oncologic outcomes.

Results

Available retrospective studies and systematic reviews suggest that elective TEVAR may reduce the risk of major bleeding complications and facilitate subsequent esophagectomy in selected patients. Elective TEVAR was associated with higher rates of subsequent esophageal resection and fewer complications than salvage TEVAR. Moreover, elective TEVAR followed by esophagectomy, ameliorates significantly patients survival. These findings support the potential role of elective TEVAR within multimodal treatment strategies, although the available evidence remains predominantly retrospective and is subject to selection bias and heterogeneity in patient selection and treatment.

Conclusions

TEVAR may represent a useful adjunct in the multimodal management of selected patients with T4b esophageal cancer and aortic involvement. In carefully selected patients, elective TEVAR may reduce the risk of catastrophic hemorrhage and facilitate subsequent curative-intent treatment, including conversion esophagectomy, although prospective evidence defining its optimal indications and timing remains lacking.

title: Assisted Reproductive Technology and Risk of Congenital Heart Defects in the Offspring: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Rinaldi R, Bujak K, Laudani C, Occhipinti G, Caffè A, Animati FM, Scarica V, Łajczak P, Flores-Umanzor E, Luna-Lopez R, Nicolini E, Piva T, Pawlas N, Regueiro A, Freixa X, Gąsior M, Ottani F, Crea F, Montone RA.

journal.title: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstractText:
Background

To date, >10 million children have been conceived via assisted reproductive technology (ART) globally. However, there are some concerns about potential adverse outcomes associated with ART-conceived pregnancies, including the risk of congenital heart defects (CHDs). This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the association between ART and the risk of major CHDs as well as their specific subtypes.

Methods

Major electronic databases were screened for studies comparing the incidence of CHD following ART-conceived pregnancies versus spontaneous conception. The primary end point was study-defined incidence of CHDs. Secondary end points included incidence of tetralogy of Fallot, transposition of the great arteries, aortic coarctation, ventricular septal defect, atrial septal defect, pulmonary valve atresia, tricuspid valve atresia, and hypoplastic left heart. Pairwise meta-analyses were performed using frequentist random-effect models to calculate risk ratios and 95% CIs.

Results

Thirteen studies, encompassing a total of 45 916 925 subjects (4986 conceived via ART), were included in the quantitative synthesis. ART was significantly associated with a higher risk of major CHD compared with natural pregnancy (risk ratio, 2.35 [95% CI, 1.68-3.28]), with significant heterogeneity across the studies. An increased risk of tetralogy of Fallot, ventricular septal defect, and atrial septal defect following ART-conceived pregnancies was found, while no difference was found on other CHDs. Prespecified sensitivity analyses were in line with the primary findings of the meta-analysis.

Conclusions

Our meta-analysis shows a potential link between ART and increased risk of major CHDs, particularly on tetralogy of Fallot, ventricular septal defect, and atrial septal defect.

title: Corrigendum to The European Bifurcation Club randomised trial of stepwise provisional stenting versus Drug Coated Balloon therapy for non-left main true coronary bifurcations: The EBC DCB Trial American Heart Journal: Volume 300, October 2026, 107463.
authorString: Broyd CJ, Arunothayaraj S, Scheller B, Eccleshall S, Lassen JF, Stankovic G, Hildick-Smith D.

title: Protective effects of icariin in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease: mechanistic basis, post-ischemic protection and translational limitations.
authorString: Wang X, Yu Z, Li X, Hu L, Sun C, Wang Y, Li L, Wu M, Liu L.
abstractText:
Context

Icariin (ICA), a prenylated flavonol glycoside from Epimedii Folium, has been investigated in experimental models relevant to atherosclerosis, myocardial infarction, and ischemic tissue injury.

Objectives

This review evaluates experimental evidence on ICA in atherosclerotic plaque biology, post-myocardial infarction remodeling, myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury, and cerebral ischemic injury.

Methods

PubMed and the Web of Science Core Collection were searched from database inception to 19 August 2026, and studies were selected using predefined eligibility criteria. Targeted searches also covered pharmacokinetics, metabolism, toxicology, botanical source, quality control, formulation, and delivery.

Results

In atherosclerosis models, ICA reduced endothelial inflammatory activation, macrophage lipid uptake, vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) proliferation and migration, and lesion burden. Several mechanistic links were tested using pharmacological or genetic perturbation. In vivo studies primarily characterized lesion burden and circulating lipids, with less direct assessment of plaque composition and stability. Post-myocardial infarction and ischemic injury studies reported reductions in fibrosis and ischemic tissue injury, together with reduced mitochondrial injury and changes in inflammatory signaling, apoptosis, and ferroptosis-related processes. Functional improvement was also reported in several models. Few studies measured parent ICA or metabolite concentrations in plaque, myocardium, or brain in the same experiments in which pathological outcomes were assessed.

Conclusions

Future studies should quantify parent ICA and active metabolites in diseased tissues while assessing plaque composition and stability in the same experiments, so that vascular effects can be related to measured in vivo exposure.

title: Lipoprotein(a)-dependent cardiovascular risk in different populations: are thresholds the same?
authorString: Mansfield BS, Raal FJ, Kovanen PT, Vuorio A.
abstractText:
Background

Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined, independent and causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and aortic stenosis. Large prospective cohort studies together with Mendelian Randomization studies have established its role in cardiovascular risk which has led to the introduction of screening and the development of Lp(a)-lowering therapies. However, interpretation of Lp(a) results in clinical practice remains a challenge, particularly across populations with significantly different baseline levels.

Discussion

Lp(a) levels vary according to ancestry. People of African ancestry having the highest median Lp(a) levels, followed by people from South Asia, East Asia and Europe, respectively. However, despite these differences, current Lp(a) risk thresholds are derived from populations of predominantly European ancestry and broadly applied across underrepresented population groups.Available evidence from multi-ancestry cohort studies have shown that while proportional risk for ASCVD may be similar across ancestries, the absolute risk associated with specific thresholds may differ. The application of a universal threshold may lead to over-classification of risk in some populations, resulting in unnecessary edicalization and strain on healthcare systems. Conversely, some populations may be under-classified by a universal threshold potentially resulting in avoidable ASCVD events.

Conclusion

This commentary explores the epidemiological, biological and methodological factors underlying variability in Lp(a) levels and their association with ASCVD across populations. We discuss the advantages and limitations of applying ancestry-specific Lp(a) risk thresholds. Lp(a) measurements in clinical practice should be interpreted in within a broader clinical and population context rather than in isolation.

title: Palmitic acid promotes hypertrophic memory in cardiomyocytes via KDM5A/H3K4me3.
authorString: Yang K, Gao R, Shi J, Wei X, Lu X, Chen H, Wei W, Hu J, Chen J, Lyu Y, Gao P, Ke C, Sun A.
abstractText:
Background and aims

Palmitic acid (PA), the most abundant saturated fatty acid (SFA), is positively associated with heart failure (HF) risk. However, its role and mechanism underlying HF remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the effects of a PA-enriched diet and potential therapeutic targets in HF.

Methods

The association between plasma SFAs and HF was investigated in a cohort of 232 592 UK Biobank participants. Mice were randomly categorized into three groups, where they were fed a PA-enriched, olive oil-enriched, or control diet for 4 weeks, followed by a 4-week dietary adaptation period on the control diet. A pressure overload model was established by transverse aortic constriction in these mice and cardiac-specific lysine demethylase 5A (Kdm5A)-knockout mice.

Results

The UK Biobank database revealed an association between high plasma SFA levels and increased HF risk. Our in vitro and in vivo results demonstrated that short-term PA treatment promoted cardiac hypertrophy and HF without further exposure to high levels of PA, indicating a pro-hypertrophic memory in cardiomyocytes. Mechanistically, PA promoted palmitoylation-driven KDM5A degradation via the ubiquitination pathway, thereby up-regulating histone 3 lysine 4 tri-methylation (H3K4me3). KDM5A/H3K4me3 promoted a pro-hypertrophic memory in cardiomyocytes, thus causing cardiac hypertrophy via a monocarboxylate transporter 4 (MCT4)-induced metabolic imbalance. Furthermore, KDM5A agonist D18 ameliorated this PA-mediated cardiac hypertrophy and HF.

Conclusions

A PA-enriched diet promotes pro-hypertrophic memory in cardiomyocytes, cardiac hypertrophy, and HF via KDM5A/H3K4me3/MCT4. The application of D18 may represent a promising therapeutic approach for PA-mediated cardiac hypertrophy and HF.

title: Surgical Ligation for Partial Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Connection With Dual Drainage in an Elderly Patient.
authorString: Tanaka T, Wakisaka H, Kimura M, Miyazaki T, Takashima N, Suzuki T.
abstractText:
Background

Partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection with dual drainage into both the superior vena cava (SVC) and left atrium (LA) is a rare congenital anomaly, with few reported cases.

Case summary

A 78-year-old woman presented with exertional dyspnea. Cardiac computed tomography revealed that the right pulmonary vein drained into both the SVC and LA, resulting in a significant left-to-right shunt. We ligated the anomalous connection with a median sternotomy. This approach allowed avoidance of complex reconstructions and cardioplegic arrest.

Discussion

Simple ligation may represent a less invasive surgical option that avoids cardiac arrest and shortens operative time. Moreover, it may prevent pulmonary venous obstruction and future heart failure caused by right heart volume overload.

Take-home message

In elderly patients with heart failure caused by partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection with dual drainage into both the SVC and LA, ligation of the left-to-right shunt may be less invasive and prevent late complications.

title: Physical Activity Counselling for Children with Congenital Heart Disease: A Pilot Study.
authorString: Fukakusa BM, Bennett EV, Voss C, Harris KC.
abstractText: It is still not known how to best help children with congenital heart disease (CHD) be more active despite many previous interventions. This study aimed to determine the feasibility and acceptability of a theoretically-based physical activity (PA) counselling intervention. This is a mixed-methods pilot study of children ages 9-12 with moderate-to-complex CHD. A 12-week intervention based on behaviour change theory was designed. Participants who did not meet the World Health Organization PA guidelines (measured via accelerometers) and expressed readiness to change (measured via questionnaires) at baseline qualified. The intervention consisted of six virtual sessions with a PA counsellor, during which participants engaged in workbook activities to learn strategies to engage in PA. Intervention feasibility (recruitment, retention, completion of measures, remote implementation, session and intervention length) and acceptability (compliance, interview feedback) were assessed. PA was measured post-intervention and one year later. Thirty-three children were recruited (recruitment success: 51%). Nine out of 12 eligible participants completed the intervention (retention: 75%) with few technical difficulties (14.5%). Completion rates of PA metrics declined over the study. It took the PA counsellor 15.5 h on average per participant to conduct the intervention. Compliance was high (attendance: 100%, workbook activity completion: 64.4%). During feedback interviews, participants denoted the importance of engaging the whole family, promoting participant autonomy and empowerment, and identified lessons learned. Although this intervention was acceptable to children with CHD, the feasibility remains uncertain given recruitment challenges and time commitment required. Successful components should be considered when designing future interventions.

title: Child Health Challenges, Ecosystem Mismatches, and the Case for State-Level Policy Innovation.
authorString: Halfon N, Russ S.
abstractText: Policy Points From 2011-2023, US children's health deteriorated across >170 indicators. Chronic conditions rose from 25.8% to 31%, risk of anxiety tripled, and autism and learning disability more than doubled. Policies based on biomedical models have failed to address these trends. Life course models regard health as a developmental process, with mismatches between children's physical, nutritional, and relational environments and the ones they are evolutionarily calibrated to expect as likely drivers of declining health. State policies can help to overcome mismatches and optimize developmental ecosystems.
