The absolute majority of the Subjects of the Russian Federation of supervised Federal Okrugs were able to ensure achievement of target values of qualitative indicators of the Program of state guarantees of free medical care for citizens in part of cardiovascular diseases treatment.

title: [THE PHYSICAL ACTIVITY OF ELDERLY PEOPLE AS FACTOR OF ACTIVE LONGEVITY].
authorString: Sodikova GO, Ananchenkova PI, Borisov AB, Borovkov SE.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Probl Sotsialnoi Gig Zdravookhranenniiai Istor Med
journal.title: Problemy sotsial'noi gigieny, zdravookhraneniia i istorii meditsiny
journal.isoabbreviation: Probl Sotsialnoi Gig Zdravookhranenniiai Istor Med

abstractText: The article considers impact of physical activity on formation of active longevity. On the basis of analysis of scientific publications, data is summarized concerning effects of physical activity on cardiovascular system, musculoskeletal system, cognitive functions, psychological state and social activity of elderly adults. It is demonstrated that regular motion activity contributes to maintenance of functional independence, to decrease of risk of age-related diseases and to support of quality of life in elderly age. The conceptual pattern highlighting physical activity as backbone factor of active longevity. The study has theoretical analytical character and can be applied under development of programs of prevention and health promotion of elderly population.

title: Sex Differences in Mortality After Myocardial Infarction: A German Nationwide Cohort Study.
authorString: Enders D, Sievert H, Luedde M, Kostev K.
abstractText:
Background

Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains one of the leading causes of death in Germany, accounting for 41 258 deaths in 2024. The evidence on sex differences in mortality after AMI is mixed, especially for outcomes beyond the acute phase. We used data from a large nationwide database to study sex differences in 12-month mortality after AMI in Germany.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study is based on data from the German Health Data Lab (Forschungsdatenzentrum Gesundheit). Adults who had a principal inpatient discharge diagnosis of incident AMI in 2023 were included in the analysis. The endpoint was all-cause mortality within 12 months. Cox models were fitted with sequential adjustment for age, infarction type, comorbidities, and prior cardiovascular medication.

Results

62 884 women and 113 019 men were included in the analysis. The women were older and had more comorbidities. The crude 12-month mortality was higher in women than in men (21.0% vs 17.8%; 251 vs 207 per 1000 person-years). After adjustment for age, however, the reverse was true: mortality was lower in women than in men (hazard ratio [HR] 0.88; 95% CI 0.86-0.90). This remained the case in the fully adjusted model (HR 0.84; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.82-0.85). In exploratory stratified analyses, men and women under age 60 did not differ in mortality, while in older age groups and after non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), mortality was lower in women (but not after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction [STEMI]).

Conclusion

Multivariable analysis revealed a slightly lower 12-month mortality among women after the diagnosis of an acute myocardial infarction. Because the adjustment included variables that may act as mediators on the causal pathway between sex and mortality, the adjusted estimates should be interpreted with caution.

title: Clinical, Patient Experience and Service Outcomes of a Leisure Centre-Based NHS Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy Service: A Service Evaluation.
authorString: McNamee G, Roberts V, Newton C, O'Donnell E, Panter C, Manecka G, Blay S, Singh G.
abstractText:
Background

Musculoskeletal (MSK) conditions place substantial burden on individuals and healthcare systems, increasing the demand for accessible, community-based care. This service evaluation assessed an NHS MSK physiotherapy pilot delivered in a leisure centre in a socioeconomically deprived area.

Methods

A retrospective evaluation of routinely collected data was undertaken for patients attending between August 2025 and January 2026. Adults referred for physiotherapy for MSK conditions received treatment in a community leisure centre. Outcomes at initial and final appointments included MSK health (MSK-HQ), pain intensity (NPRS), physical activity (MSK-HQ physical activity item), and health-related quality of life (EQ-VAS). Linear mixed-effects models evaluated clinical outcomes. Patient experience and service utilisation data were analysed descriptively.

Results

Sixty-four patients (mean age 50.6 ± 14.8 years; 60.9% female) were included, predominantly from socioeconomically deprived areas (mean Index of Multiple Deprivation 2.4 ± 1.5). 53.2% were from ethnic minority backgrounds and 13 languages were represented. Significant improvements were observed across all outcomes: MSK-HQ (+11.2), NPRS (-2.2), EQ-VAS (+19.9), and physical activity (+1.8 days/week) (all p ≤ 0.002). Sensitivity analyses yielded similar results except for physical activity. Minimal clinically important thresholds were exceeded for MSK-HQ, NPRS and EQ-VAS. Patient satisfaction was high, attendance was 72.2%, and 17.2% of patients were referred to community exercise programmes.

Conclusions

A leisure centre-based NHS MSK physiotherapy model was associated with improved clinical outcomes, high patient acceptability and promising service utility. The service engages a heterogeneous population and aligns with NHS priorities for community-based care. Further comparative and economic evaluations are warranted to establish effectiveness and inform future service development.

title: Listen to Your Heart and Mind: A Pilot Mixed-Methods Study on Combined Screening for Raised Blood Pressure, Atrial Fibrillation, Cognitive Impairment and Hearing Loss in Older Adults.
authorString: Tan I, Schutte AE, Morgan C, Brodaty H, Gnanenthiran SR, Numbers K, Liu H, Ouyang M, Incerti P, Kitterick P, Sharma M.
abstractText:
Objective

To determine the potential feasibility and acceptability of combined screening for raised blood pressure (BP), atrial fibrillation (AF) and cognitive impairment (CI) in older adults within a setting of hearing health assessment for detection of hearing loss.

Methods

We recruited participants aged 65 years or older (n = 35; mean age 73 ± 6 years, 51% females) from the community to attend a single visit lasting approximately 60-90 min. Prior to a comprehensive hearing assessment, BP was measured with an automatic BP monitor with AF detection, and CI screening was conducted using the patient section of the General Practitioner Assessment of Cognition instrument. A subset of participants (n = 16, 50% females) was interviewed post study to evaluate acceptability.

Results

A total of 21 positive screens (six raised BP; two possible AF; 13 hearing loss) and 12 potential positive screens for possible CI were detected in 25 (71%) participants. Eight participants (23%) had more than one newly detected condition. Interviews revealed that combined screening was feasible and acceptable as participants felt it was 'convenient,' 'saves time' and 'more efficient.'

Conclusions

Combined screening for raised BP, AF and CI in older adults within a hearing health assessment setting appears feasible and was generally perceived positively by participants in this pilot study. Further implementation studies should be conducted with process and outcome evaluation embedded to confirm feasibility and acceptability as well as to evaluate cost-effectiveness and health outcomes for combined screening in older adults.

title: Impact of Evolocumab on LDL-Cholesterol and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients With Established CVD: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authorString: Goel A, Naveed MA, Tandel H, Mahmood A, Mukhlis M, Reddy KSV, Maloth AK, Chauhan A, Awashra A, Verma A, Tahir HB.
abstractText:
Background

Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, and many high-risk patients fail to reach LDL-cholesterol (LDL-C) targets on statins alone. Evolocumab, a PCSK9 inhibitor, offers potent LDL-C lowering, but a synthesis of its lipid and clinical benefits in secondary prevention is needed.

Methods

We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials evaluating evolocumab in adults with established cardiovascular disease. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through April 2025. Outcomes included lipid parameters, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), individual cardiovascular endpoints, and safety, with pooled risk ratios (RR) and mean differences calculated using random-effects models.

Results

Nine trials enrolling 67,662 patients were included. Evolocumab significantly reduced LDL-C (mean difference -57.73 mg/dL), total cholesterol (-52.27 mg/dL), triglycerides (-21.21 mg/dL), and lipoprotein(a) (-10.99 mg/dL), while increasing HDL-cholesterol (3.69 mg/dL). Evolocumab was associated with lower MACE (RR 0.53; 95% CI 0.40-0.71), though this estimate should be interpreted cautiously given heterogeneity in endpoint definitions and study designs. Myocardial infarction (RR 0.74) and coronary revascularisation (RR 0.80) were significantly reduced, while cardiovascular mortality and stroke showed no statistically definitive reduction. Serious adverse events and neurocognitive effects were comparable between groups, though injection-site reactions were more frequent with evolocumab.

Conclusion

In patients with established cardiovascular disease, evolocumab provides substantial lipid lowering and reduces ischemic events without major safety concerns, supporting its use as an adjunct to statin therapy in secondary prevention.

title: Disease-Specific Optimal Blood Glucose Control Strategies in Critically Ill Patients: Retrospective Cohort Study and Network Meta-analysis.
authorString: He X, Meng J, Zhu Y, Dai X, Gao S.
abstractText:
Background

Optimal glucose targets for critically ill patients are likely to vary by underlying condition, yet a 'one-size-fits-all' approach persists.

Aim

Determining disease-specific glucose thresholds may help achieve the lowest mortality rates.

Study design

This study combined a retrospective cohort analysis of the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care-IV (MIMIC-IV) database with a frequentist network meta-analysis (NMA) of randomized controlled trials (RCTs). The glucose control targets, measured by time-weighted average glucose (TWAg), were categorized into four strata: strict, intermediate strict, liberal and very liberal control.

Results

The retrospective analysis included 21 119 sepsis, 16 957 cardiac and 4708 neurological patients. In both sepsis and cardiac patients, compared with the intermediate strict control group (110-150 mg/dL, reference), both the strict (80-110 mg/dL: HR 1.10/1.26, both p < 0.05) and liberal (150-180 mg/dL: HR 1.38/1.78, both p < 0.05) control groups showed significantly higher 28-day mortality. In contrast, among neurological patients, strict control conferred a survival benefit (HR 0.76, p = 0.013). The NMA of 35 RCTs corroborated these findings for sepsis and neurological disorders, with intermediate strict control ranking highest for sepsis (P-score 74.9%) and strict control highest for neurological disorders (P-score 71.2%), whereas liberal control ranked highest for cardiac disease (P-score 83.5%); no pairwise differences were statistically significant.

Conclusions

This study provides evidence that optimal glucose targets in the ICU are disease-specific. In the retrospective analysis, intermediate strict control was associated with the lowest mortality in sepsis and cardiac disease, while strict control may benefit neurological patients without excess hypoglycaemia. However, for cardiac disease, the NMA ranked liberal control highest, leaving the optimal target uncertain.

Relevance to clinical practice

These findings may support a pathophysiology-guided, individualized approach to glycaemic management in critically ill patients.

title: Acute effects of volume-matched isometric exercise intensity on vascular function and autonomic regulation in men with elevated blood pressure.
authorString: Jeong MJ, Kim JG, Park W, Kim JH, Jung HC.
abstractText: Isometric exercise (IE) has been introduced as an effective non-pharmacological strategy for blood pressure (BP) management; however, the influence of exercise intensity remains unclear during lower-limb IE. This study investigated the acute effects of volume-matched high-intensity (HIIE) and low-intensity IE (LIIE) on cardiovascular function in men with elevated BP. Seventeen men with prehypertension or stage I hypertension completed three randomized crossover conditions, including HIIE (60% of maximal voluntary contraction (MVC)), LIIE (30% of MVC), and a non-exercise control condition (CON). BP, heart rate variability (HRV), brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV) were measured at baseline and three different time points during recovery, while flow-mediated dilation (FMD) was measured at baseline and 30-min post-exercise. No significant BP reduction was observed. However, HIIE induced greater autonomic disturbance with elevated heart rate and reduced HRV indices during recovery (p < 0.05). Right baPWV decreased following HIIE (p < 0.05) while FMD increased after both exercise conditions (p < 0.001). Our findings suggest that volume-matched HIIE induces greater acute autonomic and vascular responses than LIIE in men with elevated BP, despite no immediate changes in BP. HIIE may provide a stronger physiological stimulus associated with vascular adaptation.

title: High Doses of N-Acetyl-P-Aminophenol Cause Acute Changes in Electroencephalographic and Electrocardiographic Activities in Wistar Rats.
authorString: da Silva ALM, Dos Reis de Freitas LG, Hamoy AO, da Paz CA, Ferreira LO, da Silveira EP, Hamoy MKO, Muto NA, Lopes DCF, Hamoy M.
abstractText: N-acetyl-p-aminophenol (APAP), or acetaminophen, is the most prescribed analgesic and antipyretic, even used in association with other drugs. Because it is easily bought in drugstores, much evidence about its toxic effects is known due to high doses or continuous use, which can lead to death in cases of intoxication. The present study aimed demonstrate the ability of APAP to change the brain and heart electrical activities, as early as significant increase in liver enzymes. Thus, a toxic dose of 1 g/kg was administered orally, and the animals were assessed every 3 h until 12 h for electroencephalography, electrocardiography and liver function data. The results showed that a toxic dose of APAP was capable of reducing brain electrical activity for the delta, theta, beta and gamma waves; however, the alpha wave activity was increased. In the heart, a reduced electrical activity was observed synchronously with the electroencephalogram. During the 12-h follow-up period, a significant increase in liver enzymes was observed. Taken together, we conclude that high doses of APAP can alter frequency brain oscillations and promote cardiac changes independently of liver damage in the first 12 h.

title: Thirst in Patients With Advanced Chronic Heart Failure Waiting for a Heart Transplantation: A Mixed Methods Study of Patients' and Nurses' Experiences.
authorString: Wefer F, Krüger L, Calo S, Möhler R, Dichter MN, Mühring A, Gummert J, Köpke S.
abstractText:
Background

Hospitalised patients with advanced chronic heart failure (CHF) waiting for transplantation may experience increased thirst due to their critical illness and therapy-related requirements. The perspective of patients and nurses is important for developing a nurse-based counselling intervention to reduce thirst.

Aims

To identify patients' and nurses' experiences and perceptions of thirst, as well as their information needs and preferences on information dissemination.

Study design

This convergent mixed methods study used semi-structured interviews with patients, focus groups and a survey with nurses in Germany. We analysed the qualitative data using content analysis and the quantitative data descriptively. We compared the results of both methodological approaches and summarized the data as meta-inferences.

Results & findings

We conducted 10 interviews with patients on intensive care units, intermediate care units and general wards during their waiting time for transplantation, two focus groups with, respectively, five nurses and a survey with 59 nurses caring for these patients. Analyses resulted in five common categories: experiences of thirst, factors that influence thirst, assessment of thirst, dealing with thirst and information about thirst. Patients' experiences with thirst differ markedly, ranging from mild to severe thirst, and they use various strategies to deal with thirst. Nurses consider thirst relevant for patients and nursing care. Strategies used in practice for assessment of thirst are very heterogeneous. In the survey, less than half of the nurses claimed to regularly assess patients' thirst. Nurses and patients wish to receive individual information and counselling.

Conclusions

Thirst in hospitalised patients with advanced CHF waiting for transplantation can be severe and is experienced differently. Standardised procedures for assessing and managing thirst on the ward seem essential to address patients' needs and preferences.

Relevance to clinical practice

Patients and nurses express a need for professional counselling on managing thirst in clinical practice.

title: Postoperative Delirium in Intensive Care Units: A Bibliometric Analysis of Nursing Studies.
authorString: Ünver S, Yeniğün Akbulut SC.
abstractText:
Background

Delirium is a common and serious postoperative complication in intensive care units, associated with increased morbidity, mortality and long-term cognitive impairment, and despite the pivotal role of nurses in its assessment and management, variations in prevalence and gaps in intervention-focused nursing research persist, underscoring the need for a bibliometric evaluation of the literature.

Aim

The aim of the study was to quantitatively analyse and visually map trends, citations, key terms and country contributions in nursing research on postoperative delirium in intensive care as well as to characterize the overall structure of the literature.

Study design

This study was conducted as a retrospective and descriptive research using the bibliometric analysis method on December 1, 2025. No time restrictions were imposed on the literature. Data analysis was performed using R Studio software.

Results

The earliest study on postoperative delirium in intensive care units within the field of nursing was published in 2001, and the analysed publications covered the period from 2001 to December 2025. In addition, 55.96% of all publications have been released in the past 7 years. The journal with the highest number of publications is Nursing in Critical Care, while the United States stands out as the country with the highest research output. It can be suggested that topics such as 'cardiac surgery', 'nursing care', 'postoperative delirium', 'postoperative care' and the 'Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit' represent areas that warrant further investigation and development in future research.

Conclusions

The analysis showed a marked increase in publications on postoperative delirium in intensive care nursing in recent years. The United States and the Journal Nursing in Critical Care were identified as the leading contributors to the literature. Thematic mapping indicated that the literature primarily focused on delirium assessment and intensive care nursing, with several interconnected research areas.

Relevance to clinical practice

The findings emphasize the critical role of nurses in delirium screening and management in intensive care units. While assessment tools are well represented in the literature, further research is needed to develop and evaluate nurse-led interventions aimed at delirium prevention and care. Enhancing nursing education and institutional support may contribute to improved patient outcomes and quality of postoperative intensive care.

title: Postoperative Delirium and the Association to Continuously Monitored Severe Deviations of Vital Signs at the General Ward After Major Abdominal Surgery.
authorString: Awada HN, Haahr-Raunkjær C, Mølgaard J, Rasmussen SM, Meyhoff CS, Aasvang EK.
abstractText:
Background

Delirium is the most frequent neurological complication after surgery and is associated with increased postoperative morbidity and mortality. The underlying pathophysiology is not fully understood, but is suggested to be multifactorial, including hypoperfusion and hypoxia; however, the role of deviating vital signs prior to postoperative delirium (POD) remains unclear. This study aimed to examine the association between severe physiological deviations detected by continuous wireless monitoring and the occurrence of POD within the first three postoperative days after major abdominal cancer surgery.

Methods

In this prospective substudy, the primary outcome delirium was assessed daily with the validated 3D-CAM questionnaire during the first three postoperative days following major abdominal cancer surgery, and patients were classified into three groups: POD, neurocognitive decline (NCD), and no cognitive impairment (controls). Vital signs (blood pressure, respiratory rate, heart rate, and peripheral oxygen saturation) were continuously monitored for up to 96 h postoperatively. The primary exposure was the cumulative duration of severely deviating vital signs 24 h before POD diagnosis. Secondary exposures included the frequency of sustained severe vital sign deviation episodes.

Results

Of 225 patients with complete 3D-CAM data, 22 (9.8%) developed POD, 73 (32.4%) had NCD, and 130 (57.8%) had no cognitive impairment (controls). The median cumulative duration of vital sign deviations 24 h prior to POD was not significantly different between POD patients and controls (204 min vs. 325 min, p = 0.63). Episodes of sustained tachycardia, bradycardia, and bradypnea in the 24 h prior to POD diagnosis were more frequent in POD patients compared to controls, all p < 0.001. In the 24 h after POD diagnosis, patients with POD also exhibited more frequent episodes of sustained tachypnea, desaturation, tachycardia, and hypertension than controls (all p ≤ 0.005). In NCD patients, deviations were intermediate: bradypnea and bradycardia were more frequent before, and tachycardia, hypotension, hypertension, and desaturation more frequent after the NCD assessment, compared with controls.

Conclusion

Although the cumulative duration of severe vital sign deviations did not differ between POD patients and controls, episodes of sustained severe vital sign deviations were significantly more frequent in POD patients before and after POD diagnosis, suggesting a potential for earlier identification of patients at risk. Whether acting on these signals alters the incidence of delirium was not tested and requires a prospective study.

Editorial comment

In this secondary analysis of a prospectively assessed high risk surgical cohort, postoperative vital sign deviations acquired from wireless technology were analysed for possible relations to postoperative delirium development. The findings show that vital sign deviation was observed often before or after delirium development, though it is not yet clear which category or measurement of vital sign deviation would be most likely to be associated with delirium.

Trial registration

NCT03491137.

title: OGT-mediated O-GlcNAcylation of TEAD1 at Serine 132 enhances TEAD1 stability and activity and contributes to atherosclerosis progression.
authorString: Yin X, Liu Z, Gao Z, Yan H, Kuang L, Guo J, Zou J, Wang L, Chen S, Wen T.
abstractText: Atherosclerosis is a leading cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, yet the molecular mechanisms driving plaque progression remain incompletely understood. O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT) couples nutrient status to protein O-GlcNAcylation, but its vascular actions appear context-dependent. In an exploratory carotid endarterectomy cohort, OGT expression and global O-GlcNAcylation were higher in plaques obtained from symptomatic patients than in plaques from asymptomatic patients. In Western diet-fed ApoE-/- mice, inducible smooth muscle cell-specific OGT deletion was associated with lower aortic lesion burden, lower serum triglyceride and total cholesterol concentrations, and reduced plaque lipid and collagen areas. Proteomic screening identified TEAD1 (TEA domain transcription factor 1) as an O-GlcNAcylated protein enriched in clinically symptomatic human samples. OGT interacted with TEAD1 and promoted O-GlcNAcylation at Serine 132 (S132); mutation of this residue reduced TEAD1 stability, nuclear accumulation, and reporter activity. In a complementary human umbilical vein endothelial cell model, OGT knockdown limited oxidized low-density lipoprotein-induced injury, inflammation, monocyte adhesion, and endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition, whereas TEAD1 overexpression attenuated these effects. Smooth muscle-targeted TEAD1 overexpression also attenuated the lesion reduction associated with OGT deletion in vivo. These findings support an OGT-TEAD1 pathway in atherosclerosis while indicating that concurrent lipid changes, plaque-cell specificity, and the relative endothelial contribution require further resolution.

title: Predictive value of exercise PETO<sub>2</sub> changes for major adverse cardiovascular events in ischaemic heart disease: An exploratory study.
authorString: Sasaki Y, Asada K.
abstractText: The difference in end-tidal oxygen partial pressure (ΔPETO<sub>2</sub>) between rest and anaerobic threshold exercise is reportedly a predictor of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in heart disease patients, but its predictive accuracy has not been verified in ischaemic heart disease (IHD). We analyzed the incidence of MACE within 3 years after cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) in IHD patients, and calculated ΔPETO<sub>2</sub> from the CPET data. Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified the ΔPETO<sub>2</sub> cutoff value in predicting MACE occurrence, after which patients were divided into low ΔPETO<sub>2</sub> and high ΔPETO<sub>2</sub> groups. Kaplan-Meier analysis using the log-rank test was performed to compare the incidence of MACE within 3 years, and multiple regression analysis was conducted with ΔPETO<sub>2</sub> as the dependent variable. Among 168 cases (mean age 66.2 ± 10.1 years; 143 males), 22 patients (13%) experienced MACE. The optimal ΔPETO<sub>2</sub> cutoff value in predicting MACE was 2.5 mmHg (area under the curve 0.888, sensitivity 77%, specificity 90%). Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed that the MACE incidence rate was significantly higher in the ΔPETO<sub>2</sub> ≤ 2.5 group compared to the ΔPETO<sub>2</sub> > 2.5 group. Multiple regression analysis identified peak oxygen pulse (peak O<sub>2</sub> pulse), ankle-brachial index (ABI), and dyslipidemia (DL) as independent factors associated with ΔPETO<sub>2</sub>. ΔPETO<sub>2</sub> may serve as a useful early indicator for predicting high risk of MACE in IHD before the onset of heart failure. Additionally, peak O<sub>2</sub> pulse, ABI, and DL were identified as factors influencing ΔPETO<sub>2</sub>, suggesting that blood flow to the lower limbs may impact ΔPETO<sub>2</sub>.

title: Maresin 2 Attenuates Hypertensive Vascular Remodeling via Inhibiting Macrophage Infiltration and Pro-fibrotic Polarization.
authorString: Peng S, Wang T, Liu J, Zhao M, Shen Z, Liu S, Wei C, Zheng Z, Xu Y, Wan J, Wang M.
abstractText: Immune-inflammatory responses are pivotal regulators of hypertensive vascular remodeling. Specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs), including Maresin 2 (MaR2), are endogenous anti-inflammatory molecules. However, the specific role of MaR2 in regulating hypertension and vascular remodeling, as well as its underlying mechanisms, remains unclear. In this study, a murine model of hypertension was induced by continuous infusion of Angiotensin II (AngII) at 1 μg/kg/min. MaR2 intervention (2 μg/kg/day) was administered either prophylactically (before model induction) or therapeutically (after model induction). Prophylactic MaR2 effectively prevented AngII-induced blood pressure elevation and vascular remodeling. Similarly, therapeutic administration after the establishment of hypertension with MaR2 significantly lowered blood pressure and attenuated medial thickening and fibrosis in the aorta and mesenteric arteries. Mechanistic studies revealed that MaR2 significantly inhibited macrophage infiltration and inflammatory responses within vascular tissues. Further in vitro and in vivo experiments confirmed that MaR2 effectively suppressed AngII-induced macrophage polarization toward a pro-fibrotic phenotype and reduced the acquisition of a myofibroblast-like phenotype (i.e., α-SMA expression) by macrophages by blocking the TGF-β/Smad3 signaling pathway. Notably, pharmacological activation of TGF-β/Smad signaling using SRI011381 partially counteracted the protective effects of MaR2 on vascular remodeling. MaR2 attenuates AngII-induced hypertension and vascular remodeling in association with reduced vascular macrophage accumulation and suppression of macrophage pro-fibrotic polarization, at least partly through regulation of TGF-β/Smad3 signaling. These findings identify MaR2 as a candidate pro-resolving intervention in an AngII-induced murine model of hypertension and support further mechanistic and translational evaluation in hypertension-associated vascular remodeling.

title: Stratifying Cardiovascular Risk in Patients With HCC Receiving Atezolizumab/Bevacizumab: A Comparison of ESC and CARDIOSOR Scores.
authorString: Stefanini B, Rimassa L, Iavarone M, Cabibbo G, Marra F, Vivaldi C, Dalbeni A, Ponziani FR, Palloni A, Lonardi S, Lani L, Federico P, Svegliati-Baroni G, Pressiani T, Ielasi L, Mazzarelli C, De Lorenzo S, Sacco R, Bruccoleri M, Celsa C, Mastro A, Masi G, Auriemma A, Stella L, Toniutto P, Villani R, Deiana C, Ascari S, Marseglia M, Granito A, Piscaglia F, Tovoli F, ARTE Study Group.

journal.title: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

abstractText:
Background & aims

The management of comorbidities has become increasingly relevant in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC) as immunotherapy prolongs survival. Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (AB) is a standard first-line option, but bevacizumab carries a risk of cardiovascular toxicities. Data on cardiovascular risk stratification in patients with cirrhosis remain limited. Identifying patients at increased cardiovascular risk is therefore clinically important, particularly given the availability of bevacizumab-free alternatives.

Methods

We retrospectively analysed prospectively collected data from the multicenter Italian ARTE database, including patients with uHCC treated with first-line AB between June 2022 and July 2025. Traditional major adverse cardiovascular events (tMACE) were defined as acute coronary syndromes, heart failure, cerebrovascular events, or peripheral ischemia, while an extended composite (eMACE) additionally included venous thromboembolism and immune-related myocarditis. Cardiovascular risk was stratified using the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) Cardio-Oncology classification and the CARDIOSOR score. Competing-risk analyses were performed considering treatment discontinuation as a competing event.

Results

This study included 538 patients (median age 69.8 years). During follow-up, 20 patients (3.7%) experienced tMACE, and 30 (5.6%) experienced eMACE. Patients assigned to the very high-risk category by ESC criteria and those with a high-risk CARDIOSOR score had a significantly increased risk of tMACE and eMACE. Both scores demonstrated a moderate ability to stratify cardiovascular risk (Harrell's c-index 0.68 for ESC and 0.59 for CARDIOSOR).

Conclusions

Cardiovascular adverse events were uncommon overall, but their incidence was not negligible in patients in high-risk subgroups. Risk scores may help identify vulnerable subgroups and support patient-tailored treatment strategies, including consideration of bevacizumab-free regimens in selected cases.

Trial registration

Multicenter ARTE database (NCT06806579).

title: Continuous Imaging of the Cardiac Cycle Metabolism With Hyperpolarized [1-<sup>13</sup>C]Pyruvate.
authorString: Redda M, Bøgh N, Hansen ESS, Kjærgaard U, Schulte RF, Laustsen C.
abstractText: Hyperpolarized (HP) <sup>13</sup>C MRI enables noninvasive assessment of myocardial metabolism. Current approaches typically acquire data only during diastole, ignoring phase-dependent metabolic changes. This study aimed to develop an imaging technique to capture HP [<sup>13</sup>C]bicarbonate production across both systole and diastole in healthy porcine hearts under rest and stress conditions. Six Danish domestic pigs underwent conventional cardiac MRI and HP [1-<sup>13</sup>C]pyruvate MRI on an MR750 3 T system (GE HealthCare) before and during pharmacological stress by injecting adenosine (250 μg/min/kg) and dobutamine (5 μg/min/kg). Metabolic imaging was obtained by single-frequency imaging on [<sup>13</sup>C]bicarbonate. Concurrent off-resonance excitation on [1-<sup>13</sup>C]pyruvate was utilized to generate a simultaneous pyruvate input function. Bicarbonate-to-pyruvate ratios (Bic/Pyr ratio) were compared from rest to stress throughout the cardiac cycle. Dynamic metabolic changes were successfully captured with sufficient temporal resolution to resolve both systolic and diastolic phases. From rest to stress, during systole the Bic/Pyr ratio increased by 150% (95% CI 50%-330%, p = 0.0076) and during diastole it increased by 170% (95% CI 50%-380%, p = 0.0083). During rest, the Bic/Pyr ratio decreased by 21% from systole to diastole (95% CI 4%-35%, p = 0.027), and during stress, it decreased by 16% (95% CI 4%-26%, p = 0.019). Simultaneous phase-resolved imaging of [1-<sup>13</sup>C]pyruvate and [<sup>13</sup>C]bicarbonate enables high-temporal-resolution assessment of myocardial metabolism during both systole and diastole compared to conventional single-frequency acquisitions. This simultaneous acquisition strategy removes the need for separate pyruvate and bicarbonate acquisitions, doubling the temporal resolution of the resulting image series, while revealing dynamic increases in Bic/Pyr ratio from rest to stress and between systole and diastole. This approach overcomes the limitations of single-phase imaging and provides a foundation for investigating phase-dependent metabolic alterations in disease.

title: Motives matter: A smartphone EMA study on the association between motives to exercise, exercise engagement and mood.
authorString: Pimpini L, Ferrand E, Mironiuc C, Schepers J, Roefs A.
abstractText:
Objective

Regular exercise is vital for preventing cardiovascular disease, maintaining a healthy body weight and supporting mental well-being, yet most people exercise insufficiently often due to motivational barriers.

Design

This study examined two types of exercise motive-functional (divided into health/fitness and enjoyment) and appearance-and their interplay with mood and exercise engagement in daily life. Two hypotheses were tested: (H1) functional motives, compared to appearance motive, predict greater exercise engagement, and (H2) higher (more positive) mood, in interaction with exercise motives, predicts greater exercise engagement.

Method

Ninety-eight healthy BMI women completed a 2-week smartphone Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA) protocol reporting exercise motive (baseline), exercise engagement (frequency, intensity, duration) and mood several times/day.

Results

Partially supporting H1, enjoyment motive predicted greater exercise frequency and duration, whereas-contrary to H1- health/fitness motive predicted shorter duration and appearance was unrelated to engagement. H2 was not supported: mood did not predict engagement and functional motives did not strengthen the mood-engagement link. Contrary to H2, the appearance motive strengthened the (same-moment) within-person association between mood and exercise intensity, such that women higher in appearance motive showed a stronger positive mood-intensity link. Multilevel temporal networks revealed that higher (more positive) mood at one assessment weakly predicted greater exercise intensity and duration at the next assessment.

Conclusions

Together, enjoyment emerges as central to exercise engagement, while positive mood temporally precedes exercise, informing future lifestyle interventions. Further research on the temporal dynamics linking mood and exercise is warranted.

title: Identification of Quality Markers for Tongmai Qiangshen Medicinal Liquor in the Treatment of Heart Failure Based on Multicomponent Qualitative-Quantitative Analysis and Integrated Bioinformatics.
authorString: Li Y, Huo J, Zhang Q, Li T, Wang S, Bao Y, Meng X.
abstractText: Heart failure (HF) is an end stage of cardiovascular diseases. Tongmai Qiangshen Medicinal Liquor (TMQSJ) is an over-the-counter traditional Chinese medicinal liquor, but its efficacy-related material basis and mechanisms in HF remain unclear. In this study, UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS was used to characterize TMQSJ constituents and prototype compounds in rat plasma. HPLC fingerprinting, spectrum-effect relationship analysis, single-compound activity evaluation, and integrative bioinformatics were combined to screen efficacy-related candidate quality markers and HF-associated candidate genes. A total of 223 compounds were characterized, including 33 prototype plasma components. Chemometric analysis identified caffeic acid, Epimedin A, Epimedin B, Epimedin C, and icariin as characteristic constituents. Spectrum-effect analysis based on 10 batches of TMQSJ and validation in DOX-injured AC16 cells highlighted Epimedin A, Epimedin B, and Epimedin C. Among them, Epimedin A and Epimedin C showed prototype plasma exposure and were prioritized as efficacy-related candidate quality markers. Integration of predicted targets of prototype plasma components with HF transcriptomic data and machine-learning analysis identified BCL2L1, STAT3, HIF1A, MAPK8, and ESR1 as five candidate core genes. Immune cell estimation and molecular docking provided computational clues. Overall, this study establishes an integrated framework linking chemical quality, pharmacological association, in vivo exposure, and mechanistic prediction for TMQSJ quality evaluation.

title: Dynamic Changes and Diagnostic Value of Plasma Tryptophan and Its Metabolites in Different Stages of Hepatic Encephalopathy Detected by Ultra-Performance Liquid Chromatography-Tandem Mass Spectrometry.
authorString: Zhou R, Shan BY, Xue ZZ, Yang ZF, Feng R, Zhong SY, Wang S.
abstractText: Hepatic encephalopathy (HE) is a severe neuropsychiatric complication of liver disease. Early diagnosis remains challenging due to insidious onset and lack of stage-specific biomarkers. Tryptophan (TRP) metabolism is closely linked to the gut-liver-brain axis and is dysregulated in HE. However, most prior studies only compared a single HE model with controls, failing to uncover stage-to-stage dynamic alterations. Here, we quantified plasma TRP metabolites across HE stages 1-4 in a rat model using UPLC-MS/MS. Compared with the Sham group, ALT and AST peaked in HE2 and declined in HE3-HE4, reflecting massive acute hepatocyte necrosis followed by enzyme exhaustion, whereas histological liver injury and modified neurological severity score (mNSS) scores progressively worsened. TRP metabolites exhibited stage-dependent shifts: TRP, kynurenine, and XA fell, whereas 5-HT and IAA rose in HE1; TA increased in HE2-HE3; KA and XA elevated, but IPA dropped in HE4. These results indicated that plasma TRP metabolic profiles are closely linked to liver injury and neurological dysfunction during HE progression and serve as candidate staging biomarkers in rat models, awaiting further clinical-cohort validation. From a broader perspective, this study reveals dynamic reprogramming of TRP metabolism in HE, providing preclinical evidence for metabolomics-oriented diagnosis and targeted therapy.

title: Development and Validation of Two Analytical Methods Using High-Performance Liquid Chromatography and Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy for the Analysis of Tunisian Marketed Pharmaceutical Product-Based Insulin and Zinc: Application in Routine Stability Study.
authorString: Ben Messaoud M, Mahfoudhi S, Amor D, Mokni Y, Louati K, Zribi K, Omezzine A, Safta F.
abstractText: Given the widespread reliance on insulin among diabetic patients, ensuring its stability is an essential task not only for preserving its therapeutic efficacy but also for safeguarding patient health and safety. In addition, insulin storage practices were frequently misunderstood that may compromise drug potency. Moreover, there were discrepancies in the shelf lives of the different insulin products offered in Tunisia. Therefore, two analytical methods for the analysis of insulin using high-performance liquid chromatography coupled to ultraviolet detector (HPLC-UV) and zinc using atomic absorption spectroscopy (AAS) in Tunisian marketed pharmaceutical product-based insulin were employed. Then the stability of these products was assessed. The study showed good insulin stability at neutral pH exposed to daylight for at least 30 days at 25°C, whereas instability was revealed only in diluted solutions at pH 2. Our work highlights the necessity for a more comprehensive evaluation of insulin stability, particularly under conditions where consistent refrigeration is not feasible. Such an assessment is essential to inform practical storage guidelines and ensure therapeutic efficacy in resource-limited settings.

title: Prehospital Births in the Region of Southern Denmark-A Cohort From 2016 to 2024.
authorString: Pedersen LL, Christensen HC, Jørgensen JS, Gradman J, Wolthers SA, Mikkelsen S.
abstractText:
Background

Unplanned births outside hospitals involve higher risks of complications for mothers and newborns and require special obstetric or pediatric skills. However, ambulance calls for childbirth are rare, making it difficult for ambulance staff to maintain their skills. In Europe, unplanned out-of-hospital deliveries constitute 0.10% to 0.61% of all births. The exact number of prehospital births in the Region of Southern Denmark remains unknown. The study aimed to determine the extent of unplanned prehospital births attended by the ambulance service outside hospitals in the Region of Southern Denmark from January 2016 through June 2024. We further aimed to identify where the unplanned pre-hospital births took place and to report any birth-related complications in the mothers or newborns encountered by ambulance staff.

Methods

The study was a cross-sectional study utilizing the pre-hospital electronic Patient Medical Record system over 8 years in a mixed urban-rural area with a population of 1.2 million people. All prehospital medical records for ambulance missions dispatched for childbirths were manually examined. The study period spanned from January 2016 through June 2024.

Results

Out of 1,137,222 ambulance dispatches, 3543 cases (0.31%) involved a dispatch code related to childbirth. Many labor incidents were considered uneventful by the prehospital personnel. Of all ambulance runs related to childbirth, we identified 310 births in the Region of Southern Denmark in which ambulance staff assisted with complicated out-of-hospital deliveries. An additional 10 labor cases were regarded as sufficiently complex that obstetric manoeuvres aimed at delaying the delivery of the baby were performed prehospitally, while the mother was rushed to hospital for delivery.

Conclusion

Births outside the hospital while the mother is in the care of the EMS were rare, occurring in 0.03% of all ambulance missions. Most of the births took place without complications for both mother and neonate. In four cases, however, the neonate was in cardiac arrest and required resuscitation. Given the limited exposure to prehospital births, we suggest incorporating training in handling these rare events into routine training for prehospital caregivers.

Editorial comment

This cohort study presents obstetrical cases that have been managed first in the prehospital setting by ambulance personnel. Obstetrical outcomes related to this are presented, and there are considerations for what can be desirable as preparation and competencies for ambulance responses for these types of cases.

title: Renal Myeloid Mechanisms, Cross-Talk in Hypertension.
authorString: Michea L, Brooks HL.
abstractText: Hypertension involves an impairment of renal sodium excretion along with activation of pro-inflammatory responses in the kidney. Dendritic cells (DCs) are professional antigen-presenting cells that sense disturbances in cell and tissue homeostasis to orchestrate T cell activation and recruitment. Renal DCs distribute as a cellular network throughout the renal interstitium, forming an interface between innate and adaptive immunity. Here, we explore what is known about renal cross-talk following prohypertensive stimuli, which modify renal DCs, T cell polarization, and renal function, leading to hypertension. We also present the phenotypic and functional heterogeneity of DCs, including literature on in vitro and in vivo signaling mechanisms in a variety of hypertensive models. Current studies indicate that renal sodium retention caused by prohypertensive stimuli requires DC function. The prohypertensive action of DCs also requires T cell function. Several cross-talk mechanisms have been proposed, such as signals from the kidney to the DC, including salt activation of DC's via RAAS receptor signaling, and DC-dependent recruitment of T cells to the kidney then promoting increased renal tubular sodium reabsorption. Knowledge gaps include specific functions of renal DC subtypes, sex differences in DC-mediated hypertension, and clinical studies on DC function in hypertension. The identification of mechanisms leading to renal DCs activation in hypertension may offer new strategies for the prevention and treatment of hypertension.

title: Intrahepatic Tissue-Resident CD8<sup>+</sup> T-Cell Programmes Associate With Fibrosis and Local Immune Remodelling in Autoimmune Hepatitis.
authorString: Stary V, Losek S, Mairinger M, Prager G, Santol J, Starlinger PP, Reiberger T, Stättermayer AF, Stary G.

journal.title: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

abstractText:
Background and aims

Autoimmune hepatitis is an immune-mediated liver disease characterized by chronic inflammation and progressive fibrosis. Tissue-resident memory T cells mediate organ-specific immunity, but their role in autoimmune hepatitis remains poorly understood. We characterized tissue-residency-associated T-cell populations and their cytokine profiles, assessed associations with disease severity and determined whether these signatures were reflected in peripheral blood.

Methods

Paired blood and liver samples were obtained from 19 patients with autoimmune hepatitis. Comparator cohorts included 20 patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and 20 surgical patients providing non-inflamed adjacent non-tumorous liver tissue. Multiparameter flow cytometry assessed tissue-residency markers, T-cell differentiation and cytokine production after polyclonal stimulation. Immune phenotypes were correlated with histological and clinical parameters.

Results

Autoimmune hepatitis was associated with compartment-specific remodelling of T-cell differentiation states and intrahepatic enrichment of CD8+ T cells expressing CD69, CD103 and CXCR6 relative to paired blood and comparator liver tissues. Intrahepatic CD8+ T cells exhibited an interferon-γ-dominant cytokine profile, whereas CD4+ T cells showed broader interferon-γ-, interleukin-17A- and interleukin-4-associated responses. Despite the enrichment of tissue-residency-associated CD8+ T cells, cytokine-producing CD8+ T-cell populations with and without a tissue-resident memory phenotype contributed comparably to the hepatic T-cell compartment. Tissue-residency-associated phenotypes correlated positively with Ishak fibrosis stage, whereas the frequency of interferon-γ-positive intrahepatic CD8+ T cells correlated inversely with fibrosis.

Conclusions

Autoimmune hepatitis was characterized by intrahepatic accumulation of phenotypically distinct and functionally active CD8+ tissue-resident memory T cells associated with fibrosis. This immune profile was not reflected in paired blood, indicating compartmentalized hepatic immune remodelling.

title: Higher frequency of homologous chromosome pairing in adult endothelial cells as compared to in neonatal endothelial cells.
authorString: Morales J, Akhtar O, Quintero Plancarte G, Hua L.
abstractText: Homologous chromosomes are spatially segregated, or antipaired, in neonatal human endothelial cells at metaphase and anaphase, which might help prevent abnormal recombination. However, it is unclear whether this antipairing persists in adult endothelial cells. To test whether the antipairing, or one homolog per nuclear hemisphere motif, is conserved in adult endothelial cells, we examined human aortic endothelial cells at metaphase. Using immunolabeling with DNA fluorescent in situ hybridization (ImmunoFISH) and high-resolution confocal microscopy to visualize the chromosomes and centrosomes, we found that small homologous chromosomes 13, 15, 17, 19, 21, 22, and the sex chromosomes (XY) exhibit a loss of spatial segregation in human adult aortic endothelial cells. In addition, fewer adult endothelial cells showed segregation for the larger chromosomes 1, 4 and XX, as compared to in neonatal endothelial cells. Notably, we observed a higher frequency of abnormal pairing in both small and large chromosomes in adult aortic endothelial cells as compared to in neonatal umbilical vein endothelial cells. These findings suggest that mechanisms governing chromosome antipairing might decline with aortic endothelial cell age.

title: Influence of a long air gap and a ratio 15:1 antiscatter grid on pediatric fluoroscopy and angiography image quality.
authorString: Fetterly K.
abstractText: Objective.X-ray angiography and fluoroscopy systems are used to diagnose and treat congenital heart disease in pediatric patients. Among the substantial variabilities in this clinical patient population is that patient weight ranges from <1 kg premature infants to large adolescents. The primary aim of this work was to assess whether an air gap or antiscatter grid is more efficient to mitigate the detrimental influence of scatter radiation on pediatric image quality.Approach.The experimental approach was guided by a 2 year review of pediatric patient imaging conditions. Uniform density water-equivalent phantoms with thickness in the range 6-24 cm were used. For each phantom thickness, the x-ray technique was manually set to mimic the technique selected by automatic dose rate control. The influence of four combinations of air gap and ratio 15:1 antiscatter grid on test object SNR was measured. The air gap was varied by changing the x-ray source to detector distance from 107 to 120 cm. The analytical methods estimated pixel-specific snr2contributions to object SNR2, thus providing for the use of iodine disks and pediatric implantable devices as test objects.Main results.Patient weight ranged from 0.5 to 134 kg. The relationship between patient water equivalent thickness and weight was demonstrated. For all phantom thicknesses, object SNR was highest using a long air gap, non-grid technique. Decreasing the air gap between the phantom and detector and use of the anti-scatter grid both degraded SNR. These major findings were consistent between iodine disks and clinical devices as test objects.Significance.The findings of this phantom study suggest that a long air gap, non-grid imaging technique may improve radiation dose efficiency of fluoroscopy and angiography imaging across a broad range of pediatric patient sizes.

title: Association of Poor Mental Health and Cardiovascular Events Among Middle-Aged and older people's: A population-based case control study
authorString: Moradi A, Norouzi M, Mosafarkhani E.
abstractText:
Introduction: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain the leading cause of death worldwide, and growing evidence suggests that poor mental health may play an important role in their onset. However, the association between mental disorders and cardiovascular events (CVE) among middle-aged and older adults in Iran has not been well explored.

Methods:

This population based case control study using data from the Sina Electronic Health Record (SinaEHR®) system between 2017 and 2024. A total of 14,674 individuals aged ≥ 50 years were included, comprising 7,337 patients with confirmed CVE and 7,337 frequency-matched controls by age and sex without CVE. Mental disorders were identified based on ICD-10 codes (F00–F99), and cardiovascular outcomes included ischemic heart disease and stroke events. Logistic regression was applied to estimate crude and adjusted odds ratios (OR, AOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) controlling for sociodemographic lifestyle and clinical variables. Results : Mental disorders were significantly more common among CVE cases (60.8%) compared to controls (39.2%, p_value < 0.001). After adjustment, mental disorders remained independently associated with CVE (AOR = 1.69, 95% CI: 1.52–1.88). Depression (AOR = 1.53, 95% CI: 1.22–1.92) and anxiety (AOR = 1.94, 95% CI: 1.56–2.40) were particularly strong predictors. Traditional risk factors also showed significant associations like advanced age (≥ 70 years, AOR = 3.39 compared to 50–59), overweight and obesity (AOR: 2.99–3.10 compared to healthy weight), hypertension (AOR = 2.12), hypercholesterolemia (AOR = 1.86), diabetes (AOR = 1.17), smoking (AOR = 1.72), and drug abuse (AOR = 2.30). Conclusion : Poor mental health especially depression and anxiety is an independent risk factor for cardiovascular events in middle-aged and older adults. Integrating mental health assessment and care into cardiovascular prevention strategies could reduce CVE burden in this vulnerable population.

title: The Centriole as a Differentiation Ratchet: A Hypothesis and an Experimental Roadmap Built on the Naturally Acentriolar Adult Cardiomyocytes of Human, Mouse and Rat
authorString: Tqemaladze J.
abstractText: The adult mammalian heart does not regenerate. After myocardial infarction, cardiomyocytes are lost permanently because the surviving cells are terminally differentiated and post-mitotic. Regenerative vertebrates such as zebrafish and newts retain proliferative, centriole-bearing cardiomyocytes and repair the heart completely, whereas mammals lose this capacity within the first postnatal week. I propose that the centriole functions as a differentiation ratchet: a heritable structural input that couples proliferative potential to centriole integrity through the mitotic surveillance pathway (MSP). The strongest natural evidence comes from the heart. Shortly after birth, mammalian cardiomyocytes undergo programmed centrosome disassembly, with pericentriolar material relocating to the nuclear envelope. Pharmacological depletion of centrioles is sufficient to drive the post-mitotic transition in human cardiomyocytes, and failure of this step is pathogenic: a mutation in the centrosomal gene RTTN causes infantile dilated cardiomyopathy. Because the adult cardiomyocyte is one of the few naturally and permanently acentriolar somatic cells, it offers a ready-made testbed for asking whether the ratchet can be reversed. A single-nucleus transcriptomic analysis of the developing human heart (fetal, young and adult) presented here shows that this shutdown is actively installed during maturation rather than a passive decay: adult cardiomyocytes reduce their centriolar program—PLK4, CEP192, SASS6, STIL and NEK2 are all down-regulated—while the p53 effector p21 (CDKN1A) is elevated, the signature of a p53-maintained post-mitotic lock. The roadmap proceeds in three steps, all conducted in cell culture: (i) release the G0 lock and assess TRIM37 and PLK1 status; (ii) restore a licensed centriole from an autologous low-entropy adult stem cell, with PLK1 and Ect2 co-delivery; and (iii) enforce a strict safety gate that includes TRIM37, p53 pathway, and contractile function assessment. Eight pre-registered, falsifiable hypotheses are stated below, and the principal risks are analyzed.

title: Wide-angled proteomics in giant cell arteritis reveals complement pathway activation
authorString: Whittle BJ, Williams M, Lomax-Browne H, Sorensen L, Maughan RT, Porteous M, Chakrabarty A, Luqmani RA, Pickering MC, Morgan AW, Peters JE.
abstractText: Giant cell arteritis (GCA) is an immune-mediated vasculitis that can cause serious morbidity including sight loss, stroke and aortic aneurysm. There is an unmet need for blood-based biomarkers and novel therapeutics. We measured plasma protein levels using the SomaScan v4.1 platform, comprising 7,273 protein measurements (SOMAmers) reflecting 6,596 unique protein targets. We profiled the proteome in 113 patients who presented acutely with possible GCA. 56 had biopsy-proven GCA and 57 did not have GCA (non-GCA). We found 144 SOMAmers increased and 151 reduced in GCA. Dysregulated biological pathways included IL6-JAK-STAT3 signalling, chemokines for both myeloid (e.g. CXCL2, CXCL3, CCL18, CCL23) and lymphoid cells (e.g. CXCL9, CXCL13), and the complement system (e.g. C9, CFHR5, C5a, Factor B). Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assays (ELISAs) confirmed elevated plasma levels of C5a, the terminal complement complex, Factor B and CFHR5 in GCA. We developed a 26-protein signature that distinguished GCA from non-GCA (area-under-the curve, AUC, 0.93) and validated the diagnostic signature in external datasets. Our data implicate terminal complement pathway activation in GCA, raising the possibility of complement-directed therapies. We show proof-of-principle that a multiplex protein biomarker could be used as a diagnostic adjunct in suspected GCA.

title: Cardiorespiratory arrest during the first rituximab infusion in a patient with refractory chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy: a case report
authorString: Velasco-Hoyos MF, Carvajal-Paz LJ, Gómez-Idrobo C.
abstractText: Background Rituximab is used off-label as rescue therapy in selected patients with refractory chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy (CIDP), but severe immediate infusion-related reactions can occur. Case presentation: A 69-year-old man with progressive, refractory CIDP received rituximab after an insufficient response to intravenous immunoglobulin and intolerance to plasma exchange. After approximately 40 mL of the first infusion, he developed abrupt respiratory compromise, hemodynamic collapse, and asystolic cardiac arrest. Return of spontaneous circulation was achieved after 10 minutes of advanced cardiopulmonary resuscitation. He required mechanical ventilation and transient vasopressor support, subsequently recovered without recurrent cardiovascular instability, and rituximab was discontinued. The precise mechanism of the reaction could not be established because serum tryptase, interleukin-6, and formal allergy testing were not obtained. Conclusion Severe and potentially fatal reactions may occur within the first milliliters of an initial rituximab infusion. Continuous monitoring and immediate access to advanced resuscitation are essential, particularly in medically complex patients.

title: Vitamin D Status in European Zoo-Housed Great Apes
authorString: Martin RJ, Moittié S, Bandelow S, Byrne S, Dobbs P, Baiker K, Grant MM, Reeves C, White K, Liptovszky M.
abstractText: Vitamin D is crucial for physiological homeostasis and cardiovascular health. Zoo-housed great apes in Europe face significant risks of vitamin D deficiency due to limited ultraviolet B (UVB) exposure, potentially exacerbating conditions such as idiopathic myocardial fibrosis. This multi-centre observational study evaluated 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25-OHD) concentrations using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry in 480 opportunistic serum and plasma samples from 334 individuals across five great ape species (bonobo, chimpanzee, Western lowland gorilla, Sumatran orangutan, and Bornean orangutan) housed in 56 European zoos. Mixed-effects models were utilised to investigate the impact of individual, environmental, and husbandry factors on 25-OHD status. Using human reference intervals, 45.7% of samples were classified as deficient or insufficient (≤ 50 nmol/L). Insufficiency was most prevalent in bonobos (71.4%) and orangutans (58.6%). Local UVB irradiance and dietary fortification via commercial pellet in the diet emerged as the strongest positive predictors of 25-OHD levels. Unrestricted outdoor access also correlated with significantly higher concentrations. Chimpanzees exhibited the highest baseline levels among the species studied. There is a high prevalence of inadequate vitamin D status among European zoo-housed great apes. Husbandry interventions, including maximising UVB exposure, providing unrestricted outdoor access, and ensuring targeted dietary supplementation, are important to mitigating deficiency risks and safeguarding long-term cardiovascular and systemic health. This is the first study which describes vitamin D status in all commonly kept non-human great ape species in human care across a broad geographical range.

title: Seasonal variation in blood pressure reactivity to stress tests in young adults
authorString: Pun DB, Jha JP, Thapa B.
abstractText: Background Blood pressure (BP) reactivity is the BP rise to a given stimulus from baseline values, and is a strong predictor of hypertension and subsequent cardiovascular events. Blood pressure exhibits seasonal variations. However, the effect of seasonal variations on BP reactivity to stress is not well understood. This study aimed to explore the effect of seasonal variation on BP reactivity due to the cold pressor test (CPT) and handgrip test (HGT) among healthy young adults in Nepal. Methods A prospective pretest–posttest study was conducted among 45 healthy students (55.6% female) with a mean age of 21.62 ± 2.93 years. Blood pressure at baseline, during and after CPT and HGT interventions were measured as per protocol, during winter (December 2023) and summer (July 2024), and the BP reactivity was compared between two seasons using analytical statistics. The significance level was set at 5%. Results Baseline mean BP were lower in summer than in winter season (SBP: 107.71 ± 12.17 vs 120.78 ± 11.31, p = 0.001; DBP: 71.49 ± 8.74 vs 77.60 ± 8.83, p = 0.001; paired t-test). During CPT, there was a significantly higher rise of BP in summer compared to the rise in winter (SBP: 25.27 ± 11.56 vs 13.84 ± 11.17, p < 0.001; DBP: 25.53 ± 10.14 vs 13.51 ± 7.15, p < 0.001; paired t-test). Similarly, HGT also raised BP higher in summer than winter (SBP: 35.07 ± 17.11 vs 25.47 ± 14.81, p = 0.008; DBP: 30.96 ± 12.12 vs 24.16 ± 11.64, p = 0.009; paired t-test); and this was confirmed in linear regression analysis (p < 0.01). Independent effect of season on BP reactivity was confirmed by multiple linear regression analysis (p < 0.05). Conclusion Baseline BP is lower in summer compared to winter; but the BP reactivity to CPT and HGT is heightened in summer compared to winter, indicating seasonal modulation of cardiovascular stress responses, which may have implications for cardiovascular risk and adaptability to environmental changes.

title: Five-Year Real-World Outcomes of iStent inject W® Combined with Phacoemulsification in Ocular Hypertension and Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma
authorString: Vallejo MP, Cervantes ÁV, Llamas SD, Solana PM, Franch ERdlR.
abstractText:
Purpose: To evaluate the long-term real-world efficacy, safety, and functional and structural outcomes in patients with ocular hypertension (OHT) or primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) undergoing trabecular micro-bypass surgery with the iStent inject W®.

Methods:

This retrospective longitudinal study included 149 eyes of 149 patients with OHT or POAG who underwent implantation of the iStent inject W®, combined with phacoemulsification, and were followed for up to five years. Outcomes included intraocular pressure (IOP), number of hypotensive medications, best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), optical coherence tomography (OCT) structural parameters, and visual field indices. Follow-up data were available at 1 year (n = 123), 2 years (n = 94), 3 years (n = 61), 4 years (n = 35), and 5 years (n = 15).

Results:

BCVA improved significantly after surgery (p < 0.01). A mild but statistically significant decline in visual field index (VFI) was observed over time (p = 0.03), consistent with expected long-term glaucoma progression. OCT structural parameters remained stable throughout follow-up. IOP was significantly reduced at all postoperative visits except at years 3 and 5, where reductions did not reach statistical significance despite a sustained downward trend. Medication burden was significantly reduced at all time points (p < 0.01). Men exhibited lower postoperative IOP than women (p = 0.02), and OHT patients had higher IOP levels than those with POAG (p < 0.01).

Conclusions:

In a real-world clinical setting, the iStent inject W® provided sustained IOP reduction, durable medication burden reduction and long-term structural stability over five years. These findings support its long-term clinical effectiveness in the management of OHT and POAG.

title: Association between psychosocial distress and a history of cardiovascular events among adults with hypertension in the SAVA Region, Madagascar : a multicenter cross-sectional study
authorString: RAZAFIMAHENINA JM, EDWIN HCC, RAZANAMIHAJA N.
abstractText: Background In the SAVA Region, data on the association between psychosocial factors and cardiovascular events among adults with hypertension remain limited, despite a potentially unfavorable health and socioeconomic context. This study aimed to identify psychosocial factors associated with a history of cardiovascular events and to determine whether these associations persisted independently of major traditional cardiovascular risk factors. Methods This secondary analysis used data from a multicenter cross-sectional study conducted between December 2024 and February 2025 among adults with hypertension recruited from four referral hospitals in the SAVA Region, Madagascar. Socioeconomic characteristics and history of cardiovascular events were collected using the World Health Organization STEPwise questionnaire. Psychosocial factors were assessed using validated instruments, including the 10-item Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10), the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), the 6-item Lubben Social Network Scale (LSNS-6), the 6-item De Jong Gierveld Loneliness Scale, and the 6-item Social Support Questionnaire (SSQ6). Bivariate analyses and multivariable logistic regression were performed using SPSS version 25.0. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results A total of 394 adults with hypertension were included. The mean age was 53.03 ± 14.3 years, and 57.6% were women. Overall, 31.47% reported a history of cardiovascular events. In bivariate analyses, perceived stress, anxiety, depression, anxiety-depressive disorders, social isolation, and social support were significantly associated with a history of cardiovascular events. After adjustment for potential confounders, perceived stress, anxiety, and anxiety-depressive disorders remained significantly associated with a history of cardiovascular events. Conclusions Perceived stress, anxiety, and anxiety-depressive disorders remained associated with a history of cardiovascular events after adjustment for major cardiovascular risk factors. These findings support the potential value of incorporating psychosocial assessment into the comprehensive care of adults with hypertension.

title: Acute Kidney Injury Following Gadolinium-Based Contrast Administration: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study
authorString: Kuki B, Toçoğlu A, Pınar M, Ercan Z, Genç AC, İslam M, Dheir H.
abstractText:
Background:

/Objectives: Gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCA) are widely used in magnetic resonance imaging and are generally considered to have a lower potential for nephrotoxicity compared to iodinated contrast agents. However, the actual prevalence of acute kidney injury (AKI) following the use of GBCA and the risk factors contributing to it remain a subject of debate today. The aim of this study is to determine the incidence of acute kidney injury following gadolinium administration (AKI-FGA) in patients undergoing contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and to evaluate the independent risk factors contributing to it.

Methods:

The medical records of all patients who underwent contrast-enhanced MRI at our hospital between January 2021 and December 2022 were retrospectively reviewed. The patients’ demographic characteristics and serum creatinine levels before and after the contrast-enhanced MRI examination were evaluated. Contrast-induced acute kidney injury (AKI) was defined according to the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria as an increase in serum creatinine of ≥0.3 mg/dL within 48 hours following contrast agent administration or a rise to ≥1.5 times the baseline value within 7 days. Patients who met the KDIGO criteria were included in the AKI-FGA group.

Results:

A total of 503 patients who met the inclusion criteria were enrolled in the study. The mean age of the patients was 60.88 ± 16.83 years, and 60.4% of the patients (n=304) were male. Following GBCA administration, a statistically significant increase in serum urea and creatinine levels and a significant decrease in eGFR were observed (p=0.001). AKI-FGA was detected in 16.5% of the patients (n=83). In the AKI-FGA group, the number of patients with a history of coronary artery disease (CAD), diabetes mellitus (DM), hypertension (HT), and congestive heart failure (CHF) was statistically significantly higher than in the group without AKI-FGA (p<0.05). In the multivariate analysis, each 1-year increase in age increased the risk of AKI-FGA by a factor of 1.03, each 0.1 mg/dL increase in baseline serum creatinine increased it by a factor of approximately 4.96, and the presence of DM and CHF increased it by factors of 2.16 and 2.92, respectively. In contrast, no statistically significant association was found between the development of AKI-FGA and HT or CAD.

Conclusions:

Our findings demonstrate that acute kidney injury can develop following contrast-enhanced MRI even in patients without a history of kidney disease. In particular, for patients who are elderly or have DM, CHF, or elevated baseline serum creatinine levels, it is clinically important to perform an individualized risk assessment prior to contrast-enhanced MRI and to closely monitor kidney function following the procedure.

title: A public-data reproducibility benchmark of a 2.5-D U-Net with a slice-level topology term for type-B aortic dissection segmentation
authorString: You L, Guo Y, Zhong X, Peng Z, Wang W, Shen L, Ge J.
abstractText:
Background

Type-B aortic dissection requires separation of the true and false lumina in heterogeneous, anisotropic CTA. A topology term may reduce fragmentation, but its reproducibility must be tested under a fixed case split and independent native-grid evaluation.

Methods

We used the public Graz type-B aortic dissection CTA collection (40 cases; CC BY 4.0) and froze a 28/6/6 case split for training, development, and held-out testing. A compact 2.5-D U-Net trained with cross-entropy plus multiclass Dice was compared with the identical model augmented by a fixed-weight (0.5) differentiable slice-level soft clDice term. Two training seeds were run for each arm. All 40 cases passed the NRRD audit; predictions for six held-out cases were restored to their native grids and scored with case-level 3-D voxel-grid Dice, voxel-grid morphological clDice, 6-connected component counts, physical-volume error, and 2,000-resample case-level paired bootstrap intervals.

Results

With seed 20261007, topology-minus-baseline differences were −0.028 (95% CI −0.053 to −0.004) for true-lumen Dice, +0.032 (−0.006 to +0.096) for true-lumen voxel-grid clDice, +0.071 (+0.037 to +0.103) for false-lumen Dice, and +0.073 (+0.048 to +0.103) for false-lumen voxel-grid clDice. With seed 20261008, the corresponding differences were −0.040 (−0.065 to −0.018), +0.013 (−0.034 to +0.071), −0.099 (−0.187 to −0.004), and −0.058 (−0.124 to −0.001). Descriptive pooled means over 12 case rows per arm were true-lumen Dice 0.577 for topology versus 0.611 for baseline and false-lumen Dice 0.409 versus 0.422; these pooled rows are not independent cases.

Conclusions

Under this fixed six-case test split, the corrected slice-level topology term did not produce a consistent benefit. True-lumen Dice was lower in both seeds, while false-lumen effects reversed direction between seeds; topology-clDice changes were small and/or interval-crossing. The benchmark supports an auditable failure-analysis workflow but does not support a general topology benefit, clinical use, external generalization, or a panvascular decision system. The 3-D clDice quantity is an evaluation descriptor on the voxel grid; the training term is slice-level and does not enforce physical 3-D connectivity.

Current executed scope and claim boundary

This executed benchmark is restricted to the 40-case Graz type-B aortic dissection CTA collection with expert true- and false-lumen annotations. All 40 cases passed the audit; the frozen case split contains 28 training, 6 development, and 6 held-out test cases. Four runs (baseline/topology arms with seeds 20261007 and 20261008) produced native-grid predictions for all six held-out cases. The current estimand is descriptive case-level segmentation performance within this single public source. AVT, AortaSeg-60, ImageTBAD, and the ancillary multi-structure CCTA collection are documented as possible future external resources, but they are not part of the current endpoint, training set, or performance claim. This is a proof-of-concept segmentation benchmark, not a panvascular clinical system. The present study does not estimate multicentre generalisation, perform a TEVAR landing-zone assessment, evaluate device fit, or use follow-up outcomes. Any virtual-TEVAR geometry extension remains separately gated future work.

title: Fetal Ventricular Longitudinal Strain Does Not Predict Neonatal Hypoxemia in D-Transposition of the Great Arteries: A Prospective Multi-Center Study by the Fetal Heart Society Research Collaborative
authorString: Shuplock J, Johnson JT, Schidlow D, Donofrio MT, McBrien A, Hornberger LK, Palmer C, Reeder R, Cuneo BF, Dean PN, Howley L, Ikemba C, Lee CK, Michelfelder E, Moon-Grady AJ, Patel SR, Peyvandi S, Punn R, Savla JJ, Shah A, Sheth SS, Soslow JH, Sun H, Svenson A, Kavanaugh-McHugh A.
abstractText: Introduction : Neonates with transposition of the great arteries (TGA) and intact ventricular septum (IVS) can develop life-threatening hypoxemia after birth. There are no known reliable fetal echocardiographic markers of postnatal hypoxemia. Using a large, multi-center prospectively recruited cohort, we analyzed fetal ventricular strain and its association with postnatal hypoxemia. Material and Methods: Eighteen centers enrolled maternal-fetal dyads. Fetal ventricular longitudinal strain and strain rate measurements were obtained. The primary outcome measure was preoperative neonatal hypoxemia. The secondary outcome measure was reported need for balloon atrial septostomy (BAS). Intra- and inter-rater reliability was assessed. Fetal longitudinal strain was compared to normative data from a previously published study evaluating strain in fetuses without congenital heart disease. Results : Longitudinal strain was performed on 79 fetuses with TGA/IVS. Of those, 29 (37%) developed postnatal hypoxemia. A BAS was performed in 45 (57%). There was no statistically significant difference in fetal longitudinal strain between those with postnatal hypoxemia and those without. Similarly, fetal longitudinal strain did not differ among those who received a BAS and those who did not. Among fetuses with TGA/IVS, while right and left ventricular longitudinal strain was similar, right ventricular free wall strain was significantly higher than left ventricular longitudinal strain. Compared to the previously published normative data, longitudinal strain for both ventricles were significantly higher in fetuses with TGA/IVS. Conclusion : This prospective multi-center study identified no association between fetal longitudinal strain and postnatal hypoxemia or need for BAS in neonates with TGA/IVS, highlighting the importance of delivery planning for all fetuses with TGA to include preparations for BAS.

title: Fracture risk associated with sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors in adults with type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, or heart failure: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
authorString: Zhang R, Li W.
abstractText: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2i) have transformed the management of type 2 diabetes (T2DM), chronic kidney disease (CKD), and heart failure (HF), but fracture risk concerns persist following the CANVAS trial signal. We conducted an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating fracture risk associated with SGLT-2i across T2DM, CKD, and HF populations. We systematically searched PubMed/MEDLINE (inception to September 2026), supplemented by ClinicalTrials.gov and reference lists. Nine RCT cohorts from eight trials were included, comprising 62,583 participants and 2,606 fracture events. SGLT-2i were not associated with increased fracture risk (pooled RR 1.087, 95% CI 0.973–1.214; P = 0.141; I2 = 41.7%). Only CANVAS showed significantly increased fracture risk (RR 1.548, 95% CI 1.241–1.931); its exclusion eliminated the signal and heterogeneity (RR 1.033, I2 = 0%). Meta-regression confirmed that heterogeneity was not explained by age, follow-up duration, or baseline HbA1c. No fracture imbalance was observed in CKD or HF trials. Egger's test showed no publication bias (P = 0.166), and GRADE certainty was moderate. SGLT-2i as a class are not associated with increased fracture risk. The CANVAS signal is likely trial-specific rather than a class effect. These findings support the removal of fracture-related warnings and reassure that SGLT-2i cardiovascular and renal benefits are not offset by increased fracture risk.

title: Blood pressure improvement and long-term outcomes after carotid stenting in patients with hypertension and atherosclerotic carotid stenosis
authorString: zhang h, chang h, jiang f, jia y, wang j, cheng z, lin y, jia z, wang j, guo y, cong l, han j, yang l.
