abstractText: Background: This study aimedto investigate the relationship between long-term blood pressure improvement following carotid stenting (CAS) and clinical outcomes. Methods: In thisstudy,178 patients with hypertensive and carotid stenosis who underwent CAS were retrospectively analyzedand divided into a blood pressure improvementgroup (BP-I, n=59) and a blood pressure nonimprovement group (BP-NI, n=77) on the basis of whether their blood pressure improved at 24 months;the other 42 nonhypertensive patients were considered blank controls (BCs). The primary outcome was the major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular event(MACCE)-free survival rate at 24months. Survival analysis was performed using the Kaplan‒Meiermethod, and Cox proportional hazards models were employed to identify potential predictors of MACCEs. Results: Blood pressure improvement wasachieved by 43.4% of the patients. The MACCE-free survival rate was significantly greater in the BP-I group than in the BP-NI group (P=0.048) at 24 months, and no difference was detected between the BP-I and BC groups; the MACCE-free survival rate was higher in the BC group, but the difference was not significant. Perioperative hemodynamics were less stable in the BP-I group, as these patients required significantly more dopamine support (p<0.01) and experiencedlonger durations of hypotension (p=0.01) than the patients in the BP-NI group did. Multivariate Cox regression revealed that a preoperative systolic blood pressure ≥140 mmHg was the strongest independent risk factor for MACCEs (HR=6.26; p<0.001), while moderate-to-high echogenicity plaques (HR=0.29; p=0.019) and a stent diameter >8 mm (HR=0.13; p=0.002) were significant protective factors. Conclusion: Long-term blood pressure improvement following CAS is a potential indicator of better long-term outcomes. Clinical trial number： not applicable

title: Patient comfort of Pulsed Field Ablation Using a Circular Catheter for Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation Under Conscious Sedation: A comparison with radiofrequency ablation
authorString: Zhang B, Wei H, ding p, chen w, shen j, hu x, li f, ge l, zhang q, wang z, li c, zhang c.
abstractText: Objective To compare the patient comfort of Pulsed Field Ablation (PFA) and Radiofrequency Catheter Ablation (RFCA) in patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (PAF) under conscious sedation. Methods 62 patients with PAF were randomly assigned to either the PFA group (n = 31) or the RFCA group (n = 31). All procedures were done with conscious sedation using dexmedetomidine and fentanyl together. Patient comfort was assessed using an intraoperative pain score. Additionally, the acute procedural success rate, procedural efficiency, and safety events were recorded. Results Acute procedural success was achieved in all patients with no major complications in either cohort. Compared to the RFCA group, patients undergoing PFA reported significantly less intraoperative pain (mean VAS score: 5.81 ± 1.72 vs. 6.87 ± 1.75, P = 0.0148) and required markedly shorter operation times (median: 94.0 vs. 120.0 min, P < 0.001). Conclusion Under conscious sedation, PFA reduces intraoperative pain and shortens procedure time compared with RFCA, while maintaining similar efficacy and safety. Trial registration: This study was registered with the China Clinical Trial Registry on August 27,2024, under registration number: ChiCTR2400088774.

title: Mitochondrial respiratory complexes, excitation-contraction coupling and mTOR signaling transcriptional programs are dysregulated in cardiometabolic HFpEF
authorString: Méndez-Fernández A, Barraza-Arellano AL, Treviño V, García-Rivas G.
abstractText: Heart failure is a leading cause of death and disability worldwide. Nearly, half of the cases correspond to HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), which is predicted to become the most prevalent form of HF in the forthcoming years. In this study, we performed a bulk RNA-seq assay to study the transcriptomic profiles of the hearts of HFpEF mice. HFpEF animals consisted in C57BL/6 mic that were fed a high-fat diet and exposed to L-NAME in the drinking water during five or eight weeks. Controls received a standard chow diet. Differential expression analysis yielded 1535 differentially expressed genes in HFpEF hearts relative to controls. 71 out of 78 DEGs contained in the GO-CC "Mitochondrial Inner Membrane (GO:0005743)" were found to be down-regulated, mostly affecting respiratory complexes I, III, IV and V in a time-dependent manner. Overrepresentation analyses also suggested that the mTOR signaling cascade is switched on, while "Diabetic Cardiomyopathy", "Cardiac Muscle Contraction" and "Cytoskeleton in Muscle Cells" KEGG pathways were detected to be affected, probably pointing at excitation-contraction coupling impairment. In summary, the transcriptomic program of the HFpEF hearts consisted in a widespread downregulation of the expression of the subunits of mitochondrial respiratory complexes, upregulation of mTOR signaling and deregulation of the genes related to the excitation-contraction coupling.

title: Wearable Single-Lead ECG Detects Fine-Grained Structural Heart Disease Through Echo-Report Supervision
authorString: Hong S, He C, Zhao Q, Huang S, Li J, Tang G, Zhang H, Liu T, Xue Z, Liu J, Chen K, Ding C.
abstractText: Structural heart disease (SHD) is a primary driver of heart failure and cardiovascular mortality, yet early detection remains constrained by the limited accessibility of echocardiography. While single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) is ubiquitous through wearables, existing AI screening models often depend on 12-lead inputs, generalize poorly across institutions, or require massive, condition-specific labeled datasets. Recent work has demonstrated the feasibility of contrastive pre-training between single-lead ECGs and echocardiography reports within a single health system. Here, we present AnyECG-Echo, a framework that advance this paradigm toward clinical translation through three key developments: (1) evaluation in a geographically independent external cohort (n = 16,621); (2) diagnostic coverage of 13 fine-grained SHD subtypes spanning myocardial, chamber, valvular, and great-vessel pathologies; and (3) dual-axis mechanistic interpretability combining electrophysiology-grounded Shapley attribution with emergent correlations to quantitative measurements. Across validation cohorts totaling n = 25,222, the model demonstrated high AUROC for high-impact subtypes, including reduced left ventricular systolic functon(AUROC 0.866–0.924), global heart enlargement (0.877–0.931), and mitral stenosis (0.836–0.906). Furthermore, we successfully validated the alignment of model outputs with established medical physiological traits, thereby enhancing interpretability. Notably, we discovered that AnyECG-Echo’s outputs function as physiologically grounded digital biomarkers that accurately track objective metrics such as LVEF and myocardial wall thickness. These findings prove that wearable single-lead ECGs can effectively detect fine-grained structural heart disease, offering a practical solution for population-scale screening.

title: Assessment of Atrioventricular and Ventriculoarterial Coupling Indices in Patients with Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome Utilizing Cardiac MRI and Invasive Hemodynamics
authorString: Reid AJ, MacBeth ML, Romanowicz J, Frank B, Alba CG.
abstractText: Background Atrioventricular (AV) and ventriculoarterial (VA) coupling indices have demonstrated prognostic value in various cardiac pathologies but have not been studied in hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS). This study assessed known and novel AV and VA coupling indices derived from cardiac MRI (CMR) and invasive hemodynamics for predicting adverse outcomes in HLHS patients with stage II palliation prior to Fontan completion. Methods CMR and catheterization data from 45 HLHS patients with stage II palliation undergoing pre-Fontan evaluation (January 2015–October 2025) were retrospectively analyzed. Known AV coupling indices and two novel indices—RA SV -RV coupling index (RA stroke volume indexed/RV end-diastolic volume indexed) and combined RA-RV-Aorta coupling index—were compared between patients with and without adverse outcomes (composite of death, transplantation, heart failure hospitalization, SGLT2 inhibitor initiation, plastic bronchitis, protein-losing enteropathy). Predictive performance was assessed using Firth logistic regression and ROC analysis. Results Ten patients (22%) experienced adverse outcomes. Known AV coupling indices did not significantly differ between groups (AUC 0.48–0.69). The RV-Aortic coupling index was significantly lower in the adverse outcomes group (0.17 vs. 0.23, p = 0.006; AUC = 0.80). Both novel indices demonstrated superior discrimination: RA SV -RV (0.11 vs. 0.17, p = 0.002; AUC = 0.82) and novel RAsv-RV-Aorta (2.13 vs. 3.90, p = 0.001; AUC = 0.86). Nested models showed that adding each novel index to RV-Aortic coupling significantly improved model fit (p = 0.036 and p = 0.048, respectively). Conclusions Novel coupling indices designed for single ventricle physiology outperformed known AV coupling indices and provided incremental predictive value beyond RV-Aortic coupling alone for adverse outcomes in HLHS patients with stage II palliation.

title: Mesenteric Adhesion and Poorer Perioperative Outcomes in Gastric Submucosal Tumors: A Retrospective Study of Endoscopic Full-Thickness Resection
authorString: Zeng Q, Sui Z, Chen Y, Feng L, Zhou M, Chen X, Zhang S.
abstractText: Background Endoscopic full-thickness resection(EFTR) has become an increasingly common method for treating gastric submucosal tumors (SMTs). Adhesion between the SMT and the adjacent mesentery represents an intraoperative challenge that can affect the perioperative clinical outcomes for patients. Objective The aim of this study was to analyze the risk factors for SMT–mesentery adhesion and the effect of SMT–mesentery adhesion on perioperative clinical outcomes. Methods We retrospectively reviewed the information of patients with gastric SMTs who underwent EFTR in our center from January 2022 to August 2026. Patients were divided into adhesion and non-adhesion groups. Perioperative clinical outcomes were compared between the two groups, and risk factors for SMT–mesentery adhesion were analyzed. Results A total of 202 patients were enrolled, and mesenteric adhesion was observed in 64 patients (31.7%). The adhesion group had significantly longer operative time (P < 0.001), greater elevation in white blood cell count (P < 0.001), and higher total hospitalization costs (P < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression analysis revealed that tumors located on the posterior gastric wall (OR = 4.110, 95% CI: 1.855–9.105, P < 0.001), maximum diameter > 30 mm (OR = 7.449, 95% CI: 2.499–22.403, P < 0.001), and extraluminal growth pattern (OR = 15.571, 95% CI: 5.803–41.781, P < 0.001) were independent risk factors for tumor–mesentery adhesion, whereas hypertension (OR = 0.396, 95% CI: 0.178–0.880, P = 0.023) was a protective factor. Conclusion Mesenteric adhesion is a significant predictor of worse perioperative outcomes following EFTR for gastric SMTs, underscoring the importance of thorough preoperative assessment. Accordingly, EFTR should be approached with caution in patients with imaging evidence of mesenteric adhesion.

title: Impact of Cardiorenal syndrome Type 1 on Mortality and Health-related Quality of Life among Patients Admitted for Acute Heart Failure in a Nigeria Tertiary Hospital: A Prospective Cohort Analysis
authorString: Oyekunle RA, Ayoola YA, Abdul-Raheem MN, Adamu A, Ayanbisi IO, Ezeugonwa RS, Fadare JO, Akintunde AA, Okolie HI.
abstractText: Background The presence of acute kidney injury in patients admitted with acute heart failure (AHF) known as cardiorenal syndrome type 1(CRS1) is a serious clinical condition that is associated with prolonged hospitalization and poor prognosis. However, few studies have been done in this area in sub-Saharan Africa especially in Nigeria. The aim of this study was to determine the impact of cardiorenal syndrome type 1 (CRS 1) on duration of hospitalization, admission outcome, rehospitalization, mortality and health-related quality of life at day 30 among patients admitted for acute heart failure at Federal Teaching Hospital, Gombe. Method This was a prospective longitudinal cohort study where 149 patients admitted for acute heart failure at Federal Teaching hospital, Gombe were recruited after ethical approval for a duration of 10 months. Acute heart failure was diagnosed according to European Society of Cardiology guidelines. Serum urea and creatinine were measured at presentation and repeated at day 2 and day 7 or at discharge. Acute kidney injury was diagnosed according to KDIGO clinical practice guideline, 2012. Duration of hospital stay, admission outcome, rehospitalization, mortality and impact on health- related quality of life at day 30 were assessed and analysed for all the patients using computer-based Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS) version 27.0. Results Out of 149 AHF patients recruited, 71 (47.7%) developed AKI either at presentation, day 2 or day 7. Patients with CRS1 have longer hospital stay (10.52 ± 5.23 vs 6.21 ± 2.67 days), increased in-hospital and day 30 hospital mortality ({15.5 vs 1.3%} and {29.6 vs 6.4%} respectively). Cardiorenal syndrome type 1 was also associated with poor health-related quality of life at day 30. Conclusion Cardiorenal syndrome type 1 accounts for 47.7% of AHF patients in this study. CRS1 contributes to longer hospital stay and it is a predictor of higher in-hospital and day 30 mortality, poor clinical outcome and overall health-related quality of life at day 30. This study provided an understanding of the magnitude of morbidity, mortality and poor health-related quality of life associated with CRS1.

title: Outcome of transcarotid versus transthoracic access for transcatheter aortic valve replacement
authorString: Nakai C, Liu J, Gowda A, Tarabichi S, Khan S, Singh K, Drzymalski K, DeLago A.
abstractText: Backgrounds: Short-term outcome of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) through transcarotid access (TC) and transthoracic access (TT) such as transapical or transaortic has been reported as alternative access options in patients who were not feasible with transfemoral access. However, mid to long-term outcomes have been poorly documented. The purpose of this study was to evaluate postoperative outcomes comparing TC with TT groups. Methods Between January 2016 and January 2024, 93 patients underwent TAVR through TC access while 62 through TT access. To adjust baseline differences, 1:1 propensity score matching was performed using the nearest neighbor method between the TC and TT groups. Results 38 pairs were matched in propensity score matching. A significant higher incidence of postoperative new atrial fibrillation was detected in the TT compared with TC groups (10.5% vs 0%, p = 0.04). 30-day mortality rate, postoperative stroke, permanent pacemaker placement, and surgical reintervention for access site did not differ between the two groups. Length of hospital stay was shorter in the TC group (4.9 ± 5.5days vs 7.7 ± 4.8days, p = 0.02). Mean follow-up term was 2.3 ± 2.1years. Cumulative survival rate in 5 years was 70.1% in the TC group and 54.3% in the TT group. There was no significant difference in mid-term outcome between the 2 groups (p = 0.47). Conclusions Transcatheter aortic valve replacement through transcarotid access was associated with lower rate of new postoperative atrial fibrillation and shorter hospital stay compared with transthoracic access. However, short and mid-term survival rates were comparable in this patient cohort.

title: Targeted Dried Blood Spot Acylcarnitine and Amino Acid Profiling Reveals a Candidate Metabolic Signature in Pediatric Heart Failure: A Cross-Sectional Case–Control Study
authorString: Abdolahpour S, Sarikhani M, Sayarifard F, Gholami M, Gorji M, Abbasi F, Rostami P, shabanian R, Mohsenipour R.
abstractText: Pediatric heart failure (HF) causes substantial morbidity and mortality, yet the metabolic derangements underlying myocardial energy failure in children remain incompletely characterized. We performed targeted dried blood spot (DBS) acylcarnitine and amino acid profiling in 30 children with HF of mixed etiology and 30 age- and sex-frequency-matched healthy controls, quantifying 44 metabolites by flow-injection tandem mass spectrometry. Seven metabolites were significantly decreased in HF patients (p < 0.05, FDR < 0.05): hexanoylcarnitine/adipoylcarnitine (C6DC), tyrosine, octenoylcarnitine (C8:1), glutamate, decadienoylcarnitine (C10:2), proline, and dodecanoylcarnitine (C12), with decreases of 23.9–48.8%. Hydroxyoctadecanoic acid (C18OH) showed the largest overall decrease (57.7%) but did not reach FDR significance. Multivariate modeling using the full metabolite panel achieved excellent, permutation-validated discrimination between groups (PLS-DA accuracy 98%, Q²=0.82; OPLS-DA R²Y = 0.835, Q²=0.708); six metabolites (C6DC, tyrosine, C8:1, glutamate, C10:2, and proline) emerged as the top contributors to this discrimination and are proposed as an exploratory minimal candidate panel, warranting dedicated validation of its own discriminatory performance in larger, independent cohorts. Pathway enrichment highlighted catecholamine biosynthesis, thyroid hormone synthesis, and aromatic amino acid metabolism, without enrichment of fatty-acid β-oxidation or carnitine-synthesis pathways. These findings indicate that pediatric HF involves a coordinated decrease in medium-chain/dicarboxylic acylcarnitines and selected amino acids alongside enrichment of catecholaminergic and aromatic amino-acid pathways, consistent with a myocardial shift away from fatty-acid oxidation. A small, low-cost DBS-based panel may hold promise as a non-invasive adjunct for pediatric HF assessment, pending external validation.

title: A Retrospective Cohort Study of Independent Predictors for Long-Term Prognosis in Patients with Chronic Total Occlusion: Focus on SYNTAX Score and Platelet-Related Indices
authorString: Zhang W, Hu S, Guo T.
abstractText: Objective: The long-term prognosis of patients with chronic total occlusion (CTO) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is influenced by multiple factors. This study aimed to identify independent predictors of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) at one year, with a specific focus on anatomical complexity assessed by the SYNTAX score and platelet activity indices. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 310 patients who underwent PCI for at least one CTO between January 2019 and June 2021. Patients were followed for one year for the occurrence of MACE (a composite of cardiac death, target vessel revascularization, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and hospitalization for heart failure). Baseline clinical, angiographic (including SYNTAX score), and laboratory data (including mean platelet volume [MPV], platelet count, and MPV/platelet ratio) were collected. Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed to identify predictors. Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank test was used for survival comparisons. Predictive performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Results: During follow-up, 64 patients (20.6%) experienced MACE. In univariate analysis, high MPV group (HR 2.13, 95% CI 1.27–3.60, p=0.004), lower HDL-cholesterol (HR 0.21, 95% CI 0.06–0.71, p=0.012), lower platelet count, higher serum creatinine, and higher MPV/platelet ratio were significant predictors. A risk score incorporating these factors effectively stratified patients (Log-rank p=0.044). In multivariable models, lower HDL-cholesterol remained an independent protective factor (HR 0.17, 95% CI 0.05–0.58, p=0.005). SYNTAX score was a significant predictor in optimized models (HR 1.04, 95% CI 1.01–1.07, p=0.020). Patients with both high SYNTAX score and high MPV had the worst MACE-free survival (Log-rank p=0.046). The full predictive model (including age, SYNTAX score, MPV, platelet count, HDL-C, creatinine) showed the best discriminative ability (AUC=0.659). Subgroup analysis indicated the predictive value of SYNTAX score and high MPV was most pronounced in patients aged <65 years. Conclusion: Lower HDL-cholesterol, higher SYNTAX score, and a profile suggestive of higher platelet activity (high MPV group, lower platelet count) are important predictors of one-year MACE in CTO patients after PCI. A model combining clinical, anatomical, and platelet indices offers improved risk stratification, particularly for identifying high-risk younger patients.

title: Health-System and Sex Differences in Cardioprotective Diabetes Therapy Among Adults With Type 2 Diabetes and Established ASCVD: A Two-Center EHR Study
authorString: Pavuluri C, Rao A, Sholle E, MA X, Gullapelli R, Nasir K, Sadhu A, Avenatti E, Kashyap SR.
abstractText: Background Despite compelling evidence that sodium–glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) reduce cardiovascular risk, their implementation among patients most likely to benefit remains suboptimal. We evaluated prescribing patterns, institutional variation, sex disparities, and neighborhood-level socioeconomic disadvantage among adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 16,765 adults with T2DM and ASCVD receiving care at Weill Cornell Medicine (n = 8,669) or Houston Methodist (n = 8,096) between 2016 and 2023. ASCVD was characterized by subtype, including coronary artery disease (CAD), peripheral artery disease (PAD), and stroke/cerebrovascular disease. Prescription prevalence of SGLT2i and GLP-1RA therapy was compared across institutions, ASCVD subtypes, sex, and neighborhood socioeconomic disadvantage measured using the Area Deprivation Index (ADI). Pooled prevalence estimates and sex-specific odds ratios (ORs) were calculated using meta-analytic methods. Results Only 28.3% (95% CI 17.3–42.6) of eligible adults received an SGLT2i, with substantially higher use at Weill Cornell than at Houston Methodist (35.2% vs. 22.2%; P  < 0.001). GLP-1RA therapy was prescribed to 27.8% (95% CI 23.1–33.0), also with significant institutional variation (30.4% vs. 25.3%; P  < 0.001). Across both health systems, women had 29% lower odds of receiving an SGLT2i than men (OR 0.71, 95% CI 0.66–0.77; P  < 0.001), whereas overall GLP-1RA prescribing did not differ by sex. Analyses across CAD, PAD, and stroke and by ADI further evaluated whether treatment gaps varied according to ASCVD phenotype and neighborhood disadvantage. Conclusions Fewer than one in three adults with T2DM and established ASCVD received either class of guideline-recommended cardioprotective therapy. By examining distinct ASCVD subtypes and neighborhood-level deprivation across two health systems, this study demonstrates that treatment gaps extend beyond overall medication use and must be understood within patients’ clinical and socioeconomic contexts. Marked institutional variation and persistent sex disparities in SGLT2i prescribing identify an urgent need for health system–level strategies to standardize care, improve equitable access, and translate cardiovascular outcome evidence into routine practice.

title: Associations between novel anthropometric variables and short-term outcomes after acute type A aortic dissection repair
authorString: Deng C, Zhan W, Tang H, Shen K, Li J, Li Z, Tian S, Tan L.
abstractText: Background: The impact of body mass index—defined obesity on outcomes after acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) repair remains controversial. This study aimed to determine the associations between novel anthropometric variables and short-term outcomes in ATAAD patients after aortic repair. Methods: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 794 ATAAD patients from January 2019 to November 2023. We performed univariate, multivariable, average marginal effect, interaction and mediation effect, and restricted cubic spline analyses to investigate the associations between anthropometric variables and short-term outcomes (including short-term mortality, ischemic stroke and acute kidney injury, (AKI), etc). Results: Relative fat mass (RFM) was independently associated with postoperative AKI in ATAAD, and each one-unit increase in RFM was associated with a 2.10% (95% CI: 0.0131-0.0288, P < 0.001) change in the probability of postoperative AKI for average patient. RFM and cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) duration had a synergistic effect on AKI (OR: 1.0004, 95%CI: 1.0000-1.0009, P=0.040). Neutrophil count partially mediated the RFM-AKI relationship (proportion mediated: 12.5%). Additionally, waist circumference (WC), RFM, waist-to-height ratio (WHtR), and body roundness index (BRI) exhibited nonlinear, U-shaped associations with short-term mortality in ATAAD, with lowest predicted probability at 907 mm for WC, 38.5 for RFM, 0.544 for WHtR, and 4.35 for BRI. Conclusions: RFM was independently associated with postoperative AKI in ATAAD patients, mediated partially by inflammatory/stress responses and synergized with prolonged CPB duration. Central obesity indicators (WC, RFM, WHtR, BRI) showed U-shaped associations with short-term mortality. RFM should be prioritized for perioperative risk assessment, especially during extended CPB procedures.

title: A Single-Cell Atlas of PVOD Across the Lifespan Reveals Cellular and Molecular Therapeutic Targets
authorString: Michki SN, Chandrasekaran P, Pogoriler J, Wright Q, Lu M, Peterson AR, Hallquist H, Cantu E, Morrisey EE, Young LR, Basil MC, Lin SM, Frank DB.
abstractText: Rationale Pulmonary veno-occlusive disease (PVOD) is a progressive and lethal disease cured only lung transplant. While genetic mutations in EIF2AK4 have been identified in some cases, 70% of PVOD patients have no known etiology. Objectives To construct a single-cell atlas to define the cellular and molecular constituents driving pathophysiology in PVOD. Methods Lung samples were collected from four idiopathic non-EIF2AK4 mutation pediatric and adult PVOD patients and age-matched controls. Analyses of single-cell RNA sequencing, Xenium spatial transcriptomics, and immunohistochemistry were performed to identify cell state changes and differential gene expression between controls and PVOD and subsequent transcriptome comparison between our PVOD and published pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) datasets. Measurement and Main Results The single-cell atlas reveals marked changes in the PVOD endothelium compared to controls. EndMT and ectopic COL15A1+ systemic venous shunts and pulmonary vein endothelium are hallmarks of PVOD. Molecular analyses reveal activation of the integrated stress response (ISR)/ATF4, TGFβ signaling, MAPK signaling, and BRD4 are potential key players in the pathophysiology of PVOD. While PVOD and PAH share both pathological and some molecular mechanisms, ISR and TGFβ signaling are more prominent in PVOD than PAH. Conclusions These data indicate that endothelial dysfunction is a primary etiology in the development of PVOD with activation of multiple pathways with druggable targets.

title: Cardiovascular Risk Stratification Among University Employees in India: Comparison of WHO/ISH, ASCVD and Framingham Risk Models
authorString: Jagtap AH, Ingole Patil AS, Kudale AM.
abstractText:
Background:

Cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk prediction is an important component of primary prevention, particularly in populations with increasing cardiometabolic risk. Several risk prediction models are available, but their estimates may differ because of differences in derivation populations, predictors, calibration, and cardiovascular outcomes. Evidence comparing these models within Indian occupational populations remains limited. This study compared 10–year CVD risk estimates generated by the World Health Organization/International Society of Hypertension (WHO/ISH) cardiovascular risk charts, the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) Pooled Cohort Equation (ASCVD–PCE), and the Framingham general cardiovascular disease risk equation among university employees in India. Methods A comparative observational study was conducted using standardized health assessment data from 266 university employees. Participants aged 40–74 years were selected to provide a common analytical age range across the three risk prediction approaches. Of 127 employees within this age range, three with documented previous ischemic heart disease were excluded because the analysis focused on primary prevention. The final analytical cohort comprised 124 participants. Blood pressure was assessed using a standardized protocol involving three readings at five–minute intervals, with repeat assessments during three subsequent weekly visits for employees with elevated initial readings. Ten–year cardiovascular risk was estimated using the 2019 WHO/ISH laboratory–based risk charts for the South Asian region, the ASCVD–PCE, and the 2008 Framingham general CVD equation. Agreement between risk categories was assessed using Cohen's kappa and linear weighted kappa. Agreement was also examined at ≥10% and ≥20% thresholds. Results The mean age of the 124 participants was 47.63 ± 6.45 years, and 86.3% were male. Diabetes was present in 25.8%, smoking/tobacco use in 19.4%, and 29.0% were receiving antihypertensive treatment. Mean estimated risk was 5.94% for WHO/ISH, 5.95% for ASCVD–PCE, and 12.86% for Framingham. High risk (≥20%) was identified in 2.4%, 4.8%, and 20.2% of participants by WHO/ISH, ASCVD–PCE, and Framingham, respectively. Exact four–category agreement was 70.2% between WHO/ISH and ASCVD–PCE, compared with 31.5% between WHO/ISH and Framingham and 26.6% between ASCVD–PCE and Framingham. Cohen's kappa was 0.502 for WHO/ISH versus ASCVD–PCE, 0.079 for WHO/ISH versus Framingham, and 0.047 for ASCVD–PCE versus Framingham. Weighted kappa values were 0.639, 0.323, and 0.342, respectively. Conclusion WHO/ISH and ASCVD–PCE produced closely similar mean risk estimates and substantially greater categorical agreement than either model showed with the Framingham equation. Framingham generated considerably higher 10–year CVD risk estimates and classified a larger proportion of participants into higher–risk categories. These findings highlight the importance of model selection when cardiovascular risk assessment is undertaken in Indian occupational populations and support cautious interpretation of risk estimates derived from models developed in different populations and for different cardiovascular endpoints.

Keywords:

cardiovascular disease; risk prediction; WHO/ISH; ASCVD; Pooled Cohort Equation; Framingham; India; occupational health; university employees; risk classification

title: Leginsulin alleviates pathological cardiac hypertrophy potentially by regulating the oxidative stress-mediated MAPK signaling pathway
authorString: Yao C, Wu M, Shen T, Xiong Z, Qi X, Hady E, Liu M, Shang X.
abstractText: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy(PCH) is a critical driver of heart failure and is associated with oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and abnormal stress-responsive signaling. This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of leginsulin, a naturally occurring soybean-derived peptide, against PCH and to elucidate its underlying mechanisms.Isoproterenol-induced cardiac hypertrophy was established in mice, and angiotensin II (AngII)-stimulated H9c2 and AC16 cardiomyocytes were used as complementary in vitro models. Cardiac remodeling, fibrosis, oxidative stress, mitochondrial function, and mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling were evaluated following leginsulin treatment.Leginsulin markedly attenuated cardiac hypertrophy and fibrosis in mice, as indicated by reduced cardiac enlargement, cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, and collagen accumulation. In AngII-stimulated H9c2 and AC16 cardiomyocytes, leginsulin suppressed the expression of hypertrophic and fibrotic markers. Furthermore, Leginsulin reduced oxidative stress by decreasing reactive oxygen species and malondialdehyde levels while enhancing superoxide dismutase activity. In parallel, leginsulin preserved mitochondrial membrane potential, increased adenosine triphosphate production, and improved mitochondrial network integrity. Mechanistically, leginsulin selectively suppressed AngII -induced activation of c-Jun N-terminal kinase and extracellular signal-regulated kinase signaling whereasp38 signaling was not significantly affected.Leginsulin protects against PCH and fibrosis by maintaining redox balance, preserving mitochondrial function, and regulating stress-responsive signaling pathways. These findings reveal a physiological role of leginsulin in cardiac stress adaptation and highlight its potential as a natural regulator of PCH.

title: STOPP/START Criteria in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in Colombia: A Cross-Sectional Study
authorString: Valladales-Restrepo LF, Pulido-Beltrán J, Muñoz-Velez M, Tafur-Ramírez ME, García-Castaño N, Gaviria-Mendoza A, Machado-Duque E, Alba JEM.
abstractText: Purpose Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a high-burden disease that requires complex treatment. The aim was to determine the prevalence of potentially inappropriate medications and therapeutic omissions by applying the Screening Tool of Older Person's Prescriptions (STOPP)/Screening Tool to Alert to Right Treatment (START) criteria in patients with T2DM in Colombia. Methods A cross-sectional study of patients with a new diagnosis of T2DM who were treated between July-2023 and June-2024 was performed. The STOPP/START criteria were applied to identify potentially inappropriate medications and therapeutic omissions. Multivariate analyses were performed. Results A total of 434 patients were included; 54.1% were women, with a median age of 71.0 years (IQR:67.0–76.0). The most frequent comorbidities were hypertension (84.6%), dyslipidemia (68.7%) and obesity (35.0%). The most commonly used antidiabetic agent was metformin (84.6%). The most common comedications were lipid-lowering drugs (89.6%) and antihypertensives (85.4%). A total of 71.7% of patients met the STOPP/START criteria, with a prevalence of 51.8% for the STOPP criteria and 47.5% for the START criteria. The inappropriate use of acetylsalicylic acid in primary prevention (15.9%) and the omission of proton pump inhibitors among users of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (18.7%) were highlighted. Patients with rheumatologic comorbidities were more likely to present the STOPP (OR:4.07; 95%CI:2.41–6.89) or START (OR:2.77; 95%CI:1.72–4.44) criteria. Discussion The high prevalence of the STOPP/START criteria in this population indicates significant opportunities to improve the quality of prescribing in older adults with T2DM, particularly in patients with a greater burden of comorbidities and exposure to multiple medications.

title: Influence of the Angiotensin Receptor Neprilysin Inhibitor Compared with Perindopril on Left Atrial Strain and Prognosis in Heart Failure
authorString: Zhang Y, Zong Q, Tang Y, Zhu Y, Zhao S.
abstractText: Backgrounds Contemporary guidelines lack support for the therapies of left atrial (LA) dysfunction. The objective of this study is to compare the effects of angiotensin receptor–neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI) therapy and perindopril on left atrial (LA) strain assessed by three-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography (3D-STE) in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). Methods This single-centre retrospective observational study included patients with HFrEF who received either ARNI therapy or perindopril. The primary endpoint was the change in LA reservoir strain (LASr), LA conduit strain (LAScd), and LA booster strain (LASct) from baseline to 6 months. The secondary endpoint was the occurrence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). Results Among the 159 enrolled patients, 135 completed the 6-month follow-up (ARNI, n = 80; perindopril, n = 55). Baseline characteristics were comparable between the two groups. After adjustment for potential confounders, ARNI therapy was associated with significantly greater improvement in LASr than perindopril (adjusted mean difference, 4.31%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 3.02–5.60; P < 0.05). Similar benefits were observed for LAScd and LASct (both P < 0.05). MACEs occurred in 6 patients (6.1%) in the ARNI group and 17 patients (28.3%) in the perindopril group (log-rank P < 0.05). Conclusions In patients with HFrEF, ARNI therapy was associated with greater improvement in LA strain and a lower incidence of MACEs than perindopril over 6 months.

title: Prevalence and Predictors of Unplanned Readmission After Outpatient Breast Cancer Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study of 191,559 Patients
authorString: Knoedler SA, Wirtz JM, Kong V, Montagna G, Phuyal D, Fabi A, Kappos EA, Rahmayanti S, Moog P, Kükrek H, Jiang J, Elfgen C, Tausch C, Heidinger M, Perozzo FAG, Bishop SN, Djohan R.
abstractText: Outpatient breast surgery has become increasingly common, yet contemporary national data on unplanned readmission after same-day discharge remain limited. Using the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (2011–2023), we performed a retrospective cohort study of adult women undergoing elective outpatient breast cancer surgery, with 30-day unplanned readmission as the primary outcome. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors, a nomogram was developed for individualized risk estimation, and machine learning models (LASSO, XGBoost, random forest) were applied for validation. Among 191,559 patients, the overall readmission rate was 1.82%, rising from partial (1.36%) to total (2.83%) and radical mastectomy (3.34%). Despite a roughly seven-fold increase in outpatient volume, readmission declined from 2.8% in 2011 to 1.6% in recent years. The strongest independent predictors were functional dependence, congestive heart failure, dialysis, operative time exceeding 120 minutes, bleeding disorders, and ASA class ≥ 3. The nomogram identified high-risk patients with excellent calibration and discriminated comparably to machine learning models. Outpatient breast cancer surgery carries low overall readmission risk that varies substantially by procedure type and comorbidity, with functional dependence and cardiovascular disease outweighing cancer-specific factors. The proposed nomogram offers a practical tool for individualized risk stratification and surgical planning.

title: Diagnostic and Perioperative Complexity when Retroperitoneal Hemangioma Mimics Sympathetic Paraganglioma: A Case Report
authorString: Laichetty A, Shen P, Lin J.
abstractText: Background. Primary retroperitoneal tumors, which comprise 0.1–0.2% of all malignancies, can encompass various etiologies, and possess nonspecific imaging features. These factors make them a diagnosis of exclusion, especially in adult patients. Additionally, fewer than 50 cases of adult primary cavernous hemangiomas in the retroperitoneal space have been reported. However, when a hypervascular retroperitoneal mass is accompanied by hypertension and ambivalent serum catecholamine levels, a functional sympathetic paraganglioma becomes the leading diagnosis as it requires a differential work up, driving a high-stakes perioperative pathway. Case Presentation. A 52-year-old man with insulin dependent type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hyperlipidemia and schizoaffective disorder had a well vascularized retroperitoneal mass incidentally identified on trauma imaging following a motor vehicular accident (MVA). Cross-sectional imaging and mildly-to-moderately elevated urinary and plasma catecholamines/Metanephrines raised concern for a functional paraganglioma. He underwent preoperative alpha then beta-adrenergic blockade and laparoscopic resection. Final Histopathology demonstrated a cavernous hemangioma with no neuroendocrine tissue. Conclusions. The combination of chronic hypertension, anxiety, and equivocal biochemistry produced a convincing phenotype for functional paraganglioma. Since unprepared resection of a functional paraganglioma carries substantial perioperative cardiovascular risk, alpha-blockade optimization was justified even though the lesion proved non-functional. Poorly controlled diabetes with marked perioperative glycemic variability added independent surgical risk. Since hypervascular retroperitoneal masses are rare in adults; if the diagnosis of a functional paraganglioma cannot be excluded, the safest course is to prepare as though the mass were one.

title: Clinically Suspected Systemic Arterial Gas Embolism during Robotic-Assisted Bronchoscopy: a Case Report
authorString: Hom BM, Rosenberg B, Xu NY, Szokol JW, McCarthy M.
abstractText:
Background: Systemic arterial gas embolism (SAGE) is a rare but potentially catastrophic complication of robotic-assisted bronchoscopy with lung biopsy. During general anesthesia, the earliest manifestations of SAGE may be limited to transient electrocardiographic or hemodynamic abnormalities. The absence of visible intracranial gas on subsequent imaging does not exclude the diagnosis. We report a case of clinically suspected SAGE during robotic-assisted bronchoscopy in which intraoperative sentinel signs preceded delayed emergence and focal neurologic injury. Case presentation: A 78-year-old woman underwent robotic-assisted bronchoscopy under general anesthesia for biopsy of a 4.6-cm right middle lobe ground-glass opacity using transbronchial needle aspiration and cryobiopsy. Significant airway bleeding occurred after sampling. Immediately after biopsy, she developed transient tachycardia, hypertension, bradycardia, and ST-segment elevation in lead V5. Although these abnormalities resolved, she was unresponsive shortly after extubation and developed right gaze deviation, facial twitching, abnormal movements, and absent right upper-extremity withdrawal to pain. Head computed tomography showed no acute abnormality, and brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated left frontal and precentral cortical diffusion restriction without visible intracranial gas. Because SAGE was strongly suspected, she received 100% oxygen, levetiracetam, endotracheal reintubation, and hyperbaric oxygen therapy at 2.8 atmospheres absolute approximately 4 hours after bronchoscopy. High-sensitivity troponin I peaked at 5,116 ng/L and left ventricular ejection fraction improved from 45-50% to 60% the following day. She was extubated on post-procedure day 10 with persistent neurologic deficits. On post-procedure day 18, she experienced hypoxic cardiac arrest associated with bilateral pulmonary emboli and an acute aortic dissection and died the following day after transition to comfort-focused care.

Conclusions:

During bronchoscopic biopsies under general anesthesia, unexplained ST-segment changes, hemodynamic instability, or delayed neurologic recovery should prompt immediate consideration of SAGE, even when initial neuroimaging is negative. Administration of 100% oxygen, airway and hemodynamic support, minimization of airway pressures, and urgent consultation for hyperbaric oxygen therapy should not be delayed while awaiting radiographic confirmation.

title: Alcohol Intake Amplifies the Association Between Triglyceride–Cholesterol–Body Weight Index (TCBI) and Incident Hypertension: A Nationwide Cohort Study
authorString: Zhang S, Dou J, Yuan X, Xue F.
abstractText: Background Hypertension remains a major public health challenge, yet early identification of individuals at high risk is still inadequate. The triglyceride–cholesterol–body weight index (TCBI) is a simple metabolic and nutritional marker, but its role in incident hypertension is not well understood. It also remains unclear whether alcohol intake modifies this association. We therefore examined the relationship between TCBI and incident hypertension and explored the modifying effect of alcohol intake in a nationwide Chinese cohort. Methods We analyzed data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). The study included 4,887 adults aged 45 years or older who were free of hypertension at baseline. Alcohol intake was defined according to self-reported intake of any alcoholic beverage in the previous year. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for incident hypertension. We also added an interaction term for TCBI and alcohol intake. In addition, restricted cubic spline (RCS) models were used to examine dose–response patterns, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were conducted to assess predictive performance across drinking-status groups, and subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed to evaluate the robustness of the findings. Results During a median follow-up of 9 years, 1,743 participants developed hypertension, yielding an incidence density of 51.93 per 1,000 person-years. In the fully adjusted model, high TCBI was associated with a higher risk of incident hypertension (HR 1.35, 95% CI 1.23–1.49), whereas alcohol intake alone was not independently associated with risk (HR 1.10, 95% CI 0.99–1.23). Joint analyses showed that participants with both high TCBI and drinking had the greatest risk of incident hypertension (HR 1.54, 95% CI 1.33–1.78) compared with low-TCBI non-drinkers. The interaction between TCBI and alcohol intake was significant (P for interaction = 0.006). RCS analyses further showed a linear dose–response association, with a steeper increase in risk among drinkers. Adding TCBI to the base prediction model led to a modest improvement in model discrimination in the overall cohort when compared with the base model (AUC, 0.641 vs. 0.627; P < 0.001). A similar pattern was seen among drinkers, where the AUC increased from 0.631 to 0.649 (P = 0.026). Among non-drinkers, the improvement was relatively small and did not reach statistical significance (AUC, 0.645 vs. 0.639; P = 0.056). Sensitivity analyses yielded consistent results. Conclusion Higher TCBI was independently associated with incident hypertension, and this association was stronger among drinkers. Individuals with both high TCBI and alcohol intake had the highest risk. These findings suggest that incorporating drinking status may improve risk stratification and support more targeted prevention of hypertension.

title: Genetic variants at PITX2, CAV1 and KCNN3, hypertensive target-organ damage and atrial fibrillation in an Uzbek population
authorString: Mashkurova Z, Zakirova D, Abdullaeva G, Radjabova G, Yusupova K, Pulatova M, Shukurova D, Ibrokhimov N, Doniyorov S, Sakhulova N, Khamidullaeva G, Fozilov K, Turdikulova S, Abdullaev A.
abstractText: Background Hypertension is the most prevalent modifiable risk factor for atrial fibrillation, yet only a minority of hypertensive patients develop the arrhythmia and the severity of target-organ damage varies widely at similar blood pressure. We examined whether common variants at established atrial fibrillation susceptibility loci relate to hypertensive target-organ damage as well as to the arrhythmia itself. Methods and Results In a single-centre case-control study, 372 patients with arterial hypertension of Uzbek ancestry (237 with and 135 without atrial fibrillation) were genotyped for five polymorphisms at PITX2, CAV1 and KCNN3 by real-time polymerase chain reaction. Associations with atrial fibrillation were tested by logistic regression under a log-additive model; associations with left ventricular mass index, carotid intima-media thickness, left atrial volume index and estimated glomerular filtration rate were tested by linear regression adjusted for age and systolic blood pressure. Three variants were associated with atrial fibrillation: rs6817105 (odds ratio 2.98 per C allele, 95% confidence interval 2.12–4.20), rs11264280 (2.38, 1.77–3.21) and rs11773845 (0.41, 0.30–0.57). Each rs11264280 T allele was also associated with a higher left ventricular mass index (5.51 g/m², 1.44–9.58) and a greater carotid intima-media thickness (0.05 mm, 0.02–0.08), and both associations were present in patients without atrial fibrillation. The rs11264280 effect allele was more frequent than in any 1000 Genomes super-population. Conclusions Genotype at the 1q21/KCNN3 locus may relate to the severity of hypertensive remodelling before the arrhythmia becomes manifest. These exploratory findings require replication in an independent cohort.

title: Baroreflex sensitivity as a target for nonpharmacological interventions in elderly patients with supine hypertension and orthostatic hypotension
authorString: Criado JR, Gevirtz RN, Kalafut MA.
abstractText: Orthostatic hypotension (OH) and supine hypertension (SH) are physiological indicators of autonomic dysfunction that are associated with an increased risk of major cerebrocardiovascular events. Since pharmacological interventions do not restore normal baroreflex control, improving the efficacy of nonpharmacological interventions that are suitable for these at-risk populations is needed. Heart rate variability (HRV) biofeedback (HRVB) intervention is a safe option to effectively target cardiovascular autonomic regulation and the baroreflex in this patient population. The objective of this study was to determine in elderly patients the relationship between autonomic biomarkers known to be increased by HRVB and impaired baroreflex responses in patients with systolic OH (sOH) and/or SH. This is a retrospective study of 273 patients (144 women; Age: 65–94 yrs) evaluated with a standardized testing protocol of the Autonomic Reflex Screen from 2015 to 2022. Analyses were performed to determine HRV indices and adrenal (BRS a ) and vagal (BRS v ) baroreflex responses during the Valsalva maneuver (VM). The study demonstrated that sOH was associated with a reduction in HRV metrics and the BRS a , independent of SH. This study also demonstrated that SH was associated with a significant increase in Phase II E of the VM and a reduction in the BRS v , independent of sOH. Our results also showed that deficits in Phase II L of the VM were only observed in patients with sOH and concurrent SH. These findings suggest a significant relationship between biomarkers known to improve with HRVB (SDNN and LF-HRV) and deficits in hemodynamic fluctuations in VM contributing to sOH and SH.

title: Prevalence, Sonographic Grading and Factors Associated with Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease among Adults with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study in Uganda
authorString: Omar AA, Sandeyl AA, Hakizimana T, Abdi FD, Hersi AG, Jayte M, Karshe AH, Osobow IM, Christopher E, Ali AH, Ibrahim SH, Ahmed ZA, Nyende L, Musa ME, Araye FA, Mswelo VE.
abstractText: Background Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is strongly associated with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and is an important cause of chronic liver disease and metabolic morbidity. However, data on MASLD among adults with T2DM in sub-Saharan Africa remain limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalence, sonographic grading, and factors associated with MASLD among adults with T2DM at Kayunga and Hoima Regional Referral Hospitals in Uganda. Methods A multicenter hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 422 adults with T2DM attending diabetes clinics at the two study hospitals. Participants underwent clinical assessment, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) and triglyceride testing, and abdominal ultrasonography for detection and grading of hepatic steatosis. Patients with known chronic liver disease, viral hepatitis, significant alcohol consumption, or exposure to medications known to cause hepatic steatosis were excluded. Factors independently associated with MASLD were assessed using multivariable logistic regression, with statistical significance defined as p < 0.05. Results The prevalence of MASLD was 54.5% (230/422). Among participants with MASLD, grade 1 steatosis was most common (175, 76.1%), followed by grade 2 (49, 21.3%) and grade 3 (6, 2.6%). In the multivariable analysis, age (aOR 2.087, 95% CI 1.243–3.504; p = 0.005 for 46–59 years; aOR 2.437, 95% CI 1.316–4.511; p = 0.005 for ≥ 60 years), hypertension (aOR 1.982, 95% CI 1.198–3.279; p = 0.008), obesity (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²) (aOR 2.237, 95% CI 1.177–4.252; p = 0.014), poor glycemic control based on HbA1c (aOR 2.550, 95% CI 1.467–4.434; p = 0.001), and triglyceride levels ≥ 2.3 mmol/l (aOR 2.509, 95% CI 1.470–4.284; p = 0.001) were independently associated with MASLD. Conclusion These findings highlight the importance of incorporating abdominal ultrasonography into the assessment of MASLD, alongside comprehensive management of metabolic risk factors, as part of routine diabetes care to facilitate early identification and management of patients at risk of progressive liver disease.

title: Pattern and Clinical Profile of Tuberculosis Cases Attending a Tertiary Care Centre in Central Kerala, India
authorString: Nandana G, Anil E, Prabaharan C, A B, I E, B D, UK D, Reddy BS, Sureshkumar P, Rose BM, S N, Francis PT, K A.
abstractText: Background Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global public health challenge despite the availability of effective preventive and therapeutic measures. India bears the highest burden of TB worldwide, and regional variations in clinical presentation and disease patterns highlight the need for institution-specific evidence. This study aimed to analyse the pattern and clinical profile of tuberculosis cases attending a tertiary care centre in central Kerala, India. Methods A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted at a tertiary care centre in Kerala. All patients diagnosed with tuberculosis between January 2024 and December 2025 were included. Data were collected from the Medical Records Department using a semi-structured data extraction tool capturing sociodemographic characteristics, clinical presentation, diagnostic investigations, comorbidities, and treatment status. Statistical analysis was performed using Jamovi 2.6.2 and SPSS 21.0. Continuous variables were summarized as mean ± standard deviation or median with interquartile range, while categorical variables were expressed as frequencies and percentages. Associations between selected variables and type of tuberculosis were assessed using Chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests. Results A total of 319 tuberculosis cases were analysed. The median age of participants was 51 years, and males constituted 61.4% of cases. Extrapulmonary tuberculosis accounted for 65.8% of cases, while pulmonary tuberculosis constituted 34.2%. The most common presenting symptoms were cough (44.5%), fever (41.4%), and weight loss (34.2%). CBNAAT was the most frequently used diagnostic modality (57.7%). Rifampicin resistance was observed in 2.8% of cases. Diabetes mellitus (31.7%) and hypertension (30.1%) were the most common comorbidities. Univariate analysis showed that age < 49 years (OR = 1.66; 95% CI: 1.03–2.65) and female sex (OR = 2.39; 95% CI: 1.44–3.97) were significantly associated with extrapulmonary tuberculosis. Conclusion Extrapulmonary tuberculosis constituted the majority of cases in this tertiary care setting, with younger age and female sex showing significant association. A high prevalence of comorbid conditions such as diabetes and hypertension was observed. Strengthening early diagnostic strategies, integrating TB care with non-communicable disease screening, and improving patient follow-up may help enhance treatment outcomes and support tuberculosis elimination efforts.

title: Resistance to thyroid hormone β (RTHβ) due to a THRB mutation (p.Arg429Gln) in a39-year-old woman initially treated for thyrotoxicosis
authorString: Assaad RE, Dahl N, Khamisi S.
abstractText: Background Resistance to thyroid hormone beta (RTHβ) is a rare inherited disorder characterised by elevated free thyroid hormone levels with non-suppressed or elevated TSH, most commonly caused by mutations in the THRB gene. The biochemical profile often mimics thyrotoxicosis or a TSH secreting pituitary adenoma, contributing to delayed or inappropriate treatment. Methods We describe the clinical course, biochemical findings and genetic analysis of a 39 year old woman who presented with palpitations, hypertension and elevated FT4 and FT3 despite a non-suppressed TSH, and who demonstrated no response to antithyroid medication. Genetic sequencing was performed. Results Initial testing showed normal TSH levels (2.45 mU/L), and elevated FT4 (29 pmol/L) and FT3 (7.6 pmol/L). Antithyroid therapy (Thiamazole) led to a paradoxal rise in TSH. Pituitary MRI was normal. Genetic analysis identified a heterozygous THRB gene variant, NM_001354712.2:c.1286G>A (p.Arg429Gln), classified as pathogenic. Antithyroid therapy was discontinued, and management was transitioned to betablockade. The patient remained clinically stable at a 24-months follow-up, and genetic counselling was initiated. Conclusion This case highlights that elevated FT4/FT3 with inappropriately normal or high TSH should raise suspicion of RTHβ. Genetic confirmation is critical to avoid unnecessary interventions and to guide appropriate long-term management and family screening.

title: Benchmarking machine learning for cardiovascular disease classification across 46 countries with geographic and temporal transportability assessment
authorString: Ng'ambi¹˒²˒³ WF, Zyambo²˒³ C, Kazembe⁴˒⁵ L.
abstractText: Background Machine-learning models for cardiovascular disease (CVD) are often evaluated with random participant splits, which may overstate performance when countries differ in prevalence, risk-factor distributions, healthcare access, and survey implementation. We benchmarked statistical and machine-learning classifiers for prevalent self-reported CVD with explicit assessment of class imbalance, calibration, explainability, and geographic and temporal transportability. Methods We analysed harmonised WHO STEPwise approach to noncommunicable disease risk factor surveillance (STEPS) surveys conducted from 2013 to 2023. The cohort included 187,791 adults, including 16,305 CVD cases, from 46 countries. Logistic regression, elastic-net logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost were evaluated using five-fold country-grouped internal-external cross-validation with survey, country-year, and class weighting. We assessed ROC AUC, precision-recall AUC (PR AUC), Brier score, calibration, threshold-dependent performance, SHAP importance, and earlier-to-later transportability. Results Weighted CVD prevalence was 7.78%. XGBoost achieved ROC AUC 0.671, PR AUC 0.162, and Brier score 0.0692; logistic regression achieved 0.669, 0.154, and 0.0694. Country-level performance varied substantially. Removing hypertension and diabetes reduced ROC AUC by 0.038–0.040. Temporal logistic-regression ROC AUC was 0.634 in Mongolia, 0.579 in Uganda, and 0.670 in Viet Nam. Conclusions Complex models produced only small pooled gains over logistic regression, whereas geographic and temporal heterogeneity was substantial. Responsible public-health AI benchmarking should prioritise minority-class performance, calibration, robustness, explainability, and transportability rather than pooled ROC AUC alone.

title: Stasis Dermatitis with Chronic Eczematous changes in a patient with Heart Failure, Chronic Kidney Disease, and Diabetes Mellitus: A Case Report
authorString: Narayanappa SKT.
abstractText: Background Stasis dermatitis is a chronic inflammatory disorder of the lower limbs, commonly associated with edema and venous hypertension. Systemic conditions such as heart failure and chronic kidney disease (CKD) may contribute to or aggravate lower-limb edema, xerosis, pruritus, and impaired skin barrier function. Diabetes mellitus may further increase the risk of skin breakdown and secondary infection. Case Presentation: A 70-year-old man with stage 3 CKD, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and heart failure presented with a 6-month history of bilateral lower-limb blackish discoloration, pruritus, peeling, and edema. Clinical examination demonstrated bilateral lower-limb edema with marked hyperpigmentation, xerosis, scaling, excoriations, and superficial erosions/crusting. The clinical picture was suggestive of chronic eczematous dermatitis with a prominent stasis component. The patient was treated with topical fusidic acid for suspected localized secondary bacterial infection and mometasone furoate for the inflammatory eczematous component. Conclusion This case highlights the multifactorial nature of chronic lower-limb dermatitis in patients with heart failure, CKD, and diabetes mellitus. The combination of dependent edema, chronic hyperpigmentation, pruritus, and scaling should prompt consideration of stasis dermatitis, while CKD-associated xerosis and diabetes-related impairment of skin integrity may contribute to disease persistence and complications.

title: Hyperventilation-Induced Heart Rate Response as a Marker of Cardiovascular Risk - Large-Scale Validation from the Courtois Cardiovascular Signature Program
authorString: Friedrich MG, Leo M, Sharma A, Thanassoulis G, Giannetti N.
abstractText: Hyperventilation-induced change in heart rate (ΔHR) is attenuated in cardiovascular patients, but validation in a large cohort was lacking. We analysed 3,134 participants from the Courtois Cardiovascular Signature Program (CCVSP), spanning five pre-specified cardiovascular risk categories from zero-risk healthy individuals to established atherosclerotic cardiac disease. ΔHR was defined as heart rate at end of 60-second paced hyperventilation minus resting baseline. ΔHR decreased monotonically across risk groups (Kruskal-Wallis H = 145.2, p < 0.001), from a median of 24.0 bpm [IQR 16.0–33.0] in Zero-Risk participants to 15.0 bpm [9.2–22.0] in those with atherosclerotic cardiac disease. After age adjustment, only the established cardiovascular and atherosclerotic disease groups remained significantly attenuated; intermediate risk groups did not. A logistic model incorporating age and ΔHR achieved an AUC of 0.659 [95% CI: 0.633–0.684], with LR + 2.17 and LR − 0.49, yielding a negative predictive value of 97.5% at 5% prevalence. An enhanced model adding history-based variables (sex, smoking, diabetes, hypertension, family history) achieved an AUC of 0.710 [95% CI: 0.686–0.735]. This study validates, in the largest prospective cohort to date, that hyperventilation-induced ΔHR is attenuated in cardiovascular disease. Age-adjusted ΔHR provides a clinically meaningful rule-out performance in low-prevalence settings, supporting its use as a simple, equipment-light pre-screening marker.

title: A Rare Presentation of Acute-Onset BCG-Induced Aortic Aneurysm: A Case Report
authorString: Parsi S, Chaudhry A, Rahmatullah ZM, Subramany R, Bagwell K.
abstractText:
Background:

Mycotic Aortic aneurysms (MAA) are saccular aneurysms of the infected aortic wall. Mycobacterium, compared with other bacteria, is less likely to cause MAA; most cases follow, but it is a rare, late, systemic, and serious complication of intravesical Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) instillation for bladder cancer. Case Presentation: A 65-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes mellitus, diabetic foot ulcer with methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) bacteremia, status post partial toe amputation, and papillary urothelial carcinoma treated with transurethral resection and intravesical BCG instillation, recently underwent a computed tomography (CT) abdomen 2 weeks ago for abdominal pain, which revealed colonic stool without other pathological findings, who currently presented with worsening abdominal pain, and the CT scan identified a new 2.5-centimeter pseudoaneurysm of the infrarenal aorta, associated with a periaortic and aortocaval mass, likely a hematoma, infectious mycotic aneurysm, or neoplastic process. The patient received intravenous piperacillin-tazobactam for presumed MSSA, a potential cause of a mycotic aneurysm, which was later discontinued after negative blood cultures. Vascular surgery consultation led to endovascular aortic stenting. Infectious disease recommended a Karius test; despite no warning signs, it returned positive for the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex, and a diagnosis of a BCG-induced aneurysm was made. The patient was treated with isoniazid, rifampin, ethambutol, and pyridoxine, then continued isoniazid and rifampin for 9 months.

Conclusion:

We presented a rare case of a BCG-induced mycotic aortic aneurysm that developed within 2 weeks. Therefore, we need a low threshold for MAA in patients with a history of intravesical BCG instillations who present with worsening abdominal pain, even if prior imaging 2 weeks ago showed no warning signs and instillations were given 2 years ago. Testing and diagnosing a BCG-induced aneurysm are necessary despite endovascular intervention, because it can further infect the stent and form an abscess if untreated.

title: Results of a Community-Based Coronary CT Angiography Screening in Asymptomatic Adults With Cardiovascular Risk Factors: The Broward County Heart Project
authorString: Lewis AJ, Estep J, Baran D, Ross S.
abstractText:
Background:

Coronary CT angiography (CCTA) and calcium scoring detect subclinical coronary atherosclerosis, but the results of community based screening in asymptomatic adults with cardiovascular risk factors are poorly described. Objective. To describe the results of the first phase of a county-funded CT screening program and their variation by demographics, health system, time, and ZIP code. Methods. Retrospective analysis of aggregate reports from the Broward County Florida Heart Project (May 2023 to September 2025). Eligible residents were those with insurance coverage, age 45 to 70 years (limited exceptions), free of known cardiovascular disease and symptoms, with at least one risk factor. Examinations at six hospitals in four health systems were classified by the program team as normal (Category 1), abnormal (Category 2), or very abnormal (Category 3), with a separate flag for other non coronary abnormality. We used Wilson confidence intervals and chi square, trend, and Mantel Haenszel tests. Results. Among 7,135 participants (58.3% men; 79.0% White, 8.0% Black, 17.2% Hispanic), 43.2% had Category 1, 45.4% Category 2, and 11.4% Category 3 results; 56.8% (95% CI, 55.7% to 58.0%) had abnormal or very abnormal results. The proportion rose from 39.3% at 45 to 55 years to 78.5% at 71 or older (trend P<0.001) and was higher in men than women (68.9% vs 39.8%; odds ratio [OR], 3.36; 95% CI, 3.05 to 3.71). Rates were lower in Black than White participants (38.9% vs 58.6%; hospital adjusted OR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.38 to 0.54) and in Hispanic than non Hispanic participants (51.0% vs 57.8%). Abnormal results ranged from 39.5% to 60.3% across health systems (P<0.001). Variation across the 50 highest volume ZIP codes did not exceed chance (P=0.53). Conclusions. More than half of insured, asymptomatic adults with risk factors screened in this community program had abnormal results, with steep age and sex gradients and unexplained variation across health systems. Black, Hispanic, and female residents were under-represented relative to the county

title: A Pathophysiological Hypothesis of Dorsocervical Fat Pad (Neck Hump), Investing Fascia, Carotid Sheath, and the Promotion of Vascular Patency and Prevention of Thrombosis
authorString: Huang X.
abstractText:
Background:

Dorsocervical fat pad, commonly referred to as neck hump, is a common soft-tissue lesion at the cervicothoracic junction. Its systemic pathophysiological significance has long been underestimated. Hypothesis: This article proposes the investing fascia–carotid sheath mechanical coupling hypothesis. The hypothesis posits that the deep indurated tissue of the dorsocervical fat pad is not merely fat but rather a fascial–ligamentous–adipose complex. This complex is centered on fibrotic thickening of the superficial layer of the deep cervical fascia (investing fascia) and includes the ligamentum nuchae, supraspinous ligament, trapezius aponeurosis, and surrounding fibrofatty tissue. Once the investing fascia loses its viscoelastic buffering capacity, abnormal shear forces generated by routine micromovements of the head and neck can be transmitted through the deep cervical fascial network to the carotid sheath. Evidence: The carotid sheath is an anatomic hub in which multiple structures coexist within a single sheath. The structures within and adjacent to the sheath can be categorized into six functional domains: arterial perfusion, venous return, lymphatic immune clearance, glymphatic cerebrospinal fluid–interstitial fluid clearance, sympathetic output, and the vagal anti-inflammatory pathway. These six functional domains are not mutually exclusive; rather, they are spatially shared, functionally coupled anatomic–physiologic units. Among these, the arterial baroreflex, sympathetic output, and the vagal anti-inflammatory pathway are neurally related pathways that participate in central integration via the nucleus tractus solitarius (NTS) and related nuclei. Venous return, lymphatic immune clearance, and glymphatic cerebrospinal fluid–interstitial fluid clearance contribute more to amplification through pressure coupling, humoral immunity, and clearance functions. Humoral immunity and pressure-coupling pathways participate in amplifying the pathologic process through mechanisms such as Ang II/AT1R-YAP, GPR146-PIEZO1, and impaired lymphatic clearance. In this hypothesis, these steps constitute a hypothetical positive feedback loop: investing fascia fibrosis → carotid sheath compression → coordinated dysfunction of the six functional domains → elevated blood pressure → pathologic vascular remodeling → increased plaque instability. Elevated blood pressure may, in turn, aggravate investing fascia fibrosis. Increased neck circumference has been clearly associated epidemiologically with cardiovascular events and the progression of carotid atherosclerosis. The latter is one of the important upstream risk factors for cerebral infarction. However, direct population-based evidence linking the dorsocervical fat pad to increased neck circumference remains lacking. Most existing studies have used neck circumference or posterior cervical fat accumulation as surrogate markers; no population-based study has used the dorsocervical fat pad as an inclusion criterion. Implications: Within this framework, eliminating the dorsocervical fat pad—that is, relieving the sustained mechanical constraint of the investing fascia on the carotid sheath—has a pathophysiological rationale worthy of systematic investigation for the prevention of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases, especially cerebral thrombosis. Nonetheless, this remains a hypothetical inference.

Conclusion:

This article systematically elaborates the anatomic basis, mechanical transmission mechanisms, pathophysiology of the six functional domains, derivation of the causal chain, relationship between promoting vascular patency and preventing thrombosis and dorsocervical fat pad, testable predictions, and interventional implications of this hypothesis. It also clarifies its evidentiary boundaries.

title: Functional Performance of Electrospun Tissue-Engineered Heart Valve Scaffolds Across Geometries Under Aortic Conditions
authorString: Dillinger H, Saberi A, Manenti M, Burgh-Vrees Ivd, Bouten C.
abstractText: Electrospun, bioresorbable polymer scaffolds represent a compelling platform for tissue-engineered heart valves (TEHVs) owing to their fibrous microstructure, tunable mechanics and inherent capacity to support host-cell infiltration and remodeling. While recent in-vitro parametric studies of bioprosthetic heart valve (BHV) geometry have used silicone cast valves and Doppler echocardiography to link design parameters to hemodynamic performance and leaflet strain, the characterization of the functional behavior of electrospun whole-valve TEHV scaffolds across clinically relevant aortic conditions and across distinct leaflet geometries remains limited. Here, we present an end-to-end workflow in which polycaprolactone (PCL) is electrospun directly onto parametrized, 3D-printed mandrels derived from two established analytical leaflet geometry models, yielding 21 whole-valve scaffolds across five geometries without cutting or suturing of flat fiber sheets. Fiber diameter, orientation and scaffold porosity were assessed by scanning electron microscopy and confirmed to be consistent across scaffolds and geometries. A subset of 8 scaffolds were tested in a pulse duplicator under hypotensive, normotensive and hypertensive aortic conditions, achieving a mean geometric orifice area of 44.51% of the total valve area and demonstrating physiological opening and closing behavior throughout. These results emphasize electrospun whole-valve TEHVs as hemodynamically competent constructs at clinically relevant aortic conditions and provide a reproducible, geometry-driven fabrication and evaluation framework to further support their translation toward regenerative heart valve replacement.
