title: Efficacy of Disease-Modifying Treatments in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Five Phase III Randomized Controlled Trials
authorString: Hung Y, Tsai C, Kao T, Wu Y, Yu W, Carigi S, Sperry BW, Perlini S, Lin Y.
abstractText:
ABSTRACT

Background

Several disease-modifying agents for transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) have been investigated, but differences in trial design and background stabilizer use complicate interpretation of their efficacy. This meta-analysis assessed their efficacy overall and by background stabilizer use.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through September 2026 for phase III randomized, placebo-controlled trials of disease-modifying therapy in ATTR-CM. Primary endpoints were all-cause mortality, 6-minute walk distance (6MWD), Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary (KCCQ-OS) score, and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), pooled with a random-effects model. Treatment effects were compared between the monotherapy and baseline stabilizer strata using a mixed-effects model.

Results

Five trials (ATTR-ACT, APOLLO-B, ATTRibute-CM, HELIOS-B, CARDIO-TTRansform; N=3497) were included. Disease-modifying therapy reduced all-cause mortality (risk ratio, 0.76; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66-0.87; I 2 =0%) and improved 6MWD (pooled standardized mean difference [SMD], 0.43; 95% CI, 0.20-0.67), KCCQ-OS score (SMD, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.19-0.55), and NT-proBNP (SMD, - 0.53; 95% CI, −0.89 to −0.18). The mortality benefit was similar whether therapy was given alone or added to a background stabilizer (pooled risk ratio, 0.77 vs. 0.71; P for interaction = 0.59), but treatment effects on 6MWD (pooled SMD, 0.49 vs. 0.14), KCCQ-OS score (0.44 vs. 0.07), and NT-proBNP (−0.65 vs. −0.13) were smaller among patients receiving a background stabilizer ( P for interaction = 0.012, <0.001, and 0.029, respectively).

Conclusion

Disease-modifying treatments reduced all-cause mortality and favored functional capacity, health status, and NT-proBNP outcomes in patients with ATTR-CM. Exploratory subgroup analyses showed smaller treatment effects on 6MWD, KCCQ-OS score, and NT-proBNP among patients receiving a background stabilizer, with no statistically significant difference in the mortality effect according to baseline stabilizer use.

What Is New?

This meta-analysis of all five phase III randomized controlled trials of disease-modifying therapy in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (3497 analyzed participants) found a lower risk of all-cause mortality (risk ratio, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.66-0.87) and more favorable 6-minute walk distance, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire–Overall Summary score, and N-terminal pro–B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP). In subgroup analyses, the mortality effect was similar with and without a background transthyretin stabilizer at randomization, whereas effects on functional capacity, health status, and NT-proBNP were smaller among patients receiving a background stabilizer.

What Are the Clinical Implications?

Among patients already receiving a transthyretin stabilizer, adding a second agent was associated with a mortality reduction similar to that seen without background therapy but with smaller incremental gains in functional and biomarker outcomes; because these findings rest on aggregate trial data and subgroup comparisons, they should be interpreted cautiously.

title: Ascending Aortic Calcium Identifies Patients at Risk Despite Normal Myocardial Flow, Perfusion and Coronary Calcium: A 13-Site Cohort Study
authorString: Spielvogel CP, Shanbhag A, Khanna S, Zuhair Kassem T, Lemley M, Yi J, Ramirez G, Kavanagh P, Kamagate A, Slipczuk L, Travin MI, Buechel RR, DeKemp RA, Alexanderson E, Carvajal-Juarez I, Packard RR, Al-Mallah M, Einstein AJ, Acampa W, Knight S, Le VT, Mason S, Rosamond TL, Miller RJ, Chareonthaitawee P, Dey D, Berman DS, Di Carli MF, Slomka PJ.
abstractText:
Background

Patients with normal perfusion, normal myocardial flow reserve (MFR) and no coronary artery calcium (CAC) on myocardial perfusion imaging are considered low risk. Yet, adverse events still occur and no routinely reported imaging marker stratifies residual risk. This study aims to determine whether fully automated ascending aortic calcification (AAC) from the attenuation correction CT stratifies risk in these patients.

Methods

In the multicenter REFINE-PET registry, AAC was quantified from non-contrast CT using deep learning aortic segmentation and Agatston scoring. Triple-normal was defined as stress total perfusion deficit (TPD) <5%, MFR >2 and CAC 0. The primary endpoint was cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or heart failure admission, with heart failure admission as key secondary endpoint. Cox models were adjusted for clinical confounders.

Results

Of 21,923 patients, 3,580 (16.3%) were triple-normal, of whom 1,322 (36.9%) had AAC (median Agatston 65, IQR 22-212). Agreement with three blinded readers was good to excellent (Intraclass correlation coefficient 0.87-0.90). Over a median follow-up of 52 months (IQR 26-69), 194 primary events occurred. Per standard deviation, AAC was independently associated with the primary endpoint (adjusted HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.09-1.40; p<0.001), heart failure admission (adjusted HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.10-1.55; p=0.003) and all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 1.17, 95% CI 1.04-1.32; p=0.009). AAC improved model fit beyond clinical factors, MFR and TPD (p≤0.009), with modest gains in discrimination (ΔC 0.007-0.009).

Conclusions

In patients with normal PET readouts, automated AAC was independently associated with adverse outcomes, most strongly heart failure admission, beyond clinical risk factors, perfusion and flow.

Clinical Perspective

What Is New?

In 3,580 patients with normal perfusion, normal myocardial flow reserve and no coronary artery calcium on PET, more than one in three had ascending aortic calcification on the attenuation correction CT. Ascending aortic calcification was independently associated with cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or heart failure admission (adjusted hazard ratio per SD 1.24, 95% CI 1.09-1.40), most strongly with heart failure admission. A fast, fully automated method scored ascending aortic calcification with agreement to expert readers similar to agreement between readers.

What Are the Clinical Implications?

A normal perfusion PET with normal flow and no coronary calcium does not mean uniformly low risk when the ascending aorta is calcified. Because ascending aortic calcification is scored automatically from the CT acquired with every perfusion PET, it could be reported routinely without additional scanning, cost or radiation. Patients presumed low risk who have ascending aortic calcification may warrant heart failure-oriented prevention, such as natriuretic peptide screening, pending prospective validation.

title: 30-Day Heart Failure Readmission and Post-Discharge Healthcare Use Among Older Australians: A Linked-Data Mixed-Methods Study
authorString: Leong CS, Kabir AYMA, Barr M.
abstractText:
Background

Heart failure (HF) is a major public health challenge in ageing populations and a leading cause of unplanned hospital readmissions. Biological, social, and economic factors contribute to recurrent hospitalisation, but gaps remain in understanding how these factors interact and patterns of healthcare use following hospitalisation.

Methods

We conducted an explanatory sequential mixed-methods study of patients aged ≥60 years with an HF hospital admission between 2016 and 2020 who completed the Sax Institute’s 45 and Up Study baseline questionnaire. Data were linked to Admitted Patient Data Collection, Medicare Benefits Schedule, and Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme data. HF readmission within 30 days of the index admission was the outcome. Cox proportional hazards models estimated crude and adjusted hazard ratios (HRs and adjHRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank tests compared survival between groups. Time-series plots mapped healthcare interactions over 1 year following the index admission.

Results

Among 4,252 patients with HF, 409 were readmitted within 30 days. Significant predictors included age ≥80 years (adjHR, 1.30; 95%CI, 1.01–1.67), 1 chronic condition (adjHR, 2.49; 95%CI, 1.41–4.40), ≥2 chronic conditions (adjHR, 1.75; 95%CI, 1.04–2.95), and alcohol consumption above national guidelines (adjHR, 1.45; 95%CI, 1.06–1.98). Time-series analysis indicated that participants with readmission had more frequent out-of-hospital health service contact following their initial HF admission than those without readmission.

Conclusions

Older age, chronic conditions, and high alcohol intake increased 30-day HF readmission risk. Differences in healthcare use after admission highlight opportunities for targeted and coordinated post-discharge care.

title: Targeted Next-Generation Sequencing Reveals Co-infection Patterns and Risk Factors for Severe Pneumonia in Influenza A(H1N1) pdm09
authorString: Lie Z, Hu Y, Chen J, Lai Z, Fang Z, Liu H, Liang J, Zeng Z, Yang Z.
abstractText: Background Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 remains a major cause of seasonal respiratory morbidity, yet predictors of progression to severe pneumonia and the associated co-infection profile remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to describe the clinical features, laboratory abnormalities, pathogen spectrum, and risk factors for severe influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 pneumonia using targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS). Methods In this retrospective single-center study, hospitalized patients admitted to Panyu Central Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University between January and December 2024 were analyzed. Based on tNGS and clinical classification, 175 patients infected with influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 were included, comprising 92 mild cases and 83 severe pneumonia cases; 121 non-H1N1 respiratory infection cases served as controls. Demographic data, symptoms, comorbidities, blood routine and biochemical indices, and co-infection profiles were compared. Uni- and multivariate logistic regression were used to identify risk factors for severe disease. Results Severe pneumonia was more common in older patients and was associated with higher body mass index (BMI), greater rates of hypertension, diabetes, smoking exposure, and longer hospitalization. Compared with mild cases, severe cases showed more frequent cough, dyspnea, nasal congestion/rhinorrhea, neutrophilia, lymphopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced eGFR, elevated creatinine, liver enzyme abnormalities, and increased erythrocyte sedimentation rate. tNGS revealed distinct co-infection patterns: mild cases were predominantly bacterial, with Haemophilus influenzae as the leading pathogen, whereas severe cases had significantly higher fungal co-infection rates, particularly Candida albicans and Aspergillus fumigatus, and more Epstein-Barr virus detection. In multivariate analysis, age, BMI, cough, dyspnea, and nasal congestion/rhinorrhea were independent risk factors for severe pneumonia, while headache was protective. Conclusion Severe influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 pneumonia is characterized by advanced age, elevated BMI, respiratory symptoms, systemic inflammation, organ dysfunction, and a shift toward fungal/viral co-infection. Early risk stratification and pathogen-directed management may improve outcomes in high-risk patients.

title: Effectiveness of Nursing Interventional Package on Vascular Symptoms, Quality Of Life and Perinatal Outcome among Pregnant Women with Pregnancy Induced Hypertension: A Pilot Interventional Study
authorString: Natarajan N, Venkatesan S, Arulappan J.
abstractText: Background Pregnancy-induced hypertension (PIH) is a major contributor to maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality, associated with vascular symptoms, reduced quality of life, and adverse perinatal outcomes. Structured nursing interventions play a vital role in managing these complications and improving overall maternal well-being. Objective To evaluate the effectiveness of a structured nursing interventional package on vascular symptoms, quality of life, and perinatal outcomes among pregnant women with PIH. Methods A quantitative quasi-experimental pre-test and post-test control group design was adopted. Twenty pregnant women with PIH were selected using convenience sampling and randomly assigned into study (n = 10) and control (n = 10) groups. The intervention included education on symptom management, foetal well-being assessment, warning signs, and relaxation techniques. Data were collected using a vascular symptom assessment scale, WHOQOL-BREF QOL-GRAV questionnaire, and perinatal outcome checklist. Post-test was conducted after 4 weeks, and perinatal outcomes were assessed after delivery. Results Post-intervention, the study group showed significant improvement in quality of life (mean difference = 7.94) compared to the control group, which showed no improvement. Significant reductions were observed in blood pressure, oedema, headache, and epigastric pain (p < 0.05), while proteinuria and weight gain showed no significant change. Perinatal outcomes such as Apgar scores and NICU admissions were better in the study group but not statistically significant. Conclusion The structured nursing interventional package was effective in reducing vascular symptoms and improving quality of life among pregnant women with PIH. However, its effect on perinatal outcomes was not statistically significant, indicating the need for further research with larger samples. Relevance for Clinical Practice: This study demonstrates that a structured nursing interventional package can effectively reduce vascular symptoms and improve the quality of life among pregnant women with pregnancy-induced hypertension. Incorporating standardized nursing education on symptom management, fetal well-being assessment, recognition of warning signs, and relaxation techniques into routine antenatal care may enhance maternal health outcomes and support early identification of disease progression. Although improvements in perinatal outcomes were not statistically significant, the positive clinical trends suggest that such interventions have the potential to improve neonatal well-being when implemented on a larger scale. These findings support the integration of evidence-based nursing interventions into antenatal care protocols and highlight the need for larger multicentre studies to establish their impact on maternal and neonatal outcomes.

title: Mapping hypertension prevalence and absolute burden across the states and districts of India
authorString: Kumar A, Rana MJ, Nandan R.
abstractText: Hypertension is India's leading risk factor for premature mortality, and national programmes now require district-level targeting. Existing evidence maps prevalence, which identifies where individuals are most likely to be hypertensive but not where the largest numbers of affected people live. This study examines the distribution of both prevalence and absolute burden across India's states and districts. Individual-level blood pressure data from the National Family Health Survey-5 (2019–21), covering 707 districts, were used to estimate weighted prevalence, with hypertension defined as mean systolic blood pressure ≥ 140 mmHg and/or diastolic ≥ 90 mmHg. District populations from WorldPop gridded estimates were multiplied by prevalence to obtain absolute burden. Districts were classified into four bivariate categories using national medians and ranked within states by cumulative burden contribution. National prevalence was 26%, ranging from 18% to 42.% across states and 11% to 49% across districts. The estimated hypertensive population was 250 million in India. Absolute burden followed a different pattern; Uttar Pradesh alone accounted for 14% of the national total despite below-average prevalence, while eight high-prevalence small states contributed only 0.8%. Within nearly every state, a small subset of districts accounted for the majority of state burden. The divergence between prevalence and burden indicates that healthcare programmes ranked by prevalence would direct resources away from the districts where the greatest number of people require care. Hypertension control programmes in India should incorporate district-level burden estimates alongside prevalence when allocating screening, treatment and follow-up services.

title: Therapeutic AIBP expression contributes to synaptic preservation and vision restoration against glaucomatous neuroinflammation
authorString: Bastola T, Hwang S, Shen Z, Choi S, Choi S, Jang E, Poudel M, Kim K, Miller YI, Weinreb RN, Ju W.
abstractText: Lowering intraocular pressure (IOP) is the only approved treatment for glaucoma, yet retinal ganglion cell (RGC) degeneration and vision loss often progress despite reducing IOP. Apolipoprotein A-I binding protein (AIBP) stabilizes ATP-binding cassette subfamily A member 1 (ABCA1) and promotes cholesterol efflux, thus controlling cholesterol-rich lipid rafts and restraining lipid raft-dependent Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) inflammatory signaling. Here we show that AAV2-mediated expression of human AIBP (hAIBP) preserves inner retinal synaptic integrity and visual function in experimental glaucoma without altering IOP. In DBA/2J mice, a single intravitreal injection of AAV2-hAIBP at 5 months protected RGCs and preserved pattern electroretinogram and pattern visual evoked potential responses at 10 months, even though IOP was indistinguishable from empty-vector controls. AAV2-hAIBP preserved CaMKII and synapsin phosphorylation, restored synaptophysin and PSD95 in the inner plexiform layer, and reduced the expression of TLR4, complement C1q, IBA1, IL-1b, and IL-6 induction in Muller glia and microglia. Comparable protection was observed in microbead-induced ocular hypertension in C57BL/6 mice, both when the AAV2-hAIBP was delivered before microbead injection and when it was delivered after IOP elevation was established. Elevated IOP reduced endogenous retinal AIBP and ABCA1 expression, and AAV2-hAIBP restored both. Protection required the TLR4-binding domain, as an AIBP mutant lacking this domain failed to preserve RGCs. Conversely, AIBP knockout retinas exhibited increased CaMKII phosphorylation and reduced synaptophysin in the absence of elevated IOP. These findings identify synaptic preservation through the AIBP-TLR4 axis as an IOP-independent therapeutic mechanism and support AAV2-hAIBP as a candidate gene therapy for glaucoma.

title: Social participation diversity and cognitive trajectories in older adults with hypertension and diabetes: a longitudinal cohort study
authorString: zhu¹ y, wang¹ j, li¹ y, zhang¹ x, chen j.
abstractText: Background Cognitive decline is a major concern among older adults with hypertension and diabetes, two common chronic conditions associated with an elevated risk of dementia and functional impairment. Although physical activity is widely promoted for cognitive health, the long-term contribution of social participation, particularly the diversity of social engagement, remains insufficiently understood in chronically ill older populations. This study examined the longitudinal associations of social participation diversity and physical activity with cognitive function and explored potential dose-response relationships. Methods Data were obtained from three waves (2011, 2015, and 2018) of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). A total of 547 adults aged 60 years and older with self-reported physician-diagnosed hypertension and/or diabetes were included, contributing 1,472 observations over 7 years of follow-up. Social participation was assessed as the number of different types of social activities engaged in during the previous month (range: 0–12). Physical activity was measured using weekly metabolic equivalent (MET) minutes derived from vigorous-intensity activities. Cognitive function was evaluated using a standardized composite Z-score based on episodic memory, orientation, calculation, and figure drawing tests. Linear mixed-effects models with random intercepts were used to estimate longitudinal associations after adjustment for age, sex, education, and disease subtype. Dose-response relationships were examined using polynomial regression models. Results Greater diversity of social participation was independently associated with better cognitive function over time. Each additional type of social activity was associated with a 0.147-point increase in cognitive Z-score (β = 0.147, 95% CI: 0.045–0.249, p = 0.005). A significant nonlinear dose-response relationship was observed (p = 0.004), with the largest cognitive benefits occurring between one and four activity types, followed by a plateau at higher levels of participation. In contrast, vigorous physical activity was not significantly associated with cognitive function (β = 0.064, p = 0.693) and did not significantly modify cognitive trajectories over time (p = 0.673). Educational attainment was the strongest covariate associated with cognitive performance (p < 0.001). No significant effect modification by disease subtype was identified (all interaction p > 0.05). Conclusions Greater diversity of social participation was associated with better long-term cognitive maintenance among older adults with hypertension and/or diabetes. The observed dose-response pattern suggests that engagement in approximately three to four different types of social activities may provide the greatest cognitive benefit. These findings highlight diverse social engagement as a potentially important and practical component of cognitive health promotion and chronic disease management in later life.

title: Population-scale trends and variations in human aortic biomechanics
authorString: Aggarwal A, Byun J, Capelli C, Danton M, Famaey N, McBride A, Pouch A, Schievano S.
abstractText: The biomechanical properties of the human aorta play a key role in cardiovascular function and disease, yet their population-wide trends and variations remain largely unknown. To fill this crucial gap, we quantified variations in aortic size, stiffness and stresses across 57,434 individuals from the UK Biobank using two-dimensional cine MR imaging and a combined deep-learning, probabilistic and biomechanical modelling framework. Aortic diameter and distensibility (inverse of stiffness) were calculated for the ascending and descending aorta, and their conditional distributions were characterised as a function of age, sex, body size and blood pressure. These observations were integrated with ex-vivo tissue mechanics to infer stress distributions across the aortic wall and the associated uncertainty. Our analysis revealed several new relationships. Larger aortas were found to be stiffer, and greater body size (height and/or weight) was associated with larger aortas with no change in stiffness. Aortic distensibility was negatively associated with systolic, but not diastolic, blood pressure. Apparent sex differences in aortic size were substantially reduced after accounting for body size. Importantly, the maximum stress was found to depend not only on aortic size, as previously thought, but also on distensibility, with lower distensibility associated with higher stresses. The results provide first-of-their-kind population-scale reference distributions for human aortic stiffness, which will improve the personalisation of computational models and digital twins. The correlation between stress and distensibility strongly supports progressing beyond the current diameter-based criteria (based on the law of Laplace) and for the inclusion of stiffness in the clinical risk assessment of aortic diseases. Overall, this study forms the foundation for personalised quantitative medicine and biomechanically informed risk stratification of aortic aneurysms and dissections.

title: Comparative Study of Single Dose Delnido Cardioplegia Versu Multi Dose Blood Cardioplegia in Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting [CABG]
authorString: Kiruthikasri G, Awasthy R.
abstractText: Cardioplegia is an essential component of myocardial protection during coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Delnido cardioplegia is a single-dose cardioplegic solution that provides prolonged myocardial protection and may reduce the need for repeated cardioplegia administration. In contrast, multi-dose blood cardioplegia requires repeated administration during the procedure and provides myocardial protection through a blood-based cardioplegic solution. The choice of cardioplegia may influence operative parameters and postoperative recovery. Therefore, comparison of single-dose Delnido cardioplegia with multidose blood cardioplegia is important in adult cardiac surgery. AIM To compare the effectiveness of single-dose Del Nido cardioplegia with multidose blood cardioplegia in providing myocardial protection during coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in adult patients. MATERIALS AND METHODS : In this comparative study, 30 adult patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting were included and equally divided into two groups. Group A consisted of [n = 15 ]patients receiving single-dose Delnido cardioplegia, while Group B consisted of[ n = 15] patients receiving multidose blood cardioplegia. The intraoperative and postoperative parameters were recorded and compared between the two groups. The parameters assessed included age, cardiopulmonary bypass time, aortic cross-clamp time, ventilation time, ICU stay, hospital stay, urine output, and serum creatinine RESULT A total of 30 patients undergoing CABG were included, with 15 patients in the Delnido cardioplegia group and 15 in the blood cardioplegia group. Significant differences were observed between the groups in CPB time, aortic cross-clamp time, and urine output (p < 0.001). Postoperatively, significant differences were observed in duration of mechanical ventilation, ICU stay, hospital stay, and peak serum creatinine between the two groups (p < 0.001). Overall, patients receiving Delnido cardioplegia demonstrated more favourable intraoperative and postoperative outcomes compared with those receiving multidose blood cardioplegia. CONCLUSION : T he present study compared single-dose Delnido cardioplegia with multidose blood cardioplegia in adult patients undergoing CABG. The findings indicate that Delnido cardioplegia provides effective myocardial protection with the advantage of requiring fewer cardioplegia administrations. Patients receiving Delnido cardioplegia demonstrated favorable postoperative outcomes, including better renal function as reflected by lower peak serum creatinine levels. Other postoperative parameters showed comparable outcomes between the two groups. Overall, single-dose Delnido cardioplegia appears to be a safe and effective alternative to multidoseblood cardioplegia in adult CABG surgery. Further studies with larger sample sizes are recommended to validate these finding

title: Hidden Genetic Disease in Coarctation of the Aorta: Insights from Whole-Genome Sequencing in a Swedish Cohort
authorString: Ellegård R, Green E, Weismann CG, Fernlund E, Malm T, Årstrand HK, Nordén A, Konow I, Kissopoulou A, Kazamia K, Gunnarsson C.
abstractText: Background : Congenital heart defects (CHDs) are the most common birth anomalies worldwide, with a substantial but incompletely characterized genetic contribution. Coarctation of the aorta (CoA) is a common CHD for which the diagnostic yield of comprehensive genomic testing remains insufficiently defined. Methods : In a single-center Swedish cohort, 19 pediatric patients with CoA with or without associated aortic arch hypoplasia, bicuspid aortic valve, or additional simple CHDs, and no prior genetic diagnosis were prospectively enrolled at the time of surgical repair and underwent whole-genome sequencing (WGS). Results : WGS identified pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in 3/19 patients (16%), and genetic variants of uncertain significance were identified in 3/19 patients (16%). Thus, genomic findings were reported in 6 patients (32%) overall, although only the pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were considered diagnostic. Several identified diagnoses had not been suspected based on clinical assessment alone, highlighting the limited sensitivity of phenotypic evaluation during early infancy. Conclusions : The proportion of genetically explained CoA in this surgically treated cohort supports the consideration of genetic testing, particularly in individuals with CoA accompanied by other congenital cardiac defects or extracardiac manifestations. Importantly, an underlying genetic disorder may be present despite the absence of overt clinical signs during infancy. Recognition of this possibility should encourage thorough phenotypic assessment and expanded clinical evaluation to identify potential genetic syndromes. Early genetic diagnosis may improve clinical management, surveillance, and genetic counseling for affected families.

title: Arsenic Impairs Critical Cellular Events of Human Cardiac Development Across Differentiation and Metabolic Maturation
authorString: Skeen BR, Duncan C, Yao F, Shewchuk B, Mruk K, Tokar EJ, Wu X.
abstractText: Arsenic (As) is a widespread environmental contaminant, with exposure occurring primarily through contaminated food and water or cigarette smoke. Maternal exposure to As represents a significant risk factor for congenital heart disease in offspring. However, the mechanisms underlying As-induced developmental cardiotoxicity remain poorly defined. Pluripotent stem cells provide an excellent platform for studying mechanisms of developmental toxicity. Embryoid bodies (EBs) derived from stem cells, can recapitulate many key events of early embryogenesis including germ layers specification. Human cardiomyocytes are derived from mesodermal progenitors. NKX2- 5 governs cardiac specification and morphogenesis, and its mutation produces atrial and ventricular defects in humans. Using an NKX2-5 reporter stem cell line, we modeled mesoderm differentiation in EBs and cardiac induction in a 2D cardiomyocyte differentiation system. In an 8-day differentiation protocol, As (0.05 μM; 3.75 ppb) significantly suppressed cardiomyocyte differentiation and cardiac induction. However, As increased mesodermal markers (HAND1, SNAI2, HOPX) gene expression. In contrast, cardiac-specific genes, including NKX2-5, GATA4, Troponin T, and α-Actinin, were markedly downregulated in the presence of As. As also reduced expression of genes related to cardiac induction, fibroblast function, and vascular markers in the cardiac organoid model. As impaired cardiomyocyte maturation related gene expressions at concentrations without affecting cardiomyocyte proliferation. In a zebrafish model of early heart development, As increased heart rate and disrupted ion channel gene expression. In conclusion, As inhibits ESC differentiation into cardiomyocytes and disrupts cardiomyocyte maturation. Combining stem cell–derived models with zebrafish exposure, this study illuminates adverse outcome pathways for As-induced congenital heart defect.

title: Filter-Free Retrograde Popliteal JETSTREAM Atherectomy Followed by Drug-Coated Balloon Angioplasty: Procedural Safety and One-Year Clinical and Hemodynamic Outcomes
authorString: Doğru A, Abud B.
abstractText: BACKGROUND: Endovascular revascularization is an established treatment for symptomatic femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease. Drug-coated balloon angioplasty allows antiproliferative drug delivery without permanent metallic implantation, while atherectomy may facilitate lesion preparation in calcified and occlusive disease. This study evaluated the procedural safety and one-year clinical and hemodynamic outcomes of filter-free retrograde popliteal JETSTREAM atherectomy followed by drug-coated balloon angioplasty, with additional assessment of dual antiplatelet therapy adherence and continued smoking. METHODS: This retrospective, single-center observational study included 107 patients with Rutherford category 4–5 femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease who underwent JETSTREAM atherectomy exclusively through retrograde popliteal access followed by Ranger paclitaxel-coated balloon angioplasty. No distal embolic protection device was used. Aspirin 100 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg daily were prescribed for 12 months. The primary procedural safety endpoint was clinically evident distal embolization within 24 hours. Longitudinal outcomes included tibialis posterior artery and dorsalis pedis artery Doppler waveform scores, Rutherford category, and ankle-brachial index. Outcomes were compared according to dual antiplatelet therapy adherence and smoking status. Exploratory multivariable logistic regression was performed for factors associated with treatment non-adherence. RESULTS: Mean age was 67.0±6.9 years, and 69.2% of patients were male. Total occlusions were present in 45.8%, PACSS grade 4 calcification in 83.2%, and adjunctive stenting was required in 21.5%. No clinically evident distal embolization occurred within 24 hours (0/107; upper two-sided 95% exact confidence limit, approximately 3.4%). At one year, mean tibialis posterior artery and dorsalis pedis artery waveform scores improved from 1.05±0.42 to 2.42±0.71 and from 1.07±0.60 to 2.28±0.74, respectively; mean Rutherford category decreased from 4.16±0.37 to 1.64±1.17, and median ankle-brachial index increased from 0.59 to 1.20 (all P< .001). Seventy-seven patients (72.0%) were adherent to dual antiplatelet therapy. At one year, adherent patients had better tibialis posterior artery (2.69 vs 1.73), dorsalis pedis artery (2.56 vs 1.57), Rutherford category (1.13 vs 2.93), and ankle-brachial index (1.218 vs 0.873; all P< .001). Forty-six patients continued smoking. Compared with patients not smoking during follow-up, continued smokers had poorer one-year tibialis posterior artery (2.24 vs 2.56; P=.036), dorsalis pedis artery (2.04 vs 2.46; P=.004), Rutherford category (2.02 vs 1.34; P=.002), and ankle-brachial index (1.044 vs 1.179; P=.004). Continued smoking was independently associated with dual antiplatelet therapy non-adherence (adjusted odds ratio, 3.43; 95% confidence interval, 1.27–9.29; P=.015). CONCLUSIONS: Filter-free retrograde popliteal JETSTREAM atherectomy followed by drug-coated balloon angioplasty was associated with substantial one-year clinical and hemodynamic improvement and no clinically evident distal embolization in this cohort. Dual antiplatelet therapy adherence was associated with better one-year outcomes, whereas continued smoking was associated with poorer outcomes and greater non-adherence.

title: Septation of the Aortic Sac and Distal Outflow Tract of the Embryonic Heart, a Hitherto Neglected Factor in the Embryology of Variants and Malformations of the Aortic Arch Complex
authorString: Männer J.
abstractText: The adult configuration of the aortic arch complex (AoAC) results from transformation of its embryonic precursor. Concepts of the embryology of variants and malformations of the AoAC traditionally focus on transformation processes that are driven by regression and persistence of embryonic vascular segments. However, such concepts cannot explain every variant or malformation since they neglect other morphogenetic processes involved in the transformation of the embryonic AoAC, such as blood vessel “migration”, and septation of the aortic sac (AoS) and distal outflow tract (OFT) of the embryonic heart. This article focuses on the hitherto neglected role of septation of the AoS and embryonic OFT in normal and abnormal patterning of the AoAC. It is shown (1) how phylogenetic “deviations” from the mammalian “standard” of AoS septation lead to the AoAC branching patterns found in non-mammalian vertebrates; and (2) how ontogenetic deviations from the human “standard” can lead to AoAC anomalies, such as “bovine arch”; subclavian artery as first branch of the aortic arch; anomalous origin of supra-aortic branches from the proximal ascending aorta; anomalous origin of one pulmonary artery from the proximal ascending aorta; anomalous origin of one common carotid artery from the proximal pulmonary trunk; and tritruncal hearts.
