title: Multi‑target mechanisms of paeoniflorin in inflammatory regulation: A network pharmacology (Review).
authorString: Zhang J, Ye J, Jin K, Sun X, Yu X, Zhao Y, Zhu N.
abstractText: Paeoniflorin (PF), a monoterpene glycoside from Paeonia roots, shows low toxicity and broad anti‑inflammatory activity. A systematic review (PubMed, through 2025) with network pharmacology indicates that PF restores mitochondrial function, raises anti‑inflammatory mediators (IL‑10 and arginase‑1), reduces TNF‑α, IL‑1β and IL‑6, and eases oxidative stress. Its effects hinge on intertwined routes, dampening TLR4/MyD88, blocking NF‑κB nuclear entry, lowering MAPK phosphorylation, reshaping JAK‑STAT, and disrupting NLRP3 inflammasome assembly. Network mapping singles out a conserved core module (MAPK1, MAPK3, HSP90AA1, TP53, ESR1, BCL2, HIF1A, IL6, IL10 and FGF2), with HSP90AA1 and ESR1 as disease‑tailored effectors in rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis (OA). PF absorbs fast and gathers in the liver with minimal toxicity, yet oral availability stays poor. Preclinical promise spans OA, colitis, and atherosclerosis, while clinical data remain thin. Synergistic pairing with other agents and structural refinement of PF broaden its reach, though such computational leads need experimental corroboration. Future efforts should improve its bioavailability, develop targeted delivery systems, and conduct rigorous clinical trials to move PF from tradition to evidence‑based medicine.

title: Design and Rationale of the CLASP II TR Randomized Trial for Severe Tricuspid Regurgitation.
authorString: Ailawadi G, Davidson CJ, Anderson AS, Hahn RT, Willert P, Gilmore SY, Vinekar C, Zhang B, Muralidhar M, Castro R, Shi L, Graham A, Feldman T, Mack MJ, Leon MB.
abstractText: Severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is a progressive disease associated with mortality, heart failure hospitalization (HFH), impaired functional status, and reduced quality of life. Transcatheter tricuspid valve repair and replacement therapies have expanded treatment options for TR patients beyond medical therapy and surgery and improved their functional status and symptoms. The CLASP II TR trial is a prospective, multicenter, open-label randomized trial designed to test superiority of tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) with the PASCAL transcatheter valve repair system+optimal medical therapy (device group) versus optimal medical therapy alone (control group) in symptomatic severe TR patients. A total of 450 patients with ≥severe TR as assessed by an independent echocardiographic core laboratory are randomized following central screening committee assessment in a 2:1 ratio (device:control). The primary endpoint is a 6-month hierarchical composite combining key safety and efficacy outcomes (all-cause mortality, durable right ventricular assist device or heart transplant, elective or non-elective tricuspid valve surgery/intervention and number of HFH) with quality-of-life improvement assessed using Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score. Additionally, clinical, echocardiographic, functional, and quality-of-life parameters are also evaluated. Patients are assessed at baseline; 30 days; 3, 6, and 12 months; and annually through 5 years. Crossover of control patients is permitted either after the 2-year visit or when the last randomized patient completes 12-month follow-up. The CLASP II TR trial will inform the safety and effectiveness of the PASCAL system compared to medical therapy alone in the treatment of patients with symptomatic, severe tricuspid regurgitation. The trial has completed enrollment, and the report of primary results is expected. Trial Registration: Edwards PASCAL Transcatheter Valve Repair System Pivotal Clinical Trial (CLASP II TR); NCT04097145; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04097145.

title: Age-specific reference values for pulse wave velocity in paediatric populations: a systematic review with meta-analysis.
authorString: Martínez-Cifuentes Ó, Nilsson PM, Saz-Lara A, Valladolid-Ayllón S, Hitado-Cifuentes AM, Martínez-García I, Cavero-Redondo I.
abstractText:
Background/objectives

Arterial stiffness, assessed by pulse wave velocity (PWV), is a key marker of vascular aging and an independent predictor of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Age is the primary determinant of PWV; however, age-specific and sex-specific reference values in healthy paediatric populations are not yet well defined. Therefore, this study aimed to establish reference values for PWV in healthy children.

Methods

A systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies reporting age-stratified PWV values in healthy children was conducted. Pooled mean estimates and 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs) were calculated using random effects models. Additional sex-stratified analyses were performed, and percentile distributions were examined to enhance clinical applicability.

Results

Ten studies were included in the quantitative synthesis. A nonlinear pattern was observed: PWV was greater in the 0-5-year age group (5.33 m/s) than in the 6-8-year age group (4.93 m/s), followed by a progressive increase up to 15-18 years (5.80 m/s). This trend was consistent across sexes. Substantial heterogeneity between studies was detected, and Egger's test suggested the presence of publication bias across several age groups, both in sex-stratified analyses and in the overall population.

Conclusion

Age is the primary determinant of arterial stiffness during childhood and is influenced by physiological processes such as arterial wall maturation early in life and puberty. Establishing age-specific reference values for PWV provides an essential clinical tool for the early detection of accelerated vascular aging and cardiovascular risk stratification from early stages of life.

title: Addressing non-communicable diseases and injuries through an equity lens: insights from the Cameroon non-communicable disease and injury (NCDI) Poverty Commission.
authorString: Saidu Y, Budzi M, Ben Bachire H, Ousmane D, Haoua F, Clarisse M, Emmanuel V, Ndom MS, Mbanga C, Karimu I, Sonyuy MF, Mensah E, Bukhman G, Gupta N, Njei B, Al Ajlouni YA, Fasawe O, Sap S, Sobngwi E, Ndom P, Kingue S.
abstractText:
Background

Non-communicable diseases and injuries (NCDIs) constitute a leading cause of premature mortality globally, disproportionately affecting low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). To curb the rising burden of NCDIs in Cameroon, the Ministry of Public Health established the National NCDI Poverty Commission to assess the burden of NCDIs, evaluate investments and expenditures related to NCDI services, and generate evidence to guide national policy formulation and resource prioritisation.

Methods

We synthesised data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2019 database and conducted a comprehensive literature review of peer-reviewed and grey literature (2005-2022) to characterise the burden and risk factors of NCDIs in Cameroon. Investments and expenditures related to NCDIs were extracted from the World Health Organization Global Health Expenditure Database and national planning documents. A two-phase priority-setting process was applied to rank NCDI conditions and identify cost-effective, context-appropriate interventions through quantitative scoring and expert consensus.

Results

NCDIs accounted for 43% of all deaths in 2019, with nearly 29% occurring among individuals aged <40 years. Disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) from NCDIs have risen steadily since 1990, with almost two-thirds (61%) attributable to conditions beyond the 'big four' disease categories of diabetes, neoplasms, chronic respiratory diseases, and cardiovascular diseases. Over half (51%) of NCDI-related DALYs in Cameroon were not attributable to quantified behavioural or metabolic risk factors in the GBD framework. Despite this high burden, only 6% of disease prevention funding was directed to NCDIs between 2016 and 2020. The Commission identified 49 priority NCDI conditions and 123 interventions for phased implementation across community, primary, and hospital platforms.

Conclusions

NCDIs are a major public health burden in Cameroon, heavily impacting the 'economically productive' age group. Rebalancing financing and integrating a prioritised package of NCDI services into Universal Health Coverage (UHC) would be essential to reduce premature mortality and financial hardship.

title: Estimated small dense low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and incident myocardial infarction in patients undergoing dialysis: a nationwide cohort study.
authorString: Kim BS, Kim HJ, Kim J, Choi N, Shin JH.
abstractText:
Background

Small dense low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (sdLDL-C) is an atherogenic LDL subfraction that may reflect lipid-related coronary risk beyond conventional cholesterol levels. Estimated sdLDL-C (E-sdLDL-C) is calculated from a standard lipid panel, but its prognostic relevance for myocardial infarction in patients undergoing dialysis remains uncertain.

Methods

This nationwide cohort study included 21,671 adults with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) receiving long-term dialysis who underwent health screening in 2009-2017. E-sdLDL-C was calculated from fasting lipid profiles and categorised into quartiles. Incident myocardial infarction and ischemic stroke were the primary and secondary outcomes, respectively, assessed through December 2022.

Results

During 166,428 person-years, 993 myocardial infarctions occurred, with 9,426 deaths before myocardial infarction. Fully adjusted hazard ratios for myocardial infarction in Quartiles 2-4 versus Quartile 1 were 1.24 (95% CI, 1.01-1.52), 1.61 (1.32-1.96), and 1.44 (1.15-1.80), respectively. The association remained significant after accounting for competing mortality. For ischemic stroke, 1,249 events and 9,254 competing deaths occurred during 165,727 person-years, with no significant association with E-sdLDL-C after full adjustment. Adding E-sdLDL-C increased the C-index for myocardial infarction from 0.716 to 0.726 (Δ = 0.010), without significant differences from models including LDL-C (0.725; p = 0.453) or non-HDL-C (0.727; p = 0.264).

Conclusion

Among patients undergoing long-term dialysis, E-sdLDL-C was associated with incident myocardial infarction after multivariable adjustment, whereas no significant association was observed with ischemic stroke. These findings support the potential relevance of E-sdLDL-C for myocardial infarction risk assessment in patients with ESKD, although its clinical utility requires further validation.

title: Disproportionate systolic blood pressure response relative to oxygen consumption identifies a high-risk haemodynamic phenotype in arterial hypertension.
authorString: De Biase N, Del Punta L, Moura-Ferreira S, De Schutter S, Iaconelli A, Di Fiore V, Taddei S, Gevaert AB, Verwerft J, Pugliese NR, Masi S.
abstractText:
Objectives

Conventional definitions of hypertensive response to exercise (HRE) rely on absolute systolic blood pressure (SBP) thresholds, which do not account for the metabolic demand driving the pressor response and show inconsistent association with pathophysiology and prognosis. Whether indexing SBP to oxygen consumption (VO2) provides independent pathophysiological information along the continuum from arterial hypertension (AH) to heart failure (HF) remains unclear. We investigated the haemodynamic and prognostic implications of the SBP/VO2 slope in patients with AH and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction.

Methods

We enrolled 970 participants with AH, including 34% with established HF. All subjects underwent baseline echocardiography and cardiopulmonary exercise testing with stress echocardiography. We categorized patients into tertiles of the slope of SBP relative to peak VO2 from rest to peak exercise; the highest tertile was used to define HRE for descriptive analyses. Patients were followed for all-cause mortality or HF-related hospitalisation.

Results

Patients with HRE (SBP/VO2 slope >5.7 mmHg/ml/kg/min) displayed adverse cardiac remodelling (higher left ventricular mass index, left atrium dilation), systemic exercise-induced vascular dysfunction (elevated peak systemic vascular resistance, reduced total arterial compliance), and reduced peripheral oxygen extraction (lower peak arteriovenous oxygen difference), despite well controlled resting BP. Over a 24-month median follow-up, a steeper SBP/VO2 slope was associated with a higher risk of death or HF-related hospitalisation, independent of peak VO2 (hazard ratio per 1-standard deviation increase: 1.21; P = 0.041).

Conclusions

In patients with AH, a steeper SBP/VO2 slope identifies a high-risk haemodynamic phenotype and may represent an early marker of progression along the continuum from AH to HF.

title: Heart Failure Predicts Contralateral Limb Progression After Endovascular Therapy for Initial Unilateral Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
authorString: Shima Y, Karashima E, Kurimoto S, Shimonaga T, Yoshino T, Toda H, Kawamura K, Takashima A, Urabe Y, Arai Y, Kobayashi Y, Okazaki T, Ohsawa N, Bando G, Irie N, Mushiake K, Inoue N, Abe M.

journal.title: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists

abstractText:
Background

Heart failure (HF) is associated with adverse outcomes in patients with peripheral artery disease. However, its impact on contralateral limb progression after endovascular therapy (EVT) for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) remains unclear. This study investigated the association between HF and contralateral major adverse limb events (MALE) after EVT for initial unilateral CLTI.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed patients with initial unilateral CLTI from the multicenter registry. Patients with prior contralateral CLTI or contralateral major amputation were excluded. The primary outcome was contralateral MALE, defined as a composite of contralateral revascularization and major amputation. Secondary outcomes included recurrent contralateral CLTI, contralateral EVT, contralateral major amputation, and ipsilateral MALE. Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models were used.

Results

Among 347 patients, 182 had HF. During follow-up, contralateral MALE occurred in 86 patients. Patients with HF had significantly lower freedom from contralateral MALE than those without HF (63.9% vs 80.3%, log-rank P = .002). In multivariable analysis adjusting for age, sex, diabetes mellitus, dialysis, albumin <3.0 g/dL, cerebrovascular disease, and coronary artery disease, HF remained independently associated with contralateral MALE (adjusted HR 2.08, 95% CI 1.29-3.35, P = .003). Heart failure was also independently associated with contralateral EVT (adjusted HR 2.06, 95% CI 1.29-3.28, P = .003), but not with ipsilateral MALE (adjusted HR 1.08, 95% CI 0.77-1.51, P = .66).

Conclusions

In patients undergoing EVT for initial unilateral CLTI, HF independently predicted contralateral limb events but not ipsilateral limb failure. These findings suggest that HF may identify patients who warrant closer clinical assessment of the contralateral limb after EVT.Clinical ImpactHeart failure (HF) is a well-established predictor of mortality in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), but its association with subsequent limb events has remained unclear. In this multicenter study, HF was independently associated with contralateral major adverse limb events and contralateral revascularization after endovascular therapy, whereas no association was observed with ipsilateral MALE. These findings suggest that HF may help identify patients at increased risk for future contralateral limb events. Incorporating HF status into post-EVT risk assessment may support closer surveillance of the contralateral limb and facilitate earlier detection of clinically significant disease requiring intervention.

title: Preconception Glycemic Control: Reducing Risk of Congenital Heart Defect in Offspring
authorString: Miao PM, Madu CO, Lu Y.
abstractText: Congenital heart defects (CHD) are among the most common birth defects and a leading cause of infant mortality. Pregestational diabetes mellitus increases risk of fetal CHD. However, this association and prevention implications have not been integrated across literature. This narrative review seeks to combine evidence of cardiac formation and biological mechanisms that frame maternal hyperglycemia as a teratogen of cardiogenesis, as well as preconception care (PCC) recommendations for diabetic women. Cardiac neural crest cells are vulnerable to glycemia-induced oxidative stress, apoptosis, and epigenetic abnormalities before cardiac septation is complete by the seventh week of gestation. CHD risk rises at maternal HbA1c levels starting from 5.6%, below the minimum for prediabetes. As the window for hyperglycemia’s teratogenic effect may close before pregnancy is confirmed, glycemic control during pregnancy is unlikely to reduce much risk of CHD, while PCC can have greater influence in reducing first-trimester HbA1c levels, lowering risk of congenital defects. Little evidence exists isolating risk of CHD from risk of fetal malformations. Disparities in access to clinical care limit the improvement it could bring to odds of CHD-free birth. Bridging gaps in evidence and implementation is crucial for bringing evidence into PCC for CHD prevention based on glycemic control.

title: Ventricular Fibrillation in PRKAG2 Cardiomyopathy: A Genetic Arrhythmia Substrate Beyond Wolff-Parkinson-White.
authorString: Visch J, Hopman LHGA, Holtus D, Kemme MJB, Amin AS, Bindraban NR, van der Velden J, Postema PG.
abstractText:
Background

PRKAG2 syndrome is a rare autosomal dominant glycogen storage cardiomyopathy characterized by left ventricular hypertrophy, ventricular pre-excitation, and progressive conduction system disease.

Case summary

We report the case of a 25-year-old woman with genetically confirmed PRKAG2 syndrome who presented with an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Echocardiography revealed preserved left ventricular systolic function with mild concentric hypertrophy and marked apical thickening. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging showed anterolateral trabecular hypertrophy without evidence of myocardial fibrosis. Electrophysiological study excluded Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome and instead identified a fasciculoventricular accessory pathway. Given the occurrence of ventricular fibrillation and the associated arrhythmic risk, a transvenous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was implanted for secondary prevention.

Discussion

This case illustrates the atypical presentation of arrhythmias that deviate from classical patterns, such as those seen in Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome.

Take-home message

Individualized risk assessment, close electrophysiological monitoring, and consideration of early implantable cardioverter-defibrillator implantation are important in PRKAG2-related cardiomyopathy.

title: Acute mental stress-induced adrenergic reactivity profiles predict distinct cardiometabolic risk trajectories over three years: the SABPA study.
authorString: Naudé D, Smith W, von Känel R, Wentzel A.
abstractText:
Objectives

We previously characterised acute mental stress-induced alpha (α)- and beta (β)-adrenergic-haemodynamic reactivity profiles cross-sectionally and related them to unique cardiometabolic risk outcomes. Whether these profiles predict future cardiometabolic risk remains unclear. We compared three-year cardiometabolic risk outcomes between predominant α- and β-responders and evaluated the prognostic value of each profile for predicting cardiometabolic risk.

Methods

Participants (aged 20-65 years) were stratified at baseline as predominant α- (n = 43) or β-responders (n = 59) defined by lowest and highest population quartiles, respectively, of reactivity in both cardiac output and Windkessel arterial compliance. Remaining participants were classified as mixed-α/β-responders (n = 227). Hypertension and central obesity at baseline and follow-up were defined using international guidelines. Other outcomes included cardiac stress (cardiac troponin-T ≥4.2 pg/ml), abnormal-glucose-tolerance (Abnl-GT; HbA1c ≥5.7% and/or fasting glucose ≥5.6 mmol/l and/or using antidiabetic medication), 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD)-risk (UCLA composite score), 24-h ischaemic events (Holter-electrocardiography) and an adverse lipid profile (high total cholesterol, low high-density-lipoprotein (HDL)-cholesterol and high triglycerides) defined by South African Heart Association/Lipid and Atherosclerosis Society of Southern Africa guidelines. Three-year risk for each outcome by adrenergic profile were estimated using covariate-adjusted Cox-proportional hazard models.

Results

At three-year follow-up, α-responders had higher prevalence of hypertension, Abnl-GT, low HDL-cholesterol, and 10-year ASCVD-risk than β-responders (all P ≤ 0.025). Both α- and β-adrenergic reactivity profiles were associated with increased three-year risk of 10-year ASCVD, cardiac stress, central obesity, and Abnl-GT (all P ≤ 0.047). The α-adrenergic reactivity profile uniquely predicted elevated risk of hypertension, high total cholesterol, and low HDL-cholesterol (all P ≤ 0.009), whereas the β-adrenergic reactivity profile was associated with lower risk of hypertension and high total cholesterol but higher risk of 24-h ischaemic events (all P ≤ 0.016).

Conclusion

Acute mental stress-induced α- and β-adrenergic reactivity profiles independently predicted distinct cardiometabolic outcomes over three-years, delineating differential pathways of cardiometabolic risk. These findings support the potential utility of adrenergic reactivity phenotypes to refine individual, psychophysiological-linked cardiometabolic risk stratification.

title: The cholesterol, high-density lipoprotein, and glucose index and its derivatives related to obesity and inflammation as novel metabolic markers for predicting new-onset cardiovascular-liver-metabolic multimorbidity: A prospective cohort study.
authorString: Sun Z, Ainiwaer A, Xu Y, Zhang G, Sun X, Peng X, Dai Y, Kadier K.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiovascular-liver-metabolic multimorbidity (CLMM), defined as the co-occurrence of at least two of cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, is an increasing health burden. We evaluated the cholesterol, high-density lipoprotein, and glucose (CHG) index and its obesity- and inflammation-derived variants for predicting incident CLMM.

Methods

This prospective cohort included 6,534 adults aged ≥45 years from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. CHG, eight obesity-derived indices, and CHG-CRP were assessed, with the triglyceride-glucose index and TG/HDL-C ratio as comparators. Associations with incident CLMM were evaluated using logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, and threshold analysis. Predictive performance was compared using receiver operating characteristic analysis, the integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), and the net reclassification improvement (NRI), with additional joint-effect, interaction, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses.

Results

At the 2015 follow-up, 406 participants (6.2%) met the criteria for CLMM. Higher CHG was linearly associated with incident CLMM (highest vs lowest quartile: OR 1.64, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.22-2.22). Obesity-derived variants showed stronger associations, particularly CHG-BMI (OR 3.13, 95% CI 2.21-4.43), which also had the highest discrimination (AUC 0.643, 95% CI 0.616-0.669) and continuous NRI (34.08%). Participants with both high CHG and high BMI had the greatest CLMM risk (OR 2.59, 95% CI 1.94-3.51). Results were robust in sensitivity analyses.

Conclusions

The CHG index and its obesity-derived variants, particularly CHG-BMI, are accessible and inexpensive candidate metabolic markers for predicting new-onset CLMM. CHG-BMI showed the highest apparent discrimination among the evaluated indices, although its AUC was modest. External population validation is needed.

title: Lactylation and exercise: A molecular link to disease alleviation (Review).
authorString: Wang J, Wu L.
abstractText: Regular physical activity improves physical capacity and overall health by enhancing cardiopulmonary function and muscle strength, reducing stress, and improving psychological well‑being and quality of life. Despite these known benefits, the molecular mechanisms that underlie these effects remain incompletely understood. Lactylation, a modification wherein lactate molecules form ester bonds with proteins, induces functional changes in these proteins. Evidence indicates that exercise can regulate lactylation, which, in turn, affects intracellular signaling pathways and metabolic processes. This modulation plays a role in promoting health and facilitating disease alleviation. The present review offers an extensive review of the mechanisms through which exercise influences lactylation and discusses the potential clinical applications of lactylation in the prevention and treatment of exercise‑related diseases.

title: An Immune-Vascular CD80/HTR2B Axis Integrates S-Palmitoylation and Vascular Inflammation in the Pathogenesis of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm: Evidence from Mendelian Randomisation, Multi-Omics, Single-Cell Perturbation and qPCR Validation
authorString: Wu Y, Ren J.
abstractText:
Background:

Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is characterised by irreversible dilatation of the abdominal aorta and a risk of rupture. Clinical assessment still relies mainly on diameter and growth rate and does not capture the immune, vascular and matrix heterogeneity of the aortic wall. Protein S-palmitoylation is catalysed by ZDHHC palmitoyltransferases and reversed by depalmitoylating enzymes. It regulates membrane localisation and trafficking of immune receptors, chemokine receptors, ion channels and vascular signalling proteins. However, whether palmitoylation-related machinery and substrates jointly define an AAA disease axis has not been systematically examined. This study aimed to identify a reproducible palmitoylation-related module in human AAA tissue, to screen axis-level cis-eQTL multiplicity-controlled significant genes and to independently define the strict genetic effect boundaries of that module at a cis-eQTL layer, to converge the module onto core targets using multi-omics, machine learning, single-cell analysis and computational docking, and to validate the hub genes at the tissue-expression level by real qPCR.

Methods:

We used GSE232911 (110 patients with AAA and 13 donors) as the discovery cohort and assembled an S-palmitoylation machinery-and-substrate axis gene set. A tissue-level module was frozen from the intersection of differential expression, the axis gene set and pre-specified AAA vascular and inflammatory programmes. We then performed axis-level cis-eQTL Mendelian randomisation (MR) screening with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR and Bonferroni double correction to select multiplicity-controlled significant genes, together with independent validation at a strict cis-eQTL layer with coloc.abf colocalisation; disease-internal consensus clustering; LASSO, random forest and SVM-RFE feature selection within the frozen module; a single-gene logistic model with two external directional checks; construction of the GSE166676 single-cell atlas; myeloid monocle3 trajectory and scTenifoldKnk in-silico perturbation; L1000CDS2, CTD, P2Rank and AutoDock Vina public-resource integration and computational docking; and real qPCR validation of CD80 and HTR2B.

Results:

The discovery cohort yielded 3,100 differentially expressed genes. The frozen three-way intersection produced a 15-gene module, including 12 up-regulated and 3 down-regulated genes. In the axis-level cis-eQTL screening layer, 161 of the 341 axis genes were estimable, and 42 reached nominal significance (IVW random-effects p<0.05); after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR and Bonferroni double correction, 9 genes simultaneously satisfied q<0.01 and p<0.05/161 and constitute the multiplicity-controlled significant genes: SORT1, BAALC, ZDHHC6, MICA, CD7, CANX, PI4K2A, GSDMD and ADORA2B (five risk-increasing and four risk-decreasing, all p<0.001). In the independent strict cis-eQTL layer (341 axis genes, 35 passing the r²<0.001 instrument gate, 15 estimable), ENTPD1 (OR 0.884, 95% CI 0.790-0.989, p=0.031) and NOD2 (OR 0.942, 95% CI 0.888-0.998, p=0.042) reached nominal significance but none passed BH-FDR<0.05 (minimum q=0.317); single-SNP and leave-one-out analyses quantified the instrument-contribution boundaries of the two signals. None of 106 coloc.abf tests showed strong colocalisation, and the outcome-region audit showed limited AAA GWAS signal in the relevant windows (Figure S1 ). AAA tissue resolved into K=3 disease-internal molecular groups (C1=40, C2=55 and C3=15). The three machine-learning methods uniquely converged on CD80 and HTR2B. The single-gene CD80 model had a training AUC of 0.9685 and remained directionally consistent in two external cohorts (AUC 0.7551 and 0.7449). The single-cell atlas retained 7,596 cells, and the myeloid perturbation converged on cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction (KEGG, k=9/50, FDR=0.00355). The druggability layer returned 38 unique perturbagens, 29 high-evidence CD80-related compounds and computational docking for both targets; the best mode-1 affinities were -7.46 kcal/mol for CD80 and -8.98 kcal/mol for HTR2B. Real qPCR showed higher CD80 (1.54-fold, p=0.0032) and HTR2B (1.66-fold, p=4.8x10^-5) expression in AAA tissue than in donor tissue.

Conclusion:

We delineate an S-palmitoylation-contextualised immune-vascular disease axis in human AAA and place CD80 and HTR2B at the intersection of multi-omics screening, computational perturbation, computational docking and real qPCR tissue validation. The genetic layer returned nine multiplicity-controlled significant genes at the axis-level screen and retained two nominal associations with their full correction boundaries at the independent strict layer. The single-cell, perturbation and docking layers provide mechanistic and druggability directions, and qPCR provides expression-level validation in human aortic tissue. Collectively, the evidence supports a testable palmitoylation-immune costimulation-vascular inflammation axis and establishes an executable framework for functional and cohort validation.

title: Beyond Mirror Imaging: Rotational Atherectomy in Dextroversion.
authorString: Koyawala N, Singh R, Yasumura K, Bienstock S, Kini AS, Sharma SK, Dangas GD.
abstractText:
Objective

To describe, to our knowledge, the first reported case of how to safely and effectively complete complex percutaneous coronary intervention in a patient with dextroversion and a severely calcified obstructive lesion in the left anterior descending coronary artery.

Key steps

A 68-year-old man with self-reported dextrocardia and progressive angina underwent preprocedural coronary computed tomography angiography, which diagnosed dextroversion, multivessel disease, and a calcium score of 1,089. Horizontal fluoroscopic inversion was applied and improved visual familiarity but did not restore true anatomical orientation. Under intravascular ultrasound guidance, a severely calcified left anterior descending lesion was treated with rotational atherectomy (1.5-mm burr) and drug-eluting stent implantation.

Potential pitfalls

In patients with dextrocardia, including dextroversion, defining anatomy before cardiac catheterization can help increase efficiency and enhance safety in this group, especially for complex percutaneous coronary intervention.

Take-home messages

Unlike mirror-image dextrocardia, dextroversion lacks true mirror anatomy, so fluoroscopic mirroring alone cannot "normalize" orientation. Preprocedural computed tomography angiography and intraprocedural intravascular imaging were essential for anatomic clarification and allowed safe, effective complex percutaneous coronary intervention.

title: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance derived myocardial strain: applications, acquisition techniques, analysis, and reporting.
authorString: Gulsin GS, Ambale-Venkatesh B, Axel L, Bluemke DA, Captur G, Cavalcante JL, Ennis DB, Epstein FH, Gerber B, Hanneman K, Kawel-Boehm N, Kelle S, Kramer CM, Lima JAC, Lamb HJ, Lu M, Marwick TH, Romano S, Young AA, McCann GP.
abstractText: Myocardial strain imaging enables quantification of cardiac deformation. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) is well suited for strain assessment due to the ability to image in any given plane with high spatial and contrast resolution. CMR strain measures have incremental diagnostic and prognostic utility over conventional clinical imaging parameters across disease states. Routine integration of CMR strain assessment in clinical practice has been hindered by the lack of agreement on imaging protocols and analysis methods, variability due to noise sensitivity, and a paucity of robust normative age-, sex- and ethnicity-specific reference ranges. In recognition of the expanding applications of strain techniques in clinical and research CMR, this joint SCMR/RSNA/EACVI scientific statement integrates data from original research studies, guidelines, and opinions from experts across the field to guide responsible and evidence-based utilization of CMR strain.

title: Clinical Characteristics and Transplacental Treatment of Fetal Ventricular Tachycardia: A Nationwide Survey in Japan.
authorString: Miyoshi T, Kim KS, Kan N, Shimada E, Kato Y, Maeno Y, Collaborators.
abstractText:
Background

Fetal ventricular tachycardia (VT) is an ultra-rare form of tachyarrhythmia, and no established management strategy currently exists.

Objectives

This study aimed to clarify the current diagnostic and management approaches for fetal VT.

Methods

A nationwide survey of suspected fetal VT was conducted across 77 tertiary referral facilities in Japan between 2014 and 2023.

Results

In total, 24 fetal VT cases from 18 facilities were analyzed. Twenty cases were diagnosed based on atrioventricular dissociation. Four were initially diagnosed as supraventricular tachycardia. VT occurred by 32 6/7 weeks of gestation in all nine long QT syndrome (LQTS) cases (LQT 2 in six, LQT 3 in two, and other in one), whereas 8/15 non-LQTS cases occurred at term. Eight of 20 cases managed as fetal VT, and three of four cases managed as fetal supraventricular tachycardia received fetal treatment. Fetal treatments were effective in 9/11 cases overall and in 8/9 LQTS cases. Side effects were observed in 6/11 cases; however, no serious adverse events occurred, except one case of lidocaine toxicity. After birth, LQTS cases were more likely to be refractory to treatment than non-LQT cases (8/9 vs. 6/14), requiring multidisciplinary management. Neurodevelopmental delay was more frequent in LQTS cases than in non-LQTS cases (6/9 vs. 2/14).

Conclusions

Transplacental treatment is highly recommended for preterm fetal VT. In particular, in cases of fetal VT diagnosed before 33 weeks of gestation, aggressive fetal treatment including magnesium sulfate and β-blockers should be considered with the possibility of LQT 2 or 3.

title: Nuclear magnetic resonance-derived lipoprotein profile and risk of atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence after catheter ablation: a case-cohort design within the PREDIMAR trial.
authorString: Belzunce ANL, Goni L, Barrio-López MT, Ramos P, Tercedor L, Ibáñez Criado JL, Amigó N, Torné P, Razquin C, de la O V, Ibáñez-Criado A, Macías-Ruiz R, Martínez-González MÁ, García-Bolao I, Almendral J, Ruiz-Canela M.
abstractText:
Background

Lipoproteins could be potential biomarkers of atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence (TAR) after catheter ablation; however, their association remains inconclusive and based exclusively on routine lipid measurements. Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) enables detailed lipoprotein characterization beyond conventional assays.

Objective

To identify a baseline NMR-derived lipoprotein profile associated with the risk of TAR after catheter ablation.

Methods

We conducted a case-cohort study (212 cases and 238 participants in a random sub-cohort, with 93 overlapping cases) nested in the PREDIMAR (PRevención con DIeta Mediterránea de Arritmias Recurrentes) trial. Conventional lipoprotein profiles were measured using the Pentra C-200 and advanced lipoprotein profiles were assessed by NMR. Lipoprotein values were normalized and scaled to one standard deviation using Blom's inverse normal transformation. Cox models were used to assess the associations between baseline lipoproteins and TAR. Additionally, a cholesteryl ester transfer (CETP)-mediated lipoprotein exchange score was constructed and evaluated.

Results

After 18-month follow-up, higher baseline remnant cholesterol (hazard ratio = 1.26, 95% confidence interval= 1.06-1.51, per SD), higher cholesterol and triglyceride content in very-low-density lipoproteins (VLDL) (hazard ratioperSD = 1.22, 95% confidence interval= 1.03-1.46) or in intermediate-density lipoproteins (IDL) (hazard ratioperSD = 1.29, 95% confidence interval= 1.09-1.52), showed increased risks of TAR. Higher triglyceride-to-HDL cholesterol ratio was directly associated, and higher triglyceride-to-VLDL cholesterol and triglyceride-to-IDL cholesterol ratios were inversely associated with recurrence. A CETP-mediated lipoprotein exchange score was directly associated with recurrence.

Conclusion

An atherogenic lipoprotein profile characterized by elevated remnant cholesterol is associated with a higher risk of TAR after catheter ablation.

title: Substrate Comprising Fibrosis and Epicardial Adipose Tissue-Associated Electrophysiological Remodeling Can Sustain Atrial Fibrillation Drivers: Insights from Image-Personalized Computational Simulations.
authorString: Chahine Y, Wood H, Telle Å, Bifulco SF, Anderson CA, Chamoun N, Kassar A, Haykal R, Ristić Z, Augustin CM, Akoum N, Boyle PM.
abstractText:
Background

Computational models of atrial fibrillation (AF) help clarify arrhythmia mechanisms, but the contribution of left atrial (LA) epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) is rarely included.

Objective

To assess whether incorporating EAT-associated effects into fibrosis-based atrial models alters reentrant arrhythmia inducibility, and to characterize the pro-arrhythmic properties of EAT-affected tissue.

Methods

LA fibrosis and EAT were quantified by LGE and Dixon MRI in 19 patients with persistent AF. For each patient, three anatomically identical image-personalized models were built (fibrosis only; fibrosis plus half-epicardial EAT effects, 0.5 mm; fibrosis plus full-epicardial EAT effects, 1.0 mm), yielding 855 simulations. In EAT regions, inward rectifier K+ current was reduced by 35%, intracellular K+ by 50%, and conduction velocity by 25%.

Results

Sustained reentry occurred in 370 simulations (43.3%), of which 306 had a functional (rotor-driven) component. Functional reentry inducibility rose from 22.8% (fibrosis only) to 41.4% (half-EAT) and 43.2% (full-EAT). At least one functional reentry was inducible in 12/19 fibrosis-only models, 18/19 half-EAT models, and 19/19 full-EAT models. Median inducible simulations per patient increased from 4 to 6 (p=0.004) and 7 (p=0.003), without significant difference between half- and full-EAT (p=0.895). Fibrosis/EAT overlap regions comprised only 2.1% of the LA wall but were the most arrhythmogenic, with a median 65.5% of their volume harboring reentry versus 8.8% (non-substrate), 37.3% (fibrosis), and 42.8% (EAT) (all p<0.001). In an exploratory analysis of PVI-only ablation patients (n=13), fibrosis-EAT overlap outside the PVI region was associated with 1-year recurrence (log-rank p=0.007).

Conclusion

Adding EAT effects to fibrosis-based models increased sustained functional reentry, with transmural depth contributing only modestly. Reentry anchored preferentially where fibrosis and EAT effects coexisted.

title: Pre-participation cardiovascular evaluation in Italian elite athletes (2023-2026): diagnostic yield, accuracy, and cost analysis.
authorString: Di Gioia G, Ferrera A, Maestrini V, Mango F, Spera FR, Ginelli D, Serdoz A, Paoletti G, Spinelli A, Fiore R, Monosilio S, Pelliccia A, Squeo MR.
abstractText:
Introduction

Elite athletes represent a unique population within competitive sports. Despite repeated cardiovascular screening during their careers, they may harbour clinically silent but potentially serious cardiovascular diseases. Therefore, cardiovascular evaluation in elite athletes may require a sensitive and comprehensive diagnostic approach.

Methods

We analyzed 1505 elite athletes, undergoing comprehensive PPS including resting ECG, transthoracic echocardiography (TTE), and cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET). Major cardiovascular abnormalities (MCA) and cardiomyopathies were established according to the final clinical diagnosis, served as the reference standard. Sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values (NPV), and ROC analyses were assessed for ECG alone and for ECG combined with CPET or TTE.

Results

MCA were identified in 17 athletes (1.13%), including 7 cardiomyopathies (0.46%) and 6 channelopathies (0.40%). CPET identified additional cardiomyopathies through exercise-induced arrhythmias, including cases not detected by resting ECG, whereas TTE identified structural and coronary abnormalities not evident on ECG. Resting ECG showed a sensitivity of 58.8% and specificity of 94.0% for MCA, with a NPV 99.5%. The addition of CPET increased sensitivity to 82.4%, although specificity decreased to 82.2%. ECG + TTE achieved a sensitivity of 76.5% and specificity of 91.5%. ROC analysis showed AUCs of 0.76 for ECG, 0.82 for ECG + CPET, and 0.84 for ECG + TTE for MCA.

Conclusion

In this highly selected cohort of elite athletes, integrating ECG, CPET, and TTE provided complementary diagnostic information and increased the detection of MCA compared with resting ECG alone. These findings support the feasibility of a comprehensive cardiovascular evaluation model in highly selected athletes evaluated within specialized sports cardiology settings.

title: Differences in Tricuspid Valve Insufficiency, Mechanical Synchrony, and Cardiac Remodeling Between Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing and Right Ventricular Pacing.
authorString: Jin Q, Li Z, Ren X, Li J, He M, Zhang Y, Wang H.
abstractText:
Background

Cardiac implantable electronic device-induced tricuspid regurgitation (CIED-induced TR) involves primary (lead-induced) and functional etiologies. The impact of left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) versus right ventricular pacing (RVP) on these mechanisms remains unclear.

Objective

To compare the incidence and mechanisms of TR among pacing modalities, and evaluate the prognostic significance of these mechanisms.

Methods

We analyzed 225 patients with first-time RV apical pacing (RVAP, n=97) or RV septal pacing (RVSP, n=78) using stylet-driven leads, and LBBAP (n=50) using lumenless leads. Echocardiography and electrocardiography were performed at baseline and 2 years post-implantation. Three-dimensional echocardiography assessed lead interference. Kaplan-Meier analysis compared event-free survival between lead-induced (LITR) and functional TR (FTR) groups. Cox regression identified predictors for adverse outcomes.

Results

Despite a higher baseline heart failure burden than RVP (P< .001), LBBAP showed the lowest TR progression rate (20.0% vs RVAP 43.3% vs RVSP 35.9%, P=.020) over 25.8 months. Mechanistically, LBBAP shortened QRS duration (vs RVP widening, P< .001) and demonstrated less lead interference than RVAP (28.0% vs 50.5%, P= .009). Furthermore, LBBAP showed greater left-heart reverse remodeling and improvement in mitral regurgitation, while preserving right-heart structure and function better than RVP. Over 37.4 months, LITR showed worse outcomes than FTR (P= .03). LITR, pulmonary hypertension, reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, and elevated creatinine were independent predictors for adverse outcomes.

Conclusion

LBBAP was associated with less CIED-induced TR than RVP, likely through reduced mechanical interference, superior electrical synchrony, and favorable cardiac remodeling. Furthermore, LITR was associated with a worse prognosis than FTR.

title: Intravascular imaging guidance in complex PCI: a meta-analysis of randomized trials across complex lesion subsets.
authorString: Basile M, Gómez Herrero J, Lara García A, de la Torre Hernández JM, Alfonso F, Pan M, Zubiaur J, Rivero Santana B, Tébar D, Jiménez Valero S, Galeote G, Moreno R, Jurado Román A.
abstractText:
Background

Recent randomized trials have reported conflicting results regarding the clinical benefit of intravascular imaging (IVI) in complex percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The aim of this research was to evaluate whether IVI guidance reduces target vessel failure (TVF) in complex PCI.

Methods

PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched through June 2026 for randomized trials comparing IVI-guided with angiography-guided PCI in trial-defined complex PCI or extractable complex-lesion cohorts. Risk ratios (RRs) were pooled using random-effects models. Prespecified analyses evaluated left main, chronic total occlusion, bifurcation, and moderate-to-severely calcified lesions, with a sensitivity analysis excluding IVUS-CHIP. Secondary clinical outcomes and potential effect modification by imaging modality were evaluated in exploratory analyses.

Results

Fifteen trials, including 11,557 patients were analyzed. IVI reduced TVF (RR, 0.70; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.56-0.86; number needed to treat, 26 [95% CI, 18-55]). Lesion-specific estimates consistently favored IVI but were not significant; all became significant after excluding IVUS-CHIP. IVI reduced target vessel revascularization (RR, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.53-0.87), target lesion revascularization (RR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.52-0.85), and stent thrombosis (RR, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.24-0.73). All-cause mortality was not reduced, whereas IVI guidance showed a borderline association with 26% lower cardiovascular mortality (RR, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.54-1.00; p = 0.05). Effects were similar for intravascular ultrasound and optical coherence tomography (interaction p = 0.93).

Conclusions

IVI guidance reduced TVF, repeat revascularization, and stent thrombosis in complex PCI, with consistent but exploratory effects across major lesion subsets and a borderline association with lower cardiovascular mortality.

title: Pathway-Guided and Patient-Centered Therapeutic Strategies in Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease.
authorString: Canonico ME, Avvedimento M, Borrelli F, Giugliano G, Gargiulo G, Piccolo R, Stabile E, Mestroni L, Taylor MRG, Chen SN, Esposito G, Bonaca MP, Lombardi R.
abstractText: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), encompassing coronary artery disease (CAD), cerebrovascular disease (ischemic stroke, IS; and transient ischemic attack, TIA), and peripheral artery disease (PAD) of atherosclerotic origin, remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide despite major advances in prevention and treatment. Although atherosclerosis arises from the convergence of endothelial injury, lipid accumulation, inflammation, and thrombosis, the relative contribution of these pathogenic processes varies markedly among individuals, due to the effects of genetics, demographic, and racial factors, lifestyle behaviors and comorbidities, several of which are modifiable. The variability in the atherosclerosis underlying mechanisms results in substantial heterogeneity in clinical presentation, disease progression, and therapeutic response. Recently, ASCVD management has expanded beyond single-pathway intensification toward pathway-guided, patient-centered, multi-targeted therapeutic strategies. Over the past decade, we have witnessed the development of highly specific therapeutics, including small-molecule inhibitors, monoclonal antibodies, and RNA-based therapies, while genome-editing approaches remain at an investigational stage. Contemporary Phase 3 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have demonstrated that several novel agents reduce cardiovascular (CV) risk, whereas others produce biological effects without improving outcomes, underscoring the need for outcome-based validation. Despite improved safety profiles and enhanced treatment adherence, the optimal integration of these therapies into clinical practice continues to evolve. In this narrative review, we evaluate evidence from established, emerging, and investigational therapeutic strategies for ASCVD prevention and treatment. We also describe the impact of endothelial-protective, lipid-lowering, anti-inflammatory, and antithrombotic, strategies on CV outcomes, with particular emphasis on differential efficacy across patient subgroups, vascular territories, and clinical settings. In addition to synthesizing evidence from contemporary clinical trials, this review proposes a novel pathway- and phenotype-based conceptual framework for individualized ASCVD management and secondary prevention. The framework integrates residual-risk phenotypes with clinical characteristics, comorbidities, vascular territory, and treatment-related considerations to support residual-risk-guided selection of complementary evidence-based therapies while balancing anticipated benefit, safety, treatment burden, and adherence.

title: Rivaroxaban for Stroke Prevention in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Without Atrial Fibrillation and With Impaired Left Atrial Reservoir Strain: Design and Rationale of the LA-HCM Randomized Trial.
authorString: Donal E, Wazzan AAL, Lairez O, Charron P, Piriou N, Biere L, Reant P, Paglia O, Labombarda F, Eicher JC, Barone-Rochette G, Ridon H, Habib G, Huttin O, Aissaoui N, Logeart D, Fauvel C, Mewton N, Galli E, Cariou E, Bernard A, Hulot JS, Fauchier L, Palassin P, Ferre JC, Ganivet A, Mansour A, Oger E.
abstractText:
Background

Current stroke prevention strategies in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) rely on the detection of atrial fibrillation (AF), although thromboembolic events may occur before arrhythmia is documented. These observations support atrial cardiomyopathy as the substrate for thrombogenesis and highlight the need for imaging-guided risk stratification. Left atrial reservoir strain (LARS), derived from speckle-tracking echocardiography, detects atrial dysfunction earlier than left atrial enlargement and has been associated with AF and thromboembolic events. The LA-HCM trial evaluates whether rivaroxaban reduces thromboembolic events in patients with HCM, sinus rhythm, no documented AF, and impaired LARS. LA-HCM is a prospective, multicentre, randomized, open-label trial with blinded endpoint adjudication (PROBE design), sponsored by Rennes University Hospital and conducted in 17 French centres. A total of 532 adults with HCM, sinus rhythm, no documented AF, and core-laboratory-confirmed LARS ≤20% are randomized 1:1 to rivaroxaban or standard care. Participants are followed for 24 months. The primary endpoint is the composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke-including newly detected silent cerebral infarction on paired baseline and 24-month brain MRI-and systemic embolism at 24 months. LA-HCM tests whether rivaroxaban improves outcomes in a population with HCM, no documented AF, and impaired LARS. It evaluates a LARS-based treatment-allocation strategy but is not designed to validate the predictive utility or optimal threshold of LARS.

title: Delirium after Aortic Arch Surgery with Hypothermic Circulatory Arrest: Clinical and Neuroimaging Insights from the GOT ICE Randomized Trial.
authorString: Hughes GC, Browndyke JN, Chen EP, Szeto WY, DiMaio JM, Brinkman WT, Markovic J, Gaca JG, Blumenthal JA, Karhausen JA, James ML, Yanez D, Li YJ, Mathew JP.
abstractText:
Background

Postoperative delirium (POD) is a complication of arch surgery with hypothermic circulatory arrest (HCA) and may contribute to long-term cognitive decline, but prospective data are limited. We examined its incidence, predictors, and neurocognitive and neuroimaging correlates.

Methods

The Cognitive Effects of Body Temperature During Hypothermic Circulatory Arrest trial compared deep versus moderate hypothermia during elective arch repair. Delirium was assessed preoperatively and on postoperative days 1-3 using the Confusion Assessment Method. Thirty-day outcomes, cognition, quality of life, and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging at 4 weeks and 1 year were compared by POD status.

Results

Of 269 patients with complete assessments, POD occurred in 34.6% and did not differ significantly between hypothermia groups (p=0.45). Patients with POD had higher stroke rates (9.7% vs 0.6%; p<0.001), prolonged ventilation (3.2% vs. 0%; p=0.017), and longer hospitalization (8.5 vs. 5.9 days; p<0.001). Affected patients had worse cognition and quality of life (p<0.001) at 30 days, with partial recovery at 1 year. Baseline imaging demonstrated reduced thalamo-cerebellar connectivity in patients who developed POD (p<0.01, p-FWE<0.05), with persistent abnormalities at 1-year. Higher baseline cognition and ejection fraction were protective against POD (OR<1), whereas longer antegrade cerebral perfusion time increased risk (OR 1.03; 95% CI, 1.005-1.05; p=0.019).

Conclusions

POD affects >one-third of patients after arch surgery with HCA and is associated with worse 30-day and 1-year cognitive outcomes with enduring imaging abnormalities. Reduced preoperative thalamo-cerebellar connectivity suggests a preexisting neural vulnerability, indicating that delirium may unmask rather than cause long-term cognitive decline.

title: Omega-3 Fatty Acids in the Management of Cardiovascular Disease Prevention.
authorString: Finocchiaro S, Cutore L, Bordonaro C, Cusmano C, Nastasi D, Nasisi F, Capodanno D.
abstractText:
Purpose

Omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids lower triglycerides and modulate inflammation, thrombosis, and endothelial function, providing a rationale for their use in cardiovascular prevention. This review examines the influence of formulation, dose, and patient selection on clinical outcomes.

Methods

A targeted PubMed search through 31 May 2026 informed the selection of randomized trials and relevant mechanistic and observational studies, complemented by guideline and regulatory documents and selected publications added during revision.

Results

Low-dose mixed eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA)/docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) formulations were generally neutral in contemporary prevention trials. JELIS reported fewer major coronary events with EPA 1.8 g/day (2.8% vs. 3.5%; hazard ratio 0.81). In REDUCE-IT, icosapent ethyl 4 g/day reduced major ischemic events (17.2% vs. 22.0%; hazard ratio 0.75), whereas STRENGTH found no benefit with 4 g/day EPA/DHA (12.0% vs. 12.2%; hazard ratio 0.99). Differences in biological exposure, placebo choice, and pharmacological properties may contribute to these findings, although their relative importance remains debated. Evidence for stroke, heart failure, and peripheral artery disease varies by population and endpoint, while higher-dose therapy requires attention to atrial fibrillation and bleeding.

Conclusion

Current evidence supports prescription icosapent ethyl in selected statin-treated patients with persistent hypertriglyceridemia, with treatment guided by cardiovascular risk, formulation, and dose rather than considering omega-3 preparations as an interchangeable class.

title: Efficacy and safety of artificial intelligence-assisted image-guided navigation in complex endovascular aortic repair: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authorString: Neri Júnior JCS, Batista FC, Estevam RVA, Heredia BC, Tinoco JA, de Azevedo GVMM, Riguetti-Pinto CR.
abstractText:
Background

Complex endovascular aortic repair exposes patients and operators to substantial radiation, contrast, and long procedures. Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted image-guided navigation, based on cloud-based three-dimensional image fusion, has been proposed to improve intraoperative guidance, but its comparative benefit is uncertain.

Methods

We searched MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science (last search July 2025) for studies comparing AI-assisted image-guided navigation with conventional fluoroscopy and digital subtraction angiography during complex endovascular aortic repair. No navigation platform was prespecified. Random-effects meta-analyses yielded mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI); heterogeneity was quantified with I2. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I and certainty with GRADE.

Results

Three retrospective cohorts (332 patients; 189 AI, 143 control), all evaluating one cloud-based platform (Cydar EV), were eligible. AI-assisted navigation was associated with a lower radiation dose (2 studies, 216 patients; MD -1435.85 mGy, 95% CI -2208.84 to -662.86; I2 = 0%). No significant differences were found in fluoroscopy time (MD -11.04 minutes, 95% CI -25.37 to 3.29; I2 = 65%), operative time (MD -16.39 minutes, 95% CI -37.21 to 4.42; I2 = 0%), or contrast volume (MD -30.59 mL, 95% CI -73.95 to 12.76; I2 = 94%). Mortality and major adverse events (single studies) did not differ significantly.

Conclusions

Cydar EV-assisted navigation may reduce radiation dose during complex endovascular aortic repair, but evidence is limited to retrospective studies of a single platform and does not establish a class effect for other AI-assisted navigation systems. Prospective comparative studies across platforms are needed.

title: Effect of auricular acupressure as an adjunct to standard postoperative care on physical and psychological outcomes following coronary artery bypass graft surgery: protocol for a randomised, single-blind, sham-controlled trial.
authorString: Allahbakhshian A, Farshbaf-Khalili A, Ghasemi K, Rahimi H, Babaei L, Radimaher F.

title: Marfan Syndrome versus Loeys-Dietz Syndrome after Aortic Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Reconstructed Time-to-Event Data.
authorString: Fischer J, Wehner S, Arobo A, Almehandi A, Passos FS, Eitel C, Kirov H, Jacquemyn X, Sultan I, Doenst T, Caldonazo T.
abstractText:
Objective

Marfan syndrome (MFS) and Loeys-Dietz syndrome (LDS) are hereditary connective tissue diseases, both characterized by aortic root and vessel involvement with an increased risk of aneurysms and dissections. Despite advances in surgical techniques and improved postoperative follow-up, the impact of surgery on long-term outcomes in these patient groups is still unknown.

Methods

We performed a systematic review and a meta-analysis to compare the postoperative long-term events. The main outcome was long-term survival. Additional outcomes were freedom from dissection and reoperation. After reconstruction of time-to-event data for the individual survival analysis, pooled Kaplan-Meier curves for the endpoints were generated.

Results

A total of 1,794 studies were identified, of which 5 were included in the analysis, encompassing 1,005 patients (MFS: 778; LDS: 227). With MFS as the reference group, there was no significant difference in long-term survival between both groups, based on age (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.919; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.58-1.45; p=0.717) or postoperative follow-up (HR: 0.997; 95% CI: 0.45-2.19; p=0.995). However, LDS was associated with higher risk of dissection (HR: 0.331; 95% CI: 0.21-0.53; p<0.005) and reoperation (HR: 0.603; 95% CI: 0.40-0.90; p=0.014), reflecting unadjusted comparisons reconstructed from Kaplan-Meier curves.

Conclusion

Although long-term survival is similar between MFS and LDS patients, those with LDS face a significantly higher risk of aortic dissection and reoperation. This elevated risk may be partly explained by the intrinsic genotypic heterogeneity of the LDS population. However, our pooled analysis could not fully adjust for this heterogeneity, underscoring the need for vigilant lifelong imaging surveillance and individualized surgical thresholds in LDS.

title: Telecardiology bridges the gap in pediatric heart care: A systematic review.
authorString: Faheem Y, Adhikari A, Espinosa-Villagomez P, Astudillo-Silva C, Bamgbose MO, Hidalgo Corral N.
abstractText: BackgroundGeographic disparities limit access to pediatric cardiology care in rural and underserved communities, contributing to delayed diagnosis, increased transfers, higher costs, and preventable morbidity. Telecardiology has emerged as a scalable strategy to address subspecialty workforce shortages. This review evaluates the effectiveness of telecardiology versus standard in-person care in improving diagnostic timeliness, access to specialist care, and clinical outcomes; its diagnostic accuracy relative to in-person evaluation; and barriers to implementation, in pediatric populations with congenital or acquired heart disease in rural or underserved communities.MethodsPubMed, Medline, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched, identifying 1200 articles; 182 underwent full-text review. After exclusions, 74 studies were quality appraised using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist, and 49 high-quality studies were included, evaluating synchronous tele echocardiography, asynchronous store and forward transmission, or remote physiologic monitoring in pediatric patients in rural or resource limited settings.ResultsAcross the 49 included studies, tele echocardiography demonstrated diagnostic concordance ≥98% versus in person evaluation, and fetal telecardiology achieved 100% sensitivity and specificity for complex congenital heart disease in select programs. In the included studies, telecardiology reduced time to diagnosis (100 vs. 147 min, P < .001), interfacility transport by up to 58%, and emergency department utilization (0.4-0.0 visits per patient month in one interstage monitoring program, P = 0.0004). Hospital survival improved from 29.8% to 54.1% (P = 0.002) in one ECMO program, and post Stage II palliation complications decreased from 34.1% to 18.4% (P = 0.02). Cost analyses showed net savings across settings. Barriers included broadband limitations, reimbursement constraints, and regulatory challenges.ConclusionsTelecardiology is a high-impact, evidence-based strategy that can improve diagnostic efficiency, reduce interfacility transfers, lower healthcare utilization, and expand access to pediatric cardiology care without compromising outcomes when implemented with adequate sonographer training and infrastructure investment; consistent with clinical experience, these requirements have limited adoption of store-and-forward fetal echocardiography at some centers. Addressing reimbursement and regulatory barriers is essential for equitable, sustainable implementation.

title: Electrophysiologist-Led Deep Sedation for Pulsed Field Ablation of Atrial Fibrillation Using a Bipolar Contact Force Focal Catheter: The DEEP-PFA Randomized Controlled Trial.
authorString: Li F, Zhou L, Zhao Y, Wei S, Feng H, Zhou M, Wang J, Kong X, Lv Y, Guo X, He L, Xia S, Jiang C, Li X, Zhang J, Liu X, Zhou N, Li S, Jiang C, Tang R, Zuo S, Sang C, Long D, Zei PC, Dong J, Ma C.

title: Coronary Vasculitis and Myocarditis in Acute Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Flares With Macrophage Activating Syndrome.
authorString: Qamar S, Luo M, Ijaz N, Masri SC, Peters A.
abstractText: Cardiovascular disease is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Although accelerated atherosclerosis is well recognized, SLE-related coronary vasculitis and microvascular injury remain underdiagnosed. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) offers unique tissue characterization that may reveal atypical patterns of myocardial injury. We describe 2 patients with active SLE who presented with acute cardiac symptoms and elevated cardiac biomarkers. CMR demonstrated both classic inflammatory findings of lupus myopericarditis (subepicardial late gadolinium enhancement and pericardial enhancement) and vascular-appearing injury, including transmural and subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement. In 1 case, coronary vascular injury occurred in the setting of systemic infection and macrophage activating syndrome, whereas in the other, coronary angiography showed normal coronary arteries, supporting a nonatherosclerotic mechanism such as coronary vasculitis or microvascular thrombosis. Serial CMR demonstrated improvement following immunosuppressive therapy. CMR can identify mixed myocardial injury phenotypes in SLE, providing critical diagnostic and follow-up information beyond conventional imaging.

title: Mitochondrial dynamics and repair differences in two mouse models of Friedreich's ataxia.
authorString: Salinas L, Figueroa F, Montgomery-Bowie CB, Cox GP, Cortopassi G, Dedkova EN.
abstractText: Friedreich's ataxia (FA) is an inherited disorder caused by reduced expression of the mitochondrial protein frataxin (FXN). Although defined as a neurodegenerative disease, cardiomyopathy is the leading cause of mortality. Cardiac manifestations of FA span from concentric hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with preserved systolic function and impaired diastolic relaxation, resembling heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), to systolic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). The molecular mechanisms driving progression towards these cardiac phenotypes remain poorly understood. We examined mitochondrial content, dynamics and mitophagy in two FA mouse models: cardiac/skeletal muscle-specific MCK-Cre FXN knockout (FXN-cKO) mice, which develop HFrEF, and inducible FXN knockdown (FXNKD) mice, which develop HFpEF-like cardiomyopathy. FXN-cKO hearts exhibited increased mitochondrial transcription factor A expression, an elevated mitochondrial-to-nuclear DNA ratio and greater mitochondrial density by electron microscopy, consistent with enhanced mitochondrial biogenesis. In contrast, FXNKD hearts showed no changes in mitochondrial content or biogenesis markers. Mitochondrial dynamics were markedly altered in FXN-cKO hearts, with reduced mitofusin-2 and increased FIS1 expression, accompanied by smaller, fragmented mitochondria. FXNKD hearts exhibited preserved fission, modestly increased fusion and mild mitochondrial enlargement. Markers of mitophagy were increased in FXN-cKO hearts, but a reduced LC3-II/I ratio suggested impaired autophagosome maturation and defective mitochondrial clearance. No changes in mitophagy were observed in FXNKD hearts. These findings demonstrate that FA-associated HFrEF is characterized by increased mitochondrial biogenesis coupled with impaired mitochondrial quality control and fragmentation, whereas FA-associated HFpEF-like phenotype shows preserved mitochondrial architecture and turnover. Mitochondrial remodelling programmes may underlie divergent cardiac phenotypes in FA and represent therapeutic targets for disease modification. KEY POINTS: Friedreich's ataxia (FA) cardiomyopathy develops as heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) or heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)-like disease, but mechanisms leading to different cardiac phenotypes are unclear. We compared mitochondrial remodelling in FA mouse models with divergent cardiac phenotypes. Frataxin knockout (FXN-cKO) mice with HFrEF phenotype showed increased mitochondrial biogenesis, fragmentation and impaired mitochondrial quality control. FXN knockdown (FXNKD) mice with HFpEF-like phenotype showed largely preserved mitochondrial structure and turnover. Distinct mitochondrial adaptations may drive phenotype-specific cardiac outcomes in FA.

title: First-Line Thrombectomy for Acute Intracranial Atherosclerotic Stenosis-Related Vertebrobasilar Artery Occlusion: Stent Retriever-Based Versus Contact Aspiration Thrombectomy Strategies.
authorString: Huang B, Lu G, Ma Y, Xie X, Zhao L, Cao Y, Jia Z, Lv P, Liu S, Shi H.
abstractText:
Purpose

To compare procedural and clinical outcomes of first-line contact aspiration thrombectomy (CAT) versus a stent retriever-based strategy in acute intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (ICAS)-related vertebrobasilar artery occlusion (VBAO).

Materials and methods

This retrospective two-center study included consecutive patients with acute ICAS-related VBAO treated between 2019 and 2024. Patients were classified by first-line strategy as CAT or an SRT-based strategy comprising stent retriever thrombectomy alone or with aspiration assistance. Primary outcomes were first-pass recanalization (FPR; modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction grade ≥ 2b after one device pass) and 90-day favorable functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score 0-3). Multivariable regression was used for outcome comparisons, with inverse probability weighting (IPW) as a sensitivity analysis.

Results

Among 129 patients, 38 received CAT and 91 received an SRT-based strategy. FPR was higher with the SRT-based strategy than with CAT (74.7% vs. 52.6%; adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.66; 95% CI, 1.15-6.16; p = 0.022). The 90-day favorable outcome did not differ significantly (48.4% vs. 36.8%; aOR, 1.69; 95% CI, 0.71-4.02; p = 0.235). In the primary adjusted analysis, the SRT-based strategy was associated with lower 90-day mortality (19.8% vs. 34.2%; aOR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.15-0.96; p = 0.041), fewer strategy switches (1.1% vs. 34.2%; p < 0.001), and shorter puncture-to-recanalization time (63.0 vs. 73.5 min; p = 0.003). IPW supported these procedural advantages, whereas clinical outcome differences were nonsignificant.

Conclusion

In acute ICAS-related VBAO, a first-line SRT-based strategy was associated with better procedural performance than CAT, including higher first-pass recanalization, fewer strategy switches, and shorter puncture-to-recanalization time.

title: Delayed left ventricular remodelling in patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction: a systematic review.
authorString: Whittaker L, Jeyalan V, Dewhurst M, Chapman M, Brown A, Gale CP, Uphoff E, Wilkinson C.

title: Z-DNA binding protein 1 (ZBP1): Molecular mechanisms and therapeutic significance in metabolic diseases.
authorString: Cai G, Liang P, Ye X, Jiang J, Yang T, Yang F, Bai Y.
abstractText: Metabolic diseases are characterized by persistent disturbances in glucose, lipid, and energy homeostasis and include obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and related cardiovascular complications. Chronic inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and dysregulated cell death contribute substantially to their progression. Identifying molecular sensors that connect metabolic stress with inflammatory tissue injury may therefore reveal new targets for disease intervention. Z-DNA-binding protein 1 (ZBP1) is a conformation-selective nucleic acid sensor that couples Z-DNA/Z-RNA recognition to RIPK-dependent inflammatory signaling and regulated cell death. Emerging preclinical evidence implicates dysregulated ZBP1 signaling in atherosclerosis, metabolic liver injury, diabetes-associated renal damage, and metabolic stress-related cardiac and neurological complications. This review examines the structural basis and regulatory mechanisms of ZBP1 activation and discusses its potential involvement in sterile inflammation, mitochondrial stress, immunometabolic remodeling, and PANoptosis. Emerging approaches for modulating ZBP1 signaling are also evaluated according to their degree of direct target engagement and translational maturity. Current evidence supports ZBP1 as a context-dependent link between abnormal nucleic acid sensing and metabolic tissue injury, although its disease specificity, therapeutic window, and clinical relevance remain uncertain.

title: Targeting macrophage-derived oncostatin M preserves cardiomyocyte mitochondrial bioenergetics and contractile function in fulminant myocarditis.
authorString: Yan Y, Sun Z, He Y, Zhuang Y, Jiang J.
abstractText:
Background

Fulminant myocarditis (FM) is an acute inflammatory cardiomyopathy with high risk of cardiogenic shock. Current management relies largely on circulatory support, while mechanism-based pharmacological targets remain poorly defined.

Methods

Cardiac CD45+ single-cell RNA sequencing, whole-heart single-nucleus RNA sequencing, ligand-target inference, spatial validation, and human plasma/myocardial analyses were integrated to define disease-associated cellular interactions. CCR2+ macrophage sorting, macrophage depletion, CVB3-stimulated BMDMs, transcription-factor perturbation, ChIP-qPCR, and promoter assays defined the source and regulation of OSM. OSM signaling was examined using recombinant OSM, OSM-neutralizing antibody, macrophage Osm knockdown, cardiomyocyte Osmr silencing, and STAT3/ERK1/2 inhibition, followed by transcriptomic, mitochondrial, contractile, and in vivo analyses.

Results

FM featured expansion of CCR2+ inflammatory macrophages, cardiomyocyte inflammatory/stress remodeling, and enhanced macrophage-to-cardiomyocyte OSM-OSMR signaling. Circulating OSM was increased in patients with FM and correlated with higher NT-proBNP and cTnI and lower LVEF. OSM was produced predominantly by CCR2+ macrophages and transcriptionally induced by IRF1 after CVB3 stimulation. Recombinant OSM aggravated mortality, systolic dysfunction, myocardial inflammation, and cardiac injury. In cardiomyocytes, OSM activated OSMR-dependent STAT3/ERK1/2 signaling and impaired mitochondrial bioenergetics, contractility, and Ca²+ handling. OSM neutralization and macrophage Osm knockdown improved cardiomyocyte respiration and sarcomere shortening after exposure to CVB3-activated macrophage conditioned medium. In vivo, OSM neutralization improved survival, cardiac function, myocardial inflammation, mitochondrial integrity, and ATP content.

Conclusion

Macrophage OSM links inflammatory myeloid activation to cardiomyocyte mitochondrial and contractile failure in experimental FM. OSM-OSMR signaling is a candidate mechanism-based pharmacological target for acute inflammatory cardiac dysfunction.

title: Immunoregulatory gene GIMAP6 suppresses lethal atherosclerotic vasculopathy and ischemic heart failure.
authorString: Xiang C, Arusha K, Springer D, Nakamori S, Cui J, Du Jiang P, Yang ZH, Zhang Y, Jing H, Park AY, Zhu MH, Weber SE, Cagdas D, Abolhassani H, Behniafard N, Smelkinson MG, Liang Q, Everest E, Kun JF, Grogan A, Wranik BJ, Vu N, King B, Treat JD, Asomaning N, Gao S, Bennett BD, Thein SL, Zerbe CS, Holland SM, Virmani R, Remaley AT, Su HC, Zheng L, Lenardo MJ.
abstractText: Controlling hyperlipidemia has reduced but not eliminated atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) as a major cause of human mortality. Here, we report that loss of the immunoregulatory gene GTPase of immunity-associated protein 6 (Gimap6) in mice causes an inflammatory vasculopathy and accelerated atherosclerosis in the absence of hyperlipidemia. These vascular abnormalities cause progressive cardiac ischemia, myocardial infarction, and heart failure, culminating in early death. GIMAP6 loss precipitates early endothelial barrier failure and a mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS)-PPARγ-CD36 lipid-influx cascade that lowers the threshold for foam-cell formation and induces IL-6/MCP-1/TNF-mediated inflammation. Human hypomorphic GIMAP6 variants, including the African-ancestry-enriched V65I allele, are associated with altered monocyte redox balance, increased CD36-mediated lipid uptake, and early ASCVD. Thus, GIMAP6 is a crucial safeguard for vascular integrity that restrains endothelial dysfunction, macrophage foam cell generation, and inflammation that can cause lethal ASCVD independently of systemic hyperlipidemia.

title: Feasibility and durability of annular stabilization using an internal fixation ring in aortic valve repair: a computed tomography-based study.
authorString: Nishida H, Abe K, Shibata S, Tabata M.
abstractText:
Objectives

Aortic annulus dilatation is a critical risk factor for late aortic insufficiency (AI) recurrence after isolated aortic valve repair. Durable annular stabilization remains technically challenging, and long-term data are limited. We evaluated the mid-term geometric stability of a novel "internal annular fixation ring" technique using an expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) ring and metallic holder.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed 27 consecutive patients who underwent isolated aortic valve repair with internal annular fixation ring technique for significant AI between January 2015 and April 2024. Aortic root geometry was assessed using cardiac computed tomography (CT) and transthoracic echocardiography, preoperatively and during follow-up. The mean follow-up period for CT was 49.0 ± 38.2 months. The primary outcome was aortic annular stability assessed by agreement between the intended intraoperative annular diameter and the average annular diameter or area-derived annular diameter measured on follow-up CT. Secondary outcomes included freedom from aortic valve reintervention, echocardiographic and CT findings, late survival, and freedom from moderate AI.

Results

Overall, concomitant leaflet repair was performed in 74.1% of patients. The intended intraoperative annular diameter ((22 mm (22-24)) was not significantly different from the average annular diameter (22.2 mm (21.4-23.4), p = 0.49) or the area-derived annular diameter (22.2 mm (21.0-23.3), p = 0.15) measured on the follow up CT. Freedom from aortic valve reintervention was 92.3% at 7 years. Although no severe AI recurred, moderate AI developed in 7 patients (25.9%); however, no patient required hospitalization for heart failure during follow-up period.

Conclusions

The internal annular fixation ring technique provides feasible and durable aortic annulus stabilization in isolated aortic valve repair. Moderate AI recurrence highlights the need for further technical refinements.

title: Value of Left Ventricular Low Voltage Area and Ejection Fraction in Predicting End-Stage Heart Failure Outcomes After Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation in Patients With Non-Ischemic Cardiomyopathy.
authorString: Afzalian A, Oraii A, Chaumont C, Rodriguez-Queralto O, Sagawa Y, Peters CJ, Zado E, Hanumanthu BKJ, Shivamurthy P, Markman TM, Hyman MC, Tschabrunn CM, Guandalini G, Enriquez A, Garcia FC, Riley MP, Lin D, Schaller RD, Nazarian S, Callans DJ, Supple GE, Kumareswaran R, Dixit S, Frankel DS, Marchlinski FE.
abstractText:
Background

Patients with nonischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) and ventricular tachycardia are at increased risk for adverse HF outcomes, and abnormal left ventricular (LV) substrate identified by endocardial unipolar and bipolar low-voltage areas (LVAs) may aid in risk stratification. This study assessed the association of LV unipolar and bipolar LVAs with end-stage HF outcomes in patients with NICM undergoing ventricular tachycardia ablation.

Methods

Patients with NICM and LV ejection fraction (EF) <50% undergoing ventricular tachycardia ablation from 2019 to 2023 were included. Endocardial voltage mapping defined confluent (>2 cm2) unipolar LVAs as <8.27 mV and bipolar LVAs as <1.5 mV during sinus or paced rhythm. End-stage HF outcomes included HF death, LV assist device implantation, or heart transplant. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression analysis assessed associations between unipolar/bipolar LVAs and end-stage HF outcomes.

Results

One hundred eleven patients with NICM (mean age, 64.6±9.8 years; 81.1% male; mean LVEF, 33.8±11.7%) were included.
